title: Chapter 1
content:
Chapter 1

Volume 1 · Chapter 1

Southern Continent coastline.

Azure waves rolled in one after another, crashing against the shore.

Seagulls spread their wings, gliding over the small boat moored below and gazing down at the man and woman.

The golden-haired man was Merlin, former lord of the First Demon Lord Palace.

The silver-haired woman was Alice, the Holy Church’s 233rd Hero.

After a series of trials, the two had spent three days and nights rowing across the strait to reach this place.

“Do we really have to do this?”

Alice bit her trembling lips, her face pale, eyes brimming with humiliation and resentment.

“Hurry up and strip. Don’t force me to get rough—I’m still a gentleman, you know.”

Merlin kept a straight face, his hand resting on the hilt of his sword, as if ready to draw and slash at any moment.

“Uuu…”

A mournful cry escaped Alice’s throat. She never imagined she’d end up in a situation like this.

She crossed her arms over her chest, her face flushed crimson, looking every bit like someone about to be—

Alice stole a glance at Merlin. Though his expression was blank, in her eyes, he seemed unspeakably lecherous and perverted.

Poor Alice. It was as if she could already foresee the scene of her purity being defiled by the Demon Lord. Tears welled in her eyes.

If I’d known this would happen, I never would’ve become that damn Hero. Who knew I’d end up in such a humiliating situation…

Merlin furrowed his brows, tilting his head in confusion. He had no idea what was going on.

Under the pressure, Alice decided to get it over with.

She unclasped the white silk cape embroidered with the Holy Church’s emblem, removed her expensive mithril light armor, peeled off her black stockings, and untied her sheer undergarments.

Even her pink panties were neatly folded and placed on top.

Her fair skin glowed under the sunlight, her graceful curves a masterpiece of nature. Her silver hair swayed in the breeze, and then there was the modest—no, the tragically underdeveloped—washboard before her chest…

Her exposed body was a perfect blend of strength and beauty, every inch of skin inviting wild imagination.

Alice knelt on the beach, her face burning red, her lips parting in shame.

She covered her chest with one hand and her lower body with the other. The overwhelming humiliation left her mind blank.

A salty breeze brushed against her skin, sending shivers down her spine.

How could the great Hero end up being violated by a Demon Lord?!

And it all started…

three days ago…

◆

Cut to the scene. Focus, focus.

Ahem!

My name is Merlin.

The third lord of the First Demon Lord Palace.

Common folk call me the Great Demon Lord of the First Palace. The Holy Church bastards call me Lucifer the Third with cheat codes.

I go by many names, but only I know the truth—I was dragged into this world by a ritual altar against my will. In other words, I’m a transmigrator, and I came with 99999999…999 skill points.

I find this utterly ridiculous. I was a five-bar regiment commander back in my world. Why did such a cursed fate have to fall on me?

The worst part isn’t the transmigration—it’s the curse I’m under.

Over time, my heart is shrinking.

Even though I’m strong and wield the demon sword Banri Garan, I’ll still die naturally because of this.

Please, no…

I’m only eighteen! I’ve only been a Demon Lord for three years. I don’t want to die yet!

Oh, right, I should explain—eighteen for a demon is like nearly two hundred for a human. So technically, I’m already an old man pushing two hundred.

Just when I thought I’d die in this world because of the curse, I stumbled upon a secret about Banri Garan.

It can extend my life!

Don’t get the wrong idea. It’s not some cheap trick where I just adjust my glasses to buy a second of life.

No, if I kill a powerful enemy, my shrinking heart gets relief, and my lifespan extends for a while.

The stronger the enemy, the longer the extension—like Saint-tier mages and warriors.

As for lower-tier opponents? Forget it. They do nothing for my survival.

From what I can tell, if I can kill the strongest being in this world, the curse might be lifted.

Unfortunately, I haven’t found them yet.

And those so-called Heroes of the Holy Church, the hope of humanity? They’re all just loudmouthed ants. Even if they’re Saint-tier, they’re pathetically weak.

I’ve been waiting!

For the day I meet the strongest being in this world and defeat them.

Then I can break the curse and stop living in constant fear of death.

But for now, I have to keep killing and scraping by in this world…

“Brother!”

A silver bell-like voice rang out behind Merlin, snapping him from his thoughts.

He turned to see a girl in an exquisitely crafted evening gown lifting the hem of her dress as she ran toward him. Her long pink hair cascaded like a waterfall, with wavy curls at the ends, adding a playful touch. Her stunning face was the picture of innocence, like a holy angel blowing a golden horn to greet the dawn. Yet, when she smiled, there was an unexpected allure that could make one’s heart race.

This girl was Lilith, a powerful succubus, one of the Seven Generals of the First Demon Lord Palace, and Merlin’s own little sister.

Merlin found this deeply awkward. He’d been an only child in his past life, yet here he was in this world with a sister.

No doubt about it—she was his real sister.

Merlin was a soul transmigrator. When he woke up, he was in the body of a golden-haired man. And because his soul was human, all his demonic traits and abilities had vanished. The only advantage he had was his good looks—no horns, not even a bald spot. If it weren’t for the complete records in the registry, the other demons would’ve roasted him alive long ago.

At first, Merlin had been thrilled to have a sister. As an only child from the real world, he’d always longed for siblings.

But over time, that excitement faded. A sister was just… a creature that fluttered around you, always needing attention. So annoying.

At this point, someone would probably jump in shouting—

Brocon! Brocon! Brocon!

Hey, hey, hey, wake up, buddy. Time to get back to work.

Merlin insists brocon is a lie. Once you actually have a sister, you won’t have such naive thoughts.

Merlin was nearly two hundred years old. He’d long outgrown the immature phase of brocon fantasies or harem dreams.

His attitude toward the opposite sex was simple: women are trouble. He just wanted to retire, eat, and wait for death.

“Brother!” Lilith’s cheeks flushed as she lifted her skirt and excitedly ran up to Merlin. “What were you muttering to yourself in front of the mirror just now? You sounded so edgy.”

“Edgy?! Ahem!” Merlin coughed twice to cover his embarrassment. “Lilith, you’re too young to understand my sorrow. I’m way past the age of acting edgy…”

“Sorrow?” Lilith tilted her head, her finger propping up her chin. “Is it because your term as Demon Lord is up?”

“Well, that’s part of it, but not the main reason…” Merlin sat on the luxurious bed and picked up the Demon Clan Daily—

The whole “Demon Lord term is up” thing? Total nonsense.

The real reason was right there on the front page.

«Third Demon Lord Simon Mammon Successfully Raids the Holy Church’s Northern Treasury!»
«Fifth Demon Lord Ronald Beelzebub Captures Enemy in a Fit of Rage!»
«Seventh Demon Lord Mike Belial Breaks Record with a Twenty-Year Hibernation!»

I think everyone gets it. The other Demon Lords are all accomplished, constantly making headlines.

And then there’s that weirdo who makes headlines just by sleeping. Meanwhile, if I so much as nap, I get called out for terminal laziness.

I’ve never once made the front page. I’d say I’m jealous, but honestly? I really am.

Every time I wipe out the Crusade Army, some other Demon Lord steals the spotlight, dragging the First Demon Lord Palace’s reputation lower and lower.

When I think about it, I’m even more cursed than Wang Feng. The whole world is stopping me from making headlines!

So it’s not that my term is up—it’s that the Council of Elders voted to deactivate me. In plain terms…

I got fired.

Just like that. Brutal. With no marketable skills, my future looks bleak.

“Brother, if it’s not your term ending, then what is it?” Lilith interrupted his thoughts, her face filled with worry. He was the most precious person in her life.

“It’s because of the curse…” Merlin set down the newspaper and calmly told his sister.

That’s right!

That damn curse!

I used to think being a Demon Lord was great—perfect for my “eat, wait, die” lifestyle.

Good food, good drinks, servants at my beck and call. Carefree.

And whenever the curse acted up, a Hero would come along to die, giving me the life extension I needed.

But reality proved that living off others leads to a dead end.

Maybe I killed too many Heroes. These days, their quality has dropped so much that even sub-Saint-tier nobodies can become Heroes.

Killing these weaklings does nothing to ease my curse.

“Your heart… does it hurt again?” Lilith asked, her voice trembling, tears welling in her eyes.

“A little…” Merlin pressed a hand to his chest, feeling the familiar shrinking sensation—the curse was acting up.

“How could this be?!” Lilith sat beside Merlin, her voice urgent. “Is there no way to save you?”

“Besides killing to extend my life, there doesn’t seem to be another way. The Holy Church’s strength has been declining every year. I’ve lost count of how many Heroes I’ve cut down. Running out of options is only natural.” Merlin spoke lightly, as if facing death itself with complete calm.

“Then what do we do? I don’t want you to die. After Mother passed, you’re the only family I have left.” Lilith clutched her skirt and began to sob.

Merlin sighed, rubbing his temples. This was exactly why sisters were such a hassle!

He didn’t want to scold her, so instead, he ruffled her hair.

“Don’t worry. I won’t die. I’ve decided that after repelling this Crusade, I’ll leave the Demon Lord Palace and go out into the world. To be honest, I’ve never even stepped beyond the Death Marsh.”

The situation was dire. This was his choice.

He couldn’t just sit here and wait for death. He had to go out there.

Find someone worthy of fighting him—someone strong enough to extend his life.

Besides, he’d been fired by the Council. Without a job, how was he supposed to live out his “eat, wait, die” dream?

So he had to go out and find work, earn more money, and build a solid foundation for his future in this world.

You ask why he doesn’t just rob people?

Please. Have some standards. As a proud and arrogant ruler, why would he stoop to such a lowly act?

Taking money from enemies is called spoils of war—that’s fine. But robbing the innocent is bullying the weak. He couldn’t bring himself to do something so shameful. Trash like that was beneath him.

Also, he had terminal laziness. He didn’t want to deal with the hassle. What if he angered the wrong people? Then he’d have swarms of flies buzzing around him every day. How annoying.

“What?! Brother… you’re leaving?”

Lilith was devastated when she heard Merlin’s decision to leave the Demon Lord Palace. She’d never heard him mention this before. It was too sudden to accept.

She knew Merlin had never left the Death Marsh—he was a homebody through and through. How could he survive out there? She had serious doubts.

Merlin lifted an eyelid, sensing a massive surge of magic approaching. Clearly, the Crusade Army was here.

“Lilith, the Crusade is almost here. Can you help me hold them off?”

“I can, but… it’s rare for you to ask me to take the initiative.” Lilith snapped back to reality, realizing that repelling the Crusade took priority. They could talk about Merlin leaving later.

“Well…” Merlin hesitated, looking awkward.

“I get it. This must be another group of weaklings unworthy of your attention, right?” Lilith seemed to read his mind. “I’ll go wipe them out!”

Merlin pressed his lips together, a cold sweat rolling down his forehead.

That wasn’t it.

He just had terminal laziness and didn’t want to move.

But saying that out loud was embarrassing. He’d just let it slide…

title: Chapter 2
content:
Chapter 2

Volume 1 · Chapter 2

Dark clouds gathered, and a cold rain fell endlessly.

The Holy Church’s Crusade Army, clad in silver armor, surged forward like an army of white ants, marching proudly toward the First Demon Lord Palace.

They raised the sacred Crusade banners high, crushing all obstacles in their path. Their advance seemed unstoppable, the very earth trembling beneath their steps.

High above, a white whale soared through the sky, its head adorned with a golden angelic halo, its tail fins spread like wings.

Its massive form cast a shadow that blotted out the sun, and it took twenty iron chains, each as thick as a water barrel, bound by a hundred earth dragons, to restrain it.

"Remember the teachings of the Goddess of Light!"

"All evil in the world shall be purged by the light!"

"Fight for the Goddess! May my body become a flame to burn all demons to ash!"

"In the name of the Goddess Maria! Grant these warriors boundless glory!"

"Aaaaaaaamen~!!!"

The red-robed Archbishop stood atop a towering war chariot, brandishing his holy scripture as he delivered an impassioned sermon, his hands tracing crosses in the air.

The warriors, inspired, raised their spears in response, their voices booming like thunder across the plain.

"Amen!!!"

Hmm...

Why do I feel like I’ve joined a cult?

Better just hurry up and defeat the Demon Lord, take the money, and leave.

Alice, standing at the forefront of the Crusade Army, thought to herself.

Her helmet concealed her face, her white cloak as pure as snow, her silver-and-gold mithril armor intricately crafted with magical runes—clearly worth a fortune.

This was the reward Alice had been promised for agreeing to slay the Demon Lord. As the 233rd Hero, regardless of her actual strength, the most important thing was that she looked the part!

Though young, Alice had trained under her master and acquired formidable skills. After reaching the high rank, she couldn’t wait to leave the mountains and make her own way in the world.

Before departing, she had stolen her master’s hidden sword, *Lament of Light*—a thin blade hailed as a holy sword, capable of dealing 200% damage to dark creatures.

Only after descending the mountain did Alice realize how impossible it was to get by without money. She regretted stealing the holy sword—she should have taken some gold coins instead.

Penniless and desperate, Alice had no choice but to accept the call to become a Hero. If she defeated the Demon Lord, the Holy Church’s reward would set her up for life.

Before long, she’d be promoted, get a raise, become Grand Commander, then Archbishop, marry a rich and handsome man, and reach the pinnacle of life! Just thinking about it made her a little excited.

Hidden beneath her helmet, Alice’s face twisted into a strange smile.

"Hero, the battle is about to begin. Are you ready?"

The Archbishop’s sudden question snapped Alice out of her daydream.

"Ah? I… of course I’m ready, just a little worried…"

"Worried about what?" The Archbishop’s white eyebrows twitched upward, exuding the pressure of a superior.

"Lucifer III seems… very strong. I’ve heard that for the past three years, every expedition has ended in total annihilation. We…" Alice hesitated, then asked, "Can we really win?"

"The warriors of the Goddess of Light do not know defeat! This time, we will surely triumph!" The Archbishop’s eyes were bloodshot, filled with fanatical resolve.

"W-Why are you so certain?" Alice asked, confused.

"Because I am the sole survivor of the last expedition! Lucifer III is not as powerful as the rumors claim! The reason for our past failures was poor preparation—and the lack of a powerful Hero like you to aid us!" The Archbishop spoke earnestly.

Hearing the Archbishop call her powerful, Alice couldn’t help but feel a swell of pride. High-rank warriors like her were rare on the continent. She was among the best.

Perhaps Lucifer III wasn’t as strong as the legends made him out to be. Maybe the previous Heroes had simply been too weak.

"And we are different now, Hero! Look!" The Archbishop raised his arm, pointing to the sky.

Alice followed his gesture and saw the restrained white whale, its enormous body radiating an overwhelming presence.

"This white whale is the Holy Church’s century-long masterpiece—a mobile siege fortress! Its power is unmatched across the entire continent! A single strike can reduce an entire city to rubble!" The Archbishop raised both hands, his red robes billowing in the wind as he declared, "Ah~! It is the strongest! The most beautiful! The most awe-inspiring weapon! The Holy Church’s greatest achievement! A marvel of countless minds! What a magnificent artificial creature!"

Alice said nothing, staring blankly at the white whale.

She felt no beauty in it—only a sense of grotesque deformity.

Though she could sense the dangerous fluctuations of power emanating from it, she remained skeptical of its claimed might.

The main force of the Crusade Army had already reached the gates of the Demon Lord Palace, where hordes of demons roared, their sharp fangs bared, their powerful black membrane wings beating as they took to the sky.

The Demon Lord’s army had already regrouped, their bloodshot eyes burning with hunger, eager to drain human blood. Their battle lust was palpable, their starvation turning them into beasts.

The demons surged upward in a swarm, a dark cloud of wings blotting out the sky as they descended upon the Crusade Army!

"Hero, consider yourself honored!" The Archbishop raised his staff, aiming it at the swarming demon horde. "Witness the Holy Church’s strongest creation in history as it makes its debut!"

An ancient chant echoed in Alice’s ears as the Archbishop waved his staff.

The white whale in the sky twisted unnaturally, as if responding to some summons, and let out a cry like a wailing infant, sending shivers down her spine.

Its tail fins spread wide, ravenously devouring the magic in the air, warping space itself. Even the golden halo above its head turned a violent crimson.

What was this dangerous sensation?

The concentration of magic was beyond anything she had ever encountered!

Had this artificial weapon truly reached Saint-tier power?!

Alice tensed instinctively, her mind blaring warnings.

Before she could make sense of it, the Archbishop let out a roar—

"Die! You filthy, wretched demons!!!"

The white whale opened its massive jaws and unleashed a concentrated blast of magic!

The brilliance outshone the sun, tearing through the heavy clouds.

The sheer power made every heart tremble, and even souls seemed to kneel in submission before such great might.

Alice didn’t see it clearly—only a beam of light slicing through the dense demon ranks, triggering a chain of explosions. A mushroom cloud of flame erupted, followed by a tidal wave of shockwaves.

The Crusade knights were scattered, some collapsing into the muddy swamp, others thrown into the air like kites.

The surging Demon Lord’s army was annihilated in an instant.

The demons were reduced to nothing before the concentrated magic blast—not even ashes remained.

Alice barely managed to steady herself, her face pale with terror, cold sweat pouring down—

Incredible!

Was this the power of an artificial weapon?

Rivaling Saint-tier strength…

No! It seemed even stronger than Saint-tier!

A single blast carried the might of a Saint-tier ultimate technique!

Alice couldn’t understand—if the Holy Church possessed such a powerful weapon, why did they even need her, a Hero?

This white whale alone was enough. She was just a figurehead!

That so-called Lucifer III probably wouldn’t even need her to step in—this whale could just blast him to oblivion in one shot.

No one in this world could survive an attack of that magnitude…

Alice’s face was ashen, her mind reeling in awe of the white whale.

"Hahahahaha—!"

"How’s that?! Despicable demons!"

"Tremble beneath the iron hooves of the Holy Church!"

"In the name of the Goddess Maria, send you demons to hell!"

The Archbishop laughed maniacally, drool dripping from his mouth, his entire body shaking with excitement.

title: Chapter 3
content:
Chapter 3

Volume 1 · Chapter 3

First Demon Lord Palace, outside.

A light rain fell, heavy dark clouds pressing down until it was hard to breathe.

The Holy Church’s Crusade Army had already reached this place, cutting through all obstacles in their path, unstoppable.

They halted outside the palace, observing the situation.

"HAHAHAHAHA...!"

"Lucifer the Third is not here! Not even one of the Seven Generals, the great demons, is present! They must have felt the terror of our magic cannons and fled in panic!"

"This is the victory of the Goddess of Light! Long live the Holy Church’s Heroes!"

"Aaaaaaaaaamen~!"

The Archbishop, standing atop a war chariot, danced and raved like a madman, convinced he had already won the war.

The Holy Church knights raised their lances high, roaring into the rain.

"Amen!!!"

And then—

The heavy gates of the Demon Lord Palace slowly creaked open with a deep rumble.

The dark, endless corridor beyond was pitch black, nothing visible within.

Yet the sound of *click-clack* footsteps echoed out, as if from high heels, slowly approaching the entrance.

"Hm?" The Archbishop’s face twisted in confusion.

Lilith stepped out of the Demon Lord Palace, her posture graceful, her beauty beyond words.

She made no effort to conceal her power, allowing her magic to surge freely, making her overwhelming strength undeniable.

As a succubus, when Lilith released her magic, it carried an enchanting effect—weaker men were easily ensnared, reduced to slaves.

Most of the Holy Church knights, upon seeing her, were consumed by primal desire, their lower halves stiffening painfully against their armor, forcing them to hunch over in discomfort.

Even the Archbishop, that old and supposedly dignified man, gazed at Lilith with a hint of greed, his eyes glazing over.

A Saint-tier mage!

This turbulent magic was indeed astonishing!

Alice steeled herself, bracing for battle with full concentration.

Lilith remained composed, her gaze sweeping over the vast Crusade Army—

"First, congratulations on making it to the Demon Lord Palace. You’ve all worked so hard, it must have been exhausting."

"Second, I pity you wretched beasts, because you will all die here!"

"How dare you disturb my intimate time with my lord brother! This is unforgivable! I’ll feed your corpses to the wild boars!"

title: Chapter 4
content:
Chapter 4

Volume 1 · Chapter 4

Lilith's forehead veins pulsed, her eyes flashing with a sickly crimson glow, her expression slightly ferocious, marring her beautiful appearance.

The Archbishop was still somewhat coherent, though slightly affected by the charm, his speech a little slurred, "A succubus who survives by absorbing male essence has quite the temper. I can speak to His Holiness the Pope and have you made a priestess. Then you'll have all the essence you could ever want."

The Church's knights listened and burst into laughter, their lewd voices making Alice feel uncomfortable all over.

"Hmph! If you want to take me away, you'll have to ask my honored brother first. You lot of beasts don't even have the qualifications to serve me," Lilith scoffed, her contemptuous gaze making people uneasy.

"You this bitch..." The Archbishop gritted his teeth in rage, "Then call Lucifer the Third out! We'll take him down and then capture you to have our fun!"

Lilith raised the crimson whip in her hand and swung it fiercely. Empowered by magic, it became incredibly sharp.

The moment it struck, countless blood mist exploded, severed limbs and debris flew everywhere, and long trenches appeared on the ground.

"Eek!!!"

The Archbishop fell to the ground, his face pale with fear, cold sweat pouring down.

"Have some self-awareness, you beasts! Do you think my honored brother is someone you can just summon whenever you please?! You don't even have the qualifications to make my brother draw his sword!" Lilith suddenly unfurled her black membrane wings and used her true Saint-tier Charm magic, "Masturbate to death right here for me!"

A pink mist spread from Lilith, instantly sweeping across the battlefield and charming a full hundred thousand Church knights.

These knightly lords, their eyes filled with seduction, took off their heavy armor and actually started engaging in... philosophical discussions with their comrades?!

Muscular bodies collided, groans of pain and pleasure intertwined, and the front of the Demon Lord Palace had become a large-scale philosophical scene.

"Hahaha, interesting! What is this?" Lilith retracted her membrane wings, pointing at the Crusade Army, "Doesn't the Church oppose homosexuality? Look at what you're doing! Shouldn't you be burned at the stake?"

Everyone was charmed and engaged in philosophy, except for Alice, who stood firm, unaffected, because she was a girl.

This was truly unbearable to watch...

Was being on the receiving end that pleasurable?

What was with those ecstatic cries?

Alice slowly drew her slender sword, "Luminous Lament," releasing her high-tier magic, silently casting her signature ice-element barrier magic.

A vast cold emanated from Alice, causing the surrounding temperature to plummet. The light rain that had been falling turned into snowflakes.

This was the best barrier magic Alice could use right now, "Realm of Zero," filling the surroundings with cold, the temperature dropping, causing the opponents to slow down due to the chill, and of course, it had another special use...

The cold gradually swept across the battlefield. The rainy weather suddenly turned into a heavy snowfall. The drop in temperature brought the knights, who had been engaged in philosophy, back to their senses.

"Hmm? Not bad..." Lilith looked at Alice, who was holding the slender sword.

The Archbishop pushed away the burly man who had been passionately kissing him and flew into a rage, "Hero, please subdue this great demon!"

"Can't you just use White Whale to blast her away?" Alice asked doubtfully.

"The White Whale has usage limits. We still need it to defeat Lucifer the Third, so please, Hero!" the Archbishop said with resentment.

There was nothing to be done. She had taken their money, so she had to handle their troubles...

Alice sighed silently and took step by step towards Lilith.

"Who are you?" Lilith looked down, narrowing her eyes.

"I am Alice Clodia, the 233rd Hero of the Holy Church. Now, against the great demon Lilith, I..." Alice lifted her helmet to make combat easier, revealing her stunningly beautiful face. Her silver hair instantly spread out, and she pointed her slender sword at Lilith—

"Execute!!!"

title: Chapter 5
content:
Chapter 5

Volume 1 · Chapter 5

"233!? What a malicious number. Heroes really are getting weaker with each generation—now even upper-tier maggots can become Heroes. The Holy Church has truly fallen..." Lilith shook her head, her tone dripping with disdain.

"Shut... shut up!" Alice's face flushed red as she angrily snapped.

She leapt forward, charging at Lilith. Her slender sword danced, weaving countless sword blooms that cascaded down like silver flakes.

Lilith countered with her long whip, its serpentine form writhing through the air.

Their intertwining whip shadows and sword flashes clashed in a fierce, tangled duel for several exchanges.

Alice, a high-tier mage, fought on par with Saint-tier Lilith—even holding a slight advantage.

Strange...

She was clearly a mage.

Why was her swordsmanship so extraordinary?

Every strike carried battle aura?

Was she a mage or a warrior?!

Lilith grew more alarmed with each exchange. Suddenly, she created distance, then lashed out with her whip in a backhanded strike, coiling it around the slender sword to try and wrench it away.

"How about this? Now you can't attack, can you?"

Alice remained expressionless and silent. Instantly, the slender sword grew scorching hot, burning through Lilith's whip. *The Radiant Dirge* was a holy sword—no dark creature could touch it.

What?!

This whip was made from dragon sinew—it could endure molten lava, yet it was being burned through?

What kind of sword was that?!

Lilith's momentary distraction gave Alice the opening she needed. She channeled all her magic into the holy sword, coating its surface with a layer of magical ice crystals—enough to pierce through even a magical barrier.

Alice had no intention of giving Saint-tier Lilith a chance to recover. She was going to end this with a single, decisive strike to the throat!

Alice focused her battle aura and struck with her final, finishing blow.

Lilith panicked, her face twisting in terror.

Damn it! I was careless. If I'd known, I would've blasted this trash with magic from the start!

Just as the crisis reached its peak—

A black shadow shot out from the Demon Lord Palace, crashing between Lilith and Alice like a meteor. The impact created a crack several feet wide, kicking up a thick cloud of dust.

"Who?!" the Archbishop cried out in shock.

As the dust settled, Merlin's figure appeared at the center, effortlessly pinching Alice's sword blade between two fingers, shielding Lilith.

How was this possible?!

My full-power strike...

Was actually blocked by just two fingers?!

Who was this man? He was so powerful!!!

Alice stood frozen in shock, her mind still reeling.

Merlin studied Alice, thinking to himself: So that's how it is. A half-baked magic and martial hybrid. Still, her combined use of magic and battle aura was impressive enough to hold her own against a Saint-tier opponent. No wonder my sister almost lost.

Merlin flicked his fingers, sending Alice flying backward. She barely managed to stop her momentum by plunging her sword into the ground, looking utterly disheveled.

Just a flick of his fingers forced me back... Who *is* he?

Merlin remained expressionless, calm and composed as he pulled Lilith behind him.

"Lilith, step back. Leave this to me."

"Brother! I can handle it! She's just a high-tier opponent. I was only careless earlier!" Lilith pouted, feeling untrusted.

"I wasn't talking about that half-baked fighter," Merlin said, lifting his gaze to the sky. "I was referring to that giant whale."

"That whale is that strong?" Lilith asked, unwilling to accept it.

"Mmm. Barely worthy of making me draw my sword."

title: Chapter 6
content:
Chapter 6

Volume 1 · Chapter 6

Merlin spoke lightly, then took the greatsword and stepped forward, facing the Holy Church’s vast Crusade Army of a hundred thousand alone.

The wind carried rain, tousling his golden hair, yet his expression remained inexplicably composed.

"The stage is set—it’s finally time for this leading man to make his entrance!"

So he was Lucifer the Third.

Yet he was the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace.

Why couldn’t she sense even a trace of magic or fighting spirit from him?

He didn’t even have the traits of the demon race—he looked exactly like a human.

Still, he was undeniably strong, far beyond what the Archbishop had claimed.

But even so, he was no match for the White Whale. She had seen its power with her own eyes.

Alice slowly stood, her mind swirling with doubts.

"Lucifer! You finally deign to show yourself! Do you remember me? I’ll repay you double for the humiliation of the last crusade!" the Archbishop exclaimed, overflowing with excitement.

"Emmmm..." Merlin pondered, scratching his ear. "Who are you again?"

The Archbishop’s face flushed crimson with rage, grinding his teeth as he hissed, "Lucifer! You’re still this arrogant!"

"Oh... now I remember..." Merlin chuckled, mocking him. "Aren’t you that blabbering charlatan from the last crusade? The one who pissed himself and ran the moment I drew my blade? You’re lucky you fled—otherwise, you wouldn’t be here to see this day."

"You—!" The Archbishop jabbed a finger at Merlin, his breath catching as he nearly choked on his own fury. "You bastard! Let’s see how arrogant you are now! I’ve come to wash away my past shame, armed with the Holy Church’s greatest wisdom—the ultimate weapon!"

"Oh." Merlin glanced at the White Whale and gave the Archbishop a thumbs-up. "Then you’re pretty awesome~!"

The Archbishop’s face went blank, feeling utterly humiliated. Merlin’s dismissive attitude stabbed deep into his pride.

His expression darkened so much it could drip water, and through gritted teeth, he spat out four words:

"F—k y—u!"

The Archbishop raised his staff and began chanting. The White Whale underwent a series of transformations before unleashing a concentrated blast of magic energy—a devastating cannon that sent shockwaves through the battlefield. Everyone present paled in fear.

Lilith’s face turned ashen. She hadn’t expected the Holy Church to possess such a terrifying weapon.

"To achieve such power, I suppose I can spare a little praise. You’ve clearly worked hard... but that’s all there is to it."

The magic cannon struck, its brilliance like searing sunlight. Merlin merely raised one hand, and the horrifying attack dissipated into nothing.

Lilith watched as the magic cannon broke apart into countless ripples before Merlin, blooming like fireworks—yet it hadn’t so much as grazed him.

"So amazing! As expected of Big Brother!"

She couldn’t help but exclaim in admiration. Though she hadn’t been harmed, the sheer force of the shockwave still pressed down on her. Truly, her Big Brother was the strongest!

The magic cannon vanished completely, leaving not even a speck of dust on Merlin. His overwhelming strength was undeniable.

Standing before the Demon Lord Palace with the demon sword in hand, his golden hair was slightly disheveled, and a disdainful smile played on his handsome face. The elegant silk robes he wore fluttered in the cold wind.

"This is your Holy Church’s ultimate weapon? It’s so pathetic it’s laughable. To be honest... it’s pitifully weak."

At these words, the Holy Church’s side fell into a brief silence—then,

Everyone’s faces twisted in shock.

Their jaws hit the floor...

title: Chapter 7
content:
Chapter 7

Volume 1 · Chapter 7

How could this be?!

That incredibly powerful magic cannon...

Was actually blocked with just one hand.

Lucifer the Third was truly too powerful.

How could such an existence possibly exist in this world?

This kind of strength... it was impossible to explain...

Alice watched with her heart pounding, her legs trembling unconsciously. Her mind was filled with the scene of Merlin effortlessly defending against the magic cannon.

She had never seen anyone stronger than her own master. For a moment, she couldn’t accept Merlin’s existence.

“H-How is this possible?!” The Archbishop’s face was filled with terror, his voice thick with disbelief. “The culmination of a century of the Holy Church’s wisdom—its power surpasses even Saint-tier ultimate techniques! It’s impossible for anyone to defend against it! How did you do it?!”

“Didn’t you survive the last Crusade?” Merlin said, tilting his head and pointing at himself with a smirk. “I’ve said it from the beginning... I’m immune to magic. No matter how powerful the spell, it has no effect on me. If you want to threaten me, send warriors of Saint-tier or higher.”

Magic immunity?!

Impossible!

How could someone be immune to magic?!

If it were true, the very foundations of magical theory would crumble!

Alice’s eyes widened. This couldn’t be real. Merlin had to be lying.

“This is impossible!” The Archbishop collapsed to the ground, his entire body trembling, his face twisted in shock as he pointed at Merlin. “Y-You... you you you... you monster! Too cunning! You’re just cheating!”

“Hmph!” Lilith scoffed, her voice dripping with disdain. “Pathetic livestock. My brother is the strongest in the world. You should consider it an honor to witness even a fraction of his power!”

“N-No... it’s impossible!” The Archbishop refused to accept reality, clawing at his own hair. “How could the Goddess allow someone like you to exist?!”

“If you can, why not have your Goddess come and deal with me herself? Sending pawns to their deaths over and over must be exhausting...” Merlin sighed, shaking his head with a bitter smile.

“Silence! How dare you insult our faith! This is unforgivable!” The Archbishop barely managed to stand, his bloodshot eyes glaring at Merlin. “Knights! Recite the scriptures together! Gather your magic!”

The Crusade Army’s knights lowered their swords and shields, beginning to chant the sacred verses in unison.

Ancient, arcane words and syllables poured from their mouths. Each released their magic, and the scattered starlight instantly merged into a dazzling silver river, surging into the sky—a breathtaking sight.

Alice stood nearby, watching in silence. It was the first time she had ever seen the combined magic of a full hundred thousand people. The overwhelming presence made her feel an urge to kneel in reverence.

The silver river of magic was absorbed by the white whale’s halo.

The surge of power had turned the golden halo a deep, violent crimson.

This artificial weapon had clearly been pushed to its maximum output.

It raised its head, split its massive jaws, and exhaled a scorching breath.

“ROOOOAR!!!”

The deafening roar, like an enraged beast, sent gusts of wind howling through the air.

Heavens!

It could still get stronger?!

The maximum output of this artificial weapon was terrifying beyond belief!

The wind howled with the roar, and Alice couldn’t keep her eyes open. The sheer pressure from the white whale made her heart race wildly.

“Brother!” Lilith called out worriedly from behind Merlin. This Crusade was different from the others—clearly, they had come prepared. The sheer scale of the magic was something she had never heard of before.

“It’s fine...” Merlin said lightly, still smiling. “This is more like it. If we’re going to fight, we should be serious. I’m starting to get a little fired up.”

“Lucifer, you bastard!” The Archbishop’s aged face twisted into a grotesque sneer as he pointed his staff at Merlin. “Feel the power of our faith! It will shatter your arrogance!”

The white whale, having gathered its power, opened its gaping maw and fired its maximum-output magic cannon at Merlin—

A violet beam of light erupted, so brilliant it dimmed even the sun. The overwhelming magic pressure made every living being tremble, unable to lift their heads.

The wind, clouds, and thunder raged, an awe-inspiring force.

The pillar of light violently tore through everything in its path, rushing straight toward Merlin.

It was over...

No one could withstand that attack.

Only a god could possibly survive.

Alice shook her head and sheathed her rapier.

Lilith chose to trust her brother, but she couldn’t help her growing unease, clutching her clothes until they wrinkled.

“For you, this is already impressive... but it’s far from enough to defeat me...”

Merlin gripped his demon sword, Banri Garan. The wind blew his golden hair back, revealing his smooth forehead.

“By the name of Lucifer, the First Demon Lord, I bestow upon you the ultimate glory!”

“Your faith... I shall trample underfoot.”

Merlin gave a slight bow, assuming the stance of a draw-cut.

Then, he closed his eyes...

◆◆◆

◆◆

◆

“Slash!!!”

The katana left its sheath, delivering a single strike!

The maximum-output magic cannon was instantly scattered. The knights were obliterated by this immense power, reduced to dust.

The wind roared violently, uprooting trees and flinging them into the unknown distance.

The force of that single slash spread like a devastating wave, and the earth itself seemed to submit.

Alice screamed as she was engulfed by the tidal wave of force.

“Why is he so powerful...?”

The Archbishop collapsed to his knees, his face blank, before turning into a pile of flesh.

The white whale in the sky had already vanished—at the moment Merlin drew his blade, it had been reduced to a rain of blood.

With just one slash, Merlin had annihilated the Holy Church’s grand army of a hundred thousand, turning them to dust.

Merlin looked at the spectacular, massive fissure before him, at the sky that had been forcibly split open, where the sunlight now shone through, painting the earth crimson.

“Sigh... You’re all still too weak...”

Merlin sighed, shaking the katana before sheathing it once more.

The Holy Church’s 233rd Crusade had once again ended in failure.

title: Chapter 8
content:
Chapter 8

Volume 1 · Chapter 8

The tightness in his chest gradually faded.

That suffocating feeling of being choked also vanished.

It seemed that white whale was quite powerful—it had managed to temporarily suppress his curse.

Merlin lifted his head, gazing at the sky that had been split open, revealing a vast expanse of azure.

Golden sunlight poured down in straight beams, illuminating the lifeless land below.

His golden hair was slightly disheveled from the battle.

His handsome face bore a hint of resolve as his sharp eyes fixed on the distance.

It seemed it was over...

The Demon Lord Palace no longer needed him.

And he should go see the world outside.

To break this damned curse, he would embark on the path of a warrior.

Perhaps he would end up endlessly swinging his demon sword, fighting until his very last breath?

Merlin gave a faint smile. This really didn’t suit him. He had only wanted to live a carefree life in this other world, yet here he was, working hard just to survive.

"Lilith, I’m leaving. Take care of yourself..."

Partings were always the most heart-wrenching. A trace of genuine emotion flickered across Merlin’s face.

"Brother!"

Lilith wailed in sorrow, tears falling like broken pearls, pattering down one after another.

After so many years together, the sudden separation was too much for her to bear.

Even though her brother was always lazy, he had stayed by her bedside whenever she was sick.

He might seem unreliable most of the time, but he was always dependable in critical moments.

He loved chocolate yet always saved some for her.

So many memories flashed through her mind like a kaleidoscope.

Overwhelmed by grief, Lilith threw herself into Merlin’s arms, sobbing with her frail shoulders heaving.

"Don’t go... don’t leave Lilith behind..."

"You really like throwing tantrums, don’t you..." Merlin held her close, gently stroking her hair. "If I don’t leave, I’ll die here sooner or later. Do you want to watch your brother die?"

"I don’t want you to die, and I don’t want you to leave me..." Lilith’s eyes were red, glistening with tears.

"You little brat, always so stubborn..." Merlin sighed inwardly. Though he was used to having this little shadow trailing after him, the thought of separation still stung. But to survive, he had to go out there.

"Brother, please don’t go..." Lilith buried her face in his chest, her voice trembling. "Why do you have to leave? Life here is so good. You have me to tease, and if you go outside, you’ll have to work to survive. A lazy bum like you with terminal sloth syndrome will definitely get fired. If you try to tease other girls, you’ll be arrested as a pervert. You’ll end up all alone in bed, reading dirty magazines. Brother, you’re useless! You won’t survive out there at all!"

Oh no...

Why did his chest ache so much?

Was his sister doing this on purpose? Her words were so harsh.

So in Lilith’s eyes, he was a useless brother?

Well, it made sense. A guy like him, without even a girlfriend, being looked down on by his own sister was only natural. He really was pathetic... hahaha...

Merlin pressed his lips together, speaking with awkward embarrassment, "Lilith, trust me. I’m the Demon Lord, after all. How could I be content staying cooped up at home? Before long, I’ll get a promotion, a raise, become a general manager, then CEO, marry a rich beauty, and reach the peak of life! Just thinking about it gets me a little excited!"

"Even if you get lucky and do well out there, I still won’t let you leave me! If I have to..." Lilith lifted her tear-streaked face, speaking earnestly, "Next time your curse acts up, just kill me to extend your life!"

Merlin chuckled softly, warmth spreading in his heart.

He ruffled Lilith’s hair affectionately. "Silly girl, how could I ever raise a hand against someone I know?"

"I don’t care! I don’t care!" Lilith clung tightly to his chest. "I just don’t want you to leave me. Even if you’re a useless shut-in, I’ll take care of you!"

Hey!!!

Stop calling me useless!

Even if I am useless, I still have dignity!

title: Chapter 9
content:
Chapter 9

Volume 1 · Chapter 9

"Lilith, I love you, but I have to leave. As long as I can lift the curse, I swear I won’t abandon you." Merlin gently pushed Lilith’s shoulder aside, his eyes filled with doting affection. "You’re not a child anymore. You can’t keep being so willful—you need to learn to be more mature."

Lilith sadly lowered her head, thinking her brother had finally changed his mind, only to realize he still intended to leave.

She knew she couldn’t stop Merlin. She lifted her small face, wearing a stubborn expression.

"Fine. If Brother isn’t here, I don’t want to stay in the Demon Lord Palace either. Once I resign as one of the Seven Generals, I’ll come find you."

Wait, she’s going to follow me?!

What if I’m struggling out there? Wouldn’t that be embarrassing?

Then I’d really be the useless shut-in she called me!

Merlin steadied Lilith’s shoulders and spoke seriously.

"Don’t follow me. It’s dangerous out there. I might not be able to protect you."

"I don’t care. I want to stay by your side." Lilith pouted, dissatisfied. "And there’s something very important I need to tell you, Brother."

"W-What is it?" Merlin raised an eyebrow, his emotions tangled.

"There are a lot of fox spirits out there. Brother, don’t you dare get tempted by them, or else—"

Lilith’s smile twisted, living up to her name as a Great Demon.

Though crimson light flickered in her eyes, they had lost their spark, becoming hollow as Saint-tier magic surged.

"I’ll kill as many as there are! Not a single one left!"

"I’ll rip out their hair strand by strand, flay their skin!"

"Then I’ll throw them into lava and roast them into jerky, and finally devour every last scrap so nothing remains!"

"Hehehehehehehe..."

Merlin was too stunned to speak, a cold sweat rolling down his forehead—

What the hell is this?

Is Lilith a psychopath?!

I hate clingy, yandere little sisters the most!

title: Chapter 10
content:
Chapter 10

Volume 1 · Chapter 10

Lilith gazed in the direction Merlin had left for a long time, her expression despondent and heartbroken.

In the end, her brother had still left her to venture out into the world.

That damned curse always threatened her brother’s life after a certain period.

Just how powerful of an enemy would he have to kill to lift the curse? Even her brother himself didn’t seem to know.

He was the strongest being in existence, yet he was shackled by such a bondage. Fate was truly unfair.

Lilith wiped away her tears, looking lost and hollow, as if she had lost her soul.

She decided that when she returned, she would submit her resignation to the council, leave the First Demon Lord Palace, and travel with her brother to find a way to break the curse.

Just as Lilith turned to leave, she sensed faint fluctuations of life.

She abruptly turned back, scanning the devastated battlefield with her gaze.

Who?!

Could someone still be alive?

To have survived her brother’s Iaijutsu slash… just what kind of luck was that? It was nothing short of a miracle…

Lilith muttered to herself, finally noticing something amiss beneath a pile of rubble—there was someone there!

A broken board on the rubble shifted, then was pushed open.

Alice stood up, her body filthy, her silver hair in disarray, no longer the radiant beauty she had been before. She looked disheveled and worn out.

The moment Merlin had drawn his sword, she had sensed something was wrong. Though she hadn’t felt any magic or fighting spirit, the oppressive force had been undeniably real—like the roar of a god, making one’s very soul tremble.

"Puh!" Alice’s head spun, and she coughed up a mouthful of fresh blood, spattering it onto the ground in front of her.

She thrust her rapier into the earth to support her trembling body. Her chest felt stifled, and every bone in her body seemed on the verge of breaking.

The aftershock of that single slash had left her gravely injured, nearly knocking her unconscious.

And this was still thanks to her mithril armor. If she had been at the center of that Iaijutsu slash, even a hundred layers of mithril armor wouldn’t have saved her.

What kind of power was that?!

The white whale’s magic had already been terrifying enough.

Yet it couldn’t withstand Lucifer III’s single slash?

And the vast Crusade Army of the Holy Church had been reduced to ashes in an instant!

Such power was beyond comprehension—it belonged to another dimension entirely.

It was… like a true deity…

Alice’s mind was foggy as she formed her assessment of Merlin:

He was too powerful. They existed in different dimensions. There was no way to compete on the same stage!

"Hm?" Lilith narrowed her eyes and turned to look at the severely injured Alice. "To still be clinging to life so tenaciously… for a livestock, that’s already quite impressive. I’ll give you a little praise—you’re one lucky bastard."

Alice barely managed to straighten herself, her face pale. She raised her rapier toward Lilith, her eyes flashing with determination. Her instincts told her that her chances were slim.

What should she do?

The power gap was too vast.

Before, she had relied on a surprise attack to catch her off guard.

But that strategy seemed useless now…

"Oh? You can still raise a sword?" Lilith’s eyes flickered with a hint of anger as she radiated Saint-tier pressure. "Know your place! A mere half-baked High-tier dare point a blade at me? Livestock like you should just obediently stretch out your neck and wait to die!"

The overwhelming Saint-tier pressure struck Alice like a physical blow, making her breath catch. Her expression turned to terror, her legs trembling uncontrollably, her heart momentarily stopping.

She couldn’t win.

Saint-tier was Saint-tier!

She had no chance in a direct confrontation!

The sheer magic suppression alone was something she couldn’t overcome.

And now, injured as she was, she couldn’t even resist…

Alice felt the colored fighting spirit and magic within her body in chaos, rendering her unable to use any techniques. It was likely the aftereffect of that single slash.

Lilith looked down at her, her crimson-glowing eyes filled with contempt. The horns on her head were sharp and menacing, her membrane wings slowly unfurling. She seemed like a great demon incarnate, her shadow spreading like a shroud.

Dark waves rippled around her body as she summoned a thick, ominous mist—likely a summoning spell.

I don’t want to die yet!

At the end of the day, I just wanted to make money.

There’s no need to throw my life away here!

If I die here, I might not even get a tombstone!

Why did I have to run into this?

I’ve only been out of the mountains for a few months!

Fear crept into Alice’s heart. After all, the demon race was ruthless, and without the element of surprise, she had no advantage at all.

And now she was facing a Saint-tier Great Demon, in her heavily injured state—she had no chance of winning.

Terrified, Alice hesitated for a moment before turning and fleeing in a panic, her cloak and silver hair billowing as she sprinted across the muddy swamp.

This undignified retreat was completely at odds with her identity as a Hero.

"Pets, go fetch that livestock back for me…"

Lilith wore a toying, sinister smile, both grotesque and terrifying, as if she had found a new toy.

She figured Alice was too heavily injured to get far. Sending her familiars would be enough to capture her alive.

The dark mist around Lilith quickly took the form of two ferocious, massive black demonic wolves.

Their black fur stood on end like a porcupine’s, their hungry eyes glowing with crimson light, their fangs sharp and deadly. They were High-tier creatures.

With a howl, the two demonic wolves obeyed Lilith’s command and dashed off at high speed to hunt down the fleeing Alice.

"Stupid maggot Hero, I’ll pull out your nails one by one."

"Listen to your beautiful screams as I cut off your head and hang it in front of the Demon Lord Palace!"

"How dare you disturb my life with my brother…"

"I won’t let you get away with this!!!"

title: Chapter 11
content:
Chapter 11

Volume 1 · Chapter 11

A deep, dark forest.

Heavy footsteps and ragged breathing echoed in the distance.

Alice ran at full speed, but gravely wounded, she seemed fast yet kept looking back warily at the hungry demon wolves.

Panic flashed across Alice’s face. Her chest felt suffocating, and the more desperately she struggled, the more searing pain shot through her body.

Behind her, the roars of beasts rang out. Two pairs of blood-red eyes flickered like specters of the black forest, hot on her trail, having devoured passing caravans before.

"Tsk! Are they catching up?"

Alice knitted her brows, her heart racing. That bloody stench was getting closer and closer.

Even though she had been running as hard as she could for a long time, she still couldn’t outpace the four-legged demon wolves.

Moreover, Alice felt her body growing heavier and heavier—she was clearly nearing exhaustion. Yet, driven by a powerful will to survive, she somehow endured.

Two demon wolves?

A Saint-tier could actually tame high-rank magical beasts as pets?

This was the first time she’d ever heard of such a thing. Even with a gap of just one tier in strength, achieving complete domination was rare. Was it because succubi were particularly skilled at temptation?

Alice felt immense pressure. It was common for Saint-tier to tame mid or low-rank creatures, but high-rank was extraordinary.

It seemed that the archdemon earlier had looked down on her, not using its full strength in their fight, instead toying with her in mockery and disdain.

Damn it! This is the first time someone has ever looked down on me...

A cold, damp wind brushed past her ears. Alice recalled her time in the snowy Alps, training under her master.

She remembered how, back then, her strength had just risen to high-rank. Filled with arrogance, she had thought herself ready to venture into the world and had demanded her master let her leave the mountain...

◆

One year ago.

"Leave the mountain? You're still too weak. While you might do well within human territories, against other races or in harsh, remote lands, you'd be crushed effortlessly. This world is far vaster than you imagine. There are many things you cannot defeat yet," her master said, profound and inscrutable.

"Master, I've trained under you for over a decade. I'm satisfied with my strength now. It's time for me to go out and make my mark," Alice declared with confidence.

"Why insist on going out? To marry a rich, handsome man? With your flat chest, you have no appeal. Forget it. Give up on that idea," her master shook his head repeatedly.

"That's not it!!! I can use my own hands to achieve my dreams, rely on my own efforts, and become the mother of a rich, handsome man!" Alice’s face burned red from her master’s sarcasm.

"emmmm..." Her master fell into deep thought, then nodded. "Seems like a grand and admirable ideal."

"R-right?! That's what I'm saying!" Alice felt her chances of leaving the mountain improving and pressed on. "I don’t want to spend my whole life on the Alps like you, still alone, like a widowed wife abandoned by her husband, poor and miserable, barely scraping by from one meal to the next."

Her master’s face darkened instantly. After a light cough, he said, "Fine. Since you have such a grand ideal, this master will lend you a hand."

Alice was overjoyed, expecting some powerful magic or martial art, but her expression quickly fell when her master pulled out a pair of black silk stockings.

"What are you doing, Master..."

"From now on, you’ll wear black silk stockings every day. Train your butt to be perkier, wear your skirt lower. When you swing your sword, thrust your hips hard—make sure your panties show. Do everything you can to take out the female lead," her master said with a wicked grin, his voice dark. "As long as you take out the female lead, you’ll be the heroine!"

title: Chapter 12
content:
Chapter 12

Volume 1 · Chapter 12

"Why do I have to wear this kind of thing?"

A fine, dense black line slid down Alice's forehead as she felt her teacher's words were utterly nonsensical.

"Black stockings represent temptation. They can make your charm skyrocket. Those cheap men all love black stockings. Don’t underestimate a pair of stockings—once you put them on, they’ll drive men wild, making them unable to resist touching or licking, all falling at your feet..." The teacher narrowed her eyes, speaking with absolute seriousness. "These black stockings are your secret weapon on the road to success. You must remember that."

"Okay... fine, I can barely accept that..." Alice darkened her face and nodded, looking extremely reluctant. "But why do I have to expose my panties? Isn’t showing panties really shameful?"

"That’s where you’re wrong." The teacher shook her head, earnestly explaining, "Exposing panties is a girl’s ultimate skill, an essential ability for every heroine. Its lethality is no less than a Saint-tier mental attack! A heroine who doesn’t know how to flash her panties is trash, completely worthless! This world doesn’t need some iron-clad virgins—it needs girls who wear as little as possible!"

"F-Flashing panties is that powerful?" Alice expressed deep doubt.

"Extremely powerful. It can deal 1,000,000% mental damage to male creatures. And with the hazy effect of black stockings, making the panties faintly visible, full of mystery—it’s the ultimate weapon against those cheap men! The barely visible panties hidden beneath the black stockings are the best!" The teacher lightly coughed, regretfully saying, "Back in my day, when I was competing with my rival for a man, I didn’t understand these things and suffered a huge loss. In the end, I ended up as a loser. That bitch was amazing at flashing her panties in all sorts of ways..."

"This... isn’t this just selling lewdness?!" Alice frowned, pouting. "I don’t want to do that..."

"Silly girl, look down at your flat chest. If you don’t add some moe points, you’re probably doomed for life. With no assets like you, how are you going to compete with those bitches for men?!"

Alice darkened her face and fell silent, feeling that her teacher’s lewd advice made a disturbing amount of sense, leaving her speechless.

◆

Why did I think of these things?

Ever since I came down from the mountain, I’ve been hitting walls everywhere.

Could it be because I wasn’t wearing black stockings and flashing my panties?

I would never agree with that! But there’s one thing the teacher said that was right.

My training is still far from enough...

Alice moved through the Black Forest, leaping over withered logs as thick as barrels. The two demon wolves behind her followed like shadows, their eyes flickering with bloodthirsty crimson light.

This world is vast, and there are many things I cannot overcome.

The first time I went to the Death Swamp, I encountered an existence that transcended dimensions.

That golden-haired man, in the wind and rain, had the audacity to spout madness in front of a hundred thousand Holy Church knights.

With just a single, ordinary draw-slash, he annihilated the enemy.

Maybe I’ll never reach that level of strength.

But even so, I...

Alice did not continue running. Instead, she hid beneath the massive withered log, tightening her grip on the holy sword, *Luminous Dirge*.

She knew she couldn’t escape. So she had to choose a desperate gamble to survive.

If she was fated to be caught, then she might as well fight!

The two high-rank demon wolves howled, leaping over the log, not expecting Alice to be hiding beneath it. Instead of fleeing, she had stopped, and now, in their mid-air state, they had become living targets.

Alice seized the opportunity, her holy sword striking out in rapid succession. Instantly, a burst of silver light erupted like a sudden blizzard, her sword technique exploding forth.

Black wolf blood splattered across her beautiful yet resolute face.

But even so—

I will live well in this world!

title: Chapter 13
content:
Chapter 13

Volume 1 · Chapter 13

The rapier's fierce, continuous thrusts sent silver light flashing coldly!

Though Alice was gravely wounded and unable to use battle aura or magic, her solid fundamentals made even ordinary sword techniques formidable. Coupled with the holy sword's double damage against dark creatures, the effects were striking.

The dense flurry of sword strikes pierced both demon wolves' eyes, sending jets of inky blood splattering across Alice's face.

The two demon wolves crashed to the ground, writhing madly as guttural howls of agony tore from their throats.

It seemed the sacred aura of *Hymn of Light* was sheer poison to the demon wolves, driving them to unbearable torment.

Alice's face was deathly pale, her breathing ragged. Just moments ago, her heart had nearly stopped, the tension unbearable.

But seeing the two demon wolves in such agony, she finally exhaled in relief, a hint of innocent joy flickering across her face.

Without lingering, Alice turned and fled toward the forest's edge, her mithril armor clinking with each step.

Demon wolves were nearly impossible to kill when she couldn't use her abilities, and their self-healing was terrifyingly potent. Simply wounding them was already a stroke of luck.

Her goal was achieved. Alice quickened her pace—if she could just delay the wolves, she could escape the forest.

Beyond it, she could see the ocean, and the Holy Church's Crusade fleet. Salvation was within reach.

The sunlight at the exit filled her with hope.

She sprinted forward, a weight lifted from her shoulders, a relieved smile on her face.

But just as she stepped out of the forest, she failed to watch her feet. A vine snagged her ankle, and she went sprawling face-first into the dirt!

Oww, ow, ow...

What am I even doing?

I survive, then let my guard down? Pathetic...

Gritting through the pain, Alice tried to stand, lifting her head to look at the Crusade fleet on the sea.

But the sight before her made her brows shoot up. Her expression froze, words dying in her throat.

The sea was raging with a violent storm. Nearly a thousand transport warships of the Crusade—some aground, some dashed against the rocks and sinking, others capsized by the waves!

Masts tangled together, hulls shattered, the scene a complete disaster.

How... how is this possible?!

Without ships, how am I supposed to get back?!

Am I supposed to swim all the way to Bristol Harbor?!

Absolutely impossible. I'm only human...

Despair crept in. Then, a strange commotion came from behind—low, guttural growls, the sound of rapid footsteps, roars growing louder, closing in fast.

The dark forest was pitch black, but suddenly, two pairs of crimson eyes flared in the depths. Something was charging out!

"No way..."

Alice's face drained of color, her eyes wide with terror.

A gust of blood-tinged wind, and black shadows burst from the forest.

The two demon wolves had already healed! Their eyes burned with malice, their massive jaws gaping, the familiar demonic sigils on their tongues glinting as their fangs lunged for Alice's throat...

Damn it!

These weren't tamed beasts!

They were contracted familiars!

Even when injured, they could draw power from their master to heal.

No wonder their eyes recovered so quickly!

Alice was still sprawled on the ground, not yet on her feet. She kicked at the earth, scrambling backward.

Staring up at the towering, bloodied maws, her mind went blank. In her panic, she had even forgotten to grab her rapier.

This is it...

Is it already too late?!

◆

Forest edge, coastline, a few minutes earlier.

Merlin stood on the rocks, great sword in hand.

The wind of his pose swirled around him, a perfect protagonist effect.

His storm-tossed sleeves and disheveled golden hair gave him the melancholy air of a wandering minstrel.

Merlin watched the howling storm and the grand spectacle of a thousand warships sinking or wrecked, a single crystal tear welling in the corner of his eye as he thought—

**Damn it!**

I finally made up my mind to leave the Demon Lord Palace.

And now I run into this kind of bad luck?!

The ships are all gone. How am I supposed to go out there and show off?

If I can't go out and show off, what's the difference between me and a stinking salted fish?!

Merlin had been at the shoreline for half an hour now. He had planned to hijack a ship to take him away, but as soon as he arrived, the storm had already capsized them all.

In the blood-red sea, man-eating sharks swarmed like sardines, rolling through the water, devouring every last sailor.

Merlin looked on, on the verge of tears. He knew no magic, couldn't swim, and while he could pull off a few flashy moves with his sword, *Iaijutsu* wasn't going to help him cross a strait.

He sighed inwardly. Who could understand the sorrow of a landlubber? *Gak gak~*

Merlin had once found a world map on a knight. After studying it, he learned this world had many nations and unexplored lands.

His current location was what humans called the Orkney Islands. The nearest continental nation was the Great British Empire. To reach the mainland, he'd have to cross the Orkney Strait.

On the map, the strait was barely a centimeter wide—but who knew how many days it would take by ship?!

Merlin fretted. He had resolved to leave the Demon Lord Palace, only to be stymied by transportation. Going back now would be humiliating if his sister saw him...

Just as he was at his wit's end, a small boat was swept ashore by the storm.

Merlin looked at the battered little vessel, an idea striking him. Maybe he could row himself away.

He picked up the oars, sighed, and his laziness flared up. Rowing wasn't his style. What he needed was a slave to do the rowing for him, then cross the strait.

"Roar!"

A wolf's howl snapped Merlin's attention.

He turned to see Alice at the forest's edge, sitting on the ground in a panic, her face twisted in fear.

Two demon wolves, jaws agape, were lunging at her, clearly intent on killing her.

Merlin furrowed his brow, stroking his chin as he fell into deep thought—

Hmmmm...

( -`ω- )?

title: Chapter 14
content:
Chapter 14

Volume 1 · Chapter 14

Two massive demon wolves opened their bloodstained maws and lunged to tear her apart.

A gust of bloodthirsty wind struck Alice’s face, making her heart clench and her expression freeze.

In her panic, she couldn’t even raise her sword to counterattack. She had no idea when her injuries would heal, and she couldn’t muster a single thread of magic or fighting spirit.

Was it too late?

Was she really going to die here…?

Alice gritted her silver teeth, her face deathly pale, and her will to live began to fade.

"Step aside."

A man’s voice suddenly rang out behind her.

The two demon wolves halted at once. Seeing Merlin behind Alice, their crimson eyes filled with fear, their bristling fur trembling. They lowered their heads in submission, sniffing around Alice’s feet. The once-savage beasts now acted like docile dogs, not daring to lift their gaze toward Merlin. Their throats emitted pitiful whimpers as they hesitated over whether to leave.

Alice was bewildered, completely at a loss for what was happening.

Why were these two ferocious demon wolves acting so strangely?

Who was the man behind her?

Why could he intimidate someone else’s familiars?

Curious, Alice turned to look—and her eyes fell upon the First Demon Lord Palace’s Great Demon Lord, the very one who had personally annihilated the Holy Church’s Crusade Army.

Huh?

Lucifer the Third?

Why was he here?!

Had he come specifically to hunt her down because he wasn’t willing to let her go?

This was the end. She might have had a chance against the demon wolves, but against Lucifer the Third, there was only death.

Alice’s eyes glazed over, her face turning even paler. Her body trembled uncontrollably, her teeth chattering, terror peaking to the point where she nearly passed out.

Recalling the overwhelming power Lucifer the Third had displayed, and how he had single-handedly slaughtered the vast Crusade Army, the 233rd Hero simply gave up on survival. She resigned herself to her fate, accepting death with grim composure.

Merlin recognized the two demon wolves—they were clearly Lilith’s familiars.

Though the Demon Lord Palace had other Archdevil Generals, none of them kept familiars. Only Lilith had a habit of raising such creatures.

The two demon wolves hung their heads, circling Alice with pitiful whimpers, looking utterly miserable.

They didn’t dare show aggression in front of Merlin, yet they refused to leave.

Merlin found their behavior odd, but a moment’s thought made it clear.

"You may return. Tell Lilith this woman is mine now."

Alice’s body jolted, her expression one of shock, her lips parting but no words coming out.

Merlin’s statement was so bizarre it invited wild interpretations, and Alice’s mind immediately jumped to the worst.

What did that mean?

What did he mean by “she belongs to me”?

He must have taken one look at her and gotten wicked ideas.

He wanted to… have his way with her, get her pregnant, didn’t he?

If only she’d kept her mask on this whole time!

Damn it! A warrior may die, but never suffer humiliation! She’d rather die than let anyone defile her!

Alice’s pale face flushed with rage. As a Hero, she felt utterly disgraced.

Her pride was shattered. She was determined not to let Merlin succeed. She wasn’t some inflatable doll for him to use whenever he pleased!

Alice secretly gripped her rapier, planning to seize an opportunity to launch a surprise attack.

If it worked, great. If not, she’d kill herself. Either way, she wouldn’t let Merlin sully her.

Of course, if Merlin happened to have a necrophilia kink, Alice would be doomed either way—she’d have no escape even in death.

The two demon wolves exchanged a glance, then turned and fled, vanishing into the depths of the forest.

"Alice Clodia? I heard your name back in the palace. You’re quite lucky, you know. You’re the first to survive under my blade." Merlin pointed at himself and smiled. "I’m Merlin Lucifer."

"That’s not…"

"I’m no longer a Demon Lord. Just call me Merlin."

"From this moment on, your body belongs to me."

"This isn’t a requisition, a negotiation, or some partner game."

"It’s a blunt, naked kidnapping. That’s right…"

"Beautiful lady, you’ve been abducted by me."

(??ω?? ?)

title: Chapter 15
content:
Chapter 15

Volume 1 · Chapter 15

Merlin did his best to make his smile look kind.

After all, they would soon be leaving the Death Swamp together on a small boat—more or less as companions.

But since Merlin had just made a highly suggestive remark, that smile only came across as lecherous and despicable in Alice’s eyes.

Alice’s delicate brows furrowed slightly. *What does he mean by that?* It seemed almost… enthusiastic? Was he trying to lower her guard so she’d be more compliant later, so she wouldn’t resist? In his dreams!

“Surprised? Shocked?” Merlin felt he truly had the potential to be a creep, grinning wickedly as he said, “In a bit, I’m going to do some very outrageous things with your body—utterly inhuman, hehehe~”

What he actually meant was using a girl as free labor to row the boat across the Orkney Strait.

For a girl, that *was* inhuman, but since Alice was the Hero—and had been his sword-wielding enemy until recently—Merlin didn’t feel the least bit guilty.

When dealing with an enemy, there was no need to be merciful. Not throwing her into the sea to feed the sharks was already generous treatment for a captive.

Outrageous? Inhuman?

So he *does* want to… have his way with me, get me pregnant, does he?

Bastard! I’ll never let this pervert succeed!

Maybe I’ll get a chance… to cut his head off with one swing of my sword…

Alice made up her mind, secretly gripping the hilt of her rapier, planning to strike Merlin down the moment she got the chance.

“Come on, miss, follow me. Don’t force me to get rough—it’s not pretty when things turn ugly…” Merlin spoke as he reached out toward Alice, intending to pull her onto the boat.

His flirtatious words filled Alice with humiliation.

As Merlin’s wicked hand drew closer, Alice’s face twisted in terror, and she could no longer suppress her murderous intent.

“Don’t touch me!”

In a flash, Alice drew her rapier and lunged at Merlin’s throat with blinding speed.

Like a gust of wind, she struck in an instant, fully determined to kill him!

“Oh~”

Merlin just grinned, flicking his finger to deflect Alice’s rapier with ease.

Then, in one swift motion, he seized her wrist, twisted it, and subdued the wildcat before him.

“Ow!” Pain shot through Alice’s wrist, cold sweat beading on her forehead as the rapier clattered to the ground. *As expected… the power gap is just too huge. I’m no threat to him at all.*

“Miss, you’ve got quite the temper,” Merlin said with an amused smile. “If I were a ruthless kidnapper, you’d already be dead.”

“Let go of me! You pervert! I’ll never submit!” Alice’s face twisted in disgust, her clenched teeth radiating defiance.

*Damn it!*

And here I thought I’d at least made it out of the Death Swamp before getting called a pervert.

Lilith actually predicted this… Looks like it’s not a good omen.

Merlin cleared his throat lightly to mask his embarrassment.

“I like ‘em feisty. Stubborn bones are my type.”

“Huh?!” A cold sweat rolled down Alice’s forehead. *Should I act weaker?* No! That’s a trap! If I show weakness, this bastard will take advantage and push me down!

“You’re my slave now. I won’t be letting you go so easily.” Merlin sighed, though in truth, he didn’t *want* to kidnap a woman. But his backside still ached, and he needed some strong labor.

“You sick, depraved sex maniac! Give me back my sword! I’d rather die in battle than let you have your way!” Alice gritted her teeth through the pain in her wrist, her voice trembling with rage.

*This idiot girl… what’s going on in that head of hers?*

If I *actually* wanted to do that to her, would I still be standing here talking?

And *she* has the nerve to call *me* a depraved sex maniac? Her mind’s the filthy one!

(ー`′ー)

title: Chapter 16 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 16 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 1 · Chapter 16

Merlin furrowed his brows, feeling a little annoyed.

"Hey, don’t call me a perverted demon. I have my dignity."

"Hmph, perverted demon, your mind is full of filth, you scum..." Alice provoked Merlin further.

"Are you forcing me to use violence?" Merlin's face darkened. He couldn’t be bothered to draw his sword against a mere high-rank opponent.

But if she shamelessly kept jumping around, Merlin would send her straight to hell without hesitation.

"Ah!" Alice’s face paled as she recalled the decisive, merciless slash at the Demon Lord Palace. Terror gripped her, and she fell silent, too scared to speak.

"Hmph!" Merlin let out a cold snort, kicking the pure white slender sword on the ground with his foot before picking it up and examining it. "The sword is good, but the person isn’t. Too weak."

Alice’s face flushed red with anger. Not only did he want to... but he also had to insult her strength? How despicable...

Merlin scoffed, tossing the sword into Alice’s sheath and returning it to her.

"Eh?"

Alice looked shocked. Why was he giving the sword back? Wasn’t he afraid she’d take the chance to kill him? This was the perfect opportunity!

She swallowed hard, and with a *shing*, drew the sword halfway.

"Don’t waste your effort. Even a hundred of you wouldn’t be my match. If I’m brave enough to return your weapon, do you think I’d fear a sneak attack?" Merlin thought this Hero was really unruly. Usually, Heroes didn’t like sneaking around, but Alice had tried it several times already.

Was she just some mercenary the Holy Church picked up randomly? She clearly lacked strict discipline and knightly spirit.

It seemed the Holy Church was running out of talent if they’d let anyone become a Hero.

Alice saw that Merlin didn’t look like he was joking. Remembering the power he had displayed earlier, fear wavered in her heart.

Yeah...

This was a man who had blocked her full-force strike with just two fingers.

How could he possibly fear a sudden attack from her?

After much hesitation, Alice silently sheathed her sword again. Maybe she could try negotiating. Lucifer the Third seemed different from past Demon Lords—maybe he was reasonable.

"What do you even want?"

"We’ve already lost..."

"Does the mighty Demon Lord not even let deserters go?"

"What do I want? You’ll find out when we get there, hehehe~" Merlin rubbed his chin, looking like a thug in a tavern harassing a decent woman.

"Disgusting..." Alice’s heart pounded in panic. The more she looked at Merlin, the more she found him lecherous. It had to be something extremely perverted.

Merlin didn’t waste words. In a flash, he appeared behind Alice and, in a princess carry, lifted her into his arms.

Alice’s expression went blank. Before she could process what was happening, her feet left the ground.

Having grown up in the snowy mountains, she had rarely interacted with men, let alone been held by one.

Merlin’s masculine scent rushed to her head, making her dizzy. Her nose burned, her heart raced, and her pulse pounded wildly—

What’s wrong with me?

Why is my heart beating so fast?

Is this... the feeling of love?

No, no, no! How could that be? This bastard is a scumbag!

And I’m a Hero, he’s a Demon Lord—how can enemies fall in love?!

"Listen, you’re really heavy. If you don’t lose some weight, you might not get married..." Merlin wore a slightly pained expression, worried Alice would struggle and waste time. He decided to just carry her to the small boat.

"I-I-I’m not heavy! It’s the mithril armor! It has nothing to do with my weight!" Alice’s cheeks burned crimson as she flustered, desperate to explain, afraid of being misunderstood.

Wait... wait a second?

Why am I flustered?

I should be struggling and screaming! I’m about to be...!

"Let’s go. It’s just a few steps away, really close..." Merlin didn’t bother explaining further. Carrying Alice, he quickly moved across the beach.

"Let me go! I’m not going! Put me down! You perverted demon! I won’t let you—!"

After spacing out for half a day, Alice finally remembered to resist, pounding Merlin’s chest with her small fists, not behaving at all.

Merlin’s emotions were complicated, his head filled with black lines—

He really wanted to throw this stupid girl into the sea to feed the sharks...
