title: Chapter 17 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 17 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 1 · Chapter 17

By the small boat.

Merlin carried Alice and, with absolutely no grace, tossed her onto the deck.

Alice felt a sharp pain in her backside and couldn’t help but furrow her delicate brows, silently cursing Merlin for his lack of gentlemanly conduct.

"Beautiful miss, let’s get down to business, hehehe~"

Merlin stroked his chin, a flicker of malice flashing in his eyes. He looked particularly wicked.

If you asked what a flower-picking bandit looked like, the answer would definitely be someone who looked just like Merlin.

Alice’s expression turned panicked, her face pale. She kept backing away until she reached the stern, with nowhere left to retreat, and began to tremble.

What should I do?

Does he… want to do *that* to me here?

I never thought my first time would be in a place like this…

Alice’s cheeks flushed crimson. She crossed her arms over her chest, her heart pounding in her throat.

"Stay away from me! I’ll never surrender!"

Merlin looked at Alice’s stubborn expression as she bit her lip and burst out laughing. "That’s not up to you. You’ll do whatever I say, or else don’t blame me for getting rough and throwing you into the sea to feed the sharks~"

Alice’s breath hitched, and she grew even more terrified.

She turned to look at the crimson sea, where schools of man-eating sharks were tearing apart the corpses of sailors.

In her injured state, being thrown into the water would mean certain death.

Alice’s face darkened even further. Compared to being eaten alive by sharks, she’d rather take her own sword and end herself.

"Y-You… what do you *really* want?!"

"Do you really not know what I want? Enough with the nonsense. I’m already impatient, hehehe~" Merlin rubbed his hands together, his anticipation for leaving the Death Swamp overwhelming.

To Merlin, who had never traveled far before, the outside world was full of allure.

Alice was already terrified, her nerves on the verge of collapse. She thought this was about to turn into some kind of Demon Lord-Hero adult film, with her as the leading lady.

Her pride couldn’t bear such a thing. She saw it as a humiliation and defilement of her soul.

Alice drew her rapier, but instead of attacking Merlin, she pressed it against her own neck. Tears glistened in her eyes as she threatened, "If you dare touch me, I’ll kill myself right in front of you!"

"Don’t think just because you’re strong, you can do whatever you want to me!"

"I’d rather die than let a pervert like you have your way!"

Wait, wait, wait!

When did this turn into *that*?!

Do I really look like a flower-picking bandit?!

What the hell is this girl thinking about all the time?!

How did such a stupid idiot become the Hero?!

All her Hero predecessors would be hanging their heads in shame!

Merlin’s face darkened. He didn’t even want to explain, because someone with a mind full of *that* would see everything as *that*.

With a sudden kick, he sent an oar flying, smacking Alice right on the forehead and knocking the rapier from her hand.

Merlin wasn’t about to let his hard-won source of labor die here. He still needed Alice to row with all her might to get them out of this cursed place. Once they reached the shores of Great Britain, her life or death was none of his concern.

"Oww, oww, oww…" Alice clutched her reddened forehead, her eyes turning red with anger. "*Pervert!* What’s with the brutality?! A guy like you will never get a girlfriend!"

Merlin felt a sharp sting in his heart, as if Alice had pricked his pride.

Yeah…

Now that he thought about it, he really *hadn’t* had a girlfriend since coming to this other world.

Even though he had the looks of a pretty boy, why were there no women around him except his sister?

Merlin recalled his sister’s sickly sweet parting words and suddenly had a revelation.

I don’t have a girlfriend… and it’s all Lilith’s fault!

Merlin found the whole thing embarrassingly humiliating, so he cleared his throat to cover his awkwardness and said, "What the hell do you know?"

"I’m going to train until I’m thirty…"

"and become a Great Mage!"

(╬￣皿￣)

title: Chapter 18
content:
Chapter 18

Volume 1 · Chapter 18

"Don’t flatter yourself! Who would even want you? Take a good look at your pathetic washboard chest—it couldn’t stir anyone’s interest even if it tried!" Merlin loomed over Alice, ruthlessly crushing her self-esteem.

"Y-You… you you… what did you just say?!" Alice’s face flushed crimson in an instant, humiliation and fury burning through her. Nothing infuriated her more than being mocked for her flat chest.

"I’ve seen plenty of women, but I’d never sink so low as to go for a washboard!" Merlin pointed at Alice, flashing a devilish grin. "You actually thought I’d be into you? What a joke! That board-flat chest of yours could double as a washboard for laundry or a brick in a fight. A weapon like that? Not only is it a total turn-off, it’d probably bruise me to death!"

"W-Who… who says I’m flat?! I’m well-endowed! You just can’t tell because I’m wearing mithril armor!" Alice, desperate to save face, scrambled for excuses, refusing to admit she was as flat as a board.

"And now you’re using mithril armor as an excuse? Aren’t you ashamed? That just makes it worse!" Merlin was exasperated. He’d never met someone so stubbornly delusional—any fool could see she was flat, yet she insisted she was buxom. "Stop embarrassing the dead Heroes of the past, you face-obsessed washboard Hero!"

"I’m not lying! And don’t act like you’ve seen it all!" Alice gritted her teeth, seething. The mockery stung worse than any physical blow.

Her rage surged. A warrior may die, but never endure such humiliation—how dare he say her chest was small!

"Uh… isn’t that armor you’re wearing… for men?" Merlin glanced at Alice’s chest, as if assessing something valuable.

"So what if it is?! What’s it to you?!" Alice glared at Merlin, finding him more insufferable by the second.

"Fits pretty well…" Merlin barely contained his laughter before adding, "I mean, your chest fits it perfectly—just like a man’s."

"W-What…?" Alice didn’t catch on at first.

"Idiot. I’m saying your washboard is as flat as a man’s! If you were really well-endowed, that armor would’ve burst at the seams by now, wouldn’t it? HAHAHA…" Merlin roared with laughter, his tactless words turning Alice’s face a dark, furious green. "With that chest that could kill a man on impact, you think I’d be into you? Pfft! Dream on, shameless flat-chested freak!"

Alice’s shame and fury peaked, her face burning like a ripe apple. She had to change the subject.

"If you’re not into me, then why did you capture me?!"

"Isn’t it obvious?" Merlin spread his hands, declaring with grand confidence, "We’re going to cross the Orkney Strait! We’re setting foot on the land of Great Britain!"

"Impossible." Alice didn’t hesitate to shoot him down.

The Crusade Army had departed from the port of Bristol with hundreds of soldiers, their ships propelled by wind magic the entire way. Even then, it took a full day and night to reach the Death Swamp.

And that wasn’t the only reason—they hadn’t encountered a single sea monster or man-eating shark along the way.

Because the Holy Church’s warships were coated in dragon dung, which repelled many dangers.

So Alice was certain: two people alone couldn’t cross the Orkney Strait.

Even if they rowed with all their might and reached the nearest part of Great Britain, they’d never survive the sea monsters lurking in the waters. Those creatures were nearly invincible at sea—even Saint-tier warriors struggled against them.

"Why impossible?" Merlin frowned, genuinely confused as to why crossing the strait would be a problem.

Alice hesitated. Their goals aligned—they both wanted to escape the Death Swamp. Maybe they could cooperate.

And Merlin didn’t seem to have any ill intentions toward her. Maybe he just wanted a companion for the crossing.

After some thought, Alice decided that if it meant leaving this godforsaken place, even teaming up with a Demon Lord wasn’t out of the question. She answered Merlin.

"The Orkney Strait is wide, and our stamina is limited. Even if we take turns rowing, we might exhaust ourselves halfway."

"Miss Washboard, I think you’re misunderstanding something…" Merlin sighed, then said seriously—

"Only *you* will be doing the rowing."

"And I’ll just be standing here, looking cool in the sea breeze…"

title: Chapter 19 — Reward Update
content:
Chapter 19 — Reward Update

Volume 1 · Chapter 19

"Aah?!"

Alice's eyes widened in sheer disbelief.

How was she supposed to cross the strait by herself? She wasn't some kind of superhero—she'd collapse from exhaustion.

Alice shook her head repeatedly, refusing no matter what.

"It's impossible!"

"Comrade, you must believe in the great proletariat's iron will." Merlin kept a straight face, speaking with absolute sincerity.

"I'll be exhausted halfway there!" Alice felt this was unfair. Why should she do all the work?

"Then I'll toss you into the sea to feed the fish and row to Great Britain myself." Merlin grinned, not mincing his words.

"That's outrageous! You have no gentlemanly manners at all!" Alice had never met a scoundrel like Merlin before.

"Gentlemanly manners won't fill your stomach, so just obey." Merlin was dead set on treating Alice like a slave.

"This isn't fair! We're supposed to be partners—how can I be the only one working?" Alice furrowed her delicate brows, shouting in protest.

"Flat-chested miss, you really take that for granted, huh?" Merlin smirked, pointing at Alice. "Who said we were partners? Get your facts straight—we have a master-and-slave relationship, so you listen to me."

"I quit!" Alice threw the oar to the ground, convinced this was an unequal treaty—only a fool would agree.

"Oh? If you won't behave..." Merlin's expression darkened, his gaze turning icy. His right hand gripped the handle of his katana as he threatened, "I'll kill you right now and dump your corpse into the sea to feed the sharks."

Alice's face paled, her heartbeat stopping for a second. Remembering how Merlin had cut down the Crusade Army without hesitation, she realized he wouldn't hesitate to do the same to her.

She turned to look at the crimson sea, where the swarming man-eating sharks circled restlessly, probably waiting for fresh human meat.

After much deliberation, Alice decided that as long as she survived, she could find another way. Maybe with sheer willpower, she could make it to Great Britain alive.

"I... I'll reluctantly agree, but it's not because I'm scared of your threats! It's because I want to leave this cursed place too, that's all!"

Merlin saw Alice trembling and knew she was lying. It seemed his intimidation still worked.

"Enough talking, let's set sail!"

"Wait, are you confident we won't be attacked at sea?" Alice's eyes were full of concern as she doubted, "I've heard the Orkney Strait is haunted by sea serpents. We only escaped them last time because we used dragon dung. If we don't prepare something to repel sea monsters, we'll be attacked. Even these man-eating sharks could smash the boat to pieces."

"Dragon dung? You people aren't bothered by the stench?" Merlin frowned, unable to comprehend.

"Add some spices to the mix, and it's not that bad..." Alice answered awkwardly.

"We do have dragon dung. In the Demon Lord Palace's underground prison, we've got your Holy Church's Sacred Dragon locked up. I cut off its wings and use it as a guard dog." Merlin said casually, recalling how the Sacred Dragon had initially been full of arrogance, but eventually lay on the ground in submission.

If he hadn't shown mercy, the Demon Lord Palace would now have a pure white dragon rug.

"Sacred Dragon Aivis?" Alice's expression was one of disbelief, her voice trembling.

"Think that was its name. Though now it's called Wangcai." Merlin said with wicked amusement.

Sacred Dragon Aivis.

The Saint-tier dragon revered by the Holy Church.

A divine emblem soaring above the Roman temples.

Rumor had it that a single sacred breath had annihilated an invading Viking legion.

How could such a mighty dragon be reduced to a guard dog?

She knew Lucifer III was powerful, but this was absurd!

To think he could force a noble dragon into submission through sheer strength...

Please, don't just drop such shocking revelations—my brain can't handle it!

A fine layer of cold sweat formed on Alice's forehead as she was struck with horror, momentarily forgetting the task at hand.

"Come on, we're running out of time." Merlin urged Alice to row.

"B-but... we need something to repel the sea serpents..." Alice still hesitated. At sea, sea serpents were apex predators.

"We don't need that. Having me is enough." Merlin shrugged.

"Where does this baseless confidence come from?" Alice's mind was filled with question marks.

"Because in this world..." Merlin faced the sea breeze, standing at the bow of the ship as he pointed to himself and declared—

"No enemy has ever survived a second strike from me!"

title: Chapter 20 — Reward Update
content:
Chapter 20 — Reward Update

Volume 1 · Chapter 20

The small boat slowly pulled away from the shore, leaving behind layer upon layer of ripples.

Alice wore a dark expression, her face twisted in bitterness as she rowed the oars with labored strokes.

Merlin stood at the bow, facing the gale-force sea winds as he gazed into the distance.

His golden hair fluttered, brushing against his smooth forehead. The demon sword Banri Garan at his waist looked ancient, giving off the vibe of a rusted piece of junk—utterly outclassed by Alice’s *Radiant Aria*, to the point of being laughably inferior.

No one would believe this was the Demon Sword, the King’s Relic of the First Demon Lord Palace, the irrefutable proof of kingship that only Merlin could wield.

The two of them sailed past the wreckage of the Crusade Army’s warships. Not long ago, these vessels had been resplendent in their glory, but now they lay in desolate ruin.

Alice sighed inwardly, relieved that she was only a hired Hero and bore no real responsibility. If she had been a true Hero, she’d have no face to return to the Holy Church had she not died here in battle.

She glanced behind them. Countless shadows of man-eating sharks crisscrossed beneath the water, lurking in the depths. Surprisingly, they didn’t attack outright but instead trailed the boat, waiting for someone to fall overboard before feasting.

“They really didn’t attack us…”

Alice frowned in confusion. Normally, these sharks would tear the boat apart and devour them alive. Yet now, they seemed to fear something, daring only to follow, not to strike.

“Isn’t that obvious? Don’t let their reputation as low-level magical beasts fool you. They may lack intelligence, but their perception is sharp—they can sense potential danger.”

Merlin turned and chuckled, amused by how little this idiot girl knew.

Alice stayed silent, but a spark of hope flickered in her heart. With Merlin around, maybe they really could cross the Orkney Strait safely.

Merlin had spent a long time in the library of the First Demon Lord Palace. As a transmigrator, his top priority was gathering information.

Even Lilith knew better than to disturb Merlin when he was reading.

After devouring countless books, Merlin had formed a basic understanding of this world.

It was a place where magic and battle aura coexisted. The power hierarchy was generally divided into four tiers: Low, Mid, High, and Saint-tier.

Saint-tier was the pinnacle most beings in this world could reach—though there might be existences beyond even that.

Merlin, for instance, felt he didn’t fit into any of these tiers at all. He was practically a bug-like anomaly.

In short, his summary of this world was simple:

A fantasy realm with medieval customs, brimming with mystical elements and unsolved mysteries.

Though the books described the outside world, there were bound to be discrepancies. So, he was genuinely looking forward to this journey.

Perhaps he’d encounter an incredibly powerful being. If he could just cut them down, maybe he could finally break this damn curse.

At the thought, Merlin’s lips curled upward, excitement and anticipation burning in his chest.

The two of them left the wreckage-strewn waters behind and drifted into the open sea.

The endless ocean was far from beautiful—storm winds howled, the waves raged with menacing ferocity, and the dark depths hid countless crimson eyes.

Alice’s heart pounded with unease. Rowing against the storm was exhausting, and the constant fear of sea monsters gnawed at her.

Even Merlin might struggle against a sea serpent in open water.

She studied Merlin’s back, doubt creeping into her mind. Finally, she spoke up. “Lucifer the Third…”

“I’ve told you not to call me that. I’m no longer the Demon Lord. The name Lucifer isn’t something to throw around. Just call me Merlin.”

“Then why did you leave the Demon Lord Palace?” Alice asked directly. A being this powerful venturing into human territory—wasn’t that a recipe for chaos?

A cold sweat trickled down Merlin’s forehead. *No way am I telling her I got fired. Too embarrassing.*

And he certainly couldn’t mention the curse. That was a secret, and he barely knew Alice. Why would he confide in her?

“I’m just too damn strong. Undefeated among the demon race, so it got boring. I wanted to go out and stir up some trouble—is that so wrong?”

title: Chapter 21
content:
Chapter 21

Volume 1 · Chapter 21

"What... what kind of excuse is this? Is this your reason for fighting?" Alice's expression twisted in disbelief. *Isn't this just making excuses?*

"Yeah, if I don't cause trouble every day, I feel uncomfortable all over..." Merlin said with a straight face, threatening, "Got a problem with that? I'll throw you into the sea to feed the sharks."

Alice swallowed a mouthful of complaints, rowing in sulky silence as she cursed Merlin's ancestors to the eighteenth generation in her mind.

She felt a deep sense of injustice. Why was someone as reckless and shameless as Merlin so powerful?

She had trained for over a decade in the freezing Great Snow Mountains, enduring countless hardships, yet she couldn't even defeat two of Merlin's fingers.

After all her sweat, tears, and suffering, she was still humiliated by Merlin, called a weakling.

The shame and frustration crushed her.

"Me... Merlin..."

"Hmm?"

"Do you have Saint-tier strength now?" Alice asked quietly.

"I don't know." Merlin answered truthfully. He really had no idea what tier he was at—maybe the tier of a total cheat?

"Surely you reached this level through extraordinary effort, right? Isn't it true that genius is 1% inspiration and 99% perspiration?" Alice hoped Merlin's strength came from hard work. Otherwise, she might start questioning her entire life.

"Are you stupid enough to believe that?" Merlin scoffed. "That's obviously a lie. They just want mediocre people like you to blindly work yourselves to the bone, squeezing out every last drop of blood to contribute a little to the world. It's a cruel, despicable lie. Mediocre people should stay grounded and know their place."

"How can that be?" Alice felt her beliefs shaking.

"So-called geniuses are those with absolute talent. If talent can be overtaken by effort, then what's the point of being a genius?" Merlin smirked. "A genius's success is something that even a million percent effort can't surpass. There's an unbridgeable gap—that's what makes them a genius."

"Th-then..." Alice numbly moved the oars, her face pale as paper, her eyes trembling. Her worldview was shattered. "Then how did you become so strong? Can... can you tell me?"

"Well..." Merlin withdrew his gaze, staring straight ahead, and told the truth—

"My mother was the second-generation ruler of the Demon Lord Palace—what you call Lucifer the Second."

"As a royal, I thought I could live a carefree life, eating and playing with my sister every day."

"But during the Holy Church's 197th Crusade, my mother died in battle."

"With no strengths of my own, my sister and I had to rely on each other. But the demon race is a cruel, survival-of-the-fittest kind."

"Without my mother's protection, my sister and I suffered endless humiliation, trampled underfoot. Every day, nobles would whip my sister to get our meager food."

"My sister was frail and sickly. Once, in the dead of winter, she fell gravely ill. We had no clothes, no food—she was on the verge of death."

"That was when I set a goal: I would become stronger to protect my sister."

"I fought rock giants in the mountains, tore apart sea demons in the ocean, slain dragons in the sky, even monsters in lava."

"I endlessly trained my swordsmanship, swinging my rusted katana every day, nearly dying countless times."

"In the end, I relied on sheer strength to kill those who had once bullied my sister, reclaimed the throne, drew the demon sword Banri Garan, and leveled my Iaijutsu skill to 99999999999999999999999."

"When I looked back, I had already become invincible."

Merlin let out a long sigh, his golden hair swaying in the wind.

He looked up at the storm ahead, his face resolute and unyielding.

Speaking so much all at once left him somewhat sentimental—

"That's it. Nothing more."

"My past is simply the epic of a prince's revenge."

title: Chapter 22
content:
Chapter 22

Volume 1 · Chapter 22

What is this?

Who would’ve thought you still need to be oppressed to grow stronger.

By the way, what does that "99999... level" mean?

Alice was deeply confused, but hearing Merlin’s muttering, she felt a glimmer of hope. It seemed she hadn’t worked hard enough—otherwise, she too could reach Saint-tier strength.

“So, in the end, you only got this far through hard work, right?”

“No way. Who worked hard? My dream is to freeload and do nothing. How could I possibly put in effort?” Merlin grinned, thumbing at himself. “This lord was born max-level. Strong as hell.”

*Pffft!* Alice coughed up a mouthful of blood. Her pride took a brutal hit. She felt Merlin was clearly toying with her. The flicker of hope she’d just kindled was instantly snuffed out. Furious, she snapped, “Then why did you sound so emotional earlier?! If you’re that powerful, how could your past have been so miserable?! Do you think this is an awards ceremony—you can’t show up on stage without a tragic backstory?!”

“I wasn’t lying. Back then, I *was* pretty pathetic—because I had power but didn’t know how to use it. I was basically a cripple.” Merlin lifted his eyelids, serious. “For example, it’s like I have a ton of HP, but no skills that cost HP, so I’m weak. Feels terrible.”

“H… HP? What’s that?” Alice’s mind filled with question marks.

Merlin shook his head. HP was something people from another world wouldn’t understand.

“Never mind. To put it simply, imagine a max-level Yasuo heading mid lane, then dumbly forgetting to level up his skills—so all he can do is auto-attack.”

“??!” Alice knitted her delicate brows, completely lost.

“Scram. I can’t explain it to you. Go home and scrub mud with a washboard.” Merlin waved his hand impatiently, frustrated that he couldn’t make her understand. The language barrier between worlds made it impossible.

“Fine, don’t explain! But why insult me?!” Alice’s pretty face flushed red with anger. She felt Merlin was deliberately hiding his training methods from her. “So stingy…”

Merlin twisted his mouth but said nothing. *I was max-level at birth, but I didn’t learn any skills, so I couldn’t use my strength. So I frantically leveled up Iaigiri. Is that really so hard to understand?*

*Or have I dropped to the same IQ as this dumb girl…*

The two moved farther and farther from the Death Swamp. Before them, the pitch-black sea and the storm clouds above merged like a heavy, inky gate slowly creaking open toward the unknown.

At first, Alice could still hear the thrashing of the man-eating sharks behind them, but now, it was eerily silent.

Curious, she turned around—only to find the shark pack had vanished without a trace.

“The man-eating sharks are gone. Did they really give up?”

“You’re too naive. Sharks flee because a bigger predator is coming. That’s the law of the food chain.”

“Eh?!” Alice didn’t get it.

Merlin’s expression remained calm, no ripple of emotion. His gaze fixed on the storm and lightning ahead, raindrops pattering against his face.

In the distance, the waves grew higher and wilder, crashing violently, blocking their path. The small boat they were in began to rock. Beneath the water, a massive shadow gradually surfaced, growing clearer—like a giant turtle rising up.

Vast stretches of the sea turned black, swallowed by the silhouette of this unknown beast. It was impossible to fathom just how enormous it was.

“Get down.” Merlin said flatly.

“Why?” Alice froze, not grasping the situation.

“Something’s coming. If you fall into the sea, I won’t save you—because I can’t swim either.” Merlin answered honestly.

Alice jumped in shock. She glanced at the water beneath the boat—nothing but darkness.

Her heart lurched. A bad premonition struck her. Instantly, she regretted going out to sea with Merlin.

Alice set down the oars and obediently lay flat in the boat.

“Didn’t you dive into the sea and tear apart a sea demon before? How can you not swim?”

“That thing *climbed onto land by itself* to steal my sardine can. I’ve never actually gone into the sea.” Merlin’s tone was a little awkward.

Alice’s forehead twitched with black lines, her expression a mix of emotions—

*That…*

Why did this feel so absurdly low-budget?

Was this sea voyage really going to be okay?

(￢_￢)

title: Chapter 23
content:
Chapter 23

Volume 1 · Chapter 23

The storm raged on, accompanied by thunder and lightning.

Dark clouds churned as if demons were stirring chaos within them. A shadow loomed over the restless sea, with waves growing higher and higher. The silhouette of the monster beneath the water was estimated to be several hundred feet long. The sea breeze carried a heavy, bloody stench. The crashing waves and thunderclaps created an ominous atmosphere.

Alice’s face paled. She didn’t know what was coming, but she had a terrible feeling about it.

Merlin remained expressionless, seemingly unfazed—except the violent rocking of the small boat was making him dizzy, and he felt like he was going to throw up...

Directly ahead of the boat, a small whirlpool appeared first, then spiraled into a towering waterspout that shot nearly a hundred feet into the air before bursting apart.

A colossal sea serpent emerged, its massive body blotting out the sky, casting a vast shadow over Merlin and Alice. Their tiny boat was no bigger than one of its jagged teeth—maybe the size of a toothpick.

Only half of the sea serpent’s enormous body was visible above the water. A flick of its tail sent towering waves crashing, and its shimmering scales glinted in the light. Its elongated neck stretched like a pillar into the heavens! Its gills twitched constantly, its blood-red eyes locked onto the two people in the boat, and its tongue flicked in and out.

"Did it get here too late and miss its meal, so now it’s angry?"

Alice tilted her head up, staring at the towering sea serpent as she muttered to herself.

She crouched on the boat, trembling, a wave of terror rising in her heart.

Speak of the devil—she had actually come face-to-face with a sea serpent.

If she had known this would happen, she never would have agreed to Merlin’s plan to go out to sea. She should have just waited for the Holy Church to send reinforcements...

The sea serpent was the overlord of the Orkney Strait, an absolute Saint-tier sea monster with unchallenged dominance in the waters. It had a taste for humans and frequently attacked merchant ships, making the sea route from Great Britain to Greenland perilous.

Old sailors whispered that if you spotted the sea serpent’s tail in the Orkney Strait, there was no point trying to escape—just kneel and pray to the Goddess of Light.

The Queen of Great Britain had once dispatched the Royal Fleet to the Orkney Strait, led by two Saint-tier mages. But the entire fleet perished, every last ship lost to the depths.

Such an overwhelming force at sea—could Merlin handle it?

Maybe Merlin was powerful on land, but at sea, with all the restrictions, his mighty iaigiri might not be much use.

Alice fretted anxiously, convinced this might be the end for her. She sighed silently to herself—whenever she was with Merlin, disaster struck. And now, the moment they stepped out, they had to run into an overlord-class sea serpent.

Alice’s face was ashen, her lips pressed together, too afraid to speak. All she could think about was what the inside of the sea serpent’s stomach looked like.

The storm still raged, with lightning occasionally splitting the sky, illuminating the sea serpent’s grotesque form, its sharp, jagged teeth, and its crimson fins fluttering like an accordion being played.

Merlin looked up, meeting the sea serpent’s gaze. His expression was blank, his eyes wide with surprise, as if he couldn’t quite believe what he was seeing.

Alice watched Merlin standing at the bow, wondering—was he really so terrified by the sea serpent that he’d gone stupid?

"Tsk! This thing..." Merlin smacked his lips, then pulled his gaze away and turned back to Alice. "Why does it look so much like a... you know?"

He stared at the sea serpent’s tiny head and absurdly long neck. No matter how he looked at it, it resembled a certain *thing*—vulgar, lewd, a blight on the moral decency of the Orkney Strait.

"Get lost!" Alice’s face twisted in exasperation, unable to hold back her furious retort—

"It’s just got a long neck, that’s all!"

"Stop twisting everything into something dirty!"

"How filthy is your mind, exactly?!"

"At least show some respect—it’s an enemy!"

o(*≧д≦)o

title: Chapter 24
content:
Chapter 24

Volume 1 · Chapter 24

The storm grew even more violent, accompanied by thunder and lightning.

Countless raindrops coalesced into threads, like the grand curtain of a theater slowly drawing open.

The massive plesiosaur loomed high above, gazing down at Merlin and Alice with a predatory stare.

Its hungry eyes glowed with an eerie red light, as if it had already decided the two on the small boat were nothing more than a meal.

"Damn it, I stay out of trouble for once, and now the neighborhood’s delivering free snacks to my door..."

Merlin stood at the bow, head held high, staring up at the powerful plesiosaur. He lightly stroked the demon sword at his waist, growing more composed as the rain poured down.

"Starving so bad you’re picking a fight with me? You must’ve lost your mind!"

The plesiosaur was intelligent enough to understand Merlin’s words. It snorted two streams of mist from its nostrils, its gills trembling even more violently—clearly enraged.

"Hey, don’t provoke it!" Alice pressed herself against the boat, her face pale. "Don’t you know how terrifying sea dragons are in the water? If we’re lucky, it might spare us!"

"Hmph~" Merlin let out a cold laugh, his battle lust rising. Baring his teeth, he grinned. "Even better if it’s strong. If it were some weakling, I wouldn’t even bother moving!"

Alice’s face turned ashen. She covered her face, speechless, thinking this idiot must have a screw loose.

"Even if I’m fine now, more power never hurts. I’ll just take it as—"

"ROOOOAR——!!!"

Before Merlin could finish his boast, the plesiosaur lowered its head and let out a deafening roar from above.

A gust of fishy wind struck their faces, sending their hair flying, their expressions twisting comically.

The roar was laced with thick, yellow drool, which splattered all over Merlin, turning him into a yellow wax figure in an instant.

The sheer force of the roar sent waves crashing in all directions. The beast’s voice shook their very souls. Its gaping maw, tall enough to swallow ten grown men, was lined with jagged, razor-sharp teeth. Its crimson gills buzzed ominously.

Alice, overwhelmed by the aura of this apex predator, fell into a daze, her face draining of all color.

Her eyes widened, her entire body trembling uncontrollably—she was utterly terrified by the plesiosaur.

The creature didn’t rush to devour them. Instead, it seemed to be toying with its prey, savoring the cruel amusement of instilling fear.

Alice barely regained her senses, her heart pounding wildly, her nerves stretched to the limit.

She was in a desperate situation—jumping into the sea meant being eaten by sharks, staying put meant being swallowed by the plesiosaur. Either way, she was doomed to become food.

But there was still a sliver of hope: Merlin. If he could unleash the same power he had used to slay the white whale, they might just survive this ordeal.

Alice looked at Merlin. He had been drenched in the plesiosaur’s drool and now resembled a lump of yellow mud, standing awkwardly at the bow, looking utterly pathetic.

"Gross..."

The stench of the plesiosaur’s saliva was unbearable. Just a whiff made her want to vomit. But for the sake of survival, she had no choice but to pin her hopes on Merlin.

"Merlin, are you okay?"

"I... I’m fine..." Merlin replied awkwardly, wiping the yellow drool from his face. "Damn, this stinks! Did this thing raid a sardine cannery or something? Its breath is disgusting..."

"That’s not the point!" Alice pounded the boat’s deck, nearly in tears. "Do something, or we’re going to end up in its stomach!"

Before Merlin could respond, the plesiosaur’s massive body suddenly shifted. The sea’s surface seemed to fold in on itself, sending up a towering wave hundreds of feet high!

A wall of raging water surged forward.

The roar of the waves was even louder than the thunder.

The monstrous wave, blotting out the sky, swallowed everything in darkness.

Merlin stared at the magnificent yet oppressive tidal wave—a force comparable to a tsunami, capable of dragging everything into the depths.

Alice was stunned, her face as pale as paper.

Now she understood why the British Royal Fleet had been completely annihilated. The sheer destructive power of these waves was terrifying—no fleet could withstand being capsized and swallowed by the sea!

No wonder it was the tyrant of the Orkney Straits, nearly invincible at sea!

Alice glanced at Merlin. Compared to the wave, he was nothing more than an ant. How could he possibly defy the force of nature?

She sighed inwardly, convinced she was doomed. Without even a pen and paper, she couldn’t even leave a final letter for her teacher.

"HAHAHAHA..."

Merlin’s expression remained calm. Suddenly, he grinned.

Faced with a threat that spelled certain death, he seemed… excited.

Merlin gripped the hilt of the katana at his waist. The demon sword hummed, vibrating in response.

His eyes burned with intensity as he stared down the overwhelming flood—

"Interesting~"

"Doesn’t even let me finish talking before spitting in my face."

"What a rude, stinking saltwater fish!"

"Thinks it’s some kind of sea god just because it’s big?"

"Since you’re so eager to die, I won’t waste my breath on you!"

title: Chapter 25
content:
Chapter 25

Volume 1 · Chapter 25

Merlin suddenly drew his sword, faster than the eye could follow!

He swung vertically, cleaving toward the sea...

The force roared like a wild beast, tearing through everything in its path.

The towering waves were instantly shattered, and an irresistible, invisible sword energy—like a beam of light—split everything before it in two!

The arrogant sea serpent, which had been flaunting its power, froze as if its soul had been ripped out.

In that moment—

The wind stopped. The rain stilled.

Even the waves ceased their churning.

All things fell into silence.

Only the mournful whistle of the katana cutting through the air remained.

Alice was completely stunned. She had no idea what had just happened, but it felt like the battle had ended the moment Merlin drew his sword. It seemed like he had finished the fight with a single strike—again.

A doubt welled up in her mind: How could an ordinary iaijutsu slash be this overwhelming? It was unheard of.

Her gaze shifted to the demon sword in Merlin’s hand. The blade was rusted, pitted, and notched, its edge chipped and warped.

How could such a broken sword, unworthy of the name "demon sword," kill an enemy in one strike? It defied all logic!

Could it really be, as Merlin claimed, that he was simply born this powerful?

Merlin flicked his katana, elegantly sheathed it with a crisp *shing*, and the sound echoed like a bell.

Suddenly, the winds howled, the thunder roared, and time seemed to lurch back into motion.

A gale kicked up, waves crashed, and Alice couldn’t keep her eyes open.

The sea itself groaned as it was forcibly split apart, a spectacle as grand as Moses parting the Red Sea.

The Saint-tier sea serpent was already dead, cut cleanly in half like rotten mud. Its kidneys, bones, and massive flesh were exposed in a perfect incision, sliding apart to stain the seawater red before slowly sinking.

The dark clouds receded, revealing a clear blue sky, and golden sunlight spilled down.

Alice’s face remained frozen in shock. She thought, *Sure enough, he ended the battle with one strike again. How could the tyrant of the Orkney Strait turn into tofu before Merlin? Did it eat too many sardine cans and get poisoned?*

Merlin stretched lazily, watching the sea serpent’s corpse slowly sink into the deep, bubbles gurgling up.

He couldn’t help but feel a surge of excitement. To encounter a Saint-tier opponent right after leaving home—what a pleasant surprise. It was like a bonus to extend his lifespan.

He had already taken down two Saint-tier beings in a single day. He figured he could afford to relax for a while.

Merlin felt even more certain that leaving the Demon Lord Palace had been the right choice. The outside world was full of adventures and all kinds of enemies. His hope of breaking his curse seemed pretty good.

“What kind of snake was that? It was spitting before the fight even started—total trash. Probably never been hit before. In our world, this thing might be good for nothing but pickling in alcohol...”

Alice hadn’t heard a word. Her mind was consumed by one thought: *Why is this cheat of a Merlin so absurdly strong? That earth-shattering iaijutsu has no cooldown—can he use it infinitely? If he’s not the Goddess of Light’s own son, I wouldn’t believe it.*

“Alice...”

“Alice?!”

“Huh?!”

Only after Merlin called her twice did Alice snap out of her daze.

“Huh what huh? Row the boat! If you dare complain, I’ll throw you into the sea to feed the sharks, hehehe~”

Threatened by Merlin, Alice had no choice but to obediently pick up the oars, her expression still dazed.

The storm had passed, and the sky turned a clear, deep blue, blending seamlessly with the sea.

A flock of seagulls skimmed the water’s surface, their claws breaking the stillness, sending out ripples.

The Death Swamp that had imprisoned Merlin for over a decade had finally vanished.

For the first time in his life, the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace left his homeland and set foot toward the human-dominated Middle Earth.

With the goal of breaking his own curse, he issued a challenge to all the strong across the continent.

A grand rural drama began, and the allure of the city quietly lifted its curtain.

Merlin supervised Alice, his sturdy laborer, as she rowed, while he stood at the bow, basking in the sea breeze.

In her mind, Alice cursed Merlin countless times: *Hurry up and fall into the sea and drown, you bastard!*

Merlin placed a hand on his forehead, gazing into the blue distance.

“Row faster, you useless washboard Hero.”

“Our destination is the land of Great Britain!”

Alice was furious and wanted to hurl the oars into the sea and go on strike.

But then she thought—if she did that, wouldn’t she be stranded at sea too?

So Alice, face flushed with anger, grumbled—

“I *know*!”

“You perverted Demon Lord.”

“Don’t need you to boss me around!”

(..??^??..)

title: Chapter 26 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 26 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 1 · Chapter 26

Azure waves rolled in one after another, crashing against the shore.

Seagulls spread their wings, gliding over the small boat moored below and gazing down at the man and woman.

Merlin and Alice, after a series of trials, had rowed the small boat for three days and three nights to cross the Orkney Strait and arrive here.

The boat slowly drifted to the shore, where a stretch of beach met a dense jungle.

Merlin jumped off the boat and looked around, feeling utterly unfamiliar with the place. He had expected to reach a city port, but instead, it was a desolate wilderness—no village in sight.

*Great, we escaped the godforsaken Death Swamp only to end up in another godforsaken wasteland.*

Alice dropped the oars, scrambled onto the shore, and the moment she did, she collapsed onto the sand, gasping for breath.

Sweat drenched her back, and she looked as if she were on the verge of death from exhaustion...

She hadn’t realized Merlin wasn’t joking—she had done all the rowing herself the entire way. It had nearly killed her.

Merlin had not an ounce of gentlemanly grace. Not only did he refuse to help, but he had also threatened Alice, saying that if she didn’t row, he’d throw her into the sea to feed the fish.

In the middle of the endless ocean, with nowhere to run, Alice had no choice but to grit her teeth and row like a slave, enduring the backbreaking labor.

Being forced to serve the Demon Lord as a slave was the greatest humiliation Alice had ever suffered in her life.

Driven by an overwhelming will to survive, Alice had somehow unlocked hidden human potential. Relying solely on her own determination and a single oar, she had crossed the Orkney Strait—a miracle for a human.

Truly, people were forced into greatness, and Alice was no exception...

Along the way, with Merlin around, aside from the sea serpent, they hadn’t been attacked even once. That, at least, was something Alice was grateful for.

But Merlin was absolutely despicable. Out of boredom one night at sea, he had forced Alice to sing for his amusement.

Furious but pressured, Alice had reluctantly sung an Alpine folk song from the snow-capped mountains.

Merlin shook his head, dissatisfied, saying it sounded like a monk chanting scripture. Then he taught her a different song to sing instead.

It sounded like some tribal shepherd’s tune—or a nursery rhyme. Alice’s mind and body rejected it entirely, but fearing Merlin would toss her overboard to the fish, she obeyed and sang—

*Happy Sheep, Pretty Sheep~?*

The cringe-worthy melody echoed across the sea. The infamous brainless sheep song had now spread to another world. Merlin nodded in satisfaction.

Alice’s face burned, tears of humiliation welling in the corners of her eyes. She felt her noble soul had been shamed, her pride brutally trampled by Merlin.

For the cruel, inhuman Merlin, Alice felt not a shred of affection. She cursed his ancestors and descendants alike—may they be born without legs, or choke on cold water.

Alice swore in silence that one day, when she reached Saint-tier and learned the ultimate secrets of the Iceblade Technique from her teacher, she would find that bastard Merlin and split his head open like a watermelon.

“Alice, where is this?” Merlin turned back to ask. “Didn’t I tell you not to stop or dock until we reached Great Britain?”

“Y-Yes…” Alice panted, struggling to speak. “Can’t you see for yourself, you idiot?!”

“Hm?!” Merlin’s expression darkened. He felt Alice was getting too bold. He put on his villainous face and threatened—

“How *dare* you speak to me like that?”

“You… you flat-chested Hero…”

“Small chest, but big attitude, huh?”

“Trying to rebel, are we?”

(ー`′ー)

title: Chapter 27
content:
Chapter 27

Volume 1 · Chapter 27

Alice clenched her mouth shut, her face twisted in humiliation, tears glistening in her eyes as if she were about to cry.

"This... this is the territory of Great Britain, the northern coast of England!"

Alice hadn’t returned to the port of Bristol because it was too far—she’d definitely collapse from exhaustion. So she’d chosen the most remote island in northern Scotland instead.

"How come there isn’t a single person here?" Merlin frowned, feeling something was off. He’d expected to see gentlemen in top hats and tails, or ladies with parasols in puffy dresses. "I warn you, don’t lie to me. I’ve read plenty of books."

"I’m not lying! This really is Great Britain! It’s just the farthest north, the climate’s too unstable for any cities to be built..." Alice explained frantically, her head swelling with frustration.

"I see..." Merlin pondered briefly, deciding to go see the legendary empire where the sun never set. "For your hard work, I’ll give you a compliment."

"I don’t need your compliment!" Alice huffed, grinding her teeth in fury.

Merlin chuckled, waving his hand. "Farewell, it’s been such a pleasant voyage at sea~!"

Pleasant my ass!

Get lost, you damn Demon Lord!

One day, I’ll cut off your head with my sword!

Alice bit her lip, seething internally. Her hatred for Merlin had reached the same level as her loathing for cockroaches—she wouldn’t rest until one of them was dead.

Merlin took a few steps, then suddenly stopped, his expression turning horrified.

He realized a critical problem: he had no money.

As a transmigrator, Merlin knew full well that without money, he couldn’t survive in society.

Should he rob the national treasury or ambush a merchant caravan?

Merlin felt that, as one of the rulers of the demon race, he still had some pride. He wouldn’t stoop to theft or murder.

Plus, if he did something so despicable, the kingdom would put a bounty on his head. Then he’d never live in peace—endless adventurers would come after him for the reward.

Even though he was a demon now, not human, he still had basic morals. That was the fundamental difference between man and beast.

He couldn’t just do whatever he wanted just because this was another world. Wearing human skin didn’t mean he could act worse than a pig or a dog.

Of course, Merlin’s morals only applied to ordinary people and friends.

As for enemies... well, of course he’d do whatever he wanted! What was there to hesitate about?!

Merlin’s eyes sparkled as he turned to look at Alice, who was kneeling on the ground resting behind him.

He was a Demon Lord, she was a Hero—they were undeniably enemies. It seemed he’d have to abandon all scruples and squeeze every last bit of value out of Alice to help himself get by in Great Britain.

Merlin’s gaze wandered over Alice, taking in her pure white mithril armor, shimmering with radiant light, its surface etched with defensive magical runes.

This was clearly no ordinary armor—it had to be top-tier, worth a damn fortune!

If he could get his hands on Alice’s mithril armor, he could probably sell it for a hefty sum. That’s right, he was going to rob her!

Merlin cleared his throat and walked up to Alice, stroking his chin with a lecherous grin. "Lovely miss, I need you to offer up something precious, hehehe~"

"W-What... what are you doing?!" Alice clutched her chest and backed away, thinking—

Something precious... does he mean my chastity?!

∑(°口°?)??

title: Chapter 28
content:
Chapter 28

Volume 1 · Chapter 28

"Take your clothes off like a good girl~" Merlin raised an eyebrow, as if teasing Alice.

"R-Really... do I have to?"

Alice bit her trembling lip, her face losing color, eyes filled with humiliation and resentment.

"Hurry up. Don’t make me get rough. I’m still a gentleman, you know."

Merlin kept a straight face, his hand resting on the hilt of his sword, as if ready to draw and strike at any moment.

"Guh..."

A deep, mournful cry escaped Alice’s throat. She never expected to end up in a situation like this.

So this pervert really doesn’t intend to let me go... I can’t believe there’s someone this disgusting in the world!
Not only does he treat me like a laborer, but now he wants to humiliate me too?!

She crossed her arms over her chest, her face flushed red, a mix of shame and anger clear on her face.

Alice glanced up at Merlin secretly. Though his expression was blank, in her eyes, he looked unspeakably lecherous.

Poor Alice seemed to foresee her own fate, her eyes welling up with tears.

If I’d known it would come to this, I never would’ve become that damn Hero. I never thought I’d face such humiliation...

Merlin furrowed his brows, tilting his head in confusion, his mind filled with question marks. What the hell is going on here?

Under the pressure, Alice finally got down to business.

She unclasped the white silk cape embroidered with the Holy Church’s emblem, removed her expensive mithril light armor, and untied her sheer undergarments.

Even her pink panties were neatly folded and placed on top.

Her fair skin glowed under the sunlight, her graceful curves a masterpiece of nature, her silver hair swaying in the wind, and her pitifully flat chest...

Alice knelt on the beach, her cheeks flushed crimson, her beauty radiant, trembling as the salty sea breeze brushed against her.

Merlin stared at Alice’s bare body, utterly confused. *I just wanted to rob her of her gear, not her dignity! How did this turn into a scene of assault? Damn it! I’m a decent man!*

"Hey! I meant for you to take off your armor, that’s all. Why are you stripping completely naked? Aren’t you cold with your ass out like that?"

"Eh?!" Alice opened her eyes, bewildered. "Aren’t you... trying to humiliate me?"

"Oh my god!" Merlin furrowed his brows, black lines forming on his forehead. "Are you that desperate for a man? What’s going on in that head of yours? Have some shame! And you’re a Hero? Your predecessors would be rolling in their graves if they saw you like this!"

"Uh..." Alice’s face burned red, her expression blank. *Did I misunderstand? Merlin never even thought about... doing that to me...*

"Oh~!" Merlin suddenly realized, muttering, "How could your mind be so filthy..."

"No, it’s not like that! I..." Alice’s face turned even redder, trying to explain.

"Alright, alright! Don’t explain!" Merlin cut her off, looking at her with disdain.

"Just look at your pathetic flat chest. How could that possibly tempt me?"

"At least grow a pair first before trying to seduce me. Right now, you coming at me like this is useless. All I can say is..."

"You, the Flat-Chested Hero, are absolutely shameless!"

Alice’s face instantly paled, as if she had just taken 10,000 points of mental damage. Her soul began to answer the Goddess of Light’s call, ready to leave her body.

She felt like her life had lost all meaning. Maybe she should just accept her fate as a useless, salty fish for the rest of her days...

"Oh, right, there’s one good thing about being flat—saves on fabric when making clothes." Merlin picked up the pile of mithril armor and walked away. His mocking voice echoed from a distance, "Flat-chested, flat-chested, hahahahaha..."

A long time passed—

Alice, still naked and kneeling on the beach, looked like she had lost her soul, utterly disheveled in the wind.

Today was her day of suffering. She had experienced the ultimate humiliation and begun to question her life.

Alice’s face twisted in grievance, and finally, tears streamed down her face. She broke down, sobbing on the empty beach—

"YAAAAAAAAAAH!"

"Damn you, Merlin, you shameless, perverted bastard!"

"I swear I never want to see you again in this lifetime!"

( >﹏<。)

The air was suddenly filled with the unmistakable scent of a Flag...

title: Chapter 1
content:
Chapter 1

Volume 2 · Chapter 1

One year later.

Great Britain, Wales.

A small village on the outskirts.

Two thieves were scouting a route that caravans always passed through. They hid behind the forest, ready to rob passersby.

Gray-clothed thief: "Senior, what do we do? If we don’t get any money today, the boss will chop us up."

Black-clothed thief: "Don’t panic, there’ll be a chance. These country bumpkins from out of town have gotten smart—they don’t seem to take this road anymore."

Gray-clothed thief: "Then what do we do?"

Black-clothed thief: "Be patient and wait. There’s bound to be someone who still takes this road."

Gray-clothed thief: "Eh? Looks like someone really is coming this way."

Black-clothed thief: "What the hell, really?"

Gray-clothed thief: "But he doesn’t look like he has any money… looks like a ragpicker."

Black-clothed thief: "That’s where you’re wrong. As the saying goes, ‘Wealth doesn’t show itself.’ He might look dirt poor on the surface, but he’s probably loaded."

Gray-clothed thief: "Oh! You’re so wise, Senior!"

Black-clothed thief: "Watch me take him down. I’ll rob him so clean he won’t even have his underwear left!"

Following the thieves’ gaze, a ragged traveler was making his way along the winding path toward the village.

He leaned on a broken branch, struggling forward with labored breaths, as if he might collapse and die by the roadside at any moment.

That’s right—this man, radiating an aura of "broke, exhausted, and starving," was none other than Merlin, the once undefeated former Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace.

The Merlin of now bore no resemblance to his former glory. His clothes were tattered rags, barely covering him like a fig leaf. Disheveled and filthy, he looked like a scavenger from the docks, the kind who polished officers’ boots for spare change.

"Damn it…"

"So poor… so tired… so hungry…"

"Damn capitalism, so stingy…"

"I just ate a few meals without paying—how dare they put a bounty on me…"

Merlin was now a wanted man, with a bounty of 5,000 gold coins, and had earned the title "Deadbeat Pretty Boy."

Most people might think eating without paying was no big deal, but Merlin had dined at every high-end restaurant in Scotland, always ordering the most expensive dishes.

Irish premium foie gras, North Arctic caviar, Iberian steak—each meal costing hundreds of gold coins.

Thus, the freeloading Merlin had been jointly blacklisted by every restaurant owner in Scotland. His wanted poster now hung on the request boards of every Adventurers Guild.

To date, Merlin had racked up a debt of over ten thousand gold coins, making him a public enemy across England. In the end, he had no choice but to flee to Wales in Great Britain, planning to continue his freeloading ways.

Do you think Merlin was useless, with no ambition?

Impossible! Merlin had genuinely tried to pay off his debts.

He had worked over fifty different jobs, from high-end lounge host to stable hand, but without exception, he’d been fired from every single one. The reason? He was a terminally lazy slacker. Skipping work and slacking off were his defaults.

Worst of all, he had slept with over thirty boss’s wives, sending the bosses into raging furies. Could he *not* get fired after that?

Merlin swore that the rumors about him sleeping with the bosses’ wives were all lies. It wasn’t intentional—those married women had all taken a liking to him, going out of their way to seduce him. So somehow, he’d ended up with the reputation of a "Boss’s Wife Slayer."

Don’t forget, Merlin was fundamentally an incubus. Though he lacked any incubus abilities, his nature and traits remained. From thirty-year-old beautiful aunts to twelve-year-old budding Lolitas, he could charm them all.

Given enough time, anyone would develop feelings for him.

Plus, male incubi were all devastatingly handsome. Women who spent time around him would inevitably fall for him—

Powerful and good-looking.

The only flaw was that he was *way* too broke.

title: Chapter 2
content:
Chapter 2

Volume 2 · Chapter 2

Merlin, who had excellent luck with women, could never be seen without a crowd of beauties around him even at his most disheveled. He navigated through their affections with ease.

This left Merlin rather helpless. Those beautiful madams would show up in the middle of the night, dressed in alluring lingerie, to pour out their sorrows about failed marriages.

As a succubus, Merlin instinctively wanted to comfort these women, to soothe their wounded hearts.

He swore he had never done anything improper—just ordinary conversation—but rumors still spread like wildfire.

The reason Merlin could maintain such a detached, untouched demeanor was largely because he had seen too many women. At the human-equivalent age of 200, he had long passed the restless years of building a harem.

To Merlin, women were delicate creatures who needed gentle treatment. His creed was simple: never force a woman to do anything, for coercion was the most despicable method.

And so, Merlin accomplished nothing, racked up a mountain of debt, and spent his days idling about, freeloading and flirting with different women. Over a year passed like this.

He hadn’t written to his sister Lilith, choosing instead to keep his current state hidden. He feared that if she saw him like this—a complete waste of a man—she’d confirm his title as the "useless older brother."

And knowing Lilith’s insane tendencies, she’d probably slaughter all those madams without a second thought. Better to stay off the radar...

Merlin felt that life outside the Demon Lord Palace was nothing but hardship. Lilith had been right—he was a useless shut-in. Out here, he was called a pervert, fired from jobs, and generally despised.

He found this world eerily similar to his original one, bound by its own social rules.

For example, last month at a tavern, he overheard a group of old mercenaries bragging. One claimed the Soviet Union had assembled a giant soldier, only for another to retort that the British still had their overseas fleet.

Merlin sighed inwardly. Wasn’t this just nations flexing their military might? Exactly the same as back home.

He mused that if it weren’t for his proud principles—his refusal to engage in thuggery like looting and burning—he could’ve, *ahem*, overthrown the British queen and made himself king long ago.

Even though Merlin scrupulously followed the rules of this world, he was still wanted by a bunch of petty restaurant owners.

Every day, a group of noob adventurers came looking for trouble, lured by the bounty on his head. They all ended up with black eyes and bloody noses, crying all the way home to their mothers.

Merlin wouldn’t deign to draw his sword against a bunch of whining, useless nobodies. Fighting anyone below Saint-tier was a waste of time.

Why didn’t Merlin just kill the restaurant owners? Because as a proud and arrogant ruler, he couldn’t bring himself to unsheathe his blade over something as trivial as unpaid meals. If he did, his name would probably be carved into the demon race’s pillar of shame by morning.

The curse on his heart hadn’t acted up lately. Over the past year, Merlin had taken down four or five Saint-tier powerhouses, using their life force to extend his own. That bought him a little more time to live freely.

Now, Merlin was trudging on foot through Wales—not to seduce every madam in sight, *ahem*—but to rest for a while and maybe find some work to get by.

He hadn’t eaten in five days. Penniless, he recalled his last meal: a stolen lamb, roasted on the spot. The shepherd had chased him with a whip for two whole miles. It had been a disaster.

As Merlin grumbled to himself, cursing society and capitalism for stripping him of his right to be a shut-in, two masked bandits suddenly leapt from the sides of the path. Their daggers flipped through the air like a juggler’s trick.

The black-clad and gray-clad thieves cackled wickedly. After a morning of waiting, they’d finally found a fool to rob.

Merlin stopped, his vision slightly blurred from hunger. Bewildered, he asked, “What are you doing?”

“Hehehe!” The black-clad bandit sneered and opened with the classic line, “The king of heaven covers the earth~!”

Merlin hesitated, then tentatively replied, “Every grain is the fruit of hard labor~?”

(?-_?)??

title: Chapter 3 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 3 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 3

The gray-clad thief whispered into the black-clad thief’s ear, “Senior, that rhymes pretty well—could he be one of us?”

“How’s that possible?” The black-clad thief spread his hands, earnestly replying, “Our kind would never be this broke.”

“Yeah, you’re right… I thought he’d taken a transformation potion too…” The gray-clad thief nodded.

The black-clad thief turned to Merlin, flipping the brass dagger in his hand. “Kid, know what’s good for you—hand over everything valuable, or don’t blame me for stripping you down to your skivvies! Hehehe~”

Merlin’s face was blank, his expression weary as he stared at the two thieves, his mood complicated.

The silence was awkward. Normally, robbery victims screamed at the top of their lungs—why was this one so calm? Was his brain broken?

The gray-clad thief sensed something was off and muttered, “Senior, he’s way too calm, not scared at all… should we bail?”

“Scared of what? Look at him—probably starved out of his mind. I’ve seen people scared stupid before.” The black-clad thief scoffed.

“As expected of Senior!” The gray-clad thief admired him.

The black-clad thief glared at Merlin, annoyed. “Hey, ragpicker, at least scream once, show some respect for my profession, will you? I’m robbing you here…”

“Huh? Wait, you’re robbing *me*?” Merlin pointed at himself, utterly stunned.

“Are you mentally disabled, kid? These stockings on our heads are just for show?” The black-clad thief tugged at the flesh-colored stocking on his head, repeatedly emphasizing his role.

Merlin furrowed his brows, his expression turning strange. *Damn it!* This is my first robbery since coming to another world! I was the former Demon Lord, and now I’m being mugged by two petty thieves?! Show *me* some respect, will you? A tiger in the plains, bullied by mutts…

“Friends, I advise you to calm down. A bright future awaits you. Rob anyone you like, but don’t rob me.”

“Why not you?” The black-clad thief rolled his eyes.

“Because if I draw my sword, you might die…” Merlin said, his face uncharacteristically serious.

“Pfft!” The black-clad thief spat, eyeing the blackened greatsword hanging from Merlin’s tattered clothes—it looked like a rotten log. “That broken stick’s a sword? Probably some firewood you scavenged. Don’t think just because you’ve got something on your waist you’re a swordsman. If I stick a *dick* on my waist, does that make me a swordsman too? Just a bed warrior, hehehe~”

*Hey!*

*That’s enough!*

This is *Banri Garan*, the proof of kings.

The noble symbol of every first Demon Lord.

Don’t compare it to a *dick*…

Merlin’s temples throbbed, his emotions a tangled mess.

“And what’s this ‘draw sword slash’?” The gray-clad thief burst out laughing, thinking Merlin was a total hick. “Even idiots can use that basic skill. Half the time the sword gets stuck in the scabbard, and you look like a moron. I thought he’d at least pull off a Starburst Abandon Heal Slash or something, hahaha…”

The two thieves doubled over, tears streaming, marveling at how many fools existed these days—even someone with *Draw Sword Slash* could try to act tough.

“Hey, you two are going too far…” Merlin’s face darkened, getting angry now.

“So what if we are?” The black-clad thief put on a face begging for a beating, licking his brass dagger with his tongue. “Hand over the cash or we’re getting rough.”

“I’ve got no money. The only silk on me is my underwear, maybe worth a few silver coins, but it’s been months since it’s seen any action. You want that too?” Merlin scratched his neck, looking helpless.

All this time, adventurers had been harassing him for the bounty, keeping him from sleeping well. Bathing was a luxury, and even using the toilet required watching his back, afraid some shameless adventurer would ambush him with a black iron sword up his—

So Merlin was trying to earn some money, pay off his debts, and live in peace.

The two thieves were furious upon hearing this. After all this staking out, they’d only get a pair of silk underwear? Unacceptable. Both made challenging faces—

“Bullshit!”

title: Chapter 4
content:
Chapter 4

Volume 2 · Chapter 4

"Cut the crap, you must've hidden the money!" the black-clad thief refused to believe, his shouting growing louder.

"Yeah! You definitely hid it. A few days ago, a merchant stuffed gold bars up his— well, you know where. You must've done the same!" the gray-clad thief chimed in.

What the hell?

Wouldn’t that hurt?

And what if it got stuck during... you know? Then you’d be screwed.

That’d definitely make the London papers: "Local Merchant Dies from Constipation..."

Merlin’s forehead twitched with black lines. He had no idea how to respond, so he just smiled.

"The nerve to still smile? Looks like you need a taste of our power!"

The black-clad thief roared, leaping like a monkey, unleashing sweeping kicks, flying kicks, and a flurry of movements at full speed.

"This one’s a low-tier warrior, master of all kinds of martial techniques. One kick can send a burning rhino flying—scared yet?"

"Oh." Merlin watched the black-clad thief’s exaggerated display with a blank face.

"Tch! Then witness my Multi-Dagger Technique! One strike equals twenty!"

The black-clad thief, unsatisfied with the lack of reaction, pulled a red apple from his pocket, tossed it into the air, and with a single swing of his bronze dagger, peeled it perfectly clean.

"How’s that? See now? Know my power yet?!"

"Wow, not bad..." Merlin clapped slowly, swallowing hard as he stared at the apple, his stomach growling.

The black-clad thief’s face darkened, feeling mocked.

He dropped the peeled apple, rage boiling inside him. He decided to kill Merlin.

Gripping his dagger, he channeled his battle aura, charging at full speed. The dagger gleamed with cold light, aimed straight for Merlin’s heart.

"Arrogant human! Die!"

"Take him down, senior!" the gray-clad thief cheered from the side.

"Tsk..." Merlin lazily clicked his tongue, drawing his katana just slightly from its sheath. A powerful sword aura erupted.

Their figures crossed in an instant. In that single moment, the outcome was clear—the fight was over.

"So... so strong..."

The black-clad thief muttered, frozen in place, his face twisted in terror.

Merlin sighed, shaking his head, and sheathed his katana with a *shing*.

A clear red line appeared on the black-clad thief’s neck. His head slid off completely, rolling to the gray-clad thief’s feet with a *thump*.

Blood spurted from the corpse in a gruesome fountain, but Merlin just stared ahead, not even bothering to look.

The gray-clad thief stared at his senior’s head, horror twisting his face. His body trembled uncontrollably, and he collapsed onto the ground—

What the hell?!

Senior was a low-tier warrior, and he got one-shotted?!

How is that possible?! Iaijutsu is such a trash skill—why is it so overpowered?!

And that rusty, chipped blade—how is it so sharp?!

Too strong! This junk collector is way too strong!

The more he thought, the more terrified he became. It felt like a dream. Then he felt a warmth in his crotch—he’d actually been scared to the point of pissing himself.

Merlin sighed, looking at the now-pissing gray-clad thief. He really didn’t want to fight a useless guy like this, but if he kept jumping around, he couldn’t blame him for being ruthless. "Isn’t it better to just live?"

"Uh..."

The gray-clad thief’s breath hitched, his face pale, eyes wide with panic.

His legs gave out, his heart nearly stopping, but the will to survive forced him to scramble up, crawling away in a pathetic escape.

"Waaaaah!"

"Mom! Mommy!"

"I wanna go home! There’s a monster here!"

Merlin twisted his lips. *Who’s the monster?*

But over the past year, the four or five Saint-tier foes he’d killed had all called him a monster before dying.

Merlin thought he was only *slightly* strong—being called a monster was a bit much.

The black-clad thief’s corpse suddenly emitted puffs of black smoke, a foul stench hitting Merlin in the face. He flinched, thinking it might be some kind of self-destruct.

But the smoke cleared, and nothing happened—except the corpse had shrunk. The black clothes now hung loosely on the body.

Curious, Merlin tore off the silk mask from the head. Revealed was a pointed mouth, sunken cheeks, long pointed ears, a huge, sharp nose, and green skin...

A goblin?!

Why was it disguised as a human to rob people?

Merlin frowned, recalling the black smoke and stench—it must’ve been a transformation potion. He’d read about those in books.

But why go through the trouble of looking human just to rob someone?

Maybe they were afraid of being discovered and having the Imperial Army wipe out their goblin tribe...

Merlin pondered for a moment, then decided it had nothing to do with him. He’d just pretend he saw nothing.

With a kick, he sent the goblin’s head rolling away. He picked up the peeled apple from the ground, rubbed off the dirt on his clothes, and *crunch*—took a bite, chewing thoughtfully.

"Don’t waste food... it’s expensive..."

Leaning on a broken branch, Merlin trudged forward with difficulty.

Toward the small village in the distance, where smoke curled from chimneys.

Would this late-stage lazy bum ever find a job?

title: Chapter 5 — Reward Update
content:
Chapter 5 — Reward Update

Volume 2 · Chapter 5

At the village entrance.

A row of broken wooden palisades stood neatly in place.

Two guards in shabby armor were collecting tolls.

Tch, what a backwater place. Even the guards look dirt-poor.

He remembered the guards in Manchester City—dressed like Holy Knights, their armor polished enough to use as mirrors.

Merlin shook his head in dismay, then blended into the crowd, planning to sneak into the village without paying.

He pulled his tattered hood low over his head, playing the invisible man, then hoisted his soy sauce jug and marched forward with his head down.

Merlin was a repeat offender; he’d used this trick to dodge tolls countless times, and it never failed.

What he didn’t realize was that big cities didn’t lack funds, so guards usually couldn’t be bothered to chase down a few copper coins from someone who looked as broke as he did.

But small villages were different. When money was tight, they made sure not a single head tax slipped through.

"Tsk!"

The guard clicked his tongue in displeasure. His eyes were sharp—he spotted shady characters like this every day. In an instant, he saw Merlin trying to sneak in and cut in line.

So he reached out and grabbed Merlin’s shoulder, refusing to let him slip away.

"What’s this? I just paid the toll." Merlin turned back, wide-eyed and innocent, putting on a convincing act.

"Cut the act..." The guard twisted his mouth and held out his hand for the money.

"Damn capitalist exploiters..." Merlin rolled his eyes, grinding his teeth as he spoke.

To avoid trouble, he reluctantly pulled two copper coins from his pouch and tossed them into the guard’s hand. Then, like a lord, he strode into the village with a swagger.

Right at the entrance was a large marketplace. Many peddlers in rags were hawking their wares, and there were plenty of street performers.

The melodious sound of rustic strings drifted over, the beats of a tambourine and the notes of a fipple flute intertwining—looked like a traveling band.

"Sir, first time here? Need me to show you some fun places?"

A few sharp-faced, wiry men immediately swarmed over, dressed in tatters but clearly skilled at hustling.

"Ah, no need—"

Merlin’s hand froze mid-air. Turns out these men hadn’t been talking to him at all—they’d rushed past him straight for the wealthy merchant behind him.

Merlin felt a pang of embarrassment. Of course, dressed like this, he looked like he couldn’t afford a thing. No way would these "guides" waste their time on him. So he scratched his head to play it off.

The "guides" shot Merlin a few covert, disdainful glances, full of hostility—probably mistaking the scruffy Merlin for one of their own kind.

Merlin curled his lip. He didn’t much care for these types. They were everywhere.

They’d recommend all sorts of ** shops to outsiders, raving about how charming the girls were, just to earn a commission.

From a transmigrator’s perspective, Merlin thought these guys were basically pimps, and they always led people to shady joints—where you’d get robbed, lose your stuff, or fall into some honey trap.

But what really grated on Merlin’s nerves was the man at the center, dressed in a black robe with a silver cross on his chest, clutching a holy scripture, straining his neck as he bellowed at the clueless onlookers:

"Long live the Goddess of Light! If you don’t chant along, you’re not human! **’s dad!"

"No faith? How can you live like that? If you don’t believe, you’re not human! **’s dad!"

"Think the scripture’s too expensive at one gold coin? Is your faith not even worth that much? If you don’t buy it, you’re not human! **’s dad!"

No matter where he went, Merlin always ran into these Roman-style preachers. They acted like **, as if the Goddess of Light was their own mother, and they went around slandering the demon race, peddling their "demon threat" theory, claiming they had to be wiped out.

Technically, now that he was no longer the Demon Lord, the Holy Church was none of his concern. But hearing these preachers twist the truth still left a foul taste in his mouth.

Just like the demon race’s books described—there was a passage he remembered vividly:

Humans are all vain hypocrites. They flushed their truth down the toilet long ago.

title: Chapter 6 — Reward Update
content:
Chapter 6 — Reward Update

Volume 2 · Chapter 6

Although Merlin had already lost any goodwill toward the Holy Church, he still enjoyed the spectacle and went to listen in.

Merlin finally managed to squeeze his way to the front of the crowd of villagers, where the preacher’s voice was easily audible.

“Have you heard of Lucifer III, the First Demon Lord of the Death Swamp?” the preacher asked.

The villagers immediately began murmuring among themselves—apparently, they had all heard something about him.

“A year ago, the Holy Church sent a fleet of a hundred thousand Crusade Army ships to annihilate him, and Lucifer III wiped them all out with a single strike—none survived!” The preacher’s spittle flew as he spoke.

Merlin pondered for a moment. Wasn’t there a Hero named Alice who survived? What do you mean *none survived*? Did she end up naked on a beach, captured by cannibals and taken as a sex slave?

“They say the Great Demon Lord of the First Palace is hideously ugly, with a green face and fangs.”

“Yeah, not only is he ugly, but he’s also a lecher. I heard the 233rd Hero from last year was… you know… to death by him. How tragic.”

Two village women chattered excitedly, clearly enjoying the gossip.

Get lost! Who’s ugly?!

I’m the so-called *Tavern Mistress Slayer*!

And who the hell did Alice, that washboard, sleep with?!

Forcing women to do that kind of thing isn’t my style at all.

Sure, she tried to seduce me naked, but I’m not some sex-crazed idiot!

These old biddies don’t know a damn thing, yet here they are spreading rumors like it’s their job…

Merlin rolled his eyes, fuming. After all this, his reputation among the villagers was that of a lustful stallion who’d mount anything that moved?!

“And that’s not all—I heard he’s not just a lecher, but a lolicon too! He especially loves girls under twelve. His Demon Lord Palace has a dungeon full of little lolis locked up for his pleasure.” A fat priest leaned in, joining the gossip circle.

“Oh my goodness, how terrifying…” A middle-aged woman immediately pulled her twelve-year-old daughter closer, as if afraid Lucifer III would descend from the sky at any moment to snatch her away.

What the hell?!

I’m not a lolicon!

The Demon Lord Palace basement is all lava—where’s the damn dungeon?!

If I really had a bunch of little lolis locked up for my pleasure, why the hell would I ever leave the Demon Lord Palace?! Are you people brain-dead? Did a donkey kick you in the head?!

Merlin’s nose was practically twisted in rage. His past reputation was being slandered, and even though he was no longer the Demon Lord, it still pissed him off.

“Lucifer III is incredibly powerful, known as the strongest of the Seven Demon Lords. And since he’s just across the Orkney Strait from Great Britain, very close by, if he were to lead the Demon Lord Army across the sea to attack Great Britain, do you think you could survive without the Goddess of Light’s protection?” The preacher spoke with fiery passion, like some kind of savior.

Sorry, but I’ve never once considered leading an army across the Orkney Strait to attack Great Britain…

Merlin shook his head, silently mocking the whole thing. There they go again with the *Demon Race Threat Theory*, acting like the demon race exists solely to conquer the world and take pleasure in slaughtering other races.

But the villagers didn’t see it that way. With just a few words from the preacher, they were all convinced, their faces filled with terror.

“So you all need to buy a copy of the Holy Scriptures to deepen your faith in the Goddess of Light! One gold coin—you won’t regret it! One gold coin—it’s a steal! The bishop ran off with his mistress, so we’re having a huge clearance sale! These premium Holy Scriptures, originally ten gold coins each, are now all just one gold coin!” The preacher bellowed with his ragged voice, frantically hawking his wares.

“Buy, buy, buy!” The crowd, thoroughly swayed, dug into their pockets for a gold coin each to purchase a useless book. The scene was a frenzy.

Merlin’s expression twisted in disbelief, his eyebrows knitted so tightly they could’ve tied a knot. He was so furious smoke might as well have been pouring out of his ears. His sense of justice was *not* at peace—

**Dad!**

You’re using my reputation to boost sales, and the Holy Church isn’t even cutting me in?!

How much money have you secretly made off me? Not even a hundred coins as a cut…

(╬￣皿￣)

title: Chapter 7
content:
Chapter 7

Volume 2 · Chapter 7

Merlin was so broke right now that he had the urge to rob a preacher.

But his current situation was already troublesome enough. If he caused any more trouble, it wouldn’t be those cowardly adventurers coming after him—it would be the imperial army.

If things really came to that, he might not even have a place to stay in Great Britain.

Merlin shook his head and watched the uncultured ruffians snatch up the deluxe scriptures, which cost only a few copper coins each, while clutching a single gold coin. His heart bled—this money should have been his!

There was nothing he could do about it. If he had known things would turn out like this, he should have raided the Holy Church’s treasury back when he was the Demon Lord.

Lost in his daydreams, Merlin wandered into the street, hoping to scrounge up some food. He was starving.

He pulled out his leather coin pouch and shook it upside down with all his might.

Well… not a single copper coin.

Merlin’s face fell. In his mind, he cursed the evil of capitalism for exploiting the last two copper coins he had.

"Damn it, where can I get some money?"

If possible, Merlin didn’t want to dine and dash. Otherwise, he’d be in debt for life.

After standing in the marketplace for half a day, Merlin’s eyes lit up when he saw a group of street performers.

Why couldn’t he busk?

Merlin never hesitated. If he decided to do something, he did it.
