He took out his begging bowl, paired it with his broken crutch, and completed the trifecta of a beggar’s look with his disheveled appearance.

Gathering his strength, Merlin began shouting in the bustling market—

"Don’t miss this, folks! I’m new in town, penniless, and trying to make a living with my incredible skills! All you shut-ins and fujoshis out there—if you’ve got money, throw it in! If you don’t, at least cheer me on! Monthly votes work too!"

After a few shouts, a crowd of onlookers slowly gathered, their faces filled with curiosity. Who knew what kind of amazing skill this ragpicker had?

The crowd grew larger, forming a wall of people. The scene was lively.

Merlin figured the time was right. He had to make these villagers’ jaws drop and get them to hand over their money.

"Here we go~!"

The crowd focused intently, watching Merlin slightly bow, poised and ready. They couldn’t help but feel a little excited.

"Secret Technique: Rapid Side-to-Side Hop!"

Merlin’s figure blurred, leaving only a streak as he oscillated between two points at an incredible speed, stirring up gusts of wind that left the crowd stunned.

The onlookers gasped. Just the way Merlin hopped back and forth was impressive enough—they figured he must be a warrior, since their eyes couldn’t even keep up with his speed.

"How’s that? Pretty amazing, right?"

The Rapid Side-to-Side Hop was usually Merlin’s way of exercising. Since he was a shut-in, he couldn’t be bothered to go out and train, so he’d just jump around in his room, honing his "skills."

A single tear welled up in the corner of Merlin’s eye. He sighed inwardly—thank goodness his legs cramped at night, otherwise who in their right mind would use Rapid Side-to-Side Hop as exercise?

Seeing the crowd’s enthusiasm, he picked up the pace, pushing the atmosphere to its peak.

"Behold! Gravity Acceleration!"

"Forbidden Technique: Multiple Shadow Clone Jutsu!"

Merlin suddenly accelerated, his figure darting like lightning, leaving countless afterimages in the air—hundreds of them. It truly looked like shadow clones, though in reality, it was just the result of his insane speed.

If there had been any knowledgeable warriors in the crowd, they might have dropped to their knees on the spot. Even Saint-tier warriors would struggle to move this fast! Hundreds of afterimages—this kind of speed was unimaginable!

The crowd didn’t understand the intricacies, but they thought the shadow clones were incredible, and the chilling gusts of wind were thrilling. They burst into enthusiastic applause that didn’t seem to end.

Merlin felt the crowd’s mood was just right, so it was time to ask for money. He held out his begging bowl and moved closer, asking for a little tip.

"Come on, friends, give a little, give a little… whatever you can spare…"

The moment the performance ended, the crowd dispersed in a flash.

The villagers were experts at freeloading. Why would they pay?

It was fun to watch, but the second money was involved, they were out of there.

The crowd scattered, leaving the scene in shambles—a desolate and pitiful sight.

Merlin stood there, his expression awkward, utterly disheveled in the wind.

His head swelled. He had put on such a show, and not even a single tip? This was ridiculous! What had he been doing all this time?

But one spectator remained—a richly dressed little boy, sniffling with a runny nose, smacking on a lollipop as he stared blankly at Merlin.

Perhaps the brat had lost interest, because he turned to leave.

After all that effort to keep one audience member, Merlin wasn’t about to let him go so easily.

So what if he was a minor? Minors had to pay too!

Merlin slapped a hand on the kid’s head, his face dark with a forced smile.

"Hey hey hey, little friend, don’t go…"

"Give me two copper coins for a meal, and I’ll teach you how to carry mid."

(ー`′ー)

title: Chapter 8
content:
Chapter 8

Volume 2 · Chapter 8

"B-big... Uncle, I don't have any money!"

The little boy looked at Merlin with fear, the lollipop in his hand nearly dropping to the ground.

"B-big... Uncle?!"

Merlin furrowed his brows, feeling terrible all over. Lately, he hadn't been dressing up, his beard had grown a bit, and he looked scruffy, but it shouldn't make him look twenty years older, right?!

He had always thought the title "Uncle" was far from him. Being called that by a bratty kid wounded his pride.

"Little friend, do you know you just offended the world's strongest swordsman and might die instantly?"

"Eh?!" The little boy gasped in shock, his snot suddenly stretching two centimeters.

"Hey, hey, hey, suck that snot back in before it flows into your neck." Merlin couldn't bear to watch and reminded him.

The little boy *slurp* sucked the snot back in with surprising speed.

"Hey, little friend, what's your name?" Merlin asked tentatively.

"I'm Henry." The little boy trembled, answering honestly.

"Henry..." Merlin repeated, putting on a serious face. "Listen, Henry. Even though you offended me, I'm quite merciful, so I'll forgive your ignorance. But this mercy comes at a price—just... two copper coins."

Even though Merlin's mercy was extremely cheap, worth only two copper coins, the way he said it sounded reasonable. But his fierce expression and the way he rubbed his fingers together clearly made it look like a robbery!

To think he wouldn't even spare the little flowers of Great Britain—truly shameless, despicable, lewd, and detestable, as expected of the Demon Lord.

Merlin, now desperate for money, had completely abandoned his dignity. As long as he could get money for food, he would do anything, even steal noblewomen's underwear to sell. But this small village probably didn't have any nobles.

Little Henry was confused and terrified. He timidly said, "I didn't bring any money with me..."

Merlin narrowed his eyes in disbelief, thinking Henry was lying. He was dressed quite richly—how could he not have money?

Then he suddenly thought of equivalent exchange—kids usually ask for something in return.

"Oh~ I see. You want to learn my martial arts, right?"

"No, I..." Henry hesitated.

"I get it, I get it~" Merlin patted Henry's shoulder with an old-man tone. "Didn't expect you to be so greedy at such a young age. Normally, I wouldn't teach anyone, but since I'm broke right now, I can make an exception and teach you a couple of moves."

Henry's big snot started flowing again, his emotions a tangled mess.

"Have you heard of a palm technique that falls from the sky? Ahem! I mean a sword technique that falls from the sky..." Merlin pretended to be profound, though in reality, he only knew how to draw his sword and slash.

Henry shook his head, but under Merlin's smooth talk, he seemed to have a tiny spark of interest.

"It's called the Gale Sword Technique, Hassaki!" Merlin continued mystifying. "Every time you hit the enemy twice, you can cast a tornado spell. Once you lift them up, you can use the ultimate move: *Aita Kiretsu Yakeita*! How's that?"

"It... it sounds amazing..." Henry's eyes sparkled, completely taken in by Merlin. "But what exactly is the move?"

"Draw Slash..." Merlin raised an eyebrow, shamelessly naming a basic skill.

"Tsk..." Henry's mood suddenly shifted, scoffing in disdain. "What? Draw Slash? Even warrior apprentices don't bother learning that. I thought it was some amazing sword technique... How disappointing."

Merlin's face darkened, his forehead covered in black lines, his brows tightly knit as if he had lost his soul. He couldn't accept it—

Wait, wait, wait!

What was going on?

Just a moment ago, he was dumbly dripping snot.

How did he suddenly become so sharp and sarcastic?!

Did my Iaijutsu, my one-slash draw-cut style, get looked down on even by a bratty kid from another world?! That's absolutely unacceptable...

((???|||))

title: Chapter 9
content:
Chapter 9

Volume 2 · Chapter 9

"Hey, old man, don’t think I’m easy to fool just because I’m a kid!"

Little Henry curled his lip, his expression complicated.

"Here’s a grown man acting so sneaky… tsk tsk tsk…"

"Ugh!" Merlin’s breath hitched, a pang of discomfort twisting in his chest.

He knew that Iaijutsu was considered a basic, trash-tier skill in this other world, far from impressive. But he never expected even a bratty kid to look down on him. Being mocked like this was *super* embarrassing.

Merlin was starting to regret maxing out Iaijutsu to level 9999999999999999999. If he’d known it would earn him so little respect, he should’ve put points into dual-wielding, or Rurouni swordsmanship, or Mountain-Cleaving Slash, or Phantom Sword Dance—something flashy!

"Fine, fine, since you put on such a show, I’ll give you a little reward…" Little Henry reluctantly fished two lollipops out of his pocket and tossed them into Merlin’s bowl.

Merlin stared blankly at the lollipops in his bowl. "Hey, kid, my Iaijutsu is *insanely* strong."

"Yeah, right. Who’d want a useless sword skill like that?" Little Henry sniffled. "Also, old man, you’re not *that* young anymore. Get a real job." With that, he stomped off, snot dripping.

"Hey! Brat! You’ll regret not learning this! When you’re on your knees begging me, I *won’t* teach you!" Merlin muttered after the boy’s retreating figure. "And stop calling me ‘old man’! It’s ‘big brother,’ got it?!"

Little Henry glanced back just long enough to hock a glob of snot onto the ground. "Ptooey!"

"Ugh!" Merlin’s eyebrows shot up. Despite his immunity to magic, he’d just taken 10,000 points of emotional damage. In the chaotic, lawless streets, his mind was in disarray—

*What the hell?!*

What kind of *rotten* little brat was this?!

He was Merlin, the First Demon Lord of the Demon Lord Palace, the one who’d wiped out a hundred thousand Crusade Army soldiers with a single slash!

And here he was, trying to *generously* teach the strongest sword technique, only to be *mocked*…

◆

Village street.

Merlin had a lollipop in his mouth, his mood sour.

Even with a katana tucked into his obi, his disheveled appearance made him look anything but a master swordsman.

Merlin was embarrassed. He knew his strength was far from weak—after all this time in another world, he’d yet to meet anyone stronger than himself.

But because he’d foolishly maxed out a useless skill like Iaijutsu, people kept underestimating him.

In the past, it had been adventurers who looked down on him. But today, it was a *brat*. That stung just a little more than usual.

Merlin didn’t usually care about reputation, but being disrespected still grated on him.

"Sigh… how did I end up like this?"

He thought back to his days in the Demon Lord Palace—fine clothes, fine food, the good life. Nothing like now, where he was half-starved and ragged.

Sure, he’d left to break his own curse, but the enemies out here were just as pathetic.

Take the so-called "Grandmaster of Qi," for example—turned out he was just leading a bunch of epileptics in a performance. Or the "Thunder Sage" Yang, who couldn’t cast a single spell, just stood there with wires on his head pretending to summon lightning. The list went on.

Merlin’s initial excitement about the outside world had faded. The fire in his heart had dimmed, replaced by a defeatist, "eat-and-wait-for-death" attitude.

*Gurgle…*

His stomach growled again. Mealtime. He couldn’t go on without eating.

He stopped walking and spotted a restaurant ahead. The place looked decent.

Merlin raised an eyebrow, licked his dry lips, and fell into thought—

*Might as well go in and eat for free. Fill my belly first.*

After all, he was already drowning in debt—tens of thousands of gold coins’ worth.

Since he’d never pay it back anyway, what was one more meal?

Heh heh heh… Tremble, restaurant owners of Wales!

Your nightmare—the freeloading pretty boy—has arrived…

ヘ(￣ω￣ヘ)

title: Chapter 10
content:
Chapter 10

Volume 2 · Chapter 10

The village’s small restaurant.

Though it looked ordinary, far from the luxury of big cities, the food here was actually quite good.

Don’t let Merlin’s penniless state fool you—when it came to enjoying life, he savored it more than anyone.

Merlin had the refined taste of a noble, the extraordinary charm of a dashing figure, and grand ambitions, the perfect template for an otherworldly high-rich-handsome man. The only difference was… he had no money right now!

A pretty face alone couldn’t sustain a man for life. He still had some dignity and wouldn’t stoop to living off a woman’s perfume money. So, for the noble ideal of “loafing until death,” gold coins were absolutely essential—the more, the better.

Though Merlin had little money, he had the haughty attitude of the high-rich-handsome. At this moment, he sat in the middle of the restaurant, subjecting the roast suckling pig, turkey, vegetable salad, and other dishes before him to harsh criticism with his exacting standards.

The restaurant had few customers to begin with. A few middle-aged men stared at this raggedly dressed outsider with bewildered expressions, finding it quite amusing. They suspected Merlin was all talk, with no money to pay, and waited eagerly for the drama to unfold.

“This roast suckling pig is terrible—there’s still hair on it! Zero stars!”

“This turkey is no good either—it’s burnt! Zero stars!”

“The salad’s bad too—it’s not washed properly, there are bugs in it…”

“No more arguing with you—everything gets zero stars!”

Merlin looked like a beggar, yet he ate like a gourmet critic, nitpicking every dish. If not for his disheveled appearance ruining the aesthetic, a change of clean clothes would have made him comparable to a country noble—maybe even worthy of strutting down a Parisian fashion runway.

The restaurant owner, dressed in a bartender’s uniform and polishing a glass, was so infuriated by Merlin’s complaints that his mustache trembled. This was the first time he’d ever encountered such a demanding customer in the village.

The owner wanted to kick Merlin out, but seeing how expensive the dishes he’d ordered were, he decided against comping the meal. He gritted his teeth and endured, secretly thinking that if Merlin couldn’t pay, he’d beat him to a pulp to vent his frustration.

At first, the owner hadn’t wanted to serve Merlin at all. One look at his tattered clothes made it clear he was a penniless vagrant—likely here to dine and dash.

But with regulars and neighbors watching, how could he, a gentleman of the British countryside, turn away a wanderer? That would be a laughingstock!

So the owner chose to endure, and even hired the marketplace’s top enforcer to lie in wait outside. If Merlin tried to skip the bill, there’d be no mercy.

“Ugh, what kind of cake is this?! It’s awful! Not sweet at all! Back when I attended high-society parties in Manchester, their cream cakes were divine…”

Merlin’s acting was over the top, nitpicking endlessly, complaining about everything under the sun.

He boasted about Manchester’s elite society, raving about how delicious their desserts were, as if to prove he was a man of the world.

In reality, this otherworldly era was medieval, and their sweets were far inferior to those of the real world. They were only slightly better than a brick-like black bread. But to Merlin, that was still an upgrade.

Back then, Merlin had worked as a server at those parties, carrying drinks among the nobles while flirting with countless noblewomen, earning himself plenty of “emotional consultation fees.”

But he’d been caught one too many times playing the green-hatted cuckold game with Manchester’s noble lords, so he was gleefully fired and left the city.

Honestly, Merlin had loved that job as a high-society server. Good food, good drinks, a new lady every day—it was the life of a god!

How many women had Merlin been close with after leaving the Demon Lord Palace?

Rough estimate: if not 99, then at least 100. From noblewomen to tavern dancers, if they were female, he’d been with all kinds.

If Lilith knew how many vixens had approached her brother, she’d probably be troubled by the endless stream she’d have to cut down…

Merlin lived this dissolute life day by day, all while searching for a way to break his curse, fully embodying the philosophy of “loafing until death.”

Back to the matter at hand: Merlin had spent half the day badmouthing the food, yet no one so much as acknowledged him, leaving him a little embarrassed.

The reason Merlin was trashing the restaurant, of course, wasn’t because the food was bad—it was his tried-and-true dine-and-dash tactic.

Any self-respecting owner, once insulted, would kick him out without charging, achieving his goal of a free meal.

This despicable trick had worked for Merlin countless times before, without fail.

But this village’s restaurant owner was different. No matter how vile Merlin’s words were, the man endured, waiting patiently for the bill to be settled.

A cold sweat trickled down Merlin’s forehead. His heart raced. He felt full—even a little stuffed—and with that came a new problem:

Damn it!

What if I can’t pay?!

Do I have to add another debt to my name?

Then my future will be…

Nothing but days of repaying debts in another world.

(??ω?? ?)

title: Chapter 11
content:
Chapter 11

Volume 2 · Chapter 11

Not having money to pay the bill was just a small matter.

If Merlin relied on brute force, even if every powerful figure in Great Britain blocked his path, they wouldn’t stand a chance. But the problem was that using force to dine and dash was just too shameless—no skill involved, and utterly humiliating.

Merlin might be penniless, but he wasn’t about to lose his dignity. He still had his pride, so he refused to do something so disgraceful.

What? You say he didn’t mind cuckolding others? Please, let’s be professional here—that’s called comforting women, the sacred duty of an incubus.

Far from shameful, in the demon race, it was actually a noble act, like a gentleman graciously yielding to a lady.

Merlin racked his brain, desperately trying to figure out how to get through this, when he overheard a few middle-aged men gnawing on lamb legs nearby, casually chatting—

“Heard Martha’s tavern is hiring male servers lately?”

“Seriously? Guess her husband’s away at war, and she can’t stand the loneliness at home.”

“All the bachelors in the village are apparently fired up about it, but every guy who applied got turned down.”

“Tch, she’s just a ** woman, and she still wants to act all virtuous.”

“Though I’ll say, Martha’s got a nice round ass. Bet it’d feel great to grab.”

“No doubt! Too bad she had a son—if it were a daughter, her doorstep would’ve been worn out by now.”

…

*Martha’s tavern?*

Merlin furrowed his brow, filtering out the vulgar chatter and focusing only on the key detail: *tavern hiring male servers.* The solution was suddenly clear.

I’ve got a new job!

The crude conversation between those two men had pointed him toward the light. The path ahead was obvious—he needed this job, had to get it, or else his pockets would stay emptier than his face, and that was a disaster.

A smile unconsciously spread across Merlin’s face. His current predicament finally had a way out. If it came with free meals, lodging, *and* a wage? Absolute bliss!

As a man with no money, no home, and no prospects, he could only take on odd jobs like this. The white-collar types in merchant banks and guilds wouldn’t hire someone like him—they preferred candidates with higher education.

“Sir, are you finished?” the restaurant owner couldn’t help but ask, practically vibrating with impatience to collect payment.

“Nope, not done yet. Stop rushing me—do you treat all your customers like this?” Merlin replied shamelessly, picking up a chicken bone from the table and rolling it around in his mouth.

“Take your time,” the owner said with a forced smile, thinking, *We’ll settle this properly once you can’t pay.*

Merlin scratched his head. Being broke was agony. He’d been waiting for the owner to go to the bathroom so he could slip away unnoticed.

But two hours had passed, and the man showed no sign of needing to relieve himself. His bladder must’ve been the size of a lake.

This was driving Merlin up the wall. He was itching to go apply for that job—and now he really needed to pee.

“Ladies and gentlemen, the fifty-seventh race at the Royal Racetrack is now open! All bettors without a ticket have three minutes to choose their horse. Please make your selections quickly.”

A soft, feminine voice rang out, catching Merlin’s attention.

It was a magic projector powered by a beast core, broadcasting a live feed from Great Britain’s racetrack. In short, it was horse racing gambling—a game where luck could make you rich overnight.

Merlin was already familiar with horse race betting. It felt strangely comforting to find it existed in this other world too.

Over the past year, he’d racked up a mountain of debt—so much that repaying it was impossible. Like many others at the end of their rope, he’d turned to gambling, hoping to strike it rich overnight through the races.

Merlin wasn’t just a hot-headed gambler who loved spouting conspiracy theories about the racetrack—he also had the worst luck imaginable. To this day, he hadn’t won a single copper coin. Worse, he had a terrible habit: he always bet everything he had, going all-in every time.

He didn’t see this as reckless. He called it *gambling momentum*—you needed the resolve to bet it all if you wanted to win big!

This bad habit had only driven him deeper into poverty. The moment he got his hands on any wages, they’d vanish at the racetrack.

Merlin felt a flicker of excitement. Today, at rock bottom, maybe Lady Luck was finally smiling on him.

Who knew? Maybe he could turn his life around with this race, pay off his debts, and become a millionaire from the slums. The thought was *thrilling.*

He reached into his underwear and fished around for a while before pulling out his betting slip—exactly for the fifty-seventh race.

Since his clothes were ragged and had no pockets, Merlin had stashed the slip in his underwear. For a gambler, a betting slip was more precious than life itself.

“Number 6…”

Merlin muttered, his hand trembling slightly as he held the slip, his heart pounding—

*What the hell?!*

Fortune rotates, right? Was it finally his turn?

His left eyelid had been twitching nonstop all day. Could this be a sign he was about to hit the jackpot?

Come on, you old nag Number 6—don’t let me down!

Whether I claw my way back from the gutter or not *all depends on you…*

(??ω?? ?)

title: Chapter 12
content:
Chapter 12

Volume 2 · Chapter 12

Merlin pinned his hopes of turning his life around on this betting slip, praying that his "unparalleled" luck would pull off the ultimate comeback.

He was certain he would win today—every omen pointed to his greatness. His left eyelid twitched wildly, the number 6 was his lucky charm, and good fortune was practically riding on his face. How could he possibly lose?!

This betting slip had an extraordinary origin. Gentlemen in Great Britain had a habit of deliberately dropping spare change in parks, allowing the needy to pick up a few copper coins to buy bread. But Merlin was different. He spent an entire night scouring the park where vagrants gathered, collecting over a hundred copper coins—enough for one silver coin—which he used to buy a betting slip from the Royal Racecourse.

Merlin was the textbook gambler: he’d rather starve than miss a bet. His reasoning was simple—

The odds may be slim, but this is my only chance to turn my life around. As long as there’s a chance, no matter how small, it’s worth the gamble!

Hmm, every gambler thinks the same way, and most end up losing their pants.

The magic projector live-streamed the racecourse, where twenty-four majestic horses were penned in stalls, ready to bolt. Scantily clad dancers performed above, and the crowd buzzed with excitement.

Merlin clutched his betting slip, eyes locked on the brown horse number 6, silently praying, *Dad, give me strength, old iron 6! Don’t let me down!*

"Sir, could you settle your bill first?" The restaurant owner still worried Merlin wouldn’t pay. One look at him, and it was clear he was a gambler.

"What’s the rush?" Merlin already felt like a millionaire. His tone was brimming with confidence as he waved his betting slip. "I’m about to become a millionaire. Show some respect—this meal’s on me, and once I win, this whole restaurant will be mine."

The owner forced a dry laugh, his mustache trembling. *All gamblers are the same, dreaming of flipping their fate overnight.*

Two sleazy uncles sipping beer nearby seemed to be into horse racing too and struck up a conversation.

"Number 4 is a sure bet this time."

"Nah, number 8’s the real deal. It’s got a high win rate."

"Shut your damn traps! Number 6 is the absolute beast!" Merlin snapped, cursing. Sure enough, he had the foul temper of a gambler.

"Seriously? Number 6 has been having stomach issues lately. It slows down halfway through the race." The pale-faced uncle grinned.

"Yeah, like it ate a bunch of croton seeds. Its backside’s like a little rocket—*pffft pffft pffft*..." The red-faced uncle’s mouth stretched to his ears.

"Screw your banana peels! Number 6 is definitely juiced today. It’ll make a comeback on the track, and if it doesn’t take first, I’ll livestream myself eating shit!" Merlin’s head suddenly sprouted a flag of defiance, ready to test the curse of *"nothing bad happens if you don’t act like an idiot."*

The two uncles sipped their beer, shaking their heads and laughing silently, waiting for Merlin to livestream himself eating shit.

The live broadcast of the race was about to begin. The straight track was cleared.

"Royal Racecourse, Race Fifty-Seven, starting soon! This event is exclusively sponsored by the London Sherlock Holmes Detective Agency!" the hostess announced energetically.

*Roll, gay-sponsored race, hurry up and start!*

Merlin was so anxious he was sweating. He felt like a student waiting for his report card, heart pounding. For every gambler, the wait before the race was pure torture—every second felt like an eternity.

"Race starts!!!"

With the crack of a starting pistol, the stable gates swung open.

Twenty-four fierce horses neighed and bolted down the straight track at full speed.

And our protagonist, Merlin—

Would he ride this high-stakes gamble to flip his life from rags to riches?

title: Chapter 13
content:
Chapter 13

Volume 2 · Chapter 13

The live broadcast of the race was unusually intense.

Twenty-four horses charged forward wildly, restless and agitated.

The commentator delivered his passionate commentary with rapid-fire London accent—

"Look! Now striding gracefully toward the judges' stand is horse number 6 from the Midland Plains! It's full of vigor, soaring in spirit like an eagle poised for flight. This is a horse that dares to strive, brimming with youthful energy. It will fight with unyielding determination and an indomitable spirit on the royal racetrack, charging forward bravely to achieve excellence!"

Fuck off! What the hell is this? A damn sports opening ceremony speech?! Give me a proper commentary!

Merlin was so furious his teeth were clenched, the veins on his forehead throbbing. He started slamming the table, the loud bangs echoing.

"Damn horse number 6! Learn from Violent Moto and kick horse number 4 in the ass! Knock it down with one hoof!"

The two beer-drinking uncles exchanged complicated looks. They felt Merlin was unusually aggressive when gambling, as if he might flip the table at any moment. Truly, he was a hot-headed gambler, completely different from his usual refined demeanor.

No matter how loudly Merlin shouted, his voice couldn't reach the racetrack.

The restaurant owner watched the trembling table, heartbroken. It had been bought just last month and was already being ruined.

Merlin's eyes were wide with rage, glued to the live broadcast. When it came to gambling, he was like this—wishing he could replace the horses and run a few laps himself. He was absolutely livid.

And horse number 6 really was a disappointment. Halfway through the race, it suddenly squirted diarrhea from its backside, probably from eating something bad. It ran slower and slower, eventually just strolling around the track.

Just as the two uncles said, horse number 6's diarrhea made it look like it had a tiny rocket up its ass, but it had no effect—it only got slower.

Merlin's face darkened. He knew he had lost, not even getting a consolation prize. Instead, he had lost a silver coin.

His whole body trembled with anger, teeth grinding loudly. Unable to hold back, he exploded into a string of curses, showcasing his terrible temper at its peak—

"Fuck me!!!"

"Your sister's three laps of bullshit!"

"Horse number 6 definitely ate croton seeds before the race!"

"Rigged! Absolute rigging! The Royal Racetrack is pushing its luck!"

"The whole world is stopping me from turning my luck around! Damn capitalism, always exploiting me! If I get the chance, I'll take you all down!"

"Old man's fucking Zhang Sanfeng monk Taiji fist Taiji swordplay mighty sailor Pikachu Digimon fat snake monster..."

Merlin's old habit flared up again. Whenever he lost a bet, he'd start hating on society, cursing all of Great Britain with wild conspiracy theories and discriminatory rants.

His actions were just as intense as his words. The table was pounded so hard it clanged, as if he might grab a sword and take revenge on society at any moment.

The restaurant owner was deeply worried, afraid this lunatic might go berserk. He quietly picked up a kitchen knife, ready to fight for his life.

The two beer-drinking uncles couldn't stop smirking, feeling Merlin's loss was entirely expected.

After a while—

Merlin sat in his chair, staring at the mess on the table with a look of utter despair, seemingly having calmed down.

Fortunately, Merlin's gambling frenzy didn't last long. After a short burst of rage, he would return to his senses and face reality.

But the problem remained: he had lost the bet. Now there was no hope of paying the bill. Did that mean he had to use force to dine and dash?

Please, no. I, the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace, actually doing something so low-class? That would tarnish my reputation.

Merlin thought a lot, but in reality, what reputation did he have? The Holy Church had already taken it all and embellished it to swindle money.

The restaurant owner wiped the table, eyes fixed firmly on Merlin, waiting for him to pay.

Merlin broke out in a cold sweat under that gaze, feeling disrespected. It hurt his pride.

He thought for a moment and decided he couldn't resort to violence—it was beneath him. He had to rely on his wit to get out of this.

"Snap!" Merlin pretended to snap his fingers. "Check, please!"

The owner wiped his hands and walked over suspiciously, wondering if Merlin actually had the money.

"Hello, sir. That'll be two gold coins."

"So expensive?!" Merlin felt he hadn't eaten that much. The owner was treating him like a sucker.

"The turkey and roast suckling pig are our specialties," the restaurant owner explained.

"Hmm, they were alright. The taste was just average." Merlin, shamelessly, changed the subject. "Actually, I think your restaurant has a nice atmosphere, but it's not very popular. Why is that?"

"That's because of our location. It's too far back from the marketplace," the owner answered honestly, knowing the situation well.

"No, no, no, that's not the main reason." Merlin shook his head, feigning profundity. "Your restaurant lacks *moe* elements~"

"*Moe* elements?" The owner was completely confused.

"Yes. Look at maid cafes, catgirl cafes—they all have their own *moe* elements. Some have this sauce, some have that sauce. High society has bunny girls with their alluring black stockings and legs. Those are all *moe* elements." Merlin spread his hands in explanation.

"Are you saying, sir..." The owner seemed somewhat interested.

"Your restaurant needs to add *moe* elements. Do you know what *tsundere* is?" Merlin said with a straight face.

"*Tsun...dere*?" The owner was thoroughly puzzled. He didn't understand at all, but he felt there was some truth in Merlin's words. Every shop should have its own unique charm.

"That's right, *tsundere*. A *tsundere* is someone who says the opposite of what they mean. Let me teach you. For example, what do you want to do right now?" Merlin's eyes were serious, like a devout missionary.

"Sir, please pay your bill." The owner answered honestly.

"Exactly. But if you were a *tsundere*, you wouldn't say that. Instead, you'd say, 'I-I won't let you pay the bill!'" Merlin slightly imitated the tone, then urged, "Try it. It'll be great for your business. It can attract a huge crowd."

"I... I won't let you pay the bill!" The owner, a middle-aged man in his forties, suddenly sounded effeminate, his mustache trembling.

Merlin revealed a sinister smile, looking extremely wicked and ominous, his demonic nature on full display.

That's right—this was all a scheme. As long as the owner said he didn't want the money, it was settled.

Merlin stood up and headed for the exit. Turning back, he nodded and said—

"Alright, as you wish. I won't pay."

"Thanks for the meal. Sayonara!"

(-`ω-)?

title: Chapter 14
content:
Chapter 14

Volume 2 · Chapter 14

The restaurant owner froze for three seconds before snapping back to reality—he realized he’d been played. Damn, this guy was such a tsundere! He just wanted to trick him into saying "no charge" himself.

"Someone! Stop him!"

The owner threw his towel onto the table. There were two things he despised most about running a restaurant. The second was credit, and the first was dining and dashing. The former still had a chance of recovery, but the latter was just outright freeloading.

The restaurant door was kicked open. The marketplace’s top enforcer had been waiting for this moment for a long time. At the owner’s call, he rushed in eagerly.

"Boss, I’m here! Where’s that little thief who tried to dine and dash? I’ll teach him a lesson—make him sell a kidney to pay the bill!"

The marketplace’s top enforcer was a group of mercenaries just scraping by, with no special abilities—just hired muscle earning a living.

This one was built like a rock, his muscles bulging under his skin, his shiny bald head gleaming as if polished with wax. He looked intimidating, but Merlin only saw a low-tier warrior—nothing more than a worthless small fry.

Of course, "small fry" was only in Merlin’s eyes. In this small village, a low-tier warrior was already impressive. Countless people couldn’t even cultivate a hint of fighting spirit or magic, doomed to live as ordinary folk.

"It’s... it’s him!" The restaurant owner pointed at Merlin, his little mustache trembling with rage. "I’ve run this place for over a decade, and this is the first time someone’s tried to dine and dash!"

"I didn’t dine and dash. Didn’t you say it was free?" Merlin shamelessly retorted, with no intention of paying.

"Who said it was free?! Don’t try your little tricks on me. Just pay the bill, and you can leave safely." The owner declared solemnly, as if he didn’t want trouble—just the money.

"Old man here ate and drank for free with his wisdom. Why should I pay?" Merlin said coolly, drawing his tachi. The blade was dark and battered, looking more like a broken fire poker. "Don’t force me to defend myself. Even I get scared when I draw this thing."

"HAHAHAHAHA—"

The enforcer roared with laughter, sensing no trace of power from Merlin—just an ordinary man.

With a broken stick tucked into his belt, he looked nothing like a swordsman—more like a country bumpkin.

The enforcer didn’t take Merlin seriously at all. He figured he was just a con artist used to scamming free meals.

"So you’re calling that fire poker a sword? And you’re a swordsman?"

"A *sword master*," Merlin corrected. He didn’t like being called a swordsman—he preferred *sword master*, because it sounded lone and wandering. And that was cool.

"Then, esteemed Sword Master, might I ask your noble name?" The enforcer sneered, mocking Merlin.

"Just a nameless nobody. Not worth mentioning. Now move aside—don’t block the way!" Merlin waved his hand, thinking that if things escalated, he might lose control, and the entire village could vanish from the map of Great Britain.

"Hmph!" The enforcer stood like a wall, blocking the door, refusing to let Merlin pass. "A man who won’t even give his name dares call himself a sword master? That’s a joke. I’ve seen plenty like you—just a few cheap tricks, out here swindling people."

"Emmmm..." Merlin’s expression twisted. He really didn’t want to waste time on a low-tier nobody, but the man wasn’t letting him leave.

"I am Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson, a low-tier warrior, a top-tier mercenary. I take all kinds of jobs—from debt collector to unclogging toilets. And if you’re bored, I can even help look after your wife." The enforcer flexed his muscles, showing off as if to intimidate Merlin into backing down.

"Oh, I don’t know what’s going on, but you just want a fight, right?" Merlin stood with his hands behind his back, then used one hand to beckon the enforcer forward, a clear provocation—

"Come on, then. I’ll even let you use one hand."

"My time is precious."

ㄟ(▔ ,▔)ㄏ

title: Chapter 15
content:
Chapter 15

Volume 2 · Chapter 15

The gold-ranked enforcer glared down at Merlin, his veins bulging with displeasure at Merlin’s blatant disrespect. Normally, any puny weakling who saw his towering frame and the oppressive aura of his lower-tier battle energy would either cower in fear or meekly pay their bill.

But Merlin was different—he seemed completely unfazed by the display of strength. This infuriated the enforcer. These days, even a peasant with no magic or battle energy dared to talk back to him? Unbelievable.

"Kid, you’ve got some nerve! You dare talk big to me, Giant Stone Johnson, even after I said I’d take you on with one hand? Impressive~ *very* impressive~"

The restaurant owner shook his head. Merlin clearly had no sense of self-preservation. How could a powerless scavenger like him possibly fight a lower-tier warrior? He should just pay up and leave. If he ended up with broken arms or legs, it wouldn’t be worth it.

"Hurry up and make your move. If you’re not going to fight, then step aside. Don’t block the way." Merlin sighed, unimpressed by the petty provocation. He just wanted to finish this quickly and go apply for that new job.

"You insolent little brat! Today, I’ll let you taste the might of my legendary iron fists!"

The enforcer lunged forward, his sandbag-sized fist hurtling toward Merlin’s scrawny frame, wreathed in faint battle energy and cutting through the air with a sharp *whoosh*. He held nothing back—this was a full-force strike meant to crush this backwater nobody into submission, to make him fear his power.

Merlin stared at the incoming fist with a blank expression. Sure, it was bigger than his own head, but it posed no threat whatsoever. He wasn’t even slightly interested.

So, with one hand, Merlin casually caught the enforcer’s fist and said flatly, "Not bad on the intimidation front. Out of 100, I’ll give you a 6..."

"What?!"
The enforcer’s face twisted in shock. His all-out strike had been stopped effortlessly. There was no fluctuation of power, no surge of energy—so how had this scruffy swordsman deflected his attack so easily? What in the hells was this guy? A mid-tier warrior? But that was impossible—mid-tier warriors were prized as elite guards for nobles. What would one be doing in a backwater village like this?

"Was that your best shot? Pretty underwhelming..." Merlin smirked, switching into full mockery mode.

"Johnson! What are you doing?! Don’t you want your payment? Hurry up and take down this deadbeat who’s trying to dine and dash!" The restaurant owner couldn’t stand it anymore and barked his orders as the employer.

After all, as the saying went, amateurs watched the spectacle while experts watched the technique. The owner couldn’t tell the difference in strength—he just assumed Johnson was going easy. How could a nobody with no magic or battle energy possibly block a lower-tier warrior’s punch?

Sweat beaded on the enforcer’s forehead as he cautiously asked, "May I ask, sir... what is your esteemed name?"

"Just a nobody." Merlin waved his hand dismissively, unwilling to reveal his identity.

A nobody? Really?

Doubt gnawed at the enforcer. Lower-tier warriors were common, but the higher you went, the rarer they became. Mid-tier warriors held status comparable to minor nobles, high-tier warriors were on par with great nobles, and the legendary Saint-tier... well, they were said to pose a threat to royal authority itself.

For Merlin to so easily block his punch, he had to be at least mid-tier, right?

But if he was mid-tier, how could he be a nobody?

The enforcer’s already slow mind short-circuited. How was Merlin stopping his attacks without any detectable power fluctuations? Maybe it was some kind of one-use magic item that nullified attacks, like a decoy golem or something similar.

The enforcer eyed Merlin’s suspiciously shady demeanor and became even more convinced he was being tricked. Merlin must be using some kind of magic tool to hide his true strength, pretending to be mysterious just to scare him off.

"Ha! I’ve got it—you’re trying to scam me, aren’t you?"

"Huh?" Merlin’s mind filled with nothing but question marks.

"Cut the bullshit! I’ve seen plenty of scammers like you—country bumpkins who mooch off others! If a kid’s cough won’t go away, a good beating will fix it!"

The enforcer launched into a rapid flurry of punches, each one infused with lower-tier battle energy, fierce and powerful. Each strike sent gusts of wind in its wake, creating a storm of afterimages.

"Oraoraoraoraoraoraora..."

title: Chapter 16
content:
Chapter 16

Volume 2 · Chapter 16

The golden enforcer's fists rained down like a storm, each strike laced with faint battle energy, as if he wanted to pulverize Merlin with boulder-sized punches. To onlookers, it looked like the Heavenly Horse Meteor Fist.

Merlin had wanted to play along and shout a string of "Muda!" but decided that was too cliché, so he switched to a more crowd-pleasing line—

"********……!"

Merlin genuinely let the golden enforcer land a few hits, but every strike, no matter how desperate, was effortlessly deflected with a single hand.

The enforcer grew increasingly alarmed. *What kind of magic tool is this?* he wondered. *A tool that nullifies all attacks indefinitely?*

A creeping unease settled in his chest. Merlin showed no fluctuations in power, yet his strength seemed bottomless. His calm, unreadable expression only deepened the mystery.

The golden enforcer refused to give up. If he couldn’t even beat a random villager, he might as well smash his head against a wall and die. So, as if his inner universe had exploded, he redoubled his efforts. His fists flew faster, the shockwaves from each strike growing more intense.

"Uh… I already said it’s useless," Merlin muttered, tilting his head slightly, his mood a mix of amusement and exasperation. Over the past year, he’d run into plenty of idiots like this—most of them adventurers.

These adventurers, when facing Merlin, would always experience a shifting illusion, one that evolved over time:

*Hmph! I can one-shot this trash villager!*

↓

*What the—? He’s got some skill! But I can still go toe-to-toe!*

↓

*What the hell?! He’s this strong?!*

↓

*I can’t win… I can’t win… Mama, I want to go home! Waaah!*

↓

*After all these years of training, what was the point? I can’t even beat a random villager… Do I even have a reason to live? Life is meaningless…*

Almost everyone who fought Merlin went through these stages, one after another. And if they stubbornly refused to back down? Well, the grass on their graves would already be three meters tall.

Their clash sent gusts of cold wind sweeping through the small restaurant. The golden enforcer’s relentless, powerful fists and Merlin’s effortless one-handed deflections created a surprisingly intense spectacle.

The two old men who had been watching the whole time were now stunned, beer spilled all over the floor, forgotten.

As for the restaurant owner, he had long since ducked under the counter, trembling like a leaf. His mustache quivered at the same frequency as… well, you get the idea. He clutched a plate over his head, terrified of stray damage, thinking: *Who the hell is this trash collector? He’s fighting the Rock like it’s nothing! He’s definitely not normal! Can I just forget about the bill? Please, don’t wreck my shop… Waaah…*

The golden enforcer had been attacking for ages, and still hadn’t landed a single hit on Merlin.

His expression was blank, his breathing ragged, sweat pouring off him like a broken faucet. *How is this possible?* he thought. *I gave it my all, and I can’t even graze his hair! The gap in power is outrageous!*

"Done yet?" Merlin asked, not a drop of sweat on him, grinning as he tested the waters. "In turn-based combat, shouldn’t it be my turn now? Have you ever heard of a fist technique that erupts from the ground?"

"C-Could it be… the… the *Shoryuken*?!" The golden enforcer’s face twisted in terror, his legs shaking uncontrollably.

"Tsk tsk tsk, wrong answer, you idiot," Merlin said, lightning-fast delivering an uppercut that soared into the air and connected with the enforcer’s chin—

"HOU~YOKU~!"

(Street Fighter players will get it—Shoryuken sounds like "Houyoku" in Japanese.)

title: Chapter 17
content:
Chapter 17

Volume 2 · Chapter 17

The gold-ranked thug lost consciousness the moment he was struck, blacked out, and his body defied gravity, shooting upward before smashing through the ceiling and dangling there.

Merlin clapped his hands once, sighed, and thought that he had taken care of a nuisance—now he could finally leave in peace, right?

But then his gaze casually landed on the gold-ranked thug’s money pouch at his waist, and an idea struck him.

Since he dared to fight me, he’s an enemy now. I suppose I’ll have to reluctantly take this money for myself~

Merlin, with practiced ease, snatched the pouch and checked its contents: two gold coins, a few silvers, and some coppers.

“Tsk! A pauper…”

Merlin curled his lip, then immediately felt a pang of self-loathing. How could he, of all people, have the nerve to call someone else a pauper?!

He pulled out two gold coins and shot a glance at the restaurant owner, instantly terrifying the man out of his wits.

Merlin looked at the pouch he had just stolen and hesitated.

“Don’t kill me! Don’t kill me! Spare me, good sir! We live in a harmonious society—we must reason with each other!”

“I don’t have a habit of slaughtering the innocent, you know.” Merlin twisted his mouth in exasperation and tossed the two gold coins onto the counter. “There’s your meal money. And don’t you dare put a bounty on my head, okay~”

The restaurant owner watched Merlin’s retreating back, then looked at the two gleaming gold coins on the counter and couldn’t help but speak up.

“Wai—wait! Could it be that you are the legendary…”

“Hmph! So I’ve been recognized again, huh? As expected, being this handsome means I can’t stay low-key anywhere…” Merlin stopped in the doorway, flicked his golden hair with a confident flourish, as if to say that his silky locks were this self-assured. “That’s right, I am the legendary Great Demon Lord of the—”

“The good-for-nothing, freeloading pretty boy of Scotland!”

Merlin staggered, nearly tripping over his own feet, his face a picture of disbelief.

He had been about to announce his grand and imposing title as Demon Lord, but the restaurant owner had beaten him to the punch with the one nickname he least wanted to hear.

What the hell?! Why is my “pretty boy” reputation louder than my Demon Lord’s mighty name?! That’s not right!

“You’re that legendary man from Scotland who kept cuckolding noble lords, gallivanting through the flowers, a wild stallion no lady could tame!” The restaurant owner knew quite a bit about Merlin’s past. “So you finally couldn’t cut it in Scotland and came to Wales to cause trouble, huh?!”

Merlin knew his reputation wasn’t great—back in Scotland, people were so worried their wives might have an affair with him that they’d even formed an anti-cuckold army. But having it all laid out like this still stung.

What made him even angrier was that he hadn’t even done anything! Just chatting with women was enough to earn him the label of a pretty boy. That was just terrible!

Actually, Merlin’s reputation among women was pretty good—they affectionately called him the “late-night confidant.”

Of course, Merlin had no idea about this embarrassing nickname. If he did, he might have died from shame and rage. He was just comforting the ladies, not serving as some noblewomen’s plaything!

Merlin’s face darkened, black lines crawling across his forehead as he gripped his demon sword and coldly declared—

“Shut up, **Dad.”

“If you say one more word, I won’t be able to resist drawing my blade.”

“This old man is a lonely, aloof, formidable, unparalleled wandering swordmaster!”

“Not some despicable, useless, lecherous, freeloading pretty boy!”

(╬￣皿￣)

title: Chapter 18
content:
Chapter 18

Volume 2 · Chapter 18

Merlin left the restaurant in low spirits, emptying the stolen money pouch into his palm to examine its contents.

Two gold coins had already gone to pay for the meal, leaving only a few silver coins and a handful of copper coins.

Merlin looked at his tattered clothes, his disheveled hair, and finally ran a hand over his scruffy, unkempt chin.

He decided to go to that Martha’s Tavern for an interview and pick up some odd jobs to earn a little extra cash and get by for a few days.

Since it was an interview, he needed to clean himself up. Being too unkempt would leave a bad impression and cost him the job.

With his mind made up, Merlin set off to find a barbershop, a bathhouse, and a tailor…

◆

A few hours later.

Merlin shook his money pouch and found it empty again, but at least he had finally tidied himself up.

After a bath, a haircut, and a shave, he looked radiant—worthy of the pretty-boy gigolo from Scotland who had bedded countless noblewomen.

With his golden hair and handsome features, he was undeniably eye-catching. If he put on a wig and walked into a women’s bathhouse, no one would scream—he’d just be taken for a flat-chested girl, and in a harmonious atmosphere, everyone would happily scrub each other’s backs.

Especially with that roguish grin always on his face, fully showcasing his incubus charm. It sent the hearts of several young women and housewives nearby racing, their faces flushing red. When had such a handsome man come to the village?

As for his old tattered clothes, those had long been thrown away.

Gritting his teeth, he spent a good chunk of his silver coins on new clothes and shoes.

A white shirt, a brown jacket, and a pair of stylish short boots.

Clothes make the man, and just like that, Merlin transformed into a minor landowner.

Of course, he didn’t want to dwell on the craftsmanship of this other world—compared to modern standards, there was still a gap. For example, those short boots would definitely hurt his feet if he wore them for too long.

But Merlin had worked as a male escort in high society before and had seen how nobles ate and dressed well. Such was the evil of capitalism—class differences were a real thing.

The reason Merlin was willing to spend his gambling winnings on new clothes to clean himself up was simple: you have to spend money to make money.

From his experience with women, since the boss was a woman, first impressions were crucial. He absolutely shouldn’t pull some “I’m different from the crowd, above such mundane concerns” nonsense.

That kind of act might catch her attention, but it wouldn’t make her like him. If it actually worked, Merlin would kneel and beg to be her apprentice, starting from level zero in the art of seduction.

To win over a female boss, first impressions were key. He needed to present himself as clean and sharp, pique her interest, and then make her feel something for him. Only then would the job be as good as his.

So Merlin was ready. With the mindset of a gold-tier female psychological consultant, he could take down the boss in minutes, work for a few months to earn some cash, then leave to search Wales for someone powerful enough to help him break his curse.

Even though Merlin had completely changed his appearance, the demon sword Banri Garan still looked painfully out of place, like a blackened fire poker stuck in his belt.

He had no choice—it was the only weapon he was comfortable with, and it was vital for keeping him alive. He had to use it, even if it was ugly. Still, he shifted the blade to his back to keep it from ruining his chances with the boss—

Ah, damn it! He meant his plan to *win over* the boss!

He was a decent man—how could he always be thinking such impure thoughts?

Of course, if any girls needed emotional comfort, they were more than welcome to come find him.

Out of humanitarian concern, they could always have a deep, *intimate* exchange of ideas.

(Fake) innocent face!

title: Chapter 19
content:
Chapter 19

Volume 2 · Chapter 19

Merlin, after much inquiry, finally arrived at the rumored tavern run by Martha, called "Moonlight Tavern."

emmmm...

Merlin couldn't help but frown, thinking the name sounded like a brothel.

To be honest, Merlin still didn't like working in such places. He had done similar jobs before, having to deal with too many women, and he simply couldn't handle them all—it was exhausting.

No matter which one he neglected, they would cry and make a scene, and then his pay would be docked.

Come on, he wasn’t a wet nurse. Could those female customers stop acting like they were starving for attention?

But since he was here, he might as well go in and take a look. If the job only required handling five or six women, he could manage.

But if it meant dealing with more than ten at once, forget it. He only had one mouth—he couldn’t possibly keep them all happy.

Merlin took a deep breath and pushed the door open...

As soon as he entered, he noticed the place was quite crowded. All sorts of people were gathered here—mercenaries, villagers, peddlers, merchants—all dressed in rather plain, commoner-style clothing. The atmosphere felt chaotic, a real mix of characters.

"Boss lady! Two ice beers and a rum!"

A burly, scruffy-bearded man raised his empty glass and shouted toward the solid wooden counter.

"Two ice beers and a rum, coming right up!"

A soft, mature-sounding voice replied from behind the counter.

Then, a young woman in a mid-length dress, with brown hair curled at the ends and a white apron tied around her waist, stepped out. She skillfully carried three large glasses and distributed them to the customers.

Merlin felt this woman had a certain mature charm—she was probably already married, a housewife, maybe even with a child.

Her features were indeed quite pretty, like a newlywed neighbor in her late twenties, already carrying the elegance of a young married woman.

Merlin had seen plenty of glamorous, seductively dressed young married women before, but this kind of slightly youthful freshness was a nice change.

After serving the drinks, the woman wiped her hands on her apron and only then noticed Merlin standing by the door. She looked slightly startled, then forced a professional smile.

"New face, huh? A traveler? Come in, come in, take a seat. What’ll it be? Rum? Beer? We’ve got whiskey too."

"Ah, no, no—I heard the owner, Martha, is hiring a male server, so I came to apply." Merlin did his best to sound polite, not wanting to come off as a lazy freeloading bum.

"HAHAHA! Another one lured in by Martha’s married-woman charm, huh? How many is this now? Thirty-something? No way you’ll succeed."

A hearty, boisterous man drinking beer blurted out, instantly triggering a wave of laughter and lewd whistles, as if they were all egging him on.

"Tsk!" Merlin furrowed his brows. He had seen his fair share of bar fights and wouldn’t mind slamming these guys’ heads under the table.

"Don’t... don’t mind them, they’re just joking." The woman forced a laugh, her face a little flushed, then gently said, "I’m Martha. If you’re here to apply, follow me."

"Eh!?" Merlin froze for a moment. He had assumed the boss would be a plump middle-aged woman, not someone so young.

Recalling the crude remarks from those uncles in the tavern just now, Merlin couldn’t help but ponder—

Young and beautiful.

Raising a child alone at home.

Husband away serving in the military.

No wonder there were so many rumors.

This was practically the classic setup for a rural smut story...
