title: Chapter 20
content:
Chapter 20

Volume 2 · Chapter 20

In a small private room of the tavern.

Merlin looked left and right.

He couldn’t shake the feeling that this room was designed for… paid companionship.

The place was drenched in pink tones, completely different from the minimalist style outside.

Merlin stroked his chin, unable to help but doubt—was this really a legitimate place to work?

“Sorry to keep you waiting. The shop gets pretty busy around noon.”

Martha entered, her face carrying an apologetic smile.

“It’s fine, I didn’t wait too long.” Merlin replied with a smile, straightening his posture like the perfect model of a five-star youth.

“I don’t have much experience with interviews myself. Most applicants are from the village, but let’s follow international conventions—start with a self-introduction…” Martha seemed even more nervous than Merlin.

Here it comes!

The highlight of any interview—the self-introduction!

A moment that breaks the backs of countless shut-ins!

A battlefield where even the bravest of socially anxious warriors fall!

But for me, it’s just a walk in the park…

Merlin took a deep breath, as if charging up a special move, then suddenly opened his eyes wide and launched into his spiel—

“I’m Merlin, a fresh graduate from the Royal Academy of Great Britain. I’m an expert in all kinds of sales techniques. I’m a kind person—I never dine and dash, I don’t have affairs with boss’s wives, I’d never do something shameless like cuckolding someone, and I’ve never been wanted by the law or buried in debt. In my view, the sales industry can be summed up in eight words: *persuade gently, persist firmly, don’t force it.* So, since your shop needs a waiter, I’m the perfect fit. Oh, and I’ve served in the Royal Navy, worked as the queen’s bodyguard in the palace, and even pacified pirates in the English Channel…”

By the end, Merlin couldn’t stop himself, his boasts spiraling further and further out of control, escalating all the way to claiming he’d once been an imperial general.

A chorus of boos erupted from the imaginary audience, but he paid no mind. Once he got going, it was like he’d downed a can of energy drink—there was no stopping him.

Merlin knew the secrets of acing interviews—how else had he landed so many jobs before? The trick was three words: *bullshit hard.* Blow the interviewer’s mind until they questioned their own existence, until they were left groveling on the floor. Who was going to fact-check his past anyway? The more he exaggerated, the more impressive he seemed, and the higher his salary would be.

Merlin rambled on for a good half hour before finally pausing to take a sip of water.

“Huh?” Martha forced a stiff smile, a cold sweat rolling down her forehead. The first part of his spiel had been fine, but the latter half had been completely incomprehensible. “Th-this… you’re *that* impressive?”

“Of course! So, what do you think?” Merlin grinned, then subtly deployed his signature pick-up artist skills, letting his hand casually drift onto Martha’s. It was soft. “Madam, I hope you’ll give me serious consideration.”

Martha’s face flushed red. There was something strangely compelling in Merlin’s gaze, making her heart race unnaturally.

She yanked her hand back in a flash, her smile turning awkward.

“Mr. Merlin, please wait a moment… let me think it over…”

“Hm?” Merlin knitted his brows slightly. *This little housewife is pretty shy,* he thought. *Doesn’t she have a kid already? Maybe she hasn’t been married long?*

Merlin had met plenty of women in Scotland. Normal married women were usually warm and bold—within a few sentences, they’d steer the conversation toward risqué topics. Some had even made *him* blush. You could only imagine how open those discussions got.

“Well, I suppose I should ask…” Martha propped up her delicate chin, tentatively inquiring—

“Mr. Merlin, are you a traveler from outside the village?”

title: Chapter 21
content:
Chapter 21

Volume 2 · Chapter 21

Merlin froze, thinking this might be some new kind of interview question, like selling the pen in his hand.

"Yes, that's right..."

Merlin nodded honestly, figuring this might be a test of sincerity.

"Then there's no problem." Martha smiled lightly, and with that single sentence, she hired Merlin.

"emmmm..." Merlin narrowed his eyes, still suspicious. "This... simple?!"

"The hiring threshold isn't actually that high. As long as you're from outside the village, no work experience is needed. You just have to be able to sell drinks." Martha nodded, dispelling Merlin's doubts.

Merlin's expression was complicated—not grateful, but thinking to himself, *Damn, if I'd known it was this easy, why did I waste so much time? I could've just come here directly. And hey, can I shamelessly ask for reimbursement for baths, haircuts, and clothes now?*

"So, Mr. Merlin, are you planning to work here short-term?" Martha asked patiently.

"Yeah, that's right. I'll only work for two months at most, then continue my travels." Merlin nodded. He really didn't intend to stay long; he still had to seek out powerful beings and study curses.

"In that case, we provide food and lodging. The monthly salary is one gold coin, and you'll get a 15% commission on every drink you sell, with no upper limit." Martha briefly explained the pay structure—base salary plus commission, just like most sales jobs.

"One gold coin?! The base salary is that high?" Merlin's eyes widened in disbelief.

A gold coin was extremely valuable. Ordinary taverns would never pay that much—usually just one silver coin, or at most 50-70 silver coins for high-end places.

One gold coin a month? That was the kind of salary you'd only find in high-end clubs frequented by nobles.

"Mhm, but our tavern operates differently during the day and night. During the day, it's normal business, but at night, we host many female customers. You'll need to push drinks as much as possible. Uh... if possible..." Martha averted her gaze, hesitating. "You can use some... special measures to sell to female customers."

"Special measures meaning..." Merlin's mind immediately conjured up some suggestive images.

"Like sweet-talking, emotional counseling, or even... private, in-depth conversations with female customers..." Martha lowered her voice, speaking very vaguely.

*What the hell!*

*Now I get it.*

*As long as you can sell the drinks...*

*It means you can do whatever you want with the female customers, right?*

This business model of using male charm to sell drinks—wasn't that just being a host at a nightclub?!

*Oh my god! I'm the Demon Lord, and now I'm reduced to working as a host in an otherworldly nightclub?*

*Isn't this a little too humiliating...*

Merlin's face darkened, his mind filled with thoughts of his own downfall. A lazy, late-stage failure like him had finally sunk to the level of being a host. Life was truly mocking him—this was a midlife crisis.

"How about it, Mr. Merlin? I think this job actually suits you quite well." Martha sincerely added. Just looking at Merlin's face and eyes, he'd have no trouble charming women, making sales twice as effective.

What troubled Merlin now was his lack of travel funds. He didn't want to starve, penniless.

Should he lower himself to take this host job?

When it came to dealing with women, he was an expert—making a fortune a day shouldn't be a problem.

But still... being a host was a bit too shameful.

Yet, though Merlin felt resistant, he was also practical. Even if he didn't have the patience of Han Xin crawling under someone's crotch, he could still swallow his pride for survival.

Plus, no one in this village knew him. Even if he worked as a host for a living, this dark chapter of his life wouldn't be exposed. He could just tough it out for now. The most important thing was to get the money first.

After much deliberation, Merlin gave a firm nod.

"I'll do it. Sweet-talking ladies into drinking? I love that."

(-`ω-)?

The mighty Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace, a figure of both prestige and glory...

Was now, forced by circumstance, secretly working as a host in a small Welsh village, peddling his charm for a living...

A male lead setup, dedicated to all of you! Long live the handsome Merlin!

title: Chapter 22
content:
Chapter 22

Volume 2 · Chapter 22

"Madam, would you mind if I asked a question?" Merlin wondered to himself.

"Not at all, please go ahead." Martha smiled warmly.

"Why insist on hiring an outsider?" Merlin asked. This kind of work would clearly be better suited for someone from the village.

"Because..." Martha hesitated for a moment, a blush rising to her cheeks. "Because I'm home alone with my child, and my husband is a soldier in Edinburgh. It's easy for rumors to spread about me. If I hired someone from the village, it would invite gossip. An outsider like a traveler is better—it avoids a lot of trouble."

Merlin didn’t say anything, but he understood Martha’s reasoning.

A young mother alone at home.

It was indeed easy for unpleasant rumors to spread.

With her husband away, it was only natural that a bunch of lazy men would set their sights on her.

The reason for hiring a stranger as an employee wasn’t hard to grasp...

◆

Next.

Merlin followed Martha, who held the room key, upstairs.

This floor was all guest rooms. Martha said she would give Merlin a free room to use as employee housing.

"This is your room. The work uniform is in the wardrobe." Martha stopped at the door and turned to hand the key to Merlin.

"Thank you. Actually, the stable would be fine." Merlin took the key, being polite, though in his mind he thought, *Who the hell would want to sleep in a stable!*

"You should rest for now. Evening is almost here. Once it is, the only customers downstairs will be women. You’ll have to do your best!" Martha encouraged him like a kind older sister.

"Don’t worry, Madam." Merlin didn’t feel much pressure. Getting women to drink wasn’t difficult, especially for someone like him—a succubus.

"Mom!" A little boy rushed into Martha’s arms. "I’m back!"

"Uh..." Merlin’s expression turned odd. This boy looked familiar—wasn’t he the little Henry he’d met at the market? So he was Martha’s son.

"Where have you been playing again? You’ve been out all day. Do you have any idea how worried I’ve been?" Martha crouched down and wiped the dirt from little Henry’s face with a towel.

"I went to the market. I heard the guards found goblin corpses outside the village. The village chief is figuring out what to do about it." Little Henry said in his childish voice, excitement flashing in his eyes—probably his first time seeing goblins. "Mom, do you think there’s really a goblin tribe in the mountains behind the village?"

"Yes, I saw them when I was little." Martha replied gently.

"Do they eat people?" Little Henry asked curiously.

"They do. They especially like to eat naughty children like you." Martha teased, hoping to scare him into behaving.

"That’s fine! I’m like my father—I know sword techniques!" Little Henry patted the crude wooden toy sword at his waist.

Martha shook her head, at a loss for what to do about her son’s reckless bravery.

"Mom, do you think the goblins in the mountains will come down to raid the village?" Little Henry was very curious, hoping for a chance to prove himself. "If they do, I’ll use my sword techniques to defeat them! Then I’ll become the village’s great hero!"

"Don’t talk nonsense!" Martha couldn’t help but scold him. She spoke seriously, "Goblins are very vicious. When I was little, I saw them raid the village and massacre villagers. If the old village chief hadn’t been a high-ranking mage, our village would have been destroyed long ago."

"Was the old village chief really that strong?" Little Henry frowned, feeling a little jealous.

"Mm-hmm, very strong. He fought the goblin tribe until they retreated again and again. In the end, he forced them to sign a peace treaty, forbidding them from ever leaving the back mountains. It’s been over twenty years since then. Even after the old chief passed away, the treaty still keeps us safe here." Martha rarely spoke of the past with her son, but today was an exception. She was truly worried he might get carried away and go pick a fight with the goblins.

"So... so cool!" Little Henry clenched his fists, his eyes sparkling. "I wonder if the current village chief knows magic. I want to learn!"

"That won’t work. The current chief is the old chief’s grandson, but he doesn’t have the talent for magic." Martha ruffled her son’s hair and said earnestly, "Henry, not everyone in this world can become a mage or a warrior. Even as a tavern owner, you can still live a wonderful life."

Little Henry frowned, clearly frustrated, but his eyes were full of determination.

Merlin had been listening to the mother-son conversation the whole time, his face darkening as he thought nervously—

The goblins outside the village... those were the ones I killed.

Was that peace treaty real or not?

This is bad. I feel like I’ve caused a pretty big problem.

Ah, well. Might as well keep playing dumb...

(ー`′ー)

title: Chapter 23
content:
Chapter 23

Volume 2 · Chapter 23

Martha wiped the dust from little Henry’s face before remembering that Merlin was still standing beside her. She quickly apologized, flustered. “N-No… sorry, Mr. Merlin, I’ve neglected you.”

“It’s fine, it’s fine. This must be your son? So cute~” Merlin forced an awkward smile, thinking to himself, *Not cute at all. This kid’s definitely going to grow up to be some reckless hothead…*

“I forgot to introduce him—this is my son, Henry. He’s usually so mischievous that you barely see him in the shop.” Martha ruffled Henry’s hair and continued, “Henry, this is Mr. Merlin, your big brother. He’ll be helping out in the shop for a while.”

“Hey~, Henry. Long time no see…” Merlin waved his hand, thinking, *Since he’s the boss’s son, better get on his good side first.*

Martha blinked, confused. *What does he mean? Do they know each other?*

Little Henry narrowed his eyes, studying Merlin carefully. Even though the man was no longer disheveled and had shaved his beard, he still recognized him.

“Ah! The scammer uncle from the market! Even without the beard, you’re still super shady~”

“Ugh!” Merlin’s breath hitched, and his face darkened instantly. His hand instinctively reached for the katana at his waist, thinking—

*Hey! You little brat, who’s shady?*

Don’t think just because you’re a spoiled kid you can say whatever you want.

I’m the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace. One swing of my blade, and gods and demons alike fall.

Let me say it again—I’m not some uncle, I’m your *big brother*. Have you ever seen an uncle this young?!

Now listen to your mother and call me big brother, got it…?

“Henry! What are you saying?! No respect at all! That’s no way to speak!” Martha’s expression turned stern. She pulled Henry close, covering his mouth, and apologized to Merlin with a guilty tone. “I’m so sorry, Mr. Merlin. Henry doesn’t know how to speak properly. Please don’t take it to heart. I’ll scold him later.”

“It’s nothing, kids are like that—blunt and honest.” Merlin smiled *kindly*, then ruffled Henry’s hair, his voice dark as he said, “You’re such a *lovable* little guy… *just begging for a beating*.”

Henry clamped his mouth shut, trembling, thinking—

*Mom, save me… this uncle wants to kill me…*

◆

Merlin entered his room and looked around.

It wasn’t as luxurious as the rooms of some high-ranking nobles, but it was still cozy enough.

He tossed his bundle onto the floor, then leapt onto the soft bed, feeling his entire body relax into laziness.

“Ah~! I’m alive!”

Merlin really wanted to sleep until he woke up naturally, but checking the time, he could only rest for a few hours before he had to start work.

He wondered what kind of ladies would come to the tavern tonight. He was actually looking forward to it.

After over a year of traveling alone, Merlin had learned a lot. He’d discovered that the world outside was quite different from what the demon race’s library books described.

Take strength, for example—being invincibly powerful didn’t automatically earn you recognition.

In the eyes of many arrogant nobles, overwhelming strength was just the mark of a brute, a warrior who relied on raw power to make a living. It was uncouth, unrefined.

That kind of thinking was common in true noble circles. Merlin had often heard such belittling remarks at high-society gatherings.

Probably only when your power was strong enough to shake an entire nation would those noble lords deign to lower their lofty heads.

Saint-tier might be powerful, sharp and formidable, but it was still far from the level needed to upend an entire empire.

He’d heard that the British royal family had a secret knight order, all of them Saint-tier, and their captain was even hailed as the peak of Saint-tier, the strongest human alive.

Merlin wasn’t impressed. He thought they were just frogs at the bottom of a well.

Because—

There *were* those who surpassed Saint-tier.

title: Chapter 24
content:
Chapter 24

Volume 2 · Chapter 24

If I remember correctly, there was a generation of Heroes who seemed to have surpassed Saint-tier, that guy who killed his own mother, Lucifer the Second, known as the "Legendary Spear Hero."

At that time, Merlin couldn’t use his powers, so he could only watch as that Hero, who had surpassed Saint-tier, personally killed his own mother, then scorned and belittled him before leaving disdainfully.

That Spear Hero was the one Merlin most wanted to fight. Even now, he could still recall that extraordinary spear technique—every thrust carried the threat of death.

But now, after leaving the Death Swamp, he had inquired everywhere, only to find that this legendary Hero had vanished without a trace, as if he had evaporated, leaving not a single clue behind. All that remained were fragments of his legend, pieced together from others’ accounts.

Even the clergy of the Holy Church knew nothing about this Hero. They only knew the legend of the Spear Hero, but not his true name. It was as if he had appeared out of thin air, only to disappear just as suddenly.

Merlin found this deeply regrettable. It wasn’t that he particularly wanted revenge—rather, the "Spear Hero" was the strongest being he had ever encountered. Perhaps he held the key to lifting the curse, and that piqued his interest.

You might say Merlin was heartless, that he wouldn’t avenge his own mother’s death?

But you can’t judge so hastily. Setting aside the fact that Merlin was a transmigrator with no real familial bonds, it wasn’t even certain whether his mother was truly dead.

He had seen with his own eyes the Spear Hero pierce her heart with a spear, yet there was no body—it was as if she had been transported away by some kind of spatial magic.

After becoming the Demon Lord, Merlin had investigated for a long time, but found nothing. That holy war remained shrouded in mystery, and to this day, whether his mother was truly dead remained an unsolved riddle.

Merlin’s impression of his mother was a good one. As the only male heir of the family, he had been well taken care of.

As for his mother, Merlin’s assessment was simple: she was an incredibly powerful warrior, and also someone capable of drawing the demon sword Banri Garan.

But back to the point—Merlin found it laughable how those frogs at the bottom of the well considered the captain of the Secret Knights to be the strongest human. It was downright ironic.

That Spear Hero had surpassed Saint-tier, yet wasn’t hailed as the strongest, while some mere Saint-tier warrior held that title. How absurd.

Merlin actually wanted to kill that overrated, composed captain to extend his own life, but it seemed like too much trouble. If he really did that, he’d have endless people coming to avenge him every day.

He had only eaten a few meals without paying and was already wanted, with weak adventurers harassing him daily.

If he killed the captain of the Royal Knights, wouldn’t the entire imperial army come after him?

It wasn’t that Merlin was afraid—he just had terminal laziness. He didn’t want to be bothered constantly, wasting unnecessary energy. He just wanted to travel in peace and lift his curse.

If it weren’t for that goal, he wouldn’t even consider repaying the debts on his back.

Merlin’s creed was to freeload and wait for death, avoiding all trouble at all costs—

*Sigh…* This is really frustrating…

“Is there any job that lets me kill monsters and earn a ton of money?”

“According to the usual novel tropes, shouldn’t I level up and change maps?”

“Why does it feel like the world outside the tutorial village is still the tutorial village?”

“This doesn’t make sense… Where’s the max-level map?”

_(:зゝ∠)_

title: Chapter 25
content:
Chapter 25

Volume 2 · Chapter 25

Merlin felt his curse was stable for now, with no immediate risk of flaring up. But he couldn’t just sit idle—he needed to improve his living standards while also hunting down those powerful, unaligned figures.

So Merlin worked odd jobs to make ends meet, all while taking out those strong, unaffiliated individuals.

For example, the Saint-tier pirates he had recently killed—the Redbeard Brothers who terrorized the North Sea.

The two pirate brothers were incredibly powerful, dominating the North Sea and ruthlessly plundering the coastal city of Elgin in Great Britain. Their rampage had reached a point where no one could stop them.

Even when the Great British royal family sent the Royal Navy to crush them, they couldn’t lay a hand on the brothers. Instead, the Redbeards ambushed them under cover of thick fog.

The proud Royal Navy, accustomed only to direct combat, panicked at the surprise attack. Their entire right-wing fleet was sunk, and the admiral had no choice but to retreat.

The incident made headlines in Great Britain, piquing Merlin’s interest. At the time, he had sensed his curse stirring and needed to prolong his life, so he took an interest in the Redbeard pirates.

Merlin lay in wait in Elgin for two months before the brothers finally appeared. To everyone’s delight, he cut them down in one stroke, leaving them screaming, “Monster!”

For reasons unknown, Merlin became Elgin’s hero, its savior. But he had gone a little too far in battle—he had accidentally sunk a few hundred Royal Navy ships along the coast.

This, of course, drew a manhunt. Wave after wave of naval officers and soldiers, armed with long muskets, came chasing after him. Fortunately, Merlin realized the situation was bad and fled.

On top of that, the light was dim and the battlefield was shrouded in smoke, so no one had gotten a clear look at his face. All they remembered was the man who, after the great battle, casually picked his nose as he walked away.

To this day, the streets of Great Britain still whisper of Merlin’s legend. He was hailed as Elgin’s legendary swordsman, a master of the blade who had slain the Redbeard Brothers in an instant and saved the coastal villagers.

Merlin had once boasted in a tavern that he was the one who did it, hoping for some glory. But no one believed him, which was a shame—it had been a rare chance to earn merit and fame.

Merlin sighed as he lay in bed. He had done quite a lot this past year, and it wasn’t without gains.

He felt it was time to write a letter to his little sister. It had been over a year, after all. Wasn’t it perfectly normal to send word home and let them know he was safe?

Merlin went to his desk, picked up a quill and parchment, and began to write—

Dear Lilith,

It’s been a year since we last saw each other. Your brother has made a name for himself out here. I live in a magnificent castle, with countless maids and servants, endless wealth, and I’m even Great Britain’s greatest hero.

Everyone envies me, admires me, worships me, trusts me.

I’m bragging this much because I want you to know I’m doing *amazingly* well out here. Far from the “useless shut-in” you called me.

In short, I’m thriving…

(Here follows Merlin’s million-word brag)

Merlin only shared the good news because he had no choice. If he admitted he was doing poorly, Lilith would worry, and it would only confirm her belief that her brother was indeed a useless waste of space—

Merlin had to work hard to uphold his dignity as an older brother. It wasn’t easy…

title: Chapter 26
content:
Chapter 26

Volume 2 · Chapter 26

Merlin changed into his work clothes, which were actually a finely tailored bartender’s uniform that made him look exceptionally handsome.

The tavern at night was indeed different from daytime—there wasn’t a single male customer left, only women of all kinds.

Dressed in glamorous, alluring outfits, they had come to this women-only revelry.

Most of them were approaching thirty, married, and seeking a little excitement.

Especially tonight—according to Madame Martha, the owner—a new, exceptionally handsome young man had joined the staff, and many beautiful mature women had come to take a look.

A little romance, a little love, reliving the feeling of first love was wonderful.

A pianist had been invited for the evening, fingers dancing across the keys, filling the air with cheerful melodies. The women, glasses in hand, chatted and laughed merrily.

Whoa, they’re all older women?

No matter, the older the better…

Merlin adjusted his little bow tie. Time to start work. He strolled leisurely onto the dance floor, weaving among the various women.

His dazzling golden hair always drew attention, and with his roguish charm, his appeal to women multiplied.

And that was without even factoring in his succubus-like allure, which had an immense pull on the opposite sex…

Merlin naturally slipped his arms around the slender waists of two women, pulling them close. With a calm smile, he said, “You two ladies look absolutely radiant tonight—more beautiful than the brightest stars in the Irish night sky. Would you care to come over and share your stories with me?”

Normally, any woman would be a little annoyed if someone just grabbed them without a word.

But the moment they saw Merlin’s strikingly handsome face, coupled with his deep crimson eyes, they were instantly captivated. His slightly flirtatious words sent their hearts fluttering like schoolgirls, their faces flushing red.

Many of the beautiful women noticed Merlin, the new face. Madame Martha hadn’t lied—this newcomer was indeed incredibly handsome and young, sparking widespread interest.

He carried himself with an imposing air, different from the others. Clearly someone used to being in charge. Later, Merlin learned she was a baroness, back visiting relatives.

This baroness walked straight up to Merlin and said haughtily, “So you’re the new one? You’ve got a nice face. What would you like to drink? I’ll order it for you.”

Merlin had seen many women in his time. He could tell this one was minor nobility. But he had even seduced duchesses—what was a mere baroness to him?

“Madam, if you keep up that haughtiness here, people won’t find you very likable.”

“What did you say? How dare you speak to me like that?” The baroness was clearly uncomfortable, feeling as if Merlin was looking down on her.

Suddenly, Merlin stepped in close, startling the baroness so much she let out a little cry, dropping her wine glass with a crash. “Ah!”

Their noses were less than ten centimeters apart, the atmosphere undeniably intimate.

Those enchanting crimson eyes made the baroness’s heart skip two beats, her face flushing in a strange, flustered way.

A flicker of timidity rose in her heart. As she tried to take a step back, Merlin’s arm wrapped around her waist, pulling her against him.

He deliberately held her tight, pressing her ample chest flat against him. With this sudden intimacy, he closed the distance between them.

“R-Rude! Let… let go of me…” The baroness panicked, but her heart was pounding, her mind spinning—maybe it was the alcohol.

Merlin flashed a wicked grin, leaning in to whisper in her ear, his warm breath tickling her, “You’re most charming when you’re flustered like this… because it’s so cute~”

“Eek!” The baroness was done for. Her ears were practically pregnant, her face burning like a sunset, her legs trembling weakly.

“Let’s go to a private room and have a proper chat,” Merlin suggested.

“Mmm.” The baroness, face still red, nodded slightly as if bewitched.

Just then, an older man barged in, dressed in fine clothes—clearly a noble. His face was flushed with urgency as he rushed over and bombarded the baroness with questions.

“Darling, what are you doing here? This kind of rural gathering isn’t worthy of you. Come, let’s go home…”

“I’m sorry, darling. Let’s get a divorce. I think I’ve found my true love.” The baroness nestled obediently against Merlin, suddenly seeming years younger.

“WHAT?!?” The baron dropped to his knees with a thud, his face a mask of shock. A nobleman, so confident in matters of the heart, had been instantly crushed by Merlin, reduced to a broken dog.

Merlin broke into a cold sweat, feeling a pang of embarrassment. Had he gone too far? Well, work was work.

Merlin proceeded to flirt with many more women, leading a whole group of them into a small private room.

“Ladies, let me tell you the tale of the Lustful Demon Lord and the Washboard Hero’s adventures in the Orkney Strait. But the night is long—let’s have some drinks to liven things up.”

The women gathered together, chattering and laughing nonstop.

A glint of malice flickered in Merlin’s eyes as he thought to himself—

Foolish women…

Let me slowly drain every last bit of value from you!

(-`ω-)?

title: Chapter 27
content:
Chapter 27

Volume 2 · Chapter 27

Night.

Behind the village.

A gray-clad thief arrived before a mountain cave, his body wreathed in a swirl of black mist.

The thick black smoke dispersed, revealing a somewhat short green-skinned goblin. His bright red eyes gleamed with terror.

The gray-clad thief pulled down his mask, revealing a pointed nose, pointed ears, and jagged teeth—he was the very goblin who had been scared out of his wits by Merlin.

The thief goblin cautiously scanned his surroundings. Only after confirming no one was around did he enter the cave.

The deep, dark cave was pitch black, but rows of torches illuminated it like daylight. Clearly, a large number of creatures lived here.

If one ventured deeper, they would find a magnificent underground palace, fortress-like and quite imposing.

Before the heavy gates stood over a dozen giant goblins, each twenty feet tall, clad in silver armor and wielding massive swords as they guarded the entrance.

The thief goblin timidly approached the gates and shouted—

"I am the thief Haser! I request an audience with His Majesty!"

◆

Inside the underground palace.

This was the dwelling of the Goblin Emperor.

Twenty years ago, he had been a tyrant who terrorized the land.

But then he encountered that high-ranking mage, the village chief, and was utterly crushed, forced to sign a humiliating peace treaty.

Since then, these goblins had lived underground for twenty years, never seeing the sun.

A few years ago, however, they heard that the old village chief had died, and his non-magical grandson had become the new chief. With their greatest threat gone, the goblins, who had lived in humiliation underground, began to secretly stir once more.

They boldly raided merchant caravans passing through the village, but to avoid violating the peace treaty—and to prevent drawing the empire’s wrath—they used transformation potions to disguise themselves as humans while committing their crimes.

Every goblin sent out had to turn in a large sum of gold each month, or they would be hanged.

Their Goblin Emperor had no grand ambitions. He only loved two things: money and female slaves.

At this moment, in the great hall, the obese Goblin Emperor lounged lazily on a bed made of stacked gold coins.

He wore a luxurious red robe, his neck and hands adorned with extravagant jewels. His green, pockmarked skin glistened as he basked in pleasure.

Beside him, five or six naked human women, collars around their necks, were serving him, taking turns licking him with their tongues.

These women were relatives of the raided caravans. Only the fairest were offered to the emperor. The less attractive ones were usually violated by the lower goblins first, then killed.

When goblins raided caravans, they typically slaughtered all the men without hesitation. The women suffered even worse fates, becoming sex slaves.

In the great hall, the thief Haser trembled on the floor, not daring to breathe, afraid of disturbing the emperor’s pleasure.

Nearby, many goblin ministers whispered to each other in hushed tones.

"Ooooh~"

The Goblin Emperor let out a satisfied groan, seemingly finished. The female slaves were promptly pulled away by servants.

"Haser, why have you returned? Did you steal any money?" the Goblin Emperor boomed.

"No... not yet, Your Majesty," the thief Haser replied nervously.

"Then how dare you come back? Do you want to be hanged?" the Goblin Emperor roared, his voice like thunder.

"No... it's not like that! I have something else to report!" Haser’s heart pounded in his throat.

"Hmm? What is it?" The Goblin Emperor’s massive belly jiggled as he lazily gazed down.

"Rek the Witch..." Haser recalled his companion, the black-clad thief who had been—

"His head was chopped off by a human in one strike!"

title: Chapter 28
content:
Chapter 28

Volume 2 · Chapter 28

"You say what? Are you sure you're not just making excuses for your own incompetence?" The Goblin Emperor heard the news with unexpected calm.

"Your Majesty, I swear on my life it's the truth!" Thief Hasser knelt on the ground, trembling violently.

"Killed by whom? Since that old mage from the mountain died, there shouldn't be many who can defeat Rekubu." The Goblin Emperor lounged on his throne, piled high with gold coins, as he questioned.

"It really was a human... and... and it was just a villager from the mountain below! They took him out in a single strike!"

Thief Hasser jerked his head, dumping all the blame onto the mountain villagers. As long as he could escape responsibility, anything went.

In truth, Merlin was a succubus, but he showed no distinguishing traits, so people assumed he was human. Thus, this goblin thief couldn’t tell at all.

And since Merlin seemed to be heading toward the village, it was convenient to let the villagers take the fall.

"A single strike? Has the mountain village produced another high-tier human?" The Goblin Emperor questioned, seemingly unimpressed by high-tier opponents.

"Your Majesty is as wise as ever! Rekubu was a powerhouse with one foot in the intermediate tier—he could even hold his own against a true intermediate fighter. Anyone who can kill Rekubu in one hit must be a high-tier enemy!" Thief Hasser climbed the pole, instantly promoting Merlin to a high-tier powerhouse.

This might have been the worst slander Merlin had ever suffered, because he wasn’t even ranked in any tier at all. Calling him merely high-tier was a bit of an insult.

"Is that so..." The Goblin Emperor stroked his chin, falling into thought. After a moment, he asked, "Gegubu, my warrior has been killed. What do you think about this?"

From the front of the crowd of goblin ministers stepped a purple-skinned goblin. His appearance wasn’t as ferocious as the others, but he exuded a sinister cunning.

This goblin, named Gegubu, was the tribe’s chancellor, deeply trusted by the Goblin Emperor. It would be more accurate to say he was full of wicked schemes rather than wisdom.

"Your Majesty, this matter is simple. Since the mountain villagers have attacked us, we should return an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth!"

"But we signed a peace treaty with the mountain villagers." The Goblin Emperor seemed hesitant.

"Your Majesty, you are far too merciful. While it is good to value integrity, being overly attached to it makes you indecisive. The moment the mountain villagers killed our warrior, that so-called peace treaty became nothing but scrap paper. It was *they* who broke the agreement—we are merely seeking vengeance." Chancellor Gegubu seemed to enjoy stirring trouble, urging the Goblin Emperor to attack the mountain village.

The Goblin Emperor found some truth in this. The humans had killed his warrior first, unilaterally violating the peace treaty.

"Moreover, that so-called peace treaty was an unequal, humiliating document that imprisoned us on this mountain! We’ve been living underground for twenty years! It’s time to overthrow human rule and establish the great ideal nation of the goblin race!" Chancellor Gegubu spoke with passionate fervor, painting his own side as the righteous one—a master of manipulation.

The Goblin Emperor, seated on his throne, clenched his fists. Remembering how he had been thoroughly defeated by the old mage from the village filled him with shame. But now that his old nemesis was dead, there was no longer any threat. He was subtly swayed.

"Your Majesty, please order a crusade against all of Wales! Start with the mountain village below. We are not the same as before—our forces are strong, our soldiers are mighty. Humans are nothing but inferior creatures, and besides, Your Majesty is already a Saint-tier powerhouse! There are only a handful in all of Great Britain who could pose a threat to you. The time has come for the goblin race to rule Wales!"

Gegubu gave a slight bow, lowering his head in false humility as he delivered his final point.

"Your Majesty, please make your decision. With just one command from you, all the wealth and slave women of Wales will be yours."

The Goblin Emperor’s heart raced. His greenish face gave nothing away as he slowly rose to his feet. Spreading his massive hands, his obese body wobbled a few times before he boomed his command—

"Order the soldiers to prepare for battle! Have the blacksmiths forge the sharpest swords and the sturdiest shields! In one month’s time, we declare war on all of Wales! Let me make this clear—this is *not* a drill! This is a war between goblins and humans!"

The ministers buzzed with excitement, their bloodlust clouding their judgment. Not a single one objected—it seemed they had endured their humiliating underground lives for far too long.

"As for you, Lord Hasser—your comrade was killed and you did nothing. How dare you return here?" Gegubu wore a wicked grin as he turned to Thief Hasser, snapping his fingers and casting a Fireball spell. "Die!"

"No... nooooooo!"

Thief Hasser screamed in agony as flames engulfed his entire body.

He thrashed and rolled on the ground, begging for mercy, his face twisted in horror.

His greenish skin turned to char, and the stench of burning flesh filled the air.

In the blink of an eye, Thief Hasser was reduced to ashes...

title: Chapter 29 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 29 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 29

A month passed in the blink of an eye.

Merlin received his salary—base pay plus commission, a full six gold coins.

It seemed Merlin had been quite the instigator, urging the ladies to drink.

Merlin and Martha had grown close, and he now addressed her as "Sister Martha."

Don’t get the wrong idea—Merlin wasn’t eyeing his boss’s wife. As his employer, it was only natural to build a good relationship with her.

To be honest, Merlin was long past the age where he’d lose his composure at the sight of a beautiful woman, blushing and daydreaming at every turn.

Don’t even try to pin that innocent, lovesick boy act on him. It just didn’t fit.

When they weren’t familiar, you wouldn’t notice, but after getting to know her, Merlin realized Martha was actually quite talkative.

She couldn’t go more than a few sentences without mentioning her husband—seemed like she truly loved the man.

Martha’s husband was a soldier in Edinburgh, apparently a mid-tier warrior, something of a local celebrity in this village. At first, the couple had run the tavern together.

But now, separated by distance, Martha managed the tavern alone while also looking after little Henry, that little troublemaker.

Merlin had once subtly hinted to Martha that there were rumors about her in the village, but she just smiled and said nothing.

Merlin was a little surprised. Most women would fly into a rage at the slightest gossip, but Martha took it in stride, as if she couldn’t be bothered to explain.

During the day, Merlin often saw sleazy old men flirting with Martha, but she just laughed it off, never responding, as if she hadn’t heard a thing.

Merlin noticed that the village still had a certain respect for women. The men might talk big, but none of them ever crossed the line with force. Maybe that was why Martha only faced rumors—no one had ever produced any proof of her being unfaithful.

Merlin treated the village gossip as just that—gossip. He wasn’t planning to stay long, so he didn’t want to meddle or stir up unnecessary trouble.

Now, Merlin had become the rising star of the Moonlight Tavern, wildly popular among the village women. All sorts of rumors swirled around him—those who didn’t know better might think he’d had something going on with every woman in the village.

In reality, Merlin hadn’t done anything beyond holding hands, flirting, and spinning tall tales.

From his experience, if you wanted women to happily open their purses, the first step was to make them fall for you.

The village men, of course, didn’t buy it. They kept a tight leash on their wives, avoiding the Moonlight Tavern at night, and silently prayed for Merlin to leave as soon as possible.

Merlin found the whole situation exasperating. Somehow, his reputation had become polarizing—women praised him to the heavens, while men branded him a demon who brought ruin to women.

But Merlin didn’t care. He was just a traveler, not planning to stay long. The men would be relieved, the women disappointed.

To Merlin, flirting with women wasn’t half as thrilling as betting on horses!

Sure enough, as soon as he got his pay, he rushed to the horse racing ticket booth and dumped all six gold coins into the 13th horse for the 62nd race, dreaming of striking it rich.

Yep, he was still this reckless, not keeping a single copper to his name, pouring everything into gambling in the hopes that luck would change his pitiful fate.

Merlin truly believed in the power of momentum—he was completely addicted.

As he walked toward the Moonlight Tavern, clutching the racing ticket he’d bought with his six gold coins, his hands trembled, his face lit up with the grin of a lovesick fool, more excited than if he’d gotten his hands on a pair of his sister’s lace panties.

He kept muttering to himself, probably half-mad already—

"Hmph hmph hmph!"

"Six gold coins on the 13th horse..."

"If it wins, the payout is ten thousand times! Then I’ll be a rich man with sixty thousand gold coins... just thinking about it gets me so damn excited..."

title: Chapter 30
content:
Chapter 30

Volume 2 · Chapter 30

"You mom's a slut! Always out there seducing people!"

"She's not! Don't slander my mom!"

Merlin was walking toward the tavern when he passed a narrow alley and heard several childish voices shouting. One of them sounded familiar.

He took a few steps back and peeked around the corner into the alley.

There was a boy surrounded by a group of slightly older brats.

Wasn’t that little Henry?

Actually getting ganged up on by kids his own age.

Well, he *does* have a sharp tongue. No wonder he’s made enemies...

Merlin watched from the alley’s entrance, not intending to intervene even if Henry was the tavern owner’s son. He just wanted to see how Henry handled himself—like watching a cockfight.

After witnessing so many world-ending spells and divine techniques, there was a certain twisted amusement in watching brats peck at each other like weaklings.

Merlin really did have a dark sense of humor sometimes...

*Clang clang clang!*

The first-ever Gazi Village Brat Boxing Championship officially begins—

Bored, Merlin started narrating in his head like a live commentator.

First, let’s introduce the competitors! Tavern Fist King Henry! His opponents: a bunch of mud-slinging village kids!

"Who slandered you? Everyone in the village knows what your mom’s like! She *is* a slut!" The self-proclaimed kid boss, hands on his hips, activated his taunt skill.

"My mom’s *not* like that! Apologize! Apologize right now!" Little Henry was furious, his childish face flushed red with anger.

"I won’t! Your mom *is* a slut! Slut! Lololol~" The kid boss made a face, stuck out his tongue, and mocked him, sending the other kids into giggles.

Commentator Merlin: Ladies and gentlemen, we’re in the calm before the storm. Both fighters are exchanging trash talk—what we call the "mouth cannon" phase. Following international conventions, one of them is about to get humiliated, and you’re gonna love it~

"You won’t apologize? Then I’ll beat you up!" Henry gritted his teeth, and it didn’t sound like a joke.

"Come on, do you dare?" The kid boss deliberately stuck his head out, full of confidence. "Hit me! Hit me~"

Commentator Merlin: Damn! I’ve never seen such a shameless demand. Henry, if you’re a man, punch him! Unleash a flurry of jabs, beat him till his own mom doesn’t recognize him. If that doesn’t work, go for a Lightning Dragon Drill to the groin—ending his bloodline wouldn’t be bad either~

"Die! You trash!" Henry roared, then without hesitation, swung a *Return My Fists* punch—sending the kid boss crashing to the ground!

Commentator Merlin: Henry strikes! One punch to the face, and the kid boss is down! Ladies and gentlemen, this proves Henry’s got some guts. For your own safety, don’t provoke brats like this in the future.

The kid boss, clutching his face in shock, hadn’t expected to get hit. He bellowed at the others, "You *dare* hit me?! Beat him up! Kill him!"

The other boys exchanged glances, then without hesitation swarmed Henry, punching and kicking while hurling insults.

Henry drew his wooden sword from his waist and swung wildly. At first, it worked, but he was outnumbered. Soon, the boys pinned him down, rubbing his face into the dirt as they ganged up on him.

Commentator Merlin: The kid boss has called in aerial reinforcements! Several divine soldiers from the sky have Henry pinned for a ground-and-pound! Extremely violent—viewer discretion advised!

The kid boss wiped the blood from the corner of his mouth, growing even more vicious. Being hit by Henry had humiliated him.

Fury surged in his heart, and evil thoughts filled his mind. He silently pulled a dagger from his waist and approached the prone Henry, intending to spill some blood.

Commentator Merlin: Ladies and gentlemen, the situation has escalated. The kid boss, unwilling to accept defeat, has lost his mind and pulled out a *knife*... Wait?! A *knife* in a brat fight?! Have I fallen behind the times? When I was a kid, we just threw mud at each other! Oh right, this *is* another world...

The kid boss, dagger in hand, stood over Henry. "I’ll tell you this, Henry—your mom *is* a slut! You’re the son of a slut!"

Henry, beaten black and blue, pinned under the group, struggled to lift his head. Gritting his teeth, he spat, "Say that again?! I’ll *kill* you!"

"Let’s see you act tough now! I’ll stab you to death!!!"

Enraged, the kid boss raised the dagger and lunged at Henry.

But the moment the dagger went up, someone grabbed his wrist, stopping him cold.

The kid boss turned, stunned, to see Merlin’s face darkened with an odd expression.

"Tsk." Merlin clicked his tongue, his expression strange, his face unreadable as he said—

"Hey, brats..."

"Fighting’s one thing, but pulling a knife? That’s going too far."

title: Chapter 31
content:
Chapter 31

Volume 2 · Chapter 31

Merlin grabbed the Child King's wrist, and with a little force, caused the Child King great pain.

"Ah!"

The Child King cried out in pain, and the dagger in his hand clattered to the ground.

Seeing that the Child King posed no threat, Merlin let go.

When Little Henry saw Merlin, he was a bit startled, remembering that Merlin idled away his days, always lounging with a large group of women, which could be called quite decadent.

"Uncle Merlin!?"

Merlin furrowed his brow, glanced at the disheveled Little Henry on the ground, and thought helplessly, I've said it a hundred times—I'm not an old man! I'm a big brother! My appearance fitting into high school is completely fine, right? Who dares to object? Watch me beat you into a new person with one strike…

"Get lost!"

Seeing Merlin was an adult, the Child King felt a bit scared and took off running.

The other boys didn't think much either, scattering like birds and beasts.

Merlin chuckled, wondering if he really was that scary. He crouched down and looked at Little Henry.

"Are you okay? Can you still get up?"

"I'm fine!" Little Henry gritted his teeth, stubbornly pushing himself up from the ground, "I don't want to be pitied by a useless old man……"

Merlin frowned, thinking, Who's the useless one? I'm just hanging out with women every day; you'll envy me when you grow up.

"Your sorry state will also worry your mother."

"Hmph! Women are just trouble……" Little Henry said in an old‑fashioned tone.

Hey hey hey, this smug little brat, who raised you to be like this?

Merlin twisted his mouth, thinking Little Henry this brat has a terrible temper and a poisonous mouth; when he grows up and enters society, he won't have anything good coming his way.

"Why fight? They outnumber you—can you win?"

"Even if I can't win, I have to fight! They slandered my mother; I won't let them off! And I'll inherit my father's swordsmanship—even if I can't use battle aura now, I will definitely learn it someday!" Little Henry looked stubborn, feeling he'd talked too much, so he flushed and said disdainfully, "Anyway, I'm better than you who only know iaijutsu; I won't be a useless person in the future."

"Emmm……" Merlin wore a complex expression, speaking seriously, "You don't realize how strong I really am—there might be no one in this world stronger than me."

"Uncle Merlin, quit bragging—I've heard that over a dozen times. Daydreaming may be nice, but doing it too much turns you into a useless person besides your face." Little Henry huffed, brushed off the dust on his clothes, then turned and walked away, "I'm going home……"

You little brat!

I really am that strong!

You worship those mid‑tier warriors every day.

Actually they're all just weaklings that can't withstand a single blow!

Don't you know the world's greatest swordsman is right beside you?!

Merlin helplessly shook his head, also needing to head back to the tavern, so he followed Little Henry, watching his small, limping back, and couldn't help but wonder.

"Your mother doesn't care about those rumors, so why do you still mind them?"

"My mother is a good person! She's definitely not a flirtatious slut! Because a group of people maliciously spread rumors and slandered my mother, I have to stand up!" Little Henry said firmly, his clenched‑jaw look quite convincing.

"Why do you have to do this?" Merlin said he didn't quite understand; rumors are like that—the more you explain, the murkier it gets, so it's better to just stay true to yourself.

"This is obvious! Dad isn't home, I'm the only man in the house! So I must protect my mother! I won't let any bad guy approach her, not even allow slander!" Little Henry pounded his chest with his fist, speaking with fervent passion, "I know my mother is a good person, she would never betray Father, and as a man I must step up and protect her! Uncle Merlin, you won't understand my feelings……"

Merlin felt embarrassed and couldn't find words; seeing tears in Little Henry's eyes, he guessed the boy, so young, had borne too much and felt wronged.

"Those lecherous old men who get close to and slander my mother are all bastards! I'll hate them for life—trampling on what others protect is cruel and unforgivable!"

Little Henry turned away angrily, continuing to walk, his small shoulders trembling nonstop, the little wooden sword at his waist battered and on the verge of breaking.

Merlin silently sighed, thinking that since he crossed over to become a demon, maybe he'd lost a lot of human feeling and now likes to coldly observe everything—

"Henry, do you want to learn iaijutsu?"

"I can teach you, as long as you have the talent."

"Not saying you'll become as strong as me."

"Normally you could even tie with an ordinary Saint‑tier."

"How about it? Interested?"

"You just need to hand over this month's pocket money……"

title: Chapter 32 — Bonus Chapters for Tips
content:
Chapter 32 — Bonus Chapters for Tips

Volume 2 · Chapter 32

"No need, Uncle Merlin. Please stop boasting, I've had enough of it already. Saint-tier is like a god-like existence; a mortal like me can never reach it. Besides, the draw-cut isn't useful at all — it's too basic. I can do it too; it's just unsheathing your sword, really. It's not cool and it's not practical. It's like old people exercising for their health." Little Henry pursed his lips, showing clear disdain for Merlin's draw-cut, because in another world it truly was useless and quite half-hearted.

Old... old people exercising for their health!

I swear this is the worst I've ever been roasted.

Two times I kindly tried to pass on martial skills, and both times the same person refused.

I am the dignified Demon Lord of the First Hall! How many people break their heads wanting to learn from me, and I don't even teach them!

Merlin sighed, feeling that Henry was stubbornly headstrong, which was a bit annoying.

To be honest, Merlin also had his own pride. Being refused repeatedly made him uncomfortable, and he decided that even if little Henry knelt down and begged in the future, he would never let him learn his signature techniques.

"Henry, you will regret this, because you are turning down an excellent opportunity — a chance to become one of the world's strongest."

"Never mind, Uncle Merlin. If you were a true powerhouse, ostriches could fly." Little Henry pursed his lips. At a glance, Merlin seemed very impressive. "Uncle Merlin, you always say you're the world's greatest swordsman, but are you as powerful as Elgin's Legendary Swordsman?"

"Elgin's Legendary Swordsman?" Merlin's expression grew strange. Isn't that me? Can I even beat myself? "It's truly uncertain..."

"You definitely couldn't win!" Little Henry was dismissive of Merlin's tone that suggested a fifty-fifty chance. His eyes sparkled with admiration. "He's a powerhouse among powerhouses, a swordsman among swordsmen, a hero among super great heroes! I absolutely want to become his disciple!"

"Oh..." Merlin frowned. It seems I'm very popular. Even a child knows me. But I am Elgin's Legendary Swordsman. So little Henry admires me so much, yet I'm right in front of him, trying to teach him swordsmanship, and he foolishly refused. How interesting.

Say, if I told him that Elgin's Legendary Swordsman is actually the Demon Lord of the First Hall, I wonder if it would make him cry? After all, those religious nutjobs from the Holy Church always badmouth me, saying I eat children every day.

How far has that rumor spread?

Here's an example.

When Merlin was in Scotland, he'd heard that if any child wouldn't go to sleep at night, the parents would threaten: "If you don't sleep right now, Lucifer of the First Hall will come and eat you!"

Then the naive little brat would believe it, cry and obediently go to sleep, growing up with a psychological shadow about the Demon Lord of the First Hall.

But the fact is that Merlin doesn't have a habit of eating people. Other demon race members might, but this unjust accusation really bugged him.

However, Merlin found it rather amusing. Both of his titles have reached the pinnacle, but they are two extremes.

The Demon Lord of the First Hall, the strongest evil great villain, who wiped out one hundred thousand Crusade Army soldiers with a single slash and severely damaged the Roman Holy Church.

Elgin's Legendary Swordsman, the strongest righteous great hero, who one-shot the Saint-tier Red Beard brothers and saved a coastal city.

He has claimed both justice and evil, black and white alike. He's ridiculously awesome!

Merlin himself didn't know whether he was righteous or evil. Perhaps he was both?

He only did what he felt was right, and refused to do what he felt was wrong, relying entirely on his own subjective judgment.

"Oh?" Merlin grinned, teasing little Henry. "You admire Elgin's Legendary Swordsman that much?"

"I super admire him! The peerless powerhouse! He wiped out a pirate fleet single-handedly, one-shot the Saint-tier Red Beard brothers, and saved coastal cities like Elgin. Righteous! Powerful! Invincible! He's simply the entire Britannia's idol!" Little Henry's face was flushed with excitement, his eyes shining. "It's a pity he capsized the navy fleet's warships and got wanted by the empire. Though the empire doesn't acknowledge his merits, in the eyes of ordinary people, he's the spotlight-focused great hero..."

"Oh? He's very powerful?" Merlin's face turned red. He didn't expect to be so popular — being praised made him embarrassed.

"Super powerful! Saint-tier is already like a god-like existence. What does one-shotting means? Just how strong must Elgin's Legendary Swordsman be? He's definitely strong beyond the heavens!" Little Henry exaggeratedly spread his arms and danced around with excitement, full of admiration. "Unlike you, Uncle Merlin, who only knows how to brag, has no real ability, doesn't take proper work seriously, and just messes around with those frivolous women."

Merlin staggered and nearly tripped over, wounded within.

He flicked his dazzling golden hair, revealing what he thought was a handsome smile, and pointed at himself.

"Henry, listen well. Actually, I am Elgin's Legendary Swordsman. Feel surprised?"

Little Henry's face remained expressionless, an underlying contempt radiating from within. He pouted his lips and spat on the ground. "Ptooey!"

"Ugh!" Merlin's face instantly darkened, the veins on his forehead twitching nonstop.

What the hell, you brat!

If you don't believe it, just don't believe it.

But what's with that look of disdain?

I really want to thoroughly beat this brat up right now...

(╬￣皿￣)

title: Chapter 33
content:
Chapter 33

Volume 2 · Chapter 33

Moonlight Tavern.

Merlin had returned with little Henry.

The moment they walked in, they ran into Martha, who strode over furiously upon seeing Henry.

"Where were you? Were you fighting outside again?"

"I wasn't, I fell on my own! I definitely didn't fight," Henry said, feeling humiliated at being beaten up like this, so he wouldn't admit he'd been fighting outside.

"For heaven's sake, you're lying again. Can you fall and end up black-eyed and bruised like that?" Martha walked over, crouched down, and examined her son's injuries. "If you keep fighting people outside, you'll have no pocket money anymore."

"Shut up!" Henry swatted Martha's hand away and huffed upstairs. "Mom, mind your own business! What if you don't give me pocket money? I can go out and do cross-dressing sex work — a bunch of weird uncles are totally into that kind of thing!"

WTF! Damn, bro...

He's been aspiring to become a queen since childhood.

His future prospects are boundless!

Merlin's old face flushed red. He felt like he'd learned another survival skill.

"This kid, seriously..." Martha looked worried, as if she felt like a total failure as a mother. "I'm sorry, Merlin. Henry caused you trouble again..."

"Not at all..." Merlin waved his hand with a smile. "I happened to run into him on the road and brought him back. No trouble at all."

"Sigh..." Martha sighed, a sense of physical and mental exhaustion in her voice. "This kid seems to be listening to me less and less. I wonder if there's something wrong with my parenting methods."

"Come on, Henry is a kid. Kids this age are a bit rebellious. It's quite normal," Merlin said lightly. After all, didn't everyone go through a rebellious phase? Plenty of people looked back after passing it and realized how stupid they had been.

"Is that so?" Martha covered her cheek, worried. "To be honest, I don't like Henry fighting outside. I'm always worried, but he seems to really like the warrior path and wants to be an adventurer. But being an adventurer isn't that easy, and it's very dangerous. I明明 want him to inherit the tavern and just be an ordinary person."

Merlin's heart stirred. Thinking about Henry's age, he asked, "Sister Martha, how old is Henry?"

"He turned fourteen this year," Martha answered.

Fourteen? He looks so young.

Could it be because of his baby face?

Baby faces are perfect for cross-dressing.

No no no, what am I thinking about? Why is my head full of big JJ moe girls?

Merlin cleared his throat to cover his embarrassment.

"Sister Martha, I'm not saying this to upset you, but a normal child can feel spiritual energy or magic around ten years old. Henry is already fourteen now, so maybe..."

Merlin didn't say it too directly, but expressed委婉ly that Henry wasn't suited for the warrior path. If he had no magic or spiritual energy by fourteen, he likely had no talent at all and could only live as an ordinary person.

Although Merlin himself had no magic or spiritual energy, he was a transmigrator, the rarest of the rare, born with immense power built in.

"I know these things too..." Martha lowered her head and sighed. "But I can't bear to crush his dreams."

Merlin also felt helpless inside. Even if he taught Henry swordsmanship, without spiritual energy, it wouldn't have any power.

"Shouldn't you try to persuade him? To be honest, struggling forward on a dead-end road is purely a waste of youth. There won't be any gains."

"I've persuaded him, but it seemed useless. Henry said that learning commerce can't save the Britons," Martha said helplessly.

Shit!

That line sounds so familiar!

Is Henry a Chinese Lu Xun from another world?

Merlin's expression turned awkward, and he thought to himself —

This kid might actually be capable of becoming a true brave warrior.

One who dares to face the bleakness of life and dares to confront gushing blood.

Oh no, I accidentally recited the textbook passage again...

title: Chapter 34 — Tipping Unlocks Extra Updates
content:
Chapter 34 — Tipping Unlocks Extra Updates

Volume 2 · Chapter 34

Merlin remembered how much Henry had talked when they came back earlier.

Now, considering Martha's troubles, Henry must have felt that being a tavern owner simply couldn't protect his mother?

It wasn't that Merlin was arrogant or bloated, he just didn't understand what the point of someone with absolutely no talent working so hard was? Every trade has its specialization — isn't that a common-sense principle everyone should understand?

Still, Merlin rather admired little Henry. At the very least, the kid knew responsibility at such a young age.

Although he would surely grow up to become an annoying hot-blooded idiot, yapping on like a fool every single day.

Speaking of which, Merlin absolutely detested hot-blooded idiots. They were all stubborn, reckless brutes with nothing between their ears. So annoying.

And if they happened to be somewhat cultured on top of that, with a natural talk-no-jutsu ability? That would be even worse. At minimum, they'd make their enemies repent and weep uncontrollably; at worst, they'd turn their enemies traitor mid-battle and self-destruct in the process.

Oh, everyone probably guessed it — Merlin was referring to a certain hot-blooded manga protagonist who could clear an entire dungeon on nothing but his talk-no-jutsu.

Someone who could literally eat off his mouth alone, becoming a ruler.

Yet he kept working so hard and ended up... as a village chief.

Meow meow meow!? Having a silver tongue is enough — what exactly was he working so hard for!?

Martha suddenly realized that Merlin was merely an outsider, and saying all this seemed inappropriate. So she said apologetically, "I'm sorry, Merlin. This is all my personal matter. I always can't help but want to vent to someone. Did I bore you?"

"It's fine, Sister Martha, you're being too polite. If you ever have any troubles, just come find me. I may not necessarily have a solution, but being a listener is no problem at all." Merlin's talent for making female friends kicked in again.

Martha chuckled and said warmly, "You really are gentle, Merlin. Perhaps that's precisely why you're so popular with girls."

"Is... is that so..." Merlin scratched his head, thinking this is literally his job. Normally, he wouldn't want to deal with a group of women either.

"Yes. When I went shopping for beer earlier, many women were talking about you." Martha was genuinely happy about it, since the higher Merlin's popularity, the more money they'd make at night.

Merlin wasn't particularly thrilled about that. But his alias getting more well-known was a different matter entirely. What if his prestige somehow didn't reach his sister's ears, but the name of his牛郎 stage name, Little Daisy, reached Lilith first? How humiliating would that be.

Worse comes to worst, tomorrow his face might actually hit the front page of the Demon Lord newspaper —

"Former Great Demon Lord Merlin, driven by financial hardship, descends to work as a host nightclub in the human world. Little Daisy's product number SINS-7XX. See seed link and cloud drive for details."

Yahoo! Nigai...

I am the head of the Seven Great Demon Lords! I don't want to do some bizarre videos like that! I'd be laughed at!

Merlin's face went pale. He really wanted to quit, otherwise he'd be shaming his whole family back in the Death Swamp! What kind of look would Lilith give him then!?

But he still didn't want to give up on such fast money. He figured he'd just need to keep a low profile at work from now on.

"You really are suited for this job. The alcohol sales this month have set new records. Our tavern owes you a lot, Merlin." Martha clearly liked him a lot — he was basically a money tree.

"I didn't do much..." Merlin responded awkwardly, wondering if he was born to be a male host. But that couldn't be right, could it? Had he put all his talent points into the wrong skill tree?

"I won't disturb you further. Please work hard tonight as well." Martha smiled and waved.

"Sure, don't worry, Sister Martha." Merlin nodded.

◆

Merlin returned upstairs, planning to rest for a bit.

Then he'd have to entertain the women during the night shift. It felt exhausting just thinking about it.

When he passed Martha's room, he noticed the door was slightly ajar, probably forgotten to be closed?

So Merlin didn't think much of it and prepared to close it for her, but the moment his hand touched the handle, his entire body stiffened, and his expression turned shocked.

Merlin widened his eyes and secretly peeked into Martha's room —

Little Henry... had put on his mother's underwear!

content:
Chapter 37

Volume 2 · Chapter 37

Little Henry was completely flabbergasted, never expecting Merlin to suddenly barge in.

Under normal circumstances, his mother Martha and Merlin should have been working downstairs at this hour—they had no business coming up here. What in the world was going on today?!

Little Henry’s eyes widened. One hand clutched at his fake chest as if terrified Merlin might see something shameful, while the other hand—still panicked—hadn’t even been pulled out of his panties yet!

“M-Merlin… Uncle Merlin?!”

How can we let little kids see such an indecent scene?” Merlin pointed at Little Henry, acting like he was about to scold this perverted son on Martha’s behalf.

Henry yanked his hand out of his underwear in a flash, switching to covering his chest with both hands. Flustered, he blurted, “M-Merlin, Uncle Merlin, how did you get in here? This is weird! This is my mom’s room!”

Merlin spread his hands with a smile. “You didn’t close the door. Can you blame me for that?”

“How could I…” Little Henry stared in disbelief. It was impossible—how could he have left the door open? One careless mistake, and now he was doomed for eternity!

“Henry, I never would’ve guessed it. You act so proper in public, but behind closed doors, you have *this* kind of hobby?” Merlin stood on his moral high ground, unilaterally condemning Little Henry. “Fine, cross-dressing is one thing—nobles wear silk stockings all the time—but why are you wearing your *mother’s* underwear? And… and you’ve got a *one-armed bandit* situation going on? That’s just sick!”

“I-I’m not a pervert!” Little Henry’s face burned crimson. He hung his head, muttering, “I just… I just wanted to make some extra money by cross-dressing…”

“So because your mom won’t give you allowance, you’re selling your body? She’d be so disappointed in you!” Merlin spoke with overwhelming righteousness, his sudden seriousness almost unrecognizable.

“Uh… I…” Little Henry’s face stayed red, but no words came out.

“I should really tell Martha about this. What you’re doing is unacceptable.” Merlin shook his head, unable to bear watching Little Henry stray further down the wrong path.

“No, please! Uncle Merlin, spare me, okay?” Little Henry lowered his head, gritted his teeth, and said, “If you let me off, I’ll do *anything* you want!”

“Oh? *Anything*?” Merlin asked, genuinely surprised.

“Y-Yes…” Little Henry nodded, humiliation flooding his heart.

*Ohhh~* Merlin felt a little thrill inside, his gaze sweeping up and down Little Henry’s body.

The air instantly filled with a *Yoooooo~* vibe, stirring the soul.

The moment Little Henry saw that shameless look in Merlin’s eyes, he knew exactly what was coming. *Looks like my flower’s not surviving today.*

But Little Henry, ever the straightforward thinker, blurted out his answer before Merlin could finish.

“Fine, fine, I get it. Uncle Merlin’s just like those other creepy old men—you’ve got a thing for this too, huh?”

“Huh? What do you mean?” Merlin was confused, feeling like his thoughts and Little Henry’s were on completely different wavelengths.

Little Henry let out a muffled sigh and flopped onto the bed in a big “大” shape, his face twisted in reluctant resignation.

He bit his lip, thinking, *My flower… it’s definitely not making it out today.*

“Come on, Uncle Merlin. I’m ready.”

“If I let you have your fun once, you’ll let me go, right?”

“Just get it over with. One and done…”

Wait, what the hell is going on here?!

I was just trying to extort some pocket money while the iron was hot!

How did the scene suddenly turn into a... *transaction*?!

Merlin’s face darkened like a lump of charcoal. *Do I look like some kind of predator preying on a grade-schooler?* This turn of events was downright bizarre.

"Stop staring, Uncle Merlin, hurry up... I hope you finish quickly. Mom will be back soon." Little Henry squeezed his eyes shut, voice trembling with worry. "This is our secret, okay? Don’t tell anyone."

What the actual—?!

Are you serious?!

What kind of person do you take me for?!

How could I possibly do that to a *trap*?!

Unforgivable! Are you insulting me?!

Merlin was furious. He felt deeply offended. He was *not* that kind of man!

His angry gaze swept over Little Henry’s body—only to find that the cross-dressed Henry was *incredibly* alluring, bearing a striking resemblance to Martha, his sister. The black stockings clung to his plump calves, the suspenders winding toward more mysterious regions.

And that *bulge*—it was somehow even more stimulating than a real girl’s. The way he carried himself, that reluctant, defiant air, it ignited an overwhelming urge to conquer.

title: Chapter 39 — Begging for Some Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 39 — Begging for Some Monthly Votes

Volume 2 · Chapter 39

Afterward, Merlin explained everything clearly.

The scene was rather awkward, though—Martha seemed quite angry.

As a result, little Henry was given a brutal beating by Martha. The scene was extremely violent.

Little Henry grew to resent Merlin even more and refused to speak to him for several days straight.

Merlin, however, felt he had accomplished a great deed—saving a young man from the future harm of cross-dressing.

◆

A few days later, at the tavern.

The tavern was always a mixed crowd during the day, filled with all sorts of people, though most were villagers.

But today was different. Three suspicious-looking adventurers had entered. They carried weapons and wore simple, practical clothing.

Of course, it wasn’t their attire that gave them away to Merlin—it was the small adventurer’s guild badges pinned to their chests.

Merlin wasn’t completely clueless. As a wanted man who had dined and dashed countless times, he was all too familiar with adventurers—those low-level ones with badges who constantly came to hassle him.

From what he knew, adventurers took jobs from the guild, completed them, and received rewards. It was a fairly free profession.

Adventurers were also ranked: Black Iron, White Silver, Gold, Mithril, and Orchid Gold.

Most of the ones who came to bother Merlin were Black Iron or White Silver—honestly, they were all weak. He didn’t even need to draw his sword; a few light punches were enough to pin them down and pummel them.

The three adventurers in the tavern today seemed to be White Silver rank: a young swordsman, a warrior wielding a massive axe, and a sweet-faced mage.

A standard party composition—two warriors and one mage.

At first, Merlin thought they were there to cause trouble for him, but that didn’t seem to be the case.

He pretended to wipe a glass nearby, but his ears were perked up, catching their conversation about goblins—

“Does this village really have goblins?” the burly, muscular warrior asked.

“Yeah, I heard those goblins live in the mountains behind the village.” The handsome swordsman nodded, taking a sip of beer.

“Really? Finally, we get to kill some goblins. I thought we’d have to go all the way to the Southern United Kingdom. I heard that place is full of non-humans who aren’t very friendly to humans—pretty dangerous.” The burly warrior sighed in relief, patting his shaved head.

“That’s great! The deadline for the quest is getting closer, and I was worried we wouldn’t finish in time.” The beautiful mage smiled, her shallow dimples making her look even cuter.

“How could that happen? Your fiancé is a famous information specialist. There’s nothing he can’t find.” The burly warrior grinned, baring his teeth.

The beautiful mage and the handsome swordsman both blushed, lowering their heads shyly. The two were lovers and already engaged—a couple of adventurers that others envied.

“D-Don’t tease us…” The beautiful mage lowered her head, her voice barely above a whisper.

“Tease you? Everyone already knows. You two are really an enviable pair…” The burly warrior chugged his beer, looking frustrated. “Agh! My all-FFF party isn’t having it! Why do all the good catches get snatched up by swordsmen?!”

“N-No, don’t say that…” The beautiful mage’s face burned with embarrassment, feeling utterly humiliated.

“Haha, let’s drop it. Back to the quest—we need to kill a hundred goblins, cut off their left ears, and turn them in to the guild. Then we’ll complete the quest and get five thousand gold coins.” The swordsman repeated the details of the commission.

“Goblins are worth that much?!” The burly warrior exclaimed in shock.

“I heard goblin ears have medicinal value.” The beautiful mage explained, seemingly well-read.

“Oh? So those green-skinned monsters are actually useful.” The burly warrior had an epiphany.

“As for the reward split, you can take two thousand gold coins.” The swordsman said.

“Huh? Why do I get more?” The burly warrior asked, puzzled, preferring an equal distribution.

“Because…” The swordsman glanced tenderly at the mage beside him and said seriously, “Once we finish this quest, we’re going back home to get married.”

“Hm?!” Merlin’s eyes widened, and his heart sank. That line was all too familiar—

Damn it!

That’s such an ominous thing to say!

This reeked of foreshadowing!

These three were definitely going to die…
