title: Chapter 40 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 40 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 40

The beautiful sorceress lowered her head shyly, her heart restless with nothing but sweetness at the thought of her upcoming marriage.

"Pfft!" The burly warrior was struck speechless the moment he heard this, spraying out the beer he had just drunk. "Seriously?! You two are actually going back home to get married?!"

"Mhm." The beautiful sorceress nodded, offering no further explanation—probably out of sheer shyness.

"Yeah, we’ve already talked it over. This is our last commission, so take as much money as you can. After all, our party’s breaking up, and from now on, you’ll have to find others to team up with or go solo." The handsome swordsman wore an apologetic look. "Sorry, forgive us for being so selfish."

"Don’t apologize! What’s there to be sorry about?! Getting married is a happy thing! I’m used to being alone anyway—going solo won’t be a problem! Don’t you dare feel guilty!" The burly warrior’s eyes welled up. After adventuring together for so long, the thought of parting ways filled him with quiet sorrow.

But marriage was a joyous occasion—stopping them would be cruel. All he could do was silently wish them well.

The swordsman and the sorceress exchanged a glance, unsure of what to say.

"Honestly, you should’ve told me sooner!" The burly warrior’s eyes reddened as he stood up and thumped the swordsman’s chest. "You bastard, you better treat her right, or I swear I’ll come to your hometown and beat you up!"

"Fine by me. You’re welcome to visit." The handsome swordsman nodded, the dissolution of their party weighing heavily on him.

"Don’t cry… It’s the first time I’ve ever seen you like this…" the beautiful sorceress consoled him.

"I’m not crying! I just… I’m just really envious of you two!" The burly warrior covered his face, his voice thick with emotion.

The swordsman and the sorceress were both moved, watching as the warrior wallowed in his own feelings.

"Barkeep! Ten beers over here!" the burly warrior shouted, ordering more drinks.

"Ten beers, coming right up." Martha replied.

Merlin watched from the side with detached calm, thinking to himself that even adventurers could share such deep bonds. He had assumed they’d just fight over commissions.

"Tonight’s on me. Let’s drink up," the burly warrior said, his mood gradually settling. "Who knows when we’ll get another chance to drink together like this."

"We’re hunting goblins tonight, so maybe we should go easy," the handsome swordsman hesitated.

"Yeah, maybe go easy," the beautiful sorceress agreed.

"You two are getting married and leaving—can’t even drink with me now?!" The warrior slammed his own chest in frustration. "Look down on us single guys, huh?!"

"Alright, alright, we’ll drink a little." The handsome swordsman wiped a cold sweat from his brow.

Martha arrived with the beers. "Here you go, ten beers."

The swordsman, upon seeing Martha, suddenly wanted to ask about the goblins. After all, he had only heard rumors and didn’t know the details.

"Barkeep, do you know where exactly the goblins on the back mountain are?"

"Well… I’ve heard they live underground." Martha wasn’t entirely sure either. Taverns were usually the best places for information, so she knew a thing or two.

"Underground, huh? Looks like we’ll need to search around." The handsome swordsman stroked his chin, muttering to himself.

Martha noticed the adventurer badges on their chests—silver rank. And since they were asking about goblins, they were probably heading to the back mountain.

"Are you planning to go up the mountain to hunt goblins?"

"Yep! We’re gonna kill a hundred green-skinned freaks!" The burly warrior downed a beer in one gulp.

"I advise you not to. The goblins on that mountain aren’t ordinary—they’re a branch of the royal lineage. They’ve never migrated to the Southern United Kingdom." Martha explained, hoping they’d back down. Even if the three of them were silver-ranked adventurers with mid-tier strength, fighting high-tier goblins would still be tough.

"Royal lineage? For lowly creatures like goblins? That’s a joke! HAHAHAHA…" The burly warrior roared with laughter.

"Of course they have royalty. Goblins are divided into tribes, each with their own emperor. And the tribe on the back mountain? Their emperor was already high-tier twenty years ago. Are you sure you’ll be fine?" Martha, being kind-hearted, felt she had to warn them properly.

The three were taken aback. The power gap between tiers was enormous—if there really was a high-tier enemy, they might not stand a chance.

"C’mon… what kind of joke is this? Goblins near a tiny village like this—how could there be a high-tier one? Martha, you’re messing with us, right?" The burly warrior didn’t believe it. If there were high-tier monsters around, this village would’ve been wiped out long ago.

"Yeah, Martha, don’t joke around. Even if there *is* a high-tier goblin, we can still run away." The handsome swordsman was skeptical too.

"I’m saying their emperor was high-tier *twenty years ago*, and now…" Martha paused, then said seriously, "he’s probably Saint-tier by this point."

The three exchanged glances, still disbelief in their eyes. A place this small couldn’t possibly have a Saint-tier monster—otherwise, wouldn’t there be rumors? Maybe Martha was just trying to scare them.

What they didn’t know was that the goblins on the back mountain had always lived underground, cut off from the outside world. How could anyone have known their emperor was Saint-tier?

"Thank you for the warning, but we still have to finish the commission. Please don’t try to scare us with baseless rumors." The sorceress politely declined Martha’s good intentions.

Martha sighed and said no more, turning away.

The three adventurers downed a few more beers before leaving in high spirits, ready to go on a killing spree that night.

Merlin didn’t say a word. None of this was his business.

Suffering from terminal laziness, Merlin hated trouble, so he simply played dumb.

He had no idea if Martha was telling the truth. But if the goblin emperor on the back mountain really was Saint-tier… well, Merlin *was* a little interested in taking it down. It’d be a nice +1s to his lifespan.

Martha watched their retreating figures with worry, sighing as she silently prayed, "I hope they come back safely."

Merlin, standing beside her, instantly felt a headache coming on. He shot her a strange look—

*Don’t say that, Martha!*

Those three had already set enough flags on their own.

And now you’ve gone and added another debuff on top of their heads for no reason!

This was a guaranteed death sentence—a big, poisonous mouthful of jinx…

title: Chapter 41
content:
Chapter 41

Volume 2 · Chapter 41

"Squeak squeak squeak!!!"

A green-skinned goblin shrieked in terror as it scrambled backward, only to be cleaved in two by a massive axe. Crimson blood sprayed outward, trickling across the ground.

The burly warrior hoisted his axe onto his shoulder, sneering as he wiped his nose. Behind him lay the corpses of many goblins.

"Hah! As expected of lowly creatures—so weak..."

After searching, the three adventurers had indeed found the goblin den. They slaughtered the weak goblins at the entrance without a single survivor.

"We can't let our guard down," the handsome swordsman said worriedly, still taking Martha's words to heart. "These are just ordinary goblins, sure, they're weak, but there are stronger ones out there. Like the giant goblins—they have strength close to high-rank monsters."

He decided that if they really encountered a giant goblin, they would have to leave immediately.

After all, giant goblins were called Royal Guards. That proved Martha was right—these goblins were of royal blood. It wouldn't be strange for them to have high-rank strength.

With their trio's power, facing a high-rank monster head-on would still leave a huge gap. They had to retreat quickly.

"Relax, I don't think there are any giant goblins here. We've gone this deep, and all we've seen are ordinary goblins. There's absolutely no danger. This quest is a piece of cake."

The warrior spoke boldly, finding the goblin fight effortless. He could take on ten by himself, no problem.

"I still think we should be careful," the handsome swordsman said uneasily, a hint of worry in his voice. "The deeper we go, the more goblins there are. This goblin clan doesn't seem like a small tribe..."

"It's fine, that tavern owner was just repeating rumors. Don't overthink it. We've been in this den for so long, and nothing's happened, right?" the female mage chimed in, her voice sweet and soothing.

"Yeah, you're just scaring yourself. Your wife has more guts than you do. I'm starting to lose respect for you," the burly warrior said, shaking his head.

The swordsman furrowed his brows and fell silent, trying to reassure himself. Maybe he was overthinking it.

The burly warrior slung his greataxe over his back, crouched down, and pulled out a dagger. He sliced off the ears of the dead goblins and tossed them to the female mage behind him.

"How many more do we need?"

The female mage put the goblin ears into her bag and replied, "Thirty-seven more goblins."

"Hahaha, we're almost done! This is too easy!" The burly warrior raised his battle-axe and shouted, "Let's keep moving forward!"

"Oh... yeah!" The female mage cheered happily, probably excited about nearly completing the quest.

The swordsman slapped his forehead, shaking off his anxious thoughts...

◆

The three continued deeper.

At first, the path was so narrow it barely fit a person.

But after dozens of steps, it suddenly opened up.

This mountain wasn't an ordinary goblin nest, filled with tunnels and small holes.

It was a true royal dwelling. The entire mountain had been hollowed out, with vast spaces deep inside.

And then there was the unmistakable structure—a pitch-black underground palace!

The three adventurers were stunned, their eyes wide, too shocked to speak.

By the firelight, they could faintly make out the grand palace. Massive goblin stone statues stood on either side, and the heavy iron gates bore the weight of years.

"Hey, hey, what is that? There's a palace underground?" the burly warrior muttered, dazed.

The female mage's mind went blank, her face pale with fear.

Only the swordsman managed to pull himself together. Remembering Martha's words and seeing the underground palace before him...

Royalty! That's right—these goblins were royalty! Their strength was definitely no lower than high-rank!

They absolutely couldn't go any further. They had to retreat immediately!

"We need to run! This is the territory of the Goblin Royalty! Now!"

"Okay!" The female mage panicked, realizing the tavern owner had been telling the truth all along!

"Oh..." The burly warrior responded blankly, still not fully grasping the situation.

The three turned to flee together—but then, disaster struck.

A giant goblin clad in silver armor, wielding a massive wolf-tooth club, crashed down from above, kicking up several feet of dust.

The trio was instantly separated—the swordsman and the mage on one side, the warrior isolated on the other.

"Watch out!!!"

The swordsman shouted, not wanting to abandon his companion, but it was too late.

The isolated warrior was terrified, his legs trembling uncontrollably. He stared up stupidly at the giant goblin, clearly frozen in fear, not even raising his weapon.

The giant goblin's eyes glowed crimson, its sharp teeth bared. Encased in silver armor, it exhaled a thick, white, scorching breath.

"Eh?" The warrior's mind went blank.

"ROAR!!!" The giant goblin let out a furious howl and swung its wolf-tooth club straight down.

The burly warrior was instantly torn apart, his flesh and blood exploding outward. He didn't even have time to scream before he was reduced to a pool of red mush!

The swordsman's eyes widened, staring in shock at the scene before him. His lively companion had been killed in an instant.

The warrior's remains still twitched, veins pulsing, but there was no sound.

The female mage snapped out of her daze, her face filled with terror as she let out a blood-curdling scream—

"Aaaaaaaaaahhhhhh!!!"

title: Chapter 42 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 42 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 42

Giant goblins actually exist?

They really are strong! Nearly high-tier power!

If I had known this, I should have listened to that innkeeper!

The swordsman’s face was filled with terror—this was his first time seeing a giant goblin. Setting aside its strength, the sheer size of the creature was enough to strike fear into anyone’s heart.

A single giant goblin was enough to wipe out three entire mid-tier adventurer parties.

"Ah... he's dead. Killed in just one hit..."

The female mage couldn’t bear the shock. Her legs gave out, and she collapsed onto the ground.

Seeing his companion was already dead, the swordsman’s strong will forced him to make a choice.

The dead were dead. The living had to survive!

"Run!"

The swordsman abruptly turned, grabbed the mage from the ground, and activated his battle aura, sprinting at full speed toward the exit.

Even with mid-tier battle aura at full power, his speed was still impressive.

But things weren’t that simple—

A surge of high-tier magical energy rippled through the air. Before the swordsman and the mage, a towering wall of blazing fire erupted!

Though the Fire Wall spell was mid-tier, under the amplification of high-tier magic, its temperature was terrifyingly high. Forcing their way through would surely turn them to ash!

The two were stunned. Staring at the scorching barrier, it seemed their only option was a desperate last stand—though their chances of survival were slim.

Cold sweat poured down the swordsman’s face. The moment he sensed high-tier magical energy, he knew they were doomed. Besides the Goblin Emperor, what other powerful being could be here?

And indeed, there was! The one who cast the Fire Wall wasn’t the Goblin Emperor. For three mere adventurers to intrude, it wasn’t worth the Emperor’s time—just a single purple-skinned goblin, Gega the Shaman, was more than enough!

"What’s all that noise outside? I thought something serious happened. Turns out it’s just three rats sneaking into our territory. How amusing~"

A shrill voice echoed from the darkness, accompanied by the clattering of armor.

Gega the Shaman, draped in a black robe, appeared at the head of a fully armed goblin army—three hundred strong.

The three adventurers had picked the worst possible time to intrude. At this moment, they were facing a fully mobilized and well-equipped goblin force.

"I am Gega, the tribe’s chancellor. I welcome your arrival, you inferior creatures. However, according to our rules, the females will be captured and trained into slaves, while the males will be killed on the spot." Gega gave a slight bow, his manner polite, but his tone dripping with malice.

The swordsman shielded the female mage behind him, his mind reeling. If a high-tier being was only a chancellor, how terrifying must the Emperor be? Had he already reached the legendary Saint-tier?! Coming here was clearly a mistake!

"My advice? Think carefully. Don’t resist pointlessly..." Gega laid out the terms, with no pretense of fairness.

"Are you joking?!" The swordsman drew the straight blade at his waist, ready to fight to the death. He never expected these monsters to target his fiancée! He couldn’t tolerate that! Even if he died, he wouldn’t let them have their way!

"Tsk! Disobedient, are we? Then there’s nothing to be done..." A sinister grin twisted across Gega’s sharp-featured face. He gave an order to the giant goblin: "Deal with them. Leave the girl alive—I have uses for her."

"Hrrooo..." The giant goblin let out a grunt, raised its spiked club, and charged like a wild beast. Each step shook the earth with a thunderous boom.

"Tch!" The swordsman raised his sword, pointing it at the giant goblin, and barked, "Hit me with every buff you’ve got!"

"Ah?! O-okay..." The female mage was clearly terrified, her reactions sluggish. She raised her staff, and magic surged as she began casting every enhancement spell she knew—

"Mid-tier Strength Boost!"

"Mid-tier Agility Boost!"

"Mid-tier Precision Boost!"

"Bleed Effect Enchantment!"

"Fire Attribute Enchantment!"

"Critical Hit Damage +200%!"

"Wind Spirit Formation, Second Phase—Activate!!!"

title: Chapter 43
content:
Chapter 43

Volume 2 · Chapter 43

The Wind Spirit Formation unfolded, a barrier magic that combined offense and defense. Not only did it enhance the agility of allies, but it could also instantly unleash a barrage of wind blades without incantation.

The mage girl poured all her mana into maintaining the barrier’s operation, clearly entering a state of readiness. Though she didn’t know if they could win, she was determined to fight with everything she had.

"OOOOOOHHHH!!!"

The swordsman’s body burned with a dazzling, flame-like aura—this was the effect of stacking multiple buff spells. He felt an enormous surge of mana flooding his body, granting him several times his usual strength. It was as if he had been reborn, his entire being transformed.

Even the sword in his hand, now imbued with fire enchantment, glowed crimson like a red-hot branding iron, crackling with energy.

The swordsman felt invincible. Even if his opponent was a fully armored giant goblin, he believed he could take it on!

"I can do this! I can win!"

"Foolish..." Gega Witch lifted her eyelids slightly, not even bothering to take the buffed swordsman seriously.

The giant goblin swung its spiked club with a wild, frenzied roar and charged forward!

The swordsman set his stance, his mid-tier battle aura boiling within him, his gaze unwavering.

"Blazing Cross Slash!!!"

With a sudden burst of movement, he didn’t retreat—instead, he surged forward, clashing head-on with the giant goblin!

His figure vanished from its original spot in an instant, reappearing right in front of the giant goblin in the blink of an eye. Boosted by multiple agility buffs, his speed was indeed terrifying, almost brushing against the threshold of high-tier power.

Leaping into the air, he swiftly swung his red-hot blade, slashing out a fiery cross in a single motion.

The flames illuminated the darkness, casting light on the faces of the swordsman and the giant goblin. This was a duel where only one would walk away alive!

The fiery cross, infused with both magic and battle aura, roared toward the giant goblin.

This could work!

If one of them wasn’t enough, then two of them together definitely would be!

I have to get her out of here, then take her back home and marry her!

The swordsman still hadn’t given up hope. Like a true warrior, he fought with everything he had.

If Merlin had been there, he might have coughed up a mouthful of blood from the swordsman’s endless flag-planting.

The Blazing Cross struck the giant goblin’s chest, instantly denting its armor and carving a massive cross-shaped gash into it. The searing attack burned straight into the goblin’s flesh.

"AAAAAARRRRGGGHHH—"

The giant goblin howled in agony, the green fur on its chest completely scorched away.

The swordsman landed on the ground, lifting his head to look at the writhing giant goblin. A smile unconsciously spread across his face. Had he succeeded? It looked like it was over...

In truth, the swordsman had no real understanding of power. Though the giant goblin was clumsy, its attack and defense were extraordinarily high—not to mention it was clad in a full set of refined armor.

As the flames dissipated, the giant goblin was only slightly charred on the chest. That devastating attack had only caused a minor injury—far from fatal.

"Eh? Why..." The swordsman’s expression turned blank, doubt creeping into his mind. That had been his strongest attack, yet it felt like he’d only given the goblin a light scratch.

"Watch out!!!" The mage girl shouted a warning, but it was too late—the enemy had already made its move.

The giant goblin raised its massive spiked club, swinging it like a golf club with lightning speed. It struck the swordsman’s side with a crushing blow.

He didn’t even have time to scream. Countless bones shattered in his body. The overwhelming force sent him flying like a cannonball, slamming into the hard rock wall before he collapsed to the ground, his fate uncertain.

"Darling!" The mage girl shrieked in shock, her face twisted in terror. If the swordsman died, her own fate would be just as grim.

The giant goblin didn’t stop its assault. In a few strides, it stood before the mage girl, looming over her. Its bloodshot eyes rolled wildly as it snorted a jet of white, scalding breath from its nostrils.

"Ah... ah... ah..."

The mage girl tilted her head back, staring up at the giant goblin. Tears streamed down her face, her complexion pale as paper, her gaze unfocused with fear.

She felt like she was already dead. She didn’t know how her fiancé was doing—if he was even alive. Even if he survived, he’d be in terrible shape.

"Stay away from me!!!"

The Wind Spirit Formation activated, unleashing over twenty wind blades in an instant. They all struck the giant goblin’s chest, but only left a few shallow cuts—completely ineffective.

"Why..." The mage girl’s expression turned hollow. She gave up resisting. After using all her techniques, she still couldn’t even defeat a single giant goblin.

"Before absolute power, what use are flashy skills? That’s why humans are an inferior species—so stupid..." Gega Witch sneered, her voice dripping with malice.

The giant goblin grabbed the mage girl and hurled her toward the goblin army behind it.

"AAAAAAHHHH!"

The countless goblins, who had been watching for a while, let out lecherous laughter and swarmed forward, surrounding the mage girl. Without hesitation, they began tearing at her clothes, their depraved hands violating her.

"Ahhhh!"

"Noooo!"

"Please, stop!"

"Some... someone, save me! Please!"

Though severely wounded, the swordsman still clung to life. With his enhanced gear, he could just barely make out the horrifying sight of his fiancée being humiliated by the goblins.

Hatred burned deep in his heart, seeping into his bones. But his shattered body refused to move. All he could do was watch, his mind clear but his body broken beyond repair.

"You... you bastards... let her go..."

Tears of regret streamed down the swordsman’s face. Blood poured from his forehead like a curtain, and though he screamed, his voice was weak and powerless.

"Save me! Save me!!! Please, spare me, stop it!"

His fiancée, the mage, was still crying for help, but he could do nothing. All he could manage was a feeble curse.

"You help these bastards! I swear... I’ll kill every last one of you! Not a single one will be left alive!"

The swordsman mustered every ounce of strength to spit out those words, but they changed nothing.

The purple-skinned goblin, Gega Witch, approached the battered swordsman. She cruelly grabbed his hair, forcing him to meet her gaze as she spoke with a sinister grin, "You want to save her?"

"You... you monster..." The swordsman glared at Gega Witch’s ugly, twisted face. His expression turned feral, teeth gnashing in fury as blood from his forehead dripped into his mouth, staining his teeth red.

"Kekekekeke..." Gega Witch let out a string of eerie laughter, narrowing her beady eyes before saying—

"Fine. I’ll give you a chance."

"All you have to do... is make a deal with us..."

Alright, the setup for Volume 2 is complete. The climax starts next. In the next chapter, my wife Alice will make her return! Also, please throw me some monthly votes, everyone. Thanks a bunch!

title: Chapter 44 — Bonus Chapter (Wife Logs In)
content:
Chapter 44 — Bonus Chapter (Wife Logs In)

Volume 2 · Chapter 44

Alice Claudia, a missing person, had returned.

This girl, who had been thoroughly humiliated by Merlin, had also been living a rather miserable life over the past year.

Having stolen her master’s holy sword, she was too afraid of being spanked by him to return to the Alps. Instead, she had been hiding out in Great Britain, continuing her life there.

As for why? She simply didn’t want to go back. If she did, her master would probably lock her up for harsh training again, and she’d never get to see the colorful world outside.

Life on the outside wasn’t easy either, but it was still better than the Alps.

Ordinary people couldn’t understand what it was like to live on a snowy mountain—endlessly surrounded by blizzards, freezing temperatures, no good food, and often waking up in the middle of the night from the cold.

Alice was already nineteen this year. As a girl in the prime of her youth, she would rather die than return to that life in the Alps. So now, she was scraping by on her own, barely making ends meet.

Ever since parting ways with Merlin on the northern coast, she had been living a bitter life.

The reason was the 233rd Crusade’s failure—she had been the sole survivor, and as a result, she had been blamed for everything.

Alice had a huge argument with those stinking holy fanatics in the Church. Due to their disagreement, she threw away the title of Hero and left the Holy Church.

She didn’t think the failure of the Crusade was her fault at all. The First Demon Lord Palace’s Great Demon Lord was a pervert beyond human capability to defeat. It was only natural that the Holy Church kept losing.

Alice could still vividly recall how Merlin had annihilated the Crusade Army with a single strike, even splitting the sea in half. Just thinking about it sent a chill down her spine. If she hadn’t been so lucky, she probably would have died in the 233rd First Demon Lord Crusade as well.

Of course, for Alice, the worst part wasn’t those holy fanatics dumping all the blame on her. It was Merlin stealing her mithril armor, which had caused her long-term and terrible consequences.

That luxurious set of equipment had actually been borrowed. After the Crusade, it was supposed to be returned. But Merlin stole it, leaving her unable to pay it back. As a result, she owed the Holy Church a huge debt—several tens of millions of gold coins.

However, considering she had once been a Hero, the Holy Church didn’t force her to repay it all at once. Instead, they allowed her to pay it back in installments, like a loan.

Alice, like Merlin, didn’t have any practical skills to earn money.

But unlike Merlin, Alice wasn’t lazy. She was hardworking. So now, she was working hard to support herself, paying back the Holy Church every month without it affecting her life too much.

Unlike Merlin, who, as soon as he had money, would throw it all away at the royal racetrack, and even during work hours, he’d be swindling women left and right.

Alice wasn’t rich, and she didn’t live in a beautiful castle, but she was managing to get by.

Even now, Alice despised Merlin deeply. If it weren’t for him, her life would be much better.

Merlin was like a broom star in her life, ruining everything good. Whenever she encountered him, nothing good ever happened.

So Alice had prayed countless times in her heart that she would never meet Merlin again in this lifetime. She hoped that this perverted, ill-intentioned bastard would disappear from this world forever.

Because in Alice’s worldview, anyone who mocked her for being flat-chested was definitely not a good person!

Now, Alice had been living in Wales for nearly a year, residing in Wrexham County.

As for her current profession?

Just look at the golden badge on her chest. That’s right—it was the proof of an adventurer, with her name and affiliated guild engraved on the back.

Alice had registered with the Adventurers Guild in Wrexham. With her high-tier strength, she had become a Gold-rank adventurer and started a new work life.

Today, Alice was riding her little donkey cart to a remote village in Wales—also the village where Merlin was.

Alice had accepted a joint commission from a group of restaurant owners posted at the guild: to capture a Scottish freeloader.

She had recently heard that this criminal had come to Wales and had been spotted in this village. So Alice’s task was to investigate and bring this pretty boy back to collect the substantial bounty.

◆

The sun gradually set in the west.

A leisurely rural breeze blew, and golden waves of wheat swayed from side to side.

Autumn—a season of both harvest and decay.

On a nearby tree, a pair of flesh-colored stockings hung, left behind from when Merlin had slain a thief not long ago. Now covered in dust, they fluttered like a flag, foretelling that the days ahead would not be peaceful.

But Alice paid no attention to these things. She sat on her little donkey cart, swaying back and forth.

The cart creaked as it advanced toward the small village.

Alice looked at the commission notice in her hands, her eyes fixed on the bounty of 5,000 gold coins. The stern expression on her face melted away, replaced by a radiant, joyful smile.

At this moment, she should have had a special effect: *Duang~* Countless flowers blooming in unison!

“5,000 gold coins! A freeloading pretty boy is actually worth this much? It should be easy to catch him, right? This is a huge score! I can buy so many pretty clothes, and I won’t have to worry about rent anymore. Hehehe~”

(?′ω`?)

The little donkey neighed softly, as if agreeing with its master’s mutterings, and steadily made its way toward the village.

This naive, cute little girl, Alice, had no idea that the Scottish freeloader was actually Merlin—the very culprit who had made her life so miserable.

All Alice could think about was the 5,000 gold coins. Little did she know, soon she would be reminded of the terror of once being dominated by Merlin, and the humiliation of being pinned down and rubbed against the ground by the Demon Lord.

The flag Alice had planted a year ago on the northern coast—*never to meet Merlin again*—was about to come true today.

But the question was—

Who does Heaven spare?

It seemed the karmic bond between the flat-chested Hero and the lecherous Demon Lord had only just begun…

Alice’s character, Merlin’s wife is amazing!

Don’t criticize her chest, the setting will be explained soon.

Still, I really need a few more monthly votes… I’m in dire need of them…

title: Chapter 45
content:
Chapter 45

Volume 2 · Chapter 45

Alice felt another easy payday coming her way—after all, a freeloading bum like this should be no trouble to take down.

A smug warmth spread through her. That 5,000 gold felt like a gust of wind had blown it straight into her hands. Delightful...

But the real problem with this commission wasn’t the difficulty—it was the wanted poster. The artist had to be out of his mind!

The bounty painter in Rexham was a man obsessed with "art." His work was practically abstract—no recognizable human forms, just chaotic scribbles that looked like they’d been made by a madman or a toddler. Yet in Wales, this style was all the rage, hailed as high art. It was enough to drive anyone insane.

As if the job wasn’t troublesome enough, this "soul artist" had to make it even harder. Comparing the poster to actual people was impossible—you’d find a hundred monsters that looked more like the sketch than any human ever could.

Seriously… did anyone actually look like a brick?

And to make matters worse, the artist had a lazy eye. His wanted posters were a complete mess—every face had double features: four eyes, two mouths, two noses, four ears.

emmmm…

*Damn it! Whoever drew this, step forward if you’ve got the guts!*
*I, Alice, swear I’ll beat you to death today!*
*What the hell is this?! Is this even a human?! Only inbred siblings could produce something this deformed!*

Fuming as she was, Alice was eventually informed by the Guild receptionist of the *correct* way to use the poster.

Because the artist had a lazy eye, she had to cross her own eyes to see the image properly.

A lazy eye? How ridiculous!

A wanted poster shouldn’t be this cryptic—it’s like some imperial code!

I’m a lady! Making a face like this is so undignified! I have an image to maintain! Crossing my eyes ruins my entire aura!

Alice had a million complaints, but for the sake of the job, she’d still squint at the poster… just in secret, when no one was looking.

Across the entire British Empire, only the adventurers of Rexham were known as the "cross-eyed hicks."

Because they were always crossing their eyes to read wanted posters, making them look utterly foolish.

Who knew how many male and female adventurers in Rexham had lost love because of this habit? Maybe that’s why their single rate was through the roof.

At this point, all she could do was shout:

*Soul Artist, you win! The world needs people like you for population control! You should write a book: "He Changed Rexham’s Adventurers Forever!"*

Right now, Alice was skulking around like a thief, nervously scanning her surroundings. Only when she was sure no one was watching did she finally cross her eyes and stare at the poster.

Her two blue pupils converged in the middle, making her look absurd—completely at odds with her usual cool demeanor. If anyone saw her, they’d probably burst out laughing.

Then, the image split in two. The abstract lines shifted, and for a moment… she could almost make something out.

After a few seconds, her eyes returned to normal.

She froze, hand pressed to her forehead, a look of revulsion creeping over her face—

*What the hell…?*

*Am I seeing things?*

*Why does the guy on this poster…*

*…kind of look like that bastard from the First Demon Lord Palace?*

(?-_?)??

title: Chapter 46 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 46 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 46

Even though the wanted poster’s criminal bore a slight resemblance to Merlin, Alice didn’t dwell on it—she figured it was just her imagination, or maybe a passing similarity.

After all, she had gone out of her way to avoid Merlin, leaving Scotland entirely and fleeing all the way to Wales in the southwest, crossing through several regions.

If she still managed to run into him here, Alice would feel like she’d been cursed with the worst luck imaginable, as if life itself had become unbearable.

Right now, Alice was riding in a small donkey cart as she entered the village, the time nearing evening.

Thanks to her status as an adventurer, she was exempt from tolls and passed through without any trouble.

The setting sun painted the sky a fiery red, and the light was beginning to dim.

A few houses glowed with warm lamplight, looking cozy and inviting. Most shops had already closed, but places like taverns and inns were still lively and open for lodging.

Even in a small village, most people seemed to enjoy the nightlife…

Though Alice was eager to start work immediately—gathering information on the whereabouts of that freeloading pretty boy from Scotland—it was getting too late to take action.

She had no choice but to find an inn for the night and begin her search for the wanted criminal first thing in the morning.

But since this was her first time in the village, she wasn’t familiar with the area. Just then, she noticed an older woman selling fruit nearby, packing up her stall to head home.

Without hesitation, Alice led her donkey over to her.

“Uh… I’m an adventurer from out of town. Do you know of any good places to stay here?”

“Hmm? An outsider?” The woman set down her fruit basket and gave Alice a once-over. “Our village has plenty of taverns and inns. What kind are you looking for?”

“Just somewhere I can relax.” Alice’s standards weren’t high—she just wanted a quiet place to rest, and maybe somewhere she could feed her donkey.

But the woman’s mind went straight to the gutter, misinterpreting Alice’s words. After all, Merlin’s stage name, “Little Daisy,” was fairly well-known in the village.

(Little Daisy was Merlin’s working alias)

Many women would visit the Moonlight Tavern in the evenings to drink and chat with Merlin. The next morning, their emotional wounds would be healed.

“Relax, huh? Oh~” The woman’s expression turned knowing, as if she saw right through Alice.

Oh what oh? Why do I sense something perverted in the air?

Alice’s delicate brows furrowed slightly. Something felt off.

“Over there,” the woman said, pointing in a certain direction with a meaningful look. “If you follow this street, you’ll find the Moonlight Tavern. They specialize in serving female guests at this hour.”

“Oh?” Alice perked up. Female-only? That was perfect. Every other inn she’d stayed in had been loud—filled with the stench of sweaty men, the reek of alcohol, and the occasional brawl, the clanging noise keeping her awake all night.

“Martha’s Moonlight Tavern is quite unique, especially in the evenings. If you’re new here, I highly recommend checking it out. They say Brother Little Daisy even puts on a heartwarming performance at night.” The woman spoke with great enthusiasm, clearly holding Merlin in high regard.

“Tha… thank you,” Alice forced a smile and thanked her, then led her donkey toward the Moonlight Tavern, her face burning as she thought to herself—

What the hell is “Little Daisy”?

Couldn’t he have picked a normal stage name?!

Ever since that London doctor declared that a certain part of the body resembled a blooming chrysanthemum…

I can never look at the word “daisy” the same way again…

(??ω?? ?)

title: Chapter 47
content:
Chapter 47

Volume 2 · Chapter 47

Alice tied the donkey outside and entered the Moonlit Tavern.

At first glance, it seemed quite ordinary, but just as the fruit vendor had said, every customer inside was a woman.

The scene before her felt less like a tavern and more like a nighttime gathering—there wasn’t any particular sense of chaos.

A makeshift stage was being set up in the center of the tavern; she had no idea what it was for.

Though Alice guessed it might be for some kind of performance…

In the distance, a few people were polishing instruments, seemingly preparing for the evening’s work.

What truly surprised Alice was the female patrons—each one was dressed to the nines, vying for attention in their finery.

Was this really a tavern?

It felt more like a masquerade ball…

Alice couldn’t help but furrow her delicate brows, confusion stirring in her mind. This was the first time she’d encountered something like this.

In truth, all of this was Merlin’s idea—turning the evening tavern into a real-world bar, using music and performances to set the mood, getting the female patrons hyped, and then ruthlessly draining their wallets.

“Is this your first time here, dear?”

Just as Alice stood there, lost in thought with a puzzled expression, Martha, dressed in a puffy skirt, approached her.

Judging by Alice’s attire, she looked like a traveler from out of town—probably a first-time visitor.

“Mm, I’m an adventurer from Rexham. I was wondering if you have any rooms available? I’d like to stay the night.” Alice spoke up, thinking she only wanted a place to rest, not to join in the fun.

Martha glanced at the golden badge on Alice’s chest and was taken aback. She hadn’t expected a Gold-ranked adventurer to show up in their village—it was a rare sight, and she couldn’t help but feel a little surprised.

A Gold-ranked adventurer must have considerable strength, right?

Though strength wasn’t the sole criterion for ranking adventurers—some could advance through experience alone—but it still gave a rough measure of their abilities.

After all, when becoming an adventurer, the initial assessment was based on strength. The stronger you were, the higher your starting rank.

Those with low-tier strength could start as Iron-ranked adventurers, mid-tier as Silver, and high-tier as Gold.

As for Saint-tier, they might start as Mithril-ranked adventurers, but since there were no known cases of Saint-tier powerhouses switching to adventuring mid-career, no one was entirely sure.

“Of course we have rooms available. Please, follow me, esteemed adventurer.”

Martha’s tone was exceedingly polite. Gold-ranked adventurers were uncommon, and most of them were formidable.

Rumor had it that across the entire Great Britannian Empire, there were only a few hundred Gold-ranked adventurers, a few dozen Mithril, and a mere handful of Adamantite—whose identities remained unknown to the public.

The only publicly known Adamantite-ranked adventurer was the old guildmaster of the London Adventurers Guild, who possessed Saint-tier strength.

So Alice, as a Gold-ranked adventurer, was quite rare and commanded respect in the eyes of ordinary folk.

Moreover, Alice was genuinely a high-tier powerhouse, making her one of the stronger figures in Great Britannia.

Alice followed Martha to the counter, received a room key, and paid for the room and deposit with a single gold coin.

“Your room is 206. It’s upstairs, take a left and you’ll find it.” Martha said with a smile.

“Oh, alright.” Alice nodded, glancing at the room number on the key.

“If you feel like coming down later to enjoy the show, you’re welcome to. The performance is free. Tonight, our tavern’s heartthrob will be doing a hot dance.” Martha enthusiastically added, sensing Alice was an out-of-towner who might be curious about local customs. “It’s quite a sight, very exotic. You should definitely come down and watch if you’re interested.”

Oh come on…

A *hot dance*? So this *is* a disreputable place!

Do I look like the kind of person who, when feeling lonely, can’t resist watching men do stripteases?

Alice’s face flushed as she cleared her throat, forcing a serious expression.

“No need. I’m just here to stay the night.”

“Alright then, I won’t disturb you further.” Martha broke into a cold sweat—she hadn’t expected to be turned away so bluntly.

Just as Alice was about to head upstairs, she suddenly remembered that taverns were hubs of information. Maybe there’d be leads on that freeloading, good-for-nothing pretty boy from Scotland.

“Barkeep, there’s something I’d like to ask about.”

“Yes, what is it?” Martha nodded.

Alice took out the wanted poster and showed it to Martha. “Have you seen this man?”

Martha took a look, her expression turning unnatural. *What in the world did this soul artist draw?* It was hideous!

“N-No… I haven’t.”

“Is that so? Then I’ve troubled you. Sorry.”

Alice put away the wanted poster and headed straight upstairs.

A flood of black lines slid down her forehead as she awkwardly thought—

Damn it!

How am I supposed to tell someone to squint and *carefully* examine this with crossed eyes…

I can’t even say it out loud! Bastard!

Wouldn’t I get hit for that?

((???|||))

◆

Alice arrived upstairs and used her key to open the door to room 206, stepping inside.

At that moment, the door to room 207 next door also opened, and Merlin stepped out, wrapped tightly in a military greatcoat.

Why a greatcoat?

Because in the eyes of women, men in uniform were irresistibly sexy—it easily stirred their desires. Plus, Merlin had layered a lot underneath, so when he performed, he could take forever stripping, buying time.

It seemed Merlin had fully embraced his role as a male escort—specifically the kind that sold *flesh*, where the women would go wild throwing money the moment he started undressing.

As Merlin stepped out, he caught a glimpse of Alice’s profile—her cascading silver hair, her breathtaking beauty. Only her chest seemed a bit… off, as if she’d stuffed padding for appearance’s sake.

Alice entered her room, and Merlin only caught that fleeting glance—he hadn’t seen her clearly.

But even that single glance left him unsettled, doubt creeping into his mind.

Merlin lifted his eyelids, stroking his chin as he muttered to himself—

*What the—?*

Why does this girl look so familiar?

She kinda resembles that flat-chested Hero from a year ago…

No, no, that can’t be. Must be my imagination.

Because that idiot Alice…

How could *she* possibly have a chest? Hahahaha!

title: Chapter 48 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 48 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 48

Alice let out a long sigh of relief as soon as she entered the room, feeling utterly exhausted.

She unbuckled the slender sword at her waist, *Hymn of Light*, and set it aside before flopping onto the bed.

The soft mattress bounced her up and down several times.

"Ahhh~... I survived..."

Alice’s usual stern demeanor melted away, her face flushed and girlish as she pressed herself into the plush bed, wishing she could merge with it entirely.

Over the past year, she had been through so much—like the Redbeard Brothers’ raid on Elkin City half a year ago.

She had been involved in that incident too. At the time, she had only gone to deal with a wild boar attacking Elkin’s villagers, but she stumbled upon the Redbeard Brothers launching a surprise assault on the city from their pirate ship.

When she heard they had kidnapped the count’s daughter, justice-driven little guardian that she was, she immediately volunteered to rescue the hostage.

The result? She got thoroughly thrashed by the Redbeard Brothers and ended up locked in a cell with the mayor’s daughter, destined to be sold as a high-class slave to another country.

If the Redbeard Brothers hadn’t been a couple, Alice might have suffered an even worse fate.

Her sense of justice bordered on foolishness. Even knowing both brothers were Saint-tier powerhouses, she still charged in to save someone. Maybe she just couldn’t bear to see others suffer. Her heart was too soft.

Even after being captured, she kept comforting the weeping count’s daughter, which left her frazzled. The girl was the same age as her, yet so fragile—like a flower raised in a greenhouse.

With magic and aura-sealing shackles on her wrists, Alice was powerless. Without her strength, what made her different from any ordinary girl?

Late that night, as she feared being sold to cannibals, a tremendous surge of sword energy tore through everything in its path. The ship split in two, and the prison door was shattered.

Freed, Alice took the count’s daughter and fled the cell, emerging onto the deck to find the pirate ship in ruins.

Flames engulfed the vessel as it slowly sank, punctuated by occasional explosions.

Alice had no idea what was happening, but she saw the pirate crew staring in terror at a man standing at the central mast, their voices shaking as they shouted—

"We’re doomed! The captain’s dead! Run for your lives! That man’s an absolute monster!"

Alice followed their gaze and saw the dark silhouette of a man casually picking his nose, muttering to himself, "Phew~... Feels good. Almost triggered the curse..."

She assumed he was some righteous hero who had single-handedly taken down the Saint-tier Redbeard Brothers to save Elkin’s people.

It had been a stormy night with no moonlight, visibility near zero. Most couldn’t make out his features—only the fluttering black cloak, his little finger twisting in his nostril, and his waist-length hair whipping in the wind.

When is a girl’s IQ at its lowest?

The answer, of course, is when she’s in love!

Alice found the man powerful, just, and with that lonely figure against the desolate scene, his voice young—he was the dream prince of countless girls’ hearts!

Her face flushed unnaturally, her heart pounding as her IQ seemed to plummet. She turned into a flustered fangirl, thinking that even if the man was picking his nose... he was still damn hot!

Just as Alice was lost in her daydream, squads of royal marines in red uniforms boarded the pirate ship. Their commander, the governor, bellowed, "Fire! Kill that bastard who destroyed royal navy property!"

Without hesitation, the marines raised their long-barrelled rifles and opened fire. Bullets whizzed through the air, and by the time Alice snapped out of it, the man she had been admiring was gone.

Later, she searched for a long time but never found him. He had appeared out of nowhere and vanished just the same.

Alice felt a pang of frustration. He had saved her, yet she hadn’t even been able to thank him. He was like a knight in her life—appearing in her hour of need, then disappearing without a trace.

Truthfully, Alice’s heart had fluttered. She wanted to meet him again. Who knew? Maybe something more could develop.

Alice was such a simple girl. That man, hailed as Elkin’s legendary swordsman, was actually none other than Merlin, the lord of the First Demon Lord Palace—the very person she despised!

If this lovestruck, fangirling fool ever found out that the man she idolized was actually Merlin, the one she hated most, she’d probably lose her mind on the spot...

Even now, recalling it all made her heart race.

She grabbed a feather pillow and buried her burning face in it, giggling shyly to herself—

"The legendary swordsman of Elkin... so cool..."

title: Chapter 49
content:
Chapter 49

Volume 2 · Chapter 49

Now Alice finally understood her master’s words.

The world outside was far greater than she had imagined—there was always someone better, a higher heaven beyond every sky.

Her own strength wasn’t all that impressive either. There were so many things she couldn’t do, and the gap between her ambition and ability was painfully clear.

She wanted to shoulder greater responsibilities, but her power just wasn’t enough. It left her with a lingering sense of regret.

Yet Alice couldn’t help but meddle in others’ affairs, always landing herself in trouble.

In her mind, if someone was about to die, how could she just stand by and watch? Taking action was better than being a cold, detached observer. She wasn’t weak or cowardly.

Alice sighed, wondering if she should return to her master’s side and continue her grueling training.

She felt she had already trained relentlessly, but then she met Merlin—that freak—and began to question her entire life.

She was a dual cultivator of magic and martial arts, which made her training far more complex and difficult than most. After more than a year, her strength had barely improved at all.

Was all her hard work really worth it? She might never even touch Merlin’s heels in her lifetime… the humiliation of it all still stung.

Alice did admire Merlin’s strength, but she couldn’t stand his character. He was a demon, through and through—cunning, wicked, the kind of man who could slaughter a hundred thousand Crusade soldiers without batting an eye. The perfect cold-blooded villain, the ultimate boss.

Compared to the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace, Alice much preferred the legendary swordsman Elgin. Rumor had it he had defeated the Redbeard Brothers with a single strike—his power unfathomable.

Who was stronger between the two? Alice couldn’t say. Both were incredibly powerful, but their natures couldn’t have been more different.

The Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace was undeniably evil—a merciless ruler who killed without hesitation.

The legendary swordsman Elgin, on the other hand, was a paragon of justice. To save a coastal city, he had single-handedly faced two Saint-tier powerhouses and killed them in an instant, then vanished without a trace, leaving no name behind.

Alice found that kind of just, powerful, and selflessly humble man incredibly attractive. Compared to him, the Great Demon Lord was nothing but scum.

Both wielded great swords, yet the difference in their character was like heaven and earth.

In truth, Alice had put the legendary swordsman Elgin on far too high a pedestal. He wasn’t some noble figure—resolving his crisis had just been a passing convenience.

Alice lay in bed, her thoughts tossing and turning as she compared the arrogant monarch and the legendary swordsman over and over.

Little did she know, both were the same person—Merlin, a penniless, gambling-addicted, fast-talking swindler.

And at that very moment, the man behind both legends had fallen so low that he was working as a gigolo, preparing for a hot dance performance downstairs.

After daydreaming for a long while, Alice decided it was time to write a letter to her master on the Alps’ snowy peaks.

She would spend a few extra silver coins to hide her return address, so her master couldn’t track her down.

Sitting at her desk, she took out stationery, dipped her quill, and wrote—

Dear Master,

I am living very well now. I reside in a magnificent castle, with no want for food or clothing, and an endless stream of glamorous balls to attend.

I have so much money I don’t know what to do with it. I owe no massive debts to the Holy Church, and I never worry about rent.

I’ve even fallen in love with Long Aotian. You’ve probably heard of him—he’s the legendary swordsman of Elgin.

So my future is truly bright. I certainly won’t end up like you, a spinster for life!

Alice added a few more lines of well-wishes, then set down her quill with a long sigh.

She gazed out the window at the vast, moonlit night, the glow of the moonlight shimmering on her beautiful hair.

The party downstairs seemed to have begun; faint strains of exotic music drifted up.

Alice pressed her palms together in a gesture of piety, her expression as devout as a church nun, and silently recited the prayer (curse) she offered every day—

“God, may I never encounter that bastard Merlin in this life.”

“He’s a filthy pervert with a mind full of impurity. Please, let him be punished.”

“Let him become a worthless vagrant, penniless until his dying day, forced to live as a lowly gigolo. May he lose every gamble, have the worst luck, and never rise above his miserable fate.”

◆

Downstairs, the music boomed.

The stage was set, and the performance was about to begin.

Merlin, dressed in a sexy military uniform, was ready to fleece the women of their money.

But suddenly, he couldn’t help but let out a loud sneeze.

Merlin furrowed his brow, rubbing his nose as he muttered to himself in confusion—

What the hell?

Why do I always sneeze at this time every day?

Is someone cursing me behind my back?

Who could it be? Do they hate me that much…

title: Chapter 50 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 50 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 50

The tavern at night.

Alice sat at a distant table, having ordered a glass of milk. She didn’t like alcohol—milk and juice were much better.

Driven by overwhelming curiosity, she couldn’t resist coming downstairs to see for herself.

Don’t get the wrong idea—Alice wasn’t interested in male stripteases.

But so many women had come to watch this so-called “Little Daisy” dance; there must be something special about him.

So Alice decided to take a look. Just what kind of magic did this “Little Daisy” possess?

Besides, she had nothing to do in her room. Might as well join the excitement.

The makeshift stage was decently built, and the hired band played a strange melody.

Even Alice, who considered herself well-traveled, couldn’t place where this music was from.

The women crowded around the runway, seemingly full of anticipation.

What in the world was this “Little Daisy”?

Didn’t these women realize they were being scammed out of their money?

So the saying “big chest, no brains” really was true. Honestly, stupid and rich…

Alice muttered to herself, though in truth, she envied their ample chests while she remained as flat as a washboard.

Speaking of which, Alice’s chest hadn’t grown at all in the past year. It stayed as calm and flat as ever, which frustrated her. Maybe it was because she practiced chest-breaking boulders as a child? A perfectly good gift for a large chest, ruined by her master’s iron hammer.

Alice harbored resentment. To maintain her appearance, she shamelessly stuffed two large chest pads into her top, propping up her washboard.

It was a desperate measure. To prevent people from always calling her a washboard, creating a little illusion was understandable, wasn’t it?

Alice sipped her milk gloomily, a stark contrast to the excited women in front of her, remaining perfectly calm.

The other women were dressed elegantly, in long gowns or formal dresses, while Alice still wore her practical, easy-to-move-in outfit, with a thin sword hanging at her waist.

She was used to it. Having a weapon on hand allowed her to handle emergencies, so even if she came downstairs to relax, she kept her thin sword sheathed at her waist.

If any thug dared to harass her, she’d skewer their flower with her blade and leave them too scared to use the bathroom for half a year.

Though, in this all-female setting, it seemed unnecessary.

Martha, wearing high heels, stepped to the front of the stage to set the mood.

“Ladies, thank you for taking the time to grace us with your presence. Now, without further ado, please welcome our rising star!”

Martha yielded the small stage to Merlin and stepped back.

“Little Daisy oppa~”

“Daisy brother!”

“Aaaah! Oppa!!!”

The women below screamed wildly, as if possessed. Their husbands at home? Forgotten. Merlin oppa was all they needed.

Alice looked bewildered. What was wrong with these people? Why did they act like they were sick? Maybe they needed electroshock therapy…

“Hmph! What a bunch of vulgar, shameless hussies!”

A childish voice rang out beside Alice, brimming with indignation.

Alice turned her head in surprise. A little boy, just like her, had ordered a glass of milk. His face screamed “society-hating,” and who else could it be but little Henry?

“Little brother, that’s a bit… harsh, don’t you think?”

Alice knew she shouldn’t meddle, but hearing such foul words from a tiny child didn’t sit right with her.

“Not harsh at all! These women probably all have husbands at home, yet they still come to places like this. Absolutely shameless!” little Henry fumed, like a seasoned social critic.

Alice was left speechless, her mouth twitching awkwardly. If that was true… then it really was a bit much.

“My mother got involved in this kind of nonsense, and that’s why people talk about her behind her back. Disgusting!” little Henry said with the gravitas of an old man, though his tiny face did little to sell it.

Alice was slightly taken aback. Was this kid the innkeeper’s son? On closer inspection, he did look a bit like her.

“But you, big sister, are so pure and unpretentious. Unlike those vulgar hussies, you didn’t rush up there. You deserve praise…” little Henry nodded, giving her an approving look.

“Th-then… thank you for the praise…” Alice responded unnaturally, grumbling internally. Being praised by a bratty kid doesn’t make me happy at all!

Not that I didn’t want to go up there—it’s just that the crowd was too big, and they might knock my chest pads loose, exposing the truth that I’m a washboard!

But she could never say something so embarrassing out loud…
