title: Chapter 51 — Tip Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 51 — Tip Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 51

“Sigh, tonight this crowd’s wallets are going to be emptied again…” Little Henry sighed, picked up a cup full of milk, gulped it all down in one go, and put on a bit of a drunkard’s expression. “Haaah, I want to drink alcohol too. Why do I have to drink milk?”

“Little kids should drink milk…” Alice felt that, although Henry wasn’t very young, he certainly had a lot of worries.

“I’m not a little kid, I’m a… cough! A real man!” Henry said discontentedly. He recalled how Merlin had spanked him the last time he dressed in women’s clothes, and it was incredibly, damnably embarrassing. “Say, you’re an adult, right? Why are you drinking milk too? Haven’t weaned off milk at your age? What a truly adult thing to do…”

Alice gave an ugly laugh, a vein throbbed at her temple, and she thought, This brat has such a nasty mouth. I feel like beating up a kid. It’s not that I don’t want to drink; my tolerance for alcohol is terrible. A little bit and I’d start acting like a complete fool. I quit drinking to avoid losing face!

“Drinking milk… it makes you stronger.”

“Is that for real?” Henry scoffed, clearly not believing it. But his gaze drifted to the golden adventurer’s badge on Alice’s chest, and he instantly froze. “G-golden Adventurer! Big sister, you’re a Golden Adventurer!?”

“Indeed…” Alice replied calmly, thinking that adventurer badges were indeed useful everywhere.

“Amazing! Super amazing! Are you a high-tier powerhouse, big sister?” Henry saw the ornate, slender sword at Alice’s waist and assumed she must be a powerful swordsman.

“Correct.” Alice felt a touch of pride, as if she were accustomed to such surprised reactions.

“Awesome! Freaking awesome!” Henry’s eyes sparkled, as if he’d seen a savior. “Sister, please teach me sword techniques! I’m begging you!”

Alice’s expression froze. She thought awkwardly, Why do I keep running into kids like this? But sword techniques aren’t something you can just learn; there are many restrictions. Especially her own Ice Sword Art, which requires a proper lineage.

However, Alice was already used to it. She knew how to handle kids.

“It’s possible, but you’ll have to keep drinking milk. Only by becoming stronger can you learn.”

“I understand. No wonder you’re a high-tier powerhouse—your insight is so different from that fraud of a swordsman who just shows off with his blade!” Henry turned and started gulping down his milk again.

A fraud of a swordsman who shows off with his blade?

Who on earth was that?

Alice shook her head, not thinking much of it, and asked about something else.

“Say, your family’s little… little Chrysanthemum seems to be really popular?”

“Big sister, don’t even mention it. That guy is our family’s male gigolo—a total fraud, with not a single good trait. He just swindles women out of their money, spending all day among them. He sells a bottle of whiskey for fifty silver coins, but he charges five gold coins. He’s black-hearted through and through!” Henry shook his head, speaking very lowly of Merlin.

“I see…” Alice nodded, also feeling that kind of person wasn’t much good.

At that moment, dynamic music started playing. The lights dimmed, leaving only colorful, flashing lamps, creating a very sensual atmosphere.

Merlin’s face was heavily made up, so much so that he looked almost unrecognizable, neither human nor ghost, extremely flashy. This was the legendary “shamate aristocrat” makeup technique.

Because of the heavy makeup, Alice couldn’t recognize Merlin; he just looked a bit familiar.

Merlin swaggered to the front of the stage in a military uniform. His agile steps were, by estimation, thoroughly sleazy.

He took off his military coat, revealing black leather pants, a collar, and his bare abdominal muscles—completely looking like a Van♂ style.

Don’t be fooled by Merlin’s seemingly frail appearance; once he shed his coat, he had muscles—very well-proportioned, even showing off his flashy mermaid line.

Merlin threw his military hat and coat into the crowd of women, instantly causing a chorus of screams.

“Waaaaah! Chrysanthemum oppa!”

I don’t know how many people fainted on the spot from seeing Merlin’s half-naked body.

Alice calmly drank her milk, but the hand holding the cup was actually trembling. The scene before her was quite a冲击, feeling like something that didn’t belong to this era.

Merlin started hyping up the crowd, playing with various catchphrases, seemingly having no shame left at all.

“Let’s get high with me!”

“Ladies and gentlemen, old and young, men and women!”

“Raise your hands, let me see your hands, okay?”

“Dong ci da ci, dong ci da ci, AV8D, the friends up there, join me!”

“Wan, tu, si rui, fo, kang mang bei bi, lai ci gou!”

“Summer summer quietly passes, driving a tractor, running you over, running you over, not letting you catch your breath~?”

“Pfft!” Alice spat her milk all over the table, her face turning green then red. In an instant, she was completely overwhelmed by Merlin’s absurdity—

Good heavens!

What on earth is this nonsense?

Go back to your original world, okay?

Our world is too small, too pure…

It simply can’t contain your bone-deep妖孽 (demon/monster)!

∑(°口°?)??

Merlin and Alice’s daughter.

Not much to say about this character, avoiding spoilers. Just know it’s a family of three.

title: Chapter 52
content:
Chapter 52

Volume 2 · Chapter 52

The music was booming, and that shameless show-off Merlin was whipping the ignorant women of Shandong into a frenzy on stage.

Before long, the small tavern was drenched in a downpour of gold coins.

The women, as if possessed, screamed "Little Daisy Oppa" and threw their secret savings onto the stage.

Shimmering coins clattered down onto the stage—he must have made a fortune in just a short while.

Alice’s expression froze, her face turning ugly. The hand holding her wine glass trembled nonstop.

This was the first time she had ever seen something like this. Leather pants and a choker—what the hell was that?! Why did it give off such a shameful play vibe?

And the man on stage, this so-called "Little Daisy"... why was he so shameless? He had thrown away his dignity to an extraordinary degree.

"Ah~, even though this old man has the face of a woman, I have to admit his money-making skills are impressive." Little Henry looked up, his expression odd, and sighed. "Sigh, no one appreciates real tough guys anymore. Instead, pretty boys like him are running the show. Is this the corruption of human nature or the decline of morality?"

Alice stayed silent, lost in thought. She didn’t know why Little Henry could spout such world-weary words, but the more she thought about it, the more it made sense.

This was no longer the era of muscular tough guys. Many manly, macho men had gone off to make BL films, and somehow, those once-fearsome gentlemen had become synonymous with that. Meanwhile, pretty boys had become the mainstream, adored by women—it was all rather baffling.

Looking at Little Daisy, he seemed no different from an ordinary pretty boy...

Wait!

Pretty boy?

Freeloader!

Meow meow meow meow?!

Alice’s entire body jolted as if she had suddenly realized something. That "Little Daisy Oppa" on stage looked awfully familiar... could it be because...

She quickly pulled out the wanted poster from her pocket, and without a second thought, she crossed her eyes in the middle of the public space, carefully comparing "Little Daisy Oppa" with the Scottish freeloader pretty boy on the poster.

Upon closer inspection... they really did look alike!

Especially that cheap, shameless aura—it was identical.

"Pfft!" Little Henry spat out his milk, completely flustered. "W-Wait, big sister! What... what are you doing with your eyes crossed?! You’re ruining your beautiful lady vibe!"

Alice ignored Little Henry. Now that she had found the fugitive, business came first.

She swiftly stood up, but the crowd of women had surrounded the fugitive so tightly that she couldn’t move. It seemed she would have to use some intimidation.

Alice’s expression turned resolute. She drew her rapier, and an overwhelming high-tier pressure radiated from her, carrying waves of chilling energy.

Little Henry couldn’t help but shiver. It was so cold. So this was the power of a high-tier warrior? So cool!

Alice pointed her sword at Merlin on the stage and shouted—

"Scottish freeloader pretty boy! You owe so much money and still refuse to surrender!"

The women below, seeing someone draw a weapon, screamed and scattered like birds and beasts, afraid of getting caught in a tavern brawl.

"Who the hell is this? Trying to mess with my money-making? Looking for death!"

Merlin was instantly furious. He had spent a long time preparing for today, and now someone was here to cause trouble.

He fixed his gaze on the silver-haired girl in the distance, surrounded by a cold aura. *What the hell!* Another adventurer coming to demand repayment? The timing couldn’t be worse. Though... this guy looked a bit like that flat-chested Hero, except for the chest...

"Arrogant fool!"

Alice saw the fugitive’s defiant attitude and thought she would have to use force to teach him a lesson.

So Alice channeled her fighting spirit, leapt forward, and pinned Merlin down on the stage, straddling him with incredible speed.

Alice pressed the tip of her sword against Merlin’s neck, preventing him from moving, her expression deadly serious.

"Stay still! You’ve racked up a huge debt and have no intention of paying it back. You need to be locked up in prison. Come with me quietly, and I won’t have to get rough!"

And this was exactly why Merlin wanted to pay back the money.

Because every day, adventurers like Alice would come to harass him, disrupting his peaceful life.

Sometimes, Merlin didn’t even have time to go to the bathroom—he was too busy dealing with these little brats. It was infuriating.

As for why Merlin didn’t just kill all the intruders—

Please, killing people just to avoid paying debts? Was that something a proud demon lord like him would do?

Merlin couldn’t bring himself to do that. He still had his pride.

Alice glared fiercely, but the man beneath her remained completely calm. This surprised her. *Why isn’t he reacting at all? Is he really that contemptuous of me?*

Merlin didn’t resist at all. He let Alice press her sword against his neck because it posed no threat to him whatsoever.

Moreover, Merlin felt that the silver-haired girl in front of him really did resemble that flat-chested Hero—especially in the chest area. The difference was night and day.

Merlin frowned. To confirm her identity, he calmly reached out and groped Alice’s chest, poking it a couple of times—*boing, boing*—

*What the hell!*

This soft feeling... it’s padding!

So it was a fake chest after all!

That meant this person was definitely that idiot Alice, no doubt about it!

∑(っ°Д°;)っ

title: Chapter 53 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 53 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 53

Even at a time like this, Merlin could calmly grope someone’s chest—it was downright shocking.

The onlookers below were all petrified, the entire scene falling into dead silence. This was probably what the legendary "wife recognition" looked like.

Merlin stared at Alice’s face for a long time, unable to confirm her identity, yet somehow recognized her with a single grope.

Alice’s expression froze. This was the first time she’d ever been groped so brazenly, and to make matters worse, she’d been squeezed a couple of times out of nowhere.

Even if it was just soft padding, being touched was still unacceptable! What if she *did* have real breasts? Then she’d have been groped for real!

After three seconds of stunned silence, a surge of overwhelming humiliation welled up from the depths of her heart, and her icy face slowly flushed red.

“YAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!”

Alice let out a piercing shriek, startling Merlin beneath her. *Damn, is she really this innocent?* he thought. *It was just a grope…*

Tears welled in Alice’s eyes as she raised her rapier and wildly stabbed at Merlin’s head.

“You pervert! Die! Die! Die…”

The rapier clanged against the stage floor with metallic *dang dang dang* sounds.

“Wait! Calm down! That’s dangerous!”

A cold sweat dripped down Merlin’s forehead as he dodged the rapier thrusts left and right. One wrong move and his head would end up full of holes!

“Die, you bastard! I’ll chop your hands off! I don’t care about humanity!”

Alice’s rapier attacked furiously, likely because Merlin had groped her chest, and now she was so humiliated and furious that she had to reclaim her dignity no matter what.

Merlin shook his head, dodging as he felt a hint of helplessness. He suspected Alice had never really interacted with men before—her reaction was way over the top.

“Hey, hey, hey, Alice, stop for a second! It’s been a year, and your temper’s gotten even worse, huh? Old friends reuniting—shouldn’t we hug instead of you drawing your sword and stabbing at me like this?”

“Eh!?” Alice snapped back to her senses, her expression twisting in confusion as she stared at Merlin’s over-the-top noble makeup. She couldn’t recognize him. “Old friends? Who the hell are you?!”

Truthfully, Merlin’s feelings toward Alice were rather strange. He’d been traveling alone all this time, with no familiar faces around, and it left him with a faint sense of loneliness.

But seeing Alice today, even knowing she had once been part of the opposing Holy Church camp, he still felt a strange warmth.

When he thought about it, they didn’t really have any deep grudges—it was just a conflict of factions.

Moreover, when they had (been forced to) cooperate to cross the Orkney Strait, things had actually been quite harmonious. They’d spent three peaceful days and nights together.

Of course, the most important thing was that Merlin was no longer a Demon Lord. There was no need to fight Alice, the Hero. The hostility from a year ago didn’t have to carry over to today.

In an instant, the enemies of the past no longer had a reason to fight. Maybe they could just sit down, have a drink, and chat like normal people.

Little did he know, even if the old enmity between Demon Lord and Hero no longer existed, Alice still hated Merlin to the bone. He had turned her life into a complete mess—saddled with massive debts, forced to run around just to survive every day.

“Hahaha…” Merlin flicked his golden hair in what he thought was a dashing manner, blinking as he tried to convey his goodwill. “Beautiful Miss Alice, it’s me, Merlin! Don’t you remember us singing together as we crossed the Orkney Strait, spending three wonderful days and nights?”

*Wonderful my ass!*

I was nearly worked to death!

And forced to sing childish nursery rhymes!

Wait—*Merlin?* The Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace?!

No way! How is he here?! Is this for real?!

What are the odds?! This has to be some kind of trick!

Alice’s body tensed, her expression flickering between shock and doubt, her eyes still clinging to a sliver of hope that she was mistaken.

Merlin seemed to notice Alice’s confusion. He wiped the thick makeup from his face, revealing a clean, roguishly grinning visage.

“I remember after we landed, you couldn’t contain your feelings and went wild declaring your love for me. Thinking back, it feels like just yesterday~”

*Pffft!* Alice coughed up a mouthful of blood that shot three meters high. The veins on her forehead throbbed violently, and her face turned crimson in an instant, as if boiling water were steaming from her pores—

Shut up!

Shameless old scoundrel!!!

o(╬≧д≦)o

title: Chapter 54
content:
Chapter 54

Volume 2 · Chapter 54

The onlookers burst into teasing remarks—anyone could see that Merlin and Alice had an unusual relationship.

*Stripping to confess love? There must be some untold story here.*

Who the hell stripped naked to confess love to him?!

It was clearly him staring at me with those lecherous eyes!

A guy like him, who never acts serious, could make even picking his nose feel like sexual harassment!

Alice’s body trembled nonstop, not from the emotional reunion of "old friends," but from sheer, liver-quaking rage.

Normally, Alice knew the power gap between her and Merlin—she’d flee in terror, never daring to fight him.

But suddenly, a flood of memories flashed through her mind like a lantern show.

She recalled how Merlin had ruined her life, leaving her destitute, forcing her to live in exhausting hardship, constantly scrambling just to pay rent each month.

This nineteen-year-old girl felt a surge of grievance—she should’ve been living comfortably at her age, but because of Merlin, she was stuck in a miserable hand-to-mouth existence.

The weight finally crushed her. In front of her enemy, she unleashed over a year’s worth of pent-up resentment. Her grievance ignited into fury, burning away her fear of Merlin.

"Die, Lucifer the Third! Just die!"

With an angry snarl, Alice’s eyes burning red, she lunged with her rapier, striking down at Merlin below.

In the blink of an eye, Merlin’s eyes widened in shock. He swiftly jerked his head aside.

The icy, sharp rapier grazed past his ear and plunged into the wooden stage floor with a loud *thunk*.

"Hey, hey, hey, Miss Alice, calm down! We were partners who crossed the strait together back then—we got along fine! I just didn’t accept your… *naked* confession of love, right? That’s no reason to kill me…"

Merlin wore an extremely awkward expression, cold sweat sliding down his forehead. He could clearly sense that her last strike had been filled with genuine murderous intent.

What the hell was going on? He didn’t think he’d ever done anything terrible to Alice. Why did she hate him so much? Besides, he wasn’t even the Demon Lord anymore—did they really need to keep up this love-hate cycle?

"Shut up, you bastard! Who was ever your partner?! You *coerced* me on that beach!"

The crowd erupted in a chorus of *oohs* at her words. Coercion? That sounded like a rather blush-inducing story.

"Wait, wait, wait—this is getting more misunderstood by the second! Who coerced whom? Don’t slander me and ruin my reputation!" Merlin frowned. He’d only wanted the mithril armor—who could’ve guessed Alice would suddenly lose it and strip herself bare?

"Stop wasting words! Just die already!"

Alice yanked hard at the rapier embedded in the stage floor, but it was stuck. For a moment, she couldn’t pull it free, turning the serious confrontation into an awkward farce.

"Heh heh~" Merlin smirked, thinking this silly girl was really dumb.

Alice’s face flushed crimson. Humiliated and furious, she abandoned the rapier entirely. Instead, she grabbed the collar around Merlin’s neck and yanked him up, shaking him violently as she furiously accused him—

"And you still have the nerve to grin like an idiot?!"

"You absolute scoundrel, do you have *any* idea how much you’ve ruined me?!"

"What you did to me on that beach was unforgivable!"

"You took the most precious thing from me, then just *patted your ass* and walked away without a care!"

"Do you have *any* clue how much psychological damage you’ve caused me?!"

"I’m working this hard now because of *your* irresponsibility!"

"The pain you left me with back then is still seared into my memory—I can’t forget it!"

"If you’re still a man, then take responsibility like one!"

○○（＞＜）○○

title: Chapter 55 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 55 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 55

"You absolute scoundrel, you've ruined me! Give back what you took from me..."

Alice grabbed the collar around Merlin's neck, her eyes red with tears as waves of grievance overwhelmed her, reducing her to sobbing like a little girl.

The onlookers all shot Merlin disdainful glares, treating him like a deadbeat who had taken advantage of her and then abandoned her without responsibility.

You couldn't blame the crowd for jumping to conclusions. Without knowing the full story, Alice's words certainly sounded like that was the case.

Most of the people here were women, and they knew how deeply the first time could be etched in one's memory—and how painful it was. So when they saw a man who wouldn't take responsibility right from the start, they all felt intense sympathy for Alice.

"Ugh~ Merlin, you old pervert, what did you do to Big Sister? That's disgusting!" Little Henry frowned, his face full of disgust. "A useless guy like you, how did you even get Big Sister's favor? You took everything and now you don't want to take responsibility? I'm losing all respect for you! Tsk!"

Alice was so lost in her sorrow that she forgot to explain, making the situation even more awkward.

"No, it's not like that! Stop guessing, you're all misunderstanding..."

Merlin kept a straight face, but black lines formed on his forehead. *This terrible line makes it sound like Alice and I had an affair. What precious thing? I only took a mithril armor from her. Wait, is that thing really that valuable?*

"Give it back to me right now, or I swear I'll kill you."

Alice didn’t try to fight Merlin again. After calming down slightly, she realized she couldn’t win against him anyway. It was better to just demand the return of her mithril armor. That way, she wouldn’t have to worry about making a living anymore.

After all, she wasn’t a Hero anymore. There was no need to risk her life fighting the demon race.

"Uh..."

Merlin furrowed his brows, looking at the girl’s aggrieved expression. What had happened to her? And why did it seem related to him?

Well, they should talk first. It had been over a year since they last saw each other. Even if they had been enemies in the past, they could still catch up.

After all, without the conflict between the Demon Lord and the Hero, there wasn’t much deep-seated hatred between him and Alice—

"Alice, calm down."

"Let’s put aside our grudges."

"And set past conflicts aside."

"Then let’s just have a few drinks together, my treat."

☆～（ゝ。?）

◆

The night was deep and quiet.

All the patrons had left the tavern.

At the counter, Merlin and Alice sat at a comfortable distance from each other, drinking.

Merlin leisurely sipped his pale yellow champagne while Alice drank milk with ice cubes.

To make Merlin lose out, Alice drank as much as she could. After all, that bastard was paying.

She ended up downing over twenty glasses, feeling stuffed, and let out a loud burp.

"Buuurp!"

Alice’s face turned red as she covered her mouth, feeling a little embarrassed by her unladylike burp.

Merlin glanced at Alice, swirling his glass as he smirked, "No one’s competing with you, so why are you drinking so fast? You have no manners as a lady. At this rate, you’ll never find a boyfriend..."

Alice was instantly furious, feeling insulted. "Whether I can find a boyfriend or not is none of your business! Stop pointing fingers at me! And I *do* have a boyfriend—you just don’t know about him!"

"Hmph..."

Merlin chuckled to himself. *A boyfriend? Yeah, right. If she had a boyfriend, why would she need to stuff padding into her bra? She’s only doing that because she doesn’t have one and wants to boost her appeal.*

"By the way, you can’t even drink alcohol? You’re this old and still drinking milk?"

"Tch!" Alice clicked her tongue, her face still red. "Is there a problem with my personal preferences?!"

A cold sweat rolled down Merlin’s forehead as he calmly took a sip of his drink. *This girl is like a powder keg. What did I ever do to her? Did stealing her equipment and seeing her... really warrant her wanting to kill me? It’s like I murdered her father or something...*

Martha wiped down a glass, occasionally glancing at Alice and Merlin. There was something intriguing about their relationship.

On the surface, they seemed to be arguing, but there was an odd, almost sparkling chemistry between them.

Martha was surprised that Merlin had somehow managed to charm a Gold-rank adventurer. Sure, he usually carried a katana at his waist like a warrior, but he didn’t seem all that strong.

She never expected Merlin to have such appeal that even high-level powerhouses would flirt with him.

Then again, Martha thought about Merlin’s usual demeanor and understood. After all, he was always popular with the ladies.

"Merlin, I’m going upstairs to check on Henry. You two clean up when you’re done."

Martha felt that Merlin and Alice had a lot to catch up on after so long, so she deliberately gave them space.

"Oh, okay, Martha." Merlin nodded with a smile.

The dim, flickering oil lamp on the counter cast a warm glow over the neatly arranged amber bottles of liquor. Outside, the wind howled, whooshing past.

After Martha left, Alice could no longer sit still. She finally spoke up, "Give me back my things. Let’s settle our debts once and for all."

"What things?" Merlin raised an eyebrow, thinking that the armor was just an external possession—surely she wouldn’t still be chasing after it now.

"The mithril armor!" Alice gritted her teeth.

"Pfft!" Merlin sprayed out his champagne, his heart skipping a beat. "Sorry, I can’t return it. I already sold it... for tens of millions of gold coins."

"Ah?!" Alice’s expression turned to shock. She slammed her hand on the table. "Get it back! Return the money! If you’re short, I’ll cover the difference. But that mithril armor *has* to be returned to me—it’s very important!"

"Well... that might not be possible..." Merlin wiped his sweat, thinking, *It’s not just about the money—it’s about a LOT of money!*

"What do you mean? Spit it out, stop beating around the bush!" Alice huffed, her brows knitted tightly together.

"The money I got from selling the mithril armor..." Merlin hesitated, black lines forming on his forehead as he awkwardly continued, "I took it all to the royal racetrack... and lost every last coin."

"So, in other words, to redeem that mithril armor, you’d need tens of millions of gold coins."

"If you can afford it, go ahead. But I sure don’t have that kind of money..."

title: Chapter 56
content:
Chapter 56

Volume 2 · Chapter 56

Alice's eyes widened, her expression turning incredulous as she froze for a full three seconds.

She had still harbored some hope—if she could just get her mithril armor back, her life would be so much easier.

But who could have imagined Merlin would take things this far? Not only had he bought her mithril armor, he had taken the money and gambled it all away!

All of it lost at the royal racetrack—how was she supposed to get that back?

It was impossible! That mithril armor was as good as gone.

Tens of millions of gold coins—she would never earn that much in her entire life. Was she supposed to sell her soul to pay it back?

This was it. This was the end. Merlin, that bastard, had ruined her life. From now on, she’d be drowning in debt, slaving away just to scrape by.

Alice’s face turned deathly pale. She had begun to question the very meaning of her existence...

Merlin took a calm sip of champagne, finding Alice’s reaction utterly ridiculous.

"It’s just a suit of armor. No need to be so stingy~"

Merlin waved his hand dismissively, though in truth, that armor *had* been extremely valuable. If his luck hadn’t been so abysmal, tens of millions of gold coins would have lasted him decades of extravagance.

"Easy for *you* to say!" Alice was so furious her vision blurred. She grabbed his collar and shook him violently, the first time in her life she had ever encountered someone so infuriating. "I don’t care! Give me back my mithril armor! Or I’m not letting this go! Do you hear me?! Give. It. Back!"

Merlin swayed like a reed in the wind as Alice shook him, listening to her voice crack with emotion. He couldn’t help but sigh internally—

Women really were such troublesome creatures. Why wouldn’t she just let this go?

Ah, it must be because of my noble aura and handsome face.

Sigh. I’ve always carried a burden—being this good-looking at such a young age.

Merlin completely misread Alice’s intentions. She had only come to reclaim what was hers.

Deep down, he knew the truth. He just didn’t want to admit it—because he couldn’t pay her back. Better to play dumb and ignore it.

"Sorry, Miss Alice, but I can’t pay you back. So my stance is this: no money, no life—take it if you can."

Merlin’s words were shameless, though a flicker of guilt lingered in his chest. After all, as the Proud King, stealing a young girl’s money was… embarrassing.

But that astronomical sum was impossible for anyone to repay. Might as well act like a scoundrel.

"You bastard! Give me back my armor right now! Stop playing dumb! I don’t care what you have to do—you *will* return it to me!" Alice’s nose was nearly crooked with rage, tears glinting in the corners of her eyes. With a sudden movement, she stood up, drew her rapier, and pressed it against Merlin’s throat. "That armor you stole has already ruined my life. If you don’t give it back, I’ll grant your wish right now—*I’ll take your life.*"

The oil lamp’s flame flickered, casting a dim, hazy glow.

Alice’s face was twisted in fury, her eyes burning with rage. She held the rapier to Merlin’s throat, her anger overcoming her fear. Their shadows intertwined in the wavering light.

Merlin’s expression remained composed, not the slightest hint of fear in his eyes—but his mood had soured.

He hated having a blade pressed to his throat. It always dragged him back to his childhood, when he and his sister had been threatened by demon nobles, forced to live in constant fear, tails tucked between their legs.

Merlin lifted his eyelids slightly, shooting Alice a glance so cold it was devoid of any humanity—the kind of look one reserved for an enemy.

"You want my life?"

"Fine. But only if you have the strength to take it."

"I crushed you before, and I can do it again now."

"Let me make one thing clear—if you dare attack me, we’re enemies from that moment on..."

title: Chapter 57 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 57 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 57

Merlin was serious. There wasn’t the slightest hint of jest in his words.

Now that he was no longer a Demon Lord, there was no reason for him to fight Alice, so they couldn’t exactly be called enemies. Though they had some past grievances, it wasn’t a big deal.

But if Alice dared to attack him now, without any reason to fight, then he would consider her an enemy.

Merlin’s attitude toward enemies had always been simple and brutal: kill.

It didn’t matter who they were—noble or common, old or young, man or woman, or even a beauty who could topple nations. If someone attacked him with murderous intent, they would be marked as an enemy, and the moment they met, he would cut them down without hesitation.

Since coming to this other world, Merlin had been raised by the demon race. Their principles of fairness—an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth—had long since seeped into his bones and become part of his very being.

If someone wanted to kill him, was he supposed to preach at them like a saintly mother and try to reform them with words?

Not a chance. If a single sword could settle an enemy, he wouldn’t waste breath on a single extra word.

Perhaps Merlin couldn’t be called purely just, but neither could he be called purely evil. All he did was act according to his own principles, doing what he believed was right.

Alice was shaken by Merlin’s icy gaze. A chill ran through her entire body, and those ruby-like eyes were like a basin of cold water poured over her head, instantly extinguishing her anger.

She recalled Merlin’s strength—it was far beyond her level. Her aggressive momentum crumbled, replaced by a creeping fear.

Merlin smiled, easing the tension. It was rare to meet an acquaintance; starting a brawl would be unsightly.

“So just calm down. We’re here drinking. Don’t ruin the mood with that sharp sword of yours. Settling things through negotiation is far smarter than resorting to violence...”

Merlin slowly moved the slender blade away from his neck with his fingers, defusing the tense situation.

Alice sat in her chair, her soul seemingly torn from her body. She felt as though her life was doomed, crushed under the weight of an enormous debt that left her gasping for breath.

She had thought that meeting Merlin might solve her troubles, but in the end, she had gained nothing.

There was nothing she could do about Merlin. She couldn’t get her money back, and she couldn’t beat him in a fight. What was she supposed to do? She was desperate too...

Right now, Alice felt an awful, humiliating sensation—as if she had been taken advantage of, and Merlin hadn’t even paid her. It was unbearably awkward.

“Aren’t you supposed to be really powerful? Why don’t you just go steal the mithril armor back?”

Alice wasn’t ready to give up. Though she didn’t like doing bad things, Merlin was already a villain, so it didn’t matter.

“Miss, we demons are a race that values fairness and truth, unlike you humans who revere hypocrisy. To us, a transaction is a sacred matter. If both parties agree, then the deal is done.” Merlin took a sip of his drink and said leisurely.

“Didn’t you say you’re not a Demon Lord anymore? Why are you still so particular about these things?” Alice knitted her delicate brows, finding it strange.

“Even if I’m no longer a Demon Lord, I was once the former Prideful Monarch. If I were to take back something I sold, I’d lose all face.” Merlin showed a hint of displeasure, feeling as though Alice was looking down on him. “By the way, aren’t you the Hero? Is it really okay for you to be encouraging me to steal?”

“It’s you who would be doing the stealing, not me. A villain like you should be doing more villainous things—it’s only natural!” Alice gritted her teeth, then her expression turned gloomy again. “Besides... I’m not the Hero anymore...”

“Huh?! You’re not?”

Merlin was surprised. He had assumed Alice was still the Holy Church’s Hero, but apparently, she had quit.

Now that he thought about it, since he wasn’t a Demon Lord anymore and Alice wasn’t a Hero, fighting each other would be utterly pointless.

There were still some lingering historical issues, but they weren’t that serious.

Merlin grinned and extended his hand, offering a gesture of goodwill.

“Since I’m not a Demon Lord and you’re not a Hero anymore, there’s no need for us to be cold to each other, right? If we set aside our past factional hostility, aren’t we just ordinary people now? So let’s shake on it—we’re not enemies.”

“Don’t touch me!”

Alice angrily swatted Merlin’s hand away and collapsed onto the table, sobbing.

She felt deeply wronged. She was terrified of her future, afraid of becoming a slave to debt, yet there was nothing she could do. Why did she have to run into Merlin, the greatest jinx in her life?

“You bastard... One day, I’ll kill you and claim the bounty from the Holy Church... *sniff*...”

Merlin chuckled, watching Alice cry into the table. It was the first time someone had declared in front of him that they would kill him. She was foolish to an impressive degree.

“If you can kill me, go ahead. But I’m not a Demon Lord anymore—I’m just an ordinary demon. A head like mine is only worth five gold coins. Not much, really.”

title: Chapter 58 — Reward Chapter
content:
Chapter 58 — Reward Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 58

Merlin was still somewhat familiar with the Holy Church’s bounties. Each of the seven Demon Lords was worth tens of millions of gold coins, while ordinary demons were only worth five.

When he first learned about the bounties, Merlin had bitterly regretted not selling himself to the Holy Church before the Council had fired him. If he had, he could’ve walked away with tens of millions—just thinking about it made his guts twist with regret.

So *this* was how much a Demon Lord was worth?!

“Waaaaah—”

Alice’s sorrow overflowed like a river, and Merlin’s words had stabbed her straight through the heart. She actually burst into tears.

Right now, she felt Merlin was like a cockroach—impossible to drive away or kill, always popping up in the most infuriating places to disgust people. She was so furious she could barely breathe.

“It’s just a mithril armor set… it’s not that serious…” Merlin calmly took a sip of wine.

“Easy for *you* to say!” Alice slammed her face onto the table, seething. “That mithril armor wasn’t *mine*—I *borrowed* it! If I can’t pay it back, I’ll owe the Holy Church *tens of millions* of gold coins! QAQ”

*Pfft!*

Merlin had just taken a sip of wine and nearly choked. His hand trembled—*how much?!*
Tens of millions?! He’d only ever dined and dashed for a few thousand at most. This girl was *loaded* with debt! She’d have to haul bricks for a lifetime and still not pay it off!

After steadying himself, a sudden sense of superiority washed over him. Turns out someone was even more useless than he was. *Oh ho ho!*

“Don’t worry about it. You’re young—pressure is good! No pressure, no motivation. Work hard, and one day you’ll pay it all back…”

*Bullshit!*

You naive girl, rest assured—you’ll *never* pay it back!

If *you* can clear tens of millions, I’ll livestream myself eating shit! *Hahahaha…*

“Shut up! You shameless old swindler!” Alice felt deeply insulted. She knew she couldn’t beat him in a fight, but she’d *never* lose a verbal battle. “I don’t want to hear some tavern gigolo lecturing me!”

“Gigolo… what’s wrong with being a gigolo? Did a gigolo kill your family? Don’t look down on people like that.” Merlin’s face flushed red. His pride stung.

For no clear reason, the two of them devolved into a verbal brawl, each hurling insults at the other. It seemed they were determined to tear each other apart with words.

“Hmph~” Alice lifted her head, her eyes still red from crying, and sneered. “You used to be a haughty ruler, basking in glory at the Demon Lord Palace. Now you’re just a gigolo in some backwater tavern, surviving by pleasing others. How *pathetic*. Disgusting!”

Merlin felt like Alice had just driven a knife straight through his heart. *It hurt.*

“I earn my money with my own two hands! What’s pathetic about that?!”

“Oh please! Dressed like a country bumpkin, carrying a hoe to the fields—you’d fit right in! That shaggy donkey outside yours? Too poor to buy a horse, huh? Tsk tsk tsk! You used to be the *Hero*, draped in gold and silver. Look at you now—*embarrassing*~”

Alice’s face twisted in pain. Her heart felt like it was bleeding. A girl being insulted like this by Merlin was *unbearable.*

“You shut up! Adventurers earn *way* more than gigolos like you! Who else am I supposed to blame for being broke?! It’s *all your fault*! I have to pay the Holy Church a fortune every month!”

“Hah, what a joke. Adventurers? What a trash profession. How *dare* they compare to the noble gigolo?” Merlin scoffed, though deep down he was *terrified*—he knew “gigolo” wasn’t exactly a proud title. But in his eyes, adventurers were all penniless too. Every adventurer who came to hassle him had pockets cleaner than their faces. So really, they were all the same—no one had room to talk.

“Our commissions pay *tens of thousands* per job! Can your gigolo work compare?!” Alice’s face burned with rage. She *refused* to admit she was worse off than Merlin.

The two were so absorbed in their argument that neither noticed how much it resembled a bitter breakup—two ex-lovers running into each other on the street, each tearing the other down just to feel superior.

“How much?” Merlin furrowed his brows, unable to believe his ears. “Tens of thousands? You’re joking.”

“Hmph! You country bumpkin! S-rank and above commissions start at *ten thousand gold coins* each!” Alice puffed up, determined to crush Merlin’s spirit.

*What the—?*
Ten thousand was *a lot*!
Were adventurers *that* profitable?
He’d had *no idea*…

Merlin’s expression wavered, his interest piqued. If Alice could do it, so could he.

“But S-rank and above commissions are *extremely* dangerous. You often run into powerful enemies—Saint-tier opponents aren’t uncommon.” Alice sighed, then sneered at Merlin. “But if you complete just *one*, you’ll earn more than a *hundred years* of gigolo work! So keep running your mouth, you *worthless* piece of trash!”

Merlin stayed silent, mentally evaluating the adventurer profession. Was it right for him?

*High chance of encountering Saint-tier enemies* = *free life extension.*
*Massive earnings* = *the dream of living in luxury without working.*

Final assessment: *This job was *perfect* for him!*

“Ahem!” Merlin cleared his throat, masking his embarrassment. He was done arguing with Alice. “Miss Alice, how *does* one become an adventurer?”

“Anyone with mana or fighting spirit can, I guess.” Alice answered offhandedly.

Merlin’s expression twisted. *That’s it?* Such a *lame* requirement? He was a freak—he had *neither* magic *nor* fighting spirit…

“What if someone has *neither* magic nor fighting spirit? Any other way?”

“Seems like you’d need another adventurer to vouch for you, to prove you’re capable.” Alice explained casually, then snapped, “Why are you asking so many questions?”

*Holy shit!*
There was *hope*!
And Alice *was* an adventurer, wasn’t she?

“Dear Miss Alice, my *old friend*, since we go *way* back…” Merlin rubbed his hands together, wearing his most obsequious grin. “How about you put in a good word for me? I’d *love* to become an adventurer.”

“Tsk. Read my lips…” Alice clicked her tongue, her face darkening with utter disgust, hatred, and disdain—inflicting *megatons* of psychological damage with a single look.

“G… U… N…!”

title: Chapter 59
content:
Chapter 59

Volume 2 · Chapter 59

Alice and Merlin parted on bad terms.

Alice already couldn’t stand the sight of Merlin, and now she was supposed to help introduce him to the Adventurers Guild? What a joke. As if she’d ever do that in a million years!

Alice returned to her room alone and flopped onto the bed, sulking.

Her mind was filled with Merlin’s infuriating, smug grin, her teeth clenched in frustration.

This time, she’d really lost big. Not only had she failed to resolve her own debts, but the bounty to capture that Scottish freeloading pretty boy had also gone up in smoke. Did she want to drag Merlin back?

Alice knew she didn’t have the strength. She couldn’t just grab him, and if she tried, she’d probably end up the one getting strung up and beaten.

All her hard work over the past half-month had been for nothing. No income, not a single coin, and to top it all off, she’d run into Merlin, that jinx of all jinxes.

A look of utter despair crossed her face. She ached for her mithril armor, but there was nothing she could do about that bastard Merlin. She couldn’t beat him in a fight, and the chance of talking him into paying her back was zero.

And Merlin’s attitude made it clear: *I don’t give a damn. Try and make me pay. Come at me if you’ve got the guts. Nobody can touch me anyway.*

Alice was at her wit’s end. Since she couldn’t solve her debt problem, the only thing left was to get as far away from Merlin as possible. She decided to leave tomorrow.

A woman’s intuition told her that nothing good ever came from being around Merlin—

“God, why haven’t you answered any of my prayers?”

“Why did you let me run into that bastard Merlin?”

“That narcissistic freak…”

“Just choke on shit and die, will you?!”

◆

The next day.

The sky was overcast, thick black clouds twisting together. It wouldn’t be long before the rain started. The air was heavy and oppressive.

Martha was preparing lunch.

Little Henry sat nearby, tapping his bowl with a spoon, looking bored.

He planned to sneak out and play as soon as he finished eating.

Merlin had been eating with them, mother and son, but right now he was in a private room, sweet-talking female customers into spending more.

Alice came downstairs first. She intended to buy some supplies for her journey, then leave the village that very night in her donkey cart, far away from Merlin.

When Little Henry saw Alice, his eyes lit up, filled with admiration.

“Big sister!”

Alice snapped out of her gloomy thoughts at the sound of Little Henry’s voice and waved with a smile.

“Big sister, where are you going?” Little Henry hurried over to her side and asked.

“I’m going to buy some things.” Alice replied in a gentle tone.

“When will you have time to teach me sword techniques?” Little Henry was full of anticipation. He thought Alice’s swordplay from yesterday, intertwined with wind and snow, was incredibly cool.

“I’ve told you, you need to drink more milk and grow taller first.” Alice ruffled Little Henry’s hair.

“I see~” Little Henry looked deeply frustrated, determined to force down a ton of milk that night. “As expected of a high-ranking warrior, your thinking is on another level. Unlike Uncle Merlin, who only knows how to use *Iaigiri*—what a trash sword technique. Even if he offered to teach me, I wouldn’t want to learn it!”

Alice’s expression turned odd. She recalled the earth-shattering *Iaigiri* and looked down at Little Henry, wondering what this foolish child had missed out on.

“I won’t bother you anymore, big sister. I’m going to eat.” Little Henry trotted back to his chair.

Alice glanced at the soup on the table, an idea forming in her mind.

“Does Merlin eat with you?”

“Yeah.” Little Henry nodded childishly.

“Which bowl is his?” Alice pressed.

“This one…” Little Henry tapped the bowl across from him with his spoon.

“I see…” A wicked smile spread across Alice’s face as she secretly pulled out a small black pouch from behind her back.

Inside were yellow croton seeds—her emergency supply.

“Sister, what are you doing?” Little Henry asked curiously, sensing this wasn’t going to be good.

“Shhh…” Alice pressed a finger to her lips, her expression dark as she threatened, “Little brother, what I’m about to do—don’t tell a soul. Not even Merlin. It’s just a little prank.”

“O-okay…” Little Henry nodded rapidly, trembling. Suddenly, this big sister seemed terrifying.

Alice untied the black pouch and poured all the mustard-yellow croton seeds into Merlin’s soup.

Little Henry recognized what they were—he’d used croton seeds for pranks before—but he didn’t dare say a word. Sweating nervously, he thought, *A prank doesn’t need this many seeds! Big sister’s trying to kill someone!*

Alice’s expression turned sinister, her smile more demonic than any actual demon. Here she was, a Hero, yet she wore a grin more evil than the Devil himself—

Damn you, Merlin!

Let’s see you squirm to death from the runs!

Ohohohohohoho…

(￣y▽￣)~*

title: Chapter 60 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 60 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 60

Alice felt refreshed after poisoning someone.

She turned to leave, intending to attend to her real business.

But as she passed a private room, she heard a voice that made her skin crawl.

"Yo! Miss Alice, you sure slept in late today!"

Alice glanced over and saw Merlin inside the room, flanked by four women, making them blush and giggle.

He looked like some foppish landowner’s son, dripping with gaudy charm.

"Hmph!"

Alice let out a cold snort, turned away without a word, and left. Deep down, she despised Merlin, this gigolo. She found him utterly vulgar.

Her delicate brows knit together, a thin layer of anger on her face. She thought—

How could anyone like a pathetic leech who survives off women’s perfume money?

What a bunch of decadent women, throwing their money away just to be deceived by this demon.

So, fanatical women really are brainless!

What do they get out of wasting so much money? It’s not like they can even sleep with him.

Sigh… what a waste of youth…

◆

After finishing work, Merlin prepared to eat.

Martha was still busy in the kitchen. Across from him, Henry’s expression was off, as if something was weighing on his mind.

Merlin sat down and looked at Henry. "Henry, why are you staring at me? Do I have lipstick on my face again?"

Henry just shook his head repeatedly, staying silent. He kept his head down and ate furiously. As for Alice slipping croton seeds into the food, he decided not to get involved. He’d just pretend he didn’t see it.

Merlin picked up his spoon, lost in thought about the Adventurers Guild as he began to eat.

But just as the soup reached his lips, he froze, his eyes locked onto the yellowish beans floating on top.

Martha added beans today?

Oh, shit! I hate beans the most…

Merlin put the spoon down, considering pouring it out, but felt it would be a waste.

Little Henry kept sneaking glances at Merlin’s reaction, as if waiting for a show.

"Henry, where’s the donkey from that silver-haired guest yesterday?"

"In… in the stable behind the house."

Merlin picked up his bowl and stood, heading toward the back of the house.

Little Henry wore a strange expression, thinking—

Are Big Brother Merlin and Big Sister in some kind of mutual scheming against each other…

◆

Evening.

The oppressive weather made it hard to breathe.

The clouds in the sky grew thicker and darker.

Normally, the sunset’s afterglow would still be visible at this hour.

But today, it was already as dark as midnight—so dark you couldn’t see your hand in front of your face.

Tonight, there were no stars. They were all hidden behind the clouds.

It seemed the long-brewing rain was finally about to arrive.

Merlin changed into a stylish outfit, preparing for the night shift.

He stood behind the counter, polishing a glass, his face completely expressionless.

Merlin was lost in thought about the Adventurers Guild, so he seemed a little distracted.

The more he thought about it, the more he realized he was actually well-suited for adventuring. Powerful enemies would help alleviate his curse, and he could earn generous rewards.

It was almost like his time in the Demon Lord Palace—except that adventurers actively ran dungeons, while as a Demon Lord, he’d been playing tower defense.

Though Merlin leaned toward the idea, the problem was that someone without magic or qi like him needed a referral to become an adventurer. And Alice, that stubborn woman, refused to help him.

It seemed that even without the conflict between the Demon Lord and Hero factions, the grudge between them was still deep. The hostility remained.

"Sigh… is there any other way?"

Merlin sighed, his face filled with worry.

"Merlin, what’s wrong?"

Martha walked over. She had been watching him sigh in the shadows for a while.

"Nothing…" Merlin set down the glass and picked up another to polish.

"You’ve been so gloomy today, not even focused on work." Martha smiled and asked curiously, "If something’s bothering you, you can talk to me. After all, I’m older than you."

Sister Martha, don’t joke.

I’m already two hundred years old.

By human standards, I’m practically an old man…

title: Chapter 61 — Reward Chapter
content:
Chapter 61 — Reward Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 61

Merlin gave a strange little smile and didn’t refuse Martha’s kindness, so he poured out his troubles.

“So that’s how it is. You want to be an adventurer, huh? Looks like you’ve already found your next goal.” Martha said with a smile.

“Yeah, it’s just a shame I don’t have magic or qi. That damn Alice won’t even introduce me.” Merlin wore a worried look.

“You probably didn’t beg hard enough. Lady Alice seems like a good person—if you just talk to her properly, she’ll agree.” Martha encouraged him.

Merlin gave a bitter laugh. If only Martha knew the history between him and Alice. It wouldn’t be that easy to convince her to help. Alice still carried a lot of prejudice against him; their old adversarial mindset was probably still there.

“Speaking of which, Martha, you’re so well-traveled. What’s the adventurer life really like?”

Merlin didn’t know much about the profession, so he asked Martha for details.

“Adventuring is a profession with a gambling element to it.” Martha replied flatly.

“Gambling?” Merlin frowned.

“Mm. Hope and death go hand in hand. High-rank commissions do pay a fortune, so for a lot of people with nowhere else to turn, it’s a profession of hope—you can make a fortune in a short time. But it’s also riddled with danger. You never know when you’ll face the unknown. Countless adventurers have died on the job, many without even leaving a name behind.”

“Is that so…” Merlin felt a pang of melancholy in Martha’s words, but high risk for high reward was only natural.

Martha’s words didn’t scare him off—in fact, they made him even more eager. If there really were people out there who could kill him, that was perfect. If they were strong enough, maybe his curse could finally be lifted.

“Though calling it ‘hope and death’ isn’t quite accurate…” Martha paused, then said seriously, “Adventurers are betting their futures. Money isn’t the main reward—what you really gain is freedom. An unshackled life. That’s why even people who aren’t short on cash become adventurers.”

“I see… haha…” Merlin gave a dry chuckle. Did his own desire to freeload and coast through life count as a love of freedom?

“If you’re set on becoming an adventurer, Merlin, don’t take dangerous commissions. Without magic or qi, you’re still too weak. Stick to the easy ones—you can still make a living. Just don’t put yourself in danger.” Martha spoke in a big-sister tone, full of concern.

*I’m so weak that even without magic or qi, I’m still strong enough to make people’s hair stand on end!*

Merlin felt a vein throb on his forehead. Did he really look that pathetic?

“I never thought you’d leave. I was hoping we could spend more time together.” Martha looked a little sad. It was rare to meet someone as decent as Merlin.

“Martha, thank you for taking care of me all this time.” Merlin had already made up his mind to go.

“That’s my line. You’ve helped me out a lot, and you’re practically a money tree. At first, I was worried you were some kind of playboy, but turns out you’re just all looks.” Martha beamed.

Merlin just smiled faintly. He was used to being misunderstood. Back in Scotland, people had accused him of all sorts of things, but some things just couldn’t be explained.

“Henry’s off playing somewhere again. I’m going to look for him. Can you keep an eye on the shop?” Martha took an umbrella with her, just in case it rained.

“Mm, I will.” Merlin nodded. That little brat Henry really didn’t give his mother a moment’s peace.

Martha turned to leave, but something else was on her mind. She turned back and asked, “Merlin, have you seen those three Silver-rank adventurers who were drinking here a few days ago?”

Merlin thought for a moment, then shook his head.

“No…”

◆

Outside the village walls.

The sky was a thick blanket of dark clouds, the night silent and pitch-black.

The heavy darkness seemed to teem with hidden monsters.

A handsome swordsman—one of the three adventurers who had been drinking in the tavern days before—staggered forward, limping and alone.

He appeared to be the only one left, his entire body covered in wounds. He looked utterly battered. Though crudely bandaged, the bright red of his injuries was still shocking to see.

The swordsman reached the base of the wall and looked around. Above, a few campfires burned, indicating that guards were still on duty.

“Hello… is anyone there?!”

After a while, on top of the wall, a drunk guard stood up, swaying with a bottle in hand. His nose was red, and he might have even been hiccuping.

“Damn… who the hell is it?! Don’t you know the gate’s closed?! *Hic*”

“I’m one of the adventurers who left the village a few days ago! I’ve finished my commission and come back! Please open the gate!”

The swordsman’s face twisted in pain. To make himself heard, he shouted at the top of his lungs.

“It’s not time to open the gate! Can’t do it! Get lost!”

The guard took another swig, seemingly unbothered.

“I’m begging you, my companions are all dead. I’m covered in wounds—please, save me!”

The swordsman’s voice was desperate, his tone heart-wrenching.

“Ugh, so annoying…” The guard was getting fed up. He shouted back, “Bring the torch closer! I need to check your face!”

The swordsman obeyed, holding the torch up to his face. The once-handsome features were now marred by blood, bruises, and various cuts.

“You really are hurt?” The guard jumped, half-sober now. He vaguely remembered the three Silver-rank adventurers who had left a few days ago.

“In the name of the Goddess Maria, please save me!” the swordsman pleaded.

“This is such a hassle… fine, I’ll make an exception!”

The guard grumbled as he opened the gate, looking thoroughly displeased.

“Damn my luck… had to run into this crap. Ruined my good dream…”

The gears of the gate groaned, chains clanked, and the heavy gate slowly lowered until it was wide open.

“Come in! What are you waiting for?” The guard was confused when the swordsman didn’t move.

The swordsman stood alone in the night, torch in hand, looking small and isolated. Then, with a thud, he dropped to his knees and began to sob, apologizing.

“I’m sorry… I’m so sorry… I… I just wanted to save my fiancée! I’m sorry…”

His voice echoed out. In the pitch-black wilderness, a sea of desperate flames suddenly flared to life.

Countless torches were lit all at once, illuminating the area beneath the gate as bright as day. They stretched nearly a kilometer, an endless sea of fire that looked like a dragon of flame in the night.

A rumbling sound surged forward, accompanied by the constant scrape of armor.

Goblins’ long tongues flicked out, their crimson eyes glinting with eerie light as they chittered like a swarm of locusts.

In the distance, lantern-like red eyes loomed, and giant shadows took heavy steps forward—massive goblins were approaching.

The goblins, well-equipped and lying in wait in the darkness, had been waiting for the gate to open before launching their attack.

The guard on the wall was stunned, his legs going weak. The alcohol had completely worn off.

As he watched the countless torch-bearing goblins surging toward them, it was already too late to raise the gate—

“G… goblins…”

“GOBLIN ATTACK!!!”

title: Chapter 62
content:
Chapter 62

Volume 2 · Chapter 62

Countless green goblins howled and roared, their short swords already ravenous for blood.

Flickering flames clustered together, forming a long dragon that surged forward.

A lone swordsman knelt on the ground, allowing the fully armed goblin warriors to trample over him.

Tears streamed down his face as he bitterly regretted his own helplessness, forced to make a compromising choice that left the village’s inhabitants in mortal peril.

"This... this is bad..."

The guard, terrified, collapsed to the ground. His horrified expression was ghastly, his pale face blending with the cold sweat.

Since it was too late to close the city gates, the best he could do was sound the alarm for the villagers—so they could flee for their lives!

Summoning his courage, the guard stood up and reached for the alarm bell.

"Goblin army is here! Everyone, run—gah!"

The heavy bell had only been struck once when a piercing sound cut through the thick, dark clouds.

A single feathered arrow *whooshed* through the air, piercing the guard’s throat and silencing the warning bell. He crumpled to the ground, powerless, blood gushing onto the earth.

"Goblin warriors!"

"Carry the glory of our king, and turn all in your path to dust with your blades!"

The purple-skinned goblin shaman, Gega Wu, stood on a chariot, waving his arms to stir the goblins’ emotions.

"The village ahead is our prey! Kill all the men! Take all the women!"

"Offer up every precious treasure to our emperor!"

"The moment to prove your loyalty to the king—has arrived!!!"

The goblins roared with excitement, raising their long swords high, screeching madly like a swarm of locusts shaking their wings.

Gega Wu was satisfied. This time, he planned to plunder every last bit of the village’s wealth and take all the beautiful women, presenting them as tribute to the Goblin Emperor.

The army advanced steadily. Gega Wu approached the wretched, suffering swordsman, his mouth stretching to his pointed ears as he sneered, "Well done. Thank you for opening the gates for us. Without a siege, we’ve saved ourselves a great deal of trouble."

"Then..." the swordsman lifted his head, tears welling in his eyes, "then, as we agreed, please... return my fiancée to me!"

"Hmm..." Gega Wu stroked his chin, mocking, "Are you an idiot? How could we ever agree to that? *Hahahaha!*"

"Ah..." The swordsman’s eyes widened in disbelief.

"Your fiancée will soon be His Majesty’s slave, trained night after night. She’ll forget all about you, hehehe~" Gega Wu grinned lewdly.

"We... we had a deal! I opened the gates for you, and you were supposed to let her go! How can you have no honor?!" The swordsman’s eyes turned red with rage, his heart filling with hatred.

"Pah, honor doesn’t fill a belly." Gega Wu scoffed, sneering at the swordsman. "At first, you were useful—you could open the gates, so you had value, and we could negotiate. But now that the gates are open, you’re nothing but a dog..."

"You bastard!!!"

Unable to contain his fury, the swordsman’s eyes burned crimson. He never imagined that after all his efforts, it would still be for nothing—his fiancée still not freed.

The overwhelming humiliation drove him to madness. Gathering the last of his fighting spirit, he lunged at Gega Wu in a final, desperate strike.

"Tsk, a brainless mad dog..." Gega Wu flicked his hand, casting a Fireball. Though it was a basic spell, empowered by high-tier magic, its temperature was scorching.

The small fireball struck the swordsman, and flames instantly engulfed his entire body, crackling fiercely.

"AAAAAAAAAAAAH!"

"You filthy bastards! I’ll—"

The swordsman collapsed weakly to the ground, black smoke and the stench of burning flesh rising from his body, his arms twitching feebly.

The flames of despair blazed across the wilderness, surging toward the village.

◆

Inside the village.

Many residents had heard the single toll of the alarm bell.

They had also seen the city gates open, and countless fires surging toward them in the darkness.

Many opened their windows, poking their heads out to see what was happening.

"What’s going on?"

"Is someone coming?"

"Is it the stationed battalion?"

The villagers chattered, completely unaware of the approaching danger.

The clatter of armor echoed through the dark corridor of the gate.

Someone with sharp eyes, aided by the firelight, seemed to make out something... a sickly green.

"It looks like..."

Silence. Oppression. Sinister dread—

"Squeeeeeeee!!!"

The goblin vanguard charged in first! Their curved blades swung violently, *slicing* through the air as they began their slaughter!

The villagers at the front didn’t even realize what was happening before their heads rolled, blood spraying in pillars, painting the ground crimson.

"AAAAAAAAAAH!"

Screams erupted as countless unarmed villagers turned and fled, jostling against each other in a chaotic, crushing stampede.

The main goblin force surged into the village like a tide. Arrows and blades gleamed in the firelight—men had their throats slit, women were stripped and dragged away, and even children were not spared the butcher’s blade.

Thick smoke billowed as the village was set ablaze, the flames rising higher, gradually spreading in all directions.

Screams and roars filled the air—this massacre feast

had begun...

title: Chapter 63 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 63 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 63

In the distance, thick smoke billowed, as if demons were attacking, baring their fangs and claws.

The heavy dark clouds, unable to bear the weight any longer, finally began to drip with a light rain.

Yet the flames of slaughter spreading through the village showed no sign of being extinguished by the drizzle.

Alice walked down the street, carrying two large bags in her arms filled with bread and apples, planning to eat them during her travels.

She was still troubled by her debts. Every purchase had to be carefully considered for her future survival—she couldn’t afford expensive things. All her suffering was that bastard Merlin’s fault!

Alice had originally intended to return to the inn, pack her things, and leave immediately. But on the way, she was drawn in by the rolling black smoke and the flickering flames.

"What’s going on? Is there a fire…?"

Alice frowned slightly. The fire seemed to be spreading rapidly.

Countless villagers, their faces pale and twisted in terror, sprinted toward her, fleeing in a panic.

They kept glancing back, as if afraid something horrific was chasing them. Even if they stumbled, they scrambled back to their feet and kept running.

"It’s coming! They’re here! Run!"

Many frantic villagers shouted as they passed her, all saying something similar.

Who were "they"?

What in the world was happening?

Alice felt something was wrong. Her instincts told her that something major must have occurred where the fire was burning.

A few villagers, having lost their senses in panic, accidentally bumped into Alice, scattering her apples and bread across the ground.

"Hey! Wait a second, I’m talking to you—"

Alice complained, furious at their rudeness.

"Run!!!"

An elderly villager stumbled toward her, barely staying on his feet.

Then, a crossbow bolt shot straight through the back of his head, the arrowhead bursting out from his throat.

The old man’s expression froze, his eyes gradually losing their light. A few drops of blood dripped from the crimson-tipped arrow in his mouth before he collapsed powerlessly to the ground.

Alice’s eyes widened, staring blankly at the scene. A few drops of blood had even splattered onto her beautiful face, making it look eerie.

What… was this?

Alice stood frozen in place, numb, as the slaughter before her sent a chill through her very soul. It was the first time she had ever seen villagers being killed in broad daylight.

The gruesome sight filled the nineteen-year-old girl with a deep, icy dread.

"Squeak! Squeak! Squeak!"

The distinctive cries of goblins rang out. In the distance, many goblins wielding curved blades and short swords chased after the unarmed villagers.

The villagers fled helplessly—many were elderly, weak, women, or children who couldn’t run fast. Many fell to the goblins’ blades.

The goblins howled, sneered, and raged, mercilessly swinging their slaughtering knives, staining the earth red.

Alice’s expression darkened. A flame flickered in her ice-blue eyes.

She didn’t know exactly what was happening, but even a fool could see that goblins had invaded the village and were carrying out a merciless massacre.

"Squeak! Squeak! Squeak!"

A goblin grabbed an old man and stomped him underfoot, raising its curved blade to stab into his heart.

*Whoosh!* A sharp gust of cold air struck as a pointed ice spike pierced through the goblin’s head, splattering blood everywhere. The old man beneath it managed to escape.

The twenty or so goblins were the vanguard. Seeing their comrade killed, they were all taken aback.

Alice raised her hand toward the group of goblins. As a high-tier powerhouse, killing goblins was effortless for her.

A single low-tier spell, *Ice Spike*, took one down.

Before she understood the situation, Alice wouldn’t recklessly expend her magic or battle aura. She would only use spells with minimal cost to probe.

The higher the tier of magic or martial arts, the greater the drain. If she ran out of magic or battle aura when facing a boss, she’d be in serious trouble, unable to fight at full strength.

Even Saint-tier powerhouses, without magic or battle aura, could be pinned down and crushed by high-tier enemies. This was a common sight.

Maintaining a full reserve of magic or battle aura was crucial. That was why low-tier spells and techniques were still essential in battle.

Ultimate techniques were only used when victory was certain or the effect was extraordinary. Otherwise, excessive drain without gain would leave her weakened, leading to a devastating loss.

Power tiers represented differences in might. Even with the same low-tier spell, the difference between a Saint-tier and a low-tier user was like comparing an ocean to a droplet—the gap in power was immense.

"Squeak! Squeak! Squeak!"

The goblin vanguard bared their fangs at Alice, their sharp teeth glinting ominously as they prepared to charge.

"Don’t think you can do whatever you want in front of me!"

Alice channeled her magic and unleashed a hundred *Ice Spikes* in rapid succession!

As someone who cultivated both magic and martial arts, the difficulty was immense, but it came with advantages—she had two different reserves of power inside her body that she could alternate between.

In simpler terms, while others had one MP bar, she had two. This made her combat versatile and her endurance long-lasting.

The hundred *Ice Spikes* radiated cold energy, firing like a machine gun—*rat-tat-tat*—turning the twenty-plus goblins in front of her into sieves, their flesh and blood reduced to a messy pulp.

Alice lowered her arm and looked toward the distant flickering flames. The situation there was likely similar—dire, with people possibly in need of rescue.

She couldn’t just stand by and watch. She had to go.

Without further hesitation, Alice activated her battle aura to quicken her pace and ran toward the scene of the disturbance. After just a few steps, she encountered a fully armed goblin army.

The two sides faced off for three seconds. The goblin warriors stared at Alice, sensing the oppressive might of her high-tier power.

Alice unleashed her high-tier barrier spell, *Zero Realm*—she had used it once before in front of the Demon Lord Palace.

Though it continuously drained her magic, it was highly effective in group battles, slowing enemies down while inflicting continuous frostbite.

"Come on, don’t blink…" Alice drew the pure silver slender sword at her waist. The *Hymn of Light*, sharp and gleaming, trembled and emitted a pleasant hum—

"Or else…"

"You won’t even know when your head rolls."

title: Chapter 64
content:
Chapter 64

Volume 2 · Chapter 64

"Squeeeee!!!"

The goblin horde let out a furious roar and charged first, baring their jagged teeth and brandishing their curved blades with reckless abandon.

In the distance, several goblin priests shook the bells in their hands, casting cold-resistance spells to help their allies endure the freezing chill of "Zero Realm" a little longer, preventing them from stiffening and dying from the extreme cold before even reaching Alice.

Most of the goblins, confident in their numerical advantage, believed they stood a chance—unaware that before true power, numbers were nothing but weeds to be mowed down with a single swing of the scythe.

Alice’s face was as cold as frost, her breathtaking beauty etched with resolve, revealing a will as unyielding as steel.

Instead of retreating, she advanced, gripping her gleaming silver rapier, and clashed head-on with the organized goblin army.

Dark clouds rolled ominously overhead, a light drizzle falling in pitter-patter drops.

Yet on the central road of the village, snowflakes drifted down, forming a bizarre spectacle.

Arcane barriers swirled around Alice, and before she even arrived, the biting wind and snow struck first!

Countless snowflakes seemed to scream in fury, intertwined with howling gales, slicing through the air like blades.

The leading goblin vanguard’s momentum crumbled instantly, unable to take a single step closer to Alice, inching forward only within the barrier.

They couldn’t even open their eyes, unable to face the righteous figure that seemed like a Valkyrie descended from heaven!

Even with the priests’ cold-resistance buffs, they were useless against Alice. How could such lowly creatures resist the might of high-tier magic?

Alice hadn’t even moved yet, but most of the goblins in front had already lost their will to fight from the cold. Some were even frozen solid, unable to take a single step.

Expressionless, Alice channeled her fighting spirit and leapt forward, her slender figure darting into the enemy ranks with terrifying speed, as if passing through an empty field!

From the moment Alice drew her rapier, the battle became a one-sided slaughter.

With a flick of her sword, screams erupted.

With a stomp of her foot, countless shards of ice exploded outward.

Alice’s movements were ghostly, her beautiful silver hair blending seamlessly with the snow and ice.

Even if the goblins didn’t blink, they couldn’t comprehend what was happening—only sensing that a monster lurked within the biting wind and snow.

When they caught sight of silver hair dancing amid the blood and snow, a sword would slash their throats, spraying crimson like scattered roses, staining the icy sky.

Ruthless, cold-blooded, and unhesitating swordplay sent the goblins into a full retreat.

Alice cut through them like melons, wielding her sharp holy blade, transforming into a silver demon, annihilating the goblin horde—

It’s been so long since I’ve been angry.

And so long since I’ve meddled in others’ affairs.

In the Death Swamp, watching that overwhelmingly powerful figure…

I realized my own weakness, constantly doubting myself.

Alice suddenly pierced three goblin heads with a single thrust, then flicked her blade, sending their skulls flying into the air, blood raining down—

Ah, that’s right.

I’m not as strong as that person.

Just as my teacher said, there are many things I cannot do.

Alice spun around, swinging her rapier, sending a group of goblins to hell—

But so what?

Even if I’m not strong.

There are still things I can do.

Live by upholding my own beliefs.

Alice flicked her blade, magic surging as she unleashed a fierce cold, turning the goblins before her into crystalline ice sculptures—

I won’t give up just because I can’t do something.

If I want to do it, then I must try.

Many things aren’t impossible just because they’re hard.

Like now—only I can save this village!

The goblin soldiers trembled in fear. This wasn’t a fair fight—it was a one-sided massacre.

Seeing they stood no chance against Alice, they turned to flee, discarding their armor and weapons in a chaotic retreat.

But Alice gave them no chance to escape. Before they knew it, her graceful figure had already appeared behind the main goblin force, her back turned to the enemy, silver hair dancing, her face devoid of any emotion.

Everyone knew how dangerous it was to turn your back to the enemy in battle, yet Alice remained composed and calm, her rapier still stained with goblin blood.

A few goblins harbored wicked thoughts, naively attempting a surprise attack—only to find their feet frozen in place, unable to move.

Not just a few, but the entire goblin army had somehow been frozen solid at some point. None had escaped, all reduced to living targets.

Alice, still facing away from them, shook the blood from her blade and sheathed her rapier with a *shink*.

"Frost Thorns..."

A mid-tier area-of-effect spell activated, and countless sharp ice spikes erupted behind Alice, rapidly spreading across the central road.

*Bang! Bang! Bang!* The spikes burst from the ground as if alive, quickly growing taller, mercilessly impaling the immobilized goblins and lifting them high into the air!

"Squeee..."

The goblin horde wailed in agony, their screams echoing like ghosts and wolves. This was not a swift death—it was slow and excruciating, their bodies turned into sieves as they endured the pain.

Blood streamed down the ice spikes, pooling into rivers, and the central road had become a hellscape for the goblins.

The entire goblin horde was wiped out, their corpses impaled on the dazzling ice spikes like the work of a skewering executioner.

Alice never once turned to look, her gaze fixed on the thick black smoke and flames in the distance—

I will be merciless...

For justice, I draw my blade!

title: Chapter 65 — Reward Chapter
content:
Chapter 65 — Reward Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 65

The tavern.

Merlin had been hearing a terrible racket outside for some time now.

The clanging and banging was downright irritating, and every so often, a scream would pierce the air.

Merlin was currently drinking with a few female patrons, and curiosity got the better of him. He stood up.

"Ladies, I’ll go check what’s happening outside."

"Nooo~ Merlin, stay with us," one of them pouted.

"Yeah, it’s probably just the neighbors having a domestic dispute."

The two women grabbed Merlin’s hands, refusing to let him leave.

Merlin pondered for a moment. These days, cuckolds were everywhere—catching a cheating spouse and starting a fight was practically routine. Maybe it was even one of his own customers. Heh heh heh~

"Alright, let’s keep chatting."

"Tell us about that business with the baroness again."

"Her? Word is the baron refused to divorce her and dragged her back by force."

Merlin and the two women carried on, spinning tall tales about his romantic escapades with reckless abandon.

Before long, the commotion outside grew louder and closer, which was odd.

*Bang!*

Someone kicked open the tavern door—

"Squee squee squee!"

Three fully armed goblins burst in, their green skin glistening, their pointed faces and monkey-like cheeks twisted into grins as they brandished their curved blades.

"Ahhhhhh!"

The two female patrons were startled, their faces contorted in terror as they screamed.

"Squee squee squee~"

The goblins cackled, delighted by the women’s reactions. Merlin, however, remained perfectly calm, still draped between the two women with not a hint of panic.

The goblins weren’t pleased. They raised their weapons and started shrieking at Merlin.

Merlin frowned, annoyed. This was ruining his mood—his refined atmosphere for picking up women was gone.

Tch!

What was up with these green-skinned freaks?

◆

In the distance, the fire showed no signs of dying down.

Rain pattered lightly against the streets.

Thick smoke rose like a warning, coiling into the sky.

If Alice hadn’t blocked the main goblin force on Central Avenue, the situation might have been far worse.

But even with Alice doing her best, some goblins had still slipped into the village.

Little Henry was still playing with his two friends. He’d been boasting about how Alice was a high-ranking sword mage and how she was going to teach him swordplay.

Under his friends’ envious gazes, he felt like the king of the playground. From now on, he’d be the top dog at Leifeng Primary!

"Whoa! Henry, look!" one of the kids pointed in a direction.

Henry followed his finger and saw rolling smoke and flames spreading.

"Maybe… someone’s house caught fire?"

"Hey, should we go check it out? Looks fun," another child said.

Before Henry could answer, he heard a familiar voice calling his name.

"Henry? Henry! Come home, it’s not safe out here!"

Martha had been searching for Henry for a while. Along the way, she’d seen a few panicked people shouting about a goblin attack, though she wasn’t sure if it was true.

But she was still worried sick about her son, and her urgency grew.

"Uh-oh! It’s my mom! Quick, hide!"

Without a second thought, Henry grabbed his friends and they all squeezed into a large barrel by the roadside. Since they were small, they fit inside with room to spare.

Martha, holding her umbrella and lifting her skirt, rushed past the barrel, her face pale with worry.

"Henry! Come back right now, stop playing around!"

Henry and his friends stifled their giggles, finding the whole thing hilarious.

This month’s bonus chapters have all been repaid, and then some.
