This month’s ticket bonus: 18 chapters (equivalent to 900 tickets), though it didn’t quite reach that.

Reward bonus: 11 chapters (equivalent to ¥550). The extra tickets balanced it out, so it’s all settled.

Starting tomorrow, I’ll begin stockpiling chapters. Bonus updates might slow down, but I’ll add as many as I can. If that doesn’t work, I’ll save them all up and unleash them in early December.

Feel free to throw your votes my way. If you’ve read my old works, you know I almost never fall behind on bonus chapters—monthly tickets and rewards are always repaid.

title: Chapter 66 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 66 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 66

"Henry..."

Martha's voice grew fainter and fainter, as if she was moving away from the wine barrels where the group of children were hiding.

"Kekekeke, this is such a great place. It'll be our secret base from now on." Little Henry grinned, certain that he could come out to play every day from now on.

"That works. Then you won’t have to go home when your mom calls you for dinner," one child said.

"Yeah, that’s right," another child chimed in.

"YAAAAH! What are you doing?! Help! Help me!!!"

Martha’s desperate cries suddenly rang out, as if she was struggling fiercely.

Little Henry’s heart lurched—he thought his mother must have run into some thug. If that were true, he would have to rush out and kill them.

The children were all shocked and suspicious. They peeked through the cracks in the wine barrels to see what was happening outside.

Green, oily skin, crossbow bolts on their backs, pointed ears, big noses, jagged teeth—goblins!

It turned out Martha had been ambushed by goblins who had sneaked in. The situation was dire.

Two goblins pinned Martha to the ground, immobilizing her. Another one pulled out a rope, seemingly intending to tie her up and take her back as an offering to their emperor, since she was rather attractive.

"Help! Someone, please save me! Please, let me go!"

"Mom—mmph!!!"

Little Henry had just shouted, ready to charge out with his small wooden sword to save his mother, but two of his friends pressed him down hard and clamped a hand over his mouth, preventing him from making a sound.

"Mmmph! Mmmph! Mmmph!!!" Little Henry growled in frustration.

"Henry, do you have a death wish?! Goblins eat people! You’ll die!" one of his friends whispered, his face pale with terror.

"Yeah, Henry, please, just stay quiet. We don’t want to die either," another child sobbed.

"Mmmph! Mmmph!!!" Little Henry roared in helpless rage, tears of frustration streaming down his face as his cheeks flushed red, his chest burning with fury.

"Save me... please, someone save me..."

Martha was in a sorry state, covered in mud and water, her strength spent from struggling. She had no energy left to resist.

The goblins bound her tightly and dragged her away.

"Henry..."

Little Henry, hidden in the wine barrel, let tears of hatred and rage fall as his friends held him down, forcing him to watch helplessly as the goblins dragged his mother away—

"Mmmph! Mmmph!!!"

◆

*Bang!*

A deafening explosion sent two goblins flying out of the tavern like cannonballs. They splattered against the opposite wall, their flesh and blood smeared across it in a grotesque mess.

A vivid description of their deaths would be like mosquitoes being swatted against a wall—uncannily similar.

"Squeeee..."

One goblin crawled out of the tavern in agony, drenched in blood, severely wounded, moving as slowly as a snail.

The goblin wailed pitifully, its eyes darting back in terror every so often, as if something horrifying was behind it.

Merlin stepped out of the tavern and crushed the goblin’s spine under his foot.

"Honestly, don’t disturb me while I’m drinking."

"Squeee... *crunch!*"

Merlin stomped on the goblin’s head, silencing it completely.

The scene was as brutal as smashing a watermelon with a bat—blood splattered like fireworks.

Merlin shook his head, but his gaze then fell on the village, half of which was engulfed in flames. Thick smoke billowed upward, coiling like a dragon, merging with the dark clouds in the sky. It was a spectacular, yet horrifying sight.

"What’s going on?"

Merlin muttered to himself, staring at the village consumed by fire, utterly bewildered.

Even though it was a drizzly day, he could still feel a wave of heat.

"Squeeee squeeee squeeee!!!"

The scene changed abruptly—hundreds of goblins descended from the sky!

A swarm so dense it blotted out the heavens, blocking Merlin’s view entirely.

They wielded curved blades and daggers, their expressions grim as they launched a ferocious assault on Merlin.

The timing of their ambush was impeccable—it was clear they were going for the kill.

Merlin, however, remained perfectly calm. A smirk played on his lips, his golden hair shimmering like sunlight in the dark night, swaying gently.

He reached for the katana at his waist and sneered disdainfully—

"Hmph hmph..."

"Pathetic weaklings... do you truly think you can *dance* before me?"

title: Chapter 67
content:
Chapter 67

Volume 2 · Chapter 67

A cold wind howled, and the distant firelight illuminated Merlin’s face.

Golden strands of hair framed his forehead, while his ruby-like eyes radiated indifference.

Swarm upon swarm of goblins descended like flies from the sky, their roars and howls grotesque, their daggers and curved blades slashing through the night as they charged forward.

Merlin had no interest in such pathetic foes, but if mosquitoes buzzed in his ear, wouldn’t he swat them?

The weak were not to be feared—what was truly terrifying was the weak who flaunted their strength.

Merlin kept his hand resting on the katana at his waist, standing motionless, his body shrouded in shadow.

With casual indifference, he used his thumb to nudge the blade slightly from its sheath, exposing just a sliver of the demon sword Banri Garan. Instantly, it unleashed a terrifying sword aura, like a demon’s world-ending strike, sending tremors through the air.

This was the same move he had used to kill the thief goblins before—effortless, careless. Merlin only used this technique when he didn’t acknowledge his opponent’s strength, an act of sheer arrogance.

Because foes this weak didn’t even deserve the honor of him drawing his blade!

With such a contemptuous attitude, he humiliated his feeble enemies.

The sword aura rampaged outward, as if invisible blades tore through the horde of goblins, slicing them all in an instant—clean, without the slightest hesitation.

Merlin’s control was flawless; aside from the swarming goblins, not a single thing was harmed.

The goblins in the sky suddenly fell silent, their shouts ceasing, their bodies freezing midair, unable to move.

Their bull-like eyes widened in terror as they stared down at the composed, golden-haired man below.

“Turn to fireworks, and make your final contribution to the world.”

With a flick of his wrist, Merlin sheathed the exposed sliver of the blade, producing a crisp metallic *clang*.

*Shing—*

A rapid succession of *pops* echoed as the entire goblin army exploded into minced flesh, their blood and gore splattering like fireworks.

This particular goblin force was truly unlucky. Of all the people they could have encountered, they had to cross paths with the former arrogant monarch, a man whose martial prowess had reached the absolute pinnacle.

Their ambush had backfired spectacularly—caught mid-sneak attack, they were mercilessly annihilated in the blink of an eye, without so much as a scream.

Merlin stood in the light rain, letting the droplets patter against his body, sliding down his neck and seeping into his clothes.

The rain washed away the blood from the ground, leaving the tavern’s entrance desolate, littered with goblin corpses.

Merlin didn’t give the goblin ambush a second thought. Instead, he casually muttered to himself—

“So this is the joy of a ‘mowing down’ game, huh?”

(-`ω-)?

◆

Central Gate.

Gegwu stood here, overseeing the army, telescope in hand as he observed the battle from atop a carriage.

The light rain and darkness obscured his vision.

At first, the battle had seemed to be going well, but soon, a scout goblin came rushing back with a report.

“Lord Gegwu! The entire western force has been wiped out—no survivors!”

“What?!” Gegwu furrowed his brow, his pointed nose twitching as he considered the implications. “Was it the work of a high-tier powerhouse?”

“N-No! We couldn’t sense any magic or fighting spirit from him at all! He just looked like an ordinary man—golden hair, red eyes, and *damn* handsome!” the scout goblin blurted out, his fear making him careless with his words.

“Who cares if he’s handsome?! We’re not *gay*bins!” Gegwu snapped, grinding his teeth.

“Y-Yes, you’re absolutely right, Lord Gegwu.” The scout goblin bowed his head.

“So what you’re saying is… our entire western force was wiped out by a *normal* man?” Gegwu asked cautiously, a flicker of unease in his voice. According to their intelligence, this village only had one high-tier powerhouse. There was no mention of anyone else.

If it had been a high-tier opponent, he could have still fought back with the help of the army. But if there was *another* powerhouse in this village… that would be trouble.

“Y-Yes! Just one person! He took out our entire ambush force in a single strike! I-I didn’t even see how it happened! That golden-haired man didn’t even draw his sword—he just flicked his wrist twice, and our warriors were all dead…” The scout goblin shivered, certain that if he had been any closer, he too would have been turned into meat paste.

“How is that possible?!” Gegwu was stunned. Goblins weren’t fruit—you couldn’t just slice through them like that! And they hadn’t even seen the attack coming!

“It’s the truth! I saw it with my own eyes!” the scout goblin insisted.

Gegwu’s face remained frozen in shock, his mind reeling. Just how strong was that golden-haired man? His power was unfathomable—one strike to annihilate a fully armed goblin army? Even high-tier fighters left traces of their techniques. What kind of nonsense was this?

Could he be a Saint-tier enemy…

Gegwu found that entirely plausible. Some people just *loved* the tired old trick of playing weak to crush their opponents. It made them look even more impressive when they revealed their true strength.

There was something deeply satisfying, it seemed, in watching your enemy’s face turn red with frustration. Truly, a vile taste…

And there *were* Saint-tier individuals who hid their power. Many of them, in fact—big shots who loved pretending to be weak. Disgusting, *disgusting~*

After much deliberation, Gegwu concluded that the golden-haired man was likely a Saint-tier powerhouse, or at the very least, at the peak of the high tier.

This was bad. He couldn’t take on two high-tier opponents, especially not when one of them had unfathomable strength and was likely a deceptive powerhouse pretending to be weak.

“And the central road forces have been wiped out too! Their bodies are impaled on ice spikes, high in the air—it’s a gruesome sight. That high-tier silver-haired sword-mage is moving this way!” the scout goblin delivered another shocking report.

“…”

Gegwu’s entire body trembled. That silver-haired sword-mage was no pushover either! Anyone capable of slaughtering a horde of goblins single-handedly was no easy target.

The situation was dire. Their initial assessment had been wrong. If they stayed any longer, they risked being caught between two high-tier enemies—a terrible position.

“Lord Gegwu, what should we do?” the scout asked respectfully.

“Retreat for now. Take the women and gold we’ve looted and return to the underground palace!”

Without hesitation, Gegwu issued the order to fall back.

The goblin warriors blew their heavy war horns, signaling a full retreat to all goblins in the village…

title: Chapter 68
content:
Chapter 68

Volume 2 · Chapter 68

The giant goblin covered the retreat of its forces, each movement making the earth tremble as it heaved its massive wolf-tooth club onto its shoulder.

Its enormous body blocked the doorway, its lantern-like eyes rolling around as it carefully scanned the surroundings, refusing to let anyone approach.

Nearby, among some ruins, the lower-tier warrior Strongson—who had been sent flying into the ceiling by Merlin’s punch earlier—clutched a black box and sneaked around, peering inside.

The box held his life savings, several hundred gold coins. There was no way he was leaving behind the money he’d worked so hard to earn.

Strongson was just a petty bourgeois man. No matter the disaster, money came first.

Even at the risk of his life, he had to retrieve his hard-earned cash.

Clutching the black box, Strongson stared at the giant goblin across from him.

When it turned its back, he seized the moment, activated his pitiful lower-tier battle aura, and bolted.

He swore he’d never run this fast—not even when he’d sprinted toward an egg cell!

Holy shit! It’s working! I’m actually getting away…

A grin of disbelief spread across Strongson’s face.

*BOOM!*

With a deafening crash, the giant goblin leapt directly in front of Strongson, blocking his path.

Strongson’s face turned deathly pale, his mind blank. He hadn’t expected such a massive goblin to be so agile—it could even jump like that!

*Tch!* The giant goblin exhaled a white, hot breath from between its teeth. It had long since caught the scent of the human and had been patrolling here, refusing to leave.

“A… a… l-listen! We can talk this out!”

Strongson was utterly terrified, staring up at the towering goblin. His legs trembled uncontrollably, and a dark yellow liquid trickled down his pants—he’d actually been scared to the point of pissing himself.

Shaking, he raised the black box, forcing a strained smile.

“M-money… I’ll give you all of it… j-just spare me…”

The giant goblin looked down at the tiny Strongson, said nothing, and roared furiously before raising its massive club, slamming it down with a thunderous crash, intent on flattening this little ant into a meat patty.

“*Eeeeee!!!*”

Strongson collapsed to the ground in terror, his teeth chattering violently, his mind filled with the certainty of death.

But just as the crisis peaked—

In that critical moment, a dazzling figure flashed in front of Strongson. Her face was obscured by silvery hair that shimmered like moonlight, and an icy aura radiated from her, sending chills down one’s spine.

Alice rushed in at the last second, raising her slender sword to meet the giant goblin’s strike head-on!

The moment the club and sword collided, a shocking impact rippled through the air, but it didn’t so much as budge Alice. She stood firm, unshaken.

As a dual cultivator of magic and martial arts, Alice’s battle aura was the real deal—high-tier. Unlike pure mages, her swordsmanship in close combat was anything but weak!

“You’re still worrying about money at a time like this? Do you even have a life left to spend it?”

Strongson was still in shock, speechless. The Alice before him radiated immense power—judging by the pressure she emitted, she was actually a high-tier powerhouse?

Alice and the giant goblin remained locked in a stalemate for a moment before she flicked her wrist, sending the goblin stumbling back a step. Then, with a surge of battle aura, she lunged forward, thrusting her sword in a straight stab that sent the goblin flying!

The giant goblin crashed into the crumbling city wall with a *gurgling* thud, looking utterly pathetic.

“S-she’s… so strong!”

Strongson watched, mouth agape, genuinely impressed. He thought to himself, *No wonder she’s a high-tier powerhouse—every move is packed with power.*

The giant goblin was only a near high-tier monster. Compared to Alice, a true high-tier fighter, there was still a considerable gap.

“Get back. Don’t stay here—it’s not safe.”

Alice advanced toward the giant goblin through the light rain. Her slender figure was captivating, her high-heeled boots stepping into puddles, sending ripples across the water’s surface.

At this moment, this swordswoman of ice and snow commanded the battlefield.

Strongson quickly scrambled to hide off to the side. With his lower-tier strength, he was no help—he’d only cause trouble.

“Sorry, but based on your brutal behavior, I have to kill you. I won’t waste words on you.”

Alice closed in on the giant goblin step by step, her face expressionless, veiled in frost.

The purple hem of her dress swayed slightly. Though the absolute territory beneath her skirt—pale and flawless—was undeniably alluring, the icy aura she emitted crushed any impure thoughts.

Alice raised her hand, and in an instant, countless ice spikes erupted like a machine gun, *rat-tat-tat*, shooting toward the giant goblin.

“*Roar!*”

The giant goblin raised its arms to shield its vitals. The incoming ice spikes all embedded themselves into its flesh, and in no time, its body was riddled with holes.

Seeing that the tide had turned, the giant goblin grabbed its club and decided on a desperate last stand, charging at Alice to grapple with her.

It sprinted toward her, using its mangled arms to block her ice spikes as it rapidly closed the distance.

Without hesitation, the giant goblin swung its massive club at Alice’s head.

The situation was critical, but for Alice, it was nothing. She had faced far more powerful beings before. This attack was still too weak for her.

Alice effortlessly deflected the giant goblin’s club with her slender sword, the collision ringing out with a *clang*.

Then, in a counterattack, she plunged her sword into the enemy’s body.

The strike seemed almost casual, as if she were toying with her foe. The thrust appeared unremarkable, like a needle in the ocean.

Yet the giant goblin collapsed with a thunderous crash, its skin turning purple from the cold, frost billowing from its body, its face frozen in an expression of sheer terror.

Alice hadn’t used any special technique—she’d simply infused her ice-affinity magic into the giant goblin’s body, freezing it to death instantly.

This death was painless, a small mercy from Alice, a hint of kindness and pity for her enemy.

Strongson, hiding in the distance, watched Alice’s powerful, beautiful, and compassionate figure and was completely stunned. If the Goddess of Light truly existed, she must look exactly like this silver-haired girl.

Alice gazed at the burning village. Just yesterday, it had been bustling and prosperous. Now, it was in ruins.

Finally, under the downpour, the flames began to die down.

Her eyes turned outward, heavy with worry. She felt she had to hurry and rescue the kidnapped people before things got worse.

Goblins were cruel by nature, fiercely hostile to other races—unlike the peace-loving elves.

And they were inherently lustful, showing no mercy to women. It was extremely dangerous.

Alice’s thoughts were decent enough, but if that indecent bastard Merlin had been here, he would’ve shamelessly commented—

*Whoa~*

*Major crisis!*

*If we don’t save these women tonight,*

*how many green hats will the village men have to wear?*

*Might as well rename the place Wales’ Cuckold Village. Or Forgiveness Village, that works too.*

*No idea why, but whenever I think about this kind of thing, I just feel like singing…*

*Of course, the answer is to forgive her~?*

(o°ω°o)

title: Chapter 69
content:
Chapter 69

Volume 2 · Chapter 69

The village after the attack.

It was in ruins everywhere, with nearly half the houses burned to the ground.

Many villagers had been killed, or worse, taken captive.

Fortunately, with Alice and Merlin present, most of the residents in the central and western areas had survived. The other parts, however, had not fared so well.

After the battle, the villagers came to their senses and gazed at their destroyed homes, overwhelmed with grief.

The village chief rang the assembly bell, gathering the survivors to discuss what to do about the captured women.

The rain in the sky showed no sign of stopping—in fact, it seemed to be growing heavier.

"Many people have been taken to the mountain behind us. Everyone, think about how to handle this. I can't decide this alone!"

The current village chief was a man in his forties. He, too, had clearly been badly shaken. Standing on the platform with a face smudged with dirt and clothes torn—likely from his escape—he looked disheveled.

"What else can we do? You all saw how terrifying those goblins were. They're all holed up in their nest, and we have no way to rescue them. Maybe... maybe we should just let it go. We can't let the tragedy continue..."

The mustachioed innkeeper, the one Merlin had once forced to pay for a meal, muttered from the crowd, his face still etched with terror from the goblins.

Right now, he was a mess, as if he had been violated by the goblins himself, his mind scarred beyond repair.

This defeatist mood spread quickly. Most of the villagers were ordinary people, and the fear of goblins ran deep. Going up the mountain to rescue the captives would almost certainly be a death sentence.

The atmosphere grew heavy. Everyone began whispering, and many were clearly prioritizing self-preservation.

But there were still those who frowned, their loved ones taken—how could they just abandon them?

"Are you joking?! My mom was taken! Am I supposed to just pretend I didn’t see it?! Don’t you have family taken too?! Do you think they don’t want you to save them?! Are you even men?! This is pathetic!" Little Henry exploded in the crowd, nearly crying from frustration.

Many people lowered their heads in shame. They wanted to save their loved ones, but they were also afraid to die.

Even the village chief on the platform looked troubled. Sending a group of villagers to fight a goblin army? That was a joke. It would be suicide.

"We need to save them! It’s only right to shed blood for family! Who wants to live with the guilt of not trying?! If you don’t save them, you’ll go to hell!" Henry shouted in desperation. He wanted to rescue his mother, but he knew his own strength wasn’t enough.

"Hmph hmph hmph, nonsense! **Papa!**" A preacher in a black robe, a silver cross hanging from his chest, stepped forward. "No one here will go to hell, because the great Goddess of Light is merciful! **Papa!**"

Some of the more ignorant villagers fell silent at the sight of the priest. Many in the village were devout, with deep faith, and they trusted the clergy implicitly.

The priest made the sign of the cross, his expression pious—

"In the name of the Goddess of Light, Maria, I absolve you of your sins! Amen!"

Countless villagers below pressed their palms together, murmuring devoutly as if brainwashed.

"Amen..."

"You’re all insane! This guy’s just a fraud who swindles money! Even the Goddess of Light wouldn’t stand by and do nothing!" Henry grew anxious, watching as everyone’s resolve crumbled. He was furious.

"What does a child like you know? I am a priest. My words are the will of the Goddess of Light. There is no need to doubt this, **Papa**." The priest clasped his hands behind his back. Mocking the ignorant was his way of asserting worth.

"You’re just manipulating the crowd! Every moment we delay, the captives are in more danger! If something happens to them, you, the fraud, will definitely go to hell!" Henry glared through the rain, shouting at the priest on the platform.

"As a priest, I will never go to hell. And neither will anyone here who has faith in the Goddess. For those who wish to repent quickly, I have a few deluxe scriptures here—only one hundred gold coins each, first come, first served! **Papa!**" The priest revealed his ugly true nature, trying to profit from the chaos.

"At a time like this, all you can think about is selling those stupid books!" Henry was so angry he nearly cried. He wished he could rush up and bite the meddling priest to death.

"Don’t misunderstand. I am purifying your sins!" The priest spread his arms, the silver cross on his chest gleaming. "We are powerless against the goblins. Knowing the enemy is far stronger and still charging to our deaths would be foolish! But we can pray here! Sincere prayer will move the Goddess of Light to help us, to save the souls of the captured in the unseen realm!"

"Father..."

The villagers below looked at the priest with awe, as if he were a radiant savior. Many began to pray devoutly, trying to change reality with their blind faith.

They’re all mad!

These people are completely insane!

Why do they trust some intangible god but not themselves?

Henry felt utterly powerless. He had said so much, yet it couldn’t compare to the priest’s single "Amen." This kind of faith was sick, beyond reason.

The rain poured down, and Henry felt like everyone had lost their minds. The sky was dark, filled with despair.

"Prayer is nothing but self-comfort. It does nothing in reality."

Alice’s voice came from behind. She strode forward in her high-heeled boots, her steps firm.

Her expression was cold, her face unreadable.

Alice had been watching from the back for a while. At a moment of decision like this, everyone’s true nature—good or evil, beautiful or ugly—was written plainly on their faces.

She felt helpless, even a little disappointed. At a time like this, so many people couldn’t see as clearly as a bratty child. It was foolish and pathetic.

"Big Sister..." Henry’s eyes regained some light, as if he had found hope again.

"Henry, you’ve done well..." Alice patted Henry’s shoulder, then stepped past him to the front.

"Who are you? Some heretic from who-knows-where? Daring to slander our sacred prayers—you should be burned at the stake! **Papa!**" The priest pointed at Alice, standing at the front of the platform, and shouted.

"My name is Alice Clodia, a Golden Adventurer of Lexham, and the 233rd Hero of the Holy Church."

Alice’s gaze was resolute, her demeanor heroic. Her silver hair, drenched by the rain, was slightly disheveled, yet she remained stunning.

She introduced herself directly, even revealing her former title as Hero.

Alice didn’t particularly like the title of the 233rd Hero. After failing to defeat Merlin, she had been burdened with many stains on her reputation, blamed for all sorts of things.

Normally, Alice would never mention that she was the 233rd Hero.

But today, to wake these foolish villagers from their delusion, she had to acknowledge her identity. Only then could she speak to the priest on equal footing.

Most of the villagers had blind faith in the clergy, so by invoking her status as Hero, Alice’s credibility would increase significantly.

The villagers below were stunned. The whispers that followed were downright cruel—

"She’s *that* 233rd Hero? She’s actually alive?"

"Out of a hundred thousand who went on the crusade, she was the only one who survived."

"Wasn’t she defiled to death by the Demon Lord? Did she come back from the dead or something?"

"I heard she was defiled by Lucifer the Third and lost her chastity."

"No, no, my version is that the Hero offered her chastity herself, and *then* Lucifer the Third defiled her, sparing her life."

"Wait, no, Lucifer the Third took a liking to the Hero, and the moment they locked eyes—*smack smack smack*—they fell in love, so the Great Demon Lord let her go."

"I don’t know the details, but the 233rd Hero definitely got *smack smack smacked* by Lucifer the Third."

"Yeah, no matter the version, she definitely got *smack smack smacked*..."

title: Chapter 70
content:
Chapter 70

Volume 2 · Chapter 70

Alice’s forehead immediately broke out in a black line, feeling her face burn with humiliation.

This was exactly why she hated her Hero title—her reputation was already in the gutter.

Sure, she and Merlin had shared some ambiguous moments in the Death Swamp, but that had only involved taking off their clothes! Nothing lewd or inappropriate had happened!

Yet no one seemed to believe that. And since Alice had survived alone, it left plenty of room for onlookers to fill in the blanks with their wild imaginations.

Without her knowledge, all sorts of vile rumors about the Demon Lord and the Hero had spread like wildfire.

Even the sex education textbooks sold on the streets used the Demon Lord and the Hero as illustrations, depicting various positions in painstaking, blush-inducing, eye-avoiding detail.

There were countless versions, each vividly described, but they all shared three common points—

1. Merlin and Alice had definitely hooked up. *Clap clap clap.*

2. In every version, Merlin was the domineering CEO.

3. Alice was always a silly, airheaded, naive girl.

Who the hell is slandering my purity?! Step forward! I’ll shove my sword through your mouth without even drawing it!

And Merlin, a domineering CEO? He’s so broke he’s pissing blood! A good-for-nothing who scams women out of money, gambles constantly, is arrogant, rude, and has no sense of when to shut up!

And who the hell is the naive, airheaded girl?! Your sister’s the naive one! Your whole family’s naive!

Alice raged against the absurd rumors, but it did absolutely nothing.

The rumors weren’t even the worst part. What truly disgusted her were the bards who, for the sake of popularity, started fabricating outrageous stories.

One of them claimed that Merlin and Alice had known each other since childhood, always in love, but as they grew up, they became the Demon Lord and the Hero, leading to a dramatic tale of love and betrayal. The climax? On the eve of the great battle, lonely and restless, Merlin and Alice had a wild, passionate encounter on the battlefield, elevating the theme of love and conflict.

What the actual fuck?!

“Goddamn *wild, passionate encounter*?!”

Would they make up any story for popularity?! This was the kind of trashy, third-rate romance nonsense meant to scam tears from little girls and feed their delusions of being kept by a domineering CEO!

Alice harbored deep resentment toward the bard who wrote that story. She felt like running him through with her sword.

Because that tale had spread the widest, and in it, she was portrayed as an absolute idiot—smiling like a fool after being tricked into bed by the domineering CEO Merlin. It was sickening!

Merlin had also heard of this Demon Lord-Hero romance drama, but his only comment was—

That domineering CEO isn’t me. Facing a washboard, I wouldn’t even want my dick to lift its head.

Alice despised her past Hero title because her purity had been slandered. In the eyes of the world, the 233rd Hero had been defiled by Lucifer III, making her a filthy person.

If Alice didn’t go to great lengths to hide her past, she might never find a husband in this lifetime.

But today, to free these stupid villagers from their brainwashing, Alice decided to acknowledge her past and shock them back to reality in the most straightforward way possible.

“Big… Big Sister… are you the Hero?” Little Henry’s eyes widened in shock. He had always thought Heroes were one-in-a-million prodigies. Little did he know Alice had just been a temporary hire.

“So… you’re the 233rd Hero? The one who brought shame to the Holy Church? The one who failed to subdue the First Demon Lord Palace and even had an affair with Lucifer III? *Daddy!*” The priest pointed at Alice, his expression filled with shock.

“I’m not here to talk about my past. I’m here to make you stop deceiving people with prayers.” Alice didn’t want to explain her history with Merlin—it was impossible to clarify, and the more she tried, the worse it would sound.

“As a former former Hero, how dare you say prayers are useless! Are you trying to become a heretic? *Daddy!*” The priest trembled with rage. Alice was interfering with his income, and as a Hero, her words carried more weight than his.

“If His Holiness the Pope in the Vatican knew you were leading people to abandon their duty to help others, I’m sure he’d be deeply disappointed in you.” Alice knew the Holy Church well—it was a mixed bag. Some clergy, like this priest, were corrupt, while others were truly devout. She couldn’t generalize.

“Y-You… what nonsense are you spouting? *Daddy!*” The priest’s conscience twinged. He still held some reverence for the Pope.

Alice had reached her limit. The priest’s mouth was spewing filth, and it made her sick. *Slap!* She stretched out her hand and delivered a sharp slap across his face.

The villagers watching below gasped in shock. The Hero had struck a priest—what a staggering sight.

“Y-You… you dare hit me?”

The priest collapsed into the filthy muddy water, raindrops pattering down on him.

“*…*”

Alice suddenly drew her slender sword and pressed it against the priest’s neck. Her gaze was icy and intimidating, curing him of his lifelong habit of adding that extra word.

“Please don’t add strange words at the end. I have a bit of OCD.”

The priest’s eyes widened in terror. Kneeling on the ground, he trembled violently, the cold edge of the sword against his neck sending a chill through his bones. He no longer dared to speak carelessly.

“Since you believe prayers are effective, then start praying now that I won’t kill you. Are you brave enough to bet your life on the power of prayer?” Alice looked down at the priest on the ground, her voice calm. “If you’re truly devout, the Goddess of Light will stop me. If you’re not, then dying by the Hero’s sword shouldn’t matter, right?”

This was a war between reason and faith. Whether these fools could break free from their brainwashing depended on who remained standing at the end.

The dark, oppressive clouds hung low, endlessly pouring rain.

Drops struck the ground, splashing in all directions.

Alice held her sword to the priest’s neck, not blinking even once.

Rainwater gathered into streams, sliding down the blade and onto the priest’s neck.

The scene was eerily silent as everyone waited for the outcome.

The priest’s eyes were wide with fear, his entire body shaking. His wavering faith had lost to his terror of death.

“S-Sorry!”

He stumbled to his feet and fled, leaving behind several deluxe scriptures.

Alice sheathed her sword and turned to face the villagers. In the drizzling rain, she shouted—

“I know you’re afraid of death. Even when your own family is kidnapped, you don’t dare to act, instead placing your hopes in useless prayers for spiritual comfort.”

“But that’s just escapism. It’s the choice of a coward. The gods won’t help fools!”

“At a time like this, you can only rely on yourselves. Isn’t it pathetic to beg for help from something intangible?”

“Many things aren’t impossible just because they seem hard. You shouldn’t give up so easily.”

“Right now, those kidnapped people are hoping you’ll come to their rescue. And only you can do it!”

“You have two choices before you…”

“Die in silence, consumed by guilt.”

“Or put down your farming tools, pick up a sword, and fight back!”

title: Chapter 71
content:
Chapter 71

Volume 2 · Chapter 71

Little Henry stood in the rain, eyes wide, feeling that Alice’s righteous, powerful, and beautiful figure was as awe-inspiring as the legendary swordmaster Elgin. It filled him with such fervor that he suspected the other villagers felt the same.

"Village Chief..."

Alice turned to face the village chief, her goal still being to gather information.

"What are your orders, Lady Alice?" the village chief snapped back to attention, his respect for her so deep that he instinctively lowered his posture.

"Can you tell me the exact location of the goblin nest in the back mountains?"

"You wish to..." the village chief hesitated.

"Do I even need to ask? Of course I’m going to save them. If we wait past tonight, it’ll be too dangerous." Alice replied earnestly. If she had known the nest’s exact location, she would have already charged in alone.

"But it’s extremely dangerous. There’s a Goblin Emperor in the nest, and it seems to have already reached Saint-tier. Even Lady Alice might..." The village chief trailed off.

Saint-tier?

I definitely can’t win against that.

The gap between power levels is hard to overcome.

But—

If not me, who else can help them?

Merlin? Yeah, he could handle a Saint-tier easily.

But am I supposed to grovel and beg a demon for help?

I’d rather die in the goblin nest...

Alice lifted her head. Though a flicker of fear toward the Saint-tier threat lingered, and she knew the odds were against her, her gaze remained unshaken.

If it’s something only I can do, then I’ll take on that responsibility—

"It’s fine. Please tell me the exact location."

◆

Tavern.

Merlin stood at the door, watching the rain fall like a curtain outside.

Inside, two female patrons sat pale-faced, still shaken, sipping their drinks.

Merlin didn’t know what had happened, but worried there might be danger outside, so he hadn’t let them leave. He couldn’t split himself in two—he couldn’t protect everyone—but at least those right under his nose were safe.

He guessed it was probably a goblin attack on the village. A faint sense of embarrassment crept in. Had he caused this somehow? Even if he had, he’d never admit it.

Now, the rain was light, the earlier flames had died down, and the night was eerily silent. It was hard to tell what was going on.

Merlin couldn’t see through the current situation, but if it was this quiet, it must be safe now, right?

He did want to go out and check, but he had promised Martha he’d watch the tavern, so he couldn’t really leave.

And why hadn’t Martha returned yet after going to find Henry? Had something happened to her?

Merlin stared at the rain, a bad feeling gnawing at him, but he decided to wait a little longer.

He couldn’t have the tavern burn to the ground the moment he stepped out to investigate—that would be a disaster.

A figure sprinted through the rain. Little Henry was drenched, his face twisted with urgency, looking utterly disheveled.

"Henry?!" Merlin called out.

Little Henry dashed into the tavern, not saying a word, and bolted straight upstairs. The two women jumped in surprise.

"Hey! Henry!" Merlin shouted again, his eyebrows knitting together.

What was going on?

Why wasn’t Henry talking?

That bratty kid looked desperate. What had happened outside?

And where was Martha? She’d gone to find Henry—why hadn’t they come back together?

Merlin’s head filled with questions. Not knowing what else to do, he decided to go upstairs and ask properly.

But before long, Little Henry came rushing back down, clutching an adult-sized straight sword, looking like he was about to dash out.

This sword belonged to Henry’s father and had always been kept at home.

Though Martha usually didn’t let her son touch it, that little troublemaker Henry had still found out where it was stored.

Henry was going to take his father’s sword and join the villagers in heading up the mountain to rescue people. Small as he was, his spirit was commendable.

"Hey, hey, hey, Henry! What do you think you’re doing with that sword?" Merlin grabbed Little Henry by the collar, lifting him up so his feet dangled in the air, swinging awkwardly.

"Let go of me! Put me down!" Little Henry struggled with all his might, but as a child, how could he overpower Merlin? All he could do was shout wildly.

"What are you doing out so late? Don’t you know it’s dangerous outside at night?" Merlin held Little Henry aloft, scolding him like an elder.

"I don’t need Uncle Merlin to look after me! Let go! I’m busy!" Little Henry was frantic—if he didn’t leave now, the main group of villagers would depart without him.

"Busy with what? You’re just causing trouble for your mother. Where is she? She went out to find you, so why hasn’t she come back? Didn’t you two meet?" Merlin frowned, feeling Henry was being far too disobedient.

Little Henry gritted his teeth in agony. "The goblins attacked the village just now... my mom... she was taken by the goblins!"

title: Chapter 72 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 72 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 72

The moment Merlin mentioned Martha, his tear ducts failed him. Tears welled up in his eyes, overflowing down his cheeks and dripping onto the floor.

Little Henry was wracked with guilt and remorse over his mother being taken away. Though he was just a small child, he had already cast aside all fear of death, ready to fight the vicious goblins to save his mother.

Recalling his own helplessness, watching as his mother was dragged away by the goblins, Henry hated himself for it. No matter what, he had to make up for his mistake.

"Ah?! Really?" Merlin froze, not expecting his guess to be almost right. But his boss lady being kidnapped was the worst possible scenario.

"Uncle Merlin, let go!" Seizing the moment when Merlin was distracted, Henry wrenched free and bolted for the door without looking back.

"Henry! Where do you think you're going?!" Merlin was genuinely annoyed, but if he ignored the boy, it left a bad taste in his mouth.

"I'm going to use my father's sword to save Mom!" Henry stopped, turning back with tears in his eyes and shouting.

"You need to stop this nonsense! You don't know anything—you'll just make things worse. Staying here is the safest thing for you." Merlin furrowed his brows, speaking impatiently.

"I don't want to! I refuse to just sit here and wait for death!" Henry roared in fury.

"What can someone as weak as you possibly do?" Merlin exuded a hint of authority, clearly angry now. He disliked people who, knowing they were weak, still recklessly rushed to their deaths. Such blind fools were truly infuriating.

"I know I'm useless, but so what? Am I just supposed to stand by and watch my mother die? Putting hope in others is worse than trying myself! Mom is the one I've always protected! So I have to go!" With that, Henry dashed outside, disappearing into the rain-soaked night. "I'm not like you, Uncle Merlin, who just eats and waits to die..."

Wait, wait, wait!

I'm one of the Seven Kings of the demon race!

No one has ever dared speak to me like this!

What's with that tone of contempt and disdain?!

Merlin knitted his brows, staring into the rain as he fell deep into thought—

*"With Dad not at home, I'm the only man in the house, so it's my job to protect Mom!"*

He recalled the words Henry had said to him on their way home together—the small yet resilient figure limping home in the fading sunset.

Even though Henry was just a child, he had the resolve to take on responsibility.

Yeah, everyone has something they're willing to stake their life to protect. Fighting to defend it is admirable.

Henry was weak—so weak he could barely lift a sword. But the way he risked his life to protect his mother was undeniably cool, commanding respect.

Even I, a king, have to take a human brat seriously.

Damn it, what's this burning feeling in my chest?

"Honestly, this hot-blooded idiot just causes trouble for everyone..."

Merlin gently massaged his forehead and sighed in exasperation—

Henry, consider yourself lucky.

I, the proud monarch of the demon race,

am willing to draw my sword for a human for the first time!

Even though I'm heartless, cold-blooded, and terminally lazy.

But I can't bear to see a child's precious thing be trampled...

Merlin felt he owed Martha a great deal for all her care. It was only right to help in a time like this.

The demon race was an absolutely fair species—if you received a favor, you had to repay it. This wasn't about morality; it was a law of survival!

Merlin absolutely refused to admit he was influenced by little Henry. Even after reincarnating as a demon for over two hundred years, a trace of human values still lingered in his heart.

Merlin turned, downing the vodka on the table in one gulp, let out a burp, grabbed his coat, and headed out.

"Mr. Merlin, where are you going?"

"It's so dangerous out there, stay here with us."

The two female patrons, seeing Merlin about to leave, were startled.

"Ladies, stay here for now. It'll be much safer to leave at dawn."

"Why are you leaving so suddenly? Can't you stay with us a little longer?" one of the girls asked, looking pitiful.

"Because... I suddenly feel like being a hero for once might not be so bad..."

Merlin smiled kindly, not lingering any longer. He turned and left, stepping into the rain-drenched night.

He draped the black coat over his shoulders, parting the heavy downpour.

Merlin looked up at the oppressive dark clouds, his face expressionless. Large raindrops pounded his handsome, refined features as he silently tightened his grip on the katana at his waist—

A hero?

That really doesn't suit me...

title: Chapter 73
content:
Chapter 73

Volume 2 · Chapter 73

Alice moved swiftly through the rain, her path carving through the downpour as if nothing could obstruct her steps.

To save time, she recklessly burned through her fighting spirit. From afar, the silver-haired girl looked like a streak of starlight tearing through the night.

Alice knew she was venturing alone into grave danger, but she had no other choice. The ordinary villagers were too weak to be of much help—they could only hold off common goblins at best.

Even though she was aware she might encounter Saint-tier enemies, she still chose to go save them.

She knew she was being a fool, an incurable idiot.

But how could she turn away when those desperate people looked at her with hopeful eyes?

Of course she had to help them. She couldn’t just stand by and watch someone die.

If she didn’t try to answer their expectations, she’d be haunted by guilt. Living with that regret would be worse than death.

I’ve always believed justice is simple—

To be the hope in everyone’s eyes and to answer each small expectation, that is justice.

So even if it’s dangerous, I have to go.

Because I’m the only one who can save them!

If I’ve become the hope in others’ eyes, then I must bear the responsibility that comes with it. That’s all there is to it!

Alice thought firmly to herself as she dashed through the rainy night. When she reached the village gate, she suddenly stopped, as if she had noticed something.

In the center of the continent, there was a charred, blackened figure—what looked like a burned corpse.

What caught Alice’s attention wasn’t the body itself, but the small silver tag around its neck: an Adventurer’s Proof!

Curious, Alice walked over. The person seemed dead, so she snapped the chain of the Adventurer’s Proof and examined it closely—

Region: Banbridge.
Name: Hobson Smith.
Class: Swordsman.

The small tag of the Hero’s Proof had already revealed almost everything about the deceased.

“An adventurer from Ireland? To come all the way to Wales for a mission…”

Alice sighed, looking at the corpse with a pang of sorrow. She silently clenched the Adventurer’s Proof in her hand.

After all, he was a fellow adventurer. Dying like this, so far from home, was tragic.

Adventurers were a profession of both romance and tragedy—free and unbound, yet always in danger.

Alice decided to take Smith’s Adventurer’s Proof to Rexham, then send it to Denmark.

The Adventurers Guild had branches all over the world, but its headquarters were in Copenhagen, Denmark. There was a special cemetery there dedicated to the souls of adventurers. In truth, it contained nothing but a towering tree.

It was nearly impossible to bring back the bodies of fallen adventurers. Without any memorials or tombstones, the only thing left to remember them by was their Adventurer’s Proof, forever engraved with their names.

When an adventurer died, their comrades would bring the tag back and hang it on the great tree in the cemetery, where it would be bathed in the morning sun every day.

Alice disliked doing this kind of thing, because every time an Adventurer’s Proof left its owner, it meant something heavy had happened.

She slowly stood up. Though she felt a pang of sadness, there were more important things to do. Now was not the time for grief.

Alice turned to leave, but suddenly felt someone grab her heel.

She looked back—was the corpse moving? A hand was tightly gripping her shoe.

A cold sweat broke out on Alice. She thought it might be some undead magic, but then realized—could Smith still be alive?

“Are you okay?”

“Hey! Wake up!”

“Hold on! Someone will come save you!”

Alice kept calling out to Smith. She couldn’t let him lose consciousness, or he would surely die.

Smith’s entire body was burned, looking like a rotting corpse, constantly washed by the rain. His condition was critical. Without Alice’s calls, his consciousness might have already scattered.

With great effort, he slightly opened his eyes and saw a golden chain swaying back and forth—Alice’s Adventurer’s Proof—

Region: Rexham.
Name: Alice·Claudia.
Class: Demon Swordswoman.

“G-Gold… Gold Adventurer…”

Smith’s eyes widened in shock and terror, as if a spark of hope for survival had ignited within him.

A Gold Adventurer meant the silver-haired girl before him was incredibly powerful. Maybe his fiancée could still be saved!

More than his own life, Smith was worried about his fiancée.

Dragging his broken body, Smith grabbed Alice’s wrist, tears streaming down his face.

“A-Alice… Lady Alice, please, help me… I beg you…”

“Eh?!” Alice was startled. She still had more important things to do, but she decided to hear him out for now. “Tell me what’s wrong. If I can do it, I’ll try my best.”

“Thank you, Lady Alice. A few days ago, our three-man party entered the mountains behind us…”

Smith recounted everything that had happened over the past few days, including what had befallen his fiancée. Alice also learned the exact location of the goblin nest and where the hostages were being held.

This information was crucial. Alice could now rescue people more efficiently instead of stumbling around blindly in the goblin nest.

Alice deduced that the villagers and the mage were being kept together—likely as slaves to be offered to the Goblin Emperor.

“So, Lady Alice, I beg you, please save my fiancée! I know my request is shameless, but I have no other choice… so… so please, show me a little mercy…”

Smith knelt on the ground, burying his face in the dirty mud as if punishing himself. His helplessness and weakness were on full display.

“Lift your head. As an adventurer, you must maintain your dignity. I’ve heard your request. Rest assured, I will save your fiancée.” Alice couldn’t refuse. She seriously promised. After all, rescuing the villagers and Smith’s fiancée could be done at the same time.

“Thank you, Lady Alice… I… I don’t even know how to repay your kindness…” Smith’s eyes welled up with tears, and he sobbed uncontrollably in the rain.

“It’s simple…”

Alice patted Smith’s shoulder, and a layer of ice instantly formed over his body.

This wasn’t meant to harm him—it would ease the pain of his burns and help him hold on.

“Lady Alice…?” Smith looked confused.

“The best way to repay me is to survive. Don’t give up. Don’t you still have to go back home and marry your fiancée?” Alice smiled earnestly. “So you must live. Otherwise, all your efforts will have been in vain. Hold on a little longer. The villagers will come save you.”

For the first time in his life, Smith felt true admiration for someone. Alice’s smile seemed to dispel the darkness and the cold, and her long silver hair was more beautiful than the Milky Way in summer.

“What’s your fiancée’s name?” Alice asked.

“Aphra… Aphra Cecil…” Smith replied.

“Then…” Alice held up Smith’s Silver Adventurer’s Proof, the chain swaying and gleaming with silver light. She spoke with unwavering resolve—

“Your Adventurer’s Proof will be returned to you by Cecil’s own hands.”

title: Chapter 74
content:
Chapter 74

Volume 2 · Chapter 74

Alice left after speaking, heading into the drizzle.

“Alice-sama, the Goblin Emperor is a Saint-tier powerhouse, the gap in strength is huge, please be careful! Please come back safe and sound…”

Smith’s voice came from behind, but Alice did not turn back, disappearing from his sight.

I know the gap in strength is huge.

So what then? Would I stand by and watch people die?

What a joke, everyone is looking to me, how could I coldly stand by.

In the Death Swamp, that bastard once said a sentence to me —

「Ordinary people should stay grounded and know themselves.」

No matter how you look at it, I will never agree with that sentence.

No one is willing to be mediocre, so one needs constant challenge and struggle.

Just like now, I know I am very likely to be defeated by a Saint-tier powerhouse.

But if I retreat, wouldn’t that prove that bastard right?

So I cannot give up, I must —

Ignite a spark of hope in despair!

◆

Underground Goblin Palace.

The Goblin Emperor examined the captured female villagers, thinking they were quite good.

“Take them to the prison behind, I’ll enjoy them one by one after I finish washing up tonight.”

Servants dragged them away with iron chains, Martha was among them, but she did not dare resist much, looking somewhat disheveled at the moment, her mind full of her son Henry.

Gegéwu stood respectfully below as a meritorious subject.

The Goblin Emperor showed a smile and said in a muffled voice.

“Gegéwu, you did well this time, what reward do you want?”

“Your Majesty, I need no reward, being able to serve the king is my honor.” Gegéwu spoke very pleasingly.

“Indeed worthy of being the prime minister, the person I trust most.” The Goblin Emperor’s big nose twitched several times, obviously very happy.

“Thank you for Your Majesty’s trust.” Gegéwu lowered his posture very low.

“Since there is nothing else, you may withdraw, I’ll wash up and prepare to enjoy the new prey.” The Goblin Emperor waved his hand, the gem ring on his hand shining incredibly.

“Yes.”

After Gegéwu withdrew, he did not rush to sleep.

Instead he ordered the soldiers to stay up all night guarding the entrance to the underground palace.

He himself also watched at the entrance, several subordinates beside him asked in confusion, “Lord Gegéwu, why add more men at the entrance today?”

“Humans are emotional animals, we kidnapped so many of them, as I expected, tonight many villagers will come to rescue them, so we have added men to ambush and wait for them to walk into the trap.” Gegéwu said with confidence, as if he had foreseen everything.

“High~ really high ah! Truly worthy of the omniscient Lord Gegéwu~” A subordinate gave a thumbs up, a string of flattery sent up.

Gegéwu laughed very happily, as the emperor’s favorite, after unifying Wales, second only to one person, above ten thousand people, so cool~

Suddenly the guards outside began to stir, as if they had discovered something?

Gegéwu walked over in confusion and asked, “What’s going on? Is there a situation?”

“Lord, it seems something is coming over?” The goblin guard pointed in a direction.

Gegéwu looked in that direction, because the night plus the rain curtain made it hard to see clearly, a white figure was rapidly approaching —

“That is…”

“A monster from the forest?”

“No!”

“It’s that silver-haired ice magic swordsman!”

When Gegéwu shouted out in surprise, Alice had already killed to the front, fully activating high-level battle aura, her speed very impressive.

Alice suddenly drew her rapier, silver light suddenly burst out, attacks came like a rainstorm, mixed with high-level battle aura, the power was unstoppable.

The pure silver 「Light Song」 shone with clear moonlight, every attack was like chopping melons and vegetables!

The goblin guards outside hadn’t recovered their senses before they died under Alice’s fierce sword rain.

Blood light and sword flashes interwove, sounding the horn of resistance.

“You damn little bitch…”

“Get lost!”

Alice roared angrily, before Gegéwu could finish speaking, she stomped on his face with a high-heeled boot.

Gegéwu flew backwards, his head hitting the rock wall and passing out.

Sure enough, a pure mage has very weak resistance when facing close combat.

“Lord Gegéwu!” The subordinates screamed in terror.

Alice did not stop, but bravely moved forward, continuing to fight alone, advancing deep underground alone.

Her steps leapt, moving forward in the dark corridor, her speed never slowing.

She slaughtered all who blocked her way, her fierce sword skills forcibly carving a bloody path in the narrow darkness!

Her silver hair shining like stars danced in the darkness, her face bearing no expression.

Wisps of cold air surged and erupted, ice thorns strangled groups of goblins, sending any goblin daring to block her steps to hell.

The dual use of magic and battle aura had reached a level that made people marvel.

Such high-difficulty skills from two major systems, yet in Alice’s hands, they changed flexibly.

Alice killed to the lowest part of the underground palace, seeing that black and majestic palace.

She was slightly distracted then regained composure, her gaze becoming solemn.

Alice was killing down madly in order to save time.

After learning the layout of the goblin nest from Smith’s mouth, she decided to cut the Gordian knot quickly, to rescue people with the fastest speed.

So she only killed those who dared to block her, arriving here in the shortest time.

If lucky, she would not have to fight the Saint-tier Goblin Emperor, and could rescue people, that would be the most ideal result.

In front of the palace gate two giant goblins patrolled holding huge mallets, after discovering an intruder, they rushed over aggressively with their weapons.

“Tsk!”

The ground rumbled, Alice met them head-on, the two enemies raised their mallets and smashed down at her at the same time.

Alice’s figure suddenly accelerated, dodging the attack, letting the enemies’ attack miss and smash into the ground, making a “boom” sound, rubble flying.

Alice passed behind the two giant goblins, swung her rapier, cutting their Achilles tendons, leaving the enemies kneeling on the ground unable to move.

Alice did not hesitate, turned —

And rushed into the crisis-filled Goblin Palace…

title: Chapter 75
content:
Chapter 75

Volume 2 · Chapter 75

Late at night.

The villagers had formed a militia, determined to march up the mountain and take back their kidnapped kin.

Those with swords took swords; those without took farming tools—hoes, shovels, pitchforks—anything that could kill a goblin. They charged forward together!

Little Henry was among them, struggling to hold his father’s longsword, which was nearly as tall as he was. Though Henry was painfully weak, his expression was resolute. Gripping the iron sword, he almost looked like… a dwarf warrior?

Little Henry knew he was in danger, but his guilt over his mother overpowered everything. He had to try. He had to live up to his duty as the only man left in his family.

The narrow mountain path twisted and turned, and the darkness made it treacherous. The storm above showed no sign of stopping, and the rain poured through the dense foliage, drumming against the makeshift militia.

The villagers carried torches, illuminating their surroundings as they pressed deeper into the mountain.

Little Henry was terrified. The heavy raindrops pounded his helmet with a clatter, making him restless and uneasy.

Along the way, the militia had already fended off several small-scale ambushes, all of them crushed by the villagers.

Little Henry had even plunged his father’s sword into a goblin’s chest. Watching the dead goblin’s tongue loll out, blood splattering his childish face, the boy was horrified, his mind unsettled for a long time.

There had been moments when death was a hair’s breadth away—crossbow bolts whizzing past his ear, a hammer striking his helmet—but he hadn’t retreated. Instead, he had fought back with renewed fury.

Little Henry realized his mother had been right: goblins were vicious. If he relied on the adults around him, he wouldn’t survive.

Though goblins were small, their strength was nearly equal to that of a grown man. For a child like Henry, they were more than a match.

So Little Henry had to fight dirty. He swung his sword at their legs, doing what he could to assist the adults.

The rain seemed to grow heavier, and Little Henry grew more impatient, worried for his mother. He saw this as his redemption.

The villagers, fully armed, were not much weaker than the goblins in combat. Moreover, the enemy’s attacks so far had been small-scale ambushes, all repelled by the militia.

In truth, the main goblin forces had been decimated by Alice, and her surprise attack had thrown the enemy into chaos, leaving them no time to deal with the villagers advancing up the mountain.

The deep, dark forest on the mountain had no light of its own. The torchlight became the only hope for many.

*Squeak squeak squeak!*

Ahead, the unmistakable cries of goblins rang out, and countless crimson eyes lit up in the dark.

Another ambush. The goblins charged, brandishing curved blades, clashing with the militia.

The clang of steel filled the air as the two sides fought fiercely.

Little Henry’s eyes widened. After a few deep breaths, he mustered his courage and roared as he charged forward—

“AAAAAAAAAAH—”

◆

At the entrance of the nest.

Gegawu, who had been knocked unconscious by Alice’s kick, was still out cold.

His subordinates frantically called out to him. The militia from the village was getting closer, and they needed Gegawu to take command.

“Lord Gegawu! Lord Gegawu, wake up!”

Gegawu seemed to regain consciousness, slowly stirring back to his senses, though his mind was still foggy.

“Lord Gegawu, you’re finally awake! The villagers are attacking!”

“What?!”

Gegawu was shocked. He shook his head violently to clear his mind.

He stepped outside and saw the long line of torches snaking through the darkness—unmistakable proof that the militia had reached the cave entrance.

Thanks to Alice’s surprise attack, their prepared forces were in disarray, with heavy casualties. It was clear they couldn’t hold back so many villagers.

“Lord Gegawu, what do we do now?” a subordinate asked in panic.

“Panic? Don’t forget—I am a high-tier mage! As long as my mana holds, ordinary villagers pose no threat!” Gegawu declared with absolute confidence.

“As expected of Lord Gegawu! Brilliant! Truly brilliant!” the subordinate fawned.

“Hmph! How dare these lowly humans think they can fight us, the noble goblins?”

Gegawu scoffed, closed his eyes, and began chanting. High-tier magic surged to life.

In front of the cave entrance, a long, narrow wall of fire erupted instantly, blocking the militia’s path.

The flames roared, taller than the trees, their scorching heat evaporating the raindrops, sending thick plumes of steam into the air. It was an imposing sight.

“Pathetic humans! Now do you see the difference in power?”

◆

The militia was stunned by the sudden wall of fire.

The searing heat washed over them, forcing them to retreat.

The villagers were panicked. They couldn’t hope to overpower a high-tier mage!

Many began to murmur. The goblin ambushes had already taken their toll, and now this impassable wall of fire made them consider turning back.

“We should charge through!” Little Henry shouted.

“That’s a high-tier fire wall! Touch it and you’ll be reduced to ash. Don’t be reckless!” Strongson quickly grabbed Little Henry, who was itching to throw his life away. Though Strongson was only a low-tier warrior, he was one of the stronger villagers.

“Then what do we do?!” Little Henry demanded urgently.

Sighing, the village chief stood at the front, staring at the blazing wall. He shook his head. “It seems we have no choice but to wait for the flames to die down. There’s nothing else we can do. If only I could use magic like my grandfather…”

“So we just stand here and do nothing? What about the people taken inside?!” Little Henry was confused. This felt like giving up entirely.

“There’s nothing we can do…” The village chief had no answer for the fire wall either.

Little Henry gritted his teeth, his face pale. He wasn’t convinced.

Then he remembered his mother telling him the story of the old village chief and the goblins. The old chief had taken a small, hidden path, climbing dangerously into the nest, and caught the goblins off guard.

But that path was said to be extremely dangerous. The villagers would never let him go alone.

After much hesitation, Little Henry quietly slipped away, disappearing from the villagers’ sight.

Not long after, Merlin arrived on the mountain and saw the group of villagers blocked by the fire wall.

Merlin looked around but didn’t see Little Henry. A flicker of worry crossed his mind.

He walked up to Strongson, shamelessly striking up a conversation. “Hey, friend. Seen Little Henry?”

Strongson instinctively glanced around, then gasped in shock. “Huh?! He was just here! How’d he vanish so fast? What the—?!”

Merlin’s heart sank. Knowing Little Henry’s personality, he wouldn’t be content to wait. He must be trying something else.

Strongson turned to see who had spoken to him—and nearly jumped out of his skin when he saw Merlin’s face.

“Y-Y-Y-You—?!”

“Hahaha…” Merlin chuckled, patting Strongson’s shoulder. “Thanks for covering my meal bill earlier…”

Strongson’s face went sheet-white. The memory of being punched and left dangling from the ceiling flashed through his mind. Merlin was at least a mid-tier powerhouse.

Merlin didn’t waste words. He strode straight toward the fire wall.

“Y-You… what are you doing?!” Strongson snapped back to his senses. If Merlin had come up the mountain with them, he must be a comrade. He couldn’t just stand by and watch him march to his death.

Merlin walked forward with nonchalant grace, not even glancing back as he replied coolly—

“What else?”

“Rescuing my boss, of course.”

“Otherwise, how am I supposed to get my half-month’s pay?”

title: Chapter 76
content:
Chapter 76

Volume 2 · Chapter 76

Everyone stared in shock at Merlin’s retreating back, convinced he had lost his mind to go courting death like this.

The wall of fire before them burned at an intense temperature—enough to reduce him to ashes.

Merlin, though he wore a long sword at his waist like some master swordsman, looked utterly ordinary, with no trace of magic or fighting spirit about him.

Only Strongson thought Merlin might be a mid-tier expert, but trying to cross a high-tier magical fire wall like this was still suicide, wasn’t it?

Undaunted by the rain, Merlin strode forward, parting the swirling mist, and approached the infernal wall of flames.

“Don’t go! That fire wall is deadly! You’ll be burned alive!” the village chief cried out, never expecting some reckless young fool to throw his life away. To him, Merlin was just a pretty-boy con artist who swindled women out of money—not some powerful figure.

“It’s fine. This heat is nothing compared to the lava in the demon race’s underground…” Merlin replied offhandedly. A mere fire wall spell wasn’t worth his concern.

“Even if you’re a mid-tier warrior, you won’t be any help in there! There are Saint-tier powerhouses inside!” Strongson shouted, thinking Merlin couldn’t possibly be as strong as Alice. What could a mere mid-tier swordsman accomplish?

“Oh? Saint-tier, you say? That makes it even better. Now I’m a little interested~” Merlin still didn’t turn back, already nearing the fire wall.

“Just leave it to that silver-haired demon swordswoman! You’re not as strong as Lady Alice—going in would only cause trouble! Stay here and wait!” the villagers urged anxiously.

“Heh, who’s causing trouble isn’t set in stone yet.” Merlin waved a hand at the villagers without looking back. “You all just wait here. Don’t do anything unnecessary.”

Alice? She was nothing.

Just a defeated foe.

Apart from being a little cute when she blushed, she was utterly unremarkable.

And yet, knowing the enemy was Saint-tier, she still went to save people. How reckless.

Did she not understand the vast gap between tiers? She’d just get toyed with.

Was it because of that vague, intangible sense of justice in her heart?

Sure, she had a foul temper and a flat chest, but that resolve to face death head-on… deserved a tiny bit of respect from him.

Just a tiny bit. Because this kind of meddlesome little justice warrior was kind of annoying.

Merlin stepped into the roaring wall of fire, as if walking to his doom.

“You—what the—ah?!”

The village chief was furious, his beard bristling with rage.

Then, the impossible happened—leaving him horrified.

The fire wall before Merlin suddenly split in two, parting a path as if the flames themselves were avoiding him. It was beyond belief.

His “Magic Immunity” constitution was undeniable—though he couldn’t stop magic, he was completely unharmed by it.

Merlin gazed at the scorching flames surging apart like a tide.

He gave a faint smile and walked through. The fire wall sealed shut behind him, as if nothing had ever happened.

At this moment, Merlin was no longer that lazy, good-for-nothing pretty boy. The moment he took things even slightly seriously, that magnificent figure was proof of overwhelming power!

That aura of standing at the pinnacle could not be concealed. Even the lowly villagers caught fleeting glimpses of his greatness.

The unrivaled sovereign of the demon race, the legendary swordsman of Elgin, the strongest force in the world…

Countless glorious titles spoke of his legendary past.

Now, tearing away the disguise of a lazy, parasitic existence, it sent a shiver through the soul.

The villagers were stunned. Some even dropped their weapons, too shocked to react. How could an ordinary man split a magnificent high-tier fire wall in two? It was earth-shattering.

Strongson’s face turned pale with shock. He had thought Merlin was mid-tier—how was he crossing the great fire wall unscathed?! Could he actually be a high-tier powerhouse?

The village chief was more worldly. Half a year ago, he had visited Elgin City and had been there the night of the pirate raid. He had personally witnessed the birth of a legendary swordsman.

That night, the city was ablaze from pirate destruction, the sky choked with dark clouds. Towering above the pirate ships, that incomparably powerful swordsman had slain two Saint-tier pirate kings in a single strike, saving Elgin City.

In the dim light and rising black smoke, all anyone could make out was his wild, long hair and that transcendent, mighty figure.

The village chief racked his memory and found that Merlin bore an uncanny resemblance to Elgin’s legendary great swordsman. Their backs were practically identical.

“H-he… could he be… Elgin’s legendary swordsman?”

The villagers were all stunned, though none had seen him before. They whispered among themselves.

“N-no… that can’t be! Why would that peerless powerhouse be in our tiny village? And working as a lowly gigolo in a tavern, living off women’s perfume money? That’s nothing like the legendary figure!” Strongson broke out in a cold sweat. Just hearing the name of Elgin’s legendary swordsman filled him with reverence.

Merlin’s usual demeanor was nothing like that man’s—let alone the gap in power.

Elgin’s legendary swordsman had killed two Saint-tier foes in one strike, a godlike feat. Merlin? At best, he was *maybe* near high-tier. How could they be the same person?

“Merlin is just Merlin. Sure, he’s got a bit of skill, but he’s only a little stronger than me—a good-for-nothing, uneducated fraud who cons women in taverns, that’s all. Hahaha…” Strongson scratched his bald head and forced a dry laugh, refusing to believe Merlin was that legendary figure.

“Y-yeah… I guess I just thought he looked a bit like that great swordsman. Must’ve been my mistake, hahaha…”

The village chief wiped his cold sweat and joined in with a nervous chuckle, thinking—

Illusion!

All just an illusion!

That legendary swordsman, revered by all, with power that shook the entire Great Britain Empire…

And Merlin, despised by villagers, weak, surviving by sweet-talking women out of their money…

How the hell could they be the same person?!

What kind of joke was this?!

(??ω?? ?)

◆

Merlin easily passed through the fiercely burning fire wall, waving a hand to clear the mist obscuring his vision.

He saw a purple-skinned goblin giving orders to some green-skinned goblins.

He didn’t know the situation, but they were clearly enemies.

Merlin stepped into the rain. Too proud to ambush, he approached like a guest and greeted them—

“Green-skins, good evening~?”
