title: Chapter 77
content:
Chapter 77

Volume 2 · Chapter 77

A few minutes earlier.

Gegwu admired the Fire Wall spell he had cast, boasting with satisfaction—

"Those trash outside could never cross my Fire Wall. With me here, there's no need to bother His Majesty; I can fully protect our nest on my own."

"As expected of Lord Gegwu, you are truly a reliable powerhouse—both mighty and wise, the embodiment of strength and beauty, the very heartthrob of our Goblin race!" A subordinate showered him with flattery, clapping loudly.

"Hahaha, that’s right~" Gegwu shook his head, thumping his chest. "I am a high-ranking mage! None of those weaklings outside are my match—let alone crossing my signature Fire Wall! If someone could pass through unscathed, I’d resign from being Prime Minister and humbly take up toilet cleaning instead~"

"Yes, yes! Lord Gegwu is truly our great savior!"

The subordinates took turns heaping praise on him, and Gegwu basked in the adulation.

"Alright, after blocking the villagers, there’s something more important to handle." Gegwu’s expression turned serious. "Hurry down and order the royal guards to capture that demon swordswoman who snuck in. Try not to disturb His Majesty, then bring her to me~"

"Lord Gegwu, do you mean…?" The subordinate asked curiously, sensing something.

"That silver-haired lass is quite the looker, fiery temper and all—right up my alley. Hehehe, you catch my drift?" Gegwu spoke euphemistically. Though he had only glimpsed Alice, it had instantly ignited his desire to conquer her. Unlike the village girls he had captured before, he wanted to break her completely.

"I get it, I get it~" The subordinate nodded repeatedly, then asked in surprise, "But shouldn’t such a fine catch be offered to His Majesty?"

"What do you mean? As the Goblin race’s heartthrob, am I inferior to His Majesty?" Gegwu’s face darkened, his purple skin turning a shade blacker.

"Dare I say no, Lord Gegwu! With your wisdom and courage, the finest catches naturally belong to you." The subordinate broke out in a cold sweat, not daring to ask further.

"Hmph, then why are you still standing there? Go!" Gegwu scoffed.

"Yes! I’ll mobilize the royal guards at once."

After the subordinate left, Gegwu continued giving orders to the others.

But then, a discordant voice suddenly rang out from behind—

"Green-skinned freaks, good evening?"

Gegwu’s eyes widened in shock. *No one should be able to cross the Fire Wall… Who’s speaking human tongue?*

He spun around and saw Merlin grinning, looking completely at ease.

"Emmmm…" Merlin glanced at Gegwu’s skin color and said awkwardly, "So there’s a purple-skinned one too. Your color’s so eye-catching—you must’ve mutated, right?"

Gegwu was stunned to see Merlin unharmed, his face pale with shock. "Y-you… you you you… How did you cross my Fire Wall?!"

"How else? I just walked through." Merlin replied expressionlessly.

"How… how is that possible?! My Fire Wall can’t be bypassed so easily!" Gegwu was flabbergasted, refusing to believe Merlin’s words, convinced he was lying.

"Believe it or not, I can’t be bothered to explain." Merlin felt conflicted. *Probably no one would believe me without seeing it for themselves. Magic immunity is too OP—it breaks game balance.*

"Who the hell are you?!" Gegwu pointed at Merlin, demanding. Anyone who could cross his Fire Wall unscathed couldn’t be a nobody.

"I am…" Merlin said with a deadpan, serious face, "the little chrysanthemum brother of the Moonlight Tavern!"

"What kind of nonsense is this?!" Gegwu’s forehead veins throbbed.

"*Pfft*, you’ve never heard of me? The legendary flower of the pimp world, the star performer of the Moonlight Tavern." Merlin delivered the lewd line with a straight face.

Gegwu furrowed his brows, realizing he couldn’t have a normal conversation with Merlin.

After calming down slightly, he recalled the salty old men from the village earlier—some might have peak high-tier strength.

Gegwu stared at the nonchalant Merlin, carefully probing his aura, but sensed not even a trace of power. This proved Merlin was just an ordinary man with no abilities—

Magic: 0 + Qi: 0 = A complete trash with nothing to offer~!

With this equation, his attitude became obvious.

"Hah, so it was a false alarm…" Gegwu sneered, disdainfully. "I don’t know how you crossed the Fire Wall, but what use is a powerless weakling like you, coming here alone?"

"I’m here to make you release the kidnapped villagers. If you obey, I’ll spare you. This is a once-in-a-century mercy—you’d best seize the chance." Merlin said flatly, his arrogant tone grating and utterly unconvincing.

"Are you out of your mind, you arrogant bastard? Do you even hear yourself?" Gegwu didn’t waste words. With a flick of his hand, he unleashed a Fireball spell, intending to burn Merlin to ashes. "A trash who only talks big—die already."

The fireball shot forward, but Merlin dispersed it with a wave of his hand, his expression souring.

"Hey, that was the lowest-tier beginner magic, right? Are you, a purple-skinned freak, looking down on me? I’m starting to get a little upset…"

"What… what’s going on?!" Gegwu’s face twisted. *How did he scatter the Fireball so strangely? Could he really be magic-immune? No way! He must be hiding his strength!*

Gegwu straightened up, deciding to take this seriously. He wouldn’t underestimate Merlin again. Channeling his magic, he chanted and unleashed a mid-tier fire spell: *Inferno Tornado*.

A storm of flames materialized, resembling a crimson tornado, and instantly struck Merlin.

"Die now!"

The fiery tempest carried waves of scorching heat, instantly boiling the damp ground. Trees and wild grass, unable to withstand the temperature, burst into flames.

Though it was mid-tier magic, the power was amplified by high-tier magic—its might was on another level.

The terrifying Inferno Tornado engulfed Merlin, raging violently.

"Let’s see you be arrogant now! This is your end!"

"As expected of Lord Gegwu, the pride of our Goblin race!"

"Lord Gegwu is sure to become a star of our people!"

"Who does this powerless Village A think he is, daring to challenge Lord Gegwu?"

The Goblin guards jeered, exalting Gegwu to the heavens.

"Hmph!" Gegwu scoffed, turning confidently to handle other matters. Merlin was just a minor hiccup, nothing more.

But then, something went wrong. The Goblin soldiers gasped in horror—

"No… impossible! He’s still alive! Unbelievable!"

"What kind of man is he? So strong!"

"He took Lord Gegwu’s attack head-on and survived?!"

Gegwu turned back—and froze.

Merlin still stood in the same spot, not having moved an inch. Around him was a sea of fire, embers swirling in the air.

The stones beneath his feet were scorched red, yet he remained completely unharmed.

Gegwu’s full-powered mid-tier spell had *no effect*?

Merlin stood in the heart of the inferno, his golden hair swaying as if he were a monarch amidst the apocalypse.

He shrugged, looking at Gegwu with disdain—

"Is that all you’ve got?"

"Honestly, I think I overestimated you."

"You seem weaker than I imagined…"

title: Chapter 78
content:
Chapter 78

Volume 2 · Chapter 78

Beneath the black curtain of rain, Merlin stood wreathed in swirling mist.

The towering figure of a king left everyone stunned.

Facing such a ferocious storm of flames, he hadn’t taken a single step back.

The scene was silent, save for the crackling of fire. Countless goblin warriors witnessed this spectacle, trembling, unable to believe their eyes.

Could this golden-haired man not be an ordinary human, but one of humanity’s strongest?

This doubt surged in the hearts of all the goblins, yet none could fathom the truth.

Magic Immunity was no joke—its effects were undeniable. No matter what divine technique was used, as long as it was powered by magic, it would have absolutely no effect on Merlin. With this skill, calling him a mage slayer wasn’t an exaggeration.

From what he could tell, there were only three ways to kill Merlin—

① Defeat him with physical damage stronger than his own.
② Natural death from a heart curse.
③ Drowning, since he couldn’t swim.

Each of these was nearly impossible. The third was especially unlikely, since Merlin knew his one weakness was swimming, so he never walked near water unless absolutely necessary.

“Uh…” Merlin spread his hands, smiling faintly. “I thought you were some kind of mutated goblin, an SSR with maxed-out stats, but turns out you’re not that strong either…”

“What in the world is going on?! How are you completely unharmed?!” Gegwu demanded, his voice trembling. There was no trace of magic or battle aura around Merlin, yet he had survived Gegwu’s full-powered magical strike without a scratch. It defied all logic!

“Since you asked so sincerely, I’ll graciously enlighten you,” Merlin said, clearing his throat. “To protect the world… *cough* sorry, wrong script. Long story short—” He paused, then cut to the chase. “I’m immune to magic, and invincible in close combat. That makes me unbeatable.”

“Th-This is impossible!”

Gegwu’s face twisted in disbelief. He was convinced Merlin was bluffing. Magic Immunity? That was pure fantasy. Magic was one of the two fundamental systems of the world—how could anyone survive if they were immune to it? It was like someone in the real world claiming they weren’t affected by gravity. Absurd.

Gegwu couldn’t see through Merlin, which made him uneasy, but he still considered him weak.

“You must be bluffing! Did you secretly use some kind of magic-defense artifact just now?”

“Emmmm…” Merlin’s expression turned complicated. He couldn’t be bothered to explain. “Think whatever you want. As long as you’re happy…”

“You bastard! How dare a lowly peasant be so arrogant!”

Gegwu’s jagged teeth clenched tight, the veins on his forehead bulging as if he wanted to bite Merlin’s nose off.

“It’s been years since anyone’s managed to anger me. I have to commend you for that. But that’s enough. Now, let me show you my ultimate technique!”

“Consider yourself honored, human!”

“I’m not human, though…” Merlin muttered awkwardly.

Gegwu pressed his palms together, and high-tier magic surged with all his might. The air grew scorching as fire elements rapidly gathered and condensed.

Merlin suddenly felt like he was in a sauna—uncomfortable, but not unbearable.

He didn’t bother interrupting Gegwu’s incantation. He was actually curious to see what new trick the goblin would pull out.

Red lightning flickered in Gegwu’s palms. With a sudden motion, he spread his hands, and a crimson spear materialized, wreathed in leaping flames.

“Th-That’s… Gegwu’s ultimate technique!”

“I remember! Gegwu hasn’t used it in ages!”

“This will decide the battle! A mere human can’t possibly stop Gegwu’s spear!”

The goblin warriors whispered among themselves, their admiration for Gegwu evident. They already seemed to see Merlin being blasted to pieces.

“Oh~” Merlin looked at the crimson spear, unfazed. “Looks pretty impressive…”

“Human, let’s see how arrogant you are now! This is my strongest high-tier magic—*Sunset Spear*! Since I developed it, no one except His Majesty has ever survived it. Today, I’ll end you with my signature move! Consider yourself honored!”

Gegwu gripped the Sunset Spear, aiming it at Merlin. His palms hissed—likely from the heat scorching his own hands.

“This magic is devastating. I ask you—do you dare face it head-on?!”

“No problem. If I take a single step, I lose.” Merlin replied nonchalantly.

Gegwu’s expression twisted in fury. How dare this lowly peasant be so insolent? What gave him the right to be so arrogant?!

“Then die with your arrogance! Burn in hell, you wretched fool!”

Gegwu hurled the Sunset Spear with all his might, piercing toward the motionless Merlin.

At that moment, the downpour abruptly stopped, and the wind reversed direction.

The fire elements in the air raged like a striped tiger charging down a mountain.

Many of the spectating goblin warriors prostrated themselves, fearing they might be caught in the crossfire.

The crimson spear carried an aura of destruction, tearing through the rain as it struck toward Merlin.

Not dodging was your biggest mistake!

Die! Take your arrogance to hell with you!

Gegwu’s sinister grin was triumphant—he was certain of his victory.

The spear shot forward, but due to Magic Immunity, its trajectory shifted slightly, grazing past Merlin’s ear!

But then—something unimaginable happened.

The crimson spear, blazing with extreme heat and radiating a chilling aura of annihilation… was caught barehanded by Merlin?!

“Hmph. You think something like this can send me to hell? How naive…”

Merlin sneered, his disdain for Gegwu evident. After all that waiting, this was the best the goblin could do? Pathetic. He had expected at least a little challenge.

Gegwu had talked a big game, but in the end, he was still far too weak to interest Merlin.

Disappointed, Merlin decided he had wasted enough time. It was time to send these foes on their way.

The goblin warriors were stunned beyond belief, as if they had witnessed a power that transcended dimensions. Their eyes were about to pop out of their sockets—

“He actually… caught it?!”

“How is this possible?! Who *is* this guy?!”

“Someone actually stopped Gegwu’s *Victory Spear*?!”

title: Chapter 79
content:
Chapter 79

Volume 2 · Chapter 79

Merlin crushed the Spear of Doom in his hand, scattering the fragments around him. The powerful magic crystals shattered like brittle glass under his grip.

What the hell!

Who the hell is this man?!

How can a human be this strong?!

Even a Saint-tier couldn’t do that so effortlessly!

Gegw’s mouth hung open, his entire body trembling in shock.

"Not done yet! Explode!"

"Hm?" Merlin lifted an eyelid, noticing the fragments of the Spear of Doom around him beginning to rage violently, the fire element erupting instantly.

The next second—*BOOM!*—a deafening explosion roared. Apocalyptic flames devoured everything, surging into a towering pillar of fire that seemed to consume the heavens and earth!

The spectacle was breathtaking. Villagers outside the wall of fire stared up in shock, retreating in terror, wondering what was happening inside.

The scorching flames burned fiercely, the extreme heat melting even the rocks!

The goblin warriors, witnessing the power of their great shaman, forgot to flatter him. Instead, they knelt and worshipped, utterly awestruck. This was no mere battle—it was a clash of gods.

Gegw was drenched in cold sweat, his magic exhausted, leaving him weak and gasping on his knees. *Finally, it’s over…* he thought. *Go to hell, you arrogant bastard…*

Then, from the heart of the inferno, a strange force rippled outward, pushing the flames apart and scattering them in all directions. The ignorant goblin warriors were instantly reduced to ashes, not even their bones remaining.

"How… how is this possible?!" Gegw’s eyes widened in disbelief as he stared at the scene before him, like the end of the world.

At the center of the scorching heat, standing atop the churning magma, was a golden-haired man—like the king of hell itself.

Merlin remained unharmed, not a single hair out of place. Magic had no effect on him.

He slowly opened his eyes, and the ruby-like gaze sent a chill through one’s soul.

"Since you managed to develop second-tier magic on your own, I’ll reluctantly praise you for that. But you’re still too weak… and…"

Merlin suddenly vanished. Gegw blinked in confusion, wondering if he had been spared.

"And I dislike weaklings prancing around in front of me, so…"

Merlin reappeared inexplicably behind Gegw, completely evading his enemy’s perception.

Gegw turned in horror, stunned by the speed—so fast it was invisible!

Only now did he realize the sheer gap in power. He had been nothing but a toy to Merlin. With that kind of speed, none of his magic could even touch the man’s heel.

"So please rest in peace, insignificant creature."

Merlin drew his katana just a fraction, the blade’s aura already overflowing.

In an instant, Gegw was sliced to pieces, blood spraying everywhere, only his head left intact.

The same contemptuous, humiliating killing move—without even fully unsheathing the blade.

Gegw’s eyes widened, filled with shame. With his last breath, he gasped, "Wh… why… didn’t you… fully… draw the blade… to kill me…"

The rain poured down, thick dark clouds hanging motionless in the sky.

Merlin, expressionless, flicked his wrist and sheathed the short-drawn katana. Turning his head, he said indifferently—

"You’re too weak. You’re not even worthy of me drawing my sword…"

◆

Alice rushed into the underground palace.

It felt far safer inside than outside.

There were few guards, and no giant goblins like the royal defenders.

The occasional patrols had been silently taken out by Alice.

As for the goblin maids, Alice had knocked them all unconscious.

Hmm…

Truthfully, Alice couldn’t even tell goblin genders apart. They all looked like grotesque green-skinned monsters, making it hard to distinguish—so she could only guess based on their clothing.

Alice infiltrated deeper until she finally reached the great hall. There, she saw the massive throne piled high with gold coins. So much money~

Her eyes lit up. She had assumed goblins were poor creatures, but who knew they were this rich? This was an unexpected windfall!

Then she realized something was wrong and tapped her beautiful forehead.

No, no! Calm down. Saving people is clearly more important than money!

If she remembered correctly, the swordsman Smith had said the prison cells were behind the throne.

Alice leapt into the hall and quickly made her way to the back of the throne. Sure enough, she found a deep, hidden passage. Her heart leapt—

This is it…!

◆

The underground prison was dimly lit.

The air was thick with the scent of lamp oil and dampness.

The only light came from the torches on the walls, making it hard to see clearly.

Prison cells lined the walls, filled with countless trembling women.

They huddled together for warmth, not daring to make a sound, likely fearing punishment.

Two goblin jailers were drinking, occasionally chatting.

"Gulugulugulu…" One chugged his drink, slurring, "Shaman Gegw really outdid himself today. Who knew he’d capture so many human women? The king’s in for a treat tonight."

"Gulugulugulu…" The other goblin took a big swig, groggily adding, "Yeah, there’s some real fine ones in there… makes me itch just lookin’ at ‘em~"

The two goblins leered, probably fantasizing in their heads.

"Hey, brother, with so many slaves tonight, why don’t we take a little taste for ourselves first?" the drunken goblin suggested.

"Th… that’s not right, is it? These slaves all belong to His Majesty," the drowsy goblin hesitated.

"What’s there to fear? We won’t kill ‘em. And they’re just lowly slaves—His Majesty won’t care what happens to them." The drunken goblin was eager to sample the goods, his mind filled with lust after drinking.

"W… well, alright! You go first, big bro! I’ll follow!" the drowsy goblin nodded vigorously.

"C’mon, c’mon! I spotted a few good ones earlier. Let’s go have some fun~"

The two goblins staggered to their feet, arm in arm, ready to indulge.

Suddenly, all the lights went out. The underground prison was plunged into darkness, so thick you couldn’t see your own hand.

"Who’s there?! Damn it, who is it?!"

"Turn the lights back on! What’s going on?!"

"Ah!"

"Gah!"

Two pained screams echoed in the darkness, then silence—only the terrified whispers of the enslaved women remained, unsure of what was happening.

A *crackle* sounded as a torch was lit. In the darkness, someone held the flame high, the silver hair shimmering with dazzling colors in the firelight. Who else could it be but Alice?

The two drunken goblins lay lifeless on the ground, their throats slit by Alice’s sword.

The torchlight flickered in the darkness, and countless frightened eyes in the cells watched her. Someone recognized the silver-haired girl.

"Lady Alice…"

Without hesitation, Alice stepped forward, using her slender sword to strike the chains. The sparks flew, making the women—already terrified from the prolonged darkness—even more anxious.

Alice swung open the prison gates, using the torch to light the path to freedom—

"There’s no time! Everyone, hurry and escape!"

"Don’t look back, and don’t hesitate…"

"With me here, you will be free!"

title: Chapter 80
content:
Chapter 80

Volume 2 · Chapter 80

Alice encouraged the group of slaves, but they were clearly still in shock and distrustful.

"Lady Alice!" A woman stumbled forward, suddenly grabbing her hand. "Henry—how is Henry? He's not...?"

By the flickering torchlight, Alice recognized Martha. Her face was gaunt, her appearance disheveled, and her eyes glistened with tears of worry for her son.

Alice nodded solemnly. "Don’t worry, Martha. Henry is fine. I saw him with my own eyes."

Martha covered her face and wept, her suspended heart finally at ease. "Thank goodness... as long as Henry is safe..."

Alice then turned to everyone in the cell and shouted, "Hurry! Follow me out of here. If we wait any longer, someone might come, and we won’t be able to escape!"

The enslaved women hesitated, suspicious that this might be a trap.

Seeing this, Martha quickly spoke up for Alice. "This is Lady Alice, an adventurer from Lexham. She’s trustworthy. Everyone, let’s go with her!"

Hearing Martha’s introduction, the women relaxed slightly. The oppressive, gloomy atmosphere lifted a little, replaced by flickers of hope. After all, they had thought they were doomed when captured by the goblins—never expecting someone to come and save them.

Alice held the torch high, leading them through the darkness. The swaying flame faintly illuminated their surroundings, reigniting hope in the hearts of these captured women.

Once outside the dungeon, Alice organized them, telling them the safest routes to take. She decided to be the last to leave, staying behind to ensure everyone escaped safely.

She hadn’t forgotten the knight Smith’s request. As each woman emerged from the dungeon, Alice asked cautiously, "Cecile?"

But they all shook their heads. Alice’s heart grew more anxious—she feared the mage might have already perished in the goblin lair.

Yet, as if heaven had heard her prayers, the last woman reacted when she heard the name "Cecile."

Alice gripped her shoulders urgently. "Are you Cecile?"

The girl who had been radiant just days ago now looked disheveled, her clothes filthy, her eyes dull, her expression lost. "Y... yes... I’m Cecile."

"Thank goodness, I finally found you." Alice exhaled in relief. Seeing Cecile alive was a miracle. She spoke earnestly, "Cecile, listen carefully. Your fiancé, Smith—"

But Cecile didn’t seem to hear her. Instead, she looked up in terror, her gaze fixed on the hulking, shadowed figure looming over them.

"A... a... it... it’s here..."

"Cecile? What’s wrong?" Alice saw the sheer fear in Cecile’s eyes, her throat as if choked, unable to speak.

"AAAAAAH!" Cecile shrieked, pointing behind Alice.

Alice’s heart lurched. She spun around—only to see a pitch-black spiked mace swinging toward her.

There was no time to draw her sword, no time to block.

*Cough!*

Alice let out a muffled groan. The attack was too fierce, too sudden—she had no choice but to take the blow head-on.

The mace struck her square in the back, sending her flying like a cannonball. She crashed through several pillars of the great hall before—*BOOM!*—she was blasted into the wall, sending dust and debris billowing. Her fate was unclear.

The impact shattered the pillars, causing the entire hall to tremble violently, the scene descending into chaos.

"Lady Alice!" Martha cried out.

All the escaping slaves were once again gripped by the terror of being controlled, their faces pale as they stared at the massive figure of the underground palace’s master.

They were paralyzed with fear, their bodies icy cold, huddling together for warmth, utterly helpless.

The Goblin Emperor had returned, wielding his weapon—a massive, heavy spiked mace, its surface etched with crimson magical runes. Clearly enchanted, its hardness and power were extraordinary, the jagged spikes radiating a chilling menace.

"I go take a bath, and already a rat sneaks in? How irritating. To think I, the king, would have to handle this myself. That Gekgew is useless."

The Goblin Emperor, his greenish skin draped in luxurious garments, wore a crown on his head. His face was grotesque and terrifying, covered in disgusting warts. Even with countless jewels adorning him, his ugliness was undeniable.

The enslaved women cowered together, staring at the Goblin Emperor’s bloated form. They were so frightened they forgot to run.

"You are all my pets! Who gave you permission to leave? Get back to your cells, now!"

The Goblin Emperor roared, his large nose twitching, his jagged teeth looking razor-sharp.

The women burst into terrified sobs, their wails filled with despair.

"Stop crying! You worthless pets—get back to your cells at once!"

The Goblin Emperor bellowed, his expression ferocious, as if he might devour them whole.

"Run! If we go back, we’ll all die!"

Martha summoned her courage and shouted, snapping the last thread of hesitation in the women.

The slaves came to their senses, driven by sheer survival instinct, and scattered in a frantic escape.

"Come back! Come back! You can’t escape! If I catch you, I’ll skin you alive!" The Goblin Emperor raged, lifting his spiked mace to chase after them.

The women stumbled forward, seemingly unable to outrun him.

The Goblin Emperor’s face twisted in fury, ready to crush the women into pulp with his massive mace.

Then, suddenly, frost began to form above his head. A colossal ice prison materialized out of thin air, descending rapidly and trapping the Goblin Emperor inside.

"Wh—?!" The Goblin Emperor was momentarily stunned, his confused gaze turning toward the dust-filled other side of the hall. "Not dead yet? Truly a tenacious rat..."

As the dust settled, Alice barely supported her battered body with her slender sword. The earlier blow had left her gravely injured—blood trickled down her forehead, staining half her beautiful face.

The once-radiant valkyrie now seemed like a fallen angel, her wings broken, reduced to a pitiful figure.

Yet Alice did not retreat. Her stunning face still bore an unshakable resolve, unwavering in the slightest.

She raised her hand, magic surging as she maintained the ice prison, preventing the Goblin Emperor from rampaging freely.

Dragging her shattered, heavy body, she slowly straightened herself, then shouted—

"As long as I’m here, I won’t let you harm them!"

title: Chapter 81
content:
Chapter 81

Volume 2 · Chapter 81

Alice had always felt that learning Ice Prison was a waste. The high-tier skill consumed a lot of energy and had almost no practical use in daily life.

But now, it had proven surprisingly effective, and she couldn’t help but feel a flicker of relief.

Though it was difficult to truly restrain the Goblin Emperor, even a brief delay was enough.

Her primary goal was to cover the escape of these people. As long as she succeeded, her trip here wouldn’t have been in vain.

Alice knew she might not make it out alive, but she had to protect these innocent people. A battle against a Saint-tier foe seemed unavoidable.

Her luck really was terrible—no matter how careful she was, she still ended up facing the Goblin Emperor.

Sensing the dire odds, Alice poured all her magic into reinforcing the Ice Prison, buying time for the hostages to retreat.

"Oh? A mere high-tier rat thinks it can trap me with Ice Prison? How delusional!"

The Goblin Emperor swung its wolf-tooth club with ease, shattering the continuously reinforced Ice Prison into countless ice shards that scattered through the air.

As expected of a Saint-tier being—the power gap was enormous!

But she absolutely couldn’t let it give chase. Not like this!

Alice retaliated with a burst of Ice Thorns. Countless thorned ice tendrils erupted from the ground like living creatures, piercing through the Goblin Emperor’s body, coiling around its waist to restrain it once more.

"You pathetic little rat! Have some shame! I’ll tear your legs apart and rip you in half!" The Goblin Emperor snarled, seemingly furious that its pets had escaped.

"I already said—while I’m here, you won’t lay a finger on them!" Alice’s expression was deadly serious as she relentlessly directed the Ice Thorns to harass it.

"You stinking rat! Let’s see how you escape my palace alive!" The Goblin Emperor roared, its eyes vicious, the veins on its forehead throbbing violently.

Escape?

Sorry, that was never part of the plan.

If she left the Goblin Emperor unchecked, it would hunt down and slaughter those fleeing women one by one.

Alice had already made peace with the idea of death. She never intended to run.

Even in the face of death, she would uphold her justice!

She was determined to fight the Goblin Emperor to the bitter end—never giving it a chance to pursue the slaves.

"Cecile!!!"

Alice called out. She hadn’t forgotten her promise to someone.

The panicked female mage, having reached the doorway, turned back at Alice’s shout.

Without another word, Alice hurled a gleaming silver object into the air. It traced a beautiful arc before landing with a delicate chime.

Cecile picked up the silver necklace from the ground, her body trembling as tears gushed forth.

It was Smith’s Adventurer’s Proof—engraved with his name. The fact that it had been removed now meant…

Tears streamed down her face like a broken string of pearls.

"Pull yourself together, Cecile! Smith isn’t dead!" Alice shouted.

"Eh?!" Cecile lifted her tear-streaked face.

"He’s waiting for you outside. He’s still alive!"

"Once you escape, the nightmare will be over. Everything will return to peace. You can go back home, get married, even have children…"

"So be brave, Cecile! Run with everything you’ve got!"

"Don’t look back. Don’t hold onto any memories of this place."

"Just escape. Fight for your own future!"

Alice raised her hand, channeling a surge of magic to slowly encase the palace entrance in ice.

Countless ice blades materialized, forming an impassable barrier at the doorway.

"Lady Alice…"

"Lady Alice!"

Cecile outside was frantic, repeatedly calling Alice’s name.

But the silver-haired girl remained unmoved, as if she couldn’t hear a thing, not even glancing toward the exit.

Alice had come here prepared to die. She had accepted her sacrifice and was ready to battle the Goblin Emperor until her last breath, never letting it leave the hall.

The palace doors were now completely sealed in ice, exuding a chilling aura.

Cecile couldn’t see inside. She knelt before the door, overwhelmed with despair—

"Lady Alice…"

◆

Stop calling me.

If you keep calling, I might falter… and turn to flee.

I’m scared too. Just enduring until this moment has taken everything I have.

Alice forced herself upright, pointing her rapier at the Goblin Emperor. The blood trickling down her face made her look like a warrior marching to her doom.

There was no retreat—only surging courage.

The moment the palace doors were frozen shut, this place had become a bloody battleground. Only one of them would walk out alive, and the outcome already seemed clear.

Alice was ready. Wounded and weary, she would still fight the Goblin Emperor to the very end!

The Goblin Emperor shuddered, and the oppressive might of a Saint-tier being radiated outward. The surrounding Ice Thorns could no longer resist, shattering one after another.

Alice furrowed her brows deeply, feeling the immense pressure of that Saint-tier aura.

"Swordswoman, do you understand the consequences of stealing my pets?"

The Goblin Emperor raised its wolf-tooth club, glaring at Alice. It knew this silver-haired swordswoman wouldn’t let it leave to give chase—so it had no choice but to kill her.

"I do. But I still won’t let you go." Alice gripped her pure silver rapier, her voice calm.

"Good. I must commend your resolve. Allow me to express a hint of respect—be proud, human. As the king of the goblin race, this is the first time I’ve ever looked at a human with such admiration." The Goblin Emperor puffed out its massive belly.

"I don’t need the pity of a filthy goblin." Alice replied coldly, irritation flaring in her heart.

"I’ll show mercy and give you two choices: lay down your sword and become my queen, or fight me to the death. You—"

"Enough. Stop wasting my time. I choose the second option."

Before the Goblin Emperor could finish, Alice had already chosen to fight to the death.

Deep down, Alice found the idea of a goblin’s affection utterly revolting. Plus, its attitude was insolent and rude. The only man she admired was Elgin, the legendary swordsman—powerful and just.

The atmosphere suddenly turned awkward and oppressive…

The Goblin Emperor’s eyes burned with fury. It had taken a liking to Alice’s beauty, her (deceptively) impressive figure, and most importantly, her high-tier strength that made her a worthy match. The thought of sharing a bed with such a spirited human woman had genuinely intrigued it.

But this silver-haired human woman had actually rejected *it*—the Goblin Emperor! This was an unforgivable humiliation!

Enraged, the Goblin Emperor hoisted its wolf-tooth club and charged straight at the tiny Alice, bellowing, "Then die! Filthy human woman! I’ll capture you and break you into my—!"

"I won’t give you the chance…" Alice swung her rapier, her silver hair cascading like a waterfall as she surged forward, her high-tier battle aura flaring. She clashed head-on with the mighty foe. "Disgusting creature. Die by my blade like the trash you are!"

The Goblin Emperor’s massive club and Alice’s slender rapier collided with a thunderous crash. The shockwaves from their clash sent tremors through the hall, shattering several supporting pillars.

With this direct confrontation, the deadly duel officially began…

title: Chapter 82
content:
Chapter 82

Volume 2 · Chapter 82

Alice and the Goblin Emperor clashed in the sealed great hall.

Despite the Goblin Emperor’s bloated frame and heavy weapon, he moved with unnatural speed. The power of a Saint-tier was undeniable—every swing carried crushing force, and Alice could barely defend, forced to dodge as best she could.

After a series of trials, her fighting spirit and magic were nearly spent. She was on the verge of exhaustion, the situation dire.

Gritting her teeth, Alice flipped away to evade the spiked club, her silver hair fanning out in a graceful arc. She countered with a backhand strike, her slender silver sword flashing like starlight. Each attack sent frost shards scattering, a dazzling display of swordsmanship.

The blade traced countless elegant arcs, stabbing toward the Goblin Emperor’s chest—only for him to block it with one hand, dismissive in his defense.

“HAHAHA! Is this your strength? Pathetic!”

“Tch!”

Alice seethed. She was being looked down upon.

Mustered the last of her fighting spirit, she leapt, thrusting straight for his throat.

“Ridiculous!” The Goblin Emperor grinned, and a surge of Saint-tier power erupted, overwhelming her. He swung his spiked club downward with crushing force, aiming to flatten her midair!

Alice paled, retracting her attack and raising her hand toward the incoming club. “Ice Shield!”

The mid-tier spell activated, forming a massive ice barrier above her, blooming like a flower.

But against a Saint-tier strike, it was useless. The hammer shattered the shield like tofu, crumbling in an instant.

Alice barely twisted away, but the shockwave still sent her flying. The Goblin Emperor’s club slammed into the ground, carving a deep crater with spiderweb cracks—terrifying to behold.

This was no technique, just the raw power of a Saint-tier.

As a high-tier, Alice was no match.

“Wretched human, do you feel the gap now?” The Goblin Emperor loomed over her. “I’ll give you one last chance—become my queen. Otherwise, I won’t hold back.”

He had been toying with her this whole time, never using his full strength. He still hoped she’d accept his proposal.

If he fought seriously, Alice would be crushed instantly.

Yet even with him mocking her, she couldn’t win. After one exchange, she was on the back foot, nearly flattened.

Every bone in her body ached, her face pale, cold sweat pouring down.

But she stubbornly propped herself up with her sword, forcing herself to stand.

“Impossible! I said I don’t need your pity!”

“Is that so? What a shame… such a pretty face, wasted…”

The Goblin Emperor tapped his spiked club against his shoulder, utterly at ease.

Alice had little magic or fighting spirit left—enough for one last push.

The situation was desperate. She had to go all in, risk everything for a chance.

If she ran out of power, she’d die. Better to gamble.

She decided to pour her remaining magic and fighting spirit into a flurry of strikes, forcing her way out of this deadly predicament!

“Next, I’ll send you to hell!”

Alice raised her sword, pressing her fingers against the cold blade. The last of her magic and fighting spirit surged violently.

“Still not giving up? Such a stubborn, wretched creature.” The Goblin Emperor sneered. “I despise women with no taste. A man as handsome as me—am I not worthy of you, a mere human?”

The fat on his face jiggled, oblivious to how repulsive goblins were in human eyes.

“Take your disgusting narcissism to the grave…”

Alice suddenly flicked her sword upward, unleashing a storm. Countless ice shards and snowflakes swirled within, a chilling gust sweeping through the hall.

Mid-tier spell: Blizzard. In moments, it recreated a natural landscape, snowflakes obscuring vision, ice shards slicing through the wind like blades.

The hall’s temperature plummeted. The blizzard spun around the Goblin Emperor, blocking his sight.

But he was a Saint-tier. Such an attack was like a tickle. He stood unmoved in the storm, untouched.

“HAHAHA! Is this your dying struggle? I thought it’d be something impressive, but it’s just a drizzle…”

The Goblin Emperor laughed, leisurely mocking her.

Alice suppressed her fear, gripping her sword tightly. For a moment, she recalled her childhood training in the Alps…

◆

The vast Alps, blanketed in snow.

Young Alice, bundled in furs, waddled like a chubby penguin.

She swung a wooden sword wrapped in chains to add weight, stabbing repeatedly at a wooden dummy.

“Teacher! I don’t wanna practice anymore! I wanna sleep!”

“No. A thousand times. You’re only halfway.” The teacher stood nearby, holding an umbrella to keep the snow off.

“Why?! Other girls get to do fun things at this hour—wear pretty dresses, eat candy! Why do I have to practice swordsmanship?!” Alice swung her sword, grumbling.

“Do I need to explain? I’m too poor to afford those things. Once you’re too tired to complain, you won’t ask for them anymore.” The teacher smirked.

“I… I can’t even find the words… You’re so stingy, Teacher…” Alice pouted, exasperated by her teacher’s cheapness.

“Stop complaining. The harder you train now, the better your chances of survival later.” The teacher said indifferently.

“But what’s the point of basic thrusts?!” Little Alice huffed.

“You should know—it’s not about flashy techniques. A simple thrust can be more effective than any fancy move.” The teacher patiently explained.

“Even against a Saint-tier?!”

“Sometimes. Most Saint-tier warriors aren’t physically invincible. They’re still human, so their hearts are their weakness. A well-placed thrust could be fatal.”

The teacher swayed in the snow, lecturing Alice, half-serious, half-joking.

“Besides, our Alps lineage has always practiced both magic and martial arts. Our strength comes from versatility—when magic and fighting spirit collide, they can unleash devastating power. If such a combined strike hits a weak point, it’ll be crippling, if not deadly.”

“But Saint-tier opponents aren’t that easy to hit…” Alice scoffed.

“Then use your wits. Ambush, poison, surprise attacks, threats, hostage-taking—anything works.” The teacher shrugged. “If all else fails, strip naked and seduce them. Why be so rigid?”

“Teacher… you’re shameless…” Alice’s expression twisted.

“My old rival did exactly that. She’d flash her skin, let tentacle monsters grope her, moaning and screaming in *harmonious* ways. Bosses wouldn’t kill her, and that trash actually survived till the final episode—then stole my man!” The teacher’s forehead veins bulged as she gnashed her teeth, snapping her umbrella handle in half—

“That vile, seductive hag proved one thing…”

“This world doesn’t need your so-called *iron virgin* nonsense!”

(╬￣皿￣)

title: Chapter 83
content:
Chapter 83

Volume 2 · Chapter 83

Alice pushed aside her memories and decided to make a desperate gamble, aiming straight for the Goblin Emperor’s heart.

“Here we go…”

Alice suddenly lunged forward, her high-tier battle aura surging violently, leaving a trail of afterimages across the ground.

With a swift leap, she kicked off the earth and soared into the sky.

From the air, she saw the eye of the blizzard—the Goblin Emperor, smirking with ease.

A surge of anger filled her. Midair, she gripped her rapier and plunged downward in a sudden strike.

The sharp blade cut through the frigid air, heading unerringly for the Goblin Emperor’s heart.

“Hehehe! I knew your blizzard was just a distraction. I’ve been waiting for you!”

The Goblin Emperor abruptly lifted his head, his face twisting as he locked eyes on Alice descending from above.

What?

He noticed her…

Alice’s heart jolted. Her attack was already committed—she couldn’t pull back now.

“HAH!”

The Goblin Emperor roared, and the oppressive might of a Saint-tier being erupted.

The surrounding blizzard dispersed in an instant, and even Alice’s momentum faltered.

With a sweep of his massive hand, he snatched her out of the air, crushing her in his grip so she couldn’t move.

“Jumping around like a pest, and now you come to me to die? Where do you think you’re running now?”

“Aaaaaah—”

Alice, trapped in his palm, let out a string of pained cries as her bones creaked under the pressure.

“Kehahahaha!” The Goblin Emperor cackled, his voice dripping with sick delight. “This is the face I wanted! This is the sound! You’re absolutely perfect! I’m growing more and more interested in you. I’d love to break you slowly…”

“Can you still laugh?” Alice coughed up a streak of blood, her voice sharp with defiance.

“Huh? You’re in my hand, and you still dare to talk like that?” The Goblin Emperor’s brows furrowed.

Alice didn’t answer. Instead, she shaped the words with her lips—

「Frost Divine Judgment」

It turned out she had already been preparing a high-tier spell above the Goblin Emperor’s head!

It was all a setup. Alice had used herself as bait, drawing his attention, while secretly casting the highly destructive high-tier spell in the air.

Frost Divine Judgment couldn’t be cast instantly—its practicality was limited—but its damage was immense. It required advance incantation before it could be unleashed.

Alice had hidden her preparations behind the blizzard, completed the chant, and then used herself as the decoy, descending from the sky.

And now—

The Goblin Emperor sensed a violent surge of magic above him.

A frosty force, like a wild horse breaking free, exploded toward him.

He looked up just in time to see a massive sword of frost—Damocles’ Frostblade—plummeting from the heavens!

The spell had been perfectly set up and guided. The powerful magic was already upon him—too late to dodge.

“ROOOOAAAAR!”

The Goblin Emperor let out a miserable howl as the frost giant sword pierced through his skull, skewering him to the ground like a shish kebab. Blood gushed like a fountain.

Alice crashed to the earth, dragging her heavily wounded body as she struggled to stand. Seeing the Goblin Emperor impaled by the frost sword, she finally relaxed.

“Y-You… you bitch! How… how dare you trick me! I won’t… let you get away with this!”

The Goblin Emperor’s life force was tenacious—he wasn’t dead yet. Blood spraying from his mouth, he cursed Alice.

“This is what happens when you underestimate me. Let me send you off properly. Feel the swordsmanship of the Great Snow Mountain!”

Alice raised her rapier. With a step, she sent a flurry of ice petals scattering in all directions.

Glacial Triple Strike—a high-tier sword technique her master had taught her. Each segment had a purpose and deadly precision.

Alice danced forward, her blade flashing as countless silver arcs cascaded down.

“First strike!”

In an instant, she severed the tendons in his limbs, rendering him powerless to resist.

“Second strike!”

A slash to the throat, injecting a deadly chill into his body to extinguish his vitality.

“Third strike!”

No more hesitation—she pierced his heart, sending him straight to hell!

Alice executed the final technique, blending magic and battle aura to form a layer of hybrid ice crystals along the blade.

This was the same finishing move she had used before the Demon Lord Palace, intending to kill the Great Demon Lilith in one strike.

“Die! You filthy creature!”

Alice drove her rapier straight into the Goblin Emperor’s heart, piercing through in an instant.

Magic and battle aura collided inside him, detonating with devastating force, ravaging his body from within.

The air fell silent. Everything settled into stillness.

The Goblin Emperor’s face turned ashen, seemingly lifeless. His arms hung limply, blood pooling beneath him like a flowing stream.

Alice pulled out her rapier and kicked his corpse to the ground.

She panted heavily, sweat and blood streaking down her face. Her magic and battle aura were nearly depleted.

“It’s over…”

Alice flicked the blood from her blade, sheathed it, and limped toward the palace exit.

BOOM—!

A deafening explosion erupted behind her. The Goblin Emperor stood up again, his green skin shifting to a fiery crimson in an instant. He opened his maw and spewed scalding white mist!

His grievous wounds healed in a flash, and every muscle on his body bulged with explosive power.

Alice turned in shock, staring up at the Goblin Emperor—now more than twice his original size, his body as majestic as a mountain—

“Don’t leave just yet.”

“Turning back so confidently isn’t a good habit.”

「Berserk Mode」

An innate ability of certain races, mostly beastkin.

It drastically boosted attack power at the cost of intelligence.

The most notable feature was the drastically enhanced self-healing—any non-fatal wound would rapidly regenerate.

And the Goblin race happened to be beastkin. Their emperor was the cream of the crop, and his Berserk Mode amplified his power to terrifying levels.

The Goblin Emperor’s body had more than doubled in size, his ornate clothes torn apart. His massive, hairy belly made him look like a butcher in an instant.

The most striking change was his skin—from green to a furious crimson, his features twisted into something far more savage, his teeth jutting out.

“Why aren’t you dead?!” Alice stumbled back in terror, defenseless without her magic or battle aura. “I pierced your heart! Even a Saint-tier—”

“Here…” The Goblin Emperor pointed to his right side, mocking her. “A goblin’s heart is on the right, not the left. Did you even read a book?”

Alice’s eyes widened in horror. She had assumed a goblin’s heart was in the same place as a human’s—how could it be on the right?

“Seems you never learned that knowledge changes fate. Can’t blame me, then. Earlier, I underestimated you. But I won’t hold back this time…” The Goblin Emperor narrowed his eyes, gazing down at her like an ant.

Alice couldn’t believe it. After all her effort, she was about to fall because of a lack of knowledge.

“You’re a disciple of the Alps Great Snow Mountain, aren’t you? That attack where magic and battle aura collide—it’s similar to the legendary Glacial Sword Saint. Though not as impressive as the tales claim.” The Goblin Emperor sneered.

“None of your business…” Alice gritted her teeth, drawing her rapier and assuming a defensive stance.

“Heh. Then die.” The Goblin Emperor suddenly swung his spiked club with brutal force.

The speed was unimaginable—Saint-tier battle aura combined with Berserk Mode.

The Goblin Emperor had barely moved, yet in the next instant, the spiked club slammed into Alice’s side, sending her flying like a broken kite.

“Cough—ahhh—”

A series of agonized screams escaped her. Without magic or battle aura, she couldn’t resist at all. A single strike had brought her to the brink of death.

Alice crashed into a stone wall before coming to a stop, her fate hanging by a thread.

The Goblin Emperor wore a sinister grin as he approached, kicking up layers of dust. He reached out with one massive hand, yanked Alice off the ground, and examined her closely.

Alice was a far cry from her former glory—covered in wounds, on the verge of unconsciousness. Blood poured down her forehead like a curtain, her chest rising and falling weakly.

Whether it was a sudden surge of lust or some twisted chivalry, the Goblin Emperor showed unexpected restraint, leaving her with a sliver of life.

“Kehahaha! Truly exquisite! The sight of you broken is so delightful!”

His face twisted into a lewd, grotesque smile.

“Then, I won’t hold back any longer…”

The Goblin Emperor extended his tongue, slowly approaching the hem of Alice’s skirt, seemingly intent on some kind of tentacle play.

As expected of His Majesty—he really knew how to have fun…

[Female lead vs. Emperor, 1400 words, includes some strategic battle.]

[Emperor vs. female lead, 140 words.]

I’ve cut as much as I can. Any less and it wouldn’t feel satisfying, any more and it’d feel padded.

One update a day feels too little, and even with over 30,000 words in reserve, it’s still not enough. I can only wait until the end of the month.

We’re in the climax now, and one update a day drags it out. Normally, I could finish the climax in a few days, but during the stockpile period, I’m sorry—I can’t release more. Please understand…

title: Chapter 83 — 5
content:
Chapter 83 — 5

Volume 2 · Chapter 83

On the other side.

A few minutes before Alice was defeated by the Goblin Emperor.

Dark clouds rumbled, and the rain showed no sign of letting up.

Little Henry had truly climbed up the rugged cliff, relying on his own willpower, stepping on the rocks one by one.

This was the interior of the underground nest, the outer area of the underground palace.

Little Henry, carrying his father’s sword on his back, caught his breath and looked around.

Worried about his mother, he hurried into the cave.

When the narrow cave suddenly opened up, what entered Little Henry’s eyes was the magnificent underground palace.

Little Henry was stunned—he had never seen anything like this before.

He thought that maybe, just maybe, his mother was locked inside, and he needed to hurry.

How high could a child’s intelligence be?

Clearly, not very.

Little Henry spotted a giant goblin ahead and, without a word, this hot-blooded fool drew the sword from his back and charged.

"You bastards! Give my mom back!"

Little Henry’s steps were at most the length of an adult’s, his little legs moving back and forth.

The giant goblin wasn’t very bright. It turned its head, glanced at Little Henry, and didn’t take him seriously at all, looking at him like a tiny bug.

"Die! Eat a sword from your Uncle Henry!"

Little Henry swung the iron sword, striking hard at the giant goblin’s foot armor, sending up a few sparks, but it didn’t do the slightest damage.

He froze, startled, but quickly snapped out of it and kept hacking away.

"Die! Die! You bastard! Give my mom back!"

The giant goblin watched Little Henry, who could only attack its toes, and burst into laughter, "Hoo hoo hoo!"

Little Henry gritted his teeth, his helmet tilted to one side, still swinging with all his might.

The giant goblin seemed to have grown tired of the game, finding it boring. It raised its massive club, its wide mouth twisting into a grin as it let out a muffled laugh.

"Ah...?"

Little Henry was so scared he fell back onto the ground. He hadn’t expected to be completely ineffective. His eyes widened in terror at the massive club raised high above him.

He was afraid now, his hot blood cooling. He really didn’t want to be smashed into pulp.

"No... don’t..."

Little Henry instinctively shut his eyes, too terrified to look at the giant goblin.

But then a gust of wind rushed past his ears, followed by a "swoosh!"

When Little Henry opened his eyes again, he saw the giant goblin had been cleanly split in half. Blood and bones sprayed everywhere before it crashed to the ground with a thunderous boom.

Merlin, the man once called useless, now stood like a god of war before Henry, his back straight, his thin frame belying his strength.

Under his black coat, he still wore his bartender’s uniform—clearly, he had come straight from work.

The rusted, notched katana was stained with the blood of various goblins, exuding a murderous aura.

Merlin flicked the blood off the blade, sheathed the katana, and turned to smile at Little Henry—

"You had good spirit just now, kid. Out of 100, I’d give you a 99."

"But you didn’t listen and ran off to such a dangerous place, so that’s minus 99."

"In the end, you still get a zero. Heh heh..."

title: Chapter 84 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 84 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 2 · Chapter 84

So... so strong!

There wasn’t even a fight.

Was it a one-hit kill?

Was Uncle Merlin really this strong of a swordsman?

Too damn cool, Mom, I wanna learn iaijutsu right now…

Little Henry couldn’t hide his admiration, his eyes sparkling like stars.

Just a while ago, he’d been nothing but scornful toward Merlin, but now all he felt was admiration, his heart overflowing with genuine awe.

Turns out Uncle Merlin hadn’t been boasting all this time—he really was this powerful. He could one-shot a giant goblin, way stronger than Big Strongson. Little Henry had still underestimated Merlin. A 9999…9999 iaijutsu to kill a giant goblin?

Merlin himself wanted to laugh. This was just boring.

Think about it—if you used a top-tier awakening skill in an online game to kill a giant sea turtle, would that be **? Pretty damn boring.

"You okay?" Merlin finished mocking Henry and then asked.

"N-no, I’m fine! Pfft! That’s not the point! Uncle Merlin…" Little Henry looked up at Merlin, his eyes as pleading as a kid begging for candy.

"W-what? I don’t have money, and I’m not giving my life," Merlin frowned, unable to bear that starry-eyed gaze.

"Uncle Merlin, please teach me iaijutsu!" Little Henry shamelessly threw his arms around Merlin’s leg.

"I tried to teach you before, but you refused. Now you’re changing your tune? No way!" Merlin struck a haughty pose, summing it up in one sentence:

*"Back then, you ignored me, but now I’m out of your league!"*

"Uncle Merlin! Please!" Little Henry did a complete 180 in attitude and *thud*—knelt on the ground.

Merlin was awkward, staring at Henry clinging to his leg. *See? Just as I predicted the first time we met—he’d end up kneeling and begging.*

"Get up. Didn’t you say iaijutsu was a useless skill and that you already knew how to use it?"

"No, I think iaijutsu is amazing now! It’s a god-tier skill! I don’t understand its essence at all—I have no talent for it!" Little Henry refused to let go of Merlin’s leg. "So please, Uncle Merlin, teach me! I’ll even crossdress for help! Whatever you want, I’ll do it—humiliate me however you like!"

"Y-you… have some dignity. I’m not into traps…" Merlin shook his leg, but Henry clung like a plaster, impossible to shake off.

"Liar! That day you spanked me, Uncle Merlin, you were so excited your grin split your face!" Henry retorted, then begged, "Teach me, Uncle Merlin! I’ll do any shame play—queen games, wax dripping, breath play, anything…"

"Tch!" Merlin’s face darkened. *What the hell? How does Henry know all this so well?*

"Get lost. I’m not that kind of person!"

"Uncle Merlin, please…"

"Get lost, or I’ll cut you down!"

Just as Henry was clinging to Merlin and the argument dragged on—

"Henry? Merlin?"

Martha and a large group of fleeing women rushed over. The moment she saw her son, she joyfully ran to hug him.

"Mom!" Little Henry abandoned Merlin and threw himself into his mother’s arms, tears streaming down his face. "Mom, are you okay? I was so worried about you!"

"You naughty child, you never listen! You’ve worried your mother so much." Martha held her son, her voice full of complaints, but her eyes welled up with tears.

"I won’t do it again, I won’t be naughty anymore…" Henry sobbed, making promises.

"Why did you come here? It’s so dangerous!" Martha was upset—she didn’t want her son in harm’s way.

"I… I wanted to save you…" Little Henry said, aggrieved.

"What could you have done? What if something happened? Your poor mother would’ve been heartbroken." Martha’s eyes brimmed with tears. She felt her son cared too much for her, otherwise he wouldn’t have risked himself like this.

"No… it wasn’t dangerous because…" Little Henry, afraid of being scolded, shifted the blame onto Merlin. "Uncle Merlin brought me here! Uncle Merlin is super strong—he’s the one who took down the giant goblin!"

*What?*

*What the hell?*

*Who brought you here?*

*This is gonna cost me my paycheck!*

No doubt about it—the iaijutsu lessons were canceled!

Merlin had been happily watching the mother-son reunion, but now he was inexplicably dragged into it.

He felt he’d already repaid the debt for the care he’d received from the boss lady. There was no need to get involved in more trouble.

Martha looked at the corpse on the ground, doubt and hope flickering in her eyes. She turned to Merlin. "Is what Henry said true?"

"Uh… yeah…" Merlin nodded. There was no one else who could’ve taken down the giant goblin, so denying it wouldn’t be right.

"Then… then could you go help Lady Alice?!" Martha suddenly asked urgently.

"Huh?!" Merlin’s eyes widened, three question marks exploding in his mind.

Martha, mistaking his hesitation for confusion, explained, "Lady Alice is fighting the Emperor alone to save us. She might be in danger. Merlin, please go help her. I know you probably can’t beat the Goblin Emperor, and it’s dangerous, but if you can just save Lady Alice…"

In the end, Martha still underestimated Merlin. She figured that if he could take down a giant goblin, he probably couldn’t beat a Saint-tier Goblin Emperor, but even so, he might still be able to rescue Alice.

"Hmm…"

Merlin hesitated. Alice had always treated him terribly, always acting so superior. And the mental damage from her "GUN" still hadn’t healed.

If Alice was getting beaten up, logically, he should be happy, maybe even mock her…

Wait! Didn’t I want to become an adventurer?

This was the perfect opportunity to do Alice a favor!

Merlin suddenly saw a turning point. If he saved Alice, his dream of becoming an adventurer might just work out. With that stubborn personality of hers, she’d never want to owe him a favor. Then—

*"Alice, I want to be an adventurer."*

*"G, U, N!"*

*"But I saved your life. You can’t do that."*

*"OK! Let’s GO!"*

Yes! That’s exactly how it’ll go!

Wait, the Emperor is Saint-tier?

Alright, I’m going to steal the kill…

Martha, seeing Merlin hesitate, grew anxious. "Go! I’ll triple your pay for the past half-month!"

"Tch! Sister Martha, what kind of person do you take me for? Do I look like someone who’d do anything for money?" Merlin put on a displeased expression, as if he’d been insulted.

"Ermmmm…"

Martha and Little Henry stayed silent, choosing not to comment.

"Right? I’m not the kind of person who’d abandon justice for profit." Merlin shamelessly praised himself, then thumped his chest. "My heart is full of justice!"

*Bullshit!*

If it weren’t for wanting to become an adventurer, I wouldn’t give a damn about Alice!

But this chain of benefits was just too perfect. Any fool would take the chance!

"Then be careful." Martha urged.

"Make sure you come back to teach me sword techniques, Uncle Merlin!" Little Henry subtly expressed his concern.

Merlin gripped the katana at his waist, turned, and strode straight toward the Goblin Palace, his black coat billowing, his gaze unwavering—

"Rest assured, I’ll clear the way."

"Nii-san, I’ll bring back that stupid donkey Alice."

"Sa, one dog!"

title: Chapter 85
content:
Chapter 85

Volume 2 · Chapter 85

Merlin walked to the entrance of the great hall and saw that it had already been sealed by crystal-clear ice.

He knew this was Alice’s doing—she was probably still inside, locked in a desperate battle with the Goblin Emperor.

Two giant goblins stood at the door, swinging their clubs to chip away at the ice, clearly trying to break in and aid their emperor in battle.

Unfortunately for them, they had just run into Merlin…

"Good evening, gentlemen. Mind getting out of my way?"

The giant goblins, upon seeing Merlin, didn’t hesitate—they raised their massive clubs and charged, their footsteps shaking the ground.

"Guess that’s your answer. Farewell…"

With a single hand, Merlin drew his katana slightly from its sheath, and a slash of sword energy erupted.

The two giant goblins were instantly shredded, their flesh and blood scattering in a gruesome display.

Merlin sheathed his blade and stepped over the carnage, approaching the wall of ice sealing the door.

Facing a higher-level enemy and still choosing to fight to the death?

Truly living up to her reputation as the "Ironing Board Hero"—stupid beyond belief…

Merlin raised his hand and walked forward. Relying on his "Magic Immunity" physique, he dispersed the ice wall effortlessly, clearing a path.

Countless shards of ice scattered and crumbled away with a cascading sound.

When Merlin entered the hall, he saw the Goblin Emperor looming over Alice, who was nearly unconscious and covered in wounds—

"Well then, I’ll help myself…"

The Goblin Emperor leered, lifting the tiny Alice with a grin. A grotesque, bumpy tongue slithered from its mouth, reaching toward the hem of her skirt.

What the hell?! There should be a censor bar here!

No, wait—dare to lick *my* wife?

No, that’s not right either—dare to disrespect *my* patron? Unforgivable!

Yes, *that* was the right reason…

Merlin nodded, muttering internally before finally deciding to take action.

The Goblin Emperor narrowed its eyes into a sleazy squint, clearly excited. It was about to enjoy its *premium prey* with its tongue—tentacle play, its favorite.

*Whoosh—*

Just as the Goblin Emperor was about to indulge, a shadow flashed before its eyes.

"Hm?!"

The Goblin Emperor blinked in confusion, as if someone had just darted past it.

It looked around but saw nothing unusual, assuming it was a trick of the light. It turned its attention back to Alice, ready to continue its assault.

Then it looked down—Alice was gone. And so was its hand!

In the blink of an eye, its hand had been cleanly severed, the wound smooth as glass.

The severed hand twitched on the ground, fingers still spasming.

"Huh?! My hand…"

The Goblin Emperor froze, and in the next second, a fountain of blood erupted from the stump, gushing with terrifying force.

The sheer volume of blood was staggering. The Goblin Emperor staggered back, staring in horror at its missing limb, screaming in agony.

"My handaaaaaaaaah!"

"My precioussssssss!"

"My life partnerrrrrrrr!"

Merlin rescued the nearly unconscious Alice, lifting her into a princess carry, cradling her against his chest. Seeing her battered and broken body, he couldn’t help but sigh—

This woman… she really goes all out for others, doesn’t she?

Merlin exhaled, a hint of reluctant admiration in his voice. Weak she may be, but her unyielding will and tenacity demanded respect.

This was the second time he had carried Alice. The first had been in the Death Swamp, but this was the first time she had been so docile, finally looking a bit like a proper young lady.

For Merlin, holding a girl’s slender body did nothing to stir his emotions. At over two hundred years old, the restless hormones of youth were long gone. He had seen far too many women to get flustered, drool, or blush over a little physical contact.

Men who couldn’t walk past a woman without losing their composure? Nonexistent in his world. Women were just troublesome creatures—that was Merlin’s honest take.

He gently laid Alice on the ground, watching her semi-conscious state with a small smile.

"You’re a complete idiot, you know that? You didn’t have to throw your life away like this."

"Ah, never mind. I won’t insult you anymore…"

"Just rest, you Ironing Board Hero. Leave the rest to me."

"Anything that stands in my way dies in one strike. If they can beat me, then I’d *welcome* the challenge."

Merlin turned to face the Goblin Emperor, who was still bleeding profusely from its severed hand, shielding Alice behind him with a blank expression.

In truth, Alice hadn’t heard a word. Her consciousness was fading in and out, her vision blurry. All she could make out was Merlin’s sturdy back, dependable and unyielding.

For a moment, the silhouette of Elgin, the legendary swordsman she secretly admired, overlapped with Merlin’s. Both figures were so powerful, so resolute, so free of hesitation.

Am I… hallucinating? she wondered. Maybe this was the light at the end of the tunnel. As her mind slipped deeper into unconsciousness, she murmured—

"Did you come to save me again when I was in danger? I… I love you so much…"

Alice, in her delirium, mistook Merlin for Elgin, the great swordsman, coming to her rescue a second time. Little did she know, it was just Merlin himself.

Merlin turned back, glancing at the unconscious Alice on the ground, and muttered in bewilderment, "What the hell is this girl rambling about now?"

"My hand! My kingly power!!!"

"I’m dying! I’m really dying…"

The Goblin Emperor clutched its severed hand, writhing in agony, its expression twisted in despair.

But then, its emotions suddenly stabilized, and a mocking grin spread across its face.

"Just kidding…"

The stump of its arm pulsed, and in a flash, a new, even more muscular arm regenerated. The effects of "Berserk Mode" were truly astonishing.

Merlin watched the Goblin Emperor’s antics in silence, saying nothing. Did it think a severed hand meant death? As if Saint-tier beings were made of tofu.

The Goblin Emperor flexed its regenerated arm a few times, satisfied with the result, then turned its gaze back to Merlin with renewed interest.

It sensed no magic or fighting spirit from him, so it assumed he was just a skilled ordinary man—after all, he had managed to sever its hand so quickly. Still, it didn’t take him seriously.

"You’re different from the others. Normally, when people see me screaming like I’m on death’s door, they’d assume they’ve already won and start cheering. But you… you just stand there, unfazed."

Merlin chuckled, completely at ease. "I get it, I get it. You like watching people’s faces when their expectations are shattered, right? A bit twisted, but unfortunately… I do too."

"Oh? Then we’re kindred spirits, hahahaha…" The Goblin Emperor laughed heartily.

"Yeah, I’ve seen that look so many times it’s gotten a little boring," Merlin said, scratching his head with a grin.

"Might I ask your name?" the Goblin Emperor inquired.

"Call me Little Daisy Brother. Hahahaha…" Merlin had no intention of giving his real name.

"A fine name, hahahaha…" The Goblin Emperor chuckled along.

The two seemed to be having a perfectly civil conversation, but it was all a facade—just a mutual display of bravado that had devolved into awkward small talk.

Suddenly!

The Goblin Emperor swung its spiked club with all its might, crushing toward the smirking Merlin. Saint-tier battle aura surged, and with the boost from Berserk Mode, the strike carried unimaginable force.

Sure enough, the Goblin Emperor couldn’t hold back any longer. Merlin’s smug demeanor had grated on its nerves.

The club cut through the air, hurtling toward Merlin’s face—

Only to be effortlessly parried by one of Merlin’s hands, sending shockwaves rippling through the dust.

The Goblin Emperor’s expression flickered with surprise. It had struck with everything it had, yet Merlin hadn’t so much as flinched. Its gaze darkened.

"You truly are no ordinary man. Might I have the honor of knowing your name?"

Merlin deflected the Goblin Emperor’s club with a flick of his wrist, then sneered—

"Your level?"

"Not worthy of knowing my name."

title: Chapter 86
content:
Chapter 86

Volume 2 · Chapter 86

The Goblin Emperor was on high alert. Even though the human before him showed no signs of magic or battle aura, the fact that he had blocked a full-force strike with just one hand proved that the man was far from ordinary—his strength was not inferior to his own.

For a moment, he even wondered if he himself was a Saint-tier warrior.

The Goblin Emperor suspected Merlin was hiding his true power—he must be, like himself, a powerful Saint-tier warrior.

"You’ve got quite the mouth on you."

"Eh, I’m being honest. You really don’t have the qualifications to know my true name." Merlin clapped his hands, brushing off the dust.

"Perhaps I’ve been impolite. Then allow me to introduce myself first..." The Goblin Emperor placed a hand over his chest and declared proudly, "I am the legitimate royal blood of the goblins, the ruler of this entire underground palace, and one of the thirteen emperors of the goblin race—Saggs the Fifth, King of the Goblins."

The goblin race had thirteen branches. Before human civilization rose, the world was filled with heteroclite races, but now almost all of them had migrated to the Southern United Kingdom.

Saggs’ lineage had not migrated. They had ruled this small place for generations, which was quite rare.

But Merlin wasn’t here to listen to history. He had no interest in the Goblin Emperor’s introduction. What he found utterly contemptible was one thing—

"A king? The leader of inferior creatures dares to call himself a king?"

Merlin’s arrogance was ingrained in his bones. He looked down on goblins with utter disdain.

Though he had the heart of a human and believed in equality, his essence was still that of a demon—a noble and haughty monarch.

Demons typically looked down on other races, and as the supreme king, Merlin’s thoughts carried the traits of the demon race.

"What did you say?" The goblin narrowed his eyes, feeling deeply insulted. "Why are you so arrogant?"

"Hah, listen carefully. Under normal circumstances, creatures like you wouldn’t even have the chance to gaze upon my radiance. The fact that I’m even speaking to you should make you proud." Though Merlin was shorter than the enraged Goblin Emperor, his presence was on an entirely different level, the gap overwhelming.

"You... a human... how dare you be so arrogant?" The Goblin Emperor pointed at himself, his voice booming with fury. "Who gave you the confidence to speak to me, the king of the goblins, with such contempt?!"

"Enough with the nonsense. Start your performance. Let me see how strong you are—whether you’re even worthy of making me draw my sword." Merlin stood in place, his lips curling in disdain.

"I am the pride of the goblin race, the youngest Saint-tier goblin in history. My speed, strength, and wisdom are all at their peak! Soon, I will launch a grand assault, unify Wales, and become the new master of humanity!" The Goblin Emperor painted a grand vision, trying to persuade him. "If you’re willing, I can make you my chancellor—second only to me, above all others!"

"Pfft! Hahaha!" Merlin couldn’t hold back his laughter. He felt like he was looking at an idiot. As a haughty demon monarch, why would he lower himself to become a goblin’s chancellor? The very idea was ridiculous.

"What’s so funny?" The Goblin Emperor narrowed his eyes, feeling that he had already lowered himself enough, yet the other party didn’t seem grateful at all.

"Take a good look at yourselves—you’re nothing but lowly worms! How dare you even think of recruiting me? Where do you get the courage?" Merlin pointed to the sky, his voice dripping with arrogance. "In this world, no one can stand above me. Even if the Goddess of Light herself descended, she wouldn’t be able to endure a single fraction of my radiance! Turning you into fertilizer for my garden would be an insult to me..."

The Goblin Emperor’s breath hitched, his heart pounding with rage. Someone this arrogant had to be at a certain level—it seemed the entire world was beneath his contempt, with not a shred of humility.

How could someone this arrogant become so strong? It was unfair.

"I swear by the name of the Goblin Emperor, I will personally send you, this arrogant fool, to hell!"

"Go ahead, give me your best performance. Just don’t disappoint me."

Merlin smirked, his hand resting on the katana at his waist. Though he was in a combat-ready state, his entire body was riddled with openings.

"Yah!"

The Goblin Emperor roared, channeling his Saint-tier battle aura without restraint. A golden flame of aura ignited over his crimson skin—he was clearly taking this seriously.

With a sudden leap, he raised his spiked club and swung down with all his might.

Merlin didn’t even blink. With one hand, he effortlessly blocked the strike.

His *Magic Immunity* couldn’t defend against physical attacks, but while he could take the hit, he didn’t want to stand there like an idiot and let himself get pummeled—he had an image to maintain.

"Waaaaahhhh!"

The Goblin Emperor was furious. Unwilling to accept defeat, he launched a relentless barrage of strikes without pause.

His Saint-tier aura raged violently, his face twisted in fury, his eyes burning with rage.

The Goblin Emperor swung his spiked club continuously, each strike infused with the full force of his Saint-tier aura. The speed was so absurd that the weapon itself was invisible—only afterimages remained.

The storm of attacks never ceased, their ferocity staggering, like a pile driver operating at an impossibly high frequency.

The air was filled with the dull sounds of impact, each strike sending shockwaves that whipped up fierce gusts of wind.

Merlin remained expressionless. He hadn’t moved an inch from his original position.

With one hand, he casually deflected every attack from the Goblin Emperor, perfectly shielding the unconscious Alice behind him.

Why?

Why was this man so composed?

Why were his full-power attacks having no effect?

Was he truly being looked down upon from the core...

Who *was* this man? His strength seemed boundless!

The Goblin Emperor’s heart was now filled with dread. He had never encountered anyone this terrifying.

He was a Saint-tier warrior, an absolute powerhouse—yet he was completely helpless against a man with no magic or battle aura?!

The Goblin Emperor was drenched in sweat. His aura was depleting rapidly. If this continued, it wouldn’t end well. He had to use his ultimate technique to finish this quickly.

Suddenly, the Goblin Emperor stopped his assault and leaped to the center of the hall, seemingly preparing something.

Merlin spread his hands, sighing. "That’s it? Is this all you’ve got? Truly disappointing. You might be a fake Saint-tier warrior."

"Stupid human! You’ll find out soon enough if I’m fake!" The Goblin Emperor stood in the center of the hall, raising his spiked club and assuming a charging stance.

"Oh? You still have a trump card? Let’s see it..." Merlin wanted to know just how strong his opponent was at his peak. Maybe there would be an unexpected surprise—

"This might be the last time you show your face, so give it your all..."
