title: Chapter 87
content:
Chapter 87

Volume 2 · Chapter 87

"Arrogant human, I admit you're strong, and worthy of my full power, but I must say, you will die by your own arrogance." The Goblin Emperor glared at Merlin, concentrating all his battle energy as he spoke. "Next, I will display the ultimate technique of the Goblin race. You better watch closely."

"Ultimate technique? Oh? Do your best..." Merlin showed a slight flicker of interest.

An ultimate technique was a special ability unique to those who had reached Saint-tier. It wouldn't be an exaggeration to call it a super finisher—an attack born from countless refinements, the most persuasive display of strength.

While one could gauge strength directly from their tier, the power of an ultimate technique was the true measure.

A Saint-tier who hadn't cultivated their own ultimate technique was nothing but an empty shell of strength, unable to stand among the very best.

"This is a martial art passed down through generations of our lineage. I haven't used it in many years because its power is too overwhelming—difficult to control. It instantly kills whoever it hits, and the backlash can even harm my own kind. Worst of all..." The Goblin Emperor spoke gravely, "every time I use it, my *ding ding* shrinks by a centimeter."

"Emmmm..." Merlin instinctively glanced at the Goblin Emperor's crotch, thinking, *What a massive side effect... must be incredibly powerful... probably?*

"But for you, even if my *ding ding* shrinks by ten centimeters today, I will use the strongest ultimate technique of the Goblin race to kill you here! Let you pay the painful price for your arrogance!" The Goblin Emperor seemed ready, preparing to strike Merlin down with his most powerful attack.

"Oh." Merlin's expression remained blank, his response indifferent, as if he hadn't even registered the Goblin Emperor's boastful rant.

"Tch! Take this! Ultimate Technique: Goblin Heavy Hammer!!!"

The Goblin Emperor roared, leaping into the air. His obese body spun and rolled midair, tracing a perfect arc.

Merlin's expression was complex—it was hard to imagine the absurd sight of a fat man rolling through the sky.

The Goblin Emperor descended from above, charging with the ferocious momentum of the Goblin's ultimate technique, the Heavy Hammer.

He wielded his wolf-tooth club, which was now imbued with burning Saint-tier battle energy, flickering like golden flames.

The Goblin Emperor's face twisted in a grimace, convinced of his victory. After all, no one had ever withstood this attack head-on. And Merlin hadn't moved—no sign of evasion, as if he intended to take the blow directly.

Was he trying to protect the unconscious woman behind him?

Hmph! In the end, this guy would be undone by his own mercy!

In truth, the Goblin Emperor was overestimating Merlin. The reason Merlin didn't dodge was because he felt no pressure at all.

Merlin, his face cold, raised a hand to shield his forehead and braced to take the Goblin Emperor's ultimate Heavy Hammer head-on!

A violent collision erupted, the might of Saint-tier oppressing everything in its path.

The shockwave sent countless fragments of stone raining down like a storm.

The ground beneath Merlin's feet cracked with a *craaaack*, a large fissure spreading outward.

Yet, in the end, this grand ultimate technique was still blocked by Merlin's single hand. He didn't even blink—clearly, he hadn't taken it seriously.

"Wh... what?!"
The Goblin Emperor stood there, mouth agape in shock, unable to believe the result. He had poured all his strength into that attack, yet Merlin hadn't so much as shifted his stance!

This transcendent power was beyond comprehension!

"Hah, that look of shock on your face—I've seen it so many times. I never thought *you* would make it too..."

As the aftershocks faded, Merlin stood there, one arm propping up the massive wolf-tooth club, completely unharmed. His clothes were a little tattered, his sleeves torn away, revealing solid, well-defined arms.

"I always thought my sister was the weakest among the Saint-tier, but you're even weaker than her. What a disappointment..."

"Y... y... you... who the hell *are* you?!" The Goblin Emperor trembled in terror, taking a step back. "No one this powerful can be a nobody!"

"The truth is, I'm not that strong. You're just too weak—unworthy of the title of King! You don't even deserve to stand on the same stage as me!"

Merlin's hand rested on the katana at his waist, his ruby-like eyes narrowing.

"Y... Your Excellency, spare me! I'll be your slave!"

The Goblin Emperor was petrified, his obese body shaking violently, desperate to trade his dignity for a sliver of life.

"Don't degrade yourself. My slaves aren't as weak as you. Keep what little pride you have left and turn to dust!"

Merlin's crimson gaze flashed, and an absolute, kingly pressure surged forth like a tidal wave.

With a soft *shing*, he drew his blade—

The Goblin Emperor instantly lost all signs of life, bisected in an instant by Merlin's iaijutsu slash. Blood sprayed from the clean cut like a funnel.

His face still bore an expression of terror as his obese body collapsed in two, flopping to the sides like wet mud.

Merlin didn't even glance at the gory scene. Instead, he flicked the blood from his katana and sheathed it.

"Looks like there are no more strong enemies left. Time to head back..."

Merlin had just taken a step forward when a dazzling golden light caught his eye—the Goblin Emperor's golden throne, piled high with countless gold coins.

*What the hell...*

*Am I about to make a comeback from rags to riches?*

*All these coins are mine, right?*

*Heh heh, looks like I'll be living in a luxurious castle, hiring a bunch of maids, and just coasting through life~*

Merlin had only taken one step forward when the entire underground palace began to tremble. Chunks of stone and dust rained down—it was collapsing.

The initial damage Alice had caused to the palace's support pillars had destabilized the structure, and now, under the strain, it was finally giving way.

But that wasn't the main issue. The underground palace was connected to the rear mountain—if it collapsed, the entire mountain would come down with it. The situation was critical.

Merlin greedily eyed the gold coins, then turned to look at the unconscious Alice.

If he moved quickly, he could take a lot with him. But if he wasted time, he wouldn't be able to escape with Alice.

It wouldn't matter if *he* got buried, but Alice was different. Her body wasn't strong enough—if she were buried alive here, she'd die for sure.

On one side: a life of luxury and comfort.

On the other: his beautiful, precious wife.

*This is fucking awkward...*

Merlin found himself stuck in a dilemma, unable to decide.

The rear mountain continued to tremble—time was running out.

*Wife or money? This needs serious thought.*

If he took the gold, he'd probably just lose it all at the races.

But if he saved Alice, he'd get a steady job that could both make money *and* ease his curse.

Now that he thought about it...

Merlin abruptly turned, scooped up Alice, and bolted for the exit. At his speed, he could still make it out in time.

Holding his wife, his figure became a blur, moving at an astonishing pace.

As Merlin distanced himself from the throne of gold coins, his heart bled. He couldn't help but shout in frustration:

"Damn it, Alice! You're the bane of my existence!"

"Do you have any idea how much gold you just cost me?!"

"If you don't get me a job when we get back, I'm not letting this go!"

"Fuck me, today is *such* a shitty day..."

(っ╥╯﹏╰╥c)

title: Chapter 88
content:
Chapter 88

Volume 2 · Chapter 88

Late at night.

The rain had stopped, the dark clouds dispersed, and the stars filled the sky.

The escaping villagers met with the rescuing villagers.

They embraced each other, tears streaming down their faces.

Suddenly, the earth trembled and the mountains shook. The towering rear mountain collapsed with a thunderous roar, as if a large section had been suddenly carved away.

"Mom, will Uncle Merlin and big sister be okay?" Little Henry tugged at Martha's hand, worry in his heart.

"They'll be fine. Merlin is a very clever man, he'll definitely turn danger into safety." Martha smiled, though she herself was also uncertain.

Just as mother and son were worrying about Merlin, a figure emerged from the depths of the forest, carrying a silver-haired girl.

"I'm back, safe and sound, and I even rescued her..."

Merlin wore a bitter smile, his heart aching for those gold coins. To others, it looked like the relief of having done his best.

"As long as you're okay, I was so worried. I thought you..." Martha sighed in relief, unable to help but cover her face and weep, probably from joy.

"Uncle Merlin, you're super amazing! I admire you more and more!" Little Henry ran up and hugged Merlin's leg, rubbing against it. "You actually managed to bring big sister back!"

"To think you really rescued her. You're not just a useless pretty boy after all, you've got some skills!" Johnson looked at Merlin with newfound respect.

Though he didn't know what method Merlin had used, he guessed that Alice and the Goblin Emperor must have fought to a draw, and Merlin had taken the opportunity to rescue Alice.

Even so, it was still impressive!

If Merlin said he had also killed the Goblin Emperor, probably no one would believe him.

"Merlin, I misjudged you before. You're actually a decent person. From now on, I won't stop my old mother from looking after your business anymore." The village chief was also amazed.

More and more people gathered around, showering him with praise.

Merlin could only smile bitterly, feeling awkward as he thought to himself—

Damn those heroics!

I’m never going to be a hero on a whim again.

Please, just give me back my billions of gold coins!

( ?? ﹏ ?? )

◆

Merlin carried Alice back to the tavern with Martha and her son.

Martha sent her son upstairs, saying she needed to give him a bath as he was filthy.

Merlin carried Alice all the way, feeling that her injuries were serious. If she didn’t receive treatment, she might be in danger.

He had abandoned so many things for the sake of his adventurer’s job. He couldn’t let Alice, his referrer, die—otherwise, he’d suffer a huge loss.

Now that the disaster was over, it would be hard to find a doctor or priest to treat Alice. So Merlin had to do it himself.

"Sister Martha, can you give me the key to Alice’s room?"

Merlin stated it plainly, without hesitation.

Martha hesitated. Handing over a female guest’s room key to a man was a serious breach of duty.

But considering everything that had happened, it was clear that Merlin and Alice had something going on—maybe they were even a couple.

And thinking about Merlin’s usual flirtatious behavior, what did he want the key for? It was obvious.

Martha handed the key to Merlin and said something meaningful.

"Keep the noise down tonight. Be gentle with Miss Alice."

Merlin’s expression turned strange, his feelings complicated—

Was there a hidden meaning in that?

No, no, I’m not going to do anything weird!

Don’t insult my healer’s intentions, okay?

Besides, I’m not interested in flat chests.

Seriously, where is Martha’s mind going?

Do I look like that kind of person?

(?-_?)??

◆

Inside the room.

Merlin tossed Alice onto the bed, an unconsciously lecherous grin spreading across his face.

"hiahiahia~"

"Serves you right for always being so mean to me."

"Now look at you, completely at my mercy~"

"Finally, the moment of revenge has come. Let’s see how I play with your body, ohohoho..."

"First, let’s strip you naked. Wax, whips, pepper spray—the full set~"

Merlin muttered to himself over Alice’s unconscious body, then pounced on his old rival like a starving tiger. His hands worked quickly, stripping off her outerwear and skirt with a series of snaps and rustles. In no time, poor Alice was nearly stripped bare, her alluring, fair-skinned body left with only a three-piece set covering the essentials.

Truthfully, Merlin had no interest in looking. What was there to see in a flat board? His own bare chest might look the same as hers—completely unexciting.

Merlin examined Alice beneath him, as if inspecting something.

Alice lay sprawled on the bed, unresponsive. Her cascading silver hair was scattered around her, looking messy. Her face was deathly pale, clearly from her injuries, and her flat chest rose and fell with each breath.

If not for her flatness, her figure would have been considered sexy—tall and slender.

Below her flat stomach, her legs were long and white enough to keep someone entertained for years. They looked tempting.

But to Merlin, who had lived for 200 years and seen through the illusions of the world, none of this held much appeal.

"Listen, Flatboard, what I’m about to do is absolutely not taking advantage of you. It’s for your treatment. As the saying goes, ‘no shame in medicine.’ If I have to expose a little, then so be it. Besides, I have no interest in you, got it?"

Merlin’s position, pinning Alice beneath him, made his words completely unconvincing. No matter how you looked at it, this was the kind of scene that would attract the vice squad.

Alice’s delicate eyebrows knitted slightly, her eyes tightly shut. Her breath brushed against Merlin’s face. In her unconscious state, she couldn’t respond, making it seem as if she was too exhausted to resist, leaving herself at Merlin’s mercy.

"Alright, if you don’t say anything, I’ll take that as consent."

Ignoring Alice’s lack of response, Merlin seemed ready to get to work.

"Cough, cough, cough..."

Merlin straightened up on Alice’s body, his throat making a phlegm-clearing sound.

Don’t get the wrong idea—this wasn’t to humiliate Alice. He was gathering saliva.

Merlin’s method of treatment, of course, was his own saliva.

Don’t forget, Merlin was a succubus. Even without the typical traits of a succubus, his constitution remained. He could attract the opposite sex, and his saliva had healing properties for their bodies—though it also had some... stimulating side effects.

Next, Merlin aimed at Alice’s body and sprayed saliva wildly to treat her.

As for the effect? Merlin was the Great Demon Lord—how could the effect be anything but extraordinary?

After preparing for a long time, Merlin looked down at Alice beneath him and said—

"Here we go! Saliva Shot, one hundred rapid-fire!"

"Ptoo, ptoo, ptoo, ptoo, ptoo, ptoo, ptoo, ptoo, ptoo..."

Merlin’s mouth worked like a machine gun, frantically spitting saliva at Alice’s wounds. The scene was too beautiful to behold.

The once-great Hero, now being humiliated by the Demon Lord’s saliva—truly a pitiful sight.

The aphrodisiac effect of the saliva took hold, causing Alice’s body to react strangely. Her fair skin began to flush a rosy pink.

Her long, beautiful legs trembled slightly, the inner thighs rubbing together oddly.

Alice seemed uncomfortable. Her entire body trembled lightly, and she let out a series of questionable sounds—

"Mmm... Hah~"

"Ahh... Mmm..."

"Hah... Ah... Nngh..."

Merlin watched Alice’s strange reactions and appearance, his forehead covered in black lines. He thought to himself, *So this is why I shouldn’t casually spit on the opposite sex—the aphrodisiac effect is so awkward when it kicks in.*

It seemed there was some reason Alice had called him a lecherous Demon Lord.

At this moment, Alice looked as if she had been drenched, performing a wet, seductive dance before Merlin.

Her entire body was covered in his saliva, looking sticky. It had even soaked through her underwear, clinging to her fair skin, becoming semi-transparent, revealing some... harmonious scenes.

Alice’s current state was like that of a woman in the throes of passion, her ivory skin glistening—it was almost too much to look at.

Merlin, seeing this, was as if he had seen a ghost. Alice’s reactions were far more sensitive than the average person’s.

He swore he had no ill intentions, but this aphrodisiac effect was troublesome. Fortunately, Alice was unconscious; otherwise, she might have pounced on him, demanding intimacy. For now, all he could do was leave this flat-chested Hero to her fate.

Merlin had intended to leave, but then he noticed Alice’s chest—her bra was gradually turning dark red.

He had no choice but to lower his head for a closer look, and in the process, he flicked the two large chest pads onto the wall.

Look at that—sure enough, they were fake. Just as flat as ever, not the slightest hint of a curve. Probably always would be. Even tailors refused to sell her bras because they couldn’t recoup the material costs...

Merlin grumbled viciously in his mind. Slowly, he lifted Alice’s bra, revealing an undiscovered wound.

Probably a scratch from her battle with the Goblin Emperor.

Alice panted repeatedly, seemingly in pain. This was the most serious injury.

Merlin lifted his head, staring at the ceiling, his expression extremely conflicted—

I swear I’ve been weaned for a long time. This situation is awkward for me too.

But for the sake of my new job, I have to lower myself and do this to this flat board...

"Cough, cough, cough... Ptoo~?"

◆

In the bathroom.

Martha was drying her son’s muddy body with a towel when she suddenly heard a "tragic scream" from Alice’s room.

"YAAAAAAAAAAH~?"

Martha dropped the towel on the floor, her heart filled with awkwardness. She had told Merlin to keep it down, but it was still this loud.

This scream was different from an ordinary one—it made people’s imaginations run wild.

Little Henry was also startled. He asked in surprise, "Mom, what’s wrong with big sister? Did Uncle Merlin hit her? She sounds like a pig being slaughtered."

"Don’t talk nonsense..." Martha fiercely knocked her son’s head, her face slightly red as she warned—

"Children shouldn’t speculate about adult matters..."

title: Chapter 89 — Crunch Time 9
content:
Chapter 89 — Crunch Time 9

Volume 2 · Chapter 89

The next day.

Alice’s room.

After the disaster, the villagers began rebuilding.

The storm seemed to have passed, and everything was proceeding in an orderly fashion.

The setting sun streamed in through the window, outside a bright, clear sky.

Alice, dressed in a nightgown, lay quietly on the sickbed, her external injuries mostly healed.

It seemed the succubus’s saliva was truly effective—even better than healing magic. Such severe wounds had recovered in just one night.

Her unconscious mind gradually stirring, Alice slowly opened her eyes and saw a somewhat familiar ceiling.

She slowly sat up in bed, her whole body aching, making her frown.

“This is… my room?”

Alice pressed a hand to her throbbing head and tried to recall. She remembered being struck by the Goblin Emperor’s spiked club, and then… nothing.

After that, she thought she saw the legendary swordsman Elgin, but now that she thought about it, that was probably just a near-death hallucination.

Finally… she seemed to have had an extremely embarrassing spring dream. She couldn’t remember who it was, but it felt like they had subjected her to some kind of neglect play.

Just then, Martha entered carrying a towel and a washbasin. Seeing Alice awake, she smiled and said, “Lady Alice, you’re awake?”

“Mmm.” Alice replied, still a little dazed.

“I was so worried about you last night.” Martha quickly set down the basin and sat beside Alice. “Lady Alice, please don’t do such dangerous things again. We’re all very grateful to you, but putting yourself in danger isn’t wise. If you had died saving us, we would have been overwhelmed with guilt.”

“It’s fine, I’m okay. And you were saved too—this is the best outcome.” Alice shook her head with a smile, then asked, “I remember passing out in the underground palace. Who rescued me?”

“Oh, Lady Alice, you really should thank Merlin properly. He’s the one who pulled you out of danger.” Martha said, still shaken by the memory.

“Y-you… what?” Alice’s eyes widened, as if she had misheard.

“It… it was Merlin who saved you…” Martha didn’t understand why Alice was so shocked.

“Eh!!!”

Alice’s expression was indescribable—a mix of horror and disgust.

She simply couldn’t believe it. That foul-mouthed, lazy, utterly indifferent Lucifer the Third had actually taken the initiative to save her?!

This defied all logic! Merlin was the pinnacle of evil, the Great Demon Lord, while she was the embodiment of justice, the Hero of Light. Even if they were no longer on opposing sides, they were still spiritual enemies. How could he have saved her? It was utterly incomprehensible!

Unless… she had fed him too many croton seeds and fried his brain? That actually seemed possible…

“Lady Alice?” Martha called out.

“Hm? What is it?” Alice snapped back to reality, still puzzled over why Merlin would save her.

“Nothing, it’s just… I feel like you and Merlin have some conflicts, but everyone makes mistakes. You can’t deny someone the chance to change, right? Besides, the way Merlin carried you out of the ruins last night… it was really impressive.” Martha tried to mend their relationship.

In Martha’s eyes, Merlin and Alice were probably ex-lovers who had broken up after a quarrel, clearly still pining for each other.

“Haha… well…” Alice forced a dry laugh, wondering what any of that had to do with her.

“You two are old lovers, right? Staying at odds like this isn’t good. Why not take this opportunity to make up?” Martha, like a seasoned matchmaker, kept urging Alice.

“No, we’re not old lovers…” Alice’s expression turned complicated. She and Merlin were clearly arch-nemeses, weren’t they? How had this turned into a misunderstanding about them being ex-lovers?

“I understand, I understand. Lady Alice is so young, of course you’d be shy about it~” Martha wore a knowing smile.

“I…” Alice was exhausted. She didn’t have the energy to explain. The more she tried, the worse it got.

She settled down to think carefully. Even though she found Merlin insufferable, and that bastard had constantly disrupted her life, now that she was no longer the Hero, all of that seemed like old grudges. She had been endlessly holding onto her resentment toward him.

But Merlin really was despicable. She wouldn’t forgive him for that.

Yet the fact remained—he had saved her. As a former Hero, being rescued by a Demon Lord was a humiliating disgrace. She absolutely could not owe him this favor; she had to repay it somehow.

As a former Hero, how could she possibly owe a Demon Lord a debt of gratitude?

The thought of having to lower herself before a Demon Lord was infuriating…

After turning it over in her mind, Alice reluctantly decided to thank Merlin.

No matter what, he had saved her, and that was a debt. As someone with noble principles, Alice felt she had to express her gratitude—albeit very reluctantly.

“Sister Martha…”

“Hmm?”

“Can you call Merlin here?”

◆

The marketplace after the disaster.

Though it no longer had the bustle of the day before, under the village chief’s leadership, the rebuilding was progressing quickly.

At that moment, Merlin had come out to buy alcohol and noticed a crowd gathered ahead. Curious, he walked over, only to see—

“Hello, everyone! I’m Bella, a reporter for the London Post.”

A middle-aged blonde woman held a magical recording device, speaking eloquently, while an assistant beside her took notes and projected images.

“Yesterday, a massive goblin army was discovered in the mountains behind this village—so numerous they threatened all of Wales. My village was the first target, but the brave villagers fought back and averted a major crisis for Wales. Today, we’ll be interviewing these heroes…”

The village chief, on the other side, could barely contain himself. His hair was meticulously styled, and he was dressed like a minor landowner, polished to perfection.

“Chief, could you tell us about the situation at the time?” Bella extended the microphone toward him.

“Ah… well, the situation was extremely urgent. But as a subject of Great Britain, I always remember Queen Elizabeth’s teachings—to rise up and fight back. Under my wise leadership, the entire village charged up the mountain and crushed the enemy like a hot knife through butter…”

The chief launched into a half-hour-long boast. In short, every achievement was his doing. Without his wisdom, the villagers would have been in disarray. He praised himself to the skies.

“I see, I see… I get the general idea.” Reporter Bella broke into a sweat, not wanting to hear any more. She awkwardly asked, “Were there any particularly outstanding heroes in this battle?”

“Ah… yes, there were.” The chief pulled forward a man named Johnson. “This is Johnson, a lower-tier warrior—our hero!”

“Alright, Mr. Johnson, what was the situation when you faced the goblin army?” Bella handed the microphone to Johnson.

“It was extremely dangerous, but as the village’s only strong warrior, I couldn’t retreat. I deeply embraced the mission of justice. As a Briton, I couldn’t let Queen Elizabeth down in a critical moment. The situation was incredibly perilous. I charged through the sea of flames, punching the Grand Vizier Gegaw, kicking Emperor Saggs—it was absolutely badass…”

Johnson began his own half-hour boast. The gist was that he was the toughest, the most amazing, and without him, the goblin army couldn’t have been wiped out.

Merlin, watching from below, was speechless. He held up both hands, forming the number “6” and repeatedly tapping them together—

666!

( .? ?? ?)

title: Chapter 90 — Burnout Countdown 8
content:
Chapter 90 — Burnout Countdown 8

Volume 2 · Chapter 90

On stage, Strongson sprayed spittle everywhere as he spoke.

From the audience, boos erupted from time to time.

After all, minor characters were always eager to steal the credit. If Queen Elizabeth was pleased, who knew—she might even grant a minor noble title.

Reporter Bella could barely stand it. She had come for explosive material, not to listen to someone brag.

"Alright, alright, due to time constraints, our interview is about to end. Mr. Strongson, do you have any final words?"

"Oh, I do..." Strongson turned to the camera, striking a philosophical pose as he declared with forceful conviction—

"Today, you might be a sissy!"

"But it's okay, there's still hope!"

"Join Strongson's Fitness Club!"

"One week of training, and you'll reclaim your manly vigor!"

"See these muscles? They symbolize power!"

"Tomorrow! You too will radiate the essence of MAN!"

Merlin slapped his forehead, his eyes stinging from the cringe.

Sigh... after all that work.

Seems like all the credit got stolen.

But honestly, *I* should be the one with the biggest contribution, right?

Capitalism truly was vile and treacherous.

Ah well, only petty people cared about empty fame.

As a proud and arrogant ruler, he wouldn’t stoop to fighting over it!

Merlin grabbed his drink and turned to leave, though inside, he was seething with envy. If he’d just arrived a little earlier, none of this would’ve happened.

Even if Merlin had announced he’d taken down the emperor himself, no one would’ve believed him. In the villagers’ eyes, Alice was the true hero.

Reporter Bella pushed through the crowd, sighing. These interviews were useless—no juicy details, just official fluff.

Just as she was about to leave, she noticed Merlin’s desolate, slightly disappointed figure, as if he’d lost all hope in society.

Bella was an experienced journalist. Often, it was these disillusioned types who spilled the best secrets.

"Sir, please wait a moment."

Bella waved over her crew and approached for an interview.

"Hm?" Merlin turned, surprised.

"Do you have any insider information about the village attack?" Bella extended the microphone.

Merlin faced the camera, his expression unreadable—complex, with a hint of world-weariness.

"I don’t know about the rest, but if heaven gave me a chance to choose again... I’d pick gold coins."

Bella froze, completely baffled by Merlin’s statement.

But as a seasoned journalist, what was she best at? Twisting the truth, of course!

"Ladies and gentlemen, the truth is out—this was all a farce staged by the village chief and the villagers, complete with paid actors, just to hype up the village’s fame. This gentleman here, for example, didn’t take the chief’s money and was left out in the cold. Look at his weary, heartbroken expression—it’s clear he’s lost all faith in society. Is this the distortion of human nature? Or the decay of morality..."

Merlin’s face darkened as he stared at the chattering middle-aged woman beside him, thinking—

What the hell?!

Is she insane...?

◆

Merlin finally escaped the brain-dead reporter’s harassment.

Back at the tavern, Martha informed him that Alice wanted to see him.

A small smile tugged at Merlin’s lips. This had to be about new work. He needed to make sure Alice handled things properly for him.

When Merlin arrived upstairs, he found someone had beaten him there—the Silver-ranked adventurers, Smith and Cecil.

The two were leaving today to return home and get married, so they’d come to express their gratitude to Alice and say goodbye.

Swordsman Smith was still injured, his entire body wrapped in bandages, leaning on a crutch while Cecil supported him.

Merlin stood at the doorway, not intruding on the moment.

"Lady Alice, thank you!" the soon-to-be newlyweds bowed deeply in unison.

"Please, don’t—" Alice, lying in bed, waved her hands frantically, looking flustered. "I’m just glad you two are safe."

"We *have* to express our thanks," Smith said earnestly. "If you hadn’t stepped in to help, we might not have made it this far."

"I didn’t do much. The only reason we made it is because of *your* willpower," Alice said awkwardly.

"No, you’re our savior. We’ll never forget this kindness," Smith declared firmly.

"Alright, I get it, but can you *please* lift your heads?" Alice pleaded, truly uncomfortable with the situation.

Only when Alice accepted their gratitude did the two slowly straighten up.

"Lady Alice, I’m truly sorry," Cecil said, guilt weighing heavily on her. "Back then, I didn’t know how to help. I left you there alone to suffer such serious injuries... Please forgive my cowardice."

"It’s fine. I went to save you, after all. If something had happened to you, I wouldn’t have been able to fulfill Smith’s request," Alice said with a smile.

"But..." Cecil hesitated, still unable to forgive herself.

"Don’t dwell on it. Running away was the right choice. If you’d stayed, you would’ve only held me back. Isn’t it best that everyone’s safe now?" Alice reassured her.

The two fell silent, staring at Alice’s hands with complicated emotions.

"By the way, you two are going home to get married, right?" Alice tried to lighten the mood by bringing up happier news.

"Yeah, that’s right," Smith glanced at Cecil. "We’re getting married. We won’t be adventurers anymore."

"Really?" Alice nodded, offering her blessings. "Congratulations. After the storm, there’s always a rainbow. Even through disaster, you made it through together."

The two exchanged a glance, their faces flushing as they grinned foolishly.

Alice awkwardly averted her gaze, thinking, *Damn these two idiots. Get out of here! I don’t want to deal with their lovey-dovey crap right after recovering from a serious injury...*

"Lady Alice, this is a small token of our gratitude. Please accept it." Cecil placed a small pouch of gold coins into Alice’s hand.

"I can’t take this!" Alice refused. She hadn’t acted for money.

"Please, just take it. It’s not much, but it’s our sincere thanks," Smith insisted stubbornly.

Alice considered her situation—she hadn’t earned any money from this job, and the target she was supposed to capture was Merlin, whom she couldn’t exactly bring in. Then she remembered her rent in Lexham was due soon. This would solve her immediate problem.

"...Alright, thank you."

Standing at the doorway, Merlin leaned against the wall, expressionless, thinking—

She was just a self-righteous fool.

And yet, people admired her.

Being a hero... didn’t seem so bad.

He couldn’t help but feel a little envious of Alice.

title: Chapter 91 — Burnout Countdown 7
content:
Chapter 91 — Burnout Countdown 7

Volume 2 · Chapter 91

Smith and Cecil left.

Alice held the still-warm gold coin in her hand, gazing out the window.

She thought this was the most dangerous thing she had done in the past year.

Though it had left her battered and bruised, she didn’t regret it—she was even glad she had no lingering regrets.

Alice figured the reason for her terrible luck was still tied to Merlin.

That’s right, it was all that bastard Merlin’s fault! He was the one who had sent her luck plummeting.

But in her most desperate, helpless moment, it was that damn teammate who had saved her. This… left Alice deeply conflicted.

"Yo, Alice feeling better?" Merlin walked in, greeting her right off the bat.

"Uh!" Alice’s expression froze, her good mood vanishing instantly. Sure enough, the moment she saw Merlin, her face darkened.

"I heard from Sister Martha that you were looking for me? What’s up?" Merlin unceremoniously dragged over a stool, striking a pose as if expecting gratitude.

"%//8/+h?~" Alice mumbled something incoherent with her back turned to him.

"Huh?! What did you say? I can’t hear you…" Merlin furrowed his brows.

"I said!" Alice knitted her delicate brows, reluctantly, "Since you went through so much trouble to save me, I’ll *force myself* to thank you, okay? But don’t get the wrong idea—this is just my mouth saying thanks. My heart still despises you! Humph~!"

What the—

This script is all wrong!

What kind of spoiled attitude is this?

Why is this girl thanking me with her nose in the air?

Merlin furrowed his brows, not particularly bothered by her tone.

"So… you’re thanking me?"

"Yeah, I am." Alice pouted, her tone terrible.

"I don’t accept. I need you to repay me. I can’t just save you for nothing…" Merlin spread his hands.

"What do you mean?" Alice glared at Merlin, suspecting extortion. Demons really were demons.

"I want to become an adventurer. Can you recommend me?" Merlin cut straight to the point.

"Read my lips." Alice cursed at him, "G, U, N!"

"But I’m your lifesaver. You can’t treat me like this…" Merlin shrugged helplessly.

"Uh… I…" Alice was at a loss for words, her expression turning complicated. She thought—

Damn it!

Why do I feel like I’ve been played?

Σ( ° △ °|||)︴

"You… you actually have the nerve to openly demand repayment?! How rude!"

Alice’s chest heaved with rage, as if she wanted to rush over and slap him twice.

Normal people would be polite, refusing repayment or at least hinting at it indirectly.

But Merlin was different—he outright demanded she repay him.

"Why *can’t* I demand repayment? Did I save you for free? We’re not related, and I had no obligation to save you. Asking for something in return is only natural, isn’t it?"

Merlin held his hands out, his reasoning so sound that Alice was left speechless.

"You… you you you…" Alice’s shoulders trembled with fury. And here she had *forced herself* to say thanks—she was such an idiot. Everything came with a price.

"I I I I… what about me? I’m not asking for your money. All I want is for you to recommend me at the Adventurers Guild so I can get a new job. This isn’t repayment for a favor—it’s a *transaction*…" Merlin urged Alice to help.

Demons loved transactions, and they never made a deal that didn’t benefit them. Without a clear chain of profit, they wouldn’t lift a finger.

Just like summoning demons through contracts—without sufficient cost, nothing could be activated.

Alice recalled the nature of demons and couldn’t help but feel a pang of regret. It seemed this wasn’t something a simple "thank you" could resolve. She had to satisfy this demon Merlin’s desires.

But Alice was stubborn. Repaying a demon? She’d rather die.

"I won’t help. Sure, you saved me, but I don’t *want* to do anything for you! And I never asked you to save me, did I? You came offering help on your own. This transaction is void!"

"Alright, alright~" Merlin clapped his hands with a grin. Dealing with someone as stubborn as Alice, force wouldn’t do much good. Better to apply external pressure—especially when her pride was already under siege. "You won’t help me? Fine. Tomorrow, I’ll tell all the bards that the 233rd generation Hero Alice is ungrateful, that she treats her savior with disdain, that she’s nothing but a shameless ingrate."

"What?!" Alice jumped in shock. She cared deeply about her reputation. Already tarnished, adding the label of "ingrate" would be unbearable. "Who’s the ingrate? *You’re* the ingrate, okay?!"

"I saved you in good faith, and yet you… tsk tsk tsk…" Merlin clicked his tongue, shaking his head, launching a sarcastic attack.

Alice’s face flushed red, her dignity under threat. "If you dare slander my reputation, I’ll make you regret it!"

"Are you threatening me? Look at yourself…" Merlin furrowed his brows, lifting his rear as if to leave. "Since you’re so stubborn, I won’t say another word. Tomorrow, I’ll make sure all of Great Britain knows Hero Alice is a heartless, unprincipled ingrate…"

"Don’t… don’t go!" Alice panicked, looking troubled. "It’s… it’s not that I won’t help you, it’s just that you owe so much money you can’t become one."

"Hah, do you take me for a fool? I only owe a few ten thousand gold coins. *You* owe *millions*. If you can be an adventurer, why can’t I?" Merlin ruthlessly exposed Alice’s sore spot.

"Don’t… don’t bring that up anymore…" Alice clutched her chest, the words cutting deep. "Please, just… don’t mention the debt. I’ll… I’ll *force myself* to recommend you, alright?!"

Merlin twisted his mouth, a strange smile spreading across his face—

Heh heh, success!

This dumb girl Alice—if you don’t put her in her place, she gets too big for her britches.

Let me make good use of your value!

Let her be the stepping stone for my rise to the petty bourgeoisie!

Hoo hoo hoo hoo hoo…

■

Late at night.

At the ruined nest in the back of the mountain.

The surviving goblins, lost and leaderless, surged in the darkness.

It looked like they were preparing to migrate elsewhere—this place was no longer livable.

*BOOM—*

A deafening explosion tore through the ruins hidden in the dark.

A stunningly beautiful woman suddenly appeared at the cave entrance. Her long purple hair half-concealed her face, her dress slit all the way up to her thighs, her fair skin glowing, her red lips parting slightly.

She stepped forward in high heels, each click-clack echoing through the depths.

"So the Goblin Sages’ lineage was hiding underground in Wales. Guess reading the London Post wasn’t a waste of time after all."

The surviving goblins were terrified, fleeing in all directions. That unrestrained pressure—it was Saint-tier, without a doubt!

Who would’ve thought that after the goblins suffered a fatal blow, someone else would come knocking?

The purple-haired woman ignored the fleeing goblins. Instead, she approached the collapsed underground palace above, her hands searching through the rubble.

After a while, her eyes lit up. She pulled the Goblin Emperor’s weapon from the debris.

The massive, heavy wolf-tooth club was covered in crimson magical runes. Held in the hands of a woman who looked as if she couldn’t withstand a gust of wind, it seemed utterly out of place.

The purple-haired woman muttered under her breath, as if chanting. The club in her hands reacted, spinning wildly.

The magical runes unraveled, and the entire club was dismantled, shifting like a Rubik’s Cube until it transformed into an exquisite red key.

"One of the keys to the Hell Legion… got it."

title: Chapter 92 — Countdown to Burnout 6
content:
Chapter 92 — Countdown to Burnout 6

Volume 2 · Chapter 92

A black vortex suddenly appeared before the purple-haired woman, slowly spinning like a black hole.

The purple-haired woman froze, then quickly and humbly knelt on one knee, lowering her proud head.

"Your Majesty."

Black Hole: "Have you obtained the key?"

"Yes," the purple-haired woman replied.

Black Hole: "So the legend is true. One of the keys to the Infernal Legion was in the hands of the Goblin Sages bloodline. No wonder they didn’t migrate to the Southern United Kingdom—they were clearly guarding the key."

Purple-haired woman: "It seems so. I never expected them to hide it so deeply."

Black Hole: "Carola, you’ve surprised me too. I didn’t expect you to gather a key so quickly. I’ll reward you when you return."

Purple-haired woman: "It wasn’t like that. When I arrived, this place was already in ruins. Getting the key didn’t take much effort."

Black Hole: "Oh? Who did it? The Sages bloodline isn’t weak—how could they be annihilated overnight?"

Purple-haired woman: "The newspapers say it was the villagers uniting to exterminate them."

Black Hole: "Hahaha, nonsense. A Goblin Emperor is usually Saint-tier. A mere group of villagers wouldn’t pose a threat. It seems there were hidden dragons among those villagers."

Purple-haired woman: "I think so too."

Black Hole: "Well, regardless, Emperor Sages was never your match. As one of the Four Heroes of the former kingdom, few in Great Britain could defeat you. Someone clearing the way for you is a good thing. Bring the key back quickly."

Purple-haired woman: "Yes, I’ll leave immediately."

Black Hole: "The plan to revive the former kingdom is already underway. The other heroes have also begun collecting keys. Once we obtain the power of the Infernal Legion, overthrowing the British Empire is only a matter of time!"

The purple-haired woman knelt humbly on the ground, her voice ringing with conviction as she swore—

"Yes! Carola is willing to offer her soul for the kingdom’s revival!"

◆

The next morning.

Merlin and Alice sat in a small donkey cart, heading toward Rexham.

"Goodbye, Merlin!"

"Goodbye, Lady Alice!"

"Goodbye, Big Sister!"

"Don’t go, Little Daisy Oppa!"

"Oppa~! Oppa~! Saranghaeyo~!"

Upon learning that Alice and Merlin were leaving, countless villagers came to see them off.

"Go back, don’t see us off anymore..." Alice waved to those behind them.

"Goodbye, beautiful ladies!" Merlin had been blowing kisses nonstop since the start.

Though many people came to see them off, most were there to bid farewell to Little Daisy Merlin.

The scene was painfully awkward—yīn shèng yáng shuāi. The ladies who often patronized Merlin’s business had all shown up, enough to form a reinforced company. The place was a sea of colorful flags and banners, a testament to just how popular Little Daisy was.

Alice huffed, turning around to focus on driving, her heart sour. She was the one who had worked hardest to save people, so why were so many there to see Merlin off? He was stealing all her limelight! She was so angry she could kill Merlin a hundred times over...

"Henry, take good care of your mother!" Merlin called out to little Henry in the crowd.

"Don’t worry, Merlin hyung! I will! Once I cultivate my battle aura, I’ll come to Rexham to find you!" little Henry shouted back.

Tch, this little brat...

So he finally calls me Merlin hyung?

But I’ve already gotten used to being called Merlin the Uncle.

Merlin gave an awkward smile, unsure what to say. As a traveler, this village was just another fleeting stop in his life.

"Merlin, marry Lady Alice soon and be happy!" Martha also sent her blessings, shouting loudly.

Merlin and Alice both staggered, nearly tumbling off the donkey cart in shock.

"Hey, hey, hey! Did you hear that? What the hell!" Merlin patted Alice’s shoulder.

"I heard it. What the hell indeed. How did we get misunderstood into that kind of relationship?" Alice said, subconsciously scooting away from Merlin to distance herself.

"I have no idea what’s going on. This feels like a curse on me. It’s terrifying..." Merlin shivered.

"Same here. In all my years, this is the most vicious curse I’ve ever heard, hands down!" Alice nodded repeatedly.

They fell silent—

Merlin: "What are you? Disgusted by me?"

Alice: "That’s my line! What do you have to be disgusted about?"

Merlin: "You think I’d marry a washboard? What a joke. That’s the most horrifying thing I’ve ever heard in my life."

Alice: "Get lost! That’s the most horrifying thing for *me*. Look at you, so poor and pathetic—it’s disgusting."

Merlin: "I’d rather be poor than be a washboard like you. Look at the send-off—I got so many people, you got so few. Clearly, you’re the unwanted one."

Alice: "Big deal if you have fangirls! Look at the women seeing you off—how old are they? Middle-aged and elderly women’s idol, and you’re still smug about it? You’re making me laugh my teeth out, hehehe~"

Merlin: "You’re just jealous! You’re a washboard nobody wants, so you’re sour about me. How pathetic~"

Alice: "Who says I’m not wanted? People who like me could circle the world a hundred times!"

Merlin: "A hundred times? Pfft! Take off your chest pads, and I bet there’s not a single one!"

Alice: "You’re talking nonsense! I wear pads to reduce shock, not to hide my shortcomings!"

Merlin: "Hahaha, nice one. That’s the first time I’ve heard ‘reduce shock’ used as such a fresh and refined excuse."

Alice: "And you’re no better! So poor you couldn’t even afford a ticket to Rexham, forcing you to hitch a ride with me. Get off! This is *my* cart!"

Merlin: "I won’t! This donkey cart is so slow, I’m doing you a favor by sitting here. My presence instantly elevates this cart’s class. Can’t you feel it?"

Alice: "Get lost, you perverted Demon King! I don’t want to see you!"

Merlin: "You, the washboard Hero, watch your tone when talking to me. Your donkey cart is *really* slow..."

Alice: "Bullshit! Mengmeng runs very fast!"

Merlin: "Mengmeng?"

Alice: "That’s my donkey..."

While they were still arguing, an Akina Mountain veteran driver in a giant, slow ox cart overtook them?!

Merlin sighed, shrugging. "See? Your donkey cart is *really* slow. Slower than an ox cart."

"That’s not right..." Alice furrowed her brows, looking at her donkey, only to find it had an upset stomach—clearly it had eaten something bad. "Hey, did your dinner soup a few days ago have a lot of yellow beans?"

"Yeah." Merlin nodded.

"Did... you eat them?" Alice asked tentatively.

"I never eat beans. I fed them to your donkey." Merlin gave a thumbs-up, smiling confidently. "See how good I am to your Mengmeng? Aren’t you going to thank me?"

"I—I’ll thank you like hell!" Alice was so furious she nearly cried on the cart. "Hiya, this is infuriating! Waaah..."

○○（＞＜）○○

In the distance, Martha cupped her cheeks, enviously murmuring to herself—

"They two look so close~"

title: Chapter 1 — Grinding Countdown 5
content:
Chapter 1 — Grinding Countdown 5

Volume 3 · Chapter 1

A week had passed since then.

During that week, the two of them were basically in a state of war.

They quarreled every single day, spitting words at each other with such force that droplets flew everywhere.

At the root of their mutual insults was nothing more than their looking down on each other, yet somehow being stuck together.

It was rather awkward. To outsiders, it looked like a couple bickering without any real malice, but in truth, both of them were fighting for their pride.

On the road, since they were in the middle of nowhere with no place to stay, they ended up arguing over who should sleep in the carriage.

Alice was the type of foul-tempered person that Merlin never showed any mercy toward, and he had no inclination to be gentle with her either, so he simply told her to roll onto the ground and sleep there herself.

But the donkey cart didn't belong to Merlin, and Alice kickingly shoved him off.

Poor Merlin spent the entire night in the dead of night, lying on his back gazing at the autumn stars, enduring the autumn wind.

He dreamed that he had stolen a lamb and was chased for two miles by a shepherd wielding a whip, which was terribly embarrassing.

Merlin was the energetic sort, but Alice was not. After arguing for three or four days, she finally showed signs of exhaustion and could go on no longer.

Alice had been particularly afraid of speaking to Merlin these past few days; as soon as she opened her mouth, they would argue until her throat felt like it was smoking after just a couple sentences.

Every night she would pray inwardly: Oh Great God, please make this bastard Merlin disappear soon. Don't let him continue to ruin my life. I have the feeling that since running into him, I'll suffer in poverty for the rest of my days. So, do you lack cross-dressing boys by your side? If you need one, just summon him over there. I think his womanly face would be more than enough to satisfy people with peculiar tastes. That's right, what I mean is that besides his womanly face, Merlin has basically nothing praiseworthy about him.

Alice seemed to be nearly driven mad by Merlin's torment, muttering things like this almost every day.

But today, Alice's suffering came to an end —

After all sorts of friction, the two of them finally arrived at their destination: Wrexham!

As a proper city in Wales, its scale could not possibly be compared to that of a small village.

There were Dorda walls, soldiers standing in neat formation, massive city gates sturdy enough to resist monster attacks, and a moat winding around it all.

A dense crowd gathered before the city gates; the place was teeming with people and buzzing with life.

Alice gazed at the city walls of Wrexham, her spirits lifting from despondency to high excitement. She cried out inwardly: Oh mother, we're finally here. I can stay far away from Merlin now and never have to argue with him again. Hurry back to the guild and send this plague god away...

Merlin's heart also grew excited, full of anticipation for his new job.

"Hey, Alice, this is Wrexham, right?"

"..." Alice's face darkened and she said nothing.

"Speak up, Alice, are you mute?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"Please don't talk to me. I need some quiet," Alice snapped irritably.

"I haven't provoked you. Why are you acting like you've been soaked in gunpowder?" Merlin frowned.

"Yes, yes, yes..." Alice nodded vigorously, rolling her eyes as she said, "It's Wrexham."

"So we've arrived already." Merlin stood up and stretched lazily, then asked casually, "By the way, how many tiers are there for adventurers?"

"Five: Iron, Silver, Gold, Mithril, and Platinum," Alice answered flatly.

"What tier are you?" Merlin asked curiously.

"Gold," Alice replied oddly.

"How weak. I thought you were amazing, but you're stuck in the middle, neither going up nor down?" Merlin shook his head and said contemptuously.

"You!" Alice grew flustered with anger, most disliking Merlin putting on airs of superiority.

"This great lord could become a Platinum-tier adventurer at will. Just watch me," Merlin said confidently. He was, after all, a tremendously powerful Demon Lord, more than capable of becoming a Platinum adventurer.

"Heh heh, good luck to you," Alice sneered twice.

The two rode in the small donkey cart into Wrexham, but they still had to pay a toll.

A small village required only a few copper coins, while the proper city of Wrexham raised the fee to one silver piece.

As an adventurer, Alice was exempt from taxes when entering or leaving her own territory.

This left Merlin somewhat dissatisfied as he glanced at Alice beside him.

"Alice, lend me some money?"

"G, U, N!" Alice pulled on the donkey's reins and shot back irritably.

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue, narrowed his eyes, and said disdainfully, "Why are you so cheap?"

Although Merlin looked down on Alice's stinginess, he paid the fee himself. Even though he was embarrassingly poor, he still had a little stash of his own, reserved for emergencies.

If Merlin were to throw his money into a horse-race betting pool, he wouldn't even frown, because there was a chance to turn things around. But handing it over unconditionally to evil capitalism made him ten thousand times unwilling.

◆

Entering the city.

Merlin felt that it was actually quite prosperous here.

Though it couldn't compare to the wealthy cities of England.

It had a countryside charm everywhere, warm and cozy.

The two arrived at the central district of Wrexham, with the Adventurers Guild right before their eyes.

Adventurers' banners flew high. It was a typical Baroque-style building, looking overall like a very large pub.

Adventurers carrying weapons streamed in and out of the entrance nonstop.

"This is the Wrexham Adventurers Guild," Alice said after tying up her donkey outside, offering a brief explanation.

"Really? It looks quite impressive." Merlin surveyed it for a moment, waved his hand, and said, "Let's go in quickly. I can hardly wait to see what the new job looks like?"

"Wait a moment." Alice called out to Merlin and said seriously, "There are some things I need to make clear."

"Hm?" Merlin turned back in surprise.

"You can recommend me as an adventurer, but the debt of you saving me must be erased completely. I don't owe you anything..." Alice emphasized.

"I know. This is our deal. I've said it before, right? For us demons, deals are an incredibly sacred thing. I definitely won't keep pestering you," Merlin said solemnly.

"Fine, follow me."

Alice walked ahead to lead the way...

◆

Upon entering the Adventurers Guild.

There were truly many people inside, wearing all sorts of clothing, each full of energy.

The layout was even more like a large tavern; it seemed the guild ran a tavern business alongside its main work.

In the center there was an information board, plastered with various commissions. Several adventurers stood there examining it with furrowed brows, apparently where they received their work.

Of course, the most unusual thing was the counter area, where people were packed in three layers inside and out.

In the center, a man clad in black armor with a massive black sword on his back stood before a crystal orb. Not a single trace of his aura leaked out; he didn't look particularly strong, and his face was hidden beneath a heavy helmet, appearing extraordinarily mysterious.

The crystal orb before him emitted a brilliant golden light, making those nearby gasp in astonishment.

"S Saint-tier!?"

"He really is Saint-tier!"

"My goodness! Who is he?"

Merlin's brows knitted deeply as he asked Alice beside him in surprise —

"S Saint-tier? Isn't that a big deal in your guild?"

(?-_?)??

title: Chapter 2 — All-Nighter Countdown 4
content:
Chapter 2 — All-Nighter Countdown 4

Volume 3 · Chapter 2

"Aside from the former guild master, our entire guild only has three Saint-tier members. To think another one has arrived today… truly surprising…"

A drop of cold sweat traced down Alice's forehead as she looked at the dark-armored heavy swordsman, her mind clouded with confusion. Very few Saint-tier warriors joined the Adventurers Guild; most earned far more serving as royal guards.

"So few? When I was the Demon Lord, not counting the Seven Generals, I had dozens of Saint-tier subordinates under my command. Your guild is truly shabby…" Merlin shrugged, finding the guild severely lacking in talent.

"Don't bring up the past. You're not the Demon Lord anymore. You're just an ordinary lazybones, a lowlife who scams women out of money." Alice said without mercy.

"Your tongue is merciless…" Merlin sighed, a trace of discontent in his heart.

While the two were bickering, the dark-armored heavy swordsman walked toward the exit, and Merlin, who was still arguing with Alice, inadvertently blocked his path.

His heavy armor clattered with every step, his footsteps utterly weighty. He stopped before Merlin, his voice muffled yet thunderous.

"Get lost."

Merlin froze. Being cursed at on the spot grated on his nerves.

He had once been the Great Demon Lord—no one dared speak to him with such insolence. Any rude fool like this would long have been sliced in half.

How humiliating, to be bullied by commoners now that a tiger had strayed from its mountain. Could a mere Saint-tier brat really jump around in front of him?

Merlin frowned, his tone displeased. "Who exactly are you telling to get lost?"

"Obviously you." The dark-armored swordsman replied coldly.

Alice noticed that the man already wore a newly issued adventurer certification around his neck. Mithril rank!

Good heavens, a Saint-tier warrior granted a Mithil-rank certification upon initial assessment!?

Alice was slightly stunned in her heart. As expected of a Saint-tier warrior, the initial rating was truly high.

Thinking about it, her own Adventurers Guild only had two Mithil-rank adventurers, which was the highest tier. As for the former guild master, no one knew his rank, but it certainly couldn't be low either.

Alice carefully examined the information on the Mithil adventurer certification—

Region: Rextrem.

Name: Claude.

Class: Swordsman.

"Tch!" Merlin was also a proud man. His hand drifted to the nodachi at his waist, his demeanor suggesting he wanted to teach the other fellow some manners. "Seems like I need to educate you on what courtesy is?"

Many adventurer colleagues had noticed the commotion. Seeing Merlin, an ordinary person, clash with a Saint-tier powerhouse who had just obtained Mithil rank, their interest was piqued.

Many thought Merlin would end up pressed flat against the ground by the other's little finger, eagerly waiting for the spectacle.

"Making way for me is your honor. Now get lost. I have many things to attend to."

Swordsman Claude unleashed his formidable Saint-tier aura, feeling overwhelmingly powerful and profound—a clear sign of someone who had resided at the Saint-tier for a long time and possessed real skill.

Everyone in the guild shifted uncomfortably. If a Saint-tier powerhouse actually struck, the entire guild would suffer!

In the distance, the former guild master, a frail old man leaning on a cane, also wore a displeased expression.

"Others have spoken to me the same way before. But later, they were dead."

Merlin narrowed his eyes. Someone with such an explosive temper really put him in a bad mood.

Alice suddenly pulled Merlin aside and whispered angrily, "What are you doing?! Starting trouble right off the bat—do you want to lose your job?"

Merlin came to his senses and said awkwardly, "I was so caught up in being annoyed that I almost forgot about the main business."

"He's a Mithil-rank adventurer. Respect is owed to him. Although adventurers are a free profession, there's still a class hierarchy within the guild. He's high-ranking, so enjoying certain privileges is only natural." Alice explained quietly beside her, hoping today's trip to help Merlin secure a job—so he could repay a favor—wouldn't be ruined by his own recklessness.

"So there's such a rule?" Merlin knew nothing of this.

"Nonsense, it's an unwritten rule." Alice impatiently explained to Merlin, then turned to Claude with an embarrassed smile. "Sorry, this guy just joined recently and doesn't understand the rules. Please don't take it to heart."

"A completely ordinary person with no aura whatsoever. I advise you to shed that arrogant attitude, or sooner or later someone will kill you. Hmph!"

Swordsman Claude snorted coldly and left the Adventurers Guild directly, leaving Merlin with his defiant back turned.

"Pfft!" Merlin pursed his lips, thinking—what's so great about Saint-tier? He'd lost count of how many he'd chopped down himself. If it weren't for having real business today, he'd surely teach this arrogant fool some manners.

Seeing the matter resolved peacefully, many people breathed a sigh of relief.

Several of Alice's familiar acquaintances approached. Among them came a thoroughly drunk fellow, burping with the smell of alcohol.

"Oh, Alice, you're back? And you brought an old flame? That Arnold guy must be crying in the toilet right now. *Burp*~"

"Hobbs, don't come over here. You reek of alcohol!" Alice protested unhappily, unconsciously covering her nose.

"Alright, alright, I'll talk to this new friend of yours…" The drunken Hobbs patted Merlin's shoulder. "What's your name, friend?"

"Merlin."

"That sounds like a magician's name. You should also have a partner named Arthur." Hobbs told a corny joke.

"Hah~" Merlin gave a forced smirk.

"My name is Hobbs Griffin, this guild's strongest adventurer. I'm not joking—I'm serious." Hobbs said with a red nose and thick alcohol breath, offering absolutely no credibility.

"Don't listen to his nonsense. He's just an Iron-rank adventurer who does nothing all day." Alice whispered.

Merlin perked up at the mention, suddenly feeling a sense of camaraderie—the kind heroes feel toward one another. This person must get along great with him!

"Young Merlin, I've never seen Alice bring a man here before. How do you tame such a wild mare? Share some experience." Hobbs' mouth started running loose, behaving like a complete street thug.

"Wild mare? More like an iron maiden…" Merlin said awkwardly.

"Young Merlin…" Hobbs paused, then said seriously, "You might be my kindred spirit. I take a liking to you. I'll take you somewhere men understand, hehehe…"

"Get lost! Hobbs, we don't have that kind of relationship! If you keep talking nonsense, I won't be polite!" Alice pretended to draw her sword, threatening him.

"Calm down, Alice. I'm just kidding. You're always so serious—that's why you're not very likable. Just look at Lucia—soft-spoken and delicate. By the way, someone sent her 9,999 roses again today. Wouldn't you be envious?" Hobbs furrowed his brows.

Alice's face flushed with anger, her slender sword halfway drawn from its sheath—

"I-I would never be envious!"

(??^??)

title: Chapter 3 — Grind Countdown 3
content:
Chapter 3 — Grind Countdown 3

Volume 3 · Chapter 3

"Not gonna draw your sword? Did I hit a nerve? If Alice would just tone down her temper, she'd definitely get roses too. Don't give up on treatment, you know…"

Hobbs took a fearful step back, still drunk but at least keeping his wits.

"I'm not!" Alice ground out through gritted teeth. "What's so great about roses anyway? You can look but you can't eat them. I don't need them!"

"Miss Alice, you're back? Long time no see."

A blue-haired swordsman approached, dressed to the nines with a rose dangling from his mouth and curling waves in his hair. His warmth had to belong to that man, Arnold.

If you had to describe him, he was like a male lead straight out of a shoujo manga.

Merlin took in the man's very particular attire — a textbook noble's outfit, adorned with expensive gems, especially the sword at his waist… pure gold inlaid with diamonds. Eighty thousand a pop!

Just looking at him screamed rich kid — I'm rich, I'm ridiculously rich!

Merlin figured the difference between himself and this guy was that he had the face of a rich second-generation kid, but not the fate.

"Lo… long time no see, Arnold…" Alice forced a thin smile that was painfully strained. Disgust was written all over her face.

"Miss Alice, it's been half a month since we last met and I've missed you so much. The caviar from Greenland, the steak from Spain, the foie gras from Ireland — it all tasted bland. Even the handful of gold coins my father, the Count, casually tosses me as pocket money can't soothe the emptiness inside me. My mind is filled with only the beautiful Miss Alice and that goddess-like face of yours…"

Arnold, a rose clenched between his teeth, gestured wildly before Alice like a vain rooster.

"*Urgh*…" Merlin covered his mouth, feeling slightly nauseous, goosebumps rising all over him. *Just talk normally, it won't kill you.* And this guy actually had a thing for Alice's chest? Where was the dignity of a noble?

"S-such amazing… dedication…" Alice's forehead vein twitched. *Every time I meet Arnold, I get blasted in the face with his wealth flexing. It hurts so much. This guy's got something wrong with his brain. My own life is already struggling enough, and now he's throwing salt in my wounds? Someone with emotional intelligence this low should be the one with a girlfriend — which he isn't!*

"Beautiful Miss Alice, please accept my rose. It was shipped from Vatican City early this morning and still has Saint-tier morning dew on it~" Arnold knelt on one knee, his manner extremely devout.

Merlin smirked awkwardly and couldn't resist the inner complaint: *You sure that dew isn't your own drool?*

"Th-that's not necessary…" Alice declined tactfully. *Who would accept anything from this guy? He'd never stop pestering me like a fly!*

"Hey hey, Arnold, come here a sec…"

Hobbs tugged Arnold over and whispered in a very mysterious tone, "Don't you see that blond guy over there? He's Alice's old boyfriend she brought back. Same type of pretty boy as you — have you not figured anything out yet?"

"What do you mean? The stench of your breath is making me dizzy…" Arnold pinched his nose, feeling like he couldn't breathe.

"You're the Count's son and you got dumbed out drinking Sanlu milk as a kid, huh?" Hobbs threw an arm around Arnold's neck and said meaningfully, "You're already a loser now. Can't you see it? That blond Merlin guy has replaced you — he's already conquered your dream girl."

"What!?" Arnold's eyes widened. "Is there really another idiot with his IQ offline who likes Alice besides me?"

"Say it like that and Alice will cry herself out in the toilet. No wait, she'd probably draw her sword and chop your head off first." Hobbs paused, stoking the fire. "You're a man, aren't you? How could you possibly swallow this insult? If I were you, I definitely couldn't take it lying down!"

Arnold shoved Hobbs aside and strode straight toward Merlin, a hint of masculinity finally appearing on his sissy face.

"You hillbilly, what's your relationship with Miss Alice?"

"Well…" Merlin thought for a moment and said calmly, "Let's call it a situationship."

Alice: "Get lost! What kind of situationship is that!?"

"What!? A dirty ass transaction? You two are already at that level!?" Arnold turned and forced a very reluctant smile at Alice. "Speaking of which, Miss Alice, your tastes are truly unique. A bit surprising, but honestly kind of cool!"

Alice: "You get lost too! You filthy-minded bastard! Why wouldn't you think 'friend' first and jump straight to ass!? You've been exposed!"

"Regardless of what kind of relationship it is, I'm guessing you must've threatened the beautiful Miss Alice, so…" Arnold drew the golden straight sword at his waist and said with a completely serious expression, "I, Arnold, eldest son of House Austin, shall challenge you, this hillbilly, to a duel today!"

"Why exactly must you duel me?" Merlin said impatiently. He could sense Arnold was a low-tier warrior, but his sword stance was full of holes — clearly someone who didn't know how to fight.

"Well…" Arnold's brain blanked. He hadn't thought of an answer.

"A man's duel is of course to compete for mating rights! Whoever wins gets to mate with Alice, ohohohoho, *burp*~" Hobbs cheered from the side.

Alice: "Shut up, Hobbs! Don't make it sound like I'm an animal! Mate my ass! Have you ever considered my feelings!? Do I look like someone who just mates with anybody!?"

"Oh right! Mating rights! Whoever wins gets to mate with the beautiful Miss Alice!" Arnold rallied, speaking with iron conviction.

Alice: "Where's your brain, Arnold!? Stop taking everything so seriously! Who gave you permission to treat my mating rights as the duel prize!? At least ask me about it first! You bastards!"

"Mating rights?" Merlin shrugged awkwardly. "I'm not interested. You win."

Alice: "Of course you'd find a way to throw shade at me even now! How much do you look down on me, you arrogant jerk!?"

"Hmph! Are you looking down on me? As a noble, I will absolutely not accept your charity!" Arnold seemed to still have some spine.

Alice: "Oh my god, has my mating rights now become charity? Please just die already. I've been complaining for a while — can you respond to me for once? Stop treating me like air!"

"Don't worry, Miss Alice. I'll take back your mating rights from this villain!" Arnold's eyes sparkled with stars.

Alice: "Who said I was worried about you!? Please, just let me say a word, okay!?"

"Enough talk — let me show you the ancestral sword technique of the Austin family. I wouldn't use it on just anyone, so I'll admit you're a worthy opponent!" Arnold struck a pose.

"Oh." Merlin picked at his ear.

Alice: "I'd advise against making a move. You'll get hurt."

"Have faith in me, Miss Alice!" Arnold waved his golden straight sword and charged forward like an idiot, "Secret Technique: Being Rich Lets You Do Whatever the Hell You Want!"

Merlin shook his head, swung his hand, and unleashed a sky-piercing fist, sighing as he said, "Cut the crap. Let's send you to the heavens…"

Arnold went *poof* — Merlin had punched him clean through the ceiling. He hung upside down, swaying like a clock pendulum.

"…" Alice.

"…" Hobbs.

The two stared silently at Arnold dangling from the roof.

"Sigh…" Merlin tilted his mouth awkwardly and thought —

*Am I the only one who thinks this guild is kinda messed up?*
