title: Chapter 4 — Grind Countdown 2
content:
Chapter 4 — Grind Countdown 2

Volume 3 · Chapter 4

Afterwards, the pitiful Arnold was carried away by Hobbs, completely clueless about what power even was. Today, he had been sent flying by an ordinary person.

The commotion didn't draw much attention, since brawls in the guild happened from time to time and everyone was accustomed to it.

Besides, Arnold was an exceptionally weak low-tier warrior who couldn't fight to begin with. A handful of villagers swarming him could probably take him down.

Meilin's overwhelming fist driving Arnold sky-high didn't prove much about his strength, so many of his fellow adventurers just treated it as a joke to laugh at.

Alice finally had some peace and quiet, and brought Merlin over to handle the paperwork.

Standing in front of the counter was an extremely beautiful girl, with an angelic face and a devilish figure. The fullness on her chest was clearly not the fake variety Alice sported, and her silk-like long hair made her incredibly charming.

This girl was named Lucia Taylor, the granddaughter of the former guildmaster Taylor.

She was the one who received constant admiration and kept getting roses delivered. She handled various commission files and daily affairs, and was hailed as the gem of the Rexhum Guild, stunningly gorgeous.

"Lucia, long time no see."

Alice approached the counter, and she and Lucia seemed to have a decent relationship.

"Long time no see, Alice. Did you come back after completing a commission? You must have had a good harvest this time, right?" Lucia set aside her affairs and came over to chat with Alice.

"Well... let's not mention it..." Alice smiled awkwardly, thinking, What harvest? Not only did the commission reward go down the drain, I almost died.

"You'll need to work harder then. A few days ago your landlord even came to the guild demanding rent, which puts us in a bit of a bind." Lucia showed a troubled expression.

"Sorry, sorry. I'll pay my rent as soon as I get back and won't cause you any trouble." Alice thought that the penny-pinching landlady was already coming to collect after only two days. What an unforgiving piece of work.

"It's alright. If you don't come back, I'll have to front the money for you first." Lucia said with a half-smile.

"You're too kind. How could I use your money?" Alice waved her hand dismissively, smiling.

"It's not really my money. It's from my suitors. Every gift and bouquet of roses they bring gets sold, and I donate the proceeds to an orphanage. If you need it..."

"No need..."

Before Lucia could finish, Alice put on a serious face and refused, wondering inwardly if she had somehow been equated with an orphan.

"Sigh, having too many suitors is quite a troubling matter~" Lucia rested her cheek on her beautiful hand, looking genuinely distressed.

Emmmm...

That's definitely a scheming bitch, right?

She's deliberately showing off to me, isn't she?

I wouldn't be even a little bit envious!

I seriously am not envious, boohoo...

Alice covered her face, her mind in a complicated turmoil, as if Lucia had struck a nerve.

"Alice, are you here today to pick up a new commission?" Lucia asked curiously.

"No, I'm here to recommend someone become an adventurer." Alice steered the conversation back on track.

"Recommend?" Lucia tilted her head in surprise.

"This guy right next to me..." Alice pointed reluctantly at Merlin beside her.

"Oh, beautiful lady, it's me." Merlin waved.

"Who is this?" Lucia looked puzzled. He was quite handsome, just giving off an irresponsible vibe.

"His name is Merlin, and he wants to become an adventurer." Alice explained from the side.

"Alice, did you find a boyfriend? You actually brought a man back. Did you finally figure things out and realize the goodness of men? I don't accept this. How could you get married before me when I'm obviously more popular? Tell me quickly, where did you nab this handsome man from?!" Lucia's expression turned somewhat unhinged. She seemed unable to accept reality, as if seeing Alice remain single was her one remaining joy in life.

Merlin frowned, wondering if this world had some kind of illness. Why did everyone keep misunderstanding his relationship with Alice? That said, this Lucia really was a bitch...

"No, we're not like that. It's just that due to some special circumstances, I need him to recommend me." Alice forced a smile, thinking that this guy Lucia only kept receiving roses herself — couldn't she let Alice have her own encounters?

"Is that so? What kind of situation?" Lucia gradually calmed down.

"He was formerly wanted by restaurant owners, so he falls into the criminal category." Alice shot Merlin a look of disdain.

"I see. So Mr. Merlin, do you plan to pay off your debts? Since Alice has vouched for and guaranteed you, the Adventurers Guild can revoke your wanted status and allow you to work while paying things off." Lucia explained.

"Sure, no problem at all." Merlin nodded. He thought that wanted warrants could be revoked? That was fantastic. No more slackard adventurers would bother him now.

"Let's test your strength first. Depending on your level, your initial adventurer rank will differ. Low-tier corresponds to Mirror Black Iron, mid-tier to Silver, high-tier to Gold, and Saint-tier... well, you saw it just now, you'd be ranked directly to Mithril." Lucia introduced.

"The higher the adventurer rank, the better the benefits, right?" Merlin asked. Before becoming an adventurer, he needed to understand the basics.

"Certainly. The monthly stipend and various privilege benefits differ. The biggest difference is still the commission levels one can accept." Lucia smiled.

"Commissions have levels too?" Merlin frowned.

"Yes, they're classified as C, B, A, S, SS, and SSS. The higher the level, the more profitable the commission. Adventurers below Gold level can barely touch S-rank commissions." Lucia explained the distinction.

Merlin frowned, thinking that if he couldn't get the highest-level commissions, becoming an adventurer would be pointless, so he asked.

"The initial ranking won't be set in stone, right?"

"No. Even with insufficient strength, one can advance through accumulated experience. By taking on more commissions step by step, you can gradually improve. I recall a Frenchman known for his perseverance. He's now 102 years old, and he completed 99,999,999,999 low-level commissions, so now he's a Silver-rank adventurer. Truly admirable..." Lucia wore an angelic smile.

Fucking hell!

One hundred billion commissions just to barely reach Silver-rank!

Wasn't this blatantly scamming people? Painting a big picture to give false hope.

You could advance, and it sounded motivational and humane, but so what? The dirt was already up to your forehead, pal!

Merlin's expression grew complicated. This ranking system had too many flaws.

"Your ranking system... is really坑人..."

"This is merely a safeguard for those willing to work hard. Of course, there's a faster way to advance, and that's by strengthening your own abilities. Once your strength improves, your adventurer rank will follow." Lucia dispelled Merlin's doubts.

In the end, it all came down to whether your own strength was sufficient.

What was that 102-year-old grandpa even clinging to? Wasting his life...

Merlin rolled his eyes. This Adventurers Guild was absolutely toxic.

"I understand Mr. Merlin has concerns, but the Adventurers Guild is fair." Lucia smiled sweetly and continued. "Even a top-tier Purple Gold adventurer, if they stop working for a long time or cause negative impacts on society, will be demoted. According to the rules, being dropped all the way to Black Iron is not impossible."

Merlin somewhat understood. After all, the guild wouldn't want to support idle people either.

"Then, does Mr. Merlin have any other questions?" Lucia asked.

"Nope." Merlin shook his head.

Lucia took out a crystal ball from below the counter. The Saint-tier heavy swordsman earlier had also used this. "Mr. Merlin, please place your hand on it. Your strength will be reflected in different colors..."

Merlin stepped forward, looked at the crystal ball, and took a deep breath. He seemed slightly nervous as he placed his hand on it—

So next...

I'll compassionately display the overwhelming power of an arrogant monarch.

Tremble before me, you humble mortals!

Hiahiahia~!

(-`ω-)?

title: Chapter 5 — Crunch Countdown 1
content:
Chapter 5 — Crunch Countdown 1

Volume 3 · Chapter 5

It's that time of year again when we sell our misery.

De Ge, play a bit of erhu, yeah, the one we always use, “River Water.”

Let me introduce him: De Ge is my partner in begging at the train station; I handle the crying and the copy, he handles the music and stirs up the crowd—our roles are crystal clear.

That's right, don't doubt it; everything nowadays is about efficiency, even begging.

Two of us begging definitely brings in money faster than one; after counting the day’s takings we only get about twenty extra yuan in the bowl.

So far, De Ge and I have been camped out at Jilin Train Station for half a year; life is just barely getting by.

Every day people come and go, and De Ge and I keep performing at full throttle, scrimping and saving a little, but nobody gives us a proper look.

In peak season we can pull in a few dozen more yuan, enough for a few packs of Wujiang pickles and a couple of buns for a decent lunch.

In the off‑season it's miserable—we have to sip cold water from the restroom to stave off hunger, and we split each bun into three pieces for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

I cry my heart out every day, De Ge sweats his head off beside me, we're almost starving to faint, but the pitiful income often wakes me up penniless in the dead of night.

But we still have to live bravely, don't we?

De Ge is mute; he used to do charity work at the bus station, but there were too many scammers, people got jaded, and folks like De Ge who truly need help end up miserable, forced to team up with me and beg at the entrance of Jilin Train Station.

De Ge has been a wandering drifter for years; with the New Year coming, he wants to go home.

As his partner, I feel I have to help, so I take on any odd jobs I can find.

Not long ago an old lady passed away; we went to mourn for her, we cried all night, but in the end they said we weren't sincere and kicked us out.

That morning the snow was blinding white, the wind harsher than ever, we trudged through deep snow back to the station, huddling in a corner to keep warm.

This can't go on; we can't earn enough, and De Ge can't afford a ticket home.

So I can only write a book to earn enough for De Ge's train fare home.

I picked up my battered Nokia I scavenged and started writing again.

Sigh, winter's back; besides earning De Ge enough for his ticket, I need to make some money for clothes—I'm still wearing a thin single‑layer shirt that looks thick but is lined with toilet paper.

It looks thick, but it's all toilet paper inside.

Last year I wrote “My Sister Never Calls Me Brother,” which barely…

…kept me barely afloat, but the royalties got me through the long winter. Thanks to the SF website and all the editors for their support.

Alright, I've said enough of the

bitter

tears

I

again

need to

with

De Ge

go

do

old

original

job

now.

As for what I'll do after De Ge leaves

what should I do?

I

of course

will keep begging.

Because that's exactly how I survived last year.

Ah, that's right, I'm still that De‑xing QAQ

This is the Nokia I use for typing, I hijack restaurant Wi‑Fi every day to upload chapters, originally wanted to take

a photo of De Ge playing erhu, but the camera's useless, so I gave up.

The new year is almost here

Hope you all subscribe hard, give some tips, and throw in monthly tickets.

Help poor

De Ge get home.

( ??? ? ??? )

Also help me get through this Northeastern endless

and bitterly cold winter……

title: Chapter 6
content:
Chapter 6

Volume 3 · Chapter 6

First.

Before testing my strength, let me vent about something.

Why in 80% of stories is testing your strength always done with a crystal ball?

Come on, I've got a bit of OCD. Can someone explain the principle behind this?

Why does putting my hand on it like this let them measure my strength?

If you wanted to be novel, let me grope a boob to measure my strength—now that might actually get my attention.

And Miss Lumia sitting here—could you not wear such a low-cut top? The football on your chest is already interfering with my focus!

Merlin was stewing, muttering his complaints about the awkward situation.

Various adventurers gathered around to watch the spectacle, curious about what level this newbie was at.

After all, a Saint-tier expert had just joined, and now a new face showed up. Everyone was naturally inclined to compare the two. It's like having fine wine in front of you and then a brick—people just want to see the comedy.

But Merlin had not a shred of magical or martial energy, which forced the onlookers to start singing a different tune.

"This newbie doesn't seem to have any aura at all."

"Probably too weak to sense."

"I think this guy is only low-tier at best, maybe black iron rank if he's lucky."

"I'm thinking the same. This guy is so weak."

"But I just saw him send Arnold flying."

"Come on, Arnold may have low-tier strength, but he's inexperienced. I could take a hundred of him without bragging."

Hey, did you see that? This is exactly like those light novels.

This is the usual routine—someone mercilessly mocking me.

Next up, I need to show them by beating the crap out of their faces.

Merlin's face broke into a slight smile. The crowd around him tensed up, as if sensing the outcome.

Suddenly, Merlin's eyes widened as he stared intently at the crystal ball, sending out waves with his gaze—biubiubiu~

The crystal ball remained completely unresponsive.

"Congratulations, Mr. Merlin. You show zero reaction, proving you have not the slightest trace of magical or martial energy. You're just a worthless villager with a combat power of five~" Lumen smiled like an angel, mercilessly ridiculing him. "You can't become an adventurer like this."

Emmmm, the entire crowd fell into an awkward silence.

Who would have expected the onlookers to end up eating their words? They just over-milked it, grossly overestimating Merlin.

After a few seconds of silence, the guild erupted in a wave of laughter.

"Is that for real? No magical or martial energy and still want to be an adventurer?"

"Forget it, buddy. This is a high-risk profession. Without a solid foundation, you'll just die."

"At the very least, get to low-tier strength before coming back. Without any power, even escort missions will be dangerous."

It was quite the contrast—previously a powerful Saint-tier expert, now reduced to an ordinary villager in Merlin's presence. The crowd couldn't help but stifle their laughter.

"That's exactly right."

Merlin muttered self-deprecatingly, still a bit calculating. He wasn't too surprised by the result.

After all, he knew best whether he had any magical or martial energy. As for why he agreed to the test—of course it was for luck! If it worked, great. If not, no big deal.

Alice watched with some bewilderment. She knew that when Merlin fought, he never sensed any magical or martial energy. But the crystal ball showing nothing meant he had literally zero magical or martial energy in his body. So how did he manage to display such overwhelming combat power every time he fought?

All this time, Alice had assumed Merlin was concealing his aura. But now it seemed he genuinely had no magical or martial energy at all.

Alice pulled Merlin aside and whispered, "Hey, what's going on? How can you have no magical or martial energy?"

"You saw me fight, didn't? When have I ever used magical or martial energy? It's not that I don't want to—it's that I literally can't." Merlin looked embarrassed.

"Then what's your deal?! With zero magical or martial energy, how do you keep beating so many monsters?" Alice was confused, unable to understand Merlin at all.

"My draw-slash skill is leveled up really high—like 99999. Does that make sense to you? With a skill that high, even a basic slash can one-shot anyone." Merlin narrowed his eyes and spoke honestly.

The draw-slash basic skill doesn't require martial energy to activate. With a high enough skill level, even a regular slash becomes incredibly powerful. But I was born with 9999—wait, 99999 skill points. How am I supposed to explain this? Nobody in this world would understand.

"What nonsense are you spouting, Alice? I'm totally lost. What are these skill points and skill levels?"

"Just think of me as an anomaly. I don't need magical or martial energy to fight." Merlin rubbed his forehead, not wanting to explain further.

Alice felt like her worldview had been shattered. She had thought Magic Immunity was already shocking enough, but now she couldn't make heads or tails of Merlin. Is this guy even from this world?

"Alice, as I said—" Merlin tried to steer the conversation back on track. "You said that as long as someone vouches for you, you can become an adventurer, right?"

Alice snapped back to attention and approached the counter. "Lumia, I'm recommending this guy. I vouch for him—I guarantee he can handle the job."

"Sorry, Alice, but that won't work. You're talking about a foreign guild member. They're called 'card adventurers'—regular people. But that organization had its headquarters shut down years ago. The current rules are clear: no low-tier strength, no guild acceptance." Lumen explained.

"Huh?" Alice was taken aback. She thought, If Merlin doesn't become an adventurer, she'd owe the Demon Lord a favor and wouldn't be able to sleep. "Can't you make an exception?"

"I'm sorry, Alice. The guild has its rules, and I'm in a difficult position." Lumen apologized sincerely.

"Fine." Merlin sat in front of Lumen and seized her small hand, clearly going for the playboy tactic, trying to charm her. "I've always noticed you're different from others. You must be a kind-hearted person. I'm sincerely begging for your help. If you'd just bend the rules a little, we could have a nice, deep conversation in private~"

Lumen placed her hand on her cheek and smiled without saying a word.

At this point, both of their inner thoughts were quite interesting, as if from a light novel.

Merlin: Women are such a hassle. I have to sell my charm like this. If I didn't have this face, I'd starve to death. Since I'm being so proactive, you'd better just give in gracefully.

Lumen: This narcissist is the most troublesome. I'm being harassed. It's really not good-looking for me to be this beautiful. But my wife is right here—why don't you behave yourself?

Alice shook her head in disbelief. For some reason, she suddenly felt uncomfortable. Probably because Merlin was harassing someone, and her sense of justice wouldn't allow it.

So she didn't hesitate—"slap!"—and knocked Merlin's groping hand away. "We're discussing serious business. What the hell are you doing? Behave yourself!"

Lumen chuckled quietly beside her, saying nothing, enjoying the schadenfreude.

"What are you doing? Stop being so aggressive!" Merlin complained, rubbing his reddened hand.

"We're talking business. Don't take advantage of the situation. Can you be serious for once?" Alice demanded, cinching in her slender waist with righteous indignation.

Above the two of them, opposing auras manifested.

Merlin: debuffed, harem member.

Alice: buffed, wife status.

title: Chapter 7
content:
Chapter 7

Volume 3 · Chapter 7

Sigh.

Alice was such a useless teammate.

If I had seduced them, I would've saved myself a lot of trouble.

Merlin couldn't understand why Alice had to meddle in other people's business. She was really only harming herself.

Alice watched Merlin with a group of predators waiting for the right moment. As long as he dared to lay a hand on Lucia, she would stop him no matter what.

"I'm sorry, Mr. Merlin, but we have our own rules here. We truly cannot offer you the position of adventurer," Lucia said as tactfully as possible.

"Are you sure you don't want to reconsider? You'll be missing out on a top-tier fighter like me."

After Merlin spoke earnestly, several adventurers nearby snickered, thinking this newbie had lost his mind.

"Mr. Merlin, please forgive my bluntness, but I can't see even a single quality about you that suggests top-tier strength," Lucia replied, shaking her head.

"Although I may seem ordinary now, I was once the legendary Sovereign of Pride, the Great Demon Lord of the First Hall. Can you understand just how powerful I am now?" Merlin said with great seriousness.

"Hahahaha—!"

No sooner had Merlin finished speaking than laughter erupted around them. The Sovereign of Pride was known as the strongest of the demon lords, a being in another dimension entirely for these adventurers—someone they would never encounter in their entire lives.

Looking at Merlin now, almost everything about him besides his face screamed mediocrity, giving absolutely no impression of a strong fighter. He was in no way connected to that demon sovereign.

For Merlin to suddenly claim he was once the Great Demon Lord of the First Hall and become everyone's joke was only natural.

At this, Merlin simply smiled, striking a pose that seemed to say, "Others laugh at my madness; I laugh at their inability to see through it." When he'd previously claimed to be the legendary swordmaster Elgin, the surrounding reaction had been exactly the same, and he had grown accustomed to it by now.

Alice, eager to repay her debt to Merlin sooner rather than later, couldn't help but speak up for him. "Really, he truly was the Great Demon Lord of the First Hall. You shouldn't laugh."

The laughter grew even louder. To everyone else, this married couple was playing off each other perfectly, exceptionally well-coordinated.

"This guy was the Great Demon Lord before? Are you kidding me?"

"Hahaha, lacking strength isn't scary, but boasting is really not a good thing!"

"If we're going to talk like that, I was once the Great Demon Lord of the Fifth Hall, Ronald Beelzebub or something. I mean, bragging freely, go right ahead."

The uproarious laughter rose and fell one after another as people began making jokes at Merlin's expense, the atmosphere growing somewhat awkward.

Alice furrowed her brows, a bead of cold sweat trickling down her forehead. What the hell was wrong with these people? Their reaction was going too far. They'd never even seen Lucifer III, so how could they possibly be sure it wasn't Merlin?

For Alice, the only person who knew the truth, this situation was truly stressful.

"Alice, I know your relationship with Mr. Merlin is special, but there's no need to go so far as to lie intentionally on his behalf," Lucia seemed to be holding back her own laughter, her attitude much like everyone else's.

"I didn't lie," Alice grew a little angry.

Just then, a loud "bang" echoed through the air—

Merlin slammed his palm on the table and rose to his feet. Though his expression remained blank, the discontent between his brows was unmistakable.

How should he describe these humans?

Ah, right—frogs sitting at the bottom of a well.

They were impossibly weak, yet they believed this tiny corner of land before them was the entire world. How laughable.

Merlin evaluated them in his heart, and a trace of chilling majesty leaked from him, rendering the crowd completely silent and pressing down on their very souls.

Alice feared Merlin might attack indiscriminately and cause a scene, so she gripped the thin sword at her waist tightly and whispered, "Merlin, are you angry? Please calm down. I didn't bring you here to cause destruction."

"What are you nervous about? Why would I be angry?"

Merlin smiled and反问 Alice, thinking to himself that he was an old man who had lived for two hundred years.

To throw a tantrum over something like this? What kind of joke was that? Had he been living in a toilet for the past two centuries or something?

Only children liked to haggle over every trifling detail. A mature person let facts speak for themselves.

After scanning the room with his gaze, Merlin said in a nonchalant tone—

"It's fine if none of you believe me; just treat it as a joke. The problem I currently face is this: I want to apply for an adventurer position, but you refuse to believe in my strength. So the solution is quite simple."

"Bring out the strongest person in your guild and spar with me. If I can beat him to the point where he doesn't even recognize his own mother, I think all our problems will be easily resolved, won't they?"

The entire hall fell silent, and whispers rippled through the crowd below.

"This newbie is awfully arrogant."

"Yeah, this attitude really makes people uncomfortable."

"Ironically, the strongest in our guild should be Lucia's father,卡尔·泰勒, right?"

"That's right, but he's currently away on a mission and hasn't returned yet. If he were here, he would definitely teach this reckless kid a lesson with just a single pinky finger."

Lucia broke into a sweat. This was the first time she'd encountered such a situation—someone coming in and immediately challenging the guild's strongest?

Merlin had a tanto strapped to his waist and looked like he knew a thing or two about martial arts, but without any trace of magic power or battle aura, he was no different from an ordinary person. Challenging a Saint-tier fighter was nothing short of suicide. Truly the height of foolishness.

"Mr. Merlin, your plan is to challenge the strongest adventurer in our guild? Please don't make jokes like that."

"I'm not joking. If you find me unbeatable, I'll even allow all of your guild's Saint-tier fighters to come at me together."

The crowd erupted into commotion once more, while only Alice remained relatively composed, thinking that even coming all at once wouldn't be enough—they were talking about someone who could obliterate the overlord of the Okinawa Strait in a single strike. How were they supposed to fight against that?

Lucia felt deep pressure, unable to tell whether Merlin was genuinely incredible or genuinely an idiot.

"Mr. Merlin, please—"

"Very well. Let this old man test your strength firsthand."

Before Lucia could finish her sentence, the guild master, Old Tyler, who had been keeping his eyes closed and resting from the beginning, approached while leaning on his walking stick.

"Grandpa, stop messing around. At your age, you shouldn't be getting involved," Lucia frowned, her expression clearly displeased.

Alice's eyes widened with a start in her heart. Master Tyler was a霸主-level warrior who had shaken the world long ago. Even now that he was aged, he remained the undisputed titan of the British martial arts circle, an absolute Saint-tier powerhouse—regarded as Wales' number one fighter. There was no need to say more about how formidable he was.

His self-created Thunderclap Fighting Style had always been renowned for its swiftness and superhuman explosive power. From what others had told her, when he was young, Old Tyler had punched a bimon giant to death with a single blow. Nobody knew just how strong he was now.

Alice had never before seen the old guild master actually fight. He always stayed at the guild headquarters, keeping his eyes closed and tending to his flowers each day—basically living like a retired elder. She had only heard from others that the old guild master was incredibly powerful. Now he was actually going to spar with Merlin?! Could this escalate into a world war?

Logic told Alice that Merlin would win, but the old guild master wasn't weak either, making it somewhat difficult to predict.

"Grandpa!" Lucia called out.

"It's alright. Every few years, some youngster who doesn't know the meaning of heaven and earth shows up. If these old bones of mine don't stretch a bit, people will think the Rexem guild has no one left and that anyone can waltz in and freeload until they die," Old Tyler said with a smile, a hint of irony aimed at Merlin.

Feeling that Merlin wasn't particularly strong and guessing her grandpa wouldn't take it seriously either, Lucia huffed and fell silent.

"Old man, you're the strongest in the guild?" Merlin asked straight out.

"No. The strongest is my son Karl. Though I am his father," Old Tyler said good-naturedly.

"Is that so? Then I suppose that means you're not weak, then?" Merlin touched the tanto at his waist.

"No, no, no, young man, you haven't understood—"

Although Old Tyler was aged and his hair was completely white, his eyes were sharp and bright, bursting with spirit. "If I rank myself second, then Karl will never be able to be called the strongest."

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue, feeling a bit annoyed looking at Old Tyler—

This old geezer.

So many tricks to showing off.

title: Chapter 8
content:
Chapter 8

Volume 3 · Chapter 8

"Since you say you're strong, then I'm at ease. Fight here?"

Merlin spread his hands, feeling the place was too cramped for a proper fight, and there were too many onlookers.

"No, it's too small here. The guild has a large enough dojo behind it. Young man, come with me."

Old Taylor didn’t waste words and turned toward the back of the guild.

Merlin thought for a moment, smiled, and followed, feeling no pressure at all.

"Everyone else, stay back. This is a private duel between me and this young man," Old Taylor said over his shoulder.

Merlin blinked, having expected a large audience, but it turned out to be an unusually private duel.

The surrounding adventurers were disappointed. They had hoped to see the old guildmaster in action, but now outsiders weren’t allowed to watch.

Alice knew the old guildmaster well—he was usually kind, but this private duel was puzzling.

"Lucia, why won’t the old guildmaster let anyone watch?"

Lucia thought for a moment, then whispered, "Grandfather is a very kind man... but he’s worried the power gap is too vast. If he defeats Merlin publicly, it might hurt his pride. A private duel avoids the mockery of onlookers."

Alice fell silent, thinking, *So that’s why... but can that arrogant Merlin really lose?* It was hard to imagine.

"But everyone knows the outcome. Merlin is just an ordinary man—he can’t win. Ever since Grandfather built the dojo behind the guild, Saint-tier powerhouses have come to challenge him every year. No one knows the details of the fights, but they all leave injured and frustrated," Lucia said indifferently.

"So strong?" Alice widened her eyes, shocked. She knew the old guildmaster was a peerless Saint-tier warrior, but Lucia’s words made him sound absurdly powerful.

"Not just that..." Lucia recalled, then said seriously, "Since Grandfather reached the Saint-tier, he has never lost a single fight."

---

The guild’s dojo behind the building.

The polished floor gleamed, and the space was vast.

Old Taylor and Merlin stood facing each other.

This highly anticipated sparring match was about to begin.

"Young man, why are you so insistent on being an adventurer in Lexham?" Old Taylor leaned on his cane, smiling as he spoke to Merlin.

"To earn endless money, then live in idle comfort until I die." Merlin spoke bluntly.

"Hahaha, you’re a straightforward one, young man." Old Taylor laughed so hard his white beard trembled.

"Don’t call me ‘young man,’ okay? Pick another title." Merlin felt awkward. Though he looked young, he was over two hundred years old—probably older than Old Taylor. Calling him "young man" was ridiculous. By rights, *he* should be calling *Taylor* "little brother."

"Then, Lord Merlin." Old Taylor paused, then continued, "Since you’re straightforward, I’ll be clear too: Lexham’s guild doesn’t tolerate freeloaders."

"I’m not a freeloader. I’m strong." Merlin patted the katana at his waist and smiled. "In my opinion, there’s no opponent in all of Great Britain who can make me take things seriously."

Old Taylor still smiled, but the arrogance radiating from Merlin made anyone uncomfortable. "As an elder, I’ll give you some advice: confidence is good for the young, but too much becomes arrogance. This world is vast—there are always stronger people out there. Even I wouldn’t dare make such reckless claims."

"Listen, old man. I *am* the ‘stronger person’ you speak of, the ‘heaven beyond heaven.’ If there’s someone above me, I’d be interested in cutting them down." Merlin replied nonchalantly.

"In all my long years, I’ve never met someone as arrogant as you. It’s sad to see how narrow-minded the youth have become, unable to see their own limits..." Old Taylor shook his head, then promised, "Fine. If you want to be an adventurer, you’ll have to show me a level of strength that surprises me."

"Couldn’t ask for more." Merlin said coolly. "Just to be safe, I’ll ask: this is a fair duel, right? Don’t come crying to me later if I smash you to pieces, old man."

Old Taylor’s forehead twitched with black lines. He felt inexplicably humiliated. How dare a powerless, non-magical ordinary man talk to him like this? Didn’t he know how strong he was?

"It will be. For us martial artists, a duel is sacred."

"Then I won’t hold back. Rest assured, I won’t take your life." Merlin flipped his katana over.

Everyone knew a katana had a sharp edge and a blunt back. To strike without killing, one only needed to use the blunt side—otherwise, the sheer power would be uncontrollable, and Old Taylor would die instantly.

Merlin wasn’t a fool. If he actually killed the guildmaster, all his efforts would be for nothing. He just needed to demonstrate his strength.

"Don’t misunderstand. You’re an ordinary man, and I’m a Saint-tier martial artist. The gap is too vast. So go ahead—attack me with all your strength. If I take a single step back, I’ll consider it my loss." Old Taylor chuckled, not taking Merlin seriously at all. This fight was just to temper the young man’s arrogance.

"Huh?" Merlin blinked, surprised. "You want me to attack you with all my strength?"

"That’s right. I’m not so shameless as to go all out against an ordinary man. Back when I charged into the Beastman Legion, my martial skills were already masterful. I made the Bemon giants weep and the Beastman Emperor’s horns snap under my hands. So go ahead—use everything you’ve got. Don’t worry about my safety."

Old Taylor took his stance, looking every bit the grandmaster—standing unshaken in the center of the dojo. Though aged, the hidden pressure he emitted was enough to make anyone outside tremble.

Merlin almost laughed. *This is a first.* No one had ever dared let him strike first before. Normally, his attacks meant instant death for his enemies, leaving no room for them to even demonstrate their skills. It was boring.

Merlin preferred giving his enemies a chance—letting them attack with all their might before cutting them down when they were at their limit. He thought that was fair. Let them know they died to someone stronger, not in confusion.

But today, Old Taylor was actually letting *him* strike first. It was surprising.

"Old man, you’re serious?"

"Absolutely. To be blunt, you’re too weak. I don’t even need to use my techniques. The sheer impact of my Saint-tier aura alone would leave you gravely injured." Old Taylor stood with his hands behind his back.

"Fine." Merlin assumed his drawing stance and said coolly, "Old man, I advise you not to blink. My draw is faster than your perception."

"Come then. Let me see what gives you the right to be so arrogant." Old Taylor narrowed his eyes.

Merlin smirked, then—

In the next instant, he drew his blade!

A second later, it was already in front of Old Taylor.

Dozen of paces closed in less than a breath—his speed was breathtaking!

The blunt edge of the katana stopped less than a centimeter from Old Taylor’s forehead, radiating killing intent. That rusted blade carried such overwhelming force!

A tidal wave of sword energy erupted, obliterating everything around Old Taylor in an instant.

Cold sweat poured down Old Taylor’s face. The towering sword energy before him filled him with terror—so icy it sent chills down his spine.

Shocked, he stumbled backward, tripping and falling hard onto his backside, looking utterly disheveled.

Merlin flourished his katana before sheathing it, then said meaningfully, "If I had used the sharp edge just now..."

"You’d already be dead." Old Taylor sat on the ground, his face deathly pale. His aged body trembled uncontrollably, and cold sweat gushed like a fountain.

*Too strong!*

*How can someone without magic or aura be this strong?*

*If I had fought back with all my strength...*

*No, even if I had, I’d still be killed in one strike!*

*Who in the world is this young man? How can he be this terrifying?*

title: Chapter 9
content:
Chapter 9

Volume 3 · Chapter 9

A tremendous boom came from the dojo behind!
The entire guild trembled several times, dust falling down.
A powerful pressure left the adventurers in the guild astonished.
Many people didn't know what was happening and began to speculate—
“This power... could the guild master have used his full strength?”
“Maybe he was just trying to scare that clueless newcomer.”
“Indeed, with such an arrogant attitude, it's normal for the old guild master to get angry.”
“The newcomer wouldn't have been killed outright by the guild master, would he?”
“No way, surely the old guild master was showing his strength to make the newcomer back off.”
“I guess the newcomer has already been scared piss-less by the old guild master, hahaha.”
The adventurers burst into laughter, only Alice felt something was off.
She had faced Merlin head‑on before; this pressure carried a killing intent, clearly from Merlin’s drawing‑slash.
Alice thought back to Merlin’s past behavior and worried—
Merlin, that reckless guy.
He wouldn’t have one‑shotted the old guild master, would he?
Then I’d become an accomplice!
Soon after.
Merlin had already left.
The setting sun’s red light shone in.
Making the already ruined dojo look even more desolate.
Old Taylor leaned on his cane, standing there with a bewildered expression, already beginning to doubt life.
Lukia stood beside him, supporting her grandfather, and said with a hint of reproach, “Grandpa, why did you go all out against an ordinary person? The neighbors were all frightened by you....
Old Taylor: No no no, I never even had the chance to use my full strength.
“I know Alice’s old flame is arrogant, but he’s just an ordinary person—what are you competing with him for, Grandpa?” Lukia continued.
Old Taylor: I wouldn’t even have a chance to compete; he really does have the grounds for his arrogance.
“Grandpa, you’re also—how old are you, getting angry at an ordinary person?” Lukia thought Grandpa was annoyed by Merlin’s arrogance, but as a Saint‑tier expert, getting angry at an ordinary person is unnecessary; look at the mess you made, though fortunately there were no casualties.
Old Taylor: They didn’t even consider me an opponent; the other side isn’t even an ordinary person! Their strength makes one’s scalp tingle....
“Thank goodness Merlin wasn’t hurt, otherwise Grandpa you’d have to take responsibility. Normally you could have driven him off with your Saint‑tier fighting spirit—was it really necessary to show your full power? From now on, curb your temper, don’t be impulsive. This time, counting the damaged buildings, we’ll have to pay a lot. Lukia said gloomily,—just a petty money‑grubber. SF3 Xiao Zhi
Old Taylor: Granddaughter, I was the one who was driven back; if Merlin hadn’t held back, you’d never see me again....
“But… Grandpa, is your strength actually greater now? Everyone in Rexelham knows this now.” Lukia sighed, feeling it will be more troublesome later.
Old Taylor: Wah wah wah, I’m wronged, it’s that Merlin who’s too strong, not me! Even if I went all out I couldn’t cause such destructive power....
Merlin’s impact was profound, to the point of alarming the Rexelham guard unit.
As the captain, Prices led a large contingent of guards straight to the guild, heading straight to the rear dojo.
Lukia heard the clatter of armor from afar; there seemed to be many, likely thinking some strong expert was causing trouble here.
Countless spear‑wielding elite guards surged in, instantly securing the area.
Prices looked a bit unkempt, stubble everywhere, shifty eyes, but his armor was polished to a mirror shine.
He strode in, drew the sword at his waist, and shouted with great vigor.
“Who’s causing trouble in Rexelham? Come out!”
“What are you shouting, Prices?” Lukia shot back with a withering glance.
“Hehehe~” Prices’ heart fluttered at that look; he especially liked beautiful women giving him a disdainful gaze, and Lukia truly was one of Rexelham’s rare beauties, making him feel delighted. “Miss Lukia, please don’t do that—I’m also acting on the Count’s orders to investigate what just happened.”
“What are you investigating?” Lukia, annoyed by Prices’ masochistic vibe, said, “My grandfather and someone else were just sparring—what’s the problem with a little commotion? Would the Count really have my grandfather go to the city guard office for tea over this?”
“No no…” Prices waved his hands repeatedly, probing, “Was it just Master Taylor sparring with someone that caused this?”
“Yeah, Grandpa lost control of his emotions and accidentally ended up like this.” Lukia felt a bit embarrassed.
“What?!” Prices’ eyes widened in shock, he glanced around, then hurried to Old Taylor’s side, fawningly smiling, “Congratulations, Master Taylor, your strength has risen five levels! Truly the pride of Rexelham, the glory of Wales, no—no, the glory of all Britain is rare indeed! Soon Queen Elizabeth herself will surely grant you an audience, Master Taylor!”
“Not… Old Taylor didn’t want to keep playing the silent gourd.”
“Sigh, Master Taylor, don’t be humble.” Prices made an exaggerated expression, “You are now the guardian deity of Rexelham; the Count seeing your progress will also be very pleased.”
“That’s not it…” Old Taylor furrowed his brows, feeling the pressure mounting.
“Don’t say that, Master Taylor, as a grandmaster of British martial arts I’ve always respected you, but you’re being too modest, putting me in a tough spot.” Prices showed a troubled expression.
“Really not…”
“I understand, Master Taylor; tomorrow I’ll tell the Count and have him send a— a banner!”
Before Old Taylor could finish explaining, Prices had already decided.
“It really wasn’t me, I’m not that…” Old Taylor muttered worriedly, looking back at the aftermath; the battle had left him hanging by a thread—Merlin may look ordinary, but his strength is unmatched across all of Britain.
I’ve lived over eighty years and never seen such a mighty swordsman; I’m still just a frog in a well.
Old Taylor still underestimated Merlin—what is little Britain? He is the world’s strongest swordsman, peerless!
The red sunset fell on Old Taylor’s aged face; before him lay ruin, and one could faintly see the tip of Merlin’s power. Merlin’s single slash nearly terrified all of Rexelham; the destructive force was extravagant.
Starting from the dojo, the sword‑qi of the drawing‑slash raged, instantly destroying everything along the way, passing through countless streets and the central plaza.
It only began to taper off at the western gate, but the western wall was still blasted open, forming a huge breach.
At that instant, the city’s residents felt a killing intent, thinking some ancient demon beast was assaulting the walls! This destructive power came from Merlin deliberately holding back, using the unsharpened side of

title: Chapter 10
content:
Chapter 10

Volume 3 · Chapter 10

The sun set.

A shocking chasm cut across the street.

Many residents had come out to gawk, exclaiming in surprise, while the guards on the western city wall were in chaos.

Merlin looked at the necklace-like object in his hand, which had a blackened iron plate attached.

This was the Adventurer’s Proof that the Guild President had personally given to Merlin. After the sparring match, old Taylor had immediately decided to recruit him into the Guild without the slightest hesitation.

That was right—Merlin had been ranked at the lowest tier: Black Iron.

This was a bit humiliating for Merlin.

Later, when Merlin had grumbled about it, old Taylor had said there was nothing he could do. The ranking system was a strict rule set by the Guild headquarters, and magic power and fighting spirit were the only criteria.

Since Merlin had neither magic power nor fighting spirit, he shouldn’t have even qualified as an adventurer. Old Taylor had made an exception this time and forced his way to recruit him.

Merlin was a talent for the Guild, and for the entire city of Rexham. That was why old Taylor had been willing to bend the rules and bring Merlin in.

After all, the stronger the people in a city, the safer it became. Just think about the village before—if not for Merlin and Alice, it would have been reduced to ashes by the goblins.

So, the strong were generally seen as the guardians of the city, highly respected. Even the high-and-mighty nobles feared losing their wealth to monsters.

Not to mention Merlin’s strength—how many high-difficulty commissions could he complete? It would greatly benefit the Guild’s future development.

Old Taylor wasn’t a fool. He had already decided to give Merlin as many privileges as possible, allowing him to act freely.

Merlin got what he wanted and was quite happy, except for this rank—Black Iron? That was a huge gap away from Alice’s Gold.

How could a defeated opponent have a higher rank than him?

That made no sense. It was truly unfair...

Merlin carefully examined the Adventurer’s Proof. It listed his basic information—

Region: Rexham.

Name: Merlin Lucifer.

Occupation: Just a villager with no magic or fighting spirit, that’s all~

Lucifer was the surname of Merlin’s family, a legitimate royal lineage. His sister’s full name was Lilith Lucifer. Humans might not recognize it, but among the demon race, the name Lucifer was thunderously famous. Their family had produced two rulers: Lucifer II, Merlin’s mother, and Lucifer III, Merlin himself. It was an illustrious noble house.

Since Merlin was no longer the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace, he could no longer use the title "Lucifer" as a Demon Lord, so he had to settle for his family surname.

As for the occupation description, Merlin was speechless. The sheer dismissive tone—what was this about? It was clear they looked down on him.

Old Taylor had explained that it wasn’t his doing. The occupation was evaluated by the Denmark headquarters, and they considered him nothing more than a villager.

Well, Merlin didn’t blame the president. He just wanted to think of some cool-sounding names—

"Cosmic Swordsman"

"Cosmic Hero"

"Cosmic Sword Master"

See? Adding "Cosmic" in front made it sound instantly awesome, right? Overflowing with dominance.

These mass-produced names fully demonstrated Merlin’s terrible naming sense and his low cultural level.

"Hehe, even though there were some setbacks, starting today, I’m an adventurer too. From now on, I can live the brainless life of grinding monsters and making money. If I get the chance, I’ll definitely buy the most luxurious house in Great Britain~"

"Don’t even think about it. Housing prices keep rising every day. The royal family has been suppressing them for years with no effect. For adventurers like us with no security, we can only rent." Alice looked somewhat melancholic as she led her little donkey.

"Don’t suddenly spread negative energy like that..." Merlin frowned.

"By the way, did you really defeat our president?" Alice was still concerned about this.

"It’s not like I defeated him. In my eyes, only death counts as a true defeat. I just displayed a little bit of my strength." Merlin said indifferently, then changed the subject. "But your president isn’t that strong. He’s pretty ordinary. The moment I drew my sword, he was so scared he fell over. If I had to compare, he’s a little stronger than the seven generals under me back in the day."

Alice fell silent. So much for the famous continent-shaking Thunder Combat Technique. So much for the paragon of Great Britain’s martial arts. So much for the battle against the Behemoth. All that bragging was useless because in front of Merlin, they were all trash!

This guy... said it so casually?

Was the president really the strongest in our Guild?

...

He didn’t even get to use a single move before being scared off...

Alice felt utterly disheartened. How many years of harsh training would it take for her to defeat Merlin and wash away her humiliation? It seemed impossible in this lifetime.

Alice, moved by the sight of the destroyed street, suddenly felt a surge of dissatisfaction. She turned her head to pick a fight. "Wasn’t what you did a bit too much? You didn’t need a large-scale attack, yet you destroyed the street."

"What’s the problem?" Merlin asked, puzzled.

"What if you accidentally hurt the residents?" Alice was quite opposed to this.

"I had it under control. I specifically chose this direction. Nothing would go wrong." Merlin said with satisfaction.

"Even if... even if no one was hurt, you destroyed the city. Aren’t you afraid the mayor will make you pay for the damages?" Alice was determined to make Merlin see his mistake.

"Ah, about that? The old president said he’d take responsibility for this. What a good man..." Merlin smiled happily.

"..." Alice was left speechless, unable to find any fault. She could only turn her face away in a huff. "Hmph."

"I’m telling you, don’t always be so serious. Learn to be more like that Lucia from your Guild—more ladylike in your speech. Otherwise, you’ll never turn things around..." Merlin looked at the washboard beside him with exasperation. She was already completely unappealing, and on top of that, she liked to meddle in other people’s business?

"I don’t want to be lectured by you. Can you just shut up?" Alice could tolerate being talked to by anyone else, but not Merlin. Just looking at him made her annoyed.

"Hmph." Merlin gave a cold laugh and swung the Adventurer’s Proof in his hand. "Alice, watch your tone with me. From now on, we’re colleagues. We’ll be seeing each other often."

"What are you so proud of? A Black Iron adventurer—the lowest of the low. My status is higher than yours by a mile!" Alice couldn’t stand Merlin’s smug expression and retorted sarcastically.

"..." Merlin’s heart twinged. What could he do about having no magic or fighting spirit? It was still better than having no job. "You’re just a rank higher. Tomorrow, I’ll take on a huge commission and earn in one go what you couldn’t make in ten years. That’ll drive you crazy!"

"Heh, good luck with that..." Alice didn’t want to argue with Merlin anymore. She turned and led her donkey away, but then suddenly remembered something. "Oh right, I don’t owe you any favors now. We’re even. Remember that!"

"Right, exactly. Let’s never see each other again!" Merlin, annoyed by Alice’s haughty demeanor, was also happy to end their temporary partnership.

"Hmph~!"

They both let out a cold snort and walked off in opposite directions.

Merlin stopped in his tracks and pulled out his pitifully thin money pouch.

The last bit of money had gone to taxes. A few horse race tickets lay quietly inside.

Merlin panicked and looked up at the darkening sky, awkwardly muttering to himself,

"Oh no..."

"Where am I going to sleep tonight?"

title: Chapter 11
content:
Chapter 11

Volume 3 · Chapter 11

The place where Alice lived was relatively ordinary.

Rent in Lexem wasn't cheap at all.

A few hundred gold coins per month, even though Alice could earn a few thousand gold coins from a single commission each month.

But after deducting 60% to repay the Holy Church, what was left had to cover various expenses, including rent.

So Alice lived something like a paycheck-to-paycheck life, with not much in savings.

After finishing dinner, Alice planned to rest for a day and then head straight to work the next day. After all, she hadn't made money from her last commission, and if she didn't work hard, she'd be sleeping on the streets next month.

In the bathroom.

Alice was soaking in a hot bath, trying to relieve her exhaustion.

Her fair, slender body looked incredibly alluring in the clear hot water, a few strands of silver hair resting on her fragrant shoulders.

Alice let out a long breath, feeling as though she had suddenly come back to life. The unpleasantness of encountering Merlin, that demon, was instantly swept away.

Thinking about how Merlin had boasted earlier, claiming he would take on a huge number of commissions just to spite her — she couldn't help but sneer.

"Hmph! In your dreams. Who would hand work over to a low-level Iron-tier? Besides, you can hardly even receive quests above S-rank. How do you expect to spite me? Heh heh heh."

Alice giggled, her laughter echoing through the bathroom as she felt that no matter what, she lived far better than some jerk like Merlin. Could an Iron-tier's income possibly exceed a Gold-tier's? Don't make me laugh.

Alice felt it was necessary to offer a prayer — a proper curse against Merlin.

"Dear Gods, please let this bastard Merlin sleep on the streets, become homeless, and live the life of a vagrant. It would be best if he suffered from hunger and cold, to the point where nobody buys his matches."

At that moment, Merlin stood by the roadside.

"Sir, would you like to buy a box of matches?"

"Ma'am, buy a box of matches, waterproof ones."

A few passing couples ignored Merlin and simply walked around him.

Penniless and without a single valuable item on him, the only thing Merlin had left was that box of waterproof matchsticks for picnics, which was probably worth two copper coins.

Having decided he didn't want to sleep on the roadside, Merlin had no choice but to take up the role of a matchstick-selling Demon Lord, though it barely worked.

Merlin sighed, squatted by the road, and lit a matchstick.

The dim yellow flame made Merlin see beautiful large houses with burning fireplaces, warmth radiating from within — enough to make him feel cozy.

With a blissful expression, Merlin didn't even notice the fire burning his fingers.

Still lost in his fantasy and unsatisfied, he lit a second matchstick.

Under the flickering light, Merlin saw glossy, delicious roasted sausages, a continuously rotating turkey, and freshly baked cakes.

He swallowed hard, feeling that wasn't enough, and quickly lit a third matchstick.

This time he saw Alice soaking in a hot bath, looking utterly content — something to be envied.

Merlin watched Alice calmly... slowly...

"Nah, let's just go to Alice's place and mooch off her food and drinks!"

Alice was half-asleep in the bathtub, drifting in a lazy state, absolutely not wanting to leave. Her mind was full of thoughts about how wonderful it would be if she didn't have to work.

*Ding dong.*

The doorbell rang, shattering the quiet in the house.

*Ding dong ding dong ding dong—*

"I'm coming! I'm coming!"

Alice hurriedly climbed out of the tub, put on slippers, and quickly wrapped a towel around herself.

"Seriously, who is it? Rushing me like this..."

Alice came out of the bathroom and walked toward the door, remembering Lucy had said her landlord was already pressuring her about rent.

What a pain. Isn't it only a few days late?

Do I really need to be harassed like this? What a wicked, money-grubbing landlady!

Alice was a bit upset, feeling that this old hag landlord only knew how to squeeze her blood and sweat, never understanding how difficult it was for a girl living alone.

Not even a few days behind on rent, and she was already knocking urgently at the door, more eager than dropping her grandson off at school.

Bristling inside, but still having to greet the landlord with a forced smile since she was, after all, her landlord.

"Landlady, I just got back and you're already..."

Alice opened the door with a bright smile, only to see the wicked Merlin standing there. Her carefully forced smile instantly froze on her face.

"Oh, good evening, Alice. Good to see you again, hehe~"

Merlin scratched his head and cheekily greeted Alice.

Alice's delicate brows furrowed deeply. She wondered how this jerk had even found her place.

"Do you always dress this sexily...?" Merlin's eyes drifted over Alice's figure. Even though she was flat-chested, a girl just out of the bath had a unique charm all the same.

Alice was exactly like that now, wrapped only in a towel with plenty exposed, and the thought that she wore nothing underneath made one's imagination run wild.

"Don't look around like that, you pervert!" Alice blushed and quickly retreated indoors, using the door to shield her body before poking her head out. "How did you find this place?"

"I saw your donkey tied downstairs and a groom nearby, so I just asked around. He told me the adventurer who uses a washboard lives here..."

Merlin answered in a remarkably honest tone.

"I'm not a 'washboard'! If I push them together, I still have breasts! You jerk!" Alice said, her face flushing red with anger.

"Does that count? If I push them together, I also have..." Merlin added, completely missing the point.

"Get lost! What are you even doing here?!" Alice glared with hostility.

At this moment, Alice looked exactly like a little dog baring its teeth at an enemy, trying to intimidate it away.

"Alice, how about letting me stay at your place for a few days?" Merlin asked tentatively, in a商议ing tone.

Alice instantly went expressionless, no longer flustered. So Merlin had come to mooch off someone else's hospitality — that meant she had every right to put on airs.

"G, U, N!"

"Please don't be like this, Alice..." Merlin flicked his handsome blonde hair, attempting to seduce Alice. "On such a lonely night, don't you feel like you need a man? My shoulder is free for you to lean on anytime. You just need to let me stay for a few days, and once I find a place, I'll leave you with wonderful memories."

Alice's face paled, her eyes going hollow. Because her hostility toward Merlin was so strong, his seduction attempt was completely ineffective.

If Alice were strong enough, she would have immediately drawn her slender sword and chased after Merlin, hacking wildly to avenge her earlier humiliation!

"Well? Alice, consider it. I'm actually quite expensive. When I used to work as a male host, chatting with me for a while cost thousands of gold coins. But today, since we're old acquaintances, it's free~" Merlin waved his hand magnanimously, acting as if money meant nothing.

"Go away! Don't stand within five meters of my door!"

Alice shouted angrily and slammed the door shut — but it got stuck. Looking down, she had somehow pinched Merlin's foot!

"Ouch, ouch, ouch!"

"Take your foot away! You annoying guy!"

Alice, in a huff, repeatedly and fiercely crushed Merlin's foot, making him grit his teeth in pain.

"Don't be like this, Alice. Can't we at least show a bit of consideration?"

"Go away! Consideration for what? I don't owe you anything anymore! We're strangers!" Alice said resolutely.

"This isn't a transaction now, is it? Aren't we old acquaintances? We should talk about feelings~" Merlin said shamelessly.

"Oh, so now that there are no chips to bet with, you want to talk about feelings? Shameless!" Alice clenched her silver teeth and said angrily.

"There's no bond between us!"

"Get lost already! You thick-skinned..."

title: Chapter 12
content:
Chapter 12

Volume 3 · Chapter 12

"Alice, we're barely friends, right? Is it okay if I stay for one night? I know it's rude to bother a girl living alone this late, but I'm a decent person and I won't do anything to you."

Merlin dared to say this precisely because he had no interest in a washboard chest, and at two hundred years old, he was already immune to the vast majority of the opposite sex.

"What kind of friend?! Disgusting! Don't shamelessly try to claim a relationship with me!" Alice was already on the verge of resorting to force. Even though she couldn't beat him, she could certainly kick him out.

"Don't you realize how lucky you are? You survived under my blade. My rule is simple: anyone I don't kill becomes my friend~" Merlin took a step forward.

"Don't come over! Stop talking to yourself and just die!"

Alice couldn't take it anymore. She raised her long leg and delivered a flying kick.

In Merlin's perception, that moment played out in slow motion. Alice raised her leg high, and her bath towel lifted in a scientifically accurate manner, revealing the mysterious area between her thighs in faint glimpses—

Holy light! Dark healing! Pixelation! All of it flashed through his mind at once!

Merlin's eyes widened in terror, his expression filled with complex emotions.

Ah~! Oh great gods!

I swear I didn't mean to look.

Although I admit this was a moment of physical and mental pleasure.

But once I knew she had a washboard chest, it became completely uninteresting.

If this world truly had an unexplored Eden, I suppose this is what it would look like....

Merlin still had time to act out his inner drama, leaving people speechless, as he Q E'd a small fart.

"Pfft!" Alice's foot slammed hard into Merlin's face, sending him flying backward.

"Don't come harassing me! Hmph~!"

Alice slammed the door shut and hid behind it, her heart pounding.

Her chest rose and fell, clearly unsettled. But after kicking Merlin, she felt secretly thrilled.

Oh my god! I did it!

I kicked Merlin!

I actually kicked the Demon Lord of the First Hall!

So satisfying! It's like revenge, hehehe....

A smile involuntarily appeared on Alice's face. She was genuinely happy.

She was also a bit foolish. Although she had kicked him, Merlin had seen everything clearly. Both sides knew who really lost out.

Alice didn't want any connection with Merlin, so after her satisfying kick, she decided to return to the bathroom to continue soaking while the water was still warm.

Outside.

Merlin touched his aching nose. His infiltration had failed, which was rather awkward.

He hadn't expected Alice to have such a foul and stubborn temper—completely immune to both soft and hard tactics.

Merlin felt he needed to come up with another plan. Rexer himself had no acquaintances here. If he couldn't extort Alice, who else could he extort?

Just as Merlin was standing there at a loss, an elderly woman in a silk dress, carrying a small leather bag, walked over. She wore light makeup, her white hair was curled, her skin had grown pale with age, and her red-lipsticked lips stood out prominently.

Merlin had seen enough of the world to recognize that this kind of attire, subtly exuding a petit-bourgeois flair, meant she was either nobility or someone who controlled resources.

The old woman walked straight up to Merlin and immediately asked, "Who are you? What are you doing in front of my house?"

"Your house?" Merlin was taken aback.

"This is my house. I just rented it to Miss Alice," the old woman nodded.

Merlin looked at the woman in front of him. So she was the landlady.

Wait! I know how to get in! Ohohohoho....

"Cough!" Merlin cleared his throat and said calmly, "I'm Alice's husband."

"Hmm?" The landlady was visibly surprised. "Miss Alice got married? She was single just last month...."

"We fell in love at first sight and had a flash marriage," Merlin lied, trying to establish a connection with Alice first.

"I see. But Miss Alice has a washboard chest, a terrible temper, an unlovable personality, and she's extremely stingy. It's surprising that someone would fall in love with her at first sight," the landlady thoroughly roasted Alice.

Yes yes yes! Exactly right!

So other people's opinions match mine!

Look at all of Alice's flaws, and yet she acts so haughty every day?

Merlin nodded vigorously, and his resentment from being kicked eased slightly.

"You look like such a distinguished gentleman. It's really a pity that you'd marry Miss Alice," the landlady said with a hint of sympathy.

Merlin felt very comfortable and extremely happy. "It's fine. For the peace of Britain, if I don't go to hell, who will!"

"At such a young age and already possessing this kind of觉悟, our eternal sun nation will surely rise among the nations of the world," the landlady seemed to be a progressive thinker.

Merlin smiled awkwardly, thinking, Sorry, miss, I'm actually older than you.

"But why are you standing outside?" the landlady asked, puzzled.

"Well...." Merlin scratched his head and said awkwardly, "Alice and I had a fight. She got angry and won't let me in."

"Is that so? Miss Alice's temper is too bad. You've really suffered," the landlady shook her head and said in an experienced tone, "Arguments between couples are normal. A couple that never argues isn't really a couple. But driving you out is a bit excessive."

"Yes! That woman is too much!" Merlin chimed in from the side.

"Since I'm here, let me help mediate." The landlady was going to intervene.

"Thank you so much..." Merlin couldn't have asked for a better opportunity to borrow someone else's strength. He thought—

Hiahiahia!

Alice, take this!

I'm throwing my landlady at you!

Inside the room.

Alice had just stepped into the bathtub and let out a satisfied sigh when something awkward happened.

"Ding dong ding dong ding dong."

Alice immediately furrowed her delicate brows and shot up, splashing water everywhere.

Gripping her fists, she shouted at the top of her lungs.

"Merlin! You bastard! Don't push your luck!"

Alice didn't even dry her body, just wrapped the towel around herself and walked out of the bathroom.

She went to her room, retrieved her slender sword, and estimated she was going to fight to the death with Merlin.

Furious, Alice rushed to open the door, brandishing her slender sword triumphantly, and opened her mouth to say—

"Are you done yet? Look at you, you want to—!!!"

Alice's lines were cut short before she could finish, swallowed back into her stomach. Her expression turned utterly astonished.

In front of her was Merlin with a meaningful smile, and the slightly bowed landlady stood before him, now looking at Alice with a face like cold frost.

Merlin felt like he was mentally overwhelming Alice from under the landlady's legs, and she had no way to counter it.

"....Good evening, landlady.... It's been a while, ha...." Alice's face changed quickly. Her smile was uglier than a cry, and she cursed Merlin to the heavens in her heart. This was going to kill me!

"Alice..." The landlady paused and said in a very serious tone, "The lease agreement clearly states that you are not allowed to wield weapons inside the house."

"Your behavior clearly violates the spirit of the contract. I'm unwilling to rent to a tenant who randomly causes damage."

title: Chapter 13
content:
Chapter 13

Volume 3 · Chapter 13

Merlin stood behind the landlady, wearing a smirk that begged for a punch, clearly mocking Alice.

Did she think this would stop her from flying into a rage in front of the landlady?

A flicker of grievance rose in Alice’s heart. She couldn’t understand why the landlady was standing with Merlin.

As much as she wanted to curse him out right then, she had to mind her manners in front of the landlady.

“I… I wasn’t sword-fighting or anything! I was just exercising~”

Alice smiled like a flower—one second a ravenous wolf, the next a docile little lamb.

“Exercising doesn’t usually involve charging out with a sword, does it? I almost thought Miss Alice was about to attack someone,” the landlady said sternly.

“Exactly! What nonsense is this?! Brandishing a sword in someone else’s house—what kind of behavior is that?! Put that sword away at once!” Merlin chimed in from behind, speaking with the authority of a man of the house.

“You—! What are you—? How dare you shout at—” Alice couldn’t stand Merlin’s shameless bullying. She raised her sword to vent her anger, but the landlady immediately intervened.

“Miss Alice, please watch your attitude…”

“…Sorry. I just got a little carried away,” Alice forced out, her furious expression vanishing as she plastered on a polite smile.

Merlin was overjoyed inside. He loved it when Alice was so furious she could barely contain herself, yet had no way to retaliate.

“Miss Alice, even though I’m an outsider, I feel I must say this: you’ve only been married a short time. Small disagreements are inevitable, so you should both show restraint and understanding. Constant arguing isn’t good for your relationship.” The landlady spoke earnestly.

Merlin struggled to keep from laughing. The landlady had just handed him the perfect opportunity. It looked like he’d be staying in Alice’s place for sure now!

“Eh?! Marriage?! What marriage?!” Alice froze, her mind filled with question marks.

“No need to hide it. I know you’re upset, but kicking your own husband out—isn’t that going a bit too far? And drawing your sword at every turn? This isn’t a joke. Marital disputes should be resolved through discussion, not violence.” The landlady spoke seriously.

“That’s not true! I have nothing to do with this guy!” Alice gritted her teeth, glaring at Merlin. What on earth had this bastard told the landlady?!

“Hmm?” The landlady looked at Merlin in surprise.

“Alice, why must you be like this? I’ve already apologized. Don’t be so angry. Why keep insisting we’re not married like that?” Merlin quickly turned the situation to his advantage, making things even more confusing.

The landlady instantly understood the situation—Alice must be speaking out of anger. “Yes, Miss Alice. Marriage is sacred. You shouldn’t just deny it on a whim. I can see your husband loves you very much. Since he’s sincerely apologized, let this little unpleasantness pass.”

“No! We’re enemies! We’re nothing like that at all!” Alice explained, aggrieved. She turned and glared at Merlin, brandishing her rapier as if ready to fight to the death. “You bastard! How dare you slander my reputation!”

“Miss Alice, if you keep this up, I’m afraid I won’t be able to continue renting my house to you. It seems you can’t control your emotions. I’m worried that one day, in a bad mood, you might… tear my house down…” The landlady’s expression darkened as she saw Alice raising her rapier threateningly.

Merlin, standing behind her, was ecstatic. *Now she’s stuck, huh? If she doesn’t let me stay, she’ll lose her place too. Perfect!*

“H-How could that be?! I don’t usually draw my sword at home…” Alice forced a smile that looked more pained than crying, her heart seething with resentment.

“Then could you please calm down and put the sword away?” the landlady suggested.

Alice trembled with rage, cursing Merlin silently in her mind. But under the landlady’s pressure, she had no choice but to lower her sword.

This place was great—close to the Adventurers Guild, well-equipped, reasonably priced. It’d be hard to find another like it in Lexham. She didn’t want to ruin this.

“Miss Alice, I hope you can show some restraint. After all, marriage is a matter between two people. Mutual understanding can resolve any conflict.” The landlady urged.

“Mmm.” Alice nodded, surprisingly not arguing. She could see that the more she explained, the worse it looked. She decided to stop defending herself. Once the landlady left, she’d settle the score with Merlin.

The landlady turned to Merlin. “You should go back inside too. It’s the middle of the night—if the neighbors see you’ve been kicked out, they’ll laugh.”

“Thank you. I didn’t expect our private matters to trouble you. Truly sorry.” Merlin said, then swaggered inside. To sell the act, he even wrapped an arm around Alice’s waist. “Dear, don’t be mad anymore. Let’s live happily together!”

Alice’s heart burned with fury. Her silver teeth ground together audibly. She could feel the heat of Merlin’s large hand through her towel, pressing against her waist.

Her face flushed crimson with suppressed anger and humiliation. She shot Merlin a venomous glare, brimming with killing intent.

“…What’s that look for?” Merlin felt a cold sweat trickle down his forehead.

Alice, at her wit’s end, secretly jabbed her elbow hard into Merlin’s chest, forcing him to back off.

Merlin stumbled back a couple of steps, clutching his chest, a hint of displeasure in his heart.

“Ahem!” The landlady ignored their silent struggle and interjected, “Miss Alice, if possible, please settle this month’s rent.”

“Oh, right. I’ll go get the money…” Alice managed a strained smile, thinking to herself that it was a good thing the knight couple, the Smiths, had given her some money. It’d be just enough for the rent.

After Alice turned and left, Merlin let out a sigh of relief. *Looks like I’ll be able to freeload here—free food, free lodging. What a steal…*

The landlady handed Merlin a spare key. “Sir, I’ll give you a spare key.”

“This…?” Merlin looked at the key, confused.

“Miss Alice still has a bad temper. If you ever get kicked out again, you can use this key to get back inside.” The landlady smiled kindly.

“You… are really too kind…” Merlin’s emotions were mixed. *She’s even giving me a key to the house? Does that mean I can just live here whenever I want?*

“Miss Alice may have a bad temper, but she’s a good girl. It’s hard for a young woman to live alone. I was truly happy to see she’d gotten married.” The landlady’s voice carried a touch of emotion. “I still remember when she first arrived, dragging her suitcase, sweating profusely as she searched all over Lexham for a place to stay. It was pitiful. It reminded me of my younger self, struggling alone, working hard until I met my partner and finally found happiness.”

Merlin turned his head in surprise, thinking to himself:

*Alice’s life…*

*…has really been that hard?*

*That sounds… pretty tragic.*

*Did I… get the better end of the deal?*
