title: Chapter 14
content:
Chapter 14

Volume 3 · Chapter 14

"Miss Alice's life is quite difficult. She often goes to big discount events, and the new clothes she gets each season are limited. I remember when she was looking for a place to live, she couldn't find a suitable one and ended up sleeping in a tavern—that's no place for a young lady. When she came to me, I mostly out of sympathy gave her the lowest price. I truly wanted to help this girl living alone."

Merlin listened to the landlady’s words, his heart stirred—not out of sympathy for Alice, but in surprise at her lifestyle. He had always assumed this ironing board lived more comfortably than he did.

Merlin suddenly remembered he was currently playing the role of Alice’s husband, so he forced a smile and awkwardly said, "I… I’ll thank you on Alice’s behalf."

"Maybe if my daughter had a child, she’d be around Miss Alice’s age. Perhaps that’s why I felt a connection," the landlady laughed.

Merlin didn’t know how to respond. He thought, *Humans really are emotional creatures… Wait! I’m not human anymore—I’m a demon now, right? It seems I’ve grown more indifferent to human emotions. Is that a good or bad thing?*

"Actually, this old woman is saying all this because I hope you’ll take good care of Miss Alice. The pressures of life can be suffocating alone, but with two people sharing the burden, it’s nothing at all," the landlady said with a warm smile.

"I will… take good care of her…" Merlin forced a smile, thinking—

*Sorry.*

*We’re not married.*

*And we’re enemies!*

*The kind that start fighting within three seconds of seeing each other…*

(??ω?? ?)

◆

After collecting the rent, the landlady left, reminding Merlin and Alice not to argue.

Alice beamed and shook her head, saying they wouldn’t, looking very polite.

But the moment the door closed—

"Merlin, you bastard! How dare you slander my reputation! Die!"

Alice drew her rapier, a cold gust swirling as she thrust it straight at Merlin.

Merlin smirked, effortlessly pinching the blade between two fingers, stopping it in its tracks.

"Miss Alice, calm down. Don’t be so worked up."

"You bastard!" Alice found her rapier immovable, as if clamped by iron tongs. The power gap was simply too vast.

"I’m not a bastard. Right now, I’m your husband. Don’t swing your sword at me—do you want to be a widow?" Merlin said with a laugh.

"Shut up! You shameless scoundrel!" Alice’s face flushed red as she cursed in fury.

"Just behave, okay? Don’t be so hot-headed. You’ll disturb the neighbors." Merlin flicked his fingers, sending Alice stumbling back two steps. "And don’t push it. If I get serious, this house will be reduced to splinters in an instant. I can just walk away unscathed, but you’ll have to pay for the damages. Think carefully before drawing your sword at me again."

"I…" Alice hesitated, rapier raised. She thought it through—if she wrecked the place, she’d be the one at a loss. So she sheathed her sword and switched to verbal abuse and physical struggle. "Get out of here! This is my home!"

"I’m just staying for a while. I don’t plan on stealing your house," Merlin said, lounging on the sofa like a boss, casually grabbing a banana and starting to eat.

What truly infuriated Alice was that after finishing, Merlin nonchalantly tossed the peel onto the floor. Did he not realize how much effort it took to mop?!

"I won’t allow it! Get out! You’re not allowed to stay here for even a second!" Alice marched over and grabbed Merlin’s collar.

Alice wasn’t dressed much to begin with—just a towel wrapped around her, which was both sexy and alluring. If Merlin weren’t so composed, he might have found his breathing quickening and his blood rushing.

"Miss, don’t be like this. I’m already in. You’re not getting rid of me…" Merlin shamelessly refused to budge.

"You scoundrel! Get out! Leave my house now!" Alice pressed her knee into the sofa, causing the towel to gap slightly, revealing a mysterious glimpse of what lay beneath.

"Why are you so stingy? I’m just staying for a bit. Once I find a proper place, I’ll move out," Merlin sighed helplessly, thinking, *This ironing board really is petty.*

"G、U、N!" Alice tightened her grip on Merlin’s collar and shook him violently, turning him into a human rattle.

Merlin’s vision blurred back and forth, but one constant remained—Alice’s chest was as flat as a plain, like she was wearing a silver-scaled breastplate underneath.

Merlin genuinely worried he might headbutt her ironing board and crack his skull, so he reached back and grabbed Alice’s butt, giving it a hard squeeze.

"Ahhh!!!"

Alice shrieked, her face burning red as she stumbled back, clutching her butt. The spot he’d grabbed throbbed painfully.

She had thought Merlin was a proper man, so she hadn’t been on guard. Who knew he was a fake? In a moment of carelessness, he’d taken advantage of her.

Tears welled in Alice’s eyes. Being groped by Merlin was a humiliating disgrace.

"You… you you you… you pervert! Sex maniac! I’ll fight you to the death…"

Merlin looked a bit dazed, flexing his hand. The feel was unexpectedly pleasant—firm and bouncy.

"Miss Alice, to be honest, your butt feels way better than your chest. Clearly, the fat’s all in the wrong place. Ha ha…"

"Shut up! Get out now!" Alice didn’t dare get too close to Merlin anymore, afraid of further harassment.

"Heh heh." Ignoring Alice, Merlin got up and dashed into the bedroom, flopping onto the bed in a starfish position. The room was filled with a girlish fragrance. "Such a soft bed, Alice. You really know how to enjoy life~"

"Get off my bed! Are you even clean? Don’t just lie there!" Alice was losing patience. She stormed into her room—if she could beat Merlin, she’d have hacked him into eighteen pieces by now.

"From today on, this bed is mine. You can sleep on the sofa. Decision made!" Merlin showed no restraint.

"Get off!" Alice scrambled onto the bed and kicked Merlin off, guarding her territory before shoving the shameless man out of her room with all her might.

"What do you even want?! This is my home! Get out now!"

"I’m just staying for a while. I don’t plan on overstaying," Merlin spread his hands, feigning innocence.

"Why should I?! I don’t owe you anything!" Alice said sternly.

"We go way back. Letting me stay for a bit won’t kill you," Merlin sighed.

"No!" Alice’s tone was absolute.

Merlin had no choice but to turn and flop onto the sofa, lazily saying, "Fine, I won’t fight you for the bed. Sleeping on the sofa should be okay, right? That’s not too much to ask."

"Bastard! Today, either you die or I do!" Alice stomped over barefoot, only to step on the banana peel Merlin had thrown earlier. Her body instantly suspended in midair. "Aaaaaah!"

In that split second—

Merlin, out of goodwill, reached to catch the falling Alice, grabbing the back of her towel.

But since the towel was loosely wrapped, it tore away with a *rip* under Merlin’s grip.

Alice instantly became completely naked, spinning in midair like a tiny tornado before *slamming* into the floor with an intimate impact.

"Uh…" Merlin’s forehead veins throbbed as he stared at the motionless, bare-bottomed Alice on the floor, his emotions a tangled mess. "Miss Alice? Alice, are you okay?"

Naked Alice didn’t respond—she had probably passed out.

Merlin scratched his head, unfolded the towel, and draped it over Alice, then proceeded to perform a *placement play*—

"Miss Alice, my condolences."

"Tonight, your bed is mine."

"And you… can sleep nicely on the floor, pu pu~"

title: Chapter 15
content:
Chapter 15

Volume 3 · Chapter 15

The next morning, bright and early.

Poor Alice woke up to find herself still on the cold floor.

She really had spent the night on the ground, still wrapped in a bath towel, and nothing untoward seemed to have happened.

Alice, in a daze, heard the sizzling sound of a frying pan—someone was using the kitchen.

Where am I?
Who am I?
What am I supposed to do?

Alice’s head was foggy, her thoughts sluggish. Probably from bumping her forehead last night.

She slowly climbed up from the floor, her body aching from sleeping on the cold hard surface all night.

Rubbing her sleep-crusted eyes, she saw someone busy in the kitchen. Oh right—
That damn Merlin!

That bastard invaded my territory!
And he even tripped me with a banana peel...

This scoundrel, I have to kick him out!

Merlin finished making breakfast and walked out carrying two plates of fried eggs.

Don’t let his usual demeanor fool you—he could cook. With an apron on, he almost looked like a proper homemaker.

No wonder he was the rising star of the gigolo world. He knew that cooking was a surefire way to win a woman’s favor.

After deep thought last night, Merlin decided that to freeload here long-term, he needed to show goodwill. Making an enemy of Alice would only backfire.

So Merlin resolved to be charming, to act like a mature man. If Alice fell for it, he could stay as long as he wanted. This was purely pragmatic, like a professional’s polite smile—no real feelings involved.

What did a girl living alone lack most?
Safety, of course. They often felt lonely, lost, helpless, even isolated in their empty homes. They craved companionship.

The cunning Merlin saw this as his opening. He’d do his best not to seem repulsive, and instead, show consideration everywhere. Slowly, he’d erode Alice’s defenses and become a permanent fixture here.

Then he could exploit her however he pleased, whenever he felt like it.

But Merlin hadn’t considered one thing: Alice’s hatred for him had already skyrocketed beyond the stratosphere. The chance of her falling for him was astronomically low.

For a normal girl, meeting a handsome, considerate man might lead to... well, certain developments after just one breakfast.

Merlin carried the fried eggs over and saw Alice awake, her forehead still a little red, glaring at him with pure rage.

"Morning, Miss Alice. Did you have a good dream last night?"

He placed a plate of eggs in front of Alice, then calmly sat down, picking up his knife and fork.

"You bastard! I’ll kill you!"

Furious, Alice scrambled to her feet without a second thought—only for the bath towel to slip off, revealing her completely naked body. Pale skin, alluring collarbones—her entire figure was exposed in the morning sunlight.

Merlin’s expression turned awkward. He gave Alice’s body a once-over, then let out a teasing whistle.

"Whew~ B"

A cold draft brushed against her bare skin, and Alice finally realized—she hadn’t put on any clothes after her bath last night.

Her face burned crimson, horror dawning on her. She’d been seen naked! The sheer humiliation was unbearable.

"Aaaaaah!"

Shame exploded within her, and Alice finally reacted like a normal girl. In a flash, she crouched down, snatched up the bath towel, and covered her vital parts.

"Miss Alice, you’re so enthusiastic. Treating me to a show first thing in the morning—I’m flattered." Merlin grinned, cutting into his eggs with his fork. "Since you’re so eager, I’ll give you my honest review. Aside from your chest, everything else is pretty decent~"

.....Y-You—!

Alice’s face burned even hotter. She shouted at Merlin, "You’ll regret this!"

"Miss Alice, please calm down. Starting the day this angry isn’t good for your health." Merlin looked at Alice, still crouched on the floor, and chuckled. "Come eat something. Try my Demon Lord-style fried eggs. To be honest, I’ve only made these for my sister before. You’re the first human I’ve cooked for—consider yourself honored."

"You stole my house, slept in my bed, and now you’re eating my food! You thief!" Alice’s eyes welled with tears as she kept backing away, planning to retreat and regroup. She was in no state to fight right now—she needed to put on clothes first. "Just you wait! I’m not done with you! Nyaaah!"

Merlin watched Alice leave, shaking his head as she stumbled away, clumsily wrapping herself in the towel.

This wasn’t how the script was supposed to go.

Normally, if someone made you breakfast, shouldn’t you be overwhelmed with gratitude?

"Damn you, Merlin! I’ll get my revenge someday!"

"I’m warning you, I won’t let this slide!"

"One of these days, I’ll beat you up every single day until you can’t fight back, and you’ll have no choice but to be my lowly servant!"

Alice stormed back to her room, cursing under her breath. But as she turned, she froze. The room looked... clean. Spotless, even. The blanket was neatly folded.

She hadn’t had time to tidy up yesterday when she got back—it had been a mess. But now... clearly, Merlin had cleaned it.

Alice had assumed Merlin would’ve trashed the place, but reality proved her wrong.

Wrapped in her dry towel, Alice sat on the bed in a daze. Maybe Merlin really was just here to stay the night... not to cause trouble.

Then she suddenly remembered something important. She rushed to open the drawer under her wardrobe and found her underwear from yesterday—freshly laundered, neatly folded, and placed inside.

This meant... Merlin had touched her underwear. He might’ve even smelled it!

The thought of Merlin sniffing her underwear with that lecherous grin made her skin crawl... So perverted...

Alice felt a little lightheaded. She pressed a hand to her forehead and thought—

What about the rest of my underwear?
Has that perverted Demon Lord defiled all of them?

Outside, Merlin finished his breakfast, deep in thought.

Alice was turning out to be a fortress of steel—way harder to crack than he’d expected. His "handsome man" strategy didn’t seem to be working.

After some consideration, Merlin realized Alice was just too stingy. Since interests were involved, then mutual benefit was the best solution. And he already had a pretty good idea.

Alice got dressed in her room, even strapping on her rapier, and marched back out, full of determination.

She slammed her hand on the table, glaring at Merlin with venom. "Let’s talk. Are you going to get out of my house or not?!"

"Alice, to be blunt—nope." Merlin shook his head. This place was nice. Nothing like his nest.

"Then what do you want?! Are you planning to just freeload here?!" Alice pressed, the veins on her forehead throbbing.

"Exactly. That’s the plan..."

"I’ll fight you to the death! Nyaaah!"

Alice was so furious she cried, drawing her rapier. If Merlin was going to bleed her dry, she’d rather go down swinging.

"Whoa, whoa, whoa! I wasn’t finished!" Merlin gestured for her to calm down before continuing. "I know freeloading is shameful."

"Then leave already!" Alice roared.

"But I’ve thought of a win-win solution. Once you hear it, you won’t kick me out..." Merlin said coolly.

"What?" Alice narrowed her eyes. She knew fighting Merlin was useless. She had to reason with him.

"Ahem!" Merlin cleared his throat and said, with uncharacteristic seriousness—

"Dear Miss Alice.

"How about we co-rent this place?"

title: Chapter 16
content:
Chapter 16

Volume 3 · Chapter 16

"Roommates?"

Alice was taken aback, assuming Merlin was pulling another deceptive trick—demons were an untrustworthy race, after all.

"Exactly. We share the house, and each of us pays half the rent. Simple, right?" Merlin spread his hands.

"Why the hell would I live with a despicable creep like you?!" Alice recoiled, both mentally and physically, at the idea of cohabiting with Merlin.

"Because you need to!" Merlin said seriously. "Think about it—your life’s pretty tight on money, isn’t it? Rent’s a huge expense, a real burden. If one person can’t handle it, two can split the load. Wouldn’t that make things a lot easier~?"

Alice hesitated, her interest piqued despite herself. She sat down in front of Merlin, silent.

Merlin’s suggestion was exactly what she’d been hoping for—halving the rent would be a dream come true. If someone shared the cost, her monthly expenses would drop significantly, and she wouldn’t be so strapped for cash.

"Roommates? Why would I room with *you*?"

"Is there anyone more suitable than me?" Merlin pointed at himself, earnest. "I’m better than some stranger, right?"

Alice pondered. Merlin was a bastard, sure, but he wasn’t a bad person. Sharing a place with a complete stranger *would* be unsafe.

"To be honest," Merlin continued, "when I cleaned your room last night, I found your little stash under the bed. When I opened it…" He gave Alice a look of disdain. "You’re *really* broke."

"...Did you touch my stash?! Did you steal my money?!" Alice demanded, panicked. That stash was her hard-earned savings—if Merlin had taken it, she’d have no recourse.

"Tsk tsk tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue, shaking his head. "Miss Alice, watch your tone. I am the proud and arrogant Demon Lord of the demon race. Stealing? That’s beneath me. It’d tarnish my noble image~"

As if someone who’d stolen another’s lamb could just forget about it.

Alice relaxed slightly but remained suspicious. She decided to count her coins later—if even one was missing, she’d fight Merlin to the death.

"Alice, think about the roommate idea…" Merlin watched her with interest, tapping his fingers slowly on the table.

Alice calmed herself. Roommates *might* work. It *would* solve her current financial struggles as a penniless spender. But she was a former Hero—living with a former Demon Lord? That was like something out of a romance novel by those bards!

"No! We’re enemies!"

"That was ages ago!" Merlin twisted his lips, looking exasperated. "We’ve both retired for so long. What’s the point of holding onto old grudges? We’re just ordinary people struggling to get by now."

Alice fell silent. The enmity between their factions had faded, but the personal resentment lingered. Still, she *did* desperately need someone to share the financial burden.

*For the sake of survival…*
Begrudgingly rooming with Merlin wasn’t impossible. He hadn’t caused any trouble, and he’d even helped clean her room. If she thought about it that way…

"You wouldn’t… harass me while we’re roommates, would you?"

Alice’s question was veiled, but Merlin understood. He glanced at her padded bra, smirked, and said, "Pfft. Don’t overthink it. How many times have I ignored you? Don’t you have a sense of your own lack of appeal?"

Alice’s face burned with anger. Being ignored so often was basically saying she had no charm as a woman. How infuriating! "...Fine, maybe. But utility bills, water, electricity, cleaning fees, maintenance—everything’s split 50-50!"

Merlin lifted his eyelids, considering. As an adventurer, making money shouldn’t be hard. He nodded. "Sure."

"My bed is mine. The bathroom—I want priority in the evenings. Same with the toilet!" Alice didn’t hold back, claiming every advantage she could.

"I want the bed too~" Merlin cared most about that.

"No way! I was here first, so I get the bed. The couch is yours!" Alice declared, dead serious.

"Fine…" Merlin shrugged. A couch was still better than a stable.

Alice thought it over and found no issues, but she had to maintain her pride. "Listen here, get your act together. I’m only agreeing to this because I *pity* you, you bastard. Don’t get the wrong idea—it’s not for any other reason. You should be *grateful* to me. Humph~!"

"Oh, I’m *so* grateful."

Merlin’s face was blank, his tone dripping with insincerity. *As if she wasn’t secretly thrilled inside.* Someone was willing to split the bills without disrupting her life.

And that was exactly the case. Alice was overjoyed. With half the usual expenses, she’d save so much each month. She could even swindle Merlin a little—what a steal!

*Hehe, this idiot Demon Lord… Let me take full advantage of him. Squeeze him dry…*

Alice’s heart swelled with glee, but then she realized—all this talk was just empty promises. She hadn’t seen a single coin from Merlin yet. How could she let him live here for free?

"Hey! If we’re roommates, you’re not freeloading this month. Hand over the money!"

Merlin froze, embarrassed. He was flat broke—where was he supposed to get the cash? "Alice, don’t be so vulgar. Always talking about money…"

"Cut the crap. No money? Get out! You’ve been stringing me along this whole time—are you messing with me?!" Alice slammed the table, glaring.

"I’ll pay you, I swear! I’ll head to the Guild right now and take on work. SSS-rank quests? Piece of cake for me. I’ll be rolling in money in no time~" Merlin was confident. He wasn’t afraid of strong enemies—he just needed dungeons to raid.

"Stop joking around! First off, can a trash-tier Black Iron like you even *accept* SSS-rank quests? And second, I’ve been an adventurer for years—I’ve *never* seen an SSS-rank quest. Do you think they just fall into your lap?!" Alice fixed Merlin with a furious stare. "Pay this month’s half of the rent *now*, or I won’t believe you’re serious."

"Relax, Alice. Have you forgotten who I am? There are seven Great Demon Lords among the demon race, and I was the strongest—the proud and arrogant one. Do you really think someone as noble as me would stiff someone on rent?" Merlin struck a haughty pose, trying to buy time.

"Bullshit! That was *then*. Now you’re a penniless bum whose only survival skill is scamming people. If I told you to sell a kidney to pay up, I bet you wouldn’t even hesitate." Alice tore into him without mercy.

*Ouch…* Does Alice really think so little of me…? Merlin reached into his back pocket and pulled out a betting ticket. "Know what this is?"

"A betting slip. Poor people’s pipe dreams…" Alice scoffed.

"Wrong! Alice, you really have no vision. That’s why I’ve always thought you were so vulgar." Merlin held up the ticket, stubborn. "Alice, listen…"

"This… is a ticket to the peak of life!"

title: Chapter 17
content:
Chapter 17

Volume 3 · Chapter 17

"Hehe."

Alice gave a cold sneer, looking down on Merlin with contempt for a man addicted to horse racing.

"What kind of life betting slip is that? It's clearly a scam to squeeze more blood and sweat from you. I know some people get rich overnight from horse racing, but I'm certain that person isn't you."

"Ugh!" Merlin was hurt inside, thinking his luck was indeed poor, but this didn't shake his bright expectations for the future. "Anyway, you have to believe in my potential. I can definitely afford the rent. If life doesn't have at least one bold gamble, it's incomplete."

"Oh, a guy working as a bartender in a tavern, yet you dare claim you have potential? That's hilarious." Alice chuckled, sitting down in front of her fried eggs, planning to devour breakfast. "I don't care—if you still want to live in my place, you must bring money. Otherwise, pack your bags and get lost early."

"Alright then." With that, Merlin snatched the fried eggs from in front of Alice.

"What are you doing? Those are mine! The eggs were bought by me!" Alice was annoyed and slammed the table.

"Since I'm paying, I don't need to pretend to be a gentleman, and I certainly don't need to curry favor with you." Merlin stuffed the fried eggs into his mouth in one bite, rubbed his hands together, and said, "It's just money, right? You wait there, I'll go sort it out right away!"

Without looking back, Merlin hummed a little tune and turned to leave. Alice, furious, threw the fork in her hand.

But Merlin moved first, and the fork stuck into the door with a "buzz" vibration.

"You bastard, don't come back to bother me!"

[Package SF Light Novel]

Later, at the guild.

"AAAAAHHHH!"

"Edward! Edward, what's wrong with you?"

"Why are you running so slow today?!"

"It must be another conspiracy! A monopolistic conspiracy!"

Merlin let out a string of screams in the guild, his betting slip crushed tightly in his hand.

Horse racing was fairly popular in Great Britain, and the crystal screens in the guild would broadcast live. Many adventurers played this game, but someone who went all-in like Merlin was indeed rare.

Lilith received roses again today, and she deliberately placed them on the counter, as if showing everyone how popular she was. As expected, she was a scheming slut. Hearing Merlin's wails, she couldn't help but roll her eyes.

What a pathetic man. Probably only Alice would like him. Such a waste of good looks—obviously, ducks are more profitable than this.

Lilith gave Merlin this evaluation in her heart. Even now, she couldn't figure out why Grandpa Taylor had given a mere ordinary adventurer like Merlin such special treatment. Could it be that he's an illegitimate child?

[Package SF Light Novel]

Although he was the lowest-ranked iron adventurer, he had violated guild rules.

Moreover, yesterday's street compensation was entirely covered by Grandpa Taylor alone.

Lilith found this suspicious because Grandpa Taylor had been unusually kind to Merlin lately, which made her suspicious.

As for Grandpa Taylor, he was still in his meditative state today. Last night, this old man hadn't slept at all, his mind filled with Merlin's sword-drawing technique.

As a man who had devoted his life to studying martial arts, he couldn't even see the sword-drawing movement clearly, let alone understand that bizarre destructive power.

Grandpa Taylor didn't ask Merlin who he was or why his sword-drawing technique was so exceptional, because everyone's cultivation was a secret, and asking directly would be too impolite.

Especially for adventurers, many of them had dark pasts. Everyone wouldn't ask about each other's history—this was already an unspoken rule.

"Merlin, little brother, I told you to buy Richard, not Edward." Drunk Hobbes patted Merlin's shoulder, already reeking of alcohol in the early morning, raised his neck and started gulping vodka. "Gulp gulp gulp gulp..."

Merlin was on the verge of tears, unfolded the crumpled betting slip, and his wages from working at Martha's for several months had just gone up in smoke. "Damn it, next time I'll also buy Richard."

"Richard, good then." Hobbes chuckled, looking like he had drunk too much. "Speaking of which, you're living with Alice?"

"How do you know?" Merlin was surprised.

"My place is right across from the apartment Alice rents. Last night, when I was going to the bathroom, I saw you getting kicked out by Alice. Hehe." The old man Hobbes laughed heartily, his nose red from alcohol.

"That... Merlin, it's a bit hard to explain."

"Are you bad in bed, or haven't you done your homework for several days?" Hobbes thrust his waist forward with very obvious implications.

"What the hell?! Get out of here." Merlin stared with wide eyes, feeling a bit resistant.

Hobbes casually embraced Merlin's neck, acting very familiar. "Stop pretending, we're all men, we understand. Alice always wears fake breasts, anyone can tell. Once you take them off, she becomes boring."

"Oh, that... I'm not denying it." Merlin said casually.

"So you need to vent appropriately, you know what I mean?" Hobbes raised his eyebrows.

"The vent you're talking about... is referring to?" Merlin narrowed his eyes.

"There's a secret place called Helen's Hideaway in the east of Lexar City. It's a man's paradise, a place we all know about." Hobbes spoke with a sly smile.

"Oh no." Merlin wasn't very interested, not because of the sage mode, but because he was over 2200 years old and genuinely didn't care much about the opposite sex.

"There's a special potion there. After drinking it, you'll see your wife as your dream lover. To be honest, even a pig would look beautiful, and you'll definitely submit your homework on time, and even exceed the quota." Hobbes patted Merlin's chest. "What do you think, little brother? Am I not saving your family crisis?"

"I want to make one thing clear, I'm not in that kind of relationship with Alice." After holding back for a while, Merlin explained.

"Stop pretending, everyone can see it. Alice has been single for a long time. She goes out for half a month and brings back a man. This is a case of a lonely dry stick meeting a raging fire, grabbing onto it like a wolf." Hobbes sighed. "Not to say anything else, I really sympathize with you. Alice is also a relatively rare golden adventurer, and you're just an iron adventurer. If you don't put in effort elsewhere, you probably can't handle this little wild horse."

Merlin leaned on the table silently, thinking this world was full of malice, and everyone misunderstood him and Alice as having an affair.

Compared to this rumor, Merlin was more concerned about his betting slip. What should he buy next time? Richard? Roland sounds good too.

"Hey, Alice is here. Are you going out to work today?" Hobbes greeted Alice warmly.

Alice saw Merlin lying on the table, in low spirits, and rolled her eyes, saying:

"What a pair of scum, matching each other perfectly!"

"Don't talk to me like that!"

"Hmph."

title: Chapter 18
content:
Chapter 18

Volume 3 · Chapter 18

“Merlin, your wife early this morning was like she’d taken gunpowder, seems she’s been suppressing for too long, you need to step it up.” Hobbs poked Merlin.

“She’s not my wife...” Merlin twisted his mouth.

Hobbs took a gulp of vodka and shook his head.

“It’s over, it’s over, this marriage won’t last long, sooner or later it’ll end.”

Alice came to the counter, sat down directly, looking exhausted.

“Lucia, give me a glass of milk.”

Lucia poured a glass of milk for Alice and asked in surprise, “What’s wrong? Your face looks so pale...”

“Don’t bring it up, that bastard Merlin broke into my house in the middle of the night,” Alice said angrily.

“Breaking into a lone girl’s house at midnight?” Lucia’s face turned red, thinking lewdly, “And then...”

“Then he wants to live with me.” Alice calmly took a sip of milk.

“...That’s so blunt?” A cold sweat dripped from Lucia’s forehead as she looked at Merlin’s lazy‑illness‑late‑stage demeanor, privately so proactive and enthusiastic, “And then?”

“At the time I had just finished bathing, only wrapped in a towel, he teased me with his mouth and even pinched my butt.” Alice squeezed out a few tears, very annoyed.

“Heh heh heh, that sounds a bit erotic,” Lucia’s face reddened a few more degrees, asking with a slightly excited tone, “He actually broke in at midnight and got all hands‑on‑you, oddly makes one… excited? No, makes one angry. What happened next?”

... Alice showed a very sad expression; she whispered, “After that, that bastard knocked me out with a banana, and I spent a while on the cold floor...”

“Whoosh whoosh whoosh~” Lucia’s face burned red, her mind racing with excitement, imagining something like—

Merlin sneaked into Alice’s house at night, then teased Alice, and finally couldn’t hold back and used his big banana on the living‑room floor, conquering Alice.

Even though Merlin has a woman’s face, the result was unexpectedly forceful...

“Lucia? What’s wrong with you? Your reaction is very strange....” Alice raised her eyebrows, a bit puzzled.

“Alice, you must have experienced a man’s wonderfulness, right? Quickly tell me how it felt?” Lucia asked enthusiastically.

“What?! ” Alice was bewildered, looking at Lucia as if she were a nymphomaniac.

“Didn’t you spend a wonderful night with your old lover Merlin, tangled on the cold floor, conquered by a big banana~” Lucia’s face turned bright red, not knowing what explicit scene she imagined.

“No! Lucia, stop your sexual fantasies right now!” Alice, irritated, wondered if she had said something wrong earlier.

The president, old Taylor, who had been meditating with his eyes closed, couldn’t help falling into thought—

Is Merlin really a strong one?

Why does he sound like a simple flower‑picking thief?

It must be to relax his mind, to make his strength...

No wonder it’s Merlin; a strong person’s mindset is different.

Yesterday, Arnold, who was sent flying by Merlin’s punch, also came to the Guild.

Although he was injured by the punch, a priest’s healing spell cured him.

Arnold is the son of the Duke of Austin, he would never think like a commoner to go see the doctor with a crow‑mask.

“Arnold, *burp*~”

Hobbs, being familiar with everyone, greeted Arnold, probably drunk, and started belching repeatedly.

Arnold saw Merlin standing still, thought for a moment, and walked straight over.

“Merlin, I didn’t expect you, country bumpkin, to be quite strong; I underestimated you yesterday....”

“Oh?” Merlin raised his head, gave Arnold a faint glance.

“Don’t think that because you won the duel yesterday you can claim Miss Alice’s mating rights! I won’t acknowledge that!” Arnold said with a serious expression.

“Pfft!” Alice, who was drinking milk, jolted, spitting the milk out, “Shut up! Arnold, you idiot! The mating rights of all the women in your family are for duels.”

“Last night I thought a lot; winning Miss Alice’s mating rights through a single duel is too childish and unfair to Miss Alice,” Arnold said seriously, completely ignoring Alice.

“I’ll give you credit for being sensible...” Alice relaxed a bit, continued drinking milk, still thinking he might joke about her mating rights again.

“So I decided to use a best‑of‑three system; the one who wins twice gets Miss Alice’s mating rights!” Arnold said earnestly, seeming to have thought it through.

“Pfft!” Alice’s poor cup of milk barely got a few sips before she splashed it all on the floor, “Arnold! Are you an idiot! Get out!”

“Today! I’ll avenge my disgrace!” Arnold drew his pure‑gold, diamond‑inlaid sword, “Come on, country bumpkin Merlin, I’ll prove you don’t deserve Miss Alice’s love, nor the right to mate with her! A beauty is only for the strong...”

“Excuse me, may I cut this guy down?” Alice’s face was like frost, so gloomy it could drip water, and she slowly drew her slender sword.

“Calm down, Alice, weapons fights aren’t allowed in the Guild,” Lucia smiled.

“What’s the point of you coming yourself? As a noble, shouldn’t you hire a few bodyguards to deal with me? That’s the typical rich‑kid routine,” Merlin asked with interest.

“Are you insulting me? As a noble you must have noble integrity; duels are sacred, letting others intervene is a petty act.” Arnold showed a hint of pride, continuing, “I, Arnold Austin, as the eldest son of the Earl’s family, disdain such base actions! I will win Miss Alice’s love under fair and just conditions!”

“Arnold, I have no interest in a fool like you, just go die—die, okay?” Alice said helplessly, especially annoyed by his persistent pestering.

Merlin smiled, thinking that even among nobles there are such characters, appearing lofty but actually a bit stupid, imagining the red‑coated musket squad drawing guns to duel felt…

“Come on, even though you’re a country bumpkin, I acknowledge your strength; as a rival, you’re a good opponent!” Arnold performed a few clumsy court sword techniques, not knowing who taught him, “Merlin, let’s duel!”

“Sorry, facing you I’m too lazy to even raise my hand to strike...” Merlin said lazily.

“You actually refused my duel? That’s not manly at all...” Arnold sighed.

“It’s not that; what does Alice’s mating right have to do with me? Dragging me into this is absurd?” Merlin sighed.

“Here we go again, Merlin‑san, *burp*~” Hobbs, slinging an arm over Merlin’s shoulder, reeking of alcohol, said, “Now you’re cohabiting with Alice, how can you say it’s nothing?”

“What?! You’re actually living with Alice!” Arnold stepped back, having trouble accepting reality.

“Yes, Merlin and Alice are cohabiting, now in a hot‑loving married state; you’ve missed your chance, Arnold, *burp*~” Hobbs, clearly drunk.

“No… it can’t be?” Arnold looked bewildered, his life losing meaning.

“Enough, Hobbs, are you trying to die! We’re not even cohabiting! Just the idea of sharing a rent, that bastard last night was an illegal intruder!” Alice, angry, felt the misunderstanding growing.

“It’s more than just cohabiting~” Lucia’s face flushed, speaking excitedly like a loudspeaker.

“Last night on the living‑room floor, Alice was already conquered by Merlin’s big banana! Hehe.....”

(●‘心动)

title: Chapter 19
content:
Chapter 19

Volume 3 · Chapter 19

What the hell is this?

Alice conquered by my big banana?

Countless black lines instantly fell onto Merlin's forehead.

"No, Lucia, what are you talking about!?" Alice exclaimed in panic.

"Alice-senpai has already... been conquered by the big banana..." Arnold's expression was blank, as if he had instantly transformed into a salted fish who had lost his dreams, and he knelt on the ground with a *thump*, "No! ! !"

"Merlin, you're actually pretty impressive, big banana burp~" Hobbes patted Merlin on the shoulder, then passed out drunk, lying on the table snoring loudly.

"Merlin!" Arnold stood up from the ground, his face full of grievance, "Don't run away! Let's duel!"

"Still not giving up?" Merlin frowned.

"Even if you used the big banana to defile Alice-senpai, it doesn't matter, I accept this challenge!" Arnold had turned a shade of forgiving green.

"Accept your mother's head! Don't get the wrong idea!" Alice's face flushed red, mixed with shame and indignation.

"Alright, alright, you want a duel, right? Hurry up then." Merlin assumed an impatient posture, deciding to send Arnold to the hospital to save himself the trouble of dealing with him.

".....Arnold heard Merlin's Rising Dragon Punch, and for a moment felt a bit uneasy, so he came up with a different idea. "Cough, measuring a man's charm is not just about martial force, but also personal ability. I've decided to show myself off properly, defeat you from the side, make Alice-senpai change her mind, and let her see my shining points."

"Oh, and then?" Merlin propped his chin up, speaking with general interest.

Arnold groped around in his bosom for a while, took out a piece of parchment, and slapped it in front of Merlin, like issuing a challenge. "This! This is a Denbighshire commission released recently, all Welsh adventurers can participate together. Let's use this to duel, how about it?"

"What is it?" Merlin frowned and took it over, looking at the commission parchment, the content was as follows -

Commission Rank: A

Details: Recently, a large number of undead have appeared in Denbighshire and urgently need to be cleared. Adventurers are now being recruited to go and destroy them. There is no limit on the number of participants, and you will receive 1000 gold coins just for participating, with 5000 gold coins for those who perform exceptionally.

Requirements: Adventurers below the Gold rank must form teams.

Bounty: 1000~5000 gold coins.

Commissioned by: The Denbighshire Garrison Regiment.

After reading it, Merlin felt the conditions were quite loose; he could just go there and mix around to get money, truly generous.

"How about it, Merlin? Let's compete using this commission! Let's see who is the one who performs excellently!" Arnold sheathed his sword, speaking seriously, "I will use my strength to prove who is the man worthy of Alice-senpai!"

"Lucia, what are they talking about?" Alice hadn't heard clearly.

"That one, it's a Denbighshire commission, it just started recruiting recently." Lucia took out a parchment with the same commission from below and handed it to Alice for her to look at herself.

Alice looked at it and said in surprise, "A large number of undead? What's going on? It's still a commission from the garrison regiment.

"I'm not clear on the specific situation, but I heard that several tomb raiders discovered an underground palace, and after sneaking in, they triggered something, and then undead creatures started appearing from that underground palace to attack the surrounding villages. It seems the situation is quite critical, and the garrison regiment doesn't have enough manpower." Lucia simply explained.

".Ma... Alice seemed to have a bit of interest in this steady job, and dark creatures were still quite easy for her to deal with, as long as she didn't run into a demon of pervert-level like Merlin, after all her pendant sword "Light Ode" has a restraining effect on dark creatures.

"Alice... Arnold walked over, not knowing where he got a rose, and bit it between his teeth.

"Stay away from me, retardism is contagious." Alice didn't give him a good look, finding Arnold this dog-skin plaster annoying.

"I'm sorry, I disturbed you, but I have serious business." Arnold started acting neurotic; although he looked like a shoujo manga male lead, his EQ was truly that of a hot-blooded retard.

"Get to the point or get lost." Alice's eyes were full of hostility.

"Cough, Alice-senpai, I am here with sincerity to invite you to join my team and go to Denbighshire for work." Arnold bowed slightly; no wonder he was a noble son, he had learned etiquette very well.

"Why should I form a team with you? You're a Black Iron rank, and your strength is so bad. I don't want to team up with someone who drags me down." Alice said without the slightest politeness.

"I knew Alice-senpai would say that. To be honest, I spent a huge sum of money to hire a Saint-tier powerhouse for this commission. If Alice-senpai wants to become an outstanding member of the destruction team and get the full 5000 gold coin bounty, it will be a breeze. If Alice-senpai is willing to join, I will feel incomparable honor."

Arnold said with confidence; since he wanted to compete with Merlin, of course he wouldn't rashly challenge him, and he had long ago found a powerful helper.

After all, Arnold had no substantial advantages, the only one being that he was rich.

"Saint-tier powerhouse? Who is it?" Alice was a bit stunned.

"It's Lord Claude, the strong person who just joined the union yesterday. He seems to have an interest in the undead of Denbighshire as well, so I used heavy gold to bribe him into teaming up with me. How about it? Does Alice-senpai have some interest...?" Arnold rubbed his hands.

"Claude?

Alice recalled that black-armored warrior carrying a heavy sword, and how he had had a bit of friction with Merlin.

However, this commission was actually okay, and it seemed there was no danger.

And with a Saint-tier powerhouse assisting, the destruction would definitely be quite easy.

Alice felt this deal wasn't a loss! It was a sure win, seemingly as long as she went there and did the bare minimum.

"I guess so, let's form a team together then.

"Alice-senpai, that is a wise choice." Arnold was overjoyed and turned to say, "Lucia, help stamp it.

Lucia rolled her eyes and stamped the team commission for Arnold, Claude, and Alice, which took effect immediately.

Merlin was also interested in this commission; as his first commission, it would be good to test the waters, so he took the commission to find Alice to form a team, after all she was the only acquaintance he had.

"Alice, let's form a team together?

"G、U、N!"

Alice revealed a disgusted expression and turned to walk out.

Although Merlin was also a powerful teammate, letting Alice form a team with the Demon Lord, her body and mind were both resistant to it.

"Tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue and frowned, thinking this dead washboard, with not much chest, had quite a temper.

"Merlin, the duel between men has already begun. I will use facts to prove that with money, one can really do whatever they want~" Arnold revealed a cool expression and left as well.

"Mr. Merlin, you have to work hard too. Although Arnold is a high-class rich handsome guy, you can't give up on your dreams either. Go home and train Alice with your big banana; I think she will fall in love with you wholeheartedly." Lucia urged from the side, her face red like a big apple, obviously very excited.

Hey? Is this 110?

There's a nympho here!

Please take her away, okay?

Merlin's brows were locked tight, his mood complicated. How many times did he have to explain before others understood that he had nothing to do with Alice?

"Miss Lucia, I want to take this commission too."

"Then... you are a Black Iron rank, so you need to form a team, right? At least two people." Lucia explained awkwardly.

"Can't I do it myself?" Merlin said seriously.

"I'm sorry, Mr. Merlin, the rules are the rules." Lucia revealed an awkward yet polite smile.

Merlin scratched his head, looked back at the adventurers in the guild, and shouted a sentence -

"Come on, come on!

"We're short one person for the Denbighshire undead commission."

"Anyone who can shout 666 is welcome! Come on, ten salted fish at a time!"

(Four●Mouth)?

title: Chapter 20 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 20 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 3 · Chapter 20

After Merlin finished speaking, the group of chatting adventurers below fell dead silent, with not a single person responding. Their eyes were as if they were looking at a clown.

Then, not long after, bursts of snickering erupted from below.

"A Black Iron wants to take an A-rank quest too?"

"Yeah, A-rank is dangerous even for Silver adventurers, let alone a Black Iron. He's probably just going to get himself killed."

"Does this newcomer think the garrison's money is that easy to earn? Denby County is just short on manpower. Black Iron adventurers are either there to pad the numbers or to serve as food for the undead."

"It's his attitude that's terrible. A salted fish who only knows how to shout '666'? How laughable. Isn't he the salted fish himself?"

"This new Black Iron seems to have no idea how deep the waters of the adventurer world really run. What attitude is that? So arrogant..."

The adventurers below were buzzing with discussion, almost all of it filled with disdain and mockery.

Many looked down on Black Iron adventurers. They were too low-level, their abilities unremarkable, and Merlin's innate arrogance made people extremely uncomfortable.

Although Merlin had passed the president's evaluation, many of his colleagues believed he only knew a few tricks of a amateur fighter, far from being fit for grand stages.

Merlin merely smiled at the reactions below without saying a word. Why would he bother jumping down to argue with a bunch of frogs croaking at the bottom of a well?

"Then... Mr. Merlin, if no one is willing to team up with you..."

"There is. How could there not be? Just wait."

Before Lucy could finish her sentence, Merlin cut her off, then went over and dragged over Hobbs, who was snoring loudly at the wine table.

Hobbs had drunk too much and was somewhat incoherent, rolling his eyes, sporting a red wine-soaked nose, and reeking of alcohol. Lucy wrinkled her nose and kept fanning it.

"He'll do." Merlin said confidently.

"Bro... add... glug glug..." Hobbs babbled incoherently.

"Then..." Lucy's smile turned awkward. She said with difficulty, "Mr. Hobbs seems to be in no clear state of mind. I need him to agree in person."

"Uh... this is... simple..." Merlin shook the drunk Hobbs. "Hobbs, do you want to go to Denby County with me to visit the brothels?"

"Go, go, must go, we're going to... bomb Denby County! Hehehe..." Hobbs perked up immediately, nodding repeatedly with an extremely lewd grin. Clearly in a drunken state, he had been tricked by Merlin.

"Miss Lucy, he agreed." Merlin smiled.

"This is..." Lucy's smile was very forced. She thought to herself, what kind of pair are these two? The moment prostitution was mentioned, they happily teamed up. This combination clearly doesn't meet the regulations, right? Besides, two Black Irons — what could they possibly accomplish!?

"Lucy..." Old Taylor, who had been standing behind the whole time, finally spoke.

"Grandpa?" Lucy turned around in surprise.

"Let them go." Old Taylor nodded in approval. He had personally experienced Merlin's strength. This quest wouldn't be stressful for him; if anything, it was like using a ox-cleaving knife to kill a chicken.

"Thanks, president~" Merlin grinned.

"... Lucy hesitated, furrowed her pretty brows, and firmly stamped —

Merlin [Hobbs]

A garbage team composed of two Black Irons.

And at this moment, they were also setting off toward Denby County in Wales!

Outside.

Arnold, as a wealthy young master, had his own luxurious carriage.

The ornate gold-plated decorations, the prancing steeds, and the coachman dressed in a tailcoat all screamed one message to anyone who saw it:

"I'm rich, come scam me anytime!"

Alice looked at Arnold's carriage and felt a pang of sour envy in her heart. Her little donkey cart, compared to such a luxurious ride, was simply too shabby. It's so nice to be rich, boohoo...

The coachman got down to help Alice open the carriage door, striking a polite gesture. His attitude was respectful — clearly a professional.

"Miss Alice, please board the carriage." Arnold fully displayed the gentlemanly spirit of ladies first.

Alice hesitated for a moment, then got into the carriage. Arnold followed her in.

Once inside, Alice found the space quite large, and someone was already seated up ahead.

A heavy black sword rested beside his leg, he wore pitch-black armor free of any impurities, and his face was hidden beneath a heavy helmet. The calm and majestic aura radiating from him could only belong to a Saint-tier warrior — could it be anyone other than Claude?

The ring-shaped interior space had Alice and Claude seated on opposite sides, while Arnold sat in the middle.

The carriage set off with a gentle rocking, the road not too bumpy.

From the very beginning, Alice had felt a trace of pressure, because across from her sat a Saint-tier powerhouse who kept staring out the window in silence, appearing extremely aloof.

Most Saint-tier experts had this kind of personality, making it hard for others to approach them. There was an invisible class gap between them.

Although Merlin was also very powerful, he lacked that untouchable aura. He was truly a freak.

Even though Alice disliked Merlin, she had to admit that Merlin was quite approachable.

"Mr. Claude... hi..."

After a long silence, Alice broke it with a greeting first. After all, they were teammates in the same party. A little communication wouldn't hurt.

"Hmm." Claude nodded, appearing very cold.

What kind of attitude is that?

Is he looking down on me because I'm Saint-tier?

That weirdo Merlin should be stronger than this guy, right?

Although Merlin is a jerk, his attitude toward others is quite likable. He's better than this guy in front of me, hmph~!

Alice felt a bit unhappy and started muttering to herself, thinking the other party was being arrogant due to his talent. She thought the jerk (husband) was still better.

Thinking of Merlin now, Alice felt a bit worried. Without her around, would he cause trouble everywhere?

By the time she returned, the whole of Rexham might already be torn apart by Merlin.

Alice's pretty brows knitted tightly, becoming very anxious. She somewhat regretted teaming up with Arnold. If she were there watching over Merlin, this time bomb, she would feel much more at ease.

Although what Merlin did had nothing to do with Alice, she had too strong a sense of responsibility. Bringing that jerk to Rexham, if something went wrong, she felt it would somehow become her fault to bear.

Arnold sensed the strange atmosphere and decided to ease it. "Mr. Arnold, this is Miss Alice. As a Gold-ranked adventurer, she'll be our teammate from now on. Let's cooperate and work together to become the most outstanding team in this crusade!"

"Forget about cooperation. Leave the strong enemies to me. You just need to chop down the small fries and tag along on the sidelines." Claude said gruffly. "If possible, I'll go to the deepest level of the dungeon. You two shouldn't continue going deeper."

Haha, Mr. Claude is worried about our safety, right? We'll be very careful and can still provide you with some assistance." Arnold scratched his head and smiled, thinking that with a Saint-tier expert backing them, there wouldn't be any danger.

"I think you may have misunderstood what I meant?" Claude turned his head to look at Arnold, his deep eyes hidden beneath the helmet.

"I said you two are both trash."

"Don't cause me trouble. Don't hold me back in the rear."

"Who gave you the illusion that you could be of any help to me?"

title: Chapter 21 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 21 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 3 · Chapter 21

"Let me be clear upfront — if you slow me down, I'll leave you behind without a second thought."

Claude's tone was resolute, brooking no question, and his attitude was so harsh it made one's skin crawl.

What an arrogant person.

Even though we're teammates, why the attitude like that?

Saint-tier is so great? Pfft, whatever...

Alice frowned, her mood instantly souring.

In the past, Alice had thought Saint-tier was incredibly powerful, but after watching Merlin slice through enemies one after another, she'd gradually grown accustomed to it and her standards had risen.

Although Merlin was also arrogant, he wasn't to the point of being repulsive. But this Claude in front of her was nothing but outright contempt for others.

Alice glared at Claude in silence, a hint of anger in her eyes. Her face, hidden beneath the helmet, seemed to carry an added air of mystery.

Arnold broke into a cold sweat, feeling the atmosphere grow tense, so he stepped in with a smile to smooth things over.

"Mr. Claude, please... don't say such ruthless things. We're only trying to help out."

"No need. I'm a Saint-tier powerhouse — why would I ever need help?" Claude paused, then continued, "Besides, this commission clearly only requires one person. Why did someone suddenly get added? Shouldn't you have consulted my opinion first?"

"This... Miss Alice is my fri... I hope you can make an exception, Mr. Claude. If possible, I can add tens of thousands of gold coins." Arnold tried to win Claude over with money.

Claude remained silent for a moment, then shifted his gaze back to the window. "This time, forget it. I don't need money. I'm only interested in the undead of Denby County. Teamming up with you was just along the way."

"I see..." Arnold took out a handkerchief and wiped the cold sweat from his brow, feeling a wave of relief in his chest.

Claude continued staring out the window without looking away, his eyes hidden beneath the helmet appearing unusually mysterious.

The atmosphere returned to calm, broken only by the creaking of the ornate carriage swaying along.

Alice frowned deeply, her mood thoroughly ruined.

If I'd known it would be like this, I'd have just gone alone.

That guy Merlin has found teammates now...

At the guild entrance.

Merlin supported the drunken Hobbs and looked around.

The carriage Alice had ridden in had long since disappeared into the distance of Rexham.

"Tch, what a hassle. Where am I supposed to get a carriage?"

Merlin muttered to himself, feeling a bit embarrassed. His pockets were rather bare, and he apparently couldn't afford a carriage to Denby County either.

Merlin glanced over at Hobbs beside him and figured this guy might actually have money — he drank vodka nonstop all day.

Merlin patted down Hobbs's chest and pulled out three horse racing tickets. Nothing else.

...

Merlin couldn't help but feel that he and Hobbs were truly brothers in misfortune — two guys of the same caliber ended up together.

This was a bit of a headache. Walking to Denby County on foot would take at least five days, while a carriage could make it in about two.

Merlin lifted his eyelids and looked at the sunset-red sky, thinking, whatever. I'll just go "borrow" Alice's stuff.

A while later —

Merlin tossed the drunken Hobbs into the back and sat in the front, driving Alice's little donkey cart.

"Menmen, let's go~!"

It seemed the two-trash Black Iron team had also set out...

The second day of departure, early morning.

A fine drizzle fell from the sky, and distant mountains seemed shrouded in thick fog.

The road to Denby County was already difficult to traverse, and now it had become even more muddy and slippery.

In Wales of Great Britain, autumn often brought constant rain, the dampness making one uncomfortable.

Merlin wrapped himself in a cowhide blanket to avoid getting wet and to keep warm, holding the reins as he trotted along at a leisurely pace.

The sight of him looked like he might pull out explosives from his coat at any moment and shout "Allahu Akbar!"

As for Hobbs beside him, he was also wrapped in a blanket, but his expression was utterly blank, as if he were confused about his own actions from the night before after getting drunk.

"Mr. Merlin... did you really agree to go to Denby County?"

"Yeah, didn't you read the commission document? It even has Miss Lucia's seal on it." Merlin answered with mild interest.

Ever since Hobbs woke up and was roused by the rain, he'd been completely bewildered by the situation. Normally when he got drunk, someone would always take him home, but today he woke up directly on the road to Denby County.

"Seriously? I remember I was drunk, right? How did I agree to this commission while not in my right mind?"

"No problem at all." Merlin said boastfully.

"Oh my god!" Hobbs covered his face, unable to believe it. "Mr. Merlin, let's... let's just turn around and go back, shall we?"

"Huh?!" Merlin's eyes widened in surprise. "We've been traveling all night. Why go back?"

"Mr. Merlin, you might not know this yet." Hobbs's face darkened, and he lowered his voice. "We can't help with the Denby County crisis. For Black Iron-rank adventurers like us, going there is just signing our own death warrants. At most, we'd be useful as bait to draw the undead's attention."

"Is it really that bad?" Merlin raised his eyebrows.

"Brother, you've only been an adventurer for one day. There's a lot you don't understand. The commissions officially posted may offer generous rewards, but that money isn't easy to earn. The undead outbreak has even left the garrison troops at a loss, which shows just how many there are. It's better for us to stay away. Before long, the London royal palace will send strong warriors to handle it. Let's not go throw our lives away."

Hobbs wore a deeply worried expression, his small eyes darting around like a thief's, clearly somewhat afraid.

"What's there to be afraid of? As long as I'm here, don't worry. Just hide behind me." Merlin patted his chest, showing absolutely no fear.

As for those mere undead, Merlin didn't give them a second thought. These creatures summoned from hell were nothing more than coming back to life once.

To Merlin, hell was the grave of the defeated. Even if they returned, they were still trash.

Moreover, undead were lifeless beings. No matter how powerful, they could not extend Merlin's life or ease the curse on his heart.

Merlin had already verified this.

Many years ago, when Merlin was the Demon Lord, a hellish undead envoy had visited, demanding Merlin submit to Satan, the ruler of hell, and become hell's representative on land.

The arrogant Merlin had naturally chosen to ignore him, and casually beheaded the undead envoy — yet his heart curse had not eased in the slightest.

At that moment, Merlin had understood: the demon sword Banri Garan, this kingly artifact, could only draw life force from the living. It had no effect whatsoever on the dead.

Hobbs furrowed his brows deeply, looking at the confident Merlin with astonishment, thinking strangely in his heart —

This kid...

Isn't he just an idiot?

((异V号1I)

title: Chapter 22 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 22 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets

Volume 3 · Chapter 22

Hobbs felt extremely conflicted at this moment, feeling as though Merlin was dragging him to his death. Why were the two of them, trash Black Iron-rank adventurers, heading straight into the center of chaos?

"Wait, Merlin, calm down a bit. Do you even understand undead?"

"Hmm? Of course I understand them. They're just creatures without intelligence, with extremely high physical resistance. As long as you crush their skulls and extinguish the fire of their souls, they can basically keep fighting." Merlin gave a crooked grin.

".-. You know that and still want to go in?" Hobbs found it hard to comprehend. He continued explaining, "Even though ordinary undead are low-tier monsters, their combat ability exceeds mid-tier, and there are so many of them. We're going to throw our lives away...."

"Hobbs, don't be afraid. I told you, with me here, what's there to panic about?" Merlin sounded a bit impatient.

"Should I not be panicked? The two of us are trash Black Iron rank, and we're charging headfirst at the undead without a priest in the party. Isn't that just stupid?" Hobbs' expression was deeply grim.

"What's a priest for?" Merlin asked, puzzled.

"A priest can disperse the souls of the dead. Otherwise, once we kill an undead, it'll come back to life sooner or later." Hobbs felt that a team with a priest was far more reliable, especially when fighting undead.

"You don't need to go through all that trouble. Just crack open an undead's skull and stomp out the soul fire. Do you really need a priest?" Merlin gave a crooked grin, thinking Hobbs was making a mountain out of a molehill.

Hobbs' expression grew increasingly panicked. He thought Merlin was an utterly stubborn fool. The skull was the strongest part of an undead's body — how easily could it be cracked open?

"I think I'll just go back on my own."

"Hobbs, why don't you believe me?" Merlin sighed, thinking that being completely without magical power or battle aura was quite troublesome.

"How can I believe you, Merlin? I'm trash fire-element magic user. You're someone with no magical power or battle aura, who only knows a bit of amateur skills. What amazing alchemical reaction can the two of us produce together?" Hobbs was deeply concerned about their partnership prospects. In truth, he wanted to attach himself to someone powerful, completely unaware that such a person was right beside him.

"Hobbs, can't you see that I'm powerful?" Merlin said seriously.

Hobbs looked at Merlin's haggard complexion, his frayed floor mat (cloak), his messy blonde hair, and his seemingly scrapped-together broken longsword, all radiating an aura of complete inadequacy, and he couldn't help but burst out laughing.

"Come on, bro. I like bragging too, but us Black Iron adventurers are just like that. Daydreams are fine, but don't take it too seriously."

Merlin pursed his lips, knowing no matter what he said, Hobbs would never believe he was powerful. But to keep the drunkard from returning to Leixem, he said, "Alice and Arnold are ahead. Their team has that newly arrived Saint-tier man, Claude. If you're scared, you can tag along with them for some experience and a 1,000 gold piece subsistence bonus. Wouldn't that be great?"

"Emm....." Hobbs blinked his eyes, then struck his palm with his fist. "Right! There's that option too. Once we get there, we can team up to chop up some little monsters, grind some experience. With that new Saint-tier guy nearby, there won't be any danger either. Who turns down free money?~"

Merlin pursed his lips, thinking that he certainly wasn't someone content to scrape by on a subsistence stipend. Get 5,000 gold pieces, spend 4,999 on horse racing tickets, and if it pays out 20 times, he'd be turned over completely.

The damn Merlin seemed to have forgotten that he owed Alice rent, or perhaps he simply had no intention of paying, wanting to mooch off her entirely.

"That Arnold fellow is, as expected, a count's son. Truly loaded — he can even hire a Saint-tier powerhouse. I really must take advantage of this. Sigh, having money is so great...." Hobbs suddenly remembered that Alice and Merlin had something going on, but now she was teaming up with Arnold. He comforted Merlin instead, "Bro, cheer up. Women are all fickle. Arnold comes with a natural intelligence-lowering aura, so he's basically no threat. If all else fails, don't you still have a big banana?"

"I don't have anything going on with Alice..." Merlin rolled his eyes, completely exasperated at being misunderstood.

"Bro, don't say that....." Hobbs patted Merlin on the shoulder, then took out two bottles of alcohol from the back of the cart, popping the corks directly. "Here, bro, vodka."

Merlin took a bottle, and the two began to chug straight from the bottles.

"Gulp gulp gulp gulp gulp gulp... *burp*~"

Merlin squinted his eyes into slits. In the chilly, drizzly weather, drinking felt wonderfully warming and incredibly comfortable.

The dense sound of horse hooves approached from behind. A group riding sturdy steeds, clad in armor emblazoned with rose-pattern crests, surged toward them, pulling an extraordinarily ornate carriage that looked far from cheap.

The lead knight on the white horse had sharp, piercing eyes — clearly the strongest in the group. His red cape billowed like a banner. How could anyone not find that handsome?

Hobbs, well-traveled and experienced, recognized the small rose crest at a glance. "What the hell, people from the Duke of Wales's retinue!?"

"Who!?" Merlin was completely baffled. Forgive him — the only Elizabeth he knew was Queen Elizabeth, ruler of all of Great Britain.

"The Grand Duke of Roses, the lord of Wales. His status is higher than Arnold's father Austin's." Hobbs explained briefly, then added, "But this entourage isn't large enough. The Grand Duke himself certainly didn't come in person. It must be a family member."

Merlin wasn't particularly interested; it didn't concern him much.

The knight on the white horse rode a few steps faster to catch up with them. His expression had been perfectly normal at first, but upon seeing the Black Iron adventurer credentials hanging around their necks, it immediately turned contemptuous.

"Tell me, do you two know which route is faster to reach Derbyshire?"

"My lord knight, it's quicker to cross the Marosa Mountains directly ahead. There's a narrow path, and your large carriage in the back might not fit through, but on foot it should be fine." Hobbs had considerable adventuring experience and knew plenty of shortcut routes. As expected of a man in his thirties.

"Heh, are you joking?" The white-armored knight sneered.

"Then... if you prefer, you can take the main road. But autumn is exactly when the Burning Rhinos migrate southward. Encountering them would be somewhat troublesome. If you want to save time, crossing the Marosa Mountains on foot is fastest." Hobbs felt the other party's temperament was quite foul, and his tone grew slightly timorous.

"Do you know who's in that carriage behind us?" the white-armored knight asked.

"A family member of the Rose Grand Duke?" Hobbs answered tentatively.

"The daughter of the Rose Grand Duke, Miss Cecilia!" the knight emphasized. He continued, "Do you think the daughter of the Rose Grand Duke would stoop to walking on muddy roads!?"

"Then... walking a bit won't kill her. Is the Rose Grand Duke's daughter some kind of disabled person?" Hobbs spoke a blunt truth.

"What did you just say?! You dare insult Miss Cecilia as a disabled person — you're asking for a beating!"

The white-armored knight drew his horsewhip and struck down. The sound of the whip cutting through the air came with sharp *whoosh* hisses. Its dark shadow sliced through the damp air.

Hobbs panicked and squeezed his eyes shut, covering his face in case he was disfigured.

Before the eye could blink, before the strike could land.

Merlin seized the vicious whip in one hand. No matter how hard the knight pulled, he couldn't wrench it back.

Mounted high atop his steed, the noble white-armored knight looked down at Merlin with contempt and sneered, "Commoner. Release my whip. Do you wish to be punished alongside him?"

"Your attitude has been inexplicably offensive from the start. You're merely a dog at a nobleman's door — what right do you have to flex your authority here? Sorry, no matter how much face your master has, it won't work with me."

Merlin yanked the whip sharply. The noble white-armored knight was instantly unseated —

He tumbled down clumsily, face-first into a big pile of mud.......

title: Chapter 23 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 23 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 3 · Chapter 23

What if the other side is some noble?

Merlin didn't even give the opponent the face of a reply—he simply hauled the white knight right off his horse.

The white knight crashed to the ground like a dog, his face buried deep in the muddy earth.

The other knights behind him stirred in agitation, some even drawing their swords. Clearly, this white knight was their leader.

Hobbs stared with wide eyes, a little stunned. He hadn't expected Merlin to be so decisive, directly humiliating the knight without a single unnecessary word.

"Heh, are you calm now? You came asking us for directions, and we kindly told you which road is shorter. You didn't thank us, that's fine—but you actually put on a noble's stinky airs? How laughable..." Merlin looked down at the white knight, his lips curling with unrestrained contempt, further stabbing at the other's dignity.

"Merlin, this isn't good, right? That guy is the Rose Duke's...?" Hobbs's face turned a bit pale. Even when beating a dog, you still have to consider the master. Causing trouble like this, saying the wrong thing could easily offend someone.

Who was the Rose Duke? The most influential lord of all Wales. Though under the jurisdiction of the London royal family, every territorial magnate was a petty emperor in their own domain.

Now these two lowly Black Iron adventurers had beaten the Rose Duke's daughter's guard. It could spiral into a whole series of troubles.

"What Rose Duke, Cabbage Duke—who cares? Don't panic. When someone hits you, why don't you fight back? An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Understand?" Merlin said seriously to Hobbs.

"..." Hobbs furrowed his brow, as if he'd heard that phrase before. "Isn't that the demon race's creed? If you say that in front of clergy, you'll be burned at the stake."

Merlin was about to crack a joke when the white knight on the ground suddenly stood up. His ornate armor was now filthy, his face smeared with mud like a clay mask.

"You two Black Iron adventurers... what nerve you have!"

"I, Kael, have never suffered such humiliation since becoming a Rose Knight!"

Knight Kael roared at Merlin and Hobbs. He tossed his helmet to the ground, revealing his messy brown hair, then casually wiped the mud off his face with his rain-soaked hand.

Then Kael drew the black long spear from his back, assumed a fighting stance, and shook his wrist. The sharp spear tip gleamed coldly, and high-tier battle aura radiated from his body, dispersing the damp air around them.

"This isn't just about insulting me—it's an insult to the Rose Duke! To protect the honor of the Rose Knights, I challenge you both to a duel!"

"Come!"

Though Kael looked incredibly hot-blooded—practically begging for someone to carve "I am a loyal dog" on his forehead—Merlin and Hobbs remained completely calm, their faces blank.

Merlin had also seen his share of noble lapdogs. A small portion of them preached loyalty and righteousness, guarding some inexplicable glory, acting like they'd been brainwashed by a cult.

"Feels like an idiot."

"Yeah, eating a mouthful of mud and acting like it's the end of the world—if he ate shit, would he kill the whole family?" Merlin muttered along.

"What are you two muttering about?!" Kael swung his long spear, high-tier battle aura surging, making the weapon extremely agile as he launched a high-tier martial technique directly at Merlin and Hobbs, aiming to turn them into a pincushion.

The fierce spear shadow shifted unpredictably, ultimately converging at a single point, bursting forth with tremendous force!

Merlin had just placed his hand on the hilt of his tachi, planning to eliminate this clueless guy, when suddenly a melodious feminine voice rang out—

"Stop it, Kael!"

Kael's whole body shuddered, quickly retracting his attack, looking behind him blankly. "Lady Cecilia..."

Slowly stepping down from the luxurious carriage surrounded and protected by the knights was a girl.

Classic golden wavy hair, ruby earrings swaying by her ears, wearing a pure white priestess-style long dress with gold thread embroidery that instantly elevated her presence, and in her hand a pure white staff radiating Saint-tier aura.

Cecilia was helped down from the carriage by her maid, her posture elegant, a flash of nobility and rebellious pride flickering in her eyes.

Hobbs looked at Cecilia and immediately wore a slightly perverted old man expression. "Hey hey, Merlin, this girl is really something, and she's the duke's daughter—total rich beauty. I think—"

"Please act normal." Merlin responded helplessly, thinking—normal? I don't feel it, she's so-so at best.

Cecilia walked up to Kael, her maid holding an umbrella closely behind.

"Kael, is the honor of the Rose Knights really that cheap? You actually want to duel with the weak? You can really say that out loud?"

Merlin raised his eyebrows, thinking—weak? Is she talking about me? No no, probably about Hobbs.

Kael lowered his spear, knelt on one knee, hand pressed to his chest, head bowed in apology. "I'm sorry, Lady Cecilia. It's just that these two commoners insulted you as a disabled person,..."

"So what? These two commoners had never seen me before, why blame them? If two ants block the path forward, should we stop walking?" Cecilia's words were laced with thorns, clearly looking down on Merlin and Hobbs.

"Lady Cecilia speaks correctly, this servant was reckless." Kael said very humbly.

Merlin felt slightly annoyed—mere seven human noble kids, yet they all spoke with such superiority. When he was the Demon Lord, he'd been far more approachable.

Cecilia was very satisfied with Kael's reaction, maintaining her noble posture as she turned to Merlin and Hobbs, feigning magnanimity. "It was my servant who disturbed the two of you. On his behalf, I offer you my apology."

"Cecilia..." Kael's eyes welled up with tears, touched beyond words.

Merlin felt that Cecilia's apology lacked sincerity entirely—she didn't even bend her waist, and the contempt in her eyes hadn't faded one bit.

"Then... isn't an apology supposed to show some chest?"

Hobbs flashed his hand over Merlin's mouth, whispering urgently, "Merlin, what are you doing? Don't say nonsense."

"..." Cecilia paused, thinking she must have misheard. Showing some chest in an apology—what did that mean? Was this blatant sexual harassment?

"You filthy bastard, what are you saying to Lady Cecilia?!" Kael grabbed his long spear and stood up, ready to fight to the death.

"Wait." Cecilia stopped the impulsive Kael.

"Lady Cecilia, I..." Kael found it hard to accept.

"Forget it, no need to get angry over foolish people. Time is tight, let's go." Cecilia held her staff, turned, and walked away. The maid quickly followed behind holding the umbrella.

"Hmph!" Kael knew what was important, so he could only snort coldly and remount his horse.

Hobbs, seeing the other side wasn't going to press the matter, relaxed and said faintly, "I'd advise you not to take the northern main road to Derby County..."

Cecilia stopped, curiously turning her head to ask, "Why?"

"Because you're likely to run into migrating herds of Fire Rhinos. We already told you that once." Merlin answered for Hobbs, then continued drinking his vodka.

"..." Cecilia smiled contemptuously, glancing at the adventurer badges around their necks, and said dismissively, "Two lowly Black Irons? What value is there in trusting words from trash mouths?"

Merlin's brows furrowed, silently capping his vodka bottle, thinking—

This noble little brat.

Her temper was even more annoying than Alice's.

title: Chapter 24 — Bonus Update for Tips
content:
Chapter 24 — Bonus Update for Tips

Volume 3 · Chapter 24

"My house is huge, and I used to get lost every single day when I was little.

"And there were so many maids that I never had to dress myself. Every few hours, I'd change into a custom-made dress made of mysterious Eastern silk. I heard just one piece of fabric cost a fortune.

"But what is money? I've never even touched it.

"To me, money is just a number with no other meaning. I think having wealth actually makes you less happy.

"I'm sick of this life where I never have to lift a finger. So, Miss Alice, do you understand what I'm saying?"

Arnold's mouth had been going non-stop the entire way, essentially flexing his wealth the whole time. He talked about all sorts of things Alice had never even heard of, like he'd die if he didn't show off.

This sort of subtle, unintentional bragging really grates on ordinary folks.

.....Alice gave a strained laugh, already immune to Arnold's posturing. *I don't understand a single thing. For heaven's sake, shut your trap and stay quiet for once!*

Even though Alice's response was consistently cold, Arnold was relentless, hoping his superior lifestyle would win her over and spark her interest.

Little did he know, the more Arnold flexed his wealth, the more repulsed Alice became. They came from completely different worlds—how were they supposed to communicate?

Seeing Alice's lack of reaction, Arnold continued on his own, "What I mean is, Miss Alice, you rekindled my will to live. I remember half a year ago, when I visited my uncle in Elgin City in my father's stead, I saw your heroic self on the road, and my heart literally stopped. If the love goddess Aphrodite truly exists, I imagine she looks exactly like you. So I made up my mind to dedicate my entire life's love to you, Miss Alice."

"....." Alice remained cold, but suddenly felt something was off. "W-we met half a year ago? I have absolutely no memory of it."

Half a year ago, Alice had indeed been to Elgin City to help deal with a giant boar infestation on the farmlands, and she had also witnessed the birth of a legend, falling for the legendary Elgin Great Swordsman at first sight.

But Arnold meant nothing to her. She had absolutely no recollection of ever meeting him, only knowing that this rich second-generation kid came to the guild to kill time.

"You're so heartless, Miss Alice. We really did meet half a year ago...." Arnold said helplessly. Seeing the confusion on Alice's face, he continued explaining, "I even proposed to you back then. Don't you really remember?"

"Huh!?" Alice's eyes widened as she let out a startled cry. "....A proposal?! I have no idea what you're talking about!"

"Maybe it happened so suddenly that you forgot, Miss Alice. That's only natural. But I still remember the scene vividly...." A look of yearning crossed Arnold's face as he slowly spoke, "I knelt on one knee, held out my hand, with a serious expression. 'Beautiful lady, I am willing to treasure you as my one true love for life. Will you marry me?'"

"Uh!" Alice got goosebumps all over and asked nervously, "H-how did I respond?"

"You told me 'G, U, N!' and then quickly vanished." Arnold said awkwardly. His first-ever proposal had ended in failure.

"Hah...." Alice wiped away a cold sweat. *Yeah, that sounds exactly like something I'd say. There's no way I would've agreed to a creep like Arnold...* But she really couldn't remember the proposal at all.

"Even though you rejected me, Miss Alice, I won't be discouraged. I'll let you see my shining side." Arnold said confidently.

"You're so annoying...." Alice said wearily.

"Relax, I'll definitely prove that I'm far superior to Merlin that backwater bumpkin. I'll make you change your mind and win back your breeding rights. I'm willing to accept this challenge...." Arnold said with utter seriousness, completely ignoring Alice's increasingly freezing expression.

"Could you please go die somewhere?" Alice gave a smile that didn't reach her eyes, her grip on her rapier trembling with suppressed rage. "I have absolutely nothing to do with Merlin that jerk...."
