"No need to explain, Miss Alice, I understand everything." Arnold assumed Alice was just trying to comfort him. "This trial in Derbyshire is my chance. I'm going to defeat my rival in an honorable duel and prove that I'm the better man."

"You're not necessarily better than Merlin. You're nobody yourself, yet you keep dragging others into this." Alice muttered under her breath, stealing a glance at the silent Claude beside her.

"Miss Alice, don't worry about the details. Wealth is also a form of strength." Arnold shamelessly shifted the subject. "Don't you think we have great fate connecting us?"

"Oh, not at all." Alice said with a blank expression.

"We met in Elgin. When I saw your adventurer registration said Rexem, I was happy, but also disappointed. Why did I live in Rexem for nearly twenty years and never notice you? You've made me waste so much of my youth. My heart hurts...."

Arnold feigned sorrow, but it lasted only a brief moment.

"But then heaven gave me a chance to make amends. After returning to Rexem, I applied to become an adventurer, and I got to see you again. I remember that day Lucia asked me if I'd been kicked in the head by a donkey to become an adventurer, and I replied: For Miss Alice, I would willingly offer my heart!"

"Get lost. Stay away from me. You're like a stalker. Disgusting!" Alice felt her scalp tingle with disgust, as if a cockroach had been eyeing her.

"Don't be so cold, Miss Alice. We're destined to be together. We both witnessed the birth of the Elgin swordsman legend. We live in the same city, and we're even working together." Arnold tried to close the distance between them.

Alice's brows furrowed, desperate to kick Arnold out of the carriage. *Destined? The only person I like is the Elgin legendary Great Swordsman.* She had only caught a vague glimpse of his silhouette, but his face in person must be handsome.

However, Alice had never told anyone about her secret crush. She kept it locked in her heart.

It would be embarrassing if anyone found out. Having a crush on a legendary hero was the sort of shallow teenage fantasy that looked delusional no matter how you spun it.

Not to mention, the Elgin Great Swordsman's identity, status, and appearance were all unknown. Liking someone so intangible would make you look like a lunatic.

"Can I ask a question?"

Claude suddenly interjected, his gaze slowly shifting from the window to Arnold.

This dark armoured greatsword wielder had been silent from the beginning, his presence so thin it was as though he had no interest in anything.

The sudden question caught everyone off guard.

"...Please go ahead, Claude..." Arnold said uneasily, sensing Claude's odd temperament and adopting an overly respectful tone.

"I often hear people gossiping about the legendary swordsman of Elgin. It seems like everyone loves talking about it. You two were discussing it just now...." Claude paused, his face emerging from beneath the heavy helmet.

"So I wanted to ask..."

"What exactly is the legendary swordsman of Elgin?"

title: Chapter 25 — Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 25 — Bonus Chapter

Volume 3 · Chapter 25

“Eh! ?” Arnold suddenly became surprised, asking, “Mr. Claude, you don't know about the Elgin swordsman incident half a year ago?

“Completely unknown...” Claude replied nonchalantly.

Alice was a little surprised, there are still people who don't know about Elgin's great swordsman? After all, countless people on that -- night witnessed the legend of a single strike killing two Saint-tier pirate kings, the whole of Britain was in an uproar, how could anyone still be completely unaware?

“Maybe... Mr. Claude has been training in the deep mountains all along, never coming out?” Arnold speculated.

“Probably.” Claude nodded and continued, “I always hear people talking about this swordsman, many say he is Britain's strongest, which makes me a bit...”

Alice's doubts dissipated, she thought he had been living in seclusion all along? No wonder he's so closed off, I don't even recognize my husband~

It seems Alice's fangirl tendency is not light; she directly fantasized about Elgin's great swordsman as her husband, which is no different from those fangirls chasing after the long-legged oppas of Bangzi country....

“Indeed, Elgin's legendary swordsman is now recognized as the strongest throughout Britain.” Arnold nodded.

“Why is he given the title of strongest?” Claude sounded very doubtful.

“Elgin's great swordsman became famous in one battle; the Red Beard brothers are famed Saint-tier pirate kings, rampaging uncontested in the North Sea. These two figures that even the royal family could do nothing about were actually killed in one strike by Elgin's swordsman!? ” Arnold narrowed his eyes, speaking mysteriously, “Think about it, how strong is this Elgin swordsman? At the very least, his strength can completely crush two pirate kings; in strength, across all of Britain, this is extremely rare.”

Claude fell silent, blandly saying, “Killing two Saint-tier? That's nothing special?”

“Eh!?”

Alice and Arnold were both surprised, still hearing a disdainful tone for the first time.

“Saint-tier is merely the threshold between strong and novice; even among Saint-tier, there are differences in strength, and there are still weaklings.” Claude said flatly, as if killing two Saint-tier wasn't shocking.

Regarding her imagined husband being questioned, Alice surely wasn't pleased, so she retorted, “The Red Beard pirate brothers aren't weaklings; they're quite strong, I've even fought them before.

“Ah! ? Miss Alice fought the Red Beard pirates? Yuan Arnold was very surprised, because challenging above one's level is tantamount to seeking death.

“Of course, but I was quickly defeated.... Alice said embarrassedly.

“Hmph, Miss Alice, being a high-tier, facing a Saint-tier naturally feels the opponent is strong, because it's not an equal match; in our Saint-tier eyes, the pirate king you face isn't anything, this is the gap between tiers.” Claude said with a very contemptuous tone, thinking Alice was exaggerating.

Alice was a bit unhappy, but she patiently said, “So according to Lord Claude's meaning, you're saying the Saint-tier pirate kings that give the royal family a headache are actually weaklings?

“Exactly, killing two weakling Saint-tier, I could also do that; it's not something worth bragging about, yet to be given the title of strongest? Truly laughable.... From beneath Claude's grim helmet came a cold laugh.

Alice felt uncomfortable all over, her dream male god being insulted; as a fangirl she certainly resented it, but freedom of speech, she couldn't blame anything, so she sat there sulking.

“Nowadays this era is no good, messed up by the British royal family into chaos, true strongs are becoming fewer and fewer; back then, an existence like Elgin's swordsman would merely be mediocre.” Claude sighed.

Alice furrowed her brows, thinking what kind of old-man tone is this? It's as if she were living in a bygone era.

Arnold, as a noble scion, thought such reactionary talk wasn't good, so he shifted the topic, “Well... actually what Lord Claude says isn't without reason; Elgin swordsman's legend arose with the times, plus the hype from various newspapers, making him Britain's strongest. As far as I know, the president of the London Adventurers Guild, Ireland's youngest genius mage, members of the royal family's secret Purple Camellia Knight Order, etc., are apparently not weaker than Elgin swordsman, they just haven't shown their strength.”

“Hmph~!” Alice snorted coldly, no longer wanting to deal with Arnold, as he was colluding with Claude, jointly doubting her idol; as a fangirl she couldn't tolerate it.

“Every era needs a hero, to become a pillar supporting human hope, letting the people place their hopes on someone whose identity is unknown—this is the incompetence of the British royal family.” Claude said glumly.

Arnold broke out in a cold sweat on his forehead, thinking Claude was acting like an angry youth, how embarrassing, “Maybe... perhaps that's the case now, many people indeed treat the Elgin legendary swordsman as a guardian deity; even Elgin has a statue being worshipped; I heard recently many people go there to pay respects, already trending toward myth.”

“Ah! ? Really?” Alice felt bewildered, her fine male god is about to be listed among the immortals.

“Indeed, it's the Holy Church spreading it, saying their scriptures long ago prophesied that Elgin swordsman is the chief knight of the Goddess of Light, to save the lower world full of sin.” Arnold himself laughed out loud, thinking the Holy Church's lot of charlatans blowing hot air is really slick.

If Merlin knew about this, I don't know what expression he'd have; perhaps he'd be speechless because I inexplicably defected to the Demon Lord Palace.

“Truly... come....” Alice said gloomily, she doesn't want her male god to become an illusory product.

“If possible, I

title: Chapter 26 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 26 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 3 · Chapter 26

"...The Four Heroes?" Arnold had nothing but question marks in his mind.

"That's right." Claude nodded and began to seriously introduce the people he considered worthy of the title of strongest—

"Dragon-riding thief Carona, who assassinated seven Saint-tier experts of the Empire in a single night and escaped unscathed. As far as I know, no one who caught her attention has ever survived her dagger. If I say she's the greatest thief in history, the historians of that bunch called Britannia wouldn't even dispute it."

"The Twin Sword Saints, brothers Zoe and Joey, their ultimate technique is arguably the Empire's strongest spear. They can even combine their skills, amplifying their power to an unbelievable degree. There's an incident recorded in history that you should know about—namely the King of Giants, who was known for his absolute defense. It was those two brothers who killed him."

"And finally, there's Bernald the Storm Warrior, a human battlefield meat grinder. He's dueled Saint-tier dragons and participated in countless battles. He was the strongest warrior of the former kingdom and the first among the Four Heroes. Pardon my bluntness, but there's no opponent he can't defeat."

"Those four are the only ones worthy of the title of strongest. Everyone else is just a clown."

Arnold listened for a long time but couldn't make heads or tails of it, since he didn't recognize any of them. "Um, Mr. Claude, who are these people you're talking about?"

"You really have zero knowledge, don't you? These four are the founding meritorious officials of the former kingdom, honored with the title of the Four Great Heroes." Alice explained to Arnold. Actually, she hadn't understood much of what Claude had said either, but she had a vague impression of those four names.

"The former kingdom? Weren't they from over 400 years ago? We're in the Britannian Dynasty now." Arnold was confused about what Claude was talking about.

"Yes, Mr. Claude, I admit the Four Heroes you mentioned are all household names, but those people are already dead. I think comparing past figures to the present is completely meaningless." Alice furrowed her delicate brows and said.

Claude fell silent and didn't respond further.

Just then, the carriage came to a stop. The carriage door opened, and the old butler in tailcoat respectfully said, "Young Master Arnold, we've been traveling for quite a long time. The horses need to rest."

"Understood." Arnold nodded, then turned to the other two. "Let's get off and stretch our legs for a bit. We can breathe some fresh air."

"Hmph!" Alice, fuming inside, got off the carriage directly.

Claude also stepped down.

He didn't join Alice and Arnold but instead walked straight toward the nearby small forest.

His pitch-black armor clattered as he strode forward with steady steps.

The heavy sword on his back looked weathered in the moonlight, its surface covered in cracks.

Claude reached a secluded spot, scanned the area, and after confirming no suspicious persons were around, he quietly chanted a strange spell.

A black hole suddenly appeared before him, a deep vortex that seemed to lead to another dimension.

Claude immediately knelt on one knee, showing great respect.

Black hole: "Bernald, how are things on your end?"

Claude: "I'm currently on my way to Derby County."

From this conversation, it became clear that Claude was none other than Bernald, the foremost of the former kingdom's Four Heroes! The being known as invincible, who was supposed to have died 400 years ago, was now resurrected!?

Black hole: "If I recall correctly, the former kingdom's prime minister was buried in Derby County. The former king once shared the secrets of hell with him. Perhaps the final key to the hell legion is hidden within his tomb."

Claude: "Your Majesty is ever perceptive. I wonder if the current surge of undead in Derby County is connected to the former kingdom's prime minister?"

Black hole: "That's quite possible. The former kingdom's prime minister was a necromancer and wouldn't die so easily. Someone may have disturbed his long slumber. But you must be careful. Someone of Saint-tier from 400 years ago—there's no telling how powerful he's become now."

Claude: "Yes, Your Majesty, please rest assured. I will personally deliver the key to the hell legion to you. A mere necromancer poses no real challenge for me."

Black hole: "As expected of my trusted general and the foremost of the Four Heroes. Show me your loyalty."

Claude: "As you command, Your Majesty."

Black hole: "However, be discreet when carrying out your tasks. Don't let anyone discover you, especially the Britannian royal family. If they sense our presence, things will become troublesome."

Claude: "I understand, Your Majesty. To conceal my identity, I joined the Adventurers Guild and am now teaming up with a group of fools heading to Derby County. With their cover, our plans will never be discovered."

Black hole: "That's good. If anyone discovers our plans, remember—leave no survivors."

Claude: "Yes!"

Black hole: "Carona has already returned with the key. Zoe and Joey have also completed their missions. Now, the only key missing to summon the hell legion is yours. Speed things up."

Claude: "I shall give my all..."

Dark clouds thickened across the sky, and the light rain had temporarily ceased.

They were drawing closer to Derby County. What awaited them might be a fierce battle—or betrayal.

Alice crossed her arms, her brows tightly knitted, resentment boiling inside her. She found Claude utterly arrogant and overbearing, especially with that condescending attitude. Although Merlin had a similar disposition, he rarely showed it openly.

Thinking about it, Alice grew a bit worried about what Merlin was doing right now. Would he have torn down the guild because he couldn't get any commissions?

A chill ran through Alice's heart. She felt it was her fault for bringing that plague god to Lexem in the first place. If something went wrong, she'd share the blame.

"Ahhh~ How wonderful!" Arnold was beside himself with excitement, slipping back into his lovesick state. "The happiest thing in the world is nothing more than stargazing on a brilliantly starry night with the girl of your dreams."

"Stargazing? It's mostly cloudy right now. Will you act normal for once?" Alice wore a thoroughly disgusted expression.

"No, as long as I'm beside Miss Alice, I feel like everywhere is sunny." Arnold activated his sparkly mode and delivered the ultimate line straight out of a shoujo manga.

"Arnold, don't you know that's disgusting? Please stop it. I have absolutely zero interest in you." Alice turned and walked away, thoroughly repulsed by him.

"Miss Alice, you'll eventually change your mind. Merlin's big banana is merely a momentary thrill. True passionate love is the ultimate pursuit..." Arnold trailed behind her like a stubborn plaster.

Hearing Arnold's voice, Alice broke out in goosebumps. She strongly disliked mentally unstable people.

Alice and Arnold returned to the carriage, ready to continue their journey, but discovered Claude hadn't come back yet.

The coachman said Claude had gone into the nearby small forest. To save time, Alice decided to go urge him herself.

She wove through the dense thicket, hating places with little light, as it always reminded her of the escape in the Death Swamp, with two demonic wolves chasing her.

Alice looked around but couldn't find any sign of Claude.

Until she heard a low, muffled voice.

"For the restoration of the former kingdom, sacrifice your spirit...."

Alice furrowed her brows and walked toward the sound. She gently pushed aside a branch blocking her view—

A pitch-black great sword fell straight down toward Alice's head!

title: Chapter 27
content:
Chapter 27

Volume 3 · Chapter 27

Under the moonlight.

Claude, clad in pitch-black armor, resembled a demon god from an ancient battlefield. His Saint-tier aura instantly dried the moisture in the air.

The pitch-black, mottled giant sword swung with terrifying force, aiming straight for Alice's forehead.

Alice's expression went blank, her eyes wide open. She was completely terrified, unable to even let out a single scream.

She thought she was dead. Yes, in that fraction of a second, she truly felt as though she had taken a stroll through hell.

But Alice had always been lucky. The giant sword halted just above her forehead, at a deathly distance of less than three centimeters.

Alice stared at the sword's sharp blade, gleaming silver, as if it possessed the power to shatter everything in its path, capable of splitting the earth and shaking the sky.

"So it's Miss Alice. I thought it was some petty thief..."

Claude sheathed his giant sword and slung it onto his back. Beneath his deep helmet, no face was visible, and his voice carried absolutely no emotion.

The moment the giant sword left her head, cold sweat broke out on Alice. She stumbled backward several steps, her eyes filled with shock and suspicion, completely unable to tell whether Claude was friend or foe.

"I apologize for startling you. I deeply regret it." Claude paused, then continued, "What brings you here suddenly?"

"We... we're about to depart. I came to notify you." Alice steadied herself slightly, her expression very unnatural.

"Trouble Miss Alice..." Claude walked straight toward the edge of the forest, then suddenly stopped. "Did you hear something just now?"

Alice hesitated for a moment, recalling what just happened, and asked faintly, "No. Did you say something?"

"Let's go, Miss Alice. If we're lucky, we'll reach Denby County by tonight." Claude left without turning back.

As for the reason Claude didn't kill Alice?

It was because if Alice, a member of this squad, died, it would cause trouble. Their current objective was to go to Denby County to get the key, and they couldn't afford to waste time.

Moreover, this squad served as his cover, like camouflage. How could he easily destroy it?

Alice stood where she was, watching Claude's retreating back without speaking, thinking to herself:

What a suspicious guy.

Overreacting like that... he must be hiding a secret, right?

What exactly is the revival of the former kingdom...

Claude waited inside the carriage.

After a while, with no sign of Alice returning, he grew somewhat puzzled and prepared to go down and look for her.

But the moment Claude stepped out of the carriage, he saw a procession of luxurious carriages passing by, escorted by knights in white armor bearing the Rose family crest. It was precisely Cecilia, who had previously had a falling out with Merlin.

Hmm? The Duke of Rose's forces? Why are they here?

Arnold was somewhat surprised and stood still to observe.

As a result, the luxurious procession stopped right in front of Arnold. A window rolled down, revealing Cecilia's beautiful face.

"Isn't this the landlord's foolish son, Arnold? Didn't expect to meet you here."

"Good heavens, Miss Cecilia, you're actually here? I remember our last meeting was a year ago at the duke's mansion ball." Arnold grinned widely, a smile that truly matched the title of the landlord's foolish son.

"I didn't expect to meet you here either. It seems you're just as foolish as you were a year ago." Cecilia said with a look of disdain, apparently looking down on someone like Arnold from the bottom of her heart.

"Hehe, Miss Cecilia is joking. Have you graduated from the seminary in London yet?" Arnold asked tentatively.

"Not yet. It's vacation now," Cecilia replied calmly.

"Instead of enjoying your vacation at home, what are you doing out here?" Arnold asked curiously.

"I'm here to resolve the crisis in Denby County on behalf of my father," Cecilia said seriously.

"What a coincidence. That's exactly the purpose of my trip as well," Arnold said with a smile.

"..." Cecilia furrowed her delicate brows, seeming somewhat displeased. Only one hero was needed to resolve the matter, and Arnold's involvement made him a competitor. "Heh, Arnold, you're just a low-tier rookie. I advise you not to go looking for death. This isn't something you can get involved in. What can you and a single groom possibly do?"

"No, no, no. I have teammates too. A high-tier demon swordsman, and a Saint-tier powerhouse," Arnold said full of confidence.

"What?! A Saint-tier powerhouse!"

Cecilia was visibly startled. Saint-tier powerhouses were as rare as phoenix feathers and unicorn horns. There weren't many in all of Great Britain. The strongest among her father's guards were merely high-tier.

Saint-tier powerhouses could only be hired by royal family members.

Just some landlord's foolish son actually managed to team up with a Saint-tier powerhouse? What a joke!

Cecilia felt extremely unbalanced inside and grew increasingly annoyed with Arnold.

"Just keep bragging! So desperate to save face..."

"I'm not,"

Arnold felt deeply wronged.

While the two noble youths were scheming against each other, the groom suddenly shouted in panic.

"Trouble! Young master! Young master! Look over there..."

Arnold turned to look and saw a long line of fire burning on the horizon, illuminating the dim evening and dotting the deepening night.

"Burning rhinos! No! It's a herd of burning rhinos!"

Fiery red skin, sharp rhino horns, bodies engulfed in flames. With every breath, they exhaled scorching air from their nostrils, shrouding themselves in white mist.

Burning rhinos are gregarious mid-tier magical beasts that migrate south every autumn. This time, Hobbs had predicted it exactly, and Cecilia had run right into them.

While a single burning rhino isn't terrifying, hundreds or thousands of them are. Can you imagine the scene of countless heavy trucks charging all at once?

Even a high-tier fighter would tremble before a herd of mid-tier burning rhinos, getting brutally trampled. They wouldn't just die; they'd be crippled.

The burning rhinos, as if gone mad, surged straight toward Arnold and the others, destroying everything in their path. The ground itself vibrated with a low hum.

"...No way? Why am I so unlucky..."

Arnold's face turned pale, and he collapsed directly onto the ground.

"Tch!" Cecilia felt embarrassed, her expression grave. She thought to herself that those two commoners from before had actually been right. What a jinx!

"Everyone, listen to my order! Protect the young lady!"

Kyle remained relatively calm, but his ugly complexion clearly showed he was under immense pressure. He somewhat regretted not listening to Merlin and the others; if only they had taken the small path.

The horses began to panic one after another, neighing restlessly.

The white-armored guards dismounted and quickly surrounded Cecilia's carriage, looking as though they were prepared to live and die with it.

"Listen well! Do not leave your positions by even a single step! Spear the ones far away, slash the ones close by. Do not let a single magical beast get near Miss Cecilia!" Kyle shook the spear in his hand, stood at the very front, and shouted with cold sweat dripping down, "The glory of the Duke of Rose is with us!"

...Arnold was scrambling and rolling on the ground, looking utterly wretched. Watching the fierce and ruthless burning rhinos draw closer, his courage was nearly shattered.

Miss Alice?

Lord Claude!?

Where did they go?!

(°口°)::

My mother complained that my hair is too long, so I'm going to Master Wang's shop at the village entrance to get a haircut. I'll continue grinding this afternoon. At least two extra chapters, maybe three if I'm lucky.

title: Chapter 28 — Bonus Chapter: Monthly Ticket Update
content:
Chapter 28 — Bonus Chapter: Monthly Ticket Update

Volume 3 · Chapter 28

Countless burning rhinos thundered toward them, the ground shaking relentlessly beneath their stampeding hooves, their roars merging into a single fearsome cacophony.

They saw no obstacles in their path, instantly crushing and obliterating everything that dared to stand in their way.

"Holy shit! This is fucking ridiculous!" Claude felt his legs go weak, as if he couldn't even stand on his own.

Cecilia's delicate brows furrowed tightly together as she watched the herd of burning rhinos closing in, unease stirring in her chest.

She had no idea how long the defense line Kael had assembled could hold — Kael himself probably wasn't confident either.

To withstand the rhino charge, Cecilia as a mid-tier priestess had to give it her all. Her magic surged, and she began casting buff after buff.

"Strength Enhancement — 200 percent!"

"Agility Enhancement — 200 percent!"

"Endurance Enhancement — 200 percent!"

"Ice-element Attack Enchantment, applied!"

"Saint Light Arbitration — fully activated!"

The white-armored knights felt power surging within them, their weapons glowing with white light as traces of frost seeped from the blades.

As for Kael, bolstered by Cecilia's buffs, he pushed his high-tier fighting spirit to its absolute peak, entering a state of full battle readiness.

The darkness was illuminated by the burning rhinos, their flames roaring as though rising straight from hell itself.

Everyone held their breath, tension coiling tight as the great battle was about to break.

But then — the heavy swordsman Claude marched right in.

Claude strode forward with long steps, his armor clanking noisily. He passed right by Arnold and Cecilia and the others without so much as a glance, walking straight to the very front and facing the surging rhino horde head-on.

What the hell was this guy?

Facing such a threatening presence without so much as a tremor of confusion in his step.

Was he standing at the very front trying to get himself killed?

Cecilia's eyes went wide as she stared fixedly at the pitch-black heavy swordsman.

As a holy priestess, she could sense absolutely no sign of a living person from him — and worse, she could barely detect the faintest trace of dark magic clinging to him.

"Sir, please don't stand at the very front. We should stick together and defend as one," Kael said, sensing that Claude was not weak and hoping to bring him into their formation — that would improve their odds of survival considerably.

"I have no use for associating with the weak. Huddling together for warmth is something only trash would do," Claude said flatly.

"What?! " Kael stood dumbfounded, wondering why this guy looked down on everyone so utterly. Then fine — go ahead and get crushed by the burning rhinos if that's how you want to die!

The darkness merged with Claude's pitch-black battle armor, though it reflected the firelight brilliantly. Facing such an enormous force, he seemed to feel no pressure whatsoever.

Claude drew the massive greatsword from his back, and golden Saint-tier斗气 erupted around him, blazing brilliantly against the night.

Cecilia and the others were all visibly shaken. They hadn't expected a Saint-tier powerhouse — no wonder he was so disdainful! He clearly looked down on them outright.

Once the distance was sufficient, Claude stepped forward with a wide stride, gripped his greatsword with both hands, and assumed his stance.

With a single fierce horizontal slash, a violent gale erupted, sending sand and rocks flying, and even the air itself seemed to freeze in an instant!

A powerful Saint-tier剑波 cleaved through the air, and in the blink of an eye, countless burning rhinos were reduced to meat paste, their blood spraying and staining the earth crimson.

A single horizontal swing, and total annihilation in an instant. The night was swallowed back into calm, and everyone present got a glimpse — however small — of the terrifying power of a Saint-tier warrior.

Alice stood at the edge of the jungle, watching the entire rhino horde get wiped out in silence, utterly speechless. She felt that Claude was different from the Saint-tier warriors she had known before — so overwhelmingly powerful it left her unable to speak.

Alice wavered in her convictions. Perhaps Claude had been right all along — even among Saint-tier warriors, there were frauds. Saint-tier was merely a threshold that separated the strong from the weak, nothing more.

Kael's jaw hung open, his mind racing with one thought: *Powerful! Incredibly powerful! No wonder he's Saint-tier!*

Arnold slowly rose to his feet, brushed the dust from his clothes, and said with a smile, "Miss Cecilia, allow me to introduce Mr. Claude — my teammate, fellow adventurer, and a Saint-tier powerhouse."

Cecilia, still recovering from her shock, descended from the carriage and demanded, "How the hell did you find a Saint-tier warrior to be your teammate? What kind of terms did you offer?!"

"Well... um... two hundred thousand gold coins," Arnold said awkwardly.

Cecilia turned on her heel and marched toward Claude, her aristocratic pride fully on display. "How much is that rich kid's idiot son paying you? I'll give you double! Join my team instead!"

"What's your purpose?" Claude asked, sheathing his heavy greatsword back onto his spine.

Cecilia glanced at Arnold nearby, noted that he was too far away to hear their conversation, then leaned in and lowered her voice. "I have secret intelligence. The necromancy incident in Denby County was triggered by two grave robbers, and that graveyard is the tomb of a former kingdom chancellor. Come with me as we delve underground to uncover the truth, and you'll be the hero of Denby County."

"I refuse," Claude said without a shred of mercy.

He intended to drop Arnold and the rest behind once they reached Denby County and act on his own — that way there would be no risk of secrets leaking.

Claude couldn't have been happier at the thought of traveling completely solo. Team-ups were impossible for him.

Cecilia was equally proud by nature, and the moment her proactive invitation was rejected, she didn't hesitate. She turned on her heel and walked away, fuming inwardly: *So what if he's Saint-tier? Who does he think he is? What an arrogant piece of trash — just keep rolling around with that rich kid's idiot son, then!* All the adventurers in Lexington were utter idiots, damn it.

"Miss Cecilia, aren't you going to catch up on old times?" Arnold spoke up at the most inopportune moment.

"Arnold, you little fucker, get lost and stop talking to me!" Cecilia directed her frustration squarely at Arnold.

"I... uh..." Arnold scratched his head, embarrassed. "What did I do?"

Cecilia simply climbed back into her carriage and called out, "Kael!"

Kael, spear in hand, immediately stepped forward with a respectful demeanor. "Yes, miss? How may I assist you?"

"Increase the caravan's pace. The faster, the better. Even if you work the horses to death, we must reach Denby County before the first half of the night!" Cecilia commanded, her face radiating hostility.

"Well... miss, is it really necessary to be in such a hurry?" Kael asked, genuinely puzzled.

"It is absolutely necessary! I must prove my capabilities to Father and show that I am a true member of the Rose Family — that I have天赋 no one else can match! This necromancy incident in Denby County is the perfect trial, and it must be resolved by my own hands!"

Cecilia's face darkened, descending into a deeply obsessive state. She crumpled her white robe in her grip, her expression twisted and ugly.

She thought of her father's dismissive attitude toward her, and fury surged within her. He had called her the most useless child in the family — lacking cultivation天赋, lacking political cunning, destined only to be married off to a remote noble and waste her entire life away.

Cecilia was a girl who refused to admit defeat. She harbored intense resentment toward her father's contempt, and this desperate need to prove herself was precisely why a young lady of her station had personally come all the way to Denby County.

"I understand, Miss Cecilia," Kael bowed his head, sympathy evident in his expression.

"We will reach Denby County as quickly as possible, and I will be the first to enter that graveyard and resolve this crisis — then Father will surely look at me with new eyes!" Cecilia said earnestly.

"But shouldn't we first organize our fighting forces to resist the undead, and prioritize eliminating the threat to the lives of Denby County's citizens?" Kael suggested.

"Who the hell cares about some minor merit like that? Is it as valuable as resolving the entire incident?" Cecilia said dismissively.

"Saving the common people is of paramount importance, and regarding your reputation—"

"Enough, Kael!"

Cecilia cut him off. Her face was dark — and despite being a priestess, she radiated not an ounce of holiness.

Looking down at Kael, her eyes cold and empty, utterly devoid of compassion, she asked —

"What does the life or death of lowborn cattle have to do with me?"

"I only care about the results. The process is irrelevant."

title: Chapter 29 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 29 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 3 · Chapter 29

This is Dengbi County, where the stationed troops had already built a camp for the incoming adventurers to reside.
Once the numbers were about right, they would organize everyone to counterattack those skeletons.
The incident originally occurred in a forest, and now some villages around it have been completely destroyed.
The undead skeletons move sluggishly during the day, but become active at night, and their combat power increases rapidly; they kill any living thing they see.
However, once daylight comes, this group of skeleton soldiers retreats into the forest, making it impossible to see what's inside.
So the commander of the stationed troops decided to rest tonight, and tomorrow morning organize everyone, taking advantage of the daytime, to launch an all‑out rush into the forest for a massive sweep, striving to quell this undead outbreak in one fell swoop.
Not a few adventurers from Wales have come, and even adventurers from other regions are present.
Rather than saying this is a pre‑battle mobilization, it's more like an adventurers' social gathering; everyone is completely relaxed, treating this place as a party.
Drinking, bragging, picking up girls to go dance at the big bonfire—basically there isn't a single serious person; even the stationed troops' soldiers are mingling with the veteran adventurers.
Soldiers are usually those who train in martial arts but haven't cultivated magic or fighting spirit, so they greatly admire this group of free‑spirited adventurers, especially those with romanticist sentiments.
Since Arnold is a noble, when his party arrived, they were received by the stationed troops' officers and allowed to stay in a single‑person tent.
This made Alice extremely happy; she wished she could have her own private room, thinking Arnold was a bit slow‑witted but sometimes useful.
Claude said he needed to rest, so he went back to his tent.
Alice watched Claude's back, saying nothing, wondering what scheme he had in mind.
Now Alice is very doubtful about Claude's identity—a remarkably powerful Saint‑tier expert who came to be an adventurer? It just feels strange.
The Adventurers Guild is all about freedom; they don't even check members' past stains, accepting anyone wholesale.
This leads to many adventurers having shady pasts—like Merlin, who dines and dashes, still considered a minor blemish.
So Alice now suspects Claude… could he be an imperial wanted criminal? Teaming up with someone like that would be too dangerous.
Claude's departure didn't disturb Arnold's mood; he even thought Claude was considerate of the atmosphere, deliberately giving him and Alice some private space.
"Ah~, Miss Alice, such a beautiful night, just you and me—why don’t we..."
"Please act normal. We need to exchange information with other adventurers." Alice sighed and muttered to herself, "If only Hobbs were here. This old guy is annoying, but he's an intelligence expert—he knows everything."
"Miss Alice, can't you see I'm useful too?" Claude activated his sparkle mode, his blue hair curled, "I'm so handsome next to you. Don't you feel proud to be seen with me?"
"Get lost…" Alice gave a look of utter disdain.
"Come on, let's have a romantic date by the grand bonfire~" Arnold deliberately made an enchanting expression, like a melancholy little prince.
"It's just to exchange information, right?" Alice frowned, thoroughly annoyed by Arnold. She silently vowed in her heart:
If I ever team up with Arnold again, I'll… livestream stuffing it…
The two arrived at the center of the camp.
This was where the most adventurers gathered.
It looked very chaotic, with people of all sorts mixed together.
Alice had sharp eyes and immediately spotted Merlin and Hobbs laughing and drinking, pouring down酒 nonstop.
It turned out these two scrap‑iron tiers had arrived at Dengbi County long ago, even faster than anyone else.
Under Hobbs' guidance, Merlin had crossed the Marosa Mountains without any obstacles, not a single danger along the way.
Although they were the last to depart from Rexham, they arrived more than half a day earlier than everyone else. The two had already been eating, drinking, and having fun at the camp for a while.
Merlin thought Hobbs was truly a talent. Full of adventure experience, a seasoned veteran, able to get along with anyone. In no time, he had gotten to know most of the adventurers here, quite the legendary social butterfly!
If he had known about such a talent when he was Demon Lord, he would definitely have recruited him and appointed him as Chief Diplomat of the First Demon Lord Palace.
In short, Merlin felt that drinking and bragging with this old‑timer Hobbs was incredibly enjoyable, though to outsiders it just looked like two odors sharing the same臭味.
When Alice saw these two, her face showed an expression of utter despair, as if she had lost all hope in life and instantly lost the motivation to do anything.
Good heavens, why are these two here?
And they reached Dengbi County faster than me.
What have I been doing all this way? My efficiency is even lower than two scrap‑iron tiers!
Alice covered her face, feeling cursed, unable to escape Merlin's shadow wherever she went. She could see him everywhere.
"Huh? Hobbs is here too, and…?" Arnold immediately put on a very serious expression. "That rival competing for mating rights with me—what a narrow road."
Alice punched him ten times in the face, having been driven crazy by her useless teammate.
"Ugh… Miss Alice, that's… sufficient…" Arnold felt a nosebleed coming on.
"Shut up, I don't want to hear you talk." Alice said, exhausted body and soul. She looked up to assess the situation, then prepared to go chat with Merlin and the others. Since they had arrived early, they might have more information.
Since there were acquaintances around, there was no need to awkwardly chat with strangers.
Hobbs was drinking with the people nearby, his nose red like a light bulb.
As for Merlin, a whole group of older female adventurers surrounded him, all big‑bosomed older sisters chatting happily, making the female adventurers laugh uncontrollably.
After all, Merlin had a delicate woman's face, looking like a fresh young meat, and older women liked this type. Combined with his succubus constitution, he was indeed quite charming.
Merlin was also helpless. It seemed his succubus talent only worked on older sisters, with little effect on peers or younger girls.
Female adventurer: "Brother, why does your certificate say you're a villager?"
Merlin: "Villager is just a cover for my powerful background. Don't worry about it. Want to team up? I'm S‑tier with my sword draw."
The female adventurers giggled, thinking this young scrap‑iron tier Merlin was cute and interesting, unaware that he was already over 200 years old.
"This idol of middle‑aged and elderly women…"
Alice gritted her teeth and muttered, a sour taste rising inexplicably in her heart, making her very angry.
So Alice marched over to Merlin's table in a furious manner and chased away all the chirping women.
"Move aside! We're here to discuss serious business!"
Most of the female adventurers were Silver‑tier. Seeing Alice's Gold‑tier certificate on her chest, they tactfully moved away, assuming Alice was Merlin's official wife or girlfriend.
Alice sat down next to Merlin without hesitation, staring at him with fierce eyes.
"Oh? Alice, you're just here?" Merlin asked in surprise. He wasn't angry about the older sisters being chased away by Alice; he had never had much interest anyway, it was just casual chat.
Alice saw Merlin's frivolous appearance and felt her anger surge. She raised her small fist and firmly bonked his forehead. Idiot! You're not serious at all outside! Running around picking up girls—this is work time, not playtime!
"Huh!?" Merlin held his forehead, completely bewildered.
Vaguely visible above the two's heads were opposing status buffs—
Merlin debuff «Consort Members +111»: _
Alice buff «Wife Status 111…»:

title: Chapter 30
content:
Chapter 30

Volume 3 · Chapter 30

Alice stared at Merlin, her face brimming with resentment. She couldn't quite figure out what was going on either, but seeing this jerk flirting with other women made her incredibly angry.

Merlin himself was completely baffled. He hadn't provoked Alice at all, yet inexplicably he'd just gotten a solid whack on the head.

Normally, if he got beaten after provoking someone, he could accept it. But getting hit when he hadn't done anything wrong at all — that truly grated on him.

And even if he did go around being improper outside, what on earth did that have to do with Alice?

"Are you sick or something? Did you forget to take your medicine before heading out?"

"You're the one who hasn't taken their medicine! You were randomly hitting on other people while on the job — can you be serious for once?!"

Alice stood tall, planting herself firmly on the moral high ground and fiercely condemning Merlin.

"Does whether I'm serious or not have anything to do with you? Why do you like meddling in other people's affairs so much? What's wrong with chatting with big sisters?" Merlin leaned lazily against the table, his face full of grievance.

"I..." Alice fell silent. She thought about it, and he had a point — what did it matter how Merlin acted toward her? But deep down she just felt annoyed. "You were the one I recommended! How will others view me if you behave like this? They'll say I deliberately brought a parasite into the guild who just freeloads and waits to die! My reputation will be ruined too!"

Hobbs watched from the side, giggling all the while. His red, wine-stained nose looked utterly comical. He saw through everything clearly and thought to himself: Alice was obviously jealous. Since when did a recommendation come with responsibility for someone's work attitude? He'd never heard of such a guild regulation.

"Your reputation was already bad to begin with. Behind your back, everyone calls you 'the irritable washboard.'" Merlin said it with ill intent, his expression torn between wanting to laugh and holding it in.

"Hah?!" Alice flew into a rage and slammed the table hard. "Who said that?! I'll chop them into eight pieces!"

"Hobbs told me..." Merlin immediately shifted the blame onto Hobbs.

Alice was furious and fixed Hobbs with a death stare, wanting nothing more than to drag that sharp-tongued guy out and beat him senseless.

Hobbs instantly shivered, grabbed the bottle, and chugged it down — drinking heavily while pretending he knew nothing.

Alice felt there were too many people around to actually beat Hobbs up, so she took her frustration out on Merlin instead. "Don't change the subject! I don't care! You're my recommendation, so you must watch your work attitude. When executing missions, you're not allowed to flirt with others — be serious!"

"Ah..." Merlin rested his cheek on his hand, his gaze drifting away, and said noncommittally, "You were the one who left me behind and went to team up with someone else. I don't want to be lectured by you."

"I..." Alice's face flushed crimson and she didn't know what to say. "I just can't stand your lazy attitude! Work seriously for me! Otherwise, can you even afford the rent?!"

"Hmm?" Merlin raised his eyelids and asked in surprise, "Didn't you wish I'd just get out of here?"

"..." Alice was speechless again, unable to retort after Merlin's sharp words. "Can't I just not like the look of you?! Seeing you freeloaf and drift along makes me think you're scum! You're wasting the opportunity I gave by recommending you! You bastard!"

"Hey, I don't like the look of you either. Your habit of meddling in other people's affairs is really annoying..." Merlin frowned, looking at Alice with utter disgust.

"What kind of look is that?!" Alice's brows knit together and a vein on her forehead twitched. "What right do you have to look down on me? You're a scumbag who only knows how to trick women out of their perfume money. How should I view you? It should be me who looks down on you!"

"I won't mention your bad temper, your nosy nature, or your stinginess. Just comparing you to the horizon — your washboard chest is enough to make people despise you, haha..." Merlin laughed heartily. He just loved seeing Alice turn crimson,憋着 frustration and completely powerless against him.

"What did you say?!" Alice's little nose was almost crooked from anger. She suddenly raised her fist and struck toward Merlin's face, infusing high-tier magic power into her knuckles, which gleamed with white cold energy. "Die!"

Merlin didn't even lift his eyelids. He simply caught Alice's small fist and said calmly, "Don't start swinging randomly. I'll counterattack."

Alice had no response. She felt like a volcano was pressing down on her chest. She couldn't out-talk Merlin, couldn't out-fight him either — there was no way out, completely dominated on every front.

o

Hobbs, watching from the side, grew a little worried. With magical power being used, he feared things might actually escalate into a fight, so he tried to mediate diplomatically.

"Alright, alright, what are you two squabbling like a married couple for? You'll end up sharing the same blanket anyway."

Merlin: "Don't talk nonsense. I have nothing to do with this washboard."

Alice: "Hobbs, if you keep spouting nonsense, I'll cut your tongue out!"

Hobbs licked his lips, sweating nervously. What were these two trying to hide? Did they think everyone was blind? Anyone could tell they were already like a married couple.

Merlin: "Hobbs, wipe your eyes clean. How could I possibly have anything to do with this washboard? With her like this, who on earth would want her? Oh right, except that blind man Arnold — he has his peculiar tastes."

Alice: "What did you say?! You're not exactly better than me either! Lazy and gluttonous, shamelessly freeloading off others! You could at best be an idol for middle-aged women!"

Merlin: "I happen to like mature women. There's more flavor to them — they're my type, okay? Hobbs, let me tell you a little secret. A year ago, on the northern coastline of Scotland, this slut Alice actually stripped naked and tried to seduce me. If I hadn't been uninterested, we'd probably have a kid by now. Now do you understand just how shameless Alice is? Hehe~"

Alice: "Merlin, you bastard! I never tried to seduce you! You were the one who misled me — you never explained things clearly! Blame your damn pervy eyes that are always leering, never serious for a moment! Hobbs, listen to this — I'll expose Merlin's dark secrets. This guy's been freeloading and conning people across Scotland, racking up a mountain of debt. He also went around hitting on nobles' wives. In Manchester, everyone hated his guts. Do you know what I found him doing when I tracked him down? He was working as a male companion in a small village, haha, I nearly died laughing~"

Merlin: "What's wrong with your mouth, you washboard? It's poison."

Alice: "You attacked me first! I wasn't about to sit here and take your lectures!"

The two of them immediately started digging up each other's dark history, mercilessly exposing every embarrassing thing about the other, and even dragging Hobbs, a complete outsider, into it — as if they wanted everyone in the world to know.

Hobbs watched the scene of this married couple wounding each other and kept silent, helping neither side. He thought arguing between couples was like stepping into a quagmire, so it was better not to get involved. He just said,

"Don't fight anymore. Give each other some face, you two. Come on, drink first."

Merlin: "Get lost!"

Alice: "Get lost!"

"Hey, why are you both taking it out on me? I'm innocent!" Hobbs looked extremely awkward, grabbed the vodka on the table, and began—

"*Gulp gulp gulp gulp gulp...*
"Gulp gulp gulp gulp gulp..."

title: Chapter 31 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 31 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 3 · Chapter 31

Merlin and Alice glared at each other, looking like they didn't get along.

But after insulting each other for a while, they gradually calmed down.

They simply refused to back down, making the atmosphere stagnant.

Hobbs put down the jug, looking a bit dizzy and feeling a bit tipsy, "Enough, can you two keep it up until tomorrow morning?"

"Hmph!" Alice turned her head away, looking disdainfully at Merlin.

"Hehe." Merlin chuckled lightly, feeling like he had won this argument.

"Alice, you came way too late; I and Merlin arrived long ago." Hobbs tried to change the subject.

"The road had some setbacks, delaying the time." Alice answered unhappily, "So where did you two come from?"

"We rode your little donkey, crossed the Marosa Mountains, and arrived here directly. Isn't that unexpected?" Merlin picked up his wine cup, beaming with pride.

"My donkey?" Alice paused, then reacted, angrily scolding Hobbs, "Who let you use my vehicle?!"

"Don't yell at me; Merlin brought it." Hobbs innocently waved his hand.

"You bastard!" Alice's anger spiked, thinking Merlin really didn't treat her as an outsider; his skin was really thick.

"Using it won't kill you~" Merlin pouted, speaking with interest, "Your donkey really runs fast. Especially when you whip its butt, it runs faster than a normal horse. Me and Hobbs—we whipped it, ha..."

Hobbs suppressed a laugh on his face, seeming to thoroughly enjoy the feeling of the donkey drifting around the curves of the Marosa Mountains.

"....What are you two doing?! It has to walk so many roads every day; I've never dared to whip it, yet you two treat it like this! Is there no humanity left?!" Alice grabbed Merlin's collar and shook it violently, "I'll fight you! You lunatic!"

"Alice, don't cause trouble..."

Merlin's head swayed like a drum,

"Your donkey is an M, the bigger the better."

"You're talking nonsense!" Alice's eyes were red, about to be cried over by Merlin.

The two argued uncontrollably, and at that moment Arnold walked over, his nostrils stuffed with two balls of cotton, presumably from being hit by Alice just now.

"Merlin!" Arnold had a serious face, speaking seriously, "Was it really because of Alice-sama's mating rights that you came over?"

"Go to hell Arnold! Don't keep saying 'mating rights'!" Alice released Merlin, glaring angrily at Arnold.

"Hmm?" Merlin lifted his head, looking at Arnold, "What's wrong with your nose?"

"Hmph, this is the mark given by Alice-sama~" Arnold instantly switched to a shoujo manga sparkling mode, smiling as he fell in love~!

The scene instantly fell into an awkward silence; Alice and Merlin looked at him expressionlessly.

Merlin: "This family... does it have some issues?"

Alice: "You only just realized? You're really slow."

Merlin: "No, I was just saying only someone with issues in their head would like you."

Alice: "If you dare say one more word, even if I can't beat you, I'll die with you."

"Cough!" Arnold coughed to hide his embarrassment, continuing, "Merlin, you can chase after me to prove you're still a man, not inferior to me as my rival, but it's all over! I'll have a brilliant performance tomorrow, Mr. Claude will take my place and charge ahead; I'll use my strength to tell you that Alice-sama's mating rights are mine!"

Hobbs looked at Arnold and clapped his hands.

Alice picked up the wine cup in front of her and threw it directly at Hobbs' head, silencing him.

"Emmm...." Merlin had a complex expression, awkwardly saying, "Actually, I don't care about Alice's mating rights; I came for the 5000 gold coin prize."

Alice suddenly felt a bit breathless, though she hated having her mating rights arbitrarily used for a duel, the fact that Merlin had no interest was the most painful.

"Ha...." Arnold lifted his hair, "Merlin, you're actually afraid, right? I understand, but there's no chance to back out. Last time's victory belongs to you, but this time, victory will surely belong to me; I already see myself and Alice-sama entering the wedding hall together, receiving everyone's blessings~"

"Oh, you add.... Merlin had nothing to say, feeling Arnold's delusion was too severe.

"Arnold, can you shut up? I really want to chop off your head right now..." Alice had a very worried expression.

"Alice-sama, don't be so cold." Arnold plopped down beside Alice, "You can rest assured; I must win the duel and rescue you from Merlin's hands, believe me!"

"Get away! Stay away from me! I'm sick of you..." Alice kicked Arnold away in her anger, making him sit on the ground.

"Damn it" Arnold stood up, rubbing his butt, frustratedly saying, "It seems Alice-sama has already taken the shape of Merlin, still longing for his big banana."

A--

"Arnold, stretch your head over here..." Alice had a blank expression, her face dark, silently drawing out a thin sword.

"However, there's no problem; in love, the one who often wins is someone like me who is persistent, Alice-sama. You'll eventually see my shining points and leave Merlin." Arnold lifted his head, gazing at the sky at a 45° angle, mournfully, "Someone like me who is willing to forgive the color of original sin on my head and is willing to take the pot... there aren't many left; I'm truly the pride of the Austin family~!"

"You see what I and Alice look like a couple, why are we all misunderstanding?" Merlin said with interest.

"Hmph, Merlin, are you showing off that you currently occupy Alice-sama? You're a despicable guy; your possession is only temporary, tomorrow is the decisive battle...."

Arnold left in dissatisfaction, presumably going to drink alone in frustration.

Merlin sighed, glancing sideways at Alice, feeling that getting along with this armor-plated warrior caused more trouble than before.

B E this novel

Alice, seeing the annoying Arnold leave, and remembering she still needed to inquire about intelligence, asked.

"Hobbs, do you know anything about this matter of comparing counties this time?"

"This intelligence still has some; only... Hobbs swayed and was pinned down.

"Tsk!" Alice clicked her tongue, angrily throwing two gold coins to Hobbs, "Speak quickly, you stingy guy."

"Hehehe~" Hobbs laughed cunningly, putting the money in his pocket—

"I've collected a lot of intelligence; combining them, I roughly figured it out, the whole matter is a bit clearer now. In the northern forest, there's the grave of the former kingdom's prime minister; it's a three-story underground maze.

"Not long ago, two tomb raiders, not knowing their fate, disturbed the soul of the former kingdom's prime minister, waking it up. This prime minister is a lich; you all know, even if the body dies, the soul lives on; these skeleton undead are all summoned by him. Judging by the trend, he wants to expand outward to widen his territory.

"So the whole matter would be easy then."

"Whoever can kill the lich in the grave is the greatest hero.

"The stationed army means clearing the undead seven times and restricting them to the forest, waiting for the royal capital to send people over.

"However, a lich over four hundred years old; even if a Saint-tier priest from the Vatican comes personally, it's not easy..."

(Note: The last line ends abruptly in the source text, so the translation ends there as well.)

title: Chapter 32 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 32 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 3 · Chapter 32

Deep night.

The time was nearing dawn.

The adventurers' gathering had long since ended, leaving behind a scene of chaos in the campsite.

Almost everyone had already fallen asleep, seeming very harmonious and peaceful.

Inside a single-person tent, Alice appeared to be in a deep sleep, but her ears twitched frequently, constantly alerting her to everything around her.

When Alice heard the clanking sound of armor, she suddenly opened her eyes and looked out of the tent. Under the moonlight, she could clearly see a dark figure passing by the tent.

Alice lifted her blanket. She hadn't even taken off her clothes inside, and her sword was still hanging at her waist.

She tiptoed to the entrance, lifted the tent flap, and looked outside—

Claude, carrying his heavy sword, walked straight toward the north gate, his steps steady, with not a hint of hesitation.

This black-armored swordsman, under the cold and quiet moonlight, seemed quite mysterious.

He really is suspicious. Tonight I absolutely have to find out who you are!

Without the slightest hesitation, Alice stealthily followed Claude, who had slipped out late at night. To avoid being discovered, she kept her distance and did not dare to approach rashly.

The two left the camp one after the other. It just so happened that Hobbs, because he had drunk too much, was outside relieving himself. Half-asleep, he seemed to see a silver-haired Alice.

Hobbs slapped his own forehead to make himself more alert, but Alice had already disappeared.

He pursed his lips and muttered to himself—

"Must have been an illusion...

book, SFA

Once outside the camp,

CCt久小、产

Alice realized that Claude was heading toward the forest in the north—namely, the graveyard where the former kingdom prime minister was buried.

This filled Alice with confusion.

Could Claude be some kind of lone hero?

Trying to solve the crisis of Dengbi County all by himself?

Alice thought that was unlikely and decided to follow all the way to figure it out.

Along the way, several wandering skeleton soldiers appeared, but Claude didn't even bother drawing his sword—he punched them apart with a single blow.

Alice felt relieved. It seemed all the undead along the path would be eliminated by Claude, which meant she wouldn't need to fight and could avoid the possibility of being discovered.

After entering the forest, Alice noticed that there weren't as many undead as she had imagined. It seemed someone had already been here before, and there were traces of battles on the ground.

Had someone already entered the forest before her?

Alice furrowed her delicate brows. She felt that the deeper they went into the graveyard, the more complicated and murky things became.

Atop the hill, there was a building resembling a temple. It looked aged, severely weathered, and the statues were so eroded that their forms could no longer be recognized.

Claude didn't stop along the way and went directly into the temple.

Alice hurriedly followed and poked her head in to see Claude standing before a set of underground stairs.

"It seems that's the entrance to the underground labyrinth..."

Alice had been away from the camp for quite some time.

Crimson sunlight spread out from the horizon.

Most people were already awake and packed and ready to head to the northern forest to exterminate the skeletal undead inside.

However, the two drunks Merlin and Hobbs were still asleep, their snoring shaking the heavens. They seemed to have completely forgotten about the undead extermination.

The two of them slept in extremely unflattering postures, sprawled out on the ground. Hobbs was even wearing flashy pink underwear. The rugged uncle on the surface didn't turn out to be this kind of person underneath.

"Miss Alice?"

Arnold's voice came from outside the tent. He had originally planned to offer his first morning smile to Alice.

But when he went to find Alice just now, she wasn't anywhere. It was as if she had already left the camp.

Suspecting that Alice was running around with Merlin, Arnold tracked them down with a heavy heart.

"Miss Alice!? "

Arnold burst into the tent and saw Merlin covered by a blanket, with a bulge underneath, as if someone were hiding there.

Good heavens! Could it be that Miss Alice came to have fun with Merlin last night and fought through the entire night right in front of Hobbs?

Oh God! How could Miss Alice have fallen so low, becoming so lewd?! How on earth can I purify this sin...

Arnold stepped forward and tore open Merlin's blanket, crying out in grief and indignation.

"Miss Alice, come with me—Eh!? "

Arnold's face showed utter bewilderment. Under Merlin's blanket there was no Alice, only a large pillow, which Merlin was夹ping between his legs. Apparently, this position was more comfortable.

Hobbs, hearing the commotion, woke up and sat up, rubbing his eyes.

"What's going on? Making so much noise so early in the morning."

Merlin felt a cold breeze and shivered, his buttocks trembling from the chill. He instantly woke up and shot straight up.

"Arnold, I swear to you—if you ever dare to lift my blanket again while I'm sleeping, I will definitely send you to hell. My blanket is fused with my body. What's the difference between you lifting it and peeling my skin off?"

"Actually, Miss Alice is missing. I can't find her anywhere!" Arnold tried to get Merlin and Hobbs to help. "Mr. Claude is missing too."

"If they're gone, they're gone. What does that have to do with us?" Merlin was in a bad mood from waking up and couldn't stand the sight of anyone.

"Vanishing overnight—don't you find that strange?" Arnold spread his hands.

"Don't you think you should go look? Look around," Hobbs said, pounding his lower back like an old man.

"I've already looked. Both of them are gone," Arnold said, looking very anxious.

"Where could Alice go? Check the ladies' room, dig through the garbage pile, a slop bucket or something—you're sure to find her there." Merlin said it offhandedly, making things very awkward.

It seemed that in Merlin's worldview, Alice was some kind of cockroach.

"To be honest, I've even checked the women's bathhouse..." Arnold said quite seriously.

"..." Merlin stared at Arnold in surprise and said awkwardly, "You really are... on the殿堂 level of stalkers..."

"Moreover, Mr. Claude is missing too. Could he have eloped with Miss Alice?!" Arnold wore a pained expression. "Miss Alice's private life... why is it so chaotic? So flighty and promiscuous—she'll turn into a skank sooner or later..."

"Stop talking. Your imagination is too rich. If Alice finds out, she'll chop you up," Merlin said expressionlessly.

Hobbs patted his forehead and calmed down slightly, pondering for a moment.

"Now that I think about it, when I was peeing in the latter half of the night, I seemed to see Alice heading north... Could she have gone to the forest graveyard alone to claim the high bounty?"

"The graveyard is so dangerous—how could Miss Alice possibly go there?" Arnold was puzzled.

"That Saint-tier rookie Claude is missing too, right? Maybe they went together," Hobbs shrugged.

"I see. With Mr. Claude there, it's much safer. It seems I'm steadily advancing one step closer to Miss Alice's mating rights. Oh hehe..." Arnold turned from grief to joy, laughing happily.

Merlin covered his face in shock. He wasn't concerned about mating rights—he was thinking—

What the hell!

Is that how it is?!

That scheming Alice!

Not playing by the rules!

She wants to take the high commission reward on her own, behind my back?!

I've been keeping an eye on it this whole time—how could I just hand it over to Alice? !

Merlin stood up with a serious expression, quickly put on his clothes, slung his nodachi over his waist, and swept away his previous lethargy, becoming filled with battle spirit.

"Merlin, what are you—"

Hobbs's eyes widened. He was scared by Merlin's lightning-fast dressing technique.

"I'm going to that graveyard too," Merlin replied calmly.

"Stop messing around. You're a Black Iron. If you go, you'll only cause trouble. Let's just follow the main group and claim the basic bounty later," Hobbs advised. A mere Black Iron adventurer going to the graveyard—was he looking for death?

"No! I can't accept just the basic bounty. The high prize money is what I want." Merlin said it calmly and walked out of the tent without looking back. This time, the enemies were undead, which couldn't be used to extend his lifespan. If he still couldn't get enough bonus money, what was the point of him coming?

Arnold put on a serious face. "Oh ho~. It seems that for Miss Alice's mating rights, Merlin is getting serious too. Although he's my rival, I appreciate this spirit of his."

Hobbs put on a serious face. "Actually, I've known for a long time. Both Merlin's body and mind are anticipating mating with Alice. You can tell from his lecherous gaze alone: =

?+●'▼●) +?°

title: Chapter 33
content:
Chapter 33

Volume 3 · Chapter 33

The underground labyrinth, third floor.

Two death knights astride skeletal steeds, their eyes blazing with azure hellfire, burned fiercely.

They gripped bone lances, wrapped in flapping black robes, their jaws chattering constantly, emitting a "clack-clack-clack" brittle sound.

Claude moved as if through empty space, positioning himself in the middle, heading straight for the great gate guarded behind the death knights.

The heavy armor clattered noisily, instantly alerting the death knights and putting them on guard.

Their skeletal warhorses grew restless, constantly scraping the ground backward with their hooves, the hellfire on their bodies surging.

The two death knights abruptly yanked their reins, directly charging toward Claude, their bone lances thrusting at him without the slightest mercy.

In the deep darkness, hoofbeats splashed, azure hellfire roaring. Though mindless undead, their combat instincts were formidable.

Claude's breathing remained steady. He raised his massive obsidian sword and brought it down with a crash, striking the hard ground with a loud "boom."

The two high-tier death knight skeletons were struck by the冲击 of his Saint-tier斗气, shattering and scattering across the ground in a hail of white bones.

The battle ended in the blink of an eye. Claude sheathed his great sword behind his back and shoved the massive gates open; a rumbling echo reverberated through the underground labyrinth.

The secret of the former kingdom, sealed for over four hundred years, was about to be revealed. Meanwhile, Alice had been following closely behind Claude the entire time.

On the way, Alice had discovered two major doubts.

First, Claude had definitely been here before. The complexity of the underground labyrinth was beyond imagination; a normal person would absolutely get lost and fail to find the entrance to the next level.

Yet Claude seemed far too familiar with the place. After entering the labyrinth, his steps never hesitated. He made turn after turn, found the entrance to the next level, and quickly arrived at the very bottom.

This left Alice extremely confused. If Claude weren't leading the way, she felt certain she would be completely turned around and unable to find her bearings.

So Alice speculated that if Claude hadn't been here before, he must have a map of the labyrinth, possibly connected to the former kingdom's chancellor.

The second doubt was that someone else had apparently entered the labyrinth before. There were signs of battle on the first and second floors, and most of the undead had been eliminated. It was only on the third floor that the undead appeared in greater numbers, though along the way, Claude had cleared most of them out.

Alice suspected that some overconfident individual had infiltrated the place beforehand—either dying on the second floor or getting so hopelessly lost they couldn't find the entrance to the third.

However, Alice didn't dwell on it. Instead, she prioritized investigating Claude's identity.

If Claude were an extremely dangerous individual, she would need to inform the Guild Master, Tyler, immediately.

Seeing Claude enter the grand hall, Alice did not follow openly but slipped in quietly behind him.

Inside the hall, it was indeed another world. Cobwebs covered the outdated decorations. Eight massive pillars supported the ceiling. Rows of golden chandeliers were thick with dust, and a red carpet stretched across the floor to the central throne.

If not for its extreme age, one could still make out traces of its former glory.

Alice held her breath, hiding behind the last pillar, not daring to approach rashly. However, from this distance, she could just barely hear the conversation.

Claude stepped onto the crimson carpet and walked directly to the foot of the throne, looking up at the figure seated upon it.

"....."

A sinister breeze swept through. Torches lining the walls flared to life, their ghostly blue flames illuminating the surroundings, and the hidden space became clearly visible.

Seated on the throne was a white skeleton in a red robe. Its skull was covered in ancient kingdom script, dense and writhing like ants. Around its neck hung a dark red key, strikingly similar to the one Carona had obtained.

It seemed certain that this being, lurking on the third floor of the underground labyrinth, was the undead of the former kingdom's chancellor.

"Who are you? Why have you invaded my place of eternal rest? Before you die, I grant you the chance to state your reason."

The lich's voice rasped and hissed like an old bellows, yet possessed an ethereal quality.

Its eyes were utterly different from ordinary undead. Within its dark, hollow sockets, two golden flames flickered constantly, appearing deeply unsettling.

That was the soulfire of the lich. As long as it was not extinguished, it could not die. And the golden color was the unmistakable mark of the Saint-tier.

"It's been four hundred years, Lord Iain. I remember the last time we met, it was when the late king was hanged in the palace," Claude said calmly.

".....Who?" The lich named Iain grew agitated, the golden flames in its eyes flaring intensely.

Claude did not remove his helmet. Instead, he pulled the great sword from his back and stabbed it firmly into the ground. "Don't you recognize me, an Imperial Storm Warrior? Lord Iain, you truly are getting old, and your memory is failing badly."

"...Bernard?! But you died long ago! Why are you still alive?!" The lich stood up in shock.

"I was resurrected by the Prince using dark magic. It's not just me; all the other heroes have returned as well. We all continue our actions as undead," Claude said in a grim tone.

"The Prince is not dead?!" The lich was shocked again.

"When the former kingdom fell, the Prince luckily escaped. He used dark magic that feasts on elf blood to sustain his life, until this day when we finally have the chance to re-emerge!" Claude stated seriously.

The lich fell silent for a moment, recovering slightly from its shock. "What is your purpose?"

"To offer our souls for the revival of the former kingdom! To acknowledge the Prince as the rightful heir!" Claude declared with unwavering conviction. "We require greater power to overthrow the Great Britannia Dynasty. Therefore, we demand the key you guard!"

"I see... you still maintain contact with Hell, don't you? The reason our kingdom was replaced by Britannia was because the late king made a pact with Satan, becoming Hell's lapdog. Hell cannot be trusted! Why are you still so obstinately mistaken?!"

"Enough, Lord Iain. As an old acquaintance, I do not wish to fight you. You cannot defeat me. Hand over the key, and I swear I will not disturb your slumber again." Claude issued his final ultimatum.

"I refuse!" The lich summoned skeletal minions and assumed a combat stance.

"Then there is no choice!" Claude drew his obsidian great sword and charged the lich, his Saint-tier斗气 surging powerfully.

"Bernard, you always thought becoming an undead was a disgrace. As a warrior, dying in battle was the greatest glory. Isn't that what you once said?" The lich raised its bony fingers, aiming at the oncoming Claude.

"Now, the revival of the kingdom is my justice!" Claude swung his great sword wildly, unleashing a barrage of Saint-tier sword techniques, seemingly intending to end the fight quickly.

"Foolish!" The lich's fingers glowed with dark light, unleashing a Saint-tier spell, "Black Death Ray."

The two undead Saint-tier powerhouses clashed and became locked in combat, the entire grand hall shaking.

Meanwhile, on the first floor of the underground labyrinth.

Merlin had entered the tomb. After walking for a long time, he encountered only a few skeletal soldiers, which he shattered with a wave of his hand.

It wasn't that Merlin enjoyed "mowing the grass." The truth was, he had gotten hopelessly lost the moment he entered the labyrinth. He couldn't find his bearings at all, let

title: Chapter 34 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 34 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 3 · Chapter 34

In the second layer of the underground labyrinth, somewhere, the Rose Knight team was lost.

When Cecilia arrived at Denby County, she didn't stop to rest, but instead went straight ahead, clearing the way through the undead skeletons and entering the interior of her destination.

The initial actions were extremely smooth, and the monsters on the first layer of the labyrinth were easy to deal with. As a high-ranking lancer, Kael cleared the way quickly by stabbing through the skeletons.

Although they encountered some minor setbacks, they still found the entrance to the next layer relatively easily and snuck into the second layer of the labyrinth.

Without encountering much difficulty, and with things going so smoothly, Cecilia couldn't help but feel a bit elated, thinking that this task was a sure thing.

Cecilia believed that as long as she completed this task beautifully and brought honor to the Rose family, her father would look at her with new eyes, no longer underestimate her, and no longer marry her off to a remote noble as a political marriage sacrifice.

However, Cecilia was still too naive and underestimated the strength of the undead in the labyrinth.

There was no need to mention the powerful undead sorcerers on the third layer; even the monsters on the second layer were more than the Rose Knights could handle, and their strength was completely different from that of the weak skeleton soldiers on the first layer.

In the darkness, Cecilia's staff emitted a holy white light, illuminating the surroundings and preventing the monsters in the darkness from approaching easily.

The Rose Knights, clad in white armor, all had ugly expressions, and some were even extremely frightened, constantly sweating cold sweat.

As for Kael, who had high strength, he stood at the front, gripping his long spear and keeping watch all around, his continuous battles making him feel extremely tired; as the main combat force, his fighting spirit was consumed quickly, and he was already sweating profusely and panting heavily.

After witnessing the strength of the undead on the second layer, Cecilia was slapped back to reality, shocked and frightened, and immediately ordered a retreat, returning the way they came, but it was too late; not only were they lost and couldn't find the exit, but countless undead were also lurking in the darkness, closing in step by step and constantly eroding the group's confidence.

On the retreat path, many members of the Rose Knight team had already died, and only about a dozen or so knights guarded Cecilia, and the situation had become critical.

What are we going to do?

If this continues, we will all die here!

Damn those information brokers! Why didn't they tell us about the strength of the monsters here!

Cecilia's forehead was constantly dripping with cold sweat, and she silently cursed herself for being too impulsive and not inquiring about the information clearly before blindly leading the knights into the tomb.

"Everyone, hold on! As long as we can figure out the structure of the labyrinth, we will definitely be able to escape!"

Cecilia lied; in reality, the hope of survival was already slim, because her magical power was almost exhausted, and it was difficult to maintain using her staff to continuously emit 'holy light' to drive away the undead.

As long as Cecilia's magical power was exhausted, the only holy light in the darkness would be extinguished, and at that time, the undead would no longer fear them, and they would rush forward to tear this group of humans apart.

The holy light technique was an intermediate-level magic that Cecilia learned at the London Theological College; although it was usually of little use and only served to blind, it had a peculiar effect on dispelling and burning dark creatures, and at this moment, the holy light was the only lifeline for this group of people.

"Cecilia, to be honest, should we..."

"Shut up, Kael! I said we can escape!"

Cecilia interrupted Kael's words angrily, not yet finished.

At this moment, everyone's nerves were extremely tense; if the hope was lost, they would all collapse instantly.

Kael looked at the countless blue flames in the distance and fell silent, each flame representing an undead creature.

"Believe me!"

Cecilia encouraged everyone and prayed in her heart -

Merciful Goddess of Light, Maria, please bless us...

At this moment of slight distraction due to prayer, a pair of white-boned hands suddenly popped out from under the ground, grasping Cecilia's legs tightly and tripping her, and no one expected that an undead would sneak under the ground and launch a sudden attack!

"Aaah!"

Cecilia was shocked and fell to the ground, and her staff also dropped to the side.

The holy light that this group of people relied on for survival was instantly extinguished, and danger approached.

The terrifying skeleton made a strange cry, climbed out of the ground, pressed Cecilia under it, had an extraordinary strength, and opened its big mouth, wanting to bite Cecilia to death.

Cecilia looked at the flames jumping in the undead's eyes and was frightened, constantly struggling violently.

"Save me! Who can save me?"

"Cecilia!"

Kael rushed back from the front, using his high-level fighting spirit to throw the undead riding on Cecilia into pieces!

He quickly picked up Cecilia and asked with concern.

"Is Cecilia safe?"
