"Staff!" Cecilia stood up in a hurry, looking around for her staff.

A weapon was a very necessary thing for a magician and a warrior, which could be used to guide magical power or fighting spirit, greatly increasing the power of a skill, equivalent to an amplifier.

Generally speaking, it was divided into heavenly, ordinary, rare, and divine weapons; Alice's 'Light Song' belonged to a rare weapon, and Merlin's 'Banri Garan' was of ordinary quality, but its unique life-stealing ability was something that even divine weapons rarely had.

Among them, divine weapons were extremely rare and were known as the strongest amplifiers, with mysterious special functions such as changing the world's laws; it was said that a low-ranking person with a divine weapon could sweep away a Saint-tier strong opponent.

Although Cecilia's staff was not a divine weapon, it was also a rare and precious weapon, which could help her survive in this critical situation.

With Cecilia's current almost-exhausted magical power, without the staff's assistance, she was afraid that she couldn't even cast the holy light technique.

Cecilia looked around frantically for her staff and finally saw it near a stone; she rushed over and picked it up.

"Cecilia, be careful!"

Hearing Kael's shout, Cecilia looked up and saw a very strange undead creature - a three-headed, six-armed creature, each holding a large knife, with a lower body that was not human but was growing on a skeletal warhorse; its huge size was heart-stopping.

"Aaah..."

The three-headed, six-armed human-horse undead made a series of dull hums, looking very powerful, and was no doubt an elite monster on the second layer of the labyrinth!

Without hesitation, it raised a large knife and slashed down at Cecilia, who was numb and defenseless.

Before the knife could fall, Kael rushed to Cecilia's front, using his long spear to block this blow, but his fighting spirit was almost exhausted, and his strength was greatly reduced, so he was directly knocked to his knees.

"Cecilia, one...run..."

"Don't...be like this, Kael..."

Cecilia took a step back, almost in a state of shock.

The undead in the darkness rushed forward, roaring and pouncing on the surviving Rose Knights.

The scene was a crushing defeat; the knights counterattacked a few times and were then overwhelmed by a large number of undead, emitting heart-wrenching screams.

Cecilia watched blankly as her knights were torn apart by the undead, eaten alive, with blood splattering and intestines spilling out like snakes from their bellies.

The scene was extremely bloody and tragic, and the knights' cries were heartbreaking and deafening.

Cecilia was powerless, her legs weak, and she knelt on the ground in a daze, murmuring -

"Why
did it have to end like this?"

title: Chapter 35 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 35 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 3 · Chapter 35

I was born into a noble family.

From childhood, I lived a life of comfort and abundance.

I received the finest education, far beyond what commoners could ever hope for.

Yet beneath the family’s glittering surface lay an iron law of survival of the fittest.

My father was the world-renowned Rose Duke. Outwardly, he was kind and affable, but in truth, he was a man of extreme coldness.

To Father, everyone existed only to generate value. Those without worth had no right to exist.

From the moment I was born, I was locked in endless competition with my siblings, terrified of being discarded by Father.

Affection? What was that? In my world, siblings were enemies. I wished they would all die, leaving only me—then I wouldn’t have to live in constant fear of being cast aside.

This environment forced me to strive endlessly, to prove myself again and again.

So I became more and more like Father—cold-blooded, ruthless in pursuit of my goals.

But this mindset didn’t help me grow. Instead, it made my situation even more desperate.

Talent is such an envied thing. Some are born with it; a little effort yields twice the results.

As for me? I was the kind with abysmal talent. No matter how hard I tried, Father never truly acknowledged me.

Because my siblings were all prodigies, each with a clear, irreplaceable role in the family.

This left me in an increasingly awkward position, more and more redundant.

I once reflected on whether this life was right, but I found no answers. I could only endure in silence.

Though I lived in a family ruled by the law of the jungle, there was one ray of light—Kyle.

I met him when I was young. He was a squire in the Rose Knight Order, a clumsy little thing, too honest for his own good, almost foolishly so.

I remember that day clearly. The sky was bright. Kyle had failed to meet his training goals and was being whipped under the scorching sun.

I thought I was cold-blooded, but in that moment, my heart softened. I stopped his punishment—perhaps out of pity.

After that, he kept trying to see me. Then one day, he knelt on one knee, offered his sword with both hands, and asked to become my knight.

I can’t recall what I was thinking then, but I actually agreed to Kyle’s request.

Later, when I calmed down, I finally understood why I had accepted. Because I was weak. Kyle was weak too. Two pitiful souls, drawn together, clinging to each other for warmth to survive.

Was it because I was so foolish, so looked down upon by Father, that I hoped Kyle could give me a little warmth?

Ah… how cruel a reason. Yet it was my only way to escape reality.

Kyle and I grew up together. He followed me like a shadow, protecting me, training desperately to grow stronger.

Now, after all my efforts, I’ve only reached mid-rank, while Kyle has become a high-rank powerhouse capable of standing on his own.

I was confused. It seemed I was Kyle’s only motivation to keep striving, so I found an opportunity to ask him secretly.

“Kyle, doesn’t all this training exhaust you?”

“Not at all! Only this way can I protect Lady Cecily.”

This fool… what good was he? Because soon—

I was about to be married off to some distant land by Father.

Then how could he protect me?

The Rose Knight Order was nearly annihilated. Kyle stood alone against the three-headed, six-armed horse undead.

And the useless eldest daughter, Cecily, was frozen in shock, having never imagined that a battle with the undead could be so brutal.

“Lady Cecily, run! I’ll hold them off!”

“What nonsense are you spouting?! Come with me!” Cecily refused to abandon Kyle, tears glistening in her eyes.

“Hah… Cecily…” Kyle, barely holding back the elite undead, laughed bitterly. “I am your knight. If you’re in danger, it’s an insult to me. Please… just run. As long as you escape, there’s still hope to live.”

“You idiot! What kind of time is this to talk about knightly spirit?! Come with me!” Cecily couldn’t help but cry.

“Nnngh…”

The undead, having finished devouring the corpses of the Rose Knights, turned their gaze toward Cecily.

Kyle was horrified. He disengaged from the horse undead and rushed to stand before Cecily, swinging his spear to drive the undead back.

“I’m sorry, Lady Cecily. I am a knight. I absolutely cannot run!”

Cecily stood speechless, sensing that Kyle had already resolved to die.

The three-headed, six-armed horse undead charged forward, swinging six massive blades like a spinning wheel of death!

“Come at me, you despicable undead!” Kyle took a wide stance, readying himself, pushing his high-rank fighting spirit to its limit. His face was a mask of unyielding determination. “Our loyalty is without blemish!”

A fierce wind howled as sparks from clashing weapons sprayed through the darkness.

Kyle wildly thrust his spear, bravely clashing head-on with the elite undead!

But the three-headed, six-armed horse undead was no pushover. Its six arms easily suppressed Kyle’s techniques, and it let out a sinister laugh.

“AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!!!”

Kyle roared, unleashing every technique he knew, exhausting all his fighting spirit, yet it did nothing against the elite undead.

The horse undead, seemingly bored, knocked Kyle back and suddenly plunged all six blades into his body with a sickening *thunk*.

“Ah…”

Cecily’s eyes widened, her lips trembling, unable to speak. Tears she had held back for so long now streamed down like a broken dam.

Blood spurted from Kyle’s body as his life seemed to drain away. His battered spear clattered to the ground.

“Kyle!!!”

The horse undead picked up Kyle’s lifeless body, gave it a shake as if losing interest, then casually tossed him in front of Cecily.

Cecily stumbled forward and caught the motionless Kyle, checking his wounds. She pressed her lips tightly together, tears falling like a string of pearls. “Kyle, Kyle, wake up… please, get up and protect me… what is this? Is this how it ends? What about the oath you swore back then…”

The three-headed, six-armed horse undead stomped forward on its hooves, the stench of death washing over Cecily.

“Nnngh…”

The undead let out a sound like mocking laughter, then raised its massive cleaver, casting a shadow over Cecily.

So this was it?

Everything was over.

My worthless, cruel, insignificant life—finally at its end, like garbage…

Cecily’s clear eyes dimmed. She stared blankly at the descending blade, accepting her fate.

A earth-shaking boom suddenly echoed from above!

Cecily looked up in shock. Countless massive chunks of debris rained down. The first and second floors had been punched through by someone!

With a thunderous crash, the rubble buried the horse undead beneath it, sending up a cloud of dust.

Cecily shielded the unconscious Kyle, covering her own mouth and nose.

As the thick dust settled, Merlin’s figure appeared atop the ruins.

Merlin slowly stood, hand resting on the hilt of his katana. His hair rustled, and his ruby-like eyes gleamed brilliantly in the darkness.

Cecily’s mind went blank. She stared dumbfounded at Merlin’s back, and for a moment, she felt this black-iron-ranked adventurer was an unimaginably powerful man.

Merlin furrowed his brow, dusting off his shoulders, and muttered to himself.

“Haven’t used my fists seriously in a long time.”

“Suddenly going all out… my back’s a bit sore.”

“I really am getting old…”

title: Chapter 36
content:
Chapter 36

Volume 3 · Chapter 36

Cecilia stared wide‑eyed, dumbfounded at Merlin, who seemed like a divine soldier descending from the heavens, her lips moving but unable to utter a single word.

Why is this black‑iron adventurer from Reckserum here?!

Did he punch through that hard, thick layer of earth with a single blow?

Such destructive power could only be wielded by a Saint‑tier master!

If this guy truly is a Saint‑tier master, why is he the lowest‑rank black‑iron?

Could there be another reason, deliberately hiding the truth…

Cecilia’s mind, overwhelmed by shock, instantly spun out countless conjectures.

From now on Cecilia dared not look at Merlin with contempt; she felt he was the true powerhouse, and he didn’t even seem angry at her disdain, caring not for any hollow reputation—unlike herself, who clings to fame and power, blinded by ambition.

Cecilia’s face flushed with embarrassment; she realized she was a frog at the bottom of a well, judging by appearances, having mistaken Merlin for a dead‑weight while she herself was the real dead‑weight.

In fact, Cecilia had completely misread Merlin, attributing him far too noble a character.

Merlin also wanted to make a name for himself, but without magic or ki, everywhere he went he was treated like a villager with a combat rating of five.

Countless undead in the surrounding darkness flickered with pale blue flames, staring at Merlin atop the ruins, and for a moment none dared to move.

Merlin twisted his neck as if warming up, and from the corner of his eye finally saw Cecilia cradling Kyle on the ground; seeing her tear‑streaked face and shocked gaze, he felt a little embarrassed.

That look reminded Merlin of a stray dog on the roadside, begging for a scrap of food.

“Oh? Isn’t this the high‑and‑mighty lady of the Rose family? What happened to you?” Merlin looked down at Cecilia with a slightly mocking tone, after all she had previously treated him with contempt.

“…We just entered not long ago, and when we went deeper into the second level we were ambushed by powerful undead…” Cecilia, still shaking from shock, explained with a sorrowful tone.

Merlin leapt down from the ruins, glanced at Kyle in Cecilia’s arms, and said calmly, “I see. It looks like you all overreached and brought trouble upon yourselves. Honestly, it’s not worth anyone’s sympathy.”

Cecilia’s face turned bright red, feeling deeply humiliated, unsure how to communicate with Merlin.

“Why did you come here? Even if you’re a priest, you can’t handle this many undead, can you?” Merlin looked behind him, where wave after wave of undead stared at him.

“…I want to replace my father and resolve the crisis in Denby County, to prove my ability.” Cecilia bit her lip as she replied.

“Ha…

Merlin smiled lightly, finding Cecilia rather amusing.

“…What are you laughing at?” Cecilia felt her dignity teetering.

“Of course I’m laughing at you. Your abilities are yours alone; when do you still need others to prove them? It’s because of such petty reasons that you hand your subordinates over to hell yourself,” Merlin said, gripping his greatsword and looking down at Cecilia. “If you were a demon‑race leader, you’d be incompetent and your subordinates would rebel without any enemy’s push.”

Cecilia furrowed her brows, clenching her lips in silence, and thought to herself, ‘Yes, everyone’s death is my fault, even Kyle’s. All my efforts… what were they for?’

Merlin shook his head, turned, and said coolly, “I’m not interested in chatting with a lady like you. I have other matters to attend to. Farewell.”

Seeing Merlin about to leave, Cecilia startled, looked down at Kyle, and felt a swirl of emotions; if she hadn’t sought help from this black‑iron adventurer, both she and Kyle would have died here, while the distant undead still watched hungrily.

So Cecilia set aside her pride, temporarily placed Kyle on the ground, lifted her skirt’s hem, and staggered toward Merlin.

“…Sir! Please don’t go! I beg you, don’t leave!”

“Hm? What do you want? I warned you not to cling to me; I have serious business to attend to.” Merlin put on a stern face, his mind already on the head of that scheming Alice.

“I… I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to waste your time, I just have a request.” Cecilia spoke with great respect, lowering herself, her face full of panic.

“What…?” Merlin feigned annoyance, though inside he was a thousand times unwilling.

“Please, sir, save us and get us out of here.” Cecilia’s tone was earnest, her hands clasped together as if praying.

Merlin sighed, not really wanting to get involved, and was about to say something when a roar suddenly erupted behind him—

“Aaaaargh…!”

The ruins shuddered as they were torn open; the three‑headed, six‑armed centaur undead had not died, crawling out from the rubble wielding six long blades, each gleaming menacingly.

A massive swarm of undead, seeing that the centaur was still alive, surged forward from the darkness with renewed vigor.

Armored skeletal soldiers, weapons in hand, slowly approached Merlin and Cecilia, the blue ghostly flames in their eyes flaring intensely.

“Aaaahhh!” Cecilia screamed, her face turning pale as she stumbled backward, unable to believe that the centaur undead, despite being pelted with stones, was still unharmed.

“Sigh, do I always carry a sarcastic aura? Always some clueless fool daring to challenge me…”

Merlin frowned, clearly annoyed by the undead; no matter how many he killed, it didn’t matter, and he couldn’t revive them.

The three‑headed, six‑armed centaur undead roared, swinging its six great axes, instantly turning into a whirlwind of dismembered bodies that charged at Merlin.

Like a battle cry, the other undead surged forward, completely unaware of the terrifying authority of the arrogant ruler.

“You trash that have died once dare to fight me? Pathetic.” Merlin instantly drew a short segment of his greatsword; a murderous blade aura exploded outward, sweeping the area.

In a single breath, the undead who dared challenge the Demon Lord’s authority were all torn apart, their dying breaths reduced to a brief hiss.

Elite centaur undead and other skeletal foes were sliced apart, turning into countless white bones that rained down, forming a bone shower.

The battle that began in an instant ended just as quickly; Merlin stood proudly on the battlefield, sheathing the short blade segment with a clearly impatient expression.

Cecilia’s face turned as white as paper, she stared in stunned silence at Merlin’s silhouette amid the bone rain, her heart pounding.

What the hell?!

She could feel no ki nor magic!

What kind of killing aura was that—what power?

This wasn’t an even fight; it was a crushing display of transcendent strength!

Who on earth is he? I can’t even guess his power level!

A casual, off‑hand attack that packs that much force—if he were serious, would he even still be human?

title: Chapter 37 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 37 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 3 · Chapter 37

-Instantaneous attack wiped out a large number of undead.

This casual strike made the other undead lurking in the darkness dare not make rash moves.

Merlin shook his hair, letting some bone fragments fall to the ground.

Then Merlin looked at Cecilia with a serious expression and pulled the conversation back on track.

"Miss, why should I save you?"

Merlin wasn't some hot-blooded idiot who liked meddling in other people's business. They were strangers, so why should he save her? Besides, his first impression of Cecilia wasn't exactly great.

"Cecilia hesitated for a moment, fully aware that nothing comes for free. "I can give you a reward?"

"Oh?"

Merlin became somewhat interested. A reward was acceptable, of course.

He was short on money now, for a better quality of life.

If saving this young lady could earn him over 5,000 gold coins, then reluctantly saving her wouldn't be so bad.

That way he wouldn't have to compete with Alice for the commission bonus either. More money, why not take it?

Originally, the boss below was just an undead, useless for alleviating his curse. If not for the money, he wouldn't have bothered to move.

It seemed Merlin had underestimated Cecilia's wealth too much. What was 5,000 gold coins? He was going to pay 400,000 gold coins when he wanted to hire Claude earlier.

Merlin cleared his throat, deliberately playing hard to get, wanting to extort a bit more.

"A reward is fine, of course, just... you know what I mean, right?"

Cecilia's face turned pale, then flushed red. She thought, such a powerful guy, yet content to be a Black Iron adventurer — clearly someone who didn't care about reputation or money. So the only thing she could offer in return would probably be... that, right?

Cecilia's intelligence left much to be desired. This was a problem that could be solved with money, but she overthought it and twisted things into something entirely different. Seeing Merlin's lecherous expression, she assumed he was hinting at physical payment. It made sense — such a powerful guy who cared nothing for fame or wealth would surely have a keen interest in possessing women's bodies.

"I... I understand. The reward will... definitely satisfy you."

Cecilia's cheeks flushed with a faint blush, and she stammered her response.

She glanced at Kael, lying barely breathing on the ground, and bit her lip, deciding to go all in.

Rather than both of them dying here, it would be better to make a sacrifice and then survive together.

Cecilia slightly raised her head to look at Merlin, unconsciously a trace of unwilling tears gathering in the corners of her eyes. Her lips moved as she spoke.

"It's okay... please be gentle... don't make too much noise... I'm still a virgin..."

"???" Merlin was filled with question marks, utterly baffled by Cecilia. He thought: I want money, what does being a virgin have to do with it?!

Cecilia blushed, biting her pale lips, and began undressing. She loosened her robe, letting it fall freely to the ground, then slowly parted the clothes on her chest, revealing her sexy and charming neck, showing off delicate collarbones that outlined a captivating allure.

Her fair skin seemed dusted with pearl powder, her shoulders showing a faint pink hue. Cecilia didn't stop, tugging at her clothes, her full bosom about to spill out.

Merlin's face darkened, his expression growing more and more astonished. Seeing this situation, he understood that Cecilia wanted to offer her body as payment.

What the hell!

Was he too much like a pervert?

Why did girls start stripping in front of him without any provocation?

Everyone thought he was some hormone-addled guy about to assault them! ?

Good heavens, this was too much. He'd always said women were extraordinarily troublesome creatures...

Merlin couldn't bear to watch anymore. He directly swatted Cecilia's hand away and closed the clothes on her chest.

He had no interest in Cecilia's bare flesh and bones, let alone wanting to look — it was quite boring, honestly.

There were plenty of prettier girls than Cecilia — he could line up a reinforced company at the First Demon Lord Palace alone.

As someone over 200 years old, Merlin had seen countless members of the opposite sex and was completely immune to women.

"What are you doing? I have no interest in this kind of reward," Merlin said.

"....But I have nothing better to offer as payment besides my body...." Cecilia's eyes glistened with tears, her tone extremely aggrieved.

"Sigh, I really can't deal with you...." Merlin sighed, finding Cecilia so troublesome — she was even more of a pain than Alice with her flat chest.

He thought for a moment, then suddenly grabbed Cecilia by her clothes and lifted her straight up.

"Ah! ...What are you doing?" Cecilia cried out.

"Hehe!" Merlin grinned and directly threw Cecilia high into the air. "There, go!"

"Aaaaaah!" Cecilia screamed, feeling as though gravity had abandoned her.

Merlin picked up Kael's spear from the ground, held it in his hand, and aimed at Cecilia in mid-air before shooting it directly!

Cecilia's face went pale with shock. What was he doing?! Was he trying to kill her?!

But that wasn't the case at all. The spear pierced through Cecilia's dress and pinned her, dress and all, onto the high cliff wall.

"Huh!?" Cecilia hung on the cliff wall, her expression completely blank.

Merlin casually picked up Kael from the ground and threw him up with ease.

Just like Cecilia, he ended up impaled on the spear stuck in the cliff wall.

Merlin clapped his hands and looked at Cecilia, saying calmly, "This should work, right? These undead basically can't climb up, so it can temporarily protect your safety."

"Sir,....I'm not asking for this. I want you to take us out of here." Cecilia felt unsafe, and those undead in the distance were already starving and restless.

"Sorry, I've already been merciful enough. I have things to attend to now." Merlin turned and walked away. Then he suddenly remembered something. "Oh right, your knight is still breathing. As a priestess, if you put in some effort, he might survive."

Cecilia was stunned, then overjoyed. She looked at Kael in her arms and silently hugged him tighter. She could abandon anyone, but she couldn't lose Kael, who had grown up with her.

Merlin shook his head and headed into the darkness, thinking: Only the last layer remains, right? Hope Alice gets beaten to the point where she can't fight back, otherwise I won't have a chance to steal the kill.

"Sir! Will you come back to rescue us and get us out of here? Please, there are too many undead here, it's a bit unsafe..."

Cecilia's voice came again. Merlin pressed his forehead, unhappy. This woman was so troublesome. He'd just give her a perfunctory response.

"Just rest assured!"

"I'll definitely come back for you!"

"I'll absolutely keep my promise!"

"I'm definitely not the type to blow you off, gu gu gu..."

title: Chapter 38 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 38 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 3 · Chapter 38

Floor 3 of the underground labyrinth.

Alice had been eavesdropping the entire time, moving with extreme caution.

Though the conversation between Claude and the necromancer had been fragmented,

Alice had still managed to piece together some information—she hadn’t come away empty-handed.

Claude was none other than Bernard, the late Hero King from four hundred years ago!

Some kind of necromantic magic had brought him back to life?!

So that meant Claude wasn’t human at all—he was an undead!

As a remnant of the former kingdom, Claude was an enemy of the Great Britannian Empire.

Judging from the conversation between Claude and the necromancer—

the remnants of the old kingdom were still active in the shadows, aiming to restore the dynasty.

And it seemed they were currently lacking power, so they were searching for some kind of key?

Alice could only deduce this much for now; everything else was still a mystery.

No wonder Claude spoke like he was living in the last century—turns out he was a four-hundred-year-old corpse.

And he kept acting like some bitter, disillusioned youth, mocking Great Britannia, when he himself had been a hero of the previous dynasty.

No wonder he said the late heroes of the former kingdom were the true powerhouses—wasn’t that just him bragging about himself?

Alice had already concluded that Claude was an extremely dangerous man. She absolutely must not get involved with him; she needed to return and report this to the Guild Master.

At this moment, the two Saint-tier undead had already been fighting for a while, locked in a fierce stalemate. Each was a dominant force in their own right, their power overwhelming!

The necromancer’s [Black Death Ray] was terrifyingly powerful. Wherever the beam passed, like a black hole’s ray, everything rotted away, turning into countless dust particles.

Claude’s swordsmanship was no joke either. His ancient, traditional sword techniques were executed with masterful precision. Several times, he had nearly severed the necromancer’s head—if not for the [Black Death Ray]’s magic being so troublesome. The moment it made contact, it would spread like a plague, causing the entire body to rot away.

If it weren’t for Claude’s exquisite martial arts and his abundant Saint-tier battle aura, he would have already been defeated and turned to dust.

The [Black Death Ray] was a magic of immense power, reducing everything in its path to dust. Moreover, it was extremely rare—this kind of magic had been lost in modern Great Britannia. Only a four-hundred-year-old monster like the necromancer would still know how to use it.

If there were other Saint-tier mages present, they would surely be amazed by the might of the [Black Death Ray].

Both Saint-tier combatants were incredibly powerful. Even Alice, watching from the sidelines, felt like she was witnessing gods clashing. Her heart trembled—when would she ever reach Saint-tier? It felt so distant.

“Bernard! What’s wrong? Have you gotten old? Your movements have slowed. How disappointing!”

The necromancer cackled darkly, sweeping his hand to unleash a Black Death Ray toward Claude.

“Zorn, let’s see how long you can keep up that arrogance.”

Claude, clad in pitch-black heavy armor, flipped away to dodge the attack before charging up a platform.

Golden battle aura, symbolizing holiness, surged around him. In a flash, he appeared right in front of the necromancer.

“Storm Rending Slash!”

Claude unleashed his signature Saint-tier sword technique. His massive black greatsword danced wildly, each swing generating violent gusts of wind. Countless afterimages of the blade flickered as it hacked down mercilessly!

This Saint-tier sword technique was truly formidable. The sheer pressure it exerted made the ground tremble slightly. If it landed, it would surely pulverize bones into dust!

“Hmph, foolish!”

The necromancer sneered, his golden flame-like eyes burning fiercely.

Suddenly, a massive black summoning magic circle appeared beneath his feet, taking up nearly half the hall.

“Behold my ultimate technique—King of Skeletons!”

The enormous black magic circle seemed to connect to another space. This was a Saint-tier summoning ultimate technique, dazzling to behold. Unlike other ultimate techniques that ended with a single powerful attack, this one allowed for sustained combat.

However, summoning magic consumed an enormous amount of mana, requiring constant upkeep to maintain the summoned creature. But a four-hundred-year-old necromancer like this one clearly had an abundant reserve. Any ordinary mage would have had their mana drained dry and turned into a mummy by now.

The duel between the two Saint-tier experts unfolded in the blink of an eye—

A ghastly white skeletal giant hand emerged from the black magic circle, clenching into a fist that struck Claude with tremendous force, sending him flying like a cannonball!

The skeletal fist was taller than Claude himself, its power so overwhelming it was shocking. Mid-air, Claude plunged his greatsword into the ground to halt his momentum, his breathing growing heavy as if injured.

A giant skeleton wearing a golden crown and draped in a red robe crawled out from the magic circle. Due to the space constraints, only the upper half of the Skeletal King emerged, with the rest still inside the circle. Even so, its presence filled the entire hall.

The Skeletal King’s eye sockets glowed with a red light. It positioned itself in front of the necromancer, forming an absolute defense that increased the pressure on Claude.

If Claude wanted to harm the necromancer, he would have to get past the Skeletal King first.

Alice’s face paled in shock as she stared at the Skeletal King. What in the world was that thing?! Could a necromancer really summon such a monstrous creature?!

“Hahaha…” The necromancer laughed uninhibitedly, the skeletal hand still raised. “Bernard! You really underestimate me! Your power is stuck in the past, four hundred years ago. But I, as a necromancer, have only grown stronger over these four hundred years. You have no chance, Bernard!”

“One strike.” Claude slowly stood up, pulling his greatsword from the ground.

“One strike?” The necromancer’s eyes flickered.

Claude assumed his stance, pointing his greatsword at the necromancer. Seriously, he said, “Next time, you won’t be so lucky, Zorn. I will use my ultimate technique to shatter your skull and extinguish your soul flame in a single blow!”

“Oh?” The necromancer spread his hands, fearless. “If I recall correctly, your ultimate technique is a special state. For its duration, you become an untiring berserker, with all your abilities greatly enhanced, and gain extraordinary perception—claimed to be able to dodge all attacks. Isn’t that the skill you used to cut down the Saha Empire’s ten thousand elite iron cavalry during the Kingdom’s Defense War, making a name for yourself in a single battle?”

“That’s right. Accept your fate, Zorn. You won’t be able to land a single hit on me.” Claude spoke with absolute seriousness. Privately, he began stirring his Saint-tier battle aura, which clung to his body like golden flames.

“Spare me the big talk. Let’s see if you can get past my Skeletal King first!” the necromancer rasped, his teeth clacking madly.

“O—” Claude took a moment to gather himself, then suddenly opened his eyes wide. The golden battle aura around him turned violent, a crimson hue surging beneath it. “Berserk Mode, OOOOOOOOOOH!” Alice nervously swallowed, feeling the pressure was no longer human—it was like a rampaging Saint-tier magical beast! Claude abruptly charged forward, seeking a swift resolution. The moment he stomped his heel, the ground cracked with shocking force, a testament to his immense strength!

Just as everyone’s nerves were stretched taut, a deafening boom echoed from above. The rock ceiling had been pierced through, and debris began to rain down.

Claude halted his assault and looked up.

“Hm? Who’s there?” The necromancer also looked up. Alice furrowed her delicate brows, wondering what was going on.

Merlin descended steadily from the black hole in the ceiling, landing gracefully on the ground. He straightened his posture, resting a hand on the katana at his waist, and flicked his golden bangs aside.

“Hmph. Ten thunderous roars echo through the heavens—time for this old man to make a grand entrance!”

title: Chapter 39
content:
Chapter 39

Volume 3 · Chapter 39

Merlin suddenly appeared here, interrupting the deadly duel between the two Saint-tier warriors.

The scene immediately froze, becoming eerily silent.

Just as the two were about to decide the winner, no one expected Merlin to appear in this manner.

The three-layer underground labyrinth, with Merlin piercing through two layers of rock walls and descending to the third layer's BOSS location! Even Saint-tier warriors wouldn't do something so reckless.

"Well, it seems I'm not too late after all..."

Merlin smiled and looked down at the Necromancer, then glanced at the other side where Claude was. He noticed Alice wasn't there.

"Hey! You, the one wielding the great sword, where's Alice? I don't see her."

Merlin's tone wasn't exactly friendly, given his bad impression of the bragging Claude, who was a fellow adventurer. If it weren't for that, he might have even wanted to slash this guy.

Claude didn't listen to Merlin and was in a state of stunned shock, wondering how this trash villager got here. Didn't the undead from the first and second layers stop this piece of garbage with no magic or qi?

Alice, hiding behind a pillar, was equally shocked, her small mouth unable to close for a moment. She thought, "Oh my god! How did this guy get here! ? Shouldn't he have been mixing with Hobbs for low wages? ? What's he doing here, directly entering the third layer! ? Is he worried about my safety and came after me! ? No, no, no! That's impossible, Merlin this jerk wouldn't care about me!"

Alice's forehead dripped with cold sweat, feeling that Merlin standing between the two Saint-tier warriors made the situation very delicate, possibly leading to a big fight.

She decided to stay hidden for now, observing the situation, and seeing how it unfolded. This level of battle was beyond her ability to interfere.

Not to mention Merlin this big pervert, just the two 400-year-old undead Saint-tier warriors alone were terrifying enough, giving Alice the impression that the Necromancer and Claude's strength was even greater than the two Redbeard pirate brothers from half a year ago!

Although Alice knew Merlin had no magic or qi, her strength was still bottomless, but facing the Necromancer and Claude together would still put her under pressure, right? At least there was some suspense.

Alice's mood became a bit anxious, wondering if Merlin was in a disadvantageous position, whether she should go and help.

Claude slowly raised his head, looking at the large hole in the ceiling of the hall, and fell into thought. Although he thought Merlin was reckless, he also realized that this black-iron adventurer had some skill.

"Hey~, I'm asking you, can you tell me where Alice, the scheming bitch, went?" Merlin, seeing that Claude wasn't responding, thought he was pretending to be cool.

Alice frowned her beautiful eyebrows, gritted her teeth, and thought, "You jerk! Who is the scheming bitch? That's Lucy's fault!"

Claude silently tightened his grip on the giant sword, staring at the carefree Merlin, and for a moment, he felt like killing. To protect the secret of the kingdom's revival, he had to eliminate all witnesses.

Just as Claude was about to act, someone else became angry first--

"Where did this little rat come from! ? Dare to intrude on my resting place, turn to dust!"

The Necromancer, recovering from shock, couldn't sense Merlin's magic or qi, so he naturally considered him a worthless person.

It flickered its golden eyes and directly waved its finger, shooting a corrosive "Black Death Ray" to kill the little fly.

But an unusual sight occurred. The straight Black Death Ray, just as it was about to hit Merlin, suddenly dissipated.

Only a few beams of light veered away from Merlin, which was very confusing....

The Necromancer's golden flame eyes trembled, shocked to retreat a step. It had never seen such an incredible thing, feeling as if its magic couldn't even approach Merlin—what was going on here! ?

"......"

Claude made a strange noise, though his face was hidden under the helmet, his reaction showed he was also shocked.

He couldn't figure out the situation anymore, feeling that Merlin should not be an ordinary person, hiding some strength. Otherwise, casually dissipating the Black Death Ray was incredibly astonishing.

Alice behind the pillar was relatively calm, having seen this before, thinking Merlin's magic immunity was very useful. The Holy Church's Crusade also suffered a big loss in this regard. For all mages, it was truly a nightmare.

"Ah?" Merlin calmly turned around, looking at the Necromancer with disdain. "You're sick, right? You attacked me first without provocation!"

"You are who? !" The Necromancer realized something was off, putting aside its disdainful attitude. "How can you dissipate my magic, what trickery are you using! ?"

"Do I have to tell you?" Merlin didn't want to waste time on the Necromancer, as it held no value for him. "Prepare to die, your life is only worth 5000 gold."

"What are you saying! ?Daring to insult me? You're asking for death! ! !"

The Necromancer raised its staff, emitting black light, as if a black hole could swallow everything.

The massive Bone King, as if receiving a command, roared, raised its arms, and clenched its fists into a hammer, ready to strike Merlin to death.

Alice's heart skipped a beat, wondering if it would be okay?

Claude below seemed to have relaxed, shaking his head and thinking, "It's over, I can't even handle the Bone King's full-force strike, and what about a guy with no magic or qi? Even if he has some obscure skills, in the face of real strength, he will be completely crushed."

"Tremble before the power of the Bone King! Haha...." The Necromancer swung its staff, aiming at Merlin, ordering the attack.

The Bone King's hammer crashed down, and before the fist even reached, a sense of tearing everything apart filled the air, making the ground shake slightly.

The attack came, and Merlin smirked, raised his hand, and bravely took the terrifying white bone hammer!

A violent wind rushed upward, and the stones flew like knives into the sky!

Merlin's feet made a "crack crack" sound, showing terrifying cracks, but he himself was unharmed.

As they say, melee is invincible, not just bragging. Merlin wasn't just magic immune; his physical defense was also at an unbearable level!

After the aftershock, the scene returned to peace--

"This is fine, really.... Alice's face turned a bit pale.

"This guy is still human, right.

Claude couldn't stay calm anymore, finding Merlin's image of taking the Bone King's hammer with one hand too shocking! If it were himself, he would have been crushed into dust by the hammer!

"No... impossible!" The Necromancer's flame eyes dimmed, panicked, and kept retreating, with its bones even dropping to the ground.

"One who can withstand the Bone King's full-force strike...."

"Such strength is impossible to exist!"

"One with such power must not be a black-iron adventurer! ?"

title: Chapter 40 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 40 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 3 · Chapter 40

“Your summon is stronger than its master; you really are a useless fool."

Merlin shatters the Bone King's fist, bows slightly, places his hand on the katana at his waist, and his ruby-like eyes become exceptionally sharp.

He does not hesitate at all; he draws his blade from its sheath and unleashes a thousand‑times‑forged sword draw slash!

“Lowly undead, fall swiftly into hell!"

With a single draw, a world‑shattering, murderous sword aura slashes out, and a mountain‑crushing pressure instantly engulfs the necromancer!

The power of this sword draw slashes through everything, carving a narrow trench in the ground, and the unstoppable strike annihilates the necromancer on the spot!

The necromancer does not even utter a scream; the golden flame in his eyes suddenly extinguishes, his skull splits in two and falls to the ground, and his entire skeletal frame scatters across the floor.

As for the massive Bone King, his condition is similar to his master's, as if life has been drained. He slowly sinks into the black magical circle.

Alice’s shocked expression freezes on her face; she had expected to see Merlin get humbled and felt a small anticipation, but the necromancer gave Merlin no pressure at all and was slain with a single blow. Huh? Why am I saying “again”?!

Claude stands rooted, completely stunned by Merlin’s power, thinking, “He took out Zorn and the Bone King in one strike? Incredible! Too powerful! No one among the Four Heroes could match that…”

It’s a pity such overwhelming strength can’t be used for the Emperor, yet he’s content to be a little black‑iron adventurer! Truly incomprehensible.

Looks like I misjudged him before; this guy is hiding his true power, he’s not a villager at all but a pinnacle swordmaster! He’s become so strong that you can’t even sense magic or ki. F牡J玩——

Even the most ordinary sword draw slash can have this kind of power; imagine how strong it would be in a serious fight?

But even so, I’m confident I won’t be outmatched in storm mode!

Claude’s inner monologue is quite rich; Merlin truly has no magic or ki and only knows the single sword draw slash. If he learned the truth, what expression would this dark warrior wear?

Now Claude no longer wants to silence Merlin, because he feels the opponent’s strength is on par with his own and lacks the confidence for a full‑blown fight.

So Claude plans to pretend to be a fellow adventurer, let this pass, and treat this as a crusade against the undead.

But there’s still one problem: the key to the Hell Legion is still on the necromancer Zorn’s body, and I need to find a way to take it quietly.

But Claude overthinks; Merlin, being a transplanter, is accustomed to looting corpses after a fight to see if there’s anything valuable.

Merlin sheathes his katana, having already earned 5,000 gold from slaying BOSSA, and casually checks if there’s anything else worthwhile.

He walks over eagerly, but reality gives Merlin a cold splash: the necromancer only has a tattered piece of clothing, the rest is just a skeletal frame, with only a red key around his neck standing out.

Merlin unceremoniously pulls it off, looks at it and finds it quite ordinary, nothing special about it.

Claude is startled to see the key fall into Merlin’s hands, not expecting him to notice such an ordinary key.

That key concerns the kingdom’s revival; if it falls into someone else’s hands, it would be disastrous!

If Merlin were a weakling, I could just cut him down and take the key back.

Situation

But the crucial point is that I just witnessed Merlin’s strength; this hard bone may not be something I can chew down.

Claude hesitates for a moment, decides to pose as a fellow adventurer and retrieve the Hell Legion’s key.

“Lord Merlin, please give me that key.”

“Hm?” Merlin turns around, feeling a bit unaccustomed to Claude’s sudden politeness, “Why?”

“This key is very important to me; please hand it over, thank you.” Claude tries to lower his stance.

Merlin hesitates; originally he thought the key was nothing and intended to discard it.

But now Claude has come to demand it, and it seems important.

Merlin isn’t a fool; Claude is a Saint-tier, and anything he wants can’t be worthless.

Perhaps this key leads to some earth‑shattering treasure; even a Saint-tier would be tempted, and the amount must be considerable.

Merlin smiles, flicks his finger, and makes the key spin in his hand.

“The key is my loot; why should I give it to you?”

Claude feels a surge of irritation; seeing Merlin’s carefree attitude makes him want to kill him, even entertaining murderous thoughts.

But the anger is reluctantly suppressed; if it can be resolved through negotiation, he tries not to resort to violence.

“This thing is very important to me; if Lord Merlin thinks it’s useless, why not give it to me?”

“Who says it’s useless? This key has treasure, you know? Even if I can’t find it, I’ll keep it~” Merlin says with a half‑smile, enjoying watching the other party get anxious while he remains unbothered.

“If Lord Merlin would hand over the key, I will remember your kindness and, one day, I will repay you.” Claude maintains his demeanor, hoping to obtain the key peacefully.

“Heh,” Merlin smirks, tilting his mouth, and says with an arrogant sneer, “I’m not interested in your repayment; don’t overestimate yourself, I have no regard for you.”

Merlin’s tone is extremely rude; he already dislikes Claude, so there’s no need to be polite.

Claude’s pride is wounded; he silently grips his greatsword, feeling an urge to go all‑out against Merlin.

The Hell Legion’s key is of utmost importance; no matter what, it must be obtained, even if it costs my life!

Claude plans to make one final appeal; if that fails, he’ll settle it by force.

“I’m willing to pay a hefty sum for the key; I wonder if Lord Merlin would agree?”

“How much?” Merlin shows a slight softening.

“200,000 gold.” Claude says calmly; that’s all he has, still Arnold’s money.

Holy crap!

200,000 for this lousy key isn’t cheap, huh?

If I put it all on a horse at the racetrack and win, I’d become a millionaire instantly!

Emmmmm, should I?

Merlin wavers, no longer twirling the key, but weighing the pros and cons.

Alone in the shadows, Alice can’t stay still and mutters, cursing Merlin for being too greedy.

Claude is a remnant of the kingdom from 400 years ago, not a good person; he came here for this key, and the matter is certainly not that simple, involving many interests—how could he easily hand over the key?

Moreover, the revival of the former kingdom will inevitably spark war, leaving the people of Great Britain destitute; Alice does not want to see peace trampled.

Alice steps forward resolutely and shouts at Merlin.

“Don’t hand over the key!”

“Hm!?” Claude is quite surprised, not expecting Alice to be here.

“Wow, Alice, you scheming bitch, as expected, you came here secretly to claim the commission bonus for yourself, leaving us behind—how unprincipled!” Merlin scowls and launches a tirade.

“Who’s here for the money? Don’t accuse me!” Alice says angrily.

“Then why are you here?” Merlin asks, puzzled.

“Shouldn’t I be the one asking you that? How did you follow me here!?” Alice retorts.

“Of course I’m after the 5,000 gold bounty; otherwise who would come over stuffed and satisfied?!” Merlin replies bluntly.

“Lying! So you really came for that, right?” Alice’s face flushes with two pink blushes.

“??? ” Merlin asks, indicating he didn’t understand.

Alice’s clarified gaze suddenly flickers with panic, her heartbeat quickening a few beats, and she says, blushing,

“Do you just want to obtain my mating rights?”

title: Chapter 41 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 41 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 3 · Chapter 41

Merlin kept a deadpan expression, a waterfall of sweat and vein marks plastering his forehead—

What the fuck is a mating right?!

How narcissistic does this ironing-board girl have to be?!

She even followed him here just to compete for her mating right?!

Fuck my ass! This ironing board has no shame!

If he wasn't on the wrong medication or had his head kicked by a donkey,

he wouldn't give a single damn about who gets this ironing board's mating right! ?

This girl,居然 with a completely serious face, said something so shameless.

"Won't you actually have guessed it right?" Alice said with a resistant expression, yet the blush on her face didn't seem to know what it was ashamed of.

"Guessed my big head indeed! Wipe that blush off your face right now! This mysterious blushing is making things very awkward, you know!?" Merlin retorted in exasperation.

"I'm blushing because I'm angry, you know!?" Alice quickly explained, afraid Merlin would misunderstand her. "I'm not blushing because I'm shy! It's all because you pervert have been lusting after me! Disgusting!"

"Disgusting!?" Merlin furrowed his brows. Someone had never rated himself that way before.

"That's right, you disgusting guy. Let me put this straight upfront: I will never let your filthy delusions come true. Your bet with Arnold was all a joke! I will never acknowledge your duel!" Alice's tone was resolute, showing a firm resistant attitude.

"Please, take a look at yourself. Stop being so narcissistic, okay? Pardon my bluntness. When you walked past me naked, even my little brother couldn't bear to look up." Merlin frowned tightly, pointing at Alice and saying seriously, "In my eyes, your mating right isn't worth 5000 gold coins."

"Ptooey!"

Alice spit out a mouthful of old blood, clutching her chest in pain as she knelt on the ground, suffering 9999 points of massive mental damage!

What!? My mating right isn't worth five thousand gold coins? Are you kidding me!? This is already insulting my dignity! !

Alice wobbled back to her feet, directly drew her slender sword, and said with a dark face,

" bastard, stop yapping and let's fight to the death!"

Claude had been watching from the side for a long time, his head growing a circle larger from the two of them arguing.

Although Alice suddenly appeared to stop him from getting the key, he didn't know how many secrets she actually knew. He still thought she had only arrived recently.

So Claude wasn't ready to give up on negotiating for the key. Continuing to play the part of an adventurer companion, he couldn't help but interject,

"Both of you, please show some consideration for this 400-plus-year-old single dog. Stop showing off your affection in public. Can we discuss serious matters instead?"

Merlin: "Show off affection!? Believe it or not, I'll chop you dead with one slash!?"

Alice: "Exactly, such an annoying guy."

Claude paused, unable to understand these two, and said seriously, "I have no intention of interfering with either of you, but could you hand over the key first?"

"Impossible!" Alice showed a serious expression, then turned and said, "Merlin! Don't hand the key over to Claude. This guy isn't alive; he's one of the Four Heroes who died over 400 years ago—Bernard!"

"Over 400 years ago?" Merlin looked down at the silent Claude and thought, if he died over 400 years ago, then what's standing in front of him must be an undead, right?

"That's right. They are remnants of the former kingdom who were resurrected through magic, wanting to restore the old dynasty." Alice paused, trying to use the briefest words possible to let Merlin understand the situation. "Claude came here for that key. It must hide some great secret. We absolutely cannot hand it over to him!"

A great secret! ?

It must be an especially valuable treasure, right?

Ohohoho, I'm about to turn things around~

Merlin grinned crookedly, and the hallucination surfaced again in his mind.

Claude stood in the center holding a greatsword, emitting a heavy oppressive aura. So Alice already knew everything.

It seemed this woman had been secretly following him here from the very beginning and overheard all the secrets.

To protect the former kingdom's restoration plan, both Alice and Merlin had to die here. Not a single one could be spared!

Claude gripped his greatsword tightly, and Saint-tier battle energy surged within him in an instant. He would pick on the soft persimmon first, charging fiercely toward Alice.

Want to know how fast a Saint-tier warrior moves at full爆发?

Before the gust of wind even reached Alice's face, Claude had already arrived, raising his greatsword to deliver a devastating downward cleave straight at Alice's forehead!

"Eh!?" Alice was startled pale. Although she had some preparation, Claude's explosive power still exceeded her imagination.

Claude was still too naive, underestimating Merlin's speed and reflexes.

At the moment the unstoppable greatsword was about to split Alice's skull open, Merlin suddenly teleported in front of her.

"Hmph, couldn't hold back any longer, could you?"

Merlin used his bare-handed sword-disarming skill to block Claude's surging downward cleave!

Raging storm winds rose up, mixed with surging Saint-tier battle energy, revealing just how murderous Claude's intentions truly were.

"!!!" Claude was drenched in cold sweat, his heart filled with shock. So fast! His movement speed was subtly faster than when he activated his storm mode!

Alice retreated half a step in terror, slowly regaining her composure, thinking, this bastard actually saved me? Is he plotting something again?

"Sorry, our rent is split half and half. I can't let this ironing board kneel here. I sure don't want to pay full rent myself."

Merlin said this calmly, that intriguing expression of his leaving one unsure whether he meant it or not.

Alice's expression instantly fell, a slight sense of loss stirring inside her. That makes sense. She knew this bastard wasn't that kind-hearted. How could he possibly protect her for no reason?

Claude continuously pressed down on his greatsword, but the blade was pinched between Merlin's hands and didn't budge an inch.

"Both of you, I don't wish to do this. If you're willing to hand me the key, we can pretend none of this ever happened, how about that?"

"Not happening. The key is mine now." Merlin openly claimed it, thinking that if this key hid a great treasure, handing it to someone else would make him a fool. He continued, "Moreover, you actually attacked us. Then I won't be polite either. Remember your arrogant attitude earlier? I'm already impatient to teach you what politeness means."

"It seems there's no need to continue talking." Claude's voice deepened.

"Merlin, stop wasting words with him!"

Alice flashed out from behind Merlin, raised her slender sword, and drove it straight toward Claude's abdomen.

The sharp Light Anthem pierced through the dark armor, impaling Claude's body as well!

Claude was a resurrected undead, belonging to dark creatures, and Light Anthem was highly effective against dark creatures, dealing double damage!

The holy sword疯狂ly burned Claude, his wounds hissing as they smoldered, filling the air with a charred smell.

Claude shook violently like he'd been electrocuted, retreating lightning-fast to create distance, clearly very wary of Alice's slender sword.

"So he really is an undead." Alice glanced at her slender sword, the filthy blood upon it slowly evaporating.

Claude crouched on the ground, clutching his smoking abdominal wound. In a cold, vicious tone he said—

"You despicable fucking couple, actually teaming up to ambush me like that!?"

(+m- )

Two extra chapters every day, and I can still repay the 3100 monthly tickets by month's end. ==

Don't panic, I can steadily repay them, and I might even add some tips for extra chapters.

title: Chapter 42
content:
Chapter 42

Volume 3 · Chapter 42

"What kind of dog-man and woman! Keep your mouth clean!" Alice said angrily, extremely resistant to that title.

"Come on, what's going on?" Merlin turned his head to look at Alice, dissatisfied, "You should be righteous, don't always attack sneakily, making it seem like we're in this together."

"Why so much nonsense? He's the enemy, just kill him already." Alice said seriously, not understanding what Merlin was playing at.

"I refuse!" Merlin objected without hesitation, continuing, "I've never had the habit of teaming up with others to fight.

"What are you fixating on? Can't you just go ahead? I'll support you from the side." Alice frowned.

"No! I've only ever accepted one-on-one duels, or one against many. Let me team up with someone? I can't accept that." Merlin showed a very serious expression.

"Are you crazy?" Alice was surprised, never having seen someone like this before.

"Anyway, you're not allowed to interfere, making it seem like we're ganging up on someone. I want to teach this guy what politeness is. You can just cheer from the side, you understand what I mean?" Merlin said seriously, it seemed he was determined to duel Claude one-on-one.

Although Claude was undead and basically had little value to Merlin.

But Merlin remembered when he first came to the guild, he had taken an instant dislike to Claude.

Now was his chance to teach this show-off a lesson, and Merlin was eager to try.

"Damn it! Alice felt a bit looked down upon by Merlin, but thinking about how she couldn't beat Claude either, it was better to stay on the sidelines. So she couldn't help but curse, "Hope your head gets smashed in."

Merlin just laughed off Alice's muttering, completely unfazed, and walked alone to Claude's side, saying just two words.

"One-on-one."

Claude slowly stood up, although he had been injured by Alice's holy sword earlier, it wasn't a big deal.

He tightly gripped his heavy sword, staring at Merlin in a low voice.

"You're not joking?"

"Of course not. Two against one is unfair, one against one gives you no excuse to lose, and you'll have to accept defeat gracefully." Merlin shrugged his shoulders.

Claude fell silent. Although he didn't have confidence in completely defeating Merlin, he felt he could manage a draw, not zero chance of winning.

As long as he killed Merlin and got the key, then killed Alice, he would have completed his mission.

Although he knew Merlin wasn't a weak guy, for the sake of the kingdom's restoration, he risked his life to accept the challenge.

Claude took off his heavy helmet, revealing his face, throwing the helmet to the ground with a clinking sound, breaking the silence.

Pale hair hung limply in strands, his face was pale and ashen, several pieces of flesh had rotted away, his left eye was completely rotted with maggots wriggling around it, his mouth was stretched to his ears revealing sharp bones.

This sight was clearly like a one-eyed zombie that had just crawled out of a coffin, making people shiver in fear, completely lacking any human feeling.

Alice frowned, catching a strong stench of decay, thinking, no wonder she had hidden herself so tightly under the armor. How could she face people like this?

"Want me to lose gracefully? You've got quite the nerve." Claude's remaining eye rolled around, staring at Merlin, "Daring to fight me one-on-one is your mistake. I've never lost in a one-on-one situation before. If you ask among the Four Heroes who is strongest in single combat, there's no doubt it's me!

"Is it interesting to indulge in past glory?" Merlin touched his waist and smiled at his katana, "You're all just products of a bygone era, in my eyes you're just trash.

"Hmph! Arrogant guy, you think I'm afraid of you? If I get serious, I could take your life in a single breath!" Claude's words became increasingly impolite, "Don't think just because you know some tricks you can be fearless in front of a real Saint-tier!"

"Whether it's tricks or not, you'll find out by experiencing it yourself. But you won't have the chance to make any comments, because Merlin showed an extremely arrogant expression, pointing at Claude, "After you experience it, you'll already be in hell. Not everyone is as lucky as Alice."

"Huh?" Alice was conflicted, was she really lucky? She hadn't felt that way at all, always unlucky being entangled with Merlin.

"Fine then, a guy without magic or combat spirit. I'd like to see how you send me back to hell." Claude placed his heavy sword behind him, assuming a charging stance, "Today I'll let you experience what a battlefield meat grinder is. Betting on the name of the First Hero, I'll definitely cut you down here!

"Please show your full strength, it would be even better if you can surprise me." Merlin mockingly gestured to Claude.

"Secret Art: Storm Mode!!!"

Claude shouted loudly, his combat spirit suddenly erupted, his combat spirit flashed with golden light, with a hint of fierce red.

o 5 SE2 small治

Status activated, Claude's entire aura underwent a qualitative change, surpassing the realm of humanity, directly rushing towards the ferocious magical beast!

Claude's body seemed to be covered in porcupine skin, surging Saint-tier combat spirit, bringing with it gusts of wild wind.

Her eyes were wide with rage, her whole body was steaming, her skin turned red, as if hiding explosive power within.

"Oooooooh!!!!"

The restless storm wind blew through Alice's silver hair, making her frown.

So strong, this pressure was even more intense than before!

It seemed Claude had acknowledged Merlin's strength.

Time to get serious:

Alice had never seen a state secret art before, usually just fierce attacks.

Merlin silently lowered his katana, ready to draw it instantly. He was now somewhat interested in Claude, because that continuously rising pressure was quite interesting.

"Whoosh!"

After the tremendous sound, Claude suddenly charged, the earth beneath him trembling and cracking.

Claude wielded his heavy sword with unstoppable momentum, rushing straight at Merlin. The wind scourged everything in its path, leaving a trail of devastation!

This speed, Alice didn't even see a shadow, just felt some monster rushing past.

Merlin remained expressionless, motionless, as if he hadn't reacted to the approaching enemy.

What's going on!?

sF light novel

Why is his whole body full of openings!

Is he deliberately looking down on me, or luring me into a trap!?

Claude was uncertain, but under the pressure of movement, there was no time to hesitate. He raised his massive sword and slashed at Merlin's neck from the side, aiming for a fatal blow.

"Hmph!"

Merlin coldly snorted, suddenly turned his head to look at Claude from the side. Even during such high-speed action, he still managed to catch the enemy.

Just as Merlin's hand gripped the hilt of his katana, Claude's expression suddenly turned horrified, cold sweat pouring down!

Under storm mode, with extremely high perception, he could sense danger approaching in advance.

When Merlin's hand gripped the katana, Claude's perception kept sounding strong alarms, putting him in a state of fear.

If this continued, he was bound to die!

Claude quickly withdrew his attack, retreating in a flash, panting slightly as he looked at Merlin. For a moment, he couldn't stop sweating.

Recalling the recent dangerous alarms, feeling very real, Claude had never encountered such a situation in his life—

"What kind of person are you!?

"Why are you so powerful!

"This feeling of danger is too unreasonable!

"Aren't you human, but a god far beyond the Saint-tier!?!"

title: Chapter 43 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 43 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets

Volume 3 · Chapter 43

Claude was still shaken by what had just happened, his face paler than a corpse, the hand holding the giant sword trembling slightly.

He could become famous in one battle thanks to the storm mode's super-perception, which could predict danger and let him avoid it in advance.

But just now, his survival skill, which he was lazy with, actually acted like crazy—reporting to himself that he was about to die!

This made Claude incomprehensible, and he had never experienced such a thing; it proved that his perception had assessed Merlin as too powerful, to the point of repeatedly reporting danger.

Claude could not understand it; everything had been fine before, but when Merlin's hand touched the giant sword, his perception instantly shattered, desperately telling himself to escape quickly, that this opponent was unbeatable!

Claude believed strongly in his super-perception; it had always been useful. Today, facing Merlin was like a glitch—there was only a danger warning, nothing else.

Now Claude dared not act rashly, but maintained the storm mode, showing a look of utmost dread.

"What's the matter? Running away suddenly is just to say this?" Merlin set down the giant sword, his expression slightly disappointed.

Alice completely didn't understand what Claude was rambling about. Merlin was a god surpassing the Saint tier? Impossible, really? Although she didn't deny Merlin's greatness, the idea of surpassing the Saint tier was too exaggerated.

Actually, Alice hadn't even seen the battle clearly; Claude's speed was too fast, everything happened in the blink of an eye. She only saw the moment Merlin was about to draw his sword, and Claude was startled back, making it incomprehensible.

Alice didn't have the ability of super-perception, so she couldn't personally experience Claude's fear at that moment.

Claude's super-perception, his evaluation of Merlin, could be described as powerful enough to make one's soul tremble.

Claude's good eye stared at Merlin in shock, asking in a trembling voice, "Tell me! Are you a god surpassing the Saint tier?!"

"Huh?" Merlin furrowed his brows, answering helplessly, "Isn't it? I've never had a level, maybe I can't even compare to a low-tier."

"Impossible!" Claude felt Merlin was lying, his emotions agitated as he said, "If it's not surpassing the Saint tier, it's simply impossible to be this strong!"

"I've already said I'm not, what do you want to do?" Merlin spread his hands, speaking lightly, "Still fighting? If I don't fight, I can still defend myself—are you afraid? It seems the first of the Kingdom's Four Heroes is nothing like this."

"Yes, that's right, I'm afraid." Claude had no rebuttal this time.

A cold sweat slid down Alice's forehead. She thought in her heart, is he going to surrender now? Indeed, this Merlin guy is too perverted.

"Want to surrender? Kneel down and sincerely beg for my forgiveness, and I might consider sparing you." Merlin's lofty posture had evidently become a habit; even at this moment, he couldn't resist trampling on the enemy's dignity.

"Don't misunderstand, although I am indeed afraid, this is actually a happy thing, because Claude's mouth was wide open, white bones visible, looking at Merlin's good eye—it actually revealed a thread of excitement. "Finally, an opponent appeared who could make me use full power! 400 years! No one has ever made me afraid, willingly letting me use full power, you are the first person who can make me excited! I am feeling unprecedented joy from the bottom of my heart"O, what a messed-up novel.

Alice frowned, looking at Claude, who was exceedingly excited, and thought, what's going on? Just now he still didn't use full power? And he feels joy because he met a strong opponent? Is this a naked battle maniac? Or has he lost himself on the path of chasing strength?

"Is that so?" Merlin answered with a blank expression, having no movement in his heart at all, completely not putting Claude in his eyes.

"Merlin, can you understand my feelings now? If it were you, you'd definitely understand my current mood!" Claude said crazily, his white hair becoming more and more disheveled, the heavy sword in his hand trembling non-stop.

"Um, I understand."

Merlin nodded, looking at Claude with calm eyes like rubies.

Claude's mindset, Merlin understood well—powerful to the point of loneliness, with no one able to match him in an equal contest.

This feeling was very uncomfortable, like losing one's value, to the point where meeting a strong enemy was like winning a lottery.

When a person becomes extremely strong and has no opponents, they will feel very lonely, like a toxin eroding a fragile spirit.

Merlin was the same; a guy as powerful as him wasn't just challenging strong enemies to lift a curse, but also for fun, awaiting someone whose strength could match or even surpass his.

"Meeting a strong enemy is a happy thing, but unfortunately, the enemy that makes me happy is absolutely not you, because you are still too weak, you don't even have the qualification for me to consider you an opponent."

"I'll make you admit it, and an evenly matched opponent." Claude raised the giant sword.

"Evenly matched? Thinking I'm evenly matched with you is an insult to me." Merlin said with a half-smile.

Alice looked at Merlin in astonishment, thinking that although she knew this guy was extremely arrogant and haughty, she hadn't expected this arrogance to reach another realm!

"No more talk! Come fight!" Claude roared, the golden battle aura on his body completely turning crimson, "For no regrets, I will certainly use full power!"

"Hmph!" Merlin coldly snorted, stepping forward.

Alice was shocked looking at Claude, and cold sweat inevitably flowed down, because that overwhelming pressure had gone up another level, making even the space seem hard to breathe in.

Claude's body suddenly appeared densely packed with black incantations, instantly strengthening his power, as if releasing an ancient ferocious beast.

That forbidden art! The madman's sacrifice!

This forbidden art had long disappeared into the flow of history; who would have thought one could see it again!

He remembered seeing it in the teacher's study, an ancient tome recording the creation of a peak warrior!

It can exchange life for a short-term burst of power, exhaust all potential, and instantly display power 100 times normal!

Alice widened her eyes, not expecting Claude to have this trump card, but after using the forbidden art, one would basically be useless.

"Oh wow, a bit interesting." Merlin grinned, still composed.

Claude held the giant sword, his whole body wrapped in fierce Saint-tier red battle aura, releasing a terrifying pressure.

Storm mode forbidden art. The madman's sacrifice, battle power suddenly increased 100 times!

At this moment, Claude, I ask, in all of Great Britain, is there anyone who can stand against him?!

"Careful, Merlin!"

Just as Claude's voice fell, he suddenly launched an attack, reaching Merlin's side in a blink of an eye. Even though his perception kept warning of danger, he still attacked without care, brandishing the black giant sword!

Alice gasped for cold air, completely unable to see the action, secretly amazed, tsk tsk! Too strong! The eyes can't keep up!

Merlin gave a light smile, his body moving slightly, suddenly drawing his sword, fast enough to tear the sky!

Relying on super-perception, Claude vaguely saw the trajectory of the draw-slash, his body slightly adjusting, thinking he could dodge!

The two figures wind-driven, directly crossing each other, mutually back-to-back, pulling apart the distance one-

Merlin maintained the draw-slash posture.

Claude was also proudly aloof.

The battle ended in a short moment, suspense rising and falling.
