title: Chapter 6
content:
Chapter 6

Volume 4 · Chapter 6

"An SSS-rank free quest... isn't that really difficult?" Merlin asked tentatively, growing slightly interested in such a lucrative job.

"It's definitely super hard. Most adventurers aren't even allowed to participate. Mithril can only go there to run errands. It's the Funds adventurers who are the main combat force." Alice recalled for a moment and narrated seriously. "The guildmaster told me that the SSS-rank quest from 30 years ago was about killing the Kraken near the coast of Norway and Greenland. Since it had awakened, it directly blocked the maritime passage, and the bounty was funded by the Norwegian Kingdom."

"The Kraken?!" Merlin had indeed heard of that monster before. It was nearly legendary, on par with deities. "You mean that giant octopus?"

"You make it sound so easy. I know you're strong, but I think even you would have a hard time defeating the Kraken. Honestly, a monster at that level can't really be described within the Saint-tier category anymore." Alice wasn't exaggerating. There were so many legends about the Kraken that ordinary people could almost equate it with a deity.

"Ridiculous. I've never really taken any Kraken seriously." Merlin smiled, thinking that if the Kraken could truly defeat him, that would actually be something worth being happy about, since this monster might just help him break his curse.

"You don't have magic or aura, but based on my estimation, your strength is close to the peak of the Saint-tier, right?" Alice asked tentatively, neither stating too high nor too low.

"Suit yourself. I don't even know what tier I am myself." Merlin shrugged.

"I'm definitely not wrong." Alice stated firmly and continued, "But I have to tell you, the guildmaster said that during the subjugation 30 years ago, there were many Saint-tier experts, and several at the peak of Saint-tier. But they either got driven back by the Kraken or were swallowed whole or lost at sea. In the end, they had no choice but to seek help from the Holy Church, who dispatched a Hero."

"A Hero?!" Merlin didn't feel that Heroes were any stronger than ordinary Saint-tiers.

"That's my senior, the Hero whose name is widely known among ordinary people." A hint of pride appeared on Alice's face.

"Who is it?" Merlin didn't care much. He had killed quite a few Heroes himself and didn't find them particularly powerful.

"The legendary Spear Hero." Alice assumed Merlin would certainly know that name and felt the Spear Hero was far stronger than Merlin.

"What?!" Merlin furrowed his brows, clearly stunned, and instantly recalled the figure of someone holding a red spear, standing atop a mountain of demon corpses.

"You seem pretty familiar with him. I heard about him at the Holy Church—the legendary Spear Hero who successfully single-handedly subjugated Lucifer II, your mother." Alice said with interest.

"That's right. You know quite a lot."

Merlin's face showed no particular emotion, remaining very calm.

He remembered that there had been many strong figures in the Crusade Army back then, and the Spear Hero was extremely arrogant.

He forbade others from interfering, demanded a one-on-one duel against Lucifer II, and emerged victorious.

Merlin had always believed his mother was incredibly powerful, capable of beating anyone as easily as she beat her own son. So she lost to the Spear Hero?

Back then, Merlin was still weak, and seeing the Spear Hero's figure had truly shocked him. He felt that person alone deserved the title of "the strongest."

That duel had been fair and square, a 1v1 with no interference. They fought so fiercely that heaven and earth seemed to darken. It was the most thrilling battle Merlin had ever witnessed.

But the outcome was regrettable. Even now, Merlin believed his mother was still alive. Without seeing her corpse, he absolutely refused to jump to conclusions.

Alice had intended to provoke Merlin, but he was far more composed and calm. She couldn't help but think, as expected of a demon, even facing his mother's death he remained so cold-blooded.

"By the way... Merlin, you seem interested in the Spear Hero. Since you mentioned Alice stayed at the Holy Church and must know a lot, aren't you a Hero too? How much do you know about the Spear Hero?"

"What are you planning?" Alice asked in surprise.

"I'm just asking, out of curiosity~" Merlin gave an evasive answer, not directly saying he wanted to kill this person and see if he could break the heart curse. Among the strong figures he had heard of, only the Spear Hero seemed to have the potential to remove his heart curse.

"I don't know much either. I just heard that this senior was super impressive, regarded as a legend by the entire Holy Church and hailed as one of the Ten Legendary Heroes."

Alice seemed to know only this much.

"The Ten Legendary Heroes?!" Merlin furrowed his brows and felt a bit awkward. Alice's words were like saying there were nine others as powerful as the Spear Hero!?

"They are ten Heroes of exceptional strength who have left indelible contributions." Alice explained.

"Are they... still alive?" Merlin asked, thinking that if they were on par with the Spear Hero, their strength must be formidable. Worth a swing of the blade.

"I don't know. I overheard the bishop, drunk and babbling about how the Legendary Heroes all disappeared. If even one of them were here..." Alice glanced at Merlin and said faintly, "he could press you, Lucifer III, into the ground and make you call him dad."

"Hah..." Merlin gave a dry laugh, thinking that in the end they had all vanished. But with such powerful people out there, there was still a chance for him to break the curse. "Then what was the result of the Spear Hero subjugating the Kraken 30 years ago?"

"I think they injured the Kraken and sent it sinking to the bottom of the sea," Alice replied, recalling what the guildmaster had said.

Merlin fell into thought. If they only managed to injure it, then if he killed the Kraken, wouldn't that prove he was stronger than the Spear Hero? The problem was the sea, which was a bit troublesome. He couldn't swim, and water-repelling magic wouldn't work on him either...

"I'm just saying, as long as we work hard, we can pay off the debt. Don't keep spreading negative vibes. It's affecting me too." Alice said indignantly.

"Then why don't we just start lounging around and waiting for the SSS-rank commission to come to us?" Merlin was still in his lazy mode.

"That won't do! We can't be like that. We need a two-pronged approach: work hard to earn money while also waiting for an SSS-rank commission. That way it's more secure." Alice put on a very serious expression and added, "So I need to reach Saint-tier as soon as possible and become a Mithril-rank adventurer. As for you, I won't expect you to escape the Iron tier."

"How troublesome..."

Merlin pursed his lips and thought about the treasure key, so he picked up the key around his neck and took a look.

As for why Merlin wore it openly around his neck, it was because he wasn't afraid of anyone stealing it. His neck was the safest place, and he wouldn't forget it.

Merlin felt waiting for Alice to reach Saint-tier wasn't very reliable. He should honestly think of other methods, like treasure hunting?

"Hey, Alice. Last time you mentioned a friend who is well-read and knowledgeable. Maybe they can figure out the secret of the key?"

"Yes, that's right." Alice nodded.

"Are they reliable? Don't let them set their sights on our treasure." Merlin asked warily.

"Of course. Although she's a Silver-rank adventurer, she's only interested in knowledge. Money means nothing to her." Alice seemed very confident about this friend.

"What's her name?" Merlin asked curiously.

"Cough!" Alice cleared her throat and answered sincerely—

"Leonardo di Piero da Vinci."

title: Chapter 7 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 7 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 4 · Chapter 7

“Merlin? !”

Merlin frowned, forgiving him for always thinking the wrong way.

This name isn't like the real-world Leonardo da Vinci, is it?

The first impression was that it was the painting of the Mona Lisa's sneer hanging in the Louvre.

That painting is too famous, and it's Leonardo da Vinci's masterpiece.

Could it be that in this alternate world, there's also a Leonardo da Vinci old man?

People have always said he was a genius, and there are rumors about time travelers.

“Yes, it's Leonardo da Vinci, what's with that expression?” Alice frowned, a bit confused about what Merlin was surprised about.

“It's nothing, nothing.” Merlin waved his hand, never having thought about revealing his secret of being a time traveler to others. “Isn't that old man very smart?”

“Which old man? Please speak politely, she's a delicate girl.... Alice emphasized.

“Pfft!” Zhou Han coughed, feeling shocked. “--A girl?! !”

“It's a girl, what's wrong with that?” Alice narrowed her eyes, very suspicious.

Merlin rubbed his temples, having nothing left to say. The portrait of Leonardo da Vinci kept popping into his mind.

It's hard to imagine that this great man also met a cruel fate in this alternate world, underwent gender transformation, and became a girl who could get pregnant.

It's understandable, now that everyone has a 'mama' image, no one can escape fate.

Merlin thought about himself, if he ever became famous, he would definitely have a 'mama' image, and there's no escaping it.

“There's nothing wrong with it, I'm very interested in seeing this Leonardo da Vinci.”

“How suddenly enthusiastic? It seems like you have something in mind.” Alice kept a wary eye on Merlin.

“Who doesn't have good intentions? You didn't say she's well-versed in knowledge?” Merlin rolled his eyes.

“Hmph, she's on a mission, probably coming back soon.” Alice said unhappily.

“When she comes back, please bring me along.” Merlin looked very serious, eager to see what Leonardo da Vinci looks like in this world.

The couple's cohabitation began.

After completing a previous commission, they needed to rest for a while.

This pair of mortal enemies, Merlin and Alice, reluctantly lived under the same roof.

But with constant eye contact, friction was inevitable, and they quarreled twenty times in one night.

It wasn't because Merlin threw his clothes around, or because he snored, causing Alice a series of complaints.

Even this morning, things were no different.

“Bang bang bang!”

Alice was dressed in a silk nightgown, looking very at home, and was pounding on the bathroom door, her face flushed, her legs tightly clamped together, trembling, covering her skirt and shouting loudly.

This look clearly showed that she had been trying to go to the bathroom all night, and her bladder was about to burst.

Alice had been waiting in the bathroom for over half an hour, but Merlin was nowhere to be found, silent as a ghost.

“You bastard Merlin! Get out! How slow are you? It's been half an hour! ?”

“Get out! Get out! The bathroom isn't just for you! Consider my feelings!”

“From now on, no one is allowed to stay in the bathroom for more than half an hour! Otherwise, you'll have to pay extra rent!”

Alice felt like she was about to burst, in pain, assuming Merlin was being stubborn, so she softened her tone.

“Please, I beg you, okay? You just... I'm so..."

Inside the bathroom--

Merlin was sitting on the toilet, treating Alice's shouting outside as air, ignoring her.

If she dares to break the door, she won't dare to casually destroy the house.

The bathroom, although small, was a magical place. It was like a bed, and looking at something inside it made one's focus very concentrated, and one didn't want to leave.

Merlin was holding a London newspaper, reading it with great pleasure. The newspaper and the bathroom were a perfect match, like beer and fried chicken.

The basic news was mostly the same, whether it was Queen Elizabeth visiting some country or some royal couple having a talk, and there was also a piece of information about himself.

“It is said that Queen Elizabeth has the intention to rescind the warrant for the Earl of Elgin, and invite him to join the Order of the Thistle, but Queen Elizabeth has not made any positive response to this.”

Merlin smiled at this, thinking that even if the queen wanted to invite him, he wouldn't go. Being a subordinate to a human queen? That's a joke. Preferring to be the king in hell rather than a servant in heaven, that's the rule of the Lucifer for generations, which he will follow to the end.

Of course, the newspaper also had information about the Holy Church's strong presence.

“The Holy Church publicly declares that the Earl of Elgin is the Redeemer Knight mentioned in the Holy Scripture, and hopes that he will go to the Vatican to accept the baptism of the Goddess of Light, to become the left and right arms of the Holy Father for the upcoming calamity, and to have the same position as the Grand Master of the Holy Temple.”

“Haha....”

Merlin patted his own head and laughed, thinking that these religious fanatics were too good at making things up. He's not a Redeemer Knight, I'm the arrogant Demon Lord who will turn over the Holy Church! Want me to go to the Vatican for the Goddess of Light's baptism? I'm not going to tear down your god temples.

Merlin had no interest in the Holy Church, although the conditions were very good, but from the beginning, he didn't like those dirty religious fanatics.

The most attractive news was about the former royal remnants, which was the headline of the front page.

“The former royal remnants have been active frequently, and the royal capital has urgently dispatched the ninth knight of the Twelve Thorny Knights, Lord Saha, to be in charge of this event. Lord Saha publicly stated that he will use all his efforts to investigate this event and eliminate the former royal remnants as soon as possible, so please rest assured.”

Merlin raised his eyebrows, embarrassedly thinking that the Order of the Thistle really mobilized? They moved quite quickly. Thinking about Claude's strength, I wonder how strong the ninth knight is? Can he beat Claude's companions?

“Merlin, you bastard! Did you fall into the toilet? Go die!”

Alice couldn't bear it anymore and shouted loudly outside.

“Tsk!” Merlin scoffed, frowned, thinking that this rag was disturbing his good mood. “Why so eager? Are you going to burst?”

“I can't hold it! ! !” Alice was delighted when Merlin finally spoke.

“Hold it! Don't call unless you have to!” Merlin rolled his eyes, not at all polite.

“Merlin! Please, okay? I really... it's so hard... Alice said with a crying voice.

“.... Merlin sighed, flushed the toilet, and took the newspaper with him. “Okay, okay, I'm coming out.”

After Merlin came out, he saw Alice with a furious look, her face black as could drip water, and her eyes very hostile.

“What's with that look? Are you going to eat me?”

“Remember, if you hide in the bathroom and don't come out, I won't let you go! Get out!”

Alice directly pushed Merlin aside and rushed into the bathroom, locking the door.

“.... Merlin smiled, not taking Alice seriously.

“Go make breakfast! It's your turn to cook! Don't think you can skip!” Alice's angry voice came from inside the bathroom.

“Tsk, so annoying.”

Merlin was annoyed and walked into the kitchen, just picking up a frying pan, when the doorbell rang.

“Merlin! Go open the door!” Alice shouted.

“You can't go yourself? ! I'm not going!” Merlin gritted his teeth and cursed, not happy with Alice's tone.

“I....... you go.... please, okay?” Alice softened her tone, looking a bit ashamed.

“Hmph.” Merlin huffed, dropped the frying pan, and went to open the door.

The person who came was Lucy, looking very urgent, as if there was something urgent.

“Miss Lucy?” Merlin was surprised, thinking she was either a fee collector or a salesperson.

“Merlin, is Alice at home?” Lucy asked.

“Yes, what's up?” Merlin answered truthfully.

“You two come with me to the guild, the Order of the Thistle has sent people to see you.” Lucy said straightforwardly.

“Eh! ?” Merlin frowned, a bit surprised.

Order of the Thistle?

Why see us?

title: Chapter 8 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 8 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 4 · Chapter 8

Merlin and Alice, having received Luce's, didn't eat the rebellion.

Instead, they went straight to the stationed guards of Reksem.

The guard captain, Plais, had been waiting here early.

"Yo yo yo~" Plais flashed a very lewd grin, rubbing his hands as he said, "Isn't this the blossoming flower of Reksem, the lady Alice who possesses both beauty and wisdom?"

"Scram..." Alice immediately showed a look of extreme disgust, as if looking at a fly.

"Oh ho~, got scolded, feels great." Plais's mysterious face flushed; he especially liked being cursed by a woman, and would love it even more if it came with a disdainful glance.

"Hmm! ?" Merlin glanced at Plais, thinking the guy was about the same age as Hobbs, both in the uncle range, but this masochistic vibe was being shamelessly displayed.

"Crazy..." Alice frowned, her face full of contempt.

"To be honest, I also enjoy Miss Luce scolding me, but that disdainful expression isn't as authentic as yours, Miss Alice." Plais's expression grew even more lewd, perhaps fantasizing about some queen game.

"Stay away from me, disgusting guy!" Alice touched the slender sword at her waist, thinking Plais was even more annoying than Hobbs—both his mouth and personality were vile, a double dose of nastiness that was deadly.

"Wow~" Plais clutched his chest, his expression delighted, "Exciting~ so damn exciting~, Miss Alice, you're the best!"

Alice rolled her eyes; she could no longer tolerate this guy, and she wasn't even familiar with Plais.

She remembered when she first arrived in Reksem, this guy would constantly cling to Luce looking for a scolding. o

At the time she couldn't stand it, so she retorted at Plais, and the pervert got excited.

Since then, Alice and Luce have been added to Plais's masochistic YY list.

"Miss Alice, if the chance arises, you must whip me hard, preferably with some chili water, that feeling..." Plais fantasized, his expression a mix of pain and pleasure, his hands loosely clenched, "Duang~, so爽! Awesome!"

Merlin's forehead beaded with a few drops of sweat; watching Plais, he thought, "This guy is also a talent! The more he gets beaten, the more he enjoys it. Is there anyone else this despicable? I can't at all understand the thrill of being hit by a girl."

"Stop bothering me, okay?" Alice put on a serious face, finding Plais increasingly off-putting.

"Don't be so cold, Miss Alice. I heard you turned down Lord Arnold's proposal yesterday; what a pity. You have no idea how many maidens in the city are pining for Lord Arnold," Plais said meaningfully.

"My partial refusal has nothing to do with you," Alice furrowed her brows, knowing Plais was a lackey of the Austin family.

"I was just rambling. Yesterday Lord Arnold came home crying miserably, and his sister beat him out of him at midnight," Plais said with a half-smile.

"Oh," Alice replied coldly.

"This friend with a woman's face..." Plais squinted, sizing up Merlin, then suddenly realized, "Oh~ you must be the rival Lord Arnold mentioned, Sir Merlin, right?"

"Rivals don't exist; I have no connection with Alice," Merlin explained helplessly.

Plais circled Merlin twice, chuckling, "The proof of this adventuring couple is already on them; no further explanation is needed."

Merlin's mood remained unchanged; being misunderstood daily had become routine, so he was too lazy to explain.

"But to be Lord Arnold's rival, I thought it would be some formidable figure, turns out it's just an ordinary person?" Plais said, slightly surprised, meaningfully, "Friends aren't just talk; your wife seems stronger than you, which gives the impression of a freeloader, and any man would feel the pressure."

"Huh?" Merlin frowned, thinking, "I have no pressure at all; a single finger could crush Alice."

"It's not a big deal; being a freeloader usually requires capital, and yours looks great..." Plais flashed a lewd grin, patting Merlin's chest, "Lord Arnold said you conquered Miss Alice with your big banana, so you must be a man with some skill, hehe."

"???" Merlin made a black question mark, still not knowing where the 'big banana' joke came from.

Alice's face flushed, she quickly interjected, "Shut up! We're here to meet the Azalea Knight Order, not waste time with you!"

"I get it, I get it~" Plais smiled, waving his hand...

"Miss Alice, don't be angry, please follow me.

Plais led Merlin and Alice to a small room that looked rather plain,

Merlin's first impression was that it resembled an interrogation chamber.

"The gentlemen of the Azalea Knight Order will be here shortly; please wait a moment."

Plais smiled and stepped out, leaving Alice and Merlin alone.

The air fell silent, an oppressive boredom settling in.

"Alice, why did the Azalea Knight Order come to see us?" Merlin asked.

"It must be about the remnants of the former main nation; we were the first to reach the deepest level of the tomb maze, so they might have important questions," Alice speculated.

"Are they asking about the key?" Merlin probed.

Alice thought for a moment and said seriously, "It's possible..."

Merlin quickly slipped the key into his clothing, "We must die before we admit we know, okay?"

"...Alice, being upright, finds it hard to suddenly lie."

"Do you still want the treasure?" Merlin began to work on Alice's mind, "This treasure might solve our problem, but we can't reveal it; just a tiny lie will do~"

Alice furrowed her brows and reluctantly said, "Ah, I understand now."

Merlin felt a bit relieved; since Alice agreed, it should be fine.

Three knights clad in silver-white armor entered, their golden engravings giving an air of nobility.

Their red capes, embroidered with azalea flowers, swayed as they walked, exuding great presence.

The swords at their hips seemed uniquely crafted; just the hilts indicated they were no ordinary weapons.

All three knights radiated nobility; it was clear they belonged to the royal exclusive knight order.

The lead knight wore no helmet, instead keeping it at his waist; his square forehead was topped with thick brown hair, and his bright eyes seemed to scrutinize everything with a hint of inquiry, possessing both the majesty of a knight and the elegance of a scholar.

The three knights moved to the opposite side; the lead knight sat opposite Alice and Merlin, placing his helmet nearby, while the other two guarded the flanks.

The apparent captain knight sat upright, assuming a questioning posture, cleared his throat lightly and said—

"Sorry to take up your time."

"First, allow me to introduce myself..."

"My name is Brent Chapman, affiliated with the Azalea Knight Order."

"Today, under orders from Sir Sahadin, the Ninth Thorn Knight, I have come to thoroughly investigate you two."

From this point onward, I'll set a flag: when Merlin and Alice's names appear again as protagonists in an old book, I'll add another chapter on the spot.

title: Chapter 9
content:
Chapter 9

Volume 4 · Chapter 9

"Investigate what?" Merlin couldn't help asking, silently tightening his grip on the key hanging from his chest.

If they'd come for this key, then there was definitely no room for negotiation.

"Why, the recent undead outbreak in Denbighshire, of course. According to the garrison's report, the two of you had contact with the remnants of the former kingdom, didn't you?" Knight Chapman explained.

"They're just here to ask about that?" Alice was a bit doubtful—clearly a guilty conscience at work.

Chapman looked at the strange expressions on Merlin and Alice's faces, figuring they were nervous. After all, the Order of the Bauhinia was under the royal family; anyone summoned by them would naturally feel uneasy, thinking nothing good would come of it.

"Don't be nervous, you two. You're Master Taylor's people—we won't make things difficult for you. Truth be told, back in the day Master Taylor once lectured us预备 knights of the Bauhinia at the royal palace. You could say we're all half-students of Master Taylor."

Merlin's expression shifted to surprise. He thought to himself, *Is that old man the guild master really that highly regarded? I never noticed at all—all he does every day is sit with his eyes closed, playing the mystic...*

"Th-then... we can rest easy..." Alice replied awkwardly, still not entirely reassured inside.

"Ahem, let's begin then. You only need to answer our questions truthfully." Chapman gave a light cough, took the documents handed over by his subordinate, and gave them a rough glance. "Did the two of you witness the full battle between the former kingdom's prime minister and Bernald, the foremost of the Four Heroes?"

"I saw it." Alice nodded, then pointed at Merlin. "He came later..."

Chapman gave Merlin a brief look, especially at his adventurer's license, and found he was a villager with no magic or battle aura. He felt a slight disdain and didn't bother paying him much attention. This time, his main purpose was to take Alice's testimony.

Merlin's lack of magic and battle aura immediately made Chapman assume he was just some guy idling his days away at the Adventurers Guild. After all, plenty of such people existed—content to drift through life without any ambition.

"Then, Miss Alice, did their conversation contain any secrets?"

"They were just... talking about restoring the former kingdom, obtaining new power or something..." Alice hadn't really understood it herself; that was about the gist of it.

"Obtaining new power? How?" Chapman pressed.

"It was just..." Alice glanced at Merlin beside her, who was making exaggerated faces at her, so she said with some irritation, "What they needed? I was too far away at the time, and I didn't hear it very clearly."

Merlin breathed a sigh of relief. This dullard Alice wasn't good at lying, so he'd have to keep an eye on her.

"I see..." Chapman frowned, feeling he hadn't gotten much out of it. He lowered his head to look at the documents. "According to the report, Bernald, one of the Four Heroes of the former kingdom, died four hundred years ago. At the scene was a resurrected undead creature. Miss Alice, do you have any information on who resurrected Bernald?"

"I... suppose it was the former kingdom's prince? I heard them mention it during their conversation—that the prince hadn't died, and was still alive." Alice said, recalling as she spoke.

Chapman's eyes widened, and he asked in delighted surprise, "Are you saying Bernald and the others said with their own mouths that Prince Copperfield of the former kingdom is not dead?"

"Yes, they said it themselves." Alice nodded. That she could be certain of—she'd heard it very clearly.

Chapman was overjoyed. This was no small gain; at the very least, they now knew who the enemy was. Without much thought, it was obvious who had resurrected the former kingdom's Four Heroes.

"Any other information?"

"They said something about... the prince surviving by drinking the blood of the elf race..." Alice recalled that line.

Chapman grew even more pleased. The elf race was extremely scarce in Britain. Even if someone wanted to capture elves from the Southern United Kingdom, they'd need to pass through customs. A careful investigation along those lines might just let them follow the trail and find the stronghold of the former kingdom's remnants.

"Anything else? Miss Alice, your words are of great help to us. I hope you won't hold anything back..."

"That's all. They started fighting right after." Alice answered.

"The necromancer and Bernald were both subjects of the former kingdom—why did they fight?" Chapman pressed.

"Not sure. Bernald wanted to restore the kingdom, the necromancer disagreed, and then... they fought." Alice shrugged.

Chapman thought for a moment, then continued, "As one of the former kingdom's Four Heroes, how powerful was Bernald?"

This question was also very important—they needed to investigate the enemy's strength clearly.

If he was formidable, then Ninth Knight Sahadin alone wouldn't be enough; they'd need the other Thorn Knights to join the subjugation.

Alice thought for a moment. Claude's consecutive explosive bursts at the end had been off the charts—he'd simply been unlucky enough to run into a freak like Merlin. So she said in a very serious tone, "Strong. Extremely strong."

A trace of doubt appeared on Chapman's face, and he said flatly, "Miss Alice, please don't exaggerate recklessly. According to the report, two Saint-tier powerhouses mutually wounded each other, and you finished off the survivor with a single strike."

"He really was that strong. Why would I exaggerate?" Alice furrowed her delicate brows.

"Miss Alice, forgive my bluntness—I am a high-rank warrior, not some ordinary newbie. As far as I know, even if a Saint-tier is at death's door, a normal attack wouldn't be something a high-rank could easily withstand. If Bernald was truly as formidable as you claim, how could you have so easily delivered the finishing blow? That defies common sense."

"We..." Alice glanced at Merlin beside her.

"I hope you'll tell the truth and assist our investigation. The Order of the Bauhinia would be grateful." Chapman said seriously.

"He really was extremely strong. But Bernald wasn't killed by me—it was this guy!" Alice pointed at Merlin, telling the truth.

"That's right, I took him down." Merlin nodded, admitting it openly.

Chapman looked at Merlin, then couldn't help snorting with laughter. He said contemptuously, "Miss Alice, are you joking? An ordinary man with no magic or battle aura—how could he possibly defeat a Saint-tier powerhouse!?"

"Mmm..." Merlin was silent, his expression blank. He thought to himself, *As expected, no one believes it. Fine, believe it or not—I can't be bothered to quibble.*

"I'm not joking!" Alice pointed at Merlin and said seriously. "This guy really is powerful! Close to Saint-tier peak, he one-shot Bernald—I saw it with my own eyes!"

At this point, it wasn't just Chapman—even the two knights beside him couldn't help snickering aloud.

"Alright, alright, Miss Alice, please behave normally. I don't know what your purpose is in wildly singing the praises of your lover here, but I do know that a Saint-tier powerhouse could kill an ordinary person with just a single finger." Chapman shook his head, wearing a half-smile, and said disdainfully.

"Your rambling nonsense right now makes me feel like it's an open insult to the intelligence of a Bauhinia knight."

\(V yr

title: Chapter 10 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 10 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 4 · Chapter 10

Merlin wore an indifferent expression; everything was as expected.
Anyway, he had no magic or fighting spirit, so wherever he went he'd be treated like a salted fish, and he'd already gotten used to it.
But Alice didn't think that way; being disbelieved made her angry, so she tugged Merlin.
"Show them the blade slash quickly, otherwise they won't believe me and they'll think I'm mentally ill!"
"Why do I have to do this?" Merlin made an impatient expression; he already despised showing his strength to a salted fish, let alone being in late-stage laziness.
As for showing his strength to Elder Tyler, it's because he wants a job.
As for showing his strength to Chapman? He has no ulterior motive, there's no need at all.
Also, it would make him look like a monkey being watched; maybe his brain is sick.
A true strong one would shout on the street every day, "I'm awesome, I'm powerful?"
This is not a true strong one, it's a self-absorbed idiot.
"Will you die if you show it?" Alice was somewhat urgent, not wanting to be looked at like a mentally ill person by these people.
"Sigh, it's too boring, I'm too lazy to move..." Merlin rested his cheek, looking elsewhere.
"Hmph."
Chapman snorted lightly, not taking Merlin at all, thinking the guy was just being mysterious.
After hearing Alice say Merlin could do the blade slash, Chapman became even more disdainful, a guy who only knows how to pose with a "POSS" garbage skill, what could be outstanding?
Now Merlin's impression on Chapman was that of an ordinary villager in the Adventurers Guild, living off free meals and waiting to die, using the blade slash to show off and cheat.
Chapman withdrew his disdainful gaze, slightly straightened his posture.
"Miss Alice, we hope you cooperate with our investigation and answer truthfully about Bernard's strength."
"He's really powerful! He also knows an ancient forbidden technique, with incredible burst power in a short time!" Alice explained, her face turning red with excitement.
Chapman sighed, had to become serious, and said seriously, "Miss Alice, you know we are the Pomegranate Knights, directly under the command of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth. If you don't cooperate with our investigation, you know the consequences."
Alice frowned, thinking the other party was threatening; if she didn't comply, she would be imprisoned, maybe other punishments.
But she had already spoken the truth, what else should she say?
Alice hesitated, wondering whether to go along with Chapman's words; this guy, being a royal knight, was somewhat arrogant.
"I really hate being threatened; is the Queen's Knight Order powerful?" Merlin was a bit upset, speaking first to Alice.
"What do you mean, sir? Are you questioning the authority of the Pomegranate Knights?" Chapman arrogantly said; he didn't want to deal with Merlin, but Merlin's bluntness made him listen.
In the cramped space, a smell of gunpowder filled the air.
"Ha, scum..."
Alice quickly covered Merlin's mouth, preventing him from speaking.
"Alright, I admit, the necromancer and Bernard aren't very strong; they're just high-level power."
"I knew it would be like that; how could a Saint-tier strong one be cut off by you?" Chapman said with a half-smile, seeming satisfied with this hypocritical answer.
Alice stayed silent, not wanting to care; whatever Chapman thought, it didn't matter to her.
"It seems the four heroes of the former kingdom are no better than this, just a name; letting Lord Saha J handle the extermination of the former kingdom's remnants is a bit of a waste of talent." Chapman laughed, shook his head, slowly stood up, as if to leave.
"That's right, I also think the four heroes are just a name; Bernard is really weak..." Merlin agreed.
Alice couldn't stand it, rolled her eyes twice, thinking Merlin's view of weakness didn't mean others felt the same; to her, Bernard was as powerful as a monster! Wouldn't it be a death if you act like a fake?
For Merlin, everyone looked weak, but from others' perspective, it was not the case.
"Hmph, Miss Alice, your lover is more honest than you." Chapman smiled.
Alice grew impatient, shouting in her mind, "We're not married! Who doesn't love their lover? These couple adventurers are truly annoying!"
"G, U, N!" Alice cursed, feeling very unbalanced.
"Finally, thank you for your cooperation, goodbye." Chapman bowed slightly, expressing knightly etiquette. Then the three knights left. SF light novel. The room returned to silence, the two remained silent. Merlin took out the key from his neck, thinking it wasn't for the key, he was lucky.
"What's wrong with this era? Even if I speak honestly, no one believes?" Alice said with a complex expression.
"We've told you, don't take it too seriously; we just need to take care of ourselves." Merlin said coolly, looking open.
"Why can't you show your strength? Do you enjoy being looked down upon?" Alice said angrily, mainly because she was misunderstood.
"Heh~" Merlin snorted, meaning something.
"An ant is mocking beside you; would you waste time insisting on stepping on it to kill it?"
The three Pomegranate Knights were preparing to return to the capital, reporting the information to the Ninth Thorn Knight Saha Ding. Along the way, many villagers recognized them as Pomegranate Knights and stopped to watch. The Pomegranate Knights were called the "Queen's Sword," highly regarded across Great Britain, representing justice and protecting the people. Unfortunately, these three were not the Thorn Twelve Knights, but ordinary knights. If the Thorn Knights came, the people would welcome them with a roar of applause and flowers.
A subordinate of the knight came up to ask Chapman, "Captain, what do we do next?"
"Return to the capital, report the important information to Lord Saha Ding. This time, having Lord Saha Ding is enough; no need for other Thorn Knights' help." Chapman and his subordinates were told what to do, not noticing that a woman with purple hair and alluring appearance walked up, the former kingdom's four heroes' Karona! She had already reached Lexerm today.
Karona looked at the three Pomegranate Knights mildly, brushed past Chapman. Chapman shivered, turned around, couldn't see the purple-haired woman, as if she vanished. How similar to the former kingdom's four heroes' dragon-riding thief Karona?
She resembled the portrait in the former kingdom's records. Legend said she was beautiful and alluring, her purple aura shining in the night. She could speak dragon language, communicate with fierce dragons, and command them. Chapman was perplexed, unsure if the purple-haired woman was a dragon-riding thief. Even if the four heroes were resurrected, why would they come to Lexerm? It seemed pointless.
"What's wrong, Captain?" a subordinate asked curiously.
"Nothing, let's go..." Chapman shook his head, left. "Can... I just..." (u--)

title: Chapter 11 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 11 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 4 · Chapter 11

After dealing with the Bauhinia Knight Order's affairs.

Alice said she wanted to train at the guild's back dojo, hoping to reach Saint-tier soon.

Even though Merlin kept making sarcastic remarks beside her, Alice didn't care.

Working hard is better than just sitting and waiting for death, right? So making use of every bit of free time for training was necessary.

Merlin happened to have nothing to do, so he followed Alice there.

Guild Master Old Tyler knew Alice wanted to borrow the dojo and didn't hesitate at all before lending it to her. Perhaps it was because he felt guilty and ashamed for accidentally turning Merlin and Alice into a couple of adventurer partners.

Alice drew her slender sword, holding it upright in front of her. The other hand rested on the shimmering blade as her body emitted a压制 that mixed fighting aura and magic power, rising steadily.

Cold air raged throughout the dojo, even forming a layer of white frost on the floor that slowly spread outward from Alice's position.

Alice wasn't Saint-tier yet, so she could only project her presence but couldn't produce the Saint-tier mark of materializing golden magic or fighting aura.

Merlin stood across from her, staring at the gusts of cold wind as if nothing were wrong, watching Alice with a calm expression.

When the high-tier pressure reached its peak, Alice finally relaxed, let out a long breath, and said helplessly, "It seems I'm still a little short of Saint-tier."

Merlin pinched the bridge of his nose and said flatly, "Lady, are you really just a little short? You're as far from Saint-tier as heaven is from earth."

"...Stop talking! If you keep this up I'll lose all my confidence," Alice pouted, very dissatisfied with Merlin's constant discouragement.

Merlin sighed and said helplessly, "You're still a mediocre dual cultivator of magic and martial arts. The training difficulty is ten times harder than someone who specializes in just one! If I recall correctly, for dual cultivation breakthroughs, both magic power and fighting aura need to meet the advancement standards, right?"

"That's true..." Alice said somewhat aggrievedly.

"Tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue and said gloomily, "Both magic power and fighting aura need to reach Saint-tier levels. When will you ever meet the standards? I estimate you'll never make it in this lifetime."

"Nonsense! My teacher is a Saint-tier powerhouse who practices dual cultivation! If she can do it, I certainly can too!" Alice retorted stubbornly.

"Your teacher isn't you, what are you getting proud about?" Merlin struck without mercy, saying impatiently, "If you ask me, you should give up dual cultivation and specialize in either magic or fighting aura. Only then do I think you have a chance at Saint-tier."

"No! When training under my teacher, I swore to become a successor of the Great Snow Mountain. I'd feel ashamed to give up halfway," Alice said firmly.

"You're just wasting your youth. What's so great about being mediocre? I never thought you were impressive with dual cultivation..." Merlin said lazily.

"That's not true! It's impressive, okay? The essence of our Great Snow Mountain is the fusion of magic and fighting aura to achieve an instantaneous ultra-high burst. I even cornered your sister back then!" Alice brought up the incident from a year ago, hoping to salvage some face.

"Please, my sister is kind of dumb. She kept swinging her whip against you the whole time. She's a mage, and playing melee combat with you clearly shows she was looking down on you," Merlin didn't understand where Alice's superiority complex came from, finding it quite amusing. "If my sister had used her 「Piercing Scream」 magic, your head would've exploded on the spot, you know?"

"I still managed to corner your sister though. Underestimating your opponent is a major taboo, and she didn't even understand that," Alice said resentfully.

"Yes, yes, my sister is the weakest among the Seven Demon Generals. If you encounter anyone else, you won't be so lucky," Merlin twisted his mouth and said contemptuously.

"Shut up! Don't crush my spirits! I'm going to reach Saint-tier through dual cultivation regardless!" Alice rejected Merlin's suggestion.

"What a stubborn fool..."

Merlin grumbled. He also wanted Alice to reach Saint-tier so she'd have access to SSS-class quests.

Judging by Alice's current high-tier status, even if there were SSS-class quests available, she could only watch helplessly. It was completely a waste.

Merlin wondered if there was some strong medicine he could get Alice to take to boost her straight to Saint-tier.

But such medicines were hard to find and not particularly good for the body. Those who reached Saint-tier through drugs were mostly fake. Given Alice's personality, she definitely wouldn't take anything like that.

However, as far as Merlin knew, there was one exception: the inheritance crystal inside a dragon's head.

The dragon race was somewhat special; they didn't need others to teach them magic or martial techniques.

Once their strength reached a certain level, they would instantly comprehend the dragon lineage inheritance.

The regret was that not every dragon possessed an inheritance crystal; it entirely depended on luck.

Some dragons were born with one naturally in their heads, much like an abnormality, completely unrelated to their strength.

For example, the Holy Dragon Avis, whom Merlin imprisoned in Deadseven Swamp, was one of the dragon race's finest yet lacked an inheritance crystal.

If one were fortunate enough to obtain a dragon inheritance crystal and slowly digest it, they could transform into a human-form giant dragon.

Merlin wasn't just thinking wildly, after all, dragon inheritance crystals were particularly suitable for dual cultivators. Just imagine if Alice possessed a dragon's powerful physique along with their massive magic power. She'd be quite formidable.

"Don't tell me what to do! I want to focus on my training, stop interfering!" Alice readjusted her magic and fighting aura, beginning to rise steadily once more.

"Isn't this too slow?" Merlin couldn't bear to watch anymore, almost furious at Alice's stupidity. "Steadily pushing your境界 like this — will it even work? Progressing at turtle speed is a pure waste of time."

"What should I do then? I've always trained this way," Alice lowered her slender sword.

"Didn't you ask me a year ago why I'm so strong? I told you I've fought giants, torn apart sea demons, and walked through magma?" Merlin said calmly.

Alice thought about it for a moment and nodded, saying confusedly, "You did say that. What about it?"

"You're so stupid. Didn't I just tell you the method to grow stronger?" Merlin frowned, silently lamenting Alice's poor comprehension. It's about near-death experiences. When you're on the verge of death, your potential erupts, which is much faster than your turtle-speed training."

"Who would go looking for death on a whim? One slip and you'd actually die!" Alice found the idea terrifying, but she couldn't deny it was a good method. After being beaten nearly to death by the Goblin Emperor and waking up, her magic and fighting aura had indeed become much purer.

"Baby, this is the fastest way to advance. Don't doubt me," Merlin said seriously.

"Don't call me baby, it's disgusting..." Alice's face turned red as she protested angrily.

"Then Miss Alice, trust me." Even when speaking seriously, Merlin gave off a teasing feeling.

"Even if I agree to train under near-death conditions, places like that are hard to come by," Alice said helplessly.

Merlin spread his hands and said with a calm expression, "Aren't I here? Don't worry, as long as I'm around, there'll be no problems."

"...What do you mean?" Alice's mood suddenly grew anxious, unsure what he had up his sleeve.

"What I mean is, I'll be your sparring partner. With me..." Merlin patted his chest and said seriously—

"Every strike will make you feel like you're definitely going to die."

title: Chapter 12
content:
Chapter 12

Volume 4 · Chapter 12

“Sparring partner?!” Alice narrowed her eyes, finding the idea quite novel.

“Exactly,” Merlin said, waving Alice over. “Go all out. If you manage to touch me even once, I’ll call it a loss.”

“Ehmmmm…”

Alice felt uneasy and hesitated. “It feels like you’re up to something. Are you trying to get back at me or something?”

“Do I look that无聊 (boring)? If it weren’t for the debt issue, do you think I’d willingly be your sparring partner?” Merlin sighed, speaking seriously. “You should be happy to have me as your sparring partner. Back in the day, the Sixth Palace Great Demon Lord Beelzebub even begged me to give his sister a few pointers, and I flatly refused. Don’t you realize how lucky you are?”

“….”

Alice recalled Merlin’s draw-cut slash, which usually left opponents on their knees, and couldn’t help but feel a bit fearful.

If possible, Alice didn’t want to fight Merlin. It was too dangerous.

It wasn’t just a matter of being on the verge of death—it was a certainty of death.

Alice hesitated and stammered, “N-no… I can’t. If you have any ill intentions, I’ll be in danger.”

“Don’t worry, I can control myself. If I couldn’t control my own power, I wouldn’t be worth the title of Demon Lord.” Merlin said this while flipping the wakizashi at his hip over, ensuring it wouldn’t kill Alice. A slip of the hand would at most result in a severe injury.

Alice’s heart gave a little jump. She thought about how she and Merlin didn’t have any major grudges, and now they were tied together by debt. He probably wouldn’t harm her, but then—

“But that’s still not okay. If you mess up the town like last time, the Guildmaster will be furious.”

“You’re such a hassle.”

Merlin scratched his head, his dislike for the troublesome woman increasing a bit more.

He looked around and spotted a few wooden swords nearby, which looked quite sturdy.

This was a dojo after all, so having wooden swords as training tools wasn’t unusual.

Merlin simply picked up the wooden swords, gave them a couple of swings, and found them satisfactory.

“Now are you satisfied? These are wooden swords that break easily. They don’t look the least bit threatening.”

Alice looked at the wooden sword in Merlin’s hand and felt a little more at ease, but then doubt crept in. “Can you even use your full strength with a wooden sword?”

“How can’t I use my full strength?” Merlin frowned, not understanding what Alice was doubting.

“Don’t you usually rely on the demon sword at your hip? That’s probably why you’re so strong,” Alice asked seriously, thinking Merlin’s strength must come from his weapon. He always used that weapon, so there must be some secret to it.

Merlin had no magic or fighting spirit to begin with. If his power came from the weapon, then that overwhelming strength made sense.

“You mean this wakizashi?” Merlin patted the weapon at his hip.

“Right. Isn’t your strength because of the weapon?” Alice paused, then continued, “A year ago during the extermination, I was chatting with the bishop, and he said your demon sword was incredibly powerful. He said you yourself weren’t that scary.”

“Hahaha…” Merlin let out a series of cold laughs. “That bishop who wet himself in fear knows nothing. This wakizashi is called Banri Garan. It basically has no power. Its main purpose is as a royal artifact to prove Demon Lord status.”

Merlin didn’t tell Alice that Banri Garan could steal life—it was a secret known only to him and his sister, Lilith.

“Royal artifact?” Alice was full of questions, having never heard of such a thing.

“Each of the Seven Great Lords of the demon race has their own royal artifact to prove their Demon Lord status. Royal artifacts are symbols of status within the demon race, not for fighting. They’re like the sacred objects enshrined in temples,” Merlin explained briefly.

“Then how come…?” Alice had three black lines on her head, wanting to say something but holding back.

“What’s the point of a weapon? It’s not like you keep it to have babies,” Merlin said with a straight face.

“Eh…?” Alice broke out in cold sweat, saying seriously, “You’re no longer a Demon Lord. Is it really okay to bring such a thing out of the Demon Lord Palace?”

“No problem. Taking it out and using it won’t kill me,” Merlin said, his face thickening with audacity. “Hehe~!”

Alice’s face darkened, and her heart trembled as she thought, Of course there’s a big connection! It’s going to be really troublesome!

“However, the royal artifact of the First Demon Lord Palace is a bit special. It was passed down from the first Lucifer. Anyone who can’t draw Banri Garan won’t be recognized as the Proud Lord,” Merlin said in a slightly somber tone.

“Eh?! It’s not something just anyone can draw?” Alice was surprised.

“Hah, try it yourself,” Merlin casually threw the wakizashi at Alice’s hip.

Alice hastily caught it and gave Merlin a disapproving look.

She carefully observed Banri Garan. She had seen Merlin use it many times, but this was the first time she had touched it up close.

It looked completely ordinary, like a common weapon bought from a roadside stall.

Alice gripped the hilt and tried to pull it out, but it didn’t budge at all! ?

Unwilling to give up, she used high-level fighting spirit and tried her best to pull the sword, her face turning red and her body trembling, but it was completely ineffective.

Alice angrily returned Banri Garan to Merlin, feeling quite displeased.

“What a strange weapon.”

“Now do you believe me?” Merlin placed the sword back at his hip, smiling ambiguously. “Actually, your rapier is of much higher quality than my sword.”

“I don’t see that. My weapon is effective against dark creatures. Usually, dark creatures get burned just by touching it, but it doesn’t seem to affect you at all,” Alice said, deflated, remembering how Merlin had handled her Light Elegy a year ago without any issues.

“It’s not like it has no effect…” Merlin extended his hand. “Give me your rapier.”

“Here,” Alice threw the rapier to Merlin. She had just examined his weapon, so it was fine for him to examine hers.

“An rare weapon. Even just holding it, I can feel a slight rejection, like a light aura,” Merlin touched the Light Elegy rapier and found it quite nice.

Alice raised her eyebrows. Normally, dark creatures couldn’t even touch it, but Merlin only felt rejection?

Merlin thought for a moment, then directly grasped the blade with his bare hand and pulled the rapier, allowing it to cut his palm.

“Hey!” Alice was startled. What was Merlin doing harming himself for?

After cutting his palm, Merlin looked at the wound, which was sizzling and emitting white smoke. He thought, Right, I’m definitely a demon…

“See? It’s not like it has no effect at all,” Merlin returned the rapier to Alice.

Alice took the weapon and looked at it. There was indeed Merlin’s blood evaporating from the blade. So it only worked if it actually injured him, while normal dark creatures would be pierced just by touching it… Merlin looked at his wound and frowned, a slight doubt creeping in. His blood was evaporating. As a demon, Merlin’s self-healing ability was quite good. The wound had healed, but it left a faint scar. What the hell? How did it leave a scar? The Church’s holy water and blessed silver items had no effect on him. Merlin looked up at the slightly呆萌 (dull) Alice and felt a little worried—there was something unusual about that sword. It wasn’t an ordinary thing. This Alice… would she be able to threaten his life in the future? = =(一"一)

title: Chapter 13 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 13 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 4 · Chapter 13

Merlin looked at Alice's dazed expression and then shook his head-
How is that possible?
How could this idiot possibly become my opponent?
Not to mention intelligence, just based on strength he doesn't even qualify to be my opponent.
Even if Alice has a divine artifact in hand, what then?
It's hard to say whether you can even touch me.
Merlin swallowed his worries and completely looked down on Alice.
However, that slender sword is indeed strange, able to leave a scar on myself? It must definitely not be an ordinary item.
Moreover, there is a repressed aura of light; no matter how you think, it's not an ordinary rare weapon, but rather seems to have its original form sealed.
Alice felt a little pleased: 'The Light Chant' works on Merlin this demon, that's good news.
Thinking about it, this sword is the teacher's collection, though I've never seen her use it; apparently it still works against Demon Lord-level Merlin, just not obviously—probably because Merlin is just too strong.
Merlin looked at Alice, not intending to delve into the origin of the 'Light Chant', and said, 'Your weapon is quite nice, though it seems sealed; do you know that yourself?'
‘Eh?!’ Alice blinked, embarrassed, and said, ‘....I know, this sword is what I stole from my teacher.’
‘Just say it seriously already…’ Merlin broke out in large beads of sweat on his forehead.
‘My teacher has many hidden swords, but only this one is placed in a very secret spot, and its appearance is the most beautiful. At the time I thought this slender sword matched my flower-like beauty, so I stole it, and unexpectedly it was quite easy.’ Alice said with interest.
Merlin's expression froze on his face, thinking 'Pfft, flower-like beauty,' at this moment he even forgot to praise himself—after all, whether one is strong is just a patch, while being handsome is a lifetime matter....
‘It’s actually sealed…’ Alice furrowed her brows, thinking she needs to find the teacher about this, but she doesn’t want to see her, maybe she’ll be dragged back to the Alps.
‘Alright, stop talking useless stuff, come on, give it your all.’ Merlin raised his wooden sword, not looking like he’s fighting, more like teasing Alice, ‘I’ll give you a preventive shot first—my strength has nothing to do with the demon sword Banri Garan; frankly, give me a broken branch and I’ll use the draw‑cut slash to instantly wipe out your hundred‑thousand Crusade Army.’
‘I’m not a Hero now, don’t call us “you guys.”’ Alice said unhappily, raising her slender sword, seeming a bit eager.
‘Think about how you were caught by me to be a laborer, stripped naked on the beach for some play—doesn’t that make you want to get revenge?’
Merlin threw out a few trash talk lines, heavily stimulating Alice’s pride: ‘If you feel humiliated, come get revenge, little washboard.’
‘Tsk!’ Alice clicked her tongue, veins jumping on her forehead.
Regarding Merlin’s claim that he could exert power with just a branch, Alice still had a bit of disbelief, because it was too exaggerated.
Merlin has no magic or battle aura, not relying on the power of the demon sword Banri Garan, so what could it be?
Could Merlin himself be that strong? Alice doubted it.
Actually Merlin isn’t strong; it’s just that his F‑rank Draw‑Cut Slash skill at level 9999 is massively boosted: no exaggeration, no understatement—whoever he slashes dies.
Alice thought Merlin using a wooden sword was a rare chance; maybe she could get revenge and defeat this bastard.
Then she’d use her high‑heeled boots to ruthlessly stomp Merlin’s smelly face, venting her anger.
Let Merlin, who usually bullies her, finally have a chance now.
Alice felt a bit excited, and thus began to act in a somewhat foolish manner.
She waved her hand, high‑rank magical power surged, releasing the high‑rank spell ‘Frost Heaven’s Judgment’.
Then Alice suddenly accelerated, gripping her slender sword and charging at Merlin.
Above Merlin appeared a huge frost sword, which came crashing down!
Then Merlin didn’t move at all; the frost sword reached his forehead and directly dissipated, turning into waves of cold air.
Merlin tilted his mouth and said lightly, ‘You really don’t learn, do you? You know I’m magic‑immune, yet you still use magic? Come on, bring real blades.’
Alice’s brows knit tight, feeling Merlin’s ‘magic immunity’ is genuine and very troublesome.
Even now Alice couldn’t figure out how Merlin did it; if the fact of his magic immunity were spread, probably nobody would believe it.
After all, it’s too abnormal; having magic immunity is like directly disabling mages—no matter what magic, it will be outright ignored.
What elf magic, draconic language magic—if it can’t hit a person, what’s the difference between that and trash?
However, Alice wasn’t panicking; the Frost Heaven’s Judgment was originally just meant to draw Merlin’s attention.
Alice had already closed in to Merlin’s front, directly unleashing her strongest technique at this stage, ‘Extreme Ice Three‑Strike’.
The slender sword in her hand instantly condensed a layer of ice crystal, filled with magic and battle aura; upon attack it directly released, producing explosive power.
‘Take this!’
Alice’s attack fiercely unleashed a strike; her slender sword instantly brought forth countless sword blossoms, silver light bursting forth.
‘Too slow.’
Merlin used his wooden sword to easily block Alice’s attack, still not forgetting to toss out a taunt.
Alice felt her body a bit off‑balance; after training her swordsmanship for so long, she was easily neutralized by Merlin’s wooden sword, and this bastard’s relaxed demeanor showed he wasn’t even using full strength.
Immediately afterward she unleashed the second segment; the flickering silver light of her slender sword sealed Merlin’s eyes.
‘Looks flashy, but it’s useless....
Merlin used his wooden sword to flick aside Alice’s slender sword, pushing her back.
This contemptuous attitude stung Alice’s pride a bit; after honing her swordsmanship for so long, she felt she couldn’t even touch Merlin.
Stubborn Alice refused to lose; finally she unleashed the third segment, a straight thrust aimed at Merlin’s heart.
‘Die, you bastard!’
‘Heh…..
Merlin gave a cold snort, his wooden sword swept sideways, striking Alice’s hand, making her cry out; her slender sword fell to the ground, feeling like a scorpion sting, painful enough to bring tears.
‘What’s the essence of the big snow mountain? Just this level.’
book,SFA
Merlin felt like he was bullying a kid, so boring.
He didn’t even need any moves; just striking her weak points made her kneel.
Merlin backhandedly returned his wooden sword to its place, assumed the draw‑cut slash stance, and without courtesy abruptly drew the blade; that killing intent instantly exploded, attacking the flustered Alice.
‘Uh!’ Alice widened her eyes, feeling a familiar pressure, a sense of inevitable death welling up, making her soul feel as if plunged into an ice cellar.
It turned out to be true—Merlin’s strength has nothing to do with the demon sword; even a wooden sword carries the same menace.
Waves of near‑death threat stimulated Alice’s potential; in an instant, her high‑rank pressure surged upward considerably, trying to escape the draw‑cut slash.
But it was useless; the draw‑cut attack was faster than perception.
‘Yah!’ Alice screamed, instantly collapsing to the ground, her forehead turning red.
‘Eh?!’ Merlin accidentally knocked Alice out with a stick, she fainted straight away; his face darkened, full of shock.
emmm.....
Sorry.
I really didn’t mean to hit Alice.
Just now my hand slipped.

title: Chapter 14 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 14 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 4 · Chapter 14

Merlin had already controlled the power of his Drawn Sword Slash to the absolute minimum, N times smaller than when he fought Old Taylor, basically posing no life-threatening danger.

But at the crucial moment when he was trying to pull back his strike, because he wasn't used to the wooden sword, his hand slipped and he bonked Alice right on the head, knocking her unconscious.

As a Great Demon Lord, Merlin could obviously control the power of his Drawn Sword Slash perfectly, exercising complete restraint, but a slip of the hand was not his fault.

Merlin looked down at the unconscious Alice, dense cold sweat and vein-lines appearing on his forehead.

By the looks of it, she wouldn't be waking up before nightfall, and when she did, she would be in a bad mood.

Merlin hoisted Alice onto his shoulder and silently left the dojo—

"Forget it, let's go home..."

Evening.

"Guuuuuu..."

Alice had changed into lounge clothes, sitting at the dining table with her arms wrapped around her knees, looking very insecure.

Her eyes were glistening with tears, looking extremely pitiful, her small mouth curled into a pout as she emitted a series of choked sobs, her petite body shivering.

She looked very wronged, making people feel sorry for Alice.

Most noticeable of all was the band-aid on Alice's forehead; it seemed she was injured.

This was put on quickly by Merlin after he carried Alice home, probably to ease his guilt over slipping and knocking her out.

Alice felt very angry. They had agreed it would be fine, and yet he still bonked her with the stick. Not a shred of trustworthiness. As expected of a filthy demon!

"Merlin... you bastard, how dare you hit me? Waaaah—"

Merlin was cooking in the kitchen at this moment, wearing an apron, making him look like a devoted family man.

If anyone saw him in this state, they would never believe he had hit his wife.

Actually, Merlin was slightly uneasy inside. Hitting Alice by accident was definitely his fault; he couldn't let her grab onto this and start infringing on his living space, coming up with some bizarre household rules.

But what you fear is what comes. Hearing Alice's complaints, Merlin's heart skipped a beat and he turned around in surprise and said—

"What? Hit my wife? Am I the type of guy who hits his wife? Whoever dares to slander me deserves a beating."

"Get lost, I'm not your damn wife, stop taking advantage of me..." Alice bit her lip and said with red eyes.

"Oh come on~" Merlin shamelessly said with a grin, "I didn't do it on purpose, can you stop holding grudges against me?"

"You did it on purpose, you bastard!" Tears began to well up in Alice's eyes, "It's definitely because I yelled at you this morning, and now you're holding a grudge and taking revenge on me on purpose, waaah..."

"I'm not that bored. It was just that wooden sword being a bit slippery..." Merlin tried to sweep it under the rug, acting nonchalant, "Next time I'll definitely be careful, and we can still play together happily~"

"Play your big head!" Alice was so infuriated by Merlin's words, "I will never believe you again! You demon! An unreliable fellow! You said nothing would happen, and yet you still hit me, eep eep eep..."

Merlin glanced at the band-aid on Alice's forehead, feeling a wave of awkwardness inside. He didn't do it on purpose; getting hit once wouldn't kill her.

"Weren't I doing it so you could reach Saint-tier sooner, so the two of us could become free people?"

"Then what was the point of hitting me?" Alice stared at Merlin with a resentful gaze and said angrily, "You got me a job, you let me live in my house out of kindness, and yet... and yet you still hit me? Is there no humanity left?!"

"Please, the job was because I saved you, and the housing is because splitting rent is more cost-effective, stop making it sound like I owe you a favor, okay?" Merlin sighed and said helplessly.

"Gu..." Alice was speechless, letting out a whimper from her throat.

"Oh come on~" Merlin came out of the kitchen, carrying the pot of soup and placing it in front of Alice, "I swear I didn't do it on purpose, can you stop dwelling on it? How many people beg me for guidance and I refuse them. You should feel honored, right?"

"G, u, N!" Alice had a belly full of grievances, and her forehead was still throbbing faintly.

"Tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue, thinking this darn woman was really troublesome.

"I don't care, you're doing all the housework for this week, or else I can't live like this anymore. We're breaking up! You go live outside!"

"Miss, wasn't I acting out of kindness? This behavior of yours makes me very unhappy..." Merlin was losing patience.

"Then leave! I was living fine on my own, you're the one who insisted on squeezing in." Alice's eyes were red, tears still lingering at the corners.

"......" Merlin nodded, mentally agreeing and preparing to slip away as soon as the work started.

"Hmph~!" Alice let out an indignant snort.

Merlin opened the lid of the pot he was cooking. It was potato stewed beef.

His cooking skills were actually quite good, and being a transmigrator, many of his perspectives differed from the people of this world, making him quite adept at eating.

Though Merlin rarely cooked himself; he was only forced to by the shared living situation, otherwise he would absolutely never pick up a frying pan.

The broth was still bubbling and burbling. The potatoes were cut into small cubes, a golden yellow, and the soft beef was bouncing around, obviously stewed for a long time, making anyone who saw it lose their appetite.

Alice silently swallowed. Just looking at it made it seem delicious. "...What is this?"

"Potato stewed beef." Merlin ladled some into Alice's plate.

"...There's also this kind of thing?" Alice had never seen it; she had absolutely never seen anyone put potatoes and beef together.

"Haven't had it before?" Merlin revealed a playful smile, remembering how Lilith's eyes had turned into little stars when she ate it for the first time.

"O-of course not!" Alice's face flushed red and she quickly explained, "I've eaten it many times, hmph~!"

"......" Merlin smiled, thinking—this is another world, how could she have eaten it?

"Looks decent, I'll reluctantly taste it then." Alice found an excuse for herself, then lowered her head, sticking out her small tongue to lick a bit of the broth. Suddenly her eyes lit up. It was so delicious, tasting wonderful.

"What kind of eating method is that? Do you think you're a cat?" Merlin frowned, unable to bear watching Alice.

"I was afraid you'd poison it, so I'm testing it first!" Alice retorted dissatisfied.

A drop of cold sweat streamed down Merlin's forehead, thinking—would he need to poison Alice if he wanted to get rid of her? That wooden bat earlier, if he had applied just a little more force, he would have done it...

Alice picked up her spoon and took a small bite of potato and beef, and she immediately lost control, as if she had discovered a new world—

What is this? !

Is this still a potato?

Wow! Soft and melt-in-the-mouth.

It even carried a hint of refreshing fragrance.

The best part was this beef, which melted upon entering the mouth.

The rich meat aroma surged forth, creating an indescribable sensation!

It's so delicious! A warm feeling spread throughout her body.

Alice's eyes sparkled as if she had discovered a new world, having never eaten anything this delicious before!

She never expected this guy to cook so well, it was too surprising.....

Alice cleared her throat, slightly covering up her embarrassment.

"...How about you skip the housework..."

"Hm?" Merlin frowned, not understanding.

"H-how about just making dinner for a week instead." Alice swallowed and became a greedy cat.

Merlin smiled, took off his apron, and said faintly—

"Please enjoy!"

title: Chapter 15
content:
Chapter 15

Volume 4 · Chapter 15

The next day.

Alice left Merlin behind and went to the dojo alone for her training.

She said Merlin was untrustworthy and didn't want him to be her sparring partner anymore, worried he'd knock her out with a staff again.

Merlin thought Alice was making a mountain out of a molehill; he would just need to pay attention and wouldn't hit her.

Although Merlin was in the late stages of his lazy cancer, he wasn't completely indifferent to everything.

Especially Alice reaching Saint-tier — it was important for both of them.

So Merlin wasn't willing to give up and planned to try persuading Alice again tonight to accept his private training.

After all, he was the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace, the strongest ruler of the demon race, someone whose sneeze could make the human world tremble.

And now he was trailing after a former Hero, shamelessly begging to coach her!?

If the other demons found out, they'd drop their jaws in shock, and might even mock him for sticking his warm face against someone's cold butt.

He thought about having some dignity. He had no designs on Alice; he just wanted to tutor her so this foolish girl could reach Saint-tier sooner.

What did Alice have anyway!? Nothing! Absolutely nothing!

Some clueless gossips might say Merlin was after Alice's looks?

Please~. Putting aside the fact that Merlin was over 200 years old and entirely repulsed by the idea of sex with women...

Merlin would admit Alice's face and figure were nice, but he'd deduct 100 points for the flat chest, and another 100 for her terrible temper and personality.

How could a woman rated negative in his mind possibly arouse his interest?

Merlin's reason for wanting to be Alice's sparring partner was simple — it was all for making a living.

The two of them had been living together for several days now, managing to scrape by.

But Merlin still found Alice's personality somewhat annoying. She was too spoiled, prickly all over, making him uncomfortable.

The other night, after Alice finished her bath, she seemed to forget to grab her slippers and told Merlin to bring them to her.

At that time, Merlin was sitting on the sofa in a full "Ge You slump," his laziness flaring up and refusing to move, so he ignored Alice.

That girl, instead, stormed out of the bathroom in her yukata, her pink bare feet leaving wet footprints all over the floor.

Since she'd soaked in hot water, Alice's legs had a faint pinkish flush, and Merlin watched with mild interest.

"What are you looking at!? Watch your damn eyes! Pervert! Remember this — if you ever forget something next time, I'm not helping you either!"

Merlin got scolded repeatedly by Alice and endured several eye-roll attacks, feeling absolutely miserable inside.

He didn't owe Alice anything. Why should he help her? He was a roommate, not a male servant!

When Alice saw Merlin ignoring her, she fumed and, before leaving, kicked him squarely on the butt with her little foot, then happily went back to her room to sleep.

At that moment, Merlin was so annoyed with Alice that if his laziness hadn't been in full force, he would've gotten up and pinned her onto the sofa. Who dares kick the Great Demon Lord with their foot? They were bold indeed.

Although daily life was full of friction, circumstances forced them to make do. What else could they do? Break up?

Alice went to the dojo alone to train, and Merlin didn't want to stay idle at home, so he went to the Adventurers Guild to drink and brag with Hobbs, along with his traditional entertainment —

horse racing.

Inside the guild, people came and went.

Everyone looked busy, but there were still those lazy members around.

That would be Merlin and Hobbs, two Iron-rank guys hanging out together, drinking and watching the live broadcast from the Royal Racecourse.

"Hobbs, what you said wasn't accurate at all. Even though I bet on Richard, I still lost."

Merlin was in low spirits, staring gloomily at the horse racing ticket in his hand. He'd listened to Hobbs and bet on Richard, but the result was laughable — he lost everything.

Merlin's life was tight right now. Not only had Alice taken his money to pay for rent, but even his discretionary spending money was a pitiful single gold coin.

And yet, Merlin still threw that one gold coin into the racecourse, and in the end, he didn't even hear a sound of winning.

They say nine out of ten gamblers lose, but Merlin — a guy who loses ten out of ten — just couldn't keep his hands off it. He dreamed day and night of turning things around.

Hobbs, drinking nearby, patted Merlin on the shoulder. "It's fine! Don't be a coward! Bet on Richard again next time! You'll definitely win it back!"

"Never mind. Your words are too fake. Next time I'll try betting on Grandy." Merlin crumpled the horse racing ticket and tossed it aside, then took a melancholy sip of beer. He felt cursed — his luck was terrible, and he lost every time he gambled!

"Don't lose heart~. You can't win all the time. Losing twice is normal," Hobbs comforted Merlin.

"Stop it. This isn't about one or two times. In the past year, I've played nearly 200 times and haven't won a single copper coin."

Merlin said it flatly, feeling exhausted inside and out.

"Hobbs stared wide-eyed, somewhat startled. A normal person would've made back some money after 200 tries. Merlin's situation... wasn't he favored by the Goddess of Misfortune? That was incredibly rare."

Old Headmaster Taylor slightly opened his eyes, paying close attention to Merlin's every move.

Yesterday, he'd heard Merlin and Alice were training at the dojo and wanted to observe, but he was tied up with affairs and couldn't make it, which left him somewhat regretful.

Today he saw Merlin so persistent about horse racing, and couldn't help but think...

Horse racing, huh?

Presumably a unique form of training.

It could instantly sharpen one's mental spirit, teaching emotional detachment from all outcomes.

As expected of Merlin. This old man seems to have learned something new again...

It appeared Headmaster Taylor was overthinking things. If this continued, the great martial arts master would inevitably be led down the wrong path by Merlin sooner or later.

"It doesn't matter. Bad luck is always temporary. You have to believe that rainbows come after storms. Try a few more times, and you'll see the dawn eventually." Hobbs kept encouraging Merlin, speaking very inspiringly.

"But where would I get the money to try a few more times? This hard-earned money was taken by Alice, that vampire." Merlin sighed worriedly and began drowning his sorrows in drink.

"I almost forgot — you're part of the Wifedom Club now. You can't be as free as before." Hobbs gave him a sympathetic look.

"We're not actually married. Don't misunderstand." Merlin couldn't resist clarifying.

"Come on. Now that you both wear the Couple Adventurer certificate, any explanation is pointless. Everyone thinks you're husband and wife already."

Hobbs swayed his cup and said casually, "Besides, Miss Alice isn't bad at all. Though her popularity isn't as high as that scheming Luqia, they still give it back and forth evenly."

"Huh? Don't joke. If Miss Luqia thrust her chest forward, Alice would immediately feel inferior, spit blood, and die on the spot." Merlin chuckled, finding the image hilarious.

"Your chest can't fully reflect a person's worth. Alice's personality is cuter than Luqia's, don't you think?" Hobbs raised an eyebrow.

"Hobbs let out a nervous laugh, finding Alice's personality anything but cute — only annoying."

"Besides, after the Deathlock incident in Derbyshire, Alice has already become somewhat famous in Wales. Just now, a purple-haired beauty came up to ask about her." Hobbs grinned.

"Who?" Merlin asked curiously.

"That one—"

Hobbs turned his head to point behind him, but couldn't see anyone. "Huh!? Damn, she was sitting right there a moment ago. Where did she go?"

Merlin looked in the direction Hobbs pointed but saw no one.

He only saw an empty table with a cup of steaming coffee that hadn't been finished—

A purple-haired woman...

Who was she?
