One night, after Malygos had consumed too much fake alcohol, he had loosely discussed the matter of inheritance crystallizations with Carolna, and inadvertently mentioned that he possessed one in his brain.

Carolna had desperately wanted the inheritance crystallization from Malygos's brain, but being unable to defeat that Divine Dragon, she had been forced to give up.

But the situation was different now. Malygos had been killed in a single blow by Merlin, and Carolna had finally obtained what she had dreamed of.

With the inheritance crystallization in her possession, Carolna became incredibly excited, her eyes revealing a morbid obsession.

Without any hesitation, she placed the crystallization directly into her mouth, swallowed hard, and downed it!

"Huh?! " Merlin was taken aback, his expression stunned, wondering whether actually swallowing it raw was really fine.

After Carolna swallowed it, she seemed to show no immediate reaction — but upon channeling Saint-tier斗气 to activate it, she still managed to unleash some of the crystallization's power.

"AAAAAAHHHHH!"

Carolna bent double, clutching her abdomen and screaming — she seemed to be in excruciating pain, the veins across her body bulging and pulsing, her appearance becoming as ferocious as if she had entered a frenzy.

An ice-blue torrent flashed across her pupils, transforming them into the dragon clan's distinctive golden, slitted pupils — snake-like eyes extremely similar to Malygos's.

A biting cold aura began erupting from Carolna's body, sending wave after wave of shockwaves rippling outward.

Merlin raised his hand to shield himself from the fierce blizzard and watched Carolna after she had consumed the inheritance crystallization.

According to ancient demon clan texts, inheritance crystallizations needed to be slowly digested to achieve the best stabilizing effect.

Carolna doing this was simply reckless — she hadn't even absorbed the crystallization's power at all, merely forcing forth a portion of it through her Saint-tier斗气.

So Merlin had no worries. However Carolna had swallowed it, he had ways to make her spit it back out.

Although it was only a fraction of its power, it was still more than enough for an ordinary person — she might even be dominated by dragon power, transformed into a frenzied killing machine.

But Merlin knew that all power came with a price. What Carolna was doing now probably meant she would never want to remain human again.

The cold aura surrounding Carolna grew denser and denser, the blizzard becoming increasingly violent. After the pain subsided, her body began to change——

Her figure grew taller and more imposing, bursting through and tearing apart her clothes to reveal the undead's rotting flesh beneath.

Dense blue dragon scales emerged across her body, covering most of her form and obscuring even her secrets.

Her limbs transformed into dragon claws — her hardened hands no longer needed any weapon. But all of these changes upon a human frame were not beautiful at all; she looked more like a biochemical monster, especially her feet, which were truly a foot-enthusiast's nightmare.

Finally, a pair of dragon membranous wings erupted from her back, slowly unfurling with impressive power!

Carolna stared at her golden pupils, looking at her sharp claws and her strong, unscarred body, deeply pleased with her current transformations.

"This is dragon clan power? It feels absolutely wonderful..."

title: Chapter 52 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 52 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 4 · Chapter 52

In the wind and snow.

Carolona transformed into a dragon-like being, her purple hair turning silver-white and fluttering in the wind.

"I have never felt myself alive before, but now the feeling of being alive is incredibly real."

"I can finally sense many living things; my sensory sensitivity is tens of thousands of times stronger than that of humans."

"All of this is- a legacy crystal bringing me this; if I can fully control it, my strength might surpass this dimension!"

"How wonderful is the power of the great dragon race? Something humans absolutely cannot compare to....

Carolona's dragon wings behind her suddenly vibrated, sending her soaring to ten thousand feet in the air.

At extreme speed, her silhouette turned into a blue-white streak of light.

Her golden pupils could see a child tens of thousands of meters deep in the forest, and her ears could hear the noise of a bustling city millions of meters away.

Carolona grew more excited, feeling explosive power filling her whole body, - - at that moment she felt like the 'god' of the entire world, an unparalleled existence, the pinnacle of all races!

"Hahahahaha.....

Carolona's laughter echoed through the sky, as if a demon from hell had regained freedom.

"The power of the dragon race! Amazing! A feeling I've never experienced before!"

"I am not human! I am the strongest existence in this world! A lofty deity!

"Who could possibly defeat someone as beautiful as me? Such a person doesn't exist, for right now I am the strongest species!"

Merlin calmly looked up at Carolona in the sky, understanding her madness—weaklings always act this way after gaining a bit of power, blinded by the illusion of strength, thinking they are the world's strongest, just like a petty citizen who won five million in the lottery.

"or"I了U

The dragon-transformed Carolona slowly descended to Merlin's head, her face bearing a contemptuous smile, as if looking down on a tiny ant.

She suddenly waved her hand and split the earth in two, rumbling apart, revealing a bottomless canyon beneath Mount Bennieweis.

The corpse of the Frost Holy Dragon happened to be on that line, directly falling into the mysterious abyss, impossible to trace.

The earth shook violently, yet Merlin remained unmoved, facing the dragon-transformed Carolona.

"Mortal, for my current overwhelming strength, what do you think?"

"No particular thoughts, just feeling you are extremely swollen, feeling good about yourself." Merlin said nonchalantly, thinking such people he had built many, but they all died from their own ignorance.

"I now have enough capital to despise you; with just a finger I can easily crush you, this weak ant without magic or battle aura~" Carolona's mindset had drastically changed, confidence bursting, she likely saw everyone as petty little fish.

"Oh, that strong?" Merlin feigned a tense expression, sensing Carolona was weaker than before Mariggos, yet she was swollen.

"Not just strong? I am now an existence that can rival gods in power!" Carolona's golden pupils burned like torches—"But I'm curious, why didn't you come earlier to interrupt me? Were you scared silly by me? Ha...."

"No, I treat all enemies this way, making them exert their full strength so they recognize their weakness and die without regret; the same applies to you." Merlin said expressionlessly, his attitude even worse than hers.

"Arrogant ant, do you deserve to say such things before me?!" Carolona's golden pupils flared with anger, shaking her dragon wings, instantly intensifying the blizzard.

."Ma'am, forgive my frankness, you are dazed by joy and have lost your reason." Merlin spoke a plain truth.

"Don't call me ma'am! I am now at my most beautiful form! The creator's crystal! The most beautiful creature in the world!" Carolona shouted, a faint dragon roar hidden within.

"Maybe my aesthetic is off? I think you look uglier than before." Merlin said embarrassedly, especially those feet, now dragon claws, utterly out of place on a human.

"Shut up! I will personally cut off your tongue, you scoundrel, so you can never speak again!" Carolona roared, then narrowed her eyes, "But before that, I have good news for you—your wife is in our hands? If you want her alive, bring the key you stole to the volcano on the Scottish border to exchange! If you come empty-handed, your wife is doomed..."

"Are you remnants of the former kingdom?" Merlin narrowed his eyes, instantly grasping much information—it seemed the key given to Da Vinci held great secrets, enough to make these people cling desperately, though Alice hadn't frozen to death in the "Ice River Descends" incident, which is also good news.

"Don't call us remnants; we are the legitimate!" Carolona emphasized seriously.

"Whatever.... Merlin waved his hand, lightly saying, " I want to tell you bad news—I and Alice are not married, do you really think I'd hand over the key for her? You're overestimating her place in my heart."

"You're truly heartless, I'm actually growing to like you more" Carolona soared into the air, her clawed hands faintly gripping, "Next I will perform a secret technique as a magic trick, silently cutting off your tongue without you noticing.

"Ha, then I'll perform a magic trick too—you will be counter-killed by me." Merlin said seriously, having no intention of letting Carolona go.

"Hmph, ignorant!" Carolona crossed her hands, golden battle aura blazing on her body, with a hint of dragon might, then suddenly spread out!

Carolona's secret technique is named "Black Annihilation Formation," using battle aura to create wide-range visual interference, putting enemies in a blinded state, seeing only pitch black, vision completely sealed.

This ultimate skill is Carolona's trump card and also the root of her legendary fame; often opponents don't know what happened before they are instantly severed head from body.

Four hundred years ago, Carolona relied on this secret technique to reach the peak of assassins, slaughtering seven Saint-tier experts in a single night without feeling any pressure.

Moreover, now Carolona has dragon power boosting her, her skills are no longer comparable.

"Eh? Something...." Merlin's vision went pitch black, like nightfall, seeing nothing, only hearing the whistling cold wind beside his ears.

He directly readied his sword-drawing stance, trying to locate Carolona's presence—though he is magic-immune, the interference from battle aura still works.

The pitch-black surroundings turned Merlin into a blind man, unable to see anything.

Although "Black Annihilation Formation" has no attack power, it is very practical.

Is it hard for a normal person to fight a blind one? Definitely not, and it's super easy. Actually

In fact, Carolona was already very close, her body flashing past Merlin's eyes, yet he didn't notice.

Ha! Can't see me? How does it feel to be a blind man? Arrogant bastard....

Carolona came behind Merlin, her hands wrapping around his face, sharp dragon claws glinting coldly, lunging at his mouth—

Look how you still call me ma'am?

I'll rip your mouth apart and take your tongue for myself! ! !

Merlin suddenly felt a chilling presence behind him, turning with inconceivable speed to unleash a sword-drawing slash!

The killing sword aura exploded, catching Carolona off guard.

Using stillness to counter movement, striking unexpectedly—the essence of the sword-drawing slash—Merlin executed it to perfection.

Although Carolona's senses and bodily speed had greatly increased, Merlin's sword-drawing slash was faster than any perception.

Carolona stared wide-eyed, utterly confused, her dragon-form body instantly split in two by Merlin's sword-drawing slash.

Merlin's lips curled, his ruby-like eyes filled with cold contempt, he said lightly—

"Truly a shame, no matter what you do, you're still too weak before me...

Factory-7)

title: Chapter 53 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 53 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 4 · Chapter 53

What's going on?

Why did he suddenly draw his sword?!

Dragon race power combined with my assassination techniques should have been overwhelmingly strong, but why...

Carolina's golden pupils lost focus, dying with questions in her eyes, and the soul fire of her base extinguished immediately.

"Arrogance isn't a good habit, auntie. You'd better obediently go to hell and reflect..."

Merlin spoke coldly, reached out his hand and grasped something in the splattered blood before him.

The two halves of dragon-transformed Carolina's corpse immediately fell to either side of Merlin, sinking into the thick snow.

Merlin spread his hands open, and the inheritance crystal of the Frost Sacred Dragon lay quietly in his palm, appearing utterly ordinary yet containing tremendous power.

"Alice is truly the darling goddess of luck..."

Merlin looked at the inheritance crystal and couldn't help but sigh, feeling that Alice was the kind of person whose wishes came true — the moment she needed something, it was express-shipped right over.

But this could be a good thing, it would greatly shorten the time until Alice reached Saint-tier.

Once she reached Saint-tier and became a Mithril-ranked adventurer, she would have the right to accept SSS-class quests.

Merlin tucked the inheritance crystal into his chest, feeling a glimmer of hope reignite for his future life of minding his own business and drifting along...

Far from the battlefield.

On an ice-encased tower, Zoe stood proudly.

The biting cold wind howled, blowing the bandages wrapped around his body.

Zoe's eyes were red and veined with血丝, as if he hadn't slept in a long time.

The unconscious Alice was tucked under his armpit, her silver-white long hair dragging on the ground.

Just now, when the Frost Ice Dragon's wide-area ultimate "Glacial Descent" struck, Alice would have died.

But Zoe felt this woman was an important hostage who couldn't die so easily, so he used his Saint-tier fighting aura to help resist the terrifying cold that swept toward them.

Plus, since they were positioned far from the center of the vortex of battle, the power of Glacial Descent had somewhat diminished, which is how Alice luckily escaped with her life.

At this moment, Zoe stood at a high place, looking down at the distant barren ground where Merlin stood in the vast sea of snow, countless towering ice spears rising from the ground, as if narrating the ferocity of the battle just now.

Zoe narrowed his eyes, staring fixedly at Merlin, gripping his straight sword at his waist tightly, and a fighting spirit rose in his heart. The thought of wanting to test his strength against him would not leave his mind. He had never left and witnessed the entire battle from afar just now...

Who is this man?

He feels really powerful!

Someone at Marigoss's level could be killed in a single slash!?

He didn't seem to be using his full strength either — he wasn't even taking this seriously.

And as for the dragon-transformed Carolina? What an idiot!

Obtaining a bit of dragon race power made her swell with arrogance, forgetting who she was?

She actually thought she had power comparable to a god? What a ridiculous delusion.

Isn't dragon race power truly that wonderful? To make Carolina's confidence swell to this extent...

Zoe stroked his chin, somewhat tempted to get his hands on the Frost Sacred Dragon's inheritance crystal and taste it himself.

But since it was currently in Merlin's hands — someone capable of instantly killing Marigoss — Zoe had to give up that thought.

Forget it, important matters first.

I should probably get this woman back to the base first.

Besides, this man's strength was rather terrifying.

Would my and my younger brother's fused ultimate technique be able to defeat him?

I'll definitely cross paths with this man again, and honestly, I'm a little looking forward to it.

Next time we meet, I hope this man can give my brother and me a good fight, don't die too easily, heh heh heh...

Zoe sneered, turned around, and silently recited an ancient incantation, causing a swirling black hole to appear before him.

He carried the unconscious Alice and slowly entered the black hole, most of his body already disappearing.

But just at that moment —

Zoe's arm was suddenly grabbed, as if bitten by some wild beast, unable to move an inch.

"Huh?"

Zoe had never encountered such a situation before. He turned around in astonishment, and when he saw who it was, cold sweat immediately poured down his forehead. His eyes filled with terror, feeling as though the Soul Reaper had fixed its gaze upon his soul, ready to drag him back to hell.

"Uh!?"

Merlin had appeared on top of the ice-encased尖塔 at some unknown moment. His face showed no expression whatsoever, and killing intent rushed toward him like a wave. Those red eyes had become extremely terrifying, making Zoe experience what a death threat truly felt like.

Damn it!

What was happening?!

Aren't he still so far away just now?!

How could he suddenly appear here!

What an terrifying movement speed!

Zoe's eyeballs were trembling nonstop, clearly panicking to a certain degree.

He felt that if he and his younger brother teamed up, they might still be able to fight Merlin, but by himself, he definitely couldn't be his match!

"Where are you taking my roommate?" Merlin frowned, his gaze cold. Under the sharp sea wind at such a height, a few strands of his hair were still tangled on his eyelashes.

Just now, Merlin had intended to leave, but he sensed a trace of magical fluctuation from here. Who could survive an attack of Glacial Descent and not be an ordinary person?

Fortunately, the distance wasn't far for Merlin's burst speed — in the blink of an eye, he had arrived right in front of Zoe!

"Answer me." Merlin said coldly, one hand reaching up to the katana at his waist, slowly pulling on Zoe's arm, attempting to drag his entire body out of the black hole.

Zoe saw Merlin about to draw his sword and immediately thought it was bad news — he was going to die!

So he quickly activated the black hole to disappear, trying to escape from this terrifying demon.

Merlin narrowed his eyes, seemingly seeing what Zoe was planning to do.

The black hole disappeared, and murderous sword intent erupted instantly!

Unfortunately, this draw-cut only severed the one bandage-wrapped arm of Zoe's, allowing him to successfully escape with the unconscious Alice.

Rather than saying it was Merlin who cut off his arm, it was more accurate to say Zoe himself gave it up, otherwise this draw-cut would have directly taken his life.

"Tch! A mere walking mummy, he sure knows how to run..."

Merlin clicked his tongue dissatisfied, glanced at the withered arm, and threw it onto the ground with annoyance.

He looked around, the entire village had been sealed by the cold wind and snow, turning into a no-man's-land.

The snow was falling heavier and heavier, gust after gust, the wind twisting the snowflakes in all directions, full of a deathly sense of gloom.

At this point, Merlin planned to go rescue Alice, and he already knew the location was the border volcano in Scotland.

Although Merlin had the ability to directly kill all the enemies and rescue Alice, there existed certain risks.

Now Alice was a hostage, and if she had been secretly fed some lurking poison, what use would it be to rescue her?

So for Alice's safety, it was better to obediently follow their demands.

It seems I must first return to Leksam and get the key back from Da Vinci...

Merlin wanted to rescue Alice not merely because they shared living expenses together, or because of the debt issue.

More importantly, there was a sense of anxiety and worry deep inside his heart — the steaming hot milk at night, and those slightly caring glances...

"Tch!" Merlin patted his own forehead and sighed, cursing himself —

"Am I a dog or something!?"

"Why can't I stop thinking about such a small favor?"

"If this continues, I'll sooner or later be led around by the nose by this troublesome woman..."

(-`0´-)

S■

Previous chapters had no problems.

I spent more than half a chapter describing Carolina's joy of obtaining power, with very obvious sentences.

Broken into separate paragraphs, with examples, explained through the mouths of both Merlin and Zoe.

Different ways of thinking, I can't explain it clearly. Would anyone not be inflated after winning fifty million in the lottery? Compared to Jack Ma, is it nothing? That guy hasn't even touched money, haha~

From now on I won't explain the plot anymore. If you can't understand it, just forget it. This volume is wrapping up anyway, starting a new volume tomorrow.

title: Chapter 1
content:
Chapter 1

Volume 5 · Chapter 1

The Scottish border volcano.

The hot magma flowed slowly underground, causing the entire temple ruins to tremble slightly.

A swirling black hole appeared in the air above the main hall, gradually expanding.

Zoi, carrying the unconscious Alice, fell down, looking extremely disheveled.

Cough, cough!

Zoi coughed incessantly, threw Alice to the side, and slowly got up on one hand, supporting himself on the ground.

His entire left arm had been cut off by Merlin, revealing rotting flesh and white bones, with sticky blood dripping onto the ground.

As an undead, Zoi's blood was all coagulated, with a faintly foul smell.

"Brother?"

A swordsman with a crying face mask and bandages all over his body walked in, stumbling and moving awkwardly, like his legs were inconvenient.

"What's wrong with you?"

Zoi asked.

"I encountered a monster and wasn't careful." Zoi's eyes were ferocious, with veins bulging on his body, as he tightly covered his severed arm to prevent the foul-smelling blood from splashing out.

"My brother is right," Joy said faintly.

"Ugh!" Zoi looked at his brother, who seemed like a puppet, and got angry, hitting Joy hard on the face, "You idiot! Is this the time to agree? Are you hoping I'll die?"

Joy's face was slapped, and his head twisted to an unbelievable extent, "My brother hit me, and it's right."

Zoi gritted his teeth, feeling that his brother had no humanity, and this mechanical agreement was full of ridicule.

"Joy, can't you speak normally?"

"My brother is right," Joy replied, his eyes blank.

"混账!" Zoi pulled out a section of his straight sword, almost beheading his brother.

"Zoi."

A slightly oppressive voice came from the depths of the temple, and a shadow holding a staff appeared in view.

The flickering firelight in the hall made Corpefil's shadow look enormous, exuding a sense of oppression.

"Your Majesty!" Zoi knelt on one knee, feeling uncomfortable with his empty left hand.

"Zoi, Carona's soul fire has gone out. Do you know what's going on?" Corpefil's voice was slightly old, and his repeated failures made him very tired.

The four heroes of the former kingdom were all strong enough to stand alone, but now they were falling one by one, as if some unknown powerful force was blocking them.

"Carona was killed by an adventurer, not just her, but also Marigold was killed together." Zoi replied seriously.

Even now, thinking back to Merlin killing the Frost Saint Dragon and Carona, Zoi felt a little frightened.

However, Zoi still thought that with his brother's fusion secret, they should have a chance to fight.

After all, it was a move famous for its attack power. If they faced it head-on, Merlin wouldn't die, but would be crippled.

Zoi thought that no human defense could be stronger than the Giant King.

Since Merlin could kill the Giant King, he was naturally a match for him.

"What?! Marigold is also dead?"

Corpefil's figure shook, obviously shocked and hard to believe.

The Frost Saint Dragon Marigold was one of the six Saint Dragons, with powerful strength that could intimidate a country!

But now he was killed by someone. Was there a legendary strongman hiding in Britain?!

If so, the great cause of reviving the former kingdom would be difficult.

"Is the person who stole the key really that strong?"

"He's a black iron adventurer," Zoi replied, seemingly seeing the adventurer's proof on Merlin's neck, which was indeed black iron.

"Ah?! " Corpefil exclaimed, as if he had heard something wrong.

A low-level black iron adventurer actually killed the Frost Saint Dragon. What was going on?!

It sounded like a joke. Were the villagers of Britain all descendants of Super Saiyans?!

"Your Majesty, although he's a black iron adventurer," Zoi said nervously, "his strength is indeed strong. I saw it with my own eyes. Marigold and Carona were no match for him. I'm afraid only my brother and I, using our fusion secret, could have a chance to win."

"My brother is right," Joy echoed.

"I thought Carona was a smart person, but..."

Corpefil had a headache, not expecting his careful actions to attract a powerful enemy.

However, it didn't matter. As long as he summoned the burning legion from hell, any strongman would be trampled under his iron hooves, and the revival of the former kingdom would be unstoppable.

Corpefil's emotions stabilized, feeling he hadn't lost yet. As long as he got the fourth key to the hell legion, he could instantly turn the situation around.

"This useless thing is dead, but the fourth key is still not retrieved!"

"Yes," Zoi said helplessly, knowing that without strong strength, taking something from Merlin would be extremely risky.

"Useless! All of you are useless! The situation is getting more and more urgent! We can't waste any more time!" Corpefil was furious, hitting the ground with his staff.

"Your Majesty, please calm down. Carona didn't die in vain. She left us a clue to the key," Zoi said, bowing his head.

"What clue?" Corpefil asked curiously.

"This woman..." Zoi pointed to the unconscious Alice, "they stole the key. Now she's our hostage. Carona told her husband to bring the key to ransom her. We just need to wait."

"Will that person come?" Corpefil had a doubt, worried that if he didn't come to ransom her, he would lose everything.

Zoi recalled Merlin's crimson eyes like a death god, and a cold sweat dropped from his forehead, "He will come. My arm was cut off by that adventurer. It's clear how much he cares about his wife."

"Is it? It seems our dream hasn't been shattered yet. Our temporary passivity will change the moment the fourth key falls into our hands!" Corpefil opened his arms, and his burning ambition still hadn't extinguished.

"Yes, Your Majesty," Zoi bowed his head.

"My brother is right," Joy echoed stiffly.

Corpefil approached Zoi, his face hidden under his black robe, only his withered hands exposed.

"Zoi, let me repair your arm?"

"No, thank you, Your Majesty," Zoi refused.

"Why?" Corpefil asked curiously.

"When that black iron adventurer brings the key, I'll kill him personally! I'll cut off his arm and sew it onto my body as my eternal achievement!" Zoi said fiercely, with a strong fighting intent.

"You are indeed the most excellent swordsman of our kingdom. I am proud of you!" Corpefil's black robe fluttered, and he pointed to the unconscious Alice with his withered hand.

"Lock this woman up with the elf in the dungeon!"

"When her husband comes to ransom her, it will be the end of Great Britain!"

"All enemies that hinder our great cause will be burned to ashes by the flames of hell!"

title: Chapter 2 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 2 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 5 · Chapter 2

A damp and gloomy dungeon.

It had been an unknown amount of time since...

Although the temple was located on a volcano, the air in the dungeon was not dry.

The sound of dripping water echoed through the narrow space, creating an eerie atmosphere.

"Mmm..."

The sound of a girl sobbing and choking back tears reverberated through the dark dungeon, a sorrowful and mournful sound like the cry of a cuckoo in the dead of night.

Who was crying?

A young girl?

Alice, who had been unconscious, slowly regained her senses, her head throbbing in pain as she lay on the cold ground.

Her long eyelashes fluttered, and she tiredly opened her eyes, her blue pupils gradually regaining their sparkle.

What she saw was a dilapidated floor covered in moss, with water dripping from the roof into a puddle.

Although torches flickered, casting a dim glow, the dungeon was still shrouded in darkness.

Alice felt a dull ache all over her body, and she slowly sat up, her head spinning.

Her face was smeared with dust, and her silver hair, usually so lustrous, was now dull and lackluster.

Where was she? This wasn't her home.

Alice looked around, feeling uneasy, and rubbed her sore forehead, trying to recall some memories.

Ah, yes, she had been knocked out by a strange woman, a thief from a former kingdom, it seemed.

They had wanted to use her as a hostage to coerce Merlin into handing over a mysterious key.

So, she must have been taken to this unknown place.

What was she going to do now? She was a hostage, and things looked grim.

Alice frowned, feeling anxious, and decided she couldn't just sit around waiting; she had to think of a way to escape.

She looked at the iron cage in front of her and thought it wasn't too sturdy; if she used her high-level fighting spirit, she could easily break free.

But when she tried to summon her fighting spirit, she found it was sealed, and she couldn't muster even a little bit of power.

She was shocked and quickly checked her body for anything that might be restricting her magic or fighting spirit.

And then she saw it: an iron ring around her neck, which wouldn't budge easily.

This was the kind of thing she had worn on the Redbeard pirate ship before, which made her a normal person, unable to use any magic or fighting spirit.

Alice felt deflated, her shoulders slumping; it seemed she was at the mercy of others now.

Could Merlin come to rescue her?

Or was he too busy enjoying himself, occupying her bed, and laughing with glee?

It was possible, given Merlin's carefree and selfish nature; he might not even care about her fate.

Alice covered her forehead with her hand, feeling the situation was becoming dire; apart from Merlin, she didn't know who else could rescue her.

As for her teacher on the Snowy Mountain, she had no idea where she had wandered off to.

That key was a big trouble; she shouldn't have listened to Merlin's persuasion and hidden it.

Whenever she and Merlin got together, nothing good ever came of it.

The remnants of the former kingdom were so obsessed with this key, obviously hiding a big secret, or maybe even treasure.

If the key really did lead to untold riches, Merlin, that scoundrel, would probably choose to keep it all to himself.

Then he would pay off their debts, take her savings from under her bed, and live a happy and carefree life.

Indeed, demons were not to be trusted.

Alice's eyes welled up with tears, and the more she thought about it, the more frightened she became; her slender body trembled like a small, abandoned kitten in the iron cage, pitiful.

Their shared debt was the only connection between them; if Merlin got his hands on endless wealth, that connection would be severed, and he would definitely not come to rescue her.

Alice didn't consider Merlin a good person, but rather someone driven solely by profit, who wouldn't bother with sentiment; after all, he was a cold-blooded demon.

However, a glimmer of hope remained in her heart: if the key wasn't treasure, Merlin would surely come to rescue her, unwilling to shoulder the debt alone.

Alice clasped her hands together and began to pray, or rather, curse.

"Oh, dear god, let Merlin be poor all his life, and never let him turn his life around."

The damp and musty smell of the dungeon made Alice uncomfortable, and she couldn't help but frown; just then, a faint sobbing sound came from the darkness beside her.

"Mmm..."

"Eh?"

Alice looked at the side, surprised; in the dark cell, it seemed she wasn't alone; there was someone else there.

"Mmm..."

The muffled sound was very soft, almost inaudible unless you listened closely.

Alice thought it was no wonder she had heard a girl crying earlier; it seemed there was indeed someone else in this cramped cell.

As she moved closer, aided by the faint torchlight, she finally managed to see the girl in the corner.

She wore a relatively luxurious blue long dress, now torn and dirty.

The jewelry she wore seemed expensive, clearly not from an ordinary family.

Her wrist was covered in scars and wounds, which looked numerous and disturbing.

Her golden hair lay scattered on the ground, mixed with grass and twigs, making her look disheveled.

This appearance suggested she had been imprisoned for a long time, tormented to the point of being unrecognizable.

But what caught her attention most were the long, pointed ears, which immediately revealed her identity.

"An elf?"

Alice exclaimed, surprised; she couldn't understand why there would be an elf here.

Elves were rare in human kingdoms, mostly living in the Southern United Kingdom like other foreign races.

A small number of elves lived in human kingdoms, mostly for business or work.

For example, the elven ambassador to the United Kingdom of Great Britain was a beautiful female elf, said to be nearly 1000 years old.

Alice wasn't seeing an elf for the first time; in her memories, they were always incredibly noble, with breathtaking beauty, elegance, and refinement.

Even elven traveling merchants, though weary from their journeys, maintained a high standard of living, with exquisite clothes and manners, though they could be haughty.

An elf as disheveled, frightened, and miserable as this one was quite rare; she must have suffered a lot.

The elven girl was crying, her knees bent, and her body curled up in a corner, trembling.

Her figure was slender, and her exposed shoulders were shaking.

She also wore an iron ring around her neck, like Alice's, presumably to prevent her from using magic or martial arts.

Even without seeing her face, you could tell she would be a beauty.

The elven girl heard someone speaking and suddenly trembled; she lifted her tear-stained face.

Her eyes, like flowing water, were beautiful, but red and swollen from crying; she looked about 17 years old, with a flawless, snow-white complexion, and a face that radiated saintliness.

When the elven girl saw Alice looking at her, she was shocked and terrified; her eyes filled with fear as she desperately shrank into the corner, crying and saying.

"Please don't look at me!

"Please don't hurt me anymore!

"For the sake of the human goddess, have some mercy on me.

"I'll be good, just don't cut my wrist again."

title: Chapter 3 — Monthly Vote Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 3 — Monthly Vote Bonus Update

Volume 5 · Chapter 3

“Eh!?” Alice was taken aback, thinking to herself, What did I do? Why is she so scared of me?

The golden-haired elf girl was holding her head, her whole body shaking, tears streaming down her face as she cowered in the corner of the wall, too afraid to approach Alice.

If the prison were a bit larger, the elf girl might have run even farther, but it was too small, and there was nowhere to hide.

Probably, this elf girl was now wishing she could burrow into the ground, and it seemed that her fear of humans had become a habit.

“Please don't hurt me, please...”

Alice looked at the elf girl with a complex expression, unsure of what she had done wrong.

But seeing the scars on her wrist, Alice realized what was going on.

It was likely that the elf girl had been tortured by the remnants of the former kingdom, making her extremely afraid of humans, and her mental state was on the verge of collapse.

“Cough!” Alice cleared her throat, trying to communicate with the elf girl and ease the tension. “I won't hurt you, trust me, okay?”

“Eh?” The golden-haired elf girl lifted her head, blinking her tear-filled eyes at Alice, and found that this human seemed kind, with clear eyes and no malice. However, she didn't let her guard down and said pitifully, “Don't cut my wrist, it really hurts.”

“No, I'm not like them, I won't hurt you.” Alice replied seriously, trying to get closer to the elf girl.

The golden-haired elf girl's body was still shaking, her eyes fixed on Alice, and she asked cautiously, “Really?”

“What, do you still have doubts? If I were with them, would I be wearing this kind of restraint on my neck?” Alice said helplessly, knocking on the iron ring on her neck, making a clinking sound. “I'm not wearing the same kind of magic-suppressing iron ring as you?”

The golden-haired elf girl looked at Alice warily, thinking she wasn't lying, and various signs indicated that they were both in the same situation.

The elf girl relaxed a bit, but still didn't completely trust Alice, after all, she was a human.

Currently, what the elf girl distrusted the most was humans, because she had been held captive by the remnants of the former kingdom for half a year, and had suffered a lot of ruthless abuse.

“Don't be afraid, I won't hurt you,” Alice said friendly, extending her hand. “My name is Alice Clodia, a golden adventurer from Rexham. What's yours?”

The golden-haired elf girl looked at Alice's outstretched hand, then at her eyes, and tentatively reached out to hold it, looking very nervous.

“What is your name? Is it inconvenient to tell me?” Alice asked curiously, feeling that the elf girl's hand was very cold, and her lips were pale, like she was lacking blood.

“No...”

The golden-haired elf girl shook her head gently, feeling the warmth of Alice's palm, and thinking, Could she really be a good person? Humans were all bad guys wearing masks, right? Although there was some risk, she still tried to believe her once. “I'm Sherry Nehemiah Lancy.”

“Alice smiled. “Sherry, that's a great name.”

The elf girl with the name Sherry blushed, thinking that addressing her by her name directly was a bit impolite.

“Where are you from? Judging by your clothes, you don't seem to be an elf living in a human kingdom,” Alice said, examining Sherry's attire and finding that the patterns on her clothes were definitely not drawn by humans.

“Um, I'm from the Southern United Kingdom,” Sherry said softly, seemingly not daring to speak loudly.

“I see,” Alice said knowingly. “I could tell you weren't an elf living in a human kingdom.”

“Is it that obvious?” Sherry looked a bit stiff.

“Of course,” Alice nodded. “Just the patterns on your clothes show a huge cultural difference. But since you live in the Southern United Kingdom, how did you end up here?”

“I snuck out to play without my father's knowledge, and I was caught by human traffickers... and I ended up here,” Sherry said sadly. Alice looked at Sherry and found her quite pitiful. “What did the people of the former kingdom do with you?”

“I don't know, but maybe they needed my blood,” Sherry said, looking at the wound on her wrist, and her expression turned melancholic.

“Blood?” Alice was taken aback, unsure of what use an elf's blood was.

“Yes, a purple-haired woman told me before that my blood was very useful to their lord, and it could be used to make a magic potion that would grant eternal youth... she advised me to eat more, not to be like the previous elf, who died after being drained of blood,” Sherry said, and tears began to well up in her eyes, feeling extremely wronged. For half a year, she had been regularly cut and bled to provide blood for someone to eat, and was kept in a dungeon like livestock, which made her distrust humans.

“Purple-haired woman...” Alice remembered Karona, but using elf blood to prolong life was unheard of. If there was no humane magic, it must be a forbidden technique.

“Alice, you're not an elf, why were you captured by them?” Sherry asked curiously, thinking that she was captured because her blood was useful, but what use was a human like Alice?

“It’s a long story, just know that I'm their hostage for now,” Alice said awkwardly, feeling helpless, and wondering what Merlin was doing now, and if he would come to rescue her.

“It's the same for us, our luck isn't very good,” Sherry's expression turned gloomy, and tears began to well up. “I've been captured for over half a year, and my father must be very worried about me, maybe he's worried sick every day, and can't eat... I'm so disobedient, if I hadn't run around, this wouldn't have happened.”

Alice didn't know how to comfort Sherry, who looked so sad.

“When I arrived, there was a dead elf in this cell, drained of blood, and I didn't want to end up like that...” Sherry covered her face and began to cry again, her small shoulders shaking.

“Don't worry, someone will come to rescue us,” Alice said comfortingly.

“No, I've been locked up here for half a year, and no one has come,” Sherry shook her head.

“That’s different, I'm a hostage, and my companions will definitely come to rescue me, and then you can go home,” Alice said seriously.

“Really? Will someone come to rescue us?” Sherry lifted her sad face, and her pointed ears twitched.

“Definitely, after all, he's my nominal husband,” Alice said, trying to boost Sherry's morale, but she couldn't help but think of her daily interactions with Merlin...

“You lazy bum! Get out of the bathroom! Are you sick?! Come out now!”

“Cooking! It's been a week since you cooked, don't be lazy! Or else I'll have it out with you!”

“Great Snow Mountain Invisible Foot, kick the Great Demon Lord's butt, ah da da da da da! So cool~!”

“Mmm...” Alice's face darkened, a cold sweat dripping down her forehead, and she said uncertainly...

“He'll come to rescue us... probably...”

title: Chapter 4
content:
Chapter 4

Volume 5 · Chapter 4

Leicester.

Outside the Adventurers Guild.

A light rain fell quietly, just a thin patter of droplets.

In the distance, it looked like intertwined gauze, dusk settling over this small Welsh town.

Arnold held a rose, gazing into the distance, speaking like a wandering poet—

"My beloved, you're like a rose with thorns, so sweet, pure, and elegant."

Hobson felt a shiver run down his spine beside him, half-sober.

"Come on, snap out of it. Why are you so obsessed? Alice and Merlin are fine as they are—stop causing trouble."

"Hobson, you've given up on marriage, you wouldn't understand. Love is about relentless, persistent effort, and that's what leads to results." Arnold wore a melancholy expression, thinking his brooding image would surely win over a crowd of girls.

"The only thing I see is you clinging desperately. Nothing else." Hobson took a sip, only to realize he'd drunk the whole cup without noticing, and his mood soured instantly.

"I believe I can make Miss Alice see reason. As long as I become more proactive, show her my passionate sincerity, Miss Alice's heart will surely be moved. Then she'll divorce Merlin and return to my side—everything will be just as wonderful~" Arnold sniffed the rose in his hand.

"Where did you get such a terrible idea?" Hobson asked expressionlessly, feeling Arnold was seriously unwell now.

"My sister, Jenna Gillian Austin." Arnold shook the rose, speaking earnestly, "She's read hundreds of thousands of romance novels, renowned as Leicester's love consultation master. Everything she says is spot-on."

"Arnold, I heard your sister has never even dated anyone. What kind of bullshit love consultant is that?" Hobson sighed helplessly.

"Jenna reads plenty of books, she's experienced. Her advice is absolutely great!" Arnold gave a thumbs-up, brimming with confidence.

"Stop talking about those spiritual comfort novels for girls. It's nothing like real combat on the battlefield." Hobson explained with a helpless expression.

"Hobson, you don't understand. Books are the legacy of human wisdom. Every story plays out life itself. Although Jenna has never dated, she's experienced countless love stories through reading—that's enough~" Arnold said arrogantly, as if he truly believed his sister's words.

"Honestly, Arnold, you're the earl's son—you have plenty of options. Why throw yourself at one tree? I heard that Rosé seems interested in you~" Hobson couldn't fathom why a nobleman's son would be so obsessed with a commoner laundry girl.

"I just don't want my first love in life to be a half-hearted affair." Arnold shook his head with affected profundity.

"You sound like you're trying so hard to say you're a virgin." Hobson's expression turned odd.

"Don't dwell on those details. Anyway, Arnold placed the rose petals into Hobson's wine cup, lifted his umbrella, and stepped into the street. "Looks like Miss Alice won't be coming back today. I'll head home first. See you!"

Hobson picked up the wine cup with the rose, gave it a sniff, thought it smelled quite nice—perfect for taking home to please his wife.

Looking at the empty town streets, Hobson couldn't help but stroke his stubbled chin and think, Arnold is really naive. Now he's got his sister as a teammate too. He's probably only going to drift further from his dreams.

After a while, a small donkey cart passed by the Adventurers Guild and stopped.

In the drizzling rain, the rider was completely soaked, her golden hair plastered to her head, with a trace of exhaustion in her expression.

Merlin had ridden hard for a long time, hadn't slept at all, and had rushed straight back to Leicester from Rowcourt Village.

That village had no survivors—everyone had frozen to death, turned into ice sculptures, erased from the map of Britain.

Could this cause trouble later? But Merlin had other things to attend to and no time to consider anything else.

"Hey~" Hobson waved his wine cup in greeting, "Merlin, you're back! Come on in, let's drink."

"Sorry, I'm in a hurry." Merlin said casually, her eyes having lost much of their former nonchalance. "Hobson, is Miss Da Vinci in the guild?"

"No, she's not here. At this hour, she's definitely in the library. What's the matter?" Hobson asked curiously, sensing Merlin was urgently after something.

"Oh, I see. Thanks." Merlin drove her donkey cart straight toward the town library without another word.

Hobson stared with wide eyes, his mind in turmoil.

Huh? What's so urgent?

I was hoping to chat with him for a bit.

Speaking of which, where's Alice?

Leicester Library.

S

SP

As an honorary member, Da Vinci had her own laboratory here.

In addition to the exclusive lab, she enjoyed many other privileges.

Da Vinci wasn't just an adventurer—she also had exceptional insight in alchemy, fully funded by the Austin family.

At this moment, in the laboratory, Rosé was napping on top of a book, drool soaking through the pages.

Rosé, as Da Vinci's partner, was always by her side—close enough that people often mistook them for lovers.

Da Vinci was conducting various experiments on the mysterious key, with books piled high around her, along with test tubes and various alchemical reagents.

ESMJKXE

By now, Da Vinci had placed the mysterious key into a test tube. After long experimentation and investigation, she had gained some understanding of it—but further verification was still needed.

Da Vinci fetched high-purity holy water from the Church, poured it into the test tube. After countless blessings from red-robed bishops and soaking in sacred vessels, it became poison to dark creatures.

The key bubbled and gurgled in the holy water, then the water turned turbid, emitting a pungent black rock.

Da Vinci quickly began careful observation, adjusting her monocle. Suddenly, a blue magical sigil appeared, with various spell formulas flowing across it.

A faint whisper echoed in Da Vinci's ear—

"We vow to offer our souls to the great Satan, becoming claws of Hell. Our souls shall burn in the flames of purgatory without fear."

Da Vinci adjusted her monocle further, and the spell formulas began to flow faster, the scene before her changing dramatically.

Her vision pierced through layer upon layer of mist, entering a deep cavern. Endless flames and corpses falling from nowhere followed—wailing and screaming, begging for rebirth.

In the darkness, countless skeletons burned with Hellfire, seemingly waiting for something, roaring continuously, wielding weapons of Hell.

At the front, a skeleton in heavy armor, its head covered in bristles, rode atop a bone dragon. Its flames burned more intensely than anyone else's.

It suddenly turned its gaze toward Da Vinci, revealing a horrifying skull, with red flames burning in its eye sockets, and it broke into a terrible laugh.

"Kekeke."

Da Vinci snapped the spell away in a flash, startled by the undead's gaze, stumbling backward. Her hand lost its grip on the test tube, which fell and shattered on the ground.

The red key lay silently on the floor, as if nothing had happened at all.

Da Vinci breathed heavily, cold sweat trickling down her forehead, her heart pounding violently. Her uneasy eyes fixed on the key, feeling as though her soul had nearly failed to return. She had never witnessed such a terrifying sight.

"Hey!? What happened!" Rosé was jolted awake, drool still clinging to her mouth. She stared blankly at Da Vinci, wondering what had occurred.

Da Vinci steadied her emotions, looked at Rosé, and spoke with lingering dread—

"This key... comes from Hell."

title: Chapter 5 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 5 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 5 · Chapter 5

“Is this hell?” Rosette furrowed her brow and asked curiously, “Does a place like that really exist? Just like heaven, it's probably all made-up.”

“Many ancient books mention it. Our world is just one of many. Birth, aging, illness, and death all follow a predetermined destiny. There are insurmountable barriers between worlds, and it's rare for them to interfere with each other.” Leonardo da Vinci carefully picked up the red key, wrapped it in cloth, and placed it on the table. He began to flip through the books. “I believe hell exists. Although alchemy is popular now, theology has been passed down for a reason.”

“So, the key Alice and them found isn't treasure, then?” Rosette asked curiously.

“No, I preliminarily determined that the key's material comes from hell,” Da Vinci said while seriously reading the book. “According to ancient records, the former kingdom's emperor unified the country and used hell's power. He had contact with hell's apostles and gave his soul to Satan in exchange for four keys. These four keys, combined with ancient magic arrays, can open the gates between our world and hell, allowing countless spirits to return to the real world.”

“Ancient unofficial history from 400 years ago? Who would take that seriously?” Rosette seemed to have heard this rumor before.

“Since someone wrote it down, someone must believe it, right? And now that this key and the unofficial history match, they must be connected.” Da Vinci said calmly.

“Connection?” Rosette seemed to be used to Da Vinci's mystical way of speaking.

“It's said that the former kingdom's emperor and hell's apostles made a deal. He gave his soul to Satan and obtained four keys. These keys can open the gates of hell and our world, allowing countless dead souls to return.”

“There is such a thing?” Rosette's expression was filled with astonishment. “I remember that historically, 400 years ago, the British dynasty launched an uprising. They used the former kingdom selling people's souls to hell's Satan as an excuse. This sparked a 20-year civil war, and the Vatican helped. Could this excuse be true?”

“Things from over 400 years ago, who can say for sure? But the former kingdom and legendary hell must have a connection.” Da Vinci slowly closed the book, feeling that he had understood most of the situation.

Rosette looked at the key wrapped in cloth curiously. “The legendary key, it's not this one, is it?”

Da Vinci was silent for a moment, then looked up and said seriously, “I think it's very likely.”

“Knock, knock, knock.”

The knocking sound at the door interrupted their conversation.

Da Vinci thought it was the librarian. “Come in.”

Merlin walked in directly, drenched and seemingly impolite.

“Da Vinci, I found you here.”

“Merlin?” Da Vinci was surprised, not expecting Merlin to find him directly.

“Hey, Merlin, and Alice, how was your honeymoon trip? Quite quick, huh?” Rosette couldn't help but tease.

Merlin glanced at Rosette, thinking that there was no honeymoon trip at all. It was far from enjoyable.

“Da Vinci, how's the research on the key going?”

“This key is full of danger. I advise you to hand it over to the royal family or the Holy Church to deal with.” Da Vinci gave his advice.

“How so?” Merlin asked, surprised that there was unexpected news.

“This key is likely a treasure from the former kingdom. It can open the gates between the present world and hell. If it falls into the wrong hands, the consequences will be unimaginable. The entire Britain will be in crisis.” Da Vinci explained briefly.

“Like that.”

Merlin didn't doubt Da Vinci's words much, as he had personally fought against hell's apostles and knew that hell definitely existed. However, he wasn't interested in those dead souls.

Now that he thought about all the things, why were the remnants of the former kingdom so obsessed with this key? Merlin almost understood. They must have wanted to gain powerful help. The hell apostles had also offered him tempting conditions, but he hadn't agreed.

“Da Vinci, please hand the key over to me.”

“I've told you that this kind of thing isn't something you and Alice can handle. You should hand it over to the royal family or the Holy Church.” Da Vinci furrowed her brow.

“No, it must be me.” Merlin said unhesitatingly.

“Hey, Merlin, Da Vinci won't harm you. If there's danger, she'll tell the truth.” Rosette said from the side.

“I know. To be honest, Alice was captured by the remnants of the former kingdom. I need this key to ransom her back. Time is running out.” Merlin said with a serious expression.

“Eh?” Da Vinci's eyes widened, surprised by the news. “Alice was captured?”

“Really or not?” Rosette stood up in shock.

“Really, they need that key.” Merlin said helplessly, not liking this kind of trouble.

“But if the key falls into the hands of people with ulterior motives, many people will be in danger. If you still have some sanity, you shouldn't hand the key over to the remnants of the former kingdom.” Da Vinci thought for a moment and continued, “And you don't have to worry too much about Alice. I heard the news that the Purple Gold Flower Knights have locked down the former kingdom's remnants' stronghold. The Ninth Thorns Knight may already be on the way. Alice will be rescued then.”

“Such things I'd rather do myself. I don't trust others. I only trust myself.” Merlin shook his hand, thinking that those Thorns Knights didn't know their strength. What if he didn't deliver the key on time and the other party got angry?

“Merlin, I think you're letting emotions cloud your judgment.” Da Vinci thought that the matter concerned the safety of the entire kingdom and couldn't let Merlin decide alone.

“Maybe, but Da Vinci, I hope you can understand.” Merlin smiled.

Da Vinci looked at Merlin, thinking differently. Anyway, Alice was Merlin's wife. If something happened to her, Merlin would definitely worry. It seemed that Merlin loved Alice from the heart.

If Merlin could read minds, he might vomit blood after hearing Da Vinci's thoughts.

Da Vinci thought that the key originally belonged to Merlin and Alice, and the way to handle it was up to them. She had said what she needed to say, so she handed the wrapped key to Merlin.

“It’s inside.”

Merlin opened it, looked, and nodded after confirming there was no problem. “Thank you for your help.”

“Honestly, the Thorns Knights have gone. What can a black iron adventurer like you do?” Rosette wanted Merlin to calm down. After all, they were fellow adventurers, and she didn't bear watching him go to his death. “And are you sure the other party has credibility? What if you give them the key and they don't return the person?”

“I'll send them all to hell, of course.” Merlin said calmly, putting the key in his pocket.

“Ah!?” Rosette furrowed her brow, and her large chest trembled. “You're just a low-level black iron adventurer. There are many things you can't do.”

“Ha, being a black iron adventurer and so what?” Merlin smiled calmly, walked to the door, and took a raincoat. “Can I borrow the raincoat?”

“Merlin, I won't stop you, but I just want to say one thing,” Da Vinci paused and said seriously, “You're not a hero. Don't indulge in romantic heroism.”

Merlin looked back at them and replied in a careless tone,

“I know I'm not a hero, of course.

Romantic heroism doesn't suit me either.

But even as a small person, some things have to be done.

I just want to bring Alice back home to do the household chores. Not for anything else.

Thinking about it, next week it's her turn to do it. If I want to use this method to avoid it, I won't agree.”

title: Chapter 6 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 6 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 5 · Chapter 6

Merlin mounted the borrowed black steed, while Alice's donkey Mengmeng had already been handed over to the groom for care.

He was going to act alone, so clearly riding a strong, sturdy horse would be faster to race through the night to the volcanic border of Scotland.

The drizzle had begun to grow heavier, and a thick rain curtain started to obscure Merlin's vision.

Big raindrops came crashing down on him like hammers, and the streets of the town welled up like blooming flowers of water.

Merlin urged the black horse into a full gallop along the town road, an unstoppable knight who seemed capable of tearing through the rain curtain, heading straight for the gates of Wrexham.

The city guard captain, Price, looked like he had been drinking again. He was swinging drunkenly inside the duty room, bored out of his mind, when he spotted Merlin riding toward him at full speed, and instantly felt the urge to invite him for a drink. So he grabbed a bottle of whiskey and stepped out of the duty room.

"Yo~! Young Merlin, wanna have a drink together?"

"Sorry, Price. Go get drinks with Hobbes. I'm in a hurry!"

Merlin urged his horse harder, his speed not decreasing in the slightest. He shot right past Price and burst out of Wrexham's gates.

Fierce horse hooves splashed puddles all over Price, leaving him a drenched and embarrassed mess.

Poor Price blinked his eyes blankly, his expression utterly bewildered. He wiped the dirty water off his face and shook his head in confusion.

"What the hell, what's wrong with Merlin today? He's in such a frantic rush!"

After bursting out of Wrexham, Merlin turned his horse around and headed straight for Scotland at a dead run.

Rain mist rose from the distant mountains, so hazy that nothing could be seen clearly. Horse hooves thundered across the ground, kicking up mud and silt.

The sky was dark and oppressive, so low it made it impossible to tell day from night.

Honestly, what a troublesome woman, Alice.

After saving her, she could just stay and work as a housekeeper for a month.

Cold red light flickered in Merlin's eyes as he pulled the hood of his black raincoat up over his head.

In that moment, he transformed into a dark knight of the rainy night, on the verge of forging a new legend.

Merlin lashed out hard with his riding crop, and the black horse let out a fierce neigh that echoed through the pouring rain.

Deep within the dim dungeon.

The two girls had lost all track of time, feeling like every second in that wretched cell was an eternal year.

"What kind of place is the Southern United Kingdom?" Alice asked idly as she chatted with the elf Shelly. "I've heard humans flee there for refuge, but I've never been."

"It's a fairly peaceful place, with dense forests, towering peaks, and vast seas. It suits all races well," Shelly said, nostalgia on her face. Her pointed ears twitched happily.

"That sounds wonderful. Are there lots of non-human races? Are there weird-looking creatures walking all over the streets?" Alice asked curiously. If she had the chance, she'd really love to see it.

"Miss Alice, that's not weird-looking. In our eyes, you humans are quite strange too. Why don't you have pointed ears or anything like that?" Shelly covered her mouth and murmured quietly.

"Sorry, that was a poor choice of words." Alice said awkwardly, thinking that different perspectives naturally led to different impressions.

"It's okay." Shelly paused and continued, "If you ever get the chance to visit the Southern United Kingdom, I'll host you. You can just walk the streets yourself and see. Although we are a multi-race nation, there are mainly nine great races. Some rare groups are hardly seen even in our country."

"With so many different cultures gathered together, wouldn't they fight?" Alice found it hard to imagine peaceful coexistence.

"Our United Kingdom has a parliamentary system. No single race calls the shots. Each race has a king, and they resolve issues through voting and negotiation in the parliament. Major disagreements basically never arise." Shelly explained patiently to Alice.

"Oh, I thought your United Kingdom was pretty chaotic." Alice said awkwardly.

"Not chaotic at all. You should come feel it for yourself if you get the chance." Shelly said with eager anticipation.

"Alright." Alice nodded.

After the lighthearted atmosphere passed, Shelly grew worried again. "If only we could get out..."

"Don't worry, we'll definitely get out." Alice couldn't help but comfort her when Shelly brought up such a sad topic.

"Thank you, Miss Alice. Having someone to talk to already makes me very happy." A rare smile appeared on Shelly's face.

"You're welcome. You look just like my little sister. I always feel like I can't just leave things alone." Alice smiled a little shyly.

"But I'm almost 400 years old, not a little sister..." Shelly said timidly.

Alice's expression froze, cold sweat beading on her forehead. She wondered why non-humans' ages were always getting bigger and bigger! They looked so young, but were actually old ladies!? This was really hard to accept!

"You two look pretty cheerful. Is this a case of weaklings huddling together for warmth? Can I join too? Because I'm also a weakling."

Joey, wearing a crying mask, appeared at the dungeon entrance at some unknown point, holding a bowl, completely without any trace of his approach.

The two girls were instantly startled, their faces draining of color as if they had actually seen a ghost. In the dark, shadowy dungeon, Joey, wrapped head to toe in bandages, looked extraordinarily eerie. And with his brother Zoy absent, it seemed he could speak normally as well.

Shelly trembled all over. Seeing the bowl in Joey's hand, she immediately knew what he was going to do — he was definitely here to take her blood.

Her terrified eyes bulged wide, her lips quivering speechlessly. Even her breathing quickened, and the scars on her wrists began to ache.

"You don't seem very welcoming. Never mind then." Joey placed the bowl at the dungeon entrance and said coldly. "Stick your hand out."

"No!!!" Shelly curled up in the corner, clutching her head, her face pale. Cold sweat and tears streamed down her face simultaneously. Her panicked hands flailed. "Please don't hurt me, I'll be obedient, please stop tormenting my body, I beg you to show some mercy—"

"Mercy?" Joey tilted his head, confused. "What's that? In my eyes, there are only the living and the dead."

"Woo woo..." Shelly's pointed ears drooped, and she began to sob chokedly.

"What are you doing? Stop this excessive behavior right now!" Alice stepped in front of Shelly to protect her, preventing Joey from getting his way.

"Excessive?" Joey murmured to himself, trembling as if something inside him had broken—

"Back when I used to cut off the neighbor's kid's fingers, people cursed at me just like that too."

"But it's not my fault. Brother forces me to do these things. If I don't obey, I get beaten."

"Even though I keep apologizing, why won't those people forgive me? It's not my fault!"

"Why, why, why, why—"

Alice furrowed her delicate brows, looking at the bizarre Joey. What was wrong with this guy? Why was he acting like a lunatic?

"Move!" Joey thrust his hand into the cell and swept it aside, easily throwing Alice away.

Alice could no longer use her fighting energy or magic, and was no different from an ordinary person. In front of Saint-tier Joey, she was like an ant, completely defenseless.

"Hrk!" Alice fell to the ground, waves of pain coursing through her body. She was definitely injured.

"Miss Alice!?" Shelly looked at Alice in panic.

"Damn it! What are you doing!?" Alice demanded through the intense pain.

"I'm sorry, but I have to do this excessive thing, or else my brother will beat me!" Joey bellowed sadly, reached out, grabbed Shelly's wrist, and dragged her to the edge of the cage.

"No!!! Please! Please! Spare me!!!" Shelly cried so sorrowfully, so mournfully, so despairingly. Tears gushed from her eye sockets like a breached dam, begging endlessly.

"Sorry, sorry, sorry..." Joey's head shook back and forth as he muttered to himself, roaring, "I've apologized already! Why won't you forgive me! It's all my brother's fault! I'm not wrong, blame my brother!"

Joey drew the dagger at his waist and ruthlessly slashed Shelly's wrist, completely unaware of his own expression at this moment.

"AAAAHHH!" Shelly screamed in pain, her delicate body writhing continuously, but she couldn't break free from Joey's grip.

Bright red blood dripped down Shelly's arm into the bowl, dripping, dripping.

Alice's tearful eyes filled with hatred, along with waves of frustration and unwillingness.

She silently clenched her fists and thought bitterly —

Dammit!

If only I could grow stronger!

If I could be like that guy Merlin—

I could fully carry out my justice!

Above the temple.

The flames of torches flickered constantly.

The enormous ancient magic array had been prepared for a long time, but the four keys were still nowhere to be seen.

This made Copeland increasingly anxious. His physical condition deteriorated with each passing day, and the frequency of needing elf blood increased.

Joey emerged from the basement, carrying a bowl of warm elf blood.

Zoy hurried forward, took the bowl of elf blood, and said blandly, "You can withdraw. Leave this to me."

"You're right, brother." Joey returned to his usual vacant state.

"Hmph!"

Zoy snorted coldly and approached alone, drawing near the frail, hunched figure ahead.

Copeland, hidden beneath his black robes, always exuded an air of mystery.

Zoy didn't get too close. At a suitable distance, he knelt on one knee and raised the bowl with his remaining arm.

"Your Majesty, the elf blood has arrived."

Copeland turned and slowly approached Zoy, gazing at the bright red blood.

"Zoy, is our great enterprise failing? This feeling is becoming stronger and stronger."

"It won't!" Zoy spoke loudly, his body trembling slightly. "As long as Your Majesty lives, we will still have the chance to rise again! Britannia only stole our fruits — they are thieves! This land forever belongs to our former kingdom! We all are willing to believe you, Your Majesty Copeland. As long as the fourth key is obtained, you will undoubtedly become the king of the new era!"

"That's true. Maybe I really am getting old. My mind is becoming less and less clear..."

Copeland extended his hand, like dried bone, to take the bowl of elf blood.

But just then, the calm blood began to ripple in a regular pattern, echoing constantly.

The entire great hall subtly trembled, as if something was moving toward them.

Copeland withdrew his hand, his gaze turning toward the exterior of the great hall, and said in a hoarse voice—

"Zoy, we have guests arriving. Go welcome them."

The pouring rain cascaded from the darkening sky.

The forest beneath the volcano was shaken violently by raging winds, as if a horde of demons danced chaotically in the night!

Countless horse hooves approached, making this stormy night seem even more chaotic.

They rode powerful steeds, clad in magnificent silver-white armor of exquisite craftsmanship, carrying exceedingly sharp weapons.

Their white capes, imprinted with familiar patterns, billowed behind them as they advanced through the violent storm!

Was there a second knight团in Great Britain as luxuriously equipped as this?

There was no mistake. The flag of the bauhinia flower rose in the dark wind and rain, fluttering powerfully, representing royal authority—

The sword of the righteous, the Bauhinia Knight團had arrived here!

title: Chapter 7
content:
Chapter 7

Volume 5 · Chapter 7

The wind kept howling, the rain pouring down harder and harder. Thunder rumbled, rolling over, the violent wind and rain fiercely pressing the trees to the side. The rolling thunder of hooves made the rainy night even more chaotic. The only light in the pitch‑black darkness was probably the firelight from the volcano’s crater, like the blaze of a flame demon descending into the world. The members of the Redbud Knights are all elites of Britain, having passed rigorous screening and assessment before being admitted to this honorable hall. They are tall and young, with rugged builds and sharp angles, their gazes steadfast, possessing absolute loyalty to the queen. This cohesion makes them unite like a wolf pack, acting with extreme swiftness, regarding orders as more important than life. As the knight order representing the crown of Great Britain, their loyalty is rightly called the queen’s sword. Almost everyone is trained from their passionate youth, needing to pass political review and undergo non‑human training to become official members. The minimum standard is intermediate strength; high‑level individuals are generally squad leaders. Such stringent conditions naturally forged the Redbud Knights’ renown throughout Britain. In the eyes of ordinary folk, the Redbud symbolizes the valiant guardians of the kingdom; justice and hope have long become their permanent insignia. Countless children of common folk have dreamed since childhood of joining the Redbud Knights, donning exquisite silver‑gold armor, cloaked in Redbud robes, becoming the envy of others. At this moment, the force that has come to Scotland numbers about three thousand knights, not many, two. Because after Squad Leader Chapman personally investigated, the kingdom’s remnants this time are not strong. There’s a high chance they are all high‑level enemies, of course they haven’t ruled out the possibility of a Saint‑tier powerhouse. Therefore, as the Ninth Thorn Knight Sahadin, he personally leads this detachment of knights to Scotland to exterminate the remnants of the former kingdom, ensuring absolute safety. The Redbud Knights in silver‑white armor cut through the night sky, the white plumes on their helmets pressed down by wind and rain, yet the high‑held flag remains steadfast. The leading knight’s armor is quite ornate, his build much more burly than other knights, his cape behind is red with a pattern, displaying his distinctiveness. His face is chiseled like a blade, full of a sharp aura, his red hair seeming as if flames burn within. His most striking feature is the red beard on his face, making him look like a hot‑tempered, fiery individual. It appears this person is the rumored Saint‑tier powerhouse, the Ninth Thorn Knight of Britain, Sahadin. The party arrived at the volcano’s base; Sahadin raised his hand, and the troupe of over three thousand immediately halted in perfect order, showing their discipline. The red‑haired Sahadin surveyed the whole volcano, especially the forest ahead, sensing a possible ambush. Squad Leader Chapman rode forward, approaching Sahadin, and said respectfully, “Lord Sahadin, based on the scouts’ intelligence, it seems this is the hiding place of the kingdom’s remnants.” “Reliable, we asked many people, including coastal slave traders; they said half a year ago an elf was sold to someone behaving strangely, after inquiring along the way, that elf was brought here, and if I recall correctly, there are ruins of the former kingdom’s temple above.” Chapman’s report was concise and clear. “Alright, everyone dismount and prepare!” Sahadin commanded. Over three thousand Redbud Knights dismounted, tidied their gear, and formed up with mages in the rear and swordsmen in front. Their faces, battered by rain, showed no expression as they drew their cold‑light flashing swords and magic‑wreathed staves, standing ready. Chapman also drew his sword, looking at Sahadin’s solemn expression with some doubt: “Lord Sahadin, according to reliable intel, the enemy’s strength may all be weak; perhaps you need not act, we can handle it fully.” “No, even a lion uses its full strength when fighting; we must never be careless. Follow behind me and obey my orders.” Sahadin said seriously. “Yes.” Chapman lowered his head, thinking that having Lord Sahadin act feels like using a butcher’s knife to kill a chicken. “These knights who came are all young; you are the new blood of the Redbud Knights. Try to avoid casualties. If we old bones fall, only you youngsters can uphold the Redbud’s spirit. So never underestimate the enemy, protect yourselves…” Sahadin, like an elder, gave young Chapman a piece of advice. “Sahadin…” Chapman felt a bit moved, thinking Sahadin is the most approachable Thorn Knight, like a neighboring uncle. As for the other Thorn Knights, they are very aloof, unlikely to pay attention to ordinary knights, and certainly wouldn’t care about their life or death. Chapman felt this suppression was already as stable as it could get, likely to just steamroll over them; even if a Saint‑tier powerhouse truly existed, it would hardly be a match for Sahadin, surely to be easily defeated, because each Thorn Knight possesses absolute strength, and a typical Saint‑tier could not compete on equal footing. Sahadin, as the Ninth Thorn Knight, is well‑known throughout Britain; his secret art is famed for its impregnable defense like a bronze wall, impervious to blades and spears—even if he were Saint‑tier, it would be hard to wound him. Once during a drill, hundreds of mages simultaneously bombarded Sahadin, yet not a single hair was harmed, showing how terrifying he is. Chapman recalled the First Thorn Knight once praising Sahadin, saying: “Even I would get a headache facing Sahadin; though I could win, it would certainly not be easy.” Chapman has always thought the First Thorn Knight is the strongest human, possibly rivaling a god‑like man; since even he said that, how could Sahadin be weak? “We must fight splendidly this time, not only for Her Majesty the Queen, but also to reestablish the prestige of the Redbud Knights throughout Britain.” Sahadin picked up his heavy shield and his battle‑hammer, marred by nicks. “Have we not always been prestigious?” Chapman asked, bewildered. “No, now a man called Elgin the Great Swordmaster has appeared; more and more civilians regard him as Britain’s savior, already posing a slight threat to our knights’ standing in the public’s eyes. Thus we take this opportunity to rebuild our prestige.” Sahadin said seriously, considering the campaign secondary; what matters is shaping the image of the Redbud Knights. “Shouldn’t we welcome more such champions of justice?” Chapman asked doubtfully. “No, a savior is never needed in twos.” Sahadin seemed to be sparring with Elgin the Great Swordmaster, explaining: “Someone like Elgin, that mysterious fellow, is more likely a commoner, whereas we, as the queen’s sword, represent royal authority; our position is being shaken, which is also why Her Majesty refuses to rescind the wanted order against Elgin—you must understand.” “Is that so? Thank you for the lesson, Sahadin…” Chapman felt a few black lines slip down his forehead, unable to stop doubting: “Could we be false justice? Elgin the Great Swordmaster embodies true justice. I never imagined that this ordinary suppression would involve so many complications…. z(° O°D)”

title: Chapter 8 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 8 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 5 · Chapter 8

“Besides establishing our prestige, there's an even more important matter, something that Her Majesty entrusted to me personally.” Sahadin's expression was grave, his brow furrowed in concern.

“Eh!?” Chapman looked startled, thinking that if the Queen herself had entrusted Sahadin with a task, it must be extremely important.

“Do you remember, half a year ago, the Elf King of the Southern United Kingdom wrote a letter to Her Majesty?” Sahadin asked, his voice calm and measured.

“Of course I remember,” Chapman replied. “I heard it was because the Elf King's youngest daughter went missing, and they suspected that someone with ill intentions had kidnapped her. So, our knights spent several months searching for the little princess in Great Britain, but unfortunately, we found nothing. Maybe she was taken to another country.” Chapman's memory of the incident was still vivid.

“So, Her Majesty is quite concerned about this matter. If it's true that the remnants of the former kingdom kidnapped the Elf King's daughter, our primary goal must be to ensure her safety. This affects the harmony between Great Britain and the Southern United Kingdom, you understand?” Sahadin explained, his tone serious. This matter was equally important to the entire Crimson Flower Knights.

“Understood!” Chapman responded firmly, aware of the gravity of the situation.

“The little princess's name is Sherry Nehmeria Lansy. Remember this name,” Sahadin instructed, so that Chapman could confirm the identity of the elf kidnapped by the remnants of the former kingdom.

“Got it, Sahadin-sama!” Chapman replied, his hand on his heart, showing respect.

“Alright, let's head up the mountain. We will annihilate the remnants of the former kingdom, leaving no one standing!” Sahadin turned to face the dark forest, raising his war hammer and roaring like a lion, his voice thunderous.

“Crimson Flower Knights, charge!

The forest.

A torrent of heavy rain had been pouring down continuously.

The leaves in the forest were drumming a rapid beat.

The knights in silver armor advanced slowly towards the top of the mountain.

They held sharp swords, their expressions serious, and their eyes alert, as if facing a ferocious beast.

Sahadin, at the forefront, cautioned his fellow knights, his eyes gleaming with vigilance.

“Be careful of your surroundings. We must complete this subjugation without taking any damage.”

“Yes, Sahadin-sama,” Chapman responded, his voice serious, his heart tense. Rainwater flowed into his eyes, but he didn't blink.

Although they had initially thought the enemy's strength might not be great and had been relatively relaxed, now, seeing Sahadin's seriousness, everyone became highly alert.

A whistling sound cut through the air, and a silver dagger flew straight at Sahadin, imbued with golden aura.

“Hmph!” Sahadin snorted, not dodging, and let the dagger, infused with Saint-tier aura, fly straight at his forehead.

“Sahadin-sama, be careful!” Chapman shouted, his heart racing, and the other knights stirred.

But something strange happened. The dagger, infused with Saint-tier aura, hit Sahadin's forehead but was suddenly deflected, flying in a beautiful arc and landing on the ground.

All the knights were shocked, not expecting the dagger, enhanced with Saint-tier aura, to have no effect on Sahadin. No wonder he hadn't dodged, confident that the enemy's attack would not harm him.

If it were them, the dagger would have pierced their bodies without a doubt.

Chapman looked at Sahadin, who stood like a mountain, and thought in awe, no wonder he was known as the 'Shield of Thorns,' some sneak attacks were beneath him. As a human, his defense was like steel, terrifying.

“Starting with a sneak attack, how despicable...” Sahadin looked up, his forehead unscathed, his defense evident.

From above, a series of cold laughs came from behind a smiling mask.

Although hidden in darkness, a flash of lightning revealed a sinister and eerie figure.
