“A tough guy, how interesting~”

Chapman was stunned, thinking incredulously, a Saint-tier strong? If not for Sahadin's caution, they would all have died here.

“Who are you? This is our territory. Unauthorized personnel are not allowed to enter! If you take one step forward, you will be killed!” The masked figure, Zoey, stood up on the high branch, her voice extremely cold.

“I am Sahadin, the ninth Thorn Knight. I have come to subjugate the remnants of the former kingdom. Who are you? Why did you attack us?” Sahadin's expression turned ugly, his tone not friendly.

“Ha! A dog of the British dynasty! I didn't expect it to be you. What a coincidence!” Zoey drew her straight sword, pointing at herself and boasting, “I am Zoey, one of the Four Heroes of the former kingdom, the Twin Sword Saints. How is it? Have you heard my name in history books? Are you scared to death?”

“What!?” Chapman widened his eyes, feeling his investigation had gone awry. He thought in shock, one of the Four Heroes of the former kingdom was a Saint-tier strong? His information was incorrect! Could it be that the female adventurer from Wrexham had told the truth?

“Is that so? You dare admit your identity in front of me. I must commend your bravery. It seems you are prepared to die!” Sahadin glared, furious.

“Prepared to die? Ha...” Zoey laughed, holding her stomach, and said seriously, pointing at Sahadin, “Don't get it wrong, dogs of Britannia. I'm here to kill you, not to die. When you lie in a pool of blood, wailing and dying, I will still be alive, stepping on your corpses and laughing!”

“It seems there's no use in talking. The remnants of the former kingdom must be exterminated!” Sahadin raised his heavy hammer, his expression like an enraged lion, and commanded loudly, “Mages, prepare for bombardment!”

The mages of the Crimson Flower Knights raised their wands, aiming at Zoey above.

“Ka ka ka, you...” Zoey crouched on the tree trunk, seemingly ready for attack, “not a single one will escape! Leave your corpses behind, dogs of Britannia!”

“Fire!” Sahadin pointed his heavy hammer at Zoey, his voice booming.

The wands of dozens of mages lit up with firelight, and the air's fire elements became extremely violent.

The heavy rain seemed to evaporate in an instant.

The mages had learned the mid-tier 'Flame Explosion' magic, which, although basic, could be combined.

The more mages, the stronger the destructive power. The magic of dozens of mages combined could rival Saint-tier magic!

In the dark, rainy night, a spark of fire ignited, and a blazing fire pillar shot into the sky, heading straight for Zoey!

The entire mountain shook with the explosion of magic, and the heavy rain evaporated instantly, rising into a vast, white mist.

“Not bad, but not enough!”

Zoey jumped down from the branch, using her ghostly form to avoid the combined magic attack, and descended with her straight sword.

“Come!” Sahadin prepared himself, like a mighty fortress, and raised his shield to meet Zoey's attack.

The straight sword clashed with the thick shield, sparks flying, as Saint-tier aura collided, evenly matched.

The heavy rain was like the curtain of a stage, slowly opening...

A crack of thunder split the dark sky!

The collision between the former kingdom and Great Britain had suddenly begun...

title: Chapter 9 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 9 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 5 · Chapter 9

The stormy weather, with its torrential rain and lightning, only added to the chaos of the battle between the two Saint-tier strongmen.

The clashing of their weapons created a "ding-dang" sound that seemed to rival the occasional thunderclap in the sky.

In just a few breaths, the two fighters had exchanged blows multiple times, their Saint-tier combat auras flaring as they clashed, each gaining the upper hand at different moments.

Zoi's swordsmanship was extremely refined, with attack angles that were very tricky and a speed that was incredibly fast. Each move had the potential to be life-threatening, and it seemed that his reputation as one of the former kingdom's Four Heroes was not undeserved.

On the other hand, Sahadin's speed may have been at a disadvantage, but his own defensive capabilities made up for it. Despite being stabbed at his vital points several times, he remained unscathed, and with his violent combat aura, he seemed to be gaining the upper hand.

As the thorn knight created by Great Britain with all its might, Sahadin's hard-core strength was definitely there, and he was more than capable of standing on his own.

"Not bad, tough-skinned scoundrel!" Zoi's straight sword danced in his hand, creating a dizzying display of ancient Saint-tier sword techniques.

"Bandit! Surrender now!" Sahadin roared, using his shield to block Zoi's attacks or striking back with his war hammer, but still getting stabbed several times. If it weren't for his incredible defensive capabilities, he might have died already. "The dual sword saints, indeed, are not to be underestimated."

The two fighters' battle was extremely fierce, and the collision of their Saint-tier combat auras created a strong gust of wind that made the surrounding knights feel terrified and unable to approach. They could only watch in awe at the two fighters' martial arts, feeling that they were at the pinnacle of human achievement.

Sahadin suddenly swung his heavy hammer, as if freezing the raindrops in mid-air.

Zoi's movements were eerie, and his speed was fast. He directly dodged to the side, and with a swift counterattack, he stabbed straight at Sahadin's chest.

"Die, you brute!"

Zoi's sword was burning with golden combat aura, and it seemed to be a powerful blow.

The straight sword pierced through Sahadin's armor, but when it was about to stab into his heart, it couldn't advance any further.

"...Sahadin coldly laughed and swung his shield to strike Zoi's head.

"Ugh!" Zoi spat out a mouthful of dark, solidified blood and flew backward like a cannonball, crashing into a giant boulder and shattering it.

Sahadin knew that his opponent wouldn't be easily severely injured, so he immediately followed up with his Saint-tier martial technique, "Heavy Hammer Spark".

The Heavy Hammer Spark could allow his combat aura to blast out in a straight line, with destructive power that was quite astonishing. He could easily destroy a city wall.

Sahadin slammed his war hammer onto the ground, causing the earth to crack and split. A mighty Saint-tier combat aura tore through the air and struck.

Zoi dragged his exhausted body and rolled to dodge, slowly getting up, looking extremely disheveled.

He twisted his broken head back, and for an undead person, this wasn't a fatal injury.

"You have some skills, I must say I'm impressed. It seems that the thorn knights are not just empty vessels."

"If you know what's good for you, you'd better surrender. I'm known as the Shield of Thorns, and almost no one in Great Britain can easily harm me."

Zoi raised his straight sword, and his Saint-tier combat aura suddenly surged. "Shadow swordsmanship..."

At Zoi's feet, a dozen black shadows suddenly appeared, slowly moving and finally transforming into Zoi's likeness, all wearing a smiling mask.

This Saint-tier martial technique was Zoi's specialty, using combat aura to transform into his helpers.

The Shadow Swordsmanship, a 400-year-old martial technique, had long been lost. Sahadin was somewhat astonished to see it today.

According to legend, the shadow split by the Shadow Swordsmanship, although not as strong as the main body, still had considerable strength. Being able to split five shadows was already quite impressive, but Zoi could split ten!

"Charge!" Sahadin gave the order, prioritizing taking down Zoi.

Chapman regained his composure, holding his sword and charging forward with a roar.

The Purple Thistle Knights clashed with the ten shadows, and the knights swung their swords with all their might. The mages provided firepower support from a distance.

However, the originally proud knights of Great Britain were beaten back by the ten shadows, which was quite a shock.

The shadows' fighting style and strength were extremely close to Zoi's, and their sharp sword techniques were almost entirely inherited.

The sharp straight sword left a trail of blood and screams in its wake.

Countless knights fell into the blood pool, slowly flowing in the rain, turning the forest into a hellish scene.

"Hmph, what a weak knight团... Zoi stood in place, coldly snickering.

Sahadin jumped into the sky, abandoning his shield and holding his war hammer with both hands.

This selfless approach undoubtedly greatly increased Sahadin's attack power, at least doubling it.

The armor-clad figure in the dark sky was like a descending god of war.

"Ah...Zoi stared blankly, muttering.

"Ha! ! !" Sahadin roared, and his Saint-tier combat aura, like a tidal wave, pressed down.

The hammer hadn't fallen yet, but the ground began to crack.

Zoi was stunned, feeling that he couldn't dodge anymore.

Sahadin's war hammer smashed down, and the second Heavy Hammer Spark arrived. The earth turned upside down, and trees and mud were lifted hundreds of meters into the air.

The volcano began to emit a deafening sound, as if it were about to erupt.

Sahadin retreated from the center of the storm, and the giant pit on the ground was shocking. Hidden magma almost burst out, nearly blasting the volcano.

Zoi lay in the pit, his body twisted and motionless, like he was dead.

Sahadin confidently turned back, shouldering his war hammer and revealing a smile. "It's over. That was quite easy."

At this moment-

"Zoi! ! !"

The badly damaged Zoi slowly stood up, his body looking extremely eerie. Although many of his bones were broken, he could still barely hold his sword.

"Not dead yet? Indeed, as the intelligence said, you are a revived undead." Sahadin turned back, feeling a bit troublesome.

"Zoi! Come out! Let's kill this guy together! Let's tear him apart! ! !" Zoi shouted, his voice hoarse.

"My brother is right." Zoi's brother suddenly appeared beside him, emitting a Saint-tier aura not weaker than his brother's.

"Hmph, it seems that this is the other dual sword saint, huh?" Sahadin still felt confident in his victory, and his tone was somewhat contemptuous.

"Shut up! You dog of Great Britain! Only when we brothers are together can we unleash our full strength! Don't think you've won, scoundrel!" Zoi's smiling mask was broken, revealing a rotten face.

"According to the records of the former kingdom's history, your brothers' fusion of essence is quite strong, and your attack power is astonishing. You even killed the giant king with superhuman defense?" Sahadin asked casually.

"So what?" Zoi's voice became hoarse.

"I'd like to experience your strongest technique...Sahadin knocked his shoulder with his heavy hammer, looking down on the dual sword saints.

"To be honest,

"I think the giant king's defense is just trash.

"You two brothers are nothing but empty names."

"In this world, the only one who can hurt me is the First Thorn Knight."

title: Chapter 10
content:
Chapter 10

Volume 5 · Chapter 10

Sahadin's eyes filled with contempt, and his confidence began to swell.

In a one-on-one fight, he didn't feel Zoey was that powerful. So what if Joey, Zoey's younger brother, joined in?

Sahadin had long ago read from the former kingdom's documents that the Twin Sword Saints' ultimate technique possessed incredibly powerful offensive ability, once defeating the giant clan's king in an instant.

But Sahadin's own ultimate technique was renowned for its powerful defense, and to date he had never encountered any rival.

Only the First Thorn Knight had ever managed to wound him, so across all of Britannia, there was no one who could catch his eye.

Now that he had run into the Twin Sword Saints, for Sahadin this was a good opportunity — a chance to prove he was even stronger than the legendary giant king!

A torrential downpour hammered down, and the loud noise still couldn't drown out furious roaring.

"You self-important bastard! Who the hell do you think you're talking to!?" Zoey panted miserably, his whole body trembling with anger.

"My apologies, but I'm a straight-shooter. I don't think your fusion ultimate technique amounts to much — anything wrong with that?" Sahadin hoisted his warhammer and beckoned to the Twin Sword Saints. "Come on then, let me see what you've got!"

"You bastard! You're nothing but a lackey of Britannia! Do you really think you can shake our legend!?" Zoey pointed his straight sword sharply at Sahadin and said coldly, "Since you want to die so badly, I'll grant your wish!"

"..." Sahadin assumed a fighting stance and said seriously, "I'm truly looking forward to this..."

"Joey!" Zoey called out loudly.

"Big brother is right." Joey appeared beside Zoey in an instant.

The brothers' figures wove together, holding their straight swords in a manner that seemed to imitate some kind of aggressive beast.

Amid the storm, their figures looked eerie; even the lightning and thunder overhead couldn't shake their stance!

"What strange movements. Is this the opening stance of the legendary Purgatory Storm?" Sahadin narrowed his eyes, his fiery red beard making him look even more like a Viking berserker.

"Our ultimate technique has never faced an enemy who could parry it. The moment we strike, the enemy dies! Back then the giant king was just as overconfident as you, but in the end he still couldn't withstand our绝技. Seems you're very confident in your defense, huh? But let me tell you, you're no match for the giant king of those days!" Zoey shouted without restraint, as if he had firmly resolved to give Sahadin a lesson.

"Big brother is right." Joey chimed in.

"Wouldn't we only know that after fighting?" Sahadin's fighting spirit surged, and he grew even more eager.

"I was planning to save my绝技 for an adventurer, but it looks like I'll take care of you overconfident fool instead!" Zoey said viciously.

"Then I'm truly honored. In that case, I'll get serious too."

Sahadin suddenly clenched his fist, his veins bulging as he struck his steel fists together with a resounding clang. "Hnnng!!!"

Sahadin had decided to go all-out. His ultimate technique was called [Body of Steel], coating his entire body with high-concentration battle energy to form an iron-hard steel skin. Its defensive power might even surpass that of a dragon's scales!

"What is that...?" Zoey stared at Sahadin's unbelievable transformation, somewhat surprised.

Sahadin let out a long breath, white scorching vapor hissing from between his teeth.

His body blazed with golden battle energy, his skin turning silver-gray with a hard metallic gleam — had he actually transformed into an iron man?

"Now I'm at my strongest state. No one can break my defense. Seeing my magnificent physique now, I think you can understand why I called the giant king trash, right?"

"Hmph!" Zoe snorted, ignoring what Sahadin said.

"I am the Thorn Shield — you cannot defeat me easily. So..." Sahadin tossed his warhammer aside and smashed his steel fists together. "I won't move an inch. Come at me with everything you've got!"

The battlefield was in complete disarray. Over three thousand Bauhinia knights had battled the nine shadows in the driving rain, and after suffering heavy losses, they had finally secured victory. With that behind them, the fight between Sahadin and the Twin Sword Saints instantly became the focal point. No one stepped in to interfere, because clashes between Saint-tier experts were beyond their capability.

Far away, Chapman slowly propped himself up with his sword. He had several wounds on his body, and blood steadily oozed from them, staining his silver-white armor.

He had nearly been killed by those shadows' bizarre swordsmanship moments ago, and fear still lingered in his heart...

Chapman turned his gaze toward the distant duel and his eyes widened. He never expected to have the chance to witness Sahadin's ultimate technique —

Is that Lord Sahadin's signature move?

He could feel the monster-like pressure even from this far away!

Although the Twin Sword Saints' strength was not to be underestimated either, Lord Sahadin was hailed as the Thorn Shield and absolutely wouldn't lose!

Chapman had great faith in Sahadin. Besides the First Thorn Knight, who else could hope to injure him?

"Joey, teach this clueless bastard a lesson!" Zoe's Saint-tier battle energy surged violently.

"Big brother is right." Joey's battle energy rose as well.

The two brothers' golden battle energies merged together.

Fusion Ultimate Technique — Purgatory Storm unleashed in an instant! A devastating aura swept across the entire field!

The Twin Sword Saints transformed into a black dragon-shaped tornado of burning bone, intertwining together to become a rotating colossal drill!

Screeching lightning flashed repeatedly, and the dense storm was torn apart as if ripped open by a zipper.

Every knight present felt the threat of death. Chapman had never before seen such ferocious attacking moves. Good heavens, exactly as the books described — the fusion ultimate technique was incredibly powerful! But Lord Sahadin would surely withstand it.

"Come on then! Let me see what you brothers can do!" Sahadin stood immovable as a mountain, his whole body tensed.

The pitch-black massive drill tornado roared and charged toward Sahadin in an instant, tearing him into countless shreds of meat!

The battle ended in an instant, without a single suspense. The power difference was a crushing, tottering one-sided beatdown!

Sahadin, the Thorn Shield formerly known for his defense, had been instant-killed by the Twin Sword Saints' fusion ultimate technique!? It was simply unbelievable!

Purgatory Storm didn't stop. It continued to tear apart the volcano and swept through all the participating Bauhinia knights, shredding them one by one — not a single one escaped.

The black tornado raged on, like a monster from hell amid the storm. The Bauhinia banners fell one after another, swallowed by filthy mud and water.

This one-sided slaughter made Chapman begin to doubt everything —

Was he really instant-killed? !

Even the First Thorn Knight of the Thorns couldn't do that!

Was there anyone who could defeat these two's fusion ultimate technique?

The Queen's sharp sword had been broken... Could it be that our knights' advance stops here?

On the road.

A dark knight cut through the pitch-black rainy night, his steed neighing repeatedly as it sprinted at top speed toward the volcano.

The volcano torn apart by the Twin Sword Saints rumbled, surging magma spewing forth, the earth trembling continuously.

Merlin slightly raised his head and gazed at the volcano before him, his brow furrowing —

"That place..."

"What happened?"

title: Chapter 11 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 11 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 5 · Chapter 11

Rainwater washed away the blood of the knights on the ground, making the ground look like a crimson mirror.

Rolling magma emerged from the ground, only to be cooled by the cold rainwater, rising into thick steam.

Countless bodies of the Violet Flower Knights lay scattered on the ground.

Almost none of them were intact, all looking like they had been torn apart by wild beasts, reduced to mangled limbs.

The few relatively intact knight corpses still had their death expressions frozen on their faces, filled with fear.

As the pride and elite of Great Britain, the Violet Flower Knights were utterly defeated before the Twin Sword Sages!

Even the ninth Thorn Knight, who everyone had high hopes for, was completely overpowered and retreated in disarray.

The 3000 members of the knight团 who came to subdue them had almost all fallen in this forest.

Only Chapman survived, as he was relatively far from the Inferno Storm and managed to cling to life.

But he was still captured by the Twin Sword Sages and treated like a toy.

"Ahhhh!

Chapman's screams echoed through the sky, his voice incredibly shrill.

Large raindrops pounded against him, his face covered in dirty mud, as he lay on the ground like a dead dog.

Chapman's hands and feet had all been crippled by Joy, reduced to being a plaything for the twin brothers to pass the time.

He felt deeply humiliated, unable to die, and instead had to slowly endure the agony of the dagger slicing through his body.

Chapman's forehead slowly trickled with blood, his expression filled with anger as he glared at the Twin Sword Sages and roared.

"Kill me! Kill me! You two scoundrels! The honor of Violet Flower cannot be insulted by you!"

"Oh oh oh~" Zoey sat on a wet rock, mocking Chapman on the ground, "You're just a dog of the British bandit dynasty, what honor do you have?"

"Don't slander us! Come on! Give me a quick death! What kind of hero are you if you toy with a knight like this?!" Chapman angrily shouted.

"Why should we go easy on enemies? You have your creed, and we have ours." Zoey's eyes looked at Chapman like he was an ant, "Do you think I don't want to kill you? We're just waiting for a man, a man strong enough to be exciting, so you're just our toy for now, to kill time...hehehe..."

"A man?" Chapman's mind was filled with doubt.

"That man will bring a key, a precious treasure that will bring back our former kingdom." Zoey looked at her severed arm and said viciously, "When that man comes, I'll personally kill him, and then kill his wife, leaving no one alive!"

Chapman didn't understand at all, looking confused.

"Joy, continue to torture him, I want to hear his pleasant screams..." Zoey commanded.

"My brother is right..." Joy continued to hold the dagger and frequently hurt Chapman's flesh, making him experience the clearest pain.

The small dagger's wounds weren't fatal, but each time it felt like a piece of flesh was being cut off, the pain was heart-wrenching.

"Uggghhh...

Chapman bit his teeth, enduring the pain and not letting himself cry out, the cut wound exposing red nerves being poured with rainwater.

"You two demons! Even if I die, I won't let you off!"

"Hmmmmm..." Zoey laughed, her shoulders shaking, and said sickeningly, "I love seeing you angry to the point of wanting to kill me, but having no way to do it, that's right! It's this kind of expression, so interesting!"

Chapman bit his teeth, enduring the pain of the dagger cutting across his ribs, his vicious eyes wanting to scrape off a piece of flesh from Zoey!

"What Violet Flower Knights, just a group of trash huddled together, like a group of kids wearing open-crotch pants, holding wooden swords and playing a knight game, stupid! Ignorant! Naive! Hahahaha..." Zoey looked down at Chapman, belittling the thing he had been guarding, worthless.

Chapman's face turned even redder, and he glared at Zoey angrily, "If a few more Thorn Knights come, you'll still be able to laugh!"

"Hmm, I'll tell you the truth, no matter how many come, it's useless, they will still be killed by our Fusion Technique, what Thorn Shield is fragile like rotten wood, laughable! Hahahaha..." Zoey cracked a smile, revealing black and rotten teeth, although her smile and mask were half-broken, it still looked extremely eerie, "I'm a bit regretful now, why didn't you bring more Thorn Knights, so I could eliminate them all at once."

Joy mechanically stabbed Chapman's flesh with a dagger, like he couldn't hear anything.

Chapman's eyelids twitched violently, his mouth corners trembled uncontrollably, and it seemed like smoke was coming out of his head.

He silently hated his own incompetence, feeling that the death of Sahardin and himself were connected.

If he had investigated more clearly, allowing the other Thorn Knights to pass, perhaps the outcome would have been completely different.

In the end, it turned into this sorry state, his own dereliction of duty! Bringing shame to the entire Violet Flower Knights...

"Cough ahhh...

Chapman endured the physical pain and let out a low roar, but it turned into a cough when it reached his mouth.

The only thing he could feel now was deep despair, reduced to being entertainment for two Saint-tier enemies, extremely humiliating.

Chapman's eyes were blank, having lost all expectations for the future.

What knight spirit, what Violet Flower's honor, all became worthless.

History always evolves surprisingly similarly, when deeply trapped in the quagmire of despair.

There will always be heroes who stand up and reignite the fire of hope.

At the foot of the mountain, a sharp horse's neigh suddenly sounded, as if it could tear the sky apart.

The rainstorm shook the border volcano.

Thunder mixed with lightning flashed through the dark clouds.

Chapman blankly looked towards the mountain, the heavy rain mist like a gauze curtain, blocking his vision, making things unclear.

A black and majestic horse, a raincoat draped on its body, a hood covering his face, but it was possible to sense his gaze fixating here.

Who had arrived?

This dark knight-like man...

Chapman's attention was attracted, unable to determine the other party's identity.

"He's here! He's finally here!" Zoey excitedly stood up, her whole body shaking with excitement, "Only that man is worthy of being our opponent! Our ultimate technique has finally found an equal match! Today is definitely a day worth remembering!"

A drop of cold sweat slid down Chapman's forehead as he watched Zoey's frenzied behavior, thinking, who was the knight below? Why did the Twin Sword Sages become so excited?

Zoey picked up a thin sword and rushed towards the mountain.

"Joy, we're..."

Merlin dismounted his horse and looked up at the volcano in front of him.

The drizzling rain made him unclear about the situation.

However, it didn't take long for Zoey and Joy to walk out of the dark forest.

Merlin narrowed his eyes, his hand on the hilt of his sword, seemingly smiling, "You actually came out to greet me?"

"It seems I have quite a bit of face~"

"But this time it's not as simple as just cutting off an arm..."

title: Chapter 12 — Monthly Ticket Update
content:
Chapter 12 — Monthly Ticket Update

Volume 5 · Chapter 12

The Twin Sword Saints had no intention of launching a sneak attack; they seemed determined to crush Merlin head-on.

This open and honorable duel inevitably stirred a bit of excitement.

Dark clouds hung low in the sky, and the torrential rain ravaged the earth without restraint.

The Twin Sword Saints stood before Merlin, straight swords in hand.

Rainwater streamed along the blades, condensing and flowing over the sharp edges.

On this night swept by the storm, everything was filled with a chilling, deadly atmosphere, making one afraid to even breathe.

A careless smile played on Merlin's face; that alone, with its infuriating expression, was enough to make his enemies furious.

Coupled with his mouth full of cheeky taunts, countless people wanted to kill this arrogant bastard.

Zoe glanced at his empty left arm and snorted, "I will naturally repay you for my left arm. I advise you to keep your idle chatter to a minimum, or you might get yourself killed by your own arrogance!"

"Ha, I've always been this way. There are many who can't stand me..." Merlin spread his hands. This was just his nature, and he doubted he could change it.

"Hmph!" Zoe snorted again, speaking calmly, "The fact that we two brothers dare to appear before you means we certainly aren't afraid of you. Relying on our Fusion Secret Art, we might even be able to instantly kill you. Prepare yourself, bastard!"

"Oh? That impressive?" Merlin said expressionlessly.

"Our Fusion Secret Art has never lost. So what if you killed the Frost Holy Dragon?" Zoe paused, speaking seriously.

"When we two brothers get serious, that massive offensive power can also instantly kill the Frost Holy Dragon."

Although Zoe knew Merlin was extremely powerful and wouldn't be easily defeated, he had confidence in the Fusion Secret Art he shared with his younger brother. That super-powered offensive capability was enough to tear apart any opponent.

Rarely encountering a rival of equal strength, Zoe was very interested in testing the limits of the Fusion Secret Art!

Having experienced countless battles, Zoe and Joey had never tasted defeat, remaining invincible thanks to their Fusion Secret Art.

Merlin was the same; relying on his Level 999 Draw Sword Slash, he had yet to meet a worthy opponent.

Both sides represented their own undefeated legends. Past and present were about to clash fiercely, deciding the victor right here!

"I'm slightly interested now. You'd better do your best. Don't think that just because you brought another mummy along, you can create the illusion that you can compete on the same stage as me. If you still get chopped down by me in a moment, you'll lose face terribly." Merlin reminded them with a half-smile, his ruby eyes flashing with contempt.

"You're just a bastard who knows how to talk big. I'll definitely make you cry in a moment!" Zoe roared angrily, deeply dissatisfied with Merlin's attitude.

"Make me cry? What are you two? You have no right to stand opposite me." Merlin raised his head, his ruby-like eyes instantly seeming to become the only color in heaven and earth. "But since you are so eager to come and seek death, then attack without hesitation. I will use facts to tell you that the gap in power is beyond dimensions..."

Zoe felt a trace of pressure. The sharp and domineering aura radiating from Merlin was indeed somewhat terrifying.

However, this pressure vanished in a flash, replaced by a surge of anger rushing straight to his head.

Zoe couldn't stand Merlin and had no intention of wasting words; he was ready to fight directly. But before that, there was one more important matter.

"Cut the crap! Did you bring the key?"

Merlin pulled the key from his chest pocket and waved it loosely in front of Zoe. "This is the one, right?"

Zoe took a close look and was instantly delighted. As long as the key was brought, he could fight without any reservations.

"My wife... ah, pfft!" Merlin's expression turned strange, and he rephrased, "Where is my roommate?"

"Want to see your wife? Of course, no problem. But there are only two ways: one is to step over our corpses, and the second is to meet your wife in hell! In hell!" Zoe said ferociously, deciding to kill Merlin directly and snatch the key. He would use his proud ultimate technique to settle the score with this powerful enemy!

"Heh, what big... " Merlin reached back to grip the katana at his waist, speaking calmly, "You've slightly angered me, so just obediently die to atone for your sins, worthless trash..."

"Joey!" Zoe bellowed.

"What brother says is correct." Joey echoed woodenly.

The Twin Sword Saints, straight swords in hand, assumed the same stance they had used to kill Sahadin, coiling like beasts ready to pounce.

Indeed, Merlin had made the brothers feel pressure, so they went all out from the start, showing absolutely no mercy.

In this battle, the Twin Sword Saints intended to decide the outcome in an instant, ending the fight with their strongest skill.

In the stormy dark night, lightning flashed through the clouds, as if demons were peering at them.

The strong wind tore the curtain of rain back and forth, carrying a unique rhythm that made one hold their breath.

On the mountain.

With all four limbs severed, Chapman stared wide-eyed at the situation below, completely motionless.

Although he couldn't see clearly, he could still make out the general picture.

Chapman was now severely injured; he could only strain his neck to watch from the sidelines, unable to do anything.

Good heavens!

Using such a terrifying technique right from the start!

Who is that person in the black raincoat on the opposite side!

Actually forcing the Twin Sword Saints to this extent?

He must be a powerhouse of equal standing, no less than Lord Sahadin.

However, this mysterious guy could never defeat the Twin Sword Saints.

Because I saw that technique with my own eyes. Even Lord Sahadin, known as the Shield of Thorns, was instantly killed by it. How could he possibly win?

Aside from the First Thorn Knight, I fear no one in Great Britain could defeat the Twin Sword Saints...

Chapman had already sung a dirge for Merlin in his heart, envisioning the same ending of being instantly killed by the Twin Sword Saints.

"Defeat in our Secret Art! This is the price for your arrogance!" Zoe roared.

"What brother says is correct." Joey echoed calmly.

"Heh..." Merlin responded expressionlessly.

The moment the Twin Sword Saints moved, they instantly transformed into a pitch-black tornado resembling a drill, rotating and writhing while emitting a "hiss-ha" roar.

This ferocious momentum seemed even more powerful than the Purgatory Storm just now, causing the low-hanging dark clouds in the sky to shift and rotate along with it.

"Arrogant bastard! Leave your life here!"

Zoe's voice came from within the depths. The Purgatory Storm rushed straight at Merlin like a beast. This explosive offensive power seemed poised to destroy heaven and earth!

"Such a weak technique, and you dare use it as a capital for pride? Truly ridiculous."

Merlin assumed a draw-sword stance, his gaze burning like a red torch.

He stared at the roaring Purgatory Storm surging toward him, his heart completely tranquil.

With a crisp sound, Merlin drew his sword. A desperate, deadly sword aura instantly exploded on the spot!

The Twin Sword Saints' Purgatory Storm was brutally sliced in half, instantly neutralizing this highly offensive secret art.

The brothers' figures emerged from the storm, their bodies devoid of any vitality. With a "plop," they fell into the muddy water behind Merlin, lying completely still.

Both of them bore obvious sword wounds, cut in a straight line. Clearly, they had been killed by a single strike from Merlin!

The torrential rain danced wildly in the wind, beating down on one living man and two corpses. That proud silhouette resembled the Grim Reaper of the night.

The congealed blood on the blade was washed away by the rain, dripping to the ground and flowing slowly...

Without a single expression on his face, Merlin vigorously flicked his black katana to clean the weapon, then skillfully sheathed it.

He turned back to look calmly at the corpses of the Twin Sword Saints, gave a thumbs-down, and said arrogantly:

"This is the gap in power that transcends dimensions."

"You two weaklings have witnessed it, haven't you?"

"You actually thought you could kill me?"

"You're still far from it."

("V- ~).~~

title: Chapter 13
content:
Chapter 13

Volume 5 · Chapter 13

On the mountain.

Chapman stretched his neck as far as it would go, staring dumbfounded at what was happening down below.

Even though the torrential rain made it impossible for him to see the specific details clearly.

The outcome was painfully obvious — the Twin Sword Saints had been instantly annihilated by that mysterious figure in the raincoat!

There didn't even seem to be much of a fight —

The Twin Sword Saints activated their strongest secret technique, the mysterious man suddenly drew his sword!

And then.... there was no more then. The battle was that simple.....

But this outcome, where pure strength completely overwhelmed, and a single slash ended the fight in one stroke, left Chapman utterly stunned, his jaw dropping right there on the spot!

Good heavens?!

What in the world was going on?!

What on earth happened down at the foot of the mountain?!

The impossibly powerful Twin Sword Saints were slain with a single blow!

Two Saint-tier strongmen of such formidable power, and they couldn't even withstand one strike from that man?!

Chapman, who had already been face-slapped so many times he could no longer think, felt his knowledge was utterly incapable of explaining the reality he was seeing with his own eyes.

He had personally witnessed the Twin Sword Saints' powerful secret technique — that was an绝技 that even Lord Sahadin, known as the Thorns Shield, could not defend against!

Yet that almost unpierceable technique was dissolved by that mysterious man down below, and then countered with overwhelming, ruthless force that destroyed the Twin Sword Saints?

This left Chapman utterly bewildered. If he told anyone about this, chances are no one would believe him.

At this moment, Chapman's entire worldview had been recalibrated by Merlin, giving him a brand-new understanding of what the term "powerful" truly meant.

He stretched his neck like an ostrich, his eyeballs nearly popping out of their sockets, which looked rather comical.

Chapman had assumed the Twin Sword Saints' fused secret technique was already among the top-tier unparalleled skills, but before a true master, it was nothing whatsoever!

That man seemed to have used merely the most ordinary drawing-slash, without any special technique at all, and directly annihilated the Twin Sword Saints.

If that mysterious man actually got serious, he would surely be even more powerful!

Chapman didn't dare imagine further. Cold sweat poured down his forehead in streams.

He felt Merlin must be a hidden master of extraordinary strength. With such power, perhaps only the First Thorns Knight in Great Britain could be mentioned in the same breath; no one else could possibly compete on the same stage!

But such a powerful man was certainly no unknown nobody — then who exactly was he?

Chapman couldn't help but start speculating about the identity of the mysterious man below, feeling that there weren't many people with such strength——

Someone who could wield a Japanese katana to supernatural perfection; someone who used overwhelming force to annihilate two Saint-tier powerhouses. Could it be....

Chapman stared at Merlin's figure below, gradually matching it perfectly with the silhouette of a certain person, with not the slightest sense of incongruity.

That's right! It was the legendary great swordmaster of Elgin, a figure whispered about countless times by countless people throughout Great Britain!

That legendary figure who, half a year ago, annihilated two pirate kings in Elgin and saved the city!

The embodiment of power and justice! The savior in the hearts of countless common folk! The mysterious nameless hero!

Other than the legendary great swordmaster of Elgin, Chapman really couldn't think of anyone else who could annihilate two Saint-tier powerhouses in a single blow.

Perhaps the First Thorns Knight, or the president of the Purple Gold Adventurers Guild in London, might also be capable, but that mysterious figure below certainly wasn't either of them.

That powerful figure, the black Japanese katana, the outstanding swordsmanship — if it wasn't the legendary Elgin Swordmaster, who else could it be?

Chapman hadn't witnessed the legend from half a year ago, but from what he'd heard through word of mouth, he still knew some things.

And now, every detail of that mysterious man below matched the descriptions people gave, which had already convinced Chapman that he was indeed that legendary figure!

A flicker of admiration passed through Chapman's eyes as he looked at Merlin; he was starting to trend toward becoming a fangirl....

Down at the foot of the mountain.

Merlin, clad in his black raincoat, looked up at the dark, oppressive sky.

Giant raindrops splashed onto his cheeks.

"Let's go, pick up that troublesome woman Alice and head b—

Merlin lowered his head and began walking toward the volcano, slightly pulling down his hood.

Chapman saw Merlin approaching closer and closer, and his emotions couldn't help but stir. He even felt a bit like a young girl seeing her idol, her heart fluttering.

"Excellency! Excellency!"

Chapman called out to Merlin, wanting to say a few words to him. That mysterious figure hidden beneath the black raincoat was quite intriguing and easily stirred one's curiosity.

If possible, Chapman really wanted to see the true face of the legendary Elgin Swordmaster. Especially after hearing all those legendarily passed-down stories, his interest in this Great Britain hero who was both righteous and unorthodox only grew stronger.

Merlin didn't stop his steps. He completely ignored Chapman, heading straight toward the shrine atop the mountain. He had come to rescue Alice and had no interest in dealing with extra matters.

Seeing Chapman lying on the ground like a dead dog, Merlin directly assumed he was asking for help, wanting Merlin to tend to his injuries.

But Merlin wasn't in the mood for that right now. Better to avoid trouble than seek it out — keep your distance.

"Huh?"

Chapman was slightly surprised, not expecting the legendary Elgin Swordmaster to be so aloof. But he didn't get angry either, since there were plenty of strong individuals with strange temperaments.

Seeing the mysterious national idol of Great Britain walking further away, Chapman couldn't help but feel a bit anxious and called out loudly.

"Legendary Great Swordmaster of Elgin!"

Merlin suddenly stopped in his tracks, wondering what he had done this time that caused someone to misunderstand....

"You are indeed the Legendary Great Swordmaster of Elgin, correct?" Chapman asked loudly.

"So what of it?" Merlin responded indifferently. He was wearing a raincoat right now, and his adventurer certificate was inside; no one could see his name or identity.

Receiving an answer, Chapman's heart couldn't help but swell with excitement.

Although Merlin had his back turned to Chapman, concealing his true appearance, and the heavy rain obscured visibility, being acknowledged with a response was still enough to excite him.

"Swordmaster, may I ask you a question?"

"Hurry up, I'm in a hurry. If you dare ask me 'which company has the best excavator techniques,' you're dead." Merlin responded with resignation.

Chapman was overjoyed and flattered, feeling that he absolutely had to ask this well — this might go down in history.

"Then... Swordmaster, do you fight for the justice in your heart?"

"You guess..." Merlin didn't want to answer such a boring question and turned to leave.

Chapman was flustered and bewildered in the wind and rain — he was actually letting himself guess?

Still, Chapman was willing to believe that the Elgin Swordmaster was righteous, because in recent times, the remnants of the fallen kingdom had caused an uproar, making the common people deeply unsettled.

And today the Elgin Swordmaster appeared here, personally slaying the Twin Sword Saints — if not for justice, then for what?

"What a shy大人....."

Chapman watched Merlin disappear from his field of vision, recalling what Sahadin had once said.

He now somewhat understood why more and more people were beginning to praise the Elgin Swordmaster.

It simply came down to the fact that Great Britain needed a hero right now — a commoner hero.

They didn't need some lofty, condescending knight lord, but rather a true executor of justice.

In the present moment, the Elgin Swordmaster's powerful and righteous image was extraordinarily charming, possessing inexhaustible appeal.

Chapman's excited feelings were hard to quell, a mysterious flush still on his face——

"I never expected I'd actually get to speak with the legendary Great Swordmaster of Elgin."

"When I get back, I'll have stories to boast about for the rest of my life."

Chapter 14 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 5 · Chapter 14

Temple. "How could this be?!" "Zoe and Joey were actually defeated instantly!" Kopfeil's face changed drastically, he retreated in shock, almost falling over. Through the crystal ball, he had already been fully aware of everything happening below the mountain. Seeing the Twin Sword Saints being instantly killed, his heart was greatly shaken. Although he had long heard Zoe say that the adventurer was strong, he never imagined he would be this strong, it's absurd! Kopfeil knows the Twin Sword Saints well, knowing their fusion secret technique is extremely powerful; neither Bernard nor Carolina could unleash such a mighty move. Yet they were killed in one blow by a mere black iron adventurer! How incomprehensible! Kopfeil even doubts the Twin Sword Saints are genuine powerhouses, their achievements just boasted. Although Kopfeil is shocked, he is not at a loss. Kopfeil feels that even if Merlin is this strong, he still has a chance to turn the tide. Because Alice, this hostage, is still in his hands; Merlin, no matter how formidable, cannot act rashly. Zoe said this couple is very affectionate, so he can just take advantage of that. As long as Merlin obediently hands over the key to the Hell Burning Legion, everyone who opposes him will die! Kopfeil hurried back to his throne, twisted the black lacquered armrest, as if triggering some mechanism. The entire temple began to rumble and shake; Kopfeil barely steadied his frail figure with his wand. One side of the temple's floor slowly opened, and from inside a red light flashed, fiery magma bubbling and gurgling. The scorching heat instantly swept across the great hall, making one feel as if in a boiler room. The wall behind the throne also changed, like building blocks breaking apart, and finally the entire underground cage was hoisted up, suspended in midair. This temple was originally used to punish prisoners; the mechanism from over 400 years ago still works. "Eh? What's happening?!" Alice exclaimed in the cage, startled, not knowing what was going on. "Ah... Alice..." Shirley appeared a bit weak, her face pallid, this sudden change left her at a loss. "Don't... Alice grabbed Shirley's little hand, calming her down, though she herself was extremely nervous. Shirley looked at Alice, pressed her hand against her chest, trying not to be afraid. This little princess had always been protected by her father; now reduced to this state, she could only rely on Alice. However, after spending so much time together, the two have become quite familiar, chatting and laughing. Especially the bandage on Shirley's wrist, which Alice personally wrapped, making her feel touched. Shirley never imagined that after knowing each other for such a short time, Alice would care for her so much. She doesn't know that Alice treats everyone this way; it's just her nature. In fact, Alice feels a little guilty, her own strength lacking, she could only watch Shirley being bled helplessly. So Alice is frustrated with her own inadequacy, and can only comfort Shirley to lift her spirits. Alice saw the figure in the black robe below, Kopfeil, and couldn't help but shout, "Hey! What are you trying to do?!" "Hehehe, what am I up to?" Kopfeil let out a series of cold laughs, "You'll find out soon enough!" "You bastard! Let us out!!" Alice couldn't help but roar. "That's impossible; you're my important bargaining chip, and I still need you to exchange for the precious key." Kopfeil said coldly. "...Then let this elf girl go!" Alice thought letting Shirley leave would also be fine. "Alice..." Shirley felt a bit guilty inside. "Don't think about it; I don't care at all about the elf's life or death, because once your husband brings the key, I will gain eternal life, and you will all die together! Having a companion on the road to hell isn't bad, right?" Kopfeil had no intention of letting anyone go as long as he got the key; he would become the new ruler of this land. "Dream on, old bastard!" Alice furrowed her brows, feeling a hint of pressure. "Hmph!" Kopfeil gave a cold snort, twisted the mechanism, and the hanging cage began to move again. The two girls grew tense again, not knowing where this iron cage was leading. The sound of gears meshing rumbled, slowly moving toward the scorching magma direction, finally stopping directly above it. The rolling magma emitted a fierce light, dyeing the girls' faces red, with a sensation of being roasted over fire; the atmosphere suddenly became tense. "Miss Alice, we... we..." Shirley clung tightly to Alice, wanting to speak but stopping, her expression full of fear, tears beginning to swirl in her eye sockets. "Don't be afraid, it's fine." Alice gently patted Shirley's back a few times, after comforting her, she turned to Kopfeil with anger and said, "What are you going to do to us?!" Kopfeil didn't speak, but twisted the mechanism. The three iron chains suspending the cage instantly broke one, making a "clang" sound! "Yah ah ah!" Shirley clung tightly to Alice, terrified out of her wits. Alice's face also turned pale, looking at the bubbling magma below, she felt as if she were about to fall. The cage now only had two iron chains left, becoming extremely unstable, swaying above the magma, ready to drop at any moment. Now Alice's neck wore an iron ring that restricted her magic and battle aura, equivalent to an ordinary person; if she fell into the magma, death would be certain. "Do you know now what I'm up to? Hehehe." Kopfeil let out a sinister laugh. "You'll get your comeuppance, bastard!" Alice's brows knitted together, she cursed fiercely. "How many people have cursed me to die, yet I'm still fine?" Kopfeil spread his hands. Alice fell silent; now her life was in his hands, she couldn't rashly provoke Kopfeil, better to say less. "Miss Alice, I still don't want to die; my father will surely be heartbroken, why is this happening, I really want to see my father again—" Shirley began to sob, the redness and swelling in her eyes never fading. A little "Don't worry, someone will come to save us." Alice softly comforted Shirley. A play The two girls shivered in the cage, comforting each other; in such dire straits they could only wait for someone else's rescue. Until now, Alice still didn't know whether Merlin had come or not; she felt uncertain, a bit anxious. Thinking about Merlin's usual conduct, perhaps he simply didn't care about her life or death. Alice couldn't help but feel worried, thinking that if she had been friendlier toward Merlin usually, things might have been better... "Boom!" A loud bang, the temple's heavy doors were smashed open by someone. A violent gust of wind rushed in, extinguishing rows of torches. Merlin gripped the waist-worn katana at his side, step by step walking to the center of the hall. He lifted the hood of his raincoat, revealing slightly damp, stubborn blond hair. Merlin stopped, staring straight at the figure hidden beneath the black robe, Kopfeil, the corner of his mouth turning up in a meaningful arc. "Yo, old...." title: Chapter 15 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 15 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 5 · Chapter 15

"Ugh..."

Copperfield was forced back half a step by Merlin's presence, not expecting him to be so fierce.

A gale swept up water spray, whooshing into the great hall.

Merlin frowned slightly, sensing that this Copperfield wasn't particularly strong — judging by his pressure, high-tier at best.

He felt a touch of disappointment. He'd thought the necromancers' boss would be Saint-tier, which could buy more time to alleviate the curse.

But it turned out to be just a petty high-tier. Looks like those Saint-tier undead are also under someone's thumb.

Merlin didn't know that Copperfield could freely extinguish the Four Heroes' soul flames; otherwise, why would four Saint-tier powerhouses obey a mere high-tier?

"You've finally come..." Copperfield narrowed his eyes, feeling the key to turning the tide was about to fall into his hands.

"Mmph..."

Alice pouted, hands gripping the bars, a pitiful expression on her face. She was a little excited inside — she hadn't expected Merlin to actually come. She'd thought this bastard would leave her to die.

She hadn't expected him to show such uncharacteristic humanity at a time like this. But Merlin's usual self was completely heartless. Suddenly taking the initiative to save her — could it be he's fallen for her?

Alice's mind raced like a lovesick maiden.

But then she immediately thought of Elgin, the Great Sword Saint she'd secretly loved for ages, and shook her head like a rattle drum —

No no no! My heart belongs to the Great Sword Saint Elgin, not Merlin!

I can't be bewitched by this demon. He's the evil Great Demon Lord!

Changing my heart this easily — how cheap am I!?

Shirley watched Alice from the side, finding her reaction very strange.

She'd always shown the Valkyrie's strong front, but the moment that blond man showed up, she instantly revealed a shy, little-girl side.

Could it be—

"Miss Alice, is that man your husband?"

"That's right, my husb— pfft!" Alice hastily corrected herself, emphasizing, "In name only! Not for real..."

"Wh-what do you mean?" Shirley asked curiously, thinking husband and wife are husband and wife — what's this "in name only" business?

"It's a long story..." Alice replied awkwardly, then started snapping at Merlin, "So slow! How come you took so long to get here!? Did you do it on purpose, wanting me to die here? You bastard!"

Merlin's attention had been on Copperfield the whole time; he hadn't seen Alice locked in the cage on the other side.

Now seeing this woman still alive and kicking, the conflicted feeling in his heart instantly vanished.

But her terrible attitude right upon meeting made the veins on Merlin's forehead throb. He was very displeased.

"You trouble-making woman who only causes chaos — you still have the nerve to yell at me? Have some self-awareness, you idiot!"

"Ah!?" Alice's breath caught. She puffed up and retorted, "What kind of attitude is that!? Think carefully — when you were wandering the streets, who took you in? Is this how you treat your benefactor!?"

"Whether a super-troublesome girl like you lives or dies doesn't matter at all, okay?" Merlin frowned. Just seeing Alice annoyed him. "But this grandpa was merciful enough to come save a deadweight like you, so shut your trap right now, got it?"

"Who wants your pity! Let me make this clear — even if you save me, I won't be grateful, and don't even think about using this to win my favor. I'd never fall for a heartless jerk like you! Hmph~!" Alice's mouth nearly reached the sky, as if she'd die instantly if she didn't suppress Merlin.

"Hah!? Win your favor? Are you kidding?" Merlin looked at Alice in disbelief, unable to stop himself from snapping back, "Your favor's worth a few gold coins? I came to save you because of our shared debt. If you die, I'm the one stuck paying it alone. How could I let a bimbo like you walk away scot-free? I'm screwed, so you don't get to be comfortable either! Let's mutually destroy each other!"

"You... you despicable bastard!" Alice was so angry smoke nearly came out of her head.

"Emmmmmm..." Shirley watched for a good while. She hadn't expected them to start bickering the moment they met, but the vibe she got was—

Their marriage is actually really good. It makes a person a little envious...

The two remaining iron chains supporting the cage suddenly snapped — one more gave way!

This sudden development made the already tottering iron cage even more precarious!

"Kyaaaaaah!" Shirley screamed, clutching Alice's slender body, trembling uncontrollably.

A cold sweat trickled down Alice's forehead. She looked down at the searing magma below, feeling death drawing closer.

The whole cage swayed dangerously, supported by only a single chain now. The situation had become critical.

Copperfield's hand rested on the mechanism lever of the throne. He spoke gloomily, "My apologies for interrupting your touching reunion, but for your wife's safety, please hand over the key first, would you?"

"She's not my wife..." Merlin remarked blandly, pulling the key from his breast pocket and dangling it in his hand. "This key, right?"

"Yes! That's it! Give it to me!" Even with his face hidden beneath the black robe, Copperfield's greedy gaze was unmistakable. He extended a withered palm, hoping Merlin would place the key in it.

"I have a few questions I want to ask?" Merlin said with a half-smile, eyes narrowing.

"You think you have the leverage to negotiate with me?" Copperfield made a move to activate the mechanism, ready to drop Alice and Shirley into the magma.

"Wait, I'm not trying to negotiate. Just a few questions." Merlin spread his hands, feigning innocence.

"Fine. Since you're so persistent, I'll humor you and listen." Copperfield was brimming with confidence. The man's wife was in his hands — what tricks could he possibly pull?

"I heard this key opens a passage between Hell and the mortal world. Is that true?" Merlin asked.

"Seems you know quite a bit. That's right — it opens the way between the mortal world and Hell." Copperfield replied in a raspy voice.

Alice was shocked. Everyone's souls went to Hell — but did such a place really exist? And what would happen if the two worlds were connected?

"So there really is such a thing..." Shirley murmured, her expression turning worried.

"Eh? Miss Shirley, do you know the key's secret?" Alice asked curiously.

"I'm not entirely sure. I only heard my father say Hell truly exists — it's a place of torment for souls, where light never reaches. The undead of Hell always want to escape their suffering and come to the mortal world to establish a new kingdom of the dead..." Shirley whispered to Alice.

Alice knitted her brows. True or false? She'd never heard of such a thing. Could it be because elven and human cultures differ?

"If the gates between the two worlds can truly be opened, the consequences are unimaginable — a crisis for the entire world..." Shirley said, uncertain and alarmed.

"Is that so? So it's true. This key comes from Hell. Have you had contact with apostles from Hell?" Merlin asked casually.

"You know about Hell's apostles too?! Their existence is a secret — who are you?" Copperfield felt a flicker of surprise.

"No need to know who I am. Just treat me as a small-time Black Iron adventurer. Right now I need you to answer my doubts." Merlin smiled, seeming quite interested in the apostles.

Alice understood less and less. What on earth were Hell's apostles!?

"You know of the Hell apostles' existence — you must have made deals with Hell too, right?" Copperfield probed tentatively.

"Unfortunately I refused that lucrative deal. Because I refuse to serve anyone. If I can be a king among the demon race, why would I be a subject in Hell?" Merlin smiled indifferently. He had nothing more to ask, and spoke with contempt, "As for you, a pitiful wretch who's made contact with Hell's apostles — you're already Satan's running dog, aren't you? Originally human, don't you have even a shred of dignity?"

"Dignity? Ridiculous! Absolute power is dignity! Do you know what the great Satan has bestowed upon me?" Copperfield spread his arms, his black robe fluttering in the wind. He shouted fanatically, his voice echoing through the entire temple—

"As long as I can open Hell's gates..."

"The great Satan will grant me endless life!"

"Eternal youth!"

"Supreme authority!"

"And a burning legion that sweeps all before it!"

"I shall rule all of Great Britain..."

"No! I shall control the entire world!"

"Become the new master of this world!"

"I shall be invincible!"

Alice and Shirley in the cage went pale. They looked at Copperfield like a madman. He was clearly ancient, yet now he seemed years younger — perhaps everything he said was true.

Though the two girls still didn't understand what was happening, Copperfield's words sounded incredibly powerful.

Endless life, eternal youth — surely only a god could grant that!?

Alice felt deep worry. That key absolutely could not be given to Copperfield.

Whether his words were true or false, innocent people could not be placed in danger!

"Possessing these is what dignity means. Can you understand?" Copperfield's tone was icy, like a king about to descend upon a new world.

"Alright alright, I get it. Quit your yapping." Merlin raised a hand to silence Copperfield, speaking carelessly, "Long story short — I give you the key, you become invincible, OP as hell, so strong you fly, smash whoever you don't like into the ground, right?"

"Right, exactly. But coming from your mouth it sounds so LAME." Copperfield broke into a waterfall of sweat with black lines of embarrassment. A bit awkward.

"Fine, I'll satisfy you..." Merlin tossed the key straight to Copperfield.

The red key traced a beautiful arc through the air, jingling as it landed, stopping right before Copperfield.

Copperfield's eyes went wide. His lips moved but no words came out. He'd actually gotten the key this easily — he found it unbelievable!

"As you wish..." Merlin made a "go ahead" gesture, arrogance dripping from every word—

"Use your strongest form and dance to your heart's content before me!"

Alice and Shirley in the cage instantly gaped in shock.

Both their little mouths formed perfect "O"s, as if they could fit an apple inside.

They never expected Merlin to do this! This incomprehensible outcome was simply impossible to believe!
