title: Chapter 16
content:
Chapter 16

Volume 5 · Chapter 16

Nobody expected Merlin to make such a choice.

Even if it meant putting the entire world in danger, he would let the other side give it their all.

Copedia was just a high-ranking mage, but just now his rambling monologue had sparked a sliver of interest in Merlin.

How strong was Hell's Burning Legion? That was what Merlin wanted to find out.

However, Merlin knew Hell was a gathering place of the undead—no matter how many you killed, it wouldn't make a difference.

But since they were fighting anyway, not letting the opponent go all out would be no fun at all. This was Merlin's arrogant nature.

The two girls in the cage stared blankly at Merlin. Just now, Copia had made it clear—once you get the key, you become incredibly powerful. Yet Merlin casually handed the key to Copia. This suicidal move was simply baffling!

Even if Merlin was arrogant and looked down on everything, his treatment of enemies was just too terrible, right?

Helping the other side become a complete and powerful being... who in their right mind would believe that?

The two girls couldn't understand Merlin anymore, unable to grasp his train of thought.

Sherry's expression grew worried as she watched Merlin's figure, thinking to herself, what was going on? She couldn't sense any magical pressure or martial aura from him at all—he didn't look like a strong person. So why was he willingly giving the other side the chance to grow stronger? Not all human men were idiots, right?

"Hey! Merlin! Are you insane?!" Alice couldn't hold it in anymore, shouting loudly, "Why did you hand over the key so easily?"

"Shut up, you slut..." Merlin's temples twitched with annoyance, "Do I need you to tell me what to do?"

5 SE novel

"You dare say that! Your whole family are the real sluts!" Alice, furious, complained, "Are you deaf? That old pervert said once he gets the key, he'll rule the world. Why did you give him the key? Doesn't that put a lot of innocent people in danger? Can you think before you act? Why are you always so reckless?"

"Shut up... Merlin rolled his eyes, casually saying, "I just want to see what this old guy's strongest form looks like. What does that have to do with you? You really think you can treat me like a hero? I'm suffering from a severe case of laziness, not interested in saving the world at every turn..."

Alice was at a loss for words. She remembered that Merlin had once been the Great Demon Lord, the embodiment of evil. No one would be surprised by his bad deeds.

But even an evil Great Demon Lord, this kind of reckless behavior was going too far, right?

Alice's face was red with frustration. With nothing left to say, she could only curse at Merlin.

"You idiot! Did you hear that? Idiot! Hehe~"

"Tch!" Merlin frowned in displeasure, wanting to kick that troublesome Alice out of the solar system.

Sherry looked at the situation with mixed feelings and quietly asked, "Miss Alice, is your husband really coming to save us? It feels more dangerous now than before. You two don't have some kind of grudge, do you?"

Alice's face showed three dark lines. She thought, of course there's a grudge, and a deep one.

Sherry, seeing Alice hesitate, nervously asked, "We won't die here, right?"

"...No, we won't. Although that guy is like this, he's still pretty formidable, so we should be fine." Alice said seriously.

"Miss Alice, you're just comforting me, aren't you? A person who can't sense any magical pressure or martial aura—how powerful could he really be?" Sherry felt a deep sense of despair, lowering her eyes, thinking that maybe even this mid-tier mage was stronger than Merlin. She had placed her hopes for survival in an ordinary person. How silly and naive she was.

"That guy is really strong, especially his sword-drawing slash..." Alice said casually, though she didn't want to admit it, Merlin was indeed powerful. She had seen it many times.

"But that's just a super low-level technique that doesn't even require martial aura? Brrr, the whole world is doomed..." Sherry made a face of utter despair, turning into a paper doll, her soul seeming to leave her body.

"Come on... come on, snap out of it..." Alice kept shaking Sherry, trying to comfort her.

Copedia stood there blankly, staring at the red key at his feet. He had thought it would take a lot of effort to obtain, but never expected it to be so easy.

He felt like he was dreaming—couldn't believe the key he had coveted for so long was right at his feet.

After losing so many keys, he had never managed to get one. Yet now, it was within his grasp.

Copedia's skeletal hand trembled slightly from his overwhelming emotions.

He picked up the key and examined it carefully. There was nothing wrong with it—it was a genuine Burning Legion key.

"Ha, hahaha, hahahaha!"

2 SE novel

Copedia let out a deep laugh, slowly lifting the hat on his black robe, revealing his true face—

A bare skull with not a single hair, yet etched with mysterious ancient kingdom characters.

His aged features were squeezed together, looking somewhat deformed. But those bald, sharp eyes still held their color.

His weathered skin was wrinkled like dry leather, his mouth stretched wide, revealing teeth that looked rusted.

"Hahahahahaha!"

Copedia raised his hands to the sky and laughed wildly, with a feeling of "the key is in my hand, the world is mine!"

His expression was mad, his withered hands gripping tightly, veins bulging from his fingers, making a shrill, ear-piercing screech that made people uncomfortable.

"I won! I won!"

"I shall become the master of the new world!"

"I will possess power that no one can stop, power that not even the gods can halt in my conquest!"

"The world! It has already fallen into my hands! I shall use the heads of the British royal family to forge a new throne!"

"Is that so..." Merlin said casually.

"You dare give me the key, you foolish adventurer. This is your greatest mistake!" Copedia pointed at Merlin, mocking, "Your life will be buried by your own arrogance! Because I now possess the strongest Burning Legion, a force no one can withstand! The entire world will be trampled by the Burning Legion's iron hooves, burning in Hell's endless flames!"

"Talking big, but is it really true?" Merlin's expression was very suspicious.

"Want to know if it's true? You'll see soon enough. Since you're the one who wants to die, let your blood be the offering to the Burning Legion!"

Copedia raised his staff high and began chanting an ancient curse. It wasn't like human spells—it was more like the deathly whispers of Hell's undead.

The center of the hall was suddenly filled with dark rock mist, and a strange stone statue appeared—countless arms intertwined, like petrified demons, with three keys embedded in them.

Copedia threw the fourth key he had just obtained into the air, and it automatically inserted itself into the statue.

Now all four keys were gathered together. The demons on the statue seemed to come alive, their eyes glowing red, their mouths opening in a chilling, eerie laugh.

"Kekekekeke..."

A massive magic circle lit up immediately, the red light blazing, filling the entire space in an instant, making people feel as though they were standing before the gates of Hell.

Dark aura spread out, forming a swirling vortex that suddenly shot up into the sky!

"Fools! Open your eyes wide and witness this thrilling moment!" Copedia, in a state of extreme excitement and madness, struck the ground with his staff, his eyes filled with blood vessels—

"Descend!"

"Great Burning Legion of Hell!"

"Use your rage to conquer this world!"

"For our shared master Satan, let us establish a new kingdom of the undead!"

title: Chapter 17 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 17 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 5 · Chapter 17

A violent black storm swept through the temple, as if composed of countless ghosts.

"Ohoooonnn…"

The wailing and keening rose all at once, as though they had suddenly stepped into the narrow corridors of hell.

"Hahahahahaha…"

Copperfield spread his arms wide, staring up at the black storm rising in mid-sky, and laughed maniacally without cease.

Merlin pressed down on the tachi at his waist with his hand. Even though his raincoat flapped wildly in the wind, his body remained immovable.

Not the faintest expression flickered across his face, but his red eyes narrowed as he thought, What kind of strange aura is this? It is so dense—it has nothing to do with this world. It truly seems there is a way to connect different worlds…

Merlin found it strange because the black storm carried a heavy scent of death qi, a particular odor of hell.

Undead would grow extremely excited upon smelling it, but for living beings, inhaling too much would cause poisoning.

It also suppressed the functioning of magic power and fighting qi. Forcing the use of magic or fighting qi would deepen the poisoning.

But Merlin would not be affected at all, since his techniques required neither magic nor fighting qi.

Alice stared dazed at the black dragon whirlwind that resembled ghosts, and a bead of cold sweat slipped down her forehead.

Her own body felt uncomfortable as well—her strength failed her, her chest grew heavy, and she could barely breathe…

What is this aura? I have never encountered anything like it.

Could the legends all be true? Does hell truly exist?

And right now, the gates between the two worlds were about to be opened.

This was bad. No enemy needed to come over.

Just this strange aura alone could kill countless ordinary people!

"Cough, cough!" Shirley covered her mouth and nose and began coughing, her face turning pale, her expression slightly pained.

As an elf, her constitution was far more sensitive than that of humans, and she could easily sense the threat brought by the death qi.

"Shirley, what's wrong?" Alice asked worriedly. Although she herself was not feeling well either, Shirley's discomfort clearly exceeded her own.

"Miss Alice, don't breathe in this aura—there is danger. This overwhelming sense of evil is even stronger than that of demons," Shirley said, covering her mouth and nose so as to inhale as little as possible.

Alice covered her mouth and nose and gazed down at Merlin.

That standing back appeared completely unaffected. She muttered to herself, Could it be because Merlin is a demon, belonging to the dark faction alongside undead, that he can resist it?

In fact, Alice had only guessed half right. Merlin was also affected—just not severely.

Truly sharing the dark faction did grant Merlin a certain immunity to the death qi from hell.

But at excessively high concentrations, Merlin would still feel physically unwell.

Although Merlin was immune to magic, he certainly could not defend against "poison."

With a crashing sound, the entire temple shook, and dust and rubble rained down.

Finally, with a tremendous roar, the temple collapsed, instantly becoming an open-air platform.

Outside, the clouds remained thick and dark, and wind and rain raged on.

The rising storm of resentful spirits seemed to connect with the black clouds in the sky.

Merlin suddenly raised his head, sensing something appearing within the storm!

The two girls also looked up at the sky. Shirley, being an elf, felt an especially sharp sense of foreboding.

As the ghost storm dispersed, a magnificent stone gate appeared in the rainy night sky.

It almost spanned the entire horizon above the volcano, towering and awe-inspiring.

The gate was carved with vivid reliefs: a handsome man holding a gleaming sword, with countless undead kneeling before him.

Below were bizarre characters resembling hymns praising Satan.

"Behold! This is the Gate of Hell! The greatest legacy of the former kingdom!!!" Copperfield raised both hands high, as if cheering.

The stone gate in the sky slowly opened from its center, emitting a deep rumble.

Within, one could faintly make out a crimson world, filled with blood and flame!

Countless undead wreathed in fire emerged from the gate, yet they were still able to hover in midair! ?

They wore pitch-black armor from head to toe, their weapons equally black—made of some unknown metal?

The red flames burning within their eye sockets blazed fiercely!

The leading white-haired dragon knight undead appeared particularly powerful, his gaze sweeping over the living below, revealing a bone-chilling coldness.

"Hahahaha!" Copperfield laughed wildly, radiating the bearing of a sovereign lord. "At this very moment! Humanity welcomes a new era. The names of every person will bear my烙印, and I shall become the spokesperson of the great Satan! I shall become the king of the new era!"

The two girls were dumbfounded, looking up at the sky. Their lips trembled but no words came out, and their entire bodies shook with terror.

Shirley had never seen such a powerful legion. It was even stronger than the elite forces of the Southern United Kingdom. It truly was the undead legion from hell! The gathering oppressive pressure was beyond words.

Alice was not faring much better than Shirley. Instead, she carefully sensed the overwhelming pressure—

One, two, three…

Good heavens! There were so many Saint-tier undead that she could not even count them! ! !

Everything Copperfield had said was true—this was indeed the strongest legion!

With so many Saint-tier undead, they could annihilate any nation in the present world!

What exactly is hell? Why are there so many powerful figures here! ! !

Alice no longer knew what to say. She could only sense countless Saint-tier undead, as well as innumerable high-tier and mid-tier monsters!

"This formation is quite impressive…" Merlin said with a half-smile, thinking that even all the armies of the demon race combined might not measure up to this Burning Legion.

Alice looked worriedly at Merlin's back, her heart growing uneasy.

Although Merlin had once single-handedly wiped out the Holy Church's Crusade Army, compared to the Burning Legion he was but an ant!

Alice deeply doubted whether Merlin could continue the legend when facing such a powerful legion.

It was all Merlin's fault for acting recklessly and handing the key to Copperfield. Now everyone would face the threat of hell.

If Merlin were defeated, the truth would likely be as Copperfield claimed—the present world would become a new kingdom of the undead.

"Pathetic adventurer. Can you still say such things now?" Copperfield narrowed his eyes, speaking as though a lord above all. "With the Burning Legion, I am an invincible existence. Standing at the pinnacle of power, I shall receive the homage of all kings!"

"What a pity. I do not know about other races, but none of the Seven Lords of the demon race would ever submit to you." Merlin narrowed his eyes, assuming an iai draw stance, and said lightly, "Next, I shall perform a trick for you. Your proud army will vanish in the blink of an eye."

"Foolish mortal! Your only fate is death!" Copperfield's eyes bulged with rage as he issued the command.

The white-haired dragon knight undead in the sky let out a roar, and the entire Burning Legion moved as one.

The dense masses of undead sped straight toward Merlin.

"Merlin…" Alice murmured, gazing at his back, a trace of hope shining in her eyes.

Iron hooves thundered, and horse whinnies tore the sky.

In the storm-lashed night, a long-awaited all-out battle arrived!

The strongest legion from hell surged forward, challenging the strongest monarch of the demon race!

Their battle cries shook the heavens as they brandished sharp blades, the气息 of death rushing toward them.

Merlin closed his eyes, quietly listening to his own heartbeat as raindrops struck his calm face.

◆◆◆

◆◆

Merlin suddenly snapped his eyes open. Even as he unleashed his full-power iai draw strike, he let out a shout—

title: Chapter 18 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 18 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes

Volume 5 · Chapter 18

That moment.

Alice felt it again.

Felt it again—the same ominous pressure from a year ago.

That slash that everyone looked down on, the one that could tear through the sky with ease and cleave the earth with calm precision.

The full-power release of strength, as if even the gods themselves could be killed in an instant.

Alice understood now—this slash from Merlin was serious, holding nothing back.

Even as Merlin drew his blade, the murderous sword pressure surged forth, unleashing a terror that all gods would dread!

A 9999-level slash, its power reaching the pinnacle, carrying the momentum of splitting heaven and earth.

The roaring Legion of Combustion faltered all at once, sending countless undead into terror.

That unstoppable shockwave of military force suddenly withered.

The white-haired lich dragon knight leading them was even more shocked, its pupils burning with red flames shrinking rapidly.

The strongest legion of Hell itself was scared senseless by just one black-iron adventurer, their fighting spirit completely gone.

Even if those undead tried to flee, it was already too late.

Because the 9999-level slash moved at lightning speed, and the invisible, murderous sword pressure was like a cannonball, cutting down every enemy before them.

The sky enemy faded, the wind and rain stopped.

"So it's over. Is this the strength you're so proud of? How disappointing."

Merlin said casually, returning to his nonchalant attitude, twirling the jet-black katana in his hand.

The massive gates of Hell were torn apart by Merlin's slash, exploding on the horizon in an instant.

The explosion lit up the night like daylight, the shockwave scattering the clouds and revealing the stars of the night sky.

The Hell Legion that had been screaming just moments ago was now completely sliced apart by the slash, turned into fragments and devoured by the flames of the explosion, none surviving.

This slash was truly a force that shook the universe!

The explosion made Kupofir look even more aged, his mouth agape in shock to an unbelievable degree, nearly fainting with his eyes barely open, his lips twitching and eyebrows jumping uncontrollably—speechless.

"How... how is this possible?!?!"

What kind of strength is this?!?!

......That's way too terrifying!

My Legion of Combustion should be the strongest!

TE

ESVIKX

\二二

To think... they were all wiped out by a single slash?!?!

My grand ambitions, my dreams...

Are they all going to turn into nothing at this moment?!?!

No!!! What was my 400 years of effort all for?!?!

I, who should have become the master of the new world, why did I run into someone with such insane power?!?!

Kupofir let out a "thud" and fell to his knees, his aged face etched with exhaustion, deep lines of sorrow, and tears streaming down his cheeks.

The two girls locked in cages were equally stunned, staring at the expressionless Merlin, not knowing what to say anymore—even forgetting to beg for help.

Sherry stared blankly at Merlin, thinking, "Is this guy for real? He has no magic or combat spirit, yet he's this strong of a Saint-tier undead!"

She awkwardly thought, "Am I misunderstanding something?! This freak! There are countless Demon Lords behind him!"

And yet he still managed to defeat them all so effortlessly?!? And who could possibly subdue this big shot?!

The chances of Elkin, my male god, standing in his boots just became even slimmer.

Alice's heart burned with resentment. The stronger Merlin became, the more she wanted to step on him with her high heels.

"A person who bows and scrapes before others, begging for power—how could someone like that be worthy of the title of king? They're all undead, that's for sure."

Merlin beautifully sheathed his katana, feeling a bit regretful. So many Saint-tier...

For several years, there would be no need to struggle to survive anymore. Fear, snot, and tears all mixed together on his face.

Kupofir turned around stiffly like a robot, his eyes filled with an extremely...

A king's aura.

This sight was embarrassing enough—completely different from before, his words and actions now seemed to pull Merlin back to reality, becoming utterly useless.

Just moments ago, Kupofir had possessed the entire world, but in the blink of an eye, he was reduced to the same state as Merlin.

This felt like riding a roller coaster from heaven to hell—an excitement that normal people would find hard to accept.

"...How did you become so powerful?" he asked, bewildered.

"Huh?" Merlin furrowed his brow, thought for a moment, and replied, "I was just trying to live a laid-back life, but I got stabbed by Merlin with the same attitude."

Alice's temples throbbed as she listened. A year ago, when crossing the Ochre Strait,

She felt it was the most lethal form of invisible boasting. "How grand! Does he not have any ambition to conquer the world?"

Kupofir thought Merlin was abnormal and, unwilling to give up, pressed, "You're so powerful, you have everything you could want. Isn't that great? If you're willing, the entire world would be at your feet—endless wealth, beautiful women,

"Good things? First Demon Lord, one of the seven sources of evil."

Alice's heart skipped a beat. She was also curious about this question. As for Merlin, the former hero turned vigilante for justice, absolutely would not allow!

If there were any evil ambitions, it would make him a public enemy to everyone! He said it himself—

"Good things... Merlin shrugged slightly, his voice carrying a trace of innocence."

"Well, it does seem that way. But thinking about it more carefully, it's really troublesome."

"I'd have to overthrow countless countries and suppress all the resistance."

"Even if I succeeded in ruling the world, there would still be rebellions from time to time, requiring me to deal with various matters."

"I'd have to properly manage this world—military, politics, livelihood, and so on—all sorts of governance."

"Oh my goodness! Too troublesome! I choose to surrender to my laziness cancer across nine worlds! Long live laziness cancer!"

Alice broke into a cold sweat, trembling as she thought, "Laziness cancer saved the world, but this man refuses to conquer it. The power that could save the world is not willing to rule it..."

Kupofir suddenly found his eyes bulging, his mind reeling in shock. He possessed absolute...

"A man like this is worthless." Merlin waved his hands dismissively.

"I'm sorry, but you haven't earned the right to know my identity. Your life is so insignificant to me, and I'm too busy living my life to care about your grand dreams of world domination. Just think of me as a small black-iron adventurer from Rexxar Town, living a life where I get clothes when I need them and food when I'm hungry. As for who I really am—don't ask, you'll definitely get it wrong!"

"No... that's impossible! You're lying, aren't you?!?!"

Kupofir stared at Merlin with the same expression he'd use to look at monsters.

"Oh? Who am I?" Merlin tilted his head, stretching lazily. With a blank expression, saliva uncontrollably dripped down.

"You must be a god! A supreme god!" Kupofir fell to his knees, his soul nearly fleeing his body. "Only a god would be like this! I finally understand why I failed! Because I'm just a mortal! The great divine beings are beyond mortal comprehension!"

"Tch!" Merlin rolled his eyes, sweat trickling down his forehead, shaking his head in disbelief—

"What is going on?"

This guy was already scared out of his wits by my transcendent strength...

title: Chapter 19
content:
Chapter 19

Volume 5 · Chapter 19

Night had fallen.

The moonlight flickered faintly and dimly behind the cover of dark clouds.

Like sesame seeds scattered across the sky, countless stars dotted the clear heavens.

A covered carriage moved slowly along a country lane.

After rescuing Alice, Merlin had rented the carriage from a nearby village, intending to return to Rexem together.

Naturally, Alice hadn't forgotten the timid elven girl, so she brought Sherry along as well and even bought her a cloak to wear.

Since Sherry was an elf, her pointed ears would stand out far too much. Covering them with the cloak would help avoid unnecessary trouble.

At that moment, all three of them sat inside the carriage.

A driver still sat up front controlling the horses, leaving plenty of room inside.

The carriage swayed along its bumpy route; the journey to Rexem would take several days.

"Miss Alice... I... I want to go back..." Sherry hesitantly raised her head and asked timidly.

"Don't worry, we'll send you home." Alice turned around and spoke seriously to Sherry. "First we'll return to Rexem to rest up, then we'll take you to the Elven Embassy in London. Someone will protect you on your way back to your homeland."

"..." Sherry fell silent, anxiously eager to return to the United Kingdom. She had been missing for so long — her father would surely be very worried.

"Don't worry. We're not like the humans who captured you. We won't harm you, and we'll protect your safety. Trust me." Alice reached out and gently held Sherry's small hand, hoping to calm her down.

Sherry looked up at Alice and felt that those clear blue eyes held nothing but sincerity.

She had been kidnapped here half a year ago and wasn't very familiar with the human world; a trace of fear still lingered within her.

If she encountered bad people halfway, it would be terrible. She'd barely escaped, only to be captured again.

With Alice and their family around, she wouldn't be in any danger — after all, she had personally witnessed that terrifying blade strike.

Plus, everyone had been a bit tired lately, and resting a little would be good.

Sherry thought Alice was a very kind human girl worth trusting, so she nodded.

"Mm, I trust you, Miss Alice. But staying at your house — wouldn't that cause any trouble...?"

"Not at all! What trouble could one more person cause? You can sleep with me." Alice smiled gently.

"Sleep... sleep together with Miss Alice!?" Sherry's eyes went wide with surprise, so startled that her pointed ears pushed up the hood of her cloak.

"What's so surprising about that?" Alice asked, puzzled. She didn't see what was wrong. Was there some taboo in elven culture?

"No, no, no! If I sleep with Miss Alice, Mr. Merlin definitely wouldn't agree, and it would cause you trouble," Sherry said nervously, her courage quite lacking. "Just... just giving me a small spot on the floor to curl up and sleep would be fine..."

Alice paused, feeling that although Sherry had said it casually, it carried a sense of habitual hardship that made her heart ache. "You're a guest, how could you possibly sleep on the floor?"

"But Mr. Merlin..." Sherry glanced briefly at Merlin, reluctant to say more.

"What does he have to do with it? Don't mind him." Alice spoke in a provocative tone.

Merlin sat across from the two girls, quiet from the beginning. He leaned against the carriage, hugging his legs, and gazed out at the vast starry sky.

"How can I not care? You two are married. At night, you'd do that sort of thing. If I took Miss Alice away, Mr. Merlin would get angry..." Sherry poked her fingers together, a strange blush rising on her small face — her mind had wandered to all the wrong conclusions.

"Pfft!" Alice pressed a hand to her chest, startled by Sherry's words.

Merlin turned and glanced at Sherry, sweating mentally. What's wrong with this girl? He had thought she was an innocent young woman, but her thoughts were just as impure...

"That's not it at all! The sofa is his territory — we've always slept separately!" Alice quickly explained, not wanting to be so deeply misunderstood.

"Separately...!?" Sherry was slightly surprised, then frantically said, "A married couple not sleeping together won't do! If things continue like this, you won't be able to have a baby..."

Alice's face darkened, black lines appearing on her forehead. Why did it have to come to having children!

"Hey, Alice, I've wanted to ask you this for a while — who is this elf? Your cellmate?" Merlin asked curiously; he hadn't yet bothered to ask about Sherry.

"Her name is Sherry. She's an elf from the United Kingdom who was captured here by the bad guys from the former kingdom. We need to send her back to her homeland." Alice said seriously.

Merlin sighed inwardly, thinking about how Alice's meddlesome nature would never change.

Alice turned back to explain to Sherry about her and Merlin's relationship. "It's not what you think. We're not truly married."

"What do you mean?" Sherry seemed unable to fully understand the relationship between Alice and Merlin.

"Due to many reasons, we were forced to form a nominal marriage. There's absolutely no real relationship between us — we're more like partners,勉强." Alice explained it simply.

"Really?" Sherry was somewhat skeptical. She felt that Merlin and Alice's relationship seemed pretty good.

"Hey, you! Say something already! Stop playing dead and making me explain everything. Trying to take advantage of me, are you?" Alice kicked at Merlin with her leg.

"Tch! Who would bother taking advantage of you?" Merlin rolled his eyes discontentedly and said casually, "Yeah, we're not actually a couple. We were forced into this by wicked debts. Think about it, Miss Elf — handsome and tall as I am, why would I marry someone with a flattened chest who sleeps on a washboard? Unless my head was kicked by a donkey."

Sherry glanced sideways at Alice's chest and thought, so it's fake after all...

"Shut up, Merlin! I shouldn't have taken you in back then. Looking back, I must have had some intelligence-lowering buff placed on me!" Alice said indignantly.

"Who knows..." Merlin shrugged, not wanting to engage further.

"Since Miss Alice and Mr. Merlin aren't truly married, then I'm relieved... B-but I've never shared a bed with a human girl before, so I'm a little nervous..." Sherry awkwardly tugged at the corner of her dress.

"Don't be afraid. Just treat it like your own home." Alice smiled brightly like sunshine.

"What are you saying, Alice? At least ask for some compensation," Merlin said, dissatisfied with Alice's spendthrift behavior.

"What compensation? This is my home." Alice emphasized.

"I paid rent too, right? Then I also have the right to manage the house." Merlin countered sharply.

Alice was speechless, thinking that indeed, the house now belonged to both of them.

Merlin rose and leaned over beside Sherry, flashing a lecherous smile.

"Guh..." Sherry felt somewhat afraid of Merlin and timidly crept closer to Alice, seeking protection.

"Miss Elf, there's no such thing as a free lunch. You understand what I mean, right?" Whenever things reached this point, Merlin's smile always gave off an evil, creepy vibe that invited misunderstanding.

Sherry's face instantly turned pale, her body trembling. She felt a sense of being forced.

Compensation... what kind of compensation?

Would someone as powerful as him need money?

Looking at that lecherous expression, it must mean he wanted some kind of special favor, right?

He was even showing it so plainly in front of Miss Alice — they really aren't a true couple after all...

After hesitating for a while, Sherry struggled bitterly in her heart. She felt that she was currently depending on others' kindness. If she couldn't satisfy Merlin, she would surely be abandoned, and what terrible things might happen afterward was unpredictable. It seemed a small sacrifice was necessary.

So resolving herself, Sherry slowly stood up.

She decided to do something very bold, very unbecoming of a princess's dignity....

title: Chapter 20 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 20 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 5 · Chapter 20

Shirley slowly stood up, her back to the two of them.

Her shoulders trembled occasionally from her intense emotional state.

"Miss Reeri?" Alice called out in confusion, not sure what Shirley was suddenly planning to do.

"Hmm?" Merlin tilted his head. Though he didn't understand the situation, he had a deeply unsettling feeling.

Shirley slowly turned around, biting her quivering lips. Her face was slightly flushed, but her eyes were like a warrior going to their death.

"Since Mr. Merlin wants compensation, as long as... as long as you don't mind... I'm willing to offer compensation that will satisfy you!"

"Oh?" Merlin's eyes turned into dollar signs, and he said shamelessly, "Just so we're clear, my desires are not ordinary~"

"I understand..." Shirley's expression was pained, her heart deeply resistant to this. It felt somewhat shameful to the elven royal family. "From your eyes, I can already tell what kind of person you are."

"Merlin, do you have any conscience at all! Miss Shirley is in a desperate situation — how can you pile on when she's already down?!\" Alice scolded angrily, feeling he shouldn't make things difficult for a woman at a time like this.

"Alice, shut up. I'm doing nothing wrong. Why should I help others for free? That's not reasonable in the first place." Merlin said seriously, thinking that if Alice wanted to be some righteous little guardian, a free volunteer, he wasn't that stupid. Demons never do anything without profit.

"Miss Alice, Mr. Merlin is right. I've received so much help from you all without reason — it wouldn't do to not show a bit of sincerity. We elves always value repaying kindness; we will never owe anyone favors." Shirley's expression was struggling, yet her tone was extremely firm, faintly revealing an air of nobility.

"..... Alice was speechless. She felt Shirley was about the same as the elves she knew — all perfectionists with a touch of obsession.

"Then please—"

Shirley bent slightly, pinching up the hem of her gorgeous blue dress, as if performing noble etiquette.

Everything up to this point was perfectly normal, but the next move scared both Alice and Merlin.

Shirley suddenly hiked her dress all the way up, exposing the view beneath, showing it to Merlin without any concealment.

"... Please enjoy the view~"

"Yaaaaah!" Alice screamed, her eyes wide as she stared at Shirley's exposed thighs, her mouth forming a perfect "O"!

"Huh?!?" Merlin's eyeballs almost popped out, his mouth twitching as he grumbled, "What the hell is this?!?"

Beneath Shirley's blue dress, she wore white stockings with lace trim along the edges.

Two straps slowly slid off her legs, eventually disappearing into beautiful sheer panties.

Such a sexy sight made any man's predatory instincts surge — nosebleeds were practically gushing upward.

Shirley's delicate body trembled, the cold wind between her legs sending shivers through her.

She felt extremely embarrassed, thinking it was far too shameful to show her panties to a man like this!

But she had heard back in the elf clan that men loved looking up girls' skirts, and if they got a peek they'd feel they'd struck it rich.

So Shirley figured this would satisfy Merlin and repay his earlier kindness.

She was the youngest daughter of the Elf King, a princess of the United Kingdom — doing something like this was certainly improper and brought shame to the elven royal family. But this silly girl had no other choice.

"H... How is it? Mr. Merlin, are you... satisfied with this... compensation?"

Alice suddenly snapped back to her senses, a strange feeling welling up inside her — she strongly disliked another girl acting like this in front of Merlin.

"Don't look! You pervert!"

Alice swung a pink-fisted punch right onto Merlin's face, stopping him from continuing to peek at Shirley's exposed view.

"Ow!" Merlin covered his face, unsure whether his eye or his nose was hurting. "Alice, you—..."

"What are you leering at?! Pervert! Can't you see how distressed Miss Shirley is?!\" Alice put her hands on her hips and berated Merlin, feeling her excuse was pretty clever.

"I wanted gold coins! Not that I wanted to look at any lewd stuff!" Merlin frowned, rubbing his nose. "This is ridiculous — why do women keep taking their clothes off when they see me? They don't consider other people's feelings at all. Even kids watching this couldn't keep themselves composed...."

"Huh?" Shirley's expression went blank, her skirt fluttering wildly in the wind.

A faint blush bloomed on both of Alice's cheeks. She remembered that two years ago she had also misunderstood Merlin's intentions and taken off her clothes on the beach.

But those were Alice's dark history — shameful memories she couldn't forget no matter how hard she tried. It was all Merlin's fault for giving those lecherous looks and not explaining himself clearly.

"Miss Shirley, please put your skirt down. Don't do this. You've misunderstood this guy..."

Shirley's face slowly flushed crimson, like boiling water, steam practically rising from her head.

In the blink of an eye, she pushed her dress back down, feeling as though she had completely humiliated the elven royal family.

So it was money he wanted. She had thought he wanted to do some lewd thing.....

Shirley covered her face and began crying softly—

"I..... This is so embarrassing. I've made Father lose face."

"How utterly shameless~ sniffle~"

"Tch!" Alice, frustrated, shot Merlin a sharp glare.

"What's with that look? Blaming me?" Merlin said nonchalantly.

"Move! Don't just stand there!" Alice shooed Merlin to the other side, then pulled Shirley over. "Don't cry, it's not shameful. It's all that pervert's fault — he doesn't even look like a good person."

"Hmm?" Merlin frowned, quite displeased inside. He didn't want to be a good person? How were all those inhuman demons supposed to feel about that?

"If you need money, just say so. As long as you can take me to the elven embassy in London, I can offer a million gold coins as compensation..." Shirley said with red-rimmed eyes, her eyelashes covered in tears, still feeling awkward about what had just happened.

"One million... gold coins!?" Alice gasped, thinking, *Oh my god! So much! That's SSS-rank quest tier starting compensation!* Who was Shirley anyway! A rich young lady from the United Kingdom!? Judging by her jewelry and attire, it was very possible!

"Really?!\" Merlin perked up, his eyes turning into dollar signs again, eager to try.

"Yes... that's all the spending money I have..." Shirley said awkwardly, worried Merlin might not be satisfied.

Alice's eyes widened. *A million is pocket change?!* Rich people really are different! A million is so much! Merlin and I couldn't scrape together anything like that even if we sold everything we owned!

"I wonder if these coins will be... sufficient, Mr. Merlin?" Shirley asked timidly, thinking that a million might be a bit little for someone as powerfully formidable as Merlin — someone who might even surpass her father — but she couldn't come up with more even if she wanted to.

"Stop! Don't mention money to me. Talking about money hurts feelings..." Merlin said shamelessly, quite seriously —

"I have justice in my heart; money is secondary."

"Protecting the safety of beautiful ladies is precisely my duty...."

"S )< =

Alice and Shirley stared at Merlin with expressionless faces, offering no comments whatsoever.....

title: Chapter 21 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 21 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 5 · Chapter 21

The autumn sky was exceptionally clear.

Stars filled the heavens, crowding against one another on the dark blue canopy.

A gentle breeze blew as the covered carriage made its way home.

Shirley seemed to have grown tired; she leaned against Alice's shoulder and had fallen asleep.

Alice looked at Shirley's steady breathing and thought how strange it was that even though she was several hundred years old, her personality was still like that of a little girl.

Merlin sat across from them, turning his head to gaze at the starry sky, lost in thought.

Alice glanced at Merlin and noticed a few strands of golden hair fluttering in the wind, which reminded her of what happened when they left the temple...

Copperfield seemed to have gone completely mad, crying and laughing in turns.

He spoke incoherently, spouting nonsense from his mouth.

His erratic behavior was utterly baffling.

In the end, he actually stumbled away and fled! ?

But Merlin didn't pursue him, nor did he kill Copperfield, which puzzled Alice greatly.

"Merlin."

"What? Don't think just because the mood is nice right now you can talk romance with me..." Merlin said flatly.

"That's not it! Where does your mind go? Would I waste time talking romance with you!?" Alice retorted indignantly.

"Then what is it? Don't bother me unless it's important..." Merlin said, utterly unromantic.

"I wanted to ask..." Alice hesitated, then asked softly, "Why didn't you kill Copperfield? He's done so much evil; he deserved to die."

"That..." Merlin thought for a moment and replied casually, "He's already gone mad. A man without any dreams is like a walking corpse, not worth being slain at all."

Alice furrowed her delicate brows, thinking Merlin should have killed Copperfield. When it came to evil, one should naturally eradicate it completely.

"In the end, I'm not a hero, and certainly not some righteous little guardian like you. There's no need to root out evil entirely." Merlin shrugged his shoulders.

"I didn't expect you to have a kind heart."

Alice said it in an odd tone, as if she were mocking Merlin.

"Do whatever you want to think..." Merlin didn't want to discuss it further.

The truth was that Copperfield was too weak and had lost all will to fight, so Merlin simply couldn't be bothered to draw his sword.

"By the way, after I was taken away, what happened to the villagers who were threatened by Malygos?" Alice was still worried about others, and it also related to this commission.

"They're all dead. Every last one of them perished. Lockecole Village has been erased from the map of Britain." Merlin said coldly.

"Huh?" Alice froze, thinking she must have misheard. There had been so many vivid faces—had they all disappeared in an instant?

"Although I killed Malygos, when he released his wide-area ultimate magic, I was ambushed by a woman with purple hair. As a result, everyone in Lockecole Village was frozen solid." Merlin briefly recounted what happened that day.

"I see. The commission failed..."

Alice lowered her head. She didn't need to think hard to know the purple-haired woman was Corona.

Those villagers were innocent, completely swept up as casualties of the struggle.

Alice was a kind-hearted girl, not made of cold stone, and at times like this she couldn't help feeling a bit sorrowful.

"If I were a bit stronger, I could have helped hold back that purple-haired woman. Maybe things would have turned out differently..."

"Alice, there aren't that many maybes. The weak being devoured by the strong is a commonplace occurrence. Even among your own kind of humans, you must follow the law of survival of the fittest." Merlin explained coldly, as if he felt no sympathy at all.

"You cold-blooded creature, can't you mourn those who died?" Alice furrowed her brows; although she knew Merlin was a demon, she was still quite displeased.

"This is merely a waste of time. It would be better to carefully consider the future and how to live on more effectively." Merlin looked at Alice, his red eyes somewhat eerie under the bright moonlight. "Honestly, Alice, don't you realize how lucky you are? When things went wrong, I came to save you. Think about what would have happened to you without me. You've died countless times, haven't you?"

"...." Alice was speechless, a cold bead of sweat rolling down her forehead. She thought he was right; if Merlin hadn't been by her side, she would already be a corpse.

"But you need to understand that no one can be lucky their entire life. When the goddess of luck turns away from you, it will surely be the moment of your death. So work hard and grow strong, before the goddess of luck abandons you, strong enough to take control of your own destiny." Merlin said in a serious tone, with no hint of joking whatsoever.

Alice fell silent, unable to find anything to say.

During this journey, she had experienced too many situations beyond her control.

That feeling of being able to only watch helplessly was something she deeply detested from the bottom of her heart!

"Alice, let me tell you something honest...." Merlin paused, took a deep breath, and continued—

"Even with power unmatched in this world, not everyone can be saved."

Below Bennewis Mountain.

The frozen Lockecole Village.

The wind blew fiercely, snowflakes dancing through the air like torn cotton wadding, drifting aimlessly in every direction.

Just a short while ago, this small village had been green and lush, basking in the joy of harvest; now it had become eternal frozen ground.

A person clad in a red robe arrived in the white expanse.

"Isn't the legendary Malygos sealed in this region?"

"How can I not even see a trace of a dragon....."

The robed man spread his arms and took a deep breath, murmuring in shock to himself—

"What happened here not long ago!?"

"There's a tremendous draconic magical aura in the air!"

"Freezing such a vast area... could it be the legendary glacial降临?"

The robed man lowered his arms, concluding that the Frost Holy Dragon must have appeared here at some point; he seemed to be an expert on dragons.

Although he didn't find the Frost Holy Dragon, he discovered the corpse of dragon-transformed Corona, cut in half by Merlin's blade.

"A dragon-transformed human? Did she consume a heritage crystal?"

The robed man crouched down, extended his finger, dipped it into a pool of congealed blood, and licked it twice. His face instantly paled, his eyes trembling uncontrollably.

"My goodness! ...This blood has the scent of a Holy Dragon!"

"Could this woman have eaten... the Frost Holy Dragon's heritage crystal!? Judging by the coloration of these scales... ah..."

In that moment, the robed man suddenly pieced together a great deal of information. If the Frost Holy Dragon's heritage crystal had been consumed, that meant Malygos was already dead!

Who had slain the legendary Six Great Holy Dragons? It was simply inconceivable!

As an expert in dealing with dragons, he himself didn't have a chance of defeating Malygos.

He could only rely on ancient sacrificial rituals to achieve control over dragons.

But a Frost Holy Dragon of that caliber would make even mental control unstable; still, it was worth a try. As for his own purposes, this wasn't entirely fruitless.

The robed man reached into his cloak and pulled out a black horn. Then he blew into it with all his might.

The robed man stared at the dragon-transformed Corona's corpse on the ground.

"Woooooo!" The song of a great dragon echoed through the surroundings.

An ancient timbre rang out, like a grey dragon wrapped in chains.

Soon, the corpse of dragon-transformed Corona flew toward him from the distance; he was one step closer to his dream.

A corner of the robed man's mouth curled upward. The snow around him rose into the air and hovered behind him.

The grey dragon flapped its wings once, snatched the two halves of the corpse, and tossed them into the air.

The robed man picked up the dragon-transformed Corona's body and swallowed it whole with a gulp.

It had been eaten by the grey dragon, and now he would put it to great use!

"The corpse of this woman... I'll need it!"

The robed man's face broke into an enthusiastic smile, and he couldn't help but mutter to himself—

"As long as I can obtain the blood of a Holy Dragon."

"Regardless of whether Malygos is dead or not, extracting the Frost Holy Dragon's blood from this dragon-transformed woman's corpse shouldn't be difficult."

"With my alchemy mastery, I can create warriors flowing with Holy Dragon blood who possess power comparable to any nation in the world!"

"When the time comes and my strength and status are sufficient... by then I'll be able to rival the Seven Lords of the Demon Race!"

"When my power and position are enough..."

"I, a learned mage renowned as a dragon expert..."

"Democritus, senior alchemist... will propose to the lustful Great Demon Lord, Lady Asmodeus!"

"I shall stand beside the most beautiful woman in this world!"

That volume has ended. Tomorrow begins the new volume.

title: Chapter 1
content:
Chapter 1

Volume 6 · Chapter 1

The three of them rode back to Saxis by carriage.

Since the quest had failed, the Guild might have already received word.

So Merlin and company went straight home without stopping by the Guild.

Poor gullible Arnold was still standing at the door, holding roses and waiting for Alice.

"...This is a human city..." Shirley peeked out from under her cloak just enough to timidly glance around.

"Huh?" Alice looked at Shirley in surprise and asked, "Has Miss Shirley never been to a human city before?"

"...No... I've always stayed in a cage and rarely got to see the outside. Those slave merchants were afraid I'd shout and cause trouble." Shirley's eyelids drooped sadly, a trace of melancholy on her face.

"Don't be afraid. Most humans are kind; the bad ones are only a small fraction." Alice said with a smile and took Shirley's hand to give her some confidence. "Welcome to Saxis. It's not exactly a big city, but it's pretty nice."

Shirley's cheeks flushed slightly, and she nodded. "Yes... thank you, Miss Alice. If you weren't by my side, I'm afraid I wouldn't be able to move at all seeing humans right now."

"And among those bad people, there are some who wear black robes and crucifixes around their necks. That group is the root of all evil — wicked to their cores. So Miss Shirley, you must be careful to avoid them." Merlin, not for the first time, threw a pot of filth at the Holy Church.

"...I see!?" Shirley's expression grew grave, and she deeply etched his words into her memory. "I'll keep that in mind. Thank you for the warning, Mr. Merlin."

Though the Holy Church held great influence in human lands, it was far from able to bewitch the non-humans of the Southern United Kingdom.

A country made up of countless races, each ethnic group held its own gods as objects of faith.

They didn't fully believe in the Church's doctrine that "the Goddess of Light is the one true God of the world," nor would they fall for the Church's brainwashing schemes.

"Enough already. Stop injecting Miss Shirley with your groundless prejudices." Alice looked at Merlin unhappily.

"Am I wrong? Just look at those priests of the Church — all dripping with wealth, talking nonsense, living luxurious lives. I have biases against the Church, but — back when I was the Demon Lord, it was thanks to that bunch of idiots keeping me alive that I could still—"

"Stop generalizing! I won't deny that the Church has some scheming individuals, but that's not the whole picture. I've met plenty of priests who said they should use love to transform the demon race, and that everyone should coexist in peace and harmony — that is the righteous path." Alice said seriously.

"Ugh~" Merlin made a gagging motion, his face twisted in utter distaste.

"...What kind of reaction is that!?" Alice felt disrespected by Merlin's disgusted expression toward her. "Demons don't need the affection of non-humans; that way of thinking is dangerous." Merlin said indifferently.

Alice glared at him, fuming silently, thinking that she had indeed heard that demons were nothing but selfish creatures — and it turned out to be true.

But Shirley's beautiful eyes didn't react at all, as if Merlin's words were no big deal.

Ordinary humans would find it strange for someone to speak so favorably toward demons, but Shirley simply blinked her pretty eyes and thought there was nothing particularly remarkable about Merlin's words. After all, the Southern United Kingdom was populated by non-humans like demons, so naturally she didn't find it odd.

"By the way, I've never actually met the Pope — does that old man look especially foolish? Is he one of those bald, scheming villain types?" Merlin thought maliciously, roughly assuming they were similar. After all, as the 233rd Hero, he had seen the Pope during the ordination ceremony in Vatican City and thought he was a decent enough fellow. "That fits the villain archetype better."

"That's not it at all! Even though he's quite old, he's still handsome!" Alice couldn't help but retort.

"That goes against all science. He's definitely a refined scum type — all charm on the surface but grotesque within. I should absolutely insult him when I get the chance." Merlin grinned, thinking that if he ever had the chance to meet the Pope, he'd draw a turtle on his forehead and thoroughly shame him.

"You're the villain here! Go take a good long look at yourself first!" Alice was indignant.

"...Hmph." Merlin snorted coldly, too lazy to argue with Alice.

Merlin and Alice brought Shirley to their home.

Alice opened the door and gestured for her to enter. "Miss Shirley, please, don't stand on ceremony — come in."

Once inside, "Then I'll..." Shirley hesitated at the doorway, feeling very ill at ease, walking in with trepidation as though she were intruding on something intimate.

Merlin followed inside, flopped onto his sofa in a dead-spam, suddenly feeling like he didn't want to move an inch for the rest of his life. He casually picked up a banana from the table and, while eating it, watched Shirley's bewildered gaze dart around excitedly like a curious baby.

"So humans all live in houses like this?" Shirley lifted her cloak slightly and asked, clearly surprised.

"Has Miss Shirley never even seen a house before?" Alice found that strange.

Shirley simply answered casually.

"It's not that I've never seen one, it's just... it feels different. It's far more modest than where I used to live." Alice offered a thin smile, thinking to herself — *modest?* Houses like this in Saxis were already pretty nice. Rich people's ideas were really hard to understand.

"...You're right. We do live in such humble quarters. Hehehe..." Shirley tried to explain.

"Modest? A house like this in Saxis is already quite good. The thoughts of the wealthy are truly hard to fathom..."

"...I'm sorry, Miss Alice, I didn't mean it that way..." Shirley's expression grew flustered. "But it's very cozy, isn't it? Too large a house would feel desolate and cold. With a house like this, it's perfect for you and Mr. Merlin's little love nest."

"Pfft!" Alice was stung again and quickly protested, "Love nest?! What is that?!" She pinched the hem of her skirt, speechless.

"Eh!? S-sorry... I said the wrong thing again..." Shirley stammered timidly.

"...It's fine. We're not married — we just happen to be roommates sharing a life." Alice said with a shrug.

"...I'll remember that," Shirley nodded like a chick pecking rice.

"Come on, let's take a bath together." Alice put down what she was carrying and pulled Shirley toward the bathroom.

"Alice, come here for a moment..." Merlin waved to Alice over his shoulder.

"What is it?" Alice escorted Shirley into the bathroom and then turned back.

Merlin was eating a banana with a meaningful look, half-smiling. Alice's face turned red instantly as she imagined something extremely filthy.

So Alice stomped over to Merlin and grabbed his wrist — the one holding the giant banana. She hadn't figured out the situation yet.

"What are you doing?! I said tonight! Why the rush?!" Merlin looked completely bewildered.

"Go die!" Alice hatefully shoved the giant banana straight into Merlin's mouth, completely jamming his throat.

"Eat it yourself, you disgusting creep!"

"As expected, you're a pervert. There's nobody more disgusting in this world!"

"Hmph!"

title: Chapter 2 — Bonus Update for Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 2 — Bonus Update for Monthly Votes

Volume 6 · Chapter 2

Alice hummed to herself and headed straight into the bathroom, ignoring Merlin.

"Cough, cough, cough..."

Merlin burst into a fit of coughing and slammed hard at his chest, as if he'd been choking on something huge and banana-shaped.

......

What the hell? !

Did I say something disgusting?

I was trying to give Alice an inheritance crystal!

How did I end up being called some perverted creep?

Merlin waited a while for his discomfort to pass, then slumped against the sofa, feeling that his good intentions were going completely unrewarded.

He took out the Frost Azure Dragon's inheritance crystal from his chest and examined it closely.

The ice-blue little crystal had no luster at all; it looked like nothing more than a fairly pretty small stone.

But that wasn't strange — inheritance crystals were always this ordinary. They required powerful magic power or battle energy to activate, only then could they produce any effect.

Merlin had considered selling the inheritance crystal, but such an ordinary-looking crystal outside would likely go unrecognized as Malygos's legacy. He'd only get the price of an ordinary gemstone, a few hundred gold coins at most. So it was better to leave it for Alice to consume.

However, converting the inheritance crystal entirely to one's own use required time, and Merlin wasn't sure how long it would take — it all depended on Alice's own fortune.

"It's a treasure, alright, but whether it turns into strength in the end... it really is up to Alice herself, isn't it?"

Merlin lay limply on the sofa, muttering to himself. He recalled Corona's terrifying form during her dragon transformation — it had been because she was far too eager for power that she'd ended up as that half-dragon creature.

As long as Alice was patient and didn't rush things, she should still be able to maintain her human form and transform into a human-shaped Frost Azure Dragon.

"Aaaahh!"

Shirley's scream rang out from the bathroom. Combined with the splashing water sounds, it couldn't help but invite all sorts of wild imaginations.

Merlin silently tucked the inheritance crystal into his chest, perked up his ears, and quietly eavesdropped while offering commentary.

Shirley: "Miss Alice, please don't... don't touch my breasts..."

Alice: "It's fine, right? Aren't we... aren't we all girls?"

Merlin: Whoa~! Alice the female hooligan, what exactly is she doing?!

Shirley: "Well, that's true, but it's still weird for girls to touch breasts."

Alice: "What's weird about it? I'll help you wash, and then you can help me wash later."

Shirley: "We could... we could do that, but... don't rub so hard, it's kind of hurt..."

Alice: "Why are you being so high-maintenance? I'm not even using much force..."

Shirley: "I feel like Miss Alice is a bit angry, like she wants to... to rip my breasts off..."

Merlin: Good heavens! What technique is this?! She wants to tear someone's breasts apart! She just called me perverted, so does that mean Alice this jerk isn't such a good person after all?!

Alice: "How could I possibly be angry? I wouldn't be envious and resentful just because you have a pair of big breasts!"

Merlin: What the hell! That's literally the truth said in reverse, isn't it! She's envious of someone having big breasts, so she wants to squeeze them until they burst to vent her frustration! How despicable can Alice be?! This is so embarrassing!

Shirley: "Mmmph! Miss Alice, don't... don't touch weird places... it's kind of uncomfortable..."

Alice: "Re-really impressive. Do your elves have some kind of breast-enlargement secret?"

Merlin: So Alice hasn't given up on her own flat chest yet? Is she planning to compromise with the elves and go for the balloon breast secret technique now?

Shirley: "Things like that... don't exist! Actually, having too-big breasts isn't great either. You constantly get uncomfortable eyes staring at you."

Alice: "Are you showing off to me? Let me see how I punish you — po pu pu~"

Shirley: "Ahhhhhhhh..."

The two girls' voices echoed through the bathroom, as if they were treating Merlin, a full-grown man, like air.

"...." Merlin sighed, leaning lazily against the sofa. He thought to himself —

By the way, about the inheritance crystal...

Could it have a breast-enlargement effect?

No way.

Merlin had initially refused to cook, but since guests were coming, he decided to show off his skills a bit.

After all, Alice's cooking was genuinely poor — serving it to guests would be embarrassing.

Merlin had even considered teaching Alice how to cook, so he could finally relax.

However, ideals are plump, but reality is skinny —

"I'm hungry, I'm hungry, I'm huuungry..."

Alice sat on a chair in a home dress, tapping the dining table with a fork in a steady rhythm, her little legs swinging back and forth.

She looked exactly like a child, unrefined and ill-mannered, living entirely carefree.

Meanwhile, Shirley beside her was much quieter — poised, elegant, graceful, and polite.

Shirley watched Alice clamor endlessly from the side, not knowing what to say at all.

Merlin wore an apron, a vein throbbing on his forehead. He cast a glance at the crying-and-waiting-to-be-fed Alice and thought —

This skirt-wearing Hero is so annoying. Has she already gotten used to ordering me around?

And I'm not even hers! Why is she making such a racket? Shouldn't it be her turn to cook?!

It seems I'll need to put Alice in her place later, to prevent this skirt-wearing Hero from developing a habit of having food served to her on a platter....

Merlin withdrew his gaze and aggressively flipped the pan.

"Don't be like that, Miss Alice. You're going to distract Mr. Merlin...." Shirley sneaked a glance at Merlin's resentful expression and couldn't help but remind Alice.

"It's fine. This will encourage him to cook faster." Alice said unceremoniously.

"But... but dining requires ladylike manners..." Shirley murmured.

"Shirley, relax. Treat this place like your own home. Merlin is basically my male servant — you can order him around however you like." Alice said with a lively little face.

"Get lost!" Merlin shouted directly from the kitchen upon hearing that.

"No no no, you can't be like that...." Shirley shivered and thought that Merlin seemed even more powerful than her father. How could one casually order such a strong person around?

"Actually, Merlin's cooking is super delicious. If you get to taste it, you'll definitely love it." Alice said confidently.

"......" Shirley curiously lifted her head and sniffed, looking surprised. "This fragrance...."

Alice also leaned in to smell carefully, and suddenly her eyes sparkled with stars. "It's meat! It's meat! Meat, meat, meat!"

"It's meat...." Shirley showed a somewhat troubled expression.

"What's wrong? Is meat not good?" Alice asked困惑.

"It's not that it's bad, it's just that we can't eat it. It would be disrespectful to the gods." Shirley said softly.

Alice thought about cultural differences and respecting another's customs, so she called out loudly, "Merlin, Shirley doesn't eat meat."

"Doesn't eat meat?" Merlin turned his head, looked at Shirley, and nodded in understanding. "I see. Miss Shirley is a mainstream elf, I get it now."

"Then make a separate dinner for Shirley, okay?" Alice said earnestly, with a slightly haughty tone.

"You shameless brat...." A vein popped on Merlin's forehead. Pointing at Alice with a rice spatula, he said viciously, "Watch your tone, or half your meat portion gets cut!"

"Guh...." Alice let out a guttural animal-like wail from her throat, her eyes red and swollen, her眼眶 seeming to brim with tears.

Merlin is such a big baddie!

He's even threatening me with dinner.

A demon! A super-evil-hearted great demon!

(*..)

title: Chapter 3 — Bonus Update with Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 3 — Bonus Update with Monthly Tickets

Volume 6 · Chapter 3

Unemployed Demon Lord [Volume 6 Dragon Blood] Monthly Ticket Bonus Update [Minor Violation]

"Miss Sherry is a guest, and for the sake of hospitality, I certainly wouldn't let her go hungry."

Merlin, wearing an apron, turned around and kept flipping the frying pan.

"If you dare stand on ceremony with me again, half my meat is going onto your plate!"

"D-darn Merlin, only knows how to bully—!" Alice couldn't help but mutter a curse under her breath.

Sherry watched Merlin busily working in the kitchen and thought that someone so powerful would even personally cook.

Wouldn't a normal person have long since slipped into a life where clothes are handed to them and meals are served on a silver platter? At the very least, such things should be left to the maids. How strange.

But this peerlessly strong man, at home, is actually a husband who puts on an apron and cooks. The contrast is so intense.

Sherry felt this gap moe of his as a cozy domestic heartwarmer was rather charming, and her impression of him scored big points upward.

"Damn Merlin, someday I'll step on his face with these high heels!" Alice said resentfully, forcing her eyes back to normal.

Watching Alice, Sherry awkwardly said, "Miss Alice, please don't be angry. Mr. Merlin was just joking."

"No, he wasn't joking. He's that kind of bad-natured person..." Alice huffed, her eyes still a bit red.

"...Sherry had a bead of cold sweat run down her forehead, not knowing what to say.

"Anyway, Miss Sherry, why can't you eat meat? I've seen elves eating meat." Alice remembered the elf traveling merchants she'd met before — they didn't hold back on dried meat either.

"Those are elves who have completely left their tribe, or half-elves. Without faith, they naturally don't have dietary restrictions." Sherry wore a deeply devout expression and said seriously, "For elves like me who believe in the Elf God Corellon, we are called orthodox elves, and absolutely cannot casually eat any meat or fish."

"I see~"

Alice nodded and thought that Merlin knew quite a lot.

Merlin walked out carrying a tray and set down his own portion.

He placed food in front of the two girls: hamburger steak and fruit salad, respectively.

"Here it is, here it is, hamburger steak."

Alice's eyes lit up, and she immediately picked up her knife and fork and took a bite.

The thick sauce enveloped the juicy patty, and with one bite—

A perfect combination of sauce and meat patty. How could this not be delicious?

Alice swayed happily and lightly stroked her own cheek, feeling as though her tongue was about to melt.

"...It's so good~"

"No matter how much meat you eat, it's not going to end up on your chest, so give it up," Merlin said, crushing Alice's spirits without mercy.

"None of your business, how annoying~" Alice glanced at Sherry's plate, which consisted entirely of vegetables and fruits, and asked, "What's that? I've never eaten it before."

"You're the one who only likes meat, right? That's salad. No meat in it," Merlin said lightly.

......Alice made a mental note, then curiously asked, "Why do some words that make people's brains short-circuit keep popping out of your mouth?"

"This... is just my personal hobby. You don't need to mind it." Merlin hesitated, thinking that he was a transmigrator — how could these natives possibly know?

Before eating, Sherry performed a somewhat elaborate ritual, like a devout believer. She clasped her hands together and murmured piously.

Of course, she wasn't praying to the Goddess of Light Maria, but to the Elf God Corellon.

After a series of rituals, Sherry took a few bites, and her eyes grew brighter and brighter, her little nose emitting joyful humming sounds.

Sherry found the vegetable medley refreshing and crisp, with wonderful flavor, especially the unique sauce, which was simply the finishing touch!

It was like a great treasure in front of her — every vegetable held a new discovery, super delicious!

"Miss Sherry, how was dinner? Was it to your liking?" Merlin asked tentatively.

"It was so delicious, this is the first time I've had something like this. Merlin, you're amazing. Not only are you incredibly strong, but your cooking skills are also so—" Sherry's eyes sparkled with pure admiration.

"Hmph, did you see that, Alice? She's so straightforward. You manage to pick bones from eggs every time," Merlin couldn't help but needle Alice.

"He's only a little better at cooking than me! What's there to be proud of!?" Alice retorted angrily.

"Not just 'a little.' You really know how to flatter yourself," Merlin said expressionlessly.

"I think... I think Mr. Merlin is really amazing..." Sherry couldn't help but speak up for Merlin.

"Eh!?" Alice felt a bitter taste in her mouth and awkwardly said to Sherry, "Actually, besides his fists and cooking skills, this guy is good for nothing."

"That's not true. I feel like Mr. Merlin has many shining qualities. He's really great." Sherry looked at Alice and cautiously asked, "Why do you have such a big problem with Mr. Merlin?"

"Hmph哼~" Merlin felt extremely satisfied inside, and his whole body practically floated.

Alice glared resentfully at Merlin, thinking: How could I not have a problem with him? This damn Great Demon Lord ruined my life, robbed me of my family's generational super-expensive Mithril armor, and left me drowning in astronomical debt. Isn't anyone in their right mind going to hold a grudge about that!?!

"He is no good person at all! Don't be fooled, Sherry. If you get too close to this guy, you'll fall into an bottomless abyss sooner or later."

"That's a really harsh thing to say," Merlin tilted his mouth into a smirk.

"I think it's super lucky for you, Miss Alice, that you can marry Mr. Merlin. Just think, having someone silently protecting you and being able to eat such delicious food every day — that's already a very fulfilling marriage..." Sherry poked her fingers together and whispered in a mosquito-like voice, "Actually, I'm quite envious of you guys..."

Alice's face flushed red, unable to deny what Sherry said.

So she lowered her head and fiercely stabbed her hamburger steak with her fork.

"We're not a real couple..."

Late at night.

True to form, Alice ignored Merlin's "lewd" unreasonable request before bed and went to sleep alongside Sherry instead.

But Alice had a habit: just before midnight, she always needed to visit the bathroom. Otherwise, she wouldn't have stumbled upon Merlin's curse acting up last time.

..6E年

Alice yawned, half-asleep with sleepy eyes, and prepared to head to the bathroom. Without a second thought, she knew that Merlin was currently sleeping like a dead pig.

But the reality was different—

*Smack.*

Alice was pinned against the wall by Merlin's wall slam and couldn't escape.

"Hmph哼哼~" Merlin sneered with a wicked grin and said meaningfully, "So you finally came out, huh?"

"W-what are you going to do!?" Alice's body pressed against the wall, trembling with fear — scared.jpg.

The distance between the two was very close, and while this夜晚 stirred the heart, it also carried intense tension.

Alice had worn very little clothing to sleep at night, and recalling Merlin's earlier "big banana" innuendo, combined with his current naughty smile, sent chills down her spine. The tiny ahoge on her head stood straight up in alert.

"What am I going to do? Don't you already know in your heart?" Merlin narrowed his eyes, dripping with heavy suggestion.

"...Know what!?" Hearing Merlin's words, Alice grew even more frightened. She thought: This is it! Judging by the pace, this must be a hint for *that* kind of thing, right?! We've been living together this long — is this pervert finally going to lose control and make a move on me? Damn Great Demon Lord!

"You're such an idiot. I was going to treat you to something delicious~" Merlin raised his eyebrow, looking utterly smug.

.....Alice subconsciously looked down, and her face instantly flushed scarlet red. She quickly covered her face, unable to bear the sight—

What the hell!

Is this harassment!?

(δ_00)

title: Chapter 4
content:
Chapter 4

Volume 6 · Chapter 4

Alice covered her burning hot face, feeling utterly overwhelmed.

At this point, she could no longer even look directly at Merlin's crotch.

He actually implied she do something so disgusting—he really was a perverted sex maniac after all!

She had always thought Merlin was a decent person, never imagining he would tear off his mask today and reveal his true demonic fangs.

Besides, if Merlin forced her to do something, she genuinely couldn't resist, and no one would come save her—she might only be able to threaten suicide.

Alice felt incredibly unlucky. She had only stepped out in the middle of the night to visit the restroom and ended up pinned against the wall by Merlin, unable to escape.

A drop of cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead. He found Alice's reaction very strange and couldn't resist asking.

"Hey, what's with that reaction?"

Alice covered her face and said nothing, thinking that this bastard made her eat something so disgusting and still had the nerve to ask what her reaction was? Good heavens! How could someone be this shameless?

"You don't happen to know what I was going to feed you, do you?" Merlin narrowed his eyes. He hadn't told Alice that he had obtained the inheritance crystal from Egypt—how did she know?

Alice's petite frame shuddered and she began trembling, thinking that with such an obvious and grotesque hint about a big banana, anyone would know what he meant.

"Oh~ so now you know you have to eat my precious treasure and you're overjoyed? You're trembling with excitement already," Merlin laughed, seeming rather pleased.

"Who's trembling with excitement!?" Alice looked up, tears brimming in her eyes, biting her lower lip, wearing an expression of utter humiliation.

"Woah~ you're now shedding tears of joy just from knowing you'll eat my precious treasure? No need to thank me, I'm only doing this for our mutual benefit," Merlin shook his head and smiled, wondering if he currently looked particularly tall, mighty, and imposing in Alice's eyes.

"Who thanked you!? I will never eat that disgusting thing! Even if you threaten me, it won't work—I'd rather die than submit to a demon like you!" Although Alice's expression was sorrowful, her eyes were filled with hostility. She felt that being coerced into doing such a disgusting thing was an insult to her dignity!

"A disgusting thing???" Merlin's mind was full of question marks. It was the first time he had ever heard someone call the Dragon Race's inheritance crystal disgusting.

"Don't think that just because you saved me... you can demand I do something so outrageous. I will never let you fulfill that disgusting desire of yours!" Alice said resolutely.

"Wait a moment, did you misunderstand something?" Merlin put on a serious face, sensing that the current frequency of his thinking didn't match hers.

"Misunderstand what?! You're simply a disgusting demon!" Alice pointed at Merlin, furious. "Although you have a debt to me for saving me, I can repay you in other ways—but I will absolutely not be coerced into eating your... that disgusting thing. You might as well just kill me!"

Merlin looked at Alice's fearful and watchful expression and suddenly had an idea. She was clearly worried he was going to do something lewd to her.

"You're the perverted one here, what are you even thinking? I want to give you this...."

Merlin took out a small ice-blue crystal, about the size of a fingernail, quite ordinary in appearance.

"What is th—ghk!!!"

Before Alice could finish her sentence, Merlin forcefully pushed the Frost Saint Dragon's inheritance crystal into her mouth.

"Swallow it obediently, it won't kill you."

Merlin covered Alice's mouth with his hand, then abruptly lifted her chin, forcing her to swallow the inheritance crystal down.

From the corner of her eye, Alice caught sight of the eerie smile on Merlin's face—especially his crimson eyes in the darkness, which appeared utterly sinister. She couldn't help but think: Oh no! This great demon lord—could it be that because I refused to satisfy his desires, he's planning to take advantage of this moment to finish me off? Damn it!!!

Only when Merlin saw that Alice had passively swallowed the inheritance crystal did he release her, then asked mildly, "How does it feel?"

"Cough, cough, cough!" Alice coughed several times in a row, then inserted her finger into her throat to try to dislodge the small crystal, but it was useless. Her face went pale and she glared hatefully at Merlin. "What do you mean? Is it because I refused to eat your disgusting thing that you want to poison me?"

"What are you thinking? Paranoid delusions. What you just ate was the Dragon Race's inheritance crystal." Merlin said smugly, thinking that with this item, Alice becoming a Mithril-ranked adventurer was inevitable.

"Roar—"

"Huh?!" Alice's eyes widened in disbelief. "The Dragon Race's... inheritance crystal?! Is it that one you mentioned earlier?"

"That's right, the item with an extremely low acquisition rate that can alter one's innate gifts." Merlin nodded.

"...Where did you get this?" Alice asked incredulously. Wasn't it said that the acquisition rate was as unlikely as Merlin winning at horse racing? That was practically impossible to obtain!

"Marigos had one inside his head, isn't that incredible?" Merlin still couldn't quite believe it himself when he first obtained the crystal.

"Mm-hmm—" Alice nodded eagerly like a chick pecking rice, feeling as though she were dreaming.

"With this, you can easily reach Saint-tier and transform into a humanoid dragon—no wait! A humanoid Frost Saint Dragon, possessing power rivaling the royals of the Dragon Race, the strength of the Six Great Holy Dragons, a formidable physique, immense magic power, and the ability to use Dragon Race combat techniques and magic." Merlin pondered for a moment about the Frost Saint Dragon's ultimate secret art, "Glacial Descent"—in principle Alice could use it too, but it would require a certain level of strength.

"...Is that so? It sounds impressive. Does this mean I'm already powerful now?" Alice looked at her own hands.

"What are you even thinking? This needs to be digested slowly—rushing it means you can't absorb it at all. Although you can temporarily gain considerable power, you'd basically never be able to revert to human form, and your personality would change drastically." Merlin warned earnestly, thinking of how Carolona's temperament after dragon transformation was similar to Marigos's, and that monstrous physique could no longer be called human.

"So does that mean, once I digest the inheritance crystal, I can step on your face with my high heels?!" Alice couldn't help but feel excited inside—this was her dream.

"What nonsense are you thinking about?" Merlin frowned.

"Ah, no!" Alice quickly covered her mouth. She had been too excited and accidentally let her inner secret slip out. "I mean, if I digest the inheritance crystal, will I become stronger than you?"

"Heh, what are you thinking? Even Marigos himself fell to me—what makes you think you stand any chance?" Merlin tilted his lips and smiled broadly, assuming Alice wanted to defeat him. Daydreaming!

Alice's expression immediately fell with disappointment. She thought—what the heck, even after fully digesting the inheritance crystal, she still couldn't beat Merlin? Her life was completely meaningless...

"Can you feel it now? Experience it yourself...." Merlin asked curiously, quite interested in Alice's current state.

"..." Alice responded, closed her eyes, and let her magic power surge within her. The pressure rose steadily...

Would Alice, after consuming the Dragon Race's inheritance crystal, undergo an earth-shattering transformation?

For details, please listen to the next installment.
