title: Chapter 5 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 5 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 6 · Chapter 5

Alice was surrounded by a chill that spread across her body, her growing aura of authority seeming no different from before.
Merlin looked at Alice from beside her; strangely, he could not sense any dragon power.
Recalling when Carona swallowed the inheritance crystal, she instantly burst with a very obvious dragon power.
But Alice, as if she had eaten candy beans, had no reaction at all.
Merlin couldn't help but think, perhaps it requires forcibly stimulating with magic and martial energy?
But if he were to do so recklessly, it would make the dragon transformation irreversible, which would be a loss.
Fine beads of sweat seeped from Alice's forehead, as if she was desperately feeling it, but the effect was not ideal.
With the chill dissipated, Alice chose to give up, feeling that it was just a waste of time.
“How about it? Do you feel a huge power surging in your body?” Merlin asked tentatively.
mmmm... Alice pursed her lips and helplessly said, “I feel nothing at all, as if I never ate any inheritance crystal, just like usual...”
“How come others, after eating the inheritance crystal, can unleash new powers, becoming dragonized and mind-blowing, while you react like you ate candy beans with no response?” Merlin was dissatisfied, thinking Alice was abnormal.
“...How would I know? Maybe you gave me a fake inheritance crystal... Alice grew indignant and blamed Merlin.
“Screw it, I couldn't have taken the wrong one! You ate the inheritance crystal!” Merlin frowned, thinking that Alice, this spendthrift old woman, shouldn't waste a treasure!
“But I really feel nothing at all? This isn't my fault, right?” Alice said awkwardly.
“Do you need some kind of stimulus?” Merlin looked at Alice with a blatant gaze.
“...What are you going to do?” Alice cautiously stepped back half a step.
“Tomorrow, let's go to the monastery; I want to properly train you a bit.” Merlin said very seriously. T
“Don't use such a wicked word as training! It sounds like we're doing something shameful—” Alice blushed and said.
“Whatever, just take it easy; tomorrow let's study it properly—”
Merlin waved his hand, returned to the sofa and lay down, instantly losing all interest,
and thought he could see some marvelous changes.
Left aside, Alice's expression became slightly unnatural, her mood complicated as she thought—
Merlin, this guy, seems to have helped me a lot...
Although it was all for mutual benefit, I still received care, right?
He not only ran so far to save me, but also gave me the inheritance crystal to eat.
Wouldn't he be afraid that after I become stronger, I would step on him? This is my dream...
Little does Alice know that Merlin never even considered her a small salty fish.
Because no matter how hard Alice tries, she will never surpass Merlin, this transcendent pervert.
Alice clutched the light blue sleep dress, hesitating whether to say thanks or something.
“That Merlin.” 5
“Ah?” Merlin turned over, looked at Alice, narrowed his eyes and tentatively asked, “Did you react?”
“No. I have...” Alice answered angrily.
“Tsk!” Merlin, like a deflated balloon, lazily lay on the sofa, “Did you not tell me to do something?”
“…I just want to say thank you—something like that...” Alice's gaze drifted, her hands gripping the hem of the sleep dress, her tone very hesitant—0
“You didn’t run to the Scottish border on purpose, did you?”
“Although I didn't want to, I still thank you.
But don't think too much; I really don't want to thank you!
Just out of courtesy, I just want to express my gratitude!
Heh, you didn't scold me as disgusting earlier?” Merlin lifted his eyelids and then asked, “By the way, where did you want to eat me from earlier?”
Alice's face quickly flushed with a nice blush, recalling that earlier she had purely misinterpreted, feeling very ashamed.
She thought she was too impure, inexplicably thinking about strange places, all because Merlin looks like he doesn't want to be a good person.
Angrily, Alice stomped her feet on the spot and couldn't help but curse Merlin.
“G, U, N!”
Seems everyone had fallen asleep.
The whole house was very quiet, making one feel as if time had stopped.
Merlin slept very deeply, seeming to still be dreaming—
The sky burned with fiery clouds, the red sunset glowing like blood.
The cross was rattling in the wind, countless Holy Church knights stood tall, eyes wide, watching the duel between two world-class warriors.
“Unnamed Gun Hero, I acknowledge your strength, but everything is over; next you will face the demon race's strongest magic, the great legacy of the first Lucifer!” Lucifer II's posture was graceful, his face stunning, hovering above the heavens, his terrifying magical pressure made countless beings tremble.
“Use any move you like; if the battle cannot be fought with full force, then there's no fun.” The handsome and strong Gun Hero swung his crimson spear into a defensive stance, “I admit you are a powerful and beautiful woman, worthy of witnessing my transcendence beyond the Saint tier's ultimate technique,
Let us properly witness the crimson flower blooming before death!
“Humans are all foolish creatures, unable to recognize their own insignificance…” Lucifer II raised his slender hand, fingers suddenly opening,
“Ultimate: Demon Arbitration!”
Suddenly, ten layers of black magic circles engraved with demonic script appeared in the sky, a fierce wind rose, and the magical elements in the air burned!
Come on....
The Gun Hero's whole body was ablaze with golden aura, very strange.
The powers of the two Saint-tier masters collided, shining brilliantly.
The entire death marsh trembled, as if it could collapse at any time and fall into the deep sea.
After the battle, the Gun Hero was unscathed, fragments of Lucifer II's clothing fell from the sky.
Countless Crusade Army soldiers inhaled a cold breath, after a few seconds of silence, they erupted in enthusiastic cheers!
“Mom! Mom! Damn…
Young Lilith's eyes were swollen, her eye sockets seemed saturated with tears, she roared angrily.
“Stop it, Lilith! Be quiet! Don't make noise!” Young Merlin covered Lilith's mouth with his hand.
“Mmm…!” Young Lilith's expression was hateful, cold as a spring, wanting to break free from her brother's comfort.
“Calm down, Lilith, we are weak, we can do nothing.” Young Merlin covered his sister's mouth, his tone showing reluctance.
Suddenly, the Gun Hero appeared before young Merlin and Lilith, holding a crimson long spear, staring at them with a cold gaze.
“What? There are two little evils…
Gun Hero raised the crimson spear, aimed at Merlin's forehead, emitting a murderous intent,
That gaze was like watching two ants hesitating whether to crush them.
Young Merlin felt the threat of death, his whole body sweating coldly like a flood gate opening, the closest moment to the death god's spear was less than two centimeters!
What? I’m just a time traveler; why would I encounter such a thing?
Even though the little sister struggled against Merlin in his arms, he still did not let go; sending her to death was a foolish act.
You are too weak, you have no right to let me kill you; it would shame my spear.
The Gun Hero turned and walked away, his red cloak fluttering, looking dashing under the crimson sunset.
In a world of predator and prey, you who are at the lowest level, you are absolutely…
Merlin looked at that powerful figure and the contemptuous words, his self-esteem was hurt like never before—
Ah~
It’s that guy.
The bastard holding the long spear!
I will definitely slaughter you myself!
Someday, this fear will all be returned to you.
An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth...

title: Chapter 6 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 6 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 6 · Chapter 6

The quiet night.

Merlin dreamed the last dream he wanted to dream.

The silhouette of a figure wielding a scarlet spear, their cape fluttering in the wind.

It was hard to erase from memory, tormenting Merlin like a nightmare.

Cold sweat beaded on Merlin's forehead as they slept restlessly on the sofa.

*Squeak.*

The elf Shelly hurriedly pushed open Alice's bedroom door and stepped out anxiously, panic still etched on her face.

She was wearing a pajama she'd borrowed from Alice, but it felt a bit tight, pushing up her chest until it nearly burst at the seams!

Alice had always dreamed of having a chest that pushed up pajamas like that, but with her flat chest, it was impossible for this life.

When Alice lent Shelly the pajamas, she saw the fullness pressing against the fabric and looked down at her own completely flat chest, and she was immediately filled with envy, jealousy, and resentment. She was almost moved to tears by how pitiful she was.

Even in ill-fitting pajamas, Shelly's sexy and alluring figure was hard to hide.

Her blonde hair was carelessly draped over her fragrant shoulders, and her pointed ears added to her cuteness.

Below her sexy collarbones was a eye-catching cleavage that made one's mouth go dry.

As for the peerless beauty of the elf race, no words were needed.

Shelly flurried over to the sofa, bent slightly forward, and shook Merlin's body while calling out to him.

"Mr. Merlin, Mr. Merlin, wake up, wake up!"

"........" Merlin frowned; it seemed someone disturbing his sleep was quite uncomfortable.

"Mr. Merlin, something terrible has happened, please wake up quickly!" Shelly persistently shook Merlin. It seemed like a very urgent situation, otherwise she wouldn't have lost her composure like this. "Miss Alice is in trouble, Mr. Merlin, stop sleeping and wake up! Is your wife important or is sleeping important?"

"Hm? Alice? Don't bother me this late at night, okay? You're so annoying, woman."

Merlin opened his sleepy, half-closed eyes in a daze, clearly still in a dreamlike state.

But when Merlin collected himself and saw the large, full chest, his eyes immediately widened.

"Hm!? These nice.... aren't these Alice's?...."

"Eek!" Shelly quickly stepped back half a pace, covering her chest with her hands to avoid Merlin's overtly leering gaze. "P-please don't tease me, Mr. Merlin, I beg you... please don't do this, you're a married man...."

Merlin sobered up a bit, sat up on the sofa, and looked Shelly over, thinking—

Why is she coming to find me in the middle of the night?

And... dressed so provocatively, so revealing~

Could she be interested in me, wanting to do something pleasurable?!

Looking at her timid manner, could she like being taken forcefully?

Merlin cleared his throat to cover his embarrassment and asked tentatively.

"Miss Shelly, what do you want? Why are you coming to see me in the middle of the night dressed so seductively?"

"...I'm sorry..." Shelly said timidly. "I also think this look is a bit shameless, but Miss Alice's nightgown is a bit tight in the chest area."

A cold sweat dropped from Merlin's forehead. Could this be Alice's fault? Unintentionally, it seemed the elf lady was looking down on him!

"What's the matter in the middle of the night?"

"Oh right! That... um..." Shelly remembered her business and quickly said, "Mr. Merlin, please go check on Miss Alice quickly!"

"What's wrong?" Merlin noticed Shelly's anxious and panicked expression and felt something was off.

"Miss Alice is radiating an astonishing cold energy that even froze me awake. At first I thought Miss Alice was training, but when I looked again, something was wrong. Her whole body was already stiff from the cold, her face was very pale, and her lips had turned purple. This definitely isn't some kind of training, right?" Shelly said uncertainly, worried about Alice's safety. They had only just become friends, and nothing should happen to her.

Merlin thought about it and his eyes widened. Could it be that after eating the inheritance crystal, the high-ranking Alice couldn't suppress that power?! It was very likely. The Frost Saint Dragon was a top Saint-tier entity; how could that power be suppressed by Alice? It might even backlash and freeze Alice to death.

"Damn it, she had no reaction earlier, why does this have to happen right when we're sleeping?"

"Hm?" Shelly didn't understand what Merlin meant and looked completely bewildered.

Merlin quickly got up and walked directly into Alice's room, where he immediately saw an incredibly unbelievable scene—

The entire room was coated in frost, the temperature very low, as if they were inside a cold storage.

And that bone-chilling cold was still spreading, showing signs of expanding outward.

Alice was curled up on the bed, enveloped in cold, shivering visibly; it seemed she was in a precarious situation.

"Mr. Merlin, what should we do?! Do you have any办法?" Shelly came over, very concerned for Alice's well-being.

Every breath they took could be seen as visible mist, drifting and dissipating in the air, showing just how low the temperature was.

"Miss Shelly, could you sleep on the sofa tonight?" Merlin said calmly.

"...No problem." Shelly nodded; where she slept didn't matter, what was important was Alice's safety.

"Then I'll handle this here." Merlin slowly closed the room door.

"Please save Miss Alice..." Shelly said in a pleading tone.

"I know, don't worry." Merlin replied calmly.

After the room door was closed.

Merlin looked at Alice curled up on the bed and couldn't help but fall into thought.

Right now, Alice's condition was that the Frost Saint Dragon's magic power was uncontrollable and kept leaking out.

And he possessed a very rare magical immunity constitution. As long as they were close enough, he could exactly help Alice suppress it.

"Sigh, if possible, I really don't want to use this method. If not handled properly, Alice might go crazy when she wakes up...."

Merlin sighed and complained, then began taking off his clothes, revealing a lean and sturdy physique like an upright pine tree.

Despite Merlin appearing slender and sporting a woman's face, his muscles were actually well-defined, with perfectly proportioned hunter's lines.

There wasn't a single wound on his entire body, except for a very obvious circular scar on the left side of his chest at his heart.

Almost no one could leave a wound on Merlin. As for the scar on his left chest, it was left by a very mysterious figure.

Although Merlin was born with immense power, he couldn't use it, as if it were sealed.

After his mother, Lucifer II, died, the young Merlin, wishing to bring a better life to his little sister Lilith, decided to reclaim the throne, kill the usurping demon nobles, and set out alone on a devilish cultivation journey fraught with danger.

In a very ancient cave, the young Merlin encountered a highly mysterious man completely wrapped in black robes.

That mysterious person was extremely powerful, making Merlin experience despair. They were invincible, vaguely even stronger than the Hero of the Spear.

The mysterious person used a wooden katana to subdue the young Merlin in just a few moves, then took out a golden spike and drove it fiercely into his heart.

From that point on, Merlin could freely use his power, but unfortunately, his heart had been marked with a curse of death from then on.

Although the scar was left by the mysterious person, Merlin never saw him again after waking up and didn't even know his identity.

That mysterious figure was neither fully good nor evil, having given him the "key" of hope but also forcibly implanting the "death" of misfortune.

Merlin tried searching for that mysterious person, but the world was vast, and finding information about someone like him was easier said than done.

Alice's breathing was already growing weaker, and the cold energy was intensifying. There wasn't much time left for Merlin to consider.

Merlin quickly stripped completely naked and climbed onto Alice's bed—

"No choice anymore, Alice. We'll both sleep completely naked...."

title: Chapter 7
content:
Chapter 7

Volume 6 · Chapter 7

Merlin climbed onto the bed and pulled the shivering Alice into his arms. Alice's lips trembled and her eyelashes were covered in a layer of frost. She was clearly unable to withstand the intense cold and was on the verge of losing consciousness. Alice was still too weak to resist the powerful energy of the inherited crystal. Merlin removed Alice's light blue nightgown and glanced at her body. Her skin was crystal clear and white, and her youthful figure gave off a sense of purity.

"Ugh, why do I always have to deal with this troublesome woman?" Merlin complained, then wrapped his arms around the freezing Alice and covered them with a blanket. The two of them slept together, creating a warm and intimate atmosphere. However, Alice's constant chill made Merlin uncomfortable and he couldn't fall asleep. It seemed that Merlin was using his body heat to warm Alice, allowing her to feel a slight warmth in the cold.

In reality, Merlin was using his magical immunity to help Alice suppress the power of the inherited crystal. If it weren't for Merlin being by her side, Alice would likely have been frozen to death by the crystal's energy. Although the scene looked intimate, neither of them had any romantic thoughts. Alice was in a state of confusion due to the cold, and Merlin had no interest in her.

The night was long, and the frost in the room was slowly receding. Alice's chill was being suppressed by Merlin's magic, and she no longer seemed to be in danger. "This person... has been struggling on their own for so long," Merlin thought. "They're a justice warrior, always helping others, but when it comes to themselves, they can't even ask for help." Many justice warriors were like this, working hard like fools and ultimately meeting a lonely end. What were they pursuing, anyway?

Merlin looked at Alice, who was curled up in his arms like a small animal, and felt a sense of melancholy. Her disheveled hair and Merlin's own chaotic thoughts both reflected their inner turmoil. Alice slowly regained consciousness, wrinkled her nose, and let out a soft hum. She seemed to feel comfortable with the warmth beside her and unconsciously snuggled closer to Merlin.

Merlin looked at Alice with a complex expression, feeling a desire to protect this innocent person from harm. "What am I thinking?" he thought. "I'm not interested in this silly girl. I'm a mature person, and I won't fall for someone like her." However, Alice's unconscious actions made Merlin feel awkward. She wrapped her arms around him, and her long legs entwined with his, holding him tight. Her cute face pressed against his chest, and she even let out a soft, happy sigh.

"Hey, hey, hey..." Merlin's face darkened, and he thought, "What is she doing? Doesn't she know she's being too forward?" However, Alice was completely unaware of her actions, and Merlin couldn't help but feel a little embarrassed. Despite his internal monologue, Merlin couldn't help but notice the intimacy of their position, with their bare skin touching.

As he thought, Merlin wrapped his arms around Alice, holding her closer. "Let's get one thing straight," he thought. "I'm not taking advantage of you. This is necessary to help you suppress the inherited crystal's power." Meanwhile, near the French coast, in the Dover Strait located southeast of Great Britain, a group of over 30 fishing boats sailed towards a small island in the center of the strait.

The fishermen, old and young, held torches and simple fishhooks as weapons. Their serious expressions indicated that they were preparing to face a strong enemy. These were the fishermen from Kent County, who had lived by fishing in these waters for generations. However, their livelihood had been disrupted by a certain alchemist who had occupied their fishing grounds and dumped alchemical potions, causing the local sea creatures to mutate into ferocious sea monsters.

The fishermen had organized themselves to drive the alchemist away and restore their lives. "Brother, we're approaching the island," a brown-haired fisherman said. "How many people do we have?" a blond warrior asked, his broad shoulders and piercing gaze indicating that he was the leader of the group. "Over 100 people, and you're a mid-level warrior, big brother. Taking down an alchemist who doesn't know martial arts or magic is a piece of cake," the brown-haired fisherman replied.

The blond warrior nodded confidently. "Of course, alchemists are just bookworms who don't know how to fight. I'm back in the village to do what's right." The brown-haired fisherman sighed. "Big brother, your return is a blessing to our village. If you weren't back, we wouldn't know what to do with that Democritus alchemist." The blond warrior patted the fisherman's shoulder. "Don't worry, I'm a mid-level warrior now, and I've had some experience as a mercenary. That garbage alchemist doesn't stand a chance."

"Just watch me take him down with one punch," the blond warrior said, his chest puffed out.

title: Chapter 8 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 8 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 6 · Chapter 8

"No wonder you're our big brother. Back then, I should've followed you around outside the fishing village. Maybe I could've become as successful as you!" The brown-haired fisherman looked deeply regretful.

"However, before we land on the island, we still can't let our guard down casually. Alchemists may not have much combat ability, but they always come up with strange gadgets, and they aren't easy to deal with. But face to face? I have the confidence to make them completely helpless in an instant." The blond warrior said with full of confidence.

"Could it be that the big brother's plan for this late-night operation was also well thought out?" The brown-haired fisherman asked in surprise.

"Naturally. A nighttime operation helps us avoid suspicion. As long as we sneak onto the island past that alchemist, we've already won half the battle. Then you 100-plus people help me hold off all the nonsense while I charge straight into the alchemist's nest and beat him until he can't even find his teeth!" The blond warrior clenched his fist, tendons rising on his arms, full of power.

"You're the strongest person in our fishing village, big brother. I didn't expect your wit to be just as top-tier!" The brown-haired fisherman's eyes widened in utter admiration. "But... is it really necessary to muster such a large force just to deal with one alchemist?"

"Better to be cautious than sorry." The blond warrior's expression turned serious as he clasped his hands and spoke earnestly. "I've heard of Democritus. He has a very eccentric personality and is a well-known alchemist with considerable expertise in dragon-related studies, earning him the title of Dragon Expert. So we shouldn't be careless; we need to stay serious about this."

"So the madman living on the island is actually that famous? We thought he was just some savage." The brown-haired fisherman looked shocked and asked试探ively. "Since he's so well-known, his strength mustn't be weak either, right? Big brother, should we invite an adventurer to handle this matter?"

"Don't you trust me?" The blond warrior narrowed his eyes, looking somewhat displeased.

"No, no, it's just..." The brown-haired fisherman immediately panicked and waved his hands frantically.

"Regardless of how famous he is, he's still just an alchemist. Besides fiddling with bottles and jars, he knows no magic or martial techniques. What kind of strength can he possibly have?" The blond warrior said seriously. He had seen alchemists before; most of them could only brew potions.

"You're right, big brother. I was worrying unnecessarily." The brown-haired fisherman said submissively.

"We're almost there. Send a signal to everyone." The blond warrior ordered.

"Roger that!" The brown-haired fisherman raised his torch, stood at the stern of the boat, and began swinging it in circles.

Then behind them, on more than thirty boats, countless torches began to rotate in response.

In the dark sea, the torches on the boats were the only light, like stars caught ablaze.

The meaning of this signal was:

「Everyone get ready! We're about to start landing on the island!」

Everything proceeded in an orderly fashion. The plan seemed to be going smoothly.

But just then——

*Swish swish swish swish.*

Something was skimming across the sea surface ahead in the darkness, making an eerie sound.

"Be on guard! Something's coming!" The blond warrior stood fully alert and sensed there were quite a few of them.

Massive schools of cod came diving from all directions, whooshing past their ears like darts, incredibly powerful.

The blond warrior quickly grabbed the cod that was lunging at his face, gripped it tightly, and looked down closely. "...What is this..."

Compared to cod, what was in his hand was more like a jagged piranha!

Its silver-white body was covered in vein-like patterns, and its mouth was filled with hard, serrated teeth that looked extremely destructive.

Its strength was far greater than ordinary cod. Even while being held in someone's grasp, it was still struggling violently. One slip and a chunk of flesh could be bitten off.

These cod, contaminated by dragon blood, had undergone massive mutation, becoming abnormally ferocious, biting at anything, and stripped of nearly all rationality.

It seemed Democritus truly was a Dragon Expert. By simply bringing back Carolena's dragon-transformed corpse, he had successfully refined Holy Dragon Blood.

But during his alchemical experiments, he casually discharged the dragon blood into the sea, instantly contaminating the entire海域 and causing many creatures to mutate, severely disrupting the fishermen's livelihood.

Yet Democritus didn't care at all. In his eyes, there was only his vast ambition——to grow his own strength and then propose to the beautiful Lady Asmodeus.

The mutated cod swarm suddenly attacked. The torches on the small boats behind immediately became unstable, and countless screams erupted as people were surely bitten.

In the pitch-black night, the menacing mutated cod became the fishermen's nightmare, their tragic cries ceaseless.

"What's going on?!" The blond warrior threw the mutated cod aside and carefully avoided its serrated attacks.

"...I don't know! We've already been very careful, moving silently. Theoretically, we shouldn't have disturbed these things!" The brown-haired fisherman kicked away a mutating cod that was trying to bite him.

The blond warrior, a seasoned mercenary with wide experience, seemed to have noticed something. "Damn it! Something much bigger must have spooked this school of cod!"

"...No way!?" The brown-haired fisherman's eyes widened, terror rising within.

"Let me ask you——on this route, are there any reefs this large?" The blond warrior stared blankly at the mountain-sized black silhouette before him, feeling an overwhelming sense of wrongness.

The brown-haired fisherman also looked up at the black silhouette and trembled in fear as he said, "...I've been here many times. There's absolutely no reef this big..."

A chilling fear suddenly surged into the blond warrior's heart. Cold sweat poured down like a rainstorm, and his premonition grew stronger and stronger.

The pitch-black silhouette suddenly opened two lantern-sized red eyes, like a deep-sea beast, instantly regaining consciousness.

The two stood frozen, locked in a stare-down with the monster. Those crimson eyeballs rolled slowly, like a predator's.

"Ah..." The brown-haired fisherman was scared silly.

But the blond warrior still pushed through his fear and shouted, "Everyone, run! Run now!!!"

The sea monster instantly opened its bloody maw, as if it could swallow a massive ship in an instant!

A straight line of waves, reaching up to 150 feet high, erupted across the sea surface in the darkness.

Several hundred people were devoured whole by the giant-mouthed sea monster before they could even react, not a single survivor.

The lamp oil from the fishing boats spilled onto the sea surface, igniting bright lines of fire that allowed people to catch a glimpse of the sea monster's silhouette in the night——

A muscular body nearly 200 feet long, with only two frog-like clawed arms and a body covered in gray scales.

Two tentacles hung down from the corners of its massive mouth, and its smooth forehead was bare.

At first glance, neither human nor fish, it was a monster of grotesque deformity.

The deformed sea monster propped up its colossal body with its two arms and let out a thunderous roar to the sky, sending wave upon wave rolling outward——

"ROOOAAAR!!!"

On the shore of the small island.

The robed Democritus silently closed his golden pocket watch and lifted his head.

From afar, he watched one of his creations in the sea, seemingly very satisfied with the results.

A faint smile appeared on Democritus's face as he muttered to himself——

"Stupid fishermen dare to oppose me?

"Not even weighing their own strength against mine.

"It seems the alchemical beasts created with Holy Dragon Blood are truly formidable..."

"Beautiful Lady Asmodeus, I'm one step closer to the assets needed to propose to you!"

title: Chapter 9 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Chapter 9 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 6 · Chapter 9

Leksam's morning.

The two of them were still tangled together, completely naked.

Their bodies intertwined in a strange jumble of limbs, sleeping in bizarre positions.

It seemed two restless sleepers always caused chaos when they were together.

They'd been hugging neatly the night before, but by morning they'd inexplicably shifted into a straddle position.

They were both fast asleep—

Merlin was sprawled out on the bed, while Alice was clinging to him like an octopus, using him as a living pillow.

They looked peaceful at the moment, but something seemed about to go wrong.

Alice's eyelids twitched slightly; she was slowly coming to.

She didn't yet realize she was sleeping next to Merlin, thinking it was Shirley.

But the unusual texture of Merlin's skin beneath her made her furrow her brows. *Hmm? Shirley's skin feels weird... Last night it was so smooth and soft, like a baby's. Why did it get rough overnight?*

Alice didn't overthink it and figured it was just the dry autumn air.

Her hand drifted across Merlin's chest, rubbing it back and forth, but couldn't find any soft, squishy breasts—everything felt hard.

Alice's眉头 furrowed deeper. *Huh? What's going on? Where did Shirley's huge breasts go? I wanted to feel them up in the morning, but overnight both melons disappeared?*

All these anomalies dimmed Alice's desire to sleep in. She slowly unfurled her intertwined lashes and squinted her eyes open.

What met her gaze was Merlin's hand—definitely not the delicate hand she'd grown accustomed to, much larger and coarser.

But the most致命 thing was something rock-hard pressing against her lower abdomen, radiating intense heat!

What was that?

And it was pulsing...

Alice blinked sleepily, reached under the blanket, touched the shocking thing, and her eyes went wide.

*Oh my god!*

*Are you kidding me?!*

*Ms. Shirley turned into a guy overnight?!*

*So elves are hermaphrodites...*

*Pfft, no way! Nothing that ridiculous exists!!!*

Alice quickly rolled off Merlin, yanking the blanket along with her to wrap around her naked, fair-skinned body.

*Damn it! Who dares do this to me?! Strip my nightgown while I was asleep! Even my panties weren't left!*

Alice was still trembling, cold sweat trickling down her forehead. She looked up to see who exactly she'd been sleeping with...

Merlin was still fast asleep. Since Alice hadn't settled down until the latter half of the night, he'd slept in late.

"Ah...."

Alice stared at Merlin, dumbfounded. The color drained from her face, replaced by a pale white sheet. She stood frozen in place!

*Wh-what is happening?!*

*Wasn't it Shirley last night?! How did Merlin climb into my bed and steal my quilt?!*

*What exactly happened to my clothes?! Were they stripped by Merlin...? Don't tell me... could it be that while I was unconscious, I already... did *that* with this pervert...?!*

Alice's eyes reddened, her lips quivering as she couldn't form a single word. She felt like she was no longer pure.

Someone sneaking into bed at midnight, stripping a girl naked, and waking up entwined—any fool would know what happened!

Alice bit her lip, tears welling in her eyes, looking utterly wronged. *Merlin's a fake gentleman after all! In the end he couldn't resist putting his hands on me without even asking!*

She was about to slap Merlin awake and demand answers when she caught a glimpse of something every man experiences in the morning. That—

What—

Alice wasn't some innocent child who knew nothing; seeing the shameful sight, she understood immediately.

"Eh!"

Alice's face flushed crimson—steam practically erupted from her ears.

She quickly covered her burning cheeks, unable to look at such a filthy thing, terrified of going blind.

*What the hell?! Why is this happening to me?! This can't be normal! Did I—did I already—last night?!*

*Those bards' jinxes... could their fabricated stories have come true?!*

Alice couldn't accept it. Grabbing the blanket, she raised her head and let out a super-high-decibel scream—

"YYYYYYYYYYYYYYAAAHHHHHH!!!!!"

"Huh?!" Merlin jolted awake, sitting bolt upright on the bed with morning gruffness. "Alice, are you sick or something?! Screaming like that at dawn?!"

"...You dare scold me?!" Alice seethed—she'd been grope and was now being yelled at?! This was outrageous! She kicked Merlin hard, sending him tumbling off the bed. "Y-you—what did you do to me last night?!"

Merlin rubbed his sore butt on the floor, frowning discontentedly. "What could I have possibly done to you? Are you imagining weird stuff again?"

"Mr. Merlin! What's wrong?!" Shirley burst into the room without knocking, panicked.

With dark circles under her eyes, it was clear she hadn't slept well either, her mind preoccupied with her only human friend, Alice.

Just moments ago, Shirley had been wrapped in a blanket on the sofa, drowsily drifting off when she suddenly heard Alice's ear-splitting scream.

Without hesitation, she rushed over, but entered at the worst possible moment—right as she saw Merlin on the floor... with the pixelated monster between his legs!

"YYYYYYYYYYYYYYAAAHHHHHH!!!!!" Shirley let out an equally high-decibel scream, her face turning bright red in an instant. She covered her eyes and retreated toward the door, desperately trying not to look.

"Huh?!"

Merlin was puzzled by Shirley's strange reaction. *What's wrong with these two girls this morning? One after another, getting weirder.*

He looked down and immediately understood, feeling a wave of embarrassment.

But Merlin didn't shy away—it wasn't manly to be ashamed. Demon race statues often depicted male demons with intricately carved, lifelike... assets. There was a slight reproductive worship element to it. Merlin had found it exasperating at first, but after two hundred years of cultural immersion, he'd grown accustomed to it.

*So what if they saw? What's the big deal? Is it shameful? Not really...*

Merlin slowly stood up, hands on his hips, striking a posture of unyielding confidence. He felt not a shred of shame, only a slight chill from the morning breeze on his bare bottom.

"What's with your reactions? Really, it's not that serious! I'm just not wearing clothes! Can you adults please act mature?"

Shirley covered her eyes, trembling silently, her sense of shame reaching explosive levels!

"You pervert, have some shame!" Alice, also covering her eyes, blushed furiously. "Put on your panties off the floor!"

"And don't wander around using Holy Light—be considerate of a hardworking priestess!"

title: Chapter 11 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 11 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 6 · Chapter 11

Although Alice was reluctant to sleep with Merlin, she had no choice.

Now it seemed that relying solely on herself, she couldn't suppress the power of the crystal.

But there was a way—if she could reach the Saint tier quickly, she wouldn't need to rely on Merlin, right?

Alice silently resolved that she must reach the Saint tier as soon as possible.

Otherwise, what was with always having to sleep with Merlin?

Alice had already experienced the Former Kingdom incident and realized her own incompetence and weakness, deciding to work harder.

But now she had an extra motivation to break through to the Saint tier—she needed to master the inherited crystal's power quickly and get out of the awkward situation of depending on Merlin.

Early morning.

After breakfast, Merlin and Alice headed straight for the monastery behind the guild.

As for Shirley, who feared humans, she chose to stay home.

Merlin glanced at Alice, who looked serious, and teased, "Why so energetic today?"

"Need I ask? Of course to... to reach the Saint tier faster..." Alice had wanted to say she didn't want to sleep with Merlin and needed to work hard, but then thought that sounded hurtful, so she changed to a milder excuse.

"Isn't sleeping with me fun? Last night you kept snuggling into my arms..." Merlin gave a meaningful smile.

"AAAAH!" Alice let out a frantic scream, her face red as she grabbed Merlin's clothes. "Don't bring that up! Forget about last night already!"

"Don't make it hard for me. That's not easy to forget." Merlin spread his hands, speaking calmly. "I can still remember your naked appearance... you hugged me, and spread your legs to pin me down..."

"Last night was all a dream! Forget it properly! Don't talk nonsense, and definitely don't remember me without clothes!!!" Alice shook Merlin violently, furious.

"I didn't want to remember such boring scenes either... flat chest, no highlights at all..." Merlin sighed, looking troubled.

"...You... what did you say?!" Alice felt her eyes tighten, wanting to cry. She raised her little fist and hit Merlin. "You bastard! You took advantage of me, yet dare to look down on me like that? How dare you!"

Merlin rolled his eyes. What a troublesome woman. I was just telling the truth...

"What are you doing? Showing off affection on the street this early in the morning..."

A familiar voice sounded, and Da Vinci and Rosetti walked over.

Seeing their prepared appearance, they seemed ready to go to work.

"Good morning, Miss Da Vinci, also..." Alice's face darkened, showing extreme displeasure. "Rosetti..."

"Can you two pay attention to the setting? Playing 'little fists punching your chest' on the street~" Rosetti's tone was sarcastic, her black skin looking warm.

Was it intentional? The moment she saw Alice, Rosetti puffed out her ample chest, as if deliberately provoking her.

"...No, that's not it!" Alice's face flushed red, angrily rebutting.

"Don't misunderstand. We wouldn't do something that boring." Merlin followed with a reluctant rebuttal.

"Congratulations on your safe return, Miss Alice. I heard from Mr. Merlin you were kidnapped? Are you alright?" Da Vinci asked with a blank expression.

"...I'm fine..." Alice waved her hands repeatedly, responding awkwardly.

"What could happen to Alice? With a washboard chest that has no killing power on men, safe as can be,噗噗~" Rosetti said with a laugh.

"Shut up, Black Mother..." Alice gritted her silver teeth, forehead veins bulging, hand gripping the sword hilt at her waist.

"Miss Alice, please cherish your love. Although Mr. Merlin is a Black Iron adventurer, that determination is something many lack." Da Vinci lowered her eyelids, speaking seriously. "To be honest, Mr. Merlin's gaze that day was very attractive. It showed me what love is?"

"Wait! Da Vinci..." Merlin felt she had misunderstood something.

"Rosetti, let's go, we're running late." Da Vinci ignored Merlin and urged Rosetti to work.

"Okay~" Before leaving, Rosetti made a face at Alice to tease her.

Alice angrily glared at Rosetti, then turned back to ask, "What did you mean just now, Miss Da Vinci?"

"Nothing much, just a misunderstanding..." Merlin shook his head, thinking irritably—

My gaze was attractive?

What did that mean...

The two arrived at the guild.

They found the magic screen area packed with people.

Seems like they were broadcasting some news, easy to attract everyone's attention.

A blonde, blue-eyed, sharp-looking woman held a microphone and stood in the screen.

No need to guess—it was Bella, the neurotic journalist from the London Post.

"Hello viewers, I'm the ace dog of the London Post... damn it! Cut that part."

Bella frowned, feeling awkward, coughed lightly, and started over—

"Clears throat! Hello viewers, I'm Bella, elite journalist of the London Post."

"The location I'm at is the central avenue leading from London to the palace."

"Shortly, the heroes heading to the volcano at the Scottish border to subjugate the Former Kingdom remnants will pass before me."

"At that time, I'll bring you first-hand interviews—watch the triumphant return of the Violet Clover Knights!"

"I think everyone knows that recently the Former Kingdom remnants caused chaos on British soil, plunging countless citizens into panic."

"But Lord Sahadin, the Ninth Thorn Knight, took the lead, declaring he would personally lead the Violet Clover Knights to suppress the Former Kingdom remnants."

"Days ago, Lord Sahadin led a secret raid on the enemy headquarters, successfully slaying all Former Kingdom remnants."

"According to official sources, the Violet Clover Knights not only returned triumphantly but also captured the leader of the Former Kingdom—Prince Copfel, from 400 years ago."

Alice frowned, embarrassed. "What? It's just a report on the previous incident."

Merlin smiled calmly, muttering, "That crazy old guy finally got caught."

Alice looked at Merlin seriously. "That's karma. Can't let that guy harm others outside."

Merlin sighed, nonchalantly. "Yes yes, the resolve of a little justice defender is high."

On the magic screen, the heavy city gate slowly opened.

Copfel, in black robes, with spiky hair and shackles all over, stumbled into view.

Copfel looked haggard, expressionless, his whole body ragged like a beggar.

He was no longer his former self. One could see how great Merlin's power was—the mental shock was enormous.

Copfel plopped to his knees, raised his hands, and looked at the sun hanging above the palace, shouting—

"Great deity!"

"Why did you descend to the mortal realm?!"

"To show your divine power is fine, but..."

"Why must you ruthlessly trample my restoration cause?!!!"

title: Chapter 12 — Bonus Chapter: Monthly Tickets
content:

Volume 6 · Chapter 12

Although it was a magical screen, it appeared exceptionally clear, with Bella providing a live commentary.

This triumphal return of the Violet Blossom Knights had turned into a grand festival in London.

Bella: "Viewers, this person is Prince Corpfiel of the kingdom 400 years ago. He has managed to far exceed the normal human lifespan, but it's certain that he achieved it through improper means!"

Bella's commentary seemed to lean towards the official narrative, suggesting that all her statements had been prepared in advance.

On either side, rows of silver-armored guards stood at attention, holding long spears to prevent the numerous onlookers from causing trouble and unnecessary commotion.

However, they couldn't stop the crowd from throwing things – eggs, rotten vegetable leaves, and small stones were all hurled at Corpfiel to express their discontent.

As an official special correspondent, Bella was free to move about without restriction.

Kneeling on the ground, Corpfiel shouted wildly, and the soldiers beside him led him away, preparing to take him to the Parliament for questioning by Queen Elizabeth herself.

As Corpfiel passed by Bella, he deliberately stopped for a moment to let her conduct an interview.

Since it was a live broadcast, it was necessary to let all citizens see the enemy's sorry state and demonstrate the authority of the British dynasty.

Bella approached him and handed Corpfiel a microphone.

"Prisoner Corpfiel, you have committed numerous evil deeds and attempted to subvert the peace of Great Britain. However, justice has been served, and you have fallen into the hands of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth. What are your thoughts now that you are about to face just punishment?"

Corpfiel stared blankly at the microphone in front of him, with eggshells, rotten vegetable leaves, and other debris on his head.

"I want to say..."

"I want to say that everyone is mortal!"

"Do you think you're so powerful?!"

"You have no idea that this world has an invincible existence!"

"If it weren't for that man's presence, you would all be my slaves!"

"He is a god! He possesses unparalleled power and strength that transcends dimensions!"

"We mortals are all ants!!!"

The guards dragged Corpfiel away, but he continued to shout, as if trying to awaken the crowd.

"We are all ants!"

"You will never know how powerful that man is!"

"Even the strongest in Great Britain combined would be instantly killed by that man!!!"

Bella turned away, holding the microphone, and said seriously, "Well, everyone has seen it. The prisoner Corpfiel has descended into a state of mental derangement, becoming a fool. It's clear that he cannot accept the reality of his defeat. Justice may be delayed, but it will never be absent. The Queen's judgment will soon be upon him!"

Merlin watched the magical screen, listening to Bella's commentary, and thought to himself that Corpfiel was indeed unfortunate to have encountered him. If not for his presence, with the formidable Inferno Burning Legion, which country could not be conquered? It could only be said that Corpfiel's timing was bad.

"Merlin, did you use your full strength with that slash that day?" Alice asked, trying to gauge Merlin's abilities.

"Hmm...," Merlin replied vaguely, with a mysterious smile on his face.

"Don't be secretive, you're so stingy," Alice complained, pouting. She suddenly thought of something and asked Merlin tentatively, "What if I said that the remnants of the former kingdom were all defeated by you, and the kingdom's crisis was also resolved by you? Wouldn't you become a celebrity then?!"

"Who says I don't want to be famous? The greater the fame, the easier it is to get good work. But the reality is that even if you say it, someone has to believe it," Merlin replied, pulling at his black iron adventurer's certificate. "Do you think anyone would believe that a black iron adventurer defeated four Saint-tier strongmen and crushed the invincible Burning Legion?"

"Um...," Alice hesitated, thinking that indeed, no one would believe it, as it was too incredible.

"You say it, and not only will no one believe you, but they'll also think you're crazy," Merlin sighed, answering dejectedly. "I've experienced countless situations like this, and I've grown accustomed to it. It's simply impossible to explain."

"Also...," Alice recalled how she had initially introduced Merlin as the Great Demon Lord, and everyone had laughed. "It's really a waste of an opportunity for fame. If one of us had a bigger reputation, we would get better-paying named requests. Like now, it's all being wasted."

"Not yet?" Merlin said with a smile.

"Eh?!" Alice was taken aback, not understanding what he meant.

"If you reach Saint-tier, you'll be a strongman, and everything you do will have a certain degree of persuasiveness. I'll pile the merits onto you, and your reputation will grow. By then, lucrative jobs will come to you automatically," Merlin said confidently, already having a plan to create a god.

After all, as a couple of adventurers, he and Alice needed to work together, and it didn't matter who became famous.

Their common goal was to pay off their combined debt and become free individuals without any pressure.

As long as Alice became a Saint-tier strongman, her merits could be piled up, and her reputation would spread.

By then, social celebrities, nobles, and dukes would all offer money to ask Alice to do things.

This way, they could avoid the current situation, where they had to give up a good opportunity to accumulate fame.

"That's how it is...," Alice realized, hitting her palm with her fist. "But won't you be jealous?"

"Our debt is combined, so it doesn't matter who has more fame. The money we earn is used to pay off the debt together. Besides...," Merlin glanced dejectedly at his black iron adventurer's certificate. "I don't have magical power or fighting spirit, and I doubt I'll ever be able to advance to a high-level adventurer. So, I have no way to accumulate fame and status. It's better to give it to you. The higher your reputation, the easier it is for us to make money. This is called mutual benefit."

At this moment, a new figure appeared on the magical screen.

He wore a tattered Violet Blossom Knight's cloak and dusty silver armor.

His body was wrapped in bandages, and he walked with a crutch, limping along.

It was the sole survivor, Chapman!

The two rows of soldiers stood like an honor guard, raising their long spears in salute.

The crowd threw colorful flowers at the injured knight.

Bella: "Viewers! The person walking towards us is our triumphant hero, the guardian of the nation, the Violet Blossom Knight! But only he has returned. I'm not sure what happened. I have an ominous feeling here. Now, please follow our camera and interview this glorious Violet Blossom Knight!"

Chapman walked laboriously down the central avenue, enjoying the hypocritical cheers and the show-like triumphal ceremony.

As he gazed at the sea of flower petals coming towards him, Chapman couldn't help but feel guilty.

He was not a hero, nor was he returning triumphantly.

He was a defeated knight, fleeing with his tail between his legs.

The true hero was not him, nor was it the Violet Blossom Knights.

It was...

Elgin, the legendary great swordsman, the unknown strongman with extraordinary abilities!

title: Chapter 13
content:
Chapter 13

Volume 6 · Chapter 13

On London's central avenue, it was as though a grand drama was being staged.

Flowers rained down from the sky, drifting gently through the air like a shower of petals.

The road to the palace was carpeted with floral rugs, and the thunderous cheers lining both sides never once ceased.

Chapman moved step by step, leaning on his cane, his heart sinking ever deeper.

He was a knight of integrity, one who strictly observed the knightly code.

And yet now he was being forced to play along with the royal family, acting out this triumphant farce.

All to make the prestige of the Bauhinia Knight Corps shine brighter, to further embed the image of Britain's guardian deity into the hearts of the people.

But the Bauhinia Knight Corps was using lies to dress up the occasion. This was hardly glorious—it reeked of base cunning.

Chapman felt that what he was doing now had already violated the original reason he had joined the Bauhinia Knight Corps.

Why had he joined the Bauhinia Knight Corps in the first place?

Of course it was to be part of that glory, to be among those who guarded the queen.

And yet now he was entangled in every manner of conflicting interests, basking in false flowers and hollow applause, disgracing his own knightly spirit.

No wonder more and more people—

were willing to believe that the mysterious Elgin, the legendary swordsman, was their savior.

Rather than trust the Bauhinia Knight Corps they could reach out and touch with their own hands.

Even Chapman himself now found himself inclined to believe that Elgin was truly Britain's guardian deity.

Chapman understood that Elgin symbolized the purest justice—that was precisely what the people needed most.

Not some haughty, show-offy royal knight who was utterly out of touch with ordinary folk, far less approachable than an adventurer who answered every call.

Chapman recalled Elgin's bearing and his words, and at that moment he felt like a complete fool.

The applause and flowers truly belonged to that nameless powerhouse, yet here he was shamelessly stealing them for himself, betraying the honest, fair spirit of knighthood.

Although Chapman was far from satisfied, he was only a squadron leader—what could he possibly do?

Merlin watched Chapman on the magic screen with a blank expression, and seeing the man's complicated gaze, he thought: Is this guy struggling with himself inside?

Bella, a reporter for the London Post, had long since memorized her interview script and was already waiting on standby.

When she saw Chapman approaching, Bella rushed forward with her microphone and asked in a mournful tone:

"Sir Chapman, why have you alone returned?"

"Because…" Chapman paused to think over his lines, then burst into tears. "Because all members of the 27th Squadron who went on the crusade this time—except for me—have all perished!!!"

Though the dialogue was scripted, Chapman's grief for his fallen comrades was genuine.

His sobs were deeply mournful, heart-wrenching to hear and tears-inducing to witness.

"Viewers at home, did you hear that?" Bella turned to the camera, tears glistening in her eyes, her performance worthy of praise. "Our heroes—the 27th Squadron of the Bauhinia Knight Corps, who took it upon themselves to protect the Queen and her people—all fell heroically on the border volcano of Scotland! They were so young, many hadn't even married, some might have died as virgins! What sorrowful news this is! *Sniffle sniffle*!"

A wave of sorrow immediately washed over the scene. Many in attendance were moved to tears as the triumphant spectacle was pushed toward its climax.

"Sir Chapman, what would you like to say to the viewers at home?" Bella held out the microphone once more.

"Though I alone survived from the 27th Squadron, each and every one of them was a fine warrior, fighting to the very last breath. Facing death, they felt no fear, no regret—for we knew that guarding all our citizens was also our duty. Even if it costs us our lives, we would die without regret. I will carry forward the spirit of my fallen comrades and continue to live on with strength!" Chapman spoke with tears streaming down his face, his expression resolute, radiating an aura of righteous conviction.

The London citizens lining both sides broke into sobs, and even the stony-faced guards couldn't help but wipe away their tears.

"...How touching, I'm sobbing..." Alice was so moved by the atmosphere that tears welled in her eyes.

Merlin glanced at the naive Alice and thought: Is this girl stupid? It's such an obvious staged performance, and she actually believed it!? How pure can one possibly be!?

"Merlin..." Alice blinked her teary eyes and asked dejectedly, "When you came to rescue me, why didn't you go save them?"

"Didn't have time. What a pity..." Merlin sighed and said quietly, "Didn't I tell you? Even for me, not everyone can be saved."

Alice lowered her head, tears gathering at the corners of her eyes, and silently thought: Merlin was right. No matter how powerful he was, he couldn't defy fate itself. Unless she grew stronger, she would someday end up in the same regrettable situation...

On the magic screen, Bella wiped the tears from her eyes. "Viewers, this is the Bauhinia Knight Corps, known as the Queen's Sword. They symbolize the elite of Great Britain. Perhaps it is this dazzling exterior that has led many to mistake them for aloof, untouchable lords. But now you've all seen it—for the sake of protecting the kingdom's safety, they are willing to sacrifice their precious lives. This selfless and noble spirit is absolutely that of Britain's guardian deity!"

It wasn't just the现场 that erupted in thunderous applause; even inside the guild, people were chatterin

title: Chapter 14 — Bonus Update for Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 14 — Bonus Update for Monthly Votes

Volume 6 · Chapter 14

Alice's eyes widened in utter astonishment, finding the sudden topic reversal hard to believe.

Had Elgin the Great Swordswoman appeared when Alice was locked up on that volcano at the Scottish border?

Thinking it over carefully, Alice felt something was off. There must be some kind of misunderstanding—

Could the Bauhinia Knight have mistaken Merlin for Elgin the Great Swordswoman?

Yeah, that had to be it. It was very possible...

She herself sometimes caught herself merging Elgin the Great Swordswoman's silhouette with Merlin's.

But although the two shared a slight resemblance, their resolve was completely different. They were definitely not the same person.

Alice stroked her chin in thought and stole a glance at Merlin, seeing that he too looked surprised.

Merlin frowned at the magic screen, thinking embarrassingly inside himself: Hey, hey, hey! Seems like yet another huge misunderstanding. Is my swordswoman silhouette going to become famous again? And I never wanted to save Britain from crisis in the first place! I only came to take Alice home and casually hacked down a few annoying obstacles. How did I end up pushed to the center of the storm?!

All the adventurers watching the livestream in the guild began to stir as well, chatting excitedly—

"Did I hear that right? Did he just say Elgin's legendary Great Swordswoman? Has she appeared again after half a year?!"

"I heard it correctly. It has to be that legendary nameless powerhouse who took down two pirate kings half a year ago!"

"If Elgin the Great Swordswoman really solved this crisis this time, then this victory ceremony will look like a joke..."

Many adventurers voiced their opinions, feeling that if what was being said was true, the royal family's handling of this had been far too clumsy and ugly.

Chapman's single sentence had directly roused a thousand waves of commotion, even causing no small chaos at the live broadcast site.

Who didn't know Elgin the Great Swordswoman among the common folk? Everyone began discussing eagerly, unsure whether what Chapman said was true or not—

"Elgin the Great Swordswoman?! Is that really true?"

"Has that mysterious hero appeared once more?"

"She's my ultimate idol! I didn't expect to see her active again!"

London citizens chattered amongst themselves, no longer throwing flowers or shouting praises, instead becoming endlessly fascinated by the topic of Elgin the Great Swordswoman.

Elgin the Great Swordswoman was Britain's national idol, especially the most beloved among the commoner class.

Whenever people gossiped about Elgin the Great Swordswoman, crowds would gather around, showing her unprecedented popularity.

Elgin the Great Swordswoman had long been praised by many as a savior-level hero. If she had also resolved this threat to Britain this time—

Then this mysterious swordswoman would once again forge a legend, and her status in the hearts of commoners would rival even Queen Elizabeth's!

Chapman's blue eyes were resolute, his expression like a warrior preparing for heroic sacrifice.

He knew what telling the truth meant. His future, fame, and fortune would all vanish into smoke.

A heavy punishment might cost him his life; a lighter one meant stripping off the Bauhinia Knight's battle robes.

No matter the outcome, Chapman could accept it. As long as he defended his knightly spirit, he could die with no regrets.

Bella, a journalist, wore an expression of sheer dumbfoundedness, thinking: Bloody hell! This wasn't in the pre-written script at all?! I can smell a scoop!

After all, Bella was a seasoned professional reporter. Faced with an unexpected blockbuster news event, how could she let it pass without action?

Moreover, Elgin the Great Swordswoman was a legendary figure riding the crest of popularity. Getting first-hand news from her would be immeasurably valuable!

"Sir Chapman, please repeat what you just said. As detailed as possible!"

"Hem!" Chapman cleared his throat, intending to spill out the full truth before anyone could stop him. "First, I pledge on my noble knight's soul that everything I am about to say is the absolute truth!"

"This is being broadcast live. The common people are all watching, and everyone wants to know the truth. Your oath, at this very moment, has been witnessed by countless people!" Bella's eyes flashed with excitement. This was the big scoop she had been hoping for most.

"The situation was as follows..." Chapman looked into the camera with honest eyes and began a concise narration—

"Our squad, under Lord Sahadin's leadership, was nearly completely wiped out. Only I survived."

"The enemy were the Twin Sword Saints of the Kingdom's Four Heroes from four hundred years ago, two incredibly powerful Saint-tier experts."

"Although Lord Sahadin gained the upper hand in one-on-one combat, he was instantly killed by the Twin Sword Saints' fused ultimate art!"

With those words, the entire nation of Britain likely fell into shock. The Thorn Twelve Knights were household names.

And Sahadin, the Thorn Shield, had a reputation known to all. Being instantly killed—what did that mean? The enemy's offensive power was beyond anything imagination could conjure!

The common folk at the London venue erupted like a boiling pot, growing restless, and the pressure on the guards suddenly intensified.

"And then?!" Bella eagerly pressed, sensing that the real highlight was yet to come.

"After that, a mysterious man whom everyone calls Elgin the Great Swordswoman appeared and killed both Twin Sword Saints with a single strike." Chapman nodded, speaking with a wry expression. "That's right! Everyone surely knows this well—another single strike that felled two Saint-tier experts!"

A round of shocked exclamations erupted among the onlookers, all marveling at Elgin the Great Swordswoman's extraordinary power.

"Did everyone think that was the limit? No! Absolutely not!" Chapman saw beyond that single feat and continued. "Shortly after Elgin the Great Swordswoman headed toward the mountain-top temple, the entire volcano began to shake, and a bizarre stone gate appeared in the sky. Countless undead wreathed in flames emerged from within it. At that moment, I felt this was the end of days, the moment humanity was doomed!"

"Why so terrified?" Bella quickly followed up.

"Because I tentatively sensed within, and couldn't even count the Saint-tier undead. Too many! No country's elite forces would have that many Saint-tier experts!" Chapman's eyes bulged with terror, cold sweat streaming down his face.

"And then!? And then what happened!?" Bella's urgent追问 made her heart race to her throat.

"Those powerful undead hadn't even emerged properly before they were all annihilated. A terrifying explosion erupted. Who else but the suddenly appearing Elgin the Great Swordswoman could have done that?!" Chapman spread his hands in terror. That night, his entire worldview had been thoroughly overturned. What great experts and renowned heroes—Elgin the Great Swordswoman was the truly strongest!

Instantly秒杀ing countless Saint-tier experts, even the No. 1 Thorn Knight might not have been able to manage it.

For a long time, the No. 1 Thorn Knight had been hailed as the strongest Saint-tier, and many had believed so.

But now Chapman显然 disagreed with that notion. Because in his eyes—

Only Elgin the Great Swordswoman deserved the title of the strongest.

title: Chapter 15 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 15 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 6 · Chapter 15

The guild hall fell silent, and a few seconds later, it erupted into a flurry of exclamations.

"Can it be true? Slaughtering countless Saint-tier warriors in seconds? Is that even possible?"

"Heavens! This isn't humanly possible! Unbelievable!"

"If it's all true, then Elgin the Great Sword might be the closest thing to a god among humans!"

Many people found it hard to believe, but some were willing to accept it.

The adventurers immediately split into two factions, arguing heatedly about the matter.

Merlin covered his face, feeling a headache coming on, and thought to himself, "This is getting out of hand! I didn't mean for it to go this far. My backside won't be enshrined in a temple, will it? More and more people will start worshiping me as some sort of savior hero. I'm a former Great Demon Lord, the embodiment of evil! How did I become a human savior? What will my old colleagues think of me?"

Alice smiled slightly, amused, and glanced at Merlin, understanding the situation. She thought, "I knew it! They must have mistaken Merlin for Elgin the Great Sword. How could one person do all that? It's hilarious that Merlin went to save me and ended up causing such a commotion, adding to my hero's reputation."

The live broadcast scene was even more chaotic.

Most of the onlookers were ordinary citizens who weren't as knowledgeable as adventurers and couldn't be divided into factions to question the situation.

These citizens didn't think much of it and were willing to trust Chapman, the knight, so they directly believed him.

"Elgin the Great Sword's strength is so terrifying! Is he a god in disguise?"

"It's possible! The Holy Church said he's the prophesied Savior Knight in the sacred scriptures, isn't he?"

"I told you! Elgin the Great Sword is Britain's savior, maintaining his mysterious image, not seeking fame or profit, a hero of the common people!"

The London citizens discussed enthusiastically, and it was hard to count how many lovesick girls swooned over Elgin the Great Sword.

Bella's hand holding the microphone trembled, shocked beyond measure, thinking, "Slaughtering countless Saint-tier warriors in seconds? Only a god can do that!"

Chapman licked his dry lips, his heart filled with excitement, and he didn't regret it, as it aligned with his knightly spirit.

"You all saw it, didn't you? Copernicus was mentally unstable, I think he was frightened by Elgin the Great Sword's extraordinary strength."

"When we caught Copernicus, it didn't take any effort at all, like catching an ordinary old man who's a bit crazy."

Chapman gritted his teeth, bearing the huge pressure, and suddenly bowed in front of the camera, sincerely saying,

"So, we Purple Violet Knights did nothing this time; we just picked up the easy part."

"Elgin the Great Sword is the hero who resolved Britain's crisis, representing pure justice!"

"But I apologize for the incompetence of our Purple Violet Knights!"

"We all want to be the kingdom's heroes who protect, but our insufficient abilities are a fact."

"For this, I, on behalf of the Purple Violet Knights, ask for the citizens' forgiveness, with a thick face."

In the guild hall, the adventurers watching Chapman on the screen remained silent for a moment.

Although Queen Elizabeth's behavior was a bit unseemly this time, the Purple Violet Knight was indeed worthy of recognition.

The London citizens on the screen also remained silent for a moment before erupting into applause, as sometimes honesty is more precious than merit.

Chapman looked at the flowers flying everywhere, listening to the applause that truly belonged to him, and felt a surge of emotion, his eyes welling up with tears.

Merlin sighed, watching Chapman bow his head, thinking, "This fool, doesn't he know that being honest isn't easy? Look, the price and retribution of honesty have come—"

"You idiot! What right do you have to represent the entire Purple Violet Knights?"

A furious shout suddenly rang out, and Chapman, who was being moved, was kicked to the ground.

"Gasp."

Chapman coughed a few times, already injured, and after being kicked, his wounds showed signs of reopening.

He slowly supported himself with his hands, lifted his head, and looked at the person who kicked him, shocked.

"Franklin Knight-Captain?"

Within the Purple Violet Knights' system, there were four levels from top to bottom: Thistle Knights, Knight-Captains, Knight-Leaders, and Knight Members.

The Knight-Captain's rank was obviously larger than the Knight-Leader's, and only second to the two Thistle Knights, with considerable power.

There were only three Knight-Captains in the Purple Violet Knights, responsible for managing the gang's大小 matters, while the Thistle Knights had more power but rarely handled trivial matters.

Franklin wore beautiful armor, had a high, curly hairstyle, and a high, curled mustache, exuding a sense of elegance.

He narrowed his eyes, with unfathomable darkness in his pupils, and his facial muscles kept twitching, clearly enraged by Chapman.

Franklin Knight-Captain brought many well-equipped Thistle Knights, making it seem like they were about to go to war in London.

"What does it mean? Why didn't you follow the script?"

Franklin came up and berated him, "Dare to defy the superior's orders? Don't you want to live?"

"It's not like that," Chapman replied seriously, sweating, "I just didn't want to go against my knightly spirit! I must tell the truth honestly!"

"What did you say?"

Franklin gripped the hilt of his sword, his anger turning into a desire to kill, "You faithless fellow, a traitor to the Knights!"

"I'm not a traitor!" Chapman shouted, his expression solemn, "I'm defending the honor of the Purple Violet!"

Franklin was taken aback by Chapman's momentum.

The surrounding crowd began to discuss, pointing and criticizing Franklin.

Bella added fuel to the fire, saying to the camera, "Viewers, you see? This triumphal farce has been thoroughly exposed, all premeditated hype. But the honest knight who revealed the truth was brutally beaten by his superiors. Do you think it's fair? This must be a problem with the British system, a distortion of morality or a degeneration of humanity!"

"Don't talk nonsense, or you'll all be thrown into prison!" Franklin shouted at the London citizens, then commanded his subordinates, "Don't take pictures! Stop filming! Go stop the journalists!"

Several Purple Violet Knights climbed the wall to block Bella's live broadcast, shielding the camera, and even assaulting journalists and snatching their magical cameras.

"Arrest Chapman!" Franklin issued another order.

Two Purple Violet Knights immediately came forward, pinning Chapman down like a prisoner, and dragged him to Franklin.

"Knight-Captain! My loyalty to the Purple Violet Knights has not changed in the slightest!"

Chapman shouted.

"Shut up!" Franklin roared, saying seriously, "You've shamed the entire Knights' honor. You had a chance to boost the Knights' reputation, but this traitor ruined it. I'll now dismiss you from your captain position and expel you from the Purple Violet Knights!"

"What?"

Chapman's face turned pale, thinking that what he had feared would eventually happen.

"Chapman, you're young and have a bright future. I thought you were the most loyal knight. Why did you betray the Knights?" Franklin suppressed his anger, hesitating whether to kill Chapman.

"I didn't betray! Occupying others' merits as one's own will shame the Knights!" Chapman shouted, pressed to the ground by two knights.

"It seems you've become incurable. We're the Queen's sword, representing—"

Franklin directly drew his sharp sword from his waist, saying cruelly,

"You betraying the Knights is betraying Her Majesty the Queen!"

"I now try you for treason!"

title: Chapter 16
content:
Chapter 16

Volume 6 · Chapter 16

"Huh?!""

Chapman looked up in astonishment at the sharp sword in Franklin's hand, which was dimming the sun, and felt a wave of bewilderment rise within him.

So it was going to end like this?

Was my life going to come to an end today?

Why is it that I, who defend the honor of knighthood, would meet such an end?!

Indeed, I cannot stretch out pure justice at any time like Lord Elgin the great swordsman...

Chapman silently lowered his head, plainly exposing his neck so as to lessen the pain.

Although he had long anticipated this ending, when faced with actual death, Chapman still felt deeply chilled.

His actions had tarnished the image of the knight order, but he would never admit to betraying Her Majesty the Queen!

Chapman said not another word and waited for the executioner's blade to fall.

Inside the guild, although the camera was disturbed by the Crimson Bower knights and the footage was shaky, one could still faintly make out some live scenes along with clear audio.

The adventurers felt it was unjust, because telling the truth meant being killed—it was obviously unfair.

If they truly did this, Her Majesty the Queen's prestige would be placed in imminent danger—

A queen who indiscriminately slaughters knights does not deserve to be loved and sworn loyal to at all.

"What the hell is going on?!" Alice put her hands on her hips, utterly disgusted by that knight commander. "What did that knight named Chapman do wrong?"

Meilin watched the livestream expressionlessly. He thought, See? This is the price of justice. Being a hero is not nearly as easy as people think.

Citizens of London at the broadcast site began raising loud protests in support of Chapman, wave after wave cresting higher, as if a riot were about to break out at any moment.

"What are these vile commoners doing? Revolting?"

A layer of cold sweat seeped across Franklin's forehead, and he felt a trace of fear.

He glanced down at Chapman and thought, It must be this traitor spreading falsehoods!

As long as he executed this source, everything would settle down!

Franklin raised the sharp sword in his hand and assumed a posture ready to behead.

"It's over," Chapman muttered while kneeling on the ground, pinned down by two knights so that he could not move at all.

"Chapman, you traitor, go to heaven and reflect properly!"

Franklin roared loudly and swung the sword in his hand with great force.

The gleaming executioner's blade made everyone's hearts leap into their throats, and it looked as though blood would splatter across the Grand Avenue any moment.

But at that very moment, something unexpected happened—

A sound of tearing through the air rang out suddenly, and golden light shot down from above!

A gorgeous straight blade, entirely plated with gold trim, appeared and was driven deeply into the ground right between Franklin and Chapman.

Franklin's executioner's blade hung suspended in midair as he stared at the sword in utter shock; obviously, its owner was no ordinary figure.

"What is this?!"

"No way! Could it be—"

Before Franklin could even finish speaking, he let out a muffled grunt as the gorgeous straight blade instantly unleashed Saint-tier battle aura, blasting him backward again and again until he took a tremendous fall to the ground.

Chapman raised his head and widened his eyes, staring at the gorgeous straight blade, upon which golden Saint-tier battle aura was slowly swirling—

This sword...

Is "Hawkeye," correct!

The personal sword of Windsor Terence Mylesfield, the First Knight of the Crimson Bower!

Could it be that Lord Mylesfield himself has arrived?!

Chapman turned his head blankly and looked up at the sky above, and a single eagle feather drifted down slowly.

The massive figure in the sky drew everyone's gaze, and the commotion likewise came to a halt.

A armored black mountain eagle with outspread wings hovered in the sky above, its enormous wings blotting out the sun, its shadow covering the ground below, and an invisible pressure released itself, leaving people too breathless to even breathe heavily.

This giant eagle was a black mountain eagle, normally dwelling in the distant desert kingdom of Ptolemy, building its nest atop extremely high mountain peaks. It was ferocious by nature; its sharp talons and beak could easily tear through armor, and a single sweep of its wings could summon storms. Its strength was comparable to a dragon in close-quarters combat.

In Great Britain, the common people were very familiar with this black mountain eagle, believing there was only one in the entire kingdom, and it was the mount of the First Crimson Bower Knight.

For a creature so ferocious and comparable to a dragon, who besides Mylesfield, the First Crimson Bower Knight, could tame it so easily?

The heavily armored black mountain eagle thundered down to the ground, its wingbeats stirring gusts of wind, forcing the London citizens on both sides to shield their faces with their hands.

A graceful figure slid down from the black mountain eagle, wearing exquisite and elegant female armor that was both beautiful and practical.

A battle robe embroidered with golden crimson bower flowers was draped over her body, declaring her identity as one of the Twelve Knights of the Crimson Bower.

This person was the foremost among the Twelve Knights of the Crimson Bower, Windsor Terence Mylesfield—a woman whose strength and beauty were perfectly combined, a powerhouse universally known throughout Great Britain, revered by countless people as the strongest at Saint-tier!

Mylesfield approached her own sword, drew it out directly, and gracefully returned it to its scabbard.

Then she removed her helmet, letting her light purple hair cascade down freely.

Her face carried astonishing beauty, and her air bangs added a touch of cuteness.

Although her aura bore a resemblance to Alice's, it was far colder, making people feel somewhat uncomfortable.

Mylesfield looked down at Chapman on the ground, a few sparks flashing in her pupils as if she were lost in thought.

"Mylesfield..." Chapman murmured, his expression one of utter astonishment.

"Release him," Mylesfield said flatly, her tone cool and carrying an air of lofty detachment.

The two knights restraining Chapman didn't even think twice and promptly let him go. After all, this was an order from the First Knight of the Crimson Bower; no one dared to disobey.

Mylesfield's gaze drifted downward, she bent slightly, and extended her hand. "Rise, Chapman."

"Huh?!"" Chapman blinked, saying in great surprise, "But I am currently a sinner who betrayed the knight order."

"No." Mylesfield shook her head and smiled faintly. "You are the true knight. Even when facing the threat of death, you were willing to protect the glory of the Crimson Bower knight order and keep it from being shamed. That alone is worthy of admiration."

"Lord Mylesfield..." Chapman began to speak, then hesitated.

"You have not betrayed the knight order, nor have you betrayed Her Majesty the Queen. I am willing to clear all accusations against you," Mylesfield said with a half-smile, her voice soft. "Hurry and stand up. A knight should not always be kneeling on the ground—it's improper. Besides, I am not Her Majesty the Queen."

Chapman did not refuse. He grasped Mylesfield's hand and slowly rose to his feet, feeling that although she was a woman, her strength was formidable.

"Lord Mylesfield!" Franklin hastily stumbled over, trying to stop him. "Chapman defied orders and openly spoke words detrimental to the knight order. This is an insult to Her Majesty the Queen and deserves the punishment of beheading to serve as a warning to all!"

"Idiot!" Mylesfield whirled around and backhanded Franklin so hard that he immediately fell to his knees—

"Franklin, look at the mess you've made."

"Are you trying to turn Her Majesty the Queen into the target of public outrage?!"

title: Chapter 17 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 17 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 6 · Chapter 17

That slap was delivered with exceptional ferocity, instantly stunning everyone present.

All the commoners stared at Mestfield in shock, unable to believe things had escalated to this point.

In the eyes of the populace, Mestfield had always been the Valkyrie of Great Britain, a living embodiment of power, elegance, and beauty.
