title: Chapter 25
content:
Chapter 25

Volume 6 · Chapter 25

On the way to the secret cottage, Merlin and Helena walked side by side.

The two kept a subtle distance between them, neither too close nor too far.

Helena walked slightly behind Merlin's shoulder, her demeanor somewhat constrained.

After all, even though Merlin had been fired from his position, he was still nominally the master of the First Demon Lord Palace.

In the face of a monarch-level demon, Helena, even as a demon general, still needed to remain respectful and avoid any behavior that might be considered rude.

Moreover, Helena had long heard of the strength of Lucifer the Third, and in the demon race, where hierarchy was strictly maintained, bowing to the strong was not such a humiliating thing.

Merlin glanced at Helena, who held her head slightly lowered, and said flatly, "You don't need to be so拘谨, you know? Can't you relax a bit?"

"No, Your Majesty Lucifer, you are the Prideful Sovereign. If my attitude were careless, wouldn't that be extremely disrespectful?" Helena was rather stubborn, still keeping her head bowed, maintaining a certain distance as she followed behind Merlin. From afar, she looked like a little maid.

"But your respectful manner makes me a bit uncomfortable. This is the human kingdom, not demon territory. There's no need for so many formalities." Merlin said awkwardly, thinking to himself that he was dressed no differently from a commoner, while Helena was dazzlingly elegant, and her excessive deference gave him an uneasy feeling.

"That won't do. The rules of the demon race apply everywhere. Your Majesty Lucifer, please don't make things difficult for me. If my liege finds out I've been neglectful toward you, I may face punishment." Helena remained unmoved, maintaining her deeply respectful attitude.

Merlin opened his mouth, then closed it again, puzzled. Helena was lying, wasn't she?

In the demon race, Asmodeus was famously good to his subordinates. How could he possibly punish anyone?

It seemed Helena was really a serious sort of person. Asmodeus must be enviable to have such a subordinate.

Merlin said no more, for pressuring a woman was rude.

"Helena..."

"What is your command, Your Majesty Lucifer?" Helena lifted her head slightly.

"Whatever matter did Asmodeus summon me for this time?" Merlin's expression carried a trace of seriousness, wanting to get some advance information.

"Um..." Helena lowered her head again and said in an apologetic tone, "I do not know what my liege wished to discuss with you."

"I see..." Merlin's expression turned grim. If even Asmodeus's most trusted subordinate didn't know, then what was it about?

"However, judging by my liege's anxious expression, tinged with a hint of nervousness, it might concern the very survival of the entire demon race." Helena's worry was plainly written on her face, her delicate brows deeply furrowed.

Merlin didn't speak. Seeing the atmosphere so solemn, he felt a bit tense himself.

By all rights, the whole world was currently in a relatively peaceful period, and the demon race was developing steadily.

A sudden crisis threatening the existence of the demon race shouldn't be happening...

"If Your Majesty Lucifer doesn't mind, may I boldly make a guess?" Helena seemed to have a keen interest in speculating about her lord's thoughts.

"Go ahead and say it." Merlin nodded, wondering if Helena, as a subordinate, might know something.

"I believe my liege's urgency in seeking you out must be related to the secret plan you are executing." Helena said with a serious expression.

"..." Merlin grew embarrassed. How could she still remember that thing?! He had only thought it was shameful to tell the truth, so he'd been showing off for nothing!

"I guess my liege is eager to see you because your secret plan hasn't gone smoothly and has already interfered with the survival of the entire demon race." Helena's mind was full of monarchs' conspiracy theories, and a demon of her rank could hardly guess the secrets involved.

"Mmm..." Merlin's face darkened, and he remained silent.

"Your Majesty Lucifer, was my guess correct?" Helena asked with a grave expression.

"Cough!" Merlin cleared his throat twice to hide his embarrassment, then put on an expression as though facing a great enemy, and exaggerated, "Yes, exactly so. Helena, you are truly brilliant. No doubt Asmodeus would be proud of you as well. Our plan is of great importance — once successful, it will allow our demon race to instantly rise among the nations of the world. But now, a small problem has appeared."

"As expected. May I ask, Your Majesty Lucifer, whether there is anything you need me to help with?" Helena placed her hand over her chest, displaying a touch of the bearing of a great demon general. "If needed, I am willing to offer my life to complete your mission!"

"No need. This is a grand plan that only a few of us monarchs can carry out — it is not something you can participate in." Merlin said mysteriously.

Helena suddenly understood and quickly lowered her head, saying with trepidation, "I-I am deeply sorry. This lowly one presumptuously attempted to join the plans of great monarchs. Indeed, I was completely overreaching myself. It was far too disrespectful."

"Don't worry about it. What you need to do is keep the secret — do not mention it to anyone, after all, this secret is too important." Merlin said earnestly.

"Understood!" Helena nodded heavily and said seriously, "I am willing to swear upon my soul not to reveal the secret. If you don't trust me, I'm willing to cut out my own tongue as proof."

"Uh! No need, no need..." A bead of cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead. Helena was being too serious, it made him uncomfortable.

"As expected of the visionary Your Majesty Lucifer, not only do you endure humiliation and bear heavy burdens, but you are also so compassionate..." Helena murmured in admiration.

Now Helena admired Merlin even more, feeling that he was different from any other demon monarch.

She recalled the words her liege, Asmodeus, had once said about Merlin, which still echoed in her mind —

"By every measure, Lucifer's personality is too similar to a human's, but his actions are indeed those of an outstanding monarch. I'm glad he isn't our enemy."

Ah~, what a high evaluation!

Having followed her liege for so many years, she had never once seen him praise anyone so highly.

It seemed now that Your Majesty Lucifer might be the finest male in the entire demon race...

Helena mused inwardly, and it appeared she was trending toward evolving into a fangirl, which was quite worrying.

In fact, Helena only remembered the first half — she had directly forgotten the second half of what Asmodeus had said:

"If Lucifer were my enemy, I'd lose the friend I could discuss fashion topics with, and I wouldn't hear about bizarre things like sexy stockings,情趣 lingerie, anal plugs, enema solutions, and other strange things..."

Watching Helena's reverent expression, a bead of cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead, and he thought to himself, covering his darkening face —

What the hell!

If Helena knew the truth —

That he was just a freeloading, ambition-less stay-at-home Demon Lord...

Wouldn't that be incredibly embarrassing?

title: Chapter 26 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 26 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 6 · Chapter 26

The two of them arrived at the underground room of Helena's secret hut.

Helena slowly opened the ancient stone door and made a "please" gesture.

"Lucifer, please come in. If there's anything you need, just call me and I'll be waiting right outside."

"Alright." Merlin nodded and walked in directly.

After the stone door behind him closed, Merlin sat down in the luxurious chair.

The large screen for remote communication suddenly lit up.

The figure that could drive people crazy appeared on the screen, still with that beautiful posture.

If it weren't for the slightly androgynous voice that brought people back to reality, the charm of the Lust Lord's beauty could indeed be considered the most beautiful "woman" in this world.

Every time Merlin saw Asmodeus, his mind would wander a bit, and thoughts like "what if this guy were really a woman" would pop up.

However, as an old friend of Asmodeus, Merlin was well aware of him and wouldn't be fooled by that superficial disguise.

Ordinary people would have long since surrendered to their sanity and become crazy fans, obsessed with Asmodeus's beauty.

"Ah!" Merlin cleared his throat and asked seriously, "Asmodeus, what urgent matter did you call me over for?"

"Indeed, it's a very urgent matter that has kept me up all night, with my nerves constantly on edge." Asmodeus's voice, with a hint of magnetism, sounded.

"Oh?" Merlin's eyes widened, and he asked patiently, "It must be something quite extraordinary to get you to this point, I presume?"

"Let's get to the point then. Asmodeus spoke and stood up, leaving his throne and slowly turning around in front of the camera.

Then, he lifted his skirt, revealing his underwear to Merlin.

"Whoa!" Merlin quickly covered his eyes, but his fingers were wide apart.

Covering his eyes was the same as not covering them, and his eyes were wide open, his eyeballs almost popping out.

Asmodeus's underwear was black, tightly fitting his rounded buttocks.

The fabric reflected a sheen, with a pattern of tulips, and at first glance, it seemed exquisitely made.

Merlin knew Asmodeus's skills were very impressive, and all his clothes were made by himself. If he didn't become a tailor, it would be a waste!

The scene before him made Merlin find no adjectives other than "sexy" to describe it.

However, the subtle bulge below still slapped him like a big ear, snapping him back to reality.

"I'd like to hear your opinion. Do you think the underwear I'm wearing now is slightly too transparent? Should I make it with gauze to highlight that kind of ambiguity?" Asmodeus turned back to the camera, his face showing no shame, and instead, a serious inquiry.

Merlin slapped his forehead, unable to help but exclaim, "This so-called emergency is just to let me see your underwear and give my opinion?!"

"Yes, that's right. Otherwise, what else could I possibly discuss with you? You're the only one I can talk to about private fashion topics..." Asmodeus said confidently, feeling that Merlin's reaction was not right, as if they had discussed many strange things before, but not like this.

Merlin looked at Asmodeus expressionless and sighed.

What crisis about the demon race's survival?

What urgent matter that kept him up all night?

It was all fake!

Asmodeus just wanted someone to see his underwear and see if it was sexy or not!

Merlin cursed in his heart, grabbed his hair, and exclaimed.

"Asmodeus, such things don't need to be notified urgently. Who else can't you ask?"

"Showing someone my underwear... Asmodeus thought for a moment and said in a low voice, "Isn't it a bit too shameful?"

"Shameful? You don't feel shameful showing me?! You don't consider whether I want to see your...your...thing! You're burning my eyes!"

"How can it burn your eyes? Your reaction is very strange... Asmodeus thought for a moment and continued, "According to my understanding, your reaction should be 'I'm so excited!' or 'The girl wearing a skirt is so cute!' or 'The cross-dresser is so fun!' and so on, right?"

"Excuse me?!" Merlin spread his hands, frowning.

"Get out! What kind of person do you think I am?!"

"Quickly put down your skirt!"

"Don't keep lifting it up. I don't want to see your underwear at all!"

"Now it makes me feel like I'm hiding in the basement watching an adult video!"

"You're really boring..." Asmodeus put down his skirt and sat back on his throne.

"Why did you suddenly come to talk to me about underwear?" Merlin asked, frowning.

"Because I'm going to have a concert at the Seventh Demon Lord Palace soon. It's a great opportunity to gather followers." Asmodeus said with a sly smile.

"A concert?" Merlin felt a bit surprised.

"Yes, a concert. This activity was suggested by you, wasn't it?" Asmodeus unfolded the fan in his hand.

"I've forgotten... Merlin thought for a moment and recalled that he had indeed told Asmodeus many things from the real world.

"I think my voice imitation practice is almost done, and it's no problem to hold a concert." Asmodeus shook the fan, looking a bit lost.

"Only I have a dance move where I lift my skirt, and without sexy underwear, it won't do..."

"Damn it!" Merlin couldn't help but curse, "Don't keep lifting your skirt! Your...your thing will make your fans question reality!"

"But I think they'll be more excited if they see it...?" Asmodeus said hesitantly.

"You make a good point. I'm speechless..." Merlin said awkwardly.

"Right? I've been wearing women's clothes for so long, of course, I know what excites them." Asmodeus smiled, covering half of his face with the fan.

"I don't deny that they'll be excited, but showing that will ruin your feminine beauty." Merlin paused and said seriously, "Don't forget, I said a long time ago that people like your female appearance, and you mustn't break that harmony."

"That makes sense... Asmodeus thought it was reasonable and continued to ask, "Do you have any good solutions?"

"Ah!" Merlin cleared his throat, raising his hand to signal silence.

"There must be a solution.

"This is an almost lost technique. I wouldn't tell ordinary people, but I'll teach you since we're friends. You must remember it and practice more."

Asmodeus's eyes sparkled with excitement, and he asked eagerly, "What technique is it? You describe it so mysteriously that I'm a bit excited."

"This technique is called... Merlin took a deep breath and said seriously.

"Hide the Yang and contain it!"

At the same time,

The entrance of the Rexham Adventurers Guild.

A luxurious carriage stopped steadily.

A knight in armor with a rose emblem, holding a long spear, quickly went to open the carriage door.

A blonde, golden-haired beauty stepped out, wearing a pure white robe and holding a magic wand. She was a priestess.

Indeed, these two were the daughter of the Rose Marquise, Cecilia.

And her most loyal knight, Kail.

For some reason, they had come to Rexham!

Cecilia's silver earrings sparkled as they swayed.

She looked up at the Adventurers Guild sign and couldn't help but reveal a smile.

"Merlin, I'm here to find you."

title: Chapter 27 — Monthly ticket bonus
content:
Chapter 27 — Monthly ticket bonus

Volume 6 · Chapter 27

Dusk fell early.

Recksum's town was draped in a red wedding gown.

The streets still had a few scattered pedestrians, but there were fewer and fewer of them.

Even the adventurers in the guild were few and far between; most had gone back to rest.

Before being saved by Merlin, Cecilia, after being stood up for a night, was still discovered by the stationed troops of Dunmire County and successfully rescued.

At that time, both Cecilia and Kel looked extremely disheveled, like street urchins fallen on hard times.

They certainly didn't look like the high-born lady and the proud knight they had been before.

Afterward, Cecilia did not blame Merlin for standing her up; on the contrary, she felt very grateful.

In such a crisis, saving her life was already good enough; there was no need to be picky.

Moreover, if it weren't for Merlin, her most loyal knight would have died in the second layer of the dungeon.

Cecilia did not want to see the knight who had been by her side since childhood die. It's better to say Kel is her friend than her loyal dog.

Fortunately, in her despair, Merlin descended from the sky like a messenger sent by the Goddess of Light, saving both her and Kel's lives.

So Cecilia, a student at the Theological Institute, reined in her lady-like temper and felt nothing but gratitude toward Merlin.

She believed everything was arranged by the Goddess in secret, and that she was favored by the divine.

It wasn't strange for Cecilia to think this way, after all, the Theological Institute teaches about gods, demons, and exorcism; the more devout one is to the divine, the better.

If Merlin knew Cecilia's naive thoughts, he might have laughed coldly, for he himself is the demon expelled from the Theological Institute.

After treating Kel's wounds, Cecilia found he wasn't seriously hurt, just needed some rest to recover.

This made Cecilia breathe a sigh of relief. When Kel woke up, he looked dazed; he had clearly thought he was done for, but now he was still alive.

Cecilia told Kel everything that had happened, especially Merlin's heroic feat of drawing his sword and defeating countless undead single-handedly.

After hearing this, Kel found it hard to believe what Cecilia said, thinking she might have been bewitched by Merlin, or perhaps drank some bewildering soup.

He remembered the elite death spirits on the second layer of the underground maze were very powerful; even with all his might, he had difficulty defeating one, yet it was actually killed by a black-iron adventurer with no magic or battle aura!

A battle that seemed like a joke—how could anyone believe it without witnessing it themselves?

As for why he and Cecilia were rescued—

Kel thought it was probably because other large forces arrived after he lost consciousness.

But absolutely not because Merlin, a black-iron adventurer, saved them, because it didn't make logical sense.

Later, Kel checked the newspaper and found that the biggest contributor to this incident was Alice, a high-ranking swordswoman.

Kel thought this was about right; a high-ranking swordswoman leading a large force to arrive and defeat that strangely-shaped death spirit wasn't difficult.

It's just that Cecilia always praised Merlin endlessly, mentioning him every chance she got, expressing her gratitude to him.

A sour feeling of unrequited love welled up in Kel's heart; after all, she had always been guarding the lady, yet unexpectedly a black-iron adventurer without magic or battle aura appeared out of nowhere. Looking at the pace of things, her status in the lady's eyes might not be secure.

Thus, the bitter-hearted Kel, enduring the pressure, boldly voiced her doubts and suggested that Cecilia might have been affected by mental magic and should see a powerful magician.

Even a properly trained high-ranking knight couldn't defeat the elite death spirit, so how could a mere black-iron villager do it?

But just as Kel finished speaking, she was met with a very severe rebuke from Cecilia—

Saying not to denigrate Merlin, that he is a very low-key powerhouse, truly not concerned with fame and fortune, and his soul has already reached a state beyond worldly matters.

This left Kel completely at a loss; he was merely a loyal knight devoted to his duty.

After being scolded by Cecilia like that, he suddenly didn't dare to speak anymore.

Since then, no matter how Cecilia praised Merlin, Kel said nothing and raised no objections.

But this thorn remained embedded in Kel's heart, making him uneasy.

Kel just believed Merlin had cast some kind of soul spell, similar to brainwashing.

Otherwise, how could the usually clever lady not notice such a huge "bug" as a black-iron villager defeating an elite death spirit?

Kel decided to go find Merlin to investigate clearly and restore the lady to normal.

This opportunity came immediately after—

After Cecilia returned home, she was scolded by her father, who was the Viscount of Roses.

As a result, Cecilia felt resentful in her heart, preparing to continue demonstrating her abilities before the couple to prove herself.

Not long ago, there was a mutation in the fish species in the Dover Strait, making it difficult for the fishermen there to survive.

This matter attracted Cecilia's attention, and she quickly decided to use this to shine brightly in the family.

However, this time Cecilia was not so reckless; she needed to be well-prepared.

So today, Cecilia had come to hire Merlin, to have him accompany her, to go deal with the incident at the Dover Strait.

With such a powerhouse as Merlin teaming up with her, it certainly wouldn't be as embarrassing as last time.

At this moment—

Cecilia looked at herself in the Recksum Adventurer's Guild and tidied up her appearance.

Previously, she looked down on these cockfighting adventurers in Recksum, but now her opinion had improved quite a bit.

After all, after seeing Merlin, she believed the adventurers in Recksum still had real hard power.

"Cecilia-sama? Is it really necessary to invite that black-iron villager? Maybe he's just a street swindler." Kel said with a worried face.

"Kel, mind your tone!" Cecilia scolded with a severe voice, "I call him Merlin-sama; you also have to call him Merlin-sama along with me. And as for me, if I say it again, Merlin-sama is a very powerful expert, not some street swindler. If you dare slander Merlin-sama again, you can just go back yourself; I don't need you as a knight anymore!"

....Very sorry, Cecilia... Kel covered his chest and apologized very unwillingly.

Cecilia confirmed there was nothing wrong with her, then took big steps toward the Adventurer's Guild entrance—

"Let's go.....

There weren't many people left in the guild.

Counting Lulucia, there were only a few.

At this moment, Lulucia was organizing the day's quests, but she saw a stranger arrive.

At first, she didn't mind, but upon seeing the crest on Kel's armor—a rose—she immediately widened her eyes.

The Rose Duchess is the lord of the entire Wales, of course Lulucia recognizes their family crest!

It's just that Lulucia didn't know the identities of these two, and for a moment she was suspicious.

"You two are?" Lulucia's tone was relatively gentle, after all, they are people from the Rose Grand Duke; don't easily offend them.

Cecilia said nothing, her expression carrying noble pride, although she was willing to rein in Cecilia's lady-like temper for Merlin, she wouldn't humble herself to just anyone.

"I am a knight of the Rose Knight Squadron, Kel, this is the daughter of the Rose Grand Duke, Cecilia-sama." Kel helped introduce.

"Eh?! ? The daughter of the Rose Grand Duke..."

Lulucia widened her eyes, a bit startled, thinking—

Wait!

Now what's the situation?

The person in front is actually the daughter of the Rose Grand Duke.

And Merlin is just the lowest-level black-iron adventurer in our guild.

Despite the vast difference in status, this high-and-mighty noble lady...

Actually used honorifics: addressing Merlin as x-sama

title: Chapter 28
content:
Chapter 28

Volume 6 · Chapter 28

Cecilia noticed Lucía's strange expression, looking quite surprised, and couldn't help but ask.

"What's wrong? Is there a problem with me looking for Lord Merlin?"

"...Of course not." A bead of cold sweat trickled down Lucía's forehead. She was bewildered and uneasy about the current situation. "Lord Merlin isn't at the guild right now. He should be at home. If you need anything, you'd better go to his house to find him."

"I see. We really came at the wrong time then. I guess we'll just have to pay a visit." Cecilia looked up and continued, "Then do you know Lord Merlin's address? If you do, I'd appreciate it if you could tell me."

"No problem." Lucía nodded.

Then Lucía told Cecilia about where Merlin and Alice lived, without holding anything back.

Having learned Merlin's address, Cecilia didn't linger at the guild but directly left with Kyle in a hurrying manner.

Lucía breathed a sigh of relief, feeling something was a bit strange.

Why was the daughter of the Grand Duke of Roses looking for Merlin?

And she addressed him with such respect — that made absolutely no sense.

Lucía racked her brains but couldn't figure it out, so she could only rub her forehead and think:

Could this Miss Cecilia...

Be having something going on with Merlin?

Looking at that respectful demeanor, it wasn't impossible.

Helena from the pleasure house today was the same — she also seemed to share some undisclosed secret with Merlin.

Good heavens, what on earth is the charm of this man Merlin?!

Alice, you'd better hold onto your marriage tightly.

Don't let some random fox spirit slip in and take advantage....

The basement of Helena's secret cabin.

Merlin gave a full explanation of the mysterious technique of contracting the yang into the abdomen, helping Asmodeus understand this cross-dressing divine skill.

Once they learned it, passing themselves off as a real woman wouldn't be far off.

"Will this method really work?" Asmodeus narrowed their eyes, feeling that Merlin's method was a bit dubious.

"It will definitely work, don't worry. I saw someone use it in actual combat. As long as you use the skill of contracting the yang into the abdomen, you can lift your skirt however you like, and I guarantee no one will be able to tell what's between your legs." Merlin patted his chest, thinking that all the random stuff he'd seen on the internet wasn't completely useless after all.

"Then I feel relieved. After practice I'll try it on my own in my bedroom..." Asmodeus covered half their face with a fan and said in a meaningful tone, "Why do you know about contracting the yang into the abdomen? Didn't you try it privately yourself..."

"Stop your delusions, I'm a proper person." Merlin said with a serious expression.

"Is that so?" Asmodeus smiled eerily. "If you ever need to wear a skirt one day, remember to let me know. I'd be happy to personally tailor a formal outfit for you."

"N-no..." Merlin answered expressionlessly, wondering why a proper man like him would need to wear a skirt.

But in this otherworldly era he found himself in, the noble rough men seemed to all wear skirts and stockings, which was slightly eye-straining.

"Don't rush to refuse me. This is just a suggestion. If you ever need one, remember to contact me~" Asmodeus winked.

"...Merlin felt like he had been hit on by Asmodeus."

"So for the concert a few days from now, what kind of panties should I wear? Should I keep them as they are now, or make them a bit more transparent?" Asmodeus asked curiously, caring about Merlin's opinion.

Merlin's face darkened, and he fell into deep thought.

Wow, don't ask me that kind of question!

It's too easy to reveal my sexual preferences — how embarrassing!

Merlin grumbled internally but answered honestly anyway.

"Wearing them as they are now is quite good, but there's a slight flaw..."

"Oh?" Asmodeus closed their fan and asked with interest, "Go on, I'm quite curious about your opinion."

"You should write the Chinese character 「正」 all over your thighs. That would make you look even more sexy and alluring — absolutely mind-blowing!" Merlin's voice carried a hint of excitement.

"Does writing the character 「正」 all over your thighs have a special meaning? Why does it feel so sexy and alluring?" Asmodeus asked in confusion, not understanding Merlin's suggestion.

"This..." Merlin paused. He hadn't actually thought about it. If he tried to explain the meaning, Asmodeus probably wouldn't accept it. "This character 「正」 means uprightness and integrity as a tattoo. But since it's written on the legs, it appears somewhat improper. Think about the strong contrast — isn't that thrilling?"

Asmodeus rested their chin on their fan, then nodded and said seriously, "As expected of my close friend. You truly have unique ideas. Among demons, only you can discuss fashion topics with me..."

Merlin held back a laugh, thinking that if he said something like this in the real world, he'd probably get beaten up.

"By the way, I have a question for you." Asmodeus suddenly changed the subject.

"Hmm? What is it?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"If a human were obsessively pursuing you, how would you handle it?" Asmodeus asked.

"Huh?!" Merlin froze and asked in return, "Why are you asking me this?"

"Because your personality and way of thinking are very similar to humans..."

Asmodeus said earnestly.

"I see. Let me think..." Merlin furrowed his brow, pondered for a moment, then answered, "A normal demon would naturally refuse. After all, in the demon race's eyes, humans are a humble species — not on equal footing at all. How could love arise?"

These words were Merlin's answer from the demon race's perspective, not what he truly thought in his heart.

Because before he transmigrated, he himself had been human. How could he possibly demean humans as a humble species?

In the demon race, which was extremely self-centered, humans were nothing more than livestock to be eaten.

How could any normal demon allow a piece of livestock to pursue them? It was the same logic as humans not falling in love with pigs.

"Your thinking is the same as mine..." Asmodeus nodded.

"But I think humans are actually quite nice. They have joys, anger, sorrow, and happiness just like us. Their intelligence is no inferior to ours. So if someone truly likes you, being together shouldn't be a problem." Merlin paused and added, "This world has many species besides just us demons. Everyone is equal — there's no basis for anyone claiming to be superior. Our demon race has way too much prejudice."

"See, it's precisely this kind of thinking that has caused you so much exclusion. Besides me and Beelzebub, the Gluttony Monarch, all the other lords think you're an idiot..." Asmodeus sighed helplessly.

"Never mind that. I don't want to talk about this." Merlin waved his hand and asked, "So, are you being pursued by some human right now?"

"That's right. It's an extremely fanatical human. They've given me a slight headache. I've already had the urge to kill them more than once, but I feel like that guy might still be somewhat useful, so I'm unsure what to do for the moment." Asmodeus rubbed their temples.

"Fuck!" Merlin sucked in a breath of cold air, his expression filled with shock as he exclaimed —

"Climbing toward a man — now that's a true warrior! Awesome..."

title: Chapter 29 — Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter
content:
Chapter 29 — Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter

Volume 6 · Chapter 29

Merlin had never seen a human dare to court a Demon Lord, besides "seeking death" there was no other description.

Looking at Asmodeus's appearance, Merlin could understand—after all, facing such a beautiful countenance, love at first sight across races was nothing strange.

But could this human really court Asmodeus? It would definitely end in failure.

Because Asmodeus was still very traditional as a demon, and at heart held humans in low contempt.

"How regrettable, he only saw my appearance, but doesn't know I'm a man." Asmodeus helplessly shrugged her fragrant shoulders.

"Is that human royalty?" Merlin narrowed her eyes.

"Not royalty, but a talented alchemist, with considerable ability. He can modify the human body to create—strange creatures called alchemical beasts, though they have no intelligence, their strength is still quite good." Asmodeus said appreciatively.

"What are alchemical beasts?" Merlin had never heard of them.

"They are pseudo-lifeforms created by alchemy, like corpses, capable only of some simple attacks, but their destructive power is still quite good. When my demon great generals faced alchemical beasts head-on, they actually felt—a bit strained."

The demon great general was an elite among demons, belonging to the great demon class, the left and right arms of the monarch, and their strength was naturally worthy of affirmation.

Depending on which Demon Lord Palace they were in, the number of demon great generals also differed. Like Merlin, who was in the First Demon Lord Palace, there were as many as seven demon great generals, and Lilith was among them.

"Are those alchemical beasts Saint-tier monsters?" Merlin tentatively asked, thinking that if one had such technology, it would be incredible—creating Saint-tier monsters to command, this ability couldn't help but be said to be very BUG-like.....

But since they were pseudo-lifeforms similar to corpses, they would certainly have no effect in alleviating one's curse.

"Not Saint-tier, though the destructive power of alchemical beasts is very close to Saint-tier magic or techniques, they fundamentally don't belong to any power tier, completely created by alchemy's strong physical strength attack." Asmodeus paused, summarizing, "Simply put, alchemical beasts are dogs mad with sharp fangs but no intelligence."

"Is that so? Since they're mad dogs, why bother? Are you planning to expand your forces and wage war on human realms?" Merlin asked with hands spread.

"I'm not that bored; I'm just prepared. If he can serve me and create a batch of alchemical beasts, my forces would get a significant boost, equivalent to several demon lord armies." Asmodeus shook the fan in her hand, helplessly saying, "But the current situation is, I regard him as a cooperation partner, yet he's thinking of courting me, which makes me extremely disgusted, lowly humans, how dare they touch my beautiful form?

Now Asmodeus could still recall the scene from back then.....

Two years ago.

Inside the Fourth Demon Lord Palace.

At this time, Helena was still serving as a demon great general.

Hearing that Democritus's alchemy was very impressive, Asmodeus wanted him to refine very beautiful gems as decorations, so she met this human.

Asmodeus looked down at the kneeling Democritus below, having said nothing all along.

Because Asmodeus could easily sense the greed and lust in Democritus's eyes, clearly he was infatuated with this Demon Lord, wanting to get close to her.

Helena: "Democritus, the mistress needs unique gems of this world, can you refine them?"

Democritus: "Of course, I am a top-tier alchemist."

Helena: "Good, what reward do you need?"

Democritus: "I need. I need beautiful Lady Asmodeus to marry me, to become my wife!"

Naturally, all the great demons in the Demon Lord Palace were stunned, thinking this human was a madman, a mere livestock, daring to propose lustful words to the lustful monarch! ? It made one's eyes pop out.

Democritus's eyes were full of obsession with Asmodeus, his bloodshot eyeballs already reaching a pathological state.

Instantly, all the great demons in the entire Demon Lord Palace wanted to kill Democritus, including Helena, magic power and battle aura raging forth.

Helena: "Democritus, you have such great audacity, a mere lowly human daring to speak lewd words to the mistress, do you want to die?"

Democritus: "I have never seen a woman as beautiful as Lady Asmodeus, expressing one's love is the human's nature."

Asmodeus said nothing, but emitted a series of light laughter, looking at Democritus's eyes like watching a clown performance.

Helena: "Human, what manner of thing are you, also daring to speak nonsense to the mistress? Prepare to die! Before dying, I will let you know, the mistress is male."

Before Helena could finish this sentence, she was interrupted by Asmodeus. At that time, he had already learned some pseudo-voice, though still imperfect, it still carried a trace of male voice, but was enough to fool the truth.

Asmodeus: "Interesting human, but what capital do you have to possess me? I am one of the seven kings of the demon race, possessing a status and power unattainable by you, in front of me you are merely an ant."2 No words small

Democritus: "Asmodeus lady, I have power that can match yours, have you ever heard of alchemical beasts?"

Then Democritus displayed his proud ten alchemical beasts before the demons, constantly bragging about his works.

Those oddly shaped monsters, though ugly, indeed had good attack power; if they could be mass-produced, they would be a force not to be underestimated.

But immediately after, they were all slaughtered by Helena, though she felt a bit of pressure, the result was still within expectation.

Democritus looked at the alchemical beasts slaughtered into pieces all over the ground, falling into a daze, feeling the gap between demonic power was huge, and needed higher-level things to strengthen alchemical beasts.

Helena: "Although your toys are quite interesting, they are still far from my race's power, with just this capital also daring to equal the mistress in equal communication, don't look at yourself what kind of person you are! Additionally I want to tell you, the mistress is male....

Asmodeus: "Enough Helena, let's go, drive this self-important human out.

In the end Helena still didn't say Asmodeus's gender, there was simply no good opportunity.

Democritus was driven out, and when leaving he still couldn't forget the lustful monarch.

Watching the Fourth Demon Lord Palace receding in the distance, he roared loudly one after another

"Asmodeus lady!"

"I, Democritus."

"Someday I will conquer you

Chapter 30 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update (Make-up for January 12)

Volume 6 · Chapter 30

Asmodeus sighed, quietly putting aside his thoughts about two years ago, looking deeply conflicted.

"Fine, I guess you're just interested in their alchemical beasts, but don't want to get tangled up with some lowly human, right?" Merlin nodded and shrugged.

"That's right. That human sent me another letter recently, saying he now has enough capital to propose to me. After a comprehensive upgrade, his alchemical beast is comparable to any army in the world. As long as I'm willing to marry him, he'll gladly give me his masterpiece as a gift."

When Asmodeus saw that letter not long ago, he was quite surprised, thinking Democritus was truly overconfident.

Although he was indeed very interested in alchemical beasts, was he really trying to marry him based on that alone? It was so overreaching it felt almost insulting.

"If you really want to cooperate with that alchemist, marrying him isn't out of the question. Honestly, humans aren't as bad as you imagine. Why not learn to interact with them?" Merlin said with a helpless bitter smile.

"What are you talking about? I am the Monarch of Lust. Marrying a human would become a laughingstock. Not everyone is like you, treating every race equally. I've always believed that the great demon race is the most excellent." Asmodeus frowned, clearly dissatisfied, clearly not enjoying Merlin's joking manner.

Merlin furrowed his brow slightly, looking half-amused and half-exasperated. So that was it. Demons held prejudice against humans just because of how low they looked down upon them? This was their era now. The Demon Epoch had long passed. Why did everyone love wallowing in past glories?

"But if Lucifer were to want to marry me, I might consider it. Back when you gave me that little gift, old lady's girlish heart really did skip a beat~" Asmodeus covered half her face with a fan, smiling happily.

Merlin immediately cursed. If he hadn't discovered back then that Asmodeus was a cross-dresser, how could he have made such a rookie mistake? It had become dark history now!

"Enough with that. Since you don't like humans, just refuse that alchemist. If he dares to harass you, just kill him outright. I don't believe that with your strength, dealing with an alchemical beast would be any difficulty?"

"There's no problem with killing them all. Those alchemical beasts are nothing but senseless walking corpses. Even with their full upgrade, they pose no threat to me at all."

Although Asmodeus knew Democritus's alchemical beasts had been upgraded, from those fragmented love letters he couldn't understand just how much stronger they'd become. The only thing the entire letter clearly expressed was:

「I'm absolutely OP right now, capable of instantly blowing your fucking ass off!」

Democritus was no longer the same as two years ago. He kept improving and perfecting his alchemy, and the power of the monsters he created was incomparable to before.

Moreover, Democritus had also obtained holy dragon blood from Dragonized Karona, causing an essential leap in his alchemical beasts—

Ferocious monstrous nature, the immense power of the dragon race, formidable scaled armor

All sorts of revolutionary changes had undoubtedly turned the alchemical beasts into outright killing machines, approaching so-called perfect creatures, striking terror into people's hearts.

Perhaps two years ago Democritus's masterpiece would have been instantly秒杀ed by Helena, but now it probably wouldn't be so simple?

Because Democritus's alchemical beasts' power was no longer what it used to be. With holy dragon blood加持, even facing Saint-tier强者, they had a chance to fight.

"Then what are you hesitating about? If you're unhappy, just kill them. Being wishy-washy doesn't suit you, Asmodeus..." Merlin said puzzledly.

"But that alchemist truly is a rare talent. I'd really feel a bit reluctant to just kill him directly."

Asmodeus paused, helplessly explaining his predicament.

"As you know, our Fourth Demon Lord Palace is located in the waters of the Qilian Mountains, closest to the Holy Church headquarters in Vatican, facing threats at all times. If we aren't militarily strong, wouldn't we just be soft persimmons for enemies to squeeze?"

"And the ugly monsters that alchemist creates could exactly compensate for our Fourth Demon Lord Palace's shortcomings, temporarily boosting my forces. To die, that's truly a pity."

Upon hearing this, Merlin immediately understood Asmodeus's troubles. For a demon monarch, protecting the Demon Lord Palace was always the top priority.

And the Fourth Demon Lord Palace was too close to the demon race's mortal enemy, the Holy Church—just separated by a sea. The geographical location was really poor.

The Holy Church could organize a temporary legion at any time and directly cross the sea to crusade against them. Extremely unfortunate.

Unlike his own First Demon Lord Palace, located in the northern Death Swamp, where it wasn't easy for anyone to find them. Peaceful development was wonderful.

Merlin sighed. It seemed Asmodeus's hesitation wasn't without reason.

Although he himself was a late-stage procrastinator who dreaded trouble, the other party was an old friend, and the secret guarding beneath the Demon Lord Palace was indeed very important. A small favor could still be helped.

"Don't worry, Asmodeus. You still have me. If there's trouble, I'm willing to help you. Besides, you're one of the Seven Demon Lords. How many people can actually defeat you?"

"You speak so sweetly..." Asmodeus covered her blushing cheeks with a fan, saying with a hint of shyness, "Actually volunteering to be the man behind my back (δδ) and willing to protect me in times of crisis. I kind of feel like I'm being forcefully kept as a mistress. Ah~ This old lady's girlish heart is stirring again..."

"What are you blushing for! You bastard! I'm doing this out of friendship!" Merlin frowned, shouting in exasperation, "We're friends, not having some dirty fling!"

"Lucifer, tell the truth. Don't you still secretly like me? Because you're thinking of our past, you're being nice to me. Indeed, your orientation has already been corrected by me, right?" Asmodeus asked shyly from the throne.

"Get lost. We have no past. That's just the dark history I can never erase..." Merlin showed an utterly hopeless expression, dripping with disgust.

"You really are a heartless male... " Asmodeus's expression fell, disappointed. "Although I'm touched that you're willing to act for me, as a monarch asking another monarch for help is a sign of great incompetence."

"You're truly troublesome..." Merlin grabbed the adventurer's permit hanging around his neck like a necklace, and said seriously—

"I'm no longer the Great Demon Lord of the First Palace."

"I am a Black Iron-ranked adventurer of Lrexam."

"The weakest kind there is..."

Cecilia and Kyle, after much inquiry, successfully arrived at Merlin and Alice's love nest.

Looking at Cecilia's starry-eyed fangirl appearance, she obviously greatly admired Merlin.

Thinking she was about to meet her idol, her heart couldn't help but feel very excited, her entire being in a state of euphoria.

Innocent Cecilia didn't yet know one fact—that

her idol Merlin was already married to Alice.

I wonder what Cecilia's reaction will be when she learns the truth?

title: Chapter 31
content:
Chapter 31

Volume 6 · Chapter 31

"Is this the place?" Cecilia surveyed the apartment building.

"Lord Cecilia, it should be this one. The address matches what the Guild administrator told us," Kyle said, nodding as he followed behind Cecilia.

"It's quite surprising that Lord Merlin actually lives in such a shabby, run-down house...." Cecilia's expression held a trace of astonishment.

A bead of cold sweat trickled down Kyle's forehead, but he kept his mouth shut, thinking to himself that his young mistress seemed unaware of the hardships common folk endured. This kind of housing was already considered quite good among ordinary people. Not everyone was born the daughter of the Rose Duke, living in gorgeous castles...

Still, Cecilia's nature wasn't bad. She just had a habit of throwing tantrums like a spoiled young lady and lacked a bit of common sense.

"Although she's so powerful, she doesn't even pursue a better life. Perhaps she's training under harsh conditions, right, Kyle?" Cecilia asked curiously, convinced this was some kind of ascetic practice on Merlin's part.

....Kyle's face darkened, not knowing how to respond.

If it truly were ascetic training, it would be far more grueling than this.

The bottom line for people living in these partition apartments was simply poverty!

If that Merlin was truly as powerful as the young mistress claimed, he wouldn't be short of money. Living in a place this shabby made no sense at all.

As expected, Lord Cecilia had been brainwashed—she couldn't even see something this simple and still went on praising that Black Iron villager.

Kyle stole a worried glance at Cecilia, completely unaware that every time Merlin and Alice earned money, they handed over a large sum to pay off debts, leaving only a tiny fraction of their earnings to barely get by.

"This is exactly why Lord Merlin is so impressive. He doesn't care about fame or wealth at all, keeping himself in harsh conditions for constant training. His spiritual realm is completely different from ours, which explains why Lord Merlin is so powerful. If you train like this day after day, it would be a miracle if you weren't strong!"

Cecilia's expression lit up with sudden realization as she kept praising Merlin, as though she had uncovered a great secret—she looked like a devoted fangirl to the letter.

Kyle kept his mouth tightly shut, but inside he felt sour and uncomfortable. His young mistress admiring someone else made him very ill at ease.

Cecilia adjusted her clothes to make herself look even more brilliant and polished.

She was about to meet her idol; she couldn't possibly show up looking anything less than perfect.

"Kyle, we should prepare to bother Lord Merlin a—..."

Inside the home.

Alice had spent the entire day showing off her cooking skills.

But since Sherry didn't particularly enjoy meat, she could only make vegetable-based dishes.

No matter how hard Alice tried, her results fell far short of Merlin's—not by just a little.

Sherry thought it wasn't bad, but even with the same vegetable salad, it simply tasted different from the one Merlin made.

Alice slumped into her chair like a deflated balloon, dejected. She thought that it must be a problem with her technique. After all, the steps were exactly the same—why was there such a huge gap?

QEZ Novel

Sherry set down her fork; she felt like she'd had enough by now. Seeing Alice sitting across the table in an apron with a crestfallen expression, she took pity on her.

"Miss Alice, please don't... don't be upset. The salad you made this time was quite good, much better than before."

"Sherry, don't do this. Suddenly comforting me just makes me feel even more pitiful...." Alice hung her head, sitting opposite at the dining table with her ahoge drooping listlessly.

"Um... Sherry didn't seem quite sure how to handle this situation, frantically searching for words. "Even though Miss Alice's cooking isn't on par with Mr. Merlin yet, reaching this level in just a few days is already amazing!"

"...Really?" Alice lifted her head slightly, seeming to desperately need someone's comfort.

"Yes! Really, I think Miss Alice is very smart already. Give it time and surpassing Mr. Merlin will be no problem. Please don't lose heart." Sherry clenched her small fists, cheering Alice on with an expression full of anticipation.

"Hmph~"

Alice's ahoge perked straight up as if recharged.

She placed her hands on her slim waist, stood up, and struck a proud pose, her entire face radiating arrogance.

"I knew I was a cooking genius! I'm definitely improving!"

"To reach this level in just a few days is truly commendable..."

"If I put in a little more effort, I'll crush Merlin in cooking without any pressure!"

Sherry's expression grew complicated, and she pressed her lips together in silence, awkwardly thinking, *Is that really possible? In every way, Miss Alice seems unable to match Mr. Merlin. I just offered a few encouraging words, and she's already floating away. Miss Alice really is an overly optimistic person....*

"Ding-dong!"

The doorbell suddenly rang, breaking the silence at the dining table.

"Hmm? Mr. Merlin seems to be back...." Sherry murmured softly.

"Good grief, this guy wandered off somewhere again without telling anyone all day and only just returned. How inconsiderate," Alice complained grumpily.

"Wandered off to do what?" Sherry forced a smile. "Mr. Merlin doesn't seem like someone who would do that kind of thing..."

"That can't be ruled out. After all, he has a prior record...." Alice said helplessly, recalling that Merlin had once gone with Hobbs to Helena's secret cabin. She hadn't been there herself, but she knew it wasn't exactly a respectable place.

"P-prior record?!" Sherry's eyes widened. Thinking of Merlin's usual "affectionate" behavior toward Alice, he didn't seem like someone who went around being unfaithful...

Alice didn't bother explaining further. She simply untied her apron and went straight to the door to answer it.

With a creak, the door opened, and Alice, without thinking, unleashed her prepared salvo straight away.

"Why are you only coming back now? Who were you out with today—huh? Who are you guys?"

Alice froze the moment she clearly saw the two people at the doorway; her prepared lines abruptly failed her.

Kyle and Cecilia outside the door were also dumbfounded. They had expected to see Merlin, but instead a silver-haired woman opened the door!?

Cecilia knew this was Merlin's home, but the fact that a silver-haired woman was inside meant they were cohabiting—that was certain!

The two girls frowned and studied each other, trying to figure out the other's identity. Neither said anything rash for the moment.

Kyle was equally stunned at first, but when he caught sight of the couple's adventurer credentials around Alice's neck, everything clicked into place. So this silver-haired girl was Merlin's wife. What a surprise.

His husband was a Black Iron villager who only knew how to bluff and swindle, yet his wife was a fine Gold-ranked adventurer. ...This was exactly what you'd call living off a woman's money. Confirmatory evidence, beyond any doubt. Their lordess's daily praises of that Merlin were indeed nothing but hot air, as expected—he truly wasn't any good at all!

A Black Iron villager managing to trick a Gold-ranked adventurer into marrying him—his skill at coaxing women was extraordinary, honestly incredible, utterly shameless!

A hint of a smile crossed Kyle's face, and the worry that had been weighing on him instantly lifted.

Since Merlin was already married, there was absolutely no way anything could happen between his young mistress and this Black Iron villager.

Moreover, numerous signs pointed to Merlin being a scumbag who deceived women's feelings. Couldn't his young mistress see that clearly now?

Kyle's spirits lifted so much he nearly felt like humming a little tune.

After studying each other for a long while, the two girls spoke in unison, both questioning the other—

Cecilia: "Who are you?!"

Alice: "Who are you?"

Chapter 32 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 6 · Chapter 32

Both girls asked at the same time, leaving each other thoroughly bewildered.

There was a hint of tension in their tone, a distinctly head-on clash.

Cecilia sensed something was off. This silver-haired woman was actually cohabiting with Lord Merlin, so their relationship must be extraordinary.

They were living together now, so what else could they possibly be doing? It was exactly the kind of relationship that made people's imaginations run wild.

Merlin was currently Cecilia's idol, someone she worshipped to the point of obsession. If he had an ambiguous relationship with the silver-haired woman before her, she would naturally feel uncomfortable.

Think about female fans in the real world who, upon learning their idol is too close to another woman, will get as irritable as Angry Birds. How frustrating that must feel!

Alice's thoughts were even more peculiar. Perhaps because Kael's presence was somewhat faint, her attention was entirely focused on the blonde young lady before her.

She thought about how Merlin often slipped out to hang out with Hobus, and wondered if he had picked up some romantic entanglement somewhere—something like hiring someone and not paying, so the woman had tracked him down. What an incredibly aggravating situation!

Merlin was a demon after all, so why was he involved with a supposedly holy priestess?!

Could it be that demons naturally enjoyed defiling pure and sacred things? Such a bizarre preference was hard to understand!

Having calmed down slightly, Alice felt she shouldn't look down on this priestess either.

After all, she was the Hero, and she had even slept with the Great Demon Lord Merlin.

Now Alice felt a flicker of worry and discomfort, as though a severe crisis had struck her so-called marriage.

She was convinced that Cecilia was some loose woman Merlin had picked up while fooling around outside.

So from the moment she arrived, Alice showed hostility—her tone and expression were far from pleasant.

She had even handed over her home address. Their relationship clearly wasn't ordinary, right?

Alice had made up her mind: if Cecilia was here to collect payment for services, then Alice could pay her first, but once Merlin returned, she would settle scores with that shameless bastard!

She had warned Merlin repeatedly before, yet he still went out to fool around and got himself tangled in drama.

Even though she was a fake wife and shouldn't meddle too much, couldn't she at least do something rather than be this pathetic?

Alice glared at Cecilia and said resentfully,

"Who am I? Why should I tell you? If you're coming to my door, shouldn't you introduce yourself first? Have you no manners at all!"

"Huh!? " Cecilia, provoked by this commoner, felt deeply offended. "Are you serious!? Asking me to introduce myself first? Lower your attitude, mere commoner. Do you even know who you're talking to?"

"I don't care who you are!" Alice waved her hand, furiously demanding, "What's your relationship with Merlin? How did you even find this place? Where's that damn man!?"

"Shouldn't I be the one asking you that? What's your relationship with Lord Merlin? And how dare you call Lord Merlin a dead man! That is utterly unforgivable!" Cecilia knit her brows sharply.

"Do I need to ask? Isn't it obvious? Can't you see that I'm the mistress of this house!?" Alice planted her hands on her hips and declared in a domineering manner, radiating the air of a true wife.

"Huh!? What nonsense are you spouting? Look at that flat chest of yours! How could Lord Merlin ever be interested in you? I could say I had unspeakable dealings with Lord Merlin in the dungeon!"

Cecilia went *thump* and thrust her full breasts forward, as if deliberately showing off her figure to Alice, who was as flat as an ironing board.

Cecilia's priestess white robe was already somewhat sexy, revealing a tantalizing cleavage, which doubled the psychological damage dealt to Alice!

Hearing Cecilia's words, Kael standing nearby felt as though green leaves were growing lushly atop his head, his mood extremely complicated.

But Kael didn't take it seriously, because Cecilia, as a priestess, always maintained her dignity and frequently said things in the heat of the moment.

Perhaps she was just competing with Alice right now. Kael had no idea that Cecilia's hot words were half-true, half-joking.

If Merlin had harbored even the slightest wicked thought that day, then Kael would absolutely be wearing that green crown.

Alice widened her eyes, secretly feeling a pang of nervousness, and said in a deliberately calm tone, "You're lying! Merlin would never be interested in you! We... we're so devoted to each other! We're inseparable, there's no room for a third person!"

"Heh heh~ Your voice isn't even steady. Are you feeling guilty?" Cecilia puffed out her chest and said sarcastically, "Some girls really have no shame. Why don't they look in the mirror and see what they're worth? Yet they desperately throw themselves at Lord Merlin."

"...What did you say!?" Alice was nearly vomiting blood from just watching Cecilia flaunt her bosom, and now being called someone who threw herself at a man only made her anger surge. "I was never throwing myself at anyone! Take back what you just said, or I won't hold back!"

"See, I hit the nail right on the head and you're already angry? Hehehe~" Cecilia covered her mouth, laughing until her whole body trembled.

"Tch!" Alice's face contorted with anger, and without any restraint, she unleashed her high-tier pressure. Cold energy instantly swept through the area.

The situation instantly grew tense. It seemed an angry Alice wasn't reluctant to start a fight right at the doorway.

"High-tier... both magic and martial arts cultivated!?"

Cecilia's face went pale as she sensed two different kinds of power, leaving her overwhelmed and at a loss.

She was merely a mid-tier priestess with no combat ability at all, no match for Alice.

Still somewhat composed, Cecilia immediately called upon her loyal hound to handle Alice.

"Kael! Protect me!"

"As you command, Lady Cecilia!" Kael positioned himself in front of Cecilia like a devoted dog, his silver lance held横 across his body.

Kael instantly unleashed his own high-tier pressure, clashing with Alice's. From the very first exchange, he was already tacitly at a disadvantage.

This situation made Kael's heart sink. He was also high-tier, so the gap shouldn't be this large.

But reality delivered a harsh lesson, making it immediately clear who was stronger and who was weaker! The gap was enormous!

Alice, blessed with the power of a Saint Dragon, was far more difficult to defeat at the same tier.

The current Alice, if facing a mediocre Saint-tier like Goblin Emperor Saggus, could hold her own in a head-on confrontation.

Alice's body was wreathed in cold energy, and she didn't even glance at Kael, instead staring angrily at Cecilia behind him the entire time.

How dare she call Alice indecent and accuse her of chasing after the Great Demon Lord!?

How was Alice supposed to be seen as such a worthless person? She wasn't anywhere near that awful!

Cecilia's words had deeply wounded Alice's pride, which was precisely why she was so furious now.

The two groups faced off at the entrance to the communal bath, neither willing to retract their pressure. A great battle was imminent!

Cecilia also sensed that Kael's pressure was at a disadvantage, but they had two people on her side!

The spearman could deal damage up front while she provided buffs and healing from behind. They would easily win, no problem at all.

"Commoner! You dare intimidate this young lady? The sheer audacity!" Cecilia's gaze sharpened, a thin scowl on her pretty face as she confidently issued her order.

"Kael, attack!"

"Show this rude woman some respect!"
