Chapter 42 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 6 · Chapter 42

"Cough!" Merlin cleared his throat to cover his embarrassment and said, "Uh... could you maybe act a little more normal? Don't call me—"

"I can't, sir. Even though you're low-key, you're still a Saint-tier powerhouse worthy of my respect. Besides, I argued with you yesterday, so showing respect is only proper!" Kyle answered earnestly, feeling that if he didn't act polite, it would make him seem completely rude.

A cold sweat bead slid down Merlin's forehead. He'd just thought of himself as a villager withoutSaint-tier status or magic aura.

But Merlin could tell Kyle was the stubborn type, so he懒得 bother.

"Whatever..."

"Thank you, Lord Merlin." Kyle bowed his head, looking thoroughly respectful.

Merlin glanced at the carriage, which seemed even more luxurious than Arnold's. He couldn't help muttering under his breath, "Miss Cecilia really knows how to enjoy herself. How much did this carriage cost?"

"You flatter her, Lord Merlin. Nobles need to maintain face when traveling, and Lady Cecilia is no exception. In truth, Miss Cecilia knows how to spend reasonably—far better than most nobles." Kyle explained, not wanting Merlin to misunderstand Cecilia.

"You really are loyal to a fault..." Three black lines appeared on Merlin's forehead.

"Thank you for the praise, Lord Merlin." Kyle wasn't offended at all. As the lady's knight, he was supposed to serve her side like a dog.

"...Merlin frowned. Did this guy have a problem in the head?

"Lord Merlin, please board the carriage quickly." Kyle gestured with a bowing motion.

Merlin shook his head and climbed into the carriage directly.

The carriage began rolling forward, smoother than expected.

They hadn't yet left Rexham, so it was still smoother than anticipated.

Kyle and Cecilia sat on one side, while Merlin, Alice, and Shelly sat opposite them.

Alice, for some reason, deliberately sat in the middle to separate Merlin and Shelly.

From the moment they boarded, Shelly had been clinging to Alice, trembling and hiding behind her while偷偷 sizing up Kyle and Cecilia across from them.

Merlin glanced at Alice and couldn't help wondering—

Alice really is quite popular, isn't she?

Why can't I see what unique charm she has?

Shelly's been living with me for days too, yet she still likes Alice more.

Is it because she's stupid and therefore lovable? Hmm, quite possibly...

Merlin muttered in his heart, completely unable to notice what charm Alice possessed.

"Good morning, Lord Merlin." Cecilia lowered her head to express her respect.

"Mmm." Merlin nodded. It was time to talk business. "Yesterday I only heard your general plan. Now I have time—can you go into detail?"

"Very well." Cecilia paused thoughtfully, then began speaking seriously. "Our mission is to eliminate an evil alchemist named Democritus, who's been entrenched on a lonely island in the strait."

"Democritus!?" Alice furrowed her brows. The name sounded vaguely familiar.

"What, you know him?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"Not personally, but I've heard he's a very powerful alchemist with a unique method. He's also known as an expert on dragons, with deep knowledge of dragonkind." Alice gave a brief explanation.

"That's not all. Based on the intelligence I've gathered, Democritus creates alchemical beasts." Cecilia added.

Merlin's eyes narrowed slightly. This was the second time he'd heard the term "alchemical beast." Asmodeus had mentioned that a certain brazen human who planned to shoot the Demon Lord into explosion was also an alchemist. Could they be the same person?

"What exactly is an alchemical beast?" Alice had never heard of it and asked curiously.

"It's a creature made from strange and unusual materials—an unthinking monster. But through the alchemist's modifications, its power is far greater than you'd imagine." Kyle explained from the side.

"Moreover, this Democritus is no ordinary opponent. The report says that recently, fish in the waters around the isolated island underwent mutations, making it hard for locals to make a living. A group of a hundred fishermen自发 organized an expedition, planning to board the island at midnight—but all of them perished at sea. This alchemist clearly has some real strength."

Cecilia's expression was grave. She felt that relying solely on herself and Kyle might not be enough to handle this incident.

"That's precisely why I invited Lord Merlin to assist. I want this operation to be foolproof."

"That doesn't put much pressure on me. Just chopping down an alchemist, nothing more. Though—exactly which strait are we talking about?" Merlin asked, puzzled.

"The Strait of Dover, between Kent and France..." Cecilia answered sincerely.

"I see... Hmm!?" Merlin suddenly realized something and hurriedly pressed, "Those fishermen who perished at sea—weren't they from the coastal villages of Kent?"

"That's correct. They were fishermen from the Kent coast." Cecilia nodded.

"What the hell, no way!" Merlin's brows locked tight. He remembered Hobbes casually mentioning not long ago—

「There was a commission from a coastal fishing village in Kent. The pay was quite generous.」

"Lord Merlin, what's wrong?" Alice looked at him strangely, sensing this reaction was abnormal.

"Lady Cecilia's matter seems to collide with another situation." Merlin calmed down slightly.

"Huh? What do you mean?" Cecilia asked in surprise.

"It appears the fishing village in Kent has already hired an adventurer to handle the same problem. Seems like a rather powerful one..." Merlin said calmly.

"Who is it?" Alice furrowed her brows.

"I'm not entirely sure either. I just remember he's an Irish 50/50-ranked, something called Elvin Johnson..." Merlin said while recalling.

Alice: "What!? It's Johnson!"

Cecilia: "Could it be the Irish genius magician!?"

Kyle: "If I'm not mistaken, it must be that fourteen-year-old Saint-tier powerhouse, hailed as the future star of magic in Great Britain!"

Everyone in the carriage except Shelly—who was just full of polite greetings in her mind—was utterly shocked:

"Your reactions are quite exaggerated..." Merlin said expressionlessly.

"Not reacting would be more abnormal, now would it? That's a magic genius—affinity with all magical elements, capable of copying others' spells. He's practically a monster!" Alice seemed genuinely shocked, her composure shaken. After all, Arnold had mentioned the Irish genius magician's name not long ago while on the carriage.

"Yes, achieving this at only fourteen is indeed terrifying." Kyle's mouth twitched, sweating profusely. He thought he and that person were in completely different leagues.

"Am I going to come back empty-handed again? Why am I running into a monster like this..."

Cecilia grew a bit uneasy.

"You folks are disgraceful, getting scared by someone's name like this..." Merlin sighed, pointed at himself seriously, and declared,

"Don't worry!"

"No matter what kind of genius they are, they'll fall gracefully before me."

"Especially magic geniuses—they're nothing but a joke in front of me."

(╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻

title: Chapter 1
content:
Chapter 1

Volume 7 · Chapter 1

The Royal Capital of London.

Within the city, lights shone brightly, showing no sign of decay.

Countless colors painted the city's vibrant prosperity.

The broad Thames River cut through the entire city, its shimmering waters breathtakingly beautiful.

As the cultural and economic center of all of Britain, it was naturally incomparable to any ordinary city.

The white palace at the center was extraordinarily magnificent; that was the residence of Queen Elizabeth, the most beautiful building in all of London.

Only the great clock tower attached to Parliament House could rival it in beauty, its height the greatest in all of London, inspiring awe at its magnificent sight.

Even at night, the clock tower still shimmered with radiance, like a torch blazing toward the sky, beautiful yet majestic.

Each time the clock tower struck, its sound echoed throughout all of London, evoking a sense of divine royalty.

Somewhere in the center of the royal capital stood a building that clashed with its surroundings, as though it belonged to another country.

Yet its graceful decorum and dignified façade both proclaimed this was no ordinary place.

Carved依次 along the entrance were nine statues, each rendered with lifelike vividness:

Elf, dwarf, orc, dragon, treant, rock man, giant, goblin, mermaid.

These were the nine kings of the various races from the Southern United Kingdom's Parliament, each a ruler over their own people.

Among them, the statue of the Elf King stood at the very center, slightly larger than the others.

It was not hard to guess what this place was. Indeed, this was the Elf Clan's embassy in Britain for the Southern United Kingdom.

It was dinner time, and the nearby streets were very quiet, but the underground of the Elf Embassy buzzed with activity...

A pitch-black underground hall.

Only torches lit the surroundings.

Before the grand mirror deep within, a beautiful female elf in a white dress murmured something to herself.

Her skin was fairer than snow, her black hair and slender waist exuding an elegant and noble aura. Her beautiful face carried a mature charm, quite unlike Shirley's innocence.

This person was the Elf Clan's ambassador to Britain, a beautiful elf named Samuel Stuart, already nearly a thousand years old.

The great mirror seemed to possess some sort of magic. It had been reflecting Samuel's figure, but slowly transformed into a vague black shadow, as though becoming someone else entirely.

Upon seeing the black shadow, Samuel immediately knelt on one knee, her manner respectful and devout.

Without much greeting, the black shadow spoke first — and it was a woman's voice!

Black Shadow: "Long time no see, Samuel."

Samuel: "Greetings, my Liege. I have come to report on the progress of the Elven Lament Grand Magic Formation."

Black Shadow: "How has it gone?"

Samuel: "It is essentially complete. All of London lies within the magic formation. Once activated, this capital of Britain, London, will be reduced to an empty city in an instant, and all the lowly humans will die, their souls sacrificed to you, our great Liege."

Black Shadow: "Excellent! The goal of my resurrection is now within reach! Once I am successfully resurrected, I will never again need to dwell within the body of the Elf King's wife. The entire Southern United Kingdom will fall under my control, and conquering the world will be nothing difficult!"

Samuel: "Congratulations, my Liege, on coming one step closer to your dream of resurrection. As the Dark Elf King, you shall surely become the master of the world!"

Black Shadow: "Indeed! I am the genius of the elf race, having mastered the power of the Elf God Corellon. My brother Lancy may be Elf King, but he is no match for me. He was even envious of my talent and ruthlessly plotted against his own younger brother. If not for my soul's great strength, I would have long fallen to hell. Until I personally kill the Elf King, I can never escape his shadow!"

A vast amount of magical power poured out from within the demon mirror, waves of black mist surging forth like angry flames spreading wildly.

Within the pitch-black shadow, only scarlet, burning eyes glowed fiercely, its emotions clearly unstable.

Samuel: "Calm yourself, my Liege. You are currently in a dwelling state. If your emotions grow too unstable, it would easily cause the consciousness of the Elf King's wife to break free from control."

Black Shadow: "That is true. With the moment of my resurrection drawing ever nearer, I should be rejoicing."

Samuel: "Yes, my Liege. Once you are resurrected, the Elf King will surely pay the price for his past misdeeds!"

Black Shadow: "What an exhilarating thought. All six million people of London will be sacrificed simultaneously, becoming stepping stones on my path to resurrection. Such a large-scale sacrifice can be said to have开创-history, with me, Arathodur Lancy, as its pioneer. Just thinking of the moment of sacrifice, what a spectacular sight it will be..."

Samuel: "This Elven Lament Grand Magic Formation that sacrifices all of London's population is indeed a feat unparalleled in history. However, although everything is in place, there is a small issue—"

Black Shadow: "What issue?"

Samuel: "To activate Elven Lament, a member of the royal family must be sacrificed as a catalyst, but there does not seem to be a suitable candidate."

Black Shadow: "Indeed, only a royal's soul can activate Elven Lament. After all, Elven Lament is one of the three forbidden spells of the elf race. As long as the soul has not fallen to hell, it can reverse life and death, though the cost is certainly no ordinary one..."

Samuel: "Then what should I do now, my Liege?"

Black Shadow: "The Elf King currently keeps his children very close, making it difficult to find an opportunity. The only choice is..."

Samuel: "My Liege?"

Black Shadow: "The only choice is恐怕... the Elf King's youngest daughter, Shirley, who went missing half a year ago."

Samuel: "Princess Shirley? It has been over half a year, and there is still no news of the young princess. Could she have already died?"

Black Shadow: "You should know that elves can sense the life and death of their children. Shirley is definitely not dead, otherwise why would the Elf King not have given up the search? He must have sensed that she is still alive."

Samuel: "I see. Forgive me, my Liege. I was being foolish just now."

Black Shadow: "Put some effort into searching. The Elf King always keeps Shirley close to his side in Britain. As her father, his perception will almost certainly be correct."

Samuel: "I will search with all my might and use every means to bring Princess Shirley back."

Black Shadow: "That is good. Once she is captured, do not hesitate. Activate Elven Lament directly and let me resurrect. With my power at that time—"

Samuel: "Understood, my Liege. I will handle it properly! Even if it costs my soul, I will ensure your resurrection!"

The black shadow in the magic mirror spread its arms, its figure strikingly graceful. If the black mist were dispelled, it would likely be a beautiful woman.

Though her figure was alluring, it could not conceal her towering ambition.

The Dark Elf King was currently in a soul state, dwelling within the Elf King's wife's body, but from that kingly aura, one could still catch glimpses of his former glory.

"When I am resurrected, it shall be the day the world is shrouded in the shadow of the Dark Elf King!"

"I, Arathodur Lancy, shall lead the dark elves toward prosperity and glory!"

"The trajectory of the world shall revert, returning to the glorious Elf Era!"

title: Chapter 2 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 2 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 7 · Chapter 2

In the basement of the Elf Embassy.

Samuel stepped out of the secret chamber, the door slowly closing behind him.

Two subordinates, one man and one woman, immediately approached.

They wore tight-fitting combat attire, their eyes bright and sharp. Their dark black skin and pointed ears were enough to reveal their identity—

Dark elves, a branch of the elf race!

All elves worship the same deity, Corellon, and share the same origins, yet two visibly distinct types of elves emerged.

The white elves represented by the Elf King, and the dark elves represented by the Dark Elf King.

Both were ancient monsters who had lived through countless ages, surviving from the Elf Era all the way to the present, which showed just how terrifyingly long the elf lifespan truly was.

Though they were biological brothers, their beliefs diverged sharply, and conflicts between them were constant.

However, the white elves had always held the dominant position, and it remained so even now.

When the Southern United Kingdom was first founded, the King's Council had allowed only one representative per race to hold power.

This thoroughly intensified the矛盾 between white elves and dark elves, and rebellion began to erupt within the elf race itself.

But the outcome was brutally harsh—the Dark Elf King championed by the dark elves was defeated by the Elf King, stripped of equal standing, and their situation grew ever more demeaning.

In contrast, the Elf King solidified his position by slaying his own brother, continuing his rule throughout the Southern United Kingdom.

Though these two dark elves resembled the pristine Samuel in appearance—both with pointed ears and handsome faces—their temperament and skin tone were entirely different.

These dark elves were Saul's trusted confidants and henchmen of the Dark Elf King.

The male dark elf was named Shapelen, a Saint-tier martial artist skilled in an ancient and mysterious dark elf combat art, his techniques vicious and ruthless beyond measure!

The female dark elf was named Shalan, a Saint-tier magician whose dark magic prowess was uncanny, causing her enemies to slowly rot away in darkness!

These two were Saul's most capable subordinates, their strength unmatched, truly her right and left arms.

As fellow worshippers of the Dark Elf King, their greatest goal was to see the dark elves rise and flourish once more.

Rather than letting the dark elves remain perpetual vassals of the white elves, living the humiliating life of dependents under another's roof.

And as for Samuel's strength?

For two Saint-tier powerhouses to submit to her, how could she possibly be weak?

But Samuel's public image had always been that of the elf race's ambassador, someone who did not use magic or martial techniques.

She constantly suppressed her pressure, ensuring no one could detect it, giving people the illusion that she was utterly powerless……

This made it easier for Samuel to hide herself and secretly do things, such as setting up the great magic array that caused the Elves' Lament.

The two subordinates stepped forward, eager to ask what had been communicated with the Dark Elf King—

Shapelen couldn't wait to ask, "Excellency Samuel, what did His Majesty Ahxiudor say?"

Shalan also couldn't help but chime in, "Has the moment to resurrect His Majesty Ahxiudor finally arrived?"

"Be patient. We still lack certain conditions for now, and must endure a while longer." Samuel shook her head, then changed the subject. "But the day when His Majesty Ahxiudor is resurrected is growing ever closer. When that time comes, our dark elf clan will surely rise."

A look of joy spread across Shapelen and Shalan's faces; there was hardly any news more thrilling than the resurrection of the Dark Elf King.

"Excellency Samuel, may I ask what conditions are currently lacking?" Shalan asked humbly.

"The great magic spell Elves' Lament required to resurrect His Majesty Ahxiudor is missing a catalyst. We must offer the soul of royalty for it to activate properly," Samuel said calmly, rather exasperated by the harsh requirements of the three prohibited spells of the elf race.

"Then what does Excellency Samuel need us to do? Please give the order and we shall carry it out!" Shapelen said with passionate fervor.

"Immediately dispatch your subordinates to search every corner of Britain and bring back Princess Shelly, who disappeared half a year ago," Samuel ordered plainly.

"Isn't Princess Shelly dead?" Shalan asked in surprise.

"No, she must still be alive somewhere……"

Samuel walked ahead and paused, her pristine aura fading away as her true appearance gradually revealed itself.

Black skin covered her entire body, crimson eyes gleamed with wickedness, and her pointed black ears twitched occasionally.

Samuel seemed as if her entire being had shattered; she grinned widely, revealing jagged, serrated teeth, the atmosphere shifting drastically.

"As soon as we capture Princess Shelly, the era that belongs to us shall arrive!

"Following in the footsteps of His Majesty Ahxiudor, we shall step by step reach the pinnacle of the world!

"Slaughtering and trampling upon the dignity of other races—isn't that simply wonderful!?"

"Ah~…… How thrilling. It's making me…… wet……"

Following Samuel's gaze downward, there was actually a deep pit in the ground, from which wails and howls of the tormented dead emanated continuously—

"Oh woooo……"

Beyond the horrifying ghostly cries, there were also the sounds of scratching against walls, enough to make one's scalp tingle with dread.

At the bottom of the pit, countless starving ghouls were being kept!?

Their fingers ended in blade-like nails, their teeth were like those of beasts, and not a single hair grew on their blue skin.

Countless red-glowing eyes in the darkness formed a scene both majestic and spine-chilling!

The ghouls were either devouring each other or desperately trying to get out to hunt for fresh flesh and blood. This scene could rightfully be called a war……

Early the next morning.

An ornate carriage slowly rolled into London, heading toward an expensive private residence.

Since Cecil was nobility, the London city guards didn't even bother to check and let her right in.

This made Merlin quietly grumble about the evils of capitalism—

Every time he entered a village, he had to pay money and register, and if he ran into troublesome guards, he'd be interrogated……

The status of nobility was truly convenient. Privileges everywhere, along with national benefits.

Merlin also wished he could get some, so his life would be far more convenient, wouldn't it?

Shelly, half-asleep, leaned against Alice's shoulder and drifted off, her breathing steady, seemingly dreaming of returning home.

Alice felt her shoulder growing numb and sore, but she couldn't bring herself to wake Shelly.

She figured the child had been exhausted all along the journey, clinging to her side the whole time and never wanting to separate.

Alice was the person Shelly trusted the most. Wandering around in a human kingdom without Alice by her side, Shelly would probably have burst into tears right then and there, unable to move.

"She really likes you, Miss Shelly?" Merlin asked lazily, propping his cheek with his hand.

"Hmph!" Alice pouted proudly. "I'm just naturally likable. Got a problem with that?"

"No, I'm just a bit curious. Miss Shelly is already quite grown up, yet she still clings like a child. It's a bit strange, don't you think? That kind of personality is usually seen in homebodies who've never traveled far." Merlin offered his speculation offhand.

"Nonsense. You think everyone is like you?" Alice couldn't help but retort.

"What about me?" Merlin looked completely innocent. Being a homebody made him proud, after all.

"Miss Shelly is just too timid around strangers, and she was abused by the remnants of the former kingdom. She maintains a constant attitude of fear toward humans, so she'll definitely feel very不安 when outside. When I'm by her side, she feels safe. That's something you can't compare to." Alice waved her hand and continued, "But Miss Shelly is about to go home now. The days of wandering outside are finally over. Though I'll miss her a bit, I'm still happy for her."

"I hope nothing goes wrong. I don't want all my efforts to go to waste……" Merlin rested his chin on his hand and gazed out the carriage window at the London streets, silently thinking—

London truly feels like a place hiding dragons and tigers, doesn't it?

But danger lurks everywhere alongside it……

This volume has many characters. Some hinted-at powerhouses will make their presence known in this volume. Just don't get face-blind.

title: Chapter 3 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 3 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 7 · Chapter 3

"By the way, London's guards are well-equipped. Look at the armor they're wearing — it's shiny enough to use as a mirror."

Merlin couldn't help but sigh in amazement, thinking about the guards in Lrexham whose armor was lucky to not even be rusted.

"Well, this is the capital after all, it's bound to be different from other places." Alice paused and said helplessly, "What, are you jealous? Housing prices here are insanely expensive. Two months' rent in the central area is enough for me to buy an apartment."

"I'm not exactly jealous. Small places have their own advantages too, everyone has their strengths." Merlin said blandly, thinking that human kingdoms were so prosperous, unlike the demon territories which looked particularly barren.

Although Merlin wasn't new to big cities, this was actually his first time in London.

It felt even more prosperous than Manchester, which he had visited before. No wonder it was the center of Great Britain.

"How about it?" Cecilia said happily, unable to hold back, "Lord Merlin, are you also interested in living in London?"

"Not particularly. It's crowded like an ant nest, a bit annoying." Merlin answered casually.

"....." Cecilia was momentarily at a loss for words, wondering if Lord Merlin was disgusted by humans. Or rather, was he subtly insulting himself? As expected of Lord Merlin, everything he says is so philosophical.

Ignoring Cecilia's fangirl-like stare, Merlin silently complained inwardly: too many gifted people, having to wait in line to buy anything, getting crushed in a shared carriage, and the worst part — one gold coin could buy a lot elsewhere, but in London it might only get you a long baguette..

Seems like Merlin isn't completely without economic sense, knowing where his wealth could survive.

"Then....." A cold sweat ran down Kyle's forehead as he couldn't help but defend his young lady, "Lord Merlin is overthinking it. London is actually quite nice. Although it's crowded, all kinds of living conditions are good, such as many entertainment venues...."

"Hmm? Entertainment venues?" Merlin showed a meaningful smile.

"That creepy grin is back...." Alice said with resignation.

"What are you talking about, Kyle!?" Cecilia reprimanded不满edly.

"I meant casinos, not something else," Kyle explained awkwardly.

"Casinos!?" Merlin instinctively perked up, feeling like the arena for a comeback was right in front of him.

Alice couldn't help but lower her voice to warn Merlin, "Don't go to those places, or I'll cut half your monthly salary."

"On what grounds do you boss me around? It's so annoying when you point fingers at me, ah..." Merlin frowned and answered in an annoyed tone.

"I'm only looking out for you! Your luck is terrible. Throwing money into a casino is like throwing it into a bottomless pit." Alice emphasized angrily.

"I think you're up to no good, trying to stop me from turning my life around, wanting to see me fail." Merlin's conspiracy theories were starting to kick in again.

"What do you want to see me fail at?" Alice's head was full of question marks, wondering if she often mocked Merlin in the past.

"You'd secretly feel pleased seeing me worry about making a living~" Merlin was convinced that was exactly what Alice was thinking.

"Shut up! I'm not the kind of person with such a terrible personality!" Alice defended herself, emphasizing, "If you spend money recklessly, it will indirectly affect me."

"Is that your excuse for hoarding my salary? Actually, the one gold coin you gave me last time was unreasonable, right? It feels like you secretly embezzled my hard-earned money." Merlin said suspiciously.

"W-whatever! I'm a person of good character!" Alice's face turned slightly red as she pointed at herself, thinking that last time she had secretly added some taxes and kept the money for herself, but she felt absolutely no guilt — taking money from the enemy isn't robbing, it's called looting~

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue, an air of disdain washing over him.

"What's with that look of contempt!?!" Alice glared at Merlin angrily.

Watching the two bicker, Cecilia asked curiously, "Aren't Lord Merlin and Miss Alice married? Why do you divide money so strictly? Isn't it all shared property?"

"Who is...gah!"

Merlin didn't get to finish his sentence before Alice covered his mouth, not letting him explain.

Alice thought, a word spoken is like water spilled — she couldn't let it slip now.

She had put on such a good act in front of Cecilia earlier, and she had to stick with it even if it hurt.

What if Cecilia found out the truth and laughed at her? That would be too embarrassing!

"Eh?!" Cecilia was stunned, not understanding what was happening. "Miss Alice, what do you mean by that?"

"Merlin... he likes to say things carelessly. Even if we are married, don't we still need to keep accounts carefully?" Alice thought for a moment and added, "Miss Cecilia, you're not married yet, you wouldn't understand."

"...Is that so?" Cecilia's eyes were suspicious, feeling that Alice's excuse was too far-fetched.

Alice deliberately lowered her voice and secretly told Merlin, "Don't explain our relationship to Miss Cecilia. Let her keep misunderstanding."

Merlin looked at Alice and pulled her hand away, wondering what Alice was doing. Why wouldn't she let him explain? Being misunderstood was a headache, wasn't it?

"It's our seminary!" Cecilia looked out the carriage window and showed a delighted smile. "Lord Merlin, quick..."

"Hmm?" Merlin followed Cecilia's gaze and his expression became uncomfortable, because straight ahead was the statue of the Goddess of Light — someone he absolutely detested.

But on the other hand, it was well-built, a typical Gothic structure full of sharp lines.

"Lord Merlin, what do you think? Isn't it beautiful?" Cecilia asked excitedly.

"It's okay." Merlin answered awkwardly, not having the heart to say he wanted to tear the seminary down.

Alice beside her barely held back laughter, knowing Merlin hated anything related to the Holy Church. Even if the seminary was splendid, Merlin would never say it was nice.

"Okay?" Cecilia was stunned, then widened her eyes. "It must be that your standards are too high, and you simply can't appreciate this place."

"...Well, I'm just...I find it annoying when a bunch of Holy Church charlatans show up in a perfectly good city out of nowhere. It's practically spreading heresy openly."

"Lord Merlin, Great Britain has good relations with the Holy Church, how can you call it a cult? This seminary was personally approved by Queen Elizabeth..." Kyle was a bit confused.

"It is a cult. Those charlatans speak nothing but lies, and their so-called piety toward God is laughable. They're all motivated by profit." Merlin criticized the Holy Church's priests without restraint.

"Lord Merlin, your words would get you pelted with eggs by believers." A cold sweat ran down Kyle's forehead.

"Hmph! Just ignorant fools." Merlin snorted and said firmly.

"Don't mind him, he always views the Holy Church through tinted glasses. It's useless to argue with him." Alice said empathetically, then turned to ask, "Miss Cecilia, as a student at the seminary, what do you study every day?"

"Praying for world peace, singing hymns together, confessing the sins of the day, practicing light-element magic, and listening to lectures from priests." Cecilia answered while thinking.

"Listening... sounds a bit boring, doesn't it?" Alice furrowed her brows, thinking she had once been the Church's Hero and never had to do any of this nonsense. In the end, strength was what truly mattered.

"It's not boring! We also have exorcism classes!" Cecilia said seriously.

"Exorcism classes!?" Alice had never even heard of this subject.

Merlin frowned, feeling it couldn't be anything good. It seemed designed to deal with demons like himself.

"Yes, this subject was recently approved by the Pope, so....." Cecilia thought for a moment and counted seriously, "Using silver needles to stab the demon's testicles, stuffing garlic into the demon's nostrils, and poking the demon's anus with blunt silver weapons...."

......Merlin's face turned dark, his brows tightly knit, black lines running down his head as he thought —

What the hell is this ridiculous stuff!?!

They're even teaching anal penetration now, there's no humanity here!

I seriously suspect the priest who designed this course is a faggot!

title: Chapter 4
content:
Chapter 4

Volume 7 · Chapter 4

Merlin's face darkened. Who came up with this new exorcism technique?! They couldn't possibly be a normal person!

He suppressed his rage at dismantling the divine academy, wanting nothing more than to beat the priest who taught exorcismology to death, in order to protect the butts of all the demons.

Although Merlin was an outlier among demons and not afraid of silver, that didn't mean other demons weren't.

Demons felt pain upon touching silver, and then being prodded in the butt with silver weapons—oh, the sheer stimulation of that, it was simply incredible.

"Pfft~!" Alice couldn't hold it in and laughed out loud, looking at Merlin with an odd expression.

"Miss Alice, please don't laugh. Exorcism is a very serious matter," Cecilia said solemnly, seeming to feel slighted.

"Sorry, sorry, I know it's serious, but I just can't help it... Pfft~" Alice imagined the scene of Merlin being prodded in the butt with silver weapons. It was such a vivid picture—truly unbearable to look at.

"Stop laughing and put those perverted thoughts out of your head, be serious, alright?" Merlin shot Alice an annoyed glance.

"You're so controlling. Can you really stop me from daydreaming?" Alice rolled her eyes at Merlin and stuck up her nose.

"Miss Alice, Lord Merlin is right. Please don't laugh. The priests who taught us exorcism all said that it is a sacred thing..." Cecilia paused, then continued devoutly, "...before performing an exorcism, one must bathe and change, then wear revealing leather armor, put on a collar, and proudly display one's muscles. Then the demon is led into a small room and tied to a bed. One silently recites, 'Thank you, Goddess Maria, for giving me a new rear,' and finally takes out the club-like silver weapon to do things everyone understands."

Merlin covered his darkening face. He couldn't listen anymore, his mind going wild. Isn't this literally 哲学 (philosophy)... No, wait—this is the homosect!

"B-but... wouldn't it hurt...?" Alice asked curiously.

"The priests say it won't. Demons only feel pleasure." Cecilia said it with a completely straight face.

"Pleasure? Pfft pfft~" Alice looked at Merlin with a meaningful smile, clearly quite eager to try.

"Get lost! Don't stare at me like that..." Merlin's butt tightened, feeling deep malice from Alice's gaze.

Alice wasn't offended. Instead, she said to Cecilia, "Can you teach me? I'd also like to bring some demon some pleasure."

"Are you kidding me? If you dare learn this, I'm cutting ties with you right now!" Merlin's hand drifted toward his tachi.

"I'm sorry, Miss Alice. Exorcismology is an independent discipline at our divine academy, so we cannot teach outsiders." Cecilia spread her hands helplessly.

"What a pity~" Alice pouted and looked at Merlin with ill intent.

Merlin secretly breathed a sigh of relief and grumbled, "Does the Holy Church have a brain problem? Why do they offer such a bizarre subject?"

"Because demons are evil beings. Every devout believer must master exorcism to be fully prepared for the holy war against the demon race in the future." Cecilia said passionately, clearly sounding like someone who had been brainwashed beyond repair.

Merlin furrowed his brow. Holy war?! Is the Holy Church planning a large-scale war against the demon race? What the hell, why must we be the poster children for evil? Is it because we demons are independent and refuse to interact too much with the outside world?

"There is no such thing as a holy war, Miss Cecilia. Have you ever seen a real demon?"

"...No." Cecilia shook her head. She had indeed never seen one—all the information came from priests' descriptions.

"Then why do you insist that demons are definitely evil?" Merlin asked curiously.

"Because the priests said demons are the most evil creatures in the world..." Cecilia answered blankly.

"To be honest, some humans are far more evil than demons." Merlin said calmly.

"...". Cecilia was at a loss for words. Heh, it was actually true.

"Miss Cecilia, please do not judge the morality of an entire race based on one-sided accounts, especially when you have never witnessed it with your own eyes. That is very impolite." Merlin said seriously.

"I-I'm terribly sorry, Lord Mer..." Cecilia had to bow her head. She realized she truly couldn't produce evidence that demons were the most evil beings, not to mention she hadn't even seen what a demon looked like.

Alice glanced at Merlin and thought—she too had once believed all demons were insane, maniacal creatures. Yet now she was cohabiting peacefully with the Great Demon Lord?! Looking back now, it was truly a little surreal.

If she hadn't seen Merlin, a demon, displaying so many upright words and deeds, Alice probably would have viewed the demon race through the same biased lens as Cecilia.

Alice felt that it was Merlin who had changed her perception of demons. Demons, like humans, could be good or evil.

Kael sensed the atmosphere growing oppressive, so he quickly spoke up, "U-um... Lord Merlin, please don't be angry. The young lady has always been rather naive."

"I'm not angry..." Merlin shook his head, thinking that as a demon himself, constantly being misunderstood was somewhat frustrating.

"Actually, the old master sent the young lady to study at the divine academy in London simply to broaden her horizons and build some connections." Kael said with a smile.

"Connections?" Merlin looked surprised.

"Yes, connections. The divine academy was funded by the royal family, and most of the students there are children of nobles. Even Her Highness Michelle, the daughter of Queen Elizabeth, studies at this academy. Friends you make here will either be powerful nobles or wealthy merchants." Kael explained humbly.

"I see. So it's a place for the second generation to gild themselves..." Merlin nodded. He had thought it was some proper institution. But then again, an academy that could come up with such worldview-shattering exorcism courses couldn't possibly be legitimate, could it?

"Er, Lord Merlin, don't be so blunt..." Kael wiped a cold sweat from his forehead. The young master really is straight-talking... An SF member here.

The group headed straight to the center of London.

There stood luxurious noble hotels. Without a title, or unless you were a noble's family member, you simply couldn't stay.

Thanks to Cecilia's connections this time, they were able to lodge at such a high-end establishment, making the trip well worth it.

After Merlin and Alice settled into the hotel, the two of them didn't hesitate and headed directly to the Southern United Kingdom's embassy in Britain with Sherry.

Sherry still wore her cloak. Looking up at the statue of her father, she felt overwhelming emotion. Even the elven guards at the entrance made her feel incredibly close—she had finally seen her own kind.

Alice glanced at Sherry beside her and smiled to herself. This child can finally go home now...

Merlin looked around, scratched his head, and muttered,

"This must be it."

"Should be right, right?"

(u--.)?

title: Chapter 5 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 5 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 7 · Chapter 5

Merlin looked in surprise at the two elf guards at the entrance, both possessing the signature pointed ears of elves.

As for their looks, they were unbelievably handsome!

If not for the armor on their bodies and swords in their hands, people might easily mistake them for welcoming attendants.

Merlin stared at the two elf brothers so intensely that they became nervous; even beads of sweat the size of beans could be seen trickling down their foreheads.

"Is this it? I've never been to London."

"Stop guessing randomly, it's definitely here." Alice responded irritably.

Merlin glanced at the statue of the Elf King at the center of the embassy but had no idea who it was.

He had only been in this other world for a maximum of 200-plus years, and something like the Elf King, an ancient monster from long ago, was truly unfamiliar to him.

Merlin cleared his throat once and said seriously to the guards,

"We've brought a lost elf with us. Could you go in and notify the Elf Clan's ambassador? See how this should be handled?"

"Let us see this elf first." The elf guard said earnestly; they needed to confirm the other party's identity.

Alice pulled Shirley forward and said softly, "Take off your hood, let them take a look."

Shirley nervously gripped the hem of her dress, hesitated for a moment, and then slowly removed her hood, revealing soft golden hair and pointed ears. Combined with her beautiful yet shy face, the two elf guards were instantly stunned.

"Oh? You're getting hard just from looking~" Merlin couldn't help but tease.

Shirley's face flushed red, and she quickly pulled the hood back over her head, too embarrassed to face anyone after Merlin's teasing.

"What are you talking nonsense about!? So annoying..." Alice huffed and raised her tiny pink fist to hammer Merlin.

They had originally thought the two guards were dumbfounded by Shirley's beauty, but that wasn't the case at all—

The two elf guards exchanged glances with each other, as if they both saw something unbelievable in each other's eyes!

"Your Highness!"

The two elf guards cried out in unison, immediately knelt on one knee, and pressed their hands to their chests, every gesture showing utmost respect.

"Huh!?"

Alice paused, completely caught off guard by this sudden change and having no idea what was going on.

How could these two tall and imposing elf warriors suddenly kneel before Shirley and cry out "Your Highness"?

Didn't that title only belong to the direct relatives of a king? No way...

Alice's eyes widened in utter shock as she stared at Shirley, thinking to herself that had she been living with the Elf Clan's princess all these days!?

Merlin kept a straight face and wasn't nearly as surprised. What's a princess? He was a Great Demon Lord!

"Shirley, are you... the Elf Princess?"

"Ruffian! How could a mere human dare to directly call Her Highness by name!?"

The two kneeling elf guards sprang to their feet in an instant, their hands gripping their sword hilts as if ready to fight Merlin to the death.

"Stop it!" Shirley summoned her courage and shouted loudly to stop the two impulsive elf guards.

"But Your Highness Shirley, we..." The elf guard hesitated, seeming somewhat troubled.

"Both of them are my friends, you're not allowed to be rude!" Shirley said in a very serious tone, her slender body trembling slightly, clearly uncomfortable with speaking in a commanding manner.

"...

The two elf guards respectfully sheathed their hostility and stepped back with deference, though they didn't move too far away.

If they learned that Shirley had been missing for half a year with no word, and now she suddenly appeared today, it was a matter of tremendous importance!

So the two guards had no intention of letting Shirley leave; they absolutely had to escort her back to the Elf King's side.

Shirley was the Elf King's most beloved youngest daughter, and when she went missing, the Elf King had even gone so far as to drain national resources to search for her.

Every human nation had been combed through by the Elf King, yet nothing was found, and now she had returned on her own! ?

This was undeniably good news for the entire elf clan.

"... Alice's astonishment had not faded, and she asked seriously, 'You really are the Elf Clan's princess?!'"

Shirley looked slightly flustered, unable to speak for a moment. She hadn't intended to hide it, but now that it had come out in the open, it was too awkward.

"Yes, I am the youngest daughter of the Elf King, the fifth in line to the throne."

...Alice still couldn't quite process it; the girl who had been clinging to her was suddenly a princess.

"No wonder she could casually produce a million gold coins. So she's the princess of the Elf Clan..." Merlin finally figured it out and asked curiously,

"Why didn't you just say so from the beginning?"

"I didn't mean to hide it, you just never asked me." Shirley said awkwardly.

Merlin's expression grew complicated, and he thought resentfully—

Darn it! Such a huge loss!

A million gold coins was too little!

If only he had known, he would have extorted her father, the Elf King...

Absolutely gouging the elf clan would have been wonderful!

Merlin and Alice were treated as distinguished guests and invited inside the embassy.

The two looked around curiously, finding it quite novel, because the elf clan's architectural culture was vastly different from humanity's—they held nature in high reverence.

It felt as though they had arrived in another world entirely, which was quite interesting.

In the reception hall, elf guards surrounded the area, forming a strict perimeter as if worried Shirley might be kidnapped by bad actors.

The maids were whispering among themselves in the background, completely at a loss over Shirley's sudden return.

Shirley felt much more relaxed here than outside. She had rarely experienced such a sense of coming home, since everyone around her was of her own kind, unlike the outside world full of humans and danger.

However, being watched by so many elves still made Shirley a bit nervous, and she sat on the sofa somewhat stiffly.

Moreover, Merlin and Alice on the opposite side weren't saying anything. It seemed that after learning she was a princess, their attitude toward her had changed.

This made Shirley very anxious. She didn't want her princess status to become a barrier between them, preventing them from getting along harmoniously as before.

Especially she didn't want to grow distant from Alice, the human friend she had worked so hard to make. She didn't want to lose her that way.

After some time passed, Merlin and Alice gradually accepted reality and adapted to Shirley's princess identity.

Merlin's mind was filled with regret over the financial loss, and he really wanted to make a massive demand, to ruthlessly fleece poor Shirley.

Alice, on the other hand, felt somewhat awkward, not sure what approach to use when interacting with Shirley, who was now a princess.

She was a princess now after all; it wouldn't be right to act like before, right? Shouldn't she show a bit more respect?

Alice felt a bit embarrassed inside. Although Shirley was over four hundred years old, she had been treating her like a younger sister.

Suddenly having to shift gears was truly a bit difficult...

Alice was lost in her thoughts when Merlin nudged her with his elbow, seeming to want to share something confidential.

Alice was already in a bad mood, so being suddenly bothered by Merlin naturally earned her no pleasant expression.

"What are you doing? Are you a monkey? Stop fidgeting."

"You're the monkey. I have something serious..." Merlin frowned, his eyes somewhat serious.

"What is it?" Alice asked quietly, assuming Merlin had discovered something major.

"Look at it this way. The Miss Shirley we rescued turns out to be the princess of the Elf Clan from the Southern United Kingdom..." Merlin lowered his voice, communicating in a tone only the two of them could hear.

"Isn't it a bit too little to only offer 1 million gold coins as报酬?"

"So I think..."

"We should go together and extort Shirley's dad, the Elf King."

title: Chapter 6 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 6 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 6

Alice widened her eyes in astonishment at Merlin, thinking, “This guy really dares to think of anything, doesn’t he? He even wants to extort the Elf King?”

“Don’t just stare,” Merlin poked Alice with his arm and said seriously, “Think about it—Shirley, that little princess, has a hundred thousand gold coins at her fingertips. The Elf King must be even richer. Why don’t we demand a reward from Shirley’s father? Set a small goal first and ask for a hundred million right off the bat~”

“Are you crazy? How can you treat Shirley like that?!” Alice said angrily, clearly disgusted with Merlin’s suggestion.

“When we were together we were friends, but now we have to sell—so we’ll have to sell her like a pig~” Merlin said with righteous confidence, putting on the face of a merchant.

“No! We can’t do that!” Alice put on a serious expression. “Helping Shirley get home was part of our duty, just a simple task. Don’t always tie everything to profit.”

“You wasteful old lady, you’re so boring…” Merlin sighed, leaned back on the sofa, and muttered, “How can I be stuck with a fool like you? I just can’t understand it.”

“...What are you saying?!” Alice snapped, “You truly are a demon—no sense of friendship at all, just pushing your own petty calculations!”

“I’m not a righteous guardian; anyone who doesn’t consider profit is a fool…” Merlin forced a laugh, glaring at Alice.

“You’re the fool, okay?!” Alice clenched her teeth, furious at Merlin.

Shirley watched the two of them from across the room, not knowing what they were arguing about, but it seemed they were about to start fighting again.

“A… Alice‑senpai…”

Hearing Shirley’s call, Alice stopped arguing with Merlin, turned around, and asked, “What is it, Princess Shirley?”

“Don’t… don’t call me that…” Shirley frowned, looking a little annoyed. “Just call me Shirley like before…”

Alice glanced at the many elf guards eyeing them and said awkwardly, “Is this not a bit… inappropriate?”

“It’s fine. Among friends we just use each other’s names. Does Alice… not feel confident enough to be a friend?” Shirley’s voice grew softer and softer, eventually sounding like a mosquito’s buzz.

“No… it’s not that,” Alice waved her hand, hesitating, “You’re a princess now, so I should be a little more respectful, right?”

“No need,” Shirley shook her head, her tone urgent. “If my status makes Miss Alice wary, you don’t have to treat me as a princess… I’m still the girl who likes to hug Miss Alice while we sleep…”

Alice hesitated, wondering if this was just a way for her to act like she always does.

“You two, when I’m asleep, what do you do in the room? Cuddling together…” Merlin said at an inappropriate moment, feeling a vague surge of life behind his head.

“G‑U‑N!” Alice glared at Merlin, “K‑R, put away your filthy fantasies. We’re just sleeping, that’s all.”

Merlin’s expression grew complicated, and he didn’t continue to provoke Alice.

“Is it really okay?” Alice asked, her mood a little uneasy.

“It’s fine. Miss Alice can just be the way she was before. I really like the way you speak like an older sister…” Shirley said, full of anticipation.

Merlin frowned, thinking that Shirley was over four hundred years old while Alice was under twenty; being called an older sister seemed like a huge loss.

“…You really like my ‘big‑sister’ tone?” Alice asked delightedly, looking as if she’d just won the lottery.

Seeing Alice’s reaction, Merlin’s face went blank, his mind racing. He thought, “I’m overthinking this. This guy is already having fun…”

The embassy’s long hallway.

Samuel changed into a purple floor‑length dress, showcasing her mature beauty.

She walked quickly toward the reception hall, eager to meet Shirley.

Sharpun and Sharan flanked her, hurrying to the hall alongside Samuel.

Just a moment ago, Samuel had been sunbathing on the rooftop, enjoying aged red wine and the sunshine.

Then the guards rushed in, panicked, reporting that the long‑missing Princess Shirley had returned on her own.

At first Samuel thought it was a joke, but the guards’ vivid description made her realize it was true.

The princess who had been missing for half a year was really back…

Samuel was overjoyed, feeling as if the goddess of luck herself was watching, granting whatever she wished.

Originally they lacked a royal elf’s soul to cast the forbidden spell. The elves wept to revive Ashudor.

They had just been about to send Sharpun and Sharan to search for Shirley, but Shirley herself stupidly showed up at the door!

Such a coincidence forced Samuel to believe that everything was guided by destiny.

In the unseen, an invisible force seemed to be helping the Dark Elf King’s resurrection, making everything fall into place.

If it weren’t for destiny’s guidance, Samuel would have a hard time explaining the source of this luck.

“Lord Samuel, the silly Princess Shirley has come herself. What should we do next?” Sharpun asked, puzzled.

“Do I need to ask? Now that the most important thing has arrived, the Great Elf Cry can be activated at any moment. We must put the plan to resurrect His Majesty Ashudor on the schedule as soon as possible,” Samuel said with a calm smile, continuing, “Once our king is revived, the tragic fate of the Dark Elf race can be rewritten, so look forward—our era is about to begin.”

“Finally… His Majesty Ashudor is really coming back? This is so exciting…” Sharan clasped her hands together, silently blessing the Dark Elf King’s resurrection.

“Exactly, it’s incredibly thrilling. His Majesty Ashudor will guide us,” Sharpun replied, his joy evident, as if the hard days were finally over.

“Don’t be careless; this is a matter of great importance. In the coming days we must check every detail of the magical array without a single oversight,” Samuel ordered. “Once everything is confirmed, we’ll release the ghouls, unleash the Elf Cry, and turn the entire human population of London into sacrificial offerings for Ashudor’s revival—our stepping stones to rise!”

“Understood!” Sharpun and Sharan answered in unison.

“In the future, London will no longer exist; it will become a human hell…” Samuel narrowed her eyes, a near‑manic grin spreading to the corners of her mouth.

Everything was already prepared.

The show was about to begin.

As for my dear little Princess Shirley?

Just get in my cage quickly…​

title: Chapter 7
content:
Chapter 7

Volume 7 · Chapter 7

Merlin was lost in thought, listening to Alice and Sherry chattering away.
It had indeed returned to normal, just like usual.
Merlin silently thought to himself, glancing around at the expressions of the elves, which kept changing.
Probably, they felt that Sherry, as a princess, had lowered her status by acting like a commoner, which made the elven royal family lose face.

"If I have the chance, I will definitely visit your country and see it for myself. It sounds interesting from what you've said," Alice said with a hint of longing, after hearing Sherry talk about many interesting things about the elves.

"Please let me know if you're coming, and I'll take care of you. I'm sorry for the trouble I've caused you for so long, and I feel indebted. Please give me a chance to repay you," Sherry said seriously, treating this as an important matter.

"Repayment and such..."

Before Alice could say "never mind," Merlin quickly interrupted.

"Repayment is necessary, like the promise we made at the beginning. Isn't that right?"
Merlin spoke with a deep meaning, his eyes frequently hinting at something, which even a fool could understand.

"Merlin, you atmosphere-killer, what are you talking about?" Alice frowned, clearly disagreeing with Merlin's realistic approach.

"This is what we deserve. Don't be polite. You're a justice defender, like doing volunteer work, but I'm not, thank you," Merlin responded without hesitation, thinking that Alice's personality was simply foolish and couldn't be expected to contribute.

"Aren't we and Sherry friends?" Alice hesitated, not daring to say something too unpleasant.

"Friends are friends, but interests need to be calculated clearly. I'm a demon, and I absolutely won't do business at a loss..." Merlin raised an eyebrow at Alice.

Alice was suddenly speechless, not knowing what to say, thinking, "Oh, Merlin is a demon, and it's not strange for him to do uncomfortable things."

Sherry was also a clever person, seemingly understanding the situation, and said seriously,
"I will keep my promise and give you the agreed-upon reward."

"No, we..." Alice suddenly felt embarrassed.

"Don't say 'no,' Alice. This is what you deserve. I, as a princess of the elven royal family, have my dignity, and I won't owe people favors," Sherry said seriously, seemingly wanting Alice to accept her kindness.

"... " Alice looked hesitant, unsure of what to do.

"Moreover, Alice and Merlin are adventurers, always traveling outside, and it seems quite difficult. I can do a little to help, which is nothing," Sherry said seriously, looking determined.

"That's right, we're quite difficult... If you could give us a few... uh!"
Merlin hadn't finished speaking when Alice covered his mouth, not letting him talk nonsense.

"You have some conscience, don't take advantage of friends, okay? You really don't have any face... I don't want it, you want it..." Alice glared at Merlin, her voice low and warning.

Merlin had a cold sweat on his forehead, thinking that Alice was really naive...

"We ask for money based on our abilities, what's wrong with that?"

"It's not okay, 100,000 gold coins is already a lot, don't be greedy," Alice said seriously in a low voice, not wanting Merlin's claws to extend to Sherry.

Merlin rolled his eyes, thinking that Alice was a fool, and the gap between millions of gold coins in debt and 100,000 gold coins in reward was huge.

It seemed that the two of them getting 100,000 gold coins as a reward was indeed not much.

Sherry smiled awkwardly beside them, thinking that Merlin and Alice showed their affection, completely without regard for time and place...

Just as the three of them were chatting, the door to the reception hall slowly opened, and Samuel walked in, looking urgent.

"Sherry, Your Highness..."
Samuel called out softly, approaching Sherry.

Her face lit up with joy, looking at Sherry, and indeed, she was the little daughter of the elven king. Although she had lost some of her innocence after more than half a year's wandering, she could still be recognized at a glance.

Samuel showed an excited expression on her surface, almost like she was about to cry, but in reality, she was extremely happy.

She almost wanted to grab Sherry now and sacrifice her soul to the great Ashurad.

"Samuel, Aunt..."
Sherry looked at Samuel with joy, her eyes full of happiness.

It seemed that Sherry and Samuel knew each other and were familiar.

Sherry didn't expect that the elven ambassador to London was Samuel, which was too coincidental.

Sherry was familiar with Samuel because she was her mother's confidante and often appeared by her mother's side. She had always called her "Aunt".

"Sherry, Your Highness..." Samuel grabbed Sherry's hand, saying with a sad expression,
"Where did you go? Why didn't you send any news? You know how worried the king was about you?"

"What's wrong with my father?" Sherry asked, concerned, when Samuel mentioned her father.

"After you disappeared, the king searched for you everywhere. He was talking about you just the other day," Samuel said, taking advantage of Sherry's weak personality. As long as she said something a little scary, she would listen to her.

"Yes... yes... " Sherry looked a bit nervous, saying self-reproachfully,
"It's all my fault for being too playful and letting my father worry about me. I'm useless and only cause trouble for others..."

"Sherry, Your Highness, don't blame yourself. You're safe now, aren't you? This is a cause for celebration. If the king knew you were back, I'm sure his biggest worry would be gone," Samuel said seriously, showing a very relieved expression.

"It seems I need to go back as soon as possible..." Sherry's thoughts of returning home grew stronger.

"Don't rush, Your Highness. Can you tell me about what happened during your half-year absence?" Samuel asked patiently.

"That would take a long time..."

Sherry and Samuel sat down together, starting a brief narrative.

Basically, it was a summary of what happened: she was kidnapped by human traffickers and then saved by Merlin and Alice.

"Is that so? Sherry, Your Highness, suffered a lot these half years. We didn't find you even though you're in Great Britain. This is our dereliction of duty..." Samuel wiped away fake tears, putting on a show for those around her.

"It's okay, Samuel, Aunt. I'm back now," Sherry comforted Samuel.

"Yes, as long as you're back safe, it's good. If anything happened to Sherry, Your Highness, we could only apologize with our lives..."

Sherry smiled awkwardly, feeling that the situation was being exaggerated.

Samuel glanced at Alice and Merlin, having noticed them from the beginning, and asked casually,
"Sherry, Your Highness, who are these two?"

"They're the ones who saved me, Alice and Merlin," Sherry introduced happily.

"Good..." Merlin responded carelessly.

"Hello, Samuel. We're adventurers from Wrexham," Alice was slightly more enthusiastic, unlike Merlin's lazy demeanor.

"Adventurers..." Samuel responded in a low voice, squinting to examine Merlin and Alice.

A high-ranking magic swordsman?

How weak! Not worth mentioning.

The other one, a black iron villager without magical energy?

Not even weak, just a complete waste!

Why could two third-rate characters save Sherry, the stupid princess?

title: Chapter 8
content:
Chapter 8

Volume 7 · Chapter 8

Samuel looked at Merlin and Alice, feeling that things were a bit strange.

Shelly had just described the matter in a thrilling manner, as if the human traffickers were very powerful.

But Shelly hadn't given a detailed account of the situation, not mentioning the remnants of the former kingdom in the slightest.

Nor had she spoken of Merlin's outstanding performance; she had merely given a simple rundown of events.

This left Samuel with limited information, and he outright dismissed Alice and Merlin from his consideration.

Samuel unilaterally assumed that Merlin and Alice had simply taken shortcuts to rescue Shelly from the human traffickers.

Otherwise, how could one high-rank adventurer plus one dispensable villager possibly defeat such powerful human traffickers?

"Hmm?" Merlin frowned slightly, catching the fleeting contempt in Samuel's eyes.

However, Samuel quickly covered it up, masking his expression with apparent gratitude as he rose and bowed to Merlin and Alice.

"Thank you for rescuing Princess Shelly. You've been a tremendous help, and this kindness will be remembered by our entire elven race."

"Oh, please, you're far too kind. We merely did what anyone would do," Alice replied politely.

"No, no. Your actions truly deserve our eternal gratitude," Samuel said earnestly on the surface, planning to brush off Merlin and Alice with empty words.

"Exactly, Miss Alice. If not for you two, I might never have returned to my homeland. Whatever reward you desire, please don't hesitate to ask," Shelly said dutifully, truly wanting to properly thank Merlin and Alice.

"—"

Merlin had only spoken one character when he felt Alice's gaze pinning him, making him extremely uncomfortable, so he hurriedly changed his words.

"Umm… ten thousand gold coins."

"…What, that?" A bead of cold sweat trickled down Shelly's forehead as she said awkwardly, "Once I return to my country, I'll give it to you right away."

"I see. Don't forget, or Alice the cheapskate here will run off to the Southern United Kingdom to demand it herself," Merlin couldn't resist throwing a dig at Alice.

"Who's a cheapskate!? Would I be that persistent!? Don't project your own petty nature onto me!?" Alice was nearly exploding with rage.

"Hehe~" Merlin grinned foolishly, secretly thrilled to see Alice so flustered.

Samuel felt nothing but utter disdain toward Merlin and Alice, thinking to himself: *As expected, they're just mercenaries after money, completely devoid of any higher purpose.*

However, Samuel didn't let it show, and on the surface remained cordial.

"Haven't the two of you eaten yet? Would you like to join us for a meal?"

Samuel's words were merely polite niceties; he had no intention of keeping Merlin and Alice around and was eager for them to leave.

"Abo—"

"Sure! Let's eat together. I'd love to try the elven cuisine."

Alice's polite refusal was never even completed before Merlin powerfully interrupted her.

Merlin still had some interest in the elven race, especially the pureblood elves.

Because pureblood elves had always been quite mysterious, dwelling deep in the forests, which stirred great curiosity in others.

Alice gazed at Merlin with a complicated expression, not knowing what to say anymore.

Samuel frowned slightly,厌恶 (disgusted) in his heart:

*A mere black iron adventurer…*

*How shameless can one be?*

Inside the embassy's dining hall.

A wide circular table sat in the center, surrounded by luxurious décor that exuded an exotic atmosphere.

The staple food of pureblood elves was generally vegetables, with almost nothing else.

But only the elves could bring out the true essence of vegetables.

Merlin found the vegetable dishes acceptable, if not as good as his own cooking—they were certainly better than what Alice could make.

Alice, on the other hand, was eating happily, seeming to have forgotten her earlier intention to politely decline.

Shelly had changed into a pale blue dress, adorned with expensive jewelry, and even wore a small silver-white diamond-studded tiara atop her head.

This outfit instantly made Shelly appear far more noble and regal, perfectly fitting her identity as a princess, nothing like the timid girl next door she usually seemed to be.

Samuel secretly glanced at Merlin, noticing his expression showed no hint of surprise, and couldn't help but feel puzzled.

The cuisine served within the embassy was prepared by highly skilled chefs—ordinary people could hardly ever eat such dishes, let alone these wandering adventurers.

So Samuel pondered for a moment and couldn't resist asking:

"Mr. Merlin, does the elven cuisine not suit your taste?"

"It's not that it doesn't suit me. It's just so-so, good enough to fill one's stomach," Merlin said bluntly.

Even Alice beside him didn't refute it, secretly agreeing that Merlin's salad tasted far better and left one craving more.

……

Samuel's breathing hitched, and the veins on his forehead throbbed relentlessly.

His lungs nearly burst with rage, his thoughts churning: *They're just commoners.*

*Commoners who have never tasted such food in their lives,* he fumed internally, *yet they dare to criticize elite elven cuisine. What right do they have? Shouldn't they look at themselves in the mirror first!*

Shelly, being more understanding, seemed to notice that Samuel was somewhat angry. She spoke earnestly, "Auntie Samuel, please don't be upset. Mr. Merlin's words aren't without merit—his cooking skills are truly excellent. That salad of his is really delicious…"

Samuel opened his mouth to reply but stopped, glancing at Shelly's serious expression.

*Salad? What is that? I've lived nearly a thousand years and have never even heard of it!*

*It's probably some garbage peasant dish, something utterly unworthy of being served at a proper table!*

*Princess Shelly has truly fallen, loving such trash food—what a disgrace to the royal family!*

*If that's the case, then using Shelly as the sacrifice to awaken the sorrow of the elves is not unjustifiable at all!*

Samuel schemed in his heart, but his tone softened as he spoke.

"If Mr. Merlin is dissatisfied, shall we prepare some non-elven dishes instead?"

"There's no need for such trouble. This cuisine is quite fine," Alice quickly said diplomatically.

"Yeah, we'll just make do," Merlin nodded, seemingly unaware that his words carried sharp edges.

Alice looked at Merlin with an expression of wanting to say something but holding back.

Samuel's face darkened considerably. She clenched her fists, the veins on her forehead throbbing visibly.

*How dare he say "make do"? Is he looking down on our great elven race!?*

*He's just a lowly human, yet he dares to be so rude!?*

Samuel frowned, finding Merlin to be a narcissistic fool who inspired nothing but disgust. Unable to help herself, she plotted something vicious in her heart:

*Forget it. Anyway, those two adventurers won't live much longer.*

*I never intended to let that pair of dogs go. They now know Shelly's true identity.*

*They might spread the word and interfere with His Majesty Asmodeus's resurrection plan.*

*Then the most foolproof method would be…*

*To make those two shut their mouths forever.*

title: Chapter 9 — Bonus Update: Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 9 — Bonus Update: Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 9

Hmph, this might be your last meal, so make sure to eat your fill...

Samuel thought to herself with malice, deciding to take action tonight to eliminate Merlin and Alice. She would then throw Sherry into the dungeon and prepare to activate the large magic circle of the Elf's Lament.

Even the Princess of the Elf tribe wouldn't be able to do anything about it. London was far from the Southern United Kingdom, and even the Elf King wouldn't be able to help.

Sherry was just a useless little princess; her death wouldn't be worth lamenting. As long as Archduke Asmodeus was revived, the era of the dark elves would arrive.

Samuel suppressed her anger and ate patiently, feeling that everything was under her control.

Merlin thought about the Elf King, a figure who spanned eras, and had numerous records in the demon tribe's books.

This old monster who had lived for such a long time could only be compared to the Sloth Lord, who was from the same era as the first Lucifer.

The Elf King's greatest achievement was promoting the great migration of different tribes and establishing the Southern United Kingdom.

Merlin was very interested in the Elf King and wondered if his strength was better than that of the legendary Hero of the Spear.

"Samuel..."

Samuel suddenly spat out the food in her mouth. Although she knew she was not young, being called "old mom" by Merlin made her feel uncomfortable.

Others usually called her "Miss Samuel," but only Merlin was so straightforward and called her "old mom" directly, making her feel bad.

Samuel bit her lip and glared at Merlin, as if she had been greatly wronged and wanted to tear Merlin's mouth apart.

Sherry was a bit timid and didn't dare to speak when she saw Samuel get angry. It seemed that being a princess for so many years had made her weak.

Alice quickly pulled Merlin's sleeve and whispered, "Don't say such obvious truths; can't you be more tactful?"

Merlin glanced at Alice and said calmly, "Why can't women face their actual age?"

Alice rolled her eyes and said resentfully, "I'm not an old woman; how would I know about this?"

Although their conversation was in a low voice, unfortunately, the Elf tribe's ears were exceptionally good.

Samuel's ears moved slightly, and she immediately heard what Merlin and Alice were saying.

Not hearing it was better; hearing the content made her even angrier.

Samuel's eyes twitched, and she was so angry that her liver trembled. She thought that this couple was ganging up on her.

Despite being angry, Samuel still chose to prioritize the overall situation and put on a fake smile.

"Merlin, is there anything special you want to ask?"

"It's not a troublesome question; I just want to ask..." Merlin paused and said seriously, "Is the Elf King very powerful?"

Before Samuel could answer, Sherry couldn't help but speak up, as it was about her father's issue and she was the most qualified to answer.

"My father is, of course, very powerful; he's considered the strongest of the nine different tribe kings and has controlled the Elf tribe for several eras. He's also the indispensable force that stabilizes the many different tribes in the Southern United Kingdom and can suppress the Flame Saint Dragon among the six Saint Dragons!"

Samuel thought to herself, "The Elf King is the strongest? Pffft! Archduke Asmodeus is the most powerful Elf leader; in terms of strength, the Elf King is nothing in front of him, with a clear gap in strength!"

"The six Saint Dragons?" Alice was surprised and thought about the inheritance crystal of the Frost Saint Dragon she had just swallowed.

"That's right; the Flame Saint Dragon represents the Dragon King in the Southern United Kingdom, but it has a bad relationship with my father and had a conflict a long time ago. Although the Flame Saint Dragon's strength is very strong, it was still suppressed by my father; I saw it with my own eyes!" Sherry said seriously.

Sherry seemed to be trying to convince Merlin that her father, the Elf King, was not an ordinary person, but she knew that Merlin was still stronger.

Because Merlin could annihilate the hell army, which even her father couldn't do, there was still a gap.

"Oh?" Merlin narrowed his eyes and said curiously, "It sounds very powerful."

"Isn't it? My father is the spiritual leader of our Elf tribe; without his leadership, our Elf tribe wouldn't be so prosperous." Sherry clasped her hands together and seemed to admire her father like an idol.

Samuel thought to herself, "Naive princess, your father, the Elf King, is a despicable person who killed his own brother by ambush and doesn't deserve to be called a leader. He lowered the dignity and nobility that the Elf should have and mixed with a group of ugly different tribes. Is this considered leading the Elf tribe to prosperity? I won't acknowledge it! Only Archduke Asmodeus can save the decadent Elf tribe."

"It sounds like Sherry's father is a wise ruler..." Alice muttered.

"Merlin frowned and continued, "A wise and brave ruler, I think that's what they say about your father, right?"

"That's right; my father is a wise and brave ruler; I admire him so much..." Sherry's eyes sparkled, and she looked forward to seeing her father soon.

Merlin didn't speak and looked at Sherry with a strange expression, thinking that she might be controlled by her father.

Merlin came from an era where sibling relationships were unreliable and had been subtly influenced to think that even parent-child relationships were unreliable.

"Excuse me, but isn't the strongest in the Elf tribe not the Elf King?" Samuel couldn't sit still and interrupted.

"Eh?" Sherry was taken aback and asked in shock, "Not my father? Who could it be?"

"Of course, it's your uncle, the dark Elf King, Archduke Asmodeus..." Samuel said with a smile.

"Ah!?" Sherry was shocked and quickly said, "Samuel, aunt, don't mention Archduke Asmodeus; this name is a taboo for us."

Samuel couldn't help but laugh in her heart, thinking that it was just a taboo to cover up the Elf King's fact of killing his brother.

"No problem, Your Highness; it's Merlin's question, and we should answer it honestly, shouldn't we?"

Sherry frowned and fell into hesitation.

"Besides, this is London, not the Southern United Kingdom; so-called taboos don't exist here." Samuel said softly to Sherry with a gentle expression.

"Taboo..." Merlin's brow furrowed, and he scratched his head, wondering,

"What is this dark Elf...Archduke Asmodeus like?"

title: Chapter 10
content:
Chapter 10

Volume 7 · Chapter 10

Alice blinked blankly, completely not understanding what Samuel and Shirley were talking about.

All she knew was that Shirley's uncle was the Dark Elf King, and apparently he was even stronger than the Elf King.

But the Elf King could suppress the Sacred Dragon of Blazing Flame, so he was obviously already very powerful.

However, from what Shirley had said, the Dark Elf King was even more powerful. What did that mean?

Alice had always felt that beings at the level of the Six Great Sacred Dragons could only be dealt with by someone like Merlin, that pervert.

But you can't really blame Alice for having a confused mindset; being around Merlin had always kept her perception of power in a constant state of being refreshed.

It seemed that being weak had long limited Alice's imagination...

Shirley hesitated when she heard Merlin ask about the Dark Elf King so bluntly.

The Dark Elf King had once ignited a rebellion that threatened the existence of the elf race, making him the greatest sinner in the entire history of the elves. No elf would willingly speak of him.

Her own father had personally designated her uncle as a taboo. Anyone who dared to discuss her uncle Aethelwood would be regarded as a heretic and arrested for questioning on the spot.

But Mr. Merlin was her savior. She truly should answer honestly, and besides, they were in London now—there was no need to...

Shirley felt Samuel's words made a lot of sense, so she patiently and seriously began to speak.

"The Dark Elf King is my uncle. Before the rebellion within the elven race broke out, he had always been the leader of the dark elves, hailed as the most outstanding king, his talent far surpassing my father's. Everyone believed he would lead the elven race back to the prosperity of the Elf Era."

"Although my uncle was extraordinarily gifted, he fell into a bizarre fixation. While everyone could see the unstoppable rise of the human era, he still insisted on the belief in elf supremacy, refused my father's proposal to establish a unified kingdom, and led the dark elves into rebellion."

"Though the rebellion was fierce, it was ultimately crushed in its infancy by my father, who successfully established the Southern United Kingdom we have today. However, because of this rebellion, the relationship between our white elves and black elves has become strained, and the entire elven race is now only holding together superficially, showing trends of being divided in two."

"Yes..." Merlin nodded, asking in confusion, "Didn't you say the Dark Elf King's strength is greater? Then why was he easily suppressed by the Elf King? That doesn't seem right..."

"Because... he used some rather... awkward methods..." Shirley hesitated, somewhat too shy to speak.

"???" Merlin's mind was full of question marks; he didn't understand what "awkward methods" meant.

Seeing Shirley too embarrassed to say it, Samuel offered to explain instead. "The Elf King assassinated his own younger brother, Aethelwood, through a sneak attack. Yes, from an outsider's perspective, this was a thoroughly despicable and shameless act, completely stripping away the noble dignity that the elven race should possess..."

Shirley lowered her head with an ambiguous expression, agreeing with Samuel's words. It was indeed shamelessly shameless, but even so, that was still her father.

"No way... The legendary Elf King actually killed his own younger brother through a sneak attack..." Alice's expression showed utter shock.

"Oh ho~" Merlin stroked his chin and said meaningfully, "What a surprising dark history..."

As one of the oldest beings in the world, the Elf King was recorded in many ancient texts.

Both demonic records and human history bore witness to his presence.

Descriptions, without exception, portrayed him as a magnanimous, righteous figure who guided the transformation and direction of the entire world.

Yet this guy, who seemed like some great prophet, actually used sneak attacks and even committed fratricide! ?

This was truly eye-opening and hard to reconcile with the lofty, righteous image of the Elf King found in the records.

"My father... was only doing what was best for the entire elven race. He wasn't... evil..." Shirley couldn't help but mutter quietly, defending her father.

"Is this Aethelwood really that powerful? Forcing the Elf King to resort to sneak attacks..." Merlin asked curiously.
