title: Chapter 18 — Moon Ticket Bonus Update (Part 2, by 2 PM)
content:
Chapter 18 — Moon Ticket Bonus Update (Part 2, by 2 PM)

Volume 7 · Chapter 18

Merlin had unilaterally concluded that the Thorns Knight was weak; any of the demon race's lords could crush these Thorns Knights single-handedly.

But put them in front of others, and it was a completely different matter entirely—for example, Alice at this very moment, who simply couldn't compete with a Thorns Knight.

The London citizens nearby saw the pink-haired masked man and realized he was the Seventh Knight of the Thorns, and couldn't help but show astonished expressions, murmuring among themselves--

"It really is Lord Morrison!? I never expected to see him here!"

"Aren't the Thorns Knights usually stationed to guard the palace? Who would have thought they'd set up a fighting ring at the marketplace?"

"So does that mean the Seventh Thorns Knight just lost to some obscure Black Iron adventurer!?"

Many people below were discussing, not only surprised by the Thorns Knight's appearance, but thoroughly enjoying the arm-wrestling match from earlier.

A tiny Black Iron adventurer defeating a Thorns Knight in raw strength—this was a massive piece of news, nearly unbelievable.

If so many people hadn't witnessed it with their own eyes, no one would have believed such an absurd thing.

Morrison's expression was embarrassed; black veins crept across his forehead as he thought, This is over. Soon, all of London will know I lost to a Black Iron adventurer. I feel like I've somewhat disgraced the Thorns Knights... Please don't let Her Majesty invite me for tea...

"Alright, aren't you going to arrest me and throw me in jail? I won't resist. Come ahead and grab me."

"...I-I-I... How could I possibly arrest Lord Morrison?" Franklin was extremely nervous, stumbling over his words. "I was just joking earlier. Please don't take it to heart."

"You're saying you were joking now?" Morrison flicked his pink hair and tilted the corner of his mouth. "Your attitude just now seemed very domineering. It hardly looked like a joke. Don't think because I'm a Thorns Knight that I'll get special treatment. If I've disrupted the capital's order, you can arrest me without any hesitation."

Even with Morrison saying this, Franklin still dared not arrest him. After all, the Thorns Knights were his superiors. How would he dare to offend those above him?

To arrest a Thorns Knight required the Queen's personal approval; otherwise, no one in the entire kingdom could threaten the Thorns Knights.

"I don't dare, I don't dare..." Franklin waved his hands frantically, an apologetic look on his face. "I'm terribly sorry, Lord Morrison. You were wearing a mask just now, and I didn't recognize you. My words were very offensive. Please don't mind."

"Franklin, I'm not blaming you. Rather, I'm questioning your professional attitude. Is this how you treat civilians normally?" Morrison narrowed his eyes and interrogated.

Franklin broke into a cold sweat. The person before him was a Thorns Knight. Though he himself was the Knight Commander, he certainly wouldn't dare to offend a Thorns Knight.

"Our Crown Orchid Knight Order is called the Queen's sharp sword, but also the shield that protects the people. This is the core spirit of our knightly order." Morrison paused, then continued. "You are a knight. Don't you have a humble heart?"

Franklin hesitated, wanting to say something but staying silent. He quickly bowed his head. "Regarding what happened earlier, I deeply apologize. I should go reflect properly."

"This arrogant and domineering attitude will cause the民众 to detest our knightly order. As the Knight Commander, you represent not yourself, but the image of the entire order." Morrison sighed, muttering to himself. "No wonder our influence is growing weaker and weaker. Everyone is chasing after some Elgin the Great Sword Master. It seems the problem lies within our own ranks..."

Franklin gritted his teeth, hesitantly speaking. "Elgin the Great Sword Master isn't worth a second thought. He's just a fugitive..."

"Enough, Franklin. You have no sense of crisis at all. If Elgin the Great Sword Master's influence continues to expand, even Her Majesty won't be able to handle him. A warrant is merely a dead letter." Morrison frowned tightly.

Alice leaned close to Merlin and whispered, "Hey, hey. You're kind of being excessive. Everyone's misunderstanding you as Elgin the Great Sword Master, you know."

Merlin rolled his eyes. *Misunderstanding my ass. I am him,* he thought. *But have I become the British Queen's thorn now? That's actually kind of amusing...*

Franklin's expression was conflicted. His lips stayed tightly shut. He felt that unless Elgin the Great Sword Master was eliminated, he would surely become a hidden danger to the Queen's rule.

In fact, Franklin wasn't a bad person. It was just his extreme loyalty that made his words and actions extreme as well.

"At the moment, I don't wish to blame you. What you stirred up recently nearly dragged the Crown Orchid Knight Order's face through the mud. I hope you strictly govern yourself, put away that disgusting attitude of yours, and don't forget the spirit of knighthood." Morrison spoke in a severe tone. On the surface, he appeared calm, but this was already reprimanding him harshly.

"Lord Morrison, I was also just enforcing the law impartially. These two destroyed the capital. By all rights, they should be imprisoned." Franklin pointed at Merlin and Alice.

"It has nothing to do with them. The fact that this place was turned into a mess is my responsibility. I will take full charge of this matter." Morrison said in an irrefutable tone.

Franklin hesitated slightly. Obviously, this wasn't quite proper procedure. If Morrison, the Thorns Knight, took responsibility, there would be no punishment at all. Major incidents would simply become minor, and minor incidents would simply vanish.

"What? Do you have objections?" Morrison asked tentatively.

"No, no! Whatever Lord Morrison says, we'll do it!" Franklin shook his head frantically, wisely choosing to obey.

Morrison turned around and smiled. "Lord Merlin, Miss Alice, you may leave now."

"Huh?" Merlin blinked, saying in astonishment, "Is that it? We're done?"

"I arranged this fighting ring, so naturally it's my responsibility that it ended up like this." A faint smile played on Morrison's face.

Alice felt delighted in her heart. She hadn't expected the problem to be resolved so easily. It was truly fortunate that no trouble had been caused.

Alice quickly pulled Merlin and they slipped away from the scene as fast as possible.

Watching Merlin's retreating back, Morrison hesitated for a moment and called out, "Lord Merlin!"

"Hmm?" Merlin looked back, puzzled.

"If next time we have the opportunity, I'd like to compete with you again. Next time, let's wrestle?" Morrison revealed his gleaming teeth.

Merlin's face darkened, falling into an awkward silence...

Back on the street to the hotel.

Alice and Merlin walked side by side.

Merlin weighed the money pouch in his hand and said meaningfully, "Making money is actually quite easy. I really hope I encounter big shots like the Seventh Knight often."

"What are you talking about? You almost caused major trouble just now." Alice furrowed her delicate brows.

"What major trouble? Worst case, I'll just chop down the entire capital. I want to leave; not that anyone could possibly stop me." Merlin said casually.

"Don't act recklessly. If you do this, you won't be able to live in human territories..." Alice said seriously, very worried about Merlin's reckless behavior.

The two chatted as they walked, completely unaware that a light purple-haired woman wearing civilian clothes was walking toward them.

She was the First Knight of the Thorns, Maisfield—the Queen's personal knight.

Today, Maisfield wasn't wearing magnificent armor but instead wore a home-style long dress, her hair tied up high into a single ponytail.

Although she still had a sword at her waist, it seemed to lack much of its usual heroic aura. She had changed considerably and wasn't as eye-catching as usual.

Alice had no idea at all that Maisfield had passed by Merlin, thinking she was just some random passerby.

But Merlin was relatively alert. Sensing a trace of powerful aura, he suddenly stopped and turned to look behind him, discovering that Maisfield had already disappeared. Her movements were exceptionally swift.

"Merlin, what's wrong? Did you see someone?" Alice looked behind them, asking curiously.

"Nothing. Let's head back..." Merlin shook his head, turning back around, thinking—

That was the First Knight of the Thorns?

She really does seem like an interesting person.

title: Chapter 19 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 19 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 7 · Chapter 19

After Merlin and Alice left, the entire incident was brought under control. The London citizens who had gathered to watch, fearing trouble, dispersed. "Excuse me, Lord Morrison, do you have any further instructions?" Franklin asked fawningly. "No, take your people and leave. I want some alone time," Morrison replied, waving his hand. "Yes," Franklin signaled to his subordinates and retreated.

Over a hundred knights moved swiftly, like a receding tide, disappearing from Morrison's sight as if they had never been there. Morrison walked back to where he had been arm-wrestling, surveying the devastated scene and couldn't help but wear a wry smile. "I didn't expect to lose to a black iron adventurer. If the other Thorn Knights find out, I'll be ruined," Morrison thought to himself, still somewhat hard to accept.

He had rarely encountered a worthy opponent in Great Britain, but today he was overpowered by a lowly black iron adventurer. Recalling Merlin's carefree demeanor, Morrison still felt a bit unsettled. That man seemed to have held back until the end, never using his full strength. The contemptuous smile on his face had remained unchanged throughout, Morrison realized he was being underestimated.

If he had known the adventurer's true strength, he would have activated his "Rakshasa" state to counter him, possibly turning the tables. Morrison felt a slight regret for not using his strongest form to fight the man. He genuinely wanted to spar with Merlin again; losing to a black iron adventurer so easily was unpalatable.

However, Morrison acknowledged Merlin's strength; if he had engaged with his full power, he believed he could have gone toe-to-toe with Merlin. He hadn't used his full strength either, nearly winning. With the "Rakshasa" state boost, Morrison was confident he could defeat Merlin. "Rakshasa" was a potential-explosion state, an essential skill for Morrison to rest and recover, which could instantly enhance his abilities, transforming him into a humanoid monster.

The "Rakshasa" state had three levels, each increasing his power exponentially, causing noticeable physical changes, and eventually transforming him into a demon-like creature. Morrison had not fully mastered it, only able to use the second level of "Rakshasa." The third level granted immense power but also left him unable to control himself, clouding his mind and causing severe mental damage, making it a double-edged sword.

Morrison let out a sigh, having rarely encountered an opponent like Merlin, and now it was over. As the seventh Thorn Knight, when not on a mission, he was usually stationed in the palace, waiting for orders. Coming out to socialize was his personal interest, hoping to meet interesting people and spar with them to alleviate boredom.

Now that his identity as a Thorn Knight was exposed, he couldn't continue this game, and Morrison felt a bit down. "Morrison," a soft, melodious voice called out behind him, familiar and pleasant. Morrison turned around, eyes widening in surprise, "Melsfield, what are you doing here? Today isn't your day off, is it?"

"It was too noisy here for me to ignore. I thought some troublemakers might be causing chaos in the capital, so I came to take a look," Melsfield replied, frowning at the devastation. "Ha, I'm sorry to disturb your day off," Morrison chuckled nervously, a cold sweat beading on his forehead.

"You have the nerve to joke?" Melsfield's expression turned serious, scolding him, "You're on palace duty today; what are you doing here? Slackers like you aren't a good example." "It was just so boring in the palace; I couldn't help myself, I wanted to find some fun," Morrison said apologetically, knowing his actions weren't right.

"A random family, indeed," Melsfield sighed, asking resignedly, "Did you cause all this? Did you encounter an enemy in the capital?" "No, no, nothing like that," Morrison shook his head, "I was just arm-wrestling, and I got a bit carried away."

"Arm-wrestling?" Melsfield raised an eyebrow, skeptical; this didn't look like arm-wrestling but a full-blown fight. Although she had arm-wrestled with Morrison, the aftermath wasn't this severe. "The opponent was quite impressive; it was a valuable experience. His strength surprised me greatly," Morrison said, reminiscing.

"Oh?" Melsfield's interest was piqued; she asked lightly, "I presume the opponent was quite strong for you to praise him like that?" "Yes, indeed," Morrison nodded in agreement. "That's normal; as the center of Great Britain, the capital often has all sorts of people, and encountering strong individuals isn't unusual," Melsfield paused and continued, "However, with your strength, in a pure test of power, you shouldn't lose, right?"

"I always thought I wouldn't lose to anyone in arm-wrestling except you, but I'm sorry to say I lost, and I lost badly," Morrison replied honestly, his expression melancholic. It was only a matter of time before the whole of London found out he had been defeated by a black iron adventurer; he might as well admit it now.

"Really?!" Melsfield's eyes widened in surprise. She knew Morrison's strength and couldn't believe he would be easily defeated. It was hard to accept that someone could surpass a Thorn Knight, a nearly top-tier combatant in Great Britain.

"Really, his power was overwhelming, especially in the final moment," Morrison recalled. Melsfield's brow furrowed, trying to process the shock, and asked, "Who was your opponent?" Morrison hesitated, his face reddening, "A...a black iron adventurer from Reckham, I've never heard of him before."

"A black iron adventurer?!" Melsfield was even more astonished; it was implausible for a black iron adventurer to defeat a Thorn Knight. "Morrison, you're not joking, are you?" "No, his strength was genuinely powerful; at least, I felt that way. If I hadn't activated 'Rakshasa,' I might not have been a match for him," Morrison said seriously.

Melsfield, seeing Morrison wasn't joking, asked curiously, "Why would someone with such strength be confined to the lowest rank of adventurer?" "He seemed to be someone who didn't care about fame...," Morrison trailed off, still visibly unsettled.

"Adventurers with weird talents are endless; when did such a person...," Melsfield's brow furrowed, tentatively asking, "Morrison, what do you think about this guy? Will he pose a threat to the kingdom?" Morrison thought for a moment before responding, "I think he's a good guy because...he can arm-wrestle and win against me; people like that can't be bad!"

Melsfield's expression turned complicated; she was tired of Morrison's simplistic logic and thought to herself, "What kind of person is this Reckham adventurer? With strength comparable to a Thorn Knight, he surely isn't an unknown figure. It seems I arrived late; if possible, I'd like to meet this mysterious man..."

title: Chapter 20
content:
Chapter 20

Volume 7 · Chapter 20

Elven ambassador.

After Merlin and Alice left, Shirley originally intended to rest, then set out tomorrow.

But Samuel seemed to have something, bringing Shirley toward the depths of the unknown embassy.

Shirley followed Samuel obediently, though she did not know where he was taking her, but she was not particularly afraid.

After all, Samuel was an elf, and Shirley was very at ease with fellow elves, unlike humans, who could only bring tension and fear.

Shirley watched Samuel's back, unable to resist wanting to inquire about the situation back home.

"Th-... Samuel auntie, may I ask how my father king is? Is his body okay?"

"Ah... Samuel paused, replying, "His Majesty's body has no problems, only his mood is getting worse, always yearning for your safety. Not long ago he personally wrote to Queen Elizabeth, hoping she would continue to increase personnel to search for your whereabouts. Your Majesty has always believed you are still in Great Britain."

"Is that so?" Shirley lowered her head, showing a very regretful expression. "It's all my fault for being too playful. If I had listened to my father king and stayed honestly in the palace, nothing like this would have happened, and I am truly a useless fellow, only adding trouble to others."

"Do not blame yourself. You are His Majesty's happy fruit. If you were not mischievous, He would have less fun. Keeping it like this is good."

Samuel showed a kindly smile.

"How... could that be? I often make the king angry." Shirley's face turned red, very embarrassed.

"This time it really was a bit over the top. You are royalty, leaving the palace casually is a very dangerous thing." Samuel turned back to look at Shirley, adding a sentence, "The United Kingdom appears stable on the surface, but crises lurk within. For you, the palace is not a prison, but the safest place."

"Th-... th-... Shirley had an apologetic expression, tugging at the corner of her skirt, looking very wronged.

"You need not apologize; no one can blame you." Samuel said meaningfully, thinking this silly princess is about to die—what use is apologizing? Shirley slightly adjusted her mood. Then she continued to ask, "And my mother after? How is she? Has her mental state been stable these past half a year? Or... has someone been handling it?" He thought to himself that no one had yet discovered the secret of Archduke Asmodeus possessing the elf queen's wife, and things were becoming more and more interesting. Samuel withdrew his gaze and said playfully, "Your mother's state is excellent, good to the point of being unbearable."

"That's great!" Shirley showed a cheerful smile, clasping her hands together and exclaiming, "A long time ago, the mother's temperament changed drastically, saying she wanted to kill the father king, as if she had contracted a mental illness, and no matter what, it could not be cured, but now there is finally some improvement, this is truly a happy event." "Yeah, it really makes one happy." Samuel could not help but show a few eerie smiles. Shirley let out a breath, and the journey home seemed increasingly anticipated, "I hope the truth comes quickly, Samuel auntie, can we leave tomorrow?"

Samuel did not answer. How could he let Shirley go home? She is the important component for the dark elf king's revival. Going home was just painting a big pie for Shirley; she must surely die in a foreign land. Samuel twisted the doorknob, opened the mechanism, and immediately a loud rumbling sound came from the depths. The wall in front of the two slowly opened, revealing a dark passage leading to the unknown darkness. "Shirley殿下, please follow me." Samuel walked in front, leading the way, and waved at Shirley. "Huh?" Shirley felt something was wrong and instinctively took a step back, "Where are we going? I'm afraid of the dark place."

"Do not be afraid, I just want you to see something. It concerns the entire elf race. As a princess殿下, you indeed have the right to know." Samuel said seriously.

Shirley hesitated, thinking that since she is also an elf, Samuel would not harm her. So Shirley foolishly nodded and followed timidly one after another "Good.... The deep corridor goes downward, making it impossible to see what's far away? A faint yin wind blows from below, carrying a faint stench, and it becomes heavier the deeper one goes. Everything seems unusual, as if something is surging in the deep darkness. Shirley has a small courage, her pointed ears twitch slightly, alert to the surroundings. She has been closely following Samuel, unknown that she is the most dangerous creature. "Oh wuwu miaomiao...." A series of ghostly cries rang out in a sinister manner, mixed with the sound of nails scratching the wall. Combined, it makes one's hair stand on end, and instantly makes one feel chilled. "Samuel auntie,.... what is this sound?" Shirley became even more afraid.

"Wait. Soon you will know."

Samuel did not speak. The two turned a corner, and a horrifying scene immediately appeared: a deep pit, countless corpses rising and roaring, like stacked human pyramids trying to climb out, longing for fresh blood and flesh. They eat each other, never knowing satisfaction, their crimson eyes flashing, forming a bizarre tableau. This scene directly made the poor Shirley stunned, dumbfounded, unable to speak, her legs going weak, almost sitting on the ground. Although Shirley is also a mage, her talent is poor, just a small low-level mage, probably cannot beat even a single corpse.

"....Samuel auntie! Why are there so many corpse ghosts here!"

"It is I who raise them, how is it,殿下? My little pets are cute, aren't they?"

Samuel does not hide it, revealing an extremely evil smile, the corner of his mouth stretching to his ears.

Shirley took a half step back, her delicate body trembling uncontrollably, stammering, "....Why raise such evil things?"

"For the dark elf race's dream, and Archduke Asmodeus's grand plan!"

Samuel laughed wildly.

"....Dark elf!" Shirley opened her eyes wide, her expression shocked.

Samuel rudely reveals his true form, retracting his white skin, letting the dark skin show, looking more ferocious than before.

"Samuel auntie, are you actually a dark elf all along?!"

Shirley's expression is unbelievable, as if she cannot accept what she sees before her.

Due to historical reasons, the treatment of dark elves among the elf race is not fair. For example, officials at the level of ambassadors absolutely would not allow dark elves to serve. And there is an obvious gap between white elves and dark elves; the most obvious manifestation is that, after Shirley returned, she never spoke a word to Summerplen. Because they are dark elves, although they are the same elf race, they are not equal in status at all; dark elves are too humble compared to white elves.

"Right, I am a genuine dark elf, the white elf appearance is merely the result of regularly taking magic medicine." Samuel laughs ferociously, the fearful expression in front of him makes her feel deeply pleased.

Shirley feels she has been trapped, something is wrong, Samuel must be abnormal! This embassy is unsafe, she must leave! So Shirley panics and turns around, wanting to escape. Suddenly, a formidable wind wall appears before her, blocking her escape route. A Saint-tier magic power constructed wind wall, interspersed with countless wind blades, emitting a frightening metal cutting sound, surging at extreme speed. If Shirley dared to forcefully pass by, she would surely be cut into pieces, turning into a pool of flesh and blood! Samuel puts down the magic wand, his face wearing a ferocious and playful smile, teasingly saying, "What do you want to do?" "My dear Shirley殿下...."

PS ■ sigh, physiology just can't come back....

title: Chapter 21 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 21 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 21

"...I want to go find my friends...." Shelly's face turned pale, her expression extremely unnatural. "I don't want to stay here."

"Wouldn't it be better to live in the embassy? You have your own kind here, it would feel like home. What friends could you possibly have in a foreign land, as an elf?" Samuel's face curled into a bizarre smile, his jagged teeth jutting out crookedly, making him look especially sinister.

"Miss Alice and Mr. Merlin are my friends. I want to go find them." Shelly gripped the front of her clothes, her heart filled with extreme unease.

"Humans are all filthy, despicable, depraved creatures. Why would you choose to trust them? Your Highness, you make me feel deeply saddened." A flicker of displeasure flashed in Samuel's crimson eyes.

"Miss Alice and Mr. Merlin are different. Please don't slander them...." Shelly grew increasingly anxious, sensing that Samuel was very abnormal, and that it was best to stay as far away from her as possible. She forced a trace of princess-like dignity onto her face. "Aunt Samuel, please lower your Wind Wall and let me leave."

Samuel gave a cold laugh and said lightly, "You don't need to go looking for those two humans, because they won't see tomorrow's sun."

....What do you mean?" Shelly's expression turned shocked, and she subconsciously took a step back. The piercing Wind Wall sliced off several strands of her golden hair.

"I've already sent my subordinates to hunt them down. By my calculations, they should be lying in a pool of blood right now." Samuel smiled, seemingly enjoying the sight of people's despair.

"Why would you do something so extreme? What did they do wrong!" Shelly frowned, her face full of anxiety. She had finally decided that Samuel was extremely dangerous.

The contradiction between the white elves and the black elves had always existed. They maintained appearances while harboring deep suspicion toward one another.

Shelly had long heard her father speak of a reactionary faction within the black elves.

They worshipped her late uncle, the Dark Elf King, and were always waiting for an opportunity to overthrow the United Kingdom.

Looking at Samuel's current demeanor, Shelly felt she was exactly the reactionary faction her father had warned about.

"Because I cannot let anyone know your whereabouts. It's obviously more reliable to keep a dead man silent, isn't it?" Samuel said briefly.

"Aunt Samuel, what on earth are you trying to do?" Shelly was completely puzzled. Aside from knowing that Samuel was extremely dangerous, she understood nothing else.

"In these situations, villains usually babble endlessly, revealing their entire plan. But I'm not that foolish. Why would I tell you my plan? You only need to continue playing the role of a silly princess and obediently do as I say." Samuel pointed at Shelly and emphasized seriously, "For me, your only value is probably your life itself."

"Uh!" Shelly shrank her body in fright, constantly stepping backward, her face turning deathly pale, her lips trembling incessantly. "Aunt Samuel, by the authority of my position as princess, I command you to let me go!"

"Your Highness, please don't be like this. To avoid physical suffering, I suggest you abandon your princess tantrums and stay here obediently. The pain will only be temporary, and before long, you will be completely liberated!" Samuel displayed an evil smile, already envisioning the grand moment when the elf would weep in agony.

"Restricting my freedom and threatening my safety—this is disrespect toward me!" Shelly forcibly maintained her princess posture, naively believing she could crush Samuel with her status. "When I return to the palace, I will definitely tell my father!"

"What a pity~!" Samuel laughed even more joyfully, finding Shelly to be a truly extraordinarily foolish waste of a princess. "You will never return to the United Kingdom, nor will you ever see the father you've been so worried about!"

"Aunt Samuel, why are you doing this? You weren't like this before...." Shelly's face went pale, her body trembling uncontrollably.

"I have always been loyal to His Majesty Althodor, and I am irreconcilable with the Elf King!" Samuel reached out toward Shelly, a chilling smile on her face.

"Come with me obediently. A private cell has already been prepared for you below."

"You are of royal princess status, and we will not treat you poorly. We will always maintain a respectful attitude toward you."

"So when we need you, please坦然ly dedicate your life for the rise of the black elves!"

***

At a noble hotel located in the central area of the royal capital.

It was nighttime, and the hotel was brightly lit.

The luxurious decorations revealed refinement in every detail, showcasing extraordinary elegance. The spire-like dome, irregular forms, and undulating lines rendered the aesthetic Baroque style with full vividness.

On the upper levels of the hotel, a person clad in black robes stood concealed, their figure almost merging with the dense darkness of night.

They were the black elf assassination squad dispatched by Samuel, skilled at silently and imperceptibly taking lives in the dark of night.

Every member was high-tier, tempered through rigorous training, having honed exceptional assassination techniques.

Though this group appeared to have average individual strength, their combined power through team collaboration was indeed no small matter.

Furthermore, assassination relies on overcoming strength with weakness, using technique to triumph—that is the most core element of an assassin.

Ten assassins gathered together, rapidly devising an assassination plan in extreme shorthand:

Assassination Captain: "The target individuals are within this hotel. One is a high-tier magic swordsman named Alice Crodia, and the other is Merlin Lucifer... cough! A scummy village person."

The atmosphere grew unmistakably awkward. This assassination squad, composed entirely of high-tier elites, was going to great lengths to assassinate an utterly useless ordinary person. It felt incredibly absurd.

Assassination Squad Member: "Are you kidding me? We need to personally handle killing a village person? Is this really Lord Samuel's order?"

Assassination Captain: "That's correct. It is Lord Samuel's personal command."

Assassination Squad Member: "...Are we being looked down upon?"

Assassination Squad Member: "Fine, assassinating that high-tier magic swordsman is one thing, but why is there also a village person? Is this a buy-one-get-one-free deal? We're a squad that can assassinate Saint-tier strong warriors, after all."

Assassination Captain: "I believe Lord Samuel has his reasons for doing this. Let us not presume to guess the thoughts of important figures. We simply follow orders and carry them out."

Assassination Squad Member: "Then let me handle both of these targets? I can take them all down by myself."

Assassination Captain: "No. During missions, we must never let our guard down. Even if we're killing an infant, we must go all out."

Assassination Squad Member: "...Understood..."

Assassination Captain: "Now we begin. We'll split into two teams of five. Move quickly, and withdraw immediately after completing the job."

The black-robed members nodded in unison, indicating they understood the captain's plan.

Assassination Captain: "Begin operation!"

At his command, the assassins leaped and soared across the hotel rooftops, simultaneously diving in different directions.

Midair, all the assassins launched clawed grappling ropes from their arms toward the windows, then shot into the brightly lit hotel!

The long-prepared hunt finally began...

title: Chapter 22 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 22 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 7 · Chapter 22

Here's a translation that follows all the rules:

Noble hotel.

After the people finished eating, they planned to go to the artificial hot spring unique to this place.

After resting, they planned to depart early tomorrow for the Dover Strait.

The artificial hot spring on the third floor, with men and women in separate areas to the south and north.

Looking at the exterior, it's gilded and splendid, luxurious to the point of dazzling the eyes.

In the central pool, there's a mermaid sculpture slowly spraying warm water from a water bottle.

Merlin inwardly sighed, no wonder it's a noble hotel, humans really know how to enjoy themselves.......

His residence, the First Demon Lord Palace, wouldn't have such a luxurious artificial hot spring due to scarce resources.

Watching the environment here being so excellent, he couldn't help but feel a little excited inside~

Thinking about the hot spring he soaked in not long ago in Roicor Village, and compared to here, it's simply incomparable.

Merlin surveyed for a while, then directly prepared to wash his body, then soak in the hot spring.

He wrapped a towel around himself, sat on a small stool, and had scalding hot water poured over his body. A very obvious scar was clearly visible on his heart area, looking a bit shocking, as if something sharp had been stabbed into it.

Merlin just liked scalding hot water, because it gives a very stimulating sensation, like a knife lightly sliding over smooth skin.

It's been a while since the last letter was written, shouldn't it be time to write another letter to Lilith now?

Merlin pondered in his heart, feeling it was time to write a letter to his sister, to prove that he's doing well outside, and not to be mistaken as a useless layabout at home, a good-for-nothing outside.

However, thinking of Lilith's words before departure, saying she would resign from the position of Grand General and come find him, and until now there's been no news, it's almost certain she's encountered some obstacle and can't leave the First Demon Lord Palace.

Merlin touched his chin, feeling it's very possible that

After he leaves, the First Demon Lord Palace will have no head, and should become very chaotic.

As his sister, only she can suppress the other great demons, and wanting to break away isn't an easy matter.

Merlin felt not a shred of guilt, on the contrary, he felt quite pleased.

Without Lilith this follower, Merlin feels his life is especially free and easy, refreshing and natural need not say more.

"Merlin-sama, shall I scrub your back?"

Kyle, wrapped in a white towel, came walking over with a washcloth, white steam rising and falling, hazy and indistinct.

This scene and situation, like a natural mosaic, making it hard to see clearly, yet inspiring wild imagination.

"Ah!?" Merlin turned his head, looked at Kyle for a moment, and all sorts of drop-the-soap, philosophical musing tropes suddenly surfaced in his mind, the atmosphere wasn't like an awkward one.

Kyle's figure was textbook-perfect inverted triangle, clearly defined muscle lines, especially the merman line and six-pack abs.

He looks to be much sturdier than Merlin, but Merlin takes a proportional route, won't give people much sense of aggression.

"Isn't it needed, Merlin-sama?" Kyle came to Merlin's side.

"Eh!? Serv( δ )ice?" Merlin had a complex expression, his thoughts not very pure, "No... I don't need you to scrub my back."

"Why? Could it be you can scrub your own back?" Kyle showed an expression of great surprise.

"...Cough!" Merlin lightly coughed, concealing his embarrassment and said, "I just don't want to easily give my back to others."

"Is that so, no wonder Merlin-sama, doing things so carefully, is the bearing of a strong person." Kyle's expression became solemn with respect, feeling Merlin's attitude is something he should learn from.

"...Wrong..." Merlin slightly adjusted his mood, and said in a deliberately profound way, "As a strong person, one must always remain vigilant, the back is a place to give to trustworthy partners, not just anyone can approach."

"Thank you, Merlin-sama's teaching, truly let me benefit greatly." Kyle slightly bowed, expressing gratitude, feeling there are many things different about Merlin, worthy of his good study.

Merlin embarrassedly didn't speak, a drop of cold sweat flowing from his forehead, thinking in his heart, what the heck teaching ah?

I just hate the philosophical position when scrubbing someone's back ah, a First Hall Master, Great Demon Lord, having a human's big bottom sitting on his butt, what's the dignity of that

Merlin felt he was wearing a woman's face, this kind of thing should be cautious, the daisy he guarded for over 400 years, can't lose his composure in the men's bathhouse.

Kyle sat on a small stool next to Merlin, opened the valve, and hot water poured from head to foot.

His expression was complex, seems to have many thoughts pressing down, but doesn't dare to say easily.

Merlin glanced at Kyle, saw he had something on his mind, and so asked candidly.

"What's wrong? So weighed down with matters, if there's a problem, I don't mind listening, anyway I'm idle with nothing to do."

"Merlin-sama,.... Kyle hesitated for a moment, and seriously asked, "Am I... especially useless?"

"Why think that way?" Merlin had foam everywhere, surprisedly looking at Kyle.

"I've always been working hard to train for the young lady, but at certain times, I found my strength is limited, can't protect the young lady at all, and feel especially useless,

What's the point of all the effort since always

Kyle's expression was resentful, silently clenching his fists, knuckles turning white, looking like he's barely restraining his emotions.

His inner heart was struggling hard, couldn't find his own value at all, if he can't even protect the young lady's safety, what face does he have to be a knight, maybe he should just go home and farm the land, = =

"Just like last time in the underground palace second layer, unable to bring the young lady out of danger, I deeply feel my incompetence, why can't I become stronger? Why is it difficult to protect the young lady even sacrificing my life? In the end, maybe I'm not suited to be a knight, the young lady needs a strong person, not I this weak person.

Merlin fell silent for a while, and said lightly, "You can have the point of self-awareness, I don't hate it."

"Eh!?" Kyle looked at Merlin in doubt, apparently didn't understand.

"I hate those guys without self-awareness the most, can't tell the enemy from us, just in front of me jumping around, honestly very annoying." Merlin sighed and continued, "You and those guys are different, having self-awareness can see the reality, in the future won't be deceived, there's still room for progress."

".....Is that so?" Kyle opened his eyes wide, a half-understanding look.

"And does young lady Cecilia really need a powerful knight?" Merlin withdrew his gaze, and said calmly, "I don't think so, she just needs a trustworthy companion, chase away that endless loneliness, briefly put is hoping someone can give her warmth and

"...Kyle was stunned, feeling Merlin's words were particularly profound, though didn't understand, but just very impressive ah have you not?

"Everyone has their own unique value, there's no such thing as useless guys, our guild has a drunkard, everyday mixing time, but his information gathering social ability, not to mention making me look again, that's his value, you just haven't encountered an opportunity to show your value..."

Merlin picked up a piece of soap, put it in his hand and showed it to Kyle, then meaningfully asked.

"Looking at the soap in my hand, what have you perceived? Hint, soap is slippery and tricky."

Kyle stared at the milky soap for a while, suddenly opened his eyes and suddenly realized, "Merlin's meaning is let me go with the flow? Don't impatiently want to prove yourself, but like soap—quietly waiting, there will always be a day of flashing light, right

"...Merlin's forehead couldn't help but slide over countless black lines, a half-speechless look thought--

Kyle is such a fool, right?

My meaning is don't go giving Cecilia some damn knight.

In the bathhouse picking up soap selling chrysanthemums, then just eating and waiting to die, why bother making yourself so tired?

Day oh, my and this idiot knight's thinking really aren't on the same channel, hard to communicate ah..... z(°△° ID}

title: Chapter 23
content:
Chapter 23

Volume 7 · Chapter 23

Kiel felt like he had received Merlin's teachings, and suddenly, his whole person was different.

It was as if he had been enlightened, and his life had become clear again... Kiel looked at Merlin with a fanboy-like gaze, and his heart was extremely admiring of him.

Merlin looked at Kiel, who was overjoyed, and his mood was very complicated - he hadn't meant it like that at all, and Kiel's imagination was too rich! Merlin felt like he was just talking nonsense, but Kiel, with his silly expression, was able to grasp the great truths of life.

Merlin scratched his head, which was covered in soap suds, and thought that he and Kiel's thought processes were not on the same channel; he estimated that even if he farted, Kiel would think it was fragrant.

Merlin thought this was terrible and decided it was better to be honest.

What if Kiel, this fool, really followed his way to the end, stupidly guarding Cecilia until the end of his life? Wouldn't that be his responsibility?

"Kiel, don't get it wrong, I mean..." Merlin said.

"Don't be modest, Merlin, I know you mean it," Kiel raised his hand, signaling Merlin not to speak, "I didn't expect you to not only be powerful but also have a talent for being a teacher, guiding lost souls onto the right path; your guidance made my soul feel purified, it's so wonderful~"

Merlin's eyebrows were tightly furrowed, and he was anxious, feeling like he wanted to hit Kiel on the head with the soap in his hand; "Kiel, calm down a bit and listen to me explain the meaning behind my words..."

"You don't need to explain it; I've understood it very thoroughly; it's no wonder the lady is so admiring of you," Kiel said, looking confident, and his admiration for Merlin rose to a new level; "You have extraordinary abilities and a noble soul; there are very few people like you, and I have to admire you; it's your personality that has convinced me!"

Merlin was about to say something but stopped, feeling like he couldn't say anything; he thought Kiel was indeed a simple-minded, muscle-bound fool.

"Thank you for your guidance; although it was just a hint, it has benefited me greatly; I've never felt so full of hope and expectation for the future," Kiel bowed deeply to Merlin, sincerely expressing his gratitude.

Merlin licked his lips, what could he say? He could only go along with Kiel's words.

This stupid knight would do whatever he wanted, and it had nothing to do with Merlin.

Let him understand it however he wanted, anyway, it wasn't like Merlin had said it out of his own mouth.

Merlin put on a serious face, patted Kiel's shoulder, and said, "Kid, your understanding ability is beyond my expectations, and I'm impressed; you'll surely become a great achiever in the future."

Kiel's eyes widened, and he was overjoyed by Merlin's sudden praise; he felt like he had been affirmed by a life coach.

He bowed his head again and expressed his gratitude to Merlin in a humble tone, "Thank you, Merlin, for your praise; actually, my understanding ability is average; it's just that your hints are quite clever."

Merlin's face was expressionless, and he thought, clever? Ha! I'm just telling you to go sell chrysanthemums! Enjoying life and doing nothing is the best; what's the point of effort?

"Don't worry, Merlin; I won't forget your guidance; I'll patiently guard the lady's side, and there will be a day when I shine," Kiel clenched his fist, and the muscles on his arm tightened, looking full of energy.

Merlin felt a headache coming on and thought to himself, please don't say I taught him! I wouldn't want to be associated with him!

Although Merlin was full of dissatisfaction inside, he still responded seriously, "Oh, work hard! Strive to become a great achiever soon!"

"I won't let you down, Merlin!" Kiel's eyes sparkled with determination.

Merlin couldn't take Kiel's enthusiasm and rubbed his soapy hair, thinking that this fool would probably never be cured...

Kiel had no idea what Merlin was thinking and instead felt like his future was bright.

Compared to Merlin, he was weak, but as long as he was willing to work hard, there would be a day when he would show his value!

He believed in himself from the bottom of his heart and decided to practice even harder.

Kiel glanced at Merlin secretly and thought that Merlin was really different, a rare and outstanding human.

But why did such an excellent Merlin want to be an unstable adventurer? And he was the lowest rank, looked down upon by everyone.

Kiel felt confused and thought that Merlin's abilities would have many better choices; why did he have to make himself look so mediocre?

"Merlin, may I ask you a personal question?" Kiel asked.

"Not gay, thanks," Merlin replied without hesitation.

Kiel was taken aback and said awkwardly, "Merlin, it's not about special preferences..."

"Then ask away," Merlin responded while rubbing his soapy hair.

"Merlin, your abilities are so strong; why are you willing to be a black iron adventurer?" Kiel asked seriously, very puzzled by this.

Merlin's action of washing his hair stopped, and he thought, he didn't want to be like this; what could he do?

The damn adventurer advancement system didn't give him any opportunity to show off!

Merlin muttered to himself, not planning to explain to Kiel that he didn't have magical energy or aura; it was too much trouble, and he wasn't familiar enough with Kiel.

"From what the lady said, Merlin, you're not someone who chases fame and fortune; it seems to be true," Kiel looked at Merlin and said, "But I think you're too low-key; it makes you seem very mediocre; I'm sure there are many people like me who misunderstand you."

"I don't really care about that; what do other people's opinions have to do with me?" Merlin replied calmly, thinking that he was a demon, not a human; and he didn't have magical energy or aura, so it was natural that he was mediocre.

"I think you should have a better life; you don't have to be a wandering adventurer; with your abilities, I think it would be no problem for you to be a thorn knight," Kiel said seriously.

Merlin smiled slightly, revealing a hint of a monarch's aloofness, "Thorn knight is good, but it's a pawn serving Elizabeth; I won't serve anyone or any force; no one has the qualification to make me serve..."

Kiel's breathing stopped, and under Merlin's pressure as a superior, he almost couldn't catch his breath.

He felt a noble and arrogant aura emanating from Merlin, like that of a monarch.

If Merlin didn't look so shabby at the moment, it would be easy to mistake him for a royal from somewhere.

Kiel calmed down slightly and said respectfully, "I was reckless; I apologize, Merlin; as a strong person, you indeed have your own choices."

Merlin smiled slightly and said, "It's okay; don't mind it..."

In the sky above the hot spring, five assassins in black robes, forming a killing team, had already prepared.

They had been waiting for the opportunity under the leadership of their captain; seeing Merlin and Kiel chatting enthusiastically below, the opportunity had finally arrived!

The assassination team leader made a few action gestures to the other four team members, and the communication was silent.

"Assassination begins!"

title: Chapter 24 — Moving rush over, back to regular extra chapters
content:
Chapter 24 — Moving rush over, back to regular extra chapters

Volume 7 · Chapter 24

The five-person assassination squad followed their leader's orders, descending from above at high speed toward Merlin, who was washing his hair.

This squad had been personally led by the captain for the assassination, rather than delegated to anyone else.

The reason was simple: the assassination captain didn't believe Lord Samuel would casually send them to kill two deadbeats—there had to be some deeper meaning behind it.

This kind of overkill did feel a bit insulting, so the assassination captain intended to lead the operation personally, ensuring the plan to kill Merlin would go flawlessly and the mission would be completed perfectly.

It seemed the assassination captain was still a very meticulous person—he didn't underestimate Merlin just because he had no magic or combat aura.

The five assassins wielded crescent moon curved swords unique to the elf race, radiating chilling murderous intent, their targets locked squarely on Merlin's neck!

The cold wind howled; the assassins in black robes resembled messengers of death, moving silently, seemingly able to end lives before their victims even noticed.

"Hmm!?" Merlin suddenly sensed a chill from behind and felt something was off.

Kyle beside him hadn't noticed a thing, still humming a tune while washing his hair, in unusually high spirits.

Although these assassins were skilled at concealing their presence, Merlin had encountered too many powerful foes—this level of malice could be detected quickly.

The assassins in mid-air wielded their curved blades with piercing attacks that made one gasp.

This group hunt was perfectly coordinated, attacking from all 360 degrees with no blind spots—utterly inescapable!

At this critical moment, Merlin showed no panic whatsoever, appearing calm and detached.

Time seemed to slow—

Merlin unexpectedly spun around and hurled the bar of soap in his hand, like a demonic bullet tearing through the air!

"Damn it, even hiding in the men's bath to throw soap!?"

Merlin's casual attack, though seemingly like a child throwing stones, produced an unexpected effect.

The soap struck one assassin's face without mercy, sending him tumbling upside down with a loud "plop" onto the floor.

That wasn't all—the flying soap bounced back and forth among the remaining four assassins, instantly eliciting a chorus of screams.

"Yeδh~!"

"F@ck you!"

The carefully planned assassination攻势 crumbled in an instant, completely schooled by Merlin's soap, left utterly subdued.

"Eh!?"

Kyle heard the strange screams and realized something was wrong, quickly turning around to look.

Seeing five assassins lying on the ground, clutching their faces in pain, he was startled.

During this time, Cecilia had booked the entire hot spring, so no one should have been allowed in.

Kyle frowned, finding this group highly suspicious, and questioned them with a harsh tone.

"...What's going on? Who are you!? Who allowed you in!?"

The assassins rose from the ground, rubbing their faces or holding their heads, clearly still shaken by that powerful soap attack.

No one would have expected Merlin to deflect a meticulously practiced group assassination with a bar of soap—leaving one deeply contemplative.

"Who are you?" The assassination captain, clutching his swollen face, slowly stood up. "You don't need to know. Just know we're here to take your lives..."

Since the assassins wore masks, their elf-like pointed ears were hidden, making it hard to guess their identities.

Merlin wasn't one to act without reason—at the very least, he needed to understand the situation.

"Calm down. Why are you trying to kill us? Have we done anything wrong?"

"Yeah, maybe there's been a misunderstanding. Let's talk first." Kyle agreed, feeling something was off.

"You don't need to know the reason. Just hand over your heads!" The assassination captain gripped his curved blade, looking like he had no intention of wasting words.

Kyle sensed these were high-tier opponents—fighting for real would be tough—but thankfully Merlin was here too, otherwise he might not even be able to speak without stammering. "Who sent you? Let us negotiate with your employer. If we've unintentionally offended someone, we can apologize—but killing us outright is a bit excessive."

"I'm sorry, you're about to die. There's no chance to meet our BOSS." The assassination captain said coldly.

"Wait..." Merlin pondered for a long time, completely unable to figure out who he'd offended in London, though he had a few guesses. "Was it the restaurant owner I drove bankrupt?"

"No." The assassination captain replied.

Merlin: "Could it be I cuckolded you?"

Assassination captain: "No either..."

Merlin: "Then it must be gambling debts I owe you?"

Kyle watched Merlin with a complex expression—he'd always thought Merlin was a saint, but from this conversation, Merlin seemed like a scumbag who drank, gambled, and... well, you know.

"Stop asking questions. You're all dying anyway! Attack!"

At the assassination captain's command, the squad charged forward with their curved blades, their swift movements leaving only afterimages.

"Merlin-sama, let me assist you!" Kyle said seriously, knowing he couldn't win against so many high-tier foes, but still able to help.

"No need, don't get in the way..." Merlin waved him off, stepping forward and assuming a stance of one man holding the pass against ten thousand.

"Uh, alright..." Kyle didn't argue—Merlin's strength spoke for itself; they didn't need his help against high-tier opponents.

"Hmph!" The assassination captain sneered. He thought Merlin was arrogant—a powerless waste with no magic or combat aura, daring to fight alone? Since the other party wanted death, he wouldn't be polite!

The assassination squad adopted a steady group combat formation—four members rushed forward to distract and hold Merlin.

Then the captain would wait for the perfect opening to deliver a fatal strike.

This tactic had been drilled countless times—smooth as silk, never failing.

But unfortunately, they were facing a cheater—what good was tactics against that?

"So you won't reason with me? I'll turn you into murals then..."

Merlin cracked his neck, warmed up his body slightly, and prepared to teach these rude fellows a lesson.

The four assassins acting as bait charged at Merlin with murderous intent, their curved blades swinging with deadly precision, looking incredibly powerful.

Then, in the blink of an eye, a dramatic scene unfolded—all four assassins were punched through the ceiling by Merlin, merging perfectly with the nude murals on the dome. These unlucky wretches didn't even have time to scream; even if they survived, they'd be crippled.

Not a shred of combat process—perfectly embodying the words "simple and brutal."

Want to hold Merlin back? Not a chance.

"You send only this few to bother me? I wonder how your employer is..." Merlin cracked his knuckles—there was no need for a sword slash at all.

The assassination captain's eyes widened in shock, his mouth agape—

He hadn't even gotten to fight and was already a lone commander!

His subordinates were all elite assassins, yet they couldn't beat an ordinary person!

Indeed, this man was no simple fellow—no wonder Samuel had entrusted them with handling him...

title: Chapter 25 — Monthly Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 25 — Monthly Bonus Update

Volume 7 · Chapter 25

The leader of the assassination team couldn't calm down, his mind reeling from the unexpected turn of events. He had thought this operation was a sure thing, but now it seemed he had hit a brick wall.

The drastic fall from heaven to hell was difficult for him to accept. "Kiel's expression froze, and he muttered to himself, "How impressive..."

Although Kiel had expected Merlin to win easily, he was still surprised by the crushing victory. Kiel thought Merlin's strength was unfathomable, and normal Saint-tier attacks usually had a pattern to them. But Merlin was different; there was no discernible battle process, and it was like watching a complete annihilation.

Merlin looked at the lone leader of the assassination team and felt that he was only a high-ranking individual, and it didn't matter if he killed him or not. So, he said nonchalantly, "If you're scared, you can run away. I won't chase you, but tell your employer that it's not a good idea to provoke me, or you'll die a terrible death."

The leader of the assassination team was taken aback, then suddenly became enraged. He said seriously, "You're belittling me? I admit you're strong, but you can't just trample on my dignity..."

"I'm doing this for your own good; don't insist on coming here to die, because it's meaningless." Merlin tightened his belt, looking casual.

"You must be a Saint-tier powerhouse, deliberately hiding your strength to catch us off guard. You're shameless." The leader of the assassination team gritted his teeth and said, seemingly very angry.

He thought that Samuel-sama handing this guy over to the assassination team wasn't without reason; he was indeed difficult to deal with. If he hadn't been cautious, he might have ended up like the others, beaten to the ground.

"Ha... Merlin chuckled, too lazy to explain, and said helplessly, "Whatever you say is fine..."

The leader of the assassination team scowled, dissatisfied, and his anger grew. He felt that Merlin's casual attitude was humiliating him.

Kiel watched Merlin and thought that hiding one's strength was indeed a bit shameless. He had also suffered a great loss from it, and if he hadn't stopped in time, it would have led to a bigger disaster.

They were completely unaware...

"Now, I give you two choices: one, go back where you came from; two... Merlin pointed to the ceiling, a hint of a smile on his face, "Become a living wall painting, like your companion."

"You bastard!"

The leader of the assassination team gritted his teeth and cursed, thinking that he couldn't possibly go back. If he failed to complete the task, he would undoubtedly be killed by Samuel-sama.

For assassins, failing to complete a task was fatal, especially for Samuel, who seemed like a kind and gentle goddess but was actually ruthless.

The leader of the assassination team didn't want to bear the responsibility of failing the task, so he had to kill Merlin.

"I won't choose either; I choose for you to die!"

"Is that so?" Merlin sighed and said helplessly, "Then there's no way out. I hope you'll learn what it means to yield in your next life."

The leader of the assassination team gritted his teeth and pulled out a bottle of pure black potion from his bag. "Let's get this over with! Don't think you've won! You're Saint-tier, but that doesn't mean anything! As long as I drink this special dark frenzy potion, I'm not without a chance of winning!"

"Oh? You have a trump card?" Merlin said expressionless, thinking that this was just another cliché...

"Special dark potion?" Kiel frowned, seemingly familiar with it.

"Do you know this thing?" Merlin asked, turning back to him.

"A bit... Kiel nodded and thought for a moment before saying, "This is a potion that can only be brewed by the dark elves. It can instantly increase combat power, entering an extremely excited and frenzied state. Normal people who drink it will basically lose their sanity and eventually explode and die, but the dark elves seem to have some resistance, and the side effects aren't that severe, although there will definitely be negative effects."

Merlin nodded, seemingly understanding, and looked at the potion in the leader's hand, lost in thought.

"But some people use this as a hallucinogen. Before the underground dark duel arena matches, they'll give the gladiators a few drops of this, and they'll lose their sanity and fight each other like beasts." Kiel's brow furrowed, and he spoke in a serious tone, "However, this is a banned potion in human territories, and it's usually destroyed. It's basically a rare commodity..."

"If possible, I don't want to use this, because drinking it will turn me into a useless waste!"

The leader of the assassination team revealed a hint of pain, seemingly reluctant to pay such a great price for power.

But when he thought of the dark elves being eaten by ghouls, he still resolutely opened the bottle of dark frenzy potion!

A massive amount of dark elements burst out, spreading around like black smoke, making Kiel frown.

The concentration of dark elements was unusually high. Kiel thought that maybe it was because of the "special" label, and it was definitely different from the rumors.

The leader of the assassination team removed his veil, revealing pointed elf ears and black skin, no longer hiding his dark elf identity.

"Prepare to die! This is all your fault!"

"Open your eyes and witness my true power!"

"You're a dark elf?" Kiel's eyes widened, completely unexpected. It made sense now that the leader could get the special dark frenzy potion.

Merlin's brow furrowed slightly, thinking that what was the dark elf doing here? And why did he want to kill himself? Was there something important that he had missed?

The leader of the assassination team drank the dark frenzy potion in one gulp, and the effects immediately kicked in. The bottle fell to the ground, shattering into countless pieces.

His expression turned painful, and his features contorted as he struggled to choke himself, like he was in agony.

The leader of the assassination team shook and knelt to the ground, scratching his neck and screaming at the top of his lungs.

"Ahhhhhhhhhhhh!!!"

A dark aura burst out from the leader's body, and the shockwave spread around, shattering the glass.

Kiel broke out in a cold sweat and had to cover his eyes. He blurted out instinctively.

"Whoa, dude, do you have to be so extreme?!"

title: Chapter 26
content:
Chapter 26

Volume 7 · Chapter 26

The Dark Rage Potion has an immense effect on humans; even a single drop produces a very noticeable result.

In addition to a short-term surge in power, it carries severe side effects.

Even if the Black Elf had some resistance to the drug, he couldn't just chug it down like a drink!

Moreover, this was a Special Grade potion, N times stronger than the standard variety. Beyond boosting combat power, its side effects were only to be imagined!

Kyle watched in dumbfounded shock, feeling that this Assassination Captain was truly insane. Did he not want to live?

Dark elements swept through the room like a storm, making it difficult to keep one's eyes open as the raging power grew rapidly.

Merlin watched the Assassination Captain with a blank expression, his mind perfectly calm. He was used to this; those driven to a dead end often resorted to such measures.

"Aaaahhhhhhh!"

The Assassination Captain screamed in agony, the dark elements around him growing increasingly intense.

He knelt on the ground, desperately scratching at his neck as if someone were strangling him.

After struggling for a brief moment, the Assassination Captain's body underwent a very obvious transformation—

His clothes instantly burst apart, turning his well-fitted black combat suit into a loose little apron.

His physique swelled, growing into a massive Black Elf giant, fully five meters tall.

His appearance became increasingly ferocious, his body covered in black fur; at first glance, he looked like an enhanced version of a black gorilla!

His fangs and sharp claws were no different from a beast's, and his massive muscles were covered in terrifying blue veins, brimming with explosive power.

The Assassination Captain looked at his transformed body, a look of delight appearing on his face. He couldn't help but throw his head back and let out a long roar—

"Roarrrrrrrrrrr!"

The massive sonic wave caused the entire hotel to tremble slightly. Even with their ears covered, the sound was piercingly loud.

The Assassination Captain's body was now enormous, looking down on Kyle and Merlin. They couldn't help but smirk, feeling that the two of them were nothing but cats and dogs to him.

"... Kyle stared with wide eyes, gazing up at the Assassination Captain who had transformed into a black giant. His mouth hung open in shock. "What the hell is this thing! Too f***ing..."

Merlin's face remained calm, as if he was accustomed to such sudden transformations. Even if the Assassination Captain turned into a werewolf right in front of him, he wouldn't be surprised.

Although the Assassination Captain was not a Saint-tier being, the combat power he unleashed in this short-term burst was absolutely capable of matching a Saint-tier powerhouse!

Truly worthy of being a Special Grade Dark Rage Potion that was priceless and unobtainable. The effect was outstanding, forcibly multiplying the Assassination Captain's strength several times over, turning him into an ugly monster capable of competing with Saint-tier powerhouses.

Although the price was a high likelihood of losing his sanity once the drug wore off, the Assassination Captain felt it was worth it as long as he could kill Merlin. It was better than failing the mission and being thrown to the ghoul feeders.

The Assassination Captain enjoyed the beauty of the power gained from the drug, narcissistically admiring his ugly body, his mind sinking into ecstasy.

"So this is the effect of the Dark Rage Potion?"

"I feel an unprecedented power filling my body!"

"Powerful, invincible, sweeping all before me! It's truly wonderful to live!"

"Worthy of being my race's mysterious potion, it has actually increased my strength to this extent!"

"Hahaha! Who else can fight me now? No one can defeat me in my current state! Hahaha..."

A layer of cold sweat broke out on Kyle's forehead. Feeling the violent power radiating from the Assassination Captain, he was indeed terrified.

If Merlin lost, both he and Kyle would die here!

Although Merlin's strength was also very strong and seemingly bottomless, Kyle was still a bit anxious, unsure if Merlin could defeat the monster-like Assassination Captain.

However, Kyle had already made up his mind. If Merlin and the Assassination Captain were evenly matched, he would have to step in to help and increase the chances of victory.

If Merlin couldn't beat the Assassination Captain in his current state, then there was no point in wasting time struggling; he might as well wait for death.

Merlin calmly picked his ear and said indifferently, "Nowadays, everyone wants to be a magical girl. It's almost embarrassing to go out if you can't transform. How does it feel? Is taking drugs really that great?"

"Heh heh heh..." The Assassination Captain let out a series of cold laughs, his massive body trembling slightly. "How can I just say it's great? It's very great. Extremely great! F***ing great!"

"Oh, I'm glad you're happy..." Merlin looked at the Assassination Captain with a complex expression, thinking that people who took drugs were usually a bit out of their minds, and he should understand them as a vulnerable group.

"You arrogant fool will never understand this beautiful feeling. You spend your whole life immersed in your own dreams, acting like a frog at the bottom of a well!" The Assassination Captain was full of confidence now. He grinned, his sharp teeth looking terrifying.

"I'm a frog at the bottom of a well?" Merlin pointed at himself in surprise, the corner of his mouth twisting into a smile. "Are you kidding? You're the frog at the bottom of the well, okay?"

"Still trying to talk tough with me? I think you don't understand the situation. Look clearly!" The Assassination Captain showed off his enhanced body, pointing at Merlin and shouting, "Your pressure is zero, while my pressure can only be described as explosive! Even if you are hiding your strength now, I am still confident I can crush you!"

"And then?" Merlin frowned, his expression as if asking if the Assassination Captain had any last words before dying.

"There is no 'and then,' because you will definitely die!" The Assassination Captain's muscular body assumed an attacking stance, his crimson pupils flickering rapidly. "Arrogant bastard, prepare to die. I will twist your head off with my own hands!"

"Hah, good momentum..." Merlin grinned indifferently, beckoning the Assassination Captain with a finger in a provocative manner. "Come on. Don't be so shocked you turn into an idiot."

"Seeking death!"

The Assassination Captain roared in anger and suddenly launched an attack.

Boosted by the Dark Rage Potion, his movements were like a clap of thunder!

His feet slammed into the ground, instantly turning the floor into shattered debris, his body moving so fast it turned into a black lightning bolt.

"So fast!" Kyle was dumbfounded, thinking his eyes couldn't keep up for a moment! His body was huge and looked clumsy, but the actual effect was baffling!

The Assassination Captain rushed to Merlin's face and swung a full-power heavy punch. An intense shockwave erupted, blasting through the wall of the entire hotel with a thunderous roar. Thick dust flew uncontrollably, and the street outside was already visible!

Kyle covered his head with both hands to protect himself from the shockwave. Even so, his arms went numb.

Damn! This attack power is too strong!

Having this kind of strength from taking drugs, he could indeed fight a Saint-tier powerhouse!

No wonder this drug was banned. If it fell into the wrong hands, the consequences would be unimaginable!

I wonder how Lord Merlin is doing? He shouldn't be in any trouble, right...

The thick dust blocked Kyle's view, making him increasingly worried about the outcome of the battle.

The evening wind from outside blew into the hotel, quickly dispersing the swirling dust and revealing the result.

Chapter 28 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 28

Alice was muttering some prayers, inadvertently applying yet another debuff to Merlin.

"You're here early."

A familiar voice rang out, making Alice shiver guiltily like a thief caught in the act. She turned in surprise toward the hot spring entrance.

Cecilia stood at the doorway with her hands on her hips, small and pretty, wrapped in a goose-yellow bath towel that barely covered her curvaceous figure.

Her ample chest instantly reduced Alice — a poor, flat-chested girl like a washboard — to crumbs. A single glance told the whole story.

"Uh, you're here early too..."

Alice's face showed a trace of fluster. She didn't turn around, but instead instinctively covered her chest, apparently not wanting Cecilia to see it.

Normally when she was out, Alice wore padding so her chest didn't look quite so pitiful.

But bath time required removing them, leaving her barren landscape fully exposed, which felt rather shameful.

After all, she was a person who cared about her dignity. If Cecilia looked down on her, how embarrassing would that be? She could've wished herself dead right then...

Alice's heart grew restless. Thinking of Cecilia's young lady personality, she might just tease her mercilessly.

"Unlike you, so cum —" Cecilia twirled a strand of golden hair around her finger and said meaningfully, "So? Isn't this place wonderful? Is this your first time at such a high-class establishment?"

"...Of course not!" Alice pouted, her face flushing as she said, "I come to places like this all the time during my travels."

"Keep bragging. Only nobles get invited in here," Cecilia covered her mouth and let out a string of laughter. "But don't worry — you're benefiting from this lady's favor. Enjoy yourself to your heart's content. Ohoho~"

"Tch!"

Alice clicked her tongue in annoyance. She thought that Cecilia and Arnold were cut from the same cloth, always showing off their wealth in subtle ways without even realizing it. Was this a common illness among noble offspring?

"I'm not bluffing. Back when I was at the Vatican, there was a holy spring ten times more luxurious than this, far more comfortable. Hmph~!"

"Holy spring?" Cecilia furrowed her delicate brows in surprise. "Isn't that a place only the Heroes of past generations could bathe in before battle? Even the Pope can't use it casually."

The Holy Spring was an extremely sacred place in the Vatican, a must-visit stop for pilgrims, with a long history and rich religious significance.

Whenever a Hero undertook a crusade against the demon race, they would bathe there once, symbolizing the washing away of filth and sin to become a warrior of the Goddess of Light.

Its importance rivaled that of the Goddess of Light Temple. Even the Pope couldn't bathe there, which showed just how highly the Holy Church regarded the Holy Spring.

Legend held that the Holy Spring was born from the saliva of the Goddess of Light, imbued with some Divine Power. Pilgrims would reverently take a sip each time they passed by.

It sounded a bit perverted — wasn't this basically forced communion with the bathwater of past Heroes?

What if one of those Heroes had a weird sense of humor and secretly peed in the spring...? "Cough!"

Alice, as the 233rd Hero, naturally had the right to bathe there once. She hadn't been bragging to Cecilia after all.

"It seems you know quite a bit. That's correct — I was indeed there... " Alice's face showed a hint of pride, then she added, "The Holy Spring is far more magnificent than this. No big deal."

"You are..." Cecilia paused, squinting her eyes as she asked, "You're a Hero?"

"..."

Alice hesitated noticeably. She was indeed a former Hero, but her reputation was rather terrible. If Cecilia found out, she might revoke everything.

So after much deliberation, Alice chose not to admit it.

"Just forget what I said earlier. I didn't say anything..."

"I knew you were bluffing. Just as I thought..." Cecilia wore an expression of understanding and continued, "Someone like you could never become a Hero. If you were as strong as Lord Merlin, I might believe it, but I suppose that'll never happen in this lifetime."

"Ugh!" Alice's face flushed red with anger. Her dream had been trampled by Cecilia, yet she couldn't even vent her frustration, which was infuriating.

"Don't worry. For Lord Merlin's sake, I won't mock you. As someone from the commoner class, you probably won't get to enjoy such luxury ever again. Isn't that a pity? Ohoho~" Cecilia covered her mouth and laughed heartily, feeling a strong sense of superiority.

Alice was somewhat angry. She truly was a Hero, but couldn't say so because of her bad reputation. The frustration of not being able to act cool was really annoying.

Cecilia hummed a tune and began washing herself, apparently planning to bathe together with Alice.

Watching the warm water trace along Cecilia's chest and flow into her bottomless, sexy valley, Alice subconsciously felt a wave of tension. *How big are they?! What did she eat growing up?!* Shirley's were also quite large, probably because she got plenty of nutrition as a child. Alice had completely lost at the starting line.

Alice naively believed that the gap between rich and poor was reflected in breast size. Remembering what she ate while training with her master as a child —

Wild beast jerky, sweet potatoes, yams. If she hadn't grown into a flat-chest, she'd have let the people down.

*Master, I hate you!!!*

Alice sighed inwardly to express her imbalance.

After finishing her wash, Cecilia came over to the hot spring. Afraid of the heat, she first dipped her toes in to test the temperature, then quickly pulled them back like she'd been electrocuted.

Cecilia's delicate body trembled like a sieve. She felt somewhat uncomfortable and gave the hot spring a look of distaste, hesitating about whether to enter.

"What kind of reaction is that?" Alice turned around in surprise and looked at Cecilia. Wasn't this a perfectly normal temperature? Can't even handle this kind of heat? Are you a child or something?

"...Who's a child here!" Cecilia retorted indignantly. *Alice can endure it, so why can't I?! I can't be looked down upon by a commoner.*

Driven by competitive spirit, Cecilia gritted her teeth and forced her way into the artificial hot spring.

The still water surface immediately rippled, ring upon ring...

Cecilia's face turned red. After enduring for a while, she finally adapted to the temperature and began to enjoy it.

"Ah~ I feel reborn..."

Alice said nothing and slightly increased the distance between herself and Cecilia. The reaction was unusually awkward.

"Hmm!?"

Cecilia sensed something微妙 and glanced at Alice beside her.

Seeing her pretending not to notice, one hand covering her flat-as-a-board chest, with a faint blush on her face, Cecilia immediately understood what was going on.

A smug smile spread across Cecilia's face. She pursed her lips and said something brutally honest:

"Heh~ really~..."

Although she said nothing aloud, her hatred for ** had already broken through the sky!

Alice's expression froze, looking a bit embarrassed.

Merlin would stare at Cecilia's chest like that?

Alice frowned, thinking what purpose? Wasn't it due to circumstances? How could she possibly get involved with Merlin otherwise?!

"It's not like that! Merlin doesn't like girls with good figures, he likes me, a rare resource! There are plenty of girls like you on the street!"

"How is that possible? Do you think I'm a three-year-old child?" Cecilia's smile grew wider, thinking if Alice were to disguise herself as a man, she would be indistinguishable from one, it was a miracle anyone could tell she was a girl!

"Hmph! Don't think you understand Merlin, I know him better than you." Alice said with a blush, her voice slightly shy, "You just met Merlin recently, we've known each other for a long time, I know him better...".

Alice's voice grew softer as she spoke, eventually becoming a whisper, probably because she was feeling guilty.

Moreover, saying such things was too shameful, Alice tried to emphasize her closeness to Merlin, but she was embarrassed herself.

"Is it just because you've known him for a long time? What's so great about that?" Cecilia's face turned red with anger.

"Nothing, it's just great, so what?" Alice narrowed her eyes, her tone provocative.

"...". Cecilia frowned, her voice turning sour, "Don't use such childish provocation, I won't fall for it."

Alice maintained a haughty posture, wanting to completely dispel Cecilia's unrealistic thoughts, "Merlin isn't interested in you anyway! So, don't like him with unfounded hopes."

"Who said I like Merlin?" Cecilia asked, frowning.

"Eh?!" Alice was taken aback, asking curiously, "Don't you?"

"That's admiration, I admire Merlin, admiration and liking are different, don't you know that?" Cecilia looked at Alice with interest.

"...". Alice thought for a moment, recalling Elgin, the great swordsman, what were her feelings for him? Were they similar to Cecilia's admiration? But she had never experienced such a feeling with a man before...

"Besides, I have someone I like..." Cecilia said, twirling her hair around her finger, showing a bit of a girl's shyness.

Cecilia looked at Alice, also wanting to share secrets with another girl, it wasn't comfortable keeping it inside.

"I'll tell you... it's not that I won't, but you have to promise not to tell anyone else."

"Don't worry, my mouth is tight," Alice's curiosity was piqued, her hair fluffing up like a dog's tail.

"...the person I like..."

Just as Cecilia was about to speak, a sudden change occurred-

A team of dark elves assassins suddenly dropped down, holding gleaming curved daggers, intent on taking Alice's life.

The cold wind arrived, five assassins in black cloaks moved swiftly, their high-level fighting spirit blending together seamlessly, a perfect team assassination術.

Although a magician-sword user with both magic and martial arts might be troublesome in a direct confrontation, this was a sneak attack, and the assassins had the advantage of a kill.

Moreover, the team members were all high-level, with the buff of team assassination, Alice was already a dead person in their eyes.

If it were before, Alice would have been unaware of the danger, stupidly waiting to be killed.

However, after consuming the inheritance crystal of the Frost Saint Dragon, Alice now had the talent of the dragon, her perception and reaction speed sufficient to cope with the sudden sneak attack!
