Those sharp ice thorns stood upright, threatening the assassins, apparently making this sneak attack much more difficult.

The series of responses happened in an instant!

Alice's strength had qualitatively improved under Merlin's training and the effect of the inheritance crystal!

The assassins in mid-air couldn't help but frown, surprised and thinking-

Damn!

How did they discover us?!

Alice’s instantly constructed defense directly obstructed the nameless assassins’ plan.

Forcing the kill might still succeed, but they would be impaled by sharp ice spikes, resulting in a mutually destructive outcome—hardly worth the cost. So the assassins tacitly withdrew their offensive, choosing not to recklessly engage Alice. Instead, they landed on the open ground of the hot spring.

She scrutinized the group of mysterious figures before her, feeling a faint pressure.

Even for Alice, facing so many high-tier opponents made victory difficult.

Cecilia finally snapped out of her daze, furrowing her delicate brows as she demanded in the haughty tone of a noble lady, “Who are you?! How dare you trespass on private grounds?! Who gave you the audacity?!”

“Heh heh heh…” One of the assassins let out a series of cold laughs, his voice sinister. “There’s nowhere we cannot go—and this place is no exception.”

“You—!” Cecilia seethed, nearly losing her temper and cursing aloud.

Though their attire already screamed trouble, she found the audacity of storming a women’s hot spring the most despicable! They were assassins in name, but in reality, no better than thugs.

“Who are you?!” Alice asked gravely, wanting to understand the situation. Launching such a vicious attack right off the bat made no sense.

“No comment!”

The assassin snarled, drawing his curved blade and assuming an attacking stance.

“—Move out, finish this quickly!”

The other four assassins raised their own curved blades, adopting eerie, synchronized postures—like some kind of formation designed for assassination!

Alice swiftly drew the slender sword “Hymn of Light” from beside the hot spring, tightening the towel around herself to prevent any accidental exposure during the upcoming fight.

She always carried a weapon with her, even while bathing—unlike Merlin, who carelessly tossed his life-dependent weapons aside without a second thought.

Actually, Alice should be grateful to Merlin. If she hadn’t constantly worried about him barging in to take advantage while she bathed, she wouldn’t have developed the habit of keeping a weapon on her at all times.

Alice pointed her sharp, elegant pure-silver sword at the nameless assassins. Her magic and fighting spirit alternated, her high-tier pressure rising steadily. A faint dragon’s might began to emanate, subtly instilling fear in her enemies.

Her expression remained stern, a drop of cold sweat sliding down her forehead—as if under pressure.

Since consuming the Legacy Crystal, she hadn’t truly fought anyone yet. Now, the opportunity had arrived.

But facing five high-tier opponents all at once was no wonder she felt the strain.

“Cecilia, stay back. Don’t get caught in the crossfire.”

“…I can fight too!” Cecilia protested stubbornly, worried she’d be dead weight.

“How is a priest supposed to fight? You’re not a combat-oriented priest.” Alice’s forehead sprouted three black lines, her expression turning unnatural. She felt that now was not the time for the healer to jump in and cause chaos.

“…” Cecilia faltered. It seemed she really didn’t know any offensive skills. She could only say, “Then… then I’ll support you from behind with buffs.”

“Do as you like.”

Seeing Cecilia’s insistence, Alice stopped arguing and instead focused on the enemies before her.

The five assassins moved, ghost-like, their approach not concentrated on a single point but spread out.

This team assassination strategy resembled a wolf pack toying with a resistant prey—highly stable, ensuring no crisis arose during the kill.

First, everyone would harass the prey, draining its stamina. Once exhausted, they would swarm and finish it off.

This hunting method applied perfectly to assassination, leaving the target doubting life itself, powerless to resist.

Alice gripped her slender sword, letting down the silver hair coiled atop her head. It spun as it cascaded down, gleaming like premium silk—breathtakingly beautiful.

Cecilia cast multiple buffs on Alice in succession. Without her staff, the effects weren’t optimal, but it was better than nothing.

At the very least, she wouldn’t just be a bystander, looking completely useless. What could she do? She was a priest, after all.

“Intermediate Strength Amplification.”

“Intermediate Magic Amplification.”

“Intermediate Defense Amplification.”

“Intermediate Agility Amplification.”

“Intermediate Blessing of the Light Priestess.”

Instantly, Alice was enveloped in multicolored halos. In a short time, Cecilia had stacked multiple amplification buffs on her.

Her abilities in every aspect surged significantly. She could clearly feel the sudden influx of power raging violently within her.

Alice flexed her hand slightly. It wasn’t the first time she’d experienced buffs.

Though Cecilia was only an intermediate priest, the quality of her buffs was decent. It seemed she wasn’t entirely a useless noble lady after all.

Cecilia, standing behind, couldn’t help but show concern in her eyes. Alice was only high-tier—could she really handle five opponents of the same level? Should she call for help from Kael and Lord Merlin?

Her intentions were good, but the only path to the hot spring was blocked by the assassins. Apart from Alice, she truly had no one else to rely on.

Whooshing winds approached as the nameless assassins swung their curved blades, creating whirlwinds, each wave higher than the last.

Their movements were eerie, every detail executed to perfection, their coordination flawless. They were determined to slay Alice here and now!

The shadows beneath their black robes obscured Alice’s vision, yet her mind remained calm.

Trained under Merlin, even in the face of death, Alice could stay composed.

Was it an illusion?

The assassins’ speed seemed slow to her, easily tracked. She could predict each of their next moves.

In truth, the elite assassins’ speed was far from slow—it was Alice’s current strength, though high-tier, that had already far surpassed these so-called assassination elites.

Thus, she found their speed lacking. In Cecilia’s eyes, however, the assassins moved with terrifying swiftness, their ghost-like shadows darting chaotically.

Magic surged, and a biting gale of ice and snow swept forth.

Facing the relentless high-tier assassins, Alice responded with ease.

With a flick of her hand, “Thorn of Ice” transformed into two long whips, lashing out at incredible speed!

The casting speed and power caught the assassins off guard. They had no time to evade.

Four of them were sent crashing to the ground, pummeled by the ice-blue thorns—cracking and snapping as their skin split and blood flowed, their pained screams echoing.

“Alice, watch out above!” Cecilia couldn’t help but shout a warning.

Turns out, one clever assassin had slipped through the net. While his comrades distracted Alice, he had hidden above, descending from the sky in a surprise aerial strike!

The assassin’s curved blade gleamed with a cold light, his fighting spirit surging as he slashed down toward Alice’s throat!

Alice didn’t need Cecilia’s warning. Her dragon-race-enhanced perception had already detected the descending enemy.

She wielded her slender sword, tracing a beautiful arc of swordplay. Her attack speed far outpaced the aerial assassin.

Blades and sword clashed in a flurry. The slender sword’s thrusts were as fast as lightning. Alice cleanly pierced the assassin’s throat, blooming a grotesquely beautiful crimson flower.

The assassin clutched his gushing neck, his face filled with disbelief, collapsing in a pool of blood amid terror and confusion.

Alice glanced at her slender sword, then flicked it sharply, cleaning off the blood. She calmly remarked,

“You all…

“are this weak?”

…are this weak?

title: Chapter 32
content:
Chapter 32

Volume 7 · Chapter 32

Alice furrowed her delicate brows, the feeling of intense discomfort growing stronger and stronger, yet she felt no pressure at all.

Although the enemies greatly outnumbered them, Alice felt no tension whatsoever.

She thought these people, who were also high-ranking assassins like herself, were a bit weak.

She had originally thought these people would be powerful and that the fight would be stressful, but instead she found herself surprised.

Her abilities in every aspect were far superior to the enemy's!

Even though they were all high-ranking, the gap in strength was not minor.

Was it because her own strength had improved dramatically, making her far stronger than the enemy?

Alice finally realized, thinking that having Merlin as her sparring partner wasn't without its benefits.

Even though she was often teased by Merlin, her self-esteem repeatedly battered, she still gained something.

A hint of a smile crept across Alice's face as she finally experienced a sliver of the joy of dominating the weak.

No wonder Merlin always acted so lazily every day. It turned out he was in such a comfortable state every day!

Actually, Alice had misjudged Merlin. The joy of teasing the weak and mowing down grass had long since worn off for him, years ago.

"What a joke, I really underestimated you guys."

Cecilia's eyes widened in surprise as she looked at Alice, thinking, Alice was stronger than she had imagined. She had thought Alice would be in a tough fight, but this was surprisingly easy. Seems like I thought too much...

The remaining five assassins slowly got up from the ground, having been beaten for a while by the two "Ice Thorns," each sustaining different degrees of injury.

Looking at their fallen comrade pinned by a sword at the throat, the assassins' expressions were somewhat complicated. They finally understood that this mission was not simple, and Alice was not an ordinary high-ranker—far stronger than imagined, with an aura that seemed to be approaching the Saint-tier.

Several assassins thought Alice was unbeatable and very difficult to deal with, all of them harboring the same thought in their hearts.

Everyone is high-ranking, so why is there such a big gap?

These guys think too much. Alice still has a long way to go before reaching the Saint-tier. The key is the high bonus from the Frost Dragon's Legacy Crystal.

They thought they were facing a human, but actually they were facing someone who would eventually become a humanoid dragon.

As a superior race, dragons possess strength and spirit that are the pinnacle of all races.

With the blessing of draconic talent, it was no longer a fantasy for Alice to dominate her peers.

"Let's go! Kill this human woman!"

The four assassins pulled out spherical black projectiles and hurled them fiercely at the ground. Immediately, a thick black smoke billowed up, obscuring Alice's vision.

This smoke wasn't just for visual obstruction—it also contained toxins. If one stayed in it too long, their body would become numb, turning them into fish in a barrel.

However, with Cecilia the priestess present, the toxins weren't much of an issue.

"Intermediate Poison Resistance Amplification!"

Cecilia cast a buff on herself and Alice simultaneously, resisting the toxins in the smoke.

The assassins hid within the rolling black smoke, playing a sneak attack tactic to make up for the gap in strength.

But Alice had draconic senses. Even without seeing the assassins, she could clearly sense their positions.

Alice's high-ranking combat spirit and magical power surged, condensing a layer of ice crystals on the surface of her blade.

Looking at this stance, it seemed she was preparing to engage these assassins in close combat.

The black smoke spread rapidly, quickly swallowing Alice's figure and filling the entire female bathhouse.

Cecilia covered her mouth and nose, unable to see Alice's figure, feeling a bit uneasy.

Within the smoke, Alice held her slender sword, sensing the enemies hiding and waiting for an opportunity to strike. She knew they were not far from her.

"Come on, what are you waiting for?"

One assassin was the first to charge out of the smoke, wielding a cold, gleaming curved sword, rushing toward Alice with the target set on her vulnerable throat!

Alice's lithe body moved like a snow elf, retreating a step and counterattacking directly.

Her sharp high-ranking sword techniques came in rapid succession, like meteors cascading down, sending the assassin and her weapon crashing to the ground!

Alice's movements were graceful and fluid, and with the enhanced attack power from the ice crystals, the fight was like cutting through melon and slicing cabbage.

The assassins, seeing another comrade fall, seemed to realize that this approach wouldn't work. Like the Pea Pleasant Saving Grandpa, they attacked one by one.

If they didn't attack simultaneously, they might not be able to take down Alice at all.

Thus, the remaining three assassins charged out at once, their high-ranking combat spirit generating sharp winds, all attacking the expressionless Alice together.

Three sharp curved swords locked onto Alice's throat, their techniques vicious and ruthless, clearly honed through countless battles!

In a critical moment, Alice suddenly raised the hand holding her slender sword, instantly forming an "Ice Wall" to stubbornly withstand this fierce combined assault!

The three high-ranking combat spirits kept striking the ice wall, finally making Alice feel a sliver of pressure.

It seemed that if the assassins had attacked simultaneously from the start, they might not have suffered such heavy losses.

The battle entered a tense state, with cracks already forming on the ice wall, threatening to collapse at any moment.

A drop of cold sweat trickled down Alice's forehead. If she let things continue like this, the ice wall would surely be broken by the assassins.

To sit and wait for death was a dead end. She had to come up with a plan.

Alice infused her combat spirit into the ice wall, causing it to explode.

The shockwave from the explosion sent the assassins retreating in succession.

The essence of the snowy mountains proved effective at this crucial moment, making Alice delighted.

She didn't overthink it, quickly condensing nearly a hundred "Ice Crystal Swords" that floated in the air.

This was Alice's favored high-level magic, with excellent area-of-effect damage and control capabilities.

Alice swung her slender sword, and the hundred ice crystal swords in the air seemed to receive orders and shot out in unison!

The scene of a hundred arrows firing simultaneously was stunning, the swooshing sounds like a beautiful symphony.

The assassins couldn't react in time, their bodies pierced by the ice crystal swords, becoming riddled with holes, completely unable to defend themselves, their screams echoing.

Finally, the last two enemies were nailed to the ground, their fate sealed in silence.

Only one assassin, severely wounded with three ice swords embedded in his body, knelt on the ground, gasping for breath.

Of course, this was Alice's deliberate choice to leave a survivor, in order to extract the truth.

Throughout the entire battle, Cecilia hadn't seen a thing. She only knew that the black smoke had dispersed, and Alice had won.

The once-beautiful hot spring had turned into a hell filled with ice swords, the temperature so low that Cecilia's breath came out in white clouds, making her tighten her bath towel for warmth.

The cold air surrounded Alice, who held her slender sword, her silver hair fluttering slightly.

Behind her, several ice crystal swords floated and swayed, still unused.

At this moment, Alice's figure resembled a female war goddess, exuding an aura of invincibility.

Cecilia furrowed her brows, looking at Alice with amazement, thinking to herself—

Amazing.

Kael absolutely can't defeat her.

Is this guy really a high-ranker?

She's performing moves that look like Saint-tier...

title: Chapter 33 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 33 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 33

Cecilia's heart was filled with trepidation. She felt that since she wasn't yet a Saint-tier expert, she couldn't tell much from observation. But once one reached Saint-tier, they would surely be an extraordinary figure! And based on her current strength, stepping onto the threshold of Saint-tier was only a matter of time. Cecilia decided to be more restrained from now on and make fewer jokes about Alice's flat chest, lest she hold a grudge.

"......"

The sole surviving assassin coughed, blood spilling from his mouth and trickling down his chin. He had likely been impaled by ice swords through his internal organs.

The former assassination elite, with three ice swords protruding brutally from his back, looked as wretched as one could possibly look.

Alice slowly approached the assassin, her surrounding cold causing frost to form on the ground with every step she took.

The assassin struggled to lift his head and looked at Alice, his eyes filled with hatred and resentment. "You bastard!"

Alice ignored the assassin and reached out, tearing off his mask to reveal the true face of a dark elf.

Alice was confused. She had no idea why dark elves would come to assassinate her, especially since she didn't believe she had ever provoked the elf race.

"Why are dark elves trying to murder us?"

Cecilia stepped out of the hot spring and came to Alice's side to ask.

"I don't know either..." Alice furrowed her elegant brows and glared at the kneeling assassin, demanding, "Why did you come to assassinate us?! Who sent you?!"

"Heh......" The assassin gave a bitter smile, his pointed ears twitching. "You think I'd tell you? Keep dreaming!"

"You're in this condition and still won't cooperate!" Cecilia put her hands on her hips beside her, looking every bit a bully riding someone else's coattails.

"Pah!" The assassin spat out a mouthful of congealed blood, his attitude incredibly stubborn as he glared fiercely at Cecilia. "Even reduced to this state, you'll never get anything out of my mouth! Want to bet I can still kill you, little priestess?"

"..." Cecilia got a bit scared and quickly ducked behind Alice, then said bravely, "What's with the aggression? Try scaring me again and I'll have my maid beat you senseless!"

A few black veins appeared on Alice's forehead as she thought awkwardly: Who's your maid? She was treating me like a servant without any hesitation.

But Alice wasn't angry. She couldn't be bothered to argue with Cecilia and continued to look stern as she addressed the assassin.

"Mouth so tough? Are you sure you want to guard your secrets even unto death?"

"Hmph!" The assassin snorted, saying haughtily, "Forget it. I won't tell you anything. Don't think you can threaten me. Do what you will — kill or torture, go ahead!"

Alice flicked her finger, and the several ice crystal swords floating behind her instantly surrounded the assassin, circling around him as if ready to turn him into Swiss cheese at any moment.

The assassin's eyes widened, his mouth trembling as he couldn't speak.

The bone-chilling cold radiating from the ice swords made his body involuntarily shudder.

Watching the ice swords circling around him filled the assassin with utter terror, and cold sweat immediately broke out across his forehead.

"You're sure you won't talk? I'll give you one last chance." Alice controlled the ice crystal swords, delivering her final ultimatum with an obvious threatening tone.

"...I..."

The assassin hesitated, unwilling to answer, and changed the subject. "...You think threats will work on me?!"

"Tsk!" Alice clicked her tongue in dissatisfaction and flicked her finger again. The ice crystal swords immediately closed in near the assassin's neck, moments away from piercing through.

"I-I-I-I-.." The assassin tensed up, his expression terrified, his whole body shaking like a sieve.

"Will you talk or not?! What's the point of guarding secrets with your life? Isn't your employer more important than your own life?!" Cecilia played the good cop, earnestly saying, "Confess quickly and you'll get lenient treatment. Resist and it'll be severe!"

"You can only threaten me now. Once our captain arrives, none of you will survive!" The assassin blustered stubbornly, apparently believing he still had hope. Once their captain arrived, he was sure they'd be able to beat Alice to a pulp.

"Such a tough mouth! You're in this state and you're still counting on your captain?!" Cecilia sneered from the side, curling her lip. "Is your captain really that formidable?"

"He's definitely stronger than you! Beating you would be like beating kids!" The assassin declared firmly.

"Just brag all you want! Your strength can't even beat my maid, so what does it matter if your captain shows up?" Cecilia said triumphantly.

"I'm not your serv—" Alice muttered indignant under her breath.

"Don't be so pedantic. Aren't we trying to get information out of him?" Cecilia whispered back.

Alice frowned in silence. She didn't enjoy being taken advantage of by Cecilia.

"You frogs in a well have no idea what real power is!" The assassin grinned with a wicked smile and continued, "Our captain is carrying a Special Grade Dark Berserk Potion! His true strength is beyond your imagination!"

"Dark Berserk Potion!?"

Both girls gasped in surprise, their expressions stunned. They clearly knew what that substance was used for.

That's right! It was that forbidden drug that temporarily boosts combat power! Even though our captain is already high-tier, after drinking a Special Grade Potion, you can imagine the effect! Even Saint-tier experts can fight on equal terms against it!" The assassin spoke arrogantly, feeling that with his captain's Dark Berserk Potion, victory was assured.

Alice fell silent, thinking: She'd heard that regular Dark Berserk Potions were already impressive. What concept was Special Grade? After drinking it, one would probably become a war machine.

Even with a Dark Berserk Potion... so what? We... we wouldn't be afraid! " Cecilia's voice trembled slightly. She was certainly not unafraid.

"You'll pay for this! Right now our captain has already dealt with your male companions, and it's your turn next!" A smug smile spread across the assassin's face, feeling that the situation wasn't problematic at all.

The two girls glanced at each other, and their expressions suddenly relaxed.

"Go find Merlin——" Cecilia murmured to herself.

"Then there's nothing to worry about. Their captain is definitely dead." Alice said calmly.

"Huh!?" The assassin's eyes widened. Their reaction was off, so he quickly continued to spread terror, "Aren't you afraid?! Our captain after drinking the Dark Berserk Potion is an invincible existence! Anyone can be easily killed! Even Saint-tier experts struggle to confront him head-on! And besides, your male companions are just one high-tier spearmen and a村民 with no utility. How can you possibly compare——"

"Oh, and then what?" Alice gave him a somewhat pitying look.

"Hurry up and release me right now! Otherwise I'll make sure you two die gruesomely! If our captain goes berserk, even I get scared! You might not even have intact corpses!!!" The assassin said viciously.

BOOM!

A tremendous explosion echoed as the barrier between the male and female hot springs was shattered.

Immediately after, a dark shadow zoomed past and crashed into the opposite wall.

Dust billowed everywhere.

The two girls looked terrified, having no idea what had happened.

When the dust settled, they could finally see what had come flying.

It was none other than the dark assassin captain who had drunk the Dark Potion. His body was covered in explosive, muscular curves, resembling a black giant.

But at this moment, the assassin captain appeared to have suffered severe injuries — his entire abdomen was caved in, which was quite terrifying.

His whole body was embedded in the wall, striking the ridiculous pose of the Snake-Style Deadly Hand, eyes rolling back, red tongue lolling out. He was clearly unconscious.

"What is this?" Alice muttered, finding it hard to recognize this as a dark elf.

The half-kneeling assassin's expression at this moment was incredibly vivid, terrified as if he'd seen a ghost, his mouth hanging open and unable to close.

Though their captain had changed drastically after drinking the potent potion, he was still recognizable — and he'd already been beaten to death.

Oh my god!

Isn't that our captain?!

How could he already be dead?!

And beaten into the ridiculous Snake-Style Deadly Hand pose!!!

The assassin member was so shocked he couldn't speak. His last lifeline was gone instantly. Wasn't he going to end up kneeling here too?!

"Oh! Alice, are you two okay?" Merlin walked over from the male hot spring side wrapped in a towel, with Kyle following behind him.

"What happened over there...?" Alice furrowed her brows, looking at Merlin, unable to grasp the situation.

"Nothing much. A few dark elves who came to pick up soap just showed up." Merlin said nonchalantly. He then suddenly noticed the surviving assassin on the ground. "Hmm? There's a survivor?"

"Ugh!" The surviving assassin shuddered all over and threw himself face-down on the ground in an instant, his face pressed flat against the floor.

"Have mercy, noble sir!" ε(TT_Tτ)3

title: Chapter 34 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 34 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 34

The surviving assassin knelt in a standard posture, prostrate on the ground, his body trembling with fear. Although he didn't understand how his team leader had died, he realized that his own lifeline was now gone. Seeing his team leader had died even after drinking a high-grade Dark Frenzy potion, it proved that Merlin or Kail's strength was not weak, and definitely not someone he could defeat. This was a recipe for disaster, and he decided to surrender quickly.

The assassin had made up his mind and dared not resist or shout anymore, prioritizing saving his life. "Huh? What's going on?" Merlin was taken aback, thinking to himself, "What am I doing? Why am I so scared?" "Nothing, don't mind...," Alice said resignedly, thinking that this outcome was already expected.

Cecilia saw Kail and felt a surge of anger. She walked up to him and scolded, "Why did you arrive so late? I was in danger, and you're supposed to be useful!" "...I'm very sorry, Cecilia-sama. As you can see, we were also attacked where we were," Kail said with an awkward smile, scratching his head. "Ha! My safety should be the top priority, shouldn't it?" Cecilia played the role of a spoiled young lady to the extreme.

"Sorry, but we couldn't easily leave our post either...," Kail said with a bitter smile, feeling helpless about the situation. If it weren't for Merlin, he would have been in a precarious position. "Seriously, I'm going to deduct your salary for this month!" Cecilia said angrily. "...This...," Kail said, looking bitter, wanting to argue that it wasn't fair, but not daring to speak up.

"Did you cause trouble for Merlin again?" Cecilia asked seriously. "I did add a bit of trouble...," Kail said, a drop of cold sweat trickling down his forehead. He thought he hadn't been needed at all and had only been a spectator, but still felt like he had caused trouble.

Cecilia was a bit angry, feeling that Kail had caused trouble for Merlin, which was her responsibility as his master. She began to lecture Kail. Now, Merlin was Cecilia's VIP guest, and if she didn't provide good service, their future cooperation would be affected. Generally, Saint-tier strong individuals had peculiar temperaments, and it was hard to find cooperative partners.

Merlin didn't pay attention to Cecilia's scolding but asked Alice, "By the way, you're not hurt? That's quite...". "You were hoping I'd get hurt, weren't you?!" Alice retorted angrily, feeling that Merlin's words were unkind. "No, I just thought you'd be defeated by the enemy or get into a tough fight," Merlin said, looking at the four corpses on the ground.

"Don't underestimate me!" Alice said with a sniff, "As long as I don't meet a Saint-tier strong individual, I'm still quite powerful." Merlin raised an eyebrow, thinking that they were both like chickens pecking at each other, and Alice was being smug for no reason. "It seems...taking stimulants and training does work...," Merlin said.

"Nothing to do with you, it's because I'm a genius! My comprehension is superb, so I made rapid progress! Hmph!" Alice didn't want to admit that her improvement was related to Merlin, as if acknowledging it would mean she was inferior to Merlin. "Every time you get arrogant, I feel like pounding you...," Merlin said expressionlessly.

"Uh...," Alice had several drops of sweat on her forehead, sensing a domestic violence vibe. "However, you did leave a live one, which is good. I'll give you some praise," Merlin said, looking at the assassin kneeling on the ground. "I don't need your praise...," Alice said resentfully.

Merlin didn't continue to talk to Alice but asked the assassin on the ground, "Hey, you...". "Y-yes, sir," the assassin replied, terrified, with cold sweat on his forehead like he had just washed his face with water. "I have a few questions for you. Answer truthfully, or you'll meet the same end as your companions. You understand what I mean, right?" Merlin said concisely.

"Yes, I understand," the assassin replied, nodding like a chicken pecking at rice. Although he felt Merlin was an ordinary person, he thought he couldn't afford to offend anyone now, as everyone seemed to be a powerful figure. "Why did you, as a dark elf, suddenly attack us? I don't recall offending the elves," Merlin said.

"A-ah...we were ordered by someone else. Actually, we were just following orders and didn't mean to provoke you. Please, have mercy and spare my life!" The assassin begged, hands clasped together, with a pleading expression on his face. "Spare you? It's not impossible, but it depends on your performance...," Merlin said with a meaningful expression, hinting at something.

"I'll definitely tell the truth. If I lie...I'll die a terrible death!" The assassin said, his sweat dripping profusely, with an extremely devout expression. Alice looked at Merlin with complex eyes, thinking that his method of combining kindness and severity was quite familiar, as if he had experience in interrogation.

As the Great Demon Lord, Merlin definitely had experience with this, having many subordinates under him. Without some skills, it would be hard to control them. "Then tell me, who sent you? Who's the mastermind behind this?" Merlin asked again.

"...", the assassin began to hesitate, but thought that if he revealed Samuel, he would be in trouble. "Say, if you don't, you'll die here right now," Merlin said, his eyes narrowing, with an obvious threat.

Those ruby-like eyes were filled with an eerie feeling, like those of a high-ranking ruler looking down on grass. There was no mercy, and it seemed like he would kill at any moment, filling people with a sense of fear. Alice stood beside him, not saying a word, as she had seen Merlin's emotionless gaze before.

When they first met, Merlin had the same gaze when annihilating the 100,000-strong Crusade Army, as if he was accustomed to slaughter and had become numb to it. Alice reminded herself not to be deceived, as Merlin was a demon, despite his human-like words and actions. The assassin trembled, showing his fear, and swallowed his saliva.

He thought that if he didn't tell, he would die on the spot. But if he revealed Samuel, he would also be doomed. However, he could try to escape from London and maybe save his life. The assassin made a decision in this extreme situation, choosing to survive for now. "I'll say! I...it's Samuel-sama who ordered us to assassinate you!"

title: Chapter 35
content:
Chapter 35

Volume 7 · Chapter 35

The surviving assassin spoke under immense pressure, uttering the name Samuel.

This name was clearly known to Alice and Merlin, and they both froze in surprise.

"Samuel..." Merlin furrowed his brow, feeling that the situation was becoming complicated.

"Isn't he the ambassador of the elf tribe?" Alice muttered, recalling that she had just sent Sherry to the elf tribe's embassy earlier that day.

The two exchanged a glance, and it was clear that they both had doubts.

"Are you serious?" Merlin looked down at the assassin, his tone threatening. "If you're lying, you're dead."

"Absolutely, I swear!" The assassin was afraid Merlin wouldn't believe him, and quickly said, "We're indeed part of Samuel's assassination team!"

"Hmm?" Merlin raised an eyebrow and continued to question, "Why did you try to kill us? We have no grudge against Samuel."

"...I don't know," the assassin was sweating profusely, and said in terror, "We're not authorized to know some big secrets. If I tell a lie, I'll die a terrible death!"

Merlin didn't say anything, but he understood this approach, it was normal.

Some secrets were impossible for subordinates to know, and their job was simply to execute orders.

Merlin glanced at Alice beside him and asked softly.

"Alice, what do you think?"

"Why would Samuel target us?" Alice frowned, also puzzled by this matter. "We haven't done anything bad, nor have we offended Samuel. Logically, we even helped them by sending their princess back."

"That's right, but Samuel did send people to kill us, and even dispatched an assassination team, which is unreasonable," Merlin stroked his chin, feeling that things weren't that simple.

"Could there be some misunderstanding?" Alice tentatively made a guess.

"What kind of misunderstanding could make them want to kill us? We don't seem to have done anything too excessive, unless counting my complaint about the elf tribe's cuisine as a reason, which would be too humorous," Merlin shrugged, feeling that the situation was somewhat inexplicable.

Alice fell into thought, thinking that it was abnormal for them to be targeted by the elf tribe's ambassador, and she felt that there was some secret lurking before her eyes, but she couldn't grasp it.

"Could it be because we sent Sherry back?" Merlin looked at Alice, wanting to know her thoughts.

"Eh!" Alice was taken aback, feeling that there was a possibility. They had just sent Sherry back to the embassy, and they were assassinated that night, and it was hard to believe that there was no connection.

"Or maybe Samuel... is a bad person?" Merlin narrowed his eyes and boldly expressed his idea.

Alice's eyes widened in surprise. Although Merlin was just making a wild guess, it wasn't impossible.

If it was really as Merlin suspected, wouldn't Sherry be in danger?

Alice became anxious, as she had always treated Sherry like a little sister and didn't want anything to happen to her.

"Merlin...".

"Hmm?" Merlin looked at Alice in surprise.

"We'll put off going to Dover Strait for now, and go to the elf tribe's embassy tomorrow to ask what's going on," Alice said seriously. If Samuel was a dangerous person, she definitely wouldn't leave Sherry behind.

Merlin raised his eyelids, thought for a moment, and felt that if Sherry had something happen to her, his 100,000 gold coin reward would also be gone.

So, after weighing the pros and cons, Merlin nodded and responded seriously.

"Alright, I was thinking the same."

"Let's go to the elf tribe's embassy tomorrow!"

...

Later that night.

Elf tribe's embassy.

The luxurious corridor was dark, with only the crimson floor stretching out.

Countless unknown oil paintings hung on both sides, many of which were honorary figures of the elf tribe.

Sharan held a candle and led the way, her expression unnatural under her dark skin.

Samuel wore a dressing gown and followed closely behind, looking a bit unhappy, seemingly woken up from sleep.

The two walked quickly, one in front of the other, towards the meeting room.

"What is it? So urgent, I was just about to sleep," Samuel's tone had a hint of anger, clearly not happy about being disturbed from rest.

"Very sorry, Samuel, Sharp said there was something important to discuss with you and hoped you'd go to the meeting room immediately," Sharan explained patiently, her pace not slowing down.

"Important matter?" Samuel furrowed his brow and asked curiously, "What is it?"

"I haven't had a chance to ask, Sharp looked anxious to see you, so I came over right away," Sharan said with an apology.

Samuel didn't ask any further questions, thinking that Sharp must have something important to discuss, otherwise, he wouldn't disturb him so late.

The two turned several corners, walked dozens of steps, and finally arrived at the meeting room of the embassy.

Sharan quickly extinguished the candle in her hand, walked a few steps, and helped Samuel open the door to the meeting room.

"Samuel, please come in, Sharp has been waiting for a long time."

Samuel nodded and entered the meeting room.

Sharan also glanced around cautiously, making sure there were no unauthorized people around, before closing the meeting room door.

The meeting room was spacious, but the lighting was dim, and only the faint candlelight allowed them to see things.

Sharp sat on a chair, sipping red tea, his expression serious, as if he had many worries.

When Samuel arrived, Sharp's pointed ears moved, and he quickly stood up and bowed slightly.

"Samuel...".

Samuel walked in front of Sharp, looked at his anxious expression, and asked seriously, "What's so urgent that you had to see me?"

"This..." Sharp glanced to the side, and it turned out that there was another person.

A person wearing a black robe, with several wounds on his body, and an extremely terrified expression, it was none other than the surviving assassin.

After learning the reason, Merlin and Alice really did let this assassin go, not taking his life.

This made the assassin extremely happy, and he directly started his escape route.

But this assassin was a bit unlucky. He had just escaped London when he ran into Sharp, who was inspecting the 「Elf's Lament」 magic circle.

The two locked eyes, and everything was silent, and the poor surviving assassin was caught by Sharp.

The surviving assassin was bound and kneeling on the ground, shivering with fear, feeling that he was doomed this time. Samuel was always ruthless and wouldn't let him off.

"Samuel, our assassination team was completely wiped out, and only this guy survived," Sharp stated briefly.

Samuel instantly understood the situation, his eyes widening in shock, and muttered.

"...".

"Our entire assassination team was annihilated!"

title: Chapter 36 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 36 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 36

Samuel’s simple account sent a shockwave through Cecilia, leaving her struggling to believe it.

"Seriously?"

"It’s true. The entire team was wiped out." Sharplon nodded, looking rather gloomy.

Cecilia glanced at the surviving assassin kneeling on the ground, his disheveled state convincing her about seventy to eighty percent.

It seemed her meticulously assembled elite assassination squad had truly been annihilated—only one useless survivor remained!

But Cecilia couldn’t understand it. Those two adventurers weren’t powerful at all—just a High-Rank Spellblade and some irrelevant Black Iron villager.

Her dark elf subordinates were all High-Rank. Killing those two fools should have been effortless.

Yet the result left Cecilia utterly stunned, unable to fathom how her subordinates had perished.

"How is that possible? Those two were weak. The strongest was just a High-Rank Spellblade. Our assassins were all High-Rank. Is it that hard to kill a Spellblade together?" Salan couldn’t hold back anymore and directly questioned Sharplon, convinced he was lying.

"It’s absolutely true. This man admitted it himself. No lie. When I found him, he was trying to flee London to escape responsibility for the mission’s failure." Sharplon looked at the kneeling assassin, his tone heavy with implication.

The surviving assassin, realizing he was being singled out, looked utterly terrified.

Cold sweat poured down him like a burst dam, and he repeatedly kowtowed—

"S-Spare me! Great Cecilia! Please don’t feed me to the ghouls!"

"I failed the mission... I’m deeply sorry. Please give me another chance!"

"I’ve followed you for nearly a hundred years! If not for my merits, then for my hard work!"

"You worthless piece of trash! You botched the job and still dare beg for mercy? You’re asking for death!" Salan pointed at the assassin, and Saint-tier magic surged, condensing into a pitch-black, flickering sphere of light. It looked like she was about to kill the useless man on the spot.

Sharplon remained completely calm, narrowing his eyes and staying silent, showing no intention of stopping her. After all, this was normal—failure demanded consequences. Otherwise, how could Great Cecilia maintain her authority?

"S-Spare me...!" The assassin’s face turned deathly pale, and he scrambled backward, but bound as he was, there was no escape.

"Stop." Cecilia finally spoke, pressing Salan’s arm down.

"Great Cecilia, this man deserves to die! There’s no need to show mercy to such a failure." Salan furrowed her delicate brows, clearly puzzled by Cecilia’s actions.

"Yes, Great Cecilia. Now is not the time for mercy. This man failed your mission and even tried to flee. If we don’t kill him, how will we maintain order?" Sharplon agreed with Salan. Reward and punishment had to be clear.

"I know. Calm down for now..." Cecilia slightly closed her eyes, speaking lightly in a way that made it impossible to guess her thoughts.

"Great Cecilia!" Salan and Sharplon protested in unison, both feeling that sparing the failure was inappropriate.

"Shut up! Do you want to rebel?!" Cecilia’s brows shot up as she roared at her two trusted aides. "Who exactly is in charge here? Do I need your permission for every little thing I do?!"

"No..." Salan suppressed her dissatisfaction and slightly lowered her head in a show of respect.

Sharplon, seeing Cecilia’s outburst, also fell silent, worried about being punished.

"Hmph!" Cecilia let out a cold snort, then looked at the trembling assassin on the ground. "Don’t worry. I won’t feed you to the ghouls. After all, you’re my old subordinate."

"T-Thank you, Great Cecilia! Thank you so much!" The assassin wept with joy, pressing his forehead to the ground, unwilling to lift it. The rollercoaster from hell to heaven was just too intense.

He felt incredibly lucky. He never expected Great Cecilia to be in a good mood today and spare his worthless life. Normally, failures were fed to the ghouls—yet she had spared him!

The assassin was so overwhelmed with gratitude toward Cecilia that he didn’t know what to say, completely in a state of groveling worship.

"I have a few questions for you. Since the entire assassination team was wiped out, how did you escape?" Cecilia asked curiously.

"..." The assassin hesitated, thinking to himself that he couldn’t reveal how he had betrayed his comrades.

"...I saw the captain was already dead, and the situation looked bad, so I ran for my life and barely escaped from them!"

"I know running was wrong, but I was scared. Please forgive my sin, Great Cecilia."

Sharplon and Salan both looked displeased, as if they wanted to kill this shameless failure. He had truly disgraced the dark elves!

But since Cecilia seemed intent on sparing the failed assassin, they, as her subordinates, could do nothing.

"The assassination captain is dead?" Cecilia knitted her brows and continued questioning. "If I recall correctly, he was carrying an extremely concentrated, top-grade Dark Frenzy Potion, right? His true combat power could rival a Saint-tier warrior. How could he have been defeated so easily?"

"It’s what I saw with my own eyes! The captain drank the Frenzy Potion, but he was still killed!" The assassin said, trembling in fear.

"That can’t be. Your targets were just a High-Rank Spellblade and a Black Iron villager. How did it come to this? Is that Spellblade some kind of celestial being?!" Cecilia’s voice was icy, her anger quietly brewing.

"Great Cecilia, we split into two teams. The captain went after the Black Iron villager, and we... we went after the Spellblade. That Spellblade was really strong. Five of us attacked together, and only I survived." The assassin spoke nervously.

"What? Five High-Rank assassins couldn’t handle one High-Rank Spellblade? Are you joking? Are you all just useless eaters?!" The more Cecilia asked, the angrier she got. How pathetic could they be? Five against one, and four were killed in return. Did they even know how to fight?!

"V-Very sorry, Great Cecilia! That High-Rank Spellblade was extraordinary! Even though we were all High-Rank, we weren’t on the same level at all. The more we fought, the more we realized the gap was..." The assassin looked despondent. It wasn’t that they were weak—it was that the Spellblade was abnormal, far stronger than a normal High-Rank.

Cecilia was deeply puzzled, feeling that the surviving subordinate wouldn’t lie. Had she underestimated that Spellblade?

"So, the assassination captain was also taken out by that High-Rank Spellblade?"

The assassin lowered his head, stammering, "It... it seems it was the Black Iron villager who did it..."

"...What?" Cecilia froze for a few seconds, then her mind was filled with nothing but question marks.

The assassin captain, who had taken the potion, was killed by a Black Iron villager...

Excuse me?

title: Chapter 37 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 37 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 37

Although the surviving assassin also found it incredible,

The captain, who had taken the potion, had astonishing combat power, rivalling that of a Saint-tier.

How could a lowly black iron adventurer possibly defeat him?

But that was exactly what had happened. The captain seemed to have been crushed, his face frozen in terror as he died.

The surviving assassin lay prone on the ground, trembling with fear, hardly daring to breathe.

Observers Shalan and Sharpuren exchanged disbelieving glances, both finding it hard to credit.

They thought that this kind of battle between an ant and an elephant was completely one-sided, and black iron adventurers were insignificant trash.

Only secret silver-level adventurers like Shalan and Sharpuren were worthy of their notice.

Samuel's expression was blank, as if he had just heard the biggest joke in the world.

"How could this be?" he thought.

He knew the power contained in that bottle of special dark potion, which could increase a person's combat power to an unbelievable level.

It was ridiculous that it had been defeated by a mere black iron adventurer.

"Are you trying to fool me like a child? How can I believe such an absurd thing?

"I think this waste isn't honest, let's kill him," Shalan's expression turned ferocious, and she felt an urge to throw the surviving assassin to feed the ghouls and listen to his pleasant screams.

"You fool, do you think we're idiots? It's a waste of Samuel's kindness!" Sharpuren couldn't help but apply pressure, thinking that at this point, the old man still dared to talk nonsense, probably because he had never died.

Faced with the overwhelming pressure, the surviving assassin was frightened, his pupils dilating and constricting, and cold sweat spreading across his pale face.

"I'm telling the truth, Samuel, please believe me! My loyalty is sworn to heaven, and I would never lie to deceive you!"

A guy who wanted to escape after failing a mission, talking about loyalty?

Samuel shook his head, exasperated.

"Fine, just go to hell and reflect on yourself."

"Eh?" The surviving assassin suddenly froze, and said dazedly, "You... you just said you wouldn't kill me."

"I only promised not to throw you to feed the ghouls, but I never promised you would live. Moreover, the price of failing a mission is to atone with your life - that's the rule."

Samuel narrowed his eyes, and his ferocious gaze completely destroyed his saintly appearance.

"Samuel... please give me another chance! Have mercy on me..." The surviving assassin was extremely frightened, his body shaking like a leaf, and his breathing was very heavy.

"Enough, die." Samuel was too lazy to talk to the waste anymore, and directly snapped his fingers.

The conference room suddenly had a strong wind, and several wind blades attacked,

The magic driven by Saint-tier magic power was very destructive.

The surviving assassin let out a scream from his throat, but before he could finish speaking, he was directly torn to pieces by the wind blades, turning into a puddle of flesh, and the scene was extremely bloody.

Shalan couldn't help but laugh twice, seemingly enjoying the bloody scene, and felt great pleasure when she saw the waste be killed by Samuel.

Sharpuren smiled faintly, thinking that killing an unfaithful guy was not important, and he approved of Samuel's iron-fisted approach.

Samuel's unhappy mood was slightly relieved, and he fell into thought, pondering the next thing.

Sharpuren looked at Samuel and asked,

"Samuel, what should we do now?"

"The assassination team leader should have been killed by that high-level magic swordsman. We should find a way to deal with him."

Samuel said with a frown.

"Samuel, if the assassination team leader really drank the frenzied potion, he could fight a Saint-tier strongman. I think it's not normal for a high-level magic swordsman to defeat him," Sharpuren said tactfully.

"Maybe we underestimated the magic swordsman's strength. Just looking at her adventurer certificate, there are many doubts. It's not impossible that she is actually a Saint-tier strongman and has used some method to hide her strength," Samuel speculated.

Sharpuren didn't speak, thinking that it was probably the case, otherwise, things couldn't be explained.

"So, Samuel, do you need me to take care of these two adventurers?"

"Yes, go and find an opportunity to deal with these two guys tomorrow. Be low-key and don't cause any big commotion. This is a critical period, and we can't make any mistakes," Samuel instructed seriously.

"Don't worry, Samuel, I will complete the task!" Sharpuren said with a serious expression.

Samuel nodded, still trusting Sharpuren, and then turned to Shalan,

"How is the elf's great magic array going? Is there any problem?"

"There doesn't seem to be any problem now. I estimate that we can check all the magic points soon," Shalan replied softly.

"Hmm... Samuel's mood finally improved, and a smile appeared on his face.

"It just takes some time to wait.

"The era of the dark elves... will come back!"

The next morning.

The first ray of sunrise rose over the horizon.

The entire capital was bathed in a golden glow.

The neat streets were bustling with people, each busy with their own affairs.

The elf embassy welcomed its first guest today, not Merin and Alice, the couple who usually showed off.

But it was the first knight of Thorn, Macefield.

She had just finished her vacation and was on duty.

She wore exquisite and delicate armor, her light purple hair cascading down, and her red thorn flower war robe draped over her, making her look heroic and stunning, and her beauty was even more eye-catching.

If Macefield wasn't the first knight of Thorn, she would probably have lived an unknown life, not being a celebrity in Great Britain.

Macefield was followed by two purple thorn flower knights, her subordinates, who handled some matters for her.

Today, Macefield came to the elf embassy with an important matter, concerning the little princess of the elf king, Shirley.

Not long ago, the elf king of the United Kingdom repeatedly asked Queen Elizabeth to increase efforts to find Princess Shirley.

But until now, there was still no news of the troublesome princess.

Previously, during the crusade against the remnants of the previous kingdom, it was said that a beautiful elf kidnapped by the southern United Kingdom was imprisoned, which had once given the purple thorn flower knights hope.

But due to Elgin's intervention, not even a single elf hair was seen, and it ended in failure.

So today, Macefield came to negotiate with Samuel, hoping that the elf king could give more time to search for the little princess.

The royal family of Great Britain was busy searching for little Princess Shirley, but they didn't know she was being held in the basement of the embassy, which was quite... urgent.

Macefield checked her appearance, feeling that there was nothing impolite, and then walked forward,

"I want to see Samuel."

"I have important matters to discuss."

title: Chapter 38
content:
Chapter 38

Volume 7 · Chapter 38

Not long after Mesfield went in, Merlin and Alice arrived.

The two stood in front of the elven embassy, briefly discussing their next move.

"Let's go find that Samuel guy and settle the score." Merlin rolled up his sleeves, looking like he wasn’t here to negotiate but to fight.

"Wait a second! Don’t just jump into violence. We haven’t even figured out what’s going on yet," Alice knitted her brows, stopping Merlin in his tracks.

"You’re such a hassle," Merlin grumbled, thinking that if the other side had already tried to kill them, they were enemies—so why not just strike first?

"But we don’t even know why Samuel wants to kill us! If it’s a misunderstanding, acting rashly will only make things worse." Alice spoke seriously, worried Merlin would charge in without a second thought.

"Ugh..." Merlin frowned, annoyed by the restraint.

"And we need to see Sherry too..." Alice still couldn’t stop worrying about the timid elven princess. If Samuel really was a bad person, Sherry’s situation might be in serious danger.

"Fine..." Merlin nodded in agreement. "If something happens to Sherry, our million-coin reward goes down the drain. After all that free food and lodging, we can’t afford to come back empty-handed."

"Can you stop thinking about money for once? Sherry is our friend. If she’s in trouble, how can we just stand by and do nothing?" Alice said earnestly, feeling Merlin was being a little heartless.

"Sherry only clings to you. She’s your friend, not mine." Merlin said indifferently, thinking that if it weren’t for the million gold coins, he wouldn’t bother with this trouble at all.

"Do you *want* Sherry to cling to you?" Alice narrowed her eyes, staring at Merlin suspiciously, her mood souring.

"What are you thinking?" A cold sweat rolled down Merlin’s forehead as he caught a whiff of something sour. "What I mean is, we’re not a charity. We have to fight for our interests. Don’t naively cling to ideas like friendship and dreams—those things won’t fill your stomach or do you any good."

Alice fell silent, realizing she *was* being a bit naive.

But Sherry didn’t do anything wrong. She’s just a child trying to get home. After all the struggles she’s been through, only to face disappointment in the end—isn’t that unfair?

Alice’s sympathy flared up, and her emotions began to spiral.

"I understand your reasoning, but if Sherry is really in danger, we might be the only ones who can save her. Who else would she turn to?"

Merlin remained expressionless, watching Alice’s earnest face. He thought she really loved meddling in other people’s business. He hated do-gooders the most, especially ones like Alice—limited in ability but always trying to save everyone.

Put nicely, she was a saint. Put bluntly, she was a fool.

But Merlin had to admit, Alice’s way of thinking—trying to live up to others’ expectations—was admirable.

Hadn’t he, too, once fought to reclaim his throne and become the third Prideful Sovereign, all to meet his sister’s expectations?

Merlin rubbed his forehead and sighed. "Forget it. Let’s just find a way inside."

Alice didn’t say anything more, just sulked as she followed behind Merlin.

"We’re here to see the elven ambassador, Samuel," Merlin stepped forward and bluntly told the elven guards.

"Ambassador Samuel is currently meeting with important guests. All others are to be turned away." The elven guard replied coldly, his expression stern.

"Tch." Merlin clicked his tongue in displeasure, feeling slighted.

What kind of attitude was this from a mere elven ambassador? He was Merlin, the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace—was he just some random nobody?

Merlin’s hand twitched toward the hilt of his katana, ready to draw.

But before he could make a move, Alice yanked him aside.

"What are you doing?" Merlin glared at Alice, annoyed, not understanding her hesitation.

"Don’t make a scene! This is the royal capital. If we cause trouble here, we’ll never be able to live in human lands again. Just be a little more careful..." Alice whispered, glancing around nervously.

"So what do you suggest?" Merlin looked at her, wondering if she had a better plan.

"First, we sneak in from the side without alerting anyone. That way, we can move freely for the next step."

"Then we find Samuel and demand an explanation for the assassination attempt. We *have* to clear this up."

"Finally, we take Sherry with us. If possible, we’ll personally escort her back to the Southern United Kingdom..."

"Huh?" Merlin had vanished.

Alice, lost in her meticulously planned thoughts, muttered to herself for a while before realizing Merlin was gone.

She looked around frantically—only to see Merlin had already attacked the two elven guards.

"Gah!"

"...Ah!"

Two pained cries later, the elven guards were knocked out cold, collapsing to the ground, motionless.

Merlin dusted off his hands and turned to Alice. "Let’s go in. The way’s clear now."

Alice’s face turned an ugly shade of purple. "What the *hell* are you doing?! I told you to be careful!"

"Am I not being careful?" Merlin spread his hands, looking completely innocent.

"How is this careful?! This is basically forcing our way in with violence! This is an armed invasion of foreign territory—we’ll end up in jail!" Alice looked utterly depressed. She hadn’t expected Merlin to choose the most direct and reckless solution, leaving them with no way out.

"It’s fine. No prison can hold me." Merlin grinned, then turned and strode inside without the slightest attempt at stealth, charging straight in.

"Let’s go. Stop dawdling. The guards are already down—we’ve got no retreat left. Might as well barge in and give that elven ambassador Samuel a good beating. Since they tried to kill us, it’d be rude *not* to return the favor."

Merlin marched straight into the elven embassy, swinging his arms as if warming up, his killing intent growing more and more obvious, not bothering to hide it at all.

Anyone who tried to harm him was already dead. Samuel was no exception. And since he was a Saint-tier powerhouse, he’d be perfect for easing the curse on his heart.

"Wait for me!" Alice hurried after Merlin, her expression on the verge of tears. *Damn it!* she thought, exasperated.

This guy never listens to me!

If we keep acting this recklessly, there’ll be no room left to maneuver!

title: Chapter 39 — Chapter Title: Moonlight Chapter Update
content:
Chapter 39 — Chapter Title: Moonlight Chapter Update

Volume 7 · Chapter 39

Inside the embassy.

In a certain room.

Sharplon was polishing his red precision steel armor.

The shiny surface had strange symbols etched onto it.

These symbols were unique to the dark elves, where they would carve elf script onto gems to achieve an enchantment effect that increased attack power.

With the symbols embedded on the high-purity steel gauntlets, the weapon instantly rose to a higher level, becoming Sharplon's most trusted weapon.

Sharplon put on the steel gauntlets and clenched his fists a few times, feeling quite satisfied.

With a sudden punch, the air vibrated, causing the entire room to shake.

Sharplon planned to take action tonight, directly taking down those two clueless adventurers.

No matter how strong the demon sword wielder was, he couldn't possibly be Sharplon's match.

Because he was confident in his black elf martial arts, with brutal, sharp, and vicious moves that often caught his enemies off guard, usually ending the battle with a crushing victory.

Sharplon hadn't seen many people who could engage in close combat with him; if his enemies were up close, that meant they had already lost half.

A dark fluctuation suddenly appeared, making Sharplon's spine feel a chill run down it.

Without a doubt, it was his old friend who had arrived.

"Shaoran, why did you suddenly come to my place? I don't recall inviting you," Sharplon said.

"I came to see how you're prepared. What's wrong, don't you welcome me?" Shaoran's pointed ears twitched, and her smile under her dark skin looked very eerie.

"It's not that...," Sharplon responded calmly, retracting his gaze to continue fiddling with his gauntlets. "The Thorn Knight isn't here, is she? You shouldn't be here instead of attending to Samuel-sama."

"They're discussing confidential matters, and no third person is allowed to be present," Shaoran shrugged, seeming quite helpless.

"Confidential matters?" Sharplon furrowed his brow, thinking that as a dark elf, Samuel shouldn't have anything to cooperate with humans on.

"Actually, it's not much of a secret; we already know about it. It's about Princess Sherry," Shaoran paused, organizing her language before saying, "The Elf King urged Queen Elizabeth to find Princess Sherry, but after so long, there's still no news, so the Thorn Knight came to explain the situation and hopes the Elf King will grant more time."

Sharplon continued to adjust his gauntlets, seemingly uninterested in the matter.

"Only the Thorn Knight thinks of this as confidential; we already know everything. Samuel-sama has been dodging her all along," Shaoran said with a sly smile. "And isn't it quite interesting that the British royal family is searching for Princess Sherry, who's actually being held underground?"

"Indeed, it's quite...," Sharplon nodded, still adjusting his gauntlets. "Although the Thorn Knight is a fool, she might represent the top-tier combat power of Great Britain."

"Are you kidding me? Can Macefield really be called a top-tier combat power of Great Britain?" Shaoran crossed her arms, clearly disagreeing with Sharplon's statement, seeming to look down on the Thorn Knight.

"Isn't she? The Thorn Knights' strength is quite good, considered the backbone of Great Britain, and Macefield is the number one Thorn Knight; saying she's top-tier combat power isn't a problem, is it?" Sharplon looked at Shaoran, thinking his idea was correct.

"No, no, no, you've only been in Great Britain for a short time and don't know much. There are many people stronger than the Thorn Knights; I know of a very mysterious man who far surpasses Macefield," Shaoran said mysteriously.

"Who?" Sharplon's interest was piqued, and he asked seriously.

"He doesn't have a name; accurately, nobody knows. He's called the legendary great swordsman, Elgin. You've probably heard of him; his reputation is causing quite a stir in Great Britain and has begun to affect countries outside of it," Shaoran said.

Shaoran paused, continuing to vividly describe Merlin's popularity.

"Many children on the streets imitate him, playing justice games; you can see how influential he is now."

"Ah, it's this man, but he's too mysterious; everything about him is hearsay. I won't believe it unless I witness Elgin's strength myself," Sharplon said thoughtfully, recalling the stories about the legendary great swordsman.

"I've heard that Elgin can kill countless Saint-tier undead with one strike; how could a human do that? Unless he's a god, the credibility isn't high. However, if it's true, he might indeed be stronger than Macefield and possibly the strongest person in this world," Sharplon continued seriously.

"Yes, killing countless Saint-tier with one strike sounds like a fantasy; apart from Archduke Arthur who possesses divine power, I think of no one else who could do it," Shaoran nodded in agreement.

"So I say Macefield is a top-tier combat power of Great Britain, and there's no problem with that. As for Elgin, there are too many uncertainties, and it's not comparable," Sharplon concluded, continuing to adjust his gauntlets.

"Then I have another convincing example: the chairman of the London Adventurers Guild, a rare purple-gold level adventurer with unfathomable strength. According to various investigations, his aura is very restrained and mysterious, but definitely above Macefield's," Shaoran said with certainty.

"A purple-gold adventurer? I'd like to exchange blows with him if possible," Sharplon clenched his fists, seeming to be filled with enthusiasm.

"If you really encounter the old chairman of the London Adventurers Guild, I advise you to run away as soon as possible," Shaoran said seriously.

"Why?" Sharplon's tone turned cold, clearly unhappy with Shaoran's words, which felt like an insult.

"According to my investigation, this purple-gold old chairman's strength can only be described as a monster; he's not a normal human, perhaps having reached some unknown realm," Shaoran said with a serious expression, seeming to fear this unknown purple-gold adventurer.

"Is that so?" Sharplon narrowed his eyes, suspecting Shaoran might be exaggerating, an unknown realm? Was that possible?

"I've heard this purple-gold old chairman is skilled in black hole magic," Shaoran whispered.

"Black hole magic?" Sharplon was puzzled, asking patiently, "What kind of magic is that?"

"It doesn't belong to any category, not the six elements or spiritual magic. If I had to say, it would be more suitable to call it stellar or spatial magic, with some similarities," Shaoran thought before speaking.

"Spatial? Astrology?" Sharplon was completely baffled, having never heard of such magic.

"No, it's not astrology, but direct attack magic with immense destructive power; it's hard to imagine anything it can't destroy. It also has properties of spatial magic; based on some records, it's difficult to deduce," Shaoran seemed unsure about the purple-gold chairman.

"Mysterious guy, is he really that strong?" Sharplon smiled faintly, shaking his head, his tone dismissive.

"Perhaps like Elgin... They're all fame-seekers," Sharplon said.

title: Chapter 40 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 40 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes

Volume 7 · Chapter 40

"Seeking fame and reputation?"

Shalan raised her beautiful eyebrows, seemingly disapproving of the statement.

"The London Guild President is completely different from the Grand Swordsman Elgin. His strength is well-documented, unlike Elgin, whose reputation is mostly word of mouth with plenty of exaggeration."

"What records?" Sharplun set down his gauntlets and asked with interest.

"Have you heard of the Four Heroes of the former kingdom?" Shalan asked seriously.

"Of course. Four hundred years ago, this land was ruled by a king with four outstanding warriors: the Storm Warrior, the Dragon-Taming Rogue, and the Twin Sword Saints. Any one of them would be a dominant force even today." Sharplun held the Four Heroes of the former kingdom in high regard, as countless historical books of Great Britain depicted them as godlike figures.

"You know quite a bit..." Shalan wore a faint, ambiguous smile.

"After all, I have to live here. I’ve read many books in my spare time." Sharplun said indifferently.

"Actually, this purple-golden old Guild President from London is the very culprit who killed the Four Heroes of the former kingdom—apparently all by himself." Shalan answered seriously, trying to make Sharplun understand just what kind of monster this so-called fame-seeking old man truly was.

"Seriously?! By himself...?" Sharplun’s eyes widened in disbelief. He found even one of them difficult to handle, especially the Twin Sword Saints’ fusion ultimate skill—it was an overpowered ability.

"I don’t know if it’s true. Some historical records say so, but I think this purple-golden President must have used some special means. Otherwise, it would have been impossible." Shalan speculated, seeming uncertain.

Still, it was a widely accepted fact that the purple-golden President had killed the Four Heroes of the former kingdom. As for what special methods he used, no one knew.

"How old is this London President?" Sharplun asked tentatively.

"Judging by appearance, he’s nearly 600 years old..." Shalan answered after some thought.

"Isn’t that beyond the human lifespan limit? Even human Saint-tier powerhouses rarely live past 300 years. Is he immortal like us elves?" Sharplun exclaimed.

"Not exactly. It’s just that this old monster’s black hole magic is bizarre. Rumor has it he might devour time to extend his own lifespan." Shalan’s face showed a hint of fear.

"How is that possible?" Sharplun frowned, finding it hard to believe.

"Though I don’t want to believe it either, it seems there’s no other explanation for a human living so long." Shalan said expressionlessly, thinking Sharplun’s reaction was the same as hers had been.

"Just what is this guy’s background?" Sharplun asked curiously.

"On the surface, he’s the Guild President of London’s Adventurers Guild and a senior councilor of the Adventurers Association. But in the past, he was the Chief Court Mage, serving the British royal family. Later, for some unknown reason, he left the palace and became an adventurer, and has been one ever since." Shalan had privately investigated quite a bit and had some understanding of the purple-golden adventurer’s past.

"With such a powerful figure in London, won’t that affect Lord Samuel’s plans? Such a potential threat can’t be left unchecked..." Sharplun concluded, feeling that this mysterious purple-golden old President was the greatest obstacle to His Majesty Asmodeus’s resurrection.

"It won’t affect anything at all. Do you not understand Lord Samuel’s strength?" Shalan wore a faint, knowing smile, having absolute confidence in Samuel. If someone could make her submit, how could they possibly be weak?

Sharplun fell silent. He knew Samuel’s strength well—it was immense and needed no further explanation.

"Lord Samuel rose to fame when Great Britain didn’t even exist yet. This London purple-golden President wasn’t even born. Moreover, Lord Samuel’s wind magic has long since reached perfection. Crushing this old human would be effortless." Shalan’s smile deepened.

"True. Looks like I was overthinking." Sharplun sighed in relief.

"Now do you understand why I said Mesfield isn’t the peak power of Great Britain? Those stronger than her are all low-key." Shalan said seriously.

"Even so, the Thorn First Knight is no fraud. The other Thorn Knights also have solid strength. We can’t underestimate them." Sharplun said cautiously.

"Hmph. Apart from the Thorn First Knight, I don’t even consider the others worth my attention." Shalan curled her lips in disdain.

"Oh? If you faced the Thorn First Knight, what are your chances?" Sharplun asked with interest.

"If I don’t let him get close, I have a 70% chance. But if he closes the distance, it’d be about 50-50." Shalan answered after some thought.

"I see..." Sharplun furrowed his brows, lost in thought.

As they continued discussing, a elven guard suddenly burst in and shouted:

"Bad news! Lord Sharplun, Lady Shalan, something’s happened outside!"

"What’s going on? Running in like this is unacceptable!" Sharplun rebuked.

"F-Forgive me, Lord Sharplun! Someone has forced their way into the embassy! They demand to see Lord Samuel, and we couldn’t stop them even with all our men!" The elven guard’s forehead was beaded with cold sweat, looking extremely uneasy.

"Who dares to be so rude? Storming our territory—do they have a death wish?" Shalan’s expression turned serious, her anger rising.

"...It’s the two adventurers who arrived yesterday!" the elven guard shouted.

Both of them froze, not expecting these two to come looking for them.

"Oh?" Shalan smiled, glancing at Sharplun. "Things just got interesting."

"Mmm. Very interesting..." Sharplun’s usually expressionless face rarely showed a smile. He casually slipped on his finely adjusted steel gauntlets, clearly preparing for battle.

He had been planning to take care of these two, but now they had come to him.

Was he just incredibly lucky, or were these two foolish adventurers incredibly unlucky?

Sharplun let out a cold snort through his nose, muttering viciously:

"Heaven’s path you refuse to walk, hell’s gate you charge into yourself!"

Outside.

Two elven guards were pinned against the wall by Merlin, their throats gripped in his hands.

"Let go!"

"Rude bastards!"

The elven guards struggled desperately but couldn’t break free from Merlin’s grasp.

Since the elven embassy was quite large, Alice and Merlin couldn’t find Samuel, so they resorted to grabbing people for answers.

But these elves were proud and stubborn, each one unyielding. After a long time, they still hadn’t gotten any information about Samuel’s whereabouts, nor had they found anyone willing to guide them.

"You want me to let go? Then tell me where your boss Samuel is." Merlin stared at the two elven guards in his hands, calmly saying:

"As long as you tell the truth..."

"Everything is negotiable."

"I’m a very reasonable person."

title: Chapter 41
content:
Chapter 41

Volume 7 · Chapter 41

Merlin flashed a playful smile at the two elven guards, his intent to threaten and coerce unmistakably clear.

On the way here, countless guards had already been knocked unconscious—these two wouldn’t be any different.

The struggling elven guards gritted their teeth, glaring at Merlin, their breathing labored.

"Damn human! Do you think we’d ever bow to your filthy threats? Don’t underestimate us!"

"Do whatever you want with us, but don’t you dare lay a hand on Lord Samuel!"

The two elven guards were defiant to the end, refusing to yield even as Merlin overpowered them.

"Tch, what a nuisance..." Merlin clicked his tongue in annoyance. These elves were like brainwashed fools, their loyalty to Samuel absurdly high. This whole trip had been a complete waste.

Alice trembled behind Merlin, unable to speak. She knew full well that she and Merlin were violating the laws of Great Britain, hurtling down an irreversible path of wrongdoing.

This was supposed to be handled carefully, but thanks to Merlin, they were now past the point of no return. She was his accomplice—there was no escaping that.

But for Sherry’s safety, she had no choice but to keep going down this wrong path. There was simply no other option.

After much deliberation, Alice chose to follow Merlin’s lead and play the villain.

The former Hero never would have imagined that one day, she’d be trailing behind the Great Demon Lord, committing crimes and beating up defenseless guards. She was a fallen Hero, a disgrace to her title.

"You... you’d better tell us where Samuel is! Or—or else we won’t be nice! Have you ever seen a fist like a sandbag? It *hurts*!"

Alice’s terrible acting was cringe-worthy. Clearly, the role of a cruel, foul-mouthed villain didn’t suit her at all—she was just forcing herself through it.

Merlin stared at her, expressionless, and muttered awkwardly, "Are you a professional? You got into the role of a bandit way too fast."

"Shut up! This is all your fault! Do you think I *want* to do this? I could strangle you right now!" Alice wore a look of utter despair, completely at a loss for words with Merlin.

"Hmph..." Merlin narrowed his eyes, thinking this had nothing to do with him. He’d just taken the simplest, most direct approach.

"You despicable humans! Did you really think you could make noble elves submit with threats? Don’t get too arrogant, you lowly creatures! You won’t leave here alive, and Great Britain won’t let you off either!"

"Yeah! So what if you’re a little stronger? Big deal! You dare barge into the Elven Embassy—this is an armed invasion, a declaration of war against the Southern United Kingdom!"

The two elven guards shouted, each trying to outdo the other, struggling desperately to break free from Merlin’s grip.

But Merlin’s physical strength was far beyond their league. His hand, clamped around their necks like a vise, didn’t budge no matter how hard they thrashed.

Alice furrowed her brows, a cold sweat trickling down her forehead. She knew they were right—breaking into a foreign embassy was a serious crime. But the arrow had already been loosed; they had to see this through to the end.

"Oh? A declaration of war? So what? Is the Southern United Kingdom that impressive? Aren’t they just a bunch of declining races clinging to each other for warmth?" Merlin sneered, his contempt for the United Kingdom evident. "And your Elven King? Just an old fogey coasting on his age. If he hadn’t lived so long, who would even care about him?"

"...Insolent wretch! How dare you slander His Majesty! Your crimes are unforgivable!"

"Human, don’t get cocky. Captain Sharron will be here soon, and then you won’t even have time to run!"

The elven guards roared, now viewing Merlin and Alice as vicious enemies.

"Sharron? Who’s that? Some big shot?" Merlin asked, genuinely confused—he had no idea who that was.

"Captain Sharron is our Chief Guard! A Saint-tier powerhouse! The true heir of the Dark Elven martial arts!"

"You’d better surrender now, or when Captain Sharron arrives, neither of you will escape! You’ll be beaten until you question your own existence!"

The elven guards were fearless, knowing full well that even if they couldn’t defeat Merlin, someone else would.

"Beaten until I question my existence? Hmm..." Merlin grinned, not taking it seriously at all.

"You can still smile? When Captain Sharron gets here, you’ll be crying before you know it. Beg for mercy now, and maybe—*maybe*—you’ll keep your lives. Though you’ll still rot in prison for the rest of your days."

"You have no idea how strong Captain Sharron is. He once served as His Majesty’s personal guard. No one has ever defeated him in single combat. If you know what’s good for you, you’ll let us go *right now*!"

The elven guards glared at Merlin, as if they could already see him being pummeled by Captain Sharron.

"I’ve never been one to fear threats. Forget it—doesn’t look like we’re getting anything out of you two." Merlin sighed, then suddenly exerted force, slamming the guards’ heads into the wall. They collapsed, unconscious.

Alice’s expression was conflicted, a tear of regret welling in the corner of her eye. She whispered sorrowfully, "Two more down... Looks like from now on, we’re fugitives on the run. The Great Demon Lord and the Hero’s wild survival story begins..."

"What’s the point in saying that now?" Merlin pressed onward, indifferent. "Come on, let’s check the third floor. Maybe Samuel’s there."

"Ugh..." Alice, like a wronged little wife, silently followed, feeling like everything was spiraling out of control.

They had only taken two steps forward when two figures suddenly appeared around the corner of the staircase—Sharron and Sharon, who had rushed over in a hurry.

All four stared at each other, momentarily stunned.

But Merlin quickly regained his composure and asked patiently, "We need to see Samuel. Could you two show us the way?"
