"Oh? You want to see Lord Samuel? Unfortunately, we can’t allow that." Sharron smiled faintly, flatly rejecting Merlin’s request. Inwardly, he pondered whether to kill these two adventurers right here and now.

After all, they *had* to die. The opportunity was perfect, and the justification was solid.

Merlin and Alice had trespassed into the Elven Embassy—an act of territorial violation. Killing them in the name of defending sovereign land would be completely justified.

Sharron’s heart raced with dark excitement. *Heaven itself is aiding me!* He’d been fretting over the lack of an opportunity, and now they’d delivered themselves right to his doorstep!

"We need to see the Elven Ambassador, Samuel. It’s urgent. Please, let us through!" Alice said gravely, hoping to negotiate directly with Samuel.

"After harming our warriors, you still want to see Lord Samuel? Delusional!" Sharon snapped, the black ring on her finger glowing as if it were a magic staff.

Saint-tier golden magic surged forth, the sheer pressure so overwhelming it made breathing difficult.

Sharon flicked her wrist, firing a hyper-condensed ball of dark energy—straight at Alice behind Merlin.

Since Merlin radiated no aura of power, Sharon hadn’t even considered him a threat and completely ignored him.

She assumed Alice was the stronger one, so she focused on her.

The density of the dark energy sphere was staggering—its terrifying power was undeniable. If it hit, the target would be reduced to a puddle of sludge, not even ashes left behind!

Alice’s face paled. She could tell Sharon’s casual attack was far beyond what she could withstand. The power gap was enormous—if she were hit, she’d die instantly!

Fortunately, Merlin suddenly stepped in front of Alice, using his magic-immune body as a shield. The hyper-condensed dark energy sphere dissipated harmlessly against him.

"Starting with an attack, huh? Pretty decisive. You don’t plan on letting us leave alive, do you?" Merlin tilted his head, smiling eerily, as if he saw right through them.

"Wha—!" Sharon’s eyes widened in shock. She muttered to herself, bewildered.

"What’s going on?"

"My attack... it just *vanished*?!"

"Just some Black Iron-ranked nobody... could he be carrying a rare magic defense item..."

title: Chapter 42 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 42 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 42

Alice secretly let out a sigh of relief; if Merlin hadn't intervened, she would have knelt the moment she arrived.

When they arrived yesterday, Sharan and Sharplen didn't show much hostility; although the pressure of the Saint-tier could be felt, it wasn't that outrageous.

Now Sharan's magic attack, waved with a hand, has an extraordinary might; this power can only be described as terrifying.

It turns out the elf embassy is also a place where hidden talents lurk; perhaps Sharan is the strongest mage here.

As for Sharplen beside her, also a guard commander, the gap in strength is probably not large.

Alice didn't expect to hit a hard nut so soon; it seems the resistance to meeting Sherry is not small.

Merlin, however, saw that the other side had a murderous intent; they launched a powerful attack right away, clearly aiming to annihilate both himself and Alice without mercy.

If last night's assassination of some elves didn't matter, Merlin wouldn't believe it now.

"You think it's a magical defense gear, huh?"

Merlin shrugged, too lazy to explain anything; after all, it wouldn't make sense to explain.

"Shout!" Sharan pursed her lips, feeling uneasy; it seems this black‑iron villager isn’t completely useless after all—being able to dispel her magic must be a high‑level magical defense item.

Sharan felt a slight inconvenience, thinking that if this trash Merlin weren't removed, it would be somewhat difficult to harm Alice.

However, Sharan still harbored doubts about Merlin; magical defense items are generally very rare and extremely expensive, not something an ordinary person can obtain—how did this black‑iron adventurer get one?

Although Sharan didn't figure it out, she didn't dwell on it; normal magical defense items have limited uses or are shattered instantly by a strong magical attack. How many attacks can Merlin block? Ten? A hundred?

Sharplen said nothing beside her and didn't act; she couldn't understand why Alice, a hidden strong one, was hiding behind Merlin.

Could it be because he's too powerful, looking down on fighting personally?

Sending a mere follower to meet the enemy—what a contemptible move!

Sharplen kept a calm exterior, but inside his blood boiled, wanting to punch Merlin to death and then test Alice to see what pride she truly had.

"If you have the guts, come at me; there's no need to attack the guy behind me. Isn't it shameful to bully a disabled person?" Merlin showed a teasing smile.

"Who's the disabled person?! We’re teammates now, don’t take this chance to blacken me!" Alice retorted angrily, thinking Merlin was indeed a bad guy who kept slandering her.

"I'm just speaking the truth, so stop making a fuss, it's really troublesome…" Merlin rolled his eyes, thinking Alice was of no help at all; at least she wasn’t a hindrance.

In fact Merlin was just drawing hate, making the opponent focus fire on him, so he wouldn't have to worry about looking after Alice.

"Whether you’re disabled or not, since you dared to trespass into our territory, you’ll pay the price!" Sharan’s face was full of anger, the Saint-tier pressure rising step by step, clearly brewing a big move to crush Merlin’s magical defense in one strike.

"Hahaha, you’ve finally found a reason to kill us; there’s no need for reason any more." Merlin said with a cold laugh, seeing that the other side had no intention to explain, only thoughts of wiping out him and Alice.

"We just want to see Samuel; why are you showing us such hostility?" Alice furrowed her brows, angry inside, adding, "We sent your elf princess back yesterday, so by right we’re your benefactors. Isn’t it a bit much to treat us like this?!"

"Elf princess? Ha, how could we have ever known? The one we delivered yesterday was just an ordinary wandering elf, not a princess. Ridiculous~" Sharan sneered, already refusing to acknowledge yesterday’s events, as Princess Sherry was replaced by an ordinary wandering elf.

This line of reasoning was clearly pre‑prepared, meant to turn black into white and deceive everyone.

Alice widened her eyes; she wasn’t a fool.

From this abnormal response, she already knew some things.

Why is Sharan hiding the fact that Sherry returned?

Obviously it’s for some purpose, proving that Sherry may already have encountered something.

Alice’s face turned icy, staring at the Saint-tier pressure and glaring at Sharan.

"Where is Sherry? We want… her…"

"....." Sharan shrugged her shoulders, playing dumb, "Who's Sherry? We don’t even know her, let alone have met her."

"You!"

"Stop talking, Alice…"

Alice’s accusatory words were cut off as Merlin intervened, urging her not to waste her breath.

"They won’t admit what happened yesterday; if we want to see Sherry, we’ll have to find her ourselves."

"Shout!" Alice’s mood was low, feeling she had made a huge mistake.

She hadn’t investigated Samuel’s group properly before sending Sherry out, a massive blunder!

Sherry is innocent, she just wants to go home; why is the journey so difficult, filled with monsters and demons? So many calamities.

If something happens to Sherry, she would also be responsible and feel guilty.

Alice gritted her teeth; if she were strong enough now, she would overturn the entire embassy and rescue Sherry.

"Find her ourselves? Ignoring our existence outright—what audacity…"

Sharan raised her arm, the golden magical power of the Saint-tier flared fiercely.

The surrounding dark elements began to manifest, turning into swirling black smoke.

"If you want to find her yourself, you can, but you have to get past us first!"

The dark elements suddenly grew violent, becoming a shockwave of immense explosive force.

This is Sharan’s Saint-tier magic "Dark Impact", using a massive magical burst to instantly corrode everything before her.

Even wearing high‑grade anti‑magic armor won’t help; it will still be corroded because this technique’s piercing power is extreme!

Sharan is confident in this move; it’s not the same as the earlier magic projectile and should shatter Merlin’s magical cube defense in one go.

The dark impact, imbued with massive corrosive power, roared toward Merlin, killing intent blazing.

But the result was the same; it vanished without a trace before Merlin.

"Hey, could you stop using magic? Boring. I think you’d rather hit my head with a wand…" Merlin sighed, already a bit fed up.

"Again ineffective?!" Sharan’s eyes widened, finding it unbelievable; she thought, "What kind of magical defense gear does this guy have that my full‑power strike has no effect? This isn’t normal!"

…Sharplen couldn’t stand it any longer, ripped off his coat, revealing black, explosive‑filled muscles, his pointed ears adorned with several jingling ear‑studs—

"Sharan, step aside."

"Leave this man to me."

"In a breath…"

"I will end this farcical battle within a breath."

(一~一)

title: Chapter 43 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 43 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 43

"In a single breath? You really have confidence... Ah..."

Merlin slanted his mouth and smiled, seemingly unimpressed by Sharpuron's pre-battle remarks.

Alice remained expressionless and didn't say much, having seen many people boast in front of Merlin, only to be defeated without exception.

"This isn't confidence, it's a guaranteed outcome. Your cube defensive item is indeed not bad, but how about facing my fist?"

Sharpuron twisted his fists, which were covered in a red metal gauntlet that shone brightly, as if showing off to Merlin.

"Why are you interfering? I can handle it. Do you think I'm incapable of dealing with a black iron adventurer? That's belittling me!"

Sharan's eyebrows furrowed, thinking that if she launched another magical attack, she could definitely crush Merlin's magical defense equipment.

"This guy's magical defense equipment is not simple. As a magician, you're at a disadvantage dealing with him. It's more suitable for me to handle. Three consecutive attacks couldn't even subdue a black iron adventurer. Do you want to embarrass Samuel?"

Sharpuron said calmly, looking serious, as if he could instantly defeat Merlin and make him unrecognizable. If Merlin could withstand physical attacks, that would be abnormal.

"Hmph! How infuriating... " Sharan showed a disgusted expression, clearly very discontent, and if she had used her full strength earlier, she wouldn't have been so embarrassed.

Sharpuron assumed a strange attack stance, with his fists clenched in front of his forehead, his left foot toe touching the ground, and his breathing very regular.

This was the starting posture of the dark elf's martial art, which integrated offense and defense.

It could instantly start with a lightning-fast strike, or transform into a protective stance, making it difficult for enemies to harm him.

The elf tribe had lived in the forest for generations, facing many unknown dangers, such as sudden beast attacks.

This martial art had an extremely long history, being the essence passed down through generations of the elf tribe.

Sharpuron, as a orthodox successor, had absorbed its essence and turned it into his own weapon.

"Unseen postures... " Merlin stroked his chin, having never seen such a strange technique before.

"There are more things for you to be surprised about."

Sharpuron said coldly, his tone devoid of emotion.

He glanced at Alice behind Merlin, wondering why she was watching from behind and not planning to intervene.

This woman was stronger, a hidden powerful figure, yet she sent a subordinate to block their way...

Did she have so much confidence in this black iron adventurer?

Hmph! Naive guy, first, I'll take care of this villager, and I don't believe that female adventurer can just sit idly by!

Sharpuron's golden aura burst out, and his body suddenly moved, transforming into a black lightning bolt. His strange martial art footsteps made his speed several times faster!

Although he was far away from Merlin, it was as if he was right in front of him, and could attack him at any moment.

For a true fighter, such a distance was already within the range of a lethal attack!

Sharpuron's speed was almost impossible to see, and when Alice reacted, the enemy had already stood behind Merlin.

Alice widened her eyes, her expression with a hint of panic, thinking that it was as she had expected, Sharpuron's strength was extraordinary, and his moves were so vicious!

"Hmph, end it... "

Sharpuron suddenly issued a hand blade, slashing towards Merlin's neck, with a sharp, saint-tier aura that tore through the air.

This attack was extremely powerful, clearly aiming to take Merlin's life!

But an unexpected scene occurred.

Sharpuron's hand blade hit Merlin's afterimage, attacking empty space, as if he had hit an illusion!

Merlin, of course, didn't use the cube; the afterimage was just a residual image left behind because Merlin's speed was faster than Sharpuron's.

"Yes, it's over... "

Sharpuron was still in shock, and before he could understand what had happened, Merlin's voice, full of amusement, suddenly came from behind him.

This meant that Sharpuron's weaknesses were now fully exposed in front of Merlin, and the situation had completely reversed, becoming extremely critical!

Sharpuron was stunned, his expression filled with terror, and cold sweat broke out immediately, thinking about what had just happened! Why did he suddenly appear behind him? He didn't even feel any magical fluctuations; could it be that he had been completely defeated just by physical speed?!

Merlin didn't give Sharpuron any extra time to consider, kicking him in the buttocks, making him fall to the ground with a thud, and assume an undignified posture.

Alice let out a sigh of relief, thinking that this brief exchange had occurred in an instant, and although the two fights ended quickly, they had gone through several rounds.

It seemed that Merlin was still incredibly strong, not taking Sharpuron seriously at all, and was still toying with this self-assured guy.

Sharan was in shock, looking down at Sharpuron on the ground, who was still sticking out his buttocks, thinking that this was the situation? Sharpuron was actually at a disadvantage when dealing with a black iron adventurer! As a fighter, he was crushed in terms of speed! It was simply unbelievable! What was the background of this black iron adventurer? It was too abnormal!

"I think you should learn to be more obedient. Take us to see Samuel, or I won't be polite... "

Merlin said carelessly.

"And Miss Shirley, we must see her!" Alice added quickly.

"Cough... "

Sharpuron coughed a few times, apparently having eaten dirt.

He slowly stood up, wiping the mud from the corner of his mouth, and looked at Merlin behind him, his mind unable to calm down for a moment.

"What the hell... "

Merlin was just an ordinary person without any magical aura or fighting spirit, but why was his reaction so fast! Even faster than him!

What black iron villager was this? This was definitely not an ordinary guy!

Sharpuron gritted his teeth, feeling humiliated at being kicked to the ground and eating dirt by a black iron adventurer.

His dignity was on the verge of collapse, and his soul couldn't accept this fact.

So, Sharpuron's anger rose, and he launched a silent attack on Merlin using his martial arts.

This time, there was no warning, a complete sneak attack.

The technique was called 「Swift Tiger's Fierce Strike」, a move used by the elf tribe to ambush fierce beasts in the forest, and now it was used on Merlin.

The attack started without any posture, directly aiming for a fatal strike, catching people off guard!

"Hmph!"

Sharpuron's saint-tier aura surged, instantly transforming into a tiger shape, and fiercely attacked Merlin, as if tearing his head apart.

Alice was taken aback, completely unprepared for the fierce counterattack!

Even her teammate Sharan was stunned, not expecting Sharpuron's sudden attack.

When Sharpuron's attack was about to hit Merlin's face, within a fist's distance, everyone thought the situation was sealed, and Merlin would at least be seriously injured, and even Sharpuron himself thought he had won, and couldn't help but show a hint of joy.

But unfortunately, Sharpuron was facing the Great Demon Lord...

Merlin suddenly used one hand to catch Sharpuron's sneak attack, grasping his punch without any warning.

"Impossible! This can be caught?!" Sharpuron's expression was stunned, his eyes wide open, and he couldn't think of this, even his sneak attack was ineffective!

Merlin slowly shifted his gaze to Sharpuron's face, grasping his fist, and spoke in a cold tone.

"I told you to be more obedient."

"You're still resorting to sneak attacks?"

"I think you need to be educated... "

title: Chapter 44
content:
Chapter 44

Volume 7 · Chapter 44

The reception hall was located on the top floor, and the soundproofing was excellent. As a result, Samuel was completely unaware of what was happening downstairs.

Samuel was fully engaged with the sudden visit from the First Knight of Thorns, Macefield, and had no idea that chaos had erupted below. Macefield, even in armor, exuded elegance and poise as she discussed Shirley with Samuel.

"Your Excellency, some time ago, Her Majesty the Queen dispatched many people to visit the honest villages of Great Britain, gathering information about Princess Shirley. However, unfortunately, we still do not know her whereabouts, and many eyewitness clues have been interrupted."

Macefield's expression was tinged with regret. Recently, Queen Elizabeth had sent out all the intelligence personnel in the army, spreading them across Great Britain to investigate. Although there were a few sightings, they were all interrupted when trying to follow up, leaving Princess Shirley's whereabouts a mystery.

"It's really no use. We've invested a lot of national resources in searching, but there's no harvest. This has caused Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth a lot of trouble. Because the Elf King insists that Princess Shirley is in Great Britain and keeps urging us, this has already affected the friendship between the two countries and escalated into a diplomatic issue."

Macefield also felt troubled for the Queen, as it was her duty as a close knight to share the Queen's worries.

"Is there really no clue at all?" Samuel asked hypocritically, knowing that Shirley was being held underground but still going through the motions.

"Well, there were indeed some very good leads, but something unexpected happened, causing all the clues to be interrupted. If we want to find Princess Shirley, I'm afraid we'll have to start the investigation from scratch."

Macefield sighed, thinking that if it weren't for Elgin, the Great Swordmaster, suddenly appearing and disrupting the entire plan, they might have found Princess Shirley by now.

"That's really unfortunate. It's been such a long time, and there's still no harvest. Our Queen may be disappointed again." Samuel showed a worried expression, completely playing the role of a selfless and concerned saint, and no one would suspect that she was a super villain.

"I'm very sorry. We've done our best," Macefield apologized politely.

"No, it's not that. It's just that Great Britain is a vast territory, and it's really hard to find one person," Samuel nodded understandingly.

"Your Excellency, may I ask a question?" Macefield asked seriously.

"Please go ahead, Macefield. Don't be polite," Samuel nodded.

"Are you sure Princess Shirley is still in Great Britain? It's been half a year, and it's possible that she might have gone to another country or..."

Macefield didn't finish her sentence, but the implication that Shirley might be dead was clear.

"There's no doubt that Princess Shirley is still in Great Britain. She's not in another country, and nothing has happened to her," Samuel replied affirmatively.

"Why are you so sure?" Macefield paused and slowly expressed some concerns.

"If this is all just speculation, it's better to give up searching for Princess Shirley as soon as possible. This is not just the Elf King's problem; it also involves our Great Britain. We've invested a lot of financial and human resources in searching for her, and if we continue like this, it will be difficult for us to assist you."

"Please rest assured, Macefield. We're not speculating. The Elf King has a clear sense of his children. If he says Princess Shirley is still in Great Britain, then there won't be any mistake. Please trust us," Samuel responded seriously, dispelling Macefield's doubts.

"Since you're so confident, I have no objections. Although we didn't gain anything this time, we didn't lose the confidence to find Princess Shirley. We'll definitely find her, so I hope you can communicate with the Elf King and give me some more time," Macefield stated the purpose of her visit.

"That's no problem. I'll find a time to communicate with the King and let him wait patiently. I won't give you too much trouble. We've already troubled Queen Elizabeth for a long time, and our King feels a bit guilty," Samuel said humbly.

"Since Your Excellency is willing to mediate, things will be easier. Thank you for your help," Macefield bowed slightly, expressing her agreement.

"Not at all. I'm the one who should thank you. Princess Shirley's disappearance has caused our King a lot of worry, and only you are willing to help us unconditionally," Samuel responded politely, but her heart was secretly laughing.

"You are too polite...," Macefield smiled, feeling that the matter was almost settled, and she could leave. "It's getting late; I'll take my leave."

"Do you want to stay for afternoon tea?" Samuel asked politely.

"No, I have a lot of things to attend to," Macefield declined tactfully.

"You're really a busy person, aren't you, the First Knight of Thorns?" Samuel teased.

Macefield didn't say anything, turned around, and left. But suddenly, she remembered something else and turned back to ask, "Your Excellency, I saw the report from the city guards, saying that your subordinates have been frequenting the capital recently?"

Samuel's expression became unnatural, and she said awkwardly, "Yes...yes."

"Is there anything that needs help? If you need assistance, please don't hesitate to tell me," Macefield said kindly.

"No, I just let my subordinates go to the capital to pick some fresh fruits," Samuel made an excuse, thinking that she would never let the Knights of Thorns help with the arrangement of the "Spirit Weeping" magic circle.

"Is that so? Goodbye," Macefield didn't suspect much, as elves were known to like fruits and vegetables.

As Macefield took a few steps away, she suddenly sensed something approaching from outside the door, extremely fast and with a hint of hostility.

This was the embassy of the Elf Kingdom; could there be enemies here?

Macefield quickly stepped back, grasped the hilt of her sword, and prepared to face the enemy.

Samuel's perception was not weaker than Macefield's, and she also sensed something strange, frowning and thinking, Who dared to intrude into her territory?!

A loud crash was heard as the wooden door to the reception hall was smashed.

Two dark objects flew past Macefield's ears.

The sudden incident left everyone stunned, unsure of what was happening.

Macefield turned back in shock, seeing Shapren and Sharan lying on the ground, both with some minor injuries.

What was happening?!

These two were the leaders of the embassy's guards!

Both were Saint-tier strong warriors; why were they defeated like this?!

Macefield was puzzled, full of doubts and surprises.

Samuel's reaction wasn't much better, thinking, Who was the intruder?! Shapren and Sharan weren't weak; they couldn't even stop the intruder, who must be extraordinary...

Shapren and Sharan slowly got up, supporting each other, and glared at the door, exuding hostility, as if ready to fight the enemy to the death.

The smoke dispersed, and Merlin appeared outside, looking casual.

He suddenly raised his head, directly looking at Samuel, his red eyes shining like gemstones.

"Good morning~"

"See you again, Auntie, the Elf Kingdom's ambassador."

"Your two dogs aren't very obedient; I helped you teach them a lesson, so don't take it out on me..."

title: Chapter 45 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 45 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 45

Samuel's eyes widened in shock and doubt as he saw Merlin.

What the...?

Could it be that Shalan and Shapuren were defeated by this guy?

No way, isn't he just a low-ranking Black Iron adventurer?!

I couldn't sense any magical power or fighting spirit emanating from him. How did a ordinary villager manage to defeat two Saint-tier strongers?!

Samuel found it hard to imagine and was unwilling to believe what he was seeing.

He couldn't explain the situation with all his knowledge, and it seemed like he had wasted his thousand years of life.

Samuel stared at Merlin, unable to find a way to respond, as everything was too sudden.

Actually, Shapuren and Shalan had done their best, but their opponent was a powerful foe. Could they have withstood the attack?

Shapuren had exchanged a few moves with Merlin, but was immediately picked up and beaten, taking several punches.

As for Shalan, facing Merlin who was immune to magic, she became useless, and her several magic spells had no effect. She even got slapped by Merlin twice, feeling extremely humiliated.

If Shalan and Shapuren's opponents weren't the Demon Lord, they would be considered powerful individuals, but in front of Merlin, they were like chicks.

Mestfeldt watched Merlin, her expression slightly dazed, but her hand tightly grasped the hilt of her sword, on guard.

Who is this guy?!

He actually humiliated two Saint-tier strongers like this.

His strength must be incredibly powerful.

But I have never seen this man before. Is he a wild person from somewhere?

Mestfeldt saw the Black Iron adventurer's proof around Merlin's neck and suddenly widened her eyes, unable to speak.

Although she didn't understand the current situation, she suddenly realized something.

Mestfeldt recalled yesterday, when Morrison said that a Black Iron adventurer from Wrexham had won an arm-wrestling game against him.

Now, looking at the Black Iron adventurer's proof around Merlin's neck, many conditions matched, and it was likely that the arm-wrestling winner was the man in front of her.

No wonder he had the strength to compete with Saint-tier strongers. If he could beat Morrison, it wouldn't be surprising.

But why did this guy intrude into the Elf Embassy? Didn't he know that this was against the law of the kingdom? The punishment could be death or imprisonment for many years.

And he did it in front of her, so brazenly, as if he didn't care about the entire Great Britain.

Mestfeldt frowned, staring at Merlin for a long time, hesitating whether to put him in prison.

"What's wrong? Why is everyone silent? I'm not going to shut up..."

Merlin said awkwardly, scanning the others.

When he saw Mestfeldt, Merlin's expression changed.

Oh, the First Knight of Thorns is here.

After arriving in London, he kept running into this little girl.

Was it fate, or was he going to be put in prison?

Whatever it was, Merlin felt annoyed, thinking that meeting the First Knight of Thorns would make things complicated and not go smoothly.

Merlin, who felt guilty, was a bit resistant to Mestfeldt, and a feeling similar to a mouse seeing a cat arose in him.

Shalan and Shapuren saw Merlin's arrogance and immediately became furious, wanting to release their ultimate techniques and fight him to the death.

"What's there to show off? Do you think you're the winner?" Shapuren shouted, his forehead veins bulging.

"Don't be too happy. We haven't used our full strength yet. If we do, the result will be completely different!" Shalan gritted her teeth, her mood similar to Shapuren's, feeling extremely humiliated.

"Is that so? I don't want to crush your spirits, but let's be realistic. Even if you have the idea of fighting to the death, you still can't be my opponent. I advise you to face reality..."

Merlin shrugged.

Mestfeldt was taken aback, thinking that this man was really arrogant. What made him so confident?

"You bastard! We won't give up. You do have some strength, but it's not that exaggerated. Take off your magic defense equipment, and let's have a good fight!" Shapuren's eyes turned fierce, thinking that he could win if he used his real skills.

Little did he know that even without using his real skills, Merlin was just playing with him, and if he used his full strength, Shapuren wouldn't be able to withstand even one blow.

"If you have some dignity, take off your magic defense equipment, and let's have a proper fight!" Shalan gritted her teeth, thinking that Merlin's magic defense equipment was too powerful and not due to his own strength.

"I don't have that thing..."

Merlin smiled helplessly.

"Don't lie!" Shalan shouted, and she was about to attack again.

Samuel frowned, thinking that Merlin was so arrogant?

It seemed that they wanted to rescue Sherry from the human traffickers, and it wouldn't be difficult. He had underestimated this small Black Iron adventurer.

Maybe he, like Alice, was hiding his strength.

This couple was really interesting, both liking to surprise people, and it had to be said that their sense of humor was quite good.

But defeating Shalan and Shapuren wasn't something to brag about...

Samuel thought calmly and was about to say something when Alice suddenly ran over.

Alice stopped beside Merlin, holding his shoulder, panting, and said, "Wait... don't run so fast. It's not like you're going to die..."

"You're just too slow, whose fault is that?" Merlin said indifferently.

Alice didn't want to quarrel with Merlin now and looked at the scene, finally finding Samuel. However, she saw Mestfeldt and suddenly stopped breathing.

"A-ah... thorn... cough..."

Alice coughed a few times to cover her embarrassment and quickly whispered to Merlin.

"Merlin, why is the First Knight of Thorns here?"

"I don't know, I was surprised too..." Merlin whispered back.

"Isn't our luck a bit bad?"

Alice was also a bit embarrassed. The first time she did something wrong with Merlin, she ran into the city guards. It seemed that being with the Great Demon Lord wasn't a good thing...

"What's the matter? Don't be afraid, just do it!" Merlin said without hesitation.

"Eh! ?" Alice widened her eyes and said in a hurry, "Is that so straightforward? You're going to start a rebellion, aren't you? Is this part of your evil plan, and you deliberately pulled me into it?"

"How could that be? Don't think in terms of conspiracy theories. The First Knight of Thorns isn't worth mentioning. To be honest, I could make her lose her fighting strength with just one breath, and she would be happy..."

Merlin's mouth curled up, giving people a slightly lascivious feeling.

"Alice suddenly stopped, her eyebrows highly arched, and said dissatisfiedly,

"Put away your dirty thoughts at this time, okay?"

"Not yet..."

"What kind of disgusting, obscene, and vulgar trick is this?"

title: Chapter 46 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 46 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 46

“What's a little unorthodox about our moves if we can defeat the enemy?” Merlin shrugged, looking nonchalant, and thought Alice was overreacting. “I've even seen someone pull out their...ahem...and claim it's a holy sword.”

“Ugh...” Alice's eyes widened, and the black hairpin on her forehead slipped down. She thought this was an extremely lewd move - did pulling out that thing really make someone a girl?!

Hmm, it seemed Alice had guessed correctly. This person was indeed one of Merlin's seven generals, and pulling out that thing really did change their gender, with no pressure at all.

“I don't want to discuss such lewd topics with you. What are we going to do now? We broke into the embassy with force, and just so happened to be seen by the First Knight of Thorn...this is going to get us thrown in jail for sure,” Alice said nervously, probably because it was her first time doing something bad, and she was very anxious.

“Don't panic, we have a legitimate reason for being here,” Merlin gave Alice a reassuring glance.

Alice pursed her lips and didn't speak, her face clearly showing her distrust. She felt like she was on a runaway boat, and had to see this through to the end.

Mestfeldt looked at Merlin and Alice chatting below for a long time, then couldn't help but speak in an extremely serious tone. “You two, what are you whispering about down there? Colluding?”

“No...it's...” Alice quickly responded, worried about being misunderstood. Although Merlin seemed to have come up with a questionable plan, she could only make do with it for now.

“What do you care? You're really nosy...” Merlin said in a teasing tone.

“What did you say?” Mestfeldt's eyebrows shot up, and she said seriously, “You two broke into the elf embassy, and you're speaking to me in this tone?”

Alice saw Mestfeldt's attitude was very official, and her expression didn't look good. She thought things might be in trouble.

“Isn't it my freedom to speak in whatever tone I want? Does that also count as a crime?” Merlin frowned and said, seemingly not fond of Mestfeldt's righteous attitude.

“According to imperial law, you two used force to break into the elf embassy, which is a serious crime. You should be arrested, and the maximum penalty is hanging,” Mestfeldt said seriously, not liking Merlin's arrogant attitude.

“Want to arrest me? That's quite a bold claim. If you have the ability, go ahead and try...” Merlin suddenly gripped the hilt of his sword at his waist, and a hint of battle intent flashed in his eyes.

“As you wish...” Mestfeldt narrowed her eyes, also gripping the hilt of her straight sword. It seemed she had the impulse to fight Merlin right there.

Samuel, who was behind them, couldn't help but stifle a laugh. If he could get them to kill each other, that would be nice too - let the First Knight of Thorn take care of these two adventurers.

“Wait a minute!”

Alice quickly stopped them, thinking Merlin didn't want to talk things through with the other party at all - as soon as there was a disagreement, he wanted to fight.

This was completely off track. They were here to investigate the reason for the assassination attempt last night, and to see Snowy, not to compete in a fighting tournament with the Thorn Knights.

“We didn't mean to break in, but we had some questions for the elf ambassador,”

“There are procedures for seeing Ambassador Samuel. You can go through the proper channels. Forcibly breaking in is a violation of imperial law,” Mestfeldt said formally, seemingly unwilling to listen to Alice's explanations.

“This matter is very important. Even if we go through the proper channels, Samuel won't see us,” Alice frowned and said, hoping to get understanding.

Mestfeldt looked at Alice and thought she was different from Merlin's exposed sharpness - she didn't seem like a bad person. So she patiently asked, “What is it? Even if it's very important, we can't just violate imperial law.”

“Really, this guy is too serious...” Merlin muttered softly.

“Samuel sent someone to assassinate us last night!” Alice pointed to Samuel behind her.

“Ugh...”

Mestfeldt was taken aback by Alice's words.

If Samuel had sent someone to assassinate a British citizen, that would be a big deal, and could directly affect the relations between the two countries.

Mestfeldt looked at Samuel behind her, and for a moment, she was suspicious.

Samuel's eyes flashed with dissatisfaction, and he quickly defended himself, “What are you talking about, adventurer? I have no idea what you're talking about.”

“Stop pretending, we know it was you who sent them,” Merlin frowned, somewhat disgusted by Samuel's denial.

“That's right. We caught the assassin yesterday, and he said it himself,” Alice added.

Samuel's expression turned ugly. He thought his subordinate was a waste - he should have killed him yesterday, and not let him be caught. He should have cut him into pieces and fed him to the ghouls!

How dare he betray me?!

Samuel cursed inwardly, maintaining his composure. “Accusing others isn't a good habit. Can you prove it was me who ordered it just by your one-sided words?”

Mestfeldt looked at Alice again, thinking this matter was complicated, and it was hard to tell who was right or wrong. She thought it was better to observe for now.

“The guy who came to assassinate us said it himself. Can that be fake?” Alice said angrily.

“Please stop slandering me. Everything needs evidence. Just because someone says I ordered it, you believe it? Can't it be someone else intentionally doing it, framing me?” Samuel cleared his name and shifted the blame to unknown enemies.

Mestfeldt thought Samuel's words made sense - she couldn't trust just one person, and needed convincing evidence to believe it.

“Yeah, if you say the person who assassinated you was sent by Ambassador Samuel, then you need to produce evidence. Otherwise, your accusations don't stand,”

“The assassins last night were all dark elves. How do you explain that? It's clearly connected to the elf tribe,” Alice responded calmly.

“Dark elves...” Mestfeldt looked at Samuel, finding it suspicious.

“That can be considered evidence? Ha! It's laughable...” Samuel remained calm and composed, “Not a few elves are wandering outside their tribes. We don't know what they do, and it has nothing to do with me.”

“Shut up!” Alice's mood grew worse, thinking Samuel was becoming more and more shameless.

Yesterday, Alice hadn't thought much of it and had directly released the assassin. If she knew this, she should have left evidence. Now she thought it was a misstep.

Mestfeldt had doubts, thinking Alice's words didn't seem fake, but without evidence, she couldn't prove it either, and couldn't rule out the possibility of smearing.

“Okay, you don't admit it, but can you let us see Snowy? We just sent her back yesterday. A living person can't just disappear, can she?” Merlin said calmly, seemingly able to see Snowy.

“That's right. We just sent Princess Snowy back yesterday!” Alice seemed to see a breakthrough and was excited.

“Snowy...main princess!?”

Mestfeldt's eyes widened in shock, and her mouth was agape. She was directly frightened.

She felt that Alice and Merlin's words contained a lot of information, and she had to take it seriously.

Mestfeldt looked at Samuel behind her, thinking - what was going on?!

Had Snowy Princess already returned?!

But why did Samuel just say they hadn't found her?!

Was Snowy Princess, the little daughter of the elf king, in this embassy...

title: Chapter 47
content:
Chapter 47

Volume 7 · Chapter 47

Mesfeld hesitated for a moment before bluntly asking Samuel.

"Lord Samuel, is what they’re saying true? Has Princess Sherry really returned...?"

"Lord Mesfeld, please trust me—Princess Sherry has not returned at all..." Samuel replied earnestly.

"You’re lying! We brought Princess Sherry here ourselves yesterday. How can you deny it so shamelessly?!" Alice was so furious she could barely think straight. She had never met anyone so brazen.

"What nonsense. The one you brought yesterday was just an ordinary lost spirit, not Princess Sherry at all. Please stop spreading such troublesome lies." Samuel spoke with feigned sincerity.

"Stop pretending! Call that spirit we brought yesterday out here and let us confront her directly!" Alice snapped, indignant.

"What a shame. That spirit left on a cruise to the United Kingdom this morning. She’s already on her way back home..." Samuel answered patiently.

"You’re lying. Sherry is still here, isn’t she?" Alice knitted her brows, pressing him.

"We’ve told you—what you brought wasn’t Princess Sherry, just a common spirit. Why are you so fixated on this?" Sharron couldn’t resist fanning the flames, backing Samuel up.

"I suspect they’re hiding something unspeakable..." Shalan narrowed her eyes, her words heavy with implication.

Now everyone was a mouse, and Mesfeld the lone cat—naturally, they were all vying for her trust.

But Mesfeld herself wavered, unable to decide whom to believe. This concerned Princess Sherry, after all.

"What in the world is going on here?"

"Lord Mesfeld, listen to me. Here’s what happened..." Samuel paused, then said with false gravity, "Yesterday, these two adventurers brought a lost spirit, but to extort more reward, they insisted she was Princess Sherry. Do you think that’s right?"

Mesfeld glanced at Alice and Merlin, wondering—*Are these two really swindlers?*

"As the former queen’s personal maid, I’ve seen Princess Sherry countless times. Would I not recognize her? Yet they keep harassing us, and today they’ve come here deliberately to stir up trouble." Samuel’s acting was convincing; he looked every bit the victim.

"Lord Samuel is right! These two are trying to blackmail us!" Shalan quickly chimed in.

"Truly a disgrace to humanity..." Sharron said coldly.

"Tch!" Merlin scowled, his hand resting on the hilt of his katana, radiating hostility.

"Who’s doing this for reward? Don’t look down on us!" Alice snapped.

Mesfeld fell into thought. Samuel’s words did seem more credible.

Alice and Merlin were just adventurers—a profession that chased profit everywhere.

Samuel, on the other hand, was the elven ambassador she frequently dealt with. He had always been trustworthy, of high moral character, and often involved in charity. The comparison made it clear who was more believable.

Mesfeld suddenly drew her ornate straight sword, pointing it at Merlin and Alice. Her pretty face darkened as she spoke sternly.

"Trespassing in the elven embassy and suspected fraud—those two charges alone are enough to land you in the royal dungeon for years..."

"Why won’t you believe us?" Alice’s voice carried a hint of frustration.

"Because your words are hard to believe." Mesfeld released a faint Saint-tier pressure, clearly restraining her full power. "But since you’re human, I’ll let this slide if you leave now. Don’t pull such shady stunts again."

In truth, Mesfeld was already bending the rules. If Merlin and Alice weren’t human, she would’ve handled this strictly by the book.

But for her own kind, she could afford to be lenient. She wasn’t heartless—she didn’t want to give the non-humans behind her something to mock.

Alice opened her mouth, then closed it again.

"Alice, move aside." Merlin said coldly, already assuming a drawing stance.

The tension spiked. Merlin and the Thorn First Knight refused to back down; a clash seemed imminent.

Samuel, in the back, grinned widely, hoping to see them both cripple each other so he could swoop in.

Alice hesitated, her mind racing through possibilities, and finally braced for the worst.

She grabbed Merlin’s arm, stopping him.

"What are you doing? Pointing fingers at me?" Merlin frowned, impatient.

"No, it’s not that. If you fight now, where will you go afterward?" Alice lowered her voice, whispering, "She’s the Thorn First Knight, the queen’s confidante. If you lay a hand on her, you’ll have no place in Great Britain. You won’t even be able to go back to your old job as a gigolo."

"Who said my old job was a gigolo?! Do you have to dig up my black history?!" Merlin’s brows knitted together, embarrassed.

"I’m just giving an example. Even if you flee abroad, they’ll hunt you down. The only place you could go is demon territory. Do you want to go back and be the Demon Lord?" Alice probed.

Merlin fell into deep thought. He really didn’t want to return to the demon race. He had escaped from there himself—what was the point of going back? To deal with his bizarre subordinates? To whip his masochistic little sister? As if!

It seemed the Thorn Knight wasn’t someone he could afford to provoke. The political entanglements were too great.

Merlin regretted it. If he had just hidden his identity, he wouldn’t be in this predicament, forced to tread so carefully.

This was getting complicated...

In the end, no fight broke out.

Merlin and Alice left the embassy empty-handed, their expressions unnatural. Running into the Thorn First Knight was just their luck.

If it hadn’t been for her, they would’ve rescued Sherry by now.

As they walked back to the inn, the streets bustled with people.

Merlin was seething inside. The 1,000,000 gold coins were slipping away, and the feeling of suffering such a huge loss made him want to scream.

Alice, however, wasn’t thinking about the money. She was worried about Sherry’s safety.

Given how reluctant Samuel was to hand her over, he must have locked her up.

Alice pitied Sherry. First captured by remnants of the old kingdom, now possibly imprisoned by her own kind—she just couldn’t escape prisons. Sherry was just a little princess who wanted to go home. Why was fate so cruel to her? Always tormenting her on her way back. It wasn’t fair.

Lost in thought, Alice noticed a mask stall beside them and stopped.

The stall sold masquerade masks, their elegant patterns exuding beauty.

Merlin noticed Alice’s odd behavior and called out, "Alice?"

Alice didn’t answer. Instead, she picked up a silver masquerade mask and placed it on Merlin’s face. It actually suited him.

"Tch!" Merlin yanked the mask off, bewildered. "What are you doing? Have you lost it?!"

Alice hesitated, staring at the silver mask in her hands. Then, as if making up her mind, she held it out to Merlin and said seriously,

"Put this mask on..."

"Rescue Miss Sherry from that poisonous woman’s clutches!"

title: Chapter 18 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 18 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 18

Merlin's mood became unsettled, and he couldn't understand what Alice was up to.
Earlier, she wouldn't let him move, and now she was telling him to wear a mask and use violence to solve the problem.
However, this approach did seem feasible - it could get people rescued without interfering with his own life.
Still, was this really okay? This person wasn't the former Hero, a justice advocate, and now she was encouraging him to do something bad.
Merlin looked at Alice with a thoughtful expression, his complex emotions prompting him to ask,
"Is this really okay?"

"Yes, this is fine. It will put us in a relatively safe position and allow us to rescue Miss Shirley," Alice replied seriously.
Merlin glanced down at the silver masquerade mask in Alice's hand and thought she seemed a bit off.
"You weren't the former Hero? You were most opposed to evil, and now you're encouraging me to do something bad. This isn't noble or just at all. If I go to rescue Shirley, you know how many people will die, don't you?"
"I know, I'm very clear about what I'm saying..." Alice rubbed the silver mask with her fingers, looking into Merlin's eyes and saying,
"Justice is inherently a path filled with blood and sacrifice. I've been clear about this from the beginning, so sometimes making changes and even sacrificing things are worth it."
Merlin furrowed his brow, unable to think of a rebuttal for a moment.
"We're not doing something bad; we're doing what we think is right. My teacher once said that the world is balanced - where there's justice, there's evil. No one can maintain absolute purity, so as long as we have a clear conscience, it's okay. Even if we use despicable means, it's worth respect."
Alice spoke firmly, seemingly determined to use extreme measures to resolve the situation.
"Is that so? I admit your teacher's idea is different, but is wearing a mask really no problem?"
Merlin had some doubts about this approach.
"If you're not at ease, we can pin the blame on Sir Elgin, the great swordsman. You see, you're often mistaken for him... You two must look alike."
Alice examined Merlin.
Merlin rolled his eyes, thinking that it was no big deal - he was actually the legendary great swordsman Elgin.
"So you sold out your idol that easily? Your idol must be really unfortunate. Don't you like him the most?"
"This... Of course, I like him... " Alice's face turned red, and she looked down quickly, her expression as if she was struggling with something internally.
"But the situation is different now. Even if we do this and it seems unfair to Sir Elgin, I think he should understand our situation."
"Why are you so sure?"
Merlin found Alice's confidence puzzling.
"Because I think Sir Elgin is a kind person and a partner of justice! If it were him, he definitely wouldn't abandon Shirley to her fate!"
Alice said seriously.
Merlin wanted to say something but stopped, thinking that her words were like a tombstone for the ideals of heroes.
Merlin thought to himself that he was the Great Demon Lord, not some hero.
As for being kind, he had no such notion; if he was selfish, that was understandable.
Merlin was now full of complaints about Alice, not knowing where to start.
"Right now, Miss Shirley might be cowering in a dark prison cell, praying for us to rescue her,"
Alice said, looking down at the mask and speaking to herself in a low voice.
"We are this child's courage to survive; she simply wants to return to her hometown..."
Merlin sighed and looked away, seemingly unwilling to get involved in the trouble.
The distant clock tower rang out, startling numerous white doves.
The melodious bell sound echoed throughout the capital, reverberating.
Merlin refocused his attention, looking at the mask in Alice's hand and thinking,
"Maybe for a million gold coins... I'll make a bit of an effort?"

"You two are useless!
Not long after Mesphilde left, Samuel began to lose his temper.
"Can't even stop two amateur adventurers? Do you two qualify as my subordinates?"

"Apologies, Samuel!"
Sharp ren and Shalan knelt on one knee, deeply sorry for their earlier misstep.
"You two didn't eat your fill today? Getting bullied by a black iron adventurer like that - if this gets out, you'll be laughed at. I'm embarrassed for you!"
Samuel's emotions were volatile.
"Samuel, if I may speak frankly, that black iron adventurer isn't simple. Although he appears to have no remarkable abilities, he's extremely strange. My magic didn't work on him several times."
Shalan said with a troubled expression.
"Not work?"
Samuel became curious.
"I suspect he has rare magic-defense equipment that can effectively counter my abilities,"
Shalan said seriously.
"Can defend against your magic? What kind of equipment is this?"
Samuel stroked her chin, very clear about Shalan's abilities - even rare magic-defense equipment shouldn't be able to defend against a Saint-tier stronger's magic multiple times.
"Not just magic defense; his strength and speed are also astonishing,"
Sharp ren added.
"Stronger than you?"
Samuel became slightly serious.
"Although I didn't use my full strength at the time, I have to admit that the black iron adventurer has a slight advantage,"
Sharp ren said seriously.
"What?"
Samuel's expression turned solemn, and she asked tentatively,
"Is he a Saint-tier stronger with hidden abilities?"
"I guess so,"
Sharp ren replied firmly.
Samuel fell into thought for a moment, thinking that if Merlin had such abilities, the silver-haired woman beside him wouldn't be weak either.
"How about his companion's abilities? That silver-haired woman?"
"That woman didn't take action the entire time; she just watched. However, I deduce that her strength is likely greater than that of the black iron adventurer!"
Sharp ren analyzed seriously.
The group thought a lot, but Alice just felt she couldn't help and ended up being considered too strong to intervene.
"Ugh!"
Samuel clicked her tongue, instantly feeling annoyed and troubled by the situation.
So Samuel thought back and forth, opened a drawer beneath her, and retrieved a box from a hidden compartment.
She took out a bottle of dark-colored potion, which still emitted a faint dark aura even with the bottle cap on.
"Dark Frenzy Potion?"
Shalan, sensitive to dark elements, recognized it at a glance.
"That's right. This is also a special-grade Dark Frenzy Potion. Two bottles were secretly transported from the United Kingdom - one was given to the leader of the assassination team, and this one..."
Samuel looked at Sharp ren on the ground and directly threw it at him.
"Sharp ren, you understand my meaning, right?"

title: Chapter 49 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 49 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 49

Sharpoon stared blankly at the bottle of top-grade dark berserk potion, his mind going blank.

Beside him, Sharon said nothing, thinking this was no different from being poisoned. If Sharpoon really drank it, he'd suffer massive internal damage. Even if he survived, his days as a warrior would be over.

"Lord Samuel, you mean..."

"Drink this and hand over those two adventurers' heads." Samuel's voice was cold, utterly devoid of emotion.

"...Sharpoon was clearly hesitating, unwilling to drink this bottle of strengthening potion, because the cost was far too great.

"Since you claim your gap with that black iron adventurer isn't that big, just drink the dark berserk potion and you'll surely crush him. Even if he's been hiding his strength from the very beginning, he's not your match." Samuel said seriously.

"But... my..." Sharpoon looked up, his expression completely bewildered.

"Is this the extent of your loyalty to me?! To achieve your purpose, you must offer everything—that is your very meaning of survival!" Samuel's face twisted into a ferocious scowl, continuing, "It's not even about taking your life, yet you won't even make this small sacrifice—how can you talk of loyalty?!?"

"Lord Samuel, please believe me!" Sharpoon's emotions flared, his face filled with panic, "Even without drinking the dark berserk potion, I can still kill these two adventurers!"

"Enough! I've heard too many promises. If you still wish to follow me, drink the dark berserk potion obediently. Otherwise..." Samuel narrowed his eyes, speaking with heavy implication, "I don't recall incorrectly—your family members are suffering from a serious illness, bedridden and paralyzed."

"...Sharpoon's eyes widened, cold sweat breaking out instantly. Samuel's words were diplomatic, but the meaning was unmistakable—a bare-faced threat.

"You'd better work hard, Sharpoon. I've always considered you my most loyal subordinate..." Samuel looked down at Sharpoon, feigning comfort.

Sharpoon's expression went blank, staring vacantly at the dark berserk potion on the ground, as if he had just been sentenced to death.

Sharon stood silently beside him, a trace of mockery flashing in her eyes, secretly rejoicing in the misfortune.

Samuel's gaze drifted out the window, and a very uneasy feeling welled up inside him.

"It seems the process of making the elves cry needs to be accelerated. Very well..."

At the moment the sun was about to set.

A crimson dawn rose on the horizon.

The sky gradually darkened, twilight quietly descending.

The capital city began entering its nightlife, countless lamps flickering on.

Under the illumination of the lamps, the palace appeared exceptionally beautiful, like the nest of an immortal phoenix.

"Just one word..."

The towering clock tower chimed once more, its melodious chimes announcing the arrival of night.

A figure plummeted silently in front of the tall building of the Elven Embassy, a long sword tucked at his waist, a silver masquerade mask covering his face—it was Merlin.

At this moment, he wore a black robe, and after some disguise, was hardly recognizable.

Merlin gave the surroundings a quick glance, finding something odd. All the lights around were already lit, except for the interior of the Elven Embassy, which was pitch black, as if completely empty.

Strange.

Had everyone already left?

Merlin furrowed his brow, feeling a bit awkward. He had just discussed plans with Alice, intending to rescue Shirley and leave the capital with her overnight.

But looking at the current situation, it seemed things had changed somewhat.

Just as Merlin was puzzled, a sudden burst of flames erupted from within the Elven Embassy, with several figures flickering and disappearing inside.

Merlin's face turned black, awkwardly thinking, "What the hell is going on in there? Indoor BBQ?"

Something felt off. Merlin could clearly sense that something had happened inside the embassy.

"Crunch!" The door of the Elven Embassy was kicked open.

An elven guard stumbled out, covered in wounds, as if clawed by wild beasts.

His expression was extremely terrified, constantly alert for what was behind him.

"...Help me!"

"Huh?" Merlin narrowed his eyes, having no intention of moving, just wanting to see what was happening.

Deep within the embassy, a series of "wailing" ghostly cries echoed, sending chills down one's spine.

A shadow resembling a wild beast suddenly burst from the embassy—pale green skin, hairless all over, sharp fangs and claws, with blood-red eyes glowing eerily in the darkness.

"Corpse-Eater..." Merlin was even more confused now. Could the Elven Embassy have been attacked by corpse-eating demons?

But corpse-eating demons usually lived in very dark places. For them to appear in the capital was truly inexplicable.

"Save me! Who will save me? Please..."

The elven guard didn't finish his sentence before being pounced on by the corpse-eater.

The corpse-eater's intelligence was low, its mind filled only with fresh blood and flesh, no different from a predatory machine.

It opened its blood-soaked mouth to tear out the elven guard's throat, and blood spurted everywhere, splashing all around!

The corpse-eater made "gulping" sounds as it devoured the elven guard's body.

"Tch!" Merlin frowned, thinking, "I hope I'm not too late. If there's such a bloodthirsty monster inside, how could Shirley, who's so timid, still be alive?"

A buzzing sound erupted, the embassy trembled a few times, and then collapsed in a thunderous crash!

Countless corpse-eaters screeched as they surged up from beneath the Elven territory.

They moved on all fours with bizarre behavior, sticking out long tongues, emitting baby-like roars.

Merlin felt as though his vision was filled with a fountain of corpse-eaters, like a swarm of locusts, instantly scattering to every corner of the capital, beginning a long-absent hunt.

The corpse-eaters had been starving for so long. Any living creature that tried to escape their blood-soaked jaws would not be spared—not even the elderly, women, or children!

"So many... this many... Are they trying to turn the capital into a paradise for corpse-eaters?"

Merlin muttered to himself, pinching his nose, finding the stench of the corpse-eaters unbearable.

The horde of corpse-eaters scattered in different directions. Though chaotic, for this core city of honesty, it was a devastating calamity. The entire capital was shrouded under the dark shadow of the corpse-eaters.

"Tick-tock."

In the distance, the towering clock tower began chiming irregularly, with a strange rhythm, as if announcing the end of the capital.

The earth trembled, with hairline cracks appearing, stretching across countless streets, instantly turning everything into a scene of devastation.

"Holy crap! What else?"

Merlin steadied himself, scanning his surroundings vigilantly.

In the distant outskirts of the capital, five pillars of light shot up into the sky one after another.

The beams of light swept across the sky, piercing through the clouds, converging at the very top of the clock tower.

Then an enormous force erupted all at once, forming a five-pointed star-shaped magical formation. Its magnitude was so vast that it enveloped the entire capital city!

Endless power burst forth from above the clock tower, and with the melodious chimes, continued to spread further.

Britain's capital.

Was about to face annihilation in an instant...

title: Chapter 50
content:
Chapter 50

Volume 7 · Chapter 50

Powerful surges of magical energy rippled through the air, echoing with the toll of a bell.

A golden pentagram enveloped the sky and earth, casting countless beings beneath its towering majesty.

This grand magic formation, brimming with unimaginable power, sent shivers down the spines of all who beheld it.

The Elven race’s Three Great Forbidden Spells—*Elven Lament*—had finally been activated. The scale of it all surpassed even the wildest expectations.

The entire royal capital, bathed in radiant gold, teetered on the brink of doom.

If the legendary Twilight of the Gods truly existed, this must be what it looked like.

Serene, sacred, tranquil—yet beneath the surface, a storm of death brewed.

Five pillars of light converged at the clock tower, merging into one before soaring into the heavens.

Chaotic bell chimes intertwined with howling winds, shattering the stillness of time. A sandstorm spiraled upward, merging with the sky, stirring the very clouds.

The light pillars from the clock tower sharpened into blades, as if tearing the heavens apart, opening the gates to the underworld.

The world darkened, and all that remained was the elves’ dirge of the end.

Dark clouds swirled slowly, coiling around the clock tower like something on the verge of awakening.

Merlin withdrew his gaze, furrowing his brow. *What the hell is going on?* he thought. *Is Great Britain about to fall?*

A magic formation of this scale couldn’t have been set up in a short time—everything had been planned long in advance.

*Gurgle... gurgle...*

Countless ghouls gathered below Merlin, wailing like infants, their long tongues flailing wildly, ravenous for his flesh.

Hundreds of crimson eyes locked onto him, surging forward in a frenzy. These mindless creatures knew nothing of power—they only craved meat. After gaining their freedom, Merlin was the first living thing they had seen. How could they let such a feast slip away?

"Ha, you want to eat *me* too? Now that’s... something," Merlin muttered with a wry smile, never imagining he’d be seen as prey one day.

*Skreeeeeeech!*

The ghouls swarmed upward, scaling buildings, forming living ladders to reach Merlin in the heights.

Their shrieks and roars were a tidal wave of hunger.

The horde blotted out the sky, claws and fangs bared as they surrounded Merlin, cutting off all escape.

"Looks like I’ll have to teach you how to pick your prey properly..."

Merlin spoke lightly, then vanished beneath the ghouls’ tide. Wave after wave of the mindless beasts surged forward, each hoping to claim a piece of him.

A lethal burst of sword energy erupted—

In an instant, every ghoul in the area was reduced to bloody fragments!

These dim-witted creatures probably died without ever understanding what happened.

Chunks of flesh and gore *plopped* onto the ground, staining the streets red.

Merlin sheathed his short tachi, gazing at the royal capital now enveloped by the pentagram.

Fires raged everywhere, screams and beastly roars echoing in a chaotic symphony.

In the distance, the dark clouds churned, and the clock tower’s pillar of light swept across the land.

The scene was one of utter desolation—Britain was truly on the brink.

Merlin furrowed his brow, wiping the splattered blood from his face with a sigh.

"Disgusting..."

---

At the peak of the clock tower stood a structure resembling a grand hall.

Stained glass windows cast prismatic hues across the chamber.

At its center, a crimson magic formation rotated slowly, ceaselessly draining the surrounding magic.

This was the core of *Elven Lament*—it required the caster’s constant upkeep. If this were destroyed, the entire grand formation would collapse.

A forbidden spell that reversed life and death indeed demanded far more than any other magic.

Samuel stood before the crimson array, chanting incantations to accelerate the spell’s rotation.

Every detail had been checked. With absolute certainty, Samuel had chosen to initiate the plan to resurrect the Dark Elven King. It seemed irreversible now.

She had dropped her disguise as a white elf, revealing her true black skin.

To greet the King’s return in her true form as a dark elf filled her with exhilaration.

Shalan yanked the chain, dragging Sherry upward.

Sherry had been locked underground for days, her cries for help met with silence. The howls of ghouls at night had nearly shattered her mind.

"Move!"

Shalan shoved Sherry forward without hesitation, pushing her toward Samuel. The thrill of bullying a princess was oddly satisfying.

Sherry tumbled to the ground, weak and helpless, with no strength to resist.

Samuel paused her chanting, sparing a moment to glance at Sherry, her face twisted in mockery.

"One night apart, and you look quite worn out."

"...What are you trying to do?!" Sherry asked timidly, her heart pounding with unease.

"Can’t you tell? As royalty, you must recognize this formation," Samuel said indifferently. The Three Great Forbidden Spells of the elves were secrets known only to the royal family. She had learned them from the Dark Elven King himself.

Sherry stared at the slowly rotating crimson array, frozen for a moment before gasping in shock. "...This is *Elven Lament*!"

"As expected of the beloved youngest daughter of the Elven King—you even know the Three Great Forbidden Spells. I suppose this is your first time seeing one. Surprised?" Samuel asked with a teasing tone.

"You—what are you doing?! This spell will turn this human city into a ghost town!" Sherry’s voice trembled, fully aware of the cost of *Elven Lament*.

"I’ve said it before—I serve His Majesty Asmodus. Naturally, I’m resurrecting the great Dark Elven King! *Hahahaha!*"

"...How could you?! My uncle—he’s evil! If he’s resurrected, it’ll be a crisis for our entire elven race! Why don’t you understand?!" Sherry cried in terror.

"Your *father* is the evil one! He murdered his own brother with his own hands—he’s no better than a beast! His Majesty Asmodus is the true king of the dark elves! The one we swear loyalty to! He will lead us into a new era—" Samuel snarled, her fangs making her look like a haggard witch.

"Why are you so obsessed with my uncle? Can’t you trust my father a little more?" Sherry pleaded, tears welling in her eyes, on the verge of breaking down.

"A man who doesn’t spare even his own kin isn’t worth our trust!" Samuel lunged, seizing Sherry by the throat and lifting her off the ground.

*Cough... cough...*

Sherry’s face paled. She realized what was coming next. *Elven Lament* required the soul of royalty as a key—and she was the perfect choice.

Sherry thrashed in Samuel’s grip, clawing and scratching, but the power gap was too vast. She couldn’t break free.

"Hehehe..." Samuel’s laughter was wicked, her eyes burning with unbridled fanaticism. Without hesitation, she hurled Sherry into the center of the crimson magic formation.

"Princess Sherry..."

"Be a good girl and serve as the stepping stone for our resurrection!" (*>ω<*)9

title: Chapter 51 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 51 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 51

Shirley was callingly thrown by Samuel into the magic circle, where an unknown force immediately snatched her mid-air!

Her arms were spread wide, as though she were enduring immense agony, her eyes rolling back as she continuously let out heart-wrenching, miserable screams.

Poor Shirley. She had hoped to return home soon, only to suffer this catastrophe for no reason at all.

She felt as if fifty sharp needles were piercing her body simultaneously, countless tortures gathering upon her, driving her to unbearable suffering.

She wanted nothing more than to end it all, yet the dream of returning to her homeland still held her together.

A crystal-clear tear fell from the corner of Shirley's eye. She could only hope someone would come save her, two figures flashing through her mind.

"Miss Alice, Mr. Merlin, please, I beg you, come save me....

Sarah gently stroked her own cheek, a morbid excitement spreading across her face. "As expected, Your Highness the Princess's voice is the most beautiful."

"Indeed. Her Highness is only now paying back the sins her father committed. It is all the punishment she deserves." Samuel wore a mocking smile as he said this in a cold voice.

"You speak wisely, Lord Samuel...." Sarah nodded, then continued, "Everything is prepared. May I ask, when will His Majesty Archdale be revived?"

"It will take some time. Once I completely separate Princess Shirley's soul, that will be the moment His Majesty Archdale is revived!" Samuel laughed grotesquely, then abruptly shifted the subject. "What about Sharplun? Where did he go?"

"He went to carry out the task you assigned him. He should already be engaged in battle with those two adventurers by now," Sarah said meaningfully.

"Is that so? Well then, there is no need to concern ourselves with that fellow Sharplun. He has no value to us now," Samuel said coldly, clearly treating Sharplun as expendable. "You may leave. I imagine the Thorn Knights have already been mobilized as well. I need to stay here and protect the magic circle. Go block those foolish youths and prevent them from approaching the Clock Tower."

"At once!" Sarah bowed slightly, excitement flashing in her eyes, as though she had long been eager for something like this.

"I've long wanted to test myself against the Thorn Knights."

"If they too can produce sounds like a young maiden's...

"How beautiful a sight that would be."

"Ah~! It's simply thrilling."

The great five-pointed star magic circle blazed with brilliant light, illuminating the entire royal capital as if it were midday.

The colossal pillar of light emitted from the Clock Tower churned the dark clouds in the sky, forming a massive vortex that resembled a gateway to another dimension.

Suddenly, at the center of the vortex, a huge red eyeball appeared, rolling around aimlessly as though it were alive!

The eerie eyeball radiated a scarlet glow. It was enormous, hovering above the Clock Tower and replacing the moon that should have been there.

This eye belonged to the Dark Elf King. The revival process had already begun, allowing him to peer once more across all of Britain from the rift between the underworld and the living world.

The Dark Elf King's red pupil blazed even brighter, as though mocking the panicked, fleeing humans. Millions of London citizens were gripped by further waves of terror.

Countless ghouls had already scattered throughout the royal capital. The hungry monsters ravenously devoured humans without restraint. No one knew how many had perished in this calamity.

The once-prosperous royal capital was instantly plunged into a sea of flames. Fear dominated the city, and the damage was beyond estimation.

At the Noble Hotel—

A ghoul leapt onto a rooftop, its scarlet pupils scanning the area before fixing on the brightly lit hotel. It immediately began drooling.

Though these monsters possessed little intelligence and knew nothing but eat, their sense of smell was unexpectedly keen. They detected from afar the scent of numerous living humans within the hotel.

The ghoul let out a howl to the heavens, drawing the attention of other ghouls, signaling that it wanted to turn the place into a feeding ground!

Swiftly, countless ghouls swept across the sky, all rushing toward where the food had gathered...

The flames of war raged, and yesterday's gleaming houses crackled in the fire.

"Mama, Mama... waaah..."

A little girl in a tattered dress stood where she was, tears streaming down her face as she held a rabbit plushie and cried pitifully.

She had likely been separated from her family during the evacuation. Terrified that danger lurked everywhere, she didn't dare move from spot to spot.

The poor child had no idea that the louder she cried, the more likely she was to attract the ghouls' attention. They had a particular craving for soft-skinned, tender little girls.

As expected, four ghouls suddenly appeared behind the little girl and pounced on her, jaws wide open, each vying to be the first to devour her.

"Awoooooo!"

The little girl was utterly terrified, her eyes bulging as she collapsed onto the ground, her expression one of sheer horror.

At this critical moment, a silver-haired girl flashed forward to stand in front of the little girl. It was Alice, who had been busy rescuing people everywhere!

"Don't you dare overstep yourselves, you filthy things!"

Alice tightened her grip on her pure silver fine sword and swung it fiercely, sending silver light flashing in all directions.

Her sword techniques, dense as raindrops, immediately pierced the four ghouls, who screamed in agony, clearly severely wounded.

The effect of [Light Aria] dealing double damage to dark creatures had once again played a crucial role!

"Hug me tight!"

Alice embraced the little girl on the ground, letting her hold on firmly to prevent any mishaps along the way.

Without hesitation, Alice took off running, rapidly retreating toward the Noble Hotel.

After all, there were far too many ghouls nearby, and they were tough to kill and highly aggressive, making them difficult for Alice to handle. If she encountered too many ghouls, Alice could very well fall into crisis.

Alice channeled high-tier battle aura, darting left and right through the narrow alleyways at top speed, continuously dodging the ghouls' attacks.

At first, Alice had been waiting at the hotel for Merlin to return with Shirley, and Cecilia had even prepared the carriage for them to leave the city.

Then suddenly the entire royal capital shook as though hit by an earthquake. The great five-pointed star magic circle unfolded abruptly, plunging the whole city into hellish suffering and reducing it to the current state of ruin.

Alice made the prompt decision to save people first, turning the Noble Hotel into a temporary refuge to resist the ghouls' assaults.

Though the hotel's owner was not pleased about accepting civilian refugees and muttered complaints, Cecilia forcefully cast "Silence" on him, which settled the matter.

(Forcing a staff blow to the head until the victim passes out = Silence spell.)

"Mama... ma..." The little girl, seemingly too frightened to think straight, was calling anyone she saw "Mom."

A vein throbbed on Alice's forehead as she awkwardly replied, "I'm not your mommy. When we're safe, I'll help you find your mother."

"Waaah..." The little girl, clearly still in a daze from fright, said nothing and simply burrowed into Alice's arms, sobbing.

Alice furrowed her elegant brows and silently held the little girl tighter, trying to make her feel a bit more at ease.

Then she quickened her pace, intending to charge out of the peril-filled alley—

Now that disaster had struck,

there were probably many more children like this who had been separated from their families, right?

All I can do is what little I'm able to manage.

How unpleasant. If only I were a bit stronger...

(=_=)

title: Chapter 52 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 52 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 7 · Chapter 52

There were many ghouls lurking in the alley. Scenting the presence of living humans, they converged toward Alice.

Alice clutched the little girl in her arms and sprinted desperately, her heavy breathing betraying that her battle energy was nearly exhausted.

She glanced back. Countless scarlet eyes were locked onto her as the ghouls closed in with hungry howls.

With a look of disgust, Alice fired ice spikes behind her to harass the pursuing horde.

She needs to speed up. At this rate, they'd definitely catch up!

Alice fretted with worry. Being attacked from both front and rear left her somewhat overwhelmed.

"Aaaooooh!"

A piercing shriek rang out. Two ghouls suddenly charged forward with clawed hands and bared fangs, as if determined to block Alice's path.

"Hah!"

Alice channeled her high-tier battle energy and swung her slender sword with all her might, cleanly decapitating both ghouls.

She didn't stop, stepping over the corpses as she continued forward.

The exit was right ahead. Victory was within reach!

Alice quickened her pace and swiftly burst out of the perilous alley.

But just then, ghouls that had been lurking on the rooftops for a long time seized upon Alice's momentary lapse in vigilance and descended from above!

The ghoul approached Alice silently, its bloodied maw gaping wide, intending to bite straight through her neck.

By the time Alice caught the stench of blood, it was already too late. Her eyes widened as she watched the creature launch itself at her.

"Miss Alice, lower your head!"

A thunderous shout made Alice drop without time to think, bowing her head like lightning.

Immediately after, a long spear came stabbing forward with blinding speed!

It pierced straight through the ghoul's skull, pinning it against the wall with its eyes rolled back.

Even mortally wounded, the ghoul still had its long tongue lolling out, a testament to how tenacious its vitality was.

Alice let out a long breath and looked at the arriving Kyle. "Thank you."

"No need to thank me. You should also be more careful, Miss Alice," Kyle said, his brows furrowed as he withdrew his spear.

"How are the refugees doing?" Alice asked patiently.

"They've mostly been settled safely. Lady Cecilia is overseeing their care," Kyle answered earnestly.

Alice nodded, her expression grave, and sheathed her slender sword. "There are no more survivors in this area. Let's head back quickly."

"If we're not here, this place will be extremely dangerous."

The royal palace.

Inside the corridor.

The palace had entered a state of high alert, with the Queen's safety as the absolute top priority.

How many waves of ghoul attacks had this place endured? After the brief disturbance, the ghouls had been wiped out by the elite Bauhinia Knight Order, and things had returned to a comparatively safe state.

But the city below the palace remained in dire straits.

Clatter, clatter, clatter.

Frequent footsteps echoed through the palace corridor. Court maids on either side paused and bowed respectfully.

Four knights clad in silver-gilt armor and draped in bright red Bauhinia war cloaks were heading outward.

From their attire, they were clearly top-tier knights of the Bauhinia Knight Order, radiating a distinctly imposing presence.

At their head was the First Thorn Knight, Meisfefurudo. Her expression was grim, deeply pessimistic about the current danger, her hand never leaving her sword hilt.

Following behind was the Seventh Thorn Knight, Morison. His countenance wasn't much better than Meisfefurudo's. Judging from his alert posture, his expression was very serious — completely unlike his usual grinning self.

As for the other two knights, they were respectively —

the Eleventh Knight, Wineifuredo. He was a middle-aged man with a thick beard that actually looked quite attractive.

Especially with his braided ponytail tied at the back — he appeared to be a stylish, fashion-forward gentleman.

Wineifuredo was known as the "Earth Magician," renowned for his composure and reserve. He spoke sparingly.

This made Wineifuredo rather low-key, the Thorn Knight with the fewest news appearances and less renown than the others.
