Yet his earth magic was absolutely masterful. An earthquake shaking mountains was commonplace with a wave of his hand, and his profound magical power was second to none.

He had secretly suppressed no small number of rebellious forces in the past. Many people remembered the boulders suspended in the sky, not knowing it had been Wineifuredo's doing.

Next to him was the Fifth Thorn Knight, Miriyasu, handsome and striking with dazzling golden long hair, his armor spotlessly polished and gleaming — the very picture of a playboy.

Miriyasu's personality was the exact opposite of Wineifuredo's. He loved performing and showing himself off. Before the great swordsman Ergin became famous across Britannia, Miriyasu had been the kingdom's talk of the town, the idol of countless lovesick maidens, the white prince of their dreams.

But once Ergin appeared, Miriyasu's halo dimmed considerably. He was no longer as popular as before — apparently, girls preferred men with an air of mystery.

This made Miriyasu envious and bitter, turning him into a quite radical figure. No one clamored more loudly than him for Ergin to be brought to justice, as if he longed to chop off the great swordsman's head with his own hands.

The reason was simple: anyone who dared to steal the title of Britannia's most handsome man would suffer a terrible fate and must be made to disappear.

Thus, Miriyasu harbored deep hostility toward Ergin and strongly supported Meisfefurudo's plan to lock up the man who had stolen his title.

Although Miriyasu was a narcissist with a somewhat petty nature, his strength was undeniable and qualified him as truly powerful.

Perhaps no one in Britannia was unaware of the title "Starlight Swordsman" belonging to Miriyasu — it was a name known to every household.

Miriyasu's swordsmanship was extraordinarily flamboyant. Rather than calling it combat, it was more like a personal performance show, full of elegance, brilliance, and beauty.

Each time he danced with his slender sword in hand, he reaped lives amid his enemies' gasps of admiration, far removed from the image of a killing maniac.

At this moment, Miriyasu's expression was calm, already itching to perform. After all, a stage so carefully prepared must not go to waste.

The Thorn Knights were in a hurry, seemingly having already kicked off their counterattack.

"How has Queen Majesty's arrangements been?" Meisfefurudo asked.

"She has already taken refuge in the secret chamber. There shouldn't be any problems — Lady Catherine is responsible for her safety," Morison replied earnestly.

"I see."

Meisfefurudo nodded, slightly relieved. "Entrusting this to Catherine should be fine."

"There definitely won't be any problems. After all, she is a Thorn Knight ranked eighth — her strength is guaranteed," Morison affirmed seriously.

"That's true. We can only rely on Catherine now," Meisfefurudo said, her brows drawn together in worry. That enormous five-pointed star outside — it was clearly no ordinary magic circle. What awful consequences it might bring was still unknown.

What should they do now?

Only five Thorn Knights were currently in the capital.

And they knew nothing about the enemy's information.

It seemed they were about to face a fierce battle.

(-"一)

title: Chapter 53
content:
Chapter 53

Volume 7 · Chapter 53

"Now, entrusting Her Majesty the Queen's safety to Catherine is the best choice. There's no need to worry too much." Winifred said seriously, her mature voice carrying a hint of magnetism.

"I know. I don’t distrust Catherine," Mesphield hesitated for a moment before saying faintly, "It would’ve been better if Sahadin were here."

Sahadin, as the Thorn Shield, was the best choice for protecting important figures.

But unfortunately, he had been instantly killed by the Twin Sword Saints not long ago.

Winifred remained silent, showing no reaction to the death of her comrade—perhaps she was just not good with words and didn’t know what to say at a time like this.

Morris, however, was more straightforward. He wore a slightly nostalgic expression. "Yeah, if Sahadin hadn’t sacrificed himself, entrusting the important mission of protecting Her Majesty the Queen to that tough guy would’ve been the best choice."

"Hmph." Milieus let out a light laugh, sweeping his golden hair behind his shoulder. "The man’s already dead. What’s the point of talking about it now?"

"Don’t say that, Milieus. He was still our comrade. It’s not wrong to mourn him a little, right?" Morris said, his expression carrying a hint of displeasure.

"Sahadin’s death, in the end, was because he was too weak. If he had been strong enough, he should’ve returned in triumph, not let Elgin the Great Swordsman steal all the limelight." Milieus said with a half-smile, as if he didn’t take his comrade’s death to heart at all.

"You really have a problem with Elgin the Great Swordsman, huh? He did single-handedly wipe out the remnants of the former kingdom. In terms of the bigger picture, he’s on the same side as us." Morris couldn’t help but state the facts.

"It’s not that I have a problem with Elgin the Great Swordsman. It’s that he abuses his power, no different from a thug. For Her Majesty the Queen, he’s an unstable factor. Isn’t it only natural to eliminate him?" Milieus said indifferently.

"But I’ve thought it over. That guy hasn’t done anything truly unforgivable. On the contrary, he’s saved quite a few civilians along the way." Morris furrowed his brow, presenting his own view.

"Morris, you’re still too naive. Judging whether a person is good or evil isn’t about what they’ve done—it’s about what Her Majesty the Queen thinks." Milieus, who clearly had his own grudge against Elgin the Great Swordsman, shifted the blame onto someone else. "Don’t believe me? You can ask little Windsor~"

"Don’t call me little Windsor, or I’ll kill you!" Mesphield glared at Milieus, furious. She hated it when people called her by her name with a "little" prefix, as if she were still a child.

"Oh~, Miss Mesphield is angry. That’s a little scary." Milieus inched away slightly, putting on a flippant air.

"As for the question of Elgin the Great Swordsman’s morality, we don’t need to delve too deep. We just need to remember that we are forever loyal to Her Majesty the Queen." Mesphield’s expression turned serious as she looked back. "Morris, when you speak, be mindful of your position. Don’t pick the wrong side."

"Hahaha, got scolded, didn’t you?" Milieus looked at Morris mockingly, wearing a schadenfreude expression.

"You’re so annoying." Morris shot Milieus a glare before changing the subject. "I just wanted to mourn Sahadin a little. It was you who had to bring up Elgin the Great Swordsman."

"The weak aren’t worthy of our mourning. If the late Sahadin knew we were mourning him, he’d probably find it unbearably humiliating." Milieus spoke with a hint of sincerity. "That guy was kind-hearted, but he’d never let his dignity be tarnished."

Morris froze for a moment, then lowered his head and muttered, "That does sound like him. That rough man really hated it when people pitied him."

"Enough. Let’s stop talking about useless things." Mesphield cut off their idle chatter and continued, "Right now, there are five Thorn Knights in the royal capital. The other knights are out on missions, so our forces are limited. Saving the capital depends on the four of us. Rescuing the civilians is our top priority."

"Oh! I’m already pumped up! Let’s smash the ghouls’ heads open!" Morris tugged at his gauntlets, made of silvery-white precious metal and covered in scratches—clear proof of his many battles.

"Once we’ve mostly cleared out the ghouls and secured the safety of the people, we’ll head to the Clock Tower together." Mesphield paused, frowning. "We still don’t understand the cause of all this, but the instigator is likely at the top of the Clock Tower. Someone capable of summoning such a massive magic formation is no ordinary foe. We must not take this lightly!"

"That’s a wise choice." Winifred nodded in agreement with the plan.

"The moment for performance has finally arrived. The mysterious enemy will only wail in despair under my magnificent swordsmanship." Milieus grinned, quietly muttering to himself, "I have to do my best. I’ll crush Elgin the Great Swordsman underfoot, reclaim my title as the most handsome man in Great Britain, and then—ha ha ha~—the most beautiful man in all of Great Britain will undoubtedly be me."

Though Milieus had kept his voice low, Morris still caught it.

Morris stared at Milieus with a blank expression, listening to his ape-like laughter, and awkwardly thought, *This guy would be better off as a star in a circus. He shouldn’t be a Thorn Knight. I always feel like there’s a traitor in our knightly order.*

"All available forces of the knightly order have assembled. Let’s move out."

Mesphield couldn’t be bothered to care about their personal reasons for fighting. As long as they shared the same goal, that was enough.

The palace gates slowly swung open. Outside, countless purple orchid banners were already fluttering fiercely in the wind beneath the dark clouds—

A full forty thousand elite Purple Orchid Knights stood in perfect formation, as if awaiting Mesphield’s command.

They were clad in full armor, gripping sharp swords, standing proudly before the palace gates.

Though forty thousand wasn’t a huge number, the Purple Orchid Knights valued quality over quantity. The combat strength of this group was far beyond that of any ragtag army.

The Purple Orchid Knights looked up at the platform where the four Thorn Knights stood, representing the highest combat power. Mesphield, in particular, drew all eyes.

Everyone knew it had been a long time since so many Thorn Knights had been deployed at once. This battle was clearly no ordinary one, and they all steeled themselves, ready for the challenge.

Mesphield let out a sharp whistle toward the sky.

Her mount, the Black Mountain Giant Eagle, descended from the heavens, landing in front of her and bowing its head.

Mesphield gently stroked the Black Mountain Giant Eagle’s smooth feathers before mounting it.

She pulled the reins, and the eagle spread its massive wings, stirring up a fierce gust of wind!

Mesphield’s lavender hair danced in the wind as she drew her golden straight sword, pointing it toward the burning city below.

"To defend the glory of Great Britain, let us draw the sacred swords bestowed upon us by Her Majesty the Queen!"

"Purple Orchid Knights—full advance!!!"

title: Chapter 54 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 54 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 54

The Noble Hotel.

Alice and Kail returned.

They found Cecilia shivering and hiding behind the door, warily observing her surroundings.

Just then, Kail had been accompanying her, but Alice had gone to rescue people for a long time and hadn't returned, causing concern for safety.

So Cecilia forced herself to overcome her fear and asked Kail to go meet Alice.

Because relying solely on herself and Kail to protect this place was quite difficult.

Moreover, the Noble Hotel was now overcrowded with many city residents.

If something happened, it wouldn't just be Cecilia and Kail who would die, but countless civilians.

With so many living humans gathered, they would inevitably attract the attention of ghouls, so Alice's powers were indispensable.

Although Cecilia usually acted superior and looked down on others, when it came to right and wrong, she still made choices.

Not just because Cecilia was essentially a kind person, but also because as a priest, her nature was to help the weak and dislike seeing too many people die.

So when Alice first proposed turning this place into a temporary shelter, Cecilia agreed wholeheartedly, even though she verbally complained, her actions showed her true willingness.

Cecilia was sweating and observing her surroundings with fear, hoping Kail and Alice would return soon, or else relying on herself to protect this place would be a joke.

In fact, as a priest, Cecilia had no combat abilities and couldn't defeat ghouls, but she could dispel them.

The priesthood had a natural restraint on dark creatures.

However, Cecilia was a timid noblewoman who, when seeing ghouls, would be too scared to move and fall into a foolish state.

"Kail, we're back," Kail called out from a distance.

Cecilia was startled, her hair standing on end.

Seeing Kail, her anxiety dissipated, but then she felt wronged.

Cecilia opened the door, ran to Kail, and hit his chest with her small fists.

"Why are you so late? You're such a foolish knight! Do you know how scared I was here? I'm so angry!"

"I'm extremely sorry, Cecilia," Kail said with an awkward expression, "Alice was searching for people a bit too deeply, and I had to look for her for a long time."

"I don't care! You're just late, and I'm hitting you! Hit you, hit you, hit you!" Cecilia continued to punch Kail's face.

"This..." Kail looked innocent, but didn't dare to argue back.

"Don't take it out on Kail; it's my responsibility," Alice said with a sigh, slightly hugging the little girl in her arms.

Cecilia stopped her tantrum, looked at Alice with dissatisfaction, and said, "Seriously, with such a big incident happening, where is Merlin? Not even a shadow can be seen! You guys went to investigate the assassin this morning, and now only you are back."

"Yes, we did go investigate the assassin," Alice nodded.

"What were the results?" Cecilia asked curiously.

"That..." Alice hesitated, thinking it was complicated to explain, involving the elf tribe.

Cecilia was puzzled, seeing Alice's reluctance to explain, and didn't develop the habit of inquiring about others' secrets, so she asked directly, "I just want to know where Merlin is? I haven't seen him all day, it's really strange."

"That..." Alice hesitated, thinking Merlin had gone to do something bad, and she didn't feel right saying it, as she was also an accomplice.

"Yes, the situation is critical now, and we really need Merlin's power," Kail said with a serious expression.

"Alice looked around awkwardly and said, "Actually, I don't know where that guy went..."

"Ha!?" Cecilia widened her eyes, finding it incredible.

"Uh, don't joke about this, Alice," Kail found this answer hard to accept.

"That guy often does this, always disappearing mysteriously, and I don't know where he goes, I'm used to it, haha," Alice laughed awkwardly, thinking Merlin had gone to do something like assassination, and she couldn't let a third person know.

"You're Merlin's wife, and you don't know where he is? How silly can you be?" Cecilia said with a frown.

"Who are you calling silly? I just don't know, okay?" Alice retorted angrily.

"Don't be like this, Cecilia," Kail thought it wasn't a good time for a fight, given the crisis.

"Move away, this woman is really careless," Cecilia pushed Kail aside and continued, "I seriously suspect you're a fake wife, can't even control your husband's whereabouts, do you understand how bad this is?"

"What's bad? I don't think so," Alice ignored Cecilia and walked into the Noble Hotel.

"What if Merlin cheats on you, has many mistresses outside, and you're such a silly girl, wouldn't you be kept in the dark forever?" Cecilia said earnestly, "Or are you the type who doesn't care how many mistresses Merlin has?"

"Alice scowled and said, "Our business, don't need you to manage, just shut up."

"Cecilia got angry, almost getting hurt by Alice's words.

Kail thought Cecilia's anxiety was reasonable, so he approached her and said gently, "Alice, our lady is just concerned, you see the situation now, we need to protect this place, without Merlin's power, it's indeed a bit difficult."

"Don't worry, we few are enough," Alice said stubbornly.

"Kail was speechless and didn't say anything else.

Cecilia noticed the little girl in Alice's arms and asked curiously, "This child is alone?"

"I found her like that, maybe she got separated from her family," Alice explained tactfully, not saying directly that the girl's mother might have died.

The little girl snuggled into Alice's arms, still looking a bit frightened.

In this chaotic situation, maybe only this fake warmth from Alice was a bit comforting.

Cecilia remained silent, still sympathizing, but not willing to show it on her face.

She didn't know how many people would die in this disaster, maybe the girl's mother was among them.

Seeing the little girl's dirty appearance, maybe she hadn't expected to become an orphan.

Cecilia thought she shouldn't have quarreled with Alice just now, it was a bit excessive.

Alice put down the little girl, helped her wipe away tears, and said kindly to the girl, "Go with this sister to a safe place, okay?"

The little girl held a rabbit doll, looked at Alice, and shook her head silently, looking like she was afraid of strangers.

Alice patiently said, "This sister is not a bad person, in a safe place, there won't be scary monsters attacking you."

The little girl's eyes flashed with fear, thought to herself for a moment, and nodded silently.

"Come, follow sister," Cecilia smiled kindly and took the little girl's hand, leading her to a safe place.

After Cecilia left, Kail finally couldn't help but show his worried expression and asked, "Alice, can we really protect this place? There are at least a few thousand refugees gathered here, and a large number of ghouls will come attracted by the smell."

Alice looked up, met Kail's anxious eyes, and seriously replied,

"At this point...

Do we have a choice?"

title: Chapter 55 — Monthly Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 55 — Monthly Bonus Update

Volume 7 · Chapter 55

“Kel fell silent, unsure of how to respond.

“Are you thinking of abandoning these refugees and escaping directly?” Alice glanced at Kel.

Kel tried to speak, but his words got stuck, and he looked down with a guilty conscience.

Alice hadn't guessed wrong; Kel thought that if they abandoned these refugees, they could escape safely.

Facing such a ferocious danger, although they couldn't win, escaping wasn't difficult.

However, doing so would be extremely inhumane, and they would have to live with guilt.

In fact, Kel wasn't a bad person; in this situation, it was natural for him to think this way.

After all, Kel was a knight who protected Cecilia, and it wasn't his duty to ensure the safety of others; everything had to consider the safety of the lady.

“If you really did that, you'd be the same as a ghoul, a monster wearing human skin,” Alice said faintly.

Kel suddenly stopped, his face pale with fear, and thought carefully; indeed, it was very bad, wasn't it the ugly side of humanity he usually condemned? He hadn't expected himself to become like this.

Alice gazed into the distance, the capital burning in flames, with the occasional screams of ghouls.

“Failing to save those in need is being an accomplice, a stain that can't be washed away for life.

“Today, you abandoned these helpless people; tomorrow, when you encounter danger, others will abandon you too.

“At that time, you'll think, 'Why didn't anyone save me? You're all unforgivable villains.'”

“You'll never recall your actions today; you'll only selfishly shift the blame onto others.”

“I didn't mean it, Alice, please don't misunderstand,” Kel said, filled with shame.

“You're only thinking of Cecilia; I understand, and I'm not accusing you,” Alice sighed.

“Sorry, Alice,” Kel's brow furrowed, feeling uncomfortable, “if Cecilia is in danger, even dying won't make up for it.”

“If it were Cecilia, she wouldn't agree with you doing this either,” Alice said softly.

Kel fell silent; although both he and Alice were high-ranking, resisting a large number of ghouls was still too difficult, and a slight mistake could lead to disaster.

“Our power is limited; if Merlin were here, it would be fine,” Kel said.

“Why not try to do it yourself when you're praying for others to help? Have some confidence; we can do it. Besides,” Alice thought for a moment and said faintly, “Merlin himself said he couldn't save everyone.”

Kel was stunned, not understanding the meaning of this sentence; he only felt a sense of helplessness.

“Graaah graaah graaah!”

A strange sound echoed, and a ghoul climbed onto the roof, howling at the sky.

Soon, countless ghouls rushed over, covering the sky, their glowing eyes like death in the darkness.

“They've come,” Alice drew her slender sword, and her high-ranking aura continued to rise.

“They must have followed the human scent,” Kel held his long spear, ready to attack.

The hungry ghouls didn't care; they swarmed forward, their mouths open wide, moving like monkeys, and their speed was extremely fast.

In the eyes of ghouls, there were no powerful enemies; as long as there was fresh flesh, they could fill their bellies.

Alice swung her slender sword, activating 「Zero Boundary」, slowing down the ghouls' movement speed.

Immediately, a hundred 「Ice Crystal Swords」 appeared behind her and shot forward rapidly.

The sound of breaking through the air was continuous; the front row of ghouls was pierced by the ice crystal swords and nailed to the ground.

Some were killed instantly, while others couldn't move; the effect of the simultaneous ice sword attack was like a meteor shower.

Any ghoul approaching Alice was pierced by the ice swords, falling into a passive state.

The combination of 「Zero Boundary」 and 「Ice Crystal Swords」 was effective; first, they were slowed down, and then the ice swords were easier to hit.

However, ghouls had strong vitality; even if injured, they didn't know how to die and continued to rush forward.

Kel entered a cautious combat state, his long spear dancing, full of power.

Every spear thrust pierced the ghoul's head, dealing a fatal blow.

Although they could withstand it for a short time, the situation was still not optimistic.

This was because there were endless ghouls rushing over, never tired.

“Alice, the situation isn't good! Kel wiped a cold sweat from his forehead and communicated with Alice while killing enemies.

Alice's slender sword cut mercilessly, her brow furrowed, knowing the situation was bad, but she still said,

“Don't panic; ghouls aren't social creatures. After cleaning up this wave, there shouldn't be more.”

Kel frowned, thinking to himself, really?

Just as Kel was puzzled, a loud shout echoed in the sky, “Aaaaahhhh!”

A dark object fell from the sky, crashing down behind Alice and Kel, sending up a massive cloud of dust.

“What...? Kel's eyes widened, looking back, unsure of what had happened.

Alice's expression was also shocked; a drop of cold sweat slid down her forehead, and she stared, clearly feeling an extremely violent Saint-tier aura.

At this moment, neither of them knew if this mysterious person, who had fallen from the sky, was an enemy or a friend.

However, it was certain that it wasn't Merlin, because Merlin didn't have an aura.

Alice and Kel instinctively took a step back, showing a defensive posture, wary of this mysterious person.

Before the dust could dissipate, it was dispersed by someone's body, allowing Alice and Kel to see the situation clearly.

A giant-like figure stood before them.

At 40 feet tall, it was like a moving house.

Its incredibly strong body had dark elements overflowing from every muscle.

Its entire body was covered in black skin, with bright red veins pulsating with life.

Although its body was massive, its head was small, with pointed ears visible.

This guy was Shaprion, under the effect of the special dark frenzy potion, completely transformed into something inhuman.

Shaprion had left the elf embassy early, so he hadn't met Merlin and chose to wait for the most chaotic moment in the capital, attacking alone.

The effect of the special dark frenzy potion was astonishing, making Shaprion's strength surge; previously a Saint-tier strong, now he was close to the peak.

“Who is this?” Kel's body trembled, unable to breathe under the enormous pressure.

“Impossible,” Alice's brow was furrowed, her shocked expression frozen on her face, “how did he become like this?”

Shaprion felt like he had endless super strong power; his strength was now beyond recognition.

He looked down at the two tiny humans, opened his mouth full of fangs, and roared,

“Two adventurers like insects; I'll twist your heads off!

“Come and die! I've had enough! ! !”

title: Chapter 56
content:
Chapter 56

Volume 7 · Chapter 56

The feeling of fear suddenly welled up from deep within Alice’s heart.

Overwhelmed by the oppressive Saint-tier aura, Alice froze in place.

There was no need to think further—Alice’s current strength was no match for Sharpren.

The enemy could have seriously injured Alice with just a flick of their finger.

As for Kyle, there was no need to mention it—he had already been completely terrified by Sharpren.

The mutated Sharpren looked down at Alice, but didn’t see Merlin, leaving him feeling a bit suspicious.

However, it didn’t matter that Merlin wasn’t there, because according to speculation, Alice’s strength was greater than Merlin’s, so she had to be more careful.

“You humiliated me so badly today—now it’s time to pay the price!!!”

Sharpren roared in anger. Since he didn’t know Alice, he decided to make a tentative attack to see what her skills were.

Sharpren raised his massive fist without hesitation and slammed it down on the stunned Alice!

The dark fist came crashing down like Mount Tai, making people feel utterly overwhelmed by the pressure.

The gusts of wind carried Saint-tier fighting spirit, and for Alice, this power was like crushing withered branches and rotten wood. If she was hit, she would surely die!

The gap in strength between enemy and ally was too great, and even a tentative attack from the other side was something Alice couldn’t withstand at the moment.

Alice, bearing the immense pressure, forced herself to move and suddenly summoned a thick ice shield in front of her.

However, in the face of overwhelming power, the ice shield seemed too fragile and was directly shattered by Sharpren’s fist.

Instantly, ice shards flew everywhere, and the violent shockwave sent Alice’s delicate body flying like a cannonball, crashing to the ground!

The power was terrifying, causing Alice to cough up blood in mid-air, her body uncontrollably bouncing and rolling on the ground before finally coming to a stop far away.

The aftereffects alone left Alice seriously injured and almost unconscious—the gap in strength was enormous.

“You bastard…”

Alice lay on the ground with her brows furrowed, blood at the corner of her mouth, staring angrily at Sharpren, feeling as if her bones were about to fall apart, and she frequently gasped for breath in pain.

“Oh my god, you’re injured like this—why are you so weak?!” Sharpren’s expression was somewhat bewildered, feeling that his tentative attack wouldn’t have hurt Alice at all, but the result made him incredulous, directly causing her serious injury! ?

Kyle came back to his senses from the panic, holding a long spear, and concentrated all his high-level fighting spirit to fight Sharpren to the death.

“Damn you! Dare to attack us? Die!”

“Hmph!” Sharpren coldly snorted, kicking Kyle into the air with one foot, as easily as kicking his son.

Kyle flew out like a kite with its string cut off, instantly losing his combat ability and fainting, unable to withstand even one kick.

Looking at his pale face and distorted posture, he was definitely seriously injured.

Alice watched all this in shock, a bit worried about Kyle’s life. If Cecilia were here, she could rush to treat him—maybe it would still be in time.

But in such a dangerous situation, calling Cecilia out would be like sending her to her death, right?

The surrounding zombies, seeing that Alice couldn’t move, drooled over fresh human meat and rushed over en masse, wanting to divide up this human.

“Damn it!” Alice’s expression became fearful, as she now had limited ability to resist and couldn’t fight off the hungry zombies.

A violent Saint-tier fist wind came rushing in, and all the zombies in her heart were crushed to pieces, saving Alice from danger.

“What?!” Alice looked at Sharpren in surprise, not knowing what he was up to.

“You’re my prey—I won’t let you die so easily,” Sharpren said viciously, showing a ferocious expression. “I’m going to torture you to death, hahaha!”

Alice clenched her silver teeth, endured the pain, picked up the thin sword, and struggled to stand up.

She angrily held the thin sword, aiming it at Sharpren, seemingly not having lost all hope.

“Still able to stand up? Good, I’ll play with you, Sharpren,” he said, shaking his huge body and speaking disdainfully. “By the way, you’re really weak—a gust of wind made you seriously injured and spit blood. I’m really surprised; I thought you were strong, stronger than that black iron adventurer named Merlin.”

“You’re so verbose, Alice,” he said. She wiped the blood from the corner of her mouth, forcibly using her magic power and fighting spirit, and instantly condensed a fused ice crystal on the thin sword.

“All right, let’s see what you’re capable of,” Sharpren said, grinning and showing his serrated teeth. “I like watching enemies struggle and be beaten to death by my fist, hahahaha.”

Alice swung the thin sword, and a huge ice cone rushed towards Sharpren.

The cold air rolled like a mountain of ice crashing down—the momentum was terrifying.

“Too small, too silly…”

Sharpren showed a triumphant smile, waving his hand and shattering the huge ice cone into pieces!

Alice took the opportunity to charge forward, activating the “Dragon Form” skill, mixing magic power with fighting spirit, and faintly forming a dragon shadow.

The wind and snow raged, and Alice stabbed the thin sword with all her strength towards Sharpren’s heart.

At a distance of just one fingernail, Alice’s thin sword was caught by Sharpren’s two fingers.

No matter how hard Alice tried, she couldn’t advance an inch!

“Do you think you can hurt me? How pathetic,” Sharpren sneered.

Bastard

Alice cursed angrily—the disparity in strength seemed to make victory impossible.

“The skill you just used seemed to be a dragon clan skill, which surprised me a bit, but your strength is too weak,” Sharpren said. He casually threw a punch, sending Alice flying.

Alice felt her body being hit hard, and even her soul was trembling.

Alice fell to the ground, unable to muster any strength, unable to even hold the thin sword.

“You’re not my match, but that black iron adventurer does have some strength—though where did he go? Why didn’t I see him?” Sharpren walked to Alice, his huge body squatting down, looking down at her and saying, “How about we make a deal? Tell me where Merlin is, and I’ll spare your life.”

“Pfft! You bastard,” Alice spat in Sharpren’s mouth without hesitation, thinking that Merlin had gone to save Sherry—how could he be disturbed?

op SE this novel_

“You’re so unique,” Sharpren said, staring at Alice for a moment and praising her. Then he grabbed her from the ground in his hand, like playing with a doll. “Since that’s the case, I won’t be polite. Maybe if I torture you, Merlin will appear—after all, you’re not his wife?”

“Release me! Hurry up and release me!” Alice struggled, feeling her bones falling apart, and Sharpren was squeezing her very painfully.

If Sharpren wanted to, he could easily crush Alice to death at any time, just like crushing a lowly ant.

“You seem to be protecting the suffering people—that’s good. It seems you’re a very kind person; I’m a little admiring of you now,” Sharpren said, looking at the noble hotel in front of him, which was full of citizens from the capital.

“What are you going to do?!” Alice’s expression became fearful, having a sinister premonition.

“I imagine that for you, Merlin is important, and these innocent citizens are also important, so I’ll give you a multiple choice question,” Sharpren said. He held Alice’s body with one hand and clenched his fist, pointing it at the temporary refuge.

“Tell me where Merlin is, and I’ll let you go—and I’ll let the refugees inside the building live.

“Two: If you don’t tell me where Merlin is, you must die—and so must these scum, but Merlin might live.

“Come on—what a classic multiple choice question?!?

‘Save the few, or save the many?’

Your choice concerns the lives of everyone, hahahaha.”

title: Chapter 57 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 57 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 57

The towering Sharlen held Alice in his palm, leaving her utterly powerless to resist.

"What are you talking about!?" Alice’s eyes filled with panic. After hearing him out, she found herself in a terrible dilemma.

"It’s an interesting game, so choose carefully. Who dies and who lives depends entirely on your whim." Sharlen’s smile was hideous, feeling as though he had finally taken revenge for the humiliation he’d suffered. "How does it feel? You’re like a god right now! You can control others’ lives with a single word. It must be wonderful!"

"You’re talking nonsense! Let me go!" Alice shouted angrily, having no intention of playing.

Although Alice knew Sharlen couldn’t truly threaten Merlin’s life, Merlin was currently rushing to save Shirley, and time was short.

If they were distracted even slightly, Shirley—that girl who only wanted to return home—would be the one to lose her life.

The door of the noble hotel slowly opened, and Cecilia poked her head out, likely having heard the commotion outside and curiously peering over.

"Alice!"

"Go back inside! Don’t come out! It’s dangerous here!" Alice loudly warned Cecilia.

"Huh!?" Cecilia froze, then spotted Sharlen’s terrifying figure and his raging Saint-tier battle aura. Her face went pale with fear, but she still mustered the courage to shout, "You black ape! Let Lady Alice go right now! Or I’ll smash your head in with my magic wand!"

"Tch!" Sharlen clicked his tongue in dissatisfaction and shot Cecilia a murderous glare.

"Eek!!" Cecilia’s soul practically left her body. Like a mouse encountering a cat, she hastily shrank back behind the door, though she couldn’t resist peeking out to watch the situation, clearly worried about Alice’s safety.

"I’ll give you three seconds to think it over before you answer. So—" Sharlen’s mouth twisted into a grotesque grin as he rasped, "The game begins!"

"Huh!? I never agreed to play such a boring game!" Alice roared, trembling to her very bones.

"Three!" Sharlen tightened his grip, forcing Alice to suffer.

"Aaaaaah!" Alice let out a painful scream. She hadn’t expected Sharlen to actually start counting down.

How was she supposed to choose!?

Save Shirley—one person—or save thousands of refugees?

No matter what she chose, she’d be a sinner!

No one would ever forgive her. If someone died because of her choice, she’d be a murderer!

Damn it! She couldn’t possibly make up her mind! Was she supposed to just watch this bastard run rampant!?

"Two!" Sharlen continued the countdown. His Saint-tier battle aura began to churn, as if he truly intended to act and flatten the temporary shelter before them into rubble.

Cold sweat poured down Alice’s face. The impossible choice drove her to the brink of madness, her mind teetering on the edge of collapse.

Let’s save Shirley first. I’m close to her—she’s just a silly girl who wants to go home!

They were both over four hundred years old, yet she was as innocent as a child of just a few years.

After suffering so much torture, wouldn’t it be unfair if she couldn’t return to her homeland!?

No, wait—shouldn’t I save the refugees first?

Shirley is just one person, while there are thousands of lives here.

"Ah—!" Panic surged through Alice’s chest. This wasn’t something that could be resolved in a single day.

"One!" The smile on Sharlen’s face grew ever more evil and terrifying. His Saint-tier battle aura surged forth. With just a flick of his fist, everything before him would be obliterated. Slaughtering these lowly humans would be utterly satisfying!

Alice’s expression grew distant and blank, drowning in boundless confusion.

This isn’t right!?

Why should I play along with this guy’s boring game?

No one should die! The one who deserves to die the most is this black elf!

That’s right! Just because he’s powerful doesn’t mean he can toy with other people’s lives!

This is definitely wrong! Who would let themselves be manipulated by a black ape!?

Alice lowered her head, her expression darkening. The immense pressure awakened something instinctive within her, and her state of mind began to shift.

Scorn. Anger. The haughty pride that scorned all things.

Beneath the crushing pressure, Alice’s potential was sparked, revealing only the tip of an iceberg. Her entire mind was consumed by the desire to resist!

Sharlen sneered, just about to unleash his fist, when he heard Alice mutter softly.

"Let me go."

"Hm? What did you say?" Sharlen hadn’t heard clearly.

"I said let me go! You卑微 black elf, don’t you dare touch me with your filthy hands!"

Alice raised her head and roared. Her ice-blue eyes had inexplicably transformed into sharp, golden vertical pupils.

Rather than resembling a serpent’s eyes, they looked more like those of a dragon—or perhaps the deceased Frost Holy Dragon, Malygos.

Her golden eyes overflowed with majesty and nobility. The unmistakable dragon pressure sent Sharlen reeling in sudden fear, a flicker of panic crossing his gaze.

This unexpected turn caught Sharlen off guard, and he froze in place.

He began to doubt whether he was holding a human or a humanoid dragon—and a particularly high-ranking one at that.

Sharlen felt that Alice’s golden eyes were strangely familiar. The Flame Dragon Emperor, one of the Nine Kings of the Southern United Kingdoms, possessed similar divine eyes that instilled overwhelming pressure with but a glance.

The Flame Dragon Emperor also held another identity: that of the Explosive Flame Holy Dragon, one of the Six Holy Dragons, whose strength rivaled that of the Elf King.

"Get lost!" Alice roared again, as mountain-toppling, sea-parting magic power surged from within her body.

The arm gripping Alice instantly froze and shattered!

Ice shards scattered, mingling with Sharlen’s severed arm.

"Huh...?"

Sharlen stared blankly at his断臂, staggered backward in shock, his expression one of utter disbelief. He was now nearly at the peak of Saint-tier, yet his arm had been broken by a high-level magic swordsman! This human woman was no ordinary foe!

"Cough, cough…"

Alice, now on the ground, coughed repeatedly as she returned to normal. The majestic presence from earlier had vanished without a trace, and she could barely recall the feeling of looking down upon the world.

Sharlen stared down at Alice on the ground, his heart churned with unease. Why had she suddenly become weak again? What had just happened!?

No, this woman cannot be allowed to live! The隐患 must be crushed before it can grow!

Gritting his teeth, the flesh on Sharlen’s face twitched occasionally as he growled in anger.

"You’re not an ordinary human! You dared to break my arm—die!"

His Saint-tier battle aura exploded to its limits. Sharlen was no longer holding back, intending to kill Alice with a single strike!

Though he had lost an arm, his strength had not diminished in the slightest. The force of his fist drove Alice’s face pale.

"Alice!" Cecilia’s heart leaped into her throat, feeling certain that Alice was about to die.

Alice stared blankly at the towering black fist descending upon her, having no choice but to accept her fate.

But just then, the sound of delightful bells rang out—

"Ding-a-ling-ling-ling—"

"Hm!?" Sharlen’s body stiffened. Terrified, he turned toward the source of the sound.

At some point, a figure wrapped in white robes had appeared, holding a shepherd’s distinctive curved staff, upon which a golden bell was gently swaying.

The white-robed shepherd was bent over, lightly tapping his lower back with his hand. He appeared frail and elderly, radiating no sense of threat whatsoever. Yet the purple necklace around his neck was unmistakable—dazzling and prominent.

That was an Adventurer Guild certificate, colored gold and purple—Rank A!

Sharlen’s eyes bulged wide, and he muttered in sheer terror.

"You’re… the head of the Royal Capital Adventurers Guild—"

"Cameron Gregor!"

title: Chapter 58 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 58 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 58

Sharplun was stunned on the spot—he never expected that at a time like this, this legendary Violet-Gold Adventurer would appear.

It was said that Cameron Gregory hadn’t left the Adventurers Guild for a long time, always staying in his old haunt, barely moving at all. Yet now, with the royal capital in crisis, this old monster had been startled into action—and just happened to appear right in front of Sharplun!

Cecilia, the Violet-Gold Adventurer, hid behind the door, staring in shock at the elderly shepherd. This was probably her first time seeing a Violet-Gold Adventurer.

Violet-Gold Adventurers were all enigmatic figures, most of them recluses who rarely showed themselves. But sometimes, they would appear in groups. Like over thirty years ago, when several Violet-Gold Adventurers had gone to Norway to slay the legendary North Sea Leviathan.

The Guild President of the royal capital, Gregory, was one of the few known Violet-Gold Adventurers. Most people were aware of his status, making him a rare exception.

Alice’s eyes widened as she took in Gregory’s aged appearance, especially the Violet-Gold Adventurer’s badge around his neck. A chill ran through her.

Region: London.
Name: Cameron Gregory.
Profession: Mage.

Though this was Alice’s first time seeing a Violet-Gold Adventurer, she had heard from Hobbes that they were all individuals of extraordinary power. The Violet-Gold rank required passing a trial of strength at the Denmark headquarters, with the badge personally awarded by the Council Leader—impossible to fake.

Alice knew little about Gregory, only that he was an ancient figure, a founding elder of Great Britain, with deep ties to the royal family. Every birthday, Queen Elizabeth would send personally prepared gifts.

Gregory pulled his white robe low, obscuring his face and adding to his mystery. The bell on his staff jingled softly.

“A black elf who recognizes me… Has my name spread all the way to the Southern United Kingdom?”

Sharplun barely regained his composure, recalling what Salan had said. He should be turning and running right now. If this had been before he took the drug, he might have chosen to avoid the fight. But now, after consuming the Supreme Dark Rage Potion, his power had surged—he might just have a chance.

Sharplun’s gaze sharpened, glaring at Gregory. He decided this old monster was a dangerous variable that needed to be eliminated first.

“Such obvious killing intent… Young people these days are so hot-tempered. Wouldn’t it be better to talk things out calmly?” Gregory’s voice was hoarse, wheezing like an old bellows.

“Cut the crap.” Sharplun narrowed his eyes, his massive frame shifting into a bizarre fighting stance—clearly preparing to use a martial technique.

Even with one arm missing, Sharplun’s strength hadn’t diminished. He could still wield the black elf fighting style with masterful precision.

“You really don’t know how to respect your elders, do you? If you’d like, I could teach you a thing or two about manners.” Gregory let out a series of chuckles, his hunched body trembling slightly.

A cold sweat slid down Alice’s face. *Is this Violet-Gold Adventurer about to make a move?*

Gregory had indirectly saved Alice’s life by shifting Sharplun’s attention onto himself.

“No need. Even if you’re an old man, I won’t hesitate to send you to hell!” Sharplun said gravely.

“Hahaha.” Gregory laughed, sounding surprisingly kind. “I’m already half in the grave anyway. If you want my old life, come and take it.”

“As you wish!”

Sharplun moved suddenly. His Saint-tier battle aura erupted at full force, and his enormous frame appeared before Gregory in an instant—too fast for anyone to react!

“Ultimate Technique: Hundred Forms Barrage!”

Sharplun’s form shifted rapidly, phantoms of beasts materializing around him—tigers, leopards, jackals, even a dragon! The attacks came in countless variations, his massive fists raining down in an overwhelming storm!

Each transformation brought a new strike, all unleashed simultaneously. The Saint-tier battle aura surged like waves, impossible to resist!

As a true heir to the black elf martial arts, Sharplun had long since mastered this technique to perfection. This Saint-tier Ultimate Technique embodied the essence of black elf combat—though diverse, every move complemented the others.

To merge so many different fist styles into one was proof of Sharplun’s extraordinary skill—worthy of the title of genius!

“Interesting… but still too green.”

Gregory shook the golden bell on his staff. A terrifying Saint-tier magical power surged, like flames roaring across his aged body.

The space before him rippled, forming a pitch-black vortex that spun slowly.

Sharplun’s fists all missed, as if striking into another dimension, unable to harm Gregory at all.

“What the—? Is this the rumored black hole?!”

The black vortex closed in on Sharplun, twisting his body as if some unseen force were snapping him in half.

“AAAAAAH! What—what is this?!”

Sharplun screamed endlessly, realizing he was trapped, unable to move an inch!

The black vortex mercilessly devoured him, blood spraying as it tore him into countless pieces.

“Didn’t expect today’s youth to be all talk with no real skill.” Gregory said indifferently, rubbing his old back with his hand.

Alice’s eyes were wide with shock as she watched it all unfold.

*One-shot.*

A single spell had killed Sharplun! Even with the power surge from the drug, he hadn’t been a match for this old man!

And it looked like the Violet-Gold Adventurer hadn’t even used his full strength. To effortlessly annihilate someone at Saint-tier… just how strong was this guy?!

And that spell just now—she’d never seen anything like it. What kind of magic had such a devastating effect?

Alice was left speechless. She couldn’t understand Gregory’s technique at all. All she could perceive was that he’d shaken a bell, and his opponent had been erased.

“Miss Alice! Are you alright?!” Cecilia, seeing the danger had passed, rushed over to check Alice’s injuries, intending to heal her.

“Don’t worry about me! Go check on Kyle—he was attacked earlier too.” Alice said solemnly.

“Eh?!” Cecilia blinked, then hurried off to prioritize treating Kyle, her expression panicked.

“Never thought I’d run into little Lexum’s girl here. Truly a pleasant surprise.” Gregory said in his raspy voice, his gaze sweeping over Alice’s Gold Adventurer badge, gathering basic information.

“Little… girl?” Alice’s expression was unnatural, but she still politely replied, “H-Hello.”

“No need to be so formal with me. Even if we’re from different regional guilds, we’re still colleagues. Otherwise, I wouldn’t have come to save you.” Gregory chuckled softly.

“Th-Thank you…” Alice responded awkwardly, gritting her teeth against the pain as she tried to stand.

“By the way, how’s little Taylor doing? Haven’t seen him since he became Lexum’s Guild President. Seems like it’s been a while.” Gregory asked curiously.

“Him?!” Alice tensed, thinking, *Little Taylor?! I can’t imagine that being our Guild President.*

“Well, tell him when you get back that he should come to the royal capital for a visit when he has time.” Gregory nodded.

“I’ll pass along the message.” Alice replied, slowly getting to her feet.

“I’ve got other places to be. Farewell, kind Lexum girl. You’re a special young one.”

Gregory waved his hand, then, leaning on his shepherd’s staff, quietly departed, leaving only the echoing sound of the bell.

Alice knit her brows, staring into the distance at the scattered remains of Sharplun’s corpse.

*What a terrifying man…*

Perhaps this was the power of a Violet-Gold Adventurer.

(∞ω∞)

title: Chapter 59
content:
Chapter 59

Volume 7 · Chapter 59

Meanwhile.

The four Thorn Knights split up to suppress the ghouls together. Thanks to the combined efforts of the entire Rose Knight order, they managed to temporarily stabilize the worsening situation.

Hordes of ghouls fell to their blades, and the turmoil was now largely under control.

As agreed, everyone needed to head to the Clock Tower and destroy the source of the chaos.

Above the Clock Tower, that crimson eye still loomed, rolling wildly as it spied on the royal capital. Judging by its appearance, Asmodus was clearly anxious, his eyeball shifting uneasily.

Fifth Thorn Knight Milieus and Eleventh Thorn Knight Winifred were the first to regroup their forces and head toward the Clock Tower. Among them was the squad leader Chapman, who had nearly been executed for revealing the truth.

Thanks to Mesfield’s protection, Chapman had escaped severe punishment, merely submitting a written self-criticism before the matter was dropped. Commander Franklin, out of respect for the First Thorn Knight, couldn’t bring himself to reprimand Chapman harshly, so he had no choice but to swallow his anger and allow him to remain in the Rose Knights. Now, these knights were facing a powerful foe, struggling to press forward.

Everything had been going smoothly—until they encountered Shalan’s ambush on the way to the Clock Tower, suffering heavy losses.

Shalan was no mindless ghoul; she was far from easy to deal with. Under the overwhelming corrosive power of her dark magic, many knights perished, reduced to pools of tainted blood.

Shalan was indeed a formidable opponent, perhaps even stronger than Sharplun. The rampant dark energy and frenzied magic radiating from her struck fear into the hearts of many knights.

"Lord Winifred, let me lead the squad in a charge!" Chapman, his expression grim, stepped forward to volunteer. "We’ll definitely carve a path through the middle!"

"Know your limits. No matter how many of you go, it’ll just be a suicide mission. Pointless sacrifices serve no purpose." Milieus said coolly, his slender rapier—engraved with intricate floral patterns—looking exquisite in his grip.

"Milieus is right. Fall back a little. This is our fight." Winifred said calmly, holding the book embedded with a blue gem—his weapon, it seemed.

Chapman had no retort. Staring at the grotesque monster before him, he felt utterly powerless. If he and his comrades charged, they’d only be a burden to the Thorn Knights.

Shalan had transformed into something monstrous—her body a writhing mass of black sludge, with jagged fangs and a head protruding from its chest. If not for her exposed head, one might mistake this enormous, shifting mass for a sewer-born sludge monster that had just crawled out of the drains.

At the moment, she resembled a parasite, her head sprouting from the creature’s torso, an unsettling sight.

The black sludge monster was a concentrated manifestation of dark elemental energy. Every time it opened its mouth, it spewed black mist—thick with a foul stench and potent corrosive properties.

This sludge monster was Shalan’s ultimate technique, *Dark Adhesion*—a kind of self-buff that caused dark energy to fester on her body, transforming her into an overwhelmingly powerful creature.

Not only was her offensive power terrifying, but her defense was equally impressive. She was nearly unkillable—even if wounds were inflicted, they healed rapidly.

Coupled with her exceptional corrosive effects, Shalan was nearly unstoppable. Any enemy that approached her would gradually be eaten away. And if she landed a hit, the consequences were even worse—her victims would be rapidly consumed, reduced to puddles of blood. Even Saint-tier warriors would struggle to resist!

"What’s wrong? Aren’t you the legendary Thorn Knights? Is this all the strength you have? Pathetic. Ha!" Shalan taunted from within her black sludge monster, convinced she was on a completely different level.

Milieus smirked. "Already gloating? You really think you’re something special?"

"Maybe she thinks she’s already won." Winifred shook his head.

"True. The ugly hag always had an inflated opinion of herself." Milieus couldn’t resist the jab, tightening his grip on his rapier.

"Inflated opinion? Ridiculous!" Shalan bared her teeth, laughing wildly. "Can’t you see the gap between us? I’ll toy with you until you die!"

Winifred furrowed his brow. The situation was troublesome. Their attacks were having little effect, and dragging this out would only lead to disaster.

"Terribly sorry, but I prefer to dance with beautiful ladies. However..." Milieus assumed a dueling stance, executing a perfect opening move from courtly swordsmanship. "It’s best you disappear quickly!"

"Hmph! When you’re dead, I hope you’ll still be spouting nonsense like that!" Shalan commanded the sludge monster to fire countless mud projectiles at blinding speed, like a downpour.

Where the projectiles struck the ground, they rapidly began to corrode, hissing and emitting white smoke.

But Milieus was no slouch. He turned into a streak of light, vanishing as he swiftly evaded the attack.

"Winifred, now!"

"Got it." Winifred nodded, opening his magic tome. A burst of golden Saint-tier magic erupted from it.

In an instant, Milieus became a starry dancer—graceful and swift, his movements so fluid and elegant that one might mistake the battle for a musical performance. The former title of "First Handsome Man of Great Britain" was clearly well-deserved.

His golden hair flowed as Saint-tier aura surged into his slender rapier. With a sudden thrust, a powerful sword energy pierced through Shalan’s sludge monster.

The sequence of movements was seamless, like a meteor streaking across the sky!

Winifred wasn’t idle either. With a flick of his fingers, the earth beneath him shattered into countless fragments, which shot forward like throwing knives, piercing deep into the sludge monster’s body.

It seemed like a one-sided battle, but Shalan was far from that easy to defeat.

"Useless!" Shalan’s black sludge monster suddenly erupted, sprouting countless black spikes like a puffed-up pufferfish.

Milieus and Winifred quickly retreated, but some of the black sludge still splattered onto them, causing minor corrosive injuries.

"You’re no match for me! Give up and die like good little knights!" Shalan roared arrogantly, her entire being consumed by madness. The thrill of dominating the Thorn Knights filled her with joy. "Want to fight me? Then send the First Thorn Knight here! Only she’s worthy of facing me!"

"Hmph. To be looked down on like this... I suppose we’ll have to show our true strength." Milieus wiped the black sludge from his face, his expression a mix of amusement and composure, never losing his elegance.

"Indeed." Winifred’s expression turned serious, as if he had finally decided to take things seriously.

A golden aura of fighting spirit and magic surged from both of them, their pressure rising steadily, forcing Shalan to feel a hint of unease.

"Lords, you’re finally getting serious?" Chapman exclaimed in awe from the sidelines.

"What are you all doing wasting time here?!"

A sharp rebuke rang out as Mesfield descended from the sky, landing firmly on the ground.

Drawing the straight sword at her waist, she calmly advanced toward Shalan, without a trace of fear.

"Do you have any idea how urgent this is? And you still have the leisure to play with this small fry? Fools!"

"Small fry?!" Shalan’s breath hitched, her face twisting in rage. "What an insolent thing to say!"

Milieus looked stunned—he hadn’t expected the First Knight to return.

Winifred’s expression darkened; he clearly disliked being scolded.

"Finally, Mesfield!" Shalan’s face contorted, her bloodshot eyes wild with excitement. "I’ve been waiting for you! What kind of Thorn Knights are these? A bunch of overrated frauds! Only you have strength worth acknowledging. Come! Let’s see who’s stronger! I’ve heard you’re called the strongest Saint-tier? Well, today I’ll crush the legend! I’ll humiliate you to death! HAHAHAHA!"

Mesfield remained expressionless, her pale purple hair swaying gently as she took step after step toward Shalan.

Her golden Saint-tier aura soared into the sky, so overwhelming it made one’s soul tremble.

In a sudden motion, Mesfield swung her sword at Shalan’s fused sludge monster, unleashing a golden sword energy that pierced the heavens—

Shalan’s eyes widened in bewilderment as she and her sludge monster were instantly bisected.

A one-hit kill. A crushing, effortless victory.

---

All the buildup is done. Finally, it’s time for the keyboard-smashing, show-off phase.

These past few days, everyone’s been cursing at me, and I don’t even know what to say.

Anyway, do as you like. After writing for over a year, I’ve seen all kinds of readers.

The refined ones, the crude ones, the ones who curse like sailors.

I’ve written long-running stories before, and all sorts of trolls have come out of the woodwork. Before I knew it, I’d built up an immunity.

Open Volume mentioned that this volume introduces many characters and ties into the content of later volumes.

But looking at it now, that warning shot I fired was useless. Didn’t do a thing.

As for the pacing—well, that’s subjective. I won’t change my rhythm just because of a few complaints.

With my first book, I catered too much to readers, and it made writing the later parts agonizing.

So if you can’t handle it, there’s nothing I can do. A story has its own natural pace. If you force it, it falls apart.

You can’t just do whatever you want. A runaway horse only ends up destroyed.

Chapter 60 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 60

The pitch-black mud monster dispersed in an instant, and Salan's body collapsed to the ground, her face still bearing the lingering terror and confusion from before her death.

Probably even in death, Salan never figured out why she lost. She had no idea just how vast the gap in strength was between herself and Mesfilth.

Vynifred stayed silent, a cold sweat trickling down his forehead.

"That was ridiculous..." Milieth muttered to himself, shaking his head.

Salan was the kind of troublesome enemy that would take an all-out fight to defeat, yet Mesfilth managed to dispatch her in a single move?

If I hadn't seen it with my own eyes, I probably wouldn't have believed it. The might of the Thorn Knights really does have a clear divide.

"...As expected of the First Thorn Knight, huh..." Chapman muttered in shock from the crowd below. Though he was just a minor figure, he had seen his share of things, especially after witnessing Elkin the Great Sword Master's legendary exploits.

Though Chapman genuinely admired Mesfilth's strength, he couldn't help but admit that there was still a gap between her and Elkin the Great Sword Master.

The entire hall of knights fell into deep admiration, and for a moment, the only sound was the flutter of wings as all eyes turned toward Mesfilth.

"For enemies this weak, you spent so long dealing with them? That's really embarrassing..."

Mesfilth slid her sword back into its scabbard and turned to face Vynifred and Milieth.

Vynifred said nothing, merely lowering his head slightly, lost in thought.

"Weak enemies?" Milieth's face twitched as he broke into a cold sweat. "Sir Salisbury is really something..."

"Don't call me Sir Salisbury." Mesfilth's expression turned stern. She found that cute little nickname quite unsuitable for herself.

"Oh, right, right..." Milieth awkwardly replied, worried that Mesfilth might actually get angry.

"Honestly, how much time did you waste?" Mesfilth adopted a more commanding tone, reprimanding them. "If you had taken things seriously, you could have defeated this kind of enemy in no time."

"Even if we could win, we'd still pay a price," Vynifred replied.

"Yeah, and we still have to head to the Clock Tower. If we drain too much magical power or combat energy, we won't be able to give it our all when we get there," Milieth explained.

"With me here, there's nothing to worry about," Mesfilth said with a hint of irritation.

...Milieth stood there speechless for a moment, then awkwardly laughed. "As expected of the First Knight, you're totally different from us. You're exactly my type, this unique kind of girl."

"What did you just say?" Mesfilth shot him a deadly glare. She had never seen anyone dare to flirt with her before.

"Sorry, I just blurted it out..." Milieth averted his gaze, unable to meet Mesfilth's eyes.

"Hmph!" Mesfilth rolled her eyes loudly, then called out to the entire squad. "All right! March to the Clock Tower at once! It seems Morrison has already arrived."

The Thorn Knights quickly formed up, and within moments had transformed into a formidable force.

Though they had fought through several battles, their combat strength remained exceptional.

Mesfilth gazed toward the distant Clock Tower, where golden light still erupted skyward, and the magical elements in the air were nearly exhausted.

25 SE of healing magic.

The crimson eye floating above began to spin wildly, and suddenly locked eyes with Mesfilth.

That hostile gaze made Mesfilth's spine chill, as if it were looking down upon her insignificant self.

It might just be a massive eyeball, but the oppressive pressure it radiated was bone-chilling. This was definitely no ordinary thing.

"Do you two know what that eye is?" Mesfilth asked.

"Maybe it's the spotlight prepared for me?" Milieth flashed a smug grin.

"I'm being serious." Mesfilth furrowed her delicate brows for emphasis.

"This... I don't know either," Milieth shrugged.

"It might be some grand ritual magic from the elves, or perhaps a curse," Vynifred said calmly. As a mage himself, he could sense certain things.

"Grand ritual magic? A curse?" Mesfilth looked puzzled.

"Our enemy seems to be an elf," Vynifred glanced at Salan's corpse behind them and continued, "With magical fluctuations on this scale, the only things I can think of are grand ritual magic or a curse."

...Mesfilth pondered for a moment and found his reasoning sound. If it were grand ritual magic or a curse, there would still be time to counter it. "Then let's go!"

Mesfilth gave the order, and immediately led the knights toward the Clock Tower.

But Mesfilth had barely taken a few steps when she spotted a figure wearing a silver mask on the central avenue, rushing past at high speed.

Judging by the direction it was heading, it was going the same way as them—toward the Clock Tower.

"Who is that?" Mesfilth asked in confusion.

"Maybe just someone passing through?" Milieth replied nonchalantly.

"It doesn't seem right to be running around outside at a time like this. He looks like a swordsman, and he's carrying a long sword," Vynifred answered after some thought.

"...No way... That's Elkin the Great Sword Master!"

Chapman couldn't help but exclaim in shock from the crowd, causing everyone to panic.

Who didn't know Elkin the Great Sword Master? Chapman's shout sent all the Thorn Knights into shock.

Even Milieth and Vynifred were taken aback. They never expected the wanted criminal Elkin the Great Sword Master to actually appear in the capital.

This is outright spitting in Queen Elizabeth's face! Brazen mockery!

In truth, Chapman had no solid basis for thinking that masked figure was Elkin the Great Sword Master. But he had been in close contact with Elkin before.

That resolute, proud silhouette, the way he walked with his sword drawn, and his dazzling golden hair—all of it easily reminded Chapman of the real Elkin.

Mesfilth remained composed and asked sternly, "Chapman, are you certain?"

"...Chapman hesitated, struggling to give a definitive answer."

"You'd better answer carefully. This concerns a wanted criminal who's been troubling Her Majesty the Queen!" Mesfilth pressed him hard.

"Although I can't be certain, the person who just passed by really did look like Elkin the Great Sword Master. That was my first reaction," Chapman straightened up and answered honestly.

"Hey, hey, hey, you'd better not be mistaken," Milieth frowned, his voice tense. "If that person really is Elkin the Great Sword Master, I'd go kill him right now!"

"...Chapman opened his mouth to speak but couldn't finish. A cold sweat broke out on his forehead."

"Chapman has met Elkin the Great Sword Master before, so his words carry some weight," Vynifred said cautiously.

Mesfilth fell into deep thought. She had urgent matters at hand, yet Elkin the Great Sword Master had suddenly appeared.

Though she couldn't confirm his identity right now, she had to investigate.

After all, Elkin the Great Sword Master plus an unknown accomplice was a thorn in the Queen's side.

As long as she caught that masked man and questioned him, it wouldn't interfere with their mission to the Clock Tower.

After reasoning through it, Mesfilth broke into a full sprint, chasing after the disguised Merlin. Some truths were about to be revealed.

"Mesfilth!" Vynifred shouted, trying to call her back.

But Mesfilth didn't listen. Her eyes were filled with determination, her mind consumed by a single thought.

If that man truly was Elkin the Great Sword Master, she wouldn't let him escape.

No one could flee from beneath my blade...

Since you've dared to infiltrate the capital alone, you'd better surrender quietly!

(...)
