Volume 7 · Chapter 61

Merlin was sprinting down the road, his gaze fixed on the distant clock tower.... A golden pillar of light swept across heaven and earth, stirring the winds. An eerie red eyeball, as if from another world, was scrutinizing everyone. Merlin sensed an ominous aura, couldn't help but frown, feeling that eye was not ordinary. Moreover, judging by the current situation, that eyeball was only a part, not yet complete. However, Merlin didn't care about those things; he was concerned about Rei's safety, after all she represented a hundred million gold coins. If he had been busy for so long and ended up with nothing, Merlin would feel displeased. A fierce wind brushed past his ears, and the distance to the clock tower kept shrinking.

Just then— Mesfield's battle aura flared up, blazing as she caught up to Merlin. She stood directly in the middle of the road, blocking his path. Mesfield wore a stern expression, her eyes like searchlights fixed on Merlin's face, growing more suspicious that this masked mysterious man was the legendary Elgin Swordsman. Merlin quickly halted his steps, a flicker of annoyance crossing his eyes, thinking, 'How is it this woman again? What a troublesome nuisance; I'm really pressed for time.' He said, 'Miss, is there something? If not, move aside, don't block the way—I have important matters to attend to.' Mesfield gripped the sword at her waist, seeming ready to draw at any moment, 'I want to ask you a question...' Merlin glanced at Mesfield twice, seeing her ready to draw, amused, he teased, 'No thanks, thank you.'

'Tch!' Mesfield's eyes flashed with a hint of anger; she despised anyone speaking to her in a frivolous tone. She then drew her waist sword, pointing it at Merlin, and said coldly, 'If you dare utter more frivolous words, I'll kill you.' 'Wow, what a temper....' Merlin smiled, spreading his hands, 'Then I'll just ask, what's the reason for blocking my way?' 'Are you the legendary Elgin Swordsman?' Mesfield pressed her sword toward Merlin, seeking an answer. Merlin stared, then rubbed his chin, falling into thought. Should he admit it or not? Now that he wore a mask, admitting wouldn't matter. Besides, once the mask came off, no one would recognize him as the Elgin Swordsman. Having decided, he lifted his head and said solemnly, 'Indeed, I am the legendary Elgin Swordsman, power and beauty.--. Damn!' Before he could finish, Mesfield swung her sword, releasing a golden blade aura with no warning. Fortunately, Merlin's evasion was maxed; he twisted his body and dodged, barely avoiding messing up his handsome hairstyle. Seeing the long gouge carved by the blade aura beside him, Merlin frowned and complained unhappily, 'Hey hey hey, what are you doing? Attacking before someone finishes speaking—too rude!'

Mesfield's face lit up with delight; her golden battle aura surged, her fighting spirit soaring as she declared, 'Elgin Swordsman! I've waited for this day for so long!' Merlin gave a faint, mocking smile, the corners of his mouth twitching with sarcasm, 'Although I'm heroic and handsome to a fault, I don't recall ever flirting with you, miss. Who are you? What unforgettable event between us makes you remember me so deeply?' 'Foul mouth!' Mesfield assumed an attack stance, her Saint-tier pressure intensifying, seemingly unwilling to let go, 'Elgin Swordsman, surrender peacefully! Destroying royal fleet property warrants severe punishment! I, in the name of the Purple Chrysanthemum Knight Order, place you under arrest!' 'Destroying the royal fleet wasn't intentional on my part; can't we just let it slide? Give me some face.' Merlin thickened his skin, refusing to admit past faults. Recalling, it was all because that stupid pirate king insisted on seeing his full strength; he accidentally lost control, implicating several thousand royal warships and even carving a huge sea trench. 'Pah! Your face is worth a few coins? You destroyed royal assets and still want to let it off? Daydreaming!' Mesfield scolded sternly. 'How... I also saved civilians from crisis? Dwelling on the past is pointless?' Merlin shrugged, completely nonchalant.

Mesfield replied, 'So what? You're the queen's enemy—capturing you is enough!' Merlin chuckled, 'The queen's enemy being the main reason? Heh, I knew.' Mesfield said, 'Looks like you're ready, then come fight!' Her Saint-tier battle aura erupted fully, like a doomsday beast descending, truly terrifying. Although Mesfield's strength was strong—considered a rare fighter—in Merlin's eyes she was still a small fry. Merlin had seen countless opponents; none he hadn't faced, and many stronger than her. Thus Merlin felt no pressure, even wanted to laugh. Mesfield knew the Elgin Swordsman was formidable, having instantly slain countless Saint-tier undead, so she went all out from the start, holding nothing back. Merlin asked lightly, 'Are you sure you can beat me?' Mesfield answered seriously, 'How would we know without trying?' A bead of cold sweat traced her forehead; she didn't want to let this opportunity slip—if she gave up, who knows when she'd meet the Elgin Swordsman again. Moreover, the Elgin Swordsman was a threat to Great Britain, a destabilizing factor that made the Purple Chrysanthemum Knight Order's situation ever more awkward; if she didn't step forward, perhaps no one could subdue him. Merlin smirked, 'Frankly, I don't need to lift a finger to deal with you...' Mesfield shouted, 'Nonsense!' She was about to act when someone intervened first.

Miles suddenly appeared behind Merlin, wielding a thin sword, his eyes burning with fervor, blood vessels densely visible! He had followed Mesfield in pursuit, seeing the tense atmosphere, instantly realizing that the man wearing the silver dance mask was the Elgin Swordsman—the new-era idol of Great Britain who had stolen his handsome title, a scoundrel! 'You are the Elgin Swordsman, aren't you?!' 'I'm really lucky; I never expected to see the real deal!' 'Today I'll take your life and tear off your hypocritical mask!' Miles roared wildly, his excited grin stretching to his ears, laughing exaggeratedly. His thin sword danced with gorgeous flair, leaving onlookers dazed, and he slashed straight at Merlin's neck. Merlin muttered, 'Tsk, get lost!' Unbothered by this fly, he turned and punched Miles in the face. Miles gasped, 'Cough!' He was flung backward, crashing into the nearby rubble, alive or dead unknown, only his rear end sticking up high. Merlin exhaled, 'Huu~' He blew on his fist, wearing a helpless expression, 'Lately it seems all sorts of demons and monsters dare to jump around in front of me...'

title: Chapter 63 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 63 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 63

Mestfield was in despair. Her body was reacting in the strangest way.

As if she might ascend to the clouds at any moment, reaching the legendary Pure Land of Bliss.

The pleasure was, of course, indescribable—anyone could understand what was happening to Mestfield right now.

Yet here she was, the proud First Thorn Knight, watching Merlin’s retreating figure with tears of frustration in her eyes.

She felt utterly worthless. Such a rare opportunity, and she had let the Great Swordsman Elgin slip away right before her eyes!

She was a Saint-tier powerhouse! And yet, she had been taken down by the enemy—with just a mouthful of spit?!

If word got out, her reputation would be ruined beyond repair!

And... and now she was in this shameful state, utterly humiliated.

Mestfield’s body grew stranger by the second. If not for her iron will, she would have already succumbed to the relentless waves of pleasure.

She pressed her legs tightly together, clamping down on her skirt, her entire body flushed pink in a way that left onlookers speechless.

Mestfield was forcing herself to endure the stimulation, trying to stop herself from making a fool of herself any further. But the pleasure surging from within only grew stronger with each wave.

"...What... is happening to me? It feels so..."

Her breathing was heavy, her eyes misty and unfocused. Then, a thought that had never crossed her mind before surfaced—she *needed* a man.

The idea shocked her. She was a virgin, untouched by any man. How could she have such bold, shameless thoughts? This was *not* normal.

After racking her brain, the only explanation she could think of was Merlin’s saliva.

What *was* in that spit? Why did it have such an overwhelming aphrodisiac effect? It was even stronger than the succubus saliva sold on the black market!

If only Mestfield knew she had been hit with the saliva of a Demon Lord-tier succubus—what would she think?

At first, she had believed that Elgin the Great Swordsman, though a wanted criminal, was still a man of justice. After all, he had saved so many people.

But now? In Mestfield’s eyes, Elgin the Great Swordsman was nothing but a shameless pervert! The most depraved kind!

Wave after wave of pleasure clouded her mind. Her dignity wouldn’t allow her to seek out a man, so she had to settle for the next best thing—a solo act. (ZW—figure out the abbreviation yourself.)

Mestfield glanced at her fingers with a conflicted expression, hesitating for a long moment before slowly sliding her hand beneath her skirt.

*Just this once. Just once, and that’s it!*

If she moved quickly, maybe she could calm her body down soon.

She didn’t need a man at all—her slender fingers would do just fine!

She could bring herself to climax at an incredible pace. She *could* do this!

Mestfield kept encouraging herself, but just as her fingers beneath her skirt were about to brush against her most intimate place, she froze.

She clenched her hand into a fist and pounded the ground, trying to force herself to calm down. *What am I doing?!* The First Thorn Knight, engaging in such a shameful act in the middle of the street?! How disgraceful! Not only would she bring shame upon Her Majesty the Queen, but she would also tarnish the reputation of the Purple Thorn Knights! No, she had to hold on!

Mestfield tried to hold her final line of defense, but Merlin was a Demon Lord-class demon. How could the effects of his saliva be so easily overcome by sheer willpower?

Just then, Winifred arrived with the main force of the knight order. Seeing Mestfield kneeling on the ground in such a peculiar state, he assumed she must have been seriously injured. He called out, “Mestfield, what’s wrong? Did Elgin the Great Swordsman wound you?”

Mestfield’s heart lurched at the sight of Winifred. She didn’t want anyone to see her in this indecent state.

The presence of a man was too stimulating—she feared she wouldn’t be able to control herself.

So Mestfield quickly lowered her head, nearly burying her face in her own chest, struggling to maintain her composure.

“Stay back, Winifred! Keep your distance!”

“Huh?!”

Winifred was taken aback by her outburst, confused by the situation.

The other knights were also stunned, whispering among themselves.

Fortunately, Winifred was experienced enough to sense something unusual.

Perhaps there was a hidden danger around Mestfield—anyone who approached might trigger it.

“Mestfield, what’s going on? If you need help, just say the word. I’ll find a way.”

“I—I’m fine! Go check on Milieus! He hasn’t moved since earlier!” Mestfield forced her voice to sound normal, hiding her true state. She used Milieus to divert attention, thinking, *How could I possibly bring myself to say I need... that kind of help?!*

“I’ll go now!”

Winifred felt the situation was serious. Two Thorn Knights had been defeated by Elgin the Great Swordsman—just how powerful was this mysterious man?

And Mestfield was the most outstanding of the Thorn Knights. The fact that even *she* had fallen to Elgin was unthinkable!

Winifred felt a deep sense of unease. He approached the ruins and pulled up Milieus, who was still face-down on the ground, shaking him vigorously.

“Milieus! Milieus! Wake up!”

“Ugh... what...?”

Milieus groaned as he regained consciousness, his mind still foggy, giving off an air of utter confusion.

His handsome face was swollen from Merlin’s strikes, blood dripping from his nose...

“Milieus, what happened? Why do you look like this?” Winifred demanded.

“Oh! I remember now—it was Elgin the Great Swordsman! That bastard actually dared to hit my beautiful face! Jealousy! He must be jealous of my beauty!” Milieus, now fully awake, immediately started ranting about Merlin, convinced the attack was born of envy over his looks.

Winifred’s face darkened, a bead of sweat rolling down his temple. He couldn’t comprehend Milieus’ logic. *He hit you because you’re handsome? That’s not the reasoning of a true warrior...*

Milieus looked around, confused. “Where’s Elgin the Great Swordsman? Did he already escape?”

“Seems like it.” Winifred nodded.

“How is that possible?” Milieus widened his eyes, turning to Mestfield. “Even the First Thorn Knight couldn’t stop him? Unbelievable. Just how strong is that guy...?”

Winifred stayed silent, equally shocked by Mestfield’s defeat.

“Wait... Mestfield, why do you look so... strange?” Milieus frowned.

“Indeed, it’s a bit...” Winifred also stared.

Mestfield covered her mouth, her body trembling slightly. The succubus’ aphrodisiac effect showed no signs of fading—it only grew stronger.

“Hey! Mestfield, what’s wrong? Are you feeling unwell?” Milieus asked bluntly.

Mestfield was on the verge of losing control. Suddenly, she stood up with a blank expression and said flatly,

“I need to take care of something private. Don’t follow me.”

With that, Mestfield vanished from everyone’s sight in a flash, faster than someone holding in their urine!

“Private matter?” Winifred was puzzled.

“Tsk! You’re so clueless. Mestfield’s a woman—she has her monthly thing, you know~” Milieus said with feigned wisdom, as if he understood everything.

“Oh, right! I almost forgot...” Winifred slapped his forehead.

In reality, Mestfield was desperate. She had decided to take matters into her own hands—literally.

She would use her fingers to relieve her... physiological needs.

The First Thorn Knight, in the midst of battle...

Was actually engaging in such a shameful act behind the backs of countless men. Heh heh heh~

Chapter 64 — Bonus Update: Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 64

Clock Tower.

Intense magical elements swept around.

Ferocious wind surged from the crimson magic circle.

Quickly plunging the area into a pitch-black vortex.

The forbidden magic of "Elf's Lament" continued unabated, and the timing for the Dark Elf King's resurrection grew increasingly ripe.

Crimson light flooded the great hall, accompanied by Shelley's miserable screams--

"Aaaaaaaaaaaaah!"

The high-decibel shriek sent chills down one's spine, making it hard to fathom what kind of agony would wring such a piercing sound.

Shelley was at the center of the crimson magic circle, her body suspended midair, her movements slightly twisted in a way that made onlookers ache in sympathy.

Her eyes rolled back, tears streaming down her face uncontrollably.

The consciousness she had clung to was slowly beginning to scatter, no longer able to withstand the tsunami-like onslaught!

After all, Shelley was a frail soul, unable to endure such torturous agony, and at moments like these, death had become nothing short of deliverance.

"Hehehe, hahaha..."

Samuel, wand in hand, continuously channeled the forbidden magic circle, feeling as though the moment of the Dark Elf King's resurrection was drawing ever nearer, already within grasp.

The age belonging to the elves was about to arrive...

No, it was the age of dark elves!

Samuel's heart pounded with indescribable excitement. Once the Dark Elf King was successfully resurrected, he himself would become a figure of unparalleled majesty, ranking just below one but above tens of thousands.

"Soon, very soon, His Majesty the great Athudor shall return to this world and reign supreme!"

Samuel laughed wildly, utterly devoid of any dignity or elegance, his eyes consumed only by madness.

The Dark Elf King's resurrection was now at roughly ninety percent. As long as he waited a little longer, the balance of the world would be turned upside down, and everything would bear the name of "Athudor."

Once Shelley's consciousness fully scattered, the Dark Elf King could be reborn in his complete form, rather than merely peering into this world through his eyes as he could now.

"Princess Shelley, I advise you to abandon your futile resistance and willingly surrender your soul, contributing your strength to the establishment of the new world. Although this shall be the age of dark elves, it will bring glory to the entire elven race..."

Samuel hadn't even forgotten to urge Shelley on, hoping for her willing cooperation.

"I believe it's terribly impolite to force a beautiful lady to submit through violence. What do you think, Lord Samuel...?"

A clear, resolute male voice suddenly rang out, stirring quite a commotion in the darkened great hall.

After all, apart from Samuel and Shelley, there were no living souls left in this place.

The sudden voice startled Samuel. He didn't know who could have arrived here and feared the resurrection plan might be disrupted.

"Who?!"

Samuel bellowed angrily, his mood souring. He couldn't afford any mistakes at this critical moment.

Though he could pause momentarily, if he failed to inject mana into "Elf's Lament" for too long, the entire grand magic circle would collapse outright.

"HAVE you forgotten me already, Lord Samuel? Didn't we meet at a ball in the royal palace before?"

The Seventh Thorn Knight, Morrison, walked forward slowly. In the dim light, one could barely make out his bright smile and somewhat stylish pink hair.

"Oh~" Samuel recognized Morrison and spoke calmly. "The renowned Seventh Thorn Knight himself. What brings you to my doorstep with such leisure?"

"You've caused quite a commotion, plunging the entire royal capital into crisis. With such turmoil and unrest, do you really think any of the Thorn Knights can afford to idle?" Morrison shrugged helplessly.

"Hmph, since you've appeared here, it proves that Saran, who lay in ambush along the way, has already been defeated, hasn't she? Truly a useless piece of trash."

Samuel was in a foul mood. He had hoped Saran could block the Thorn Knights, but now an irritating pest had slipped through anyway.

This was a critical juncture; one careless move and everything would be lost. Samuel's anger was understandable.

"You laid an ambush along the way? What a pity—I didn't encounter any..." Morrison shook his head.

"Slipped through the net..." Samuel frowned, unable to fathom where Morrison had come from.

"Nevertheless, your subordinates, no matter what, probably wouldn't stand a chance against the other Thorn Knights," Morrison said with a shrug, looking remarkably at ease.

"Hah, so confident?" A cold sneer curled Samuel's lips.

"We're the elite of all Britannia. Do you take us for good-for-nothings? Without real skill, how could any of us be among the twelve?" Morrison explained indifferently.

Whether it was Millius or Winifred, both possessed formidable strength.

As for Maysfield, the First Thorn Knight, there was hardly anything to say.

"Between you and me, the Thorn Knights are basically good-for-nothings in my eyes. Even the renowned Maysfield, I have the ability to trample underfoot..." Samuel wore an ambiguous, half-smiling expression.

"Lord Samuel, you've truly changed so much. Think back to who you used to be—so beautiful and elegant, simply the most dazzling socialite at every ball. But now you've become so hideous. It's quite disappointing..." Morrison's face showed a hint of melancholy.

"Did my dark elf appearance frighten you?" Samuel's tone was utterly flat.

"A bit, perhaps. At first I thought you were an ordinary person. I never expected you to be someone who could operate a grand magic circle entirely on your own strength..." Morrison gripped his gauntlets, seemingly preparing to get serious.

"There's even more to astonish you. What you see is merely the tip of the iceberg," Samuel sneered.

"Is that so? I have no interest in seeing it at all." Morrison twisted his gauntlets, then glanced at Shelley at the center of the magic circle. "Before I make my move, I'd like to ask—who is that beautiful elven lady?"

"I don't mind telling you, but don't be frightened."

Samuel paused and continued, "She is Her Highness Shelley, the youngest daughter of the Elf King. How does that strike you? Surprised?"

Morrison was suddenly stunned. He never imagined that the elven princess everyone had been searching for was right here!

Judging from the current situation, she had been held captive by his men—that explained why they couldn't find her all this time.

Morrison's expression instantly grew grave. He understood the gravity of the matter and knew he had to rescue the elven princess as quickly as possible. That was the pressing emergency.

"You bastard, actually harboring the princess all this time. What in the world are you plotting?"

"You needn't know. Just understand this—from today onward, Britannia shall cease to exist," Samuel said sinisterly.

"Really? I'll see for myself what confidence you draw from, Lord Samuel..." Golden battle aura suddenly erupted from Morrison's body, scattering the surrounding darkness.

"Though fighting a woman is somewhat inelegant, I won't hold back against a venomous wretch like you."

"As long as I'm here, your ambitions will never come to pass!"

title: Chapter 65
content:
Chapter 65

Volume 7 · Chapter 65

Morisson’s figure darted back and forth like a cheetah.

To an outsider, it was nothing more than a golden blur.

As the seventh Thorn Knight, Morisson’s strength was far from weak—enough to crush most people.

But before Samuel, he was still a small fry facing a master, completely on the defensive.

This showed that Samuel, who appeared to be a frail woman, possessed a power that could only be described as terrifying!

Morisson was highly skilled in close combat, but against Samuel, it was useless.

Because Samuel was a wind-type mage, and Morisson couldn’t find any opening to close the distance and unleash his martial techniques.

The situation was dire. After several exchanges, Samuel remained composed and unmoving, while Morisson was already showing signs of fatigue.

A devastating tornado struck, forcing Morisson to scramble like a monkey, looking utterly pathetic.

His counter punches were all blocked by thick wind walls—he couldn’t even break through Samuel’s defense!

?

Samuel wasn’t even using her full strength. She had spared some energy to maintain the *Spirit’s Lament* grand magic circle, yet she still had more than enough to deal with Morisson.

Several fierce wind blades shot out, their power seemingly capable of tearing through space itself as they sliced through the air!

Morisson barely dodged with a series of flips before landing heavily on the ground, propping himself up with one hand as he glared at Samuel.

“Hahaha~” Samuel let out a light laugh, her voice dripping with disdain. “This is your strength? How pathetic. I feel like I’m watching a monkey perform…”

“Tch!” Morisson curled his lip, a cold sweat rolling down his forehead. Samuel’s power was far beyond what he had imagined! His combat skills were useless against her—he couldn’t even get close!

“I told you Thorn Knights are all useless. Do you believe me now?” Samuel bared her fangs, mocking him. “Maybe you’re impressive in Great Britain, but out here, you’re nothing but a bunch of weaklings who don’t belong on the big stage.”

“That’s—” Morisson gritted his teeth and slowly stood up.

“Having trouble accepting reality? After seeing someone as powerful as me, are you starting to question your life?” Samuel’s lips curled up, her tone haughty.

“Not at all. I’m not that weak.” Morisson adjusted his gauntlets and said seriously, “Let me tell you, we Thorn Knights are far from weak. Each of us has our own unshakable convictions.”

“Hmph. Then keep deluding yourselves in your little circle. Unable to witness true strength, you’ll forever live in your own dreams like a bunch of country bumpkins.” Samuel sneered. “Even Mesfield is just an overhyped fake—nothing more.”

“Country bumpkins, huh?” Morisson’s gaze turned serious, his voice calm. “I admit you’re strong. Wind magic is powerful, and I’ve always struggled against defensive mages. But that doesn’t mean I have no chance of winning.”

“Defensive mage?” Samuel acted as if she’d heard the funniest joke in the world. “You’ve got some nerve. I was just toying with you like a monkey. If I had been serious, you’d already be dead.”

“Is that so? Then I beg you—get serious. Let me witness the profound mysteries of elven magic!”

Morisson roared, and the Saint-tier aura around him suddenly transformed, surging like a raging beast!

His skin gradually turned crimson, veins bulging violently as if they might burst at any moment.

In a short span, Morisson had transformed into a red-skinned monster, his presence now many times stronger than before!

This was Morisson’s ultimate technique—*Rakshasa*—transforming from human into a battle-crazed demon, with all his abilities skyrocketing!

“Oh? Interesting…” Samuel remained composed, as if Morisson’s move was barely worth her attention.

“Let’s have a proper fight!” Morisson stomped the ground and shot forward like a red lightning bolt, nearly shattering the clock tower’s floor.

“Do you think turning into a red-hot crab makes you my equal? Foolish!” Samuel flicked her fingers, and a violent storm erupted, howling as it lunged at Morisson.

“Hah!” Morisson shattered the storm with a single punch and closed in on Samuel.

“Not bad…” Samuel, unfazed even in danger, still had the leisure to mock.

Morisson’s eyes flashed crimson, and his second punch followed instantly. Though it didn’t land, the sheer force of the punch’s wind alone was enough to tear a person apart!

Just then, a massive tornado suddenly spiraled up from beneath Samuel’s feet, encasing her in a 360-degree, flawless defense—offense and defense in one!

Morisson, as if possessed, drove his fist into the tornado. His gauntlet shattered, his arm injured, and he was sent flying by the impact!

“Feel your own powerlessness! Hahaha…” Samuel let out manic laughter, hooking her finger as two tornadoes lashed out like whips, striking the airborne Morisson and spinning him into a whirlwind top!

Morisson crashed into the wall, collapsing to the ground, motionless. The intricate stained glass shattered, and his body was covered in fresh, bloody wounds.

“With strength like yours, you dare challenge me? I have no interest in bullying children…” Samuel shook her head with a smile, speaking casually. “Among the Thorn Knights, only Mesfield could exchange a couple of blows with me—and even then, just a couple.”

“What a joke… *cough*…” Morisson, his body still crimson, forced himself up with his fists.

“Can you even stand? I advise you to give up. If you keep this up, you’ll die a miserable death.” Samuel taunted.

“Do you really think I’ll just give up because you tell me to?!”

Morisson’s Saint-tier aura grew even more violent, shifting from gold to black!

His crimson skin grew even more lustrous, and with a few twitches on his forehead, two red horns burst out!

This was the second stage of *Rakshasa*—he now truly resembled a demon!

Morisson’s power surged once more, and even his wounds healed instantly!

“You can still get stronger? Are you a cockroach?” Samuel’s expression turned serious. Even from a distance, she could sense the near-maddening pressure.

“I will defeat you honorably!” Morisson’s voice had grown hoarse, but the fury in his tone was overwhelming.

“You’d better be careful. I’m nothing like I was before.”

“To be honest… even I’m afraid of this power.”

“Because it’s so overwhelming, I can barely control it…”

Outside.

Merlin tilted his head back, gazing up at the 300-foot clock tower, deducing that the source of the chaos must be at the top.

“So high… Well, with my body, it’s not that difficult…”

Merlin frowned, crouched down, then exploded upward, intending to leap directly to the top of the clock tower.

The sonic boom shattered countless stained-glass windows, raining colorful shards down below.

The flat ground was left with shocking cracks, as if a monster had stomped across it.

And just as Morisson and Samuel’s clash of the weak had reached its climax…

The true powerhouse arrived.

title: Chapter 67 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Chapter 67 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 67

"Hahaha..." Samuel laughed as if he had heard the funniest joke in the world, his stomach aching slightly. "Are you living in a dream? You actually think you can kill me? How amusing. It seems you’ve gotten too into your role—do you really think you’re the great swordmaster Elgin?"

Morison, sprawled on the ground nearby, wore a complicated expression. Samuel was a powerful Saint-tier warrior—even he couldn’t defeat her. How could an ordinary person with no magic or aura possibly win? Wasn’t that just a fairy tale?

"Too into my role? That’s a first for me." Merlin curled his lips into a smile, his masked face hiding his true thoughts.

Samuel’s smile deepened, her curiosity piqued. "You’re really in a hurry to die... Well, let me ask—what’s a trash villager like you doing here?"

"At first, I came to save Sherry," Merlin said, staring at Samuel with no hint of jest. "But now, I’m more interested in killing you."

Morison furrowed his brows. *Save Sherry?* Who was this masked man? Could he have some connection to the Elven Royal Family?

"You’re living in a dream, talking big like that. Hehe~"

Samuel sneered, not the least bit angry—she didn’t even consider Merlin worth her attention.

In her eyes, Merlin was just a tiny ant she could crush at any moment.

Would you bother stomping on an ant buzzing at your feet? Probably not. That was exactly how Samuel felt—arrogant to the extreme.

"But it’s a shame. You can’t save Sherry, and you certainly can’t defeat me!"

"Oh..." Merlin replied indifferently. "You think beating this little pink-haired guy means you can crush anyone? Honestly, he’s trash too. Does beating a rookie give you a sense of achievement? Your pride sure is cheap."

Morison’s eyes widened. He never expected this man—who seemed neither friend nor foe—to insult him at a time like this! No face left at all! *Leave a little room in dealings, and you’ll meet again someday!*

How had he, a Thorn Knight, been reduced to a worthless stepping stone?

"Who’s trash?! Watch your mouth! I’m the Seventh Thorn Knight—I wasn’t even using my full strength earlier!"

"Could you please stop making noise?" Merlin glanced at Morison on the ground. "Since you’re a loser, just shut up and don’t distract me. Okay?"

Morison was left speechless, humiliation burning in his chest. He, the Seventh Thorn Knight, had been looked down upon by a villager with no magic or aura! How unbearable!

"You’re surprisingly arrogant," Samuel’s expression twisted into a snarl. "Do you know why I’ve wasted so many words on you instead of killing you?" She laughed. "Because killing a bug like you would be beneath me! I can’t even be bothered to lift a finger to cast a spell on you."

"Your act is so over-the-top it’s spiraling..." Merlin said, his expression unreadable. "Too lazy to even lift a finger to kill me? How ridiculous."

"Regardless of who you are, don’t interfere. Stay out of my way."

Samuel’s fingers twitched, and a storm wall of immense destructive power rose between her and Merlin. Countless wind blades swirled rapidly, hissing as they tore through the air—capable of shredding any enemy who dared cross.

Against a powerless weakling, this wind wall was more than enough.

Samuel continued channeling *Elven Lament*, the Dark Elven King’s resurrection progress at 98%. After ten millennia, he was about to return to the world!

Merlin knew he couldn’t delay any longer. He had to save Sherry first—now wasn’t the time for idle chatter.

So Merlin strode forward boldly, as if intending to break through the wind wall head-on.

Morison’s heart jolted in shock. *This masked man must be out of his mind!* He was just an ordinary person—how could he charge into Samuel’s wind wall? That was suicide! He’d be shredded instantly!

"Hey, calm down!" Morison shouted. "I know you’re eager to save her, but don’t throw your life away! Be patient—help will arrive soon!"

Merlin ignored him, sprinting forward as fierce winds whipped around him. He crashed straight into the wind wall—

"You’re not Elgin the Great Swordmaster! You’re just an ordinary man—stop living in a dream!" Morison yelled desperately, certain Merlin was about to die.

But the gruesome scene never came.

To Morison’s shock, the wind wall *retreated* as if avoiding Merlin, parting to reveal Samuel still channeling her spell!

Morison fell silent, eyes wide in disbelief. *What the hell?* How did the wind wall just... open? What had this masked man done? Could he really be the legendary Elgin the Great Swordmaster?

The thought left Morison uncertain. If the legendary Elgin *was* just an ordinary man with no magic or aura... that would be earth-shattering.

Samuel poured all her strength into *Elven Lament*—the resurrection progress had reached 99%!

Seeing this, Samuel burst into laughter. The Dark Elven King’s return was imminent.

"Rise, my lord!"

"Fill this world with endless darkness!"

"Let the era of the Dark—*BLAM!*"

Before she could finish, Merlin, who had somehow passed through the wind wall, punched her square in the face. Her face twisted, teeth and blood spraying from her mouth.

"*Cough!*"

Samuel cried out, her body thrown off balance as she crashed into a thick wall.

The Dark Elven King’s resurrection progress froze—stuck at 99%.

Samuel barely managed to stand, her expression a mix of shock and stupor, blood dripping from her mouth. "H-How...? How did you, an ordinary man, pass through my wind wall unharmed?!"

Merlin glanced at the *Elven Lament* spell circle, now halted, and finally relaxed slightly.

He rolled his shoulders, a smirk playing on his lips. "Passing through a wind wall? What’s so surprising about that? Is it really that difficult?"

Morison’s face was blank, his gaze locked on Merlin’s back, his mind racing. *Heaven’s sake... How did he do it?*

He had effortlessly injured Samuel!

*I fought with everything I had and couldn’t even touch her, but he...*

title: Chapter 68
content:
Chapter 68

Volume 7 · Chapter 68

Samuel watched a bead of cold sweat roll down Merlin’s forehead, sensing something was off.

Now she finally realized one thing: the mysterious masked man before her was far from weak.

How could an ordinary person, who couldn’t sense magic or aura, cross her Wind Wall unscathed?!

That was impossible. She was probably a fake Saint-tier powerhouse!

Samuel’s expression turned grave. She silently wiped the blood from the corner of her mouth with her arm and decided to get serious.

"What a joke! A normal person crossing my Wind Wall would be torn to shreds! Yet you came through completely unharmed—that’s not normal!"

Morris thought the same, but recalling Merlin’s initial introduction, he wondered: Could this man really be the legendary great swordsman of Elgin? How could someone without magic or aura be this strong? It was too unbelievable!

"Hmph, this isn’t worth bragging about, but I’ll tell you the truth: no matter how powerful your magic is, it won’t have the slightest effect on me. So if you’re thinking of killing me with magic, save your breath. I’d advise you to grab that staff and face me in a proper duel instead." Merlin spoke seriously—he wasn’t joking. Compared to magic, smashing his head in with a staff would clearly be more effective.

"You expect me to believe that nonsense?" Samuel smirked, convinced Merlin was just bluffing.

"Suit yourself." Merlin shrugged, offering no further explanation.

"In all of Great Britain, the number of people who can harm me can be counted on one hand. You must be someone of renown, right?" Samuel narrowed her eyes, her voice dripping with suspicion. "Who are you?"

"Didn’t we meet this morning? You’ve already forgotten how I humiliated your two subordinates?" Merlin grinned, not revealing his name but dropping a hint to jog her memory.

"What?! It’s you!" Samuel froze for a moment, then her eyes widened. No wonder her Wind Wall had no effect—this mysterious masked man was the Black Iron adventurer from this morning, the one with a rare magic-defense artifact. Even Salan had suffered at his hands!

Merlin just smiled, having long anticipated her reaction.

"Did Sharron die trying to kill you? Even after drinking a top-tier Dark Rage Potion, he still wasn’t your match?!" Samuel’s voice trembled with shock. She knew that after taking the potion, Sharron had the strength to fight a peak Saint-tier warrior head-on. Yet he had still lost to Merlin. It seemed she had no choice but to take this Black Iron adventurer seriously.

"Emmmmm..." Merlin’s mind filled with question marks. He had no idea what she was talking about. "I don’t know what you’re saying, but I’m fine, so that’s all that matters."

Morris lay on the ground, observing the situation. If Samuel had met the legendary great swordsman of Elgin, then she must know his identity! This was a major breakthrough!

Samuel fell into deep thought. There was no doubt about it—Sharron must be dead. Even if this Black Iron adventurer wasn’t the one who killed him, it had to be that high-ranking demon swordswoman. Otherwise, Merlin wouldn’t be here!

The crimson magic circle at the center lost its power as Samuel’s magic supply was cut off, causing the suspended Sherry to drop to the ground. The flickering formation dimmed, losing its original color.

"......" Morris blinked, feeling this was a good omen.

Panic set in for Samuel. If she kept letting Merlin stall her, the entire Dark Elf King resurrection plan would fail. All her years of effort would go to waste!

But to continue the resurrection, she had to remove Merlin, this thorn in her side, or she’d keep being interrupted.

"Get out of my way!"

"You think I’ll just leave because you told me to? That’d make me look pretty pathetic." Merlin wore a carefree smile.

"You bastard, do you have a death wish?!" Samuel gritted her teeth.

"I just love watching you so flustered and helpless." Merlin spread his hands.

"Don’t think some rare magic-defense gear gives you the right to flaunt yourself in front of me!" Samuel pointed her staff at Merlin, her voice deadly serious. "With my power, destroying your defenses is only a matter of time!"

She wasn’t joking. As a mage, facing someone with magic-defense equipment was indeed troublesome, but with her transcendent strength, she could still erase Merlin from existence. She had absolute confidence in herself!

"Plenty of people have tried to destroy me. None succeeded. You’ll just be another one." Merlin’s eyes flickered with a crimson glow as he responded with disdain.

"Arrogant fool! You’re all talk! Die!"

Samuel roared, gripping her staff and slowly spinning it in front of her. Golden Saint-tier magic surged forth, its terrifying pressure rising by the second.

Morris, despite his injuries, was stunned. Samuel was finally serious—and her true power was terrifying. She was clearly on the same level as Mesfield!

Samuel swung her staff, and nine apocalyptic tornadoes materialized, surging toward Merlin with devastating force. Wherever they passed, destruction followed. The sheer power was horrifying!

But before Merlin, all magic was trash.

The nine terrifying tornadoes dissipated into nothingness in front of him, as if their magic had been completely drained.

Merlin hadn’t moved an inch. He simply watched Samuel’s display.

When the storm cleared, Merlin shrugged helplessly. "That’s it? You’re not as strong as I thought."

Morris’s jaw dropped. Now he was absolutely certain: this masked man, misunderstood by all, was none other than the legendary great swordsman of Elgin! There was no doubt. Samuel’s magic had no effect on him—it had to be because the power gap was just too vast. The great swordsman of Elgin was indeed as strong as the rumors claimed!

"Why?! How is this possible?! What kind of magic-defense artifact are you wearing?! My full-power spell had no effect at all?!" Samuel couldn’t believe her eyes. Her expression twisted, clearly unwilling to accept this reality.

In her nearly thousand years of life, she had never heard of any magic-defense artifact this effective. Normally, a sufficiently powerful magic surge could shatter it with ease.

But Merlin defied all logic. Her magic attacks had zero effect on him. It was incomprehensible!

"Looks like you’ve exhausted all your tricks. Had your fun yet?" Merlin assumed a sword-drawing stance, his gaze locked in, his ruby-like eyes flashing continuously.

"Then it’s my turn."

"Come on, let me use your death to put a perfect end to this grand spectacle..."

title: Chapter 69 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 69 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 69

Samuel’s eyes were nearly popping out of their sockets, her head throbbing with rage as hatred thickened on her face.

In her eyes, Merlin was just an Iron-ranked adventurer, the weakest of the weak—someone she would have ignored without a second thought in the past.

But now, this insignificant Iron-ranked adventurer was a thorn in her side, and she had no way to deal with him.

The main issue was that her magic had no effect on him at all?

This made Samuel doubt her life. She was an elite Saint-tier mage, yet here she was, stumped by an Iron-ranked adventurer!

If word got out, no one would believe it. They might even revoke her status.

Samuel couldn’t understand it. Her magic had always been unstoppable, yet she couldn’t break through Merlin’s magical defenses. What kind of magical defensive equipment was he using? Could it be some kind of divine artifact?

But divine artifacts were so rare—how could one possibly be in the hands of a mere Iron-ranked adventurer?

Little did Samuel know, Merlin possessed the world-level bug known as [Magic Immunity]!

Merlin stood in a sword-drawing stance, his gaze fixed on Samuel. Calmly, he said, “Though I have other ways to defeat you, I still choose the simplest and most direct method: slaughter.”

Samuel gritted her silver teeth, teetering on the edge of furious madness, beyond reason.

“I’ve had a few casual chats with your so-called Princess Sherry,” Merlin paused, then continued in a deep voice, “That girl doesn’t have any grand dreams—plain and ordinary, to put it bluntly.”

“But she has one conviction: an unwavering determination to return to her homeland.”

“No matter the suffering, she endures it all.”

“Even if I’m not a particularly just man, I can’t help but admire her a little.”

“But you—you’re the one crushing her small dream, stomping all over the one thing she’s held onto.”

“In my eyes, Sherry is just a lost girl trying to find her way home. The fact that she’s being bullied by a poisonous woman like you is truly unacceptable.”

“So, Princess Sherry’s wish to return home—I’ll make it come true for her!”

“And you? You’ll fall by my blade, tumbling into hell to suffer eternal humiliation.”

Morris, though confused by the situation, managed to piece together that Princess Sherry had indeed interacted with Elgin, the Great Swordsman himself.

Samuel’s expression twisted repeatedly. She, a distinguished Saint-tier mage and the most capable subordinate of the Dark Elf King, was being lectured by an Iron-ranked adventurer!

This was a blatant humiliation. She absolutely could not tolerate it. As a proud elf, how could she let a human look down on her?

The most troublesome part was the magical defensive equipment on that bastard. If she could just destroy it, she’d easily kill this Iron-ranked adventurer!

Samuel’s face contorted into a terrifying scowl. She steel her resolve to fight Merlin to the death, determined to crush him with her ultimate technique.

The magic formation of [Elven Lament] was growing dimmer by the second. Samuel’s anxiety deepened—time was running out.

With a sudden, violent motion, she slammed her staff into the ground, cracking the earth beneath her. A wild, unstoppable pressure surged upward!

“A mere human, daring to preach to me! Do you think you’re qualified to lecture me? Without your magical defensive equipment, you’re nothing!”

“Already lost control of your emotions? Then farewell....”

Merlin gave a faint, indifferent smile. His body moved in a blur, charging straight at Samuel.

No schemes, no tricks—just a direct, honorable duel.

“Don’t think your magical defensive equipment makes you invincible!” Samuel’s victorious magic power surged like a monster, roaring as if it were bellowing at Merlin. “Next, I’ll destroy you—and that precious defensive equipment of yours—all at once! With my strongest spell: Wind King’s Judgment! No one has ever survived this spell unscathed. I could even kill the Elf King with it!”

Wind King’s Judgment was Samuel’s ultimate technique—a wide-area, devastating attack with 360 degrees of relentless, inescapable offense!

Countless wind blades, sharp enough to slice through space itself, shot out at extreme speeds in all directions.

Their immense cutting power would gravely wound any enemy. The claim that this move could kill the Elf King was no exaggeration.

The Elf King, one of the oldest rulers, naturally had formidable defenses. But even he would face mortal danger under Wind King’s Judgment!

This proved that Samuel’s ultimate technique was indeed extraordinary. She had every right to be proud, to look down on the Thorn Knights.

Morris lay on the ground, his face pale, sensing the deadly aura. He was stunned. What kind of pressure was this?! Too strong! It could only be described as monstrous. Did she intend to level the entire kingdom?!

A tidal wave of golden Saint-tier magic power erupted, violently shaking the entire space. The Clock Tower trembled as if on the verge of collapse.

The initial shockwave alone made hearts skip a beat—proof of its extraordinary power!

Ultimate wind forces burst from the staff planted in the ground, whistling as they spread outward.

For a moment, it was like a white mandala blooming, dragging everything toward a final, inescapable death!

The air reeked of destruction. In an instant, the great hall was reduced to ruins, the walls and floors carved into ravines by the wind blades!

Morris’s expression filled with despair. This is it, he thought. If this continues, the entire Clock Tower will be destroyed! How could anyone survive such a terrifying attack?!

Samuel channeled her staff, continuously unleashing Wind King’s Judgment, her mockery unchecked:

“Hahahaha! What do you think? Isn’t my ultimate technique terrifying?”

“I haven’t used it in a long time, but today, I’ll let you witness true power!”

“You dared to be arrogant in front of me—you forced my hand. Now do you finally realize your mistake?”

“Why aren’t you saying anything? Already turned to dust? Hahahaha!”

Samuel laughed maniacally, the swirling wind blades obscuring her vision, making her believe she had already won.

But no matter how powerful Samuel’s magic was, what use was it against Merlin?

Merlin faced no resistance, no obstacle. He moved straight through the countless ultimate wind blades, crossing the storm of death, and appeared right before Samuel!

“...What?! Impossible!”

Samuel was stunned, her mouth hanging open. Terror filled her mind. How had Merlin passed through Wind King’s Judgment?!

Even magical defensive equipment couldn’t withstand wave after wave of ultimate wind blades. How could it have no effect?!

Was he even human?! How could such a person exist?!

How could a mere Iron-ranked adventurer have such power?!

There was only one possible explanation: he was a cheater! A damn cheater!

“You said you’d let me witness true power? I’ll return those words to you exactly as they are....”

Merlin’s voice was devoid of emotion, cold as the grim reaper claiming lives.

A crimson glow flickered in his eyes, instantly filling Samuel with dread.

Then, Merlin’s hand pressed down on the hilt of his katana. In the blink of an eye, he drew it, executing a single, fluid Iaijutsu slash.

Samuel’s head separated from her body, spinning through the air, her face still frozen in disbelief....

title: Chapter 70 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 70 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 70

Merlin beheaded Samuel in a single stroke, cleanly severing his head.

Samuel’s head spun through the air, his expression frozen in the disbelief of his final moments, eyes wide with shock and regret.

Even in death, Samuel never understood why he had died—why his magic had no effect on Merlin.

His consciousness dissolved, carrying the bitterness of unfulfilled ambition, leaving behind nothing but a cold corpse.

Blood cooled in midair, and Samuel’s head bounced to the ground like a deflated ball.

The stiffened body sprayed a fountain of blood, swaying before collapsing, twitching uncontrollably.

Merlin exhaled deeply, flicked his great sword twice, then sheathed it with a flourish.

Morris’s eyes nearly popped out of his skull, his mouth twitching, his heart pounding uncontrollably—

This… this was the power of Elgin, the Great Swordsman!

He had always assumed the legends exaggerated his strength!

But now, witnessing it firsthand, the reality was far more shocking!

Samuel had been a powerhouse, arguably even stronger than Mesfield.

Morris had trained so hard, yet he couldn’t even touch the hem of Samuel’s robe!

But Elgin the Great Swordsman had just one-shot Samuel in a single strike?!

This… this defied all logic!

A fine sheen of cold sweat broke out on Morris’s forehead. The sheer terror in his heart lingered, the overwhelming power of Elgin the Great Swordsman too absurd to comprehend. Those legendary instant kills were clearly no exaggeration!

"Lord Elgin, the Great Swordsman!"

"Hm?" Merlin dusted off his shoulders, watching the dirt fall away. "What is it?!"

Morris wanted to clarify one thing. A talent like Elgin the Great Swordsman—if he were an enemy, he’d be a terrifying threat. But if he were an ally, he’d be the strongest comrade imaginable!

"Not… a villain?" Morris pressed, his voice tense.

Merlin shook his head. "No."

Morris’s expression tightened. "Then… not a hero?"

Merlin shook his head again. "No."

Morris was confused, unable to categorize Elgin the Great Swordsman.

"What does it matter to you whether I’m good or bad?" Merlin frowned, his tone impatient.

"Please, don’t be angry, my lord!" Morris said earnestly. "I only want to understand your nature. Perhaps you could join us, serve Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth—no, serve the entire British Empire! You wouldn’t have to hide your true identity anymore. You could live openly, with honor!"

Morris’s voice was passionate, his offer bold. This was his plan: if Elgin the Great Swordsman pledged himself to Queen Elizabeth, the Thorn Knights would gain an unstoppable force. It would ease the queen’s worries and bolster the empire’s power—a perfect solution.

But this all hinged on one condition: Elgin the Great Swordsman couldn’t be irredeemably evil. Only then could he be a true ally.

If he were a villain, the only option would be to eliminate him.

And as a wanted man, Elgin the Great Swordsman must crave recognition. Serving the queen would be his chance to clear his name.

This opportunity was rare—overcoming obstacles would be difficult, but if Elgin the Great Swordsman became the queen’s ally, it would benefit everyone.

"Hah…" Merlin let out a cold laugh, amused by Morris’s attempt to recruit him. "Your queen has a bounty on my head, and you expect me to become her subordinate? That’s like slapping me and then offering me a date. Not interested."

"The bounty is no issue!" Morris insisted, his voice rising. "I’ll personally petition Her Majesty, explain everything! If you prove you’re not a villain and swear loyalty to Britain, her grace will surely overlook the past. Please, trust me!"

Merlin smirked faintly. So his bounty could just be lifted like that?

The queen had hunted him for so long—clearly, she had a grudge.

He waved a hand, utterly uninterested in Morris’s offer.

"Not interested."

"Eh?!"

Morris froze, stunned that Elgin the Great Swordsman would refuse.

This was an offer most would kill for! Yet Elgin the Great Swordsman didn’t even care?

Morris’s expression grew desperate. He cursed his lack of negotiation skills and pressed on.

"My lord, don’t refuse so quickly! Are you truly uninterested in becoming a Thorn Knight?"

"Not at all." Merlin shrugged. "What’s so great about being a Thorn Knight?"

"Hah?!" Morris’s eyes widened. Others would beg for the chance, yet here Elgin was, dismissing it outright!

"I won’t bow to anyone—not even your queen. If she wants to control me, she’d better be prepared to get cut down." Merlin spoke seriously. The idea of the First Demon Lord Palace’s Great Demon Lord serving a human was absurd.

"Uh…" Morris felt an undeniable kingly aura radiating from Elgin. He was so arrogant, so untamed—impossible to tame.

BOOM—BOOM—BOOM—

The clock tower trembled again, as if some unknown force was invading.

"W-What’s happening?!" Fear crept into Morris’s heart. He scanned the area—the crimson magic battle had faded, Samuel’s corpse lay still. What could possibly threaten them now?!

Merlin’s expression was also puzzled, unable to identify the force disturbing the clock tower.

Then, a raspy voice echoed, like the furious howl of the dead—

"Foolish mortal! How dare you interfere with my resurrection!"

"Isn’t life good enough for you? Why insist on such folly?!"

"I, Ashdoll, now declare your death!"

"Even if I return to the crevice between Hell and the mortal world, you won’t fare any better!"

Merlin and Morris looked up together. Through the glass dome, they saw a massive, blood-red eyeball in the sky, like a crimson moon.

Its sharp pupil resembled an abyss, glaring down at them with unbridled rage.

Ashdoll, the Dark Elf King, had long awaited this resurrection. But Merlin had ruined it—who knew when the next chance would come?

Filled with despair, Ashdoll decided to vent his fury on Merlin. Before being dragged back into the crevice between Hell and the mortal world—

He would use the "Divine Power" to annihilate Merlin and Morris right here!

title: Chapter 71 — Happy New Year.
content:
Chapter 71 — Happy New Year.

Volume 7 · Chapter 71

“不… impossible? That eye is a living creature?!” Morrison’s eyes widened to their limits, his heart trembling uncontrollably. He had always assumed the eyeball was just some ritual object, never expecting it to be an independent lifeform!

Merlin slightly furrowed his brows, showing no fear of the furious gaze but instead sensing a faint, eerie aura—completely different from anyone he had encountered before!

If Merlin’s guess was correct, the owner of that eye was definitely no weakling. It possessed a power he had never seen before!

“Though I have only one eye, it’s more than enough to annihilate you!”

“This is an insurmountable power—you’ve certainly never seen its like!”

“Come, mortal! Tremble before the power of a god!!!”

The crimson, slender pupil in the sky suddenly lit up, radiating a blood-red brilliance that swiftly illuminated the entire royal capital.

All living beings were instantly enveloped in a deep crimson terror, as if the apocalypse had arrived early.

A violent gale abruptly rose, whipping up debris from the ground and surging toward the solitary eye in the heavens.

It seemed a world-ending force was quietly brewing—but so was the threat.

Behind the Dark Elf King’s single eye, a black vortex slowly materialized, like a path leading to another dimension.

This was the crevice between the mortal world and hell, the wandering ground of souls!

Asmodeus could no longer be revived. He was certain to be dragged back into the crevice, but before vanishing, he was determined to take down the bastard who had stopped his resurrection!

An immense energy was gathering, its intensity shockingly terrifying. The pressure was almost unbearable—far beyond what Saint-tier magic could achieve! It was as if it transcended the very framework of the world.

Merlin’s brows knitted together in rare concern. The power amassing in the sky was extraordinary, radiating a dangerous presence.

Meanwhile, Morrison, lying on the ground and unable to rise, was utterly stunned. He had never experienced such energy before—it was almost as if it transcended dimensions. “Heavens! What… what kind of power is this?! It’s… it’s too terrifying!”

Merlin’s expression turned serious, his spirits lifting as he fixed his gaze on the eye in the sky, realizing he had to take this threat seriously.

After a long buildup, the Dark Elf King’s eye finally launched its attack.

A beam of crimson light shot straight from the eye, blasting downward toward Merlin and Morrison.

The colors of the world faded in comparison—nothing could rival even a fraction of the blinding intensity of this crimson beam!

It was as if a red sun had suddenly risen, illuminating the entire royal capital like daytime!

The magical elements in the air were instantly drained, and the seaside grew scorching hot.

“It’s over… this power… the entire capital will be reduced to ashes!” Morrison cried out repeatedly, his face pale. The sheer absurdity of this power left him with only one way to describe it: the power of a god!

In truth, the Dark Elf King’s power was exactly as Morrison imagined.

This attack, which seemed like a magic cannon, was not actually fueled by magic at all.

It was a transcendent power—*Divine Power*.

Asmodeus had inherited a portion of the power of Koreilon, the Elven God, allowing him to wield *Divine Power*—a unique energy far surpassing both magic and battle aura. It truly transcended this dimension.

Its destructive capability could effortlessly annihilate cities, a realm far beyond what magic or battle aura could ever achieve!

Such a high-order power was naturally rare, so it was no wonder Morrison was so flustered.

Asmodeus had dominated the elven race for so long, and now it made sense. How could someone so powerful have been defeated by the Elven King? It was truly unfathomable!

So, what was Merlin’s state of mind as he faced such an overwhelming attack?

He was excited. A reckless, unbridled smile still hung on his face, his heart brimming with anticipation for the slaughter!

Because the Dark Elf King, wielding *Divine Power*, seemed even stronger than Merlin’s hypothetical rival—the legendary Spear Hero!

This was no illusion—it was a very real sensation.

If the Spear Hero was powerful beyond Saint-tier,

then the Dark Elf King was *far* beyond Saint-tier!

The gap between them was undeniable, impossible to ignore!

Merlin now felt that the Dark Elf King must have been the strongest existence—what a pity he was already dead.

If he weren’t dead, Merlin would have been very interested in cutting him down to see if it could lift the curse on his heart.

But Merlin wasn’t a greedy man. This trip had already yielded a satisfying harvest.

When he had slain Samuel, his heart had sent a wave of relief, clearly easing the curse and greatly extending the time before its next flare-up.

Merlin’s will to fight was now burning fiercely. Even if the Dark Elf King was already dead and held little meaning for him, a battle was still worth having.

Because Merlin wanted to know his own limits, and the Dark Elf King was the perfect touchstone!

If Merlin could easily suppress the Dark Elf King, then the legendary Spear Hero would surely be no match for him either—proving, by extension, that Merlin was the stronger one!

The overwhelming beam of *Divine Power* roared toward him, but Merlin had no intention of dodging. He wanted to experience this power firsthand.

So, with arrogant defiance, he raised a single hand to block it—a rare show of respect for an opponent. Normally, he wouldn’t bother defending against foes.

The *Divine Power* beam struck Merlin, causing his body to tremble slightly as he was forced half a step back.

*Divine Power* was not magic, so the techniques it produced were entirely different. This rendered Merlin’s magic immunity useless—he couldn’t nullify this new force, only endure it head-on.

The rampant energy ravaged the surroundings, reducing them to further ruin. Merlin’s clothes were torn to shreds, nearly leaving him a naked, perverted madman.

The gale was so fierce that Morrison couldn’t keep his eyes open, but the unyielding, mighty back of Elkin the Great Swordsman was seared into his mind.

A direct confrontation?! That was possible?!

Morrison couldn’t believe it. Such a thing should have been impossible.

Yet Merlin had created many miracles before—this was just one more.

The brutal *Divine Power* beam was shattered by Merlin. Though his clothes were in tatters, he himself appeared completely unharmed.

“He… he actually did it?! How is that possible?!” Morrison exclaimed repeatedly, unable to believe the scene before him. This apocalyptic strike had been powerless against Elkin the Great Swordsman!

If all twelve Thorn Knights had charged together, Morrison was certain they would have been wiped out—there would have been no way to block it!

“You… you withstood my *Divine Power*?! How can a lowly human like you manage such a thing?!”

The giant eyeball in the sky trembled violently, clearly agitated. It couldn’t comprehend how Merlin had emerged unscathed.

“You’re pretty strong, you know? If you weren’t already dead, I’d be very interested in a proper fight.” Merlin narrowed his eyes, not sounding like he was joking.

“…A mere ant, yet you boast so boldly.”

The Dark Elf King seemed unable to hold on any longer. He could no longer remain in the mortal world and was passively swallowed by the inky vortex.

“Remember this, human. I will *never* let you go.”

“You can’t be lucky forever.”

“When I succeed in reviving, that will be the day you die, human!”

With that final roar, the Dark Elf King was completely devoured, returning to where he belonged.

“And just like that, he’s gone? What a shame…” Merlin sighed faintly, lifting his hand to examine a scorched wound. Clearly, it was from the clash with *Divine Power*—

It had actually managed to damage his flesh?

It felt like a magical attack, yet its nature was entirely different.

This Dark Elf King’s strength… was truly extraordinary…

title: Chapter 72 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 72 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 7 · Chapter 72

Merlin fell silent as he looked down at the wound on his hand.

His magic immunity had never once failed him before.

Yet against that mysterious eyeball's laser, it hadn't been dispelled directly.

This could only mean one thing—the attack just now wasn't magical power, but some other form of strength.

Merlin didn't yet have much understanding of "Divine Power," so the information he could gather was quite valuable.

Still, leaving a mark on himself was generally undesirable—it was probably a force higher than magical power.

Most people believed the Saint-tier was the limit of humanity, but Merlin believed someone could surpass it.

Yet now it seemed there were even higher realms, something Merlin himself wasn't entirely clear on—unheard of.

Still, this was good news for Merlin. It proved that truly powerful individuals existed, and his chances of breaking the heart curse were great!

This Dark Elf King was quite formidable.

If I could face him while he's still alive, I might actually get excited...

Merlin sighed and looked at the small wound on his hand, shaking his head in resignation. It wasn't a big deal.

In fact, since the Divine Power hadn't killed Merlin, the Dark Elf King was surprised too—just didn't show it on his face, thinking it was because his own strength hadn't fully recovered.

As for Morrison beside him, he didn't even feel surprise anymore, just stood there blankly as if he'd lost his soul.

When that Divine Power laser cannon had struck, he'd felt an unprecedented fear, nearly fainted on the spot.

Morrison stared at Merlin's retreating back, his mind filled with one thought: awesome, awesome, fucking awesome.

Morrison now deeply admired Elric the Great Swordsman. Beyond "awesome," he couldn't find any other words to describe him.

Seems all those exaggerated rumors were true, no exaggeration at all. Whether it was instantly killing two pirate kings or instantly killing countless Saint-tier undead, Elric the Great Swordsman could do it all effortlessly.

Before, Morrison thought Melfield was the strongest Saint-tier. But now that position had been shaken by Elric the Great Swordsman.

Merlin felt things were handled well enough and went to check on Snow.

If possible, he wanted to take Snow back to the hotel and flee the capital overnight.

Merlin glanced back at Snow lying on the ground. Right now, she had fallen unconscious.

Due to being within the great magic formation of "Elven Lament," Snow's spirit had suffered tremendous trauma. She seemed to have aged suddenly, and her golden hair now had several strands of white silk.

Merlin turned toward the unconscious Snow, but had only taken a few steps when a shrill shout rang out.

"Pervert! You dare spit on me to humiliate me! Go to hell, you bastard!"

Merlin paused, looked up, and saw Melfield descending from above!

Melfield wielded a straight sword, golden combat aura blazing around him, exuding the aura of someone about to split Mount Hua. Clearly, he intended to capture Merlin.

The other two Thorn Knights were also nearby, attacking like heavenly sentinels.

Vivian's face was grim and silent, with rocky giant fists floating beside him, pounding down relentlessly.

As for Miles, he was probably the most enraged. His slender sword danced elegantly, unleashing a barrage of meteor-like sword rain, shouting loudly.

"Such a minor criminal, daring to hit my handsome face! This humiliation I'll return to you in full!

The three Saint-tier Thorn Knights attacked in unison, nearly cutting off all of Merlin's escape routes.

Such a coordinated assault on a single enemy was rare even in Britain!

"Hmph." Merlin smiled calmly, not taking these guys seriously at all.

Morrison snapped back to his senses, seeing his companions attacking Elric the Great Swordsman. He was terrified—thought they were all ganging up on someone they couldn't beat, only to be killed in one strike!

"You... you stop! Elric the Great Swordsman isn't the enemy!"

Morrison shouted urgently, thinking that if they really fought, there'd be no chance to ease tensions, only making things worse.

The three Thorn Knights didn't hear Morrison's warning at all. Their eyes were fixed only on Elric the Great Swordsman, wanting to capture him and reclaim the honor of the Thorn Knights.

The combined assault crashed down with a thunderous sound, shaking the entire clock tower, nearly breaking the building apart!

Thick dust rose up, sweeping through the ruined hall, making it impossible to see clearly.

"..."

Morrison had no choice but to cover his mouth and nose, staring intently at the conflict.

He didn't know how things were going, hadn't expected his intervention to be useless, and they'd still started fighting.

He didn't know why. The three companions were unfriendly toward Elric the Great Swordsman.

Melfield and Miles, that was expected—they'd never liked Elric the Great Swordsman.

But Vivian was strange. He'd always been the most neutral, calm one. Why had he turned Elric into an enemy?

Morrison was very worried—not about Elric the Great Swordsman, but about his companions' safety.

After witnessing Elric the Great Swordsman's strength, Morrison felt that among the Thorn Knights, no one could easily defeat this mysterious man.

Yet the result was a false alarm—Morrison had worried for nothing.

As the thick dust settled, the three Thorn Knights stood stiffly, looking at the scene before them—now completely ravaged.

Elric the Great Swordsman, who had been right before them, was now nowhere to be seen, as if he'd evaporated, vanishing without a trace, leaving not even the slightest mark.

Facing the three Thorn Knights' combined assault, Merlin had moved freely; they couldn't stop him at all.

Morrison's eyebrows knit tightly. The attack just now had no blind spots—escaping was extremely difficult. Most Saint-tier warriors would be instantly defeated. Elric the Great Swordsman truly lived up to his reputation...

Melfield stared blankly at the spot, muttering, "He actually escaped. Our combined ambush was completely useless."

"...How did he do that?" Miles looked shocked, covering his face, unable to accept it. "We had him locked down. He was right there before us. How did he disappear in the blink of an eye? What kind of trick was that..."

Vivian's expression turned serious. He sensed the enormous gap in strength, a thread of despair rising in his heart. "If Elric the Great Swordsman didn't use a space-transfer movement technique, there's probably only one explanation..."

"What explanation?" Melfield asked uncertainly.

"Elric's legendary great sword..." Vivian paused, sweat dripping from his forehead, his expression very serious as he said, "His speed and strength completely crushed us three."

"To be precise, even all three of us combined aren't as strong as this guy."
