title: Chapter 73 — Cheers
content:
Chapter 73 — Cheers

Volume 7 · Chapter 73

Mersfield suddenly paused, clearly having difficulty accepting this conclusion.

However, he had no choice but to admit that Winifred's words made a lot of sense. The only reason he hadn't sensed any fluctuation in magical power earlier was probably due to just one explanation.

That was because Elgin the Great Sword Master hadn't used any magic at all, but instead relied on absolute speed and raw strength to evade the combined assault and toy with all three Thorn Knights.

Even a single fly would have found it impossible to fly out of the situation back then, yet Elgin had managed to do it! Such movement speed was truly rare in this world.

All three Thorn Knights combined weren't as strong as Elgin the Great Sword Master. The gap in their power was unusually massive!

Winifred was someone who was unwilling to lie, so coming to such a conclusion meant he was likely not far off.

This was still a conservative estimate, since Winifred hadn't personally witnessed Elgin unleashing his full power. If he had, the assessment might have been even more one-sided.

"...What?" Milesius's expression twisted. "How could the gap be that big?"

"I'm telling you the facts, not exaggerating in the least." Winifred frowned deeply and spoke seriously. "Didn't you ambush Elgin the Great Sword Master before and nearly get your face smashed in by a single punch? Don't you have any idea how vast the gap is?"

"...Milesius was speechless. He really couldn't mount a defense,只能 turning red in the face and throat as he forced an explanation. "I still didn't use my real abilities, and moreover, Elgin the Great Sword Master knew I was planning to ambush him at that time, so he deliberately exposed a weakness in his back, waiting for me to take the bait!"

Winifred shook his head. It was easy to see that Milesius's explanation was weak and feeble — he had simply been thoroughly beaten.

"Winifred, you're really stupid. Why feed others' ambitions while crushing your own morale?" Milesius looked displeased and couldn't resist shooting back a remark.

"I'm merely stating a fact. I don't want to argue with you, Milesius."

Winifred frowned and shut his mouth, remaining silent.

"Mersfield! Do you also admit that we're weaker than Elgin the Great Sword Master?" Milesius turned to ask.

"This..." Mersfield hesitated, thinking to himself that he had never gone all-out against Elgin. However, if all the rumors were true, then he definitely wouldn't be his match.

Besides, during their brief exchange earlier, he had been on the back foot the entire time. Perhaps he really was weaker than Elgin the Great Sword Master.

Even though a vague foreboding stirred in Mersfield's heart, he absolutely couldn't admit it lightly before actually fighting. He was the face of the Thorn Knights — if he admitted it, the prestige of the London Knight Order would drop significantly.

Morrison, watching from afar, wrinkled his brows and thought, Elgin the Great Sword Master had already disappeared — what were these people arguing about?

Hearing Morrison's shout, the three snapped back to their senses and remembered the serious matter at hand.

"Morrison, how did you end up injured like this? Did Elgin the Great Sword Master do this?" Winifred hurried over and supported Morrison.

"Did Elgin the Great Sword Master do this?" Mersfield walked over, examined Morrison's injuries, and felt the severity of his wounds. He thought that this bastard Elgin hit far too hard, showing absolutely no mercy.

He had once believed Elgin was merely an idle knight-errant, but now it seemed entirely a one-sided imagination of his — utterly rotten.

And he even spat on Mersfield's face, making him turn into... that disgraceful sight! All he could do was avoid everyone's gaze and secretly handle his nearly uncontrollable desires alone in private, which was absolutely humiliating.

So now Mersfield no longer wanted to arrest Elgin alive. Instead, he wanted to kill him outright, so he couldn't ease his sense of humiliation.

But in the end, Mersfield still couldn't figure out how Elgin the Great Sword Master's saliva worked — it had the same effect as an aphrodisiac, and an even stronger one at that! Perhaps there was poison in it.

Mersfield blushed slightly recalling that pleasure. It felt... pretty good, indeed. But it was an insult to his dignity!

Milesius glanced at Morrison's injuries without thinking and directly pinned the blame on Elgin the Great Sword Master.

"This bastard is exactly what Her Majesty the Queen predicted. Elgin the Great Sword Master is a threat to the empire's safety. If possible, he must be eliminated! Perhaps this incident is also connected to this guy."

"That's not true, you're all misunderstanding..." Morrison's face darkened as he said speechlessly, "The mastermind behind this incident is the Elf Tribe. It should be an internal conflict between the White Elves and the Black Elves, and we got dragged into it inexplicably."

"The Elf Tribe?" Mersfield paused. He recalled encountering Sarah, the commander of the Elf Tribe's embassy, on the road and sensing something suspicious back then. He didn't expect this chaos to truly be related to the Elf Tribe.

"Yes, Samuel orchestrated all of this. She's actually a Black Elf. In order to revive the Dark Elf King, she wanted to sacrifice the entire capital..." Morrison explained briefly, getting the story across in just a few sentences.

"Samuel..." Milesius narrowed his eyes, muttering to himself. "It's actually her. I always thought she was a gentle and kind elf. I never expected her to be a ruthless radical."

Winifred's brows knit together as he fell silent, thinking that Britain couldn't solve this matter on its own. They would need the Elf King from the Southern United Kingdom to assist.

"Where's Samuel? Don't tell me she ran away?!" Mersfield was extremely annoyed, thinking that Samuel had always pretended to be a good person, but it was all deception. If he didn't kill her with his own hands, he'd be letting down the citizens of the capital who had died!

"She's already been killed by Elgin the Great Sword Master..." Morrison said seriously.

"...Mersfield froze, surprised in his heart. What was going on? Why did Elgin the Great Sword Master kill Samuel? Did they have a personal grudge, or was he here to save the crisis?

When he intercepted them halfway, Elgin had said he had urgent business — it turned out he wanted to slay Samuel.

Was he trying to be a hero, deliberately saving the capital's citizens?

No way. That pervert isn't a decent person! There must be some selfish motive!

Mersfield's hatred toward Elgin the Great Sword Master was now very high, and his prejudice had grown greater than before, so he simply refused to believe Elgin was a representative of justice. He was just a lustful scoundrel who caused chaos wherever he went!

"Why is it Elgin the Great Sword Master again?! What is that bastard thinking? Putting on a show deliberately?! Does he really want to steal the spotlight so badly?" Milesius immediately showed disgust, grinding his teeth in anger.

"What could his purpose be? It's worth deep consideration..." Winifred stroked his chin's beard, pondering.

All three Thorn Knights couldn't fathom Elgin's purpose and motivations, unaware that he had come solely for the ten million gold coin reward, and resolving the London crisis was merely a side effect.

"Never mind all that for now. Quickly save that elf girl — she is the Elf King's youngest daughter, Princess Shelly!" Morrison pointed at the unconscious Shelly on the ground.

The three showed expressions of great shock, aware of the gravity of the situation.

"Princess Shelly is actually here?!" Milesius asked in surprise.

"Yes, it seems she was kidnapped by Samuel and made into a sacrifice." Morrison answered gravely.

"We exhausted ourselves searching everywhere for Princess Shelly, only to discover she was framed by her own kind, and right under our noses. What irony..." Winifred said with a complicated expression, feeling that so many people had been searching like headless flies, which was simply foolish!

Mersfield quickly ran over, picked up Shelly from the ground, and after quickly checking her condition, his expression immediately grew grave, filled with concern. He turned and said seriously to the others:

"Quickly bring Princess Shelly back to the palace and have the best court healers come over!"

At the top of the Clock Tower.

The moon was bright and stars were sparse, the wind格外 loud.

Merlin was lurking here, keeping his eyes fixed on the movements of the Thorn Knights below. Seeing that they were going to rescue Shelly, he immediately felt relieved.

The reason he hadn't taken Shelly himself was because he could see she had suffered spiritual damage, and he had no way to treat it.

Succubus saliva was definitely useless — it could only treat external wounds.

Cecilia's实力 as a priest was insufficient, making it difficult to treat spiritual damage as well, so he could only leave her to these Thorn Knights to mobilize royal authority.

As long as Shelly didn't die, the ten million reward was still his, so Merlin had no worries.

Besides, Shelly was an important protected figure of the British royal family and should not face any harm.

Perhaps after waking up, Shelly would understand that there are still kind humans in this world, more trustworthy than her own malicious kin.

Merlin withdrew his gaze and stood at the highest point of the Clock Tower.

The dark clouds had dispersed early, bright starlight shimmering, illuminating the silver gleam of his masquerade mask.

Moonlight flowed like water, ruffling his pitch-black robes as the wind swept.

His golden hair rustled softly, his eyes gazing down upon all living beings below, a unusual emotion welling up in his heart.

Merlin gripped the cheap-looking odachi at his waist, his dark silhouette resembling a demon god in the night.

After the disaster, surviving citizens stepped out of their homes, cautiously observing the scene outside, and directly saw this moment.

A resolute, powerful, invincible figure, standing atop the Clock Tower in the darkness, wind whipping his black robes sharply.

Elgin the Great Sword Master was at the height of his fame. Such a similar silhouette — how would the common folk think of anyone else? They felt Merlin must be the legendary sword master!

"Th-that's... Elgin the Legendary Sword Master?!"

"My goodness, this strong person has actually come to the capital?!"

"It must be him! He's the one who saved us from our crisis!"

"That's right! It must be Elgin the Great Sword Master, the hero of the capital!"

"Indeed, Elgin the Great Sword Master is the savior of the empire! The hero of humanity!"

"Long live Elgin the Great Sword Master! The real person looks a thousand, ten thousand times more handsome than the rumors!"

"This time too, he must have taken down the formidable enemy with only his own strength, right?!"

"Hero! Hero! Her..."

Cheers rose wave after wave, one louder than the next, ringing through the entire capital!

"Ugh, this matter has blown up again..."

Merlin furrowed his brows deeply, disliking this constant feeling of being misunderstood.

He glanced back at the crowd of onlookers below, his figure flickering, instantly vanishing into the dark night, a faint sound echoing in the wind.

Fools!

"I'm not the hero you all imagine."

"I'm the Great Demon Lord that makes you tremble in terror..."

title: Chapter 74 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 74 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 74

The capital city, ash rising.

After the turmoil, the city was in ruins everywhere.

Many residents came out, anxiously searching for missing family members.

Or they stared at their burning property, weeping bitterly.

Yet most still felt fortunate, believing they had survived the chaos by sheer luck, and couldn’t help but piously thank the Goddess of Light for her protection.

At this moment, a few black-robed preachers jumped out, preaching on the streets.

The priests claimed that someone had shown disrespect to the gods, so they had been punished by demons, but the Goddess of Light took pity on the innocent and sent the Salvation Knights to save the suffering sinners.

Merlin just scoffed, too lazy to argue. Let these charlatans spout their nonsense. In their eyes, the entire universe belonged to the Holy Church anyway.

If they found out the Salvation Knights were actually the Great Demon Lord, they’d probably collapse on the spot.

Merlin felt his identities were piling up—he was slowly becoming a spokesperson for all factions, and it was absurd.

The common people had many reasons not to trust the Holy Church. They still called Merlin "Elgin the Great Swordsman," finding the name more down-to-earth.

After all, in the eyes of the onlookers, Elgin the Great Swordsman was a hero who protected the common folk, belonging to no faction, free from class conflict.

This incident had once again made Elgin the Great Swordsman’s name explode in popularity—unmatched in the spotlight!

Rumors were spreading wildly that Elgin the Great Swordsman had saved the empire from crisis. Many had seen with their own eyes the man standing at the top of the clock tower, facing the biting wind, overlooking the world below.

No one would believe there was no connection between the crisis being resolved and Elgin the Great Swordsman’s appearance.

It wouldn’t take long for the tale of saving the capital to spread, and countless people would hear the name Elgin the Great Swordsman once more.

Perhaps Merlin never expected that his silhouette alone would have such growing influence, gradually affecting more and more people.

Even his infamous reputation as the First Demon Lord was being overshadowed by Elgin the Great Swordsman.

In an instant, he had transformed into a hero who saved the world, deeply rooted in people’s hearts.

But with greater influence came greater troubles...

Noble Hotel.

After the disaster, the refugees in the hotel had all left.

The owner woke up, saw the mess before him, and fainted again.

Though Merlin had single-handedly taken down the boss, the Purple Thorn Knights’ contributions couldn’t be ignored—most of the ghouls in the capital had been cleared by them.

Without their united efforts, the chaos wouldn’t have been suppressed so quickly.

But the moment Elgin the Great Swordsman appeared, he stole all the limelight and credit.

It seemed everyone was only interested in Elgin the Great Swordsman. No one even discussed the Purple Thorn Knights, which was a little disheartening.

Merlin shook off everyone and returned alone to the Noble Hotel.

With so many people around, his current disguise was particularly eye-catching.

So Merlin had no choice but to sneak in like a thief, climbing up to the third-floor window.

Merlin didn’t plan to return to his own room. Instead, he went straight to Alice’s.

When he had left earlier, he had changed clothes in Alice’s room, so his casual attire was still there. Naturally, he had to go retrieve it.

He could also take the opportunity to discuss Sherry’s situation—Alice was probably worried too.

It had to be said that Merlin had a natural talent for sneaking around. He climbed to the third floor without making a single sound, perfectly embodying the role of a flower-stealing bandit. It almost made one suspect he had some shady past profession.

*What the hell is this inexplicable excitement I’m feeling?*

Suddenly, he felt like he’d mastered another survival skill. If he ever lost his job, he wouldn’t have to worry...

Merlin thought darkly, scrambling up to the third-floor window with all limbs. Directly in front of him was Alice’s room.

Through the clear glass, Merlin surveyed the scene inside.

But what he saw left him awkwardly frozen, the black lines on his forehead drooping.

*What the hell is this?*

After the battle, Alice and Cecilia began treating their wounds.

Because of Sharplen’s surprise attack, both Alice and Kail had been injured, with Kail, being the weaker of the two, taking the worst of it.

So Cecilia carried the unconscious Kail to her room for priority treatment.

Alice’s injuries weren’t as severe, so she had to endure a little longer, letting Cecilia treat Kail first before coming back for her.

But Alice was only forcing herself to hold on. Having been struck twice by Sharplen, her injuries weren’t light either.

Before Cecilia arrived, Alice decided to administer some first aid herself, applying a topical ointment.

So what Merlin saw at that moment was Alice secretly undressing in her own room.

Perhaps due to her inner anxiety, Alice hadn’t even bothered to close the curtains. As a result, she inadvertently gave the suddenly returning Merlin an eyeful.

Alice had already removed her top, revealing her smooth, bare back and graceful curves. She looked especially alluring, exuding the innocent charm of a budding young girl.

Fortunately, Alice had her back to the window and hadn’t turned around. Otherwise, it would’ve been a full-on mosaic of divine light!

But even if she had turned around, there wouldn’t have been much to see—her chest was as flat as a washboard. If it covered her face, it’d be a bare-faced boy!

Faced with this sudden stroke of luck, Merlin remained completely calm inside, not a single impure thought in his mind. It wasn’t like he hadn’t seen Alice naked before. He just felt he had once again witnessed the power of the "backshot."

Alice held a red ointment in her hand, presumably for treating external injuries, and was struggling to reach her back with her arm, trying to apply the medicine to the scrapes there.

But her arms were a little too short, making the process difficult, and one couldn’t help but lament the importance of practicing yoga.

A cold sweat broke out on Alice’s forehead, her face flushed red. She felt her waist and back aching—she never expected applying medicine to herself would be so exhausting.

Now she actually wished someone would come help her, but then Merlin’s annoying face flashed through her mind.

Alice froze, stunned. *Why was the first person I thought of Merlin?!*

She smacked her own head, embarrassed. *Am I insane?*

*Why would I think of that bastard?*

*How could I let Merlin do something like this?*

*That’d just be handing him a free show for no reason!*

It’d look like she was deliberately tempting him—shameless!

The man she liked was Elgin the Great Swordsman. How could she get involved with another man like that?

Alice forced herself to calm down, banishing Merlin from her thoughts.

But she couldn’t help wondering—now that everything was over, how was Merlin doing? Why hadn’t he returned yet?

Merlin had no choice but to impersonate Elgin the Great Swordsman. Otherwise, moving around the capital would’ve been inconvenient.

Though Alice felt this was somewhat disrespectful to Elgin the Great Swordsman—a symbol of justice, being impersonated by an evil Great Demon Lord.

But she believed the real Elgin the Great Swordsman would understand. After all, she was doing it to save poor Miss Sherry, forced to do things she didn’t like.

And Merlin wasn’t the type to go overboard with anything. Even if he was pretending to be Elgin the Great Swordsman, he probably wouldn’t do anything unforgivable.

If Merlin had acted recklessly and tarnished Elgin the Great Swordsman’s name, Alice wouldn’t have forgiven him.

A drop of sweat rolled down Merlin’s forehead. *What is Alice muttering to herself in there?*

Just as he was puzzling over this, Alice seemed to finish treating the wound on her back and started bending over to take off her skirt. A hint of white underwear was faintly visible.

Merlin’s eyebrows immediately knitted together, feeling like he was about to lose his mind.

*I’m gonna fucking explode!*

*This shameless, profligate woman—*

*Disagrees with me and now she’s taking off her skirt?! Damn it! Who the hell wants to see your bare ass?!*

*Put your damn skirt back on, you—!*

title: Chapter 75 — Obsessed Woman
content:
Chapter 75 — Obsessed Woman

Volume 7 · Chapter 75

Merlin had a complicated expression, standing outside the window like a lecher, peeking at Alice undressing.

Alice, completely unsuspecting, never imagined someone would have the audacity to climb up to the third floor just to spy on her changing clothes.

In truth, Merlin didn’t even want to look at Alice. But ever since they started living together, he had seen too many of her alluring moments, and as a result, he had become completely desensitized.

The facts proved that even if your own wife was as beautiful as a celestial, there would come a day when you’d be utterly unimpressed.

Merlin hadn’t even hit a home run yet, and he already felt this way.

Alice’s purple dress was already half off, revealing her cartoon bear-printed panties. She was grinning as she noticed Merlin peeking at her.

Merlin, overwhelmed with shame, covered his darkened face, thinking, *Why is Alice such an idiot? Why does she have to wear such childish underwear that only little girls would find cute? Is she trying to be this stupid?*

Come on! She’s an adult! She should wear sexy underwear, not fawn over kawaii bears. Can’t she act a little more mature? It’s unbearable to look at!

Merlin silently thanked his luck that Alice wasn’t *actually* his wife—otherwise, he might have exploded on the spot.

He swore to himself that he would never marry a woman like Alice, or he’d never be able to turn his life around.

He couldn’t stand Alice anymore. Her childish underwear was an eyesore, an insult to his intelligence.

So Merlin raised his hand and knocked hard on the glass to alert Alice that he was back, telling her to stop undressing because he had no desire to see her naked.

*Bang bang bang!*

“Eh?!”

Startled by the knocking, Alice froze, terrified. She yanked her dress back up, turning her head in a panic—only to see his expressionless, stinking face.

Merlin’s gaze drifted downward, taking in Alice’s underwhelming chest. He couldn’t help but sneer, clicking his tongue in disdain. “Tch~”

Alice lightning-fast covered her chest, taking two steps back. Her face flushed red like boiling water, and she let out a high-pitched scream.

“*Aaaaaaaah!*”

Overwhelmed with shame, Alice snatched her high heel from the floor and hurled it at Merlin, determined to kill this pervert.

The heel shattered the glass, striking Merlin square on the forehead and knocking him off balance—he tumbled from the third floor.

After a while…

Merlin still climbed back up and entered Alice’s room.

“I finally came back, and you throw a shoe at me? You have no humanity…”

Merlin rubbed his forehead, his expression displeased.

“…Can you blame me?” Alice’s face burned red as she defended herself. “It’s your fault for peeping at me changing! Pervert! Shameless!”

At this moment, Merlin was still wearing his black robe, but his silver masquerade mask had been removed, revealing his true face.

Alice had hastily put her clothes back on, but she didn’t look very dignified. She seemed sluggish, as if in a post-intimate state, with several exposed glimpses of skin she hadn’t had time to cover. She had no choice but to let Merlin in first.

After all, she was his accomplice—she didn’t want anyone else to see him.

“Don’t jump to scolding me, okay? It was just a coincidence. I just got back and saw you undressing. I knocked on the glass to make you stop, wasn’t that the right thing to do?” Merlin said, his expression slightly serious.

“…Is that so?” Alice looked guilty, suspicious as she asked, “…You’re that decent?”

“Hmph!” Merlin coldly scoffed, his expression full of disdain. “I just didn’t want to see your naked body, so I stopped you. Your figure is unbearable to look at—it would make me lose all faith in women.”

“…What did you say?! Bastard! You peeked at me for so long, and now you have the nerve to insult me?! That’s outrageous!” Alice trembled with rage, feeling like she was the one at a disadvantage, yet this guy still looked at her with utter disdain.

Merlin broke out in a cold sweat, suddenly recalling a meme: *A dog that, after humping, barks at the person for being ugly.*

“Calm down. I don’t want to argue. By the way, how did you get injured?”

“That black elf, Sharplen, I don’t know what got into him, but his power became much stronger. He came here to kill you and me. As a result, both Keir and I got hurt…” Alice explained briefly, the wounds on her body aching faintly, though she refused to show it, not wanting Merlin to look down on her.

Merlin froze, recalling that Samuel had mentioned something before. Now he finally understood—it was a subordinate sent to kill him, but they had missed.

“I remember Samuel’s subordinates are Saint-tier, right? With such a huge gap in power, how did you and Keir survive?”

“We almost died, but the president of the Capital’s Adventurers Guild suddenly appeared and killed Sharplen in an instant.” Alice explained.

“The president of the Capital’s Adventurers Guild?” Merlin frowned, unfamiliar, but it seemed like Arnold had mentioned him before.

“Yes, his name is Cameron Gregory. He’s a very old Purple Gold adventurer. Not only is he incredibly powerful, but his background is also mysterious. Our guildmaster is just a junior in front of him.” Alice said seriously, still covering her chest.

Merlin was stunned, falling into deep thought. He recalled that, according to the distribution of adventurer ranks, Purple Gold seemed to be the highest level.

“Are Purple Gold adventurers very strong?”

“Do you even need to ask? Each and every one of them is powerful, with considerable adventuring experience. Pure strength alone isn’t enough—they’re the cream of the crop among adventurers.” Alice said solemnly.

“I see…” Merlin nodded, lost in thought, then abruptly changed the subject. “Well, as long as you’re okay…”

“Eh?!” Alice’s expression turned shocked. She never expected Merlin to say something so gentle. Could it be… he was concerned about her?

For a moment, Alice’s heart fluttered like a startled deer, and she unconsciously began to daydream.

Merlin paid no attention to Alice. In a few quick motions, he stripped completely naked, summoning holy light to punish the monstrous thing between his legs.

“*Aaaaaaaah!*”

Alice shrieked, hastily covering her eyes, terrified she might go blind. She had seen Merlin naked again!

What was going on? Did demons have no sense of shame at all?!

They loved stripping naked and running around! That was perverted!

Alice’s sense of shame exploded. Her voice cracked as she shouted, flustered, “You bastard! Hurry up and cover that filthy thing between your legs! Stop letting it swing around in the open, okay?! It’s indecent!”

“You’re overreacting. I’m just changing clothes…” Merlin sighed in exasperation, picking up his original clothes and starting to put them on.

“…But can’t you be more careful?! Don’t just strip naked in front of me all the time, okay?!” Alice was so tense her earlobes turned red, utterly embarrassed. They were a man and a woman alone together—what was with the stripping?!

“I can’t change clothes without taking them off, you idiot…” Merlin grumbled impatiently.

“…I’m a girl too…” Alice muttered, sneaking a peek at Merlin through her fingers. Her face turned even redder, and she quickly covered her eyes again, panicking as she thought—

*What am I doing?!*

*Don’t… don’t peek at him!*

*So what if he has a good build, lots of muscles, and a well-proportioned body?*

*What else is good about him? He’s not even a fraction as good as the great swordsman Elgin!*

*But… why is my heart pounding like this?*

*And it’s beating faster and faster…*

*If this keeps up… won’t I become the legendary ‘obsessed woman’?*

title: Chapter 76 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 76 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 7 · Chapter 76

Alice covered her eyes, daydreaming beside her.
She felt as if she were sitting on pins and needles, so nervous that her heart fluttered.
Alice was a bit confused, wondering when she and Merlin had become so casually honest with each other?
Merlin, dressed, looked at Alice and reminded, "Aren't you going to ask about Miss Snow Lily?"
"Yes—yes!" Alice snapped back, thinking it was all Merlin's mischief, that he almost forgot such an important matter. How was Miss Snow Lily? Why didn't you bring her back?
"The situation is somewhat special; we brought her back, and the situation might get worse." Merlin replied indifferently.
"What do you mean?" Alice said, seeing that Merlin had already put on his pants, so she was no longer so shy, and she set her hand down, putting away her shame.
"Lily suffered a mental injury, which we cannot handle. If we delay treatment, bigger problems may arise, so we can only hand it over to those thorn knights. We should not interfere further." Merlin said seriously.
"Can we rely on those thorn knights?" Alice said worriedly, some distrust in her voice.
"They have been searching for Miss Snow Lily, intending to send her back to the United Kingdom. This involves national relations, so it shouldn't be a problem." Merlin didn't finish his sentence.
Alice felt a little worried, wanting to see Miss Snow Lily, but she was now under the protection of the thorn knights, so it would be hard to see her.
Alice was somewhat concerned about Miss Snow Lily, thinking the girl was pitiful.
If possible, Alice wanted to personally send Miss Snow Lily back to her hometown.
Merlin glanced at Alice, casually saying, "Don't worry too much. Although those thorn knights aren't very powerful, they still have plenty of resources at their disposal."
Alice remained silent, not lying, thinking that given her situation, handing it over to the thorn knights was best.
"And this concerns our million-dollar reward. I don't want to see the meat in my mouth disappear." Merlin shrugged.
"Money isn't important; what's important is Miss Snow Lily's safety, right?" Alice replied dissatisfied.
"If there were no reward, I'd definitely be too lazy to care about Miss Snow Lily's life or death." Merlin answered without courtesy.
"...Can't you show some gentlemanly manners? Living with a beautiful girl like Miss Snow Lily, don't you have any thoughts?" Alice narrowed her eyes, unsure of the purpose of her question, probably testing.
"What thoughts could I have? Seeing a mother and then kneeling to lick? ...Merlin couldn't think of a good adjective, so he said, "You idiot."
Merlin, after all, was the Great Demon Lord, a proud monarch; seeing a woman and being unable to move would be too disdainful.
"........Alice averted her gaze, two small blushes on her face, feeling somewhat relieved."
Merlin looked at the red potion for treating injuries on the table, expressionless, and said, "How are your injuries?"
"...I'm fine, - Miss Cecilia will come to help me treat..." Alice answered softly, then mustered courage to ask, "Have you been... caring about me lately? Are you not up to some devilish plan?"
"Ridiculous, I'm afraid you'll drag me in, okay?" Merlin showed a somewhat disdainful expression.
".....Alice's face turned bright red, exhausted both mentally and physically by Merlin's rebuke."
"I have a way to get you better quickly, come on." Merlin, still not wearing his upper body, looked unkind; he patted the bed, implying, "Lie down obediently; as long as it's an injury, it should be fine."
"Uh, really... is it really okay?" Alice raised her eyebrows, looking at Merlin's sexually suggestive behavior, which seemed like a bad act! I wonder if you could put on your shirt, deliberately expose yourself to tempt me to fall?
"Your injury isn't light, is it? I can see it. Waiting for Miss Cecilia to treat isn't a solution; I can help you, and the effect will be better. Merlin spread his hands and said ="
"When did you start part-time nanny, ah no, part-time dad?" Alice asked nervously, feeling Merlin was unreliable.
"What part-time dad? I'm a male succubus, naturally gifted at healing the opposite sex, making them both physically and mentally in a state of pleasure and excitement." Merlin explained calmly.
....huh. !Succubus!
Alice was quite shocked, a bit hard to accept in a short time. Wenxing
Although she knew Merlin was a demon, she didn't expect him to be a succubus skilled at confusing hearts, and a very rare male succubus!
No wonder her heart always raced around Merlin; it must be due to his succubus nature, not because she had feelings for him.
She cursed Merlin as a pervert, not wrong at all; succubi are notorious for being lewd, always liking to seduce and confuse the opposite sex.
Alice felt she needed to be careful in the future, not to be inexplicably mentally controlled by Merlin.
"The treatment you mentioned won't... be a very erotic one, right?"
"Why do you think of erotica? Accusing me of hitting you, oh... Merlin replied expressionless, thinking humans are too biased against succubi."
"Don't you succubi like to do lewd things? They easily lead people into endless carnal desire." Alice expressed her view.
"Screw it, don't think twisted, okay? My treatment is very serious." Merlin said sincerely.
Alice hesitated, thinking her injuries were indeed worsening, and Miss Cecilia was urgent; why not try to believe Merlin once?
Moreover, Merlin had never done strange things to her before, so he could be considered respectful.
So Alice hesitated, then lay flat on the bed, hands guarded over her chest, always on guard against Merlin.
Now Alice's face was flushed, eyes panicked and wary, she was wearing a bit less, as if in a business rhythm.
"..-. like this?"
Merlin nodded, turned over and rode on Alice, pressing her down, showing an evil smile.
"Hmm?" Alice stared blankly, then felt the position was extremely dangerous, "Eh! ! ?"
"Don't shout, I'm about to start, cough... Merlin said seriously, brewing saliva."
"Shit... bastard! You pervert really have no good heart, right? Want to take the opportunity to do something lewd to me..."
"It's really just ordinary treatment," Merlin's expression became complicated. Long
"Stop lying! You clearly had a plan from the start; when the opportunity came, you finally couldn't resist extending your claws to me. I'm right, aren't I?"
Alice blushed, eyes watery, almost crying from fear.
"mmm.... Merlin was at a loss for words, too lazy to explain."
"I warn you not to act rashly! Don't think I'm easy to bully now that I'm injured; if you dare..."
"I just spit a few droplets of saliva and that's it." Merlin explained mildly.
"... spit saliva?"
Alice's expression was stunned, she thought a little, couldn't figure it out, feeling that Merlin was trying to infringe upon her in a disguised way.
So Alice became more afraid, her tears sparkling as she said.
"Only a demon would believe saliva can heal? You clearly want to do something lewd to me, and want to spit saliva to insult me, where? Into my mouth, right? ... Isn't that a disguised forced kiss? Get away, bastard!"
"You... really have your mind full of lewd tricks... Merlin sighed helplessly, continuing, 'Remember that time you were barely breathing under the Goblin King? I was...'
Alice recalled that morning when she woke up, her body sticky, it couldn't be...
??

title: Chapter 77 — Monthly Vote Bonus
content:
Chapter 77 — Monthly Vote Bonus

Volume 7 · Chapter 77

The scene fell into a honey-sweet awkwardness.

Alice reacted first, pushing Merlin's chest and said in a flustered manner, “Get up, get up!”

Merlin's face darkened, knowing he was misunderstood, he turned back to explain, “It's not like that, I'm helping Alice with treatment, don't misunderstand.”

“When I was little, seeing parents do that kind of thing they'd always use treating illness as an excuse, right? Adults are really cunning...” Cecilia's expression was terrible, her tone a bit strange.

“Uh!” Merlin was at a loss for words, feeling his explanation was indeed a bit pale and powerless.

“Miss Cecilia! It's not what you think!” Alice explained with a crimson little face.

“Don't mind me, Alice... Cecilia's gaze wandered, feeling she was very redundant here, still quickly leave, give this fiery couple some private space,” “Just... just pretend I never came, you continue what you didn't finish just now, be careful with the volume, the soundproofing here is a bit bad, don't disturb the others....”.

“Miss Cecilia!” Alice was almost crying with urgency, loudly calling out —

“Please don't leave me here!”<

At the same moment.

In the golden and magnificent palace.

A bedroom somewhere strictly protected by knights.

This is Queen Elizabeth's temporary sleeping quarters.

A row of maids were on standby here, waiting for orders.

Everyone looked solemn, as if they were doing something very important.

Three Thorn Knights were guarding the door —

Milierus, Morrison, and Winfred were all there.

Morrison's appearance was though ragged, but he was basically fine, after treatment by the court priest, he had almost fully recovered.

They were all on standby here, deeply worried about Shirley's safety.

Shirley as the elven little princess, if something happened to her in the Great Britain Empire, that would be a very serious problem, concerning everyone.

“Can Princess Shirley pull through?” Milierus couldn't help breaking the silence.

“Tsk!” Morrison clicked his tongue unhappily, frowning and said, “Don't talk as if the little princess is already on her deathbed, okay? Can't you think about the good side?”

“You're simple-minded and strong-limbed, but I'm not like you, be realistic, I just saw Princess Shirley's injuries aren't light, we should prepare for the worst.” Milierus said coldly.

“Milierus, why are you so pessimistic? We shouldn't give up hope until the last moment, right?” Morrison frowned tightly, his mood not good.

“Don't argue, keep quiet.” Winfred couldn't help stopping the two, saying seriously, “The little princess is still being rescued, if you want to fight, you'd better go outside.”

Morrison and Milierus looked at each other unhappily, snorted, and were too lazy to argue further.

“Although the elven little princess is seriously injured, we brought her here in time, from my experience, there shouldn't be any big problem.” Winfred said闷闷, the explanation was still objective.

At this time, Mesfield came out from inside, his face not looking good.

Morrison's face was anxious red, couldn't help asking bluntly, “How is it?”

“She's already out of life danger, estimated to wake up tomorrow, not...” Mesfield's eyebrows were tightly knitted.

“Not what?” Milierus asked curiously.

“The healer said Princess Shirley suffered mental trauma, after waking up she may have sequelae, forgetting some things.” Mesfield said seriously.

The three all fell silent, no one spoke, whether amnesia is serious or not completely depends on how precious the past memories are.

“Won't she know nothing after waking up?” Morrison's expression was grave, feeling the matter was troublesome.

“It’s not clear yet, but the healer means it needs observation, no conclusion can be drawn for now.” Mesfield hesitated.

... Morrison nodded, his face ugly.

Winfred fell into deep thought, saying in a self-blaming tone, “I didn't expect the elven princess to be in the capital, we went to great lengths to search everywhere, and the result was right under our noses, indeed for those villains, the most dangerous place is the safest place, we were really blinded.”

“Winfred, you don't need to blame yourself, Princess Shirley was betrayed by her own kind, we couldn't have imagined it, the contradiction in this matter mainly lies within their United Kingdom, it has little to do with us, as long as Princess Shirley is not in life danger, we have completed Her Majesty the Queen's mission.” Mesfield said seriously, telling Winfred not to be too nitpicky.

Winfred sighed, and didn't continue to delve into this issue.

“There’s definitely something fishy about this, Elgin the Great Swordsman is always elusive, this time he actually appeared in the capital? No matter how you think about it, it has something to do with this chaos, maybe:-.” Milierus stroked his chin, starting to promote conspiracy theories, “Elgin the Great Swordsman, is the mastermind behind it also possible”

“= behind the scenes black hand also maybe”

... Mesfield was suddenly stunned, really couldn't rule out this possibility.

“No! Milierus, don't alarmist here, I know you have opinions about Elgin the Great Swordsman, but the behavior of maliciously slandering is really shameless!”

Morrison said righteously, thinking to himself that he was on site, he couldn't see Elgin the Great Swordsman as the mastermind, on the contrary he came to rescue.

“This is not malicious slander, it's well-founded, do you know why he suddenly appeared in the capital?” Milierus said unhappily.

“Although I don't know very clearly, he seems to be here to save Princess Shirley, he can't be the real culprit.” Morrison argued.

“Rescue Princess Shirley? Could it be that Elgin the Great Swordsman knows Princess Shirley?” Mesfield seemed to have discovered some major information that could be followed up to catch this mysterious man.

“Should be familiar.” Morrison answered.

Mesfield showed a few points of surprise, if Shirley wants to come, ask him, you can know Elgin the Great Swordsman's real identity, at that time under the sunlight, this bastard who insulted himself will be nowhere to hide.

“This is really good news, maybe we can use Princess Shirley to find Elgin the Great Swordsman's true self.” Winfred's brain

“Right, make good use of this clue, we can remove Her Majesty the Queen's heartache!” Milierus' eyes flashed with excitement, expecting to say, “Haha, I'm already impatient to fight this bastard, to avenge last time's arrow!”

“I advise you to give up...” Morrison said seriously, not like joking.

“Hey hey, Morrison, you're becoming more and more like a traitor.” Milierus' face looked ugly.

“I'm not a traitor, I'm considering your life safety... Morrison paused, black lines covering his forehead, terrified to continue

“Elgin the Great Swordsman is very powerful, I've never seen someone with such strong strength.”

“According to my conservative estimate, even if we the Thorn Twelve Knights together...”

“Probably also difficult to resist...”

title: Chapter 78 — Exposure
content:
Chapter 78 — Exposure

Volume 7 · Chapter 78

Morrison wore an expression of utter seriousness; he was not joking at all.

At first, Morrison had been just like everyone else, believing that the great swordmaster Elgin was merely hyped up by too many people. His strength was hardly weak, but he surely wasn't anything extraordinary either—certainly not on a pathological level.

However, now, Morrison was visibly shifting into the role of a devoted fan, holding the great swordmaster Elgin in extremely high regard. He felt on the verge of joining Elgin's fan club, especially after having witnessed his combat with his own eyes.

If the great swordmaster Elgin's effortless秒杀 of Samuel, a battle with no suspense whatsoever, was already bordering on monstrous in its strength, then—

Following that, the laser attack from those large eyes carried such terrifying power that it was utterly gruesome—yet the great swordmaster Elgin had blocked it head-on with one hand?!

This was no longer mere monstrosity in strength. This was something transcendent, a power that leapt entirely beyond the bounds of comprehension!

Morrison now felt that everyone in the kingdom was courting death by opposing the great swordmaster Elgin.

Ideally, since the great swordmaster Elgin had yet to commit any unforgivable crimes, bringing him into the Bauhinia Knight Order would be the best solution.

As for the charge of destroying the Royal Navy, Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth could revoke it at any time.

The reason for issuing a joint warrant for the great swordmaster Elgin simply stemmed from Her Majesty's unease over an unknown powerhouse roaming freely within the homeland.

If he could mediate this situation, perhaps he could turn the great swordmaster Elgin into a combat asset for the empire and resolve Her Majesty's deepest concern.

Maysfield stared wide-eyed, unable to speak, thinking to himself: Is the great swordmaster Elgin really that powerful? For Morrison to say something like this.

"Are you speaking in earnest?" Winifred frowned, feeling that such words could not simply be ignored.

"Absolutely nonsense!" Millius was emotionally unbalanced, believing Morrison was elevating their enemy to the heavens. "All four of us Thorn Knights combined wouldn't even be his match? What kind of joke is that! I'm not even talking about Maysfield. Even when I'm serious, I have the ability to defeat—"

"It's impossible..." Morrison shook his head and said earnestly, "You haven't witnessed the great swordmaster Elgin's strength with your own eyes. If you had seen it as I have, you would never say such things."

"Morrison, you damn fool, why do you revere a wanted criminal like the great swordmaster Elgin so much? Don't forget your own identity!" Millius shouted angrily, very nearly wanting to throw hands with Morrison.

Morrison's face showed resolute determination. Rather than arguing with Millius, he chose silence.

Winifred remained relatively calm, since he also felt the great swordmaster Elgin's strength was formidable. The other three Thorn Knights would struggle greatly to defeat him, but for the entire squad combined to still fall short was somewhat too exaggerated.

"Morrison, is the great swordmaster Elgin truly already at that level of strength?"

"Yes. I am absolutely not exaggerating here. That kind of power is simply beyond anything we could hope to overcome." Morrison's expression seemed hollow, as if his soul had left his body. He felt an overwhelming sense of despair, and witnessing the great swordmaster Elgin's strength had directly made him question his entire existence.

Seeing Morrison's dispirited demeanor, Maysfield instantly felt a wave of irritation. To be struck so low by some lowly wanted criminal—it was truly embarrassing for Her Majesty.

Maysfield then furiously grabbed Morrison's collar, aggressively shoved him against the wall, and glared at him in wrath.

"Morrison, you are a Thorn Knight! We serve as the Queen's sword, the elite force of Britannia. Now one great swordmaster Elgin has you this dejected and defeatist. What sort of conduct is this!? Pull yourself together at once!"

"...Morrison suddenly froze, gazing at Maysfield's valiant face, momentarily speechless.

Winifred and Millius, seeing Maysfield's anger, instantly dared not speak recklessly, for the First Thorn Knight still commanded respect and authority.

"The opponent is only a wanted criminal. No matter how strong, he is still our enemy. Don't let yourself be so crushed that you lose all confidence! With me here, I can definitely defeat that bastard. Trust me!" Maysfield said firmly, believing that in a direct confrontation he should be able to triumph over the great swordmaster Elgin.

"That kind of power... is beyond an existence we can overcome. It is we who are unclear-headed and cannot perceive the gap in strength..."

Morrison pried Maysfield's hand off his collar, hesitated for a long while, and then spoke honestly.

"We should not oppose the great swordmaster Elgin, or the consequences will be catastrophic. Even Her Majesty the Queen has underestimated his strength. We ought to show goodwill toward him."

"--What did you say!?" Millius was stunned.

"Morrison, are you serious?" Winifred also thought he had misheard.

"Yes, I am serious. If given the opportunity, I will personally petition Her Majesty the Queen to revoke all measures targeting the great swordmaster Elgin and invite him to join the Thorn Knights, to become a new force of the empire." Morrison said with a very solemn expression.

Both Millius and Winifred were completely dumbfounded, thinking that for a Thorn Knight to say such things was outright treasonous.

Openly shielding a wanted criminal could easily result in execution by Her Majesty's orders. The situation was extremely grave.

Neither could comprehend what the great swordmaster Elgin had灌 brew into Morrison's head, to make him willing to go to such lengths to whitewash a wanted criminal.

Maysfield slowly snapped back from his shock and said with a serious expression, "Morrison, do you know what you're doing? As a Thorn Knight, you wish to defend a wanted criminal judged by Her Majesty the Queen? This goes against Her Majesty's will!"

"Whatever..." Morrison waved his hand and turned to leave, his red Bauhinia knight's robe fluttering behind him.

"I do this all for the future of the empire..."

"I believe Her Majesty will also understand my intentions."

The next morning, dawn.

A tinkling sound rang out from everywhere.

All the people of the capital city began their busy routines.

Reconstruction after the disaster had already begun, and the desolate scenes were swept clean.

As the center of the entire Britannia Empire, the capital's reconstruction would likely be completed within half a month, once again restoring its former prosperity.

In front of the Noble Hotel.

Merlin and the others had already boarded their carriage, planning to depart the capital that day and head toward the Strait of Dover.

They had already delayed in the capital for several days. If they didn't leave soon, they might not complete their mission in time.

After all, that Irish magical prodigy Johnson was no pushover either. He had likely already arrived at the Strait of Dover. If they didn't hurry, they wouldn't even catch a warm soup.

Kael still had bandages wrapped around his body, but under Cecilia's slave healing, he was essentially fine and would recover with a bit of rest.

Inside the carriage, Cecilia leaned against Kael's shoulder, drowsy, dark circles under her eyes—likely exhausted from treating people continuously.

Kael blushed and silently helped pull the wool blanket over Cecilia to keep her warm.

Yesterday, Alice still hadn't accepted Merlin's saliva treatment. Since it sounded unreliable and was somewhat disgusting, Cecilia had ended up helping instead.

Right now, Alice wore a white-and-blue long robe, gazing toward the royal palace with a melancholy expression. She was deeply worried about Shelly, wondering how that girl was doing now and hoping she hadn't encountered any坏人, making the journey home even more difficult.

Alice really wanted to see Shelly before departure. Though they had only just met, failing to properly bid farewell would be a regret.

However, since Shelly was currently in the main palace, it would be very difficult to arrange a meeting before they left, so she had to abandon that thought.

Merlin came to Alice's side and said softly, "There is no feast that never ends. Don't worry about Shelly. She is safe now and should be able to return to her homeland soon."

"...Alice blushed. Being seen through by Merlin made her uncomfortable. "I'm not worried about Shelly at all! I'm just watching the sunrise! Hmph!"

"Stop pretending. I know exactly what's going on in your head." Merlin sighed and said carelessly, "You'll meet her again when the time comes. Miss Shelly is a princess, thoroughly pampered and beloved by countless people. We're not the same. So stop worrying about that and focus on getting those million gold coins instead..."

"You... you say such horrible things! Have some humanity, will you? You're twisting our friendship completely..." Alice glared at Merlin, huffing in annoyance. "I curse you! May those million gold coins vanish completely, not a single coin left!"

"Huh? If I don't get them, you don't get them either. What's the difference?" Merlin waved his hand and turned toward the carriage. "Let's go, or I'll leave you here."

"W-wait..." Alice stomped her foot angrily and hurried after him. "Wait for me!"

Cecilia's private carriage slowly made its way through the streets.

Just as they were about to pass through the city gate leaving the capital, a massive shadow engulfed their carriage, startling everyone nearby into stepping back.

Above the carriage, a enormous black eagle hovered in the sky, its predatory aura radiating wildly. It spooked the horses, making them refuse to move forward and neighing incessantly.

The sudden occurrence caused a stir among the four inside the carriage.

"What happened!? What's going on!?" Cecilia woke from her sleep, a saliva mark at the corner of her mouth, her face a picture of complete confusion.

"S-someone's intercepting us?" Kael observed through the carriage window.

"Who's intercepting us?" Alice's eyes widened, her tone somewhat guilty. She and Merlin had done something wrong yesterday. Were they exposed already today?

"Don't panic. Let me see..." Merlin opened the carriage window and looked up at the sky.

He saw the black mountain eagle flapping its wings, stirring up a fierce gale!

Riding atop it was Maysfield, his expression grim, his gaze fixed on the carriage below. He amplified his voice with斗气 and shouted—

"Merlin Lusifur!"

"Alice Crody!"

"I now, in the name of the Thorn Knights—"

"Request that both of you accompany me!"

Alice quickly grabbed Merlin's arm, shooting him nervous sidelong glances.

[What do we do? Were our plan from yesterday discovered?! Didn't you say we never used the great swordmaster Elgin's identity to do anything bad!?! Why are they coming straight to us!?]

Watching Alice's panicked expression, Merlin sweated and thought—

Tch. No way...

Could my true identity...

Be exposed already?
