title: Chapter 79 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 79 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 7 · Chapter 79

A massive and luxurious ship was docked here.

A few white doves streaked across the sky, leaving behind fleeting white trails.

The fluttering flags made it clear at a glance that this was a vessel reserved for royal travel—it looked like a moving hotel.

Below.

Sherry stood in a deep purple silk gown, her feet in crystal high heels, standing gracefully before Alice and Merlin. Her pointed ears twitched now and then.

Her face was slightly flushed, and she stared at the couple before her with a hint of shyness, looking rather adorable.

Merlin and Alice had not been summoned by Mesfield because last night’s plan had failed or because Elkin the Great Swordsman’s identity had been exposed.

It was simply that Sherry wanted to see her human friends before leaving the Kingdom of Great Briton.

So she had asked Mesfield, and Mesfield, with no other choice, had made an exception to bring Alice and Merlin just in time before the ship to her homeland departed from the royal capital.

Merlin and Alice knew the Thorned First Knight wasn’t here to pick a fight, so they relaxed.

“Miss Alice, Mr. Merlin, I’m leaving for my homeland now,” Sherry said gently.

“Oh? So you’re finally going back?” Alice’s expression softened. She felt Sherry had been through so much—it was a relief she could finally board the ship home.

“Mhm, we’ll depart soon. It should take about half a month to reach the Southern United Kingdom.” Sherry nodded.

“That’s good. But who will protect you on the way? What if you run into bad people again?” Alice asked worriedly.

“It’s fine. The First Thorned Knight, Lady Mesfield, is escorting me personally. There won’t be any major problems.” Sherry gave Alice a reassuring smile.

Alice’s expression turned unnatural. She lowered her voice. “Then we…”

Merlin was still a little concerned. He probed cautiously, “Did the First Thorned Knight ask you any… strange questions?”

“Strange questions?” Sherry tilted her head in confusion.

Merlin narrowed his eyes, feigning nonchalance. “About Elkin the Great Swordsman.”

“Oh, right! That’s the famous one Alice mentioned.” Alice chimed in.

Sherry thought for a moment, then shook her head blankly. “Lady Mesfield did ask me privately this morning if I knew Elkin the Great Swordsman… but…”

“Huh?!” Alice froze. She recalled Sherry had always stayed indoors, completely out of touch with the outside world.

She probably hadn’t even heard of Elkin the Great Swordsman, the man currently on everyone’s lips. She was completely in the dark.

As it turned out, when Mesfield had questioned Sherry that morning, Sherry had just stared back in confusion, having no idea who Elkin the Great Swordsman was. She couldn’t provide any clues.

Seeing this, Mesfield had dropped the matter, assuming it was a side effect of psychological trauma. Even if Sherry had once encountered the mysterious Elkin the Great Swordsman, she had likely forgotten.

Mesfield was deeply disappointed. Such a crucial lead had just snapped. It seemed her revenge for being spat on would have to wait.

Sherry looked at Merlin and Alice curiously. “Did something happen?”

“No, not at all.” Alice forced a dry laugh, finally putting her suspended heart at ease.

“Yeah, we were just asking casually.” Merlin echoed, thinking to himself that, fortunately, his peaceful life wouldn’t be disrupted for now. It was still safe.

Sherry noticed their odd behavior but didn’t dwell on it. In her eyes, they were just being overly cautious—she even thought the Thorned Knights had coached them.

“Miss Alice, after I leave, you must take care of—”

“Shouldn’t *I* be the one saying that to *you*?” Alice replied awkwardly.

“It’s the same either way. Thank you both for taking care of me this whole time. I’ll treasure these memories. If you ever get the chance, come visit the United Kingdom. I’ll treat you well.” Sherry beamed like a child.

“We definitely will. Then we’ll have to trouble you, Your Highness Princess.” Alice didn’t hold back.

“Miss Alice, please keep calling me Sherry. ‘Your Highness Princess’ makes me uncomfortable.” Sherry embarrassedly shook her head, seemingly not wanting their friendship to be strained by status.

“…Alright, then I’ll keep calling you Sherry.” Alice didn’t refuse. She continued, “Speaking of which, when I found out you were a princess, I was really shocked. If I’d known earlier, I would’ve treated you better. Making you stay in such a small room… it must’ve been uncomfortable.”

“No, no, it wasn’t like that. The time I spent with you was happy.” Sherry hesitated, as if holding back more words.

“But…?” Alice asked curiously.

“It’s just… Miss Alice’s underwear was too small. Especially the chest part. When I wore it at night, I couldn’t sleep. It felt… a little hard to breathe.” Sherry’s forehead beaded with a drop of cold sweat.

Alice’s face darkened instantly. Her goodwill toward Sherry plummeted, and her body trembled with rage. She felt inexplicably mocked for her flat chest.

“Calm down. If we kill her, we won’t get paid.” Merlin pressed down on Alice’s shoulder and whispered.

“Before I leave… can I hug you both?” Sherry’s eyes sparkled with hope.

“Of course. Come here. Don’t hold back. Feel free to act spoiled with me…” Merlin silently opened his arms.

Alice’s mood soured instantly. A vein throbbed on her forehead. She shoved Merlin aside and hugged Sherry first.

Above their heads, two opposing status effects faintly appeared:

Alice’s buff: «Wife Status +1»

Merlin’s debuff: «Harem Member -1»

Merlin’s eyebrows knitted together as he sensed deep malice.

“Take care on the road. Don’t run around recklessly once you’re home.” Alice gently patted Sherry’s back.

“I know, Miss Alice. You take care too.” Sherry replied earnestly. “I hope you and Mr. Merlin have a happy marriage.”

Both of their expressions froze. The atmosphere instantly turned awkward.

“I… think I’ve been cursed again,” Merlin muttered quietly.

“You’re right. The malicious matchmaking forces are everywhere.” Alice said gravely.

Mesfield approached from a distance and stopped beside Sherry. “Your Highness Sherry, it’s time to depart.”

“Oh, alright.” Sherry waved goodbye to Merlin and Alice.

Mesfield glanced at Merlin and Alice, recalling the conflict at the Elven Embassy two days ago. She bowed slightly. “Thank you both for protecting Princess Sherry all this time. I sincerely apologize for the unpleasantness that occurred before.”

“It’s fine. We didn’t take it to heart.” Alice waved her hand dismissively.

“Yeah, it doesn’t matter. What matters is… one million, one million…” Merlin repeated, trying to subtly remind Sherry—*one million!*

Sherry looked innocent and confused. “Huh?”

“Ah, the reward. One million gold.” Merlin answered seriously.

“A… reward? Was there such a thing?” Sherry’s face fell. She couldn’t recall at all.

Mesfield looked at Sherry and apologized. “I’m sorry. Princess Sherry has suffered psychological trauma and has selective amnesia.”

Merlin’s face darkened. His hand instinctively reached for the katana at his waist.

Alice glanced at Merlin and muttered under her breath, “Calm down… just calm down a little…”

Merlin’s expression twisted dramatically, a mix of fury and sorrow flashing across his face. His emotions were a storm.

*Damn it!*

*Selective amnesia?!*

*She didn’t forget her dreams. She didn’t forget her mom.*

*But she forgot about the reward?!*

*After all my hard work, this is how it ends?!*

*Even the most heartless director would at least give me a bento with fried chicken!*

*Son of a—*

*I really want to unleash a twelve-hit combo straight onto the elf princess’s forehead!*

( o0_0o)

After Sherry returned to her homeland.

Merlin and Alice were on their way back to the carriage.

The scorching sun cast its light down as citizens bustled around, rebuilding their homes.

Alice was in high spirits, holding a large bouquet of fresh flowers still glistening with dew—clearly just picked.

These flowers were all gifts from the residents Alice had helped. Many hadn’t forgotten her kindness.

After the disaster, seeing the savior from the day before, they had nothing valuable to offer—so they gave wildflowers to express their gratitude.

Though the gifts weren’t much, Alice was clearly delighted, feeling truly cherished.

Worth mentioning was the little girl Alice had helped—she had been reunited with her mother.

The girl and her mother had come together to give flowers, calling Alice “Angel Sister!” Alice was so overjoyed she could barely contain herself.

This made Merlin roll his eyes beside her.

*Alice didn’t even do anything! I was the one who suffered! Shouldn’t they be kneeling and bowing to me in gratitude?!*

But Merlin wasn’t surprised. It wasn’t about having invincible power to gain recognition. Even small people doing what little they could were still beloved. He understood that.

Alice sensed the negative aura radiating from Merlin beside her and asked displeasedly, “What’s wrong? Jealous of me?”

“Tch! Who’s jealous of you?!” Merlin scoffed, lying through his teeth. “I’m just annoyed that after all that work, I didn’t even get a single copper coin.”

“Don’t dwell on it. Don’t we still have Lady Cecilia’s request?” Alice thought optimistically.

“Easy for you to say. One million gold! If I take it to the racetrack, with a bit of luck, I could dominate the whole place!” Merlin said stubbornly, seemingly determined to strike it rich at the races.

“Give up on the idea of getting rich quick through gambling. It’s better to be steady.” Alice silently schemed in her heart to tighten the purse strings on Merlin, or else their hard-earned savings would vanish.

“Sorry, but I don’t want to become someone like you—without dreams.” Merlin smirked mockingly.

“—Without dreams?! My dream is to marry Elkin the Great Swordsman!” Alice blurted out, face red.

Alice had said it without hesitation. Since Merlin already knew, she didn’t feel too ashamed.

Merlin’s forehead beaded with cold sweat. He was too exhausted to retort. “Now you can say it so shamelessly, without any restraint…”

“I don’t want to hear it from *you*! What’s your rush to earn money for, anyway?” Alice deflected.

“I just want to get away from you as soon as possible.” Merlin didn’t mince words.

Alice’s face darkened. A strange tension gripped her heart. “You… you want to leave me that badly?”

“Isn’t that what *you* want?” Merlin narrowed his eyes.

“I—I do! Of course I do! I wish you’d disappear right now! Stop loitering in front of me all the time! I don’t need you! Humph!” Alice puffed out her cheeks and huffed.

“I feel the same. So hurry up and earn money. Sherry was a golden opportunity…” Merlin patted his own thigh meaningfully.

“Even if we didn’t get money, we still gained friendship! Being friends with a princess sounds amazing!” Alice’s expression lit up slightly.

“Friendship doesn’t put food on the table. In the end, I’m the biggest loser. I got nothing, while you have a whole pile of flowers…” Merlin grumbled sourly.

“Uwah, so you *are* jealous of me! Like a child!” Alice couldn’t help but tease. After a moment’s thought, she added, “But… thank you for saving Sherry.”

“Hm?” Merlin looked at Alice, who was holding the bouquet.

Alice cleared her throat twice, her face flushing. “I-I think… when you pretended to be Elkin the Great Swordsman… it was… kind of… cool…”

“What the hell are you talking about?!” Merlin’s whole body broke out in goosebumps.

“Don’t ask!” Alice’s face burned as she stammered incoherently. She pulled a single flower from the bouquet and thrust it at Merlin. “This is your reward. I’m feeling *very* generous, so I’ll give you one. Just one! Take it with gratitude!”

“Eh?” Merlin stared blankly, feeling pitied by Alice.

Alice forced the wildflower into Merlin’s hand, then quickly stepped back as if to flee. “Let’s go! There are new adventures ahead!”

“…” Merlin’s expression was complex as he looked at the wilted wildflower Alice had shoved into his hand. It looked a little pathetic.

*Is this her way of caring about me?*

*She really is a meddlesome person…*

(ﾟ∀ﾟ)

■ToBeContinued

title: Chapter 1 — Calm
content:
Chapter 1 — Calm

Volume 8 · Chapter 1

A winding path stretched ahead.

A luxurious carriage was on its way to the Strait of Dover.

To reach the final destination, they first had to arrive at a fishing village along the Kent coast.

From there, they would take a boat to a small island at the center of the strait.

Although Merlin hadn’t received Sherry’s million-gold reward, Cecilia’s offer was acceptable—it met the standards of an S-rank mission.

200,000 gold coins would be enough to cover his periodic debts and live comfortably for a while.

So Cecilia’s commission was crucial for Merlin and Alice. They had to find a way to complete it, even if it meant using underhanded tactics like snatching the last hit.

Merlin didn’t want to go on this long trip only to end up with nothing. Paying rent would become a headache if that happened.

He could dump the mess on Alice, but she had been keeping a close eye on him lately, as if afraid he might run away.

Clearly, she didn’t trust him—after all, he was a demon. Getting a Hero like Alice to fully trust him was no easy feat.

Alice feared that if disaster struck, Merlin, that heartless demon, would abandon her and flee back to the demon race.

Then she’d be doomed, crushed under a mountain of debt.

After days of travel, they were almost at the coastal fishing village.

Looking back, they could see the vast, endless sea where the sky and water merged.

Merlin gazed out the carriage window, sensing something was off. Their group had wasted a few days in the royal capital. Who knew if that genius mage, Johnson, had already arrived here and solved everything?

That would be the worst-case scenario—the mission would fail, and they wouldn’t even get a single sip of soup.

Still, Merlin and his group had to come check. If they could snatch the last hit, it would be a guaranteed profit.

Alice sat beside Merlin, frowning in worry. She was anxious they wouldn’t make any money—life was already on the brink.

Kyle’s injuries had mostly healed, though his hand still had a minor wound, wrapped in a white bandage. He sat upright, proper and composed.

Cecilia felt the atmosphere was a bit oppressive and couldn’t help but break the silence.

“We’re almost there.” Cecilia glanced out the window.

“Yeah, we should reach the fishing village in a few hours.” Kyle nodded beside her.

“Is the ship ready?” Cecilia asked seriously.

“Don’t worry, Lady Cecilia. I arranged everything while we were in London. By the time we reach the village, our Rose family’s warship should be waiting there.” Kyle said humbly, as if, aside from being a bodyguard, he also had to double as a secretary.

“Good. Well done, Kyle. Truly my loyal hound.” Cecilia patted Kyle’s shoulder, though since she was shorter, it looked a bit awkward.

“Thank you for the praise, Lady Cecilia~” Kyle pressed a hand to his chest, his face flushed with embarrassment—he really was like a dog!

Alice, sitting beside them, was speechless. *Loyal hound*? That didn’t sound like a compliment. Why was Kyle so excited?

“Lord Merlin, we’ll be arriving at our destination soon. How are your preparations coming along?” Cecilia asked, as if making final checks to rally everyone.

As the strongest force in this mission, Merlin was naturally crucial, so Cecilia was particularly concerned about him.

“Huh?” Merlin snapped out of his daze, glanced at Cecilia, then silently turned back to the scenery outside. “Isn’t it just about chopping down some guy named Nengxing? Why do I have to be serious about this?”

Alice’s expression turned complicated. She was worried—Merlin’s work attitude was too lackadaisical. They were in a desperate situation now. If they didn’t earn money, they might drown in debt. Was his nonchalance just an act?

“As expected of the ever-prepared Lord Merlin. You must have everything ready, right? Truly remarkable. I should learn from you—you’re actually the most serious person here.” Kyle looked at Merlin with admiration, even mentally taking notes, wondering where the gap between himself and the strong lay. “Lord Merlin doesn’t need any preparation at all.”

“Shut up, Kyle. You underestimate Lord Merlin too much.” Cecilia scolded, then continued, “To be Lord Merlin’s opponent, you need no preparation. He is always in his strongest state. I think a guy like Democritus wouldn’t even be able to provoke Lord Merlin’s fighting spirit.”

“Uh, so that’s how it is.” Kyle suddenly realized, then groaned in frustration. “I actually underestimated Lord Merlin again. How rude of me.” An ordinary shut-in was being twisted into something else by these two.

Merlin stayed silent, sweating internally. *Shut up, you idiots. If real shut-ins heard this, their faces would be red with embarrassment!*

Alice, seeing these two blindly worship Merlin, felt a pang of jealousy. She couldn’t help but retort, “Stop guessing wildly. Merlin’s just lazy, that’s all.”

Cecilia huffed, “Shut up. Even if you’re Lord Merlin’s wife, I won’t let you slander my idol!”

“That’s right, Miss Alice. Lord Merlin is just too strong, so he can’t be bothered with trivial matters. The label of ‘lazy’ doesn’t suit him at all.” Kyle said earnestly, feeling Merlin’s mindset had transcended worldly concerns.

“Exactly. Miss Alice, as Lord Merlin’s wife, how can you not understand your own husband? Tsk, you’ll never amount to anything in this lifetime.” Cecilia glanced at Alice’s fake chest and muttered, “If it weren’t for rare resources, I’d—”

“What did you say?!” Alice’s face flushed red with anger, grinding her teeth. *These fanboys and fangirls are so annoying! Can’t they be reasonable?*

She shot a sideways glance at Merlin, expecting him to refute it, but he just kept his usual expressionless, deadpan face. *Doesn’t this guy care at all?*

Actually, Merlin knew it was hard to explain, and he couldn’t be bothered. He understood it wasn’t a real marriage, but he just sighed and said, “Stop talking nonsense. I just don’t find the opponent challenging, so I can’t take it seriously.”

“Just as I thought. Truly the mighty Lord Merlin.” Kyle nodded as if he’d seen through everything.

“See? Hmph~” Cecilia smirked at Alice, feeling she understood Merlin better.

Alice glared at Merlin, feeling ignored. *Does this guy even have a serious enemy? Maybe one will appear someday.*

Merlin said indifferently, “But the situation is a bit grim. That 14-year-old genius mage might already be here.”

Alice and Cecilia’s faces showed a hint of worry. It seemed they were also concerned the disturbance might already be over.

“We’ve been traveling day and night. We can’t be that late, right? And Ireland is much farther away than we are. Johnson can’t have arrived this quickly.” Kyle still held onto a sliver of hope.

“I’ve been staring outside since earlier.” Merlin pointed outside, his tone serious. “As a chaotic zone—”

“Don’t you think it’s *too* peaceful here?”

(~_~)=3

title: Chapter 2 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 2 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 2

The mention of this by Merlin made everyone feel something was off.

It was supposed to be a chaotic area, yet it was unnaturally calm, as if nothing had happened at all.

This seemed abnormal, and people couldn't help but wonder what had occurred here.

"That's true, this road is too quiet," said Kyle, frowning.

"Yet the fishermen here have lost their means of livelihood, and there isn't even a single refugee on this road. That's strange."

Merlin touched his face, thinking of several possibilities.

"Do you know what happened?" Alice asked, bumping her arm against Merlin.

"Perhaps that genius magician from Ireland has already resolved everything, and the fishing village has returned to peace. Or perhaps we and the magician from Ireland have arrived too late, and the fishing village has already been wiped out by some alchemical beast," Merlin said casually.

Alice's eyebrows were tightly knit; she felt neither outcome was good, and both were unfavorable to their side.

Nowadays, Alice was under pressure from life and desperately wanted to earn money, so she least wanted the commission to fail.

"Merlin-sama's reasoning is very sound, and the situation is quite severe," said Cecilia, nodding seriously. "It seems we need to speed up our pace. Once we arrive at the fishing village, I will arrange for us to land the island as quickly as possible, and won't waste any time."

Merlin gazed at the bright sky outside, speaking carelessly:

"Rather than considering all this, it's more reliable to pray that that 14-year-old brat gets lost."

At the fishing village at this moment.

The situation was completely different from Merlin's guess.

Johnson hadn't even arrived here yet.

The fishing village hadn't been slaughtered by alchemical beasts either.

And it was in an unexpected state.

Chaos!

The entire fishing village had been taken over by Democles, turned into a breeding ground that provided experimental materials at any time.

But Democles's underlings were not alchemical beasts, but genuine humans from the fishing village itself.

Originally people from the same roots, the villagers were now divided into two camps: the scoundrels serving Democles, and the helpless villagers who had become meat on the chopping block.

All of these changes must be traced back to the beginning.

In order to resist Democles's wanton behavior and drive him away from the island in the sea area.

So the fishing village organized a team of over 100 people to attack, mostly fishermen, intending to land on the island at night and catch Democles off guard.

But things went wrong. Democles was very shrewd and had prepared in advance, letting his alchemical beasts hide in the sea, and the team of over 100 people all perished in the sea.

However, one person survived and was captured by Democles, becoming a prisoner.

That person was the golden-haired warrior who led the fishermen to attack Democles, the very man who had just returned to the village with great pride, named Mark.

At first, this golden-haired warrior Mark thought he was doomed to die and be buried at sea, but when he woke up, he found himself locked in a cage by Democles.

Mark suffered all kinds of inhumane torture and human experiments. If he weren't a mid-tier warrior, he would have died long ago.

In the dark basement, repeatedly injected with strange serums, endless pain made Mark feel despair, deeply regretting having provoked Democles, the alchemist.

But on a certain day, Democles offered Mark a chance to barely gain freedom, at the cost of betraying his fellow villagers.

Democles was an alchemist, naturally needing various experiments. Rats as test subjects were too low-grade; he didn't want to use them, preferring to use real humans for his experiments.

So, using freedom as a condition, Mark was ordered to transport 10 humans to the island in the sea area regularly, providing them as experimental test subjects for Democles.

He would also help Mark improve his strength for free, and after delivering 10 humans, Democles would grant Mark his freedom.

Of course, Democles wasn't foolish; to prevent Mark from disobeying, he forcibly injected him with poison. If it activated, Mark's body would rot and die.

Each time Mark delivered villagers to the island, he would receive part of the antidote. He had to obediently complete the tasks assigned by Democles to achieve complete freedom.

Mark, who had suffered endless despair and torment, agreed without hesitation, deciding to preserve his own life by delivering the villagers to Democles as experimental test subjects.

Democles refined Mark's body with alchemical potions, giving him an invulnerable physique, and his strength also rose to the high tier.

Mark, who had willingly become Democles's lackey, returned to the fishing village and used violence to suppress the villagers, quickly taking control of the entire village, becoming a true tyrant.

Mark was now a high-tier warrior; these villagers couldn't defeat him, so they could only endure the abuse in silence.

Mark sent villagers to the island in the center of the sea area in batches, making them into test subjects who were sent to their deaths, exchanging for the meager antidote to prolong his life.

He also recruited some strong villagers to be his henchmen, working together to serve Democles and oppress the villagers.

The entire fishing village instantly turned into a slaughterhouse.

No one could escape the village, as if imprisoned in a cage.

The villagers desperately awaited death, with many already sent to Democles's laboratory, living on the brink of death.

Even the village chief had been among the first to be taken away, probably already dead at Democles's hands.

At this moment, inside the tavern in the fishing village.

Mark, accompanied by his underlings, was running amok, and drinking and eating for free wasn't enough; he wanted to find other forms of entertainment.

Now Mark was fearless, he was the strongest man in the village, like a king who was invincible, no one could do anything to him.

Whoever didn't like it, he killed; whoever he fancied, he took.

Seeing a pretty girl, he would pounce on her like a beast; seeing a fine-looking man, he would insert needles.

If anyone dared to resist him, they would be burned to death on the spot.

Mark had transformed from a young man returning home in glory to a wanton, lecherous brute, doing every evil deed, more demonic than demons.

"Bang!"

The elderly tavern owner was forcefully pushed onto the table, as if he had provoked them.

The two strong thugs beside him wore evil grins, clearly having ill intentions.

Mark's face was covered with some green scales, making him look inhuman and ghost-like, as if suffering from a skin disease.

This was the price of gaining power; refined by Democles's alchemical potions, Mark had already become half an alchemical beast.

"What are you doing here? I'll give you money, the finest wine is also free for you to drink, what more do you want from this old man?" The elderly tavern owner's eyes were filled with fear, his voice trembling.

"We don't need these things, we want to have fun, to release the energy that's about to explode. Do you understand?" Mark's face was ferocious, squeezing the elderly tavern owner's neck tighter.

"Fun? Cough, cough!" The elderly tavern owner was a bit short of breath, his old bones nearly falling apart.

"Yes, where is your granddaughter? I remember she's quite pretty," Mark's eyes revealed undisguised greed, his long tongue licking his lips as he spoke.

"Come out and serve us, let us have a good time."

"Otherwise, I'll burn down your tavern, then kill your entire family, hehehe."

title: Chapter 3 — Monthly Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 3 — Monthly Bonus Update

Volume 8 · Chapter 3

Mark felt like a king after taking control of the fishing village—he could do whatever he pleased without any obstacles, and the thrill of absolute power was intoxicating.

Anyone who dared to stand in his way was either dead or reduced to a lab rat, sent to Democritus’s experiments.

His greed, now fully awakened, could no longer be satisfied by ordinary things.

When he heard the tavern owner’s granddaughter was quite the beauty, Mark’s lust was immediately piqued—he wanted a taste.

The two burly thugs beside him grinned lecherously, their faces twisted with vulgar amusement.

The elderly tavern owner’s eyes widened in shock as he stared at Mark, realizing these bullies hadn’t come for treasure but for his granddaughter. No wonder they hadn’t been satisfied with all the fine things he’d handed over—they had other designs.

“Hey, old man, don’t play dumb with me. You think I won’t snap your neck?” Mark bared his sharp fangs, slamming the old man onto the table and tightening his grip around his throat.

*Cough, cough!* The tavern owner gasped for air, his body wracked with pain. No matter how hard he struggled, he couldn’t break free from Mark’s iron grip. His face turned ashen, like a corpse’s.

An ordinary man stood no chance against a high-tier warrior—the gap in strength was simply too vast.

“Hehehe~” Mark let out a string of creepy laughter, savoring the thrill of bullying these helpless people. “Speak up, old man. Tell us where you’ve hidden your granddaughter, and we’ll spare you. Otherwise…” His voice turned sinister. “You’ll wish you were dead by the time we’re done with you.”

The tavern owner, weak from struggling, still managed to glare defiantly. “You bastards… You dare set your sights on my granddaughter? I’d rather die than hand her over to the likes of you!”

“Oh?” Mark smirked, his grotesque face twisting into something even more horrifying. “You’ve got spirit, old man. But people like you usually die young.”

“Yeah, you’re just a withered old bag of bones. Why not retire in peace? We won’t *kill* your granddaughter—we’ll just have some fun with her,” one of the thugs chimed in, his voice dripping with mock concern.

“That’s right, just a little fun. We won’t do anything *too* extreme,” the other added with a smirk. “Whether your granddaughter ends up broken or not… well, that’s just her luck, isn’t it?”

The two thugs nodded along, playing the good cop and bad cop to squeeze the old man for answers.

“You’re dreaming!” The tavern owner roared, his voice trembling with rage. “I’ve lived long enough. Do what you want with me—cut me, kill me, I don’t care. But you’ll never lay a finger on my granddaughter!”

“Hahaha!” Mark let out a string of light, mocking laughter, completely unashamed. “Hey, hey, old man, are you *sure* you want to defy me? Right now, I’m the guardian god of this village. Without me smoothing things over with Lord Democritus, this whole place would’ve been wiped out by alchemical beasts. Do you have *any* idea how *merciful* I’ve been to you people?”

“Exactly! The great and merciful Lord Mark is the savior of this village!” one of the thugs chimed in, showering Mark with flattery. “Without him, none of us would be alive today. So isn’t it only natural for you to show your gratitude by handing over your granddaughter?”

“Did you hear that, old man?” Mark boasted, puffing out his chest. “I’m your benefactor. Without me, you’d all be dead by now!”

“If this is what it means to live under your ‘protection,’ then I’d rather die!” The tavern owner, though old, gritted his teeth with a dignity that commanded respect.

“Old bastard, courting death, are you?” Mark didn’t hesitate—he struck the old man across the face with a brutal backhand, then jabbed a finger into his chest. “What kind of mutt are you to talk back to me? It’s an *honor* for me to take your granddaughter! If it weren’t for Connie’s looks, I wouldn’t even bother with her!”

*Cough!* The tavern owner’s lips trickled with blood from the slap, his mind reeling. “I—I won’t let you have your way!”

“That’s not for you to decide.” Mark rubbed his palm, his smile not reaching his eyes. “Oh, and I almost forgot—your son, wasn’t he sent to Lord Democritus? Must be rough. By now, he’s probably just a pitiful lab rat, injected with all sorts of strange concoctions every day. The agony…” He shook his head. “I can’t even bear to think about it.”

The tavern owner’s face went pale at the mention of his son. His heart clenched—Mark didn’t sound like he was joking. His son might really be suffering right now.

“I’ll give you a choice,” Mark said, narrowing his eyes with cold malice. “Hand over your granddaughter to me, and after I’m done with her, I’ll spare your whole family. But if you resist…” His voice dropped to a whisper. “Not a single one of you will live.”

The old man’s eyes filled with despair. He was trapped—no matter what he did, someone would suffer. All he could do was roar in defiance, “You demon! Why are you doing this to us?!”

“Because Lord Democritus has given me a future,” Mark declared, as if it were the most natural thing in the world. “So it’s only right that you weaklings exist to amuse me, isn’t it?”

The two thugs burst into mocking laughter, delighted by the old man’s despair.

“How can you be so heartless?” the tavern owner spat, his voice shaking with rage. “Aren’t you from this village too? We finally have a warrior among us, and it turns out to be a monster like *you*!”

“So what if I am?” Mark spread his arms, his arrogance knowing no bounds. “I’m the emperor of this village now—the strongest being here! Because I’m invincible, I can do whatever I want! See something I like? I take it. See a pretty girl? I ride her. I’ll be the shameless, inhuman ‘New Century Sower’ if I want to! Morality? Doesn’t exist. If it feels good, I do it! HAHAHA!”

“You’re nothing but a hollow puppet with power!” the old man snarled, refusing to back down. “I’ll never let you ruin my granddaughter!”

“If the old bastard wants to die so badly, I’ll grant his wish!”

Mark raised his hand, high-tier battle energy surging as his fingers turned into blades. He was about to slice the old man’s head clean off.

But just as the situation reached its most critical moment—

“STOP IT!” a sharp, furious voice rang out. “You bastards, let go of my grandfather!”

Everyone turned to see a girl in a white dress crawling out from under a table. There was a hidden room—she must have been hiding there the whole time.

The girl was stunning, even in her apron. This had to be Connie, the tavern owner’s granddaughter.

Her face was a mask of fury and fear, her body trembling as she clutched her skirt, knuckles white. “You want me? Here I am! Now let my grandfather go!”

The tavern owner’s face twisted in horror. “Connie! Who told you to come out?! I told you to hide!”

“B-But…” Connie stammered, tears welling in her eyes. “I can’t just let them take you away from me…”

The old man’s heart shattered. Helpless, he screamed, “RUN, CONNIE! DON’T LOOK BACK—”

Before he could finish, the two thugs clamped their hands over his mouth, muffling his desperate cries.

Mark sauntered over to Connie, his eyes burning with unbridled lust as he looked her up and down. “Miss Connie… you came out on your own, huh? If you’d done this sooner, your grandfather wouldn’t have had to suffer so much.”

“Give me back my father!” Connie mustered her courage, her voice shaking as she glared at Mark’s scaly face. “And stop hurting my grandfather! He’s old and frail—”

The thugs ignored her completely, sneering as they forced the old man’s head up, making sure he had a clear view.

“Anything you want, I can make it happen, Miss Connie,” Mark said, lifting her chin with a clawed finger, his voice dripping with malice. “All you have to do is… serve us properly. If we’re satisfied, your whole family lives.”

Connie’s face flushed crimson—she knew exactly what he meant.

But Connie was fiery by nature. She had no intention of submitting.

With a sharp motion, she slapped his hand away and spat directly into his face. “Pfft! Ugly freak! Who would *ever* serve the likes of you?! Get out of our house!”

Mark’s expression went blank. He hadn’t expected resistance at a time like this.

He touched the spit on his face, and rage surged through him.

Sure, he was hideous now—covered in grotesque scales, neither man nor beast—but how *dare* some girl humiliate him like this?!

His pride shattered, Mark shoved Connie to the ground with brutal force, then mounted her, pinning her beneath him. “You little slut! You *dare* reject me?!” he hissed. “I’m the strongest man in this village—I deserve to be treated like a king!”

“No one gets to insult me and live! I’ll teach you your place right here, right now—make you *beg* for it!”

Like a madman, he tore at her clothes.

*Rip!* With one violent motion, Connie’s dress was shredded, exposing swaths of pale, flawless skin. Her ample chest threatened to spill out, her slender, graceful figure laid bare.

Mark’s excitement reached a fever pitch. His eyes were bloodshot, his mind consumed with the thought of violating the girl beneath him.

“STOP! Don’t do this! You monster! Get off me!” Connie flailed, pounding her fists against him, struggling with all her might—but against a high-tier warrior, her strength was meaningless.

“Shut up, you worthless bitch!” Mark snarled, slapping her across the face to stun her into submission.

The blow left Connie dazed, her vision swimming. She could no longer resist, leaving her at Mark’s mercy.

He hoisted her long legs onto his shoulders, flipped up her tattered skirt, and roughly tore away her undergarments, exposing her most intimate parts. Then, with a cruel grin, he undid his own belt, freeing his filthy weapon.

“Watch closely, old man,” Mark bellowed with sadistic glee. “Watch how I defile your precious granddaughter! HAHAHA!”

“Mmmph! Mmmph! MMMPH!” The tavern owner’s tears streamed down his face as he sobbed uncontrollably, overwhelmed by grief and helplessness. There was nothing he could do but watch as these monsters had their way.

The two thugs cackled, yanking the old man’s hair to force his head up, making sure he didn’t miss a single moment.

Just as all hope seemed lost, the tavern door creaked open.

Two figures stepped inside.

A golden-haired woman with a generous figure, and a silver-haired little guard.

“So there *are* still people here.”

“After all that searching, I didn’t think we’d find a single soul. I almost thought this place was completely abandoned.”

title: Chapter 4 — Trash
content:
Chapter 4 — Trash

Volume 8 · Chapter 4

After Merlin's group arrived at the fishing village, they found the place eerily deserted.

There was hardly a soul on the streets or alleys; it looked like a ghost town, as if every single villager had vanished overnight.

This made Merlin and his companions quite embarrassed — there was no one to ask for information.

So they split into two groups to search for the villagers in the fishing village, and that's how Merlin and Alice ended up finding this little tavern.

The two of them appearing out of nowhere directly shattered the current situation, making everyone afraid to make a move.

The entire fishing village was now under Mark's control, plunging into an unprecedented crisis, with no outsiders having come around for a long time.

Nobody expected that at such a time, strange guests would show up in such a remote little village.

The tavern's small wooden door creaked open, and light gradually streamed in from outside —

The elderly tavern owner was being viciously pinned to the ground by two burly thugs, Connie's clothes were torn to shreds, and she was currently being ridden by Mark below, becoming the center of everyone's attention.

Alice and Merlin weren't fools either; they could understand the scene at a glance. It was clearly a bunch of scoundrels breaking in to assault a good young woman.

"Oh my~ how fiery." Merlin casually glanced at Mark, who was about to force himself onto Connie. If he had arrived a moment later, the arrow already nocked would have been loosed.

"How disgusting!"

Alice saw Mark preparing to violate Connie, and the flames of anger in her heart surged up instantly, veins appearing on her forehead.

Her expression was one of disgust, ten times worse than if she had seen a cockroach. She deeply despised acts of rape.

After all, Alice was also a girl, and she naturally detested such evil behavior, understanding the fear and pain a girl would feel when violated.

If she hadn't been unsure of the situation at the moment, Alice might have already drawn her sword and severed Mark's head.

"What are you lot doing!? Let that old man and that girl go right now!"

"Mmph mmph!!!" The tavern owner, seeing someone had arrived, didn't care about anything and started shouting loudly, as if calling for help.

Connie, still dazed after being slapped, lay limply on the ground with no reaction whatsoever.

"Who do you think you are? Daring to meddle in our business? Get lost!" one of the thugs immediately cursed.

"Yeah, looks like you're outsiders. We won't make things difficult for you, so just disappear from our sight! Or else we won't be polite!" the other thug snarled in agreement.

"Doing something worse than beasts and yet daring to be so arrogant — absolutely outrageous!" Alice's sense of justice blazed furiously, and her hand immediately went to the hilt of her slender sword at her waist.

"Calm down, calm down. I know we suddenly interrupted your fun, and anyone would be annoyed in a normal situation," Merlin said expressionlessly, nonchalantly. "But forcing yourself on a woman isn't cool, right? There's zero chivalry in that, and also, if you livestream making babies, it'll get censored, my friend."

"Exactly, you bunch of bastards. Your ideological awareness is somehow lower than a demon's — pathetic!" Alice angrily chimed in.

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue in dissatisfaction, wondering if Alice's flat chest was somehow dragging him down.

"I think you lot don't want to live!" One of the thugs stood up, rolled up his sleeves and was ready to fight. He seemed completely unafraid of Merlin and Alice, his attitude ridiculously arrogant.

Mark, still riding Connie, hadn't said a word. Instead, he was seriously studying Merlin and Alice.

Because the entire fishing village had been sealed off long ago, so the sudden appearance of two travelers was very suspicious.

Moreover, Mark was worried that a powerful person might arrive and threaten his rule.

But as for these two in front of him, Mark couldn't help but ponder inwardly —

The blonde gay-looking guy in tight clothes looked extremely ordinary, radiating absolutely no aura of strength.

The black iron adventurer certificate around his neck was sufficient proof of his strength and status — he was utterly insignificant trash.

As for the silver-haired girl next to him, holy crap, a beautiful girl rarely came to the fishing village!

That outfit was kind of sexy, her face was both cute and pretty, her temper was fiery, totally my type!

Her figure was damn sexy — those legs, that butt, those big (fake) boobs!

I'm gonna lick it all up, prprprprpr (drooling)

Compared to that, Connie beneath him wasn't that great anymore; the interest instantly faded.

Since the silver-haired beauty was with trash, her strength probably wasn't great either.

So the guy could be handed over to Democritus for experiments, and the girl would be taken care of in minutes for his own amusement. That settled it~

Mark looked at Alice, licked his lips, and his wicked intentions became unmistakably clear.

Fantasizing about someone else's wife right to their face meant he didn't have Merlin in his eyes at all. Mark completely failed to realize he was ignoring the most formidable person present.

Alice was currently wearing a white robe, and her golden adventurer certificate was hidden inside the robe, so Mark never saw it.

If Mark had known Alice was a gold-class adventurer, he probably wouldn't have been so careless.

"Disgusting." Alice's face darkened, feeling a chill run down her spine. She thought Mark was too ugly — he had scales growing on his face. Was he even human?

"You two, cut the nonsense. Forget about that old man for now. Go kill that blonde guy, and leave the girl. After I'm done with her, I'll give you a turn too~" Mark said in an commanding tone, thinking two people could easily handle a black iron adventurer. After all, the combat power of most black iron-level adventurers was barely a step above ordinary people.

"Alright~"

The two thugs kicked the tavern owner aside and eagerly approached Merlin, full of fighting spirit.

They swung their fists and charged at Merlin recklessly, completely unaware of what kind of monster they were facing.

"Sending two villagers to handle me? I'm really being looked down upon, am I?" Merlin smiled crookedly, watching the two approaching villagers, too lazy to even move.

Two dull thuds echoed, and the two burly thugs went flying backward like cannonballs.

They zoomed past Mark's ears and crashed violently into the liquor cabinet, shattering countless bottles and jars.

Mark turned around in shock, seeing his two thugs already lying on their backs with their eyes rolled up, foaming at the mouth, unconscious!

What kind of move was that!?

So fast! He couldn't even see the shadow of a punch!

This black iron adventurer was off — he definitely had real combat strength!

Mark slowly turned his head back and carefully studied Merlin, not daring to be dismissive anymore, his expression turning grave.

"Enough already." Merlin rubbed his shoulder, expressionless. "Why do people always like sending a group of small fries to deal with me? Clearly the small fry here is the one next to me."

"Hey!!" Alice's face turned red with anger, thinking Merlin was so annoying. Maybe he should change his name to Someone-Who-Needs-to-Make-Insults-Every-Day斯基!

"I'm a proper big boss, yet I spend all day picking up trash," Merlin sighed, frowning, and glanced contemptuously at Mark. "By the way, can you get off that girl first?"

"Even if you're mating, there's no need to rush, right?"

"You've been riding her since before and won't get off. It's making me inexplicably uncomfortable, hey."

(-"一)

title: Chapter 5 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 5 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 8 · Chapter 5

The elderly tavern owner, seeing this scene, immediately looked as if they had seen hope.

Feeling that it hasn't cooled down yet, perhaps there is still a chance to save it.

Although Merlin is a Black Iron adventurer, the scene just now seemed not very weak, right?

The tavern owner knew the fishing village had hired a Silver adventurer, but that Irish genius magician had not arrived here for a long time.

Instead, the unknown Black Iron adventurer arrived at the fishing village first. The gap between Black Iron and Silver is huge; this is simply not the same level of person!

Although the tavern owner didn't know what Merlin and Alice were here for, right now he could only hope they could alleviate the immediate crisis.

Even Connie, who was collapsed on the ground, seemed to see a savior, blushing and desperately covering her exposed delicate body.

Facing the pressure, Mark had to stand up, pull up his pants, and said viciously.

"So you aren't an ordinary Black Iron adventurer, I really underestimated you just now."

"You only just realized that?" Merlin said with a blank expression.

"Being able to force this great me to take action counts as you having some strength." Mark's scales began to slowly shine with a luster, and strands of cold air came out. "But everything is over. Once we start fighting, you will have no way to fight back! You'll just scream in pain!"

"Oh~" Merlin raised an eyebrow and asked curiously, "By the way, I wanted to ask just now, what's going on with the scales on your body? They look very strange."

"This is a gift from Lord Democritus!" Mark spread his arms, high-tier fighting energy rose up, as if filled with power. "The alchemical strengthening potion made from dragon blood can make me mutate, doubling my strength. Fighting is like being a monster, with endless power!"

"Dragon blood?" Alice frowned her beautiful brows, thinking that dragon blood isn't uncommon, but the quality varies greatly. Looking at Mark's posture, the dragon blood used seems to be very high quality.

"Now you know fear, right? It's not too late to kneel and beg for mercy!" Mark clenched his fists, full of provocation.

"No need. I want to ask you what you're thinking? Doesn't it feel like a loss to become so ugly? Being strong is a matter of a strong dose of medicine, but being handsome is a matter of a lifetime." Merlin said with a meaningful tone.

"Shut up, being handsome isn't important. With strength, you can force yourself on women. Who are you to tell me?" Mark said very unhappily.

Merlin nodded and clapped lightly, looking at Alice and said in a low voice, "Awesome, awesome. This guy is also a talent. I think he can be taken to breed with a sow."

Alice's facial muscles twitched, she didn't want to respond, feeling it was too obscene.

"Dare to insult me! You're seeking death!"

Mark's figure moved, and he launched a fierce attack, shattering the tavern's floor.

The cold air on his body circulated, forming a storm-like momentum, and it was a killing move right from the start!

Merlin was just about to make a move when Alice blocked him in front, making people puzzled, "What are you doing?"

"Leave him to me. I've wanted to slaughter him for a long time." Alice's face was gloomy, and killing intent was written all over her face.

Merlin didn't speak, a drop of cold sweat flowed down his forehead, awkwardly thinking, sometimes when women get angry, it's quite scary.

"Hahaha, little bitch actually came knocking on my door herself. I want to see what you're capable of? Don't just know how to talk, if I pin you to the ground and rub you hard later, don't cry~" Mark had a lewd smile on his face, spouting nonsense.

"I'll make you shut up forever right now!" Alice took off her white robe to facilitate combat, and drew her thin sword; the Gold Adventurer's badge on her neck was swinging brightly.

"Gold Adventurer!?" Mark froze for a moment, then his expression became serious. "I see, you are the strongest one. But it doesn't matter, even if you have the same strength as me, you can't defeat me! Because I am invulnerable to swords and spears!"

Alice didn't speak, but instead sprayed out surging cold air, quickly condensing a layer of fused ice crystals on the surface of the thin sword to meet him head-on!

Mark waved his fist, and suddenly a sky full of fist shadows attacked, ruthlessly bombarding Alice.

Alice's figure suddenly changed, easily dodging countless fist winds, and a backhand sword technique poured out!

The two exchanged blows in a flash, their figures quickly crossed paths, and the battle ended in an instant.

Alice indifferently sheathed her thin sword, not even turning her head.

"My proud scales, actually..."

Mark's strong body crashed to the ground and died, not even finishing his sentence.

His body was riddled with stabs from the thin sword, hardening into a human beehive, bleeding endlessly.

Originally, Mark thought the scales on his body were invulnerable to swords and spears, and fighting Alice head-on would not put him at a disadvantage.

He didn't know that Alice was already a relatively strong existence among high-tier adventurers, and it was simply not easy to defeat her.

Plus the blessing of the fusion crystal of magic power and fighting energy, the destructive power is not ordinary.

Mark's proud scales became tofu directly under Alice's sword, pierced in an instant.

Merlin slightly frowned, thinking this girl Alice seemed to have become much stronger? With this, she has hope for Saint-tier.

The elderly tavern owner widened his eyes, not expecting there to be a Gold Adventurer here. Looking at the sharp sword technique just now, her strength is very strong!

He thought, after all this, that Black Iron adventurer wasn't the main combat power?

Although the adventurer badge written husband and wife, this Black Iron adventurer is completely a moocher.

The tavern owner didn't think much, feeling that being saved was a good thing. In his eyes, the Gold Adventurer was already very powerful.

However, deep worry followed, because the tavern owner knew that besides the bully Mark, there was an even more terrifying power in the village, making all villagers dare not act rashly.

"Are you okay?" Alice covered the exposed Connie with the white robe she had taken off, asking with concern.

"I'm fine." Connie said in a low voice, her face turning red, feeling that Alice, this heroic girl, was very handsome.

Alice felt slightly relieved, thinking that she and Merlin came in time, otherwise an irreversible tragedy would have happened.

Connie, the elderly tavern owner hurriedly limped over, obviously also injured. He came to his granddaughter's side and said earnestly, "Why are you so disobedient, child? Didn't I tell you to hide? Why come out in such danger? Do you know that Grandpa was almost scared to death by you just now? Bully Mark kills without blinking. If anything happens to you, what use is my old life left for!"

"Aren't I worried about Grandpa you?" Connie said with teary eyes, with a crying voice, "Dad has already been taken away. If Grandpa has any accidents, I will have no relatives left."

The tavern owner was immediately speechless upon hearing this, and sighed deeply. "Forget it, luckily nothing happened. If this Adventurer Lord hadn't stepped in to help, we would be dead today. Why don't you thank him quickly?"

"Thank you, Adventurer Lord." Connie lowered her head slightly to express her gratitude.

"You're welcome." Alice waved her hand with a smile.

"Cough, cough, cough!" Merlin's expression was complicated, constantly emitting a negative magnetic field, brushing up his presence.

A drop of cold sweat slid off the tavern owner's forehead, and he said awkwardly, "And that one there, although he looks like he's not very useful, he is at least with this young lady. Let's give him a symbolic thanks too."

"Tsk!" Merlin's face turned black, his forehead veins jumping wildly, angrily thinking—

What do you mean I'm not useful? What a joke!

I, the great Demon Lord, actually have to live in Alice's shadow?

As long as this old man doesn't extort me, I really want him to taste the flavor of the intelligence-dumbing-down aura right now.

(_Flat)

title: Chapter 6 — Strong Blow
content:
Chapter 6 — Strong Blow

Volume 8 · Chapter 6

Connie hesitated, glancing at Merlin before bowing her head slightly. "Thank you, adventurer..."

"Don’t mention it." Merlin waved a hand dismissively, unimpressed by gratitude for what he saw as a trivial act.

With a creak, the tavern door swung open, and Kiel and Cecilia rushed in. They had clearly heard the sounds of a fight and hurried over.

Inside, they saw three corpses on the floor—evidence of the recent struggle.

"Lord Merlin, what happened?" Cecilia asked urgently.

"Nothing serious, just a few petty thieves." Merlin shrugged indifferently.

"Petty thieves?" Kiel looked at the three dead bodies. The scaly-skinned Mark was one thing, but the other two were ordinary humans. Killing them so casually didn’t seem right.

Alice noticed Kiel’s confusion and explained for Merlin, "These three were the village bullies. When we arrived, they were causing trouble."

"Ah, so this village really does have problems. Everyone seems to be living in fear." Kiel nodded, suddenly understanding.

"Fear of what?" Merlin frowned, looking at Kiel in surprise.

"We checked a few places and found that this isn’t an abandoned village. The villagers are just hiding in their homes, too afraid to come out or interact with strangers." Kiel explained concisely.

"Yeah, when we tried to enter, we were almost mistaken for bandits." Cecilia added, still indignant.

"What’s going on?" Alice turned to the white-haired tavern owner, puzzled.

The tavern owner studied Merlin’s group. They were an odd bunch—especially Cecilia, whose priestly robes, though plain at first glance, were clearly made of silk upon closer inspection. Silk was an extravagant luxury in Great Britain, far beyond the means of commoners. Only the greatest nobles could afford such garments.

Sensing Cecilia’s high status, and with the promised Mithril-ranked adventurer still nowhere in sight, the tavern owner wondered if this group might be the key to solving their crisis.

"To be honest," he sighed deeply, "our entire fishing village has been under the control of these scoundrels. They’ve committed unspeakable crimes, leaving the villagers too terrified to do anything but hide in their homes."

"How did the village end up like this?" Merlin asked, surprised.

The tavern owner let out a long, mournful sigh. "It’s a long story. Ever since that alchemist, Democritus, began conducting his mysterious experiments on the island, our lives have been ruined. We had no choice but to organize a raid. Mark, the only warrior in the village, led the villagers on a nighttime expedition to the island. But most of them... perished in the sea..."

Alice knit her brows slightly. She could understand the villagers’ actions—hiring powerful adventurers was expensive, and considering the cost, taking matters into their own hands made sense.

"Only Mark returned... but he was no longer human." The tavern owner looked down at Mark’s corpse, unable to suppress the hatred in his eyes. "After he came back, our nightmare began. He oppressed the villagers, committed atrocities, and even kidnapped people, sending them to the island in the Dover Strait to serve as Democritus’s test subjects."

"How could he be so cruel? He was from the same village!" Alice didn’t know that Mark had been poisoned and forced to obey Democritus.

"I don’t know the details either. If you hadn’t arrived today, we might have continued living in this hell." The tavern owner sighed again, deeply grateful to Alice.

After a brief exchange, Merlin’s group had a clear picture of the situation.

"It seems our competitor hasn’t arrived yet?" Cecilia said seriously, a flicker of relief in her voice. It meant they still had a chance.

"That’s strange. We were delayed for so long, yet that person is even slower than us?" Alice said, suspicious.

"Maybe something came up at the last minute?" Kiel stroked his chin thoughtfully. "This could be a good thing. We can take the initiative and resolve the issue first."

"Exactly! If we act now, I’ll be able to hold my head high in front of Father. He’ll finally acknowledge me!" Cecilia’s eyes sparkled with hope as she asked, "Lord Merlin, what do you think?"

All eyes turned to Merlin, waiting for his decision. After all, he was their strongest fighter.

"Hmm..." Merlin narrowed his eyes, thinking for a moment before saying casually, "It’s not impossible. But is the ship ready?"

"It should arrive by tomorrow morning." Kiel answered seriously.

"Then we’ll set out at dawn tomorrow. The faster we finish this, the better." Merlin decided with a wave of his hand.

The tavern owner was confused, unable to grasp what these outsiders were planning.

"Uh... judging by your accents, you seem to be from Wales. What brings you here?"

"Do you really need to ask?" Merlin turned to the tavern owner. "We’re going to the island to take down that alchemist, of course."

"Wha—!" The tavern owner froze, then exclaimed in horror, "That’s impossible! You shouldn’t be so reckless!"

"Huh? What kind of reaction is that? Taking out the alchemist would be a good thing for your village." Merlin found the old man’s response bizarre.

"It *is* a good thing, but you have to know your limits!" The tavern owner’s expression was awkward. He didn’t think Merlin’s group stood a chance against Democritus.

"What do you mean?" Merlin felt the old man was underestimating them.

"With just the four of you, you can’t possibly defeat that alchemist. Don’t go throwing your lives away." The tavern owner spoke gravely, his tone heavy with concern. "I know you mean well, but Democritus is far beyond your level."

"Yeah, our village chief already hired a Mithril-ranked adventurer. If we just wait a little longer, our crisis will be resolved. There’s no need for you to risk your lives against such a powerful enemy." Connie couldn’t help but chime in, convinced that Merlin’s group wasn’t ready for Democritus.

The village had already lost a hundred militiamen in their failed raid—proof that the alchemist was not to be trifled with. And Mark had been a high-tier warrior, yet he had been completely subdued by Democritus. It didn’t take much to realize that the alchemist was strong enough to crush high-tier opponents.

Looking at Merlin’s group, the strongest among them seemed to be Alice, a high-tier Gold-ranked adventurer. Going up against Democritus would be suicide, wouldn’t it?

Merlin’s group, however, didn’t seem particularly bothered by the tavern owner’s doubts. Cecilia even wore a faint, superior smile.

Even if Democritus was powerful, they still had to take him down. And with Merlin on their side, the enemy’s strength didn’t seem like much of an issue.

"You really are frogs in a well." Cecilia pointed at Merlin, her face deadly serious as she launched into a shameless boast. "This man here..."

"Is Merlin, the Cosmic Swordsman, a Saint-tier powerhouse hiding his true strength."

"Every time he turns on his ‘show-off mode,’ everyone else can only stand there in stunned silence, trembling in awe!"

(。.V.))

title: Chapter 7 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 7 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 8 · Chapter 7

“Shut up, I’m...” Merlin brushed his golden hair and said with a weary expression, “Acting cool is like the wind—it’s always with me.”

Alice’s expression turned complicated, and she couldn’t help but grumble inwardly, “Stop this foolishness! You’re giving off such a low vibe, it’s embarrassing!”

The tavern owner and Connie wore blank expressions. Despite Cecilia’s glowing praise of Merlin, the black iron adventurer badge around his neck held no weight as proof.

A lowest-tier black iron adventurer is actually a Saint-tier powerhouse hiding his true strength?

Are you kidding? Only someone with a twisted mind would willingly be a black iron adventurer scorned by everyone.

If a deranged guy like Merlin is a Saint-tier powerhouse, then Saint-tier powerhouses must be worthless.

The tavern owner and Connie didn’t believe Cecilia’s words, thinking it absurd that they were revolving their plans around a black iron adventurer.

“Besides, the silver-tier adventurer you hired still hasn’t arrived, has he?” Cecilia smiled faintly, “Instead of waiting endlessly here, why don’t we resolve your crisis first?”

“We’re not concerned about that. We’re worried about your safety. After all, you’re my lifesavers. I can’t bear to watch you go to your deaths—my conscience wouldn’t allow it.” The tavern owner said earnestly, believing Merlin’s plan to confront Democritus was extremely risky.

“Yes, you don’t need to rush to the island in the center of the sea. It would be better and safer to wait for that silver-tier adventurer to arrive and go together.” Connie couldn’t help but agree with her grandfather, thinking this group seemed insane and couldn’t gauge their own strength.

Even if alchemists lack combat skills, they can create numerous monsters.

Connie thought these ferocious monsters alone were beyond the capabilities of the four of them.

“Please don’t worry about us. As long as Lord Merlin agrees to join us, there won’t be any problems.” Kyle said confidently. As a devoted fan, he naturally trusted his idol completely.

The elderly tavern owner couldn’t help but feel a headache, wondering if he hadn’t made himself clear. Why were these outsiders so stubborn?

Connie, seeing their persistence, couldn’t help but wonder: Was this black iron adventurer truly that powerful? As they claimed, was he a Saint-tier powerhouse hiding his strength?

A beast-like howl suddenly echoed, seemingly from the street outside, immediately halting the tavern’s conversation.

Kyle and Cecilia grew tense, detecting a faint scent of blood in the air.

“What’s that sound?” Alice frowned, her brow furrowing.

“Old man, does your village keep magical beasts?” Merlin asked, frowning as if sensing something.

The tavern owner and Connie’s faces turned pale with terror, as if something they feared had appeared.

“No! Our village doesn’t keep magical beasts. These are alchemical beasts! Mark brought them back and raised them!” Connie stammered, hiding behind her grandfather in fear.

“These monsters usually only listen to Mark. Now that Mark is dead, have they gone berserk and started killing people on the street?!” The tavern owner’s eyes widened in shock, never imagining Mark’s death would cause such chaos.

“What are alchemical beasts?” Alice asked curiously.

“I think I’ve heard of this before...” Kyle touched his chin thoughtfully, “Many alchemists are obsessed with creating intelligent life and resurrecting the dead. After extensive research, though they haven’t created highly intelligent beings, they’ve produced monsters that exist between the dead and the living, known as alchemical beasts.”

“Are they hard to deal with?” Cecilia asked anxiously.

“They’re bloodthirsty monsters with razor-sharp teeth and claws that can destroy anything. Ordinary magicians and warriors can’t handle them...” Connie’s face turned pale, her voice trembling as she explained.

“Then we can’t just stand by and do nothing!” Alice drew her slender sword from her waist and declared energetically, “Let’s go and kill these beasts!”

“Miss Alice is right. Since this happened right in front of us, we can’t ignore it.” Kyle’s otaku spirit was ignited by Alice, and the flames in his eyes burned fiercely.

“Also...” Cecilia’s forehead was slick with cold sweat, and she was in a difficult position, so she could only agree.

Merlin frowned, looking at Alice’s heroic demeanor, and felt unhappy in his heart. This righteous little guardian’s bad habit had flared up again.

The elderly tavern owner widened his eyes in shock and said, “Those guys are dangerous, and there’s more than one of them!”

“So what?” Alice turned to the tavern owner and said seriously, “If we do nothing, your village will truly disappear from the map of Britain.”

“Uh!” The tavern owner was speechless, looking at Alice in astonishment and thinking, What an extraordinary person! She’s the very embodiment of justice and beauty, the Goddess of Light’s representative on earth!

“Leave the weaklings to you. I’m not interested. I’m going to stay here and have coffee.” Merlin waved his hand, uninterested in what was happening outside.

“Come with us too. We’re a team!” Alice dragged Merlin away, not letting him slack off.

The alchemical beasts, with their grotesque forms, were slaughtering villagers on the street.

They had no intelligence whatsoever and were nothing more than wild beasts that knew only how to kill and eat.

Alchemical beasts had no fixed appearance, and most were deformed monsters. It wouldn’t be strange if they had three heads.

The only common trait was their strong defense and exceptional attack power, as if they were born solely for slaughter.

Democritus provided alchemical beasts to Mark to help him suppress the villagers and taught him how to control them.

But now that Mark was dead, these alchemical beasts were out of control, like wild horses that had broken free from their reins, constantly attacking innocent villagers.

The small village was plunged into chaos.

Screams immediately echoed through the area, transforming the once-silent village into a “lively” scene.

Some residents hid in their houses, too afraid to come out, while others tried to flee but were captured by the alchemical beasts and devoured alive on the street.

The alchemical beasts sniffed the scent of humans on the street to hunt for prey. Even those hiding in their houses would likely become prey—it was only a matter of time.

On a small hill beside the fishing village, a mysterious figure in a brown cloak looked down at the chaos below from a high vantage point.

The mysterious figure wasn’t very muscular but had a lively aura. A bundle was slung over his shoulder, and he appeared to be a traveler from a distant land.

He slowly pulled back his hood, revealing a face that was slightly childish.

His facial features were distinct, with dark, deep eyes, a high nose bridge, and lips of moderate thickness.

His gray, slightly long, messy hair swayed in the wind on the mountaintop.

The red earrings on his ears were particularly eye-catching, swaying and shaking with his movements.

This young man was the legendary genius magician, the fourteen-year-old Saint-tier powerhouse, Erwin Johnson.

After getting lost numerous times and struggling to find his way, he finally arrived at the designated location and was about to begin his work.

Johnson touched his nose and smiled faintly.

“This should be the right place, right? It shouldn’t be wrong.

“Then...

“Let this genius use magic to restore peace to all this chaos!”
