title: Chapter 8 — Copy
content:
Chapter 8 — Copy

Volume 8 · Chapter 8

Screams erupted everywhere as deformed alchemy beasts rampaged through the fishing village, their fangs and claws easily harvesting human lives.

"Help! Help! Help!"

A deformed alchemy beast with no facial features at all picked up a villager on the ground, opened a bloody mouth, and was about to swallow him whole.

The villager struggled desperately, but the power gap was too great; he was grabbed by the alchemy beast, just like picking up a chick.

At a critical moment, *whoosh whoosh whoosh*, three ice swords stabbed hard into the alchemy beast's belly, causing it to retreat two steps and emit cries like a baby.

The innocent villager fell to the ground, his face covered in tears full of bewilderment, still not knowing what was happening.

Alice, Kyle, and Cecilia quickly approached the scene, while Merlin followed slowly behind, seemingly having no intention of fighting at all.

The three of them had already taken down two alchemy beasts, so it wasn't like there was no harvest.

At first, they thought this kind of monster wasn't hard to deal with; if a few people went together, the difficulty shouldn't be too high.

But reality was that the battle process was very strenuous; the alchemy beasts attacked living things like maniacs, and their defense capabilities were amazing.

If the wounds weren't fatal, they could still continue the attack.

A slight mistake and they would be torn to pieces by the alchemy beast's claws; the danger level was extremely high.

Fortunately, there didn't seem to be many of these monsters, seemingly only five or six in total, and Alice and Kyle could barely handle them.

As for Merlin, he watched the show from start to finish, having absolutely no intention of helping, instead thinking back to something earlier—

When in Rexus, he and Asmodeus had discussed alchemy beasts.

Turns out it was this kind of monster? Low intelligence, only capable of hunting, they could be used as cannon fodder.

In his view, the alchemy beasts' strength wasn't anything special; they shouldn't have reached the level that made Asmodeus care this much.

Could it be that these few alchemy beasts were too weak? Or was there a higher-level existence?

Merlin felt it was very possible; he wondered what kind of alchemy beast that alchemist, who wanted to "shoot" Asmodeus, had created that could move the Monarch of Lust?

But speaking of which, the alchemist being exterminated this time shouldn't be the one who wanted to "shoot" Asmodeus, right?

Merlin touched his chin, thinking it probably wouldn't be; if it were the same person, that would be too coincidental!

"Quickly get to the side!" Alice yelled at the bewildered villager, holding a thin sword, and rushed directly toward the alchemy beast that was pulling the ice sword from its belly.

The villager came to his senses and quickly scrambled away, crying and shouting without looking back, clearly terrified out of his wits.

"Miss Alice, I'll assist you!" Kyle waved his spear and charged over, seemingly intending to tank the first wave of attacks to provide space for Alice's output.

After all, Alice was stronger than Kyle, so letting her handle the attacks was the best choice.

"Middle-tier Strength Amplification! Middle-tier Defense Amplification!" Cecilia cast buffs on the two of them from behind.

The alchemy beast instinctively smelled danger and raised its sharp claws to attack Alice.

Kyle quickly closed in, blocking with his spear and oscillating high-tier fighting qi to shock the alchemy beast back.

Immediately after, Alice launched her attack; her thin sword stabbed out frequently, like starlight across the night sky, bringing up countless ice cones to stab at the enemy.

Merlin watched them fighting so hard; if it were him, he estimated he could beat the alchemy beast into a cripple with just one finger.

Thinking that he and they were teammates, right? If he didn't put in some effort, wouldn't they look down on him?

"Then... do you need help?"

"No need, Lord Merlin; for this kind of trash, how could I trouble you to make a move? Isn't that insulting you? Just leave it to us." Cecilia said with full energy.

"......Yes..." Merlin's face darkened, thinking that it was rare for him to want to help, yet they didn't need him?

A huge ice giant sword condensed into existence, then crashed down heavily, penetrating the alchemy beast's body!

A "Frost Punishment" that ruthlessly ended the enemy's life.

The heavy cold air dispersed, revealing Alice and Kyle.

Sweat dripped down Alice's face, and she was panting heavily; it looked like the continuous battle had consumed a lot of her magic power and fighting qi.

"How many are left?"

"Seemingly not many left..." Kyle answered with a frown, looking a bit tired as well.

"Yo, Alice, good work~" Merlin said inopportunely, seemingly teasing the "washboard."

"You guy, why don't you help a bit! Otherwise why call you here! ? Is watching us work so hard fun?" Alice said angrily.

"Sorry, I..." Merlin said faintly, thinking that it wasn't that he didn't want to help, but that Cecilia had put him on such a high pedestal that he couldn't back down.

"Helping won't kill you? Isn't it very easy for you?" Alice's face turned ugly with anger.

"What are you saying? ! With enemies of this level, how could you be embarrassed to ask Lord Merlin to make a move? Just obediently be a good meat shield and stand in front!" This worshipper, Cecilia, seemed to be sick in the head.

Alice's vein throbbed on her forehead, thinking this little fan girl was really annoying!

She didn't make any sense at all; she really wanted to give her two slaps to let her see Merlin's true face.

Just as Alice was about to say something, a loud "boom" echoed, and a residential house was directly knocked down and collapsed.

An incomparably huge two-headed alchemy beast, its whole body wrapped in broken chains, rushed out, with a lizard-like head constantly spitting and swallowing a red tongue.

At a glance, it felt completely different from the previous alchemy beasts; it belonged to the elite level, with powerful four-limb claws and full aggression.

The shadow of the two-headed alchemy beast drowned out Alice and Kyle, covering them in darkness.

"......What kind of monster is this?" Kyle stared blankly with widened eyes, feeling the gap in strength.

"...". Alice didn't speak, her mood also quite shocked, not expecting such a level of alchemy beast to suddenly appear.

The ones just now were already difficult enough; now a more powerful one had arrived, how could they possibly win?

Moreover, Alice's magic power and fighting qi were almost depleted, making the battle very disadvantageous in this situation.

"Kyle!" Cecilia saw the situation was wrong and hurriedly shouted for him to dodge, but it was too late.

"Roar!" The two-headed alchemy beast roared, raised a huge fist, and fiercely smashed it toward Kyle, who was closest.

"Cough!" Kyle coughed up a mouthful of blood and flew backward like a cannonball, crashing into the ruins.

"Ah!"

Alice came to her senses, fused ice crystals onto her thin sword, and slashed wildly at the two-headed alchemy beast, but it didn't have much effect.

The thin sword struck the two-headed alchemy beast's belly fiercely, sparking, showing its general defense capabilities.

In her desperation, Alice summoned "Ice Thorns"; two long ice whips covered in thorns rushed out from the ground, wrapping around the two-headed alchemy beast, but were easily broken by the monster.

Alice widened her eyes in panic, not expecting the strength of this two-headed alchemy beast to be so strong; it was simply not on the same level as the previous ones.

"Bad!"

The two-headed alchemy beast counterattacked without hesitation, opening its bloody mouth wide and lunging at Alice, bringing a gust of bloody wind.

... Merlin sighed, touching the sword at his waist, and slowly walked toward the two-headed alchemy beast, as if about to start his "show-off mode," but in the end, I still have to clean up the mess...

As soon as the words fell, a Saint-tier pressure suddenly rose behind Merlin, and a sound of breaking the air suddenly rose!

"Ice Thorns!"

A strip of ice thorn exactly the same as the one Alice had just used brushed past Merlin's ear and struck the two-headed alchemy beast straight on.

The seemingly soft thorns instantly turned into blades, instantly beating the two-headed alchemy beast's body into two halves!

The alchemy beast didn't even have time to scream; its blood exploded out like a fountain and burst apart right there!

Alice's "Ice Thorns" were used for control, while the other person's "Ice Thorns" were used to deal a fatal blow; with the same appearance, the power was completely different, showing the gap in strength at a glance!

Everyone was a bit surprised and looked back together, wondering who had suddenly arrived.

Johnson, with a slightly childish face, slowly walked to the front of the crowd, his earring swaying slightly.

"True magic isn't used like that? Not only is the power weak, but it's also very LOW...."

Merlin's face darkened, and a cold sweat slid down his forehead; looking at this fourteen-year-old stinky brat, he thought, "Oh my!"

I didn't get to show off, and I feel very uncomfortable ( =

(°∞叭)

title: Chapter 9 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 9 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 8 · Chapter 9

Alice stared at Johnson in shock, thinking this guy didn’t look very old—he was just a kid at most!

To reach Saint-tier at such a young age, and even perfectly mimic the magic she had just used...

Wait! Mimic *her* magic?!

Alice snapped back to her senses, as if realizing something. She glanced at the Adventurer’s Proof hanging from Johnson’s neck and suddenly understood. *Mithril rank.*

Name: Elwin Johnson.
Profession: Magician.

The simple information on the Mithril Adventurer’s Proof made everything clear to everyone—the long-awaited Irish magic prodigy had finally arrived.

Alice’s expression turned solemn, three black lines forming on her forehead. *This* was the legendary magic prodigy? He looked so young!

There was no harm like comparison. Alice felt an indistinct sense of frustration, and it was *not* pleasant.

They had both used *Ice Thorns*, yet the power wasn’t even on the same level.
Even Alice herself didn’t understand—*Ice Thorns* was meant for control, but in Johnson’s hands, it had become an unstoppable offensive spell!

If she set aside the gap in strength, even in terms of understanding magic, Alice was far behind Johnson.

Being outdone by a 14-year-old brat—Alice’s pride was *wounded.*

Cecilia stayed silent, eyes wide. She hadn’t expected Johnson to show up. Now the pressure was immense—she’d have to compete with this Irish magic prodigy to see who could resolve the fishing village’s crisis first.

Kyle slowly crawled out of the rubble, his mind filled with awe at Johnson’s magic. This was the most abundant mana he had ever seen.

And the Saint-tier pressure was so stable, not a hint of disorder—like a neat army standing before him.

It seemed the rumors were true: though young, he was a genuine powerhouse, one who could rank among the top in all of Great Britain.

“Magic is about channeling the forces of nature for your own use. Only by stimulating every thread of magical elements with spiritual power can magic’s strength be fully unleashed. Using magic the way *you* did just now, Auntie, is simply a waste of mana…”
Johnson wagged his finger, looking at Alice with what seemed like disdain.

Merlin smirked crookedly, watching Johnson. *This guy reaching Saint-tier at such a young age is impressive, and he has unique insights into magic… but his temper seems a bit full of himself. Do all so-called ‘geniuses’ have this kind of arrogance?*

“…What did you say?!” Alice’s face flushed with anger. She was actually being lectured by a 14-year-old brat—it was infuriating!

“What? Am I wrong? This genius rarely gives pointers, you know. You should feel honored.”
Johnson sighed, his words sharp as knives.

“Who cares about your pointers?! You actually called me *Auntie*?! Where do I look like an aunt?! I’m clearly a *young lady*!”
Alice trembled with rage. So *that* was the real issue—she was so young, yet being called *aunt* was driving her insane!

Merlin’s forehead broke out in a cold sweat, black lines forming. *Alice really fixates on the weirdest things… her priorities are on another level!*

“Hmph!” Johnson coldly scoffed, glancing at the Gold Adventurer’s Proof around Alice’s neck.
“If it weren’t for the fact that we’re fellow adventurers, I wouldn’t even bother with you. And at my age, becoming a Saint-tier powerhouse, surviving countless battles, being a universally acknowledged magic genius, and receiving a personal award from Her Majesty the Queen—what’s wrong with calling you *Auntie*?”

“…You little brat, so full of yourself! Just because you have a halo over your head?!”
Alice’s brows knitted tightly. At first, she thought they could all be polite as fellow adventurers, but this guy had *no* intention of being polite!

“That’s exactly it—I *am* amazing. And I’m not a little brat. Sure, I’m 14, but my *mental* age is already very mature, unlike *some* immature aunts~”
Johnson shrugged, putting on an innocent look.

“Im…mature?” Alice was left speechless, probably seething with internal injuries.

Usually, it was Merlin who got mocked, but today, it was Alice’s turn.

Actually, Johnson *had* noticed Merlin, but since he was only an Iron-rank adventurer, Johnson didn’t care and ignored him outright.

Merlin stared blankly at Johnson, thinking, *This kid’s personality is awful. He really needs some discipline.*

“By the way, what are you adventurers from Rexham doing here? On a mission?”
Johnson asked curiously.

“None of your business. Can’t we just be here to sightsee?”
Cecilia suddenly interjected, seemingly unwilling to let him know they were here to steal the credit.

“Oh?” Johnson smiled faintly. “I was just saying, this village hired *me* to resolve the crisis, so I’m here. You don’t need to trouble yourselves with guarding the place.”

Johnson’s words were a bit cold, but in this line of work, it was perfectly normal.

Fellow adventurers were often rivals. There were plenty who stole each other’s jobs, so Johnson’s guarded attitude was understandable.

For adventurers, having a commission snatched away midway was *extremely* humiliating.
It would make many colleagues look down on you, doubting your abilities.

“We never planned to steal your job, but if the village’s crisis gets resolved early, that’s not our fault.”
Merlin said meaningfully, thinking that if he just *happened* to take care of that alchemist, wouldn’t this little brat’s trip be for nothing? The thought made him a little excited.

“With *you*?” Johnson glanced at them, curling his lip. “Ridiculous~ I advise you not to overestimate yourselves. This mission is rated SS-rank—it’s *way* beyond your capabilities. Oh, right, you don’t even *qualify* to accept it.”

“Tsk!” Merlin clicked his tongue in dissatisfaction. If beating up a little kid wouldn’t get him judged, he’d have already kicked Johnson into outer space.

Alice’s face was dark, her inner rage burning fiercely. She no longer wanted to talk to Johnson at all, her mind fixated on the malicious title of *“Auntie.”*

Kyle, however, had a different take. *This 14-year-old genius mage is still just a kid… probably praised too much, and now he’s floating on air.*

Just as Johnson had made the atmosphere unbearably awkward, the elderly tavern owner, seeing no danger outside, hurried out, his face piled with obsequious smiles.

“Oh my~! You must be… the Mithril adventurer from Scandinavia?”

“Can’t you see for yourself?” Johnson lifted the Mithril Adventurer’s Proof from his neck and gave it a little swing—everything was self-evident.

The old tavern owner squinted carefully, then beamed with joy. After waiting and waiting, the great savior had finally arrived!

With this Mithril adventurer here, resolving the fishing village’s crisis was only a matter of time.

A Mithril adventurer meant absolute Saint-tier strength—something Alice’s group couldn’t compare to at all.

Who was more distinguished? Wasn’t that obvious…?

The old tavern owner was over the moon, rubbing his hands together, speaking with extreme caution, terrified of offending Johnson.

“You… you’re the adventurer our village hired, right? We’ve been waiting for you for so long… You’ve finally come, just… a *little* late…”

“…What’s strange about being late?”
Johnson smiled indifferently, spreading his hands and tilting his head coolly.

“As a strong man, making a grand entrance at the end isn’t the rule?”

title: Chapter 10 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 10 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 10

Alice rolled her eyes. *Late by a little?* It’s way past that! If it weren’t for us, this fishing village would’ve been a feeding ground for alchemical beasts already!

The elderly tavern owner, of course, dared not voice his anger at Johnson’s arrogance. After all, the man was a Mithril-ranked adventurer—the village’s salvation depended on him. So he gritted his teeth and forced a flattering smile. “Well… it’s true what they say. The strong always make their grand entrance last. Anyone who shows up early is just a nobody. That’s how stories are written.”

“I’m a magic prodigy!” Johnson flicked his gray hair. “Someone as powerful as me can’t just appear out of nowhere. Naturally, I have to make my dazzling debut at the most critical moment—it’s only fitting for my status.”

“Y-Yes, absolutely!” the tavern owner lied through his teeth, using the same tone one would use to humor a child. “As long as you’re here, that’s what matters. You’re such a famous and busy man—it’s already a miracle you could spare the time to come to our little village.”

“Glad you understand.” Johnson nodded, his heart swelling with pride.

“Of course, of course! You’ve brought hope to our village. Surely you can resolve our crisis with ease?” The tavern owner wrung his hands, probing carefully.

“You mean that alchemist on the island? Please. I’m a magic prodigy. One Fireball spell is all it’ll take to solve the problem.” Johnson was brimming with confidence, not the least bit stressed by the mission.

“No wonder you were knighted by the queen at just fourteen—the rising star of tomorrow! Our village is truly honored to have hired an adventurer of your caliber.” The tavern owner, a master of flattery, had Johnson eating out of the palm of his hand.

“Hmph hmph. I’m a bit tired now. Been walking for days. Find me a decent room to rest in.” Johnson rubbed his shoulders, feigning exhaustion.

“Of course, of course! Traveling all the way from Ireland to Kent must’ve been exhausting. My tavern has excellent rooms—I’ll prepare the best one for you. What do you say?” The tavern owner decided to treat Johnson well. If the man got upset, he might not lift a finger for the village.

“Where’s your tavern?” Johnson asked.

“Just to the north,” the tavern owner replied warmly.

“Oh~ So that’s it?” Johnson nodded, then pointed in a direction. “Over there?”

The tavern owner froze, awkwardly reminding him, “Uh… esteemed adventurer, that’s south.”

“Ahem!” Johnson coughed twice to cover his embarrassment. “I know. I was just saying the scenery over there is beautiful. Where’s your tavern? Lead the way.”

“Right this way, please.” The tavern owner hurriedly guided Johnson to his lodgings.

Alice looked in the direction Johnson had pointed—nothing but ruins. *Not beautiful at all.*
*Is this kid… insane?*

Merlin, however, saw the truth. *No wonder he arrived so late. The guy’s completely directionally challenged! It’s a miracle he even made it here in one piece.*

Cecilia only cared about securing the credit for themselves. She urgently asked, “Lord Merlin, what should we do now?”

Kyle, dragging his aching body over, fretted, “Now that this ‘genius mage from Ireland’ is here, and he just copied Lady Alice’s magic so effortlessly… the rumors are true. He’s a Saint-tier mage with serious strength. Won’t this mess with our plans?”

“It *is* a problem. He might solve the whole thing before we even get a chance. Then we’d have come here for nothing.” Alice scowled, still seething. “And his attitude is *terrible*—he called me *auntie*! Since I’m his auntie, it’s my duty to educate this brat properly. How about we feed him some croton seeds? He’ll be stuck on the toilet for half a month. That’ll keep him from interfering.”

“Ooh, a whole bag of croton seeds! Guaranteed to glue him to the outhouse for six months!” Cecilia nodded earnestly in agreement.

“Perfect. It’s settled.” Alice’s eyes burned with vengeance and fury at the word *auntie*—she’d even abandoned her Hero’s dignity over this.

“Hey, hey, hey!” Merlin furrowed his brow, cutting into their unsettling conversation. He silently chided Alice, “You used to be a Hero. Isn’t this a little *too* underhanded, even for you?”

“Even if I *was* a Hero, I refuse to let anyone call me *auntie*. I’ll smash that brat’s head in.” Alice gritted her teeth in a whisper.

“I’ve met Heroes before. They had morals. They wouldn’t throw a fit over something like this. Were you even a *real* Hero?” Merlin sighed, letting a few cold sweats slide down his forehead as he muttered back.

“I’m a girl. Age is a matter of life and death. Hero’s morals? What’s that? Don’t need ‘em.” Alice casually whispered in return.

*What the hell…* Merlin was too exhausted to argue. *If the old Heroes knew Alice was like this, they’d probably faint in the bathroom from sheer humiliation. She’s willing to throw away her Hero’s dignity over the word “auntie”…*

“Lord Merlin, what are you two whispering about?” Cecilia, sensing the urgency, pressed again. “This situation is bad for us. A powerful rival like him is a major threat.”

“Yes, Lord Merlin. This mission is very important to our young lady. Please take it seriously.” Kyle chimed in diplomatically.

“Relax. We’ll set out at first light tomorrow.” Merlin glanced in Johnson’s direction, then smirked. “As for that pompous brat… he’s no threat at all.”

“As expected of Lord Merlin! You must already be confident about stealing the credit. I *knew* bringing you here was the right choice. If you say it’s fine, then it’s *definitely* fine.” Cecilia’s eyes sparkled with admiration. If Merlin said there was no problem, then there *was* no problem.

*Stealing the credit…* Merlin’s expression turned complicated. *That sounds so ugly. Makes me sound like some desperate, credit-grubbing headhunter…*

“Lord Merlin, are you *sure* it’s fine? He *is* a famous genius mage. Taking his prey won’t be easy, right?” Kyle wasn’t doubting Merlin’s strength—he just thought the credit would be hard to snatch, given the other man’s power as a holy and mighty Saint-tier warrior.

“What’s so hard about it?” Merlin replied indifferently, sweating internally. *The guy’s just a walking compass failure.*

*Give that kid a little boat, and he’d struggle to even find the island in the middle of the strait. If he doesn’t just row in random circles and end up in the Caribbean…*

title: Chapter 11 — Obsessed Fan
content:
Chapter 11 — Obsessed Fan

Volume 8 · Chapter 11

Night.

The tavern owner, of course, wouldn’t only entertain Johnson.

He certainly hadn’t forgotten whose hands had saved his and his granddaughter’s lives.

So the tavern owner treated Merlin the Wanderer well too, and let them stay for free.

But only three rooms remained, and a small disagreement arose over how to assign them—

“Thank goodness there are three rooms. That’s enough for us.” Kael sighed in relief, thinking that if there were too few, Cecilia would probably throw a fit.

After all, Cecilia was a noble young lady, used to having a room all to herself.

If she suddenly had to share with someone else, she’d likely be disgusted by the idea.

“Eh?! Three rooms? Does that mean two people have to share?” Alice asked in surprise.

“Yeah.” Kael nodded, not understanding what Alice found so surprising.

“Then who shares with who? Me and Cecilia?” Alice asked tentatively, as if she’d already forgotten their fake marital status.

“Of course not. Miss Alice should obviously share with Lord Merlin.” Kael stated it as a matter of fact, seeing nothing wrong with a husband and wife sharing a room.

*Pffft!* Merlin nearly choked on his own spit. Share a room with Alice? What a joke. She’d probably smother him with a washboard in his sleep. And they weren’t even a real couple—why would they share a room? Did they take him for some lecherous Demon Lord? Damn it all!

“Wha—?!” Alice’s eyes widened in horror, her face a picture of sheer terror. “Why would I have to share a room with *this* guy?! I refuse!”

“Yeah, who’d want to share with a washboard like her? If it were some busty lady, I might *consider* it.” Merlin said seriously, flatly rejecting Kael’s suggestion.

Alice’s face darkened at Merlin’s dismissive tone. Did he really just look down on her like that? She was a girl too, damn it!

“Hah!” Merlin smirked, glaring at Alice without an ounce of politeness. “You’re the one who should have some self-awareness, you damn fool.”

“You’re the one who needs self-awareness! What about me isn’t good enough for you?! I’m the one who *hates* the idea of sharing a room with you the most!” Alice snapped, terrified of being outdone by Merlin.

“Do you think *I* want to share a room with *you*? This is an insult to me! Every inch of you makes me want to puke—*blegh*!” Merlin gagged, as if he’d swallowed a fly.

“You pervert! I—I—” Alice ground her teeth, so furious she could barely form words.

“Washboard, hehehe~” Merlin grinned, delighted by Alice’s rage. The more she seethed, the happier he felt. A demon’s joy was indeed built on the suffering of his enemies.

Cecilia and Kael stared at the “couple” in bewilderment, completely lost as to why they’d started arguing. Were these two *really* married? It was hard not to doubt.

*Cough!* Kael cleared his throat to mask his awkwardness and interjected, “So… Lord Merlin, Miss Alice, you two *really* don’t want to share a room?”

“Who’d want to share with *this* washboard?!”

“Who’d want to share with *this* pervert?!”

They answered in unison, shutting Kael down. The poor bystander was just trying to help, but their emotions were clearly unstable.

Kael froze, a cold sweat forming on his brow. “But… you’re husband and wife. Sharing a room shouldn’t be a problem, right?”

“Yeah, aren’t you two married? Sleeping together is only natural…” Cecilia chimed in, unable to resist adding her own thought.

Merlin’s lips twisted into a wry smile. He was too tired to explain anymore. After being misunderstood so many times, he’d reached his limit.

Alice hesitated, unwilling to answer. If she denied it now, after claiming to be Merlin’s wife before, wouldn’t that just make her look like a liar?

So Alice thought it over and decided to keep up the act with Cecilia and Kael. Getting caught now would be too humiliating.

“I just don’t want to share with *this* guy. No other reason.”

“…What’s going on here?” Kael scratched his head, even more confused by this “married couple.”

Cecilia seemed to have an idea. She leaned in and whispered to Kael, “Maybe they’re having a lovers’ quarrel? Think about it—couples argue all the time. They’re probably in a rough patch. We shouldn’t interfere too much.”

“Right, right, it must be a lovers’ quarrel…” Kael glanced at Merlin and Alice, who were glaring at each other, and became even more convinced.

Merlin frowned, watching Cecilia and Kael whispering to each other. He had a bad feeling about this.

“In that case, Lord Merlin, if you don’t mind… how about I share a room with you? It’d be better for the two ladies to each have their own room.” Kael was quite the gentleman, speaking earnestly.

“Hmm?” Merlin looked at Kael. He didn’t seem like that kind of guy, so there was no issue. “No problem. I don’t mind.”

“No! I don’t agree!” Cecilia pouted, clearly displeased with the idea.

“Lady Cecilia, now’s not the time to be stubborn…” Kael said, looking troubled. He hadn’t expected the noble lady to reject the plan.

“I’m *not* being stubborn.” Cecilia knitted her delicate brows, emphasizing her point.

“What’s wrong with this? Why don’t you agree? Do you *want* to share a room with Merlin?” Alice narrowed her eyes, suddenly suspicious of Cecilia. If *she* could share a room with Merlin, then no other woman should be allowed to—her chest burned with jealousy.

“Wha—?! What are you even *saying*?!” Cecilia’s face flushed crimson, furious. “Don’t look down on me! Do you think I’m the kind of person who’d throw myself at someone? As a noble, I have *some* self-respect!”

“Then why are you rejecting Kael’s suggestion? Letting the men share is a perfectly good idea!” Alice asked, confused. Wouldn’t it be great if she and Cecilia each had their own room?

“Lord Merlin is our strongest fighter! How could we make him squeeze into a room with Kael? That’d be disrespectful to Lord Merlin!” Cecilia declared righteously, fully embracing her role as a devoted fangirl.

Alice’s expression twisted in outrage.

“You brain-dead little fangirl! Can you be *any* more ridiculous?!”

Today’s been busy at the hospital, so I’m typing this on my phone. Probably won’t be home until tomorrow, so the update’s a bit short—sorry about that.

title: Chapter 12 — That One
content:
Chapter 12 — That One

Volume 8 · Chapter 12

Alice’s expression darkened. She felt the preferential treatment for Merlin had gone too far, and her disdain for his brainless fans was skyrocketing.

“That makes sense. Then I’ll take a room to myself.” Merlin stroked his chin and agreed without hesitation.

“Ah?!” Alice glared at Merlin, displeased. “How can your face be so thick? If you take a room by yourself, then what about—”

“You’ll figure it out yourselves, won’t you? What else can be done?” Merlin said, full of self-righteous indignation.

“You—!” Alice’s face flushed with anger, pointing at Merlin’s nose, speechless.

“If Merlin-sama takes a room to himself… what about me?” Kyle scratched his head awkwardly, embarrassed. “Should I sleep outside? Then Cecilia-sama and Alice can each have a room.”

“No!” Cecilia refused immediately. She felt Kyle worked hard every day, and making him sleep outside would make her seem like a cruel host.

“Then I can’t share a room with Cecilia-sama either?” Kyle’s face was written with embarrassment.

“What are you scheming?!” Cecilia raised her staff and whacked Kyle’s head hard. “…I’ll share with Alice. It’ll be a tight squeeze, but you and Merlin-sama can have a room to yourselves.”

“…Isn’t that a bit much? Cecilia-sama, you’re a noble lady. Is it really fine for you to squeeze into a room with someone else?” Kyle looked astonished. The young lady he remembered should have been very resistant to getting too close to commoners.

“Desperate times call for desperate measures.” Cecilia paused, then said seriously, “I’m not being unreasonable. The situation is special, so enduring a little hardship is fine.”

“Waaah…” Kyle instantly burst into tears, overcome with emotion. He felt Cecilia had changed a lot and become much more considerate. “The young lady has finally grown up. If the Duke knew, he’d surely be overjoyed.” *sniffles*

Merlin’s mouth twitched, and he broke into a cold sweat. *What does Kyle take Cecilia for? A giant baby?!*

“Hold it in! Stop your blubbering, it’s disgusting!” Cecilia snapped angrily, seemingly embarrassed.

“We’re sharing a room?” Alice asked tentatively. In her eyes, Cecilia had always been rather haughty. If possible, she didn’t want to share with this noble lady.

“What’s the problem with me sharing with you?” Cecilia flicked her voluminous golden curls, speaking in a smug tone. “I’m a noble, you know. Sharing a room with me is an honor. You should use every trick in the book to flatter me.”

“…Who would flatter you?!” Alice fumed, indignant. *I’ve really had enough of this noble lady!*

It looked like tonight would be another annoying night…

---

Night fell.

The room where the two girls were staying.

Just as Alice had expected, staying with Cecilia was not pleasant.

Whether it was intentional or not, Cecilia had been relentlessly criticizing every aspect of the accommodations since the beginning.

This won’t do, that’s no good—it’s far less comfortable than her carriage. She kept feeling like a cockroach might scurry out from somewhere.

It was as if staying in this shabby little inn was an insult to her, a noble lady of the Rose family.

“A small village is just a small village. The living conditions are way too poor! Is this even a place for people to stay?! It’s practically a doghouse!” Cecilia stomped her feet in frustration.

She had thought the accommodations here would at least be passable, but the shabbiness far exceeded this noble lady’s imagination!

To be fair, this was the worst place Cecilia had ever stayed in. It was incomparable to where she usually lived.

The tasteless decor, the simple bed and table—even the ceiling showed signs of dampness.

After all, this was a remote fishing village. Having an inn of this standard was already quite good.

But Cecilia, a noble lady, was staying in such a shabby place for the first time. Complaining a little was understandable.

Not everyone lived in luxurious mansions like Cecilia, leading a decadent life with everything handed to them.

“…”

Alice sighed, rolled her eyes, and continued pretending to sleep, not wanting to acknowledge Cecilia’s childish complaints.

She felt Cecilia was making trouble out of nothing. The environment here was fine—it was acceptable for a temporary stay. What was there to complain about so much?

As an adventurer for a year, Alice had stayed in all sorts of rundown places. If it was really bad, she’d just camp outside with not even a blanket.

Right now, having a roof over her head and no drunken brawls was already pretty good in Alice’s book.

“Seriously! Our bathroom at home is better than this place, and cleaner too. Now I’m worried I’ll get bitten by cockroaches in the middle of the night!” Cecilia, seeing Alice wasn’t responding, started acting up even more, trying to draw attention.

Alice slightly furrowed her delicate brows. *Is she trying to show off her wealth?* Just how luxurious was Cecilia’s home? Most commoners lived in places like this.

“Alright, enough. Go to sleep. We have to take a boat to the island tomorrow morning.” *yawn*

“Alice…” Cecilia sat down beside Alice and asked seriously, “Do you really think this place is livable?”

“Why wouldn’t it be? We’re traveling. Can’t you lower your standards a little?” Alice turned over, gazing at Cecilia indifferently.

“I feel wronged! By the way, we’re the saviors of the innkeeper’s life, right? But the only luxury suite here was given to that bratty Irish kid! Isn’t that disrespectful to us?” Cecilia was still bitter about this. She felt the innkeeper had been too good to Johnson, and his gratitude lacked sincerity.

“Don’t dwell on it. In the innkeeper’s eyes, that genius mage is the great savior. Naturally, he’d want to treat him well.” Alice said coolly.

“Nonsense! Merlin-sama is the great savior! He deserves the best treatment!” Cecilia insisted stubbornly.

“Who would believe you if you told them Merlin is powerful?” Alice knitted her brows.

*Damn it!* All because Merlin-sama is too modest, and these fools are ignorant. Cecilia couldn’t help but grumble. Naturally, she lacked the confidence to make others believe Merlin was strong—unless Merlin himself was willing to show off his strength.

“Stop grumbling and go to sleep.” Alice gave one last reminder, already heavily drowsy.

“Hmph!” Cecilia had no choice. She angrily threw off the blanket, got into bed with Alice, and then wrapped her arms tightly around Alice’s waist, pressing her entire body against her.

“…” Alice helplessly mumbled, feeling Cecilia’s two large breasts pressing hard against her back. *This is a declaration of war! My pride has been trampled!*

“Hmph hmph, I’m commandeering you as my body pillow. Be honored!” Cecilia said shamelessly, though in truth, she was just afraid of cockroaches.

Alice didn’t respond. She only felt the two soft mounds against her back were pure torment. There was no harm in comparison.

“By the way, Alice, are you and Merlin-sama having a fight?” Cecilia asked curiously.

“Why do you ask?” Alice countered, surprised.

“Because aren’t you two married? Married couples should sleep together, right? But you both seem so reluctant. It’s strange.” Cecilia whispered.

“That…” Alice’s gaze wandered, uncomfortable with the question. “There are all sorts of reasons. I can’t really answer.”

“So it *is* because of *that*, huh? Because *that* came, so it’s inconvenient to do *that*…” Cecilia narrowed her eyes, as if she’d uncovered a great secret.

“What are you talking about?” Alice’s brows knitted tightly, not understanding.

“You know, that thing girls get every month.” Cecilia smirked proudly.

“…” Alice’s cheeks flushed a light pink, and she stammered, unable to speak.

*Cecilia… what is she even thinking about?*

*Does she always have such dirty thoughts?*

title: Chapter 13 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 13 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 8 · Chapter 13

Alice kept her mouth shut, not saying a word. Though she wanted to explain, the situation didn’t allow it.

If she admitted that she and Merlin weren’t truly married, wouldn’t Cecilia just mock her?

*I knew you and Lord Merlin weren’t really married. With your personality, how could you possibly be worthy of him? Oh ho ho~*

With Cecilia’s nature, she’d definitely say something like that—how embarrassing would that be?

After hesitating for a long time, Alice chose to stay silent. Let Cecilia guess all she wanted; she wasn’t going to give a direct answer anyway.

Seeing Alice’s silence, Cecilia assumed she’d guessed right. “So it *is* like that, huh? Well, makes sense. Since you’ve got your period, that kind of thing is forbidden. But you should drink more hot water.”

Alice knit her delicate brows slightly. *Cecilia knows so much… Who taught her all this? Is noble knowledge really this extensive?*

“Miss Alice, have you and Lord Merlin… already done *it*?” Cecilia asked curiously, not the least bit shy.

*Pfft!* Alice’s whole body jolted. *What the heck is “it”?! She and Merlin didn’t have that kind of relationship at all!*

“What’s with that reaction? Have you or haven’t you?” Cecilia refused to let it go.

“…Who knows…” Alice deflected, unwilling to answer directly.

“You don’t know if you’ve experienced it *yourself*?” Cecilia tilted her head, staring at Alice’s back, then suddenly thought of a possibility. “Oh~, are you just shy? You’re usually so carefree, but privately, you’re surprisingly maidenly?”

“…” Alice froze, her face slowly turning red. “W-Who’s… who’s shy?! I just don’t want to answer!”

“Don’t want to answer?” Cecilia couldn’t help but let her imagination run wild. She spoke meaningfully, “Perhaps your first time with Lord Merlin didn’t go well, or left a bad impression? Maybe Lord Merlin is too… intense in private, not gentle at all, so you didn’t like it?”

“…What kind of topic are you even bringing up?! Just go to sleep!” Alice pulled the blanket tight around herself, her little face flushed crimson. *Why is Cecilia so open-minded? I’m still pure and innocent—I don’t want to talk about such explicit things!*

“Hm?” Cecilia abruptly paused, sensing something off about Alice. “Then it must’ve hurt a lot the first time, which is why you’re so against it? Don’t tell me you and Lord Merlin are still in some marathon love chase—I won’t believe that.”

“…” Alice was at a loss for words. She felt like Cecilia had cornered her completely.

“It must be that, right? The bone-deep pain made you too afraid to try again. As a fellow girl, I totally get it.” Cecilia said with the wisdom of an old soul.

The more Alice listened, the more uneasy she felt. She asked in surprise, “You’ve… experienced it?”

“…How could I? I just heard the little maids at home talk about it. They all said the first time hurts so much you almost pass out.” Cecilia answered seriously.

“…That bad?” Alice furrowed her brows. *How would I know? I’ve never experienced it. Where does she get all this strange knowledge?*

“You don’t know it hurts? Then—”

Cecilia narrowed her eyes, sensing something slightly amiss.

“It hurts! It hurt so much, of course I know…” Alice said through gritted teeth, her face burning red.

“So my guess was right—you and Lord Merlin have already…” Cecilia nodded knowingly, then changed the subject. “Besides the pain, did you feel anything else?”

“Why are you asking so much? Go try it yourself and find out…” Alice answered evasively, her heart pounding.

“I’m just curious! Tell me~” Cecilia pressed relentlessly.

“…I don’t want to answer.” Alice abruptly ended the topic. *How would I know if there’s anything else? If I make something up, I’ll get caught in a lie.*

“You’re shy again, huh? Hee hee~” Cecilia teased.

“Why are you so curious about *us*?” Alice’s tone grew impatient.

“No, no, I’m just curious about *you*,” Cecilia said earnestly.

“About *me*?” Alice’s expression turned confused.

“Yeah. How did someone as plain as a washboard like you climb up and manage to take Lord Merlin for yourself? You two don’t even seem like a match.” Cecilia cut straight to the point.

“…” Alice was speechless, awkwardly replying, “What’s not a match? Anyone can see Merlin got the better end of the deal.”

“No, no, I think Lord Merlin is a powerful man, so he must have many options…” Cecilia pondered, then answered seriously, “Like the Third Princess of Germania!”

“Huh? What’s so special about that princess?” Alice asked curiously.

“Well, that princess is now of marriageable age, but she still hasn’t found a suitable partner. But the King of Germania said that anyone who can defeat Germania’s First Warrior can marry the Third Princess.” Cecilia explained leisurely.

“That’s way too careless!” Alice thought that if some old man defeated the First Warrior, the Third Princess would be in for a miserable time.

“I think Lord Merlin could give it a try. If he succeeds, he’d become royalty!” Cecilia mused.

“Hah?! Why would Merlin do something so pointless?! I’d never allow it!” Alice quickly rolled over, glaring at Cecilia as she spoke seriously, like a cat whose tail had been stepped on.

“Hah, you’re jealous! So you *are* worried about Lord Merlin, huh? With so many better options out there, yet he chose to marry *you*.” Cecilia teased meaningfully.

“…I’m *not* jealous! Merlin wouldn’t do something so stupid anyway. Humph!” Alice huffed, turning her head away in a sulk.

“This just proves Lord Merlin is a devoted, charming man. It’s impressive, really—most nobles have at least five mistresses.” Cecilia looked at him with admiration.

…Alice curled her lip in a cold smirk. *A devoted man? The one who sneaks off to Helena’s secret room? He’s no better than Hobbes—they’re birds of a feather.*

“You two must have such a good relationship. Was your first meeting super romantic?” Cecilia couldn’t resist being nosy.

That question hit Alice’s sore spot, and she couldn’t help but start ranting.

“It was *nothing* like that! The first time we met, Merlin almost killed me! Then he treated me like a slave the whole way, stole my treasure, and left me in a terrible state!”

“How romantic! It’s like the troubadours’ tales of a domineering CEO and a clueless girl~” Cecilia’s eyes sparkled.

“G…” Alice’s face darkened, and she vowed silently never to say another word to this brainless fan.

Time passed slowly.

Both girls eventually fell asleep.

But in the middle of the night…

A sudden, violent chill jolted Cecilia awake, as if she’d been plunged into the dead of winter.

Cecilia bolted upright in bed, rubbing her arms frantically to warm up. Her breath came out in white puffs.

Shivering, Cecilia stared at Alice beside her, convinced the cold was radiating from her.

Panicked, Cecilia shook Alice violently and called out loudly.

“Miss Alice! Miss Alice, wake up!”

“Ugh…” Alice slowly regained consciousness, her head throbbing and her entire body aching with stiffness.

“Miss Alice, what’s going on?! Are you deliberately keeping me awake in the middle of the night?!” Cecilia complained indignantly.

Alice blinked, then quickly checked her body. Her arms were already being corroded by the cold, turning a bluish hue.

She still couldn’t control the inheritance crystal of the Frostwyrm Sacred Dragon. Now it was acting up again, and the power was backlashing.

*Damn it! It’s happening again?*

If she didn’t do something fast, she’d freeze to death!

Last time, Merlin had helped her…

But now…

Alice lifted her head, her expression grave, a flicker of hesitation in her eyes.

Should she go knock on Merlin’s door in the middle of the night?

title: Chapter 14 — Sleeping Together
content:
Chapter 14 — Sleeping Together

Volume 8 · Chapter 14

Cecilia was shivering beside her, feeling that the cold aura radiating from Alice was incredibly terrifying, and she didn't dare approach her lightly.

If this continued, they wouldn't be able to sleep at all, and she might even catch a cold from the chill.

Cecilia noticed that Alice's delicate brows were tightly furrowed, yet she remained completely silent, and she felt something was seriously wrong.

"Miss Alice? Miss Alice?"

"Huh?!" Alice came to as if waking from a dream. She felt that the ice-attribute magic she had been cultivating should normally be immune to cold erosion, but now it was being completely overwhelmed by the Frost Dragon's magic, on the verge of being eroded to death. This terrified her deeply. It seemed that some things, while excellent, were absolutely not to be consumed recklessly.

"What's wrong with you? Are you cultivating some kind of magic?" Cecilia furrowed her delicate brows and asked seriously.

"I... I..." Alice answered incoherently, feeling that it would be impossible to explain clearly to Cecilia, who probably didn't know much about inherited crystals either.

"I feel like your situation isn't good. Should I go call Lord Merlin?" Cecilia saw that frost was already beginning to form on Alice's body. If this continued, she might be frozen solid. She had never heard of someone freezing themselves while cultivating magic, so clearly something had gone wrong.

"..."

Alice hesitated. Looking at her hesitant expression, it was obvious she didn't really want to seek Merlin's help.

As expected, still that stubborn girl. She wanted to compete with Merlin over everything, so asking her to beg Merlin for help was something she'd rather die than do.

Although Alice was no longer the Hero now, her sense of justice and sense of mission remained, and going to beg the Great Demon Lord to save herself would always trigger intense resistance.

What should she do now?

If she didn't handle this, something bad would happen.

Did she really have to go knock on Merlin's door at a time like this?

She had a feeling it would come across as wrapping herself up nicely and voluntarily delivering herself to Merlin for his enjoyment.

Wasn't this basically knocking on a pornographic door? Going to find Merlin in the middle of the night would easily lead to misunderstandings!

Even if nothing happened, no one would believe she was still innocent. This was so terrible...

Alice held her forehead, feeling dizzy and lightheaded, her mind growing increasingly muddled. If she kept delaying, this was an extremely dangerous situation.

How had Merlin helped suppress the Frost Dragon's magic last time?

Oh right! They had to strip naked and sleep together...

Good heavens! What was this melodramatic method! This was inappropriate for minors!

Running to find Merlin in the middle of the night to strip naked and sleep together? If something didn't happen, she wouldn't even believe it herself!

After all, she was the former Hero of the Hall, the embodiment of justice and courage for one year.

She was actually going to strip naked and go find the Great Demon Lord to sleep with him!? This was too humiliating!

And they had recently had a falling out with Merlin, making it clear she disliked being in the same room as him.

Going to find him now would be so embarrassing, and that bastard would definitely mock her.

Alice was caught in turmoil, struggling bitterly within herself, while her body's abnormal reactions grew more and more intense, and it seemed even moving was becoming difficult.

"Miss Alice? What are you hesitating about?" Cecilia looked at Alice and felt the situation was getting worse and worse. "If this continues, you'll get sick from the cold. Let me go call Lord Merlin for you."

"N-no need..."

Alice glanced at Cecilia and felt that even speaking was becoming somewhat difficult.

She knew her situation was dangerous, but her stubborn personality refused to beg Merlin.

However, the situation was now critical. She couldn't suppress the Frost Dragon's magic herself, and it seemed only Merlin could help her.

This wouldn't do. As long as the green hills remain, there'll always be firewood. If she died halfway through, how could she ever deal with that bastard Merlin?

After thinking it over, Alice decided to find Merlin without telling Cecilia, so she could save at least a little face.

"It's fine. It'll be okay in a moment. It's an old problem. I'll go out and rest for a bit."

"Huh?!" Cecilia's eyes widened, suddenly stunned. "Are you really okay?"

"Yes, it's fine." Alice got out of bed, threw on a long robe, and left the room.

"..." Cecilia watched Alice's unsteady gait and felt the situation wasn't good at all. She couldn't help but think suspiciously:

Is she really okay?

From any angle, she was clearly barely holding on!

Even though she and Lord Merlin were husband and wife, why did they feel so distant?

Meanwhile, in Merlin's room.

The flame of the oil lamp flickered and swayed, illuminating the somewhat sparsely furnished room.

Merlin sat in a chair, holding a quill pen, diligently writing something.

It had been a while since he last wrote to his sister Lilith. It was time to send another letter to let her know he was safe.

Although Merlin was a transmigrator and his family bonds might not be real, and he and Lilith were only siblings in name,

Merlin had already lived in this other world for over 200 years, and throughout those long years, much of his behavior had been assimilated by this world.

So he did have a special affection for Lilith, that little tagalong sister of his.

Everyone thought Merlin loved his sister dearly, which was why he wrote to her so frequently, right?

NO! NO! NO! Anyone with such thoughts was still too young.

Just imagine what an old man who had been pestered by his sister for nearly 200 years needed?

Of course, it was freedom! To shake off the little tail behind him and live freely!

If Merlin didn't write to his sister from time to time, Lilith would become anxious and uneasy, thinking something had happened to him.

Then Lilith would tear relations with the Demon Race Council and forcibly leave the First Demon Lord Palace to come find Merlin.

So in order to keep Lilith in check, Merlin was forced to write to his sister regularly, telling her he was fine and to stay home and not come out!

This way, Merlin could continue to live freely outside without worrying about being pestered by Lilith—

"Dear, lovely, charming, unparalleled sister, your brother is living an incredibly comfortable life outside. My career is booming. Everywhere I go, everyone loves me, flowers bloom in my presence. So many factions are already fighting bloody battles to compete for my attention. Have you heard of the British Thorn Knights? They seem very interested in me and have extended an olive branch. I'm currently torn between whether to become a Purple Gold-ranked adventurer or join the Thorn Knights. Of course, working for others is impossible—I'll never work for others in this life. I just want you to know that your brother isn't some useless shut-in. Even outside, I'm a revered figure admired by thousands..."

Merlin wildly bragged to Lilith in the letter. Regardless of reality, as long as he painted himself in the grandest terms possible, that was all that mattered.

This way, Lilith would become frustrated and furious, unable to do anything about it, and would have even less reason to leave the palace to come find him.

"Knock knock knock!"

A knocking sound interrupted Merlin's letter-writing train of thought.

"Who is it!?"

"Knock knock knock!" The person outside didn't respond.

"Tch! What a pain..."

Merlin complained dissatisfied, got up to open the door, and saw Alice wrapped in a robe.

She was looking up at him with her pale little face, shivering.

From the outside, Alice didn't seem to have any obvious abnormalities besides her panicked expression.

"What are you doing here this late? If you're deliberately disturbing my rest, I'll punch your head in."

Alice looked at Merlin, her heart still wavering, but the backlash of the Frost Dragon's magic was growing more and more violent, and she had no choice left.

So Alice lowered her head, bit her lip, a pair of rosy blushes rising to her cheeks, and without saying a word, she threw herself into Merlin's arms—

"Let's... let's sleep together..."
