title: Chapter 15 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 15 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 15

Alice’s sudden attack left Merlin stunned, his entire body frozen as if struck by a petrification spell.

His eyes widened in shock, and he couldn’t help but let out a gasp.

He instinctively tried to retreat, but Alice was pressed too close—there was no shaking her off.

Merlin raised both hands, as if to prove his innocence, desperate not to be misunderstood or falsely accused.

His mind screamed, *Judge! Someone come quick, this one’s playing dirty and running me over!*

Alice’s face burned crimson, her head buried in Merlin’s chest, too afraid to meet his gaze. She dreaded that this heartless man might mock her, wounding her pride.

Right now, Alice’s heart was a storm of nerves. Her voice, usually sharp and fiery, had shrunk to a timid whisper—transforming her from a feisty chili pepper into a proper young lady.

But Merlin’s magic immunity truly worked wonders. The moment Alice embraced him, the violent frost of the Ice Dragon’s divine magic within her withered away, as if dispersed, no longer backlashing against her.

Alice’s emotions were a tangled mess. *So being close to Merlin really does help…*

It made sense now—last time, when they’d slept together naked, there had been a reason. And this time, it seemed…

*Oh no, how am I supposed to bring this up with Merlin?*

*…*

*We’ll sleep naked together, but you’re not allowed to do anything improper to me!*

What kind of lunacy was this—showing up in the middle of the night, then forbidding any physical contact? And what if Merlin lost control? If things escalated, she’d be powerless to stop him.

She should never have consumed that inheritance crystal. In the end, she’d only ended up losing herself.

Alice grumbled internally, resolving to stay on high alert tonight. She absolutely couldn’t let Merlin sully her pure soul.

Merlin looked down at Alice, who was clinging to him, sensing something was off.

Why was this flat-as-a-board woman barging in on him in the middle of the night? And why was she so… enthusiastic?

The feel of skin against skin suggested she hadn’t bothered to dress properly—just thrown on a robe before coming to find him.

And now she was going on about sleeping together—was this some kind of pretext for *other* activities?

He knew he was an irresistibly charming man, but he didn’t recall ever flaunting it in front of Alice.

When had she even developed feelings for him? Was she so overwhelmed by loneliness tonight that she couldn’t contain herself?

Years of experience told Merlin that something this abnormal had to be supernatural. He needed to stay calm and investigate.

“…What the hell are you talking about?”

Alice’s face burned all the way to her ears. *This bastard Merlin is doing it on purpose!* She was already too embarrassed to say it once—now he was making her repeat it? How cruel!

Though her pride was wounded, she still needed his help. She swallowed her dignity and spoke again, voice trembling.

“…Sleep with me… Is that so wrong?”

“Huh?!” Merlin’s brows furrowed instantly. This was getting awkward. “Are you sick? It’s the middle of the night, you’re not asleep, you come here demanding we sleep together—are you trying to seduce me?”

“I-I’m not trying to seduce you, okay?! I’m not that kind of easy woman!” Alice’s cheeks flushed crimson as she stammered, flustered. “…Me coming to you for this is an *honor*! You should be *grateful* and weeping with joy!”

“Emmmm…”

Merlin knit his brows, pressing his hands against Alice’s shoulders and ruthlessly pushing her away. “I refuse!”

“Eh?! Don’t!” Alice yelped in shock, clinging to him like a stubborn plaster, refusing to let go. “Don’t push me away! Why are you pushing me away?! Do you even have a heart?! You’re *awful*…”

“Stop clinging to me, you’re *annoying*…” Merlin shoved at her, feeling like he’d been saddled with an unwanted accessory.

“I’m *not* annoying! Any normal man would be over the moon if a beautiful girl came to his room in the middle of the night asking to sleep with him! You should be cheering, not complaining!” Alice still had confidence in her looks—assuming one ignored her figure.

“Why would I cheer? Get off me. I don’t want to sleep with you at all.” Merlin’s face darkened. “And didn’t you *hate* me the most when we were assigning rooms? Now you have the nerve to come crawling over here—how shameless.”

“…” Alice’s face burned even hotter, as if a knife had just twisted in her heart. “You… you *bastard*! Are you even a man?! I’m a living, breathing woman offering to sleep with you, and you *reject* me? Are you *gay*?!”

“I’m *not* gay! Stop slapping labels on me, will you?! And *you*—why the sudden urge to sleep with me? Did Cecilia do something to you?” Merlin’s brows tightened, his expression serious.

“Th-That’s…” Alice hesitated, too embarrassed to explain. It would make her sound weak, unable to resist the backlash.

“Oh~” Merlin watched her struggle for words and seemed to guess the truth. “Did Cecilia have smelly feet, snore, *and* fart in her sleep? Is that why you couldn’t take it anymore?”

“Shut up! Don’t pin a man’s disgusting habits on a girl! If Cecilia heard you say that, she’d cry herself to sleep in the bathroom!” Alice hurriedly stopped Merlin, feeling Cecilia had been slandered horribly.

“Then I don’t get you at all…” Merlin looked down at Alice, confused. “What *do* you want? I don’t want to sleep with you, period.”

“D-Do you really not want to sleep with me? Don’t you even want to… hold me?” Alice’s face burned as she gathered her courage to ask.

“Want to *what*? Your board of a body nearly choked me to death, okay?!” Merlin’s expression soured. Sleeping with Alice sounded like a form of torture.

“…” Alice glared at him, her heart shattered. *Even now, he won’t stop mocking me… Does he have no soul?*

“What’s *really* going on? If it’s nothing, stop bothering me. Just say what you need.” Merlin put on a stern face, immune to Alice’s attempts at seduction.

“…” Alice lowered her head, hesitating. “I… I just want to sleep with you, that’s all. It’s *purely* for sleeping, nothing weird! Don’t you *dare* misunderstand!”

“Hm?!” Merlin studied her like a cat with its tail stepped on. Something was definitely off. Then, a possibility struck him. “Is the inheritance crystal’s magic backlashing again?”

“Ugh!” Alice clamped her mouth shut, face burning, too flustered to speak. She hadn’t expected Merlin to see through her so easily. Panicked, she blurted out—

“I didn’t *mean* to come find you, okay?!”

“If it weren’t for the magic backlash, I *never* would’ve knocked on your door at this hour!”

“So don’t you *dare* misunderstand! I’m *not*—*absolutely not*—trying to seduce you into doing something criminal, *hmph*!”

title: Chapter 16 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 16 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 8 · Chapter 16

Alice put on a show of innocence, making it clear she had a legitimate reason for coming—she wasn’t just here to seduce him on a whim. She wasn’t that kind of frivolous girl.

"Now you understand why I came to find you, right? ...It’s not like I ran over here in the middle of the night to tempt you or anything..."

"So it *is* because of the Inheritance Crystal, huh? Come to think of it, the last flare-up wasn’t that long ago."

Merlin asked, puzzled, sensing something was off.

From his own calculations, the magic backlash should persist until she reached Saint-tier, with a cycle of about one month.

But it hadn’t even been a month since the last time. Such a rapid recurrence forced Merlin to suspect something.

There was likely only one explanation for this.

But it absolutely wasn’t some nonsense about Marielus seizing a body and reviving—ancient demonic texts stated there wouldn’t be major side effects. The Frost Holy Dragon was dead, and that was that.

"Have you been forcing the Inheritance Crystal’s power lately?"

Alice froze, then began to rack her brain.

But she couldn’t recall anything. The only real danger she’d faced recently was that drug-crazed Sharplen attacking her.

At the time, her will to survive had been overwhelming, then her mind went blank for an instant. When she came to, Sharplen’s arm was already frozen and shattered.

Could it be that she *had* forcibly activated the Inheritance Crystal’s power then?

Alice wasn’t sure herself. She stared at Merlin, her expression confused.

"I’m not sure either... but when you went to rescue Sherry, a Saint-tier Dark Elf ambushed me. I *did* lose control then—I froze his arm."

Merlin tilted his head, serious. "You... how dense can you be? If you force the Inheritance Crystal’s power, you won’t be human anymore. You’d become something between human and dragon—calling you a freak wouldn’t be an exaggeration."

"...That serious?!" Alice jolted, looking horrified. She didn’t want to turn into something like that.

Merlin just smiled without answering, recalling how Carolina had swallowed the Inheritance Crystal, then used Saint-tier Battle Aura to forcefully awaken draconic power—only to become grotesquely deformed, resembling the legendary Harpy.

"But once is fine. Just be careful before reaching Saint-tier. Try not to use the Inheritance Crystal’s power. The more active the dragon’s power is, the worse the backlash gets." Merlin said earnestly.

...

Alice’s face was a mask of terror, her heart still pounding. She’d have to restrain herself from now on. She didn’t want to become a monster.

Between dragon and human? What the hell was that? A little dragon girl?!

Merlin looked at the confused Alice in his arms and decided she couldn’t leave his side tonight.

Only his magic-immune physique could protect her life.

Left to her own devices, Alice wouldn’t be able to resist the Frost Holy Dragon’s magic corruption.

Merlin slightly opened the door behind him, then said to Alice:

"Come in. It’s not like we can’t share a bed tonight."

Alice’s face flushed. She craned her neck to peer past Merlin. The room was pitch black, only the flickering light on the desk visible. It seemed Merlin hadn’t been asleep when she arrived—he’d been busy with something.

If she went in now, wouldn’t that mean... doing *that*? Sleeping together, bare and entwined...

Oh God! Why did she have to do this?!

She’d never been in a relationship, had no girlfriend, had never even kissed anyone. So why was she always tangled up with Merlin, letting this bastard take every advantage while she could never fight back?

At this rate, her life would be ruined, filled with nothing but Merlin’s name. Her dream of a romance with the great swordsman Elkin would shatter into pieces.

Alice’s expression twisted in despair. She stared at Merlin’s room but didn’t step inside. The moment she left his side, the magic backlash began to stir again.

"Come in already. I’m not going to eat you..." Merlin frowned, not understanding what Alice was worried about. Did he really look like a villain to her?

Alice looked at Merlin and decided that if she stayed alert, nothing bad should happen.

And it wasn’t like she’d never shared a bed with him before. There was no need to be this nervous.

A chill swept over her. She couldn’t hesitate any longer. If she stayed too far from Merlin, she’d struggle to suppress the backlash.

"Well... since you’re sincerely inviting me, I’ll reluctantly accept~"

"Begging for my help and still acting like this? Goodbye!" Merlin said, moving to shut the door, ready to leave this pitiful girl out in the cold.

"D-Don’t... don’t do that!" Alice panicked and threw herself into Merlin’s arms, clinging tightly to him, puffing out her cheeks like a hamster mid-meal, tears glistening in her eyes. "You big jerk! Always bullying me!"

And it wasn’t Alice being oversensitive—she’d come to him in desperation, only for this bastard to toy with her. Wasn’t he just the worst?!

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue in displeasure, looking down at the sulking Alice. He helplessly twisted the corner of his mouth, sighing inwardly.

*Damn tsundere. So troublesome...*

Just as Merlin and Alice, this old married couple, were having their little "heated" exchange,

another girl was lost in anxious thoughts, unable to sleep because her father had been taken by Democritus—his fate unknown.

This was the aged tavern owner’s granddaughter: Connie.

Connie was a child who cared deeply for her family. She’d been constantly worried since her father’s abduction.

Though she was still a young girl, blooming with youth, her sense of responsibility far surpassed that of most adults.

After learning of her father’s capture, Connie was filled with despair. She had no power to rescue him, so all she could do was offer meaningless prayers each day.

Her grandfather was old and could barely manage the tavern. Her father was the true backbone of the place.

Without him, the family would fall apart, and the ancestral tavern would collapse.

For an ordinary family, losing financial support was a catastrophe.

So Connie, as a member of the family, had to find a way.

Fortunately, two groups had arrived at the tavern: the strange Lexum adventurers, and the Irish genius mage hired by the village chief—Johnson.

Comparing the two, Connie felt Johnson, the renowned Saint-tier powerhouse, was more trustworthy.

So, late at night, wearing a brown windbreaker, she went to find Johnson, hoping to ask him to look after her father when he went to take down Democritus, to ensure his safety.

But Johnson was arrogant and childish. He flatly refused:

"I’m only here to kill that alchemist. Everything else? I couldn’t care less. Don’t disturb my rest. Goodnight."

Sure enough, Saint-tier powerhouses were all eccentric, and most treated the lowly with disdain.

Rejected so harshly, Connie had no choice but to turn to Merlin for help, hoping he’d protect her father.

Connie wasn’t a foolish girl. She was good at reading people. Though Merlin looked like an Iron-rank adventurer, his companions seemed to revolve around him, obeying his every word—including a noblewoman.

Connie didn’t believe a noble would follow the orders of an Iron-rank adventurer. The other two high-tier members also seemed to listen to Merlin.

All signs pointed to Merlin being extraordinary. Even if his strength wasn’t obvious, he must have something special.

The noblewoman had even called him a hidden Saint-tier powerhouse. Maybe it was true?

So she was willing to take the gamble—ask Merlin to look after her father and bring him back safely.

Connie slowly approached, stopping in front of Merlin’s door. She stared at the room number for a long time, making no further move.

As the tavern’s manager, she knew where this group was staying. She also knew that at this late hour, Merlin was likely alone in his room—the peak of a man’s loneliness, and the perfect time to strike a deal.

It seemed Connie, despite her youth, wasn’t as naive as she appeared.

She raised her hand, bit her lip as if making a resolution, then—*knock knock knock*—rapped three times on the door.

She had steeled herself. Merlin was her last lifeline. She *had* to get him to agree.

If he refused...

Connie would have to resort to a desperate, bittersweet measure—offering her most precious possession: her virginity.

title: Chapter 17 — Sleeping Together
content:
Chapter 17 — Sleeping Together

Volume 8 · Chapter 17

In the room.

Alice stood in the middle like a pitiful hostage, her face flushed, hesitating to move. She seemed restrained, especially when her gaze fell on the large bed—her expression turned strange, her mind filled with wild thoughts.

Next, would she and Merlin have to sleep on this bed...?

Take off all their clothes and hold each other while sleeping? Damn it, why was she having such shameful fantasies?

What had come would come—she truly couldn’t escape Merlin’s clutches!

What terrible sin had she committed to deserve this endless torment...?

Alice tightly pressed her lips together, staring at the bed in silence. She felt that sleeping with Merlin was dangerous—something embarrassing was bound to happen.

But Alice had no choice now. To survive, she had to rely on Merlin, to endure and spend the night with him.

If it were just ordinary sleep, that would be fine. What she feared most was whether Merlin would lose his mind and do something shameless, like making advances.

Merlin, however, didn’t feel much at all. In fact, he wasn’t the least bit tempted.

He was far more relaxed than Alice had imagined, without a hint of mental pressure.

Merlin walked over to Alice and patted her shoulder, wearing a deeply meaningful—no, a deeply *suggestive*—smile. He said casually, “Eh?”

“Wha—?!” Alice’s eyes widened, her expression disbelief as she stared at Merlin, clearly startled. “...So direct?!”

“If I’m not direct, what do you expect? Isn’t this just to help you suppress the magic from the inheritance crystal? Or do you have other ideas?” Merlin narrowed his eyes, his expression growing even more suggestive.

“I... I, I... what ideas could I have?! Don’t just assume you know what I’m thinking, okay?!”

Alice was so nervous her words came out disjointed.

Didn’t Merlin feel even a little shame?

They were about to sleep together—how could he not be the slightest bit flustered? His calmness was infuriating.

Surely he was just used to this kind of thing! Just how many innocent women had this bastard defiled when he was the Demon Lord?!

Alice glared at Merlin with disdain, looking every bit the wronged wife, as if she held a deep grudge against his past.

“What’s that look for? Do you have a grudge against me?” Merlin said, annoyed, feeling inexplicably scorned.

“Hmph~!” Alice coldly sniffed, refusing to answer. No matter how she looked at him, Merlin seemed like a promiscuous womanizer—who knew what kind of heinous things he’d done in the past.

“Hurry up and take off your clothes.”

Merlin couldn’t be bothered to argue with Alice. He took the lead, quickly stripping off his shirt to reveal his solid upper body.

Alice covered her eyes but couldn’t resist peeking through her fingers, thinking, *Isn’t this guy being a little too eager? Such enthusiasm is definitely suspicious.*

“Hurry up. Can you stop hesitating? Didn’t you come to me? If you don’t want to, you can go deal with the inheritance crystal’s magic yourself. Then I can sleep peacefully without your washboard—”

Merlin said helplessly, growing impatient as Alice still hadn’t moved.

“Who would crush you to death?! Don’t just take the chance to insult me!” Alice retorted, her face red with anger. She thought this was her first time asking to sleep with a man, and yet the scene was so crude and unromantic—she couldn’t help feeling a little disheartened.

As a girl in the bloom of youth, Alice, like any ordinary girl, had fantasized about romance, dreaming of heart-fluttering moments with her prince on a white horse—like with the great swordsman Elgin.

Reality, however, was far from ideal. Not only was her sleeping partner not Elgin, but it was the man she despised most.

Alice felt the magic of the Ice Frost Sacred Dragon within her surging again, no longer calm.

“...Do we *have* to take off all our clothes?”

Merlin sat on the edge of the bed, looking at Alice’s restrained demeanor, and smiled. “Are you shy? It’s not like it’s the first time we’ve slept together. Why worry about this now?”

“...What are you talking about?!” Alice’s eyes widened, as if he’d struck a sensitive nerve. “Last time... last time I was unconscious, okay?! It was all *your* decision!”

“Then what are you worried about? Are you afraid I’ll do something bad to you?” Merlin narrowed his eyes, his tone heavy with implication.

“Well... that *is* part of it...” Alice didn’t evade the question but answered frankly.

“Relax. I have no interest in you that way. If it weren’t for our shared debt, I wouldn’t even bother saving you...” Merlin said indifferently. The candlelight flickered across his face, his ruby-like eyes especially dazzling.

Alice’s expression turned unnatural. Hearing Merlin’s words, she felt a pang of hurt, a wave of disappointment rising within her.

She *should* be happy he said that... but she couldn’t shake the feeling that he looked down on her. Was it because she lacked feminine charm?

“As for whether we need to take off all our clothes...” Merlin examined Alice for a moment before nodding. “No, sleepwear is fine. Something thin, though. Since the situation isn’t as bad as last time, you don’t need to strip completely.”

Alice finally let out a sigh of relief. It was good they didn’t have to be completely naked—she’d probably die of shame if they did.

Even if she was somewhat familiar with Merlin, this kind of thing was still unbearable.

Alice removed her robe, revealing a light blue nightgown.

Even if she wasn’t completely bare, it was still plenty alluring—especially since the hem was a little short, faintly revealing her underwear.

Alice furrowed her delicate brows, her face still flushed, but she was no longer as shy as before.

She tugged at the hem of her nightgown and slowly walked to the bed. Without so much as glancing at Merlin, she quickly slipped under the covers, her movements swift and decisive.

A chill swept over Alice, and she couldn’t help but poke her head out from the blankets.

“Aren’t you coming in? What are you doing out there?”

Merlin scratched his cheek, thinking that even if it wasn’t the first time they’d slept together, it still felt a little awkward.

But Merlin didn’t overthink it. He simply slipped under the covers and lay down beside Alice.

Once they were both in bed, they adjusted their positions slightly before settling into silence, each turning their backs to the other, neither willing to look back.

It didn’t seem like anything particularly exciting was happening...

The atmosphere was faintly intimate, their body heat intertwining.

Merlin’s expression was serious, silently brooding. He thought, *Is this enough?* With Alice awake and conscious, he felt strangely restricted.

Alice, meanwhile, stayed buried under the blankets, not daring to poke her head out. Her heart was racing, her face burning hot.

Another wave of cold surged through her, making her uncomfortable. Clearly, she was too far from Merlin—she needed to be held close for the suppression to work.

Alice’s expression twisted in conflict. *If I, a girl, take the initiative to hug Merlin... wouldn’t that seem like I’m seducing him?*

What should she do? It was so cold...

Alice shivered, gritting her teeth as she endured it, unwilling to speak up.

Merlin rolled his eyes. He wasn’t an idiot—he could feel the cold spreading toward him.

With no other choice, Merlin sighed and took the initiative. He turned over and wrapped his arms around Alice, pulling her into his embrace.

“Better now?”

Alice was startled, a flicker of panic crossing her face.

She hadn’t expected Merlin to suddenly make a move. His warm, large hand was now resting on her waist.

Held in Merlin’s arms, she felt protected.

His masculine presence washed over her, the warmth instantly dispelling the cold. The backlash of her magic was immediately suppressed.

Even though Alice disliked Merlin touching her like this, it was clear he meant well.

After a moment’s hesitation, Alice, her face still red, replied—

“Mmm... yeah.”

title: Chapter 18 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 18 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 18

On the large bed.

Alice turned her back to Merlin, hugging her slender body as she buried herself under the blankets, refusing to come out.

Merlin wrapped his arms around her from behind, his hands resting on her delicate waist.

Their breaths mingled, pressed closely together...

Though the situation was unavoidably intimate, the two somehow managed to stay quiet, not immediately resorting to violence.

The room was completely silent, save for the howling wind outside. The candlelight, filtered through the dim yellow glass shade, flickered, casting indistinct shadows.

Alice’s face burned crimson. Hidden under the blankets, her eyes were wide open, her expression tense—she didn’t dare breathe too loudly.

Even in Merlin’s embrace, her heart refused to settle. Her body was rigid, as if constantly on guard.

...Why didn’t this guy give me a heads-up first?

Just grabbing me like that was terrifying! I thought he was going to do something terrible!

And besides, this bastard is way too practiced at this! He didn’t even hesitate before pulling me in.

No gentlemanly grace at all—at least ask how I feel about it...

Alice fumed silently, still worried Merlin might lose his mind and do something reckless.

She secretly gathered her magic and fighting spirit beneath the covers. If Merlin dared to make a move, she’d strike back instantly.

But the moment Merlin held her, the surging backlash of magic vanished without a trace—it was surprisingly effective.

If the atmosphere weren’t so awkward, Alice might have relaxed and gone to sleep.

“...So, you touching my waist is fine, but if you dare touch anywhere else, I’m flipping the table, got it?”

Merlin, faced with Alice’s warning, could only sigh helplessly. “I won’t touch you improperly. What kind of person do you take me for? I’m the proud Overlord of Arrogance—do you really think I’d stoop to taking advantage of you?”

Alice lowered her head, face still red, and muttered under her breath, “Who knows?”

Tch. Merlin rolled his eyes, unable to resist a sarcastic jab. “You’re such a washboard. Have some self-awareness, will you? Right now, all I feel from your waist is flatness. Probably your chest is just as flat—how am I even supposed to tell the difference? And do you really think your *nonexistent* chest has any appeal to me?”

Alice’s face burned with rage. She gritted her silver teeth—she’d only been warning him, and now he was mocking her?!

“Drop dead!”

Furious, she jabbed her elbow hard into Merlin’s side to vent her frustration.

Merlin furrowed his brows, looking down at the girl in his arms. *This one’s got a temper. Flat-chested and won’t even let anyone mention it?*

“What’s with you? Who said you could mock me for being flat? You’re the one who saved me, not them!” Alice huffed, thinking that if Merlin had left her in such a miserable state and then mocked her, the emotional damage was doubled—it hurt like hell.

“...Favoritism? Why am I the exception?” Merlin felt a pang of injustice.

“Because it’s just *you* who can’t! If you mock me, you’re heartless, humph!” Alice said without hesitation, convinced that Merlin had already wronged her enough—mocking her on top of that was unforgivable.

“...Troublesome woman...” Merlin twisted his mouth, muttering to himself, not intending to argue with Alice.

After all, by now, he was used to her terrible temper.

Even if Alice was as flat as a board, Merlin had to admit—she felt pretty comfortable in his arms. Her body was soft and warm.

Especially the scent on her—it always lingered near his nose, giving him a strange sense of calm.

If this girl ever decided to act like a proper lady and stay quiet... wouldn’t she actually be a great woman?

Merlin’s old face flushed slightly. The number of girls who could get this close to him wasn’t many. Alice was one of the few who didn’t treat him with kid gloves.

Back when he was the Overlord of Arrogance, he’d had his fair share of interactions with the opposite sex—excluding Lilith, the hidden hand who’d sabotaged all his romantic prospects. There had still been a few others.

But most of them had been terrified of his identity as the Great Demon Lord, obeying his every word like mindless puppets. It was boring beyond belief.

Alice, though, was different. She fought back. She argued with him, even cursed at him.

Because they’d been on opposing sides before, she still held clear hostility toward him.

Merlin found that... not bad. At least Alice was lively, not cowering in fear.

*What the hell?*

*Am I an idiot?*

*Why do I suddenly feel like I’m developing some kind of submissive tendencies?*

A wave of clichéd drama vibes hit him square in the face...

Merlin forced himself to calm down, stopping his wandering thoughts about the washboard in his arms. If he kept this up, he’d end up in trouble.

Alice seemed to find it stuffy under the blankets, so she poked her head out, taking a few deep breaths.

Then, she side-eyed Merlin suspiciously, her voice laced with doubt. “Were you just imagining something evil in your head?”

“Are you insane? Even if I was, how would you know?” Merlin frowned, his face darkening.

“I just felt a deep, chilling malice—it gave me goosebumps. Clearly, you were thinking something wicked about me.” Alice said warily, still not trusting him.

“Why do you always assume I’m some kind of pervert?” Merlin knitted his brows, genuinely puzzled.

“Because you *are* a pervert! You’re always leering at people, and you even went to Helena’s secret room. Anyone who goes there is *not* a good person!” Alice declared with absolute certainty.

Merlin was left speechless. *I only went once, and Hobbes dragged me along—how did this become an indelible black mark on my record?*

“...And!” Alice paused, then said seriously, “You’re not allowed to hit on me, and you’re not allowed to have *ideas* about me either. I won’t let you get away with it!”

“Your baseless confidence is *so* annoying...” Merlin’s face broke out in a cold sweat, black lines forming across his forehead. *As if the great Demon Lord would ever force himself on a woman. When have I ever done something so despicable?*

“I don’t like you, okay? I’m only using you to suppress my magic backlash. So don’t you dare get any ideas about me!” Alice said with complete sincerity, as if genuinely worried their relationship might become ambiguous.

Merlin nearly burst out laughing. *This girl actually just openly admitted to using me? Normally, people at least try to hide that kind of thing.* Alice was stupid to a whole new level. If she were a villain’s ally, she’d be the ultimate useless teammate.

“I like Elgin the Great Swordsman, not you. If you have any wicked thoughts, give up now—I’ll resist with my life, humph!” Alice puffed out her cheeks, as if warning Merlin not to try anything.

“...I have no words.”

Merlin still held Alice’s slender body, but inside, he was laughing uncontrollably.

This washboard was *hilarious*.

She’d climbed into *his* bed of her own accord, yet put on the act of a chaste and virtuous woman.

Her mind was filled with thoughts of Elgin the Great Swordsman’s back, completely unaware of his *second identity*.

This idiot—*body in my camp, heart with the enemy*...

Kind of cute, though?

(...)

title: Chapter 19 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 19 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 19

Merlin looked down at Alice in his arms, feeling a little charmed by this silly girl, and couldn't help but tease her.

"What's with you? You climb into my bed of your own accord, but you're thinking of Elgin the Great Swordsman. Is that really okay?"

"...What does it matter?" Alice's face turned red as she flustered in response.

"You're such a hypocrite, openly lusting after Elgin the Great Swordsman, slamming a green hat right on someone's head..." Merlin's tone was strange, clearly teasing Alice to see her reaction.

Sure enough, Alice in Merlin's arms shifted uncomfortably, as if trying to distance herself from him.

But after a few struggles, Alice stopped resisting. Instead, she started making excuses—

"There's nothing I can do about it, is there? I don't have any other choice right now, do I?"

"Anyway, I only like Elgin the Great Swordsman. As long as... as long as I remain pure myself, then it's fine."

"And as for tonight, you're not allowed to tell anyone. We'll pretend it never happened. Keep it to yourself."

Alice's tone was firm, making her stance clear: she just wanted to suppress the backlash of the Ice Frost Holy Dragon's magic power and had no intention of getting involved with Merlin.

Merlin's eyebrows furrowed tightly. He felt inexplicably annoyed, thinking, *Isn't my own back the one I'm looking at? Why is this washboard obsessed with my back but hostile to me in person?*

Even Merlin himself didn't notice the faint, almost imperceptible twinge of jealousy in his heart, which had already begun to harbor a slight dislike for the identity of Elgin the Great Swordsman.

Anyone could understand Merlin's mood—most people would call it jealousy.

"Alice, I'll be honest with you. I am Elgin the Great Swordsman." Merlin finally said.

"Ah?!" Alice turned her head to glance at Merlin, then immediately elbowed him, huffing, "Are you trying to trick me? Do you take me for a fool? How could you possibly be Elgin the Great Swordsman? There's not a single similarity in your demeanor!"

Merlin rubbed his chest, his expression full of grievance, and said seriously, "I really am Elgin the Great Swordsman. Tell me, what about me doesn't look the part?"

"Are you just too into your role? Wake up." Alice knitted her delicate brows, not believing Merlin at all. "Don't think that just because you've pretended to be Elgin the Great Swordsman once, you're the real deal. Do you think my IQ is that low?"

Merlin was left speechless by this idiot. This was the second time he had admitted his identity, and she still didn't believe him.

Was the difference really that huge just because it was him? Did he need to maintain some kind of mystery?

Merlin's face darkened as he silently vowed that if he ever admitted his identity to Alice again, he would be the biggest idiot. Never again, absolutely never a third time!

"You? Elgin the Great Swordsman? Stop slandering him. I admit you're a little... maybe a tiny bit stronger than Elgin the Great Swordsman, but you feel like completely different people. Don't even try to fool me, humph!" Alice said against her better judgment.

Based on Merlin's usual actions, his strength wasn't just a little bit superior to Elgin the Great Swordsman's. But Alice would always side with Elgin the Great Swordsman and would never admit it.

Moreover, whenever Merlin faced Elgin the Great Swordsman, it was always an instant kill. Maybe Elgin the Great Swordsman had never used his full strength, so deep down, Alice still held a sliver of hope that Elgin the Great Swordsman might be even stronger than Merlin.

Merlin kept silent, watching Alice's agitated back and thinking to himself, *Let her keep being arrogant. When Alice finds out that Elgin the Great Swordsman is me, I'll mock her to death...*

After a series of bickering, the two finally calmed down. Their breathing echoed faintly in the small space.

Merlin remained silent, seemingly unable to sleep, perhaps because Alice in his arms was restless, constantly moving around.

Alice, with her back to Merlin, was also unable to sleep, her mind filled with chaotic thoughts.

Merlin's warmth and his unique presence made Alice's heart flutter slightly. Even in the dead of night, she couldn't calm down.

*Thump, thump, thump!*

At that quiet moment, a knock on the door startled them both.

Merlin looked toward the room's entrance, completely clueless about who would come at this late hour. It was hard to tell.

"Who is it?" Alice turned her head to look at Merlin, her heart filled with unease. It would be embarrassing if someone saw them like this.

"I don't know either..." Merlin shook his head, then threw off the blanket and got up. "I'll go check. You stay here."

Alice's brows knitted tightly. She wondered if Cecilia was worried because she hadn't returned yet, so she couldn't hold back and came to Merlin's room in the middle of the night to see what was going on.

Thinking this, Alice felt it was very possible. After all, Cecilia wasn't a bad person; she was the type who was cold on the outside but warm on the inside.

Alice quickly grabbed Merlin's wrist, stopping him from leaving, her expression hesitant as if she had something to say.

"What are you doing?" Merlin asked in surprise, turning back.

"It's probably Cecilia." Alice replied seriously.

"Are you sure?" Merlin narrowed his eyes.

"Mhm. I told her I'd be out for a while, but I haven't come back yet. She must be worried." Alice answered awkwardly.

"Oh, in that case, it's simple. I'll go tell her that you're staying here tonight and won't be going back." Merlin replied indifferently.

"No!" Alice's expression turned serious as she rejected Merlin's idea.

"Huh? What do you want then?" Merlin's brows twitched, asking impatiently.

"You tell her I'm not here, that I might have gone out to train. Tell her to go back to sleep and not to worry about me." Alice emphasized, even coming up with the lie for Merlin.

"Why say that? What's wrong with you being here?" Merlin was confused.

"Don't ask. Just answer the way I told you." Alice puffed out her cheeks, looking very displeased.

"Such a hassle..." Merlin shook off Alice's hand and walked straight to the door.

Alice, her face red, quickly hid under the blanket, covering her entire body to avoid being discovered.

The truth was, Alice was worried that Cecilia would look at her strangely. She had sworn she would never sleep with him, yet here she was, sneaking into Merlin's room in the middle of the night.

This situation—saying no with her mouth but her body being honest—was too embarrassing. Alice didn't want to be teased or mocked by Cecilia.

Merlin opened the door and saw Connie standing neatly in front of it. She looked restrained and anxious, her fingers nervously intertwined.

She was wearing a brown robe that wrapped around her slender figure, and the light makeup on her face made it clear she had prepared herself before coming.

Merlin was slightly taken aback. He hadn't expected the visitor to be Cecilia, but rather Connie, the granddaughter of the tavern owner.

Connie's face slowly turned red as she lightning-fast covered her eyes, not daring to look at Merlin. Her heart pounded wildly, unable to stop. After all, she was a girl in the throes of spring fever—how could she handle such stimulation? She couldn't even speak.

Images of Merlin's figure, which had left a deep impression on her, kept flashing through Connie's mind.

Merlin looked down at himself and felt a little embarrassed. He changed the subject and asked, "Miss Connie, what brings you here so late at night?"

Connie tried her best to calm herself, but the blush on her face wouldn't fade.

She kept her head lowered, almost burying it in her chest, looking shy and timid.

She bowed slightly and muttered in a very soft voice, "G-Good evening, Lord Merlin. I have something I'd like to ask of you..."

title: Chapter 20 — Loneliness
content:
Chapter 20 — Loneliness

Volume 8 · Chapter 20

Alice hid under the blankets, not daring to breathe, her expression tense as if she were in the middle of a guerrilla battle.

At first, Alice had thought it might be Cecilia coming to check on her out of concern, but that clearly wasn’t the case.

Alice listened carefully to the voices outside and recognized Connie, the tavern owner’s granddaughter.

This left Alice deeply puzzled—what could this girl possibly want with Merlin in the middle of the night?

Did Connie have some request? But why couldn’t it wait until morning? Why come now, at this hour?

She couldn’t believe that someone who had grown up in a tavern, dealing with so many customers, wouldn’t know basic etiquette.

Alice grew suspicious and decided not to interfere for now, choosing instead to keep observing...

"Eh?!"

Merlin froze in shock—he never expected Connie to come to him with a request at this hour.

His previous impression of Connie was that she was a shy girl who couldn’t even look people in the eye without blushing.

But now she was here in the dead of night, so it must be something important.

Merlin cleared his throat, his expression turning serious. He figured there was no harm in listening—if it was too much trouble, he’d refuse outright.

"Miss Connie, I’m curious why you’ve come to me so late at night. What kind of help do you need? At this hour, many things would be... inconvenient."

Merlin laid out his terms upfront, just in case some overly troublesome matter landed on him.

"That... Connie’s face flushed as she buried her head low, her fingers twisting nervously. "I’m very sorry, Mr. Merlin. I know coming at this hour disturbs your rest, and I feel terrible about it. But this matter is extremely important to my family, so I had no choice but to come now. I hope you can understand."

Merlin looked at Connie’s pitiful expression and felt a flicker of curiosity—what could she possibly want? He had no entanglements with her, no shared interests. There was no reason for him to engage with a complete stranger.

"I’ll leave as soon as we’re done talking. I won’t disturb your rest any longer," Connie couldn’t help but add.

Merlin furrowed his brow, scratching his head. "What’s the matter? Just say it."

"...Can I come in? It would be better to discuss this inside..." Connie muttered in a near-whisper, her face burning even redder. Since the topic might involve a "transaction," it would be safer to talk in private.

Alice’s body trembled under the blankets. Her eyes widened instantly—something felt very off.

Coming to bother Merlin at this hour was one thing, but now she wanted to enter his room?!

A lone girl, unguarded, entering a man’s room in the middle of the night...

What did that imply? Even an idiot could figure it out!

She was at least Merlin’s nominal wife, right? So entering his room wasn’t *that* strange.

But Connie and Merlin weren’t close—why should she just waltz into his room?!

Was she planning to seduce Merlin next? To stir up some... primal impulses?!

Alice thought it was entirely possible, but she couldn’t rule out that Connie might genuinely have a serious matter. For now, she could only watch and wait.

Merlin hesitated, glancing at Alice hiding under the blankets. He pondered for a moment.

Letting Connie in shouldn’t be a problem, right?

It was his room, after all. He could let anyone in if he wanted.

Even if Alice protested, it would be a futile protest—he’d just crush it with overwhelming force.

Besides, Connie had come so late to discuss something with him. He’d feel bad refusing.

And come to think of it, why was Alice still hiding under the blankets instead of coming out?

Merlin withdrew his gaze, too lazy to guess Alice’s thoughts. He simply nodded and stepped aside, clearing the doorway.

"Alright, come in..."

Alice rolled her eyes under the blankets, instantly furious. A wave of jealousy surged through her.

Damn it, Merlin, you bastard! Why let Connie in?!

So he *was* a pervert after all! Never changing, huh? Any female in sight and he just can’t resist!

Was he openly trying to cuckold her while she was still in bed?!

And letting Connie in like this—it was as if he didn’t even consider her feelings! How cruel could he be?!

Alice bit the blanket with her teeth, her face flushed with indignation. She pitifully hummed a tune of despair in her heart.

As the saying went, a mountain couldn’t have two tigers. Alice certainly wouldn’t allow another woman to spend the night in Merlin’s room.

"Excuse me..." Connie gave a slight bow and entered Merlin’s room with obvious restraint.

Merlin checked outside, saw no one, and shut the door with a loud *thud*.

Connie flinched at the sound. Being alone in a room with a man made her heart race, her entire body tense as she stood frozen in place.

"What’s there to be nervous about? Sit." Merlin gestured to the chair beside him and sat down himself.

"O-oh, okay..." Connie sat down in a fluster, keeping her head low and silent, her fingers fidgeting with her robe.

"Just say what you need. No need to hold back." Merlin tapped the table with his fingers, studying the nervous girl.

"...Okay." Connie nodded, clutching her skirt tightly. She gathered her courage and spoke. "The thing is... my father was recently captured by a bully and handed over to that evil alchemist. Now his life hangs in the balance. My grandfather and I are both worried sick. If we lose him, our family won’t be able to survive..."

Merlin frowned, a hint of annoyance rising. Connie had laid it out this far—anyone could see where this was going.

She was obviously going to ask Merlin to help rescue her father. But Merlin hated these kinds of troublesome matters—his mind and body both resisted the idea.

"Mr. Merlin, didn’t you say you’d be heading to the central island of the sea tomorrow?" Connie paused, then earnestly made her request. "So I’m begging you—please save my father and ensure his safety. I’d be endlessly grateful..."

Alice, still under the blankets, let out a silent sigh of relief. So Connie *did* have a legitimate reason. And for their group, this would be an easy task—she thought Merlin should agree.

"I refuse." Merlin’s face remained blank as he bluntly rejected her, leaving no room for negotiation.

"Eh?! Why?!" Connie hadn’t expected such a firm, unyielding refusal.

"Why...?" Merlin stroked his chin, pondering for a moment before casually smiling. "Because it’s too much trouble. I don’t want to deal with it. It’s that simple. We’re going to exterminate Democritus’s alchemists, and we’re in a hurry. It’s best not to have anything else slowing us down."

Alice knitted her brows, mentally scolding Merlin. *Don’t just casually reject a girl’s plea!* She came all this way in the middle of the night, risking danger to ask for your help! Don’t be so heartless! We could easily help her along the way! Why does he have to be so cold sometimes?!

"Mr. Merlin, I’m begging you, please save my father! I’ll reward you handsomely..." Connie’s words were sincere, her voice trembling on the verge of tears.

"Sorry, Miss Connie, but we’re quite busy ourselves. I can’t accept your request. Please leave." Merlin’s expression remained impassive as he unceremoniously dismissed her.

Connie’s fair face darkened, as if storm clouds had gathered.

She clenched her gray robe tightly, her body trembling.

It seemed that to save her father, she’d have to use her last resort...

Connie lifted her crimson-stained face, tears glistening in her eyes, and asked seriously,

"Lord Merlin... are you lonely?"

title: Chapter 21 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 21 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 21

"Eh? Lonely?"

Merlin’s mind filled with question marks. He couldn’t understand why Connie would suddenly say that.

They had just been calmly discussing the rescue, so why had she abruptly switched to a completely unrelated topic? It made no sense, and he couldn’t follow her train of thought.

Merlin narrowed his eyes, sensing something was off. He asked seriously, "…What do you mean?"

Alice, hidden under the blanket, looked shocked. Though she didn’t react too strongly, she caught the faint scent of a fox spirit and couldn’t help but feel a pang of unease.

Even though Alice wasn’t Merlin’s real wife, the situation still left a bitter taste in her mouth. She felt an inexplicable irritation, as if she were about to be cuckolded.

Connie lowered her gaze, her lips trembling as she struggled to speak. She clenched her robe tightly, her fingers digging into the fabric.

The girl had run out of options. The only thing left she could offer was her most precious possession—something she hoped would move Merlin.

As long as Merlin was a man, he *should* be interested in her. That would be more persuasive than anything else.

Spending one night with Merlin in exchange for her father’s safety… it wasn’t a bad deal.

Connie’s eyes gradually hardened as she forced back her tears, replacing them with fierce determination.

"Mr. Merlin, don’t you understand what I mean?"

"Hm? What do you want?" Merlin studied Connie, his guard rising.

Connie lowered her head, her face flushed crimson as she bit her lip. The front of her robe was already wrinkled from her grip.

Her slender body trembled slightly, as if she were gathering her courage to launch a very "passionate" assault.

After steadying herself, Connie spoke in a deliberately calm voice, slowly and clearly.

"If… if Mr. Merlin is willing to help me save my father, I… I’m willing to provide… some *special* services…"

Alice nearly screamed from under the blanket. Connie’s words left her utterly stunned.

So much for coming in the middle of the night with good intentions—this was proof!

*Special services?*
The only services she could think of were *not* good ones!

Wasn’t the only issue that Merlin refused to save her father?
Why would she think to use her body to make him comply?

Silly girl, wake up! Merlin is a demon—he puts profit first. He wouldn’t care about something like this!

And besides, if she wanted help, why not come to *me*? I would’ve agreed to save her father…

Alice grumbled to herself, convinced Connie was acting like a vixen, seducing her *nominal* husband. How shameless!

"Ah! ?" Merlin realized what was happening and quickly said, "Sorry, I don’t need any special services. If Miss Connie has nothing else, please leave."

"Doesn’t Mr. Merlin feel lonely by himself?" Connie replied in a fluster, clutching her chest as she whispered, "If Mr. Merlin wants… I’ll do my best to satisfy you, to make you feel… pleasure and comfort…"

Merlin’s eye twitched, and he broke out in a cold sweat. *What the hell?* Why did girls keep trying to throw themselves at him? Did he really look like a stud horse or something?!

Alice was so furious her lungs felt like they might explode. This blatant seduction was disgusting! She wasn’t dead yet! The Adventurers Guild certificate clearly stated she was Merlin’s wife—did she look that easy to bully?!

Without hesitation, Connie untied the thin cords of her gray robe and flung it open, revealing the alluring figure beneath.

Clearly, she had come prepared, wearing lingerie far too mature for her age.

Her body was slender, but her chest was impressively full, practically spilling out.

A white lace bra lifted her proud breasts, creating a deep, enticing cleavage that seemed ready to burst free at any moment.

Pure white stockings clung to her legs, the lace tops blending seamlessly, giving them an elastic, supple look.

A sheer veil draped over her body added a hazy, dreamlike allure, making it impossible to see through completely.

Pale skin, ample chest, long legs and neck—everything about her was intoxicating!

"WTF?!" Merlin’s eyebrows twisted together. He was completely stunned. *This is lingerie!* She’d actually come wearing lingerie—she’d clearly had impure intentions from the start!

"Mr. Merlin—"

Connie threw herself at Merlin, clinging tightly to him, her face red as she pleaded, "Mr. Merlin, please, save my father! I’ll do anything you ask!"

"N-no, no, no—" Merlin pushed her back, flustered. "Miss Connie, calm down! Don’t do this! We genuinely don’t have the time to save your father. If we did, we’d try…"

"I won’t give up! Mr. Merlin, please, just say you’ll do it!" Connie pressed her body against him, her desperate actions making it impossible to look away. "I can’t think of any other way to save my father. Please…"

Merlin was forced back step by step until he was cornered. It wasn’t that he was afraid of Connie or couldn’t handle her—it was that no man knew how to reject a woman who was this determined to… *mate*.

If he hit her, that would be far too ungentlemanly.

If he went along with it… well, Merlin simply wasn’t interested in Connie. He didn’t want to get tangled up in some inexplicable relationship with this girl.

As a result, Merlin was stuck, unable to think of a good way to get rid of her.

Truthfully, Connie’s body *was* hot. Her face might not compare to Alice’s, but she had a great pair of assets.

The moment she pressed against Merlin, her chest flattened into a pancake shape, the sensation indescribable.

And her silk-stockinged legs weren’t idle either—they kept rubbing against him, making the hairs on his skin stand on end.

Here was Merlin, the mighty First Great Demon Lord, reduced to a passive, flustered mess, his hands raised as if to ward off any misunderstandings. He felt like he was the one carrying the ball in a game of *ball tag*!

He was at his wit’s end. Back in the day, whenever noblewomen or lonely older sisters came to him at night, it always ended up like this. Even if he did nothing, the moment he stepped out that door, he’d be labeled a "gigolo," a "playboy," a "male escort"—no matter how innocent he was.

"Mr. Merlin… please, don’t hold back. My body… do with it as you… as you please!" Connie hesitated, her face burning as she stammered, "To be honest… I’m still a virgin. If my body can satisfy you, I’d consider it an… an honor…"

Merlin was left speechless, his eyes wide with embarrassment. Then he remembered—Alice was *still in the room*.

*Come help me out here!* Was she just going to sit back and watch the show?!

Wait—why not use Alice as a shield?

A sudden idea struck him. Merlin put on a serious expression and said to Connie, "Miss Connie, I’m sorry, but I’m already married. You know that, right? The Adventurers Guild certificate makes it clear."

"It’s fine… I won’t tell anyone. I’ll forget everything that happens tonight. I swear I won’t interfere with you and Miss Alice’s relationship. Just… pretend this was all a dream."

Connie spoke timidly, aware of how shameless she was being—she was essentially trying to break up a marriage. But she had no choice. It was all for her father.

"EXM?!!" Merlin’s expression was one of sheer disbelief as he watched Connie rise onto her toes, clearly about to kiss him.

Finally, Alice couldn’t take it anymore. She had been watching the whole thing through a gap in the blanket.

And Merlin hadn’t just failed to handle the situation—he’d made it *worse*!

*Unbelievable!* She wasn’t dead yet!

How dare she do this right in front of her, in *her* own bed?! This was outrageous!

With a swift motion, Alice threw off the blanket and sat up in bed, wearing nothing but a thin nightgown.

"*Ahem!*" She coughed loudly to get their attention, then gave Merlin a tight, insincere smile.

"…Darling, what *exactly* are you two doing?"

title: Chapter 22 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 22 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 8 · Chapter 22

"Pfft!"

Merlin spat out his drink the moment he heard the word "dear," his expression twisting into something indescribably complicated—

*What the hell?! Alice is going all out, even calling me "dear" now?*

Why didn’t she show up earlier? Why wait until now?

If she had come out sooner, none of this would’ve happened!

The situation was… awkward. This was some next-level drama—original wife catching the mistress in the act. What even was this?

Merlin clapped a hand over his darkened face, choosing to go offline temporarily to dodge the storm.

"Eh?! Alice… Miss Alice… how… how are you here?!"

The moment Connie saw Alice, her shocked expression froze on her face. She had never expected Alice to be here.

As the tavern manager, Connie had already checked the lodging records. Alice was sharing a room with Cecilia, while Merlin had his own.

If she hadn’t known the inside story, Connie never would’ve dared to come alone in the middle of the night to find Merlin, let alone consider the idea of… physical compensation.

But now, here she was—caught red-handed seducing someone else’s husband. No explanation could justify this.

And her current appearance… it was far too suggestive, like some cheap tavern girl.

Her mind went blank. Had she even remembered why she came here?

Shame and sorrow crashed over her like a wave, suffocating her.

Connie’s face flushed red, then darkened to an eggplant purple. She bit her lip, tears welling in her eyes, feeling utterly wronged, too humiliated to lift her head.

The way the two of them were entangled was… unbearable to look at. Calling it indecent would be an understatement—this was the kind of scene that would get you arrested in a vice raid.

Connie was practically straddling Merlin, her arms wrapped around his neck. Her soft, boneless body pressed tightly against him. And the way her chest was flattened against him… that was the most scandalous part.

The atmosphere was no longer just awkward—it was frozen solid. The moment Alice burst in, everything stopped, as if time itself had been hit with *The World!*

Alice’s heart shattered into a million pieces at the sight of Merlin and Connie. The vinegar in her veins was so thick it was hard to breathe.

She hadn’t wanted to come out at all—her clothes were a mess, and she was afraid of making the scene even more awkward. But Connie had gone too far, getting more and more aggressive.

Merlin had already said he was married, yet Connie still wouldn’t back off? She even wanted to take things further—unforgivable!

Even if their marriage was just in name, Alice was still Merlin’s wife on paper. Shouldn’t she at least get basic respect? How dare some vixen try to *cuck* her in front of her face?! Was her presence that insignificant?

Alice would *never* allow this. She’d die before wearing that humiliating green hat!

"Dearest, stop playing dead. Give me a 360° breakdown—what kind of textbook position is this? Why have I never seen it before?"

Alice straightened her posture, looking every bit the refined young lady, her back ramrod straight.

She wore a thin, light blue nightgown that faintly revealed her slender figure. Even if Alice was a bit… flat, it didn’t detract from her beauty.

The only flaw was that the nightgown was a little short, failing to cover the white panties beneath—printed with little bears, giving off a childish vibe~

She swept her silver hair back with her hand, letting it cascade down, shimmering under the starlight from the window. For a moment, she looked like a galaxy brought to life.

Truthfully, Alice just wanted to silently flex, showcasing her charm to outshine Connie and make her feel inferior.

Women were strange creatures like that—best friends behind closed doors, but the moment a man was involved, they’d turn into ruthless rivals in a battle of allure.

Sure enough, once Connie regained her senses, she felt her own beauty paled in comparison to Alice’s. It was like a little girl standing before a mature, elegant woman—completely outmatched!

Connie quickly scrambled off Merlin, snatching up her gray robe from the floor to cover her exposed body.

"Cough!" Merlin cleared his throat, masking his embarrassment. "To my dear wife, as you can see, Miss Connie came to my room in the middle of the night for a… *wrestling* match. But I think this is all a misunderstanding. Don’t take it to heart…"

"Uh…"

Alice flinched at the words "dear wife," her body trembling. She nearly lost her composed demeanor.

This pervert! How dare he take advantage of the situation like this?! So shameless!

But this was all part of the act. She wouldn’t refute it—for now, she’d begrudgingly accept the title.

Regaining her composure, Alice feigned innocence. "Wrestling? That sounds fun! Can I join too?"

"Uh… that might not be a good idea," Merlin said, his expression unnatural. *Wrestling together? That’d be way too…*

"Then what about Connie? Can I join you two for wrestling?" Alice turned to Connie, her words deceptively polite.

Connie was no fool—she understood Alice was giving her an out, a chance to leave.

Flushing, Connie gave a slight bow, her voice apologetic. "S-Sorry, Miss Alice, for disturbing your rest. I… I have other matters to attend to. Goodnight."

Before the words were even out of her mouth, Connie bolted from Merlin’s room like she was fleeing for her life, not daring to look back, leaving the two of them in disarray.

Silence returned to the room. The little incident had left both of them uncomfortable.

"Phew~" Merlin exhaled, shrugging. "Didn’t expect something like this to happen. Alice, what do you think?"

"Hmph~!"

Alice shot Merlin a furious glare, then rolled over and buried herself under the blankets, clearly intending to sleep in a huff.

"Eh?!" Merlin blinked, flustered. "Hey, hey, hey—what did I do? Why are you suddenly mad at me?"

"Heartless! Always flirting with other women and causing trouble for me!" Alice muffled from under the covers.

"We’re not *really* married, so why are you even upset?" Merlin smirked, tilting his head.

"Not… not *really* married, but we *are* in name! Your flirting damages *my* reputation!" Alice huffed, as if she could come up with a million excuses.

"Uh…" Merlin found the reasoning flimsy, but he couldn’t exactly reject it. "Connie’s visit was a sudden situation. I had no idea what she was even doing here!"

"Are you *stupid*?! What does a girl come to a man’s room for in the middle of the night?! Use your brain!" Alice snapped, exasperated.

"Aren’t *you* here in the middle of the night too? And we’re getting along just fine," Merlin said, spreading his hands.

"I…" Alice was left speechless, forced to scramble for another excuse. "It’s different with me! When Miss Connie came, you should’ve rejected her! Why’d you let her in, and then… *hugging and holding* each other shamelessly?! You *are* a pervert! Disgusting!"

"Eh?! It’s *my* fault?!" Merlin pointed at himself, dumbfounded. "She’s the one who pounced on me! What does that have to do with me?!"

"You *must* have had impure thoughts, which is why you didn’t reject her right away." Alice concluded, then added, "Shut up. I don’t want to argue. Sleep!"

Merlin’s forehead dripped with three black lines. *I did reject her, but it didn’t work!* Women were such troublesome creatures—so much drama, and no logic!

After venting internally, Merlin felt sleep creeping in. He slipped under the covers, intending to continue sharing the bed with Alice.

But not long after, Alice kicked him off the bed with one swift motion. *Thud.* He crashed onto the floor.

"Y-You… what was that for?! Mutiny?!"

"Don’t touch me! Go find those fox spirits outside!" Alice’s voice was laced with sourness and displeasure, still dwelling on what had happened.

"But… I need to help suppress your backlashing magic!" Merlin frowned.

"It’s already much better. I don’t need you anymore!" Alice muttered from under the blankets, her mouth firing off complaints. "Tonight, you sleep on the floor! Not allowed on my bed! Reflect on your actions!"

"Meow?!" Merlin’s brows knitted together, a cold sweat sliding down his temple—

*Wait, this is* my *bed, isn’t it?*

Why was *he*, the original occupant, being kicked out?

Had Alice gotten *way* too into character, actually believing she was his wife?!

(??ω?? ?)

title: Chapter 23 — Prelude
content:
Chapter 23 — Prelude

Volume 8 · Chapter 23

The next day

Merlin and Alice woke up, and the two of them came out of the room together.

They both looked a little exhausted, as if they had been through an all-night battle.

Though no actual fighting had taken place, last night’s situation had been more or less the same.

The married couple had argued almost the entire night, verbally attacking each other with every old grievance they could dig up.

In the end, probably because they were both too tired, they had somehow fallen asleep in a daze.

As a result, when they got up in the morning, Merlin and Alice were both sporting heavy dark circles under their eyes—proof of how "fierce" last night’s "battle" had been.

As soon as the two stepped outside, Keith and Cecilia were already waiting for them, ready to set off at the crack of dawn to the central island of the sea.

Cecilia had known exactly where this little vixen had spent the night the moment Alice didn’t come back. Where else could she have gone but Merlin’s place?

Cecilia wasn’t stupid. She knew full well what Alice had been doing with Merlin in the middle of the night—alone together, hehehe~

So Cecilia hadn’t been so tactless as to go looking for Alice. What if she interrupted something good? That would’ve been rude.

And sure enough, just as Cecilia had expected, Alice had spent a very "pleasurable (♂♀)" night with Merlin.

But the sight still surprised her a little. Merlin and Alice both had such heavy dark circles under their eyes—

Good heavens! They even have dark circles!

Just how wild had they been last night?

It was obvious they had been "battling (♂♀)" all night long!

Even if they were deeply in love, they shouldn’t go without rest for a whole night! That kind of thing needed moderation!

Wait! Merlin’s face wasn’t just dark under the eyes—he looked a bit haggard too…

No way! Was Alice really that ferocious?!

They were husband and wife! She should at least show a little consideration for Merlin!

This kind of relentless demand was practically draining him dry to death!

Cecilia’s expression turned unnatural. Her delicate body trembled as she stared at Alice, her gaze shifting strangely.

Merlin and Alice ran into Keith and Cecilia the moment they stepped out in the morning, and both looked a little awkward.

For a moment, neither knew what to say. It would probably be hard to explain anyway.

Alice even shrank back behind Merlin.

She had thought that getting up early might let her avoid Keith and Cecilia.

But who would’ve thought those two had woken up even earlier and were already waiting outside the door—

This was bad. What now?

She and Merlin had come out of the room together.

If she said nothing happened last night, would they believe her?

As if! In Cecilia’s eyes, she was probably already a desperate, meat-hungry woman who had snuck over to Merlin’s room in the dead of night for satisfaction!

Alice’s face darkened. She pressed a hand to her forehead, silent, wishing she could find a cellar to crawl into.

Merlin’s eyes darted around as he forced a laugh. “Yo, Keith, you two are up early!”

“Good morning, Lord Merlin…” Keith gave a slight bow to show his respect. “Did you sleep well last night?”

“Uh… it was… fine…” Merlin scratched his cheek and replied faintly.

“Must’ve been great, right? I’m sure it was a night of physical and mental satisfaction…” Keith kept a straight face as he spoke with heavy implication.

Alice’s face flushed red. Sensitive as she was, she instantly caught the double meaning in Keith’s words—he was clearly teasing them.

“Do you even need to ask? Just look at how radiant Miss Alice is—she must’ve had a very pleasant night~!” Cecilia couldn’t resist chiming in with a mocking remark, her eyes narrowing into slits as she smiled.

“Y-you… you you you… what are you implying?! Don’t look down on me! Nothing happened last night! Stop talking in riddles!” Alice, face burning, retorted emotionally.

“What a weak excuse~” Cecilia covered her mouth, looking at Alice with disdain. “You rushed out in such a hurry last night and didn’t come back all night. I knew you’d gone to Lord Merlin. I remember someone swore they’d never share a room with Lord Merlin, but oh ho ho, turns out you’re all talk but no action, huh?”

“N-nonsense! Who’s all talk?! I… I just had a little trouble last night, that’s all!” Alice refused to admit it, glaring at Cecilia with hostility.

“Pfft~! Who’d believe that?” Cecilia scoffed. “Look at how exhausted Lord Merlin is. Just how desperate are you? Don’t you know we’re going to subdue the alchemist today? And yet you’re still so insatiable. What if Lord Merlin can’t focus in battle? Can you take responsibility for that?”

“Ptooey!” Merlin spat out a mouthful of old blood, thinking to himself: Do I really look like someone who’s overindulged? I just didn’t sleep well, that’s all…

“In-insatiable?! I… I’ll fight you for this!” Alice, humiliated and furious, immediately gripped the slender sword at her waist.

“Calm down…” Merlin blocked Alice and awkwardly said, “There’s nothing between us. We just argued all night. Don’t jump to conclusions…”

“I and Miss Alice have been waiting outside for a long time,” Keith paused before adding, “So it’s hard for us to believe that arguing could leave you looking like this…”

“Tch!” A cold sweat rolled down Merlin’s forehead as he thought awkwardly—

These two…

Were getting a little too nosy with their gossip, weren’t they?

?

The carriage was already prepared outside.

Alice went alone to the inn’s counter to pay the bill.

The other three had already boarded the carriage outside, ready to head for the coast.

According to the plan, a Rose family merchant ship was already waiting for them there.

The distance to the shore of the Duforl Strait wasn’t too far—it looked like it would take a few hours to get there.

Connie, seeing Alice approach, immediately panicked. She kept her head down, not daring to look at her.

Recalling the events of last night, Connie felt extremely embarrassed and didn’t want to remember any of it.

She had actually dressed up like *that* and tried to seduce someone else’s husband in the nude.

No matter how she thought about it, she was a bad girl, undeserving of sympathy or forgiveness.

Originally, she had wanted to ask for help to save her father, but after being caught in the act, she was now too ashamed to bring it up.

Connie stood nervously, stiffly in place, clutching her apron and not daring to speak freely.

Alice stopped in front of Connie, also feeling awkward. She didn’t have a good impression of Connie.

She always felt that this girl, young as she was, had too much scheming in her.

To think of using her body to seduce Merlin to achieve her goal—this was what Alice disliked most about Connie. In her mind, she had already lumped her in with vixens.

Still, for the sake of saving her father, choosing such an extreme method… Alice did feel a little sympathy.

“Three rooms.” Alice said coolly.

“S-six… six silver coins…” Connie stammered, her face red as she refused to lift her head.

Alice tossed six silver coins onto the counter, then casually said—

“I heard your father was taken away last night?”

“We’re heading to the island now. If we’re lucky, we might run into your father.”

“I’ll personally make sure to look out for him…”

title: Chapter 24 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 24 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 24

Connie stood frozen in place, her expression stiff on her face, utterly bewildered by Alice’s offhand remark.

She had done something truly outrageous last night—yet Alice was actually willing to help her rescue her father, despite everything? This left Connie completely at a loss, and she couldn’t help but feel that Alice was a good person.

Normally, people would at least resort to violence when dealing with a fox spirit. But Alice was entirely different—she seemed exceptionally tolerant.

Comparing herself to Alice, Connie suddenly felt ashamed. The gap between them was enormous.

No wonder Mr. Merlin had refused her no matter what last night. Turns out, he already had such a wonderful wife at home. It made sense that he wouldn’t accept her.

Compared to Miss Alice, she was far too immature...

Connie silently reflected to herself, then widened her eyes and asked seriously, “Miss Alice, y-you... you’re not joking, are you?”

“No, we really are in a hurry and can’t afford any delays, but I’m willing to help you personally.” Alice said calmly. Though last night’s awkward incident had happened, she had no intention of blaming the girl. Maybe she hadn’t had a choice either?

“Th-then you’d be doing me a huge favor. Thank you, Miss Alice...” Connie’s expression was conflicted, her words stumbling. “I don’t even know how to repay you.”

“There’s no need for repayment. It’s just a small effort on my part.” Alice paused, then added, “And don’t get your hopes up too much. If your father has already been killed, there’s nothing I can do.”

“I understand that.” Connie pressed a hand to her chest, her expression turning melancholic. “If we can save my father, that’s the best outcome. If not... then it’s just fate, I suppose.”

“Then—” Alice turned and started walking away without looking back.

Connie watched Alice’s retreating figure, sensing she was still angry—her words had been so cold.

But all Connie could do was apologize. She couldn’t do anything else.

Alice suddenly stopped in her tracks, as if remembering something. She turned back and said indifferently, “Oh, before I go, there’s something I want to tell you.”

“Even in despair, never betray yourself. That’s the most pathetic thing you can do.”

---

Inside the luxurious carriage,

Four people gathered to discuss their next steps.

“Regarding the ship, everything is ready. As agreed, our Rose family’s merchant vessel is already waiting offshore.” Kael gave a brief introduction.

“Just make sure it’s not a ship from an important trade route. If Father finds out, I’ll be locked up again when I return.” Cecilia said worriedly.

“Don’t worry, Lady Cecilia. The ship we’ve arranged is quite inconspicuous. The Duke won’t notice a thing.” Kael said confidently. Besides his duties as a bodyguard, he occasionally acted as Cecilia’s secretary—truly an all-purpose lapdog.

“Which ship is it?” Cecilia furrowed her delicate brows. She hadn’t been involved in the arrangements, so she didn’t know the details.

“It’s the William, which we acquired from the Mediterranean not long ago.” Kael patiently replied.

“The William?” Cecilia blinked, seemingly unaware she even owned such an asset.

“Captain Dennis commands the William. Before the Rose family acquired it, he was running a coffee smuggling operation in the Mediterranean. After the acquisition, he’s been transporting Swedish herring cans.” Kael paused, then continued seriously, “Since Captain Dennis hasn’t been with the Rose family for long and is still handling remote trade routes, Lady Cecilia can rest assured. The Duke definitely won’t realize he’s missing his monthly supply of herring cans.”

“That’s good.” Cecilia nodded in relief.

“This William isn’t just any merchant ship—it’s more like a warship disguised as one.” Kael added with a smile.

“Why?” Merlin asked curiously.

“Before, the William operated in the Mediterranean, which, like the Caribbean, is infested with pirates. To protect itself, the ship is equipped with twenty high-quality cannons and one powerful magic cannon. Its firepower rivals that of a royal navy warship. I think it should be more than enough to handle any dangers we encounter at sea.” Kael stroked his chin thoughtfully as he answered.

“I see. This trip sounds like it’ll be a breeze.” Merlin nodded, thinking that if they didn’t have to exert themselves, that was for the best. Stable, energy-saving mode—edge OB.

“Will we reach the island today?” Alice was more concerned about time.

“If everything goes smoothly, we should arrive by tonight.” Kael unfolded a map, placing it in front of everyone, and pointed. “Once we reach the coast, we’ll be in the Dover Strait between the Britannic Empire and France. The destination island is southeast of Great Britain. With Captain Dennis at the helm, we won’t be slow.”

Alice felt slightly reassured. With Connie’s matter still weighing on her, the faster they moved, the better.

Though she appeared cold, Alice had always been kind-hearted. That habit was probably unchangeable.

“Speaking of which, did any of you see that brat Johnson this morning?” Merlin narrowed his eyes. That insufferable, self-proclaimed genius mage seemed to have vanished—he hadn’t been seen all morning.

“No.”

Kael and Cecilia shook their heads.

“Right, where *is* Johnson? He didn’t leave before us, did he?” Alice looked worried.

“Probably not. Lady Cecilia and I were the first ones up, and we didn’t see him.” Kael answered seriously.

“Hmph!” Cecilia let out a cold snort, her tone lukewarm. “He’s just a kid. Kids always sleep in. He doesn’t understand that the early bird catches the worm.”

Alice knit her brows, sensing that Johnson’s sudden disappearance was no simple matter. Could he have already left ahead of them?

Merlin, however, remained expressionless, seemingly unbothered by Johnson’s absence. Instead, he thought to himself:

That directionally challenged brat—can he even find the right place?

---

Behind the luxurious carriage,

A brown steed followed closely, ridden by a youth with a hint of immaturity—none other than Johnson himself.

Just because I’m directionally challenged doesn’t mean I’m stupid.

And for a genius, being directionally challenged is just an unnecessary trait!

Johnson gripped the reins tightly, his eyes burning with intensity as he fixed his gaze on Merlin’s carriage. A reckless grin spread across his face.

I suspected those two Reksum thugs with their beady adventurer eyes were no good.

Sure enough, as I thought—they’re all after the alchemist on the island.

But too bad. That’s *my* prey. I won’t let anyone else lay a finger on it!

Even if these guys are my competitors, I still have to thank them for leading the way. Heh heh heh...
