title: Chapter 25 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 25 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 8 · Chapter 25

The carriage slowly came to a halt.

Merlin and his party disembarked directly.

The scenery before them was already vastly different—no longer the slightly desolate fishing village, but a dense cluster of bizarrely shaped reefs and an endless, horizon-blurring sea.

A few white clouds hung in the distant sky, while towering waves crashed against the shore, pounding the reefs with a thunderous roar.

The howling wind whipped past their ears, making it difficult to hear anything clearly.

Not far away, a merchant ship painted white, bearing the flags of the British Empire and the Rose Family, was docked there.

Though it appeared harmless at first glance, the twenty ominous cannons mounted on deck betrayed its true nature.

Most striking was the massive silver cannon on board, its rear fitted with a charged magic crystal—undoubtedly the rumored magical cannon.

The magical cannon was inscribed with arcane runes and powered by magic crystals, which could store energy cast by mages, allowing for two or three uses. The crystals were extremely expensive.

As for the cannon’s power, it depended on the quality of the magic crystal. If it contained Saint-tier magic, the cannon’s might could rival Saint-tier spells.

It was impressive that a non-military figure like Captain Dennis could equip his merchant ship with such a weapon to deter pirates. Clearly, this Captain Dennis was no ordinary man.

The four of them stepped off the carriage and looked around.

"Where are they? Why hasn’t anyone come to greet us?" Cecilia had never encountered such a situation before. Usually, servants would be waiting eagerly for her arrival.

"There they are!" Kael pointed toward the merchant ship in the distance.

Merlin and Alice followed his gaze. Beneath the *William*, a small wooden boat was slowly approaching, unhurried.

Since the shore was lined with reefs, the *William* couldn’t dock directly, so a small boat had to be sent to fetch Merlin’s party.

On the small boat, a well-built sailor in fine clothing rowed vigorously. At the bow stood a man full of vigor—undoubtedly Captain Dennis.

Captain Dennis was an older man, his temples streaked with white, but his full beard was well-groomed, exuding refinement rather than roughness. He wore an impeccably tailored coat with a pristine inner lining, giving him an air of sophistication.

On his head was a slightly worn captain’s hat, mismatched with his attire, as if it held sentimental value.

Despite his age, Captain Dennis carried himself with an imposing presence. His sharp features and hawk-like blue eyes seemed to be forever scanning the horizon.

"Honestly, he’s just a servant, and he dares to put on airs?" Cecilia’s expression soured slightly. She resented that Captain Dennis hadn’t come to greet her immediately.

In the past, servants would have rushed to fawn over her. Today, she’d encountered an oddball, and the contrast left her deeply unsettled.

"Putting on airs... isn’t that a bit of a stretch?" Kael said awkwardly, a bead of sweat sliding down his forehead.

"This Dennis should have come to welcome me earlier, not arrive now in a slow little boat." Cecilia spoke seriously. As a noble, she took hierarchical etiquette very seriously.

"Lady Cecilia, Captain Dennis is a seasoned sailor with considerable talent. Before joining the Rose Family, he served as a naval commander for the Kingdom of Spain. He’s only been with the family for a short time, so he hasn’t yet earned the Duke’s full trust. He has every reason to be proud. You should endure this for now—after all, we need his help." Kael, fearing Cecilia might throw a noble tantrum, did his best to persuade her gently.

"I know that already, I don’t need you to teach me!" Cecilia huffed, glaring at Kael. "Disrespecting me is one thing, but disrespecting Lord Merlin is unforgivable. I’ll tolerate it this time, but if it happens again, I’ll have this old man expelled from the Rose Family and sent back to his Mediterranean homeland!"

"Er..." Kael’s face flushed with embarrassment. He didn’t dare contradict her, only nodding repeatedly. "Yes, yes, you’re absolutely right, my lady..."

Merlin shot Cecilia a displeased glance. *This isn’t about giving me face—she’s just using me as a shield.*

Alice shook her head and muttered under her breath, "A total black-hearted..."

Merlin’s expression turned unnatural. He stayed silent, ignoring Alice’s sarcasm.

The small boat reached the shore. Dennis leapt off, his black military boots splashing through the shallow water along the reefs as he strode toward Merlin’s party.

As he drew closer, Merlin noticed a scar on Dennis’s face. The man radiated a sharp, military aura—Kael hadn’t been exaggerating; this guy had indeed been a soldier.

Though aged, Dennis moved with steady steps. He approached Cecilia, then, right in front of her, put on his white gloves.

He placed his left hand over his right chest, removed his old captain’s hat with his right, and gave a slight bow—a perfectly executed salute.

"Greetings, radiant Lady Cecilia. My apologies for not welcoming you sooner. Please forgive my rudeness."

"It’s fine. The wait wasn’t too long..." Cecilia replied coldly, clearly still displeased.

"Ah, my friend Kael! I knew you’d come. It’s been a year since our last drink together." Dennis gave Kael a bear hug without the slightest hesitation, ignoring everyone else.

"Dennis, thank you for bringing the ship here." Kael’s expression was awkward as he caught Cecilia’s disapproving glare.

"If it’s your request, I’d sail from the Arctic Ocean to be here by nightfall." Dennis returned to normal, speaking only to Kael.

Merlin observed Dennis and Kael. It was clear they were friends, though the age gap suggested a bond between generations—perhaps a friendship that defied years.

Cecilia’s face darkened. She hadn’t expected Dennis to disregard her, a noble lady, treating her as an afterthought while prioritizing Kael. She seethed internally.

But the circumstances were special. Cecilia had to endure it—for the greater good.

Dennis glanced at Merlin and Alice, nodding in acknowledgment. These two must be part of the group.

"Yes, Lord Merlin and Lady Alice." Kael introduced them warmly.

"Pleased to meet you." Alice gave a small nod.

Merlin remained expressionless, offering no reaction.

Dennis froze for a moment. His good friend had addressed Merlin as "Lord," with clear respect—so he must be someone of note.

But when Dennis noticed the iron Adventurers Guild emblem around Merlin’s neck, he was stunned. How could a low-ranked adventurer command such respect from Kael?

Though puzzled, Dennis didn’t show it. Instead, he waved a hand and put his captain’s hat back on.

"Time is of the essence. Let’s board the ship."

Cecilia’s dissatisfaction grew. She felt as though Dennis was the one in charge, reducing her to a mere servant, devoid of the respect she deserved.

Spoiled by her upbringing, she itched to put Dennis in his place. But before she could act, someone else appeared.

"Where are you all headed? To the island in the middle of the strait?" The so-called genius mage, Johnson, suddenly stepped forward, rubbing his nose. "As it happens, I need to go there too..."

"Mind if I hitch a ride on your big ship? Heh heh~"

title: Chapter 26 — Fairness
content:
Chapter 26 — Fairness

Volume 8 · Chapter 26

Hearing such a childish voice, Merlin the traveler was surprised and turned around.

Johnsson stood behind them with his hands on his hips, looking extremely composed. "Is it really that surprising to see me? You don’t seem very welcoming~"

Merlin stroked his chin, puzzled. How did this brat get here? Did he follow their carriage the whole time? No wonder this directionally challenged guy found the place—turns out their group had unknowingly led him here.

Alice furrowed her brows. So he *did* follow them. This would make their mission much harder. They had to take down that alchemist first and rescue the kidnapped fishermen. Things were getting a little complicated.

As for Cecilia and Kail, their expressions were far from pleasant. They too felt the pressure. They had assumed Johnsson wouldn’t be able to keep up, giving them a huge advantage, but reality had just slapped them in the face.

After all, Cecilia had prepared for this for a long time. She didn’t want any mistakes to ruin everything—if all her efforts went to waste, that would be disastrous.

"You all woke up so early just to try and ditch me. How unfortunate for you. I already thought you were acting suspicious, so I’ve been secretly following behind you this whole time. Aren’t you *so* surprised right now?" Johnsson smirked, his lips curling into a smug grin.

"Is this person part of your group?" Dennis, seemingly unaware of the situation, asked curiously.

"No, no, no. This guy’s here to ruin our plans," Kail said seriously, as if afraid Dennis wouldn’t be able to tell friend from foe.

"Oh..." Dennis glanced at Johnsson, surprised by the Mithril Adventurer’s badge on his chest. He hadn’t expected such a young Mithril-rank powerhouse.

"Ruin *your* plans? I think you’ve got it backward, old man. It’s *you* who came to ruin *my* good time. You want to steal my prey. As expected, adults are all the same—no good, always scheming." Johnsson didn’t hold back, sneering.

"Scheming is a bit much, don’t you think?" Cecilia knitted her delicate brows, annoyed. "We were never on the same side to begin with. We just happen to have the same goal. If that’s the case, then let’s compete fairly. Everyone relies on their own strength."

"Fair competition? You’re right, Auntie. I *love* fair competition—where I crush my opponents with overwhelming power and make them realize just how weak they are." Johnsson spread his hands, his red earrings swaying slightly.

"Don’t call me Auntie, you little brat!" Cecilia gritted her teeth, brimming with hostility.

Alice shot Cecilia a sympathetic look. *So he called her Auntie too, huh? Sorry, but being young really does let you get away with anything.*

"Since we’re competing fairly, let’s be open about it. I’ll lay it all out first..." Johnsson raised his thumb, then dramatically pointed at himself. "Having me as your opponent is your misfortune. I’m the universally acclaimed magic prodigy, a Saint-tier powerhouse at just 14 years old. I’ve *never* lost a duel, and you’ll all become my defeated underlings. Compared to my past opponents... you’re all *pathetic* weaklings~"

Merlin’s face darkened, his brows furrowing. *This kid may be young, but his arrogance is off the charts. What do I do? I’m struggling to resist the urge to beat up this little punk.*

"As for that alchemist, Democritus? To be honest, I could kill him with a single Fireball. No pressure at all~" Johnsson shook his head, looking completely at ease.

Alice felt a pang of worry. From all the rumors, Johnsson wasn’t just a braggart—he genuinely had incredible strength. Achieving so much at such a young age was enough to make anyone jealous. Maybe this kid *could* back up his words, which would make their mission a lot harder.

"Yeah, yeah, you’re amazing, we get it. Us little dried fish won’t argue with you." Cecilia had no intention of engaging Johnsson further. She turned and called to Kail, "Let’s go."

"Wait!" Johnsson suddenly raised his hand, serious. "If you’re taking a boat, could you... take me with you?"

"Hah?!" Cecilia’s eyes widened in disbelief as she stared at Johnsson.

"Sir, we’re competitors. There’s no reason for us to take you along," Kail said earnestly.

"Yeah, you’ll have to figure it out yourself. Aren’t you a magic prodigy? This shouldn’t be hard for you." Alice smiled, thinking that if they left Johnsson behind, their side would have a pretty big advantage.

Even if mages knew spells like Flight, their mana was still limited. They couldn’t fly indefinitely.

"You said you wanted fair competition, but now you won’t even let me on the boat? That’s clearly an underhanded way to suppress me!" Johnsson’s logic seemed different from most people’s, and he instead accused Merlin’s group of foul play.

"Why *do* we have to take you on *our* boat?! The boat is ours! Whether we take you or not is *our* choice!" Cecilia huffed, retorting furiously.

"Excuses~" Johnsson chuckled, tilting his nose up. "I think you’re just afraid of me. You’re worried that in a fair competition, you’d lose without a doubt, so you’re trying to hold me back in any way you can to stop me from moving forward. But how pitiful—deep down, you’ve already admitted you’re the weaker ones~"

"...What did you say?!"

Cecilia was so angry her eyebrows twitched. She wanted to argue with Johnsson, but Merlin stopped her.

"Lord Merlin?!"

Merlin looked at Johnsson, then calmly smiled. "Let the kid come along..."

"But Lord Merlin, isn’t that a bad idea?" Kail hesitated.

"It’s fine. Let him on the boat. We’ll all go to that island together." Merlin paused, then said seriously, "Trust me."

Cecilia and Kail exchanged a glance, then fell silent. If Merlin allowed Johnsson on the boat, they couldn’t really say much.

Still, seeing how confident Merlin looked, Cecilia and Kail weren’t too worried.

"Are you *sure* it’s fine? Letting Johnsson tag along is just asking for trouble," Alice frowned, dissatisfied.

"What’s there to be afraid of? I’m just giving this kid a fair chance to compete. That way, he can’t make excuses later." Merlin paused, then quickly whispered to Alice, "Besides... how hard is it for me to take candy from a baby?"

"..."

Alice blinked, then muttered, "That’s a terrible analogy..."

Merlin just smiled faintly, then turned and waved to Johnsson. "You can come with us on the boat."

"Hmph. For someone so unremarkable, you sure talk big..." Johnsson scoffed, not even sparing the Iron-rank adventurer a proper glance.

"Funny you should say that. I also like fair competition. Are you satisfied now?" Merlin spread his hands, adding coolly, "Just don’t cry and make excuses when you end up with nothing. That would be too..."

title: Chapter 27 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 27 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 27

Merlin’s tone wasn’t the least bit timid—in fact, it was even sharper than Johnson’s.

This left Captain Dennis utterly baffled. A Black Iron adventurer daring to confront a Mithril one head-on? It was astonishing.

Mithril adventurers were exceedingly rare, and the vast majority were absolute powerhouses at the Saint-tier. Every Mithril adventurer was a prized asset of the Guild, a star attraction used to draw in commissions. The gap between Black Iron and Mithril was immense, and the difference in treatment was like night and day.

Yet this Black Iron adventurer, who radiated nothing but ordinariness, was entirely different. His arrogance was almost palpable, utterly disregarding the chasm in rank as he spoke down to a Mithril powerhouse without the slightest hesitation.

Captain Dennis had seen his fair share of the world, yet he couldn’t detect anything special about Merlin. Even his old friend Kael treated this Black Iron adventurer with deference.

Dennis knew Kael’s strength inside and out. Proud and aloof as Kael was, he would never bow his head to a mere Black Iron adventurer.

The only explanation was that Merlin was stronger than Kael—and not just by a little. Only that could make his old friend show such respect.

Dennis furrowed his pale, thick eyebrows, studying Merlin intently. Unconsciously, he retracted his dismissive attitude and began reassessing this Black Iron adventurer.

Dennis himself was a high-ranking warrior, yet he couldn’t sense even a hint of imposing presence from Merlin. This only deepened his surprise, filling him with even more questions...

Johnson’s youthful face darkened instantly. A Black Iron adventurer daring to speak to him so disrespectfully—how dare he!

Johnson hadn’t taken Merlin seriously at all, practically ignoring him. But now, he had no choice but to face him directly.

“Make me cry? ...Just a lowly Black Iron adventurer with a big mouth.”

“I’m just giving you a heads-up in advance. I hope you can still keep that ‘I’m better than everyone’ attitude by the end, you conceited brat.”

Merlin curled his lips, sneering with utter disdain.

“Old man, don’t think I’m easy to bully just because I’m young. Be careful you don’t end up under *my* foot... you little punk.”

Johnson narrowed his eyes, silently clenching his fists. This Black Iron adventurer was getting on his nerves more and more.

How could a worthless bottom-tier adventurer dare speak to him in that condescending tone? He was the superstar of Great Britain’s magical circles, the youngest Saint-tier powerhouse. Even Her Majesty the Queen praised him!

No one had ever dared speak to him so rudely. Everyone addressed him with humility!

Johnson was used to being fawned over. The sudden appearance of this thorn in his side infuriated him for no clear reason.

Faced with Johnson’s mockery, Merlin merely smiled faintly, ignoring the childish nonsense.

“Let’s go. Time’s tight.”

The others turned and followed Merlin, slowly making their way toward the small boat nearby.

“Tch! Spit!” Johnson spat on the ground, glaring at Merlin’s defiant back as he fumed inwardly.

What’s with this Black Iron adventurer?

Did he just join the Adventurers Guild and doesn’t know the rules?

Forget it. He’s just some clueless fool who doesn’t know his place.

Just wait. I’ll crush him completely, make him question his life.

I’ll make him slink away from the adventurer profession like a dog.

A trash-tier Black Iron thinking he can compete with *me*, a genius? Ridiculous...

Time passed.

The group had settled aboard the merchant vessel *William*.

The massive armed merchant ship had over fifty crew members, each with clear duties, keeping everything running smoothly.

Captain Dennis lived up to his reputation. No matter the conditions, he could navigate the ship steadily. With just a glance at a nautical chart, he understood it perfectly.

The early waters were far from calm. Waves rolled violently, and the wind whipped the sea, repeatedly slamming into the *William*.

The entire ship trembled and swayed. The flags of Britain and Rose wavered as if they might snap at any moment, while the howling wind roared like thunder, refusing to settle.

Yet under Captain Dennis’s command, everything proceeded without a hitch. They cut through the turbulent waters and advanced boldly toward the central island of the Dover Strait!

By nightfall, the sea had calmed, a light mist rising as the hazy moonlight spilled across the waves...

The *William* sped forward smoothly, drawing ever closer to its destination.

Since Johnson had no fondness for this group, he had locked himself in his room the moment he boarded, avoiding everyone’s gaze. No one knew what he was doing holed up in there for so long.

Cecilia, on the other hand, had fallen prey to her noblewoman’s habits. She found the merchant ship filthy—the lingering stench of herring cans made the air unbearable.

Unable to tolerate it, Cecilia complained a few times before moving into the best room on the entire ship, after which she didn’t come out again.

This left Kael deeply embarrassed, and he quickly apologized to Dennis on her behalf.

Dennis understood Cecilia’s noble temperament and didn’t take it to heart. Instead, he pulled Kael aside for a drink, and Merlin and Alice were invited as well.

With nothing else to do, the two accepted the captain’s invitation, and they all gathered in the *William*’s dining hall to drink.

The food on the ship was undeniably poor—either canned goods or rotten tomatoes. Even the alcohol was the cheap rum favored by pirates.

Alice didn’t drink, so she simply sat quietly beside Merlin, sipping plain boiled water.

“Kael, what are you all planning to do on the island this time? You never mentioned it before. I’ve heard the waters there have been restless lately...” Captain Dennis asked curiously.

“We’re here to take down an alchemist named Democritus and restore peace to the area,” Kael replied seriously.

“Democritus? That name rings a bell...” Captain Dennis stroked his thick beard.

“You know something about him?” Kael raised his glass, asking in confusion.

“I don’t know much, just that the man’s a dragon expert. He used to be a core member of the Imperial Research Institute, but he was kicked out for conducting inhuman experiments. After that, he got tangled up with the Dark Adventurers Guild.”

Captain Dennis answered thoughtfully.

“Huh?!” Kael froze. He knew most of that, but the last part was news to him. “That alchemist has ties to the Dark Adventurers Guild?”

“It’s just rumors I picked up while sailing, some from the capital. After Democritus was expelled from the Imperial Research Institute, he kept up his unethical experiments. The ones funding and supporting him were the Dark Adventurers Guild.”

Captain Dennis took a large swig of rum.

Kael’s brows knitted together as he silently set down his glass.

“There’s that too, huh...”

He couldn’t help but feel a pang of worry. If they took down Democritus, would they end up provoking the Dark Adventurers Guild, that den of desperadoes?

The Rose family was no weakling, but it was still best to avoid unnecessary trouble—especially with evil organizations.

After all, the Rose family wasn’t like the great noble houses in the capital, with their overwhelming wealth and influence. Even Queen Elizabeth would hesitate before crossing them.

Merlin, listening from the side, was completely lost. He couldn’t help but interject.

“What’s this Dark Adventurers Guild you’re talking about?”

“Sounds interesting...”

“Are they like our fellow adventurers?”

title: Chapter 28 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 28 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 8 · Chapter 28

“Cough cough...”

Alice had even choked on her drink, because what Merlin had just said was too incredible for her to accept at this moment.

The Adventurers Guild and the Dark Adventurers Guild were obviously different, and they were fundamentally opposed from the inside out!

As for colleagues—Alice, being a former Hero, would never, dead or alive, associate with a bunch like that!

“.-.-. What are you babbling about? Who among us is a colleague of theirs?”

“That...” A bead of cold sweat slid down Merlin’s forehead as he awkwardly replied, “Aren’t we all adventurers?”

Alice rolled her eyes and said awkwardly, “Please, that’s not the same thing at all.”

Captain Dennis glanced at Merlin with a faint expression, thinking this guy seemed a bit lacking in common sense. Was he really a peer of Kelsor’s?

It wasn’t that Merlin lacked common sense entirely—he was just a bit lacking when it came to human norms.

After all, for most of his time, Merlin had lived in the demon world of this other realm, and he didn’t understand the humans of that world very well.

If you asked Merlin about demons, he’d probably talk at length like a scholar, dazzling everyone with his knowledge.

“Merlin, s-sir...” Kelsor looked at Merlin with surprise and asked, “You don’t know what the Dark Adventurers Guild is?”

“You mean it’s completely different from our Adventurers Guild?”

Merlin narrowed his eyes.

“It’s not just different—it’s fundamentally distinct.” Alice paused, then continued, “Inside the Dark Adventurers Guild, they’re all vicious and cruel people, with filthy souls. Many of them are notorious death row criminals from various countries. Unless they’ve committed some major crime and been exiled as wanderers, these people gathering together—how could they be like our respectable Adventurers Guild?”

“Is that so...” Merlin nodded and continued curiously, “So what does this Dark Adventurers Guild do? Rob, loot, burn, and pillage?”

“...Not quite that bad. They do have some rules, they’re not entirely lawless.” Alice gave a balanced assessment, then continued to spill the beans, “But their methods are ruthless. As long as the client is willing to pay, they’ll do anything. Even if it means slaughtering family members, they won’t hesitate. They’ll use any means necessary to complete the client’s requests.”

Merlin fell silent, thinking that approach was pretty straightforward, no beating around the bush. It seemed the Dark Adventurers Guild’s business model was similar to the regular Adventurers Guild, but the fundamental gap was huge.

“Although the Dark Adventurers Guild and our business model are similar, those guys have no moral bottom line—they serve only the highest bidder.” Alice paused, then casually added, “Many people with ill intentions will spend a lot of money to get them to do dirty work. Killing and arson are everyday occurrences. These all violate the Empire’s laws and the Adventurers Guild’s interests, so these people are all top-level wanted criminals in various countries, and they’re also targets the Adventurers Guild needs to crack down on.”

“Oh, I see...”

Merlin nodded, thinking that since the Dark Adventurers Guild existed, there must be a market for them.

After all, the regular Adventurers Guild wouldn’t accept dirty jobs like killing and arson.

So it made sense that a dark side would emerge. Human evil desires need people like them to help fulfill them.

“Do they have a lot of members?”

Alice hesitated. “This... there’s no specific number, and they’re not just in Great Britain. They have a presence in every country. They don’t have fixed bases. The known Dark Adventurers Guilds number four: Deep Frost Gaze, Phoenix, Bold Demon Celebration, and Azure Blue Flame...” Alice recalled as she introduced them to Merlin.

“It sounds like they don’t have as many members as the regular Adventurers Guild. Why can’t we just wipe them out quickly?” Merlin asked in confusion, thinking that the regular guild’s numbers should be enough to crush these outlaws. Yet they had survived for so long.

“They live in the shadows, very mysterious. Although the Adventurers Guild has organized several raids before, the results weren’t great—either they came up empty or suffered heavy losses.” Alice’s tone was somewhat awkward, as if she didn’t want to mention these things.

“It sounds like the Adventurers Guild is pretty useless...” Merlin said with a smirk.

“This is an unavoidable situation. I’ve heard those guys are no weaklings either, each one a killer, and in situations where the enemy sees us but we can’t see them, how could we have the advantage?” Alice made excuses for her seniors.

“Everything is just an excuse for incompetence...” Merlin said casually, then shifted topics, “Speaking of which, the Dark Adventurers Guild actually suits me pretty well.”

At that, Dennis and Kelsor both looked unnatural. If Merlin said such things on the street, he might get invited for tea by the guards.

The Dark Adventurers Guild represented absolute evil. Speaking in favor of them was far worse than insulting the clergy.

Alice frowned with worry and said, “What nonsense are you talking about? That kind of place wouldn’t suit you at all!”

“I’m just joking. Why are you so tense?” Merlin shrugged.

“...Alice was at a loss for words, glaring at Merlin angrily without saying anything.

Thinking about it, Merlin used to be the evil Great Demon Lord. Wanting to join the Dark Adventurers Guild wasn’t impossible. No wonder Alice was so worried.

Alice wouldn’t admit that she felt inexplicably melancholy and uncomfortable now that Merlin was suddenly leaving her side.

“Rumble—”

A tremendous rumble erupted, like an earthquake striking the plains, instantly shattering the peaceful night.

The wine bottles on the counter table shattered with a crash, tables and chairs all flipped over!

Even the candle chandelier on the upper floor suddenly fell to the ground and went out, plunging the scene into darkness!

The entire William’s ship shook violently, swaying like a level-10 earthquake—showing just how powerful the impact was!

Outside William’s ship.

The sea became furious, with massive waves rolling endlessly!

The sky had turned dark with heavy clouds, and the bright moonlight had long disappeared from sight.

The enormous waves rose and fell like a storm signaling the end of the world!

And the one responsible for all this was—a seemingly grotesque giant monster.

A 200-foot tall robust body, with powerful frog-like claws, covered in gray scales.

Two feelers dangled from its massive jaws, and its smooth forehead was bare.

This giant, powerful monster was like a giantized puppy fish—so wasn’t it the aquatic alchemy beast that had destroyed over 100 militiamen just recently?

The puppy fish alchemy beast was like a moving island, inspiring awe from everyone. William’s ship looked like a tiny mouse in comparison.

The shaking of William’s ship earlier was the result of this alchemy beast’s attack.

At this moment, William’s ship was damaged and had begun to slowly sink—a very critical situation!

The giant puppy fish alchemy beast opened its bloodthirsty jaws and let out a terrifying roar at William’s ship.

A gust of blood-wind and rain swept over, and the tiny William’s ship trembled helplessly before this monster, its mast snapped in two.

The powerful sound waves made everyone’s hair stand on end, and the entire merchant ship risked being shattered—things were extremely dire!

In the distance, on a central island.

Demitrius, dressed in a red long robe, stood on the platform holding a telescope, facing the wind and rain to observe the situation.

When he saw William’s ship in a critical sinking situation, not only did his mouth curl into a smug smile—

“Didn’t expect a few more rats to show up. You really don’t give up, do you?”

“Let me see what you’ve got!”

title: Chapter 29 — Oh No
content:
Chapter 29 — Oh No

Volume 8 · Chapter 29

Democritus, dressed in a red robe and holding a telescope, watched the movements of the William from start to finish.

At this moment, the William had become perilously unstable, its small hull swaying violently in the storm.

The lower part of the ship was damaged and cracking, slowly sinking into the sea.

Now, Captain Dennis had only two choices left.

The first was to sit and wait for death, letting the William sink slowly while everyone escaped on small boats.

The second was to move quickly, reach the island before the William went under—provided they could kill the giant salamander alchemy beast.

Either choice was fraught with danger; one wrong move, and the entire crew would be lost at sea...

Democritus, however, was completely at ease. He enjoyed watching from afar, sneering all the while.

"Why do some people fail to understand the gap in power and insist on rushing to their deaths?"

"One after another, they come to harass me, yet not a single one is worth fighting..."

"Forget it. Consider this an after-dinner entertainment. You’d better make it exciting for me, hmph hmph hmph~"

The massive salamander alchemy beast roared repeatedly, its shadow looming over the hearts of everyone on the ship...

Inside the William’s dining hall.

The sudden jolt had tilted the ship, turning the once-orderly scene into chaos.

The four people inside had all tumbled to the floor, their faces blank with confusion, unsure of what had happened.

An oil lamp fell, its small flame flickering, allowing the shaken group to see their surroundings.

"What’s going on?!" Kail shouted in panic, slowly crawling up from the floor, his face pale.

"I don’t know... It feels like the merchant ship hit a reef..." Alice furrowed her delicate brows, sensing something was wrong.

"That’s impossible. I’ve checked the nautical charts—there are no large reefs along this route. And we’re still some distance away from the central island of the sea region," Captain Dennis said, standing up slowly, his answer confident yet heavy with concern.

As an experienced sailor, Dennis knew exactly when they should arrive. This was not the time. A wave of worry surged through him.

"Then what’s happening?" Merlin asked, sweating nervously. He hoped they wouldn’t have to fight at sea, especially not in a large-scale battle that could damage the ship.

Merlin couldn’t swim. He dreaded naval combat—if he fell into the sea, he’d be at the mercy of the currents.

Unless absolutely necessary, Merlin would never draw his sword on the open sea. One misstep, and they’d all be doomed.

"This feeling... it seems like our ship was attacked by something..." Captain Dennis said, his brow furrowed, his face darkening.

"Seriously? Are there any sea monsters in this area?" Alice asked anxiously. She recalled the sea serpent Merlin had slain in the Orkney Strait. If it was a monster of that caliber, it would be tough—but with Merlin around, it should be manageable.

Alice seemed to have forgotten that Merlin couldn’t swim. A year ago in the Orkney Strait, if there had been no other choice, Merlin would have been forced to fight at sea.

"There shouldn’t be. I’ve sailed these waters for years and never heard of any sea-dwelling monsters here," Captain Dennis paused before continuing. "Besides, this is a fishing ground for locals. How could monsters appear here?"

"Maybe it’s a mutant?" Kail mused.

"A mutant?" Alice asked, confused.

"Haven’t you heard the rumors about the fish here mutating and becoming aggressive? Maybe there’s a big one out there..." Kail answered seriously, thinking it was plausible.

Just as they were speculating, the William’s first mate burst in, his face pale with sweat.

"Captain, it’s bad! Our ship’s been attacked by an unknown giant monster! There’s a huge hole in the hull, and the crew can’t patch it. At this rate, we’ll sink soon!"

"What?! We’re sinking?!" Merlin’s eyes widened, his mouth hanging open in shock. He couldn’t believe it—he hadn’t even been on the ship that long! Why was his luck always this terrible?!

"Sinking?!" Kail froze for a moment before dashing out of the dining hall. "...I need to check on Lady Cecilia!"

Kail vanished from sight without a backward glance. The first mate, now inside, urgently asked, "Captain, what do we do now?!"

"How far are we from the island?" Captain Dennis asked calmly.

"Less than a nautical mile," the first mate replied, his expression grim.

Captain Dennis hesitated, his hawk-like eyes flickering. Finally, in a thunderous voice, he ordered, "Command all hands to full speed ahead! Gunners, take your positions! Prepare to engage with everything we’ve got!"

"Aye, sir!" The first mate saluted and rushed out of the ruined dining hall.

Captain Dennis picked up his old captain’s hat from the floor, dusted it off, and placed it firmly on his head. Without hesitation, he followed, his weathered back hinting at the bearing of a former naval commander.

"What should we do? We have to do something, right?" Alice turned to Merlin, whose face was also grim.

"I think we should steal a lifeboat and slip away unnoticed~" Merlin said, dead serious.

"Are you insane?!" Alice snapped, outraged. "How could you suggest that? That’s way too heartless!"

"The ship’s sinking! If we don’t run now, are you trying to get us killed?!" Merlin’s forehead was lined with black veins, convinced Alice was plotting his demise.

"You could just help kill the monster! Captain Dennis said if we go full speed, we can still make it to shore!" Alice urged Merlin to lend a hand.

"If I help, the ship will sink faster. My attacks are too powerful—it’s easy to hit the William too..." Merlin muttered awkwardly.

"Really? You fought on a ship last year and nothing happened!" Alice knitted her brows, suspecting Merlin was just making excuses.

"Miss, a big ship and a small boat are the same to you?!" Merlin was tempted to perform open-skull surgery on Alice to see how her brain worked. "Plus, we’re dealing with a massive monster. My Iaijutsu could easily cut the beast and the William in half together!"

"..." Alice froze, stunned. "That bad?"

"Isn’t it obvious?" Merlin said flatly, awkwardly thinking to himself—

And I can’t swim. My combat power in water is zero.

What should I do? Should I ditch Alice and escape on a lifeboat by myself...

In a room aboard the William.

Johnson peeked out the window, watching the giant salamander alchemy beast outside. A smug smile spread across his face.

"Time for my grand performance~"

Before he could finish, Johnson vomited on the floor, his face pale, drenched in cold sweat.

Truth was, Johnson suffered from severe seasickness. His refusal to leave his room was to hide it from others.

Looking at Johnson’s agonized state, his seasickness was clearly severe—it had completely drained his ability to fight.

"Ugh, I’m dying... dying..." Johnson groaned, sprawled on the cold floor.

Ireland’s genius mage—utterly useless!

title: Chapter 30 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 30 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 8 · Chapter 30

Dark clouds rolled, thunder roared, and lightning split the sky.

The heavens were darker than night itself, like an abyss devouring the world.

With a monstrous howl, the grotesque alchemical beast raised a fist the size of a war chariot and slammed it down.

The William’s ten polished cannons fired in rapid succession—*boom, boom, boom*—sending flames several meters high.

The massive steel shells struck the beast’s body, but its gray scales deflected them, sending sparks flying in all directions.

Though the cannons did no real damage, they did pause the beast’s attack, giving the William a chance to escape.

Old Nils stood at the highest point of the ship, his expression unshaken. The water on his face could have been rain or cold sweat from fear.

"Lads, push harder! Full speed to the island! ! !"

Captain Nils’ roar was loud enough to drown out the thunder. The crew below sprang into action, their efficiency rivaling even the Imperial Royal Navy.

Inside the ship, the sailors—each one powerfully built—strained with all their might to row the massive oars. Even as seawater rose past their knees, not a single man retreated.

To these brave sailors, the ship was their home. This was their most basic conviction—everyone was prepared to live or die with the William.

Captain Nils swung his arm hard, and the rudder spun wildly. The entire ship turned sharply, charging straight toward the island.

The grotesque, tadpole-like alchemical beast slammed its fist down, but it only grazed the William’s hull, sending up a wave a hundred feet high that crashed against the sea.

The William rocked violently under the impact, becoming unstable.

But Nils gripped the wheel tightly, controlling the ship as if he and the William were one.

Under the captain’s veteran skill, the battered William barely endured the shock—but a few crewmen lost their footing and tumbled into the vast sea, likely doomed.

The William, now at full speed, cut through the water, leaving ripples in its wake.

Though it was just a merchant ship carrying herring cans, its speed was in no way inferior to a lightly loaded pirate vessel.

The deformed alchemical beast hesitated for a moment before letting out an indignant roar. It swung its two thick, powerful frog-like arms and gave chase, refusing to let the William go.

...

The beast’s lantern-like eyes rolled wildly, locked onto the William.

Despite its enormous size and lack of legs, it moved with terrifying speed—it would catch up to the small, damaged ship in just a few strides.

Captain Dennis steered the William forward, riding the wind, but in his heart, he dared not relax. If they couldn’t find a way to slow this monster down, they would all be devoured.

The first mate stumbled up, his face twisted in terror, his words stuttering: "...C-Captain! W-What... what do we do now? !"

"Stop panicking, you bastard!"

Captain Dennis roared. Normally, he looked like a down-on-his-luck noble—refined and gentle.

But in this desperate moment, the old gentleman had a rough edge, cursing freely.

"Where the hell is my Italian magic cannon?! Use it! Blow that son of a bitch to hell!"

"...Aye!" The first mate hurried below to make the arrangements.

Everyone could see the monstrous creature drawing closer, the situation growing more critical by the second.

A curtain was pulled back by several sailors, revealing the magic cannon integrated into the ship’s hull. The massive barrel stood sixty inches tall, gleaming like a steel giant.

The thick cannon barrel pointed skyward, its polished surface reflecting the light—clearly well-maintained.

Several men carried a Saint-tier magic crystal up the deck. It was as large as a water buffalo’s head, cumbersome to move.

The crew worked together to load the Saint-tier magic crystal into the cannon, then frantically turned the gears to aim the barrel at the approaching alchemical beast.

The charging began. The entire cannon rumbled to life, draining most of the magic crystal’s power. The muzzle glowed with an increasingly deep red light.

First Mate: "Captain! The magic cannon is fully charged!"

"Fire! ! !" Captain Dennis bellowed without hesitation.

A deafening *boom* shook the sea’s surface.

A brilliant beam erupted from the cannon’s muzzle, striking the alchemical beast square in the face without missing.

The red light, infused with fire elemental energy, packed the force of a full-powered strike from a Saint-tier mage!

For a moment, the sea turned crimson, waves churning as the pitch-black sky lit up like day.

The grotesque alchemical beast let out a pained *"Wooaaargh!"* and stopped in its tracks, even recoiling from the blast.

"We did it! We won!"

"Die, monster!"

"Taste the power of the magic cannon!"

The crew cheered and embraced, convinced the crisis was over. Even if the beast wasn’t dead, it had to be severely wounded!

On the highest point of the distant island, Democritus still watched through his telescope. He couldn’t help but chuckle. "Oh? Not bad. But what a shame… my little pet is about to get *angry*~"

The glow of the magic cannon faded.

As the light dissipated, the alchemical beast’s scorched body came into view, wisps of white smoke rising from its scales. Its blood-red eyes spun restlessly.

How was it possible? They had unleashed the full power of a Saint-tier magic crystal, yet the beast had only suffered minor injuries!

This wasn’t the cannon’s fault—the alchemical beast, crafted from dragon’s blood, had a unique gift.

Most didn’t know that dragon scales had extraordinary defensive power, or that they possessed extremely high magic resistance.

Many lower-tiered magical attacks did little to no damage to dragonkin—some even had no effect at all!

And the gray scales covering the alchemical beast were a variant of dragon scales, granting it high defense and strong magic resistance.

"ROOOOAR! ! !"

The deformed alchemical beast was enraged—how dare its prey attack it?! This was a grave insult!

It redoubled its speed, charging at the William with even greater ferocity, determined not to let a single person on board escape.

The crew froze, standing dumbfounded in place. Their prized weapon had failed so miserably.

A sense of overwhelming despair took root in their hearts...

The brave sailors stared at the monstrous, gaping maw rushing toward them, already preparing for death. It seemed unstoppable.

Captain Dennis looked toward the distant shore. There was still some distance to go.

But the beast behind them was closing in fast—it didn’t seem intent on giving them time to reach land!

A cold sweat rolled down Captain Dennis’ forehead. His hands trembled on the wheel. Despair filled his mind—

*God, if you have any mercy for us, please save us...*

But what was Merlin doing at this critical moment?

In one of the William’s emergency storage rooms:

"One life ring isn’t enough, right? Bring me a few more."

Merlin was preparing his escape. Since he couldn’t swim, he was worried about drowning, so he wanted to be thoroughly prepared.

If the ship really sank, and he—unable to swim—ended up flailing helplessly in the water, that would be far too embarrassing.

If the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace drowned, the other Demon Lords would laugh him into oblivion. He’d be nailed to the pillar of shame for all demonkind!

Now, Merlin had strapped six or seven life rings around himself, protecting every angle. Then he went to look for a lifeboat.

Merlin sighed in embarrassment, looking down at himself. He felt bloated all over, as if—

"I feel like I could be a spokesmodel for Michelin tires right now."

●-●)

title: Chapter 31 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 31 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 8 · Chapter 31

Merlin was also at his wits' end right now. The thing he hated most in this life was traveling by ship.

Every time, he felt an overwhelming sense of dread, as if the ship might sink at any moment.

And now, of all times, he had to deal with this mess. Merlin’s mood was utterly gloomy.

While Merlin was practically a king on land, at sea, he was nothing more than a bronze-tier amateur.

Since he couldn’t swim, if he fell into the water, he’d be completely helpless—with the added risk of drowning.

Don’t let his fearless demeanor on land fool you; at sea, he had plenty of concerns.

*Sigh… In this cold, cruel world, only this life buoy offers a hint of warmth, willing to accompany me through this…*

Merlin mused poetically. Right now, nothing felt familiar—except the life buoy, which gave him the comforting feeling of family.

Why didn’t Merlin learn to swim?

Well, it wasn’t because he was lazy.

The truth was, Merlin had terrible coordination. When it came to swimming, he had absolutely no talent for it.

Lilith had urged Merlin to learn, to overcome this weakness. She’d even recruited many of the demon race’s swimming experts to teach him personally.

Unfortunately, after three months of intense training, Merlin still couldn’t even manage a doggy paddle—he’d nearly drowned, leaving everyone in stunned silence.

Most demons in the demon race knew that Lucifer III, the First Demon Lord, was a complete landlubber, and they often teased him about it.

*"Hey hey, did you know? The mighty Lord of Pride can’t swim at all! In the water, I could take him down with one finger!"*

What could Merlin do? He was desperate. He had an instinctive fear of the ocean and large bodies of water.

It seemed swimming was a survival skill he’d never master. All he could do was stay vigilant and tread carefully.

Merlin glanced at the life buoy around him and decided that was enough. Even if he fell into the sea, he’d easily float back up.

*"Perfect, I’ll just sneak onto a lifeboat and get to shore~"*

---

Outside the SF light novel,

The weather was atrocious, with a freezing, bone-chilling wind howling across the deck.

The sea was far rougher than usual, as if the sea god himself was venting his fury.

The tiny William’s Hope struggled through the waves, looking as though it might capsize at any moment.

Yet Captain Dennis refused to give up. He gripped the wheel, stubbornly pushing toward the shore.

The William’s Hope was sinking deeper by the minute, with seawater frequently sloshing over the deck.

Behind them, the grotesque alchemy beast gave chase, lunging forward like a rabid dog!

It roared furiously, its voice shaking the very soul, driven by an instinctive desire for revenge after the earlier attack.

Its massive body moved with terrifying speed, seemingly parting the waves as it advanced.

The situation was dire. Everyone’s heart was shrouded in the shadow of being devoured by that monstrous maw…

Captain Dennis’s mind was a whirl of anxiety. He could sense the beast’s overwhelming power—this was no ordinary foe.

The known powerhouses on the ship were the 14-year-old magic prodigy Johnson and the enigmatic Merlin.

Johnson was a Mithril-ranked adventurer with a well-known reputation—there was no doubt about his strength.

But the crew’s relationship with Johnson was poor. Whether he’d even help was uncertain.

The ship’s magic cannons packed the punch of Saint-tier spells, yet they barely scratched the beast. Would Johnson struggle against it?

As for Merlin… Captain Dennis still harbored doubts. Though Keith claimed he was a Saint-tier powerhouse, Dennis had never seen proof.

After their brief interactions, Dennis couldn’t spot a single thing about Merlin that screamed "strong." Suspicion lingered.

A flicker of despair crept into Dennis’s heart. It seemed neither Merlin nor Johnson could be relied upon. He’d have to find another way.

Alice burst out of the cabin, her face pale with panic. She’d seen the hull flooding—things were looking grim.

The tadpole-like alchemy beast surged forward with a howl, startling Alice so badly her face drained of color.

*…What in the world is this monster?*

Just by its appearance, Alice couldn’t tell what species it was. It looked like some grotesque hybrid of different creatures.

*"We’re doomed…"*
*"No! I don’t want to die!"*
*"I still have a wife and kids back home!"*

Many crew members wailed in despair. As the monster closed in, most had already given up hope.

*Whoosh!*

Alice drew the slender sword at her waist, her high-tier magic surging.

With a flick of her blade, hundreds of ice-crystal swords materialized in the air around her.

*"Hah!"*

With a sharp cry, the ice swords shot forward in a dense volley, stabbing toward the charging alchemy beast.

But the beast’s gray scales deflected every single one. Not a scratch—it didn’t even slow the creature down.

*Tch! You’ve got to be kidding me…*

Alice knitted her delicate brows, her expression turning grave. This was trouble.

At a moment like this, she couldn’t help but wish Merlin were here. But the moment they’d set sail, that guy had vanished—no one knew where he’d gone. It was infuriating.

Even if Merlin’s Iaijutsu might damage the William’s Hope, it’d still be better than being eaten alive!

Alice’s frustration grew. Normally, she couldn’t stand how Merlin was always underfoot, but now that she needed him, he was nowhere to be found! It was maddening.

The cabin door swung open, and Johnson stumbled out, his face ashen, cold sweat pouring down like a waterfall. He looked like he was on death’s door.

*"Ugh!"* Alice froze, her expression twisting in disbelief. *This bratty show-off actually gets seasick?*

Johnson’s steps were unsteady. He collapsed to the ground, stretching out a hand, and weakly muttered,

*"…Help me up… I… can… ugh…"*

The pathetic Johnson vomited again. The ship’s rocking had only gotten worse, and now his head was spinning.

*"This guy’s useless… can’t count on him…"* Alice deadpanned.

The William’s Hope’s plight grew more desperate by the second. Captain Dennis’s face was set in grim determination, but reality had him breaking out in cold sweat, his heart lodged in his throat.

The deformed aquatic alchemy beast opened its gaping maw—large enough to swallow ten William’s Hopes in one gulp!

With no emotion, it charged forward, ready to devour ship, sea, and all in a single bite!

*"This is bad…"* Alice’s face paled, all color draining away as she stared in shock at the monstrous jaws bearing down on them.

*Merlin… where are you?*

Forget the Chengkang for now—just hurry up and blow this thing away!

---

On an island in the sea.

Democritus, holding a spyglass, watched the scene with amusement, clearly enjoying their desperate struggle for survival, their descent into despair.

*"Hmph. So in the end, that’s all they amount to? They’re nothing more than playthings for my pet."*

*"Farewell, foolish mortals… heh heh heh…"*

Democritus’s crimson robes billowed as he turned to leave. But just then—an anomaly occurred.

The ferocious alchemy beast, which had been charging forward with a roar, suddenly stopped mid-lunge, frozen in an inexplicable rigidity.

*"Hm? What’s going on?"* Democritus furrowed his brow, confused.

The proud, towering alchemy beast—its massive body split cleanly in two. The two halves of its corpse toppled in opposite directions.

Bright red blood bloomed like fireworks, instantly staining a vast stretch of the sea crimson.

The beast, which had been unstoppable moments ago, was now inexplicably dead?!

Democritus’s eyebrows twisted together, his face darkening. Shocked, he muttered to himself,

*"…What the…?!"*
*"How was this done?!"*
*"What in the world happened?! Why was my adorable pet taken out in an instant…?!"*
