title: Chapter 32 — Fear
content:
Chapter 32 — Fear

Volume 8 · Chapter 32

Just before the massive alchemical beast opened its bloody mouth and roared, intending to swallow the William whole.

Everyone looked at that abyssal giant mouth, the thick stench rushing toward them, nearly causing them to faint.

The waves frequently surged, dark clouds rolled between the horizon, and not a shred of light could penetrate through.

But just at this moment—killing sword qi suddenly exploded, instantly sweeping through everything in front.

The surging alchemical beast immediately stopped, as if it had instantly lost its life, its large mouth wide open and motionless.

The raging wind stopped, and the furious sea surface also slowly calmed down.

The alchemical beast's huge body was instantly split in two, falling to both sides, splashing up hundred-foot-high waves.

Blood shot out into the air, nearly dyeing the entire nearby sea red, and the bloody smell grew even stronger.

This sudden turn made everyone present stunned, with faces full of big, written-in-caps confusion.

Just moments ago it felt like we were at the entrance to hell, but now we were instantly transported to heaven.

This roller coaster-like feeling gave everyone a huge shock.

Regaining a new life made the crew's mood very excited, and they slowly looked behind them—

Merlin at this time was wearing N lifebuoys on his body, looking somewhat bloated, clearly looking like a deserter.

His expression was solemn, his face a bit ugly, and he slowly sheathed that rusty-looking broken sword, then twisted his neck.

"Sigh, there's no way about it, if I didn't make a move, I wouldn't have been able to survive this tribulation..."

Because the alchemical beast was an artificial lifeform and had no power level, the curse relief Merlin had had on it was of no use at all, it was just a waste of effort.

However, at that time Merlin had no choice, he had to draw his sword, otherwise he and the William would have to travel together in the alchemical beast's stomach.

Actually, Merlin didn't want to draw his sword either; he originally just came out to find a lifeboat and run away, who knew that as soon as he went out, he saw an alchemical beast like a giant salamander rushing over with its bloody mouth wide open.

The situation was critical, giving Merlin absolutely no time to choose, so he could only decisively draw his sword, first not worrying about whether the William would sink or not, just cut first and ask questions later.

The wind and rain were swaying, bone-chillingly cold.

Everyone stared at Merlin, as if looking at an alien.

"It was... that Black Iron Adventurer who did it, right?"

"Should be right, the attack just now seemed to come from his side..."

"So strong, to actually cut that monster in half with one strike, how powerful is that attack? Clearly our magic cannons didn't work at all."

The crew below were discussing it heatedly, all thinking Merlin was a freak, to be able to one-shot such a monster, he must be Saint-tier strength, right?

But Merlin happened to be wearing a Black Iron Adventurer's Badge on his neck, this strong contrast made many people very confused.

Have Black Iron Adventurers become this awesome now? This was a common question in many crew members' hearts.

Captain Dennis moved forward facing the wind and rain, his expression wooden, his hand still tightly gripping the rudder, but his gaze never left Merlin's body.

To be able to one-shot that monster with one strike, what kind of terrifying power is that?

Having this level of strength, even among Saint-tier experts, is very outstanding.

It seems that Kyle's respect for this Black Iron Adventurer is not without reason.

Sure enough, this seemingly lazy guy, although wearing the lowest-level Adventurer's Badge, is actually a genuine Saint-tier expert.

Captain Dennis's eagle-like eyes were bright, and the suspicion he held for Merlin in his heart instantly vanished, leaving only awe for the strong.

After the battle, the William calmed down, and Johnson's seasickness symptoms slightly improved; seeing the scene before him, he was slightly surprised.

Actually killed it?! A mere Black Iron Adventurer could actually do such a thing!

In this industry, the Black Iron level is the bottom layer, most of them are good-for-nothings just passing time!

How could he do such a thing? This guy has some tricks up his sleeve, he is simply an anomaly among Black Irons!

No wonder he dared to challenge me, it turns out he has some real strength; I said, why would a Black Iron Adventurer dare to be so arrogant with me?!

Johnson narrowed his eyes, becoming worried; he stared dead at the carefree Merlin, if everyone were a target, then this blonde man was his great enemy.

Alice ran to Merlin's front, asking depressedly, "Where did you go, you guy? Why are you only here now?"

"Wasn't I just going to leisurely ensure my own safety? What's the problem?" Merlin spread his hands, his expression helpless.

"..." Alice's expression was unnatural, looking at the N lifebuoys on Merlin's body, looking completely like a moving lifeboat, "Why are you wearing so many lifebuoys?"

"Can't swim just in case...". Merlin shrugged his shoulders, actually he didn't want to be like this either.

"What are you worried about? I will, if you drown, I will save you." Alice answered with a serious face.

"You?" Merlin narrowed his eyes and sized up Alice, then curled his lip and said, "Come on, Heroes are guys you can't trust, at critical moments it would be good enough if you didn't kick me into the deep sea."

"Why do you have to do such excessive things?! How much do you distrust me? Stop looking down on people, you! Although I did think that way, I haven't planned to put it into action yet!" Alice vented a whole stream of complaints, directly spitting out her inner thoughts.

"You bastard, you really thought about murdering..." Merlin responded with a dark face, raising his guard against Alice.

"....Cough, cough!" Alice's face turned red, and she quickly coughed lightly to cover her embarrassment, "By the way, didn't you say you couldn't draw your sword on a big ship? Didn't you just draw it? And it didn't cause any trouble at all, you clearly just didn't want to help, right?"

"No trouble at all? Is that really the case?" Merlin frowned tightly, already having a bad premonition.

Boom—

A huge sound immediately rang out, plunging everyone on the ship into panic.

This sound was like something breaking, the entire William started to shake, apparently losing its proper balance.

"What's wrong?!"

Alice suddenly looked back, directly seeing a horrifying scene.

The William's stern was almost completely gone, neatly cut out with a large incision.

The cargo in the cabin and the ship's wood shavings all fell into the vast sea.

Due to the attack on the stern, the entire William lost its balance and started tilting and shaking.

Things on the ship, many started sliding down, and a few unlucky guys didn't hold on tight and directly sank into the pitch-black deep sea.

In an instant, the entire William fell into chaos, screams were incessant, and everyone started prioritizing saving their own lives.

All of this was caused by Merlin's attack, he didn't lie; to use the slash that killed the huge alchemical beast, it was bound to affect the William.

Look at now, karma has come, right?

The William's sinking speed increased, the sea crazily swallowed the tilted and shaking hull, there was still a distance to the island!

"Why did it turn out like this?! That's a bit too exaggerated! Merlin, you bastard, can't you control yourself a bit?!!"

Alice had to grab the mast, shouting in panic, fearing she would fall, feeling as if her whole body had lost gravity.

"Blame me?" Merlin was fully wrapped in lifebuoys, unhurriedly leaning tightly against the ship's edge, posing in a scared JPG pose—

"I said I didn't want to draw my sword on the ship, wasn't you guys forcing me?"

"Are you satisfied now? We're all going to hell together!"

"Funny, keke"

title: Chapter 33 — Extra Chapter for Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 33 — Extra Chapter for Monthly Votes

Volume 8 · Chapter 33

The broken William sped across the sea, shaking like a dilapidated old car, using all its strength to rush towards the island ahead.

The dark clouds in the sky were slightly heavy, and above the small island, lightning and thunder flashed, as if an unknown demon lived there.

Although the sea surface wasn't shaking as violently as before, the sailing conditions were better than they had been.

But unfortunately, the William was severely damaged and had lost its balance, making it extremely difficult to accelerate forward.

Bone-chilling seawater was flooding back frantically, but the part of the William submerged was increasing, making the situation extremely critical!

The scene was in chaos, and all the crew members were like headless flies, looking everywhere for a place to survive, completely losing their anchor.

Even though this group of brave sailors dealt with the sea all year round, at a time like this, the desire to survive still overcame everything.

Alice was hugging the mast, panic-stricken; it was night now, and the sea was pitch black, so god knows what was in the water—if a monster came for an intimate encounter, they were dead for sure.

"Merlin! Think of a way quickly! ? Anything works!"

"What way can I have! ? Just wait and save yourselves, sending a cool song to..."

Merlin leaned against the ship's edge, trembling in response; don't look at him being calm on the surface, but inside he was panicking like crazy, his pants were almost falling down.

"Shit, shit, shit... Johnson was the unluckiest, because he wasn't an adult and was short, he couldn't grab anything and was rolling randomly on the ship; his seasickness symptoms seemed to be getting worse, 'Dizzy, my head hurts so much, I'm gonna die...'"

At this time, the William was no longer glamorous; the entire stern was gone, looking like a runaway wild horse galloping across the sea.

Captain Dennis gripped the rudder tightly, using all his strength to keep the William balanced.

In the wind and rain, although his figure was old, he stood unmoving, as if wanting to be a great mountain, becoming the crew's last psychological defense line.

Not fearing danger and keeping one's head calm at all times are basic qualities of being a captain.

Dennis was indeed experienced; although the William had sunk halfway, and the hull was severely damaged, he could still maintain the William's balance.

Such sailing skills were indeed as Kyle said; he had his own proud capital.

However, no matter how experienced Captain Dennis was, he couldn't withstand this situation.

The current crisis was already increasingly beyond Captain Dennis's control, making it very difficult to make up for it through technique.

The William had sunk halfway; if no rescue measures were taken, it would definitely sink before reaching the island.

Cold sweat broke out on Captain Dennis's face as he estimated the distance between the island and the William; finally, gritting his teeth, he made a ruthless decision.

"Everyone! All of you damn well calm down!"

This voice was particularly harsh; it was hard to imagine such a loud voice coming from an old man.

The panicked crew looked in unison at the helmsman captain, their expressions utterly blank.

Even Merlin and Alice were startled, looking at that figure facing the storm.

Seeing that everyone had calmed down, Captain Dennis loudly ordered.

"Now throw all the unimportant things overboard to reduce the ship's weight! Including our 20 cannons, and the magic cannons, throw them all into the sea!"

The crew members widened their eyes in unison; these weapons were their family assets and were very valuable, so throwing them away like this was a bit too much of a pity.

The first mate also felt this was inappropriate, so he braved it and spoke to Dennis.

"Captain! This isn't right, is it? These are our family assets; throwing them away is too much of a pity, isn't it!?"

It wasn't just the first mate; even the other crew members were unwilling; meeting pirates on the sea was a common occurrence, and without these weapons as deterrence, the consequences would be terrible.

"Throw them away! ! !" Captain Dennis shouted with an unquestionable tone, continuing, "Money can be earned again if it's gone; our greatest loss would be if we were buried in the sea, so we must make a choice now, throw them all away!"

The crew members below discussed it among themselves, all a bit hesitant; these weapons counted as everyone's common property, so throwing them away was really a bit hard to bear.

In the end, the first mate made up his mind and loudly said to the crew.

"The Captain is right; now, except for essential life supplies, throw away everything else, leaving nothing behind!"

Having no choice, everyone started to act; if they continued to carry the weight, the William would sink faster.

The action began; twenty finely crafted cannons were pushed into the sea one after another with a thud, splashing countless waves.

There were also many messy things: life supplies, tons of rum, fine tequila, and a series of high-end furniture; looking at this, Merlin felt a bit heartache.

Kyle came out of the cabin holding Cecilia, protecting the young miss with all his might; seeing the situation outside, he was instantly stunned.

". . . What is going on here?"

All the messy things were abandoned and thrown into the deep sea, leaving only necessary pure water and some food.

The cabin was violently opened, and countless sardine cans were poured into the sea, creating a momentary shimmer of silver.

These sardine cans were imported from Greenland; they hadn't even been cashed in yet and were already floating away, making the crew very uncomfortable.

Finally, the most expensive magic cannon was also pushed off the ship by the first mate and others; watching the treasure slowly sink, everyone's mood was very complicated.

Captain Dennis clearly felt the William's speed increase and the sinking progress slow down slightly; it was all the result of reducing the weight.

"Hold on tight! We're going full speed ahead! !!"

The William, lightly equipped, instantly transformed into a sword cutting through the sea, charging at an incredibly fast speed, with waves rippling behind it and leaving white wakes.

The small island ahead was now visible, and this speed seemed to truly turn the rotten into the miraculous.

Captain Dennis turned the rudder, trying to stabilize the William as it sped at full velocity.

The hull was shaking constantly, making a clicking sound; the William was already in a terrible state, and now it was even worse, starting to collapse from the middle, looking like a shoe horn flying across the sea.

In a final struggle, the broken William rushed onto the shore and crashed headfirst into the sand ---

Successful landing!

At the highest point of the island.

Democritus, wearing a red robe, silently put down his telescope, his face looking a bit ugly.

"Really? They actually landed?"

Democritus had felt something was off since the alchemy beast was killed, feeling that the people coming this time were not ordinary.

Being able to choose to dump the clutter at a time like this and then fight to the death proved that this captain had extraordinary courage and decisive action.

Moreover, there was someone who could one-shot his small pet, meaning there was a person of considerable strength present.

It seemed he had to be serious; before proposing to Miss Asmodeus, he absolutely would not allow anyone to ruin my plans!

"Hmph, troublesome guys, prepare to die."

Democritus grinned and leisurely turned, thinking happily in his heart.

Foolish people, you will just struggle in front of me.

That frogman alchemy beast from just now was just the weakest in my works!

Next, prepare to tremble deeply and despairingly howl in front of my masterpiece, which I am proud of...

凸(‘0)凸

title: Chapter 34 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 34 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 34

In the underground chamber beneath the island.

This was the only tall mountain on the small island.

Its interior had long since been remodeled by Democritus into an alchemy laboratory.

Though it looked a bit crude, it was small but complete—every facility was sufficient for Democritus to conduct research and create all manner of ferocious monsters.

Democritus had once been a figure of renown in the field of alchemical academia, even specially recruited by Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth into the Imperial Research Institute.

The Imperial Research Institute was a key institution nurtured by the royal family, filled with alchemical fanatics of high intelligence, engaged in all manner of alchemical research across various imperial domains. The most useful among them was likely the development of new weapons.

Democritus stood out due to his peculiar fondness for alchemical beasts, but his inhuman experimental methods were met with disdain by his colleagues.

Many in alchemy were madmen, and Democritus was one of them. He had strayed further and further down the wrong path of alchemical beast research, eventually becoming a bloodthirsty fiend.

In the eyes of others, the alchemical beasts Democritus created were powerful but grotesquely ugly.

Yet Democritus saw them differently—he found his creations adorable, his obsession bordering on the perverse.

Because his alchemical research had begun to tarnish the royal image, this pitiful man was exiled, no longer a citizen of the Britannian Empire.

After years of wandering, Democritus encountered a patron in his life: Swinburne, the acting guildmaster of the Dark Adventurers Guild, Gōki Raizan.

Swinburne valued Democritus’s alchemical expertise and his reputation as a dragon specialist, hoping he could provide high-purity Saint-tier dragon blood.

After multiple negotiations, the acting guildmaster of Gōki Raizan and Democritus formed a partnership.

Swinburne would provide full financial support, while Democritus would produce Saint-tier dragon blood.

With mutual agreement, they established Democritus’s own alchemy research facility on this small island.

As for the Saint-tier dragon blood—once Democritus obtained Corona’s dragonified corpse, he had already extracted and purified it, delivering the first batch to Gōki Raizan.

With the Saint-tier dragon blood in hand, Democritus poured it entirely into his alchemical beast research, granting these little darlings partial dragonkin power, vastly boosting their strength.

During this time, Democritus created three most outstanding works—his trump cards, and the capital he would use to propose to the Lust Monarch.

If time could rewind many years ago—

If Democritus, with his alchemical beasts empowered by dragonkin strength, had used them as leverage to propose to Asmodeus, the outcome might have been entirely different.

His little darlings would not have been so easily defeated by Helena, the Demon General, nor would they have suffered the humiliation in the First Demon Lord Palace, forced to leave beautiful Sicily in bitter resentment.

So now, Democritus was brimming with confidence, believing his wings were fully grown, that he was worthy to stand as an equal to the Lust Monarch, and that marrying the most beautiful woman in the world was within reach!

The corridor seemed endless, like an underground maze.

The entire mountain had been hollowed out by Democritus, filled with danger and traps at every turn.

Holding a torch, Democritus advanced through the dark, deep corridor until he reached a place resembling an underground arena.

“Roar…”

Faint growls echoed repeatedly, as if he had entered some kind of monster nest. The stench of blood was overwhelming, making it difficult to breathe.

Democritus stopped, using his torch to light a nearby brazier. A series of *hiss* *hiss* sounds followed.

One after another, braziers flared to life in a circular pattern, illuminating the vast underground space.

The circular space resembled a beast-fighting arena, or perhaps a prison for caged beasts. The rock walls were stained with blood and other horrifying marks.

At the center were three grotesque, hideous giant beasts, each different and monstrous in appearance.

The first resembled a lion but had two heads, three tails, its body covered in gray scales, with bursts of cold mist exhaled from its mouth. Its fangs were razor-sharp.

The second looked like a mammoth but had black skin and red fur. Its long trunk was lined with barbs, and horns protruded from its forehead. Its forelegs were far thicker than its hind legs, making it appear grotesquely unbalanced.

The last one resembled a vulture, with hard gray feathers that gleamed. It had two massive pairs of wings, and its talons glinted with a cold light—clearly lethal weapons.

These three were Democritus’s masterpieces, imbued with near-peak power. A large portion of the Saint-tier dragon blood had been used on them.

Marijus, as one of the ascending dragons—the Frost Saint Dragon—possessed immense power. His blood was a treasure, capable of creating many powerful creatures.

These three alchemical beasts, made with Marijus’s blood, not only had terrifying strength but also dragonkin power. Their might was self-evident—they were far from weak.

Though these three masterpieces were much smaller than the toad alchemical beast outside, they were still enormous compared to humans. Their power was incomparable, the difference as vast as heaven and earth.

As for the materials used in their creation—apart from Saint-tier dragon blood—there were living humans, magical beasts, various melted gemstones, and more. The common trait among them was their low intelligence, possessing only the instinct to hunt and feed.

This was a problem Democritus had been trying to overcome his entire life, and his lifelong pursuit: to create alchemical beasts with higher intelligence, to rival the Creator.

The three alchemical beasts had been in a state of slumber, but the sudden light woke them. They began growling and looking around.

Upon seeing Democritus, they ferociously charged at him, as if starving and wanting to devour him!

This was the common flaw of alchemical beasts—low intelligence, unable to distinguish friend from foe, knowing only slaughter.

But Democritus had his own way of dealing with these creatures.

He took out a horn from his bosom, its surface covered in black text and spiraling patterns.

This horn was his treasure, specifically designed to bewitch dragonkin, with miraculous effects. It was called the *Dragon-Bewitching Flute*.

Democritus had discovered it in an ancient ruin during his youth.

“*Hmmmm…*”

As Democritus blew the horn, it emitted a strange, ancient sound that made one’s skin crawl.

The three powerful alchemical beasts immediately stopped in their tracks, swaying as if entering a controlled state.

Though they were alchemical beasts, they had been created with Saint-tier dragon blood, so they could not escape the flute’s influence.

“Now, now, my darlings, even if you’re hungry, you can’t eat me, can you? I’ve prepared something else for you…”

Democritus walked to the wall and fiddled with a mechanism. Suddenly, a large cage descended from above, filled with living humans.

They were part of the fishermen sent by Bō. Since there were too many to use, they were being used as feed for the alchemical beasts.

The ten humans inside the cage were terrified, their faces pale, their eyes wide with fear as they stared at the three alchemical beasts glaring at them.

“P-please, spare us, my lord! We’ll do anything, even be your slaves!”

“Yes, please, don’t kill us! We can do any work you ask!”

“My lord, have mercy! Don’t kill me, please don’t kill me!!!”

Pleas overlapped as the ten villagers scrambled to beg for Democritus’s mercy. Fear had robbed them of their sanity, and they wept uncontrollably.

“Shut up and throw them to me!” Democritus roared, his expression ferocious. “You worthless meat machines, what value do you have?! How dare you beg me for mercy? Your only worth is as food for my little darlings. Be happy! Isn’t being eaten while smiling the happiest thing?!”

The villagers fell silent, kneeling on the ground with expressions of despair, each believing they were doomed.

“Eat up, my darlings!” Democritus snapped his fingers and continued, “Eat your fill. You’ll have work to do later, and you can’t do that on an empty stomach, now can you~”

The three powerful alchemical beasts easily tore open the iron cage and began devouring the villagers, taking huge bites as if starved.

For a moment, crimson blood splattered everywhere, staining the surrounding rock walls. The villagers’ desperate, bloodcurdling screams echoed through the deep underground.

“What a wonderful sound…” Democritus wore an expression of ecstasy, looking up at a black coffin above. Inside was the crystallization of his life’s wisdom.

“I cannot fail. Miss Asmodeus, you will become my woman.”

“I’m going to fuck you so hard you’ll scream, and even if you beg for mercy, I won’t let you go!”

“HAHAHAHAHAHAHA!”

title: Chapter 35 — Action
content:
Chapter 35 — Action

Volume 8 · Chapter 35

The battered *William* was moored at the shore.

The entire hull had run aground on the beach, looking utterly pitiful.

Thanks to Captain Dennis’s wise decision, the death toll was low—most had survived.

Now, the survivors were on the shore, tending to their immediate needs.

The crew unloaded essential supplies from the *William*, seemingly preparing to stay and repair the ship for a while.

Captain Dennis slowly removed his captain’s hat and pressed it to his chest, gazing at the wrecked *William* with a hint of melancholy on his sharp-featured face.

The *William* had been with him for over thirty years—it felt like family. Seeing it in this state was heartbreaking.

Alice surveyed their current situation. The surrounding jungle was dense, and a towering mountain loomed before them. The evil alchemist was likely hiding there.

Merlin stumbled off the ship, his legs still shaky from the earlier ordeal.

He had even thrown away the life rings he’d been carrying—none of them had been useful in the end.

They owed Captain Dennis their lives. If not for his experience, the *William* would have sunk halfway here.

Merlin followed Alice’s gaze, sighing as he placed his hands on his hips.

“Finally on land… that scared the hell out of me…”

Cecilia was helped off the ship by Kael, who seemed worried she might fall.

Her face was pale, her expression blank—she was clearly still shaken.

When the accident happened, she had been napping in her cabin. Then, suddenly, the ship was about to sink.

This was her first time experiencing something so dangerous. The sheer terror of it all had left her deeply unsettled.

Kael glanced at her. Though he was still shaken himself, he couldn’t help but try to comfort her.

“Are you alright, Miss?”

“…Y-Yes…” Cecilia stammered.

“If you’re scared, I could… pat your head?” Kael ventured cautiously.

“Wha—?!” Cecilia’s face flushed red. She shoved Kael away, huffing, “What the hell? Do I look like a child to you?!”

“No, no, I just thought you were still shaken and wanted to comfort you,” Kael said awkwardly.

“…I don’t need it! So what if we almost sank? It’s no big deal. Look at me—I’m not panicking at all.” Cecilia’s legs trembled as she spoke, completely unconvincing.

“I’m really sorry this happened. I didn’t expect an ambush at sea,” Kael said, full of self-reproach. He felt terrible for putting her in danger.

“Forget it. I don’t feel like blaming you~”

Cecilia waved her hand dismissively, then noticed Captain Dennis standing nearby, his face etched with worry.

She realized she bore some responsibility for this mess.

After all, she was the one who had called him here for help. Now that the *William* was damaged, it was only right to compensate him.

So Cecilia walked over, cleared her throat, and spoke in a polite tone.

“Captain Dennis, I’m sorry about what happened.”

“It’s fine. For sailors like us, this is just another day at sea. The ocean is a lawless place—battles are inevitable. This level of damage is something I’ve always been prepared for.” Captain Dennis spoke with neither joy nor sorrow, like a mature man who saw no reason to blame Cecilia—especially since she was the young lady of the Rose family.

“You don’t need to worry. I’ll compensate you in the name of the Rose family. You won’t suffer any major losses,” Cecilia said earnestly.

Captain Dennis looked down at her in surprise. He had initially assumed Cecilia was a spoiled, unreasonable brat, but now he saw she had a kind heart.

The current losses were severe for the crew, so there was no reason to refuse her goodwill.

Dennis gave a slight bow, expressing his gratitude.

“Thank you for your generosity, Lady Cecilia. If you’re truly willing to compensate us, that would be a great help. I speak for the entire crew of the *William* when I say we’re grateful.”

“Don’t mention it. As long as you’re working for me, I won’t let my people suffer,” Cecilia said haughtily, though inside, she was overjoyed. At first, she had found Captain Dennis’s pride irritating, but now he had lowered his proud head before her. It gave her a real sense of accomplishment.

“Next, my crew and I will perform some basic repairs on the *William*. Also…” Dennis pulled something from his coat and handed it to Cecilia. “Take this.”

“This…?” Cecilia examined the cylindrical object in her hand. There seemed to be a pull cord at the bottom.

“It’s a smoke signal. Kael mentioned you’re going to confront the evil alchemist. If you encounter danger you can’t handle, set this off. We’ll come to your rescue as quickly as possible.” Dennis spoke seriously, clearly pledging his loyalty.

“Alright…” Cecilia smiled as she tucked the signal away, thinking it might come in handy.

Johnston, his face still pale, crawled off the *William*. The moment his hands touched solid ground, he was overcome with shock and joy.

“Land! It’s land! Oh my god! I’m alive! HAHAHA~”

Johnston clutched the sand in his hands, his eyes filled with more affection than if he’d seen his own father. After all that seasickness, he had never loved dry land more.

Alice looked toward the distant mountains, feeling they needed to act quickly. The evil alchemist still had the kidnapped fishermen in his grasp.

If they delayed any longer, those innocent people would be in even greater danger. It was best to resolve this as soon as possible.

“Everyone! There’s no time to lose—let’s move out. The alchemist’s hideout is likely in those mountains.”

“I’m fine with whatever. We can leave whenever,” Merlin replied nonchalantly.

“Don’t we need to rest a little?” Kael asked doubtfully. After such a dangerous ordeal, a short break would help them stay in peak condition.

“No need. Let’s get moving,” Cecilia said, sounding almost excited. This was tied to her own interests—she could barely wait.

Kael felt a cold sweat trickle down his forehead. *Fighting while exhausted? That can’t be good…*

“…” Alice knitted her brows. “We don’t have time to rest. That alchemist has a lot of fishermen imprisoned. Every minute we waste puts them in more danger.”

“Hmm?” Merlin caught a whiff of something off. He probed cautiously, “You damn fool… did you go and promise something ridiculous again, making this mission even harder?”

“…What was I supposed to do? We can’t just ignore people in danger, can we? Even if our main goal is to resolve the crisis at sea, saving innocent lives is important too.” Alice paused, then added with a sour tone, “And someone had to clean up the mess after *someone* spent last night cuddling with an underage girl.”

“???” Merlin’s face twisted in embarrassment, his mind filled with question marks. *This nagging shrew… is she mocking me? It’s not my fault she threw herself at me!*

As the four of them debated, Johnston strode over, looking completely revitalized now that he was on solid ground. He shot them a disdainful glance.

“Thanks for the ride. You all can keep chatting here—I’ll be going ahead.”

Johnston waved them off without a backward glance and marched into the forest, brimming with confidence.

“For me, this mission is a walk in the park~”

“I could clear it with just a few spells.”

“Out of gratitude for the boat ride, I’ll even leave you some soup to drink…”

title: Chapter 36 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 36 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 36

The thicket on the island looked very dense.

It was gloomy, as if no trace of light could seep through, and from time to time came eerie howls like wild beasts.

The sound of branches slapping against each other always gave the feeling that someone was whispering nearby.

Although Johnson was young, his bearing was cautious—truly an experienced adventurer.

At this moment his expression was a bit unnatural, his face ugly, and a few strands of black hair had slipped down onto his forehead.

As for the reason, of course it was because of—

"You guys, why are you clinging to me so desperately?"

Behind Johnson, Merlin walked closely behind, showing no intention of keeping his distance.

"What can I say? We're all heading to that mountain. We're just... walking together." Merlin answered helplessly, not wanting to be misunderstood.

"That's right. You think anyone wants to follow you? It's just a coincidence that we're going the same way!" Cecilia chimed in, supporting Merlin.

"Just a coincidence, you think I'd believe that? This is the first time I'm going to the mountains, and you're clinging to me like a shadow. Even your excuses aren't worth writing down. Johnson paused, his tone impatient as he said, "Let me be upfront—I have no interest in playing escort for you guys. Surely it's too shameless to ask me to be your free bodyguard?"

"Ah?!" Cecilia immediately got upset, speaking in her little fan's tone, "We have Merlin-sama with us. Do we really need this brat to be our bodyguard?"

Johnson turned his head to look at Merlin, recalling what happened on the William, and felt this man was not easy to deal with. He was probably the strongest among them, reaching Saint-tier strength.

But compared to himself? That was worlds apart. Even if he was Saint-tier, what did that matter?

Saint-tier was just a threshold between strong and weak. The gap in actual strength was still insurmountable.

Johnson was still very confident in himself. He was a famous magic genius far and wide. How could he be weaker than some unknown Saint-tier?

"Don't be so conceited. The enemy is an alchemist who needs a laboratory. Besides being built into the mountains, nowhere else would suit..."

Alice frowned at Johnson, adding, "It's such a simple truth that anyone would understand. It's not like we're deliberately following you."

"Yes, we know you're the magic genius from Ireland. But please don't look at us with condescension." Keil said politely.

"Hmph!" Johnson scoffed, his face arrogant as he said, "Suit yourselves. If you get into danger, don't think I'll spare you just because we're colleagues."

Everyone was speechless, thinking Johnson was being petty, always suspicious of others.

"Hey, Alice, this brat is really something..." Merlin whispered behind Alice's back.

"Yeah, he's a total narcissist. Probably been spoiled rotten and has gotten conceited." Alice nodded in agreement.

The two reached a rare consensus, which was quite unexpected.

"If I had a son or daughter, I'd definitely not want them to be like this." Merlin sighed, thinking Johnson had great potential—a 14-year-old Saint-tier who mastered all elements of magic was quite a freak. But his personality was too bad, destined to amount to nothing.

"You'll have a son or daughter? Don't be ridiculous. Who would be blind enough to look at you?" Alice showed a disdainful expression.

"I'm just using a metaphor. I'm sure I wouldn't like this brat." Merlin shrugged, his expression helpless as he said.

Alice thought about it and nodded, agreeing, "I don't wish for my future children to be like this brat either. So arrogant, he'll get beaten up sooner or later."

"When the time comes, I'll shamelessly grab the kill. This kind of behavior—snatching little kids' candy—feels oddly satisfying~" Merlin wore a very evil smile.

"Ew... that's a weird taste..." Alice groaned, feeling complicated. This guy was always interested in strange things.

While Merlin and Alice were chatting like this, the figure ahead—Johnson—suddenly stopped, his expression turning alert.

"What's wrong?" Cecilia was puzzled, not knowing what was happening.

"Something's coming... Keil seems to have sensed something. And there are a lot of them."

The Merlin and Alice behind them also grew slightly alert, and the surroundings filled with a "rustle, rustle, rustle" sound.

The footsteps came pattering, clearly on four legs, and the complex rhythm indicated there were many.

"What kind of thing?" Cecilia moved closer to Keil, seeming a bit worried.

"Probably those annoying monsters we encountered before. They seem to particularly like making killing machines." Alice's brows were tightly knit, sensing a foul stench from all directions. Without further thought, she knew they had been surrounded.

"Really? It's those annoying monsters again, and so many of them... Cecilia hid behind Keil, feeling the pressure. But it was fine since Merlin was nearby, so nothing should go wrong.

"They're annoying? I can just use a spell and easily take them down. It's like cutting through butter." Johnson waved his hands with a carefree smile, not forgetting to mock, "The reason you find them annoying is probably because you're too weak?"

"Hah, they're just trash. What's there to be proud of? Merlin-sama defeats far more than you. What are you even worth!" Cecilia, the little fan, immediately defended Merlin's reputation and attacked Johnson.

Alice looked at Cecilia with complicated feelings, secretly feeling a bit jealous of how good this fan was to Merlin.

"I'm just lacking true strength. Don't underestimate me, or you'll regret it." Johnson's expression turned serious, wanting to show off his power, prove himself, and shut Cecilia up.

Cecilia was frightened by Johnson's determined gaze and fell silent.

Although Johnson was young, that aura of a strongman was genuine.

With his reputation backing him, he was certainly not someone to be mocked lightly.

The thicket rustled and swayed, and suddenly a huge crowd of snarling and clawing alchemical beasts charged out!

"Grr... woof! woof!"

They had different shapes and colors of fur, with only one common feature: sharp fangs and a fierce, unafraid nature.

The alchemical beasts had long since caught the scent of human presence, all driven by hunger, rushing forward in a frenzy.

The alchemical beasts gathered together, forming a dense, endless mass. No one could tell how many of these vicious monsters there were.

"Weak little brats daring to come before me? Either you're reckless, or you're just lowly creatures without wisdom!"

Johnson raised his right hand, and his magic ring immediately glowed golden. The fire elements in the air grew restless.

"Die!"

The raging flames soared up like an explosion, magnificent and terrifying, erupting from Johnson's hand and incinerating the front row of alchemical beasts.

This Saint-tier magic was called "Wildfire," with extremely strong offensive power. The explosive flames could easily blow apart anything, a truly spectacular sight.

But Johnson wasn't done yet. He raised his left hand, and the other ring glowed as well.

A fierce wind suddenly blew, carrying sharp wind blades in a fan shape, striking the massive crowd of alchemical beasts.

The same Saint-tier magic, "Storm Roar," created violent winds that made the enemies unable to move forward, and the wind blades could cause widespread damage—both offensive and defensive.

But that wasn't all. The wind assisted the fire, instantly multiplying the power of the flame attack, unleashing something like a magical ultimate technique!

"Wildfire" combined with "Storm Roar"—this combo had excellent results, making people involuntarily break into cold sweats.

The wind swept along with the flames, tearing through everything in its path. The destructive aura was chilling, as if it would consume everything before it!

In an instant, all the alchemical beasts that had launched their surprise attack were buried in the wind and fire. Terrible screams that made one's hair stand on end echoed endlessly, with not a single survivor.

The flames faded, and the ground was scorched red. The thicket ahead was completely burned to ashes, with scattered flames barely clinging to life.

The ground was littered with burned alchemical beast corpses, some already turned to ash.

"Hmph!"

Johnson let out a cold sweat, quietly lowering his arms, then slowly turned his head, his eyes looking down disdainfully at the people behind him.

Sparks drifted in the air, lifting his gray hair. The air was filled with the smell of grilled meat.

Johnson smiled calmly, his red earring swaying as he said with an arrogant tone,

"The truly powerful aren't just all talk..."

title: Chapter 37 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 37 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 8 · Chapter 37

Having unleashed two big moves back to back, Johnson didn't so much as pant for breath—the depth and steadiness of his magic power was truly astonishing.

Aside from Merlin, the other three now looked at Johnson differently, feeling that this hot-tempered little pretty boy was a bit too strong!

Kyle and Cecilia were both stunned, eyes wide, thinking that Johnson was simply a monster-tier mage, leaving Saint-tier mages of the same level eating his dust by several streets—the power wasn't even on the same level!

Johnson's understanding of magic had indeed reached a very high standard. Compared to Johnson, other mages'差距 was obvious at a glance—the gap was no ordinary one. Truly worthy of being hailed as Ireland's magical prodigy; his strength was exceptionally formidable!

Alice's understanding of magic was higher than Kyle's and Cecilia's, so she could see even more. The two Saint-tier spells Johnson had casually cast were extremely difficult and could not be released lightly. To anyone who understood magic, this left them nothing to do but marvel inwardly.

Not to mention how profound Johnson's magic power was—being able to casually cast two Saint-tier spells, and knowing how to combine them to amplify their power into something like a magic secret art of devastation.

That alone already left the vast majority of mages far behind; his command of magic had reached a shocking degree.

Moreover, he could cast them simultaneously—two different schools of magic, neither interfering with the other, complementing each other. Aside from Johnson, Alice really couldn't think of a second person capable of such a thing.

As for affinity with all magic elements, that was purely Johnson's personal talent, something that simply couldn't be compared.

Alice made her comparisons in her heart, and though she resisted it inwardly, she had to admit that Johnson's strength was—really that of a genius.

"Now you finally understand the gap in strength, huh? I don't like showing off—you all forced me to demonstrate my power. Feeling pretty hopeless now?" Johnson waved a hand and strode toward the mountain range ahead. "Stay far away from me. I have no intention of letting you hold back my pace. Trying to steal my credit is simply a fool's dream."

"Huh!?" Cecilia's expression turned displeased, and she muttered sourly, "You're only a teensy bit impressive, that's all? You're nowhere near Lord Merlin. Right, Kyle?"

"Y-yeah, that's right," Kyle replied with an awkward laugh, thinking to himself that it wasn't a teensy bit impressive—it was insanely impressive.

Merlin watched Johnson's back, unconsciously stroking his chin, thinking with great interest—

This fellow...

Was a bit interesting.

Beneath the pitch-black earth.

Democritus had made every preparation.

He was just waiting for this group of death-seeking fools to walk right into his hands.

The entire mountain had been remodeled by alchemy, filled with all kinds of mechanisms that Democritus could activate with ease.

If a battle broke out here, Democritus would feel no pressure at all—he would be delighted.

Because he could freely use the alchemical mechanisms to turn the entire underground into his own playground, fraught with peril at every turn.

And at this moment, Democritus was hiding in a secret chamber, watching everything outside through a crystal ball. He already knew everything that had just happened.

That group of alchemical beasts had also been personally dispatched by Democritus to launch the attack, with the purpose of finding out who was the strongest fighter among this party—to get a clear picture for himself, so that when the time came he could counter them accordingly.

After seeing Johnson's strength, Democritus was genuinely taken aback, and after glancing at his mithril adventurer's certificate, he was thoroughly shaken.

He hadn't expected these filthy villagers to hire such a powerful mithril adventurer.

Who was Johnson? With fame that great, how could Democritus not have heard of him—the prodigy mage held aloft by all, a genius adored like the moon among stars.

The frogman darlings he had deployed at sea must have been easily wiped out by this Johnson as well. Aside from him, no one else in this group should have been capable of it.

Facing the dazzling genius mage of Ireland, Democritus felt a trace of pressure—but it vanished in an instant, immediately replaced by a face full of smugness.

In the past, Democritus might have been scared pants-wettingly terrified, but now he was a completely different man; in his hands he held power rivaling a nation's elite.

The three masterpieces in his grasp had been crafted from massive quantities of dragon blood. Though they couldn't match the Frost Saint Dragon in strength, they could come astonishingly close.

Add in the draconic talent bonus—scales with the ability to resist magic—and Johnson running into those three fellows was simply his bad luck.

Democritus slowly turned around, gazing at the various mechanisms and buttons before him, muttering with a meaningful smile—

"The fourteen-year-old Saint-tier powerhouse Johnson, is it?

"How interesting.

"But his legend ends today, because my masterpieces are going to grind him into the dirt."

The party's destination was the mountain range.

So even though Johnson told Merlin and the others to keep their distance, they still had to travel together.

Intuition told them that the entrance to Democritus's laboratory was near the foot of the mountain.

As it turned out, Johnson's sense of direction was so bad he couldn't find the place at all, and nearly got lost.

In the end it was Alice who found the entrance, calling the others to go in together.

Johnson felt his face couldn't quite take it, so he could only say with deep significance—

"Hmph. I found this entrance ages ago. I just didn't say anything—I was testing your intelligence. I didn't expect your IQ to be not bad at all~"

Johnson's transparent face-saving nonsense left Merlin and company speechless. So he's a lost cause with directions, that's all. Would it kill him to just admit it?

After entering the interior of the mountain range, there was an endless tunnel stretching on without any visible end.

Johnson walked at the very front on his own, though he had no idea of the direction—but even a blind cat bumps into a dead mouse now and then, and walking in a straight line couldn't be wrong.

Merlin and Kyle walked in front, keeping Alice and Cecilia protected at the very back, looking every bit the gentlemen.

"I keep having this ominous feeling..." Cecilia felt uneasy and edged closer to Alice, seeking a sense of security.

"Don't scare yourself. We've only just come in—no one would set up traps right at the entrance," Alice answered, drawing on past experience.

"Rest assured, Lady Cecilia. If danger appears, I will absolutely block it in front of you." Like a loyal dog, Kyle blazed with burning devotion.

"Mm, you'd better keep your word..." Cecilia said, her face flushing red—probably electrified by Kyle's earnest cluelessness.

"Yeah, I would absolutely never break my promise! Protecting my lady is my duty!" Kyle declared with utmost seriousness on his face.

Alice stood to the side with a smile that didn't reach her eyes, the lovey-dovey bomb these two had detonated making her whole body uncomfortable; she nearly couldn't hold back from barking "woof woof" in protest.

Compared to Kyle, her nominal husband in name didn't seem to show the slightest reaction. Damn you, Merlin, hurry up and say something? Even comforting me a little would be fine....

Alice fixed her gaze on Merlin, firing off resentful brainwaves again and again, hoping to hear some warm words from his mouth as well.

Heaven rewards the diligent. Merlin seemed to sense Alice's resentment-laden stare, and with a moment's thought he knew exactly what was going on.

Merlin turned back with an expressionless face, the corner of his mouth twisting to the side, and said in an indifferent tone—

"What are you glaring at?

"If we run into danger, you'll be the first one I throw out—this washboard of yours makes a perfect decoy."

"Heh heh. Pretty mean, right? Bet you didn't see that coming? =

title: Chapter 38 — Old Man
content:
Chapter 38 — Old Man

Volume 8 · Chapter 38

Merlin speaks with absolutely no courtesy; getting a warm word out of him is harder than reaching the sky.

“....

Alice glared unhappily at Merlin, feeling that this guy not only failed to say anything warm but actually wanted to harm her, simply terrible.

Originally, being tortured by the flashing lights of the two beside her was uncomfortable, and she hoped Merlin would help her out of this.

The result was lol; indeed, Merlin is still that Merlin, so don't expect him to become some kind of househusband.

Alice had bitterness in her heart, but didn't dare say it out loud, especially since Merlin was originally a person who didn't know how to read the atmosphere?

"What are you glaring at? Don't want to listen?" Merlin raised his eyebrows, looking provocative; if this were in an arena, the opponent would have already been unable to resist and thrown a punch.

"Ah!?" Alice's forehead veins jumped as she angrily said, "Why are you looking back? Do you have anything to say to you? Turn around quickly, looking at your effeminate face makes me want to vomit, vomit~

Merlin froze for a moment, wondering if the resentment brainwaves he had sensed just now were incorrect; it shouldn't be.

Could it be that Alice was just cursing me in her heart, not asking me to make her look bad?

Merlin cleared his throat to cover his embarrassment and said carelessly.

"You still want to kick me into the sea with one foot, so this is my way of revenge against you; it's very fair.

"Hmph~!" Alice hugged her fake chest and angrily snorted.

Cecilia and Kyle watched this clearly from the side, thinking in unison, what the hell? This is the way this couple expresses love? It's really quite special.

As for Johnson, he just glanced back and disdainfully complained in his heart, stupid adults, full of mating thoughts, is flying chess fun?

Just as the atmosphere was slightly awkward, Merlin suddenly shouted, scaring everyone.

Kyle beside him immediately became alert, gripping the long spear in his hand, while Johnson in front also looked back warily, Saint-tier magic slowly surging.

Alice was also shocked, taken aback by Merlin's sudden shout.

Cecilia tightly hugged Alice beside her and threw herself into the embrace of the fake breasts, her expression full of big written "confused," not knowing what was going on?

....What are you doing! ? Suddenly shouting, are you trying to scare a few people to death?" Alice couldn't help but complain a few words loudly.

"Is it monsters again? ! Or something even more terrifying!" Cecilia's face was pale, very worried about meeting danger at a time like this.

Looking at that pitch-black corridor, unable to see the end, no one knew what danger was lurking ahead.

"Merlin Lord, what's wrong with you? What happened?" Kyle had been on guard for a long time without finding anything and couldn't help but ask Merlin's situation.

"....... Merlin's face turned black, wanting to speak but stopping, his body not moving at all, as if worried about triggering something.

"Uncle, did you trigger some hidden weapon?" Johnson said thoughtfully, raising his entire body's alertness, as no one could know what dangerous mechanism lay in this deep corridor.

"I am not Uncle, you stinky brat!" Merlin cursed directly out of anger.

"Merlin... Merlin Lord, did you really trigger some mechanism?" Kyle's tone couldn't help but become worried; if some danger was triggered, it would be quite bad, especially since the space was too narrow to dodge back and forth conveniently.

"Hmm, I feel like my foot stepped on something, and the ground grid point sank a bit." Merlin's brows furrowed as he continued to speak awkwardly, "But looking at the current situation, I feel that as soon as my foot leaves the ground, it will trigger.

"Okay..." Johnson's expression was helpless as he faintly said, "I'll say it upfront, I won't meddle in other people's business.

"Go play with mud over there, who needs you?" Merlin said expressionlessly with a sarcastic remark, thinking this stinky brat was taking himself way too seriously.

Johnson's face turned black, his mood bad after being retorted by Merlin; he had originally thought that if Merlin were willing to bow and beg, he could help out.

As for now? Johnson had made up his mind to not care.

"Why did Johnson, who was walking in front, not step on the mechanism, but you stepped on it?" Alice asked depressedly, feeling helpless towards Merlin.

"Merlin Lord's luck is really bad, okay.... Cecilia isn't helping Merlin speak this time either, slightly a bit nervous.

"You bunch of bastards, don't say cool words at a time like this, okay? Can the current situation blame me?" Merlin's face turned black, his brows furrowed high.

Alice's expression was expressionless as she thought, calculating the distance, some mechanisms should have appeared by now; if it were too calm, it wouldn't be normal.

"Your luck is indeed bad to a certain realm; so many people are fine, but you stepped on it, tsk tsk....

"Shut up, I don't want to be mocked by you, this European; even if my face is black, you roast me? There's no law here! Careful I loosen my foot and shout Allah Akbar! BOOM! We all finish together!" Merlin couldn't help but threaten, a wave of "I am African, I fear no one" momentum rushing towards him.

"...Don't mess around.." Alice retreated half a step, worried that this guy Merlin might twitch his brain and take revenge on society.

"Yeah, calm down, Merlin Lord, I didn't mean to mock you... Cecilia said shivering, hiding behind Alice.

"Hmph, all be honest, don't stimulate me." Merlin threatened smugly.

"Then Merlin Lord, what should we do now?" Kyle asked with a serious expression, worried that something might go wrong.

"In a moment, when I take my foot off the ground, you quickly retreat and guard against danger; there shouldn't be a problem." Merlin thought of a countermeasure.

"Okay, we'll do that." Kyle nodded and turned back to talk to the girls, "Ladies please retreat, and if there is danger, run for your lives first."

Cecilia and Alice nodded and retreated slightly further, staying far away from Merlin, this extreme element holding a bomb.

"I'm about to lift my foot, everyone pay attention... Merlin reminded seriously.

Everyone became alert, raising their spirits to the fullest, preparing to deal with the next situation, the atmosphere was not just generally depressing.

Merlin took a deep breath and suddenly retreated two steps, gripping his sword tightly and posing to draw his blade, whoever dared to rush up would be cut.

The others also took a confused breath, checking the situation nervously, fearing the appearance of unknown danger.

Result, nothing happened.

"Hmm!?" Merlin relaxed and scratched his head, "Looks... nothing happened? Haha, false alarm~

"Really a big surprise...." Johnson pouted, feeling that Merlin's behavior didn't make him look like a strong person at all, he simply came to make a joke.

Kyle guarded for a while and found that there was really nothing, immediately relaxing his breath, "Cecilia Lord, nothing happened, there was simply no mechanism hidden.

No sound came from behind, appearing extremely quiet.

"Cecilia Lord?"

Kyle slowly turned back and saw that the two girls behind him had disappeared, leaving a deep bottomless big hole on the ground.

He quickly ran over to check; they had been fine just now, but in the blink of an eye they were gone, they definitely fell down.

"Cecilia Lord! ! !"

Merlin became nervous and turned to look behind, only then discovering the bad situation; it turned out the mechanism had already been triggered.

In the dark and bottomless cave, Alice's annoyed friendly greeting voice faintly came.

"Merlin! I f*** your grandpa!'

"F*** your grandpa!

"Your grandpa!

"Grandpa!"
