title: Chapter 39 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 39 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 8 · Chapter 39

A bead of cold sweat slid down Merlin's forehead as he maintained an awkward yet polite smile.

What in the world was this? These traps were absurd—attacking people from behind?

Not that it was his fault, though. Who could have predicted such a ridiculous, inescapable mechanism?

Merlin could faintly hear Alice’s "greetings" in the distance and didn’t even know how to respond.

"Lady Cecily!" Kael collapsed to the ground, pounding his chest in despair, his voice trembling with panic. He never expected the young lady to fall. Losing all composure, he wailed, "Why were you so careless?!"

"How could you just leave like this? What am I supposed to do without you?!"

"It’s all my fault for letting my guard down! I’ve doomed you to this disaster!"

"Even if I return, how can I face the Duke?!"

"Lady Cecily, I’ve failed you! It’s all my fault—I’m unworthy of being a knight...."

Merlin stared at Kael in stunned silence. They weren’t even dead! He was talking as if Alice and Cecily had already perished. Wasn’t this treason? Stop with the nonsensical doom-and-gloom already!

"Lady Cecily, I once swore to protect you with my life..." Kael clenched his fists, hot tears streaming down his face, his voice thick with grief. "And now you’ve left me behind first. This is my shame as a knight! Even if I die to atone, it won’t make up for my failure. Rest assured, Lady Cecily—even in death, I will follow you!"

Merlin’s face darkened with exasperation. This guy was too damn earnest. Besides "idiot," he couldn’t think of another word to describe him.

Seeing the dimwitted Kael about to leap down after them, Merlin jolted in alarm. Who knew what horrors lurked below? Was he trying to get himself killed?!

Merlin stepped forward and smacked Kael’s blockhead hard.

"Calm down! Alice and Cecily aren’t dead. What are you losing your mind over?"

Kael rubbed his forehead, his face flushed, struggling to speak. "...But Merlin, Lady Cecily... she..."

"Yeah, yeah, I get it. They’re both fine, perfectly safe. Didn’t you hear Alice cursing me out just now?" Merlin spread his hands in explanation.

"But... what if something *did* happen to Lady Cecily...?" Kael’s expression was miserable, his heart heavy with worry.

"Relax. Alice had enough energy to insult me, so clearly neither of them is hurt. If they were, they wouldn’t have the presence of mind to greet my ancestors." Merlin said lightly, amused by how devotedly Kael played the loyal hound. He probably would’ve happily wiped Cecily’s backside if she asked.

"Merlin, you’re oversimplifying things!" Kael’s eyes welled up again, his voice trembling. "Lady Cecily has *never* been in a situation like this before! She must be terrified, cowering in a corner, shaking and crying. She *absolutely* can’t be left alone!"

Merlin clutched his face, now thoroughly darkened. *This bastard would die without Cecily?* How pathetic.

Impatient, Merlin grabbed Kael by the collar and barked, "Pull yourself together! You’re not her father. What’s the point of agonizing over something so trivial? She needs to learn independence, got it?!"

"E-Excuse me, Merlin...?" Kael’s eyes widened, his mind going blank under Merlin’s glare.

"Besides, Alice is with her. That girl’s great at taking care of people. There’s nothing to worry about. Our priority is completing this mission." Merlin spoke seriously.

Kael pondered for a moment, then his expression turned solemn. "I understand, Merlin. You’re telling me to toughen up. This is my greatest trial, my biggest obstacle to growth. If I can’t even endure a single setback, then I don’t deserve to become as strong as you, right?"

"???" Merlin’s face twisted in confusion. *What the hell?* Why did everything he say get twisted into some grand life lesson by these people?

"I see what you mean now, Merlin..." Kael wore an enlightened expression, nodding earnestly. "It’s not about always protecting Lady Cecily by her side. I need to help her grow, to learn independence. That’s what’s best for her future. As expected of Merlin—every word you say is packed with wisdom."

"...Yeah." Merlin said nothing, just gave an awkward nod, not bothering to shatter Kael’s delusions.

"But... wasn’t this all *your* fault, Merlin?" Kael harbored a hint of resentment but didn’t dare voice it, instead giving Merlin a pitiful look.

"Ah..." Merlin coughed twice to cover his embarrassment. "Don’t dwell on the details~"

Kael stared at him with a complicated expression.

"Let’s go. Alice and the others will probably find a way out."

Merlin turned around—only to find Johnson had vanished without a trace, leaving behind an empty space.

No need to overthink it. Merlin knew this guy had ditched them to race ahead and take out the Alchemist Hydra himself.

Merlin’s face darkened as he clenched his fists, grinding his teeth. "That little brat... can’t take a joke."

The entire mountain range was rigged with traps.

Alice and Cecily had only triggered the first one.

This trap, as ridiculous as it seemed, served a clear purpose: to scatter invaders and pick them off one by one.

Below was a separate space, with a deadly alchemical beast guarding the end.

But Democritus would never have imagined that his plan to divide their forces had failed completely—both Merlin and Johnson were now heading straight for him.

Below was a pool of stagnant water, so when Alice and Cecily fell, they weren’t injured—just thoroughly drenched, looking utterly disheveled.

The two girls climbed onto the shore, staring into the pitch-black unknown before them, filled with mystery and danger.

Scattered torches faintly illuminated their surroundings. The rock walls were stained with dried blood, sending chills down their spines.

Even the pool behind them was a deep crimson, as if dyed by the blood of some creature.

Cecily, as soon as she scrambled ashore, began sniffling and complaining, her entire body filthy. "What *is* this water?! It stinks to high heaven! How could there be such a disgusting place? My clothes..."

Alice wrung out her clothes and shook her silver hair, finally feeling a bit better.

Then she surveyed their surroundings, sensing an ominous presence. From the depths, a faint, ghostly wail seemed to echo.

"What *is* this place..."

title: Chapter 40 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 40 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 40

Alice’s delicate brows knitted together as the oppressive darkness around her seemed to brim with unseen dangers.

She had to be careful—one wrong move could spell disaster.

Alice wasn’t inexperienced; she had a sharp instinct for danger honed by her adventures. The air here reeked of blood, thick and suffocating. This was no place of peace. From what she could tell, this looked like some kind of testing ground. The scattered corpses of alchemical beasts around them only confirmed her suspicion.

And indeed, this was where Democritus conducted his experiments on alchemical beasts—testing their combat capabilities. Those that failed to meet his standards were slaughtered and discarded by the blood pool. That crimson pond was likely formed from the blood of all those defective creatures, its stench so foul that Cecilia couldn’t stop frowning.

Alice tilted her head back, staring up at the massive hole they had fallen through. It was far too high to climb. If they wanted to reunite with Merlin and the others, they’d have to find another way out. There was no other choice.

But the situation was far from ideal. Unknown dangers could be lurking, waiting for them. One misstep could mean death. This was the lair of that wicked alchemist, after all—filled with alchemical beasts, and perhaps even more terrifying creatures beyond that.

A faint, mournful wail echoed through the darkness. Alice couldn’t tell if it was the cry of a human or the hungry roar of an alchemical beast.

Cecilia, however, seemed completely oblivious to the danger. She wrung out her damp, filthy clothes with a scowl, grumbling nonstop.

“What kind of cursed place is this?! It’s filthy! The stench is unbearable! I’ve had enough—I want to go home! I’m a daughter of the Rosé family! How dare I be reduced to this disgusting state? It’s an absolute disgrace!”

Alice couldn’t help but feel a headache coming on. Cecilia wasn’t a bad person, but she was being far too fussy. Just because her clothes were dirty, she was already ready to give up.

“Why did only the two of us fall down here? That idiot Kael better hurry up and come save me! Moron, imbecile, fool—my knight is completely useless…” Cecilia’s eyes welled with tears. Fear gnawed at her, and she could only take it out on the unfortunate Kael.

Alice sighed in exasperation and spoke seriously. “It’s too high up. Even Merlin and the others wouldn’t be able to reach us from there. We’ll have to find our own way out.”

“How is this possible? If the two of us weaklings stick together, won’t that just make things worse? Why am I so unlucky…” Cecilia’s face fell into a pitiful expression. The thought of having to rely on Alice filled her with despair.

After all, Alice was nowhere near as powerful as Merlin. Only a strong companion could provide a real sense of security, and Alice simply didn’t measure up.

“Hey, hey, hey—you’re being way too harsh!” Alice’s face darkened in indignation. “You’re the weak one here, not me. Don’t just lump us together like that!”

“Huh? Compared to Lord Merlin, aren’t you just as weak?” Cecilia argued, full of self-righteousness.

“…Ahem!” Alice coughed lightly, masking her embarrassment. “Who would even compare themselves to that inhuman monster? It’s impossible to match him.”

“What do we do now? Without Lord Merlin here, it’s so dangerous! That damn Kael—why didn’t he jump down with me? He’s so disloyal!” Cecilia pouted, complaining as she nervously scanned their surroundings. A foreboding sense of danger crept over her.

“Stop complaining. Instead of standing here whining, we should look for another exit. Maybe we’ll find a way out directly.” Alice tried to stay optimistic.

“No, I have a bad feeling about this. What if we just stay here and wait for Lord Merlin to come rescue us? That sounds much safer.” Cecilia’s expression was earnest. She genuinely believed this was the better plan.

“Staying put is the most dangerous option. There might still be monsters around here. They’d probably catch our scent.” Alice reasoned that if they lingered, they might attract even more creatures.

“…” Cecilia’s fear took hold, her face draining of color. She muttered to herself, “…But without Lord Merlin’s power, if we wander around blindly, we might get lost.”

“You need to believe in yourself sometimes. Always relying on others will backfire one day. Why not try saving yourself for once?” Alice was growing increasingly frustrated with this spoiled noble girl. She couldn’t handle even the slightest setback.

“That’s impossible! What can you and I even do?” Cecilia deflated like a punctured balloon, completely giving up.

“Then do whatever you want. I’m going to find a way out on my own.” Alice turned away without hesitation, not even glancing back.

Cecilia panicked. Alice was her last lifeline. If Alice left her behind, she’d be utterly helpless.

After all, Cecilia was just a traditional priestess. How was she supposed to fight? Unless she was a battle priestess, that was a different story.

She quickly grabbed her staff and, sniffling, hurried after Alice. She didn’t dare move alone—not when Alice was stronger than Kael.

“Wait for me, Miss Alice! Don’t leave me behind!”

The corridor twisted and turned in a slow, winding path.

Alice held a torch, moving cautiously through the darkness.

Cecilia followed closely behind, clutching the hem of Alice’s clothes as if afraid she’d be left behind.

The flickering torchlight only illuminated a short stretch ahead. The deeper darkness beyond remained unseen.

The farther they went, the more uneasy they felt. The faint, mournful wails grew clearer, like agonized shrieks.

A gust of wind, thick with the scent of blood, brushed past them, making both girls feel sick. They covered their noses and pressed on.

Alice’s heart pounded. Was there really a way out here? Or would they just hit dead end after dead end?

Cecilia wasn’t idle. As she followed Alice, she used her staff to carve marks into the walls, just in case they got lost and needed to retrace their steps.

As they turned a corner, Alice suddenly heard something. She quickly pulled Cecilia into the shadow of the wall, her face breaking out in a cold sweat.

“…Miss Alice, what’s wrong? Don’t tell me…” Cecilia’s face paled, too afraid to finish her thought.

“Something’s alive.” Alice summed it up in three words, her guard now at its highest.

Though she’d only caught a fleeting glimpse, Alice could sense the presence of a living creature. She didn’t know what it was, but she felt they should be careful.

Alchemical beasts were incredibly difficult to deal with. If possible, Alice didn’t want to fight—it would put them at a severe disadvantage.

“I *told* you we should’ve stayed put! Now look—we’ve run into something terrifying, haven’t we? Whimper…” Cecilia whimpered, her expression utterly miserable. She felt as though her youthful life might come to an end today.

“…” Alice pressed a finger to her lips, signaling Cecilia to stay quiet. Any noise could make the situation even more dangerous.

Cecilia, like a timid little mouse, immediately fell silent. She stayed in place, wiping her tears, feeling as though every extra second she survived was a miracle.

Once the area fell silent, faint, murmured whispers drifted through the darkness, carrying fragments of information—

“Father… I’m so sorry… I fear I won’t be returning. It’s only a matter of time before I die here.”

“Connie, my beloved daughter… Father is sorry. This darkness is like hell itself. I see no hope.”

“From now on, I’ll have to entrust you with Grandfather’s care… Please… I hope you’ll continue running the family tavern…”

“Great Goddess of Light… if You can hear my prayers… grant me a shred of mercy.”

“Hurry and summon me to Your side… end the endless suffering I endure here…”

title: Chapter 41 — Lair
content:
Chapter 41 — Lair

Volume 8 · Chapter 41

The murmurs and prayers of a middle-aged man drifted over slowly, accompanied by deep responses, making it slightly creepy.

"...Who is this?" Cecilia asked in a very small voice, looking surprised.

Alice was relatively calm; hearing the other person speak human language, it was obviously not a monster they had encountered before, but a living human.

Judging by the information from his self-talk just now, wasn't this middle-aged man Miss Connie's father? How did he escape?

Alice turned back to give Cecilia a reassuring look; as long as it wasn't a ferocious monster, it would still be okay to talk about.

"It's okay, don't be afraid, come with me."

"....Won't there be any danger?" Cecilia said fearfully, holding onto Alice's clothes tightly, terrified of being left behind.

"No, isn't there me protecting you? The corner is a human, so there's no need to be afraid." Alice comforted Cecilia and told her to follow.

Although Cecilia was still worried, she could only listen to Alice now, since she was the only combatant by her side.

The two girls, one in front of the other, walked over holding torches...

Connie's father had offended Mark in the past, so he was caught in the first batch and used by Democritus as a guinea pig.

Although there had been over sixty people traveling together, almost all of them were dead with very few survivors; either used by Democritus as experimental material or fed to Alchemical Beasts as food.

Now, there were probably fewer than twenty surviving fishermen, and Connie's father was one of them; he could be considered a very lucky man.

Just not long ago, Democritus had devoted all his energy to dealing with Merlin and the others, no longer paying attention to the Alchemical Beasts' movements, allowing this group of slaughter monsters to run rampant. They directly destroyed the cages imprisoning the remaining humans and began greedily gnawing on human flesh, crunching and chewing like they were eating snacks.

Seeing that the situation was wrong, Connie's father took the first opportunity to escape during the chaos.

He kept searching for an exit, wanting to escape this human hell.

But he despairingly discovered that there was simply no exit here; only the place where they were imprisoned allowed him to see the sky outside.

That place itself was a nest for a vulture with multiple pairs of wings; it was huge, and its feathers were as hard as steel.

It radiated a cold aura all over its body; it was exactly one of Democritus's three masterpieces.

Therefore, the place where the fishermen were imprisoned was extremely special; it was an open-air nest, convenient for this deformed vulture to come and go.

After Connie's father discovered that he couldn't leave here, he fell deep into despair; even if he wasn't eaten by that monster vulture, he would still die of thirst or starvation in this darkness.

He would die of thirst or starvation in the darkness.

So Connie's father gave up resistance early on and hid in a corner, silently waiting for the call of the Goddess of Light to end all his troubles.

Connie's father had suffered greatly here, constantly watching friends from a village die as Alchemical Beasts cut open their bellies and tore out their intestines. The screams had already completely shattered his mind; death was obviously the best relief. If it weren't for the relatives he still worried about, he probably would have committed suicide long ago.

Alice and Cecilia came before Connie's father, using the torch to illuminate his haggard, yellow, and emaciated face.

Connie's father was obviously a bit mentally unstable; even though two living people were standing right in front of him, he was still muttering to himself incessantly.

Seeing this situation, Alice couldn't help frowning, but she still patiently called out in a low voice, "Hello, are you Miss Connie's father?"

Connie's father trembled all over and blankly raised his head. Seeing Alice and Cecilia, and the dim yellow glow of the torch, he could barely make out the faces of the two girls.

However, at this time Connie's father's spirit and emotions were unstable; he thought he had been found by some monster!

"....Don't come over! Don't kill me! Please, beg you! ...."

Connie's face was pale as he shrank back desperately, looking as if he were about to be scared to death.

Alice felt a bit helpless, thinking about how to communicate in this state?

Cecilia worried that Connie's father's shouting would attract other monsters, so she quickly stepped forward to cover his mouth, saying with a terrified expression,

"You be quiet! Look clearly, we are not those monsters."

Connie's father calmed down slightly. He looked carefully at Alice and Cecilia, and the blankness on his face instantly vanished, replaced by tears filling his eyes.

He never expected to see strange humans here; it felt even closer than seeing relatives!

Moreover, the sudden arrival of strangers here proved that there was an exit, and he could ask about how to escape.

Connie's father burst into tears, "Wuwuwu," feeling that he had received the Goddess of Light's pity; it turned out that praying in despair was indeed useful.

"Have you calmed down? If you have, blink your eyes." Cecilia covered Connie's father's mouth.

"Mmm... Connie's father blinked frequently; because he was too sad, it looked more like he was squeezing out tears.

Cecilia hesitated for a moment, then released Connie's father and silently hid behind Alice.

"You... you are humans from outside, right?" Connie's father's expression was incredibly excited, as if he had seen the light of survival.

"That's right." Alice nodded and added, "We have met your daughter, Miss Connie; she asked us to come save you."

"..." Upon hearing his daughter's name, Connie's father's eyes instantly filled with tears. "My daughter and father, are they okay?"

"Yes, they are both fine." Alice answered with a confident tone.

"That's wonderful... Connie's father breathed a sigh of relief and said casually in a pleading tone, "Please... take me out of this ghostly place.

"It's a pity, we can't find an exit either." Alice's expression became gloomy; she had thought Connie's father knew something, but looking at the situation, it was obviously impossible.

"No... that can't be right, then how did you come here?" Connie's father became excited all over again, on the verge of being dominated by despair.

"We fell down here; it's very hard to go back the same way." Alice said awkwardly.

"It's over...". Connie's father widened his eyes and lowered his head with a hollow gaze. "We will all die here; there's no way to leave."

Infected by the atmosphere, Cecilia became even more terrified and silently clenched the hem of Alice's clothes.

Alice felt that Connie's father was too lacking in ambition; he was already predicting failure before anything had happened, which really affected her mood.

"Cheer up, we still have a chance! Since this place was designed by that alchemist, there must be an exit!"

"No, there won't be an exit. Even if there is, it's probably in that monster's nest...." Connie's father hugged his head, saying with full despair.

The expressions of both Cecilia and Alice turned ugly; sure enough, there was that kind of monster here as well.

It seemed things were going to be a bit difficult, because Alchemical Beasts were monsters with thick skin and high attack power, and even Alice found them difficult to deal with.

Alice's face darkened as she thought it over; she felt they couldn't just stay here and wait for death, so she had to give it a shot and said,

"Where is the nest? Take us there."

"No, no, no!" Connie's father shook his head like a rattle drum, saying in a serious yet terrified tone,

"That monster is far too powerful; it's simply not something you can defeat, so don't go and throw your lives away..."

title: Chapter 42 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 42 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 42

To this day, recalling that gray, ugly vulture, Connie's father was still terrified, his face bloodless, his mind filled with images of that monster pecking at human flesh.

Cecilia—upon hearing this—immediately didn't want to wander around here anymore; she wanted to return to the original spot and wait for Merlin to come back and save them.

"Miss Alice, I... we should go back, everyone says there are very difficult monsters here."

Although Alice knew she wasn't particularly powerful, being denied before they even fought made her feel quite aggrieved.

"No, waiting to die is the worst-case scenario. If three or more monsters show up, even I probably wouldn't be able to handle them, so it's better to try and fight for it."

....Cecilia was speechless; this situation of having wolves in front and tigers behind made things difficult for her as well.

Alice turned to Connie's father and said, "Don't worry, leave that monster to us to deal with; you just need to lead us there. If we win, you and I will both be able to get out."

"We can't win, why do you insist on going to your deaths? That monster... I'm afraid as humans, we cannot defeat it." Connie's father said with a painful expression, not wanting to return to the torture-filled hell at all.

"Why not try to resist? Do you want to wait for death here?" Alice frowned her beautiful brows, feeling that people without fighting spirit were as annoying as Merlin.

"I don't want it to be like this either, that monster is too powerful; even you guys can't defeat it. I have seen the strength of that ugly monster with my own eyes, so you might as well give up on that hopeless idea early on....." Connie's father lowered his head and said blankly, "Rather than being eaten by a monster, it's better to stay here and slowly wait for death."

Alice looked at this middle-aged man having no ambition at all and felt truly uncomfortable; Miss Connie had even considered the thought of selling herself to save this father of hers.

His daughter could have that kind of sacrifice consciousness, why is this father so lacking in ambition?

In a fit of anger, Alice grabbed Connie's father off the ground; as a high-level adventurer, grabbing an ordinary person was very easy.

"Wake up a bit, okay? Is this how you treat Miss Connie? Do you know what efforts she made for this incompetent father of yours while you were trapped here? You don't know anything, just thinking about dying comfortably, you coward!"

....Connie's father, feet off the ground, was scolded by Alice, his mind a bit dazed.

"Do you still remember your daughter Connie?" Alice asked seriously.

".....Of course I remember, how could I forget my daughter..." Connie's father answered with a conflicted expression.

"Then don't you want to see her again?" Alice pressed finally, hoping Connie's father would have some fighting spirit.

"I want to! Of course I want to! Who doesn't want to see her..." Connie's father began to shed tears.

"Then make an effort then. If you are willing to wait for death here, you will definitely never see your daughter again. If you try to make an effort, there is still a chance. Waiting for death here, or being eaten by a monster, either way it's death, why won't you make an effort?" Alice tried her best to persuade Connie's father; as long as he could lead the way, it didn't matter what.

....Connie's father was still somewhat hesitant; facing a death threat, anyone would waver.

"Rest assured, you just need to lead the way for us, leave the rest to us." Alice added another sentence.

Connie's father swallowed nervously; indeed, he still wanted to see his family, so he gritted his teeth and nodded, "Okay, I'll lead you there!"

Alice immediately relaxed and put Connie's father down.

The nearby Cecilia was still somewhat worried and very afraid; after all, Alice's strength didn't give her much sense of security.

"Miss Alice, is it really okay? He said that monster is very strong."

"How would I know if I don't really go at it with real weapons?" Alice looked into Cecilia's eyes and insisted on trying, "You just stand behind and support me, leave the rest to me."

The end of the underground testing ground.

Broken cage fragments were everywhere.

As for the bloodstains, there were countless of them, seemingly all fresh, looking shocking to the eye.

A huge gray vulture spread four pairs of wings that blocked out the sky, exuding a bone-chilling cold aura all over its body.

This cave had no dome; looking up, one could see the sky covered in dark clouds, and it was probably known that this deformed vulture could come and go freely.

The surviving fishermen seemed to be fewer than ten people left; they huddled in corners to keep warm, unable to run even if they wanted to, only covered in the shadow of the vulture, slowly waiting for death.

The deformed vulture spread its wings, immediately giving a feeling of blocking out the sun; the only exit had already been blocked by it, and the surviving villagers could only cry in despair.

The vulture seemed to want to eat one by one, so it didn't directly kill all these humans at once.

The deformed vulture struck out like lightning, snatching a fisherman with its beak.

"No! Don't! ! !" the villagers shouted in panic.

The vulture used its eagle claws to fiercely trample the fisherman and started pecking directly, blood splashing everywhere, and the poor fisherman went silent immediately.

It tore off a piece of human flesh and swallowed it down with its neck raised, seemingly enjoying it.

Just then—

A "whoosh" sound of breaking the air rang out, a super-large ice sword attacked, exactly Alice's "Frost Judgment".

The giant ice sword fiercely collided with the deformed vulture's feathers, turning into countless ice chips, unharmed!

The vulture seemed to be stimulated and slowly turned its head, glaring at Alice outside with scarlet eagle eyes.

Connie's father, due to excessive fear, ran out immediately and hid behind the door; other villagers also took this opportunity to scatter in a mob, finding places to hide themselves.

"Tch! It actually didn't work...." Alice pouted, drawing her thin sword from her waist, "Cecilia, buff me!"

From that one probing attack just now, Alice felt a very obvious gap in strength.

Although the Alchemical Beast didn't have strength close to this, the combat ability of this vulture was definitely extraordinary; even its feathers were so hard!

So Alice had to seize every opportunity to strengthen herself to narrow the gap in combat ability.

But when Alice called out, she saw no response from Cecilia at all.

Cecilia looked at the huge vulture in front of her and was completely scared silly, silently gripping the magic wand in her hand.

"Cecilia! ! !"

The deformed vulture shrieked, shaking its multiple huge wings, and dived down from the air, its sharp eagle claws striking directly.

On the other side.

Johnson, having shaken off Merlin and Kyle...

He was indeed lost, not knowing where he was at all, walking around in a complete mess.

On the way, he broke through quite a few traps and hidden weapons, none of which could hurt him.

At this time, Johnson had walked into a dead end again; he scratched his head, looking puzzled.

"Damn it! Where exactly is that alchemist?"

As soon as the words fell, the wall in front of him suddenly made a rumbling sound and slowly opened to both sides.

Johnson looked indifferently into the darkness inside the door, the corners of his mouth curling up, "Is this inviting me? You really have a death wish..."

Johnson walked in without hesitation, taking big steps; there were no traps or hidden weapons on the way, it was just too dark, making people feel a bit creepy.

When Johnson slowly walked to the center, a hissing sound rang out, and braziers lit up one after another, illuminating this mysterious place.

A circular platform, supported by several large pillars, the central area was very vast, covered in beast scratches and bloodstains.

Simply put, this place is like the entire Colosseum of the Holy Roman Empire moved directly underground!

It looked very much like a replica, full of a magnificent feeling.

On the high platform, Democritus, wearing a red robe, spread his arms and shouted loudly like a king—

"Oh, you who are hailed as the Elgin genius magician, welcome to my playground!

"Of course, this is not just my playground, it is also...

"Your eternal resting place
