title: Chapter 44 — Lone Wolf
content:
Chapter 44 — Lone Wolf

Volume 8 · Chapter 44

Kael saw Merlin laughing too uninhibitedly, too shamelessly, and couldn’t help but lower his voice to remind him.

"Lord Merlin, mind your image. You’ll lose fans like this...."

"Right, right, must be elegant, must be a gentleman."

Merlin rubbed his cheek, reined in his laughter, and put on an icy, aloof expression.

Johnston hadn’t figured out the situation yet. When Merlin said they were there to steal the kill, he instantly felt a surge of anger.

*...Job...*

"That’s right, I’m this shameless~" Merlin admitted without hesitation, then added, "And you keep talking about fair competition, yet you ditched us—so you’ve got no right to call us shameless, do you?"

"Shut up, old man! This guy is *my* prey, and you’re not allowed to interfere!" Johnston slowly straightened up. The wound on his chest was shocking, blood oozing steadily. If he hadn’t urgently summoned a weak magic barrier earlier, the Twin-Headed Lion King would’ve already killed him.

Merlin didn’t speak. Instead, he glanced at Johnston’s wound, and his urgency to steal the kill vanished. He figured the brat was about to get a lesson.

Thinking about Johnston’s usual rotten behavior, a little setback would do him good. So the best move was to wait and watch—let reality give him a harsh wake-up call....

Merlin made up his mind, then watched Johnston with a half-smile, already picturing him being pinned to the ground and rubbed into the dirt.

*[Garbled text]*

"How can you do this?! Didn’t we agree to fair competition? Aren’t you going back on your own words?! I’m furious!"

"Shut up! Why would I care about you lot?! This damn alchemist is *my* prey, and if anyone dares try to take him from me, I won’t be nice about it!" Johnston clutched his chest wound, roaring in rage.

At this point, Johnston was in a state of extreme fury, his hatred for Democritus burning deep. He wanted to incinerate this bastard on the spot.

Johnston’s temperament was childish—he’d never been injured by anyone except his father. But today was an exception. For Johnston, today was a day of shame, and the scars on his body were the marks of that humiliation!

He was a magic prodigy, the center of attention—how could a powerless alchemist have hurt him? It was unbearable.

He *had* to crush this damn alchemist, then spit on his corpse to avenge his shame!

Johnston’s fighting spirit surged; the flames of rage in his chest burned so fiercely that he forgot the pain.

"Are you a child? So stubborn. You’re already injured—why not let us help?" Kael frowned, still trying to persuade him. Otherwise, all the effort he and the young lady had put in would go to waste.

"Not needed." Johnston said coldly.

"Hahaha...." Democritus, standing on the high platform, burst into laughter, unable to resist sneering. "You pathetic trash, actually arguing over *my* kill? Truly... hilarious.... or..."

"What’s so funny? A scoundrel like you deserves to be sent to hell!" Kael snapped at Democritus, puzzled. Why was this guy so fearless even when facing two Saint-tier powerhouses?

"Cut it out!" Democritus seethed, glaring down at Kael and Merlin. "You and that guy over there are nothing but ants in my eyes. I could crush you with a single finger, yet you dare hop around in front of me. Do you *want* my little darlings to finish you off?"

The vigilant Twin-Headed Lion King and Heavy Armored Mammoth roared, seemingly unable to contain their bloodlust, eager to slaughter the humans before them.

"Spouting nonsense! You clearly haven’t seen Lord Merlin’s true strength!" Kael said angrily, feeling indignant on Merlin’s behalf.

Merlin, however, didn’t feel much of anything. A careless smile hung on his face—he was long used to this sort of thing. How others saw him didn’t matter.

"Two little mice, shut your mouths. Honestly, I don’t even want to bother with you. Talking to you is a waste of time." Democritus sneered. "If you resist, just obediently become food for my little darlings. In the end, turning into shit is the peak of your worthless lives! Hahaha...."

Kael was about to retort, but Merlin stopped him with a gesture, signaling him to hold his tongue.

"Lord Merlin?" Kael looked confused.

"It’s fine. No need to argue with a frog in a well." Merlin said with a smile. With him here, Democritus was doomed today. Getting angry at a dead man was pointless.

Kael sighed. If Lord Merlin didn’t mind, then he had no choice but to stay silent.

Democritus, seeing the two nobodies finally shut up, assumed they’d been intimidated by his presence. He couldn’t help but feel a little smug.

"Irish brat, you’re the only opponent I acknowledge. But unfortunately for you, you’re already doomed." Johnston gritted his teeth, his Saint-tier pressure surging wave after wave.

"Is that so? As long as I’m still standing, I haven’t lost. Don’t be so overconfident, or you’ll fall flat on your face."

"Seems the earlier fight didn’t make you face reality. You were *this* close to dying, yet you still can’t see the power gap? How pathetic~" Democritus spread his arms, baring his teeth in a wild laugh. "Do you really think your strength can beat my babies? Let me tell you—the idea of you defeating my masterpieces is nothing but a fairy tale. Hahaha...."

"Really a fairy tale?" Johnston curled his lip, narrowing his eyes. "I wasn’t even using my full strength earlier. Don’t get cocky too soon."

"Hmph! Then keep struggling in front of my two little darlings!" Democritus’ eyes were bloodshot with excitement. "I can’t wait to hear your delightful screams!"

The Twin-Headed Lion King and Heavy Armored Mammoth kept growling, slowly closing in on Johnston, their eyes green with hunger.

Johnston snapped his fingers behind his back. Several pillars of light suddenly descended from the sky, trapping Merlin and Kael inside. They couldn’t move freely.

This was the Saint-tier spell «Holy Light Cage», used to restrain enemies and deal damage. Its strength was absolute—it wouldn’t be broken easily.

"Stay put in there until this is over. If you force your way out, the holy light will burn you to death."

"Ah?! What?!" Kael froze, disbelief in his voice. "This is way too shameless! Despicable!"

Merlin, however, wasn’t as worked up. He stroked his chin, smiling. "This brat’s got some nerve...."

"I absolutely won’t let you interfere...." Johnston undid his outer coat, revealing the bloodstained white silk underneath. Then, with a flourish, he tossed the coat aside.

"Because....

"This kill is mine alone!"

(-"-)

title: Chapter 45 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 45 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes

Volume 8 · Chapter 45

"This family..." Kail glared at Johnson's retreating figure, his voice brimming with frustration. "This is so unfair!"

It was no wonder Kail was in such a foul mood. After all, Johnson's actions had severely limited their options.

Now, trapped in a cage of holy light, they might end up with nothing to show for their efforts.

Merlin, however, remained unconcerned. A faint, mocking smile played on his lips as he watched. Johnson's defeat seemed inevitable to him.

The man had nearly lost his life fighting those two alchemical beasts. Clearly, the enemy was not to be underestimated. So Merlin decided to wait and watch. Once Johnson— that bratty little show-off— was thoroughly humiliated, he would step in to finish things, making sure the boy admitted defeat wholeheartedly.

Merlin stroked his chin, grinning to himself. Even with his magic immunity, he had no intention of breaking out of this cage to join the fight.

Seeing Merlin’s indifference, Kail wondered: *If even Lord Merlin can’t easily break free from this cage, then Johnson must truly be a formidable opponent...*

The two alchemical beasts roared, then charged forward with terrifying ferocity, as if intent on slaughtering every living thing in their path.

The Dual-Headed Lion King spun its massive form, whipping up a blizzard as it charged with a furious roar.

The Heavy Armored Mammoth swung its tusks, rushing to the front to block the incoming magical assault.

"Hey! You two beasts, get out of my way!!!"

Johnson’s golden Saint-tier magic surged violently as he unleashed a rapid barrage of Saint-tier spells.

In an instant, a dazzling array of magical elements—seamlessly switching, combining without cooldown—erupted with even greater power than before!

The magical elements in the air danced like lively sprites, all obeying Johnson’s command.

An unparalleled display of magic unfolded at Johnson’s fingertips—
and it had only just begun...

Elsewhere.

"Cecilia!!!"

Alice shouted desperately, calling for Cecilia’s aid to strengthen her.

But the foolish girl seemed frozen in fear, unmoving.

The vicious Steel Vulture spread its wings, diving from the sky with brutal force, its target locked onto Alice.

Alchemical beasts had the instincts of predators—they could tell at a glance that Alice was the stronger of the two.

For safety’s sake, it would kill Alice first, then toy with Cecilia at its leisure.

The situation was dire, and the Steel Vulture was too fast. Alice had no choice but to raise her rapier in a desperate block.

The Steel Vulture’s beak clashed violently against Alice’s rapier, sending sparks flying!

*CLANG!*

A deafening metallic ring echoed through the space.

Unable to withstand the force, Alice was sent flying backward.

"Cough—ah!"

She cried out in pain as she crashed heavily into the rocky wall, kicking up a cloud of dust.

Cecilia fared no better. Even though she hadn’t been struck directly, the hurricane-force winds from the Steel Vulture’s dive sent her tumbling to the ground.

As the dust settled, Alice barely managed to prop herself up with her rapier, blood trickling down her forehead.

She gritted her silver teeth, her almond-shaped eyes wide with defiance as she glared at the Steel Vulture, her gaze burning with unyielding resolve.

The power gap between Alice and the Steel Vulture was simply too vast. In a single exchange, she had been reduced to critical condition, left with no ability to resist.

The Steel Vulture circled in the air, letting out eerie, triumphant shrieks—as if mocking Alice’s weakness.

Cecilia finally snapped out of her daze, remembering what Captain Dennis had told her earlier.

Panicked, she fumbled in her pocket and pulled out the signal flare, pulling the cord without hesitation.

*Whoosh!* A burst of red smoke shot into the sky, soaring outward where Captain Dennis would surely see it.

Alice steadied herself, raising her rapier toward the Steel Vulture in the sky. "Cecilia! Healing! Buffs!"

"...Okay!" Cecilia clutched her staff tightly, her voice trembling. "Intermediate Healing!"

Alice’s wounds eased slightly. At least she no longer felt like her bones were being crushed, the pain nearly knocking her unconscious.

Cecilia might only be a mid-tier priest, and her healing wasn’t exceptional, but it was better than nothing.

Without delay, Cecilia began casting a rapid succession of buffs on Alice:

"Enchant Weapon: Heavy Strike!"

"Physical Penetration Amplification!"

"Intermediate Attack Boost!"

"Intermediate Strength Boost!"

"Intermediate Magic Boost!"

"Intermediate Agility Boost!"

A relentless barrage of enhancements piled onto Alice, each one stronger than the last.

Even Cecilia could sense the overwhelming power gap between Alice and the Steel Vulture. This might be their last chance to turn the tide.

Feeling the surge of strength coursing through her, Alice channeled a layer of fused ice crystals onto her rapier, hoping it would be enough to pierce the Steel Vulture’s defenses.

Once everything was ready, Alice let out a fierce battle cry and launched herself straight toward the Steel Vulture in the sky.

"HAAAAAAH!!!"

She moved like lightning, her silver hair flowing behind her like a comet’s tail—a silver streak slicing through the sky!

She pushed her power to its absolute limit, prepared to gamble everything on this single strike to decide the battle!

Her eyes blazed with fighting spirit, and the rapier in her hand gleamed sharper than ever before!

But then—

The Steel Vulture, watching Alice’s approach, suddenly flapped its massive wings, creating a storm of opposing winds that clashed violently, generating a terrifying vortex of chaotic air currents.

The force was horrific—capable of tearing apart any living thing, like two spinning circular saws, its power staggering!

And Alice was caught right in the middle of it, battered relentlessly.

"AAAAAAAAAAH!!!"

She screamed in agony, as if countless blades were slicing into her flesh, as if she were being torn apart. She teetered on the edge of collapse.

Trapped in the vortex, Alice’s body twisted slightly, struggling against the immense distorting forces.

The Steel Vulture hadn’t even exerted its true strength—just a flick of its wings had unleashed such devastating power. It was terrifying.

As the storm dissipated, Alice crashed powerlessly to the ground, lying motionless.

"Miss Alice!!!" Cecilia sobbed, her voice breaking.

She tried to rush forward to check on Alice, but the Steel Vulture descended from above, landing beside Alice’s fallen form.

Cecilia’s face paled, her legs refusing to move. Fear seized her entirely.

Alice lay on the ground, no longer feeling pain. Her body was drained, exhausted, as if she could just close her eyes and sleep forever.

She caught sight of Cecilia, frozen in panic in the distance. Her fingers twitched weakly—

*Idiot... run...*

*This thing is too strong...*

*There’s no way I can win...*

*So run, Cecilia... don’t look back...*

*Just... one thing... I regret... never stomping Merlin’s face with my boot...*

Her eyelids grew heavy. Unable to resist any longer, she closed her eyes, and her consciousness faded away.

The Steel Vulture let out a low growl, then slowly lowered its head, opening its beak—clearly intending to savor Alice’s flesh at its leisure.

Just then, the long-dormant power of the Ice Dragon began to stir.

Without Alice to suppress it, it would soon break free.

Alice’s unconscious body suddenly jolted upright. With her slender arms, she forced back the Steel Vulture’s beak, preventing it from reaching her.

Her eyes, now glowing with golden pupils, burned like reborn flames—yet they held no emotion, only emptiness.

Her wounds healed at impossible speed, sealing shut in an instant. Then, blue-white dragon scales erupted across her body, spreading rapidly, even covering her cheeks.

The dreaded Dragonification had begun... once again.

title: Chapter 46 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 46 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 46

Alice’s body was covered in blue and white dragon scales, shimmering like the finest gemstones.

The scales had also spread across her cheeks, though they stopped halfway, as if the transformation had been interrupted.

At this moment, Alice seemed like a fusion of dragon and human, yet she retained a striking beauty—more like a Valkyrie clad in heavy armor!

The dragon transformation had come to a complete halt. Alice had not achieved full 100% dragonification; instead, it had stopped midway.

Looking at her mask of scales, though not as comprehensive as Carolina’s full transformation, Alice’s dragonification was conservatively estimated to be over 50%!

Her current power was likely approaching that of a true dragon, with all manner of innate enhancements.

But unfortunately, this power had been forcibly awakened by Alice’s desperate will to survive—it would surely come with a price.

The reason her dragonification had stopped was that, unlike Carolina, Alice had not sought power out of greed. Instead, she had activated the inheritance crystal purely out of the desire to live. Thus, the transformation had met resistance and been forced to cease.

In a way, this had saved her. If she had fully transformed into a dragon, Alice would have become a true dragonkin, forever unable to return to her human form.

But even partial dragonification was more than enough for Alice to deal with this Steel Vulture.

After all, the Steel Vulture was made from the blood of the Frost Holy Dragon, while Alice’s inheritance crystal contained power closer to the essence of the Frost Holy Dragon itself. When a father fought his own creation, what resistance could there be? None at all—only absolute domination!

Alice’s consciousness had fallen into dormancy. The only reason she could still move was due to the instinctive actions controlled by Malrigus’s magic.

Her face showed no expression, as if she had become someone else. Those blazing golden eyes, though terrifying, were utterly hollow.

Alice pressed both hands against the Steel Vulture’s beak, resisting its incomparable crushing force, yet it could not harm her in the slightest.

Her power had reached an extraordinary level—even the blue and white dragon scales on her body possessed a hardness far beyond what the Steel Vulture, a mere imitation, could compare to!

“Alice…”

Cecilia stared at Alice’s bizarre form, murmuring her name, no longer able to recognize her.

Though her appearance hadn’t changed much, her demeanor was completely different—as if she had suddenly become someone else.

Cold, emotionless, like a superior being gazing down upon all with disdain, as if surveying the world from on high.

Or perhaps it was just Cecilia’s imagination, but within the rolling cold aura radiating from Alice, she seemed to see a noble and majestic dragon, glaring fiercely at the inferior creature before it.

Cecilia watched Alice with mixed emotions. Even transformed like this, she remained beautiful, but now she exuded an overwhelming, distant pressure that made her impossible to approach.

…Is this still Miss Alice?

The Steel Vulture exerted all its strength, trying to sever Alice’s arms with its beak, its massive body trembling with effort.

Alice’s indifferent gaze shifted, her burning golden eyes locking onto the Steel Vulture, her sharp pupils contracting.

The Steel Vulture’s crimson eyes flickered with fear for a moment, its entire body freezing in place.

This was the pressure of dragon blood—high-ranking dragons possessed an absolute intimidation over other creatures. And Alice, being of the same origin as its "father," wielded that power even more potently.

But this strange state passed in an instant, replaced by rage. The Steel Vulture flapped its multiple wings, trying to carry Alice into the sky.

Alice’s body erupted with a burst of force, sending the Steel Vulture flying. With a flick of her hand, the slender sword *Luminous Elegy* flew into her grip.

The Steel Vulture panicked, whipping up gale after gale, forming massive turbulent currents that mercilessly assailed Alice below.

“…!”

Cecilia shielded herself from the hurricane-force winds, struggling to keep her eyes open.

Alice stood unshaken, her gaze fixed on the Steel Vulture. With a single swing of her sword, the stormy currents dispersed entirely.

Then, with a sudden leap, she launched a ferocious assault, her sword moving so swiftly it seemed to vanish, silver light flashing as it struck the enemy.

Even without any martial techniques or magic, Alice was already overwhelmingly powerful. Wherever her blade passed, flesh split and blood spilled.

The Steel Vulture’s pride—its hardened feathers—were like tofu before her sword, easily pierced, leaving its body a bloody mess!

Alice swung her sword repeatedly, her face devoid of any expression, utterly cold—as if she were looking at nothing more than a worthless cockroach.

…She’s so strong…

Cecilia stared in bewilderment, her eyes wide. Alice had gone from being on the brink of defeat to completely overpowering this monster in the blink of an eye!

The change was too drastic for Cecilia to accept. Clearly, Alice was not herself right now.

It wasn’t just the change in strength—Cecilia could distinctly feel the dragon’s might radiating from Alice, a unique pressure that made her tremble continuously.

Cecilia couldn’t understand what was happening to Alice. Did she have some connection to a high-ranking dragon? Otherwise, how could she explain this distinct dragon-like aura?

The Steel Vulture shrieked in agony, its ear-piercing wails growing desperate as its repeated defenses proved useless, swiftly suppressed by Alice’s relentless assault.

Unable to endure the one-sided beating, it resorted to extreme tactics.

With a furious roar, the Steel Vulture launched the iron-hard feathers from its body—hundreds of them shot out like arrows.

The air was filled with the whistling of feathers, each one as sharp as a blade, razor-edged.

Alice was struck and sent flying, crashing from the sky into the ground, her body sinking deep into the earth.

“Alice!” Cecilia cried out, wondering if she had been defeated so easily.

But sure enough, Alice quickly stood back up, not a single injury on her aside from a bit of dust. The blue and white dragon scales still gleamed.

“Ah!” Cecilia gasped in shock. This kind of defense… it was impossible for a high-rank Magic Swordsman to possess!

Alice lifted her head, staring at the enemy in the sky, her expression unchanging—no joy, no sorrow, no emotion at all—as if she intended to kill this monster without hesitation.

The Steel Vulture seemed to sense fear, flapping its four pairs of wings as it soared upward, as if trying to escape.

Alice slightly crouched, gathering strength for a moment before shooting upward like a meteor, trailing fierce winds. In the blink of an eye, she appeared high above the Steel Vulture!

“So fast!” Cecilia’s face was filled with terror. Alice didn’t seem human anymore—she was far too powerful compared to before!

Alice gripped her slender sword, descending from the heavens with unmatched momentum!

The holy sword slashed downward, a flash of silver light—and the battle was over.

Alice landed silently, then abruptly swung her sword, flinging off the blood until it was clean.

Soon after, the Steel Vulture’s massive bisected corpse crashed to the ground, twitching and flailing in agony.

Drops of crimson blood rained down, pattering against Alice’s expressionless face.

Cold air and dragon’s might swirled endlessly. Alice’s burning golden eyes showed no sign of dimming.

The Valkyrie, bathed in blood and carnage, exuded an aura of dread and unease…

title: Chapter 47 — Draw Sword
content:
Chapter 47 — Draw Sword

Volume 8 · Chapter 47

The Steel Vulture was cleanly bisected by Alice, its severed corpse rolling across the ground as if consumed by lingering resentment before finally lying still.

Blood rained down from the sky, pattering against the earth, dyeing the land crimson.

Alice stood motionless beneath the downpour of blood, her burning golden eyes sharp yet hollow.

Cecilia crouched to the side, staring at the towering, unmoving figure of Alice. A chill ran down her spine, and she didn’t dare approach.

"So strong... This power has completely surpassed High-tier, hasn’t it? How is this possible..."

Cecilia nervously swallowed, her throat dry. Alice had suddenly erupted with a strength far beyond anything she’d shown before. And that rampant, oppressive dragon’s might radiating from her was terrifying—no one dared get close. It was as if she had suddenly transformed into a different species entirely.

She couldn’t understand why this had happened. Was this blood-drenched valkyrie standing before her really the same Alice who usually pouted in frustration?

Cecilia felt a creeping fear. She didn’t know what to do, and a thought gnawed at her—had Alice lost herself to some dark power?

A crisp sound shattered the silence. The jade pendant that never left Alice’s neck slowly slipped free, clinking as it hit the ground.

The cord had clearly been damaged at the start of the battle, and now, under the strain, it had finally snapped.

This pendant had been a gift from Alice’s teacher on her eighth birthday. He had told her it was the only memento left by her mother, making it all the more precious.

Alice knew she had been an orphan since childhood, raised by her teacher. Naturally, she treasured this pendant, always wearing it around her neck. After all, it was the only connection she had to the mother she had never known.

She knew little about her mother, and her teacher refused to speak of her. Whenever young Alice had asked, he would change the subject or pretend not to hear.

After her persistent pestering, her teacher had finally said she had been found at the foot of the Great Snow Mountain. Probably abandoned during a famine, as her family couldn’t afford to keep her.

As for anything else, he claimed to know nothing. Whether that was true, Alice had no way to confirm.

Outside, Connie’s father, sensing the silence within, curiously poked his head in. What he saw left him stunned—Alice stood there, sword in hand, while the monstrous creature lay in two halves.

The sheer absurdity of the scene filled him with disbelief. A High-tier adventurer had actually slain that beast!

Heaven! That monstrous, ferocious creature—how had they done it?!

It was incredible. This kind of strength could rival even Mythril-tier adventurers!

Connie’s father wiped away tears, overwhelmed with relief. It seemed the great Goddess of Light had not abandoned him after all.

The fishermen, who had been hiding, also emerged one by one, their faces alight with excitement. They stared at the blood-drenched valkyrie in the center, unable to hold back their exclamations.

"That Golden adventurer is so strong!"

"Unbelievable... She completely dominated the fight."

"Now we can finally go home!"

The fishermen chattered excitedly, cherishing their hard-won freedom. To them, this time had been like living in hell, with no hope of survival.

Cecilia knew this couldn’t go on. Gathering her courage, she stepped forward, trying to communicate with Alice.

"A... Alice..."

A sharp gust of sword energy suddenly lashed out, grazing Cecilia’s ear. A few golden strands of hair drifted to the ground.

Cecilia’s voice died in her throat. She didn’t dare make another sound, her face pale, her body trembling. For a moment, she had felt death brush past her—she had nearly been cleaved in two by Alice’s sudden strike!

Lowering her head slightly, she saw the ground beside her. A long gash had been carved into the earth by the sword energy, and a distant wall had collapsed from the force.

Alice’s current strength was terrifying—even a casual swing carried such destructive power!

Cecilia looked at Alice, whose golden eyes still burned. The blue-and-white dragon scales covering her body shimmered, making her too dangerous to approach.

Even the fishermen were too afraid to come near, utterly confused by the situation.

Alice stared at Cecilia. The golden light in her eyes abruptly faded, as if all her strength had vanished. She collapsed to the ground, and the dragon scales receded like a retreating tide.

"Miss Alice!"

Cecilia rushed forward, cradling Alice in her arms. After a quick examination, she realized the injuries were serious—immediate treatment was needed.

What surprised Cecilia was that as the dragon scales vanished, so did the oppressive dragon’s might. Alice returned to normal.

Cecilia couldn’t help but marvel. "What *is* she? How can she change so completely?"

Just as Cecilia was administering emergency care, Connie’s father suddenly shouted from outside:

"Monsters! There are more monsters!"

Connie’s father scrambled over, his face twisted in panic, as if something terrifying was approaching.

Cecilia looked up in alarm. At the entrance stood an alchemical beast, its bloodshot eyes fixed on the humans inside.

Damn it! Why now?!

They hadn’t seen a single one on the way here!

This was bad—Miss Alice was unconscious, and there was no one left who could fight!

What were they supposed to do? Why did she always end up in these impossible situations?!

Tears welled in Cecilia’s eyes as fear and helplessness gripped her. The Steel Vulture had been like a lord here. Now that it was dead, the weaker, starving alchemical beasts had lost their restraint. Drawn by the scent of humans, they had come to feed.

If one had arrived, others would follow the trail.

Sure enough, more and more deformed alchemical beasts surged forward, a swarming, dark mass.

They stared hungrily at the humans, drooling, ready to pounce.

The fishermen were overcome with despair, their faces ashen as they gaped at the horde outside.

"We’re doomed... We’re all going to die..."

"Why are there *more* of these things?!"

"I don’t want to die! I don’t want to die!"

The fishermen scattered in terror, desperate not to be torn apart by the grotesque creatures.

Cecilia clutched Alice tightly, thinking, *Are we really going to die here?* Damn it all—she hadn’t even proven herself to her father yet! She refused to accept this!

The alchemical beasts could no longer contain their hunger. With a collective roar, they charged, baring their terrifying fangs, ready to tear the humans apart!

Then—an explosion thundered, startling the beasts into halting their advance.

The wall behind Cecilia collapsed, and sunlight poured in.

Smoke filled the air, tinged with the scent of sulfur.

The sea breeze dispersed the haze, revealing a group of figures. At the forefront stood a man in a captain’s hat, his attire impeccable and sharp. Though his hair was white, his spirit was undiminished—it could only be Captain Dennis!

Behind him stood his brave crew, their expressions grave, their gazes resolute. They were as disciplined as any royal navy.

The entire crew of the *William*, armed with their finest weapons, had arrived just in time!

Captain Dennis’s hawk-like eyes locked onto the swarming, grotesque alchemical beasts. He instantly understood the situation.

Without hesitation, he drew his naval command blade, pointing it straight at the bloodthirsty creatures.

"Brave sailors! The moment to show our loyalty to the Rosé family has come!"

"All hands—"

"Draw steel!!!"

title: Chapter 48 — Bonus Chapter with Monthly Ticket Support
content:
Chapter 48 — Bonus Chapter with Monthly Ticket Support

Volume 8 · Chapter 48

The sailors behind Dennis all drew their naval cutlasses, their expressions stern and fearless, like a death-defying suicide squad.

Though their strength wasn’t overwhelming, it was enough to clash with these ferocious alchemical beasts a few times and then find a way to retreat unscathed.

Time ticked away with crisp, unending clangs. The sailors at the rear loaded their muskets, preparing to provide covering fire.

The moment Cecilia fired the smoke signal, Captain Dennis had already noticed the commotion. He quickly halted the repairs on the *William* and rushed over with all his crew, sparing no time.

To save time, Captain Dennis made a bold and decisive move—he ordered his men to use explosives to blast through the mountain. The results were beyond expectations!

Cecilia stared at the crew of the *William*, her gaze somewhat dazed. Through the gentle sea breeze, these sailors, who had wandered the vast ocean, now seemed like divine reinforcements sent from heaven. Their arrival was impossibly timely.

Tears welled in Cecilia’s eyes, threatening to spill. She finally understood the wisdom in her father’s words: *More friends, more paths.* She never expected that, despite her usual foul temper, there would still be people willing to come to her aid in a time like this…

Cecilia was overwhelmed with emotion. Indeed, she was a girl who would never learn her lesson without hardship.

Everyone prepared themselves for a brutal fight against the alchemical beasts.

"Charge!!!" Dennis roared from the ship, his voice like thunder, shaking everyone to their core.

"AAAAAAAAH!"

The sailors let out a battle cry, brandishing their gleaming naval cutlasses as they charged forward, clashing with the alchemical beasts.

Dozens of sailors formed a musket squad, firing in rapid succession—*bang, bang, bang*—to ease the pressure on their allies. For a moment, long tongues of flame and thick smoke erupted from the muskets, a barrage of steel suppressing the beasts, sending them howling in pain.

The frontline sailors roared to boost their morale, wielding their cutlasses with fierce precision—clearly, they were all veterans with the blade.

The alchemical beasts were caught off guard at first, but they were killing machines, not to be underestimated. They quickly launched a ferocious counterattack.

These monsters were extraordinarily powerful. The sailors could only hold out for a while—there was no way they could wipe them all out.

Dennis rushed to Cecilia’s side and gave a slight bow. "Lady Cecilia, please forgive our late arrival."

"It’s fine, Mr. Dennis. Hurry and cover the refugees’ retreat." Cecilia spoke calmly, no longer using her usual haughty tone.

"I understand. Please, Lady Cecilia, retreat at once as well." Captain Dennis said earnestly.

Cecilia nodded, then suddenly remembered something. "Wait! Mr. Dennis, Alice’s pendant—bring it to me."

Right now, with Alice in her arms, it wasn’t convenient for her to reach it. She had to ask Captain Dennis for help.

Cecilia felt that the pendant, which Alice had kept close to her, might be something important—it couldn’t be discarded carelessly.

"Understood."

Captain Dennis hurried over, picking up the broken pendant from the ground. He gave it a quick once-over—and was instantly stunned.

His weathered face twisted in shock, his expression darkening as his brows knitted tightly together, as if recalling something from the distant past.

In his youth, Captain Dennis had been a man of great prestige, serving as a naval commander for the Kingdom of Spain—a position equivalent to high nobility. He had been well-versed in the Spanish royal family, even receiving a personal audience with the king. But due to political strife, he had been ousted from office and forced to take up a merchant’s life.

Now, on the back of Alice’s pendant, there was an engraving that caught his attention—a bull’s head against a backdrop of a blazing sun.

Dennis knew this symbol all too well. Wasn’t this the royal crest of the Kingdom of Spain?

It represented supreme royal authority. Only members of the royal family were permitted to engrave such an emblem on their possessions.

But how had it ended up on a pendant belonging to an adventurer? This was far too unusual—far too strange.

Captain Dennis turned to look at the unconscious Alice, his mind racing with doubts.

*Could this young girl… also be a member of the Spanish royal family?*

If so, why had she ended up in Great Britain, working as an adventurer?

A flood of questions surged into Dennis’s mind all at once, and he couldn’t make sense of them in the short time he had.

The Kingdom of Spain was the only human nation with the power to rival Great Britain for dominance over the seas. Its strength was formidable.

If a member of their royal family had washed up in Great Britain, that would be an extremely serious matter—one that couldn’t be taken lightly.

Just as Dennis was lost in thought, the entire mountain began to tremble, dust and debris raining down as it seemed on the verge of collapse.

"Eh?!" Cecilia froze, muttering in confusion, "What’s happening now?!"

Captain Dennis paled, standing up and shouting to all the fighting sailors—

"All hands! Cover Lady Cecilia and the fishermen’s retreat!!!"
Before the mountain could collapse entirely.

Let us rewind the timeline and see what was happening on the other side.

The battle there was far, *far* more intense—ten times over!

The two trapped in the cage could only watch passively as the fight unfolded.

Merlin sat cross-legged on the ground, idly watching Johnson’s performance, waiting for his turn to be pinned down and ground into the dirt.

Kyle, on the other hand, was beside himself with worry. He feared that if Johnson actually won, Cecilia’s efforts would be for nothing.

"Lord Merlin, it looks like Johnson is about to win. Can’t you do something?" Kyle asked anxiously.

"Relax, don’t panic. Johnson might be strong against normal monsters, but these two clearly have incredible magic resistance. They’re practically the natural enemies of mages." Merlin said indifferently, thinking to himself, *I’m magic-immune myself—what does magic resistance even mean?*

For mages, facing an enemy with high magic resistance was a deadly situation. The only solution was to overwhelm them with even greater magical power—there was no other way.

Even though Merlin had reassured Kyle, he was still worried. No matter how he looked at it, Johnson seemed incredibly powerful.

"Die already, you two beasts!"

Johnson roared, combining fire and earth elements once more. The two elements erupted with terrifying force, summoning a massive flaming meteor from the sky that crashed down onto the heads of the two alchemical beasts!

The arena was rocked by an explosion unlike any before—fire and debris flew everywhere, the temperature soaring as if they were standing inside a furnace. The sheer destructive power was terrifying.

The two alchemical beasts let out agonized howls from beneath the scorching meteor, their cries piercing, as if they’d been stabbed.

"This… should be the end, right?" Johnson panted heavily, sweat pouring down, soaking through his white shirt.

Even with his immense strength and exceptional magic, his mana was finite. He couldn’t keep this up forever.

Moreover, fusion magic consumed an astronomical amount of mana—something ordinary people couldn’t even fathom!

After such a prolonged battle, Johnson’s mana was nearly depleted. If he still couldn’t win, he’d be in serious trouble.

But these two alchemical beasts weren’t about to go down so easily.

From beneath the burning rubble, the Dual-Headed Lion King and the Heavy Armored Mammoth slowly rose to their feet. Despite the devastating attack, they had only suffered minor injuries—nothing critical.

The two powerful alchemical beasts fixed their crimson eyes on Johnson, letting out low growls, as if mocking him.

"How is this possible?!" Johnson’s eyes widened. He was exhausted. He had already unleashed so many fusion spells—why couldn’t he even defeat two beasts? This was an insult to his reputation as a magical prodigy!

Never before had he encountered an opponent like this. The magic he took such pride in was now barely effective!

*Damn it!* If this keeps up, I’ll lose. Who knows how many bastards are waiting for me to fail, just to laugh at me!

Most importantly, I *cannot* disgrace my father. I am his pride and joy!

Even my late mother had high expectations for me—she hoped I would bring glory to the family!

I *cannot* fail! I am a genius! A prodigy admired by all!

I will make the name of Johnson echo across the entire world! I will restore our family’s former glory!

Johnson gritted his teeth, clenching his fists. The last of his Saint-tier mana surged violently, yet he still refused to give up.

"Brat, do you finally realize how pathetic you are? You dare think you can fight me? You’re delusional! Go train for a few hundred years before you even think of bridging the gap between us!"

Democritus stood on the high platform, grinning from ear to ear. He had foreseen this outcome long ago.

Still, seeing Johnson reduced to this state filled him with sheer delight.

Democritus spread his arms wide, his expression wild with arrogance as he taunted the gasping Johnson below.

"My power is beyond your reach! What kind of ‘magical prodigy’ are you? You’re just a bratty little kid! Daring to intrude on my territory was the biggest mistake of your life. Go to hell and repent!"

"Shut your filthy mouth! Don’t get cocky just yet! We’ll see who’s laughing last!" Johnson raised both hands, the magical rings on his fingers glowing brilliantly as his remaining Saint-tier mana erupted, swirling around him like armor.

"Ultimate Technique: *Wind Dragon’s Roam!*"
"Ultimate Technique: *Thousand-Soldier Thunderstorm!*"

He unleashed two Ultimate Techniques without hesitation—both clearly copied from his enemies.

*Wind Dragon’s Roam* was stolen from a mage who had once come to challenge him. The rampaging wind dragon would tear everything in its path to shreds—leveling cities was child’s play.

*Thousand-Soldier Thunderstorm* belonged to an evil fugitive. A supremely powerful lightning spell, not only was its attack force immense, but its area of effect was vast as well—even dragons would fall from the sky.

Johnson’s expression was grave, his teeth nearly grinding to dust as he fixed his gaze on the two alchemical beasts before him.

He knew this was his final strike. After this, he wouldn’t have any mana left.

To his left, the wind element swirled, a faint dragon taking shape. To his right, the lightning element crackled, thunder rumbling with overwhelming killing intent.

Then, Johnson suddenly clapped his hands together. The two Ultimate Techniques began to fuse, unleashing an unprecedented force. The monstrous pressure it emitted was terrifying.

*Pffft!* Kyle spat out a mouthful of water, his eyes widening in shock. "Good gods! He can even *fuse* Ultimate Techniques?!"

"...This... this is... this is defying the heavens!!!"

title: Chapter 49 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 49 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 8 · Chapter 49

A bead of cold sweat slid down Democritus’ forehead as he stood on the high platform, feeling the pressure. *No way… can he even fuse ultimate techniques?* He never expected this bratty kid to have such a powerful trump card hidden away! So the title of “genius mage” wasn’t just empty praise after all, huh?

The Dual-Headed Lion King and the Heavy Armored Mammoth seemed to sense the danger in the air. They charged forward with terrifying speed, intending to disrupt Johnson’s spellcasting.

But it was too late. Johnson wasn’t about to give these beasts a chance. He pressed his palms together, then clenched them into a mighty fist and swung it down. His strongest magic erupted in an instant.

“Fused Ultimate Technique—Wind-Thunder Annihilation!!!”

The fully charged ultimate move exploded forth!

A violent tempest, paired with devastating lightning, unleashed an unstoppable force!

The fusion of two elemental ultimates produced power far beyond what ordinary magic or techniques could achieve. It wasn’t a simple 1+2 addition—it was exponential, reaching a terrifying level!

The storm, infused with the might of lightning, struck both alchemical beasts head-on. They let out ear-splitting howls of agony.

But the wind and thunder didn’t stop there. The entire mountain trembled, and the arena was blasted straight through. Countless fragments of rock rained down. The cowardly Democritus ducked under the platform, shivering in fear of being caught in the crossfire.

The meditating Merlin slowly opened his eyes, watching the storm and lightning rage before him. He nodded to himself. *Not bad at all… especially for a fourteen-year-old kid.*

But this fused ultimate technique still wasn’t enough. It couldn’t compare to the Twin Sword Saints’ fusion from before—it was far too immature.

The Twin Sword Saints’ fused ultimate had been far more refined, far more powerful. The gap in strength was on a completely different level.

The storm dissipated. The Dual-Headed Lion King and the Heavy Armored Mammoth were in a horrific state, countless wounds exposing stark white bone. Clearly, they were beyond saving.

*…Huff…*

Johnson panted heavily, sweat soaking his body. His mana was completely drained.

But seeing the beasts in such a state, he couldn’t help but feel a surge of excitement. He clenched his fists. “I… I won!!!”

“Cough… cough…” Democritus crawled out from under the platform, coughing, then suddenly sneered. “Brat, don’t be so naive. My little darlings are far stronger than you think~”

The wounds on the Dual-Headed Lion King and the Heavy Armored Mammoth began to slowly heal. With a *squelch*, they stood back up, their crimson eyes rolling wildly.

How could such grievous injuries heal so quickly?!

Kyle’s expression turned ice-cold. He never expected these alchemical beasts to be this formidable. Not only was their offensive power insane, but their self-healing was absurdly strong too!

…

Johnson’s face paled. He dropped to his knees with a *thud*, his eyes filled with despair.

That was my strongest magic… why didn’t it work?!

What *are* these monsters?! How can they have such ridiculous power?!

It’s over… everything’s over. I’m going to be humiliated in front of everyone.

I, who carry the fate of my family… am this weak? I’m nothing but a worthless failure!

Johnson had begun to question his entire existence. With his mana exhausted, he was powerless.

“HAHAHAHA…” Democritus laughed maniacally, pointing at the kneeling Johnson with a mocking grin. “That’s right! I was waiting to see that look of utter despair on your face! It’s *perfect*! My alchemical beasts were born for slaughter. They won’t truly die unless they suffer a fatal blow! Now do you understand what *real* despair feels like, brat?! Serves you right!”

Johnson remained silent on the ground. He had no excuses. He was outmatched. No better than a cripple.

“Die already…” Democritus said coldly, as if discarding a toy he’d grown tired of.

The Dual-Headed Lion King roared, baring its sharp fangs, and lunged at its prey, aiming to tear out his throat.

The Heavy Armored Mammoth trumpeted, swinging its massive tusks, as if it wanted to play with Johnson’s head like a ball!

The situation was critical. It was finally time for the true protagonist to make his entrance.

“Finally my turn?”

Merlin slowly stood up, then—using magic—simply walked out of Johnson’s Holy Light Cage as if it were nothing.

“Eh?!” Kyle’s eyes widened in shock. “So Merlin-sama could just walk out this whole time?!”

“A flimsy cage like this could never hold me.” Merlin shrugged.

“Hmmm…” Kyle pondered for a moment, then put on a serious face. “As expected of Merlin-sama. I suppose this is a lesson in staying calm in the face of danger. True gold always shines in the end. I’ve learned something new today.”

“Uh… sure, whatever.” Merlin gave an awkward chuckle, waving his hand as he walked toward the helpless Johnson.

Watching Merlin’s back, Kyle’s heart swelled with admiration. *That regal bearing… it makes this devoted follower yearn for more.*

If Merlin had been born into another race, he’d no doubt be an outstanding leader.

Kyle thought to himself, completely unaware that this man was actually the infamous Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace, whose name alone struck fear into hearts.

The two alchemical beasts raced each other, eager to finish off the detested mage. In a blink, they closed in on Johnson, ready to deliver the killing blow.

Johnson, his face blank with resignation, had already accepted his fate. He felt utterly worthless.

Just as the attacks were about to land, Merlin appeared in front of Johnson in a flash. He raised both hands and *blocked* the combined assault of the two powerful alchemical beasts. The ground behind him instantly cracked in a massive web of fractures.

The sheer physical might on display was undeniable!

Kyle’s face lit up with excitement. *As expected of Merlin-sama! He’s the strongest!*

Johnson, still on the ground, snapped back to reality. Watching Merlin physically repel two such powerful foes left him stunned. *No way… this old man’s physical strength is this insane? He’s already holding his own against two beasts!* …This is impossible…

“H-How is this possible?! He actually resisted a direct strike from my two darlings?!”

Democritus’ eyes bulged in disbelief. The scene before him was incomprehensible.

How could a mere Iron-ranked adventurer withstand the might of his masterpieces?! It defied all logic!

Unless… he was a hidden powerhouse? But even if he was, he should’ve crushed them effortlessly!

Democritus was furious. He felt insulted. He roared, “Useless trash! Put some effort into it! Have you forgotten how many humans you’ve devoured?! A pathetic excuse like him should be easy prey!”

“Hmph!” Merlin gave a cold snort, then said indifferently, “Baka yaro.”

“What kind of bird language is that?!” Democritus’ mind was filled with question marks. He had no idea what that meant.

“Cough… cough…” Merlin covered his mouth, masking his embarrassment. He’d accidentally slipped into a language from another world. “It means… you’re an idiot.”

“Are you calling me uncultured?! Bastard! Kill him!” Democritus, feeling mocked, furiously ordered the alchemical beasts to attack.

The Dual-Headed Lion King and the Heavy Armored Mammoth redoubled their efforts, trying to crush Merlin to death under their combined might.

Though the cracks behind Merlin spread with a *crack-crack-crack*, they couldn’t budge him even a little. The difference in power was simply on another level.

“With this much strength, you dare flaunt your power in front of me? How naive.”

Merlin forced the two powerful alchemical beasts back, then took a step away to create space.

Then, his hand gripped the hilt of *Banri Garan*. In a flash, he drew the blade and executed a two-slash combo at lightspeed!

A lethal sword aura erupted. Both alchemical beasts were cleanly bisected, suffering fatal wounds, and died on the spot.

Democritus on the high platform was so shocked he fell onto his backside. His eyes nearly popped out of his head, and his jaw dropped low enough to fit a whole apple. He was utterly stunned.

*My… my masterpieces… were insta-killed by an Iron-ranked adventurer?!*

Good heavens! This world has gone mad! How could there exist a man this powerful?!

title: Chapter 50 — Make-up Update
content:
Chapter 50 — Make-up Update

Volume 8 · Chapter 50

The dual-headed lion king and the heavy armored mammoth, which had been nearly invincible—boasting not only immense offensive power but also self-healing abilities—had just been instantly slaughtered by Merlin with a single strike?

The remaining three onlookers were all stunned, unable to comprehend what they had just witnessed. It was simply unbelievable.

Democritus was so terrified that he collapsed to the ground, staring at Merlin below with sheer horror, his lips trembling as he struggled to form a single word.

My masterpiece! My life’s work! My capital!

How could it be one-shot by a Black Iron adventurer?!

This man was unnatural. If he wasn’t dreaming, then Merlin was absurdly overpowered!

Those creations should have effortlessly crushed Saint-tier mages. In his eyes, they had no fatal weaknesses.

Yet they had fallen so easily. It was incomprehensible...

Democritus stared at Merlin, his entire body trembling. He no longer dared to underestimate this man.

After all this, it turned out the most unassuming Black Iron adventurer among them was the strongest fighter of the group.

The two powerful alchemical beasts hadn’t even managed to let out a dying scream before suffering fatal, unhealable wounds and collapsing dead on the spot.

Their massive bodies crashed to the ground, and crimson blood spurted into the air before pattering down in thick droplets.

Merlin’s ruby-like eyes were cold, even redder than the blood suspended in the air. A mocking smile played on his face.

He slowly sheathed his greatsword, then rubbed his shoulder before casually remarking,

“So that was your masterpiece? Killing them was almost too easy.”

Johnston behind him nearly coughed up blood. He lifted his head, his face etched with shock as he stared at Merlin’s back, his expression unreadable.

So strong... strong enough to make him doubt his own eyes.

Were those two monsters really that weak? To be cut down so effortlessly?

No, his strongest spells hadn’t even been able to kill them. How could they be easy opponents?

The truth was clear: it wasn’t that the alchemical beasts were weak—it was that this old man was ridicuously overpowered!

Johnston had assumed Merlin was just an ordinary Saint-tier powerhouse, but now it was obvious he was far beyond that. In fact, Johnston couldn’t even compare.

The way Merlin had casually slaughtered the alchemical beasts, the offhand remark—every action stabbed deeply at Johnston’s pride as a magical genius.

“As expected of Lord Merlin! So strong!” Kail, ever the loyal cheerleader, didn’t forget to sing Merlin’s praises. He had already been freed from the light prison—Johnston’s magic had been exhausted, so the Holy Light Cage could no longer be sustained.

Merlin glanced at Kail, and a cold sweat slid down his forehead. He had been feeling pretty good about himself, but Kail’s over-the-top flattery made him feel a little cheap.

Democritus scrambled to his feet, his words stumbling out in panic. “What did you do?! What kind of technique was that?! How did you kill my masterpiece in one strike?! That’s impossible!”

“Just a normal iaijutsu...” Merlin shrugged and said seriously.

Johnston’s face twisted. He stared at Merlin as if he were an idiot. *Impossible!* That had to be a lie! Iaijutsu was a low-level technique, all flash and no substance. It didn’t even require battle aura to use. How could it have the power to instantly kill two formidable monsters? It was a pipe dream!

“Are you joking?! Do you take me for an idiot?!”

Democritus felt his intelligence had been insulted. He cursed furiously, “Bastard! You must be hiding some kind of power! Otherwise, how could you have defeated my creation?!”

“Tch.” Merlin sighed helplessly and said indifferently, “Believe whatever you want. The most important thing is to be happy.”

The power to instantly kill his pets, yet confined to a Black Iron adventurer... Democritus narrowed his eyes, growing even more curious about Merlin.

Even Johnston behind him shared the same doubt. With the strength Merlin had just displayed, he could easily be a Mithril-ranked adventurer. Why would he stay at the despised Black Iron rank?

If Merlin had magic or battle aura, he wouldn’t mind raising his rank. But the reality was cruel.

“An adventurer can’t be your true identity, can it? With that kind of power, you’re definitely not some nobody.” Democritus paused, then said seriously, “Just who the hell are you? Why did you come to subjugate me? I don’t recall ever seeing someone as powerful as you...”

“Me?” Merlin touched the hilt of his sword at his waist, cleared his throat, and answered seriously, “I am the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace.”

Silence fell. The atmosphere turned painfully awkward.

Merlin felt a few black lines form on his forehead. *What the hell?* Were these guys doing this on purpose? Leaving him hanging like this was *so* embarrassing!

Democritus blinked, dumbly sizing Merlin up. No matter how he looked, Merlin was human—no demonic traits or aura at all. And yet he claimed to be one of the Demon Lords? He wasn’t even a minor demon!

Surely this bastard was lying again! Time and time again, he had deceived him with lies. He clearly didn’t take him seriously at all!

Damn it! He absolutely wouldn’t let this bastard leave here alive for daring to look down on him!

Democritus’s forehead veins throbbed with rage as he snarled at Merlin,

“You? A Demon Lord? Who the hell would believe that?! Do you think everyone’s blind? Can’t you see he’s human?!”

Merlin silently sighed. *The world really is going downhill.* Even when he told the truth, no one believed him.

Johnston shared Democritus’s skepticism. He couldn’t associate Merlin with the Demon Lords at all.

But Johnston was curious—how had Merlin completely concealed his battle aura? He couldn’t sense it at all.

If he hadn’t witnessed Merlin’s overwhelming strength firsthand, Johnston would have still thought he was just an ordinary man.

“L-Lord Merlin, stop joking around. The Demon Lords aren’t as noble as you. Every word you say is so profound.” To Kail, his devoted fanboy, Merlin was like a life mentor. It was hard to imagine him as a ferocious Great Demon Lord.

“Fine...” Merlin nodded, then spread his hands and said, “I’m just Reksumu’s Black Iron adventurer, a gambling addict who never learns, a con artist who’ll do anything for a buck. I’ve seduced octogenarian grandmas and ridden nine-year-old lolis. They call me the rising star of the gigolo world—Little Chrysanthemum.”

Johnston and Kail stared at Merlin, expressionless, their emotions a tangled mess. They had no idea how to respond.

But Democritus was different. He flew into a rage, slamming his fist on the table on the high platform.

“Enough! You’re doing this on purpose! Mocking me with that arrogant attitude! You’ll pay for this!”

“I wasn’t mocking you...” Merlin put on an innocent face, wondering why this guy was so sensitive.

“Don’t think that just because you defeated my two creations, you can beat me! Those were just the engagement gifts I planned to give to Lady Asmodeus. I still have something stronger—my ultimate weapon, the pinnacle of my life’s alchemy, with extraordinary power! It’s enough to make every human kingdom tremble!” Democritus boasted proudly from the platform, still confident that his ultimate weapon would turn the tide.

But Merlin had already tuned out most of it. He only caught the first part.

*Engagement... alchemy... alchemist...*

Merlin’s eyes widened as everything suddenly clicked.

“So *you’re* the one who proposed to Asmodeus, huh? Ha! What a small world~”

“W-What? How dare you address Lady Asmodeus by name without honorifics?! Show some respect, you bastard!” Democritus raged, his face contorted. Even he used “Lady,” yet this guy was so casual—did he have no respect for his dream goddess?!

“No need. Asmodeus and I are close. No need to stand on ceremony.” Merlin replied nonchalantly.

“What nonsense are you spouting?! A human like you, close to Lady Asmodeus?! Preposterous! *I’m* the one who understands Lady Asmodeus!” Democritus pointed at himself, his eyes bloodshot, his clothes disheveled in his frenzy.

“Yeah, yeah, I’m not arguing with you. But...” Merlin looked up at Democritus and said seriously, “Giving up on proposing is for the best. Your personality is twisted—you’d only bring trouble. Also, Asmodeus is a man, so stop calling him ‘Lady,’ okay?”

“Wha—What did you just say?!” Democritus froze, his expression confused.

“I said Asmodeus has a dick. You’re proposing to a man.” Merlin repeated calmly, putting it in the simplest terms possible.

Democritus blanked, his face twisted as if he’d heard something incomprehensible—more baffling than any alchemical puzzle.

Asmodeus... was a man with a *huge dick*?!

That couldn’t be! How could the supremely feminine Lady Asmodeus possibly be a man?!

She was more beautiful, more radiant, more enchanting than any woman—practically a miracle of creation!

If she were a man, then what was the point of women existing at all?!

From a certain perspective, men could be entirely self-sufficient.

This had to be a lie. This bastard was slandering his goddess for no reason. What was his game? Was he trying to steal her mating rights?!

“Hey, are you even listening to me? Asmodeus is a man. He just has a very feminine face and figure. Based on my estimation, if he pulled out what’s between his legs, it’d probably be bigger than yours~” Merlin said with a straight face, hoping this poor guy would realize what he was getting into.

“Shut up! Shameless old fraud! How dare you slander my perfect goddess! You won’t leave here alive today!” Democritus gritted his teeth, clearly enraged.

“....” Merlin crossed his arms, exasperated. “What motive would I have to slander Asmodeus? You’re just completely fooled by his appearance.”

“Hmph! I don’t believe you!” Democritus narrowed his eyes, as if he had it all figured out. “You’re calling Lady Asmodeus a man just to make me give up on pursuing her, so you can have exclusive mating rights, right?!”

“Tch!” Merlin’s face darkened. He pressed a hand to his forehead, depressed.

*Damn it, does this guy really want exclusive mating rights with a cross-dressing lolicon?*

This was hopeless. This guy was beyond saving...

title: Chapter 51 — Immortality
content:
Chapter 51 — Immortality

Volume 8 · Chapter 51

"How come you're silent now? Did I guess right?" Democritus wore a smug grin. "As expected, you bastard also fell for Miss Asmodeus and want to compete with me for mating rights. Though I must admit, you and I share the same... taste."

Merlin stayed quiet, thinking, *Being infatuated with a big-breasted loli to the point of losing my soul—I really don’t want to be on the same level as this guy in terms of taste...*

"But too bad, Miss Asmodeus will ultimately become my woman. You don’t even have the right to compete with me! Only the strong are worthy of possession!" Democritus inexplicably treated Merlin as a rival in love.

"Calm down, friend. I have no intention of competing with you..." Merlin’s expression was complicated. *This guy’s brain circuits must be from Akina Mountain, right?*

"Even if what you say is true, so what if Miss Asmodeus is a man? Cuteness is justice!" Democritus declared passionately, clearly deep in the throes of obsession.

"Forget it. A guy like you is beyond saving. Just come over here and let me chop you up so I can finish this job." Merlin placed his hand on the hilt of his sword, no longer willing to argue. Facing someone so obsessed with male beauty, no amount of words would help.

"Don’t speak so lightly. Do you really think you can easily take me down?" Democritus scoffed, his arrogance on full display. "You have no idea of the heavens’ height or the earth’s depth. Next, I’ll show you my true power!"

He flicked a mechanism, and the sound of gears turning echoed through the arena. "Now, witness the miracle of alchemy—the pinnacle of my lifelong knowledge, the most perfect killing weapon ever created. Even I am captivated by its beautiful form!"

Chains trembled ceaselessly as a black iron coffin crashed to the ground, landing in the center of the arena.

The coffin was covered in dense alchemical runes, exuding an ominous aura.

Johnson furrowed his brow, vigilant. *What is this now? Could there be something even stronger than the last monsters?*

"Open your eyes wide and watch closely!"

Democritus bared his teeth in a feral grin, his mouth nearly splitting to his ears. "This is my greatest masterpiece, a testament to my wisdom and foresight in alchemy. I treat her like my own daughter. Those two alchemical beasts earlier were nothing but my dogs!"

Merlin remained expressionless but was somewhat curious. After all, alchemy was a human invention—other races didn’t believe in it. Creating such a highly aggressive bio-weapon was still novel to him.

The coffin’s door slowly swung open, revealing a dark, chilling interior.

It looked like a massive freezer, and a cold mist spilled out as the door opened.

A ferocious aura erupted, so thick and threatening that everyone had to brace themselves.

Kyle nervously swallowed, sensing something extraordinary inside. He felt like he was being stared down by something extremely dangerous.

Johnson had a foreboding feeling, one he hadn’t felt with the previous two alchemical beasts. The sheer intimidation was on a completely different level.

From the darkness of the coffin, a pair of crimson eyes suddenly snapped open, like red lanterns of warning.

The slender pupils contracted and dilated, resembling a snake coiled in a cave.

"No way..." Merlin’s eyes widened slightly. It felt familiar.

The monster in the darkness moved slowly, chains clanking as it stepped out of the massive black coffin.

A colossal dragon’s body, powerful limbs—each step shook the ground, and its tail swept violently behind it.

Two enormous wings unfurled, stretching as if waking from slumber. Its body, covered in blue-white scales, shimmered faintly with a golden hue, clearly enhanced by alchemy.

Everything about it was identical to a dragon, except for the head—it was human, with a mouth full of jagged, saw-like teeth. Its lips could split into three petal-like sections, revealing a pointed tongue. It was grotesque beyond measure.

What surprised Merlin wasn’t the monster’s strength, but its face. Though now more twisted and hideous, he could still vaguely recognize it—this was the dragonified form of one of the Four Heroes of the past, the Dragon-Taming Thief, Carolina.

When she had dragonized before, she still retained some human features, almost like a dragonkin. But now, Democritus had turned her into a true monster—a dragon with a human face.

"Damn, you’ve really had it rough. Even in death, you get no peace, and now your body’s been turned into this..." A cold sweat rolled down Merlin’s forehead. *This isn’t my fault, right? Carolina was just unlucky.*

"Look, you insects! Do you see it? This is the greatest miracle in alchemical history—the weapon of weapons! This form, born for battle—how beautiful it is!" Democritus spread his arms, his eyes filled with fanatical ecstasy.

Johnson and Kyle were speechless, both terrified by the ultimate alchemical beast before them. Far from finding it beautiful, they felt its appearance was a form of psychological damage—like something straight out of an abstract painting.

This was nothing like the two alchemical beasts Merlin had just slain. The wild, beastly aura was on a completely different scale. If alchemical beasts had a food chain, then this dragon-human abomination was undoubtedly the apex predator.

The dragon-human Carolina locked eyes with Merlin, as if recognizing an old enemy. A roar erupted from her, rage twisting her features—some instincts still lingered.

She stomped the ground, and the entire arena cracked, earth flipping upward. The raw physical power was terrifying.

If not for the special chains restraining her, she would have lunged forward to tear Merlin apart.

The three barely kept their footing. Johnson and Kyle were in awe of the monster’s absurd strength—it rivaled the might of a dominant magical beast.

Johnson felt that even at his peak, he’d struggle to defeat such a creature. A sense of helplessness crept into his heart.

"Tremble, mortals! Don’t hold back your praise! Feel the immense power of alchemy, then grovel on the ground and await your death!" Democritus was supremely confident in his trump card. The dragon-human Carolina was the prototype for all new alchemical beasts—her power was extraordinary.

Merlin let out a dry chuckle, indifferent. "Waiting meekly for death isn’t really my style."

"Hmph! Then this is farewell, you fools who don’t know your place!" Democritus sneered from above. "This alchemical beast is different from the others. Its power is so great that it’s beyond my control. So even if you beg for mercy now, it’s too late."

As soon as he finished speaking, the chains on the dragon-human Carolina shattered. With a deafening roar, she flapped her wings and charged at Merlin, unable to contain her hatred any longer.

Her dragon claws, sharp as the finest blades, swung down mercilessly, as if to tear Merlin apart—the human who had wronged her.

"Hmph!" Merlin scoffed, drawing his blade and sheathing it in one fluid motion.

The dragon-human Carolina’s head fell clean off, rolling on the ground as blood spurted from the severed neck.

The headless body wobbled before collapsing, motionless.

"...Impossible! How?!" Democritus’s face twisted in shock, then twisted into a scornful smirk. "Did you really think it would be that easy? Idiot~"

"Hm?" Merlin sensed movement from the corpse behind him and turned to look.

From the severed neck, countless crimson tendrils burst out like blood vessels, rapidly extending and reattaching to Carolina’s head.

In an instant, the wound sealed at lightning speed, healing perfectly.

The dragon-human Carolina stood up again, glaring at Merlin with crimson eyes, flicking her tongue with a hissing sound.

"HAHAHA..." Democritus laughed maniacally, pointing at Merlin below. "Fool! Did you think you could defeat the great miracle of alchemy? I told you this alchemical beast is the strongest, most perfect weapon in history! With immense power and an undying body, any fatal, lethal, or annihilating damage heals instantly. It has no weaknesses—it exists solely for slaughter! Do you feel despair yet?!"

Johnson’s face paled. He never expected Democritus to hide such a monster. Not only was its offensive power overwhelming, but its immortality made it an unsolvable existence! It was terrifying—who would’ve thought alchemy, something so minor, could create a being that... no, surpassed ancient magical beasts!

Johnson no longer dared to underestimate Democritus. Even as an alchemist, he could produce power that inspired fear. Just the alchemical beasts he’d created—even if several Saint-tier warriors fought together, they might struggle to kill it.

Kyle felt a wave of despair. How were they supposed to fight something with an undying body? There was no strategy—no matter how much effort they put in, it would just revive at full strength. Even Merlin would be troubled by this, right?

The dragon-human Carolina flicked her tongue at Merlin, as if taunting him. With her undying body, she had nothing to fear.

Merlin remained silent, gripping his sword hilt. He could sense that the alchemy-enhanced Carolina was stronger than before.

But increased strength was trivial to Merlin. The real problem was this immortality.

Past enemies had occasionally possessed powerful regenerative abilities, but fatal wounds usually meant death.

But Carolina? She could survive even decapitation. This was the first time Merlin had ever seen such a thing.

"Aren’t you going to say anything? Are you already in despair, ready to kneel and beg for mercy? HAHA..." Democritus crowed triumphantly from his high platform.

"Not at all." Merlin turned, curling his lips into a faint smile. "I think this is actually kind of fun."

title: Chapter 52 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 52 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 52

This was the first time Merlin had encountered an enemy with such remarkable self-healing abilities, and he couldn’t help but find it a little intriguing.

Perhaps this alchemy-made creature could keep him entertained for a while.

Kail stared at Merlin in shock, thinking that even with such overwhelming power, Merlin’s only reaction was to call it *interesting*? As expected of Lord Merlin—this must be the mindset of a true powerhouse.

Johnson felt much the same as Kail, his mind far from calm. Any monster without weaknesses would be a nightmare for anyone, right? But this old man was acting far too strange. Was he genuinely that skilled, or was this some kind of delaying tactic?

"Interesting?" Democritus narrowed his eyes, his voice dripping with malice. "You bastard, your arrogance knows no bounds! I’ll admit you’ve got some skill—far stronger than that so-called 'genius' on the surface—but if you think you can defeat my ultimate alchemical weapon, you’re dead wrong!"

"I *can* defeat it easily..." Merlin glanced at the dragon-human hybrid, Karona—who seemed to be female—and added, "All it takes is a single spit."

"Are you joking?!" Democritus threw his hands up, trying to make his enemy understand the magnitude of what he faced. "This alchemical beast embodies my life’s wisdom and blood! It’s a perfect weapon—flawless in attack and defense, with the blessing of immortality! How could it *lose*?!"

Democritus wasn’t exaggerating. If you excluded Merlin, a world-class anomaly, the dragon-human Karona was indeed terrifyingly powerful.

Saying she could destroy an entire nation was an overstatement, but intimidating a royal family? That was effortless.

Karona’s strength was enough to make rulers uneasy—even fearful.

"Is that so? Then I’ll show you exactly how it loses," Merlin said indifferently. "Immortality? No big deal."

He smirked, tilting his head. "There’s no enemy I can’t finish in one strike. If there is... well, then two strikes will do~!"

"...You insolent bastard!" Democritus slammed the table in fury. "Let’s see what you’ve got to back up that arrogance!"

With a roar, the dragon-bodied Karona unleashed a frost dragon’s breath, a direct assault on Merlin.

Merlin didn’t even dodge—he nullified the breath on contact. But the surrounding area began freezing rapidly!

Johnson’s heart jolted. *She can even use dragon’s breath?!* What *was* this creature?!

The ice spread steadily. Johnson’s magic was exhausted, leaving him powerless. He scrambled backward, but the frost crept faster than he could retreat.

*Damn it!* What now? Should he swallow his pride and beg these people for help?

Just as Johnson hesitated, Kail swiftly scooped him up and carried him far away.

Since Johnson was small, Kail lifted him as easily as a chick.

"Huh?!" Johnson blinked, then glared at Kail. "Put me down! I’m not so pathetic that I’d beg *you* for help!"

"What’s the point of pride now?" Kail replied seriously. "I’m just worried you’ll slow Lord Merlin down."

"*What?!* Johnson’s face burned with humiliation. "I’ve just run out of magic, that’s all! A lucky E-rank like you wouldn’t understand!"

"Sure, sure," Kail paused, then added, "For now, just don’t get in Lord Merlin’s way. That’s all we can ask of you."

"Tch!" Johnson scowled, his pride stinging, but he couldn’t deny the truth.

Karona lunged at Merlin in close combat. Though alchemy had stripped her of intelligence, she retained some instincts.

Her razor-sharp dragon claws lashed out with terrifying speed, each strike whistling past Merlin’s ears.

But to Merlin, it was all too slow. He effortlessly tracked every attack.

"Hmm, so her abilities have been enhanced to *this* level... Not bad."

Merlin muttered, his figure darting up and down, leaving only an afterimage where he stood. Karona couldn’t land a single hit.

"Hah! Now do you see how powerless you are?" Democritus sneered from the platform, his mood improving as he assumed Merlin was struggling. "Against my ultimate weapon, all you can do is scamper like a monkey!"

"Tsk." Merlin glanced at Democritus. He’d just been testing Karona’s strength.

Seizing the moment Merlin’s focus lapsed, Karona swung a crushing fist down, aiming to kill.

Merlin barely raised his arm in time to block. The collision sent a shockwave through the frozen ground, splitting it into a massive spiderweb of cracks!

"Hmm, her body, reinforced by alchemy, is nearly on par with a Frost Saint Dragon’s..."

Merlin sighed, then suddenly punched Karona, sending her crashing into the arena wall, kicking up a cloud of dust.

Democritus broke into a cold sweat. *Just raw physical strength can clash with my ultimate weapon? What kind of man is this?* It was unthinkable for a human!

He knew his creation’s limits. After countless alchemical enhancements, it had reached this peak. If not for her immortality, Karona would’ve been pummeled to death by Merlin’s fists long ago...

"ROOOOAR!"

Karona burst from the dust, her crimson eyes burning with even greater fury as she glared at Merlin.

But Merlin had already drawn his sword, his ruby eyes sharpening. He seemed to be taking this seriously now.

"I dislike women who won’t take a hint," he said coolly. "So I’ll be a *little* more serious..."

The crisp sound of a blade being unsheathed rang out. Merlin swung—

A devastating sword energy erupted, a world-ending tsunami of destruction surging forward!

Karona was obliterated on the spot. But the force didn’t stop there.

The entire arena was cleaved through, the blade’s energy tearing through the mountain, splitting the island apart with a *crack-crack-crack*, before finally bisecting the sea itself before grinding to a halt!

Cecilia and her group, who were retreating, froze at the sight.

A violent gale erupted, and the dark clouds in the sky slowly parted under the shockwave. The might of a single strike had shaken the very heavens!

The earth and sea, split in two, made it seem as if divine wrath had descended—no other explanation fit such a miraculous, terrifying sight.

The murderous sword energy seemed to herald the apocalypse, leaving all who witnessed it trembling.

"...What *is* that?!" Cecilia, carrying the unconscious Alice, paled as she muttered to herself.

"...!" Even the usually composed Captain Dennis was terrified, whispering under his breath.

"It’s like the gods themselves are enraged... It’s too horrifying..."
