title: Chapter 53 — Narrow Escape
content:
Chapter 53 — Narrow Escape

Volume 8 · Chapter 53

The entire mountain was cleaved in two by Merlin’s single slash, and it began to tremble violently.

The earth-shattering sword aura unleashed a terrifying storm.

In an instant, everything before him was reduced to ruins—no life could possibly survive such a strike head-on.

The tremors had yet to cease; the lingering might of that slash had not dissipated, still erupting continuously.

Democritus, Johnson, and Kyle all stood with their eyes wide and mouths agape, stretched to their human limits.

They didn’t speak. No chaotic thoughts cluttered their minds. Their brains were blank.

Witnessing a strike that seemed nothing short of a miracle, they were left with nothing but shock—shock beyond words. The silent scene spoke volumes: their astonishment was indescribable, no language could capture their feelings.

That draw-cut just now rivaled the blow that had decimated the Holy Church’s Crusade Army a year ago. But that had never been Merlin’s limit.

Looking back half a year, the draw-cut Merlin used to slay two Pirate Kings had been even stronger—it had reshaped the very terrain.

It had carved a massive sea trench into Elgin’s coastal domain, split open by Merlin’s blade alone.

The storm raged before finally dissipating.

Beyond the mountain, the devastation was visible—it had been cut straight through!

Fragments of rock rained down, thudding against the ground.

The once-roaring dragon-headed Lamia, Carona, had been slain by Merlin in the first instant, reduced to a pool of blood on the ground.

Merlin’s strike had been so overwhelming that Carona had no chance to heal—she was obliterated on the spot.

It seemed Democritus’ prized "immortality" had been effortlessly dismantled by Merlin, without the slightest suspense.

“What? She died that easily? I was just warming up.”

Merlin held his greatsword, casually tapping the flat of the blade against his shoulder, looking utterly indifferent, even a little mocking.

“This wasn’t true immortality, was it? A simple, brute-force solution was enough. It was just a sandbag with its self-healing cranked up a few hundred times.”

Johnson’s expression twisted in frustration. *A sandbag?! That was already insane!* How strong *was* this man? What kind of enemy would he even consider a real threat?

Wait—judging by that slash, maybe his true enemies existed in another dimension entirely!

He recalled his father’s teachings: *There’s always someone better. Never overestimate yourself.* And now, facing an existence he could never surpass, Johnson felt the crushing weight of the gap between them. As a prodigy of magic, this was the first time he’d encountered someone who outclassed him in every way. His heart was a storm of conflicting emotions.

Kyle felt much the same—he *knew* Merlin was strong, but he’d still underestimated him. The man was far, *far* beyond what he’d imagined.

A slash like that… if someone claimed Merlin was the strongest in the Great Britain Empire, Kyle might actually believe it now. The miracles Merlin created were too many to count.

“This is the strongest monster your life’s work produced?” Merlin sheathed his greatsword and lifted his gaze to the stunned Democritus on the high platform. “Honestly? It’s underwhelming. You made me take this seriously for nothing. Your ultimate weapon is a disappointment.”

*Drip… drip…*

A faint sound echoed around Democritus. It wasn’t water.

Democritus had pissed himself. A pale yellow liquid seeped from his crotch, gushing out like a broken dam.

He never could have imagined that a mere Black Iron-ranked adventurer like Merlin would possess power beyond his comprehension—a perfect embodiment of the word *overwhelming*!

Democritus had known Merlin was no weakling, but he’d never expected him to be *this* absurdly strong—completely defying his predictions. The shock was so great that he’d lost control of his bladder.

*What the hell is this power?!*

Is *Iai Slash* really this useless of a skill?! How is this possible?! This is *insane*!

A normal draw-cut shouldn’t unleash a force comparable to nature itself!

This kind of power… it had to transcend the rules of this world!

Who *else* could wield such power besides some intangible god?! It was impossible for a human!

Democritus looked at the blood puddle where his ultimate weapon had been and realized his situation was dire. He was isolated, with no backup, and no more cards to play.

The inherent frailty of alchemists was laid bare—anyone here could kill him with a flick of their pinky.

“……What *are* you?!” Democritus shrieked, his voice trembling.

“This transcendent power… how could a mere human possibly—?!”

He pointed at Merlin, his hands shaking, refusing to accept reality.

He felt like all his years of effort had been for nothing. What was the point of dedicating himself to alchemy if he’d still be crushed by true power?

Democritus began to question his life, his craft, even the purpose of his struggles.

“You’re not the first to say that.” Merlin gave a faint smile.

“……You’re *not* human! I’ve never offended someone this powerful before!” Democritus’ face was ashen, cold sweat pouring down him.

“You haven’t offended me, but your head’s worth a lot. That’s enough.” Merlin’s hand rested on his sword hilt, his gaze locked onto Democritus. “Seems like the only thing of value left on you is that neck of yours. Be a good boy and let me take it.”

“D-Don’t… don’t kill me…”

Terrified out of his wits, Democritus collapsed onto the ground, his ass landing in his own urine, a pathetic, flailing mess.

The only thought in his mind was *escape*. If Merlin set his sights on him, he was dead.

Fortunately, the entire mountain range was under his control. If he used it right, there might still be a chance!

Democritus activated a hidden mechanism. The entire mountain began to collapse, the thunderous roars echoing like a storm.

Thick smoke suddenly filled the space, obscuring all vision.

The tremors made it hard to stay upright, and massive debris rained down from above.

The smoke was so dense that the path ahead was invisible—but Merlin’s slash had left an opening, a potential escape route.

Merlin wasn’t about to let Democritus get away, not when his livelihood was at stake.

With impossible speed, Merlin dashed toward the platform—only to find Democritus already gone!

A hole in the ground remained, leading downward. It seemed the man had used some kind of mechanism to flee underground.

Democritus wasn’t a fool. He’d prepared escape routes and traps in advance, and his speed had exceeded Merlin’s expectations.

“Merlin! We have to go—now! If we don’t, we’ll be buried!” Kyle dragged the dazed Johnson, shouting.

Merlin had no choice. He turned and swiftly retreated toward the exit, scowling as he cursed under his breath.

“Damn it! That bastard’s *lucky*!”

(-_-)

title: Chapter 54 — Monthly Ticket Extra Update
content:
Chapter 54 — Monthly Ticket Extra Update

Volume 8 · Chapter 54

Due to the collapse of the mountain, the entire small island was shaking like it had been hit by an earthquake.

Especially after being slashed by Merlin, it had become even more fragile.

Democritus had successfully escaped early using his own mechanical secret passage.

However, he was terrified, worried that Merlin wouldn't give up and would chase after him.

So, despite not being good at physical activity, Democritus didn't dare stop running, even though he was exhausted and gasping for breath.

He was afraid of being stared at by those ruby-like eyes, and then being sent to hell with one slash.

The dense underbrush on the island was now an obstacle for Democritus as he fled.

He breathed heavily, like he was oxygen-deprived.

His red robe was torn and tattered from being cut by thorns, and he looked utterly disheveled.

Damn it, damn it, damn it.

What kind of monster was that sword-wielding man?!

Could a human really reach that level of strength just through perseverance?!

It was impossible! Even alchemy had its limits, and there was no way to create that kind of power!

A single swing of his sword could cut through the island? That kind of power was probably on par with the strongest warriors in the world.

Legend had it that some people would receive the favor of the gods and become so-called demigods. Was that black iron adventurer, Merlin, one of those legendary beings?!

Democritus's face was pale, and his eyes were filled with tears of fear. All he could think about was escaping, getting as far away from the monster, Merlin, as possible.

He rushed out of the underbrush and arrived at a cliff, quickly taking out a horn and blowing it.

On the horizon,

A black giant dragon, bound by chains, slowly flew over, flapped its wings, and landed in front of Democritus.

This was a dragon that Democritus had tamed, and its level was relatively high, but it was still far from the six great holy dragons.

Democritus hastily mounted the dragon and controlled it to take to the skies, leaving the small island behind.

Boom!

A loud noise came from behind, and Democritus looked back to see that his base had completely collapsed, sending up a massive cloud of dust.

Looking at his laboratory, where he had spent years working, suddenly being destroyed, Democritus couldn't help but feel sad.

He had finally gotten to the point where he was about to turn things around, but then that adventurer had come out of nowhere and ruined everything.

All of his carefully crafted alchemical beasts had died.

Even his ultimate weapon hadn't survived.

It was like he had been set back to square one, with nothing to his name.

Those were all his assets for proposing to Asmodeus. Now, it was all for nothing.

Democritus sighed sadly, riding the black dragon as it flew further and further away from the island.

It seemed that he would have to start over. But as long as he had a green mountain left, he wouldn't worry about running out of firewood.

He still had some dragon blood that he had manufactured, which was a good thing.

As long as he didn't die, relying on his excellent alchemy skills, it was only a matter of time before he could recreate an alchemical beast comparable to his ultimate weapon.

For now, though, it was better to be as far away from that monster-like man as possible.

Asmodeus, I won't give up on you.

Four days passed.

During these few days, Merlin and his group hadn't left the small island, but had stayed there the entire time.

Captain Dennis and his crew had cut down many trees on the island to repair the damaged William's vessel.

Because the hull was severely damaged, especially the stern, the crew worked overtime for four days to repair the William's vessel.

Although it wasn't perfect, it was at least seaworthy again, and there was no problem returning to the interior.

Previously, Cecilia had promised Dennis that she would compensate him, so he didn't have to worry about the William's vessel. After returning, they would renovate it at a shipyard.

In fact, Cecilia didn't have that much money. The magical cannon that had been pushed into the sea alone was something she couldn't afford to compensate for with her pocket money.

However, Cecilia's situation was now completely different. Although that detestable Democritus had escaped, the turmoil in the Moreau Strait had been calmed, and in a certain sense, she had completed her task.

For Cecilia, this was a great achievement, enough for her to brag about in front of her father and to hold her head high among her siblings.

So, the Duke of Roses might take responsibility for compensating for the losses Cecilia had caused and would praise her.

Her pocket money would naturally increase.

After all, Cecilia had brought honor to the entire Rose family and had contributed to the improvement of the family's status. As her father, the Duke of Roses wouldn't scold her.

Although Cecilia and Kayle hadn't contributed much during this trip, the hired Merlin had been the main force, cutting down three monsters and driving away the evil alchemist.

So, this achievement naturally fell on Cecilia's head as the employer, and she was extremely happy about it.

She had even specifically mentioned it to Johnson, worried that he would try to steal the credit.

"This matter was solved by us, and it has nothing to do with you. I heard from my knight that you were beaten to a pulp, so don't try to claim that you were the one who calmed the turmoil. We will pierce your mask of genius without hesitation."

Johnson was extremely displeased when he heard this, especially the phrases "beaten to a pulp" and "pierce your mask of genius," which deeply hurt his pride.

He was indeed a genius, and he didn't wear a mask. As for being beaten badly, it was largely because his magic had no effect on the enemy, who had strong resistance.

However, Johnson didn't explain much, too lazy to argue with Cecilia, a noble lady. Instead, he retorted.

"Shut up, old lady. I haven't sunk to the point of stealing others' credit. Don't look down on people."

Cecilia was furious at being called "old lady." If Kayle hadn't stopped her, she would have argued with Johnson until the end of time.

Although the group was arguing fiercely, everything was moving in a positive direction.

Merlin and Alice would receive 200,000 gold coins, as previously agreed, and they had already received a large sum of money.

Although it was still a significant gap from repaying their debt of several million, this small step forward was a big step for Merlin and Alice.

Even if they deducted the amount they would use for repayment, they would still have 60,000 gold coins left, enough for them to live comfortably for a while without worrying about their livelihood.

It seemed that if this trend continued, their lives would get better and better.

Johnson had been distracted these few days, even refusing to chat with Kayle, appearing cold and detached, like he was ignoring everyone.

He seemed to be deliberately avoiding everyone, often going to gaze at the fault line on the small island that Merlin had cut open.

He kept pondering the gap between himself and Merlin, but the more he thought about it, the more desperate he became. Even if he used all his might to cast magic, he couldn't achieve Merlin's level of destructive power.

The gap in strength was obvious, and it made Johnson, a young magical genius, doubt his own abilities, feeling that no matter how hard he tried, he would never be able to catch up to Merlin.

It was worth mentioning that Captain Dennis had been visiting Alice these few days, appearing very enthusiastic, seemingly wanting to ask her something.

However, Alice had been in a coma the entire time, and Captain Dennis would just visit and then leave.

He left Merlin to take care of her alone, as in the eyes of outsiders, Merlin was Alice's husband.

At this moment, in a room on the William's vessel,

The comatose Alice lay on the bed, breathing steadily, but her consciousness hadn't recovered.

Merlin sat beside the bed, looking at Alice with a serious expression, and couldn't help but touch her pale face, saying in a low voice,

"This person really is quite bold."

"She knew how to run away when she saw me a year ago. What's wrong with her now?"

(°∞叭)

title: Chapter 55 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 55 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 55

Today was an important day for everyone.

After Captain Dennis personally inspected the ship, the William had been repaired and today was the day it would set sail back to the continent.

The wind and weather were both favorable for sailing, so it was estimated that it would take less than two days to return to the mainland of the Britannian Empire.

After all, the William had been severely damaged and couldn’t move as quickly as it had on the way here. It could only rely on a small amount of manpower and wind to proceed.

The repaired William moved slowly, the entire ship creaking and groaning, making one feel as if it might fall apart halfway through the journey.

However, Captain Dennis had given his personal guarantee that it was absolutely sturdy. The repairs were solid, and as long as they didn’t encounter a major storm, there would be no problems.

Only after hearing Captain Dennis’s assurance did everyone feel slightly at ease and return to their tasks.

The William sailed smoothly across the sea, leaving ripples in its wake.

A few seagulls flew in formation, skimming the water’s surface before soaring into the sky and passing over Cecilia’s head.

At this moment, Cecilia stood proudly at the bow of the William, gazing at the vast, endless sea ahead.

She felt that when she returned, her father, who had never looked at her properly before, would finally see her in a new light.

If the Britannian royal family were to bestow some kind of honor upon her, that would be the icing on the cake.

Cecilia decided that as soon as she disembarked, she would quickly summon a group of newspaper reporters to properly publicize her great achievements.

“Cecilia.”

Cecilia turned her head, displeased. “Hmm? Where were you just now? As my knight, running around like that is unacceptable.”

“My apologies, I was just checking on Miss Alice,” Kael answered awkwardly.

“Miss Alice has woken up?!” Cecilia asked in surprise.

“Not yet. She’s still unconscious,” Kael said with a worried expression.

Cecilia was also concerned. If Alice remained in a coma, she would feel guilty. “Then does Lord Merlin have any leads? Is there any way to wake Miss Alice? She’s been asleep for four days now.”

“Lord Merlin said he doesn’t have a solution either. If there were a healer who specialized in mental magic, they might be able to help, but there isn’t one on the ship. Johnson seems to only know offensive mental magic, so we can only wait for Miss Alice to regain consciousness on her own,” Kael said helplessly, understanding that the young lady was worried, even if she didn’t say it aloud.

Cecilia sighed silently. It seemed there was nothing to do but wait. She turned back to the sea and muttered, “I just feel like I’ve held Miss Alice back. If only I were stronger...”

Kael’s expression turned unnatural. He understood the young lady’s feelings—she must be feeling some guilt.

Kael felt the same way. He thought he had been useless, holding Merlin back.

Earlier, Lord Merlin had clearly been able to catch up to the evil alchemist and kill him.

But in the end, he had to help Kael and Johnson escape the collapsing mountain.

Without Merlin’s help, with Kael’s strength, it would have been difficult to escape unscathed while carrying Johnson. He would have been buried alive.

So Kael himself felt useless. If he had known, he would have let Merlin act alone. He hadn’t been any help at all.

“But speaking of which, Miss Alice is really strong. She even seems to know some dragon-specific skills,” Cecilia suddenly said, recalling Alice’s figure from before. Her power had truly been explosive.

“Eh? Dragon skills?!” Kael’s eyes widened in shock.

“Mhm. It was like she turned into a humanoid dragon, with an incredibly strong dragon’s presence. She even grew dragon scales on her body!” Cecilia said seriously.

After hearing Cecilia’s description, Kael thought to himself. Some dragons, upon reaching a certain level of strength, could indeed transform into humanoid forms. But Alice was clearly not a dragon, so there was only one other possibility.

“Maybe she’s a Dragon Warrior or a Dragon Mage?”

“What’s that?” Cecilia furrowed her delicate brows, completely confused by Kael’s rambling.

“They’re legendary people who can wield the power of dragons. They can apparently undergo the kind of transformation you described. I’ve heard they can gain dragon talents and might even be stronger than actual dragons. But almost no one knows the exact method to obtain dragon power,” Kael said thoughtfully, as if recalling a distant memory.

“Where did you learn all this?” Cecilia’s eyes widened. She didn’t think Kael read that often.

“Miss Cecilia, there’s no need to be surprised. My father was a hunter. Before joining the Rose family, I traveled with him everywhere, so I’ve heard many strange and unusual stories,” Kael replied with a smile.

“I see.” Cecilia nodded, enviously. “I wonder how Miss Alice managed it.”

Seeing Cecilia’s envious expression, Kael couldn’t help but worry. “Miss, please don’t go around asking. If it’s a secret, prying would be rude, especially when it comes to personal cultivation.”

“I know that.” Cecilia puffed her cheeks in frustration before sighing. “It’s just that Miss Alice suddenly became so powerful. It really surprised me.”

“Maybe... maybe the enemies just weren’t strong enough, so you got that impression?” Kael ventured cautiously.

“How is that possible?! That vulture with multiple wings was really strong. The power Miss Alice unleashed at that moment was definitely Saint-tier,” Cecilia said with absolute seriousness.

“Eh?! Really?” Kael’s eyes widened in shock.

“Mhm.” Cecilia nodded, recalling how Alice had swung a sword at her. “I experienced it firsthand. It’s true. It was completely beyond my imagination. Maybe it was the sudden explosion of such immense power that caused Miss Alice to lose consciousness.”

“That’s very possible. I never expected Miss Alice to have such potential. It seems like it won’t be long before she becomes a Saint-tier powerhouse.”

Kael had long suspected that Alice’s strength far exceeded that of a normal high-rank. After hearing Cecilia’s words, he suddenly understood—her potential couldn’t be measured by common sense.

“Actually, Lord Merlin’s strength is also beyond my imagination.”

“How so?” Cecilia perked up at the mention of Lord Merlin.

“Do you remember when the island was split in two, as if struck by lightning?” Kael said with a grave expression.

“Of course. That day nearly scared me to death,” Cecilia replied earnestly.

“That was Lord Merlin’s doing. Just a single draw-slash,” Kael said concisely.

“Eh?!” Cecilia’s eyes widened. She had always assumed it was the enemy’s doing. She never expected it to be Merlin! That was truly unexpected. So Lord Merlin’s power was that strong? Maybe he could stand alongside the empire’s top powerhouses!

“It feels like Lord Merlin’s power has no limits. He can effortlessly resolve anything. I even doubt whether Lord Merlin is truly just a Saint-tier powerhouse. Maybe there really is a higher tier beyond that,” Kael furrowed his brows, deep in thought. No matter how long he pondered, he couldn’t determine the limits of Merlin’s strength. All he felt was that the enemies before him were too weak.

“Kael, how strong do you think Lord Merlin is?” Cecilia asked tentatively, wanting a rough estimate.

Kael crossed his arms, took a deep breath, and made a bold guess.

“Conservatively speaking... Lord Merlin’s strength is by no means inferior to the Thistle Kingdom’s First Knight.”

title: Chapter 56 — Awakening
content:
Chapter 56 — Awakening

Volume 8 · Chapter 56

Kyle made a very conservative estimate. Given what he knew of Merlin now, it was hard to imagine just how powerful he had become.

But in the eyes of the people of Great Britain, the Thorn First Knight was already a peak powerhouse of the empire, widely known to all.

So when Kyle rated Merlin’s strength as no weaker than the Thorn First Knight, it wasn’t an insult—it was high praise.

Cecilia’s eyes widened, her shocked mouth hanging open. The Thorn First Knight was Queen Elizabeth’s personal guard, a symbol of royal authority.

To this day, the name Cecilia had heard most often was that of the Thorn First Knight, Mesfield—universally acknowledged as the empire’s strongest.

Now Kyle believed Merlin was no weaker than the Thorn First Knight, which was the same as saying Merlin stood at the very pinnacle of the empire’s power.

"Are you serious?"

"Mm. This is my conservative estimate. I don’t even dare confirm it myself, because I can’t see through Merlin’s strength at all."

Kyle spoke with an awkward expression, recalling that godlike power. Maybe Merlin was even stronger than the Thorn First Knight.

"And Merlin is too bizarre. Normally, you can’t sense even a hint of pressure from him. If I hadn’t seen it with my own eyes, I’d probably still think he was just an ordinary man. If I told others Merlin was on par with the Thorn First Knight, I doubt anyone would believe me."

Cecilia fell silent. Though Merlin was currently just an Iron-ranked adventurer with no reputation to speak of, with this kind of power, he was destined for greatness. Sooner or later, he would rise to prominence.

Cecilia secretly resolved to establish a good relationship with Merlin and his wife. That would be greatly beneficial for her own future.

After all, Merlin’s strength was undeniable. Powerful individuals were always sought after by major factions.

But before Merlin became famous, it would be better to take the initiative and build ties with him under the Rose family’s name, securing an advantage ahead of others—

*Sigh.* "Isn’t this couple… monstrous?"

---

Inside a cabin on the ship.

Merlin had already heard from Cecilia about what had happened to Alice.

Looking at the unconscious Alice on the bed, Merlin couldn’t help but feel a little helpless. This girl was too impulsive, too prone to acting on emotion.

Most Heroes were overflowing with a sense of justice and not much in the way of brains—Merlin had long since grown used to that.

But when it happened to Alice, he felt an indescribable frustration. She was just too naive.

If you threw Alice into a real-world pyramid scheme, Merlin was certain she’d dive in headfirst and never come back. She was that kind of idiot.

No one was made of stone. Merlin wasn’t heartless either. After spending some time with Alice, seeing her in this state left a bitter taste in his mouth.

He had told Alice not to use the power of the Inheritance Crystal. With her current pathetic strength, she couldn’t control it at all.

But on second thought, Merlin realized it wasn’t entirely Alice’s fault for being reckless. Even if she hadn’t consciously activated the Inheritance Crystal’s power, in moments of despair, her potential might have subconsciously flared up. Maybe it wasn’t her intention.

Merlin sat beside her, peeling an apple, occasionally glancing at Alice. Though he claimed he didn’t care about the fate of the "washboard Hero," his actions told a different story.

Merlin could only justify it to himself as a psychological need for companionship. After being alone for so long, maybe he just wanted someone around.

The William was still afloat, though the entire ship swayed unsteadily. The repairs weren’t perfect.

Because she had forcibly activated the Inheritance Crystal’s power, the strain on Alice’s body was severe. She had been unconscious for four days without waking.

But now, Alice’s condition was improving. Her silent mind slowly began to stir.

Alice slightly opened her eyes. The first thing she saw was a slightly damp ceiling.

*Where is this?*

Confusion filled her mind. Hearing the sound of waves outside, she realized she was on a ship.

Panic set in. She had no idea which ship she was on or where she was being taken.

Then, her peripheral vision caught Merlin peeling an apple beside her. That eased her mind somewhat.

A familiar face meant this place was safe. There was no need to worry too much.

Alice squinted, studying Merlin as he peeled the apple. A mix of emotions surged within her.

*Is he… taking care of me?*

It certainly looked that way. The apple he was peeling was probably for her.

So this bastard could be considerate? He had a conscience after all. He wasn’t the kind of villain who’d take advantage of someone in trouble.

He usually acted like he couldn’t care less, even threatening to harm her, but in the end, he turned out to be a decent guy.

Alice’s face flushed. *What’s wrong with me?* Had Merlin brainwashed her? How could she think well of the Great Demon Lord? She should draw a clear line, stand in absolute opposition!

Merlin seemed to sense Alice’s gaze. He stopped peeling the apple and looked at her strange expression.

"Mm." Alice gave a soft hum in response.

Neither of them expected their first conversation after days of silence to be so mundane, devoid of any great joy or sorrow.

"Looking better. Your face is quite rosy~" Merlin grinned, teasing her.

Alice’s embarrassment deepened, her face turning even redder. She couldn’t help but retort, "Shut up, you!"

"Waking up to see me by your side—aren’t you overwhelmed with emotion? Almost in tears?" Merlin probed, seemingly very interested in Alice’s current thoughts.

"As if! I’m not moved at all! Don’t get the wrong idea!" Alice hesitated, then muttered insincerely, "Waking up to see my enemy’s ugly face… I feel terrible. I’d rather pass out again."

"Tsk." Merlin clicked his tongue in exasperation, shrugging. "Can’t you be a little honest? I won’t laugh at you."

"Hmph~!" Alice pouted, sulking. "Like I’d ever believe you."

Merlin felt a pang of annoyance. He had taken care of Alice for four days, and she hadn’t even said thank you. Anyone would feel unbalanced.

Alice had just woken up and felt a little thirsty. Conveniently, there was a glass of water on the nearby table within reach.

*Self-sufficiency is the best policy.* Alice decided to get it herself. She wasn’t about to ask Merlin for help.

But as she leaned forward to grab the water, Merlin snatched it away first.

"What are you doing? I’m thirsty." Alice glared at him, puffing her cheeks, convinced he was deliberately making things difficult.

"Want water? Too bad, I’m thirsty too." Merlin unceremoniously downed the entire glass in one go, even licking up the last drops, then let out a satisfied sigh. "Ah~! Hehe."

Alice gritted her teeth in fury. The tiny bit of goodwill she had managed to accumulate vanished in an instant.

So Merlin was still Merlin.

She had actually thought he was a decent person just now. How naive of her!

title: Chapter 57 — Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 57 — Bonus Update

Volume 8 · Chapter 57

Alice glared at Merlin, her hands clutching the bedsheet she had wrumpled up, lips parting but unable to form words.

This Merlin was so inhumane! Was he really someone I misjudged?

He was a genuine demon to the core, loving to toy with others, utterly rotten!

Alice was in a bad mood. She had just awakened and already Merlin had annoyed her so much she really wanted to punch his smug face.

"What 'what' of it? Got a problem with me?" Merlin held a cup and struck an extremely elegant pose.

"You brute! That's how you treat a patient!? That's so inhumane!" Alice invoked higher authority, escalating the issue to the level of basic humanity.

"My apologies, but I'm a demon. Things like humanity simply don't exist in me." Merlin tilted the corners of his mouth and said smugly.

Alice thought about it and Merlin had a point. What would a demon need humanity for? So she changed her wording. "What kind of grudge do I have against you? Why do you always bully me!?"

"Me? Bully you? I'm so merciful, how could I possibly single you out to torment? Even when bullying someone, you have to distribute your attention evenly. That's what fairness looks like." Merlin said shamelessly.

"Stop spouting nonsense with such a straight face. I don't want to hear your twisted logic. I only know that refusing me water is clearly abuse to satisfy some psychological satisfaction." Alice knitted her brows, feeling as though Merlin spoke of bullying others as if it were perfectly natural.

Merlin chuckled softly, set down the empty water cup, and picked up an apple that had been mostly peeled. He cut off a small piece. "Eat the apple first. Wait a bit for the water."

Alice looked warily at the small piece of apple Merlin offered, her gaze darting back and forth between his face and the apple.

Is he messing with me?

Thinking about how nasty this guy could be, it wasn't entirely impossible.

Was he really feeding me right now? He had never done something like that before.

Despite being wary of Merlin, Alice was so thirsty that eating some fruit would be fine.

So the eager Alice decided on a swift action, opening her mouth wide and moving quickly to take a bite.

But then — *crack* — the sound of teeth colliding echoed, and she bit at nothing.

"Hehe, wanted the apple?" Merlin scraped the piece of fruit off the knife and popped it into his own mouth, deliberately chewing loudly. "So sweet and refreshing~!"

Alice's face slowly flushed red. As expected, even with some caution, she had been played by Merlin, and not only that, she had been mercilessly mocked.

She felt Merlin was being somewhat disrespectful toward her. After all, she was half a patient right now! To make fun of her like this! How despicable!

Actually, Merlin still held grudges. Who told Alice to have such a bad attitude right after waking up? This was simply returning the favor in kind.

"You brute! I never want to see you again—umph!"

Before Alice could finish her sentence, Merlin stuffed an apple piece into her mouth, leaving her momentarily speechless.

"Eat it. Don't think I'm abusing you," Merlin said in a meaningful tone.

Alice blinked her lively big eyes, gave Merlin a fierce sidelong glare, then huffed and ate the apple. "Hmph~!"

"Anyway," Merlin crossed his legs and prepared to ask about the dragon transformation, "I already warned you. Why did you still forcibly use the power of the inheritance crystal?"

"Huh?!" Alice, holding the apple, raised her head blankly. "When did I use the power of the inheritance crystal?"

"Without using the inheritance crystal's power, how did you survive against Cecilia?" Merlin tilted his head inquiringly, feeling like Alice was as confused as someone who had drunk too much, completely unaware of what had happened.

"Did I really use it? How come I have absolutely no idea?" Alice's expression grew more and more puzzled.

Merlin sighed inwardly. As expected — she had unconsciously activated the inheritance crystal.

"You did use it. Otherwise, how could you have been unconscious for so long?"

Alice's eyes widened. The apple in her hand fell onto the bed, her face going completely blank.

"Seriously..." Merlin pressed a hand to his forehead, saying wearily, "I told you not to use it carelessly. There will be side effects. And yet you still couldn't control yourself."

"Side effects!?" Alice quickly checked and moved her limbs. They seemed fine and still movable, and she didn't feel any discomfort in her body. "What side effects!? I feel pretty good~!"

"Are you really treating my words as wind passing your ears!?" You won't be able to turn back into a human, you idiot." Merlin tilted the corners of his mouth, already at a loss for words about Alice's dense nature.

"Really!?" Alice was startled. She didn't want to switch races at all. Being human was quite nice.

"Don't believe me? Look at your own belly yourself. Aren't there still dragon scales that haven't faded?" Merlin answered calmly, hoping Alice would face the seriousness of her situation.

Alice quickly sat up and tugged at the hem of her clothes. Then suddenly her face reddened, remembering Merlin was still there.

So Alice glanced warily at Merlin, silently turned around, and secretly lifted the fabric to look.

Merlin showed a hint of a smile. He thought, this girl Alice — what's there to be shy about? It's really baffling. Does she worry I'll lose control if I see her belly?

Alice slowly lifted her clothes and carefully inspected. Indeed, on her lower abdomen, there was a layer of dragon scales grown right onto her skin.

The dragon scales covered an area that was neither too large nor too small, perfectly fitting her lower abdomen. They appeared in an icy crystalline blue-white, looking like gemstones.

But Alice's face immediately fell. She felt terrible. Those scales didn't match her formerly flat belly at all and looked extremely unsightly.

"AHHHHHHHHHHH!"

Merlin, hearing Alice's high-decibel scream, remained completely calm, since this reaction was entirely within his expectations.

Alice remembered what Merlin had said. If she forcibly activated the inheritance crystal's power, she might never be able to turn back into a human.

Thinking of this, Alice's face turned pale. She didn't want to become a monster covered head to toe in blue-white scales!

So Alice dropped her clothes, hurriedly turned around, tears welling up in her eyes, and pitifully asked Merlin, "What should I do? Can the scales on my belly really not be removed?"

"What do you think? Who told you to be disobedient and insist on using power you can't control?" Merlin spread his hands, putting on an aloof posture of detachment.

"This isn't entirely my fault either. I didn't even know what happened myself." Alice put on a bitter face, feeling very unlucky to have ended up like this for no reason.

"Hah."

Merlin shamelessly let out a laugh, placed his hand on top of his head making a dragon horn shape, and grinned.

"You're about to become a little dragon lady~. Don't you feel thrilled~?"
