title: Chapter 58 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 58 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 8 · Chapter 58

Alice glared at Merlin, this heartless man. Not only did he refuse to help her find a solution, he didn’t even offer a word of comfort—instead, he turned around and mocked her.

Happy about turning into a little dragon?!

Who the hell wants to become a little dragon?! I just want to be human!

Neither human nor dragon, forced to survive in the cracks between them?!

Alice was furious at Merlin, but more than that, she felt wronged. Before she knew it, she was overwhelmed with sadness.

What if her entire body ended up covered in dragon scales?!

How was she supposed to live in human lands then?! She’d definitely be treated like some freakish monster.

The more she thought about it, the more aggrieved she felt. Her eyes welled up with tears, glistening as they circled her sockets, and her little mouth puckered.

“Emmmm…” Merlin watched Alice’s pitiful expression and felt a pang of discomfort. Was he being a little too harsh?

Sure enough, Alice felt her fate was cursed. The tears, too heavy to bear, spilled over—*pat pat*—and she burst into sobs. “Waaah!”

A cold sweat rolled down Merlin’s forehead. *She’s crying already?* He thought. *Now she’s pretending to be some fragile damsel? I’m not buying it!*

“Wuuu…” Alice covered her eyes, her sobs breaking through as the tears refused to stop. She still found the energy to curse Merlin. “You heartless bastard… you actually mocked me… I—I hate you so much, AQ!”

“Huh?! It’s all my fault?” Merlin blinked, feeling wronged himself.

“It *is* your fault! It’s *all* your fault!” Alice wailed, her voice thick with tears. “Ever since the beginning, you’ve been nothing but trouble for me! We’re always getting scammed, drowning in debt, and now I can’t even stay human!”

Merlin awkwardly scratched his cheek, left speechless.

He hadn’t done it on purpose, but somehow, he always ended up dragging Alice into these messes.

Maybe it really was true—what goes around comes around. If you play the game, you pay the price.

Seeing Alice’s tears fall without end, Merlin’s heart softened slightly. Maybe bullying this silly girl all the time *was* going too far.

“Ahem! Stop crying. It’s not like you’re fully dragonified yet, right? There’s still a chance to fix this.”

“Eh?!” Alice stopped sobbing, lifting her head, her red-rimmed eyes questioning. “Really? There’s a way to make the dragon scales disappear?”

“There is.” Merlin stroked his chin, thinking seriously. “To control the power of the inheritance crystal, first, you need to reach Saint-tier. Based on my calculations, if you hurry and reach Saint-tier, you should be able to retract the scales at will.”

Alice stared at Merlin, wiping her tears. “You’re not lying to me, are you?”

“No, I’m not. Normally, only Saint-tier can use part of the inheritance crystal’s power. For someone at your level to force it… that’s just reckless.” Merlin sighed, looking at Alice with a sympathetic gaze.

---

Alice gradually regained her composure. So, reaching Saint-tier would let her remove the dragon scales on her stomach…

But when would *she* ever reach Saint-tier? It felt impossibly far away. She hadn’t even sensed the slightest hint of a breakthrough.

She pressed a hand to her abdomen, feeling how the dragon scales had made it hard as stone. The idea of forcibly tearing them off vanished from her mind.

“So I have to reach Saint-tier… but who knows when that’ll happen.”

“You’d better work harder. Otherwise, things might get worse.” Merlin said indifferently.

“What do you mean?” Alice asked, worry creeping into her voice.

“You should know—stronger power devours the weak. That’s a fundamental rule of this world. In other words, if you can’t suppress the dragon’s power, it’s very likely to consume and replace you. The truth is that cruel.” Merlin’s tone was deadly serious.

“You mean… I’ll be devoured by the dragon’s power?” Alice’s face went blank, a flicker of fear flashing in her eyes.

“Isn’t it already happening? Right now, it’s just your stomach. But it’ll slowly spread to the rest of your body. In the end, you’ll become a mindless, power-filled husk.” Merlin laid it out bluntly, without mercy.

“Ah…” Alice’s eyes widened in shock. The dragon scales on her stomach suddenly felt ice-cold, as if they no longer belonged to her, as if they’d already been stolen away.

“To be honest with you, I’ve been checking your body every day, lifting your clothes to see how far the dragon’s power has corrupted you. It looks stable now, but it’s spreading a little more each day. At this rate, the moment you stop being human is getting closer and closer.”

Merlin hadn’t wanted to tell Alice this, but if he didn’t, she might not realize she was facing a slow, creeping death.

After much deliberation, he decided the truth would do more good than harm. Besides, Alice had a right to know.

This time, Alice had truly brought it on herself. The dragonification might seem to recede temporarily, but beneath the surface, it was like a slow-acting poison, gradually consuming Alice as a person.

The problem was, Alice’s own strength was too weak—she couldn’t suppress the dragon’s power at all.

If this continued, she’d end up like Karona, completely abandoning her humanity.

Karona, as a Saint-tier powerhouse, could fully dragonify and still retain her consciousness. But Alice, at her current level, couldn’t. Her entire mind would vanish, leaving only the cold-blooded personality that had swung a sword at Cecilia—something approaching Marius.

Inheritance crystals were mysterious things. You couldn’t just consume them recklessly. For someone like Alice, who acted on impulse, they wouldn’t help—they’d kill her.

Now, Merlin was starting to regret it. If he’d known this would happen, he never would’ve let Alice consume the inheritance crystal.

He hadn’t considered her impulsive nature or emotional instability, which was how they’d ended up in this mess.

Moreover, ancient demonic texts had very little recorded about inheritance crystals. None of them mentioned such a terrifying devouring power.

If Merlin had known, he never would’ve allowed Alice, at her level, to take such a thing. She had poor control over power, making it all too easy for the inheritance crystal to turn her into a puppet.

“Alice, I’ve warned you many times, but you still opened the door to your own death. This world is fair—gaining immense power always comes with a price. Even if you realize the danger now, the dragon’s power will slowly drag you into the abyss. So, Alice, you need to move faster. Because the time you have left… isn’t much.”

After hearing this, Alice was thrown into a panicked daze. Her head spun, and she nearly fainted right in front of Merlin.

Even if she avoided activating the dragon’s power from now on… was it already too late?

This power would slowly corrupt her, eventually replacing her entirely?!

Oh god… wasn’t this an emergency?! If only her mindless body survived, that was no different from death!

Alice’s lips trembled. Her heart was a storm of terror, and her expression turned hollow, as if she’d just heard her own death sentence.

“Merlin… tell me the truth. How much time do I have left?”

Merlin hesitated, his expression grave. “Three months.”

“The time you have left… is three months.”

“If you don’t reach Saint-tier within three months… then, unfortunately, you won’t be *you* anymore.”

(——)

title: Chapter 59 — Royal Family
content:
Chapter 59 — Royal Family

Volume 8 · Chapter 59

Merlin finished his rough estimate of the time and fell silent, no longer speaking, giving Alice ample time to prepare herself mentally.

After hearing this, Alice felt as if her entire world had collapsed. She was plunged into a haze about her life, as if a thick fog had obscured the path ahead.

What?

Three... thirteen months?

I only have three months to reach Saint-tier?!

That’s far too short! Even if I try my hardest, it doesn’t seem like there’s enough time!

Has the dragon transformation already become unstoppable? In three months, my consciousness will be devoured by the power of the dragon race.

But as far as I know, there’s an insurmountable gulf between High-tier and Saint-tier. Countless people spend their entire lives stuck at this barrier.

It’s not just a matter of talent and strength—there’s also an element of luck. You need the perfect moment to ascend.

Saint-tier is the threshold to becoming a true powerhouse. It’s absolutely not something you can reach so easily. I’ve been stuck at High-tier for years, and to this day, I haven’t had the slightest sign of advancing to Saint-tier.

Alice knitted her delicate brows tightly, feeling a dull ache in her head. She unconsciously pressed her hands to her forehead, at a loss for what to do, a deep sense of helplessness welling up inside her.

Merlin watched Alice’s troubled expression and silently sighed. *Has this girl finally realized how serious things are?*

Alice suddenly thought of something and turned to Merlin, her face flushed as she asked, “Merlin, don’t you usually help me suppress it?”

“Before, the dragon race’s power hadn’t yet begun to corrupt your body. Now the situation is different—your body has already started to be eroded. Even I don’t have a good solution. The only thing I can think of is to race against time and try to reach Saint-tier as quickly as possible. Maybe that will still let you suppress the power of the inheritance crystal.” Merlin paused, then deliberately added, “At the end of the day, it’s because you’re too weak, Alice.”

Alice had no response. She silently clenched the blanket on her lap, her features twisted in silent distress.

Damn it… I don’t want to die yet. There’s still so much I haven’t done.

Is it really going to end this simply? Am I just going to be consumed?

It’s so unfair… At the very least, I should see *him* one more time.

The figure of Elgin, the Great Swordsman, flashed through Alice’s mind. She still couldn’t forget this mysterious man.

As the first man to ever make her heart race, of course she harbored girlish fantasies about him.

Merlin felt he should offer Alice some comfort. Otherwise, the crushing pressure might break her spirit.

“Don’t worry too much. You still have three months, right? I think there’s still a chance. I’ll do my best to help you. But during these three months, you absolutely must not use the dragon race’s power, or else there really won’t be any saving you.”

“I-I wasn’t worried at all!” Alice muttered in a low voice, her eyes red.

“Hm?” Merlin furrowed his brows, feeling that Alice’s reaction was far from normal.

“Before I see Elgin the Great Swordsman again, I absolutely refuse to disappear like this! There’s still so much I need to say to him!” Alice’s expression turned stubborn, clearly not yet broken.

Merlin’s expression turned unnatural, awkwardly thinking to himself, *I am Elgin the Great Swordsman… I never expected my identity to become Alice’s emotional pillar. Well, I suppose it’s a good thing for her.*

“Speaking of which…” Alice’s gaze turned wary as she stared at Merlin, her face flushing, “What did you do to me while I was unconscious these past few days?! Every day, you’d lift my clothes and… I’m a girl too, you know! At least consider my feelings! It’s so disrespectful!”

“Ah?!” Merlin’s brows knitted tightly, but internally, he felt nothing—he even wanted to laugh. “What’s the big deal about looking? I’ve already seen every part of you. Why are you making such a fuss?”

Alice’s face gradually turned as red as a ripe apple. “Th-That’s still not okay! Who would do something like that?! Taking advantage of a girl while she’s helpless, lifting her clothes… You pervert! It’s disgusting!”

“Tch!” Merlin showed a look of impatience, then seriously said, “Do you think I *wanted* to look? Every time I see that washboard of yours, I get the urge to kneel on it.”

“You—!” Alice, seeing Merlin’s contemptuous expression, instantly wanted to leap off the bed and smash his head in.

But as the two remained at an impasse, the door to the room was suddenly knocked three times.

*Thud. Thud. Thud.*

“Who is it?” Alice wondered aloud.

Merlin didn’t know either. He turned toward the door and said, “Come in.”

The door slowly opened, and Captain Dennis walked in, seemingly no longer as busy as before.

Merlin’s expression showed slight surprise. Over the past few days, Captain Dennis had come by at this exact time every day to check on Alice’s condition, showing unusual concern.

This left Merlin puzzled. How could a man of his age care so much about a stranger he didn’t even know? It didn’t make sense.

Captain Dennis saw that Alice had woken up and seemed to breathe a sigh of relief.

He removed his old captain’s hat and gave a slight bow. “Good evening, Mr. Merlin, Miss Alice.”

“Oh~, good evening, Captain Dennis. You’re here again,” Merlin replied with a faint smile.

Captain Dennis nodded at Merlin, then turned to Alice. “Miss Alice, you don’t seem to be seriously injured, I hope?”

“It should be fine, I think,” Alice answered vaguely, feeling no need to share the details of her condition with an outsider since it wasn’t a big deal.

“That’s good. You’re truly a lucky one,” Captain Dennis sighed.

“So, Captain Dennis, is there something you needed today? I’ve noticed you’ve been coming at this time every day. Are you looking for Alice for some reason?” Merlin studied Captain Dennis, genuinely curious.

Alice looked at Merlin, then at Captain Dennis, her face filled with surprise. *What’s going on?*

“That’s right. I do have some business with Miss Alice.” Captain Dennis nodded, then took out Alice’s jade pendant from his pocket.

“Ah!” Alice’s heart jolted when she saw the pendant. She quickly felt her neck—it was indeed gone. “That’s mine!”

“Yes. You dropped this during the battle. Since it seems important, it should be kept safe.” Captain Dennis returned the pendant to Alice.

Alice hastily examined it, then secretly let out a breath of relief. Thankfully, only the cord had broken—nothing else was damaged.

This was the only memento of her mother, a unique connection even though they had never met. She couldn’t afford to lose it.

Merlin had often seen Alice wearing the pendant and had assumed it was just for decoration. He hadn’t realized it was so important to her.

“Thank you, Captain Dennis, for bringing it back to me.” Alice clutched her pendant, expressing her gratitude.

“You’re welcome, Miss Alice.” Captain Dennis paused, then began to ask about what truly concerned him. “May I ask you a question?”

“Eh?!” Alice froze for a moment, then softly said, “Yes, of course.”

Merlin glanced at Captain Dennis, thinking, *So there really is something else.*

“Ahem!” Dennis cleared his throat, his hawk-like eyes gleaming as he asked seriously, “Are you a member of the Spanish Kingdom’s royal family?”

title: Chapter 60 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 60 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 8 · Chapter 60

Merlin couldn't help but furrow his brows, staring at Alice with a look of utter disbelief, as if she were some kind of alien.

Alice, a member of the Spanish royal family?! How was that even possible? With her personality, she didn’t look like a princess at all!

If someone said Alice was a wild mountain girl, *that* he could believe.

A princess? No way. What was Captain Dennis thinking to have such a misunderstanding?

Merlin almost laughed out loud. Captain Dennis must have a screw loose. Just look at her character—what kind of princess would act like that?

"Eh?!"

Alice's eyes widened in shock, her face filled with astonishment. Captain Dennis's question had caught her completely off guard.

She was a member of the Spanish royal family? How was that possible?!

She had been training with her teacher in the Great Snow Mountains since she was little. She had no connection to the Spanish Kingdom at all.

What could have made Captain Dennis come to such a huge misunderstanding? It was so strange.

Alice took a moment to calm herself before answering seriously.

"Then I'm not some Spanish royal. I'm just an ordinary person. I don’t know why you’d have that kind of misunderstanding."

"Not royal?" Captain Dennis froze, his expression turning serious. "But the pendant you’re wearing has the royal emblem of the Spanish monarchy."

"Ah?" Alice blinked, picking up the pendant and examining it. She pointed to the sun-and-bull design on the back. "You mean this?"

"That’s right. In the Spanish Kingdom, that design represents the royal family. I once served as a high-ranking naval commander there, so I’m very familiar with that emblem." Captain Dennis spoke earnestly, hoping for an answer.

Merlin had never been to the Spanish Kingdom either. He looked at Alice’s pendant, wondering how she had gotten her hands on such a thing.

Truthfully, Captain Dennis’s enthusiasm had a touch of selfishness. He was from the Spanish Kingdom—it was his homeland. But because of his arrogant and unyielding personality, he had been ostracized and left, unable to make a name for himself there.

If Alice really was a member of the Spanish royal family, it would be a turning point in his life.

Captain Dennis could beg the princess to plead his case to the king, seek forgiveness for his past offenses, and return home. He wouldn’t have to wander in Great Britain anymore.

But even Captain Dennis himself wasn’t sure if Alice was really a princess, so he could only ask indirectly.

"So this is the Spanish royal emblem?" Alice picked up the pendant, examining the back carefully. She gave an awkward smile. "I only just found out. I always thought it was just a normal pattern."

Captain Dennis’s heart sank. Things were looking bleak, but he still wasn’t ready to give up.

"What a shame, Captain Dennis. I’m not royalty. This pendant was a birthday gift from my teacher. It’s also the only thing my mother left me." Alice smiled, feeling that Captain Dennis’s misunderstanding was far too great.

"Then... what was your mother’s name?" Captain Dennis asked patiently, thinking that he had some knowledge of the royal consorts. Maybe if he knew Alice’s mother, he could confirm if Alice was the daughter of one of them.

"I’m not sure. Even my teacher doesn’t know. I was abandoned by my parents. My teacher said that when I was born, there was a famine in the villages below the mountain. Children being abandoned was common." Alice showed a hint of sadness, but her expression was detached. She didn’t blame her birth parents—after all, in the face of disaster, difficult choices had to be made.

Merlin looked at Alice, thinking that she usually seemed so carefree, but it turned out she was the tragic heroine of some backstory. He had really underestimated her.

Captain Dennis couldn’t help but feel a headache coming on. Refusing to give up, he pressed further. "Then what’s your teacher’s name?"

"Sophia Castro Clodia." Alice answered sincerely.

Captain Dennis’s brows shot up in shock. "That’s not the mysterious powerhouse from the Alps, the Frost Sword Saint?!" he exclaimed. "Miss Alice, you’re actually her—"

Alice’s expression turned unnatural. She casually badmouthed her teacher. "It’s not a big deal. My teacher is just an old spinster—"

Merlin raised an eyebrow. He thought Alice was being pretty harsh. Did she have a bad relationship with her teacher? If her teacher found out her student was calling her an old spinster, she’d probably faint in the bathroom.

"That ‘spinster’ part isn’t what matters," Captain Dennis responded awkwardly before continuing. "I’ve heard of this Frost Sword Saint. She’s lived in seclusion in the Great Snow Mountains for years. Her strength is unfathomable."

"My teacher *is* pretty strong." Alice nodded.

"Stronger than me?" Merlin interjected.

"Shut up. No one asked you." Alice’s face darkened. What nerve this Merlin had, acting like he had any right to speak?

After glaring at Merlin, Alice turned back to continue her conversation with Captain Dennis.

"I think you should understand now. I’m not some royal. I have no connection to the Spanish Kingdom. I’ve been training with my teacher since I was little. Even my name was given to me by her."

"But this emblem clearly—"

Captain Dennis felt a deep disappointment. His hope of returning home might be shattered.

Alice spoke up first, patiently explaining to Captain Dennis, "Maybe it was something that fell out of the palace? I’ve heard that sometimes the maids in the palace steal small things to sell for extra money. Maybe this pendant ended up in my birth mother’s hands."

Captain Dennis was left speechless. He had to admit that what Alice said was a common occurrence. In any kingdom’s palace, maids stealing small items was something that happened often—it was just that most people turned a blind eye.

Alice herself thought this was all a joke. How could she possibly be a member of the Spanish royal family? It was too absurd.

Moreover, her teacher in the Great Snow Mountains had always insisted she was abandoned by a village woman. She had never mentioned anything about the Spanish royal family.

Still, Alice was a little curious. She couldn’t help but ask Captain Dennis patiently, "Captain Dennis, why did you think I was a member of the Spanish royal family? It’s so strange."

"Actually, I wasn’t just making wild guesses. It would be unreasonable to assume you’re royalty based solely on a pendant. Even I wouldn’t believe that." Captain Dennis sighed.

Merlin took one look at Dennis’s expression and knew there was more to the story. Normally, who would think Alice was a princess? She didn’t have the slightest air of nobility or elegance.

"Actually, about twenty years ago, when I was still a high-ranking naval commander..." Captain Dennis lifted his head, his gaze deep as if he had returned to many years ago, and began to recount.

"A shocking event rocked the entire Spanish Kingdom. The whole royal family was stunned."

"During that time, the people were all terrified. The entire kingdom went into lockdown."

◆

PS
Whether Alice is a princess will be filled in later. There are also three side stories: Merlin’s past, Alice’s past, and the legendary birth of the great swordsman Elgin. I want to write these three, and they’re connected to a lot of things, but I still have my old series to work on. I basically don’t have much time, so I’m really worried. Let’s see how it goes.

title: Chapter 61 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 61 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 61

"Old King issued a curfew overnight, forbidding anyone from leaving the Kingdom of Spain. That turmoil lasted a full half year, stirring fear in everyone's hearts."

Captain Dennis' white eyebrows knitted tightly, as if reluctant to recall that period. It was indeed a major event in the Kingdom of Spain.

"What kind of event would restrict freedom? What on earth happened?" Alice asked curiously.

Merlin also found it unusual. Normally, no monarch would restrict freedom unless absolutely necessary—it would only provoke resistance.

"It was a certain night twenty years ago. Queen Josephine was assassinated, and the killer turned out to be a Sword Saint from within the royal court. He also abducted the little princess, who was only a few months old at the time. That princess was the king’s only daughter, the First Princess of the Empire, and the third in line to the throne. As the sole female in the royal family, her status was extremely special and important." Captain Dennis paused before continuing, "After it happened, the entire royal family was shocked. It was the first time a royal guard had ever assassinated a member of the royal family, which led to the turmoil that followed. The old king ordered a complete lockdown and spent half a year searching for the culprit and the First Princess, but unfortunately... there was no trace of them. They had no choice but to give up."

"So that's what happened."

Alice listened with a sigh, finding it all rather fascinating.

"Hmm..." Merlin showed little interest and asked, "What does this have to do with Alice?"

"If the First Princess were still alive, she’d probably be around Miss Alice’s age. There are just too many coincidences surrounding her, so..." Captain Dennis pressed his wrinkled lips together and said with a helpless tone, "That’s why I can’t help but think Miss Alice might be the First Princess who was abducted twenty years ago."

"That’s impossible! How could I be that princess? You must be mistaken. I’m as ordinary as they come!" Alice responded awkwardly. Saying she was a princess felt like a joke to her.

"Exactly. Alice is an ordinary person through and through. Where does she look like royalty? It’s absolutely impossible." Merlin stroked his chin thoughtfully. "Her only notable feature might be her... ironing board of a chest. Even more ordinary than most."

"Just because you don’t speak doesn’t mean people will mistake you for a mute." Alice forced a smile, her forehead veins throbbing as she trembled with rage at Merlin’s words.

Captain Dennis finally gave up. Maybe it was all his imagination. He was just too desperate to return to his homeland.

It seemed he was being unnecessary here. He should leave as soon as possible.

Captain Dennis slowly stood up and put on his tattered captain’s hat.

"Then I won’t disturb the two of you any longer. Farewell."

---

Night fell.

Merlin stepped out of the cabin and leaned over the side of the ship to get some air.

The bright moonlight shimmered like water, reflecting on the sea’s surface in a dazzling silver glow.

It was as if shattered silver plates were scattered across every corner of the world.

A gentle sea breeze carried a hint of warmth, rippling across both sides of the William.

Merlin didn’t say it aloud, but he was still worried about Alice’s situation. After all, the Saint-tier was the greatest hurdle—countless people had faltered here, spending their lives in regret.

How talented was Alice? Merlin gave an honest assessment: she was ordinary, with no remarkable traits or outstanding qualities.

Especially compared to a genius like Johnson, Alice seemed far too insignificant. There was simply no comparison.

If Alice had Johnson’s talent, Merlin wouldn’t worry at all. Three months would be more than enough for her to rise from High-tier to Saint-tier.

But the problem was that Alice was ordinary. For her, three months was like walking a tightrope—extremely dangerous.

To say that Merlin and Alice lived together without any emotional bond was impossible. After all, it was unnatural for someone you spoke to every day to suddenly disappear. Anyone would feel a sense of loss.

Even though Merlin was a demon, and had assimilated quite well over the past two hundred years, he had still crossed over from another world. Some traces of humanity were hard to erase.

Merlin felt his special training methods were becoming less effective. Alice had grown accustomed to them and no longer felt the same intense sense of crisis. The effect of awakening her potential was far weaker than the first time, and her progress was limited.

So Merlin believed that what Alice needed now was a breakthrough opportunity, not just him accompanying her in training.

*Gulp.*

The cabin door creaked open. Johnson, pale-faced and drenched in cold sweat, rushed to the ship’s side and vomited violently into the sea.

*Ugh!!!*

"Ugh..." Merlin frowned, watching Johnson with a hint of disgust.

This is awful... Johnson’s face twisted in pain. Seasickness was absolutely torturing him.

"Well, good evening, kiddo~" Merlin flashed a meaningful smile, his tone full of teasing.

"Hm?" Johnson turned his head curiously, only to freeze when he saw Merlin.

"What’s with that reaction? You look like you’ve seen a ghost." Merlin watched Johnson with a complex expression.

These past few days, Johnson had been avoiding Merlin the most. He hid every day, yet here he was, embarrassingly running into him even while vomiting.

Johnson’s first instinct was to flee. He didn’t want to talk to Merlin at all. The psychological barrier was too great.

He had boasted so much about his genius, only to be utterly humiliated by the enemy, pinned down and crushed. In the end, he had to be saved by Merlin.

If Merlin hadn’t intervened, Johnson would have died for sure—eaten by monsters, with no ability to resist.

It wasn’t just his pride that was hurt; his face burned with shame. Even now, he felt a stinging pain.

Truthfully, Johnson was a little grateful to Merlin. But that gratitude was overshadowed by humiliation and the fact that he, a genius, had been outmatched by a mere Black Iron adventurer.

His confidence had taken a brutal hit, and his personality had become much more reserved. The arrogance in his speech had vanished.

He stiffly turned around, intending to leave, but Merlin suddenly grabbed him by the neck and lifted him into the air.

"Where do you think you’re going? Since you’re out, let’s have a proper chat."

"Let go of me! You old man! Don’t touch me!" Johnson struggled, but his legs were too short to reach the ground.

"Hmph." Merlin let out a cold laugh, his mouth twisting into a smirk. "What’s this? I did save your life, you know. Is this how you treat your savior?"

Johnson was at a loss for words, his expression twisting in conflict. Finally, he gritted his teeth and said, "There! I said thanks! Are you satisfied now?!"

"How half-hearted. Not a bit of sincerity." Merlin wore a playful smile.

"What do you *want* from me?!" Johnson glared at Merlin, suspecting he was being mocked.

"Just keep me company for a bit. I have something I want to ask you." Merlin thought that perhaps he could ask Johnson about Alice’s path to Saint-tier.

After all, this kid was a genius. Merlin himself had never reached that level, nor had he experienced it, so he had no reference.

The two of them, one tall and one short, leaned over the ship’s edge, staring at the shimmering moonlight in silence.

Johnson, seeing that Merlin’s request was so simple, didn’t refuse. He had questions of his own for Merlin anyway.

From time to time, Johnson spat vomit into the sea. His stomach was empty, yet it still churned uncomfortably.

Once he had somewhat recovered, he glanced at Merlin under the moonlight.

Merlin rested his cheek on his hand, his ruby-like eyes gazing into the distance as if lost in thought.

The sea breeze gently lifted a few strands of his golden hair, and the bright moonlight seemed to rest like feathers on his shoulders.

Coupled with his face, which was as beautiful as a woman’s, he suddenly exuded a soft, delicate charm.

Johnson’s face flushed with two patches of red. He became flustered and quickly turned his head away.

*What the hell?!*

This can’t be right...!

He’s definitely a man, right?!

So why does he look even prettier than the big sisters at the guild?!

Am I sick? Do I need electroshock therapy?!

//w/Y

title: Chapter 62 — Epilogue
content:
Chapter 62 — Epilogue

Volume 8 · Chapter 62

Johnsson’s youthful face flushed red, and he quickly averted his gaze, not daring to glance at Merlin even once.

He didn’t think he had any *that* kind of tendencies, so why did he suddenly find this old man so impossibly handsome?!

Good heavens! What’s wrong with me?! I’ve always liked the big sisters at the Guild! It can’t be some old man!

Johnsson became completely flustered, twisting his head away in silence. Oddly enough, his seasickness seemed to ease a little.

In truth, Johnsson had simply imagined Merlin as the ideal version of himself—hardly some romantic infatuation.

The feeling could be summed up in two words: admiration.

Merlin shot a sidelong glance at Johnsson beside him, utterly baffled. What was wrong with this bratty kid?

"Hey, kid, what’s up with you?"

"N-nothing… nothing at all!" Johnsson stammered.

"Weirdo…" Merlin withdrew his gaze and returned to staring into the distance.

Johnsson gradually regained his composure, sneaking another peek at Merlin before lowering his head again.

"Old man, can I— ouch!"

Before he could finish, Merlin flicked his forehead, eliciting a sharp cry.

"Call me little brother. I don’t like ‘old man’—makes me feel ancient."

"Damn it…" Johnsson clutched his forehead, glaring at Merlin. "L-little… cough! Big Brother Merlin!"

"Hm?" Merlin lifted an eyelid. Not *little brother*, but *big brother* was close enough.

"I…" Johnsson bowed his head, hesitating. "Can I ask you something?"

"Go ahead." Merlin replied indifferently, secretly pleased. He’d been wondering how to ask about advancing to Saint-tier, and now the kid had handed him the perfect opening.

"You… why are you so strong?" Johnsson lifted his head, deadly serious.

"Hah…" Merlin laughed, amused. Everyone asked him this. "Born this way."

"Liar! That’s impossible!" Johnsson scoffed, agitated. "No one’s born with power like yours! Don’t think I’m some naive kid you can fool!"

"You just refuse to accept reality," Merlin said, spreading his hands in mock helplessness. "What would I gain by lying? It’s meaningless."

"Uh…" Johnsson blinked, realizing Merlin had a point. His shoulders slumped. "Right… Big Brother Merlin really *is* a true genius. If I hadn’t seen your absurd power with my own eyes, I’d never have believed it. Someone like me, who gets cocky over the tiniest achievement, doesn’t deserve to be called a magic prodigy. Compared to you, I’m still wet behind the ears…"

"Yep, you’re right. I *am* a genius." Merlin agreed without a hint of modesty, not bothering to deflect.

"Uh…" Johnsson hadn’t expected Merlin to admit it so bluntly, so shamelessly. His heart ached even more. "Then why are you content staying at Black Iron rank?! It doesn’t make any sense!"

"Because…"

"I get it—it’s about passion, right? Of course, someone like Big Brother Merlin, a freakish genius, would think differently." Johnsson hung his head, brows knitted, sinking into despair.

Merlin’s expression darkened. *Kid, can you let me finish?* Do you think I *want* to stay at this level? The Adventurers Guild has their damn rules! Otherwise, I’d be a Mythril-ranked adventurer in a heartbeat!

"Starting today, I’ll never call myself a genius again," Johnsson muttered, head still bowed, face twisted in distress, tears welling. "Father was right—there’s always someone better. I should never think too highly of myself."

Merlin sighed, then teased, "You’re already amazing. Saint-tier at your age, mastering so many spells, with full elemental affinity? Back when I was your age, I was still playing in the mud~"

"Eh?! Seriously?!"

Johnsson’s head snapped up, stunned. He’d been drilled by his father since childhood to reach this level. But Merlin had been goofing off and still surpassed him? What was the point of all his desperate training?

Unbeknownst to him, Merlin had just pulled off another effortless flex. And he wasn’t done—

"Seriously. I’ve never *tried* to get stronger. It all just… happened."

"Just like that… and you became this strong?" Johnsson stared blankly, utterly bewildered.

"Yep. Because a ‘genius’ is just a giant in the eyes of the mediocre. It’s all relative. To you, I’m a genius. But to some absolute ruler out there, I’m trash." Merlin paused, gazing at the starry sky. "So you’re too young to stress over this. It’s pointless…"

"Uh…" Johnsson fell silent, not quite grasping Merlin’s indifferent attitude. It was as if nothing mattered to him. "I’m nothing like you. I carry the weight of my family’s revival. My parents have poured so much into me—I *cannot* let them down. I *have* to restore the Johnsson name as the greatest magical lineage!"

"Are you sure that’s not just an excuse?" Merlin said offhandedly. "Maybe your parents just want you to be great, not to shoulder all that."

"That’s not it!" Johnsson snapped, reverting to "old man" in his anger. "Someone as cold as you wouldn’t understand our family’s sacred mission!"

"Then keep at it. You’ll never surpass me anyway." Merlin gave him a look of pity.

"Don’t get cocky!" Johnsson glared, clenching his fists, burning with resolve. "One day, I *will* crush you under my foot. Mark my words!"

With that, he stormed off without a backward glance. Merlin, recalling Alice’s situation, called after him, "Kid, wait up."

"Do you need something else, old man?" Johnsson’s tone was venomous, clearly fuming.

"I’ve got a question for you." Merlin wasn’t bothered, too lazy to argue with the brat.

"If you’re just gonna waste my time, forget it. I don’t want anything to do with you. Late-stage laziness is contagious." Johnsson’s words were sharp, his expression disgusted.

"Tch!" Merlin was annoyed. The kid was just as insufferable as before. "Do you know how a High-tier can reach Saint-tier in just three months?"

"Ah?!" Johnsson’s eyes widened. Merlin was *still* subtly flexing. Indignant, he retorted, "Are you joking, old man? Do you look down on Saint-tier so much? No one can reach Saint-tier in three months!"

"Eh?! Really?" Merlin scratched his head. He’d never done it himself, but it *seemed* simple enough.

"Of *course* not! Becoming Saint-tier isn’t that easy! You need strength, luck—everything has to align perfectly at the right moment!" Johnsson was dead serious. *How could Merlin not know this?* Was he *that* clueless?

"You’re a magic prodigy, right? Even *you* can’t do it in three months?" Merlin refused to give up. If it was truly impossible, then the "Washboard Hero" was doomed.

"Absolutely impossible! It took me *three years* to go from High-tier to Saint-tier!" Johnsson emphasized, then boasted, "In the entire empire, that’s already considered unheard of."

"Three months? That’s a pipe dream."

"As far as I know, the fastest anyone’s done it is a year and a half."

"That record belongs to a mage named Swinburne. His talent was far beyond mine."

"Though… he had a corrupt heart. Now he’s apparently in the Dark Adventurers Guild…"

◇

The next day, the *William* docked.

Everyone bid farewell to Captain Dennis. The compensation would be handled later by Cecilia, so there was no need to worry.

As for Johnsson, he grabbed his luggage and marched off without a word, like a lone wolf. Given his terrible sense of direction, he’d probably face countless trials just trying to get back to Ireland.

As for the naive Miss Connie, she had finally reunited with her father, and the family was whole again.

Cecilia, on the other hand, wasn’t in a hurry to return to Wales. Instead, she gathered many reporters from Kent, ready to publicize the Rose family’s achievements.

Among them, of course, was the shameless, unscrupulous, and utterly unethical reporter—a familiar face:

"Hello, viewers! I’m Bella from the *London Post*. I know some of you are groaning, *‘Not her again!’*"

"To be honest, I’m the *only* reporter in the entire British Empire. Don’t dwell on such boring details."

"Now, down to business. I’m currently in a fishing village along the Kent coast. Not long ago, the waters where the local fishermen worked were thrown into turmoil, leaving the people here destitute, struggling to survive, and facing all kinds of persecution."

"Fortunately, the crisis has been resolved, and the ones who stepped in to help were none other than the noble daughter of the Welsh Rose family. So let’s hear from Miss Cecilia Rose."

Bella, microphone in hand, followed by her cameraman, approached Cecilia, who was already poised and ready—dressed in a formal gown as if attending a ball, with light makeup and perfect posture.

Kyle, meanwhile, had polished his armor until it gleamed like a mirror, standing at attention like a soldier awaiting inspection.

"Greetings, noble Miss Cecilia."

"You flatter me." Cecilia nodded gracefully.

"May I ask why you traveled all this way from Wales to help these fishermen?" Bella extended the microphone.

"Because the spirit of the Rose family is to aid the weak. My ancestors were once pillars of the empire. Though they left us no fortune, they passed down a great legacy—a spirit that inspires every generation of Roses. From a young age, I was taught that when others are in need, we must never stand idly by." Cecilia sang the praises of her family, crafting a flawless image. Once she returned, her father the Duke would surely shower her with praise.

*Clap clap clap clap!* Kyle applauded loudly beside her, playing his part perfectly—one to sing, one to flatter. "As expected of Lady Cecilia! Truly the finest of the Rose family!"

"..." A cold sweat rolled down Bella’s forehead. She pressed on, "Did you face any danger during this mission?"

"Danger was inevitable. But under my father, Duke Rose’s guidance, I could never retreat like a coward! We fought back fiercely and drove the enemy away!" Cecilia declared with conviction, as if she’d endured a brutal battle herself.

"As expected of Lady Cecilia! Brave! Invincible! The most righteous of the Rose family!" Kyle’s hands *clap clap clap* echoed beside her.

Bella was getting fed up. This interview was going nowhere. She gave up on Cecilia and turned to Kyle instead.

"Sir Knight, after the battle, did you manage to capture any of the culprits?"

"Ahem!" Kyle cleared his throat, dead serious. "Regrettably, the enemy was cunning. We failed to capture the mastermind."

"No mastermind? I smell a conspiracy…" Bella’s expression turned suspicious.

"Eh?!" Kyle, still too green, fumbled under the reporter’s pressure. "Don’t just say things like that!"

"Tsk tsk tsk, the look in your eyes, Sir Knight… you’re hiding something~" Bella grinned wickedly, sensing a scoop.

"You—! Ahem!" Cecilia nearly forgot they were on camera and had to maintain her composure. "Miss Reporter, please don’t spout nonsense."

"Ladies and gentlemen, as you can see, there’s clearly more to this story…" Bella turned to the camera, spinning wild theories. "A major incident involving the fishermen, yet no mastermind was caught. One can’t help but suspect the Rose family is behind it all—staging this for fame, resorting to any means necessary. Is this a twist of human nature… or a collapse of morality?!"

"Shut up, you hack!"

Chaos erupted as the two sides lunged at each other.

◇

Inside a luxurious carriage, Merlin and Alice had chosen not to join the commotion, instead enjoying a moment of quiet.

The racket outside, however, still caught Merlin’s attention.

"These people are ridiculous. Can’t they just be quiet for once?"

He muttered to himself, then glanced down. Alice was right beside him.

Perhaps from sheer exhaustion, she had fallen asleep, instinctively using Merlin as a pillow, her head resting on his shoulder.

She slept soundly, her breathing steady, even letting out little "huu huu" sounds. Her tiny nose twitched now and then—probably dreaming of something delicious.

Merlin had initially thought to push her away—his shoulder was starting to ache, and it wasn’t comfortable.

But then he remembered what Alice was about to face, and his heart softened. He abandoned the idea.

His gaze drifted to the window, where pink petals danced in the wind like the tail of a white steed—

*Today’s an exception.*

*I’ll let her use my shoulder for a while…*

title: Chapter 63 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 63 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 8 · Chapter 63

An unknown amount of time had passed.

In a certain cave within the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

Democritus, who had barely escaped with his life, was here.

A considerable amount of time had passed since his base was destroyed.

Democritus had fled from the Dofor Strait all the way to the Austro-Hungarian Empire, hiding in this mountain cave.

He had not given up. He hoped to obtain power rivaling that of a Demon Lord, and then pursue the woman of his dreams.

Democritus’s demands were not high—he only needed to create an alchemical creation on par with an ultimate weapon to succeed.

He had received word that Asmodeus was holding a concert at the Fourth Demon Lord Palace. This was a perfect opportunity to meet a demon.

So Democritus came up with a bold plan: he would bring his brand-new creation and, in front of countless demons, propose to Asmodeus!

Democritus himself thought this was very romantic. Once Asmodeus witnessed his talent, she would surely be moved.

As the time drew near, a loud laugh suddenly echoed through the cave.

“Success! I’ve finally done it!”

“Who would’ve thought using a Storm Dragon as alchemical material would work so well!”

“After modifying the dragon’s blood, it can enhance any living being… I really did it!”

“Now even a Demon Lord won’t be my match!”

The voice came from deep within the cave, the man seemingly in a state of extreme excitement.

In front of Democritus stood a monstrous, crimson creature, its body radiating scorching sparks that slowly rose into the air.

The monster’s massive, pitch-black eyes, like two great lanterns, locked onto Democritus, its thunderous breathing filling the space.

Its eyes were so dark that no one could tell what kind of creature it was.

Due to the excessive brightness, Democritus’s alchemy skills had improved even further, and he had created a monster even stronger than the Dragon-Man Karona!

Democritus couldn’t help but indulge in wild fantasies, muttering to himself:

“Asmodeus, I will definitely give you a huge surprise at the Fourth Demon Lord Palace.”

“Miss Asmodeus, wait for me.”

---

The Fourth Demon Lord Palace.

Located on the beautiful island of Sicily in the south.

At the heart of the Holy Roman Empire.

It was perfectly situated in the Mediterranean, and the southern region was one of the places most frequently invaded by the Holy Church.

The fact that the Fourth Demon Lord Palace still stood tall despite the Holy Church’s repeated crusades was proof of the strength of the successive Demon Lords of Lust—none of them were foes the Church could easily swallow.

A demon walked toward the main hall at the center, where a grand performance was about to take place.

At this moment, all the demons of the Fourth Demon Lord Palace, whether they were materialized or in spirit form, were gathered here. Asmodeus, the Great Demon Lord of the Fourth Palace, was their supreme ruler.

The host was none other than the Great Demon Lord herself. No matter what, they had to show their support for their lord.

In truth, Asmodeus had secretly issued an order: any demon who failed to attend would be strung up and whipped a thousand times. This threat alone was enough to ensure a full house.

In reality, many demons had brought their families along, and the crowd had swelled to an enormous size.

The road was packed with demons, a sea of black, most of them fallen angels with dark wings.

There were only two types of fallen angels: those with membranous wings and those with feathered wings.

Though their numbers were few, occasionally, one could spot a demon whose soul had been harvested and turned into a fanatical devotee of Asmodeus.

Most of these demons had come to show their support for their lord’s… peculiar hobby.

Asmodeus’s cross-dressing was like a drug—an addiction that had spread throughout the entire demon race.

Her beauty when dressed as a woman was simply too breathtaking, her charm irresistible. It was a phenomenon that had taken over the demon world.

In her own territory, the situation was even more severe. Many couldn’t go a day without seeing Asmodeus in a dress, their eyes constantly flickering with anticipation.

In front of the main hall, a stage had already been set up, grand in scale, adorned with all kinds of colorful lights.

Democritus, of course, had also successfully blended into the crowd, preparing to propose during the performance.

He had coated his entire body in alchemical concoctions to mask his human scent, ensuring he wouldn’t be detected. As long as he didn’t speak, he would remain safe. But the moment he did, his human voice would give him away.

Democritus knew that the demons around him were brutal creatures. To them, humans were nothing more than food—objects without emotions or feelings.

But Democritus believed love transcended race. He had fallen for Asmodeus, and marrying her was his greatest dream.

At this moment, all the demons had gathered, whispering among themselves, still unaware of what kind of performance was about to take place.

“Everyone~”

A thunderous heavy metal song suddenly blared, and spotlights converged at the center of the stage.

Asmodeus, riding an ascending platform, rose into the air above the stage, waving and blowing kisses to the demons below.

Democritus, hidden among the crowd, could barely contain his excitement. Asmodeus’s voice had reached a level where it was indistinguishable from a real woman’s!

Asmodeus had prepared extensively for today’s event, so her entrance was nothing short of spectacular—dazzling beyond compare!

At this moment, Democritus’s eyes were fixed solely on Asmodeus. He truly believed she was the most beautiful woman in the world.

“Heavens! Miss Asmodeus! Incredible!”

Even the scorching sun paled in comparison to her beauty!

“I must propose! This demoness must become mine!”

Democritus was so overwhelmed with emotion that, after such a long time without seeing her, tears welled up in his eyes.

“My lord is the most beautiful in the world!”

“Damn, I’m so turned on!”

With Asmodeus’s grand entrance, the entire crowd erupted. Cheers and applause rolled like waves, punctuated by whistles.

“Sorry to keep you waiting! Next, I’ll start with a hot dance for you all!”

With that, she shed her outer garment, revealing an ultra-short skirt and a highly revealing top underneath.

Good heavens… Many male demons in the audience immediately started bleeding from their noses.

And then there were the black silk stockings and high heels—so seductive!

This was practically a pole dance from the human world!

There was even a pole set up at the center of the stage. Clearly, Asmodeus had been fed some strange knowledge.

No need to guess—it was definitely that meddling Merlin’s doing!

“Holy shit! Holy shit! Holy shit! I’m about to explode!”

Blood spurted from Democritus’s nose like a fountain, and he couldn’t stop sniffing.

Democritus’s mind was consumed with one question: what was Asmodeus wearing under that ultra-short skirt?

He was standing near the front, and his height gave him a perfect view. But when Asmodeus lifted her leg during the dance, Democritus froze, his face turning deathly pale.

“What the—? What *is* that thing between her legs?!”

It couldn’t be some kind of decoration, could it?

Could it be true what that black-armored adventurer had said—

“There’s a human scent!”

“I smell it too!”

“It’s a human! That guy’s a human!”

The surrounding demons began to murmur, their bloodthirsty eyes locking onto Democritus.

Even Asmodeus on stage noticed, her gaze settling on the mysterious figure in the black robe. “Hmm?”

Democritus broke out in a cold sweat, his face ashen. He realized he had backed himself into a corner.

But fortunately, Democritus still had an ace up his sleeve, so he wasn’t completely panicked—

In a fluster, he pulled out a horn from his robes and blew it with all his might.

“Buuuuuum—”

The deep, resonant sound of the horn echoed through the air, as if calling forth something ancient.

Suddenly, a massive, crimson-scaled dragon, wreathed in sparks, descended from the sky with a thunderous roar!

It landed steadily behind Democritus, letting out a furious bellow. Its golden pupils glared at the surrounding demons, its entire body radiating scorching heat. Its power was extraordinary!

“ROOOOOOAR!”

This was Democritus’s new ultimate weapon—a refined gold dragon, his mount, created by combining high-purity holy dragon blood.

Its strength far surpassed that of the Dragon-Man Karona, especially in defense and regeneration, which were even more remarkable!

Democritus threw off his black robe, revealing himself to the demons, and roared:

“All of you, back off! Whoever dares to provoke me dies!”

The demons weren’t afraid of Democritus himself, but the alchemical beast behind him exuded such a chaotic and overwhelming presence that none of them dared to act recklessly.

This was demon territory. A single rat had infiltrated their ranks, and the demons were furious, itching to tear the intruder apart. But this was also—

“Oh? I thought it was someone important. Turns out it’s just that foolish human who came to propose to me years ago.” Asmodeus twirled a strand of her pink hair between her fingers. “What’s the matter? Still not over it? Did you come all this way just to propose to me again?”

“You… you cross-dressing freak! I curse you!” Democritus was seething, his emotions completely out of control. He felt he had been deceived.

“Beauty is not bound by gender. All living beings yearn for beauty and seek beautiful things—it comes from the depths of the soul.” Asmodeus smiled faintly. “But calling me disgusting… that’s a bit much, don’t you think?”

The crowd erupted in cheers, their instincts as demons overwhelming their better judgment.

Democritus’s face twisted in rage. He felt that all his efforts up to this point had been for nothing—completely wasted.

“If I had known you were a man, I would’ve never proposed to you, even if you killed me!” Democritus roared, his emotions far from calm.

“Then whose fault is it that you had such a misunderstanding?” Asmodeus looked down at him, her red eyes flashing. “I never said I was a woman.”

Democritus’s breath caught in his throat, his old face flushing red.

Asmodeus was right—it was all because of his own lustful, filthy desires.

Democritus was no longer thinking clearly. Anyone else in his position would have gone mad on the spot, losing all sense of reason.

He felt that all his hard work had been for nothing, utterly ruined.

In his shame and fury, Democritus wanted to erase this black mark from his history.

“Bastard! You’ve deceived me for so long! I’ll kill you, you cross-dressing freak!”

Asmodeus’s eyes turned icy, her voice cold. “Pathetic human.”

Democritus glared at Asmodeus, his voice dripping with venom. “Don’t think I’m afraid of you just because you’re a Demon Lord! Now, I’m your equal!”

Asmodeus’s eyes filled with killing intent. “My refined gold dragon is the perfect alchemical beast. It’s more than worthy of a Demon Lord, don’t you think? Watch me kill you with my own hands, you cross-dressing freak! Attack! Take him down!”

At its master’s command, the refined gold dragon, its body ablaze, soared into the air. The heat waves rolled off it in waves, sending all the demons into a panic. This alchemical beast’s power was terrifying—far beyond what they had expected.

Asmodeus let out a light chuckle, watching the ferocious dragon. “Your toy seems a bit… outdated.”

The refined gold dragon roared, its scales glowing as they were reinforced. Every flap of its steel-like wings sent shockwaves through the air.

This extraordinary alchemical dragon charged straight at Asmodeus, its massive, hardened body like a giant iron hammer!

Yet, incredibly, Asmodeus stopped the devastating strike with a single finger.

No, they hadn’t seen wrong. That violent impact had truly been halted by the slender finger of the Demon Lord of Lust!

The stage where Asmodeus stood had already shattered and collapsed from the force, reduced to countless fragments.

“Hmph. Is this the best you’ve got?” Asmodeus sneered. “Alchemy is fine for amusement, but to think you’d bring it into battle… that’s just a question of intelligence.”

Asmodeus’s face was filled with disdain. She didn’t even consider Democritus, this foolish human, worth her attention.

The refined gold dragon struggled, but in Asmodeus’s grip, it was like a toy, unable to move even against the strength of a single finger.

“Wretched thing, sinking into desire and depravity…” Asmodeus’s voice was cold.

The moment her words fell, a pink storm erupted, carrying with it a kind of illusion that warped space itself.

This was Asmodeus’s phantasm attack—it trapped one’s soul forever in a world of fantasy and delusion.

No matter how strong the enemy’s body was, if their soul was ensnared, they were nothing before Asmodeus!

The refined gold dragon’s golden pupils dimmed, the flames on its body rapidly extinguishing. It crashed to the ground with a thud and didn’t move again—clearly, it was dead.

“What?! How is this possible?!”

Democritus’s eyes widened in shock, and he dropped to his knees with a thud.

It had been killed in a single strike?!

Not even its self-healing ability had worked—it had just died.

But it was supposed to be stronger than the first ultimate weapon! How had it ended up like this?!

Democritus’s lips trembled. In an instant, he was consumed by terror. He clutched his hair and howled, his mind spiraling into madness.

This was the power of the Demon Lords? How could such godlike beings exist in this world?!

This defied all logic!

“Humans are just snacks. Eat him.”

Asmodeus didn’t even glance at the man on the ground, her voice light as she spoke to her subjects.

The countless demons, their eyes filled with malice, let out a cheer.

The maddened Democritus could only watch in horror as countless demons lunged at him, their massive jaws snapping and tearing into his flesh.

Blood spurted, and his eyes, wide with terror, stared up at the dark, overcast sky.

“Retribution…?”

*To Be Continued*

title: Chapter 1 — Interrogation
content:
Chapter 1 — Interrogation

Volume 9 · Chapter 1

The capital of the Great Britain Empire.

It was already deep into the night, yet the royal palace was brightly lit.

The magnificent hall was supported by twelve thick pillars. Over twenty massive crystal chandeliers illuminated the space, making it as bright as day.

A long red carpet stretched all the way to the high platform, where a woman who appeared to be in her late twenties sat on the solemn throne.

Her features were cold, yet carried an aloof beauty that defied her age. Cascading golden hair rested on her exposed shoulders, and her luxurious long dress dragged on the floor, its hem held up by two maidservants standing respectfully beside her.

In her left hand, she held a golden scepter, and in her right, a dazzling orb known as the "King's Apple," symbolizing supreme authority. A radiant, eye-catching crown sat atop her head—such unmistakable traits marked her as the empire's supreme ruler, the Queen Elizabeth so often spoken of by the people.

Beneath the throne stood only three individuals, all members of the Purple Thorn Knights.

One was Chapman, a squad leader, another was Franklin, the Knight Commander. The last was naturally the strongest knight of the Thorn Knights, the renowned Mesfield.

All three had been summoned to the palace by Queen Elizabeth late at night, seemingly for an urgent matter.

Franklin stood respectfully to the side, head bowed, awaiting the queen’s orders at any moment.

Meanwhile, Mesfield and Chapman knelt on one knee, not daring to lift their heads, completely unaware of the current situation.

Mesfield had just returned after escorting Sydney back to the Southern United Kingdom, only to be called here by Her Majesty.

"Chapman, I have a question for you. Can you swear not to lie?" Queen Elizabeth’s voice was magnetic, carrying a hint of vicissitude despite her youth, brimming with the imposing presence of a ruler.

"Your Majesty, please ask. I swear on my life I will never deceive you with lies." Chapman struck his chest over his heart to express his loyalty.

"Very well. I can sense your burning loyalty. Then..." Queen Elizabeth paused, lifting her head to stare down at Chapman. "Not long ago, you personally stated that the Great Swordsman Elgin slew countless Saint-tier warriors in a single strike. Is this true?"

"Absolutely. I was there at the time. Though I didn’t see it with my own eyes, no one else could have accomplished such an unimaginable feat." Chapman’s expression was deadly serious, his candid demeanor leaving little room for doubt.

"Is that so? What does this Great Swordsman Elgin look like? I heard you communicated with him directly." Queen Elizabeth pressed further.

"This..." Chapman hesitated for a moment before continuing. "At the time, the man wore a mask. I didn’t see his true face, but judging by his voice, he didn’t seem old at all—quite the opposite, he sounded young."

"To possess such unbelievable strength and yet be young? That is clearly abnormal." Elizabeth narrowed her eyes, her tone light but sharp. "Perhaps this mysterious swordsman is not human, but a long-lived member of another race..."

No one below the throne spoke. The reasoning made sense—humans who wielded such immense power were usually aged monsters.

If this Great Swordsman Elgin was young, then there was only one explanation: he was not of the human race.

"Then, what do you think of this man’s character?" Elizabeth asked again.

"..." Chapman faltered, then answered with some reservation. "It’s difficult for me to judge whether he is good or bad, but personally, I don’t believe he is an enemy of our empire. He seems to act purely out of interest. Perhaps we could extend an olive branch and make him a new force for the empire."

"Oh? Not long ago, Morrison petitioned me with a similar suggestion, urging me to accept the Great Swordsman Elgin. Did you two coordinate this?" Queen Elizabeth said, her expression ambiguous, neither smiling nor frowning.

"Eh?!" Chapman’s eyes widened. He hadn’t expected that, aside from himself, someone else—especially the Seventh Thorn Knight—would speak on behalf of a wanted criminal.

"So, you all want me to pardon this fugitive who destroyed royal property, and you’ve even joined forces to pressure me? Do you no longer respect me, your queen?" Queen Elizabeth’s voice carried a hint of menace, clearly displeased, even angered by the suggestion.

"I dare not!" Chapman abruptly lowered his head, cold sweat dripping from his nose. He had never intended to provoke Her Majesty’s wrath.

Chapman’s status was nothing like Morrison’s. As a noble Thorn Knight, Morrison could advise the queen without serious consequences. But Chapman was merely a squad leader—if the queen took offense, she could easily have him executed. The difference in treatment was vast.

Queen Elizabeth’s mood had soured. A man as powerful as the Great Swordsman Elgin running amok in her territory was an extremely destabilizing factor.

Because Queen Elizabeth could not control this mysterious figure, any ruler would instinctively fear an uncontrollable power. As the queen of all Great Britain, she naturally shared this sentiment. The Great Swordsman Elgin filled her with dread, keeping her awake at night, fearing her rule might be overthrown.

Initially, Elizabeth had taken a laissez-faire approach, issuing a wanted order in hopes that the man would leave the empire of his own accord.

But who could have predicted that the uproar would only grow worse, forcing her to address the issue head-on? She had no choice but to confront this mysterious man.

Not long ago, this enigmatic powerhouse had even come to the imperial capital! He had humiliated the Thorn Knights before vanishing without a trace.

Elizabeth was furious. The entire Purple Thorn Knights represented royal authority, and the Great Swordsman Elgin’s actions were a clear display of contempt for her rule.

Worse still, people around her had recently begun speaking in favor of the Great Swordsman Elgin. This was an ominous sign.

Thus, the man himself—Merlin—had become a thorn in Queen Elizabeth’s side. If she did not eliminate him quickly, he would pose a threat to her position.

"The Great Swordsman Elgin is undoubtedly a heathen of the worst kind. He destroyed royal property and humiliated my knights—this is a blatant provocation against the entire empire!" Queen Elizabeth’s voice was severe, her tone icy. "And yet, you want me to accept a wanted criminal? Do you wish to bring shame upon my crown? Does some filthy fugitive deserve a place at the empire’s core? Do not jest with me again."

"Yes, Your Majesty." Chapman replied, trembling, not daring to lift his head, his body drenched in cold sweat.

Queen Elizabeth took a moment to compose herself, then looked down at the First Thorn Knight, who had remained silent all this time. "Mesfield... my most loyal subject..."

Mesfield’s kneeling form shuddered, an inexplicable tension gripping her. Cold sweat beaded on her forehead.

She could tell Queen Elizabeth was in a foul mood, and there was a sense of settling scores. That was why she had stayed silent.

She feared being questioned about the incident when the Great Swordsman Elgin had appeared in the capital. During that event, she had contributed nothing, only suffering a humiliating defeat.

In the end, she had even let the fugitive Elgin escape, treating the capital as if it were his own home—coming and going as he pleased!

Mesfield slowly lifted her head, her expression resolute. "I am here, Your Majesty."

"You’ve heard everything just now. So, I must ask..." Queen Elizabeth paused, her tone grave. "With your abilities, could you kill multiple Saint-tier warriors in an instant?"

title: Chapter 2 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 2 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 9 · Chapter 2

Facing Queen Elizabeth’s questioning, Mesfield’s entire body tensed up, and beads of sweat as large as beans slid down her cheeks.

She knew what Her Majesty was asking—could she, like Grand Swordsman Elgin, slaughter countless Saint-tier powerhouses?

Mesfield searched her heart and knew she couldn’t possibly do such a thing. It was as absurd as a fairy tale, utterly unbelievable.

The only beings capable of instantly killing countless Saint-tier warriors would have to be gods from the dawn of the world’s creation. Mesfield couldn’t think of any other creature, human or otherwise, who could achieve that.

So, regarding the miraculous claims Chapman had made, Mesfield still harbored doubts. It simply wasn’t something a human could do—even for other races, it was likely impossible!

Yet many who had witnessed Grand Swordsman Elgin in action had been awed by his overwhelming power. Even Thorn’s Seventh Knight, Morrison, had abandoned all thoughts of opposition and was determined to recruit this fugitive to their side.

This left Mesfield puzzled—what kind of magic did Grand Swordsman Elgin possess? How could he make one person after another submit and worship him? Was his power truly invincible?

Mesfield recalled her own confrontation with Grand Swordsman Elgin. Apart from finding his mouth sharp, she hadn’t seen any earth-shattering strength. Moreover, she hadn’t even fought him seriously yet—who was stronger remained uncertain!

But now, suddenly questioned by Her Majesty, Mesfield felt a surge of insecurity and didn’t know how to respond.

If she said she couldn’t do it, that would mean she was clearly inferior to Grand Swordsman Elgin, which might disappoint the queen.

But if she claimed she could, that would be lying, which went against her upright and honest nature.

After much deliberation, Mesfield decided on a compromise, hoping to muddle through.

“Your Majesty, I can take on ten of them!”

“Oh? Ten? That’s quite a number. Truly worthy of my proudest knight. That’s already very impressive,” Queen Elizabeth paused before emphasizing, “But I asked if you could, like Grand Swordsman Elgin, instantly kill countless Saint-tier warriors—not just a mere ten.”

“...” Mesfield’s expression froze. Defiantly, she lifted her head and said, “Your Majesty, the claim of instantly killing countless Saint-tier warriors is still full of doubts. Perhaps—”

“Enough, Mesfield. I only want a direct answer.” Elizabeth cut off Mesfield’s words, uninterested in any explanations.

Mesfield reluctantly gritted her teeth and replied, “...I cannot.”

Queen Elizabeth sighed, waves of disappointment washing over her. “That’s enough.”

It wasn’t that Elizabeth’s expectations of Mesfield were too high, but as the Thorn’s First Knight, acclaimed as the empire’s strongest knight, she couldn’t even measure up to a fugitive. If this got out, the citizens would likely laugh themselves silly—it might even cause significant unrest.

Mesfield clenched her fists and suddenly lifted her head. “Your Majesty, please trust me. Give me one more chance. I will personally present Grand Swordsman Elgin’s head to you!”

“Sounds interesting,” Queen Elizabeth said meaningfully, “But I’ve heard that even with all three Thorn Knights working together, you still couldn’t capture him. That makes me doubt your strength.”

“...” Mesfield opened her mouth but then closed it, her face flushing red at the memory. She hadn’t been in any state to fight properly back then. Under normal circumstances, how could Grand Swordsman Elgin have escaped so easily? “Your Majesty, I wasn’t at my best that day. If I face him again, I’m confident I can defeat him!”

“Is that so?” Queen Elizabeth nodded faintly. “I don’t want to put too much pressure on you, Mesfield. After all, you are my most beloved knight.”

“It’s not pressure, Your Majesty—it’s trust! Even the sharpest sword is no different from scrap iron if it’s never used!” Mesfield knelt on the ground, her voice ringing with conviction.

“I believe in your strength. If a good opportunity arises, I will make use of you.” Queen Elizabeth’s voice was melodious.

“Thank you, Your Majesty.” Mesfield bowed deeply, silently vowing to make Grand Swordsman Elgin pay the price. Otherwise, she would have no face to continue as the Thorn’s First Knight.

“You two may withdraw for now. There’s nothing more for you here.”

Queen Elizabeth dismissed Chapman and Mesfield with a wave of her hand, as if she had nothing left to say.

“Mesfield, you’ve worked hard escorting the Elven Princess back to her homeland. Go and rest for a while.”

“Thank you for your concern, Your Majesty.” Mesfield bowed in gratitude.

“When you had your audience with the Elven King, did he say anything?” Queen Elizabeth asked.

“The Elven King said he was grateful for Your Majesty’s assistance and that if you ever needed help in the future, he would not refuse.” Mesfield answered respectfully.

“Hmph. A worthless favor.” Queen Elizabeth coldly scoffed before saying, “You may go.”

Mesfield and Chapman withdrew, leaving only Queen Elizabeth and the Knight Commander, Franklin, in the great hall.

“Franklin...” Queen Elizabeth called out.

Franklin quickly knelt on one knee, his manner the picture of reverence. “What are your orders, Your Majesty?”

“Don’t be fooled by my words about Mesfield being my most trusted knight. Franklin, you are my true confidant. There are matters that aren’t suitable for Mesfield to know, but you are a different story.” Queen Elizabeth spoke cunningly, likely having used the same line on many others to inspire devotion.

Sure enough, Franklin’s heart swelled with joy upon hearing this. “Thank you for your high regard, Your Majesty! My loyalty will withstand any test!”

“I know.” Queen Elizabeth nodded before continuing, “You saw it yourself—I’m at my wit’s end with this Grand Swordsman Elgin business. What do you think we should do?”

“Your Majesty, is there even a need to ask? Any unstable factor beyond your control must be eradicated without mercy. Especially someone as powerful as Grand Swordsman Elgin—if he remains in your territory for long, he will inevitably become a menace, threatening your great rule.” Franklin spoke with absolute seriousness, clearly a radical.

“Hahaha...” Elizabeth let out a silvery laugh, clapping her hands. “Worthy of being my confidant. Your thoughts align perfectly with mine, unlike some knights. You truly understand me.”

“Your Majesty flatters me.” Franklin twirled his small mustache, practically floating with pride.

“That’s right. Grand Swordsman Elgin is already starting to threaten my rule. Even among the Thorn Knights, there are those who worship him. So, the number of his worshippers among the empire’s citizens must be beyond count. We must crush him in the cradle before he becomes a force that could overthrow the empire!” Queen Elizabeth’s voice turned sinister, her entire demeanor shifting to that of a tyrant.

“Your Majesty, do you have a plan?” Franklin asked cautiously.

Queen Elizabeth gave a subtle signal to a nearby maid, who understood and presented a box to Franklin.

Franklin’s heart pounded with uncertainty as he slowly opened the black box. Inside was an ancient, brown leather-bound book, its pages filled with the script of the former kingdom.

“This is—?”

“This is the legal code of the former kingdom. It records many evil spells, as well as some secrets of the underworld. It’s spoils of war we seized from Coppelia.” Queen Elizabeth said expressionlessly.

Franklin’s entire body trembled as he stared wide-eyed at the tattered ancient tome before him. This treasure was invaluable—just the ancient magic alone would drive external mages wild!

And now, this priceless relic of the former kingdom lay quietly before him? It felt like a dream.

“Franklin, next I will entrust you with a highly confidential mission...” Queen Elizabeth narrowed her eyes and lowered her voice. “We will deceive the entire empire and create the strongest hero in the history of Great Britain...”

title: Chapter 3 — Undercurrents
content:
Chapter 3 — Undercurrents

Volume 9 · Chapter 3

Sir Franklin the Knight was stunned, having not understood what Queen Elizabeth meant, and felt very confused.

"The... the strongest Hero?"

"Exactly. To create the strongest hero in history, representing our supreme royal authority, thereby consolidating my rule," Queen Elizabeth's gaze deepened, as if a scheme was brewing in her mind.

"...Franklin, I sense Her Majesty is playing a grand chess game, and the strongest hero can be created at will? Most heroes need a societal environment and the times. So, Your Majesty, what do you intend to do? Do you need my help?"

"Indeed, I need you to carry out this secret task. Conceal your identity and do not tell anyone, including your most trusted relatives..." Queen Elizabeth looked down, her tone serious, and asked, "Franklin, can you fulfill this?"

Franklin's face hardened, and he suddenly hammered his fist against his own chest, "Please, Your Majesty, rest assured. I swear I will guard this secret with my life and will never let anyone know!"

"Very well, Franklin, you are truly the person I trust most," Queen Elizabeth nodded approvingly and continued, "I have heard that the Ho‑Ghost Praise within the Dark Adventurers' Guild has been seeking a way to bring the dead back to life, hasn't it?"

"Huh?" Franklin looked startled, not understanding why the queen suddenly brought it up. "Yes, that evil faction has been stirring in the shadows. The Ho‑Ghost Praise's activities have become especially frequent; in recent years they have been searching for a method to resurrect the dead, hoping to revive the former guildmaster who fell thirty years ago while subduing the North Sea Giant—Palmer, the Flaming Ho‑Ghost."

"Then let us begin the mission," Queen Elizabeth stared into Franklin's eyes and said seriously, "I don't care what method you use; you must contact the members of the Ho‑Ghost Praise in the Dark Adventurers' Guild and give them the former kingdom's codex."

The air in the great hall fell still, not a single sound could be heard, and even a pin could be heard dropping.

Franklin's eyes widened, his mouth temporarily unable to close, unable to comprehend what Queen Elizabeth had said.

It should be known that the Dark Adventurers' Guild is an extremely dangerous presence to any nation, like lawless terrorists.

They have no restrictions; they do whatever they please, and as long as there is sufficient profit, they commit virtually every evil.

Many countries list them as targets for extermination and absolutely forbid their existence.

However, they have no fixed base, accustomed to roaming for missions, which has caused several extermination attempts to fail repeatedly.

Among them, the Ho‑Ghost Praise is especially unique; even though its guildmaster is dead, it remains renowned.

That is thanks to the exceptional talent of the guildmaster's son, Swenburn.

Swenburn, who became acting guildmaster, did not let the guild collapse; on the contrary, its momentum grew even stronger.

Nevertheless, Swenburn has not given up the ambition to resurrect his father and lead the Ho‑Ghost Praise back to its pinnacle.

Such an extremely dangerous evil force, and Queen Elizabeth now intends to assist them in achieving that ambition?!

Franklin could not fathom what the queen was thinking; such a act of aiding the wicked is nothing short of courting death!?

"Your Majesty, you... you're not joking, are you?! Handing this former‑kingdom codex that contains resurrection secrets over to the Ho‑Ghost Praise!"

"I am not joking; I am serious. Do you have any objections?" Queen Elizabeth's expression was contemptuous, as if she saw nothing wrong with her decision.

Franklin could see that the queen had already made up her mind, but he felt he had to warn her, "Your Majesty, please think this over. The Dark Adventurers' Guild consists of the most vicious and ruthless people; their greed is likely more than just money, and they could act against the Empire. So we must absolutely avoid any cooperation; this is like courting a tiger!"

"Franklin, calm down a bit. We are not cooperating with the Ho‑Ghost Praise; we are using them. Do you understand my meaning?" Queen Elizabeth said calmly.

"Using?" Franklin stared blankly, "If we give this former‑kingdom codex to the Ho‑Ghost Praise, we will inevitably raise a tiger that will become a menace. This act is nothing short of digging our own grave, Your Majesty!"

"It seems your mind is not sharp enough, Franklin..." Queen Elizabeth gave a half‑smile that seemed to look down on Franklin's timid demeanor, "On the surface it appears we are helping the Ho‑Ghost Praise fulfill their ambition, but in reality this is an indispensable step in our plan, building the most splendid stage for the birth of the strongest Hero..."

"Your Majesty's i..." Franklin sensed something vague, but could not put it into words.

"We will deliver the former‑kingdom codex to the Ho‑Ghost Praise, assist them in achieving their ambition, and then continuously spread rumors of the guild's threat to the Empire, stirring panic among the people. When their fear reaches its peak, the hero's stage will be perfectly set..." Queen Elizabeth said confidently.

Franklin's eyes widened, and he instantly understood what the queen intended, "Then we will personally eliminate the Ho‑Ghost Praise and restore the royal family's prestige to its peak!?"

"Exactly, that's the plan. The activities of Erkin the Great Swordmaster within the Empire have seriously undermined the royal family's standing, so we must act," Queen Elizabeth nodded.

"But... associating with the Dark Adventurers' Guild doesn't seem right," Franklin hesitated.

"In extraordinary times, extraordinary deeds are required. We care about the result; as for the process..." Queen Elizabeth curled her lip, speaking calmly, "Who cares about that?"

...Franklin was at a loss; it was hard to offer any advice on the queen's statements.

"As long as my plan succeeds, the royal family's position will return to its pinnacle, unshakable and brighter than before. How much trouble can a mere wanted criminal cause?"
