Queen Elizabeth let out a series of light laughs and continued, "We will show the people with facts who the Empire's most trustworthy guardian truly is..."

"Your Majesty's methods are indeed brilliant. Who will represent the royal family as the Empire's Hero?" Franklin no longer had doubts and thought the plan feasible.

"The most suitable candidate is, of course, Messefield, the Empire's strongest Thorn Knight," Queen Elizabeth said seriously.

"But..." Franklin seemed still hesitant, "The Ho‑Ghost Praise is filled with powerful members; acting guildmaster Swenburn claims to be a demonic magician, and after we give them the former‑kingdom codex, that terrifying guildmaster may return to the world. Relying on Messefield alone might be insufficient."

"It's not that simple. According to the former‑kingdom codex, the resurrection ritual will cause a great commotion. We will detect it first, then dispatch Messefield to defeat Palmer before he can be revived. As for acting guildmaster Swenburn? I think Messefield can handle him without much trouble; I trust my knights," Queen Elizabeth said calmly, having planned everything long ago.

"Then..." Franklin lifted his head and tentatively asked, "Does this mean we don't need to inform Lord Messefield?"

"Messefield is too upright; she would surely refuse such actions, so keeping her in the dark is the best choice," Queen Elizabeth explained.

"Understood, Your Majesty. I will proceed at once and will not disgrace the mission!" Franklin performed a knightly salute.

The Empire's undercurrents churn, conspiracies intertwine, and the calm is gone....

title: Chapter 4 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 4 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 9 · Chapter 4

Wrexham, Wales.

Merlin and Alice had been back for half a month now.

Cecilia had kept her promise, depositing a full 200,000 gold coins into Alice’s bank account.

After deducting debts and taxes, Merlin and Alice had received nearly 60,000 gold coins between them.

Excluding the monthly rent of 5,000 gold coins, the remaining funds were more than enough for Merlin and Alice to live comfortably for a long while.

Even the landlady, who had come to collect the rent, was surprised—Alice had paid up without a single hitch for the first time ever.

As previously agreed, the landlady gave Merlin and Alice a couple’s discount, halving the rent.

This moved Merlin deeply; he felt the landlady was a kind person. But not a single coin of the remaining money made it into his hands—every last bit was seized by the wicked Alice.

Merlin, of course, knew his earnings were separate from Alice’s. By rights, he should have received half the profits.

But Alice, that vampire, kept squeezing the poor peasant with every excuse imaginable, claiming that if she gave Merlin his share, he’d just throw it all away at the racetrack. It would be a waste.

Moreover, living together meant unexpected expenses would come up, so they needed a risk fund—all their earnings should go into it, and only in emergencies could either of them withdraw from it.

No matter how beautifully Alice phrased it, it couldn’t hide her miserly nature and the fact that she was monopolizing Merlin’s assets.

After all, in the end, Alice talked about shared property, yet most of the money ended up in her hands.

As a result, Merlin didn’t come out completely empty-handed—out of tens of thousands of gold coins, he received a whole 100. Not a coin more.

Merlin was extremely displeased. Furious, he raged at Alice, that stinking landlord, stopping just short of throwing her out and seizing her wealth to redistribute the land.

Hadn’t he done the most work on this mission? Yet Alice, who seemed to have done nothing but float by, had hogged all the rewards. How was that fair?!

Merlin felt deeply wronged. At the very least, he should have gotten 10,000 gold coins, right? 100 was treating him like a child!

But Alice remained unyielding. No matter how fiercely Merlin’s verbal barrage struck, she stayed completely unmoved.

Alice thought to herself: That bastard Merlin had messed her over so badly—she deserved compensation now, didn’t she? Otherwise, she’d be the one at a loss!

And this was just the beginning. The suffering she had endured was far worse than anything Merlin could imagine. How could she just let bygones be bygones? When dealing with a demon, she would never show mercy.

So no matter how hoarse Merlin’s throat became from shouting, Alice refused to compromise. Then she simply retreated to her room and went to sleep.

Sure enough, the next day, just as Alice had predicted, even with only 100 gold coins, Merlin had thrown it all away at the Royal Racetrack.

As for the result? Heh. Not even a sound was heard.

Thus, the desperate Merlin had no choice but to go back to Hobbes to freeload, clinging to whatever he could sponge off.

Alice seemed to understand the urgency of her situation. Since returning, she had thrown herself into training, spending every day at the training grounds until she was utterly exhausted before coming home.

But in Merlin’s eyes, the results weren’t great. Her progress was painfully slow, like a snail’s pace. The road to Saint-tier was long and arduous—who knew if Alice would ever succeed.

Indeed, three months was far too little time for Alice. Even with her frantic training, the returns were negligible.

Merlin knew Alice had been at High-tier for a long time now, stuck in a bottleneck—the awkward gap between High-tier and Saint-tier.

It was an extremely uncomfortable position: not good enough for the top, yet better than those below. Countless people had been stuck here, achieving nothing.

So Merlin was genuinely worried about Alice’s dire situation.

If this so-called "Hero" fell, Merlin wouldn’t be happy—he’d feel it was letting her off too easy.

After all, all the debts would then fall on Merlin, and he’d have no way to repay them. He’d have no choice but to return to demon territory and go back to being a shut-in.

Meanwhile, at the Adventurers Guild in Wrexham—

“Merlin, brother, how much do you owe me now?” Hobbes stared at the beer tap, his expression full of resentment as he watched Merlin drink his ale.

“Hmm? Have I ever borrowed money from you?” Merlin swayed his cup, looking genuinely surprised.

“Yes, you have! Every time you come see me, you just drink my beer for free. I’d estimate I’ve spent at least 3 gold coins on you by now. That’s not a small amount. I think you should pay me back.” Hobbes looked helpless, feeling like he had reached the pinnacle of freeloading, only for Merlin to surpass him.

“Well…” Merlin held his beer, his gaze shifting evasively. It wasn’t that he didn’t want to pay—it was that his pockets were embarrassingly empty. “Aren’t you the one treating me? If it’s a treat, then there’s no need to pay back, right?”

“Merlin, why are you being so stingy? Friendship is about give and take. With you, it’s all take and no give.” Hobbes seemed to have a lot of pent-up frustration.

“Hehe~” Merlin grinned shamelessly, awkwardly saying, “Don’t make me sound so petty. It’s not like I have a choice. Aren’t you always saying I’m a member of the Henpecked Husbands Club? Helping each other in times of trouble is only natural. Don’t always bring up money—talking about money all the time hurts our friendship.”

Hobbes’ expression turned complicated. Merlin’s face was thicker than he had imagined. “Merlin, don’t get this wrong. I can’t be the one treating every time. Last time, I even took you to Helena’s secret cabin. That one outing cost nearly 500 gold coins. As a long-standing member of the Henpecked Husbands Club, I’m broke too. You can’t just endlessly sponge off me like this.”

“How could I sponge off you? Don’t misunderstand, okay? This is emotional exchange between friends~” Merlin said with a straight face, showing no intention of being polite.

“What kind of joke is that? Emotional exchange means mooching off me and draining my savings.” Hobbes made a bitter face, feeling deeply pained.

“…” Merlin raised his glass, patting Hobbes’ shoulder with a laugh. “What’s the big deal? Don’t sweat the small stuff~”

“Speaking of which, didn’t you just get back from a mission? You should have some pocket money, right? As a friend, I think you should go settle your tab.” Hobbes said meaningfully.

“What a shame… my pocket money is already gone at the racetrack. Richard screwed me over again…” Merlin said awkwardly.

“Brother, you’re really something else. I’ve never seen you win at the races. This is weird—you’re an anomaly among gamblers. Normal people at least win enough for a few drinks…” Hobbes now realized something was off. Ever since he’d gotten to know Merlin, they’d been to the races over a hundred times, and every single time, Merlin had lost everything. His luck… was truly unbearable to witness.

“Who knows? I don’t get why my luck is so…” Merlin sighed, a cold sweat dropping from his forehead as he spoke with a look of utter despair.

“Maybe I’ve been cursed… or blessed… by a mysterious force from the East… (my wife)”

(°∞哟)

title: Chapter 5 — Chaos
content:
Chapter 5 — Chaos

Volume 9 · Chapter 5

Hobbs took one look at Merlin’s gloomy expression and decided the guy couldn’t be blamed for being broke.

After all, Alice’s stinginess had reached legendary levels—she’d only given Merlin 100 gold coins, practically treating him like a beggar.

As a fellow henpecked husband, Hobbs sympathized deeply and patted Merlin on the shoulder.

“I totally get you, man. Having a tiger wife at home is rough. You’ve got it tough, right? Since your strength’s not as good as your wife’s, you must be getting pushed around a lot at home, huh?”

“Eh?!” Merlin stared at Hobbs in shock, wondering why Hobbs saw him as some kind of punching bag for his wife’s temper.

“What I’m saying is, a man can’t just rely on his looks to freeload. No matter how handsome you are, people get tired of it eventually. Real strength is what speaks for you.” Hobbs nodded like a seasoned veteran.

Merlin’s face remained blank, but his chest felt tight. Who the hell was freeloading? If anything, Alice was the one clinging to him like a little follower. This was ridiculous—now he couldn’t even afford to go out without being looked down on? And they actually thought he was some pretty-boy mooch?

“Merlin, my brother, just look at yourself—you’re the perfect example. With that pretty face, you managed to snag a Gold-rank adventurer and even married Alice. So how’s that working out for you?” Hobbs, his nose flushed red from drink, said with feigned sympathy. “Because your strength isn’t as good as Alice’s, you’re constantly suppressed, can’t fight back, and have to live in silence, with your pockets emptier than your face. If this ‘women on top’ situation keeps up, Merlin, you’ll end up a slave at home with no say at all…”

“Hold on.” Merlin raised a hand to stop Hobbs, feeling this was getting way out of line. “I need to make one thing clear—I’m not freeloading, and I sure as hell won’t let Alice walk all over me.”

“Tsk!” Hobbs clicked his tongue, looking like he’d seen through everything. “I get it, I get it. It’s just a pride thing, right? What’s there to hide from me? Truth be told, my situation at home isn’t much better than yours.”

Merlin blinked, then narrowed his eyes. “…In that case, I think *you’re* the one who deserves pity the most.”

“Same here, buddy.” Hobbs chugged his drink.

“We’re nothing alike. Don’t lump me in with you.” Merlin frowned, clearly rejecting the comparison.

“Oh? If we’re so different, then Alice shouldn’t be controlling your money, right? So this round of drinks should be no problem for you. Go ahead, treat us—it’s your turn.” Hobbs, deadpan, extended his hand for money, probably fed up with Merlin mooching off him.

“Uh…”

Merlin forced an awkward smile, a cold sweat rolling down his forehead, and pushed Hobbs’ outstretched hand back. “…Alice, that damn woman, has me crushed under her thumb. Turns out a guy like me, a so-called freeloading pretty boy, works his ass off only to have every hard-earned coin snatched away by that woman. Tell me, is there anyone more miserable than me? Sniff…”

Seeing Merlin’s pained expression, Hobbs felt a kinship in shared suffering. “So that’s how it is, huh? Merlin, don’t say any more. You’ve got it worse than me. Next time, I’ll treat you to… a certain *small A* place.”

“Eh? Then…” Merlin froze, wondering why every time he hung out with Hobbs, they never ended up anywhere decent.

“What? You don’t want to go back to Helena’s secret cabin? The girls there were all great, weren’t they?” Hobbs, now a little drunk, had turned downright lecherous.

“Great, just great. Thanks, Chief, for the hospitality. From now on, I’m staying in the Henpecked Husbands Club forever. I’ll be a lifetime honorary member. Everyone here’s a real talent, and they all say such nice things. I love it here.” Merlin, desperate to keep freeloading, had resorted to shameless flattery.

Hobbs gave Merlin a thumbs-up, then stopped chatting and tried to finish reading his newspaper before heading home.

Since they were sitting across from each other, when Hobbs raised the paper, Merlin could still see parts of the back page.

「The legendary great swordsman Elgin appears in the capital, furiously slays Samuel, a radical Black Elf executive, and saves the Empire from crisis!」

The incident of Merlin cutting down the Black Elf Samuel had caused a huge stir in the capital, and since it hadn’t been long, the news still dominated the front pages of all the major papers.

After all, these newspapers didn’t care much about the queen’s preferences—they just chased sensational stories. Whatever the public wanted to know, they’d deliver.

Right now, the hottest figure in the Great Britannia Empire was none other than Elgin the Great Swordsman. His admirers grew by the day, and his popularity surged higher and higher.

Countless imperial onlookers viewed Elgin the Great Swordsman as a savior, practically elevating him to the status of a legendary hero.

Almost everyone was intensely curious about this mysterious powerhouse. Though no one knew who he really was, they loved imagining him in all sorts of grand, imposing forms—and the hype only grew wilder by the day.

“Hm?” Merlin spotted a report about himself and, piqued with curiosity, snatched the newspaper from Hobbs.

「Black Elf radical executive sets up a forbidden magic array in the capital, nearly dooming the entire city. At the critical moment, Elgin the Great Swordsman arrives in the nick of time, resolving the Empire’s greatest crisis—the legendary champion lives up to his name!」

「The Thorn Knights played a limited role in this incident; the Seventh Knight, Morrison, was severely injured. The Empire’s future security is a growing concern!」

「Many citizens claim the Empire’s safety depends on Elgin the Great Swordsman. The Violet Thorn Knights have made no statement, and the Fifth Thorn Knight, Milieus, has refused all interviews.」

「The Capital Merchant Guild has jointly written to Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth, requesting the revocation of Elgin the Great Swordsman’s wanted status. A hero should not suffer unfair treatment. Many citizens have echoed this sentiment.」

「Yesterday, Queen Elizabeth publicly stated that it is too early to judge Elgin the Great Swordsman’s character. We must not allow opportunists to exploit the situation. There are suspicions of someone secretly manipulating public opinion to disrupt the Empire’s stability and harmony. The public must keep their eyes open and not be deceived by someone’s dazzling facade.」

Merlin scanned the bold, exaggerated headlines—he didn’t even need to read the details to know what was going on.

He felt like he’d stirred up something big this time—big enough to shake the entire empire.

Could his shadow really be that influential? If this kept up, he might end up as the queen’s biggest thorn in her side.

Merlin stroked his chin, amused. This was getting interesting—he hadn’t done a thing, yet he’d somehow become the hottest legend of the moment.

Of course, there was also news about the Holy Church:

「The Pope, currently in the Vatican, has publicly declared that the Salvation Knight bears the mission of the Goddess of Light to save the world. Resolving the Great Britannia crisis is the greatest divine miracle. He hopes the Salvation Knight will travel to the Vatican to meet the Pope and receive a glorious baptism.」

“Tsk!” Merlin twisted his mouth in disdain, rolling his eyes at the news.

These damn holy frauds really had no shame—they’d jump on any bandwagon to stir the pot.

I’m the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace, what the hell do I have to do with those bastards…

title: Chapter 6 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 6 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 6

Merlin was left speechless by his old rivals. Whenever something good happened, those Holy Church fanatics would always barge in and ruin it.

They spouted incomprehensible nonsense, claiming the entire universe belonged to the Holy Church—shameless to the extreme!

And what was even more absurd was that he, the former ruler of the demon race, had somehow been labeled as the Goddess of Light’s redeeming knight?!

There wasn’t even the slightest connection! If the other demon lords found out, they’d probably abandon the Demon Lord Palace and launch a crusade against him. The demon race’s laws were strict—betrayal by a ruler had never happened in history, and the entire race would never tolerate such a disgrace...

Merlin stared blankly at the newspaper before choosing to ignore the Holy Church’s clownish behavior. He had long since grown numb to their antics.

Hobbes watched Merlin with keen interest and said, "Merlin, are you also interested in Elgin the Great Swordsman?"

"Huh?! No, no, don’t get the wrong idea! I was just looking..." Merlin waved his hands, thinking, *Interested in myself? I’m not that narcissistic.*

"No need to be shy about it. It’s not some unspeakable thing. Lots of people are into Elgin the Great Swordsman these days. In fact, there are even—" Hobbes shook his head, clearly relishing the gossip.

"Fans?!" Merlin’s expression turned odd. *How come I’ve never seen any of that?*

"Yeah, groups of people who idolize someone. Like a mini version of the Holy Church, except they worship Elgin the Great Swordsman instead of the Goddess of Light." Hobbes calmly took a sip of his drink.

"Really? I’ve never noticed." Merlin’s mind was filled with question marks.

"This trend just started recently. I’d bet every city in Great Britain has them. Even here in Lexington, there’s a fan club for Elgin the Great Swordsman. The leader is Jenna, the daughter of Earl Austin—oh right, Arnold’s little sister. That girl who’s always reading romance novels." Hobbes wore a knowing smile.

"Elgin the Great Swordsman’s influence... has really reached this level?" Merlin found it hard to believe. He had some mental preparation, but this still exceeded his expectations.

"Yeah, it’s insane. I’ve never seen anyone in the empire reach this level of fame—almost on par with the queen." Hobbes paused, then pointed outside. "Don’t believe me? Go take a look. Kids used to play at being Thorn Knights, but now? They’re all scrambling to be wandering swordsmen like Elgin the Great Swordsman."

Merlin’s expression turned uneasy. *If this keeps up, my shadow is going to reshape the entire empire. Even children are starting to worship me. What’s going to happen next? This is a threat to the empire’s foundations! I must be the biggest thorn in the rulers’ sides now.*

As a former ruler of the Death Swamp, Merlin understood the implications all too well. If his subordinates and people started pledging loyalty to someone else, it would be a devastating blow to his rule.

"You know the city where the legend of Elgin began? It’s practically become a pilgrimage site now. Lots of people go to see the statue of Elgin the Great Swordsman’s shadow. Elgin used to be a small coastal city, but overnight, its prosperity has rivaled Edinburgh’s..." Hobbes stroked his beard thoughtfully. "If I had to guess, the number of Elgin the Great Swordsman’s fans across the empire might even surpass the size of the regular army. That’s not a force to be ignored. If they ever cause trouble... tsk tsk tsk, the empire would be in deep trouble."

Merlin clicked his tongue in disbelief and covered his face in despair. *This can’t be happening. My peaceful days are over?*

*I just wanted a lazy, quiet life. Why has it come to this?*

*Why do I have no reputation myself, but my shadow is worshipped like this?*

*Damn it, what am I supposed to do? At this rate, I’ll probably end up as an enemy of the entire nation soon!*

Wait... what am I panicking for? Who even knows that I *am* Elgin the Great Swordsman? Even Alice doesn’t acknowledge me. What’s there to fear?

Merlin lifted his head, regaining his usual composure. For the first time, he felt that quietly showing off without fame was a good thing—at least it kept trouble away. "Yeah, the most enviable part is the female fans. I bet you could assemble an entire division’s worth of combat power. If you had a different fan every night, you’d probably need a week just to get through them all without repeats." Hobbes cackled, his entire demeanor turning lecherous, his eyes brimming with envy.

Merlin’s expression turned unnatural, his whole body feeling uncomfortable. *Hobbes, you shameless old rogue! What are you even thinking?! Do you take me for some kind of person?! This is slander in the dark! Who would do something so ridiculous?! Even if I wanted to, my sister would probably kill every woman in Great Britain before I could even try!*

"Oh?" Hobbes’ eyes lit up, his expression turning lewd. "Merlin, are you jealous too? Everyone wants female fans. Don’t let my age fool you—I still have the heart of a young man, full of passion~"

"No, no, no, I’m not jealous, thank you." Merlin shook his hands repeatedly, thinking, *I’m Elgin the Great Swordsman myself—what’s there to be jealous of? I just want fewer troubles in my life!*

"Don’t play coy. We’re all men here~" Hobbes punched Merlin’s chest and winked at him.

"Fine, whatever makes you happy..." Merlin forced a dry laugh, thinking, *This pervert Hobbes—if he weren’t so afraid of his wife, he’d probably be out committing crimes by now.*

Hobbes happily took a sip of beer, then sneakily glanced at the counter before tugging at Merlin’s sleeve. "What now?" Merlin frowned, already annoyed.

"Look at Lucia’s state..." Hobbes deliberately lowered his voice, as if plotting something.

Merlin followed his gaze. Lucia rested her left cheek on her hand, twirling a feather pen in her right, her eyes glazed over as if lost in thought or daydreaming.

Her silky hair cascaded down, half-covering her face. As the Adventurers Guild’s poster girl, Lucia was undeniably lovely—angelic face, devilish figure.

Yet now, she, who was usually sharp and efficient, seemed distracted, as if burdened by some worry.

"So what? Isn’t that normal?" Merlin said.

"Normal my foot! Can’t you see she’s acting like a lovesick girl?" Hobbes furrowed his brows, as if it were obvious.

"Miss Lucia is at that age—isn’t it normal for her to have a crush? What’s the big deal?" Merlin smirked, thinking Hobbes was like a creepy stalker uncle, always watching a high school girl. In the real world, this would be grounds for a police report.

"It’s not a big deal, but do you know *who* she’s fallen for?" Hobbes narrowed his eyes, trying to pique Merlin’s curiosity.

Merlin’s forehead broke out in a cold sweat, black lines forming above his head. He had a bad feeling about this. "...Who?"

Hobbes’ expression turned serious as he patted Merlin’s shoulder. "Isn’t it obvious? The hottest sensation right now..."

Merlin’s heart pounded.

"Lucia, that scheming vixen, has fallen for the legendary great swordsman of Elgin."

title: Chapter 7 — Overlord
content:
Chapter 7 — Overlord

Volume 9 · Chapter 7

Hobbs spoke with great animation, as if the mere mention of gossip turned this middle-aged man into a real-life Detective Conan in an instant.

For men of his age, gossip was practically the secret elixir of a second youth.

Merlin narrowed his eyes, glancing at the daydreaming Lucia, and asked in surprise, "Seriously? Lucia seems so rational usually. She doesn’t even spare a glance for most people—how could she fall for someone like Elgin the Great Swordsman, a man with no name, no background, nothing?"

"You wouldn’t understand..." Hobbs tapped the table with his fingers, putting on an air of wisdom. "This is the classic case of a beauty falling for a hero. There’s no logic to it. What girl doesn’t dream of her other half being a man who commands the winds and clouds? And Elgin the Great Swordsman just happens to fit that fantasy perfectly. That’s why he’s got so many fangirls at the conference."

"Hmmmm..." Merlin’s expression turned complicated as he looked at Lucia in the distance. "But what you’re describing usually happens to girls with no romantic experience. Lucia doesn’t strike me as that naive. She seems emotionally mature..."

"Tsk! Let me tell you more..." Hobbs was getting into it, determined to win Merlin over. "Just the other day, Lucia came to me in secret to ask about Elgin the Great Swordsman. It was obvious she was interested—she was practically running a background check on him!"

"Do you know Elgin the Great Swordsman well?" Merlin asked, his voice tinged with unease.

"Not *that* well, but I know the basics. Though none of that matters." Hobbs waved a hand dismissively. "All you need to know is that Lucia is into this mysterious guy and wants to date him."

Merlin’s brows furrowed in confusion. "But what does Lucia even see in him? It feels weird for a girl to just fall for some man whose name she doesn’t even know."

"Let me break it down for you..." Hobbs took a swig of beer, set the glass down, and said seriously, "First, Elgin the Great Swordsman is absurdly powerful—undeniable fact. That gives a girl a sense of security. Second, he’s famous, which means wealth and status. And most importantly, he’s the hottest topic right now. Whoever becomes his wife would instantly become a celebrity! Lucia’s ideal partner is someone like a dragon soaring through the heavens—tall, rich, handsome, the center of attention. Simple as that."

"Whoa..." Merlin gasped, awkwardly muttering, "But the way you describe it makes her sound like a scheming gold-digger."

"Lucia *is* a scheming gold-digger. You’ve known her for ages—what’s new?" Hobbs stole a glance at Lucia, then lowered his voice. "Between you and me, a lot of noble sons have been chasing after her. But she never gives them a straight answer, never fully rejects them either—just keeps them all on the hook. That way, her value keeps going up."

"Damn..." Merlin narrowed his eyes. *She really plays the long game. I always thought she was just a gentle, approachable girl...*

"Hmph hmph~" Hobbs swirled his glass, his voice carrying a hint of lewdness. "If *you* were Elgin the Great Swordsman, you could go sleep with Lucia right now~"

"Pfft!" Merlin spat out a mouthful of tea, completely flustered. *Get lost! Do I look like some kind of breeding machine?*

"Why are you so worked up? I was joking..." Hobbs looked at Merlin in confusion, casually remarking, "It’s not like you’re *actually* Elgin the Great Swordsman. So calm down—you’re not sleeping with Lucia anyway. Give it up. If Alice found out, she’d hack you to pieces."

"Yeah, true."

Merlin nodded, thinking to himself, *What a coincidence—I *am* Elgin the Great Swordsman.*

As for Alice hacking him to pieces? *Pfft. As if.*

Merlin didn’t continue the conversation with Hobbs. Instead, he went back to reading the newspaper to settle his thoughts.

One piece of news caught his attention, and he unconsciously read it aloud:

"Today, Franklin, the captain of the Purple Gold Flower Knights, publicly announced that the dark Adventurers Guild, Gōki Raisan, has entered the empire. Residents are advised to stay vigilant, protect their safety, and report any suspicious individuals to the local garrison immediately."

Merlin couldn’t help but stroke his chin. *Is this Gōki Raisan really that dangerous? To put the entire empire on alert...* Though, now that he thought about it, Alice had mentioned something about them before.

"Ah, Gōki Raisan..." Hobbs nodded, suddenly chiming in from the side. "There’s been a lot of news about them lately. It’s got people pretty nervous."

"You seem pretty knowledgeable about the dark guild?" Merlin looked across at Hobbs.

"Wouldn’t say I’m an expert, but I do know a fair bit. After all, 30 years ago, Gōki Raisan was known as the strongest dark Adventurers Guild in all the human kingdoms. They were infamous—just the mention of their name struck fear into people’s hearts. Their methods were brutally cruel, leaving corpses in their wake wherever they went. Even royal families didn’t dare provoke them lightly. They were *that* terrifying..." Hobbs spoke seriously, his hand shaking as he held his glass—no exaggeration in his tone.

"Hmm?" Merlin’s interest was piqued. He pressed further. "From what you’re saying, Gōki Raisan sounds incredibly powerful."

"30 years ago, they were absolutely a fearsome organization. And they were *loud* about it too. Other dark guilds kept a low profile, hiding in the shadows, but not Gōki Raisan. They operated in broad daylight, swaggering through human lands. Everyone *knew* they were a wicked, dangerous group, but almost no one dared to challenge them. That’s how strong they were..." Hobbs said gravely, his brows furrowing.

Merlin listened, stunned. *They were so powerful that they could just waltz through human territory?* Even the demon race wouldn’t dare charge through human lands so brazenly.

"If I remember right, those maniacs did *anything* for money. If you paid enough, they’d even kill a king for you." Hobbs recalled as he spoke.

"Seriously?!" Merlin was shocked. A king was the highest ruler—if they could kill one, Gōki Raisan was beyond reckless.

"Dead serious. I don’t lie about this stuff. It *happened*, and it was huge news. Everyone knew about it. The former emperor of Germany, Wilhelm II—he was taken out by Gōki Raisan." Hobbs’ expression was solemn; he wasn’t joking.

"Wait, they *did* that?!" Merlin raised his eyebrows, utterly disbelief.

"Before they killed Wilhelm II, Gōki Raisan had already sent out a death notice in advance. It caused total panic in Germany. The palace beefed up security—*all* the royal powerhouses were there, including Saint-tier knights and countless court mages. But none of it stopped Gōki Raisan. Their people *toyed* with the guards, and their guild leader was unstoppable, cutting through every strong opponent in his path. In the end, in front of *everyone*, he chopped off Wilhelm II’s head..." Hobbs’ face was etched with deep fear as he briefly recounted the shocking event from 30 years ago that had sent tremors through the entire human world.

Merlin listened, his expression shifting repeatedly. He couldn’t help but ponder:

*This Gōki Raisan is insane...*

*They actually had the power to stand against an entire kingdom’s royal family?*

(亚_亚)

title: Chapter 8 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 8 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 8

After that incident, the royal families of all human nations began to feel deeply insecure, no longer daring to provoke the Howling Specter Guild lightly. Even the entire German Empire chose to endure in silence, because the Howling Specter Guild was simply too powerful to resist—at least, not with the strength of Germany alone.

Hobbes sipped his drink as he spoke, recounting the events of those years with the precision of a living historical archive. "But the Howling Specter Guild’s glory didn’t last long. After their president died, they declined, becoming far more low-key. They no longer flaunted their power openly, lurking in the shadows of various nations. I’ve heard they’ve fallen to the level of a second-rate dark adventurers guild. Still, even a starving camel is bigger than a horse—they must still have some hidden strength."

"What’s interesting is that after the Howling Specter Guild’s president died, the human royal families regained their confidence. They formed a united army and began wiping out dark adventurers guild strongholds everywhere, executing even suspected members without mercy. The German Kingdom was the most aggressive, probably to avenge their late king. Their cavalry even pursued them all the way to the Ptolemaic Dynasty. In the end, all nations signed a treaty to jointly resist the dark adventurers guild. If any country faced a large-scale dark guild presence, all others were obligated to send troops to assist in the extermination. That’s how things stabilized."

"The dark adventurers guild, though not completely wiped out, all began to keep a low profile, no longer operating openly. The Howling Specter Guild had been legendary, representing the peak of dark adventurers and a force that dared to defy the light. But with the death of their powerful president, everything came to an end."

Merlin listened with a mix of emotions, silently taking a sip of beer, his gaze flickering.

In his view, the Howling Specter Guild was simply too damn arrogant—so much so that they looked down on everyone else.

How dare they kill the highest ruler of a nation?! Who would have the audacity to do that without absolute strength to back it up?!

And yet, the Howling Specter Guild had done it, relying purely on brute force, with no tricks or deception.

Merlin thought that if this were the real world, the Howling Specter Guild would be a bunch of reckless hotheads, playing by their own rules.

And to make it worse, before killing the German Emperor, they even issued a public notice: *"I’m coming to kill you. Wash your neck and wait."*

How arrogantly shameless could one be to pull off something like that? They didn’t fear increasing the difficulty of their task—they were confident they could take down the German royalty.

Merlin couldn’t help but laugh in disbelief. If this were a game, the Howling Specter Guild would be a group of hardcore players who only tackled the highest difficulty, each one performing godlike feats.

"From what you’re saying, this Howling Specter Guild president was incredibly powerful?"

"Powerful? That’s an understatement!" Hobbes said seriously. "The Shadow Flame Specter Palmer was already a dominant force thirty years ago, leaving countless people seething in silence. Even now, he’d still be a first-rate powerhouse. Take our British Empire, for example—if we exclude those legendary, elusive old monsters, the only one who could face him might be the first Thorn Knight..."

Hobbes paused, realizing something was off. "Ah, no, I should add one more—Elgin the Great Swordsman. So, two people."

Merlin just smiled without comment, thinking Hobbes was wrong. In his mind, there was almost no one who could match him. What was a mere Shadow Flame Specter Palmer? He’d never even heard of the man.

"The Shadow Flame Specter Palmer’s strength is undeniable—he was a hegemon-level figure thirty years ago. The fact that he could single-handedly defeat multiple Saint-tier warriors of Germany proves his power was likely near the peak of the Saint tier. The knights who protected Wilhelm II were no pushovers; even now, they’d still be considered strong. But Palmer defeated them all alone and then beheaded the old king right in front of them, thoroughly humiliating the German royalty. What does that tell you? It means he didn’t even need to use his full strength to do it..." Hobbes took a sharp breath, his own speculation, but it was likely close to the truth.

The Shadow Flame Specter Palmer was at the peak of the Saint tier, standing alone among the dark adventurers guild, so powerful that he didn’t fear any faction.

Beheading Wilhelm II was just a mission. Even when faced with an onslaught of royal powerhouses, Palmer didn’t need to use his full strength.

Otherwise, he wouldn’t have confidently announced the assassination in advance. From the very beginning, he had held the German royal warriors in contempt.

Among the German royal powerhouses thirty years ago, not a single one was a match for Palmer.

If Palmer had gone all out, he could have clashed head-on with the Frost Holy Dragon Marius without being at a disadvantage.

Merlin scoffed, feigning a carefully crafted expression of disdain. "If this Palmer was so incredible, how did he end up dying?"

"Well, that was just bad luck," Hobbes said, lifting his eyelids as if carefully recalling. "Thirty years ago, a major event occurred—the legendary North Sea Leviathan appeared in the Norwegian Sea, rampaging and devouring the land and passing merchant ships. You know what the North Sea Leviathan is? It’s a world-ending sea monster said to have existed since the Age of Gods, far beyond what humans could oppose. But this Shadow Flame Specter Palmer was too arrogant. The Leviathan flicked him with a single tentacle and killed him on the spot..."

"Hmm?!" Merlin frowned, his attention not on the Shadow Flame Specter Palmer but on the campaign against the North Sea Leviathan. "Why did so many people go to fight the North Sea Leviathan back then?"

"Officially, it was to defend human maritime routes. But there were rumors that the North Sea Leviathan guarded the tombs of the gods or some treasure left behind by them—maybe it was the gatekeeper of some kind of secret realm. I’m too weak to know the details. That was a raid only the absolute top-tier powerhouses could participate in. For small fry like us, it’s just hearsay to pass the time after meals."

Hobbes drained his beer in one gulp.

Merlin recalled the Gun Hero. Alice had mentioned that this man had also participated in the North Sea Leviathan raid before mysteriously disappearing. Could there really be some kind of secret realm?

"Hobbes, I’ve heard the Holy Church’s Gun Hero was part of the raid. How much do you know about him?"

"Oh~ the Gun Hero? Of course I know him—he’s one of the Ten Legendary Heroes, the man who single-handedly slew the Great Demon Lord Lucifer II." Hobbes put on a know-it-all expression.

"If you know, then tell me." Merlin’s interest was immediately piqued. Maybe Hobbes knew some secrets.

"The raid party back then was star-studded. Powerhouses from all walks of life emerged, and even some reclusive old monsters made an appearance."

Hobbes paused, then continued, lost in thought. "Among them, the Gun Hero was one of the most dazzling..."

◆

Update after midnight. If there’s no update, I probably fell asleep.

title: Chapter 9 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 9 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 9

"Damn bright..." Merlin narrowed his eyes. Just how blinding was this guy?

In Merlin’s mind, the Spear Hero was probably the strongest human he had ever seen.

Up to now, Merlin had never encountered anyone like the Spear Hero—imposing, with strength that defied comprehension.

"Hmm, yeah. Back then, there were so many powerhouses, but a lot of people said the Spear Hero was the strongest. Who knows if it’s true? I can’t really judge based on hearsay alone." Hobbes spoke seriously, though he didn’t commit to the claim.

"The strongest, huh..." Merlin pondered. It wasn’t impossible. After all, that man who had once humiliated him was indeed terrifyingly powerful.

"I heard the Spear Hero was an orphan from childhood, raised in a monastery as a reserve for the Temple Knights. He was quiet and withdrawn, but his talent was so outstanding that he was chosen to become an official Temple Knight. He stayed in the Vatican, and after years of effort, he was selected as a Hero to go to war. His famous battle was the subjugation of Lucifer the Second, which earned him a place among the Ten Legendary Heroes. It’s quite an inspiring rags-to-riches story." Hobbes nodded as he spoke.

"Is that so?"

Merlin expressionlessly took a sip of beer. He had zero interest in the Spear Hero’s past. All he cared about was whether this guy could lift his curse.

The curse on his heart was the most dangerous thing, lurking inside him for years. As long as it wasn’t removed, he’d always fear it flaring up suddenly.

As for the Holy Church taking in orphans—Merlin wasn’t impressed. Taking in orphans was just a pretense; turning them into a private army was their real goal.

In his view, the demon race and the Holy Church weren’t so different. If someone had no use, they’d be eliminated.

"Oh, right! Speaking of which, there was that unpleasant business between the Flame Demon Lord Palmer and the Spear Hero..." Hobbes suddenly remembered, as if the memory had been buried too deep in time.

"Hmm? Those two had a conflict?" Merlin asked with interest.

"I only heard about this, so I can’t confirm if it’s true." Hobbes set down his cup and said seriously, "Rumor has it that a long time ago, someone paid a huge sum to hire the Flame Demon Lord to assassinate the Pope. But the attempt failed, and the matter was dropped. At the time, the Spear Hero was the Pope’s guard. When he faced Palmer, he defeated him so badly that Palmer was left severely injured. I don’t know if it’s true, but it seems a bit suspicious. Both are powerhouses, yet the Spear Hero completely crushed him. Feels off, doesn’t it?"

Merlin thought it over. It was probably true. He had seen the Spear Hero’s strength with his own eyes. There were very few who could defeat someone like that.

"Probably. The Spear Hero is pretty strong, after all."

Hobbes was taken aback. Merlin usually responded to his stories with nothing but disdain, so it was rare for him to agree. "Merlin, you could take the Spear Hero as your role model! He worked hard to become a Legendary Hero. You could work hard to resist Alice’s oppression!"

"Forget it. If someone wants to be my role model, they’d better be on the same level. The Spear Hero isn’t enough..." Merlin swirled his drink calmly, thinking, *A Hero as a role model for a Demon Lord? That’s a joke. Let’s see if I can’t even kill him first.*

"Hey hey hey, you’re drunk again, talking big." Hobbes wore a wistful expression, sighing. "Guys like us, the bottom-feeders, will never reach the Spear Hero’s level. I wonder what kind of life the strong live. Must be a million times easier than ours, right?"

"..." Merlin gave a dry chuckle but didn’t respond. *What kind of life do the strong live?* Wasn’t the perfect example right in front of him? He was an overwhelmingly powerful swordsman, yet it made no difference. He still had to freeload meals and drinks, just like Hobbes. Their lives were practically identical.

"What’s so funny? It’s got to be a life of luxury and indulgence. So envious..." Hobbes’s face twisted into a lecherous grin as he let his imagination run wild.

"Stop daydreaming. Even the strong live the same kind of life as us." Merlin wore a mysterious smile.

"How’s that possible? You think everyone’s like you—a black-iron-ranked adventurer who starts slacking off the moment you get your license, eating off your wife and putting up with her temper? That’s no way to live with dignity!" Hobbes couldn’t resist tearing Merlin down.

"Who’s eating off their wife?!" Merlin’s expression darkened. He put on a serious face. "Let me tell you the truth. The one without dignity at home is Alice. She’s the one with no pride. I’m the one who calls the shots. If I tell Alice to go east, she wouldn’t dare go west. She’s practically a cheap maid!"

Hobbes started off smirking, probably thinking Merlin was just boasting again.

But then his expression slowly froze, his face twisting into something unreadable as he kept shooting Merlin strange looks. His complexion looked off.

"Hmph!" Merlin curled his lip, striking a haughty pose. "Look at your face—you don’t believe me, do you? You think I’m bragging again? You really underestimate me."

Hobbes’s expression was priceless—twitching eyebrows, pouting lips, his face contorting in bizarre ways. But with that thick beard of his, and that bright red drinker’s nose, it was hard to tell what he was really feeling.

"What’s with that weird reaction? Do I have any reason to lie? I, cough—" Merlin cleared his throat, nearly slipping up and calling himself Demon Lord. "A real man like me, eating off Alice? Don’t make me laugh. A year ago, Alice was nothing but my slave, just a strong laborer for rowing boats."

A sharp *crack* echoed from behind Merlin. Listening closely, wasn’t that... Alice?

"Uh!" Merlin’s eyes widened. He turned his head and saw Alice standing there, arms crossed over her chest, staring at him with a look full of meaning.

"Heh heh..." Hobbes awkwardly stood up, sensing that a domestic war was about to erupt. He didn’t want to get caught in the crossfire. He scratched his head. "Oh, Alice is here? What a coincidence. Guess your training’s over. Well, I’ve got a lot of important things to do, so I’ll take my leave—"

Before he even finished speaking, Hobbes vanished in a flash, his escape speed absolutely king-tier.

Seeing the situation turn sour, he had ruthlessly sold out his friend without hesitation. Hobbes was clearly a pro at this.

Now, only Merlin and Alice remained, facing off against each other.

"Cheap maid, rowing laborer... Very impressive, Merlin..." Alice’s face was as cold as if covered in frost. She looked like she was about to suffer internal injuries from sheer rage.

"Ah... uh..." Merlin’s expression stiffened, his gaze darting around as cold sweat beaded on his forehead.

*Fuck, could this get any more unlucky?* So embarrassing... (∞吻∞)

title: Chapter 10 — Return
content:
Chapter 10 — Return

Volume 9 · Chapter 10

On the way home.

It was already nearing evening.

The crimson sunset burned the sky, dyeing all of Rexham in red.

Most of the people on the streets were heading home, bustling yet far calmer than usual.

Alice stomped ahead, still fuming over the insults Merlin had just thrown at her.

How dare he! She had been kind enough to let that damn bastard move in, and he had the nerve to badmouth her behind her back!

So ungrateful! Had she ever talked trash about him before? A white-eyed wolf like him deserved to die a hundred times over!

Alice radiated anger, though in truth, she herself had never stopped secretly insulting Merlin, even slapping him with a "poverty debuff" that amplified his misery tenfold.

She marched forward, her silver hair swaying like silk, not once glancing back at Merlin, as if she were throwing a tantrum.

Merlin, meanwhile, wore an expression of complete indifference, his hands clasped behind his head as he leisurely followed behind Alice.

His gaze was fixed on the sky, showing no intention of apologizing.

Since mutual roasting had become their habit, they were even—neither had the right to call the other out.

Merlin felt he had only spoken the truth. To him, Alice was nothing more than cheap maid labor. What was wrong with that?

Still, letting the tension drag on wasn’t ideal, so he decided to take a roundabout approach.

"Ahem... So, Alice, how’s your training going? Any progress?"

Alice’s shoulders twitched. She lowered her head in silence, clearly not wanting to talk about it.

The truth was, she was desperate. She wished she could reach Saint-tier overnight.

These past few days, every time she looked in the mirror, she saw the corruption spreading faster. Even with the naked eye, she could see the blue-white dragon scales creeping outward, slowly consuming her body.

On top of that, her training to break into Saint-tier had stalled. It felt like she was spinning her wheels, and the despair was crushing.

Alice herself thought three months was far too short. With no signs of a breakthrough yet, she feared that by the deadline, she’d be finished—just as Merlin had said.

"You look like..." Merlin narrowed his eyes and said coolly, "Things aren’t going well, huh?"

"I know they’re not! So what? It’s none of your business!" Alice snapped, glaring at Merlin. Right now, she couldn’t shake the feeling that he was laughing at her.

"Oh?" Merlin blinked, then grinned. "That’s some spirit."

"Aren’t I just your cheap maid? Why would you care if I live or die?" Alice shot back, glaring at him.

"I don’t." Merlin answered without hesitation, still smiling.

"Hmph! I knew it!" Alice huffed, speeding up. "You really are a heartless demon! I saw right through you!"

"Hehe~" Merlin quickened his pace to catch up. "Still, I’d rather have someone to share the debt with."

"So you’re saying even if you’re in deep trouble, you’ll drag me down with you?" Alice narrowed her eyes, convinced Merlin had never meant well.

"Exactly. That’s only fair, isn’t it?" Merlin spread his hands, seeing nothing wrong with his logic.

"Shameless!" Alice snapped, furious.

"Don’t be like that. This isn’t even shameless." Merlin sidled up beside her, grinning. "So, how about this—starting tomorrow, I’ll train with you. Maybe it’ll speed things up a little."

"Didn’t you say your special training isn’t effective anymore?" Alice eyed him suspiciously.

"It’s not *that* effective, but it’s better than nothing, right? At least it’s better than you running around like a headless fly with no direction." Merlin smirked, offering to keep her company.

Alice fell silent, her heart wavering. After all, Merlin was strong. Training with him might actually help her improve faster.

She knew his near-death training had lost its edge, but if he was willing to spar with her, that was still a good thing.

Maybe he wasn’t completely rotten. Maybe, just maybe, this was his roundabout way of caring?

...No, that was impossible. That bastard always put his own interests first. He’d never care about someone for no reason.

A tiny flicker of warmth stirred in her heart, but her mouth still instinctively grumbled. "I... I don’t need your help, humph!"

"Wow, so proud..." Merlin furrowed his brow at Alice, then said flatly, "Fine, forget it. I was just being lazy about training with you anyway."

Alice’s eyes widened as she stared at Merlin. She had only said that offhand—she never expected him to take it seriously!

"What are you looking at? You got what you wanted. Problem?" Merlin feigned innocence.

Alice suddenly grabbed Merlin’s arm, her face slowly flushing red as she stayed silent—a perfect display of a tsundere whose words were the opposite of her true feelings.

Merlin watched her expression, even letting out a small, animal-like whimper from his throat, making it hard to watch without pity.

"Look! It’s Mr. Karl!"

"Really? Mr. Karl’s back!"

"Mr. Karl!"

Just as Merlin and Alice were locked in their stubborn standoff, the street suddenly erupted in commotion as people rushed to see what was happening.

"What’s going on?" Merlin turned toward the street, sensing the arrival of some important figure.

"Hmm?" Alice watched the reactions of the people around her and suddenly realized. "Oh! Mr. Karl must have finished his mission and returned."

"Karl?" Merlin squinted, as if his memory was faulty.

"Didn’t I tell you before? Mr. Karl is the old guildmaster’s son. He’s the star adventurer of our guild." Alice explained, exasperated.

"Ah~ Right." Merlin nodded, instantly recalling who Karl was—the son of old Taylor, one of the guild’s three Mithril-ranked adventurers.

The street was now packed with people lining both sides, standing still as they whispered excitedly to one another.

Many waved their arms or held flowers, and cheers and whistles rang out from time to time. Karl clearly held a special place in the hearts of Rexham’s people.

After all, Karl had always been kind, helping countless residents of Rexham. He was respected by many, the most beloved adventurer in the entire city.

And he was the face of the Rexham Adventurers Guild. Though many mocked Rexham’s adventurers as "cross-eyed," everyone knew the powerful brawler named Kael was a man worthy of respect.

Now—

This symbolic strongman of Rexham had returned in triumph after completing his mission...

title: Chapter 11 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 11 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 11

The sky was already nearing dusk, yet the street had suddenly come alive with bustle thanks to Karl's return.

"Mr. Karl!"

"Welcome back, Mr. Karl!"

"Welcome home, Mr. Karl!"

Cheers and applause rose and fell in waves. Nearly every resident of Rexrum held Karl in high regard, and they were sparing no words of praise.

Karl had already become an iconic figure in Rexrum—a man of boundless enthusiasm, so it was no surprise he received such a grand welcome.

"Oh dear~" Merlin lifted an eyebrow with a sigh, "It seems Mr. Karl is quite popular here in Rexrum?"

"Of course he is," Alice said, shooting Merlin a look, "Mr. Karl isn't only powerful, but also righteous. Naturally, everyone loves him—completely unlike certain demons."

"...Merlin forced a chuckle to himself. Righteous companions can't fill your stomach. Just look at the Munis family—every last one of them died a tragic death. What a miserable fate."

In the distance—

A middle-aged man in a plainclothes uncle guise was walking slowly toward them. His looks weren't handsome, but he carried a rugged masculinity with sharp features and a blue beard stubble on his chin.

He wore ordinary, dusty clothes that looked worn and tattered, slung a travel backpack over his shoulder, and his face bore the marks of someone who had rushed back overnight.

His tall, muscular frame seemed to carry wind with every step. His exposed arms were riddled with bulging veins, radiating explosive strength.

His neck bore a silver adventurer's badge that jingled as it swayed, proudly displaying his identity.

This disheveled yet bold-looking man was surely the famous Rexrum star—fighter Karl.

At this moment, Karl wore an awkward yet polite smile, waving at the endless crowd of cheering residents.

"Thank you, thank you. You're all too kind..."

Karl's expression was somewhat helpless. He clearly wasn't good at handling such scenes, his smile and gestures stiff and unnatural.

Among the crowd, Merlin and Alice had no intention of approaching, but Karl's sharp eyes spotted them.

Though he didn't recognize Merlin, Karl did know Alice beside him—after all, Alice had joined the guild a while ago.

"Hey there~! Isn't that Alice?" Karl stopped in his tracks and walked straight over.

"Uh..." Alice, caught off guard by Karl's sudden approach, responded awkwardly, "Long time no see, Mr. Karl. You just got back?"

"That's right. I went all the way to Athens—far as hell, nearly died from exhaustion halfway there, haha!" Karl laughed heartily, his clean white teeth with dramatic lighting effects gleaming so brightly it looked like he could endorse toothpaste for Black people.

"This trip lasted really long. Was it because the mission difficulty was high?" Alice asked curiously. Compared to usual, Karl had been gone for quite some time.

"Mission difficulty wasn't that high. Just went and beat up a few rampaging fugitives." Karl scratched his head with a helpless smile.

"Then why did it take so long to come back?" Alice couldn't help but wonder.

"This... Karl's expression turned awkward, as if there was something hard to say, "I accidentally punched the wrong person. I unintentionally hit Athens' hero, Cardmos, and things got a little out of hand. Luckily, the Viscount Austin vouched for me, otherwise the Athens city lord might have kept dragging me around for every excuse under the sun."

"Eh?!" Alice's eyes widened as if she had heard something unbelievable.

"That Athens hero Cardmos wasn't exactly reasonable either. After drinking, he started going crazy and even came to provoke me. I couldn't stand it, so I knocked him out cold for seven days and seven nights, haha." Karl laughed cheerfully, clearly still amused by the memory.

Alice fell silent, a cold sweat dripping down her forehead. If she remembered correctly, that Cardmos was a famous warrior of the Greek Kingdom, said to have dragon-like swimming abilities. To think Karl had knocked him out for seven days and seven nights with a single punch—was he mocking the Greek warriors in some elaborate way?

Only now did Karl notice Merlin beside him, realizing he was a stranger. "This... gentleman..."

"Merlin. He just recently joined the guild." Alice introduced him.

"Oh really, a newcomer huh..." Karl stroked his stubble and bluntly said, "You don't look very strong. With that delicate face, I bet you're bound to make the girls jealous."

"Pfft~!" Alice burst into laughter beside him, feeling that Merlin was stuck with that effeminate label.

"Tch!"

Merlin frowned in annoyance. He hadn't planned on saying anything, but Karl's words had already rubbed him the wrong way.

Did he just say I don't look strong? Is he judging by appearances? If I went all out, I'd probably scare this old man half to death.

No wait, I'm over 200 years old. This guy in front of me is at most a recently weaned toddler.

Merlin's face darkened as he glared at Karl, clearly not pleased with his earlier dismissive remarks.

"Haha, you've got some complaints about me?" Karl seemed unfazed by Merlin's displeasure, instead patting Merlin's shoulder like an elder, "Little brother, don't take what I said to heart. Even if your strength isn't great, it doesn't matter. As long as you yearn for freedom in your heart, everyone is an adventurer. I refuse to end up like my old man—rigid and uptight. When it comes to living, the most important thing is to be happy."

...Merlin gave a crooked smile, his expression extremely stiff.

Karl looked down at Merlin's black iron adventurer's badge, intending to remember this new guild member, but then was shocked by another piece of information.

Spouse: Alice. Clodius.

He quickly checked Alice's golden adventurer's badge, which displayed similar information.

Spouse: Merlin. Lucifer.

Since Karl had just returned and was completely unaware that Alice and Merlin had married, this sudden discovery was hard to believe.

"Eh?!" Karl looked at Merlin, then turned to Alice, "I've only been gone this long, and I didn't expect Alice to have gotten married."

Merlin remained expressionless, at a loss for words.

Alice wore a helpless expression, saying nothing.

Both were in the state of not wanting to explain, because they were always misunderstood, and explaining seemed pointless anyway.

After all, they knew what was going on. Who cared about such boring things?

"Sheesh~ Did I come back this late? I missed the wedding entirely. I'm really sorry about that..." Karl said with a forced laugh, seeming genuinely apologetic.

Merlin's expression remained unchanged. He thought: A wedding? What's that? Can you eat it?

Alice rolled her eyes, thinking in her head: This is ridiculous. Who would marry a demon anyway? That's impossible.

"Well then, little brother..." Karl placed his hand on Merlin's shoulder, his expression serious and sincere, "You're totally giving off the vibe of living off your wife, you know that?"

Merlin's face flushed a deep red, his expression gradually darkening, and he blurted out a single word.

"Tch!"

(+~m7)

title: Chapter 12 — Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 12 — Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 12

"Little brother, this won't do. As a man, you must learn to strive for self-improvement, otherwise it's too easy for people to look down on you." Karl said earnestly, as if lecturing Merlin, completely ignoring the other man's ugly expression.

You couldn't really blame Karl for looking down on people. Anyone who saw Merlin and Alice's engagement would think Merlin was a gigolo. After all, the common impression of an Iron-ranked adventurer was someone who did nothing, living off welfare until they died.

In contrast, Alice was a young Gold-ranked adventurer with limitless potential, a respected anomaly.

Given such a stark difference in status, it was only natural to assume Merlin was a gigolo.

On top of that, Karl was a hot-headed man who, deep down, despised the likes of Merlin—a "pretty boy." So he couldn't help but criticize.

Alice stood beside them, stifling her laughter. She clearly had no intention of helping Merlin explain himself—she just enjoyed watching him suffer.

"You shouldn't always rely on a woman to support you. That's no way to live long-term. Do you really enjoy living without dignity?" Karl, a middle-aged man around the same age as Hobbes, spoke with more integrity than the latter.

"ATM..." Merlin's expression darkened, nearly blending into the shadows. It was clear how upset he was.

"Even if Alice doesn't seem to mind, you should still try harder. To be honest, I look down on gigolos like you." Karl's expression turned serious, then suddenly shifted. "I originally thought Alice would end up with Arnold. Sure, Arnold isn't much himself, but at least his father is decent."

Alice's expression darkened as well. *Who would ever date that idiot Arnold? Does he think I'd lower my standards?*

What Merlin hated most right now was the label "gigolo." The Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace, constantly mistaken for a gigolo—what kind of nonsense was this?!

Merlin felt he had to act tougher, otherwise he might really end up stuck with the "gigolo" reputation. That would be too humiliating.

"I'm not a gigolo. Please stop misunderstanding me, okay?"

"Alright, alright, I get it. I don't think you *want* to be a gigolo either. Maybe you're just doing it to survive. Even if you're weak, just an Iron-ranked adventurer, I still think people who work hard are cool!" Karl gave a thumbs-up, flashing his neat white teeth, leaving Merlin utterly confused.

*Damn it...* Merlin couldn't help but curse. Why wouldn't this guy listen to him? Was he too self-absorbed?

"Even if I don't approve of your love, I'll still give you my blessings. See you later!"

With a flourish, Karl waved his hand and strode away, his carefree demeanor as if he had just enlightened a lost young man.

Merlin and Alice's darkened expressions gradually returned to normal as they watched Karl leave. Both felt a mix of emotions.

Merlin: "Why doesn't this guy listen to me..."

Alice: "He's always been like that."

Merlin: "He seems like a simple-minded fool."

Alice: "Can't deny it. I think so too."

Merlin: "I really hate these self-righteous people."

Alice: "Me too."

Merlin: "Do I look like a gigolo to you?"

Merlin looked at Alice with a complicated expression, his eyes narrowing into slits.

Looks like another heated argument was brewing tonight...

---

Rexham Adventurers Guild.

At this hour, there weren't many people left. The Guild usually didn't accept commissions at night.

The receptionist, Lucia, was still in a daze. The feather pen in her hand spun ceaselessly, yet today's work hadn't progressed at all.

As Hobbes, the old drunk, had said, Lucia seemed to have developed a strong interest in Elgin the Great Swordsman, even harboring feelings of admiration and affection.

Her mind kept flashing with that mysterious name, wondering what Elgin the Great Swordsman looked like. Rumor had it he wasn't very old—maybe he was a good match for her?

Even Lucia herself felt she was in love. Liking a mysterious man whose name she didn't even know—it was a strange feeling.

You couldn't really blame Lucia for daydreaming. At her age, she naturally admired brilliant figures. And Elgin the Great Swordsman was so famous right now—so many girls liked him, so he must be an extraordinary man!

Lucia thought that if a man like Elgin the Great Swordsman were to date her, she could just about accept it.

As for why? Hobbes, that sly old fox, had already analyzed it perfectly. It basically matched Lucia's mindset.

Even if it made her seem a bit calculating, Lucia just wanted her other half to be the center of attention. That way, she would also bask in the spotlight.

What girl didn't dream of being a star, the focus of everyone's affection?

Lucia was no exception. She often fantasized about being a pampered princess, living under the dazzling limelight.

And the man who fit all of Lucia's expectations was none other than the currently red-hot Elgin the Great Swordsman—powerful, young, just, and worshipped by countless people.

On top of that, the air of mystery surrounding Elgin the Great Swordsman was intoxicating. That very mystery was what made him so alluring.

"Lucia, my precious daughter! Your dashing father is back!" Karl burst through the door with great fanfare, his face beaming, as if he wanted to surprise his daughter.

Lucia's spinning feather pen paused for just a moment. A flicker of joy passed over her face, but then the pen resumed its spinning.

She remained expressionless, staring blankly ahead, as if only half-interested.

"Oh, is that so? Welcome home."

Lucia's tone was cold, devoid of any emotion, as if she were just going through the motions. It was heartbreaking.

"Uh..."

Karl's enthusiastic expression froze on his face. Cold sweat beaded on his forehead. He had no idea what he had done to upset his daughter.

She was throwing such a fit the moment he walked in, putting him under immense pressure! He had no idea how to cheer her up!

Karl deflated like a punctured balloon, trudging over to Lucia with slumped shoulders before silently setting down his bag.

"My dear daughter, what's wrong? It's rare for your father to come home. Why are you so cold? Who made you angry? I'll go smash them until they can't take care of themselves!"

"Huh?" Lucia looked annoyed. "What's wrong with my attitude? That was a very warm welcome."

"I didn't feel even a hint of warmth from you... just pure disdain..." Karl pulled a long face, dejected.

"Even a background actor should put in a little effort at the crucial moment..."

title: Chapter 13 — Ordinary
content:
Chapter 13 — Ordinary

Volume 9 · Chapter 13

Lucia rolled her eyes so hard they nearly spun in their sockets, her face stretched into a skin-deep, joyless smile.

"Welcome home, Father. It’s so wonderful to finally see you again."

So fake. And dripping with insincerity.

Uncle Karl’s expression twisted into something complicated—he’d finally made it home, yet he wasn’t getting the welcome he’d hoped for.

"Tch, what a pain." Lucia turned her head away, her entire face screaming impatience.

Karl’s face paled. His heart sank. He tried to sweet-talk her. "Lucia, my precious little heart, who upset you? Tell Papa. I’ll make them pay!"

"Who else could it be but you?" Lucia said with perfect seriousness, her gaze sweeping over her father with open disdain.

"Huh?!" Karl scratched his head, bewildered. "I don’t remember doing anything to upset you."

"How could you not? You disappeared on a mission for so long—didn’t it occur to you to send a single letter home? Do you have any idea how worried Grandpa and I were? We thought you’d died out there!" Lucia’s eyes burned with anger, clearly still holding a grudge.

"Ah… that…" Karl faltered. Going completely off the grid *was* a bit much, even for him.

"Mom was right about you. You’re heartless. All you ever think about is fighting. You don’t care about your family at all. I hate that about you…" Lucia’s expression turned solemn, even tinged with sadness.

Karl bowed his head, his face suddenly stricken—Lucia had brought up his late wife.

His wife had passed away from a serious illness. Lucia had still been a child then, sensitive to everything around her.

At the time, Karl had been away on a mission, vanishing without a trace.

By the time he returned to Rexham, his wife had already been buried. He hadn’t even seen her one last time.

That had made young Lucia resent Karl deeply, convinced he had no sense of responsibility.

Even Karl himself was wracked with guilt, feeling like a terrible person for failing his wife and daughter.

Over time, their father-daughter relationship had only barely improved to the point where they could speak to each other.

Now, hearing it brought up again, Karl’s entire mood plummeted.

It was hard to imagine a burly man in his forties looking so utterly defeated, like a scolded child.

"I’m truly sorry. I didn’t mean to disappear. It’s just… I got tied up with some things in Athens. Otherwise, I would’ve checked in regularly."

"Got drunk, beat up a Greek Hero, and got arrested by the Lord of Athens. Had to have Count Austin bail you out…" Lucia sighed, exasperated. "Honestly, why do you always cause trouble everywhere you go? Don’t you realize how much hassle that creates for others? You’re not a kid anymore, yet you still act like this."

Karl’s face darkened. Being scolded by his daughter left him speechless, utterly humiliated. At least there was no one else around to witness it.

"Lucia, please… I know I’m an idiot. Can’t I just apologize?"

Lucia shot him a sidelong glance. Every time things got to this point, her father would suddenly look so pitiful that she couldn’t bring herself to stay mad.

"Fine~. Just be glad you made it back safe. That’s what matters most."

Karl lifted his head, his face lighting up with surprise. He felt forgiven. His precious daughter still loved him after all.

"Go see Grandpa at the dojo. Stop loitering here. I’ve got work to do." Lucia feigned impatience.

"Right, right." Karl stood up, realizing he should go see the old man.

"Then I won’t keep you any longer, my dear. I’ll go visit your grandfather now."

Old Taylor had been trying to figure out the source of Merlin’s immense power and his unique training methods lately.

But with Merlin’s carefree attitude toward life, Old Taylor realized he could never imitate it—if he tried, he’d just end up a lecherous old pervert.

After all, in Old Taylor’s eyes, Merlin might be strong, but on the surface, he came off as nothing more than a good-for-nothing freeloader who mooched meals, occasionally visited brothels, and had all the bearing of a lowly street thug. There was no trace of the dignity or mindset one would expect from a powerful figure. It was utterly baffling.

If Old Taylor hadn’t personally experienced a fraction of Merlin’s overwhelming strength, he’d probably dismiss Merlin as an unmotivated young man.

Yet the reality was the exact opposite, forcing Old Taylor to reconsider. Truly, one couldn’t judge a book by its cover. With power that immense, Merlin must have long since stopped caring about *appearing* strong.

After pondering Merlin’s strength for a long time, Old Taylor could only reach one conclusion:

Perhaps Merlin had seen through everything, living freely and indulging his every whim, achieving true liberation of the soul.

With such a transcendent mindset, how could his power *not* soar beyond ordinary limits? It was a realm no common person could ever reach.

Merlin had attained extraordinary strength with an ordinary body—no doubt he had his own unique philosophy on power.

Old Taylor sighed in admiration. His own understanding was still far below that of a young man like Merlin. It was shameful.

Of course, all of Old Taylor’s high-minded theorizing was completely off the mark. The real explanation for Merlin’s power could be summed up in three words: *cheat code protagonist.*

At the moment, Old Taylor had changed into loose training clothes and stood with his hands clasped behind his back in the center of the dojo.

He knew his son was returning today, and as per tradition, they would spar to see if his skills had improved.

BOOM—BOOM—◆

title: Chapter 14 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 14 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 9 · Chapter 14

Karl and Old Taylor’s relationship was hard for outsiders to understand—it was a bond of blood thicker than water, a father-son connection.

Yet in life, they were also rivals, constantly sparring and testing each other, which was a common sight.

To onlookers, it looked like they were beating each other half to death, but in truth, both always held back, stopping just short of real harm.

Uncle Karl had been stubborn and hot-headed since childhood, quick to throw punches at the slightest provocation. Coming home with a bruised face was practically routine for him.

Now in his forties, even after years of Old Taylor’s guidance, his temper hadn’t changed one bit—a testament to his unyielding nature.

But under Old Taylor’s mentorship, Karl hadn’t become a mindless brute. Instead, his strength had grown at an astonishing pace.

Slowly, the brawling street kid of Rexham had grown into the star adventurer of the city, the most beloved man in all of Rexham.

Old Taylor took immense pride in his son, though he’d never admit it aloud. His response was always the same dismissive remark: *"Too green."*

Uncle Karl, for his part, had always seen his father as the ultimate goal, the one he had to chase for the rest of his life. And so, he had worked tirelessly to this day.

Now, Karl’s strength was nearly on par with Old Taylor’s. He was no longer the reckless youth who could be pinned down with ease.

Karl thought his father was getting old, so he often called him *"Old Man"*—not as an insult, but as a way to spur him on, hoping he’d stay as vigorous as ever.

The two mocked each other, pushing each other forward. This strange dynamic had endured all these years.

Now, seeing Karl dismiss Merlin as useless, Old Taylor couldn’t help but find it amusing.

After all, Merlin was someone even *he* had to be wary of. His own son Karl probably wouldn’t stand a chance against him.

"You’ve got the wrong idea. That new kid, Merlin—his strength is extraordinary. He’s far from the useless waste you think he is."

Uncle Karl’s expression turned odd. He stared at Old Taylor’s serious face, confusion creeping into his mind.

*This Merlin… where on earth is he supposed to be impressive?*

From what he could tell, the guy was nothing but a freeloading, good-for-nothing bum.

So why was the Old Man calling him extraordinary? Praising him, even?

In all his years, he’d never once heard his father compliment anyone. And yet…

Uncle Karl felt a pang of discomfort. He needed to have a serious talk with Old Taylor about this.

"Old Man, you’re not senile yet, so cut the jokes. Do you really think I can’t tell if Merlin’s strong or not?"

"What you see is only the surface. You haven’t witnessed his true power. Judging someone based on first impressions is unfair. Many things can’t be understood without experiencing them firsthand. Our Taylor family’s Thunder Strike Martial Art isn’t the strongest, so never underestimate anyone."

Uncle Karl waved his hands. "Whoa, whoa, whoa—why are you suddenly so serious? That’s weird, even for you. Merlin’s *clearly* a piece of trash. I don’t sense a single ounce of magic or fighting spirit from him. Even his Adventurer’s Guild card says he’s a *useless villager*. And now you’re telling me he’s strong? How am I supposed to believe that?"

"I’ll admit, Merlin *looks* like a completely useless man. But if you let appearances deceive you, that’s your biggest mistake." Old Taylor’s tone was like a lecture, as if scolding Karl for still not knowing how to think at his age.

"Old Man, you’re talking nonsense. Merlin’s just a Black Iron adventurer. How could he possibly be strong? Even if you *are* getting old and muddled, there’s a limit—"

Uncle Karl sighed in exasperation. If a guy like Merlin could be considered strong, then the world had gone completely mad.

"Brat, why can’t you wrap your head around this? I’m not losing my mind—I’m telling you the truth. Merlin’s strength is the real deal. In fact, it might already surpass both you and me. Calling him the strongest adventurer in the Guild wouldn’t be an exaggeration."

Old Taylor paused, locking eyes with Karl before continuing. "As for him being ranked as a Black Iron adventurer… well, that’s unavoidable. Merlin seems to have no magic or fighting spirit, so he’s stuck at that level. But that doesn’t change the fact that he’s a powerhouse."

"Good lord…" Karl shook his head, a mix of disbelief and amusement on his face. "A guy with no magic or fighting spirit being called strong? That’s ridiculous. If people actually believe that, then this world’s gone insane."

"At first, I didn’t believe it either. But the facts were right in front of me—I had no choice but to admit that Merlin is an *exceptional* kind of strong. His power is far beyond that of a Black Iron adventurer. He’s at least Mithril rank."

Old Taylor had made a conservative estimate. Little did he know, even calling Merlin Mithril rank was still an understatement.

Originally, Uncle Karl hadn’t wanted to pay much attention to Merlin, the newbie. In his mind, the guy was nothing more than a freeloading bum.

But what he *couldn’t* stand was the idea of this good-for-nothing being seen as a powerhouse, receiving praise and admiration from others.

Especially not from his own father, Old Taylor—who had *never* praised *him* like that, yet was now showering Merlin with compliments.

Proud and stubborn, Karl couldn’t bear it. Why did his father admire a *bum* instead of *him*?

Uncle Karl took a deep breath, deciding not to argue with his father any longer. Instead, he spoke with firm resolve.

"Old Man, stop. No magic, no fighting spirit—*that* makes someone ordinary. That’s just how it is. And a strong man without any kind of presence? That’s just hype. There’s no such thing as an *exceptional* freak like that."

Old Taylor sighed. It seemed today, he’d have to put his old face on the line to make his son see reason. "I’m not calling Merlin strong without proof. When he first joined the Guild, I sparred with him… and I lost."

"What?!" Karl’s eyes widened in shock, his face a picture of disbelief.

"Granted, we weren’t going all-out—it was just a light sparring match. But if Merlin had been serious… I’d have been *completely* destroyed. That sword draw of his… it could cleave the earth in two. A single swing, and the very heavens seemed to tremble." Old Taylor’s expression was grave as he recalled the sight of Merlin cutting through all of Rexham. If Merlin hadn’t held back, Old Taylor might have been killed on the spot.

"...You’re telling the truth?" Karl could barely believe his own ears.

"I have no reason to lie." Old Taylor replied flatly.

"...Hmph."

Uncle Karl fell into a daze, his expression shifting unpredictably.

Old Man was already stronger than him, and now he was admitting defeat to *Merlin*?!

Was that seemingly useless bum, Merlin, actually *stronger* than Old Man?!

Impossible! Old Man was a pillar of Britannia’s martial world. There weren’t many who could match him.

Karl refused to accept it. Deep down, he couldn’t bring himself to believe that this newcomer, Merlin, was truly that strong.

He had spent his whole life chasing his father’s shadow, seeing him as the most worthy rival. He had endured countless hardships to reach where he was today.

And now, some pretty-faced young man comes along and *easily* defeats his father? Who could accept that?

Uncle Karl clenched his fists, then suddenly lifted his head, his eyes flashing with golden lightning, his fighting spirit surging.

...

"I’m going to spar with that newbie, Merlin."

"Whether he’s truly strong or not—I’ll find out for myself."

(≧ω≦)

title: Chapter 15 — Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 15 — Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 15

The next day, early in the morning.

Even though Merlin and Alice had an on-and-off relationship, cultivation was still a serious matter.
