So, despite the heated argument at home the day before, Merlin still accompanied Alice to the training hall early in the morning.

"No... don't you dare 'accidentally' hit me..." Alice turned her head, worried.

"Tch!" Merlin rolled his eyes and gave an unsettling smile. "Relax~ I've been handling a blade for years. How could I keep making such low-level mistakes?"

"I still feel like you're up to no good..." Alice muttered suspiciously, recalling last night's shouting match. Maybe Merlin was holding a grudge and planning to get back at her.

"Fine, then I'm leaving." Merlin turned and walked away without hesitation.

"Wait, don't! I was just joking!" Alice grabbed Merlin and stopped him from going home.

"Hmph." Merlin twisted his mouth and gave a cold snort before continuing to accompany Alice.

"Honestly, such a petty man. No wonder you've been single for over 200 years..." Alice huffed in frustration.

Merlin's expression turned complicated. *What's wrong with being single for 200 years? It's not like it affects anyone else. Why is this even a point of criticism?*

The two were locked in their little mind games, enjoying the back-and-forth, when they spotted Arnold standing at the guild entrance, holding a rose.

"Ah..."

Merlin slightly opened his mouth, expression blank. He didn't even have the energy to mock the situation anymore. How many times had Arnold pestered Alice like this? A fine noble son, now reduced to Alice's persistent shadow, impossible to shake off.

Every day, he drowned himself in delusions, hoping for a grand, passionate romance with a flat-chested girl. There were plenty of well-endowed beauties out there—why fixate on Alice, a lost cause?

Diversify, think long-term—that was basic common sense, yet Arnold didn't seem to grasp it.

Merlin felt sorry for Arnold. If it were him, Alice would have been kicked out of the solar system long ago.

"Another one of your obsessed admirers. How romantic, hehehe~"

"I'm going to punch you to death!" Alice raised her tiny pink fist, seething with rage.

She could feel Merlin had no intention of helping her resolve this annoyance, and was even mocking her. It was infuriating.

Technically, Merlin was her nominal husband, right? Yet he showed no willingness to help at all.

This made Alice sulk. She got upset when Merlin flirted with others, but when she was the one being pursued, Merlin didn’t show the slightest concern or jealousy.

It was unbalanced. Did Merlin not have a single impure thought about her because she was flat?!

Arnold was dressed casually today—spotless white undershirt, naturally curly blue hair tied back. He held a vibrant rose glistening with morning dew, standing at the guild entrance with a self-satisfied expression, lost in fantasies of confessing to Alice.

His relentless persistence was admirable, but his constant harassment was just annoying.

How many times had Alice rejected him already? Yet this guy had the resilience of a cockroach—impossible to kill.

Arnold seemed to notice Merlin and Alice. He straightened his back, like a peacock courting, and approached Alice.

He didn’t mind Merlin’s presence. After all, he knew they were a fake couple, so pursuing her was fine.

"Good morning, Miss Alice. Another beautiful day, isn’t it~"

Arnold performed a noble bow and presented the rose to Alice, instantly switching into dazzling mode, making her scalp tingle.

"This is a rose I prepared early this morning. Please accept it, Miss Alice. Though it’s just an ordinary rose, it carries my most sincere affection."

Alice’s beautiful face froze. She instinctively took a step back, trembling all over, as if Arnold’s cringeworthy words had given her goosebumps.

Merlin watched Arnold with a complex expression. *Couldn’t this guy just act normal? If he spoke properly, maybe he’d have a chance. Who gave him such terrible advice?*

In a shoujo manga, this might be charming, but in reality, it was just awkward and nauseating.

Of course, all of this was the fault of Arnold’s self-proclaimed "love guru" little sister. If not for her constantly feeding him bad ideas, Arnold might still be a normal person.

"Arnold, can you stop harassing me already?" Alice’s expression was wooden. Endless harassment had pushed her to the brink of biological despair. "I’ve seriously told you countless times—it’s impossible between us. Please, just give up. I’m begging you, is that not enough?"

"Love is born from relentless pursuit. If you’re begging me to stop, that just proves I’m close to success." Arnold smiled confidently. "There’s no need to hide your true feelings. If you’ve fallen for me, just express it boldly. I’ll respond enthusiastically."

Alice forced a stiff smile. "Do you realize you’re making things worse? Stalking someone won’t get you anywhere. It just makes you more annoying."

"How could that be? All women appreciate a loyal partner. My persistent pursuit and constant declarations of love—even if you have a heart of stone, you must feel at least a little moved, right?" Arnold’s eyes sparkled with excitement.

"Who taught you this nonsense?" Alice’s face darkened, trembling with rage. She refused to believe Arnold’s low emotional intelligence could come up with such ridiculous tactics.

"Of course, my adorable little sister." Arnold practically glowed with pride.

Merlin facepalmed. *With a sister like that, it’d be better to cut ties as soon as possible...*

Alice’s expression remained blank as she took the rose from Arnold’s hand and threw it straight into the nearby trash can. Her face twisted in disgust.

"GUN!!!"

---

Training hall.

The two didn’t waste time and chose to focus on their cultivation.

Dealing with Arnold, that cockroach, was just a waste of their precious lives.

Merlin and Alice stood facing each other, seemingly preparing to spar.

Alice slowly drew her slender sword, channeling her high-tier magic and fighting spirit.

Her mood was still sour—Arnold had ruined her morning.

"Hey, hey, you’ve got a devoted admirer now. Shouldn’t you be happy?" Merlin stood across from her, speaking casually, his teasing tone clearly at Alice’s expense.

"Shut up! Wait until some creep starts stalking you every day—then you’ll know how disgusting it is!" Alice glared at Merlin, furious. This bastard had no idea what he was talking about.

Just as Merlin and Alice were chatting, Uncle Karl entered the training hall in casual clothes.

"Good morning, you two. Training already? How diligent..."

"Mr. Karl?!" Alice was startled and lowered her sword. She hadn’t expected Karl to show up at a time like this.

"Sorry to interrupt you. Heh..." Uncle Karl scratched his head awkwardly.

"Do you need something from me?" Alice asked, confused. Interrupting someone’s training was rude.

"Sorry, Alice, I’m not here for you..." Uncle Karl glanced at the indifferent Merlin, his tone meaningful. "I actually came specifically to spar with this young man, Merlin."

title: Chapter 16 — Enough
content:
Chapter 16 — Enough

Volume 9 · Chapter 16

Merlin heard Uncle Karl’s words and slightly lifted his eyelids, finding it somewhat interesting. He never refused someone who took the initiative to challenge him.

"A sparring match?"

Alice widened her eyes, looking at Uncle Karl, then at Merlin, whose face remained expressionless. She found the whole situation unbelievable.

She had assumed Karl was just passing by to take a look, never expecting him to actually challenge Merlin to a sparring match!

As far as Alice knew, Karl was hailed as the strongest adventurer in the guild, his strength seemingly on par with the old guildmaster.

Yet this radiant, middle-aged man in his forties had never taken the initiative to challenge anyone before. And Merlin had only recently joined the guild—he was still considered a newcomer.

Uncle Karl was usually very considerate toward newcomers and got along with them easily. But now, he was actually taking the initiative to challenge someone, as if deliberately making things difficult for the new guy.

Alice’s heart was filled with doubt and confusion. She couldn’t figure out what Karl was trying to do. Had Merlin somehow offended him? Why else would he insist on sparring with him?

"Mr. Karl, why do you want to spar with Merlin? Is there some misunderstanding?"

"Alice, don’t overthink it. There’s no misunderstanding. I just want to have a friendly sparring match with young Merlin here to get to know each other better. After all, Merlin is a new member of the guild. Sparring to understand each other is perfectly normal. I’m not good with words, so communicating with fists is the most sincere way."

Karl said this earnestly, grinning with a toothy smile that made him seem even more approachable.

But even though Karl spoke in a friendly manner, his true intentions were obvious. His strong battle lust was clear—he wanted to see if Merlin was truly a powerhouse stronger than his own father.

"But..."

Alice hesitated. It wasn’t that she was worried about Merlin—she had seen firsthand just how strong this cheat of a man was.

She was more concerned about Mr. Karl’s safety. If Merlin accidentally slipped up, the guildmaster’s son might end up dead on the spot!

She was familiar with Merlin and knew he could hold back, but Karl had come in with such an aggressive attitude. Merlin probably wouldn’t go easy on him just because of that.

Alice glanced at Merlin, who showed no reaction, and offered a well-meaning warning.

"Mr. Karl, I advise you to drop this idea. Don’t just casually challenge Merlin to a sparring match."

"Hah... Uncle Karl let out a hearty laugh, glanced at Alice, and said, "Relax, I won’t break your little sweetheart. This is just a light sparring match, nothing serious."

"That’s not the issue!" Alice’s face flushed red in an instant. *Who’s worried about Merlin getting hurt? I’ve never even seen him injured!* And what *little sweetheart*? That sounds terrible!

"I understand." Uncle Karl waved his hand dismissively, stepped forward, and said, "I’m just borrowing your little sweetheart for a while. It’s not like I won’t give him back. Don’t be so stingy~"

"This isn’t about being stingy!" Alice’s face burned with embarrassment. The phrase *little sweetheart* was just too awkward.

Ignoring the flustered and exasperated Alice, Karl turned to Merlin and asked, "What do you say, young man? Care to spar with me?"

"Oh?" Merlin crossed his arms and asked with a hint of confusion, "Why must I spar with you?"

"At first, I thought you were some weak, useless bum who joined the Adventurers Guild just to freeload until death. But it seems that’s not the case..."

Uncle Karl paused, a slightly displeased smile appearing on his face before he continued, "Yesterday, I was talking with my old man about you. He said you were incredibly strong and couldn’t stop praising you. So I thought I’d come see for myself—are you really that outstanding?"

Alice shot Karl a complicated look. *He’s challenging Merlin just for that reason?*

"The old guildmaster is right. I *am* pretty amazing," Merlin said with a smile, spreading his hands. Then, with heavy sarcasm, he added, "But I’m not interested in sparring with you. Someone at your level isn’t enough to get me excited. I can’t even be bothered."

"Oh ho~" Uncle Karl’s smile froze on his face. In a mocking tone, he said, "Nowadays, the younger generation sure has a temper, one bigger than the next. They don’t understand the rules at all. Our guild may not be some grand guild overflowing with powerhouses, but it’s not the kind of place where people can just look down on us."

"Sorry, I’m just stating the facts. I’m not looking down on the entire guild. As for your sparring request—allow me to decline." Merlin had no interest in exchanging blows with Uncle Karl. He saw no point in it.

"Fine, I’m not an unreasonable man," Karl sighed, turning to leave. But then he looked back and added, "Though it seems you really *are* a useless bum with no dreams, just coasting through life day by day... Oh, and a freeloading gigolo at that. How pathetic."

*Tsk.*

Merlin clicked his tongue in displeasure, a vein throbbing on his forehead. He was *not* happy with the "freeloading gigolo" remark.

*Have I been too lenient lately? How dare everyone call me a gigolo?*

This kind of bad habit couldn’t be allowed to continue. It was time to show these ants what real power looked like.

Seeing that Uncle Karl was about to leave, Merlin finally spoke up, calling out to him.

"Hm? Something on your mind?" Uncle Karl put on an innocent face, thinking to himself, *Sure enough, the young ones can’t resist a little reverse psychology.*

"Your attempt at goading me was pretty clumsy, but congratulations—it worked, to an extent." Merlin, expressionless, clapped his hands once. "I accept your sparring match. But if you get hurt, I’m not taking responsibility."

"Wha—?!" Alice stared at Merlin, thinking, *He accepted just like that?* Was the "freeloading gigolo" comment *that* damaging to him? Normally, he wouldn’t even budge when provoked!

Uncle Karl let out a dry chuckle, his smile now tinged with seriousness. "For someone so young, you’ve got quite the mouth on you. Fists don’t have eyes—if you get hurt, you’ve got no one to blame but yourself."

Merlin gave a faint smile but said nothing. Instead, he walked off to the side, seemingly to fetch something.

Uncle Karl got what he wanted and grinned, clearly planning to give this newcomer, Merlin, a proper lesson.

He refused to accept that Merlin, so young, could possess strength surpassing even his father’s. That was just unnatural.

And the fact that his own father, usually so stingy with praise, had heaped nothing but compliments on Merlin only made Karl, a man in his forties, feel even more unbalanced.

Merlin returned with a wooden sword, swinging it a couple of times to get a feel for it before saying indifferently, "Alright, this’ll do."

Uncle Karl looked at the wooden sword in Merlin’s hands—the kind commonly found in any dojo—and frowned. "Why use a wooden sword instead of the real blade at your waist? Are you looking down on me?"

"It’s not that I’m looking down on you," Merlin raised the wooden sword, pointing it at Karl, and smirked as he said,

"For someone at your level, this wooden sword is more than enough."

title: Chapter 17 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 17 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 9 · Chapter 17

Here's a translation that follows all the rules:

Looking at Merlin's outrageous appearance, Alice had a blank expression; she was already used to him being like this.

Perhaps Merlin wasn't intentionally doing this, but at times like this, he would always give off a disdainful feeling, filled with mockery and arrogance.

Normal people would definitely be unhappy after seeing this; their first reaction would be to rush forward and beat Merlin senseless.

However, Merlin had said that his strength had nothing to do with his weapon; meaning, whatever weapon he uses is fine!

Alice looked at Karl; she saw his thick smile stiffen on his face, and the veins on his arm twitching continuously.

See? Sure enough, he was provoked by this guy, !

I told you, if Merlin wasn't strong, he would have been beaten to death by countless people already...

A subtle worry lingered in Alice's heart; she hoped Karl wouldn't take it too seriously. If Merlin messed up, he'd probably lose his job, after all.

Karl the uncle was a bit angry; he thought sparring was supposed to be based on fair conditions, which was only proper.

But Merlin didn't use the real sword at his waist; instead, he used a ordinary wooden sword against himself. Wasn't this clearly looking down on people?

Although I wouldn't dare claim to be the strongest fighter in the empire, I'm still among the best; the guild's strongest adventurer.

But now, being looked down upon by a newcomer like this? The strong sense of disparity—how could it not make someone angry?

Karl put away his smile, revealing a serious expression; obviously, he had no more patience for this newcomer's various discourtesies.

"I think you'd better use the real sword at your waist; that would seem more fair."

"Don't get me wrong, what weapon I use makes no difference; there's no real difference. Actually, I quite like the wooden sword because it feels comfortable in my hand." Merlin waved the wooden sword in his hand, feeling quite good.

"What a brazen young man. If I defeat you, won't you use this wooden sword as an excuse? Saying you didn't give it your all or something?" Karl preemptively said harsh things, while also blocking Merlin's retreat.

"I had no intention of using my full strength, nor did I think of making any excuses, because in my eyes, you're impossible to defeat." Merlin set down the wooden sword, beckoning at Karl the uncle, provokingly saying, "Attack to your heart's content, let me see just what kind of ability the guild's strongest actually has."

Karl's eyes changed; his temperamental self was already unable to bear the impulse to beat up Merlin.

A newcomer can be arrogant, but there needs to be a limit; going too far is disrespectful to a person.

This was the first time Karl had seen Merlin act like this—a newcomer with absolutely no respect for a senior; one could say he was completely without regard for others.

So Karl had no intention of holding back; he wanted to teach this young man who had no idea how high the sky is a lesson. If Merlin didn't have the capital to be arrogant, it wouldn't be unreasonable for him to lie in bed for a few months.

Golden battle aura suddenly exploded from Karl the uncle, and under the crackling sounds, it slowly formed a thunder armor. Electric current continuously surged around his body, as if a fierce beast was attached to him, awe-inspiring!

...

Alice paused her breathing; she was clearly shocked by this scene, wondering if this was the Thunder Fighting Technique of the Taylor family?

Extremely fast action ability, and outstanding attack power. Almost all power was concentrated on attack.

Even the legendary beastman king could go head-to-head with it, showing how terrifying his actual combat ability was!

They say that before the enemy even realizes what's happening, they'll be knocked down by the fierce continuous attacks of the Thunder Fighting Technique, with no chance to catch their breath!

Alice felt this kind of enemy was very tricky; fast speed, high attack power. If she was slightly distracted, she'd definitely be completely defeated, Merlin.

Merlin had a blank face; his eyebrows didn't even jump once. It seemed he felt no pressure at all.

Ah~, Merlin really is still this dead face; even at this kind of time he can space out...

Alice was already speechless about Merlin; at the very least, be serious and give due respect to your opponent!

"You newcomer, you'd better be serious, otherwise you might receive heavier...."

Just as the words fell, Karl's severe electric light flashed; his whole body like a golden meteor rushed out.

Because of Karl's powerful speed, the air around him all shook, as if a storm was created out of thin air!

Alice had to cover her eyes, being pushed back a step, wondering, what kind of power is this?! Just at the start, it's so fierce? !

"Interesting~" Merlin tilted his mouth, revealing a few points of mocking smile. Speed decides the winner? What a coincidence. His speed isn't slow either.

Karl, who was suddenly attacking, wanted to catch Merlin off guard. If he killed him in one blow, it would prove that his father was really old and confused.

Karl didn't hold back; a windmill-like kick kicked past, targeting Merlin's head!

Under normal circumstances, an ordinary person's head would be directly kicked open, and an opponent of the same level would also fall into a paralyzed state.

Speak of the devil, and the devil appears—

Karl's attack arrived at Merlin's front in the blink of an eye; this speed was so fast it made people want to slap their thighs in admiration!

Golden electric light surrounded him; Karl's killing move was about to land, but Merlin remained calm under pressure, lightly crouching down, easily dodging the attack with a posture similar to dodging bullets from The Matrix.

Karl's expression was slightly startled, thinking that his speed was so fast, yet he could still avoid it?! A guy with such reaction ability is certainly not an ordinary person!

Karl didn't hesitate much; turning his fist, which was as brilliant as a meteor, slammed out, densely packed punches flying toward Merlin. Golden battle aura turned into electricity dancing during the process.

"Oh? Not bad fist speed, but still too slow, little one."

Merlin's figure was like a ghost, dodging with even faster speed, leaving behind blurred afterimages.

Densely packed fists, almost all brushed past the edge, actually didn't hit Merlin at all?! ?

Karl finally felt Merlin was a bit frightening; his fists actually couldn't touch Merlin, showing that the opponent's speed crushed him! ?

And almost all were brushing past empty, like this new person was teasing himself, full of malicious taste.

The Thunder Fighting Technique is indeed a swift martial art; using speed alone could make the Taylor family famous as a martial arts family.

But today he met a demon-like young man; without using battle aura, using only physical speed, he crushed Karl's proud Thunder Fighting Technique?! ?

It's simply having dignity thrown on the ground, then mercilessly stomped on by feet.

From Alice's side view, it was even more bizarre, because both Karl and Merlin were using speed to duel.

This caused Alice, at this level of player, to simply not be able to see what was going on; she could only see the two's afterimages in the air, wildly colliding, sometimes sparking electricity and fire!

Alice had a large writ of blankness; her lips moved but couldn't say a word, being frightened by the fight between the two people.

She watched with her eyes the two afterimages leaping and jumping, her delicate body involuntarily trembling.

"Is this really what was said about gods fighting?"

title: Chapter 18 — Brute
content:
Chapter 18 — Brute

Volume 9 · Chapter 18

Watching the afterimages of the two clashing violently in the training hall left Alice completely stunned.

Their speed was so incredible that Alice’s eyes couldn’t keep up with the details—she could barely follow their movements at all.

As expected of the Thunderclap Close Combat Style, renowned for its ferocity. The relentless attacks came without the slightest hesitation—one wave had barely passed before another surged forward!

The lightning-fast strikes left no room for the enemy to breathe, capable of crushing them in the briefest moment of shock, like a thunderous suppression.

Though Uncle Karl was undeniably powerful, unfortunately, he had met someone even stronger—Merlin, a cheat of a man who played by no rules at all!

If Uncle Karl wanted to defeat Merlin, he’d need power beyond even a cheat code. Otherwise, he wouldn’t stand a chance.

A cold sweat trickled down Alice’s forehead as she thought: *If I were the one sparring with Uncle Karl, I’d probably lose instantly without a single chance to fight back!*

The Thunder Armor surged wildly around Karl, as if endlessly unlocking his potential.

Saint-tier Battle Qi raged around him, whipping up a gale sharp enough to cut, making it impossible to approach!

Karl’s fists flew out repeatedly, crackling with golden lightning, so fast they were nearly invisible.

The *crackle-pop* of impacts rang out ceaselessly. The dense, overlapping afterimages of his fists were like a human Gatling gun—*rat-tat-tat*—without pause!

*Why?!*

*Why can’t I hit this guy?!*

This was absurd! His fists were faster than sound, yet he couldn’t even graze a single hair on this man’s head!

What the hell?! This was the first time he’d ever encountered an opponent like this—someone who looked young but had power at this level.

Even without using Battle Qi, relying purely on physical strength, he could overpower me… That was… kind of terrifying…

Karl’s expression turned grave, beads of sweat forming on his forehead. His usual smile had vanished completely.

He frantically tried to deduce the source of Merlin’s strength, unaware that this guy was simply a freak with no magic or Battle Qi.

Merlin’s form flickered, effortlessly evading Karl’s crushing fists. With an unimaginable speed, he adjusted his position, rendering every attack useless.

“What’s wrong, old man? Tired? Your fists don’t seem as fast as before. As expected, your family’s martial arts aren’t suited for endurance battles. If you don’t finish the opponent quickly, you’ll end up on the defensive.”

Merlin’s lips curled into a disdainful smirk. He even had the leisure to taunt Karl, clearly not taking the sparring seriously—just toying with him.

But it seemed Merlin had grown tired of playing. He swung his wooden sword, easily deflecting both of Karl’s fists.

With practiced ease, he twirled the wooden sword around his wrist before viciously striking Karl’s joints, disabling his ability to fight!

The entire counterattack happened in the blink of an eye—no hesitation, no delay!

Karl gasped in pain, quickly retreating to put distance between himself and Merlin.

His arms hung limp, numb and trembling slightly. He wouldn’t be able to use them for a while.

Karl stared at Merlin in shock, realizing that unless he used his true abilities, he wouldn’t be able to subdue this newcomer.

Even though Karl had a vague sense that Merlin’s strength was on par with his own, he still refused to accept it.

“Satisfied now?” Merlin slung the wooden sword over his shoulder, saying indifferently, “Everyone says I’m not a kept man. Looks like using fists to settle things is the only way people will believe it.”

“…Yeah.” Karl clenched his fists, letting his Saint-tier Battle Qi surge as he tried to quickly recover his arms. “Now I admit you’re not a kept man. You’re someone with extraordinary power, worthy of being the father of such a strong son. No wonder Alice didn’t choose Arnold but instead chose to be with you. Even if it seems like she’s settling, it’s still the smarter choice.”

“Hey! Uncle Karl, that’s not what you said earlier!” Alice’s eyes widened, feeling like Karl had flipped his stance too fast. She’d been randomly slandered!

“Then that’s that.”

Merlin lowered the wooden sword from his shoulder, saying casually, “I’m not interested in sparring with you any longer. Just remember not to call me a kept man again.”

“Wait!” Karl suddenly stopped Merlin, his expression serious. “The sparring isn’t over yet. Let’s continue.”

“Uh… Uncle Karl, isn’t this going too far?!” Alice tried to intervene, worried that Karl was now determined to fight Merlin to the death.

“It’s fine. Seeing things through to the end is a good habit.” Karl dismissed her with a wave.

“You won’t stop until one of us falls, will you?” Merlin frowned slightly, looking impatient.

“That’s right. This is my request. Please indulge me.” Karl’s expression was solemn, his face filled with determination.

“Fine. I’ll make you lose your fighting ability in an instant. Come at me with everything you’ve got.” Merlin sighed, holding his wooden sword across his chest.

Karl’s expression darkened. He decided to use his true strength. Otherwise, his title as the strongest adventurer in the guild would be meaningless.

“Thunderclap Close Combat Style: Tiger Form!”

A sudden surge of golden Battle Qi enveloped Karl, forming a majestic golden tiger, vivid and lifelike, crackling with golden lightning.

The tiger-shaped Qi wrapped around Karl, transforming him in an instant into a ferocious beast. His veins bulged, as if containing explosive power!

The Qi tiger’s eyes were fierce, its low growls menacing and constant, baring its fangs at Merlin in a display of sheer aggression.

“Uh…” Alice’s face paled. *Was this still just sparring? This looked like he was dead serious!*

“HAAAH!”

With a roar, Karl charged forward. The tiger’s howl whipped up a fierce wind, nearly knocking Alice off her feet!

The Thunderclap Close Combat Style wasn’t just known for its speed—it also had the Mimicry ability, allowing the user to take the form of various birds and beasts, granting them the combat traits of a wild animal.

When Mimicry was activated, combat power multiplied, and with the beast-like fighting style, it often left enemies at a complete loss.

Golden lightning coiled around Karl, making him seem like a true, majestic tiger. As he charged at Merlin, it was like a tiger descending upon its prey—unstoppable!

This was his most skilled technique, one that had defeated countless enemies.

He was a different man now compared to before. With the speed of a tiger, he could crush his foes!

Rookie, watch closely. There’s a reason I’m called the strongest adventurer in the guild.

In the blink of an eye, Karl was in front of Merlin, his speed several times faster than before!

“Oh? Not bad—” Merlin barely lifted his eyelids.

Now, Merlin faced a ferocious, roaring lightning tiger, ready to tear him apart.

Karl shaped his hands into tiger claws and lunged at Merlin with all his might, holding nothing back!

A normal person wouldn’t have been able to react to such a swift attack. But Merlin was a cheat of a man!

Merlin raised his wooden sword, lightning-fast, and blocked Karl’s claws, effortlessly withstanding the brutal strike!

For a moment, lightning and storm winds intertwined, exploding outward from the point of impact, forcing Alice to squint.

Karl’s expression turned to shock. No matter how much force he applied, he couldn’t budge Merlin’s wooden sword even a little. *How was this possible?! This was his full-power strike! And yet it was blocked so easily?! Were his eyes playing tricks on him? Did this Merlin not only have insane speed but also unmatched strength?!*

Merlin lifted his head, speaking indifferently as he pushed Karl back, swinging his wooden sword with practiced ease.

With a reverse strike, he smashed the wooden sword against Karl’s head, knocking him unconscious.

Karl collapsed with a *thud*, falling into a deep slumber. He probably hadn’t even seen how he’d been taken down.

Merlin raised his wooden sword, tapping it lightly against his shoulder. He looked down at Karl and sighed.

“Tsk. A brute. What’s the point of all those flashy tricks?”

title: Chapter 19 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 19 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 9 · Chapter 19

Alice's expression was blank as she stared at Uncle Karl lying motionless on the floor.

Just a moment ago, he had been charging in with divine fury, hacking down gods and cutting down Buddhas.

But in the next instant, he was knocked out cold by Merlin's staff.

As expected, there's still a considerable gap between Karl's strength and Merlin's. Even putting pressure on him is difficult.

Just now, Uncle Karl was already being serious, yet Merlin casually knocked him out. Their combat power isn't even on the same level!

And Merlin wasn't even getting serious—he didn't even use his face-drawing sword technique. It was like he was beating up a little kid...

"Staring..."

Alice gave Merlin a strange look, wanting to say he was being a bit too disrespectful.

"What kind of look is that? We're sparring fairly, yet you have complaints with me?" Merlin narrowed his eyes and said with annoyance.

"Hmph!" Alice pouted and said seriously, "You're hitting a bit too hard."

"This is considered hard? Come on, I've held back a lot already. What more do you want?" Merlin sighed, putting down the wooden sword in his hand. "Besides, this guy himself came to challenge me, right? If I hold back too much, someone who admires martial arts won't be satisfied."

"..." Alice frowned slightly, speechless. She thought about how Karl usually admired martial arts and was a righteous person.

Book S, victory granted by charity might be the greatest restraint for him. SE novel.

"What should we do next?" Merlin looked down at the unconscious Karl.

"Emmmm..." Alice thought for a moment and said seriously.

"Maybe we should send Karl back home..."

Time passed quickly.

It was evening.

People were leaving the Adventurers Guild, but there were still quite a few people drinking.

The guild was like this—on one hand it was a platform for accepting quests, on the other hand it served as a tavern.

After sending the unconscious Karl back, Alice and Merlin spent the whole day training in the dojo.

It was already getting late, but the two of them still hadn't come out.

However, at this time, the guild received an unexpected visitor who seemed quite unfamiliar.

She wore a magnificent puffy dress, looking like a little princess.

Her blue hair was cut to her shoulders and swayed gently, with a white hairpin on her head adding a touch of cuteness.

The girl's eyebrows carried an air of nobility, her mouth pouted so high it looked like someone had upset her.

Behind her, two maids followed respectfully. From this entourage, it was clear she was the daughter of some wealthy family.

That's right! This girl is Jenna Gillian Austin, the beloved daughter of the Austin family, and Arnold's younger sister.

According to rumors, she is a "Love Information Master" and the president of the "Elkin Great Swordsman Rekku Support Association." But in reality, she seems to be just a proud romantic girl.

She's never been in a relationship, yet she gives others dating advice based on her own imagination from reading girls' novels. She's caused her own brother no end of trouble—truly the epitome of a useless sibling!

As for being the president of the Elkin Great Swordsman Support Association?

Actually, Jenna doesn't even know who Elkin the Great Swordsman is. But at her age, she often fantasizes about her own prince charming.

Who doesn't hope their prince charming is a powerful and good-hearted man?

So young Jenna instantly fell for this mysterious man, imagining all sorts of things, and soon declared herself the president of the support association, gaining quite a following.

Today, Jenna didn't come for anything else—she came to speak up for her incompetent brother.

Because early this morning, Arnold came home crying and locked himself in his room.

After asking carefully, Jenna found out that he had been rejected by a woman named Alice!

She was very angry, feeling that her brother was useless, and also felt that Alice was ungrateful.

The Austin family is a prestigious noble family in Rekku, famous and respected. Countless commoner girls throw themselves at them, eager to marry in.

Yet this Alice is different—her brother confessed multiple times but was rejected each time. That seems a bit much, doesn't it?

There are many girls pursuing her brother, so there's someone for every taste. He's clearly in demand.

But this Alice doesn't even look at her brother? What's going on? How can a commoner girl have such high standards?

Jenna admits her brother is a bit useless, but he's not so pitiful as to be rejected repeatedly.

So Jenna isn't convinced. Today she specifically came to confront Alice, demanding an explanation.

Moreover, Jenna doesn't understand what kind of personality Alice has. When she gives advice to others, it usually works out well.

But when she gave advice to her brother, not only did it fail to help him achieve his goal, it kept hitting roadblocks with Alice!

If this continues, Jenna feels her title as a love master is in jeopardy, which would damage her status in Rekku.

The Austin family's daughter entered the guild, drawing the interest of many chatting adventurers.

After all, Jenna is somewhat famous in Rekku, so naturally many people recognized her.

"What's this place? This is where my brother works? It's so shabby, looks like a stable..."

Jenna pressed her waist and surveyed the area, finding it fresh and new since she had never been here before.

"Miss, this is the Adventurers Guild, not a stable." One of the maids quietly reminded her.

"Yes, miss. Lord Austin is friends with President Taylor, so please don't say such unpleasant things here." The other maid chimed in.

"Ahem!" Jenna coughed lightly, her face turning embarrassed. "I know, no need to remind me."

Lilith was busy working when she saw Jenna arrive, so she quickly came out from behind the counter to greet her.

"Hey there~! Isn't this our Love Master Miss Jenna? What brings you here today?"

Jenna looked up at Lilith, catching a whiff of scheming, and said, "I have something to take care of here."

"Looking for Arnold? He came by in the morning and left soon after." Lilith assumed Jenna was there to find her brother.

"Who's looking for that useless brother of mine?!" Jenna's expression soured as she said seriously, "I'm not here for him."

"Who then? If it's convenient, I'd be happy to help." Lilith said enthusiastically.

"It's the girl my brother has been pursuing—Alice Clovis. I want to see her now." Jenna's tone carried a hint of irritation.

"Looking for Alice? She's training in the dojo. I wonder what business you have with her?" Lilith sensed Jenna was in a bad mood and wondered what she wanted with Alice.

"I want to talk to her about my brother's matter. Why does she keep rejecting my brother's sincere confessions?!" Jenna pressed her waist and complained,

"Is my brother not charming enough, or does Alice have too high standards?

(.--.)

title: Chapter 20 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 20 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 20

Lucia’s expression turned awkward. *So she’s here to demand an explanation?*

It’s just Arnold getting rejected over and over—what’s the big deal?

If it were up to her, she wouldn’t even give Arnold a second glance. The guy had the emotional intelligence of a rock.

Poor Alice, getting harassed by that dimwitted landowner’s son. Pfft~

Lucia found it amusing but kept her composure, maintaining an awkward yet polite smile.

“Why does Alice reject my brother? He’s done so much for her! He buys the freshest roses from the flower shop every day, and he even works at this dump of an Adventurers Guild. Do you have any idea how much he’s sacrificing?” Jenna scowled like a shrew, venting her frustration at Lucia since Alice wasn’t around.

“I’m sorry, Miss Jenna, but I don’t understand.” Lucia’s face darkened, clearly annoyed by the insult to the Guild. “The Adventurers Guild is a public organization, not some ‘dump.’ Even your father, Lord Austin the Count, has relied on our help countless times.”

.....Jenna’s face slowly flushed red. Lucia’s retort left her speechless—her father *did* frequently work with this “dump.” “I—I didn’t mean it like that! I just don’t understand why some commoner girl like Alice would reject my brother!”

“Miss Jenna, you claim to be a love expert, right? Then you should know that love depends on fate, not class.” Lucia spoke calmly, hoping Jenna would see reason.

“Nonsense!” Jenna knitted her brows, firing back aggressively. “Common girls all dream of marrying into nobility! They fantasize about being kept by a nobleman, drowning in gold coins, and their favorite line is *‘I’ll buy your love with money. I love you—are you scared?’* That’s the kind of thrill they get from being dominated by a nobleman!”

“???” Lucia’s mind filled with question marks. She felt physically unwell. “Miss Jenna, what’s your basis for saying that? Why do the girls in your stories sound like they have no brains?”

“Novels, of course! So many romance novels have this exact plot—it *has* to reflect the true desires of women!” Jenna looked deadly serious, clearly disliking being questioned.

“Mmmmm....” Lucia fell silent, staring at Jenna. *This girl... isn’t she an idiot? How could novel plots possibly happen in real life?*

“Anyway, my brother has confessed to her *so many times* and failed every single time! That’s not normal! It’s a total insult to our family!” Jenna’s expression turned grave as she earnestly defended Arnold. “Do you have any idea how much his self-esteem has suffered? He comes home crying every day. As his sister, I can’t stand it anymore! What’s so wrong with the Austin family that she’d reject him?!”

“I think...” Lucia forced a polite smile, awkwardly replying, “the problem might be with Arnold himself.”

“What?! You’re saying *my brother* isn’t good enough for her?!” Jenna refused to back down, immediately lashing out. “Sure, my brother’s a little effeminate, but he got his looks from my mother—he’s still decent-looking, right? He’s practically the dream prince for most girls! Plus, with the Austin family’s noble background, he’s an *exceptional* catch!”

Lucia’s smile didn’t reach her eyes. A vein throbbed on her forehead—Jenna had really gotten under her skin.

The Austin family was respectable in Lexham, but in the grand scheme of the empire? They were nothing special.

And Arnold’s behavior was insufferable. Who with working eyes would ever look twice at him?

Lucia realized talking to Jenna was a waste of time. The girl was too worked up to have a rational conversation.

“Miss Jenna, to be honest... Alice is already married.”

“Don’t lie to me! My brother told me it was just a Guild system error—not a real marriage! And even if it *was* real, so what? She can just divorce and marry into our family!” Jenna paused, a smug look spreading across her face. “The Austin family has always been open-minded. We don’t care about someone’s past.”

Lucia forced out a strained smile, a bead of sweat rolling down her temple. *This is hopeless. I’ll just leave it to Alice.*

---

Not long after—

Alice and Merlin emerged from the Guild’s rear training grounds, looking like they’d just finished a session.

But neither of them looked pleased. The training clearly hadn’t gone well.

Just as Merlin had said, even with him accompanying her, Alice’s progress was limited.

Three months wasn’t much time, and the pressure was mounting.

“Alice, come here for a moment. Someone’s looking for you.” Lucia beckoned.

“Hm?” Alice snapped out of her thoughts, then noticed Jenna beside Lucia. Her expression turned awkward.

“Who’s that?” Merlin whispered, assuming she was Alice’s friend.

“Arnold’s sister. A *really* annoying one. Probably here to vent on behalf of her useless brother.” Alice muttered back.

Merlin’s expression turned complicated. *Is Arnold from another world or something?*

Getting bullied outside and then running home to his little sister for backup? That’s pathetic!

Even *I* find it embarrassing, and I’m his brother in this analogy.

Merlin thought of his own sister, Lilith. When she was wronged, she’d come to *him* in tears. But with Arnold? The roles were completely reversed.

The two of them had no choice but to go over and see what this was about. At the very least, they needed to know what was going on.

“Miss Jenna wants to talk to you. You two chat—I’ll go handle some things.” Lucia wisely chose to step away, not wanting to get dragged into the mess.

Jenna sized Alice up and down. It was her first time seeing Alice in person. *She’s pretty cute. Nice figure too.*

“That’s right.” Alice nodded. She *had* seen Jenna before, but they weren’t familiar.

At first, Alice had only heard about Jenna from Arnold—apparently, she was highly gifted, well-read from a young age, and carried an air of world-weary wisdom.

But then Alice learned Jenna’s reading material was nothing but romance novels. *This girl’s beyond help.* She’d assumed Jenna was the brains of the Austin family, but it turned out the siblings were equally clueless.

“I don’t see what’s so great about you.” Jenna put on an air of superiority, ready to confront her. “Why do you keep rejecting my brother’s heartfelt confessions?!”

“What’s so wrong with my brother?! Is he not good enough for you?!”

“My brother has sapphire-blue hair, legs as graceful as a stallion, a waist as slender as a poplar, lips like cherries—”

“Ah~, so beautiful! How can someone be *this* beautiful?! It’s enough to make anyone cry~!”

(>∞<*)

title: Chapter 21 — Explosive Hammer
content:
Chapter 21 — Explosive Hammer

Volume 9 · Chapter 21

Merlin looked at Jenna with a strange expression, wondering where she had dug up those words. Was it really appropriate to use them on a man like Arnold?

Alice rolled her eyes, seemingly annoyed with dealing with Jenna. She had no choice but to say, "So it's just a matter of incompatible personalities, not anything else. Arnold and I simply aren’t a good match."

"What’s not a good match?! What part isn’t a good match?! My brother has hair like silk, legs as graceful as a steed, a waist as slender as a water snake, and lips like cherries—anyone who sees him would cry from how perfect he is~!" Jenna’s thought process seemed off, constantly using feminine terms to praise her brother. In her eyes, Arnold was probably just a pretty boy.

Alice was left speechless by Jenna’s outburst. Suppressing her anger, she said, "It has nothing to do with Arnold’s looks. It’s just that there’s no spark, understand? This kind of thing is hard to explain. All you need to know is that no matter what your brother does, I can’t feel anything special for him."

"Why? You have to give a convincing reason! After all, my brother—"

"Shut up! He’s so perfect that anyone who sees him would cry, right?!"

Before Jenna could finish, Alice cut her off, leaving her a bit stunned.

"Uh, yeah, that’s right!"

"Miss Jenna, I’ve heard about you. I know you always read those girl’s novels, but those are just stories—they’re not the same as reality. Please don’t try to force those silly, sweet tropes onto me, okay?" Alice explained helplessly, her expression already growing impatient.

"My brother confesses to you every day. Don’t you feel even the slightest flutter in your heart? Aren’t you being a little too heartless?" Jenna argued, feeling Alice was being pretentious. Any normal girl would be overjoyed to be pursued—it proved she had charm.

"Sorry, but no flutter—just annoyance. Though I’ll admit, Arnold is a good person." Alice wore an awkward expression.

"Don’t suddenly play the ‘good person’ card! Doesn’t that just make my brother seem even more pitiful?!" Jenna furrowed her delicate brows and continued, "Unless… you just don’t want to marry into the Austin family? Do you have any idea how many people would kill to get in? Plenty of noble ladies want to form alliances with our family. If you married into the Austins, you wouldn’t have to be an adventurer anymore, living a rough life. As a noblewoman, you’d be respected by countless people. Isn’t that tempting enough?"

"Sorry, but I’m not interested. It does sound tempting, but that kind of life isn’t for me. Most importantly, I don’t like Arnold, so how could I marry into your family?" Alice retorted, thinking Jenna was far too naive. In a way, her emotional intelligence seemed even lower than Arnold’s.

"Emmmm…" Jenna stared into Alice’s eyes, realizing her romance novel experience wasn’t helping. "This doesn’t make sense! If you were normal, you’d be dreaming of being kept by a noble! Why refuse? You should be blushing right now, not this!"

"Who’s blushing?! You’re the abnormal one, got it?!" Alice couldn’t hold back anymore and started complaining, "Just look at your brother—he’s a grown man acting like a giant baby! Who would actually fall for him?! Have some common sense, okay?! Stop reading so many romance novels and misleading yourself! You’ve never even been in a relationship, so stop lecturing me! Why is there no one in the Austin family with a functioning brain?!" QEz

"...What did you say?!" Jenna’s face darkened, feeling Alice was insulting her family. "A mere commoner like you—don’t get cocky just because my brother likes you! Don’t think you can spout nonsense here!"

In truth, Alice was at her limit. She didn’t want to waste time on Jenna at all.

On top of that, her training had been going poorly, so she was already in a bad mood. Then Jenna had to come and pick a fight, so her sharp words were understandable.

In Alice’s eyes, Jenna was just a sheltered little girl whose understanding of love was limited to the worldview of her novels.

Trying to lecture Jenna with grand wisdom would probably be like talking to a cow—completely useless.

"I’m not spouting nonsense. If you want to preach to me, wait until you’re an adult. And for the record, I *do* like someone—just not Arnold."

The person Alice liked, of course, was the elusive dragon-slaying swordmaster, Elgin.

But Jenna didn’t know that. She assumed it was Merlin, who had been silently watching the whole exchange.

Jenna sized Merlin up, thinking his face was the kind women would envy, and he radiated the aura of a man who lived off others.

"Oh~ So you like *this* type, huh? He’s basically the same as my brother~"

Alice saw Jenna eyeing Merlin and immediately realized the misunderstanding. "Wait, no! It’s not what you think!"

Jenna ignored Alice and turned to Merlin directly. "You’re her sweetheart, right?"

"? ? ?" Merlin pointed at himself, his mind filled with question marks. *Why am I being dragged into this again?*

"Hmph!" Jenna crossed her arms, serious as she said, "My brother has already set his sights on her. I’m giving you a chance—know what’s good for you and leave. Otherwise, you won’t like the consequences."

"Oh?" Merlin looked at Jenna with keen interest, the type who responded better to kindness than threats. "Are you threatening me?"

"That’s right, I *am* threatening you. So what?" Jenna wanted to drive Merlin away to give her brother a better shot.

Merlin let out a dry chuckle. He was used to being threatened by all kinds of powerful figures, but being threatened by a little girl was a fresh experience. "What if I don’t leave Alice?"

"The Austin family has a lot of influence in Lexham. You’d better not try to fight a losing battle, or you’ll regret it." Jenna put her hands on her hips, speaking with an air of superiority.

"Yo yo yo~ ‘Regret it’?" Merlin smirked, spreading his hands. "Too bad. I never back down from threats. You might as well give up."

"Ah?!" Jenna was instantly furious. She felt like both Merlin and Alice were deliberately opposing her, showing no respect at all. "You look like the type who mooches off women—what gives you the right to be so arrogant?! Do you believe I’ll have you arrested?!"

"Tsk!" A vein throbbed on Merlin’s forehead. *Called a freeloader again.* He jabbed a finger at Jenna’s nose. "You little brat, watch your tone, or I’ll teach you a lesson."

"Don’t point at me when you talk, peasant!" Jenna glared at Merlin’s finger, seething inside. It was disrespectful.

"So what if I do? Bite me." Merlin shot her a scornful look, thinking this little brat needed to be put in her place.

"Eeeek!!" Jenna, provoked by Merlin, felt her dignity was under attack. So she opened her mouth and bit his finger.

"..." Alice’s eyes widened. She never expected Merlin to actually get bitten!

"Holy crap! She really bit me?!" Merlin quickly shook his hand, trying to pry her mouth off.

"Ow!" Jenna was flung aside by Merlin and lost her balance, tumbling to the ground. Her fluffy skirt flipped up, revealing the white bloomers underneath.

"Miss!"

"Are you alright, Miss?!"

The two maids behind her rushed forward, helping the disheveled Jenna to her feet and checking for injuries.

Behind the counter, Lucia covered her mouth, laughing silently. *This silly girl actually got bullied… Now Alice and the others are in trouble. Jenna’s infamous for being unreasonable…*

"Are you a dog or something? You actually—" Merlin frowned, wiping the saliva off his finger. *Even Cecily, another noble, is better than this. At least she doesn’t bite people when she’s angry.*

"....." Jenna’s expression was one of shock. She slowly got up from the ground, her lips trembling as she pointed at Merlin, unable to speak.

"I-I-I… What’s wrong with me? Got a temper, huh?" Merlin mimicked Jenna’s stutter, deliberately provoking her.

"You—you actually hit me?!" Jenna’s face flushed crimson. She cupped her cheeks, muttering shyly, "This is the first time a man has ever dared to bully me like this…"

"So bad… so bad…"

title: Chapter 22 — Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 22 — Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 22

"Ugh, this disgusting feeling."

Merlin took half a step back, staring at Jenna’s shy and bashful expression, completely confused about what was happening.

What the hell is this?! Why is this brat blushing?! She’s making *me* feel awkward!

Why would she make that face after falling? Could she be... one of those *masochists*? The kind who enjoys being bullied more and more? So they *do* exist in this other world!

Damn it, why do I have a bad feeling about this? Am I going to get targeted by this freak?

Merlin pressed his lips tightly together, becoming cautious. He didn’t want to engage with Jenna just yet—better to see how things played out first.

Even Alice was confused, unsure what was wrong with Jenna. Did falling make her stupid? Normally, shouldn’t she be furious, cursing Merlin out? Why the sudden shyness?!

Alice couldn’t help but nudge Merlin with her elbow, curious. "Merlin, what’s going on?"

"How the hell should *I* know?" Merlin whispered back, shaking his head. He couldn’t figure Jenna out either. If she was the type who got off on being bullied, that was trouble.

Jenna cupped her flushed cheeks, her entire being still immersed in the feeling of being bullied by Merlin just now.

She had read plenty of romance novels aimed at women, and one type of character was always popular—the cold, domineering man.

Jenna had always been the pampered jewel of her family, never bullied by anyone. But just now, Merlin had thrown her to the ground, and for the first time, she felt *truly* bullied.

At first, she had been angry, furious, humiliated—but then, an overwhelming sense of pleasure had taken over, and she was completely hooked.

She finally understood—this was what it felt like to meet a man even more dominant than herself. The thrill of being controlled, of being thoroughly bullied... it was indescribable.

"Tch, you just love bullying me, don’t you? Can’t you at least admit I’m not just some freeloading weakling? You’re *so* manly, at least give me that!" Jenna pouted.

Merlin and Alice both widened their eyes, their expressions darkening. Something was *very* wrong here. Jenna’s head had to be messed up.

Getting bullied and then reacting like *this*? She had to be a masochist, right? The world of masochists was just incomprehensible!

In the distance, Lucia’s feather pen had fallen to the floor, but she didn’t even notice. She was lost in thought—

*What in the world is wrong with Jenna?*

Why wasn’t she raging, chasing after Alice and the others in a fury? Instead, she was acting *shy*? Had she... fallen for Merlin?!

This was absurd. He was just a low-ranked Black Iron adventurer. It was one thing if Alice was smitten, but why was Jenna, a noble lady, affected too?

Lucia couldn’t make sense of it. Jenna’s reaction was completely unexpected, nothing like what she had anticipated.

(*Dor*... what a mess.)

"Okay, fine, I admit you’re manly," Merlin said, "but you’d better stay the hell away from this woman. There are plenty of better girls out there—some far away, some right in front of you."

Jenna kept shooting him suggestive glances, practically advertising herself. It was as if she had already moved on from Elgin, completely forgetting about him.

"Tsk!" Alice knitted her brows, her face darkening. She didn’t see how Jenna was any better than her.

"No, no, no, I’m *not* manly enough, I’m *not*!" Merlin waved his hands repeatedly, as if trying to ward off a crazy woman.

"This isn’t the time to be shy~" Jenna’s face was still flushed, her fingers fidgeting as they poked at each other. "You should know, I rarely take a liking to a man. You’re the first one who’s made me want to... *keep* you."

*Puah!*

Merlin coughed up a mouthful of old blood. *Me? The great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace? Being kept by a little human girl?* The sheer humiliation was enough to send him to his ancestors.

"Get lost, you shameless bitch! Stay away from me!"

"Ohhh~"

Jenna clutched her chest as if struck, her delicate body trembling.

But the pain was fleeting—replaced instantly by overwhelming excitement and heavy breathing.

Her cheeks burned crimson, her eyes filled with a sick, obsessive infatuation. She looked like a complete lunatic.

"Calling me a shameless bitch... No one’s ever insulted me like that before. And you did it so *dominantly*... It’s *amazing*~"

"Disgusting!" both of them said in unison, their eyebrows shooting up. They were at a loss—what kind of logic was this? The more you bullied her, the happier she got?!

"I can’t take this anymore. Let’s bail." Merlin muttered.

"Yeah, we should avoid her." Alice nodded firmly.

The two of them bolted out of the guild hall without a second glance, desperate to escape Jenna’s warped obsession.

Seeing Merlin leave, Jenna panicked. She hiked up her fluffy skirt and chased after him.

"M-Merlin-sama, wait! ^=^"

Lucia at the counter finally snapped out of her daze, blinking rapidly as if waking from a dream. She mumbled to herself, "What in the world did I just witness..."

---

Nighttime.

At the Taylor residence.

Uncle Carl, who had been in a coma, suddenly jolted awake.

Merlin’s single strike had kept him unconscious for an entire day.

Uncle Carl sat up in bed, gasping for air, cold sweat sliding down his sharp, angular face.

Even in his dreams, he couldn’t forget the sight of Merlin’s wooden sword smashing into his forehead.

He looked around and, recognizing his own bedroom, finally relaxed a little. It seemed he had been carried back after his defeat.

"Stinkin’ brat, you’re awake?" Old Taylor’s voice rang out.

Uncle Carl’s head snapped up—he hadn’t even noticed Old Taylor standing behind him.

"Ah, what—? Oh, it’s just you, old man."

"You passed out, and I was the one who carried you back. What’s wrong with me being here?" Old Taylor’s tone was cold, as if displeased with Carl’s reckless challenge to Merlin.

"I didn’t mean it like that, it’s just..." Uncle Carl scratched his head awkwardly, his body still aching. Clearly, he hadn’t fully recovered from Merlin’s beating.

"Hmph. Embarrassed to be seen like this?" Old Taylor’s stern face softened slightly, a hint of amusement in his eyes.

"Tch..." Uncle Carl felt a pang of bitterness. "It’s not *that* bad."

"How was the fight with Merlin?" Old Taylor asked cautiously, genuinely curious about the battle. He hadn’t fought Merlin seriously himself, but he knew his own limits. If Merlin went all out, he doubted he could last even a second against the young man’s blade.

"It was... terrible. There was no suspense at all." Uncle Carl paused, sighed, and admitted honestly, "From start to finish, that kid Merlin had me pinned to the ground."

title: Chapter 23 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 23 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 23

Old Taylor’s aged face showed no expression as he leaned on his cane, swaying slightly, as if everything had gone exactly as he expected.

"That feeling was absolutely terrible." Karl Uncle clutched his forehead, a hint of despair creeping into his voice. "My strength was completely crushed by him. No matter how hard I fought, I couldn’t win."

"It was like facing an insurmountable mountain. All I felt was my own insignificance—nothing else."

"I fought that rookie with everything I had, and yet he didn’t even seem to use his full strength. He still beat me so badly I couldn’t fight back at all."

"I’ve been through countless life-or-death battles and never once given up hope of surviving."

"But when I sparred with Merlin, I felt nothing but despair. That guy is impossible to defeat."

He shuddered. "It’s terrifying. How can someone reach that level with just physical strength, without using aura at all?"

"Too terrifying. I can barely believe it. I even started doubting whether Merlin is even human."

Old Taylor sat quietly beside him, listening to his son’s lingering fear without interrupting. After all, Merlin was an incomprehensible existence. Accepting reality would take time for self-reflection.

Even Old Taylor himself, after sparring with Merlin, had his lifelong confidence shattered and had spent a long time in gloom.

"There’s no need to doubt that. Merlin is definitely human. I’ve examined him thoroughly for a long time and sensed no trace of any non-human aura."

Karl Uncle’s thick eyebrows knitted together. "Then what’s with that inhuman strength?"

"That’s the part I can’t figure out either." Old Taylor furrowed his pale brows, awkwardly admitting, "Merlin is ordinary in every other aspect. Only his *Iaijutsu* carries an oppressive aura of death. How long must one train to reach that level? It’s an unsolved mystery. Everyone’s cultivation is a secret, and it’s not proper for us to pry."

Karl Uncle’s expression froze in shock. *Iaijutsu*? That garbage technique? It didn’t even require magic or aura—just flashy posturing. But in their spar, Merlin hadn’t used *Iaijutsu* at all!

Did that mean his strength wasn’t even worth Merlin’s ultimate move?

Karl Uncle felt a fresh wave of frustration. He had attacked with everything he had, yet couldn’t even force Merlin to reveal his true power.

Listening to Old Taylor’s praise, Karl Uncle couldn’t help but want to see Merlin’s *Iaijutsu* for himself. Could a low-tier skill really be refined to such a level?

"But I think this must be a difference in realm." Old Taylor said mysteriously.

"Realm?" Karl Uncle frowned, not quite understanding his father’s words.

"Yes, the realm of understanding the essence of power." Old Taylor nodded, continuing in his aged voice, "You know that those with talent in magic and aura all strive tirelessly on the path to strength. Yet their final achievements differ greatly. Setting aside talent and effort, what remains is the difference in realm."

Karl Uncle stayed silent, staring at his father with a mix of confusion and hope, as if seeking a way to grow stronger.

"Merlin gives off the vibe of an idle, ordinary man who takes everything lightly and lives without restraint." Old Taylor paused, as if he had uncovered Merlin’s secret to power. "Perhaps it’s precisely this transcendent realm that makes Merlin so strong, far surpassing us pioneers."

Karl Uncle said nothing, but in his mind, he thought: *How does that look like anything but a good-for-nothing wasting his life? If he keeps being this lazy, won’t he just get weaker?*

"What’s that doubtful look for?" Old Taylor’s gaze carried a quiet authority, feeling his son’s skepticism was an insult to his judgment.

Karl Uncle’s expression twisted awkwardly, sweating internally. *If I believe the old man’s nonsense, I’d have to be an idiot!*

"Hmph!" Old Taylor coldly scoffed. "Brat, do you think I’m talking nonsense? Right now, I can only perceive Merlin’s worldly realm. As for deeper aspects, I still need to study further."

Karl Uncle’s embarrassed expression froze on his face. *Study further? More like the old man himself can’t bring himself to believe that "living in decadence" nonsense!*

"Speaking of which, old man, where did this Merlin come from? Someone with that kind of strength shouldn’t be a nobody. He definitely wouldn’t be content as an Iron-rank adventurer."

"He was brought back by Alice from outside. As for Merlin’s background, it’s not proper for me to ask." Old Taylor said leisurely.

"Sure is a mysterious guy. Like he appeared out of thin air." Karl Uncle stroked his beard. "No wonder Alice chose to be with Merlin. Now I finally get it. At first glance, they actually seem like a good match. Young people really are full of energy, huh?"

Old Taylor’s expression turned unnatural. *Weren’t they always arguing before becoming a couple? All the black pots are on me now?*

"Still, old man, have you considered promoting Merlin’s adventurer rank? In my opinion, Merlin is more than qualified to be a Mithril-rank adventurer." Karl Uncle said seriously, not holding a grudge over being beaten senseless by Merlin. Instead, he chose to let it go. After all, they were both adventurers from the same guild. In the future, they might even become partners on joint missions.

"I’ve thought about it, but the guild’s rules aren’t up to me. The final say lies with headquarters. Even if I proposed raising Merlin’s rank, it would be rejected immediately." Old Taylor wore a helpless look. "You know as well as I do—someone like Merlin, without magic or aura, won’t be recognized by headquarters. Maybe I’d have to use some personal connections, but the timing isn’t right yet. Merlin still lacks the prestige to make the adventurer headquarters take notice."

"I see." Karl Uncle nodded in understanding. After all, a physically powerful Merlin was an anomaly. No precedent like this had ever appeared among the world’s adventurers. It was only natural he wasn’t acknowledged. "When I fought him, I felt like he wasn’t even using his full strength. And his wooden swordplay was incredibly skilled—sharp angles, fierce momentum, comparable to veteran swordmasters. With Merlin’s combat power in our guild, we’d definitely gain a competitive edge. Maybe we could even stand up to oppression from the big guilds. It’s a shame Merlin is so unknown. What a waste."

"Don’t worry too much about that." Old Taylor paused, then looked at Karl Uncle with a smile. "Have you forgotten about the Adventurers’ Tournament held every four years?"

"That grand gathering of adventurers might just be the turning point for Merlin’s rise."

title: Chapter 24 — Meeting
content:
Chapter 24 — Meeting

Volume 9 · Chapter 24

"Adventurers Tournament."

Uncle Karl muttered to himself, pondering for a moment before nodding—it seemed feasible.

The Adventurers Tournament was a grand event held in rotation among the human kingdoms, taking place once every four years. Any adventurer registered with the headquarters could participate, regardless of their kingdom, with no restrictions whatsoever. Even a Black Iron adventurer could openly challenge a Mithril or even an Orichalcum adventurer.

Of course, all of this was based on mutual consent—no one would advocate for such a suicidal act.

The tournament was a stage for adventurers to showcase their strength, but it was also a battle for rankings between guilds, involving numerous interests. During the competition, powerful figures from all walks of life would come to watch, and all human kingdoms would broadcast the matches live. It was the greatest spectacle for all of humanity.

Adventurers could use this platform to rise to fame, becoming sought-after celebrity adventurers and reaping both fame and fortune. After all, an adventurer’s income relied not just on their rank but also on their reputation. Without fame, it was difficult to secure high-paying missions.

As for the guilds, they too stood to benefit. The tournament was a reshuffling of all guilds—those ranked at the top would gain numerous privileges and boost their reputation. For example, if the Rexham Adventurers Guild secured a top-three position, who would dare call them the "Cross-Eyed Adventurers" anymore? They’d probably have to line up to lick their boots.

Uncle Karl nodded, convinced that with Merlin’s overwhelming strength joining them, the next Adventurers Tournament was worth a shot.

"Indeed, even if Merlin is a Black Iron adventurer, he has the ability to stand out in the tournament."

"Merlin’s addition is great news for us. Maybe the next tournament will finally let us shake off the 'Cross-Eyed Adventurers' stigma," Old Taylor said, stroking his white beard.

"Yeah, if we’re lucky, we might even break into the top 16. Thinking about last time’s defeat… it’s still hard to swallow," Uncle Karl sighed.

"There was nothing we could do about it. Without me, the entire guild only had you and Tony as Saint-tier powerhouses. Breaking into the top 16 was always going to be difficult," Old Taylor said leisurely, not putting too much pressure on his son. "But now it’s different. With Merlin joining, the top 16 should be within reach."

*Creak—*

The room door swung open, and Lucia stormed in, fuming.

"What are you two doing? Why aren’t you downstairs for dinner?"

Old Taylor coughed awkwardly, looking embarrassed.

"Honestly, I know you haven’t seen each other in a long time, but that doesn’t mean you can skip dinner just to chat!" Lucia stood with her hands on her hips, acting like the mistress of the house. "And Grandpa, you didn’t even eat lunch—just sitting here keeping Father company. As an old man, you should know better!"

"Huh?" Uncle Karl stared at Old Taylor in surprise, thinking, *Has Father been here taking care of me all day? What a grumpy old man with a heart of gold.*

Old Taylor felt a little humiliated and covered it up. "This old man just had nowhere else to go. I’m just resting here."

Lucia didn’t bother arguing with her grandfather. She turned to her father, exasperated. "Dad, you’ve gone too far! You’re a grown man, and yet you’re running around challenging people to duels? Did someone knock you out?"

"This was just a friendly sparring match with an old friend," Uncle Karl said, sweat dripping down his forehead as black lines formed above his head. *Getting wrecked by a rookie in front of my daughter is way too embarrassing. For the sake of a father’s dignity, I’d better not admit it.*

Time passed swiftly, and two months later—

In a remote town of the Sunset Empire, located within Wales.

Far from the core cities, it lacked the expected prosperity, instead exuding a sense of shabbiness. Weeds overran the streets, dilapidated houses swayed in the wind, and the grayish-blue church bell tower stood dull and lifeless.

*Ding ding dang dang*—the bell tolled, echoing through the town, startling a flock of crows into a series of harsh, mournful caws.

This was the sunset bell. Since the remote town was surrounded by mountains on all sides, it had already been shrouded in twilight long before the sun actually set.

The residents had long since returned home. Wispy columns of smoke rose from chimneys, and flickering lights in countless windows made the darkness feel eerily quiet.

The only people left on the streets were either homeless vagabonds or drunken, unemployed vagrants, stumbling about in groups of three or four.

Of course, there were also those with various agendas—like this particular individual.

After two months of lurking in the black market and gathering intelligence, Knight Commander Franklin had finally made contact with someone from the Howling Specters.

He had fully explained his purpose—that he possessed something the Howling Specters urgently needed. As for the specifics, he hoped to discuss them in person with their leader, Swinburne.

Franklin’s request had taken a long time to receive a response. Swinburne had agreed to meet him in this small town—and only at night.

Swinburne had his reasons for choosing such a remote location.

The Howling Specters were no longer the powerhouse they once were. Members had either died or left, leaving only a pitiful four behind. Now, they were on the brink of dissolution, struggling just to survive. Many predators circled them, eager to devour the former king.

The Dark Adventurers Guild was a ruthless place. There were no rules or systems—only brute force spoke, and the law of the jungle reigned supreme. If a guild was weak, it was only natural for others to swallow it whole. Even the Howling Specters now faced such internal and external crises.

Externally, they were suppressed and hunted by the forces of various nations. Internally, other dark guilds eyed them hungrily. The space left for the Howling Specters to barely survive was dwindling by the day.

Thus, as acting guild leader, Swinburne had to be extremely cautious. He absolutely could not afford any mishaps.

Meeting in a remote location was safer. If the visitor turned out to be imperial pursuers or predators from another dark guild, Swinburne could make a quick escape.

A man who had managed to keep a crumbling guild afloat this long was no fool.

Still, there was hope. If Swinburne could revive his father, Palmer, he would regain control of the narrative—and returning to their former glory might not be impossible.

This was why Swinburne was willing to risk being devoured just to meet Franklin.

Franklin wore a black robe, completely concealing his identity as a Royal Hibiscus Knight. He couldn’t afford to be recognized. He carried a top-secret mission from the queen, and any exposure could upend the royal family’s image, plunging the empire into crisis.

Franklin knew he was about to meet the leader of a dark guild, so he remained on high alert. He couldn’t let the tiger bite back.

Clutching a wrapped package containing the former kingdom’s codex, he moved through the streets, turning a few corners before suddenly spotting a rundown café named *Sailo Riverside*.

The shoddy decor, the old display window adorned with cheap trinkets, the swaying sign above the door creaking with every gust of wind—

"This must be the place."

title: Chapter 24 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 24 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets

Volume 9 · Chapter 24

Franklin was just about to step forward toward the agreed-upon coffee shop.

Then a drunken vagrant lunged at him, reeking of alcohol.

Ugh—

Without hesitation, Franklin drove his fist into the drunk’s face, sending him crashing to the ground with a pained scream, several front teeth scattered across the pavement.

This was a critical moment for Franklin. He couldn’t afford distractions.

Especially since, as one of the three Knight Captains of the Order, he was well-known. Someone might recognize him.

To prevent that, he had to eliminate all risks—ruthlessly, if necessary.

Franklin adjusted his black cloak and pulled his hat low, hiding his true appearance.

Then he kicked the collapsed vagrant aside and headed straight for the coffee shop.

*Ding ling ling—*

Franklin pushed open the door and found only one person inside, in the corner. Not even the shopkeeper seemed to be around.

In truth, the place had already been reserved by Swinburne. For an important discussion, fewer outsiders were better.

The sole man in the shop had short red hair, neatly combed upward to expose his forehead. He wore meticulously tailored clothes, the buttons adorned with intricate patterns. Though he looked to be under thirty, there was a mature, world-weary aura about him.

A cigarette burned slowly in his hand, sending up pungent smoke that made one’s nose wrinkle.

This must be Swinburne, the acting president of the Howling Specter Guild. He didn’t radiate any sense of evil—instead, he seemed like a refined noble of high taste.

Swinburne slightly lifted his eyelids, glancing at the entering Franklin, his face completely expressionless.

So this was the current leader of the Howling Specter Guild?

He didn’t exude the slightest air of someone in a position of power.

Though Swinburne seemed harmless, Franklin didn’t dare underestimate him.

If memory served, Swinburne had been a Saint-tier powerhouse long ago. He’d risen from High-tier to Saint-tier in just a year and a half—a man of extraordinary talent.

Just how strong was Swinburne now? Franklin couldn’t even imagine, but he suspected it had reached an unfathomable level.

Under Swinburne’s gaze, Franklin felt an immense pressure, his body trembling involuntarily, as if stared down by a beast of prey.

Now he had to negotiate with this monster?

It felt dangerous. He couldn’t shake the feeling that Her Majesty the Queen was playing with fire by trying to use the Howling Specter Guild.

Franklin fretted internally, deciding he must proceed with caution—he couldn’t let this man slip beyond the empire’s control.

He pulled his hat lower, slowly approached Swinburne’s table, and sat down across from him.

Swinburne flicked his cigarette ash, his tone calm. “You’re the one who came to see me?”

Franklin nodded. “That’s right.”

“Then let’s skip the useless talk and get to the point.” Swinburne’s eyes gleamed like a starving wolf, cutting straight to the chase. “I hear you have something we desperately need?”

“Yes.” Franklin didn’t elaborate, simply answering calmly.

Swinburne picked up the nearby wine bottle and filled his glass. “Do you know what we need right now?”

“I do. The method to resurrect Shadowflame Howler, perhaps?” Franklin was certain—if it wasn’t for this, it wouldn’t be worth negotiating with the Howling Specter Guild.

“Oh?” Swinburne lifted his head, a flicker of alertness in his eyes. “You seem quite knowledgeable about us. You wouldn’t happen to be a colleague from another dark guild, or perhaps a lackey of the empire?”

Franklin tensed, fearing his identity might be exposed. He forced himself to sound composed. “No.”

“But you won’t even show your face. That makes me doubt your identity.” Swinburne smiled.

“You don’t need to know who I am. Just know that I can be of great help to you. Otherwise, we part ways here and now.” Franklin issued a veiled threat, worried that revealing his Knight Captain status might affect Her Majesty’s standing.

Swinburne stared at Franklin expressionlessly, then burst into laughter. “Relax. Everyone has secrets. I’m not so unreasonable as to pry.”

Franklin exhaled slightly in relief. If the other man had flown into a rage, he would’ve been helpless.

Then Swinburne lifted his head and said seriously, “Show me what you’ve brought.”

Franklin hesitated for a moment before reluctantly handing over the bundle from his cloak.

Swinburne opened it and froze at the sight of the thick, ancient leather-bound book, its pages covered in dense, archaic script from the Former Kingdom.

As a man of vast learning and a Saint-tier mage, he couldn’t fully decipher the Former Kingdom’s language, but he could infer its general meaning.

Swinburne’s eyes widened, fixed on the Former Kingdom Codex as if gazing into another world, brimming with mystery.

“This is…”

“This is the Former Kingdom Codex. It contains many lost ancient spells, including the forbidden art of resurrecting the dead.” Franklin said slowly, watching Swinburne’s expression. The man’s eyes burned with undisguised desire.

“Well? Isn’t this exactly what you’ve been desperate to get your hands on?”

Swinburne regained some composure, and in an instant, understanding dawned. He couldn’t help but laugh. “HAHAHAHA—”

“Eh!” Franklin panicked, bewildered. “What’s so funny? What’s amusing about this?”

Swinburne wiped the smile from his face, his expression turning grim. “Who are you?”

Franklin felt the pressure mount, his voice tense. “You don’t need to know who I am.”

“Let me take a guess.” Swinburne leaned back in his chair, pondering for a moment before speaking seriously. “You’re from the royal capital, aren’t you? No—more precisely, you’re someone close to the Queen. Someone with access to imperial secrets. That narrows it down considerably.”

“Why do you say that?” Franklin’s tension spiked, cold sweat soaking the back of his shirt.

“The Former Kingdom Codex was seized by the Queen not long ago. Yet here it is, in front of me. Don’t you find that suspicious? I doubt some petty thief could’ve infiltrated the imperial treasury. So there’s only one possibility—you’re a high-ranking figure close to the Queen.” Swinburne narrowed his eyes, scrutinizing Franklin.
