Franklin’s eyes widened. He felt as though Swinburne had guessed nearly everything about him, but he still couldn’t admit it—that would threaten Her Majesty’s position.

“I’m not. You must be mistaken.”

Swinburne didn’t respond. Instead, he clamped the cigarette between his lips—

Then, in a sudden motion, he snatched the wine bottle and smashed it against Franklin’s head. Shards of glass exploded outward!

“Agh!” Franklin let out a pained cry, utterly stunned.

Swinburne grabbed Franklin’s hair and slammed his head against the table, unleashing an overwhelming Saint-tier pressure!

Blood trickled from Franklin’s head, spreading across the table. He was pinned, unable to move.

Swinburne, cigarette still burning in his mouth, leisurely lifted Franklin’s hood, revealing his face.

“Well, well~”

“If it isn’t the famous Knight Captain Franklin.”

“What’s this? Are you betraying that old hag Elizabeth now?”

title: Chapter 25 — Arrival
content:
Chapter 25 — Arrival

Volume 9 · Chapter 25

Swinburne loomed over Franklin, pressing his head firmly against the table with a voice as cold as ice.

Crimson blood trickled from Franklin’s forehead, slowly spreading across the table before dripping onto the floor with a steady *plink, plink, plink*.

Franklin’s heart pounded in terror, cold sweat beading nonstop. His eyes were wide with fear and confusion. Even if he wanted to resist, Swinburne’s overwhelming Saint-tier pressure crushed any chance of movement. In that moment, Franklin’s mind raced through countless thoughts before he chose loyalty—he would take all the blame to protect Her Majesty the Queen’s honor.

“Y-Yes! I… I betrayed Queen Elizabeth…”

“Oh? Why?” Swinburne narrowed his eyes, pressing further.

“Because…” Franklin hesitated, then fabricated a flawless lie. “Because I wanted to become a Thorn Knight… but I was never recognized. So… so I wanted to destroy the Empire!”

“That’s your goal?” Swinburne’s expression remained blank as he bit down on his cigarette holder. “You wanted to use us to openly oppose Elizabeth?”

“Y-Yes! Otherwise, I wouldn’t have handed over something as important as the former kingdom’s codex to you…” Franklin added nervously, his voice trembling. “You’ve been suppressed by the royal families for years—don’t you want revenge? Our interests align. We could cooperate perfectly!”

Swinburne’s face stayed impassive as he exhaled rings of smoke, then suddenly laughed. “Hahaha! Do you take me for a child? You’re not telling the truth at all.”

“H-How could that be?!” Franklin tensed up, convinced his words were airtight. Why wouldn’t Swinburne believe him?

“What do you gain from us destroying the Empire? Without a massive benefit driving you, you’d never hand over the former kingdom’s codex to us.” Swinburne paused, then continued with a mocking tone. “And betraying the Empire just because you couldn’t become a Thorn Knight? Who would believe such a childish reason? Are you testing our intelligence?”

Franklin’s face twisted in shock, his mouth agape. He hadn’t expected Swinburne to be so suspicious—no matter what he said, trust seemed impossible.

Swinburne had no patience left. He extended his hand in front of Franklin, and a flicker of cerulean flame suddenly ignited in his palm, burning steadily.

The flame was small, but its heat was scorching. The temperature in the café spiked instantly, as if they were standing inside a furnace. The immense Saint-tier magic made Franklin’s heart race—he didn’t dare breathe. If that flame touched him, he’d be reduced to ashes in a blink.

“You have one last chance. Tell the truth, or die.”

Franklin’s expression twisted into something feral, his earlier composure shattered, leaving only a maddened bloodlust.

“…”

He stared at the cerulean flame, its eerie glow like a ghostly fire.

He weighed his options carefully. This was a matter of life and death.

Should he remain loyal, or save his own skin?

In just a few seconds, he chose survival. *A man can always rebuild if he lives.*

Franklin swallowed nervously, his eyes locked on Swinburne in terror.

“If… if I tell the truth, will you really let me go?”

“Of course. The Dark Guild always keeps its word.” Swinburne said seriously.

“…Then I’ll talk…” Franklin hesitated, then after a moment’s thought, said, “Her Majesty the Queen wanted to use you…”

Swinburne extinguished the flame in his palm and narrowed his eyes. “Use us for what?”

“She wants you to move freely within the Empire, spreading your threat as you go. Then the Thorn Knights will eliminate you, creating a heroic legend for the people to worship.” Franklin spoke bluntly, laying everything bare under the threat to his life.

“Hah…” Swinburne burst into laughter, his face dripping with ridicule. “What a foolish queen. To consolidate her power, she’s resorting to such desperate measures. That old woman Elizabeth really is an idiot. With such a stupid ruler, the Empire’s downfall is only a matter of time. If my father, Palmer, were to return from hell, does Elizabeth think she could defeat us? What’s a mere Great Britain? Even if all the human empires united, they’d be nothing but trash before my father!”

Franklin’s face froze. *So it’s true…* The Noble Phantom Praise only lacked a resurrection ritual. Once the Shadowflame Noble Phantom Palmer was revived, the fallen Noble Phantom Praise would rise again in an instant!

“I have one more question.” Swinburne’s smile faded, his tone serious. “Why would Elizabeth resort to such extreme measures? It doesn’t make sense…”

“Because… because of Elgin the Great Sword…” Franklin hesitated, then answered honestly. “His actions within the Empire… have already begun to shake Her Majesty’s position.”

“Hahaha, I see. I should actually thank this Elgin the Great Sword. Without him, our long-held wish might not have been fulfilled so soon.” Swinburne grinned triumphantly, clearly in high spirits.

“I… I’ve told you everything. Can… can you let me go now…?” Franklin asked tentatively.

“Oh? Did I ever promise to let you go?” Swinburne’s face twisted into a sinister grin, his expression unsettling. The corners of his mouth curled as if he were making a grotesque face. Suddenly, a roaring cerulean flame erupted in his hand, as if he were about to strike.

“…This isn’t what you agreed to earlier! You promised me!” Franklin’s face was twisted in sheer terror. *This is what happens when you make a deal with a tiger—coming here for the Queen was a mistake!*

“Did you misunderstand something? When it comes to enemies, we have no need for cheap promises.” Swinburne smiled, and the flames in his hand surged violently.

Franklin’s face turned ashen, as if he’d already been sentenced to death…

*Ding ling ling!*

The café door was kicked open. The pitch-black surroundings were eerily silent.

Swinburne walked out of the ruined café alone. There was no sign of Franklin.

He had a nearly spent cigarette between his lips, slowly walking away from the silent café into the darkness.

*BOOM!*

A sudden explosion erupted. The once-intact small café was swallowed by the deep blue flames, blazing fiercely in the darkness!

A wave of heat rushed forward, slightly tousling Swinburne’s red hair. He exhaled a long breath of smoke from his lungs and looked up at the endless night—

“The moment to reclaim our past glory… has finally arrived.”

title: Chapter 26 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 26 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 26

At the exit of the small town, two middle-aged men stood waiting, as if standing by for orders.

They were veteran members of the Haunted Ogre Praise, and among the four remaining, these were two of them.

One was Cooper, a Saint-tier swordsman, dressed in a practical, form-fitting outfit with a short sword strapped to each side of his waist. His face bore strange tattoos, resembling the totems of some tribe, exuding an air of mystery and eeriness. He leaned against a tree, his gaze fixed on the exit, seemingly waiting for Swinburne.

Cooper was a wanted criminal from the Austro-Hungarian Empire. With nowhere left to turn, he had been taken in by the Haunted Ogre Praise. He had been sentenced to the highest threat level in the empire for consecutively killing 11 nobles, which had led to a relentless pursuit by the imperial army. With no other choice, Cooper fled the Austro-Hungarian Empire and joined the notorious Dark Adventurers Guild.

By nature, Cooper was greedy and lustful. The 11 nobles he killed all shared a common trait—they were immensely wealthy and each had a beautiful wife. These were the kind of people Cooper targeted. Under the cover of night, he would easily infiltrate their mansions, relying on his Saint-tier strength to slaughter all the guards. Then, he would gather the nobles and their female relatives in a room. In front of the noblemen, he would violate their wives, daughters, and mothers without mercy, forcing the men to experience the depths of despair, their wails of agony echoing until their spirits shattered completely. Only then would Cooper kill the noblemen and the violated women, taking all their wealth with him to continue his life of debauchery, searching for his next target.

It sounded like Cooper was a psychopath, but in reality, he was just seeking thrills. Every time he used his lower body to violently take another man’s wife, listening to the nobleman’s howls of despair, he would feel the pleasure of being at the top of the food chain. For him, controlling others’ fates and toying with them as he pleased was the greatest joy in life.

Cooper had no grand ambitions. His life motto was to live each day to the fullest—life is short, so why make things hard on yourself?

Cooper was born into a fatherless family; his mother was a local cheap prostitute, which left him with no social standing. As a child, he endured endless bullying, leaving him with indelible scars and a warped, distant personality. As an adult, he joined the imperial army. Thanks to his exceptional talent, he was groomed intensively and became a respected Saint-tier powerhouse. Yet, the shadows of his childhood never truly faded, eventually driving him to become a murderous madman, committing atrocities wherever he went.

Cooper excelled in the Austro-Hungarian Empire’s military swordsmanship, wielding dual short swords. Though his techniques were flashy, they were highly practical, capable of fierce head-on combat as well as stealthy assassinations in the dark, embodying the concept of attack to its fullest.

The other man was a mage dressed in a long robe. He was quite old, his face lined with wrinkles, holding a staff and hunched over, his pale beard drooping to his chest. This man was named Sammy, serving as the vice president of the Haunted Ogre Praise. Once, he had been in his prime, but now he was nothing more than a lone commander.

Old Sammy was from the same generation as Yōen Gōki Palmer. In his youth, he had served as the president’s right-hand man, carving a path of bloodshed and making invaluable contributions to the establishment of the Haunted Ogre Praise. Initially, he had even been Swinburne’s mentor, acting as his guide. But as Swinburne’s extraordinary talent allowed him to surpass Sammy’s strength and escape his control, the old man could now only obey Swinburne’s every command while living out his retirement.

As someone from Palmer’s era, Old Sammy’s strength was naturally formidable. He was particularly skilled in magic grafting, applying the powers of various magical beasts to his own body. He could even transplant parts of magical beasts onto himself to enhance his abilities—a truly sinister form of magic. His old title, "Beast Sammy," hinted at this: a man who controlled the power of magical beasts with a human body.

Unlike Cooper, the newcomer, Old Sammy had no perverse hobbies. However, he placed great value on honor, and his greatest dream now was to restore the Haunted Ogre Praise to its former glory.

At this moment, both men were waiting for Swinburne to emerge so they could proceed with the next phase of their plan.

"Damn, this is slow. Maybe I should find a pretty girl to keep me company and pass the time," Cooper said, scratching his ear as if unable to resist the itch of boredom.

"Hmph..." Old Sammy let out a cold laugh, his hoarse voice rasping, "What girl would dare keep you company? Even if one did, she wouldn’t live to see the end of it."

"Why not?" Cooper retorted, flashing a lecherous grin. "I think Grace is perfect. She’s got a smokin’ hot body. Every time I see her tits, I can’t help but drool. If I could just suck on them hard, oh man, that’d be amazing. Hehehe~"

"Grace isn’t someone you can even dream about," Old Sammy said with a sinister chuckle. "If you dare lay a hand on her, I guarantee your balls will be served on a plate the next day."

"Even if it costs me my balls, I’d still do it to sleep with Grace~" Cooper was practically drooling, his heart pounding with excitement.

"I think you’ve got a death wish," Old Sammy couldn’t help but warn. "Grace is Swinburne’s woman. If you touch her, you’ll die a horrible death."

"Tch!" Cooper curled his lip, clearly annoyed, and muttered, "Damn it, if Swinburne ever kicks the bucket, I’m definitely gonna bang his wife."

"You’re just talking big," Old Sammy mercilessly dashed Cooper’s hopes. "With Swinburne’s strength, unless he runs into some ancient monster, there’s barely anyone who can beat him."

"Tsk... What a pain..." Cooper’s brow darkened, clearly resentful of Swinburne. "By the way, when is Miss Grace coming back?"

"Her current mission is a tough one—assassinating the president of a merchant guild. It’ll probably take a while," Old Sammy replied indifferently.

"Oh? Even Miss Grace feels the pressure? That opponent must be no joke," Cooper mused. In his mind, Grace was incredibly strong, nearly catching up to Old Sammy.

"It’s just that the opponent’s guards are troublesome. There’s no real pressure..." Old Sammy said with confidence.

Just as the two were discussing Grace, Swinburne appeared, smoking a cigarette as he leisurely strolled over.

"President~" Cooper teased with a smirk. "How’d things go?"

Swinburne lifted his eyelids slightly, glancing at Cooper, and casually twirled the old kingdom’s codex in his hand. "Pretty smooth, I’d say."

"What’s that?" Cooper narrowed his eyes, staring at the tattered leather-bound book in Swinburne’s hand with curiosity.

"This is the codex of the former kingdom. It contains the forbidden magic of resurrection," Swinburne said, the corners of his mouth twitching upward.

"M-My... my goodness..." Old Sammy’s eyes widened, as if he could already see the future where the Haunted Ogre Praise would reclaim its glory.

"That’s right." Swinburne nodded, unable to hide his smile as he said seriously, "All the dark guilds’ power structures are about to be reshuffled. Because my father is coming back from hell very soon..."

title: Chapter 27 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 27 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 27

...It was...

Old Samy felt a little excited. He hadn't expected things to go so smoothly—they had already found a way to resurrect Palmer.

With this, once Palmer was revived, it would only be a matter of time before the Howling Ghost Praise returned to its peak.

Old Samy stared at the former kingdom's codex in Swinburne's hands, his emotions remaining unsettled for a long time.

"Just came to take a casual look, and yet we gained an unexpected harvest? It seems heaven does not intend for us to perish."

"Teacher Samy, I don’t believe in fate. If things have gone so smoothly, it’s because everything was inevitable." Swinburne emphasized seriously.

"...That’s true. We were never meant to exit the stage of history." Old Samy nodded in agreement.

"As long as we use the forbidden secret art of the former kingdom to revive my father, and then use the Holy Dragon’s blood obtained from Democritus to..." Swinburne pondered for a moment, suddenly feeling an overwhelming excitement. "My father will become even stronger than before! He will return in his full, mighty form, an existence unmatched by anyone!"

"Exactly. With the old president’s power, uniting all the dark guilds will be a piece of cake." Old Samy said earnestly.

"That..." Cooper, who seemed a bit impatient, interjected, "I don’t really understand the situation, but it seems like something worth celebrating, right?"

"Cooper, you’re new here. You don’t understand what the old president means to us. He represents the glory of the Howling Ghost Praise." Old Samy’s tone was serious as he emphasized.

"Uh, fine..." Cooper hadn’t been with the Howling Ghost Praise for long and didn’t quite grasp their obsession. As long as he got paid to do the job, it was fine. "So what’s our next task?"

"We need to find a place that’s easy to defend but hard to attack, then immediately begin the resurrection ritual. Not a moment can be wasted." Swinburne said gravely.

"Huh?" Cooper’s expression was a bit lazy, awkwardly saying, "Do we have to be in such a hurry?"

"We’ve already been noticed by the Empire. To avoid unnecessary trouble, the sooner, the better." Swinburne said seriously.

"Being noticed by the Empire? What’s that about?" Old Samy’s aged face showed a hint of shock.

"This codex from the former kingdom was deliberately given to us by that old hag Elizabeth. She wants to use us to consolidate her position, but all of it will be in vain." Swinburne revealed a smug smile, full of confidence. "The day my father is revived will be the day the Empire perishes!"

"Tch, that bitch Elizabeth, actually trying to use us. She’s really asking for it! When the old president returns, the first thing we’ll do is destroy Great Britain!" Old Samy said angrily, feeling a hint of humiliation.

"So we need to hurry. Before someone comes to ruin our plans, we must finish everything." Swinburne already knew what would happen next. There would definitely be many of the Empire’s lackeys coming to hunt them down. But this passive situation would be reversed once Palmer was revived.

"What about waiting for Grace?" Cooper asked tentatively, his mind indeed heavy with lust.

"No need. The three of us are enough. Even if the Empire’s First Thorn Knight comes, it’s not certain he can defeat me." Swinburne commanded in a tone that made Cooper behave.

"......" Cooper nodded, feeling a bit disappointed inside, but given Swinburne’s overwhelming strength, he didn’t dare to act recklessly.

Swinburne ordered them to start the resurrection plan immediately and then take revenge on the Empire.

He flicked the cigarette butt from his mouth, casually throwing it to the ground. Suddenly, a vast expanse of deep blue flames surged up, instantly engulfing the entire town!

The blue flames blazed into the sky, burning everything in the remote town to ashes, roaring as they reached the heavens.

The screams and wails from behind came in waves. By tomorrow, probably no one would remember this place.

Swinburne’s eyes blazed like torches, his expression like a defiant warrior resisting fate, without the slightest hint of mercy—

That bitch Elizabeth dared to look down on them?

Then she better wash her neck clean and prepare to pay the painful price!

---

For the past two months and more... Merlin had been acting as Alice’s sparring partner, assisting in her training. Unfortunately, Alice’s progress had been far from noticeable, as if she had hit an insurmountable bottleneck.

Whether Merlin was there or not, it seemed to make little difference. Alice was stuck in a stalemate, unable to advance.

And the most critical issue was the dragonification corruption, which had been accelerating far faster than before.

Now, Alice’s body was covered in dragon scales over more than 50% of her surface, making it increasingly difficult to conceal.

Alice could no longer wear her usual clothes. She had to switch to long, concealing garments, even in summer.

Otherwise, she might scare people or attract strange stares.

After all, in human lands, suddenly encountering someone with scales on their body would inevitably shock people, making them suspect she was some kind of foreign race.

So, to avoid causing trouble for others, Alice had no choice but to live in this sneaky, hidden way.

In truth, Alice felt a little wronged. She felt more and more like a monster, living in hiding. It was something she would have found unimaginable in the past!

Alice deeply regretted it. If she had known, she never would have consumed that Ice Frost Holy Dragon’s inheritance crystal. Then she wouldn’t have ended up in such a dire situation today.

These past few days, Alice had been in low spirits, completely lacking the mood to argue with Merlin. She would always hide in her room, heartbroken, feeling as if death was not far away.

In the past, she had felt young, with plenty of time to live freely. But now, her life had to be counted by the day—how tragic!

It wasn’t that Alice was being overly pessimistic. The situation was simply too dire, making her tense and sensitive.

For over two months, her strength had improved at a snail’s pace. Recently, no matter how hard she tried, there was no progress at all.

Alice had already given up hope. The day she would become a Saint-tier powerhouse seemed infinitely distant, as if there was no hope left.

Moreover, the three-month deadline Merlin had mentioned was drawing nearer. She could feel her body gradually stiffening, becoming less responsive.

Even last night, Alice had sadly considered in her room whether to leave a will, to distribute her assets.

Because Alice had been so down lately, she hadn’t even argued with Merlin, which made things feel off. Merlin felt like something was missing from his life. It was as if without a daily argument with Alice, his day felt incomplete—how pathetic.

But Merlin wasn’t so tactless. Seeing Alice in this state, he naturally wouldn’t provoke her. Instead, he silently took care of this unlucky girl.

The first ray of morning sunlight spilled down. Today was another day of training as usual.

Even though having Merlin accompany her in training didn’t seem to help, Merlin still felt it wasn’t right to leave Alice alone.

After all, that inheritance crystal had been obtained by Merlin. He couldn’t help but feel that Alice’s misfortune was somewhat his responsibility. He still had a bit of a conscience.

Merlin and Alice left together, beginning another busy day.

Alice wore a white robe, pulling the hood up to cover the dragon scales on her neck.

Merlin felt a sudden chill, as if something filthy was staring at him. He couldn’t help but shiver.

At the far end of the apartment corridor, Jenna peeked her small head around the corner, her face flushed, secretly watching Merlin. Her eyes were filled with infatuated stars, and unconsciously, drool had begun to drip from the corner of her mouth.

"Cold and cruel Merlin-sama is so manly today as well, huff huff~"

title: Chapter 28 — The Proposal
content:
Chapter 28 — The Proposal

Volume 9 · Chapter 28

These past couple of months, Jenna had been sneaking glances at Merlin every few days, her face glowing with infatuation.

She found that cold, domineering aura of his quite charming, yet she completely overlooked his severe case of laziness.

Jenna, this naive little girl, was usually impossible to pull back once she fell into a daze, always chasing after her own idealized prince on a white horse.

Who knows what kind of messed-up thinking this girl had, managing to see that aloof Merlin as cold and domineering? Could it be that his aura of authority was leaking through?

Moreover, even Arnold felt something was off with his little sister lately, but he wasn't offering any advice. Every day he'd sit there clutching his toy bear, chuckling to himself, lost in some infatuated daydream.

This left Arnold quite baffled. What on earth was wrong with his sister? Did she finally set her sights on that guy?

Arnold tried to probe around casually, but Jenna just made up excuses and avoided the topic.

After all, Jenna held the title of Love Master. Now she'd suddenly fallen for Merlin but couldn't figure him out—wasn't that just embarrassing?

But Jenna was getting a bit frantic, because as a Love Master, she had no tricks up her sleeve for Merlin.

Over these past two months, Jenna had tried every method to win Merlin over, but this guy seemed completely impervious to both soft and hard approaches.

Not even the classic "accidentally bumping into love" routine worked. Even his "stranger danger" vibe was written all over his face, making people feel uncomfortable all over.

So this little lovesick girl could only sneak glances at Merlin in this pitiful way, at least getting some visual satisfaction.

Merlin sensed the predatory gaze, scanned his surroundings, and sure enough spotted Jenna peeking around with her little head, drool literally dripping as she stared at him.

"Ugh... Arnold's idiot sister..."

A bunch of dark lines appeared on Merlin's forehead, his face turning slightly ugly. He was already getting pretty fed up.

Lately, Merlin had noticed Jenna always lurking in the shadows watching him. But since she was a masochist, the more he scolded her, the more she enjoyed it, leaving Merlin feeling helpless.

Merlin was in a rather helpless mood now. Being stalked felt really uncomfortable, like swallowing a fly.

Jenna, upon realizing she'd been caught, quickly ducked her head back down, her heart racing.

She pressed her palms against her flushed cheeks, internally delighted, and mumbled with a drip of saliva.

"...Crap, I got caught by Master Merlin... hehe..."

"H-Hey, why is it her again? Ugh!"

Alice puffed out her cheeks, looking like a hamster stuffing food, glaring at Merlin with obvious displeasure.

What was so great about this scoundrel? There were countless people better than him. Why was she always clinging to him?

Tsundere inner monologue: "That's my husband—get lost, you fox spirit!"

"Tch!" Merlin rolled his eyes, awkwardly saying, "What are you staring at? Are you trying to publicly humiliate me or something?"

"Hmph!" Alice sniffed disdainfully. It seemed like she had nothing to do with Merlin, but she just couldn't help feeling annoyed.

"Let's just ignore this freak. If we get entangled with her, it'll only get more troublesome. Let's go."

Merlin decisively didn't want to deal with Jenna's infatuation. Better to avoid trouble than invite it.

"Yeah, let's go."

Alice tugged at Merlin's sleeve, her mood slightly improved.

.

The training ground.

Merlin was here with Alice, practicing martial arts.

A fierce cold energy suddenly attacked. Merlin swung his wooden sword in a fierce arc, shattering it.

"Cough!"

Alice let out a pained cry, her body flying backward. She crashed into the ground ten meters away, finally coming to a stop.

She knelt on the ground, supporting herself with her thin sword, panting heavily, sweat dripping down her face.

The blue and white scales on Alice's neck were already quite prominent, and even her arms showed them. The situation was clearly much worse than at the beginning.

Merlin stood in place, watching Alice's condition with a frown. He felt she was starting to go down a dangerous path, only chasing quick results and gradually losing her proper composure.

Alice took a breath, then pushed herself up, gripping her thin sword and pointing it at Merlin, declaring firmly:

"Let's go again!"

"Fine..." Merlin tapped his shoulder with his wooden sword, putting on an indifferent act. He clearly wasn't in the mood to fight anymore.

"Why? I'm still fine! Let's continue!" Alice's fighting spirit flared up, seemingly unwilling to give up so easily.

"You've lost your calm. You keep wanting to achieve results through increasingly harsh methods. This won't lead to anything good—it'll only end up hurting yourself."

Merlin's expression turned serious as he spoke. Wasn't cultivation something that couldn't be rushed overnight? Like this, his strength wouldn't improve at all, and worse, he might end up hurting himself.

"It's fine, I can still continue..." Alice said stubbornly, with a hint of melancholy in her eyes.

"No."

Merlin firmly refused. This wasn't something to take lightly.

......

Light novel.

Alice bit her lip and stayed silent, lowering her head, gripping her thin sword tightly. Her slender body began to tremble involuntarily.

A wave of immense sadness washed over her, making Alice feel more wronged than ever. She thought she was so unlucky.

Three months wasn't enough time at all. It was impossible to break through to Saint-tier in just three months. With so little time left, she could only feel desperate.

Alice's eyes turned red, her nose started to run, and she felt like crying. Tears swirled in her eyes.

"A... what am I supposed to do? I don't want to... turn into a little dragon. I want to live..."

A cold sweat broke out on Merlin's forehead. Wait, was she actually about to cry? Come on!

Usually she was so fearless, undaunted by heaven or earth. How had she suddenly transformed into a helpless little girl?

What the hell! Such a drastic change was hard to accept...

Merlin looked away. He didn't like seeing girls cry and whimper, always feeling some inexplicable resistance.

"Three months..."

Alice bit her lip, tears glistening as she spoke, "Three months is too short for me... How exactly am I supposed to ascend to Saint-tier? Now there's less than half a month left..."

"Don't cry, okay? Calm down."

Merlin sighed helplessly.

"..."

Alice bit her lip, trying hard not to make any sound. She didn't seem to want to cry in front of Merlin, showing her weak side.

But emotions were hard to control. Her mouth pouted, eyelashes clinging to tears, looking even more pitiful.

"This damn girl..."

Merlin pressed his hand against his forehead, feeling a headache coming on, completely at a loss for what to do.

He thought to himself, did the demon race have any solutions? Since the ancient demon texts mentioned the Successor Crystal, maybe there was other information he'd overlooked.

If Alice still couldn't break through to Saint-tier by the end of this week, he'd have no choice but to take her back to the Death Marsh. Perhaps there would be a way.

But he didn't know whether this stubborn girl would be willing to come with him.

Merlin pondered for a while, then looked at Alice and spoke in a more serious tone:

"Alice, would you like to come back to my hometown with me?"

"Eh?"

Alice was stunned, her eyes flickering as she seemed to drift off somewhere.

"...What exactly do you mean?"

"Are you... proposing to me in disguise?"

title: Chapter 29 — Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 29 — Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 29

Alice's face flushed red. Merlin's words felt ambiguous—what did he mean by asking her to return to his homeland with him?!

The more she thought about it, the more it sounded like a marriage proposal, leaving Alice completely flustered.

But she didn’t want to cause any misunderstandings, so she decided to probe carefully. Otherwise, if things turned into a joke, it would be too embarrassing.

"I...,"

Merlin rolled his eyes in exasperation. "Where is your mind going? As long as my brain isn’t waterlogged, how could I possibly propose to you? Miss, have some self-respect..."

"Hmph!" Alice huffed, pouting, yet an inexplicable sense of loss welled up inside her. "Then what do you want?"

"Come back to the demon race with me. Maybe we can find a solution to your dragon transformation problem. After all, our demon race has a long history—perhaps we can find a way." Merlin said seriously.

"R-Really?" Alice’s heart stirred, a glimmer of hope returning to her eyes.

"It’s not guaranteed, but there’s a chance. Isn’t that better than just waiting here to die?" Merlin shrugged, feeling that the path he offered Alice was a safe one.

Alice fell into hesitation, weighing Merlin’s proposal. Reality and pride clashed in her mind—

Should she go to the demon race with Merlin?

How could she? Who would go to the demon race’s territory with Merlin?

She was once the Hero—had she really fallen so low as to seek help from demons?

What a humiliation! No, she didn’t want to become Merlin’s slave.

And Merlin really thought too little of her, didn’t he? He’d already decided she couldn’t become a Saint-tier powerhouse.

Damn it, stop underestimating me!

Alice suddenly lifted her head, pouting with reddened eyes. "No need. I won’t go to the demon race with you. I believe in myself."

Merlin instantly pressed a hand to his forehead. This stubborn mule of an Alice was beyond help. Why was she so obstinate? This was a matter of life and death! Couldn’t she just set aside her prejudices and bend a little to survive?

"Alice, are you serious?"

"Mhm. I absolutely won’t regret it." Alice said with utmost sincerity, tightening her grip on her rapier once more.

Merlin furrowed his brows. This stupid girl’s personality was truly the worst. Wasn’t he just trying to help? And she didn’t even appreciate it! Relying on others a little wouldn’t kill her.

"If there’s nothing else, you should leave. I still need to continue training. And tomorrow, I won’t need you to accompany me either. It’s not like there’s been any progress." Alice said sternly, outright chasing Merlin away.

Probably still holding a grudge over being looked down on, huh?

Indeed, a girl this stubborn was hard to get along with... even for Merlin.

---

After being chased away by Alice, Merlin had no choice but to return to the Adventurers Guild and continue drinking gloomily with Hobbes.

Merlin looked thoroughly dejected. He snatched Hobbes’ cup and started freeloading drinks again.

Hobbes watched as his cup was about to be drained by Merlin. This wouldn’t do!

So Hobbes quickly snatched his cup back, signaling Merlin to stop stealing his alcohol.

"Merlin, wait a second. What’s wrong with you? You look like you’ve been a victim of domestic abuse. Did Alice hit you?"

"Pfft! How is that possible? Me, getting hit by Alice? You’re joking..." Merlin scoffed, thinking it was more likely he’d be the one hitting Alice.

"Then what’s wrong? You look so gloomy~" Hobbes examined Merlin, then subconsciously hugged his wine bottle tighter, as if guarding it from a thief.

"..." Merlin hesitated, then gave a rough explanation. "It’s just that Alice and I have been a little... unhappy lately."

"Oh? Marital discord? That’s a good thing! Couples who don’t argue aren’t normal." Hobbes wore the expression of someone who’d been through it all.

"...It’s not really a dispute." Merlin scratched his head, feeling that calling it a "dispute" with Alice was a bit too serious.

"Hmm?" Hobbes narrowed his eyes, as if he’d figured it out. He wore a lecherous grin and whispered, "Is it a lack of harmony in your private life? Has Alice been too demanding, leaving you struggling to keep up? That’s why you’re so annoyed..."

Ugh... Merlin frowned. This old man Hobbes couldn’t think of anything but nonsense. What was going on in that head of his?

"Wow, impressive. Who knew Alice, so young, would have such high... needs. They say thirty is like a wolf, forty like a tiger, fifty can pull the earth up by sitting—Alice is going to be unstoppable in the future!" Hobbes looked horrified, patting Merlin’s shoulder sympathetically. "Friend, you’re in for a tough time."

"Get lost!" Merlin swatted Hobbes’ paw away. "What kind of nonsense are you spouting? None of that’s true."

Hobbes looked utterly confused, unable to grasp what had happened between Alice and Merlin.

"I’m just confused why Alice doesn’t trust me. Is it because I’ve tricked her before?" Merlin stroked his chin, looking perplexed. He felt Alice had a strong bias against him, always on guard.

"Ah~" Hobbes chuckled, suddenly understanding. He spoke with confidence, as if he had it all figured out. "So it’s a trust issue between husband and wife? You should’ve said so earlier! I’m an expert on this. Sure, I visit Helena’s secret room every day, but in over ten years of marriage, I’ve never had a trust crisis!"

"Go on..." Merlin asked with interest. If Hobbes was this confident, maybe he’d actually say something useful.

"Take more kidney-tonifying medicine, turn in your family homework on time, settle conflicts in bed, not out of it. Trust me, if your skills are good enough, trust issues won’t exist."

Hobbes said with a wicked grin. If this were the real world, this man would’ve been arrested long ago.

"..." Merlin sighed, looking away. "I actually believed you’d have a good solution. I must be an idiot."

At the table closest to Merlin, three adventurers were passionately discussing something.

"Hey, did you hear? The Rakshasa Faction has already entered the Empire. Rumor is their goal is to overthrow the kingdom."

"That’s old news from months ago. I heard the Rakshasa Faction wants to revive the guild leader from 30 years ago—the awe-inspiring Phantom Flame Rakshasa!"

"Seriously?"

"This is inside info from the Empire. Everyone knows now, and people are panicking."

"It’s probably true. Yesterday, a remote town in Wales was destroyed. They say members of the Rakshasa Faction were seen there."

"This is bad. If the Rakshasa Faction succeeds, the Empire might face another catastrophic calamity."

"Yeah, more and more people are fleeing to the king for refuge. I’ve even been thinking about leaving the Empire for a while to lie low."

Merlin withdrew his gaze, his brows knitting deeply. His mind was restless, like a stormy sea.

What was going on?

He couldn’t shake the feeling that Britannia had been unusually chaotic lately...

(°の∞)

title: Chapter 30 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 30 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 9 · Chapter 30

Merlin felt something was off. Ever since he went to the royal capital, everything around him seemed to have become restless.

"Is... the Empire not at peace?"

Merlin muttered thoughtfully, looking at Hobbes across from him, wondering if this well-informed man might know something.

"Isn't it? Things have been really unstable lately. The entire empire is on high alert, checkpoints everywhere have extra personnel, and the royal capital isn't even allowing outsiders in anymore." Hobbes paused meaningfully. "The most unlucky ones are probably the local garrison troops. That guy, Price, hasn't been home for over half a month now. Really unlucky."

"Is this because of the Houki Reisai incident?" Merlin narrowed his eyes, probing cautiously.

"Exactly! The Houki Reisai has been causing such a stir lately. My wife keeps telling me to come home on time, absolutely no wandering around outside. Everyone's on edge, terrified of running into those Houki Reisai people." Hobbes looked at Merlin, raising an eyebrow. "Those guys kill without hesitation. Wherever they appear, rivers of blood follow. You get it, right?"

"So dangerous?" Merlin stroked his chin, looking thoughtful.

"Too right! Just last night, I heard a small town was massacred. The Empire already confirmed it was the work of Houki Reisai. No doubt about it." Hobbes frowned, clearly disliking this martial law lifestyle. It felt restrictive. Now, any suspicious behavior outside would get you stopped and questioned by the guards.

Merlin didn’t respond. Instead, he felt that Houki Reisai, as a dark guild, was acting far too openly. Not at all like thieves trying to stay hidden.

Po)5

CCZ Xiaoxin

"Lately, the Empire has been issuing a lot of alert messages. Even the major newspapers are saying Houki Reisai is extremely dangerous. Everyone’s scared of being targeted by them. Now more and more people are starting to lose hope. If this continues, it might cause even greater chaos." Hobbes speculated, suddenly turning into a great prophet.

"Come on, the Empire is so huge. How could a small dark guild throw it into such disarray?" Merlin thought Hobbes was exaggerating.

"How couldn’t it? Think about it—Houki Reisai wants to revive Palmer. Didn’t I tell you before how terrifying that monster is? It makes sense that it would threaten the Empire’s safety." Hobbes said seriously.

Merlin fell silent, wondering if Palmer was really that overpowered. He couldn’t help but feel Hobbes was too weak, so maybe he saw everyone else as incredibly strong.

This wasn’t about Merlin not trusting Hobbes—it was just that everyone had different perspectives. The gap in strength naturally led to huge differences in perception.

Often, someone others considered invincibly powerful would, in Merlin’s eyes, basically be a noob, not worth mentioning.

"By the way, the calls for the Great Swordsman Elgin have been pretty loud lately..." Hobbes suddenly said.

"Ah?!" Merlin’s eyes widened in disbelief.

"What’s so surprising? When people are in panic, they naturally hope for a hero to step up and eliminate the threat. Look, is there anyone more popular than Elgin the Great Swordsman right now?" Hobbes spread his hands, as if stating the obvious.

...Merlin was left speechless. He thought to himself that he really didn’t want to go out wearing the mask of Elgin the Great Swordsman and cause trouble anymore. It would only end up disrupting his life sooner or later.

Sigh, what a hassle.

Why do these humans have to be so obsessed with me?

I’m just a fleeting, beautiful legend.

The perfect hero you imagine doesn’t exist. He just wants to freeload and live an easy life...

Night fell.

The two prepared to eat dinner and then sleep.

Merlin tied on an apron, acting like a considerate man as he prepared the meal.

Truthfully, Merlin didn’t want to cook at all. He found it boring, a complete waste of his precious life.

But Alice was in no state to cook or help with anything right now.

Merlin wasn’t so unreasonable as to pick a fight with Alice over this, nitpicking every little thing. There was no point.

Moreover, Merlin did feel a tiny bit of guilt. If he had known Alice’s emotions were this unstable and prone to backlash, he would’ve been better off feeding the inheritance crystal to a dog.

QE This novel

At this moment, Alice sat woodenly in her chair, looking unusually docile, as if she had lost her soul.

There was no expression on her face, her eyes empty, staring at the white plate in front of her, lost in some unknown thoughts.

Alice had lost her usual vitality. Even Merlin, seeing her lifeless state, felt uncomfortable, an inexplicable irritation gnawing at him.

Normally, Alice would be noisy at times like this—if she went quiet, it was like she was dead. She had to at least mock Merlin a couple of times to feel happy.

Though Merlin usually found it unbearably annoying, he didn’t exactly hate Alice’s clingy, bratty behavior.

Now that Alice was this quiet, like a proper lady, Merlin couldn’t stand it. He even felt a little pathetic for feeling this way.

Wasn’t this better? At least no one was bothering him. He could quietly do whatever he liked.

Wasn’t this the peaceful life he had always dreamed of? This sense of loss was truly inexplicable!

Merlin kept trying to reassure himself, but he had to admit—he really did prefer Alice when she was lively.

Alice was in a terrible mood, so sad she didn’t even know what to do with herself.

Her mind was filled with the approaching deadline, how much longer she had to live, or if there was anything she regretted not doing.

Merlin untied his apron, then carried over the dinner and placed it in front of Alice.

"Eat up. Your favorite hamburg steak. No one’s going to fight you for it this time."

Merlin said teasingly, but Alice acted as if she hadn’t heard, leaving him feeling utterly bored.

"Just eat first. You’re so lucky, nothing bad will happen to you. Maybe at the last moment, the Goddess of Fortune will remember she has a daughter and come through for you. Trust me."

Alice remained silent.

"Tch!" Merlin rolled his eyes, thinking, *This idiot is going to drive me crazy if she keeps this up!*

Alice looked at her arm, now covered in blue and white dragon scales, which showed no sign of stopping, already spreading toward her palm.

In about a week, Alice would probably be unable to show her face in public at all. She’d have to hide in some cold corner, waiting for the moment her consciousness was devoured.

Alice lowered her arm, her eyes reddening as a wave of sorrow washed over her. She bowed her head, her lips trembling as she whispered,

"Hey... Merlin..."

"If I’m not here anymore... will you be happy?"

title: Chapter 31 — Forbidden Land
content:
Chapter 31 — Forbidden Land

Volume 9 · Chapter 31

"Huh?!"

Merlin's gaze wavered visibly at Alice's sudden question, and he froze mid-motion with his knife and fork in hand.

Would he be happy if Alice disappeared?

That... was a question worth pondering.

Logically speaking, life would return to peace, so he should be happy, right?

After all, he had no ambitions—he just wanted to find a chance to freeload until death, living a life of idle leisure.

But would that really be the case? Without that troublemaker around, it seemed like there would be a lot less fun.

After a brief moment of thought, Merlin decided to give a perfectly normal answer—anything else would just cause unnecessary trouble.

"Uh... Of course! I'd definitely be happy! One less source of trouble—isn't that something to celebrate?"

Alice's expression turned aggrieved, as if deeply hurt. Merlin seemed to have no humanity at all.

They had lived together for half a year—if someone suddenly vanished, shouldn't he feel some sadness?

At the very least, if Merlin disappeared, she would feel a little unsettled. She might not be heartbroken, but she would definitely feel some resistance or discomfort.

Alice silently clenched her fists, unwilling to accept this. She couldn't help but press further.

"Then... then you wouldn't feel sad?"

"Sad? Why would I feel sad? That would be the abnormal part..."

Merlin spread his hands, feeling that he and Alice were fundamentally different—perhaps even different species. Their values just didn't align.

And the only reason Merlin and Alice were together was mutual benefit. As for any other reason? He truly couldn't think of one.

"...You have no humanity!" Alice's eyes reddened. Hadn't she treated him well? She had recommended him to the Adventurers Guild, taken in a homeless man like him... She never expected this outcome. He was nothing but an ungrateful wretch!

"I *am* a demon, okay?" Merlin's expression was complicated as he met Alice's gaze. "First, I admit that if you disappeared, it would affect me to some extent. But it wouldn't be fatal. As long as I return to the demon race, nothing could bother me. Do you understand? We're just a community of shared interests. Even if we separate, neither of us would fail to survive."

Though Merlin said this, he certainly didn't want to return to the Death Swamp. After all, who would want to go back after being a shut-in for over 200 years?

"Get out of my sight! Go back to where you came from! I never want to see you again!"

Alice, eyes red, stood up with a *whoosh* and stormed back to her room, not even finishing dinner.

Merlin furrowed his brow, staring at Alice's tightly shut door, his thoughts in disarray.

I only spoke the truth. What's wrong with that?

Why is that nagging woman throwing such a tantrum? Is she going through early menopause...?

---

Late at night.

Merlin was fast asleep on the sofa, covered with a blanket, when he heard faint, intermittent sobbing.

His eyes snapped open. He sat up, frowning, and looked toward Alice's room.

What was wrong with Alice at this hour?

Merlin got up and walked to Alice's door, listening carefully. The crying was unmistakable.

It was so late, yet Alice wasn't asleep—she was alone in her room, heartbroken.

The choked sobs came in broken bursts, occasionally punctuated by mumbled words too quiet for anyone to make out.

Merlin felt an inexplicable stir in his chest, his mood turning restless. Should he go in and comfort Alice?

He raised his hand, intending to knock, but after a few flickers of hesitation, he silently lowered it again.

After some thought, he decided Alice probably needed to be alone right now. She definitely wouldn't want to see him.

Forget it. Tomorrow morning, he'd go ask Asmodeus if there was a solution...

---

A sealed underground chamber.

On the screen of a remote communication device sat a woman of incomparable beauty.

Asmodeus looked at Merlin and asked softly, "So... Merlin, what brings you to me today?"

"Just a small problem I wanted to ask about." Merlin scratched his head awkwardly.

"You actually took the initiative to come to me? That's rare." Asmodeus teased. "Ask away. As a friend, I'll answer anything you want to know."

"Ah-hem!" Merlin cleared his throat and got straight to the point. "How much do you know about the Dragon Clan's Legacy Crystals?"

"Oh? Legacy Crystals?" Asmodeus seemed somewhat familiar with the topic. "Aren't those rare items that grant the power and heritage of the Dragon Clan?"

"Then I have to ask..." Merlin paused, then asked seriously, "If a human is being corrupted by a Legacy Crystal, is there any way to stop it?"

"Corrupted by a Legacy Crystal? Just how weak is this host?" Asmodeus sounded surprised. "Under normal circumstances, this shouldn't even be a problem."

"Well, they *are* quite weak. Not even Saint-tier." Merlin replied awkwardly, thinking that anyone below Saint-tier would barely register in the eyes of demon lords.

"Hah?" Asmodeus was genuinely shocked, half-laughing. "Someone below Saint-tier dares to absorb a Legacy Crystal? That's practically suicide! Seeking power beyond one's control will always backfire. That's an unchanging rule."

Merlin's expression turned awkward. While he bore some responsibility, the real issue was Alice's unstable emotions—she kept forcing the Legacy Crystal's power to activate, leading to the current uncontrollable situation.

"May I ask who's this unlucky person?" Asmodeus asked curiously. Given that Merlin had come to her specifically for this, the person must be important.

Otherwise, based on Asmodeus's understanding of Merlin—a terminally lazy demon—he wouldn't bother with other people's problems.

"Uh..." Merlin hesitated, but didn't see much point in hiding it. "It's the one living with me. Things are bad—she's starting to suffer backlash from the Legacy Crystal's power."

"Oh? Sounds urgent." Asmodeus sighed.

"Do you have any way to stop the corruption?" Merlin asked patiently, feeling time was running out.

"This..." Asmodeus paused, then answered sincerely, "Basically, no."

"Is that so..." Merlin let out a deep sigh. He had expected as much.

"But there *is* a way to delay it..." Asmodeus suddenly changed the subject.

"Eh? What is it?" Merlin perked up, sensing a possible turn for the better.

"Immerse that pitiful human in the Blood Pool at the very bottom of the Demon Lord Palace..." Asmodeus's tone was unusually serious, as if she wasn't joking.

"You should know that the greatest secret of our demon race is the Blood Pools guarded beneath each of the seven Demon Lord Palaces. The underground cores of these pools are interconnected, forming the grandest sealing array in history, suppressing the Great Demon Gods of the Old Covenant. If the seal weakens, it would mean the end of our demon race. That's why we demons cannot leave the Demon Lord Palaces for too long—maintaining the stability of the Blood Pools is the key to the survival of our race."

Merlin's brow furrowed. As one of the Seven Demon Lords, he naturally knew this secret—he just didn't see how it related to Alice.

Beneath the seven Demon Lord Palaces, the Blood Pools sealed away the monsters from the dawn of creation—the ancestors of the demon race, the Great Demon Gods of the Old Covenant.

The demons of the Age of Gods were nothing like those of today. They had no human form; they were all colossal beasts that shook the heavens and the earth.

All demons of the current era were newcomers, a subspecies of the Old Covenant Demon Gods. Though still demons, they were creatures of a new age.

At the twilight of the Age of Gods, the Great Demons of the Old Covenant also faced their downfall, giving rise to the new generation.

These demon gods were sealed in the Blood Pools by the first Seven Demon Lords, marking the end of the old era.

Before sinking into the Blood Pools, the Old Covenant Demon Gods made an oath that still unsettled many demons to this day:

*"When we once again see the sun outside, we shall bring a perfect end to all civilizations!"*

The power of these demon gods was too great to be destroyed—they could only be sealed. Yet they still writhed, requiring constant maintenance of the Blood Pools to keep them suppressed.

This was also the fundamental reason why the demon race always stayed within their own territories, reluctant to venture outside.

Even the activities of the Demon Lords were restricted by the council—none could leave their Demon Lord Palace for more than 14 days.

As for Merlin, who had been exiled, naturally he wasn't bound by this rule. Still, the Blood Pool beneath the First Demon Lord Palace should have someone maintaining it.

After a moment's thought, Merlin realized it must be Lilith handling the seal. Otherwise, with that girl's temper, she would have long since left the Death Swamp to find her brother.

"You know all this, but what does the Blood Pool seal have to do with the person at my place?"

"The Blood Pool's property is time cessation. Time inside the seal is completely frozen. So, you could use it—immerse that human in the Blood Pool, and any abnormal state will halt." Asmodeus explained. Few knew of this method, but since Merlin was the former Demon Lord of Pride, it was fine to tell him.

"Ah, I see..." Merlin stroked his chin, tempted. If it could stop Alice's dragonification, that would work.

"But this won't fundamentally stop the dragonification—it's only a way to indefinitely delay it." Asmodeus added indifferently.

"Tch! If it can't solve the root problem, what's the point of mentioning it?" Merlin scoffed, feeling Asmodeus was wasting his time.

"You can indefinitely delay the human's corruption by the Dragon Clan's power, buying enough time to find another solution. When the time is right, you can pull her out of the Blood Pool and treat her." Asmodeus calmly unfolded her fan.

Merlin fell silent. The method wasn't impossible—it was a stopgap measure. But if no solution was found, Alice, submerged in the Blood Pool, would essentially be a living corpse. Who knew how long it would take to find a way to reverse the dragonification?

"But I advise you not to do it." Asmodeus paused, then earnestly warned, "A mere human isn't worth it."

"The Blood Pools are a secret of our demon race. Absolutely no outsider must know of them."

"Even if this human is important to you, don't use the method I just mentioned."

"Because—"

"A mere human has no right to set foot in our sacred forbidden ground."

title: Chapter 32 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 32 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 32

Merlin stared at Asmodeus with a blank expression, but said nothing. Instead, he seemed quite understanding.

The attitude of most demons toward humans was basically on par with livestock, showing no mercy whatsoever.

If Merlin weren't a human soul who had transmigrated, he would probably feel the same as other demons—indifferent to human life and death.

Putting it on an equal footing, humans would care about the life and death of a stray dog, would they not?

Demons viewing humans is the same as humans viewing stray dogs; it's not some strange perspective.

Seeing Merlin's expression of complete indifference, Asmodeus couldn't help but continue—

"If you truly take a human to the blood pool, that would be a fundamental error. Then, certainly, a series of troubles would ensue, at the very least the Council would not tolerate it.

"You should know, the blood pool seal is the foundation of our demon race's survival. If such a secret concerning the survival of our race were known by another race, it would place all our kin in danger.

"Perhaps the Council wouldn't need to issue an order; countless demons would rush to kill that human, and you would also be held responsible. You must think this through carefully..."

Merlin gave no indication, but merely grinned, laughed dryly, and said, "You don't need to remind me of such things; I know it myself. Don't be so serious. I was just asking casually. For the sake of one human, to cause myself trouble? I haven't been stupid enough to do that."

"Then..." Asmodeus nodded, slightly relieved.

"Since there's no way around it, I'll go back. Thank you for telling me so much..." Merlin stood up to leave.

"Don't be so polite, after all, you are my cherished..." Asmodeus gave a shallow smile, making one's heart race.

Merlin smiled and turned to leave. Just as he pushed open the door, he saw Helena standing respectfully outside, waiting to see him off.

Helena saw Merlin emerge from the inner chamber and gave a slight bow, expressing her respect for the monarch.

"His Majesty Lucifer..."

Merlin nodded, about to walk away, when Asmodeus suddenly spoke up, seemingly with some hidden concern.

"Friend, wait a moment."

"Is there anything else?" Merlin turned his head in surprise.

"Not to forget, you are the former haughty monarch, one of the seven kings of the demon race. The Council does not allow demons to intermarry with lowly humans. If ordinary demons intermarry with humans, they will be exiled. Your identity is difficult to handle so simply. Perhaps your name will be engraved on the demon race's pillar of shame, subjected to hostility from your own kin, and even that group of old fellows in the Council might not be able to sit still; they might propose erasing this shame of the demon race. Then, what you face will not be blessings but a sweeping demon king..."

Asmodeus's expression was serious; he wasn't joking with Merlin. As a friend, some things must be said in advance, such as becoming enemies.

"Why say these things?" Merlin gave a light smile, appearing nonchalant.

"You won't like a lowly human woman, will you? If you do, I hope you look back and don't reach a point where it's irreparable with regret." Asmodeus looked into Merlin's eyes, waiting for his answer.

The nearby Helena was also somewhat surprised, gazing at Merlin in astonishment. It was hard to imagine that the great demon lord, the proud monarch, would like a human woman. This was truly incomprehensible.

Humans would like a monkey, obviously not.

Similarly, demons would not like humans either, for in their eyes, humans are lowly beings.

If a demon and a human were to intermarry, the matter would be very serious, completely going against the demon race's position.

Helena stared at Merlin, feeling somewhat uncomfortable in her heart. The demon race has many excellent women; why get entangled with a human girl? Indeed, what the master said is correct; Lucifer among the seven monarchs is the most peculiar in character, and his behavior is too close to humans.

Merlin was silent for a moment, shook his head, and smiled as he tilted the corner of his mouth—

"How is that possible?"

Alice was still preparing to cultivate, though hope was already faint, she still refused to give up easily.

As for Merlin, who knew what he did early in the morning?

He was thrown aside, and not even a word of comfort. He was truly heartless to the extreme.

Alice didn't say anything on her mouth, but her heart was still very sad, hoping Merlin could comfort her.

The result was very chilling; Alice was very disappointed in Merlin. After all, he is a demon; how could one expect him to be like a Bodhisattva with boundless light?

Poor and pitiful Alice felt weak and pitiable. Not even her nominal husband cared about her; there was not a bit of feeling.

When Alice entered the guild, she happened to run into Da Vinci and Rosetti, who had just returned. It seemed they had returned this morning, intending to tidy up in the guild now.

"Alice~ , here here!" Rosetti greeted enthusiastically, her ample bosom swaying, making people dizzy.

"..."

A drop of cold sweat slid down Alice's forehead; she wasn't too willing to touch Rosetti.

Nevertheless, since they were somewhat familiar, Alice had to walk over and gave a slight greeting.

"... Good long time... "

"Good long time, Alice lady." Da Vinci—seriously responded.

"Did you complete the mission and come back?" Alice asked tentatively.

"Of course it is. This time the gains were considerable, and we also met quite a few good men, constantly clinging to me, it's really annoying~" Rosetti waved her hand and started her bragging habit again, as if without stimulation Alice would die—.

"Hmm.

Alice frowned tightly, a little regretful for having spoken to Rosetti.

"Tsk tsk, having such large breasts is annoying. If they were a little smaller, there wouldn't be so many lowly men coming to bother me. I think your washboard, Alice, is good enough; basically no opposite-sex interest, and no one would bother you. I'm so envious~" Rosetti's expression was deep with meaning, clearly without a trace of envy.

Alice's small mouth was wrinkled, thinking if you truly envy me, just swap with me! Why show off in front of me! ! Does my existence just mean to set off how big your group of bitches' boobs are?

"Also Alice, where is your husband Merlin? Why haven't I seen him with you?" Rosetti curiously asked, always feeling that Alice's mood wasn't good.

Alice had a complex expression, seeming not too willing to answer this question.

"Hmm?" Rosetti narrowed her eyes, suddenly thinking of something, and smiled, "Surely not? In such a short few months, did you quarrel with Merlin? Haha, as expected, having small breasts means no rights. The great golden adventurer was actually dumped by a black iron man. Although you are troubled, I won't mock you; we are still good sisters; look at my pure eyes, hehe~"

Alice looked at Rosetti's pure eyes; it was full of sarcasm, simply gloating!

Thus Alice rolled her eyes; to not be looked down upon by Rosetti, she had to harden her skin and say one—

"Absolutely not!

"We haven't quarreled. At home every day we are in love! Humph~ !..."

...

title: Chapter 33 — Mission
content:
Chapter 33 — Mission

Volume 9 · Chapter 33

"Is that so?" Rosetti's expression turned puzzled as she asked in surprise, "If you two are so lovey-dovey, why isn't Merlin with you?"

"Well..." Alice hesitated, recalling last night's events. She felt that her relationship with Merlin was now strained.

"Oh ho~" Rosetti seemed to have thought of something and said meaningfully, "That Merlin guy doesn't look very honest. Did he leave you alone at home and go out gallivanting by himself?"

"That's not true!" Alice retorted angrily, hesitating before adding, "We... we just have our own things to do today. It's only for today that he's not by my side."

"Oh? Really?" Rosetti narrowed her eyes, still seeming a bit disbelief.

Even the usually quiet Da Vinci couldn't bear to watch anymore. He spoke up to remind her, "Rosetti, stop it. Don't always target Miss Alice."

"Fine, I'm just bored..." Rosetti shrugged her delicate shoulders. It was rare to find some amusement, but now it was being stopped.

"Speaking of which, Miss Alice, have you been feeling unwell lately? You look... very pale." Da Vinci looked at Alice, feeling as if she had fallen seriously ill.

"..." Alice wanted to say something but stopped herself. She thought that telling them about her condition probably wouldn't help. After all, being an adventurer was a dangerous profession. The Adventurers Guild was like an iron fortress, but adventurers came and went like flowing water. It wasn't uncommon for someone you had a pleasant chat with yesterday to be reported dead the next day.

"Yeah, Alice, you do seem strange. It's not even cold, so why are you dressed so thickly? You even have a long robe on. Aren't you afraid of getting heatstroke? Take it off." Rosetti smiled, feeling that Alice was wrapped up too tightly, which made her uncomfortable to look at.

"......"

Alice panicked and pressed down on her hat. She thought, how could she face anyone in her current state? Her entire body was covered in scales, like a monster. If it caused any disturbance, that would be bad.

So Alice tightly gripped her long robe, ready to prevent anyone from trying to take it off.

"I don't want to take it off... I feel more comfortable this way..."

"What are you talking about? How can you be comfortable wearing so much?" Rosetti, who was always causing trouble, stood up and hugged Alice from behind. She reached around to help take off the long robe.

"Come on, take it off and let me see your body. It's been so long since we've seen each other, and suddenly you're dressed like this. It's making me uncomfortable too, ohoho~"

"....Stop messing around!" Alice knitted her delicate brows, looking troubled as she clung to her robe, refusing to let go.

"Alice, don't be shy. Take it off, okay? Are you perhaps insecure because you're flat-chested? Don't worry, I won't laugh at you. Even if you're wearing padding, I won't tell anyone~" Rosetti, like a lecherous woman, kept urging Alice. She felt that Alice seemed different today, acting strangely and deliberately avoiding everyone's gaze.

"...Who's insecure?! It's not like that at all! Let go!" Alice struggled, refusing to let this troublemaker have her way.

"Come on~ come on~ hehehe~" Rosetti's face was full of anticipation as she tried to undo Alice's long robe.

Alice's brows furrowed tightly, and a layer of anger had already risen to her face. She felt that Rosetti was being disrespectful.

If people found out that she had dragon scales growing on her body, she would definitely receive strange looks!

Just as Alice was about to scold Rosetti for her unreasonable behavior, Uncle Karl burst in, looking dusty and weary. He immediately shouted loudly,

"Everyone, quiet down! I have an urgent matter to discuss with all of you. Come over here!"

The noisy guild instantly fell silent. Even Rosetti stopped pestering Alice. Everyone put down what they were doing and gathered around Uncle Karl.

Uncle Karl was the number one adventurer in the guild, and he was known for his generosity and enthusiasm, so everyone in the guild was willing to listen to him.

Alice slightly adjusted her clothes and watched as Uncle Karl stood on a table, looking like he had something very important to say.

What had happened?

It was the first time she had seen Mr. Karl look so grim. It was too strange.

Alice slowly moved closer, wanting to know what was going on. She felt that the situation seemed very urgent.

Uncle Karl saw that almost everyone had gathered around. He cleared his throat and said seriously,

"I have received notice that the Dark Guild, Gouki Raisan, has settled in Wales. They are currently carrying out a secret plan in the highest mountain nearest to Rexham. The headquarters wants us to assist the Empire in exterminating this group of dangerous individuals. The reward will be 10,000 gold coins and a 3-year tax exemption. Only Gold-rank adventurers and above can participate. Those who are interested, come sign up with me!"

The adventurers below began to discuss among themselves, seemingly weighing the pros and cons. All tasks were voluntary, and the guild would not force anyone to take on a mission.

"Is this for real? It's actually Gouki Raisan?"

"If Karl says so, it must be true. I never thought they would return to Wales!"

"I've heard that Gouki Raisan's members are very powerful. This mission might be life-threatening. The difficulty seems extraordinary."

"Yeah, even though I've heard that Gouki Raisan's current strength is much weaker than before, they still don't seem like an easy opponent."

"But the reward is very generous this time. Plus, the tax exemption is quite substantial. It's a very attractive offer."

The adventurers were abuzz with discussion. Although the reward was generous, everyone was trying to avoid risk. After all, no one was a fool willing to throw their life away.

"Karl, will you be going with us?" one adventurer asked curiously. It seemed that having a powerful person along would greatly increase their chances of survival.

"Of course! I'll be the vanguard, the first one in. All you have to do is stay behind me and cheer me on!" Uncle Karl grinned, showing his big white teeth, giving everyone confidence.

Seeing that the guild's ace was going and even leading the charge, everyone instantly felt more reassured. With Karl there, the mission might go very smoothly.

Many people began to have a lucky feeling, and with the heavy reward, they started to sign up enthusiastically to participate in this extermination of the Dark Guild.

"....." Rosetti sighed and complained angrily, "We just got back and haven't even had a chance to rest, and now we have to go fight again. This is really..."

Alice's expression changed rapidly. In a short amount of time, she thought about many things and finally decided to participate in this extermination mission, but she would go alone.

After all, she was already forced to the edge of a cliff and absolutely could not retreat. She could use this opportunity to go all out!

If she died in battle, she would have no regrets. If she failed, it would be because her skills were inferior, and she couldn't blame anyone else!

Alice's gaze became firm. She inched forward a bit and said patiently,

"Mr. Karl, I want to participate."

"Oh? Alright, but you should bring Merlin along."

Uncle Karl said seriously, feeling quite pleased inside. This time, for the extermination of Gouki Raisan, he was the only Saint-tier present, which made him feel a bit of difficulty.

Although Saint-tier powerhouses were generally strong, it was still hard to fight against many with just two fists. The more combat power on their side, the better.

If Merlin didn't come, Karl would have to be the main combat force himself, facing these dangerous individuals head-on, while the other high-ranking adventurers would have to hold them off.

But with Merlin there...

Karl felt he could go all out, charging straight into the heart of the enemy alone, which would make things much easier.

"This...."

Alice lowered her head, not wanting to bring Merlin along. Instead, she wanted to go secretly by herself.

But since Karl had mentioned it, Alice knew she had to agree verbally.

"I will. I'll tell Merlin later."

"That's good." Uncle Karl nodded, feeling much more at ease about this mission. After all, Merlin was a bit stronger than himself.

"When?" Alice asked.

"Tomorrow at dawn. The sooner we act, the better. We need to strike with lightning speed before the enemy has a chance to settle in!" Uncle Karl clenched his fist, full of confidence as he spoke to Alice.

"Dawn..." Alice lowered her head, her expression a bit unnatural.

So soon... there's no time to prepare at all...

---

Rexham's streets.

Merlin walked through here, appearing much quieter than the bustling crowd around him.

However, his furrowed brows still betrayed Merlin, as if he was entangled in various worries, leaving him to silently endure the torment.

Merlin had thought for a long time. Even now, Asmodeus's warning from earlier still echoed in his ears.

He was indeed a demon, but his soul and consciousness clearly did not belong to this world.

If he considered his position, he really shouldn't care about Alice's life or death.

Humans were inferior beings to demons and had nothing to do with him.

But should he really consider things from a demon's perspective? Before his transmigration, he had been human.

Merlin had lived in this other world for over 200 years. Many of his thoughts had already aligned with those of the demon race, but sometimes, his human nature was hard to completely erase.

Asmodeus's warning wasn't without reason. He had said those things for Merlin's own good.

If Merlin considered things from the demon race's perspective, ignoring Alice would clearly be the correct choice, with no major flaws.

But doing so made Merlin feel a bit uncomfortable, even unwilling.

Merlin looked up at the blue sky and white clouds above, then sighed deeply, feeling troubled by the choices before him.

He thought for a moment and decided that he would definitely take Alice back to the demon race, even if this flat-chested girl resisted. He would tie her up and take her back if he had to.

It might provoke protests from many demons, and even other monarchs and the council might oppose him.

But Merlin didn't care. It was better to do something without regret than to have a clear conscience.

Merlin's expression remained blank as he looked at the azure sky, already prepared to make enemies with the entire demon race.

"In three days, if Alice still refuses, I'll kidnap her."

"She's just a flat-chested girl with no human rights anyway."

(四wo)

title: Chapter 34 — Monthly Ticket Bonus (Two-in-One)
content:
Chapter 34 — Monthly Ticket Bonus (Two-in-One)

Volume 9 · Chapter 34

Deep at night.

Merlin had long since fallen into a deep sleep, and even in his dreams he was pondering how to kidnap Alice.

On the other side, Alice didn't seem to have gone to sleep yet. The sliver of dim light still showed through the crack under her door.

Since the departure time was early dawn, it was already getting very close, so Alice had no intention of sleeping. She was preparing to leave directly.

At that moment, Alice was sneaking around her own room, packing various travel gear.

She wore a white robe that covered most of her dragon-transformed body.

The sharp "Light Aria" was strapped at her waist, wiped spotless.

After getting everything ready, Alice crouched down and quietly pulled out a large chest from under her bed, as if hiding some secret.

She carefully opened it, and golden light suddenly spilled out. Inside were gold coins and various jewels and other valuable items.

This was Alice's secret stash, containing nearly all her savings, but at the moment it seemed completely worthless to her.

Because Alice felt that this trip was more likely to end in disaster than success; she was essentially going to throw herself at it.

If she could make it to Saint-tier, her future would surely be bright.

If she failed, then aside from her little treasure hoard, there'd be nothing left for her either.

Alice wouldn't look so resolute unless she were facing such a perilous situation. She had already prepared herself mentally for everything.

Alice slowly closed her little treasure chest, then sat at her desk, picked up a quill pen, and left Merlin a letter.

Rather than calling it a letter, it was more like a final will, with some last blessings for Merlin.

After everything the previous night, Alice walked out of her room and saw Merlin still fast asleep on the sofa.

Alice hesitated for a moment, then tiptoed over to Merlin and crouched down to look at his face.

After all, Alice and Merlin had lived together for nearly half a year. Although they argued most of the time, it would be a lie to say there wasn't any affection between them.

It's just that Merlin had a sharp tongue and sometimes didn't care at all about other people's feelings, which made Alice's impression of him fluctuate.

Even when Alice thought Merlin was actually a decent guy, she'd never admit it verbally. She'd cover it up with sarcastic remarks instead.

Alice herself couldn't quite put her feelings for Merlin into words. In plain terms, it was a mix of love and hate, and she often gnashed her teeth at the guy.

Without Merlin, her life now would definitely be better. She wouldn't have such enormous debt.

But after getting to know each other slowly, this guy wasn't entirely irredeemable. He occasionally showed concern for others, which Alice rather liked.

Of course, this was only on the surface. It could never compare to her ideal of the great swordswoman Elgin, whose noble silhouette flashed through her mind at all times.

"Hmm..."

Merlin furrowed his brows slightly, as if dreaming. He reached out and scratched his belly. There was not an ounce of dignity in his sleeping posture.

His sleeping habits were terrible; it was almost unbearable to look at.

Alice muttered a complicated commentary, then reached out and pinched Merlin's nose to let him experience what it felt like to have trouble breathing.

Merlin immediately started snoring, sounding like a pig grunting, which made Alice unable to hold back a chuckle.

A smile appeared on Alice's face, and her heart felt much better. She silently released Merlin's nose.

Fine. There's no party that doesn't end. It's about time. I should be leaving.

If things go poorly, this might be our last meeting. Indeed, we're different people.

Goodbye. I wish you happiness in the future.

Alice stood up, took a deep breath, and then left the house silently without looking back.

At the entrance of the Adventurers Guild.

It was already past midnight. Unlike usual, the place was brightly lit, and four carriages were parked outside. It was quite lively.

Lexham's Adventurers Guild had several hundred members. There were over twenty Gold-ranked adventurers, and only a handful of Mithril-ranked ones.

Of those twenty-odd Gold-ranked adventurers, over ten had come to participate in the current hunt against Rakshasa. They were gathering at the entrance, making final preparations and exchanging intelligence.

Dozens of torches lit up the entrance, making it feel as bright as daytime. Even the nearby residents could tell something big was happening tonight.

Alice saw Da Vinci and Rossetti were also there, but she didn't see Uncle Carl, so she approached curiously to ask.

Although Da Vinci was only a Silver adventurer, her partner Rossetti was Gold-ranked, so under the teaming rules, she would also be going on the expedition.

Besides, Da Vinci wasn't good at combat. She was mainly a support-type mage. Other than not being able to heal, she was pretty capable in every other aspect.

After all, Da Vinci was skilled at researching bizarre inventions and alchemy. She'd never put any energy into her own cultivation.

"Miss Da Vinci, where is Mr. Carl? Why isn't he here?" Alice walked over curiously to ask, finding it a bit strange.

"Mr. Carl has already gone ahead. He plans to clear as many obstacles as possible to pave the way for us." Da Vinci replied seriously.

"Mm." Alice nodded, thinking that although it was a bit reckless, it really fit Mr. Carl's personality.

"Eh?! " Rossetti looked stunned and asked oddly, "Why isn't Merlin accompanying you?"

"Alice lowered her head, somewhat embarrassed, not knowing how to answer. She just quietly hugged her arms tighter.

"This is a bit too much. You're going on a mission, and Merlin, as your husband, doesn't even accompany you?"

Rossetti's expression turned slightly disdainful. Looking at Alice like a pushover, she felt that couple matters weren't really her place to comment on.

But given the current situation, Merlin letting Alice come alone made Rossetti feel quite strange, even a bit sympathetic toward Alice.

"So they must have had a fight."

"No, that's not it. I came on my own. It has nothing to do with him." Alice quickly explained, not wanting to be misunderstood.

"Mmm..." Rossetti thought for a moment and decided that since action was imminent, it was better not to meddle. "Never mind. He's just an Iron adventurer. He's neither here nor there for our operation."
