Alice secretly sighed in relief, feeling she'd barely gotten away with it. She looked up at the night sky covered by thick clouds and had the feeling it would rain tomorrow.

Things are resting on me now...

In the capital of Britannia.

The queen's bedchamber was still brightly lit. It seemed no servant was resting.

The sound of clacking footsteps echoed down the corridor. Metfield, clad in exquisite armor, walked along the red carpet toward the queen's quarters.

Metfield's expression was grave. Being summoned urgently by Her Majesty at such an hour was unprecedented.

If there weren't an emergency within the empire, the queen would never have called her at such an awkward time.

Normally, by this hour, the queen would have already gone to bed. Calling for her this late was highly abnormal.

Metfield herself didn't know what was going on. She had a feeling of urgency, so she decided to just meet the queen first and find out.

At the far end, the magnificent double doors slowly opened by two maids, who then stood respectfully aside to welcome Metfield.

Arriving at the bedchamber.

She wore a white silk nightgown, standing by the floor-to-ceiling window, looking out at the rebuilding capital.

Elizabeth already knew Franklin was dead, but she couldn't care less. He was just a chess piece.

Everything was going smoothly now. As long as they continued following Elizabeth's script, a hero from the royal family would inevitably emerge.

Her position would then be consolidated, and she would gain unprecedented influence!

Elizabeth smiled with the air of a mastermind, feeling that things were becoming increasingly favorable to her. She now only needed to send Metfield to eliminate Rakshasa, and the hero's script would be brought to a perfect conclusion.

Metfield quickly stepped forward and knelt on one knee. "Your Majesty, I have arrived."

"Did I disturb your rest?" Queen Elizabeth turned around and said apologetically.

"No, Your Majesty. I wasn't sleeping either, so there was no rest to disturb." Metfield said with reverence, though her heart felt warm.

"Then that's good." Queen Elizabeth nodded with a smile.

"I wonder what matters Your Majesty needs me for at this hour?" Metfield raised her head slightly and asked earnestly.

"There truly are some matters that require you to act quickly. There's also some danger involved. I wonder if you're willing to accept?" A harmless smile played on Elizabeth's face.

"As long as it is Your Majesty's command, I will face fire and water without hesitation!" Metfield said with a resolute tone.

"Very good. As expected of my most trusted knight." Queen Elizabeth nodded satisfied, and personally helped Metfield to her feet.

"Rise. There are no outsiders here."

Metfield stood up and asked earnestly, "I wonder what troubles Your Majesty? Could you share it with me?"

"My reign. This is a severe threat to our empire." The queen paused, then revealed her mission.

"Before the Blackflame Rakshasa revives, I want you to hurry to Wales and eliminate all of these dangerous individuals, relieving the empire of this crisis."

Metfield bowed her head and responded without hesitation.

"At once!"

The next day.

A drizzling rain tapped against the eaves.

Outside, a fine misty rain was falling. Normally, Alice would kick him hard on the butt to wake him up.

But Merlin was still in a deep slumber. This guy actually overslept!?

The curse's infection, after more than two months, had flared up again!

But just then, a crushing pain from his contracting heart suddenly surged. He fell off the sofa onto the ground, desperately clutching his chest to ease the pain.

Merlin's eyes snapped wide open. A cold sweat broke out. He thought, Who was that Saint-tier powerhouse I took down last time? Oh right, it was that black elf named Samuel.

Merlin's forehead beaded with cold sweat, and he repeatedly sucked in breaths through his teeth.

The sickness was coming more frequently now. Was it just his imagination?

He hadn't expected it to flare up again within merely two months. Looking around the house, he noticed it didn't seem normal. Alice wouldn't normally go out in weather like this.

He wondered if this lazybones had also overslept and hadn't gotten up yet.

He turned his gaze toward Alice's tightly closed bedroom door. The intense pain in his chest gradually eased, and he slowly stood up, then gently pushed open Alice's room door.

Merlin felt something was off, so he forced himself to endure the pain.

He spotted a note on the desk, as if Alice had deliberately left it for him.

Merlin frowned, feeling that something was wrong. He picked up the letter Alice had written in the early hours. The ink was already dry, meaning she had left some time ago.

Merlin hesitated for a moment, then quietly walked over and slowly read it.

"Merlin, I will not give up. I'm facing the greatest challenge of my life. If I succeed, it's my fortune. If I fail, I'll die without regrets. Dying secretly out there alone might not be a bad thing either. At least it preserves my last shred of dignity. I know you wouldn't come looking for me, after all, we only came together for mutual benefit. This is probably my last act of kindness. I'm leaving all my assets to you. This process hasn't been pleasant for you, and you weren't keen on returning to Yun Changlong anyway. —Alice Claudya"

Merlin finished reading the letter left by Alice with a stunned expression, looking utterly incredulous.

Alice actually left on her own?! What the hell! Where could she possibly go?

This was a time of great danger. How foolish would someone have to be to make a choice like this?!

She actually planned to go out alone and quietly wait to die? Merlin found this absolutely incomprehensible.

He couldn't imagine things turning out like this. Such behavior might make sense for someone like her, but for Alice, it was hard to accept.

After all, Alice was too independent. The contracting pain in his heart grew sharper, forcing him to breathe harder to cope.

A wave of sorrow rose in Merlin's heart, as if something important had been taken from him, leaving him feeling a profound lack of security.

He felt empty inside, as though something crucial were missing, but he himself couldn't quite pinpoint what. Among the people he'd encountered in this other world, some mattered deeply, while others didn't.

Merlin thought about how in his two hundred years in this other world, he had completely vanished without a trace, as if he had never existed at all.

But if he disappeared now, leaving such a massive debt behind, it would be far too easy on her!

What demons, what humans?

I am Merlin. That's all. Just cut through all the troubling problems with my blade!

Overwhelmed and frustrated, he crumpled the letter into a ball and threw it harshly onto the ground.

Merlin's brows locked tightly together as he strode大步 to the doorway and pushed the door open.

Then, enduring the pain of the heart curse, he threw on a black raincoat and stepped directly into the rain.

Gripping the demon sword Banri Garan at his side, its red glare flashed恼火ly through the downpour. His two eyebrows knit together, and his eyes burned with burning red anger as he gritted his teeth and muttered.

"That troublesome woman. Truly the stupidest I've ever seen."

title: Chapter 35 — Thunder Beast
content:
Chapter 35 — Thunder Beast

Volume 9 · Chapter 35

The rain fell endlessly, swaying like thoughts in the wind.

Merlin burst out of his house and rushed straight to the Adventurers Guild, his expression grave. The drizzle splashed onto him as he wove through the fine rain.

The crushing pain in his chest gradually faded, allowing Merlin to calm down. His top priority was still to bring Alice back—who knew what that troublesome woman was planning? But Merlin suspected Alice was taking a desperate gamble, risking everything for a last stand.

Merlin shoved open the guild’s door, his entire body drenched, rainwater dripping from his mud-caked hair onto the floor. He scanned the room but saw no sign of Alice. Many familiar faces seemed to be missing as well.

*Damn!*

Merlin’s first thought was that Alice had already left. Judging by the dried ink on that letter, she must have been gone for some time.

Fortunately, Hobbs was still there, chatting with other adventurers. When he saw the drenched Merlin, a flicker of shock passed through his eyes.

"Merlin?! What happened? What’s going on?"

Hobbs found Merlin’s solemn expression strange, especially paired with his bedraggled, rain-soaked appearance—so unlike his usual self.

Merlin approached Hobbs and urgently asked, "Hobbs, where did Alice go?!"

"Huh?! You don’t know? She went to subjugate the Demon Lord Gozan..." Hobbs blinked in confusion, wondering how Merlin could be unaware. Hadn’t Alice told Karl to inform Merlin when she returned? Had Karl never done so? What were this husband and wife up to?

Merlin’s eyes widened as a flood of thoughts raced through his mind. *Subjugate Demon Lord Gozan?* He hadn’t heard a single word about this! Was Alice acting on her own again? Damn it! This was nothing but trouble!

"Where exactly is Demon Lord Gozan’s location?" Merlin demanded.

"Head north. There’s a mountain range closest to Rexham called the Kexili Mountains. I heard it’s there..."

Hobbs didn’t waste words, giving Merlin the information concisely. He could tell Merlin was shaken.

"Thanks, Hobbs..."

Merlin turned and left the guild without another word, not knowing how long Alice had been gone. But he had to hurry.

Hobbs stared blankly at the guild door, the light drizzle outside blurring the scene.

*What in the world is going on...*

Wales, the peak of the Kexili Mountains.

A ring of warning magic had been set up around the mountain’s outer perimeter. If anyone launched a surprise attack, Swinburne would detect it immediately and respond accordingly.

The night’s rain showed no sign of stopping, shrouding the entire mountain range in a thin, rolling mist like a sea of clouds.

At the very summit, the peak had been forcibly leveled into an open-air platform. A massive magic formation was already laid out there, carved with dense, intricate runes of the Ancient Kingdom.

Though Swinburne had only studied the Ancient Kingdom’s texts for a short time, he had already grasped the structural principles of resurrection magic.

Swinburne stood before the magic formation, sensing the time was right. He could begin the spirit-summoning ritual.

Old Sammy stood behind him, already detecting a strange spatial energy from afar. It seemed this Ancient Kingdom formation had opened a planar gateway.

A faint smile played on Swinburne’s lips as he casually burned the Ancient Kingdom tome in his hands to ashes without hesitation.

A priceless treasure passed down for centuries was destroyed so effortlessly, with no trace of regret.

Though the book contained countless ancient spells—each one capable of causing an uproar if revealed—it held little use for Swinburne. He only needed the forbidden resurrection technique.

Since he couldn’t use it, no one else would either. This was the perfect expression of Swinburne’s selfishness.

Old Sammy watched in silent agony, feeling it was a terrible waste of a rare artifact, but he didn’t dare voice his protest.

"Is it about time? Can we start...?"

Swinburne nodded and took out a vial of high-purity Holy Dragon blood refined by Democritus, pouring it directly into the magic formation.

Instantly, the entire massive formation flared crimson, rapidly illuminating the surroundings. The spectacle was so grand that it could be seen even from the base of the mountain, like a torch suddenly ignited!

The crimson light bathed Swinburne’s face as the center of the formation began spewing a black, sludge-like substance that slowly spread outward.

Faint ghostly howls accompanied the black ooze as it took on a humanoid shape, struggling desperately to break free from the shackles of another plane.

These were spirits wandering in Hell, trying to escape endless torment, forever seeking cracks between dimensions.

Old Sammy’s eyes widened in shock—this was likely the first time he had ever seen such a thing. "Has it... succeeded?"

"No..." Swinburne paused, watching the spirits emerging from the formation. "This is only the beginning..."

Old Sammy’s expression grew solemn. It was hard to imagine the old Guildmaster surviving amidst those layers of black sludge.

"The Ancient Kingdom’s forbidden resurrection technique is truly remarkable," Swinburne said after a moment, speaking seriously. "It can bring my father back in his prime. The only downside is that it requires constant guidance, which is a bit troublesome." He paused again. "From now on, I will continuously chant my father’s name to assist his return from Hell. This will require ample time and a secure environment."

Old Sammy nodded firmly. "Leave that to me. To ensure the old Guildmaster’s successful return, I’ll do whatever it takes. No one will be allowed to disturb this ritual." Though aged, his strength remained formidable.

"Then I’ll have to trouble you, teacher..." Swinburne said politely.

"There’s no need for formalities," Old Sammy replied with unwavering loyalty. "If the old Guildmaster can return, it will fulfill my lifelong wish. Even if I die, I’ll have no regrets." He hesitated for a moment. "By the way, where’s that brat Cooper? I don’t see him around."

"I’ve already stationed him in an ambush along the path," Swinburne explained. "This mountain has only one obvious route—easy to defend, hard to attack. As long as Cooper holds off any intruders there, we’ll be safe here. Of course..." He lifted his head, uncertain. "We can’t rule out attacks from other directions. We mustn’t let our guard down."

Old Sammy nodded in understanding.

Swinburne’s face remained expressionless as he pondered his plans for after his father’s resurrection. Should he temporarily avoid the Empire’s wrath, or confront them head-on? Either choice would depend on his father’s condition upon revival. But one thing was certain: once his father returned, his own status would soar.

Swinburne could already see his bright future—second only to one, yet above all others, the pinnacle of power!

Just then, the warning magic at the mountain’s base was triggered. Swinburne’s head snapped up, and he immediately sensed it—a Saint-tier powerhouse.

"What’s wrong?" Old Sammy noticed Swinburne’s odd reaction and couldn’t help but ask.

"I didn’t expect someone to arrive so quickly, and a Saint-tier at that. Truly amusing..." A contemptuous smile curled on Swinburne’s lips.

"So soon?" Old Sammy was also taken aback. The ritual had only just begun, yet an enemy had already arrived—and a Saint-tier one at that. The situation was far from optimistic. "Which direction? Is it Cooper’s position?"

"No, it’s the steep cliffside path. They must be planning a surprise attack. How naive." Swinburne felt no pressure at all.

Old Sammy straightened his back, his aged eyes burning with determination. "This reckless fool... I’ll handle them myself."

"Mm." Swinburne nodded, then said meaningfully, "I’ll leave it to you, teacher..."

The jagged, rain-slicked cliffs gleamed as if newly polished, with rivulets of water trickling down their surface.

Uncle Karl moved at incredible speed, rapidly closing in on the mountain’s peak.

The torch-like glow at the summit pulsed ominously, as if something immense and dangerous was brewing.

Uncle Karl’s expression was grave, a foreboding sensation rising from the depths of his heart. Something was wrong.

*What in the world is that?*

What were Gozan and his group planning?

*Forget it. End this quickly!*

Golden battle aura surged around Uncle Karl, forming the Lightning Armor that enveloped his entire body, crackling with energy. In an instant, he transformed into a Thunder Beast amidst the rain.

"No matter what traps lie ahead, I’ll smash through them with my fists!"

title: Chapter 36 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 36 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 36

The reason Uncle Karl dared to charge deep alone was not just because he knew Merlin would arrive and felt at ease.

The biggest reason was that if he could take down the Gouki Reizan, it would reduce casualties for his guild.

As the successor to Old Taylor, once his father stepped down, Uncle Karl would likely become the new guildmaster. Many matters had to be considered from the guild’s long-term development.

Moreover, when facing a Saint-tier opponent, he had to take them on himself. Sending those Gold-rank adventurers, who were only there to restrain the enemy, to their deaths would be an irrational choice.

Uncle Karl was no sadist who enjoyed trampling others—even twenty years ago, he had still been a hot-blooded young man!

The rain never stopped. The closer he got to the mountain peak, the thicker the stench of blood became.

Thin mist swirled in all directions, obscuring the distant scenery. Only the torch-like crimson glow remained sharply visible, unsettling to the eye.

Uncle Karl was wrapped entirely in the golden Raijin’s Armor, moving at an incomprehensible speed. He wanted to reach the summit as soon as possible to see the current situation.

He was prepared. No matter how powerful the enemy was, he would eliminate the threat in the shortest time possible and pave the way for the main force.

Uncle Karl knew of the Gouki Reizan. Even as a child, he had heard of this powerful and terrifying organization—wherever they went, rivers of blood followed.

Thirty years ago, parents didn’t scare children to sleep with tales of demons. They used the thugs of Gouki Reizan instead. It was far more effective than the demon race.

That showed just how much influence Gouki Reizan had wielded in human kingdoms back then—a name alone was enough to strike fear into hearts.

But now, Gouki Reizan was nothing more than a dying organization. So Uncle Karl wasn’t afraid. Instead, his fighting spirit burned fiercely!

Who didn’t want to conquer the fears of their childhood? Uncle Karl was no exception.

The thin mist was slowly dispersed by Uncle Karl’s charge. At the mountainside, Old Sammy suddenly burst out from the fog!

Old Sammy had been lying in ambush for a long time. He lunged forward with a roar, swinging the magic staff in his hand and striking Uncle Karl’s abdomen with all his might.

Uncle Karl’s forehead bulged with veins—he had taken serious damage!

If not for the defensive effect of the Raijin’s Armor formed by his battle aura, that staff strike would have knocked him out cold.

Uncle Karl’s body flew backward. He steadied himself, clutching his stomach as he glared at Old Sammy. This was the first time he had ever seen a mage engage in close-quarters combat!

Old Sammy was nothing like a normal mage. Because he had integrated the power of magical beasts into his own body, he excelled in melee combat!

As for the staff in his hand? Now that he was old, he just used it as a walking stick. Nothing more.

“HAHAHA! Where did this little rat come from? Daring to trespass on our territory! If you want to die, just squeak, and this old man will personally send you off!”

“Hmph!”

Uncle Karl spat out a mouthful of blood, slowly rising to his feet. The golden lightning around him surged violently.

“Send me off? Old man, you’ve got quite the mouth on you…”

“Young man, don’t get too arrogant. I’m in a good mood right now, so I’ll advise you to scram. Otherwise, I won’t mind tearing you in half alive.”

Old Sammy didn’t take Uncle Karl seriously. He wanted to intimidate him with overwhelming strength. These were extraordinary times—if he could avoid a fight, he would.

“Heh heh, what a coincidence. I’m in a good mood too. I’d love to beat up an old geezer like you for fun.” Uncle Karl’s will to fight was strong. If someone was an enemy, he wouldn’t underestimate them just because they were old.

“I see you’re courting death. As the vice president of Gouki Reizan, I’ve never had a young man dare to be so insolent in front of me!” Old Sammy narrowed his eyes, his killing intent already stirred.

“So what? Who’s courting death isn’t set in stone yet, old man…”

Before the words even finished, Uncle Karl, his body crackling with lightning, vanished from where he stood. Only the echo of thunder remained in the air.

In the next instant, his fist slammed into Old Sammy’s chest. Lightning erupted on impact, the speed so staggering it left onlookers stunned.

“Gah!” Old Sammy’s eyes widened as he let out a muffled groan, completely caught off guard by the sudden strike.

“Old man, now do you know who’s courting death?” Uncle Karl rolled his eyes, his tone dripping with disdain.

“Hmph… So that’s how it is…” Old Sammy slowly lifted his head, his beard standing on end as he glared fiercely at Uncle Karl. “The Taylor family’s Raijin Close Combat Art… truly impressive.”

Uncle Karl furrowed his brows. Why did the old man look like he’d only taken a light injury? This was too strange! How could a mage’s body be this resilient?

“But it’s still too green! Thirty years ago, your family’s Raijin Close Combat Art was nothing but a crude, unrefined technique!”

Old Sammy discarded his staff. A surge of bestial energy exploded from his body, forcefully repelling Uncle Karl.

His clothes burst apart, revealing a terrifying physique composed of various transplanted magical beast parts. This was the true form of Gouki Reizan’s vice president!

Muscular, brimming with the auras of countless beasts, his writhing veins pulsed with formidable power. He was no longer human—he was a fusion of man and beast!

Red scales, bear-like claws, a massive, throbbing heart, and a jet-black scorpion tail!

Old Sammy’s eyes glowed crimson as he loomed over Uncle Karl, his previously aged demeanor swept away. He seemed to have regained the vigor of youth!

Uncle Karl’s eyes widened, his pupils trembling slightly. He couldn’t comprehend the monstrosity before him—

A crimson scorpion tail, the claws of a mountain bear, the scales of a black swamp viper, the heart of a dragon…

And many other parts from high-ranked magical beasts, each of which would normally require a team to take down.

Yet now, the traits of these monsters were all concentrated in a single human body. His combat ability defied all conventional logic.

Uncle Karl sensed a creeping danger. Unconsciously, he muttered to himself.

“…What is this…”

“Hmph! Ignorant youngster. This is my proudest magic—harnessing the brutal power of magical beasts for my own use!” Old Sammy spread his arms, making himself look even more monstrous and terrifying. “Now that you’ve seen my magnificent form, do you still think you can defeat me?”

A cold sweat trickled down Uncle Karl’s forehead. Faced with such an overwhelming presence, he couldn’t help but tense up.

“Cat got your tongue? Scared speechless by this old man?” Old Sammy roared, charging forward with a howl. “Today, I’ll teach you what it means to respect your elders! Your fresh flesh and blood will be mine! A fine meal to fill my belly! HAHA…”

“I don’t get magic or whatever, but if it’s a monster, there’s nothing my fists can’t take down!”

Karl activated the Tiger Form of the Raijin Close Combat Art. The surging Raijin’s Armor transformed into a resplendent tiger, enveloping him completely.

The two forces clashed head-on, the impact so violent it made the mountain itself tremble.

The roars of beasts and the howls of the tiger resonated, drowning out the patter of rain…

---

At the mountain peak.

The magic circle emitting the red glow let out mournful wails. The black sludge continued to multiply, and many spirits from the abyss wept in agony.

Swynburne stood in the rain, expressionless, watching it all. He felt no pity for the wandering spirits—only endless indifference.

Suddenly, he heard footsteps approaching from behind, step by step, as if the rat had already been disposed of.

“As expected of you, teacher. You resolved the intruder so quickly. Though this was likely just a scout. Stronger ones might be coming next.”

Swynburne turned to speak to the figure behind him, wanting to flatter Old Sammy a bit and keep him by his side to fend off enemies.

The thick fog obscured the newcomer, who said nothing in response.

Abruptly, something dark was hurled through the mist. It arced through the air and landed at Swynburne’s feet, spinning in circles.

That dark object was Old Sammy’s head, his face still frozen in an expression of sheer terror.

……

Swynburne froze, his pupils contracting in shock. He stared blankly at Old Sammy’s head.

Teacher…

He was already dead?

title: Chapter 37 — Prey
content:
Chapter 37 — Prey

Volume 9 · Chapter 37

Swenburne stared blankly at his teacher’s severed head, his eyes wide with shock.

He knew his teacher was no ordinary Saint-tier warrior but an exceptionally powerful one.

As a senior member of the Haogui Ritual, who had followed Youyan Haogui across the land, how could he possibly serve as vice president without immense strength?

Old Sami, Swenburne’s mentor, was undeniably skilled in magic, yet he had been killed by someone?

The terrified expression frozen on his face before death showed that the enemy’s power had far exceeded his expectations.

Swenburne looked up at the mist behind him, unable to see who was coming, only a vague shadow.

The mist slowly cleared, revealing Uncle Carl with a smug smile.

Uncle Carl wiped blood from his mouth; he was injured, and the battle with Old Sami had clearly taken a toll on him too.

“Haha, you’re the acting president of the Haogui Ritual, aren’t you? Finally, I get to meet you.”

Swenburne remained silent, studying the man before him. He noticed the secret silver adventurer’s proof on Uncle Carl’s neck, which gave him some insight into the situation.

I thought you were an imperial lackey? Turns out you’re from the Adventurers Guild after all.

The Adventurers Guild and the Dark Guild have always been at odds, doing similar work but with fundamentally different natures.

The Dark Guild also disrupts the market and damages adventurers’ reputations, so the two organizations have long been enemies, unable to tolerate each other’s existence.

Swenburne felt calmer and wasn’t pressured; instead, he found Uncle Carl quite interesting.

“That’s right, I’m the acting president of the Haogui Ritual.”

“I didn’t expect you to admit it so easily; I thought you were extremely cunning.” Uncle Carl tightened his black gold gauntlets, their intricate patterns exuding a wild aura.

“Your strength poses no threat to me, and I have no need to hide my identity,” Swenburne said blandly, his expressionless face showing no emotion.

“Hmph!” Uncle Carl curled his lips unhappily. “You’re pretty bold. Whether I’m a threat or not, we’ll know after a fight.”

Swenburne sensed something and thought Uncle Carl might be an unreasonable jerk.

But there was still a resurrection magic array, and if possible, Swenburne didn’t want to fight.

“Why are you interfering with us? We’ve only been in Wales for a short time and haven’t interfered with the Adventurers Guild’s interests.”

“You’re a bunch of evil scum, and I don’t need a lot of reasons to kill you,” Uncle Carl said bluntly.

Swenburne sighed, realizing this man was indeed unreasonable, and communicating with a fool was a waste of time.

“Alright, now I’ll give you two choices: leave quietly, or this will be your burial place!”

“Why ask? Of course I choose to fight to the death!”

Uncle Carl’s body suddenly erupted with golden fighting spirit, and a vivid tiger made of lightning roared angrily at Swenburne.

“You’re a fool with a simple mind and clumsy limbs; it seems you haven’t seen what true power is yet.” Swenburne said calmly, cursing him.

“Shut up! Your filthy mouth! I hate it when people call me a fool!” Uncle Carl couldn’t contain his anger and launched a fierce attack first, intending to use the overwhelming power of Lei Huowan Jun to suppress Swenburne.

book,SFA

“Disappear, Fool!” o1→C it

Swenburne frowned, his eyes narrowing as he stared at Uncle Carl.

Then he snapped his fingers, and golden magic surged out, transforming into towering, eerie blue flames!

The mountain peak seemed to explode, and the huge flames, like blooming violets, burned everything to ashes!

The strange flames generated waves of heat, rushing toward Uncle Carl like a tidal wave!

Terrified and with nowhere to hide, Uncle Carl was engulfed by the flames, falling helplessly down the mountain into unconsciousness.

No one expected Uncle Carl to be defeated by Swenburne in just one encounter, with no suspense whatsoever!

Swenburne lowered his arm, looked up at the dark sky, and coldly snorted to himself:

“Hmph, the adventurers from Rexham are not that strong after all.”

At the foot of the mountain,

several guild carriages arrived.

The main force of the Rexham Guild also arrived at this time.

More than a dozen golden adventurers got off the carriage and prepared for the upcoming fierce battle.

However, the towering, eerie blue flames erupting at the mountain peak immediately shocked everyone.

The drizzle in the sky seemed to evaporate instantly, becoming scorching hot.

Looking at the spectacular scene and the immense power of the Saint-tier warriors, the adventurers present felt frightened.

Alice got off the carriage, looked up at the scene, and unconsciously muttered:

“What is this?”

Looking for great books? Search here.

A cold sweat broke out on Alice’s forehead, and she felt there was a terrifyingly powerful magician at the mountain’s peak.

“Will Mr. Carl be okay?”

“He should be fine; he’s our guild’s strongest adventurer.”

The two people next to her whispered privately. Though they said he would be fine, their serious expressions showed doubt.

Da Vinci’s monocle projected a parsing magic array to detect the ferocious blue flames and commented:

“This magic power is very strong.”

“Huh?!” Rosetti was stunned. “Does that mean Mr. Carl can’t solve it?”

“Preliminary estimates suggest yes. This magic power has reached a level comparable to Saint-tier monsters.” Da Vinci analyzed.

“No, that can’t be right. Mr. Carl shouldn’t be defeated so easily, right?” Alice’s expression was unnatural. If Mr. Carl couldn’t win, then this expedition would surely mean certain death for them.

“I’ve analyzed Mr. Carl’s power before, and it’s hard to compare with these flames. Normally, Mr. Carl would lose.” Da Vinci said expressionlessly, continuing, “But combat involves many factors, and Mr. Carl isn’t without a chance. The enemy’s strength is formidable, and we must not let our guard down.”

“Understood,” Rosetti nodded, twisted her wrist, and said seriously to the adventurers, “Follow Da Vinci’s arrangements. She can devise a plan with a higher success rate, improving our survival chances. Any objections?”

The dozen golden adventurers looked at each other, saw no problem, and nodded in agreement.

These adventurers were familiar with Da Vinci; she was wise and meticulous, and many consulted her when they had problems.

Now was not the time to fight individually; improving team efficiency was the urgent priority.

Seeing no objections, Rosetti raised her arm and shouted:

“Let’s go!”

On the path leading to the mountain peak,

Cooper, with two short swords at his waist, stood in the rain, looking down at the golden adventurers with a superior air. Hehehe~

Here they come! Finally, some toys to entertain me!

There are so many beautiful women inside—big breasts, expressionless faces, and...

Cooper’s eyes locked onto Alice’s face, and he couldn’t take his eyes off her, thinking she was the most beautiful.

I’ve decided! She’s my prey!

That silver-haired woman is amazing; her cute face is clearly seducing me to violate her!

Cooper’s eyes revealed unconcealed greed, and he stuck out his tongue to lick his lips.

“Hehehe~”

“I smell the scent of a virgin.”

(Body. Heart)

title: Chapter 38 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 38 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 38

Adventurers marched along the rugged mountain path toward the peak, the crimson light radiating from somewhere filling them with deep unease.

Rosetti marched at the forefront, looking like a belligerent type, his expression serious, completely lacking the cheerful air he had had before.

This mission, Da Vinci had already analyzed; the enemy's strength was not to be underestimated, so Rosetti had to take things seriously.

As Da Vinci's partner, Rosetti always believed in her analysis.

Often having Da Vinci as his strategist was what kept Rosetti from many risks.

Alice in the depths of the party, she seriously guarded her surroundings, silently gripping the short sword at her waist, ever vigilant of the dangers around them.

The main force reached the halfway point on the mountain, where lush foliage made everything feel mysterious.

"Everyone, raise your guard. The current position is dangerous and easy to fall victim to a sneak attack," Da Vinci said seriously.

"Sneak attack? Who is so shameless? I'll beat him until he can't take care of himself!" Rosetti said with a relaxed expression.

As soon as his words fell, the grass rustled, and a black figure darted out—sure enough, an ambush was set up here!

Cooper had been lying in wait here for half a day, preparing to find a good opportunity to annihilate this group of golden adventurers and then capture Alice.

But since these people had heard Da Vinci's words and become vigilant, they simply couldn't find a good opportunity.

Since Cooper's position had been guessed, he no longer needed to hide; facing him head-on was obviously the best choice.

"Don't be so serious, everyone—let's play!"

Cooper's figure continuously shifted, and in an instant he seemed to transform into a cold snake; in the blink of an eye he had rushed to the front of the main group.

Saint-tier battle aura slowly burned on his body; two short swords flickering with silver light encircled his body, looking like a circus clown.

"Magicians stay back! Warriors, advance!" Da Vinci suddenly issued an order.

Over ten golden adventurers moved swiftly; those holding shields flashed forward to block, while magicians fell back to form an initial defensive formation.

Rosetti held out both hands and immediately equipped gauntlets of alchemical armor. Red claws flashed with cold light, and red veins occasionally twitched, as if they were living weapons.

This was a weapon crafted by Da Vinci for Rosetti, called the Living Alchemical Equipment. Made from beast limbs, it had infinite uses.

Besides formidable destructive power, it could also enhance the wearer's combat ability. Most importantly, this living alchemical equipment could preserve the abilities the beast had in life!

For example, the claw gauntlets on Rosetti's hands were forged from the limbs of a shadow leopard, retaining the characteristic of attack speed. Every swing was visible only as a afterimage!

Pfft, these high-level newbies, thinking they could block me just by grouping together? Ridiculous!"

Cooper shouted, gripping his short swords and breaking straight through from the front. He played no strategy at all, wanting to win with brute force.

A loud sound rang out; the short sword and shield slammed together violently. Cooper's Saint-tier battle aura pressed down!

Three golden adventurers were struck back consecutively, barely able to keep up with Cooper's steps, but they were simply unable to block him!

After all, Cooper was a Saint-tier powerhouse—how could three high-level adventurers hope to block him?

"Frontline, scatter!" Da Vinci issued another instruction.

The three shield-bearing adventurers instantly scattered. Before Cooper could figure out what was going on, Rosetti suddenly burst out from behind the shield.

"Die!!!"

Rosetti roared, and his living alchemical gauntlets suddenly glowed red, striking directly at Cooper's chest.

Cooper was startled; this punch would certainly injure him. Luckily, his strength was superior.

In between, Cooper suddenly flipped in the air, just barely dodging Rosetti's fist, almost grazing his nose!

"Alice!" Da Vinci instructed again.

"I know."

Alice drew the fine sword at her waist. Instantly, silver light burst forth, and she ruthlessly stabbed, using the [Balance] skill on Cooper.

Cooper's pupils contracted slightly. He had to admit he had been a bit too arrogant; he hadn't expected this group to move so quickly, practically as one whole.

However, cautious close-quarters combat was Cooper's specialty, and his strength was strong; in a small-scale battle, he wouldn't easily fall behind!

Cooper's body began to rotate in midair, agile like a circus performer, deftly avoiding Alice's fine sword; only the clothes on his chest were sliced.

"What!?" Alice was slightly startled, not expecting that even in this state she could still dodge her lethal attack.

Cooper retreated a bit, disheveled, creating distance between himself and this group. He had to take things seriously; otherwise, who knew what would happen.

"Missed by a bit!" Rosetti said dissatisfied, looking somewhat regretful.

"Heh, your temper is as big as your chest. Looks like I could touch it~" Cooper revealed a lecherous gaze, sticking out his tongue to tease Rosetti.

"Good. If you want to touch me, you'd better have the ability." Rosetti didn't blush, and deliberately thrust out her ample chest.

"Too bad, I'm only interested in your chest, but what arouses my desire is that silver-haired beauty, hehehe~" Cooper's gaze fell on Alice, revealing a greedy expression. "Little beauty, you wait first—"

"Will you just be mine later~"

"Ugh, disgusting!" Alice furrowed her beautiful brows, her expression disgusted to the extreme.

"Then then next" Cooper took out six black spheres from his waist, grinning and saying, "It's my performance time."

As soon as his words fell, Cooper slammed the six black balls onto the ground. Thick black smoke billowed out immediately, making it impossible to see the surroundings.

The golden adventurers were instantly surrounded in the middle, completely unable to tell east from south or west.

This black smoke was very pungent, obviously containing some toxin that would cause people to lose their ability to resist.

"Everyone, gather around me!" Da Vinci shouted loudly.

The other adventurers hurriedly gathered around Da Vinci, jointly warding off the upcoming attack.

Da Vinci waved her magic wand and bestowed a mid-tier toxin resistance buff on everyone; otherwise, this thick black smoke would crush them.

Da Vinci felt something was amiss. She surmised that this enemy's attack was aimed at her, so her mood was also rather uneasy.

This time, Cooper was planning to directly eliminate the troublesome Da Vinci, because he noticed that these people were all moving around this girl with three missing traits as their center.

If he took out Da Vinci, this group would just be a flock of birds; the principle of capturing the thief first by capturing the king, Cooper also understood.

Everyone remained silent, tense, not saying a word, holding their breath in the thick black smoke, all checking Cooper's position.

A piercing sound suddenly rang out; a short sword stabbed straight toward Da Vinci, targeting her temple!

Under obstructed vision, almost no one reacted in time. Da Vinci was directly in danger.

Da Vinci held out both hands; her living alchemical equipment rapidly expanded, forming a shield to protect herself.

This shield was made of beast scales, having excellent defensive capability, but after making a crisp "dong" sound, it was directly pierced by the short sword.

However, this living alchemical equipment seemed to still have something. The tip of the short sword was only a few millimeters from Da Vinci's eyeball. She couldn't speak, her heart nearly stopping, feeling she had just brushed past death, nearly being done in by the enemy!

"Da Vinci, you haven't..." Rosetti couldn't see anything, but felt something must have happened.

"Da Vinci, calm down a bit."

"Really?"

Cooper's voice suddenly rang in Da Vinci's ear, like a hellish ghost's call.

Da Vinci suddenly opened her eyes wide, her face deathly pale, a thread of fear flashing in her eyes.

Cooper struck Da Vinci with a fist without a shred of mercy, not caring about showing compassion for a beauty.

"Cough!"

Da Vinci let out a miserable cry, being struck to the ground and falling directly into unconsciousness.

"Da Vinci!" Rosetti was about to rush forward to help, but was kicked in the abdomen by Cooper.

"Ah!" Rosetti cried out in pain, rolling on the ground, her consciousness beginning to blur. Bastard

"Heh!" Alice's fine sword suddenly struck out, trying to pierce Cooper's throat.

"So weak~" Cooper revealed a playful smile, raising the short sword in his hand. Even as he slashed down, a shock wave formed by Sacred Power instantly sent Alice flying backward.

Other adventurers had just barely reacted, swarming up without any order!

"I don't like men. You just go down to hell obediently~"

Cooper held short swords in both hands, his expression cold. Instantly dancing, he killed over a dozen male adventurers outright!

The thick black smoke dispersed. Only Cooper stood in the center, surrounded by several corpses, all dying from a single sword stroke.

It was raining lightly, washing the blood on the ground, somewhat desolate.

"Comfortable! Indeed, the feeling of a blade cutting through flesh is the best."

Cooper twisted his neck, feeling he had only warmed up.

His gaze fell on the soft Alice on the ground. Instantly, a greedy expression appeared, and he took large steps toward her.

"Beauty, I'm coming, hehehe~"

"Despicable"

Alice stretched out her hand, trying to retrieve the fine sword not far away.

However, the injured Alice moved sluggishly, not at all like her usual carefree self.

Cooper came before Alice, slowly squatting down, lifting her pretty face with his hand.

"How should I play with you next?"

"Get away!"

Alice stretched out her hand and gave Cooper a tight slap, thoroughly disgusted at anyone touching her.

Cooper touched his cheek, his expression full of bewilderment. His face had been scratched by Alice's nails, forming a few red marks.

"You this nasty bitch, daring to slap my face? I'll do you now, make you ah ah scream!"

Cooler's cold face, planning to ruthlessly toy with Alice, letting her experience what humiliation is, and then kill her despairingly.

Cooper flipped over and rode on top of Alice, suppressing her body.

He used his hands and feet, and moved toward Alice's skirt.

Chapter 39 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter (6000 Characters)

Volume 9 · Chapter 39

“Let go of me, you bastard!”
Alice struggled wildly, trying to break free from Cooper’s grip.
But how could a high‑rank magic swordsman resist the power of a Saint‑tier expert?
Alice’s eyes burned with anger, humiliation welling up inside her, forcing her to glare at Cooper.
“If you dare touch me, I’ll never let you off!”
“Hahaha! Excellent, excellent. Many women I’ve pressed beneath me have said similar things, but before long their bodies will become honest~”
Cooper sat on Alice, one hand ruthlessly suppressing her unruly struggles, the other hastily trying to undo her outer robe.
“I can tell you’re a virgin; your scent is different. I love a blank slate like you. Rest assured, as long as you obediently cooperate, I’ll be a little gentler and let you experience endless pleasure.”
“No… no‑shame! I will definitely kill you!” Alice’s eyes turned vicious, a killing intent surging from deep within.
“Hehehe~… being shameless is practically a compliment to me, thank you, beautiful lady.”
Cooper yanked open Alice’s white robe without hesitation, revealing the clothing underneath; large patches of dragonified scales instantly appeared.
Especially on her arms, the blue‑white scales were neatly arranged like dazzling jewels, covering her entire visible body.
Even Alice’s cheeks bore a few dragon scales, showing just how far her dragonification had progressed.
Cooper stared blankly at the scales on Alice’s body, apparently never having encountered this before.
“Hey hey hey, what’s going on? Are you even human?”
Alice felt deep humiliation, golden light flickering in her eyes as her pupils constricted slightly.
Unable to control her emotions, Alice’s latent dragonification began to stir again.
Her power noticeably increased; the golden pupils flickered in and out, exuding intimidation.
“Get lost! Or you’re dead for sure!”
“Ugh!”
Cooper was somewhat startled, the golden gaze making him feel uneasy, as if being stared down by a superior species.
But under Alice’s deliberate suppression, the intimidation wasn’t that strong.
Cooper disliked women looking down on him with contempt; he drew his short sword and viciously stabbed it through Alice’s palm, pinning her to the ground.
“Ahhhhh!”
Alice let out a shrill scream, both hands overlapped and pierced, a piercing pain surging through her, threatening to overwhelm her consciousness.
“I told you, stop threatening me. Women like you, who think they’re above everyone else, I’ve seen plenty. I love taming women like you—it lets me feel the thrill of conquest.”
Cooper wore a teasing smile, roughly gripping Alice’s chin. Seeing the dragon scales, he showed no retreat, only excitement.
“I’ve played with many women; beings like you—neither human nor ghost—I’ve never met before. This is truly novel. Watch me toy with your body, make you feel ecstatic, haha~”
“I… I will kill you…”
Alice gritted her silver teeth, enduring the pain; beads of blood trickled from her palm, continuously eroding the surrounding rainwater.
She felt the dragon race’s power surging inside her, frenziedly devouring her sanity, making it hard to keep control.
She didn’t want to die; she fought with all her might to suppress the impending berserk power, clinging to her sanity, unwilling to simply vanish from this world.
Yet the bastard before her planned to take advantage of this moment to violate Alice’s purity, leaving her feeling powerless to resist.
Now Alice faced a dilemma, hard to choose—
If she wanted to protect her purity, she should let the dragon race’s power run wild, resulting in her disappearance from this world.
Or she could preserve her life by submitting to this despicable man’s violation, losing her purity instead.
Either choice was agonizing; Alice hated being touched by men she didn’t like, because she had someone she liked—the elusive Elgin Sword Master existing only as a silhouette.
But Alice also didn’t want to die; she was young, with many wonderful moments left to enjoy. Vanishing from this world now would be a pity.
This fish‑and‑bear’s‑paw predicament left Alice torn between advancing and retreating, only waves of humiliation making it unbearable.
Cooper could barely hold back, eagerly fumbling with his belt, preparing to do the deed out in the open, unabashed.
Alice, tormented by the dragon race’s power, felt utterly helpless; unwilling tears welled up, sliding down her cold cheeks—a pitiful sight.
Why?!
Why did I have to encounter this?!
From childhood to now I’ve always faced such desperate choices!
Do I really look that easy to bully…?
◇

Long‑ago memory.
Deep winter in the Alps’ snowy mountains.
In this season all things struggle, seeking a sliver of hope for survival.
Mercilessly killing the opponent, turning them into a stepping stone for the survivors.
Wolf packs, though their movements have lessened, still search for prey to fill their bellies, trying to endure the long, cold winter.
Countless unseen places stage the farce of the strong devouring the weak, which they uphold as the so‑called truth.
Snow blankets the landscape like thick goose‑down coats, covering the towering snow‑capped mountains.
Biting icy winds sweep past a pitch‑black cave, carrying beautiful snowflakes…
“What are you doing, teacher?! Let me down!”
Little Alice was hauled by the teacher toward the cave, she struggled fiercely, but to no avail; she could only flail her limbs, trying to resist.
Upon reaching the cave entrance, the teacher tossed little Alice straight inside, his face devoid of expression, appearing extremely cold, then slammed the iron gate shut and locked it with a heavy padlock.
“Ouch!” Little Alice fell to the ground, feeling pain; she held back the urge to cry loudly and complained, “Teacher, what are you doing!? Because you can’t find a boyfriend, you’re taking it out on me!? Give me some sense! Old maid!!!”
“Just keep being stubborn; next I’ll lock you in here for seven days. You must figure out how to survive—I won’t care whether you live or die during those seven days.” The teacher paused, adding with a wicked grin, “Oh, and here’s some good news: you have a companion—a wolf that’s been starving for over a month. Get along nicely~”
“Ah?!” Alice stared blankly, looking behind her; in the deep black hole, a pair of emerald eyes fixed on her, its sharp fangs still terrifying for a little girl.
“See? He seems to welcome you!” the teacher couldn’t resist teasing.
“Waaah waaah waaah!”
Alice burst into tears—she was just a helpless little girl, why treat her like this?
She rushed to the iron gate, tears streaming, begging for forgiveness, hoping the teacher would pardon her.
“Teacher, I was wrong; I won’t call you an old maid anymore, let me out, please… sob sob sob…”
“I already said, for these seven days I won’t care about your life or death; you have to find a way to survive on your own.” The teacher smiled ambiguously, seemingly truly indifferent to Alice’s safety.
“What did I do wrong? Please don’t lock me up with the wolf… I swear I won’t call you an old maid again…” Little Alice pleaded pitifully.
“This has nothing to do with that; I’ve noticed your training has been slack lately. Without strict discipline, you won’t behave.” The teacher spoke decisively.
“Teacher…” Little Alice looked at him pitifully.
“Don’t look at me with puppy‑dog eyes; I don’t buy that.” The teacher paused, then shifted tone, “I’m doing this for your own good—forging one’s mind is crucial for anyone; it determines how far you can go in the future.”
“No way! You’re just venting your frustration by tormenting me!” Little Alice wailed, complaining.
The teacher stared expressionlessly, sighed slowly, and said, hoping Alice would understand—
“Long ago in ancient Greece there was a city‑state called Sparta. Though its population wasn’t large, it produced many elites and countless brave warriors; no one dared look down on them. Spartan infants had to undergo a life trial: parents washed them with strong liquor, then elders checked their health. Those who couldn’t endure the test or were deemed weak by the elders were abandoned in the infant‑exposure field to die alone. In adolescence they were sent into the wilderness to endure a perilous baptism; only boys who survived could inherit their fathers’ spears…”
“I don’t want to hear a story! Quickly let me out!” Little Alice grew anxious, shaking the heavy iron door angrily.
“It’s precisely because of your mindset that you need training; I’ve realized I’ve been too indulgent with you, which would create dependency—a bad omen.” The teacher said seriously.
“How have you been good to me? You always treat me as a punching bag!” Little Alice bared her tiger teeth, shouting furiously.
“Hmph, if a brat like you had been born in ancient Sparta, you wouldn’t pass the first test; as an infant your body is naturally weak, I should have tossed you into the infant‑exposure field to fend for yourself.” The teacher half‑joked, half‑serious, as if provoking Alice. “Do you know how those youths who survived alone in the wild managed to live?”
“Wh… what?!?” Little Alice’s nose twitched high, nearly dying of anger at her teacher.
“Those youths faced such dangers, chased by beasts or even stronger magical beasts—normally a dead‑end situation—but a few children managed to survive.” The teacher locked eyes with little Alice, speaking earnestly, “The surviving children shared a trait: they achieved self‑transcendence, accomplishing the impossible; their sole driving force was simply to stay alive—to surpass their weak selves for the sake of survival, turn themselves into predators, and seize a sliver of life in this cruel world of the strong eating the weak. Those who refused to change perished; only those who adapted themselves to the environment lived.”
“I don’t get it…” Little Alice’s brows knotted tightly, completely bewildered.
“Tsk! You dimwit student might as well go die; at least your flesh could save that starving lone wolf in here. But as your teacher, I’ll give you a gift…” The teacher flung a rust‑stained iron sword at Alice, then said, “This is your weapon—either struggle to survive, or become wolf dung~”
After saying that, the teacher turned and left, locking Alice and the wolf inside together, not even glancing back.
“Teacher! I was wrong! Let me out!”
Little Alice begged desperately, but the teacher had already vanished; all she could see was the endless white snow.
In her heart she cursed the teacher’s whole family, endlessly complaining about his narrow‑mindedness and constant bullying.
Suddenly remembering there was still a wolf in the cave, Little Alice hastily picked up the rusty iron sword from the ground to defend herself.
Seeing the pair of glowing green eyes in the depths, Little Alice felt terrible, terrified; at this moment she hadn’t cultivated any battle qi or magic power—she was just an ordinary person.
Little Alice was still a bit naïve, trying to befriend the hungry wolf.
“Little… little wolf, we… we’re both pitiful; let’s… be friends…”
The wolf, feeling threatened, stepped forward a baring its fangs, letting out a low, muffled growl.
Alice instantly clamped her mouth shut, on the verge of tears, clutching the rusty iron sword and shivering at the cave mouth.
At that moment she seemed to grasp a truth: the law of the jungle is basic; she was merely prey in the wolf’s eyes.
Time began to fly; seven full days passed, each day feeling like an eternity for Alice.
She felt utterly exhausted in body and mind, constantly on guard against the wolf, fearing she’d be eaten.
Hunger and cold intertwined, Little Alice tasted despair—
Day 1.
Little Alice felt bitterly cold; she didn’t dare sleep lightly at night.
The wolf deep inside stared at her fixedly, as if starving, wanting to devour this human, yet wary of the rusty iron sword.
Day 2.
Little Alice tried to keep her composure; she felt hungry, her stomach growled, and even when thirsty she could only eat a few mouthfuls of snow.
At night she heard strange noises; the wolf inside was scraping its claws against the rock wall, unclear what it intended.
Day 3.
Little Alice felt extremely fatigued; her eyelids grew heavy, yet she still dared not sleep, her stomach aching from hunger.
The wolf in the cave noticeably stared at Alice more often, as if waiting for her weakest moment to strike.
Day 4.
Little Alice’s mind began to falter; hallucinations appeared, dark circles under her eyes grew pronounced, her body felt weak, she couldn’t muster strength.
The wolf’s gaze on Alice glowed with hungry green light, saliva dripping from its mouth.
Day 5.
Little Alice was starving; she had to eat snow to fill her belly, gaining a slight sense of satisfaction, drowsiness nearly driving her mad, yet she still refused to sleep.
The wolf this time tried to approach Alice, but she drove it back with the rusty iron sword; their tentative harmony seemed about to end.
Day 6.
Little Alice could no longer bear the hunger; her gaze drifted toward the lone wolf in the depths, imagining the taste of wolf meat.
Indeed, the law of the jungle holds true—harmony is useless; survival is the key!
The wolf also grew restless, repeatedly baring its fangs at Alice, equally hungry, it had already made up its mind.
Day 7.
The relationship between the two completely changed; they were no longer merely coexisting.
In each other’s eyes, the other was merely prey to keep oneself alive—one of them had to die.
Alice no longer saw herself as weak; hunger had reshaped her self‑perception—if she wanted to live, she must kill that wolf.
Eat its meat, then sleep soundly without worry; only then could she revive herself.
Nothing is impossible; ahead and behind are dead ends—why not change oneself?
The law of the jungle cannot be altered by anyone; I would rather become a predator, because—
I also want to live! Achieve transcendence, then live more openly!
Little Alice’s body was frail, swaying, her vision blurred.
The starving wolf lunged at Alice frenziedly, but in its stupidity it slammed headfirst into the rusty iron sword, impaling itself to death.
Alice felt a warm trickle slowly flow into her throat; this substance wasn’t tasty, like pouring molten lead into a stomach.
It was purely forced down by sheer willpower; later Alice turned over and lay face‑up asleep—
Only afterward did she learn that wolf meat carries an untreatable illness.
Moreover, the wolf’s leg had already been broken by the teacher, leaving it with no combat strength.
◇

Search for quality books.
A light drizzle pattered.
Cooper was riding on Alice; this scene bore an uncanny resemblance to that distant memory.
Earlier, the starving wolf had turned human, now eyeing the girl before him with intent to devour her.
Alice closed her eyes, her heart gradually calming, as if awaiting death’s arrival.
Indeed, the weak are unsuited to survive in the law of the jungle; now I must seek change, achieve self‑transcendence…
Cooper loosened his belt to free himself for the act, then grabbed Alice’s skirt, preparing to pull it aside and peek at the girl’s secret place.
Just then, the dragon scales on Alice’s body receded like a tide, restoring her former smooth skin.

Alice desperately wrenched free the short sword piercing her palm, splattering layers of blood, she rose and gripped Cooper's wicked hand tightly, not letting him touch her.

"Ugh!" Cooper raised his head in surprise, not expecting the girl beneath him to still have the ability to resist.

"Get lost."

Alice said each word clearly, her silver hair wet and clinging together, her eyes more determined than ever, filled with stubbornness.

Cooper felt something was off, quickly snatched up his short sword and retreated, fastening his waist belt, crossing the two short swords before his chest in a defensive stance.

Alice picked up her slender sword, slowly stood up, the blood seeping from her hands flowing with the rain, like a suffering angel, bloody yet still beautiful.

Suddenly! Golden magic and battle aura burst forth, two forces entwining Alice's body, each locked in a fierce struggle, intertwining.

Saint-tier! This is the sign of reaching the threshold of the strong!

Without a doubt, Alice has succeeded!

"Oh? You can actually reach Saint-tier at a time like this? How amazing!" Cooper narrowed his eyes, stuck out his tongue to lick clean Alice's blood on his short sword, finding the situation becoming interesting.

Alice said nothing, only wanting to kill Cooper, the man who humiliated her.

She flicked her wrist, suddenly thrusting out countless silver lights, her slender sword whistling through the air without cease.

"Hmph! Naive~"

Cooper crossed his two short swords in his hands, instantly locking Alice's slender sword, then swiftly shifted to force her to keep retreating.

Alice barely managed to steady her wobbling form, feeling that even though she was Saint-tier, she still lagged behind Cooper.

"You're just a rookie who just reached Saint-tier, you don't even know how to control Saint-tier power; with your current ability you think you can face me head-on? You're dreaming!"

Cooper threw the two short swords in his hands into the air; strangely, the swords didn't fall but hovered, spinning rapidly, absorbing battle aura.

Gradually, these two short swords turned into golden spirals, a destructive aura surged forward, as if it could strangle any enemy!?

This is Cooper's ultimate technique, gathering all battle aura into the two short swords; its powerful spiraling attack can easily pierce any defense, and even kill from a hundred paces away!

Back when Cooper was in the Austro-Hungarian Empire, he relied on this absolute skill to dominate, slaying many pursuers, striking terror into those who heard of him!

Cooper's face bore a ferocious grin, feeling that killing Alice was as easy as squeezing an infant.

"I'll let you see true Saint-tier power—die! You arrogant **!"

The two golden short swords spiraled and shot forth, aiming straight at the wounded Alice, intending to slay her!

Now that Cooper sees Alice is a Saint-tier powerhouse, he no longer wishes to violate her, after all there's the risk of a counterattack costing him his manhood.

Although Cooper likes women, he also wants safety; who would risk losing their lineage for a moment of pleasure?

The golden spiral killing intent surged in waves, nearly altering the surrounding rain, the metallic trembling roar whistled in.

This devastating momentum is something Alice now cannot block, even if both are Saint-tier, the gap in strength is huge.

Having just reached Saint-tier, Alice is like a novice, unfamiliar with controlling such power; how could she possibly match the seasoned Cooper!?

Alice's face turned deathly pale; she could only sidestep, a rotating short sword grazing past her neck!

"Haha, what a pity, my attack cannot be dodged!"

As Cooper's words fell, the short sword made a 180° turn in midair, bringing the rotating golden battle aura back for another strike.

Alice's heart jolted; she hastily raised her slender sword to block, otherwise her body would surely be pierced!

Clang!! A loud crash!

The two swords violently collided, sending up visible sparks!

"Cough!!!"

Alice screamed, spitting out a pool of blood, directly shaken by the impact into severe injury.

This attack was indeed extraordinary, no wonder Cooper is full of confidence.

Alice's delicate body flew backward, only to suddenly crash into someone's embrace.

Oh no! Could there be another enemy!?

Alice panicked, hastily lifting her head, intending to raise her slender sword for a counterattack.

But what entered Alice's vision was that familiar face, so familiar it couldn't be more familiar.

Ruby-like eyes, wet golden hair tangled on her forehead, a handsome face bearing hints of fatigue.

The Alice who had fallen into someone's arms instantly widened her eyes, lowered her guard, and instinctively cried out—

"Me... Merlin!?"

title: Chapter 40 — Rage Slash
content:
Chapter 40 — Rage Slash

Volume 9 · Chapter 40

Merlin rode non-stop, finally catching up with Alice. Seeing no major problems, he slightly relaxed.
However, regarding Alice's sudden advancement, Merlin was still somewhat surprised.
Previously, no matter what method, she would be stuck at a plateau, but when facing a Saint-tier enemy, she suddenly advanced.
As Merlin knew, advancement generally happens in a stable state, but Alice advanced mid-combat, which was puzzling.
Could the pressure and threat he gave Alice be less than that of a mere Saint-tier strongman?
Merlin seriously suspected it was because he was too familiar with Alice, making her not fear him, thus no pressure.
Seems mixing too close with Alice has no benefits. Even a proud demon lord couldn't scare a human girl, embarrassing.
Merlin had a dark face, facing Alice's astonishment without speaking, seemed in a bad mood.
Looking at Alice's disheveled clothes, the padding on her chest was showing. Even an idiot could guess what happened.
Though Merlin knew they weren't real spouses, they were nominal couples. Being taken advantage of by some random man? Too much loss of face!
Merlin vaguely felt a green hat hanging over his head, making him very unhappy, like a boulder on his chest, couldn't breathe.
Dark clouds rolled in the sky, crawling like long snakes through the gloomy sky.
Rain intensified unnoticed, pattering into the loose soil halfway up the mountain.
Merlin wore a black raincoat, hood from behind, rain pattering on the clothes, subconsciously hugged Alice to his chest.
His scarlet eyes stared at the man opposite holding a short sword, not hiding his murderous intent.
The one who made Merlin feel a distinct human, Cooper was probably the first in history.
Alice felt weak all over,勉强 could hold her sword, previous wounds started aching, had to lean on Merlin to support herself.
"What are you doing here?"
Alice questioned again, thought Merlin appearing suddenly was abnormal.
Hadn't she written a final letter, even left the small treasury to Merlin.
Didn't Merlin say he was strong and returning to his homeland? And said such extreme words.
Now all conditions met yet he doesn't return, instead runs to find her for what?
Alice scrutinized Merlin, couldn't understand what this seemingly carefree guy was thinking.
Merlin averted his gaze, looked down at Alice full of confusion, said lightly, "Need to ask? Of course I came for you."
Alice's expression became unnatural, looking at Merlin with a weird gaze.
Really came for me? 5
But why? I didn't notice anything on me that Merlin desires.
Could this demon have feelings for me? Shouldn't be.
Alice had question marks in her head, face slightly red, turned away her head, tentatively asked.
"Why suddenly come for me? Didn't I tell you not to look for me? You go back to your hometown happily, I even prepared travel expenses for you."
Merlin looked at Alice's pouting appearance, couldn't help finding it funny, thinking this washboard is pouting at whom? Did he provoke her?
"I didn't say I must return, and my hometown has nothing, how could the colorful outside world be less interesting?
"Most importantly, my interest is watching others suffer, can't stand others being happy. If you disappear so easily, isn't that a loss for me?
"So your hustle for a tight life is my greatest pleasure. You think you can just pack up and leave? Dream on~
"You bastard!" Alice squeezed out strength, grabbed Merlin's collar, her indignant look like she wanted to bite him to death.
Actually hearing Merlin's answer, Alice felt a bit disappointed, thought Merlin was really an insensitive guy.
At first Alice thought Merlin came because subconsciously he still had feelings for her.
But result made Alice feel heart cold, didn't expect Merlin just dragged her to suffer together, made her liver tremble.
"Sigh, stop it." Merlin sighed, pulled Alice's hand off his raincoat, let her lie flat on the ground. "Rest for a while. That pervert leave it to me to handle."
Alice stared at Merlin huffily, said nothing, turned her face aside, "Hmph~!"
"Oh? Interesting." Cooper looked at Merlin's black iron adventurer badge, immediately showed a playful smile. "An iron adventurer, wants to fight me alone? Haha, ridiculous, I heard the world's funniest joke~"
"Is that so? You think it's funny? I'll soon make you unable to laugh." Merlin walked slowly to Cooper's front, face with disdainful smile.
Cooper's smile faded, face became ugly, thought a weak iron adventurer being arrogant before him, against all reason, probably can't see the gap in strength.
"I think you lost your mind? How? Because I took advantage of your wife, so saving face by acting hero before me?
"Shut up! Bastard!" Alice cursed angrily, still thinking of killing that lecher Cooper.
"I'm not because of that voice, for some personal reasons, you make me unpleasant, so I'll kill you." Merlin said without fluctuation.
"Shout! Vanish! SMi."
Cooper squinted eyes, expression狰狞, two short swords spinning beside him, shot out.
Powerful golden spiral invincible, seemed to tear Merlin apart.
However Merlin used only two fingers, caught the flying short sword, no matter how Cooper urged, couldn't advance a hair!
Merlin used two fingers to forcefully snap the short sword, this horrifying attack was easily broken.
"Your strength is only this level? Disappointing.
Cooper widened eyes, thought somewhat unbelievable, actually someone could block his strongest martial art with hands! ?
And the other was just an iron adventurer! ? Impossible! ? How did they do it!
Impossible! Impossible! Must be luck!
Cooper infused all power into the last short sword, force shot out.
"A garbage villager, don't get too arrogant!" CEz小治
Fully activated ultimate attack power doesn't disappear, speed almost too fast for naked eye; only saw a golden meteor piercing the rain!
But Merlin's speed can only be described as perverted, at this level attack, how could it hit him! ?
"Eh! ? Where!" Cooper widened eyes, cold sweat immediately flowed, blinking Merlin disappeared from spot! When Cooper puzzled, Merlin suddenly appeared before him, single hand grabbing his terrified face, slammed into ground dirt.
"Cough aaa!"
Cooper heavily injured coughed out a mouthful of blood, whole face into mud, subconsciously ate mouthfuls of dirt.
Too fast! What kind of speed! ?
My attack can't catch up with this man!
What iron adventurer! ? This is super strong! ! !
Cooper's brain full of terror, in few moves completely crushed, no resistance at all!
"Sinful mortal, fall into eternal sleep."
Merlin expressionless, looked at panicked Cooper on ground, slowly drew his waist katana.
Black raincoat fluttered in wind, irregularly swaying, red eyes flashed without mercy.
Merlin raised the rusted katana, even if swinging down...
Blood splashed, tiny blooming into weird flowers in rain, =
Speckles of crimson, flew splashing on his cold cheeks

title: Chapter 41 — Severed Arm
content:
Chapter 41 — Severed Arm

Volume 9 · Chapter 41

Cooper was pinned to the ground by Merlin, his body twitching violently before he died on the spot.

Merlin slowly stood up, looking at Cooper’s corpse on the ground, and felt much better.

A soothing sensation spread from Merlin’s heart, as if the curse had received an offering and was now settling.

Alice wasn’t particularly surprised. Cooper had been caught by Merlin—he’d just had bad luck.

The surrounding adventurers were either dead or wounded. No one had witnessed Merlin furiously beheading Cooper.

Merlin wiped the specks of blood from his face with his sleeve and turned to Alice.

"How are you? Not hurt, are you?"

Alice glanced at Merlin, huffed, and turned her head away. "Hmph! None of your business. You don’t actually care about me—you just want to laugh at me. Stop pretending!"

"Hehe~" Merlin grinned, thinking Alice was just throwing a little tantrum. "Fine, I’ll be honest. If you were gone, I *would* feel unhappy. Is that answer good enough?"

"Liar!" Alice said flatly, thinking, *Would Merlin really feel unhappy if I disappeared? Don’t be ridiculous. He’s a demon—nothing but lies.*

Merlin clicked his tongue. *I finally tell the truth, and she doesn’t believe me?* Had he lied so often that she couldn’t tell the difference anymore?

Merlin sighed, then flashed a playful smile and locked eyes with Alice. "Seriously. If you suddenly left, I wouldn’t be happy. I’d feel… off, like something was missing. Sure, you’re clumsy, but I think two people are more fun than one."

Alice pressed her lips together, her cheeks flushing pink as she awkwardly lowered her head.

*Was he telling the truth? Or just messing with me?*
*Do we even have any feelings for each other? Even a little?*
*But Merlin’s always teasing me… who knows if he means it?*

Alice chose not to believe him. She lifted her head, flustered. "S-Stop spouting nonsense! You’re just saying that to cheer me up, aren’t you?"

"Not entirely." Merlin raised his eyelids, thinking for a moment before continuing. "Mostly, I just don’t want to go back to the Death Marsh yet. And if you’re gone, it’s unfair to leave me suffering alone to pay off debts. Misery loves company, right?~"

"So—so you just don’t want me to be happy, do you?!" Alice fumed, indignant. *How dare she almost think Merlin was a decent guy—he was just out to screw her over!*

"Is that so?" Merlin spread his hands, shrugging helplessly. "I won’t deny I have a lousy personality. I think it’s great."

Alice was so furious she couldn’t speak, glaring daggers at Merlin. If she weren’t injured, she’d challenge him to a 300-round duel right then and there.

Merlin dropped the smirk, serious for once. "Congratulations on becoming a Saint-tier powerhouse. Feel less lost now?"

"Shut up! I was never lost!" Alice pouted, instantly denying her earlier tearful breakdown.

"Heh."

Merlin poked Alice’s cheek with his finger, teasing her. "You were crying in your room last night like a little kid."

"GUN!" Alice slapped his hand away, face burning red. "I-I was not! You must’ve imagined it!"

Merlin twisted his lips. *This board… so dishonest.*

As Merlin’s inner monologue continued, a massive eagle soared across the sky, heading straight for the mountaintop.

The eagle was enormous, its pitch-black feathers like steel, effortlessly parting the rain curtains. It was Black Mountain Eye, the mount of the Thorn Knight.

It seemed Mesfield, who had accepted the Queen’s mission, had arrived to eradicate the dangerous faction led by Gōki Raisan with decisive force.

Alice stared blankly at the eagle cutting through the sky, its wings shaking the air. "The First Thorn Knight is here!"

Merlin frowned. *Why is that knight here?* Maybe there were even stronger foes at the summit. In cases like this, more hands made light work.

Merlin decided to follow and see for himself. If nothing else, he could snatch a few kills.

"Alice, rest here for a bit. I’m going up to the mountaintop to check things out."

"Eh? If the Thorn Knight is here, we don’t need to do anything." Alice asked, confused.

"We still need to see for ourselves. Ignoring it completely wouldn’t be right." Merlin slowly stood up.

Seeing Merlin’s determination, Alice had no choice but to nod, her face still flushed as she muttered, "Then… be careful."

Merlin looked up at the mountain peak, where a crimson glow burned like a torch, filling him with an ominous premonition.

At the mountaintop,

Swynburne manipulated the massive magic circle before him. Black, sludge-like matter gathered thicker and thicker, and numerous spirits lingering in Hell drifted toward the center.

The black sludge coalesced into a humanoid shape. The initial resurrection of the Phantom Flame Gōki seemed complete—only a few steps remained.

The figure made of black sludge struggled, opening its mouth to emit a piercing, agonized howl!

The winds suddenly raged, the rain growing fiercer as if the very heavens were darkening.

"Hahahaha—"

"Almost… almost… the ritual is nearly complete!"

"Return, Father! Let all our enemies of old tremble before your power!"

Swynburne’s eyes were bloodshot, his excitement at its peak. The moment for the organization to reclaim its former glory was drawing near.

A sudden eagle’s shriek tore through the sky, shattering the ritual’s required silence.

"Hm?" Swynburne looked up at the Black Mountain Eagle, eyes widening. "No way… already?!"

A figure descended from the sky at breakneck speed—it was the First Thorn Knight!

Mesfield wore intricate gold-and-silver armor, her lavender hair flowing wildly. Gripping a razor-sharp longsword, she charged straight at Swynburne.

"Uh!" Swynburne hadn’t expected the Empire’s lackey to arrive so quickly. Caught off guard, he hastily summoned a magic shield. Dark blue flames roared to life before him, blocking all attacks.

"Die!" Mesfield’s entire body blazed with golden battle aura, radiant as the sun. She raised her sword and slashed downward.

Swynburne’s Phantom Flame shield shattered under Mesfield’s strike like tofu. The defense was cleanly sliced apart.

At the same time, a severed arm arced gracefully through the air before hitting the ground, twitching violently.

title: Chapter 42 — Extra Chapter (5000+ Monthly Tickets)
