Chapter 42 — Extra Chapter (5000+ Monthly Tickets)

Volume 9 · Chapter 42

The storm had died down, but the severed arm lay still on the ground.

Merlin held her sword, her crimson cloak billowing behind her.

“You’re right, my right hand—it’s already gone, the joint itself has been severed.”

Merlin had cut off her own arm with a single, brutal stroke, then followed through with the same motion, severing her own hand.

She was a knight of the thorn order, and this opponent wasn’t someone who could be easily taken down!

Svenburn roared in pain, his severed arm dripping blood, the flow seeming like a fountain. He stumbled back, shocked to see his own hand had been cut off just moments ago, suffering a severe injury.

He pressed his hand against the stump, summoning a faint blue flame that burned relentlessly at his wound, trying to stop the blood flow. The faint crackling sound of roasting meat filled the air, leaving behind a smoky scent.

Svenburn’s face turned pale, his body trembling uncontrollably, sweat pouring down his face like an open floodgate.

Merlin stood upright, her body trembling, her clean sword dripping with blood. She fixed her gaze on Svenburn.

Seeing his wild expression, his mouth constantly cursing, Merlin’s heart remained calm.

“You’re the proxy leader of the Rakshasa Guild, the one behind the *Hauguh Ritual*? I’ve seen your portrait. You look like the kind of guy who’d be a match for Merlin.”

Svenburn clenched his teeth, his face turning a sickly shade of purple, clearly losing his mind from the shock. His mind was filled with nothing but the thought of how Merlin—

“Imperial lackey! You dare cut off my arm! You must pay the price for this, you’re no match for me!”

“Why don’t you just surrender, you’re wasting my time. You can learn more about the Dark Guild’s secrets.”

Merlin’s expression remained cold and indifferent as she said, “Stop acting like a fool in front of me. What kind of creature are you that you don’t recognize?”

“You’re just a dog, stop showing off in front of me!”

The imperial knight’s entire body suddenly surged with power, the pressure of the Saint-tier surging in a short span!

Merlin’s one-handed swing produced a torrent of blue flame like a wave crashing down, raising the temperature in the area so sharply that the rain couldn’t stand it—it instantly turned into steam, vanishing.

The fire then surged forward in a wave, aiming to burn Merlin into ash. The intensity was clearly meant to reduce her to a pile of ashes.

“Help!”

Merlin felt immense pressure from the sheer heat alone, which made her think twice. If the fire came at her, she wouldn’t just die—she’d be left crippled. Fortunately, the mountain’s peak was narrow, making it easier for Merlin to dodge.

Merlin darted left and right, avoiding the flames, but the fire was strange—it seemed to follow her, relentless and unyielding.

“What’s going on? You were so confident before, why are you running around like a rat? Come on, hurry up!”

Svenburn kept shifting his stance, trying to focus on something else, but his wide-ranging fire attack had Merlin’s arm burning red.

Just for a moment, Merlin’s focus slipped, and her arm was scorched by the flame, the heat instantly burning through her skin.

“Ssss—”

Merlin quickly removed her armor from her arm, then collapsed to the ground, her breath ragged.

“Go to hell!”

Svenburn saw Merlin’s desperate expression, then lunged forward, his sword flashing with golden light.

The entire blade glowed with an intense golden radiance.

Merlin was the Empire’s first knight—her strength was undeniable.

Merlin suddenly opened her eyes, her sword flashing, severing the massive fire with a single stroke.

“As I said, you’re not my match!”

Svenburn stared at the fading embers, his expression frozen in disbelief. It seemed his attack had been easily repelled—something he hadn’t expected.

Earlier, Svenburn had heard Merlin was called the strongest knight of the Empire. At first, he thought she was just a name with no substance, but now he had changed his mind. This Merlin wasn’t just strong—she was formidable, at least on par with the best.

Svenburn’s expression was grave as he stared at Merlin, his eyes narrowing.

“Don’t get too excited yet. The battle hasn’t even begun.”

“Not bad for the Empire’s first knight. I admit your strength, but don’t get too cocky.”

Now, he was just a wounded wolf hiding in the corner, barely clinging to life. He urged them:

“You’re the *Hauguh Ritual*’s second-in-command, and you’re acting like a human. I didn’t intend to kill you. If you’re still alive, use this chance to shine again, to revive your past glory.”

Svenburn had a strong obsession, and he wouldn’t let go of this.

Merlin’s expression relaxed.

She didn’t need pity for the weak. This was an insult to her dignity.

“You’re just a dog from the Empire. Don’t act so proud in front of me. The outcome will be decided in the next round!”

A deep, chilling pressure surged, reaching its peak.

If it weren’t for seeing Svenburn as a human, one might mistake him for a demon.

To have reached this level of training with a human body was already at the limit of potential.

Merlin’s expression was grave, and she had to heighten her alertness to respond in time.

Svenburn locked his gaze on Merlin, and suddenly, a massive green magic circle appeared around her, flashing with light.

This was Svenburn’s strongest ability—blocking all magical attacks except fire, with an immense tearing force.

Even rare metals like silver could melt within the circle, posing a severe danger.

Merlin felt the air around her was filled with volatile fire energy, as if it were going mad.

Her instinct told her this was dangerous, and she had to retreat quickly.

But Merlin saw the magic circle was too large—she couldn’t enter it in one move.

In an instant, a towering column of crimson fire erupted into the sky, as if trying to carve a hole through the heavens. The surrounding rocks began to melt, even turning into monstrous, fiery creatures that consumed the magic circle.

Svenburn gasped, his magic drained in an instant. He forced his sword through the flames, breaking free from the circle, his armor scorched, rain turning to steam on his body, producing a sizzling sound.

The golden aura on his body surged uncontrollably. If he hadn’t acted in time, he would have been burned alive inside.

Merlin furrowed her brow, her breath ragged, recalling how she had just been fighting.

“How did you escape?”

Svenburn stared wide-eyed, finding it hard to believe. He hadn’t expected a knight’s willpower to be this strong.

Breaking free from his own fire was something even a child could do.

Merlin’s strength was beyond words—even a Saint-tier warrior would be reduced to ash in an instant with such an ability. This Merlin’s body was far stronger than expected.

Merlin didn’t give Svenburn much time to think, raising her sword and slashing—blood sprayed everywhere.

“Ah!”

Svenburn shrieked, retreating as he entered the resurrection circle. The black sludge around him seemed alive, eagerly consuming his body.

Almost instantly, his physical form vanished, possibly heading to another world.

This was the final step of the Forbidden Revival Ritual from the old kingdom. It required a living sacrifice to resurrect the dead from Hell, and the exchange was equal.

Perhaps he had already—

Svenburn had originally planned to use the lives of Old Sammi or Cooper as a sacrifice to resurrect his father, the Afire Rakshasa Palmer. This obsession was beyond comprehension.

“What is that?” Palmer’s voice echoed faintly.

Merlin’s brow furrowed, staring at the swirling black sludge.

From the beginning, she had wanted to dive into the black waves, but now she felt a surge of unease.

Those black things—she could sense their power. With a single strike, she unleashed a burst of blade energy, aiming to shatter the strange object.

The force of her attack was repelled, making the blade energy ineffective.

Suddenly, a fierce wind erupted, converging toward the center of the resurrection circle, then exploded outward.

The swirling black sludge began to take human form, countless wandering spirits scattering like they’d encountered something terrifying.

Merlin’s eyes widened, feeling as if she couldn’t open them. The black sludge was slowly forming into human shapes.

The sludge receded, revealing a middle-aged man’s face—his body was heavily rotted, exposing his white bones, with blue flames burning in his eyes.

Merlin’s eyes widened. Though the man’s body was rotted and his bones were exposed, she recognized him—this was Palmer, the former ruler of the *Hauguh Ritual*, who had once ruled the human Empire.

The Rakshasa Guild was nearly extinct now, with only him remaining as a lone commander. And Merlin’s face paled. Though she could defeat his son, she wasn’t sure she could defeat him—his father.

Palmer’s reputation was legendary—thirty years ago, he had nearly terrified the entire human Empire.

A man with such a name and strength would never be underestimated. Even now, she couldn’t ignore this dangerous factor threatening the safety of the Empire.

Merlin didn’t know what was happening, nor did she know that the *Hauguh Ritual* had already been erased from history, reduced to a shadow.

Suddenly, a voice came from behind her, and Merlin turned just as she spat a mouthful of saliva on her forehead.

Merlin froze, feeling a chill run down her spine. She touched her forehead, feeling the sticky residue of the man’s saliva.

Merlin didn’t know why she was being spat on, but she looked at the man with suspicion. He was wearing a black raincoat, a katana hanging at his waist, and his face was covered by a torn cloth, making it impossible to see his true identity.

Merlin felt a strange familiarity with the man, recalling a particularly annoying scoundrel.

Merlin’s eyes narrowed as Merlin’s Merlin smirked, pointing at himself.

“You’ve been chasing us relentlessly, Merlin the Great Sword.”

“Remember when I spit on you in London? Haha!”

title: Chapter 44 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 44 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 9 · Chapter 44

The rain gradually lightened, and the dark clouds in the sky thinned.

Palmer, his entire body gaunt and skeletal, stood silently in the rain.

From the beginning, he had watched the British female knight and the mysterious figure in the black raincoat argue, without interfering. After all, having returned 30 years after his death, he wasn’t very familiar with the current situation, so he chose to observe quietly and gather as much information as possible.

However, Merlin’s conversation with the Thorn First Knight had been utterly unenlightening, which left Palmer rather disappointed.

Merlin, seeing Palmer’s lack of reaction, grew impatient. “Hey, hey, hey, I’m talking to you! Can you hear me? Did you go deaf when you were resurrected? I remember the undead don’t need ears to hear...”

Palmer’s burning gaze swept over Merlin. He found the man mysterious and frivolous in manner, nothing like a decent person at all. And yet, he had deliberately come to seek him out—how strange.

“Who are you?”

“Me?” Merlin pointed at himself, thought for a moment, then replied, “You don’t even recognize me? I’m the renowned Elgin, the Great Swordsman of the Empire!”

“Pfft!”

Mesfield shot Merlin a scornful glare, furious. What shamelessness! Clearly just a rogue who threatened the empire’s safety, yet he dared to pose as a hero? And “renowned across the entire empire”? Bullshit! He was just a wanted criminal!

Mesfield inwardly sneered, feeling increasingly unwell. Her breathing grew heavy, and she could only ease the sensation by subtly rubbing her legs together.

Palmer had never heard of “Elgin the Great Swordsman.” This name meant nothing to him—clearly someone who had risen to prominence only after his death.

But when Palmer probed Merlin’s strength, he detected no imposing presence at all. The man was nothing more than an ordinary person, leaving Palmer speechless.

Back in his day, his reputation had been legendary—ordinary people would be terrified just at the sight of him. And now, some insignificant commoner dared to speak to him so arrogantly? The times had truly changed. After his death, all sorts of charlatans had crawled out of the woodwork to play at being heroes.

“Never heard of you.”

“Ah...”

Merlin furrowed his brow. It made sense—his hidden reputation had only grown in recent years. What could a man dead for 30 years possibly know?

“Who I am doesn’t matter. You just need to answer a few questions for me. Do you understand?”

“Why should I answer your questions?” Palmer’s voice was hoarse, dripping with disdain. A mere ordinary man dared address him?

“No reason. If you refuse, I’ll just kill you. It’s that simple.” Merlin shrugged, not bothering to waste more words on Palmer.

“Hahahaha....”

Palmer burst into a sinister laugh. The idea was ridiculous—being threatened by an ordinary man. In his eyes, Merlin was nothing but an ant, while he was a giant who could crush him at any moment. An ant boasting about killing a giant? Wasn’t that absurd?

Still, Palmer found it amusing. He decided to humor Merlin and hear his questions. He was curious what an ordinary man, unafraid of death, would ask him.

“I’ve heard that 30 years ago, you all rushed to campaign against the North Sea Leviathan. What made you all swarm there? It seems odd.”

Merlin asked seriously.

“Hah! Rumor has it the North Sea Leviathan guards the ruins of the gods, where infinite treasures lie. Whether it’s true or not, people will naturally flock there.” Palmer paused, the flames flickering around him. “If one were lucky enough to obtain a legendary divine artifact... I think anyone would understand that such power could dominate the world.”

“I see....” Merlin nodded. Though Hobbes hadn’t given him the full story, it seemed the situation matched what he’d said—most of them had been gold-diggers.

“You’re just an ordinary man. Why are you interested in this? It has nothing to do with you, does it?” Palmer’s hollow eyes rolled restlessly.

“Hah, it *does* have nothing to do with me, and I don’t care about the gods’ ruins either...” Merlin chuckled without elaborating, then continued, “Do you know the legendary Spear Hero? I heard he disappeared during the campaign against the North Sea Leviathan. Do you know where he went?”

“Hmph!” Palmer’s deep blue flames suddenly surged—he was clearly angered. “That bastard must’ve perished at sea! Even if the gods’ ruins *do* exist, he’d never be able to enter!”

“Oh?” Merlin narrowed his eyes. The man who had left such a shadow on his heart being killed by a mimic? That didn’t sit right. “This is all just your speculation, isn’t it? There’s no proof the Spear Hero died at sea.”

“What did you say?” Palmer locked eyes with Merlin, a flicker of killing intent surfacing. How dare an ordinary man question him? That was a death wish!

“I heard you were once beaten half to death by the Spear Hero. So of course you’d be bitter. Slandering your rival isn’t exactly uncommon, is it?” Merlin spread his hands.

“Nonsense!” Palmer’s deep blue flames flared violently, his raspy voice turning icy.

“Mmmm....”

Mesfield, sprawled on the ground, was flushed crimson. Even with her mouth tightly shut, she couldn’t stop the moans from escaping.

She didn’t understand why Elgin the Great Swordsman kept asking about things from 30 years ago. Was there some secret behind it? But she certainly didn’t believe in something as vague as the gods’ ruins.

Mesfield hadn’t even been born 30 years ago, but from what she’d heard, those who returned from the North Sea Leviathan campaign all called it an elaborate hoax.

She also noticed that Elgin the Great Swordsman seemed particularly interested in the legendary Spear Hero. Could this mysterious man have ties to the Holy Church? Was he perhaps one of the Goddess of Light’s Redeemer Knights? But that couldn’t be—weren’t those all just fabrications?

“Since you won’t say where the Spear Hero is, I won’t bother asking further. But since you were pinned down and thrashed by him...” Merlin paused, spreading his hands again. “Tell me, between me and the Spear Hero, who do you think is stronger?”

The question seemed frivolous, but it was the one Merlin most wanted answered.

In the past, Merlin had been weak, deeply shaken by that man, leaving a lingering shadow in his mind. But now, things were different. Merlin had grown—how could he resist comparing himself?

The Flame Specter thought Merlin was an idiot. A powerless mortal, with no presence to speak of—apart from drooling over women, he didn’t seem to have a single ounce of combat ability.

The other was a figure of legendary glory, with transcendent strength and an aura of myth. How could these two even be placed on the same stage for comparison? There was no basis for it!

Palmer felt his intelligence had been insulted. Wasting so much time on a fool had sent his rage soaring. “Mortal, your ignorance makes my head ache!”

“You? *You* dare compare yourself to the Spear Hero? What nerve! Who the hell do you think you are?!”
