Chapter 45 — Chapter Update: 12,000 Votes Secured

Volume 9 · Chapter 45

Merlin couldn't help but sneer, his brow immediately furrowing. What did he mean, calling himself ignorant?

How could you possibly know who's strong and who's weak without seriously fighting?

Merlin was a bit displeased. Originally, Palmer was just a resurrected undead, and he had no particular interest in him.

But if you keep provoking Merlin, then he definitely wouldn't mind watching this guy.

"Who am I? Haha, if I'm a scallion, then you're not even worth being a scallion~"

"Cough!" Palmer gave a cold snort, and the indigo flames on his body began to burn fiercely. "Your ignorance has exceeded my tolerance limit. In my eyes, you're just nothing but an ant."

Is that so? Actually, you're about the same as an ant in my eyes too, but I'm just a little stronger..." Merlin showed a sly smile, measuring with his hand, estimating less than a few millimeters. "It's just this tiny bit~"

"You're looking for death..."

Palmer's soul fire burned even more intensely, and the flames surrounding him erupted as well.

At first glance, it seemed like a demon of flames had descended, bathing in the indigo hellfire—truly an undead!

A ordinary person, daring to make boasts against the one who's gone crazy at twenty! Truly not knowing their own limits!

Palmer suddenly moved, attacking when his master couldn't react.

He was a martial artist in life, and no one surpassed him in close combat.

Now with an immortal body and enhanced by the blood of the sacred dragon, his strength was even greater than before!

How fast was Palmer at that moment? Simply put, before a person could even arrive, the wind from his punch had already slammed into Merlin's face!

A tremendous punch! Merlin was launched like a cannonball, crashing heavily into the ground and sinking into the dirt.

Due to Palmer's overwhelming power, the entire mountain range began to shake, producing countless cracks. It looked like with one more circle, the whole mountain would be flattened!

The rock fragments lost their center of gravity and flew up to the sky. From the waves below, you could tell the power of Palmer's single strike!

All along, the invincible Merlin had been defeated by Palmer with a single punch! ? And he looked so pathetic, which was simply unbelievable!

"...Such a powerful attack."

Mersefield watched in stunned amazement, his face turning from red to pale, his lips trembling as he couldn't speak.

A short and swift strike instantly stunned Mersefield, making him forget that he was still in a state of arousal.

Palmer's punch this time was several times stronger than the machine gun fire earlier. If it were him, he would definitely die!

Mersefield turned around and saw Merlin planted in the ground like a broken puppet, legs up in the air, motionless, looking like he was dead.

Sure enough, Elkin the Great Sword Master wasn't a god either. Facing the tyrant from 30 years ago, he could only be defeated!

What about those stories of one slash killing countless Saint-tier undead? Obviously all boastful nonsense. Now this undead couldn't even kill one, and was knocked down by a punch!

It seemed Elkin the Great Sword Master's strength was about the same as his own, not as exaggerated as people claimed...

Palmer loosened his fist a few times, his hoarse voice carrying a cold snort. "Just an ant, full of boastful words. The fact that he's still alive now is already a miracle."

"Is that so? I was just speaking honestly. Why does it become boastful when it comes to you? That's interesting..."

That voice wasn't anyone else—it was none other than the motionless Merlin on the ground. With that relaxed tone, it seemed like he was completely fine.

"Huh?!" Mersefield was stunned, thinking in shock, how is this possible?! He had just taken such a powerful attack, and he wasn't seriously injured? How could that be?!

Merlin suddenly jerked upright from the ground like a carp, standing up. Apart from being a bit dirty on his body, he seemed to have no other problems.

"...Mersefield's expression froze on his face, thinking, really nothing wrong? That's really strange! I couldn't even withstand that punch! How does this pervert do it!

Palmer was shocked to see Merlin standing up unharmed.

My full-power punch couldn't even kill an ordinary person?!

I feel like my strength hasn't disappeared, but rather has increased significantly. Yet the result is like this?

It seems this man has some tricks up his sleeve, definitely not as simple as an ordinary person. At least this ordinary person is worth taking seriously.

"Ah, it seems your strength is only this much."

Merlin tapped his shoulder and twisted his neck, stretching like an elderly person doing warm-up exercises.

"To be honest, the kind of punch you threw, I could easily dodge. But since you fought the Gun Hero, I wanted to feel your strength, and the result is..."

"You're really a loser, no wonder you were seriously injured by the Gun Hero. With your strength, you're far behind the Gun Hero~"

Palmer was completely stunned, not expecting to be insulted like that. He was the tyrant who had once shaken the human empire just last year, yet he was belittled to nothing. Even the fact that he was just defeated was apparently intentional?! How infuriating! This is outrageous!

The indigo flames on Palmer's body burned even more intensely, as if he had transformed into a sun in hell!

At this moment, Palmer was extremely angry. No one had ever dared to insult him like this.

30 years ago, he was at the peak of his glory. 30 years later, he was insulted by a young upstart.

How could he accept such a huge gap?

"A conceited brat! I want to see how you can withstand my punches of hundreds of millions per second!"

As soon as he finished speaking, Palmer leaped up, jumping into the sky, apparently planning to strike from above with continuous attacks!

He turned in mid-air and then plunged down, like a divine soldier bathing in hellfire!

Before the attack even arrived, Palmer's overwhelming pressure had already caused the entire mountain range to tremble. This round of strikes might flatten the entire mountain!

"Too bad, you won't get the chance to show off..."

Palmer's head was smashed into the dirt with a loud crash, but only his body stopped. His head was already rolling on the ground.

As for Merlin's drawing action just now, Palmer didn't even see it clearly. His head just flew up directly!

Goodness! Why is this man so strong?!

In his lifetime, this was the first time he had seen such an unusual draw slash!

He must not have used his full strength. If he used such a low-level technique and could defeat me, then if he gets serious...

It's hard to imagine the gap between us. It can only be described as being on different dimensions.

Because Palmer was an undead, his soul fire wouldn't extinguish, and he wouldn't die. Otherwise, he probably wouldn't be thinking so much.

Merlin descended from the sky with no expression on his face, holding a rusty sword and approaching Palmer's rolling head.

"Why? Why are you so strong? Even that Gun Hero..."

Merlin pierced Palmer's head with the sword, extinguishing his soul fire, and the terrified voice was cut off.

"Weaklings, forever unable to see their own reality."

"Where did you come from? Just go back where you belong."

"Only in the garbage dump of hell is where you belong to exist."

title: Chapter 46 — Hi Forest
content:
Chapter 46 — Hi Forest

Volume 9 · Chapter 46

After extinguishing Palmer's soul fire, Merlin sheathed his great sword and prepared to leave.

Though Palmer had been the dominant force thirty years ago and his strength was indeed formidable, before Merlin, all of that amounted to nothing.

All that boasting loud enough to shake the heavens, and in the end, he was still just some fool who got instantly killed—completely useless.

This Wraithflame Tyrant was truly unlucky. He had only just been resurrected before running into Merlin; otherwise, he might have really stirred up chaos across the continent again!

Merlin was disappointed in Palmer. He had thought that a man who once threatened the human nations would be far stronger, but in the end, he was only this level—being pinned down and humiliated by the Gun Hero was only natural.

Mesfield watched all of this in shock, utterly bewildered. The tide of battle had turned back and forth, yet in the end, the once-dominant Wraithflame Tyrant had still been slain by the Great Sword Hero Elgin.

And what was supposed to be an earth-shaking, ghost-weeping battle had ended in the blink of an eye.

Just like the many rumors circulating within the empire—an instant kill, no dragging it out at all!

No way... Could all those rumors be true?!

Elgin the Great Sword Hero’s strength had reached an inhuman level!

Perhaps Hopman had never lied from the start—this mysterious man had indeed instantly killed countless Saint-tier undead!

Mesfield’s stunned expression froze on her face. She never could have imagined that the invincible Palmer would be instantly killed by Merlin!

Now, she finally understood the seventh knight Morrison’s abnormal reaction—why he said that if everyone fought together, they still might not be able to defeat Elgin the Great Sword Hero, and that acceptance was far wiser than hostility.

This was no joke—it was the truth. Even Mesfield herself was starting to waver, doubting whether she could defeat this mysterious man.

But Mesfield was unwilling to accept this. How could she, the empire’s strongest knight, submit to the tyranny of a thug?

And she had already been spat on twice in a row—such a humiliating disgrace, how could she possibly swallow this insult?!

But considering the empire’s interests, she really shouldn’t dwell on it... yet a warrior could be killed but not humiliated!

Mesfield’s shock and fury intertwined, and for a moment, she even forgot the waves of arousal surging through her body. The way she looked at Elgin the Great Sword Hero now carried a hint of fear.

Merlin turned his head to look behind him and saw Mesfield glaring at him with a murderous gaze. “Hey hey hey, what’s that look for? Got a problem?”

“I...!”

Mesfield gritted her teeth, her face twisted in rage. She truly could not accept Elgin the Great Sword Hero.

A despicable scoundrel like him becoming a pillar of support for Her Majesty the Queen would be a disgrace to the royal family.

It would only bring shame to the monarchy! Who would want to be colleagues with a ruffian who went around spitting on women?!

Mesfield’s face darkened. If she weren’t severely injured right now, she would have already drawn her sword and taken this bastard’s head!

“I’ll kill you someday! Don’t think you can keep getting away with this. Once my injuries heal, even if I have to turn all of Great Britain upside down, I’ll find you!”

“You really do love me deeply, huh? Hehe~” Merlin grinned, knowing full well Mesfield didn’t mean it that way, but teasing was his hobby.

“Bastard!” Mesfield, humiliated and furious, pounded the ground. Gritting her teeth, she said, “You just wait! I absolutely won’t let you off!”

“Oh? Still so full of energy. Looks like the aphrodisiac effect hasn’t worn off yet~” Merlin’s eyes curved into crescents, looking rather lecherous.

“You—!”

Alice glared at Merlin. If he hadn’t brought it up, it might have been fine, but now that he had, it was undeniable.

The waves of pleasure surging through her body were unbearable, and her face instantly burned red.

Alice endured the strange, overwhelming sensations, her slender body trembling on the ground, small whimpers escaping her lips.

“....!!!”

“Hahahaha~” Merlin laughed heartily, finding Mesfield’s state rather amusing. He waved his fingers. “Then until we meet again, aroused knight lady.”

With that, Merlin left without a backward glance, subjecting Mesfield to the ultimate form of neglect play—leaving her alone in the middle of nowhere to suffer through her arousal.

Probably the only things around here were wild dogs, and there didn’t seem to be anything else. As for how Mesfield would resolve her situation... that was none of Merlin’s concern.

“Come back! You bastard!”

Mesfield clutched between her legs and shouted at Merlin, only to watch his figure disappear from sight.

She bit her lip, looking utterly wronged, tears glistening in her eyes.

“Damn it...”

The light rain continued to fall, and the dark clouds in the sky showed signs of dispersing.

Mesfield’s body grew hotter, her skin flushing red all over.

She lay on the ground as if exhausted, her breathing heavy, and soon she was drenched in sweat.

As expected, Merlin’s saliva was too potent—its effects lasted a long time, and it was extraordinarily effective.

If any black market dealer who sold aphrodisiacs saw this, they would surely sigh in defeat, declaring their own products fake, not worth a fraction of Merlin’s saliva!

What was she supposed to do now?

She really felt like she needed a man.

Otherwise, she was going to burn up... and... and her whole body itched so badly...

Even with Mesfield’s strong will and pride, she still couldn’t resist the overwhelming power of Merlin’s saliva.

After all, she was still a woman. A succubus’s saliva was like an intense drug to the opposite sex, capable of making someone lose themselves in minutes.

Though Merlin had come from another world and had no demonic traits, he had retained this Demon Lord-level saliva, which couldn’t help but make one suspect a hint of malice.

The thought of finding a man had crossed Mesfield’s mind more than once, but she was deeply reluctant. She was an imperial knight—how could she, under the influence of a drug, go around looking for men to satisfy her desires? That wouldn’t make her a knight, but a shameless harlot!

And it would bring shame to Her Majesty the Queen. She might even be dismissed from imperial service.

But Mesfield wasn’t naive either. She understood the concept of self-sufficiency.

Mesfield lifted her crimson face, nervously scanning her surroundings, seemingly checking if there was anyone suspicious nearby.

After a thorough search, she confirmed that the area was safe—apart from a single corpse, there were no other presences.

Since the environment had already provided for her needs, what was she waiting for?

Mesfield blankly extended two fingers, biting her lip with the expression of someone about to make a noble sacrifice.

There was no other choice—she had to rely on herself!

This was just like always. She was going to turn into a strange girl sooner or later!

Now she finally realized she needed a boyfriend. If things kept going like this, what was the difference between her and a female beast?!

This was all Elgin the Great Sword Hero’s fault! Damn him...

Mesfield cursed the bastard who had spat on her in her mind, finally unable to endure the loneliness—

She slipped her fingers beneath her skirt, doing something unspeakable...

title: Chapter 47 — Monthly Ticket Update
content:
Chapter 47 — Monthly Ticket Update

Volume 9 · Chapter 47

Actually, there were two more people at the peak of this mountain range—Bella, a reporter for the London Times, and her cameraman assistant.

Bella, who pursued scoops and was good at fabricating stories, naturally had good connections.

She had secretly climbed up here, hoping to get some hot news to boost her own reputation.

How could such a major event as defeating the demon lord not involve her?

But this trip turned out to be quite fruitful.

She had originally expected to capture footage of Mesfilld slaying enemies.

Instead, she ended up seeing Mesfilld get knocked to the ground by a single punch from the enemy, and never get back up again.

Just when Bella felt this place was very dangerous and was preparing to leave, Elkin the Sword Master appeared!

Bella made a quick decision not to leave, but to keep filming.

That was Elkin the Sword Master! The empire's most popular figure! So many topics!

As long as she held out, she might get first-hand visual material of Elkin the Sword Master!

Bella had already seen the sales figures of other newspapers, which were far behind the London Times.

In the end, the result didn't disappoint Bella—Elkin the Sword Master killed an enemy that even the empire's strongest knight couldn't defeat, and it was an instant kill!

This made Bella feel incredibly shocked. It seemed the rumors were true—Elkin the Sword Master was even stronger than the Thorn First Knight, with a clear gap.

Moreover, the threat of the demon lord lately had been widely discussed. Now the threat had been personally handled by Elkin the Sword Master—this was the rhythm of becoming the empire's savior!

If it's the times that make heroes, then no one is more suitable than Elkin the Sword Master right now!

This was hot news. Bella felt her promotion and raise were just around the corner, and she was a little excited thinking about it~

Unfortunately, it was raining and foggy, and the surrounding mist was quite thick, making the footage not very clear.

But as long as she could confirm that mysterious man was the rumored Elkin the Sword Master, that would be enough to make a big deal out of it.

"How's it going?" Bella asked the assistant beside her.

The assistant kept filming, muttering, "The fog is too thick, it's hard to make out clearly. It seems like it's already over—Elkin the Sword Master has already left?"

"Ah?! Left?! Where did he go?" Bella was immediately excited.

"Can't see clearly..." the assistant responded with a sigh.

"Useless! Get up, let me have a turn!" Bella snatched the assistant's magical photography device and started examining it herself.

As the lens kept zooming in, like a telescope, she could see very far.

Combined with the rain stopping and the fog beginning to dissipate, she could finally see the scene in the center.

She could vaguely see Mesfilld kneeling on the ground, her hand reaching under her skirt, neck tilted back.

Her whole body was flushed with a rosy red, wearing an expression of being lost in pleasure and unable to pull herself away...

Bella stood there blankly, putting down the magical camera, and then her expression twisted into something exaggerated.

"Holy crap! What did I just see?!"

"What's wrong? Let me see?" the assistant leaned in, very curious.

Bella hesitated, then waved her hand, "No, no, no, stop looking! Let's just leave, there's nothing worth seeing here."

The assistant scratched his head, looking at the thin mist in the distance, completely unaware of what had happened.

Bella stroked her chin, furrowed her brow, and sighed inwardly.

Even the empire's strongest knight was still a girl.

kSFA

It's better to take this with understanding. Let's just delete the footage from earlier and pretend it never happened.

But what exactly happened back then? Why did this happen?

Mesfilld's relationship with Elkin the Sword Master... seemed a little suspicious.

A few days later.

The London Times broke its historical sales record.

The reason was simple—they had written a very eye-catching front-page headline.

"The demon lord threatening the empire, Elkin the Sword Master single-handedly wiped out!"

"Elkin the Sword Master's first visual reveal! Top reporter narrates the full process of witnessing!"

Such eye-catching news instantly echoed through every street and alley of the empire, and the printed newspapers were snatched away as soon as they were distributed.

It forced the London Times to rush print overnight, barely managing to maintain supply.

Many people felt like they had been saved by Elkin the Sword Master, simply the savior in everyone's hearts.

Otherwise, the recent commotion about the demon lord's threat had everyone living in fear and unable to rest peacefully.

Little did they know that all of this was a stage play orchestrated by Queen Elizabeth herself, and there was no real threat at all.

But it seems even Queen Elizabeth didn't expect that after all her scheming, she ended up being the one who made Elkin the Sword Master's wedding dress!

In the capital city, many people abandoned their work to rush out and buy newspapers, eagerly discussing Elkin the Sword Master. Even the city reconstruction work fell into an awkward stagnation.

Even many young girls went crazy fighting to grab newspapers, just to see a photo of Elkin the Sword Master himself.

Unfortunately, the photos were blurry, mostly obscured by the fog. But his sturdy build still caused quite a stir, and a large number of female fans became infatuated.

C or 牡 small play

More and more people began to sing praises for this mysterious hero, and Elkin the Sword Master's influence reached unprecedented heights.

As for the Queen of Britain? Her position was already hanging by a thread.

Regarding Queen Elizabeth's order to issue an arrest warrant for Elkin the Sword Master, more and more people began to be dissatisfied.

A queen who is greedy for power and ignores public opinion—what use is she?!

In the palace.

Mesfilld knelt on one knee below the throne, her expression grave, with sadness flashing through her eyes.

In the end, this incident had blown up, and worse than ever before.

Mesfilld felt she had done her best, but no matter how hard she tried, she couldn't defeat Elkin the Sword Master.

Even that unlucky guy, the Flames Demon Lord, couldn't fight back against a single punch from her—how could she possibly win?!

Mesfilld felt she was about to face the Queen's wrath, and wouldn't get any good treatment.

Queen Elizabeth silently put down the newspaper, her face darkening, looking at the Mesfilld below who dared not raise her head, and tore the newspaper apart.

"A bunch of hopeless losers!"

Queen Elizabeth was furious, stumbling and staggering down from the throne, approaching Mesfilld. The maids behind her trembled with fear.

This wasn't because Queen Elizabeth had a bad temper, but because she had prepared everything so carefully—building the stage to create a hero, letting Mesfilld take the spotlight, only to end up benefiting Elkin the Sword Master, further expanding his influence!

Queen Elizabeth glared at the kneeling Mesfilld, her eyes filled with rage and blood vessels bulging, grinding her teeth to ask.

"Why didn't you successfully defeat the demon lord, and instead let someone else take the credit?!"

"Because... because 30 years ago, that Flames Demon Lord was resurrected, and my strength was insufficient to..." Mesfilld furrowed her brow and continued.

"If it weren't for Elkin the Sword Master suddenly appearing and killing this thug, the empire would probably be in a critical situation right now..."

"Your Majesty, though I don't want to admit it, this mysterious swordsman's strength is truly terrifying."

Although it might look like Mesfilld was speaking on behalf of Elkin the Sword Master, this was simply telling the truth.

As a subordinate, Mesfilld had to let the Queen know the real situation, but in her heart, she still hated Elkin the Sword Master, grinding her teeth in frustration.

Queen Elizabeth was shaking with rage all over, pointing her finger at Mesfilld.

Failure is failure, and you still come up with so many excuses!

I didn't expect that after preparing everything, Mesfilld would still be so useless!

Even a fool would get a decent result after investing so much!

Unable to accept it, Queen Elizabeth's vision blurred, and she fainted from anger...PS

The next episode will end this volume. Get ready for your tickets, the next episode is super exciting.

title: Chapter 48 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 48 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 9 · Chapter 48

The Adventurers Guild of Rekserum was in a state of wild celebration.

Every time a new Saint-tier warrior emerged from the guild, they would throw a massive party—this time was no exception. Alcohol flowed freely, though the more expensive bottles had already been drained long ago. After all, even the cheap stuff couldn’t dampen the enthusiasm of this crowd.

Uncle Karl stood on a table, holding his drink aloft, his grin wide and slightly drunk. Despite having suffered serious injuries earlier, his robust body had recovered quickly after a few days of rest, leaving him as lively as ever.

“Congratulations to our guild’s Alice for becoming a new Saint-tier warrior! This is monumental for us—it’s the shot in the arm Rekserum needs! Let’s toast to our rising star!” he bellowed, raising his glass to cheer on Alice, who was the center of attention today.

Nearly every adventurer in the guild, regardless of rank, had gathered in a dense, swaying mass. They all raised their glasses in response to Karl’s toast, celebrating the new powerhouse among them.

---

Alice stood in the middle of the crowd, holding her milk, basking in the praise of so many people. She looked a little awkward, clearly not used to being the center of attention. But she was happy—finally, she had crossed the threshold into the ranks of true warriors.

Her teacher had always said she was talentless, that she’d never reach Saint-tier in this lifetime. Now, she must be hurting inside. *Hahaha!* Who would’ve thought she’d get here? Now that she was a warrior, she’d shine brighter than ever, her future as bright as the sun!

Alice’s mood was euphoric, tinged with a smug satisfaction. She still didn’t fully control her Saint-tier power, but that was just a matter of time. Soon, she’d have the chance to stomp Merlin under her high heels—just waiting for the right moment.

The crowd suddenly parted, and Old Tyler walked over, holding a small box.

“Alice, headquarters has approved your promotion to Secret Silver-tier adventurer. Congratulations—you’re the third in the guild. Here’s your proof.” He opened the box, revealing a gleaming Secret Silver-tier adventurer’s badge inside, its light pulsing beautifully. The details were the same as before, including the name of her husband—Merlin—clearly displayed.

“Thanks,” Alice took the badge, feeling her efforts had finally paid off. Now she was one of the guild’s elite, able to take on high-level quests and clear her massive debts sooner rather than later.

Meanwhile, Merlin and Hobbes sat apart from the crowd, drinking silently.

Hobbes watched Alice with envy. “She’s only been here a year, and already she’s Secret Silver? That’s insane. Every Secret Silver-tier is a pillar of this guild—her future treatment will be *way* better than ours.”

*Sigh.* “Alice is really climbing now, while I’m just stuck here, watching.”

“Don’t dwell on it,” Merlin said, swirling his drink. “If you hadn’t been an adventurer and had gone into imperial diplomacy instead, your achievements would’ve been just as impressive.”

“Oh, please,” Hobbes scoffed, taking a sip. “The empire would’ve never hired someone like *me*.”

He patted Merlin’s shoulder meaningfully. “But you? You’re the one who’ll have problems now. Alice is a Saint-tier *and* a core guild member—your life at home just got a lot harder. She might start giving you a hard time.”

Merlin swatted Hobbes’ hand away. “What nonsense. I’m the boss of the house—how could she ever give *me* a hard time?”

Hobbes smirked. “Oh, come on. Even if your bed skills are top-notch, you can’t control her now. You know how it is—once someone gets a little success, they start thinking they’re untouchable.”

Merlin’s expression darkened. *Why does this old man always think I’m the one getting bullied at home?*

“You’re still just a Black Iron-tier,” Hobbes leaned in, lowering his voice. “Alice is Secret Silver now. That’s a *huge* gap. You need to wake up, brother. Otherwise, you might wake up one day and find your wife’s gone—and you’ll have no idea why. Start sending her little gifts, pull out the romance moves.”

Merlin nearly laughed. *Does Hobbes really think so little of me?* Just because he’s Black Iron-tier? Level doesn’t matter. Alice being Secret Silver means she can take on S-tier quests, which is *good* for me.

*Who in their right mind would look at a washboard like her?*

If someone actually did, Merlin would probably kill him and drag Alice back home. As for Arnold… well, he’s useless in a fight.

---

Alice floated over to the counter, grinning as she ordered another glass of iced milk. Her mood was *incredible.*

“Congratulations, Alice,” Da Vinci said from his chair. “Now that you’re Saint-tier, I’d love to study the subtle changes in your body after reaching this level. If you have time, come help me with some experiments.”

“No problem,” Alice said, patting her fake chest. “Alice, congratulations! Now that you’re Saint-tier, you’ll be even more charming…” Lucy hesitated, then pivoted. “Well, *compared to me*, you still have a long way to go.”

Alice scoffed, sitting down in frustration. “Typical—using me to boost your ego. How sneaky.”

“Hey, you’re the star today,” Lucy said, sliding another glass of iced milk toward her.

“Saint-tier? What’s the point?” Rossetti chimed in, watching Alice’s promotion. “No matter how strong you get, you can’t fix a *flat chest.*” She heaved her own ample bosom, smirking. “Like drinking milk—no matter how much you consume, your chest won’t grow. *Hahaha!*”

Alice’s face twisted in fury. “You—you *bitch!* I’ll fight you to the death!”

She rolled up her sleeves, ready to defend her “washboard,” when Arnold suddenly appeared, holding flowers.

“Beautiful Alice,” he said, bowing. “Congratulations on becoming a Saint-tier warrior.”

Alice averted her eyes, not even reaching for the flowers.

“I love you!” Arnold declared again.

Alice rolled her eyes, turning away with a stern expression. “I don’t love you. Stay away from me.”

She was annoyed—Arnold kept chasing her, and she had *no* interest.

Rossetti, burning with jealousy, took the opportunity to pour something into Alice’s glass while she wasn’t looking. *Let’s see her make a fool of herself.*

---

Meanwhile, Merlin and Hobbes kept talking, now discussing the legendary swordsman, Elgin.

“That Elgin is *serious* power,” Hobbes said. “Single-handedly wiped out the Cult of the Howling Ghosts. I heard Palmer was just revived and got killed instantly.”

Merlin sipped his drink, amused. *Yeah, yeah… it was me.* He didn’t say it aloud, but his pride swelled.

The two kept chatting, Merlin’s ego puffed up by Hobbes’ praise—his face even flushed.

Then—*BOOM.*

A deafening cold blast erupted from nowhere, freezing the entire guildhall in an instant. Ice spread across the floor, and everyone gasped, their breath visible in the sudden chill.

Alice swayed unsteadily, her face flushed, her eyes glazed—she was *drunk.*

“Alice?!” Arnold’s face paled. The cold radiating from her was overwhelming; he couldn’t even approach.

“Get away, Arnold! I *hate* you!” Alice swung at him.

Arnold clutched his cheek, bewildered. *Why did I get hit?*

Rossetti hid a smirk behind her hand, delighted. *This is perfect.*

Alice stumbled toward Merlin, her expression a mix of anger and drunkenness. No one dared stop her—they all moved aside, watching as she “drunk-walked” toward him.

“Alice…?” Hobbes stared, his drink forgotten.

“Move! This is *my* seat!” Alice slapped him across the face, shoving him aside.

“Uh… can’t fight… can’t fight…” Hobbes scrambled away.

Merlin frowned deeply. *What the hell is wrong with her?* Drunk people don’t just start swinging at people, do they? *Damn it.* I don’t want to babysit a drunk.

Alice didn’t hesitate—she straddled Merlin, wrapping her arms around his neck and locking eyes with him.

“What the hell are you doing, you reckless woman? Trying to rebel?” Merlin threatened, trying to push her off.

“I’m *what*?!” Alice reached into her chest and yanked out her two padding inserts.

Merlin’s eyebrows shot up. *What the hell is she doing?* Trying to seduce me? *Might as well put them back.*

“Die! Die! Die! Die! *Die!*”

Alice swung the padding wildly at Merlin, left and right.

*Thwack. Thwack. Thwack.*

Merlin’s head jerked like a bobblehead, his humiliation clear to everyone watching.

*What the—?! This drunk woman actually dared to hit me?!*

Alice kept swinging, muttering between strikes.

“It’s all your fault! You ruined me!”

“This bastard made me owe so much money!”

“My life is miserable because of you!”

“You just lie around all day like a lazy slug, doing *nothing!*”

“Do you know how much I *hate* you? Every day, I dream of stomping you with my heels!”

“Then locking you in a cage and *reforming* you—only letting you out when you’re *good!*”

“You *monster!* Die! *Die!*”

Most of the adventurers watched in stunned silence, unsure if Alice was serious. A Secret Silver-tier warrior, *bullied at home?* It didn’t make sense.

Arnold’s face was a mask of longing. *I’d love to get hit with those pads too…*

Alice finally stopped, swaying slightly, her drunkenness making her eyes glaze over.

“Hey… you… you *jerk.*” She sniffled, her voice thick with emotion. “Sometimes… I *do* think you’re okay…”

Merlin’s face darkened. *First she beats me, then she tries to sweet-talk me? No way. I’m not falling for that.*

Alice’s eyes welled up, her lips trembling. She looked like she might cry at any moment.

Merlin was confused. *What’s wrong with her?* One second she’s crying, the next she’s laughing—what’s going on?

“But sometimes… I *do* like you a little…” Alice’s voice cracked, her cheeks flushed.

“Oh, so now you’re the ‘hit me first, then feed me candy’ type?” Merlin scowled. “Dream on. I’m not falling for it.”

Alice didn’t respond. Instead, she tossed the padding aside, grabbed Merlin’s collar, and *kissed* him—hard.

*Mmmph!*

Merlin froze, his hands hovering uselessly in the air. The sensation was strange—Alice’s lips were soft and cold, like mint candy.

The watching adventurers erupted into murmurs. Alice was usually so reserved—now she was making out in public? *The power of alcohol!*

Lucy dropped her glass, shattered on the floor. *So that’s how it is…*

Rossetti smirked. *She needed liquid courage.*

Da Vinci sighed. “Alice…”

The most pained was Arnold. His heart shattered. *She kissed Merlin… in front of me…*

Alice pulled back, her face burning red. She hiccuped, then collapsed into Merlin’s arms, passing out.

Merlin’s stunned expression stayed frozen. He touched his lips, his emotions tangled.

*What the hell…? Did she just… kiss me?*

It *was* nice… but she was clearly a first-timer—her technique was *terrible.*

---
*To be continued.*

title: Chapter 1 — Trick
content:
Chapter 1 — Trick

Volume 10 · Chapter 1

Midnight.

The royal palace was enveloped in silence.

Outside the queen’s bedchamber.

Mesfield stood in quiet wait, ready to receive orders.

Elizabeth had collapsed from sheer emotional turmoil during the audience in the great hall. Afterward, she was carried here, and the court physician had been summoned to diagnose her condition.

Mesfield kept her head bowed, her expression dark, biting her lip in silence. Her mind was consumed by the detestable figure of Elgin, the Great Swordsman.

If not for that bastard, Her Majesty would not have been so anxious, would not have taken such risks, and would not have suffered this crushing blow to her spirit—leaving her so disheartened.

Even Mesfield herself had been affected. The failure of this operation had left her position hanging by a thread.

To this day, she could still recall the look Queen Elizabeth had given her just before fainting—a gaze filled with utter distrust.

For a knight, that was fatal. Without the monarch’s trust, there was practically no reason to exist.

Mesfield felt utterly ruined by Elgin, the Great Swordsman. This failure was a mortal blow to her. Her spirit had withered; she felt she had betrayed the queen’s expectations. She was unworthy of remaining the First Knight—might as well return home and till the fields.

It wasn’t that Mesfield’s heart was too fragile, unable to bear the slightest setback. Rather, most people who witnessed Elgin’s strength firsthand would be overwhelmed by despair, abandoning any thought of resistance, lamenting their own weakness, and questioning their pitiful lives.

Just look at Morrison, the Seventh Knight. He had been so level-headed, yet after seeing Elgin cut down a high-ranking dark elf with his own hands, he had defected on the spot, siding with the enemy and even trying to recruit others to their cause.

Mesfield had to admit that the gap between her and Elgin was vast—so vast that they couldn’t even compete on the same stage. She was filled with despair, and she couldn’t deny that Morrison’s choice had been the right one.

Now, Queen Elizabeth was directly challenging Elgin, which was not just unwise—it bordered on suicidal.

While Mesfield admired Her Majesty’s unyielding stance—her refusal to compromise with outlaws—she couldn’t shake the feeling that this approach was reckless, driven by emotion. It reminded her of the queen’s late twin sister, whose personality had been equally inscrutable.

Mesfield felt that Queen Elizabeth’s judgment had been clouded by power, that she could no longer see the situation clearly, and her actions were growing increasingly ruthless.

But as a subordinate, Mesfield couldn’t voice these thoughts outright. She could only remain silent.

She wondered why the queen had changed so much. The death of her twin sister, Isabella, must have dealt her a devastating blow, altering her nature entirely.

Other than that, Mesfield couldn’t think of any other reason for Queen Elizabeth’s transformation.

Mesfield had entered the royal palace during Elizabeth’s youth, serving as her personal knight for many years.

Back then, Elizabeth had been kind and compassionate, full of sympathy for all, even showing no disdain for the poor.

She had treated Mesfield without the slightest air of royalty, often acting like an older sister and teasing her to cheer her up.

Mesfield had adored that version of Her Majesty, willing to lay down her life to protect her.

But after Elizabeth’s twin sister, Isabella, died, she changed overnight—as if she had become a different person.

She grew quick to anger, her gaze turning fierce. She showed no mercy to those who disobeyed her, even coming to despise the poor and wishing to exterminate them.

Mesfield did not like this version of the queen, for Elizabeth was becoming more and more like her deceased sister.

The bedchamber door creaked open, and an elderly man with white hair emerged—clearly the court physician who had been treating the queen.

Mesfield quickly stepped forward, patiently asking, “How is she?”

The court physician replied, “No serious harm for now. It’s just that Her Majesty is in poor spirits. With proper emotional support, she should recover.”

Mesfield let out a small sigh of relief and nodded. “That’s good.”

The court physician said, “Lady Mesfield, Her Majesty seems to wish to see you. When you go in, try not to contradict her. Be sure to soothe her emotions.”

“...” Mesfield hesitated. She didn’t want to face the queen right now, but she had no choice.

Inside the bedchamber.

Mesfield entered and saw Queen Elizabeth sitting on a silk and velvet bed, her gaze fixed on the pitch-black midnight outside the window.

“Your Majesty.”

Mesfield knelt on one knee, her voice reverent as she called out, fully prepared to be berated.

“I’ve thought it over. This time, it wasn’t your fault. After all, no one could have predicted such a sudden turn of events.” Queen Elizabeth spoke indifferently, though these were merely superficial words to keep Mesfield in her service.

“...” Mesfield’s expression turned unnatural. The more the queen refrained from punishing her, the more uncomfortable she felt. So she took the initiative to request punishment. “Your Majesty, please don’t say that. I intend to resign from my position as Thorn Knight and return to my hometown.”

Queen Elizabeth froze, turning to look at Mesfield. “What nonsense are you spouting? Are you going to resign just because of one setback?”

“I have brought shame upon Your Majesty. This is a grievous error I cannot atone for. Stepping down is the lightest punishment I can accept.” Mesfield said earnestly, feeling it necessary. Otherwise, she would carry this stain and have no face to remain in the Rose Knight Order.

“There’s no need. How many years have you served me? Over a decade, right? If you suddenly left, I’d feel lost. It was just one failure—what’s the big deal? We haven’t been completely defeated, have we?” Queen Elizabeth said calmly, her mood seemingly much steadier.

Mesfield said nothing, maintaining her silence. In truth, facing an overwhelming force like Elgin, the Great Swordsman, hadn’t they already lost? Why couldn’t the queen admit that?

“Mesfield, do you truly believe you’re at fault?” Queen Elizabeth asked, looking at her.

“Yes.”

Mesfield didn’t lift her head, admitting her mistake.

“Then I’ll give you a chance to redeem yourself. If you succeed, I’ll overlook your past failures.” Queen Elizabeth narrowed her eyes.

“You...” Mesfield lifted her head, confused. “What do you plan to do?”

“We will sow confusion. We’ll create a fake Elgin, the Great Swordsman, to replace him.” Queen Elizabeth’s face twisted into a sinister smile.

“Eh?!” Mesfield’s eyes widened, and she cried out in surprise.

A fake Elgin to replace him?!

What kind of scheme was this?

Where could they even find someone capable of matching the Great Swordsman?!

title: Chapter 2 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 2 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 10 · Chapter 2

Melfield felt that Queen Elizabeth’s plan was far too unreliable.

First, the power of Grand Swordsman Elgin was simply too overwhelming. Finding someone who could match him would be nearly impossible. If the people didn’t believe it and the fake Elgin was forced to demonstrate his strength, the deception would be exposed in an instant. In the eyes of the public, Elgin’s power was practically divine. If the substitute failed to meet expectations, they would never accept him. In the end, it would trigger a crisis of trust in the royal family—no one would believe a word they said, and the empire would be thrown into turmoil.

Second, it was a matter of Melfield’s personal principles. She was far too upright to stoop to such schemes. Playing with underhanded tricks made her feel corrupt, and her pride as a knight made it impossible for her to engage in such lowly, groveling behavior. It was nothing short of an insult to herself.

“Your Majesty, this won’t work, will it?”

“Oh? What won’t work?” Queen Elizabeth knitted her delicate brows, clearly displeased by the dissent.

“Grand Swordsman Elgin’s strength is extraordinary. If you intend to replace him, you’ll need someone of equal power. To be honest… I don’t think such a person exists within the empire…” Melfield spoke carefully, trying not to provoke the queen’s sensitivity.

“Melfield, you must understand—we only need someone to replace him, to pretend to be Elgin. Strength isn’t the point. What matters is making everyone believe that Elgin stands with the royal family, not as some rogue force of justice outside our authority…” Elizabeth paused, a smug smile spreading across her face. “Who told that bastard to hide his identity and refuse to show himself? We can take full advantage of that. We’ll hollow him out completely, turn him into a hero of the royal family. This will solidify my rule and stabilize the empire.”

Melfield furrowed her brows, her heart heavy with disapproval. It was despicable. Shameless.

How could the ruler of an empire resort to such underhanded schemes to secure her reign? It was disgraceful. What had happened to the innocent, kind-hearted woman she once knew? Had time truly destroyed everything, changing a person from the inside out?

Even if the plan was feasible, Melfield couldn’t bring herself to support it. It was treating the people like fools.

“But the gap in strength would be impossible to hide. This won’t work.”

“That’s simple enough to fix. If strength is lacking, we’ll make up for it with acting. Don’t you understand something so basic?” Elizabeth smiled knowingly, as if she had already thought through every detail and planned it meticulously.

“Acting?” Melfield’s eyes widened in disbelief. Could acting really cover up a lack of strength? How? And wouldn’t that just be an even more obvious deception? Why would Her Majesty, as the ruler of a nation, be willing to sink to such a vile level?

“Exactly. We’ll have a few strong warriors cooperate. The fake Elgin can deliberately defeat them, making it seem like he’s powerful. And what do these fools know, anyway?” Elizabeth looked at Melfield and continued, “They only know Elgin is a hero. So we’ll brand this hero with the royal family’s mark. In the end, we’re the ones who won’t lose out.”

Melfield stood frozen, stunned by the sheer audacity. To stage such a farce… and the risks were enormous. If the real Elgin flew into a rage, his strength would be impossible to contain.

It seemed Her Majesty had truly become consumed by greed, driven to such lengths by a single rogue.

If this were exposed, the consequences would be catastrophic—internal unrest across the empire.

Melfield wanted to stop the queen, to prevent things from spiraling out of control.

“But if you do this, it might provoke the real Elgin. If he comes after us, it won’t end well…”

“Wouldn’t that be even better?” Queen Elizabeth suddenly said, her smile growing mysterious.

“Eh?!” Melfield’s expression turned to shock. Had she not made Elgin’s strength clear enough? Provoking him would be fatal—so why did the queen seem almost pleased?

“If that mysterious swordsman dares to show himself, he’ll fall right into my greatest trap.” Elizabeth paused, a flicker of ruthlessness flashing in her eyes. “We will kill Elgin without mercy.”

……

Melfield’s brows knitted tightly. She hadn’t expected that the queen’s plan to have someone impersonate Elgin was just a front—her true intention was to kill him. But with his strength, who could possibly do it?

“Your Majesty… who do you intend to send to kill Elgin? Even I am no match for that man.”

“If one of you isn’t enough, then gather the other Thorn Knights. I refuse to believe that so many of you can’t take down a single Elgin!” Queen Elizabeth said viciously.

“With Elgin’s strength, even if all the Thorn Knights…” Melfield trailed off, embarrassed. After witnessing that man’s power firsthand, she was starting to believe Morrison’s words.

A man who could instantly kill the overlord from thirty years ago—even if all the Thorn Knights fought together, it might still be difficult.

“It doesn’t matter. I have another candidate in mind—someone who can definitely defeat Elgin…” Elizabeth said with absolute confidence.

“Who?” Melfield asked, her expression puzzled.

“Gregory, the president of the Capital’s Adventurers Guild. The peerless Violet-Gold Adventurer.” Elizabeth paused, then added casually, “Though adventurers usually refuse commissions with political strings attached, my influence is enough to have Gregory take the job under his own name and help us deal with this troublesome man.”

“Gregory…” Melfield murmured, recalling the extremely mysterious figure in the capital—a monstrous old man who had lived for a full four hundred years. Since the founding of Great Britain, the royal family had maintained close ties with this sorcerer who wielded the power of black holes. That eerie black hole magic was nearly impossible to resist; it was said to be capable of slaying anything, even devouring time itself!

And he bore the title of Violet-Gold Adventurer, the highest rank in the profession, so rare that they could be counted on one hand. Each was an extraordinary figure, their movements unpredictable, their identities shrouded in secrecy.

Melfield furrowed her brows, unable to help but compare the two in her mind.

Gregory was indeed incredibly powerful… but could he really defeat Elgin?

title: Chapter 3 — Reality
content:
Chapter 3 — Reality

Volume 10 · Chapter 3

"One person isn't enough, so we'll use human wave tactics. If that still doesn't work, we'll ask Gregor to help." Queen Elizabeth seemed determined to force Elkin the great swordsman to submit no matter what. "I refuse to believe it—how can all these people fail to catch even a single fugitive!

Mesphield felt uneasy. Although she had never actually seen Gregor act, based on various rumors he was roughly the kind of ancient monster who kept a low profile and stayed out of the public eye. But whether he would actually agree to help Elkin the great swordsman remained an unsolved mystery.

"Your Majesty, I humbly speak my mind, but Your Majesty's actions may enrage Elkin the great swordsman, and then there will be no way to resolve it."

"What does it matter if there's no way to resolve it? I am the supreme ruler of the entire empire—should I bow down to a mere wanderer?!" Queen Elizabeth was getting irritated, her eyebrows knit tightly together.

"I think Your Majesty should show some goodwill toward Elkin the great swordsman and ease the tense relationship."

Mesphield said seriously, having witnessed the man's true strength, she felt even more convinced that Morrison's choice was the rational one.

Although Mesphield herself didn't want to admit it about this fugitive, for the sake of the empire's interests, she could only choose to step back.

"Mesphield, hold your tongue!" Queen Elizabeth shouted angrily, completely unwilling to listen anymore. "Are you going to defy my wishes too? What's wrong with you and Morrison? Are you plotting to betray me? Do you want me to bow down to a mere fugitive? That's absolutely impossible! You just need to do as I say! Do you understand?!"

Mesphield lowered her head, her face flushed red, clearly not in a good mood.

But facing the pressure from Her Majesty the Queen, she could only grit her teeth and respond—

"..."

book.SFA<

Morning.

Alice walked out of her room wearing her nightgown.

She looked slightly pained, as if her head was beginning to throb.

It seemed that even drinking a little would affect her vision.

Alice pressed her hand against her forehead, intending to wash up and then take control of her newfound strength.

Because she had gotten drunk during yesterday's celebration, Alice had completely forgotten what had happened yesterday.

She only remembered everyone gathering together to offer blessings for her becoming a Saint-tier warrior, and then everything went blank.

"What... happened?"

Alice frowned, trying hard to recall, but couldn't remember anything. She just felt parched, her throat dry and sore.

As soon as she stepped out, she saw Merlin in the kitchen making breakfast, apparently frying eggs with a sizzle in the pan.

Looking at Merlin in the kitchen, Alice felt an indescribable warmth.

For a moment, she felt dizzy, suddenly getting the feeling of married life—peaceful and serene, with no worries at all.

Alice's expression suddenly became conflicted, and she felt a bit unable to accept it, puzzling over it.

What the hell is this newlywed aura?

Why has Merlin suddenly become so diligent today?

This isn't normal! Usually he's lying lazily on the sofa, motionless as if struck by lightning.

Oh~ This must be the fake Merlin, right?

Maybe Merlin got stimulated? I'm already an advanced Mithril adventurer, while he's still a lowly Black Iron adventurer.

Hehe~ I've finally turned my life around, thinking about it makes me a little excited.

Alice wore a slightly smug smile, thinking that Merlin's unusual diligence this morning was surely due to her.

And according to the original plan, Alice was about to rise up and become a famous adventurer known throughout the empire.

This was all understandable, after all, with Merlin's help beside her, it was better to heap all the honors onto Alice rather than let unrelated people benefit.

Who let Merlin mess with his own death, anyway? He couldn't escape the fate of a Black Iron adventurer.

Merlin seemed to notice Alice, turned around and said casually, "Hey, morning."

"..."

Alice instinctively blushed, feeling that Merlin's attitude toward her had changed somewhat. Was she imagining things?

Since when did I start blushing? Am I really moved because this guy saved me?

Stay calm. He's the Great Demon Lord who brings chaos to the world.

But yesterday, Merlin looked pretty handsome. Not... not that he's particularly handsome...

Alice confused herself, feeling her emotions had stabilized, and she could talk to Merlin properly now.

"Why are you so diligent today? That's strange. Are you feeling unbalanced?"

"What's unbalanced?" Merlin raised an eyebrow.

The small novel.

"I'm now a Saint-tier warrior, a Mithril adventurer..."

"In front of me, you're all trash."

Before Alice could finish speaking, Merlin cut her off with a disdainful tone.

"You!"

Alice was so angry she turned red in the face, not expecting to be provoked so early in the morning.

She took a deep breath, decided not to argue with Merlin, and instead asked, "By the way, what happened during yesterday's celebration? I can't remember anything."

"You got drunk, you're still drunk now." Merlin rolled his eyes, thinking, How nerve-wracking is this girl? Doesn't she know what good deeds she's done? Speaking of which, what was that creamy smell on yesterday's chest pad?

Alice was stunned, her expression extremely surprised, seemingly taken aback by her drunken behavior.

She had been drinking milk all evening yesterday, hadn't she accidentally consumed alcohol?

Alice became worried that she might have done something embarrassing, and quickly pressed, "Did I do anything shameful while drunk yesterday?"

"You actually don't remember?!" Merlin was amazed, then said with a meaningful expression, "Then I absolutely won't tell you what you did..."

"Say it or you'll die! What did I do?!" Alice pressed eagerly.

"Hmm-hmm..." Merlin smiled and stayed silent, thinking, Alice kissed me yesterday, such an awkward thing—how could I possibly tell her?

"If you won't say it, I'll ask someone else! Hmph!" Alice angrily went back to her room, but seeing how mysterious Merlin was, she was still worried about what embarrassing things she might have done while drunk.

Merlin withdrew his gaze, thinking, I'd better not tell Alice about the kissing incident.

It happened in a drunken, disoriented state. If she knew, who knows what this girl might do.

Merlin hadn't taken advantage of the girl, let alone someone like Alice who was always keeping her head down and avoiding eye contact.

Merlin continued frying the eggs, feeling slightly nervous inside, worried that Alice might go check her own treasure chest.

Now it was empty of coins and jewels, filled entirely with gambling tickets.

That's why Merlin suddenly became so diligent, acting like he was trying to please Alice—because he felt guilty.

Damn it!

Alice, please don't mess with your treasure chest.

I'm really afraid you won't be able to accept this tragic reality.

(∞ kiss)

title: Chapter 4 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 4 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 10 · Chapter 4

Alice returned to her room, preparing to take off her nightgown and change into casual clothes to go out.

Her mind was still lingering on what had happened earlier—

Did I get drunk yesterday? And then... I made a fool of myself?

Why did that happen? Could it be that Lucia accidentally poured alcohol into the milk?

Thinking about it, that scheming bitch Lucia might actually do something like that...

Oh my god! What on earth did I do last night?

It must have been something incredibly embarrassing—so embarrassing that even Merlin refuses to talk about it...

Alice’s heart grew uneasy. She seriously suspected she had streaked naked through the streets. The shame was so overwhelming it could reach her ancestors.

After all, when someone goes wild from drinking, they could do anything. When she was little, she had once sneaked a drink and nearly burned down her teacher’s house.

Oh divine gods, please bless me—let me not have done anything too shameful last night, or I’ll never be able to show my face again...

Alice sincerely prayed from the bottom of her heart, continuing to change her clothes, when she suddenly remembered something.

She had left her savings with Merlin. Thinking about it, he was probably coming to see her soon. He wouldn’t have touched her lifeline, right?

Merlin should know better. After all, that money was for living expenses, not for paying off debts.

To avoid ending up homeless and eating dirt, Merlin shouldn’t have touched her savings. He should know what’s important.

But it seemed Alice had underestimated Merlin. In his eyes, such a massive debt was already nearly impossible to repay.

And while gambling on horse races was also nearly impossible to repay, the chance wasn’t zero. If one day, by some insane luck, he hit the jackpot, it would be a ten-thousand-fold return.

Merlin had the classic gambler’s mentality—he’d rather bet on probability than live honestly.

Otherwise, how could the once great Demon Lord end up fired and living like a stray dog on the streets?

You could call Merlin a non-mainstream? He’d never admit it. The reason he always lost at gambling was because the officials rigged it.

Alice confused herself for a moment, then her hands, which had been changing clothes, suddenly stopped. A hint of suspicion flashed across her face—

Wait!

There’s no way Merlin, with his thick face, would easily let her savings go untouched.

And that bastard always hoped that one day, he’d strike it rich by betting on horses.

A man with that kind of obsession—how could he leave free money untouched?

Alice’s heart lurched. She dropped her casual clothes, crouched down, and pulled out her savings box.

She quickly opened it, only to find that the gleaming gold coins were gone. In their place was a box full of white slips of paper.

Alice’s eyes widened. She stared at the scene before her, wishing it was all a dream. Those coins were her entire savings. How had they turned into worthless paper?

Though it was only a little over 50,000 gold coins—most of which had been earned from helping Cecilia—it was a significant sum for Alice, who had built it up step by step.

Alice picked up one of the slips and examined it carefully. It had the royal racetrack’s emblem and noted how many bets were placed, which horse, and which race and date.

The name “Richard” was deeply imprinted in her mind. Though she disliked horse racing, she was familiar with that name.

Alice’s body swayed slightly. She felt a bit dizzy, as if she couldn’t quite accept the reality before her...

Merlin nervously flipped an egg in the pan. The scent of burning already filled the air, showing just how flustered he was.

Why couldn’t he control his own hands?

Every time he passed a betting station, he couldn’t resist the urge to buy a few tickets. If others could win big, why couldn’t he?

Merlin muttered to himself, but just then, a terrifying, ear-piercing scream echoed—

“Aaaaaaaaaaaah!”

Merlin was so startled his whole body jolted. The spatula in his hand nearly clattered to the floor. That tragic sound—it had to mean he’d been found out.

Sure enough, Alice burst through the door, barefoot, and stormed straight up to Merlin. She thrust a handful of betting slips in his face and shouted,

“Merlin! What are these?!”

“Uh...” Merlin averted his gaze, awkwardly saying, “These are tickets to a glorious future~”

“Cut the crap!” Alice gritted her teeth and dumped the pile of betting slips onto Merlin’s head. They fluttered down like snowflakes.

“Tsk!” Merlin clicked his tongue, feeling Alice was being a bit too violent. “Miss, can’t you calm down a little?”

“How am I supposed to calm down?!” Alice pointed at the scattered betting slips, furiously saying, “Over 50,000 gold coins—all turned into worthless paper!”

“Alice, watch your language. These are called tickets to a glorious future~” Merlin said in a very refined tone, once again emphasizing that she shouldn’t use a low-class term like “betting slips.”

“Fine, fine, tickets to a glorious future, right?” Alice nodded, not bothering to argue with Merlin. She continued, “Can you tell me what you were thinking? Why did you buy these useless things?! Do you even realize what you’ve done?!”

“Of course I do! I’m working hard for our massive debts. Even if the chances are slim, we still have to try, don’t we? I believe that one day, the Goddess of Fortune will smile upon me instead of always wearing that stinking, smug face.” Merlin grew more animated as he spoke, adopting a heroic and resolute expression. “I will prove with actions that even if I’m at the very bottom of the non-mainstream, I will never surrender! Resistance is the destiny of demons!”

“Shut up! Stop painting yourself as some grand, noble rebel—it’s disgusting!” Alice was so angry she poked Merlin hard in the chest. If her strength had been stronger, she would have beaten him to a pulp long ago.

“Hey!” Merlin rubbed his chest and said seriously, “Don’t get physical. I’m warning you—otherwise, I’ll fight back.”

Alice’s cheeks puffed up in rage. She barely managed to control her temper. “My savings... the money I saved for our livelihood—you turned it all into a box of worthless paper! How are we supposed to live this month? Are we supposed to go eat dirt on the streets?!”

“It’s fine, so what if we eat dirt? I’ve long since gotten used to that kind of life!” Merlin fumbled behind his back and pulled out a letter. “And... here, you wrote it very clearly—you gave me your savings. It’s all in black and white. You can’t deny it. How I use that money is my freedom~”

“Yiiiiii!” Alice was furious. She snatched the letter and tore it to shreds, then grabbed Merlin by the collar. “I should’ve known you were being so diligent this morning because you felt guilty! Right now, I want to fight you to the death!”

“Calm down a little~” Merlin spread his hands, feeling Alice lacked vision. “Horse racing is all about luck, but it can make money grow. Compound interest—if we keep at it, it’ll be interest on interest, rolling and rolling, endlessly...”

“Pfft!” Alice spat, glaring at Merlin as she angrily said,

“Shut up, you shameless old fraud!”

title: Chapter 5 — Bonus Chapter: Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 5 — Bonus Chapter: Monthly Tickets

Volume 10 · Chapter 5

"Give me back my money!! I want you to return it right now!" Alice gnashed her teeth in fury, looking like she wanted to take a bite out of Merlin.

"Come on, have a little faith in me. We agreed all the money would be mine, didn’t we~" Merlin shamelessly played dumb, knowing Alice couldn’t do anything to him.

"Who said all the money would be yours?! I meant if something happened to me, then the money would go to you! But I’m fine, so why did you spend all my savings?!" Alice grabbed Merlin’s collar and refused to let go, seemingly ready to fight him to the bitter end.

You couldn’t blame Alice for being this angry—she had every reason to hold onto Merlin’s mistakes and not let go.

After all, that was the savings she had painstakingly accumulated over more than a year. Now it had all turned into a box of worthless paper. How could she not be furious?

"Tch! If I’d known it would turn out like this, I wouldn’t have saved you. What a hassle..." Merlin sighed with an indifferent expression, looking utterly exasperated.

"What did you say?!" Alice hadn’t heard clearly, but she had a feeling it wasn’t some kind of apology.

"Fine, fine, I’ll pay you back. How about this—when I turn my investments around, I’ll pay you back double?" Merlin painted a grand picture to distract Alice.

"I don’t believe you! You’re always in a state of constant loss and misfortune. If I believed you could actually turn a profit, I’d have to be out of my mind!" Alice pointed at her own head, feeling like Merlin was insulting her intelligence.

"..." Merlin felt a sharp pain in his heart, as if he’d been looked down upon. He still believed he had a chance to make a comeback. With so many betting slips, he refused to believe he couldn’t win even a single copper coin! If his luck improved just a little, he’d turn everything around in an instant!

"Pfft!" Alice knitted her delicate brows, unable to resist taking a jab at him. "With your attitude and your abysmally bad luck, if you ever won even once, the whole world would probably end!"

"..." Merlin’s expression turned complicated as he suddenly sensed a deep, personal malice.

It looked like it was settled—Merlin had just been cursed by his own wife again.

---

Inside the Adventurers Guild.

Merlin and Hobbes drank and chatted idly.

"Merlin, you’re mooching off my drinks again today. Do you think I’ll live long enough to see you buy me one?" Hobbes wore a look of despair.

"Uh..." Merlin gave a dry chuckle and patted Hobbes’ shoulder. "You will, you will. Definitely. Look into my convincing eyes."

Hobbes felt like all his money had gone down the drain. No matter how he looked at Merlin’s eyes, all he saw was a man hopelessly addicted to freeloading.

"..." Merlin sighed and looked away, drinking his beer in silence.

"What’s wrong, Merlin? Not happy today?" Hobbes asked curiously, noticing the irritation in Merlin’s expression.

Merlin pursed his lips. How could he be in a good mood after being thoroughly cursed by Alice first thing in the morning?

After that, things seemed to have gotten simpler—probably because Alice realized this good-for-nothing Merlin would never pay her back. Continuing to make a scene wasn’t going to solve anything, so she might as well squeeze Merlin, this fat sheep, for all he was worth.

So Alice had assigned Merlin household chores, and even his allowance from future missions would be withheld by Alice until the debt was repaid!

In an instant, the unlucky Merlin was exploited by this nouveau riche wife of his, reduced to a penniless fool who could only mooch off Hobbes for drinks, his pockets emptier than his face.

The wool comes from the sheep’s back—Merlin couldn’t escape. In the past, he at least had some income, but now it looked like everything would go straight to Alice.

Sure, Merlin tended to throw any money he had into the betting stalls, but that was still better than having absolutely nothing in his pockets, right?

Now, Merlin could only hope that this huge box of betting slips would earn him some face and let him make a grand comeback!

Merlin forced a smile at Hobbes and pretended to be calm. "Hah, nothing’s wrong. I’m fine."

"..." Hobbes narrowed his eyes, clearly not buying it. "Oh~ I get it. Alice is a Saint-tier powerhouse now. Did you get scolded at home?"

"? ? ?" Merlin’s head filled with question marks. How was that possible? The one who always got scolded at home was Alice.

"I understand. After all, the gap between you and Alice has only grown wider. I’ve told you before—play more romantic moves. Otherwise, your wife will only grow more disdainful of you. You have to realize that women are very jealous creatures. Comparing husbands is extremely important to them. So you need to pull out all the stops to make Alice devoted to you!" Hobbes, in the tone of a seasoned married man, began lecturing Merlin on newlywed advice once again.

Merlin rolled his eyes. Did he really look that easy to underestimate?

So what if she was a Mithril-ranked adventurer? What was so great about that?

Merlin didn’t want to talk about domestic matters, so he changed the subject to betting. "How’s the horse racing scene lately? Is Richard doing well?"

"Oh yeah, he’s been winning streak after streak." Hobbes’ face lit up as he spoke, clearly keeping up with the latest trends.

"Then I can rest easy..." Merlin secretly let out a breath of relief, feeling that the momentum was in his favor. If this kept up, he was absolutely going to make a comeback.

Hmph! That damn nagging wife of mine ignored me today, but tomorrow I’ll make her regret ever looking down on me! Merlin thought triumphantly, imagining the scene where he would thoroughly humiliate Alice. It felt amazing!

"Did you bet on Richard?" Hobbes asked curiously.

"Yeah, I put about fifty thousand gold coins on him. All on Richard." Merlin wore a cryptic smile.

Hobbes froze for a moment, wondering to himself—since when did Merlin have that kind of money? Then why was he still mooching drinks?

"Man, you said you were broke. Where’d you get fifty thousand gold coins?"

"It’s... Alice’s money..." Merlin admitted awkwardly, looking a bit embarrassed.

"Pfft!" Hobbes sprayed beer all over the table, his eyes wide. "Alice let you use fifty thousand gold coins to buy betting slips? Good heavens! Why don’t I have a wife like that?!"

"She didn’t let me. I... used it without asking." Merlin muttered quietly.

Damn! You actually dared to steal from your wife’s private stash? Do you have a death wish?! That’s so reckless—you’re really going to get hacked to pieces by Alice!

Hobbes looked at Merlin with a horrified expression, as if seeing him in a new light.

Merlin immediately facepalmed, not wanting to talk to Hobbes anymore. He thought Hobbes had quite the imagination—did he really think Merlin, a noble one of the Seven Demon Lords, would go so far as to *steal* from Alice’s private savings? That was way too degrading.

Hobbes, seeing Merlin stay silent, assumed he was admitting to it and couldn’t help but feel a twinge of admiration.

Daring to take his wife’s private money—how bold! To pull off something so risky... impressive.

Sure, he’d thought about doing it himself, but he’d never had the guts. He was too much of a coward.

Who would’ve thought that the unremarkable Merlin would actually do something he, Hobbes, would never dare to do? Truly admirable.

Hobbes was a little convinced. He could already picture Alice chasing Merlin with a rapier, hacking at him as he fled in all directions.

"Hobbes, Brother Merlin, you’re both here?"

Uncle Karl walked over, holding a drink, and joined their conversation.

"Oh? Karl, why aren’t you at work?" Hobbes asked in surprise. He figured Karl was usually a workaholic, so it was odd to see him at the guild like this.

"I’m taking a few more days off. Need to spend more time with my girl, otherwise she’ll say I’m irresponsible again..." Uncle Karl sighed and sat down silently.

"Is that so?" Hobbes glanced at the busy Lucia behind the counter. "It’s not easy for her either. Lucia’s not getting any younger. I think she should find a boyfriend, then she wouldn’t always be clinging to you, her father..."

"No way! If anyone wants my girl, they’ll have to step over my dead body!" Uncle Karl said angrily, seemingly unwilling to even consider the idea of his daughter getting married.

"Uh..." Hobbes felt a cold sweat trickle down his forehead. He thought Karl was going too far—it was because of a father like him that Lucia didn’t dare to casually date anyone.

"But lately, that girl seems to have taken a liking to the great swordsman Elgin. She keeps talking about him, even saying she wants to marry that mysterious man..."

Uncle Karl stroked his stubble, muttering thoughtfully.

"Pfft!" Merlin was instantly shocked and sprayed beer all over the table. He was stunned—

What the hell?! What’s going on?!

Why does everyone want to—
