title: Chapter 6 — True and False
content:
Chapter 6 — True and False

Volume 10 · Chapter 6

Merlin felt things were getting a bit awkward. Was his back really that cool? Even a scheming bitch like Lucia could be captivated?

Uncle Karl and Hobbs looked at Merlin in surprise, feeling his reaction was a little strange.

They had just been talking about Lucia—how could he suddenly blurt that out? It was a bit too rude.

Uncle Karl curiously asked, "Brother Merlin, what's wrong with you?"

"........" Merlin coughed a few times, waving his hands to indicate he was fine, but his eyes couldn't help but glance at Lucia, who was busy nearby.

Uncle Karl didn't take it to heart. He calmly took a sip of beer and continued, "I don't know why, but my girl has suddenly taken an interest in the Great Swordsman Elgin. Just like all the other young girls these days, she doesn’t even know his real identity or what he looks like, yet she blindly follows the trend and falls for this mysterious guy. It’s really baffling...."

Merlin's expression turned complicated. In his mind, he screamed, *I don’t fucking understand either! Are these people’s brains broken?*

"Tsk tsk tsk, Karl, maybe you're just too old. Even though I'm about the same age as you, I still have a better grasp of the current situation..." Hobbs said with a chuckle, feeling that while he wasn’t as outstanding as Karl in other aspects, his mind was still sharp.

"Oh? You know the reason..." Uncle Karl asked in surprise, thinking Hobbs often had insightful observations.

"Mysterious men are attractive to women, especially younger girls. They always fantasize about what he’s like, and in their minds, he ends up perfectly matching their ideal image. Don’t you think that’s appealing?" Hobbs explained confidently.

Merlin calmly sipped his drink on the side, thinking, *Was wearing a mask a mistake?* But if he didn’t wear it, it would cause a whole other set of problems...

"That makes sense. Mysterious charm~" Uncle Karl crossed his arms and asked, "Then if I put on a mask, would Lucia like me a little more? Right now, I feel like my position as her father can’t even compare to this mysterious Great Swordsman Elgin..."

"Karl, forget it. At your age, it’s hard to attract young girls. Plus, Lucia has probably seen enough of you as her father—she’d recognize you even if you were turned to ash. What’s the point of a mask? There’s no mystery there."

Hobbs couldn’t help but speak the truth.

"Ugh!" Uncle Karl’s heart took a heavy blow. Did that mean he was failing as a father, unable to even catch his daughter’s attention?

"And right now, the Great Swordsman Elgin is all the rage in the empire! He’s so popular it’s ridiculous. Who would’ve thought a fugitive could be this well-loved? It’s enough to make a man jealous. This isn’t a fugitive—it’s a national savior..." Hobbs took a bitter sip of his drink, seemingly envious. "So, Karl, just give up. You can’t compare to the Great Swordsman Elgin. And Lucia’s at that age where her heart is fluttering—it’s completely normal. Just let it go..."

"Damn it!" Uncle Karl furiously slammed the table, startling both Merlin and Hobbs. "It’s just some mysterious guy! What am I lacking? Why does my precious daughter worship someone else instead of me? Am I, as her father, not tall, strong, and impressive enough?!"

"Emmmmmm..."

Merlin looked embarrassed, thinking, *So that’s what Karl’s really upset about. He really dotes on his daughter.*

"Karl, Lucia isn’t that cute little loli she used to be. How could she still be infatuated with you, her father? Even if you’re the strongest martial artist in the world, in her eyes, you’re just a sloppy old man."

Hobbs twisted his mouth, feeling Karl was out of touch with reality.

"I don’t accept that! Don’t let me catch the Great Swordsman Elgin, or I’ll punch him to prove to my girl that her old man is the most reliable one—not some guy who’s too cowardly to show his face!" Uncle Karl clenched his fists, fuming. "How dare he seduce my daughter? He’ll have to go through me first!"

Merlin covered his darkening face, thinking, *Who the hell seduced your daughter? This has nothing to do with me at all...*

"But the Great Swordsman Elgin’s strength is said to be unmatched. You really shouldn’t..." Hobbs felt Karl was being unreasonable. If he remembered correctly, anyone who had opposed the Great Swordsman Elgin hadn’t ended well.

"So what? This is about my standing in my daughter’s heart. I have to make her understand that in this world, only her father is dependable!" Uncle Karl clenched his fists, brimming with fighting spirit.

Hobbs fell silent, knowing Karl’s personality—once he made up his mind, not even ten oxen could pull him back. Merlin, meanwhile, looked a bit annoyed, thinking, *When you’re down on your luck, even the black pots fall from the sky.*

Just as everyone was busy, Alice entered the guild, seemingly intending to ask about last night’s drunken antics. When she saw Merlin, she immediately let out a "Hmph."

Merlin responded with a side-eye, not backing down.

Alice ignored Merlin and walked straight over, opening with a question: "Hobbs, did I get drunk last night? Did I do anything outrageous?"

"Outrageous things..." Hobbs rubbed his still-sore face, too embarrassed to say. "Nope~"

Alice saw Hobbs’ odd expression and turned to someone else. "Mr. Karl, what did I do last night?"

Uncle Karl glanced at Merlin, then awkwardly said, "You don’t even know what you did last night?"

"...I do."

Alice answered honestly. Uncle Karl looked at Hobbs, then whispered mysteriously, "Then we absolutely must not tell her."

Hobbs nodded repeatedly. "Right, we can’t tell her."

"? ? ?" Alice’s head was filled with question marks. *What on earth did I do last night?* She couldn’t get an answer, so she went to find Lucia.

"Lucia, what did I do last night?"

"You don’t know?!" Lucia blinked, then flashed a mysterious smile. "Then I absolutely won’t tell you~"

"...." Alice sighed, wondering why no one would tell her. *What shameful thing did I do last night?*

"What’s wrong? Are you in a bad mood because of last night’s drunken rampage?" Lucia set down her quill and asked.

"It’s not just that. That bastard Merlin spent all my savings on horse racing bets. It’s infuriating..." Alice pouted, sneaking a glance at Merlin.

"Eh?! That’s so reckless!" Lucia looked shocked.

"Right?! He doesn’t care about my feelings at all!" The more Alice thought about it, the angrier she got. Letting Merlin off the hook seemed too easy.

"You should learn to be more assertive, or you’ll never keep these jerks in line..." Lucia flicked her hair, looking smug. "Like all the guys who chase after me—they’re always trying to win my favor, but I never even give them a second glance. Hahaha~"

Alice’s expression turned complicated, thinking, *She’s definitely doing this to show off. No doubt about it. Why does she have to hurt my innocent heart like this?*

Just as everyone was busy, the guild’s large screen suddenly cut to an emergency live news broadcast. Bella held a microphone in front of the camera, dressed elegantly, and spoke slowly:

"Hello, everyone. We interrupt your regular programming for this breaking news.

"Just moments ago, the imperial government released an announcement. The rumored Great Swordsman Elgin has..."

"...been found."

title: Chapter 7 — Monthly Patron Update
content:
Chapter 7 — Monthly Patron Update

Volume 10 · Chapter 7

The news hit like a meteor crashing into the planet, instantly sending the entire guild into chaos.

After all, Elgin the Great Swordsman was the hottest topic right now, and any news about him was bound to draw attention.

And now, reporter Bella had just announced that she’d found Elgin the Great Swordsman *himself*?! ?

This revelation left everyone stunned. For so long, people had assumed Elgin the Great Swordsman was hiding his identity, never letting anyone know who he really was—yet now, he was suddenly appearing in person?

On top of that, everyone was curious about this mysterious wanderer, wondering who he really was. Such a shocking development—who could stay calm?

And with the royal Purple Thorn Knights failing to act, public dissatisfaction growing by the day, Elgin’s slaughter of the Ogre Worshippers and saving the empire from crisis had only made people think this mysterious man was the empire’s savior, with unprecedented attention focused on him.

“Huh?! ?” Merlin put down his drink and stared at the giant screen, his expression one of utter disbelief. *What the hell?* Elgin the Great Swordsman himself was found? But I’m right here! Who the hell are they talking about? !

Adventurers in the guild dropped everything and rushed to gather beneath the magic screen, hoping to get a clearer look.

“Is this real? Is that Elgin the Great Swordsman himself?! ?”

“Seems so, and it’s official news from the empire.”

“Does that mean Elgin’s been caught?! That’s insane!”

“No way, Elgin’s too strong—how could he be taken so easily?”

“Exactly. Maybe this mysterious strongman has already reached some kind of agreement with the royal family, which is why he’s appearing so openly.”

The crowd below buzzed with speculation, confused and eager for more details, sensing something big was about to happen.

“No way? This mysterious guy actually showed up? That’s…” Karl took a slow sip of beer, frowning. “Well, at least now we know what he looks like. If I get the chance, I’ll go meet this guy myself—I want to see what kind of trash my daughter’s been eyeing.”

Merlin’s forehead darkened with a mental *fuck off*, thinking, *Just stop looking, it’s me, this trash…*

“This is weird…” Hobbes stroked his beard, sensing something off.

“What’s weird, Hobbes?” Merlin asked, puzzled.

“Elgin the Great Swordsman’s been wanted for so long, right? Now he’s just appearing out of nowhere—doesn’t that seem… off?” Hobbes paused, then continued slowly. “Queen Elizabeth is known for her iron-fisted rule. She’d never back down, let alone lift the bounty. And Elgin’s too powerful to ever compromise. So why is he showing up in the capital now? Doesn’t that strike you as strange?”

“Strange? Too strange!” Merlin nodded rapidly, thinking, *I’m right here, and I don’t have cloning magic—how the hell did the empire find me? This is way too weird!*

“Exactly,” Hobbes said. “The empire finding Elgin the Great Swordsman like this? That’s impossible unless there’s some secret deal. Otherwise, the queen would drag him in and punish him without hesitation. This ‘peaceful’ meeting? No way. She’d never let it happen.”

“Makes sense…”

Merlin thought it was likely, but this so-called “Elgin the Great Swordsman” was clearly an imposter. *I’m the real deal—why is this happening?*

Who the hell has the balls to fake me?! Did my sword skills get rusty, or is this guy just *that* arrogant?

Merlin had never expected something so absurd to happen. He was actually curious—who the hell thought they could pull this off? First time someone’s dared to impersonate me.

“Elgin the Great Swordsman and the queen’s relationship is already tense enough, and now he’s doing a live broadcast? Something’s definitely up…” Hobbes summed it up, watching the screen. After finding Elgin, it seemed they were planning some kind of press conference.

Sure enough, Bella continued on-screen:

“According to official imperial news, Elgin the Great Swordsman himself will appear shortly, standing at the highest platform in the palace.

“Everyone will get their first look at this mysterious hero. Rumor has it he’ll remove his mask so all can see his true face!

“Stay tuned for this historic moment!”

The adventurers in the guild immediately started whispering among themselves, sensing something was *very* off.

Public appearances went against Elgin’s usual style—this lack of subtlety had everyone suspicious.

“Public appearance? And he’s *removing his mask*? Is this even Elgin the Great Swordsman?”

“Yeah, way too out of character. Someone who breaks their own rules like this must’ve gone through something serious.”

“Maybe Elgin’s already made peace with the queen and isn’t an enemy anymore.”

The adventurers debated wildly, each theory seeming plausible.

Merlin’s brows knitted together. Not only was someone faking him, but they were making sure *everyone* knew.

Did he *want* to be recognized? This guy’s acting like he’s trying too hard.

Merlin usually kept a low profile, but now some show-off imposter was making him look bad.

“Holy shit! He’s *removing his mask*? That’s taking it too far! If something goes wrong, Elgin might not even be able to survive in the empire—this is sealing his own fate!” Hobbes widened his eyes, though he’d expected a public appearance, he’d never guessed they’d go this far.

Now Hobbes was even more convinced Elgin had reconciled with the royal family—otherwise, why risk such a bold move?

Alice and Lucy, unable to contain their curiosity, rushed to the screen, clearly fascinated by Elgin’s first public appearance.

“Hmph!” Karl saw his daughter so excited and nearly exploded. He slammed his fist against his leg, his voice dripping with resentment.

“Damn it! It’s just Elgin the Great Swordsman—how dare he turn my girl into this?! I’ll settle with that bastard sooner or later!”

“Calm down, Karl…” Hobbes patted his shoulder, sensing this guy was about to storm off to the capital to confront Elgin.

“Tsk!” Merlin scoffed, watching Alice’s excited expression. Her eyes gleamed with anticipation—this fake Elgin was getting her all worked up.

*She’s this hyped over an imposter? Ugh, this is annoying…*

title: Chapter 8 — Monthly Patron Update
content:
Chapter 8 — Monthly Patron Update

Volume 10 · Chapter 8

From the screen one could see countless citizens gathered below the palace, a massive crowd, people packed together. They raised their heads, all wanting to see the true colors of the Elgin Great Swordsman. The highest platform at the top of the palace was the most prominent building, and there was also a magic circle to amplify sound. Speaking here, almost the entire capital could hear; it was used for the queen to address the nation and issue orders, an important place. Now they allowed the Elgin Great Swordsman to appear here, showing how much the royal family values him, and also hinting from the side that relations were easing. While everyone was waiting, the camera slowly moved upward—A woman dressed in pure white formal attire walked out, standing at the forefront, drawing everyone's gaze onto herself. Her dignified appearance, expensive jewelry, and the brilliantly shining crown on her head marked her as the empire's ruler, Elizabeth! Elizabeth opened her arms, facing the countless citizens, displaying her magnificent bearing; the whole empire could see her figure. "My fellow citizens, today I will announce a series of good news!" "I know you worship a certain hero and have heard countless astonishing rumors about him." "He possesses terrifying power, plus a mysterious identity unknown to anyone, and moreover glorious battle records of defeating countless Saint-tier powerhouses." "I think you have already guessed it, correct—he is the legendary Elgin Great Swordsman!" Immediately, enthusiastic cheers erupted below, mostly in support of this legendary figure. Many people saw the queen openly confronting the Elgin Great Swordsman issue, obviously indicating that things were easing. Elizabeth looked at the cheering crowd below, couldn't help but sneer, thinking, "A bunch of foolish citizens, you will never imagine that this El Great Swordsman is mine~" "This man was once wanted for inheriting several thousand royal ships and damaging imperial assets." "But today, I will tell you the good news....." "Effective immediately, I will revoke the wanted notice on the Elgin Great Swordsman and also bestow upon him his outstanding merits!" "Thank him for his continual contributions to the empire and his silent protection of the citizens." The citizens now in the capital all began to loudly cheer, many started praising the queen's wisdom. Originally, because the Purple Orchid Knight Squad had been ineffective lately, the people were somewhat dissatisfied. But now the direction of public opinion has shifted directly; everyone thinks the queen is a wise ruler who understands the people's sentiments. Adventurers in the guild watching the broadcast began to discuss, thinking the queen actually adopted a conciliatory policy—"Did I hear wrong? The iron-fisted queen actually voluntarily revoked the wanted notice on the Elgin Great Swordsman?" "Yes, simply unbelievable—is this still that iron-blooded ruler?" "The change is so fast; I still thought the queen would sooner or later repress those who support the Elgin Great Swordsman, but her attitude has softened." Most people found the queen's attitude strange; her initial kindness was puzzling. However, Alice thought it was great—since the queen personally lifted the wanted notice, her dream male god is now innocent, no need to hide; she can live openly in the sunshine, carrying out just deeds. Alice believed she would soon see what the Elgin Great Swordsman looks like in reality, finally no longer having to yearn for that magnificent silhouette alone. "Looks like the Elgin Great Swordsman is no longer a wanted criminal, so we can see his true face—what kind of handsome man would he be?" Lucia blushed with infatuation. Behind her, Uncle Carl rolled his eyes, thinking, "Why does my daughter always think about handsome men? Isn't ability more important when looking for a partner?" "Yeah, I'm also really looking forward to it." Alice happily agreed, her mood excited. "If he's super handsome, that would be perfect—a man with both power and looks is really hard to find; as long as his personality is acceptable, he's practically the perfect existence." Lucia seemed even more excited than Alice. "Mm-hmm." Alice nodded like a chick pecking at grain, fully agreeing with Lucia. Indeed, brainless fans are no different; sharing the same hobby, they get along well and have common topics. Uncle Carl behind her felt heartbroken, thinking Hobbes was right—his daughter has grown up, and the day she leaves him is not far away. "Wow, this is possible—directly revoking the wanted notice. If you say the queen didn't reach an agreement with the Elgin Great Swordsman, no ghost would believe it!" Hobbes gave a bland evaluation, catching a whiff of conspiracy. Merlin remained silent, wondering if he should pay attention to Alice for a moment, watching her excited state, feeling a bit stifled—"What medicine is this human queen selling in her gourd?" "And she even fabricated a fake Elgin Great Swordsman..." "What exactly does this woman want to do?" On site. Queen Elizabeth continued to... sense the crowd, slowly saying SF light novel "I know everyone is curious about Elgin's identity; now I will tell you—the true identity of the Elgin Great Swordsman is Luke Oberon, the eldest son of the Oberon ducal house!" Upon saying this, the crowd below immediately stirred a bit; everyone thought the Elgin Great Swordsman was a commoner, never expecting a noble—this was somewhat unexpected, not quite like the fantasy—Actually Elizabeth deliberately chose the duke's son to impersonate the Elgin Great Swordsman, after all, both are nobles, able to represent the interests of a class, completely dispelling the fantasies of these commoners! Elizabeth wanted them to know that protecting their mysterious hero is the noble ruling class, not some grassroots hero—don't overthink, just obey the rulers' commands. Even the adventurers in the guild exploded, unable to help discussing—"Oberon family? Is the Elgin Great Swordsman the son of a noble?" "Real or fake? It feels a bit subtle." "Yeah, but if one can easily defeat Saint-tier powerhouses, then it's about right." Alice and Lucia were also somewhat surprised, but they could accept it. "Oberon family? I never expected this man to still be a noble—isn't that great?" Lucia pondered how to win over the Elgin Great Swordsman, feeling this man was too perfect—strong power, handsome looks, and a noble—this is practically a textbook Mary Sue male protagonist! "Is he the eldest son of the Oberon family?" Alice felt a slight doubt; having seen the Elgin Great Swordsman before, his sloppy attire hardly resembled a noble, more like a beggar. "What is the Oberon family? Is it very powerful?" Merlin asked Hobbes in astonishment. "It's very powerful; Duke Oberon is the queen's right-hand man, controlling northern England, the family deals in weapons, and the kingdom's military weapons are all supplied by the Oberon family—you say, isn't that impressive?" Hobbes paused, then continued, "But the Elgin Great Swordsman just happens to be a member of the Oberon family, which is a bit strange..." Merlin furrowed his brow, kept his eyes on the screen, wondering how this farce would end—after all, his strength is there; if he can't convince the crowd, rumors will collapse on their own. Elizabeth slightly stepped aside and loudly said, "Please come forward, Elgin Great Swordsman, the mysterious hero everyone has been waiting for!" A man in a black robe, wearing a masquerade mask, with a katana at his waist walked out. He looked somewhat similar to Merlin's usual attire, except for—His build was a bit bulky, he looked rather fat—"Pfft!" Merlin spat out a mouthful of old blood, feeling his intellect insulted, thinking—Damn! What the hell is this?! How do I feel my intellect is being insulted?! Even if you find a fake Elgin Great Swordsman, at least get the build right!!! z(°O°I)

title: Chapter 9 — Performance
content:
Chapter 9 — Performance

Volume 10 · Chapter 9

This impostor posing as the great swordsman Elgin is similar to Merlin in every way: a black robe, an ordinary katana, and that silver mask.
Only his somewhat plump figure leaves people speechless, being several times larger than Merlin's.
His rotten belly sticks out forward—who would believe that the great swordsman Elgin is a nimble fatty!
Merlin puts on an expression of disbelief, his heart stirred with considerable shock—
"Damn! This can't be a mistake, can it?"
"This is the eldest son of the Ofrey family—how is he anything like me?!"
"Aside from the decorations, he bears no resemblance to me at all!"
"At least find someone handsome to impersonate me! Who the hell would believe this guy is the great swordsman Elgin?!"
"Merlin feels his body and mind have been insulted—not because someone is impersonating him, but because the impersonator isn't handsome enough!"
The impostor Elgin strides forward, approaches Queen Elizabeth, and waves at the crowd below like a celebrity.
The citizens of the capital below instantly became restless, boos rising and falling, all speaking words of distrust.
Because most people have already seen photos of the great swordsman Elgin, albeit not very clear, but they could still tell he had a good physique.
After waiting so long, we get someone somewhat overweight—who could accept believing he is the great swordsman Elgin?!
"I don't know what Queen Elizabeth is thinking—she's treating the populace like idiots to deceive them."
"Unless the people's eyes go blind, nobody would believe it."
"Moreover, the fake Elgin's appearance—who knows how many appearance-obsessed fangirls had their hearts shattered, faintly showing a shift from pink to black."
SF Mao Xiao said
"Get lost, get lost, get lost
I don't know if it's the prepared rhythm? The citizens below the royal palace start to heckle, demanding the fake Elgin get lost."
Obviously, most people find it hard to accept this reality, and the chaotic scene seems ready to erupt into a riot at any moment.
The fake Elgin shows no fear, standing firm on the spot; seeing his black robe fluttering, he actually has a bit of presence.
"Indeed, it turned out this way—Elizabeth muttered to herself, a bead of cold sweat sliding down her forehead, as if she had long known this would happen, yet she felt no remorse."
"In fact, Elizabeth's choice of the Ofrey family's eldest son as the fake Elgin was also a helpless move; it's not entirely her fault."
"When they began selecting candidates for the fake Elgin, some embarrassing interests emerged, making it impossible to choose arbitrarily."
"They needed to safeguard the royal family's interests while ensuring the nobility's ruling status, so the candidate choice became quite limited."
"Everyone knows Elgin's glory is immense; this plan amounts to stripping away honor, a cushy job."
"The Ofrey duke rushed to the palace overnight, pleading with Queen Elizabeth to let his only son serve as the fake Elgin."
"The Ofrey guild is already quite old; Luke is his only son, born late in life, so he is highly valued."
"Who wouldn't want their son to soar to great heights? The Ofrey duke is the same—he eagerly wants this opportunity to transfer Elgin's glory to his sole son, Luke."
"Seeing Luke's physique, Queen Elizabeth immediately found herself in a dilemma—she knew he was too fat, bearing no resemblance to Elgin's former image, but thinking of the Ofrey family's wealth and their status as the empire's armory, possessing over half of the empire's arms, she wavered."
"If this opportunity were given to the Ofrey family, it would obviously be a good thing, strengthening the bond between the royal family and the Ofrey family and consolidating rule."
"So Elizabeth steeled herself and gave this opportunity to the Ofrey family, making them the beneficiaries of Elgin's glory."
"The adventurers in the guild were also like an exploding pot, all feeling their IQ had dropped off."
"No way! This fatty is the great swordsman Elgin?!"
"I also think it's impossible—how could this happen?!"
"Elgin should have a normal build, right? From the newspaper photos before, you could see..."
"Everyone felt it was strange, as if the royal family was treating everyone like idiots, showing no respect at all."
"‘Wuwu~’ Lucia instantly showed a disgusted expression, feeling utterly disappointed: ‘How can the great swordsman Elgin be a fatty? This is far from what I imagined—is this really Elgin?’"
"‘Impossible, this must be fake?’ Alice furrowed her brows, unable to believe the stranger she saw on the screen."
"A few years ago I had seen the real Elgin; his build was somewhat similar to Merlin's, but he certainly wasn't this fat—did he gain weight over a year?"
"‘I’m the one being looked down upon by this noble little fatty? Why is my daughter’s eyesight so…’ Old Man Karl muttered silently, his heart hurting tenfold."
"Hobbs hurriedly turned back to Merlin and said, ‘I take back what I said before; with this conduct, I doubt I could ever turn grass into fans.’"
"‘Merlin feels awkward, thinking, what does this have to do with me? Speaking of which, looking down on fatties isn’t right either—there are also great potentials among them, right?’"
"The fake Elgin remains composed; even with a torrent of curses below, he stands unmoving, as if he hadn't heard anything."
"Elizabeth is somewhat unable to handle the situation; if this continues, the wisdom will only intensify."
"However, Elizabeth is no fool; she knows people will not believe this, so she has prepared a backup plan—she must let this farce of pointing at a deer and calling it a horse end perfectly."
"‘Please quiet down a bit; I know you have doubts about Elgin himself. Even when I learned the truth, I found it hard to sleep, but the fact is, he is Elgin!’’"
"Luke, posing as Elgin, stands tall like a soldier undergoing inspection, but his rotten belly just won't suck in."
"The crowd below began to shout insults, feeling that their imagined hero had been insulted, unable to accept reality."
"‘Alright, words without proof—I believe in seeing is believing. Next, Elgin will demonstrate his strength in a duel with my knights; then everyone can judge for themselves whether he is truly Elgin.’"
"After Elizabeth finished speaking, she gave a glance to those behind her, signaling to proceed as planned—to make Luke appear as a true powerhouse!"
"Immediately, two knights stepped out from behind, wearing exquisite silver armor trimmed with gold: the Fifth Thorn Knight Miliuss and the Tenth Thorn Knight Vinifred!"
"The two Thorn Knights appeared in the public's view, their faces shrouded in gloom and dissatisfaction—clearly they were not in a good mood."
"Elizabeth satisfiedly smiled and said to all the empire's subjects:"
"‘I think you all know the status of the Thorn Knights in the empire, and their strength is unparalleled.’"
"‘Then, moving on’"
"‘Elgin will display his strength before everyone, taking on two at once and defeating them!’"

title: Chapter 10 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 10 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 10 · Chapter 10

Queen Elizabeth’s words had just fallen, and the crowd fell silent at once, seemingly done with their cursing.

Elkyn the Great Swordmaster was about to put on a show of one versus two in front of ten thousand people—what a spectacle to watch!

After all, Elkyn’s legendary battle had been a single strike killing two pirate kings, creating an unprecedented frenzy.

If the fat man in front of them had equal strength, even if he couldn’t match the name, being called Elkyn the Great Swordmaster would at least have some credibility in terms of power!

And what did the onlookers love most? Of course, they loved a good show. Now that this man claiming to be Elkyn the Great Swordmaster himself was about to fight two Thorn Knights, what kind of spectacle could be better? There was no reason to miss it.

The crowd roared again, already eager to watch the show, and they glared at the man claiming to be Elkyn the Great Swordmaster, ready to drown him in spit if he lost.

Millius and Winifred’s faces grew even uglier, as if something had displeased them, as if they’d been suppressed.

The adventurers in the guild began murmuring, finding the situation suddenly interesting.

“Fighting two with one? And against two Thorn Knights at that?”

“If he really has that kind of strength, maybe he *is* Elkyn the Great Swordmaster.”

“Maybe he ate something and got this fat in no time.”

As everyone debated, many began to waver, thinking that if he could win, then Luke *might* actually be Elkyn the Great Swordmaster.

“Could it be that the eldest son of the Overre family—is he really Elkyn the Great Swordmaster?” Hobbs turned to Merlin, wanting to hear his opinion. “Merlin, what do you think?”

“Bullshit. If I were him, I’d go shit in my pants!” Merlin snapped back, thinking, *I’m the real Elkyn the Great Swordmaster—what’s this fraud good for?*

“Why are you so sure? If this guy can defeat the two Thorn Knights, that would actually make some sense,” Hobbs said awkwardly, though he was skeptical too—still, seeing was believing.

Merlin hesitated, realizing he couldn’t just claim to be the real Elkyn the Great Swordmaster. “I dunno~”

Onstage—

Elizabeth stepped aside, then spoke sternly. “Elkyn the Great Swordmaster, show us your strength.”

Luke patted his waist where his katana was sheathed and said seriously, “I don’t wish to harm these two knights. Give me a wooden sword.”

This statement sent shockwaves through the crowd. The onlookers’ mouths dropped open in disbelief.

Who would’ve thought Elkyn the Great Swordmaster would say something like that? Facing two of the empire’s strongest knights, he had the audacity to speak so arrogantly in their presence, dismissing them outright. And he didn’t even want to use real weapons—he wanted a wooden sword, clearly signaling he wouldn’t use his full strength and would instead strike the empire’s Thorn Knights with a careless attitude!

After a moment, the crowd erupted in enthusiastic cheers, their blood boiling over Elkyn’s bragging.

Even the guild hall fell into chaos—everyone had come to watch the show, but now it had turned into a full-blown performance!

“Damn! That flex was perfect. Karl raised his thumb silently, thinking the same as Merlin—both of them loved sparring with wooden swords.

“If he’s strong enough, I can accept him being fat,” Luciara said meaningfully beside him.

“What are you talking about?” Alice deadpanned, though she felt a little excited inside.

Merlin scoffed, embarrassed, thinking, *This guy’s flexing is on point—I’ll give him 82 out of 100, and the remaining 18 I’ll give him in the form of 666. Even if he’s a fake, his flex is pretty high.*

The two Thorn Knights across from them looked even more furious. If it weren’t for the queen’s orders, they would’ve beaten this duke’s son so badly his own father wouldn’t recognize him.

Under Queen Elizabeth’s pressure, even Millius and Winifred had no choice but to submit, forced to follow the queen’s script and lose to Luke on purpose—otherwise, they’d have no way to explain themselves to her.

But Millius and Winifred understood that this meant abandoning their dignity, willingly becoming pawns for Elizabeth’s interests.

Their ultimate loyalty was to Queen Elizabeth, and even as Thorn Knights, they had to obey orders.

Originally, Elizabeth had planned to have Mesfield come perform, but the first knight’s reputation was too strong, and he still had value to exploit.

So Elizabeth had to settle for Millius and Winifred instead.

“Are you sure you want to face my two knights with a wooden sword?” Elizabeth asked.

“Absolutely!” Luke nodded, striking a cold, aloof pose.

“Bring him a wooden sword.”

Elizabeth ordered a servant, her heart darkly amused as she watched her plan unfold smoothly.

She had already given her orders—Millius and Winifred would put on a show, losing to Luke on purpose.

This would highlight Luke’s strength, making it easier to convince everyone that he *was* Elkyn the Great Swordmaster.

*Hahaha*, that damned Elkyn the Great Swordmaster—who would’ve thought I’d find someone to replace him?

Elizabeth watched as Luke took the wooden sword, then spoke solemnly.

“Begin.”

The moment her words fell, the two Thorn Knights launched a brutal assault.

“Go! Finish him!” Millius snarled.

“Yeah!” Winifred grunted in response.

Millius drew his slender sword, golden Saint-tier battle energy surging from his body as his blade danced twice, like a Blade Dancer.

He stomped the ground with all his might, unleashing a vicious thrust straight for Luke’s throat—it looked terrifyingly powerful!

Winifred was more subdued, summoning flowing soil from thin air, wrapping it around his arms to form a massive drill.

Saint-tier magic fueled his attack as he charged toward Luke with overwhelming force!

The two Saint-tier knights’ forms intertwined, their presence crushing, as if they meant to bury Luke beneath their combined might.

“Pathetic!”

Luke’s wooden sword flickered—

The two Thorn Knights stiffened as if struck, collapsing backward before they even reached him, crashing to the ground in a heap.

They looked utterly humiliated, as if their combat ability had vanished instantly.

Elizabeth smirked in satisfaction, thinking, *Perfect. They played their parts well. Now everyone should believe that Elkyn the Great Swordmaster is just a fat man. If the real Elkyn the Great Swordmaster isn’t satisfied, let him show up here in person. Hahaha~*

The onlookers were stunned, their eyes wide as if they’d just woken from a dream.

What? Those were Thorn Knights—the empire’s elite fighters!

And they’d been effortlessly defeated by this fat swordmaster with a single swing of his wooden sword?!

Could it be that the legendary Elkyn the Great Swordmaster was now just a fat man?

title: Chapter 11 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 11 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 10 · Chapter 11

“No way! One hit! One strike and he knocked out two Thorned Knights?!”

“He was even using a wooden sword—clearly, he wasn’t showing his true strength!”

“So strong! This guy must be the legendary Elgin Great Swordsman—no doubt about it!”

The adventurers started buzzing excitedly, stunned by what they’d just witnessed.

The Thorned Knights, representing the empire’s strongest warriors, had been defeated in a single strike by this fat swordsman. And that strike hadn’t even looked powerful—just a casual swing.

Yet the fight was over. The two Thorned Knights were in disarray, barely able to lift their heads.

How strong was this fat swordsman? He must be the legendary Great Swordsman.

In the face of absolute strength, there was no choice but to believe this was the real Elgin Great Swordsman.

But the onlookers couldn’t see the truth: Luke’s strength was only that of a low-tier warrior, a joke compared to the Thorned Knights.

That lackluster strike wasn’t Luke holding back—it was just his actual strength. No amount of effort would change that.

Still, Luke had a good father. Duke Overre was the queen’s favorite, so this impersonation gig wouldn’t have fallen to anyone else.

[OP SE4’s Xiao Zhi]

“Hmm~” Uncle Karl stroked his beard, muttering, “This guy’s got some real skill, even if he’s a bit chubby.”

“Holy hell!” Hobbes turned back, stunned, and told Merlin, “It’s really the Elgin Great Swordsman! His disguise and fighting style match perfectly!”

“Mm.” Merlin replied coolly, almost smirking.

Since Merlin had fought these two Thorned Knights before, he knew their strength wasn’t weak at all. But they’d been defeated in a single strike by this fat swordsman—clearly, he’d been holding back.

Though Merlin could see through it, the onlookers couldn’t. To them, Luke was just *so* strong, unstoppable!

Look at Alice and Lucy, the two little fans up front, their eyes sparkling with adoration.

Merlin’s forehead veins throbbed. Seeing Alice like this made him furious. If she were staring at the *real* swordsman, he wouldn’t mind. But this Luke was a fake, and Alice was acting like a lovestruck fool—Merlin was *not* happy about that.

Merlin usually went out flirting, and Alice would be furious with green-eyed jealousy. Now, finally, he had a reason to wear the green hat himself.

As the saying goes: *If you play in the mud, you’ll get dirty.* The heavens don’t spare anyone.

---

In the capital’s square, the crowd below the walls was stunned, then erupted in cheers and exhausted shouts of praise.

Seeing Luke effortlessly defeat two Thorned Knights, everyone was convinced he was the real Elgin Great Swordsman.

Most people realized looks could be deceiving—maybe the Great Swordsman had gone through some trouble recently, which was why he’d suddenly gotten fat.

Chris stood on the platform, striking an icy, aloof pose, and the crowd below cheered even louder, as if a hero had descended upon the capital.

Milius and Winifred on the ground slowly stood up—they hadn’t been hurt at all, just part of the plan.

“This bastard,” Milius growled, his eyes smoldering. “If he weren’t the duke’s son, I’d have cut him down with one strike already. Losing to a low-tier warrior like that—it’s an insult!”

“Calm down, Milius,” Winifred said seriously, though her own eyes flickered with frustration. “This is all by the queen’s order. We just have to go along with it.”

Milius sighed. “If the real Elgin Great Swordsman were this weak, it’d be fine. But having some fake with no real strength strutting around like this—it’s unbearable.” His expression darkened. “I’d love to expose Luke’s true face in front of everyone.”

“Save it,” Winifred said, suppressing her own anger. “This is for the empire’s sake.”

“Don’t you think the queen’s getting too ruthless?” Milius couldn’t hold back. “She’s using every dirty trick, even ignoring our honor. It feels like she’s walking down the wrong path.”

“We shouldn’t criticize the queen’s actions,” Winifred said wearily.

Milius sighed again. Arguing with Winifred’s stubbornness was pointless.

---

Luke looked down at the sea of poor citizens below and explained his sudden weight gain. “Before, my physique was actually pretty good. But recently, I was cursed by a villain’s evil magic, and overnight, I gained a lot of weight. No matter how my body changes, I’m still that mysterious hero—always protecting you in the shadows.”

The crowd erupted in applause. Now that they knew Luke was the Elgin Great Swordsman, whatever he said seemed right, and his words rang with passion and conviction.

These lines were clearly scripted by Queen Elizabeth to cover up the truth, and they worked well.

Luke then ripped off his mask, revealing his true face—short brown hair, a chubby face covered in freckles, the kind of look you’d expect from a spoiled landlord’s son.

“From today on, I won’t hide behind a mask anymore. I’ll stand in the sunlight and protect the entire empire!”

The cheers below were deafening, as if today were a day worth remembering—a legendary hero finally recognized by the empire.

Elizabeth thought the performance was going well. The gains today far exceeded her expectations.

If the real Elgin Great Swordsman never showed up, all his glory would be hers. Even if he did appear, he’d face a combined assault from multiple Thorned Knights and the Purple Gold Adventurers.

Last night, Elizabeth had already written a personal letter to Gregory, asking him to assist her plan in his own name.

She cleared her throat, using an amplification magic array to project her voice, and announced the final news:

“From today, Elgin Great Swordsman Luke Overre will join the royal guard’s Thorned Rose Knights, becoming an honorable knight sworn to protect the empire.

“Starting tomorrow, a procession will be organized to travel across the empire.

“I will let every citizen witness the glory of this hero!”

---

title: Chapter 12 — Emotion
content:
Chapter 12 — Emotion

Volume 10 · Chapter 12

At the entrance to the palace's high platform.

Mestfield wore exquisite armor, her crimson cape swaying gently. The golden wisteria embroidery on it rippled like a banner in the wind.

She stared at the man pretending to be Elgin Great Swordsman Luke, her face completely expressionless.

Mestfield was fully aware of the Queen’s plan—she had even participated in it herself. Even if Queen Elizabeth’s methods were shortsighted and foolish, she had no choice but to assist with all her strength.

Seeing Milieus and Winifred endure humiliation and deliberately lose had left her feeling uneasy. As a knight herself, witnessing two comrades forced by the Queen to throw a match against Luke naturally put her in a foul mood.

Many knights valued honor above life itself, and Elizabeth’s actions were nothing short of a brutal trampling of knightly dignity.

When Mestfield saw the Queen’s smug smile, a wave of helplessness surged within her. She silently gripped the hilt of her sword.

Why?

Why had Elizabeth become like this?

Wasn’t this just like her sister, resorting to underhanded tactics?

None of the promises she had made were kept. Instead, the ideal kingdom she once dreamed of was slipping further and further away.

Mestfield’s expression darkened, her eyes flickering with dissatisfaction, even a hint of resentment.

Milieus and Winifred approached with gloomy faces, clearly in the worst of moods. They stopped in front of Mestfield, as if they had something to say.

“You’re the one the Queen trusts the most, aren’t you? So why didn’t you stop her from doing something so stupid?” Milieus immediately questioned her.

“Mestfield—” Winifred furrowed her brows, as if trying to stop him from saying too much.

“We are merely knights. We have no right to interfere with Her Majesty’s decisions.” Mestfield’s response was official, devoid of personal emotion, purely professional.

“Easy for you to say,” Milieus scoffed, pausing before continuing with a sarcastic tone, “The mighty First Knight.”

Mestfield knitted her delicate brows, saying nothing, but shot Milieus a fiery glare.

Milieus turned away and walked off, muttering coldly, “A trash like Luke? I could crush him with one finger. Reincarnation really is an art.”

Winifred said nothing either, leaving in silence without looking back.

“Tch!” Mestfield bared her teeth in frustration, slamming her fist into the wall—

Damn it!

One fake Elgin Great Swordsman had thrown the empire into such chaos!

Inside the Adventurers Guild.

Most adventurers had come to believe this was the real Elgin Great Swordsman. The strikingly similar attire and the inexplicable, overwhelming strength were more than convincing.

His obese physique could be explained by some unorthodox magic—who knew what kind of curse magic the Elgin Great Swordsman had fallen under?

As for his identity? No one had ever known the true identity of the Elgin Great Swordsman to begin with. The rumor that he was a commoner was just hearsay.

A small minority still harbored doubts, but their numbers were too few to sway the majority.

Finally, Queen Elizabeth’s announcement that the Elgin Great Swordsman would be joining the Wisteria Knights took many by surprise. Still, everyone was curious about the Great Swordsman, and the news of his upcoming tour through the regions had piqued their interest.

“A tour through the regions? Maybe I’ll get a chance to spar with him.” Uncle Karl stroked his beard, his combative nature impossible to hide.

“Hey, hey, hey, cut it out, Karl. You’re always stirring up trouble,” Hobbes said, a bead of sweat rolling down his forehead.

“What’s there to be afraid of? As a man, I should have some spirit in me. Am I supposed to be scared just because the Elgin Great Swordsman is famous? Impossible!” Uncle Karl downed his beer in one gulp and left with a flourish.

“This family really doesn’t think about the consequences,” Hobbes sighed, turning back to Merlin. “See? The Elgin Great Swordsman has clearly reached some kind of reconciliation with the royal family. He’s even been recruited into the Wisteria Knights.”

“Mmm.” Merlin gave a perfunctory response, thinking to himself that it made perfect sense for his impostor to be accepted into the Wisteria Knights. It was just the royal family’s way of telling everyone that the Elgin Great Swordsman belonged to them—that all along, the royal family had been silently protecting the people.

But then that fake, Luke, had claimed he was cursed to become fat, which made Merlin want to laugh and cry. He was immune to magic, for heaven’s sake—what kind of curse could affect him?

Of course, almost no one knew about his magic immunity. Apart from the few who had seen it with their own eyes, no one would suspect the Elgin Great Swordsman was a fraud based on that flaw.

Seeing Merlin’s lack of interest, Hobbes tried to probe further. “You should look at Alice and Lucia. Those two little fangirls look so excited.”

Merlin barely lifted his eyelids and saw Alice and Lucia chatting animatedly. It was obvious they were talking about the fake Elgin Great Swordsman.

Merlin felt a twinge of annoyance. Here he was, the real deal, right in front of Alice, yet she couldn’t even see it. Instead, she was gushing over some impostor. Where was the justice in that? It was utterly baffling.

Watching Alice’s delighted expression, Merlin felt a pang of bitterness. Did that stupid woman have a problem with her eyes? How did that fraud look anything like him? It was downright unpleasant.

Merlin didn’t really care about the empty title of Elgin Great Swordsman, but having someone impersonate him still rubbed him the wrong way.

To Merlin, a title was just a label for a person’s identity—nothing more, nothing less. But Alice seemed to be all about labels, and now she was falling for a fake. It left Merlin feeling helpless.

Hobbes, seeing Merlin still unresponsive, urgently said, “Merlin, can you at least show some concern? Your wife is about to have her soul stolen by the Elgin Great Swordsman. That’s not a good omen, you know!”

“What’s there to be afraid of? Do I care about Alice? Ridiculous.” Merlin smirked, his tone dismissive. “Who she likes is none of my business. I’m not the kind of man who lets Alice lead me around by the nose.”

“Are you just giving up?” Hobbes looked awkward, sensing an air of despair radiating from Merlin.

Merlin figured he shouldn’t meddle. He and Alice weren’t really married, so why bother with her business? Besides, who Alice liked was her own choice. Merlin wasn’t stupid enough to start acting like a husband just because they’d lived together for a few days.

Merlin thought this was the kind of embarrassing thought only someone like Sis would have.

“Alright, I get it. After all, there’s too big of a gap between your status and Alice’s right now. It’s normal to feel the pressure,” Hobbes patted Merlin’s shoulder and continued, “Clearly, Alice has moved past the ‘looks’ phase and become more practical. It’s only natural for her to find a better man. Welcome back to the Single’s Club.”

“Tsk.” Merlin clicked his tongue, thinking, *What does that impostor have that compares to me?* It felt like everyone was counting him out.

The table suddenly shook. Jenna had snuck into the guild and slowly poked her small head out from under the table.

Her eyes were filled with infatuation as she looked at Merlin, her heart sparkling pink.

“Merlin.”

“Kuhahaha~”

title: Chapter 13 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 13 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 10 · Chapter 13

Merlin’s body suddenly tensed, a chill creeping up his spine as he nearly dropped his wine glass.

Jenna’s gaze fixed on him like she wanted to devour him whole, her saliva visibly pooling and retreating in thick, slurping gulps.

Merlin’s face darkened. *Could this bitch get any more disgusting?* She’d been lurking from afar before, but today she had the nerve to creep closer—didn’t she fear his fists? Oh right, the harder he hit her, the more she’d enjoy it.

“Merlin-sama,” Jenna purred, her eyes locked onto him, a strange laugh bubbling up from her throat. “Koo-hey-hey~”

“Oh? Isn’t this our love expert Jenna?” Hobbes drawled, not taking the naive girl seriously at all.

Hobbes had met Arnold’s sister Jenna before—though they didn’t chat much, they’d crossed paths a few times. So he immediately adopted a teasing tone, their friendship with Arnold making it natural.

“It’s me. You got a problem?” Jenna emerged from under the table, hands on her hips, striking a haughty pose.

“No, no,” Hobbes waved awkwardly. “I was just wondering why your brother didn’t come today?”

“Pfft!” Jenna scoffed, twisting her lips in obvious disdain. “Don’t even mention that useless piece of trash! My brother got slapped by Miss Alice the other day and’s been moping ever since. With me right here giving him brilliant advice, he still can’t even handle a commoner girl—what a disgrace to the Austin family! How could I have such a worthless older brother?!”

Merlin’s face darkened further. *If Arnold didn’t have this pig of a sister dragging him down, his success rate might’ve been higher.* It was her constant meddling that kept him stumbling, making Alice despise him more by the day. Calling her own brother useless—where did this idiot get her confidence?

Merlin saw his own reflection in Arnold. Back in the day, his own sister used to treat him like a stay-at-home with muscles but no brains.

Hobbes broke out in cold sweat, stammering, “If it weren’t for you constantly giving him terrible advice, Arnold wouldn’t keep failing with Alice.”

“What did you say?!” Jenna’s arms crossed over her chest. “You’re questioning *my* love master status?!”

Hobbes forced a stiff smile. *Love master my ass.* Just because she’d read a few shoujo novels didn’t mean she’d ever experienced real passion.

Though Hobbes internally roasted her, his face remained polite and embarrassed.

“I’d never dare question the noble Miss Jenna,” he said smoothly. “Your schemes for Arnold are all *fantastic*—keep up the great work!”

Merlin shot Hobbes a look. *This guy’s usually tight with Arnold, so why push him into the fire now?* Typical surface-level brotherhood.

“Of course I’ll keep advising my brother,” Jenna simpered, her gaze locking onto Merlin with a doe-eyed grin. “So he can win over Miss Alice… and then *I* can reasonably be with Merlin-sama.” *Koo-hey-hey~*

Merlin’s brows knit. He almost let loose a curse, but remembered Jenna’s masochistic tendencies and bit it back.

Hobbes perked up. *Something’s up here.* He nudged Merlin with his elbow, whispering, “When did you start hooking up with Arnold’s sister? Impressive—even a count’s daughter’s into you.”

Merlin rolled his eyes. “You’re talking nonsense. She’s the one who keeps throwing herself at me—I’ve done nothing.”

Hobbes narrowed his eyes, sizing Merlin up. “I hate this face-based society. Why do you always attract decent women? It’s unnatural.”

Merlin smirked internally. *If Hobbes slapped Jenna seven times, she’d probably see him as a godlike hunk—but she’s a masochist, so who’s gonna reason with her?*

“Uh… uh~” Jenna blushed, hands clasped demurely beneath her. “Merlin-sama… do you have time tonight? For a candlelit dinner… together?”

Merlin’s expression darkened. *Candlelit dinner?* His mind flashed to something far less romantic—dripping wax, whips, the kind of “romance” this noblewoman had in mind.

Hobbes nearly sprayed beer. He yanked Merlin aside, hissing, “Dude, you’re an idiot! You *have* to say yes—Jenna’s a count’s daughter! You’re basically hitting the jackpot!”

“Sorry, but all I feel is disgust,” Merlin deadpanned. *A woman who drools over me like that? No thanks.*

“Right now, the gap between you and Alice is huge,” Hobbes said, glancing at Jenna. “Look at Alice—she’s about to kick you to the curb and find someone new. You need to secure a backup plan. And Jenna? She’s a count’s daughter. If you hook up with her, you’ll marry into nobility—no more worrying about food or clothes for life. A sweet deal, why reject it?”

Merlin sucked in a breath. *“You’re basically telling me to be a kept man.”*

“Pfft, too crude,” Hobbes smirked, raising an eyebrow. “I call it *maximizing one’s natural talents.*” He leaned in conspiratorially. “Between you and me, if I were twenty years younger, this opportunity would’ve been *mine*.”

“Get lost,” Merlin shoved Hobbes away. *This guy’s mind is filthier than a sewer.*

“So, Merlin-sama?” Jenna purred, eyes gleaming with expectation.

“No,” Merlin replied coldly. “I heard you’re the leader of the Great Swordmaster Fan Club, right? He’s touring soon—when he hits Rexam, why not take him to a candlelit dinner instead?”

Jenna scoffed, lips curling. *“What, Elgin the Great Swordmaster? That fat lump? Not even a fraction as handsome as Merlin-sama.”*

*(Four resounding slaps.)*

title: Chapter 14 — Hatred
content:
Chapter 14 — Hatred

Volume 10 · Chapter 14

“Compared to that dead fat guy, the great swordmaster Elgin, I think Merlin’s domineering aura is way more attractive.”

Jenna, this little fangirl, didn’t even try to hide it and blurted it out, making Merlin’s face turn red.

Merlin wondered if he really had such a domineering aura. Why couldn’t he feel it at all?

Maybe Jenna’s imagination was just too rich—she saw domineering vibes everywhere, like she was suffering from delusional parasitosis.

The more Hobbs looked at Jenna, the weirder she seemed. He quickly pulled Merlin aside and whispered in a low voice, “Merlin, aren’t you a little *too* strong? How did you even win over the count’s daughter? She’s completely smitten, and I just don’t get it.”

“Get lost! What nonsense are you talking about?” Merlin frowned, not wanting to hear it.

“You’re basically Arnold’s *nemesis*—you stole his love interest, and now you’re even eyeing his sister Jenna. That’s just ruthless, cutting off all ties. No doubt about it, you’re *strong*,” Hobbs said, giving Merlin a thumbs-up. He thought Merlin was brutal for taking Alice and now trying to charm Arnold’s sister Jenna.

“Tsk!” Merlin pushed Hobbs away, thinking, *What does it have to do with me?* It was like he was deliberately provoking Arnold.

“Merlin, come on… let’s have dinner together. It won’t take up much of your time,” Jenna said, suddenly leaning closer to Merlin, trying to get closer.

“Stay away from me. Don’t come near me,” Merlin panicked, clearly not knowing how to handle Jenna’s clingy behavior.

So, without thinking, Merlin kicked Jenna’s chair, sending her sprawling onto the cold ground, her butt making an intimate contact with the floor.

“Ow!” Jenna yelped, her expression twisting into pain.

Merlin’s eyebrows twitched. He swore he hadn’t done it on purpose—it was just an accident. But now he’d accidentally made things worse!

Hobbs saw Merlin dare to bully the count’s daughter and was stunned. In Rextham, who knew Jenna had a terrible temper and loved throwing her rich-girl tantrums? Now that she’d been humiliated by Merlin, she’d definitely find a way to get revenge.

“Merlin, you’re doomed. You messed with Jenna—you won’t be able to stay in Rextham.”

“Y-you—” Jenna sat on the ground, glaring at Merlin, unable to speak.

Then her face flushed crimson, and she covered her cheeks shyly, stammering, “You… you *bullied* me again… so domineering… so *manly*… it’s *so* attractive…”

Hobbs nearly dropped his beer in shock.

Merlin shrugged at Hobbs, helpless about running into a masochist. He had no idea how to handle it either.

Hobbs calmly took a sip of his beer, sighing slightly, “I hate this society that judges people so much by their looks.”

The Elgin Great Swordmaster incident had finally come to an end.

Adventurers had been gossiping privately about when the legendary hero would parade through Rextham.

Alice and Lucia at the counter naturally started chatting too. As fans of the great swordmaster, they had plenty to talk about.

“Elgin the Great Swordmaster looks pretty good, I guess,” Lucia said, pausing. “Even if he’s a little fat, maybe he’ll get back to the physique in those photos.”

“I *definitely* remember you saying you’d *never* like fat men—like a boar in heat,” Alice deadpanned.

“Did I say that?” Lucia narrowed her eyes, as if she’d forgotten already.

“You did. *Absolutely*,” Alice nodded, thinking Lucia’s mood swings were ridiculous.

“Oh~” Lucia waved her hand, laughing. “It’s just a minor flaw. Even if Elgin’s a little fat, it doesn’t hide his other good qualities. Maybe he’ll even get back to the physique in those photos. Plus, he’s the only son of the Duke of Overley—wealth and prestige go hand in hand. A man like that is *rare*.”

Alice stayed silent, thinking Lucia wasn’t actually into Elgin—she was just after his money and status.

“A man like Elgin the Great Swordmaster must have *so* many girls fawning over him,” Lucia sighed. “Just thinking about it gives me pressure.”

“Yeah, lots of girls like him,” Alice said, frowning slightly. “But… there’s something *off* about him.”

“What’s off?” Lucia asked, confused. She thought Alice had always admired Elgin, so why was she acting so cold?

“I saw Elgin a year ago. Even if I didn’t recognize his face, I could feel the long-standing arrogance of someone used to high status—like he had no interest in anything. How to put it… if Luke *was* Elgin, he’d still feel a little… *ordinary*. There’s just something *off* about his aura.”

“Ordinary?!” Lucia rolled her eyes. “Your standards are *way* too high. He defeated two Thorn Knights in one go—that’s power on par with Mesfield! And he didn’t even use his full strength—he was just sparring with a wooden sword! Plus, he’s the heir to the Overley family, the most powerful in the empire. Even the queen gives them respect.”

Alice was speechless. She’d only said it felt *off*—she never claimed Luke *wasn’t* Elgin. Why was Lucia so obsessed?

“Anyway, I was just joking. Don’t take it seriously.”

“Aren’t you also a huge fan of Elgin? Now that you know the truth, aren’t you happy?” Lucia asked, surprised.

Alice hesitated, then said awkwardly, “Of course I’m happy. I *do* like Elgin.”

Alice just didn’t want to admit it too openly. She *did* feel something was wrong, but now that she thought about it, Luke *did* look like the real Elgin.

But she also had feelings for Merlin—she’d already compared him to Elgin in her mind more than once.

If you ignored Merlin’s flaws and his Demon Lord identity, he was *exactly* the Elgin she’d imagined.

But now this fake Luke was messing with everything, making her confused. Who was she *really* supposed to like?

Merlin *was* Elgin, but she refused to believe it.

Now that the real Elgin had been revealed, Alice felt a little disappointed.

This conflicting mess was torturing her, making her unable to decide.

“If you keep talking like that, Merlin will cry himself to death in the bathroom,” Lucia said, exasperated, studying Alice.

“Huh?! Why?” Alice blinked, confused.

“Aren’t you with Merlin? But you’re secretly into someone else—how could that *not* make him uncomfortable?” Lucia smirked, like she knew Alice was a hypocrite who never admitted the truth.

Alice stammered, then remembered Merlin had spent all her savings. “I don’t care what *he* thinks! We’re not even *really* married—who I like is my own business. Stop treating us like a real couple, okay?”

“Really? But every time Merlin gets close to another girl, you get *so* jealous. Isn’t that proof you like him?”

Lucia laughed harder, thinking Alice was just a hypocrite who never admitted her feelings.

“I *don’t* mean that!” Alice’s voice lost all confidence, like she was refusing to admit it.

“Alice, I think you’re confusing *liking* and *admiring*,” Lucia frowned, thinking Alice was just confused.

“What’s the difference?” Alice asked, her romantic experience nowhere near Lucia’s.

“Big difference,” Lucia said seriously. “Liking someone means you want to be with them *forever*, see them every day. Admiring someone just means you respect their talent—it’s *completely* different.”

Alice stayed silent, her brows knitting together.

*Do I just admire Elgin the Great Swordmaster?*

*Then who do I—*

*Is it Merlin?*

---

Deep in the night, at the highest peak of the Kesiri Mountains.

The place was in ruins, with faint traces of a broken spell formation.

The stars shone brightly, and the moonlight spilled down like silver.

This was where the Rakshasa Cult had been destroyed not long ago—now lifeless and desolate.

At the peak, the last survivor of the Rakshasa Cult, Grace, stood in a purple robe.

Her fiery red hair danced in the wind, untouched by the mountain breeze.

She held a white, skull-shaped staff, her eye sockets glowing with eerie red light, like a ghost had taken residence inside.

Since Grace had been out on an assassination mission, she hadn’t been with Swinburn when the attack happened, so she’d escaped.

If she’d been there during the crusade against the Rakshasa Cult, she’d probably be dead too.

The last message Grace had received from Swinburn was to meet him here. But she hadn’t expected her comrades to all be dead.

Even her lover, Swinburn, had died here. She could only collect his body, feeling the cold.

Grace held a crumpled cigarette in her hand, staring at the blackened, gnawed-on corpse in front of her.

She knew Swinburn’s habits well—she could tell instantly that this was his body.

Grace’s tears flowed like a fountain, sliding down her cheeks and dripping into the damp earth.

Her sorrowful expression was heartbreaking, her features twisted as she bit her lip, unable to speak.

Grace clenched her cigarette tightly, her hatred plain on her face.

“Who did this?!”

“Who *killed* Swinburn?!”

“I’ll make that killer suffer the most agonizing death!”

title: Chapter 15 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 15 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 10 · Chapter 15

In the grand hall of the royal palace, Queen Elizabeth sat upon her lofty throne.

Behind her, several maids stood respectfully to the side, their hands clutching the hem of her gown. Below, Luke knelt on one knee, pretending to be the legendary Elgin Blade Lord, his head bowed in deference.

As members of the imperial ruling class, Queen Elizabeth and the House of Aurelius shared many common interests, and now they were both guarding the secret of the Blade Lord.

However, Luke represented the family’s interests even more. If he took control of the Elgin Blade Lord’s position, the prestige of the Aurelius family within the empire would soar like the midday sun!

“Luke, how does it feel to become the Elgin Blade Lord now?” Queen Elizabeth asked from her elevated position.

“It’s fine. The feeling of being worshipped by countless people—it’s truly something to aspire to,” Luke replied, lifting his head slightly without hesitation.

Queen Elizabeth narrowed her eyes, finding Luke’s answer still unsatisfactory.

“No…” Luke paused, forcing a smile onto his chubby face. “I know all of this is a gift from Your Majesty. I will remember this favor forever. If Your Majesty has any needs, the Aurelius family will do everything in your service—cross fire and water, die a thousand deaths without hesitation!”

“Hah…” Queen Elizabeth let out a light laugh, pleased with Luke’s response. “Not bad, not bad. You truly are the only son of the Aurelius family. Your wisdom in reading the times is no weaker than your father’s. I’ve always been clear about rewards and punishments—honest people will be rewarded well, but those who are restless will never see the light of dawn. Do you understand my meaning?”

“I understand, Your Majesty. Please rest assured,” Luke replied respectfully, knowing the queen’s warning was about fearing he might betray her or rebel after gaining the Elgin Blade Lord’s prestige.

“I hear the Aurelius family has been expanding its private army recently, and the smoke from the foundries has already drifted into the capital…” Queen Elizabeth narrowed her eyes, scrutinizing Luke below. “What do you intend to do? Do you really want to show me your muscles?”

Luke, kneeling below, was startled, his body trembling. He was clearly taken aback.

By all rights, expanding a private army was a secret—how did the queen know?

It seemed the queen’s spies were everywhere, even infiltrating the Aurelius family!

In truth, the Aurelius family was indeed plotting in secret, aiming to overthrow the entire empire. Otherwise, they wouldn’t be so eager to expand their military.

Currently, the Aurelius family’s combat strength was formidable, capable of directly challenging the royal bloodline. How could they possibly be content to remain subordinate?

Everyone seeks to leave a bold mark in history, and the aging Duke Aurelius is no exception.

If the queen’s rule ever wavers, the Aurelius family will bare its fangs and become the empire’s new rulers.

Luke quickly regained his composure, trying to convince Queen Elizabeth of his family’s loyalty and clear their name.

“Your Majesty, please do not doubt our family’s loyalty. We are expanding our private army solely to defend against external invasions. If we didn’t lack manpower, we absolutely wouldn’t do this.”

Though Queen Elizabeth spoke diplomatically, Luke easily understood her meaning—it was a thinly veiled threat.

“This is a time of peace. Where are these external invaders coming from? Do you take me for a child?”

Luke hesitated for a moment before replying patiently. “Our family’s lands lie in northern England, where dense forests hide countless demons. Recently, many beasts have burst from the woods, attacking villages. If we don’t expand our private army, we may struggle to repel their invasions. I hope Your Majesty understands.”

“Repel demonic invasions?” Queen Elizabeth smirked. “According to imperial law, a duke’s private army cannot exceed thirty thousand. If it does, they will face punishment, and I will consider your family a threat to the empire. I assume you know this rule?”

Luke nodded, sensing this was a direct threat.

“I entrusted you with the task of impersonating the Elgin Blade Lord and bestowed his honor upon your family. These benefits won’t come for free,” Queen Elizabeth said meaningfully.

“I understand. I will explain Your Majesty’s intentions to my father and try to reduce our military strength to ease Your Majesty’s concerns,” Luke replied, fully grasping the queen’s warning.

“Good. As long as the Aurelius family remains obedient, your descendants will receive royal favor for generations,” Queen Elizabeth paused before shifting to a threatening tone. “But if you harbor any ill intentions, I will send my army to crush your family without hesitation. Our royal bloodline has stood on this land for over four hundred years, possessing secrets you can never match.”

Luke chose silence, sweat beading on his forehead.

Queen Elizabeth had chosen the Aurelius family as a beneficiary purely to consolidate her position.

Since she intended to weaken the Aurelius family, to prevent them from acting recklessly, she had to offer some concessions.

This was Queen Elizabeth’s policy of appeasement—suppressing opponents without direct conflict. Now, the Aurelius family had been struck hard.

“Starting tomorrow, you will travel as the Elgin Blade Lord to various regions for a procession. I will arrange many people to protect you in secret, including my Thorn Knights and a purple-gold ranked adventurer,” Queen Elizabeth said casually.

“A purple-gold adventurer?!” Luke’s eyes widened. Such a high-ranked adventurer was mysterious—even bringing one along was impressive. The royal family truly had deep resources.

“Is it…?” Luke began.

“Yes, it’s the old guildmaster of the capital. He has deep ties with our royal family and will protect you in secret,” Queen Elizabeth replied with a hint of cunning.

Luke grew concerned, hesitating. “What if the real Elgin Blade Lord comes looking for me?”

“And what if he does? With so many people protecting you, what do you have to fear?” Queen Elizabeth asked in confusion.

“I worry… the real Elgin Blade Lord’s power is too strong…” Luke lowered his voice, sounding uncertain.

“Don’t worry. Even if my knights fail, I know a little about Gregory’s strength. A four-hundred-year-old ancient monster—do you really think he’d lose to the Elgin Blade Lord? Go boldly. You are the true Elgin Blade Lord,” Queen Elizabeth’s words seemed like a shot of adrenaline, injecting confidence into Luke’s heart and eliminating his doubts.

“As you command! I will complete this mission well,” Luke replied, his excitement rising. This “procession” was just an excuse for him to show off across the regions, and with the Thorn Knights and a purple-gold adventurer as his bodyguards, what did he have to worry about? He could just flex to his heart’s content!

Queen Elizabeth rubbed her temples and waved her hand dismissively.

“Alright, go. Don’t forget what your family promised me.”

Outside, four Thorn Knights waited, awaiting the queen’s summons.

Merfield, Morrison, Millais, and Winifred were all present.

Morrison frowned in confusion. “Your Majesty, what does she want with us?”

“Pfft!” Millais scoffed, exasperated. “What else? She must want us to protect the duke’s stupid son.”

Morrison’s expression darkened. He suspected Millais was still angry about being ordered to lose on purpose earlier.

“Millais, let go of this morning’s grudge. We should understand the queen’s intentions,” Winifred muttered.

“Hmph!” Millais snorted, clearly in a foul mood.

Morrison hesitated, awkwardly saying, “Shouldn’t we reconcile with the real Elgin Blade Lord? If everyone calms down and talks, I think all grudges can be resolved, right?”

“This matter…” Merfield grew uneasy, recalling the humiliation of being spat on. “I’ve already suggested this to the queen.”

“What?!” Morrison was stunned. If Merfield, as the first knight, had advised the queen, it should have had an effect. After all, she carried far more weight than he did.

Millais and Winifred also seemed unsettled. They hadn’t expected Merfield to speak up for the Elgin Blade Lord.

“Really? You also think we should reconcile with him?” Millais rolled her eyes, gripping her hair in frustration. “Good heavens, are you all mad? That lowborn mercenary—how could he ever join our ranks?!”

“I think Merfield must have her own reasons,” Winifred remained composed.

To be honest, I personally despise the Elgin Blade Lord. That filthy, despicable, disgusting man—he’s nothing like us…

Merfield took a deep breath and spoke seriously. “But for the empire’s sake, we should indeed reconcile with the Elgin Blade Lord, rather than continuing this pointless confrontation. It benefits no one.”

“What does the queen think? Did she accept your suggestion?” Morrison asked eagerly.

“Isn’t it obvious? The queen didn’t listen to me at all. Instead, she chose to refuse any compromise, which is why she’s staging this fake Elgin Blade Lord farce,” Merfield sighed in resignation.

“So it’s like that…” Morrison felt awkward, muttering, “That man is incredibly powerful. If he stood with us, he’d be an unstoppable force. But as an enemy… he’s terrifying.”

“Morrison, stop boosting his reputation and diminishing your own. Do you think the Elgin Blade Lord is strong because you’re too weak?” Millais sneered from the side, looking down on Morrison.

“What did you say? You can say that because you’ve never seen the Elgin Blade Lord’s true strength, right? If you had, you’d respect me too,” Morrison’s eyes flashed with anger as he clenched his fists.

“To be honest, if I were serious, aside from Merfield, I wouldn’t fear…” Millais raised her chin defiantly.

“Shut up…” Merfield furrowed her brows, clearly in a bad mood. “Even as a knight, I… I can’t beat that man. Morrison is right—there’s a huge gap between us and the Elgin Blade Lord.”

At these words, the other three Thorn Knights exchanged stunned glances.

They had never imagined that the proud First Knight would ever admit defeat to anyone.

title: Chapter 16 — Taunt
content:
Chapter 16 — Taunt

Volume 10 · Chapter 16

Even though Meisfield hated to admit it, losing to the great swordsman Elgin was simply too humiliating!

But the ghost-flame Demon Lord Hao Gui, someone she herself couldn't defeat, had been instantly defeated by that nasty guy. Facts spoke louder than words, leaving no room for Meisfield to rationalize.

However, to make these people a bit more clear-headed, Meisfield had no choice but to state the facts. Otherwise, someone like Milius would surely think everything was fine as long as she was around.

The other three Thorn Knights all stared at Meisfield in bewilderment. You see, the First Knight was already considered the strongest combatant within the Begonia Knight Order.

If even Meisfield had been defeated by Elgin the Great Swordsman, then within the Thorn Knights... was there anyone who could still beat the Great Swordsman?!

"Really? You were actually defeated by Elgin the Great Swordsman?" Morrison was the first to recover from his shock and asked in surprise.

"...Well, I wasn't defeated head-on, exactly," Meisfield hesitated, deciding to preserve a little dignity for herself. "I simply witnessed Elgin the Great Swordsman's strength with my own eyes, so I concluded that I would hardly have a chance of winning against him."

"What was that?" Milius let out a small sigh of relief, finding this easy enough to understand. "Why are you and Morrison both falling for the same trick? Since you didn't fight seriously, it doesn't even count as defeat. Don't be fooled by flashy tricks. Morrison has a simple mind, but surely your brain isn't as simple as his, Meisfield?"

"Hey! Milius..." Morrison's face instantly darkened, somewhat angered. "Why do you always have to mock me? If you've got a problem with me, just say it directly. If you can't keep your mouth shut, let's go spar outside."

"Hmph~" Milius hummed lightly and stroked his golden hair. "I don't like sparring with brutes. It lacks all elegance."

"Tch!" Morrison clicked his tongue in dissatisfaction. The more he looked at Milius's attitude, the more annoyed he became.

"Enough, stop arguing," Meisfield stepped between Milius and Morrison and said seriously, "Listen carefully, Milius. Elgin the Great Swordsman's strength is absolutely not just a show. Have you forgotten how he punched you into the ruins that one time?"

"..." Milius's brows immediately furrowed, feeling somewhat embarrassed. "That was because I wasn't taking it seriously! If I had been, how could I have let him escape so easily?!"

"Whatever you say..." Meisfield had no desire to waste more time on Milius and said indifferently, "Anyway, I can't defeat that guy. As for you two, figure it out yourselves. Morrison's thinking is also for the benefit of the Empire, and I don't see any major problem with that."

"Ugh!" A vein pulsed visibly on Milius's forehead, and he retorted defiantly, "Meisfield, has your strength regressed? If that's truly the case, then let me be the First Knight instead~"

"Are you serious?" Meisfield narrowed her eyes, sensing that Milius was deliberately provoking her.

"So what if I am?" Milius was stubborn and refused to yield. "By the way, our last spar was four years ago, wasn't it? Back then, you were indeed stronger than me. But who is stronger now? It's not certain!"

"Never mind... this is the royal court..." Winifred, who had been keeping silent, finally couldn't resist stepping in to mediate. "I think there's some truth in what Meisfield and Morrison said. If Elgin the Great Swordsman's strength is truly formidable, it wouldn't be a foolish choice to make him one of us. Moreover, after Sahadin's death, the Ninth Knight position has remained vacant."

"Huh!?"

Milius never expected Winifred to side with Morrison and Meisfield as well, which was rather unbelievable.

Milius usually had the closest relationship with Winifred, and Winifred had always been a quiet type who rarely spoke up.

Now that he had suddenly expressed his opinion, it was likely because he couldn't stand seeing Milius's current behavior either, right?

Milius grew somewhat angry and didn't bother hiding his irritation as he said earnestly, "Make Elgin the Great Swordsman join us? Are you kidding me! I absolutely will not agree. That low-class wanted criminal—does he deserve to become a Thorn Knight?! I think all of your brains have gone soft!"

Meisfield sighed, watched Milius silently shake her head, and thought to herself—

Milius had let far too many personal emotions interfere. He hadn't considered the Empire's interests at all.

Was it simply because that guy was slightly more handsome, slightly stronger, and slightly more popular than him...

What else could there be? Where did such intense jealousy come from?!

Luke left the throne hall, putting distance between himself and Queen Elizabeth.

He secretly exhaled a breath of relief, feeling significantly more at ease.

A slightly sinister expression crept onto Luke's chubby face as he viciously thought to himself—

What a bunch of crap about the ruler of the Empire!

She was nothing but an old woman blinded by greed and ambition!

Haha, just you wait. Before long, the Empire would see a new dynasty rise.

The new rulers of the Empire would be our House of Awrfrey, and I would become a noble prince!

They wanted to pacify us with Elgin the Great Swordsman's honor—how laughable. In the face of absolute power's temptation, what was honor worth?!

When our military strength grew enough to rival the Kingdom's army, that would be the time House Awrfrey raised its rebellious banner!

At that point, I would make full use of Elgin the Great Swordsman's identity. With a single call, hundreds would answer, igniting a wave of rebellion across the entire Empire.

And at that time, Elizabeth, that old woman, would be nothing but a bitch. Hahaha...
