Luke's eyes gleamed with fierce light as he already envisioned his starry, brilliant future. Imperial prince—what an enviable title.

Just as Luke was lost in his dream of becoming a prince, he suddenly noticed several Thorn Knights arguing ahead. Remembering the performance they had put on for him that morning, an overwhelming sense of superiority surged within him, and he couldn't resist walking over to tease them a bit.

"Oh~ Have the distinguished knights started quarreling?"

The moment they heard Luke's voice, Milius and Winifred immediately turned their heads toward him. The hostility in their eyes was completely unhidden.

Meisfield and Morrison's expressions were equally grim. After all, this noble young master had trampled upon the honor of the Knight Order.

"What are those looks for? Like you want to kill me or something..." Luke spread his hands and smiled at Milius and Winifred. "Thank you both for playing along with me this morning. When I return, I'll have my father reward you well. You've got to at least give the extra actors some chicken legs, or else there'll be resentment."

"You little punk, who do you think you are? If it weren't for Grand Duke Awrfrey backing you behind the scenes, someone like you would have been hacked to pieces long ago!" Milius immediately erupted in furious anger.

"Hah!? Who in the entire Empire doesn't know my father's name? Even Her Majesty the Queen gives him a measure of respect. Who dares to lay a hand on me?" Luke revealed a knowing smile, extraordinarily arrogant.

"Tch!" Milius immediately gripped the hilt of his sword, golden Saint-tier battle aura erupting around him.

"Milius!" Meisfield was startled and lightning-fast grabbed Milius's shoulder, preventing him from acting impulsively.

"Oh ho ho~ How frightening, My Knight. I'd advise you to stay calm. Tomorrow I'm departing on my tour of the regions. You're my bodyguard, so if anything happens to me, you'll all be held responsible and won't escape punishment~" Luke curled his lips upward and swept his gaze across the Thorn Knights before him, speaking in a scornful tone, "Make sure you behave yourselves properly then. Don't let me down..."

title: Chapter 17 — Moon Ticket Bonus Update (Next Update Around Midnight)
content:
Chapter 17 — Moon Ticket Bonus Update (Next Update Around Midnight)

Volume 10 · Chapter 17

Night.

Merlin and Alice returned home.

Even though there had been that little farce with the fake Elgyn Great Swordsman today, Merlin didn’t seem to mind. It was just an empty title, after all.

Did he really have to rush to the royal capital in the middle of the night and hack this Luke to death?

Merlin thought it over carefully. No, there was no need. So what if it was just the empty title of Elgyn Great Swordsman? What was the big deal?

To Merlin, who had lived for over two hundred years, he was long past the age of reckless bravery. Empty glory might feel good for a moment, but afterward, all that remained was endless emptiness.

"Alright, let’s eat."

Alice carried over the potato beef stew, placed a portion in front of Merlin, then removed her apron and hung it aside.

Merlin’s eyelids drooped as he noticed the potatoes in the stew were slightly blackened. Cold sweat immediately broke out on his forehead.

"I swear, why is your cooking still this bad after all this practice?"

"What?! My cooking is bad? This is already really good, okay?! I’ve improved by leaps and bounds. Which eye of yours sees it as the same as before?" Alice planted her hands on her hips, shouting indignantly. She always felt like Merlin was nitpicking.

Merlin, expression unshaken, used his fork to lift a piece of beef from his plate and held it up for Alice to see. "Miss, can you explain this hair on the beef? And it’s covered in potato broth..."

"..." Alice’s face darkened, momentarily at a loss for words. She blurted out the first thing that came to mind, "That’s… green onion!"

"Get out! Does your green onion look like this?! Even GMO isn’t this messed up!" Merlin was thoroughly appalled, furiously roasting Alice.

"...So noisy." Alice puffed up her cheeks in anger, feeling mocked. "It’s just a cow hair, what’s the big deal? It’s not like it’ll poison you!"

Merlin pressed his lips together. *I might actually get poisoned,* he thought. Even though he was immune to magic, his poison resistance was practically zero.

"You even *know* it’s a cow hair?! Why didn’t you clean it properly before cooking?! Your food is practically dark cuisine incarnate! After all this practice, your cooking hasn’t improved one bit. I think you’re trying to murder me!" Merlin’s eyebrows shot up, utterly exasperated.

"...Who’s trying to murder you?!" Alice’s beautiful face turned icy, her tone even more unyielding than Merlin’s. "It was *your* turn to do the chores, okay?! I’m only helping because you saved me before. Otherwise, do you really think I’d be this kind?"

"But who would eat your dark cuisine?" Merlin gave her a playful look.

"Then don’t eat it!" Alice yanked the stew back from in front of Merlin, huffing. "Pay me back!"

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue in dissatisfaction, pulling the stew back toward himself. "Don’t bring up money every time. It hurts our relationship. I was just teasing. Besides, I’m not a picky eater..."

"Hmph!" Alice plopped down, secretly pleased that she had Merlin by the tail.

"Alice..." Merlin called softly, then continued, "What do you think about that Luke from today?"

"What’s there to think? He’s the Elgyn Great Swordsman—powerful and noble..." Alice said sulkily.

"Aren’t you obsessed with the Elgyn Great Swordsman? Now that the real one has revealed himself, why do you seem so unhappy?" Merlin narrowed his eyes, sizing her up like an old fox.

"It’s just a little disappointing. He’s not quite what I imagined. I don’t know why, but I just don’t feel that spark. There’s something... off about him." Alice answered seriously. She knew she admired the Elgyn Great Swordsman, but for some reason, Luke didn’t stir that fluttering, heart-racing feeling in her. Still, she did respect and admire him.

"No spark? So you’ve transferred your feelings? Maybe to me?" Merlin asked bluntly, as if it were the most natural thing in the world. After all, he *had* saved Alice so many times—it wouldn’t make sense if she didn’t feel *something* for him.

"..." Alice’s face slowly flushed red. She glared at Merlin, lost in thought. "D-Don’t... don’t talk nonsense! Who would be stupid enough to transfer their feelings to *you*?! Have some self-awareness, will you?!"

"Then..." Merlin hesitated, sensing her reaction wasn’t quite what he’d expected.

"As if *you* could compare to the Elgyn Great Swordsman! You’re way behind, okay?! Sure, he might not be as strong as you, but at least he’s a *just* man! And he’s a noble, highly respected, rich—compared to him, you’d get *instantly* crushed to dust!" Alice, hiding her true feelings, proceeded to tear Merlin down.

"But lately, *I’m* the one being mistaken for the Elgyn Great Swordsman. That Luke hasn’t done anything! He’s just taking credit for *my* work!" Merlin spread his hands in exasperation, feeling Alice’s constant belittling was unreasonable.

"He’s the real deal, and you’re the fake. Just that alone makes him *way* better than you." Alice puffed up her cheeks.

"Alice, *I* am the Elgyn Great Swordsman. Don’t you think I look the part?" Merlin had already forgotten how many times he’d admitted this.

"Hah!" Alice grinned scornfully. "Not even close. I don’t see a single thing about you that resembles the Elgyn Great Swordsman. If you gained three or four more rings around your waist, *maybe* I’d believe you."

Merlin rolled his eyes, left speechless. *So I have to get fat for her to believe me?* He was the real one—did he really need to match the fake’s physique? This was ridiculous.

Alice, her face still flushed, stole a glance at Merlin. Remembering what Lucia had said, she fell into confusion once more.

*Like or admire?*

Even she wasn’t entirely clear.

*What exactly do I feel for Merlin?*

Every time she saw Merlin getting too close to other girls, her heart twisted uncomfortably.

Sometimes, when he showed even the slightest bit of concern, her heart would flutter. She’d think, *He’s not so bad.*

Was this what it felt like to *like* someone? Could such complicated emotions come from just admiring a person?

And this damn Great Demon Lord was her *enemy*—how could she possibly feel affection for him?

She *should* like the Elgyn Great Swordsman. But that Luke... he didn’t feel right. Knowing his true identity had left her a little disappointed.

Maybe Lucia was right—her feelings for the Elgyn Great Swordsman were just pure admiration. The person she *actually* liked was someone else.

*If only Merlin really were the Elgyn Great Swordsman... that would be perfect...*

Alice’s mind swirled with strange thoughts, the blush on her face deepening.

"What the hell are you blushing for?" Merlin snapped at her without hesitation.

...Alice panicked, quickly lowering her head, utterly flustered.

...

"Just... just eat your damn food."

N/w/Y

title: Chapter 18 — Brand New
content:
Chapter 18 — Brand New

Volume 10 · Chapter 18

More than half a month had passed.

Everything was proceeding according to plan.

The empire was a cauldron of hidden currents; on the surface, all was calm, but every faction harbored its own schemes.

The Overly family had not honored their promise. Instead, they were secretly expanding their military and preparing for war.

In just over half a month, they had not only expanded their influence across northern England but had also covertly recruited countless local powerholders.

By rough estimates, the Overly family’s strength was now on par with the royal army. With multiple Saint-tier powerhouses at their disposal, even if they faced all the Thorn Knights, they seemed capable of holding their own.

Yet, on the surface, the Overly family remained courteous to Queen Elizabeth, showing no hint of hostility.

Under the pretense of defending against magical beasts, they were quietly bolstering their own forces, preparing for the queen’s eventual suppression.

The Overly family was one of the empire’s founding noble houses, with deep roots and immense influence. Unless pushed to the brink, they would not act recklessly.

Queen Elizabeth was no fool. Sensing the danger, she secretly ordered the empire’s military forces to move north, positioning them like sharp blades at the Overly family’s throat as a deterrent.

In addition, Elizabeth did not abandon her conciliatory approach. She continued to extend goodwill to the Overly family and pushed forward with Luke’s plan to impersonate the great swordsman Elgin, hoping to keep the Overly family in check.

Now, Queen Elizabeth was less concerned about the Overly family and more worried about the real Elgin.

Thus, eliminating the true Elgin had become her top priority, which seemed reasonable.

During this time, Luke’s impersonation of Elgin continued smoothly.

The parade, organized by the Rose Knights, had departed from the royal capital and traveled through the empire’s cities and towns.

Now, they had already entered Wales and were expected to arrive in Wrexham today, allowing the people to behold the “great swordsman Elgin.”

As for Merlin and Alice, their recent interactions had been uneventful, almost peaceful.

However, Jenna, that infatuated girl, seemed to have grown bolder in her frustration. She kept sneaking peeks at Merlin or harassing him.

Merlin was helpless and dared not scold or hit her—after all, for a masochist, punishment was a reward.

If he tried to discipline her, she might sink even deeper, making it far harder for Merlin to ever win her over.

In contrast to Jenna, Arnold had been unusually well-behaved lately, likely still nursing his wounded pride.

Alice, meanwhile, had spent the past half-month singing Elgin’s praises, constantly declaring how wonderful, how outstanding he was, and how he surpassed Merlin in every way—as if she would die if she didn’t provoke Merlin.

This left Merlin thoroughly exasperated. *He* was the real Elgin! How was that impostor better than him in any way?

It was like a bootleg mocking the original, calling the original trash—where was the justice in that?

Merlin couldn’t be bothered to argue with Alice. Ignoring her provocations, he simply spoke less.

Alice had been busy cultivating lately, eager to master Saint-tier power and the innate gifts of the dragon race, hoping to elevate her strength to the next level. At the very least, she didn’t want to keep getting crushed by enemies and owing Merlin favors.

As a Saint-tier powerhouse, Alice’s strength had already undergone a qualitative leap—she was nothing like her former self.

For someone like Alice, who cultivated both magic and martial arts, reaching Saint-tier was several times harder than for ordinary people. Such individuals were likely as rare as phoenix feathers across the entire world.

But the greater the difficulty, the greater the reward. By mastering both magic and fighting spirit, Alice became far stronger than an ordinary Saint-tier warrior. Her combat versatility made her an extremely difficult opponent.

Moreover, with the secret techniques of the Great Snow Mountain, she could fuse magic and fighting spirit into a third, brand-new power system, unleashing far greater combat potential—likely multiplying her strength several times over.

Add to that the various innate gifts of the dragon race, as well as the vast magic and fighting spirit reserves of the Frost Saint Dragon, and Alice’s transformation was inevitable. Her power was bound to soar.

Now, Alice could use some of the dragon race’s martial techniques and spells. She could also partially transform her body at will, instantly boosting her combat abilities.

Even the aura she emitted carried a distinct dragon’s might, enough to intimidate foes. Weaker-willed opponents might lose their will to fight on the spot.

Ordinary Saint-tier warriors carefully controlled their magic and fighting spirit output, but Alice no longer needed to worry. With the Frost Saint Dragon’s power sustaining her, she could expend her energy freely. This alone set her far above other Saint-tier warriors.

The Frost Saint Dragon’s inheritance crystal within Alice had not yet been fully absorbed. So far, she had only assimilated 25% of its power.

Since her own strength was still insufficient, the remaining 75% remained beyond her reach. She would have to keep growing stronger, slowly absorbing the rest. Once she reached 100%, her power would likely peak at the pinnacle of Saint-tier, rivaling that of the Frost Saint Dragon, Malgus.

Alice was still racing toward becoming a humanoid Saint Dragon; she was not yet complete.

Perhaps when she truly reached that state, she might uncover other secrets as well?

Even with only 25% of the dragon’s power and immature control, it was more than enough for self-defense. Defeating a group of mediocre Saint-tier warriors would be effortless.

In the training hall—

Alice was delighted by the changes in herself, her joy impossible to conceal.

A cold mist swirled around her, as if a great dragon stood guard.

The frigid temperature swept through the surroundings, instantly freezing into frost. The ground, too, was coated in a layer of ice.

Pale magic and fighting spirit overflowed from Alice’s body, intertwining with each other.

Alice attempted to control this new power, testing how much it could enhance her strength.

A deep blue shard of ice floated above her palm, radiating chilling mist as it spun.

Alice’s expression turned serious. She decided to try fusing the two forces using the essence of the Great Snow Mountain’s techniques.

She poured a surge of fighting spirit into the blue ice. Instantly, its surface transformed into a golden hue.

The translucent, golden color made it resemble a floating golden crystal—beautiful to behold.

Fusing Saint-tier magic and fighting spirit had produced a new power, a third form distinct from the basic systems of magic and martial energy.

It was an independent, brand-new force, and its offensive capabilities were even greater!

Alice immediately beamed with pride. Though she felt her golden ice was still far from matching her teacher’s, she was satisfied. At the very least, she was getting closer to his level!

“Hmm?” Merlin furrowed his brow, eyeing the golden ice floating in Alice’s hand. He felt a faint sense of threat.

“Seems interesting…”

(..)

Sorry, I’ve been dragged to the gym by my family lately.

A few days ago, I ran 500 meters and threw up from oxygen deprivation. My family said my physique was terrible, so…

I’ll still add more chapters, don’t worry~!

title: Chapter 19 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 19 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 10 · Chapter 19

Alice’s heart raced with excitement as she recalled how her teacher could summon golden frost everywhere, its power brimming with both magic and martial energy—just a few ice spears could send even a demon beast fleeing in terror. She had envied it so much!

Now, she could do it too. Granted, her ability still lagged behind, but this was her first step—truly a giant leap toward catching up to her teacher’s pace!

Alice was certain that if she returned to the Alps Snow Mountain now, her teacher would jump in shock. After all, she was the legitimate heir to the mountain’s legacy, even if her teacher seemed to have only her as a student—though that was fine by her.

Merlin had initially scoffed at Alice’s teacher, but now he had to admit the woman was impressive.

To merge magic and martial energy into a new force—that technique alone was already incredibly difficult.

“How about it? Do I impress you now?” Alice smirked, looking at Merlin with pride.

“Pathetic little brat,” Merlin drawled, curling his lip in disdain.

Alice’s mood soured instantly. She had expected at least a little praise, but all she got was mockery.

“Fine, let’s spar,” she huffed, determined to see just how far her progress had brought her. She still hadn’t given up on her dream of stomping Merlin into the ground with her high heels.

Merlin casually picked up a wooden sword and stepped forward, saying lazily, “Let’s play.”

“Pfft!” Alice scoffed, her irritation flaring at his dismissive attitude. She clearly sensed he was looking down on her.

Her Saint-tier aura surged, radiating a palpable dragon’s presence—so strong it almost made her seem like a colossal wyrm.

Magic and martial energy swirled around her, forming a golden armor-like glow that was almost blinding.

Merlin frowned slightly, thinking, *Just 25% of her power, and she’s already this terrifying? That inheritance crystal is something else.*

Alice flicked her slender blade, and golden ice swords materialized in the air, their frigid presence making the air tremble. They hovered, trembling with eagerness, as if ready to pierce Merlin at any moment.

Her attacks had evolved—now perfectly blending magic and martial energy, unleashing a force far stronger than before.

Before, Alice’s ice attacks had been a dull blue, with mediocre effects. But now, they had undergone a transformation. These golden frosts were as sharp as rare metals, their edge unmatched.

Though the cost in magic and martial energy was steep, Alice didn’t mind. The dragon’s blood in her veins ensured an endless supply.

“Hah!” Alice cried, and the golden ice swords shot toward Merlin like wild horses, their sharp *swoosh* cutting through the air like a symphony.

Merlin had been lounging, but as the ice swords neared—just a finger’s width from his eyes—his pupils contracted in shock.

Reacting instantly, he swung his wooden sword, shattering the blades with ease.

“Hahaha! You’re finally nervous!” Alice grinned, thrilled by her rapid progress. She had reached a point where she could genuinely threaten Merlin.

Before, he had always sparred with her half-heartedly, but now he’d actually shown hesitation. It was unthinkable—unless she had grown stronger, there was no other explanation!

Alice felt exhilarated, sensing her dream was within reach. The day she could sing *The Internationale* as a freed peasant was coming soon.

“What’s there to be smug about? I just wasn’t expecting that,” Merlin sighed, thinking *This girl’s head is in the clouds. She’s got a long way to go.*

He glanced at the shattered ice swords on the ground, their golden shimmer unsettling.

Merlin had been stunned—why had his magic immunity suddenly failed? Normally, these attacks would have bypassed him entirely. But these golden blades had pierced through, and if he hadn’t reacted in time, they might have actually hurt him. That would’ve been humiliating.

Actually, his magic immunity hadn’t failed—it just couldn’t defend against this new fusion of magic and martial energy.

Magic immunity nullified all magic-based attacks, but Alice’s ice crystals were beyond mere magic. This was a fresh, unprecedented force, one his immunity couldn’t counter. That’s why he’d been caught off guard.

“Hmph!” Alice sniffed, smugly declaring, “I’m not some invisible nobody you can ignore anymore. Admit it.”

“Tsk,” Merlin clicked his tongue, curious. “So the Alps Snow Mountain’s essence is merging magic and martial energy?”

“So what if it is?” Alice tilted her chin higher, her confidence skyrocketing compared to before.

“Nothing, just impressive. Your teacher isn’t weak at all,” Merlin said casually, admitting that mastering such a fusion was far rarer—and far harder—than most magic combinations.

“Of course not! My teacher’s amazing. If she weren’t such a spinster, I think her personality would be even better,” Alice said proudly, though she still felt guilty for stealing money—and worse, the *Light Hymn*—from her.

“Your mountain’s technique is basically using ice magic to seal martial energy, then forcibly blending them together, right?” Merlin probed.

“Huh?!” Alice blinked, stunned that Merlin had seen through it so clearly. The guy had no magic or martial energy, yet his insight was razor-sharp. “…Yeah, that’s right. But not just anyone can pull that off.”

Merlin chuckled helplessly, thinking *Her fusion is impressive, but she’s still leagues behind me.*

“Alright, let’s see what happens when I fully transform…” Alice raised her blade, her eyes flashing gold as dragon scales rippled beneath her skin.

But just then, Lucy pushed open the training hall’s door.

Lucy was breathless, her chest heaving, her face flushed with excitement. Whatever had happened, it had clearly thrilled her.

Alice quickly suppressed her transformation, frowning. “Lucy? What’s wrong?”

Lucy took a moment to steady herself, then grinned. “Alice, come on—*hurry*—”

“Elgin’s coming! The parade’s about to pass the Guild’s gates…”

title: Chapter 20 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 20 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 10 · Chapter 20

“Is that so?!” Alice’s eyes widened instantly; being able to see the people who worshiped her made her feel very excited.

“Yeah, we’re almost at the gate. If we’re slow we’ll probably miss it, let’s go.” Lucía waved at Alice, seeming herself a bit impatient.

“No more training, no more training, we’re going to see Erkin the Great Sword Hero.” Alice quickly sheathed her rapier, grabbed Lucía’s hand, and headed off together.

“I heard Erkin the Great Sword Hero will stay in Reckserum for one night, and tomorrow morning he’ll head to the next place—” Lucía replied happily.

“Is that so? That’s great....” Alice felt a little hopeful, estimating she could watch Erkin the Great Sword Hero for a long time.

The two girls chatted and laughed as they held hands and left, not even looking back, leaving Merlin awkwardly stranded on the side.

The entire training hall was suddenly left with only Merlin standing alone, a light cold wind blowing and making everything feel chaotic.

Merlin looked at Alice’s happy back, feeling a bit sour inside, and couldn’t help feeling…

This…

“The fake Erkin the Great Sword Hero just ignored me as soon as he arrived?”

“Damn it, I’ll go see too. Does this guy act cool more than me?”

Outside.

The whole town of Reckserum erupted in celebration, as if a grand festival were taking place.

Residents of all ages and genders flooded the streets, eager to catch a glimpse of Erkin the Great Sword Hero’s presence.

The streets were packed with crowds, people pressed together, leaving a clear path in the middle for the parade to pass.

The garrison troops stationed in Reckserum were also deployed, setting up barriers to maintain order and prevent civilians from rushing forward.

As the battalion commander, Plais was swamped, constantly organizing the crowd, sweating profusely.

“Seriously, what kind of pointless parade is this? Doesn’t everyone have things to do?”

“And they chose Sunday to come to Reckserum, really picking the worst time…”

Such complaints kept surfacing in Plais’s mind, leaving him feeling exhausted.

In a small town like Reckserum, there are rarely grand events; life is absolutely comfortable, especially for the stationed guards.

Yet the arrival of Erkin the Great Sword Hero was like giving the garrison extra work for no reason, unnecessarily increasing their workload.

Plais lazily stood at the edge of the crowd, ordering his subordinates to keep an eye on the excited people and prevent any trouble.

However, Erkin the Great Sword Hero is hailed as an imperial hero, so how could there be few fans? Many in the crowd were still chatting…

“Should be coming soon.”

“Exactly, it should be soon, I can hear the cheers over there.”

“I never expected to see Erkin the Great Sword Hero in person, what luck!”

The residents of Reckserum discussed heatedly; a hero appearing in peacetime is truly a focal point for everyone.

Moreover, a group of pretty girls nearby had prepared flower baskets and ribbons, all dressed flamboyantly.

“Erkin the Great Sword Hero is coming soon, what do we do? I’m so excited.”

“Don’t worry about being excited, number 0…”

“Erkin the Great Sword Hero, we love you, that’s right, isn’t it?”

These girls clearly seemed to be Reckserum’s fan club, and they even had chants, which was surprising.

Plais watched those youthful, beautiful girls and couldn’t help swallow his saliva.

For a nearly forty‑year‑old single man, these girls were a huge temptation.

Plais silently thought, “Erkin the Great Sword Hero, what an enviable man! If I had that many fans, I’d be thrilled.”

Alice and Lucía were also in the crowd, looking around, seeming to share the same excitement as everyone else.

Alice tiptoed, seeing the front of the parade still far away, moving slowly, “Isn’t it still far?”

“Get ahead of the crowd, you want to stay at the back? Then you won’t see anything,” Lucía said with a smile.

“........” Alice responded awkwardly.

Lucía looked around, curiously asking, “Strange, why didn’t Merlin come with us?”

“Huh? Why would he come with us?” Alice asked, puzzled.

“Isn’t he your husband? He should be jealous, right? Did they argue again?”

“No, don’t guess,” Alice said, blushing and awkward, “We’re only married in name; it would be weird for him to be jealous.”

“Is that so?” Lucía’s expression became complicated, seeming hard to understand the relationship between Merlin and Alice.

“And just as you said, I only admire Erkin; that cold‑blooded Merlin wouldn’t get jealous,” Alice said, sounding deflated.

“Well… it seems… but not…”

“This…” Alice hesitated, finding it hard to refute Lucía’s words, feeling Merlin was usually cold and only a partnership of convenience, wondering if she had any charm at all.

“Actually I also admire my father, but he gets angry easily; compared to him, Erkin the Great Sword Hero is quite outstanding,” Lucía said with longing, instantly switching her idol.

“Eh?” Alice stared, surprised, “Is that Mr. Carl?”

“Yes, before my mother died she always said my father was a great hero, and I felt proud watching him defeat villains, but over time I thought… ” Lucía paused, then said flatly, “He’s just a hot‑blooded old man, isn’t he?”

“…Alice no longer knew how to react to Lucía, feeling Mr. Carl was pitiful, being despised by his own daughter…”

Merlin appeared, seeing the sea of people before him, and he frowned. “Heavens, Erkin the Great Sword Hero is that popular?”

Before Merlin hadn’t thought he was that popular; now it seemed he was becoming a star in minutes.

Merlin looked around and saw Alice laughing with Lucía.

Plais saw Merlin, bored with no one to chat with, and greeted enthusiastically, “Merlin buddy, over here!”

“Here’s a good spot, you can see better!”

Plais gave Merlin the green light to come forward, since they’d hung out before, he trusted him.

Merlin, a bit embarrassed, thought it over and then walked over, waving.

“Long time no see, Plais.”

“Long time no see, you’re also here to see Erkin the Great Sword Hero? So you’re a fan too?” Plais asked, surprised.

“....” Merlin was speechless, showing a half‑smile, thinking “What the hell, a fan of Erkin the Great Sword Hero?!”

“I am the real Erkin the Great Sword Hero, do I really need to watch a fake?!” ε=('o、))

title: Chapter 21 — Hidden Dangers at Four Corners
content:
Chapter 21 — Hidden Dangers at Four Corners

Volume 10 · Chapter 21

"I'm not a fan of the Great Swordsman Elgin or anything. I just came to take a look out of curiosity."

Merlin gave a bland explanation, wondering who looked like a fan — it was just one guy. Did he really need to care?

"Is that so..." Price paused, then said in surprise, "There aren't many people these days who aren't followers of the Great Swordsman Elgin."

"By your tone... Could it be that you're also a fan of the Great Swordsman Elgin?" Merlin frowned, having a hard time imagining someone like Price — a thug-like guard captain — worshipping a hero besides money and women.

"No no no, no matter how strong the Great Swordsman Elgin is, he has nothing to do with me. It's just that this man has way too many admirers these days. Out of ten people, almost seven can't stop praising him. It's completely unreasonable," Price said with a wry expression, his shrugged shoulders suggesting even he found it rather helpless.

Merlin fell silent, thinking — had the Great Swordsman Elgin's curse become this vicious? He should have never posed as Elgin in Elgin a year ago.

"By the way, brother Merlin, what have you been busy with lately? It's been a long time since we went to Helena's Secret Cabin together, and I don't think I've seen you join us since..." Price brought up a rather personal topic.

"..." Merlin awkwardly scratched his cheek. He had snuck over a few times on his own, but it was all for serious business.

"What? Brother Merlin, are you dissatisfied with the girls at the Secret Cabin?" Price guessed with a knowing smile. "Then your standards are way too high. The girls at the Secret Cabin — if you took them to the Royal Capital, they'd all be first-class beauties. The fact that they're staying here in Rexham to develop is such good fortune. It's truly a blessing for all of us Rexham men~"

Merlin couldn't help but frown, wondering if he looked like someone who couldn't extricate himself from indulging in the opposite sex. He had seen plenty of beauties. The girls at the Secret Cabin simply couldn't ignite any impulse in him.

"Even if those girls don't satisfy you, isn't there still the madam? Miss Helena is breathtakingly beautiful, comparable to a perfect goddess." Price looked up, smacking his lips enviously. "And I remember back when we first met, Miss Helena's gaze toward you was already different. Perhaps she has feelings for you. I think you should consider developing something..."

Merlin's expression became unnatural. Helena was Asmodeus's subordinate. Was he picking her up or exploiting her position? Neither sounded good.

"If I could get spit on fiercely by Miss Helena, that would be such an exhilarating thing~" Price's old face flushed red, suddenly wearing an expression of longing — he was probably fantasizing about various perverted scenes again.

"..." Dark lines seemed to twitch on Merlin's forehead. He found this old man somewhat disgusting. Perhaps this was why he was still single. "I just don't want to go. There are no other reasons."

"Oh? That's not how a normal man would think," Price stroked his chin, sizing Merlin up. Suddenly a possibility struck him. Oh ho~ — had Alice been managing him too strictly? So married men really do have it rough, with zero freedom. Unlike me, I can go wherever I want~"

"Huh?! ?" Merlin's head was full of question marks. Alice restricting his freedom? What kind of cosmic joke was this?!

"But brother Merlin, don't worry. This is precisely the time to test your wisdom. Just use every trick in the book to slip past Alice's surveillance~" Price said enthusiastically.

.... Merlin was speechless and temporarily didn't want to talk to Price, because the parade approaching in the distance was nearly upon them....

The parade was quite massive, consisting of several thousand people.

They marched majestically into Rexham Town, and for a moment you couldn't even see the end of the procession.

The entire troop appeared extremely disciplined, without a trace of chaos, radiating vigor.

The members were almost all正规 knights of the Bauhinia Knight Order, each clad in silver armor and carrying exquisite, magnificent weapons.

The countless spears bore bauhinia flags fluttering in the wind, dancing majestically in the sky above the town, like warriors returning in triumph.

Queen Elizabeth had clearly put great effort into this parade. To shape the royal family's glorious image, she had dispatched many powerful individuals and an splendid procession.

At the front were knights riding noble steeds, serving as the vanguard clearing the path ahead.

◆

Well-trained steeds, heads held high, made the entire procession seem full of morale.

Following them were the infantry squares, their gleaming silver armor forming a flowing river of silver, exceptionally beautiful.

Right behind were dozens of giant carriages pulled by earth dragons, adorned with gilt decorations and bright red carpets covering the entire carriage.

Luke wore formal attire. Though his belly in front was quite large, it still conveyed a certain heroic bearing.

He wore a kind and amiable smile, continuously waving and greeting the onlookers on both sides.

Luke's appearance suggested he might truly see himself as a hero, gladly accepting the praises of the cheering crowd.

Behind Luke's carriage, four Thorn Knights followed, providing full-time protection of Luke's safety.

Any hostile person seeing the magnificent Thorn Knights would have long since lost their nerve.

Furthermore, with four Thorn Knights present, anyone wanting to cause trouble would need to carefully consider their own worth.

Aside from the four Thorn Knights, Gray Guild Master Gregori naturally came along as well.

However, Gregori's movements were mysterious. Rather than following the main group, he chose to weave through the crowd.

This elusive approach allowed him to conceal himself — almost no one would be able to discover him.

Gregori did this purely out of personal disposition. He disliked being radiant, under the spotlight of thousands of eyes.

He preferred to keep a low profile. If possible, he wouldn't need to lift a finger the entire time — ideally.

Gregori had agreed to Queen Elizabeth's conditions, but he was only responsible for dealing with the real Great Swordsman Elgin.

As for whether Luke lived or died? That was plainly outside his duties. No need to concern himself with it.

However, Gregori did feel some pressure about confronting the Great Swordsman Elgin. He had heard that this man could instantly slaughter countless Saint-tier undead?

If that was true, Gregori felt he needed to go all out and properly exercise his aging bones to take him down.

Gregori was wrapped in a black robe, guarding against his surroundings.

Despite the waves of cheers from the citizens, it was still impossible to mask the undercurrents surging — crises lurking at every turn.

In a certain corner, Grace slowly removed her hood, letting her crimson long hair cascade loose.

The skull staff in her hand began glowing with a sinister red light, as if coming alive.

Grace's eyes locked onto Luke in the carriage, her expression unconsciously beginning to twist into a vicious grimace as she gritted her teeth —

"That bastard is the Great Swordsman Elgin, right?"

"I've finally found you."

"The murderer who took my beloved—"

(▼皿▼#)

title: Chapter 22 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 22 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 10 · Chapter 22

Milius glanced at the smug figure and couldn’t help but curl his lip. "Tch! A worthless piece of trash basking in cheers like some hero—doesn’t that seem a bit ridiculous?"

Winifred’s expression turned uneasy. He muttered, "Milius, we’re on a mission. It’s best not to let personal feelings get involved."

"So what if we’re on a mission? I’m not going out of my way to cause trouble, but watching this garbage prance around really pisses me off. If it weren’t for his good-for-nothing father, what would he even amount to in front of me?" Milius laced his fingers behind his head, lazily sprawled out. "Ah~ I hope the real Elgin the Great Swordsman hurries up and cuts this fraud down. That’d make me feel a little better~"

"Enough already, stop saying things that make people sick." Mesfield’s mood soured the moment Milius brought up Elgin the Great Swordsman. "Luke’s at least on our side. Elgin the Great Swordsman is the enemy. What kind of mindset is it to wish for Luke’s death?"

"So what if I can’t stand him? Are you trying to censor my mouth now? Don’t make me laugh." Milius narrowed his eyes, clearly annoyed by Mesfield’s meddling.

"We just need to complete the mission His Majesty assigned us. Nothing else is our concern. Don’t go around spouting things that might incite the others." Mesfield spoke sternly, trying to shut Milius up.

"Oh? If I could incite you lot, would I still be wasting my breath here?" Milius remained unyielding, refusing to back down even an inch.

....Mesfield’s eyes flickered with a hint of anger. She strongly disapproved of Milius mixing personal feelings into their duty.

"Milius isn’t entirely—"

Morrison, who usually didn’t get along with Milius, suddenly spoke up. His unexpected support left Mesfield even more confused.

"Oh? Rare for you to agree with me~" Milius smirked, shooting a provocative glance at Mesfield.

"Morrison, what are you saying?!" Mesfield was clearly displeased. She hadn’t expected Morrison to take Milius’s side at a time like this.

"...Just stating the truth. As a knight, I find a powerless man like Luke disgusting. And we’re even helping him cover it up—makes us look like accomplices." Morrison paused before continuing, "I find the whole thing humiliating."

....Mesfield froze. She could sense it too, but she just couldn’t bring herself to say it out loud. Morrison was being too blunt.

"Hah! See, Mesfield? Even the usually honest Morrison thinks I’m right. Don’t you want to see that trash Luke bleed out in front of you?" Milius’s hand unconsciously drifted toward his sword hilt.

"Shut up!" Mesfield was getting angry now. If this kept up, she wouldn’t be able to control these Thorn Knights at all. "Don’t forget your positions! We are knights of Her Majesty the Queen! Defying Her Majesty’s will is treason—punishable by death!"

Milius and Morrison immediately fell silent, staring at Mesfield’s serious expression. She clearly wasn’t joking.

Treason meant only one thing—death.

Seeing that they’d both quieted down, Mesfield said earnestly, "Our only task is to ensure Luke’s safety. No more discussing anything else!"

"Don’t be so serious, we were just joking, little Windsor~" Milius flashed a grin, instantly diffusing the tension.

"Don’t call me by my name!" Mesfield snapped coldly.

"...Fine, fine, don’t get so worked up." Milius replied awkwardly.

Morrison chose to stay silent, not wanting to provoke Mesfield any further. She was terrifying when angry.

Winifred, who had been zoning out, happened to catch a glimpse of a suspicious figure—Gracie—lurking in the shadow of an alley. Her questionable attire drew his attention.

"We shouldn’t be arguing like this. Keep an eye on our surroundings."

"This town..."

"Seems to have more hidden dragons and crouching tigers than we thought."

At the very rear of the ornate carriage stood a pockmarked man with shifty eyes. He gave off the vibe of a scheming opportunist, not a decent bone in his body.

This man was Luke’s only confidant in the area, as well as the one person he trusted most.

The pockmarked man served the Overle family and had been assigned to attend to Young Master Luke’s daily needs. His strength was high-tier.

As Luke’s sole confidant, the pockmarked man naturally took it upon himself to ensure Luke’s safety. Hearing the earlier argument among the Thorn Knights, he couldn’t resist sneaking forward to report.

"Young Master, those Thorn Knights are really unhappy with you. Seems like they’re all hoping the real Great Swordsman shows up and chops you to pieces."

Luke had been smiling and waving at the crowd, but upon hearing his confidant’s report, his smile froze on his face.

"You heard that clearly?"

"Absolutely, sir. If it weren’t for the Queen keeping them in line, they’d have probably walked off the job already!" the pockmarked man said seriously.

"Tch!" Luke’s face twisted in irritation, his expression ugly as he muttered, "No matter. Given the current situation, those Thorn Knights wouldn’t dare let me die so easily. I’m the Overle family’s only son. If I die, the royal capital will have to face the full might of the Overle family’s private army! My father won’t spare a single member of the royal family—not even the Queen’s lapdogs!"

"You’re right, Young Master." The pockmarked man nodded obsequiously, echoing Luke’s words.

"Let those Thorn Knights bark for now. Once our family’s power grows to the point where even the royals can’t touch us, the entire empire will change hands. All the water and land will belong to the Overle family. What’s a mere kingdom’s army? Their outdated equipment is already obsolete—how could they compare to our family’s private forces?" Luke’s face twisted with a cruel, smug grin. "If it comes to war... in just thirty days, the Overle family’s elite troops will be at the palace walls."

"Whoa~" The pockmarked man’s eyes widened in shock and disbelief. "We’re already that powerful?"

"Of course. Our expanded private army is made up of elite mercenaries—every single one a hardened veteran who’s tasted blood on the battlefield. How could they possibly compare to those pampered royal soldiers?" Luke paused, then added with a hint of regret, "Though our organization isn’t fully formed yet. We need time to consolidate. Once everything’s ready... I will be the prince of a new empire~"

The pockmarked man looked worried and ventured cautiously, "But the kingdom has the Twelve Thorn Knights defending it. Even with the Ninth Knight dead, there are still eleven Saint-tier powerhouses left. Each of them has the strength to fight ten thousand men... won’t they be hard to deal with?"

"Hahahaha, ridiculous! Do you think our family has been sitting idle? We’ve been planning this rebellion for three years already. We’ve already won over seven top-tier powerhouses—four of whom are none other than the legendary Elemental Four Sword Saints!" Luke stroked his chin proudly as he spoke.

"The Elemental Four Sword Saints?!" The pockmarked man was confused—he’d never heard of them before.

"Hah, it’s normal you don’t know them. The Elemental Four Sword Saints are reclusive legends. They’ve been training on a drifting island in the Chaotic Seas this whole time and almost never set foot in human lands." Luke stroked his chin, recalling. "I once heard..."

"The combined power of the Elemental Four Sword Saints can easily slay the Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace."

(~V~)

title: Chapter 23 — Monthly Patron Update
content:
Chapter 23 — Monthly Patron Update

Volume 10 · Chapter 23

The scarred man had never heard of the Four Elemental Sword Saints, but he was absolutely familiar with the legend of the First Demon Lord Palace’s Great Demon Lord.

That demon—who, decades ago, had wiped out ten thousand elite Crusade Army soldiers with a single wave—still terrified the human world to this day!

Humans instinctively felt an overwhelming fear, trembling at the land across the Aokuni Strait, dreading that the demons of the Death Swamp would burst out and begin slaughtering them, eventually achieving dominance.

Of course, these were just the lies the Holy Church’s priests had been spreading. The truth wasn’t nearly as exaggerated.

In reality, the 233 Crusade Army forces Merlin had cut down weren’t particularly strong to begin with. The Church had lost so many men that their manpower and finances were now depleted, leaving them far weaker than before. Who would still fund the Church if humanity no longer had a common enemy?

When money was involved, even if the Church stubbornly persisted, it was like blindly letting an arrow pierce their knee—becoming a threat to all of humanity.

But as the First Demon Lord Palace’s Great Demon Lord, Merlin was unfortunately in a much more dangerous position.

Just thinking about the rumors surrounding the First Demon Lord Palace’s Great Demon Lord made the scarred man’s face pale with fear, his bones trembling uncontrollably. In the Death Swamp now, those cold corpses—those ten thousand elite Crusade knights—must already have been devoured by demons, reduced to nothing but frozen bones, right?

The scarred man swallowed nervously, stammering, “Th-that Four Elemental Sword Saint… could he really… kill the Great Demon Lord?”

“Great Demon Lord?!” Luke hesitated for a moment before speaking indifferently, “Killing the First Demon Lord Palace’s Great Demon Lord isn’t impossible, but if he’s a recluse over a hundred years old, a Saint-tier elder… his combat strength might cause real trouble.”

The scarred man was still cautious. “Master, you can’t say things like that lightly! If we underestimate the enemy, won’t Britain just become a prize in their hands?”

“You don’t need to worry about that,” Luke said. “The Four Elemental Sword Saint’s strength—my father once told me that in their prime, the Four Elemental Sword Saints were legendary figures. Even the Nine Kings of the United Kingdom dared not provoke them. Later, for some reason, they chose to retire, standing on the side of the Overley family in the Chaos Sea’s Drifting Island, which will definitely become our family’s ultimate trump card.”

“Now, if they unite, how powerful would they be?! But I’m glad they’re on our side as allies rather than enemies. This Four Elemental Sword Saint is already terrifying enough!”

The scarred man’s face twisted in shock. From what Luke said, the Four Elemental Sword Saints were figures whose names alone carried weight. Even the Nine Kings of the United Kingdom were incredibly powerful—like the Flame Saint Dragon and other legendary beings, such as the immortal Elf King and the Six Great Dragon Sword Saints. Their strength had clearly reached an unimaginable level.

These powerful figures wouldn’t lightly provoke such an existence. If these four could easily slay the First Demon Lord Palace’s Great Demon Lord, their current strength must be beyond comprehension.

But why, in their prime, did they choose to retire?

“Master, may I ask—since these four Sword Saints say they retired because they were too powerful and felt deep loneliness…”

“I’m not entirely sure,” Luke said with a mysterious smile. “But I heard my father mutter something about how only peak-level warriors could understand such things—it has nothing to do with us.”

“Yes, yes, yes,” the scarred man nodded repeatedly, feeling that the world of those strong beings was beyond his comprehension. Their reason for retiring was truly admirable.

But if the Four Elemental Sword Saints retired because they were too invincible and felt lonely… that made sense to the scarred man. “So Master, you’re saying we’re lucky to have such a powerful ally?”

“Money?” Luke raised an eyebrow in surprise. “You think we could hire someone like the Four Elemental Sword Saints with money?”

The scarred man blinked, realizing he’d never considered that.

“Oh? So Master’s father has a strong connection with them?”

“When my father was young, he once helped the Four Elemental Sword Saints,” Luke said proudly.

If money could hire someone like that, it would be too easy. It seems the empire is about to change hands.

The scarred man raised his thumb in approval, flattering, “It’s as if the gods are secretly aiding Duke Overley!”

“Of course,” Luke said coldly. “Those Thorn Knights? They’re nothing in front of the Four Elemental Sword Saints. Killing them would take no time at all.”

When the time comes, the empress and her daughter—those who dared resist the Overley family—will have their bones hung on the palace walls for all to see, declaring the fall of the royal bloodline. As for the queen’s remaining allure…

The scarred man suddenly understood, his expression shifting. “So when the time comes, the high-and-mighty empress will become the most wretched woman in the empire?”

“Exactly,” Luke said with a smirk.

The grand procession moved slowly forward, the crimson thistle flags waving as the crowd nodded in greeting.

Luke, seated in the luxurious carriage, waved and smiled at the cheering crowds, the deafening roar shaking the ground.

The girl fans erupted in shouts of “I love you!” and other nonsense, making Merlin—who was just a fake—feel incredibly awkward. Their eyes were sparkling, clearly in a state of excitement.

As for Alice and Lucy, seeing their idol, they immediately turned to Merlin and said, “Little brother, look at your wife! Don’t you dare let her go!”

“Tsk tsk tsk,” Piers watched Alice and clicked his tongue, finding her adorable when she cursed, but now? Her soul was practically being devoured by that sight. If he were in Merlin’s position, he wouldn’t be able to resist either.

Elgin the Great Sword Saint had been stolen away—this was the thrill of being cuckolded, and Piers felt a slight irritation, almost wanting to swing his sword at Merlin.

Merlin rolled his eyes and ignored him, though he did feel a little bothered by the fake.

The other girls had no connection to Merlin, and he had no interest in them either. Alice, however, was different—she was his wife in name, if not in reality.

But Alice was clearly different. No matter how you looked at it, she was in a state of high excitement, looking utterly smug.

Merlin glanced at the smug fake on the carriage, wondering who the hell he thought he was, comparing himself to him?

Damn it, was Alice blind? This fraud couldn’t even begin to match up to the real Elgin the Great Sword Saint!

And as he thought about the consequences of his actions, a sudden deafening roar split the air—like thunder.

Merlin narrowed his eyes, debating whether to step in, when a voice boomed across the crowd:

“Elgin the Great Sword Saint!”

“I’ve been waiting for you for a long time…”

title: Chapter 24 — Come to Fight
content:
Chapter 24 — Come to Fight

Volume 10 · Chapter 24

Uncle Carl suddenly charged into the fray, blocking the进程 of the Bauhinia Knight Order's parade procession.

He spoke with a voice like thunder, directly provoking Luke on the carriage, eager to settle things with a fight.

Carl was the kind of person who was practically obsessed with battle, unable to restrain his desire to spar whenever he encountered a strong opponent.

Besides, Uncle Carl treated his daughter Lucia like the apple of his eye.

Thinking back to Lucia's childhood, the phrase she said most often was that she loved her dad the most.

Uncle Carl had always considered himself his daughter's hero, so he was especially careful about his image.

But now that Lucia had grown up, she no longer seemed as adorable as she used to be, and treated her father Carl with a lukewarm indifference.

Worse still, Lucia had now fallen under the spell of Elgin the Great Swordmaster — he was no longer the hero in his daughter's heart.

How could Uncle Carl possibly accept such a thing? His heart turned icy cold, and he desperately wanted to thrash Elgin the Great Swordmaster right in front of his daughter, using facts to prove who was the hero worth relying on.

The vanguard of the knight order immediately came to a halt. The cavalry horses at the front whinnied loudly, and the entire parade procession fell into slight disarray.

"Presumptuous! Who are you?! How dare you interfere with the Bauhinia Knight Order's parade formation!"

Chapman, who was serving as the squad leader among them and had been leading the cavalry contingent this time, was startled by Uncle Carl's sudden appearance.

A group of his subordinates around him drew their cavalry swords, their expressions grim, looking ready to fight fiercely.

Commoners who dared to block an advancing procession would likely be绞死, so whoever dared to step forward must have been a tough nut to crack.

"Hey, don't be so worked up~" Uncle Carl grinned, his white teeth dazzlingly bright. "I'm not deliberately looking for trouble. I just want to spar with this Hero of the Empire. I have no intention of causing chaos."

Most of Rexham's residents knew Carl, so the moment they saw him blocking the parade procession and challenging Elgin the Great Swordmaster, they erupted into chatter, unable to hold back their discussions —

"Did I hear that right? Is Carl going to challenge Elgin the Great Swordmaster?"

"Carl wouldn't joke about something like this. He seems to be serious."

"This is going to be good. But I'm backing Carl — after all, he's Rexham's own star!"

The gathered crowd began to stir restlessly, and even the Bauhinia Knight Order in the parade drew their weapons, preparing for battle.

The atmosphere suddenly grew tense, with an edge of swords drawn at any moment. It seemed like a single misstep could set things off.

"Oh man...." Price instantly covered his darkening face and said awkwardly, "How could Mr. Carl cause trouble at a time like this? The Bauhinia Knight Order is no pushover. What should we do? If a real fight breaks out, my hard-earned salary will vanish into thin air!"

Merlin watched Price trembling beside him and thought: Is it really that bad? Carl was always someone easily swept away by battle lust. He had long been shouting about wanting to spar with Elgin the Great Swordmaster, and now he had actually followed through — already charging in.

But Merlin did not step forward to stop him. Instead, a faint smile appeared on his face, because the current situation was extremely advantageous for him.

If Uncle Carl challenged the fake Elgin the Great Swordmaster and thoroughly beat the impostor, wouldn't all these lies collapse on their own?!

Merlin stroked his chin and chuckled mischievously, already unable to wait and see how this group would dig themselves out of this mess.

"What... what is Mr. Carl doing?!" Alice stared with wide eyes, covering her mouth in surprise, finding it hard to believe.

"Huh!" Lucia's expression shifted from astonishment to irritation. "What is that idiot father thinking?! Why is he challenging Elgin the Great Swordmaster?!"

Alice remained silent, thinking: Isn't this obvious? Isn't it because Lucia has been talking about Elgin the Great Swordmaster non-stop lately, making Mr. Carl feel insecure?

"Stupid dad! Come back right now! Stop causing trouble for others!" Lucia waved her thin arms and immediately started scolding her father.

Several dark lines dripped down Alice's forehead, and she couldn't help but think inwardly: Lucia, mind your own image a little — this is embarassment incarnate.

Hearing his daughter scolding him from the crowd, Uncle Carl's entire aura deflated like a punctured balloon. But to prove he was still a reliable father, he stubbornly persisted in wanting to fight Elgin the Great Swordmaster.

"Everyone stand down. My opponent is Elgin the Great Swordmaster. I do not wish to injure any of you."

Before the words had even finished echoing, battle energy erupted from Uncle Carl's body, rolling like golden lightning, looking utterly intimidating!

That formidable Saint-tier pressure placed immense stress on the cavalrymen in the front ranks, making it hard for some to breathe as cold sweats of shock poured down their faces.

Even the well-trained horses at the front, which had been composed until now, began to grow restless, pawing the ground in panic with their hooves.

Facing a Saint-tier powerhouse, Chapman's气势 immediately weakened. It was only then that he carefully took in Uncle Carl's appearance — and when he saw the Mithril Adventurer certification around his neck, he felt this was going to be a tremendous hassle. < = =

"Sir, please do not disrupt our parade plans. If you wish to spar with Elgin the Great Swordmaster, please do so through proper channels, rather than forcibly blocking our path."

Chapman's tone had become polite, standing firm but no longer lofty and condescending as before. He was attempting to negotiate with Uncle Carl.

The other party was a Saint-tier powerhouse, and neither his status nor his strength was something Chapman could handle lightly. He would have to await the Thorn Knight's orders.

"We won't delay you for long. It'll be over soon...." Uncle Carl looked up at Luke, whose face had turned green on the carriage. "Hey! Elgin the Great Swordmaster! Weren't you so strong? Come down and let's spar!"

Luke's expression on the carriage grew increasingly dark. Everything had been smooth sailing up until now, and he never expected to hit a snag in Rexham — this was truly bad luck.

Luke definitely did not want to go down and spar with Uncle Carl, because as a low-tier warrior, there was no way he could defeat a Saint-tier powerhouse. He would be crushed into the ground, and when that happened, his secret of impersonating Elgin the Great Swordmaster would be exposed — not to mention his family's reputation would suffer.

Luke's eyes darted nervously, unable to meet Uncle Carl's combat-ready gaze. For a moment, he did not know how to handle the situation.

The onlookers seemed to be waiting for Elgin the Great Swordmaster's response. Many of them began to grow suspicious —

Wasn't Elgin the Great Swordmaster incredibly powerful? Why didn't he even dare to accept Carl's challenge? Was this really the same Hero who had instantly defeated countless strong enemies?

The murmurs occasionally rose from the crowd, and many people started growing suspicious, feeling that Luke's cowering behavior looked terrible.

"....Young master, what should we do?" the pockmarked man quickly asked, anxiously breaking into a cold sweat. "If this continues, you'll be looked down upon."

"Stay calm. We'll choose to evade...." Luke responded quietly, then stepped to the front, putting on a look of disdain and arrogance.

"What a pity — I am too powerful."

"Someone with your level of strength is not even worthy of sparring with me!"

title: Chapter 25 — Monthly Vote Bonus
content:
Chapter 25 — Monthly Vote Bonus

Volume 10 · Chapter 25

Merlin had been in a pretty good mood, watching Luke’s antics with amusement.

But Luke’s arrogant words left Merlin feeling distinctly uneasy.

How could this guy be so smooth with his bragging? Was he afraid of getting his ass handed to him in front of everyone and losing face? Merlin’s expression grew stiff, and he started to find Luke a bit disgusting. Admitting he wasn’t the legendary Elgin Blade Master wouldn’t kill him, but now he was just forcing it.

Luke lifted his chin haughtily, his tone dripping with superiority. “Besides, I’m a knight of the Thistle Knights now. There’s no reason for me to spar with someone like you—a commoner. And frankly, your strength doesn’t even pique my interest.”

Luke dared to say this because he had plenty of people protecting him. The Thistle Knights would go all out to shield him, and they certainly wouldn’t want his true identity exposed—otherwise, they’d all be finished together.

Right now, the Overley family and the royal family were tied by the same thread—if one fell, they all fell.

So Luke had no reason to risk himself by sparring with Uncle Karl. Let those Thistle Knights handle it.

And with that legendary Golden Adventurer Guildmaster watching in secret, he was in a position of absolute safety. He could just keep flexing.

“Hmph!”

Uncle Karl sneered, his brows knitting in fury. The nerve of this guy, looking down on him just because he was the head of the Adventurers Guild.

Uncle Karl wasn’t the type to back down easily. The more challenging the opponent, the more it stirred his fighting spirit.

“Your mouth’s pretty big, isn’t it? If you’re not brave enough to spar with me, then you’re just a fraud looking for fame. A real strongman wouldn’t even hesitate to accept my challenge. Or are you even the real Elgin Blade Master?”

His words made the crowd even more doubtful. Everyone thought Karl was the more dominant one, while this Elgin Blade Master seemed cowardly.

All those legends about Elgin’s strength—if he was really that powerful, why wouldn’t he accept Karl’s challenge?

And this was Rekserum, Karl’s hometown. Even if Elgin had more fame, he couldn’t compare to Karl’s personal reputation.

“This Elgin Blade Master looks kinda weak, huh?”

“Yeah, something’s off. He can take down two Thistle Knights with one swing, but he won’t even accept Karl’s challenge.”

“Maybe this Elgin Blade Master is fake? I thought he was fat, and that already seemed suspicious.”

More and more people started doubting Elgin, murmuring among themselves. Clearly, something wasn’t right.

“Hmm?” Luciya furrowed her brows, frowning. “Why is this Elgin Blade Master being so cautious? My dad couldn’t possibly win against him.”

Alice stayed silent, her thoughts swirling. This Luke—was he really the Elgin Blade Master? Last year, he’d been so reckless and bold, but now he seemed hesitant. Could it be because he’d become a royal knight?

“No way, Elgin Blade Master is supposed to be strong, right? Why won’t he even accept Mr. Karl’s challenge?” Price sounded exasperated.

Merlin couldn’t help but smirk, his mood lightening. Uncle Karl was doing a good job. Sometimes, that simple-minded brute wasn’t so bad.

“Tsk.” Luke could hear the whispers of doubt around him and grew flustered. If things kept going like this, even if he did nothing, trouble would still find him. “Fake? What nonsense! I just don’t deign to waste my time on a weakling like you!”

“Pretty words anyone can say.” Karl beckoned him over, taunting. “If you still consider yourself a man, come down and fight me!”

Luke’s face darkened with anger, but he couldn’t lash out. He glared at the Thistle Knights, willing them to step in—if they didn’t, his fake identity would be exposed, and they’d all be finished.

The four Thistle Knights behind him already knew what was happening, but they stayed out of it, choosing to watch.

If possible, they didn’t want to cause a scene in public—it would be hard to clean up. But now, if they didn’t intervene, the situation would only get worse, and they’d have no way to explain it to Queen Venefred.

Venefred frowned. “What do we do now?”

“This…” Mesfield pinched his brows, looking annoyed. “Damn it, Rekserum’s adventurers are always causing trouble. They love stirring things up everywhere.”

Morrison stayed silent, recalling that in the capital, he’d met a black-iron adventurer named Merlin—also from Rekserum—who seemed pretty strong. Adventurers were weird enough, but Rekserum’s seemed especially odd. Even a black-iron could be that powerful.

“Who’s going to handle that silver adventurer?” Mesfield glanced at the others. “We can’t let him keep this up—it’s a threat to our plans.”

“I’m not bothering,” Millius replied lazily, showing no intention of helping.

Venefred stayed silent, just as uninterested in assisting.

Both of them still resented the way they’d been set up by Luke. As long as he didn’t die, they wouldn’t lift a finger.

“Tsk.” Mesfield clicked his tongue, finding the situation annoying. “Fine, I’ll go.”

Just as he took a step forward, Morrison pulled him back.

“Let me handle this silver adventurer. You’re the first knight—it wouldn’t look good if you just stepped in casually.”

“Uh…” Mesfield’s expression twisted slightly. “Then… I’ll leave it to you.”

“Perfect. I’ve always been curious about Rekserum’s adventurers.”

Morrison put on his gloves and strode forward, standing in front of Karl.

Luke finally allowed himself a smirk. Of course, they’d step in to help. These Thistle Knights weren’t stupid, huh?

Merlin frowned slightly, studying Morrison. There was something familiar about him—then it clicked. Wasn’t this guy the seventh Thistle Knight who’d arm-wrestled him? Now he was guarding this fake Blade Master?

“Oh? I’m looking for Elgin Blade Master, not you Thistle Knights.” Karl’s face darkened. “Can’t you just mind your own business?”

“Sorry, but Elgin Blade Master is now part of the Thistle Knights. I can’t just stand by and watch.” And I don’t even need him to step in—I’ll handle you myself.

Hidden in the shadows, Grace’s smile twisted into something grotesque, her whole body trembling with excitement. Bloodshot veins pulsed in her eyes—

Fight!

Let them fight!

The more chaos, the better. Then I can strike—

And kill Elgin Blade Master, that wicked criminal, once and for all.

title: Chapter 26 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 26 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 10 · Chapter 26

The shadowy figure of Grace hesitated to act, clearly weighing her own concerns.

There were four Thorn Knights guarding the team, each a Saint-tier powerhouse.

This put Grace under immense pressure—killing Luke under the watchful eyes of four Thorn Knights would be difficult and risky, and any reckless move would leave her paying a devastating price.

After learning of Swinburn’s death, Grace had investigated the killer, only to find the culprit’s name splashed across the newspapers. She had finally tracked down the Great Swordmaster Elgin, and she certainly didn’t want all her efforts to go to waste—or to risk her own life in the process.

So Grace was now acting with extreme caution, refusing to strike unless she was certain of success.

Just as she was struggling to find an opening against the four Thorn Knights’ defenses, Uncle Carl unexpectedly came to her aid.

As long as those two brutes fought, chaos would erupt, giving her the perfect opportunity. When everyone was distracted, Grace would unleash a devastating magical assault on Luke, aiming to obliterate him instantly!

Grace’s Saint-tier magic surged within her, preparing for a strike so swift it would leave no time for reaction—to finish off the so-called “Great Swordmaster Elgin”!

“Tsk,” Merlin clicked his tongue, annoyed. *Thorn Knights are such a pain—why do they keep complicating things?*

“Oh! Mr. Carl is about to fight the Thorn Knights—all of them are martial artists. This should be fun!” Price stroked his beard, finding the prospect amusing.

Meanwhile, Lucy groaned and rubbed her temples, her face dark with frustration. “I can’t stand this idiot of a father. Why provoke the Thorn Knights? And of course, it’ll be Grandpa who has to clean up the mess!”

“Calm down, Lucy,” Alice comforted her.

Uncle Carl, facing Morrison’s challenge, naturally had no fear. He had come to stir trouble, and it didn’t matter who he fought.

“Alright, you asked for it. Don’t come crying to me when things go south.”

Uncle Carl didn’t hesitate, slipping on his black iron knuckle-dusters, their glow radiating an eerie mystery.

“Don’t think just because you’re older you can beat me. Let me tell you, I’ve beaten plenty of old-timers like you—you’re nothing special.” Morrison adjusted his weapon to perfection, barely containing his battle lust.

“Hmph! I love fighting tough-talking fools. I’ve heard Thorn Knights are all top-tier, so today I’ll test that theory.”

Uncle Carl’s words barely finished when golden lightning battle energy erupted from his body, roaring like a wild beast snarling at its enemy.

Morrison wasn’t to be outdone—his own battle energy surged, his skin turning a fiery crimson, like scorched steel, twisted into a grotesque, demonic visage.

Without hesitation, Morrison activated the first layer of his *Rakshasa* technique, his abilities doubling as his body transformed into a weapon in an instant.

“Roar!”

Both Saint-tier warriors bellowed, slamming into each other head-on, their fists crashing with enough force to vanish from sight. A violent storm erupted, crashing over the onlookers like a tidal wave, sending them sprawling.

Carl and Morrison were both formidable martial artists—direct clashes meant brutal physical collisions. The crackling lightning energy and the volatile crimson aura clashed violently, neither willing to yield.

Their fists flew straight for each other’s foreheads, each desperate to shatter the other’s skull. This wasn’t sparring—it was a full-blown battle, a clash of titans.

But just as everyone expected an explosive collision—something impossible happened.

A black hole suddenly appeared in front of both men, swirling like a vortex.

Their fists plunged into the abyss—and then reemerged, striking their own faces with crushing force.

The sight was surreal—each man was punching himself. The entire space twisted unnaturally, as if their fists had been warped back to attack them.

“Ugh!”

Carl and Morrison staggered back, their faces already contorted from the blows.

Merlin frowned, baffled. *What kind of magic is that?* That black hole—it seemed to warp space itself, sending their own attacks back against them! And the magic’s pressure was overwhelming, clearly the work of a powerful figure.

Alice was just as stunned, her eyes darting around. *Could it be…?* The capital’s Guildmaster had come too? The same man who had saved her not long ago?

“…What the hell was that just now?” Lucy muttered to herself.

Luke’s brow furrowed, his back slick with cold sweat. *A single spell just dropped two Saint-tier warriors?* That purple-gold Adventurer was no joke—he was a true powerhouse! If the Four Elemental Sword Saints faced this Guildmaster, their chances of victory would be slim at best!

If rumors were true and Gregory had close ties with the Year Clan, that would be the biggest obstacle to the Overley family’s ambitions!

Luke’s instincts flared, his wariness toward the elusive Gregory intensifying. With this man in the capital, the plan for regime change would face serious resistance.

“That’s black hole magic… quite the oddity,” Millius mused, his eyes narrowed.

“No wonder they still sing his praises in the royal court after 400 years. He’s a legend,” Winifred sighed in admiration.

…Mesfield had nothing to say. *This level of power is ridiculous.* And that black hole magic—why was it so bizarre? It toyed with Saint-tier warriors as if they were nothing. No wonder the king had summoned him. Maybe he could truly take down the real Elgin…

Morrison clutched his swollen face, stunned. He had been struck by his own fist—how? But he couldn’t deny the shock of Gregory’s power. He hadn’t even seen the attack coming before he was sent flying.

Carl sucked in a breath, his hand pressed to his face. He slowly looked up, his eyes widening as he saw a hunched figure in a black cloak, a staff in hand, approaching. The wobbling purple-gold Adventurer’s badge around the old man’s neck was just visible enough to reveal his identity.

…Gregory…

“Your lightning-like battle energy—you’re the Taylor boy, aren’t you?” Gregory’s voice was rough, gravelly.

Grace, hidden in the shadows, broke out in a cold sweat. She quickly pulled up her hood and turned to leave, her eyes flickering with terror.

*Why?*

*Why did this parade attract a purple-gold monster?*

Adventurers were supposed to stay out of political strife!

No—she couldn’t act now. She’d be obliterated instantly!

She’d retreat for now. Wait until nightfall, when the city was quiet, and then finish Elgin for good.

(End)

title: Chapter 27 — Dementia
content:
Chapter 27 — Dementia

Volume 10 · Chapter 27

After a series of disturbances, the Purple Mist Flower Knights' parade in Rexthem finally came to an end.

Since they were both adventurers, and Gregory got along well with Elder Taylor, he went to visit the guild in Rexthem.

At this time, in the Rexthem guild, many adventurers who had temporarily lost interest in Elkin the Great Swordsman were instead directly coming to gawk at Gregory.

Gregory was a magician filled with legendary tales. He had served as a court magician's advisor when the empire was first established, and after leaving the royal family, he became a famous purple-gold adventurer. To ordinary people, this was already quite glorious.

Many adventurers didn't leave, but instead drank wine while watching Gregory and Elder Taylor's table.

The relationships between guilds were very delicate. They were colleagues, but due to absolute competitive relationships, they often snatched each other's business.

After all, everyone needed to develop. The stronger the guild, the more commissions they received, which directly affected their own interests.

Gregory, as the guildmaster of the capital's Adventurers Guild, although friends with Elder Taylor, was still in a state of opposition.

At this moment, the two guildmasters sat facing each other chatting, like old friends reunited.

"Long time no see, Taylor. I remember the last time we met was ten years ago. You've aged quite a bit too..." Gregory's voice was hoarse, sounding somewhat like an old bellows wheezing.

"I'm not the same as you. Time spares no one." Elder Taylor sighed, then continued, "But speaking of which, why didn't you let me know in advance when you came to Rexthem? I could have come to meet you."

"No need for such formalities. I'm here on the queen's commission, otherwise I wouldn't have had the chance to come to Rexthem." Gregory said in a deep voice. "If it weren't for seeing your kid causing trouble on the street, I probably wouldn't have come to visit."

Getting involved with the Thorn Knight-like situation would only cause trouble. When Gregory saw Carl and Morrison fighting on the street, he stepped in to stop it out of friendship with Elder Taylor, to prevent things from escalating.

"Oh? The queen's commission? It must be about Elkin the Great Swordsman, right?" Elder Taylor narrowed his eyes, seeming to have some suspicions.

"Did you guess that?" Gregory was surprised.

Elder Taylor deliberately lowered his voice, speaking only the two of them could hear, "That point... is fake Elkin the Great Swordsman. Although he performed defeating two Thorn Knights, that sword technique was just child's play, with no hint of a strongman's aura, not matching the rumors about Elkin the Great Swordsman at all."

"Hahaha, your eyes are still as sharp as before..." Gregory laughed, his frail old body shaking.

"You're accepting the queen's commission, aren't you interfering in politics? We adventurers have strict rules, absolutely not allowed to get involved in political conflicts." Elder Taylor tried to remind Gregory.

"No problem. I'm acting in my personal capacity, with no relation to the Adventurers Guild." Gregory said casually, seemingly not taking the rules seriously.

"You're no longer a court magician anymore, is it worth taking such a big risk?" Elder Taylor's expression became strange, feeling that although Gregory was an adventurer, he always seemed to serve the royal family.

"This is only natural. When I was still weak, I was taken in by the empire's first king Egbert, who showed me great kindness. So I think about repaying that kindness to the king's descendants within my ability." Gregory said leisurely.

"You're already so old, yet still so emotional?" Elder Taylor said with a helpless expression.

"Not talking about this..." Gregory waved his hand dismissively, looking around and saying, "Your guild is developing well, seems like there's a strong will to strive?"

"Of course. I'm always fantasizing about surpassing the capital's guild, wanting my guild to rank ahead of yours." Elder Taylor said meaningfully.

"Hahaha, that's interesting..." Gregory suddenly laughed, saying calmly, "Leaving aside the huge gap between your Rexthem guild and mine, even Wales' first guild wouldn't give you a seat. The dominant guild in Wales is the Addalf Guild. If you want to surpass me, you first need to cross the big mountain in front of you."

"Becoming Wales' number one guild is just a matter of time for us." Elder Taylor said confidently.

"Where did you get such confidence? The Addalf Adventurers Guild is full of talented people, and there are plenty of troublesome characters." Gregory paused, then added, "Moreover, what does it matter if you become Wales' first? Our guild is located in the capital, with absolutely insurmountable advantages. I advise you not to have too many expectations."

"To be honest, we've recruited a very powerful new person, with an unlimited future. They might make you drop your jaw." Elder Taylor said proudly, his pale eyebrows lifting.

"Oh? A new person? Which new recruit?" Gregory asked curiously. Someone who could make Elder Taylor so concerned must be quite outstanding.

"Right over there." Elder Taylor pointed with his finger, secretly indicating the distant Merlin and Alice, but actually pointing only at Merlin.

Gregory didn't know who Elder Taylor was pointing at, but he noticed the two people.

Because of the black iron adventurer's certificate hanging from Merlin's neck, it wouldn't attract his attention, so he was simply ignored.

Gregory carefully examined Alice, scrutinizing her, then his eyes lit up, thinking this girl was not ordinary.

He remembered the last time they met in the capital, he had even saved Alice. At that time she was just a high-ranking adventurer, and in the short time since, she had already become a Saint-tier powerhouse.

Moreover, she was practicing both magic and martial arts with extreme difficulty, her combat strength far exceeding expectations, and seemed to have some rather unusual powers.

This talent was quite good. No wonder Elder Taylor was so proud. With proper cultivation and training, she would absolutely become the pillar of a guild.

After Gregory finished examining her, he retracted his gaze and slightly nodded, saying, "This girl is indeed good, with excellent talent. Her dual cultivation in magic and martial arts will make her combat strength far surpass ordinary people. I feel she also has some dragon's breath, I wonder if she has some connection with the dragon race?"

Elder Taylor was taken aback when he heard the girl was mentioned, but he wasn't talking about Alice, it was the golden-haired man beside her!

"Not her, but the golden-haired man beside her. He's our guild's biggest catch."

"Huh?"

Gregory turned his head to look, re-examining Merlin, and found no pressure at all, just like an ordinary person.

Combined with the black iron adventurer's certificate on his neck, it was simply someone at the very bottom of the guild, nothing unusual at all.
