Gregory turned his head back to look at Elder Taylor, and his mood became a bit complicated, filled with disbelief.

Is this guy already suffering from senile dementia?

This black-iron young man is the new person with an unlimited future?

What a joke. It gave me goosebumps all over.

(Kiss)

title: Chapter 27 — Monthly Patron Update
content:
Chapter 27 — Monthly Patron Update

Volume 10 · Chapter 27

Gregory couldn’t help but ask in exasperation, “You’re not joking, right?”

“Of course not,” Old Tyler replied seriously. “That man’s name is Merlin. Don’t let his black iron adventurer rank fool you—he’s incredibly strong.”

Gregory let out a dry chuckle, thinking to himself that someone of Merlin’s caliber would never be accepted by his guild, yet Old Tyler treated him like a treasure. Had the Adventurers Guild of Raxum really degenerated this far?

At a table in the distance, Merlin and Alice were also targeting Gregory.

“That old man’s magic is a bit weird,” Merlin remarked casually.

“Black hole magic, you know? A lot of people find it strange—no one knows where he learned it from. Rumor has it many have fallen for it,” Alice added, still admiring Gregory.

Merlin turned to Alice, curious for more details. “Really?”

“How could it be fake? They say black hole magic can easily crush enemies, warp space, and even ignore all attacks—any attack that hits him gets redirected by the magic. It’s absolutely insane,” Alice said, clearly well-informed.

“Sounds interesting,” Merlin mused, thinking that such a redirection spell would likely be useless against him. If he used *Blade Draw* and the attack was redirected back at him, wouldn’t that be dangerous?

“Besides, that old guildmaster is incredibly powerful—his mana is overwhelming, practically a Saint-tier peak. Even in Great Britain, he’s a figure who commands respect. They say every emperor has called on him for help when facing troublesome matters,” Alice explained earnestly.

“Black and white, both handled with ease? Pretty smooth,” Merlin remarked casually before adding, “Though I doubt he could beat me.”

“Could you be a little more humble?” Alice deadpanned.

“What did I say wrong?” Merlin frowned.

“He saved me once—can’t you show him a little respect?” Alice said sternly.

“Because he saved you, I *have* to respect an old man? Why?” Merlin replied innocently.

“What’s wrong with you? Why do you always sound like you’re about to explode when talking to me?” Alice snapped.

“What? I’m being normal,” Merlin spread his hands.

Alice narrowed her eyes, recalling today’s events, and cautiously asked, “Could it be… you’re jealous because I went to see the legendary swordsman Elgin?”

Merlin raised an eyebrow at her. “How could I be? Jealous of you? The sun would have to rise in the west for that.”

Alice’s face darkened, and she abruptly stood up. “Fine! Stay here! Even if you come back tonight, I won’t open the door for you!”

With that, Alice stormed off without a backward glance, leaving Merlin standing there in the wind, bewildered.

Merlin watched Alice’s retreating figure, feeling a strange unease. He muttered under his breath, “I don’t need you to open the door for me—I’ll just climb in through the window…”

Merlin was actually a bit angry, though he hadn’t realized it himself. Seeing Alice’s starry-eyed admiration for the fake Elgin had made him irritated and unbalanced.

Merlin didn’t think he was jealous—he just found it repulsive how obsessed Alice was with that guy.

“Tsk tsk tsk,” Hobbes clicked his tongue as he approached, glancing at Alice’s disappearing figure before turning to Merlin. “Brother, remember what I said? Alice is clearly getting more and more dissatisfied with you. Now she’s just dumping you outright—no feelings at all!”

“Don’t talk nonsense,” Merlin rolled his eyes, thinking that his relationship with Alice had become unusually complicated, teetering on a delicate edge where even the slightest breeze could reveal hidden tensions.

“I’m not lying—this is experience talking. You and Alice were never equal to begin with. They say beautiful women love heroes, but Alice’s soul is practically being seduced away by that fat guy Elgin,” Hobbes sighed, patting Merlin’s shoulder. “But I feel for you—if things don’t work out, just let go. The world is full of beautiful women—no need to cling to one tree.”

“What nonsense!” Merlin’s face darkened, his hair seemingly twisting in frustration. He had never planned to cling to Alice like that—what was Hobbes talking about?

“When the time comes to let go, you should. Forced emotions won’t bring happiness,” Hobbes glanced at Merlin, who remained silent, assuming he was lost in sorrow. “But don’t worry—you’ve got a backup. Isn’t little Jenna waiting for you? If you marry her, you’ll never want for food or clothes.”

Merlin groaned, covering his face. “Shut up, Hobbes. Say one more word, and I’ll punch you.”

As the sun set, casting a fiery glow over the small town of Raxum, Alice stomped home, kicking pebbles along the way, the sound echoing like raindrops.

She puffed out her cheeks like a feeding hamster, furious and hurt.

Her silver hair swayed behind her as she hurried along, her expression tense with frustration.

“Stupid Merlin! Damn Merlin! Die already!”

Alice muttered curses under her breath, likely wishing all sorts of misfortunes upon Merlin.

“How dare he talk to me like that? When did I ever provoke him?”

“That bastard—he always picks on me, treating me like a soft target!”

And what was he made of? His heart?

“He worships Elgin so much, yet he won’t… won’t get jealous at all?!”

Alice was most angry not because of Merlin’s rude tone, but because he hadn’t shown any jealousy—this made her feel deeply unsettled.

Normally, when she saw Merlin flirting with other girls, she’d feel uncomfortable.

But Merlin? No reaction at all. Did that mean her charm was so lacking that he felt nothing?

The more Alice thought about it, the angrier she got. She wanted to punch Merlin’s head to vent her frustration.

Though she knew she and Merlin weren’t truly married, seeing him so cold still made her furious.

Alice fumed all the way home, determined to lock the windows—even if Merlin tried to climb in at night, she wouldn’t let him in.

Meanwhile, one of Luke’s henchmen, a squint-eyed man, strolled over, stroking his chin as he leered at the passersby.

He tilted his chin, his gaze lingering on the girls walking by, his eyes wandering over their chests without missing a single one.

This time, the squint-eyed man had been sent by his master to scout for beautiful women. As night fell, Luke wanted to ease his loneliness in this remote town of Raxum, and the only way to do that was to find pretty girls to spend a “pleasurable” night with.

Luke had a very unique preference—unlike most men, he favored flat-chested women.

This preference ran deep in the Overley family, generation after generation, all drawn to girls with small chests.

If a voluptuous beauty stood before Luke, he’d likely just smirk and show no interest.

But if a flat-chested beauty appeared, the result would be the opposite—Luke would be deeply intrigued.

As Luke’s trusted henchman, the squint-eyed man naturally understood his master’s tastes, so he was now searching for flat-chested girls to present to Luke.

It was no secret that flat chests were a rare commodity. The squint-eyed man had been searching for a long time without finding a suitable one.

But fate favored the determined—when he saw Alice walking toward him, he froze, his eyes flashing with excitement.

The squint-eyed man had helped Luke scout for flat-chested beauties countless times, and he’d seen his fair share of women. At first glance, he knew this girl was a *super* flat-chested beauty!

Even if Alice used the most advanced padding, the squint-eyed man’s lecherous eyes could still tell her chest was definitely padded.

Damn! Impressive! This must be top-tier merchandise!

His master would definitely be satisfied, and he might even get a big reward.

The squint-eyed man felt incredibly lucky—he could go back and complete his mission perfectly.

However, Alice’s shining secret silver adventurer badge around her neck made him hesitate.

If it were an ordinary girl, it would be easy—she was a secret silver adventurer, not someone low-ranking. If he handled her poorly, it could cause trouble.

The squint-eyed man even doubted whether his master could control a Saint-tier strong woman—he didn’t want to provoke her and get his ass kicked.

Alice was still cursing Merlin in her head, completely unaware that she was being watched.

After careful consideration, the squint-eyed man steeled himself and approached her, no matter what—he had to bring her back.

So, the squint-eyed man strode up to Alice and gave her a very gentlemanly greeting.

“Hello, beautiful miss. Seeing you alone, don’t you feel a little lonely?”

Alice glanced at him, finding his appearance slightly sleazy, but still replied politely, “You’re crazy.”

The squint-eyed man was taken aback—this was the first time he’d met a girl with such a terrible temper. He had been so polite, but she immediately shot him down. “Uh… my master would like to meet you. Would you do me the honor of accompanying me?”

Alice frowned, curious. “Who is your master?”

The squint-eyed man gestured politely, smiling. “Please, follow me… you’ll know who my master is when we arrive.”

title: Chapter 28 — Trouble
content:
Chapter 28 — Trouble

Volume 10 · Chapter 28

After the parade, the entire town of Saxis seemed to have returned to calm.

Captain of the guard Price finally got some rest, swaying unsteadily down the main street with a bottle in his hand.

From the look of him, he was probably heading to a tavern to hang out with his useless friends for the night.

But through his drunken haze, Price spotted two figures in the distance that looked strangely familiar.

So he shook his head clear, pulled himself together, and looked more carefully.

Holy crap! Isn't that Alice?! What is she doing with some other guy?

Hmm... isn't this man one of Luc's trusted aides? The one with the mole on his face...

Price suddenly sobered up, sensing something was off, and a vague feeling that trouble was about to brew.

As captain of the guard for Saxis, he knew the mole-faced man's background well — he was an escort for the Oakrey family.

But now he was with Alice, and the two had absolutely no reason to know each other. That was highly suspicious.

Price ducked into a nearby alley and peeked out, watching intently to figure out what was going on.

The mole-faced man bowed and led the way, then stopped in front of the most upscale restaurant in Saxis, grinning and making a welcoming gesture.

Alice stood at the entrance, hesitated for a long time, and then walked inside with a wary expression.

Price's eyes widened instantly. He felt like he'd discovered a huge secret, catching a faint whiff of domestic infidelity.

Oh my god! No way!?

Is Alice about to cheat on someone? Why come to a fancy restaurant this late, with a complete stranger?

Poor old brother Merlin... is he about to get played for a fool?

Price felt a twitch of tension. The mole-faced man was Luc's lackey, and they'd arranged to meet at such an upscale place — clearly, this was Luc setting a trap for Alice.

And considering Alice seemed to deeply admire the great swordsman Erkin, this looked like it could go very badly.

Price frowned slightly and weighed the pros and cons in his mind—

No, I have to tell Merlin about this.

Alice entered the fairly upscale restaurant.

Beautiful piano music drifted through the air in slow, graceful notes.

Fine wines lined the counter neatly, polished to a shine.

Crystal glassware gleamed, reflecting the red carpet below.

Flickering candlelight cast a warm, dim glow, adding a hazy elegance to the entire dining room.

"Where is he?" Alice asked, puzzled.

"He's right over there. You may go ahead." The mole-faced man pointed toward a corner.

Alice scanned the room and indeed spotted a slightly portly back at a distant table that looked somewhat familiar.

She hesitated for a moment, then slowly walked over, wondering who it could be.

Luc had booked the entire restaurant, so this was a perfect private space.

Alice approached and took a closer look at the man in front of her — and then her eyes widened.

Oh my god! It's actually Erkin the Great Swordsman!?

...He really wanted to meet with me specifically?

Wh...why is this happening? What could this possibly be about...

Alice felt happiness strike too suddenly, almost unable to process it. Stars seemed to sparkle in her eyes.

Luc noticed Alice's reaction and his own eyes lit up. His trusted man had found an excellent girl, perfectly matching his standards.

The only issue was the silver adventurer's token around her neck, which gave Luc a slight sense of pressure. This girl wouldn't be easy to take advantage of.

But seeing Alice's speechless, amazed expression at the mention of Erkin the Great Swordsman filled Luc with smug pride. The name alone was powerful — there were always fangirls wherever he went.

"Please take a seat, miss. There's no need to be surprised. It's only you and me here. I'm merely an ordinary noble, not Erkin the Great Swordsman."

"O-oh... alright." Alice sat down with a hint of nervous restraint, though her heart was still racing.

If Merlin were present, he would've been dumbfounded, and no doubt would've complained that this wasn't the real Alice — usually so carefree and unrestrained, but in front of the great swordsman Erkin, she instantly transformed into a proper, well-mannered young lady, speaking in soft, polite tones.

"I imagine you're also my admirer, correct? It's plain to see from your lovely eyes~" Luc spoke with standard noble eloquence, a slight tremor in his voice that made him sound rather charming.

"...Is that so?" Alice felt a touch embarrassed, wondering if she'd been praised.

"You must have many questions for me, don't you? Ask away boldly. Being chosen by me means you're a lucky girl~" Luc adopted an approachable demeanor, attempting to draw closer to Alice.

"Then... then I won't hold back..." Alice paused, composing herself, "...You went to Erjin a year ago, didn't you? Why did you go there?"

"This..." Luc hesitated. He wasn't actually Erkin the Great Swordsman — who knew what he'd done in Erjin? But he needed to spin something positive. "I heard the Red Beard pirates were raiding the empire. As a noble of high honor, it was my duty to protect the empire's stability. But more importantly, I wished to rescue those common folk from suffering. Wherever injustice appeared, I would inevitably draw my sword in defense."

"Wow~" Alice gasped with admiration. Erkin the Great Swordsman's character was exactly as she'd imagined. "So you joined the Crimson Flower Knight Order for the same reason?"

"More or less." Luc nodded, fabricating on the spot. "To a large extent, I didn't want to become a隐患 to the empire or let various regions fall into chaos. Otherwise, I would never have revealed my identity and become a Crimson Flower Knight."

"And how do you feel now? Do you have any other plans? Will you continue traveling as before? Will you keep your ranger identity? Will we ever see you acting in justice again? You won't choose retirement just because you became a knight, will you...?" Overcome with激动, Alice fired off a rapid barrage of questions.

"...Luc's expression grew awkward. His lips twitched repeatedly, and a trickle of cold sweat formed on his forehead. Dammit, this woman is so annoying!?

Meanwhile, at the guild, Merlin was drinking heavily alongside Hobbs, sharing a sort of companionship in despair.

Price burst in hastily, collapsing against Merlin and Hobbs's table, gasping for breath.

Hobbs jumped in fright and asked in astonishment, "Price... what's wrong with you?"

"....Big trouble... has happened," Price stammered.

"Hmm?" Merlin frowned. How could big trouble happen when it was so quiet outside?

"Mer... just listen..." Price didn't waste time, locking eyes with Merlin and speaking briefly—

"Erkin the Great Swordsman is currently seducing your wife!"山(°口°山)

title: Chapter 28 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 28 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 10 · Chapter 28

Merlin's face was expressionless as he fell into a few seconds of stunned silence, then he burst into laughter and waved his hand dismissively.

"Haha, don't lie to me. Who would be hungry enough to hit on Alice? Just look at how Alice behaves—"

"Eh?" Price was thrown off by Merlin's reaction. Normally, a man hearing that his wife was being flirted with would be furious, right?

"Merlin, take this seriously. Look at Price's expression—he doesn't seem to be joking at all." Hobbes patted Merlin, trying to get him to act normal.

"Are you serious? How could Elkin the Great Swordsman flirt with Alice? I don't think he'd be interested in Alice. Maybe he's interested in Rukia instead." Merlin didn't believe it, thinking Price was probably joking or had misread the situation.

"It's true! I just saw Alice being led into a pretty fancy restaurant. The one escorting her was a trusted aide of Elkin the Great Swordsman. It's definitely him. This Luke is really interested in your wife." Price grew more agitated as he spoke, feeling that at the very least Merlin should react. He wasn't acting like a normal man at all.

Merlin looked up at Price's anxious expression and seriously asked, "What evidence do you have for these claims?"

"I saw it with my own eyes. My... younger brother..." Price pointed to his own eyes and added, "Besides, who in the empire doesn't know? The men in the Ofray family are all breast connoisseurs. They only go for flat-chested women. Just imagine how tempting Alice must be to them."

Merlin's stunned expression froze on his face. He thought to himself, No way? Since when did Alice become so sought-after? Why does everyone keep eyeing her?

"Merlin, look what I told you. It really is true—fearing the worst, you're already imagining the worst. You're acting like you're about to get sliced down by Elkin the Great Swordsman any minute now." Hobbes wore an excited expression, thinking he'd guessed right.

Merlin's face gradually darkened, his mood turning sour.

Why is this Luke guy being so brazen? He's shameless!

Even if he's pretending to be me, he's using a fake identity to hit on Alice!

She's supposed to be my wife on the surface, yet he just ignores me completely!

Who gave this fake the guts to do this? Does he want to die?

Merlin clenched his fists silently. Though he hated to admit it, a trace of murderous intent stirred within him—he wanted to eliminate this fake Luke.

Hobbes patted Merlin's shoulder beside him. "Friend, be strong."

Price also patted Merlin's shoulder. "Right, stay strong. To get through life, you've got to learn to bear a little green on your head~"

"Get out of here! I haven't been cuckolded yet!"

Merlin shooed away both of their hands and thought to himself, I'm a distinguished Great Demon Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace. Are you telling me I'm going to get cuckolded by some fake imposter? Isn't that the ultimate disgrace?!

So Merlin stood up in a hurry, grabbed the wakizashi from the table, and left the guild to investigate the situation.

Hobbes: "Tch tch tch, this guy—says he doesn't care, but his body betrays him completely."

Price: "Feels like there's going to be a bloody mess tonight. How tragic~"

book.SFA

The restaurant.

Restaurant SF light novel.

Because Alice was too curious about Elkin the Great Swordsman, she kept asking questions.

Her little mouth moved like a machine gun—she never stopped.

At first, Luke could patiently answer, making up excuses to get by. But now he was starting to struggle with Alice's increasingly pointed questions.

Alice was basically a curious little baby, always full of questions about her idol, and she felt something was different.

Luke wasn't the real Elkin the Great Swordsman anyway, and he'd been careful with his lies.

Facing Alice's increasingly probing questions, he was getting more and more uncomfortable.

Luke had come here to sleep with a girl, not to answer questions. He was starting to deviate from his original purpose.

"Aren't you a noble young master? Don't you run into trouble every time you go out? Did your father, Duke Ofray, know you were Elkin the Great Swordsman at first?"

Luke couldn't take it anymore. He covered his darkened face and shouted angrily, "Enough!"

"Eh?" Alice was stunned, not knowing what she had done wrong, wondering why the other person suddenly got angry.

Luke snapped his fingers, and a waiter immediately brought over a glass of red wine and poured one for both of them.

Then Luke lifted his goblet, swirled the red wine inside, and decided to speak plainly—no more beating around the bush.

"How about we cut the crap and be straightforward?"

"...What do you mean?" Alice didn't quite understand, sensing that Luke's attitude had changed from before.

"I want to sleep with you. How about a price?" Luke said without hesitation.

"Eh?" Alice was taken aback, thinking she had misheard. "You want to... sleep with me?"

"That's right. Spend a wonderful night with me, and I'll give you generous wealth." Luke said directly, pushing his corrupted belly forward and leaning back in his chair.

Alice immediately narrowed her eyes and scrutinized Luke, feeling that he was vastly different from the Elkin the Great Swordsman in her mind.

Especially after he proposed sleeping with her, her impression of Luke plummeted to rock bottom, and she started to feel disgusted.

She had only been a little infatuated with him, which was why she asked so many questions. But this guy actually wanted to take advantage of her!

Is this really Elkin the Great Swordsman? The person I admire would never do something like this! Even Merlin, who often bullies me, at least never insulted me like this.

Alice's mood soured. She felt insulted. Paying for sex—this is exactly what those cheap bar hostesses do!

"What do you take me for? Are you insulting me?"

"Come on, don't pretend. You admire me, don't you? I'm Elkin the Great Swordsman. Spending the night with me is what you've been waiting for, isn't it? And there's a large sum of money to be made—wouldn't that be absolutely perfect?" Luke shrugged, making his intentions clear, not wanting to waste any more time.

"Are you joking?" Alice suppressed her anger and asked doubtfully, "With that kind of behavior, you're really Elkin the Great Swordsman? In my mind, he would never do this. I was told that Elkin the Great Swordsman is a very righteous guy."

"Haha, I'm the genuine article—Elkin the Great Swordsman, no doubt about it." Luke put on a theatrical performance, thinking that his authenticity wasn't that important anymore.

"If you're really Elkin the Great Swordsman, then I'm truly disappointed!"

Alice picked up her goblet and splashed wine all over Luke.

Then Alice didn't look back at all, turned around and left, disappointed in Elkin the Great Swordsman. She hadn't expected this guy to be a lecher!

Luke stared blankly at his wine-stained shirt, with red wine dripping from his head, looking extremely disheveled.

He was furious, and in a fit of desperation to keep Alice from leaving, he shouted at the pimply-faced boy at the door, "Stop her! Don't let her leave!"

title: Chapter 29 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 29 — Bonus Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 10 · Chapter 29

Now Luke was a bit annoyed. As a noble, he had been splashed with wine by a commoner—pure insult!

For a moment, Luke's mind was full of wanting to teach Alice a lesson. He had always hated disobedient girls.

Luke seemed to have been blinded by rage, forgetting that Alice was a Saint-tier powerhouse. If she wanted to leave, who could stop her?

The mole-man who received the order immediately felt immense pressure. Block a Saint-tier powerhouse? Was he joking?

He was just a high-tier warrior. How could he possibly deal with a Saint-tier? It was basically suicide.

The other party was a Saint-tier adventurer, and his young master dared to say so bluntly that he wanted to sleep with her? Wasn't that asking for death?

Any Saint-tier powerhouse had high dignity. Was that something you could get with money?

The mole-man thought for a moment. Facing Luke's pressure, he could only grit his teeth and go for it, but he had to smile to avoid getting hit.

"Miss, don't leave. We can still talk, can't we?"

"Get lost."

Alice said a dirty word without any courtesy. Her eyes immediately changed, shimmering with brilliant gold, her pupils turning sharp and thin, inspiring both fear and awe.

A faint dragon aura was released, leaving the mole-man completely stunned. The absolute species suppression made him unable to breathe; for a moment, his heart was startled into stopping.

Alice was now a human wielding dragon power, and specifically holy dragon power. This faint dragon aura wasn't something ordinary people could resist. Severe cases would drop dead on the spot; mild cases would instantly lose all fighting spirit.

"Ugh!"

The mole-man couldn't say a word. Fear was all that remained in his heart. He collapsed directly to the ground, face ashen, cold sweat pouring out.

Even recalling Alice's golden pupils made the mole-man shudder. He thought, 'What kind of human is this? It's literally a human-shaped dragon!'

Alice left without looking back, her mood at its worst because—

The idol in her heart had collapsed...

Alice walked out of the upscale restaurant, her anger making her hair stand on end.

Her mind was full of Luke's disgusting appearance and his insulting remarks.

"What the hell! ? What did you take me for! ?"

"Do I look like a cheap girl?"

"Damn! I didn't expect Elgin the Great Swordmaster to be this kind of person!"

"I used to thought about marrying Elgin the Great Swordmaster, but this guy is so disappointing!"

"I actually admired such a crappy guy. Thinking about it, how disgusting!"

"Even that bastard Merlin is 100 times better than Elgin the Great Swordmaster! No comparison at all!"

"Although that Merlin guy has a bad heart and likes to bully people, his character is still decent. He's way better than this Elgin the Great Swordmaster!"

"I've been blind! Looks like if you don't get to know someone personally, you'll never know what they're really like!"

Alice felt a bit headachey, her mind a mess. She seemed unable to find her life goal for a moment, losing a lot of motivation.

"Hmm? !" At this moment Merlin had just arrived, and happened to run into Alice right as she left.

"Eh? !" Alice was stunned. She hadn't expected to run into Merlin right after leaving.

The two locked eyes, their gazes slightly awkward—

Merlin: Shit! How did this guy come out? Did everything end? Looks like nothing happened, scared me shitless, thought I was joining the Cuckold Club, good....

Alice: What the hell is this bastard doing here? So weird. If going home, it should be in the completely opposite direction, right? Did he come on purpose? Maybe he's following me? Suspicious.....

The two stared at each other on the street for a short while, their gazes shifting repeatedly, both trying to guess the other's thoughts.

Merlin was the first to look away, glancing around as if he had just arrived in Lexham.

No comparison, no hurt.

Because Elgin the Great Swordmaster's image had collapsed in Alice's heart, she now found Merlin much more agreeable.

So Alice adjusted her mood slightly and asked abruptly.

"How did you come here?"

".... Cough!" Merlin wanted to speak but held back, quickly coughed twice, and said seriously, "I came to look at the scenery. After all, I've been in Lexham for so long and haven't explored yet. Running into you, what a coincidence~"

Alice's eyes changed, she puffed her cheeks, making a somewhat angry face.

"Although Merlin's answer had no problem, Alice was a bit suspicious. 'No way Merlin would suddenly rush here for no reason?'"

"Besides, Alice was a bit disappointed. Merlin's answer didn't match what she had in mind."

"Did someone tell you I was here? So you came charging over because you felt unbalanced?"

"... Merlin chuckled. Internally embarrassed, even if it was true, he wouldn't admit it. "What joke? I was just passing by. That's all~"

"Hmph!" Alice pouted her little mouth, instantly deflating like a punctured balloon.

"Words... Merlin narrowed his eyes, pretending nonchalance. "Why were you at that restaurant?""

"Nothing, I just cursed out a bitch." Alice walked over and nudged Merlin slightly, muttering—

"Let's go, go home together...."

Inside the restaurant.

Luke looked at his wet, luxurious clothes, stained with sticky red wine, feeling utterly frustrated.

The mole-man collapsed on the ground was still in a state of excessive panic, trembling constantly, his eyes filled with confusion.

Seeing his subordinate so useless, Luke couldn't help but angrily yell.

"You useless thing! Why did you block that bitch?! How did our family raise such trash?!"

The mole-man on the ground recovered slightly, quickly stood up and smiled apologetically. "Young master, this isn't my fault either? That was a Saint-tier powerhouse, a Mithril adventurer, and that gaze just now was too weird. Even risking my life I couldn't stop her?!"

Luke calmed down a bit, thinking it made sense. He was just a high-tier subordinate. "How could he possibly block a Saint-tier? Their strength is on a completely different level.

"Tch! Taking you was a mistake. If I had known, I should have begged Father to send a Saint-tier as my escort!

"This...." The mole-man felt awkward. He thought it wasn't his fault either; wasn't it because Luke's words were too explicit?

Creak—

The restaurant door opened, and a person with a slender figure wearing a black robe walked in.

This suddenly appearing mysterious person immediately broke the restaurant's silence.

"Hmm? You..." The mole-man asked in surprise, looking at the figure, seemingly a very hot female.

The black-robed person slowly removed her hood, revealing beautiful glory. Her long red hair swayed gently, and the skull wand in her hand looked very eerie. If not Grace, who else could it be?!

Grace's gaze fixed directly on Luke in the corner. She instinctively showed a smile, her lips curling into a slightly savage expression—

Elgin the Great Swordmaster....

Found you. Prepare to die!

All alone here? That's literally digging your own grave. L_

title: Chapter 30 — Sever
content:
Chapter 30 — Sever

Volume 10 · Chapter 30

Grace was also a stunningly beautiful woman; her pretty face alone was enough to captivate anyone.

Luke's anger vanished in an instant. He glanced at Grace a few times, but when he saw her generous bust, his interest died completely.

"Miss, this place has been booked by me. If you wouldn't mind, I'd ask that you leave."

The pockmarked man suddenly caught on, remembering that the young master disliked women with large breasts and had a particular fondness for those with flat chests.

So the pockmarked man cleared his throat, preparing to kick Grace out.

"That's right, miss, our young master has booked this place. Please leave."

A slightly sinister smile still lingered on Grace's face, sending a creeping sense of wrongness through the room.

She had been watching for a long time, and now was the perfect moment to strike!

Gregorio was catching up with Old Taylor, and the Thorn Knights didn't seem to be anywhere near Luke.

As a Saint-tier powerhouse, killing Luke would be an absolute breeze!

It was as if fate itself had arranged this — a near-guaranteed assassination opportunity. How could she possibly let it slip away?

Luke dared to come to such a remote restaurant by himself. He was practically delivering himself to her!

Finally... finally I can take revenge for Swinbourne. For my lover, I will make the Elgin great swordsman suffer beyond death itself!

Grace's eyes shifted to the pockmarked man. Golden Saint-tier mana began to seep from her, and an overwhelmingly crushing pressure slammed into him like a tidal wave.

"Want me to leave? Do you even have the strength to make that happen?"

"Ugh!" The pockmarked man's breath caught. He was too terrified to speak, his legs nearly giving out. That pressure was far more brutal than Alice's had been just moments ago.

"Hmph." Grace sneered, raising her skull magic staff and sweeping it past the pockmarked man's face.

The skull staff suddenly emitted an eerie red glow, as though some vengeful spirit resided within its eye sockets, greedily devouring souls.

Fear flashed across the pockmarked man's eyes. His mouth hung open, unable to utter a sound — as if he had suddenly gone mute.

His body began to age at a visible, horrifying speed. He grew gaunt and pallid, as though every ounce of his vital essence had been siphoned away.

In the blink of an eye, the pockmarked man was reduced to human jerky, collapsing weakly to the floor, completely lifeless.

Not far away, Luke witnessed the scene and was utterly terrified. His face drained of color, cold sweat spreading across his forehead.

Luke was not a fool. Seeing his subordinate gruesomely killed, he already understood that Grace was no kind person — she was vicious and ruthless.

And she appeared to be looking for him specifically. Who knew what awaited him next? He guessed he might end up as meat jerky too.

Luke began trembling uncontrollably. He stood up shakily and nervously retreated backward, pointing at Grace.

"Wh-who are you!? ...How dare you kill my subordinate! ...I-I'm the sole heir of the Aofrei family! If you dare show me any disrespect, I'll make sure you regret it! You'll die with your eyes wide open!"

Overcome by fear of Grace, Luke's speech became incredibly halting and stumbling.

Grace glanced at Luke's spineless display, a flicker of doubt crossing her eyes.

She wondered: How did this garbage manage to defeat Swinbourne? Was she misinformed?

Could he really be the legendary Elgin great swordsman? Why did he show zero trace of a true warrior's bearing?

Grace found it hard to fathom, but she couldn't be bothered to dwell on it. Who knew if the other party was playing the fool to ambush her? To avoid complications, it was better to eliminate him quickly.

"Threatening me? Are you even worth threatening? Aren't you the Elgin great swordsman? I've heard you're incredibly powerful. Today I'll test that claim."

Upon hearing that the other party was looking for the Elgin great swordsman, Luke realized he had simply been cursed with misfortune — reduced to a scapegoat. He immediately began to stammer a pitiful explanation.

"I-I... I'm not the Elgin great swordsman! I'm a fake!"

"Heh heh, don't take me for a fool. If you refuse to fight with your true strength, then just surrender and let me kill you~"

Grace pointed her staff at Luke. Mana began to surge around her, and the skull staff's eye sockets blazed with intensifying red light.

"Die! For the crime of killing my lover, pay with your life!"

Saint-tier magic erupted in a violent burst — a crimson spiral wave shot directly toward pale-faced Luke.

Grace's specialty was barrier magic, so her offensive techniques were limited. But against a weakling like Luke, it was more than sufficient.

Grace's offensive magic was somewhat特殊 — it required soul sacrifices to activate and had strict usage limitations.

Thus Grace frequently killed humans like the pockmarked man, storing their souls within her staff for her own use when casting offensive magic.

Magic that demanded such a terrible price naturally possessed immense destructive power, reaching the level of ultimate magic arts.

The red spiral wave emitted ear-splitting roars, nearly shattering the entire restaurant in moments. The situation was extremely urgent—

With a thunderous boom, Mestfield descended from the sky, crashing through the restaurant's roof and entering the heart of the conflict.

"Stand down!"

Luke snapped back to his senses from terror and hurriedly scrambled under the table, curling up with his backside raised, shivering uncontrollably.

Facing the overwhelming force, golden battle aura instantly surged around Mestfield's body, raging like a wild beast.

She drew the straight sword at her waist and delivered a thunderous slash.

The ferocious red spiral was instantly cleaved in two, dissipating on the spot!

Mestfield retreated half a step, her elegant brows knitting together. *This woman isn't weak at all?*

"Huh? You b—" Grace hadn't expected the First Knight to suddenly attack, nor that she could sever her magic with a single strike. This level of strength was truly beyond her ability to resist.

Before Grace could finish her curse, Mestfield charged straight at her.

With a fierce slash! She severed Grace's arm clean off!

"Aaaaaah!"

Grace let out a bloodcurdling scream as her severed arm spun through the air, tracing a ghastly arc.

She pressed her hands against the stump, retreating repeatedly, as gushing blood erupted like a fountain, unrestrained!

Blood dripped and pooled on the ground. The slender severed arm twitched uncontrollably where it lay. The scene was horrifying to behold!

Even Grace herself could never have imagined that in a single exchange, she'd be left disabled. The Thorn First Knight's strength was truly as formidable as they said.

Grace's face was pale, drained of all color, cold sweat streaming down her brow. She slowly raised her head, her eyes filled with venom—

"You—"

"Remember this!"

"I will kill all of you!"

"Even if you cry and kneel, begging for my mercy, I will never forgive you!"

(“▼皿▼)

title: Chapter 31 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 31 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 10 · Chapter 31

Rogues like Grace were pure threats. Letting her go would be an enduring disaster.

Melfield understood this as well. He charged toward the wounded Grace with his sword drawn, hoping to deliver a killing strike.

But from beneath Grace's feet rose wisps of crimson blood mist. A fierce wind erupted, and she vanished from the spot instantly.

Tch!

Melfield frowned deeply. She had clearly come prepared, using a barrier magic spell to teleport away.

From the start, Melfield had felt uneasy about Luke. If he stepped away for even a short while, what could that guy be up to?

And the usually composed Sir Freas had mentioned during the parade that he had spotted a suspicious redhead woman whose appearance closely resembled a certain member of Howling Praise's lineup, though he couldn't quite confirm it.

Melfield grew worried and bid farewell to the other Thorn Knights early, intending to check on Luke. On the way, he had sensed a trace of Saint-tier pressure that made him uneasy.

He felt something was amiss and quickened his pace, eventually arriving in time to save Luke's useless life. Otherwise, the consequences would have been unthinkable.

If this mission ended in failure, Melfield wouldn't even know how to answer to Her Majesty the Queen. Even Elizabeth herself might have a breakdown.

Melfield resolved to keep a close watch on Luke from now on. That redhead woman sounded genuinely vindictive and unlikely to let him go easily. He had to proceed with caution.

After their brief exchange just now, Melfield judged that although Grace wasn't as powerful as Swinburne, her strength was still no joke. Better safe than sorry.

Hearing that the area outside had grown quiet, Luke emerged shakily from under the table, trembling. Seeing the severed arm on the ground, he breathed a slight sigh of relief, though dissatisfaction still lingered.

Hey, are you a complete waste? Why didn't you kill that woman who was trying to murder me? You're the First Knight, yet you can't even manage something like this? How disappointing.

Melfield remained silent but was growing angry inwardly. It was remarkable enough that he could keep this guy alive, and yet he still had so much to complain about.

I never imagined impersonating the Great Swordmaster Elgin would be this dangerous. Why didn't you tell me this earlier? If anything had happened to me, all of you Thorn Knights can prepare to be hanged! Luke wiped the cold sweat from his forehead and grumbled. Put more effort into your jobs, you worthless knights. If I ever encounter something like this again, I won't let you off easily!

Hmph!

Melfield was nearly at his limit. This Luke was unreasonable and then went further to make things difficult?

It seemed like a lesson was in order.

Melfield turned, grabbed the collar of Luke's clothes, and slammed his fat body against the wall, glaring at him with cold eyes.

Luke's feet dangled off the ground as he struggled desperately, unable to escape Melfield's grasp. Panic surged within him. What was the other man planning to do? Was he trying to assassinate him while he had the chance?

....What are you doing!? I am the sole son of the Oakfay Family! If you dare treat me like this, you'll reap what you've sown!

Luke tried to sound brave, but Melfield had his throat grabbed, making it hard to breathe. His large face flushed red.

Enough with the threats! Do you think I'm afraid of you? If it weren't for Her Majesty's orders, what difference would your life or death make to me! Melfield's expression turned furious, itching to punch Luke senseless.

Her Majesty ordered you to protect me properly, not to lay hands on me... Please calm down. Let's talk about our grievances rationally... Luke began to falter, cold sweat pouring down his forehead.

Melfield punched the wall beside Luke with a thunderous boom. Cracks spiderwebbed across the stone, unsettling to behold.

Don't think we're obligated to protect you. In our eyes, you merely need to stay alive. As for getting injured or having your limbs chopped off and reduced to a cripple — those are not within our duties!

.... Luke was completely speechless, overwhelmed by terror. But even so, he fumed inwardly:

Just wait.

Once the Oakfay Family takes over the Empire,

we'll execute every single one of you Thorn Knights first. Not a single one will escape!

How dare you threaten me like this. We'll see who laughs last!

On the way home,

the fiery sunset spilled across the cobblestone path.

Winding and twisting, with no visible end to the alley, its warm hue soothed the spirit.

Merlin walked in front, Alice followed behind, and the two headed home together.

Merlin had originally wanted to go in and lecture Luke severely, but Alice had slipped out beforehand.

That took the edge off Merlin's irritation. He couldn't be bothered to hold a grudge against Luke as long as no Damocles green hat was dangling precariously above the Great Demon Lord's head.

Still, Merlin felt this matter needed to be addressed. Even if he didn't care about the reputation of the Great Swordmaster Elgin,

someone was using his name to swindle and deceive everywhere, which Merlin found hard to accept. He hadn't done anything, yet he had been cursed at numerous times for it.

Merlin pondered whether he should eliminate that fake and prove he wasn't the real Great Swordmaster Elgin, clearing his name in the process.

Just as Merlin was contemplating serious matters, Alice, silently trailing behind, was in a turmoil of her own, her mind swirling with strange thoughts:

The Great Swordmaster Elgin doesn't even compare to Merlin. Could a guy like Merlin, with all his malicious tendencies, actually count as a good man?

That can't be right, surely. It must be because I have no romantic experience, so I perceive Merlin as somewhat decent.

After witnessing how despicable the person she admired truly was, Alice found Merlin growing more appealing by the moment. And they knew each other's secrets well enough — there didn't seem to be any major hidden truths between them. They seemed increasingly like a couple living together.

Alice recalled what Lucia had said and found it quite accurate. Liking someone and admiring someone were completely different emotions.

Alice felt that initially, she had only admired the figure of the Great Swordmaster Elgin and harbored no other thoughts.

But with Merlin, there existed other peculiar feelings within her. She did not want this guy to suddenly disappear from her life one day.

As habits gradually formed, she found she might have become unable to do without a wretched fellow like Merlin.

Though Alice was reluctant to admit it, perhaps this was what it felt like to fall for someone?

Perhaps without realizing it, I've already grown fond of this fake guy...

A faint blush crept onto Alice's face as she muttered incessantly to herself, her gaze falling slightly vacant as she watched Merlin's silhouette ahead.

She hesitated, then reached out and tugged at the back of Merlin's clothes, like a child lacking a sense of security gripping a lifeline.

Merlin felt a tug behind him and stopped abruptly, turning to look at Alice.

Alice clutched Merlin's clothes and refused to let go, her cheeks flushed red as she deliberately lowered her head to avoid eye contact.

What are you doing? Merlin furrowed his brows and asked in a peculiar tone.

Nothi...ng... Alice answered shyly.

Stop acting like a child. So troublesome... Merlin couldn't help but complain.

Shut up! I'm going to hold onto you and increase your pressure, hmph~! Alice huffed and turned her head away, her attitude somewhat unreasonable.

Tch, do as you please... Merlin decided not to bother with Alice and continued walking home.

Alice felt her face burning and obediently followed behind, still clutching Merlin's clothes as she gazed at his nonchalant背影 and thought to herself:

I am the former Hero.

He is the great Demon Lord beyond redemption.

The mortal enemies we were destined to be...

Can we truly fall in love?

title: Chapter 32 — Monthly Pass Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 32 — Monthly Pass Bonus Chapter

Volume 10 · Chapter 32

Rexem's alleys.

Red magic circles were carved onto the walls.

This was Grace's barrier magic, which could be pre-deployed in a certain location.

Whenever danger struck, one could promptly teleport over here, making it quite a practical escape spell.

The crimson magic circle suddenly flared to life, emitting eerie red electric light.

Grace's heavily wounded body emerged from the magic circle, then tumbled to the ground in a wretched state.

.......

Grace coughed repeatedly, feeling incredibly weak and unable to muster even a shred of strength.

Blood slowly oozed from her severed arm wound. On closer inspection, it actually had a dried-out feel, revealing just how much blood she had lost.

"...Curses... that Thorn Knight dared to ruin my plans...."

Grace's face was pale, her expression twisted with venomous hatred, yet she still refused to give up, already plotting her next scheme in her mind—

It seems I must separate the Thorn Knight and that purple-gold monster.

Otherwise, each one might jump out and interfere with me.

Perhaps I need to set up another barrier at the next location, forcing this group to split apart.

The next stop on Elgin the Great Sword Saint's grand tour seemed to be..... Crussam.....

The next day, dawn was just beginning to break.

Merlin opened his room door, carrying his long black robe, and stepped out quietly, not planning to wake Alice.

He had thought about it all night and decided that Luke couldn't be left unchecked—he needed to handle this matter himself.

That guy dared to use his name to pursue Alice; who knew if he might also pursue others?

To put it bluntly, he was using Merlin's name to lead a bunch of innocent bystanders astray.

This went against the rule that demons respected truth, which made Merlin rather displeased.

Although Merlin didn't care about any empty reputation, someone打着 his banner to roam around and gratify their own selfish desires still needed to be dealt with by his own hands.

If a tiger doesn't show its power, do you think I'm a sick cat?

Merlin thought helplessly, glancing down at the silver ball mask in his hand, engraved with exquisite patterns—

I'll have to act under Elgin the Great Sword Saint's name again.

Honestly, it's quite frustrating, making it seem like I'm some sort of coward hiding in the shadows.....

In order to avoid unknown risks,

the entire Bauhinia Knight团 of the tour chose to leave Rexem under the cover of night.

Mesfield wanted to complete the mission as quickly as possible, fearing that delay might bring trouble, so the entire party's marching speed had been increased.

Overnight, they arrived at Crussam, a very small town, and began their tour there, allowing people to behold the Hero's radiance.

Crussam was located in northeastern Wales, near Rexem, but was not particularly large—even the Adventurers Guild wouldn't choose to establish a branch there. Still, it was a peaceful and tranquil little town.

However, at this very moment, the entire town seemed to be experiencing a grand festival. Clapping and thunderous cheers filled the air, while the fragrance of wild flowers drifted around.

Bauhinia flags stood in rows, fluttering gently in the warm wind as the knights surged into the town in magnificent procession.

Their heads-high steeds and upright armored knights all looked spirited, as if proclaiming the might of the empire.

The crowds were somewhat crowded, but nothing could dampen the people's enthusiasm. The cheers rose wave after wave.

Former tavern owner Martha, accompanied by her young son Henry, had also come here, hoping to see Elgin the Great Sword Saint with her own eyes.

Actually, Martha wasn't very interested in Elgin the Great Sword Saint; she only knew him as an obscure ranger.

But Martha's son, little Henry, was different—he was completely fascinated by Elgin the Great Sword Saint, worshipping him to death.

After all, little Henry was at an age where any boy instinctively liked heroic figures and wanted to become like them.

Now, Elgin the Great Sword Saint was the Empire's top idol with countless fans. Little kids probably didn't even play hide-and-seek anymore; instead, they were all competing to pretend to be Elgin the Great Sword Saint fighting monsters. This showed just how enormous Merlin's influence had become.

Little Henry had been pestering his mom for a long time and finally had the opportunity to come and see his beloved hero in person.

As for whether Elgin the Great Sword Saint was real or fake, little Henry had no idea at all. He only knew that the somewhat overweight guy on that carriage was the legendary hero.

Little Henry's eyes were now filled with sparkling stars, twinkling every second, turning into an utterly devoted fanboy in moments.

Luke stood on the ornate carriage, slowly proceeding down the town's central avenue, smiling and waving to the crowd.

Although yesterday's events had been quite unpleasant, Luke still enjoyed the feeling of being admired. Seeing so many people below him worshipping him instantly lifted his mood.

However, under Mesfield's pressure, Luke was no longer daring to act recklessly.

Facts proved correct—the Thorn Knights only needed to protect Luke's life; as for accidental injuries, he couldn't blame anyone else.

Furthermore, Luke hadn't expected that Elgin the Great Sword Saint actually had enemies. This tour was extremely dangerous. If things went wrong, he could easily become an unfortunate scapegoat!

Luke's face wore a grin, but inside he was swearing up a storm, mentally cursing Queen Elizabeth's entire ancestry. He thought this was no cushy assignment at all—it was clearly a dangerous one! Just when he thought the real Elgin the Great Sword Saint wasn't coming to cause trouble, his enemy showed up first!

Don't take on more than you can handle. With Luke's skills, how could he possibly withstand the pursuit of a Saint-tier expert? At best, he'd be on his knees begging for mercy in minutes.

The current Luke was much more rational. He no longer wanted to continue pretending to be Elgin the Great Sword Saint and just wanted to finish the tour and go back quickly. Otherwise, with a certain red-haired woman always wanting to kill him, he'd catch a serious illness from fear sooner or later.

Vinefrede glanced up at Luke and asked in a low voice, "Someone wants to kill Elgin the Great Sword Saint? Could the opponent really be a member of the Rakshasa?"

"No doubt about it. That appearance matches the portrait exactly. I guess they're here seeking revenge against Elgin the Great Sword Saint," Mesfield said seriously.

"Hah, now we don't even need to do anything. This young Master Luke is so scared he'll pee his pants, crying and begging us to protect him," Millius openly began gloating.

"Millius, can you be serious for once? This is very important. Our mission is already under threat. Are you willing to go back and face Her Majesty's wrath?" Mesfield said very angrily.

"Pfft!" Millius pursed his lips, looking completely unconcerned. He was secretly hoping someone would just take out Luke already so he could vent his own frustrations.

"Then we need to stay more vigilant, otherwise it'll be easy for the enemy to find openings," Morrison said gravely. Although he disliked Luke, he still prioritized the Queen's mission.

"Exactly. I suspect that girl might also be here. We can't let Luke out of our sight," Mesfield nodded.

Inside a certain crate.

The skull magic staff slowly floated in midair, while magical patterns on the ground spread wildly in all directions.

Ancient chanting sounded softly, every syllable sending fierce magical ripples trembling through the surrounding area.

The one-armed Grace suddenly opened her eyes, a manic smile spreading across her face as she loudly shouted—

"Tremble and twist, O earth!"

title: Chapter 33 — The Truth
content:
Chapter 33 — The Truth

Volume 10 · Chapter 33

Grace’s specialty was barrier magic—not offensive spells.

Right now, she was using barrier magic to reshape the entire landscape of Krusam, slicing apart anyone who stood in her way.

Red magical runes spread out from the skeletal staff like writhing worms, erupting across the entire town of Krusam!

The central parade route.

Waves of cheers and applause crashed over the crowd.

Luke smiled and waved to the spectators on either side, but his heart pounded with unease.

The memory of yesterday’s red-haired woman still sent chills down his spine, fearing she might burst from the crowd to assassinate him at any moment.

Several Thorn Knights stood alert, scanning the surroundings and fixing their gazes on a few suspicious figures.

If anyone dared make a strange move now, they’d face the wrath of the Crusade Army.

As for Gregory, he was nowhere to be seen—lingering far behind the procession.

Gregory’s only task was to deal with the real Elgin Swordmaster and ensure Luke’s safety. It wasn’t his responsibility to worry about this.

The magical runes suddenly spread beneath Mesfield’s feet, stretching toward the distance.

“What is this?” Mesfield furrowed her brows, her expression puzzled, unfamiliar with magic.

But Venifered beside her was an authoritative mage, instantly recognizing it. She gasped, “A large-scale barrier spell!”

“What?!” Mesfield froze mid-step, then lightning-fast drew her longsword and bellowed, “All units, alert!”

But it was too late—the barrier spell had already activated.

The entire town of Krusam trembled as the ground beneath them seemed to liquefy, rolling violently.

The once-solid earth churned wildly.

The onlookers, already startled, let out terrified cries.

Their faces pale, they frantically glanced around, many scattering in panic.

“No way… again?!” Luke’s eyes widened as he quickly knelt on the carriage, trembling violently, praying silently that he’d be spared.

The four Thorn Knights stood frozen, like headless flies, scanning the area in confusion.

In an instant, the entire Thistle Knight Order’s procession descended into chaos.

“What’s happening?!” Mesfield shouted.

“This barrier spell was clearly set up long ago. We’re at the center now,” Venifered said, pulling out her spellbook to prepare for battle.

“Hmph, we’ve been played,” Millius raised an eyebrow, his hand gripping his sword hilt.

“What should we do now? We should kill the caster as fast as possible, right?” Morrison said seriously.

Before he finished speaking, the barrier spell’s effects erupted violently.

Mesfield’s surroundings twisted unnaturally, moving rapidly as the distance between her and her companions stretched.

The scenery before her shifted continuously, abstracting into a blur, as if she were entering a time-space tunnel.

Mesfield felt a chill—it wasn’t the world around her changing, but *her* being violently expelled from Krusam’s center.

Sure enough, when she blinked again, she was already at the outskirts of the town, facing a massive red magical barrier that sealed the entire settlement from the outside, like an inverted lantern covering the land.

Traces of Saint-tier magic flickered across the barrier, reinforcing its defenses to keep anyone out.

Since Mesfield had been forced out, the other three Thorn Knights likely faced the same predicament.

“Damn it! Why did things turn out like this? Was it that woman from yesterday?”

Mesfield’s forehead broke into cold sweat—something was terribly wrong. Now, on the brink of disaster, Luke was left without the Thorn Knights’ protection. He’d likely face certain death, and no one could guarantee his survival.

Gregory probably wouldn’t lift a finger either, choosing to stand aside.

If that happened, Queen Elizabeth’s entire plan would collapse—disastrously so!

No! She had to break through at all costs. The faster she got Luke out, the better his chances!

Mesfield’s golden battle energy erupted violently as she slashed at the magical barrier with her longsword.

The immense force made the barrier tremble, but it held.

Mesfield gritted her teeth, focusing her strength to shatter it—

Damn it!

She needed time.

But whether Luke could survive was still uncertain…

---

Inside the barrier.

The once-vibrant town now lay in ruins.

Krusam was in shambles, with broken structures jutting from the wreckage.

The sky turned an eerie crimson, hiding the outside world entirely.

The townsfolk panicked, trapped inside the barrier, clueless about what was happening.

Their faces twisted in terror as they stared around, their hearts filled with dread for what might come next.

Among the crowd, Martha and little Henry clung to each other, scanning the area with wary eyes.

“Mom, what’s happening?” Henry asked, voice trembling.

“Don’t worry, maybe it’s just some trouble,” Martha forced a calm tone, though she felt uneasy.

“Won’t we be in danger?” Henry pressed, sensing his mother’s trembling.

“No, your favorite Elgin Swordmaster is here, right? He’ll protect us,” Martha reassured him.

“Right! Elgin Swordmaster is super strong—he’ll never let anything happen to us! He’s the best!” Henry’s eyes sparkled as he mentioned the Swordmaster, instantly forgetting his fear.

Martha smiled faintly but said nothing, her gaze shifting to the ornate carriage.

The Elgin Swordmaster was hunched over, trembling like a scared rabbit, burying his head in shame.

Martha frowned, her worry deepening. If the Swordmaster—supposedly so powerful—was this afraid, what hope did they have? Would they all die here?

Luke was now at the brink of terror, hugging his head as his face turned ashen and sweat beaded on his forehead. He regretted ever pretending to be the Elgin Swordmaster—he might be hunted to the ends of the earth. Why had he been so foolish? This wasn’t about the Overre family’s honor; he’d been made a scapegoat for the queen’s schemes!

The Thistle Knight Order’s formation collapsed as wails of agony erupted from the front.

Countless burly knights crumbled into dried husks, their life essence drained dry!

“Hold them back!” Chapman, as the squad leader, kept barking orders at his men.

But no matter how many rushed forward, they all met the same fate—collapsing into lifeless husks, like dried corpses.

Grace strode forward, her red hair billowing as if a demon had descended.

Her skeletal staff glowed crimson, leaving nothing but withered corpses in its wake!

Chapman’s lips trembled, his face frozen in terror—he couldn’t speak.

Without the Thorn Knights to back them, they were nothing but scattered ants.

No one could stand against Grace’s unstoppable might—not even slow her down!

As the knights lost most of their numbers, their morale crumbled. No one dared challenge Grace, all too afraid of meeting the same fate.

The massive Thistle Knight Order formation bowed their heads in silence, powerless to stop her.

Grace slowly lifted her head, her eyes bloodshot with excitement as she grinned savagely.

“Elgin Swordmaster, come down and die.”

“I want to see who can save you now!”

“Didn’t you kill my lover with your own hands? Let’s see how strong you really are!”

Chapman looked at Luke, trembling on the carriage, and thought, *This is it.* If Luke’s fake identity as the Elgin Swordmaster was exposed, the consequences would be catastrophic.

Though Chapman was worried, facing Grace himself left him paralyzed with fear. Remembering how the others had turned to husks, he didn’t dare breathe.

The townsfolk, seeing the situation, realized Grace must be here for the Elgin Swordmaster.

They watched as Luke trembled in fear, their confusion growing.

“Why is the Elgin Swordmaster so scared?” one asked.

“He’s supposed to be so strong—why isn’t he fighting back?”

“Exactly! What’s he afraid of? Is this really the guy who slaughtered so many Saint-tier warriors?”

The crowd grew suspicious, their doubts mounting.

Grace frowned slightly, finding it unlikely that Swinburn had been defeated by someone like this. But she couldn’t rule out the possibility that Luke was bluffing, waiting for her to slip up.

“Elgin Swordmaster, come down and fight me!”

“Since you killed my lover, you’ll pay for it in blood!”

Grace knew the Swordmaster’s reputation was legendary, and she had some understanding of his strength.

But she loved Swinburn deeply—this grudge was worth dying for.

Little Henry couldn’t stand it anymore. Seeing his idol so helpless, he shouted, “Come on, Elgin Swordmaster! Fight back!”

Before he could finish, Martha clamped a hand over his mouth and glared sternly.

“Don’t speak nonsense, do you hear me?”

Luke on the carriage shuddered violently, slowly lifting his bloodless face. Overwhelmed by fear, he was on the verge of collapse.

He looked around, seeing everyone staring at him with expectant eyes, and felt the pressure crush him.

He wasn’t the Elgin Swordmaster—he couldn’t fight back. He’d die horribly.

No! If he went down now, he’d be killed without explanation. Maybe admitting the truth would give him a chance!

Luke chose to save himself, wobbling as he tumbled off the carriage, his jowls trembling.

His face ashen, he locked eyes with Grace and, with a *thud*, knelt down.

His tears broke, and in front of everyone, he wailed, “Please… spare me!”

“I’m not the real Elgin Swordmaster!”

title: Chapter 34 — Double Update for Moon Votes
content:
Chapter 34 — Double Update for Moon Votes

Volume 10 · Chapter 34

At these words, the scene erupted into commotion.

Chapman felt a bit dizzy, thinking, oh crap, this guy just admitted it outright, what should we do now?

Compared to Chapman's worries, the onlookers exploded instantly, all thinking they must have heard wrong——

"Seriously? This guy isn't the real Ergin Great Sword Saint?"

"I don't know, but he admitted it with his own mouth."

"I think it's possible. If he's as powerful as the rumors say, why is he so scared like this?"

Gossip rose and fell everywhere, and many people looked at the kneeling Luke with different eyes, filled with disgust after being deceived.

Little Henry rubbed his small wakizashi at his waist, his eyes full of disappointment. "Mom, is he a fake Great Sword Saint?"

Martha felt awkward, not knowing how to soothe her son's disappointment. Should she pat his head or not answer at all.

Actually, Martha didn't believe this guy was the Ergin Great Sword Saint either. How could a Hero be so spineless, kneeling to an enemy?

"I'm not... not the Ergin Great Sword Saint, please spare me..."

Luke was finally crushed by fear, tears streaming down his face as he begged for mercy, hoping Grace would let him go.

Grace narrowed her eyes, studying the spineless man before her, wondering if he really wasn't the Ergin Great Sword Saint. Impossible! He must be plotting some scheme to make me let my guard down!

"What kind of joke is this! If you're not the Ergin Great Sword Saint, then who is!?"

"I really'm not! I just came over to impersonate him!" Luke cried out in explanation.

"I think you just don't want to admit it? You killed my lover, and you think you can walk away alive!? Don't think some underhanded tricks will help you escape here!" Grace grew somewhat annoyed, worried that after all this effort she'd end up with nothing.

Grace knew the Thorn Knights outside were breaking through the magical barrier, preparing to charge in. She definitely wouldn't be able to escape; death was certain. What if she paid such a high price only to never even meet the real Ergin Great Sword Saint? That would be a disastrous loss!

Luke was completely confused, having no idea that the Ergin Great Sword Saint had killed Grace's lover, so he begged for mercy through sobs. "I really'm not the Ergin Great Sword Saint! If I were, how could I be kneeling and begging for mercy? I heard that guy is incredibly powerful!"

"Shut up!" Grace suddenly raised her magic wand, pointing it at Luke, already burning with the urge to annihilate him. "Even the Empire's queen admitted you were the Ergin Great Sword Saint, and you're still making excuses to me? Accept your death peacefully!"

"Ugh!!!"

Luke was terrified, rolling his eyes repeatedly, feeling like his heart might stop.

Dark yellow liquid slowly leaked from his** pants — he had actually been scared into wetting himself by Grace!

"This... this is all... it's all a conspiracy..."

The watching villagers began to doubt whether Luke was really the Ergin Great Sword Saint. He'd been scared to the point of losing control of his bladder.

Such a cowardly fellow was far too distant from the arrogant figure described in legends — impossible for them to be the same person.

Although young, Little Henry could tell this Ergin Great Sword Saint was a fake, purely deceiving people's emotions.

"Tsk!"

Grace looked at Luke's spiritless state and felt very dissatisfied — it was far different from the bloody battle she had imagined.

She grew somewhat suspicious of Luke's true identity and decided to test him. She released a magical attack directly.

The Ergin Great Sword Saint wasn't supposed to be very strong, right? If he were truly powerful, she couldn't possibly kill him so easily.

Golden magic surged around Grace's body, and a cruel light appeared in her eyes as she said coldly,

"Since you're this useless, then die!"

The skull magic wand suddenly lit up, unleashing a crushing wave of death-infused energy that shot straight toward Luke.

"No... don't ahhhh... gaah!"

A scream of agony rang out, and the weak Luke couldn't even resist a single attack!

He died miserably on the spot, dissolving into a pool of dark, viscous blood water.

"Hiss~" Chapman sucked in a cold breath, feeling that with Luke's death, everyone would likely face a grim fate.

Besides, Luke was the only son of the Ofrey family, holding a high status.

Given Grand Duke Ofrey's advanced age, he probably couldn't have children anymore.

The death of the sole family heir was a devastating blow, likely drawing in many factions.

It seemed the fuse of the Empire's turmoil had already been lit, and peace was unlikely to return.

Martha quickly covered her son's eyes so he wouldn't see the gruesome scene.

However, Little Henry was deeply disappointed inside, feeling that the Ergin Great Sword Saint he had hoped for so long turned out to be a fake.

"He was taken down so easily? He's definitely a fake, right?"

"Defeating two Thorn Knights alone earlier was also acting, right? How could someone that weak exist? He's worse than our village guards."

"It's probably fake. How could someone that weak? I heard the real Ergin Great Sword Saint is a man who could beat a Saint-tier强者 around..."

The townspeople chimed in one after another, completely trashing Luke's reputation. Some even felt a bit angry, as though they had been deceived.

Many had traveled through the night to see the Ergin Great Sword Saint, only to find a fake, leaving them incredibly disappointed.

Merlin, hiding in the crowd, pulled down his hood with a slight smile, feeling much more at ease.

Actually, he had arrived here from REXHAM far earlier, intending to kill Luke himself. But Grace had shown up halfway, making his efforts unnecessary. She hadn't hesitated to kill Luke outright.

This was the first time Merlin felt that making enemies everywhere wasn't necessarily a bad thing. Sometimes things going wrong could actually help him.

Now that Luke was dead, Merlin's resentment vanished instantly. As long as no one used his name to swindle people around, and the truth would spread soon enough.

But right now this town was completely isolated from the outside world. Although Merlin could freely leave thanks to his magic immunity, he decided to observe the situation first.

Grace stared expressionlessly at the pool of bloodwater on the ground, as though her soul had been lost.

Even Grace herself hadn't expected to defeat the Ergin Great Sword Saint so easily.

This was completely inconsistent with the legends of his power — clearly Luke was a fake!

After all this effort and nearly paying the price of mutual destruction, she had only killed a fake!?

Grace couldn't accept reality. In the end, she still hadn't avenged Swinborne. All for nothing —

"Aaaaaaaaaaaaaah!"

Grace frantically clawed at her hair, letting out a despairing wail, her patience completely exhausted.

She had bet everything. Once the barrier was breached by the Thorn Knights, she was dead for sure. Yet she had no idea where the real Ergin Great Sword Saint was!

Unable to avenge her lover, Grace's mind collapsed. Like a one-armed female madwoman, she began screaming.

Grace's expression was grotesque and unhinged, tears streaming from her anger, looking completely broken!

She could barely think anymore, only wanting to find the real Ergin Great Sword Saint at any cost, by any means!

"Ergin Great Sword Saint, where are you!? Where are you!? Come out! Come out to me!"

Grace pointed her skull magic wand at the innocent crowd, ready to slaughter. Even if she was doomed, she'd take everyone with her — not a single person in this town would survive!

The residents of Krusam immediately panicked, utterly terrified.

Grace, who killed without remorse, had left a deep impression on them. No one wanted to die miserably, turning into a puddle of black viscous water.

Screams erupted everywhere. Even wanting to flee, there was no path. The terror on their faces was more intense than watching a horror film.

Martha instinctively hugged Little Henry tight, not wanting him hurt, an endless anxiety rising inside her. What should they do now?

Merlin watched all this expressionlessly, his heart perfectly calm. He thought this Grace had gone mad — acting recklessly. If he hadn't followed her, even if she killed everyone here, she still wouldn't find him, right?

"Who among you knows the Ergin Great Sword Saint's whereabouts, speak up now, or I'll make you all die here!"

"Do you also want to turn into viscous water like that guy just now? If you don't want to, then behave yourselves!"

Grace's Saint-tier pressure rose steadily, as though she were about to cast a great magic at any moment, slaughtering everyone. After all, she was fighting with her back to the river — why not drag a few陪葬 along?

But the townspeople seemed even more panicked, because the Ergin Great Sword Saint appeared and disappeared like a ghost. Who knew where he was now?

Grace's pressure was truly forcing people to the edge of death.

However, at this moment——

Little Henry broke free from his mother's grasp and ducked through adults' legs, running out.

His face wore the ball mask, a small wooden sword at his waist, looking rather comical.

"Henry! Henry!" Martha kept calling her son's name, but the surrounding crowd was too packed to get out, unable to pull him back.

Merlin's eyes widened slightly as he noticed Martha and her son. What the heck, why's this brat here!?

Little Henry ran to the opposite side of Grace, drew his small wooden sword, and gathered his courage to shout loudly.

"I... I am the Ergin Great Sword Saint!!!"

At these words, the townspeople fell silent, gazing at Little Henry. Such a tiny figure claiming to be the Ergin Great Sword Saint — no one would believe it.

Even Grace across from him laughed lightly, finding the situation amusing. "You're the Ergin Great Sword Saint? What a joke. So the hero worshipped across the entire Empire is actually a milk-sucking brat?"

Little Henry was at an immature age, maintaining a protective attitude toward the person he admired.

After all, many热血 boys existed in their youth, and Little Henry was one of them.

"As long as you wear the mask, everyone is the Ergin Great Sword Saint! A big baddie like you will surely face retribution sooner or later!"

Merlin's old face flushed. Don't make me sound like an actual hero! My dignity as a Great Demon Lord is ruined!

Grace nodded, a flash of ferocity in her eyes, and without hesitation unleashed a magical attack toward Little Henry.

"You'll pay for your naivety. Disappear!"

The skull magic wand lit up again, sending forth a death-infused shockwave, ruthlessly aiming to turn Little Henry into viscous water!

Before the words had barely finished——

Merlin suddenly descended from the sky, catching the bewildered Little Henry with one arm, while his other hand used his magic immunity to nullify all of Grace's attacks!

Although Merlin didn't consider himself a good person, he and Little Henry had some connection. During his days working as an escort in the tavern, he'd received plenty of care from Martha.

Turning a blind eye to someone in danger was something Merlin couldn't bring himself to do. He'd just consider it repaying Martha's kindness.

Merlin's disguised appearance shocked everyone present, because his costume looked exactly like the Ergin Great Sword Saint!

The ball mask, golden hair, black robes, and a red katana at his waist — completely identical!

Merlin easily dispersed Grace's magical attacks, and then looked at the madwoman across from him with an amused smile.

Grace's eyes widened, speechless at the disguised Merlin. Someone hiding in the crowd who could easily scatter her attacks — an unexpectedly powerful existence. Could it be... the real Ergin Great Sword Saint?

Chapman, peeking from behind, saw Merlin's back, and his heart unexpectedly quickened. Oh my god! That familiar silhouette! No mistake, he must be the real Ergin Great Sword Saint! To appear at a time like this — how unexpected!

As for the onlookers, they buzzed with discussion. Although many dared not be certain, they felt it was highly likely——

"Could it be..."

"Is it..."

"Perhaps..."

People whispered to each other, no one certain of the black-robed man's identity, but their hearts filled with anticipation.

Merlin, seeing no further danger, set Little Henry down and looked down at the troublesome brat.

Little Henry had already switched into fangirl mode, his eyes full of stars. His intuition told him this was his idol!

A few strands of black sweatdrops slid down Merlin's forehead. What a troublesome kid! Stop giving me those earnest gift-requesting eyes!

"You... you're the Ergin Great Sword Saint, right?" Little Henry asked hopefully.

"Heh, you guess~" Merlin tilted his head, wearing a mask that Little Henry couldn't recognize.

But after hearing the voice, Little Henry showed a hint of confusion and asked strangely, "Why does your voice sound a bit like Little Daisy-brother?"

"Cough cough..."

Merlin nearly spat out a mouthful of old blood. His days as an escort were his dark history. Don't just casually bring up his stage name from back then!

He was, after all, a堂堂 Great Demon Lord. Show some respect, damn it!

Didn't everyone have an embarrassing past? Having gone into the service industry to make a living, so what!?

Merlin took a deep breath, looked at Little Henry as an adventurer, reached out, and firmly flicked his forehead.

"Scram, kid. Don't cause trouble here."

Little Henry, despite having many things to say, realized the situation was special and obediently ran back to his mother.

Merlin straightened up, gripped the katana at his waist, and approached the opposite side of Grace, intending to make a move.

"you wouldn't be..." Grace narrowed her eyes, still uncertain.

"That's right, I'm the Ergin Great Sword Saint you've been seeking at all costs." Merlin didn't dodge, openly admitting it, then raised one finger——

"Ah, right, I need to add one thing."

"Different from the fake just now, I'm the genuine article."

title: Chapter 35 — Instant Kill
content:
Chapter 35 — Instant Kill

Volume 10 · Chapter 35

Disguised as he was, Merlin had no qualms about openly admitting his identity as the legendary Elgin Blade Master.

After all, he was wearing a mask—who could possibly recognize him? He could do whatever he pleased.

Truth be told, Merlin still hadn’t figured out what was going on, but from a few things Grise had let slip, he’d pieced together a rough idea.

Judging by the way she’d been acting, it seemed like he’d killed someone, and this madwoman was here to take revenge. Otherwise, she wouldn’t have spared no expense to come after him.

Merlin had seen plenty of situations like this before. After all, the number of people who’d died under his blade was too great to keep track of.

Still, there were always those with ties to the dead who’d come looking for trouble, fearless in their pursuit of vengeance.

For those blinded by hatred, Merlin had always been merciless—no explanations, just the sword.

After admitting he was the real Elgin Blade Master, the citizens of Krusam erupted into a frenzy, whispering and buzzing among themselves.

“This *is* the real Elgin Blade Master!”

“I think so… I’m not entirely sure, but compared to that guy earlier, his presence is completely different.”

“Yeah, he matches everything I’ve heard about the Blade Master—he must be the real deal!”

Because of Luke’s impersonation earlier, the townsfolk had been unsure about Merlin’s true identity, so they could only guess.

But most of them had seen how effortlessly Merlin had deflected Grise’s magic attack, so they were willing to believe that the masked man before them was the genuine Elgin Blade Master.

Grise’s eyes widened in surprise at Merlin’s unshaken admission. She had assumed the mysterious man would act like the coward before her—deny his identity and beg for mercy on his knees.

Instead, he had more backbone, openly admitting who he was. It seemed he had nothing to fear.

Grise narrowed her eyes. Now that the real culprit was here, there was only one way forward—blood for blood.

“Fine. Since you dare admit it, I’ll grudgingly accept that you’re a man.”

Merlin said nothing, only smiling silently as he weighed the idea of killing her.
