“I’ve been hunting you down for a long time. Now that you’ve shown your face, things are simple…” Grise raised her skull-staff, aiming it directly at Merlin. “Today, it’s either you die or I do!”

“Hah, quite the grudge you’ve got there?” Merlin smirked, asking, “I don’t think I’ve ever seen you before. Why are you so determined to kill me?”

“Why do you think?” Grise’s anger flared, her frustration boiling over. “You know exactly what you did! You’ll pay for it in blood!”

“Hmm?” Merlin scratched his head, feigning embarrassment. “I’ve always had a terrible memory, but I really don’t remember ever crossing paths with you.”

“Disgusting…” Grise clenched her teeth, glaring at him. “You killed my lover!”

“Oh? Who was your lover?” Merlin’s expression twisted in confusion—he had no idea who he’d killed, and he’d never bothered to care. That was just his nature.

“The deputy head of the Howling Ghosts, Swinborne!” Grise’s fury only grew, disgusted that the Elgin Blade Master didn’t even remember the name of the man he’d murdered.

Merlin raised an eyebrow, thinking hard—but still, nothing came to mind. He’d killed two people that day, but who knew which one was Swinborne? Still, it didn’t matter. They were all dead, and there was no point dwelling on it.

“Sorry, no memory of it.”

“…You bastard!” Grise’s face darkened, her anger burning like wildfire. “You don’t even remember your opponent’s name? Not even the basic decency to respect them?”

“Don’t take it personally…” Merlin raised a hand, finding her words absurd. “Look, anyone who dies under my blade is just a weakling in my eyes. Their names don’t mean anything to me—you understand?”

“…” Grise’s face twitched violently, her features contorting in rage. Her voice came out through gritted teeth. “What an arrogant piece of filth! How did someone like you become the empire’s hero?”

“To be honest, I don’t really get it either.” Merlin shrugged, thinking to himself that he was the Great Demon Lord, yet somehow people saw him as a hero—something he’d never intended.

Grise gritted her teeth, her jaw cracking as her fury reached its peak. No matter how strong the Elgin Blade Master was, she would drag him down with her.

“Die, Elgin Blade Master! I’ll drag you to hell!”

As Grise’s golden battle energy surged, Merlin moved like a ghost, appearing in front of her in an instant, his hand gripping the hilt of his katana at his waist.

Too fast!

Grise’s face paled with terror, her heart pounding in panic—she had never expected him to be that quick!

Before she could even react, he had already severed her head with ease.

Grise felt her life flash before her eyes, her fate hanging in the balance as he toyed with her existence.

The thought of using barrier magic to escape had barely crossed her mind when a flash of steel appeared before her.

She felt herself weightless, the world spinning wildly as she collapsed to the ground.

Her eyes widened in disbelief—she saw her own headless body not far away, blood spraying like a fountain before she convulsed violently on the ground.

How… how could he be so strong?

Grise’s gaze dimmed, replaced by emptiness. She was clearly dead.

The entire confrontation had been over before it even began—a complete display of overwhelming power.

The madwoman Grise had been cut down instantly by Merlin, who showed no mercy and gave her no chance to flee.

Merlin felt a pleasant warmth spread through his chest as his life force was replenished, the curse quieting for a while.

He sheathed his katana and stood straight, looking down at Grise’s corpse.

Merlin shook his head, exhaling lightly. “Now that everyone’s sure I’m not that fake guy, they still don’t take me seriously…”

The onlookers fell into a stunned silence, their voices dying away. They had all been too shocked by what they’d just witnessed.

No one had seen Merlin’s move clearly—one moment, the enemy was there; the next, their head was on the ground.

The silence didn’t last long. Soon, a deafening roar of cheers erupted, crashing like waves.

Chapman stared at Merlin’s back, his expression dazed as he swallowed hard.

This… this was the true power of the Elgin Blade Master!

Too strong. The queen would surely be uneasy if she knew…

title: Chapter 36 — Monthly Vote Bonus
content:
Chapter 36 — Monthly Vote Bonus

Volume 10 · Chapter 36

Cheers erupted from all sides as many threw flower petals from their hands into the air, giving the true hero a baptism.

Yellow wild petals slowly descended, settling on Merlin's shoulders and trembling continuously, symbolizing glory.

Merlin stood motionless in place with a deadpan expression, his heart completely unshaken, appearing extremely calm.

Because Merlin wasn't pursuing something like this in the first place; everything was within reason.

As the Great Demon Lord of the First Palace, Merlin cared nothing for the hollow fame of honor, and this cheering was merely their own wishful thinking.

Merlin felt a trace of awkwardness, thinking to himself that hadn't I come to save these villagers?

It was just that this woman happened to be Saint-tier and could be slashed to relieve the curse; otherwise, what reason would I have to meddle in their affairs?

Really, these people are unbearable. They inexplicably push me onto the path of a hero.

I'm a Great Demon Lord who slaughters indiscriminately. Can't you lot show some fear toward me? Please have some respect for my profession, okay?

Merlin stood in place with a dark expression, motionless, his mind feeling somewhat awkward. These people had elevated him so high that he barely had the heart to lose his temper.

The crowd's murmurs of admiration came nonstop, offered without any disguise, streaming straight into Merlin's ears—

"This has to be the real Elgin the Great Swordsman, right?"

"There's no mistake. With such formidable strength, could it be anyone other than Elgin the Great Swordsman?"

"Good heavens, just now the opponent seemed like they couldn't even react before being beheaded. With this kind of strength... he could be called the Empire's strongest, couldn't he?"

Of course, among the crowd, young Henry was perhaps the most thrilled of all. What could be more blood-pumping than seeing the hero he admired in person?

"Mom! Mom! That's the real Elgin the Great Swordsman! It's really him!"

"I know, stop getting so excited. Be quiet."

Martha rolled her eyes in exasperation, looking at the silent Elgin the Great Swordsman. He felt like a person from another world entirely, yet that figure still seemed familiar, as though he'd seen him before?

Because of Grace's death, the barrier magic had lost its mana support.

It instantly dissipated naturally, revealing the clear sky above.

Meesfield retracted his ferocious Saint-tier battle aura, watching all this unfold, feeling it was somehow unbelievable.

What the hell! What's going on here?!

Did that crazy red-haired woman die?

That can't be. Could Gregory have taken her out...

Meesfield was extremely puzzled inside. He felt Gregory was a rational guy who would absolutely not choose to meddle in others' business.

Because on this trip, Gregory had come specifically to deal with Elgin the Great Swordsman; he had zero responsibility for dealing with that crazy woman.

Meesfield understood quite well how this group of adventurers thought—they were basically machines that stopped at nothing to complete their missions.

And Gregory had only come out of respect for Queen Elizabeth. Whether he'd lend his full strength remained to be seen.

Meesfield quickened his pace and headed swiftly toward the central avenue, intending to check the situation first—

If Luke survived, that would be the greatest stroke of luck...

Merlin felt there was nothing more to do, so he planned to leave. But at this moment, a man possessed by obsession charged directly at him!

"Elgin the Great Swordsman! We meet again!"

Millius rushed back to the central avenue from the town's outskirts first, gripping his thin sword and thrusting straight at Merlin, wanting to settle things with this mysterious man once and for all.

Actually, deep down Millius was filled with jealousy toward Elgin the Great Swordsman and still harbored ill will over how this man's sudden appearance had stolen the spotlight that should have been his.

Millius himself was supposed to be the Empire's most handsome, most popular, coolest swordsman who could charm thousands of women. But Elgin the Great Swordsman's arrival had shattered his long-held sense of peace.

If there was anyone in the Thorn Knights who harbored the greatest hatred toward Elgin the Great Swordsman, it would definitely be Millius.

Millius dreamed day and night of defeating Elgin the Great Swordsman to prove who was the most charismatic man in the Empire!

His graceful figure combined with his sharp sword instantly unleashed a sword technique as brilliant as starlight, sword flashes carrying golden battle aura forming a net of blade light that pressed toward Merlin!

Merlin lifted his eyelids slightly, instead of retreating he advanced, raising his foot to kick Millius hard in the face, allowing this unlucky bastard to have an intimate encounter with his sole.

"Ugh!"

Millius let out a shriek and was sent flying backward, slamming hard into a wall and crashing through an entire residential house.

At this moment, Morrison and Winifred also rushed back. Seeing their companion in such a wretched state, they had no time to worry about Elgin the Great Swordsman and quickly went to aid Millius.

The two helped the utterly battered Millius up from the rubble, noticing the black shoe print still on his face—it made him look like a boyish idol actor who'd suddenly switched to comedy roles.

"Hey, you okay?" Winifred asked.

"Millius! Wake up, wake up!" Morrison repeatedly patted Millius's cheeks, trying to rouse him.

Merlin's kick had been quite brutal; he nearly kicked Millius unconscious. Hearing his companions' calls, Millius quickly shook his head to clear his senses.

"...I'm fine, don't worry about me."

Millius pushed away Winifred and Morrison, rubbed his face, and felt a dull, aching pain bordering on numbness.

What the hell! Why does that bastard Elgin the Great Swordsman always target my face with full force?!

This is my livelihood! How dare he show such disrespect! I really need to teach this guy a lesson!

Millius glared venomously at Merlin. Despite the shoe print on his face, his gnashing-teeth expression still carried some semblance of menace.

"You ruthless fellow—you always go after my face! Are you just that jealous of my beauty?!"

Winifred and Morrison's faces simultaneously darkened beside him. *Who cares whether you're handsome or not during a fight?!*

They found Millius's words hard to watch and both chose silence.

"Who are you?" Merlin's head was full of question marks; he had absolutely no idea who Millius was.

"...Who am I!?" Millius pointed at himself, thinking, *Can you ignore me this much?* "I'm the only one whose masculine charm is your equal! Remember this properly? We must settle who wins between us!"

"So troublesome. I don't feel like I have much masculine charm anyway. Skip that boring stuff—you win," Merlin replied carelessly.

"Ah, so perfunctory..." Millius was immediately disappointed. He'd always treated Elgin the Great Swordsman as an equal opponent, never expecting him to be such an uninspired jerk—

"Be more serious!"

"I've fantasized countless times about defeating you and proving with facts that the man in the Empire worthy of being called both beautiful and wise is—

Only me!

(;'0)o

title: Chapter 37 — Reversal Blade
content:
Chapter 37 — Reversal Blade

Volume 10 · Chapter 37

---

Merlin listened to Milesius's self-important speech and felt inexplicably awkward. What kind of man boasts both beauty and strength?

"Friend, calm down. I suspect you've got some kind of dramatic spirit possessing you—stop adding unnecessary scenes to yourself for no reason. Everyone's time is precious."

"Someone like you, shining so brightly, how could you possibly understand the sorrow of people like us?" Milesius lifted his head, his eyes filled with resentment, and said earnestly, "Before you appeared, I always had beautiful women surrounding me. Whatever I did, people who worshipped me followed behind. But after you showed up, everything changed! Everyone's talking about you! Even though you always wear a mask and refuse to show your true face, there are still plenty of pretty girls崇拜ing you. Why? I'm clearly more charming!"

A waterfall of black lines appeared on Merlin's forehead. "Don't hold a grudge over such a trivial matter. How boring are you?"

"Boring? You really don't know the hunger of the starving when you're full. I'm dedicated to becoming a flower-path man who captivates ten thousand young women, and your appearance completely crushed my dream! Don't you have any idea how despicable your actions are?!" Milesius said with a straight face.

"..." Merlin pressed his lips together, his expression growing complicated, at a loss for words.

"Enough. You're getting more and more strange by the minute." Winfred, who was always calm, could barely watch this anymore.

"Yeah, you've really brought down the dignity of our Thorn Knights." Morison whispered, his face full of embarrassment.

"Don't interfere with me. I need to make my position clear—I want this guy to know what a terrible person he is." Milesius said seriously.

Morison and Winfred both looked awkward. They thought this had nothing to do with立场? This was purely Milesius's personal complaint!

"Hey! Elgin the Great Sword Master, this is a rare opportunity. The three of us are going to defeat you right now and end your arrogant legend!" Milesius paused, then continued, "With so many people watching right now, I'm going to prove with facts that you're not invincible after all!"

"I'm saying... aren't you annoying? You can't blame me just because no girls崇拜 you? By that logic, aren't all the bachelors in the world my fault?" Merlin frowned tightly, feeling this accusation was rather far-fetched.

"Good that you understand that." Milesius wore a serious expression.

Merlin rolled his eyes, his face turning dark. He thought there was no reasoning with someone who already disliked him from the start.

"Hey, Milesius, this isn't good, is it? Shouldn't we prioritize reconciliation?" Morison whispered.

"Yes, now that Luke's fake identity has been exposed, it's very unfavorable to His Majesty. If His Majesty insists on continuing down this path, the consequences will be troublesome," Winfred analyzed.

"Can't you think about it differently? Luke is already dead. Our mission has seriously failed, and we'll definitely face His Majesty's wrath when we return. But if we capture Elgin the Great Sword Master, isn't this an opportunity to make amends?" Milesius paused, then continued, "Think about how much His Majesty valued this mission. Now we've messed everything up—do you think we'll have a good outcome when we return? The chance to turn things around is right in front of us. Do we still have a reason to choose otherwise?"

Although Milesius had a lot of personal emotions mixed in, they had to admit he made a lot of sense. The situation was indeed special.

"Her Majesty the Queen has explicitly ordered us to protect Luke's life with our lives. Now that Luke is dead, how can we explain ourselves to Her Majesty when we return? If we capture Elgin the Great Sword Master, the outcome might be completely different. Have you considered this?" Milesius showed a very serious expression.

Winfred fell silent, seemingly agreeing with Milesius. Recalling Queen Elizabeth's serious expression and the tone of her final orders, if they returned like this, there would likely be no good outcome.

Morison hesitated, looked at Elgin the Great Sword Master, silently clenched his fists, and was already swayed.

Although Morison knew Elgin the Great Sword Master was very strong, there truly was no choice now.

"For the sake of caution, shouldn't we wait for Methusfield to return?"

"We can't afford to wait. What if Elgin the Great Sword Master leaves and we can't stop him? Think about last time at the Clock Tower—he somehow escaped," Milesius said with a serious expression.

Morison took a deep breath and said simply, "Let's do it."

Milesius smiled, turned to face Elgin the Great Sword Master, and said, "Come then, we can hardly wait to test our skills against you."

"I'd advise you to behave yourselves—it's inevitable that you'll get hurt fighting me," Merlin replied carelessly.

"Really? Make sure you don't cry later..."

Milesius gathered his golden battle aura, and the slender sword in his hand immediately burst forth with a dazzling, luminous glow.

He forcefully pushed off the ground and surged forward like a shooting star, taking the lead!

Milesius appeared very focused, his movements comparable to the most perfect dancer, with star-rending power on his blade!

Winfred followed closely behind, opened his magic book, and created a rock hammer out of thin air. It was entirely black, resembling an extremely rare metal with extraordinary hardness. Its massive size seemed to want to crush the enemy into meat paste!

Finally, Morison directly activated the second state of "Rakshasa," his entire body turning red, blood light erupting, power surging through him, and two ghostly horns growing from his forehead!

The three Thorn Knights didn't hesitate and rushed forward together, wanting to catch Elgin the Great Sword Master off guard.

With the combined power of all three Thorn Knights, it was rare to encounter such an enemy throughout the empire—those capable of resisting must be few and far between!

The onlooking crowd erupted into a series of gasps. They felt this was completely different from when Luke faced the Thorn Knights on the screen before—just from their momentum, you could sense they were serious.

As expected, the Thorn Knights in their serious state still managed to impress!

Merlin curled his lips, feeling these guys were underestimating him too much. Did three people really think they could just wander around in front of him?

Although the strength of the three Thorn Knights was not weak, in front of Merlin, all strong men were just those who appeared strong on the outside but were weak on the inside.

Facing the combined attack of three enemies, Merlin flipped his katana 180 degrees around his waist, then slightly raised his eyelids—

A pleasant sound of unsheathing rang out, and the Reverse Blade Iai Slash was unleashed!

Fierce sword qi erupted; the entire ground cracked, and the air screamed!

The three Thorn Knights hadn't even had time to get close and rush to Merlin's side before they were blasted by the shockwave—

title: Chapter 38 — Two Extra Chapters for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 38 — Two Extra Chapters for Monthly Tickets

Volume 10 · Chapter 38

Three Thorn Knights let out cries of agony, spitting blood as the shockwave sent them flying, critically wounded on the spot.

Their bodies lost control, and they flew backward like cannonballs, crashing hard into the ground!

Milius and Winifred fainted instantly, without a shred of resistance left.

Good thing Morison was at the very back, taking less of the impact; he could barely still maintain his consciousness.

He lay on the ground, feeling a tightness in his chest as if a heavy stone weighed upon him.

Morison gritted his teeth and muttered, feeling that he was simply not on the same plane as the great swordsman Elkyn; the gap in power was far too vast.

This was already Merlin showing mercy, using the reverse-blade draw cut; if he had used the sharp side, these three Thorn Knights wouldn't have even known how they died?

Merlin hadn't yet considered this bunch of fools to be enemies, and wasn't ready to lightly entertain killing intent.

The citizens of Krusam were all dead silent, likely terrified; no one expected the Thorn Knights to be defeated so easily.

Luke, though a fake, could at least trade a few blows with the Thorn Knights when he fought them. But as for Merlin, this group of Thorn Knights didn't even get a chance to get close before being completely defeated.

Chapman stood with his mouth open, his expression full of disbelief. Was there anyone within the empire who could defeat the great swordsman Elkyn? The gap was simply too

Merlin sheathed his katana, brushed off the dust from his shoulders, and said with a helpless sigh:

"Sigh, you forced me to act. Wouldn't it be better to just behave yourselves?"

Mesfield finally arrived at the scene at this moment, only to see three of her comrades lying on the ground, with not a trace of Luke anywhere!

Oh no! Where did Luke go?!

Could he have already...

Damn it! How am I supposed to explain this to Her Majesty the Queen?!

Who did this? Could it be...

Mesfield's gaze fixed on the great swordsman Elkyn, and anger surged within her; she wanted nothing more than to cleave him into pieces right then and there.

Golden battle aura swirled all over her body as she fiercely drew the straight sword at her waist and swung it at her enemy in a brutal strike.

"Elkyn the Great Swordsman!!!''

"Hmm?"

Merlin turned his head to look and silently extended a single finger, pressing it against the tip of Mesfield's sword, easily blocking the attack.

A storm erupted between the two instantly, making those around them barely able to keep their eyes open.

"What the hell did you do?!" Mesfield demanded furiously. No matter how much she increased her strength, she couldn't so much as budge the guy's finger.

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue and said helplessly, "Why is it you again? Don't be so agitated, alright? Every time I see you, you get all worked up like this. It's a bit much for me to handle—"

"Shut up! I'll make you pay for every single humiliation I suffered before!"

Mesfield had no interest in idle chatter. Remembering past humiliations filled her mind with nothing but the desire to hack Elkyn the Great Swordsman to death.

This showed just how high her hatred for Merlin was—so extreme she couldn't think clearly anymore.

Mesfield's Saint-tier pressure suddenly escalated by several levels. She swung her blade from behind, targeting Merlin's neck.

"Die!"

Merlin calmly and casually spat a wad of saliva toward Mesfield, intending to resolve this foolish woman with his well-known trick.

But this time Mesfield was sharper too; acting swiftly, she used her sword to block Merlin's saliva directly.

"You despicable—"

Mesfield didn't finish her sentence before she felt a chill run down her forehead.

She froze, instinctively reaching up to touch it, and saw the sticky fluid coating her hand.

Mesfield's face went instantly pale. She had guarded against everything, only to fall for this!

"Stupid woman. Did you really think I could only spit once?" Merlin looked at her with sympathetic eyes, as if deliberately mocking her.

*Ding!*

Mesfield's sword clattered to the ground. She dropped to her knees right there, drenched in cold sweat, as that familiar pleasurable sensation surged back up.

Her face flushed red. She pressed her legs together and pressed her skirt tightly between her thighs with both hands.

Even so, Mesfield still couldn't control herself. Her delicate body trembled uncontrollably where she knelt.

Somewhere in the distance, Chapman couldn't quite figure out what was going on. He felt that Mesfield's reaction was extremely strange and didn't know what had happened. Why had she become so abnormal after being spit on?

"Hah~." Merlin let out a breath, turned his body, and planned to leave. Playing around with these Thorn Knights wasn't interesting anymore.

"C-come back! I... I absolutely... will n-not... forgive..."

Mesfield's face was flushed red. Swept by the waves of pleasure in her body, she couldn't find the strength to resist; she could only manage weak protests.

Merlin didn't even look back,懒得 paying attention to Mesfield. As for how she dealt with it, that wasn't his concern.

However, before Merlin had walked a few steps, he suddenly stopped, because someone had suddenly blocked his path, apparently unwilling to let him leave so easily.

Gregory had watched the entire scene unfold. He hadn't helped the Thorn Knights at all, nor did he lift a finger when Luke died.

This entirely matched the conditions Gregory had agreed to with Queen Elizabeth—he was only responsible for dealing with Elkyn the Great Swordsman.

Gregory held a magic wand in his hand, his hunched back barely concealed beneath his black robes, unable to hide his aged appearance.

Seeing the other party remained silent, Merlin spoke first. "What do you mean? Are you here looking for trouble too?"

"Handle me?" Merlin frowned, a slight smile forming. "Are you sure you have the ability to handle me?"

"Yes. I truly do have the ability to handle you. This is not something that needs questioning."

Gregory paused, then continued, "Although your strength is not weak, and your abilities are formidable, to me, that is hardly something worth praising."

"In that case..." Merlin paused, tilting his head as he continued, "I suppose I'll have to fight you then. But let me say this upfront—I won't hold back just because you're an old man. Anyone who stands opposite me will receive no courtesy."

"Haha..." Gregory laughed and said calmly, "Young people nowadays are all so overbearing. They completely fail to understand the gap in strength. Are you certain you can defeat me?"

Mesfield, enduring the waves of pleasure one after another, watched Gregory and Elkyn the Great Swordsman face off.

Would Gregory be able to take down that bastard Elkyn?

It should be fine, right? Gregory's strength was so formidable, and his bizarre black hole magic might produce miraculous results!

A trace of anticipation appeared in Mesfield's eyes. She desperately wanted Elkyn the Great Swordsman to be beaten to a pulp—that would at least give her some comfort.

"Of course. And when it comes to dealing with mages, I don't even need a sword. Fists are sufficient~"

Gregory fell slightly silent, his tone carrying a hint of dissatisfaction. "Young people shouldn't be too reckless. There is always someone greater, and beyond the sky, another sky. Your attitude may very well place you in an extremely unfavorable situation."

"I'm stating facts. When I fight mages, I treat them like I'm disciplining my own son. You can call me the Mage Slayer~" Merlin said seriously with hands on his hips. He wasn't exaggerating at all.

What did magic immunity mean? All mages were mere mortals in front of Merlin. Mages could probably only swing their wands to bonk his head to deal any damage.

"Haa..." Mesfield heard Merlin's words and felt utterly dismayed. How much did Elkyn the Great Swordsman despise others? Saying he could beat all mages like sons—he'd make any mage bristle with rage!

However, Gregory merely hesitated for a moment, and far from getting angry, he laughed. "Interesting! It's the first time I've met a young man as fascinating as you—bold and unreserved, letting your sharp edges show freely. I appreciate people like you."

"Huh?!!" Mesfield's eyes nearly popped out of her head. She thought it was too abnormal for Gregory not to be angry. And

It wasn't just Mesfield; even Merlin was completely bewildered. Normally, the other party would have exploded with rage long ago. Why was this purple-gold Old Guild Master not playing by the rules?!

"I won't kill you, but I'd like to ask..." Gregory extended his arm and said earnestly, "Would you be willing to join the Adventurers Guild in the capital? Although your relationship with Her Majesty the Queen is strained, I can help mediate on your behalf and restore your good name."

"Huh?!" Merlin was quite startled. He hadn't expected the other party to suddenly extend an olive branch.

"I don't think you're a bad person. You just need freedom. Perhaps becoming an adventurer is a pretty good option. What do you think?" Gregory asked again.

"No need. I refuse." Merlin waved his hand. He was already an adventurer; there was no need to switch places.

"Don't refuse so hastily. According to my agreement with the Queen, I definitely have to subdue you today. But I see you as a talented individual and don't wish for a life-and-death struggle. So how about we play a game?" Gregory suggested tentatively.

"What game?" Merlin narrowed his eyes, wanting to know what scheme the other party was plotting.

"You stand still and let me land three punches on you. If you can injure me, I'll let you leave safely. If you can't, then why don't you join my guild?" Gregory said confidently.

Mesfield furrowed her elegant brows. If she remembered correctly, Gregory's black hole magic could nullify all physical attacks.

No attack at all could harm him. It seemed Elkyn the Great Swordsman was about to stumble. Gregory had won for certain!

A smile finally couldn't be suppressed from spreading across Mesfield's face. She was happy to see Elkyn the Great Swordsman suffer.

Even the common people began discussing among themselves, feeling that Gregory's刁难 was baffling.

Merlin walked up in front of Gregory and asked seriously, "Old man, are you serious?"

"Yes. I never break my word." Gregory answered patiently.

"Let's get this straight first. Even if you scammed me, I won't give you a single coin." Merlin raised one finger.

"I wouldn't do that." A dark line appeared above Gregory's head. What did he take himself for? Was he some kind of elderly man short of living expenses?

Before Merlin finished speaking, he exploded into action—a punch slammed out fiercely, aimed directly at his opponent's abdomen.

Gregory's heart remained perfectly calm. He even wanted to laugh, feeling absolutely no pressure whatsoever.

*Hmph! Naive young man.*

*Do you really think you can hit me?*

*I simply need to use my power to transfer it away through the black hole, and it will be completely neutralized—*

A black hole appeared at Gregory's abdomen, swirling like a vortex.

According to the standard script, Merlin's punch would definitely hit empty air, with all force transferred away by the black hole.

But reality was not that simple. Merlin's fist passed straight through the black hole and was not diverted at all!

What?!

Gregory's face filled with horror. He was startled for the first time in his life. His black hole had completely failed?! ?

With magic immunity, Merlin rendered all sorts of magical tricks useless. None of it existed in front of him—all that nonsense was trash!

Merlin's fist struck Gregory's abdomen without mercy. A fierce gale erupted instantly, the ground trembled and cracked, and even the air itself vibrated!

"Agh!"

*Thump! Thump! Thump!*

He was smashed through countless walls and houses, flying straight out of the town, and crashed hard into the massive rock face outside!

Then came a thunderous boom—the large mountain outside the town actually collapsed, sheared through completely by a huge section.

From Merlin's position to the mountain outside town, a thick column of dust rose along this straight line, rolling skyward in towering waves!

The power of this single punch was too much for Gregory to handle. He was critically injured on the spot and utterly overpowered by Merlin in one blow.

Gregory had indeed been too dismissive. Merlin's physical strength was far beyond what ordinary people could endure. Even if he survived, a severe injury would strip him of layers of flesh.

Even Gregory himself likely couldn't have imagined that Elkyn the Great Swordsman's swordsmanship was not only formidable but that his fists were this terrifying as well, leaving not a single flaw!

Gregory's body was deeply embedded in the cracked cliff face, spitting blood as if someone had nails driven through him, pinning him to the wall.

*Th-* This is the strength of Elkyn the Great Swordsman?

As the legends said, truly unparalleled. Far more powerful than the rumors suggested.

But my black hole magic can neutralize all attacks. Why does it have no effect on Elkyn the Great Swordsman?

This is too strange, it makes one want to think...

Gregory gradually grew dazed and then fell into a deep unconsciousness, not knowing how long it would take before he awoke.

The spectators, long accustomed to the drama, were all dumbstruck, their shocked murmurs filling the air.

"My goodness, can a punch really have this much power?!?"

"...He's too damn strong! I can't understand any of this! That's a purple-gold-ranked adventurer!"

"As expected of Elkyn the Great Swordsman. Has he already become this terrifying?"

Mesfield was also stunned into silence, her cheeks tingling with phantom pain. *What is going on?!* It was supposed to nullify all attacks! How was she blown away in the blink of an eye?! This has to be some kind of joke! Gregory was someone whose strength shook the entire empire!

"Huff~" Merlin blew on his smoking fist, a bead of sweat sliding down his forehead. With an expression of sympathy, he said—

"So I'm the one supposed to be the one hitting people?"

"I've lived for over 200 years—

"It's the first time I've ever heard such a shameless request."

(∞)

*To be continued*

title: Chapter 1 — Feeling Out
content:
Chapter 1 — Feeling Out

Volume 11 · Chapter 1

Merlin had returned from Krusam by late at night.

After absolutely wrecking Gregory, he hadn't lingered. Instead, he made his exit amid the admiring gazes of the crowd.

As for Mesfield's furious screaming, Merlin simply ignored him and didn't bother.

Judging from the lingering effects of the succubus's saliva, Mesfield likely didn't dare make any rash moves. He could only sit obediently on the ground, doing his best to suppress those waves of pleasure.

Merlin's purpose for this trip had been achieved. By the end of a few days, news of Luke impersonating the great swordswoman Elgin would likely spread across the empire. Queen Elizabeth's prestige would probably be completely ruined.

Luke's death, too, would be immediately reported to Grand Duke O'Frederick.

As the sole heir to the family, and moreover, as the child born to the aging duke in his later years, his importance was plainly obvious.

It was almost certain the entire O'Frederick family would plunge into extreme grief. That the empire would descend into chaos was already a foregone conclusion.

But Merlin was entirely unaware of all this, and none of it directly affected his own interests, no matter how big the mess he'd caused.

When Merlin arrived at his home, he knocked on the door. But very quickly he heard the thundering footsteps of someone charging toward him inside.

*I've got to be kidding me...*

Why can I feel this woman's murderous anger even through the door?

A few black lines slid down Merlin's forehead. He wondered if Alice, having not seen him all day, thought he'd somehow run off.

The truth was that when Alice had discovered Merlin missing early in the morning, she was quite startled.

Where could that guy have gone? He didn't even leave a note.

She felt deeply unsettled, a bit uneasy. She waited at home all morning but still saw no sign of Merlin.

So, squirming with anxiety, Alice went out to search. She asked around the familiar faces at the guild, but apparently nobody had seen Merlin today.

Even Captain of the Guard Price had no record of Merlin leaving the city, as though he had simply vanished into thin air.

Alice immediately fell into a panic. *Could this guy have abandoned me and secretly ran back to his hometown?*

Thinking about it, Merlin's scheming nature actually made this entirely plausible. Weren't demons just supposed to play around and then flick their tails and leave?

Back at home, Alice started packing her luggage, determined to chase after Merlin and drag that ungrateful man back.

She hadn't even finished packing when a knock came at the door. Alice's eyes widened. It was almost certainly Merlin. Even through the door, she could smell that musk.

She flung open the door—

"What in the world are you in such a rush about?" Merlin asked, clearly surprised, and immediately stepped into the house.

"......" Alice stopped mid-sentence. Seeing Merlin return, she instantly breathed a sigh of relief. She was actually quite happy, so much so that she'd temporarily forgotten to complain.

She had harbored deep resentment earlier, but now that he was back, it melted away by more than half.

Merlin made no explanation about where he'd been.

As soon as he came in, he collapsed onto his sofa, looking somewhat weary, his aura of chronic laziness radiating outward.

"So tired. Lying on the sofa doing absolutely nothing really is the happiest thing in the world."

Seeing Merlin's lazy posture, Alice felt a surge of irritation. She'd been worried herself sick, and this scoundrel was so relaxed? That wasn't fair!

Her expression darkened, her resentment flaring up again. She shot mental telepathic blasts at Merlin repeatedly, putting on the air of someone who'd explode if ignored.

Merlin glanced at Alice. A cold bead of sweat slid down his temple. "What's with that expression? You mad at me or something?"

Alice stomped up to Merlin and, in a very serious tone, demanded, "Where did you go today? I couldn't find you at all since early morning!"

"Me?" Merlin pointed at himself. He figured it was inconvenient to explain that he'd gone to deal with some fake, so he just said, "Where I go is my own business. Why do you need to know my whereabouts? Knowing when to mind your own business is important. Can you at least respect my privacy?"

"......" Alice was stumped and blushed as she said, "...I'm not trying to pry into your privacy. I was worried you might run off. We share joint marital debt, so I need to know."

"If I, the Great Demon Lord, truly were running away, I'd do it openly. Sneaking around doesn't suit my style," Merlin said solemnly.

Alice narrowed her eyes. She obviously didn't believe him. Given Merlin's personality, anything was possible. Demons were simply untrustworthy creatures.

"Fine. Then where did you go today? Why are you only back now?"

"...I went out for a walk~" Merlin traced a little circle with his finger.

"Who's gonna believe that?" Alice seemed suspicious, taking another step toward Merlin. "You didn't go hanging around some strange place again, did you?"

Merlin lifted his eyelids slightly and asked flatly, "And what exactly counts as a 'strange place'?"

"Quit playing dumb with me. You know exactly what I mean—places guys like you like to mess around. Where else would it be?" Alice had run out of patience and went straight to the point. "That secret hut of Helenas, of course. Don't think I don't know anything."

"I don't. I rarely go to places like that, unless it's urgent..." Merlin said meaningfully, which really just referred to finding Asmodeus.

"Urgent?"

Alice's face turned bright red and her thoughts immediately went to the most lewd interpretation.

Thinking about it, Merlin was over two hundred years old. Surely he had normal human needs?

Was it true that whenever he couldn't hold back, he'd run there to relieve himself?

Alice secretly narrowed her eyes and looked at Merlin with an entirely different gaze.

"Even if it's urgent, you can't go to a place like that! As your nominal wife, I absolutely forbid it!"

"Tch." Merlin clicked his tongue and rubbed his neck. "This kind of thing is also beyond one's control..."

A sour feeling rose in Alice's chest, and she said jealously, "I knew it. You and Hobbs are birds of a feather! You're no good either!"

"Huh!?" Merlin frowned. How did he somehow get equated with Hobbs in Alice's mind?

"Have you fallen for the girls at the secret hut? Especially that madam Helenas?" Alice suddenly dragged Helenas into this.

"Helenas?! What are you talking about?" Merlin looked genuinely puzzled.

"Helenas isn't the most beautiful woman all across Rexum? Gentle personality, enchanting figure, and a face full of alluring charm. She's the dream lover of nearly every man in Rexum," Alice said very seriously.

Merlin figured that with Alice's scattered attention, she wouldn't notice something like that, so he asked curiously, "Who told you that?"

"Lucia told me," Alice answered.

Merlin thought for a moment and realized that Helenas was herself a fallen angel, so her racial advantage was obvious. She naturally held strong allure for humans.

"I'm sure you were completely captivated by Helenas as well. Compared to her, I'm just average-looking and my personality's terrible. I'm hardly the pleasing type..." Alice appeared to have her eyes closed, but she was actually peeking at Merlin through a slit.

This was merely Alice's test. If Merlin said some sweet words, she'd be very pleased.

But how would Merlin notice Alice's girlish sentiments?

Merlin's reaction was simply an expression of disbelief. Surprised, he said, "Good heavens! Alice, this is the first time you've shown any self-awareness. You've scared me."

"......" Alice's face showed a trace of grievance, letting out a pitiful sound from her throat.

*Damn it!*

*This bastard Merlin actually agreed without hesitation!*

*Why won't he comfort me? Doesn't he have even a shred of affection for me?*

*This is too much! T_T*

title: Chapter 2 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Extra Update
content:
Chapter 2 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Extra Update

Volume 11 · Chapter 2

Alice felt that Merlin completely failed to understand her. She wasn't trying to self-deprecate just now — it was simply modest speech.

She felt she was only missing a few inches in the chest area, so how was she inferior to Helena?

She just wanted to see if Merlin could say something nice, but instead she was left feeling deeply disheartened.

Alice's expression darkened instantly, and she glared at Merlin in a huff.

That forlorn, resentful little gaze looked as though Merlin hadn't submitted his homework for several years.

"...... What, did I say something wrong? I feel like everything I said was the truth..." Merlin looked utterly innocent.

"......" Alice pointed at Merlin, too speechless to talk. She almost wanted to strangle this guy.

Merlin felt the atmosphere growing awkward. His gaze fell on a large box on the floor — it was the luggage Alice had packed earlier.

"Hm? What's that? Are you going somewhere?"

Alice was still fuming and couldn't help letting a string of angry words spill out. "Yes, I'm going back to University Mountain. I don't want to live with you anymore!"

"Hehe~" Merlin grinned wide, delivering another blow to Alice. "If you're trying to run away from debt, going back to the Great Snow Mountains won't help either. Unlike me — once I return to demon territory, there's no one who can lay a hand on me."

"......" Alice was so furious she couldn't even speak. It felt so unfair.

Merlin strolled over to the box leisurely and opened it directly. On top, placed neatly, were Alice's panties.

On the pink underwear, there was a cartoon bear pattern, radiating an overwhelming air of childishness.

Merlin picked up Alice's panties with two fingers from his phone, examining them expressionlessly.

"Tch, so... childish..."

Alice's face flushed red instantly, as if blood were about to drip from it. Having Merlin stare at her underwear made her humiliation level explode.

She hurried over, snatched her panties right out of Merlin's grip, and said angrily, "Don't touch my underwear, pervert!"

"Uh..." Merlin frowned, awkwardly thinking — it's just underwear, what's the big deal?

Alice threw the panties into the box, grabbed the suitcase, and headed back to her room.

"You terrible guy! I never want to talk to you again, hmph~!"

With a loud bang, Alice's bedroom door was slammed shut hard, clearly giving Merlin the cold shoulder.

Merlin stared at the closed door, stood bewildered for a moment, pursed his lips, and thought confusedly —

Is this woman on a washing board crazy?

She's acting like she swallowed gunpowder.

When did I ever provoke her?

(∞吻)<

A few days later.

The matter of Luke impersonating the Great Swordmaster Elgin had spread like wildfire and became common knowledge throughout the realm.

The impersonation scandal had caused an uproar within the empire, and Queen Elizabeth faced an unprecedented credibility crisis.

Many people felt severely deceived. The Great Swordmaster Elgin, whom they had eagerly anticipated, turned out to be a fake.

Even worse, the queen herself had been playing games, deliberately recruiting some guy to deceive everyone. That was the most repulsive part.

After all, who would trust a ruler who spoke nothing but lies? No one was willing to say a good word for Queen Elizabeth.

The Great Swordmaster Elgin was the hero in many people's hearts, yet Queen Elizabeth had actually recruited a fake to impersonate him to consolidate her position. This chilled many hearts.

The royal family's face was completely lost this time. For the moment, Queen Elizabeth offered no response and seemed to be contemplating countermeasures.

Moreover, recently several people within the empire had begun voicing their dissatisfaction toward the queen, making Elizabeth feel as though she sat on pins and needles — deeply uneasy.

If she didn't quickly think of a strategy, it would likely stir even greater public discontent, easily igniting waves of opposition against the royal family.

Elizabeth was very worried about events spiraling beyond her control. These past few days she had been in a constant state of dread, fearing the entire empire would fall into uncontrollable chaos.

To prevent such a dire situation, Elizabeth had issued警戒 orders across all regions.

No matter what methods were used, she would crush those discontented citizens. Any signs of rebellion would be met with thunderous suppression.

Elizabeth demonstrated her iron-fisted rule, ruthlessly stabilizing the current situation and barely maintaining control.

However, the empire's greatest threat was not those complaining citizens — it was the Aoffray family guarding northern England.

Queen Elizabeth already knew that the Thorn Knights had failed to protect Luke, resulting in the death of Duke Aoffray's only son.

For Elizabeth, this was simply fatal. No matter what she did, she probably could never steady this long-prepared ticking bomb.

Luke was the sole heir of the Aoffray family. Such a tragic death was virtually indistinguishable from extinguishing their entire lineage, effectively ending the Aoffray family line.

Elizabeth no longer had time to care about the Great Swordmaster Elgin affair. Her immediate priority was suppressing the impending Aoffray family rebellion. She couldn't allow anyone to threaten her rule.

So Elizabeth had already mobilized other factions within the empire, forming an encirclement to prepare for the complete eradication of the Aoffray family.

The entire Britannia Empire was in a state of internal turmoil and external threats. One careless move could bring about the total overthrow of the monarchy.

Queen Elizabeth was extremely dissatisfied with the Thorn Knights' actions this time. Not only had they failed to protect Luke, but they had also ignited the fuse of rebellion!

But what surprised Elizabeth the most was Gregory. Ever since being punched by the Great Swordmaster Elgin, he remained in a deep coma with absolutely no signs of waking up.

Elizabeth had previously been full of confidence in Gregory — he was a Purple-Gold-tier adventurer, a magical advisor from Britannia's founding era, and his strength was more than worthy of being called the empire's guardian deity. Yet the result left her profoundly disappointed.

Elizabeth had to admit that the Great Swordmaster Elgin's strength far exceeded Gregory's — it was something she couldn't control at all.

With such a powerful and destabilizing factor roaming freely within the empire, how could Elizabeth possibly feel at ease?

So Elizabeth decided to deal with the Aoffray family first, then figure out other methods to handle the Great Swordmaster Elgin.

At this moment, in the corridor leading to the royal palace hall—

Methfield, Millius, Morrison, Winifred.

The four Thorn Knights, having received the queen's summons, hurried toward the throne hall to deliver their report.

All four felt uneasy in their hearts. After all, they had failed at such a monumental task without even capturing the Great Swordmaster Elgin.

They knew very well the magnitude of their blunder. Facing the queen's wrath would be inevitable.

Methfield's expression was somewhat grave. He had already heard about the Aoffray family's activities — they seemed to be frantically expanding their military forces, with their ambitions written plainly on their faces.

Behind him, the other three Thorn Knights were all bruised and battered. Their injuries from Merlin's beating had not yet healed, and they looked thoroughly wretched.

Morrison glanced at Methfield, who walked at the forefront, and asked timidly,

"Methfield, do you think..."

"Could His Majesty expect us to atone for our failures with our lives?"

(°△°)

title: Chapter 3 — Rage
content:
Chapter 3 — Rage

Volume 11 · Chapter 3

Morrison's question instantly tugged at the thoughts of everyone else.
It wasn't just Morrison who had this worry; even the other Thorn Knights were concerned.
Militus and Vinifred looked over, hoping Mesfield could give an answer.
After all, Mesfield was the queen's personal knight, and his relationship with the queen was far closer than anyone else's.
Mesfield remained silent, head lowered, his expression looking rather solemn, not knowing how to answer.
In fact, even Mesfield himself had no idea what Queen Elizabeth was thinking.
The queen valued this operation greatly, yet now a major mistake had occurred; what punishment would follow, no one could guess.
If it were before, Mesfield could be certain the queen would not be harsh.
But now Mesfield felt the queen's temperament had changed a lot, no longer shining with the holy mother's radiance as before.
So Mesfield also found it hard to reach a conclusion, unsure how the queen would deal with them.
Still, Mesfield chose to believe, thinking the situation was so dire that the queen would not do something as foolish as cutting off her own limbs.
"Rest assured, Your Majesty will not exterminate us; a scolding is certainly inevitable, after all we made a major mistake in this operation."

......Morrison gave an embarrassed response, his heart slightly calming.

Militus was still uneasy and couldn't help asking, "Surely they won't let us off easily, right? I always feel that the queen suddenly summoning us is not a good thing."
"Why would you say that?" Mesfield turned to ask, feeling Militus was being overly alarmist at this time.
"I also have an uneasy feeling, after all we failed to protect Luke, and the Ofrey family has become increasingly restless, inseparably linked to us; if the imperial armory rebels, the consequences would be unimaginable." Vinifred paused, then continued his analysis, "If the Ofrey family holds us responsible and puts pressure on the queen, given her temperament, it's very likely she'll use us as bargaining chips in a game, buying some peace."
Mesfield bit his pale lip; though he didn't want to admit it, Vinifred made some sense.
Think of Queen Elizabeth growing ever more cold-blooded; perhaps she won't have any other thoughts, acting solely from self-interest.
Yet Mesfield refused to acknowledge this point—she had been by the queen's side since she was little, having seen the kind sister she once was, before she became Britain's ruler.
"Not so; now is a critical time, cutting off one's own limbs would be irrational—we must trust the queen."
"Don't be naive, Mesfield; the empire never lacks talent. I heard several other Thorn Knights have already returned; our role could easily be replaced." Militus couldn't help but interject, thinking Mesfield was nothing more than the queen's loyal dog, never thinking for himself.
"What do you mean?" Mesfield suddenly stopped, turning to stare into Militus's eyes.
Militus met Mesfield's gaze, silent for a moment, then said, "Nothing."
In fact, Militus had a mind to leave the Purple Jasmine Knights, not just himself.
I estimate the other three Thorn Knights share the same thought, but none are willing to voice it outright.....

The palace hall.
Queen Elizabeth held her scepter, seated upon the throne.
A woman with brown long hair, wearing exquisite beautiful armor, with a red cloak bearing a purple-gold floral pattern draped over her back.
She had a slender figure, eyes closed, long lashes meeting, her magic staff slightly taller than herself, the tip adorned with a white-bird-like pattern, looking very dignified and elegant.
This person is the Eighth Thorn Knight, Catherine; when Mesfield is absent, she is solely responsible for the queen's safety.
Catherine excels in ritual and barrier magic; she is also quite mysterious, few can understand her, making her a rather special existence among the Thorn Knights.
Her non-confrontational attitude means she rarely communicates with others; to the other Thorn Knights she is like a stranger.
Furthermore, since joining the Purple Gold Flower Knights, Catherine has never displayed her true strength; outside knowledge of her is scarce, as if she were a transparent person, and many commoners don't even know her name.
Yet to become a Thorn Knight, Catherine must undoubtedly possess some outstanding ability.
Below are a few more Purple Jasmine Knights, weapons in hand, standing by below for orders; Chapman is among them, seemingly having received some command.

Mesfield led the way into the hall, followed by Militus, Morrison, and Vinifred.
The four Thorn Knights walked upon the scarlet carpet to the foot of the throne, each dropping to one knee and lowering their heads.
"Your Majesty, we have come." Mesfield said respectfully, a faint unease stirring within him.
Queen Elizabeth slightly lifted her eyelids and asked lightly, "Do you know why I summoned you?"
"I....Mesfield hesitated, furrowed his brows, and said ruefully, "I know; we feel deeply sorry for failing to protect Luke."
At first Mesfield thought these deeds were done by Elgin the Great Swordsman; after learning the truth, he realized Elgin the Great Swordsman was merely among the White Tiger populace.
This left Mesfield with mixed feelings, feeling like a villain himself, yet Elgin the Great Swordsman is indeed a threat to the empire—an indisputable fact.
"Why are you so useless? Didn't I make things clear before departure?" Queen Elizabeth's tone was clearly angry, obviously having been driven to a certain point.
"We....Mesfield gritted his teeth, answering seriously, "We were momentarily careless; the enemy hid in the dark, setting up a magic barrier in advance, which separated us from Luke, so....so we...."
"Excuses, why didn't you guard beforehand! You've made things turn out like this!" Queen Elizabeth snapped angrily.
"Deeply sorry, we underestimated the enemy's obsession; we didn't expect that even gravely wounded, she would still try to assassinate Luke." Mesfield paused, adding, "The enemy's target was Elgin the Great Swordsman; Luke was merely an unfortunate scapegoat..."
"Not only did you fail to protect Luke, but you also let Elgin the Great Swordsman beat them into a pig's head, throwing away all the honor of the Purple Jasmine Knights!" Queen Elizabeth trembled with rage, recently vexed and overwhelmed, her anger now directed at the Thorn Knights.
"I have always been clear about rewards and punishments.
"Since you have made such a great mistake, you must pay the corresponding price!"
(皿')

title: Chapter 4 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 4 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 11 · Chapter 4

The four Thorn Knights below listened, and expressions of astonishment immediately appeared on their faces.

Indeed, the outcome they had feared most had come to pass.

From Queen Elizabeth's tone, it was clear she intended to hold the several knights accountable for the incident.

Melfield immediately raised his head. He felt the empire was in a precarious position right now.

If she insisted on assigning blame at a time like this, it hardly seemed like a good moment.

Of course, Melfield wasn't afraid of punishment—he was more concerned that if he were penalized, who would handle the disruptive element of House Ophrey on behalf of Her Majesty the Queen?

"Your Majesty, please calm your anger."

"Calm my anger? And what do you suggest I do to calm it?" Queen Elizabeth paused, then said in a complaining tone, "Now that Luke is dead, the only chance to appease House Ophrey has vanished completely. If I don't stay on high alert against them raising their rebel banners, can you blame me? Isn't all of this a consequence of your incompetence?"

"..."

Melfield was left speechless. She felt it was indeed partly related to her—if she had been more careful, she could surely have prevented Luke from being harmed.

But ultimately, Luke was merely a scapegoat for the Elgin Great Sword Master. If he hadn't impersonated the Great Sword Master, nothing would have happened at all.

"Moreover, we still haven't subdued the Elgin Great Sword Master! I laid out everything so meticulously, yet you kept disappointing me!" Queen Elizabeth's eyelids twitched violently, her mouth curled in continuous spasms, and it was as if steam were rising from the top of her head.

"Your Majesty, surely you are already aware—even Lord Gregory was knocked unconscious by the Elgin Great Sword Master. How could we possibly hope to subdue a non-human creature like him!" Melfield's heart pounded almost out of her chest, and her tone carried a trace of aggression. "Don't you understand? A powerhouse like the Elgin Great Sword Master is far beyond anything we can restrain. Peaceful reconciliation is far wiser than provoking conflict!"

"Silence! Melfield, you have enormous gall—are you attempting to subvert superiors with insubordination!?" Queen Elizabeth's face paled, and she glared at her with utter hatred.

"N-no..." Melfield lowered her head, tightly biting her silver-clenched teeth, looking thoroughly unwilling to accept this.

"I know the Elgin Great Sword Master's strength cannot be easily overcome, but if someone seeks to rise above royal authority, I absolutely will not permit it!" Queen Elizabeth spoke decisively, leaving no room for negotiation whatsoever.

Melfield's brows were furrowed so tightly they seemed impossible to unlock, the worry etched across her forehead. "But... but we really have done our utmost..."

Actually, Melfield felt somewhat inadequate—every time she faced the Elgin Great Sword Master, she couldn't unleash her full strength. A single spittle from that opponent had left her in an extremely passive position, utterly unable to resist.

"Enough. I no longer wish to hear those pale and weak explanations. Starting today, you will lose your identities as Thorn Knights, and then be imprisoned in the imperial dungeon to await sentencing." Queen Elizabeth spoke in a cold tone. This was her verdict—completely unforgiving.

"No..." Millius wiped a bead of cold sweat from his forehead, his expression somewhat displeased.

Even Winifred and Morrison's faces flickered with dissatisfaction.

It was clear the several Thorn Knights deeply resented such punishment—it was a little too excessive.

Melfield raised her head and looked straight at Elizabeth upon the throne. "Your Majesty, yes, failing to subdue the Elgin Great Sword Master was indeed due to our insufficient ability, but the matter with Luke was entirely brought about by House Ophrey's greed. Therefore, I beg you to grant us one more opportunity—we will certainly prove useful again."

"I have already given you many opportunities, yet you failed to seize them properly. It would be best if you reflected in the prison cell." Queen Elizabeth's thin lips parted slightly—merciless and cruel.

"Your Majesty! Now is precisely when the empire is descending into chaos—a time when talent is most needed! Imprisoning us is truly inappropriate. Please consider this more carefully!" Melfield said very unwillingly. If she herself were locked up, who would lead the entire Bauhinia Knight Order?

"There is nothing inappropriate about it. After all, the four of you are no different from good-for-nothings. Moreover, the other Thorn Knights have already returned to the royal capital—there is simply no need for you at the moment." Queen Elizabeth said calmly, as though she had long since made up her mind.

Just as Melfield was about to say something further, Millius suddenly rose to his feet.

"Ah—! I'm absolutely fed up. I refuse to be imprisoned!"

This disrespectful act frightened everyone present—even Catherine beside Elizabeth stirred slightly.

"Millius, what are you doing?" Melfield frowned delicately.

"What's the matter?" Millius directly drew the slender sword at his waist, his gaze casual and indifferent. "Of course I must fight for my own freedom. I don't care about being a Thorn Knight anymore, but if you want to lock me up—sorry, I won't compromise."

Millius's action was nothing short of gross disrespect—having the audacity to draw his weapon inside the great hall was a clear sign he held no regard for Queen Elizabeth at all.

The sudden outbreak of conflict left everyone somewhat astonished, sensing that things could easily escalate into a life-and-death struggle within the great hall.

Millius was not someone who could be manipulated at will. Since the queen had already torn off her kindly mask, he felt no need to maintain his reverence either. He had already decided to leave the Bauhinia Knight Order.

"Please calm down—don't do this." Morrison's expression darkened. He felt Millius was already losing his composure.

"Yes, put your sword away quickly, or else Her Majesty won't limit herself to merely locking us up." Winifred couldn't help but chime in.

"Everyone, please wake up! Rather than throwing my life away for an unreasonable person, I'd rather be dead! Don't you see it yourselves?" Millius's eyes widened as he spoke earnestly. "Her Majesty has become increasingly strange—it's like she's a completely different person from before! To achieve her goals, she has become reckless and abandoned all caution!"

None of the other Thorn Knights spoke. Their expressions darkened alongside his. They weren't fools—they could see Queen Elizabeth's temperament had fundamentally shifted, though they dared not say much about it.

Elizabeth upon the throne grew dark-faced, a layer of frost descending over her features.

"Are you serious, Millius...?"

"Absolutely correct!" Millius aimed the slender sword in his hand directly at Elizabeth upon the throne, speaking without any reservation, "What kind of Thorn Knights is this? I quit! From now on, I'm leaving the royal capital and claiming my freedom! Henceforth, I shall have nothing to do with the royal family!"

Millius's tone was decisive, without the slightest hesitation. He was resolutely determined to turn his back on the royal family.

The other Thorn Knights' expressions flickered uncertainly, unsure of what to think.

Melfield felt as though a sharp file were sawing back and forth through her heart—she dearly wished not to witness this scene.

"When did freedom become something so cheap?" Queen Elizabeth said coldly, then gave a subtle glance toward Catherine beside her—

"Catherine."

"Move. Suppress and subdue all these treacherous rebels who have committed the gravest crimes!"

title: Chapter 5 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 5 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes

Volume 11 · Chapter 5

Ding-dong--

Katherine, who had been silent, slightly raised her wand and tapped the ground below, producing a crisp sound.

The gravity barrier magic laid out in the hall suddenly activated!

The floor of the grand hall lit up with gray magic arrays, and the pressure within the space changed, increasing severalfold all at once!

This surging pressure bore down almost entirely on Messelfield and the other three, instantly suppressing them!

This barrier magic was filled with tremendous magical power, and it had taken considerable effort to set up. Combined with the fact that Catherine herself was an expert in barrier magic, the effect after activation was naturally extraordinary.

The pressure within the magic array surged dramatically, making it impossible for anyone to stand upright, as if several great mountains had crashed down.

This barrier magic could amplify gravity, and in a minute's time, it could press down on anyone who resisted, making them unable to lift their heads.

Vivian and Morrison were crushed by the enormous gravity right on the spot, their faces pressed against the ground, unable to move.

Both of their faces were somewhat distorted, like two little insects stuck to the ground, and the floor cracked under the pressure with a crisp sound!

From this moment on, Catherine's formidable strength became evident—at a ratio of one against two, no less. Although she was always closing her eyes and acting very low-key, she was clearly no weakling!

Vivian lay on the ground, sweating coldly, thinking, "She had already set up an ambush?"

"That bitch Catherine... doesn't even spare any feelings..." Morrison gritted his teeth and resisted the gravity, veins bulging on his forehead.

Milieth was still trying to resist, golden battle qi surging within him, attempting to push back against that massive gravity.

However, this gravity barrier had been carefully laid out. If it were so easy to resist, Catherine would likely have been ruined.

"Ploosh"—with a loud crash, Milieth, unable to withstand the pressure, fell to his knees, shattering the tiles beneath him!

The ground beneath Milieth's supporting hands cracked further and further, like a dense spiderweb, as his golden battle qi burned fiercely.

He glared with fiery eyes at Catherine, who was calmly resting with her eyes closed, unwilling to surrender so easily, repeatedly resisting the several-fold gravity field!

In the end, Milieth's strength was limited, and he was violently crushed into the ground, with no suspense whatsoever.

"Damn it!"

After all, Catherine had secured the advantage of timing and terrain, so Milieth's defeat in the struggle was entirely normal.

Several guards, wielding sealing collars that suppressed magical power and battle qi, approached and promptly placed them around Vivian and Milieth's necks, instantly reducing them to cripples, collapsing on the ground.

Although the Thorn Knights were each very strong, once sealed by the collars, no matter how powerful they were normally, they would become ordinary people, unable to struggle or resist.

Captain Chapman approached Morrison's side and awkwardly said, "I'm sorry, Lord Morrison. I was just following orders."

"It's fine." Morrison gritted his teeth, his eyebrows trembling with anger.

Chapman thought for a moment, then placed the sealing collar around Morrison's neck. Without battle qi to support him, he immediately lost all strength and collapsed onto the ground.

Queen Elizabeth watched these guys all lying on the ground, motionless, as if bowing to her, and felt greatly satisfied.

However, there was still one person who hadn't fallen—Messelfield, who remained steadily standing in the grand hall.

Even though the ground beneath Messelfield's feet was already cracked, and despite the intense gravity, she stood firm and unshaken.

A guard holding a sealing collar saw Messelfield's indomitable stance and hesitated to move forward, fearing that one careless move would cost him his life.

Messelfield's expression was filled with resentment, her lips bitten until they turned white, her eyes burning with flames of fury.

She felt that the Queen's actions were too extreme. Even though the mission had failed, she had still made contributions.

Such disrespect—wouldn't the Queen eventually lose everyone's support?

Wasn't this the kind-hearted Elizabeth who used to enjoy jokes?

She had become just like that tyrannical Isabella! How did this happen?!

Messelfield looked at the Queen on the throne—not only Milieth, but even she herself wanted to rise up in rebellion.

"Messelfield, what look is that..." Queen Elizabeth's expression turned serious as she said, "Are you also planning to defy my orders?"

Messelfield's lips moved but she couldn't speak, struggling internally. She was still reminiscing about the old Elizabeth, who had been like an older sister to her.

Queen Elizabeth narrowed her eyes and glanced at Catherine beside her, signaling her to increase the power.

Catherine, with her eyes closed, nodded slightly and tapped her wand against the ground again with a crisp sound.

The gravity within the barrier magic array surged once more, several more times, and the entire floor of the grand hall could no longer withstand the pressure and began to collapse.

Yet Messelfield remained unmoved, still standing firm in the center of it all.

Although Messelfield was very uncomfortable, she managed to endure this gravity.

Catherine's eyelids fluttered slightly, and for the third time, she struck her wand against the ground. The gravity in the barrier increased several more times!

At this point, the pressure within the magic array had become terrifyingly intense—this gravity could easily crush a person into mincemeat.

Yet Messelfield, who was not the First Thorn Knight for nothing, remained unaffected, only beginning to shiver slightly.

She felt the excruciating gravity, as if several sacred mountains were pressing down on her shoulders.

Truly worthy of Catherine, who excelled in barrier magic—she could suppress all four Thorn Knights with her own power alone, a truly remarkable strength!

Normally so quiet and unassuming, who would have thought that when she finally showed a bit of her power, it would be so astonishing!

Messelfield broke into a cold sweat on her forehead, and the ground beside her had already turned to powder under the intense gravity, forming a terrifying large pit.

Seeing Messelfield still resisting, Catherine couldn't help but pout, raising her wand to increase the gravity further, intending to finally crush the First Knight.

But just as she lifted the wand halfway into the air, Catherine slowly lowered it again, realizing that if she continued to pour in more magical power, the entire palace would likely collapse instantly.

Catherine had no choice but to descend, picking up the sealing collar from a guard's hand and approaching Messelfield.

Messelfield saw Catherine's tightly closed eyes, yet she could sense the gaze like an abyss.

"Messelfield, don't resist. His Majesty has no intention of killing you—he only plans to hold you for a while. This is all just a temporary measure in these chaotic times." Catherine finally spoke, her voice sounding like a moving nightingale.

"Why did you have to go to such extremes?" Messelfield pushed against the force, squinting her eyes to ask.

"The Emperor's intentions are not for you and me to guess. We only need to obey." Catherine paused, then countered, "Didn't you used to tell me that you would be willing to sacrifice your life for loyalty? So why are you resisting now? Does your loyalty mean so little?"

Messelfield bit her lip and fell silent. The straightforward girl truly didn't want to betray her oath.

Catherine showed no hesitation, placing the sealing collar on Messelfield's neck herself, completing the suppression of the Thorn Knights.

Messelfield felt her body go limp, unable to muster any strength, her battle qi vanishing like it had never existed, collapsing to the ground with a thud.

At this moment, all four Thorn Knights were suppressed by Catherine, and the mission was completed smoothly.

Catherine looked down at Messelfield and said with a calm tone:

"You should all take this opportunity to rest."

"The rest is best left to others."

"Although your rank is first among the Thorn Knights, there are still those stronger than you in the ranks."

"Stronger than... me?"

title: Chapter 6 — Ox Three
content:
Chapter 6 — Ox Three

Volume 11 · Chapter 6

Merlin made no real resistance in the end and was subdued by Catherine, who then placed a sealing collar on her, reducing her to an ordinary person.

Her silence stemmed from the hope she still held for Elizabeth, and she didn’t want to break the oath she had taken when becoming a knight.

Merlin glanced at Catherine, then at Elizabeth seated on the throne, her gaze flickering with obvious reluctance.

Catherine, who had been keeping her eyes closed, hadn’t been joking earlier. The order of the Thorn Knights wasn’t determined by strength.

Besides the Thorn Knights who had already appeared, there were indeed others who weren’t inferior to Merlin—some even held the upper hand.

When Elizabeth saw Merlin subdued and the sealing collar placed around her neck, she finally exhaled in slight relief.

She looked down at the four knights kneeling on the ground and spoke in a voice so cold it could freeze the air:

“Take them down and lock them in the imperial prison!”

Several guards stepped forward, pressing down on the four Thorn Knights and leading them out to be sent to the strictly guarded imperial prison.

“Damn it, you should have resisted with me just now!” Millius grumbled angrily.

“Shut up,” Morrison snapped, his brows knitted into a tight knot. “Complaining won’t solve anything.”

“Maybe this punishment is only temporary. We should stay calm,” Winifred remained relatively composed, unlike Millius’s restless frustration.

As Merlin was led away, she kept glancing back at Elizabeth, finding it unbearable to be locked up like this.

Chapman, responsible for the escort, saw Merlin’s reluctance and awkwardly said, “Merlin, we—”

Merlin pulled her gaze away and replied in a haughty tone, “Let me go. I’ll walk myself.”

The guards escorting Merlin looked at Chapman, seemingly unwilling to make their own decision.

Chapman considered Merlin’s character and nodded reassuringly, “Let her go.”

The guards released Merlin, giving her a degree of freedom as a show of respect for the Thorn Knight.

Merlin strode out of the hall without a backward glance.

But before leaving, her peripheral vision caught sight of a golden-haired girl in the corner of the hall—

The girl wore a snow-white silk gown handmade by the palace, and a silver crown rested on her head.

She looked innocent and lovely, with delicate eyebrows like crescent moons, and a slender yet graceful figure—somewhat resembling Elizabeth.

Judging by her appearance, she was young, timidly hiding behind a pillar while stealing glances at Merlin.

Merlin stared at the girl and instinctively muttered, “Michelle.”

Chapman, seeing Merlin pause, couldn’t help but remind her, “Merlin, we should hurry.”

Merlin hesitated, as if wanting to speak to Michelle, but the situation didn’t allow it.

She gave Michelle a doting look before resolutely leaving.

Michelle watched as Merlin was led away, her face betraying deep concern as she clutched her chest, crumpling her clothes. “Winchester...”

This girl named Michelle was Elizabeth’s own daughter and the empire’s first successor.

In the palace, no one was suitable to accompany Michelle, to chat with her, or to let her express the emotions she dared not show her mother.

Only Merlin would often come to keep Michelle company, and over time, she became like a sister and friend.

To Merlin, Michelle always reminded her of Elizabeth in her youth, so she grew fond of the princess.

Michelle had always treated Merlin as her closest companion. When she heard that her mother had summoned Merlin angrily, she came to check on her out of worry.

But she witnessed the worst possible outcome—Merlin was about to be imprisoned by her mother?!

Michelle’s heart was filled with anxiety. She wanted to save Merlin but dared not anger Elizabeth.

Since her mother’s sister died, Elizabeth’s temperament had changed drastically, making Michelle feel uneasy and afraid to speak freely.

Watching Merlin being imprisoned, Michelle felt helpless, standing there in despair.

After the four Thorn Knights were led away, Catherine turned to Elizabeth and asked, “Your Majesty, how should we handle them?”

Elizabeth rubbed her temples and spoke indifferently, “Lock them up first, then write a letter to Duke Overley, informing him that the knights responsible for protecting Luke have been imprisoned and asking him to come to the capital personally to deal with them.”

Catherine’s eyelashes fluttered as she cautiously asked, “Your Majesty intends to let Duke Overley execute them himself?”

“Of course not. This is just a gesture of goodwill, a signal of reconciliation, to flatter him. If Overley backs down now, it will be a happy ending for everyone.” Elizabeth analyzed.

Catherine gradually understood Elizabeth’s meaning. She didn’t actually want to imprison Merlin and the other four Thorn Knights—she just needed a pretext to give Duke Overley an easy way out.

By showing goodwill and baiting him, the rest would be much simpler.

But was it really that easy? The only heir of the Overley family was dead, and the aging duke had no chance of having children, effectively cutting off the Overley family’s bloodline. This was a grudge that could never be reconciled.

Catherine raised her head and looked at Elizabeth, cautiously asking, “Your Majesty, if Duke Overley really comes to the capital, do you truly intend to reconcile?”

Elizabeth let out a cold laugh. “How could that be? That old fool Overley can’t have children anymore. Luke’s death is a disaster for his family—if he dares come to the capital, I’ll kill him at any cost and erase the Overley family from imperial history forever, eliminating any future threats.”

Elizabeth’s eyes burned with killing intent, her expression colder than frost.

Catherine said nothing, keeping her eyes closed, her thoughts inscrutable.

“Still, we must prepare for defense in case the Overley family makes a desperate last stand. The empire’s military forces have already moved toward northern England. I think Overley has noticed, and the end is near. After this, I’ll need to meet with the various regional lords....” Elizabeth paused, then remembered something. “Oh, right—Hamilton, Dexter, and Emanuel, the three Thorn Knights, have returned, haven’t they? Why aren’t they here to see me now? I need them at a time like this—their strength is indispensable.”

“They returned last night. By the time—”

Catherine’s words were cut off as the heavy doors of the hall were slowly pulled open.

Knights clad in exquisite, elegant armor and draped in crimson hollyhock war cloaks entered the hall—

The three new Thorn Knights had arrived.

title: Chapter 7 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 7 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 11 · Chapter 7

The three Thorn Knights who had just returned to the capital yesterday wore expressions of varying intensity, exuding an aura of sharp intelligence and formidable strength from afar.

Each was clad in spotless armor, their crimson battle cloaks billowing behind them as they marched.

Two of the Thorn Knights were warriors—one a swordsman, the other a warrior wielding a battle-axe. Bringing up the rear was a mage, a floating magic crystal ball hovering in their hands, lending an unsettling air to their presence.

The third Thorn Knight, Dexter, was a renowned warrior of the Thistle Knight Order, a powerhouse among the twelve Thorn Knights. Even among his peers, Dexter’s strength ranked among the highest.
