Few could stand against him in direct combat; most were crushed instantly by his overwhelming, devastating force.

Dexter’s battle-axe techniques were infamous for their brutality. He had once fought three Saint-tier warriors without yielding an inch, and once thrown into battle, he became a blood-drenched berserker, his axe reaping lives without mercy. Known as the Unmatched Beast of Britain, his reputation struck fear into enemies before they even drew breath—sometimes, his name alone was enough to break their will to fight.

The sixth Thorn Knight, Emmanuel, was a traditional British swordsman, wielding a broadsword of England. He excelled in rapid strikes and had a deep-seated rivalry with Milieu, finding the latter’s effeminate arrogance deeply grating.

Though Emmanuel was impatient and disliked delays, his skill was a match for Milieu’s, their strength nearly equal. He kept a low profile, rarely appearing in public, but his efficiency was undeniable. Though not widely renowned in the empire, he was no one to underestimate.

Due to his hot temper, Emmanuel’s standing within the Thistle Knight Order was poor, and he was not well-liked by the other Thorn Knights. Once, during a mission, he drew his sword without hesitation and attacked Mesfield when the latter’s hesitation frustrated him. The speed of his strike was terrifying, leaving Mesfield under immense pressure.

Both warriors were built powerfully—broad shoulders, thick chests, radiating raw strength and a sensual, muscular presence. Yet Dexter towered over Emmanuel, his frame far more imposing, like an armored colossus.

The last was the tenth Thorn Knight, Hamill, a gaunt figure who looked as though a strong wind could topple him. His cheekbones jutted sharply, his face sunken, his hair greasy and clumped together, with streaks of pale white. Deep wrinkles marred his face, one eye larger than the other, and his teeth had a slight overbite, giving him a lecherous appearance.

Hamill likely knew his appearance dragged down the Thorn Knights’ collective allure, so he habitually wore his cloak’s hood low, keeping a discreet profile.

“Never judge a book by its cover” perfectly described Hamill. Though he often carried a crystal ball—making him seem like a suspicious fortune-teller—his true power was formidable. Known as the Empire’s Dreamweaver, his illusions were masterful, blurring the line between reality and deception. He could conjure terrifying visions, striking fear into enemies before they even struck, blending trickery with magic.

Many asked what Hamill’s crystal ball was for if not divination. His answer was always the same: *“To create the most real world.”*

Now, the three Thorn Knights had returned and entered the grand hall to pay homage to Queen Elizabeth.

They saw the devastation within the hall and exchanged glances of mild confusion before dismissing it.

The three knelt before the queen’s throne, heads bowed.

“Your Majesty, it’s been a while,” Dexter spoke first, his voice deep and thunderous.

“Your return is welcome,” Elizabeth said, probing gently. “Have you heard about the recent unrest in the empire—Elgin the Great Swordmaster and the unrest among the Overley family?”

“Indeed,” Dexter replied earnestly. “We’ve heard of Elgin’s rampage and the Overley family’s recent agitation.”

“What are your thoughts on the matter?” the queen pressed.

“Apart from thinking Mesfield is useless and the Thorn Knights guarding the capital are incompetent, we have no other opinions,” Dexter said bluntly.

Elizabeth laughed softly. “Why do you say that?”

“To be humiliated by a fugitive like this? Mesfield’s incompetence has disgraced the Thistle Knight Order. If we had been here, the outcome would have been different,” Dexter said with a smirk.

“Exactly,” Emmanuel scoffed, his tone dripping with disdain. “Mesfield is a weakling. If she had been decisive, things wouldn’t have escalated this far. In short, she’s useless. If I’d been there, I’d have eliminated her first.”

“Hahaha, terrifying,” Hamill chuckled darkly from the side.

Elizabeth clapped her hands in amusement, clearly pleased. “Bringing you back was the right choice. With you here, things wouldn’t have spiraled this badly.”

“Of course,” Dexter said respectfully. “Compared to Mesfield’s hesitation, our efficiency far surpasses hers. No one could serve Your Majesty better.”

“As Your Majesty’s blade, we need no thoughts of our own—only to turn Your Majesty’s will into dust,” Hamill said, his voice raspy and unsettling.

Elizabeth approved of their answer, which perfectly matched her expectations. “Your presence gives me great comfort. Though Elgin remains the empire’s greatest threat, he can wait—for now, there’s a more dangerous enemy circling us.”

“Your Majesty speaks of the restless Overley family?” Dexter asked seriously.

“Precisely,” Elizabeth nodded. “The Overleys are expanding rapidly, likely plotting to overthrow the empire. Our top priority is eliminating that old fool.”

“Then we’ll handle it,” Emmanuel said, raising his head, his eyes burning with fervor. “We’ll wipe out the entire Overley family in a few days.”

“After that, we’ll deal with that arrogant Elgin the Great Swordmaster.”

“Frankly, I’ve heard his name so much since returning, my ears are numb. If possible, I’d like to sever his head now and present it to Your Majesty.”

(ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ*:･ﾟ✧

title: Chapter 8 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 8 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 11 · Chapter 8

Queen Elizabeth heard Emmanuel's words but said nothing.

The three Bramble Knights had just returned, and they were clearly still unfamiliar with Great Sword Saint Elgin. They may not even know that he had beaten Gregory to the point of serious injury and unconsciousness.

That was why they dismissed him so lightly. Otherwise, they would have been far more careful.

Elizabeth did not care about such talk. She still had her trump cards, and it would suffice if the Bramble Knights could offer some assistance.

"There is no need to rush. The Aulfray family is the empire's arsenal. If possible, I do not want to cause excessive damage. As for Great Sword Saint Elgin, we can set that aside for now."

"Then what does Your Majesty plan to do?" Dexter asked tentatively.

"I will write a letter to Grand Duke Aulfray to probe the boundaries. You three should avoid traveling around recently and remain in the capital on standby," Elizabeth said seriously.

"Yes, Your Majesty."

Dexter and Hamilton had no objections and chose to follow the queen's wishes.

But Emmanuel wore a displeased expression. The impatient man detested waiting.

"Your Majesty, dealing with the Aulfray family, wouldn't it be simpler to just charge right in and eliminate them directly?"

"I have heard Grand Duke Aulfray has recruited several Saint-tier warriors alongside a large number of mercenaries. Among them are undoubtedly powerful individuals. We still need to be cautious." Elizabeth looked up at the three below her. "You are all my treasures. I do not want anything to happen to you."

"Thank you for your concern, Your Majesty, but I doubt the Aulfray family could recruit anyone truly formidable. Mercenaries are just people who work for coin — they have no fighting will at all. Most are nothing but worthless frauds."

"I think the same way. Heh heh heh—" Hamilton let out a series of gloomy laughs.

"Your Majesty need not worry excessively. Though the Aulfray family is powerful, they are nowhere near strong enough to threaten your rule. If you wish, we are willing to serve as the vanguard in crushing the rebels." Dexter spoke with a serious expression.

"I simply do not wish to wage a war without proper preparation. Once Seth returns, we will have near certainty of wiping out the Aulfray family head-on." Elizabeth said earnestly.

"Seth is coming back too?!" Dexter widened his eyes in visible surprise.

Seth was the second-ranked Bramble Knight. Though he had not been a member for long, his formidable strength had won the respect of many knights.

"That is right. That man's strength is no inferior to Maysfield's — he may even hold a slight edge." Elizabeth paused, then added with a smile,

"I intend for Seth to replace Maysfield."

The next day.

The first rays of morning sunlight poured in, making the entire rental room bright and cheerful.

Merlin woke with messy hair, looking quite disheveled, and groggily held his breakfast.

No one knew what Merlin had been doing the night before. He looked listless, dark circles under his eyes, completely drained of energy.

Alice had gone out early to pick up the newspaper and was not in the room at the moment.

The two of them subscribed to the paper whenever they had nothing better to do, reading the latest news so they would not be left behind by the times.

Merlin cut into his fried egg with a knife and fork, looking every bit like an elderly person, trembling as he brought the egg toward his mouth.

At that moment, *bang* —

Alice suddenly pushed open the door and came back in, holding a newspaper, her face flushed and beaming with excitement.

"Good news! Merlin, good news!!!"

Merlin was startled by the excited Alice and jerked violently — the fried egg on his fork *splat* onto the floor.

His expression darkened instantly. He stared at the ruined egg, feeling both sorry and heartbroken for the waste.

Could such a disaster strike so early in the morning? This had to be a bad omen.

He looked up at Alice, his face full of resentment, and said in an irritated tone,

"What are you doing?! Can't you be quiet in the morning?!"

"..." Alice saw Merlin's sour mood and huffed angrily. "Why are you being so fierce? I'm here to tell you good news!"

"What good news? Did my fifty-thousand-gold horse racing ticket finally win?" Merlin asked impatiently, still unwilling to accept his cursed luck.

Alice was speechless at his question. With his luck so catastrophically low it practically touched the earth's core, there was no way he would win anything. Still dreaming of sudden wealth? Keep dreaming — in dreams, anything is possible.

Seeing Alice stay silent, Merlin assumed she had silently confirmed it. His eyes widened, and an uncontrollable tremor surged through his heart.

Oh heavens! The Goddess of Fortune has not completely abandoned me yet! What is meant to come, will come!

In no time, I will get promoted and a raise, become general manager, take the CEO position, marry a beautiful rich woman, and reach the pinnacle of life. Just thinking about it makes me a little excited, hehe~~

Merlin felt his utterly jinxed fate might still be salvageable — he was not yet beyond redemption.

"Hey... wake up. Stop dreaming and think about something real."

Alice raised her hand, wanting to rap Merlin on the forehead.

But she did not dare to actually hit him, so she dejectedively lowered her arm.

"How could you possibly win?! My savings were definitely squandered by you, with not even a splash heard!"

"Tch!" Merlin was instantly disappointed, his interest vanishing completely. He asked carelessly, "Then what's the good news? Are you so happy because the silly bear underwear at the tailor shop went on sale?"

Alice's face flushed red, and she pointed at him in anger. "Do not joke about my underwear! My habits do not need criticism from someone like you!"

"..." Merlin snorted, poked the egg on the floor back up with his fork. "Then what's the good news? I'll listen, I suppose."

"This."

Alice unfolded the newspaper in her hands and held it up for Merlin to see, saying seriously, "That Luke before — was a fake Elgin the Great Sword Saint. The real one is someone else entirely!"

"Hmm?" Merlin put down his knife and fork and narrowed his eyes at the bold, black headline on the paper —

「A Royal-Devised Lie: Luke Was the Fake Elgin the Great Sword Saint!? The True Hero Still Lurks Somewhere in the Crowd!」

Merlin gave a helpless smile, thinking this news had finally reached the public. He wondered what that human queen planned to do about it.

But none of this surprised him. He had been there, after all.

"Oh, Luke was the fake Elgin the Great Sword Saint. And then?"

"And isn't this thrilling news?!" Alice clasped her hands together, her eyes sparkling, muttering to herself.

"I knew it! How could the man I admire be like that?"

"It seems the real Elgin the Great Sword Saint is indeed someone else!"

"What should we do?"

"The more I think about it, the more I feel the real Elgin the Great Sword Saint must be a remarkable man, so mysteri—..."

After hearing this, Merlin rolled his eyes and pressed a hand to his forehead, helplessly thinking:

Damn it!

It reignited so easily?

Can you not fantasize in front of me, of all people?

Don't I, the Great Demon Lord, deserve some dignity?.....

(∞叭)

Volume 6 has refreshed itself. The morning update has already been replaced.

title: Chapter 9 — Letter
content:
Chapter 9 — Letter

Volume 11 · Chapter 9

Alice finished speaking and couldn’t resist glancing at Merlin out of the corner of her eye, as if checking for any reaction.

This was also a test, really—if Merlin were jealous, he’d surely explode like thunder.

But Merlin didn’t even flinch, let alone react. His face barely changed at all, as if he hadn’t heard a word.

“Elgin the Great Blade Master is *so* handsome, way better than you...”

Alice wasn’t giving up so easily, adding another sentence to see if she could provoke him.

But Merlin stayed the same, even nodding this time. “Yeah, he’s great. Really stands out.”

Alice’s face instantly turned ugly—first pale, then red, her whole body trembling with rage.

She slammed her fist down on the table with a *bang*, making it echo loudly.

“What’s wrong with you? Can’t you give *any* reaction?”

Merlin put down his chopsticks, not liking being interrupted during breakfast. “What do you *want*?”

“I’m praising Elgin the Great Blade Master! Why aren’t you jealous?” Alice demanded, indignant.

“???” Merlin’s brain was full of question marks as he spread his hands. “Why would I be jealous?”

Alice’s face burned red. *Of course* her *nominal* husband would praise other men—it was unnatural for him not to be jealous! Any normal person would feel uneasy. Unless Merlin didn’t care about her at all.

She deliberately muttered, slurring her words on purpose. *You’re at least a male, right? Fighting for mating rights is instinct, isn’t it? And… and I’m your nominal wife. Getting jealous would be the bare minimum of respect for me.*

“???” Merlin’s entire expression twisted in confusion, utterly baffled by Alice’s train of thought. “Why would praising someone else have anything to do with me? And if I *were* jealous, that wouldn’t make us fake husband and wife—it’d make us *real* hus—”

Alice’s breath hitched, her face flushing as she fell silent. Her heart raced—*right*, if he got *really* jealous, wouldn’t that make us a real couple?

Merlin saw Alice’s silence and her flushed cheeks, his eyes widening as his expression shifted.

“Hey… you—you don’t actually like me, do you? Trying to turn fake into real…?”

Alice jolted like a cat with its tail stepped on, her face twisting through a series of expressions in rapid succession.

Her cheeks burned crimson, as if she’d drunk too much, and she stammered out an explanation before she could think.

“…N-no way! A-A-Absolutely not! A=!”

“Look at you—*disgusting*. I’d *never* like you!”

“…Fake into real? What nonsense! Unless I’m blind!”

“I’m going to train now… you just stay home and have your *white daydreams*, huh~!”

As soon as she finished, Alice spun around and bolted out the door, not even glancing back—afraid Merlin would misread her.

Merlin stared at Alice’s reddening ears, his expression growing more confused by the second, lost in thought.

Alice slammed the door shut with a *bang* and vanished from Merlin’s sight.

Merlin pulled his gaze back, staring down at the dust-covered fried egg on his plate, muttering to himself in bewilderment.

“Is Alice losing her mind? Does the Inheritance Crystal have side effects like this? I’ve never heard of that…”

Merlin thought Alice had gotten *weird* lately. Before, she’d always looked at him with disgust, like he was a fly. Now she’d blush when she saw him—just like those love-struck girls outside.

Merlin’s mood was a mess. Alice seemed to have feelings for him, but her words were just as sharp as ever. Was he imagining things? Maybe Alice didn’t mean anything by it—he was just overthinking.

Or… maybe he was the one developing *unusual* feelings for this *mopboard*?

“Shit.”

Merlin clapped a hand over his mouth, his eyes wide with shock as he carefully reconsidered in his head.

*Calm down.*

We’re just symbiotic. We’re just paying off that massive debt so we can go our separate ways. There’s *no* way love could happen—this is ridiculous. I must be losing it. I should go wash my face.

Alice leaned against the door, head bowed, but didn’t rush off. Her mind was in chaos.

*What am I thinking?!*

Why was she so desperate for Merlin’s reaction?

Now she was *obsessing* over his thoughts—was she really starting to like this jerk?!

Alice’s face burned, and she instinctively covered it, mortified. She’d have to be *way* more subtle next time, or Merlin would notice something—this was *way* too embarrassing.

But then she replayed Merlin’s words in her head: *“If I got *really* jealous, that wouldn’t make us fake husband and wife—it’d make us *real* husband and wife.”*

Her heart suddenly raced, her whole body twisting with awkwardness, nothing like her usual sharp, confident self.

Alice *had* been hoping Merlin would get jealous. Even if he didn’t react, she could still indulge in her fantasies.

Alice was lost in her daydream when a sudden chill ran down her spine, like she’d been locked in the gaze of something malevolent.

In the shadows, Jenna’s face darkened as she glared at Alice, her nails scraping against the wall with a *skritch skritch* sound, muttering bitterly to herself.

*Damn it. Merlin’s not even leaving the house today?*

*Why does this airhead have to show up?*

*I’ve been hiding here all night…*

---

**England, Northern Region.**
**The Magical Beast Forest Frontline.**

This was the territory of the Overley family, also serving as the empire’s armory.

Merchant-soldiers would often sell their magical beast materials here, which the Overley family would then process into sharp weapons, distributing them across the empire. It was a natural treasure trove.

This was also the densest area for mercenaries in the country. Unlike adventurers, mercenaries had far more income streams—besides paid missions, they could hunt magical beasts for resale. Adventurers, on the other hand, rarely found sellable rare materials; their job was mostly solving problems for others.

The number of free mercenaries dwarfed that of adventurers, scattered across the world. Some even grew into mercenary bands, conquering territories and becoming state-sponsored warlords.

After all, mercenaries had no barriers to entry—anyone could join. While adventurers were free, they still had guild regulations.

At that moment, in the duke’s manor, the queen’s personal letter had been delivered to the study.

The message was clear and concise: the Uprising Knights who failed to protect Luke had been imprisoned, and the Overley Duke was summoned to the capital for judgment. The queen deeply regretted the unfortunate demise of the noble son and requested the duke to grieve appropriately.

Duke Overley’s eyes bulged with fury. The angrier he got, the darker his face turned, veins throbbing on his forehead. Finally, he couldn’t hold back—he tore the queen’s letter to shreds and hurled it to the ground, roaring:

“Damn *Elizabeth*!”

“You think I’m a fool?!”

title: Chapter 10 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 10 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 11 · Chapter 10

Overfrey Duke was so angry his whole body was trembling, crumpling up Elizabeth's handwritten letter into pieces, feeling his dignity had been insulted.

His head looked very small, almost shrinking into his shoulder blades.

On his head, only a few strands of gray-white hair covered it; his two sunk-in eyes were dull and lifeless, lacking any spirit.

Despite wearing extremely splendid noble attire, he still appeared spiritless.

It was probably because of the news of his son Luke's death that Overfrey was deeply struck, his whole person on the verge of collapse.

Luke was the only heir of the family, and the continuation of the entire family depended on him.

However, the unfortunate heavens had dealt a heavy blow to the entire Overfrey family. Even if they could rule the empire, they would face a predicament of no successors.

Now Overfrey was elderly, and it was only at over sixty that he had a son like Luke. Now he was over eighty.

To make an old man about to die get back on the bed and restore his vigor, even if he took pills, who knows if it would be useful!

So now Overfrey Duke no longer cared about replacing the British dynasty; his mind was full of revenge against the royal family, and he wouldn't let Elizabeth have an easy time even if he died.

"Overfrey Duke, what's wrong?"

A person of short stature, with a monkey-like appearance, walked over.

This person was named Gabry, the family steward and also Overfrey's trusted military advisor.

The suggestion to replace the British dynasty and have Luke impersonate Erkin Sword Master was also proposed by Gabry.

It was meant to raise the prestige of the Overfrey family and increase their cards for replacing the British dynasty.

Overfrey had always trusted Gabry, because the entire family's unprecedented prosperity was thanks to Gabry's counsel and strategy.

However, this time such a thing had happened, and Luke's death had struck Overfrey deeply, but he did not mean to blame Gabry.

After all, Gabry's motivation was always the prosperity of the Overfrey family; making some mistakes was understandable.

"Damn Elizabeth, actually wanting to use a few thorn knights as scapegoats so I won't investigate Luke's death!" Overfrey Duke was trembling with anger. Zhou Han

"This indeed is a bit too much..." Gabry nodded. With his short stature, he only reached Overfrey's knee.

"This damn Elizabeth, she just likes to play small tricks, and wants to trick me into going to the royal capital—it's simply a dream!" Overfrey Duke heavily slapped the table.

"This must absolutely not go; the situation is now extremely sensitive. With Elizabeth's cruel character, she will probably kill you on the spot to eliminate future troubles. If something happens to you, the entire Overfrey family might disappear just like that!" Gabry said seriously.

"I know, if I go, I probably won't be able to come back. Speaking with fists is often more effective than with words." Overfrey Duke responded calmly.

"Exactly. Next, we just need to prepare to conquer the empire with force; completely no need to compromise with Elizabeth." Gabry paused, then continued, "Now your family is strong in troops and horses, with formidable power, and more than several Saint-tier powerhouses have joined. You are fully capable of fighting the royalty without any worries."

"That's right. Now I don't need to look at the royalty's face to act. Bringing the Overfrey family to a new height is my pursuit."

Overfrey Duke nodded, his mood slightly eased.

"Overfrey Duke, the timing is already mature. I think we can set out on an expedition immediately upon starting today, crush the British dynasty, and for the sake of Young Master Luke, I think there's no need to hesitate any longer." Gabry suggested, his eyes shining.

"...Overfrey Duke seems to have some hesitation," Elizabeth was beside him with many thorn knights. "Can our current power really crush them?"

"It's enough. I can guarantee it with my own life," Gabry approached Overfrey Duke and said seriously, "Now we have nine Saint-tier powerhouses. Among them, five are mercenaries who have licked the blade's edge, rich in combat experience, and there is also the Elemental Four Sword Saint who came from the Chaotic Sea—a superpowerful existence. How can those few thorn knights compare?"

"...Overfrey Duke clearly hesitated for a while, pondering whether to follow Gabry's advice."

"Not to mention those combat-experienced mercenaries. Single-handedly, the four Sword Saints can easily crush the thorn knights. The imperial throne is already in our pocket," Gabry's eyes grew hot. Redding

"But the royalty still has their cards. They have been able to stand firm on this land for 400 years naturally because they have other foundations that others cannot shake." Overfrey Duke said with an unhappy brow, as if even now with strong troops and horses, he still felt apprehensive toward Elizabeth.

"Still have cards? Impossible! I've carefully investigated all the thorn knights; there should be no one who is an opponent of the Elemental Four Sword Saints..."

Gabry furrowed his brow, feeling Overfrey Duke's concern was unnecessary.

"Overfrey Duke, you still underestimate the British dynasty too much. Having defeated the once-flourishing former kingdom, how could they possibly have no reliance?" Overfrey Duke slowly stood up, coming to the window. He pulled up the red curtains, allowing the crimson sunset from outside to shine in, filling the entire study.

"The Overfrey family also calculated the merits of the founding of Britain. For the royalty, probably no one is more familiar than me.

"As I know, 400 years ago, the first king of Britain, Egbert, once signed a contract with a superpowerful existence."

"That superpowerful existence swept everything aside, almost crushing all obstacles, helping Egbert unify the entire Great Britain..."

"What is that superpowerful existence?" Gabry asked with a trembling voice, feeling it was a very ominous thing, and cold sweat unconsciously broke out on his forehead.

"That is a lifeform with an extremely long lifespan, belonging to the magical beast category, but with high wisdom, clearly possessing divinity." Overfrey Duke paused, then continued, "It has existed since ancient times on this land, lying in wait in the oldest lakes, named the Fairy of the Lake."

"The Fairy of the Lake?" Gabry opened his eyes wide, embarrassed, saying, "A lowly creature, never heard of this monster."

"You haven't heard of it is very normal; these are the secrets of the royalty, and only a few distinguished families know." Overfrey Duke glanced at Gabry, then continued, "The Fairy of the Lake is a very powerful existence. Although it belongs to magical beasts, it has great spirituality, without any feeling of butchery and blood-drinking, it looks like a holy deity, perhaps having survived since the ancient era. Perhaps not many top magical beasts in the magical beast forest can compare to the Fairy of the Lake..."

Gabry immediately gasped for cold air, feeling it was incredible. The top magical beasts in the magical beast forest are fearsome existences at the peak.

There might be a few controllers capable of destroying a country, with extremely long lifespans, and every one pulled out might cause a world-sized crisis!

However, this group of top magical beasts—there are apparently not many that can compare to the Fairy of the Lake! ?

Gabry slightly stabilized his mind, feeling a wave of pressure in his heart, and asked in a nervous tone—

"Could it be that this terrifying existence is still within the royalty's control?"

title: Chapter 11 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 11 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 11 · Chapter 11

"Of course, the lake fairy is the guardian deity of the royal family. Back then, Egbert somehow managed to sign a contract with such a monster." Duke Ofrei nodded. If not for his fear of that powerful existence, he would have rebelled long ago.

"...The lake fairy wouldn't be in the capital, would it?" Gabriel thought of a possibility. If the House Ofrei marched on the city, what kind of powerful existence would they face?

"You guessed correctly. The empire's so-called ancient lake is actually an underground lake, and the royal palace sits directly above it." Duke Ofrei confirmed.

Gabriel fell silent at once, his expression shifting between light and shadow as he turned something over in his mind.

"Although the lake fairy's power is formidable, its usage comes with many restrictions. It requires royal blood, and after each summoning, it enters a hibernation period of two hundred years. Elizabeth will never resort to using it unless absolutely necessary." Duke Ofrei added.

Gabriel thought for a long time, then urged on, "My lord need not worry. Although the lake fairy is powerful, the Four Elemental Sword Saints may very well be able to handle it."

"Are you joking?" Duke Ofrei's eyes widened as he stared at Gabriel with alarm and disbelief.

"Rest assured, my lord. I have my ways. Don't you trust me?" Gabriel narrowed his eyes, his expression full of confidence.

Duke Ofrei pondered and found that Gabriel always proved to be far-sighted. Every plan he proposed had been entirely correct; without him, the house would never have reached its current prominence. Trusting him was only natural.

"Since you are so confident, then I will trust you."

"I will certainly not let you down, my lord. Shall we begin the journey to overthrow sovereignty tomorrow?" Gabriel suggested.

"Not yet..." Duke Ofrei's face showed traces of grief, and grinding his teeth, he said harshly, "I want to bury Luke first before I lay hands on that bitch Elizabeth!"

Late at night.

The brightly lit royal palace.

Queen Elizabeth's bedchamber.

A few of the queen's maids tidied up her bedroom, preparing it for her to rest.

The bedroom door was slowly closed, and the maids left one by one, carrying trays and brooms, still chatting as they went —

"Have you heard? Lord Mesfield seems to have been imprisoned."

"I've heard. How pitiful. Perhaps it's because that great swordsman Elgin was just too difficult to handle."

"True. After all, he's the man who defeated countless Saint-tier undead. Even Lord Mesfield would find it hard to subdue him."

"You have no need to worry about Lord Mesfield at all. He's the First Knight, and Her Majesty wouldn't hand down severe punishment lightly. Why not care more about Lord Millius? A man like him being imprisoned — he'd surely lose several pounds just from the stress. It breaks my heart."

"Oh, give it a rest, you little flirt. As if he'd ever look at you!"

The maids chattered and drifted away, quite amused, completely unaware that someone was watching them from behind.

Princess Michelle crouched in a corner, peeking out at the maids with a nervous expression.

Only when they had completely disappeared from sight did she dare lift her skirt and quickly step out from the corner.

Michelle was far too worried about Mesfield; it felt as though countless ants were gnawing at her.

So she decided to go see how Mesfield was doing in the dungeon. Otherwise, she wouldn't be able to sleep a wink that night.

Although Michelle held the title of princess, she certainly wouldn't be allowed to enter a filthy place like a dungeon. She would need Queen Elizabeth's permission.

But there was another way — if she obtained the royal household seal used within the bedchamber, she could go anywhere without obstruction.

So Michelle resolved to secretly sneak into Queen Elizabeth's room, steal the royal seal, and then visit Mesfield in the dungeon.

Michelle tiptoed to the bedroom door. The surrounding lanterns cast a dim golden glow, stretching long shadows that flickered in the night air.

She looked left and right, and only when she was sure no one was around did she dare open the door and enter the queen's bedchamber.

After stepping inside, Michelle looked around. Everything felt unfamiliar, so different from the memories she held from her childhood.

A few years ago, Elizabeth seemed to have deliberately distanced herself from her daughter Michelle, always treating her with coldness.

As a result, Michelle felt her own mother had become a stranger. She no longer dared to wander into this very bedroom and could only seek comfort from Mesfield.

Michelle didn't linger. She immediately got to work, carefully searching through drawers and corners. After checking each spot, she neatly put everything back exactly as she'd found it, wanting to leave no trace.

She searched for a long time, growing increasingly anxious. She worried Queen Elizabeth might return suddenly, leaving her with no explanation.

At last, her patience paid off. In a small cabinet within the dressing table, Michelle found a tiny golden badge.

It bore an engraving of a lion and a unicorn, with the royal crest at its center — it was indeed a royal badge, granting a series of privileges.

Overjoyed, Michelle pressed the badge into her palm and prepared to leave. But just as she was about to go, she noticed a small black box in the drawer that looked completely out of place, strange and unsettling.

What was this?

Why had her mother put it in the dressing table?

Curious, Michelle picked up the black box and slowly opened it, discovering a string of brilliant sapphire pendants within. They shimmered brilliantly, reflecting the light all around them.

She felt strangely familiar with them. If she remembered correctly, these pendants had been a gift from her grandfather to her mother. There were two in total — the other one was on Aunt Isabella's person.

But that was a long time ago. Her mother seemed to haven't worn the pendant in ages.

Michelle held the sapphire pendant in her hand and turned it over, only to discover carved characters on the back. The name leapt into view —

[Isabella]

Upon seeing that name, Michelle felt a wave of dizziness rush through her head. She sensed she had uncovered some great secret, but couldn't quite grasp its tail.

This pendant didn't belong to her mother — it belonged to her mother's elder sister, Isabella!

But at her aunt's funeral years ago, she had personally seen her aunt buried with that pendant around her neck!

Then why did another one of Aunt Isabella's pendants appear here?!

...This was far from normal. Something about this was deeply wrong...

Michelle's finely arched brows furrowed slightly. She sensed things were not as simple as they seemed.

There was no way she would believe her mother had dug up her aunt's grave and retrieved the pendant from inside.

Then the answer gradually began to come into focus. Who exactly was the one ruling the empire now?

Could it be...

Michelle suddenly raised her head, her eyes widening. A flicker of terror touched her expression as her body slowly stiffened, a bone-chilling coldness seeping into every part of her being.

A pale white face suddenly appeared behind Michelle. It wore a somewhat rigid smile, and a low voice spoke —

"Michelle, what are you doing here?"

title: Chapter 12 — Emerging
content:
Chapter 12 — Emerging

Volume 11 · Chapter 12

Queen Elizabeth had barely returned when she spotted Michelle standing there, and a flicker of irritation crossed her mind.

After all, Elizabeth had once told Michelle that she was not allowed to wander into her bedroom uninvited.

Yet here Michelle was, striding in without hesitation, having pulled out the black box that had been sitting on the dresser.

Elizabeth moved silently to Michelle's side and, seeing her playing with the pendant, spoke up at once.

The moment Michelle heard her voice, her eyes widened in shock, her whole body trembling—an exaggerated reaction born of panic.

Though Michelle sensed something was wrong, she dared not show it, quickly forcing an innocent expression instead.

"...Mother... you... you're back?"

Michelle hastily slipped the pendant back into the box and rose slowly, her expression apologetic and her heart pounding with unease.

Queen Elizabeth regarded her with a disdainful gaze, as if trying to see straight through her thoughts.

"I've only just returned. How is it that you're here?"

"I... I had something I wanted to ask you, so I could only wait here." Michelle's voice wavered, her face flushed. She had only come to steal something, not with any real request, but in this situation she could only fabricate a lie.

"You want to ask me something? What is it?" Elizabeth narrowed her eyes and inquired.

"...Michelle's expression tensed. After a moment she said, "I was hoping you wouldn't punish Miss Windsor. Please let her go."

Elizabeth's words faltered, her brows knitting slightly though she kept her tone neutral. It was obvious she found the idea of anyone pleading for the Mercer family distasteful.

Holding Mercer was nothing more than a bargaining chip; she couldn't just release her on a whim.

Besides, Michelle was still young and didn't understand such matters. Mercer was certainly not going to be freed.

Elizabeth's expression gradually grew sterner, her voice sounding gentle but carrying an undercurrent of authority.

"No. Mercer has failed her missions time and again and deserves punishment. This isn't something you can simply decide to forgive."

"Please, Mother, let Miss Windsor go. She must have had no choice but to act as she did." Michelle pressed her palms together, putting on a supplicating expression, tears glinting in her eyes. "I really don't want to trouble you, but this time, I still hope you'll... break..."

"Michelle, don't try to interfere with my decision. The choices I make are beyond your ability to change. This domain isn't somewhere you can even set foot in. Just focus on your own affairs." Queen Elizabeth replied coldly.

"M-Mother..." Michelle wanted to argue a little longer, slowly edging closer to this unfamiliar mother.

"Enough, Michelle. It's late. You should go home. I'm tired too." Queen Elizabeth dismissed her without courtesy, making herself seem unapproachable.

Michelle, like a deflated balloon, didn't dare say anything more and slowly left the bedroom.

"Good night, Mother."

"Good night, Michelle. Sweet dreams."

The bedroom door closed softly behind her. Michelle slowly opened her palm, revealing the royal crest badge lying quietly in her hand.

Inside the bedroom, Elizabeth opened the black box and took out her own sapphire pendant.

She stared at the name "Isabella J" and fell into deep thought.

Imperial Prison.

This prison was ancient, located far from the palace.

It often held political prisoners, though it wasn't the most secure prison in the empire.

The empire's most secure prison lay beyond the capital, named Azkaban Prison, where the empire's most vicious criminals were kept.

The former prince Copernicus had been imprisoned in Azkaban, under strict surveillance.

It was deep night, with wisps of dark clouds swirling across the sky, obscuring the cool moonlight.

At this hour, the ordinary imperial prison received a very special visitor—Princess Michelle came to visit Mercer late at night.

Because Michelle carried the royal administrative badge, she faced almost no resistance and was led by the guards into the imperial prison.

The prison was divided by gender, but since Mercer was a member of the Thorn Knights, the warden didn't make things difficult for her and assigned her a comfortable single cell.

[SE novel]

Mercer had already taken off her heavy, ornate armor and changed into casual clothes, instantly transforming into a girl with a slender figure.

Her light purple hair fluttered gently in the evening breeze, her face showing no trace of its former masculinity, appearing cold and distant.

Mercer sat on the cold floor, her mind in turmoil. Ever since entering this cell, she couldn't stop thinking.

Why had Queen Elizabeth changed like this?

To achieve her own goals, she resorted to all manner of underhanded tactics.

She even discarded the dignity befitting royalty, resorting to such despicable tricks as impersonation?

Was it really because of that Elkin, the great swordsman who had barely done anything truly wicked, that the emperor felt so uneasy?

And she had the audacity to imprison several Thorn Knights—how was that different from cutting off her own arm?

If the Ovre family's rebellion were to begin, who would deal with it?

Mercer felt a wave of worry, but just then Michelle's voice rang out, breaking the silence of the prison.

"Miss Windsor!"

Michelle wore a white long robe, lifting her hood as she hurried to the cell door.

"Michelle... Mercer's eyes widened as she stood up and walked toward the princess. "What brings you here?"

"Of course I'm worried about you. I wouldn't be able to sleep if I didn't come see you." Michelle's eyes flashed with genuine concern.

"...Mercer was at a loss for words, her heart warming as she smiled. "What could I possibly have? I'm fine."

"I just tried to plead with Mother on your behalf, but it didn't work. Miss Windsor, am I really useless?" Michelle's expression grew gloomy, feeling helpless about everything.

Mercer was surprised inside, not expecting Michelle to have pleaded for her. "Michelle, you don't need to do this. Don't bother with unnecessary matters. The emperor entrusted me with a task that I failed repeatedly, and being punished is not something to be pitied. You don't need to do so much for me."

"But those things aren't your fault... Michelle's voice carried a hint of indignation.

"It's fine. I swear to be loyal to the emperor, and no matter what decision he makes, I will choose to respect it." Mercer said seriously, though she was displeased with the queen internally, she didn't want Michelle to get caught up in the chaos.

"..."

Michelle lowered her head, remembering that blue pendant from earlier, and a flood of questions rose in her heart.

She felt this matter shouldn't be shared with others, but keeping it inside made her very uncomfortable.

She began to doubt—was the Elizabeth before her really her true mother?

Mercer was someone Michelle trusted, so she couldn't help but ask in a low voice.

"Miss Windsor, have you ever thought about... my mother?"

"Isn't she really just my deceased aunt?"

title: Chapter 13 — Chapter Title: Moonlight Chapter Update
content:
Chapter 13 — Chapter Title: Moonlight Chapter Update

Volume 11 · Chapter 13

Maysfield's heart trembled uncontrollably, unable to imagine what shocking words had escaped Michelle's lips.

Michelle was Elizabeth's own daughter, and yet she was now questioning her mother's very identity!?

Maysfield calmed herself slightly and tried to compose a serious expression.

"Princess Michelle, do not speak foolishly. If anyone else were to hear these words, it would not be a small matter."

"I know it's not a small matter, but I truly feel this way...." Michelle lifted her head and asked earnestly, "Don't you feel the same, Sister Windsor? Mother sometimes looks far too much like my aunt...."

Maysfield did not speak but chose silence, for as Michelle had said, this illusion had surfaced more than once or twice. Yet Elizabeth's older sister had long since passed away, and Maysfield herself had been present at the burial.

"I feel like our current Mother is my aunt, not my real mother...." Michelle only dared to speak such truths in front of Maysfield.

"Princess Michelle, do not speak so recklessly, or you will bring trouble upon yourself!" Maysfield said in a very stern tone, fearing the young princess might lose herself to wild speculation.

"Sister Windsor, I am not speaking carelessly. I just saw the pendant grandfather gave Mother, and it bears the name Isabella. But Aunt had long since been buried with that very pendant. There is no way Mother could have retrieved it. If you think about it carefully, there can only be one explanation...." Michelle's expression held no trace of joking whatsoever, hoping to gain Maysfield's agreement.

Maysfield's face went numb. Hearing Michelle's words, her previously calm heart was instantly tossed into a raging storm.

She also had some impression of that sapphire pendant. Back when she had first become a knight, Elizabeth had said she would give it to her.

However, Maysfield had felt it was inappropriate and had declined. But what in the world was she supposed to make of Isabella's name written on the back of Elizabeth's pendant? This was far too abnormal.

"Perhaps.... perhaps it is just a coincidence.."

Maysfield replied with cold sweat trickling down her face, still unwilling to believe such a terrifying possibility. What if the one ruling them was not Elizabeth at all, but Isabella—having posed as the queen for so long without anyone knowing? This was the kind of situation that could bring about the fall of their nation in the blink of an eye.

"It cannot be a coincidence. Ever since Aunt passed away, I have felt that Mother became a completely different person. No one knows my true mother better than I do." Michelle's eyes were serious, hoping Maysfield would believe her.

Maysfield's expression flickered with a hint of surprise. After thinking briefly in her mind and combining the queen's recent behavior with the sapphire pendant incident, it did seem highly suspicious—far too much like Isabella.

Elizabeth and Isabella were twin sisters. If one wished to impersonate the queen, there would be virtually no difficulty at all.

If everything Michelle said was true, and the current Elizabeth was in fact Isabella in disguise, this matter would become extremely complicated.

"Princess Michelle, are you being serious? You are not lying, are you?"

"Sister Windsor, why would I lie at a time like this?" Michelle countered, her furrowed brows making her appear exceedingly serious.

Maysfield calmed herself slightly and asked quietly, "Your Highness, what do you intend to do?"

"I currently have no factional support behind me, so it will be difficult to investigate this on my own. I plan to seek outside assistance." Michelle's thinking was still clear; rather than confronting her mother immediately, she had chosen to pull in reinforcements.

Maysfield fell silent, feeling that Michelle was still being rational. This investigation could be tied to the very fate of the entire empire.

If she could, Maysfield would gladly lend Michelle covert aid, but with her own status of imprisonment, she feared it would be nearly impossible to act.

"Your Highness, whom do you plan to ask for support?"

"The Duke of Roses in Wales. Currently, most of the kingdom's forces have been sent to the northern front of England to repel the AUFREI family. His strength is enough to shake the current Royal Guard of the capital." Michelle's thinking was remarkably clear, and she had already determined who to approach for outside aid.

"Would the Duke of Roses be willing to assist you?" Maysfield's expression grew puzzled. She had heard of this extraordinarily低调 duke, along with many rumors portraying him as a cold and aloof man.

"He will." Michelle nodded firmly, speaking with absolute certainty.

The disturbances were beginning to surface, becoming common knowledge among the people.

Though the official channels regarding the tears of the empire had not released any news, everyone knew it in their hearts.

Although the rebellion by the imperial princess was about to break out, the news of an impending civil war within the empire was spreading through the streets. Elizabeth's move to gather military forces from across the land toward northern England was far too obvious—clearly forming a pincer movement aimed at the AUFREI family's territory.

This military mobilization had a significant impact, instantly overshadowing the matter of Queen Elizabeth deceiving her people. Most people were preoccupied with concerns about the empire's internal strife rather than the queen's deception.

Everyone worried the empire would plunge into an era of chaos and warfare. Witnessing such extraordinary movements by the royal family, the common folk were thrown into waves of panic.

Count Austin, lord of Thorne, also responded to Queen Elizabeth's call, dispatching his family's private army to join this turmoil.

At this moment, maintaining the peace of Leks was no longer possible.

Arnold, the leader of the Stone family, was the one who answered the call. As the townsfolk came out to see him off, scattering flowers into the sky—

"I shall ride forth with the AUFREI duke's heavy cavalry. When my blood stains the battlefield and I become a martyr of Lecks, do not forget to offer flowers in my memory. And do not forget to present a bouquet on my behalf to Miss Alice. Lastly, bid farewell to Miss Alice for me."

Arnold spoke with great fervor, moving and inspiring—like a soldier on the brink of death on the battlefield, filled with a sorrowful grandeur.

"Stop acting so ridiculous~" Hobbs could not hold back his吐槽, "With your cowardly nature, the moment the charge horn sounds, you will be the very first deserter on the field."

"Do not tease about these things in front of Merlin. It is highly impolite to provoke someone's wife right before their eyes...."

Merlin chuckled awkwardly nearby, not particularly minding. Alice was hardly his true wife anyway, and after the debts were settled, they would each go their separate ways.

Arnold was about to depart from Lecksim shortly, but upon seeing Merlin and Hobbs, he could not resist dismounting to chat for a few words.

Now, not having been able to see Alice before leaving Lecksim weighed on Arnold's heart.

Actually, today he had dressed in splendid armor, with the Austin family crest proudly displayed on his back. He did not want to appear sloppy or inferior before Alice.

"Ahem! Ahem!" He lightly cleared his throat twice, looking serious as he waved the rose in his hand.

"I hereby declare before everyone—Miss Alice is the goddess I dream of night and day. To not clearly express my feelings would be a regret I carry for the rest of my life."

Hobbs watched Arnold enter his sparkling poet mode and shivered all over, his flesh crawling—

This guy, heading to the battlefield like this—

Really going to fight on the front lines?

title: Chapter 14 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 14 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 11 · Chapter 14

"Arnold, please act normal. Do you know what Alice hates about you the most?" Merlin couldn't help but ask.

"...what?" Arnold's expression grew awkward.

"It's that you always blurt out cheesy, romantic lines at the drop of a hat. It's so impractical!" Merlin said exasperated, wanting to perform a craniotomy on Arnold to see how his brain circuits were wired.

"Hmph, these moving verses were all taught to me by my sister. There's absolutely nothing wrong with them." Arnold said confidently, convinced his sister Jenna had reached a near-obsessive level. "Actually, don't you not letting me speak those cheesy lines mean you're trying to sabotage me?"

"Huh?!" Merlin suddenly froze, thinking: Has Arnold's head been kicked by a donkey? Would I sabotage him?!

"If I don't keep saying romantic verses, I'm afraid I'll have absolutely no chance of winning Alice-sama's heart, and....." Arnold pointed at Merlin and said earnestly, "The despicable, shameless, ill-intentioned man Merlin! Will forever possess Alice-sama's love~"

Merlin rolled his eyes, wanting to leap onto Arnold and pound the idiot with his fists!

Then Hobbs patted Merlin on the shoulder and whispered softly.

"Alright, don't bother keeping score with Arnold. Some people privately say that Count Austin married his own sister before giving birth to Arnold and Jenna. Think about it—what kind of freak would come out of an inbred marriage? It's only natural if his brain is missing a few strings."

"???" Merlin's expression turned strange, looking somewhat unable to accept it. He thought: No way? Inbreeding? What kind of nonsense is this?! Is it real?

"By the way, where is Alice-sama? Why haven't I seen her yet?" Arnold looked around anxiously. He thought the main force was already departing, and he probably couldn't stay in Ralexham for much longer either.

"Don't wait. She won't be coming out today." Merlin said wearily.

"Why...?" Arnold was puzzled, feeling Alice wasn't the type to sit quietly at home.

"Because Alice is busy with something else." Merlin recalled how Alice had been sitting in her room this morning, deep in thought about her next money-making plan, and couldn't help feeling a bit embarrassed.

The reason was simple. Since Merlin had dumped Alice's secret stash into horse racing, their lives had instantly become tight.

If they didn't go find work soon, the two of them could only maintain their living for about half a month—it was already in precarious condition.

Alice wasn't the type to passively wait for death; she was busy planning her next commission to earn enough living expenses.

"That's such a shame~"

Arnold showed a melancholic expression. He was looking so handsome today, and the fact that he hadn't seen Alice was quite disappointing.

But this emotion only flashed by for an instant. Arnold seemed to have remembered something else.

"Ah right, Merlin. My sister has been murmuring about you a lot lately, right? Saying you're so Man, so masculine..."

"Puh!"

Merlin spewed a mouthful of blood. Hearing about Jenna made his whole body feel terrible.

Thinking about it, this masochistic girl had been using all sorts of methods to secretly spy on and tail him lately. She was practically a professional paparazzo.

And she was impossible to scold or hit—the more you hit and scold her, the more enjoyable it seemed for her, and she'd only become even more annoying than before. The only solution was still to ignore her.

Merlin shifted his gaze away, seemingly not wanting to discuss Jenna with Arnold. Then he said,

"Merlin, seriously, I have a very good proposal. Want to hear it?" Arnold revealed a surprisingly serious expression for once.

"What is it?" Merlin raised his eyelids, feeling that nothing good would come from Arnold's mouth.

"How about I marry my sister to you, and you let Alice-sama over to me?" Arnold said with a straight face, delivering a line that could make someone vomit three liters of blood.

Merlin's expression remained flat, but his face quickly darkened. What was this nonsense?! Jenna's disposition like that—was she really worthy of being used as an exchange? No one would want her even if paid! And treating Alice as an object—was that really okay? No wonder Arnold couldn't win Alice over. Judging by this situation, maybe in his next life he'd stand a chance.

Even Hobbs beside him was somewhat unable to watch anymore, thinking: How could that mentally deficient kid compare to Alice? But if she were to marry Merlin, that would be more than sufficient. The Austin family's wealth would turn Merlin into a rich man in minutes. Since it was a losing situation either way, better to bow beneath Jenna's pomegranate skirt.

"Hey hey hey, consider it, Merlin."

"Get lost." Merlin pushed aside old Hobbs the indecent one.

"Merlin, how about it? I'm being serious. And don't worry—Jenna absolutely won't refuse. Even if she resists, it won't matter. As her older brother, I can absolutely make this decision." Arnold thought this idea was brilliant. Exchanging his sister for Alice-sama—very profitable!

Merlin felt both speechless and at a loss, thinking: Could that masochistic Jenna ever resist? She'd practically beg to throw herself at you. And would she even need Arnold's approval? It felt like these two siblings were truly...

"Stop. I wish you a one-way trip to northern England."

"..." Arnold felt the curse dripping with malice, but he didn't care. "Hmph, I will definitely return as a hero and come back in triumph. At that point, Alice-sama will definitely see me in a new light."

Almost as soon as he finished speaking, Arnold mounted his warhorse and slowly rode away in the direction the column was exiting the city, enjoying flowers and applause all along the way.

Merlin looked at the long cavalry procession and couldn't help but sigh, "It feels like the Empire is getting more chaotic by the day."

"Isn't that right? That fake, Luke, who impersonated the great swordsman Elgin, is dead. A great war is now unavoidable." Hobbs commented.

"Is it related to Luke's death?" Merlin's heart stirred.

"I heard the Ofrey family has never been peaceful. Having Luke impersonate the great swordsman Elgin was the queen showing goodwill toward the Ofrey family. But since Luke died, things have gotten complicated. He was the only son of the Ofrey family. This is a hatred that cuts off the family line—they certainly won't resolve this peacefully." Hobbs said seriously.

Merlin fell silent, a trace of astonishment on his face. He thought: Damn it! Are all these things I caused? An inexplicable butterfly effect that triggered a civil war in the Empire!

Meanwhile, Arnold was leaving Ralexham when he saw Alice walking toward him in a hurry. His heart surged with joy.

So Arnold wanted to show off. He reined in his warhorse, puffed out his chest, and spoke in a magnetic voice.

"Alice-sama, today I will..."

"Oh, good luck, goodbye~"

Alice seemed to be in a hurry, throwing out a perfunctory remark before leaving without even glancing at Arnold.

"Eh!?"

Arnold's face went completely blank. He had been preparing for several days, yet he hadn't aroused the slightest interest from Alice.

Arnold immediately pounded his chest in frustration, unable to understand why he couldn't measure up to Merlin! ?

Alice went straight to Merlin and, without preamble, said, "Come on, let's go home."

Hobbs beside him immediately understood, repeatedly winking and raising his eyebrows at Merlin, hinting that he was henpecked.

Merlin felt embarrassed and proudly said, "I can't just go home whenever you tell me to. Where's my dignity?"

Alice glanced at Hobbs beside her, then leaned close to Merlin's ear and whispered, "We have a guest at home."

"Who?" Merlin frowned.

"Cecilia and Kyle, and also....." Alice paused and continued, "Her Imperial Highness, Princess Michelle of the Empire."

"Huh!?" Merlin's eyeballs nearly popped out. His mouth twitched twice, and he was astonished in his heart:

An empire princess?!

Coming to find him for what?

It must be that fangirl Cecilia who brought her over...

title: Chapter 15 — Transformation
content:
Chapter 15 — Transformation

Volume 11 · Chapter 15

At Merlin and Alice's home.
Michelle, Cecilia, and Kyle had only just arrived here not long ago.
Over the past half month, with Cecilia's help, Michelle had already met the Rose Duke.
Although Michelle is a princess, facing the Rose Duke, a regional governor, alone still brings deep pressure.
After all, Michelle is still too young in grade; wanting to speak face-to-face with someone like the Rose Duke, she is clearly not yet qualified.
Fortunately, Michelle is Cecilia's classmate, and with Cecilia acting as a buffer, she can barely communicate with the Rose Duke.
Michelle frankly told the Rose Duke her suspicions about Queen Elizabeth, pleading for him to stand by her side and help investigate whether Elizabeth truly is her mother.
Hearing Michelle's words, the Rose Duke was greatly surprised, never expecting Princess Michelle to doubt the queen's true identity! ?
If what Michelle says is true, then the empire has been directly controlled by an illegitimate queen, which indeed sounds terrifying.
The Rose Duke had never imagined such a terrifying thing; for a moment he found it hard to believe Michelle's words and difficult to give a clear answer.
Just because of a sapphire pendant plus Michelle's intuition, outright denying the queen seems overly childish.
Yet with Michelle's continual persuasion and many doubts, the Rose Duke couldn't help but waver and also began to suspect Queen Elizabeth's identity.
If Elizabeth truly is her sister Isabella in disguise, to maintain legitimacy they would surely need to topple the false ruler and support Michelle as the new King of Britain.
心)I广牡」\说
However, the Rose Duke temporarily could not fully believe Michelle's words, gave her no clear answer, and instead chose to go to the capital to personally verify it.
Michelle, failing to fully convince the Rose Duke, felt deeply disappointed, sensing that the Rose Duke refused to believe her, feeling her trip was in vain.
However, just when Michelle felt powerless, Cecilia suddenly said someone could help her, and that person's strength was not inferior to any Thorn Knight! Absolutely able to help Michelle, at least guaranteeing her safety.
Upon hearing that the person's strength was not inferior to a Thorn Knight, Michelle knew it would be a great help, so without hesitation she hoped to meet this person.
Cecilia naturally wouldn't refuse, taking Michelle by carriage through the night straight to Merlin and Alice's home.
When seeing Alice, especially the mithril adventurer's proof on her neck, Michelle's eyes lit up, thinking that the existence Cecilia said could match a Thorn Knight was this person!
If this female Saint-tier adventurer were willing to help her, that would certainly be a good thing.
Michelle felt she had met a benefactor, but then Cecilia and this female adventurer were talking about a certain 'Merlin', and then the adventurer left midway, leaving Michelle's group at home.字
Michelle was very puzzled, unable to figure out what was happening, wondering if she had been rude and thus disliked by this female adventurer.
At that moment, the three were seated at the table, and Alice had already served them three cups of coffee-
Michelle sat down, feeling uneasy, very eager for support; Alice, being a Saint-tier powerhouse, naturally fell within the scope of what they were seeking.
However, the sudden departure left Michelle feeling somewhat frustrated; after all, she too knows etiquette, so why did it feel like she was being excluded?
“Cecilia, that Alice... ah no, is Lady Alice.
“Don't worry about the title; Miss Alice is very open-minded, won't fuss over etiquette, just call her Miss Alice, which also feels friendly.” Cecilia said, lifting her hot coffee.
“Eh! ? You all address her like that?” Michelle widened her eyes, thinking Cecilia was being terribly impolite.
“Yeah, I and Kyle both call her that.” Cecilia said without hiding it.
Beside them, Kyle didn't speak, just gave a muffled nod.
“Isn't this rather rude? It shows we don't respect people.” Michelle said embarrassedly.
“When we first met Alice, she was still a high-tier gold adventurer, so we were already used to her; I never expected..... Cecilia paused, somewhat deflated, saying, “I never thought that in such a short time she would already become a Saint-tier powerhouse, how fast.”
“.....Yeah, Miss Alice is already a Saint-tier powerhouse; I faintly feel I'm useless, indeed talented people are just different.”
Kyle felt like bursting into tears, his heart somewhat unbalanced; he had worked so hard, now he too is high-tier, but not long ago Alice was still high-tier, and in just a few months she transformed into a Saint-tier powerhouse, dealing a heavy blow to his confidence.
Cecilia's expression also grew somewhat gloomy; clearly she and Alice are about the same age, yet she remains a mid-tier priest while they are Saint-tier powerhouses, truly infuriating.
However, Cecilia recalling Alice's body covered in dragon scales couldn't help but now feel a creeping dread; perhaps back then there were already signs of breaking through Saint-tier.
The master and servant duo instantly sank into dejection, struck down by Alice's rapid achievements.
Although Cecilia feels she should address Alice as 'Lady', recalling their past arguments, she just couldn't bring herself to speak.
Michelle sensed the atmosphere was heavy, so she quickly changed the subject: “Then..... why did Lady Alice suddenly leave? Was I being overly rude somewhere?”
“No, Miss Alice just went to find her husband, Lord Merlin.” Cecilia waved her hand.
“Huh? !” Michelle's expression turned odd as she asked in surprise, “Isn't the person we're looking for Lady Alice?”
“No no no, although Miss Alice is strong now, we're looking for someone stronger—namely, her husband, Lord Merlin.”
“Real or fake?” Michelle's mouth formed an O, she was astonished, not expecting there to be an even stronger powerhouse.
“Of course it's true; Lord Merlin is not only powerful in strength but also a sage, young yet having already seen through life, countless times pulling me out of confusion, truly a mentor in the eyes of many.” Kyle couldn't help but add a line beside them.
Instantly, Michelle's eyes filled with little stars, full of anticipation for Lord Merlin; surely he must be a remarkably outstanding person.
At that moment, Merlin and Alice returned, entering one after the other.
Seeing Merlin, Cecilia rushed over excitedly to his side and introduced, “Michelle, this is the Merlin I just told you about.”
“Really? This is Mei... Michelle sprang up excitedly, but upon seeing Merlin's adventurer's proof, her expression instantly froze on her face, the little stars in her eyes vanishing, replaced by emptiness and indifference—”
What the heck?
This isn't the lowest-rank iron adventurer, is it?
He basically has no ability, just a lowlife scraping by at the very bottom of the adventurer's world, eating and drinking for free....
