title: Chapter 16 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 16 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets

Volume 11 · Chapter 16

Michel's face was completely expressionless, feeling that his expectations had been in vain. He was even starting to suspect whether Cecilia was deliberately mocking him.

He had just been praising Lord Merlin to the skies, only to find out he was just an Iron-tier adventurer?!

It felt like he was being treated like a child, like he was an idiot without any ability to discern!

Clearly, this Lord Merlin seemed weaker than Miss Alice, yet he talked such big talk. Didn't he worry about twisting his tongue?

And any fool could see it — this man was clearly a gold-digger, living off women!

Michel felt deeply frustrated, thinking that asking Merlin for help was nowhere as good as begging Alice to assist him. This Lord Merlin seemed completely superfluous.

Seeing Michel's lack of reaction, Cecilia urged, "Michel, say hello quickly. This is Lord Merlin, incredibly powerful. By my conservative estimate, he's on par with the First Knight."

Merlin frowned slightly, thinking: First Knight? Must be Messfield, right? On par with me? Pfft! Don't blacken my reputation, okay? That woman was defeated by a single spit from me. Why does it feel like everyone in the world keeps underestimating me? Is it just because I'm a shut-in who's never left home?!

"???." Michel was full of question marks, feeling his IQ dropping by the line. He thought: I might believe that Miss Alice here can hold her own against Sister Windsor, but saying some ordinary Iron-tier adventurer is on par with Sister Windsor... come on, don't treat me like a retard just because I'm young.

Cecilia saw Michel acting as if he'd lost his soul and couldn't be moved, and frowned, asking, "Michel, what's wrong with you?"

Michel hesitated, thinking that Cecilia had come to help him, so at least he owed her basic courtesy.

So Michel nodded toward Merlin, showing no contempt, and spoke in a gentle tone.

"Hello."

Merlin nodded to acknowledge, saying nothing, putting on a rather aloof demeanor from the start. An imperial princess? She looked so young, even younger than Cecilia. I wonder what kind of trouble has come knocking again.

"Lord Merlin, Lord Merlin, do you miss me?" Cecilia's eyes were full of stars.

"Why would I miss you?" A waterfall of dark veins appeared on Merlin's forehead.

"Someone as cute and charming as me would surely make you unable to tear yourself away, right?" Cecilia stepped closer to Merlin, somewhat confident in her charm.

Alice couldn't bear to watch anymore. She was still alive, and this person was flirtin g with Merlin right in front of her. The sheer nerve.

So Alice unceremoniously stepped in front of Merlin, striking a wife-protecting stance, and said coldly, "Miss Cecilia, please behave yourself. I'm still right here, so please respect my position."

"Hmph." Cecilia pouted and muttered, "Old nag."

"....What did you say?!" Alice's expression immediately darkened, and she said angrily, "You flirt with Merlin right in front of me and have the gall to act justified?"

Merlin glanced at Alice, thinking they were a fake couple anyway, what was she getting serious for? How strange....

Kyle stepped forward, bowed slightly, and said with great respect, "Lord Merlin, long time no see. I apologize for troubling you again."

Michel's expression shifted continuously on the sidelines, wondering why everyone in this group was so respectful toward this Iron-tier adventurer? It felt like they were all orbiting around him. Hey! He's just an Iron-tier adventurer. Why are they all so obsequious? It was as if they'd suffered an IQ-depressing blow.

Actually, what confused Michel the most was Alice. Clearly a Saint-tier powerhouse, yet she seemed to hold Merlin in such high regard.

Merlin looked at Kyle, feeling he was the only relatively normal person here, and impatiently asked, "Why are you here again? What do you want?"

"We have something we need your help with." Kyle said earnestly.

"Pfft." Merlin clicked his tongue dissatisfiedly and said coldly, "If it's troublesome business, scram early. I don't welcome trouble...."

"...." Kyle was embarrassed, thinking Merlin would treat them as friends, never expecting to be seen as a bother. That was really hurtful.

Cecilia quickly came to Michel's side and said earnestly, "Lord Merlin, this is Her Imperial Highness, the Princess. She has something she'd like to ask for your help. Please, I beg you."

"Can't help it, scram." Merlin said with distaste. With the empire in such chaos now, he didn't want anything to do with the royal family.

Michel's brow knitted in turmoil, a trace of irritation rising inside him. Why was this Iron-tier adventurer so arrogant? He had come to request Miss Alice's help, not this guy's. Wasn't he taking himself too seriously?

"....Lord Merlin, don't be so heartless." Cecilia said awkwardly.

"It must be a super troublesome matter, right? I'm particularly afraid of trouble, so you'd better not make a fool of yourselves." Merlin waved his hand, clearly intending to show them the door.

Kyle pondered for a moment and tentatively asked, "I wonder how much compensation Lord Merlin requires this time?"

"Compensation?"

Merlin's heart stirred instantly. Not that he was vulgar, but he genuinely needed it.

But the empire was in chaos now. Getting involved with a princess might seem like courting big trouble.

If they couldn't resolve it quickly, they might need to invest a lot of energy, which was not worth it!

To Merlin, time was life, and it was extremely valuable.

title: Chapter 17 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 17 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 11 · Chapter 17

Merlin looked at Alice, thought for three seconds, nodded, and said, “Unfeeling? Back then I treated you as a strong laborer, and I still can—what’s there to be unwilling about?” Alice’s cheeks puffed up instantly, she glared at Merlin angrily, her face slowly turning red, “You’re ruthless!” “I really am that ruthless.” Merlin nodded solemnly. Alice was furious, dissatisfied, saying, “Pay me back, return the money you squandered from my little treasury! If you hadn’t blown my savings on horse‑race bets, we wouldn’t be this poor now.” “Um…” Merlin broke out in a cold sweat on his forehead, awkwardly averting his gaze. “Anyway we need this reward, don’t go around singing the opposite tune, or we’ll really be eating dirt…” Alice said with a serious expression. “Tch, what a hassle…” Merlin rolled his eyes. Alice ignored Merlin and turned to Cecilia and the others, saying one by one, “In short, everyone sit down and let’s talk first.” After quieting down, Michelle recounted her own affairs and voiced her suspicion of Queen Elizabeth. Although Merlin had no interest in Michelle’s ordeal, he still felt secretly shocked. The ruler of the entire empire was actually not legitimate? Someone was impersonating?g5h Merlin thought this was extremely serious, threatening the very foundation of the empire. U Actually, after Mother was defeated by the Gun‑wielding Hero, there had also been a great demon trying to seize the Demon Lord’s throne, but Merlin personally slew it. Thinking of how urgently Michelle wants help, it’s not hard to understand. After all, at the negotiating table, it’s never about words but about harder fists. Alice, hearing Michelle’s words, stared wide‑eyed in shock, finding it unbelievable. “Queen Elizabeth isn’t real? She’s actually your aunt Isabella?!” Michelle nodded, answering seriously, “Although I still can’t be certain now, I feel Mother is abnormal.” Beside them, Cecilia and Kyle said nothing, apparently they had heard this before, so they weren’t that shocked. “…Isn’t that impossible? Queen Elizabeth being fake…such things…” Alice found it hard to believe, thinking the matter too bizarre and tied to the fate of the whole empire; relying solely on Michelle’s word made it hard to convince. “Lady Alice, I know my words lack proof, but I still ask you to believe me—no one knows my mother better than I do. If I weren’t sure there was a problem, I would never have fled the palace to seek outside aid.” Michelle said earnestly. “……Alice hesitated, unable to agree for a time.” Seeing this, Merlin lowered his voice and told Alice, “Look, this is definitely a huge muddy mess; if mishandled it could drag us in, so I suggest we politely refuse and then think of other ways.” m Alice stayed silent, fell into thought, feeling Merlin made sense—as an adventurer, getting involved in political strife is the biggest taboo. Moreover, anyone can see the empire is in chaos, war could break out at any moment; helping Michelle in such a sensitive matter surely won’t be easy. Alice was weighing it, stole a glance at Merlin, saw his nonchalant demeanor, obviously not wanting to meddle further. “Lady Alice, if you’re willing to help me, I will give you the greatest reward within my power.” Michelle said sincerely. “Miss Alice, you just need to protect His Highness Michelle’s safety; exposing the queen’s true face will be handled by my father.” Cecilia chimed in on Michelle’s behalf. “Yes, the duke has already begun intervening; in a few days he’ll lead the Rose family’s elite troops to the capital. With the duke’s involvement, you certainly won’t be easily dragged into trouble.” Kyle said seriously. Alice’s doubts lessened, but seeing Merlin’s unmoved attitude, she seemed truly unwilling to be tangled in trouble. However, this task seemed not difficult—just need to protect Princess Michelle, plus the pressure of poverty, leaving her little choice. “What do you need us to do?” When Michelle saw Alice relent, she was overjoyed—gaining a Saint‑tier powerhouse was obviously a great help! She then steadied her spirit, feeling Alice was more reliable than the wavering Rose duchess. “You only need to guard my safety and lend a hand at critical moments; that’s all.” er “……”.. Alice felt this personal task could be accepted, she furtively nudged Merlin, “How about it? I think we can.” “Don’t let immediate profit drive you; when the time comes you’ll get burned, I won’t help you wipe your ass.” Merlin muttered, considering this a troublesome matter, unlike his enthusiasm for Cecilia’s earlier private task. “You’re treating me like a kid? Hmph~!” Alice retorted angrily. Nearby, Cecilia and Kyle couldn’t help whispering to each other, one after another: “Kyle, do you not feel…” “Alice…” “has become gentle…” “a bit…” “clingy to Merlin.” “Miss, I won’t hide it—I sensed early on that after Alice became a Saint‑tier powerhouse, she seems to care more about Merlin than before, already heading toward an old married couple direction.” Michelle felt odd, thinking Alice as a Saint‑tier powerhouse has no opinion at all? She keeps looking at the black‑iron adventurer’s face, too strange. Could Merlin not only be eating soft rice but also be the head of the household?! ! Michelle felt her eyes were about to go blind, really wanting to exclude Merlin. “Merlin, this matter is important—I hope you give it serious thought.” Alice lowered her voice, whispering, “Besides, the other side promised not to cause trouble; they just need us to serve as guards for a while.” i “Tch, I don’t want to take a task that ties me to royalty.” Merlin said stubbornly. \ say Alice’s expression froze instantly, she silently stretched out her little hand, face dark, saying, “Pay up, return the money you squandered from my little treasury right now.” Merlin’s forehead was instantly covered with countless black lines, feeling the situation embarrassing. That damned old lady, always demanding rent like a landlord, truly shameless. Merlin withdrew his gaze, looked at Michelle, and asked seriously, “Your Highness Michelle, although there’s a hint of copper smell, I still want to inquire about the reward—after all, this concerns my livelihood, so how much reward do you intend to give us?” “After the matter is settled, I’m willing to pay 700,000 remuneration, with half as an advance.” Michelle’s expression looked painful; this was already her limit. Alice kept tugging Merlin’s sleeve, constantly hinting, “700,000, 700,000, 700,000~” “……” Merlin watched Alice, seeing the love and justice in her eyes vanish, completely turning into a golden $ sign. Alice this troublesome girl… sometimes also shows superficiality. = ((异V号1I)

title: Chapter 18 — Contradiction
content:
Chapter 18 — Contradiction

Volume 11 · Chapter 18

Though their communication hit some bumps along the way, Merlin and Alice still reluctantly agreed to Michelle's request.

If it hadn't been for Alice bringing up the matter of payment and constantly pressuring Merlin on that front, Merlin certainly wouldn't have agreed to something like this. It wasn't in his nature, given his preference for avoiding trouble.

But since Michelle had made a promise to personally oversee their safety and ensure neither Merlin nor Alice would be dragged into any complications, Merlin found he could accept the situation. After all, it was just short-term guard duty, and as long as they stayed clear of the Empire's chaos, he could manage it.

On top of that, his family was in dire financial straits at the moment, and 700,000 in remuneration was a substantial sum that could solve their immediate hardships.

So Merlin had very little room to negotiate. Though he liked to joke about surviving on dirt, deep down he still preferred a comfortable life.

And Alice had already been won over by money, pulling Merlin aboard by any means necessary, leaving him somewhat unable to back down.

At that very moment, Merlin and Alice were riding toward the Rose Duke's residence alongside Cecilia.

Michelle had secured Merlin and Alice as her guards, but whether they would uncover the truth ultimately depended on the Rose Duke's cooperation.

Inside the carriage, both Cecilia and Kael were lavishing attention on Merlin, fussing over him with endless care.

"Lord Merlin, would you like some fruit?"

"Lord Merlin, you must be thirsty! Would you like some water?"

"Lord Merlin, would you like me to massage your shoulders?"

The two were swarming around Merlin like attendants. This wasn't how one treated a hired guard — he was being treated like a lord!

Kael was pounding Merlin's shoulders from behind while Cecilia sliced fruit with her own hands.

Merlin, draped lazily across the carriage sofa, was making occasional humming sounds of contentment, likely because it felt far too comfortable.

Alice, sitting nearby, glared at Merlin with a dark expression, her eyes full of disapproval at his current state.

"Kael, it's too light. Put some force into it." Merlin said indifferently, feeling that Kael's shoulder-rubbing technique was quite amateurish.

"Understood, Lord Merlin. I suppose this is also a form of personal growth, is it not? One must master the small things before achieving greatness." Kael increased the pressure, kneading Merlin's shoulders. "As expected of Lord Merlin, every action you take is filled with profound meaning."

"Umm..." Merlin kept a straight face, unwilling to ruin the lofty image he'd built in Kael's mind, and chose silence instead.

Alice rolled her eyes, utterly baffled by why Kael would think so much. Merlin was simply a petty person! He only didn't want to give up the free massage! He was absolutely not some noble soul!

Cecilia finished cutting the fruit and speared a piece, offering it to Merlin. "Lord Merlin, here, open wide~"

Merlin accepted it without hesitation, then critically remarked, "Not fresh at all."

Alice didn't want to look at Merlin's grotesque face anymore and covered her eyes, thinking, *Why is he becoming so inflated?!*

"...Not fresh?" Cecilia set down the fruit tray with an aggrieved expression. "How dare they deceive me! I specifically instructed the servants to purchase only morning-picked fruit! Such unacceptable behavior calls for immediate dismissal. How could such ingredients possibly be worthy of the noble Lord Merlin?"

"Umm..." Merlin felt uneasy speaking again. He'd eaten worse things in his life — he was only half-joking. She didn't need to take it so seriously.

Michelle's expression grew increasingly strange. She couldn't understand why her classmate Cecilia would be so obsequious toward a Black Iron-rank adventurer.

After all, Cecilia belonged to the noble class. Why behave so subserviently? It made no sense.

Watching Merlin's smug, entitled demeanor, Michelle felt a spark of irritation. *A freeloader. What right does he have to be so arrogant?*

Before Michelle could say anything, Alice lost her patience first. "Hey, you two — ease off a bit! Have some dignity. Constantly flattering this guy is only going to make him inflate until he explodes."

"It's fine. To serve Lord Merlin is my honor. Even something as simple as massaging shoulders allows me to grow in new ways." Kael said earnestly, looking completely bewitched in the eyes of any outsider.

"Precisely. That Lord Merlin would spare time to assist us is already the greatest favor. I feel guilty just for repaying him to this extent." Cecilia wore a deeply sincere expression.

"You..." Alice was speechless. She wondered if their eyesight had failed them — how could they not see that Merlin wasn't nearly as outstanding as they claimed?

"Hehe, Alice, are you terribly envious of me?" Merlin flashed a teasing grin.

"...Who's envious of you? You utter engine of negativity!" Alice huffed and shot Merlin a sideways glance.

"Hmph!" Merlin shifted his leg toward Alice. "Here, I grant you permission to massage my legs. Cherish this opportunity."

"Tch! Go to hell!" Alice ground her teeth in anger and jammed her small fist firmly against Merlin's thigh.

Merlin pulled his leg back, a slightly embarrassed look crossing his face. "So fiery. Many people would kill for the chance to cling to my leg."

"I wouldn't deign to." Alice sniffed coldly, uncomfortable at seeing Merlin surrounded by so many admirers.

Merlin narrowed his eyes. Was she truly uninterested, or merely pretending? In the end, wasn't it always her who cleaned up his messes?

Too lazy to argue further with Alice, he suddenly recalled this mission and turned to ask the silent Michelle across from him.

"Princess Michelle, if it turns out Queen Elizabeth is the real deal — if everything is merely your illusion — what then?"

"That won't happen. I trust my intuition." Michelle replied with absolute conviction. Recalling the sapphire pendant, she felt the likelihood of it being an illusion was quite low.

"I'm speaking hypothetically. If Queen Elizabeth is an imposter, you can't produce any evidence either, can you?" Merlin studied the imperial princess carefully, noting that the childish innocence on her face had not yet fully faded.

Michelle had initially wished to ignore Merlin, but seeing confusion on Alice's face as well, she felt compelled to answer. "If everything truly is my illusion, I will bear full responsibility."

"I see. Well, that's good enough. As long as we won't be implicated, that's all that matters." Merlin secretly exhaled in relief.

Michelle's expression darkened. *Does this guy really think so highly of himself?!* She had only come to request Miss Alice's assistance. There was barely any connection to Merlin. Who would consider a Black Iron-rank adventurer a significant asset? Unless their brain was broken.

In truth, Michelle also had a proud streak. Seeing Merlin so actively distance himself from the situation, she couldn't help but speak up.

"Mr. Merlin, please do not misunderstand."

"I only came to request Miss Alice's help. You have nothing to do with this."

"As a Black Iron-rank adventurer, you provide absolutely no assistance to me. You're merely padding numbers."

"And even if something goes wrong, who would bother pursuing a Black Iron adventurer?"

"You're overestimating your own importance. Please face reality. Thank you."

title: Chapter 19 — Bonus Update for Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 19 — Bonus Update for Monthly Votes

Volume 11 · Chapter 19

"In the end, I still don't know why you came along. Nobody invited you, right?"

Michelle hugged her own chest and glanced out the window, clearly harboring long-standing grievances against Merlin. She finally couldn't hold it in and launched into a sharp complaint.

She hadn't invited Merlin either, yet she had considered him an important combat asset. And yet on the journey, he acted like a pompous lord—how could anyone endure that?

Michelle figured if Merlin kept a low profile, it would be fine. But he was so high-profile it became disgusting, so being called out with harsh words was only something he brought upon himself.

"Huh?" Merlin slightly widened his eyes and asked in surprise, "Are you serious?"

"Did I say anything wrong? Since you're just here to tag along, I hope you'll keep a low profile. Just paddle along appropriately." Michelle spoke with absolutely no courtesy.

Merlin didn't respond. Instead, he smiled faintly. He wasn't really bothered by Michelle's snide remarks—he was a 200-plus-year-old elder after all. Getting angry at a young girl would lose him dignity.

"Hah..." Alice laughed out loud. Although she couldn't beat Merlin, seeing someone else look down on him made her feel inexplicably satisfied. It was a sense of triumph.

"What are you laughing at?" Merlin rolled his eyes. Was it really that funny? She thought he was a slacker, so what?

"I laugh because I want to. None of your business?" Alice retorted haughtily.

"Tch!" Merlin glanced at Michelle and said flatly, "You told me to just tag along. Don't regret it later~"

"Hah, who would regret it? From start to finish I've thought of you as a fraud. Deliberately deceiving Alice-sama's feelings. Otherwise, with your qualifications, how could you possibly be Alice-sama's husband?" Michelle paused and muttered, "If it weren't clearly written on the Adventurers card, I'd have thought you were just the handyman who takes care of chores around Alice-sama."

"Pfft!" Alice covered her mouth and laughed, her shoulders trembling. Those words really pleased her.

"Tsk!" Merlin shot Alice a glance, thinking: Do I really need to be mocked for you to be this happy? Your psychology is twisted.

Although Merlin didn't mind, Cecilia and Kyle beside him were growing restless. They couldn't help but defend Merlin.

"Michelle, although Merlin is only a Black Iron adventurer, his strength is no weaker than the First Knight," Cecilia said seriously.

"That's right, Your Highness Michelle. We shouldn't judge a book by its cover. If you had the chance to see Merlin-sama's true strength, I'm sure you'd change your opinion of him." Kyle said with deep feeling. He had also thought Merlin was a lazy slacker back then, but his swollen face hadn't even subsided since then.

"Don't joke around, Cecilia. This Mr. Merlin is not on the same level as my sister Windsor. Even if you compare them side by side, it would be an insult to my sister." Michelle's eyes were full of disdain.

"Hehe~" Merlin smiled without speaking, quietly watching this little girl.

"Michelle, we're not lying to you. Merlin-sama truly is an extremely rare powerhouse. I hope you can show him some respect. Otherwise, our introduction was for nothing." Cecilia's expression carried a hint of seriousness.

"I think your heads must be addled. In what way does this Mr. Merlin look like a powerhouse? What's so special about him that you're groveling like this? Clearly, it's Alice-sama who's the real Saint-tier powerhouse, right?" Michelle turned her head away, seemingly unwilling to communicate further with Merlin. "I don't see anything particularly special about Mr. Merlin, and I don't understand why you all worship him so much."

Merlin looked at Michelle, his expression turning peculiar. *This little girl... She's not old, but her temper is certainly not small.*

When their carriage arrived at the Rose Duke's mansion, they saw that the entire city was nearly filled with armored soldiers, each with a stern expression and high spirits.

The massive army marched in grand formation toward the city outskirts, their synchronized footsteps thunderous and intimidating—far off, it felt like an earthquake.

Countless black banners adorned with roses and thorns flew high, displaying status and honor, like a grand parade.

This was the private armed force of the Rose family—the Rose Knights at the forefront, totaling a staggering 50,000 strong!

With their strict discipline and powerful strides, they were indeed a magnificent army, proving the Duke's caliber in military governance.

In front of the ducal mansion, a middle-aged man with flowing golden hair held a map and discussed something with a knight beside him.

His attire was exceedingly refined—a tight-fitting upper garment that hugged his frame, paired with a lower skirt reaching his knees, loose and flowing.

A red cape draped over his shoulders bore a rose-patterned crest. Combined with his well-proportioned figure, he looked both noble and fashionable.

This was the lord of all of Wales—the Rose Duke, the highest-ranking official in the region.

At this moment, the Rose Duke was about to lead the troops on campaign, studying the map to choose the nearest route, occasionally asking his knights for input.

The knight beside the Rose Duke was burly, and the scars on his face alone told of a ruthless fighter who had slaughtered on battlefields.

His name was Marren, commander of the entire Rose Knight Order and the Rose family's sole Saint-tier powerhouse, serving as the Duke's personal guard.

Marren had followed the Rose Duke since early on. Through his own strength, he had become the Duke's most trusted subordinate.

With years of military experience, the Rose Duke would also set aside his status to consult Marren on various matters.

The Rose Duke folded up the map. Having selected a route, he asked, "Marren, has Cecilia returned?"

"Reporting to Your Excellency, the young lady has not yet returned. However, she should be back today."

"That child... She's been going to Rexem quite a lot lately. I wonder what she's doing there, insisting on bringing Her Highness the Princess along." The Rose Duke's expression was filled with concern.

"She might just be going to relax. After all, the young lady and the Princess are classmates." Marren said seriously, thinking that with Kyle accompanying them, nothing should go wrong.

The Rose Duke sighed. His youngest daughter was rather ordinary and had a strong playful streak. Now the main force was about to depart, yet the Princess still hadn't returned.

But as they spoke of Cao Cao, Cao Cao appeared—Cecilia and the others had already come back.

"Father, I've returned." Cecilia walked quickly up to the Rose Duke.

Marren nodded to Kyle behind Cecilia, acknowledging him. It was both a greeting and an affirmation of his work.

Kyle had been trained under Marren from the beginning. Marren was technically his superior, but one could also call him a teacher.

"Your Excellency the Duke, I apologize for causing you trouble." Michelle stepped forward and slightly lifted the hem of her skirt to express her apology.

"No need to worry, Your Highness. I understand that after such an incident, one's mood needs to settle. I'm curious—what did you do in Rexem?" The Rose Duke asked, puzzled.

"We found two strong allies to assist us, mainly responsible for guarding Your Highness's safety." Cecilia stepped aside and gestured to Merlin and Alice behind her. "Ta-da! These two are them."

"Hello." Alice nodded.

Merlin merely rested his head on his arm, showing no reaction toward the Rose Duke.

The Rose Duke narrowed his eyes and scrutinized Merlin and Alice. Seeing that Alice was a Mithril adventurer, his eyes lit up instantly.

Adventurers almost never involved themselves in political struggles—they were hard to recruit.

He never expected his least capable youngest daughter to have gone to Rexem and managed to recruit a Mithril-level adventurer!

This was a time of great crisis. Every Saint-tier powerhouse was a powerful trump card that needed careful treatment.

"Miss Alice, thank you for your support of the Empire. I will remember your kind assistance."

"You flatter me." Alice nodded, her smile somewhat stiff—she clearly wasn't accustomed to such occasions.

The Rose Duke then turned to look at the other powerhouse beside her, intending to inspect the second strong ally. But when he saw Merlin, he subconsciously dismissed him and began scanning around in confusion...

What was going on?

Didn't they say there were two powerhouse allies?

Where's the other one?!

title: Chapter 20 — Suppression
content:
Chapter 20 — Suppression

Volume 11 · Chapter 20

The Duke of Roses glanced around, sensing no other powerhouse in sight.

Wasn't there supposed to be two of them? Why did it look like there was only this one female adventurer?

He reluctantly refocused his gaze on Merlin and scrutinized him once more.

Could this Iron-rank adventurer really be the second powerhouse? Impossible. It was like a joke.

If Cecilia hadn't mentioned two strong individuals, the Duke of Roses would have assumed Merlin was merely Alice's baggage-carrying lackey.

Merlin barely noticed the Duke's piercing stare. Instead, he gazed at the adjacent mansion, marveling at its extravagance—somewhat surpassing his own Demon Lord Palace, which mainly suffered from being far too old-fashioned and dated.

"Father, with those two protecting Her Highness Michelle, you can rest assured." Cecilia said earnestly.

"Hmm, that's true." The Duke of Roses nodded. Though he said it aloud, he wasn't pleased in his heart.

Because Cecilia was essentially undermining him, subtly interfering with the Duke's plans.

The Duke had originally intended to assign guards to Michelle—guards he could fully trust. They would both protect Michelle's safety and serve as effective surveillance. A win-win situation.

Yet Michelle had recruited two adventurers as guards, which felt like it was slipping beyond his control.

The Duke didn't fully trust Michelle. After all, the suspicions about Queen Elizabeth were nothing but one-sided claims.

So the Duke planned to test her himself. He had two backup schemes prepared to ensure his own safety:

One—if Queen Elizabeth was fake, the Duke of Roses would use the banner of preserving the imperial dynasty's legitimacy to openly attack the capital, then install Michelle as the new queen, making himself the biggest beneficiary.

Two—if Queen Elizabeth was real, the Duke would personally hand Michelle over to Her Majesty, absolve himself of all responsibility, and receive rewards for returning the princess.

Both plans were profitable for the Duke of Roses, provided he could maintain tight control over Michelle.

But Merlin and Alice's arrival had disrupted his plans, irritating him somewhat.

Fortunately, Michelle had chosen two guards, and Merlin appeared pathetically weak. This gave the Duke a perfect excuse to forcefully station his own people beside Michelle for surveillance.

"Although Your Highness found two adventurers as guards, one of them appears rather lacking in ability. For Your Highness's safety, I believe a replacement would be in order," the Duke of Roses said委婉ly—not particularly harsh.

"Huh?" Merlin immediately wore an ambiguous expression. Lacking in ability? Was he talking about him?

Michelle furrowed her delicate brows, feeling uncomfortable. She disliked others interfering with her decisions. Although Merlin seemed like a mere bystander in her eyes, he was someone she had personally chosen, and replacing him on a whim felt disrespectful.

Moreover, Michelle understood the Duke's cold-blooded nature—he wouldn't do anything pointless. She had a gut feeling he was plotting something.

"Father, you've misunderstood. Lord Merlin is actually a very strong adventurer." Cecilia couldn't help but explain from the side.

"Yeah, Your Excellency, if you don't believe us, go ahead and test him," Kael also grew restless.

"Both of you shut up. My decision is final and open to no argument," the Duke's tone grew sharp—he clearly disliked being interrupted. "Do I need to test? Don't I know that adventurer ranks are based on combat strength?"

Cecilia and Kael chose silence. Faced with the Duke's pressure, they dared not push further.

"Merlin, looks like you're being looked down on again," Alice whispered quietly to him.

"Shut up. Normal procedure. I'm used to it," Merlin replied flatly.

"What does Your Highness think? For your safety, I believe you need two genuine powerhouses, rather than having an Iron-rank adventurer padding the numbers." The Duke paused, then glanced at Meron beside him. "Meron is the commander of the Rose Knight Brigade. He is strong and trustworthy. I suggest you replace that Iron-rank adventurer with him, so that Meron and this Miss Alice can jointly serve as your guards. Surely that would be far safer."

Michelle narrowed her eyes. She faintly sensed the Duke's distrust toward her. This wasn't about protecting her—it was about placing her under house arrest.

As a princess of the empire, Michelle naturally detested such behavior. Her expression darkened instantly. Though young, she still managed to convey a trace of authority.

"No need, thank you for your kindness, Excellency. I don't require your people to protect me. These two adventurers are more than enough. I hear Lord Meron is your personal guard, so it would be better if he stays by your side for your own protection."

"Your Highness, I hope you understand my sincerity. This journey will be extremely perilous, and ensuring your safety is paramount. I don't wish for you to come to any harm before the matter is thoroughly investigated. Besides, entrusting your safety to an Iron-rank adventurer seems far too childish, doesn't it?" The Duke used Merlin as a focal point to heavily pressurize Michelle, making it difficult for her to refuse.

Michelle felt a rising annoyance but found it hard to counter his words, which appeared reasonable on the surface.

The Duke shot Meron a subtle glance, signaling him to drive Merlin away and take his place.

Meron nodded and walked directly up to Merlin, saying, "You can leave. We don't need you here. Your position has been taken by me."

"Wait, I..."

Alice was somewhat dissatisfied, but before she could finish her sentence, Merlin stopped her, intending to handle it himself.

"Let me leave? Are you serious?"

"Yes. Her Highness the princess is of noble birth, and entrusting her to an Iron-rank adventurer like you is far too flippant. It's more reliable for me to protect her. Where you came from, you should obediently return to." Meron crossed his arms and blew on his mustache haughtily.

"What if I refuse to leave?" Merlin's expression turned playful, showing no respect for Meron.

Meron immediately narrowed his eyes, sensing Merlin was a ruffian. Against such a person, violence was clearly the best solution.

Meron stepped forward without hesitation and pointed a finger at Merlin, his tone stern and threatening.

"Know your own worth, you waste. I've seen plenty of trash like you. Don't think you can mooch your way around everywhere. Wanting to serve as the princess's guard? You're utterly unqualified. If you dare say no, I'll cripple you right here, right now."

Merlin's eyebrows rose high. He nodded toward Meron and, with lightning speed, seized his finger and bent it at a sharp 90-degree angle, letting the man experience what true pain felt like.

In front of the Duke's mansion, a bloodcurdling scream erupted—

"AHHHHHHH!"

title: Chapter 21 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 21 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 11 · Chapter 21

That scream was extraordinarily piercing, and the entire army's marching pace ground to a halt as soldiers stopped in their tracks to watch the situation unfold.

Even quite a few soldiers had their hands gripping their sword hilts, ready to swarm forward at the Duke of Roses' slightest command.

The atmosphere suddenly grew tense. Cecilia and Kael didn't dare say a word. Neither had expected that Malen's remarks would provoke Merlin.

The Duke of Roses' expression darkened instantly. He hadn't anticipated that this Black Iron-ranked adventurer would actually attack his own subordinates. The gap in strength between them was like a bottomless chasm. Couldn't the other party see that? The kind of person who'd do such a thing was one of only two types: either someone who didn't fear death, or a fool.

Based on the Duke's understanding of Malen, his personality was proud and he couldn't stand humiliation. This matter wouldn't end easily, it seemed.

The Duke of Roses decided not to intervene. Malen was his own Knight Commander, and being humiliated was, indirectly, a blow to his own face.

Besides, so many people were watching. Even if Malen killed Merlin, the Duke intended to suppress the matter. His dignity could not be lost.

However, the Duke of Roses harbored some apprehension toward Alice beside Merlin. It appeared they were a married couple. He wondered whether the conflict could still be resolved peacefully.

Malen clutched his painfully torn finger and kept backing away, feeling as though his joint was already beginning to swell.

He hadn't expected his threats to fail and instead receive a severe beating, losing face publicly in front of everyone.

Malen kept his mouth shut, cold sweat trickling down his forehead as he glared viciously at Merlin across from him.

"I've never liked people with foul mouths, and you even dared to threaten to cripple me? How interesting. Go ahead and try~"

Merlin rubbed his wrist and struck a pose as if accepting a trial, intending to teach this knightly uncle a lesson. Otherwise, he'd truly become a Ninja Turtle.

Michelle's shocked expression froze on her face. She found Merlin's actions unexpected. That was the Saint-tier Knight Commander, and this mere Black Iron adventurer showed absolutely no sign of fear?!

Michelle's resolve wavered slightly, and she began to wonder whether Merlin was actually a hidden powerhouse.

"Merlin, um... isn't this a bit excessive?" Alice said with some concern. She couldn't foresee how this would end, and after all, this guard position came with considerable perks, and she didn't want to give it up.

"What's this? I haven't even drawn my blade, and that's already being generous." Merlin replied indifferently.

"Uh..."

Although Alice knew Merlin well and understood he was deliberately avoiding a full-blown confrontation, that was already being quite polite.

But the others around them felt Merlin's words were incredibly arrogant, lacking even the most basic respect.

"You bastard, you actually dared to break my finger?! " Malen ground his teeth and said, his chest nearly bursting with rage. After decades in the House of Roses, everyone respected him, and today he was humiliated by a low-ranking adventurer.

"So what?" Merlin lifted his chin loftily, looking down his nose at Malen.

"I think you're looking for death!" Malen bristled, golden aura flickering faintly around him as combat intent stirred within.

Kael sensed things were going badly and couldn't help but ask in a low voice, "My Lord Duke, what should we do now?"

"Whatever." The Duke of Roses replied with just two words, clearly unwilling to intervene. Besides, his own Knight Commander had been humiliated, and he also hoped Merlin would be beaten to the ground.

Kael had no choice but to walk up to Malen and urgently say, "Teacher, please calm down. Lord Merlin is not a bad person."

"Kael, get lost!" Malen cursed angrily. "When did you start giving me orders?!"

"..." Kael was left speechless and could only retreat grudgingly.

Malen stared at Merlin and said seriously, "You seem very confident in yourself. In all my years, I've never seen a Black Iron adventurer so arrogant!"

"That's just because you haven't seen enough~" Merlin smirked.

"Do you really think a Black Iron adventurer like yourself has the ability to serve as Her Excellency's guard?" Malen probed.

"You mean this?" Merlin lifted the Black Iron adventurer token around his neck and casually tossed it aside. "It's just an ornament. It has no practical use whatsoever."

"Excellent~" Malen narrowed his eyes, his facial muscles twitching repeatedly. "I'll see exactly what you're capable of!"

Malen directly raised both fists, appearing ready to educate this reckless adventurer through hand-to-hand combat.

Malen, a swordsman by trade, choosing to fight Merlin with his fists clearly showed he held the other in contempt, thinking fists would be more than enough.

Golden aura erupted around Malen, surging across his body like flames. An ordinary person would be killed with a single punch!

However, his goal was to cripple Merlin. Otherwise, he couldn't establish authority within the Knight Order.

Whoosh--

Wind sounded, and Malen launched his attack without hesitation!

One punch, incredibly fast, surged toward Merlin as though an entire mountain range was crushing down.

But with Merlin's monstrous speed, how could Malen possibly land a hit?

Merlin made no extra movements at all. He retreated to advance, closing the distance in an instant.

He extended his right hand, pressing his middle finger and thumb together, and in one seamless motion placed it against Malen's forehead.

"Huh?! " Malen suddenly froze, unable to comprehend what had happened. The other party was already in front of him!

Merlin raised an eyebrow and grinned wickedly. "Boom!"

Then Merlin's finger flick shot forward, his middle finger striking Malen hard on the forehead.

A sharp crack echoed, and a violent gust of wind erupted from Merlin's position, scattering the surrounding dust!

Malen let out a pained scream as his body seemed to defy gravity, flying backward through the air.

The force of Merlin's finger flick was enormous, far beyond what a mere minion could withstand.

Malen crashed through the Duke Manor's gate, shattering it, and lay motionless on the ground, seeing stars before his eyes, the entire world spinning around him.

The outcome of this conflict was already obvious. The Rose Knights' Commander, Malen, had been rendered completely defenseless by a single finger flick from Merlin! It was hard to believe!

Kael and Cecilia had both covered their eyes, seemingly sympathetic toward Teacher Malen. They had warned him not to provoke Lord Merlin lightly, but he refused to listen. And now? Knocks him out with one finger flick. Even more humiliating!

Alice watched the disheveled Malen on the ground with an expressionless face, thinking: This was the Duke's strongest knight?! Not that impressive, was he? Barely seemed better than herself, let alone matching Merlin.

The Duke of Roses' composed, steady expression instantly turned pale gray. His eyes widened in terror, his heart unable to calm down.

My Knight Commander...

Was actually severely injured by a finger flick from a Black Iron adventurer?!

title: Chapter 22 — Mist
content:
Chapter 22 — Mist

Volume 11 · Chapter 22

Duke of Roses' eyes nearly popped out of his head as he stared at Maeron lying on the ground, unable to find his voice.

His mind felt completely stuck, struggling to process what he was witnessing. His strongest guard had been defeated by—someone of the lowest-ranking adventurer?

Duke of Roses twisted his stiff neck and focused his gaze on Merlin, carefully taking him in again.

Who exactly was this Black Iron-ranked adventurer?

Why would someone of Black Iron rank possess such power?!

It was too unbelievable. Were the adventurers of Lexington already terrifying enough to reach such a level?

Innermost shock surging within him, the Duke of Roses no longer dared to underestimate Merlin so easily.

If a single Black Iron adventurer already had this level of strength, then wasn't the female adventurer Alice beside him something truly outrageous?!

"You wanted to cripple me? That's pipe-dream nonsense." Merlin twiddled his fingers and said nonchalantly, "With this level of strength, you wouldn't even come close to matching one of my fingers, heh~"

Every soldier of the Rose family watching was dumbfounded, their eyes gleaming as they looked at Merlin.

Maeron was their commanding officer, exceptionally powerful and always the backbone of the knights.

And today, he'd kicked an iron plate and gotten taught a lesson by a Black Iron adventurer?!

"Was Lord Maeron defeated by a single flick of his forehead?"

"This Black Iron adventurer is so strong. It's my first time seeing someone this powerful."

"What kind of joke is this? How could someone with this strength be a Black Iron adventurer? Shouldn't he be Mithril at least!"

The soldiers began murmuring amongst themselves below, speculating about Merlin's identity and finding this adventurer exceedingly mysterious.

Michelle stood frozen in place, her gaze toward Merlin entirely changed. She no longer dared to look at him with any trace of contempt.

...Isn't he a Black Iron adventurer?!

How could someone like him possess such overwhelming strength?!

Capable of effortlessly defeating the Commander of the Rose Family's Knights.

This level of strength—it was probably on par with Sister Windsor by now?

One truly must not judge a book by its cover. Under that cheap, inferior Black Iron badge actually lay astonishing combat power!

A pale flush spread across Michelle's face as she recalled her terrible attitude toward Merlin, filled with deep regret.

Having witnessed just the tip of the iceberg of Merlin's true strength, Michelle no longer doubted his standing in the slightest. He was entirely capable of sharing the stage with the Thorn Knights.

Michelle composed himself somewhat, then raised his head to speak to the Duke of Roses.

"Your Grace, I believe Lord Merlin's strength speaks for itself now. Do you still feel it necessary to assign Lord Maeron as my guard?"

.....The Duke of Roses narrowed his eyes. Having misjudged Merlin's strength and now unable to find another excuse to plant an眼线, he could only let it go. "There is no need for that. It seems Your Highness is a fortunate person, able to find two reliable individuals to serve as guards. This is indeed a comforting matter."

Michelle remained silent, feeling that he had successfully avoided the Duke of Roses' harassment, though he knew he still needed to be careful going forward.

The Duke of Roses then turned to Cecil and Kyle to give instructions. "Cecilia, you will stay at the estate."

"Father, I want to go with you as well," Cecilia said earnestly.

"What could you accomplish if you went? Stay obediently at home and don't cause trouble wherever you go. Kyle, you are in charge of keeping an eye on her." The Duke of Roses mounted his warhorse.

"Yes, my lord." Kyle bowed respectfully.

Cecilia looked somewhat dissatisfied but unwilling to defy her father's authority outright, so she simply stayed where she was, sullen and silent.

The entire Rose family procession began moving again, and the unconscious Maeron was also lifted to his feet by several soldiers.

Intimidated by Merlin's strength, the Grand Duke of Roses was reluctant to casually insert anyone near Michelle, though he planned to personally keep watch over him to prevent Michelle from suddenly fleeing before the matter was fully investigated.

Michelle secretly exhaled in relief, then turned to look at Alice and Merlin beside him, saying earnestly, "From now on, I'll be relying on both of you."

"We're on the case!" Alice patted her chest confidently.

Michelle's gaze fell upon Merlin once more, his expression slightly awkward, a reddening spreading across his face.

Recalling how he had treated Merlin before, he couldn't help but feel a trickle of embarrassment, at a loss for words.

Michelle felt it necessary to apologize to Merlin; otherwise, he'd be unable to sleep peacefully for the rest of the journey.

"....Lord Merlin, I hope you won't hold grudges about what happened before. It was purely my eyes playing tricks on me—I failed to see your strength clearly. I... I wish to formally apol—"

Michelle bowed deeply, finally setting aside his proud demeanor in front of Merlin, even adopting the honorific "Lord" to curry favor.

"N-no, no, no. This lowly one cannot accept such an apology from Your Highness. Moreover, you weren't wrong before—I really am just here as a background extra~" A hint of playful amusement flickered across Merlin's face as he delivered a sharp barb.

"...." Michelle's face flushed crimson instantly, rendered speechless by Merlin's retort. He couldn't help but think: apologizing doesn't seem to help anyway!

"Merlin, don't be so petty." Alice whispered at a lowered volume.

"What kind of pettiness is this? I simply hold a firm belief in my role as a mere extra." Merlin answered with a thoroughly serious expression.

The Royal Capital.

Beneath the entire royal palace, the interior was actually hollow.

Caves and tunnels crisscrossed densely, and underground rivers surged ceaselessly below.

At the deepest level lay a luminous lake, its faint glow rising into the air.

This was the legendary hibernation site of the Lake Maiden, the guardian deity of the Britannian royal family.

Secret passages within the palace led here, known only after the heir to the throne reaches adulthood.

At this moment, Elizabeth carried the hem of her skirt, a shining oil lamp in hand, descending slowly from the spiral staircase.

The brilliant lamplight illuminated only a small area around her, barely enough to make out the ancient, mottled steps ahead.

Elizabeth did not descend too far, instead turning off midway into a corner and proceeding along the passage.

Ahead lay profound darkness, with no visible end—but suddenly, a faint light caught her eye.

As Elizabeth continued forward, the light grew brighter, gradually revealing a prison cell at the尽头.

And inside, a person seemed to be confined—a frail figure with gorgeous golden hair.

She wore ragged clothes,借着 the dim light, writing something with a quill.

The dampness in the cave was heavy, dripping and pattering as though it were raining, and occasionally the sound of underground rivers surging could be heard.

When Elizabeth arrived before the rusted prison cell, all mysteries dissolved, and she could barely make out the scene before her.

The woman locked inside this cell

was none other than Elizabeth herself?!

title: Chapter 23 — Sisters
content:
Chapter 23 — Sisters

Volume 11 · Chapter 23

It was not so much that the person in the cage was Elizabeth as it was the real Elizabeth.

Outside the cage, a woman holding an oil lamp was Elizabeth's twin sister, Isabella.

Several years ago, the old king of Britain passed away from illness, leaving only two daughters behind, Isabella and Elizabeth.

As the eldest daughter and first heir to the empire, Isabella was supposed to inherit the throne and become the new ruler of the empire.

But due to Isabella's eccentric personality, foul temper, and heavy aura of hostility, she was unsuitable to be the new ruler.

So the old king, uncharacteristically, passed the throne to his youngest daughter Elizabeth, making her queen of the empire.

However, Isabella felt endlessly disappointed, feeling that everything had been taken away from her by her younger sister Elizabeth, and she was deeply unwilling to accept it.

Thus, several years ago, she successfully orchestrated a conspiracy to replace Elizabeth —

Isabella spent a fortune to buy a potion and drank it, after which she became like a corpse with all traces of breath gone for seven days.

So Isabella chose to drink the potion, using false death to deceive everyone, making them believe she was already dead.

Then she ordered her trusted subordinates to dig her out, completing the act of coming back to life.

After emerging from the grave, Isabella immediately went on to kidnap Elizabeth and imprison her here.

Finally, the trusted subordinate who had assisted Isabella was also poisoned and killed by her, sealing off any possibility of the secret leaking out.

Such ruthless and pitiless iron-fisted methods, no wonder the old king dared not hand the empire over to Isabella…

Since then, Isabella assumed Elizabeth's identity and began a new reign.

Although Isabella had tried very hard to imitate her sister, that severe aura of hostility would still occasionally make people suspicious.

Elizabeth in the prison cell looked somewhat haggard, having lived in this dark and sunless cage for several years now.

She had not left this place for food, clothing, shelter, or anything else, able only to write things each day to pass the time.

Clothes for washing and daily meals were all delivered by Isabella herself.

Though Elizabeth appeared somewhat listless overall, her eyes shone with vitality.

"Sister, you're here? You seem earlier than usual today?"

Elizabeth sensed Isabella outside, didn't even look up, and continued scratching away on a piece of cowhide paper with a quill pen.

"What are you doing? I've noticed you writing things a lot lately." Isabella looked at her sister inside the cage.

"I'm writing my memoirs. Maybe when I die, someone will remember me. I don't want to leave without leaving anything behind; at the very least, I need to prove that I truly existed," Elizabeth replied calmly.

"That's impossible. I am Elizabeth now. You're the already-dead Isabella. Even if you die, no one will mourn you. The person they'll always remember is me," Isabella said bluntly, thinking her sister was overthinking things.

"I know that well enough. Although we're twin sisters and look identical, our souls will forever be different, and the memories we've experienced cannot be replicated. You can never become the real me," Elizabeth said in an even tone, seemingly indifferent to the fact that she had been replaced.

"You're just being stubborn. Everything of yours belongs to me now, and you can only be imprisoned here with nothing. That is the gap between you and me. Gradually, everyone will forget you. That's reality, my poor sister…" Isabella showed a hint of mocking smile.

Elizabeth slightly furrowed her delicate brows, thinking this didn't bode well.

She stopped writing her memoirs and silently set down her quill.

"Sister, did you come today just to mock me? How shallow."

"Of course not. I came to tell you that Michelle suddenly went missing." Isabella said casually.

Hearing her daughter's name, Elizabeth's calm face showed a slight disturbance, and she couldn't help but press further.

"Missing? At such a young age, where could she have gone?"

"I don't know. I've already sent many people to search, turning the entire capital upside down, but we can't find a trace of her," Isabella said without any emotion in her voice.

Elizabeth lowered her head, worry knitting her brows. She recalled that her daughter was due to have her coming-of-age ceremony in about a year, so what was going on with this sudden disappearance? It was too strange.

Watching her sister's expression, Isabella couldn't help but tease, "You're quite worried, aren't you?"

Elizabeth said nothing, wanting to affirm that her sister should continue helping search, but she couldn't bring herself to say it.

"Don't worry, nothing terrible should have happened. I suspect Michelle has secretly left the capital on her own," Isabella said with a casual smile.

"What makes you say that?" Elizabeth looked up to ask.

"My royal administrative badge was stolen, and there's nowhere she can't go with it," Isabella said, having discovered this fact.

"Why would she do something like that? Didn't you say she was always obedient?" Elizabeth said with a serious expression.

"My foolish sister. Obedience is only on the surface. When you and I were at Michelle's age, didn't we tell plenty of lies ourselves?" Isabella said with pointed sarcasm toward Elizabeth.

"…" Elizabeth lowered her head and fell silent, secretly worried about Michelle's safety.

"Perhaps Michelle has discovered my secret. Half a month ago, she snuck into my room and was playing with the keepsake Father Left us — that sapphire pendant," Isabella said without hiding anything, directly voicing her speculation.

Elizabeth's eyes widened. Based on her knowledge of her daughter Michelle, she should easily be able to notice certain suspicious things.

But Isabella was ruthless and cruel; if Michelle had learned the secret, how could she possibly let her live?!

Elizabeth's face paled, and her eyes filled with wariness as she stared at Isabella.

"…Perhaps Michelle didn't notice anything. Maybe she just went out to clear her head."

"At a time like this, you still want to deceive me. If Michelle didn't notice anything, why would she suddenly leave the capital without a word? I'm not a fool. Do you think I'll fall for such a lame excuse as 'clearing her head'?" Isabella's tone carried a trace of anger.

"…That's not it. Michelle is still just a child; she probably doesn't understand much. I hope you won't lay a hand on her," Elizabeth's expression showed some pleading.

"Are you begging me?" Isabella's face showed a hint of amusement.

Elizabeth lowered her head, lips moving but unable to speak a word.

"What a pity, my sister. When it comes to power, there is no affection. Just as I've imprisoned you here," Isabella said coldly.

"What do you intend to do? Michelle is still just a child…" Elizabeth's emotions rose.

"So what?" Isabella paused, her eyes cold, saying without expression —

"Since Michelle knows my secret, I cannot possibly let her live.

"I will kill her with my own hands. If you want to follow your daughter to hell—

"I will respect your choice and not stop you…."

title: Chapter 24 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 24 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes

Volume 11 · Chapter 24

A few days later.

The Rose Family's private army, a full fifty thousand strong, marched majestically into the English region.

They did not follow the queen's orders to reinforce the northern defenses of England and repel the restless House of Orfre.

Instead, obeying the Rose Duke's summons, they quickly made their way directly to the royal capital and established camp beneath the towering city walls to regroup.

Several towering siege engines were already nearly as tall as the city gates themselves.

The Rose Duke had naturally come prepared. His fifty-thousand-strong private army served as an impressive show of force, enough to make Isabella uneasy.

If his own strength weren't formidable enough, what could he possibly negotiate with that iron-fisted queen? Without any leverage whatsoever.

In truth, under normal circumstances, the Rose Duke's fifty-thousand private army wouldn't amount to much and would pose no real threat.

Because under normal conditions, the capital's garrison numbered around one hundred thousand soldiers, all heavily armed and elite.

But now was an extraordinary time. Most of the capital's defending troops had been dispatched to the northern English defenses to prepare for the impending rebellion.

So now only twenty thousand royal guards remained in the capital. Against the Rose Family's fifty thousand elite troops, they could only tremble in fear, those pitch-black trebuchets striking terror into their hearts.

The Rose Family's private army established camp outside the capital, forming a siege, and the entire city instantly fell into a desperate situation of isolation and despair.

It was as though Isabella had been directly pushed onto the executioner's block, the sharp blade seemingly ready to fall at any moment and sever her head.

This unexpected move left Isabella restless and unsettled. Even if she ordered the kingdom's army to return from the north, it would likely take seven days.

Looking at the situation now, negotiation had become her last lifeline. Isabella had no choice but to accept.

The Rose Duke intended to use three questions to determine whether the current queen was real or fake. These were matters he had personally experienced with the queen. If the current Isabella were truly genuine, she would be able to answer easily, proving that everything Princess Michelle had said was one-sided nonsense.

But if the queen couldn't answer, then the Rose Duke planned to lead his army directly into the capital, uphold the legitimacy of the imperial family, and place Michelle on the throne, making himself the greatest beneficiary.

The Rose Duke's audience was granted without any obstruction.

Furthermore, a temporary ducal residence had already been arranged within the capital, a signal of goodwill from Isabella.

The Rose Duke had not yet openly stated that Michelle was with him. Instead, he had her enter the capital in disguise and temporarily reside at the ducal residence, guarded by Merlin and Alice.

Before departing, the Rose Duke instructed his knight commander, Maren, to keep a close watch on Michelle and not allow her to wander freely. He then proceeded alone to the palace to audience the queen.

The palace was illuminated with bright lights, their colorful glow radiating throughout the surroundings.

In the grand hall, Isabella sat upon the throne.

Below her were the Four Thorns Knights: Catherine, Hamilton, Dexter, and Emmanuel.

The Rose Duke entered the hall in a magnificent red formal gown, his leather boots clicking against the red carpet with each step.

He reached the center of the hall and did not kneel, but instead gave a slight bow in greeting to Isabella.

"Your Majesty, it has been quite some time."

"Yes, it has been a long time." Isabella paused, responding tactfully. "We are currently in a period of turmoil for the empire. You didn't go to reinforce the northern defenses. What brings you to see me amidst such a busy schedule?"

"I was merely passing through, so I stopped by to visit Your Majesty." The Rose Duke replied calmly.

Isabella immediately narrowed her eyes, scrutinizing the Rose Duke, feeling that this man spoke with a straight face without the slightest hint of embarrassment!

He had specially traveled all the way from Wales just to visit her, and behind him led fifty thousand troops of his private army!

This was clearly not a visit, but an outright threat, a blatant display of his military might!

Isabella could not read the Rose Duke at all. She had no idea what thoughts lay beneath that gentlemanly exterior.

"Visit me? Are you joking? Surrounding the capital with fifty thousand private troops and still claiming it's a visit? Spare me the pleasantries. What is your true purpose in coming here? You haven't reached some understanding with the House of Orfre, have you?"

Isabella had run out of patience and decided to get straight to the point, wanting to know exactly what the Rose Duke's intentions were.

"No, I don't have particularly deep ties with Grand Duke Orfre, and reaching an understanding with him is impossible." The Rose Duke spoke in a calm tone.

"Then what do you want? Stationing a massive private army outside the capital — doesn't that sound like something a treacherous vassal would do?" Isabella's expression grew grave.

"To be honest, I recently heard some rumors concerning Your Majesty, so I was quite puzzled and couldn't help but come myself to investigate." The Rose Duke said meaningfully.

"What rumors?" Isabella had a bad feeling about this.

"Someone said you are not the real queen, but rather the queen's older sister, Isabella." The Grand Duke said without hesitation.

Upon hearing this, Isabella's expression clearly became unnatural, but she quickly concealed it and composed herself.

However, the four Thorns Knights below showed puzzled expressions, wondering where these rumors had come from.

Isabella looked down at the Rose Duke from her throne, unease rising within her. She felt this rumor couldn't have come from nowhere.

"Why would you believe such a rumor? It's nothing but slander!"

"Calm yourself, Your Majesty. I am merely suspicious. Although I find it hard to believe as well, all these words came from your own daughter, Princess Michelle." The Rose Duke brought up Michelle and continued, "Princess Michelle said that the late king gave you and Isabella two heirlooms, but the name on your heirloom isn't Elizabeth — it's Isabella. That does seem rather puzzling."

The four Thorns Knights below looked at each other with strange expressions, but dared not discuss it privately. Instead, they glanced at Isabella.

"Hahaha, interesting. Michelle is going through a rebellious phase. Due to a disagreement with me over the previous imprisonment of Meshfield, we've had a falling out, so it's understandable that she'd say something inexplicable." Isabella deftly sidestepped the issue, using Michelle's young age as an excuse and hoping to let the matter pass.

"Then how do you explain the matter of the late king gifting you a pendant?" the Rose Duke pressed.

"After my sister passed away, to honor her memory, I swapped my pendant with hers. Do questions like this warrant suspicion?" Isabella smiled, though her heart churned with unease.

The Rose Duke's expression turned serious. So everything Michelle had said was indeed nonsense?

How could Queen Elizabeth be a fake? This was too abnormal.

This concerned the very succession of the empire — how could such an error occur?!

Nevertheless, to be thorough, he decided to continue pressing.

The Rose Duke was a cautious person. He trusted neither Isabella nor Michelle entirely.

"I see. It seems Princess Michelle was being far too mischievous. Spouting such words only causes trouble for others."

The faces of the four Thorns Knights relaxed somewhat, believing this was all just a misunderstanding caused by a spoiled princess — nothing major.

"Exactly. How could anyone trust a child's words? Besides, they're all just angry outbursts. I am the legitimate ruler of this empire — there is absolutely no reason to doubt that." Isabella said composedly, appearing completely unfazed.

"You're right, Your Majesty. I will send Princess Michelle back shortly. Please remember to instruct her not to speak in ways that sow suspicion." At this point, the Rose Duke was still undecided.

"You may send Michelle back. I have many things to say to her." A hint of ruthlessness flashed in Isabella's eyes. She had no intention of letting Michelle off.

"I heard Princess Michelle studies at the Academy of Theology. Do you still recall whose suggestion that was?" The Rose Duke asked tentatively.

The Rose Duke furrowed his brow slightly. He had suggested that Michelle attend the Academy of Theology himself. With such an obvious answer, how could the queen not know?!

"Surely you at least remember your youngest daughter, don't you?"

A flicker of confusion crossed Isabella's expression, followed by an embarrassed smile. "It's been so long — I'm not very clear on these details anymore."

The Rose Duke's face darkened further. This was growing increasingly strange. The youngest daughter's name, Cecilia, had been personally chosen by Elizabeth herself. And as Michelle's classmate, how could the queen not even remember her youngest daughter's name?! Moreover, there were no rumors of the queen suffering from amnesia. Why was her memory so poor?

"Then surely Your Majesty remembers the last time you visited Wales?"

Isabella was now feeling the danger. The Rose Duke wasn't asking questions at all — he was probing.

She wasn't Elizabeth. Her memories didn't align with the Rose Duke's at all, making it nearly impossible to answer correctly.

Isabella began to feel panicked, so she feigned exhaustion and said softly,

"That's enough. I'm already tired and don't wish to answer these pointless questions for now. You may return. Tomorrow, head north to England to suppress the Orfre family's rebellion."

"Very well. Then I shall take my leave. I wish Your Majesty good health as well."

The Rose Duke gave a slight bow and turned to leave, walking toward the hall's entrance.

Something was very wrong. The queen seemed completely unaware of past events?

These were all straightforward, easy-to-understand questions, yet she couldn't answer a single one.

It seemed Michelle's suspicions were justified. The current Queen Elizabeth had problems...

The Rose Duke wrestled with a decision in his mind — should he lead the Rose Knights and storm the palace?

Watching the Rose Duke's departing back, Isabella's face grew extremely dark, killing intent becoming ever more prominent.

That ferocious gaze seemed to wish to devour him alive.

After the Rose Duke left, an eerie silence fell over the hall.

The four Thorns Knights remained silent, standing wordlessly below without departing.

The gloom on Isabella's face slowly lifted, replaced by composure.

She slowly raised her head and spoke in a commanding tone.

"Hamilton, Dexter, Emmanuel."

Catherine, whose eyes had been closed, raised her head and looked at Isabella upon the throne in confusion.

The three male Thorns Knights stepped forward, knelt on one knee, and spoke in unison.

"What are your orders, Your Majesty?"

"I order you — before the Rose Duke leaves the capital, secretly assassinate him." Isabella narrowed her eyes, speaking with absolute conviction.

"I will absolutely not allow him to see tomorrow's sunrise."

"Before dawn—"

"I must see this man's corpse here."

title: Chapter 25 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 25 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 11 · Chapter 25

Isabella finished giving her orders, but the Thorn Knights below were all bewildered, unable to understand this mission.

Katherine slightly furrowed her delicate brows, finding it inexplicable that the queen wanted to assassinate the Duke of Roses, who commanded heavy military forces.

With civil strife imminent in the empire, this was a time when capable people were needed most. The Duke of Roses' army was widely renowned throughout the empire.

If they assassinated the Duke of Roses, it would only complicate matters and indirectly make enemies for themselves.

Katherine strongly advised against the queen doing this, but she couldn't understand why she had made such a decision.

"Isn't this unwise?" Hamilton muttered in a hoarse voice.

"..." The irritable Emmanuel didn't speak, but there was still some doubt in his eyes.

Only Dexter showed a bit of leadership temperament, daring to raise a voice of dissent before the queen.

"Your Majesty, why must we do this? The Duke of Roses is also a pillar of the empire. Isn't it improper to assassinate him in secret?"

Isabella had originally thought she could deceive the Duke of Roses, but after his repeated probing at the end, she had exposed herself.

Although it all sounded like trivial small talk, Isabella could feel the hidden dangers everywhere — it was by no means simple.

Even though the Duke of Roses appeared amiable on the surface and said he would return Michelle and then head to the northern frontier,

Isabella didn't believe such pleasant-sounding promises at all, especially after asking those three questions.

Isabella increasingly felt that the Grand Duke of Roses was someone she needed to eliminate. If she let him leave the capital alive, tomorrow she would face the fifty thousand troops of the Rose family.

The capital's military forces were now dangerously thin and could hardly withstand the Iron Cavalry of the Rose family!

In truth, neither Isabella nor the Grand Duke of Roses was anyone to be trifled with. Their peaceful conversation earlier had already been an underground contest of countless maneuvers.

To keep these Thorn Knights on her side, Isabella had to tell some lies to deceive them.

"Haven't you realized it yet? The Duke of Roses will rebel against the empire. If he leaves the capital unharmed, tomorrow morning the city gates will be smashed open by the Rose family's army with his own hands!"

The four Thorn Knights below were all shaken, startled by the queen's words.

In that brief conversation just now, they hadn't detected the slightest hint of rebellion from the Duke of Roses. On the contrary, it had seemed relatively peaceful.

"Your Majesty, you're not joking, are you? The Duke of Roses just agreed to go reinforce the northern frontier." Dexter said, puzzled.

"How cunning is the Duke of Roses — don't you know well in your hearts? Right now, an entire fifty-thousand-strong army is stationed outside the capital's gates. No matter how beautiful his words are, they can't disguise the fact that he's surrounding the entire capital. You think such an ambitious man is being obedient after just a few sentences?!" Isabella's voice rang out, full of confidence.

The Thorn Knights instantly fell silent. After thinking about it for a moment, the Duke of Roses did have problems.

Did he really only suspect the queen was a fake and mobilize an entire army to surround the capital because of that?

The Thorn Knights started overthinking it. Considering the Duke of Roses' cunning reputation, it was indeed hard to trust him.

"Moreover, I've already received a secret report that the Duke of Roses has been getting quite close to Grand Duke Afurei recently. And now he's sending private armies to surround the entire capital. Such obvious ambition is written all over his face!" Isabella said with a thoroughly serious expression, fabricating the secret report out of thin air. It seemed she was dead set on putting the Duke of Roses to death.

All the Thorn Knights' faces changed color. They didn't doubt the authenticity of the report; they just felt things were turning for the worse.

If the report were true, and the Duke of Roses was closely connected to rebels, then wasn't the move to surround the capital even more incriminating!?

All four Thorn Knights grew tense. If they let the Duke of Roses leave, the consequences would be unimaginable.

"Your Majesty sees far ahead. We didn't consider enough." Dexter lowered his head, feeling that questioning the queen had been a mistake.

"I suspect that once the Duke of Roses returns to his residence, he will hurry to leave the capital. He'll likely take Michelle with him, using my daughter's life as leverage to threaten me. So you must kill him before he leaves, otherwise those armies glaring hungrily outside the capital will cause our fall by morning." Isabella paused, then said seriously, "This mission will be carried out by the three of you. Katherine, stay behind on standby."

"Yes, Your Majesty!"

The three Thorn Knights — Dexter, Emmanuel, and Hamilton — answered in unison.

"As for Michelle..." Isabella rested her hand on her aching forehead and said faintly —

"Try to ensure her safety. Bring her back alive."

◇

The capital.

The temporary duke's residence.

Only four people were in the hall: Merlin, Alice, Michelle, and the Knight Commander Maelon.

Michelle sat in a chair, looking somewhat anxious, worried about the results of the Duke of Roses' investigation.

If the Duke of Roses hadn't found anything out, she estimated she'd simply be sent back to her mother.

Michelle's heart was uneasy, and she occasionally felt the distant Knight Commander Maelon's gaze fixed on her.

Maelon was responsible for keeping an eye on the little princess. He paced back and forth at the doorway, feeling that the sky had grown completely dark and the duke should be returning soon.

His eyes occasionally stole glances at Merlin standing by the window. The scene of being defeated by a flick to the forehead was still vivid in his mind.

Maelon couldn't figure it out at all — why would a Black Iron-rank adventurer be so powerful?! He was completely different from the good-for-nothings he'd seen before. This guy truly had formidable strength.

Recalling the situation back then, the other party seemed to have no magical aura or battle energy pressure at all. He had relied purely on physical power.

Not relying on battle energy to enhance one's body and still possessing such strength was, in Maelon's eyes, unbelievable.

Though Maelon felt quite humiliated, he had to admit Merlin's strength, and he was itching with curiosity to figure out the reason behind it. So he swallowed his pride and approached.

"U-um... Mer... Lord Merlin?"

"Hmm?" Merlin withdrew his gaze and casually glanced at Maelon, wondering what this defeated subordinate wanted.

"Wanting to pick a fight? Did you forget I gave you a concussion?" Merlin said expressionlessly.

"N-no, no, Lord Merlin, you jest. I'm not here to pick a fight. I just want to ask a question." Maelon rubbed his hands together, trying to keep his posture as low as possible.

"What is it?" Merlin felt puzzled inside. He didn't think he could have any real connection with this knight commander.

"Um... Your physical strength seems unprecedentedly powerful. Even a single flick carries such tremendous impact. I was wondering... how do you train?" Maelon asked cautiously. Asking about someone's training methods was impolite, but he was just so curious!

"Oh~ That's simple. Training, hmm..." Merlin put on a suddenly enlightened expression, then said in a very serious tone, "First, you need to疯狂ly abuse yourself until you reach the brink of death, until you can be mercilessly trampled by a huge group of rock giants. Then do standing long jumps for hundreds of millions of times, until you can cleave dragons in the sky in two. After that, be thrown into the deep sea ten thousand meters down, to have an intimate encounter with sea demons, until you're nearly unconscious from oxygen deprivation. Finally, this part is the most amazing — dive into flowing molten lava to take a bath, until the lava trolls are so furious they pack up and move away. Complete those four tasks, and you'll become as strong as me..."

"I..." Maelon was speechless, so scared he almost went dumb. His嘴角 twitched and trembled nonstop —

What the hell!

What kind of joke is this?!

Is this even training?! This is clearly throwing your life away!
