title: Chapter 26 — Evacuation
content:
Chapter 26 — Evacuation

Volume 11 · Chapter 26

Maelun's gaze toward Merlin changed completely; if what was just said is true, then this is simply something no human could do!

Although his heart was filled with shock, Maelun did not believe Merlin's words, thinking the other was deliberately concealing something.

Having suffered a setback, Maelun reluctantly left, not even angry, after all cultivation is a personal secret.

Merlin watched Maelun leave, thinking, "What's going on? Don't you believe what I said? I didn't tell a single lie!"

Alice curiously came over and asked in surprise, "What were you two talking about? Why does that knight captain look so embarrassed?"

"He asked me how I train to become as strong as I am, and I told him a series of self‑harming training methods, but he seemed not to believe me." Merlin spread his hands, looking somewhat innocent.

"Don’t apply the demons’ training methods to humans—people will die; only someone with a screw loose would believe that!" Alice frowned, a few black lines sliding down her forehead.

"No way, I’m still jumping around, aren’t I?" Merlin shrugged his shoulders.

"You’ve had enough..."

Alice rolled her eyes, thinking, "Who would compare themselves with this pervert?! We’re not even the same species!"

Merlin glanced at Michelle not far away and asked softly, "How is that human princess doing?"

"She looks rather tense, doesn’t she? If the queen is really a fake, the situation inside the empire will only become more complicated, and a state of internal and external troubles will destroy any peace." Alice said helplessly, feeling that she was merely an adventurer and many things were simply beyond her.

"Tch, what a hassle—finally able to have a quiet life."

Merlin’s brows were locked tight with worry, making him feel inwardly irritated; he deeply disliked this turbulent and precarious feeling.

Thinking back, leaving the Death Swamp was just to alleviate the curse and then live a peaceful, uneventful life, right?

But no matter where he went, he could never calm down, always getting inexplicably dragged into chaos.

Yet he still couldn’t return to the Death Swamp; having achieved nothing out there, he’d be dragging a heap of debt and tail between his legs back—sure to be looked down upon by Lilith.

Besides, his curse hasn’t been lifted; if he went back he’d just be waiting to die, after all the Death Swamp is demon‑race territory, Saint‑tier powerhouses are all allies, and he hasn’t even gone mad enough to start cutting down his own allies....

Merlin glanced at Alice beside him, really wanting to ask her a question, curious how she would answer.

"....What are you looking at me for?" Alice noticed Merlin’s gaze, feeling that this guy was again scheming about her in his mind.

"Nothing, that uh..." Merlin gave a light cough, pretending not to care as he asked, "If the empire falls into turmoil and it’s no longer suitable to live here, would you be willing to go back to the Death Swamp with me?"

Alice’s heart skipped a beat; she instantly widened her eyes at Merlin, her expression showing a hint of panic.

"What’s going on? Are you asking if I’m willing to go back to my hometown with you?"

.-.This subtext—does it mean you want to take me away?

"Why do I have the feeling that you want to drag me back to be your concubine?"

"But come to think of it, why would I go with this guy? He probably doesn’t have any romantic feelings for me, right? How strange...."

Alice felt this was Merlin’s forceful roundabout confession of love, but having been teased too many times, she was immune and appeared much calmer.

"....Why do you want to bring me along when you go back to the Death Swamp?"

Merlin wanted to speak but stopped, himself caught in confusion, not knowing for a moment how to answer Alice.

Yeah, I could just go back by myself; why bring Alice along?

How strange—why would I say something so nonsensical?

Maybe it’s because I’ve gotten used to having Alice around; if she weren’t here, there’d be far less fun—surely that’s it!

Merlin kept nodding to himself, having convinced himself, then turned to Alice and spoke very seriously.

"Because teasing you is one of the great joys of my life; even if I bring you back, I’ll still tease you, otherwise I’d be terribly bored."

Alice’s face instantly fell; her surging excitement turned instantly into a dead pool, she stared at Merlin expressionlessly, thinking this guy was treating her as a toy, utterly lacking any humanity—quickly give back my pure feelings from earlier, you bastard!

"Don’t build your fun on my pain—you really are the person I hate most! Want me to go back to the Death Swamp with you? Dream on! I’d rather die than go back with you! Hmph~ !"

title: Chapter 27 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 27 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 11 · Chapter 27

The Duke of Roses looked grave, not wanting to waste time because the situation was too urgent.
"Really? Will assassins come attack us?" Michelle stared wide-eyed, never expecting things to turn out like this.
"Exactly, if the false queen is truly Isabella, with her ruthless and cruel nature, she will certainly not let us go; if we can escape the capital sooner, our chances of survival will be greater," the Duke of Roses analyzed.
Michelle's expression turned panicked, thinking that because she knew the secret, her aunt wouldn't even spare her?!
So Michelle didn't hesitate any longer; preserving her life was paramount. She picked up the black robe nearby, preparing to disguise herself.
"There's no time to lose, let's go quickly."
The Duke nodded, then turned to his knight commander and said, "Maelen, if we encounter any danger on the road, then you'll be the only one we can rely on."
Maelen's expression instantly turned stern, and he gave a firm, resonant reply: "Rest assured, my lord; I have followed you for many years, and no matter what strong foes we meet on the road, I will become your shield."
The Duke patted Maelen on the shoulder to encourage him, then said to Merlin and Alice, "You two will also have to rely on me more; protecting Her Highness Michelle is of utmost importance. I heard you are friends of little Cecilia, and I trust you completely."
"Please rest assured, Duke; we will devote ourselves fully to protecting Her Highness Michelle's safety," Alice replied earnestly.
Merlin, meanwhile, wore a carefree expression, pursing his lips and saying, "It has nothing to do with me; I'm just here to make up the numbers, don't mind me."
The Duke and Michelle's expressions instantly became unnatural, feeling his lack of motivation worrying.
Beside them, Maelens sensed the atmosphere was off, coughing repeatedly but daring not to say more.
"Lord Merlin, I have already apologized to you; what must I do for you to forgive my previous rudeness?" Michelle said, her face full of displeasure, her heart torn.
Alice couldn't help but whisper to Merlin, "You guy, try to read the room a bit? Think about the 700,000 gold reward—don't quarrel with money. We're pretty destitute right now..."
Seeing Alice pleading for him, Merlin stopped his listless remarks and let out a sigh—
"Ah, truly troublesome...."

The night sky was a deep azure, as profound as an unseen ocean's depths.
The pale white moon was surrounded by flickering stars of various colors.
On such a quiet and peaceful night, the streets of the capital suddenly rang with the clatter of armor colliding like clattering noises.
Dense as raindrops striking, it was obvious the numbers were large.
A line of torches illuminated the surroundings, swiftly heading toward the temporary duke's manor.
Led by the ugly-looking Hamel, a small squadron of exactly five hundred Crimson Flower knights marched to exterminate the Duke of Roses.
Silver armor reflected the firelight, footsteps echoed, yet they did not disturb the residents, carrying out their mission stealthily.
The tightly shut gates of the temporary duke's manor were instantly shattered by the shockwave from the crystal ball in Hamel's hand; his hunched figure stepped into the courtyard and, facing the knights behind him, commanded:
"Search! If you see the Duke of Roses, execute him on the spot; if it is Her Highness Michelle, bring her back alive!"
The knights behind him surged into the manor, torches and weapons in hand, beginning to search everywhere.
Hamel lifted his head, observing the surroundings, feeling it was a little too quiet, giving him a sense of something unusual.
Sure enough, not long after, the knight captain returned to report to Hamel: "My lord, we have searched every corner of the manor and found neither the Duke of Roses nor Her Highness Michelle."
"Tsk!" Hamel clicked his tongue in dissatisfaction, his tone tinged with irritation: "Did they already run away? How fast! Indeed, as His Majesty predicted, the Duke of Roses' wolfish ambitions to flee the capital and incite rebellion are exactly as expected; his sneaky escape shows he has a guilty conscience."
"Lord Hamel, what should we do now? Have we already arrived too late?" the knight captain asked curiously.
"It doesn't matter if this traitor gets a head start; His Majesty had already anticipated this step. Aside from me, the other two Crimson Flower knights have already taken separate actions, setting up ambushes on the essential routes out of the capital; they surely cannot escape the capital!" Hamel's hoarse voice sounded extremely fierce, and it seemed Isabella had already set the trap.
"Then what should we do now?" the knight captain asked, puzzled.
"We will now move to surround the capital's city gates, launching a pincer attack from front and rear, so these rebels cannot fly away!" Hamel issued the order, adding:
"We must be careful not to harm Her Highness Michelle."
"This Duke of Roses is now using the little princess as a hostage, restricting our actions...."

In the capital's back alleys.

In

Night fell, the moonlight flickering between the clouds' veil.
The Duke of Roses led Michelle, Maelens, Merlin, and Alice in covert action.
The five figures moved swiftly through the darkness, taking a rather winding route toward the city gate.
Both the Duke of Roses and Michelle wore black robes to conceal their identities, making them hard to notice.
The Duke of Roses chose not to bring guards, because this covert escape should stay low‑key; a large group would be too conspicuous and easily draw pursuers.
Moreover, the Duke avoided taking a carriage for the same reason—it would be too obvious and could easily lead to an unknown ambush en route.
The Duke had already planned everything; all he needed was to reach the city gate, fire a signal flare, and his subordinates would meet him there.
Now the distance to the capital's gate was growing closer, and the escape plan seemed to be going smoothly.
"Your Highness, please hurry; we need to act before the enemy moves..."
"..I know this little path SF..."
Michelle seemed not adept at exercise; sweat already appeared on her forehead, and her breathing grew heavy.
To prevent Michelle from slowing them down, the Duke could only forcibly pull her into a quick jog.
Maelens expression grew grave, staying close behind the Duke of Roses, constantly vigilant of the surroundings.
Merlin and Alice stretched out behind them, likewise keeping watch, their attention focused on Michelle.
Although Merlin's ability far surpassed Alice's, he did not feel particularly tense, his face showing no expression.
When the clouds shifted, revealing a thread of pure moonlight—
Merlin: "There's an ambush ahead."
Just as Alice was stunned, in the midst of the group's escape route, a sudden change erupted!
The irascible Sixth Crimson Flower knight, Emmanuel, emerged slowly from the darkness, his boots tapping the ground with a soft pat‑pat.
"Good evening, ladies and gentlemen."
"I have been waiting for you here for a long time."
"I don't know whether this surprise of mine will catch you off guard."

title: Chapter 28 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 28 — Extra Update for Monthly Tickets

Volume 11 · Chapter 28

The star-filled sky stretched dark and endless above.

Emmanuel wore a suit of finely crafted silver armor, its surface gleaming under the brilliant moonlight, dazzling to behold.

Behind him, his red skin rippled gently, the golden thorn-flower patterns across his back exuding an ancient, primal aura.

"Just as His Majesty predicted— you don't take the main roads, instead hiding in the shadows of night, sneaking through back alleys. Isn't that just walking right into our trap? Hahaha!"

Emmanuel's lips curled into a grin, though the expression carried a chilling, almost feral edge.

"Tch!" the Duke of Roses muttered, shaking his head, "So we've been outmaneuvered? How infuriating..."

Michelle, terrified by Emmanuel's presence, quietly slipped behind the Duke of Roses.

She knew Emmanuel well enough— a hot-headed brute who'd attack even his own allies if they got in his way, showing no mercy or courtesy. He was nothing more than a killing machine born solely to complete his mission.

That's why seeing Emmanuel in his unhinged state, Michelle instinctively feared him. Perhaps the other Thorn Knights could still be reasoned with, but this madman never listened to anyone!

Mairen stood ready for battle, her hand gripping the hilt of her sword at her waist, crouched like a fierce leopard poised to pounce at any moment.

Alice mirrored Mairen's reaction, her fingers tightly gripping her thin sword, eyes filled with hostility as she glared at Emmanuel.

"As His Majesty said, Lord Duke—you really are cunning..."

Emmanuel's face bore a sneer, as if he looked down on everyone present.

Slowly, he drew the wide-bladed English sword from his waist, its edge catching the moonlight and flashing with cold, deadly gleams.

"But your cunning won't save you— in my presence, you're all doomed!"

"I'm cunning? How ridiculous. The real liar is the woman sitting on that throne." The Duke of Roses replied coldly.

"Enough talk. Just hand over your head—I only need that."

Emmanuel disliked talking. What was the mission? Just do it. Nothing was simpler than killing.

His golden aura erupted violently, coalescing into a dense sphere of energy upon his wide blade.

Emmanuel's brows tightened. In the blink of an eye, his form became a streak of shadow, charging straight at the Duke of Roses, aiming directly for his throat!

"Lord Duke, watch out!"

Mairen, drawing on her Saint-tier energy, drew her sword first and stepped in front of the Duke, blade raised to block!

Clang! The two swords collided with a deafening crash, sparks flying in all directions!

"EEEEEEK!" Michelle, overcome with fear, let out a shrill scream and ducked, covering her ears.

Facing Emmanuel's direct assault, Mairen felt a deep chill run down her spine. His strength was overwhelming— even the pressure of his Saint-tier aura alone left her feeling powerless.

Like a magnificent tiger eyeing a small white rabbit, ready to devour it at any moment.

Though both Mairen and Emmanuel were Saint-tier warriors, the gap between them was too vast. They were simply not on the same level.

Mairen barely managed to deflect Emmanuel's strike, breaking into a cold sweat as she stepped back.

"Tch! Annoying fly— you dare stand in my way?" Emmanuel roared, swinging his sword with brutal force. "Get out of my way!"

"Cough!" Mairen, unable to withstand Emmanuel's attack any longer, spat up a mouthful of blood and was sent flying backward, crashing into the wall with a loud "thud."

"Hmph, weakling. Stay there and be a good audience— what are you trying to prove?" Emmanuel rolled his eyes, ignoring Mairen entirely. "Next up... it's your turn, Duke..."

"..."

Michelle hid behind the Duke of Roses, too afraid to even breathe.

A cold sweat trickled down the Duke's temple. He thought bitterly, his knight commander was nowhere near the level of the Thorn Knights.

"Both of you— grab onto me."

Merlin suddenly appeared behind the Duke of Roses and Michelle, his voice carrying deep meaning.

"Huh?!" Michelle stared blankly, confused about what was happening.

The Duke of Roses was equally puzzled, unsure what Merlin meant.

But Merlin didn't bother explaining. He scooped up Michelle, who was barely two heads shorter than him, and tucked her under his arm.

With a casual grab, he lifted the Duke of Roses to his feet.

Without saying a word, Merlin launched forward with an astonishing burst of speed, sweeping past Emmanuel in a blur. In the blink of an eye, all three of them had vanished from sight.

Interestingly, as Merlin brushed past Emmanuel, he gave him a disdainful smirk— a blatant mockery.

In truth, Merlin could have easily beheaded Emmanuel right then and there. But the Duke of Roses and Michelle were pressed for time, so prioritizing their escape from the capital over cleaning up a fake was the better choice.

"Ugh!"

Emmanuel's eyes widened in shock, his face pale with terror.

What the hell was that redhead?

If he wasn't mistaken, wasn't that a black-iron adventurer?

How could someone with such an unbelievable speed exist?!

In that instant, his speed had completely surpassed Emmanuel's perception. There was no time to react at all!

Emmanuel stared at the empty alley, unable to see the faintest trace of Merlin and the others.

For a moment, cold sweat beaded on Emmanuel's forehead. He sensed that this golden-haired man was likely a powerhouse far beyond his own.

Emmanuel had never encountered such a situation before. A fierce sense of danger flickered within him, and the invisible threat made his arms tremble uncontrollably.

"Damn it!"

Emmanuel, unwilling to let his targets escape, turned to chase after them and settle things with that golden-haired man.

But standing in his path was a silver-haired female swordsman, slowly drawing her thin blade from its scabbard. A chill began to sweep through the air— it was Alice, who had been lurking nearby.

Alice, seeing Merlin lead the Duke of Roses and Michelle away, felt it necessary to hold Emmanuel back and prevent him from interfering with their escape plan.

"Where are you going? If you want to catch up to them, I advise you give up. Your opponent is me!"

"And me too!"

Mairen leaned on her sword to stay upright, gritting her teeth against the pain as she slowly rose, ready to team up with Alice to deal with this Thorn Knight.

"Tch!"

Emmanuel narrowed his eyes, eyeing Alice up and down. Noticing the silver adventurer's badge on her neck, he didn't feel the slightest pressure.

Still, two Saint-tier warriors together— even for Emmanuel, he had to take them a bit more seriously. Otherwise, he might end up in a ditch.

Emmanuel found himself caught between them, but he showed no sign of panic. Instead, his Saint-tier pressure continued to build.

His golden aura blazed like raging flames, Emmanuel's eyes bulging like two dice about to burst, veins throbbing on his forehead.

"You two are going to stop me?"

"What a joke..."

"Why does everyone refuse to die?"

title: Chapter 29 — Ambush
content:
Chapter 29 — Ambush

Volume 11 · Chapter 29

Alice's body began radiating golden magical power and fighting spirit, intertwining like rising steam.

The temperature around them plummeted, cold frost attacking from all sides with a hissing sound.

In just a few breaths, a thin layer of ice formed on the ground, making one feel as if standing in deep winter!

White cold energy slowly condensed, gradually forming a massive blizzard dragon that let out a furious roar toward Emmanuel!

Emmanuel narrowed his eyes, looking at Alice. The intense cold made each breath feel like it was piercing his internal organs.

And that obvious dragon pressure continuously intimidated his enemies!

Emmanuel felt a trace of threat. This demon swordswoman was not someone to be taken lightly; he had to take things seriously.

Although Emmanuel faced two enemies, he could easily crush Meren. It was only Alice who gave him that sense of threat.

"Huh!" Meren's eyes widened. He was scared by the aura radiating from Alice—especially that overwhelming dragon pressure that made his very soul tremble. For a moment, he felt this female adventurer was nothing short of a great dragon!

"Heh heh... How interesting." Emmanuel smiled, the corners of his mouth turning up in a particularly ferocious manner. "Woman, congratulations. You've successfully aroused my interest. I really want to kill you now!"

"Don't speak so lightly. When the time comes, you won't even have a face left to show the Thorns Knights." Alice slowly rotated the slender sword in her hand.

"You really are a special woman. How did you get that dragon pressure? Have you practiced dragon-race martial arts or magic?" Emmanuel asked testingly.

"I have no need to tell you. Words are useless. Come, let's fight!"

The moment Alice finished speaking, a brilliant cold light appeared in the air, condensing into eight incredibly sharp ice swords!

Cold energy radiated in all directions. The ice swords pointed at Emmanuel and immediately shot forth, the sound of tearing through the air continuous and unremitting!

Emmanuel's pupils contracted. He launched himself into the air, beginning to dodge rapidly. Several golden ice swords skimmed past his ears.

For those he couldn't avoid, Emmanuel had to raise his broadsword to block, producing sharp clanging sounds of impact.

What kind of ice is this?!

It's so hard! Far beyond normal寒冰 created by magical power!

Emmanuel felt a certain pressure. After just one brief exchange, he judged that Alice was an opponent worth taking seriously.

After reaching Saint-tier, Alice had relied on the Frost Sacred Dragon inheritance crystal, and her strength had advanced tremendously.

This secret technique of the Great Snow Mountain, which fused with ice crystals—its hardness and offensive power were truly frightening!

Emmanuel landed. A red line suddenly appeared on his face, and dark red blood slowly trickled down.

It seemed Emmanuel had done his best to dodge, but he was still grazed by the ice swords.

"Damn it, to actually be able to hurt me... I have to compliment you on this one."

Emmanuel wiped the blood from his face with his hand. Although he wore a smile, there was an added seriousness to his expression.

Alice said not a word. She raised her slender sword and thrust fiercely forward, instantly creating a barrage of flashing silver light and ice shards!

Meren wasn't standing by watching either. He charged forward directly, launching fierce slashing strikes in rapid succession.

In the darkness—

Emmanuel's broadsword countered with Saint-tier fighting spirit erupting again, making it difficult for both to close in.

The three of them traded blows back and forth in the alley, the sound of weapons clashing ringing out continuously, sparks occasionally cutting through the blackness—

On the other side.

Merlin had led Michelle and Duke Rose away from the vortex of conflict.

Only when the surroundings grew quiet did he stop walking and set the two of them down.

By now they were very close to the northern city gate. The endpoint of escaping the royal capital was just ahead!

"We're temporarily safe. We should be able to escape safely." Merlin said calmly.

Michelle and Duke Rose were still somewhat shaken, their expressions tense as they looked around in all directions.

Duke Rose wiped the cold sweat from his forehead. "Thank you, Lord Merlin, for your tremendous assistance. I will forever remember this favor."

"No need. I only saved you as a side matter." Merlin replied indifferently.

"...Duke Rose felt somewhat awkward, but couldn't very well argue. After all, his current safety depended entirely on Merlin."

Michelle felt the area was safe and let out a long breath. It seemed Emmanuel hadn't pursued them—they must have been held back.

She looked up at Merlin's tall figure, feeling somewhat guilty in her heart. She had treated him so poorly before, and yet now she was being saved by him...

Michelle hesitated for a moment, her cheeks flushing slightly, and spoke in a timid tone.

"...Lord Merlin, thank you for your teaching. Please..."

"I did it for the money. Otherwise, I wouldn't meddle in someone else's affairs." Merlin's reply was cold.

"...Michelle felt disappointed in her heart. She hadn't expected Merlin to still hold a grudge."

Merlin paid no mind to Michelle and instead spoke to Duke Rose. "According to the plan, we're supposed to break through from the north gate, right? I remember the north gate of the royal capital was heavily guarded—the hardest to break through?"

"Don't worry about that. The most dangerous place is the safest place. Normal people wouldn't think we'd leave the capital through the north gate. Furthermore, the royal palace is currently short-handed and can't cover everything. Even if there's an ambush, it would be in other directions. So while the north gate seems impregnable, it's actually the easiest path." Duke Rose paused and continued, "I've already made all the plans. My people will be waiting at the north gate to rendezvous with us."

Merlin had nothing to say, thinking to himself that this Duke Rose was indeed cunning, calculating everything throughout.

Duke Rose took out a cylindrical object from his chest and pulled hard toward the sky. Instantly, a dazzling spark shot into the night sky!

The signal flare rose into the sky, becoming brilliantly conspicuous for an instant!

Duke Rose's signal flare fired, and the family knights outside the north gate would immediately begin their action—killing the guards on the royal capital walls and using ropes to rescue themselves and Michelle.

"Very well. There's no time to lose. Your Highness, let's move quickly. My people have already begun their action."

The three of them moved quickly toward their destination—the north gate.

Duke Rose chattered beside Michelle, urging her to hurry.

Merlin followed behind, preventing this 700,000 gold coin reward from going down the drain.

Just as they were about to reach the base of the city gate, Merlin smelled a faint but distinct trace of blood. His brows furrowed instantly.

"Tsk. Be careful. There are enemies ahead."

Duke Rose and Michelle both widened their eyes and temporarily slowed their pace, looking forward.

More than fifty corpses lay on the ground. Dark red blood flowed slowly, gathering into puddles on the ground.

All these corpses wore Rose family armor and cloaks. The family crests on their cloaks were very obvious—they were clearly Rose family knights!

The torchlight flickered continuously, shadows swaying constantly in this grim scene.

Beneath the heavy city gate stood a very imposing figure. That massive musculature and stature made one feel deeply uneasy.

A giant axe rested on the ground. Rose knight blood flowed slowly across its surface, exuding tremendous intimidation.

The Third Thorns Knight, Dexter, had long been waiting here. He slowly turned his head and grinned broadly—

"Does Your Grace wish to leave the capital alive?"

"First you'll have to ask my axe if it agrees!"

title: Chapter 30 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 30 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 11 · Chapter 30

Merlin, standing behind them, rolled his eyes. *What's the safest place is the most dangerous place?* Right until they still got caught in the end?

Michelle looked at the bloody scene, her expression deeply unnatural, her heart trembling with terror, her lips quivering as she couldn't speak a single word.

Duke Rose had never expected every step of his planning to be within the enemy's grasp. Looking at the corpses of his family knights scattered across the ground, he could only silently clench his fists.

He glaringly glared at Dexter, feeling as though all his escape routes had been blocked off. The subordinates who were supposed to come rescue him according to plan seemed to have only two or three survivors, and they were currently cowering in the corner, completely paralyzed by fear.

Duke Rose gritted his teeth, his body trembling — not from fear, but from unbearable anger!

"You really bite hard, don't you?"

"It's not that we bite hard, but everything was already within Her Majesty's expectations."

Dexter turned around, his crimson cloak fluttering wildly. Standing over two meters tall with a burly, massive build, he looked like a giant.

He casually swung the thousand-jin great axe, instantly summoning a fierce wind that was impossible to face.

Dexter hoisted his great axe onto his shoulder and slowly walked toward Duke Rose.

"You really are as cunning as His Majesty described. He said you would choose to escape through the north gate, the most heavily defended entrance, because the most dangerous place is the one people are least likely to notice. As His Majesty predicted, I've been waiting here for so long, and you finally showed up."

*Tsks!* Duke Rose clicked his tongue, unable to withstand Dexter's imposing presence, and took a half-step backward. *Why has every move I make been anticipated by this fake queen?! What am I supposed to do now to escape?!*

"Since you've encountered me, the empire's strongest warrior, stop thinking about escaping and just come forward to meet your death!" A murderous gleam flashed in Dexter's eyes as he looked at Duke Rose as though he were already a dead man.

Michelle hid behind Duke Rose, too terrified even to draw a breath. It was the first time she'd ever seen an Thorn Knight kill someone. They always appeared so polished and glamorous on the outside, but their true nature was no different from an executioner's!

Duke Rose's mind raced frantically, trying to find a way to break the deadlock, but he had no idea where to start.

Moreover, Dexter was the third-ranked knight, widely renowned. In terms of sheer power alone, he was likely the strongest among the twelve knights!

His invincible martial prowess would turn any battlefield into a meat grinder. A single punch could shake the heavens; a single stomp could shatter the earth!

Apart from negotiation, Duke Rose couldn't find any other way to ease the situation.

"Dexter, calm down first and listen to me...."

"Hmm? Last words? Very well, I allow it." Dexter hoisted his great axe, momentarily halting his steps and no longer pressing closer to Duke Rose.

Duke Rose composed himself slightly and spoke earnestly, "You've all been deceived by the queen. The woman sitting on the throne isn't Elizabeth at all, but Isabella, who feigned her death several years ago! What you're doing right now goes against the legitimate will of the royal family!"

"Hahahaha...." Dexter burst into unrestrained laughter, his voice resembling thunder on a cloudy day.

"Huh?"

A bead of cold sweat dripped down Duke Rose's forehead. He didn't see anything amusing about what he'd just said.

"Lord Duke, I'm amazed you can tell lies with such righteous indignation. If Her Majesty hadn't warned me beforehand, I might have actually fallen for your nonsense!" Dexter paused, speaking as though he already knew everything, "His Majesty said you would falsely accuse her identity, raise a rebellion under the banner of crusading against a fake queen, and then ally with the Avrey family to overthrow the empire together. I suppose you used this same lie to deceive Her Highness the Princess, correct?"

Duke Rose's forehead vein twitched. *I haven't even thrown mud yet, and this fake queen is already counter-attacking to get me killed?! This is outrageous?!*

"Everything I just said is the absolute truth, and it wasn't me who suspected the queen's identity, but Her Highness Michelle! Would Her Highness frame her own mother?! "

"Ridiculous. Do you think I would believe that?!" Dexter snorted coldly and said dismissively, "Her Highness Michelle is still young. What could she possibly understand? She must have been bewitched by you, a treacherous minister! Otherwise, why would she suspect His Majesty?!"

Duke Rose felt that the other party already had a preconceived notion and wouldn't listen to reason, so he could only ask Michelle to speak. "Your Highness, please, say something. This man has been brainwashed. With just my explanation alone, it would likely be too feeble."

"......" Michelle hesitated for a moment, then plucked up her courage and shouted loudly, "Dexter-sama, everything Duke Rose says is true. My birth mother is a fake. That cruel and cold-blooded person is not my mother at all; she is plainly my aunt! If you find it difficult to make a choice, then I beg you to let us go!"

Dexter sighed, looking at Michelle with sympathy in his eyes. "Your Highness, it seems you've been severely bewitched. Stop throwing childish tantrums. Come back with me; His Majesty misses you very much."

"I will not return! If I go back, I won't have a good ending!" Michelle loudly rejected the olive branch Dexter extended.

"Then I'll have no choice but to use some rough methods..." Dexter said helplessly, his gaze shifting to the others. "Aside from Her Highness Michelle, all of you are to die!"

Both Duke Rose and Princess Michelle showed expressions of utter despair. Trying to make a brute like that see reality was probably harder than scaling the heavens!

Seeing the situation had reached a deadlock with no chance for negotiation, Merlin spoke up, "Do you need my help? If you're willing to take responsibility for killing a Thorn Knight and ensure the trouble doesn't come back to me, I'll help you take down this big guy."

"Huh?!"

Duke Rose's eyes widened. He never expected Merlin to be so confident about defeating the third knight?!

Although Duke Rose believed Merlin was a powerful figure, believing he could defeat a Thorn Knight was a bit of a fairy tale.

Duke Rose didn't think Merlin's strength could reach Dexter's level. There was still a gap between the two.

"Forget it, Sir Merlin. That man is the famously renowned Third Knight. By sheer martial prowess alone, he can intimidate an entire region."

"That's right, Sir Merlin, you shouldn't forcefully clash with him. The man is the empire's foremost warrior, notorious for his ferocity. Even our First Knight, Sister Windsor, would never lightly choose to directly confront an enemy like Dexter."

"Oh?" Merlin looked at the massive figure opposite with an expressionless face. "Is he really that formidable?"

"Yes, Sir Merlin, you're merely a hired hand. Given the circumstances, just leave. There's no need to recklessly throw away your life." Duke Rose's expression suddenly grew composed, as though in his final moments of flight he had already accepted his fate of failure.

Merlin glanced at Duke Rose, then at the burly Dexter across from him, and silently thought —

*He hadn't wanted to clash with a Thorn Knight in the first place, worried it would bring trouble.*

*But now it seems...*

*I have to step in and teach this big guy a lesson. Otherwise, Alice and I won't get paid and will end up eating dirt.*

title: Chapter 31 — Bonus Chapter: Monthly Ticket
content:
Chapter 31 — Bonus Chapter: Monthly Ticket

Volume 11 · Chapter 31

The Dexter on the other side had actually heard what Merlin said, assuming it was some powerhouse who didn't even fear himself.

But then he saw the Adventurer Guild certification on the guy's neck, with a utterly worthless "Villager" stamped on it, and he immediately lost interest in talking.

"Did I hear that right? A Black Iron adventurer is daring to threaten that he'll take me out?!"

"Am I not strong enough to wield my axe anymore, or is this guy completely full of himself?"

"Boasting this huge without a care for his own tongue getting caught!"

Dexter had been fairly angry at first, feeling insulted, but as he kept fuming, he ended up laughing at himself.

Mainly because a Black Iron villager claiming to be able to defeat the Thorns Knight was just so unrealistic, like some kind of joke.

"Hahahaha! How entertaining, are all adventurers like this now? I don't mind teaching you how to face reality."

Merlin looked at the Dexter across from him and calmly said, "Not every adventurer, actually only I am this full of myself."

Dexter's smile instantly disappeared, his face turning dark, his eyes fierce like a demon beast, "Are you serious? Trash Black Iron villager."

"What if I am a villager? As long as I can knock you down, then I'm the baddest villager around." Merlin picked at his ear, and just this careless attitude was already getting under the other guy's skin.

"Lord Merlin..." Duke Rose widened his eyes. He had assumed throughout the journey that Merlin was a man of few words, but this guy spouted so much trash talk! And he was directly clashing with such a powerful Thorns Knight!?

"Lord Merlin, if you keep provoking him like this, w..." Michelle wanted to say something but stopped, feeling that Merlin was looking for death.

Although Michelle knew Merlin had some strength, comparing him to a Thorns Knight still seemed like a stretch.

Duke Rose and Merlin both thought Alice was the strongest between the two of them, after all, adventurer ranks were divided by combat power.

"What's there to be afraid of? A Thorns Knight is no big deal." Merlin said casually, thinking to himself that he had already hammered down several of them.

"You arrogant kid who doesn't know the height of the sky or the depth of the earth. After I kill this traitor Duke Rose, it'll be your turn!"

The moment he finished speaking, Dexter suddenly snatched up his blood-soaked battle axe and erupted from where he stood, swinging it wildly toward Duke Rose's head!

Both Duke Rose and Michelle turned pale. Since Dexter's attack was too sudden, the two couldn't even cry out in shock — they could only stand frozen like fools waiting for death!

Before the speed of a blink —

Just before Dexter's axe came down, Merlin suddenly flashed in front of Duke Rose, extending his hand and pressing one finger against the blade of the giant axe, successfully blocking the attack.

Cracks instantly spread across the earth centered on Merlin's feet, and a raging storm soared into the sky — you could see how terrifying the force of that axe strike was.

Merlin's glove had already been torn to shreds by the chaotic wind currents, but no matter how hard Dexter pushed, he couldn't budge that single index finger!

This situation shocked all three people present. They had all expected someone to die, but instead things took a dramatic turn.

Duke Rose, being closest, could see Merlin blocking the attack with one finger. His thoughts raced: This— this— this— What is going on!? The Empire's First Hero's attack was blocked by Merlin with a single finger! What kind of ironclad physique is this!? Only "terrifying" could describe it!

Michelle's small mouth formed an "O" shape, unable to close it, her heart churning for a long time. A single finger blocked the Third Knight's fierce assault!? Even Sister Windsor couldn't do that! Why does Lord Merlin possess such incredibly powerful strength? It was incomprehensible. Being a Black Iron adventurer was such a waste of talent!

Just with Merlin having this level of strength, the two couldn't even imagine what Alice was like — she must be on par with a Purple Gold adventurer!

"Why are you two just standing there? Get out of here. Leave this to me." Merlin spoke, breaking their shock.

Duke Rose came back to his senses, and said seriously to Merlin, "Then please be careful, Lord Merlin."

After saying that, Duke Rose quickly grabbed Michelle and retreated, rejoining the few surviving knights.

With Merlin's intervention, the success of this escape plan was now a guarantee.

"Hey, big guy, still want to fight? If you call it quits now, I suppose that would work too..." Merlin looked at the hulking figure in front of him wielding the giant axe.

At this point, Dexter was just regaining his composure and realized Michelle and Duke Rose had already fled.

His heart was deeply shaken. His full-power attack had been nullified by a single finger of Merlin!

Was he really a Black Iron adventurer!? Nobody would believe that! He was basically a tiger wearing a fake badge!

Such a sharp axe that couldn't even scratch the other guy's skin was truly inconceivable!

This was Dexter's first time encountering something like this. Nearly no one dared to directly confront him.

"You interfered and let imperial traitors slip away from my sight. Do you think I'll just call it quits?"

"If you want to fight, be my guest. I'll go along with you." Merlin smiled faintly.

"Even though you're a Black Iron adventurer, someone who can block my strike is certainly no ordinary person. I admit, you are a strong one." Dexter no longer dared to underestimate Merlin and had to take him seriously.

"And then?" Merlin frowned.

"And then I will never let you go. By covering Duke Rose's escape, you will be treated as an enemy!"

The Saint-tier pressure emanating from Dexter's body suddenly intensified, shooting upward sharply, and the pressure on his axe reached terrifying levels!

It seemed Dexter planned to suppress Merlin through raw strength, grappling to decide the victor — to defend his dignity as the Empire's Hero!

The ground beneath Merlin's feet couldn't withstand such immense pressure, starting to crack continuously with loud pops, spreading outward like spiderwebs.

"Aaaargh!" Dexter began roaring, the veins on his arms and face bulging, his skin turning red as if scalded by boiling water.

Golden Saint-tier fighting spirit raged around him, constantly increasing in power, yet Merlin's little finger never moved, impossible to budge even slightly!

Their size difference was enormous, making it look like Dexter was bullying a child.

But the reality was the opposite — Merlin was ruthlessly mocking the Empire's strongest warrior.

The ground shattered into countless fragments, sending fierce winds soaring into the sky. This was not a contest of the same level whatsoever!

Merlin calmly commented with one phrase, then swung a backfist at extreme speed, punching straight into Dexter's abdomen.

Dexter's armor instantly exploded into countless shards, as if struck by lightning!

"Cough!"

Dexter's eyeballs bulged, a bitter taste flooded his throat, and he spat out a mouthful of blood — clearly his internal organs had been injured by Merlin's blow.

His body flew uncontrollably backward, crashing to the ground and rolling repeatedly.

Dexter finally accepted reality — this unremarkable Black Iron villager in front of him possessed unimaginable strength!

"I think there's no need for us to fight to the death. I don't particularly want to have much to do with you Thorns Knights. At the end of the day, I'm also an adventurer. Taking money to do a job is only natural. That's all." Merlin rubbed his neck, seemingly showing signs of some old-age ailment flaring up.

Dexter slowly propped himself up using his giant axe, his face somewhat pale, blood coating his teeth and the corners of his mouth — clearly in severe condition.

Who exactly was this guy?

He had never heard of anyone among adventurers besides that group of Purple Gold monsters who were this powerful.

And yet he was a Black Iron adventurer. This wasn't normal. Why would he be content lingering at the very bottom?

Dexter managed to stand up. A堂堂 Third Knight beaten to this state by a Black Iron villager — if this got out, nobody would believe it.

"Taking money to do a job, how arrogant of you. You're the first person to push me this far — I almost respect you."

"Shall we just call it even then? I'm not particularly interested in killing you." Merlin shrugged.

"Call it even!? No way! If I let you go like this, then I'm not worthy of being called the Empire's First Hero!!!"

The golden fighting spirit around Dexter intensified once more, his skin burning like fire, every blood vessel seeming ready to burst.

In that moment, Dexter's silhouette resembled a God of War wielding a giant axe, burning through his own life force!

"It seems you have no intention of listening to reason?"

Merlin's eyes turned cold, his red pupils contracting as if passing sentence on his enemy's death.

To be honest, Merlin's patience was limited, and Dexter's persistent pestering had crossed the line.

Merlin wrinkled his brows, his expression darkening, his tone already becoming somewhat serious.

"I'm not afraid of your Thorns Knights; I simply despise the endless trouble that follows."

"Someone like you isn't even worth my proper attention—"

"But if you dare to harass me endlessly, even if gods stood before me, I'd knock them down just the same!"

Dexter launched himself skyward, completely ignoring Merlin's warnings, his heart filled with unwillingness to be defeated by a Black Iron villager.

Golden fighting spirit engulfed his entire body, and in the night sky, he resembled a radiant sun.

Paired with the enormous full moon overhead, the knight wielding a giant axe temporarily transformed into a Reaper of Death harvesting lives!

His massive pressure dispersed, causing the very ground to tremble slightly.

This was Dexter's ultimate technique, "Heaven-Shaking Earth-Shattering," sacrificing his own life force to unleash an overwhelmingly powerful martial art!

Concentrating all his magic power into a single point, he struck downward with everything he had. Even vast mountains could be cleaved into chasms.

Every time he used this move, Dexter would lie bedridden for half a year — a truly costly ultimate technique.

In his entire life, Dexter had only used it twice before. This third time was aimed at Merlin. As for his previous two opponents, they had already been reduced to meat paste.

The man known as the Empire's Strongest Hero was finally revealing his true edge, shaking heaven and earth.

Dexter descended from the sky, his giant axe cleaving down viciously, his target directly aimed at Merlin.

That moment was like a golden comet striking the earth, so震撼izing it made one's soul tremble!

A tremendous crash, the most colossal sound ever, rivaled the repeated peals of thunder.

The earth didn't just crack — it turned to powder, the ground undulating in layers, wave after wave.

The destructive force of the shockwave was even more ferocious. Centered on this spot, a quarter of the Royal Capital was reduced to ruins!

The ground shook violently and continuously. Everyone in the entire capital could feel the obvious tremors, as if the end of days had arrived.

The kicked-up dust resembled a mushroom cloud, soaring into the sky and obscuring the stars and full moon above.

Merlin's figure slowly walked out from within the dust cloud. The tanto at his waist had been drawn at some point —

The rusted, notched blade was stained with faint traces of crimson blood, dripping onto the ground one drop after another.

A long-lost sense of comfort spread through his chest, as if he had received a sacrifice and found joy.

Behind Merlin, Dexter stood motionless within the massive crater, his giant axe still in hand, a petrified expression of terror frozen on his face, his eyes hollow and lifeless.

Merlin paused, wiped the blood from his tanto, and slid it back into the red scabbard at his waist.

The giant axe in Dexter's hands promptly snapped into two pieces, a split tearing through his throat as blood gushed uncontrollably, and he collapsed to the ground, dead.

Merlin glanced back at Dexter's corpse, brushed some dust off his shoulder with his hand, and sighed —

"A guy lost in empty fame."

"How boring."

title: Chapter 32 — Draw the Sword
content:
Chapter 32 — Draw the Sword

Volume 11 · Chapter 32

Time rewound — the three on the other side were still locked in combat.

The towering wall was blasted to rubble, dust and smoke billowing everywhere.

Three figures charged out of the smoke, blades clashing in a frenzy of sparks!

Alice's thin sword flashed at high speed, a dense rain of steel pouring down in an instant!

Golden ice cones assisted, occasionally shooting at Emmanuel's vitals.

Magic and qi collided back and forth; Alice's varied moves caught Emmanuel off guard.

Maelin's golden qi surged, his sword seeking awkward angles, giving Emmanuel no small amount of trouble.

Although Emmanuel was stronger than both Alice and Maelin, fighting two against one still put him at a slight disadvantage.

"Tch! You two are so annoying!"

Emmanuel complained angrily, thinking he had to get serious or he'd be pressed the whole time.

Colored qi suddenly rose on Emmanuel, his wide sword sweeping down in a single slash!

Blades collided with a thunderous crash, Alice and Maelin forced back hard.

Emmanuel's eyes burned with anger, glaring at the two opposite him.

"Don't get too cocky, you two trash..."

Alice stepped back a few steps, barely stabilizing her stance. She could sense the gap in strength, and the opponent didn't seem serious — even if she suppressed him now, it was probably temporary.

Maelin was already sweating beside her, breathing noticeably heavier. That wave of combat had clearly drained him.

Emmanuel was overwhelmingly strong, with vast reserves of qi. Alice had the ice dragon's magic and qi backing her — she'd never tire easily.

Maelin was different from the other two; he was ordinary. If this continued, he'd only slow Alice down.

Alice felt the situation was bad. If they couldn't end this quickly, things would turn ugly — she'd be worn down by attrition, and the slight advantage they had would vanish.

Just as Alice prepared to coordinate a second assault with Maelin, a tremendous "boom" shattered the night's silence.

The ground shook violently, the entire imperial capital rippling, as if a massive earthquake had struck.

"What's going on?!" Alice cried out, steadying herself.

"Seems like something happened over there?" Maelin looked in one direction, face pale with fear.

Alice frowned, following Maelin's gaze — and saw a horrifying sight:

In the direction of the north gate, a towering column of sand and dust erupted into the sky, like a massive explosion had occurred.

Rolling smoke obscured the night sky; the moon and stars dimmed instantly.

Alice's brow furrowed, a vague unease rising in her heart —

Wasn't that the direction Duchess Rose had retreated toward? Had they encountered a powerful enemy?

Even here, the destructive pressure was palpable.

But with Merlin there, it should be fine, right?

Thinking of Merlin's usual strength, Alice felt somewhat reassured. Whoever had cornered Dexter must have been desperate to use such a devastating move in the royal capital.

"Uh..."

Emmanuel's eyes widened, staring at the apocalyptic scene in the distance, his heart trembling uncontrollably —

What the hell? What happened over there?

Could Dexter have used that move?

Who had pushed Dexter to this point?

Could it be that blonde man...

Emmanuel's pupils constricted. The three who fled — only that black iron adventurer seemed capable of fighting Dexter.

But Emmanuel thought it was all over. He knew Dexter, the empire's strongest warrior — no one could survive his Trumph. With that level of destructive power, that blonde man was probably already pulp.

Still, Emmanuel admitted the blonde was strong. Pushing Dexter to use his ultimate was no small feat; few could do that.

Emmanuel turned to Alice, a smug smile on his face, speaking with disdain.

"It looks like it's over. Your companion is dead as a doornail."

"Nonsense! Merlin-sama is probably a strong man — I genuinely respect him," Maelin shouted back.

"Merlin? That blonde guy? Don't be naive..." Emmanuel laughed, shaking his head seriously. "He's already dead. I've never seen anyone survive the Third Knight's ultimate. Do you really think some guy named Merlin could produce that kind of destruction? Ha!"

A cold sweat dripped from Maelin's forehead. He wavered, heart pounding — could Merlin really beat the Third Knight? He wasn't sure. If something went wrong, the Duke was a goner.

"That guy isn't dead. Don't judge someone's strength with your narrow eyes," Alice said calmly, not thinking Merlin was inferior to anyone — she'd seen him overcome impossible enemies many times.

"Is that so? Then you two might soon see your companion's corpse." Emmanuel laughed sinisterly.

"You'd better worry about yourself..." Alice raised her thin sword and called out, "Maelin-sama."

"I know. For now, forget the Duke — we have to deal with the immediate threat." Maelin took an attacking stance, apparently also realizing the importance of ending this quickly.

"Ha ha, you really think you can handle me? Too bad. I was just playing with you earlier, but now..." Emmanuel planted his wide sword forward, his gaze turning cold. "Since Dexter's side is done, I'll get serious too. Neither of you gets to leave — both die here!"

"Don't talk like you've already won. Who knows how this ends." Alice's holy-tier pressure surged, the cold air fiercer than before.

"Right. Though you're the Thorn Knight, I don't feel you're invincible!" Maelin's aura was equally fierce.

"Oh? Watch now — I'll show you an insurmountable gap in power..."

Emmanuel's qi slowly surged. His pupils contracted twice, then he slashed through the air!

Alice instinctively took a defensive stance, but only felt a breeze pass by — nothing happened!

"What? Intimidating us?"

"Maybe. I'm just clearing out some annoying mice first."

Emmanuel finished speaking — Alice suddenly felt warm liquid splatter onto her face.

She widened her eyes, numbly touched her cheek, and saw her hand covered in fresh, hot, crimson blood.

"Eh?!"

"What happened?!"

title: Chapter 33 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 33 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update

Volume 11 · Chapter 33

"...Ma Lun, my lord..."

Alice turned her head to the side and saw that Ma Lun had already collapsed in a pool of blood, his face still twisted with the expression of death.

It seemed even Ma Lun himself didn't know what happened—he was suddenly and completely killed for no apparent reason.

In the instant Emmanuel swung his sword, Ma Lun was defeated. It seemed he had finally gotten serious.

Alice's eyes trembled as she realized her comrade had been killed in an instant, leaving her alone to face Emmanuel.

What just happened?!

Emmanuel was twenty steps away from them.

Why—without any warning at all—was Mr. Ma Lun killed from such a distance?!

Could this man be attacking from range? He's clearly a swordsman, but this isn't normal...

Alice's heart was uncertain, unable to discern the other's technique, and instinct bred fear.

"Hahaha... Em... you think you're so great now, don't you? That pesky rat is finally done for. Now I can slowly torture this stinky woman to death! Hahaha..."

Alice slowly turned back, her eyes flashing with panic. Originally, with Ma Lun's assistance, she had been holding her own against Emmanuel. Now that Ma Lun was dead, she had no choice but to face him alone.

Honestly, Alice wasn't confident in herself. Though her strength had improved dramatically, compared to the Thorn Knight, there was an obvious gap. Winning easily was nearly impossible.

"I suppose you're terrified now, afraid of my strength. But there's nothing shameful about that—every enemy I face breaks into cold sweat. Most of them feel fear." Emmanuel paused, narrowed his eyes, and explained, "I'm the top-ranked Thorn Knight. Do you understand now? Your enemies can't even react before I cut them down—they don't even realize what happened. I'm a swordsman born solely to harvest lives. Twenty steps and a kill?"

Alice furrowed her brows and thought for a moment, "Drawing speed? Because it's fast, it's painful..."

"But you don't need to worry. Since my draw speed is so fast, when you die, you won't even have time to feel pain—you'll only see a brief afterimage."

As soon as Emmanuel finished speaking, he swung his wide blade horizontally through the air. The speed was so fast that Alice couldn't even see where he was aiming before her throat was targeted.

Alice's pupils contracted instantly, and she hastily raised her thin sword to block. A vague impression of an extremely high-speed sword slash—like a fierce beast blinking—attacked!

The massive impact sliced against her blade, producing a sharp scraping sound as sparks flew.

Her thin sword was bent backward by the high-speed slash, as if it might snap at any moment. This kind of invisible attack...

Alice's eyes widened in shock, breaking into a cold sweat. With the help of the sparks, she could barely make out the speed—it was incredibly fast. If she hadn't relied on her instincts to defend, she would have lost her head by now!

With Alice's current speed, she could hardly evade such attacks, like a lamb waiting to be slaughtered. She was slammed hard against the wall behind her.

With a loud crash, Alice couldn't withstand the high-speed slash and was sent flying uncontrollably.

"Cough!"

Alice let out a pained cry, feeling her qi and blood churning violently—she had clearly been struck with internal injuries. The blade's edge, in a cold voice, said, "Next time..."

"Oh? You actually managed to endure it. Not bad... but..." Emmanuel touched his face, his luck still holding out. The high-speed slash seemed to resemble Merlin's...

Alice finally understood what Emmanuel's sword technique was about. It was somewhat similar to rapid blade release, but compared to that, the power was vastly different—uncomparable.

"Sorry, but I've never lost when it comes to luck!" Using a strategy of rapid assault.

Alice's golden magical energy and fighting spirit surged up, quickly closing the distance to Emmanuel, preparing to engage him.

"Hah, still want to fight me in close combat? How naive..."

Emmanuel casually swung one slash, and a high-speed sword slash was launched instantly!

Alice waved her hand, and a golden ice wall appeared out of nowhere, trying to block the attack.

However, the hard ice wall was no match for the high-speed slash—it was cleanly severed in two. She tried to strike from the side, thrusting her thin sword out.

Where the sword tip passed, a trail of golden ice crystals flowed out, making her attack extremely sharp.

"Interesting, but getting close to me is your biggest mistake!" Emmanuel's eyes focused, shaking his wide blade. The high-speed sword slash exploded in place!

In an instant, the air currents turned into countless sharp blades, tearing everything around Emmanuel apart. Alice was left with wounds all over her body, blood spurting everywhere.

The sword slashes struck Alice, slicing through her fragile body with a "whoosh, whoosh, whoosh." In the blink of an eye...

"Aaaaaaah!"

SF light novel-style wolf biting into her body.

A piercing pain spread through her, and Alice couldn't help but let out a desperate scream, as if being torn apart by countless wolves.

Alice retreated helplessly and fell to the ground, looking quite disheveled. She had been seriously injured from the start.

Her clothes were already stained with red blood, like a blood rose scattered across a silver frost.

Wherever the sword slashes passed, they would tear through skin and flesh, impossible to withstand. After the attack, her body was completely destroyed.

Alice's clothes were tattered and she couldn't stop bleeding, feeling utterly drained. It seemed she was caught in the current...

788.

3

But fortunately, she had the dragon race's innate talent—powerful self-healing ability that could repair the damage she received. It wasn't very obvious.

However, Alice hadn't fully digested all the inheritance crystals. Her incomplete dragon race talent meant her self-healing wasn't as effective. It seemed the opponent wasn't giving her any chance.

Alice's eyes began to glow with a faint golden hue. She was about to unleash the dragon race's power to heal her body. A fiery smile spread across her face as she narrowed her eyes with a sinister expression.

"Do you understand the gap between us now? At least you died understanding." Emmanuel said, "Farewell, foolish female adventurer!" With that, he moved to strike.

Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh—three high-speed sword slashes attacked without mercy, taking advantage of Alice's heavily wounded state and the swirling sand.

Boom, the high-speed sword slashes exploded in place, generating an incredibly sharp wind that whipped up a thick cloud of sand.

No matter who was inside, they would have been torn into pieces by the sword slashes forming the current. Only a few strands of life would remain...

"Hmph, this is the consequence of overestimating yourself. Even a small fox has been reduced to pieces."

Emmanuel sneered, turned around, and walked away without even looking back. In his eyes, Alice...

But Emmanuel hadn't taken more than a few steps before he stopped moving, as if pulled by something.

He turned around and saw his heel had been frozen in place by golden ice.

"Huh?"

Emmanuel couldn't help but wonder, looking toward where Alice was.

The sandstorm gradually settled, and Alice, holding her thin sword, stepped out of the dust.

Her eyes had turned a brilliant golden, with sharp pupils—like a dragon's eyes.

Blue and white crystalline scales had grown across her body, even spreading to her face, like a jewel.

Even the severe injuries she had just sustained were visibly healing at an incredible rate, restoring her to perfection. This was truly alarming.

It was clearly an immature "Dragon Transformation"—though only at 25%, the change in appearance was already so dramatic.

"Overestimating myself? Are you talking about me?" Alice's voice carried a slight tremor.

"...Emmanuel's eyes widened as he stared at Alice's current form, his heart filled with disbelief.

What is this posture?

Is this female adventurer not human?

title: Chapter 34 — Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 34 — Bonus Chapter

Volume 11 · Chapter 34

Alice's body already bore dragon scales, along with several very obvious draconic features—

Translucent crystal-clear scales, gleaming golden eyes, and that rampant draconic pressure...

Right now, Alice had only digested 25% of the inherited crystal, which was only enough to make dragon scales grow on her body.

But this 「Dragon Transformation」form had limited duration; she couldn't sustain it for long.

So Alice had to move faster—finish off her enemy within the 「Dragon Transformation」time window.

Otherwise, not only would she overextend her power, she'd also lose whatever slim advantage she had left.

The changes brought by 「Dragon Transformation」were quite significant. Alice's various abilities all multiplied, and the myriad draconic talents were strengthened. She felt brimming with power throughout her body.

Unlike before when she couldn't control it, now that she'd become a Saint-tier expert, Alice could to some extent control the power of 「Dragon Transformation」. She wouldn't lose her reason and hack wildly like before—instead, she'd turned this ability into an unstoppable weapon!

Alice felt that right now she could face Emmanuel head-on without fearing him.

She felt her defensive ability after dragon transformation was already sufficient to handle that troublesome ultra-high-speed sword aura.

Just now, when those three vicious sword auras came at her, Alice instantly completed her dragon transformation.

The result was that those three sword auras didn't pierce through her dragon scales—they sparkled with sparks and dissipated.

When Alice realized this, she immediately felt her chance to counterattack had arrived. She could use the dragon transformation state to crush this Thorn Knight in one move.

Actually, Emmanuel was already strong enough, but Alice inherited the power of the Frost Holy Dragon.

Compared to the Frost Holy Dragon, Emmanuel seemed far too insignificant. To break through a Holy Dragon's scale armor defense, there was probably no chance at all.

But Alice's dragon transformation wasn't complete yet. Her scale defense couldn't compare to a true Frost Holy Dragon, but it was more than enough against Emmanuel.

Alice's golden pointed pupils stared at Emmanuel, her fierce draconic pressure released without restraint.

The coldness was even more ferocious than before, constantly eroding the surroundings, slowly turning the area into a freezing polar region!

Alice silently tightened her grip on the slender sword in her hand; a layer of pale frost had already frozen onto it.

Emmanuel was pressed down by the ferocious draconic pressure to the point where he could barely breathe, feeling as though he were being intimidated by a superior species.

Although Emmanuel appeared extremely calm on the surface, his heart was uncontrollably trembling inside—

Is this female adventurer really human?!

What kind of joke is this! How could a human possibly have draconic features!

Could this person be a giant dragon rumored to be able to transform into a human?!?

Impossible! If she really were a dragon transformed into a human, her power would've already skyrocketed!

He'd heard that only the most top-tier Holy Dragons among dragons could achieve that, and this woman's power显然 fell short...

Emmanuel was deeply puzzled inside, sensing that he was about to face a grueling battle ahead.

"...Are you really human?"

"I'm obviously human," Alice replied indifferently.

"Don't joke around. Growing dragon scales and possessing draconic pressure—surely you're not some half-breed?" Emmanuel narrowed his eyes, trying to clear up the doubts in his heart.

A flash of irritation crossed Alice's golden pupils; she felt Emmanuel was insulting her.

"If you really are human, then what about these obvious draconic features?"

Emmanuel had no idea what an inherited crystal was, of course—after all, such things were extremely rare and only recorded in ancient texts from long ago.

"I have no need to tell you!

Given that the 「Dragon Transformation」time was limited, Alice didn't want to waste more words. She drew her sword and charged!

Saint-tier magic power and battle energy surged wildly as she attacked with full force from the start.

"Tch!" Emmanuel felt deep pressure and swung his wide-bladed sword, unleashing three ultra-high-speed sword auras!

Alice's figure instantly became ghostly, dodging two of them while the third slammed into the scales on her body and bounced right off!

At this point, Alice's abilities had improved dramatically—not only could she dodge sword auras, she could also tank them head-on. The extent of her power growth was evident.

Uh... Emmanuel hadn't expected his attacks to be useless. After growing dragon scales, how much stronger had this female adventurer become?!

Alice closed the distance to Emmanuel in an instant. Golden ice crystals surfaced on her blade, and she struck down with a thunderous slash!

Emmanuel raised his sword to block, but was forced back step by step, clearly struggling to hold his ground?!

Damn it! Her strength is this formidable too! I can't even resist head-on?!

Emmanuel managed to steady his stance, but Alice pressed forward relentlessly without pause.

That slender sword, shimmering with silver light, unfurled a dense barrage of sharp sword techniques like a cascading waterfall!

Alice's expression remained blank; under the moonlight, she resembled a valkyrie, showing zero mercy toward her enemy!

"Darn it!

Emmanuel hadn't anticipated Alice's abilities strengthening to this degree. The situation completely reversed, leaving him caught off guard!

His eyes widened in panic as he continuously retreated, but he was still pierced by Alice's slender sword in his right arm—the one holding his weapon.

Immediately afterward, using the wound as a medium, Emmanuel's entire right arm was frozen solid by golden ice, completely disabled!

Emmanuel fell to the ground and quickly half-squatted, looking at his numb arm and sharply inhaling through his teeth.

"Damn woman! How dare you treat me like this?! I'll never forgive you!

"From the moment you tried to kill me, there's no room for reconciliation between us." Alice held her slender sword and steadily approached Emmanuel step by step.

Emmanuel was so furious he nearly ground his teeth to dust,凶光 flashing in his eyes. He planned to fight this female adventurer to the death—whoever felt fear first would become a cold corpse!

But just then, an uninvited guest suddenly appeared, interrupting the slaughter—

"Emmanuel, look at your wretched state. Truly embarrassing."

Both Alice and Emmanuel paused, turning their gaze in the other direction.

A strange figure with a hood, a hunched frame, and a crystal ball floating above his hand slowly walked forward.....

He wore exquisite armor and a red magnolia war robe—wasn't this the ugly Tenth Thorn Knight, Hamilton?!

After searching the temporary duke's mansion, per the queen's orders Hamilton headed toward the north gate, but on the way sensed two colliding pressures, so he came directly here. Now he saw Emmanuel being driven back by Alice, shaking his head privately and thinking this reckless man was truly useless.

Alice furrowed her delicate brows, feeling that this Hamilton was very strange. His pressure was almost nonexistent and illusory; unless carefully investigated, he felt just like an ordinary hunched old man and was easy to overlook.

Hamilton bowed his hunched frame, slowly approaching here. In a raspy voice he slowly spoke—

"A sixth-rank Thorn Knight like you actually getting beaten by a female adventurer?"

"This severely damages the dignity of our Thorn Knights. You'd best retreat quickly."

"Leave this woman radiating draconic pressure to me. Heh heh heh..."

title: Chapter 35 — Giant Demon
content:
Chapter 35 — Giant Demon

Volume 11 · Chapter 35

Hamil smirked, clearly eager for a match with Alice, his interest piqued.

Alice’s forehead beaded with cold sweat as she silently retreated two steps, widening the distance between herself and the two Thorn Knights.

Hamil raised the crystal ball in his hand, his gaze locking onto Alice as strands of Saint-tier magic energy began to seep out.

“Then… let’s begin,” he said. “Proving you could push Immanuel to this point shows your strength isn’t weak. But in my presence, you won’t last ten seconds before your heart stops, turning you into a cold corpse.”

Alice’s expression darkened, the pressure from the two Thorn Knights doubling. Facing Immanuel alone had already required a life-or-death gamble—now Hamil had joined the fray. If they combined their strength against her, defeat was inevitable.

“To have dragon bloodline talent… you truly are a mysterious woman,” Hamil mused. “I’ll turn you into a living corpse, my puppet.”

“Stop!”

At Immanuel’s sharp command, Hamil froze mid-step, his confusion evident as he stared at him. What was he thinking, halting him in a two-on-one scenario where victory was guaranteed?

“What’s wrong? You can’t handle the enemy, so let me deal with it—what’s the problem?”

“There’s a *big* problem,” Immanuel said coolly, struggling to his feet. “My enemy is my prey. This woman must die by my hand alone. If you interfere, I won’t hold back.”

“What are you talking about? Now isn’t the time for stubbornness!” Hamil snapped, frustrated. “You’re already in this state—why insist on handling her yourself? That’s the dumbest move!”

“You think I’m defeated?” Immanuel shot back, his icy gaze fixed on Hamil. His right arm was completely frozen in golden ice, rendered useless.

Hamil’s expression flickered with unease. He knew Immanuel’s temper—when pushed, he’d slaughter allies without hesitation.

“Hmph. I haven’t lost yet,” Immanuel said coldly.

Hamil’s forehead broke into a cold sweat. Though he kept his mouth shut, his thoughts seethed: *Damn Immanuel. That arrogant bastard would be better off dead.* (or 牡J现)

Immanuel stepped forward, his demeanor far more composed. He clearly intended to fight Alice to the death in her dragon form.

“Woman, you *are* strong—I’ll grant you that,” he said. “But now, I must fight seriously.”

“I am,” Alice replied coldly, sensing her dragon transformation nearing its limit. She might only have one chance to decide the battle.

Immanuel scoffed, switching his broadsword from his ruined right hand to his left. The seemingly meaningless gesture was actually a signal—his full power would only unleash when wielding his left hand.

As a left-handed fighter, using his right hand had only allowed him to tap into half his strength. Now, with the blade in his dominant hand, his true might surged forward.

Alice frowned, sensing the shift in Immanuel’s aura. His entire body radiated killing intent, veins bulging on his left arm as he unleashed long-repressed power.

Hamil’s eyes widened in shock. *Immanuel… finally switching to his left hand?* He must be taking this seriously. His left-hand swordplay was ten times faster than his right, and his attack power had doubled—even Mesfield, the First Knight, would be sliced to pieces if he slipped up. The outcome was clear: this female adventurer was doomed.

“I’ll strike with my left hand at supersonic speed,” Immanuel declared, holding the broadsword across his chest. “Watch your back.”

Alice’s brows knit as she retreated half a step, adopting a defensive stance. Her slender blade pointed at Immanuel.

She recalled the Saint-tier spell her teacher had taught her—one with blinding speed, called *Frost Lance*.

If she could unleash it at full power, combined with the golden ice she’d absorbed, she might have a chance.

Magic and martial energy intertwined across her body, converging at the blade’s tip. A spiral of frost began to form.

Immanuel’s sharp Saint-tier martial energy erupted in full force. His gaze locked on, and a supersonic sword slash tore through the air.

The invisible blade formed a dense net, halting even the wind as it sliced through everything in its path.

The devastating attack bore down on Alice. A normal person would’ve been torn apart by the supersonic blade.

But Alice didn’t flinch. *“Frost Lance!”* she roared, and the gathered cold energy exploded.

“Hah!”

Alice’s blade erupted in golden frost, resembling a knight’s lance, and shot forward at an impossible speed.

The Frost Lance pierced Immanuel’s armor, plunging deep into his vulnerable chest.

“Gah!” Immanuel spat a mouthful of black blood, his expression a mix of shock and disbelief as the golden ice lance embedded in his torso.

Alice didn’t hesitate. She poured every ounce of magic and martial energy into the attack, pushing with all her might.

“AAAAAAH!”

The Frost Lance, as if alive, began to grow wildly, shoving the wounded Immanuel backward.

The golden lance carried him across the capital’s streets at blinding speed, like a falling meteor.

Finally, Alice’s Frost Lance impaled Immanuel onto the city wall 6,000 feet away—where he died instantly.

Alice pulled her blade free, gasping for breath. The strain was evident.

*Thud thud thud!* Her body suddenly split into dozens of jagged wounds, blood spraying like red roses in midair.

Her dragon scales shattered, leaving her tattered and broken, scattered across the ground.

Alice collapsed to her knees, blood pouring from her wounds. She propped herself up with her blade, barely conscious.

Every nerve screamed in agony, every cell torn apart. Even in unbearable pain, she forced herself to endure.

Moments ago, she’d had no choice but to brace against Immanuel’s supersonic blade net. Without her dragon scales, she’d likely be dead now.

Alice’s golden pupils returned to normal, her scales fading away.

In her critically wounded state, she couldn’t maintain her dragon form—her self-healing couldn’t even stabilize her.

She felt like a broken doll, her magic and martial energy stagnant as dead water.

Hamil watched the Frost Lance pierce the capital, his expression grim. *This woman is strong… she actually killed Immanuel.*

Though she was now severely injured, she couldn’t be underestimated. He’d have to eliminate her quickly.

Hamil’s gaze shifted to Alice, kneeling on the ground. His voice was chilling.

“Brilliant. *Too* brilliant.”

He clapped slowly, his eyes burning with fanatical admiration. He’d assumed Alice would die to Immanuel—but instead, she’d turned the tables.

Hamil realized he’d underestimated her. A fighter of this caliber demanded his full attention.

“You’re stronger than Immanuel,” he said. “I’ve revised my opinion of you.”

“If I could, I wouldn’t want to fight you…”

“But you’re on the side of the Rose Duke, making you no different from a traitor disrupting the empire.”

Alice coughed, blood flecking her lips. Her internal injuries were severe, her vision blurring.

Immanuel’s attack had been too brutal—her 25% dragon bloodline talent couldn’t heal her quickly enough.

She was paralyzed with pain, her body numb, her strength nonexistent. She was nothing but meat on a slab.

“So… before you die, do you have any last words?” Hamil asked, probing.

“…Cough…”

Alice struggled to speak, her wild, untamed gaze answering for her.

Hamil smirked, then sobered. “To honor your strength, I’ll show you my ultimate technique.”

“Inside my crystal ball lies the truth.”

“Open your eyes. Witness the legendary tyrant of the Goddess Era, who once ruled the seas!”

Hamil smashed the crystal ball to the ground. A vast mist erupted, spreading across the capital.

He laughed wildly, his bloodshot eyes rolling as he spread his arms. “Awaken! The deep-sea tyrant, the nightmare of all mankind!”

The mist dissipated, revealing the ground turning to mud, water surging up until it became an endless ocean.

The moon turned blood-red, the stars twisted into something unnatural, the sky darkening.

Alice realized she was now on a tiny island adrift in a vast, black sea.

A monstrous roar echoed from the depths, as if some colossal creature moved beneath the waves.

Suddenly, a pupil the size of 500 feet split the water, its crimson hue and serpentine iris resembling an ancient horror.

Alice, at its center, felt like an ant. A single eye that large—what monstrous form must it belong to?

A malevolent aura spread, as if she’d been transported to another world.

*Boom boom boom!* Four massive tentacles burst from the sea, rising into the sky. Each was thicker than the palace’s towers, stretching upward as if to drag the moon itself to the ground. This was a godslayer-level monster.

A normal person would’ve died on the spot, their will to fight shattered by the sheer terror of those tentacles. No one could fathom the true size of this beast.

Alice’s face paled as she stared, sinking into despair.

Her body stiffened, an icy chill seeping into her bones, her soul fading.

Her lips trembled as she thought—

…This is…

The legendary North Sea Leviathan.
