title: Chapter 53 — Epilogue
content:
Chapter 53 — Epilogue

Volume 11 · Chapter 53

Two Thorn Knights were fighting for their lives right under the watchful eyes of the Lake Sprite. The further they battled, the more noise they made.

The sky-covering vines of the Giant Wood Guardian swept toward them, an overwhelming presence that struck fear into anyone who looked upon it.

Merlin's expression remained resolute and unyielding as he glared at Katherine, who stood across from him with a smile on her face.

The countless vines mercilessly engulfed him without leaving even the slimmest gap. Dodging? Simply impossible.

"Merlin, I once considered you a friend. But since you betrayed Her Majesty the Queen, I will now spare no mercy in cutting you down."

From within the rolling mass of vines, a violent Saint-tier pressure suddenly surged upward. Golden battle aura seemed about to break through the siege!

Sheathed in golden light, the intimidating vines were instantly reduced to碎屑 before being sliced to pieces, as if distorted by powerful force.

Broken vines fell in all directions, revealing Merlin at the lowest level—

He held two swords in his hands: one was his original straight-bladed sword, while the other was a golden light sword radiating fierce battle aura!

This golden light sword was extremely bizarre, carrying an enormously strong pressure of its own as the shining aura slowly evaporated.

"Converting aura into sword?! "Katherine's brows furrowed immediately. She sensed that Merlin had started taking things seriously and was even using his signature technique.

The aura-to-sword technique was Merlin's family inheritance, traditionally passed only from father to son under extremely strict conditions.

However, there were no males in Merlin's generation—only Windsor, so they made an exception and passed it down to her.

Because the Merlin family had served the royal house in low-key fashion for generations, very few people knew about the aura-to-sword technique. It was undoubtedly an extremely difficult skill and exceptionally powerful in critical moments.

Condensing one's battle aura to such a high degree that it forms a solid entity requires the user to have extremely precise control over their aura; otherwise the air sword would easily dissipate.

A sword condensed from battle aura reaches an inexplicable level of attack power, making it virtually an undefendable technique.

It can ignore any defense and strike directly at the enemy's physical body while disrupting their magic and battle aura to achieve a sealing effect.

Because the sword itself is composed of battle aura, it can penetrate various types of defensive armor without leaving any trace.

For example, when someone raises a shield to block the battle aura sword, they would be penetrated and injured, yet the shield itself shows no damage whatsoever—a truly unstoppable move.

Merlin's expression turned serious. Gripping both swords, his battle aura surged violently upward like an invincible mighty knight.

"You want to cut me down? Don't speak so lightly about it, Katherine!"

"Alright then." Katherine raised her hand—which had various colors painted on it—looking mysterious. "Then I'll show you a bit of my true strength."

Both parties glared at each other. Their killing intent clashed like dragons and tigers locking horns. For the time being, neither could gain the upper hand.

But just then, someone else entered the fray, interrupting their battle—

"Sorry, I have something urgent to attend to. Could you two mind moving a bit farther away? I'd rather not accidentally injure anyone."

This person was completely naked below, wearing only a small red Spartan-style apron, with something unspeakable on his head.

That's right—a pair of white pantyhose, pulled completely over his head, with both legs flapping in the wind like flags.

Other than Merlin, who else would it be? Though the two Thorn Knights opposite probably couldn't hold back anymore.

Merlin was planning to make a move. He didn't hesitate to kick Merlin and Katherine out of the way so he could claim his own space to fight.

Katherine glanced at Merlin. This guy was nothing but a lunatic with pantyhose on his head—so glaring it was painful to look at. "Where did this pervert come from?! How did you even get in here?!"

"..." A large drop of sweat rolled down Merlin's forehead. He thought awkwardly, so I really am misunderstood as a pervert after all? Fortunately she can't see my face, or else my lifetime reputation would be on the verge of ruin. By the way, seeing the world through thin pantyhose has its own peculiar charm~

"Get out! The palace grounds are no place for someone like a pervert to casually enter!" Katherine's words were cutting. For someone who came charging in wearing stockings on his head, his first impression was terrible.

"Hah, so what if it's the palace grounds? This lord of mine has been to even more dangerous places." Merlin's tone remained calm, treating Katherine's intimidation like wind past his ears.

"I think you're looking for death...." The Giant Wood Guardian behind Katherine rustled, shifting its focus slightly toward Merlin.

Katherine didn't take Merlin seriously at all. She couldn't sense any pressure from him—he was probably just an ordinary villager who had sneaked in.

But Windsor was somewhat more sensitive. She kept scrutinizing the man wearing white pantyhose on his head.

Feeling a certain familiarity—especially the cheap street-market-style katana at his waist that looked ridiculously common.

Windsor couldn't help but recall the bastard who always spit water everywhere, so she cautiously put a question.

"You... the Great Swordmaster of Elgin?"

"Huh!? " Merlin stumbled backward in fright. Shocked, he thought, What the hell! I've already humiliated myself by wearing pantyhose on my head, how can this little brat still recognize me at a glance!

It must be because of my unique charm, right?

"You can't be serious... You're really the Great Swordmaster of Elgin!" Windsor gripped both swords tightly. Her hatred instantly shifted toward Merlin. It showed just how much she despised the Great Swordmaster of Elgin!

"The Great Swordmaster of Elgin!?" Katherine was momentarily stunned. Her hatred also shifted. "Why does a wanted criminal like you dare to openly appear in the palace grounds?! Are you deliberately provoking us?!"

Before Merlin could say anything, the Lake Sprite hovering above the palace in the distance suddenly stuck out its tongue and let out a loud roar.

"Hisss!"

The Lake Sprite seemed to sense a threat. Having recognized Merlin as the man who had attacked her earlier, she immediately became alert.

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue in dissatisfaction, looking at the two Thorn Knights before him. "Since you won't step aside, don't blame me if your arms and legs get broken."

"Hmph! Such big talk! I'd like to see what tricks you've got!" Katherine's battle fervor ran thick. She knew the Great Swordmaster of Elgin had defeated several strong opponents in a row, but relying on her barrier magic, she wasn't without fighting ability either.

Windsor raised her guard to full attention, sharply staring at the Great Swordmaster wearing pantyhose on his head, especially wary of him spitting saliva—she was almost used to it by now.

Merlin had no interest in these two female knights. His target was the Lake Sprite taunting him in the distance. He intended to beat it until it could no longer regenerate.

He lowered his body, pressing the great sword downward, gripping the hilt tightly, and took a deep breath—

Dark clouds carried rolling thunder. Wind掠过 his ears fell into stillness. Only the drumbeat of his heartbeat pulsed forward.

◆◆◆

"Slash!"

Merlin's eyes snapped open wide. The ancient blade left its scabbard with a crisp metallic ring that echoed around them!

The Iaijutsu burst forth at full power—in an instant, wind and clouds changed color, heaven and earth were annihilated.....

title: Chapter 54 — Monthly Ticket Update
content:
Chapter 54 — Monthly Ticket Update

Volume 11 · Chapter 54

The wind rose and clouds surged, the earth trembled and mountains shook.

Merlin unleashed his power fully, his sword flashing from the scabbard with a devastating force that commanded heaven and earth.

The blade and scabbard ground against each other violently, that metallic screech as sharp as thunder rolling across the sky!

Merlin paid no mind to the two ants before him; his target was the screaming lake spirit.

This was simple, brute-force power clashing against power. Who was stronger? Only time would tell!

Though Merlin's appearance was somewhat unseemly at the moment — his bare body wrapped in an apron, a pair of white silk stockings perched atop his head like a hat while the two legs flapped wildly in the wind — that arrogant aura ruling over all remained completely undiminished. The Great Demon Lord's majesty raged forth, truly worthy of the title among the Seven Kings of the Demon Realm!

Those who refused to heed his warnings and deliberately blocked the steps of an arrogant sovereign would surely be reduced to dust, adding another triumph to the record of the ever-victorious king!

Merlin wanted to see whether his full-power sword draw could annihilate heaven and earth, or whether the lake spirit's immortality could turn decay into wonder.

His hand rose and his blade fell — even as it came down, that seemingly ordinary body moved with the posture of a grandmaster, every detail reaching a exquisite level of mastery.

The rusted blade shredded through the air in that single instant, turning crimson, igniting a devouring fire.

A force that could tear apart the cosmos exploded outward with tremendous force, surging skyward like the collision of celestial bodies, sending tremors that would make even the gods fear.

The earth turned to powder in an instant, the shockwave destroying everything in its path as the ground itself rose and fell like ocean waves.

Crack! Lightning-like fissures split open the earth.

Rumble! Even the thunderbolt seemed to dodge the murderous edge of his attack.

The surging, desolate sword intent swept forward like a hurricane birthing a tsunami, transforming into the most cold and ruthless power and crushing everything in its path.

The two Thorn Knights before him were blasted away on the spot, utterly unable to withstand that overwhelming force, forced to seek shelter from the violent turbulence alone.

Even so, the shockwave's turbulent current was beyond what an ordinary person could endure — that tearing agony would drive one straight into unconsciousness.

Merlin's target had not been those two, however; they were only left critically injured. Otherwise, both female knights would have died instantly.

"Aaaaaaaaaah!"

Katherine's scream was hoarse and desperate, her body nearly shattered by the force of Merlin's attack — she felt as though she might break into pieces.

....What kind of unfathomable power is this?! It's too abnormal!

No pressure could be sensed from him at all, yet that single sword could unleash unmatched power!

Good heavens! Why does such a terrifying existence even exist? A man like this isn't just a threat to the empire — he's a threat to the world itself!

Elgin the Great Swordsman, as the rumors said, was indeed that strong. He couldn't be defeated by strength alone....

Katherine suffered endlessly in the turbulent currents, blood beginning to flow from all seven orifices, her delicate frame bearing grave wounds in multiple places.

Compared to Katherine, Mesfield could barely hold her ground, but she too was seriously injured from the constant shockwaves.

After all, Mesfield was a warrior, and a warrior's physical resilience far surpassed that of a magician.

Darn it! Is this truly Elgin the Great Swordsman's real power?!

What a terrifying man! Were all the feats he'd shown before just him messing around?

Mesfield bit down hard on her silver teeth, her consciousness already on the verge of scattering — she was in grave danger.

The two Thorn Knights were blasted apart by the shockwave, sent flying somewhere unknown.

That devastating, desolate sword intent ran rampant along its path, slaughtering all living forces in its way.

The earth churned and the sky shook, the entire royal capital trembling as though on the brink of destruction!

Above the palace, the lake spirit's expression turned to terror. Just as she attempted to escape, she was instantly overwhelmed!

The lake spirit let out a shrill, heart-rending scream — a sound like a baby's cry, piercing and awful.

The sword intent completely shredded the enormous water demon, obliterating it until not even a scrap remained.

Her magical energy dissipated, and even if she wanted to resurrect, there was no opportunity left.

Because the underground river that supplied her power had also been severed by Merlin, leaving the lake spirit in an inescapable trap!

When the matchless sword-qi storm passed, only the pockmarked royal palace remained.

The dark clouds above split open with a colossal gash, as though forcefully cleaved by an axe, revealing a clear azure sky beneath.

Merlin's strike had carved a long, narrow rift valley into the ground, permanently altering the terrain of the entire capital region.

The fissure almost severed the earth entirely, like a scar carved across the land, running straight through the capital's walls.

The queen's palace appeared to be no more — only broken walls and scattered ruins remained, radiating desolation.

Whether the lake spirit was dead was still unknown; the water demon slain earlier had not been her true body.

But with Merlin's strike, there was nowhere she could hide — it wouldn't matter where she tried to take refuge.

That royal guardian deity, even if immortal, would surely suffer immeasurable harm.

The wind stirred up swirls of dust as it swept past. With the lake spirit's suppression gone, the underground lake began to surge upward, and the capital would surely be swallowed soon enough.

Merlin rested his longsword on his shoulder and spoke in a thoroughly uninterested tone:

"What royal guardian deity? She was nothing special."

"My full-power sword draw used merely one ten-thousandth of my strength...."

Time passed.

When Mesfield finally awoke from her unconsciousness, the first face she saw was Elizabeth's.

She was lying with her head resting on Elizabeth's lap, cradled in the queen's arms.

Ever since Merlin had shown that ferocious expression toward Elizabeth, the queen had harbored deep distrust toward this mysterious adventurer.

When Merlin drew his blade and the heavens and earth shook, Elizabeth, hiding in the small wooden house, had felt profoundly uneasy — as though the end of days had arrived.

Elizabeth hadn't followed Merlin's warning; instead, she had escaped outside, only to stumble upon Mesfield being blasted through the air, her face pale as she lay motionless on the ground.

Elizabeth had been terribly frightened, unable to imagine who had beaten Mesfield into such a state. Clearly someone incredibly strong — even Mesfield's considerable power hadn't been enough to resist.

Panicked and helpless, Elizabeth had no choice but to drag Mesfield back to the small wooden house and care for her until she woke.

Among the twelve Thorn Knights, Elizabeth and Mesfield shared the deepest bond — as liege and retainer, they had been inseparable.

After all, Mesfield had become the queen's personal knight since childhood, and her feelings toward Elizabeth went far beyond mere loyalty.

When Mesfield saw Elizabeth before her, her eyes widened in sheer disbelief. She had never dreamed of seeing the queen in person, yet now she appeared right before her eyes! ?

"You're awake? That's wonderful — I thought you might never regain consciousness."

Elizabeth's sorrow turned to joy, her eyes glistening with tears as she cupped Mesfield's face in her hands.

Mesfield slowly came to her senses. The queen before her was the very architect of the empire's destruction, the sinner of the entire realm.

Mesfield quickly sat upright. Just as she opened her mouth to say something, sweetness flooded her throat — and she vomited a mouthful of blood right then and there.

It seemed the lingering force of Merlin's sword draw had dealt Mesfield considerable damage; her physical condition was dire.

"Are you alright?! Who did this to you?!" Elizabeth leaned in close.

"Get lost!" Mesfield shoved Elizabeth away harshly, grabbed the straight sword lying on the ground, and thrust it viciously toward the queen's throat — her eyes filled with hatred.

"You've pushed so many people into an abyss of suffering! You're no real Elizabeth!"

"I will avenge countless souls drowned in that flood! Die, you false queen!"

title: Chapter 55 — Unveiled
content:
Chapter 55 — Unveiled

Volume 11 · Chapter 55

Methfield wielded a straight sword and stabbed mercilessly at Elizabeth's throat.

She had already lost all hope for the queen, as she had repeatedly made wrong judgments for her own status.

Countless ordinary people had perished underwater, yet she refused to turn back, resorting to every despicable means.

If she hadn't still harbored some illusion about the queen, Methfield would have drawn her sword long ago!

Looking back on everything that had happened, Methfield couldn't imagine that this was the same Elizabeth she had known before.

After Michelle's visit, Methfield grew even more convinced in her suspicions: the queen before her was absolutely not Elizabeth!

So Methfield abandoned her knightly beliefs; even if misunderstood by everyone, she would put this tyrant to the sword.

The sharp blade cut through the air, and just as it was about to pierce Elizabeth's throat—

"Windsor."

Methfield abruptly halted her sword, staring blankly at Elizabeth.

Her expression was somewhat dazed, as though recalling something very long past.

Windsor—that was a form of address she hadn't heard the queen use for her in so long.

She had always been called Methfield, but the old queen used to affectionately call her by her given name in private.

This sudden call stirred something within Methfield, and she felt a tremor in her heart, thinking the queen was trying to play on emotions out of fear of death.

But the moment she thought of all the atrocities the queen had committed, Methfield couldn't bring herself to let her go. This wasn't the time for nostalgia.

"What is it? Are you feeling afraid too? Think about the people who died because of your reckless decisions—they were more afraid than you!"

Elizabeth understood what was happening. It must have been her sister impersonating her, driving Methfield to despair; otherwise, there was no way she could have turned to regicide.

"Windsor, calm down. I really am Elizabeth, the real Elizabeth!"

"Shut up! I know exactly who you are! You're Isabella! You wretched bastard who stopped at nothing to seize the throne!" Methfield ground her teeth. "So many people chose to believe you, and yet you callously kept deceiving them!"

Elizabeth was speechless. She couldn't imagine what Methfield had experienced to harbor such hatred for her own sister.

"The real Elizabeth has probably already fallen victim to your cruelty. You heartless woman, blinded by power—can't you even spare your own sister?" Methfield grew angrier with each word, her inner fire rekindling as she raised her sword. "Today, for the sake of upholding the royal lineage, I will send you to hell with my own hands!"

"Wait, Windsor! I really am Elizabeth! I didn't die—I escaped!" Elizabeth looked exasperated, then lowered her head and unclasped the sapphire pendant around her neck, handing it to Methfield. "This was a parting gift from Father, meant for both my sister and me. It's proof enough of my identity!"

Methfield searched Windsor's eyes, then suspiciously took the pendant, examining it carefully. She noticed Elizabeth's name engraved on the back.

She froze on the spot. According to the information Michelle had provided, the fake queen possessed a pendant engraved with Isabella's name. And this pendant bearing Elizabeth's name must belong to the real queen. In that case, the queen before her...

Methfield clenched the pendant, raised her head, and asked in a near-shaking tone, her expression stunned.

"...You're really Elizabeth?"

"Of course! I'm your big sister~" Elizabeth hugged her, wrapping her arms around Methfield's neck. "Long time no see, little Windsor, haha."

Methfield suddenly stiffened, hardly able to believe it. Everything felt too coincidental.

Gradually, she began to accept that this was truly Elizabeth. If it had been Isabella, she certainly wouldn't have been this close; there had always been an insurmountable master-servant gap between them.

For a moment, Methfield felt as though she had returned to the old days—she would have been willing to lay down her life for Elizabeth.

Tears welled up. Finding the real Elizabeth had to be the luckiest thing imaginable.

"Your Majesty, where did you go? Why—why were you replaced by someone calling themselves Elizabeth?"

The once-resilient Methfield suddenly appeared vulnerable before Elizabeth, softening in a way that made her seem almost girlish.

"Don't be sad. I've come back, and everything will be alright." Elizabeth patted Methfield's head, speaking in her sisterly tone. "As for where I went—it's a long story. My sister kept me imprisoned in a dungeon below the palace, and I couldn't make contact with the outside world the entire time."

"I see."

Methfield's emotions gradually steadied. Though she didn't know the full details, she could piece together a general picture.

Isabella must have resorted to despicable means behind the scenes to seize the throne.

This tale of switching the princess for a commoner left Methfield somewhat taken aback.

"How did you escape then? Surely Isabella wasn't suddenly filled with remorse?"

"Well..." Elizabeth hesitated, her face flushing slightly as she thought back to everything that had just happened—she found it hard to bring up.

"I was rescued by an adventurer."

"This person's character is a bit too... questionable."

"Questionable..." Methfield frowned, unsure what the queen had experienced.

Elizabeth hesitated as well. The things Merlin had done earlier were difficult for her to articulate.

She was a queen, after all—just sexually assaulted by an Iron-rank adventurer. However she framed it, it was humiliating.

And recalling Merlin's threats as he left, she felt immense pressure, a bitter silence weighing on her.

If she told Methfield that Merlin had stolen her stockings, Methfield probably wouldn't stay calm—she would definitely go after him. That would infuriate Merlin, and if he really tossed her stockings into an auction, the consequences would be unthinkable.

Just imagine: thousands of upper-class gentlemen vying to bid for her stockings. Where would the queen's dignity be then?!

After thinking it over, Elizabeth decided it was better not to mention it—it would only damage her image.

"Actually... he's not too bad. It's just that this adventurer... has a rather short temper."

"What!? How dare someone show disrespect toward Your Majesty! I will surely teach that ignorant adventurer a lesson!" Methfield's anger flared instantly, her grip tightening on her sword.

"Don't get so worked up. He did save me, after all. His attitude may have been poor, but I can't repay kindness with hostility," Elizabeth said nervously, trying to calm Methfield.

"Protecting Your Majesty's dignity is my duty." Methfield said stubbornly.

"...Elizabeth forced an awkward smile and changed the subject. "By the way, who did this to you? You're badly injured."

"...Methfield furrowed her brows, feeling nauseous just thinking about the man who had spat at her. "I was fighting Catherine, hoping to meet Isabella, when suddenly Earl Ginn emerged as a great swordsman. He drew his katana and destroyed the entire palace. I was severely wounded by the residual shockwave of that mighty sword energy."

"That Earl Ginn great swordsman again."

Elizabeth seemed to recognize the name, muttering to herself. "While I was imprisoned, I heard my sister complain about this mysterious man more than once. I wonder what kind of fellow he is."

"What kind? I used to be unclear, but now I know—he's just a pervert who wears stockings on his head and runs around naked!" Methfield ground her teeth, resentful to the core.

"Eh???" Elizabeth suddenly wore a confused expression, her brows drawing tight as she thought—

No way, this can't be a coincidence?

Stockings on his head.

Katana at his waist.

Running around naked.

Wait... I think I've discovered something!

title: Chapter 56 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 56 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 11 · Chapter 56

Although Elizabeth found it hard to believe that Merlin, with his perverted conduct, could make the strong ones donated by the empire turn the world upside down.

However, from the information spoken by Melfield, it seemed that besides Merlin, Elizabeth truly couldn't think of anyone else.

Moreover, the entire capital had fallen into chaos; Elizabeth couldn't imagine, besides Merlin's perverted self, who else would wear stockings and run around bare-assed in the streets.

However, Elizabeth wasn't quite sure. The swordsman threatening the entire empire was actually a perverted iron-class villager.

Always feeling that the two of them weren't in the same world, making it difficult to compare them, the difference was too great.

Elizabeth pondered for a moment, stepping forward to verify the information with Melfield.

"That Elgin swordsman... is he wearing white stockings, with a red apron tied around his waist, a nodachi like a street stall item attached to his waist, giving off a very LOW overall impression?"

"Eh?! " Melfield was genuinely stunned for a moment, not expecting Elizabeth to describe the perverted man's outfit so accurately, "Your Majesty, could it be that you've seen the Elgin swordsman? And you've had contact with such a dangerous person?"

........

Elizabeth instantly became nervous, her eyes darting around, a bit worried that Melfield would see through something.

She was very angry about Merlin's perverted behavior of wearing her stockings and running around outside.

But she didn't dare say much, fearing retaliation from this scoundrel Merlin.

She thought for a moment, deciding to gloss over it; if she admitted having contact with the Elgin swordsman, Melfield might suspect that the white stocking was hers.

Her own stockings had been stolen; what happened? It would definitely cause serious misunderstandings, right? !

Elizabeth's hesitant state of mind just happened to be what Merlin wanted. Thinking about why those girls who had their naked photos taken were under someone's control, it was quite understandable—afraid of losing face!

"I... I haven't had contact with the Elgin swordsman, I just saw a weird person from afar. Hearing you say that, it turns out that... that perverted fellow is actually the Elgin swordsman?"

Melfield didn't think much of it, feeling relieved in his heart. If the queen were to take a stance on the Elgin swordsman, who knows what unpleasant things might happen.

"Exactly, that naked perverted fellow is the Elgin swordsman, acting so flippantly, like a street ruffian!"

"Right, I see too." Elizabeth nodded, seeming to bear a grudge against Merlin as well.

"Previously I thought this guy was just a troublemaker who causes trouble everywhere, but now it turns out he's a licentious young master! Melfield's degree of dislike for the Elgin swordsman suddenly went up another level, "Not only is his mouth toxic, he also likes to put women's stockings on his head, how disgusting, and yet he can still be worshipped as a hero by so many people? I can't... ".

"Is... is indeed... Elizabeth felt immense pressure inside, that stocking is mine! Although it wasn't given voluntarily, being called disgusting, she always feels a bit responsible. SF4Z j i treatment

"I don't know if that stocking is genuine? I suspect the woman wearing that stocking isn't a good thing, but rather a slut who mingles with the Elgin swordsman, actually giving this pervert the stocking, it's simply lacking any shame!" Melfield felt internally aggrieved, thinking the woman who gave the stocking was unchecked.

".....

Elizabeth's face darkened, having bitter words she couldn't say. She was coerced, simply not a slut at all.

Being looked down upon by her favorite knight so much, it was hard to rebuke anything, she felt very desperate.

Elizabeth increasingly didn't want to reveal Merlin's identity; this Elgin swordsman was the adventurer who saved herself.

Seeing Elizabeth's ugly complexion, Melfield strangely asked, "Your Majesty, what's wrong? Are you not feeling well?"

"N-no... commoner's... I just feel that Windsor seems to hate the Elgin swordsman so much, it's no longer an objective attitude." Elizabeth felt as if she were tied to the same rope as Elgin swordsman, enduring insults together.

"This... Melfield hesitated, had to seriously say, "Although I feel the Elgin swordsman isn't purely a bad person, he likes to insult women, this is an undeniable fact.

"Insulting women?" Elizabeth felt a bit, just now Merlin's attitude was indeed very disrespectful.

"Exactly, he likes to spit women's saliva, inducing... inducing a special state, and he likes to run naked wearing women's intimate clothing.

Melfield said with a complex expression, thinking of the climax induced by being spat on, he really didn't want to say such a thing.

"However, this guy's strength is truly heaven-defying, I have to admit, this guy's power, I fear has the capital to go head-to-head with the empire.

Elizabeth fell silent; if not for Melfield suddenly mentioning it, she would never have discovered that Merlin was the Elgin swordsman.

It seems Merlin didn't speak from the beginning, although he is an iron-class level, defeating the thorny knights is certainly effortless.

However, this also brought up a new problem; different from what his sister said, Elizabeth feels Merlin doesn't have such deep hostility toward the empire.

And he also rescued herself from the prison cell, besides the awkwardness of stealing her stockings, he hasn't done anything too excessive.

Elizabeth feels she needs time to think carefully, although Isabella's hard set of obviously won't work.

"Your Majesty, what is your attitude toward the Elgin swordsman?" Melfield paused, seriously saying, "Although I don't want to admit it, with our strength, I fear it's very difficult to deal with that pervert.

Elizabeth could also understand Melfield's helplessness, after all, the royal cards, the lake fairies, had been defeated.

The entire empire's usable power, it seems, is also very difficult to defeat the Elgin swordsman.

And now the opponent is using stockings to threaten, making herself feel somewhat at a loss.

Now that the Elgin swordsman's identity is known, this is her only advantage.

So she temporarily doesn't plan to reveal the Elgin swordsman's true identity, but hides it down.

Elizabeth sighed, her mind was messy, she could only temporarily avoid this problem one by one.

"Windsor, don't worry."

"Under say

"After everything calms down, let me think carefully before deciding..."

The submerged imperial capital, even the palace couldn't escape.

With massive water wanting to retreat, it probably needs a long time.

At this moment, only some tall buildings are positioned on top of the sleep, such as the clock tower.

Merlin stood at the top of the clock tower, the water below had already spread to two-thirds of the position.

Surrounding was all a sea of water, looking like there was no way out, the non-swimmer Merlin was trapped here.

Merlin felt someone would come to rescue him, just be patient and wait.

The wind at the top of the tower was especially strong, roaring like a cow, making people almost unable to stand firm.....

Merlin put his hands on his waist, wrapped in a Spartan apron, the two legs of the white stockings dancing flutteringly.

Looking at the surging river water in front of him, he took a deep breath with relish, the stockings almost near his nose.

A faint trace of fragrance, as if the smell of perfume, stimulating Merlin's sense of smell one-

"Um~"

"The queen's fragrance."

"I fucking am indeed a connoisseur. To think I gave myself a cowardly blockhead"

title: Chapter 57 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 57 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 11 · Chapter 57

Merlin quickly bowed his head, pinching his nose shut, his brow furrowed in concentration as he thought to himself—

No, no, I should stay calm.

How could I get so addicted to the scent of a woman?

I'm the Great Demon Lord, I should be more mature and maintain my dignity.

If this keeps up, I'll eventually awaken an attribute that's too embarrassing to even look at.

Besides, this is my first time stealing a woman's stockings. It seems like those bandits wearing stockings must have been in an extremely excited state when they committed their crimes.

Hmm, I've learned something new again. I'm proud of myself...

Merlin calmed his mind, unaware that Alice would arrive at the battlefield in 30 seconds.

Alice had been waiting at the camp for a long time.

But he hadn't come back! !

Alice couldn't help but worry, fearing something had happened to Merlin.

Recalling Merlin's inability to swim, she worried he might have slipped and drowned in the water.

If such a lame death were to spread among the demon race, it would probably make demons laugh until they dropped their fangs.

Alice thought it wasn't impossible that Merlin had drowned, and she sat restlessly in the tent.

Although she always cursed Merlin as a bastard, at times like this, her concern was incredibly genuine.

Despite thinking Merlin had many flaws, she had grown somewhat accustomed to them. And deep down, there was a faint emotional bond pulling at her heart. Alice didn't want Merlin to leave her side.

So Alice left the camp alone, rowing a small boat to search for Merlin in the capital.

Her injuries hadn't fully healed yet, so she could only drag her exhausted body to find Merlin.

The lake water rippled gently, the small boat rocked lightly, and Alice's mood was like this boat—always restless and unable to settle.

Alice gripped the oars and rowed, sending up layer upon layer of ripples. Suddenly, she saw a figure standing atop the clock tower, one hand resting on his hip, defiantly facing the howling wind, wearing nothing but a red apron.

On his head was some strange white thing, fluttering in the wind like a scarf, giving off an imposing presence.

Merlin had deliberately chosen such a conspicuous spot to stand, making himself easy to spot. As expected, his plan worked.

However, Alice couldn't quite tell who that person was at a glance. But that disheveled silhouette always reminded her of someone.

It was Elkin the legendary swordsman. A year ago, when they first met, that hero was just as disheveled, yet his presence was unmatched.

Alice felt the figure on the clock tower resembled Elkin the swordsman, and her heart stirred with excitement.

Could it really be that coincidental? Elkin the swordsman appeared here.

Such an elusive man, and she actually ran into him?

Although Alice was clear in her heart that the person she liked was Merlin, not Elkin the swordsman, recalling the events on the pirate ship, she still wanted to express her admiration and say thank you.

If it weren't for Elkin the swordsman, she might have been sold off to who knows where by the pirates.

So Alice rowed faster, speeding toward the clock tower that was about to be submerged.

Upon reaching the base, Alice gathered her energy, leaped up forcefully, and arrived directly at the top of the clock tower.

Seeing that back figure, Alice felt a surge of emotion, thinking she was about to meet her idol.

But then she couldn't make out the person's face clearly. He was wearing white stockings on his head, and Alice's expression froze instantly.

What the hell?!

The hero I admire is a pervert wearing stockings?!

Something's off about this atmosphere. Did I get the wrong person?

Alice stood frozen in place, not daring to approach, deep doubts rising in her heart.

But Elkin the swordsman had already sensed someone's arrival. He slowly turned around, one hand gripping his waist, and casually said,

"Hey, Alice, you came fast."

Hearing the voice, Alice didn't need to think about it—she immediately knew who it was. It was her own idiot cousin!

The excitement in her heart instantly turned to ice water. She had actually mistaken this pervert for Elkin the swordsman. How incredibly stupid of her!

Thank goodness, thank goodness. I knew it—Elkin the swordsman wouldn't be this perverted!

Sure enough, Merlin was the most perverted one of all, putting on such an imposing act that he even made himself hallucinate.

Wait, that's not the point! Where did Merlin get those women's stockings?!

title: Chapter 58 — Farewell
content:
Chapter 58 — Farewell

Volume 11 · Chapter 58

Alice felt she had no choice; she had a feeling Merlin had some weird kinks.

Since he couldn't get what he wanted from her, he was reaching for other women instead.

On the surface it looked like he was sacrificing himself, saying, If not me, then who?

But inside, she was thinking sourly that if he was going to steal someone else's underwear, he might as well steal her own!

She was, after all, the woman officially recognized as his wife! She wouldn't feel jealous and uncomfortable about it, and she definitely didn't want Merlin this demon running roughshod over other people!

Alice looked at Merlin with a complicated expression, thinking that this bastard at least had a wife at home! Always daydreaming about the stockings of other women—how much did he look down on her? Was her charm not even enough to compare with some random woman from outside?

"Hah~" Merlin looked at Alice's serious face and couldn't help but laugh. "What nonsense? Why would I need to steal your stockings and panties? Even a rabbit wouldn't graze right by its own burrow."

"I'm preventing you from getting arrested as a pervert, you idiot! I've never actually been married, and suddenly I'm a widow for no reason—I don't want to go through something like that!" Alice lifted her chin, her cheeks flushed red, and muttered seriously, "I-I mean, if you have any other terrible delusions you want to act on... in a way, I might pretend I didn't see..."

"Hiss~"

Merlin sucked in a breath of cold air, thinking that this Alice girl had one heck of an imagination!

What kind of terrible delusion was she talking about?! Was she thinking he was going to do something filthy with women's clothing?!

Damn it! Don't look down on people like that! He was the Great Demon Lord; would he really do something so sleazy?!

Even if he would! It still wouldn't be Alice's underwear!

Those childish panties with little bear prints exuded such a juvenile vibe that even a straight-laced guy would lose interest in seconds, okay?!

Merlin's face darkened, his eyes narrowing as he figured Alice was indirectly calling him someone with a low threshold for turn-ons.

"I'm warning you, don't underestimate me. Even if you kill me, I'd never set my sights on you. And I need to emphasize one thing—these stockings weren't stolen; they were looted~"

......Alice's breath caught, her eyes widening as she stared in disbelief. "Isn't that even worse?! At least stealing requires some skill! Looting is just completely crushing someone's will!"

Merlin's expression grew awkward; Alice's jabs were starting to sting. "Can you stop obsessing over these stockings? Do you really think I enjoy wrapping things like this around my head?! I'm suffering in silence here!"

"Please, what suffering are you enduring there?! From the looks of it just now, you seemed pretty pumped up—couldn't you tell you were enjoying yourself in secret!" Alice paused, then complained with rising irritation, "And I asked you to deal with the water demon, not to use it as an excuse to go flirt with other women!"

"I handled it properly, see~" Merlin nodded his chin toward the direction of the royal palace. "That water demon has been scattered—I don't know if it's dead, but it'll definitely suffer fatal injuries."

Alice glanced into the distance. He had actually completed the task properly, but the once-magnificent royal palace was now reduced to crumbling ruins, and that massive crevasse that looked like a whale sucking in water—how much would that cost to compensate for?! He'd gone a bit overboard.

"....You weren't seen drawing your sword, were you?"

"Do you think I wear stockings on my head for decoration? Obviously no one saw me do it." Merlin tugged at the stocking on his head.

"......" Alice was momentarily speechless. She somewhat understood Merlin's reasons for suffering in silence, but she was still a little jealous. "Then couldn't you have found something else to use? Why did it have to be... such a despicable thing?"

"If I could've found anything else, do you really think I'd be wearing this鬼 thing?! Do you want me to tear a piece off this tiny apron of mine?" Merlin casually lifted his apron to show Alice just how helpless he was, but in doing so revealed something far more scandalous.

"Yaaaaah! My eyes! Stop flaunting R-rated stuff so blatantly, you jerk!" Alice covered her eyes with both hands, her delicate body trembling, her face instantly flushing as red as a boiled lobster.

"Hehe~" Merlin let down his Spartan apron and decided to spare Alice further bullying.

"You jerk, how long are you going to keep wearing this stocking?! Are you addicted or something?!" Alice stomped over to Merlin in a huff, grabbed the white pantyhose off his head, and declared, "No more wrapping disgusting things like this around your head! Have some sense of shame!"

Merlin quirked his mouth slightly, his hair a bit disheveled. He didn't say anything about Alice's action, but deep down a trace of melancholy lingered. Had he really awakened some incredible attribute?!

"Good grief..." Alice pouted cutely, glanced at the stocking in her hand, curiously sniffed it, and was immediately even more surprised.

"This..."

"It seems pretty high-quality! Definitely not something an ordinary person could afford!"

"...You...you...you actually...you actually went out behind my back and hooked up with a wealthy woman in the imperial capital?!"

"...."

Merlin furrowed his brows, thinking—if he could find a rich sugar mama, why would he still work so hard as an adventurer running around daily?!

What kind of childhood had Alice experienced? She looked so proper most of the time, but what exactly was going on in that brain of hers?!

Merlin found it hard to meet Alice's furious, embarrassed gaze and couldn't resist retorting.

"Why do you have such a rich imagination?! Sure, I've thought about being kept by a rich woman, but out of dignity, I've never actually gone through with it."

Alice sucked in a sharp breath, rolling her eyes as she demanded, "Don't change the subject! Explain yourself—why does every time you go out and run around, you end up hooking up with some random woman?! And this time it was a wealthy woman?! We're both working-class folks under the same roof—how can you be so awesome?!"

"Well...." Merlin stroked his chin and said seriously, "I guess it's a racial talent."

"Eeeeeeeeh!!!" Alice nearly exploded from anger, tore the stocking in her hand into pieces, balled them up, and hurled them away fiercely.

"Hey! Those were the Imperial Queen's stockings—they have commemorative value!" Merlin felt a bit of attachment; they could at least be used as leverage.

"Keep dreaming! You think someone like you could hook up with the Imperial Queen? It had to be some shameless noblewoman! Disgraceful! Sleazy! Hmph~!" Alice felt much better after tearing up the stockings.

"Pfft!" Merlin clicked his tongue, watching the useless stocking fragments drifting in the air, and fell into deep... thought.

The stocking fragments swayed in the wind, intertwining and spiraling, flying toward an unknown direction.

Perhaps someday, when Merlin gets married, he'll recall this moment countless times—

Merlin running freely under the setting sun, waving the girls' stockings above his head.

That was his lost youth...

title: Chapter 59 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 59 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets

Volume 11 · Chapter 59

Alice noticed Merlin was a bit distracted, reached out and grabbed his chin, twisting his face back to look at her.

"Afterwards, I'll be keeping an eye on you. Don't think you can still go around flirting recklessly with fox spirits behind my back. I'll be watching you—"

Seeing Alice's eyes seem ready to kill him, Merlin instantly rolled his eyes and thought gloomily—

Is this woman possessed by a drama queen or what?

We're not even real husband and wife, and yet she wants to restrict my freedom?

Damn it, this trend feels a bit concerning....

Night fell.

The sky was a deep black, almost a color of despair and purity.

Without the accompaniment of moonlight or starlight, it was as if dark clouds had covered the brightness.

A horse rushed out of the royal capital's boundaries, carrying a mysterious figure.

Judging by the figure, one could vaguely tell it was a woman.

She wore a black robe, apparently deliberately trying to conceal her identity, not wanting to be easily recognized.

Isabella had run out of trump cards and reached a dead end, forced to flee quickly.

The imperial capital had become extremely unsafe, fraught with crises. The Rose family's army had surrounded the palace in small boats, intending to capture Isabella alive.

However, the cunning Isabella refused to sit idle and wait for disaster. She chose a strategic retreat—saving herself meant there would still be hope for tomorrow.

Isabella had not yet given up hope of making a comeback. The kingdom army stationed in the north could still be utilized.

There were many elite soldiers and officers within the kingdom army. If handled properly, perhaps she still had a chance to rise from the ashes.

This was Isabella's last resort. There were no more choices left for her.

Reaching this point, Isabella felt a trace of despair. She felt that none of her decisions had been wrong, yet the results kept disappointing her time and again.

Perhaps if she hadn't encountered Merlin, this world-class BUG player, Isabella might have gone much further. But instead, she had kicked an iron plate!

The Lake Fairy was Isabella's proudest trump card; yet someone unknown had defeated her.

If she hadn't been hiding in the basement all along, Isabella would almost certainly have been obliterated by Merlin's sword aura in the first moment!

Terror and unease swirled within Isabella. Who was this invisible opponent? Which powerful figure had Duke Rose summoned? To possess such terrifying strength—having even broken the Lake Fairy!

The Lake Fairy was the guardian deity of the imperial royal family, the foundation upon which Britain was built, its power absolutely not to be underestimated.

Even Isabella had believed that as long as she controlled this ancient power, she could rest easy and suppress all rebellious forces.

But reality had given Isabella a lesson, slapping her face hard.

The pitch-black night was hazy, making it impossible to see the path ahead.

Hoofbeats splashed, the sound echoing across the vast plain.

Isabella urged her horse to speed up, wanting to escape this chaotic area as quickly as possible.

Those Rose family soldiers might finish searching the palace without finding her and then come chasing after her.

However, the already uneasy atmosphere was suddenly broken by a rumbling sound—

The ground before Isabella began to shake, and suddenly a broad earthen wall rose up, blocking her path.

Her mount was startled and neighed loudly. Isabella lost control and fell off the horse.

This suddenly appearing earthen wall had disrupted Isabella's plans. Clearly, someone had deliberately set an ambush here.

Isabella slowly sat up, terror and unease rising within her. She had no idea who was lying in ambush.

She raised her head and saw Winifred approaching slowly, holding a magic book. It seemed this massive earth wall was his doing.

Isabella was startled within. She hadn't expected it to be neither the Rose family nor anyone else, but her own Thorn Knight.

Thinking about it, Winifred had been imprisoned by her. How had he escaped?

And his attitude was clearly to settle scores with her, which was far from friendly!

Damn it! Why pick such a time! Was heaven determined to destroy me?!

Isabella turned and ran, but suddenly a slender rapier pointed at the tip of her nose.

Bathed in the moonlight, the rapier shimmered with silver light, as if stars were slowly flowing within its shadows.

Aside from Meriuses, who else could it be?

Meriuses held his slender rapier and addressed Isabella on the ground in a teasing tone.

"Your Majesty, where are you off to? We've been waiting for you here for a long time. You're finally here."

Isabella felt the bone-chilling cold emanating from the rapier. She had never imagined that a Thorn Knight's sword would ever be pointed at her!

"What... what are you going to do!? Drawing a sword on me—has this become betrayal!?"

"Betray you?" Meriuses wore a provocative smile and tightened his grip on the rapier. "Shouldn't you be the one who betrayed us? If things weren't still unclear, I would have ended this fake right now with a single thrust!"

A stream of cold sweat ran down Isabella's forehead. Hearing Meriuses's words, her heart skipped a beat.

No way... has the matter of my impersonating Elizabeth already been exposed!

This is bad. If that incident were exposed, what terrible fate awaited me...

Isabella's expression was panicked. She refused to admit anything and was still trying to use her queenly identity to turn danger into safety.

"What fake? Meriuses, I warn you not to talk nonsense. There must be a misunderstanding here!"

"Stop deceiving us with your clumsy acting. You are not the true queen, correct? You are actually Her Highness Princess Isabella." Winifred walked closer, his face completely expressionless.

"What nonsense are you talking about!? If there's a misunderstanding between us, we can talk it through. But what you're doing right now is no better than banditry! You speak of loyalty and righteousness with grand words, but this is how you treat me!?" Isabella ground her teeth and made an angry protest. "I am your queen!"

"That's enough. We've seen enough of your act of touting someone else's prestige. Lord Maesfield has already told us everything. She was the one who sent us to ambush here, fearing you might suddenly flee the capital. And indeed, you do seem to have a guilty conscience." Morrison stepped forward, looking down at Isabella on the ground, and said seriously, "Whether or not you are the true queen, please come with us. Everything will be brought to light."

"You have no right to refuse at this point. If you resist, we'll have no choice but to use force—"

The next day.

The Rose Legion had already occupied the royal capital, but they had not yet found Elizabeth or Maesfield. However, they had found Catherine, who was in a coma.

The duke ordered Catherine to be temporarily imprisoned and continued a carpet-style search of every corner of the capital, hoping to find the fake queen.

Such a large-scale search would only be a matter of time before they found the true queen, Elizabeth.

As for the fake queen Isabella, she was held captive by Morrison and the other two Thorn Knights, awaiting Maesfield's return.

The three groups all had their reservations, existing in a delicate balance.....

However, the troublemaker himself, the great swordmaster Elgin, had chosen to slip away quickly that very day.

Whenever facing any kind of trouble, wiping everything clean and patting one's ass to leave was Merlin's greatest strength.

Inside a tent stationed outside, the two of them discussed—

Merlin leaned over slyly and said with a grin, "Oh great Alice, my treasure, let's get out of here quickly. Nobody can threaten Michelle's safety anymore. We've completed our mission. Everything has been resolved. Let someone else handle the cleanup. We can return in peace now."

Alice's face flushed. She hadn't expected Merlin this bastard to call her "oh great treasure." Although it was a bit childish, it was quite pleasing to her ears.

But Merlin lowering his posture right from the start made her feel something was off—there must be something suspicious!

So Alice furrowed her brows, narrowed her eyes and scrutinized Merlin, as if looking at a criminal.

"...What's with that look? It's like you're staring at a fly." A drop of cold sweat ran down Merlin's forehead. Being stared at by Alice made him feel unnerved inside.

Alice saw that guilty look on Merlin's face and recalled this guy's habit of straying with other women. Could he have fathered a bastard outside and not wanted to take responsibility?

Such a dramatic soap-opera scenario didn't seem entirely impossible. Merlin did have the face of a scoundrel, and he was especially shameless with her.

Alice unhurriedly set down her cup of hot milk, took a deep breath, and questioned suspiciously.

"Why are you in such a rush to flee? Did you do something bad and feel guilty?"

"What are you talking about? Someone honest and straightforward like me would have any wrongdoing written all over my face.不信 you can look at my innocent eyes~" Merlin blinked at Alice, sending flirtatious signals nonstop.

Alice immediately got goosebumps. Unable to bear Merlin, she coolly remarked, "Disgusting. Behave normally."

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue. Seeing that his coaxing tactic had no effect whatsoever, he had no choice but to speak to Alice in a serious manner.

"Alice, haven't you noticed how chaotic things are here right now?"

"The fake queen is nowhere to be found, the true queen's whereabouts are unknown, there's no leadership, and only the young Michelle is being swept along by the currents."

"In order to avoid deeper trouble, we should slip away quickly, cut all ties, and not get involved in anything that follows."

"And you also saw how much destruction I caused in the imperial capital. If someone holds a post-war reckoning, wouldn't we be the ones suffering?"

Alice thought it over and agreed. There was no need to stay any longer. It was time to return to Rexum.

However, recalling that Merlin had taken a wild woman's stockings the day before, Alice felt anger welling up from within, and her jealousy surged again.

"Humankind Era, Year XXX, Month XX, Day XX. My husband cheated on me behind my back in the imperial capital, finding himself a rich older woman, and even stole her stockings as a keepsake. This openly green-hat-giving vile behavior—I will remember it for the rest of my life!"

"What's there to be afraid of? Didn't you flirt with a rich woman in the capital? With that kind of money, you wouldn't be stressed, would you? Just loosen your belt and the cash flows in, right? That's your specialty, after all~ Little Daisy the Player~"

Merlin was speechless. He hadn't expected his dark history to be dragged out like this. Countless black lines slid across his forehead, and his heart grew extremely anxious.

Alice this idiot! That rich woman was the true Empress of the Empire!

Actually, what I'm worried about isn't the destruction of the imperial capital at all—it's that I robbed the empress's stockings!!

That pair of stockings had originally been intended as leverage to blackmail Elizabeth, to keep her from causing trouble...

But now, those stockings used to humiliate the queen have been torn to shreds by this spendthrift woman!!!

title: Chapter 60 — Olive
content:
Chapter 60 — Olive

Volume 11 · Chapter 60

Merlin could tell Elizabeth cared about her reputation—that much was obvious when he had robbed her of her stockings.

Those stockings, though they looked terribly shabby, could in a sense serve as an umbrella of protection.

But the stockings had already been torn to shreds by Alice, and that protective umbrella was gone.

This left Merlin feeling exposed. If Elizabeth were to reach out and demand them back, he was afraid he'd be left with nothing to offer.

A trick born from nothing could hold out for a moment, but it couldn't hold out forever.

Besides, Duke Rose had already increased the number of troops searching for the queen. Running into Elizabeth was only a matter of time.

By then, Merlin wouldn't even know what expression to wear when facing the imperial queen—

With the stockings in his possession, Merlin had felt completely confident. If Elizabeth dared cause trouble, he would have made a big deal out of the stockings.

But now that they were gone, Merlin felt it would be safer to avoid her锋芒 and keep as much distance from the imperial queen as possible.

Even though their brief encounter had convinced him that Elizabeth was harmless, who knew what the real queen was really thinking? It was an unknown whether she might fly into a rage and strike back.

So Merlin planned to leave this mess of a place with Alice as soon as possible, avoid any direct encounter with Elizabeth, and pretend that the whole incident of robbing the stockings had never happened.

"Alice, now isn't the time to expose my dark history, is it? I'm serious—we can't help with anything by staying here."

"What? You finally feel some shame?" Alice sized Merlin up, with a hint of sourness in her heart.

"I don't feel ashamed. I didn't steal or rob—I earned money with my own abilities~" Although Merlin felt his past work at the tavern was embarrassing, it wasn't exactly at the level of being shameful.

"Shameless. What you did was deception and swindling." Alice retorted angrily, shooting Merlin down.

"Understand it however you like. But that's not the point. The point is I didn't find a rich woman to sponsor me—if I had, I'd have definitely waved goodbye to you and left." Merlin grinned and cracked a joke.

Alice narrowed her eyes, and the soup spoon in her hand slowly bent under her grip, showing just how furious she was.

What's so great about a rich woman?!

I'll become a rich woman too! When that happens, even if this jerk comes crawling on his knees, I won't give him the time of day!

Alice calmed herself slightly and set herself a lofty goal of becoming a rich woman, not forgetting to put down her rival in the process.

"Don't worry. With your attitude, no rich woman with blind eyes would ever come after you."

"To be honest with you, the stockings you tore apart earlier came from the wealthiest woman in the empire, and she's going to come to your door to demand them back..." Merlin curled his lips into a smile and deliberately spoke in a meaning-laden tone. "You understand what I'm saying, right?"

Alice's eyes widened, her breath caught, and an uncontrollable shiver ran through her heart...

Afternoon.

Outside the military encampment.

A carriage bearing the seal of the Rose family was parked there.

Merlin and Alice planned to leave first, having decided they would no longer continue helping.

Although the matter had not yet been fully resolved and they were still short-handed, Merlin and Alice's mission was already over.

Their original purpose had been to protect Michelle's safety, and now the resistance forces had been eliminated—there was no longer any power that could threaten the princess.

Although Alice had kindly wanted to stay and help out, she chose to leave first to prevent Merlin from getting entangled with some wealthy widow from the capital.

Actually, Alice wasn't entirely sure whether what Merlin had said was true, but recalling that guy's flirtatious nature, she decided it was better to be cautious.

She certainly didn't want Merlin to be lured away by a rich woman. It was safer for him to obediently return to Lecxem with her.

The Duke and Michelle came out to see them off. Since Merlin and Alice had helped enormously, they deserved at least this courtesy.

"Are you really going back? The two of you aren't considering staying? There may be a victory celebration later."

"Thank you, Your Grace. We have our own matters to attend to, so we'll take our leave first. Besides, there shouldn't be any dangerous evil forces here anymore that could threaten Her Highness Michelle." Alice replied with a smile.

"Oh... it does feel rather sudden. I was hoping I could properly reward both of you at the celebration banquet." Duke Rose showed a disappointed expression.

"What a pity. If I hadn't been pursued by a rich woman, I wouldn't need to slip away so quickly. But then again, Alice worries about being cheated on~" Merlin shrugged helplessly.

"A rich woman?" Duke Rose looked puzzled, not understanding the reference.

Alice suddenly spun around, grabbed Merlin's clothes, and with a dark face complained, "Shut up, you bastard! Do you think strutting around collecting flowers is something to be proud of? Keep a low profile! Don't I have any dignity?!"

Merlin kept a straight face and said softly, "Don't get so worked up. I was just joking."

In truth, Merlin knew very well that as one of the Seven Kings of the demon race, he could never possibly have any entanglement with Elizabeth, a human empress.

Their different standings meant they certainly wouldn't easily end up together. Being in such a position inevitably involved countless interests.

Besides, the empire's law stipulated monogamy. Even though Merlin and Alice were husband and wife on the surface, they would still be bound by those restrictions—unless Elizabeth herself was willing to be Merlin's mistress.

But just thinking about it was impossible. As the imperial empress, how could Elizabeth ever humiliate herself to become an adventurer's mistress?

Finally, if Merlin were to compare Alice and the empress Elizabeth side by side, he clearly preferred Alice—the simple and lovely great treasure—in his subconscious.

Michelle hesitated behind them for a long while before stepping forward and bowing slightly. "Lord Alice, Lord Merlin, thank you both for your help. I will keep this favor in my heart. If you ever need anything in the future, I will certainly not refuse."

"No need to be so polite, Your Highness Michelle. This was all within our duty." Alice smiled as she answered, feeling a great sense of pressure accepting thanks from the imperial princess, since she and Michelle weren't yet as close as she was with Princess Shirley.

"Enough with the useless pleasantries. What about the other half of the payment?" Merlin asked at a very inopportune moment, fairly worried about this, since it concerned his livelihood.

Alice rolled her eyes at Merlin, feeling that this guy really knew how to ruin the atmosphere—she could have made a friend out of Michelle.

Merlin paid no mind to Alice's eye roll; he wasn't an idealist and looked down on the values of righteous little guardians.

"Then... once things stabilize, I will definitely pay you back. Trust me." Michelle hurriedly replied.

Merlin found this credit arrangement somewhat exasperating but could only wait patiently. Considering the current局势 was still turbulent, it seemed quite difficult for a young princess like Michelle to produce so many gold coins.

"Fine. Two months. Don't forget."

"I will definitely not forget. I can guarantee it with the honor of the royal family." Michelle placed her hand over her chest with a serious expression.

Alice leaned close to Merlin and whispered, "Alright, don't press so hard. We've already received 350,000 gold coins—that's enough to handle our urgent needs."

Merlin sighed. Being subjected to Alice's pillow talk all day was enough. "Let's go."

"Wait a moment!" Duke Rose suddenly called out to Merlin and Alice, apparently having something else on his mind.

"What now? Surely there's nothing else to bother me with? I told you not to push your luck—this is going too far..." Merlin's face darkened, his expression thoroughly impatient.

"Lord Merlin, please don't get so worked up. I'm not here for you, but rather to ask Lord Alice..." The Duke of Rose explained.

"......" Merlin looked awkward, wondering why the duke wanted to see Alice. Didn't he realize this silly girl was跟着 him around?

"Lord Alice..." The Duke of Rose turned to look at Alice, his manner polite as he earnestly asked—

"Would you be willing to give up your work as an adventurer..."

title: Chapter 61 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 61 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 11 · Chapter 61

“Eh?!”

Alice froze for a moment, confused by the situation.

To be named Grand Knight Commander of the Rose Knights?

That was the highest position in a knightly order!

Given that the previous commander, Sir Malen, had already died, the duke seeking a replacement was only natural.

But why her? Merlin was far stronger than she was...

Alice grew suspicious. Facing the duke’s olive branch, she was at a loss for words.

In the duke’s eyes, Alice was still more powerful than Merlin—supernaturally so.

He assumed Alice was a low-key adventurer who never flaunted her strength, which was why she had no reputation.

A warrior capable of driving back the lake spirit was worthy of being the queen’s honored guest! Indeed, in the duke’s perspective, the lake spirit had been defeated by Alice, and not just him—Michel beside him believed the same.

Merlin had acted alone the entire time, secretly handling the lake spirit’s threat. Only he and Alice knew the truth; everyone else was clueless.

The duke and Michel assumed they had called upon Alice, and that was how the lake spirit had been dealt with. Merlin had only provided cover for their escape and contributed little else.

Even the deaths of the three Thorn Knights in pursuit were attributed to Alice’s primary efforts in their eyes.

Thus, in the duke’s and Michel’s view, Alice was a low-profile yet extraordinarily powerful warrior.

If Michel had any real authority, he might have immediately offered even better terms to compete with the duke for her allegiance.

“How about it, Lady Alice? My Grand Knight Commander’s salary is over ten thousand gold coins, and you can relocate from some backwater like Reckham to Cardiff, the capital of Wales. I’ll even arrange a grand estate for you.” The duke made generous promises, treating her like a fair employer.

Adventurers, with no job security, often went hungry when tasks dried up. Though they called it the most passionate profession, in reality, they couldn’t compare to those on the royal payroll—and it was far more dangerous.

The duke wasn’t ignoring Merlin on purpose; with his wealth, hiring a second Saint-tier powerhouse was nearly impossible.

In the end, comparing Alice and Merlin, he naturally chose Alice—she was simply *stronger*.

Alice hesitated, tempted. The duke’s offer was truly enticing, practically a verbal contract for a stable future.

Merlin, however, bristled. *Why was Alice being offered this olive branch while he got nothing?*

He didn’t care about being Grand Knight Commander—even if the duke begged on his knees, he’d refuse. The position would restrict his freedom, binding him to endless constraints.

For a Great Demon Lord to work under human nobles? The humiliation was unbearable.

But this feeling of being overlooked galled him. It was like a stray dog chasing after the wind while he remained stuck in place.

“Wait—why are you offering this to Alice but not to me as your Grand Knight Commander?”

“Lord Merlin, to be frank, I can’t afford two Saint-tier warriors. Compared to you, Lady Alice offers better value—she’s clearly stronger.”

“What?!?” Merlin’s eyes widened as he pointed at Alice. “Which eye of yours sees her stronger than me?”

“Lady Alice is the one who drove back the lake spirit—that monster. She’s already among the empire’s top-tier swordsmen.”

Alice puffed out her chest proudly, her face radiating smug satisfaction.

Merlin couldn’t stand her smug expression and snapped, “Duke, you’d better clarify: the lake spirit you’re talking about was actually taken care of by me.”

“Don’t joke, Lord Merlin. I know your strength is formidable, but compared to Lady Alice, you’re still a notch below. Frankly, sincerity earns more respect than hollow bravado, don’t you think?” The duke spoke diplomatically, though he privately thought Merlin was just a kept man blowing hot air.

Merlin’s expression darkened. *Alice’s rank was only N tiers above his? Why the hell was there such a misunderstanding?*

Alice glanced at Merlin, then decided to clarify, “Really, that water spirit was taken down by Merlin. I didn’t do anything.”

“Alright, alright, Lady Alice, I understand your kind—you’re brilliant but too modest. But let me tell you, excessive modesty is just another form of showing off.” The duke felt he’d seen through the pair.

“Indeed, Lady Alice, you don’t need to be so humble. I assumed you were just an ordinary Saint-tier, but your strength far surpasses even the empire’s top knights.” Michel chimed in beside him.

“Please accept our praise, Lady Alice. It’s what you deserve.” The duke bowed his head in reverence—strong warriors deserved respect in this world.

...... Alice’s face twisted into an awkward, dazed expression. *Why couldn’t she make herself clear? Now she sounded like some scheming bitch.*

“So, Lady Alice, have you considered becoming Grand Knight Commander?”

“Ehhhhhhh.”

Alice hesitated, leaning close to Merlin and whispering, “Merlin, are you going?”

The duke noticed Alice constantly deferring to Merlin and thought she lacked decisiveness. To secure this powerful warrior, he added, “If Lord Merlin wishes to join as well, he’s welcome—but the pay and benefits won’t be as good, since my knights only need one Grand Knight Commander.”

“What do you think?” Alice asked Merlin, her tone suggesting the duke’s offer was decent. The real appeal? Merlin would become *her* subordinate. How delightful.

Merlin rolled his eyes and muttered bluntly, “No. You go if you want. I’m the Great Demon Lord—I don’t like being controlled.”

Alice’s face darkened. She hadn’t expected Merlin to reject such a good deal.

What to do? If Merlin refused, she couldn’t go alone. It would be meaningless.

If she left him behind, she’d worry constantly. *What would he turn into without her?*

He’d probably wander the world, eating and drinking at others’ expense, causing trouble wherever he went.

And... she didn’t *want* to leave him either.

Alice’s face flushed, and she sighed softly. This rare chance to suppress Merlin—she had to let it go.

“Duke, thank you for your kindness, but we’ll pass. Though adventuring is unstable, we’re still happy with our lives... I’m sorry.”

Alice pulled Merlin away, turning to leave.

“Hey, the offer was pretty good! Why refuse?” Merlin frowned, confused.

“It’s my choice. Don’t question me, hmph!” Alice huffed, her cheeks tinged with pink.

After Merlin and Alice left in the carriage, Michel couldn’t help but ask, “Duke, why did Lady Alice refuse such generous terms?”

The duke watched the carriage disappear into the distance and sighed deeply. “Because of love.”

---

**England’s Northern Frontier.**

The region had been restless lately, teetering on the edge of war.

Duke Overley had already buried his only son. With nothing left to strive for, his sole desire was revenge—and to elevate his family to unprecedented glory, even if only temporarily.

The coming war wasn’t just about vengeance. It was a moment of historical upheaval, where the Overley family would topple the dynasty and seize the pinnacle of power!

The entire Overley clan had been preparing for years, sharpening their blades and gathering strength. Now, their ambitions were about to become reality.

---

**The next day. The northern frontier of the kingdom.**

Dawn’s light pierced the morning sky, awakening the sleeping land.

This was the empire’s first line of defense, meant to repel threats against the queen.

Now, it faced the Overley family’s rebellion—the most dangerous outpost.

Fifty thousand royal soldiers stood firm here, the empire’s elite, their armor gleaming.

The soldiers stood tall, their spirits high, ready for the brutal battle ahead.

Though the royal army was often criticized in peacetime—spoiled, arrogant, and acting like the queen’s lapdogs—now, they stood loyal, facing the terrifying enemy in a defensive stance.

Opposite them, ten thousand Overley soldiers stood in dense formation, clad in black armor, their bloodthirsty gazes fixed ahead.

Even their weapons differed—their blades were forged from demon-beast materials, enchanted with magical runes, proving the Overley family’s vast wealth.

Beyond the soldiers, mercenaries, beasts, and other powerful allies stood ready. Over a hundred siege engines loomed, their sheer size a testament to the Overleys’ resources.

Though the empire had prepared, they had still underestimated the Overleys’ combat strength—far beyond expectations.

This was an unfair war. The royal army would be crushed by the Overleys’ combined forces. The power gap was glaringly obvious.

The knights of the royal army shrank back, many sweating nervously.

A black eagle soared overhead, as if taunting them—or declaring their doom.

The aged Duke Overley charged forward atop a black bear, his ambitious eyes burning with fury.

He cast aside his heavy helmet, drew his longsword, and roared from the depths of his soul—

“The vile queen murdered my son! She will pay for this in blood!”

“Let us ravage Britain’s lands! Plant the Overley banner everywhere!”

“Kill!!!”

---
*(Author’s note: This chapter is for the trolls.)*

First, my conditions were clear: Merlin acted alone. The princess and duke knew nothing.

Imagine Merlin as an ordinary student at Osseban Academy, and Alice as the student council president.

In reality, the ordinary student is a prodigy who scorns the council presidency.

From an outsider’s perspective, how would they view the ordinary student Merlin and the council president Alice?

Need I say more? The council president Alice is obviously stronger! She’s the *council president*, how could she be weaker?

This is simple logic. I’ve emphasized it at least three times in the first volume.

Merlin’s strength was shown by bullying the Knight Commander and enduring the Third Knight’s attack.

What else? That’s it. Does this reveal all of Merlin’s power?

He solved 1+1=2, and the onlookers said: *So impressive, a genius!*

Who believes that? Not me. Meanwhile, the council president Alice might still be struggling with multiplication tables.

Ultimately, the trolls are just God’s perspective. They know everything, but the characters in the story don’t.

Like the Demon Lord’s opponents—many think he’s weak because they’re in God’s perspective, but the Demon Lord’s enemies don’t know his true strength.

I’ve made all this clear in the story, at least three times.

title: Chapter 1 — Old Wounds
content:
Chapter 1 — Old Wounds

Volume 12 · Chapter 1

A few days later.

The news of the Ofré family's rebel forces sweeping everything before them and the kingdom army's crushing defeat spread like wildfire throughout the empire.

Many residents of England began fleeing their homes, escaping to the surrounding areas.

Even remote Wales unexpectedly received a large influx of refugees, causing chaos everywhere.

In fact, the reports were sugar-coated—the defeat was practically a compliment to the kingdom army.

The first battle of the rebellion was nothing more than a one-sided massacre with no logic to it!

The moment the two armies clashed, the kingdom army was thrown into disarray by the rebels.

Swords flashed and fell, and those pampered knight lords were beheaded one after another, no different from chopping vegetables.

On top of that, it was said that the imperial capital was also in turmoil, with the queen's palace having been flattened to the ground.

Many people felt that the empire was on the verge of collapse, that the British dynasty was just barely clinging to life, and who could possibly stop the Ofré family's iron cavalry?

Although the kingdom army had been defeated from the very beginning of the war, many local lords' private armies were still desperately resisting the Ofré family's iron cavalry.

Even the remote town of Lecester was in a state of panic, with people whispering in the streets and alleys about these events, feeling that there was no safe place left in the empire.

Almost everyone believed that the Ofré family's iron cavalry would reach the capital within half a month...

Merlin and Alice had just returned to Lecester the night before and were planning to rest for a while.

Alice's injuries from before still hadn't fully healed, and she was listless and lacking energy at home.

The two of them didn't have to worry about living expenses for now. This trip had been quite fruitful, with a surplus of one hundred thousand gold coins.

Although Alice didn't say it aloud and always wore a sour face, the sudden filling of their empty coffers made her very happy.

At home.

Golden sunlight filtered through blue curtains, casting light into the living room.

The dazzling brightness shone directly onto Merlin's face, forcibly waking him from the sofa.

Merlin frowned deeply, rubbed his eyes, and went to the bathroom.

He surveyed the house, then checked the time, and suddenly felt something was off...

Normally, Alice, that energetic person, should have been up long ago and would have dragged him out of bed too.

Yet today, it was already close to noon, and he hadn't seen Alice anywhere, which wasn't normal.

Merlin tugged at his messy hair and walked to Alice's room, only to find the door tightly closed.

"Hey, Alice, are you still sleeping?"

No sound came from inside, as silent as a still pond, as if there were no one there at all.

Merlin couldn't help but feel puzzled, thinking that maybe Alice had gone out early without waking him?

So, with a puzzled expression, Merlin opened the door and saw Alice lying in bed motionless.

On the floor were the clothes she had just taken off the night before, scattered haphazardly and not picked up.

Usually, Alice was far more diligent about cleanliness than Merlin, but today she was incredibly messy, which was strange.

When Merlin spotted the pink oil stick underwear on the floor, with a little bear printed on the butt, several dark lines crossed his forehead.

Damn it! I really can't stand this childish woman anymore.

You're already not a child, so why can't you wear more mature underwear?

So many panties, each with a smiling little bear on the back—what kind of juvenile preference is this?

I'm starting to develop a phobia of childish panties. I really want to tear apart those stupid smiling bears...

Merlin ranted in his mind, awkwardly averted his gaze, and looked toward Alice on the bed.

He saw that Alice's face was somewhat pale, her eyebrows tightly knit, with beads of cold sweat on her forehead. She seemed to be ill.

"Huh?" Merlin's heart skipped a beat as he stepped closer.

Generally, cultivators who practice martial arts prioritize forging their physical constitution, so getting sick was almost unheard of.

The only reason Alice could end up like this was probably due to the old wound from her fight with the Thorn Knight flaring up.

"Hey, Alice, are you alright?"
