Merlin reached the bedside and patted Alice's face, trying to wake her up.

"...Alice slowly woke up, showing a somewhat uncomfortable expression."

Merlin crossed his arms and asked calmly, "What's wrong with you?"

"I feel... I can't muster any strength, aching all over." Alice answered in a low voice, putting on a pitiful expression.

When Merlin heard Alice's description, he immediately understood what was going on—this was the result of her old wound not healing properly and her body slowly recovering.

Not only was it not a bad thing, but a good thing. Indeed, the dragon race's healing abilities were impressive—unless it was a fatal injury, recovery was always fast.

Merlin felt that this weakness was only temporary. With a few days of rest, Alice would return to her usual energetic self.

"Oh? Can't muster any strength? Isn't this the perfect time for me to bully you? How convenient~"

Alice was startled and hiccupped, her eyes widening as she glared at Merlin.

Seeing Merlin's lecherous grin, Alice felt a bit panicked inside.

"...What are you going to do? Taking advantage of someone who's helpless—that's only something a villain would do."

"I think I've always been the villainous role, so taking advantage of someone when they're down isn't inappropriate." Merlin stroked his chin and replied with a sly expression.

"Meow..." Alice's eyes began to shine, covered by a layer of crystal-clear tears. Her eyelashes fluttered several times. "You're like this even when I'm sick—if you're not going to comfort me, at least don't try to bully me. Are you really happy to see me die? You shameless demon, after all I did to take you in, and you treat me like this."

Seeing Alice's indignant expression, Merlin felt a bit helpless. He seriously said, "Come on, come on, stop scaring yourself. You're not going to die. It's just that your dragon race's innate healing ability is repairing your body, so it's draining your energy. That's all."

Alice had never experienced this before and thought she had a terminal illness. After hearing Merlin's explanation, she finally felt somewhat relieved.

"...Really?"

"Of course. I have no reason to lie to you. But ending up like this is entirely your own fault. When you can't win, just run away. Why insist on fighting to the death with someone?" Merlin couldn't help but make a comment.

"...I don't need your help." Alice puffed out her cheeks, turning her head away in a huff.

"To be honest, I could cure you with just a sip of my saliva. But you insist on finding a slow priest. What do you think? Want me to spit on you right now?" Merlin's mouth moved suggestively, as if he could spray out succubus saliva at any moment.

"...No thanks." Alice curled up in the blankets, only her eyes visible. "That's disgusting."

"Ugh!" Merlin sighed impatiently, stood up, and walked away. "Then just stay home and recover. See you~"

"Huh?"

Alice was genuinely taken aback, watching his beautiful back with complicated feelings.

She thought to herself, I'm sick and unable to move around. I need someone to take care of me right now.

Yet Merlin just shrugged and was about to leave without even caring about her!

Her husband of convenience was so spineless. Even when Merlin was unwell, she had been considerate of him...

Alice glared at Merlin, her cheeks puffed out like a hamster storing food, and said angrily—

...Wait!

"You shameless demon!"

"Don't you want to take care of a sick and helpless me?"

"I'm your wife in name, you know. You should take responsibility. Hmph~!"

title: Chapter 2 — Curse
content:
Chapter 2 — Curse

Volume 12 · Chapter 2

Merlin stopped in his tracks and looked back. "Take responsibility, what is this? You talk as if I did something rude to you. We're only spouses in name, so I'm warning you, don't start acting the drama queen. I really hate troublesome fa—"

"…." Alice was speechless. She bit her lip, blushed, and muttered softly, "Aren't we a married couple in everyone else's eyes? My body feels terrible right now… if you abandon me, people will laugh at us."

"Ha. I've already been taken for a man who lives off a woman. Do I still care about that?" Merlin twisted his lips slightly, looking like he had zero intention of dealing with Alice's little trouble.

"….." Alice had no way to deal with Merlin, so she put on a pained expression instead. "…Khoo! I feel like my time has come. I'm about to die, khoo khoo!"

Merlin looked at Alice's pitiful state and found himself at a loss. A huge bead of sweat rolled down his forehead. He didn't seem to buy the act at all.

Alice grew anxious inside. Her face turned even paler, her eyes shimmering with watery gloss as she pleaded pitifully, "At a time like this, I only wish… I wish someone could keep me company. Even a demon would do, I won't be picky…."

"Bah!" Merlin scrunched up his face, turned his head, and walked out of Alice's room.

Alice stared at the empty room and let out a mournful whimper from her throat.

Her eyes glistening with tears, she rolled over and hugged her pillow for a sense of security, like a stray cat.

She felt small, miserable, and helpless, with no one to love her, brought to the lowest point imaginable.

Alice thought Merlin was being far too cold-blooded. He wasn't remembering any of the good old days at all, even though she'd always been so nice to him…

"That heartless demon Merlin. He's right — no good being comes from evil creatures. Waa…"

"Hey, that's going too broad, you brat."

Alice had been complaining to herself when she heard Merlin's voice again and nearly jumped out of her skin.

Merlin had intended to leave, but somehow he came back halfway. What was he thinking about?

Alice's eyes went wide. She flipped back around and confronted him, huffing, "Why are you back?!"

"I was thinking I didn't have anything better to do, so I decided to be generous and come look after you~" Merlin said casually.

"…Didn't you say you didn't want to take care of me? Your heart just softened?" Alice narrowed her eyes and asked suspiciously.

"Don't misunderstand." Merlin interrupted Alice's妄想, his expression serious. "I just want to wait until you're done so I can bully you some more. After all, life has no fun without bullying you~"

Alice stared at Merlin, her face slowly flushing red with anger. She felt like this demon was treating her like some kind of pet.

"I don't need your care at all!"

"Oh? That's great then. I'll go find Hobbs for a drink." Merlin said he was leaving.

"Eh, eh, eh!" Alice frantically called after him. "I… I didn't mean that. If you insist on taking care of me, I guess I can reluctantly accept it!"

Merlin's expression darkened. He didn't say anything, thinking to himself — this troublesome guy, why is it that everything she says sounds so unpleasant?!

Alice pulled up the covers, hiding half her slightly flushed face, and mumbled, "Since you're so eager to take care of me, I'll reluctantly say thank you, hmph~!"

//w//Y

The utterly dilapidated imperial capital.

The floodwater had already receded along the underground rivers, revealing the ruined scene.

Buildings were soaked and rotting, the ground muddy like a riverbed.

Many imperial capital residents had returned and wore lost expressions about the future.

It was as if the empire were in the midst of a rebellion, unable to begin rebuilding the capital for the time being.

And that massive chasm in the center made even those who wanted to reconstruct feel powerless against it.

Although it was now fully exposed that Isabella had impersonated the queen and ruled the empire for several years,

Elizabeth's crisis had not truly been resolved. She was still in a dangerous situation.

The House of Overfrey to the north was like wolves and tigers, furiously pushing straight into the imperial capital's territory, their intention to establish a new rule quite obvious.

Duke Rose had originally been constantly urging his subordinates to search for the fake queen, but then Meisfield returned with the real queen Elizabeth in tow.

The moment they met, the atmosphere was thick with hostility. Meisfield and Elizabeth were surrounded by soldiers and nearly caused an incident.

Fortunately, Elizabeth explained her identity and the full circumstances of many things in the end.

Upon learning the truth, Duke Rose sighed deeply inside. He settled the queen in comfortably, telling her to rest first and deal with the rebellion crisis afterward.

The next day, Sir Morrison and two other knights returned, bringing the fake queen Isabella under custody, drawing a period to the royal family's internal unrest.

Upon hearing about this, Catherine fell into deep remorse. She hadn't expected to be the deceived party. Making enemies with Meisfield had been foolish.

However, Elizabeth held no intention of blaming Catherine. Instead, she readmitted her. After all, during times when talent was needed, some mistakes could be overlooked.

Besides, Catherine was only a victim herself — deceived by Isabella with no knowledge of the inner workings.

It seemed the royal family's internal strife had been smoothed over, but an even greater threat arrived straight after, endangering Elizabeth.

House Overfrey's army was invincible in combat. The private forces of various nobles couldn't mount a single counterattack as the Overfrey troops advanced straight south toward the imperial capital.

By rough estimate, reaching the imperial capital's territory would likely only take a week.

The royal army had suffered a crushing defeat, and the private forces of every lord fled at the mere sight of the enemy.

Four of the Twelve Thorn Knights were dead, five remained by Elizabeth's side, and the rest were elsewhere, unable to return in time.

The mightiest of them all, the Lady of the Lake, appeared to have been injured by Merlin and fallen into a century-long slumber, unable to be used again.

Although that great water demon was merely a replica of the Lady of the Lake, not her true body, and she hadn't even used her full power,

Merlin's strike had been too ruthless. It had still damaged the Lady of the Lake's spirit.

From this perspective, Elizabeth's remaining trump cards to resist House Overfrey were pitifully few. The situation did not look optimistic.

With the royal palace destroyed, Elizabeth had set up a residence somewhere in the capital as a temporary palace to handle affairs.

—

At that moment, in a certain room, Isabella sat in a chair before a mirror.

Her complexion was dreadful, her face haggard, a far cry from the vibrant energy of former days.

Isabella had given up all hope. Though she appeared free now, she was actually under house arrest by Elizabeth, monitored whenever she did anything.

Elizabeth stood behind her older sister, wearing a golden crown upon her head, having reclaimed what was rightfully hers. "Sister, did you ever imagine this day would come? The reason you couldn't become queen is because you're far too obstinate and prone to losing your reason. Father's choice was not wrong!"

"Hateful!" Isabella grabbed her makeup box and smashed it into the mirror, cracking it. A vicious grin spread across her face as murderous intent flashed in her eyes.

"Elizabeth, I curse you!"

"You will surely be trampled to pieces by House Overfrey's cavalry, leaving not a single bone behind!"

title: Chapter 3 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 3 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 12 · Chapter 3

Isabella was trembling with rage, her disheveled appearance eliciting a measure of pity.

“Is this what you expect?” Elizabeth asked calmly.

“Exactly. I want you to die now. I truly regret it—back then, when my heart softened, I didn't kill you! From childhood to now, you are the person I hate most!” Isabella didn't turn around; instead, she looked at the woman behind her through the mirror.

Elizabeth could imagine how mad Isabella was, and she understood her attitude.

Theoretically, Isabella should be the first in line for the throne, but in the end, it was Elizabeth who became queen.

Isabella was extremely dissatisfied with this. All her efforts had come to naught—how could she not hate?

“No matter what you say, you are unfit to be the empire's queen. Your father knew your nature, so he didn't choose you—everything was arranged for the better.” Elizabeth believed her father choosing her was correct.

“But I was so close to succeeding! It was all due to Elgin the Swordsman... Isabella stared blankly, her eyes wide open, bloodshot—yes! It's all because of this mysterious bastard! If not for him constantly opposing me at every turn, I would still be the empire's ruler! No one can defy me! Falling to this state now, it's not that my strategies were wrong, but that Elgin the Swordsman is a brute! It's all his fault! If this guy had died sooner, how could I possibly be imprisoned here!”

Elizabeth took a deep breath, vaguely feeling that her sister was about to go mad.

She had heard many things about Elgin the Swordsman from Messfield.

About this mysterious man, she had gained some understanding.

Recalling Merlin's appearance, Elizabeth's heart stirred, and she couldn't calm down.

Who would have thought that a whole empire, nearly the size of a kingdom, would nearly be brought to collapse by a lowly iron-rank adventurer!

Elizabeth temporarily needed to deal with the Overre family and Elgin the Swordsman's matters, so she could only put them aside for now.

However, Elizabeth already knew who Elgin the Swordsman was. Even if Merlin ran away in a short time, she knew.

She needed to figure out how to get her stockings back. They were always in the hands of that perverted man, making her feel extremely embarrassed.

Also, after hearing about Elgin the Swordsman's formidable strength, Elizabeth felt even more apprehensive of Merlin, and dared not act lightly toward this man.

If possible, Elizabeth wanted to talk things through, trying her best to avoid causing more bloodshed. Coexisting without interfering with each other might be the best choice.

Elizabeth had had brief contact with Merlin, who was Elgin the Swordsman. Although she felt this man had a quirky personality and was a bit perverted, he didn't seem like someone utterly evil.

At the very least, Elizabeth felt she and her sister were different; she could calmly sit down and have a good talk with Merlin.

Moreover, Elizabeth felt she had an advantage—she knew Elgin the Swordsman's true identity.

The other party's secretive actions were surely for his own reasons. If utilized slightly, perhaps the grudge could be resolved.

Elizabeth looked at her sister pulling her hair out, falling into madness, and could only let out a deep sigh.

“Sister, even now, do you not know what you did wrong? For the sake of consolidating your position, can you use any despicable means?”

“Be quiet! I don't need you to mock me! Since I've already become like this, why don't I just kill myself!” Isabella gritted her teeth and said resentfully.

“I won't let you die, just as you once did to me. But I hope you reflect properly.” Elizabeth didn't want Isabella to die. To strike down one's own kin was something she couldn't do.

“Get out! Get out of here! I don't want to see you!” Isabella flipped the dressing table in front of her, making a clattering sound for a moment.

“Well...” Elizabeth turned to leave, and as she was about to go, she said one last thing.

“I will come see you again, Sister...” <

Elizabeth gently closed the door and stepped out, taking a deep sigh.

Outside, four soldiers were guarding the door, not allowing Isabella to move freely.

When Elizabeth's daughter Michelle was waiting outside for a long time, seeing her mother come out, she went up to her, “Mother, how is it?”

Elizabeth shook her head, saying helplessly, “She is having a hard time accepting reality now, and her emotions are not stable.”

“I also don't want to intentionally provoke Aunt's anger...” Michelle lowered her head, showing a look of grievance.

“It's fine, this has nothing to do with you.” Elizabeth patted Michelle's head affectionately and said, “If it weren't for you, I'm afraid Mom wouldn't have seen the outside world yet. You've really grown up, Michelle...”

Michelle felt a bit comfortable being patted, and her face inexplicably turned red. Being praised by her mother, she felt inexplicably proud.

“Don't worry about anything. From now on, everything heavy will be handled by me. Many burdens aren't something you of this age can control.” Elizabeth didn't intend to involve Michelle in anything; she intended to take full responsibility for the mess at hand.

Michelle nodded, and suddenly recalled the matter of hiring Merlin and Alice, “Then... Mother, can I have some money?”

“What do you need money for?” Elizabeth was somewhat puzzled. Currently, they were in the midst of war, and the finances were tight.

“I hired two powerful adventurers, and only paid a general commission.” Michelle said with great conflict.

“Is that so...” Elizabeth suddenly realized what was going on, recalling that Merlin had said it was Michelle who had hired him.

“This matter will be handled by Mom, so you don't need to worry.”

Temporary Royal Palace's grand hall.

@ SF Light Novel

Although this place cannot compare to the palace's splendor, it barely counts as solemn.

Some officials residing in the imperial capital have all come, standing on both sides.

Nowadays, the Rose Duke can be called the most popular person, living in a state of mutual benefit.

The entire imperial army are followers of the Rose Duke, making his status rise to a very high level in just a few days.

Messfield, Millius, Morrison, Katherine, and Wynefred, the five Thorn Knights, also gathered here.

Because there is an urgent crisis now; the Overre family has marched south, and Isabella must issue orders to maintain the situation.

The hall's door was slowly opened by the guards, and Elizabeth, wearing a splendid gown, walked in gracefully.

Everyone lowered their heads slightly, bowing slightly, showing respect to the queen.

Elizabeth nodded at each person and then climbed onto the high platform, sitting down regally.

“Thank you all for gathering here today. I believe you also know that the empire is at a critical juncture of life and death. The Overre family has ill intentions, marching south, dealing a major defeat to our kingdom's army, and heading straight into the empire's interior...” Elizabeth paused, straightening her back, and her expression gradually became severe.

“So relying solely on local private troops is hardly enough to stop the Overre family's iron cavalry.

“We need to counterattack, use strategies of surprise, and shatter the Overre Duke's momentum!”

title: Chapter 4 — Mercenary
content:
Chapter 4 — Mercenary

Volume 12 · Chapter 4

Elizabeth's tone was very serious, even with a hint of dignity, making one fully feel the crisis of the current situation. The ministers and knights below immediately became solemn, looking up at the queen, awaiting her next orders. Duke of Roses noticed Elizabeth's face looked somewhat exhausted and couldn't help asking, "Your Majesty, you look a bit tired. Although we now face a great enemy, please still take care of your health." "It's fine, I have no problem. Moreover, the Ofrey family could press their armies at any moment; we have little time to rest and must quickly devise a response." Elizabeth said, furrowing her brows. "Please rest assured, Your Majesty, the Thorn Knights are always at your command; even if we sacrifice our lives, we will not hesitate!" Mesfield spoke on behalf of the other Thorn Knights, expressing their stance. "Thank you. In this rebel war we are at a disadvantage, but who will ultimately laugh is still unknown; we are not without a chance to turn the tide." Elizabeth paused, then got straight to the point, asking, "Duke, could you briefly explain the current situation?" "According to the battle reports sent back from the front, the fifty‑thousand‑strong royal army has been nearly annihilated, with hardly any survivors. The Ofrey family's combined force of one hundred thousand is unstoppable, pressing straight toward the imperial capital." The Duke of Roses paused, his tone embarrassed, and said, "Now we can only rely on the private armies of local lords to delay the enemy's advance, but the disparity in strength is huge; Ofrey would likely need only..." The ministers began to discuss anxiously, their faces showing panic, each feeling a hint of fear; everyone could see the predicament, and at any moment they might be slaughtered by the Ofrey family. "Why is the royal army so weak? Unable to even resist—could it be that they lost their fighting spirit in peacetime?" Elizabeth wore a wistful expression, feeling that the royal army, as part of the imperial establishment, should already be considered a strong force. Their equipment is of high standard, their treatment second only to the Purple Orchid Knights, yet they were routed by the Ofrey family in an instant, which Elizabeth finds hard to accept. "Although partly due to loss of fighting spirit, the root cause is simply the vast gap in strength between the two sides." The Duke of Roses responded seriously. "A gap that large?" Elizabeth furrowed her brows, seemingly not accepting this explanation, since the royal army's strength is not weak. "Exactly, setting aside the overwhelming disparity in numbers, even the equipment of the royal soldiers is probably inferior to that of the Ofrey family." The Duke of Roses said a very realistic remark; he clearly saw where the difference lay. "..." Elizabeth nodded, seeming to have realized something. "Although the royal army's equipment can be called excellent, compared to the Ofrey family's private forces backed by the great treasure trove of the Magic Beast Forest, they are still far behind. Their weapons are made from magic beast materials and reinforced with magical runes; before them, the royal army is utterly helpless." The Duke of Roses shook his head helplessly. ofi small "Go on..." Elizabeth instantly became interested; although the Duke of Roses was pessimistic, it is indeed the reality. "Moreover, the Ofrey family has recruited many powerful mercenaries, whose combat ability already far surpasses that of the royal army by a large margin. I heard that among these mercenaries there are many strong individuals, the most famous of whom is probably the 'Black Wolf Mercenary Group'—a force not to be underestimated." The Duke of Roses said seriously. Upon hearing the name 'Black Wolf Mercenary Group', the ministers present all showed looks of astonishment, involuntarily covering their mouths and whispering nervously, as if they feared this mercenary group. Even a few of the Thorn Knights were surprised, never expecting the Ofrey family to be able to enlist such power. Seeing the reactions below, Elizabeth's eyes showed doubt: "What is the Black Wolf Mercenary Group? Why are you making such expressions?" "Your Majesty may not know, the Black Wolf Mercenary Group is an organization active in the Magic Beast Forest, the most renowned mercenary group there. It consists of only five people, yet each has reached Saint‑tier—truly elite among elites." The Duke of Roses had investigated and knew something about this group. Elizabeth's eyes widened; she felt this mercenary group was excessively outstanding, indeed a force not to be underestimated. "You should know that every Saint‑tier powerhouse is precious; for a great noble like the Duke of Roses, having just one Saint‑tier bodyguard would already be satisfying." "Yet the members of the Black Wolf Mercenary Group actually consist of five Saint‑tier powerhouses. If it were a strict regulation, the entry requirements could no longer be described as harsh but rather exaggerated to the extreme." "Having five Saint‑tier powerhouses on duty already rivals a relatively large Adventurers Guild." "However, the Adventurers Guild usually represents a region, while this mercenary group is completely free and hard to control." "In fact, that is exactly the case: wherever the Black Wolf Mercenary Group goes, they are respected, and even nobles treat them as honored guests. A wandering team achieving such feats is already quite excellent." "Their group only accepts elite individuals who have reached Saint‑tier; the missions they take on are extremely dangerous. As long as one can afford the high price, they will work for anyone. Many great nobles within the empire have hired them as guards, but few can keep them, because the high hiring cost is too much for most people to bear." The Duke of Roses explained. Elizabeth understood this point well; the Thorn Knights are mostly her own trainees, requiring little payment, but mercenaries motivated by profit are different—they seek to drain their employers' blood. "It is said these five members come from all over the world; they have been adventurers, bandits, soldiers, etc., but they share one trait: they do not fear death. The ferocity of the Black Wolf Knights is notorious in the trade; no one dares to provoke them lightly, for fear of losing their lives..." The Duke of Roses frowned, his brows knitted on his forehead. Elizabeth's heart could not calm for a long time; she did not know whether the Thorn Knights could help her resist these people. "Being able to forge such a powerful team, their captain Kassayeg is naturally no ordinary person. I think everyone knows how dangerous the depths of the Magic Beast Forest are; that place has never been fully explored, holding many secrets, and Kassayeg is the only man who has explored its interior and returned alive. His body covered in burn scars is the best proof..." The Duke of Roses said in a stern tone, trying to let everyone understand this man full of adventures. For a moment the ministers all showed fearful expressions; legend says deep in the Magic Beast Forest dwell terrifying magic beasts, and even a Saint‑tier powerhouse entering would likely not survive. How exactly did Kassayeg escape? If he relied on strength, then that strength is terrifying indeed! Queen Elizabeth's expression grew grave; hearing the Duke of Roses' analysis, she felt pressure mounting, thinking— The opponent's strength seems extraordinary. How should we respond? Relying on the Thorn Knights.... I don't know if we can withstand these five desperadoes. (。δ_6)

title: Chapter 5 — Monthly Ticket Update
content:
Chapter 5 — Monthly Ticket Update

Volume 12 · Chapter 5

Elizabeth felt a deep worry in her heart, believing that the power she now controlled was very weak and could not resist the formidable O'Fre army.

Even if the Thorn Knights could counter the Black Wolf Mercenary Corps, there were still a hundred thousand troops behind them!

Even Saint-tier champions are not invincible; once their magic and fighting energy are exhausted, they become very weak, and the mass-man strategy is not impossible to counter.

Elizabeth felt that she still had too few cards in her hand; if the lake spirit could still be used, she would not fear the onslaught of the O'Fre family.

For some reason, Elizabeth suddenly recalled Merlin, the Great Swordmaster Elgin; his strength seemed no weaker than that of the lake spirit's substitute.

If Elgin the Great Swordmaster were willing to help the empire, the current difficulty could be easily overcome.

Perhaps I should lower my stance and seek…

A flicker of panic flashed in Elizabeth's eyes as she pressed her hand to her forehead.

What am I thinking? That I would actually seek help from Elgin the Great Swordmaster?

With the situation so unclear, Elgin the Great Swordmaster and the royal family still had unresolved grudges.

Seeking a non-ally, non-enemy figure on one's own is obviously not a wise choice.

Elizabeth's idea of asking Merlin for help was mainly driven by her mistrust of this man.

The man who stole her stockings—does his character truly deserve trust? Gong Dingchen.

Moreover, as queen, Elizabeth's relationship with Elgin the Great Swordmaster was unclear, making it difficult for her to decide.

Melfield, seeing the queen's worried expression, quickly spoke with a firm voice, “Your Majesty, please rest assured; the members of the Black Wolf Knight Corps can be boldly entrusted to us.”

“Yes, Your Majesty, do not have any concerns. As your blade, we have fully prepared ourselves—nothing is more important than your survival.” Morrison also couldn't help but agree.

“Thank you all. I have no concerns; I just need to consider some matters carefully.” Elizabeth's frown did not lift, and she turned to the Duke of Rose, asking, “Besides the Black Wolf Mercenary Corps, what other powerful cards does the enemy hold?”

“The intelligence I know is about this much. The enemy's strongest card is the Black Wolf Mercenary Corps; there is probably no stronger foe. The remaining troublesome ones are likely those monster beasts.” The Duke of Rose said honestly; that was all the information he had.

“Monster beasts…” Elizabeth felt a headache, realizing that those tamed monster beasts were also difficult to handle.

“That’s right. Those low-level monster beasts tamed by the O'Fre family may not be powerful, but their combat ability far exceeds that of ordinary soldiers. When their numbers grow, they are not easy to deal with.” The Duke of Rose finished his serious explanation and continued, “These are roughly the O'Fre family's entire strength now. How to respond is up to Your Majesty to decide.”

Elizabeth fell silent, thinking carefully.

The situation of the enemy being stronger than me left her feeling helpless.

The O'Fre family's power is several times that of the kingdom; a direct confrontation would certainly yield no good outcome.

If she were to request external intervention casually, it could bring wolves into the room; she could not consider this thought unless absolutely necessary.

Elizabeth thought left and right, and could only take some risk—a gamble-like decision. If successful, it could instantly resolve the crisis.

“I need two warriors to lead a small squad, maneuvering around, infiltrating the enemy's rear, and assassinate the O'Fre Grand Duke before the army reaches the imperial capital.”

The ministers below immediately began to discuss, debating whether the queen's order was reasonable; it would be hard to reach a conclusion in a short time.

“Assassinate… O'Fre?” The Duke of Rose's forehead dripped cold sweat, feeling that the queen's action had a hint of risky pursuit of wealth.

“Yes, it's to assassinate O'Fre.” Elizabeth slowly stood up from the chair. “The O'Fre family's army is not stable; most of them gather only for profit. The truly loyal are few. If we kill the O'Fre Grand Duke, the alliance will crumble, the army will fall apart, and the empire's threat will vanish.”

After hearing the queen's explanation, the ministers whispered to each other, and no opposition emerged.

Because the situation was dire, not taking some risky measures would likely fail to break the stalemate.

Even the usually cunning Duke of Rose did not oppose it; he thought this was a choice the queen had to make.

If nothing were done, letting the O'Fre family wreak havoc, by the time they reach the imperial capital it would be too late.

Trying to rely on the few remaining troops to repel a hundred thousand joint army? That was like joking.

“The problem is that this task is extremely dangerous; if it goes wrong, it could end with no return. To look after each other during the process, I need two warriors. I wonder who among you has the courage to take on this task?” Elizabeth did not hide the risk, stating plainly that it was a very high‑risk mission.

“Your Majesty, please entrust me!” Melfield was the first to kneel on one knee, refusing to retreat.

“We are also willing to take on this task!”

The other four Thorn Knights did not hesitate; they also knelt on one knee to request.

Even knowing that this assassination task was a death or survival gamble, everyone was prepared for death.

Elizabeth found the situation obviously awkward; she thought she only needed two people, why were they all jumping in?

Melfield frowned, his expression dissatisfied,

“What are you doing? This task is significant; obviously handing it to me is the safest! Why are you all just messing around?”

“Don’t say it so lightly. I also want to kill O'Fre, that old thief. Don’t just think about eating meat; you don't even give others a bowl of soup,” Morrison said helplessly. “Anyway, there are two slots; I must be counted as one of them.”

“....” Melfield grew irritated inside, feeling that Morrison was a hot‑blooded bastard.

“None of you are suitable; let me go instead. I previously caused the queen so much trouble.”

Catherine closed her eyes.

I think.

Catherine closed her eyes, but her tone was very serious, still feeling guilty about defending the fake queen earlier.

Catherine, I said we don't need to dwell on this matter…

This is not a dilemma; it's a punishment for a mistake…

Uh… Elizabeth didn't know what to say.

Why are you all fighting? This assassination task clearly suits me and Wenifred best; it's basically…

Milius stood up proudly, his expression arrogant.

He felt this task was most suitable for him.

“Yes, we two are the most suitable.”

Wenifred also stood up, agreeing.

Among the Thorn Knights, only two excel in speed; unfortunately, Emmanuel, that arrogant fellow, is dead. So the most suitable person to execute the assassination of the O'Fre Grand Duke is…

Milius pointed at himself without hesitation—

Only I!

title: Chapter 6 — Repay
content:
Chapter 6 — Repay

Volume 12 · Chapter 6

Although Miliuthus had a somewhat haughty demeanor, his tone was indeed serious.

“What nonsense are you talking about?” Mesfield turned his head back, dissatisfied.

The usually silent Venifred couldn't help but speak up—

“Miliuthus is right; only the two of us are suited for this mission.

“I and Miliuthus are orphans who grew up in the same orphanage, friends since childhood; no one knows him better than I do.

“His swordsmanship is swift, as fast as starlight, very suitable for fighting in cramped spaces, so assassinating Duke Ofre is naturally no problem.

“And my magic can assist Miliuthus, helping him complete the task better; in terms of coordination, I doubt anyone in the Thorn Knights is more in sync than us.”

Miliuthus nodded, proudly saying, “Venifred is right; we are indeed the most in-sync partners.

“This is a very important mission; don’t joke around at a time like this.... Mesfield’s tone grew a bit stern.

“This isn’t a joke~” Miliuthus spread his hands, explaining, “Mesfield, your martial movements are too big; you’re not suited for assassination. Catherine excels at barrier magic for defense, and Mori....kohe, as long as you don’t mess things up midway, that’s fine. All things considered, the only ones fit for this task are me and Venifred.

“Hey, you bastard, you were clearly looking down on me just now?” Morison looked dissatisfied, feeling he’d been full of mockery, as if you were saying you’re much stronger than me—?

“Hmph, at least I won’t be shouting and yelling during an assassination~” Miliuthus couldn’t help but mutter.

“What did you say?” Morison narrowed his eyes, not in a good mood. Gongding die

“Enough, there’s no need to argue over this.

Elizabeth spoke up to stop Miliuthus and Morison, telling them to quiet down.

Although Miliuthus and Morison couldn’t stand each other, under the queen’s pressure they had to rein in their tempers.

Elizabeth fell silent, carefully weighing the pros and cons.

Although Miliuthus has an impulsive side, now it seems that having Miliuthus and Venifred act together for the assassination is indeed better.

After all, being able to coordinate, their默契 is excellent—a helpful factor.

This market gamble, if successful could turn the tide; if failed would make the situation even worse.

Elizabeth lifted her head, looking down, and said in a pleading tone—

“Miliuthus, Venifred…”.

“Then I’ll entrust this plan to the two of you,”__

二

A few days later.

The town of Rexham.

Weak Alice, under Merlin’s care, has regained her spirits, no longer listless and unable to lift her weapons as before.

In fact, the injuries Alice sustained in battle with the Thorn Knights were severe; if placed on an ordinary person, they would definitely be fatal.

However, Alice has been strengthened by dragon blood, so a little rest is enough for her to recover.

These days Merlin has been belittling Alice with his mouth, saying some sarcastic things, but his behavior is still honest, taking care of this female Hero.

Alice frequently feels goodwill toward Merlin, but it’s always suppressed by those harsh words, leaving her completely unable to read what the Great Demon Lord is thinking.

Perhaps it’s exactly as Merlin said—just wanting to take good care of himself, then bullying himself for amusement.

Still, since Merlin can take care of himself, Alice feels somewhat grateful, at least having someone to rely on.

Although only a few days have passed, she’s experienced the feeling of being looked after, and it’s still quite pleasant.

Alice for the first time thinks that living together isn’t such a bad thing.

Although the other party is a demon, Alice feels he’s different from ordinary demons; he always carries a touch of humanity, not the bloodthirsty nature of demons in rumors.

In fact, Merlin is already an anomaly among demons; normal demons are extremely bloodthirsty, craving fresh flesh and blood like executioners.

They regard humans as livestock, similar to chickens, ducks, and fish.

Think about how humans treat livestock, and you’ll know how demons treat humans.

Alice feels that the things she cannot do, Merlin can do; if not, the two of them together can manage, just like having a strong backing supporting her.

The concept of “family” gradually forms in Alice’s mind, though she herself hasn’t realized it.

Alice only feels that when she’s ill, someone else will care for her; when life gets difficult, the two can work together, and this warmth makes her long for it.

Sunlight streams through the curtains, as if opening a tunnel.

_book.SFA

Tiny dust particles drift in the tunnel, wandering without pattern. s dead big small activity

Alice walks out of her room, rubs her messy silver hair, and stretches.

Her body has improved greatly; she no longer needs Merlin to keep taking care of her.

Alice looks around and sees Merlin still sleeping on the sofa, the blanket kicked onto the floor.

“Geez, you’re still sleeping like that…”.

Alice walks over, intending to wake Merlin, but then thinks—these past few days of taking care of me might have tired him out?

So Alice abandons the idea of violently waking him and instead helps pick up the blanket from the floor, gently covering Merlin with it.

Let him continue resting =

Alice gazes at Merlin’s sleeping face, thinking, and her face slowly reddens as she hurriedly lowers her head—

What am I doing?!

Does this make me look like a real wife?!

Calm down, after all this guy has taken care of me, so I’m just giving a small repayment—nothing else.

Yeah, that’s right…..

After a while.

Alice busies herself in the bathroom for a bit.

She comes out holding a basin, inside which are some clothes.

Just as Alice steps out, she happens to see Merlin waking up, sitting on the sofa rubbing his eyes.

“. . . You’re awake?”

“Yeah, how did you get up? Are you feeling okay?” Merlin asks in surprise.

\say

“..uh, I’m fine now.... Alice pushes her messy hair behind her ear, responding awkwardly.

“.....Merlin nods, pulls the blanket over himself and lies down; looking at this, he clearly wants to catch another nap.

“Hey! You’re awake, so don’t go back to sleep—do you want to sleep forever?!” Alice says angrily.

“Don’t nag, you always say I have no conscience, and you’re not still cursing me to die….” Merlin weakly retorts.

“....

Alice is momentarily speechless, unsure how to make Merlin more energetic.

She herself is normally full of energy, seeing Merlin lazy just makes her resistant.

The air falls into an awkward silence, making things awkward.

Alice stands there holding the basin, thinks for a moment, then suddenly says, “Merlin, I’m going to wash clothes next; do you have any dirty laundry? I…. can help you wash….”

“Huh?!” Merlin turns his head, giving Alice a surprised look, as if he’s seeing an alien.

“. . . It’s not that I absolutely need you to wash my clothes….” Alice feels guilty, her face red as she hesitantly tries to cover up—

“Anyway, I have to wash my own clothes too, so helping you wash a few… is no problem.

“…Don’t get the wrong idea; I’m not doing this to repay you!”

“Hmph~!”

title: Chapter 7 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 7 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 12 · Chapter 7

Alice wanted to help Merlin wash his clothes, as a way to violently repay him for taking care of her before.

However, Alice's stubborn personality made it impossible for her to say it directly, so she had to express her meaning indirectly.

However, Merlin found it a bit hard to accept, feeling that Alice was acting as if she had taken the wrong medicine.

Under normal circumstances, Alice would absolutely never help Merlin wash his clothes, and she might even scold him disdainfully.

“You want to help… wash clothes?”

“I didn’t say that, I was just asking casually.” Alice maintained her haughty attitude, “If… if you need it, I’ll just wash it for you, just as a side note.”

“You’re not possessed by something, are you?” Merlin asked, squinting his eyes suspiciously.

“What nonsense are you spouting!” Alice felt angry at Merlin’s reaction, feeling looked down upon.

“Good heavens!” Merlin scratched his head, incredulous, saying, “That Alice who always complains about me… actually wants to wash my clothes? Tell me, did the sun rise from the west today?”

“…How can you be like this? I’m being kind for once!” Alice was so angry she couldn’t speak.

“Do you have some ulterior motive toward me? If so, just say it straight, don’t play these sugar‑coated cannonballs.” Merlin wore a wary expression.

Alice furrowed her elegant brows, her expression unnatural.

Obviously I rarely show kindness, yet Merlin doesn’t appreciate it! ?

I just wanted to repay him, but he treats me as if I have some nefarious plot—truly, my good intentions are wasted on him like feeding a dog’s liver and lungs.

Alice turned and walked away in anger, without pausing.

“If you don’t need it, forget it, saves trouble,

“Wait!”

Merlin called out to Alice, turned around and flipped through.

He directly threw out the underwear he had changed last night.

“Pa‑chi” — what a coincidence — it instantly smeared onto Alice’s face.

“….Alice’s delicate body visibly shuddered, as if she had turned to stone.”

“Since you’re so eager, then help me wash my underwear, thanks for the trouble.”

After saying that, Merlin covered himself with a blanket, preparing to continue resting, not wanting to be bothered.

Alice’s delicate body trembled, not from fear but from being infuriated by Merlin.

Damn it!

What the hell does this bastard demon mean! ?

Can’t you at least have a better attitude? This is treating me like a maid!

I don’t owe him anything, why is he acting like this toward me?=

And why wash anything else? It just had to be the underwear…

Good heavens, please have some shame! This sort of thing should be washed by oneself, right?

I’m a girl too! My relationship with this bastard hasn’t reached the point of being completely open—consider my feelings!

Alice, after having underwear smeared on her face, was mentally ranting nonstop.

Those underwear probably haven’t been washed yet, and a faint hint of Merlin’s body scent drifted over, making Alice feel awful, on the verge of a breakdown.

Alice yanked off Merlin’s underwear and threw it hard onto the ground.

Then, huffing and puffing, she stomped over to Merlin, kicked his lazy butt with her foot, hands on her hips, and shouted loudly.

“Get up! Hurry up! You’re not allowed to sleep!”

“Huh?!” Merlin rolled over, looking at Alice with suspicion, “You little… I think you, this slutty woman, are deliberately causing trouble, always making a fuss early in the morning…”

“Who… said it was intentional? Since the clothes belong to both of us, you should come help, and furthermore… underwear, this kind of personal clothing must be washed by yourself!” Alice displayed an unquestionably dominant demeanor.

“But you weren’t saying that just now?” Merlin’s brows knotted together on his forehead.

“Can I take back what I said now?” Alice said angrily, thinking that if she were a little gentler, Merlin would bully her.

“Tsk!” Merlin clicked his tongue, unable to hold back a complaint, “Fine, you have small breasts, so you’re right.”

“Eee!!!” Alice instantly flared up, smoke practically rising from her head.

Outside, the sun shone brightly, the azure sky stretching as far as the eye could see.

The light was so clear it seemed to pass through crystal, and upon closer look there were other hues.

A gentle breeze swept by, mixed with the scent of decaying grass.

Outside the apartment where the two lived was a small courtyard, where clothes were hung on poles to dry.

At this moment the sunlight was abundant, perfect weather for drying clothes.

Merlin and Alice were busy in the courtyard, spreading out the washed clothes to dry.

One wonders if passersby would see this scene and smile knowingly, likely taking them for a married couple.

“Tsk, in the end it’s still going to be a hassle for me, thanks for saying all those nice things earlier…… Merlin, wearing a gray sweat‑shirt, handed Alice each piece of clean clothing one by one.

“It’s not just my clothes; you have plenty too, so coming to help is perfectly reasonable.

Alice responded angrily, taking the clothes Merlin handed her and hanging them on the rack to dry.

At home, Alice’s attire isn’t heroic; she wears a white strappy sundress, giving a homely feel.

“Pfft!”

Merlin felt dissatisfied inside, thinking that after taking care of Alice for so many days, she never even said thank you—truly an ungrateful white‑eyed wolf.

He casually picked up a bundle of white clothing and slowly unfolded it—

Ah geez! The slutty woman’s childish bear‑print panties!

Enough already, why do you like wearing such childish underwear?

Alice is at least an adult; can’t she wear something more substantive and sexy?

Whoever marries Alice as a wife is truly cursed with eight lifetimes of bad luck!

Naturally flat‑chested and already lacking any distinctive feature, she still likes such insubstantial underwear, completely lacking any allure….

Merlin couldn’t be bothered to comment on Alice’s preferences; he silently unfolded the childish bear underwear and passed it over.

Alice took it, adeptly slipped it onto the clothing rack, and just as she was about to lift it high, she suddenly felt something was off.

Wait, this triangular fabric looks awfully familiar… or something like that.

Alice examined it closely, then suddenly gasped, her face reddening at a visible speed.

She lightning‑quickly took off her own underwear and balled it up in her hand.

“Mer‑Merlin, I’ve told you several times already—don’t touch my underwear!”

“It’s not my fault; I took it out of the basin.” Merlin shrugged his shoulders.

“....”

Alice was at a loss for words, thinking she must have been too hasty after washing and forgotten to separate them.

How could such underwear possibly be left outside to dry? In the main hall, with crowds coming and going, those bear panties flapped like a flag for everyone to gawk at—what a melodramatic scene!

Alice felt her face might as well have sunk into the ground, so she blushed and silently gathered up her underwear.

“Such private clothing shouldn’t be hung outside; it must be kept indoors. Could it be… could it be that you’d be happy if so many people saw my underwear?”

“I’m not happy, but that’s a question I should be asking you….” Merlin pointed to a black pair of boxer shorts on the clothesline and said, “Why can you so openly hang my underwear outside? Don’t I deserve any face?”

“….Alice watched the boxer shorts fluttering in the wind like a pirate flag, her face instantly flushed red, she embarrassingly tapped her head, stuck out her tongue and blinked, saying—

“Sorry, I just wasn’t paying attention.”

“Heh heh~”

title: Chapter 8 — Future
content:
Chapter 8 — Future

Volume 12 · Chapter 8

"Heh? What the hell are you talking about?!" Merlin's face flushed with anger, veins throbbing at his forehead. "I really want to punch your head in."

"What's your problem?! I didn't mean to!"

Alice, whose temper was never exactly small, plucked Merlin's underwear off the line and flicked it onto his face in retaliation.

Merlin peeled his underwear off his face, narrowing his eyes at the person in front of him, strongly tempted to hang Alice the bastard on the clothesline himself.

"I think you've been needing a good scolding?"

"So what?" Alice turned around, puffing her cheeks, refusing to yield an inch.

"Whatever." Merlin pursed his lips and said coolly, "I can't be bothered arguing with someone who wears children's underwear. It'd lower my IQ."

"Eh!?" Alice's face slowly flushed red, and she turned away in irritation. "Don't you dare give me your opinion on my taste! And those aren't children's underwear — they're cute-style underwear! Isn't a little bear cute enough? You should kneel and apologize to the bear!"

"..." Merlin hesitated, not feeling any cuteness whatsoever. Instead, he found it ridiculously childish and downright creepy. "Never mind. I don't want to argue with a dreamless person like you. It's too low-class."

"Tch!" Alice clicked her tongue, displeased, and locked horns with Merlin. "Which eye of yours says I have no dreams?"

"An adult wearing such childish clothes — what kind of dreams could they possibly have?" Merlin spread his hands.

"Why is your definition of 'dreams' so shallow?" Alice gave him a look of utter disgust, then proudly declared, "My dream is to achieve great things on my own, reach the pinnacle of life through hard work, earn everyone's respect, carry love and justice to the very end, and finally crush you, the Great Demon Lord, under my heel in humiliation. Heh heh~!"

"Your nerve is truly boundless…"

Merlin quirked the corner of his mouth. Alice still wanted to stomp on him? She was living in daydreams. Probably never going to happen in this lifetime.

And those painfully awkward sentiments about love and justice — just hearing them made his head throb. Speechless, truly.

Merlin sensed Alice had left out a few sentences, so he tilted his mouth and teased,

"Aren't your dreams also supposed to include marrying the great swordmaster Elgin? Why aren't you bringing that up?"

"…" Alice's eyes darted around nervously as she awkwardly replied, "I don't want that anymore."

"Why?" Merlin pressed curiously.

"Tha… that's none of your business! It's my own matter." Alice's face flushed red, and she looked away, refusing to answer.

Merlin sighed with exasperation and chuckled. Was Alice somehow embarrassed by his earlier words?

"Don't just talk about me, alright? What about you, Mr. Lazybones? Do you have any dreams at all?" Alice asked with keen interest.

Merlin instantly fell speechless. His greatest goal remained lifting the curse on his heart.

Once that life-threatening factor was resolved, he could peacefully coast through the rest of his days.

But if he had to call it a dream… it hardly qualified. It was more of a worry he carried.

Merlin paused and realized he'd never actually thought about this — what he wanted to do afterward, or what lay ahead.

"…Never thought about it…"

"Hehe, I knew it. You've got the gall to mock me, but you're nothing but a dreamless salted fish yourself, spending every day loafing along without a care, never once considering what you're chasing after or what your future holds…"

Alice felt she'd won, so she hummed a cheerful tune and went back to happily hanging the laundry. Having Merlin completely at a loss for words made her feel extraordinarily smug — a first for her, by heavens.

Merlin fell silent, a hint of perplexity crossing his features as he pondered the future—

Dreams. Hadn't he thought about something like this before?

Marry an ordinary woman, earn a lot of money, never worry about food or clothing.

Have a child afterward — preferably a girl — and that would already be more than enough.

Then find some idyllic land where spring lasts all year round, and live a life completely free from trouble…

Perfect. Absolutely perfect. This was the life he wanted!

None of the chaos concerned him; he only wished to become a free speck of dust and live in peace.

But this hardly counted as an ambitious dream, did it? It was almost embarrassing to say out loud.

Only a cranky old man would think like this. But precisely because he'd lived so long, he understood how precious the ordinary could be.

Merlin sighed and thought that if it weren't for this damn curse on his heart, he could have already been living this kind of life.

Fate always played ridiculous contradictory jokes. The more Merlin clung to these消极 thoughts, the harder it became for him to sit idle.

Autumn sunlight bathed everything beautifully, and fallen leaves carpeted the courtyard, soft and brittle from the sun's warmth.

A gentle breeze swept from above, stirring the damp clothes hung high; white bedsheets swayed leisurely overhead, like flags.

Alice tucked her disheveled hair behind her ear and focused intently on her task, the hem of her skirt fluttering slightly and revealing her smooth, shapely calves like tender autumn lotus roots.

Her loose silver hair cascaded and interlaced behind her, impossible to look away from.

A wave of fragrance drifted toward Merlin, leaving him somewhat dazed and wondering — was that Alice's scent, or something else?

All things considered, Merlin thought Alice looked beautiful right now. Every touching detail of her beauty struck straight at his heart.

Beautiful, gentle, kind — capable of making everyone feel her warmth and approachability.

Sure, she had a bit of a temper, and occasionally acted foolishly, posing as a little guardian of justice — but none of it was truly objectionable.

If Merlin's earlier fantasy weren't false, Alice was practically the spitting image of the wife he'd imagined — matching every condition perfectly.

After all, although Merlin was a demon, at his core he still possessed a human heart. A girl like Alice was exactly the kind he'd been drawn to.

Merlin gazed blankly at Alice's graceful figure, something within him quietly stirring—

Perhaps marrying a woman like Alice wouldn't be so bad after all.

Living quietly in this little town — wasn't that exactly what he'd hoped for?

But Alice certainly wouldn't want to be with someone like him, right? Her head was full of ambitions to achieve greatness.

Besides, his curse hadn't been lifted yet. This peace was only temporary.

Merlin calmed himself slightly and noticed that Alice, due to her height, had to stand on her tiptoes just to hang the clothes.

So Merlin walked over and gently took the wet garment from her hands, approaching from behind.

"Let me. Your injuries just healed — you should rest for a bit."

"Eh!?" Alice jumped in surprise, looking up to see Merlin's chin standing solemnly behind her, happily lending a hand—

Had this guy swallowed something wrong?

He never helped around the house normally…

Why the sudden change of heart?

(w -.)?

title: Chapter 9 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 9 — Monthly Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 12 · Chapter 9

Merlin took a hanger, put the clothes on, and hung them up high.

This sudden approach, a wave of masculine aura, immediately left Alice a bit at a loss.

Alice bit her lip, her small face flushed like boiling water, her heart inexplicably quickened a few beats.

Merlin's overly enthusiastic gesture immediately left Alice a bit at a loss, her heart racing and she got flustered.

"What are you doing? This guy suddenly acting like this toward me, he must have some ulterior motive, right?"

Alice coughed lightly twice, trying to calm herself, pretending to be indifferent as she asked.

"...What are you doing? I can handle it myself, no need for your help."

"I see you're short, so it's quite a strain, right? Let me take care of this."

Merlin ignored Alice's awkward remarks, thinking that even though he didn't say it, he might be happy inside.

"Who is short! Bastard!" Alice hissed, puffing up like a startled pufferfish, "Give me the clothes, I'm not disabled, I don't need your help."

Merlin looked down at the angry Alice, said mildly, "Can't you stop being so grumpy? I'm not someone who helps people often; you should be grateful."

"No, I... need!" Alice pursed her lips, tightened her waist, acting ungrateful.

"I rarely care about you, so don't act so stiff, okay?" Merlin frowned, thinking he was being kind.

"...". Alice paused, narrowed her eyes suspiciously, "You suddenly care about me, you must have some illicit intention, right?"

"Ha!" Merlin felt awkward, thinking why would he be suspicious when he's a good person?

Alice saw Merlin not answer, immediately showing a realization expression, "So you guessed right, didn't you? Give me the clothes, I'll make my own clothes, I don't need your help."

Merlin avoided Alice's outstretched claws, helplessly asked, "What did you guess? I have no intention toward you?"

"Demand... demand my intimate clothes or something..." Alice answered seriously.

"It won't happen, who would demand your intimate clothes? No temptation at all, even if you give them to me for free, I won't take them!" Merlin complained.

"Ah? You, the thief of women's stockings, saying such words, you have no persuasive power at all!" Alice also retorted.

Merlin, stammering, couldn't help but drop a cold sweat, thinking his dark past wasn't that uncommon, being caught by Alice was indeed uncomfortable.

Alice, don't misunderstand, your injury is fine, I'm just afraid you'll have a problem, so you should rest a bit more.

Of course I have no ulterior motive toward you, just worried your old injury might flare up and trouble me, that's all~.

Alice felt relieved after hearing that, but still a bit disappointed, still hoping Merlin would care for her proactively, not with some ulterior motive.

Whatever... whatever you want, I won't be grateful to you anyway, huff!

Merlin sighed, hanging each piece of clothing on the clothesline, "You stinky woman, your mouth is truly unforgiving."

Alice secretly glanced at Merlin, then lowered her face with a flushed face, thinking that since Merlin had taken care of her for so many days, she should be a bit better toward him, at least thank him properly.

So Alice became indecisive, her two fingers twirled like swords, she organized a polite sentence in her mind, but when it reached her mouth it turned into--

"Before, you worked hard to take care of me, I reluctantly thank you, you should gratefully accept my thanks, huff!"

.....Merlin didn't speak, but his hand motion froze, a few black lines ran across his forehead, he thought, can this guy speak properly? Why is he so haughty when thanking? Indeed, he must truly dislike me from the heart?

Alice awkwardly lowered her head, her expression immediately became embarrassed, she thought, what's wrong with me? I clearly didn't intend to say it like that, why did my thoughts turn into something else when spoken? Now Merlin might think I'm a ungrateful white-eyed wolf.

Don't worry, I have no other business anyway, caring for you is just a bit of fun for me," Merlin said calmly.

".......I had guessed it long ago, huff!" Alice hissed, turning her head away, feeling frustrated, seeing that she was indeed more disliked, how can I get closer to this guy? QA...

Both were trying to read each other's thoughts, feeling that the other was hating them.

However, at that moment, two scavengers suddenly appeared outside the door.

One was an elderly, frail man with a hunched tall stature, carrying a cane.

The other was a small boy, no more than five or six years old, with delicate skin, a face like soft dough.

Their clothes were somewhat tattered, and they looked gaunt, as if they'd experienced disaster, appearing very exhausted.

Although the old and young beggars were very untidy, their behavior was quite polite.

"Esteemed gentlemen, we are refugees from the Imperial Capital, we've been traveling for half a month, could you spare us some food?" The elder stood outside the door, pleading with a frowning brow.

Both looked outside, showing puzzled expressions, though they knew many people had migrated from the Imperial Capital recently, but seeing people unable to eat was a first.

"Is the situation in the Imperial Capital worse again?" Merlin whispered.

"Maybe, not everyone who leaves their hometown does so smoothly, most ordinary people are in a difficult situation," Alice replied softly.

Merlin looked at the beggars outside, recalling the flooded Imperial Capital, understanding that many people prioritize survival over money, so they can only rely on aid on the road.

"We haven't eaten for two days, if possible, just give us some food, please help us in the name of the Goddess of Light, I'll remember your kindness for a lifetime."

The elder had a cross drawn on his chest, the boy just hid behind his grandfather without speaking.

"Wait here, I'll go find some food for you."

Alice saw the old man and grandson pitiful, her heart softened, seeing them suffer made her uneasy.

If possible, Alice wanted to help these people within her ability.

Although she didn't have the strength to quell the current rebellion, she could still give some food.

So Alice didn't discuss with Merlin, turned and went upstairs back to her room.

Merlin shifted his gaze to the old and young scavengers outside, seeing their tattered clothes, feeling a bit uneasy.

"Ha, is this getting worse?"

In this constantly turbulent situation, it seems I can't be detached from it...

title: Chapter 10 — Black Wolf
content:
Chapter 10 — Black Wolf

Volume 12 · Chapter 10

Merlin stared at the old man and young boy outside, feeling that this whole mess was at least partially his doing.

The little boy seemed somewhat frightened when he saw Merlin, and quietly hid behind his grandfather.

The old man smiled at Merlin, feeling that he didn't look like a suspicious person either. He wondered what the other fellow was staring at him for.

Noticing his own lapse in composure, Merlin gave a slight smile. "How have things been in the imperial capital lately? From the looks of you two, it seems you've gone through quite a storm."

"Chaotic, just chaotic. I heard the long-reigning queen is actually Princess Isabella, who's been impersonating Queen Elizabeth to rule the empire. But the real Queen Elizabeth has already been found and is dealing with troubles in the north." The old man sighed helplessly and continued, "But the armies of Awfre are unstoppable at the moment. The queen probably can't hold them off. Many people have been forced to flee their homes and take refuge elsewhere."

"I see..." Merlin nodded, stroking his chin and thinking that indeed, things were becoming increasingly chaotic. That water demon he had defeated seemed to have been the empire's last ace in the hole.

Alice came out of the house, her arms full of things — bread, fruit, and a bag of goat's milk.

"Eat up."

Alice handed the bread and goat's milk to the old man, letting them divide it among themselves. After all, the little boy looked quite young and would need some milk to supplement his nutrition.

"Thank you. Thank you for your kind charity. May the Goddess's holy light always shelter you and grant you her greatest blessings." The old man's eyes welled with tears as he expressed his gratitude, taking the food with both hands.

"It's nothing precious, no need to be so formal." Alice responded awkwardly.

"No, no, no! All food is a gift from the Goddess of Light. The fact that you're willing to share it with us proves that you are a kind person." The old man couldn't stop praising her, his expression full of tearful gratitude.

Alice offered a polite smile and thought that this old man must be a follower of the Goddess of Light, otherwise he wouldn't keep mentioning her nonstop.

She took out an apple, wiped it on her clothes, and handed it to the somewhat shy little boy.

"Go ahead and eat. No need to be so formal with your elder sister."

The little boy hesitated for a moment, glanced at his grandfather as if seeking permission.

Seeing his grandfather's affirmative gaze, he dared to take the apple and said gratefully,

"Th-thank you, big sister..."

Watching Alice, Merlin felt a warm sensation welling up inside him — the kind of feeling that made one want to draw close without resistance.

If someone said Alice was a goddess right now, he supposed some people might actually believe it.

"So... do you know what's happening at the front lines?" Alice asked curiously, quite interested in the state of the war.

"Terrible. The kingdom's army was defeated right from the start, and they can only rely on private armies from local lords to resist. But the tide is still overwhelmingly one-sided. It's only a matter of time before they reach the imperial capital." The old man said with a deeply pessimistic expression.

"..." Alice furrowed her delicate brows and muttered softly, "Arnold went to reinforce the front lines too... I wonder how he's doing..."

"Oh wow, so you do worry about Arnold after all. You fickle woman, hehe~" Merlin couldn't help but tease.

"That's not it! Arnold is our colleague after all. I'm just normally concerned about him." Alice retorted seriously.

"Right..." Merlin scratched his head and furrowed his brows, thinking:

That pushover Arnold, with combat power of all of five.

Who the hell knew what that guy was going through at the front lines?

At worst, he'd already died to some unknown AOE attack...

Northern Scotland.

The Awfre Coalition Corps was engaged in battle with the private army of the Austin family.

The Coalition Corps was unstoppable, crushing everything in their path in an almost unimpeded advance.

After the kingdom's army was defeated, no private army from any local lord had been able to stop the Coalition Corps. Quite a few nobleprivate forces had already been completely annihilated!

At this point, the Black Knights of the Coalition Corps had already reached the gateway into imperial territory. Pressing further would directly threaten the royal capital.

However, the Austin family's strength was not great, appearing extremely insignificant beneath the iron hooves of the Coalition Corps.

Arnold had come to fight in place of his father, but the cowardly fellow had long since been scared half to death, trembling on his mount.

Gazing at the vast dark mass of elite cavalry opposite, Arnold was at a loss, having absolutely no idea how to respond.

In truth, Arnold had originally thought that coming to the front was just a formality, that he wouldn't actually have to fight.

But the kingdom's army was defeated in an instant, and the unfortunate Arnold was forced to stand there bravely.

The officer assisting Arnold in command had already been shot through the throat by an arrow barrage and died gruesomely on the spot.

Even the soldiers sent out to scout never returned — some were hacked to death by enemies, others devoured by magical beasts.

The Austin family's army was like prey being slowly consumed by a serpent, bit by bit. Now only heavily armored bodyguards remained.

Looking at the black press of the Coalition army opposite, Arnold felt his liver trembling with fear and really wanted to wheel his horse around and flee.

The disparity in strength between friend and foe was too great. Look at their army's composition, then look at his own — what was there to fight?! Run!

But many soldiers were watching Arnold, preventing him from fleeing at will.

Although Arnold was the foolish son of a wealthy landlord, he was at this moment the backbone of the soldiers.

If Arnold was so terrified that he ran away, it would be a severe blow to his family and bring shame upon his father.

"Lord Arnold! What do we do now?! The enemy's numbers are too strong! Those magical beasts alone are incredibly difficult to handle, and our entire vanguard is dead!" A soldier who had fought through countless battles came to report, an arrow shaft protruding from his shoulder — clearly gravely wounded.

A layer of cold sweat seeped out on Arnold's forehead. What should he do? How should I know?! Is it too late to say now that he was just here as a figurehead?

The sky was gloomy, dark clouds slowly churning, and beast-like roars occasionally rang out from the opposite side.

The Austin family was already at its last gasp. Facing such a formidable army of a hundred thousand, they were as insignificant as ants!

"Lord Arnold, we—"

The soldier's words were cut off mid-sentence by a deafening explosion!

A massive stone flew through the sky and came straight at Arnold.

Bang! A large crater was smashed into the ground, and Arnold's mount was knocked down on the spot, letting out a piercing neigh!

"Ai ai ai!" Arnold cried out in a panic, tumbling headfirst to the ground with a mouthful of mud.

"My lord! My lord!"

A group of soldiers ran over to help Arnold up. If he died, the entire army would scatter and flee.

"Cough! Cough!" Arnold kept coughing, spitting out the mud from his mouth, and said with a doleful face, "Who the hell was that?! Why do their catapults seem to have eyes?!"

Hardly had those words left his mouth when chaos erupted in the front of the army, with cries of shock ringing out nonstop, as though they had seen something terrible.

"Heavenly—!"

"That... that's the Black Wolf Mercenary Group!"

"It's the Black Wolf Mercenary Group charging at us!"

title: Chapter 11 — Top Secret
content:
Chapter 11 — Top Secret

Volume 12 · Chapter 11

Arnold's face drained of color the moment he heard the name "Black Wolf Mercenary Group," and his body began to tremble.

Arnold hadn't known much about the Black Wolf Mercenaries before, but he had certainly heard plenty of rumors along the way!

Many lords' private armies had encountered this group of five, and their fates were all the same — slaughtered down to the last man!

Arnold never imagined that his family's tiny faction would run into such a terrifying opponent. It was as if the God of Death himself had set his sights on them!

Although the enemy was merely a five-person squad, every member was a Saint-tier powerhouse. In a charge, they were far more terrifying than any beast legion!

Arnold had long heard that the Black Wolf Mercenaries were ruthless bastards who showed no mercy to their enemies and fought with extremely cruel methods!

Now that his family's private army was nearly wiped out, the allied forces had no need to send their main army. Instead, they dispatched mercenary groups to clean up the battlefield and strangle the remnants of House Austin to death!

Gazing at the panicked, churning crowd ahead, Arnold's heart trembled uncontrollably. He found his own legs unable to move, frozen by fear.

"AHHHHHHHHH!"

A blood-curdling scream suddenly erupted. The heavily armored knights at the front, who had been used to shield against the rain of arrows, were smashed apart by heavy shields and sent flying in every direction!

Sparks flew, and the screeching sound of metal colliding was as震撼ating as an explosion!

A single sweep of the massive axe raised waves of bloody carnage, shearing dozens of the frontmost soldiers cleanly in half!

A burly knight wielding a巨斧 and a heavy shield charged into the crowd. He was clad in gray armor that encased his entire body. If one looked closely, one might mistake him for a steel-armored beast!

The sudden appearance of such a powerful fighter filled the soldiers with terror. Many were so frightened they couldn't even speak!

Corpses littered the ground, which only added to the terrifying presence of the axe-and-shield knight. No one dared approach to challenge his power!

His height of nearly three meters was striking. In a daze, the soldiers half-believed they were facing an iron little giant!

Under the pressure, everyone began to retreat, occasionally letting out panicked shouts of his name —

"....Hall!"

"It's the humanoid chariot Hall!"

"Run! Run away!!!'"

Hall was the knight in the Black Wolf Mercenary Group renowned for his defense, providing the team with its strongest protection!

Legend held that Hall had been raised by the Beastman tribe. He had a vicious temper, was bloodthirsty by nature, and many of his behaviors were utterly incompatible with humanity.

However, due to his extraordinary physique, he had once participated in the Holy Church's Eastern Crusade. His ruthless attacks earned him a fearsome reputation, and he was hailed as an unstoppable humanoid chariot!

Later, his barbaric habits led to his expulsion from the Holy Church army, and he was taken in by the commander of the Black Wolf Mercenaries, becoming a member of the group.

"Hehehe, where are you running? Come play with me!"

Hall roared, swinging his巨斧 and slaughtering the soldiers before him without mercy. The sight of blood spraying everywhere made hearts race with terror!

With a "swish" of splitting air, a pitch-black feathered arrow shot in from an extremely tricky angle!

After piercing one soldier's throat, it didn't stop. It continued through dozens of warriors' vital areas with plop, plop, plop sounds.

With just a single arrow, he achieved the effect of skewering meatballs on a stick. The skill was nothing short of admirable!

On a distant rock stood a female dark elf wearing leather armor. She had a slender figure and wore a red scarf around her neck, making her look strikingly heroic.

The dark elf was named Dorin. She was an elf who had turned away from her tribe. Having lost her faith, she became recklessly uninhibited and took up the life of a wandering ranger, eventually being recruited by the mercenary group.

Dorin's skills were superb, and with the blessing of her elf heritage, she could easily kill her enemies with ease.

"How boring..."

Dorin lowered her longbow and adjusted her scarf, apparently not very interested in the one-sided slaughter.

On the other side, a black shadow suddenly emerged from the shadows behind the army's rear ranks. A man in a black robe, his face covered, grinned wickedly.

"Hall, don't just have all the fun by yourself. Take me along, heh heh heh..."

With a flick of the dagger in his hand, a brilliant mist of blood erupted from the center of the soldiers. His precise killing method left the soldiers no time to react before they met their gruesome deaths.

This sudden thief was also a member of the Black Wolf Mercenary Group, named Nedam. He was originally an elite assassin trained by the Eastern Ptolemaic Dynasty. After learning too many secrets, he was hunted and fled to Britain.

His strength was formidable, and prey marked by him rarely escaped death. Nedam's assassination techniques were hard for enemies to detect, and his secret arts lurking within shadows greatly enhanced his power.

Often, by the time a target felt a chill at the nape of their neck, they were already dead.

Dark clouds rolled across the sky, gradually forming a vortex. A faint gleam of light flashed from within the deep black hole.

Instantly, ten thousand bolts of thunder shot out from the depths of the vortex, with crackling explosions ringing continuously.

The lightning streaked like a laser beam from the front all the way to the rear of House Austin's forces. Blood-curdling screams echoed everywhere, and scenes of utter horror could be seen at every turn.

Wherever the lightning passed, the land appeared scorched by flames, and deep gullows were carved into the earth.

On a distant mountain peak, a white-haired mage lowered his staff and ceased his devastating thunder barrage.

This mage who commanded thunder was named Cuton. In terms of destructive power, his magic was the strongest in the Black Wolf Mercenary Group!

Cuton didn't have any particularly remarkable past. He was simply a veteran member of the mercenary group and an old friend of the commander, Kazayeg.

The two had graduated from the same magic academy and were close companions who had jointly founded the elite-focused Black Wolf Mercenary Group.

A slight sneer appeared on Cuton's aged face as he casually evaluated, "What unit is this? They're weaker than anything we've encountered before. At least before, we could find some decent fighters. Here, there are only some rabble."

"You're right. They really are too weak. Perhaps they're just some ignorant nobles sending people to make up the numbers..."

This voice sounded somewhat raspy, making one feel slightly uncomfortable.

This person was the commander of the Black Wolf Mercenary Group, Kazayeg. He was one of the main combat forces hired by Grand Duke Oliver.

Kazayeg appeared even older than Cuton and was a disabled man. He held a staff and observed the battle from a wheelchair.

His entire body was wrapped in thick black robes, making his appearance impossible to discern, rendering him extremely mysterious.

Facing such weak troops, there was simply no need for Kazayeg to lift a finger, so he could only sit quietly and watch the battle.

"Is the Grand Duke looking down on us? Making us do nothing but cleanup work is truly unpleasant..." Cuton stroked his beard, his eyes revealing severe dissatisfaction.

"There's no need to worry about such things. In fact, we play an extremely important role in Grand Duke Oliver's plan..." Kazayeg paused, speaking in a mysterious tone.

"In fact, I've already received the Grand Duke's top-secret mission."

"As long as we complete it successfully, our mercenary group will become the greatest contributors."

"At that time, both power and wealth will be within our grasp..."

title: Chapter 12 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 12 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 12 · Chapter 12

"A top-secret mission?" Kerton frowned in confusion, having never heard of such a thing.

"That's right, but I can't go into the details now. You'll know when the time comes." Kasyeager said with a gloomy smile.

"If you have no objections, then that's good. We're just mercenaries who do the job for money. Don't fall into some trap and become cannon fodder for Duke Olfrey." Kerton warned Kasyeager.

"Don't worry. My calculations are clearer than anyone else's. It's us who'll be using Duke Olfrey, not the other way around." Kasyeager paused and continued, "Besides, we're only taking what we need. Who would be stupid enough to sell their life to the duke?"

"That's true. If there weren't enough profit to drive us, who would side with the duke?" Kerton sneered.

"You seem to have quite a grievance against Duke Olfrey?" Kasyeager asked in a hoarse voice.

"Not that big. I just don't want our mercenary squad to become a mere backdrop under the duke's command, with all the benefits going to those four Sword Saints." Kerton's tone carried a hint of dissatisfaction. He felt irritated just thinking about the four mysterious figures standing behind Duke Olfrey.

"I see..." Kasyeager nodded, slightly understanding Kerton's thoughts.
