After all, the four who were hailed as the Elemental Sword Saints were Duke Olfrey's trump cards, so it was only natural that they received higher treatment.

Even Duke Olfrey's attitude when speaking to the four Sword Saints was different, seeming somewhat reverent.

Looking at it this way, the Black Wolf Mercenary Squad did seem somewhat like a mere supporting act, far inferior in status to the Elemental Four Sword Saints, even bordering on being mere foot soldiers.

"You can probably see it too. Duke Olfrey treats the Elemental Four Sword Saints like deities, while to us, he seems to treat us no better than temporary workers." Kerton's deeply wrinkled face overflowed with anger. He felt he hadn't received the respect he deserved from the duke.

"Don't worry about these issues. In fact, although Duke Olfrey's attitude toward us is merely so-so, the compensation he gives us far outclasses the Elemental Four Sword Saints by several streets." Kasyeager said with certainty.

"Why are you so sure?" Kerton asked curiously, growing more puzzled about that top-secret mission.

"I can't say yet for now. You'll know when the time comes. As long as we complete this secret mission, the benefits our mercenary squad will gain will be unprecedented! Even if we have to risk our lives for that old man Olfrey, it'll be well worth it." Kasyeager spoke with great conviction. What had Duke Olfrey promised him? That he would sell his life so unwaveringly.

Kerton didn't speak and chose silence, because the leader of the mercenary squad was Kasyeager, and their decisions had never had any major problems. Perhaps they had truly picked up a big business deal after all.

"Moreover, the reason Duke Olfrey treats the Elemental Four Sword Saints with such respect is perfectly normal. There's no need for you to feel strange about it." Kasyeager gazed into the distance and said in a leisurely tone, "The strong deserve preferential treatment, after all."

"How strong are the Elemental Four Sword Saints? Did you test them?" Kerton furrowed his brows. He hadn't yet investigated the four Sword Saints' strength specifically.

"Very strong. They're on a completely different level from us. Even if our entire mercenary squad fought together, we still couldn't defeat any single one of them." Kasyeager spoke seriously, wanting Kerton to face reality.

"No way?! That exaggerated?!" Kerton felt a wave of terror surge through his heart.

"I was once dissatisfied with the duke's differential treatment just like you. Then I placed a curse on the Elemental Four Sword Saints, wanting to test their reactions, but it was forcibly dispelled in an instant. Their strength is simply not to be underestimated." Kasyeager said in a low voice.

Kerton instantly sucked in a cold breath. Kasyeager was a Dark Priest! Especially skilled in all sorts of vicious curses. Usually a single curse spell could at best make the target instantly lose their combat ability, and at worst kill them on the spot, even if the target was a Saint-tier expert!

Yet the Elemental Four Sword Saints could dispel the curse instantly. If they weren't relying on items to forcibly break free, then their strength needed serious study.

Kerton knew Kasyeager's strength very well. Anyone who could break free from his curse would undoubtedly far surpass him!

Thinking about this, Kerton couldn't help but feel cold sweat trickling down his back. He somewhat understood Duke Olfrey's attitude toward the Elemental Four Sword Saints.

The chaotic battlefield, with killing shouts shaking the heavens!

Soldiers of the Austin family fell in droves into pools of blood, completely unable to withstand the ferocious attacks of the enemy.

Hall, Doreen, and Nedham — just the three of them were enough to make the soldiers completely unable to fight back. It was almost like playing a grass-cutting game.

Those heavily armored knights were turned into mush in an instant by the Black Wolf Mercenary Squad's sweeping attacks, utterly incapable of withstanding even a single blow.

Arnold watched his own troops fall one after another, his face turning deathly pale. He felt that if he didn't surrender, he'd hardly escape death himself.

Blood sprayed everywhere before his eyes. Screams filled the air, and a desolate scene unfolded all around.

Arnold had thought he was facing the main forces of the Olfrey family, but the truth was otherwise.

The enemies he faced were merely a small branch of the United Legion.

The main combat forces of the Olfrey family were still en route here. These troops before him were, at most, the vanguard.

But even this small vanguard was more than enough to crush Arnold's private army.

Arnold decided to throw in the towel. He scooped up a handful of mud and smeared it messily across his face.

Then he promptly pulled out a feather arrow stuck in the ground beside him and jammed it into his armor, pretending to be an arrow wound.

Finally, Arnold "splattered" onto the ground and lay completely motionless, beginning his long act of playing dead. Countless fleeing soldiers trampled over his body, but he stubbornly kept his mouth shut.

Can't see me~ can't see me~ can't see me~

Meanwhile, on the other side.

The assassination squad dispatched by the queen had already set out.

The assassination squad was drawn from the Crimson Cherry Blossom Knight Order, numbering a full 3,000 soldiers.

Such a nearly suicidal assassination operation was unsuitable for a large-scale troop deployment.

But 3,000 Crimson Cherry Blossom Knights was already a considerable force, and every single one was an imperial elite who obeyed orders without question.

The assassination squad split into two groups, led by Meriuss and Winifred, launching their operations in two separate forces.

The two groups flanked from different routes, avoiding direct confrontation with the main Olfrey force.

They had agreed to rendezvous on the plain the United Legion had marched across, consolidating their strength there.

If the plan went smoothly, the assembled assassination squad would be positioned behind the United Legion, which would be far more advantageous for carrying out the assassination.

At this moment, Winifred had already arrived at the agreed-upon plain, but the plan didn't seem to be going smoothly at all.

The ground was piled high with the corpses of Crimson Cherry Blossom Knights. Broken spears, many severed clean through, and shattered swords were sticking out everywhere.

A force of 1,500 men — it seemed they had been wiped out by a single person?!

The blood of countless knights flowed across the ground, eventually converging into streams, making the scene even more gruesome.

Winifred stood upon the battlefield, his armor shattered beyond recognition, his crimson cherry blossom cloak torn to tatters.

His arms had been severed, leaving clean cuts. Dark red blood trickled slowly from the stumps, making him look like a human stick.

Winifred's face was deathly pale. Cold sweat rolled down his forehead, and his expression was utterly numb.

Even though every wound on his body throbbed with excruciating pain, all he could feel was numbness. This was evident from his terrified and blank eyes.

Opposite Winifred stood a mysterious figure in black robes, silent and unmoving, with no discernible aura.

The sword in the mysterious figure's hand was particularly bizarre — it glowed emerald green, looking as though someone was holding an entire jade gemstone.

He raised the gemstone sword, and a powerful Saint-tier pressure immediately surged upward, allowing everyone to clearly sense strength at the peak of the Saint tier.

Rune characters instantly lit up and slowly wriggled across the gemstone sword, and suddenly fierce winds erupted!

The mysterious figure casually swung his sword. Winifred's head was cleanly severed, flying high into the air.

Thorn Order's Eleventh Knight, Winifred, has fallen.

title: Chapter 13 — Close Friend
content:
Chapter 13 — Close Friend

Volume 12 · Chapter 13

The red sun on the horizon gave a gentle leap and rose above it.

The plain was covered in corpses, sunlight shining upon the blood-stained earth.

Only one headless corpse stood in the center, its blood obviously having dried up completely.

Winifred had already fallen in battle. He hadn't expected the enemy to have set an ambush, waiting for them to walk right into it.

That man wielding the emerald gem sword was far too powerful for Winifred to handle.

By himself, he had wiped out the Jacinth Knight Order, and it hadn't even required much effort.

Although the enemy had anticipated the queen would launch a surprise attack, they did not know that the assassination squad was splitting into two groups.

By the time Millius arrived here with the other team, he found a desolate, gruesome scene everywhere.

The Jacinth knights gazed at the corpses covering the ground in shock, having no idea what had happened.

This mission had been a secret. How could anyone possibly know about it? It must have been the enemy who calculated it.

"What happened..."

A bead of cold sweat trickled down Millius's forehead, and he felt this mission had become impossibly difficult.

He looked around and spotted the headless corpse standing in the middle of the battlefield, his expression freezing.

Even without a head, Millius could still recognize who it was. The tattered Jacinth battle armor had already revealed everything.

Millius's expression grew troubled, his brows knitted together, and a wave of sorrow rose in his heart.

As close friends who had grown up together in the same orphanage, seeing this sight made Millius deeply unsettled.

He knew Winifred's strength well, and considering how things had ended, one could imagine just how powerful the enemy was.

Millius walked over to Winifred's corpse and picked up the spellbook from the ground, brushing off the dust.

"Winifred, what have you been through..."

"Lord Millius! There's... there's another survivor here!" A knight shouted loudly.

Millius's eyes widened. He stowed away Winifred's spellbook and turned toward the voice.

Chapman, the captain of this lucky Jacinth knight squad, had survived as the sole survivor.

However, he had been gravely wounded in combat with the enemy. His face was pale, and he looked like he was on his last breath.

Chapman was helped upright by several knights and only managed to catch his breath after drinking some water.

"What happened here? Why are all the people dead?" Millius asked in a rather urgent tone.

"What happened here was that mysterious man..." Chapman paused before continuing, "Lord Winifred did his utmost but still couldn't defeat that guy. His expression grew somewhat dazed. 'Wind Sword Saint? Who is that? I've never even heard of him!'

Millius's gaze trembled. The mysterious man's strength was incredibly formidable, not only sweeping away our entire force with a single strike but also shattering Lord Winifred's magic with one slash.

"I'm not... not entirely sure, but that unimaginable enemy might also be hiding such terrifying abilities..." Chapman said with a panicked expression. This information would interfere with the current assassination plan. With such a powerful person guarding the other side, what exactly should they do now?

Millius fell silent, then raised his head and asked through the severe pain in his body, "What should we do now? Lord Millius..." Chapman looked toward Winifred's headless corpse, lost in thought for a moment. "Regarding this assassination mission... should we continue?"

Millius didn't speak but instead gazed at Winifred's headless body, drifting into memories.

He and Winifred were both orphans, adopted by an orphanage in a certain small town.

Millius had been calm since childhood while Winifred was hot-tempered.

Their personalities were completely opposite, yet somehow they became friends, which was quite perplexing to outsiders.

The most punished child at the orphanage, someone others disliked.

Millius used to get beaten by the nuns whenever he stole beef.

That afternoon, young Millius was lying face-down on a bed covered with straw matting, determined to confirm all the children were settled before leaving.

Outside, the nun carried an oil lamp for her patrol. As soon as she passed, Millius secretly lit his lamp and began flipping through a cheap basic magic textbook.

His injuries didn't bother young Winifred as he groaned, cursing under his breath, "That terrible old nun. She must be going through menopause. Always taking her anger out on me."

"Eating beef — that was everyone's rations." Winifred responded faintly.

"You can't blame others. You were the one who wanted to eat meat. Did you think it was all yours? The bold die fat, the cowardly die hungry!" Millius gritted his teeth and retorted angrily.

"Shut up! You nerd," Winifred responded indifferently, seemingly unwilling to say more.

"Is that so." Millius seemed somewhat dissatisfied with Winifred's reaction. "What are you reading? You'll get beaten if the old nun catches you."

"An introductory magic book," Millius replied faintly.

"Oh~ so diligent, huh? A few days ago, a Jacinth knight came and said that someone with talent like mine would find it easy. But most people, like me, have average talent. Becoming a Jacinth knight isn't difficult at all." Millius smiled wryly. "Don't make it sound so simple. You're talented. If I don't work a little harder, I won't have any chance at all."

Winifred showed a hint of bitterness. "You want to become a thorn knight so badly... What's the point of becoming a thorn knight?"

"To become someone respected by everyone, and so no one dares to bully me freely."

"You wouldn't be as shallow as me, right? Just to escape this damn place."

"I'm not as shallow as you," Winifred retorted impatiently.

"And then?" Millius looked at his companion but couldn't figure it out.

"So I want to protect this place. After becoming a thorn knight, I want to change the harsh living conditions here so every child can eat their fill and stay warm, and become an example for them, letting them know that even orphanage kids can achieve greatness in the future." Winifred said with determined eyes.

Millius couldn't help but quietly avert his gaze and muttered under his breath: "Your home, huh?"

"That's pretty boring."

title: Chapter 14 — Monthly Ticket + Updates
content:
Chapter 14 — Monthly Ticket + Updates

Volume 12 · Chapter 14

"Mirius...

Chapman noticed Mirius was somewhat distracted and couldn't help but remind him.

The situation is critical now; we need to make a decision immediately, and once we're full, it won't be easy to handle.

Mirius put away his thoughts and stopped looking at Vinnifred's headless corpse.

He scanned the area and saw all the knights watching him, waiting for his decision.

Mirius took a deep breath, and it seemed he had already reached a conclusion.

"Everyone return to the capital. Don't continue this assassination mission..."

Mirius issued the order to abandon the mission. It had to be said, this was a wise choice.

Now that Vinnifred has fallen, it would be very difficult for Mirius alone to carry out the assassination.

Moreover, the opponent known as the Sword Saint is very powerful, and Mirius didn't feel confident either. He couldn't let the others continue to die for nothing.

Upon hearing Mirius's decision, many of them sighed with relief, thinking they no longer had to fight to the death.

But before Mirius finished speaking, he added another sentence.

"You return to the capital, and tell Her Majesty the Queen that I may never come back."

"Eh?!

This statement caused many knights to be startled, feeling a hint of melancholy in his words.

"Lord Mirius! ...What do you mean?!

"Mirius declared firmly, 'I will act alone and continue this assassination mission. If I succeed, I will achieve glory and honor; if I fail, I will die in the attempt.'

"Come on, calm down!" Chapman was alarmed and quickly tried to persuade him, "Lord Vinnifred has already fallen, our assassination team's strength has been greatly diminished, and the enemy still has mysterious experts guarding them. It's already very unsuitable to continue this secret mission. Even Her Majesty the Queen would surely understand this point and would not agree to your reckless action!"

"This is my own decision, and has nothing to do with anyone else." Mirius's tone showed no hesitation, having already made up his mind.

"Then..." Chapman lowered his head, clenched his fists, gritted his teeth and slowly stood up, "If Lord Mirius insists on continuing the assassination mission, then I shall follow you!"

"I want to go too!"

"I can go as well!"

"......

The time passed, and many knights stood up, wanting to accompany Mirius to the front, with an atmosphere of intense emotion in the air.

Mirius looked at the knights before him and felt that it wasn't necessary to bring these people along to die.

Moreover, the initial plan was to take these people for a diversion, creating an opportunity to assassinate Duke Overre.

Now that the team has been wiped out and Vinnifred is dead, this strategy was obviously no longer viable.

"No, you're all just weaklings of various levels.

Just you wanting to come with me? What a joke!

Take a good look in the mirror, you'll only hold me back and won't be of any help.

It's obviously more convenient for me to act alone. I prefer to fight solo, which allows me to use my fists without any restraint.

So you should all just go back obediently and not cause me trouble. Let my loyalty to you be fulfilled by me alone.

Farewell, foolish knights."

Mirius turned away without looking back and started moving toward the coalition forces, intending to enter the enemy's territory alone.

"Mirius...

Chapman's expression was tinged with sorrow and anger, his eyes even reddening.

Even a fool could see that Mirius was going to make a desperate last stand alone, possibly never returning.

Although many knights wanted to follow Mirius, they were deeply affected by his words and felt completely discouraged, unable to take a step forward.

Despite being elite knights of the Purple City Flower, they still had a long way to go before reaching the Saint-tier. Even if they followed, they would only be a burden to Mirius. It was better to stay behind and defend the last line of the capital.

The red sun leaped out from the morning mist, and the golden light illuminated the plain.

The wind, like an invisible giant hand, lifted the sand and stones, making it hard to see.

All the knights watched Mirius's retreating figure, bidding him farewell. This might be the last time.

The red light fell upon Mirius's body, adding to the melancholy of the lone hero.

Mirius stopped in front of Vinnifred's body, took off his red Purple City Flower battle robe, and draped it over the corpse, concealing the headless remains.

"Although you're quite boring...

But I still respect you.

Coalition Forces Camp.

At this point, the time had already entered the evening.

It only takes two or three days to reach the capital.

By then, we will surround the royal city and force Queen Elizabeth to step down.

At this moment, in the luxurious tent, a grand feast was being held to reward the meritorious.

On both sides of the hall, two long tables covered with silk were arranged neatly, filled with exquisite appetizers and expensive wine.

Duke Overre sat in the main seat, his face red and healthy, looking quite happy because things were going so smoothly, making him seem younger.

The advisor Gabriel stood respectfully beside the duke, holding a wine bottle and occasionally glancing up to observe the situation.

At the end of the dining table sat four mysterious figures, all wrapped in black robes, their faces hidden from view.

These four were the famous Elemental Four Sword Saints, with extraordinary sword skills and mastery over fire, earth, water, and wind elements. Their combat power was astonishing, and they were Overre's trump card, not to be used unless absolutely necessary.

There's no need to introduce the Elemental Four Sword Saints' strength. They were once even boastful about being able to kill the First Demon Lord Palace.

"Elizabeth, that cunning woman, actually sent the Thorn Knights to assassinate me! If it weren't for Gabriel's foresight, we would have suffered considerable trouble." Duke Overre praised his subordinate with a sentence.

"Not at all, it's my honor to share your burdens, Lord Duke." Gabriel wore a smile and then said, "The real heroes are the four Sword Saints. They are the greatest contributors."

"That's right, right. We should thank the four elders..." Duke Overre raised his wine cup and spoke sincerely, "This time's trouble, thank you all for your great help. As long as I become the new emperor of the empire, I won't forget to reward you all."

Fire Sword Saint: "I just like people like you, Lord Duke, who are so decisive! But we only helped you because of our past friendship, not for any trivial benefits!"

Earth Sword Saint: "That's right. If the Duke thinks we came out of the chaos sea just for benefits, that's really underestimating us."

"Oops, Duke Overre felt awkward, a drop of cold sweat slid down his forehead, 'I'm sorry, I was too impulsive. I forgot our past friendship. How can such feelings be measured by money?'

"Right, the Duke and the four Sword Saints have a lasting friendship, hehe~" Gabriel wore a smile and added, "But this time, eliminating the empire's assassination team, we should especially thank the Wind Sword Saint. Without him, we wouldn't have resolved this so quickly."

Wind Sword Saint: "It's nothing big. The opponents weren't very strong, probably just at the level of a regular Saint-tier."

"...A Saint-tier? Duke Overre's expression became unnatural. He thought, 'No matter what, they are Thorn Knights, but to the four Sword Saints, they seem too weak, which explains why he said it so casually.'

Water Sword Saint: "Please rest assured, Lord Duke. As long as we are here, no one in the entire empire can stop your path to the throne. Even if you mention the Lake Fairy, we can still fight it. After all, we have fought against the demon race rulers before."

"With you here, I can rest easy." Duke Overre nodded, smiling broadly and raised his wine cup, "Come, let's toast to friendship!

A sudden explosion erupted, and Mirius, dressed in silver armor, descended from the sky, directly landing on the dining table.

The grand banquet instantly turned into chaos, with wine and food splashed all over the floor, cups and plates scattered everywhere.

Mirius scanned the area, not recognizing anyone, but recognizing the Duke Overre holding his wine cup was enough.

He slowly drew the sword at his waist, stood arrogantly on the dining table, and looked down at everyone.

"I've arrived just in time, haven't I?

Such a grand feast, it's a shame to miss it."

title: Chapter 15 — Obsession
content:
Chapter 15 — Obsession

Volume 12 · Chapter 15

At the banquet, an unexpected guest suddenly appeared, shocking everyone present.

This was the main base of the Allied Legion! How did this guy sneak in?!

This question deeply lingered in Duke Auster's mind. He never dreamed a Thorn Knight would raid in at a time like this!

The Elemental Four Sword Saints watched Milenius standing on the dining table, acting recklessly. None of them moved; they probably hadn't reacted yet!

"...The Sixth Thorn Knight, Milenius!"

Duke Auster had seen Milenius before. He cried out in shock, his face contorted with fear, his wrinkled skin creasing together.

"Oh?" Milenius tilted the corner of his mouth. "You still recognize me, old man."

Duke Auster's eyes filled with unease. He thought: Did the Queen send two Thorn Knights?!

Killed one, and there's still one more! Doesn't the Queen fear heavy losses?!

According to intelligence, there are only five Thorn Knights left beside the Queen. That's quite few.

Sending two to carry out an assassination—if they fail, how can the Queen fight against my army?!

Duke Auster couldn't understand at all. He felt Queen Elizabeth was betting too heavily.

Actually, Elizabeth knew this too. But the situation at hand was like breaking the cauldrons and sinking the boats—if she didn't fight, she probably couldn't withstand the Allied Legion's advance either.

Beside him, the staff officer Gabriel finally snapped back to reality. Relying on the presence of the Elemental Four Sword Saints, he threatened, "Hmph! How dare you—"

"Shout for mercy! Who do you think you are?" Milenius glared at Gabriel, releasing his killing intent without restraint. Gabriel's mind went blank. He couldn't resist the fierce killing intent, shivered, and fell to the ground. Goosebumps covered his entire body. He dared not speak another word.

Milenius didn't bother with a small fry like Gabriel. He pointed his sword directly at Duke Auster. "Next, I'll take your life!" "...My life!"

Duke Auster was too old to withstand such a scare at close range. His legs trembled so badly he could only shake on his chair.

"Run!" the Sword Saint:

"Easy to say!"

"He doesn't take us seriously!" the Sword Saint: "Want to touch the Duke? Ask us if we agree first!" the Sword Saint: "Such suicidal behavior is boring. Several of you! Kill him! Leave no survivors!!!"

Duke Auster cried out in panic. "The Four Sword Saints are still here! How dare a mere Thorn Knight... be so brazen here!"

Gabriel hid at the back, opening his mouth to speak.

Milenius's golden aura suddenly erupted, his pressure like waves crashing around them. The candles instantly went out. The Great Sword Saint: "Foolish child, think carefully. If you dare to move even a little, we'll kill you right here. Don't believe me, try it."

"Say whatever you want. I love a challenge." The moment the words fell, Milenius moved like lightning. His flowing golden hair added elegance to his sword technique.

The Elemental Four Sword Saints didn't bluff. As Milenius moved, all four struck at once. They drew their bizarre gem-encrusted swords, each a different color, and slashed at Milenius!

A deafening explosion shook the surroundings. The long dining table shattered instantly, and the solid floor was cracked. The combined attack of the Sword Saints was terrifyingly powerful, yet Milenius vanished in the blink of an eye before their strikes landed!

"So fast!" The Sword Saints cried out in unison, shocked. They hadn't expected Milenius's speed to be so astonishing, underestimating the man's strength. At that moment, Milenius had already appeared before Duke Auster in an instant. The oppressive pressure was like a death omen!

"Help!" Duke Auster turned pale. Milenius held nothing back, immediately using his ultimate sword technique—"Meteorite Fall." The sword was the culmination of Milenius's years of training, all power concentrated in a single point, a killing blow!

Milenius's sword technique was inherited from an old knight captain of a certain knight order, with power converging at the tip. The destructive force of that thrust could tear through stars!

Milenius reached Duke Auster. Golden Saint-tier aura gathered on the blade, faintly forming a—telephone? He thrust suddenly!

"Fatal—" Duke Auster cried out. The pendant around his neck suddenly blazed with intense light, forming three layers of magic shields. The pendant was no ordinary item—it was a gift from the Four Sword Saints to Duke Auster, an ultra-rare magic defense artifact!

This magic defense artifact came from the mysterious Chaos Sea, said to easily block attacks from Saint-tier powerhouses, even Ultimate Magic. Extremely rare.

Could block... but the three layers of magic shields were shattered two in a row by Milenius's Meteorite Fall! The last one also developed cracks under the relentless assault!

"...No!" Duke Auster watched the magic shield shatter, his face contorted in terror. Gabriel beside him was also too panicked to speak, crawling to hide at the back. His eyelids flickered as the violent aura crashed against the barrier. The last magic shield was pierced through by Milenius, his thin sword slowly entering and piercing into Duke Auster's chest.

"Die! You damn thing!!!" Milenius's face was full of rage. He was about to succeed, piercing through Duke Auster's heart!

"Ahhhhh!" Duke Auster's eyes bulged. He could already feel the thin sword cutting through his breastbone. Pain beyond despair!

At that moment, the Four Sword Saints rushed in, their gem swords swinging together, cutting Milenius's body into four pieces from behind! The whole Milenius instantly became a limbless torso, blood spraying, the scene horrific!

Milenius fell through the air, his eyes vacant, his body no longer obeying him. Before his eyes, his sword slowly rotated—memories of becoming a Thorn Knight with Vernonfred... years ago, the eleventh knight's mansion...

"Vernonfred, let's go to the imperial capital merchant guild's banquet tonight!" Milenius leaned against the door, his tone flirtatious. "We're newly made Thorn Knights, with high status. Those important figures will surely welcome us~"

"No, I'm not going." Vernonfred held a feather pen, writing furiously at his desk. "What? Are you kidding? This is our chance to mingle with important people. Don't waste it."

Milenius paused, then continued. "And we can boost our prestige this way. Guys like me—handsome and strong—are in high demand among those circles. We might even meet delicate noble ladies who faint at the drop of a hat~"

"A group of women? I can't handle that." Vernonfred replied calmly, seemingly unaffected.

"Tsk!" Milenius felt somewhat displeased. He asked seriously, "What are you busy with?" "Writing replies to the children at the orphanage. Must reply seriously."

Vernonfred answered. "How many?" "Almost 100." Milenius's forehead beaded with cold sweat. Replying to 100 letters from kids—what a workload. "Forget those boring things. Come to the banquet with me and have fun."

"Forget it. I can't even afford the entry fee." Vernonfred showed a wry smile. "Ah?!" Milenius frowned. "Thorn Knights get paid well. Where's your money?"

"Need to ask? Donated it all to the orphanage. I only kept what I need for expenses." Vernonfred answered without arrogance or humility. "You're an idiot..." Milenius muttered, confused by his friend.

"Oh right." Vernonfred remembered something and looked up. "The headmistress mentioned you in her letter. She praised you for being accomplished. She said you were proud and stubborn. Though you always caused trouble as a child, seeing your achievements today, she's genuinely happy for you."

The orphanage's... Milenius frowned, grumbling darkly. "I hate that old nun. She always hit me. Now she's even proud of me? How annoying..."

"Don't say it like that. The headmistress is serious. She hopes you'll visit the orphanage someday..." Vernonfred showed a...

smile. "After all, I have no desire to go back. I cut ties with the orphanage long ago. Why do you care so much about me?" Milenius said with a full...

-ius not donating was in both our names, together." Vernonfred thought, then continued. "I'm sure the headmistress will be moved when she sees your..."

name, why do such a boring thing?" Milenius felt uncomfortable. "You're not good at expressing yourself. If no one explains, people will keep misunderstanding you."

"What a joke toward Milenius!" Milenius turned and walked away without looking back. Vernonfred froze, saying nothing, continuing to reply to the orphanage letters. A moment later, a money bag was thrown onto Vernonfred's desk. Milenius's voice from the door: "Count me in for the orphanage donation. I hate owing people..."

Seeing Milenius cut into pieces before him, Duke Auster let out a sigh of relief, his face easing. Seeing Milenius's vacant gaze freeze, he actually bit down on the fallen sword hilt, using his remaining waist strength to spin in midair and slash out a final sword! Straight at Duke Auster!

Spinning... ahhhhhhhhh!" Duke Auster's blood gushed out.

Looks like he can't escape this fate! After this, the Elemental Four Sword Saints were all stunned, their hearts trembling uncontrollably! They thought Milenius's obsession was so strong—he was truly a madman!

title: Chapter 16 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 16 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 12 · Chapter 16

One-armed, he flew through the air and landed on the ground, spinning in circles, followed immediately by a mournful, piercing scream—

“Ahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh!

Overre, the Grand Duke, clutched his severed arm. Crimson blood spurted out from the wound in a gushing torrent.

The sheer volume of blood was enough to make anyone's eyes water, dyeing the surrounding walls a deep red.

Overre's face was pale, his body swaying unsteadily before he finally collapsed onto the ground, falling into a faint.

After Milieris delivered his final blow, he fell to the ground motionless, clearly having lost all signs of life, dead to the core.

He had done his best, but due to the circumstances earlier being too terrible, he had only severed Overre's arm and failed to inflict a fatal wound—truly a pity.

Overre had long been clear about his own fate, but even so, he couldn't take Overre, the Grand Duke, with him—such a pity.

The scene was a shambles, the site of the battle looking as if it had been swept over by magical beasts.

The Elemental Four Sword Saints stood in place, staring blankly at Milieris's corpse, all stunned by the obsession just now.

If this man wasn't a lunatic, then what he just did was too reckless, inspiring deep fear...

A body hacked to pieces into four or five parts, yet still able to bite down on a ceremonial sword with its teeth to deliver a final strike?

This formidable fighting will left the Four Sword Saints speechless, and an emotion of genuine admiration welling up in their hearts.

—Gabri, who had been hiding in the corner, stepped out and helped support the fainting Overre, the Grand Duke.

“Lord! Lord! Wake up, ah!

“Someone! Someone! Quick, find a priest!”

Gabri rushed out to find someone to come help quickly. Overre was old, and who knew if he would die from such severe injuries?!

The Wind Sword Saint withdrew his gaze, sheathing the gem sword, and said casually, “This man is not simple. Compared to the previous one who held a magic book, he is different.”

The Earth Sword Saint nodded in agreement, saying, “Right. Besides being too young, I feel this man has no major flaws. The astonishing speed just now left me somewhat taken aback. If I were to face him alone, I feel I would have to take it seriously.”

“Not only that, you all were too one-sided. The sword techniques displayed by the Thorned Knight just now were extraordinary...” The Water Sword Saint walked over to Overre, the Grand Duke, and pulled down the pendant around his neck, showing it to everyone, “This rare magic defense item has been shattered. Can you understand the power this knight just displayed?”

The Wind Sword Saint and the Earth Sword Saint said nothing, clearly feeling some shock.

However, the irascible Destruction Sword Saint didn't think it was a big deal, saying casually, “It's just broken. What's the big deal?”

“This thing is from the rulers of the Chaotic Sea. According to legend, this might be a fragment of a certain divine artifact, though not complete, it can still display one ten-millionth of a divine artifact's power. Now that this item is completely ruined, can you still not understand the power this young man just displayed?” The Water Sword Saint, being more rational, continued analyzing, “Even we would have to exert our full strength to crush the defense of a divine artifact fragment, yet this young man can do it too, showing his talent is very high. If he continues to train, perhaps one day he can surpass the Saint-tier and reach that mysterious level.”

“Ridiculous! We've struggled for a hundred years without breaking out of the Saint-tier's shackles. Can a dead man do it?!” The Destruction Sword Saint's tone was very unyielding.

“You have to know that everyone's initial talent is different; that's normal.” The Water Sword Saint answered.

“Hmph, saying more is useless; the other party is already a dead man.” The Destruction Sword Saint stepped forward, raising a entirely crimson gem sword. Suddenly, a flame of red fire ignited on the blade, “Let him turn to ash, despising us, unworthy of a whole corpse!”

“Wait.” The Wind Sword Saint stepped forward to block his companion, looked at the body on the ground, and said with deep meaning—

“This young knight was worthy of being a respectable enemy.”

“Humiliating a corpse is too base.”

“The sword techniques displayed at the end are worth our burying him...”

Milieris's solitary action was not without value.

This time, Overre, the Grand Duke, was severely wounded and became a one-armed disabled person.

Adding to the uproar and impact, it affected the marching speed of the entire allied army, almost causing it to stagnate.

Due to Overre's injury, the entire army halted and took defensive positions in place, “reducing the pressure on the imperial capital quite a bit, and buying precious time.

In the military tent, Overre, the Grand Duke, lay unconscious for three full days and three nights before waking up. His left arm had been severed by Milieris, and it had been temporarily treated and bandaged.

The Elemental Four Sword Saints stood guard in their respective sectors, not moving about. As the acting advisor, Gabri received the news that Overre had awakened and came running over immediately.

“Grand Duke, you’re awake?” Gabri came to Overre's bedside.

“Um.” Overre nodded. “It was a close call; I almost didn't die. This Milieris man is truly terrifying.”

“Unexpectedly, the Queen actually sent two assassins, really spending a lot of effort to try to put you to death,” Gabri showed a look of grief and indignation.

“Yeah, the Queen clearly has no mercy. I was thinking of just placing her under house arrest, but now I just want to execute her publicly!” Overre looked at his severed arm, and his inner hatred rose linearly.

“The Grand Duke's wish can be realized soon; don't forget, we now have an absolute advantage. As long as the Four Sword Saints stand on our side, the plan to overturn the kingdom will absolutely not fail.” Gabri paused, analyzing, “I just received a report. Previously, due to internal strife within the royal family, the lake fairies—this big weapon—had already been used up. For us, this is an excellent opportunity.”

“Right, the Empire now is just a shell, without the lake fairies, who can still threaten the Four Sword Saints? The distance to realizing my ambition is getting closer and closer,” Overre, the Grand Duke, calmed down slightly.

“The Grand Duke is right, and the claws we sent out should have now reached the mission site. Only the Queen guarded by three knights—what can they resist?” Gabri showed a sinister smile.

“Is...” Overre, the Grand Duke, also smiled with delight, saying slowly—

“Perhaps when we reach the imperial capital...”

“Our family's flags will already be planted on the walls.”

The vague moon disappeared, disappearing somewhere unknown.

Ink-black like the sky, not a single star appeared.

Within the imperial capital, opposite the temporary palace, was a mountain covered in lush forest.

Under this pitch-black moon, it seemed even more mysterious, giving a sense of unknown danger.

The black wolf mercenary squad, renowned as an elite team of five, suddenly appeared here, hiding within the forest.

Heavy-armored knight Horl, dark elf archer Dorlin, dark shadow Nidham at this moment, and lightning mage Kton four of them gazed down below.

They slowly made way for a path, and Casayeg, sitting in a wheelchair, came to the front, looking at the temporary palace below and grinning wickedly—

“It seems it's time for our black wolf mercenary team to go on a killing spree...

title: Chapter 17 — Thought
content:
Chapter 17 — Thought

Volume 12 · Chapter 17

The Black Wolf Mercenaries slipped in through a secret path and reached the temporary palace ahead of everyone.

Cassaiye accepted the Duke of Ofle's commission, and it seemed they could carry it out right away.

"Captain, what do you want to bring us here for? This is the enemy's stronghold..." Nidam asked tentatively.

"Yeah, now you should be able to tell us what this mysterious mission is about, right?" Kaidun stroked his beard.

The others all wore expressions of confusion, having no idea there was any mysterious mission at all.

"The mysterious mission is just a one-in-a-million opportunity..." Cassaiye turned his wheelchair around and said with a sinister smile, "Duke Ofle promised us that as long as we take down Queen Elizabeth, we'll be heroes of the new empire. At that point, we won't only get noble titles, but also vast estates!"

"No way!? We'll get estates too? Are you kidding me?" Kaidun's eyes widened in shock, thinking the reward was too good to be true.

The other three members sucked in a cold breath, finding it hard to believe that Cassaiye had struck such a big deal with the Duke.

Getting noble titles and vast estates meant a bright future ahead. The entire Black Wolf Mercenaries would completely break out of their current predicament and become noble lords, no longer living a life of wandering from place to place.

This reward was tempting to everyone. Even though the mission was full of danger, there was still a need to try their luck.

"It's not a joke. I've already made a contract with the Duke. As long as we complete the mission, this promise will definitely be fulfilled." Cassaiye paused and continued, "You all know what it means to become nobles and get estates, right? It means we'll be superior beings from now on, with our own territories. The Black Wolf Mercenaries' status will rise dramatically."

"Great, this is amazing! I can barely contain my killing urge!" Nidam's eyes were filled with fanaticism.

"I never expected such a reward. If I become a lord, I can do whatever I want!" Holler struck his axe against his shield excitedly, "Then what are we waiting for? Let's charge in right now and kill them all, take the Queen's head back and report!"

"Wait a minute, with such a generous reward, this mission must be very dangerous, right? It probably won't be that easy." Kaidun said calmly.

"Yeah, she's the Queen of the entire empire. She must have powerful guards protecting her. If it were that easy, why would the Duke bother finding us?" The quiet Duolin agreed.

The group fell silent for a moment. Although great rewards call for brave men, none of them were fools. They didn't want to die recklessly.

"Don't worry about that. The palace guards are weak now, not like before, so our pressure isn't that great." Cassaiye sneered, "The real enemy we need to face is the Thorn Knights. According to the intelligence, there aren't many of them, and with our strength, we can still fight them!"

"But the Thorn Knights are not easy to deal with. Are we really okay? Especially that famous First..." Kaidun hesitated, worried about running into trouble with the Thorn Knights.

"It's fine, we can try. If it really doesn't work out, we'll retreat." Cassaiye looked at everyone and seduced them, "Think about the reward the Duke gave us. I think even with the danger, it's worth us trying."

"...Well, Kaidun had nothing to say. Trying is definitely fine, after all, the temptation of the reward is too strong.

"Duolin, take action. Go greet the other side first." Cassaiye gave the order.

Duolin sighed, drew his bow and shot an arrow that sliced through the dark night sky.

The arrow split in mid-air, instantly forming a dense rain of arrows.

The sound of arrows whistling through the air was continuous, countless arrows raining down on the temporary palace...

Temporary Palace.

The conference hall was quiet.

Elizabeth sat alone in the main seat, her face full of worry.

Behind her stood Morrison and Mesfil, both expressionless, guarding her side.

The atmosphere was quiet, not a single word.

Chapman had already reported everything to Elizabeth, withholding nothing.

Such a severe situation was difficult for Elizabeth to handle, and she had to think carefully.

Morrison and Mesfil could understand the Queen's distress, but they found it hard to help.

Regarding the deaths of Milieth and Vinyfre, Elizabeth felt sad, thinking her abilities were insufficient, and the information she could obtain was limited. She hadn't even anticipated that the enemy had strong cards up their sleeves.

If it was just the Black Wolf Mercenaries under Duke Ofle, Elizabeth felt that Milieth and Vinyfre, the two Thorn Knights, could handle the assassination without any resistance.

However, according to Chapman's report, Duke Ofle had even more powerful enemies under his command, easily killing Vinyfre. They could probably deal with the other Thorn Knights without much effort either.

Although there was no news, Elizabeth felt that Milieth was probably doomed and wouldn't return.

However, learning that the Allied Forces had stopped for three or four days gave Elizabeth some time to think about countermeasures.

The deaths of the two Thorn Knights made Elizabeth feel responsible. She had thought too simply, and the failure of the assassination mission made the situation worse than before.

Elizabeth lowered her head, her mind in chaos. The Allied Forces were about to launch a massive invasion, and her defenses were already in disrepair.

She had already sent people to accelerate construction, but there was too much to do. Perhaps they could only build a single wall.

On top of that, the lake fairies were defeated by Merlin and fell into a hundred-year sleep, unable to be used again, making the situation even worse.

Now, she only had three Thorn Knights left, and it was hard to say whether they could withstand the Allied Forces.

Moreover, besides the Black Wolf Mercenaries, there was an unknown Sword Saint present, making things very troublesome.

Elizabeth was uncertain whether the knights could defeat the enemy. The pressure this created was overwhelming.

What should she do? It was almost impossible to resist with her current strength. It seemed she had to seek some aid.

Should she ask other countries for support? That would definitely require giving up some imperial interests.

Moreover, neighboring countries were not kind-hearted. They might take this opportunity to make excessive demands.

But without relying on foreign support, who else could help her get through this crisis?

Elizabeth thought and thought, and suddenly Merlin's figure flashed through her mind, as if she had grasped the last straw.

Elrkin the Great Swordsman could defeat the lake fairies. With the current situation...

It seemed only this man had the ability to help her get through this crisis.

But, would she really have to bow her head and beg for help?

title: Chapter 18 — Raid
content:
Chapter 18 — Raid

Volume 12 · Chapter 18

Elizabeth recalled Merlin's despicable face when he robbed her stockings, and a wave of panic rose in her chest.

Although the great swordsman Elkain certainly had the ability to help her, the past grievances were fresh in her memory. Would he really come to her aid without regard for past animosity?

Still, the previous incidents had all been orchestrated by her own sister. Merlin had even rescued her from the cage. Perhaps he didn't harbor too much ill will toward the empire.

But then she lowered her head, thinking of begging help from a pervert who had stolen women's clothing. She couldn't help but feel that as a queen, she had lost all dignity.

Elizabeth's expression grew complicated. Although she could think of Merlin immediately, her instincts still recoiled at the thought of relying on someone she didn't truly understand—someone powerful and perverted.

Moreover, the conflicts and threats from Elkain the great swordsman and the royal family hadn't been resolved yet. Now, asking for help felt like she was lowering herself.

Meredith secretly glanced at Elizabeth, noticing her worried and anxious expression. "Your Majesty, what's wrong? You look so uneasy."

"......"

Elizabeth forced out a faint smile.

"So it's about the allied forces marching their armies here soon, isn't it?" Morrison blurted out without hesitation.

"......"

Elizabeth's smile became awkward. Though she tried her best to hide it, the problem at hand was obvious to anyone.

o5

CCZ's

Meredith, seeing the queen's strained smile, tentatively asked, "Your Majesty, can't we use the lake fairy one more time?"

Meredith was also worried about resisting the allied forces. Even Saint-tier powerhouses weren't invincible. With enough human wave tactics and attrition, once magical power or combat spirit was exhausted, their strength would drop significantly.

Moreover, besides the Black Wolf Mercenaries, there was also a mysterious sword master aiding them from the shadows. This lineup was already quite formidable. It seemed that Duke Overre had been preparing this rebellion for a long time, and it was no small matter.

"Now we can't use it anymore. Although that water spirit was just a proxy of the lake fairy, the proxy was still connected to the real one. Even though Elkain didn't kill it, the real lake fairy still suffered heavy damage. Preliminary estimates suggest the lake fairy may need several hundred years to recover..." Elizabeth frowned as she explained.

"So the lake fairy didn't use its full strength when it faced Elkain?" Morrison asked curiously.

"No. According to historical records, the lake fairy's power was much greater than that water spirit proxy. It probably underestimated Elkain's strength, which is why it suffered so much..." Elizabeth speculated.

"That's right..." Morrison nodded, thinking, "I once saw that water spirit from afar. I thought that if several Thorn Knights combined their strength, they could suppress it. All this time, it turned out to be just a proxy."

"Your Majesty, how exactly does the lake fairy exist?" Meredith asked, curious about this guardian of the empire.

"It's hard to explain in detail. The lake fairy is a royal secret. Only those with royal succession rights can know after coming of age." Elizabeth, unable to directly reveal the lake fairy's secrets, gave a vague explanation. "But the lake fairy is an aggregate of water elements. After countless ages of cultivation, it gained its own wisdom. So once it settled down, when we rebuilt the capital, we needed to repair the underground rivers. It could help the lake fairy accelerate its..."

"Since we can't use the lake fairy's power, resisting the allied forces will be quite difficult..." Meredith looked up and asked carefully, "Your Majesty, do you have any good strategies now?"

"......"

Elizabeth fell silent, forced to face the reality before her. Without relying on external forces, it would be difficult to break through the current predicament.

Did she really have to bow down to Elkain? That pervert even used her stolen underwear as leverage!

I'm the queen of the empire, and now I have to beg a fetish pervert for support? I really can't stand it...

But the current situation is quite troublesome. It's probably necessary to try to win over Elkain?

It's just about liking women's underwear. As long as he agrees to keep it secret...

I could send Elkain an entire truckload of stockings. That should be enough to satisfy him...

If Merlin knew about Elizabeth's ridiculous thoughts, he'd probably say something like "damn, I've got to explain this..."

Elizabeth made up her mind and decided to write a letter to Merlin, inviting him to the capital for a face-to-face meeting.

"Wilson,

Get me some paper and pen.

I want to write a letter. Light novel

Meredith nodded and headed out, wondering which letter the queen wanted to write at this time. Was she asking for support from other kingdoms?

But before Meredith had taken a few steps, a strong sensation suddenly alerted her. A murderous intent was rushing toward them.

Meredith drew her sword sharply, stepped back several paces, and placed Elizabeth behind her, shouting a warning.

"Huh?"

Elizabeth was startled. She hadn't expected an enemy attack at this moment. The allied forces hadn't even arrived yet. Could this be a small-scale raid?

"Your Majesty, please hide. Leave this to us!" Morrison quickly put on his boxing gloves and shielded the queen.

Elizabeth had no choice but to crouch down awkwardly and hide under the table.

At that moment, a series of whooshing sounds filled the air as a massive swarm of locusts descended.

The black elf archers' arrow rain from Doreen came crashing down, impossible to withstand.

These arrows seemed to be enhanced, with extremely strong attack power, flying like bullets that could pierce through walls.

The sound of constant impacts echoed as the temporary palace was riddled with holes under the arrow rain!

Black feathered arrows pierced through the walls, turning the entire conference hall into a mess, indiscriminately injuring people inside!

The red carpet instantly turned into thorns, with countless arrow feathers stuck into the ground, continuously increasing.

"Yaaaaah!"

Elizabeth, overcome with fear, let out a scream and crouched under the table, trembling and clutching her head.

Meredith and Morrison reacted swiftly, using their weapons to block the arrows continuously!

Clang, clang, sparks flew as their weapons collided. The two figures darted around, nearly blocking every arrow that could harm Elizabeth!

After the chaos settled, Elizabeth slowly opened her eyes, a bit confused about what was happening.

"Who launched this attack? Could Overre's forces have already entered the capital?!" Morrison asked urgently.

"Morrison, stay here and protect the queen. I'm going out to investigate..." Meredith gripped her straight sword and charged out, her brow furrowed with thought.

Who was it?

Daring to attack so brazenly...

Do they think I don't exist?!

title: Chapter 19 — Monthly Vote Bonus Update
content:
Chapter 19 — Monthly Vote Bonus Update

Volume 12 · Chapter 19

"Hey! Mesfield!" Morrison also wanted to go out and check the situation, but was immediately assigned work.

Mesfield burst straight out of the meeting hall, roughly estimated to be going to settle scores with the invading enemies.

Morrison felt a wave of embarrassment inside, turned around to look at the queen, and quickly stepped forward. "Your Majesty, are you alright?"

Elizabeth looked around in terror, her heart still racing and somewhat shaken. "Pa...past..."

Morrison helped the queen to her feet and tentatively asked, "Your Majesty, do you understand what's going on?"

"It must be Duke Aoffre's vanguard squad, taking advantage of our thin defenses to launch a surprise attack," Elizabeth said, gradually calming down.

"Your Majesty, should we find somewhere to take cover?" Morrison asked.

"There should be no need. The fact that the enemy dares to attack so brazenly means the entire temporary royal palace is within their control. Hiding anywhere will make no difference..." Elizabeth's delicate brows furrowed, her expression grave.

"I've been targeted by the enemy."

Below the temporary royal palace residence.

After slaughtering the guards, the Black Wolf Mercenary Group swaggered in.

However, out of the original five-person squad, only three were present.

Shadow Thief Nedum and Dark Elf Archer Doreen had been assigned other tasks and were moving about separately.

Kasayeg had already set up various traps, waiting for the Thorn Knights to stupidly jump out.

The Black Wolf Mercenary Group was a complete trinity of warrior, fighter, and mage, and they had always fought in coordination with each other, achieving twice the result with half the effort.

So Kasayeg was not panicked at all. Even facing Thorn Knights, among the five of them banding together, they wouldn't necessarily lose.

"How strange. Why is there absolutely no movement? Did an arrow barrage wipe out the other side?" Kerton felt it was too quiet and found it uncomfortable.

"Hahaha! I think these guys are scared off. What Thorn Knights? Is that all the courage they have!?" Hall swung his war axe in a showing-off manner.

Kasayeg rolled his wheelchair forward slightly, examined the situation, and said calmly, "How could that be? Thorn Knights are not something you can deal with casually. Do you think they're all good-for-nothings who just coast along until they die?"

Before the words had even finished echoing, a crisp tinkling sound rang out, and all the glass upstairs shattered completely.

Mesfield, wanting to save time, had jumped straight down from the fifth-floor window.

The courtyard was bathed in moonlight, white as silver, and Mesfield's pale purple hair streamed out behind her, radiating a commanding aura.

Amidst the scattered shards of colored glass around them, her graceful figure displayed both elegance and sharpness.

Mesfield descended from the sky, landing straight before the three members of the Black Wolf Mercenary Group. She swung her straight sword twice in her hands, her divine power surging.

"Who are you people!? How dare you attack the queen's residence! If you don't explain yourselves clearly, you won't be leaving here today!"

"Kekke..." Kasayeg let out a string of eerie laughs, speaking in a sinister tone. "I didn't expect to run into the First Thorn Knight right off the bat. Seems like I hit the jackpot. Very well. The Black Wolf Knight Order will start with you first!"

"Black Wolf Knight Order..." Mesfield narrowed her eyes, growing alert. "So you really did come. Since you've sided with Duke Aoffre, I no longer need to hold back."

"Hold back? You've got a lot of confidence..." Kerton stroked his beard, gripping his magic staff tightly. "Where are the other Thorn Knights? Is there only one knight in the entire temporary palace?"

"I don't need anyone else. Dealing with the lot of you, one person is more than enough!" Golden battle aura surged from Mesfield's body, and she prepared herself for a life-and-death struggle.

Actually, there were only three Thorn Knights present now. Morrison was responsible for protecting the queen, and as for where Catherine had gone, even Mesfield wasn't entirely sure — she was probably resting somewhere.

"One person?! Haha! What enormous... courage..." Kasayeg burst into loud laughter, silently gripping the armrests of his wheelchair until his knuckles showed a faint pallor. "You think a single person can handle the Black Wolf Knight Order? Don't kid yourself! Just because you're the First Knight doesn't mean you can look down on others. Killing you would be as easy as pie!"

"Then stop wasting words. Let me see how strong you really are," Mesfield grew increasingly alert.

"Sigh, self-righteous guy. Hall!" Kasayeg bellowed out an order. "Go! Trample this famously renowned First Knight into the mud! This is your chance to make a name for yourself, so don't waste it."

"Got it!" Heavy Knight Hall stepped forward, wielding a giant axe and shield, striking a stance. "I am Hall, known as the human war chariot in the Holy Church's eastern expedition! Come, let me see the Thorn Knight's skills!"

Watching Hall tap his war axe against his shield in mockery, Mesfield couldn't help but feel annoyed inside, deciding to take down this big guy first.

Mesfield's gaze sharpened. Her figure moved like a cannonball, erupting forth in an instant!

The transition from stillness to motion was extremely fast, as sudden and overwhelming as thunder, and her sword techniques exploded forth like a violent flood and tsunami!

Mesfield wielded her straight sword with one hand, her golden battle aura surging rapidly alongside her high-frequency sword techniques!

Shhhk! The ferocious sound of the blade slicing through the air was extremely shrill, sounding like a violently played violin!

An ordinary person would probably have been beaten back step by step by now. However, Hall, a veteran reaper of lives who had seen countless battles, was no pushover either.

Hall raised his thick shield forward, instantly forming a defense as solid as copper walls and iron ramparts, nearly watertight!

Mesfield gritted her silver teeth, her straight sword striking repeatedly, but all of them were blocked by Hall's shield.

clang clang! Shocking sounds continued, sparks of blazing fire flying from the collisions between sword and shield!

Mesfield's sword speed had already produced layer after layer of afterimages, yet she still couldn't break through Hall's defense.

Behind them, Kasayeg and Kerton both wore cold smirks, clearly looking down on this First Knight.

Mesfield's heart grew a little flustered. Damn it! This man's defensive technique is so skilled. My sword techniques can't seem to gain the upper hand!

"Hahaha! What's wrong?!" Hall grinned ferociously, baring his teeth, looking like a wild beast. He continuously made micro-adjustments to his stance, blocking all of his opponent's attacks. "Are you really the famous First Knight from legends? Your strength is nothing special at all. Please, put some effort into it. I'm about to fall asleep. If you don't show me something real, we'll end up killing you, haha..."

"Tch!" Mesfield was somewhat provoked into anger. She suddenly gathered Saint-tier battle aura and launched a pinpoint piercing thrust. "You talk too much!!!"

A loud bang resounded, and Hall's shield was forced to deform outright, the center portion caving inward.

The ground suffered intense impact, cracking and splitting apart in an instant!

Hall was forced to half-squat to withstand Mesfield's relentless assault, a trace of cold sweat forming on his forehead—

Such overwhelming power!

If a few more attacks of this caliber land on me, I won't be able to hold out!

As expected of the legendary First Knight! This domineering strength is rather intimidating...
