title: Chapter 20 — Thrash
content:
Chapter 20 — Thrash

Volume 12 · Chapter 20

Melsfield's ruthless swordplay made Hall feel pressured, forcing him to take a step back.

"Tch!"

Kasayge clicked his tongue in dissatisfaction. Seeing Hall at a disadvantage against Melsfield, he could no longer sit still in his wheelchair.

He gave his curved magic staff a flick, instantly casting a weakening spell on Melsfield, intending to support Hall in defeating the First Knight!

A wicked grin spread across Kasayge's face, his expression turning monstrous.

"You said you could handle us alone before, so let's just go all at once, heh heh..."

Black energy wisps slowly coiled around Melsfield, draining her strength until she was drenched in cold sweat and barely able to stand.

Kasayge was originally a Dark Priest — not skilled at healing, but excellent at blanketing enemies with every manner of curse and debuff, slowly dragging them into the abyss of death.

The curse spell he had just unleashed would severely weaken Melsfield's combat prowess, and its effects would grow stronger over time until she became a ruined woman unable even to lift a sword!

Kasayge had already calculated everything. In just a moment, the thorny First Knight before him would be a corpse!

A flicker of annoyance crossed Melsfield's eyes. She had never expected the enemy to fight her one-on-one — of course they would resort to underhanded tricks once they grew impatient.

She felt waves of dizziness, and the sword in her hand suddenly seemed to grow impossibly heavy, as if sapping her very life force.

Melsfield knew she couldn't drag this out. Gathering herself with full concentration, she resolved to end this quickly.

"I knew you'd all gang up on me, but thinking a mere curse could bring me down is a grave mistake!"

As Melsfield raised her sword to counterattack, sharp whistling sounds cut through the air — three feathered arrows came hurtling toward her!

The arrows came at extremely tricky angles, their tips glowing faintly red, as if coated in some deadly poison.

The three arrows spread apart, striking from three different directions, forming a pincer formation!

In this desperate situation, the weakened Melsfield felt panic well up inside her. She shifted from offense to defense, using her sword to block the three incoming arrows and prevent herself from being struck.

Although Melsfield managed to deflect the arrows, she was forced back and given no time to catch her breath before the enemy launched a ferocious follow-up assault.

"Let's see how you like my shield strike?!?!?"

Hall charged forward like a war chariot, rolling thunderously toward her, raising his shield to smash it hard into Melsfield's head.

"Cough!"

Melsfield spat blood as her body was launched backward, crashing heavily into the palace complex of the temporary royal residence and kicking up clouds of dust.

But that was far from over. Ketton, skilled in lightning magic, immediately added pressure with his own attack. Golden magical energy surged, and he unleashed the spell "Thunderstorm!"

Silver-white lightning tore through the dark night sky, answering the call and savagely hammering Melsfield amid the swirling dust with crackling strikes.

Kasayge smirked triumphantly, shrugged his shoulders, and said cheerfully,

"What First Knight, huh?"

"Absolutely pathetic, heh heh heh..."

Up on a distant tower.

The dark elf shooter Doreen quietly lowered her bow, feeling her job was done.

She had been providing long-range support here, helping her team establish an advantage, or covering a retreat if things went wrong.

So far, Doreen had only seen one enemy — Melsfield — and she had been hit by wave after wave of devastating blows.

Doreen guessed Melsfield was probably dead and intended to call it a day, descending to regroup with her teammates below.

But the moment she turned around, a massive vine lashed toward her like a whip!

Doreen's eyes widened in alarm. Relying on her agile reflexes, she repeatedly leaped backward, flipping over the edge of the tower to dodge the strike!

After landing on the ground, Doreen looked up and saw a female knight with long brown hair standing before her — none other than Catherine!

"You have some nerve storming the imperial capital uninvited..."

Catherine's eyes seemed never to open, giving her the appearance of a blind person — or perhaps as if she were utterly dismissing her opponent.

Behind Catherine, towering wooden guardians had appeared at some point, solemnly guarding her side.

Doreen felt the oppressive aura radiating from the woman and couldn't help but shiver inwardly. She judged this enemy to be powerful and by no means to be underestimated!

Doreen flung her scarf behind her, quickly retreated to create distance, then nocked three arrows in quick succession!

The three arrows split once again mid-flight, suddenly becoming an extremely ferocious barrage of arrows so dense it made one's scalp tingle with dread.

"Don't even want to talk things over?" Catherine narrowed her eyes, standing completely still.

Countless vines rapidly gathered before Catherine, instantly forming a wooden shield.

Thud, thud, thud — the dense arrow barrage rained down upon the wooden shield, unable to cause the slightest damage!

Doreen's expression grew grave. She nocked another arrow, pulling the bowstring back into a full moon as all her strength converged.

"Piercing Arrow!"

The bowstring vibrated with a sharp twang. This piercing arrow carved through the air like a blade, its red trajectory straight for her enemy.

This attack was no joke. The wooden shield was directly pierced through, and the arrow flew straight toward Catherine.

Yet Catherine remained unfazed. A water vortex slowly formed before her, completely neutralizing the piercing arrow's destructive force — as though it had struck rubber and become firmly stuck, motionless.

Catherine had already arrived at this location long before. Would she only set up a single barrier magic? A barrier combining offense and defense was already in place.

"Lis...?" Doreen's eyes widened, her heart pounding internally. Barrier magic of two attributes!?! How is this person doing this?!

"I advise you to surrender. Within my barriers, you have zero chance of victory — you can't even escape."

"Oh? You really think I'd run?" Doreen sneered, her pointed ears twitching. She casually tossed her bow and arrows to the ground and withdrew a potion bottle from the pouch at her waist. "It's rare to encounter a decent prey. I'm going to kill you!"

Catherine's expression shifted slightly, a hint of killing intent stirring. She had originally intended to capture an enemy alive, but it seemed there was no need now.

Doreen downed the potion in one gulp, a grimace of pain crossing her face before her tight-fitting outfit began to tear apart.

Her body swelled to more than twice its original size, becoming exceptionally burly, every muscle bulging with raw power.

Doreen's expression turned ferocious, no longer calm as before — she had become a snarling beast, low guttural growls rumbling from her throat.

"Raaaaarghhhhh..."

Exactly right. The potion she had just consumed was a dark berserker elixir unique to the dark elf clan — the same type the elven ambassador had given her subordinates earlier.

However, the concentration of this particular dark potion was far weaker. Still, her strength had doubled, and her physique had become extraordinary.

"How does it feel?!? Now you're afraid, aren't you? Can you still face me with that calm expression?" The enhanced Doreen flexed her claws menacingly. "I'm going to tear your face apart, hehehe!"

"How boring. You gave up your own chance to live. Did I not make myself clear?" Catherine raised her ring-adorned hand, Saint-tier magical energy surging. "Within my barriers, you have zero chance."

Before her words had even finished fading, the ground began to tremble. Dozens of giant tree vines shot upward from the earth, their thick trunks twisting through the sky and blotting out the sun!

Doreen's expression went blank. She stared at the colossal vines rising like immense tentacles, surrounding her with no way to escape...

"Farewell." Catherine turned away, not bothering to look at Doreen even once.

Dozens of vines crashed down from above like a tidal wave, brutally beating the enhanced dark elf Doreen senseless....

title: Chapter 21 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 21 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 12 · Chapter 21

A tremendous bang echoed, and the pressure around Kasaeger grew suffocating, as if his mind was being scorched alive. A faint tremor shook the earth.

The massive vines slowly writhed, sending chills down the spines of onlookers.

Damn it! Dorine's pressure has vanished! There's a powerful enemy over there!" Cold sweat beaded on Kasaeger's forehead.

"Could it be another Thorn Knight? This kind of pressure..." Cuton gazed toward that direction and said solemnly in a low voice, "Dorine couldn't have held her off at all."

"Should I go reinforce her?" Hall volunteered, eager to face the other Thorn Knight.

"No need. Let's finish off the ones right in front of us first!" Kasaeger looked at the unmoving battlefield, where smoke still billowed. "Hall, go behead the First Knight!"

Msfield's pressure had never fully dissipated, so Kasaeger couldn't afford to let his guard down.

Rather than splitting their strength to rescue others, it was safer to eliminate the enemies before them first.

"Got it!" Hall approached slowly, his great axe already thirsting for blood.

Several streaks of sword intent flashed through the air, dispersing the smoke and revealing Msfield's figure. She was battered and bruised from shield strikes and lightning bolts.

Since Kasaeger had cursed her with a weakening hex, Msfield could not unleash her full strength and could only cling to consciousness by sheer force.

Blood trickled slowly down Msfield's forehead. She held her longsword in her right hand and looked coldly at the three before her with scornful eyes.

"You ate my Thunderstorm and still aren't dead? Your hide really is thick..." Cuton felt a bead of cold sweat roll down his forehead.

"After all, she is the legendary First Knight. It would be more unreasonable if we defeated her so easily," Kasaeger remained relatively calm.

"She's still alive after all that? Not bad. She'll keep me entertained a bit longer. Hey!" Hall took his stance and flashed a mocking grin, ready for a second round of assault.

"Pah!"

Msfield said nothing and spat the pooled blood from her mouth onto the ground.

She decided to get serious now. Staring at the crushing pressure of the curse, she frantically stirred her internal Fighting Qi!

With a gesture of her left hand, golden Fighting Qi slowly gathered, forming a sword of pure golden energy!

"Condensing qi into..." Kasaeger's eyes widened slightly. He had never seen such a technique before and sensed it was extraordinary.

"What is that?! Can Fighting Qi be solidified into a physical form?!" Cuton had never seen anything like it either and found it fascinating.

"I'm not sure, but it feels dangerous..." Unable to answer, Kasaeger just warned Hall, "Hall, be careful. Don't lose when you're already ahead..."

"Hehe, don't worry. I've pretty much figured out this First Knight's swordsmanship. I can handle her without breaking a sweat!" Hall was full of confidence, a heavy battle lust flashing in his eyes.

Kasaeger said nothing but felt a trace of unease deep inside. Still, he had faith in Hall's defenses.

"When you go to hell, I hope you still remember the words you just spoke!"

Msfield's figure moved like lightning. Without any special countermeasure, she charged straight at Hall, looking to clash head-on!

Hall sneered, thinking what nonsense this First Knight was — truly naive!

He had already tested it before: frontal attacks were useless against him!

Hall set up his defensive stance, raised his shield in front, and prepared to block the attack before turning it around and counterkilling his opponent!

However, Hall's hopes were dashed as a dramatic turn of events unfolded.

Msfield's Fighting Qi sword completely ignored the shield defense and pierced straight through Hall's shield, and even the sturdy armor behind it failed to stop it.

That golden qi sword pierced through Hall's body, his heart directly torn apart by the fighting energy, inflicting a fatal wound!

Hall's face was filled with disbelief. He never expected his thick defense to be penetrated by such a qi sword.

His face went pale, drained of all color. He glanced blankly at Msfield, then coughed up a mouthful of blood from his throat.

Hall's mighty frame swayed unsteadily, his eyelids rolled back, and he collapsed to the ground, lifeless.

Bizarrely, Hall's shield and armor were completely unharmed, yet the man himself was dead.

This bizarre scene felt as though they had been attacked by a ghost.

In truth, Msfield's qi condensation sword was exactly like this — defenses were mere decoration against a qi blade, as it specialized in damaging flesh and blood.

"...What just happened?!" Cuton was stunned, looking at Hall's cooling corpse on the ground in utter disbelief.

Kasaeger was equally speechless. Despite his broad experience, he had never encountered such a technique before.

"Now it's your turn, both of you!"

Msfield did not stop. Wielding both her longsword and her qi sword, she closed the distance to Kasaeger and Cuton in an instant.

"Don't come any closer!"

Cuton roared, panic written across his face. Mages naturally felt terror when swordsmen closed in on them.

Under normal circumstances, if a mage allowed an enemy warrior to get within one meter, they had effectively already lost half the battle!

Sacred-tier mana erupted from Cuton's body as he wildly swung his magic staff. Lightning flashed violently, crashing down upon Msfield with devastating force.

But Msfield remained calm and swung her golden qi sword once. The lightning magic was decisively cleaved in two!

"What?! ...Ugh!"

Cuton's face twisted in terror before he could finish his sentence. Msfield's right hand thrust her longsword forward, killing him instantly!

Seeing Cuton dead, Kasaeger knew staying meant certain death.

Without hesitation, he sharply turned his wheelchair around and began sprinting to escape.

Kasaeger silently prayed that Msfield would not withstand the curse, giving him a slim chance to survive.

But how could Msfield easily let an enemy slip away?

Kasaeger frantically pushed his wheelchair, but then felt something pierce through his body. A gleaming golden qi sword lay on the ground before him.

"..."

Kasaeger's teeth chattered in terror, making a clicking sound as his aged body trembled like a sieve.

He looked down at his chest and saw dark red blood already staining his clothes.

"...As expected of the Thorn Knights' First Knight... so... strong..."

Kasaeger felt his life rapidly slipping away as he slumped from his wheelchair.

His face, still bearing an expression of disbelief, retained the不甘 and terror of his final moments.

Slaying three Saint-tier warriors in a row had pushed Msfield to the verge of exhaustion. Especially while being relentlessly weakened by the curse, forcing her to draw upon her Fighting Qi had already caused some internal damage to her own body.

Msfield knelt on one knee on the ground, leaning on her longsword to support herself, gasping for breath with cold sweat soaking her. She looked utterly worn out.

"Tired? My chance has finally come. Die, you wretched knight!"

The assassin Nemdam suddenly emerged from Msfield's shadow, a razor-sharp dagger in his hand.

He radiated a powerful Saint-tier aura and fiercely drove his blade toward Msfield's neck as she knelt!

The lethal strike was too fast to react to, resembling a vengeful ghost from hell come to drag its target to the underworld!

Nemdam had been lurking for a long time, waiting for the perfect opportunity to assassinate.

Now Msfield was physically weakened. If not now, when?!

Msfield had already sensed the killing intent behind her, but her exhausted body could barely respond!

Just at that critical moment! A dark figure descended from the sky, exuding an overwhelming presence and an aura of pure evil.

Any church official present would instantly recognize it — that was the unmistakable breath of a demon!

Nemdam's mind thundered with shock. Sensing that terrifying killing intent, his body convulsed in terror, and he was mercilessly slaughtered on the spot!

Msfield had no idea what had happened behind her. As she slowly turned her head to look—

A majestic man stood there—

[(<>∞●): To be continued in the next chapter!]

title: Chapter 22 — Call for Help
content:
Chapter 22 — Call for Help

Volume 12 · Chapter 22

Melsfield looked behind her, and a tall figure came into view—

A black knight clad in dark armor and wielding a long spear stood in the night.

This armor looked deeply uncanny, its bizarre shape and strange engravings giving the impression that it had not been forged by human hands at all.

Coupled with its pitch-black coloration that blended seamlessly into the darkness, the overall impression was something like a vengeful spirit made flesh, the aura of a demon released without restraint.

The helmet was the most terrifying of all—complete with a triangular shape, carved to resemble a beast, with sinister fangs rendered vividly lifelike.

It was unknown who was wearing this fearsome armor, but striding openly through the streets would likely frighten civilians to fainting.

After all, that unmistakable demonic aura would be felt even by ordinary people, and they would surely accuse the city guards of allowing a demon invasion.

The mysterious man, having easily dealt with Netham, slowly turned and looked at Melsfield.

He rested his weathered bronze-yellow spear on his shoulder and let out a laugh.

"Melsfield, how pathetic. You've been reduced to this state by an enemy like this?"

"...Melsfield paused, then furrowed her delicate brows. "Cess!"

Cess's helmet parted like a beast opening its mouth, revealing his true face. He was slightly older than Melsfield, nearing thirty, with a short braid tied at the back, "Sorry I'm late. I ran into some trouble on the way—those priests mistook me for a demon and wouldn't let me pass. It took me half a month of explaining to clear things up. I really worked up a sweat convincing them."

"It's... fine," Melsfield lowered her head and let out a relieved breath. "As long as you're back, Your Majesty needs your strength."

"Oh?" Cess raised his head and glanced around, casting a casual eye over the four corpses on the ground. "Has the capital already become this weak? Some common bandit can just barge in and launch a surprise attack."

Melsfield clenched her teeth and barely managed to rise to her feet.

"The story is a long one. You've been away from the capital too long; there's much you don't know..."

Melsfield had no time to catch up with Cess. Instead, she hurried back to check on His Majesty.

On the way, Melsfield explained the current situation to the returning Cess in full.

Cess listened and felt deeply shaken. He couldn't believe so many things had happened during his absence.

Just from Melsfield's account, he felt his heart skip beats, as though he had missed out on so much.

"That great sword master Elkyn—I've heard his name even out here. I didn't expect him to be this arrogant."

"Arrogant?" Melsfield thought of that great sword master and felt a surge of anger rise within her. She ground her teeth as she said, "That bastard looked down on everyone and brought tremendous trouble upon His Majesty. He treated absolutely no one as worth his regard."

"I see..." Cess stroked his chin and said meaningfully, "Actually, I'm quite interested in strong opponents. If possible, I'd like to test my skills against that great sword master."

"Don't even think about it. That man's power is monstrous, far beyond anything we can comprehend." Melsfield urged him gently, thinking Cess still didn't understand how overwhelmingly strong Elkyn was—if he wanted to fight, he'd need to be on a comparable level at least.

"Hmm? Melsfield, aren't you someone who never likes to admit defeat? Why are you backing down so easily?" Cess found this odd.

"This is simply unavoidable. If you had the chance to face that great sword master Elkyn and witness that transcendent power with your own eyes, I doubt you'd have any desire to challenge him." Melsfield frowned and spoke very seriously.

"Are you joking? The guy flexes his muscles once and you've already lost all will to fight? That doesn't sound like you, Melsfield."

Cess's tone carried a teasing quality.

Melsfield glanced at him and said flatly, "I've given you my warning. How you choose to take it is up to you, but the situation remains unclear. Don't go provoking that great sword master Elkyn, or you might only make matters worse."

"Are you ordering me around? Given how much you fear that great sword master, I'm becoming ever more interested in him~" Cess smiled and spread his hands. "Since His Majesty has forbidden infighting and you never spar with me, I'll have to beat him from a different angle to prove myself victorious over you."

"What do you mean?" Melsfield stopped walking, annoyed by Cess's tone. This was a time of chaos; stirring up discord now would only cause trouble.

"If I defeat that great sword master, doesn't that prove I am the strongest among the Thorn Knights?" Cess wore an amused grin.

"Why do you always treat me as your rival?" Melsfield felt a nagging displeasure inside her.

"You're always called the leader of the Thorn Knights, but I think I'm more suited to the role. If it weren't for having joined the order too recently, I'm certain I'd be commanding the knights instead." Cess was blunt, holding nothing back.

Melsfield glanced at his carefree eyes, then looked away and walked ahead. "I've never considered myself a commander of the knights. As long as I can stay by His Majesty's side, I'm content to serve even as a squire."

A flicker of surprise passed through Cess's eyes. He narrowed them, gazing at Melsfield's retreating back, lost in thought...

◆

The conference hall was in utter disarray.

Morrison and Catherine had already returned here earlier.

Dozens of guards stood watch with alert eyes, fearing unknown dangers.

After slaughtering the Black Wolf Mercenary Group, the area had temporarily regained safety—just enough to resume operations here.

With the storm having passed, Elizabeth gently pressed her hand to her forehead. Her complexion was poor, clearly still shaken.

Protected by Morrison, Elizabeth had not been physically harmed, but the fright she had endured was certainly significant.

When Melsfield and Cess entered, they both knelt on one knee in unison.

"Your Majesty, are you alright? The danger has been eliminated; you may rest easy now," Melsfield said.

"You've worked hard." Elizabeth raised her head and spotted Cess beside her, her expression suddenly stunned. "Cess!?"

"It's been a long time, Your Majesty. I deeply apologize for arriving so late." Cess pressed a hand to his chest in a gesture of respect.

"There is no need to blame yourself so. Now is a time of crisis for the empire. The fact that you've returned is the greatest support you could offer." Elizabeth offered a smile. Though Cess's return might not turn the tide, it was better than nothing—the more strong allies, the better the odds.

"You flatter me, Your Majesty..." Cess smiled faintly, a touch of pride in his heart.

"The empire now needs your strength. I hope you will help me overcome this present crisis." Elizabeth said earnestly.

"Rest assured, Your Majesty. Since I've returned, it is my duty to lift your burdens." Cess spoke with confidence, then shifted his tone. "However, the house of Overfly is unduly powerful, and a mysterious strongman sits in attendance. Four knights alone may find this rather difficult. I wonder if Your Majesty has any strategy prepared?"

"Against forces beyond our ability to confront, strategy holds limited value. Therefore, I intend to invite someone to lend us support." Elizabeth's expression revealed a hint of helplessness.

Morrison and Catherine looked at Elizabeth in surprise. They hadn't expected the queen to lower herself to seek reinforcements; they had thought she would persevere stoically to the end.

Indeed, Elizabeth and Isabella were different. The older sister was proud and haughty, while the younger was far more diplomatic.

"May I ask, Your Majesty, who you plan to summon for our aid?" Melsfield inquired curiously.

"...Elizabeth was silent for a moment, sensing there was no need to reveal this just yet. She chose to remain somewhat mysterious.

"When that person arrives, you will understand."

title: Chapter 23 — Monthly Ticket Plus Updates
content:
Chapter 23 — Monthly Ticket Plus Updates

Volume 12 · Chapter 23

A few days later—

The war had spared Rexem, and it rested in a relatively calm state.

However, as the conflict between the Olfrey family and the empire intensified, more and more people were left homeless.

They were forced to abandon their homes and flee from the war-torn heartland, with Wales in the far west becoming the best choice.

The streets and alleys of Rexem were far busier than usual, packed with people coming and going in a slightly cramped atmosphere.

Most of them weren't locals of Rexem, but refugees from elsewhere who had come to escape the turmoil of war.

Many traveled with their families, stopping by the roadside to rest, or, feeling uneasy, pressing onward deeper into Wales.

The massive influx of people had Prince, the captain of the stationed force, running around in a complete tangle, and he could only assign additional hands to maintain order.

Alice and Merlin had been keeping a low profile recently, instead enjoying a long-earned peaceful life.

Merlin spent his days with nothing better to do, wandering aimlessly through the streets of Rexem or going to drink with Hobbes.

Alice, meanwhile, was busy with her training, hoping to sharpen her strength even further—at the very least, to reach a level where she wouldn't hold Merlin back.

However, two days prior, Merlin and Hobbes had drunk a little too much and returned home very late, which instantly made Alice furious and filled her with anxious dread.

Thinking of Merlin's usual habit of flirting with women wherever he went, Alice suspected he had gone out to fool around.

So this morning, Merlin felt rather helpless and somewhat caged—Alice insisted on tagging along wherever he went, terrified he might slip away on his own.

Merlin found that conversing with a character like Hobbes was far more interesting than dealing with Alice, and he insisted on taking a day off, refusing to accompany Alice on her training.

Alice believed that Merlin always went astray thanks to Hobbes, and her resentment toward the old man grew deeper by the moment.

With a crowd of good-for-nothing friends by his side, could Merlin really learn anything good? Impossible!

And on top of that, he went fooling around by himself but insisted on dragging Merlin along with him—no morals whatsoever...

A wave of sour jealousy rose in Alice's heart. She thought to herself: I'm a beautiful young lady—could I possibly rank lower than some old man in Merlin's eyes?

At the Adventurers Guild, Merlin and Alice sat close together, their invisible aura of affection making many a single person nearby barely able to endure it.

Hobbes, clutching his wineglass, sat alone across from them, looking somewhat panicked, and occasionally had to endure Alice's resentful glare.

The three of them sat around a table, occasionally chatting about the current situation of the empire.

After all, this topic was extremely hot right now—everyone was speculating whether the empire was on the verge of a dynastic change.

Hobbes slowly lifted his eyelids, casting a wary glance at Alice, looking every bit like a thief.

What's with her? Seriously...

He could have been having a perfectly pleasant chat with Merlin, but because Alice was there, he couldn't say whatever he wanted.

For instance, he could have mentioned to Merlin the pretty girls he'd spotted recently, or joked about how Lucia's derrière had grown another size~

But with Alice hanging around, it felt like he was under surveillance. As a fellow member of the Wife-Tyrant Club, he certainly couldn't drop dirty jokes that might get Merlin in trouble at a time like this.

Besides, had Alice been a bit too strict lately? She kept clinging to Merlin and following him everywhere, as docile as ever...

Hobbes calmly took a sip of beer, stealing a look of admiration toward Merlin, who was busy reading the newspaper.

He couldn't help but think that Merlin was ridiculously impressive. They were both Black Iron-rank adventurers, yet Hobbes had none of the same charm Merlin possessed when it came to picking up women.

After all, Alice was a Saint-tier powerhouse widely respected in society—yet she could be so thoroughly tied down by Merlin. It was truly a strange phenomenon. Was it perhaps because Merlin had recently exceeded his quota of household chores?

Hobbes recalled the rumor about Merlin conquering Alice with his legendary big banana, and a wisp of wicked smile crept onto his face—

Holy crap! That's an innate talent. I can't compete. I really can't...

Alice caught the lecherous grin on Hobbes's face and instantly boiled with anger. She slammed her palm hard on the table and snapped, "Hobbes! What are you laughing at?!"

"Pfft!" Hobbes sprayed the beer in his mouth, hastily wiping the table with his sleeve. "...I-I wasn't laughing at anything! Alice, will you please calm down? I haven't done anything to provoke you recently..."

"Not laughing at anything?" Alice narrowed her eyes and said sternly, "Then why do I sense such a slimy aura..."

"Cough! Cough!" Hobbes started coughing and put on an innocent old-man act. "It's all in your imagination! Don't you have a huge bias against me? You always look at me through colored glasses. I'm the most upright person in the entire guild. There's no such word as 'slimy' in my dictionary."

"Who the hell would believe you? You took Merlin to that kind of place as soon as he arrived, and you still dare call yourself an upright person?" Alice growled like a young lioness on the verge of anger.

"Well..." Hobbes broke out in a cold sweat and suddenly found himself speechless.

"A few days ago, Merlin came home so late—was it you, you old pervert, who took him out fooling around again?!" Alice had been holding back for too long and could no longer contain herself.

"N-no..." Hobbes furrowed his brows, leaning forward with his hands spread wide in an innocent pose. "A few days ago, Merlin and I were just drinking a bit too much here at the guild. We didn't go to... any strange places to fool around."

Alice was so furious she drew the slender sword at her waist in one motion, the blade pressing against Hobbes's neck. "I want to hear the truth. Don't you dare try to糊弄 me with excuses. Do you hear me?!"

This commotion attracted quite a few curious glances from around the guild, everyone wondering what had happened.

But Hobbes was accustomed to stirring up trouble, and who knew what had set Alice off again—so the crowd largely ignored it.

"Uh..." The wineglass in Hobbes's hand fell to the floor. He looked down at the slender sword at his neck, the cold steel making him shiver. "N-no, no, Alice, please calm down. If there's a problem, we can talk it out. No need to draw your sword every time—what if you lose control by accident and hurt me?"

"Save it. I want the truth." Alice pressed insistently.

"You can just ask Merlin. Please stop threatening me with a sword!" Hobbes forced a smile, genuinely afraid of Alice. If she had been drinking, she might have gone and chopped the Empire's queen herself.

"I suspect you two colluded and cooked up some excuse together. So spit it out—where did you two go that night?" Alice held the sword to his throat.

"Why are you interrogating me?! Alice, you should be the one pressuring your own Merlin!" Hobbes looked on the verge of tears, a trace of sorrow in his expression—

"You can't just pick on me because you pity your pretty little sugar baby at home!"

"One day after another coming to me for free food and drinks, the other day after day drawing a sword to threaten me to death..."

"What am I supposed to do?! I'm completely desperate here..."

title: Chapter 24 — Letter
content:
Chapter 24 — Letter

Volume 12 · Chapter 24

"I've done nothing wrong, have I? You two are bullying me like this, is there any humanity left in you?..."

Hobbes felt the coldness of the rapier pressed against him, his eyes glistening with tears, looking pitiful indeed.

It seemed Hobbes had been putting up with that scolding pair of humans for a long time. Today, pushed to the brink by Alice, he finally couldn't hold it back and vented his grievances.

...Alice felt a wave of awkwardness. If she could press Merlin for information, she would have long ago. The problem was she couldn't beat that demon with force, so coercive interrogation would only get her clobbered in return.

In short, Alice was a coward. She picked on the weak and feared the strong. Since she couldn't defeat Merlin, she settled for taking out her frustration on poor Hobbes.

Merlin found himself unable to watch anymore. After all, Hobbes had treated him to plenty of drinks. If Alice really slipped up and cut him, his reliable meal ticket would be ruined.

So Merlin lowered his newspaper and looked at Alice with an exasperated expression. He said seriously,

"Put your sword away. Stop causing a scene. Didn't you say the guild forbids fighting? And besides, a mithril-ranked adventurer pointing a sword at an iron-ranked adventurer—shouldn't you feel ashamed bullying someone weaker? Just keep quiet..."

Hobbes glanced sideways at Merlin and thought this guy spoke quite bluntly. Alice would be angry about that, right?

After all, Merlin relied on her at home and probably had no real authority, did he?

Hobbes's expression stiffened. He imagined the foul-tempered Alice committing domestic violence right there on the spot, and he immediately began to shiver.

However, Alice's reaction was quite different from what Hobbes had expected...

Alice looked at Merlin, hesitated for a few seconds, and then obediently sheathed her sword. She glared silently, her cheeks puffed up like a provoked pufferfish.

Hobbes frowned, finding Alice's reaction utterly baffling.

With Alice's terrible temper, she should be arguing with Merlin, right?

What was going on? What method had Merlin used to tame Alice so perfectly? Incredible...

Hobbes stroked his chin, his mind inevitably drifting toward more suggestive thoughts. "

"I'm not causing trouble! It's your fault for coming home so late the day before yesterday, sneaking off to do something filthy behind my back!" Alice glared at Merlin, resentment clear on her face.

"Tch! Why do you have such an overactive imagination?" Merlin raised his eyebrows. "I just drank a bit too much with Hobbes the other day, which is why I got home late. That's all."

"I'd rather believe the devil went to heaven. You with your track record, how many times have you lied to me?" Alice muttered resentfully.

"Well..." Merlin scratched his cheek, a bead of cold sweat trickling down his forehead. He thought the count really was high. Who told Alice to be so gullible~

"Really...

Alice lowered her head and grumbled angrily,

"It's already so late. Why not just come straight home instead of wandering around outside? Only abnormal people don't come home at that hour. You're not homeless, you know. Wandering around like a vagrant outside—don't you feel ashamed?"

Hobbes calmly took a sip of beer, his expression twisting. He figured this must be Alice's way of showing concern. Surprisingly clumsy, wasn't it?

"Huh? What do you mean I look like a vagrant? You're insulting me..." Merlin's brows knit tightly, feeling like Alice was inventing new ways to insult him.

"Pfft!"

Hobbes sprayed his drink everywhere, screaming internally. Good heavens! Merlin was a peculiar flower among men.

Not only did he fail to sense Alice's care, but he also took her委婉 way of expressing it as an insult.

Hobbes was somewhat at a loss. He felt Alice and Merlin's personalities were practically incompatible. That they could be together was nothing short of a miracle!

Alice's expression remained blank, but her eyes showed traces of helplessness and disappointment.

She hadn't meant to scold Merlin at all. She simply wanted to say that she would worry when he came home so late.

Instead, Merlin looked at her with clearly hostile eyes, as if provoking her.

Alice's anger surged. Feeling that her kindness had been thrown back in her face, she fired back irritably.

"So what if I'm insulting you?! You have the nerve to run around outside? Have you considered my feelings?!"

"I am a worshipper of freedom! Do I need to report to you what I do? Don't make me laugh!" Merlin sneered, ignoring Alice's mood entirely.

"Grr!!" Alice's anger rose sharply. If she could beat Merlin, she would have already flipped out.

"Hey hey hey! Stop arguing. This is the guild, not your own home. Creating a family scene here will make us a laughingstock," Hobbes jumped out to mediate. "Let me tell you privately. We have a lot of single older folks in our guild who love watching couples break up. You two shouldn't become their table talk. Within three days, it'll spread through every street and alley of Rexum..."

Merlin and Alice shot each other sidelong glares, clear disgust deep in their eyes. Both let out snorts and fell silent, entering what amounted to a cold war.

Hobbes felt somewhat awkward but dared not speak. After all, nothing was more troublesome than getting caught in a quarrel.

Merlin ignored the angry Alice beside him and continued reading his newspaper—

「The Ofrae family army approaches the imperial capital; the queen faces an unprecedented crisis!」

Although the country was in turmoil, some newspapers remained remarkably dedicated, continuously reporting on the front lines so that many could understand the current situation.

Merlin didn't even need to read the newspaper to deduce the grim reality. Just by looking at the increasing number of refugees outside, it was clear that life in the imperial capital was not easy.

Merlin wasn't worried about the queen's fate, but rather concerned about himself.

He knew Alice's personality too well. She liked to meddle in other people's affairs. Could this little righteous guardian watch refugees starve to death outside? Impossible.

Alice would certainly let her compassion run wild, emitting a saintly halo, and go all out to rescue those helpless strangers.

Recently, the food at home had already been given away by Alice. But against the massive tide of refugees, those provisions were but a drop in the ocean.

Merlin seriously suspected that Alice might one day impulsively hand over everything they owned to relieve the refugees.

Although Merlin deeply appreciated Alice's humane nature and the warmth she radiated, and didn't want to interfere too much...

Sacrificing their own interests to help refugees was a different matter entirely. Merlin didn't see himself as running an orphanage, nor did he possess such lofty moral standards.

So regarding those pitiful refugees, Merlin believed that helping them was a matter of conscience, but not helping them was equally justifiable. He felt no responsibility or obligation either way.

However, Merlin was worried Alice might lose her head in a moment of passion.

So Merlin paid more attention to the root cause of this problem—the war.

If the war were quelled, the refugee problem would naturally be resolved!

Once peace returned, these refugees would go back to their hometowns and resume their lives...

"The war seems to be nearing its end recently, Hobbes. What do you think?" Merlin asked curiously.

"Does that need saying? The Britannian dynasty will collapse within half a month," Hobbes gave his guess.

"Half a month? That fast?" Merlin was somewhat surprised.

"Think about it. How long did the Ofrae family take to march from the north all the way to the imperial capital? Not very long, right? That reveals a major issue..." Hobbes stroked his small mustache.

"What issue?" Merlin sat up straight.

"The ruler won't tolerate fighting on their own territory because it damages property, so Duke Ofrae reached the capital in such short time..." Hobbes paused and lowered his voice. "The Britannian royal family is merely hanging on by a thread. The Ofrae family's strength is on a completely different level. The royals can do nothing against them."

"Oh~" Merlin nodded, finding Hobbes's reasoning sound.

"Perhaps the royal family is already a spent arrow. Us common folk shouldn't bother worrying blindly. Let's wait for the proclamation of the new kingdom..." Hobbes showed traces of pessimism, somewhat uneasy about the future.

Just then, Lucía walked over from behind the counter and placed a letter on the table in front of Merlin. "Mr. Merlin, you have mail. It should have arrived this morning."

"Oh?" Merlin picked up the unopened letter, inner curiosity rising—

A letter? Who sent it to me?

No way!?

Could it be that Lilith found out about my dark secret~

title: Chapter 25 — Invitation
content:
Chapter 25 — Invitation

Volume 12 · Chapter 25

Merlin looked at the envelope with a puzzled expression; he rarely communicated with others, so there shouldn't be anyone idle enough to write him a letter.

The only guess was his sister Lilith, far away in the Death Swamp; only she would have a reason to write to him.

Merlin thought of his overly controlling sister, and he couldn't help feeling gloomy.

He had always sent letters anonymously, so logically Lilith shouldn't know where he was, right?

"Who sent you the letter?"

Alice beside him had the same doubt, reaching out to take it, wanting to see what was written.

As a result, Merlin was quick-eyed and quick-handed, hiding the letter behind his back, his face full of vigilance.

"What are you doing? Still trying to snatch it?"

"What's that reaction? I just want to look." Alice said, puffing her cheeks.

"Tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue, speaking solemnly: "This is a letter addressed to me, not to you, so don't just barge in and try to take a look, okay?"

"What's wrong with looking? Petty!" Alice's curiosity itched unbearably; the more Merlin refused to let her see, the stronger her urge to peek.

"Come on, this isn't about being petty or not; you're trying to invade my privacy. The letter is addressed to me, what right do you have to look?" Merlin said with a complex expression, feeling Alice was going too far.

"Fine, if you don't want to look, then don't. As if I care—humph!" Alice turned her face away, sulking at Merlin.

Merlin couldn't be bothered with the huffy Alice; instead, he stared at the unknown letter, lost in thought.

Normally, it shouldn't be a letter from Lilith; it should be from someone else.

Merlin carefully examined the information on the envelope: only his address, no sender's address.

This is obviously the same as the letters he sends—both are anonymous, so there's no way to trace who sent it.

Even the wax seal on it is ordinary, revealing no useful information.

Thus, Merlin, unable to figure it out, didn't think further and simply tore open the top of the letter, pulling out the contents.

Merlin thought that if someone could send him a letter, there might be a secret; before looking at the content, he cautiously observed his surroundings like a thief.

Luka had delivered the letter and left, Hobbs calmly drank his beer, and Alice was sulking with her face turned to the other side.

Merlin felt the situation was still safe, so he openly unfolded the letter paper, looked at the content, and immediately widened his eyes.

Although the content wasn't lengthy, it was extremely shocking; just looking at Merlin's expression told how stunned he was.

"Dear Lord Merlin, although it hasn't been long since our last meeting, I have never forgotten the terrible things you did to me in the little cottage."

"However, the purpose of my writing this letter is not to blame you for anything, but I hope you can come to the imperial capital to discuss some matters."

"Of course, whether you come or not depends on your willingness; I won't force you to do anything, but there are some things I must say upfront.... J"

"According to my investigation, I have learned some of your secrets; you are actually the Elgin Swordmaster wandering in the imperial capital, right?"

"No matter how you hide, the fact that Elgin Swordmaster is an imperial wanted criminal is indisputable, and I now know your identity."

"But you have always concealed your identity; I suppose you have your own reasons.... J"

"So whether you come or not, Lord Merlin, please consider it yourself, but I cannot guarantee that your identity won't be made public."

That is the content of the letter; there is no joint signature at the end, so one can say the other party is hiding their identity to a great extent.

But Merlin doesn't need to guess; it's easy to know who it is, after all, the embarrassing incident in the little cottage just happened not long ago.

Merlin hesitated a moment, then lifted the letter to his nose and sniffed carefully; although the scent was faint, he could still catch a hint of a familiar aroma.

Based on my experience, I judge that this letter paper carries the queen's scent! ? Or that familiar scent.....

Merlin quickly balled up the letter into a lump; his heart couldn't calm down, feeling that after his identity was exposed, things had become troublesome.

Beside him, Alice had just wanted to peek, but Merlin destroyed the letter; this strange reaction startled Alice.

"How... how? What does the letter say?"

On the opposite side, Hobbs' face also showed some doubt, thinking Merlin's behavior was odd, as if he had been caught with his hands in the cookie jar.

"Ah?" Merlin, as if waking from a dream, looked at Alice, stuffed the balled letter into his pocket, planning to later secretly tear it into pieces and throw it away—"Nothing much?"

"Nothing? Then why are you acting like a thief?" Alice asked suspiciously.

"Yeah, Merlin, did something happen?" Hobbs asked curiously.

"No, no, it's just an ordinary...." Merlin chuckled, giving a casual explanation—

"There's no need to talk about this; anyway, no one would believe I'm the Elgin Swordmaster."

"Even if I did, I'd probably be laughed at by Alice and Hobbs."

After the matter was temporarily settled, on the way home.

Alice kept thinking about the letter's content, really wanting to know what was written on it, or who the sender was.

However, having considered that it would involve Merlin's privacy, Alice didn't feel comfortable pressing him for answers.

After all, Alice felt that she and Merlin weren't truly husband and wife, so they still needed some space.

If they were truly husband and wife, sharing secrets would be normal.

But as nominal spouses, forget it; Alice felt that constantly prying into Merlin's secrets would make her seem annoying.

So Alice could only suppress her doubts, hoping Merlin would voluntarily tell her.

Alice felt that if Merlin regarded her as a trustworthy companion, he would surely share the secret.

However, Merlin had no intention of doing so; he planned to handle this trouble entirely on his own.

Merlin felt his handling was a bit off; he shouldn't have meddled and rescued Elizabeth in the first place.

This caused his identity to be exposed, and troubles came flocking in, annoying him to death.

Merlin absolutely does not want to admit to being the Elgin Swordmaster; if he did, living a peaceful life would be almost impossible.

But now Merlin's true identity has been discovered by the imperial queen; he feels his weakness has been grasped by her, and this feeling of being controlled is not pleasant at all.

As long as Elizabeth intends to fight to the death and begins to suppress Merlin with an iron fist, it will become an endless battle.

However, Merlin feels Elizabeth is more rational than her sister; she didn't use force but sent a mysterious letter, wanting to meet face to face, so there might still be some room for maneuver.

Merlin let out a deep sigh, gazing at the setting sun on the horizon; the blood-red light was blindingly bright.

It seems I must go alone to the meeting.

Even if it's a Hongmen banquet, I still want to go and take a chance.

I want to see what kind of tricks this so-called great queen is playing.

title: Chapter 26 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 26 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Votes

Volume 12 · Chapter 26

Evening.

Merlin and Alice held their dinner.

Checking the time, it was already very close to bedtime, yet Merlin still had no intention of saying anything about his troubles.

On the surface Alice appeared calm, but inwardly she was growing anxious, hoping Merlin would bring up the letter himself.

But Merlin had no intention of dragging Alice into it; he wanted to handle it on his own.

Because based on past experience, whenever this girl got involved, things always became extremely complicated, tied up worrying about every angle.

At this moment the two of them silently ate their meal, not uttering a single word, and the atmosphere felt rather strange.

The house wasn't particularly large, but it was warm and cozy.

Bright lamplight swayed gently above, casting a warm tone.

Today Alice was the one cooking, and while it wasn't as good as Merlin's culinary skills, she had improved considerably.

She no longer grabbed ingredients and threw them into a pot haphazardly, cooking in a confused mess like before.

Alice had picked up no small amount of Merlin's cooking techniques, and she'd even encountered many unfamiliar new terms—though she didn't understand a single one of them.

It seemed that subconsciously, Alice was rapidly marching down the path of a homemaker, completely unaware of it herself.

Watching the time slip away rapidly, Alice grew restless. She couldn't help but look up and asked bluntly.

"What did that letter say today? You've been gloomy ever since you finished reading it. Do you have something on your mind?"

"Hm?" Merlin looked up, feeling a bit uncomfortable at Alice's complicated expression. "Nothing. Just some small matter."

Alice rolled her eyes. Thinking that if it were such a small thing, why the troubled look? Was he telling her or not? She wouldn't die! Maybe she could actually help.

"Then... aren't you going to tell me?"

Seeing Alice's expectant look, Merlin immediately felt annoyed.

Even if he told her everything, he was Elgin the Great Sword Hero, and his true identity had been discovered.

Alice would definitely say: Please act normal. Stop with the dramatic persona. You really think you're Elgin the Great Sword Hero? That person is way more outstanding than you, blah blah blah....

Merlin didn't even need to probe—he would definitely get that response, so he was too lazy to explain.

Besides, this matter had little to do with Alice. It was entirely a game between him and Queen Elizabeth, with no need to drag Alice in.

"It's not something particularly important, so don't worry about it."

"What do you mean don't worry about it? I can see you're miserable and seem troubled, so I wanted to see if I could help!" Alice's eyes darted away, expressing her concern in a rather tactful manner.

"Why the sudden enthusiasm? Shouldn't you be happy that I'm tangled up in trouble~?" Merlin said with a teasing tone.

"Why would I be happy?! Am I the type of person who gloats over others' misfortunes?!" Alice retorted resentfully.

"Yesss~" Merlin grinned and asked cautiously, "When things are abnormal, it must be suspicious. Come on, confess—are you plotting something?"

"That's enough!" Alice slammed her palm on the table and rose, her expression darkening. She thought: I was only trying to be kind, so why does Merlin always push me away? Plotting something? With someone as penniless as him, what benefit could there possibly be?!

"....What's wrong?" Merlin frowned, not understanding what Alice was so agitated about.

"Merlin, we... " Alice hesitated, then said, "We count as... as comrades, right?"

Merlin thought for a moment and nodded. "I suppose so."

"Then...." Alice paused and spoke seriously, "I hope you won't hide things from me. If you have any troubles, you can tell me. If possible, I hope you can trust me a little more."

After saying that, Alice turned and left without looking back, hoping Merlin would confide in her the next day.

But Merlin watched Alice's departing figure with some difficulty, and helplessly thought—

She speaks so well, but what good would it do even if I told her?

Alice couldn't help with anything; she would only make things worse.

To simply and clearly settle things with the human queen, he still had to go alone.....

The next day before dawn.

Merlin rose early, while it was still dark.

He quickly packed the essentials needed for the road and still planned to depart alone, heading to the Imperial City to meet Elizabeth.

Now Merlin faced a predicament where he was under everyone's spotlight, with Elizabeth using it to threaten him.

Although the letter hadn't said much, the undertones of a warning were overwhelming.

Merlin didn't want to face the situation after his identity was exposed—things were fine as they were now.

If his identity were exposed, Merlin's peaceful life would no longer exist. He'd have to deal with legions of people coming in admiration, or enemies appearing out of nowhere, and most critically, tearing relations with the Empire would mean no easy days ahead.

Even though Merlin didn't fear any enemies or conflict with the Empire, at this moment there was something he needed to protect.

Remembering Alice's warm figure hanging laundry not long ago, he felt a certain attachment to such scenes.

So Merlin wanted to guard the hard-won peace he currently had, and he certainly didn't want to see Alice looking worried.

Merlin draped on his black robe, tucked his katana at his waist, and wiped the silver mask in his hand.

"Preparations are mostly complete. Let's go...."

Merlin put on the mask and quietly left the house. On the table he left Alice a letter, telling her what he was going to do—

「Alice, don't panic if you can't find me. I have no intention of abandoning you and running away.」

「Actually, yesterday's letter didn't contain any big secret. It was just that some rich woman in the Imperial City wants to meet me.」

「So I need to go out for a bit. I'll be back soon, don't worry.」

Not long after.

Alice woke up and saw Merlin was nowhere to be found, instantly panicking.

Her intuition told her Merlin probably wasn't the irresponsible type—not with their shared debt still looming.

If that suddenly fell entirely on Alice's shoulders, she'd want to die.

He wouldn't just leave without a word.

Alice didn't bother fixing her mussed appearance from just waking up and searched everywhere for traces of Merlin's departure.

She easily found the note on the living room table. Alice nervously picked it up and read it carefully....

Alice's expression instantly became complicated. Surprise, annoyance, dissatisfaction, and worry all surged up at once.

Rich woman! ?

What rich woman! ?

Alice thought about it carefully before it clicked—previously, Merlin had stolen a rich woman's stockings.

Once she grasped the meaning, Alice became enraged and tore Merlin's letter into shreds.

Alice felt her eyes tighten, with a sudden urge to cry, and her heart churned with imbalance—

Damned Merlin!

This is openly cheating on me, isn't it! ?

Slipping out to flirt with a rich woman and then deliberately leaving a note to tell me about it—how cruel can you be....

title: Chapter 27 — Hijacking
content:
Chapter 27 — Hijacking

Volume 12 · Chapter 27

Several days later.

The main forces of Aofulei had already breached imperial territory.

Nearly a hundred thousand elite troops marched valiantly and proudly straight toward the heart of the capital.

Along the way they easily swept through the resistance, and regional lords throughout the land suffered heavy losses.

Although Aofulei had lost an arm, it in no way dampened his ambition to become emperor.

As long as his side possessed the Four Elemental Sword Saints, any resistance force within the empire was hardly worth mentioning.

At the temporary palace, Elizabeth wore a permanently clouded expression, her heart deeply uneasy.

Because according to the combined army's marching speed, they would assemble outside the capital city in just three days.

By then Elizabeth would either have to surrender or be forced to fight; either option spelled the end of the Britain dynasty.

Moreover, there was still no word from Great Swordmaster Elkine; she did not know whether he would come to the capital to meet her in person.

Elizabeth sighed, her eyes shifting repeatedly. If Merlin refused to come help her, she had already decided to minimize casualties and surrender to Grand Duke Aofulei.

Maysfield watched the queen's sorrowful appearance and felt a sudden pang of disappointment. Being unable to share Elizabeth's burden made her feel particularly inadequate.

But this was unavoidable. Though Maysfield was a Saint-tier expert, she was not a god. Facing a vast horde of a hundred thousand cavalry, she was equally at a loss and could only silently await the final judgment.

Even without engaging the enemy's mysterious Sword Saint, the hundred-thousand-strong army's sheer numbers tactic and relentless attrition left Maysfield with zero options — killing her twenty times over would be no difficulty at all.

After all, magic power and fighting spirit were not infinite. Maysfield was mortal, too. What could she possibly accomplish against such a powerful army?

However, unlike the other Thorn Knights, Maysfield harbored special feelings for Elizabeth and had already steeled herself to the conviction of dying alongside the queen, guarding her until the very last moment.

"Your Majesty, the combined army drawing close to our city walls grows nearer by the moment. Enemy scouts have been coming to gather intelligence from time to time. What should we do?"

Facing Maysfield's inquiry, Elizabeth fell silent for a moment, then replied evenly, "First, wait patiently. Trying to turn the tide relying only on us is far too difficult. What we need now is a boost of morale — that is, reinforcements."

"Reinforcements?" Maysfield furrowed her delicate brows, confusion rising within her. "Can reinforcements alone reverse our dire situation? I wonder which army would possess such strength — surely not aid from another empire?"

"Not any army. It's one person." Elizabeth replied calmly.

"Huh?! N-next—"

Maysfield stood dumbfounded, finding it hard to believe. She had no idea who this reinforcements figure was.

Could the queen really intend to confront a well-equipped combined army with a single individual?!

She found it hard to imagine any powerful figure capable of such an unthinkable feat.

That was an entire army of a hundred thousand people! They weren't some crops to be casually reaped! Even a Saint-tier expert would be worn to death by sheer numbers — let alone the fact that a mysterious Sword Saint held command on the opposing side!

Unconsciously, Maysfield's mind flashed with the image of Great Swordmaster Elkine. Rumor had it that this man had once single-handedly overwhelmed a suddenly appearing undead legion.

Aside from that, Maysfield could hardly think of anyone else who could accomplish such a thing.

But Great Swordmaster Elkine bore a certain antagonistic relationship with the empire, so Maysfield felt it was unlikely to be him.

"That's right. Just one person." Elizabeth nodded.

"..." Maysfield's eyes widened, her voice filled with disbelief. "You can't be serious? The current situation is so desperate; relying on a single powerhouse to turn the tide is hardly realistic, unless that person's strength has reached utterly heaven-defying levels!"

"We can only pin our hopes on others now. If they refuse to help us, I will choose to surrender and minimize casualties." Elizabeth's tone was extremely calm, as if discussing something entirely casual.

Hearing Elizabeth's decision, Maysfield's heart was rocked by towering waves. This felt like the most catastrophic outcome imaginable.

Elizabeth was the supreme leader of the empire. Surrender and defeat led to the same outcome — neither would end well for her.

Think of any deposed ruler in history. None had ended well, had they?

Alive, she'd face humiliation and abuse. Dead, her body could be dug up and desecrated. There'd be no decency whatsoever!

Maysfield could not bear to see such a fate unfold. Moreover, Elizabeth was a woman who still possessed a captivating charm — who knew what she might endure after surrender?

"Your Majesty, you absolutely cannot surrender! Even dying in battle would be better than this decision to let others slaughter us at will! I am willing to fight for you until my last breath!"

"Now now, Windsor, I know you care about me, but as a sovereign, I must make choices. Rather than letting so many suffer — let me bear the responsibility of surrender alone." Elizabeth's tone radiated profound helplessness.

"... Maysfield opened her mouth, then closed it again, speechless.

"Don't worry. We are not yet at the end of our rope. There is still a chance." Elizabeth turned, her back to Maysfield.

"You may withdraw for now. I wish to rest."

"Very well, Your Majesty. Stay safe, and please summon me if anything unusual occurs."

Maysfield bowed her head, her expression fraught with worry, then abruptly turned and departed.

But halfway there, she stopped in her tracks, curiosity about that mysterious figure swelling within her.

"Th-then, Your Majesty, would you allow me to ask who that man is?"

Elizabeth was silent for a moment, then spoke leisurely —

"If all goes well..."

"You should know very soon."

Night fell deep.

The round moon, high in the sky, cast a cold, pale light.

Through the clear glass, it shone into Elizabeth's bedroom.

Elizabeth stood by the window, gazing at the tranquil scene outside, and a wave of reflection stirred within her.

This peace was merely temporary. Before long, the combined army of House Aofulei would trample upon this place.

Elizabeth felt the situation growing increasingly dire. She estimated that House Aofulei would launch their assault within these few days, and by then, whether to fight or surrender, she恐怕 wouldn't have a choice.

Her only hope probably lay with Great Swordmaster Elkine — this was her last straw.

A chill wind blew, and the heavy white curtains stirred gently.

"Ah... Wait!!!"

A dark figure suddenly appeared in the private bedroom. Judging by his build, a masked man.

This mysterious man had materialized behind Elizabeth in an uncanny instant and seized her.

Even if Elizabeth wanted to cry for help, her mouth had been covered before she knew it, and not a single sound could escape.

Merlin pressed close to Elizabeth's graceful, full-figured form, his hand around her throat.

It was as if he could snap her neck and kill the empire's queen at any moment.

Merlin leaned even closer to Elizabeth, his lips brushing against her ear, and said in a sinister tone —

"I hear you wanted to see me?"

"Well then..."

"Here I am now."

Chapter 28 — Extra Chapters for Monthly Votes

Volume 12 · Chapter 28

Merlin stands behind Elizabeth, embracing her delicate body, completely under his control since the second.

To outsiders, their position looks somewhat awkward, perhaps even suitable as a reference picture in a physiology textbook.

Merlin blocks Elizabeth's mouth with one hand and grips her throat with the other, preventing this queen from moving.

If Elizabeth dared to resist at this moment, she might lose her life before she knows it.

Merlin looks down at Elizabeth, his face full of mischief. He could make her completely disappear from this world in minutes if he wanted to.

He is the symbol of evil, the Great Demon Lord. How could a mere human queen dare threaten him? Does she not know how to write the word "death"?

Merlin finds himself laughing more and more, wondering what Elizabeth is thinking?

Can a weakling have the right to negotiate conditions? Absolutely not.

All initiative has always been in Merlin's hands and has never changed.

Actually, Merlin arrived in the imperial capital ahead of schedule this morning, easily avoiding everyone's sight and hiding in the temporary palace.

It's just that there are always people by Elizabeth's side, so it's not easy to make a move. The opportunity comes when the queen rests alone late at night.

At this moment, Merlin holds Elizabeth's life in his hand, while others simply don't know.

This means Merlin can kill and silence her. If Elizabeth dies, his secret as an Elgin Sword Saint will never be exposed, and his peaceful life will grow stable.

However, Merlin is not a complete demon, and he has no intention of becoming a killer who doesn't blink at taking lives. He still wants to figure out what Elizabeth wants to do?

→6E Novels

Merlin lowers his voice, using a tone nearly like a whisper to mock Elizabeth as she says,

"You really have a big guts, daring to threaten me?"

"To be honest, those who dared to threaten me are already dead."

"So, you will probably meet the same fate."

"I have things I want to protect, and the reason to reap your life is already sufficient."

"But I'm a bit curious. Since you know I'm the Elgin Sword Saint, you should understand my strength, right?"

"Still daring to come provoke me, are you not afraid of catching fire?"

After finishing, Merlin looks down at Elizabeth's frightened expression, very much wanting to know what this woman is really selling in her gourd?

Actually, Elizabeth is at the end of her rope, otherwise how could she possibly seek help from Merlin?

But Elizabeth had no choice; she had to gamble, using the method of attacking with poison.

Because Elizabeth and Merlin had brief contact before, she felt this man is not someone who cannot reason with, perhaps they could sit down and talk peacefully, perhaps he would become the key figure turning the situation around.

However, the way they met still caused Elizabeth some shock. This extremely rude move, as a queen, she is experiencing for the first time.

With my skill, leaving here without anyone noticing is utterly effortless; no one will discover who did it. As for my true..."

Although the person in front of Elizabeth looks like a weak woman, Merlin knows that no one among monarchs is a lamp that doesn't oil.

"I didn't mean to threaten you; I just purely want to chat face to face with you." Elizabeth's tone is quite calm, no panic showing.

"What? I don't want to get involved with royalty. Aren't you guys always wanting to clear me out?" Merlin says with a cold smile.

"That was my sister's strategy, not having much to do with me..." Elizabeth continues to defend herself, saying, "You once saved my life, so I still feel grateful to you, thinking the previous grievances can be resolved by sitting down and talking."

"Oh? So it seems..." Merlin raises an eyebrow, speaking with a meaningful tone, "You also have the matter of robbing your stockings on your mind, right?"

Elizabeth's face instantly turns red, like a crab cooked thoroughly, puffing out hot air, having to lower her head.

"Hah, actually shy, it's just a piece of intimate clothing, is it necessary to care so much?" Merlin says with a teasing tone.

"Not... it's not like that..." Elizabeth bites her lip, enduring the reddened face, as if she has endured for a long time, gathering her courage

"Mr. Merlin, please don't touch my chest while speaking, okay?"

"You are clearly a married man, please show some self-respect."

title: Chapter 29 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 29 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 12 · Chapter 29

Elizabeth hadn't wanted to say anything, but Merlin's grope had already been resting on her chest for quite some time.

She had been enduring the shame welling up inside her, but being so openly fondled by a man was unbearable for both body and mind.

At first, Elizabeth had wanted to pretend she hadn't noticed and endure until it passed, but in the end she found she couldn't do it.

With a burning hand plastered against her bosom, if she could still play dumb and keep quiet, she'd be worthy of a contest with the Ninja Turtles.

Originally, Elizabeth felt her life was in Merlin's hands, so she tried hard not to provoke him, and didn't dare complain immediately even though she was being taken advantage of.

But Elizabeth was a queen, and at the very least had basic dignity.

"Eh!?"

Merlin froze, feeling that the hand he'd put down to plug Elizabeth's mouth was now touching something round and soft.

The texture was like a sphere, yielding and full of mysterious elasticity.

Holy crap! This feel? Peak of life right here...

Merlin swiftly yanked his thieving hand off Elizabeth's bosom, but the other still gripped her throat, not letting go of the leverage over the imperial queen.

He coughed lightly to cover his embarrassment, using a serious tone to make excuses for himself.

"Umm... sorry, I didn't mean to on purpose just now, I was just subconsciously looking for somewhere to put my hand..."

"Uh..." The blush on Elizabeth's face hadn't faded yet, and she was instantly thunderstruck by Merlin's words, thinking, somewhere to put your hand!? Are you serious?! You literally grabbed my boobs! This is clearly sexual harassment on purpose! Can men not resist the invisible pull of a woman's chest or what!?

Actually, Merlin really hadn't meant it on purpose. He barely knew where his hand had landed just now.

It was possible Elizabeth's chest was so large that when he put his hand down, it just happened to rest right on top.

"D-don't joke around... You must be someone whose head is full of filthy thoughts, right? Robbing me of my clothes and then shamelessly assaulting my chest!" Elizabeth was a bit emotionally ruffled, scolding in a low voice, "You're already married, so why can't you control your depraved desires?"

"This..."

Merlin's expression became somewhat unnatural, feeling a bit awkward, as though Elizabeth had seized the moral high ground with no chance for rebuttal.

Damn it! It really is impossible to clear up a misunderstanding when you're framed, huh?

Wait... something seems a bit off here...

Merlin suddenly seemed to have discovered something. He became alert and narrowed his eyes as he questioned her.

"How did you find out I'm a married man?"

If Merlin remembered correctly, last time he met Elizabeth, the iron-rank adventurer card had already dissolved inside the lake fairy's body, and afterward he had applied for a replacement adventurer card.

So logically, Elizabeth shouldn't have known he was a married man. This could only point to one possibility.

"I..." Elizabeth hesitated, and after careful consideration told the truth, "I privately investigated you in detail. For me, uncovering your background wasn't difficult."

"Oh?"

Merlin felt uncomfortable, as if his secrets were being spied upon, and a ripple of anger rose within him.

He didn't like anyone knowing his background. If Elizabeth knew too much about him, he would have to ruthlessly silence her.

In Merlin's heart, this queen who appeared harmless on the surface was never someone he could trust.

Unlike Alice, who was relatively innocent and whom Merlin could lower his guard around and show some authenticity,

When facing a ruler skilled in political maneuvering and scheming, Merlin had no choice but to stay on his guard. He didn't want to end up hunted by all humanity with no place to survive in the human world.

Merlin tightened his grip on Elizabeth's neck slightly, testing as he asked,

"How much do you know about me right now?"

"Uh..."

Elizabeth saw Merlin's attitude become serious and couldn't help but feel frightened, remembering she was still being held hostage.

To put Merlin at ease and show she meant no harm, Elizabeth reluctantly shared some things.

"Based on the information I privately gathered, you must have smuggled into the country from another nation, correct?"

"Smuggled?" Merlin frowned, finding things a bit strange.

"That's right. You suddenly appeared within the empire's borders two years ago, with no prior warnings or any rumors about you beforehand. I think besides smuggling, there doesn't seem to be any other reasonable explanation." Elizabeth answered calmly.

Merlin stayed silent, wanting to continue listening and see just how much Elizabeth had actually figured out.

"When you became famous in Elgin, you weren't an adventurer. During that time you scammed food and drinks everywhere, got jointly wanted by restaurant owners, harassed several married women, was chased out of Manchester, and was later brought to Rexham by a woman named Alice Claudya, where you became an iron-rank adventurer, and finally married her." Elizabeth recounted steadily. Although the information sources were somewhat inaccurate, the basics were roughly correct.

Merlin was slightly surprised. Though his true origins hadn't been uncovered, almost every trace of his activities in the Britannia Empire had been captured. Also, harassing married women was completely unnecessary!

"Although your own identity still has some疑点 and seems quite mysterious, your spouse I've found out quite a bit about. She's quite extraordinary..." Elizabeth's expression showed a hint of amusement.

"What do you mean?" Merlin wondered internally. He himself was a demon residing in the Dead Swamp, but Alice was human, so it seemed normal she'd have more of her background uncovered.

"Your spouse, Miss Alice, seems to have previously lived near the Great Snow Mountain. After coming of age, she joined the Holy Church's Crusade against the First Demon Lord Palace and became the 233rd Hero, rumored to have been defiled by the Arrogant Monarch." Elizabeth paused and added with a sigh, "People have always thought the 233rd female Hero had fallen into the Arrogant Monarch's sexual slavery, never expecting she would quietly and low-key become an adventurer. It's truly lamentable..."

Merlin's inner heart grew slightly unsettled. To be honest, before coming here he had somewhat looked down on Elizabeth, this human queen, thinking she was at most someone who got a good reincarnation and relied entirely on foolish knights for protection.

But Merlin hadn't expected Queen Elizabeth to have done so much private groundwork, stripping Alice's background bare with almost no great secrets left.

Merlin couldn't help but sigh at his own insufficient understanding of the empire. At the very least, the covert intelligence network was indeed accurate and astonishing, actually able to provide so much information?

As befitting an empire with over four hundred years of heritage, its underlying foundations were real. It couldn't be worthless in every regard, or it would have perished N times over long ago.

However, Merlin's mood remained extremely complicated, and he had to secretly vent at the melodramatic rumors—

Get lost!

I've never once defiled Alice, you board-scrubbing nag!

And locking her up as a sexual slave kind of thing...

Damn it, who the hell started that rumor? Show yourself if you've got the guts!

Let me see if I don't slap you into a spinning top right where you stand!
