title: Chapter 30 — Treasure
content:
Chapter 30 — Treasure

Volume 12 · Chapter 30

"Your spouse later left the Holy Church, but because the legendary Hero's mithril armor was lost, enormous debt was incurred and has not yet been repaid." Elizabeth paused for a moment, then continued, "So after you married, it was counted as joint debt. That's truly bad luck."

"……" Merlin's expression darkened. It was like a scab that had just formed being torn open again. Who would've thought registering as a couple at the Adventurers Guild would merge debts?

"These are all the information I've investigated. I haven't concealed anything. I've expressed my sincerity for negotiation. What about you, Great Swordmaster Elgin?" Elizabeth pointed at the hand gripping her neck, signaling Merlin to let go.

But Merlin had no intention of releasing her. He narrowed his eyes and demanded, "Why were you secretly investigating so many things behind my back?"

"Because your strength makes me feel uneasy. Some matters must be clarified. No one would feel at ease about unknown, powerful forces beyond their control, right?" Elizabeth said earnestly.

Merlin remained silent, thinking this wasn't surprising. As the Empress of the Empire, maintaining the stability of her rule would naturally be her top priority.

"Besides, I want to negotiate with you. The outcome has already been decided before we even sit at the negotiating table. I need sufficient preparation." Elizabeth responded calmly, adding at last, "Though I know so many secrets, I haven't revealed them. Because you, as the Great Swordmaster Elgin, always hide your identity—I suppose you have your own reasons?"

"No special reasons. I just don't want trouble coming to me." Merlin said coolly.

"Meaning you want a quiet life? But with such huge debt, I imagine life isn't easy?" Elizabeth probed indirectly. If Merlin had desires and greed, this would be easy to handle. Merlin furrowed his brow, not in a good mood—he'd been hit right on the mark.

Isn't it easy? It's actually not easy at all!

Although life was relatively peaceful, he worried about trivial matters every day.

Constantly anxious about the future, especially when money was tight.

Actually, Merlin was quite the spoiled type, living hand-to-mouth. Being able to live alongside Alice, supporting each other, was already beyond his best performance.

Seeing that Elizabeth seemed sincere, it appeared she genuinely wanted to talk this through, which made things much easier.

So Merlin released Elizabeth and turned to sit comfortably in the chair like a grandmaster.

"What exactly is your purpose? Just say it plainly. I don't like beating around the bush. Guessing back and forth is too troublesome. Don't waste my precious time."

Elizabeth turned to face Merlin, deciding to be direct and state her request bluntly, "I wish to ask your help, Lord Merlin, to assist me in repelling the rebel forces invading from House Olafre."

Merlin took a deep breath and slightly closed his eyes, thinking it was indeed this matter after all.

Actually, Merlin had long guessed Elizabeth's little scheme in his heart, but never expected she would really want his help.

After all, his relationship with the Empire was somewhat like enemies. Asking for his help seemed very unrealistic.

But thinking about Elizabeth's current situation, Merlin could understand the other party's gambler's mentality.

"Help me? Sounds like a joke. You were hunting me everywhere before. Aren't you afraid I'll take revenge for past grievances?"

"That was my older sister's order, not mine. But for the trouble caused to you by my sister, I am willing to apologize and revoke the arrest warrant against you, and will no longer interfere with your life." Elizabeth put on a serious expression, adding, "So I hope you can set aside past grievances and help me at this critical moment. I will remember this kindness forever."

"Sorry, I'm not some saint. You want me to let it go just like that? That's too easy on you, isn't it?" Merlin rested his chin on his hand, his smile full of mockery.

Elizabeth frowned, suddenly at a loss for words, feeling that making such a request was indeed somewhat rude.

Merlin spread his hands and said with a half-smile, "Besides, I have no reason to help you. What does the Empire's survival have to do with me? An adventurer like me who wanders everywhere just needs to find a peaceful country and…"

"But if House Olafre becomes the ruler of the Empire, it will make the Empire worse than before. Wars will be more numerous than any period. And if they expand to other human nations, there will be no place to escape, unless it's the forbidden land of the demons." Elizabeth said with certainty. "I understand Grand Duke Olafre well. He's a man full of ambition. His greedy desires are hard to satisfy."

Hearing this, Merlin couldn't help but fall into deep thought, wondering whether to help Elizabeth save the Empire.

If what Elizabeth said was true and Olafre was indeed a man with enormous ambition, then wherever he hid, it seemed he wouldn't be able to live peacefully.

Plus, Alice was easily swept up by hot blood and might make unexpected moves.

Considering this, better to endure short pain than long pain. Before things escalated beyond control, handle it himself.

But… surely such a thing shouldn't be done for free?

Thinking of the tens of millions in debt on both him and Alice, it was suffocating. Perhaps he could take this opportunity to demand a lion's share, blackmail heavily.

After all, one Empire's power might just be enough to repay the enormous debt…

Merlin immediately stroked his chin, revealing a devilish evil smile, his clever little calculations clicking away in his mind.

"Helping you repel the invading enemies isn't impossible…"

The moment Elizabeth saw Merlin concede, her heart swelled with joy. "As long as Lord Merlin is willing to help me through this crisis, I'll agree to any request."

"…" Merlin chuckled. Seeing Elizabeth so enthusiastic made him quite happy. He felt his freedom was just around the corner. "Since you're so sincere, I can help you. But only… you understand what I mean, right?"

Elizabeth suddenly went quiet, her face flushing an eerie shade of red.

Looking at Merlin's lecherous, perverted smile, she felt strong resistance in her heart. But to protect the Empire, some sacrifices were necessary.

Fortunately, Elizabeth had long anticipated this situation and come prepared to play along.

"Fine, I understand."

After finishing speaking, Elizabeth went to open the cabinet and fumbled around for something.

Merlin stroked his chin, thinking this queen was quite the player—she must be going to fetch an invaluable treasure.

After returning, her face flushed, Elizabeth presented a delicate small box with both hands to Merlin. "Please accept this as my gift of thanks. I think this should satisfy you."

"Excellent, excellent. As long as it satisfies me, I can help you wipe out the invading army…"

Merlin made a serious promise and opened the box in front of Elizabeth.

But there were no jewels inside—only two pieces of silk fabric.

His expression froze, and he reached out to pick up and unfold the two items.

One was a flesh-colored stocking, the other was a black stocking…

Merlin looked up and blinked in confusion, his face full of disbelief—

Wait!

What's going on!?

Is the so-called gift this kind of nonsense?

Wanting to satisfy him with just two stockings…

Who does he think he is! Don't look down on people like that! Bastard! !

(#'皿')

title: Chapter 31 — Dreaming
content:
Chapter 31 — Dreaming

Volume 12 · Chapter 31

Elizabeth turned her back to Merlin, her expression somewhat complicated, seemingly not wanting him to see her current facial expression.

"I think this should satisfy you, right? I wore these a few days ago. They should perfectly match your requirements, satisfying your rather... peculiar mindset."

Elizabeth spoke euphemistically, refraining from using words like "pervert" or "disgusting."

Merlin looked at the two pairs of pantyhose in his hands, a giant "embarrassed" symbol flashing across his face, caught off guard by Elizabeth's gift of thanks—

What the hell! Does this human queen have shit for brains?!

What am I supposed to do with pantyhose! Does she really think I'm some kind of pervert?!

I can't eat these things, and they sure as hell can't be used to pay off debts!

And what's with deliberately wearing them a few days in advance?

Is she worried they wouldn't be "original flavor" enough to satisfy my perverted cravings!?!

Merlin immediately rolled his eyes and threw the pantyhose hard onto the floor, feeling thoroughly humiliated.

Go away! Who needs such boring stuff? Don't look down on people like that, you bastard!"

"Eh?! " Elizabeth was startled by Merlin's reaction. It was quite different from what she had imagined—she had thought this man would smile lecherously and obediently accept it. "Don't you like this kind of gift?"

"Like my ass! Don't go assuming my preferences!" Merlin's expression grew somewhat unhinged.

.....Elizabeth bit her lip, then plucked up the courage to mutter, "But you're clearly a fetishist. Receiving intimate clothing from a beautiful woman should make you overjoyed, shouldn't it?"

"Overjoyed my ass! Do beautiful women not shit?! Do you think the things you've worn are worth anything? I don't give a damn about them!" Merlin's brows furrowed tightly, his eyes bloodshot with anger.

Elizabeth calmed down slightly and extended her hand. "Since you don't like it, why did you rob my pantyhose last time? Please return them to me quickly."

A bead of cold sweat involuntarily trickled down Merlin's forehead. He thought: Elizabeth's white silk stockings were torn apart by Alice. Return them? Yeah, right!

But he couldn't mention that. That pair of stockings was leverage, to prevent Elizabeth from burning bridges.

If Elizabeth didn't behave, he planned to use that pair of stockings to thoroughly humiliate her.

So Merlin awkwardly cleared his throat twice and gave a calm, serious explanation.

"Cough! Well, I can't return them, but I also won't use them for anything weird, because I'm not some kind of fetishist. I just took them.... to keep as a memento..."

"A memento?"

Elizabeth wore a suspicious expression, sensing that Merlin was making excuses and was clearly a fetishist who refused to admit it.

But then she thought: Merlin was a married man. Maybe he had some collecting habit, to make up for regrets from his youth or something.

Elizabeth narrowed her eyes and probed with an odd tone, "Does your spouse know about your strange hobby? Collecting other women's private clothing—it's quite disgusting. Could it be that due to an unsatisfying private life, you're substituting sexual fantasies with women's clothing and emotionally cheating?"

"What nonsense? Stop talking nonsense!" Merlin felt uncomfortable under her stare and quickly changed the subject. "Let's not get hung up on pantyhose, okay? This is not what I need at all. What I truly need is money."

"Money?" Elizabeth paused, surprised that it could be solved with money, and felt a wave of relief. "How much do you want?"

"Ahem..." Merlin stroked his chin, a flicker of cunning merchant gleaming in his eyes. "Just help us pay off the debt we owe to the Holy Church? How about that? Not too excessive, right?"

"Pay it all off?!" Elizabeth's eyes widened, and she let out a startled cry, instinctively covering her mouth with her hand.

"Haha, what's with that reaction? You're the supreme ruler of the empire, after all. Paying off my debts shouldn't be difficult..." Merlin spoke casually, making it seem like he was just asking Elizabeth to do him a small favor.

But Elizabeth's shocked expression meant things were not simple—and this request was starting to feel like it would cost her dear.

The inherited Hero's Mithril Armor was extremely precious, passed down through the Holy Church for thousands of years, a legendary piece of protective gear worn by countless Heroes.

Back when they besieged the First Demon Lord Palace, if Alice hadn't been wearing that armor, she might have been killed by Merlin's Iaido Slash in the first wave.

Even fighters on the level of the Spear Hero had once been its owners—you can imagine the value of this set of armor.

Because of this armor, Merlin and Alice needed to repay tens of millions of gold coins—a sum so exorbitant it made their scalps tingle!

What did tens of millions of coins mean? The entire Britannia Empire would need twenty full years of tax revenue to pay it off!

For the empire, this would mean twenty years of halted development, increased taxes on the populace, and certain widespread grievances.

No wonder Elizabeth showed such a shocked expression. She found Merlin's lion's-share demand unacceptable. This wasn't a negotiation—it was outright robbery!

"Not difficult? Are you joking? With such harsh terms, how could I possibly agree?"

"Oh?" Merlin turned and headed for the door, not even looking back. "Then let's drop it. Find someone else for help. Maybe there's someone else who can help you repel the rebels~"

Elizabeth grew tense instantly, her face draining of color, her lips bitten pale.

She clearly sensed Merlin was taking advantage of the situation, but she had nothing to say.

Because besides Merlin, Elizabeth couldn't think of anyone else who could handle the current disastrous state of affairs.

Gnashing her teeth, Elizabeth raised her head and called out to Merlin, who was about to leave.

"Please wait, sir. I accept your terms!"

Merlin stopped in his tracks, the corners of his mouth curling up. He spread his hands and turned around with a smile. "That's more like it. I have the ability to deal with those rebels, and you only need to pay a small sum to secure your throne. It's a fair transaction~"

"Fair..." Elizabeth frowned. Honestly, she felt absolutely no fairness whatsoever—only a wave of powerlessness and the humiliation of being at someone else's mercy!

"Then it's settled. You can rest easy and sleep soundly. As for those rebels—they're a ragtag bunch. Leave it all to me." Merlin gave Elizabeth his word.

Elizabeth didn't speak, only felt the sting of损失. To bring in Merlin as an outside force, she had suffered such a heavy loss!

Merlin suddenly remembered something and pivoted his question. "By the way, how did you figure out that I am Earl of Elgin, the Great Swordsman?"

"My knights reported that the Great Swordsman of Elgin is a man who wears pantyhose on his head and acts like a pervert..." Elizabeth sighed softly. "At a time like that, aside from you, I can't think of anyone else who would do something like...."

....Several black lines slid down Merlin's forehead as he thought:

Is this guy really throwing me under the bus like this?!

Why would seeing someone wearing pantyhose on his head automatically point to me?!

The next day.

Temporary Royal Palace, Conference Hall.

Since Merlin had agreed to assist Elizabeth in repelling the rebels, he had rested here overnight—but there were other matters to attend to.

As the powerful reinforcements for this war, Merlin needed to meet with the two sides' forces—namely, the four Thorn Knights.

The reason was that everyone was temporarily an ally bound by a common enemy, so mutual understanding would help them fight together.

Although Merlin felt he was sufficient on his own and saw no need for a messy pre-battle meeting, he remembered this was Elizabeth's territory and kept quiet, just observing proper etiquette.

At this moment the sun was cresting the horizon, but the weather looked ominous.

Thick dark clouds pressed in from the north like ancient monsters, shrouding the ruined imperial capital, blocking out any trace of light.

Several key figures had gathered inside the conference hall, but the atmosphere was deathly silent, exuding an inexplicable pressure.

The crimson carpet had just been cleaned, and the tables and chairs were polished to a shine.

Flower vases sat upon the carpet, filled with freshly picked tulips. A faint fragrance lingered in the air.

Wearing a silver mask and black robes, Merlin sat upon the main throne. This outfit made it hard for anyone to discern his true appearance.

Only Elizabeth knew Merlin's identity—the knights below had absolutely no way to tell.

Merlin was sitting in the very seat that originally belonged to Queen Elizabeth—a temporary throne representing the pinnacle of imperial authority, which no one dared to sit upon.

But Merlin cared not at all. He sat wherever was comfortable, showing zero respect for class etiquette.

Because right now, Merlin was the one calling the shots, and everyone had to read his mood.

So Elizabeth said nothing, pretending not to notice—though her expression was visibly sour, clearly unhappy inside even if she didn't say it aloud.

It was like a low-level alt being bullied by wild monsters, when suddenly a max-level alt came to carry them through the dungeon. Even if the max-level player had a bad temper, you'd still have to swallow your pride—because, well, they're the carry~

Merlin swaggered into the throne, sitting in an extraordinarily casual pose, one foot propped up on the armrest, his odachi serving as a cane.

He hadn't experienced the feeling of looking down from above in a long time. Today was the perfect opportunity to savor how domineering he used to be among the demon race!

Merlin surveyed the knights below, a hint of mockery playing on his face. He hadn't expected to meet them this way.

Beside him, Elizabeth stood somewhat stiffly, her expression somewhat unnatural, looking like the humiliating picture of someone who had been bullied.

She was the Empress of the empire!

Why did she look more like Merlin's maid right now!?!

Not a shred of dignity...

Why is this man so rude?! Give me some face in front of the knights!

Elizabeth felt wronged, like a pitiful fledgling whose nest had been taken over, being bullied mercilessly.

Catherine, Morrison, Seth, and Melfield—the four knights—stood below, their expressions varying but all visibly shocked.

From Merlin's black attire, mask, and odachi, everyone seemed able to guess his identity.

That man who had previously been wanted by the empire—why was he now standing peacefully beside the queen? ! !

Melfield's eyes were wide with horror, his lips trembling as he stared at the masked man on the throne, unable to speak—

What is going on?!

Am I still dreaming?!

(0n0o)

title: Chapter 32 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 32 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 12 · Chapter 32

The several Thorn Knights below were all dumbfounded, with only Seth, who had just returned, remaining somewhat composed.

Although Seth had never personally seen the great swordmaster Elgin, from the legendary image, he could vaguely identify that the mysterious masked figure sitting on the throne was the mastermind who had thrown the kingdom into chaos!

Looking at the reactions of the others, Seth grew even more certain of his thoughts, and the identity of the person above was now confirmed.

Could that man be the great swordmaster Elgin?

The legend spoke of a powerhouse who had ruthlessly beheaded the Pirate King, President Houki, and countless undead...

These were all genuinely formidable enemies. If the rumors were all true, then this man was truly powerful!

At the very least, when facing the great swordmaster Elgin, I wouldn't have full confidence in victory, but a fifty-fifty chance should be achievable.

But this guy is a wanted criminal, and yet he dares to appear openly here?

What a brazen fellow, showing absolutely no regard for us knights.

Seth narrowed his eyes, his expression gradually darkening, with fierce battle intent in his gaze. His hands itched, eager to test himself against the great swordmaster Elgin.

But Seth was puzzled inside, because after probing for a long time, he hadn't detected any pressure emanating from the great swordmaster Elgin. He was practically no different from an ordinary person.

Whether a magician or a warrior, the pressure on one's body is hard to conceal, unless relying on some particularly rare and powerful concealment items.

The inability to ascertain the great swordmaster Elgin's exact strength left Seth unable to fathom it, with no rough measure of the great swordmaster's power in his heart.

This only made Seth more eager, desperate to strike and test himself against the great swordmaster Elgin.

Even if the great swordmaster Elgin had some concealment method on him, when he made a move, his pressure would inevitably leak out. At that point, it would be easy to determine what tier his strength was at.

Merlin smiled and looked down at the knights below, finding it quite amusing. Not long ago they had been shouting for his blood, and now they were all completely silenced, looking at him as if they'd seen a ghost.

Katherine and Morrison didn't make a fuss, their hearts filled with unease and suspicion. The great swordmaster Elgin should be considered an enemy of the empire. What was the situation with him strutting in here so brazenly? And the queen beside him seemed very calm, showing no obvious hostility.

The other knights all chose to observe quietly, but only the foremost, Maysfield, lost his composure. His mind clouded with heat, he directly drew his sword in front of Queen Elizabeth, his golden battle aura surging forth as he roared—

"Elgin! Great! Sword! Master!"

That voice seemed to come from the depths of hell, laced with the grinding of teeth and a slightly hoarse tone, revealing just how deep Maysfield's hatred for the great swordmaster Elgin ran.

At that moment, a flood of humiliating memories surged into his mind, and he was consumed with uncontrollable rage!

Merlin, sitting on the throne above, bared his teeth in a cold sneer.

He didn't take Maysfield seriously at all, instead recalling how this knight had been spat on by him several times. I wonder if she'd grow fond of a succubus's saliva~

Merlin rested his cheek on his hand comfortably and responded in a teasing tone.

"Isn't this the knight lady I spat on? What's wrong? Do you need to be this excited just seeing me? Your face is all red~"

The other knights, unaware of the situation, didn't make any rash moves.

But Maysfield was so infuriated by the great swordmaster Elgin that she nearly fainted, her delicate body trembling.

She was blushing from excessive anger, so don't say it with such loaded meaning!

"You despicable bastard! Why are you here!? And sitting on Her Majesty's throne! Get down this instant!"

Queen Elizabeth felt a wave of embarrassment inside. She hadn't expected Maysfield's reaction to be so extreme, putting her in an awkward position.

As for her throne being occupied by Merlin, it didn't really matter. A throne was merely symbolic, after all, and besides, he was their big shot ally.

"Hmph!" Merlin pursed his lips, and seeing the other's poor attitude, he casually replied, "I come when I want, I leave when I want. Mind your own business."

Maysfield's pupils contracted, and she gritted her teeth, saying, "You're courting death!"

Before the words had even finished, Maysfield raised her sword and struck fiercely, charging toward Merlin on the throne, her mind set on perishing together with this despicable man!

Merlin secretly complained about the trouble and was about to brew up a spit attack to make this knight lady scram, when Queen Elizabeth beside him couldn't bear to watch anymore and loudly shouted—

"Windsor! Stop fooling around!"

Hearing Elizabeth's voice, Maysfield had no choice but to stop, retracting her battle aura as she asked in surprise.

"Your Majesty? I'm protecting you!"

"Enough. Calm down first. Do not draw your sword against Lord Swordmaster. He is a distinguished guest I invited..." Elizabeth said in a serious tone.

"Huh!?!" Maysfield's small mouth hung open, finding it all unbelievable.

The Thorn Knights below were also astonished, increasingly confused by the situation before their eyes.

Not long ago, the great swordmaster Elgin had been an enemy of the royal family, and now in a flash he had become an honored guest. This enormous shift in status caught everyone off guard.

"Your Majesty! The great swordmaster Elgin is an enemy who threatens your position! To dare sit on your throne is an act of great disrespect!" Maysfield desperately wanted to beat up that guy, but the queen seemed to disagree.

"It's a time of great crisis. Trivial etiquette can be overlooked. Moreover, Lord Swordmaster and I have reached an agreement and reconciled our past grievances, becoming our reliable ally..." Elizabeth explained concisely.

"...When did that happen!?" Maysfield was shocked. She felt the reconciliation came too suddenly, hard to accept.

"Last night." Elizabeth said calmly.

The several Thorn Knights勉强 pieced together the situation. It seemed the enemy of the past had become an ally today.

Last night, the queen and the great swordmaster Elgin had reached some kind of reconciliation, turning this powerhouse who had loomed over the empire for so long into the key figure who would turn the tide of battle!

As for this result, the several Thorn Knights had different reactions—

Morrison naturally felt a touch of joy inside, because he had always believed that winning over the great swordmaster Elgin was the right choice, and now being able to fight side by side was naturally a good thing.

Katherine's face showed no expression, unable to discern any emotion, seemingly following the queen's wishes.

Seth, on the other hand, had itching hands, pondering whether to go up and provoke the great swordmaster Elgin right now to test this guy's strength.

Maysfield's attitude was very clear, written all over her face. She couldn't accept becoming allies with such a pervert, her body and mind both in resistance!

"Cough, cough!" Elizabeth, seeing the oppressive atmosphere, lightly cleared her throat twice to break the silence. "Let me formally introduce again. This is Lord Elgin the great swordmaster. Although we had some conflicts before, when crisis arrives, none of that matters. I hope everyone can get along and jointly resist the rebel army that is about to come."

"Mm, please take care of me..." Merlin casually offered a polite remark, then added—

"Oh, right.

"I'm the big shot. I guarantee you all a free win.

"When the enemy comes attacking...

"The four of you salted fish only need to shout 'GG' from behind me. Yeah~"

title: Chapter 33 — Drama Queen
content:
Chapter 33 — Drama Queen

Volume 12 · Chapter 33

"How is it? Did everyone understand what I meant?

Merlin sat on the throne, resting his chin on his hand and said casually.

At this word, everyone fell silent; no one responded.

However, the already discordant atmosphere instantly became more tense. Below, the four thorn knights were bristling with resentment.

"What's the matter?" Merlin frowned, dissatisfiedly said, "Do you have any objections to me?"

Elizabeth awkwardly covered her face, feeling depressed inside. Couldn't he say something a bit more gentle? Starting off with full mockery, the knights would certainly not accept being looked down upon like fish!

Even the usually calm Katherine had some displeasure in her brows, let alone the others.

Katherine found the Elgin swordmaster in front of her extremely arrogant, completely self-centered, and arrogant to the point of being disgusting.

However, recalling the terrifying power of that sword draw not long ago, Katherine immediately would not dare to refute.

Since Elgin swordmaster had such amazing power, a combined army of 100,000 seemed no big deal. No wonder he could so nonchalantly say that the thorn knights were all fish... Regarding Elgin's strength, Katherine didn't say it on the surface, but in her heart she still had to acknowledge it. If Elgin swordmaster was really an ally, it seemed other people wouldn't be needed.

Morrison's expression was unnatural, a drop of cold sweat flowing from his forehead. He thought Elgin swordmaster's words were too ugly. Even if he had strength beyond others, it wasn't necessary to say they were all just fish that could only shout 666...

Seth's fighting intent grew even thicker. For the first time, he had encountered such an arrogant person, and still saying disparaging words right in front of him.

He liked fighting powerful people very much, and it was a great improvement to his training.

Of course, severely slapping the face of an arrogant fellow was also one of his hobbies.

Seth was very interested in Elgin swordmaster, wondering what it would look like if he stepped on him firmly.

"Speaking of which.... Mesfield snapped back to his senses and asked tentatively, "By the way, does the powerful support His Majesty mentioned refer to Elgin swordmaster?"

"Correct, the support I called in is the swordmaster here. He will help us resist the rebel's attack, so everyone is a united front, allies. The previous unpleasantness is best not mentioned again; we have already reached an alliance, and I hope everyone cooperates and doesn't cause chaos at a time like this." Elizabeth said very seriously, clearly trying to smooth over the contradictions between the thorn knights and Elgin swordmaster in the middle.

Actually, Elizabeth had already anticipated today's tense situation, so she had never dared to say who the support was, fearing that if Elgin hadn't arrived yet, this side would cause a commotion.

Now it seems Elizabeth was indeed prescient.

"Joke! This kind of base, mean, perverted man is simply not worthy of trust! Finding a dog as an ally is even stronger than him!" Mesfield didn't buy it, staring at Elgin swordmaster and unleashing a tirade.

Merlin narrowed his eyes, a few black lines awkwardly sliding down his forehead. He thought he had only spat at that female knight a few times. Was he attacking him so much? The hatred of killing one's father is not so easy...

"Why must it be this man? Shouldn't there be other more reliable allies?" Mesfield paused, suddenly thinking of someone, "By the way, Mr. Gregory, the purple gold adventurer, his strength combined with ours should be enough to cope with this crisis..."

"I had already visited Mr. Gregory, but since he was knocked unconscious by the swordmaster last time, he is still in a coma." Elizabeth's tone was a bit embarrassed.

"..." Mesfield was at a loss for words. How long had it been, and he was still in a coma?

Merlin raised his eyebrows curiously, recalling that old man who used black hole magic. He had only punched him once, why hadn't he woken up? Was it because he was too old and couldn't stand the fussing? Goodness, he smelled a faint scent of being cheated...

"But

"Enough, Windsor, I have already made a decision."

Mesfield was about to continue arguing, but was interrupted by Elizabeth.

"Do you have a better method? If it's feasible, I can adopt your suggestion."

Mesfield was instantly at a loss. She didn't have a good suggestion; she just didn't like Elgin swordmaster, so her words were too full of personal feelings.

Being asked by the queen, Mesfield couldn't help but feel dumbfounded. After careful thought, she felt that Elgin swordmaster was indeed a strong person who could turn the situation around.

Besides this man, it seemed there was no other choice.

Mesfield felt she was a bit too young. Before interests, were there ever permanent enemies?

The calm Mesfield no longer opposed but silently sheathed her sword.

"Understood, I respect Your Majesty's meaning, but I am a bit curious about the alliance contents. I wonder what benefits that base man got, to be willing to help the empire through this crisis?"

"...Elizabeth secretly glanced at Merlin, and said seriously, "This is a secret, and cannot be said for the time being."

Mesfield suddenly frowned, feeling something was off. Elizabeth's evasive behavior seemed to hide a secret.

Elgin swordmaster had always performed like a person with no desires or needs. How did the queen win this man over? And they finalized it in one night... this....

Wait! Could it be that I discovered a big secret?

Mesfield's expression became strange, his eyes wandering between the queen and Elgin swordmaster's face, and his face inexplicably turned red.

Thinking about the queen's husband having died when Michelle was only two years old, the queen had been a widow for almost ten years.

After all, she is a woman. How could she have no needs or fantasies?

One night, a lone man and a widow negotiating normally? It's hard to believe!

And the queen and the swordmaster's attitudes changed so much in one night, it seems something deep exchange of mind and body must have happened, right?

Damn! What did this man do to the queen?

Could it be that he has already established a physical relationship with the queen, indirectly controlling the imperial?

Combining Elgin swordmaster's various perverted behaviors, Mesfield felt her guess was pretty much correct.

Her thinking suddenly went astray, thinking the two of them never had a serious negotiation, but a battle of the sheets!

Mesfield's whole body was filled with anger, thinking Elgin swordmaster had defiled the queen's purity and wanted to poop on his head!

So Mesfield again put his hand on the long sword, hesitating whether to tear his face open.

Windsor! What are you doing? I already told you to back off, don't continue to provoke some trouble!" Elizabeth saw Mesfield's weird reaction and scolded.

"...."

Mesfield, considering the queen's face and under pressure, had to endure his anger and silently bowed and retreated.

She thought there was definitely something weird. The queen was protecting the swordmaster a bit too much! If there were no other intimate relationships, it wouldn't make sense!

Could the queen have been conquered by Elgin swordmaster? How disgusting! Why is such a perverted man!

Mesfield's mind was in a turmoil, and she saw an ominous sign of the queen having some ambiguous relationship with the swordmaster.

Seeing that everyone's emotions had stabilized, Elizabeth let out a slight breath of relief and summarized, "Then next, everyone prepare..."

"Wait." Someone seemed to have some dissatisfaction.

Elizabeth looked at Seth strangely, and asked, "Is there anything not right?"

Seth walked from behind to the front. He could no longer suppress the fighting intent in his heart.

This was a rare opportunity, and he must grasp it well. If he could win against Elgin swordmaster, he would be the strongest thorn knight, no doubt!

Seth was not wearing armor but a single robe. However, his solid arm muscles fully demonstrated his warrior identity. "I've heard Elgin swordmaster is a strong person, but I have never seen it with my own eyes, so I don't acknowledge this person of unknown origin! To assist him in resisting the rebels, I refuse!"

"." Merlin's faint response, resting his face on his hand and said casually.

"Are you hard of hearing?"

"Who needed your assistance?"

"I am letting you be a fish in the rear, pulling a squad."

"Begging you don't act like a drama queen, forcibly adding drama to yourself..."

title: Chapter 34 — Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 34 — Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 12 · Chapter 34

Seth was left speechless by Merlin's retort, appearing particularly embarrassed.
He made the other party look high and mighty, while he himself was looking for trouble for no reason.
Seth narrowed his eyes; although he was furious inside, he didn't show it on his face.
"Interesting, your tongue seems stronger than your ability."
"Really?" Merlin responded with indifferent interest, completely unwilling to pay attention to Seth.
"Since Your Excellency the Great Swordsman is so confident, why not have a match with me?"
Seth said, pulling out a bronze-colored iron rod from behind his back and holding it across his chest.
Immediately, as if triggering a mechanism, the rod unfolded to both sides, forming a shining copper spear!
"I love fighting strong opponents; that moment of a duel where life hangs by a thread truly addicts me. So, Great Swordsman praised by countless people, can you make me feel a pleasure from the depths of my soul?!"
Merlin didn't speak, but narrowed his eyes, looking down arrogantly at the wild Seth, whose provocative expression clearly showed he was getting excited.
What the heck?
Is he an idiot?
But that battle-crazy gaze is utterly pure.
Using combat to keep body and mind extremely tense, frequently experiencing near-death experiences is indeed a very effective training method.
However, this method doesn't last long; one gradually becomes numb to death, and training hits a bottleneck that's hard to break through.
Just like Alice, who no longer wavers before ordinary dangers, her mind has become steadfast, but it's also hard to train using extreme methods.
This man's reckless challenge of others is likely an attempt to break through his current bottleneck and reach the peak of the Saint-tier.
Although I somewhat admire his courage, it's truly regrettable that he picked the wrong opponent.
Merlin twisted the corner of his mouth, showing an obvious contemptuous smile as a response, looking as if he couldn't be bothered to pay attention to Seth.
"Seth! What are you doing?! Put away your weapon!" Elizabeth's tone was somewhat stern.
Although I already knew this would happen, Elizabeth still didn't expect the Thorn Knights to have such strong opinions against Elgin the Great Swordsman, with them jumping out one by one to reject him.
"Your Majesty, sorry, but I won't obey you on this matter. I'm sure you just heard what that Great Swordsman said. We're just sidekicks; he intends to single-handedly fight the hundred-thousand-strong allied army." Seth chuckled, teasing, "I can't pretend I didn't hear that."
"Calm down a bit, Your Excellency the Great Swordsman isn't joking; he really can do it. Haven't you heard his rumors while traveling outside?" Elizabeth furrowed her brows, her mood becoming agitated.
"It's precisely because I've heard those unbelievable rumors that I'm skeptical; a man of unknown origin should never be trusted easily." Seth's eyes flashed with dissatisfaction, obviously looking for an excuse to fight Merlin.
In fact, Seth already knew those rumors, after all his companions seem to firmly believe in Elgin the Great Swordsman's achievements.
But these are just general accounts, not saying that Elgin the Great Swordsman always finishes off strong opponents instantly.
So Seth is confident that, if he gives his all, he could achieve feats comparable to Elgin the Great Swordsman; a fifty-fifty chance doesn't seem like a fantasy.
As long as he wins or gains an advantage, that proves he's stronger than Mersefield, and the title of strongest Thorn Knight would be his.
Furthermore, Seth is increasingly dissatisfied with his own strength; he urgently needs a breakthrough to prove he still has great room for improvement. If he can reach the peak of the Saint-tier, he would be a ruling existence within the empire.
So Seth thinks Elgin the Great Swordsman is a good touchstone; he can take the opportunity to test whether he can break through his bottleneck.
"Wanting to oppose the hundred-thousand-strong allied army with just one person's strength—isn't that just daydreaming? As far as I know, no one has managed that; ordinary people exhaust their strength mid-battle. So, Great Swordsman, could you spar with me? Let me see if your strength can bear the responsibility of turning the tide."
Merlin sneered, thinking, 'Are a hundred thousand troops that many? I'd guess the corpses of the Holy Church's crusade army in the Death Swamp haven't even cooled yet~'
Elizabeth was instantly at a loss for words; she somewhat understood Seth's nature—once he sets his mind on something, he won't turn back; he must achieve his goal.
Coincidentally, Elizabeth hasn't personally seen Merlin fight yet; she can take this chance to study him, to see if he's really as others say.
Catherine and Mersefield said nothing and didn't stop him, which amounts to silent approval of Seth's actions.
Only Morrison was somewhat worried, kindly reminding Seth with a sentence.
"Hey! Don't be so impulsive; you can't beat the Great Swordsman, so don't bring suffering upon yourself."
"Hah, a joke~" Seth snorted coldly, speaking seriously, "How would you know without trying? You and Mersefield are the same—scared silly by this guy, have you even lost the most basic fighting spirit?"
Mersefield's expression turned displeased; he thought Seth's words were unpleasant, and he believed he was merely suspicious of a relationship between the queen and the Great Swordsman, his mind in turmoil, not lacking fighting spirit.
"No, Elgin the Great Swordsman is already our ally now; don't deliberately provoke him." Morrison furrowed his brow, unable to hold back, speaking frankly: "With your strength, you really can't win; better not go up and humiliate yourself. Now the allied army presses upon us; we have a common enemy."
"Huh? Do you think I'm as useless as you?" Seth grew a bit angry; his battle spirit rose on his side, while Morrison's side kept belittling.
Morrison was left speechless, immediately shutting his mouth and saying nothing; he thought his good intentions were being treated like pig's lungs, truly a thankless effort!
"I know the empire is now in a dire life-or-death situation; shouldn't we be even more cautious?" Seth raised his copper spear, pointing at Elgin the Great Swordsman on the throne, "Handing over the empire's crisis entirely to such a mysterious figure is inherently unreasonable, so I want to personally test whether he can bear the responsibility!"
Elizabeth felt somewhat uncertain, thinking Seth's words made some sense.
Although she had personally witnessed Merlin's draw-cut slash turning the palace into ruins, which already showed his extraordinary strength.
But Elizabeth was still curious about what Merlin's posture looks like when he fights, and why Mersefield feels powerless, even self-abandoning, whenever he brings it up.
Could Elgin the Great Swordsman really be that terrifying, already reaching a point where others can't even catch his dust?
"Hahaha...... Merlin laughed from the throne, looking down and saying, 'Good, since you're so persistent, I'll accept your challenge. When you understand what a heaven-and-earth difference is, I hope you willingly become a salted fish shouting 66...."
"Bring it on!" Seth gritted his teeth angrily, brandishing his copper spear, golden battle aura surging from his body—
"Watch my valiant bearing closely, Mersefield...."
"I'm not like you idealists!"
"I'll take the multiple scenes of the strongest Thorn Knight!"

title: Chapter 35 — War Armor (Part 2)
content:
Chapter 35 — War Armor (Part 2)

Volume 12 · Chapter 35

Elizabeth saw the two about to spar and quietly moved away, afraid of accidentally hurting herself.

As for Seth's personality, Elizabeth was fairly familiar with it.

They're calling it a spar, but who knows what it'll end up looking like?

If things get out of hand later, Elizabeth is ready to intervene and teach the Church a lesson—just probe each other for now, don't destroy the temporary palace.

The other three Thorn Knights stepped aside, yielding the center to give Seth ample room to display himself.

As for Seth's taunting, Miesfield said nothing, and even seemed to want to laugh. He himself couldn't beat Elkin the Great Swordmaster, so does Seth think he can take advantage?

Seth held a copper spear and lifted his head, staring straight at Merlin on the high platform, seeing the other's contemptuous gaze, his heart's anger grew by another three points.

Doesn't anyone stand up for me?

Want to use this lazy posture to spar with me?

Look down on people, huh! I must return the favor!

Seth's eyes focused, and the golden battle aura on his body surged. With a roar—

"Drink! ! !"

Seth's figure shot upward. Due to his speed, outsiders could probably only see a streak of golden light, like a runaway horse—

A drop of cold sweat trickled down Miesfield's forehead. He thought in his heart that Seth's strength seemed to have progressed another step.

In the blink of an eye, Seth arrived before Merlin, and the long spear in his hand—changed. Suddenly, it stabbed out!

The sound of piercing the air was mournful, as if a powerful blade had sliced through the air!

Those who heard it got goosebumps, and their eardrums trembled instinctively!

Heng!

This stab contained eight percent of my battle aura!

If this man remains nonchalant, then let's wait for a slap in the face!

I don't want a fifty-fifty split—I want a crushing victory!

Seth's spear, which had just thrust out, suddenly began to rotate. Like a golden spiral flash of lightning, it viciously stabbed toward Merlin's throat.

"Hah, true year... Merlin let out a cold laugh, lowered his head, and made no movement.

The powerful spear attack stirred up a series of dust, turning the conference hall upside down!

Sand and stones flew, and the decorative glass around them shattered instantly!

The onlookers had to retreat half a step, using their arms to shield their eyes against the flying sand.

Wait until the flying sand and dust dispersed, and everyone looked concerned toward the high platform—

The once gorgeous high platform was now in ruins, ravaged by the battle aura and completely messed up.

Seth maintained the posture of thrusting his spear and stopped, unable to advance even an inch!

The tip of the copper spear wasn't a shield or hard armor—just a single finger?

With Seth's attack using eighty percent of his power, it was actually blocked by Merlin's single finger! Without using any special defensive method!

Just a brief probing attack, and the winner was already decided!

The huge gap in strength was self-evident, making Seth experience what despair feels like!

At the end of the day, Merlin never regarded Seth as an equal, because this guy with a demonic possession couldn't even qualify as an opponent.

Seth jumped around like a monkey the whole time, while Merlin remained imposing and unmoving, sitting steadily on the throne the whole time, never receiving even a scratch.

Merlin propped his head with one hand, one hand supporting the tip of the copper spear, lazily leaning back on the throne.

His expression was disdainful, looking at Seth with contempt, and he said calmly.

"Is this the extent of your strength?"

So weak...

"Then please contentedly be a nice fish."

Seth sucked in a cold breath, his pupils constricted, and his eyeballs darted about nervously.

Elizabeth's small mouth opened wide. For a moment, time didn't match up, and she thought the gap in strength was truly worlds apart! They weren't on the same level at all! This is the iceberg tip of Elkin the Great Swordmaster's power? Indeed, as Windsor said, it's incredible!

Several of the Thorn Knights beside him were also moved, falling into silent contemplation.

Miesfield silently clenched his fist, his heart surging with an uncomfortable sense of imbalance. Fate is really unfair!

Why does Elkin the Great Swordmaster, this pervert who steals women's underwear, spits women's saliva, and hides poison in his mouth, have such formidable power!?

If Elkin the Great Swordmaster wasn't immensely powerful, how could the Queen possibly curry favor with this filthy man! ?

Miesfield had a bad mood, and half-willingly assumed the Queen and the Great Swordmaster must have a thing forced upon her.

"Wanting to find confidence from me, you've chosen the wrong enemy, you fool!

Merlin flicked his finger, shaking the space, and knocked Seth back continuously.

Seth fell from the high platform and barely stabilized his form, lifting his head to look at the invincible man above, and his whole body couldn't help but tremble—

Is this Elkin the Great Swordmaster? !

Damn it! Strength is even greater than the rumors!

I exerted all my strength, yet I couldn't do anything against his finger?

Too powerful, in my life, I've never encountered such an enemy—

Seth's face was pale, cold sweat sliding down his forehead. That huge strength gap made him want to give up; he finally experienced what Miesfield felt.

"I advise you not to take yourself too seriously; no one has any expectations of you. You're just one of the mundane masses. If you want to challenge me, you're still short by millions of years..." Merlin said from on high, looking at this idiot Seth and finding it funny.

Seth's figure in his eyes gradually retreated, becoming like a pool of dead water, filled with despair.

What a joke! I'm a recognized genius!

From small to large! No one has ever dared use the word "ordinary" to describe me!

I lightize others, but others cannot lightize me!

Seth's heart burned with anger, his eyes bloodshot, and his deep hatred was completely unhidden.

Kacha kacha, the sound of metal cutting and colliding rang out, accompanied by faint roars similar to beasts.

A red flame swept over Seth's body surface, and a layer of black armor appeared, with an eerie shape and patterns, letting

This set of armor seems to be Seth's bottom card, perfect armor with no dead angles in defense. It seems this is a sign of going all out.

"Seth! That's enough, what do you want to do! ?" Elizabeth said.

"Sorry, Your Majesty, I also have my dignity. To endure such insults, even in a dream, I wouldn't sleep peacefully." Seth glared at the Great Swordmaster above, "So I have to start seriously, even if I give it my all to defeat the opponent—even if it's just one finger, it's better than doing nothing!"

"Seth, are you an idiot? Didn't you hear the Queen's meaning! ? Still not put down your weapon!" Miesfield said discontentedly.

"Yeah, Seth, look open-minded." Morrison also chimed in.

Katharine said nothing, kept her eyes closed, as if what was happening had nothing to do with her, like she was sleeping.

"Shut up all of you! What do I do? Do I need you to point fingers! Be quiet for a point and watch! You're also worthy of becoming the Empire's top knights? Embarrassing!"

Seth roared, and didn't forget to mock all the knights.

The arrival of Elkin the Great Swordmaster was simply like defecating on top of the Purpleflower Knights' team's head.

Originally, the accusations against the Purpleflower Knights were for guarding the Empire's safety, but now they have to rely on Elkin the Great Swordmaster, with no dignity to speak of.

Several Thorn Knights actually chose to surrender and lick Elkin the Great Swordmaster's boots in various ways. Seth looked down on these people in his heart.

....This bastard... Miesfield gritted his teeth in anger, silently gripping his waist sword, some wanting to forcibly interfere.

Merlin's contemptuous expression changed slightly, not sighing at how much Seth was cornering himself, but because he was interested in the bizarre black armor on his body.

Because from the very beginning, Merlin could clearly feel that the armor on Seth's body was emitting a demonic aura specific to demons!

Because this aura was extremely intense, ordinary people could feel it, let alone Merlin, who is a demon.

Merlin felt this demonic aura familiar, and a bit intimate, unbiddenly a doubt arose in his heart—

This armor looks so familiar?

Seems like I've seen it before, but who's was it?

This demonic aura isn't on Seth, a human body,

Clearly it's cold iron armor, why does it emit a demonic aura like a living demon?

All these doubts made Merlin furrow his brow, feeling that something was weird.

He could definitely be sure this armor was from the demon race, but whose it was, he couldn't think of for a moment.

Merlin's various memories flashed, feeling that this armor with its own life should belong to a certain demon monarch.

Actually, the origin of this armor is very mysterious, not even Seth himself knows, but one can guess it belongs to the demon race.

When Seth was young. He went everywhere to practice and improve his strength.

On a certain island in the Black Sea, Seth found an altar guarded by demons.

Seth and the demons engaged in a fierce battle, barely surviving, and in the center of the altar, he found this bizarre armor.

Seth fought with the armor a few rounds, nearly losing his life, but it seemed he got the black armor's recognition, becoming its new owner, able to use it freely.

Seth was very excited about this, treasured it, and had been using this mysterious treasure.

This armor is very wonderful, as if it has its own life and consciousness—even if no one is wearing it, it can move freely and can also hide by parasitizing in a human's flesh.

When worn, the person's combat ability increases several times, becoming extremely powerful, comparable to a real great demon!

And the combat method also becomes brutal, like a demon possession!

And it makes the host forget pain, no matter what severe blows they suffer, they won't feel pain, and can maximize combat efficiency, becoming a slaughterous berserker!

However, Seth knows this black armor has some bad things, namely it's bloodthirsty, feeding on living creature's blood.

If the armor doesn't bathe in blood for a long time, it will devour the host's blood, eating the owner alive.

So Seth rarely stays in the stable imperial capital, but wanders everywhere, looking for strong enemies to improve himself, and feeds this evil thing on the way.

Although the black armor is very strange, Seth doesn't care, he only cares about pursuing pure power.

"Elkin the Great Swordmaster! Let you see my true power!

Seth's veins bulged on his face, and his blood was gurgling, being frantically devoured by the armor on his body.

This is the price of using the black armor, to make it move, first feed it with your own blood.

Seth roared, and a helmet similar to a beast's head "clank" locked onto his face, completely hiding his features.

Merlin grinned, as if remembering something, regarding the origin of this bizarre armor, he wasn't showing any signs of panic.

Seth held a long spear and took a stance, but didn't move for a long time, the whole armor constantly making "clank" discordant sounds, as if fighting against him.

What's going on!

Why doesn't the armor listen to my command?

Instead, it's secretly confronting me, not obeying my will!

Seth's black armor was sweating profusely, for the first time encountering this situation, making him feel scared and at a loss.

"What's wrong? Why is Seth not moving?" Miesfield furrowed her brows, sensing a strangeness.

"I don't know, it seems this armor doesn't listen to Seth?" Morrison furrowed his brow.

Miesfield secretly worried, instinctively protecting the Queen behind her—she had always been afraid of this black armor, thinking it evil, and now it's become abnormal, must be guarded against.

Clack clack—

A series of strange sounds came out, the black armor's back completely opened, and Seth was forcibly ejected!

Seth cried out, falling to the ground, his face pale, the terrifying blood vessels still hadn't faded.

As the owner, he was actually rejected by his own armor! ?

Seth was weak, his expression unwilling as he lifted his head and glared at the black armor, his blood being drained in an instant.

"..What happened ah! ?" Elizabeth cried out in surprise, finding the scene unbelievable, Seth can't control his own armor?

The black armor closed up, like a demon stimulated and awakening, looking from afar, this armor really came to life!

The black armor moved, stepping forward with a hula la sound, stopping at the base of the high platform.

It raised its head high, looking at Merlin on the throne, with a soul seemingly winking in the deep eye sockets.

Finally, this self-aware armor knelt on one knee, lowering its beastly head, expressing submission and infinite respect to Merlin.

This movement made Merlin grin, patting his forehead, vaguely knowing what was going on? This armor indeed belongs to someone he knows, and it even recognized its true identity!

However, the others present were not so calm.

They all opened their eyes wide, showing surprised expressions, and their hearts stirred up a storm—

What's going on! ?

Seth's armor bowing to Elkin the Great Swordmaster! = =

title: Chapter 36 — Buddha's Light
content:
Chapter 36 — Buddha's Light

Volume 12 · Chapter 36

Merlin’s reaction was surprisingly composed—he didn’t seem shocked at all. It seemed he had already anticipated the appearance of this jet-black armor and the heavy demonic aura emanating from it, as if he had some prior knowledge of it.

Such an eerie design, thick with demonic essence, and capable of acting on its own without any external force—these were rare qualities. Armor with so many extraordinary traits was bound to be a precious relic.

Merlin quickly searched through his distant memories and immediately found the answer.

This peculiar black armor belonged to Mammon, the gluttonous sovereign of the demon race, the Great Demon Lord of the Third Demon Lord Palace. Though the memory was long faded, Merlin could still vaguely recall the origins of this armor.

Long ago, Mammon collected an immense amount of rare black gold to forge a royal suit of armor for himself. He also employed special techniques, fusing the souls of living beings into the armor, giving it its own consciousness and will so that it could fight for its master or act independently, becoming the most trusted ally.

Merlin couldn’t recall who Mammon had commissioned to forge this armor, but he had heard the process was brutally bloody. A noble demon who dared defy Mammon’s authority was thrown alive into the furnace to refine the armor, and vast amounts of rare black gold were poured in to give it the perfect skeletal structure.

After taking shape, Mammon further tempered it with his own blood, amplifying the demonic essence to its limits, making it a rare living demonic armor.

Finally, he sacrificed 1,000 humans to feed the armor, granting it self-awareness—only then was the work complete.

It was said that this black demonic armor itself possessed the strength of a Great Demon and could evolve toward even higher tiers, along with countless other extraordinary traits, making it nearly a perfect piece of equipment.

However, Merlin remembered Mammon once saying that the armor was far from perfect—it had a flaw so glaring that it could be considered a failure.

Its intelligence was low, barely matching that of a four-year-old human child, and it could only understand and execute simple commands.

Thus, Mammon never truly cherished this black demonic armor; instead, it was a neglected toy among his many treasures. Compared to other priceless artifacts, this armor ranked only as mid-tier, nothing extraordinary.

Yet Mammon was satisfied with its ability to have a soul and self-awareness. He had even boasted about it to Merlin once, even pulling it out to show him.

That was why Merlin felt a sense of familiarity—he had seen this armor before. It was just one of Mammon’s toys.

Though it was merely a novel plaything, the thick demonic aura it emitted could rival that of a Great General beneath a demon sovereign, proving its strength was no joke.

Seeing the black demonic armor kneel on one knee before him, expressing submission, Merlin understood—he wasn’t surprised at all.

After all, Merlin was the supreme sovereign of the Seven Demon Lords, his status equal to Mammon’s, the Great Demon Lord of the Third Palace. No ordinary demon could approach him.

In the rigid hierarchy of the demon race, class oppression was absolute. Lower-ranking demons had no rights. If Merlin had ordered them to die, the demons under the First Demon Lord Palace would have obeyed without hesitation, slaughtering each other in droves. Such pathological obedience was terrifying.

Though this black armor had limited intelligence, it was still a demon, and the rigid class structure was ingrained in its very being.

Moreover, it had seen Merlin in person. Instantly, from his demeanor, appearance, and the sword *Banri Garan* in his hand, it recognized his identity.

*Banri Garan* was the sacred blade passed down through generations of the First Demon Lord Palace, used to prove the sovereign’s authority. Almost every demon knew of it.

Even though Merlin wore a mask, hiding his true face, the fact that he held *Banri Garan* made his identity unmistakable.

Thus, the black demonic armor immediately chose its allegiance, ejecting Seth and kneeling before Merlin, expressing its submission without any hostility, refusing to serve as a human’s helper.

Merlin was a sovereign among the demon race, his power unfathomable. This black armor was merely a product created by Mammon—how could it dare oppose a sovereign? That would be laughable.

The bizarre actions of the black armor shocked everyone present except Merlin.

In their eyes, this armor was strange, exuding demonic energy, and belonged to Seth, capable of enhancing his combat power.

But now, this armor—belonging to Seth—had betrayed him, disobeying his master’s commands. Instead, it had ejected Seth’s blood, then knelt before the Great Sword Master Elgin!

It seemed the armor had abandoned Seth and chosen Elgin.

Had Seth never truly been the master? Had he never fully controlled this demonic armor, but instead gathered it for some other purpose?

These questions swirled in everyone’s minds, leaving them bewildered.

“What’s happening? Why is Seth’s armor kneeling before the Great Sword Master?!” Morrison’s face twisted in confusion, unable to remain calm.

“I don’t know… this is too strange…” Mesfield’s expression mirrored Morrison’s—she couldn’t make sense of the situation.

“It looks like the armor betrayed Seth and no longer obeys his commands… or rather…” Catherine stroked her chin, pondering for a moment. “The fact that it could betray so easily proves Seth never truly controlled this strange armor. They were only together for some other reason.”

Elizabeth listened to Catherine’s analysis without comment.

She looked at Merlin on the throne, utterly confused by the current situation.

Elizabeth sensed that Merlin was far more mysterious than just an adventurer—this man was shrouded in enigmas.

The veins on Seth’s face had receded, leaving his complexion deathly pale.

He had never expected the black war armor to betray him, completely defying his will and refusing to obey.

All this time, he had treated the armor like a companion, yet it had betrayed him without hesitation, showing no mercy.

Seth’s body was severely weakened. Gritting his teeth, he glared at Elgin, the Great Sword Master, and demanded, “What did you do?! How could you control this armor?!”

Merlin didn’t answer. Instead, he shifted the conversation, speaking calmly. “Where did you get this armor?”

“…” Seth froze. He knew little about the armor’s secrets, but Elgin seemed to know something, so he hesitated. “…On an island in the Black Sea.”

“Ah, I see.”

Merlin’s expression relaxed. The Black Sea lay between the Austro-Hungarian Empire and the United Kingdoms, right within the influence of the Third Demon Lord Palace.

Seth was truly a lucky man—didn’t he realize the dangers of venturing into the Third Demon Lord Palace’s territory? And yet he had stolen Mammon’s treasure.

It seemed Mammon didn’t value this armor at all. Otherwise, it wouldn’t have been left on a wandering island as bait to lure greedy treasure hunters, rather than stored in the palace’s vault.

This was Mammon’s twisted amusement—a simple trap, like a mousetrap or a treasure chest monster.

The Third Demon Lord Palace’s location wasn’t bad—it could yield rare gems—but it lacked the most basic necessity: food.

Mammon, the gluttonous sovereign of the demon race, was incredibly wealthy. His personal fortune could rival that of the entire demon race, a reputation known far and wide.

Thus, many reckless humans dared to risk their lives to seek treasure in Mammon’s domain.

Many rare treasures were placed on these drifting islands, tempting the greedy to take them.

But the islands were either rigged with traps or guarded by powerful demons. Most people failed, and Seth was one of the rare lucky ones who succeeded, relying on his own Saint-tier strength.

Those who failed were imprisoned by Mammon and kept like livestock, eventually becoming food for the demons, solving the Third Demon Lord Palace’s food shortage.

This game seemed fair—without greed, one wouldn’t die. Even if a lucky few managed to take Mammon’s treasures, they did so at enormous risk.

Mammon, among the Seven Sovereigns, was the most severe collector. Even if an item had no use for him, he would still hoard it, increasing his wealth. He wanted to possess every treasure in the world, adding to his collection, just to feel pleased looking at them every day.

Though Mammon was rich, he was also miserly to the extreme—so stingy that he wouldn’t let anyone take advantage of him, not even his closest children. If they dared touch his treasures, he would kill them himself.

How miserly was Mammon? Merlin had once heard a vivid story.

At the dawn of the Age of Exploration, countless human empires sent ships to discover new lands, expanding trade to distant places, and piracy became a profession.

These desperados didn’t just plunder—they loved hunting for treasure.

They found Mammon’s hoard in the Black Sea, stole it, and lived in luxury for a long time.

But their luck didn’t last. Retribution came. The pirates all died horribly, and even their descendants perished, as if cursed. Only when they returned Mammon’s gold coins to the Black Sea did the misfortune stop.

Not a single coin was missing from Mammon’s treasure after hundreds of years!

In truth, it was all Mammon’s doing. He knew who had taken the gold and sent demons to kill them one by one. Those who survived were brought to the Third Demon Lord Palace to become demon food.

Mammon only needed a small excuse—anyone who took his things would pay with their life.

Clearly, Mammon’s miserliness was easy to understand.

Thus, when Merlin looked at Seth, it was as if he were looking at a dead man. The man had even dared to steal Mammon’s treasure—he was already close to death.

Mammon would never forgive anyone who stole from him.

The reason Seth was still alive was likely because Mammon hadn’t yet discovered his armor had been stolen.

And indeed, Seth had only obtained the armor as the Thorn Knight just two years ago.

For long-lived demons, two years was but a blink of an eye.

So Mammon hadn’t noticed his treasure was gone yet.

But then, the armor kneeling on one knee raised its head and extended its hands, using its fingers to form strange symbols, attempting to communicate with Merlin.

*“Great Proud Sovereign, allow me to serve you.”*

*“I am willing to burn my own soul to eliminate your troubles.”*

*“Please give me a chance to become your most loyal servant…”*

Merlin clicked his tongue, frowning in embarrassment, thinking to himself:

So this was a revolution in betrayal?

Mammon’s subordinates…

Seemed like their loyalty wasn’t very high at all.

title: Chapter 37 — Refusing
content:
Chapter 37 — Refusing

Volume 12 · Chapter 37

The pitch-black demonic armor used its fingers to form all manner of strange characters, attempting to communicate with Merlin.

These were the script of demons—no one but demons, or those well-versed in demonic culture, could possibly understand them.

Apart from Merlin, no one present had any idea what the armor was trying to say.

"What's going on? What is that armor saying?" Morrison's mind was filled with question marks, utterly confused.

Catherine knew more about such things. Though she couldn't translate it fully, she could roughly guess the meaning. "It seems to be pledging loyalty to the Great Swordsman, wanting to serve him."

"That can't be right! Doesn't this armor belong to Seth? How could it betray him so easily?!" Mesfield found it hard to believe.

"It's likely that Seth never truly tamed this armor. Their relationship was one of mutual use. Upon meeting the Great Swordsman Elgin, it has now decided on its true master for the first time." Catherine speculated, thinking that seeking the protection of a powerful being was an instinct shared by all creatures.

The demonic armor had its own consciousness. Choosing the far stronger Great Swordsman Elgin as its master was only natural.

Catherine didn't know that the armor's previous master had been the Demon Lord of Greed, one of the peak existences of the demon race.

Even if it sought a new master, it wouldn't choose someone weaker than Mammon.

Thus, as the Demon Lord of Pride, Merlin became the armor's best choice—no one was more suitable to wield it.

The armor's power wasn't weak, but it depended on its host. It grew stronger with a strong host, weaker with a weak one.

With Merlin's strength, he could likely unleash the armor's full potential with ease, perhaps even triggering an evolution.

The demonic armor continued to gesture, expressing not only its desire to submit but also recounting its past and some of its secrets.

After Mammon lost interest in the armor, he had abandoned it on a small island in the Black Sea, using it as bait to lure reckless humans seeking treasure.

But the armor had developed its own consciousness. No longer just cold metal, it could think for itself and needed to consume fresh blood to survive.

Life on the isolated island was dull and monotonous. The armor felt imprisoned, sensing it had been discarded by Mammon, no longer cared for.

Over time, deprived of fresh blood, the armor's consciousness teetered on the brink of collapse, at risk of dissipating entirely.

But in its moment of despair, a young man named Seth, covered in wounds from a fierce battle, arrived and opened its cage, finding it.

From that moment, the armor decided to betray its original master, Mammon, and parasitize this young man named Seth.

It was a fair trade: the armor gave Seth power, and Seth gave the armor hope for survival.

Whenever Seth fought enemies, the armor would absorb their blood to sustain itself, attempting to evolve and break free from Mammon's control.

Now, the opportunity had come. If Merlin was willing to take it in, freedom would be within easy reach.

Merlin watched the armor's gestured narrative and roughly understood its past. He stroked his chin, falling into thought.

Should he take this armor or not?

He didn't seem to need it himself. Alice might, and giving it to her wouldn't be bad.

But the armor was essentially a demon, wasn't it? Demons were arrogant by nature and looked down on humans. It probably wouldn't allow Alice to control it.

Not all demons were like him—a transmigrator with a unique worldview.

Moreover, this thing had betrayed its masters repeatedly. It clearly had a tendency to switch sides, making it untrustworthy.

Who knew if it might betray at a critical moment and cause a disaster...

After much deliberation, Merlin decided to refuse the armor. The reason was simple: who would dare take something that betrayed its masters time and time again?

Though the armor's current intelligence wasn't high, as it grew and evolved, it might develop restless ambitions, which would be unsafe for Alice.

Elizabeth watched the exchange between the armor and Merlin, feeling increasingly uneasy. Those strange hand gestures were clearly from another race. Could the Great Swordsman Elgin be a demon?

The same doubt arose in Seth's mind. Why could his armor communicate with the Great Swordsman Elgin? Could they both be from the same place?

Weak and injured, Seth slowly stood up, glaring at the Great Swordsman, his teeth clenched as he shattered the silence.

"Hey! Great Swordsman, what are you whispering about with my armor?!"

Merlin turned to look at Seth, calmly replying, "Nothing much."

"You can understand that bizarre sign language?!" Seth furrowed his brows.

"Well, I can. What's the problem?" Merlin tilted his mouth into a smirk.

"Why can you understand demonic script?! Are you a demon too?!" Seth roared, his heart filled with suspicion and unease. He was certain the armor came from the demon race. If it could communicate with the Great Swordsman Elgin, then they must be from the same place!

At this, everyone present turned their gaze toward Merlin, their eyes like searchlights converging on him.

This wasn't just Seth's doubt—it was a question on everyone's minds at that moment.

If the Great Swordsman Elgin was actually a demon, that would be a huge problem.

Great Britain was under the Holy Church's domain. Ordinary people would naturally feel hostility and rejection toward demons.

If Merlin revealed his demonic identity now, he might end up in a precarious situation, hunted by all.

"This..." Merlin, faced with Seth's accusation, looked somewhat unnatural. He quickly weighed the pros and cons in his mind.

I can't admit to being a demon. Humans inherently distrust and fear demons.

Like when I first met Alice and we weren't familiar, her attitude toward me was terrible, largely because I was a demon.

That kind of first impression could easily cause trouble. So, better to deny it.

Merlin decided to conceal the truth, secretly relieved that the demonic armor couldn't speak human language. Otherwise, his secret would be exposed completely!

"No, I'm not a demon. Who says understanding demonic script means you're a demon? I just happen to know a lot about demonic culture. I've studied it a bit. Maybe some scholars in the empire can read demonic script too. Does that make them demons as well?"

Seth was left speechless, finding Merlin's words made some sense.

Elizabeth slightly relaxed her guard, thinking Merlin might just be exceptionally knowledgeable. Maybe she was overthinking.

The other Thorn Knights didn't suspect him either. In truth, there were indeed scholars who studied demons and could read their script.

Moreover, though Merlin was the Great Demon Lord, he didn't emit the unique aura of a demon, so it was natural he wasn't suspected.

Seth's face flushed with anger as he forced himself to ask, "Then what did the armor just say?"

"Do you really need to ask? You can probably guess." Merlin propped up his face, curling his lips without a hint of politeness.

"..."

"You're such a pathetic human. Letting you use it is a waste of its potential."

"So it's begging me, the big shot, to take it along so it can show off, soar to new heights, and reach the pinnacle of life and all that~"
