title: Chapter 38 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 38 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 12 · Chapter 38

"What... what?!"

Seth was genuinely stunned. Hearing Elgin the Great Swordsman's words, he clearly struggled to accept the reality.

This suit of armor had been with him for so long—how could it just betray him? That was far too arbitrary!

Seth felt Elgin was lying, deliberately deceiving him.

"Are you spouting nonsense?! This armor has been with me for years—how could it betray me?!"

Merlin almost laughed upon hearing this. Years? Was that a long time? The lazy Demon Lord had lived through several epochs!

Demons had incredibly long lifespans. With proper care, they could practically live forever.

Humans might consider years a long time, but to demons, it was nothing.

Moreover, this demonic armor originally belonged to Mammon. If it could betray Mammon after hundreds of years, what were Seth’s mere few years worth?

"Do I have any reason to lie to you? That armor just expressed its intent—what other meaning could kneeling have besides submission?"

"I... "

Seth was at a loss for words, unable to refute Elgin. He had to admit the other man’s point.

A deep sense of unwillingness surged within him. He had sacrificed so much for this armor.

Almost every moment, he was in battle, feeding it blood to sustain this somewhat sinister piece of equipment.

Yet he had gained nothing but betrayal!

Seth was confused. Why had the armor chosen Elgin over him?

"Why... why did it choose you?! I’ve paid such a heavy price for it!"

"Isn’t it obvious? Because I’m stronger than you. If a weapon has its own will, it will, like any human, instinctively choose to ally with the stronger party." Merlin responded indifferently, pitying Seth like a child who’d had his toy taken away.

Seth had no retort. He *was* weaker than Elgin, but his heart still refused to accept it.

He felt cheated, as if he’d lost everything.

Lost in confusion, Seth began to fixate stubbornly, determined to reclaim the armor.

"This is clearly mine! I am the master of this armor! No matter its will, what’s mine is mine!"

"How foolish. *Your* armor? *Your* possession? That’s the funniest joke I’ve ever heard." Merlin’s face twisted in mockery, genuinely amused by Seth’s words.

"What’s so funny?" Seth furrowed his brows, seeing nothing laughable in his statement.

"You, its master? That’s just your one-sided delusion." Merlin paused, then continued seriously, "This armor never considered you its master—you were just a tool to it. To the armor, you were a blind, power-hungry fool, easier to control and use to ensure its own survival. Once it finds a more suitable host, you’ll naturally be discarded."

"Uh..." Seth’s eyes widened, his resolve wavering. Though he didn’t want to admit it, he could sense the armor’s disobedience—its hunger for enemy blood, even his own, its insatiable greed.

"You think you’re the master? In truth, the armor wants to control *you*, to turn you into *its* slave." Merlin slowly rose from his throne, looking down at Seth. "And that’s exactly what’s happening. You’ve grown dependent on this demonic treasure. Without it, you’re nothing. Over time, you’ll become nothing more than the armor’s pet, losing your soul, reduced to an empty shell that only exists to feed it."

After these words, Seth was overwhelmed by a deep sense of powerlessness. He couldn’t confirm if Merlin was telling the truth, but his words carried a strange, persuasive magic.

Was he truly becoming a puppet of the demonic armor? Was everything of value being slowly devoured...

Seth suddenly noticed his body stiffening, a bone-deep chill seeping into him. For the first time, he felt a flicker of fear toward this hard-won treasure.

The other knights watching exchanged worried glances. If Elgin’s words were true, the situation was dire.

In truth, Seth’s own strength wasn’t among the top of the Thorn Knights. But with the armor, he underwent a qualitative change, his power rivaling the peak of Saint-tier!

Elizabeth felt a surge of worry. Was Merlin just playing mind games? With the Thorn Knights already weakened, she couldn’t afford for Seth to be in danger.

"You think possessing the armor gives you power? But you don’t realize you’re walking into the abyss of despair. This armor demands blood to sustain itself. The day you stop fighting, the day you stop feeding it enemy blood, it will mercilessly devour its so-called master to fill its belly, then seek out the next host." Merlin stepped down from the platform, stopping before the demonic armor, his voice low. "So you’ll never be able to stop the killing. You’ll charge down the lonely path of a demon, and even the last scraps of your worth will be squeezed dry."

"Lord Great Swordsman, you’re not joking, are you?" Elizabeth couldn’t help but ask, feeling Seth was being pushed to question his very existence.

"A long time ago, while traveling, I heard legends about this armor, so I know some secrets. As for whether they’re true... that’s for you to judge." Merlin didn’t commit fully, afraid of revealing too much and being linked to the demon race. "I think Lord Seth has already noticed, hasn’t he? His strength hasn’t improved in a long time—it’s even regressed."

"..."

Seth’s heart trembled uncontrollably. He stared at Elgin in shock—how had he known exactly what had been troubling him?

Ever since donning the armor, Seth had felt that no matter how hard he trained, his strength refused to grow. Instead, it was *declining*.

Seth had been tormented by this, and now, hearing Merlin’s words, could it really be connected to this eerie armor?

Seeing Seth’s reaction, Merlin smiled. "You don’t actually think this armor only feeds on your blood, do you? That would make the price for its power far too unfair."

"You mean..." Seth unconsciously used a respectful tone, seeking guidance.

"The armor doesn’t just sustain itself on your blood—it also drains your power to evolve. That’s why no matter how hard you train, you can’t break through your limits." Merlin explained.

Seth fell silent, his resolve wavering. This armor was too important—it had turned him from ordinary to extraordinary!

The sheer amplification of power allowed him to crush powerful foes, even becoming one of the top Thorn Knights.

Recalling the intoxicating feeling of overwhelming enemies with the armor’s strength, Seth was addicted. He couldn’t bear to give it up.

After standing at the pinnacle of power for so long, the thought of letting go was unbearable. Seth was no exception.

"You... you’re lying! In the end, you just want me to give up the armor so you can take it for yourself!"

"Hmph. Who would want such a tedious thing? My power doesn’t need any external boosts." Merlin sneered, pitying Seth’s numbness to his own plight.

In truth, his words were meant for the demonic armor—an outright rejection of its submission. He wouldn’t accept it.

*Crack, crack.* The armor understood Merlin’s stance. Its entire frame trembled violently before dissolving into a wisp of black smoke, coiling around Seth and merging into his body.

A chill ran through Seth. Sensing his treasure had returned, he exulted, "Hahaha! See?! The armor chose me! That proves everything you said was a lie!"

Merlin sighed. Seth was beyond help—blinded by his treasure, doomed to a tragic end.

He walked over to Seth and patted his shoulder, speaking in a voice only the two of them could hear—

"Whether it’s a lie or not... I think you already know the truth deep down."

"I advise you to return this armor to its rightful owner. Don’t cling to it like a fool."

"Otherwise, you’ll die a miserable death, unable to escape your fate..."

"The true master of this armor is someone you cannot afford to provoke. I think you know who that is."

title: Chapter 39 — Inquiry
content:
Chapter 39 — Inquiry

Volume 12 · Chapter 39

.“.....

Seth stared blankly, his eyes widening as his pupils contracted violently.

Because Merlin had spoken in a roundabout way, yet was clearly hinting at a powerful demon lord.

He had foretold that if Seth didn't return the demon armor, he would easily meet a miserable death.

Seth knew this demon armor belonged to Mammon, but he wasn't very familiar with the stinginess of the greed lord—a single coin wouldn't even let others touch it.

So besides being amazed at Merlin's knowledge of demons, Seth had no other thoughts about Merlin's final words.

No matter how Seth thought about it, Merlin felt he had made his point clearly, treating it as a well-intentioned reminder.

As for whether Seth believed it? That had nothing to do with Merlin at all; there was no need to meddle in strange affairs.

After all, Merlin was currently being fed to the demons and didn't want to get involved in mysterious incidents.

Moreover, besides being somewhat familiar with Asmodeus, Merlin wasn't close to other lords—some he hadn't even exchanged words with.

Some demon lords even looked down on Merlin, this young lord, thinking he lacked experience and didn't understand how deep the demon waters ran.

Merlin had been holding back the whole time, not saying everything clearly.

Because he feared that the more he said, the greater the risk of exposing that he himself was a demon.

So under the premise of not revealing his identity, Merlin gave Seth as much warning as possible.

Merlin didn't say anything more to Seth and walked toward the outside of the conference hall, apparently intending to rest.

However, Merlin stopped halfway and remembered to remind them about the rebel army, adding a sentence as he turned back.

"When the rebels attack, just let me know. You all only need to stay in safe places—I'll handle the troublesome guys myself. See you~"

With that, Merlin left the conference hall without looking back, leaving everyone in bewilderment.

The atmosphere was unnervingly quiet; for a moment, no one knew what to say.

The most emotionally unstable was probably Seth, brooding over what had just happened.

Although Seth couldn't determine whether Elkin the Great Swordsman's words were true or false, he'd rather believe they were all exaggerations and scaremongering.

Most of Seth's achievements today could be attributed to the demon armor's power.

If it weren't for this armor forcibly boosting Seth's strength, he probably wouldn't have qualified to become a Thorn Knight.

Recalling all the times he had controlled that power, Seth became even more reluctant to give up this treasure, wanting to keep it by any means necessary.

"That... Elkin the Great Swordsman was just lying, right? He said a bunch of nonsense, which is really strange."

Seth was anxious inside, lacking confidence, and broke the silence, hoping his companions would side with him.

The other three Thorn Knights remained silent.

Everyone could see the demonic nature of the armor, but couldn't determine whether Seth continuing to wear it was good or bad.

If they let Seth give up the armor, it meant he would fall behind and lose his qualification as a Thorn Knight.

"....What's wrong with you all? Why aren't you saying anything? Don't tell me you actually believe that guy's words?!" Seth's forehead broke into cold sweat, feeling inexplicably nervous.

"Can't say for certain. The Great Swordsman also mentioned earlier that he only heard rumors, and it's hard to tell truth from fiction." Elizabeth spoke up.

"Right! The Great Swordsman was just passing along hearsay. How could we believe someone who won't even show their true face?!" Seth's emotions flared up, as if he had grasped a lifeline.

The knights glanced at each other, feeling that Seth had worn this armor for a long time without any issues—it was probably just rumors after all.

"Perhaps the Great Swordsman was just joking?" Morrison chuckled.

"It must have been a joke! I can be certain of that!" Seth quickly agreed, his expression somewhat self-deceiving.

"Seth, you've been wearing this armor—haven't you felt any discomfort? Anything like the backlash the Great Swordsman mentioned?"

Elizabeth looked up and asked seriously.

"No! How could there be such a thing? I've always been fine!" Seth answered with absolute certainty, though it was true that his strength had been difficult to improve since wearing the armor.

"....Elizabeth nodded, thought it over carefully, and then said nothing more."

"So promise me—if any problems arise, throw away this armor. Don't sink deeper into the mud."

As night fell, the moon flickered behind the dark clouds.

It seemed a storm was coming, washing away the empire mired in chaos.

At this moment, the queen's bedroom was peaceful and quiet, yet couldn't hide the precarious situation.

Elizabeth stood by the window, watching the rolling dark clouds outside, occasional flashes of lightning revealing the fierce sky.

She was contemplating how to counter the Ofré family's allied forces next.

Although they had found Elkin the Great Swordsman as a powerful ally, she couldn't be too careless and needed to prepare for failure.

Even though Merlin said to leave everything to him alone, Elizabeth was still uneasy and planned to set up two defensive lines.

If Merlin failed, the Thorn Knights would form a new defense line as the second safeguard against Ofré breaking into the imperial capital.

Elizabeth thought carefully, already sensing the enemy drawing closer, her heart slightly uneasy.

Meredith stood behind Elizabeth, guarding her, his furrowed brow clearly troubled.

She recalled today's events, wondering if the queen and Elkin the Great Swordsman had some kind of affair?

Meredith had never liked Elkin, and now hearing that he was involved with the queen made him even more irritated.

Elizabeth felt it was getting late and turned to tell Meredith, "Windsor, you should go rest first. There's nothing happening here."

CCtz/sf

Okay...

Meredith nodded but wore an hesitant expression.

"What's wrong?" Elizabeth raised her delicate brows.

"...I have a question I want to ask Your Majesty?" Meredith clenched her fists, mustering courage in secret.

"Just ask directly. No need to be so formal..." Elizabeth smiled.

"This question concerns Your Majesty's privacy, so I'm a bit hesitant to ask, but I'm very curious about it. So..." Meredith lowered her head, her expression showing some inner conflict.

"Just say it. There's no one else here. I'm your sister, after all." Elizabeth crossed her arms and struck a commanding pose.

Meredith blushed, feeling an odd sensation deep inside, but emboldened by Elizabeth's encouragement, she became more daring.

"Your Majesty... are you and Elkin the Great Swordsman... having an affair?"

Elizabeth nearly fainted, her mouth twitching, her eyebrows twitching uncontrollably, unable to speak. Inside, a million wild horses seemed to gallop past.

...What did you say?!

Who's been sleeping with Merlin, that bumbling fool?

title: Chapter 40 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 40 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 12 · Chapter 40

Elizabeth was stunned by Maysfield's sudden question, not knowing how to answer.

Her husband had passed away long ago, and she had no intention of remarrying.

But the idea that she was having an affair with the Elgin Great Swordmaster was pure nonsense—where did this misunderstanding come from?

Elizabeth calmed herself down and spoke in a very serious tone.

"What are you talking about? How could I possibly have... that kind of relationship with the Elgin Great Swordmaster?"

"It's just that I have some doubts..." Maysfield lowered his head, his brow furrowed tightly. "Why was it so easy to invite a mysterious figure like the Elgin Great Swordmaster, who is always on the move? Why was he willing to help us despite what happened before? Why are you so defensive of the Elgin Great Swordmaster? If there isn't a deep, intimate relationship, I find it hard to understand all of this..."

"..." A cold sweat dripped from Elizabeth's forehead. She felt Maysfield's suspicion was not entirely unreasonable. "What intimate relationship? We just negotiated for one night, reached an alignment of interests, and cooperated. Don't overcomplicate things."

"We treated the Elgin Great Swordmaster as an enemy before, and after one night, all the grudges were resolved. I don't think it's realistic to just say it was negotiation." Maysfield looked at Elizabeth with a hurt expression, his tone full of suspicion. "A man and a woman alone together late at night, after one night, all the enmity is gone... was this really solved by negotiation?"

"Windsor! Wait! Don't say such baffling things!" Elizabeth's eyes widened, feeling that the misunderstanding was hard to clear up.

"Actually, Your Majesty and the Elgin Great Swordmaster are already in that kind of relationship, aren't they?" Maysfield muttered, very conflicted.

"What kind of relationship!? Don't guess wildly!" Elizabeth's head felt like it had doubled in size.

"Forcing Your Majesty to stoop to such a compromise is my incompetence... I'm sorry to you!" Maysfield clenched his fists in frustration, thinking that Elizabeth had made a physical transaction with the Elgin Great Swordmaster.

"emmmmmm..."

Elizabeth said nothing, her face dark, at a loss for words at Maysfield's lewd speculation.

But thinking about it, she couldn't really blame Maysfield. Her private negotiations with Merlin were indeed easy to misunderstand.

Elizabeth looked at Maysfield's dejected expression and sighed inwardly, explaining seriously.

"Windsor, calm down. You need to understand that in this world, there are no eternal enemies, only eternal interests. The Elgin Great Swordmaster and I simply found common ground, so we cooperated. It's nothing like what you think."

Maysfield calmed down a little and asked tentatively, "Is... that true?"

"Silly girl, what do you take me for? I am the Empress of the Empire. How could I do something so despicable?" Elizabeth tapped Maysfield on the forehead, almost exasperated with her knight.

"..." Maysfield lowered his head and said quietly, "I just don't want Your Majesty to have anything to do with that despicable, shameless, perverted man..."

"Honestly, Michelle is not a child anymore. How could I be so casual? Shouldn't the first priority be my daughter's feelings?" Elizabeth said helplessly.

"..." Maysfield had nothing to say, finding some logic in that. It seemed she had been too sensitive. "Alright, I'm very sorry, Your Majesty. So what benefits did you give the Great Swordmaster?"

"This..." Elizabeth paused for a moment, then smiled and answered, "Secret. I can't say what was negotiated. It's confidential. If I told you, it would violate the spirit of the contract."

Elizabeth couldn't conveniently tell Maysfield about the deal with Merlin, nor could she tell anyone.

After all, Elizabeth had promised Merlin to keep everything secret and not reveal anything about him.

Now that the relationship between the royal family and the Elgin Great Swordmaster had finally eased a bit, she couldn't go messing things up.

Maysfield showed a disappointed look, feeling that the true identity of this detestable man was right in front of her, and perhaps she could pry for information indirectly.

Now Maysfield held a heavy grudge against the Elgin Great Swordmaster, still remembering those insulting spits of saliva.

"Since Your Majesty has invited the Elgin Great Swordmaster, you must know his true identity quite well, right?"

"Yes, I know the face behind the mask, and I know his true identity." Elizabeth gave a definite answer.

"Can Your Majesty tell me? I really want to know who the Elgin Great Swordmaster is!" Maysfield pressed urgently.

"Of course not. The Elgin Great Swordmaster has always hidden his identity for his own reasons. Keeping the secret is the most basic prerequisite for cooperation." Elizabeth showed a hint of apology.

Maysfield was greatly disappointed, feeling that the Elgin Great Swordmaster's true identity was right in front of her, yet she couldn't get the answer.

She had finally found clues to follow up and avenge the arrow wound, but was thwarted at every turn.

Elizabeth carefully studied Maysfield's reaction, as if she had discovered a big secret. "Windsor, why do you lose your cool every time the Elgin Great Swordmaster is mentioned? You get all worked up, your breathing quickens, your face flushes... Could it be that you're smitten and have fallen for him?"

"Ah?! No!" Maysfield was so startled she stammered, completely losing her composure.

"I never thought cute little Windsor would have her heart flutter too. What an eye-opener, hoo hoo~" Elizabeth said in a teasing tone.

"..." Maysfield frowned in disgust, as if a toad had crawled onto her foot, thinking—

What the hell is "heart flutter"!?

Those reactions are from anger!!!

The next morning.

Black clouds gathered into a single mass, like a thick sheet of iron, slowly sinking toward the ground, seeming to have already reached the horizon.

Rainstorms came in bursts, raindrops forming lines that crisscrossed into a vast white sheet, like a heavy stage curtain.

Within the Empire, the O'Frey Family's combined军团 marched imposingly toward the final battlefield.

Black armor clattered loudly, as if declaring that the flames of war were about to burn this land.

A full army of over a hundred thousand soldiers crowded together, their steady steps approaching the fragile Imperial Capital.

At this moment, the Imperial Capital's defenses were poor. The city walls had been loosened and weakened by the great flood summoned by the Lake Fairy earlier.

Even the defending soldiers were not many, most of them hastily assembled troops.

The remaining Kingdom Army plus the Bauhinia Knight and the Rose Family's private army totaled less than twenty thousand.

Before the mighty combined军团, they seemed utterly insignificant, and the Imperial Capital swayed in the wind and rain, on the verge of falling at any moment.

The elite combined军团 was strong and well-equipped, the soldiers all using powerful enchanted weapons, with magical beasts and mercenaries also aiding.

Several sturdy magical beasts, the Black Wool Elephants, pulled a giant magic cannon slowly forward, exuding immense pressure!

Towering siege weapons lined up in neat rows, constantly approaching the fragile Imperial Capital.

War drums thundered, and the choir's hymns drifted faintly...

The wind was especially strong at higher points, roaring like an ox, making it hard for people to keep their footing.

Yet at the top of the Clock Tower, the tallest building in the Imperial Capital, Merlin stood, gazing at the unstoppable combined军团.

His black robe was battered noisily by the wind and rain. Merlin, wearing his mask, pulled up his hood and narrowed his eyes slightly—

"They sure came fast~"

"But what a pity..."

"Now it's time for the mowing game :<" =

(。v。)

title: Chapter 41 — Resistance
content:
Chapter 41 — Resistance

Volume 12 · Chapter 41

The rear of the allied legion.
A battle chariot as solid as bronze walls and iron slowly advanced toward the imperial capital.
To avoid unknown risks, Grand Duke Ofrey employed a rather sneaky method of attack.
He had his subordinates take the first step into the imperial capital to attack the royal city, while he himself hid at the rear.
When Grand Duke Ofrey reached the borders of the imperial capital, the war might already be over, and he could directly begin the coronation ceremony of the new emperor.
Inside the chariot, the slender staff officer Gabry was discussing the next steps with Grand Duke Ofrey.
“Black Wolf Mercenary Corps hasn't returned for so long; the assassination plan must have failed.” Grand Duke Ofrey slammed his hand hard on the table, dissatisfied, saying, “Hey! What a bunch of useless trash! I gave them so many benefits, and they keep bragging about how strong their team is, comparable to the Thorn Knights, yet they have absolutely no effect!
“Please calm your anger, Grand Duke, you can't say that.” Gabry gave a gloomy smile, “The Black Wolf Mercenary Corps isn't completely useless either; just treat them as our vanguard, used to probe the queen's background and give that stinking woman a blow to her morale.
“Also, I suppose that little girl Elizabeth must have been terrified, right? Being able to casually dispatch a five‑person assassination squad of Saint‑tier experts shows how deep my background is, far surpassing the empire's control.” Grand Duke Ofrey's aged features scrunched together, “But the Black Wolf Knight Corps is really too useless; the imperial capital's defenses are lacking, and even just a few Thorn Knights can't handle it.
“Even if the Black Wolf Mercenary Corps lags behind the empire's top Thorn Knights, they should still be able to inflict some damage on the enemy, paving the way for our next plan to assault the royal capital and further weaken the empire's strength.” Gabry added from the side with a gloomy tone.
“It seems the Black Wolf Mercenary Corps only has this much worth....” Grand Duke Ofrey nodded.
“This war, we still have to pin our hopes on the Elemental Four Sword Saints; they four are our main fighting force. With them, capturing the fragile imperial capital is merely a matter of time.” Gabry paused, speaking seriously, “I suppose the imperial capital now has no one capable of resisting the combined assault of the Elemental Four Sword Saints. When the time comes, Grand Duke, you will proclaim yourself the new emperor—who would dare not submit?”
“Hahaha....” Grand Duke Ofrey burst into laughter, his white beard trembling, full of confidence in the Elemental Four Sword Saints, “You truly are my strategist; you’ve grasped my thoughts completely.”
“Grand Duke, you’re making me laugh.” Gabry bowed slightly.
“The Elemental Four Sword Saints have already been sent out as the vanguard; judging by the time, it seems they have already clashed head‑on with the empire, right?” Grand Duke Ofrey stroked his chin.
“Yes, but given the current strength of the empire, they probably can't withstand our iron hooves; even those poor Thorn Knights will end up as souls beneath the swords of the Four Sword Saints.” Gabry speculated, considering the disparity in strength between the two sides, the outcome is already clear.
The imperial capital, after internal strife, has become riddled with holes, and even its last trump card, the lake fairy, has fallen into a deep slumber.
The current situation is practically tailor‑made to give the Ofrey family an excellent opportunity.
If even this face‑to‑face output method could be defeated, there would be no other explanation besides stupidity.
“That’s certainly the case; perhaps by the time we enter the imperial capital’s territory, the war will already be over and Elizabeth will have become our prisoner.” Grand Duke Ofrey said, his face glowing with honor and a ruddy complexion, slowly.
“We have the Elemental Four Sword Saints leading a force of one hundred thousand allied troops.
“Facing only a few Thorn Knights and less than twenty thousand miscellaneous soldiers.
“The outcome of this is already obvious; even a fool can see it...
“With such an absolute advantage, tell me how we could lose?
The frontline battlefield within the imperial capital.
The clouds in the sky are low and heavy.
As if they could press down onto the ground at any moment.
Occasionally, electric light flickers, tearing a gap in the sky.
Violent rain pours down from the clouds, the massive curtain of rain torn and tossed by the wind, swaying unpredictably.
The main force of the hundred‑thousand allied legion, led by the Elemental Four Sword Saints, is marching forward through the wind and rain, vigorous and high‑spirited, approaching the imperial capital and forming an encirclement.
Regardless of the wind and rain lashing them, these black‑armored soldiers never halt their steps, seeming unstoppable.
Looking afar, the plains of the imperial capital are trampled by dense ranks of cavalry.
Dozens of large engineering devices slowly move, like giants flexing their fists within the legion!
Four figures, completely wrapped in black robes and riding warhorses, walk at the forefront, steadily leading the troops.
The Elemental Four Sword Saints, as the supreme commanders of this assault on the imperial capital, have been ordered to capture it before Grand Duke Ofrey arrives, eliminating anyone daring to resist.
At this point, the distance to the imperial capital is sufficient for it to serve as the battlefield of the decisive clash.
Thus the Elemental

title: Chapter 42 — Identity
content:
Chapter 42 — Identity

Volume 12 · Chapter 42

The sky was alive with wind, clouds, and thunder.

The massive high-output magical cannon glowed with waves of crimson as it entered cooldown.

Enormous raindrops battered the heated barrel, releasing puffs of white mist that were instantly vaporized.

The stormwater washed away the embers of the lightning cannon's blast, leaving the air cool and sharp as if laced with mint.

A great mist rose at the gates of the royal castle, then vanished as quickly as it had appeared.

Standing alone before the castle gates, facing the vast host of a hundred thousand allied troops, was Merlin, his face concealed behind a silver-white mask.

The fierce storm lashed against Merlin's black robes, making them flutter like a cape in the air.

Merlin's gaze was disdainful as he surveyed the massive army before him, showing no hint of fear.

He drew his long sword, plunged it into the earth, then placed both hands on the hilt in a stance of challenge.

That proud figure in the midst of wind and rain commanded respect, and no one dared approach. The mighty allied army, which had been poised to advance, was suddenly held fast in awe.

Though the soldiers hid behind their heavy helmets, their chilling eyes betrayed them, and an illusion of invincibility took root in their hearts.

Just moments ago, that had been the ultra-high-output magical cannon, crafted at great expense by Archduke Overre—far more powerful than the cannons aboard William's ship!

Its tremendous destructive force was meant to obliterate the empire's living forces. A single shot carried the power of magical essence itself!

Yet just now, that cannon—which they had taken such pride in—had been effortlessly deflected by the masked stranger, seemingly with just one hand.

This left everyone utterly bewildered. The ultra-high-output magical cannon had not inflicted a single injury, instead dissipating as if it had malfunctioned.

The Four Sword Saints stood dumbfounded, unable to comprehend what they had witnessed. Had they stepped forward, they would likely have hesitated to face the magical cannon head-on.

While they might not have been killed outright by a single blast, they would almost certainly have suffered grievous wounds.

Yet that mysterious man had not been harmed at all, instead bouncing back energetically as if nothing had happened.

The Four Elemental Sword Saints were filled with doubt. They had assumed the imperial capital was already in its final throes, with no remaining strength to resist.

Then suddenly, a mysterious figure had charged out, forcing them to take the situation seriously and reconsider their plans.

Inside the imperial capital, Elizabeth had acted according to Merlin's request, leaving him to fight alone outside.

But within the castle walls, the Thorn Knights formed a second line of defense—a final safeguard.

Even if Merlin could not hold back the allied army, none of the others would be able to either.

Still, this gave Elizabeth some peace of mind, allowing her to make additional preparations, which was far from useless.

At that moment, on a temporary observation platform, Sir Meredith, Sir Seth, and Sir Morrison stood watching the situation outside the imperial capital.

If something went wrong with Archduke Elkin's forces, they might need to respond quickly and organize an effective defense.

Below the observation platform, the imperial army was densely packed, composed of the royal army, the Purple Embroidery Knights, and the Rose Knights.

Though hastily assembled and lacking coordination, it was better than nothing.

The soldiers of the imperial army were nervous, their hands trembling involuntarily, lacking confidence in the outcome of this battle.

Among the Thorn Knights, Catherine, skilled in defense, did not engage the enemy but remained by the queen's side to guard against any assassins sneaking in from outside.

Seth's face showed no expression at all, like a soulless puppet, sitting silently in the corner of the observation platform.

He could not forget what Archduke Elkin had said to him yesterday—that if he did not return his armor, he would die a horrible death.

Though only a few words, they had dealt a fatal blow to Seth's spirit, nearly driving him to the brink of collapse.

What Seth feared most now was that the armor would bring him trouble, turning him into a slave to the armor, with his future completely ruined.

Seth was not in the mood to fight, his mind scattered and unable to focus his attention.

Unlike Seth, Meredith and Morrison were both deeply worried about the situation, especially regarding their companion, Archduke Elkin.

Although the Thorn Knights had had their share of grievances with Archduke Elkin in the past, facing a common enemy, they still hoped he would sweep the enemy aside.

"Who would have thought that scoundrel would actually charge out alone to face the enemy?!" Meredith muttered, slightly surprised.

"Yes, we have to admit, his courage in facing the entire allied army alone is admirable. If it were me, I absolutely wouldn't dare to do that."

A cold sweat trickled down Morrison's forehead.

"But it seems like there's no problem. Perhaps Archduke Elkin can really defeat the entire army by himself!" Meredith's eyes were fixed on the lone figure standing in the storm in the distance.

"I think there's no problem. I've never seen Archduke Elkin go all out before." Morrison paused, then seriously analyzed, "The fact that he was able to deflect that magical cannon is truly incredible. If that's the case, then heavy weapons like that might not work against him at all."

"Indeed, who knows what tricks that man is pulling? How could he possibly disperse the magical cannon's power?" Meredith sighed.

In the corner, Seth lowered his head, his expression awkward, silently tightening his grip on his long spear.

Outside the imperial capital, the battle raged on.

The Four Sword Saints were still in shock, their minds racing with what to do.

"I want to go test myself against him. Who would dare stand in our way alone? He must be fearless!" The Fire Sword Saint spoke with anger, feeling insulted by the enemy. They had expected the empire, cornered and on the brink of annihilation, to unleash some spectacular counterattack, only to send out a single man, which was laughable.

"Stay calm. This mysterious guy doesn't seem easy to deal with. Didn't you see how the magical cannon was dispersed?" The Earth Sword Saint whispered quietly.

"Maybe he has some magical defensive artifact on him? Otherwise, how could he not be injured at all? That's unnatural." The Wind Sword Saint suddenly interjected.

"That's right, I agree. Magic doesn't work on that man, so it's better to hold back our magical attacks." The Earth Sword Saint said seriously.

"Why are we making such a big deal?!" The Fire Sword Saint grew impatient, tugging at his reins. "The empire has only sent out one man to face us. Isn't that a joke? I think the empire has no talent left, only able to send one person to fight. Ha!"

"I suspect it's not that simple. An empire's resources are usually deep. Perhaps sending one person to fight is a strategic move, and we should be cautious." The Water Sword Saint said carefully.

Everyone fell silent, agreeing that something was indeed strange. On one side, a hundred thousand well-equipped troops were poised to attack, while on the other, only a masked stranger stood alone.

This incongruous scene left everyone deeply puzzled. Who had the courage to face an entire army alone?

At that moment, a subordinate slowly approached and leaned in close to the Water Sword Saint's ear, appearing to have gathered some information.

"That man—who exactly is he? He seems very strong. But I'm interested in testing myself against him." The Wind Sword Saint became intrigued by Merlin and wanted to engage in combat.

"Let's not act rashly for now. I've just received a secret report." The Water Sword Saint's expression turned grave after hearing the report.

"I suspect that..."

"That man is none other than the currently thriving Archduke Elkin."

(End of Chapter)

title: Chapter 43 — Bonus Chapters for Monthly Votes
content:
Chapter 43 — Bonus Chapters for Monthly Votes

Volume 12 · Chapter 43

"Erkin Great Swordmaster?!" Earth Sword Saint looked astonished, as if he recognized the name. "That's the guy rumored to frequently one-shot Saint-tier strongmen? Heard he's invincible, and many call him the Empire's savior."

"It's just speculation for now; we can't accurately determine the other party's identity, but many subordinates seem to think it's that rumored man." Water Sword Saint locked his gaze on the distant figure.

"I heard Erkin Great Swordmaster has a bad relationship with the royal family; he couldn't possibly be here blocking us, right?" Earth Sword Saint asked in surprise.

"What a damn swordmaster! Charge and cut them down!" Fire Sword Saint had no patience; this endless probing was getting on his nerves.

"Don't rush; let the legion go ahead and test the waters first—it'll be good for scouting the path." Water Sword Saint waved at the commander beside him and shot him a meaningful glance.

The commander understood, dispatching a fast-moving troop of nearly ten thousand soldiers to sortie quickly, accompanied by several dozen magical beasts—giant gray wolves!

As the war horn sounded, the formation of magical beasts and knights roared and charged toward Merlin.

The wind and rain kept howling, and thunder occasionally roared across the sky.

The heavy rain poured down densely, making it hard to open one's eyes.

The combined legion of ten thousand soldiers shouted and killed, their faces hideously fierce!

The magical beast wolves leading the charge bared their bloody fangs, revealing sinister tusks, already starving.

"What a chore~"

"Want to test my strength, then think of other countermeasures?"

Merlin smiled lightly, thought for a moment, and instead of using Iai Slash, drew his katana.

His wrist flicked, the blade tip pointing at the fiercely approaching enemies, easily tearing through the dense rain.

Rainwater flowed along the blade, yet couldn't wash away the mottled rust and weathered dullness.

Merlin didn't intend to use Iai Slash; he just wanted to show off a bit to give the enemies a taste of fear.

A dozen magical wolves leading the charge growled, their thick hind legs kicking hard, pouncing on the prey!

Merlin's eyes narrowed, his figure turning into a black phantom, the katana in his hand spinning.

His steps were swift, his slicing speed ghostly and unpredictable; consecutive strikes left the magical wolves slain, bursting into layers of blood mist!

The vicious magical beasts merely let out a few mournful cries before losing their life force.

The charging soldiers were stunned, holding their weapons with wide eyes as they stared at the mysterious man in black robes, trembling uncontrollably.

Merlin stood atop the giant wolf, slowly withdrawing the large blade from the corpses, looking down at the soldiers.

"What's wrong? Scared stupid? You guys are really boring. Since you dared charge up, you must have brought a death wish, right? Then let me get more excited! Please perk up, or dying in a muddle is too much of a waste!"

Stimulated by Merlin's words, the soldiers were enraged, roaring as they charged with their weapons.

The dense army of ten thousand surrounded Merlin like water squeezing through a sieve, trying to crush the mysterious strongman with numbers.

Countless weapons flashed with cold light toward Merlin, the sky thundering, but couldn't possibly drown out the brutal charging sounds!

Merlin laughed disdainfully, advancing instead of retreating, charging into the dense enemy crowd and beginning a ruthless massacre!

His movements were unpredictable; the soldiers couldn't see his figure, only barely catching the corner of his black robe.

Merlin's blade fell, and the ten-thousand-strong legion plunged into chaos instantly; the piercing screams were horrifying to behold!

Blood became worthless at this moment, because from afar, blood fountains surged with the rhythm of Merlin's blade swings.

The soldiers' hot blood, full of anger just moments ago, was severed by the rusty katana in the next instant, spraying into the air.

The originally black muddy ground was stained by the soldiers' blood, and the mud took on a dark red hue!

Merlin was invincible within the enemy encirclement, instantly transforming into a leaping spirit, flickering ghostly among the enemy siege.

He swung the katana in his hand, skillfully reaping lives, mercilessly, like a beast out of control, frantically devouring the enemy's flesh and blood.

Sure enough, when Merlin went berserk, he was no different from a heartless big villain—no, even worse!

The ten-thousand-strong combined legion with numerical advantage fell into a passive position, unable to do anything against Merlin at all, instantly descending into chaos.

They couldn't beat him in a frontal assault at all, only being slowly played to death by Merlin; their fate was miserable.

So many people swinging swords and knives wildly, yet not even Merlin's hair tip could be touched.

The four Elemental Sword Saints watching from afar, seeing Merlin's incomparable back, immediately fell into deep worry.

"That man's swordsmanship is sharp; he's a true strongman. Looks like he really is Erkin Great Swordmaster." Wind Sword Saint narrowed his eyes.

"Something feels off. That's not Erkin Great Swordmaster." Water Sword Saint stared wide-eyed at the katana in Merlin's hand, her heart trembling uncontrollably. "Look closely at the knife in that man's hand! Does it look familiar?!"

The other three Sword Saints, seeing Water Sword Saint's terror, looked carefully in surprise, especially at the katana in the mysterious man's hands, and were immediately shocked.

"Good heavens! No way!"

"Good grief!"

"Why is the King's [sword] in that person's hands?!"

Meanwhile, Merlin was like a Demon Lord descending, making the combined legion experience what despair truly meant.

Before a true strongman, numerical advantage is just a prop; no matter how many more people, it's just sending them to their deaths!

title: Chapter 44 — Interrogation
content:
Chapter 44 — Interrogation

Volume 12 · Chapter 44

The watchtower within the imperial capital.

Morrison watched as Grand Swordmaster Elkwin handled everything single-handedly while still winning easily, unable to hold back his inner sigh.

"What piercing sword technique? It's completely flawless. I could never reach that level."

Beside him, Mesfield said nothing, her feelings complicated as she agreed that Grand Swordmaster Elkwin was indeed extremely powerful.

But this was of no benefit to her at all; it might even cause some harm.

Queen Elizabeth had asked Grand Swordmaster Elkwin for help precisely because the Thorn Knights couldn't handle it, their abilities limited.

If this continued unchecked, Mesfield felt the queen would grow dependent on Grand Swordmaster Elkwin and no longer need the Thorn Knights.

Mesfield pouted, her tone sour as she sneered.

"What's so impressive? I could do that just as easily. Isn't this just picking on the weak? Can you harvest crops and also create an army off it?"

"That's not harvesting at all." Morrison turned to look at Mesfield and retorted, "Didn't you see the grand swordmaster's sword technique? It's as if he was born to kill, with not a single wasted movement. A full ten thousand troops surrounded him, and they could do absolutely nothing against him."

"I think he was mediocre. I didn't see anything impressive," Mesfield said defiantly. She wouldn't admit it out loud, but in her heart she was still remarkably astonished by Grand Swordmaster Elkwin's calm composure.

"Tch! How can you say he was mediocre?" Morrison furrowed his brows and explained, "Grand Swordmaster Elkwin never showed the slightest sign of fatigue throughout. That was a combined siege of ten thousand soldiers! Can you maintain such composure and stay in peak condition at all times? A normally outstanding warrior would've already fallen apart."

"Shut up already. Pack your things and go hang out with the grand swordmaster. The Thorn Knights won't be able to keep you around anymore," Mesfield said, annoyed that Morrison kept praising Grand Swordmaster Elkwin. She felt this guy's loyalties had completely shifted.

Morrison was left speechless, countered by Mesfield with nothing to say in return.

In truth, Morrison was happy. An former enemy who had now become a powerful ally.

Of course, the more powerful Grand Swordmaster Elkwin was, the easier it would be to turn the tide and resist the allied forces.

Seeing Grand Swordmaster Elkwin crush the enemy's encirclement so effortlessly while still appearing fresh, Morrison rejoiced from the bottom of his heart.

"I don't mean anything bad by it. The grand swordmaster is our ally now. I just feel it's lucky to find such a powerful external force."

Mesfield rolled her eyes and couldn't resist underming him. "Don't trust that despicable man completely. We should stay more vigilant."

Morrison looked at Mesfield and asked in surprise, "Mesfield, why do you have such hostility toward Grand Swordmaster Elkwin? It's a bit too strange. Did he do something outrageous to you?"

"That—"

Mesfield thought about it. Recalling the humiliation from back then made her extremely infuriated, and she quietly clenched her fists.

But these matters were not easy to tell others. So Mesfield said in a sarcastic tone, "Nothing particularly outrageous."

"Intuition. A woman's intuition tells me this guy is no good."

"Huh." Morrison immediately put on a forced smile and helplessly thought to himself, *Intuition?*

That excuse was far too strained, wasn't it?!

Meanwhile, at the frontier of the war.

All four Elements Sword Saints bore expressions of utter shock.

Watching the mystical man in the opposite army holding his blade, their hearts refused to remain calm.

Although the katana overall looked extremely ordinary, its rusty blade would make people believe it was scrap metal at best.

Yet this unremarkable katana sent all four Sword Saints into astonishment, triggering instant联想s about something.

The Four Elements Sword Saints were all now elderly men past a hundred years old, warriors who had reached Saint-tier a century ago.

However, before their retirement, they had significant ties to the demon race and were not as ignorant of demons as ordinary people.

In fact, the Four Elements Sword Saints' retirement was inextricably linked to the ruler of the First Demon Lord Palace at that time—Merlin's mother.

Back when the four sword saints had first gained fame in their youth, they were at the height of their popularity. The four brothers' combined secret sword technique was simply invincible.

It wasn't merely an ordinary sword technique—it leveraged powerful elemental forces to greatly amplify their joint sword skill.

The Sword Saints had also acquired four extremely rare swords that appeared to be plain gemstones but were actually high-concentration natural crystals of a single element.

Each swing of an Element Blade could awaken elemental power, allowing ordinary sword techniques to hit as hard as magic!

Ordinary mages could hardly find elemental crystals. Just having a small piece would drastically accelerate one's cultivation, so the effect of such rare crystals was truly astonishing.

And yet the Four Sword Saints acquired four of them? Their luck could only be described as defying the heavens.

After the Four Elements Sword Saints rose to fame, they swept through many renowned strongmen of a hundred years ago, consistently achieving victory.

Their reputation grew ever larger, becoming the strongest quartet of their era—just like how Grand Swordmaster Elkwin was at the height of his powers today.

However, gradually, the Four Elements Sword Saints grew numb to victory, their cultivation hitting an impasse they couldn't break through. Desperately seeking to shatter the Saint-tier seal, they attempted to step into that unknown realm.

So the Four Elements Sword Saints set their sights on the demon race's rulers, choosing as their first target Lucifer II, the Proud Lord of the First Demon Lord Palace—Merlin's mother.

Though the Elements Four Sword Saints' strength had stalled, they had heard rumors that demon lords were extremely powerful. But this couldn't stop their determination to break through Saint-tier!

The four sword saints desperately needed to battle truly strong opponents to identify their own shortcomings, or else their entire lives' achievements would stagnate.

So in their youthful arrogance, the Four Elements Sword Saints crossed the strait by ship to the First Demon Lord Palace and challenged Lucifer II!

But the Four Elements Sword Saints had overestimated themselves. Back then, the four young sword saints were near the peak of Saint-tier—roughly comparable to Mesfield's current level.

They fought fiercely but could not defeat the Proud Lord. Merlin's mother utterly crushed all four of them!

If they hadn't had instant-transmigration scroll items on their person, they likely would've died in the Swamp of Death.

Later, disheartened by their defeat, the four sword saints crossed the vast ocean and retired to the unknown Chaotic Seas.

There, they hoped to test their luck—if fortune smiled upon them, they might encounter an opportunity that would help them break through.

If they were unfortunate, then they would die in the Chaotic Seas and never return.

Now that they dared to re-emerge from the Chaotic Seas, the four sword saints' strength had likely improved significantly, as if they had encountered something beneficial there.

The fact that the four sword saints dared to cross swords with the demon race's Proud Lord showed they were confident in defeating Merlin's mother and avenging their past disgrace!

After centuries of cultivation in the Chaotic Seas, the Four Elements Sword Saints' strength had surged from near the peak of Saint-tier to transcending Saint-tier's peak and nearly brushing against the threshold of the next realm—comparable to the Lake Fairy's substitute!

"It must be correct. That is the King's Relic belonging to the Proud Lord, Banri Garan!" the Water Sword Saint answered with certainty.

"How could a demon race King's Relic end up in a human's hands?! Has the First Demon Lord Palace changed rulers over the centuries?!" the Earth Sword Saint asked in astonishment, as if encountering a demon lord within the human empire was as shocking as seeing a UFO.

"It's impossible. Demon lords don't casually walk around outside, and besides, demons live for a long time. They wouldn't easily change rulers unless they died," the Water Sword Saint paused, then continued, "But we personally experienced Lucifer II's strength. How could she have died within a few centuries? I've never heard of any prodigy emerging within a hundred years. Only now, with the four of us joining forces, do we stand a chance against Lucifer II."

Apparently, the Water Sword Saint had not yet deeply studied the demon race and didn't know that the katana Banri Garan could only be wielded by successive Proud Lords—it was common knowledge that only a lord could equip a King's Relic.

"Then who exactly is this mysterious man? He's not Grand Swordmaster Elkwin, nor does he seem affiliated with the demon faction," the Wind Sword Saint's tone was filled with dread and unease.

"Right? Just thinking about it makes my head explode. The opponent has no demon aura—he's clearly a human. Yet he's wielding a demon King's Relic. Who is he?!" the Fire Sword Saint was beside himself, stamping his feet in frustration.

"It's difficult to confirm for now. Why don't we ask that man directly?" the Water Sword Saint suggested.

"That's right. That man is extraordinary in combat. Anyone else who goes up will only be signing their death warrant. Only us can handle him." The Wind Sword Saint nodded, unconsciously revealing intense battle intent.

The rain and wind showed no signs of stopping. Merlin sheathed his katana back into its scabbard, standing among the dead soldiers' corpses that had been piled into several small hills.

Four sword saints wrapped in black robes approached at a leisurely pace, their aged faces retaining firmness, their flowing beards exuding an air of seasoned generals.

Merlin did not move but instead scrutinized the four approaching individuals. Though he couldn't identify which reinforcements they were, sensing their overwhelming pressure, he determined they were rare and formidable warriors.

"Who are you?!" the irritable Fire Sword Saint asked bluntly.

"Me?" Merlin tilted his head and thought for a moment, then replied blandly, "Grand Swordmaster Elkwin."

"Bullshit! Do you take us for uneducated fools?!" the Fire Sword Saint bristled and glared, angry. "Grand Swordmaster Elkwin is hailed as the empire's hero! How could he possibly have ties to the demon race?!"

"You—" The Water Sword Saint pointed at Merlin's weapon and asked seriously, "Named Banri Garan. It is a King's Relic belonging to the demon race's Proud Lord. Only a lord can wield it."

"Oh?" Merlin showed a trace of surprise and said, "You're actually able to identify it? That's quite remarkable. You must have come into contact with the demon lords to know about a King's Relic, haven't you?"

In truth, most people couldn't recognize the blade in Merlin's hands. Unless one understood the demon race, but such people were rare, which is why Merlin found it so surprising.

"Stop beating around the bush! Answer our questions directly!" the Wind Sword Saint glared, his voice rolling like thunder. "Why does a demon King's Relic belong to you?! That clearly belongs to Lucifer II! Did you steal it?!"

"Stole it? Hah." Merlin chuckled and stroked his chin, leisurely saying, "Lucifer II? Ah, yes? She's my mom."

All four sword saints were so startled they nearly spat out their breath, their faces frozen in utter shock, their eyes bulging as if they might fall out of their sockets.

title: Chapter 45 — Grapple
content:
Chapter 45 — Grapple

Volume 12 · Chapter 45

Although it was just a brief conversation, Merlin had already figured out that these four in front of him knew something about demons, and seemed to have seen his old horse before.

Since his demonic identity had already been seen through, there was no need for Merlin to conceal it any longer, so he casually let his true identity slip.

But if Merlin hadn't spoken up, it would have been fine—revealing his true nature at this moment made the four Sword Saints feel as though lightning had struck them. They couldn't believe that the man before them, who showed no demonic aura or features whatsoever, could be the son of Lucifer II!

"Ha, was there really a need to be so surprised? I'm not often in the mood to reveal my true identity to others." Merlin smiled.

"You're the Demon Lord's son?! That's impossible!" the Earth Sword Saint exclaimed, finding it hard to believe.

"What about it? Don't I look like it?" Merlin touched his face, feeling strange. He held the Banri Garan in his hand—was that really a fake?

"You have not a single trace of demonic aura on you—impossible for you to be a demon!" the Wind Sword Saint declared firmly.

"This is a bit complicated to explain," Merlin said with some difficulty, thinking to himself, If I weren't a reincarnator, I'd probably be like a normal demon—skin black as pitch, horns growing from my head, and an overwhelming demonic aura.

"Stop pretending! You're really just a human, aren't you? That sword you're holding must have been stolen through some trickery!" the Fire Sword Saint snapped irritably.

"Let's all calm down. Maybe he's telling the truth," the Water Sword Saint said quietly, signaling his companions not to lose their composure.

"Are you kidding? Do you actually believe this guy's nonsense?" the Earth Sword Saint asked in disbelief.

"Come on, he claims to be the Demon Lord's son? How could that be? Doesn't he look obviously human?" the Fire Sword Saint retorted angrily.

"I think the sword itself isn't fake. That's the Demon Lord's royal scepter, a symbol of the rulers' authority. How could something like that end up on a human? That in itself doesn't make sense," the Water Sword Saint said calmly, analyzing the situation. "We've all witnessed the demons' power firsthand. If this royal scepter were stolen, how could he be strutting around so confidently?"

The others fell silent upon hearing this, realizing the Water Sword Saint had a point—the sword couldn't be a forgery.

Moreover, the possibility of theft was slim, since the royal scepter was the demons' proof of identity. If it were stolen, there would surely be some reaction.

The Water Sword Saint steadied his companions and then asked, "You're really the son of Lucifer II, aren't you? Not lying to us?"

"Why would I lie to you? If you hadn't recognized my sword, I wouldn't have been able to admit it." Merlin shrugged.

"You're a liar through and through. Just now you claimed to be the great Elkin swordsman," the Water Sword Saint narrowed his eyes.

"I am indeed the great Elkin swordsman," Merlin said awkwardly.

The four Sword Saints' expressions turned odd, sensing that this mysterious man's spirit was somewhat abnormal—he had been rambling nonsense from start to finish.

"Water Sword Saint," the Fire Sword Saint said, narrowing his eyes. "The Empire's Hero is actually the Demon Lord's son?"

Merlin thought for a moment and nodded. "Something like that."

"Hahaha, the great Elkin swordsman is actually a demon, and yet he's been hailed as the Empire's Hero. How ironic," the Water Sword Saint said with a sneer, then added with a sinister tone, "Do you take us for fools? How could we possibly accept such an outrageous claim so easily?"

"Believe it or not, it's up to you," Merlin waved his hand dismissively. "Since I've already revealed my identity, shouldn't you all be reporting yourselves now?"

"Hmph!" the Fire Sword Saint scoffed loudly. "Listen up, we are the Elemental Four Sword Saints, legendary warriors who dominated the empire a century ago. This time, we're here to take down Queen Elizabeth's head!"

"Elemental Four Sword Saints?" Merlin furrowed his brow, puzzled. "Never heard of you. Some amateur ragtag group?"

"What did you say?!" the Fire Sword Saint's face flushed red with rage. "When we were active across the continent, you hadn't even been born yet!"

"To be honest," Merlin said with a complicated tone, thinking to himself, At my age, I've probably already exceeded the limits of a human lifespan.

"Enough! I can't take it anymore! This little brat spews nonsense with every word—none of it true. Let's just settle this quickly and march on the imperial capital!" the Fire Sword Saint couldn't hold back any longer.

"I'm thinking the same thing," the Wind Sword Saint said, revealing a sharp killing intent.

Without the slightest hesitation, the four Sword Saints decided to team up and kill this mysterious man right then and there.

They slowly drew their swords from their waists—each blade a different colored gem representing wind, water, fire, and earth, and the four elements erupted and intertwined in the air.

The Fire Sword Saint's body ignited in a fierce blaze, instantly vaporizing the rainwater around him—proof of just how scorching hot his vicinity was.

The Wind Sword Saint unleashed a powerful tornado, forcing the surrounding rainwater to flow upward in reverse, soaring into the sky.

The Earth Sword Saint acted like a conductor, commanding the earth beneath his feet to flow and shift like living things across his blade.

The Water Sword Saint seemed to be receiving an amplification from the rainy weather, and his water current was the largest of the four, violently tearing through the surroundings.

The massive pressure descended like a surging tide, roaring and bearing down on Merlin.

This terrifying pressure was enough to overwhelm even an ordinary Saint-tier warrior, who might faint from shock and lose consciousness on the spot.

Now, the four Sword Saints had grown immensely powerful—utterly incomparable to when they challenged Lucifer II, and they had even begun to brush against the threshold of transcending the Saint tier!

"Oh my~" Merlin raised an eyebrow, glancing at the swords in the four Sword Saints' hands, sensing a faint familiarity—as if she had seen them before.

The Elemental Four Sword Saints gave Merlin no time to remember, launching their attack almost simultaneously, charging straight at him.

Their sword techniques were extremely sharp, appearing loose but actually striking with relentless precision, their coordinated teamwork perfectly complementary.

The multi-colored gem swords suddenly transformed into a shower of blade shadows, dazzling and disorienting, leaving no room to evade.

The four Sword Saints moved with incredible speed—covering dozens of steps in the blink of an eye, enough to take a life.

Merlin's pupils constricted slightly, and she bent down just in time, barely deflecting the incoming slash, the blade grazing past her nose.

The waves rose and fell, and immediately three more swords descended in unison, nearly cutting off Merlin's retreat.

"Oh? Looks like you're not so easy to deal with."

Merlin narrowed her eyes, slightly energized, and began to fight back, her form becoming a shadow as she maneuvered in the narrow space.

Far away, on the observation platform,

Meredith watched the battle outside the palace, a thin line of cold sweat trickling down his forehead.

That's the expert that Duke Overre brought in?

There are four of them! I thought there was only one!

If it weren't for the luck of having summoned the great Elkin swordsman, I doubt we Thorn Knights could have held them off.

And their strength is so formidable—stronger than the golden-ranked adventurer Gregory by a whole level.

That ferocious pressure, even from this distance, I can feel it. It's truly unsettling.

title: Chapter 46 — Helpless
content:
Chapter 46 — Helpless

Volume 12 · Chapter 46

Not just Meisifuerde—even the nearby Morrison was astonished.

"What intense pressure! Far surpassing ordinary Saint-tier powerhouses—it feels like it's already beyond the Saint tier."
Morrison frowned, secretly clenching his fists, shocked by the opponent's strength.
Although he had long known the Oufei family had hired powerful reinforcements, the enemy's strength still exceeded Morrison's imagination.
And there were four more peers—inevitably making one's heart race with fear.
Under normal circumstances, the four Thorn Knights in the capital right now would be completely unable to block the Elemental Four Sword Saints.
Just by feeling the pressure not on the same level, one could tell the Thorn Knights would have no chance against the Elemental Four Sword Saints.

"Yes, with such strength—who knew Duke Oufei could hire them. Looks like our intelligence work was terrible; the enemy's overall power far exceeded our expectations." Meisifuerde frowned, thinking it was lucky Merlin was outside blocking them, otherwise his group would have been at a complete loss.
"What do we do? The Great Swordsman is alone—should we go help him?" Morrison asked tentatively.
"This..." Meisifuerde hesitated, then shook his head. "No need. I think the Great Swordsman is still handling things with ease. He should be able to deal with it himself—he's the one who repelled the lake fairy, after all."
"Also..." Morrison wiped sweat from his forehead.

Seth, sitting quietly in the corner, finally came to his senses and stood up, walking to the edge of the watchtower, glancing at the situation outside the royal city.
He saw the Elemental Four Sword Saints launching a combined attack, their sword blades ruthlessly stabbing at Merlin.
But Merlin seemed unbothered, quickly creating distance, always escaping from awkward angles.
Whether it was Seth's imagination or not, he felt Merlin was deliberately doing it—clearly toying with the four old men, wanting to see just how far the enemies' limits went.
Feeling the intense pressure from the four Sword Saints, a bead of sweat the size of a fist slid down Seth's forehead—
So strong.
Facing a siege of four super-powerhouses and still handling it calmly?
So what Elgin the Great Swordsman said about blocking the combined army wasn't a joke.
Damn! Why is the gap between me and the Great Swordsman so—

The four Sword Saints' sword techniques flew out in quick succession, coordinating with each other, trying to kill the masked man before them!
But the more anxious they got, the more terrified they felt.
Because the four Sword Saints discovered that no matter what sword technique they used, they couldn't land a hit on him. So much time had passed, and they hadn't gained the slightest advantage.
The four Sword Saints' sword techniques were dazzling, constantly besieging Merlin.
But Merlin's evasion speed gave the four Sword Saints a huge headache, as if they were being toyed with.
Rampant battle aura swept and destroyed everything, chaos reigning in the surroundings.
Debris flew everywhere, the ground split with crisscrossing trenches—
"Don't jump around like a monkey in front of us! You damn brat!"
The Fire Sword Saint, in a fury, raised his crimson blade and brought it crashing down!
A scorching sword energy slashed toward Merlin, as if sealing off the enemy's escape routes!
But Merlin just shifted slightly, and the scorching sword energy grazed past his feet.
The ground was cut deep by the heat, stones melted, steaming with a sizzling sound.
"Hah, decent momentum, but your aim needs work."
"Crap!" The Fire Sword Saint, in a rage, wanted to charge forward and keep fighting, but was stopped by the Water Sword Saint.
"Calm down. This guy isn't easy to deal with. He hasn't shown his true strength—we need to go all out." The Water Sword Saint said seriously.
"Yeah, he's mocking us. If we keep going like this, we won't kill this brat—he'll wear us down first." The Earth Sword Saint's forehead beaded with cold sweat; after the prolonged fight, he'd clearly consumed a lot of battle aura.
"Bloody hell, where did the Empire hire this guy? To have such strength at such a young age—unimaginable." The Wind Sword Saint frowned.
Merlin rubbed his slightly sore neck and laughed.
In that brief exchange just now, Merlin had already remembered who these four were.
When the Elemental Four Sword Saints challenged Lucifer II, Merlin had been a little kid with no real power.
But Merlin could still vaguely remember those four young men—foolishly coming to provoke the First Demon Lord Palace, only to be beaten without any ability to fight back.

After so long, those four young men had become white-haired old men, and Merlin couldn't help but sigh inwardly.
"I remember who you are. I've seen you before."
"Oh? So you've heard of our four brothers' names? But you might not even have been born yet!" The Earth Sword Saint said without courtesy.
"You challenged my mom when you were young, got a good beating, and finally fled with a scroll tucked between your tails—am I right?" Merlin smiled playfully.
The moment he said that, the four Sword Saints across from him instantly showed shocked and uneasy expressions—they hadn't expected this mysterious person to know such things!
The dead men instantly lost their composure, recalling their earlier words, and began thinking frantically—
Strange!?
Why does this mysterious guy know about our youthful misdeeds!?
That was something that happened between the four of them—a secret that should never have been told to anyone else!
The only possibility was that this man before them was a demon, and affiliated with the First Demon Lord Palace!
Looks like he wasn't lying earlier—maybe he really is Lucifer's son.
The four exchanged glances, each seeing doubt and unease in the others' eyes.
The Water Sword Saint looked across and asked tentatively, "Could you really be Lucifer II's son?"
"Authentic." Merlin shrugged.
The four Sword Saints all showed chilled expressions—this time they didn't doubt Merlin's identity.
For a moment, all the humiliation from before flooded their hearts, making their emotions complex.
"Why does the King's Artifact have in your hands? Are you the new Arrogant Lord!?" The Earth Sword Saint exclaimed.
"Smart. I am Lucifer III." Merlin grinned.
The four Sword Saints looked at each other, all feeling utterly incredulous.
"But as a demon lord, why are you wandering outside demon territory!?" The Wind Sword Saint asked with agitated emotion.
"Hmm." Merlin touched his chin, embarrassed. "I got fired by the Parliament. Technically speaking, I'm not a lord anymore. Heh, disappointing you all."
"Pfft!"
The four Sword Saints widened their eyes in shock, once again startled into spitting out their drinks—
A Demon Lord who got fired!?
Since the demon race was born, several epochs ago—
Such a pathetic Demon Lord—probably the first in history!

title: Chapter 47 — Vote for More Updates
content:
Chapter 47 — Vote for More Updates

Volume 12 · Chapter 47

The four sword saints looked at each other, feeling that this young new Demon Lord was truly a disgrace beyond words.

To actually be fired by the demon race's council—it was truly unbelievable.

"So, you're the new monarch of the First Demon Lord Palace. Then where has Lucifer the Second gone?!" the Wind Sword Saint asked in astonishment.

The others seemed to care about this question as well, and they all looked toward Merlin—after all, this involved a grudge from a hundred years ago.

The reason the four Elemental Sword Saints had come out of seclusion was not only to repay the old favor of thrashing the Orfray family, but also to wipe away their previous shame at the Death Swamp!

"My mom seems to already be dead," Merlin said faintly. From his tone, one could not sense any joy or anger at all.

"Who?! Lucifer the Second was an extremely rare peerless powerhouse. Just who defeated her?!" The Earth Sword Saint's face was full of disbelief.

"The home of the legendary Spear Hero," Merlin recalled briefly and said.

"What?! It was actually that running dog of the Holy Church, the man known as the closest to god!" The Wind Sword Saint's expression changed greatly, apparently also knowing about the Spear Hero.

"No, how could Lucifer the Second possibly be killed? Even if the Spear Hero was stronger, it would not have been so easy to accomplish!" The Water Sword Saint seemed to have a different conjecture.

"Oh? Why?" Merlin narrowed his eyes, recalling that his mom seemed to have been easily defeated. Could there be something he did not know?

"Because both of them are powerhouses who transcend Saint-tier! If they fought, then wanting to put each other to death would have come at an extremely painful price!" The Water Sword Saint answered with firm conviction.

Merlin became puzzled. He had always thought his mom was a Saint-tier powerhouse, and had never felt that she had already stepped beyond Saint-tier.

But as for the Spear Hero, Merlin could very clearly sense that power, far beyond the scope of Saint-tier. Could it be that his mom had always been hiding and suppressing her own strength?!

This was not such a strange thing either. The former Merlin had been a genuine weakling, relatively immature and numb when it came to sensing power, relying mostly on guesses. Perhaps he had never clearly understood where his mother's power truly stood.

"Beyond Saint-tier?" Although Merlin knew one could cross that threshold, he did not understand it at all.

"What? Your strength is not weak, yet you completely do not know the meaning of transcending Saint-tier?" The Water Sword Saint smiled disdainfully and said with profound meaning, "That is a realm only the geniuses among geniuses can reach. It is widely circulated among true powerhouses, a strength stage called the Ancestor Realm. It is said that after reaching the Ancestor Realm, one's strength undergoes a perfect transformation, allowing one to draw upon the natural power between heaven and earth."

"???" Merlin frowned tightly, thinking, Ancestor Realm? Is that what transcending Saint-tier is called? This was the first time he had heard of it.

Still, Merlin had not come away completely empty-handed. At first, he had already suspected that his mom was not dead, but had used some method to escape.

Today, after hearing the words of the four Elemental Sword Saints, Merlin became even more certain of his own thinking. His mom was not dead at all, but was using the false appearance of death to deceive someone.

Just what was it that made his mom choose this method to disappear from the public eye?

Could it be that within the demon race, there was some extremely threatening existence? One that forced his mom to do this?

Merlin's face was full of suspicious clouds. For a moment, many possibilities surged into his mind, but none received a convincing answer.

"Lucifer the Second and the Spear Hero are both super powerhouses above Saint-tier. How could they possibly die so simply, as you say? You are clearly deceiving us." The Water Sword Saint's eyes turned cold.

The momentum of the other sword saints also became sharp. Toward Merlin's repeated "lies," they clearly no longer had much patience.

"Regarding my mom, I actually do not know much either," Merlin said innocently, spreading his hands.

"Forget it. Whether you know or not does not matter. Since Lucifer the Second has gone missing, finding her son is the same. The mother's debt is paid by the son!" the Water Sword Saint said maliciously.

"What do you mean?" Merlin raised his chin, thinking that these four seemed to have an indelible hatred toward his mom.

"Lucifer the Second inflicted upon us damage that can never be erased. We will absolutely not let that woman go—"

As soon as the words fell, the four Elemental Sword Saints threw open the black robes on their bodies, revealing the **upper bodies they had been hiding all along.

Merlin's expression changed slightly. He was somewhat shocked by the bodies of the four sword saints. He had not expected to see such a shocking sight.

The bodies of the four Elemental Sword Saints were covered in crimson-red scars, like one ravine after another, interwoven across their bodies. They no longer looked like human flesh at all.

"This is the humiliation your mother inflicted on us. It can never be erased!" the Water Sword Saint roared.

"Take a good look at our burned bodies. Can you comprehend our resentment?!" the Earth Sword Saint demanded.

"These scars often wake us in the middle of the night. They have become our nightmares. The marks of humiliation are like our hatred for Lucifer the Second—we cannot forget them!" The scars on the Wind Sword Saint's body throbbed faintly.

"Since you are Lucifer the Second's son, then repay the debt for her!" The Fire Sword Saint pointed at Merlin opposite him and said angrily, "Revenge against Lucifer the Second is our long-cherished wish. I never expected to meet the new Pride Monarch here. This is fate!"

Merlin looked at the four sword saints opposite him and did not speak.

Looking at their shocking scars, it was clear how badly they had been bullied by his mom. That had not been a fair battle, but pure torture.

Merlin slightly understood the fanaticism in these fellows' eyes. It was undisguised hatred, and it had already burned onto him.

"Since you are the new monarch, then killing you will also count as us defeating the Great Demon Lord of the First Palace. We will not let such a rare opportunity slip by!" The Water Sword Saint's tone did not hesitate in the slightest.

"Aren't you few Saint-tier? My mom transcended Saint-tier. With such an obvious gap, you do not think you have a chance of beating my mom, do you?" Merlin frowned.

"We are already different from before. When we entered the unknown chaotic sea region and encountered the true ruler of the world, we learned just how insignificant this world really is." An expression of reverence unconsciously appeared on the Water Sword Saint's face. "From that moment on, we brothers underwent a complete transformation and rebirth. That was the grace bestowed upon us by the great Ruler of Chaos!"

"Ruler of Chaos? What the hell is that?" Merlin found it hard to understand.

"Shut up! Do not show disrespect to our master!" the Fire Sword Saint roared.

"The Ruler of Chaos is the strongest existence in the unknown sea region, the absolute ruler at the top of the food chain." The Water Sword Saint's expression was cold and stern as he said seriously, "As long as we can submit to it, we can obtain transcendent power!"

"Look at our rapidly advancing strength. All of this was given to us by the Ruler of Chaos."

"As long as we join forces, even your mother Lucifer the Second would be someone we could fight."

"As for you, the Demon Lord—"

"We want to crush you as easily as pinching an ant to death!"
