title: Chapter 48 — Moon Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 48 — Moon Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 12 · Chapter 48

“Hahaha” Merlin chuckled lightly, looking at the few people opposite whose heads had been blown away by the wind, “Interesting. So it turns out you’re just dogs under a king’s command?”

“No, this is the Wind Saint correcting Merlin’s words about the reasonable surrender to great power. ‘With our age, we’ve already reached the limit of human life, and still living here—haven’t you sensed any strangeness?”

“Oh?”

Merlin raised an eyebrow, thinking the normal human lifespan limit is—two hundred years. This is still a lifespan increase that only Saint-tier powerhouses would experience.

Ordinary humans who can live to a hundred are few and far between. If not for some secret arts, like Gregory, it would probably be difficult to prolong life.

So the four Elemental Sword Saints living until now is indeed very abnormal.”

“Since you’re the son of a Demon Lord, then let us show—the gift bestowed upon us by the Great King of Chaos!!”

As soon as the voice fell, a thick stream of black gushed out from the four of them, surging into the sky!

This jet-black stream, mixed with tiny crystals under the purple starlight, surrounded an area of a hundred meters.

The distant allied forces were hard-pressed to retreat, and the soldiers fell into panic, some at a loss.

Even the thorn knights on the observation tower in the imperial capital were astonished by this spectacular sight.

“What is this?! Why did a black storm appear out of nowhere!” Morrison shouted.

“I don’t know, but this feels very weird!” Mesfield widened his eyes.

“This power is unprecedented—where on earth does it come from!” Seth could also not suppress the shock in his heart.

The thorn knights were too far away to feel that strange power physically.

But Merlin, at the center of the storm, could sense all kinds of incongruities.

Because the oppressive aura radiating from the four Sword Saints opposite had completely changed, as if they were a different person!

It’s not that Merlin has seen little, but this oppressive aura makes him feel + unfamiliar.

Although this world has many races, oppressive auras have always been somewhat similar. But now the oppressive aura on the four Sword Saints is very strange, as if— a void, impossible to fathom.

This sense of incongruity, Merlin has only felt from creatures from Hell, but these few living people in front of him can feel power from another world!

“Ahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh!”

The four Sword Saints screamed in the storm. Merlin watched as, at the chests of the few people opposite, a human face vaguely appeared?

This strange face gradually became clear, turning a purple-black color.

The pulsating blood vessels around it continuously converged blood toward the face on the chest.

The畸形 face’s crimson eyes lit up, and suddenly opened its mouth, emitting a distorted moan.

“Oh—wailing”

0. SF novel

Merlin’s brow tightened, and his heart felt a slight shock. What the hell is this?! What are these guys keeping in their bodies!!

The storm dispersed, and the four Sword Saints completed a series of changes, appearing in a new posture.

Their chests had strange faces growing on them, the skin faintly turning purple, and the faces had been eroded half away, looking terrifying.

Merlin narrowed his eyes, feeling the unknown oppressive aura, and murmured, “What on earth is this monster-like body—”

“Monster? No!” The Sword Saint of Wind opened his arms, speaking with immense pride, “This is evolution!!!!”

“Right, it’s species evolution! And we merely received the favor of the King of Chaos, getting the opportunity for great evolution!” The Sword Saint of Earth grinned.

“Ha, just to gain power, to become a slave of a king? Why do you say it with such pride?” Merlin’s expression was full of contempt.

“You simply don’t understand anything. Evolution is the great trend of this world, irreversible. Regardless of which era, evolution is to better adapt to survival, and it is honorable!” The Sword Saint of Water paused, meaningfully saying, “The world has myriad races, yet the Chaos race is not listed, because they are a brand-new race that appeared under the influence of energy from another realm. They don’t need to cultivate martial arts or magic; they are born with immensely powerful talents. Relying solely on instinct to fight can place them at the apex of the world. If not for the turbulence beneath the unknown sea blocking it, I think the human era would have ended long ago, welcoming a new Chaos era!”

“There’s no need to explain so much to this little ghost; he simply wouldn’t understand the Great King of Chaos’s strength.” The Wind Sword Saint sneered.

“That’s right. A species that, just by looking once, makes one feel a sense of submission—ordinary people are indeed difficult to understand.” The Water Sword Saint nodded.

“Although I don’t know what you encountered in the Chaotic Sea at your position, do you think you can win me with your current power?” Merlin shrugged casually, speaking lightly, “To be honest, besides your appearance becoming incredibly ugly, I don’t feel any threat, though the oppressive aura has changed quite a bit, the strength seems about the same as before.”

“Is that so? Really laughable. I hope you’ll still have such confidence later!” The Sword Saint of Water smiled with deep meaning, “Brothers, let us demonstrate our true power, to properly educate the son of Lucifer II.”

“Tch!” Merlin suddenly felt displeased, disliking the word “education.”

The four Sword Saints placed their differently colored gemstones together and chanted a few incantations. The black gale storm suddenly swept up again.

The storm’s power was a hundred times more violent than before, truly incomparable, making it somewhat difficult to even open one’s eyes!

This is the Elemental Four Sword Saints, utilizing the power of the King of Chaos, casting their own Saint-tier Secret Techniques!

Although their Secret Techniques are simple, their destructive power is not to be underestimated. They perfectly fused the power of the four people, thereby causing their battle power to rise linearly.

The originally Saint-tier Secret Technique had vaguely attained the pressure of the Boundary realm, reaching a new peak—Boundary realm Secret Technique!

Merlin slightly raised his spirits, unable to help but warn himself, thinking this is the pressure of the Boundary realm? Four combined together can reach this realm. They want to use this to oppose my mother’s ultimate move now?

The Elemental Four Sword Saints defeating the lake fairy isn’t blowing smoke; they truly have this strength. They have always been aiming at the Demon Lord Monarch level if they’ve worked hard. If they didn’t have some confidence, how could they spout such words?

Far away on the observation tower.

“What is this pressure situation?! Why is it so terrifying!” Seth could no longer maintain his composure, looking alarmed.

“Is this a joke?! Human oppressive aura can actually be so strong, seeming to have completely transcended the Saint-tier realm. What on earth did it!” Morrison couldn’t believe the scene in the distance.

“It’s over, everything is over. I didn’t expect the Overfrey Count to have actually brought— Mesfield, who had no color in his face, slowly closed his eyes, his body trembling even more violently—

This despairing oppressive aura?

Right, it’s the legendary Boundary realm.

It seems the war is over, no matter how one resists, it’s impossible to win.

The power of the Boundary realm is impossible to defeat—even Elgar, the Great Sword Saint

title: Chapter 49 — Neat
content:
Chapter 49 — Neat

Volume 12 · Chapter 49

Mestfield wasn’t very familiar with the Transcendent Realm either—she had only heard about it from the elders of her family, who described it as a legendary boundary.

Among ordinary people, those with the talent for cultivation were already a rare few.

After extremely arduous training, those who could break past the Saint-tier were even rarer, to the point of being one in ten thousand.

For many, reaching the Saint-tier was already a dazzling peak—transcending it to ascend to the Transcendent Realm was something ordinary people didn’t even dare to dream of.

Mestfield felt a deep sense of foreboding. If things continued like this, no matter what defenses the Imperial Capital employed, they would be useless.

She recalled the words of her family’s elders: if facing a Transcendent Realm powerhouse, even ten Saint-tier warriors attacking together would be of no use. The sheer power gap was absolute!

Still, Mestfield clung to a sliver of hope for Archswordmaster Elgin, praying for a miracle.

If the outcome disappointed her, she would not hesitate to flee with Elizabeth.

The bird-shaped clouds in the sky twisted, as if pulled by some mysterious force, gradually forming a vortex.

The wind and rain intensified, converging upon the four Sword Saints, as if brewing a new technique.

Though the four Sword Saints had not truly reached the Transcendent Realm, by combining their power, they had barely stepped into its tier.

The sheer oppressive might of their technique alone already carried the force of the Transcendent Realm.

To defeat Lucifer II, the Four Elemental Sword Saints had honed this move for a century—and now, with its very first use, it triggered a slight anomaly in the heavens and earth.

Merlin narrowed his eyes, gripping the hilt of his katana tightly, raising the tip high as he prepared to strike.

A sudden clap of thunder echoed across the sky—then, with a burst of momentum, the strike was unleashed!

The four Sword Saints simultaneously left their positions, scattering in four directions, subtly forming a surrounding formation!

Dark purple mist swirled around them as they streaked across the sky like shooting stars.

Merlin’s gaze flickered, his vigilance sharp as he observed the four Sword Saints positioned in the four cardinal directions.

This was clearly a formation meant to annihilate him here—he could watch two, but he couldn’t defend against an attack from behind!

The four Sword Saints arced through the air, shifting their focus in unison toward the center—then struck with all their might!

From afar, the four Sword Saints looked like four black meteors, converging from the east, west, north, and south!

Their combined attack merged in an instant. Merlin’s pupils contracted sharply!

A flash of dark purple light passed—then came an explosion so terrifying it seemed otherworldly. A deafening thunderclap erupted, temporarily robbing everyone present of their hearing—

A towering mushroom cloud of dark purple shot into the sky, reaching hundreds of feet high.

The shockwave tore through the thick layer of storm clouds, ripping open a circular gap.

The earth trembled violently, spiderweb-like cracks spreading in a horrifying display.

The distant allied army was caught in the blast—nearly half perished within its range. The once-orderly ranks were thrown into chaos, men and horses collapsing in an instant.

Had the core battlefield been closer to the Imperial Capital, even Elizabeth in the royal palace might not have escaped. As it was, the capital’s gates and defensive walls were reduced to rubble in moments.

The terrifying power of the Four Elemental Sword Saints left everyone in awe. Lightning flickered within the mushroom cloud, and the very heavens seemed to darken in response.

“It’s over with that strike.”

Seth’s expression was filled with terror. Witnessing such horrifying power firsthand left him with no will to resist.

He felt the four Sword Saints’ strength was beyond comprehension—it seemed to have already surpassed the Saint-tier, reaching a height ordinary people could never hope to attain.

Facing such power, Seth felt that even if he donned his demonic armor and fought with all his might, he would still die a miserable death.

“No way… Archswordmaster Elgin actually lost?! Killed in an instant by a counterattack?!” Morrison could hardly believe his eyes. It was as if he were dreaming.

All this time, Morrison had considered Archswordmaster Elgin’s strength undeniable. But now, sensing that power beyond the Saint-tier, his faith wavered—he felt that no one could survive at the center of such an impact.

“Just as I expected. Archswordmaster Elgin was powerless to change his fate. Facing the power of the Transcendent Realm, he has already fallen.”

Mestfield muttered to herself, her face pale. She had long foreseen this outcome.

This result was exactly as the elders of her family had described—the Transcendent Realm was entirely different from the Saint-tier, belonging to a completely different level.

Mestfield fell into deep thought. Archswordmaster Elgin was likely dead in the explosion. She needed to consider her next move.

Witnessing the desperate eruption of Transcendent Realm power, she had no thought of resistance. Even if all the Thorn Knights attacked together, they would still be crushed.

She didn’t ponder for long before deciding to ignore Elizabeth’s wishes and take her far away from the dangerous Imperial Capital.

“Morrison, Seth—it’s clear Archswordmaster Elgin has failed. We need to respond!”

“What are you planning to do?” Seth turned back, his eyes unconsciously betraying his panic.

“No matter what, we need to retreat for now. Take His Majesty with us!” Mestfield said gravely.

Seth licked his dry lips and nodded heavily. “Alright, let’s retreat.”

Just as Mestfield and Seth were about to act, Morrison—who had been watching intently—suddenly spoke up.

Morrison refused to give up hope. He still clung to the desperate chance that Archswordmaster Elgin might emerge victorious.

As the wind and rain dispersed the black mist, a figure could faintly be seen standing at the center of the battlefield.

Morrison’s heart leapt when he saw only one person still standing. He cried out in excitement:

“Look! Look over there! It’s not over yet!”

“What?”

Mestfield and Seth, hearing Morrison’s shout, both turned to gaze at the devastated center of the battlefield.

The thick mist gradually cleared, revealing the man standing at the heart of the impact—none other than Merlin.

Merlin’s sword had been drawn at some point, and he looked relatively unharmed, though his black robe was tattered, torn apart by the earlier explosion and chaotic currents, making him look like a bedraggled beggar.

Though the final burst of Transcendent Realm power from the four Sword Saints had been immense, Merlin felt it was nothing special—just a little more troublesome than a Saint-tier opponent.

For a brief moment, Merlin was reminded of the Gun Hero, but the threat level of their power was far, far weaker.

He turned to look at the ground, where the four Sword Saints lay dead, their faces frozen in expressions of disbelief.

Perhaps only in death did the Four Elemental Sword Saints realize they had severely underestimated this young Demon Lord. His absurd power far surpassed even his mother’s.

Merlin let out a long breath, returning his katana to its sheath. He muttered indifferently:

“This isn’t bad, either.”

“Family should stick together, nice and neat.”

title: Chapter 50 — Broken Spear
content:
Chapter 50 — Broken Spear

Volume 12 · Chapter 50

On the lookout tower, the three Thorn Knights were all stunned.

Looking at the only figure still standing at the center of the distant battlefield, they simply couldn’t calm down.

The storm unleashed by the Elemental Four Sword Saints just now felt like a dream—it didn’t seem real at all.

Yet, at the final moment, the combined power the Four Sword Saints had erupted with had reached the transcendent realm beyond Saint-tier!

This legendary realm was something most people could never hope to attain. Many assumed Saint-tier was already the peak.

Feeling the overwhelming pressure, the Thorn Knights were utterly terrified, convinced that Elgin the Great Swordsman would be crushed to death under such force.

But then, inexplicably, the tide turned. The ferocious Four Sword Saints were defeated and fell, leaving everyone bewildered.

Just look at the horror frozen on their faces as they lay dying—who knew what terrifying ordeal those four had endured before their deaths?

The three Thorn Knights stood frozen in the wind and rain, taking a long while to finally come back to their senses.

“Wha—?” Morrison couldn’t believe his eyes. He pinched his own cheek hard, and the sharp pain made him grin. “Good heavens! He actually won?! To defeat that kind of overwhelming power… it’s incredible! As expected of Elgin the Great Swordsman! I knew this man couldn’t lose!”

Yeah…

Seth snapped out of his daze, swallowing hard in shock. *Is this real?* He thought. *They actually won?* After the enemies combined their strength, they should have reached a level beyond Saint-tier, right?

To win so effortlessly… Elgin the Great Swordsman’s power must have already transcended the Saint-tier by a mile. It was on a completely different level.

Indeed, no matter how hard he tried to break through, Seth realized he might never reach Elgin’s level—not even close. Just touching the man’s heels would be an impossible struggle.

Seth lowered his head, clenching his fists until his knuckles turned white. Though his face was filled with unwillingness, recalling his past challenge to Elgin made him feel utterly foolish.

Only now did Seth realize how ridiculous he had been—like a clown, prancing around before a true powerhouse. Elgin had clearly been toying with him, treating him like an insignificant ant.

Melfield stood beside them, silent, but his mind was a storm of chaos, unable to settle for a long time.

*This has to be a joke…*

Those were warriors who had reached the transcendent realm!

How could they have been taken down so easily?!

Damn it! How did Elgin the Great Swordsman do it?!

This was nothing like what his family elders had told him. Weren’t transcendent realm warriors supposed to be nearly invincible?

Just where was the limit to Elgin’s power? Could it be that there *was* no limit?

Melfield’s face paled. He was stunned speechless by Elgin’s strength. He hadn’t expected to have underestimated the man *again*.

Now, Melfield was deeply suspicious of Elgin’s true identity. With such overwhelming power, there was no way there wouldn’t be *any* information about him.

After the brutal battle, the battlefield was left in ruins.

The sky was a churning mass of dark clouds, torn open in one spot, forming a bizarre patch of clear sky.

The allied army on the opposite side, caught in the crossfire, was in disarray, unable to reorganize an effective offensive.

Moreover, many soldiers had been terrified by the power of the Elemental Four Sword Saints—just the shockwave alone had sent countless men to their deaths.

This was the first time since the rebel army’s uprising that they had suffered such a devastating blow—and it had come from their *own* allies.

Merlin turned to look at the four Sword Saints’ corpses lying behind him. His thick brows furrowed slightly. Something felt… off.

Logically, killing the Elemental Four Sword Saints with the demon sword *Banri Garan* should have brought a soothing sensation to his cursed heart.

Every time he personally slew a Saint-tier warrior, his heart—plagued by the curse—would be nourished, delaying its next flare-up.

Yet, strangely, this time, his heart had *no* reaction at all. The only time this had happened before was with the undead.

Merlin stared at the four corpses, a puzzled expression creeping across his face. They had been alive and kicking just moments ago—this lack of reaction made no sense.

But then he recalled how the Elemental Four Sword Saints had activated a power that didn’t belong to them—that grotesque human face on their chests. Maybe there was something unnatural about their bodies to begin with.

So Merlin walked over, intending to examine the enemies’ corpses closely to see if there was anything unusual.

By now, the purple-black skin covering the Four Sword Saints had already receded, returning to their normal complexion. The grotesque human faces on their chests, too, seemed to have lost their vitality, withering away—except for the Water Sword Saint’s corpse, where the face still looked relatively fresh, not as shrunken as the others.

Merlin approached and crouched beside the Water Sword Saint’s body, staring intently at the bizarre face.

It looked completely out of place, its features utterly unfamiliar—nothing like the Sword Saint’s own. It was as if it had been *parasitizing* them.

Just as Merlin stroked his chin, lost in thought, the withering face on the Water Sword Saint’s chest suddenly *twitched*. Its crimson eyes snapped open, the pupils rolling wildly as it scanned its surroundings.

“Hm?” Merlin was taken aback. He hadn’t expected *this* thing to still be able to open its eyes. Did that mean it had its own consciousness?

The grotesque face locked onto Merlin, its mouth splitting open to reveal rows of hideous, saw-like teeth. With a shriek, it *lunged* forward.

“UOOOOOORGH!”

The face’s body tore free from the Water Sword Saint’s corpse, blood spraying everywhere. It was clearly a monstrous, purple-black centipede-like creature with a human face on its head!

The horrifying sight was reminiscent of a giant, sentient centipede.

The face-centipede bared its fangs and lunged at Merlin, as if searching for a new host—otherwise, it wouldn’t survive.

“Tch.”

Merlin’s brows shot up. In the nick of time, he struck out with a single punch!

The explosive force slammed the creature into the ground, reducing it to a bloody pulp under his fist.

The face-centipede let out a few pitiful wails before falling still, dead.

Merlin’s brows knitted together, still shaken. He couldn’t help but mutter, “What the hell *was* that?”

Merlin forced himself to calm down, recalling what the Elemental Four Sword Saints had said earlier. Had he discovered something?

So the “great blessing of the King of Chaos” was *this* disgusting thing?

What kind of blessing was this?! It was clearly a means of *control*, turning them into pawns for someone else’s use!

Thinking about it, these men should have been long dead—their lifespans had far exceeded human limits.

Could it be that those grotesque faces had forcibly extended their lives, which was why his curse had no effect on them?

Merlin considered the possibility. Otherwise, this was just too abnormal.

If these four were nothing more than pawns… then who was the real mastermind pulling the strings?

Merlin lifted his gaze, looking into the distance, a flicker of suspicion rising in his mind.

*The true enemy is someone else…*

---

A luxurious armored carriage rolled slowly along the road, pressing toward the royal capital with unstoppable momentum.

Duke Overray had already entered imperial territory. Soon, he would reach the gates of the royal city.

At this moment, Duke Overray lounged leisurely on a sofa, one hand holding a wine glass, savoring an expensive red wine with great satisfaction.

The arm that Merlin had severed from him still hadn’t been treated. He planned to get a prosthetic after winning this war.

Becoming the first one-armed king in the empire’s history… didn’t sound like such a bad thing.

Duke Overray sipped his wine, his gaze drifting to the window of the carriage. Outside, the rain poured endlessly, showing no sign of stopping.

But the foul weather didn’t bother Overray in the slightest. In his estimation, the war should already be over.

With the power of the Elemental Four Sword Saints, they should have long since slaughtered the kingdom’s resisting forces, along with those few overconfident Thorn Knights, and stormed the royal capital, capturing the queen to await his arrival.

Duke Overray felt he had nothing left to do. All he needed was to meet up with the main army, take control of the empire, and his future would be nothing short of *brilliant*.

“Disaster! Your Grace! It’s terrible!” Advisor Gabriel stumbled into the carriage, his face a mask of panic. He rushed all the way to Duke Overray before dropping to his knees.

“Tch!” Duke Overray was startled, nearly dropping the wine glass in his hand. “What are you doing?! Can’t you speak calmly? What’s with all this frantic rushing?!”

Gabriel swallowed hard, then said seriously, “Your Grace! The front lines—there’s been a catastrophe!”

“Hah! With the Elemental Four Sword Saints holding the line, what kind of catastrophe could there be? The plan to overthrow the empire is as solid as it gets.” Duke Overray was already basking in the joy of victory. “When you say ‘catastrophe,’ you don’t mean our iron cavalry has already flooded the royal capital, do you?”

Overray couldn’t fathom any possible setback in this war. The Elemental Four Sword Saints were so powerful that the mere presence of a few Thorn Knights wouldn’t be enough to defend the capital. The odds were practically zero.

“No, Your Grace! It’s *worse* than that!” Gabriel paused, then spoke in a grave tone, hoping to pull Overray back to reality. “The Elemental Four Sword Saints… are dead.”

Duke Overray didn’t speak. Instead, his eyes widened in shock, nearly stupid with fear.

The wine glass slipped from his hand, shattering on the floor—a testament to how shaken he was by the news.

Duke Overray stood up, grabbed Gabriel by the collar, and yanked him off the ground.

“What did you say?! This is no time for jokes! How could they lose with such overwhelming power?! Unless they were all *idiots*!”

“Your Grace, I’m not joking!” Gabriel pointed outside, continuing, “A messenger just came from the front lines in a panic—the Elemental Four Sword Saints were all killed by a mysterious man!”

“WHAT?!” Duke Overray’s mature, composed face turned ashen in an instant. His eyes widened in terror, and he collapsed onto the floor.

“H-How is this possible?!”

“With the Elemental Four Sword Saints dead… we’re doomed!”

“This was supposed to be a war even a *fool* could win! Why… why did it all fall apart in *my* hands?!”

title: Chapter 51 — Chaos
content:
Chapter 51 — Chaos

Volume 12 · Chapter 51

Gabri stared at Duke Aufle's reaction, which was on the verge of falling apart, and didn't know what to say, so he could only stand there stiffly.

"Who did it? Who did it?! Could the lake fairies of the royal family have been used again?!" Duke Aufle grabbed onto Gabri's clothes and wouldn't let go, his eyes wild with bloodshot veins.

"No, according to the scout's report, they deduced that the opponent was the great swordsman Elkin, Gabri stammered."

"How could that be?! The grudge between the great swordsman Elkin and the royal family—how could it be resolved so easily?!" Duke Aufle said in disbelief.

"The front lines can't confirm it either, it's just speculation, but the Four Sword Saints really were killed by the opponent." Gabri was sweating coldly on his forehead.

Duke Aufle's expression grew blank, his hopes dashed by the current situation, and he gradually reverted to an extremely aged appearance, with not a trace of vitality left.

The death of the Four Sword Saints hit Duke Aufle hard, devastatingly so. He felt it was now impossible to win this war, the tide already turning against them.

Duke Aufle sat down listlessly, as if he had lost his soul, tilting his head and saying nothing.

Seeing the duke in this state, Gabri tentatively asked, "Your Grace, what should we do now?"

"What else can we do? Surrender," Duke Aufle said with heavy sighs.

"Huh?!" Gabri's eyes widened in disbelief, "No, that can't be right! If we surrender now, we won't have a good outcome. We should resist to the end, that's our only chance of survival!"

"Are you blind?! Haven't you seen that the Four Sword Saints are already dead? What do you have left to resist with?!" Duke Aufle was so angry he slammed the table, feeling as though Gabri was trying to kill him, "It would be better to surrender early. Perhaps we can still beg Elizabeth for mercy and secure a peaceful old age."

"Your Grace, please come to your senses. How could Elizabeth possibly spare you? In any era, those who fail in rebellion never meet a good end. Rather than kneeling down to beg for forgiveness, it's better to fight to the death!" Gabri said, unwilling to give up, believing that the grand cause of overthrowing the empire was already more than half complete. To give up now would be too irrational.

"It's not necessarily so. As long as I surrender my rights and choose to become an ordinary person, perhaps I can survive," Duke Aufle, devoid of fighting spirit, his mind filled with how to keep himself alive.

"Your only son was killed because of your relationship with them. Don't you want revenge?!" Gabri couldn't understand and pressed on.

"I do want to, but now I no longer have the ability to take revenge. How can I fight back?!" Duke Aufle sighed deeply and resignedly said, "Fine then, let's just surrender. Rather than being cut down by the kingdom's army like a worthless dog, I'd prefer a more dignified death."

"Don't give up so easily! We've worked so hard to get to this point!" Gabri paused, speaking mysteriously, "Perhaps there's still a chance for a turnaround. If we keep pressing the attack, if we surrender now, it's all over!"

"A turnaround? What kind of turnaround? Without the Four Sword Saints' help, we have no chance at all! Moreover, the opponent has the great swordsman Elkin on their side, someone who can kill the Four Sword Saints. Who knows how terrifying his strength has become?" A wave of fear surged through Duke Aufle's heart. The royal family suddenly summoned the great swordsman Elkin, and this sudden power caught him off guard.

"Your Grace, please believe in me. Do not issue the retreat order," Gabri said with profound meaning.

"Enough, Gabri. I know you're saying this for my own good, but our situation is already hopeless. Surrender is the best choice," Duke Aufle waved his hand, exhausted in both body and spirit, "You may retire. I want to be alone for a while."

Gabri's face fell, his body stiffened, and he clenched his fists silently, clearly displeased with Duke Aufle's decision.

He glared at him with hatred, his face pale with anger, his breathing growing heavier, as if a volcano were about to erupt at any moment!

Gabri now thought Duke Aufle was being stubborn, which was not a good omen. If they surrendered, all their efforts would be in vain.

"What are you still doing here? I told you to retire!" Duke Aufle, annoyed, snapped, his temples throbbing.

"Fine then. Since you, this old fool, want to surrender, you're useless now. This mess is all yours to handle. As for you, this old corpse, since you have no family left, just obediently go to hell," Gabri's mouth curled into a sneer, his attitude suddenly turning arrogant.

"What nonsense are you spouting, Gabri?!" Duke Aufle was completely shocked, having never seen Gabri's attitude so vicious before.

OP SFE this novel

"You don't seriously think I'm actually serving you, do you? To be honest, you're just a chess piece. I serve the great King of Chaos!"

As soon as the words left his mouth, Gabri's body suddenly swelled, his clothes tearing apart, and his entire form transformed beyond human limits!

Originally short and small, his body suddenly grew to over two meters tall, his skin turning dark brown, like old tree bark pasted onto his body.

His legs were bent, his feet large with hard claws, seemingly very skilled at jumping.

His hands turned into beast-like claws, his head resembled a cockroach, with long antennae waving wildly.

Clearly, Gabri was never an X-class. What method had been used to hide within human skin?

Duke Aufle was terrified, his eyes bulging, his lips trembling, unable to utter a single word!

"How dare a mere human give me orders? If you weren't the stepping stone for our Chaos clan to subdue the outside world, you'd already be dead!" Gabri's voice became a deep double tone, impossible to distinguish male from female.

"What kind of monster are you?!" Duke Aufle was horrified, retreating step by step, already terrified.

"Monster? Haha, I am one of the Three Heroes under the Chaos King's throne—Black Blade Lahman, belonging to the Chaos clan, one of the highest-ranking groups in this world. You, a humble human, should be kneeling down and offering your body to be flogged in submission."

Lahman, transformed from Gabri, pointed at Duke Aufle, his tone extremely disdainful, his forehead bearing six red eyes that looked quite terrifying.

"Gabri, you're not Gabri. Where is he?!" Duke Aufle's mind was on the verge of collapse.

"Given how long I've been by your side, I'll let you in on the truth. Our Chaos clan lives in the unknown seas, which are extremely barren and unsuitable for survival. In order to continue our great clan, we must expand outward. Britannia's fertile territory is what we plan to conquer, and you are the puppet we have our eyes on—using your hands to take over this land, providing convenience for our clan." Lahman paused, speaking with deep meaning, "If it weren't for our clan's plans, how could I have helped this lowly human? Making your family incredibly powerful, capable of contending with the royal family? All of this is for the continuation of our clan."

"What?!" Duke Aufle broke into a cold sweat, realizing he had been manipulated all along—expanding the army, strengthening the family, launching a rebellion, all within someone else's plan! He was just a puppet being manipulated at will!

"Enough. You're useless if you won't obey. Off with your head, Your Grace." Lahman raised his hand.

"No! Ahhhhh!" Duke Aufle crouched in the corner.

Lahman swung his hand, and with his claws, he severed Duke Aufle's head, ending his life.

Thud, thud, thud, Duke Aufle's head fell to the ground, his body collapsing lifelessly, blood flowing profusely, staining the carpet red.

Lahman flexed his fingers a few times, his arm muscles slowly rippling—

"The Four Sword Saints were truly useless. This kind of strength is worthy of serving the great King of Chaos? Dream on!"

"In the end, it still needed me, the real one, to come out."

title: Chapter 52 — Ignore
content:
Chapter 52 — Ignore

Volume 12 · Chapter 52

The tower of the Imperial Capital.

With the death of the Four Holy Swords upon which the allied forces relied, the soldiers suddenly lost their backbone, and many were left in a state of confusion.

On the ground, there were still some survivors who had been caught in the crossfire, wailing and calling for help.

Their intuition told them that as long as that masked man didn't die, this war could never be won.

Moreover, after the death of the Four Holy Swords, there was no movement from Duke Overre in the rear, so the soldiers could only stand by and wait, some caught in an awkward position of not knowing how to advance or retreat.

"What should we do now? It seems the enemy has lost their fighting spirit." Morrison asked in confusion, wanting to know what the others thought.

"Now is the perfect time. We should break out and catch them off guard." Seth immediately got into high spirits, thinking that now was the ideal opportunity to make a name for himself. He couldn't let Elkin the Great Swordsman have all the glory.

"No, being too aggressive will only trigger their resistance. And even though the Four Holy Swords are dead, the enemy still has the advantage in numbers. If we force a fight, our losses won't be small." Mespil disagreed with going all-out.

"So your meaning is..." Morrison tentatively asked.

"We should use a conciliatory policy. As long as they're willing to surrender and lay down their arms, we won't make things difficult for them." Mespil said seriously.

"Shouldn't we consult Her Majesty the Queen about this?" Morrison felt it wasn't right to make decisions on his own.

"No need. Does the Queen really enjoy watching you all fight to the death?" Mespil replied with confidence.

"This... well... not necessarily..." Morrison awkwardly answered.

"Just do as I say, there won't be any problems." Mespil said sternly.

Then the Thorn Knight commanded the royal army to march out of the city, planning to use both persuasion and force to completely resolve the remnants of the allied forces.

QFSF Light Novel

The center of the battlefield.

After the intense assault, this place had already become a wasteland.

Although Merlin felt something was a bit strange, as if there were hidden hands pulling the strings, simply examining the bodies of the Four Holy Swords didn't reveal much suspicious.

Just moments ago, wasn't it said that this chaotic tribe was hard to get out of the unknown seas?

How did they manage to get out? Could there be other members of the chaotic tribe...?

All these doubts made Merlin's head spin, with a persistent feeling of unease troubling him.

But Merlin wasn't one to dwell on things. Now that the biggest problem for Elizabeth had been solved, he should go collect his due and then return to Luxtherem.

Merlin turned his back and left, showing no interest in the mess before him, heading toward the royal palace.

But he hadn't gone far when the allied forces behind him began to stir up a commotion.

Fear, anxiety, and shock-filled shouts rose up one after another.

"That... what is that monster?!"

"What's going on! Why did they rush out from behind!"

"Is it a demon beast? A beastman? What exactly is that guy with a cockroach head?!"

Merlin stopped in his tracks and looked back in surprise, as a strange creature was approaching at an unimaginable speed, rushing toward him furiously!

An eerie humanoid figure, dark brown skin, sharp teeth and claws glinting with cold light, with a cockroach-like head on top, its feelers waving wildly around its mouth. This was the transformed Gaburi, known as one of the three great heads of the Chaos King's court—Kuroha Rahman.

"Huh?"

Merlin looked puzzled. He had never seen such a creature before. Even consulting all the demon race archives, there was no record of such an odd being.

In Merlin's own understanding, it was as if a bizarre creature straight out of Lovecraftian mythology had come to life—an existence that was hard for ordinary people to comprehend.

What's going on?

Is this an enemy?

Merlin was somewhat unsure, temporarily unable to determine this guy's identity.

Rahman's forehead had six red eyes, which briefly locked onto the disheveled Merlin who looked like a beggar.

But he didn't detect any hostility, nor any oppressive pressure. He was just like an ordinary person, so his interest quickly faded.

What the hell?

Just another cannon fodder passing by?

Braver than most, this vagrant who dared to wander around the center of the battlefield. Doesn't he fear death?

Where's the guy who defeated the Four Holy Swords? Has he already retreated to the royal palace?

Well, that's fine. Let me go meet that guy, and while I'm at it, I'll take care of Elizabeth, clearing the way for my tribe's future...

Ignoring Merlin, Rahman's gaze was fixed on the grand city gate ahead, and he suddenly quickened his pace, rushing into the city with a fierce cry!

"Wait..."

Merlin raised his hand and let out a single syllable.

But Rahman seemed not to notice Merlin, rushing past him at high speed without even looking back.

In Rahman's eyes, Merlin was probably just a tiny ant. Speaking another word would be a waste of life, let alone lowering himself to deal with a vagrant.

Merlin awkwardly said the last two words, his hand trembling slightly as he slowly lowered it.

A light breeze swept past, leaving him alone in the desolation, looking rather disheveled.

Merlin slowly turned his head to look behind him, his expression somewhat blank. A strand of black hair had slipped down to his forehead.

I...

Was I just ignored?

The royal army, under the command of the Thorn Knight, was preparing to disperse the allied forces outside the city.

The three Thorn Knights were directing them, fully prepared.

"The Queen truly picked the right person. It's no wonder it's Elkin the Great Swordsman—someone who can handle everything single-handedly. If only he were one of us Thorn Knights, how wonderful that would be?" Morrison, riding his horse, sighed and said, "Standing shoulder to shoulder with a strongman is always a special kind of enjoyment, Seth. Don't you think so?"

Next to him, Seth remained silent. Facing Elkin the Great Swordsman, he had completely lost all confidence. The opponent's strength was so desperate that it only made him feel powerless.

Seth felt that even if he could master the demon armor skillfully, he still couldn't fight against Elkin the Great Swordsman. It would be nothing but courting humiliation.

Mespil rolled his eyes and couldn't help but criticize Morrison, saying, "You should keep your mouth shut and stop saying such strange things. Right now, we're just in special times. What we need is Elkin the Great Swordsman's strength, not this guy with questionable values. Once the rebellion is over, who knows what attitude the Queen will take toward him!"

"I believe the Queen is a rational person and absolutely won't dismiss him lightly." Morrison said with unwavering confidence.

Mespil was annoyed in his heart, feeling that one of his teammates was a traitor. He was about to rebuke him when a series of screams echoed from the front of the formation.

"...Monsters!"

"There are monsters attacking!"

"No... no one is allowed to pass!"

The three Thorn Knights immediately went on high alert, only to see the front being attacked, with thick clouds of blood mist erupting repeatedly.

"What's going on? What happened!" Mespil broke into a cold sweat.

Suddenly, a dark figure like a dagger tore through the royal army's formation, with unstoppable momentum crushing the enemy and tearing countless soldiers into pieces, rivers of blood flowing.

Rahman arrived in front of the Thorn Knights, his nails stained with fresh blood. He slowly lifted his deformed head, all six eyes narrowing.

"Where is he?"

"Where is the man who defeated the Four Holy Swords?!"

"Come out! Let me see the man who defeated the Four Holy Swords..."

(v)9

title: Chapter 53 — Moon Vote Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 53 — Moon Vote Bonus Chapter

Volume 12 · Chapter 53

The three Bramble Knights were terrified by Rahmann's appearance, having never seen such a hideously bizarre visage in their lives.

Compared to Rahmann, the beastmen were almost impossibly beautiful — quite elegant by comparison.

They had likely never encountered the Chaos Clan before, completely unable to fathom that such grotesque races existed in this world.

"What… what is that…?" Morrison stared with wide eyes and muttered.

"Boldness! Who do you think you are?! Daring to trespass in the Royal City?!" Mesfield roared with fury. Although she had no idea who the intruder was, someone so recklessly slaughtering the kingdom's army was obviously no good.

Rahmann wasn't offended by Mesfield's ignorance — it was only natural.

The Chaos Clan was a race confined to living in the Unknown Seas. Long ago they had been human as well, but they had been invaded by an unknown power and transformed into an entirely new race.

Beneath the Unknown Seas lay turbulent currents powerful enough to tear everything apart, restricting the Chaos Clan's expansion beyond their domain. If it hadn't been for the discovery of a secret passage decades ago, it's unlikely anyone in this world would ever have laid eyes on them.

"The Royal City? From the moment I stepped foot here, this land belongs to my clan. You ants better kneel down quickly and obediently offer water and soil to the Great Chaos King!"

"What nonsense are you spouting? Who the hell do you think you are!" Mesfield's forehead veins throbbed. The meaning of "water and soil" was essentially all that the Empire possessed. If not for Rahmann's bizarre appearance, she would have assumed he was some kind of madman from nowhere.

Seth had been startled at first, but then realized he couldn't sense any pressure from the opponent at all. It was almost like Lord Elgin the Great Swordmaster — apart from the creepy exterior, he seemed like an utterly ordinary fellow, not particularly strong.

However, recalling how Rahmann had forcefully torn through the kingdom army's defense just now, Seth deduced the opponent's strength must be around the Saint-tier threshold — not yet at a terribly powerful level. With the current forces, they could probably overwhelm him through sheer numbers.

So Seth shouted loud orders to those soldiers who had been too scared to move.

"What are you all standing around for?! Move out! Bring down this foreign race together!"

The kingdom army soldiers glanced at one another, then immediately drew their swords and charged forward with war cries.

Blade flashes and sword glints interlaced, almost completely obscuring Rahmann's field of vision.

"Pathetic. What good does it do to throw more ants at me?"

Rahmann bared his jagged teeth, splayed his five fingers, and made his five claw-like fingernails vibrate.

His body moved, and with a casual wave of his hand he began reaping the soldiers' lives. As he slaughtered them, he let out a sinister, eerie cackle that made the flesh crawl.

Those ordinary-flesh nails were sharper than any blade. The armor the soldiers wore was like paper — a single grazing slash would pierce through and deal grievous wounds.

The expression on Seth's face gradually stiffened, cold sweat dripping down his forehead. What in the world was happening?

This guy clearly had no aura or pressure at all — how could his strength be so terrifying? Was he also at Lord Elgin the Great Swordmaster's level?

And how exactly did this guy get in? Why didn't Lord Elgin stop him?

Seth's heart churned with dread and uncertainty. He felt that the monster before him absolutely required him to step in personally to handle it.

"Damn it! Where did this guy come from? He's so damn hard to deal with!" Mesfield furrowed her elegant brows.

"Let me fight you!!!''

Just as Mesfield and Seth were about to make their move, someone else acted first.

Morrison let out a bellow and directly donned his gauntlets, charging straight at Rahmann. This wasn't a mistake — as soon as he engaged, he activated his secret art "Rakshasa," instantly driving himself into the second phase. His body radiated red, his battle aura was agitated and riled up like a provoked beast, and two ghostly horns began faintly forming on his head.

Morrison's speed was astonishing; in an instant he resembled a flash of red lightning as he punched Rahmann square in the face.

Both figures crashed together into the nearby city wall, the thunderous impacts echoing ceaselessly and kicking up clouds of dust.

It looked as though Rahmann had been critically wounded — as if the battle had ended.

"…We should have won, right?" Seth muttered to himself. Taking Morrison's punch head-on would surely have been agonizing — he should have at least been unable to keep going.

"I hope so…" Mesfield nodded, though unease gnawed at her insides. This opponent dared to march in alone — things probably wouldn't be this simple.

As the thick dust settled, the result was revealed —

Rahmann grabbed Morrison the same way one would lift a chick, dragging him out of the ruins. His body showed nothing more than superficial scratches.

"What!? Morrison has already been defeated!?" Seth's eyes bulged.

"What's going on!? That was way too easy! Why did Morrison lose his fighting capability as if he hadn't resisted at all!?" Mesfield exclaimed in shock. So this man really was extraordinary — far more difficult to handle than she had imagined!

Rahmann tossed the unconscious Morrison aside and paid him no further attention.

Morrison looked utterly drained, his body seemingly hollowed out, his condition extremely weak.

"You're still too green, charging up so foolishly. You can't sense my aura and assume I'm weak, can you?"

Mesfield and Seth said nothing. Their expressions grew grave — they were forced to take this seriously.

"Hahaha, just as I suspected. The most foolish thing about humans is dividing strength into rigid tiers and relying on aura to judge an opponent's power. They never understand the true essence of strength. What a terrible habit…"

Rahmann spread his hands open and sneered in a chilling voice.

"Our Chaos Clan is naturally incapable of practicing magic and battle aura. But we possess extraordinary天赋 that compensates for our shortcomings and allows us to leap above tens of thousands of races as the strongest. My body hungers for magic and battle aura to the point of madness. In other words, the very source of your power is merely our food!"

"What sort of nonsense are you babbling? Don't think that because you defeated Morrison, the Bramble Knights are some pushovers. Without fully unleashing his power, Morrison's strength only ranks in the middle tier." Fire blazed across Mesfield's body as battle aura erupted around her, condensing a golden aura blade in her hand. I'll see for myself whether your nails are harder or my sword is sharper!

"Oh? So confident…" Rahmann ran his tongue along his fingernail.

Mesfield noticed Seth hadn't moved at all and couldn't help but remind him, "Seth! What are you doing?!"

Seth snapped back to his senses, a layer of cold sweat beading on his forehead.

He knew he needed his own power now, but to fight alongside Mesfield he would need the Demon Armor — otherwise his strength still fell short of the First Knight. Yet remembering what Lord Elgin the Great Swordmaster had told him, he hesitated. If he continued using the Demon Armor, he would be completely consumed and reduced to a puppet of the armor, with no future at all.

"Seth! What are you hesitating for?!" Mesfield barked again.

Damn it! Why do I care so much about what Lord Elgin said? What exactly am I afraid of? To gain stronger power — so what if I become a demon!? I just want to grow stronger! That's all!

Seth cursed himself inwardly, gritted his teeth, and was instantly encased in a fearsome jet-black armor, his spear clamped tightly in his grip.

"You say magic and battle aura are your food? Then I refuse to believe it. With my armor on, let's see who's really the prey!"

The two knights joined forces against Rahmann, one of the Three Great Demons of the Chaos Clan. Near-Saint-tier-peak pressure rampaged mercilessly through the surroundings, devouring and crushing all enemies in its path…

Mesfield's fighting spirit surged wildly, and she snapped out:

"You'd better take this seriously. If you get beaten into helplessness in one instant, it won't be very interesting."

A light drizzle fell from the heavily overcast sky.

Blood flowed like rivers across the ground, gurgling into the Royal City's sewers.

The soldiers' corpses were piled into mountains. The two great knights, Mesfield and Seth, lay smashed into the cracked earth like two flies swatted flat. Both had completely lost their combat capability, their consciousness scattered and drifting.

"Tsk tsk tsk~" Rahmann stood in the dreary rain, watching the two unconscious figures before him as he clicked his tongue mockingly and tapped his tendrils.

"Did I not make myself clear enough?"

"Magic and battle aura are my food — which means…"

"Every attack you throw at me is completely ineffective."

title: Chapter 54 — Incoming
content:
Chapter 54 — Incoming

Volume 12 · Chapter 54

The innate ability of the Chaos Clan was to devour mana and battle energy, rendering all magic and martial techniques completely ineffective.

This wasn't an ability exclusive to the Three Great Powers—it was something any chaotic异族 possessed, the capacity to absorb both mana and battle energy.

This was precisely why the Chaos Clan stood at the apex of the food chain among countless races. After all, other races all cultivated power through mana and battle energy.

However, the Chaos Clan's absurdly overpowered devouring ability allowed them to completely counter every other race. Combined with their unique talents, there was simply no contest against the strong of other bloodlines.

Thanks to the turbulent currents below the Unknown Seas keeping them confined, otherwise conquering the world and ushering in a new Era of Chaos wouldn't have been empty boasting.

If one were to compare, the Chaos Clan's ability seemed far more powerful and comprehensive than Merlin's magic immunity.

They could absorb not only magic but also weaken martial techniques—not merely dispersing power, but absorbing it to strengthen themselves.

One need only look at Rahmann's transformation now to see this. His originally two-plus-meter frame had suddenly grown to over four meters tall,堪称 a little giant!

His brown-black skin had grown even harder, and the straight swords on his hands gleamed with metallic luster—he seemed even more formidable now.

Rahmann's current state showed a faint evolutionary trend, growing stronger than when he first appeared.

For the Chaos Clan, these mages and warriors were precious resources—especially those who had reached Saint-tier. They could absorb their power, helping themselves evolve into even more powerful killing machines.

This was why Rahmann hadn't delivered the killing blow against the three Thorn Knights. If he truly occupied the Britannia Empire, these Saint-tier strongmen would all be kept like livestock, providing a constant stream of mana and battle energy to fuel the race's continued evolution.

It was much like vampires, who for their own survival might secretly imprison humans to draw their blood.

At this moment, the three Thorn Knights' battle energy had been completely drained by Rahmann. Stripped of their combat ability, they lay on the ground like slabs of rotten meat, unconscious.

The surviving royal soldiers had either fled or were secretly hiding in dark corners, too terrified to come out. An enemy on this level was beyond anything they could handle.

Thick raindrops splattered against the rooftops with a steady drumming sound, and the dark, oppressive sky seemed ready to collapse.

Sensing no enemies remained nearby, Rahmann's gaze locked onto the distant Royal Court. The six eyes atop his head simultaneously blazed with fanaticism.

"Well, since we've already come this far, we can't just stand around doing nothing, can we?"

"Let's just take the chance to eliminate the empire's queen and bring this entire land under our race's complete control."

Rahmann started forward, shifting his four-meter-tall muscular frame toward where the queen resided.

But before he had gone far, Rahmann suddenly sensed another evil aura and froze mid-step.

"Hmm?" Rahmann turned his head and saw Seth—who had been completely drained of battle energy—get to his feet, clad in pitch-black armor that concealed his face. "What the hell? You can still stand? Your power was completely drained by me—you don't need to put on a show..."

Click clack click clack clack.

Accompanied by a series of strange sounds from the armor, subtle changes occurred across Seth's armored body.

He hunched over, his arms dangling limply, thick black smoke surging out from within the armor's seams.

Rahmann felt something was off. Logically speaking, once battle energy was drained to zero, movement should have been impossible. Why could this guy still move?

"Wait— who are you?"

"Urghhh..." Seth let out some painful groans, unable to form coherent words.

"Whatever, it doesn't matter who you are. Either way, you can't possibly stop me." Rahmann sneered viciously.

In the next instant, Seth lunged forward and delivered a devastating punch that sent Rahmann's head snapping to the side.

"Hah— what incredible guts you have..." Rahmann's body went rigid, all six crimson eyes locking onto Seth.

The current Seth was in a completely unconscious state. The reason he could still fight was entirely the will of the demon armor itself, which seemed to have a particular interest in the blood of the Chaos Clan.

Seth showed no signs of stopping. Forming his fingers into a blade, he stabbed viciously toward a fatal location—the heart!

However, the gap in power was simply insurmountable. Halfway through Seth's attack, the massive Rahmann clamped his arm between two fingers and lifted him into the air.

Seth struggled helplessly in mid-air. No matter how hard he pounded against Rahmann's fingers, he couldn't break free.

"Pfft!" Rahmann spat out the blood in his mouth and said meaningfully, "Your strength is impressive. If you'd been able to use that power earlier, you would've caused me considerable trouble. But I absorbed the battle energy of three Saint-tier experts. If you really want to put it in perspective, my strength is comparable to your Sect Realm masters—do you understand?"

It seemed Rahmann didn't understand the nature of the demon armor and still believed Seth retained consciousness.

The armor on Seth's body emitted another series of clicking sounds, and from within the seams, black thorn-like tendrils shot out, stabbing deeply into Rahmann's arm and beginning to greedily suck on his blood.

"Oh? Blood drinking? What a greedy little fellow. So you want to eat me? How interesting." Rahmann extended his fist and said without much effort, "But I have more important matters to attend to. Scram and get lost."

One punch—extremely fast—rained down with tremendous force, striking Seth squarely!

Like a baseball player driving a ball into the stands, Rahmann sent Seth flying into the unknown...

---

Royal Court.

Elizabeth paced back and forth, having done so repeatedly for quite some time now.

She had no idea what the current situation was outside, and no messengers had come to report.

This left Elizabeth extremely anxious, deeply worried about events outside, with a persistent sense that something terrible was about to happen.

Several hundred Violet Knight captains were stationed here. Captain Hope was also guarding the area, constantly on alert for any intruders.

Catherine stood quietly beside Elizabeth. Though she appeared to be resting with her eyes closed, her attention was entirely focused on the queen.

"Your Majesty, please stay calm. Nothing terrible should happen. If anything does occur, Mesfield will return immediately to report."

Elizabeth forced a weak smile, wondering if her unease had already begun affecting those around her.

Catherine hesitated for a moment, then tentatively asked, "Your Majesty, I have a question I'd like to..."

"Go ahead." Elizabeth looked at Catherine.

"Why did you choose Elgin the Great Sword Master to assist us? Is it truly the case that the royal family has no trump cards left? Bringing in someone with unknown background carries enormous risk, doesn't it?" Catherine's eyebrows furrowed slightly.

"We do still have trump cards, but it's better not to use those. As for why I asked for Elgin the Great Sword Master..." Elizabeth paused thoughtfully, then smiled, "Rather than continuing to clash with someone this powerful, it's better to seek terms for coexistence. That way everyone wins—a far better outcome than mutual destruction. Besides, Elgin the Great Sword Master is currently our ally. Isn't that better than having another enemy?"

"Well..." Catherine had no response. She continued, "Then after the war ends? How will we deal with Elgin the Great Sword Master?"

"That matter... we'll discuss it later..." Elizabeth lowered her head and didn't give a clear answer.

The originally calm atmosphere was suddenly shattered. A sound of tearing air rang out, and the glass on the windows began to vibrate violently, rattling noisily!

Catherine's delicate brows shot up in alarm. Sensing danger, she quickly threw herself at Elizabeth—

"Your Majesty, watch out!!!"

title: Chapter 55 — Monthly Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 55 — Monthly Bonus Chapter

Volume 12 · Chapter 55

The shattered glass was completely pulverized, and the walls above were torn apart by an overwhelming force, collapsing entirely.

Deafening booms echoed as massive chunks of debris rained down, and the Violet Thorn Knights huddled together, raising their shields to protect the great hall.

The falling boulders sealed the hall’s exit, leaving the group with no chance of escape.

The jagged, precise cuts on the broken stone suggested they had been sliced by a razor-sharp blade, the deep gouges shockingly stark.

In that instant, Catherine lunged and tackled Elizabeth to the ground, shielding her beneath her body to prevent the queen from harm.

Once the tremors subsided, Catherine carefully helped Elizabeth back to her feet, remaining vigilant of their surroundings.

“...What happened?” Elizabeth was still shaken, unsure what had caused this sudden attack. Could it be a catapult strike from the Allied Army?

“Your Majesty, be careful—it’s an enemy assault!” Catherine tightened her grip on her staff, positioning herself in front of Elizabeth, leaving no opening for the enemy.

Dust kicked up by the debris spread in all directions, obscuring their vision.

But through the gaping hole in the ceiling, a massive silhouette slowly emerged, accompanied by heavy, thudding footsteps.

“Protect Her Majesty!” Chapman roared, issuing the command to the knights around him.

Dozens of Violet Thorn Knights encircled Elizabeth, raising their shields to form what seemed like an impenetrable defense.

Elizabeth was uneasy, never expecting an attack at a time like this. It caught her completely off guard.

If the enemy had breached this far, did that mean Elgin the Great Swordsman had failed?

If he hadn’t been defeated, the enemy never would have made it into the imperial capital. And the Thorn Knights seemed to have met a grim fate—there hadn’t been a single word from them!

Elizabeth’s brows knitted tightly as anxiety gnawed at her. Her mind raced, searching for a solution.

Rahman parted the thick smoke and appeared before them, peering through the massive hole into the hall.

Everyone was stunned by Rahman’s bizarre appearance—no one could comprehend what kind of creature this was.

Even Elizabeth, who had seen much of the world, couldn’t identify which race Rahman belonged to.

“...What in the world is that thing?” Chapman muttered in disbelief.

“I don’t know, but everyone, be careful,” Catherine said, her expression growing grave. “If this thing made it here, it means the front lines have already fallen.”

Rahman surveyed each person below, and when his six crimson eyes fell on Elizabeth hiding at the back, they lit up with amusement. He braced his hands against the walls.

“Greetings, everyone. Out of courtesy, allow me to introduce myself. I am Rahman of the Black Blade, one of the Three Great Generals under the Chaos King. I declare that, from this day forward, all of you are my slaves. Everything in this empire now belongs to the great Chaos King. So, Your Majesty... would you mind dying for me?”

Elizabeth recoiled in terror, her face pale with dread.

“Chaos King? Never heard of him,” Catherine said coldly, sensing the enemy’s clear intent. She had to tread carefully.

“You’ll know soon enough when our great king sets foot on your land,” Rahman said reverently, his voice slow and deliberate. “When you witness his magnificent presence, you will bow in sincere submission.”

“What nonsense are you spouting?” Catherine radiated the imposing aura of a Saint-tier power, attempting to warn him off. “You think you’re worthy of our submission?”

“Worth or not, it’s all decided by strength.” Rahman grinned savagely. “If you refuse, we’ll just beat you until you do.”

Elizabeth stayed silent, her mind racing. If Elgin the Great Swordsman had truly fallen, then none of them stood a chance against this foe.

“Before we begin, I have a question,” Rahman pondered aloud. “I didn’t encounter any overwhelmingly powerful figures on my way here. How did you manage to defeat the Four Elemental Sword Saints?”

At this, everyone fell silent. The implications were staggering.

Elizabeth’s eyes widened. No overwhelmingly powerful figures? Did that mean he had never even crossed paths with Elgin the Great Swordsman?

That couldn’t be... Unless Elgin had unilaterally broken their agreement and fled alone!

Elizabeth turned the possibilities over in her mind, but that was the only explanation that made sense—unbelievable as it was.

Rahman, growing impatient at their silence, sneered. “Forget it. The Four Sword Saints were nothing but pawns—their status doesn’t even compare to an ordinary member of the Chaos race. There’s no point in dwelling on it. Your Majesty, come here and die.”

No sooner had the words left his mouth than Rahman reached out, his massive hand lunging toward Elizabeth at the back. His sharp, menacing claws sent a chill down everyone’s spine.

“Protect Her Majesty!”

Chapman bellowed, and dozens of Violet Thorn Knights surged forward, desperate to stop Rahman’s massive arm.

“Get lost, you insignificant insects. I’ve no interest in crushing ants.” Rahman flicked his hand dismissively, and the knights were sent flying, slamming violently into the walls. Their fate hung in the balance.

The power gap was simply too vast. Even a high-ranking knight like Chapman was helpless, forced to watch as the enemy did as he pleased.

“Your Majesty, step back—leave this one to me...” Catherine said gravely, her face darkening.

“Be careful.” Elizabeth took half a step back, giving Catherine room to act.

Catherine raised her long staff and struck the ground with a forceful *ding*—a crisp, resonant sound that echoed endlessly through the hall.

A radiant light burst from the floor, and an enormous white magic formation materialized, enveloping the entire hall in a layered magical barrier—a seamless, absolute defense!

This was a pre-prepared defensive spell array Catherine had set up, consisting of three layers. Under normal circumstances, even a group of Saint-tier attackers would need time to break through it.

Rahman stared at the glowing barrier before him and let out a cold laugh. “Oh? Interesting. But utterly useless.”

With that, he reached toward the demonic defense array—and his hand passed straight through all three layers, absorbing the magic within. The barrier shattered effortlessly.

Since Catherine had been continuously feeding magic into the barrier, she suffered severe backlash.

She dropped to one knee, her face ashen, cold sweat beading on her forehead.

What’s happening?!

Why is my magic being drained?!

It’s... as if it’s being devoured!

What kind of monster can absorb magic?!

Catherine felt her magic nearly depleted, her entire body weak and unsteady.

“Catherine! Are you alright?” Elizabeth rushed to her side, trying to help her up.

“Your Majesty, you still have time to worry about others? Better pray for yourself!” Rahman cackled, his razor-sharp claws shooting toward the defenseless Elizabeth.

“Your Majesty!” Catherine mustered the last of her strength, shoving Elizabeth behind her. She locked her gaze on the incoming claws, and the ring on her hand began to emit a faint glow...

Just as the claws were about to strike—

A black shadow flashed past from outside.

Merlin drove a powerful punch straight into Rahman’s face, smashing it into a grotesque, twisted shape.

“You overgrown cockroach, who the hell do you think you are?” Merlin snarled. “Who gave you permission to ignore me?!”

“Get over here! We need to have a *serious* talk!”

title: Chapter 56 — Sea Zone
content:
Chapter 56 — Sea Zone

Volume 12 · Chapter 56

The suddenly appearing Merlin caught Rachman completely off guard, who had failed to sense the enemy's approach at all.

-..What kind of power is this?!

How much force!

After absorbing so much power, I'm actually having trouble holding it back!?

Merlin's punches forcibly distorted Rachman's face, making his already ugly features even more ugly and twisted.

The power behind each punch summoned biting gales of storm wind, kicking up fragments of stone like scythes and shaking the surroundings!

Elizabeth and Catherine had no choice but to cover their eyes, finding it hard to make out the situation before them.

Merlin's single punch carried considerable force, sending Rachman's burly and enormous body flying, and he followed right after.

The two disappeared far from the grand hall, heading who-knows-where.

When the storm subsided, Elizabeth and Catherine looked around and found that Merlin and that monster who called itself belonging to the Chaos Clan had vanished without a trace.

If not for the glaring hole in the ceiling of the grand hall, one might have thought all of this was just a dream, as if nothing had happened at all.

After a long silence, Elizabeth broke the quiet as though waking from a reverie, unable to say with certainty, "That person who suddenly appeared earlier...should have been Grand Swordmaster, right?"

"Yeah, even though it was fleeting, it was definitely that man...." Catherine calmed down slightly and gave an affirmative reply.

Elizabeth immediately breathed a sigh of relief, having worried that Grand Swordmaster Elgin would unilaterally violate the agreement and simply abandon the mess before him, wipe his hands clean, and walk away.

But it was fine now. Grand Swordmaster Elgin wasn't that bad; he still had a bit of respect for contracts.

Now that she knew Merlin hadn't left, Elizabeth felt far more at ease than before, and the flustered expression on her face had disappeared.

"That's good. With Grand Swordmaster Elgin here, that monster shouldn't be able to cause too much trouble earlier."

Catherine frowned, recalling the events from just now, and couldn't help but feel puzzled inside. "Your Majesty, do you know what that monster was? It seemed to be calling itself the Chaos Clan."

"I don't know. It looked somewhat like the Beast Race, but it felt completely different. I've never seen any race with such a bizarre appearance...."

Even after thinking carefully, Elizabeth couldn't give an answer, knowing nothing at all about the self-proclaimed Chaos Clan member from earlier.

"Is that so, how strange...." Catherine lowered her head, her expression looking even more puzzled.

"What's wrong? Is something not right?" Elizabeth asked patiently upon seeing Catherine's troubled brow.

"Just now, I briefly clashed with that monster using barrier magic, but in an instant, more than half of my magical power was lost, as if it had been drained away by the enemy, and the barrier magic was destroyed outright." Catherine paused and added, "If I hadn't stopped supplying power in time, I might have fainted from magical exhaustion by now."

"That is indeed very strange. In theory, this world has diverse races, but one that can absorb others' magical power.... that's completely unheard of."

Elizabeth's brows knitted together, a hint of bewilderment leaking into her tone. If the Chaos Clan truly possessed such an absurdly overpowered ability, then things would be rather troublesome.

Because all races cultivated magical power and battle energy to gain strength, yet here appeared a species that fed upon magical power and battle energy.

This meant that all races were prey to the Chaos Clan, placing them at a higher position on the food chain.

Although Elizabeth didn't understand the Chaos Clan, she had heard of another piece of information.

"However, it said their king resides in the Unknown Sea, which is a forbidden zone where even gods are said to struggle to tread...."

"The Unknown Sea?" Catherine looked over in surprise, apparently quite curious about that place.

"That's right. It is said that within the Unknown Sea lies a gate to another world, belonging to the civilization of another world. Anyone who enters the Unknown Sea has never come out alive." Elizabeth paused, recalling as she spoke. "During the old Age of Navigation, many imperial families sponsored expeditions to explore the Unknown Sea, but they all mysteriously disappeared. Only empty ships drifted on the sea, as if the crew had been erased. No one knows what they experienced. It remains an unsolved mystery to this day, and eventually, when trade routes were established, everyone deliberately avoided that sea."

"There's really such a dangerous place...." A bead of cold sweat trickled down Catherine's forehead, and she felt deeply shaken inside upon hearing Elizabeth's words.

"Coughhhhhh!"

Rachman crashed to the ground and slid dozens of meters before finally coming to a stop, somewhat dazed from Merlin's blows.

Merlin quickly followed behind and came after, looking at Rachman on the ground and saying, "I called out to you when we were heading outside the city, and you ignored me? You're the first person to disregard my existence like this."

Rachman slowly rose to his feet, his six crimson eyes looking contemptuously at the masked man before him. "So that's how it is. I initially thought a lost beggar was wandering around the battlefield."

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue, frowning. "Which eye do you have that makes me look like a beggar?"

"A guy like you who radiates an ordinary aura from head to toe not being ignored would be the strange thing, right?"

Rachman slowly squatted down in front of Merlin, his towering nearly five-meter muscular frame looking down upon the tiny human before him.

Looking at the man before him who resembled a homeless drifter, Rachman found it amusing and said in a teasing, dismissive tone.

"But your strength is considerable. Being able to punch me flying with a single blow shows you have some skill, albeit only a tiny bit."

"...Merlin let out a cold sneer, completely unmoved by such words.

"If I were to get serious, someone like you, an ant....." Rachman extended his massive hand and pinched with two fingers. "I'd only need two fingers to crush you, and you'd die a horrible death, reduced to a pile of meat paste."

"Cut the nonsense. My time is precious. Weren't you also invited by the United Legion?" Merlin asked calmly.

"So what?" Rachman's expression turned mocking, feeling that the tiny human before him was powerless against him.

"That's enough. Come over and accept your death, then." Merlin beckoned provocatively at Rachman with a finger.

"Huh?"

Rachman froze, disbelief flashing in his eyes, wondering if he'd misheard.

He could sense that the human before him possessed not a single iota of magical power or battle energy — he was completely an ordinary person.

And yet this utterly commonplace existence, thisNobody among the masses, was actually ordering him to come accept his death!?

If this wasn't a joke, then it was blatant contempt for him!

Rachman narrowed his eyes. He had originally had no interest in this tiny human, but now a killing intent arose.

"It seems you haven't grasped the situation. I am one of the Three Great Leaders of the Chaos Clan! You other races are nothing but livestock in my eyes. Moreover, I've now absorbed the power of four Saint-tier experts, my strength unprecedented and unrivaled, comparable to your so-called Ancestor Realm. An ant like you, what do you have to take my life? You ought to know when to brag and when not to!"

Merlin didn't say a word. His nodachi flashed from its sheath like lightning. Even as he executed a quick-draw strike, the menacing sword intent vanished in an instant—

Rachman's voice abruptly stopped. His body went rigid, and he gazed blankly at the nodachi raised high in Merlin's hand.

"Ho....how is this possible...."

"A mere...a mere ant, actually...

A red line appeared on Rachman's enormous body, and then blood gushed forth as his body was cleaved in two by Merlin's single slash.

The two halves of the corpse crashed heavily to the ground, spasming continuously — clearly dead beyond recovery.

Merlin returned his nodachi to its scabbard, looked down at Rachman's corpse, and casually muttered —

"I want to break...."

"Who cares whether you're strong or not?"

title: Chapter 57 — Victory Celebration
content:
Chapter 57 — Victory Celebration

Volume 12 · Chapter 57

Merlin looked down at Rahhman's corpse, a faint confusion stirring in his heart.

For his heart still felt no easing of the curse.

Probably because the Chaos Tribe didn't cultivate magic or martial energy, so Merlin's curse relief had no effect on them.

Chaos Tribe? Truly a baffling race—no need to practice magic or martial arts, yet possessing such formidable combat power.

Merlin frowned, feeling his trip hadn't yielded much; perhaps in a few days, the curse on his heart would recur.

Elizabeth, unable to rest easy, had sent Catherine to check the situation, fearing unexpected developments—perhaps she could help at a critical moment.

Though Catherine hadn't been willing to leave Elizabeth, afraid of more ambushes.

But under Elizabeth's repeated requests, Catherine had no choice but to come and take a look.

The moment Catherine arrived, she saw Elgin the Great Swordsman swing his sword and kill Rahhman.

Huge raindrops fell head-on, splashing on the ground like blooming flowers.

The huge-bodied Rahhman was cleaved in two, his corpse spraying blood as it hit the ground.

What seemed like an ordinary scene actually shocked Catherine immensely—

Such a formidable enemy, unable to resist even one strike from Elgin the Great Swordsman?!

He was supposed to be able to absorb magic and martial energy, yet before Elgin he couldn't even fight back!

Actually, the Chaos Tribe's ability to devour magic and martial energy had no effect on Merlin at all, since he possessed neither.

Cold sweat seeped from Catherine's forehead, quickly washed away by rain. Though her eyes were always closed, it didn't affect her vision.

She couldn't figure out what method Elgin used to perfectly bypass the enemy's troublesome abilities and defeat him so easily.

Catherine didn't believe the self-proclaimed member of the Chaos Three Giants had been weakened; the only explanation was probably—

Not that Rahhman was weak, but Elgin the Great Swordsman was overwhelmingly strong...

After Rahhman fell, the Allied Legion completely collapsed, unable to organize another offensive.

Elizabeth acted decisively, immediately organizing remaining forces for a counterattack.

The remnants of the Allied Legion were pushed back continuously and soon surrendered, declaring defeat in the war.

A week later—

Victorious Elizabeth successfully suppressed the rebellion, taking over all of House O'Frey's wealth for the capital's revival.

However, when dealing with the O'Frey family, the Duke was already dead, which surprised Elizabeth for several days.

She didn't know O'Frey was killed by Rahhman; she speculated that O'Frey might have chosen suicide upon seeing the war lost.

Of course, what puzzled Elizabeth most was the monster claiming to be from the Chaos Tribe; no matter how she investigated, she couldn't get convincing results.

So Elizabeth didn't dig deeper, temporarily setting aside the issue and prioritizing the capital's revival.

Once the empire's situation stabilized, Elizabeth planned to send people to explore the unknown seas again.

Turbulent Britain restored peace; news of victory spread quickly, and displaced capital residents began returning home gradually.

Noble lords who participated in suppressing the rebellion received merits, territorial rewards, and local privileges.

Now the capital showed a thriving scene; though it looked dilapidated, revival was only a matter of time.

Restoring the lake beneath the capital was also Elizabeth's top priority; it was the habitat of lake fairies and hid the empire's lifeline, so it had to be repaired soon.
