Elgin the Great Swordsman's heroic deeds in defeating the Allied Legion quickly spread throughout the empire.

Regarding Elgin, the people worshipped and admired him, praising him as an unprecedented hero.

Many knew he was in the capital now, so these days the dilapidated capital grew crowded, almost overflowing.

Many gathered beneath the royal walls, even setting up tents to stay overnight, unwilling to leave just to catch a glimpse of the real Elgin the Great Swordsman.

The scene was comparable to the Holy Church's grandest pilgrimage ceremony; without exaggeration, even the capital's most prosperous days couldn't compare.

Clearly Elgin's influence had reached unprecedented heights; people seemed to love this nameless hero more than their queen.

Merlin the Demon Lord, inexplicably, had solidified the position of imperial savior; everyone was willing to believe this pretext.

Yet at this moment, Merlin was like a laborer, struggling to collect his wages—

The royal conference hall had only Merlin and Elizabeth present.

"Your Majesty, the situation seems stable now. My task is complete. I wonder if you'll fulfill our agreement?" Merlin sat at the conference table, leaning against a soft sofa.

"Uh?" Elizabeth sat opposite Merlin, blinking her big eyes innocently. "Agreement? What agreement?"

"Tch!" Merlin frowned, annoyed by Elizabeth's feigned ignorance. In any era, withholding workers' wages was shameful.

"Oh~ I remember now. Helping you repay the debt to the Holy Church, right?" Elizabeth looked enlightened.

"Correct. We had an agreement. Don't think you can get away with it. Not a single copper coin less." Merlin said with a serious expression.

"Well..." Elizabeth pondered for a moment, then looked up seriously. "No problem. I'm willing to assist you economically to repay your help this time."

"That's more like it~" Merlin showed a satisfied smile, thinking he'd soon be free again, feeling a bit excited.

"However, before I fulfill my promise, you need to do me a small favor, or I won't repay the Holy Church debt..." Elizabeth turned the conversation, adding a condition.

"Ah?!" Merlin froze, sitting up straight immediately, saying with displeasure, "Hey, stop right there. Don't push your luck, or we'll split. I won't let you off."

"Mr. Merlin, please calm down. We're negotiating peacefully now. If you're unhappy, we can discuss it."

Elizabeth said with a smile.

But this had almost no effect on Merlin, who was immune to beautiful women's smiles. Who knew what conspirator's face hid behind that kind smile?

"No deal. You need to pay the debt now, and no extra conditions. That's the bottom line."

"I'll pay your debt, but you only need to do a small favor..." Elizabeth paused, continuing, "No need for you to travel weary, no need for force. You just need to wear a mask and walk around the capital once."

"Hmm?" Merlin tilted his head. It sounded as easy as a walk, so he asked, "What do you mean?"

"Don't worry, it's nothing bad..." Elizabeth's slightly pursed lips curved into a beautiful arc—

"I've arranged a grand parade for you. I hope you'll participate."

"This is a stage built specifically for heroes. You're the protagonist..."

(~-v- )~

title: Chapter 58 — Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 58 — Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 12 · Chapter 58

"A grand parade?" Merlin furrowed his brows, clearly disliking the idea.

"That's right, I assume you've heard?" Elizabeth paused before continuing, "There are already huge crowds gathered outside, all eager to catch a glimpse of you."

"So what? Those people out there have nothing to do with me." Merlin sighed in exasperation. As the Great Demon Lord, he found it absurd that he had somehow become a hero. If the demon race found out, they would brand him a traitor and execute him.

If Merlin were just an ordinary demon, he wouldn’t worry about such things. But as a noble monarch, his every word and action represented the demon race. It would be all too easy for rumors to reach the Demon Council, where they would mock him mercilessly.

Merlin was grateful he always wore a mask—no one knew his true identity. Otherwise, he wouldn’t be able to stay in the human empire, and the demon race would be furious with him.

"How can you say they have nothing to do with you? You’re currently the most celebrated figure in the empire—your fame has even spread to other empires. As a public figure, you have a responsibility to guide your followers." Elizabeth reasoned, both emotionally and logically.

A bead of sweat rolled down Merlin’s forehead. *Followers? What nonsense!* Since when had he become the object of some cult’s devotion?

"Fine, even if I have some responsibility, there’s no need to make such a fuss with a grand parade. Can’t you just use some forceful measures to disperse them?"

"I’m afraid I’ve already tried that," Elizabeth said with a sigh, rubbing her temples. "It didn’t work at all. This is a critical moment for the empire’s revival, and this situation is really giving me a headache~" She stole a glance at Merlin’s expression. "I’ve already prepared the money for you, but this issue is tying up all my energy, so I haven’t been able to fulfill our agreement~"

"Tch! You’re really something..." Merlin gritted his teeth, finally understanding the saying *"the debtor is the boss."* Elizabeth was cunning—this wasn’t really about dispersing the crowd, but using his fame to stabilize the current situation.

And indeed, Elizabeth had her own calculations.

Right now, the imperial royal family’s prestige was indeed inferior to that of Elgin the Great Swordsman, whose influence was overwhelming. Choosing to confront him by force would be unwise—two tigers couldn’t share the same mountain.

Moreover, Elgin the Great Swordsman’s strength was undeniable; the imperial royal family couldn’t possibly challenge him.

Fortunately, Elizabeth saw that Merlin didn’t seem to have grand ambitions, making him relatively safe—someone who wouldn’t provoke her unless provoked first.

But the most crucial point was that the empire *needed* Elgin the Great Swordsman. They absolutely could not afford to make an enemy of him.

A nation’s survival in this world required formidable military deterrence—a trump card. Without it, other empires would covet them, leading to brutal invasions and plunder.

The current era of relative peace existed precisely because the military strength of each empire was balanced.

Now, with the Lake Spirit in prolonged slumber, Britannia’s trump card was lost, weakening its deterrence against other empires.

In this situation, Elgin the Great Swordsman became extremely important. Elizabeth intended to fully leverage his fame, making him the empire’s nominal protector.

All these factors combined led Elizabeth to adopt a gentler strategy toward Elgin the Great Swordsman, eager to ride the wave of his popularity.

In other words, she wanted to *heavily* capitalize on Elgin the Great Swordsman’s influence to achieve two goals:

First, to show all the empire’s citizens the friendship between Elgin the Great Swordsman and the royal family, stabilizing the domestic situation and demonstrating the royal family’s broad-mindedness.

Second, to put on a show for the other empires watching like hawks—basically, to signal: *We’re on good terms with Elgin the Great Swordsman. Don’t think the Lake Spirit’s absence makes us an easy target.*

Elizabeth’s little schemes were, of course, transparent to Merlin. He was a ruler himself—how could he not see through such simple calculations?

Merlin had his own considerations, but his desire for a peaceful life took precedence.

He certainly didn’t want the empire to be in constant turmoil—it would disrupt his relatively quiet existence.

Even if Merlin wouldn’t go looking for trouble, some things had a way of finding him. Plus, there was that *annoying woman* at home who kept shouting *"Justice will prevail!"* every day.

Merlin would *never* admit that he was actually looking forward to Elizabeth’s promise—that was the *real* reason he agreed to make an appearance.

The next day, the grand parade organized by Elizabeth began.

A ray of sunlight broke over the horizon, shining directly onto the central avenue of the imperial capital, illuminating the statue of Britannia’s founding emperor.

Though the capital was now somewhat dilapidated, far from its former glory, it did little to dampen the people’s enthusiasm.

The area outside the capital’s walls was packed with people, not a single patch of ground visible. Small disturbances broke out from time to time, but since everyone seemed to be there for Elgin the Great Swordsman, no major incidents occurred.

For this parade, the remaining Purple Thorn Knights were fully deployed—several thousand of them, maintaining order at the scene.

Several newspapers and media outlets had also arrived, eager to capture images of Elgin the Great Swordsman for a major story.

Reporters pushed forward with all their might, fighting for the best vantage points, nearly coming to blows.

The square was even more crowded, with people milling about in a vast, surging sea, like waves in the ocean.

Many of Elgin the Great Swordsman’s admirers wore matching silver masks and black robes, some even holding replicas of *Banri Garan*—whether genuine or fake was anyone’s guess.

One had to admire the merchants’ business sense. For the sake of profit, they could produce anything, and as long as it was connected to Elgin the Great Swordsman, it would sell like hotcakes.

If any elder of the Demon Council were to witness this scene, they would likely cough up blood in rage—counterfeiting a royal artifact was a capital offense, punishable by death!

Inside the palace corridor—

Chapman led several elaborately dressed Purple Thorn Knights, escorting Merlin while also preventing any troublemakers from rushing forward.

Merlin had also been given a thorough makeover for the occasion. Though his outfit hadn’t changed much, the black robe he wore was far more ornate than usual.

Pure black fabric trimmed with gold, a high-standing collar—he looked far more imposing.

Whether it was intentional misdirection on Elizabeth’s part or not, Merlin’s black robe bore the royal crest at the chest—a golden lion.

As they approached the end of the corridor, preparing to face the cheering crowds, Chapman followed respectfully behind Merlin, his face tense and his forehead beaded with sweat. After hesitating for a moment, he spoke:

"...Great Swordsman, I... I have a small request. I don’t know if you’d be willing to fulfill it. Once we go out, I fear I won’t have another chance."

"Hm? What is it?" Merlin turned his head as he walked, sizing up the middle-aged man.

Chapman fidgeted awkwardly before pulling a pen and paper from his pocket. His face was flushed with excitement. "Could you... give me your autograph?"

"To be honest, I’ve admired you for a very long time."

title: Chapter 59 — Going Together
content:
Chapter 59 — Going Together

Volume 12 · Chapter 59

...This...

Merlin hesitated, looking at Chapman’s small, hopeful eyes. He really couldn’t bring himself to refuse.

“All you need to do is write your name. If it’s really inconvenient, then forget it.” Chapman gave an awkward smile, not pushing too hard. “Actually, the day after tomorrow is my daughter’s fifth birthday. She’s just like me—we both admire you very much. So... I wanted to get your autograph as a birthday gift for her.”

Merlin knit his brows slightly. Though he disliked the hassle of signing things, Chapman’s feelings as a father touched him.

Children’s wishes were usually simple. Maybe a gift that could make someone happy was enough.

Merlin still had a vague impression of Chapman. He seemed to have first met him among the guards in Lexham.

Back then, Chapman hadn’t been particularly polite—he’d thought Merlin was a fraud, a liar spouting wild, baseless boasts.

Merlin remembered all of this. But then, most people looked down on him. You couldn’t blame Chapman for not recognizing quality. Who would have guessed that this powerless, iron-ranked adventurer with no magic or aura was actually Elgin, the renowned Great Swordsman whose name shook the empire?

Now, Merlin almost wanted to laugh. Recalling Chapman’s attitude back then, and seeing him now, nervously asking for an autograph, he found it all rather amusing.

Merlin had no intention of making things difficult for Chapman. He wasn’t the kind of petty person who’d hold a grudge against a minor figure over such things—especially when the man seemed like a decent father.

“What’s inconvenient about this? If you want a hundred, I’ll sign a hundred.”

Chapman, seeing the Great Swordsman Elgin extend his hand, quickly and respectfully offered the paper and pen. “Then... I’ll trouble you...”

Merlin took the paper and pen and immediately began writing with a flourish. But after just two strokes, a sudden jolt of alarm shot through him.

Because of his own habits, Merlin had nearly written his real name, which would have exposed his true identity.

A cold sweat beaded on Merlin’s forehead. His eyes widened in shock—he’d almost made a huge mistake.

Chapman noticed the Great Swordsman’s strange reaction and asked in surprise, “Are you alright? Is something wrong?”

“Nothing.” Merlin shook his head, quickly scratching out what he’d written before signing “Elgin, the Great Swordsman” at the bottom. He even added a “Happy Birthday” before handing it back to Chapman.

“Thank you, my lord. Thank you so much...” Chapman’s heart swelled with joy as he took the autograph and examined it. But then his smile gradually froze on his face.

How should he put this?

The Great Swordsman’s handwriting was... kind of ugly.

---

At the end of the corridor, the four Thorn Knights waited, ready to accompany Elgin the Great Swordsman. Though in truth, they were just there for show.

It seemed Elizabeth had gone to great lengths. Every place where the royal family could gain influence had been meticulously arranged.

Apart from Katherine, the other knights still bore bruises and swelling on their faces—clear signs their injuries hadn’t fully healed.

Among them, Seth looked the worst. His face was pale, and he seemed exhausted.

Compared to the damage Rahman had inflicted, the harm from the demonic armor appeared even more severe, placing a tremendous burden on him.

The four Thorn Knights stood in pairs, listening to the deafening cheers from outside, all of them silent.

Those cheers weren’t for the Thorn Knights. They were for Elgin the Great Swordsman, wave after wave of roaring acclaim.

Mesfield knit her delicate brows, her mood souring as she listened to the cheers.

She had always assumed that after the war, Queen Elizabeth and Elgin the Great Swordsman would return to their icy relationship, openly hostile once more.

Then Mesfield could finally drop the pretense, seek revenge against Elgin the Great Swordsman, and reclaim her dignity.

She knew she couldn’t beat Elgin the Great Swordsman. But a tree lives by its bark, a man by his face—she couldn’t let the humiliation that vile man had subjected her to go unanswered!

But reality had slapped Mesfield hard across the face. After the war, not only had Queen Elizabeth not fallen out with Elgin the Great Swordsman, but their relationship had suddenly warmed up, as if they were in a honeymoon phase?

Her Majesty had personally organized a grand parade to celebrate Elgin the Great Swordsman’s achievements, repeatedly showcasing how close and intimate the royal family and the Great Swordsman were. Anyone who didn’t know better would think they all shared the same pair of pants.

Mesfield was far from satisfied with this outcome. Her resentment festered with nowhere to go.

Beside her, Morrison listened to the cheers outside and sighed in admiration. “As expected of Elgin the Great Swordsman. To attract this many people... Truly, a hero is beloved wherever he goes.”

“What kind of hero is he? He just got lucky. Otherwise, he’d be nothing but a rat everyone wants to stomp on.” Mesfield huffed, unable to contain her anger.

“How can you say that? The Great Swordsman isn’t a bad person. He goes around helping the weak and punishing evil. Why do you hold such a grudge against him?” Morrison asked, confused.

Mesfield recalled those streams of spit and felt her entire body tremble with rage. “That despicable man doesn’t deserve trust!”

Morrison, seeing Mesfield’s furious expression, couldn’t begin to guess what she was thinking. He could only offer gentle advice. “Come on, whatever grudges you had in the past, you should let them go. Right now, we’re still in a cooperative relationship with the Great Swordsman.”

“That’s *now*. Who knows about the future?” Mesfield muttered defiantly.

“You said the same thing before, and yet...” Morrison shrugged.

Mesfield was left speechless, her face flushed crimson. Being proven wrong so often had left her almost numb to the embarrassment.

“Just don’t go looking for trouble, Mesfield...” Katherine suddenly spoke up, her eyes still closed as she rested.

“What do you mean by that?” Mesfield turned to look at the composed Katherine.

“You three couldn’t even handle the enemy before, and Elgin the Great Swordsman cut him down. The power gap is that obvious. Where do you get the courage to pick a fight?” Katherine said indifferently.

Seth lowered his head, silently clenching his fists. Ever since returning to the capital, he’d been dealt blow after blow. He’d thought his strength was decent, but after encountering a true powerhouse, he realized he was nothing but a tiny shrimp.

“If it weren’t for that weirdo’s tricky abilities, how could we have been completely helpless? Don’t make it sound like we’re useless!” Mesfield snapped in frustration.

“What’s the difference? A loss is a loss. Making excuses just makes you look pathetic.” Katherine paused before continuing, “Right now, the empire needs Elgin the Great Swordsman. He’s an indispensable factor in maintaining stability. That’s all there is to it.”

Mesfield opened her mouth to retort, but then caught sight of Elgin the Great Swordsman approaching, escorted by the Rose Knights.

Merlin saw the four Thorn Knights waiting for him, so he waved his hand with exaggerated gravitas. “Comrades, greetings. Comrades, you’ve worked hard.”

“Yes!” Mesfield curled her lip, her face darkening. Disgust radiated from her eyes, written all over her forehead.

Merlin, sensing the wave of hostile energy, couldn’t help but sweat in embarrassment.

*Tsk! What the hell!*

Is this female knight a lunatic?

Why does she hold such a grudge against me?

It’s not like I did anything but spit a few times. Is it really that serious?

Unless...

...it’s because I haven’t spat at her in a while, and she’s grown desperate from the withdrawal?

Merlin considered the possibility and shot Mesfield a playful, suggestive grin.

*Cough cough cough cough...*

Mesfield’s body went rigid. Her expression twisted into something unreadable, her face flushing pale one moment and green the next.

*What is this supposed to mean?! He’s clearly mocking me!*

Does he think that just because he’s in a high position now, he can do whatever he wants?!

Unforgivable! A knight may die, but she cannot be humiliated!

Mesfield drew the sharp sword at her waist, ready to charge forward in a desperate attack.

“Elgin the Great Swordsman! I’ll take you down with me!”

Morrison quickly wrapped his arms around Mesfield’s waist to stop her. “Calm down! You can’t beat him!”

“Let go! Don’t stop me!” Mesfield’s eyes turned red, and she was so furious she nearly cried.

“I’ll die with that bastard!”

title: Chapter 60 — Chance Encounter
content:
Chapter 60 — Chance Encounter

Volume 12 · Chapter 60

“Mesfield, stay calm! If you can't beat them, don't pick a fight, or Her Majesty the Queen will be the one in trouble!” Morrison grabbed Mesfield tightly, afraid she would cause trouble at this moment.
“I don't care! Even if I can't beat them, I'll die together with that despicable ruffian!” Mesfield swung her sword repeatedly, but she was too far from Elgin Sword Master and couldn't reach him at all.
“Tsk tsk tsk! Really troublesome~” Merlin clicked his tongue and shook his head, speaking with a troubled tone, “It's all my fault, all my fault. I'm often deeply troubled by my own charm…”
“What nonsense are you spouting!?” Mesfield gritted her teeth, her gums itching with hatred.
“You must be fascinated by my charm, otherwise you wouldn't be so deeply infatuated with me now, right?” Merlin looked at Mesfield with a helpless expression.
“You!”
“Alright, alright, you don't need to say more, I already understand…”
Before Mesfield could finish speaking, Merlin cut her off and continued.
“Your love for me has surpassed life and death; you even want to die together with me. I have to admire your resolve, Miss, but unfortunately I have no interest in women who are brawn-heavy and brain-light like you~”
“You… you…” Mesfield trembled with anger, her sword fell to the ground, her eyelids flipped, and she fainted on the spot.
“Mesfield! Mesfield!!!” Morrison shook Mesfield, but there was no response. “Someone! Someone! Hurry and call a healer!”
“Ah, how did this happen?” Merlin sighed, tossed his blond hair, and said with a sense of regret—
“Learning that I cannot accept her truth, she fainted from sorrow…”
“Indeed, too much charm is also a sin.”
◇
Outside, crowds surged, everyone waiting for Elgin Sword Master to appear.
The Imperial Capital's main avenue was cleared, making space for the parade.
This parade isn't very long; basically just a loop around the Imperial Capital's streets.
Yet its grandeur was extremely lively, surpassing even the annual National Founding Festival, unprecedented in scale.
At a certain spot, an old face was doing a live broadcast of this grand parade—
“Hello everyone, I'm Bella, a reporter from the London Post, and I'm currently at the forefront of the Imperial Capital.”
“The rebellion threatening the Imperial Capital was finally quelled half a month ago; Her Majesty the Queen suppressed the rebel army of ten thousand with only a small force and executed the rebel leader, Grand Duke Ofrey.”
“However, while we focus on Her Majesty's achievements, we must not forget the greatest contributor to this war—the legendary Elgin Sword Master.”
“Lord Elgin Sword Master reached a true reconciliation with the royal family and also assisted the royal family in winning this seemingly unwinnable war.”
“According to insiders, Elgin Sword Master single-handedly slew several strongmen of the allied legions, playing a crucial role in the victory.”
“Therefore, behind me today will be a parade personally planned by Her Majesty the Queen to showcase Elgin Sword Master's wartime achievements.”
“At that time, we will be able to witness with our own eyes this imperial hero who has long remained hidden in the shadows…”
The unscrupulous reporter Bella was explaining the situation to everyone, but the roaring cheers were deafening, forcing her to speak loudly, her throat almost smoking.
In the crowd, someone led a small donkey over, seemingly also coming to see Elgin Sword Master.
She had a slender, lovely figure, a dazzling silver hair that shone brightly, though her face bore a heavy sorrow, making people hesitant to approach.
If she weren't walking with her head down, she would probably attract many onlookers' wooden pipes?
Since Merlin left over a month ago, Alice has been feeling like she's sitting on pins and needles at home every day.
She can't sleep at night, can't eat, and this has almost become her normal state.
Look at her figure; over the past month she seems to have lost a whole circle, her mind filled with where Merlin went.
Although Alice doesn't say it out loud, her inner sense of loss is still unbearable for her.
Having grown accustomed to Merlin's presence, his sudden disappearance without a word always makes Alice feel heartbroken, as if she's been used up and tossed aside.
Even though Merlin told Alice to just stay home and wait, she still couldn't bear her inner anxiety and panic, went out alone to find Merlin, hoping to drag that heartless guy back home.
According to Merlin's note, he seems to have come to the Imperial Capital to find a rich woman, so Alice rode her little donkey Mengmeng straight here, wanting to try her luck, hoping to bump into Merlin.
However, along the way Alice heard that Elgin Sword Master would hold a grand parade in the Imperial Capital, and it's not a fake—it's the genuine Sword Master.
Alice couldn't help but feel moved, deciding to swing by to see her idol male god, anyway Merlin might also be in the Imperial Capital, so it wouldn't waste time.
However, Alice's attitude toward Elgin Sword Master has changed a lot since she realized she likes Merlin; she no longer has any other thoughts about the Sword Master, and probably just admires him purely.
Alice led her little donkey forward, looking left and right, wondering why Elgin Sword Master hasn't arrived yet—has the parade not started?
At that moment, the crowd's cheers suddenly rose a few decibels, the sound wave changed everything, and the grand parade began—
The heavy gates of the royal palace were slowly pulled open by a few soldiers, and a procession of several thousand people marched out of the palace, walking straight down the central avenue.
Merlin stood at the front of the parade; when he appeared before the public, over a hundred cannons fired in succession, booming throughout the royal capital.
Such high-level treatment is only given when receiving foreign dignitaries, showing how high Elgin Sword Master's status is.
Merlin wore a polite smile, occasionally waving to the crowds on both sides to express his goodwill.
The crowd's cheers grew even more excited; flowers were tossed high into the air, and applause rolled like thunder across the sky.
They shouted hoarsely Elgin Sword Master's name, reaching out, imagining they could touch him.
Probably the most enthusiastic were the fan association in the crowd, who unfurled long banners reading “Elgin Sword Master, we? you!”
This fan association seemed mostly female; they usually looked elegant, but now they've turned into fierce women, baring teeth and claws, wanting to rush forward and hug Elgin Sword Master.
Just look at the scratches on the faces of the soldiers maintaining order—you can tell how tough it is to deal with these people.
A bead of cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead; he thought, “Women are really troublesome. If they catch me, I might be eaten down to the bone.”
Although Merlin's mind was full of complaints, he still politely waved at those fierce women, purely out of professionalism.
As a result, many pampered young ladies fainted happily, lost in thought, probably having sweet dreams.
Merlin unconsciously quickened his pace, wanting to finish this meaningless parade quickly and then leave this place of right and wrong.
However, after taking just two steps, Merlin stumbled, nearly falling flat on his face, because he saw his home's shrew—
“I go!”
“No way!”
“How did Alice come here?”
“Wasn't she supposed to stay home and wait for me?”
Σ(っ°Д°;)っ

title: Chapter 61 — Slap in the Face
content:
Chapter 61 — Slap in the Face

Volume 12 · Chapter 61

Merlin never expected Alice to come here, thinking this guy should be well-behaved and obedient, staying quietly at home to cultivate.

Coming out to look was one thing, but actually killing all the way to the imperial capital... it caught him somewhat off guard.

Merlin felt a bit of regret now. If he had known this would happen, he wouldn't have told Alice that he ran to the imperial capital.

The dense crowds on both sides reacted strangely when they saw Elkin, the great sword hero, and began to exclaim, chattering away non-stop.

Hobbs, who was accompanying him on the side, sensed that something was amiss. He hurried forward and whispered, "Great sword hero, is something the matter?"

"Cough!" Merlin gave a light cough, disguising his embarrassment and awkwardness, and vaguely responded, "No, I'm just not feeling well."

.......

A cold sweat trickled from Hobbs's forehead. He thought Elkin, the great sword hero, was a veteran who had seen it all, yet he turned out to be so bashful.

So Hobbs smiled, wanting to calm Elkin down, after all, this parade wasn't just to promote Elkin's merits, but also to show other empires.

"Great sword hero, there's no need to be tense. If you're too tense, it might cause trouble. Just take it as a stroll."

"Got it, I know. Let's go." Merlin nodded and continued the grand parade, his eyes occasionally glancing at Alice, who was isolated on the other side.

Alice seemed to notice that Elkin was a bit off. After seeing her, she seemed to be moved—at least, that's how it felt, giving off a strange vibe.

But that's not the main point. Alice's focus was on her idol, and she was excited throughout, never stopping her applause.

However, the more Alice looked at Elkin, the more he seemed like the unscrupulous Merlin at home, with similar build and temperament.

If Alice didn't know how vastly different their qualities were—one an evil Demon Lord, the other a hero representing justice—it would have been impossible for them to be the same person.

Likely, Alice would bite the bullet and insist that Merlin was Elkin, definitely not running away. There was no need to take off the mask to look, because the two shared many similarities.

After all, Alice had long since recognized herself; the person she liked was this bastard Merlin. She had basically given up on Elkin.

Merlin glanced at the excited Alice in the crowd and couldn't help but touch his chin. The bad water in his stomach suddenly churned.

If I think about it, Elkin's identity as a great sword hero isn't Alice's idol, maybe?

Perhaps she isn't looking for me, but came to spectate Elkin.

Damn it, why do I always get overshadowed by my own silhouette?

If I suddenly disappeared, would Alice not worry?

No, this is a rare opportunity; I must not miss the chance to tease her once.

Cool hehe~

Merlin stopped walking, his eyes locking directly on Alice, planning to take this opportunity of the grand parade to tease her good next time.

"Hmm?" Alice was stunned, her clapping motion froze. She thought strangely? Why is Elkin great sword hero staring at me? Does she have something impolite? !

"Great sword hero, what's the matter?" Chapman saw Elkin suddenly stop and was very puzzled inside.

Merlin said nothing but signaled Chapman not to talk too much.

This made Chapman suddenly blank, not knowing what Elkin great sword hero was trying to do in the middle of the road?

Merlin turned his head and walked up to Alice, looking at her with meaningful eyes, a hint of a smile but not speaking.

Alice's breath stagnated, repelled by Elkin's aura, and she instinctively took a step back, thinking—

.. .this. this. . . what's this situation! ? Why is Elkin great sword hero coming after me! ?

Does she have some unique quality that attracts him? Could it be... because of my face and figure... and so on.

Speaking of which, why does the great sword hero smile look so much like our dead ghost, a bit hateful.

Alice's heart was suspicious, and she unconsciously became tense, completely unclear about the situation.

"...... What are you going to do?

Merlin looked at Alice's nervous and somewhat restrained reaction and almost laughed out loud.

He thought, wow, this bitch, she never speaks like this at home; if she doesn't agree with something, she curses at me non-stop.

Now it's good, facing her idol, her whole person changed, cautious like a modest girl. Indeed, the power of an idol is limitless~

However, all these illusions are useless to me; even if Alice wears clothes, I know she has a few moles on her body!

Don't pretend to be a literary girl like that; everyone knows you're a willful, unreasonable shrew!

?

Merlin inwardly harshly criticized Alice for pretending to be literary, said nothing, but used a very lewd motion to stroke, lifting Alice's pointed chin.

"Huh! ?" Alice's face was lifted up, her face slightly red, and her eyes looking at Elkin were filled with something incredible.

Merlin became more and more pleased, thinking, yoyo, her face is red, clearly Alice this person likes Elkin, towards me she would never do this, feeling it's time to talk to Alice.

Alice's whole body went stiff, being moved by Elkin's action and at a loss, her heart suddenly beat a few beats faster—

Sure enough! This person has other intentions towards me!

Why did she choose me? No! I need to calm down!

I just admire Elkin, it's definitely not like...

Alice frowned, and with a slap, she slapped Elkin's lewd hand away, delivering a crisp slap to his face.

The onlookers and guards were all dumbfounded; no one stepped forward to stop it. Whoever looked at it would think Elkin the great sword hero was openly molesting a beautiful girl.

The originally thunderous applause stopped abruptly, replaced by dead... silence...

Alice slapped Elkin and felt a bit regretful, feeling she was too impulsive. "Sorry, .--- I have someone I like."

Merlin was just about to speak but was stopped by the slap, his whole body dazed. He touched his numb face, looking at Alice with utter disbelief. In his life, no one dared to slap him, Alice was the first.

Although all this happened under unknowing circumstances, it still made Merlin feel unprecedentedly shocked.

"However, I am very grateful that you once saved me in Elkin. I hope you won't forget your original intention; I will always silently support you." Alice's heart was in a mess, barely managing a smile, then turned and led the little donkey away, gradually disappearing into the crowd.

Merlin watched Alice leave, not saying a word throughout, because he was stunned by Alice's slap and forgot to communicate with her.

The onlookers began to whisper amongst themselves, discussing the just now commotion, with polarized opinions—some said Elkin the great sword hero molested women, while others said Elkin demonstrated love and was rejected, how pitiful.

Chapman felt tremendous pressure. Elkin's arbitrary actions had somewhat deviated from the plan, which wasn't a good omen.

So Chapman hurriedly walked up to Elkin, his expression somewhat anxious, and low said.

"Great sword hero, . . . are you alright?

"Ah, . . . Merlin came to his senses, rubbing his face, clearly internally chaotic.

Alice's slap left Merlin completely bewildered, not knowing what she was thinking?

". If you have such thoughts, you can tell me, I can take you to the biggest place in the imperial capital. You shouldn't make a mistake at this time.

Chapman said with a head full of sweat, fearing that this grand parade would be ruined.

"Tsk! Thinking what? I just . . . looked at . . . the girl just now was familiar... Merlin said vaguely, though his face didn't show much fluctuation, his heart was somewhat uneasy.

Resolutely slapping my ear? !

Isn't this girl's idol me! ?

By rights, seeing me should be heart-fluttering and throwing herself at me, right?

How could it be so abnormal, slapping my ear? Truly hard to understand.

Speaking of which, if Alice doesn't like Elkin, then who would it be... (u - .)?

Dark and damp mountain cave.

The faint sound of flowing water bubbling.

SF.

Moist rock walls covered in green moss; droplets condensed on the ceiling occasionally fall on the stones, making a " patter" sound.

In such a dark and silent space, one always feels creepy and uneasy.

The dim torchlight flickered, barely able to see a few scenes.....

In the center of the mountain cave, there sat a woman with a graceful figure, her back to the outside.

Her white skin shone with luster; her naked shoulders were as beautiful as ivory sculptures.

She wore a gorgeous black evening dress, the skirt spread all over the ground, emitting a faint fluorescence.

A strand of pink long hair cascaded down, atop her head was a crown, everything looked extremely coordinated. But curiously, the woman's back had twelve pairs of black wings, and a huge exaggerated demon horn grew on her head, like ram horns curving. Besides that, this absolute Demon Lord level!

A hunched old man suddenly appeared at the cave entrance, kneeling on one knee, speaking respectfully.

"Your Majesty, the prince has been expelled from the demon race by the parliament, and now it seems he is wandering in human territory; I can no longer collect his news. The First Demon Lord Palace is now controlled by the little princess.

This mysterious woman fell silent, and a mature female voice rang out in the cave, "Everything is within my expectations; there's no need to be alarmed.

"However... the elder hesitated, his voice hoarse, "Sending the prince to wander in human territory is always extremely dangerous. Are our plans moving too slowly?

"To deal with the impending calamity, I must touch the power of the deities; otherwise, it's hard to cope with this calamity. As for Merlin

+ Two-winged fallen angel of Demon Lord level hesitated for a moment, responding lightly—

"Since he can reclaim his throne, it proves his power has gained other monarchs' recognition; don't worry about his safety.

"I have always believed my son is the best, and I still firmly believe this at present.

* ToBeued

Afterword

Let's talk about the situation, it's not that I update less, it's just that I'm too busy now.

My old book needs to be rushed to the conclusion; the second volume's plot has reached a rather critical point.

There are many pits accumulated beforehand that need to be sorted out, and I must draw a relatively complete outline timeline.

Otherwise, this book is easy to write chaotically, write messily.

Today the group members should know, I sorted out the pits from beginning to end, busy with a forehead full of sweat.

So a bit slower, to ensure no problems later.

As for those who stir up trouble at every turn, I'm too lazy to deal with them.

My old book has suffered from stirrers and spammers, so I don't want to be hurried.

Asking is useless; I will definitely follow my own pace.

At this stage, I must sort out some things, roughly just these matters...

title: Chapter 1 — Return
content:
Chapter 1 — Return

Volume 13 · Chapter 1

Morning.

The blood-red sun rose over the horizon, bathing the peaceful town of Leicester in sunlight.

The townspeople left their homes and began their day-long labor, with the market becoming the busiest place.

News of the suppression of the rebellion spread throughout the streets and alleys, finally bringing the brief war and turmoil to an end and restoring peace to the British Empire.

The experts who had predicted the royal family's defeat before the war were all proven wrong, and to ease their embarrassment, they hastily explained that it was all because of Sir Ergen's sword prowess, and if not for him, the royal family's rule would have ended long ago.

Sir Ergen's feat of holding back the chaos was also widely praised, and for his resistance against ten thousand united forces, it was almost impossible for people to imagine.

Many people thought that Sir Ergen might be a reincarnated deity, since such impossible miracles always seemed to follow him around.

Sir Ergen's name had been deeply engraved in the hearts of the people of the British Empire, and his image would probably appear in history books someday.

Not to mention exaggeration, even other empires had heard of Sir Ergen's deeds, completely changing the stories that bards used to sing.

Bards had previously sung about the scandalous love between the Demon Lord and the Hero, which made many people happy to listen, but now they needed to add another tale about Sir Ergen's heroism.

Sir Ergen's attire also became a model for many people, and sword stalls selling the same style as the sword master could be seen all over the street.

On the way back, Merlin had been mistaken for a fan of Sir Ergen many times, the reason being that the red scabbard sword at his waist was too similar to Sir Ergen's.

Merlin couldn't help but feel a deep sense of regret, his distinctive features having been stripped away completely, and wondered if it was sick for him to be a fan of Sir Ergen and fall in love with himself? ?

Merlin was thinking about whether to dye his sword black to avoid causing trouble.

By this time, the streets of Leicester had become less crowded, and the refugees who had been seen everywhere had all returned to their homelands one after another.

Captain of the town defense squad, Pluss, took a deep breath. Although he was extremely fond of Sir Ergen's female fans, he also had to admit that this time it was thanks to their kindness.....

At home.

Alice woke up early, cleaned the house from top to bottom.

Merlin wasn't there, and she always felt her mind wasn't fully present when doing things. These days her memory wasn't very good either, and even her cultivation had become completely unmotivated, remaining at a level that could hold her own against the Thornbush Rider, probably around the middle of the Saint tier.

Actually, Alice's rate of strength improvement had already become terrifying, almost growing without any hindrance, and if she were to say it out loud, it would probably scare a large number of people.

This was all thanks to the inheritance crystal of the Frost Dragon, continuously and silently providing power, subtly strengthening Alice, making her strength grow like a sailboat with the wind, fast enough to be called a light novel.

However, Alice's utilization rate of the inheritance crystal's power was still only 25%, and further improvement might bring other changes.

This time, in the imperial capital, Alice gained nothing at all, not only did she not find Merlin, but it seemed like she was also harassed by Sir Ergen.

This made Alice feel completely confused, and her mood was quite gloomy.

Although being harassed by her ideal image might not be too bad of a thing, but Alice didn't like Sir Ergen, and being harassed made her heart unable to calm down, feeling some repulsion.

Alice was making breakfast, a simple soup and bread, staring at the boiling water for a long time, then instinctively turning around to look at Merlin's doghouse, which is where Merlin slept, thinking:

Won't he come back today?

What's the matter, why can't he tell me where he went?

In theory, Merlin couldn't leave me behind, after all, there's still the common debt between us, and it seems like he doesn't want to go back to his family in the demon race.

Is it the career disease of the cowboy, making the rich woman a horse to ride, using his body to exchange money?

Damn it! Rich women are no good! ?

I'll become a rich woman eventually, and make this bastard high and mighty, and use money to hit him until he licks my shoes with his tongue, hah!

Merlin has no idea about Alice's "grand ambitions"

At this moment, he had already arrived at his home, standing at the door, hesitating whether to go in.

Merlin stood at the door, touching his chin in thought.

Previously being hit by Alice, he didn't really care, after all, he didn't know who he was, and getting harassed by strangers would make anyone angry.

Merlin thought that since Alice went to the capital to find him, it was probably because she was too worried, and it was easy to see from her appearance that she had become a bit thin, and he had indeed gone too far.

Merlin regretted leaving only a letter for Alice and leaving without saying goodbye, there were some things that really needed to be said clearly face to face.

Now Merlin had some strange feelings in his heart, like a child who had done something wrong, feeling too scared to enter the house.

Merlin felt this wasn't a good sign, wondering what Alice might do? A mere lieutenant general, wanting to overturn the world?

However, Merlin thought to himself that he was at fault first, and being too arrogant might make Alice even more dissatisfied, so he took a little consideration of her feelings.

Merlin took a deep breath, showing an expression of wanting to have a blood battle to the death with this righteous little hero, and opened the door and walked in.

"Hiccup! A great sound from the sky, I'll make a grand entrance!"

Merlin's devilish ideas were very simple, as long as the skin was thick enough, nothing would get through, wanting to use his own passion to cover up the awkwardness, and finally smiling to forget everything.

However, the facts were not so simple, Alice's reaction was extremely cold...

On the stove, the soup on the pot was bubbling, Alice wearing an apron, holding a spoon, staring at Merlin with a blank expression, the atmosphere fell into a dead silence.

The water on the stove was boiling, Alice wearing an apron, holding a spoon, staring at Merlin with a blank expression, the atmosphere fell into a dead silence.

My goodness! He actually came back! Not a dream, right?

Alice pulled back her gaze, not expecting Merlin to come back so suddenly, although she was excited inside, she didn't know what to say on her mouth.

"What the hell? How old are you, still acting cute? Be mature."

"....Merlin was immediately hit, feeling unbalanced in his heart, reminding in a warning tone, "Hey, hey, I'm back, you didn't even say a welcome word?"

Alice glanced at Merlin, her face had no expression at all, showing a coldness, "Oh."

Merlin wiped the sweat off his forehead with his hand, feeling confused in his heart, being defeated by Alice's cold reaction, thinking that since she went to the capital so worried to find him, why did she react like this? Shouldn't she be overjoyed and ecstatic by now...

Alice was diligently making her soup, her face cold and her small mouth drooping, showing a look of "don't come near me", but in fact, she had already been smiling inside her heart--

This guy finally came back.

He's been a bit good...

Happy~

title: Chapter 2 — Past Sins
content:
Chapter 2 — Past Sins

Volume 13 · Chapter 2

Merlin's expression grew complicated. Alice's reaction was completely different from what he had imagined.

In Merlin's impression, Alice should have been a particularly persistent person, likely someone who couldn't tolerate even the smallest transgression.

Her突然 leaving without a word for over a month was, by any measure, quite excessive. She should have been making him answer for it.

But Alice's reaction left Merlin thoroughly surprised. It was somewhat difficult for him to accept.

To be honest, Merlin had already prepared himself for being interrogated by Alice. It turned out that wasn't necessary after all. Alice seemed not to care about the matter at all.

"Alice, I left without saying goodbye for over a month. Give me some kind of reaction, okay?"

"What kind of reaction were you expecting?" Alice turned her head to look at him.

"Any reaction would do. Don't be like now, so completely calm it's unnatural," Merlin set down his luggage and spread his hands. "The way you're acting right now is making me incredibly uneasy. Really, I feel uneasy. It's like... like facing a venomous snake. It seems quiet, but there's always the risk of being bitten at any moment."

Hearing Merlin's comparison, Alice immediately rolled her eyes. She set down the spoon in her hand and responded, huffing with annoyance.

"I see. So in your eyes, you're treating me like a venomous snake you want to avoid at all costs? Which eye of yours makes me look like a venomous snake? No one has ever evaluated me like that before!"

"Don't suddenly throw a tantrum, okay? I'm just making an analogy," Merlin replied awkwardly.

"You're clearly insulting me. Everyone calls me a little angel; only you treat me like a venomous snake." Alice shot Merlin a sharp glare. "Tch... heartless..."

"... Merlin was at a loss for words. A bead of cold sweat rolled down his forehead. He thought he was just making an analogy. Why was Alice being so serious about this?

"Fine then. If I'm a venomous snake, isn't it dangerous for you to stay with me? Then pack your things and leave quickly. This house was rented by me anyway, hmph!" Alice's attitude was arrogant and brash. She looked entirely unbothered.

"Hey, are you out of your mind? Kick me out the moment I get back? That's completely unrighteous," Merlin frowned.

"I never reason with devils, hmph!" Alice snorted, her little nose curling up toward the ceiling.

"Don't misunderstand. I didn't mean to insult you. You're simply acting abnormally right now." Merlin responded quite seriously.

"How am I abnormal? Clearly, it's your eyes that have the problem."

Despite not hiding it, Alice still harbored some resentment toward Merlin for not explaining things to her and leaving on his own for so long.

So although Alice didn't say it outright, she would subtly and implicitly poke at Merlin with sarcasm. Only then would she feel a bit more balanced inside.

"I was gone for over a month, and now that I've finally come back, can't you give me some kind of reaction?" Merlin narrowed his eyes.

"What reaction should I give? Do you want me to wave banners and shout loudly to welcome you back?" Alice pouted, her face full of disdain.

"That's not necessary. Based on your personality, you should have been digging into my whereabouts. Maybe even writing me a self-criticism letter or something," Merlin shrugged.

"Why do you see me as such a harsh person?" Alice said dissatisfiedly.

"Because that's exactly what you are, miss. Please have a bit of self-awareness. Even when I go out drinking with Hobbes, you question me from every angle. I disappearing without a word for over a month—how could you possibly let that slide?" Merlin paused, then asked tentatively, "Aren't you about to tie me to a chair and torture me for information, forcing me to confess everything I did during that month and a half?"

.....

Alice clearly wavered. From the look on her face, she seemed somewhat tempted.

Alice had indeed thought about using a forceful attitude to dig into everything, but it simply wasn't realistic. Torture required her to be far stronger than Merlin; otherwise, there would be zero deterrence.

Alice was well aware of the vast gap in power between them. There was nothing she could do about that guy. She might as well wash up and go to sleep. Everything was possible in dreams.

"I... I don't want to know where you were messing around! What does it have to do with me? I have no interest in your private life!"

Alice said this lie without even blushing or catching her breath. Though her words claimed disinterest, inside she was extremely concerned and eagerly looking forward to Merlin confessing everything honestly.

If Merlin deliberately hid the truth, Alice would have absolutely no way to handle it and would have to drop the matter.

"Huh?!" Merlin slightly widened his eyes, feeling a trace of surprise. This didn't seem like Alice's usual demeanor. "You really don't want to know what I did during that month and a half? You have absolutely no interest at all?"

"....."

Alice wavered again. Seeing Merlin's grinning face, resentment welled up inside her heart.

She felt like she was always being led by the nose by Merlin, and this guy always seemed to see through her inner thoughts.

How could Alice not care about what Merlin had been doing? She was just too embarrassed to cling persistently and ask, as if she were being petty and meddling too much, which would only breed resentment.

She and Merlin were only sharing a living space, not truly husband and wife in any meaningful sense. Being too controlling about certain matters wouldn't be appropriate.

Actually, during this period, Alice had reflected on herself properly. She wondered if she had been too demanding of Merlin, always wanting to enter his world and mold him into her ideal version of him.

Perhaps it was precisely because of her overly aggressive mindset that Merlin felt some resentment toward her, which ultimately led to his sudden departure without explanation.

This worried Alice considerably. Recalling what Merlin had said, she felt that although the two of them were now cohabiting, personal space was still necessary.

After all, everyone has secrets they don't wish to share with others. Merlin had them, and naturally, so did Alice. Being overly aggressive would certainly cause dissatisfaction.

So Alice's attitude had changed significantly. Instead of interrogating Merlin relentlessly, she chose a much gentler approach.

"No interest. I don't want to know. If you wanted to tell me, you probably would have said it already, right?"

Merlin's brow furrowed tightly. He wondered what had happened to Alice. In the past, she would have pointed at his nose and shouted "confess and receive leniency, resist and face severe punishment." How had she suddenly evolved into a zen-like girl?

"I... well..." Alice's eyes wandered. She mumbled and shifted her tone. "If you insist on saying it, I can reluctantly listen. Of course, this isn't because I want to know—that's not why I'm saying it!"

..... Merlin gave a dry chuckle, slightly relieved. After going in circles, she still wanted to know after all. As expected, Alice was still the same old Alice.

"Act... actually, there does seem to be something I need to....." Alice's expression twisted纠结.

"Ask away. It's fine." Merlin nodded, as if he had been expecting this all along.

"Have you... re...." Alice hesitated. Two red blushes rose to her cheeks. She asked in a low voice, "Have you resumed your old profession?... starting that flesh-selling trade again?"

..... Merlin's face went completely expressionless. The whole person seemed utterly hopeless and lifeless—

"Silence, Alice."

"You dare defame my character."

"Hurry up and stop those filthy delusions in your head."
