title: Chapter 3 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Extra Update
content:
Chapter 3 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Extra Update

Volume 13 · Chapter 3

“You haven't gone back to your old line of work, have you?” Alice looked surprised, thinking that the letter had said he was going to the capital to find a rich woman—so wasn't that just picking up his old trade again? Sure enough, compared to being an adventurer, this guy Merlin preferred getting pampered and living off women.

“Are you calling me back to my old line of work? Don’t treat me like some shameless guy, okay? Or are you saying that in your eyes, I’m just some guy with no standards or aspirations?” Merlin frowned, emphasizing that he was a man with ideals and pursuits, and wouldn’t stoop to returning to his old ways.

Alice thought it over carefully, recalling Merlin’s usual lethargic demeanor, and nodded seriously. “Well, based on your past behavior, I think there’s a good chance you’ve secretly returned to your old line of work. After all, that kind of job makes way more money than being an adventurer.”

“Get lost, you—say what you mean…”

Merlin rolled his eyes and his face darkened. He was especially averse to his own embarrassing past, and having Alice rip off that scab again was just too cruel.

Although working as a bartender in a tavern wasn’t really what Merlin had intended, who could say they’d never hit hard times? This was just a last resort.

Getting pampered by rich women for money, or working hard when broke—both were normal operations.

Even though Merlin was very reluctant to bring up his own embarrassing history, Alice kept bringing it up, intentionally or not, making him extremely uncomfortable.

“What exactly did I do to make you think I’ve gone back to my old line of work?”

“Didn’t your letter say you were going to the capital to find a rich woman? Besides going back to your old line of work, what else could you be doing?” Alice thought Merlin didn’t seem to have any other notable skills besides using sweet talk to swindle money.

“Finding a rich woman is going back to my old line of work? Can’t you keep your thoughts pure? We’re just negotiating a business deal.” Merlin said with exaggerated seriousness.

“Business deal?” Alice narrowed her eyes, her expression turning odd, with a meaningful look. “Emmmmmm…”

“What kind of face are you making? Are you thinking something inappropriate?” Merlin looked at Alice with a strange gaze. “I never expected that you, a former great Hero, would look so proper and dignified on the surface, but really… pfft.”

“I…” Alice was blushing from Merlin’s teasing and quickly tried to defend herself. “Where am I thinking something inappropriate? I’m warning you, don’t make false accusations against me!”

“Who’s making false accusations? Look at that expression of yours, clearly corrupted by bad influences—you must be thinking of physical transactions. It’s terrible how even the Hero has become so unserious these days.” Merlin seized the moral high ground and furiously condemned Alice’s depraved thoughts.

Alice’s face was burning red, and she couldn’t help but get angry. “This is so annoying! It’s all because of you, you’ve never been serious, so I can’t even think about you normally! You didn’t say anything from the start, just left me a letter and ran off to find a rich woman. A man and a woman alone… what kind of proper business deal could that be?!”

Merlin heard the resentment in Alice’s tone and realized she had probably been wanting to complain about this all along but just hadn’t had the chance.

Now that the opportunity had come, Alice had injured herself out of anger, and she could finally vent her frustration instead of keeping it bottled up.

“Alice, you’re too biased against me. I’m a demon, and for us, transactions are sacred. How did it become something so dirty in your mouth?”

“Enough already! I’ve heard that line about demons considering transactions sacred way too many times…” Alice put down her spoon, turned off the stove fire, and walked over to Merlin. “A former bartender who survived by pleasing women, and a middle-aged woman with money to burn, desperate as she is—how could anything proper come from the two of you being together? Get real!”

“Yet the facts are that it really was just a normal transaction. I only needed to temporarily help maintain the rich woman’s status, and she could help us pay off the Church’s debts, making us free people. Do you understand what I mean?”

Merlin said mysteriously, not intending to tell Alice exactly what he had done in the capital, but instead speaking in a more indirect way about his journey.

Because Merlin deeply knew that Alice would find it hard to believe he was actually Elkin the Great Swordsman, and if he revealed the truth, Alice might tease him for being dramatic and mock him mercilessly.

“…Alice suddenly looked puzzled and asked, ‘Is all of this true? That rich woman can help us solve the debt crisis? She doesn’t have any other ulterior motives, right?’ Alice tentatively asked, ‘So you went to the capital this time purely on official business. Even if you left without saying goodbye, she would understand. But if it’s for some other reason…’ Her heart felt a little more at ease. If Merlin harbored any evil thoughts, that would be completely unforgivable.”

“That’s right.” Merlin nodded seriously, though it felt somewhat unreal. “Aren’t we already free people now? Has the Church’s debt been paid off?”

“Then…” Alice thought for a moment, feeling that the situation wasn’t that simple; there were still things Merlin was responsible for. Merlin’s expression was troubled, his brows knitted in worry.

“Although I also hope things go smoothly, but the reality is…” His tone was meaningful. Alice frowned, not understanding what Merlin meant.

“Huh? What does this have to do with me? I just helped maintain that rich woman’s status, but when it came time to collect the payment, I was…”

“Let me explain it to you. Although I did help out quite a bit this time, I still haven’t received what I’m owed. I won’t accept any credit or deferred payment. I want my share paid in full, upfront.” He placed the weapon on the table, the threat of force clearly implied. The sudden, brazen move made her nervous, and the air grew thick with tension.

Merlin saw Elkin the Great Swordsman actually showing up.

The tension in the air was palpable. The guy, Merlin, had no choice but to take things seriously, his hand unconsciously moving to his waist.

Facing Elkin the Great Swordsman, who was soaring above everyone else in strength.

“Insolent fool! Daring to threaten the Queen!”

The suggestion was for Meadsfield to calm down.

“Winston, calm down.” Queen Elizabeth restrained herself, but under the pressure, she had no choice but to loosen her grip on the sword at her waist, respectfully standing guard beside her.

Meadsfield broke into a cold sweat, realizing he was up against his own interests. Of course, it wasn’t impossible to negotiate… Queen Elizabeth hesitated slightly, speaking in an extremely calm tone. “Since Master Elkin is so eager to receive his payment…”

“If you could return my personal belongings that were stolen from me, I’d be willing to discuss terms. But this involves my dignity, to be honest…”

(∞)

title: Chapter 4 — Deviant
content:
Chapter 4 — Deviant

Volume 13 · Chapter 4

Hearing Queen Elizabeth's request, Merlin couldn't help but feel a bit stuck, somewhat at a loss.

After all, Elizabeth's demand was perfectly reasonable—those undergarments definitely had to be returned.

Otherwise, as the empress of an empire, she'd always feel like she'd been robbed of her lingerie.

Besides, Merlin wasn't some fetishist. Even if he did nothing, just holding onto them would invite suspicion.

But the main problem Merlin faced was—

Elizabeth's stockings had already been shredded to pieces by Alice, that spendthrift!

Now she's asking Merlin to return them? Impossible! They're gone, gone for good!

Yet the chance to escape that enormous debt was right in front of him—why give up such a golden opportunity? Merlin really didn't want to let it go easily.

Beside him, Mesfield listened, half-comprehending, but she understood clearly enough: the Great Swordsman Elgin, that pervert, had robbed the queen of her intimate apparel. That was an enormous humiliation!

Elizabeth was the empire's supreme ruler, and now she'd been robbed of her undergarments by Elgin the Great Swordsman—imagine the rumors! Elgin the Great Swordsman was indeed a pervert. Not only did he like spitting on women, but he also had the sick fetish of collecting women's clothing. Disgusting to the extreme!

"You great swordsman, you wretched bastard! Just what have you done to Her Majesty?! I'll fight you!!!"

Mesfield could bear it no longer. She drew the long sword from her waist, ready to go down with Elgin the Great Swordsman in a mutual kill.

"Hm?" Merlin lifted his eyelid slightly and said calmly, "I didn't do anything. I just took one of the queen's stockings. Don't get so worked up. Whoever doesn't know would think I had a blood feud with you."

"...You pervert!" Mesfield cursed, veins throbbing on her forehead. "Have you been doing filthy things behind everyone's back using the mistress's belongings?!"

"Hehe, what filthy things could I possibly do? You go ahead and describe them~" Merlin leaned back in his chair, looking utterly at ease.

Mesfield's face flushed crimson. Unable to say it outright, she muttered, "...How would I know what kind of pervert does in private?!"

Elizabeth felt awkward, sensing the argument was making her lose face. "Calm down, Windsor. Sheath your sword. This isn't how a lady of your standing should behave."

"Your Majesty! This bastard has committed an unforgivable crime! We can never show mercy to such a vile, shameless wretch!" Mesfield gritted her teeth.

"Windsor, this is between the Great Swordsman and me. Don't be so sensitive. I know exactly how to handle it." Queen Elizabeth said seriously.

"But, Your Majesty—" Mesfield wanted to protest further, but seeing Elizabeth's stern gaze, she had no choice but to back down. She sheathed her sword, sulked beside her, and kept bombarding Merlin with telepathic attacks.

"So, Great Swordsman," Elizabeth steered the conversation back on track. "I've already made my position clear. What exactly is your intention?"

Actually, Elizabeth was betting that Merlin wouldn't return the stockings—she'd asked for them back multiple times before, and Merlin always dodged the topic, giving no indication he intended to return them.

Elizabeth had vaguely sensed something. Before, Merlin had emphasized he wasn't a fetishist, and now that they weren't enemies, the stockings should rightfully be returned to her.

But Merlin's reaction was unreasonable. There was probably only one explanation—Merlin had likely lost the stockings.

So Elizabeth seized on that possibility. She wasn't refusing to pay, but she could stall as long as possible. At the very least, the empire needed time to recover.

Merlin hesitated. The stockings were impossible to return, but he didn't want to abandon this golden opportunity.

He thought it over and decided to buy a replacement pair. Stockings were basically the same anyway—there shouldn't be much difference.

As long as he could fool them, he could say goodbye to that crushing debt. It was worth the risk!

Merlin feigned calmness, speaking with an air of total confidence.

"Fine. You just need to prepare the money. I'll return your belongings tomorrow—"

But the next day—

"Here—" Merlin placed a pair of white stockings identical to Elizabeth's, neatly folded, in front of her. "I think Your Majesty has nothing left to say now, right?"

"This..." Elizabeth stared at the stockings before her. A cold drop of sweat formed on her forehead. She felt immense pressure. She never expected Elgin the Great Swordsman would actually return something like this. Now she was in an awkward spot.

Merlin flashed a triumphant smile. He felt this was solid. Elizabeth surely couldn't find an excuse now.

"Is this... Her Majesty's stockings? Don't try to fool us with fakes!" Mesfield said cautiously. Her intuition told her Elgin the Great Swordsman wasn't someone easy to trick. Would a pervert really return his hard-won stockings so meekly? That was highly abnormal.

"...Of course it's real. Why would I use fakes to trick you?" Merlin appeared composed on the surface, but inside he was panicking like crazy.

Mesfield grew suspicious. She picked up the white stockings from the table and, right in front of Elizabeth, held them up to her nose and sniffed.

Elizabeth saw Mesfield's action and felt her face burn with embarrassment. As the queen, her dignity was on the verge of collapse. She blushed and whispered, "Windsor, what are you doing? Don't make strange gestures in public..."

Mesfield said nothing. She sniffed the stockings, frowning, sensing something was off.

Merlin's tension spiked. *No way? Can that female knight actually sniff something out?*

No—stay calm. She shouldn't be able to smell anything. As a knight, how would she be so familiar with the queen's scent?

Merlin put on a serious expression, trying to project an air of unshakeable calm to confuse his opponent.

Mesfield raised her head and threw the white stockings onto the table. "This stocking isn't the queen's at all! You actually tried to deceive us with this thing! Shameless!"

Elizabeth's heart jolted. She shot Merlin a helpless look. "Great Swordsman, that's really too lacking in sincerity."

"Nonsense!" Merlin straightened his back, speaking righteously. "On what grounds do you call it fake? I warn you, don't make baseless accusations!"

"There's absolutely no scent of the queen on this. How dare you claim it's the one you took? Are you trying to fool us?!" Mesfield stated decisively.

"Why can you sniff out the queen's scent like some old hand at this?!" Merlin's eyes went wide, a chill running through him. It seemed he'd discovered a shocking secret—

*I always felt this female knight gave off weird vibes.*

Turns out, I'm the fake one...

*This female knight is the one with improper intentions toward the queen!*

(。口。)

title: Chapter 5 — Pretty Good
content:
Chapter 5 — Pretty Good

Volume 13 · Chapter 5

Elizabeth regarded Mesfilfield with a strange look. Though Merlin's banter was irrelevant, something still felt off.

Mesfilfield looked like a cat whose tail had been stepped on, his face turning red at a visible speed. "...-I know what's going on, don't change the subject! The problem now is you're deceiving us with fakes!"

"This, ah..." Merlin scratched his cheek with a finger, putting on an air of calm. "It's just a pair of stockings, isn't it? What does it matter if the queen wore them?"

"It matters a lot!" Mesfilfield knitted his brows, speaking with hostility. "Who knows what you're doing with the monarch's personal items?! This is a matter of dignity!"

"No need to make such a fuss. I don't have that kind of twisted taste. Even if I spat on you a few times, you really don't need to take it this far, do you?" Merlin spread his hands.

"You bastard..." Mesfilfield was grinding his teeth in anger, his mind filled with thoughts of perishing together with Elkin the Great Swordsman.

"Lord Elkin, since you have no particular perversions, why not return what you stole from me?" Elizabeth seemed to have sensed something.

"I don't want to return it, so I won't. There's no particular reason." Merlin said casually, thinking, Of course I don't want to return it. Didn't Alice tear up and throw away the stockings?

"That's truly unfortunate."

Elizabeth lowered her head. Though Merlin didn't say it outright, she could guess about seven or eight parts of it.

"What do you mean by 'unfortunate'? You don't want to sweep this under the rug, do you? Let me say this upfront—I don't like doing useless things..." Merlin was tired of hiding it, so he decided to come clean with Elizabeth.

"Since you can't return my things, I naturally can't fulfill my promise right away. Moreover, when I made the agreement with you earlier, I never specified a time for fulfillment." Queen Elizabeth said, both emotionally and logically.

"Hey! You're being too much. I hate doing business with people who have no credit..." Merlin slowly stood up from the chair, looking ready to fight.

"What are you doing?! " Mesfilfield was in high spirits, striking a sword-drawing pose.

"Please calm down. If we have differences, we can discuss them. The best approach is to find a mutually beneficial area and achieve a win-win situation." Although Elizabeth's face wore a smile, a bead of sweat slid down her forehead.

"I just want to get back what's rightfully mine. Is that too much to ask?" Merlin shrugged.

"But the debts you're carrying are simply too enormous—over 97 million gold coins. That's not a small amount. In any country, it couldn't be paid off just by opening one's mouth." Elizabeth had to reveal some facts.

...Mesfilfield instinctively sucked in a cold breath, staring at Elkin the Great Swordsman with a face full of shock, thinking, What on earth did this man do? How could he owe that much money? It's unbelievable!

Merlin didn't speak, but inwardly felt awkward, thinking, Good grief, don't say the specific numbers out loud. Every time I hear it, I feel like I'm dying inside.

Fairy Tale

"With the British Empire's financial strength, helping you repay the debt would take at least 20 years even if we did nothing. Even if I wanted to keep my promise, I'd fall short. Besides, the empire needs reconstruction now, and money is needed everywhere." Elizabeth's tone was full of helplessness.

Merlin thought, I owe that much money, and Elizabeth paying it all off in one go is indeed a bit much to show. After all, a country's productive capacity is limited—it's not a printing press.

"So what do you want to do? Let me say this upfront, but I definitely won't be a free laborer."

"Since I promised to help you repay the debt, I won't go back on my word. Your debt will be handled by us royals. We'll intervene, but it requires installment payments—it can't be paid off all at once. Besides, our royal family has good relations with the Holy Church. I've had many private exchanges with the Pope, and I can say a few good words. Your debt pressure will be greatly reduced, and perhaps you won't even need to repay such a huge amount." Elizabeth expressed her thoughts. Though it wasn't that she didn't want to repay, she was currently short on funds.

Merlin thought it over carefully and found that Elizabeth's offer was indeed tempting. Not only did she promise to help repay the debt, but she would also help negotiate with the Holy Church. With the queen's prestige, there would surely be some discount.

He wasn't stupid enough to pressure someone to death over debts. Given Elizabeth's current abilities, repaying the debt was almost impossible.

Merlin recalled the debt collectors of the real world, who were very cautious about pressuring people to death—not out of fear of trouble, but because when someone dies, who would the money be collected from?

It would become a case of the dead having no one to settle accounts with, leaving only bad luck. It was better to keep people alive, occasionally squeezing out some blood.

Anyone who wants to kill someone for not repaying money is either crazy or just a stubborn idiot...

"Well, it's not that I can't accept it, but I need a deadline. What if you keep delaying indefinitely?"

"Thirty years. Within thirty years, I will definitely fulfill my promise and help you escape from the heavy debt." Queen Elizabeth responded seriously.

Merlin lowered his head, putting on a thoughtful expression. "By the way, Princess Michelle still owes me money."

"Since you calculate so clearly, I won't be polite then. During the Elkin incident, you sank fifty imperial warships. Each ship costs 30,000 gold, totaling 150,000 gold. I'll offset that against what Princess Michelle owes you. As for the rest, I'll consider it a favor for helping suppress the rebellion. What do you think?" Elizabeth calculated carefully.

Merlin pursed his lips, looking at Elizabeth, and suddenly had a face full of black lines, cursing a dirty word in his heart—

WRNMM.....

"That's how it is."

Merlin put away his memories, not directly saying who the other party was, but expressing his meaning in a very indirect way.

"You really stole someone's stockings?! That's so disgusting! I'm becoming more and more disappointed!" Alice jabbed her finger hard into Merlin's chest, not knowing how to rant anymore. "You must have some unspeakable perversions. You can tell me if you want..."

"What do you want to tell me?" Merlin frowned.

"You know it yourself! Perverted demon!" Alice blushed, scolding angrily.

"Who's the pervert? The situation was complicated at the time. I didn't steal it because of some perversion." Merlin said seriously, emphasizing one point. "Besides, it's all your fault for being impulsive. If you hadn't torn that rich woman's stockings, we'd already be free. Why didn't I stop you back then? Now I'm full of regret."

"You're lying. Just because I tore one pair of stockings, all those tens of millions went down the drain? That's possible! Don't make up a story and pin the blame on me. I won't fall for that! Hmph~!" Alice puffed out her cheeks, looking like a hurt pufferfish.

Merlin's brows knit together. He wondered when he had made up a story. There was no need for that. The failed payment was inseparable from Alice, this spendthrift.

"Actually... we still haven't cleared the debt... it's fine..." Alice muttered in a very small voice.

"Huh? What did you say?!" Merlin's eyes widened, thinking he had misheard.

"......". Alice shook her head, looking down, blushing and saying nothing.

If we hadn't owed so much money, we probably wouldn't have had any reason to be together.

This guy probably left long ago. Nothing could hold him back.

It's fine like this now, although it's a bit hard. But at least he can stay by my side...

title: Chapter 6 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 6 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 13 · Chapter 6

Actually, Alice understood Merlin's rather terrible personality quite well — when trouble unrelated to him appeared, he either played dead or pretended not to see it.

If it weren't for the debts piling up, and creditors chasing him everywhere except demon territory, that guy Merlin would have run off long ago.

He'd stay obediently by Alice's side? Not a chance. He'd have gone off to live carefree somewhere else ages ago.

That's why Alice felt that being burdened with massive debt wasn't necessarily a bad thing — at least she got to be with Merlin every day.

Now Alice wasn't like she was at first, frantically anxious to repay the debt. Taking it slow was actually pretty nice.

If Alice and Merlin really became free people, whether they could continue living together was truly an unknown.

Merlin looked at Alice, deep in thought, and felt this guy must be crazy. She actually said the current situation was pretty good — truly incomprehensible.

Alice's face reddened but she didn't speak, feeling both indignant and embarrassed. She broke the silence: "In other words, you went out for over a month and accomplished nothing, came back empty-handed?"

"..... Although I don't want to admit it, the facts seem to be exactly that." A drop of cold sweat appeared on Merlin's forehead.

"Then all that talk you gave was the same as saying nothing at all?" Alice's delicate brows furrowed high, speaking helplessly, "I feel like everything you said before was fake. Maybe you spent this whole month fooling around and made up a huge lie to deceive me."

Merlin rolled his eyes, asking dissatisfied, "Miss, which of your eyes saw me tell a lie?"

"The gold coins we owe aren't something ordinary people can help repay at all. And just because I tore that pair of stockings, the opportunity fell through. However you think about it... it feels fake, right?" Alice felt Merlin's story had too many holes — it simply didn't hold water.

"Do you know who that wealthy woman is? She's the richest woman in this empire." Merlin countered.

"Who?" Alice narrowed her eyes. The richest in the empire should be the ruler. "Could it be Queen Elizabeth?"

Merlin snapped his fingers, dead serious: "Smart. Didn't expect you to guess right. Your intuition's pretty sharp."

Alice's expression shifted from calm to suspicion, finally full of disdain. She looked Merlin up and down with her eyes: "Just you—"

"What about me?" Merlin grew puzzled, wondering if he'd said something strangely wrong.

"Forget it. The empire's queen is high and mighty — how could she possibly have anything to do with you? Daydreaming isn't shameful, but taking dreams for reality is a bit much." Alice shook her head, feeling Merlin had lost his sense of place lately, always saying things that were obviously lies at first glance.

"...." Merlin gave a dry laugh, thinking: as expected. In Alice's eyes, my ceiling is very low — impossible to have any connection with big shots. Good thing I didn't tell the truth just now, or who knows how much this stinky woman would mock me.

"If there's something you don't want to say, just don't say it. I'm not forcing you, so why fabricate outrageous things to deceive me?" Alice huffed and turned her head away, face red: "As long as you're willing to come back... I actually don't care about anything else..."

"Hm?" Merlin narrowed his eyes, catching a whiff of that sour stench of romance. "Hey, you rookie Hero — are you **?"

"Ah?! Wh-what... what 'in love'! I'm not! You... don't talk nonsense!" Alice exploded like a cat whose tail got stepped on.

"Your words were too ambiguous, made me misunderstand a little..." Merlin stroked his chin, looking thoughtful.

"What's there to misunderstand? You're the one thinking crooked. I only... only said that because you didn't come back, I couldn't go out to work here. Couple adventurers are supposed to be together!" Alice racked her brains for an excuse.

"Is... that so..." Merlin frowned and nodded seriously, thinking: someone as principled as Alice could never harbor illusions about a demon like me.

"Honestly, don't just casually misunderstand me. You're the one who likes to ** casually, you demon. Hmph~!" Alice turned toward the stove, grumbling at Merlin's back: "Hurry up and pack your things. Perfect timing for dinner, then accompany me to train."

Merlin was just taking off his coat. Hearing Alice's words, dissatisfaction instantly rose: "Are you kidding? I just got back and you're already making me accompany you. Got any humanity? Don't I need to rest...."

"Just being my sparring partner, won't make you exert much effort." Alice opened the simmering pot and picked up the spoon.

"But you're too weak. Being your sparring partner is completely meaningless. I'd fall asleep while fighting." Merlin resisted a little. He'd finally returned and his mind was full of nothing but rest.

"Ah?! Know your limits! Falling asleep while fighting? I may not beat you, but I'm not weak to that extent!" Alice defended herself very seriously.

"When you frequently fight little kids, you gradually become numb to victory. No motivation at all. Even winning gives zero sense of accomplishment. You get what I mean?" Merlin's words sounded tactful, but every word hit the mark.

"Who's a little kid?! Your arrogant attitude is truly annoying! Ah, I've had it. I regret it. You'd be better off not coming back!" Alice spat out a spiteful line.

"Tsk! I've only been back for how long and you're already sick of me. Truly heartless~" Merlin said with a complex expression.

"Who made your mouth so vicious?" Alice said angrily.

"Fine. I'll accompany you for four hours. Not a minute more." Merlin said ungraciously.

"Enough. I feel like I'm about to break through. There's a trend approaching Saint-tier peak." Alice suddenly said.

"Ah? How long since you reached Saint-tier? Breaking through this fast? Did you do special training while I was gone for over a month?" Merlin asked curiously.

"Nope. I just stayed home normally....." Alice answered blankly.

"......" Merlin thought carefully. Maybe it was the Inheritance Crystal's doing?

As long as Alice hadn't fully digested this thing, it could continuously supply her power, imperceptibly raising her strength.

Like someone was pulling her running nonstop, making her cultivate with a rocket booster strapped to her back — how could her strength not grow fast?

But Merlin speculated: once the Inheritance Crystal was completely digested by Alice, it would probably return to normal.

"Here!" Alice ladled a bowl of soup for Merlin, placed it before him: "Eat up. You look like you haven't eaten yet?"

Merlin looked down — it was actually his favorite food. "Impressive. Braised beef with potatoes. What a coincidence, it's my favorite. You didn't make this on purpose, did you?"

"Mm."

A faint blush rose on both of Alice's cheeks. She hesitated, stammering.

Actually, these past few days Alice had been cooking two portions — just waiting for Merlin to return.

And knowing he liked braised beef with potatoes, Alice's menu had been very monotonous lately.

But with Alice's personality, she could never admit she'd prepared it specially. Instead she'd say—

".... What are you joking about?!"

"I'd never specially prepare anything for you!"

"This is just a coincidence. Put away your disgusting delusions!"

"If you keep this up, I... I won't want to talk to you anymore, hmph~!"

(.--.)

title: Chapter 7 — Legacy
content:
Chapter 7 — Legacy

Volume 13 · Chapter 7

Beyond the waters of the Britannia Empire, there lies an unknown small island. This is a secret stronghold of one of the Four Great Dark Guilds, the Azure Ghostflame.

After the老牌 Dark Guild Howling Demon's Praise was completely wiped out, the Dark Guilds had gradually fallen into a three-way standoff.

Howling Demon's Praise's territory was ruthlessly carved up and occupied by the other Dark Guilds, making the fragile balance of power increasingly precarious.

The remaining three Dark Guilds had all begun a quiet but frenzied campaign of external expansion, their ambitions to unify all Dark Guilds gradually surfacing.

The Deep Cold Gaze, the Phoenix, and the Azure Ghostflame were the three largest Dark Guilds, and after Howling Demon's Praise disappeared entirely, they chose to swallow up smaller guilds, continuously expanding their own strength.

This war in the shadows had grown increasingly intense, and it was certain that the three Dark Guilds would eventually determine a winner, birthing an emperor to rule the dark side.

But for now, during this period of standoff and cold war, everyone was still exercising restraint, because none of them had the ability to completely devour the others.

However, the current balance being shattered was only a matter of time. All three Dark Guilds were seeking breakthroughs in power, wanting to swallow the rest entirely.

Among the three remaining Dark Guilds, the Phoenix held a slight lead with the strongest influence. After continuously swallowing several Dark Guilds, its scale had become the largest.

But the Deep Cold Gaze and the Azure Ghostflame were not about to show weakness either. Though they were at a slight disadvantage when confronting the Phoenix, neither of them was a soft target. As long as they gained access to more powerful strength, crushing the Phoenix was not impossible.

The Azure Ghostflame had no fewer than five Saint-tier powerhouses, including the guild master Humphrey, making it a formidable force among the Dark Guilds, second only to the Phoenix in terms of strong personnel.

Don't be fooled by the fact that Howling Demon's Praise was only four people and still counted as one of the Four Great Dark Guilds — all four of them were Saint-tier powerhouses.

Among the Dark Guilds, strength was measured by how many Saint-tier powerhouses one had. The more, the stronger.

So if Howling Demon's Praise hadn't declined, they would likely have been able to contend with the other Dark Guilds as well.

Azure Ghostflame's guild master Humphrey bore the nickname the Crazy Butcher, a result of his eccentric personality and his mind often being in a frenzied state — in short, he was something of a madman.

He held an intense worship for slaughter, referring to the act of killing as "purification" — purifying the world's trash and waste, making things infinitely more beautiful.

So he regarded slaughter as an ordinary matter, and was somewhat obsessed with this pathological behavior. The number of people who had died under his hands was, by estimation, beyond counting.

Humphrey's strength was at the peak of the Saint-tier, and he was a middle-aged man with sunken eye sockets and a slightly gloomy demeanor, constantly exuding an aura of bloody scent.

At this moment, on this small island, the Azure Ghostflame was holding a secret meeting in the conference hall, hoping to make plans for the guild's future.

"Our guild is at a very critical period. If anything goes wrong right now, or if we simply stand still and stop expanding our influence, we'll soon be left far behind by the other two guilds, unable to continue bearing the pressure from the Phoenix. In the end, we'll either submit or be single-handedly slaughtered. According to the intelligence we just received, the Phoenix has already acquired seven Saint-tier powerhouses. The Deep Cold Gaze has even purchased twenty magical artillery cannons and discovered a secret method for controlling magical beasts, dramatically boosting its strength. If this continues, our situation will be extremely dire. We must strengthen the guild's power immediately to avoid becoming someone else's prey."

The speaker was named Eden, a Saint-tier magician who served as the Azure Ghostflame's strategist, more like a strict steward handling all matters big and small within the guild.

The Azure Ghostflame's achievements today were inseparable from Eden's efforts and his decisions on important matters. Through steady and solid management, they had reached this point.

"Has the situation really become this severe? Wasn't it just a short while ago that you said our strength surpassed the Deep Cold Gaze's?" asked Laure, a Saint-tier martial artist, in surprise.

"That was a month ago. Right now, everyone is expanding their forces. Our pace has lagged far behind. If this continues, we'll eventually be eliminated." Eden said helplessly.

"We don't need to worry about the Deep Cold Gaze, right? We're allies, aren't we?" said Oswald, a Saint-tier archer, in a detached tone.

"The Deep Cold Gaze consists of nothing but wolves and tigers. They can't be trusted at all. They've been eyeing us for a long time. If it weren't for the Phoenix's overwhelming strength, they'd have made a move against us long ago." Eden analyzed seriously.

"The idiots from the Deep Cold Gaze want to oppose us? Let them weigh their own worth first. Aren't they afraid that my sister and I will slice their guild master's head off?"

"Sister is right. The Deep Cold Gaze are all cowards who bully the weak and cower before the strong. Do they really think they can compete with our Azure Ghostflame? That's nothing but foolish dreaming."

Two very similar delicate voices rang out, their tone full of enchantment. Judging solely by sound, one might mistake them for a single person speaking.

Eden raised his head and looked toward the main seat at the conference table. Two figures with fiery figures, clad in revealing red clothing, stood out — their exceptionally full breasts bouncing beneath the silk fabric, their vivid red lips looking extraordinarily alluring.

These two were Saint-tier assassins named Yuna and Vina. They were twin sisters who had been subdued by Humphrey and became his women.

At this moment, Humphrey sat at the main seat, his arms wrapped around Yuna and Vina's slender waists, embracing them on both sides in a simply delightful pose.

"You two little foxes, your mouths are sweeter than usual, haha..."

Humphrey appeared unrestrained, causing the two sisters beside him to become a wave of bashful shyness.

"Guild master, this isn't a joke. Our current situation is truly dire. If things continue like this, being swallowed by one of the other two guilds is only a matter of time." Eden frowned, his tone very serious.

"Surely you're not raising false alarms here, are you?" Vina teased.

"Yeah, we're one of the Four Great Dark Guilds with deep foundations. Anyone trying to swallow us would pay a price beyond imagination." A disdainful smile appeared on Yuna's face.

"This concerns our very survival. There's no room for carelessness. You two should also take this seriously." Eden's expression was cold.

"Eden, I understand your feelings, but there's no need to be so tense. Since the Deep Cold Gaze and the Phoenix are eagerly expanding their strength, we naturally cannot fall behind." Humphrey gave a sinister smile.

"Does the guild master already have a plan?" Eden asked in confusion.

"It's that thing. We just obtained a clue not long ago..." Humphrey released the twin sisters and lazily leaned back on the sofa.

"The legacy of Count Dracula."

"That is a legendary top-tier vampire, an existence that neither ages nor dies, known as the Bloody Impaler."

"What he left behind — without a doubt, it must be a rare treasure. It would be perfect for our use."

title: Chapter 8 — VIP (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 8 — VIP (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 13 · Chapter 8

Fighter Laurie, hearing President Humphrey's words, instantly swept away his previous dejection, sat up straight, and curiously asked, “Dracula's heritage? What is that?”
You don't even know that? Legend says Dracula is the first vampire in history, the oldest existence of the blood clan, it's said to be the ancestors of vampires. Archer Oswald seemed to know this, chatting with Laurie, “It is said that in ancient times, Dracula was a count of the Holy Roman Empire, he was brave and warlike, liked to impale enemies on wooden stakes; this cruel method made enemies terrified, until Dracula betrayed the Goddess of Light and was cursed, thereafter he gained the immortal blood clan power, accompanied by a thirst for blood.”
Um, hearing that sounds kinda weird, I've never even seen a vampire.... Fighter Laurie said embarrassedly.
I've heard that vampires are all descendants of Dracula, and vampires themselves exist between humans and the undead; even if they stand before you, it's hard to tell with the naked eye. Oswald, hugging a bear, proudly boasted about his knowledge.
"...So that's how it is...." Laurie felt a bead of cold sweat trickle down his forehead.
It's pretty much what Oswald said—Dracula possesses immortal bloodline power and abundant wealth; as long as we can obtain his heritage, what are the Deep Sea Eye and Phoenix? In front of us they're just petty clowns. Humphrey said with a cold smile, as if he looked down on the Deep Sea Eye and Phoenix; in terms of standing in the dark guild world, those two are far behind.
What the president says is right—no wonder he's the man both I and my sister favor. Yuna leaned her head on Humphrey's shoulder.
When the president shows his righteous vigor, he's even more charming than usual. Vina reached out and touched Humphrey's chin.
Hahaha, you two aren't just sweet‑talking, are you trying to cheer me up? Humphrey, embracing both of them, even when laughing couldn't hide the gloom on his face.
President, that clue came from a drunkard we met; its reliability is limited—who knows if that drunkard was lying? Eden frowned, feeling things weren't as easy as imagined, and after recalling something continued, “Besides, legend says Count Dracula was killed by a vampire hunter; as for where he was buried? That remains a mystery to this day.”
I certainly know the uncertainties, but I just love a sure‑profit deal. Humphrey chuckled.
But President— “Don't say it, Eden, I'm the president.” Eden wanted to say something but was cut off by Humphrey. Seeing the president's stern gaze, Eden fell silent; if he kept talking, he might risk his life. Eden had followed Humphrey for a long time, feeling the president was like a lunatic; when unhappy, his companions would show no mercy and kill.
No matter what, we've seized the opportunity; Dracula's inheritance is rich, and it could very well bring our guild unprecedented prosperity, so regardless of whether this clue is true, we have the necessity to investigate. Humphrey stated his stance, thereby settling the matter.
"........" Eden nodded, even though he felt it unreliable in his heart, he didn't dare speak—who would dare defy the president, that murderous maniac? "But do we need to mobilize the whole guild to infiltrate Great Britain to look for clues?"
No need to mobilize so many forces; it would alarm the royal family. However, I heard the British Empire recently experienced internal turmoil, so its defenses should be weak; we only need to send two people to investigate. Humphrey turned his gaze to Laurie and Oswald, nodded and said—
Then this task is yours two; I look forward to your good news....
Rexham.
These past few days Merlin has been observing Alice; from their sparring, it's clear her strength is rapidly increasing.
Alice being able to defeat the Thorn Knight is the best proof, although she herself also suffered a rather embarrassing serious injury.
But it's obvious that Alice's power level is already close to that of the Thorn Knight, even to the point of being on par.
According to Merlin's speculation, Alice hasn't been lying; she truly is nearing the peak of the Saint-tier, and the inheritance crystal within her seems to be approaching 50% utilization.
Merlin felt that Alice hadn't done anything special, yet her strength surged like a rocket, improving incredibly fast—indeed the dragon clan's inheritance crystal is a miraculous treasure capable of transforming one's very being.
At this moment in the Adventurers Guild, everyone is busy as usual, except for two idle people—
"Merlin, I'm begging you, can you stop coming to bother me for no reason?" Hobbs said, his eyes brimming with tears.
"Why?" Merlin set down his cup and looked at Hobbs.
"You come to me for drinks, never spending a penny; I'm about to be drunk into poverty by you." Hobbs said, somewhat frantically, feeling Merlin was being unreasonable.
"Don't worry about these details; friends drinking ahead of time isn't that hurtful to feelings, right?" Merlin raised his cup, smiling, "Cheers to our friendship~"
"Hold on a moment." Hobbs put on a serious expression, pressed down Merlin's raised cup, "Have you been betting on horses lately?"
"Isn't the Royal Horse Racing Track closed? After all, the queen is in crisis." Merlin asked strangely.
"It's not really related to the queen; the Royal Horse Racing Track, though Queen Elizabeth holds some shares, is actually controlled by the Rothschild family—they are the world's largest consortium, their wealth even slightly surpasses that of the Knights Templar; due to internal strife in the empire, fearing looting by rebels, they temporarily shut it down." Hobbs explained in a sentence.
So that's how it is.... Merlin furrowed his brows, only then realizing the Royal Horse Racing Track belongs to the Rothschild family—no wonder it's found worldwide; it turns out business has grown to this extent.
The Rothschild family's influence is enormous, having penetrated nearly every empire except the non‑human races; even banks have their involvement, let alone the frenzy‑money‑sucking Royal Horse Racing Track.
Rumor has it that this super‑powerful family controls over 50% of the world's wealth, and they are even creditors to many imperial rulers—looking at them, they are like emperors lurking in the world's shadows.
Speaking of which, Merlin is still a diamond‑tier guest of the Rothschild family; when he enters expensive venues, he apparently receives top‑tier treatment.
If Hobbs hadn't brought it up today, Merlin wouldn't have remembered this matter; long ago, Rothschild family personnel had informed him, congratulating him on becoming the first ever diamond‑tier guest.
But back then Merlin had just lost everything, feeling low‑spirited, and didn't pay much attention to it; he soon forgot.
As for the reason, Merlin poured tens of millions of gold coins into that family; not enjoying some special treatment—what kind of person would that be?!
"Speaking of which, I'm still a diamond‑tier guest of the Rothschild family."
"Pfft!" Hobbs spat out a mouthful of old blood, clutching his chest, his whole body shocked as if struck by lightning.
"...You... what did you just say?!"
"Diamond guest—"

title: Chapter 9 — Worry
content:
Chapter 9 — Worry

Volume 13 · Chapter 9

Here's a translation that follows all the rules:

<<<BEGIN TRANSLATION>>>
Merlin glanced at Hobbs with a faint smile, "What kind of reaction is this?

Hobbs set down his wine glass, pointed at Merlin, and said seriously, "How on earth could you be a diamond patron of the Rothschild family?

"Really, lying about something like this is pointless," Merlin shrugged his shoulders.

"Alright, stop joking. I discovered that you, Merlin, have no other special hobbies—you're just too fond of daydreaming," Hobbs paused, smiling, "The Rothschild family? That's an existence that can loom over all human empires with a single hand. Being called an invisible emperor is no exaggeration. They control the economic lifelines of most empires. Not blowing my own horn, but even Queen Elizabeth has borrowed money from their family.

"And then?" Merlin said calmly, seemingly not very interested in this family, since he himself had become a diamond patron with several tens of millions of gold coins, and yet he still wants to reasonably get them back? That's basically impossible.

"Then I beg you to keep both feet on the ground, our imperial queen isn't a diamond patron of the Rothschild family, so how could you be?" Hobbs couldn't believe Merlin was so capable, and continued, "Diamond patrons are the Rothschild family's most sincere friends. They receive special favors, and even the family's privileges are opened up to them. Just imagine the family's massive power—if you were a diamond patron, I don't think you should be appearing in the impoverished adventurer's guild, but rather living a life of luxury in high society."

Merlin looked at Hobbs without speaking, but thought to himself that not long ago, when he had Alice's inherited hero armor, he was practically a tycoon, and he had indeed enjoyed himself in high society. But good times didn't last long; soon he became poor again. Just a small play.

Thinking about it, besides Alice standing a bit farther back, it was largely thanks to that armor's protection that she could survive under Merlin's blade. This shows just how terrifying its defense is. Such an expensive item isn't strange at all.

That inherited armor, which has been worn by generations of heroes, is extremely difficult to forge. It requires a complete chunk of top-grade mithril and has been blessed by the goddess's favor, already approaching the level of a divine artifact.

"Moreover, the conditions for becoming a diamond patron are extremely stringent. The required amount of gold is astronomical. Where on earth do you get so much money?" Hobbs scrutinized Merlin from head to toe, feeling that this shabby-looking man has nothing to do with the words "rich beyond compare."

Merlin lifted his head, his gaze becoming hazy, as if he were a mature old man who had experienced many vicissitudes, "To be honest, once upon a time, I was also rich beyond compare~"

Hobbs smacked his lips and said in a tone of helplessness, "Just as Alice said, this guy's ego keeps coming up...

"Tch, Alice that little fool would understand anything," Merlin pursed his lips, thinking, well, I can't explain it to Hobbs. Poverty limits this guy's imagination.

"Alright, alright, you were a big tycoon before, I believe you," Hobbs didn't want to argue with Merlin anymore. He changed the subject and asked, "The royal horse racing field started operating again yesterday. What do you think? Any interest in having a go?"

"Yeah~ Could you lend me some? Alice that woman is restricting my wallet, making me feel so embarrassed..." Merlin said seriously.

A drop of cold sweat trickled down Hobbs's forehead, thinking that lending to Merlin is basically like a meat bun hitting a dog—once it's gone, it won't come back. So he suddenly changed his words, "I was just asking around. I think horse racing isn't a good habit; it should be condemned. So I also advise you to play less. Small gambling brings joy, large gambling harms the body~"

Merlin narrowed his eyes, surprised, "These words also came out of your mouth?

"Cough cough! This isn't the important..." Hobbs embarrassedly coughed a few times and changed the subject, "Didn't you spend a lot of money yesterday and buy a lot of horse racing tickets? You should have won quite a bit, saying you're bald this time wouldn't be acceptable.'

Merlin recalled spending Alice's small fortune on horse racing tickets, and responded awkwardly, "Such a pity, letting you anticipate it for nothing..."

"....No way!" Hobbs widened his eyes, looking at Merlin's expression and guessing the gist. He couldn't help but think, with so many horse racing tickets, not one hit! This can't be described as just bad luck anymore! It's almost as if the goddess of luck has cursed him! A man abandoned by the gods, how pitiful......"

"Yo! Hobbs, Merlin old brother!" Karl, holding a wine glass, grinned and walked over.

"Oh? Karl, you're already back?" Hobbs felt slightly surprised.

"Back not long ago." Karl smiled and answered.

Actually, just two days ago, Karl had completed his task and returned. Today he saw Hobbs and Merlin chatting idly here, so he came over.

Karl is very optimistic about Merlin, thinking this guy will definitely shine in the future, so he particularly dotes on this super newcomer.

Whether the Rexham guild can flourish in the future depends on whether Merlin can make a name for himself in the adventurer's competition.

"Is it because you quarreled with Lucille? You feel whether you come back or not, she's the same, and your face has absolutely no joy of a father returning," Hobbs showed a meaningful look.

"You have to understand, my daughter is currently in a rebellious phase. She'll get better sooner or later," Karl showed a confident look.

Hobbs didn't say anything, thinking, who is Karl trying to fool? Lucille is already this old, and she's still in a rebellious phase? She's clearly entered early menopause, that's for sure.

Karl pretended not to see Hobbs's contemptuous gaze, and turned to chat with Merlin,

"Merlin old brother, how have you been recently?"

"Just getting by, I can only maintain my life by chatting with my mouth every day..." Merlin responded awkwardly, thinking, isn't Karl intentionally bringing up old wounds? He's been busy lately and hasn't gotten anything, he's just feeling gloomy.

"Unbelievable? Lucille said you and Alice went to the capital not long ago. At that time, the kingdom's situation was unstable. Taking this opportunity, you didn't make a fortune?" Karl felt it was unlikely, and joked, "Now you and your wife are already able to receive private commissions. You definitely haven't missed out on meeting big shots. We're all in the same line of work, so don't hide things from each other."

"Really didn't make any money? Look at what Alice is doing?" Merlin pouted, pointing them toward the quest notice board over there.

Hobbs and Karl looked in the same direction and saw Alice, graceful and upright, standing in front of the notice board, seriously selecting tasks.

Alice frowned, her face dark, supporting her chin with her hand, looking at the densely packed tasks on the notice board, unavoidably getting a headache.

She had been standing here for a long time, carefully checked all the tasks, and as a result, her gaze became increasingly gloomy, her face writing "impoverished"—

No longer suitable tasks to accept.

Either the reward is too low, or it looks too simple.

Not even an S-class task exists, it's simply unacceptable.

What to do?

Could it be that I can no longer afford this stinky man, Merlin! ?

title: Chapter 10 — Meeting
content:
Chapter 10 — Meeting

Volume 13 · Chapter 10

Karl and Hobbs withdrew their gaze, looking at Merlin awkwardly. Seeing the two of them so eager to take on a mission, it seemed these past few days really hadn't been going smoothly.

"Really? What exactly were you busy with in the imperial capital?" Hobbs had a slight bead of sweat on his forehead.

"It's not that there were no gains, it's just that they weren't particularly pleasing to the eye." Merlin showed a melancholic smile.

"It's fine, fine. You and Alice can now receive private tasks with generous rewards. In the future, it will definitely get better." Karl laughed and comforted Merlin—sentence, feeling he couldn't let his confidence take a hit, maybe something would go wrong.

Merlin said nothing, thinking Karl was right. In the future, Alice's reputation would only grow higher. When the time came, the money-grubbers wouldn't dare trample the threshold, would they?

"Moreover, the quests on the notice board are actually quite few, especially S-rank and above. This requires some luck, so don't be discouraged. Be patient, and you'll surely have gains." Karl spoke very politely.

"Yeah, look at Karl. His private commissions have never stopped; he's busy every day, and the clients are all prominent figures." Hobbs pointed to the side.

"Compared to Mr. Karl, we have no fame. Good tasks won't come looking for us." Merlin responded helplessly.

"Don't worry, it's just a matter of time before you two surpass me. If I'm not mistaken..." Karl turned back to look at Alice, narrowing his eyes and said, "Alice's strength seems to have grown again. I haven't been gone that long? I didn't expect you'd already grown to this extent. It won't take much time before you surpass me."

Seeing Alice grow so rapidly, Karl couldn't help but nod in satisfaction. Now the guild's strength had increased. The underground adventurer competition tournament was truly worth looking forward to. Maybe the best performance in history would appear.

"Really didn't expect Alice to turn from a carp into a dragon. When will I be able to leave the iron-ranked adventurer tier?" Hobbs couldn't help but sigh.

Merlin awkwardly smiled, thinking Hobbs really knew how to joke. If Hobbs could leave the iron tier, I would have already been purple gold by now.

"Our guild's situation is quite good. Alice's strength gets stronger every day. In the future, she will accomplish something. If Ralph also returns, the guild's powerhouses would be complete." Karl said with longing.

"By the way, Ralph, this fellow went out on a mission, and it seems it's been more than half a year since he returned? Could something have happened?" Hobbs frowned.

"Yeah, it's been a long time. But with Ralph's strength, there shouldn't be any major issues. If it's still silent after waiting a while, we must go look for him." Karl tightened his brows.

Merlin curiously lifted his head and asked curiously, "Who is Ralph?

"Huh? Didn't Alice tell you?" Hobbs strangely asked.

"No." Merlin shook his head blankly.

"Ralph, that is, another silver-ranked adventurer in our guild. He's been here for a long time, considered an old member, haha."

Karl laughed heartily, recalling, "That fellow has always treated me as a competitor, but he's always been unable to beat me."

Merlin recalled what Alice said: there were three powerhouses above Saint-tier in the guild. Originally, this Ralph was one of them. It's just that he had never seen him before.

It seems Alice couldn't find a suitable job for a while, so she walked back dejectedly, sitting beside Merlin.

"How was it?" Merlin asked tentatively.

Alice shook her head disappointedly, sighing, "Not good at all. There really wasn't anything suitable. Do you want to do brick-carrying work?

" Doing brick-carrying? I, my hall... Merlin instinctively wanted to say Great Demon King, but suddenly felt something was wrong and quickly changed his words, "I, the great Merlin, going to carry bricks is really embarrassing."

"There aren't any better jobs, though. Rent is due soon, and all sorts of expenses. We'll have to tighten our belts again, QAQ" Alice's mouth was wrinkled, looking like she had suffered a great grievance.

Merlin felt awkward, thinking he hadn't gambled recklessly either. How was money being spent so fast? Would he have to spend another period of waking up from sleep due to poverty?

"Everyone, long time no see!"

Arnold appeared at the guild at some time, cheering and greeting everyone. However, his arm was wrapped in bandages, apparently having taken some hits during the rebellion suppression war.

However, the good thing is that Arnold luckily survived. One must say, this guy's luck is really good.

"Arnold? You also returned?" Hobbs widened his eyes, adding impolitely, "I thought you would die, although you this guy are timid and useless, but you are a chosen one, ah."

"Hey, Hobbs, you old fellow, give me some face. I went to the battlefield for the family's honor, experiencing nine deaths out of ten on the battlefield. You're belittling me too much at this time." Arnold said seriously.

"Yeah, Hobbs, Arnold this guy is rarely brave. We should encourage him." Karl poked Hobbs beside him.

"Well, Arnold is really awesome!" Hobbs couldn't help but agree.

Arnold lifted his head, raising his nose to the sky. He didn't notice the sarcasm in Hobbs's words at all.

"Arnold, I heard you this time replaced someone in the army and went head-to-head with the allied forces? It's truly worthy of a second look. Previously, I still thought this was a fellow without backbone. Now it seems you are also an admirable man." Karl said seriously.

"That's right. Although he usually looks refined, for the family, I'm willing to shed my blood." Arnold spoke loftily when talking about it, completely forgetting his awkward state when encountering the Black Wolf Mercenary Group almost two times.

"Get lost. You're definitely the first one to run away, so you were lucky to survive. Don't say you're so great, okay?" Hobbs couldn't help but interrupt.

"Tsk tsk tsk! Hobbs, your prejudice against me is too great. Everyone has a brave side. I am an existence who stood on the battlefield until the last seconds. At that time, the famous Black Wolf Mercenary Group hacked over, and I and my knights bravely resisted until the end, although we ultimately ended in defeat, but we played an important role in dragging the allied forces' steps." Arnold raised his arm wrapped in bandages, proudly saying, "This injury is the most powerful proof against me, and also my merit medallion.

Everyone remained silent, quietly watching Arnold's performance. In fact, no one took his words seriously.

"Miss Alice, I finally saw you. Do you know how difficult this was?" Arnold walked toward Alice, his emotion very excited, as if he had a belly of bitter water.

Alice felt there were too many people around, in between her image engineer, embarrassed to swear.... what ah? "

"When I was almost dying on the battlefield, do you know what I was thinking?" Arnold's eyes were filled with deep affection.

Alice felt the people around her were a bit numerous, between her image engineer, embarrassed to swear.... what ah? "

"I was thinking that if I died, I would never see the beautiful Miss Alice again. This thought was like seeing firelight in despair, letting me persist under such恶劣 conditions. So I want to thank you. It was you who gave me a new life, giving me the courage to live on." Arnold said with his expression, not knowing if he was supposed to be singing some poetry here.

Hobbs and Karl got goosebumps, really unable to stand this guy Arnold, always saying mushy words without blushing or panting.

Alice expressionless, slowly stood up, and conveniently pulled Merlin, "Let's go home. There's a fly that can't be killed here, buzzing and annoying."

"Good... Merlin is also a bit tired, wants to go home and sleep."

The couple directly stood up and left, completely ignoring Arnold.

"Hey! ? Again ignoring me! ? Too much...." Arnold's face showed a big "awkward" character, saying embarrassedly

"Wait!

"Miss Alice, I have serious business!"

"My father wants to see you ah

title: Chapter 11 — The Mansion
content:
Chapter 11 — The Mansion

Volume 13 · Chapter 11

Hearing Arnold say that, both of them stopped in their tracks, feeling that there really seemed to be something serious going on.
Arnold's father is the Earl of Austin, the manager of the whole Rexham, and he seems to have a pretty good relationship with the elder Taylor.
As the lord of the town, he suddenly summoned Alice and Merlin, leaving both of them feeling puzzled.
“Lord Earl wants to see me? Why?” Alice frowned, looking puzzled.
“My father wants to see you, isn’t that obvious?” Arnold became a bit bashful, somewhat like a sissy.
“Huh?” Alice had a head full of question marks, not understanding what he meant.
“Ah~, I see, you’re here to meet the parents? To pursue Alice, your old man even rolled up his sleeves to help.” Merlin said with mild interest.
“What!?” Alice widened her eyes, unsure if Merlin was serious, feeling Arnold had evolved into a mama’s boy, and to harass her, the whole family had jumped in!
“Hahaha, as expected of Merlin, you figured it out at a glance.” Arnold suddenly got pumped up like he’d taken a stimulant, pointed at Alice and shouted passionately, “Exactly! Come to your senses, Miss Alice! You’re already the Austin family’s destined daughter‑in‑law; no matter how you argue, you can’t escape this fate. My father said that if you agree to marry me, he’ll accept any conditions. Come, Miss Alice, follow your heart and turn into my embrace! hiahiahiahia~”
Alice kept a straight face, listening to Arnold’s baboon‑like laughter, and instantly felt speechless.
So Alice turned around, grabbed Merlin, and completely ignored Arnold, that dimwit child.
“Let’s go, Arnold’s mind isn’t clear anymore; we shouldn’t stay here or we’ll get our IQ dragged down.”
“That’s right.” Merlin nodded and turned to leave.
Plop—
Arnold dropped to his knees on the spot, tears streaming down his face as he pleaded pitifully with Alice.
“Sorry, Miss Alice! It’s my fault! I shouldn’t have spoken nonsense! Please give me another chance!”
“My father never said those things; he just has something to discuss with you, as for the reason…”
“I’m still not clear about it either!!!”
◇
Late at night.
The moon rose into the bleak sky, a expanse of glittering whiteness.
The sky was dotted with stars, a rare fine weather with not a single cloud.
At that moment, the guest hall of the Earl’s mansion was brightly lit.
Candle after candle illuminated it as clearly as daytime.
The long, narrow table could easily seat twelve people, with flowers placed on it, their fragrance drifting slowly.
The crimson carpet was soft and comfortable; stepping on it gave a constant sensation of being massaged, making one marvel at how well the Earl knows how to enjoy life.
Many portraits hung on the walls, resembling Arnold somewhat; they must be the ancestors of the Austin family.
Normally, such an occasion should have only Alice and Arnold alone together, but an uninvited guest showed up—
“So… why did you also come along, Merlin? I didn’t invite you at all!”
Arnold jumped up in a frenzy, feeling terrible; he had originally thought this was a heaven‑sent opportunity to be alone with Alice and whisper sweet nothings.
As a result, Merlin’s shamelessness was so great he could fling the hardest shield several streets away, so thick it made one’s scalp tingle.
Arnold was utterly dissatisfied, feeling he could never get a chance, yet Merlin ruined it; as long as Merlin was there, how could Miss Alice possibly be interested in him!!!
“What’s wrong with me coming along? You’re making a big deal out of nothing.” Merlin said nonchalantly.
“I didn’t invite you! Why do you insist on coming?! This makes no sense!” Arnold’s expression grew gloomy to the point of tears—don’t even mention how stifled he felt inside.
Alice glanced sideways at Merlin, a tiny spark of expectation igniting in her heart, hoping Merlin would say she was his wife, making it natural for him to tag along; she couldn’t help but imagine a little scene—
「Merlin swept Alice into his arms, pointed at Arnold’s nose, and said in an overbearing tone, “I warn you, Arnold, don’t covet Alice—this guy is my woman; if you harass her again, don’t blame me for not being polite!」」
Alice’s eyes filled with tiny stars; she inwardly hoped Merlin would say something like that, which would make him seem especially charming.
Look at Alice day‑dreaming—just a cheesy Mary Sue little scene sends her into fantasies; she really has no ambition.
“I just saw it’s mealtime; popping over for a free meal isn’t bad, plus Alice and I are partners, so of course we should come together for anything—what’s the problem?” Merlin flashed a cheeky grin; he really did look like he was just here to mooch a meal.
“Uh!”
Alice nearly had Merlin’s words make her cough up blood; her face went from pale to white, and the Mary Sue day‑dream in her mind shattered into pieces.
Cough cough! Indeed, this is Merlin all right—how could an evil demon lord possibly care about me?
To actually fantasize that this jerk could get close to me—I’m really too naïve!
Merlin is still the same old guy; he’s not worth any expectation from me!
In his eyes, is my worth not even worth a meal?
Damn it! This unfaithful, heartless man—I’ll never harbor any illusions about this jerk again!
Alice calmed herself, then turned her gaze to Merlin, those widened little eyes brimming with anger.
“Uh, what’s that look of yours? Are you trying to kill me?” Merlin shrank back embarrassedly, big beads of sweat rolling down his forehead.
“Merlin! How can you do this!? You’re seriously looking down on Miss Alice!” Arnold frowned and sprang up from his chair.
Alice silently nodded in her heart, “Yeah, that’s good—let Arnold quickly educate Merlin, this clueless guy who doesn’t know how precious I am; how could I be equated with just a meal?”
“Since mooching a meal is your intention, I’ll treat you to ten meals—please leave Miss Alice and yield her to me!” Arnold said solemnly.
“Ar‑nold!” Alice gritted her teeth, her Saint‑tier battle aura erupting instantly, the room’s temperature plummeting; she thought, why is everyone else’s equivalent so noble, while I’m only worth ten bowls of rice!? You’re looking down on people!
“Y‑yes… sorry…” Arnold sat down, trembling on the spot, not daring to breathe loudly.
Creak—
The sound of the door opening rang out; Jenna peeked through the crack, her eyes like a hungry wolf, flashing a greedy green light, drool pouring out.
“Lord Merlin, hehehe…”
“Huh!?”
Merlin felt his heart skip, his spine go cold, and instantly noticed Jenna peeking from outside the door.
No way!? I actually ran into that masochistic pervert miss!? Do I have to be this unlucky!
Speaking of which, that look like a beggar seeing a drumstick—what’s that supposed to mean!? I’m a demon lord! Show some respect!
Hey hey! Don’t stare at me drooling! It’s about to drip into the crevice squeezed between my chest…!
Damn! Is this supposed to be a saliva‑wet‑temptation ploy!? What are these kids thinking these days!?
“Slurp~” Jenna sucked the long strand of saliva back in, looking satisfied.
Holy shit! Are you kidding me!?
She sucked the viscous stuff back again! Now it looks even more disgusting!!!

title: Chapter 12 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 12 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 13 · Chapter 12

Merlin felt that Jenna was practically not an Earthling; it would be more reliable for her to quickly roll back into outer space.
Indeed, being with a masochistic alien like Jenna, Merlin had no good way out, and felt uncomfortable.
It felt as if a super giant beast was staring at him; Merlin wondered to himself that he had never encountered a troublesome fellow like Jenna.
Alice also noticed Jenna drooling outside the door, her eyebrows furrowed, thinking she almost forgot that Jenna was the prized jewel of the Austin family and would definitely run into her here.
Seeing Jenna clearly showing affection toward Merlin, Alice felt uneasy and subconsciously became wary, to prevent this guy who enjoys romance novels and collecting experience from taking extreme actions toward Merlin.
“Oh? Jenna, you’re here? Why didn’t you come in?”
Arnold turned back to look, noticing his sister’s behavior was somewhat abnormal; she usually rushed in all carefree, but today she had suddenly become reserved?
Indeed, is it because of Merlin? I see, that girl is not in love; my sister is already at that age.
Just as my goal is Miss Alice, my sister’s goal is Merlin; perhaps we can take this opportunity to cooperate and achieve the accomplishment of staying together with Miss Alice.
Arnold smiled and nodded, feeling that with Jenna, the “love master,” by his side again today, things would become very smooth.
Jenna blushed, her heart racing with excitement; she had heard that her father would invite Alice over today, and she didn’t expect Merlin to be there.
Presumably all this is destiny’s choice, unbreakable! I and Merlin will inevitably become an enviable celestial couple.
After several repeated “coincidences,” who would still doubt that my destiny and Merlin’s were not intertwined?
I am so lucky, being favored by the divine; I don’t know how to repay.
It seems I must seize this opportunity, try to make the manly Merlin bow under my plum skirt, cool, huh?
Jenna’s eyes glittered with little stars; that look made her want to devour Merlin in one bite, completely unmasked.
A bead of sweat slid from Merlin’s forehead; it seemed like he should leave quickly, but leaving now would be rude?
“Cici.” Alice made a strange sound, wanting to talk to Merlin.
“Um? What are you doing?” Merlin replied softly.
“Look at Jenna’s eyes; she clearly wants to eat you, right? How do you feel now?” Alice probed.
“I already regret coming here; I want to leave quickly.” Merlin whispered.
Alice was somewhat satisfied with Merlin’s reaction, and seriously said, “Now is not the time; we have already promised to meet with Earl Austin, and leaving now would make the other party lose face. We will definitely eat this dinner.”
“So what do you want to do? I’ve been watched by a mother wolf all the time, this is not good. As my nominal wife, shouldn’t you do something?”
“Hum, now you know to ask me? What did you do early?” Alice snorted, angrily continued, “Arnold harasses me every day, but you never helped me?”
“.......”. Merlin frowned, suddenly at a loss for words.
“Then let’s cooperate; I’ll protect you, and you must protect me.” Alice proposed a condition.
Merlin thought for a moment, looked at Jenna’s wolfish eyes, and couldn’t help but nod, “Alright, I promise Arnold won’t bother you.”
Me… me… Alice got serious, solemnly promised, “With me here, I definitely won’t let…”
Both united against a common enemy, they temporarily formed an alliance, unaware that mutual care and protection between spouses is normal.
Jenna came to the dining table, saw that Arnold’s seat was better and close to Merlin, so she arrogantly said, “Wasteful brother, I’ve taken over this spot; no objections, don’t you hurry and step aside?”
“Ah?!” Arnold frowned, clearly unwilling, because this seat was close to Alice.
However, since Alice and Merlin are so close, Arnold had become a thorn in his sister’s eye, somewhat hindering, preventing Jenna from watching her male god.
“Ah, what? If you dare to appear within a radius of one meter, I’ll report you to my father, saying you are idle all the time; don’t you just leave?” Jenna pointed to the side, telling Arnold to get up and vacate.
“...... Arnold’s face flushed red, his whole body trembling, feeling that his sister was not giving him face in front of outsiders, so he shouted angrily, “Just leave!”
Jenna looked proudly at Arnold vacating the fengshui treasure, feeling happy.
We Austin family, Jenna’s status is higher than Arnold’s; after all, she is much smarter than her brother and wins the parents’ favor.
Arnold was somewhat foolish, always at a disadvantage, naturally lower status than his sister Jenna.
Merlin felt awkward, seeing Jenna’s haughty demeanor, he didn’t like it; too arrogant and disobedient, it would definitely exhaust people.
Actually, Merlin likes girls who are outwardly coquettish but inner gentle, especially caring, understanding, occasionally a bit temperamental; that’s his type.
Emm, isn’t that Alice? Perfectly fits Merlin’s preference for a girl with inner depth.
Jenna slowly sat down, showing a dignified, cultured appearance. “Merlin, I didn’t expect you would come; why didn’t you give me a heads‑up? If I had known you would come to our house, I would have dressed properly; appearing in casual clothes before you is too rude.”
Alice squinted, feeling that although Jenna was younger, she seemed to have some experience, so she launched a gentle attack.
Not good! I must give this girl a lesson, otherwise…
So Alice, before Merlin could speak, she immediately leaned onto Merlin’s shoulder like a small bird, appearing very affectionate with him.
Miss Jenna, don’t…
Miss Jenna, don’t worry; my husband and I never mind such trivial matters; besides, who are you dressing for? Merlin’s gaze has always been on me, he has no interest in other women.
Merlin stared blankly, seeing Alice so quickly get into the role, not too good…
Merlin smiled, then wrapped his arm around Alice’s fragrant shoulder…
“That’s right… my wife…”
