title: Chapter 13 — Language Blockage
content:
Chapter 13 — Language Blockage

Volume 13 · Chapter 13

Hearing Merlin call her his wife, Alice's heart suddenly felt restless, stirring like a fawn jumping around.

Alice awkwardly lowered her head. Even though they were pretending to be a married couple, it felt no different from the real thing. When did they become so skilled at this?

Alice, being held in Merlin's arms, felt an immense sense of satisfaction. She didn't usually get opportunities like this.

Merlin secretly glanced at Alice and saw her face had turned red. He was suddenly startled--

Damn, no way?

This Alice could even blush while acting?

...Too realistic. Professional actors aren't even this dedicated.

Merlin felt inferior by comparison and had to adjust his mindset, playing along with Alice's performance.

Now, anyone with eyes could see that Merlin and Alice were a married couple. The way the two stuck together made it impossible to doubt.

"Giggle giggle..."

Jenna's expression stiffened, her face alternating between red and white, her teeth grinding together. Watching Alice leaning against Merlin, she felt an overwhelming sense of displeasure inside.

If not for Jenna wanting to maintain her dignified image in front of Merlin, she would have already slammed the table and started cursing at Alice outright.

How dare you seduce Lord Merlin right in front of me, you damn fox spirit! Clearly you don't respect me at all?!

After seducing my brother, you're still not satisfied? You won't even let Lord Merlin go! You carnivorous woman, shouldn't you know when to stop!

If a tiger doesn't show its power, do you take me for a sick cat!?

Jenna's facial muscles twitched as she suppressed the fire in her heart, grinding her teeth as she spoke.

"Miss Alice, what are you doing? Can you please stop taking advantage of Lord Merlin and scram to the side, okay?"

Alice frowned, feeling provoked by Jenna's aggressive tone, a wave of imbalance rising in her heart.

Seriously, what's so good about Merlin? How did this noble lady fall for him?

Alice couldn't figure out Merlin's merits. Although this guy was somewhat gentle and very reliable, she could list his bad habits nonstop for three days and three nights and still not finish.

It seemed Alice still didn't understand the principle of a perfect match despite unlikely origins. Jenna liked men who were gentle yet firm, and very domineering. Merlin perfectly fit her inner expectations.

"Jenna, what are you talking nonsense about?" Arnold beside them said unhappily, emphasizing, "It's clearly Merlin taking advantage of Miss Alice. You've got it backwards. Look at his groping hands, damn it....

"You're talking nonsense! It was clearly this fox spirit who approached him first. Lord Merlin is not that kind of person!" Jenna and Arnold argued back and forth.

Merlin smiled faintly, thinking that since he and Alice were now pretending to be a married couple, taking advantage of his wife wasn't taking advantage at all. That was called reasonable affection.

"Who's the fox spirit? I'm leaning on my husband's shoulder. Does that bother you?" Alice couldn't stand Jenna's humiliating remarks much longer.

"Your husband? Don't be ridiculous. You witch, hurry up and let go of Lord Merlin. Using fake breasts to seduce is too despicable!" Jenna hit the nail on the head, striking right at Alice's sensitive spot.

"...What did you say!?" Alice trembled with anger. She couldn't help having fake breasts--it was all due to malnutrition on the big snowy mountain during childhood.

"Alice and I are a married couple. Hugging each other is normal. Why are you guys getting worked up over nothing?" Merlin spoke up to help Alice. In order to make Jenna scram quickly, he had to appear as a married man to make them back off.

"...Lord Merlin, ...you're just saying that casually, right? You're not actually a couple...." Jenna was startled by Merlin's words, finding it hard to believe. Tears of unwillingness rose to her eyes, making them watery.

"Impossible. You're not a couple at all. The titles are all fake." Arnold paused, speaking very seriously, "Hurry up and let go of Miss Alice. Can't you see she's uncomfortable? Her face is all red. It must be because you're gripping too hard and making it hard for Alice to breathe!"

"Right! You're a fake couple! What kind of propriety is this, sticking together like that? Fox spirit, hurry up and leave Lord Merlin. He's mine!" Jenna suddenly caught on. She thought Merlin and Alice weren't really a couple either. What was the point of being all clingy?

"Hahaha..." Merlin smiled, showing an apologetic expression. "I'll be honest with you. Matters of the heart are hard to explain. Alice and I have been living together for a long time. To say there's no affection would be a lie. Actually, our pretend relationship became real long ago. We're already a genuine married couple."

Alice looked up at Merlin, thinking this guy was really committed to his acting. If she didn't know they were just getting through this trouble together, she'd almost believe it was real!

...What was this restlessness in her heart? Colder, she told herself. If I actually fall for it, I lose!

Alice showed a helpless expression, leaning on Merlin's shoulder, and said with a hint of bitterness.

"I'm very sorry, Arnold. Merlin and I are already a real married couple. It's impossible for me to be with you. So... I hope you can find happiness in the future."

"No!!! " Arnold wailed in great pain, suffering the loss of "the one closest to the water gets the moon first."

"L-lies, you're lying, right?" Jenna's eyes widened, her expression becoming dazed, feeling so stimulated she questioned her whole life. But she soon realized something was off. "Pull yourself together, useless big brother! You believe whatever they say? Unless we're fools!"

"Eh?" Arnold looked up, as if grabbing the last straw of salvation.

"You say you're a real married couple? Heh heh, who are you trying to fool!?" Jenna looked at Alice, seemingly already feeling like she had won. "Where's the real couple that doesn't have children!? Why don't you give birth to a child so I can see? If you can't, nobody will believe you! Anyway, until you have a child, I won't give up on Lord Merlin!"

"Right! Miss Alice, you say you and Merlin are a real couple. But why haven't you gotten pregnant yet? That's not normal!?" Arnold's hope immediately reignited, feeling he still had a great chance.

"...Alice was speechless, thinking she and Merlin had been living together for almost a year now. Since they claimed to be together, not having a child was indeed strange. How could she make this troublesome sibling pair give up?

"Aha~, I knew Miss Alice was lying to me, right? I almost took it seriously...." Arnold put his hands together, saying gratefully, "I feel like the Divine Lord is giving me a chance. I can pursue Miss Alice again..."

"Tsk tsk!" Alice secretly signaled to Merlin, as if wanting to discuss something.

Merlin leaned over and said awkwardly, "Tsk! These two siblings are a bit troublesome. Arnold is manageable, but Jenna seems hard to fool.

"Yeah, without children we can't shut their mouths. This is really terrible," Alice nodded.

Both were deep in thought at the same time, worried about being entangled by this sibling pair, silently thinking...

Merlin looked at Alice and asked meaningfully, "Ali...

Alice turned to look at Merlin, feeling this guy's gaze was somewhat fiery, seemingly holding another layer of meaning!

Facing such a gaze, a flash of panic suddenly darted through Alice's eyes. Her heartbeat suddenly accelerated, and blushing, she said--

"...Y-you..."

"Why are you looking at me?"

ε9(.><)93

title: Chapter 14 — The Banquet (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 14 — The Banquet (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 13 · Chapter 14

Alice was frightened by Merlin's gaze, her heart skipping a beat.

Where am I supposed to get a child? Does he want me to give birth to one myself?

But doing it alone wouldn't work either — don't I still need Merlin for that?

Wait! What am I even thinking?! Calm down!

Alice felt she couldn't keep up the act; she had a feeling this was going to end in disaster.

So Alice pulled away from Merlin's shoulder, looking at him with a guarded expression, bracing for him to say he wanted her to bear his child. However —

"What's with that reaction? I just wanted to ask where you'd dig up a child from..." Merlin frowned, finding Alice's flushed face weird.

...Alice froze mid-motion, as if a bucket of cold water had been dumped over her. She felt a surge of indignation. "Why are you asking me? How would I possibly know?"

Over on the side, Jenna immediately broke into a smug smile, thinking: *Sure enough, there's something going on. My guess was right — Lord Merlin is going all out to shake me off.*

Jenna felt she was at a disadvantage alone; she needed her brother beside her as a wingman. She pulled Arnold over and whispered.

"Bro, did you notice? Those two definitely have something fishy going on~"

"Yeah, it's definitely off." Arnold nodded.

"Then listen to me, and I'll guarantee you win over Miss Alice." Jenna narrowed her eyes, signaling Arnold to obey.

"How?" Arnold was all ears, thinking Jenna was about to give him advice.

"I'll launch an offensive on Lord Merlin; you make a move on Alice. We'll split up and operate separately." Jenna said seriously.

Arnold nodded, thinking: *As expected, my sister wants to help me. This is great — maybe I'll have a major breakthrough tonight~*

Just then, the hall doors were slowly pushed open by a servant, and a middle-aged man with a receding hairline walked in. He looked even older than Duke Rose.

His most distinctive feature was probably the mustache on his face — twisted and curled into a spiral hook, looking rather amusing.

This had to be Arnold and Jenna's father, Count Austin, the lord of the entire Rexham.

Count Austin saw Merlin and Alice, smiled and nodded. "Didn't expect you two to already be here. Just now I was tangled up in affairs and had to steal time to deal with them. Please forgive my tardiness."

Alice smiled, about to respond, but Merlin spoke first.

"No problem, we're very tolerant of lateness."

"Uh..."

Count Austin froze for a moment. He had just been addressing Alice; the Merlin beside her seemed awfully eager to show off.

So Count Austin quickly cleared his throat to cover his embarrassment and continued.

"Good then. Shall we have dinner first?"

"Huh? Aren't you going to tell us what you need us for?" Alice asked in surprise.

"No need to rush. You're guests, and it's dinner time. Let's eat first; my request can wait until after." Count Austin smiled and ordered the servants to bring the dishes quickly.

Merlin and Alice exchanged a glance; neither was quite sure what the lord of Rexham wanted.

But with Elder Taylor and the Count seemingly on decent terms, they didn't worry about being put in a difficult spot.

The evening banquet began.

Servants lit more candles and wheeled in cart after cart.

They placed one delicious dish after another on the table and poured red wine for everyone.

Since Alice couldn't consume alcohol and feared embarrassing herself in this setting, she declined and switched to water.

Merlin looked at the spotless cutlery that could double as mirrors and silently cursed wretched capitalism.

But looking at the beautifully plated dishes, Merlin thought the Count's chef was quite skilled — definitely not some random cook; the real deal.

A pianist walked to the corner of the hall, warmed up briefly, and began to play — a soothing and elegant piece.

Most servants had already left, leaving only a few highly attentive ones standing by, ready to be summoned at any moment.

This setup... Count Austin seemed to have prepared it deliberately, wanting to give Merlin and his wife a good impression.

Alice looked at the food on the table and felt something was off; this was clearly a prelude to asking a favor.

*Sizzle.*

"Hmm?"

"Feels like Austin's got something big going on. Should we leave now? The Count's request is probably high difficulty." Alice said with some worry.

Merlin thought for a moment and replied quietly, "We're already here. Eat first, then go. Look how lavish this is — we don't usually get a chance like this. If the Count's matter turns out too complicated, we can still decline. You just say you're pregnant; I doubt he'd dare make things difficult for a pregnant woman, right?"

"You're the one who's pregnant! Don't use me as a shield — I'm not doing it!" Alice got a headache from Merlin's antics.

"I'm a man; if I say I'm pregnant they'll believe me~" Merlin shrugged innocently.

...Alice silently clenched her fist, an urge to fight Merlin rising in her heart.

"May I ask if the dishes suit your appetites?" Count Austin asked with concern.

"Pretty good." Merlin nodded.

"Excellent." Alice forced a polite, awkward smile.

The banquet proceeded in a relatively harmonious atmosphere, with almost no conflict.

With their father present, Jenna and Arnold had to keep a low profile and didn't actively stir up trouble.

But the way Jenna and Arnold ate left Merlin a bit speechless — probably because they were noble offspring.

Their eating movements were exceptionally stiff, looking particularly affected.

Jenna felt this was a chance to raise her favorability; she couldn't blow it. She pushed the fresh beef toward Merlin. "Lord Merlin, eat more, build up your strength. That'll make you healthier."

Seeing his sister so attentive, Arnold was inspired. He hurriedly placed the fruit salad in front of Alice. "Miss Alice, eat more fruit — it'll be good for your skin."

Their father, Austin, was slightly startled — first time ever seeing his son and daughter so concerned about guests. Usually they just perfunctorily went through the motions.

Alice and Merlin looked down at the "kindness" Jenna and Arnold had sent over. To eat or not to eat was the question — eating would play into their hands, not eating would make Austin lose face.

But after just a few seconds of thought, Alice came up with a plan. She speared a piece of her own pre-cut fruit and held it to Merlin's mouth.

"Hubby, ah~"

Merlin jumped, thinking: *Alice is impressive, she even knows this move. Though it's a bit nauseatingly sweet.*

Though Merlin felt some resistance, he still accepted Alice's feeding with a smile that didn't reach his eyes.

"...So good." Merlin commented, then quickly turned the tables, cutting a small piece of beef and offering it to Alice. "Come on, wifey, open wide, ah~"

...Alice's expression flickered with embarrassment. She thought Merlin learned fast and accepted graciously. "Delicious~"

The background behind the couple seemed to blur and shift, turning into pink flower petals that flashed and blinded the two across from them!

Jenna and Arnold couldn't take it anymore — they'd wanted to break this pair up, not watch them feed each other!

The siblings burned with jealousy and slammed the table, their knives and forks bending in their grip.

Fake!

Fake!

All fake!

And *duang duang duang* flower petal special effects?!

This fake couple has gone full drama queen — dare they be any faker?!

Ten thousand ten

title: Chapter 15 — Hunter
content:
Chapter 15 — Hunter

Volume 13 · Chapter 15

Merlin and Alice stopped showing off their affection and looked across at Arnold and Jenna, wondering if they'd finally reached their limit?

Even Austin, who had been seated at the head of the table dining, was startled by his children's sudden behavior and asked in surprise.

"What's wrong with both of you?"

The glass-hearted Arnold was the first to break down, running out in tears, "Damn it! Why doesn't Miss Alice like me?"

Austin suddenly froze, not knowing what to say about his son's outburst.

Though he understood that Arnold liked the girl Alice, the woman was clearly already married.

Snatching someone else's partner was obviously unethical, and he didn't much support his son's ideas about Alice.

Moreover, Arnold's abrupt departure from the table made Austin lose face, appearing too rude in front of guests.

Seeing her brother flee, Jenna silently sighed that he was truly mud that couldn't be plastered on a wall, and said loudly, "You two should wrap it up! You're obviously a fake couple, stop pretending like you're really married!"

"We are a real couple, I don't know what you're talking about?" Merlin shrugged, feeling incredibly pleased inside.

"I don't get it either~" Alice chimed in agreement.

The couple's demeanor was entirely provocative, radiating an irresistible urge to get hit.

"How many times does this fox spirit have to keep it up? Tell me! How much money will it take for you to leave Lord Merlin?!" Jenna stared down Alice, delivering the classic losing female second lead's Mary Sue declaration.

"Jenna! What are you doing! Yelling and screaming like this—what sense of propriety is that?!" Austin slammed the table, his curved mustache quivering with anger.

"Father,...." Jenna wanted to explain.

"Get out! I'm punishing you by confining you to the house for three days, and copying the teachings of the Goddess of Light three times over!" Austin exuded a father's oppressive authority, brutally suppressing Jenna's defiance.

"...." Jenna felt deeply wronged, immediately wiped her tears and ran out, constantly muttering, "Waaah, Lord Merlin is such an idiot!"

With the siblings fleeing one after another, the hall immediately returned to quiet, no longer tense with scheming and intrigue.

Merlin and Alice secretly exchanged glances and smiles; their scheme had finally succeeded. Without those persistent pests around, even the air seemed fresher.

"How great, those siblings are finally gone," Merlin muttered to himself.

"Yeah, being pestered gave me a headache," Alice rubbed her temples, looking thoroughly exhausted.

Count Austin slowly turned his head and looked over, saying in an apologetic tone, "I'm sorry, my children have caused you trouble."

"N-no... it's nothing...." Alice awkwardly smiled and waved her hand.

"I know Arnold is also an adventurer from your guild, and he's received plenty of your care over the years. I never expected he would embarrass himself in front of you today." Count Austin paused and continued, "Rest assured, Arnold's rude behavior will be properly dealt with. I'll give him a good scolding later."

"Surely that's not necessary?" A cold sweat trickled down Alice's forehead. "Arnold and Jenna didn't mean any harm, we can understand."

"....Is that so? No wonder Arnold likes you, Miss Alice. You truly are an understanding and considerate girl." Count Austin wiped the sweat from his brow with a handkerchief. "But seeing how affectionate you and Lord Merlin are today, I know this boy doesn't stand a chance. I will sincerely bless the two of you, and I'll make Arnold give up on Miss Alice."

Alice didn't argue, thinking it would be nice if Arnold stopped pestering her in the future, sparing her a lot of headaches.

"Count, perhaps we shouldn't dwell on these trivial matters. Didn't you have something to discuss with us? Let's talk about it now." Merlin got straight to the point. He was full now, and it was time to hear what Austin's request was.

"As for this...." Count Austin sat up straight and glanced at the servants around him, waving his hand. "Everyone, you may withdraw."

The servants quickly cleared the dining table and cleaned the room, bowed slightly, and retired.

Merlin and Alice frowned at each other, wondering what could possibly be so secretive that it needed to be discussed in private?

"Please follow me, both of you." Count Austin rose and headed toward the deeper part of the hall.

The two exchanged a glance, communicated briefly with their eyes, then rose and followed.

Count Austin came to a cabinet adorned with decorations and twisted it a few times, and the sound of grinding gears echoed.

Soon after, a hidden passage appeared in the wall not far away. There was actually a basement!?!

Count Austin lifted an oil lamp and stood at the entrance, gesturing for them to enter.

"Please, both of you."

As the three entered, the dark and narrow passage filled with uncertainty.

Count Austin carried the oil lamp, leading the way down the stairs into the depths.

Their footfalls echoed around them, and between the thick dust, Alice couldn't help but cough a few times.

It was hard to imagine how long it had been since anyone had visited this place, resembling an ancient ruin from centuries ago.

At the bottom, Count Austin lit a torch, and then dozens of torches flared to life one by one in a ring.

The underground scene suddenly opened up, allowing them to take in the situation—

There was no treasure here; it looked more like an armory.

Weapons lined both sides, from swords and spears to fairly old firearms, everything imaginable.

They appeared to be crafted from silver, slightly blackened on the surface, yet still revealing sharp glints of cold light.

At the top hung a relatively large portrait of a fierce-looking man with scruffy facial hair.

Out in the open, no one would be surprised if they took him for a highway robber.

However, the eyes of the man in the portrait bore a strong resemblance to Austin and Arnold.

Merlin surmised the man in the painting must be an ancestor of the Austin family.

"Merlin, look quickly, there are several demon skulls on that wall," Alice whispered a warning.

Merlin followed Alice's gaze and was suddenly startled, his heart sinking.

Gray-skinned, hideously distorted, pointy-eared monster heads hung on the wall, hollowed out and used as decorations.

At first Merlin was frightened, but he quickly composed himself and replied to Alice in a low voice.

"Those aren't demons. Demons have deep black skin and their ears aren't nearly this pointed. The biggest difference would be their teeth—we wouldn't have such prominent, sharp fangs. It's almost like a habit."

"T-then what are they? They look a bit....." Alice muttered.

"If I had to guess... vampires?" Merlin offered his answer. He thought vampires were a rather special species, very secretive, with no recorded cases of mass appearances.

However, based on some historical records, it was proven they had existed. Though they looked similar, they were definitely not demons, being closer to humans and the undead.

"....Vampires?!" Alice's eyes widened, seeing for the first time a special species from stories that truly existed.

"I think both of you have seen enough...." Count Austin interjected,打断ing Merlin and Alice's thoughts, speaking in a calm tone.

"All the weapons here are meant to fight against legendary vampires."

"This portrait is of my grandfather, a vampire hunter full of legend."

"He was the one who personally took down the once-powerful Dracula...."

title: Chapter 16 — Curse (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 16 — Curse (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 13 · Chapter 16

Merlin had already suspected it, but hearing Austin's certain answer still gave him a start inside.
He turned his head again, looking at the few vampire heads, feeling that such things were not common at all, comparable to rare magical beasts.
In the historical records, the positioning of vampires is very low; they do not belong to any of the myriad races, but are regarded as a variant of humans and undead.
According to legend, vampires originally did not exist; they became immortal and undead, hated evil beings, only after being abandoned and cursed by the goddess.
However, the truth of this saying is hard to judge; even the demon race's classics hold doubts about it, because the demons have fought the goddess for countless ages, and their evaluation of the Goddess of Light is just cold‑blooded*, making it hard to imagine that those the goddess despises could still live forever.
Most people believe Dracula is the oldest bloodline, although there are many versions of the story, but in short it's nothing more than God letting Dracula continue to suffer, not allowing him to die.
Holy shit! There's such a pleasant punishment method, stop BBing, quickly give me a full service, I'm constantly worried that the heart curse will arrange……
Merlin was full of malicious complaints in his mind, thinking that as fellow villains, how come they get immortality while he constantly faces death threats, what a huge difference in treatment.
Merlin did not look down on the blood clan, because the classics recorded their rather bug‑like racial ability—
One is bloodlust; vampires survive by drinking blood, and while drinking they can stimulate their potential, moving extraordinarily fast, and also gain part of the prey's power,
Put simply, drinking blood makes them stronger and allows them to absorb the enemy's strength, a two‑way self‑enhancement ability.
Vampires have a strong craving for the blood of powerful races, especially demons, almost to a pathological degree.
They might regard human blood as mere food, but demon blood would be treated as a strengthening agent, used for nourishment.
Because the compatibility between demons and vampires is truly excellent, they can achieve perfect synchronization; after drinking demon blood, the vampires' strength can rise several levels.
The other is self‑healing; if the demon race's classics contain no exaggeration, then the vampires' self‑healing ability is absolutely god‑level—nothing can kill them except silver weapons and sunlight.
Legend says that as long as a vampire is not completely killed, leaving even a drop of blood, a piece of flesh, or even a single cell, they can recover to their original perfect state, having reached the pinnacle of tenacity.
This is also the basis for the claim that vampires were cursed by the goddess, because such a perverse self‑healing ability is something no race has ever possessed; it is as if the world's will has imposed the concept of 'immortality' on the blood clan, giving vampires immortal self‑healing, which fits the goddess's curse perfectly.
Things like ultra‑fast regeneration and perfect self‑healing are pathetically weak compared to the vampires' abilities.
Which race has the most tenacious vitality? The blood clan appears, and all other races can only bow down in admiration.
When Merlin saw this record, he found it hard to believe; if it were really that exaggerated, even if he slashed a billion blades he couldn't kill a vampire, unless he used proper methods and silver weapons.
The eerie bloodlust and perverse self‑healing make the blood clan look perfect in every way, yet Merlin always harbored doubts, feeling something was off.
Alice, on the other hand, was utterly shocked, pointing at the vampire heads and saying, “Is… is that really a vampire?!”
“Exactly, it’s true,” Austin said seriously. “My grandfather is an expert in dealing with vampires; these specimens have been specially treated and pose no threat.” He added that the special treatment likely destroyed even the cells, otherwise those vampires, even if only skins remained, would still have a risk of resurrection.
Alice stared wide‑eyed, her expression somewhat dazed, her little mouth unable to close.
She had never encountered a vampire in her life, never expecting that the creature from those legendary tales actually existed.
Moreover, the Austin family’s ancestors were actually vampire hunters, and they even slew the famous Dracula?!
Even though Alice doesn’t know much about vampires, she had heard the monster’s name before; apart from demons, it’s probably the only thing that can make humans feel panic.
Austin saw Merlin and Alice’s reactions, which were within his expectations, and continued, “I suppose both of you are seeing vampires for the first time? It’s normal to find it hard to accept in a short time.”
“Yes, it’s my first time seeing one; I can’t really imagine they truly exist, I thought they were just fictional stories, or perhaps a type of demon.” Alice nodded.
“What does ‘demon’ mean? There’s no such low‑level creature as vampires among demons.” Merlin frowned, rebutting Alice.
“If it’s not a demon, then it’s not a demon—what are you getting worked up about?” Alice rolled her eyes, thinking Merlin still had some sense of belonging to the demons, even though they’d been kicked out.
“I’m merely correcting your inappropriate remark,” Merlin said emphatically, “throwing all sorts of random stuff into the demon race—this isn’t a dumpster, it’s going too far.”
“Haha, you two don’t need to argue like this; the blood clan, as a mistakenly appeared race, having some misunderstanding is normal.” Austin chuckled.
“Hmph!” Alice glared at Merlin angrily.
“The blood clan has very strict bloodline restrictions; their birth rate is extremely low, but they can create thralls. However, as the number of thralls increases, the blood clan’s power becomes weaker, so the vampire population stays limited, always within a certain boundary; compared to all the races in the world, their numbers are negligible.” Austin said kindly.
“… Is that why most people haven’t…?” Alice nodded, half‑understanding.
“Did you summon us this time for the vampire matter?” Merlin asked tentatively.
“Exactly,” Ofre nodded, continuing, “My ancestors were powerful vampire hunters; they pursued Count Dracula for many years and finally got to see this blood‑thirsty noble in person, but because the opponent was too strong, they had no choice but to adopt a mutually destructive method to eliminate the menace for the people. Yet the result was regrettable—Count Dracula did not die, and it seems my ancestors even provoked him, causing the entire family’s bloodline to be cursed by him.”
“A curse?” Merlin narrowed his eyes, instantly interested; he himself had a curse, and there were still things he couldn’t explain.
“Yes, a truly terrifying curse….”
Austin slowly turned his back to Merlin and Alice, slightly lowered his clothes, and revealed his shoulder.
At that moment, Alice and Merlin could clearly see a tooth mark on Austin’s shoulder, as if it had been pierced by two nails!
Although Alice couldn’t make sense of it, Merlin stroked his chin; having come from the modern world and seen movies, he felt the mark resembled those of European vampires, a strong sense of déjà vu.
Austin noticed both of them examining him and went on to describe the trouble that has plagued his family for hundreds of years.
“This mark is present on every member of our family from birth; Arnold and Jenna have it too.”
“Our family members never live past fifty; on their fiftieth birthday, they will surely die mysteriously.”
“In a single night, their blood will be drained without any warning, their bodies withering into empty husks…. ”

title: Chapter 17 — Treasure
content:
Chapter 17 — Treasure

Volume 13 · Chapter 17

Alice was taken aback, hearing of such a bizarre method of death for the first time.

Being mysteriously drained of blood to death was far too abnormal.

Alice wondered if a vampire had attacked during the night, causing such a bizarre death.

"My Lord Earl, could this be a vampire attack? But simply claiming a sudden, unexplained death carries no real persuasiveness."

"Absolutely not. At first, our family also thought that way, but the result was different. Our grandfather was drained alive right before our eyes. There was no vampire attack. Aside from a curse, there is no other explanation," Austin said helplessly.

"......" Alice nodded, thinking that if it was truly a curse, it would indeed be troublesome. As far as she knew, simple curses could be dispelled by mages and priests, but there were many bizarre curses where, unless the caster was killed, there was little else one could do.

Merlin stroked his chin, quite interested in the Austin family's curse, but compared to his own cardiac atrophy that could claim his life at any moment, this was considerably weaker.

However, Merlin felt he could study it in depth—perhaps he might still gain something from it.

Although Merlin's life was fairly comfortable now, with the heart curse hanging over him like a ticking bomb ready to explode at any moment, he couldn't completely settle his mind.

"Since this curse has such a severe impact on your family, why hasn't it been resolved by now?"

"Our family has been trying for generations, attempted many solutions, but none have had any effect. I'm afraid only by killing that legendary Dracula will our family's tragic fate come to an end," Austin explained.

"If you know the solution, then just go kill that Dracula. Why drag it out for hundreds of years?" Merlin asked perplexedly, feeling that Austin showed no real attitude of effort to lift the curse.

"Lord Merlin, I understand everything you're saying. I also want to kill Dracula, but the techniques for hunting vampires have been lost in our family. That ancestor who perished alongside the vampire is probably the last vampire hunter in our family. Those who came after, fearing Dracula's retaliation, mostly stayed away from vampire hunting entirely. So I'm well-meaning but powerless," Austin said with considerable frustration.

"In that case......" Alice paused. "My Lord Earl, what you're looking to commission us this time......"

"That's right. Please, Lady Alice, help us break free from our fate, kill Grand Duke Dracula, and lift this curse that has plagued our family for centuries." Austin stated his request, bowing slightly. "Only you can help our family. If we succeed, we will repay your kindness to the best of our ability."

.......

Alice hesitated somewhat, but seeing Austin bowing before her, she found it hard to refuse.

She felt this mission had some difficulty—it wasn't as easy as she had imagined.

Although Alice had never met Dracula, from various stories she could still discern that this progenitor vampire was an extremely powerful existence.

Moreover, his personality was extremely cruel and heart-stopping; it was rumored he had once impaled imperial soldiers on wooden stakes for all to see.

Alice had little confidence in herself. Facing Grand Duke Dracula alone would likely be a situation where disaster was more likely than success.

"I have no other choice either. I'm already 43 years old, and there are only seven years left before the family curse takes effect." Austin sighed and said earnestly, "I heard from Duke Rose about Miss Alice's valor. Even across the entire empire, you rank among the top powers. So I believe as long as you take this on, you will definitely help our family overcome this crisis."

Alice looked at Merlin, wondering what he meant.

If they were going to help Earl Austin, Merlin was also a companion, so she needed to consider his opinion.

Merlin adopted a contemplative expression, thinking this mission could be accepted—it was a good chance to witness a vampire. "Very well. We can help your family. Leave that vampire grand duke to me."

"Then... shouldn't we rely much more on Miss Alice?" Austin asked in surprise.

"Huh? Rely on her?" Merlin's head was full of question marks.

"What's your issue?" Alice glared at Merlin angrily, very dissatisfied with his questioning tone.

"Exactly. Grand Duke Rose evaluated both of you, saying that although Lord Merlin's strength is quite good, compared to Miss Alice there is still a considerable gap."

Austin answered awkwardly, not quite sure what was wrong with what he had said.

"Heh heh~, how about that?" Alice's little nose curled up toward the sky. Even if she couldn't beat Merlin in a fight, she was more than happy to have the upper hand in words.

Merlin clicked his tongue, thinking helplessly that while raising Alice's status had been the original plan, seeing this shrew look so smug was still infuriating.

But fortunately Merlin didn't care about such things. Whether he or Alice was stronger made little difference—in the end, both of them benefited.

"Alright, we accept this mission. Tell us the location of that vampire grand duke?"

"This... is probably not easy to arrange, there is some difficulty." Earl Austin showed a troubled expression; it seemed there was another hidden circumstance.

"Huh!?!" Alice suddenly paused, tentatively pressing further. "You don't happen to not know Grand Duke Dracula's location, do you?"

"......" Austin nodded, forced to admit this fact.

Alice's expression turned strange. She thought that Earl Austin was both asking her and Merlin to help while completely not knowing where the vampire grand duke hid. The world was so vast—how were they supposed to find him?! They couldn't just be like headless flies, traveling everywhere and hoping for luck.

"You're not joking, are you? Your ancestor was a vampire hunter, right? And he saw a vampire count with his own eyes. How could he not know the location?" Merlin frowned. He had thought this was a relatively simple mission, but now it didn't seem to be.

"In truth, I'm not very clear about my ancestor's life as a vampire hunter. It was all told to me by my grandfather, so I don't know Dracula's whereabouts very well either," Austin said with an apologetic smile.

"Then what should we do? You're not expecting us to figure it out ourselves, are you? We know absolutely nothing about this so-called Dracula." Merlin was somewhat impatient, his tone carrying a hint of complaint. "You should have made this clear from the beginning. Really...."

"Lord Merlin, please don't get excited. Although I don't know Dracula's exact location, it's not like I have zero clues." Austin paused, then shared some clues.

"My old subordinate, Baron Barton of Ireland, recently obtained a treasure map concerning a vampire ruin.

"Due to its importance, I ordered him to keep it safe. This is important information.

"You can go directly to Ireland and find Baron Barton. Just mention my name and you can obtain that treasure map.

"I think information about Dracula should be recorded on it..."

title: Chapter 18 — Holy Silver (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 18 — Holy Silver (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 13 · Chapter 18

Late night.
Merlin and Alice have already returned home, and the two are thinking about today's events.
Although Austin has already given out clues, there are really many uncertain factors.
Moreover, Austin said the treasure map in the baron's hand is news he just received a few days ago.
Even Austin himself hasn't looked at it yet, and cannot be sure that it definitely contains information about Count Dracula.
If the treasure map turns out to be some useless doodles, that would be terrible; the two would have wasted their effort, which is quite troublesome.
Especially for Merlin, he has a heart-withering curse that can flare up at any time, so he definitely cannot waste too much time.
If things are too peaceful and comfortable, it would be destructive for Merlin; under constant threat to his life, he can't afford to relax.
If I recall correctly, Merlin last killed a Saint-tier powerhouse was the two Thorn Knights; afterwards, the Four Sword Saints and the Chaos Overlords did not meet the requirement to alleviate the curse.
Calculating the time that has passed, Merlin's heart curse has been dormant for quite a while; it feels like it will start to act up soon.
This isn't Merlin scaremongering; it's based on past patterns—it's time to find some prey to fill his belly.
Despite facing threats, Merlin remains relatively calm, takes it in stride, and has long been accustomed to the feeling of angina.
Even now, Merlin still hasn't intended to tell Alice his secret, because he hasn't fully trusted and accepted Alice, always keeping a certain distance.
At this moment, Merlin lazily leans on the sofa, playing with the special weapon Austin the Count gave him—
A sharp katana forged from holy silver, its whole body gleaming with silver light, reflecting a chilling cold!
This sword is something left by Austin's vampire hunter ancestor, perfect for Merlin to use.
It is said the weapon's raw material is a holy silver vessel, namely the silver pot used to hold the Holy Church's holy water, which after melting was forged.
The holy silver vessel, after years of soaking in holy water, also retains a hint of spirituality, thus it has the ability to severely wound and deter dark creatures.
The appearance of the holy silver katana is far more splendid than that of the demon sword Banri Garan; the blade bears exquisite engraved patterns, looking like a quite expensive work of art.
However, the rating of this katana should be high-grade, not yet rare; for example, the demon sword Banri Garan and Light's Canticle are rare-grade, far superior to the holy silver katana.
But the holy silver katana excels against vampires, capable of inflicting lethal damage on the blood race—this point the demon sword Banri Garan cannot do.
The holy silver katana and Light's Canticle share similar traits, both dealing massive damage to dark evil objects, but their quality is not on the same level; the holy silver katana is left far behind by dozens of streets—
Because Alice's rare slender sword Light's Canticle can wound Merlin's flesh, but this holy silver katana cannot do so at all— the superiority is clear!
So when departing, Austin forcibly shoved a weapon into Merlin's hands, yet gave none to Alice.
One would think it's because Austin the Count worries Merlin might encounter vampires and run into trouble he can't easily resolve.
With this holy silver katana, he can effectively slay vampires with extraordinary self-healing ability, preventing them from constantly regenerating and reviving.
Although Merlin thinks he doesn't really need it, he accepted it without refusing, because it's made of silver— at least if unused it could be worth some money; why not eat a snack delivered to your door?
Austin the Count understands propriety; after the task is completed, he promised Merlin and Alice a fairly objective reward, which still makes the two somewhat tempted.
Of course, it's not like the elf princess who splurges, offering a million gold coins as pocket money at the drop of a hat.
You should know that the United Kingdom where Shirley resides is a gathering place of the nine major races, the most prosperous nation in this world.
But the United Kingdom operates under a council alliance system, belonging to none of those races individually, but shared by all nine major races.
Even if you pull out the strongest individual from the human empire, it still can't match the United Kingdom; but if you add up all of the human empire, it surpasses the United Kingdom in strength.
Thus, as the little princess of the elf race, Shirley taking out a million gold coins as pocket money is not strange; Michelle princess tightening her belt can only scrape out 350,000 gold coins.
Moreover, the hundred-thousand and million gold coins are the total pocket money of the little princesses over several years, which definitely includes part of their own savings.
For example, the daughter of the Rose Duke, Cecilia, hired Merlin once; whether she can afford to hire him again is another matter.
Because the amount paid for hiring Merlin once likely overdrafted Cecilia's several years of pocket money plus her savings.
Otherwise, adventurers taking private commissions would be making too much money, clearly not matching reality.
If the princesses could easily come up with that much money, why wouldn't they frequently hire Merlin to do work for them?
"Your mouth really stinks...." Merlin curses unhappily, then continues, ""Regarding this trip, we need to go to Ireland to find Baron Barton to learn the situation; hearing Austin say he once served as the commander of the Edinburgh garrison, two years ago after retiring he became the lord of Gao Wei city, we may need to prepare one"
"Hmm." Alice nods absentmindedly, her hands clasping the cup as if she has something on her mind.
Merlin falls silent, thinking that going to Ireland he might also run into that directionally challenged little shota; Johnson, hailed as a magic genius, truly is an ill-fated encounter, always bound to meet.
".... Alice mutters—
"Ah, I know what you want to say? We're set to depart tomorrow, saving time, right?" Merlin looks at Alice, seeing her reaction is somewhat strange.
"......" Alice furrows her lovely brows in rebuttal, looking somewhat angry.
"What do you want to say then?" Merlin wonders, feeling Alice today always seems a bit dazed.
"That...." Alice rubs her cheek with her finger, can turn her head away to avoid Merlin's gaze—
"To outsiders look...
"We really are that like unrefined absorption =WN/w/Y

title: Chapter 19 — Ideal
content:
Chapter 19 — Ideal

Volume 13 · Chapter 19

Alice turned her head away, unwilling for Merlin to see her slightly flushed face.

She didn't have any messy thoughts, she just felt that many people would automatically assume she and Merlin were a married couple without even thinking about it.

For that reason, Alice really wanted to know how Merlin saw it — whether he had a different perspective.

Especially today, when she and Merlin had some physical contact, being held in his embrace while he called her "wife" nonstop, showing off their affection like that…

Although deep down Alice didn't actually dislike it — she quite enjoyed being clingy with Merlin —

she still felt something was off. What exactly was their relationship?

Being so close every single day was definitely abnormal, right!

Alice believed that she and Merlin were still potential enemies, yet she seemed to want to keep him by her side more and more each day. That wasn't a good sign at all; whatever their relationship became in the future, it would be impossible to explain clearly.

So now Alice really wanted to probe indirectly, to ask Merlin what his attitude toward her was. Would he, would he… also have some similar feeling of wanting to be together?

After listening to Alice's inexplicable question, Merlin couldn't help but frown, stroking his chin as he muttered, "True, it is strange. I've explained it many times already, but whenever people see us together, they automatically assume we're a married couple. That's obviously not normal."

"....Right? I've been feeling it was weird too, why is it that—." Alice lowered her head, acting slightly coy. "Why are we always taken for a married couple and stuff? It's as if it's destined by fate or something."

After saying that, Alice's cheeks turned even redder, and she completely dared not lift her gaze to look at Merlin.

Alice swore that was the most cheesy thing she had ever said in her entire life; even she felt a wave of physical discomfort from her own words.

Actually, Alice had put it very tactfully. What she really meant was that she and Merlin were blessed by fate, their paths intertwined by destiny, and that was why people kept misunderstanding them as a couple.

But Merlin wasn't having any of that. With a completely straight face, he evaluated, "Hmm, I also feel an overwhelming sense of malice from the world around us, as if it's some kind of curse. It's subtly bringing you and me together. Truly terrifying."

"Uh." Alice turned her head, her delicate brows knitting tightly together. She had expected Merlin to say something romantic, but instead he treated being together with her as pure malice. It sent chills down her spine!

Noticing Alice's displeased expression, Merlin asked in surprise, "What's with that look? Am I not right?"

"Of course that's wrong! Why aren't you ever mistaken for a couple with other girls? But whenever you're with me, people think we're married. Doesn't that suggest a rather subtle connection?" Alice narrowed her eyes, trying to complicate the issue.

"What are you trying to say?" Merlin responded expressionlessly.

"We… we're always misunderstood as a couple. Could it be because… that fake one…" Alice stammered, her face flushing as she gathered her courage. "What if I… were your other half, the one destined for you!?"

The moment those words left her lips, the air in the room fell into a deathly silence.

Aside from Alice's nervous, uneven breathing, there seemed to be no other movement.

Alice's heart was both nervous and excited, with a hint of anticipation, hoping to see some reaction from Merlin.

The other half destined for her — the meaning was crystal clear. Alice just wanted to hear Merlin's response, to see if he had any desire to be with her.

"Hahahaha…"

Merlin's reaction was somewhat unexpected. He burst out laughing, leaning back on the sofa and looking at Alice with a strange expression.

"...What's so funny! What's there to laugh about!" Alice pouted angrily, feeling that Merlin was not respecting her.

"Destined other half? What are you talking about? Don't you realize I was just playing along with your foolishness back there?" Merlin looked at her with pity, as if she were the idiot.

"…What…" Alice was puzzled, unable to understand what Merlin meant.

Merlin tugged at the black iron Adventurers Guild card around his neck. "Miss, our information is carved into this card. Anyone who sees it will naturally assume we're a married couple. You're overthinking things again. 'Destined other half' — only a Mary Sue girl would have such a train of thought."

Alice's face slowly flushed red, like water boiling in a kettle, steam puffing out in bursts.

So that was the answer after all. There was no way Merlin would have thoughts of being with someone like her.

In the end, it was all her own wishful thinking. After all, he was a demon — he couldn't possibly be as emotionally complex as she was.

Alice forced a smile to hide her embarrassment.

"You're right. I was overthinking it, wasn't I? Since we spend so much time together, it's only natural that we'd become familiar enough for others to misunderstand."

"That's probably it…" Merlin nodded, then feigned casualness as he asked, "Actually, you don't like me, right?"

"—Of course not. I… I despise you. How could I ever develop feelings of fondness for you?" Alice said with a fake smile, speaking contrary to her true feelings, completely unable to retreat.

"Hahaha, what a coincidence — I feel the same way." Merlin was somewhat at a loss at Alice's declaration of "despising him," so he swallowed hard and said, "This makes it very clear. We both find each other unpleasant, so there's absolutely no chance of being each other's destined partner."

"Y-yes… now that I think about it, I feel much relieved." Alice waved her hand. On the surface she looked perfectly fine, but inside she felt profoundly disappointed. "It's getting late. Good night."

"Good night." A drop of cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead as he watched Alice return to her room.

Alice went back to her room and, not wanting Merlin to notice her disappointment, closed the door very softly.

After confirming Merlin could no longer see her, Alice dashed onto her bed, hugged her pillow, and let herself wallow in sadness —

In the end, it was all just my one-sided longing on my part.

That Merlin…

Never once thought about being with me.

QAQ<>

Outside.

A dark cloud of gloom settled over Merlin's face as he looked at Alice's tightly shut door and thought.

Alice still holds such strong prejudice against me, as expected.

After all, I've done so many unreasonable things to her in the past.

This hostility toward me — it probably won't change even in the future.

I actually thought it would be nice to be with Alice, but luckily I didn't say it out loud. Otherwise I would've lost all face today…

Merlin rubbed his forehead, still feeling a lingering chill, as he recalled that day when Alice was hanging clothes to dry in the sunlight. Even now, he could still feel waves of warmth coursing through him, making him subconsciously indulge in the memory —

At those moments, if only there were a cute daughter around…

That would be the pinnacle of my ideal life.

title: Chapter 20 — The Wilderness
content:
Chapter 20 — The Wilderness

Volume 13 · Chapter 20

The next day, Merlin and Alice set off for Ireland.

Their preparations were fairly thorough. In addition to the food and water needed for the journey, they also brought a letter written in Austin's handwriting to prove their identities.

If they went to Ireland and Lord Barton failed to recognize Merlin and Alice as those sent by Austin, then all their efforts would have been in vain.

Merlin and Alice traveled in their own cart, pulled by their donkey, and their pace wasn't too slow.

Although Merlin wanted to hire a more comfortable carriage, this extravagant idea was rejected by Alice.

Alice believed this was precisely the time to spend money and absolutely could not allow Merlin to squander it carelessly; they had to be frugal.

However, Merlin didn't even scold Alice for her household management skills, instead mocking her for being stingy.

Alice couldn't understand why Merlin never considered their current situation, always thinking of getting through each day as it came.

Their little donkey, Momo, was so cute and faster than an ordinary horse. Raised from a young age, it was especially obedient.

What was so great about a comfortable carriage? The most important thing when traveling was efficiency!

At this point, the two had been driving the donkey cart for five days and five nights, and had already entered the territory of Ireland....

This was a remote suburban area of Ireland, where the wasteland was carved with gullies, like the wrinkles on an old man's face etched by the harsh winter.

Momo stepped over the broken stones, clopping along toward the city of Galway.

Merlin pulled the reins, expressionless as he controlled the donkey. To be honest, he had had enough of riding in the cart.

Alice was rummaging through the packages, apparently planning to eat something. Since they were traveling, the food was all quite simple.

However, Alice still considered Merlin's picky nature and, in addition to bread, had also bought a jar of apple jam.

Alice took out a piece of bread, spread a layer of jam on it, and handed it to Merlin.

After all, driving the cart was quite hard work, so it was normal for Alice to give Merlin some care.

Merlin glanced at Alice, took the bread into his mouth, and couldn't help but mutter, "Bread and jam again. It's been five days, and we eat this every time. Can't you change it up a bit? Can't you prepare a few more menu options while we're away? It's like we're going to be dry all the way through...."

"...Is this my fault?!" Alice widened her eyes, feeling very wronged.

"You're in charge of logistics. If not you, then who? If I had prepared it, the food for five days wouldn't have been the same. You're really terrible at living,简直 like a..." Merlin paused, thinking of an adjective, "like a wild man living in the mountains."

"...." Alice felt hurt by Merlin's words and recalled her difficult childhood life in the great snow mountains. She immediately became angry. "Have you even looked at the current situation? Always thinking about enjoying yourself, eating and drinking wildly now. I ask you, what about next month's rent?"

A cold sweat dripped from Merlin's forehead, and he was at a loss for words.

"It's all because you squandered my savings, it's all your own fault! Still blaming me? Shameless! If you don't want to eat, then don't! I'll save it! Hmph~!" Alice snatched the bread from Merlin's mouth and decided to let him starve this time; he was too ungrateful.

"You!" Merlin frowned at Alice, still savoring the sweet taste of the apple jam.

"What about me? Do you have a problem?" Alice lifted her little face, ready to argue with Merlin to the end. She had kindly bought a jar of jam, and Merlin was still picky and fussy. It was annoying.

Merlin looked away, staring at the donkey's butt in front of him. "Alright, if you don't want to eat, fine. When we get there, I'll definitely roast your donkey and eat it!"

"What are you doing!? Don't eat my Momo! We rely on it entirely for our journey....." Alice showed hostility, like a wild dog protecting her territory.

The little donkey let out a mournful cry and suddenly knelt down, refusing to move. This sudden move nearly caused Alice and Merlin to fall off the cart.

"See? It's all because you said you were going to eat it, and it's scared to death and won't move!" Alice was furious.

"Ugh!" Merlin raised the whip beside him and狠狠ly whipped the donkey twice. "Get up! Get up now!"

"Stop it, stop it! What good will beating it do!?" Alice snatched the whip from Merlin's hand, quite protective. "You have to comfort it properly!"

"Comfort a donkey? Are you joking?" Merlin was amused by Alice's foolishness.

"Watch," Alice said, placing her hand on the donkey's butt and speaking softly, "Momo, get up. It was all a joke just now. We won't eat you. Come on, be a good boy and get up~"

To Merlin's astonishment, the donkey indeed got up again and started moving forward.

"See? I told you beating it was useless," Alice said proudly, her little nose翘ing up to the sky.

Merlin couldn't help but sweat, thinking what kind of donkey this was? Had it become a spirit?

"Did you raise this donkey yourself?"

"Yes, it was adorable when it was little. It's only a year old now and is especially obedient to me," Alice explained.

"Can it understand human speech? Are you an idiot?" Merlin said helplessly.

Alice rolled her eyes and said to the donkey in front, "Momo, is Merlin a big idiot?"

The little donkey actually responded to Alice, making a "neighing" sound, as if in agreement.

"Hehe, see? Even the donkey thinks you're an idiot~" Alice laughed, feeling that this donkey was worth raising.

Merlin didn't say anything, but the veins on his forehead were faintly visible as he暗暗 thought—

Just you wait.

Someday I will eat your donkey clean....

Far away.

Two figures stood in place. They were none other than two officers from the Dark Guild, the Azure Flame, Lory and Osved.

The two had been ordered by the guild master Humphrey to come here to investigate Lord Barton's acquisition of the vampire ruins map.

However, their journey had been full of misfortunes and was not going smoothly. The horse they had hired died on the way.

But now there was still a distance to the city of Galway, and relying on their legs was too slow and tiring.

Therefore, Lory and Osved decided to wait here and see if there were any passing merchant caravans, planning to directly seize a carriage.

Just then, Merlin and Alice's donkey cart caught the two's eyes, instantly giving them hope.

"Hey hey hey, a carriage is coming," Lory pushed Osved beside him.

Osved looked up, using the archer's excellent eyesight to instantly understand the situation. "What carriage? That's a donkey cart."

"Is it?" Lory was stunned, then waved his hand. "That's not important. It's a vehicle that can move. How about it? We'll use force to kill the owner and seize this cart? I'm getting so bored in this godforsaken suburb."

"Wait! Calm down a bit. The owner of this donkey cart is a bit unusual, doesn't seem like a soft target," Osved seemed to have a new discovery, making Lory lower his killing intent.

"What?" Lory, a martial artist, naturally had worse eyesight and perception than Osved.

"There are two people, one of them...." Osved paused, licked his dry lips, and frowned.

"...is a Mithril Adventurer. He doesn't seem to be weak."

title: Chapter 21 — Car Transport (Monthly Vote Bonus)
content:
Chapter 21 — Car Transport (Monthly Vote Bonus)

Volume 13 · Chapter 21

Austen noticed the mithril adventurer credential around Alice's neck and immediately lost any desire to kill and rob them.

Mithril-ranked adventurers were often quite strong, serving as the main combat forces for many guilds, making them far from easy to deal with.

But Austin and Laurie had missions to complete, so they couldn't afford to waste time on the road or get entangled with a powerful figure.

So Austin abandoned the idea of using force right away. It wasn't that he couldn't beat that mithril-ranked adventurer — it was that he feared getting caught up in trouble from which they couldn't extricate themselves.

However, Laurie still didn't understand what Austin was thinking. Impatiently, he said, "What are you afraid of!? That guy's just a single mithril adventurer. Don't tell me we two Saint-tier experts teaming up can't even win!?"

Austin shot Laurie a look and said helplessly, "We can't even be sure whether we could win. If this mithril adventurer is at the peak of Saint-tier just like the guild master, it would be difficult for both of us combined."

"That's impossible, there aren't that many peak Saint-tier folks." Laurie said wearily. "Peak monsters are all big shots of various regions. You don't just run into them easily."

"You can't rule it out completely, and... " Austin narrowed his eyes, looking at the approaching Merlin and Alice. "This mithril adventurer, who dared to choose a weak iron-level noob as a teammate, is obviously suspicious. Either he's overconfident or he's really strong."

"Huh? You're saying the other person has an iron-level teammate!? " Laurie's expression turned strange. From what he knew, mithril adventurers wouldn't team up with low-level rookies because they feared being dragged down during missions.

"Yes, not only that, that iron-level teammate is actually her husband... " Austin's expression grew awkward. He looked like the lower-level iron one was being kept as a sugar baby.

"No way, a proper mithril adventurer getting married to an iron rookie! How is that even possible! " Laurie couldn't quite believe it, but his eyesight wasn't as sharp as Austin's, so he still couldn't make out the details clearly.

"I'm not lying, it's true." Austin nodded. At first, he himself had been puzzled, wondering why someone would bring along a rookie teammate and then actually marry them. Even as a sugar baby arrangement, that was a huge investment!

"Good heavens, this world is too crazy! " A female mithril adventurer willing to marry the lowest-tier iron rank? Their social standings weren't even on the same level! " Laurie felt completely disconnected from the world, having witnessed something the most bizarre imaginable.

"Who knows what's going on? Maybe this mithril adventurer likes keeping young pretty boys?" Austin responded awkwardly.

"Probably living off a woman then. Otherwise, there's no reasonable explanation." Laurie nodded.

The two temporarily abandoned their thoughts of using force and instead chose a softer approach.

They planned to speak politely and see if they could hitch a ride, asking Merlin and Alice to give them a lift.

Alice and Merlin had obviously also noticed someone ahead, looking somewhat in a hurry.

"There are people ahead, looks like they're in some kind of trouble," Alice whispered to Merlin.

"Be careful. Running into two suspicious characters in the middle of nowhere is a bit off," Merlin whispered back.

"Mm, I know. There's a trace of pressure on them. They don't seem like ordinary people," Alice frowned slightly.

Merlin nodded and looked at the two. The pressure was hard to judge — it felt fluctuating and indistinct, either not very strong or deliberately suppressed.

Actually, traveling alone as adventurers was very dangerous, especially when bandits or some sketchy characters would occasionally jump out on the road.

But the ones they should be most wary of were the members of the Dark Guild, because while bandits might just be after money, Dark Guild members came straight for your life!

Because normal guilds and dark guilds were mortal enemies, and whenever they crossed paths, neither side would show mercy.

As Merlin and Alice's donkey cart passed by, Austin and Laurie hurriedly approached, their attitudes extremely warm.

"Hey! You there, please stop!"

Merlin tugged on the reins, bringing the donkey cart to a halt, and carefully studied the two before him.

Austin and Laurie were studying them as well, both simultaneously thinking to themselves: indeed a pretty boy, not just an iron rookie but a complete ordinary person. Joining the Adventurers Guild was probably through some nepotism.

Since they were now close enough, they could gather more information. Austin and Laurie discovered that Alice was a demon swordsman who practiced both magic and martial arts. They immediately felt it would be troublesome, but were glad they'd abandoned the idea of attacking earlier, or there'd be no way out now.

The difficulty of mastering both magic and martial arts simultaneously was great, and they would have an advantage in fights at the same tier. Whichever of Austin and Laurie stepped up for a duel, neither could expect an easy win.

"What do you want?" Alice asked sharply. Looking at the way Austin and Laurie were dressed, they didn't look like traveling merchants, nor wandering mercenaries.

"It's like this, honorable sirs. We brothers plan to go to Gaowei City to handle some matters, but we've encountered some trouble along the way. Could you possibly give us a ride? I assume you two are also heading to Gaowei City?"

Austin put on a distressed expression. The road before them was the only exit to and from Gaowei City, so he didn't need to ask Merlin and Alice in detail to know their destination.

"Trouble? What kind of trouble?" Merlin looked at the two in front of him, finding something suspicious.

"Our horse died of illness on the road, so we can only beg you to do us a favor and give us a ride to Gaowei City. We'll remember this kindness forever, and if we meet again in the future, we will definitely repay you." Austin spoke very courteously.

"Yeah, we were also surprised that our horse died on the road. If we hadn't encountered this misfortune, we certainly wouldn't have troubled you," Laurie chimed in from the side.

Merlin glanced toward the nearby area and there was indeed a carriage, with the horse already lying motionless on the ground. It seemed these two weren't lying through their teeth.

Alice felt these two people seemed normal enough, apparently without any ill intent, so she secretly asked Merlin, "What should we do? Let them get on?"

"Shouldn't, we don't know them," Merlin said, not wanting to meddle in others' affairs.

"But they look very distressed. Giving them a ride is just a small effort..."

"Stop, stop, stop!"

Alice hadn't even finished her sentence before Merlin cut her off, his expression somewhat grim. Clearly, the two had a disagreement.

Merlin thought to himself: as expected, Alice is still Alice. Her name as a mindless knight of justice is well-deserved.

"We don't know their identity. What if they're bad people? I may not think these two can cause too much trouble, but if they damage the donkey cart, it would be enough to give us a headache for a while."

"Mm, that makes sense." Alice nodded and turned to say, "No, we can't help you. I don't even know who you are, how could we possibly let you just hop on? What if you're members of the Dark Guild? Then we'd be in real trouble."

Austin and Laurie's hearts both skipped a beat, wondering whether their identities had been seen through. It was all just this woman making things up randomly.

"We're not bad people!"

"Nonsense! Who writes 'bad person' on their face?" Merlin said impatiently.

"We're just going to Gaowei City to visit old friends, nothing else. Please trust us," Austin pleaded.

"Yeah, we're in the materials business, not members of any Dark Adventurer Guild," Laurie was getting anxious too.

"Sorry." Alice pursed her lips. She simply couldn't risk the donkey cart being damaged. Out in the wilderness, if the cart broke down, they'd have to walk to Gaowei City on foot.

Merlin flicked the reins, setting the donkey cart in motion again, not even glancing back at the two pitiful figures.

"If that's the case, we can pay!" Austin called out loudly.

"Yeah! Pay, just treat it as a rental!" Laurie followed up.

Merlin reacted as if struck by lightning, quickly yanking the reins tight to stop the cart, and turned around with a sly grin, "If you were gonna pay, you should've said so earlier. Cut the chatter, get on!"

"Hey!" Alice bristled like a fluffed-up little cat, baring her teeth at Merlin in dissatisfaction, thinking to herself —

She had thought Merlin was some cautious and steady guy.

Isn't he way easier to persuade than me (:_` )?
