title: Chapter 22 — Awareness
content:
Chapter 22 — Awareness

Volume 13 · Chapter 22

Alice glared at Merlin, unhappy that he had been so easily bought by money.

She had originally offered to let them ride along, but Merlin had refused.

Now he agreed once money was given — didn't that make her the really bad guy!?

Alice rolled her eyes and poked Merlin's back with her finger.

"I'm telling you, can't you have a little integrity?"

"What's wrong with that? Helping others is a noble virtue. What's the matter with you? They just want a ride~" Merlin's mood shifted faster than flipping a page, suddenly becoming enthusiastic.

"I wanted to help them at first too, and you called me suspicious!" Alice ground her teeth in frustration, suspecting Merlin was a fake friend who could sell her out at any moment.

"Did I? I don't remember, haha." Merlin shrugged his shoulders and denied everything.

"You...." Alice gritted her teeth, genuinely wanting to smear the apple jam in her hand all over Merlin's forehead to vent her anger.

"What are you two standing around for? Get in." Merlin waved at Oswd and Laurie below. "We're not far from Gowei City anymore. I think we'll arrive today."

"Okay, okay." The two hurriedly climbed into the carriage and sat in the back, thinking—

This man is so materialistic...

I thought he was someone with backbone...

The group got along relatively peacefully on the journey, with no disputes arising.

Oswd and Laurie had no intention of causing trouble and simply rode quietly.

As long as they could reach Gowei City peacefully, fighting would hardly be worth the loss.

This close-range encounter made the two even more surprised.

They could feel the faint dragon aura radiating from Alice, growing more confused by the moment.

What was wrong with this woman? Did she cultivate dragon magic?

Oswd and Laurie couldn't figure it out, and the more they thought about it, the more unapproachable this silver-haired woman seemed.

Although Alice faced away from the two strangers, she could sense their gazes lingering on her, and she felt some resistance welling up inside.

Merlin appeared calm on the surface, but in his mind he was plotting how to squeeze money out of those two idiots.

For Merlin, this was second nature. If they needed him, they should expect to pay up.

"Two gentlemen, I wonder how much you plan to pay us?"

"This..." Oswd hesitated. He hadn't brought much money on this trip. "You've done us a favor, so it certainly won't be little. How about one gold coin? That's enough to hire a quite nice carriage."

"How could one gold coin be enough? There are no other carriages out in the middle of nowhere, so we essentially have a monopoly. How could a monopoly price be just one gold coin? You're really joking." Merlin spoke with an loaded tone.

Alice's expression stiffened. Here we go again, this guy is trying to extort people once more. Just pretend I didn't hear that.

Doing wrong things alongside Merlin always filled Alice with a heavy sense of guilt; she felt sorry for others.

"One gold coin still isn't enough? Then how much do you want?" Oswd asked in confusion, thinking a mere Iron-rank novice had too many strange quirks.

"About a thousand times that, at least?" Merlin said without batting an eye as he extorted them.

"Pfft!" Oswd nearly spat out his drink, his face full of disbelief. "What!? A hundred gold coins for a donkey cart? Are you kidding me?"

"Do I look like I'm joking?" Merlin turned his head, his expression utterly serious.

"Sir, a thousand gold coins could purchase a chariot pulled by pureblood steeds. We're merely offering a donkey cart. Isn't this asking far too much? This is clearly a case of opening your mouth wide like a lion." Oswd felt this man had enormous nerve. If this were usually, he would have already killed such a lawless guy.

"That's right! I told you not to push your luck! Do you really think we're easy to bully!?" Laurie couldn't hold back any longer.

Alice beside them covered her face in embarrassment, at a loss for words. Merlin was too bold — his opening bid was basically robbery!

"Dislike our donkey cart? Fine, get off now and don't ride." Merlin said coldly.

"You!!"

Laurie had a hot temper and was angry enough to resort to violence, but Oswd held him back.

"Hey hey hey, stay calm."

Oswd thought it over. It was better to prioritize the bigger picture. If they failed to complete their mission, the Guild master, that madman, would impose severe punishment.

Losing some money now wasn't such a bad thing. The main thing was completing the mission — that was what mattered most.

"Fine, you say a thousand gold coins, then it shall be a thousand gold coins. We're willing to pay."

Alice's expression became uncomfortable. She thought, they're actually agreeing to such an unreasonable demand!? Shouldn't we resist people like Merlin to the end!?

"That's the spirit. Now, if you get off, who knows if you'll find another ride later. Actually, we're also taking quite a risk. If you were bad people, we'd suffer huge losses." Merlin said with a smile.

Oswd and Laurie sat with dark faces, silently cursing Merlin's ancestors across eighteen generations in their hearts.

But Oswd figured they still needed to chat with these two. What if Merlin got annoyed and raised the price again?

"I wonder what the two of you are going to Gowei City for?"

"We?" Merlin thought about it and figured it was fine to say. "We're going to Gowei City to find Baron Barton."

"Tsk!" Alice glanced at Merlin and nudged him with her elbow, trying to stop him from talking carelessly.

Adventurers' missions were secret — how could they just blab to strangers? Fortunately, Merlin hadn't said too much.

But the moment he said it, Oswd and Laurie were internally shocked, since their destination was also that same Baron Barton.

The two parties' purposes completely collided, and they were even sitting in the same carriage. The coincidence was hard to believe.

"I wonder what business you have with Baron Barton?" Oswd narrowed his eyes and asked tentatively.

"Are you royal knights? Investigating my background? We're all heading to Gowei City, so it's better not to dig too deep." Merlin said calmly. The map to the vampire ruins was a great secret — he couldn't just spill it everywhere.

"R-right... I suppose that's our impoliteness then." Oswd forced a smile that didn't reach his eyes.

Alice felt somewhat relieved. It seemed Merlin still had some sense of propriety.

However, the two of them started whispering behind his back, clearly very interested in Merlin's search for Baron Barton.

"What are they looking for Baron Barton about?" Laurie asked secretly.

"I don't know, but it must be something extraordinary." Oswd's eyes grew strange.

"Could it be... also for the blood tribe ruins?" Laurie asked tentatively.

"It's possible. Since we were able to obtain clues, others are likely the same." Oswd analyzed.

"What should we do then? If these two adventurers are also after the ruins, conflict is inevitable." Laurie frowned deeply.

Oswd fell silent. Although he tried to avoid conflict, it seemed impossible to escape. Everyone appeared to be heading toward the same goal.

"Regardless of whether they're after the ruins or not, it's better to kill a thousand by mistake than let one slip through."

"Since there's a possibility of fighting later, why not strike first now?"

"Prepare to make a move. No matter the cost, eliminate those two adventurers...."

title: Chapter 23 — Inferior
content:
Chapter 23 — Inferior

Volume 13 · Chapter 23

Merlin and Alice completely failed to notice the approaching danger, still trusting these two people.

Oswid and Laurie slowly gathered fighting spirit in their hands, planning a sudden attack to catch the other party off guard.

However, Merlin's perception was still very powerful; he sensed a faint pressure from behind.

"Hmm?"

Just as Merlin was about to turn back to check the situation, someone broke the silence.

"Wait, please wai—t, could you give me a ride? I need to get to Gaowei City."

This sudden change startled Oswid and Laurie instantly; they hurriedly withdrew their fighting spirit and sat obediently in the back.

Merlin thought, what's going on today? Why are so many people suddenly asking for a ride halfway?

He lifted his eyelids to look, and the person before him made him freeze—it was a rather familiar guy.

"Ah... the directionally challenged..."

"...." Johnson stared blankly, and upon seeing it was Merlin, his expression immediately turned strange.

".... Big Brother Merlin, why are you in Ireland?!"

The party of four became five, and the carriage instantly became somewhat crowded.

Neither Merlin nor Alice expected to run into this Irish magic prodigy halfway.

This really is a different kind of fate; Ireland is so big, yet they bumped into each other on the road.

Since Johnson was an acquaintance, Merlin and Alice didn't hesitate and let him onto the carriage directly.

But Oswid and Laurie in the back felt tremendous pressure, and for a while neither dared to act rashly.

Originally, facing Alice—a Mithril adventurer—Oswid and Laurie still had some confidence in striking first.

Now another Mithril adventurer, Johnson, had been added to the carriage; no matter how confident the two were, they didn't dare act recklessly at a time like this.

Because the title of Copy Magician Johnson carried far more weight than Alice's; don't be fooled by his mere teenage appearance—his strength could not be underestimated.

Oswid and Laurie had no choice but to behave themselves and think of another way to eliminate Merlin and Alice.

"Brat, what are you doing here?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"Don't call me brat! It's really unpleasant!" Johnson's face darkened; he clearly didn't want to see Merlin, as it always reminded him of his previous humiliation. "I'm an adventurer from Gaowei City; what's strange about me appearing here?"

"Alright, but did you get lost again? You don't even recognize the roads in your own hometown, do you?" Merlin wore a playful expression.

"Who's lost?! I'm not directionally challenged, I just... just love the scenery along the way too much." Johnson lifted his head and said in a chuunibyou manner, "Today, Ireland's wind is still so clamorous~"

"If you're not lost, then why are you miserably begging for a ride?" Merlin retorted, clearly meaning to undermine him.

"You're so noisy!" Johnson gritted his teeth in anger, looking extremely aggressive.

"Speaking of which, little brother Johnson just finished a mission and is heading back, right?" Alice spoke in a big-sister tone.

"Hah! Don't call me little brother; that annoys me even more than brat, you padded-chest wom—" Johnson curled his lip, his face full of disdain.

"Uh...." Alice's face flushed red with anger, an urge to strangle Johnson rising in her heart. Such a vicious mouth at such a young age—he must have suffered some trauma in childhood, to have not a single friend.

Johnson's gaze swept over the Mithril adventurer badge on Alice's neck, then he was greatly startled. He probed the aura on Alice more carefully, and his whole demeanor turned sour.

Alice's current strength was almost on par with Johnson's; both were sprinting toward the peak of Saint-tier.

"... You've already become a Saint-tier expert? Why so fast? Clearly half a year ago you were just a high-stage rookie..."

Seeing Johnson's astonished look, Alice's momentum immediately rose, and she said smugly, "What's so strange about that? This big sister is a genius too; you should learn from me."

Merlin silently rolled his eyes at the side, thinking, what bullshit genius? If not for the Frost Saint Dragon's inheritance crystal, she'd probably still be a nobody.

"How is that possible? Merely half a year to become a Saint-tier expert—this speed can no longer be described as genius, it's... did you cheat?" Johnson narrowed his eyes, finding Alice's terrifying growth rate hard to believe. Half a year ago she was a high-stage rookie he looked down on; now how did she become a Mithril adventurer?!

Oswid and Laurie exchanged a glance, both seeing shock in the other's eyes.

Reaching Saint-tier in just half a year—isn't that a bit too terrifying?

Both felt a little fortunate; good thing they hadn't acted just now, or they might have kicked an iron plate.

"What's there to be so surprised about? If you admit you're envious of me, this big sister can teach you my cultivation insights." Alice smiled meaningfully, clearly wanting to suppress this little brat.

"What nonsense! Don't get too cocky! Don't think just because you're a Saint-tier expert you're my equal; in seniority, I'm your senior!" Johnson said very unwillingly, but inside he was panicking, always feeling he would be crushed by Alice in the future.

There was already a Merlin riding on Johnson's head and shitting; now there had to be an Alice too?

And a husband-and-wife joint suppression at that—the humiliation multiplied. Johnson's pride couldn't accept it.

A few black lines popped out on Alice's forehead; she thought, why does this brat have such severe self-esteem issues? The slightest imbalance and he throws a tantrum.

"Don't celebrate too early. I'm a magic genius; sooner or later I'll advance again and leave you mediocre lot unable to catch up." Not wanting to dwell on this topic and disturb his mindset, Johnson asked another question. "By the way, what are you guys suddenly doing in Ireland?"

"We have a mission; we need to find Baron Barton." Merlin explained concisely.

"Ah? Looking for Baron Barton?" Johnson froze noticeably, clearly showing concern.

"What's wrong? You seem to know something?" Alice detected Johnson's oddness.

"Nothing much. Just that Baron Barton's reputation isn't good, and his character is indeed terrible." Johnson spoke without any reservation.

"How so? Tell us in detail." Merlin turned his head back.

"Baron Barton is extremely greedy and has a severe class mentality; he oppresses subordinates and commoners, causing widespread resentment. Even my father was made things difficult by him, but given my father's powerful background, he didn't dare go too far." Johnson summarized simply.

"I see...." Alice knitted her brows; she hadn't even met this Baron Barton yet and already felt a hint of trouble.

"Relax, we just have some business with him; we don't intend to have deep dealings." Merlin replied indifferently, thinking that with Count Austin's letter of introduction, they shouldn't be made things difficult.

"Regardless...." Johnson paused, kindly reminding Merlin and Alice—

"Dealing with that lowly man, I advise you to keep your guard up.

"If that guy shows his greedy face, he won't even spare his own kin."

title: Chapter 24 — First Strike (Moon Vote Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 24 — First Strike (Moon Vote Bonus Chapter)

Volume 13 · Chapter 24

Merlin and Alice did not continue the topic, as continuing to discuss it might reveal the details of their mission.

However, this Baron Barton was not a decent person at all; without a doubt, he would certainly cause no end of trouble for what lay ahead.

Johnson finally shifted his attention to Oswald and Laurie, who had remained silent throughout, acting strangely gloomy.

“Those two...

“As for them? They’re much like you, just hitching a ride.” Merlin explained briefly.

“Yes, yes, our horses died on the road, so we had to trouble others for help,” Oswald replied politely.

“Indeed, it’s quite embarrassing. There are too many unscrupulous merchants these days,” Laurie added with a smile.

“Hmm?” Johnson frowned, feeling that the two men before him looked somewhat familiar, as if he had seen them somewhere before?

Oswald and Laurie felt deeply guilty, their eyes darting around, unable to meet Johnson’s gaze directly.

“Haven’t we met before?” Johnson asked in confusion.

“No, no, we’ve never met,” Oswald quickly denied.

“That’s right, we come from very far away; how could we have met? Haha,” Laurie said awkwardly, scratching his head.

Johnson still felt that the two men before him were somewhat strange. He lowered his head and pondered carefully. Such familiar faces must have been seen somewhere.

He soon recalled some details: the Guild had portraits of wanted criminals, and naturally, members of the Dark Guild were among them.

Although there were slight differences, the two men before him were basically similar in appearance, which suddenly made Johnson become alert.

“You two... aren’t members of the Dark Guild, are you?”

Confronted by Johnson’s direct question, both men’s hearts skipped a beat, becoming extremely tense.

If their identities were discovered, peaceful coexistence would be difficult, and a fierce battle would ensue.

“No, no, how could we possibly be members of the Dark Guild?!” Laurie hurriedly denied.

“Exactly, if we were members of the Dark Guild, how would we dare to walk around openly?” Oswald smiled, though his palms were sweating.

Johnson’s eyes still filled with suspicion; the more he looked, the more they resembled members of the Dark Guild. However, since they were sitting in the same carriage as Merlin and Alice, it might also be an illusion.

Alice looked at Oswald and Laurie, feeling that their reactions were somewhat abnormal, overly nervous.

“They are material merchants, visiting friends in Gowen City,” Merlin said calmly, without much suspicion.

“..... Well.....” Hearing Merlin say this, Johnson slightly retracted his doubts, thinking—

Maybe it’s all my imagination?

After all, portrait paintings are often inaccurate.

The travelers kept pushing forward, and finally, just as the sun set below the horizon, they safely arrived at Gowen City in Zhou Ireland.

The evening sunlight was exceptionally rich and solemn, as if pure molten gold had been poured over the majestic Gowen City.

This place was not the most prosperous city in Ireland, roughly comparable to Rexem, but its city defenses seemed quite good.

The bricks on the walls were of superior stone quality, sufficient to withstand numerous attacking enemies.

Compared to this, Rexem’s city was truly old; it seemed Count Austin was not very concerned about defense.

In reality, it was because Baron Barton, as the city lord, had amassed considerable wealth. Fearing robbery by bandits, he had invested heavily in constructing the city defenses.

After entering the city, Oswald and Laurie took the lead in bidding farewell, intending to attend to other matters—

“Your Excellency, we still have matters to attend to, so we will take our leave first,” Oswald pretended to be a good-natured man.

“Very well, then... you understand, right?” Merlin casually rubbed his fingers together, signaling that payment was due.

“I understand, I understand,” Oswald looked back at Laurie behind him, hinting for him to take out the money to settle the matter peacefully.

Laurie, with a dark face and full of dissatisfaction, took out a bag of gold coins and handed them to Merlin, feeling that this trip had been a huge loss.

Merlin opened the bag and glanced inside, instantly knowing that the amount was approximately correct; the other party was still a person of credit.

He had thought there would be many twists and turns; Merlin was even prepared to use force, yet it turned out to be completely unnecessary.

Alice stood by silently, thinking, Oh my god! They actually paid? Making money is too easy! ? Clearly, I am different from Merlin; this guy survives solely by scamming and deceiving. How unfair!

Johnson, standing nearby, didn’t say anything, but he understood this was some kind of transaction agreed upon earlier. Whether good or bad, it was best not to get involved; this was an unwritten rule among adventurers.

Merlin nodded satisfactorily, surprised by how smooth it had gone. Although he was not a good person himself, he had to praise the other party’s credibility.

“Alright, then please take care, Your Excellencies. We won’t see you off.”

“Goodbye, perhaps we shall meet again,” Oswald said with a meaningful tone, and then he and Laurie departed on their own.

Once the two had distanced themselves from Merlin’s group, Laurie finally couldn’t hold back and asked Oswald.

“That kid was obviously scamming us. Are we just going to let it go? We are people of the Dark Guild; under normal circumstances, such bastards would have already been flayed alive. How could they still be hopping around freely?”

“Laurie, you are always too impatient. It seems the Guild Master was right to send me with you.” Oswald paused, speaking slowly, “Isn’t it just losing some money to avoid disaster? What’s the big deal? We must strive to avoid any troubles we can prevent. Is it worth tearing relations with that despicable man over 1,000 gold coins?”

“But I just can’t swallow this anger. Isn’t it true we could defeat them? As long as we seize the opportunity, we still have a chance,” Laurie said defiantly, likely experiencing this humiliation for the first time.

“What’s the use of being brave and aggressive? Don’t forget our objective, which is to investigate the Vampire ruins!” Oswald emphasized, analyzing, “Let alone whether we can win against those two Mithril-rank adventurers; even if we could, we would pay a certain price and risk exposure of our identities. At that point, the difficulty of completing our mission would increase. Do you understand that the losses would outweigh the gains?”

“Tsk!” Laurie clicked his tongue in annoyance. Although displeased, he had to admit that Oswald’s words were reasonable.

“Our primary goal is to investigate the Vampire ruins. Paying some price for this is justified. Don’t forget, if the mission fails, that madman the Guild Master will not spare us,” Oswald said seriously.

“But those two adventurers seem to have the same objective as us. Is it really okay to just let them be?” Laurie said unwillingly.

“For now, there’s no need to worry about those two guys....” Oswald thought for a moment, deciding on the next plan—

“We will act first and go meet the drunkard who provided the clue.”

“If those two adventurers become obstacles to our actions, then eliminate them at any cost...”

title: Chapter 25 — Hatred
content:
Chapter 25 — Hatred

Volume 13 · Chapter 25

“Hmph~”

Merlin kept weighing the money bag in his hand, humming a cheerful tune. Obviously, he was delighted to have inexplicably earned an extra 1,000 gold coins.

Alice looked at Merlin’s smug expression and felt somewhat displeased inside; after all, when he conned and deceived people, she felt like an accomplice.

However, 1,000 gold was already a considerable sum, and Alice was also tempted, wondering how she could monopolize Merlin’s wealth.

Johnson stood by, watching Merlin with a blank expression, and suddenly asked, “Brother Merlin, did you swindle those two people?”

“Tsk!” Merlin turned around dissatisfied, emphasizing, “That wasn’t swindling; that was a transaction where both parties were satisfied. Don’t think of me as so bad, okay?”

“Ummm...” Johnson was speechless, thinking that charging 1,000 gold for a ride was clearly taking advantage of someone’s misfortune!

“Alice, see? Making money is this easy. You should learn from me~” Merlin said in a teasing tone.

“Learn my ass! Shameless!” Alice cursed, feeling deeply unbalanced inside.

“Hehe, just take that naivety into your grave,” Merlin smiled. Every time he saw Alice frustrated, he felt inexplicably happy!

Alice was so angry she couldn’t speak, thinking, I only swindled them out of 1,000 gold, yet he doesn’t feel ashamed but rather proud? Demons are indeed demons; a dog can’t stop eating shit!

“I’ve arrived.” Johnson stopped walking; it seemed they had reached the entrance of the Adventurers Guild in Highway City.

Merlin and Alice stopped and looked over. They found that the Adventurers Guild here was similar to Rexem’s, just a bit more calm and orderly.

“Then we shall part ways here,” Merlin said calmly.

“Uh... aren’t you planning to come in and sit for a while, visit our guild?” Johnson asked tentatively.

“But we still have missions to attend to, and we need to hurry. Sorry about that,” Alice replied apologetically.

“Yeah, kid, we’re very busy. Besides, what’s there to see in a guild? How boring?” Merlin shrugged his shoulders.

Alice shot Merlin a glare, thinking, Can’t this guy speak properly?! No wonder he often makes people angry; it’s because his mouth is too foul!

“It’s not like that. It’s my father who wants to meet you...” Johnson hesitated.

Alice and Merlin both paused, surprised that Johnson’s father wanted to see them. They heard that this man had even compiled magic textbooks.

“Earlier, when I dealt with that alchemist, didn’t you help me a lot? So my father has been wanting to invite you to dinner to thank you,” Johnson muttered.

“I see. I didn’t expect you to realize that you received our care,” Alice smiled, feeling much better inside.

“Don’t misunderstand. I mostly received care from Brother Merlin, nothing to do with you. I just included you out of politeness when thanking,” Johnson said with a blank expression.

“....” Alice felt struck by lightning, thinking this child was really not cute at all. What was he showing off for?

“Oh? To treat us to a meal, fine. When we finish what we’re doing, we can come over,” Merlin nodded, acting superior.

“Don’t overthink it. Our family never wants to owe anyone favors. That’s all. Then...” Johnson waved his hand, turned around, and walked into the guild. “See you later.”

“Shall we go meet that Baron Barton?” Merlin said to Alice as he turned back.

“Mm. Younger brother Johnson said that Baron Barton has bad character. We should be careful,” Alice followed Merlin.

“Rest assured, I’m quite good at dealing with villains,” Merlin tossed the gold coins in his hand.

Alice nodded, seeing the money bag thrown high into the air, and snatched it away in one move.

“What are you doing!? Give it back. This is mine,” Merlin frowned, feeling that Alice, having grown familiar with him, was starting to push her luck.

“Yours? The carriage was mine. They rode my carriage, so the money naturally belongs to me,” Alice said righteously, quietly putting the money bag away.

“What kind of joke is this? I worked hard on my tongue to get this money. I put in labor!” Veins bulged on Merlin’s forehead.

“This is only a part of it here,” Alice paused, then laughed softly. “Don’t worry, I won’t embezzle your share. I’m just keeping it safe for you for now.”

Damn it, you’re trying to fool ghosts with that lie! I’ve told you N times,” Merlin was extremely dissatisfied inside, feeling maliciously suppressed—

“The money always goes to you, and it has never come out again!”

At the Baron’s Mansion in Highway City.

This was Baron Barton’s residence, appearing extremely grand.

It stood out uniquely in the entire Highway City, giving off a luxurious feeling.

In the reception hall at that moment, the mansion’s butler was secretly receiving two members of the Dark Guild.

There were only three people present, and it seemed their conversation content was highly confidential, impossible for others to know.

“What is your name?” Oswald asked.

“Steve.”

“Haha, I didn’t expect that the person who revealed the Vampire Ruins to us would be the Baron’s butler. How ironic~” Laurie showed a mysterious smile.

Opposite Oswald and Laurie sat a middle-aged man with a serious expression. Looking at his straight posture and stern demeanor, he was likely a former military officer.

Steve was the butler of this mansion, having served Baron Barton for three years. He usually appeared very amiable, but unexpectedly took the initiative to contact the Dark Guild.

“That’s right. I pretended to be drunk and revealed that the Baron possessed a treasure map to the Vampire Ruins,” Steve said calmly.

“You’re an interesting guy. To make such a move betraying the Baron, it seems you have great grievances against him,” Oswald narrowed his eyes and said meaningfully.

“Yes, I hate Baron Barton to the bone. I hope this bastard dies soon!” Steve clenched his fists, anger surging on his face.

“Aren’t you the Baron’s butler? Taking his money while hating him so much—that’s not the mindset a servant should have~” Oswald became increasingly curious about Steve.

“Mr. Oswald, I think you understand that everyone has secrets difficult to utter. I do too. You only need to know that many people in this world wish for Baron Barton’s death, and I am one of them. Serving as the butler of this mansion is merely to lurk beside the Baron. When the time is ripe, I will definitely deliver a fatal blow to him!”

“Oh? This killing intent is genuine. It seems you truly are the Baron’s enemy,” Oswald narrowed his eyes and said in a tempting tone. “So, by deliberately leaking information to attract us here, what exactly do you desire us to do for you in your heart?”

“I hope you can...” Butler Steve paused, then said fiercely through gritted teeth—

“Send Baron Barton, this bastard, to hell!”

title: Chapter 26 — A Visit
content:
Chapter 26 — A Visit

Volume 13 · Chapter 26

Steve's words sent a shock through Osward and Laurie, who stared at the man, the Baron of Barton's butler, in stunned silence.

Steve's eyes brimmed with unmasked hatred, his clenched fists white-knuckled, a palpable aura of killing intent radiating from him.

"Hahahaha, you're quite the interesting one. A servant, yet you wish to kill your master?" Laurie laughed loudly, slapping his thigh.

"Mr. Steve, if I may ask, why are you so determined to see the Baron of Barton dead?" Osward inquired with curiosity.

"That's none of your business for now. All you need to know is that I want the Baron of Barton to descend to hell. Since you're after the vampire clan's treasure, and I want the Baron dead, our interests align to some extent. We can cooperate."

"Alright," Osward nodded, speaking leisurely. "So, you deliberately leaked the clues to the vampire clan's ruins to get us to eliminate the Baron of Barton?"

"Exactly. As a reward, I can assist you in obtaining the map to the vampire clan's ruins. After all, you know nothing about the Baron of Barton. My assistance certainly won't leave you empty-handed."

The two exchanged a glance before leaning in to whisper to each other.

"Can we trust what this guy is saying?" Laurie asked in a low voice.

"I don't see any major issues. His hatred for the Baron of Barton was genuine just now," Osward nodded.

"Then we agree to kill the Baron of Barton, and let him assist us?" Laurie probed with a tentative tone.

"It's unavoidable. As this man said, we know nothing about the Baron of Barton, and we're completely in the dark. With his assistance, obtaining the map to the vampire clan's ruins would be much easier."

"That's true..." Laurie rubbed his chin, thinking that a little cooperation wouldn't hurt, everyone had their own needs.

"Besides, the boss told us to leave no traces of our actions, so every single person in Highgate must be killed, including this butler Steve. We're just killing a baron提前." Osward smiled, having already decided not to spare a single person in the city.

"Haha, right, almost forgot. Not a single person in this city can be left alive." Laurie smiled evilly.

Members of the Dark Guild usually acted decisively. To cover their tracks, indiscriminate massacres were the norm.

After their discussion, the two straightened up and looked at Steve with utmost seriousness, showing no signs of their intention to massacre the city after obtaining the map.

"Alright, Mr. Steve, we agree to cooperate with you. As long as you help us obtain the map to the vampire clan's ruins, we have no problem helping you kill the Baron of Barton," Osward responded earnestly to Steve.

"Are you really sure? The Baron has a Saint-tier mercenary protecting him, and he seems to be quite strong," Steve, an ordinary man, couldn't discern true strength. But since they were both Saint-tier强者, a fight would likely be difficult to resolve.

"...Osward chuckled nervously and waved his hand. "Laurie, tell Mr. Steve what we do."

"Mr. Steve, we know exactly what level of强者 a local baron can hire. Besides..." Laurie patted his chest earnestly. "We are members of the Dark Guild, born for killing, you understand?"

"Alright, if you say it's no problem, then the cooperation is set. I hope we can work together pleasantly," Steve nodded, believing the two men.

Osward suddenly remembered Merlin and Alice from their group and curiously asked, "Mr. Steve, if I may ask, how many people did you tell about the map being on the Baron?"

"I don't know, I can't remember. I think quite a few people heard, but most didn't believe it," Steve said helplessly.

"Why do such a stupid thing? I suspect this is why Alice and Merlin, those two adventurers, were drawn here," Laurie felt somewhat dissatisfied in his heart.

"I wanted to kill the Baron of Barton, but my own strength was limited, so I naturally had to seek external help," Steve paused and mused. "I planned to use the fact that the Baron had treasure to attract greedy people to kill him. That's all."

"啧!" Laurie tutted, thinking this had completely complicated things. Originally, they could have steadily obtained the map, but now they had to be on guard against others dividing their attention.

"Mr. Steve, you really didn't need to do this. It will only backfire," Osward said seriously.

"I had no choice. To provoke others' greed, I had to do it this way," Steve shrugged his hands.

Osward sighed, accepting the situation, and asked instead, "What about the map? Is it on the Baron?"

"Yes, that map has always been in his chest, preserved like the most expensive treasure. He's also interested in the vampire clan's ruins and is planning to recruit a group of people to explore and obtain more wealth," Steve said calmly.

"What!?" Laurie immediately became tense, feeling the situation was troublesome. If the Baron of Barton himself went to search for the vampire clan's ruins, he would become an obstacle to the Azure Flame.

"That map was obtained by the Baron three years ago at great cost. Initially, he thought it was just scrap paper, but after I secretly spread the news, many people became interested. The Baron then realized the map was a priceless treasure and valued it even more," Steve recalled.

"Then what are we waiting for!? We absolutely cannot let the Baron of Barton get there first. We must kill him immediately and seize the map!" Laurie stood up angrily, the situation becoming increasingly urgent.

"There's no need to rush. The Baron isn't at his estate these days; he's out on business. He should return soon, and then we'll have the opportunity to obtain the map," Steve explained the current situation.

"Damn!" Laurie swung his fist, forcing himself to calm down, thinking that the gods had been against him lately.

Just as the three were discussing热烈ly, a servant knocked on the door from outside and entered.

He first bowed slightly to Steve, the butler, and then reported seriously.

"Mr. Steve, there are two guests outside who want to see Lord Barton."

"Who are they?" Steve frowned and looked up.

"According to the guards... two adventurers from Lexham..."

title: Chapter 27 — Burned Down (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 27 — Burned Down (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 13 · Chapter 27

Outside the Baron's residence.

Merlin and Alice came here to wait for an audience.

Although they knew it was impolite to come so late to see Baron Button, they still felt it was better to see the treasure map of the vampire ruins early.

Merlin waited for a while but saw no one. He immediately lost patience and muttered to himself, "Strange, why so slow? Let's just barge in."

"Don't! Wait a bit. Can't you have a little patience?" Alice said, puffing up with annoyance from the side.

"It's been long enough already. If no one comes to let us in soon, we'll use force," Merlin said casually.

"Please, it's only been two minutes and you're already this anxious? Do you think you're the king? What if Baron Button is on the toilet and has to rush out to see you bare-assed?" Alice mocked Merlin for having no patience.

A bead of cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead, and he really didn't want to see a middle-aged man's bare butt.

"Besides, we're here to borrow the treasure map. We need to be polite and avoid any impropriety. Didn't younger brother Johnson say Baron Button has a bad temper?" Alice chattered away by his side like a little secretary.

"Ah, you're so annoying. Say two fewer words, my ears are already growing calluses." Merlin expressionlessly used his pinky finger to scratch his ear.

Alice's expression turned conflicted. She thought to herself, where was she being annoying? Wasn't she just kindly reminding Merlin? Truly, no good deed goes unpunished in this family.

The Baron's mansion gates slowly opened, and Steve walked out. He glanced directly past Merlin, but when he saw the mithril adventurer's proof on Alice's neck, he immediately became solemn and asked politely,

"Are you two here to see the Baron, my lord?"

"That's right. We need to see Baron Button. It's very important," Alice nodded and said.

"What a pity. Baron Button went out on an inspection a few days ago and hasn't returned yet," Steve said in a slightly apologetic tone.

Alice was taken aback, thinking, No way? What a coincidence? We finally came to Highweal City, and the Baron isn't even here!

"Tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue and pressed further, "Then when exactly will he be back?"

"It should be within a few days. Not too long," Steve answered truthfully.

Merlin and Alice felt a little relieved, seeing they wouldn't have to wait too long.

"May I ask what brings you two here? If it's appropriate, I can inform the Baron," Steve said, putting on a very amiable face.

Merlin and Alice glanced at each other. Feeling he was the Baron's steward, they decided it wouldn't hurt to say, as long as they could see Baron Button.

So Alice looked at Steve and earnestly stated their purpose, "We heard from Earl Austin in Rexham that Baron Button recently obtained a treasure map of Dracula's ruins. We'd like to take a look; there might be information we need on it."

"Oh~" Steve said, immediately assuming he had successfully attracted new treasure hunters with the news he'd released.

"Here is a letter of proof from Earl Austin. Please give it to Baron Button when he returns. We'll come back then." Alice pulled out a letter from her pocket, the bright red wax seal still bearing the Austin family crest.

"I will certainly convey everything to the Baron," Steve said, nodding as he took the letter from Alice.

"Then we'll visit another day."

Alice nodded, pulling Merlin, who was still unhappy, away.

Merlin was just annoyed that Baron Button wasn't home, making the trip for nothing.

Steward Steve watched Merlin and Alice's backs, his eyes flickering continuously, lost in his own thoughts.

He looked at the letter in his hand, seemingly already having other plans.

"Tsk, not even home. What a pain." Merlin couldn't help but complain on the road.

"What can you do about that? Everyone has their own business. He's not going to just sit at home waiting for your grand arrival, is he?" Alice's words carried a sharp edge.

"No need for that. I was just thinking, why would the lord of a city be running around? Probably because there aren't enough troublemakers, leaving him with so much free time," Merlin said maliciously.

"You're just looking for chaos, aren't you?" Alice frowned, feeling Merlin had problematic values.

"No, don't think of me as that dark, okay? I'm a good person." Merlin spread his hands, looking utterly sincere.

Alice's expression was complex. Too lazy to criticize him, she asked about their next move, "Where should we go now? Since Baron Button isn't back, let's find a place to stay first."

"Didn't that brat Johnson just offer to host us? Perfect, we can go there. It'll even save us the cost of lodging." Merlin said, hugging his own arms with a meaningful tone. "As the one who saved Johnson's life, I'm sure I'll receive the highest规格 treatment."

"Umm..." Alice pursed her lips, hesitantly evaluating, "I feel like you..."

"Your face is inexplicably getting thicker."

Steward Steve didn't rush back to the parlor. Instead, he went to a secluded part of the Baron's mansion.

After thinking for a moment, he managed to tear open the envelope and read the contents.

This was a personal letter from Earl Austin, which neither Merlin nor Alice had read yet.

The entire letter was written in the tone of a superior addressing a subordinate.

It didn't contain any special information, nor did it mention the family's Dracula curse.

Instead, it instructed Baron Button to show the vampire ruins treasure map to Merlin and Alice, giving them every convenience.

If necessary, the map should be handed over to Merlin and Alice, and the Austin family would compensate Baron Button later.

Roughly, these were the contents. While it didn't seem crucial, it proved that Merlin and Alice's identities would receive significant help.

Steve fell into deep thought. He didn't believe these two proper adventurers would engage in some evil plot to help him assassinate Baron Button.

However, Oswald and Laurie could, but they had only agreed to help after obtaining the vampire ruins treasure map.

Now, Merlin and Alice had arrived with Earl Austin's proof letter, giving them a more legitimate and direct priority to take the map.

Conflict and contradiction immediately arose. These two groups had come for the same goal, and a choice had to be made.

After much deliberation, Steve felt the outcome was clear. Oswald and Laurie's group would be more beneficial to his objectives.

So, Steve took the proof letter from Merlin and Alice, lit it, and burned it to ashes.

He watched the flames flicker, the ashes rustling down, and murmured to himself,

"You were sent by Earl Austin, you say?"

"Who knows?"

"As long as I stubbornly deny it, you'll just be suspicious individuals from Rexham."

"Even if you contact Earl Austin again, this time is enough for me."

"My plan to assassinate Baron Button is flawless; I won't allow anyone to sabotage it."

title: Chapter 28 — The Banquet
content:
Chapter 28 — The Banquet

Volume 13 · Chapter 28

Steve returned to the lounge from outside, intending to continue discussing the next plan with Oswald and Laura.

However, Oswald and Laura were very attentive to what Steve had just said outside, wanting to know the specific purposes of Merlin and Alice.

"Mr. Steve, I wonder what those two adventurers outside wanted from you?" Oswald asked tentatively.

"They want the baron's map, just like you," Steve answered truthfully.

Oswald and Laura both felt a jolt in their hearts; sure enough, as expected, everyone's purposes were the same, but the map only exists once and cannot be given away; conflict between the two forces was clearly inevitable.

"Did you agree to them?" Laura questioned.

"Mr. Steve, I hope you can see the situation clearly. Between us and those two adventurers just now, you can only choose one side," Oswald said very seriously.

"I know, of course I'll choose your side. Those two adventurers simply can't help me kill Baron Barton," Steve lifted his head, looking at the two seriously, "As long as you fulfill your promise, help me get rid of Baron Barton, I—will definitely hand over the map to you."

"That's good." Oswald secretly let out a sigh of relief, feeling that Steve was still somewhat reasonable, knowing that doing dirty work like killing for profit was more reliable to entrust to the Dark Guild, "Don't worry, killing, we are professionals."

Laura still had some misgivings, secretly telling Oswald, "What should we do next? Should we let those two adventurers continue their actions?"

No way, the baron hasn't returned yet; we can first remove the obstacles on the road to success," Oswald thought for a moment, and already had a decision in his heart.

"Within these few days, we'll find an opportunity to send those two adventurers to hell!"

The dinner wasn't held in the guild.

Johnson heard that Alice and Merlin were going to stay in High City for a few days, and imitating the adults, he showed them hospitality, letting them stay in his house for a while.

At a certain residence, Johnson opened the door with a key and led a path in, "Come in."

Merlin and Alice, carrying a few greetings, walked in and began to look around Johnson's house.

Johnson's house wasn't particularly luxurious, but it was definitely big and spacious, two stories tall, looking like an old mansion from the outside.

Inside, it seemed to be in a retro style, appearing solemn and elegant, several streets away from Merlin and Alice's residence.

However, Johnson's house gave a feeling of a library; the four walls of the first floor were filled with all kinds of books.

Many books were piled on the ground, although giving a messy feeling, the pervasive literary atmosphere made it easier for people to feel calm and peaceful.

Alice: "So big"

Merlin: "Good"

The two surveyed for a while, giving completely different evaluations. C Five Word Treatment

A vein jumped on Johnson's forehead, annoyedly saying, "If you hate the mess, you can go live elsewhere; I didn't ask you to live in my house."

"Although a bit messy, it's barely okay—after all, it saves money," Merlin spread his hands.

"Tsk!" Johnson clicked his tongue in dissatisfaction, thinking this picky man's own place probably wasn't that great either?

Alice curiously picked up a book from the ground at random, flipped through it a few times, "Actually it's about magic; aren't you guys generation after generation of magic masters? Do you need to look at this kind of thing?"

"Don't touch randomly! Do you have no manners!" Johnson snatched the book from Alice's hand immediately, feeling Alice was somewhat rude.

"Just looking at it? Why such a big reaction?" Alice raised her eyebrows charmingly, feeling somewhat aggrieved in her heart.

"This book is ours; many are not seen outside, and there are many secrets inside; don't flip through randomly," Johnson's face full of hostility, meaningfully saying, "If you dare to touch randomly again, I won't care if you're a guest or not; I'll definitely let you taste the power of knowledge!"

"Pah! Miser!" Alice turned her head away, finding this little bastard increasingly annoying.

"Miser just means miser, anyway, you just won't see anything for real," Johnson walked in front, waving at the two people behind, "Follow me, my father—will be back soon; I'll first find a room for you two, a husband and wife, right?"

Merlin: "Separate."

Alice: "Live separately."

The two looked at each other; they didn't feel surprised or inappropriate at all; of course they should live separately if they could, it would be strange to live together with extra rooms.

Johnson frowned, his expression weird, puzzledly asking, "Do you have a disease? Aren't you a couple? Why live separately? Won't it be awkward?"

Merlin had no expression, said nothing, just helplessly thought, see, now that he's out on the street, living separately from Alice would be met with bizarre looks.

Alice glanced at the side of Merlin, two small red clouds surfacing on her face, seriously saying one

"Hurry up and show the way, you ask too much!"

"Even if I told a little kid like you, you wouldn't understand <"

Time entered late night.

The father of young Johnson had already finished his work and returned.

Johnson himself prepared a table of food, looking quite good.

It seemed that usually Johnson was the only one at home, and had already become a capable housekeeper.

Johnson was still young, his looks could be considered handsome, also a famous mage; housework was very capable.

Merlin guessed that when Johnson grew up, he would definitely be the type welcomed by many girls; worthy of being the tomorrow's star of Great Britain, image engineering perfect!

A round table, various dishes placed on it; the roasted suckling pig in the middle, with the aid of the candle's glow, was reflecting golden oily light, just looking at it made one's appetite large.

Just opposite Merlin, a white-haired old man was smiling at them all over his face, his attitude very good.

This person's figure was thin, wearing a dark blue robe, appearing quite old.

He was holding a long black magic wand, looking at the gleaming material; it shouldn't be an ordinary thing.

Obviously this was Johnson's father, the president of the High City Adventurers Guild, and also an authority figure in magic.

From the beginning, Merlin could feel that the other party was intentionally hiding his pressure, not letting others detect his strength, making people a bit hard to figure out.

However, Merlin didn't mind this; hiding strength was very common; who would recklessly release pressure walking on the street?

Merlin looked at all the dishes on the table, silently swallowed a mouthful of saliva, and approached Alice, covering his mouth to secretly satirize one

"Tsk tsk tsk!"

"Johnson's cooking at such a young age is already better than you"

"Aren't you ashamed? Really embarrassing~"二

title: Chapter 29 — Non-Human (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 29 — Non-Human (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 13 · Chapter 29

Alice's entire body shuddered, as if struck by lightning.

She felt deeply humiliated by Merlin's sarcasm, as though he were mocking her for being stupid.

Alice turned her head stiffly, wearing a smile that didn't reach her eyes.

"Not embarrassing at all, what's the big deal?"

"Brother Johnson probably has a good teacher to instruct him."

"What about me? All I have around me is an ancestor who complains and groans at the slightest thing."

A bead of cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead. He thought he shouldn't say any more, or else Alice might jump up and punch him to death.

"I suppose you two are the adventurers from Rexham that our son spoke of—Mr. Merlin and Miss Alice. You don't need to be so formal and stiff around us; just call me Old John." Old John nodded to both of them, hoping to ease the tense atmosphere.

"Hello. We're sorry for causing you trouble by coming to Galway City." Alice responded with a hint of apology.

Merlin didn't make any gesture at all beside her, acting more at ease than in his own home, his eyes fixed on the roasted suckling pig in the center, thinking about how to devour it quickly.

"No trouble at all, Miss Alice, you're too polite. Make yourself at home here; you can stay as long as you like." Old John glanced at his son Johnson beside him and said seriously, "After all, you are our son's saviors, so consider this our way of repaying you. This child was born to me in my later years; he is my only son, and I have great expectations for him. I don't want anything dangerous to happen to him. If anything were to befall him, our family might completely lose its future."

Johnson stood by with his head bowed, saying nothing, unable to read his emotions. In front of his father, this kid seemed much quieter than usual.

Alice gave an awkward smile and continued, "Since you're so worried about him, why not have him give up being an adventurer and choose a more stable occupation instead?"

"There are reasons for that." Old John paused and said helplessly, "Our family has produced many renowned magicians across generations, making us a distinguished family. But because many members of the family became complacent, we declined. Johnson is the most talented child in our family and our hope. Being an adventurer is clearly the fastest shortcut to reviving the family; no other profession can compare."

Alice was at a loss for words, thinking that Johnson, at such a young age, was already a Mithril-ranked adventurer traveling the world, which clearly wasn't something someone his age should be doing.

Could it be because of the heavy burden? Being forced to carry the mission of reviving the family on his shoulders, gritting his teeth and pushing forward.

Alice looked at Johnson, who was keeping his head down, and for some reason, felt that although this guy had a foul mouth, he was actually quite pitiful.

"From beginning to end, you've been forcing this mission onto this kid, haven't you? Have you ever asked what he wants to do himself?" Merlin suddenly interjected.

"I want nothing more than to revive our family; that's beyond question!" Johnson immediately looked up and shot back.

"Is that so? Then I'll pretend I didn't ask."

Merlin shrugged, thinking that Johnson's words might not be entirely true. Surely there would be a desire to shed the burden and do what he wanted, just as leaving the Demon Lord Palace was partly about wanting to throw off that burden.

But judging by Johnson's strength, already nearing the peak of Saint-tier at such a young age, reviving the entire family was probably only a matter of time.

Merlin felt he shouldn't have spoken up just now; he had meddled in Johnson's family affairs. If he had known this would happen, it would have been better to stay silent and mind his own business.

"Mr. Merlin, right?" Old John looked at Merlin, as if he had something to say.

"Hmm? What is it?" Merlin looked up.

"You don't yet understand our family. Our family has walked the path of studying magic for generations, dedicating ourselves to the magical arts. To us, this is glory, just like me personally compiling magic textbooks—it's something that benefits countless future generations." Old John said seriously.

"Then why don't you—" Merlin hesitated. Honestly, he couldn't stand the old fogey's attitude; they were completely different kinds of people.

"Johnson told me that your strength is astonishing, that you can slay a monster with rapid regeneration." Old John seemed to have a deep interest in Merlin.

"So what?" Merlin looked at Old John. Although the man was aged, his eyes sparkled with sharpness; he was clearly a cunning old fox.

"Nothing, I'm just finding it hard to believe. If Johnson hadn't told me himself, I would have thought it was a joke." Old John paused and voiced his thoughts. "An Iron-ranked adventurer managing to easily defeat a monster that even Saint-tier experts struggle against—this itself is jaw-dropping."

"It's nothing special. Those monsters were just so-so, barely reaching the level that would make me take them seriously." Merlin waved his hand casually.

"Hmph!" Johnson raised his eyelids, clearly very dissatisfied, repeatedly shooting death glares at Merlin.

Alice chuckled awkwardly beside him, thinking Merlin really couldn't talk his way out of anything. Wasn't he indirectly mocking Johnson's weakness?

"Haha, Mr. Merlin truly is a remarkable person. I know Johnson's strength well; when he fuses with the magical secret art, he can unleash power far beyond normal levels. Ordinary monsters are no match for him. The fact that you were able to kill it proves you're truly strong." Old John put away his smile and said seriously.

Merlin didn't respond, staring at Old John's shrewd eyes, wondering what this aged human was plotting.

"Johnson said you have no battle aura, yet possess extraordinary combat power unlike your appearance, so I'm quite curious."

Johnson studied Merlin and said slowly, "What do you rely on to defeat monsters? As far as I know, even if you practice the Drawing Slash to its utmost limit, without relying on battle aura, it's nearly impossible to achieve the effect of cleaving the earth."

"You haven't practiced the Drawing Slash to its utmost limit, so how do you know it's impossible?" Merlin countered, seemingly unwilling to answer Old John's question.

"The power ordinary people can unleash is always limited, but when combined with battle aura, it can multiply many times over. That's the difference between ordinary people and cultivators. You have no battle aura, yet you've accomplished the impossible. Isn't that strange?" Old John was full of curiosity, pressing on relentlessly.

Merlin rolled his eyes, thinking: If you had 9999 skill points, you'd be pretty awesome too!

But Merlin felt the other party was being pushy, trying to dig out his secrets, so he might as well lay it all out.

"What exactly do you want to know? Just say it directly."

"Mr. Merlin really is a man of few words. Then I'll be direct." Old John paused and said solemnly, "Actually, you're not human, are you?"

"Uh!" Alice's breath caught, her expression frozen on her face, her heart filled with terror—

How did he figure that out!?

No one had ever been able to tell that Merlin was a demon all this time!

No way, could this guy's true identity have been exposed!?
