title: Chapter 30 — Descendant
content:
Chapter 30 — Descendant

Volume 13 · Chapter 30

Merlin's expression turned grim as he heard Alice's words.

Alice's mood instantly grew tense and uneasy upon hearing Old John's skeptical remarks.

Alice couldn't fathom how Old John had figured it out. Under normal circumstances, Merlin showed no demonic traits whatsoever, not even in his aura.

What method had the man used to determine Merlin's identity?

Just because one could unleash extraordinary combat prowess without relying on magic or fighting energy didn't mean one could jump to conclusions so hastily, did it?

Alice had once desperately wanted to expose Merlin's true nature and make him a pariah.

But her current mindset was entirely different from before; she didn't want anyone to learn the truth about Merlin.

After all, the British Empire was deeply rooted in the Holy Church, with many followers of the Goddess of Light. Demons were, in an intangible sense, the enemies of all humankind.

If his identity were exposed, Merlin would surely choose to leave, and then where would she be left?

Alice felt restless and wanted to speak up in Merlin's defense, but with Old John insisting firmly, she didn't know how to begin.

Compared to Alice, Merlin remained far more composed, showing no signs of surprise or panic—just a calm acceptance.

This old man wasn't simple at all.

Earlier, she had underestimated him. She hadn't expected his perceptiveness to be so sharp.

He could see right through that she wasn't human. This guy was really something.

No matter what, as a demon, she couldn't hide it forever—it would eventually be exposed.

There was no point in concealing it any longer. Might as well just admit it openly.

Merlin sighed, resigning himself to fate. Since he had already been seen through, there was no harm in being straightforward.

"That's right, actually I—"

"You're a divine breed, aren't you?"

Before Merlin could finish his sentence, Old John suddenly interrupted, uttering a rather obscure term.

Merlin: "Huh?"

Alice:

Both of them fell into a daze upon hearing Old John's words, suddenly sensing something was off—their train of thought was clearly not on the same wavelength.

"Divine breed?" Merlin felt a bit ignorant, having never heard of such a race before.

"Yes, that's right, the divine breed. You could also call them the divine clan. In layman's terms, they're descendants of gods." Old John stroked his beard and recalled, "I once read in an ancient book about records of the divine clan producing offspring with lower races. They inherit divine power without cultivation, born with innate strength—truly just like Mr. Merlin here, able to unleash extraordinary power without relying on magic or fighting energy."

Although Alice didn't understand what Old John was talking about, she was certain it was all a misunderstanding—a false alarm. It seemed Old John hadn't discovered that Merlin was a demon, but had instead reached a bizarre conclusion.

Merlin frowned slightly, taking Old John's words seriously. Divine breed? If he recalled correctly, when the Frost Sacred Dragon was killed, that lizard had claimed to be a descendant of the divine clan before dying.

Could it be that he was actually connected to these divine breeds?

Merlin stroked his chin and began to think carefully, falling into a state of confusion.

"Mr. Merlin, am I right?" Old John felt confident in his guess, believing it was unlikely to be wrong. "Your body carries the bloodline of the divine, surely because in the distant mythological era, your ancestor sacrificed themselves for a god."

Merlin's expression grew complicated as he thought, What the hell is this guy talking about? He was definitely a time traveler, through and through.

Although over 200 years had passed, his memories before the journey remained crystal clear.

That was a modern era with skyscrapers, cars, and planes—a world completely different from this one where magic and martial arts intertwined.

Before the journey, he had been an ordinary high school student in mainland China!

Merlin was certain Old John had it all wrong; he wasn't some descendant of mortals.

Still, to dispel Old John's suspicions, Merlin decided to play dumb.

"I'm not entirely sure myself, haha."

"You're definitely not wrong. You must be the divine descendant recorded in the ancient texts. I used to think it was just a fabricated legend, but after Johnson told me about your deeds, I finally realized the truth." Old John looked at Merlin with eyes full of curiosity, "Individuals born with innate divine power do exist, and you, sir, are that one in a million exceptional being."

Alice narrowed her delicate brows, sensing that Old John's words were no longer mere praise but outright worship. Could it be that Merlin's demonic ancestor was actually related to the ancient gods? Was it really that exaggerated?

Merlin's expression grew unnatural as Old John's flattery went too far, making even himself feel like he wasn't himself anymore.

"Uncle John, you might be misunderstanding me. The reality might not be as dramatic as you imagine."

"Then is there some other reason?" Old John shot back.

Merlin was at a loss for words, thinking it best not to say anything more—let the other person believe what he wanted. Even if he claimed to have been born with 9999 skill points, it might only make Old John even more bewildered.

"I think your ancestor was probably some divine being, though such inherited divine power should fade over the long passage of time. It's rare to see a case of ancestral reversion like yours, and the ancient texts don't even mention such phenomena." Old John stroked his beard and said leisurely.

Merlin nearly spat out a mouthful of blood. He had read the Lucifer family genealogy, and there was no mention of any divine names.

Merlin's mother was a genuine devil, born in the twilight of the mythological era, but at that time, Lucifer the Second was still an unweaned infant!

As for his father? He didn't exist at all.

Lucifer the Second intensely despised men, using the power of a succubus to reproduce asexually, giving birth to Merlin and Lilith. The two had no father.

However, using succubus power for reproduction could lead to unstable bloodlines—tending toward either succubus or devil traits randomly, and sometimes both.

It was precisely because he understood his own family background that Merlin found Old John's nonsense all the more ridiculous.

"That's probably because I don't know myself very well either. Maybe it's just as you said—I might be some kind of..."

"It's perfectly normal not to know. After all, your situation is extremely rare, and in the present day, such cases have basically gone extinct. I've only read about them in ancient texts." Old John nodded.

"Please don't spread this around." Merlin worried that Old John's wild conjectures would cause him trouble.

"Of course not. Your being a divine descendant is merely my speculation. Promoting such unfounded claims would violate the principles of our research." Old John said seriously, putting on his pedantic scholar demeanor, "Besides, since you'll be staying with me for the next few days, we can have a proper discussion, and I can also show you that ancient book."

Merlin forced a smile and nodded, his heart aching with silent suffering.

This old man was really too annoying.

He wanted to leave this ghostly place as soon as possible.

If he had known it would come to this, he would have rather died than stay here.

title: Chapter 31 — Potion
content:
Chapter 31 — Potion

Volume 13 · Chapter 31

Alice, listening beside him to Old John's remarks, which seemed true, quietly asked Merlin. "Hey, are you really a descendant of the divine race?" "Pfft, if I were a descendant of the divine race, would I be hanging out with you? Come on, use a little brain—don't just believe anyone. This old guy is obviously addled from reading too much." Merlin replied in a low voice to Alice, his tone clearly rejecting this nosy old fellow. "Is .?" Alice nodded, quietly adding, "But it's already lucky that your demon identity hasn't been noticed." "Nonsense, if I didn't admit it, who could tell?" Merlin rolled his eyes helplessly, saying, "It just so happens that they think I'm some descendant, so for now we'll go along with the mistake. After we get through these few days we'll leave quickly—I've hated bookworms my whole life." "Are you afraid of people with such strong curiosity?" Alice narrowed her eyes, as if trying to find Merlin's weakness. "Bookworms aren't scary; it's bookworms combined with nitpickers that become frightening." Merlin paused, then said softly, "You didn't see that from the start this old man always raises objections? Whenever we have a slight disagreement, he comes back with ten reasons to counter us—I'm basically beaten." Alice felt a bead of cold sweat on her forehead, thinking maybe elderly people all have this flaw? Beside her, little Johnson hadn't spoken a word, just kept his head down, feeling waves of helplessness, thinking indeed, Merlin is a legendary oddball, no wonder he's so heaven-defying; it's only natural that I can't compare to him.

Old John sighed, "I never imagined in my lifetime I'd see the divine descendants recorded in ancient texts—it's truly not lived in vain." He then said, "I hope, Mr. Merlin, you can come to my study tonight so we can discuss the matter of divine descendants properly." "Haha, sure," Merlin gave a forced smile, thinking, "What a hassle—does this mean I'm not allowed to sleep? Indeed, there's no such thing as a free lunch."

"Oh, I almost forgot—Old John reached into his pocket as if searching for something, 'I have a gift for you.'" "Eh? A gift?" Alice gasped, startled, thinking what have she and Merlin done to deserve a gift? "You didn't save my son's life? So I must express my gratitude." Old John said solemnly. "There's no need for such courtesy—you let us stay here, that's already ample repayment." Alice waved her hands repeatedly, wanting to refuse:τ_ "No no no, you saved my son's life; merely letting you stay a few nights can't count as repayment—that's too casual. If outsiders knew, they'd say the Johnsons are stingy. Moreover, giving you a gift is proper; you shouldn't feel guilty." Old John insisted firmly, not allowing Merlin and Alice to refuse. Merlin frowned slightly, thinking it seemed little Johnson wasn't lying; their family dislikes owing others, and such family credit is always high.

"This is exactly it—Old John took out a glass test tube and placed it before Alice, 'This gift is specially prepared for Miss Alice; please don't dislike it. To us it's still somewhat precious, but compared to my son's life it's trivial—I think it's most suitable as a gift.'" When little Johnson saw his father produce this, his eyes widened in shock, as if beholding something utterly unbelievable. "Father, what is this?! No way! This can't be given as a gift—you..." "Alright, alright, don't worry about this. I know you have reservations, but Mr. Merlin and Miss Alice helped you; this is what they deserve." Johnson wanted to voice opposition, but his father cut him off directly—his dissatisfaction could only be swallowed, for this was a treasure his father had spent three years collecting for his own cultivation, now just handed over like that—could it be that three years of effort were wasted?! Seeing Johnson's strange reaction, Merlin couldn't help but frown slightly, glancing at the small test tube before Alice on the table. The glass container held a blue liquid, faintly emitting a dim glow; otherwise there was nothing special about it. It looked completely ordinary—could there be hidden mysteries inside, making it a rare treasure? Merlin, thinking of Johnson's attitude, grew more convinced of this notion; the contents of this bottle are definitely not simple. Alice stared blankly at the small bottle before her, puzzled, asking, "This..." "This is ultra-high-concentration non-attributable magical element." Old John stroked his beard and said leisurely. "Ah?!!" Alice's eyes widened, clearly astonished; she thought the technology to condense magical elements into liquid was unheard of, and yet they had gathered an entire small bottle—the effort required is unimaginable! Merlin also felt a surge of astonishment, looking over at Old John in disbelief—this was the first time he'd seen such a thing; however, being able to fit such a huge amount into a small bottle proves it could greatly accelerate one's cultivation speed. Ordinary people normally absorb magical elements from the air very slowly, but if such a concentrated liquid were available, one could imagine that the era when Saint-tier powerhouses walk everywhere would have begun! Merlin was stunned by Old John's trick, forced to reassess this old man; if this could be mass-produced, this old fellow would be the world's richest—heaven wouldn't allow it otherwise! "Our family possesses a secret technique that can condense magical elements from the air for use, though production is slow; this bottle of magical element took me three whole years to complete." Old John explained lightly. Merlin narrowed his eyes, thinking indeed so—just that it can't be mass-produced is a pity; otherwise the Johnson clan would have soared, there'd be no need to be adventurers, selling these concentrated magical elements every day would suffice. Alice's face showed a hint of hesitation; after thinking, she raised her head and said seriously, "No, this is too precious—I can't accept it. In fact I didn't really help Johnson's brother, so taking this would bother my conscience." Merlin felt embarrassed, almost having his jaw drop from Alice's words; he quickly gave her repeated glances and whispered, "You're an idiot! Take this, don't refuse—free meat on the table

title: Chapter 32 — Locked
content:
Chapter 32 — Locked

Volume 13 · Chapter 32

Merlin furrowed his brows, suddenly realizing something: how could Johnson, at such a young age, already possess Saint-tier strength? Old John must have been involved.
Since Old John could produce this side-effect-free concentrated magic power liquid to boost strength, there's no reason not to give it to little Johnson.
Merlin had thought Johnson was a little genius, but it turns out the family just has the nutrient solution, so it's no surprise he's stronger than others.
Alice, after hearing Old John's words, immediately became unsettled, staring fixedly at the concentrated magic power element on the table.
You know, each stage of strength level is quite arduous, especially when hitting a bottleneck; one might easily fall into stagnation.
During the critical bottleneck period, many people get stuck here for a long time, and the probability of a steady breakthrough in cultivation is minuscule.
But with the concentrated magic power element before us, it's a different story—it will surely achieve twice the result with half the effort.
Alice felt hesitant, saying she didn't want it, yet it felt too precious to shamelessly accept.
Seeing Alice undecided about the small bottle on the table, Merlin decided to make the decision for her.
So Merlin bluntly took the concentrated magic power element from the table and cheerfully slipped it into his pocket.
“Then thank you, Mr. Old John, for your kindness—I'll accept it on Alice's behalf.”
“Hey! What are you doing?”

Alice frowned, dissatisfied with Merlin's unilateral decision, not even consulting her before taking it!
Merlin looked embarrassed, thinking, why is Alice acting all high and mighty now? She should just shamelessly accept it.
This is exactly what we need right now; hesitating is just hypocritical~
Merlin leaned close to Alice, deliberately lowering his voice, reasoning with her emotionally and logically.
“I'm not helping you? Can't you calm down?”
“How am I helping you?” Alice frowned, feeling Merlin was just finding ways to lower her lofty image.
“If you're embarrassed to take it, me taking it for you is the same.” Merlin said solemnly.
“I didn't intend to take it.” Alice responded seriously.
“Don't pretend, you're being hypocritical—this isn't something you need right now?” Merlin narrowed his eyes, thinking Alice was putting on a show; clearly her eyes hadn't left the concentrated magic power liquid earlier, just like a little match-selling girl peeking at a turkey through a window.
Alice was at a loss for words, wanting it inside but too embarrassed to say so.
“This bottle of concentrated magic power liquid is mine; even if I'm a petty person, it's mine and has nothing to do with you. You remain that radiant, great Hero.” Merlin lifted his head, speaking calmly, “You should thank me, after all, I gave you a step up~”
“It's noisy, I never wanted it—it's all your meddling.” Alice said angrily, obviously not speaking her true feelings.
“Don't want it? Fine then.” Merlin nodded, whispering, “I'll just secretly drink it myself—I've never tried magic power element before; maybe my body isn't compatible with it.”
“Mmm!” Alice puffed out her cheeks, glaring at Merlin like an irritated pufferfish, full of hostility.
Merlin pressed his lips, a few black lines slid down his forehead, and he silently complained to himself,
this guy who says one thing but does another.

Alice was at a loss for words, wanting it inside but too embarrassed to say so.
“This bottle of concentrated magic power liquid is mine; even if I'm a petty person, it's mine and has nothing to do with you. You remain that radiant, great Hero.” Merlin lifted his head, speaking calmly, “You should thank me, after all, I gave you a step up~”
“It's noisy, I never wanted it—it's all your meddling.” Alice said angrily, obviously not speaking her true feelings.
“Don't want it? Fine then.” Merlin nodded, whispering, “I'll just secretly drink it myself—I've never tried magic power element before; maybe my body isn't compatible with it.”
“Mmm!” Alice puffed out her cheeks, glaring at Merlin like an irritated pufferfish, full of hostility.
Merlin pressed his lips, a few black lines slid down his forehead, and he silently complained to himself,
this guy who says one thing but does another.

After the John family dinner ended in a relatively harmonious atmosphere,
Merlin and Alice went their separate ways, returning to their rooms.
Old John was fairly enthusiastic, attending to both of them thoroughly.
But he constantly bothered Merlin with obscure magic theory questions and talk of nonexistent divine descendants.
This annoyed Merlin somewhat; he had no way to deal with those eager for knowledge, finding it hard to tolerate the old man's constant nagging.
Old John seemed especially fond of Merlin, wanting to learn about the traits of divine descendants through him.
If conditions allowed, Merlin suspected Old John wanted to dissect him, becoming the world's first living specimen of a divine descendant.
But Merlin is certainly no such descendant; he couldn't say anything about it.
Finally, Merlin couldn't take it anymore, being the first to leave the table, he went straight to his room to rest, refusing all of Old John's invitations.
Alice also returned to her room afterward, seeing the concentrated magic power liquid left on the table that Merlin had taken.
It seemed Merlin had already come by, dropped it off, and left immediately.
This thing is of no use to Merlin anyway, given his magic-immune physique; drinking it would be no different from drinking water.
Alice picked up the bottle of magic power liquid, wondering what to do next.
Should she just drink it down and then begin normal cultivation?
But this bottle of magic power liquid could only push her magic to the Saint-tier peak; for battle aura she'd still need to think of something else.
Sigh, why am I a dual magic and martial cultivator? Cultivation difficulty is N times that of ordinary people, and it's especially troublesome.
Alice sighed inwardly; she is the heir of the Great Snow Mountain, and the future of the Great Snow Mountain lineage rests on her.
However, Alice felt she should go see her teacher to learn some Great Snow Mountain-specific magic martial techniques.
Otherwise, if she keeps using dragon tribe magic and martial arts every day, can she still be considered her teacher's sole disciple?
After reflecting, Alice drank the magic power liquid in one gulp, then sat cross-legged on the bed, entered a state of emptiness, and began the long process of digesting the magic power.

Three days passed in the blink of an eye.
Merlin went to the baron's manor every day to inquire, asking whether Barton had returned.
Alice remained in a state of cultivation, never leaving her room, not even eating.
Considering Alice was at the critical stage of breaking through her bottleneck, Merlin didn't bother to disturb her for fun.
As for the John family's father and son, they seemed busy during the day and only returned at night.
From these days of observation, Merlin discovered that Johnson was the family's pillar—almost everything was his responsibility.
Thinking about how young Johnson was, shouldering almost the entire family's burden, it's truly not easy.
What annoyed Merlin most, however, was Old John; these days the old man kept trying to bother him, wanting to chat.
But Merlin refused all those invitations; he had no patience to listen to the old man's endless chatter.
As time entered deep night, the round moon hung high, cold light spilling down.
On the roof opposite the John residence, two figures stood—Oswald and Laurie.
They had ascertained Merlin and Alice's positions; tonight they planned to strike first, removing the obstacle in their mission.
“This is the place, get ready to move.”

title: Chapter 33 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 33 — Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets

Volume 13 · Chapter 33

Merlin sat in his chair with a bitter expression. He had been trying to avoid Old John's invitations, but he had underestimated the situation. Without warning, Old John had barged into Merlin's room and started talking nonstop.

He was knowledgeable about all sorts of mysteries and never ran out of things to say.

Today, he had been relentless. Finally, Merlin had no choice but to agree to have a detailed discussion in the study.

*It's hard to bend beneath someone else's roof,* he thought.

He truly felt this way. He vowed that from now on, he would have absolutely nothing to do with the troublesome John family.

Old John handed a cup of hot black tea to Merlin, nodded warmly, and said, "Mr. Merlin, please help yourself."

Old John also nodded with a smile, taking the black tea, his mind full of how to get through this.

He wondered if Merlin was confused about his identity? If there were any questions, Merlin could ask him freely. He would answer sincerely.

"Mr. John seems to be putting on the posture of an expert. In terms of knowledge, Merlin must feel inferior to himself."

"No, I have no questions." Merlin shook his head earnestly. *Questions? They don't exist.*

"I think—Mr. John, you're probably surprised to learn that you're a descendant of the divine race. Don't you feel panicked or lost?"

"I understand your concerns. As a normal person, I would naturally want to figure things out as soon as possible."

"I feel that whether I'm a descendant of a god or not isn't important." Merlin spread his hands, wanting to block the topic. After finishing, perhaps he could go back to his room and have a good sleep.

"If you don't care about your identity, then allow me to ask you this." Old John pondered.

Merlin held the cup, looking at his forehead, thinking *Damn it! Am I not able to escape today?*

Old John picked up his pen and feather, asking with a serious expression, "Since you're a descendant of the divine race, don't you feel any magic power?"

"Third Category Power? What does that mean?" Merlin showed a confused expression. He didn't quite understand what Old John was talking about.

"Ah, in the current world, the two recognized major cultivation systems are magic power and battle qi. Other than that, any power usable by people is called Third Category Power." Old John explained briefly, as if teaching a class.

*Third Category Power? It doesn't seem like that!* Merlin thought. *It has absolutely nothing to do with me!*

*All the precious points were added to Sword Drawing Slash.*

He felt that the fusion of these powers should belong to the Third Category, outside the two major systems.

Although Alice could immune, he couldn't immune the golden ice crystal fusion.

After thinking, he raised his head and answered uncertainly.

Old John inhaled sharply, asking in surprise, "You don't have any Third Category Power?"

Merlin shrugged his shoulders, indicating that he was also innocent.

Old John wrote Merlin's words down very seriously in his notebook, meticulously, "Descendant of the divine race really is—"

"Powerful and amazing to the point of making one tremble, yet requiring no external support. Through this, one can glimpse the remote Creator God. The gods are so—"

Merlin didn't speak. Instead, a bead of cold sweat dripped from his forehead. *What kind of nonsense is this? I'm not a descendant of the divine race.*

"Inherit such powerful abilities, are there any side effects? Will there be no limitations? Can it be used anytime and anywhere?" Old John asked another question.

"The side effects are—as guessed, controlling powerful forces must come at a corresponding price. It seems you're not having it easy either." Merlin nodded seriously with a gloomy expression.

"Yes, it's not easy at all." Old John picked up his pen, ready to record at any moment, planning to treat this notebook as a—

"Descendant of the divine race's first-hand materials." This isn't convenient, just know that having this power isn't a good thing." Merlin declined Old John's request. This secret, even Alice hadn't been told, let alone others?

"Can you lend me that book to read?" Old John continued asking. Merlin just wanted to see that ancient book because he was tired of being asked and wanted to use reading as an excuse to stall for time.

*Almost forgot—I want to have you look at that book too.*

"Yes, yes, yes." Old John tapped his forehead, feeling quite happy that Merlin was so interested.

He turned and entered a relatively hidden side chamber, taking out a thick-bound red book.

The original was already quite worn, still somewhat incomplete, and written in obscure ancient elvish script. This is what I translated.

"Thank you." Merlin pretended to flip through it, thinking he could use it as a storybook to pass the time.

The book's content was large, divided into Creation Chapter, Gods Chapter, and Elf Chapter, obviously sorted chronologically.

*It's about to end. Perhaps the original author died during the Elf Era, so there are no records of the demon and human eras afterward.*

But in the Elf

"The gods chapter—seeing the gods' tyranny and oppression of all races, treating all races as ants in the lowest tier, people lived in suffering."

Just then, a human who called himself a demon descended from the sky. He slaughtered the gods, made the gods bathe in—

[The gods chapter, the people welcomed a new dawn. A self-proclaimed demon human descended from the sky, he slaughtered the gods, making the gods bathe in the dusk of death. Merlin couldn't help but emit a cold laugh, feeling the author must be an elf, the美化 tendency is very obvious. This history is fabricated nonsense.]

This passage has no such记载 in the book.

The demon race's history—humans descended from the sky? Like a comedy~

*What's wrong with it?*

*It's similar to my situation.*

And—

title: Chapter 34 — Infiltration
content:
Chapter 34 — Infiltration

Volume 13 · Chapter 34

Merlin looked at the ancient book manuscript in his hand, his expression growing increasingly peculiar, especially at that one sentence—"A human who claimed to be a demon fell from the sky."

If this wasn't because that distant author had a momentary lapse and deliberately wrote a grammatically flawed sentence, then this situation was incredibly similar to his own! Wasn't he also a demon that people always mistook for a human? Wasn't this a bit too coincidental?!

Merlin stroked his chin and fell into deep thought. Assuming all of this were true, it would prove that several eras ago, someone had faced the exact same predicament as him.

However, Merlin always harbored doubts about this point. Whether the events narrated in this ancient book were authentic still needed further—

And besides, the book in his possession was a copied manuscript. Who knew how far old John had managed to translate it? What if there were some discrepancies?

Most importantly, Merlin trusted the records of the demon race more. No clan respected history more than the demon race. Their accounts could be guaranteed as truthful—unless there were exceptional circumstances that prevented them from speaking, but they would absolutely never tell lies.

Merlin had long since browsed the library of the First Demon Lord Palace. Regarding records of this world, there was simply no mention of a superhuman falling from the sky. Perhaps such an event never happened at all, and it was all fabricated.

Noticing Merlin's pensive expression, old John beside him wondered if he'd made some new discovery, so he stepped forward enthusiastically and said, "What is it? Does Mr. Merlin have some unique insight?"

"Ah, no." Merlin shook his head. "Just one sentence has been troubling me."

"What is it? If there's anything you don't understand, you can ask me. While I wouldn't say I'm proficient in every race's language, I do consider myself quite knowledgeable." Old John puffed out his chest confidently. In fact, his knowledge was genuinely extensive; he had already translated most of this book written in ancient Elvish.

"Alright." Merlin handed the book to old John and pointed to the self-contradictory sentence. "This 'a human who claimed to be a demon'—could it be a grammatical error? Or perhaps a mistranslation?"

"Ah~" After reading it, old John's expression shifted to one of sudden understanding. Stroking his beard, he said, "A mistranslation is impossible. That is precisely what the original text means. A human who descended from the sky and claimed to be a member of the demon race personally brought an end to the gods' civilization."

"Hmm?" Merlin frowned and said awkwardly, "Isn't that contradictory? Is he a human or a demon?"

"Actually, when I first read this passage, I was also deeply puzzled. Why would a human call themselves a demon? That's highly irregular." Old John wore a bewildered expression and continued, "But after thinking about it later, there's only one most reasonable explanation."

"What is it?" Merlin became curious. This record described a demon who had personally destroyed the gods—was there such an unprecedented great figure in the demon race? He had never heard of it.

"Perhaps a half-demon. Someone with a small amount of demon bloodline but mostly human. In that case, they could use their human form to call themselves a member of the demon race." Old John said this with complete seriousness.

Hearing this far-fetched explanation, Merlin's expression immediately turned strange, because what old John said simply did not match reality.

The proportion of demons willing to bear children with humans was exceedingly slim, much like how humans find it hard to look at an orangutan ** and view them as animals.

Of course, it wasn't impossible that a few eccentrics might be born who harbored special preferences for other races, but such situations were extremely rare. In any case, over his 200 years of life, Merlin had never seen any demon fall in love with a human.

But it was actually quite common for humans to harbor affectionate feelings toward demons. The reason was obvious to anyone—after all, the demon race had the exquisitely alluring succubi.

"That situation is impossible, Mr. John. You still don't quite understand the concepts of the demon race."

"Why? Doesn't this hypothesis have any persuasiveness?" Old John couldn't quite understand why Merlin was denying it.

"Because the demon race is a clan with extremely strict bloodline hierarchies. They would scarcely consider humans, and even if a half-demon were truly born, it would not be acknowledged. It would absolutely face intense rejection." Merlin said seriously.

"Is that so? It turns out demons have such strict class distinctions."

Old John seemingly didn't understand demons very well. After all, demonic territories were very mysterious, and it was difficult for humans to even set foot there.

Although the Holy Church had organized human crusade armies many times, they almost always returned in crushing defeat.

Furthermore, the priests deliberately exaggerated the demonic threat, which resulted in much of the information being inaccurate.

"Mr. Merlin, you seem to know a lot about demons. Could it be..."

"Uh, well—" Merlin suddenly grew tense and covered it with a laugh. "I once visited the Demon Lord's Palace, so naturally I know a bit more."

"I see. With Mr. Merlin's strength, even in demonic territory, you should have no problems." Old John nodded and didn't harbor much suspicion.

Merlin glanced at it a few more times. The subsequent history was basically more or less the same as the records of the demon race, so he lost interest and closed the book. "The authenticity of this book is still questionable. A human claiming to be a demon who fell from the sky and destroyed the gods—this claim is completely unbelievable. Perhaps it was merely the original author's fanciful imagination."

"Not necessarily. Mr. Merlin, you need to understand that many history books have significant overlapping portions, which proves that some events were very likely truly experienced." Old John shook his head.

"Oh? You believe the outrageous events recorded in this book?" Merlin looked at old John in surprise, thinking that a learned old man like him shouldn't believe in such groundless unofficial histories.

"There are countless books recording history in this world, and many originals can no longer be found. But the account of a human claiming to be a demon falling from the sky to destroy the gods does not appear for the first time—it appears many times. Just to take myself as an example," old John thought for a moment and continued seriously, "I have personally read over a hundred different history books, and the account of a human claiming to be a demon falling from the sky appears a full thirty-plus times. Moreover, those books are all very ancient texts, and their records may be closer to the era of the gods. Although the argument of human-demon hybridization has been denied, we cannot completely rule out the possibility that in that distant era, a particularly extraordinary hero once appeared."

Merlin didn't speak. Instead, he stroked his chin and fell into deep contemplation—

That's right.

Why would so many history books have similar records?

Except for truly having happened, there seemed to be no other reasonable explanation. SEA0G.c

Why did that human call themselves a demon?

Could it be that in the distant era of the gods, someone extremely similar to him had truly appeared?

Elsewhere.

Alice was wholeheartedly cultivating, entering a state of mental emptiness where she was completely unaware of the outside world.

A layer of cold sweat beaded on her forehead, and the golden magic power surging through her body continuously pushed toward higher levels.

Alice had gone without food or drink for three days, fully dedicating herself to breaking through to the peak of Saint-tier. It seemed to be going quite smoothly.

At this critical moment, the door to Alice's room was slowly pushed open, and Lorry, a masked and disguised member of the Dark Guild, found her room.

Lorry saw Alice kneeling on her bed in cultivation and couldn't help but narrow his eyes and reveal an evil grin, secretly thinking—

Haha.

She's actually in the middle of cultivation?

This is truly a heaven-sent opportunity!

Watch me break her neck while this big woman is completely unaware!
