title: Chapter 35 — Surprise Attack
content:
Chapter 35 — Surprise Attack

Volume 13 · Chapter 35

Laurie was going to handle this silver-ranked adventurer alone, and based on the previous information, the opponent's strength wasn't very weak.

Although Osvide was providing remote support from outside, during the infiltration, Laurie still felt a bit tricky and nervous, thinking he would encounter a fierce battle.

To quickly take down this female adventurer, besides technique, one had to make good use of the advantage of a sudden attack.

However, after arriving here, Laurie discovered that he had been thinking too much, completely giving himself unnecessary trouble.

Because this manor had absolutely no defenses, it was very easy to infiltrate.

And Alice was in a state of relaxed cultivation, with her perception of the outside world reduced to the lowest point.

Everything before her eyes could be considered a perfect assassination scene; various conditions were very favorable to Laurie, the uninvited guest.

So Laurie instantly became excited, feeling that the opportunity was sent by heaven, and at this moment, why not act?

Laurie crept into the house, concealing all his breath, making not a sound.

He came to Alice's back, a trace of smugness flashing in his eyes.

Haha, too easy...

Unexpectedly, I came at just the right time.

This stupid woman has absolutely no defenses.

Laurie raised his right hand, forming it into a blade, preparing to split Alice's head open and kill her.

Die, foolish adventurer!

Laurie shouted in his heart, and suddenly golden battle aura ignited in his hand, without hesitation, he slashed down!

Wind split like a knife, raging in the small room, some crisp items were shattered in the blink of an eye.

But a confusing scene then occurred.

r small

Laurie's knife attack on Alice suddenly halted in mid-air, suspended directly above her forehead.

For a moment, the two were in a stalemate, the situation becoming somewhat peculiar.

Alice had somehow woken up from her cultivation state.

Just as Laurie's knife attack was about to strike, Alice suddenly turned her head, gazing at this uninvited guest.

Although the just-woken Alice didn't understand the situation, from the masked person's posture before her, as well as the undisguised killing intent, it was absolutely a mysterious enemy who had stealthily infiltrated.

Fortunately, she had just finished her cultivation, otherwise, if she were a bit slower, something would have happened.

Alice immediately raised her vigilant heart, guarding against the enemy possibly launching an attack; if the opponent showed any attack trend, she would not be polite and would counterattack fiercely!

"Eh.

Laurie gazed at the other's eyes, those brilliant golden slit pupils in the night, like hot flames burning fiercely.

... What situation?

How did this woman suddenly wake up!

Is this too much of a coincidence? Really unlucky!

This guy's strength is indeed not weak, although the pressure of battle aura is slightly weaker, but the power of magic...

Is already on par with that crazy president! He is a powerhouse at the peak of the Saint tier!

It seems I must make some reaction, otherwise I'll *drop here. The only advantage is that I'm closer to her; if the opponent uses magic against me, I still have the advantage.

But just now's state...

Laurie's cold sweat streamed down, his body as if petrified, difficult to move, even a bit trembling.

Alice's golden pupils were overwhelmingly deterring, especially the dragon might radiating from them, making Laurie really feel some difficulty breathing, and fear arose in his heart.

Dragon race has obvious deterrence against inferior species; normal people would feel some panic and bewilderment.

Laurie secretly swallowed a mouthful of saliva, seriously doubting whether his opponent was human; could it be that he had already learned to transform into a human form?

Laurie's knife was suspended above Alice's forehead, he really didn't have the courage to press down, he was thinking of ways to overcome the pressure of facing an enemy, like this, the one who would drop first would definitely be himself!

After three days of effort, Alice's strength at this moment was basically considered to have reached the peak of the Saint tier, although only in terms of magic power, battle aura hadn't made much progress, but it was already enough; even looking across the entire Britannia Empire, one could get infinitely close to those famous strong ones.

If Alice's magic power hadn't reached the peak of the Saint tier, probably wouldn't have full confidence to win against the first knight Mesfield.

However, now, Alice's combat power had surpassed Mesfield, and was vaguely approaching that purple-gold president Gregory.

Even the previously arrogant Elemental Four Swords Saint, in a one-on-one duel, was not Alice's opponent.

At this moment, the power of the inheritance crystal in Alice's body had been utilized by her to 50%, and her overall strength level had been raised again; dragon martial arts and magic had also been very well imprinted in her mind. or a small toy

Although Alice's battle aura progress hadn't improved much, she was still in a bottleneck, but her physical strength, under the nourishment of dragon power, had become increasingly formidable.

"Who are you? What is your purpose for infiltrating mine?"

Alice questioned with a very serious tone, and the hostility in her eyes became even stronger.

No! If this continues, I will be suppressed by this woman!

Laurie, in a hurry, desperately bit his lip with his teeth.

He used pain to wake himself up, and barely broke free from the effect of dragon might.

Laurie without any hesitation, shouted angrily, and had been holding up his knife for a long time, slashed down fiercely!

"Drink!

A loud collision sound rang out, the bed being shattered by the fierce force, a moment fierce wind swept out!

But this knife strike, was blocked by Alice with her hand, and did not cause fatal injury.

Alice grabbed Laurie's wrist, a look of anger on her pretty face.

"You dare.

"...

Laurie widened his eyes, his pupils shrinking a bit, not expecting Alice to block his attack while under suppression.

I am specialized in close combat, you know! Now I can't do anything to a half-baked magic swordsman, huh?

Laurie felt a bit tricky, because the cold air from Alice's body kept attacking his body.

Alice saw that the opponent's attack was clearly intent on putting her to death, so she also began to counterattack.

Only to see Alice's gaze concentrated, horrifyingly cold air suddenly exploded on the spot, raging around everything!

"Bad!"

Laurie was greatly alarmed, this cold air, a billion times more terrible than the ice point, was hard to deal with.

Must create distance, otherwise one would be frozen to death!

Laurie quickly broke free from Alice's restraint, retreated backward to create distance.

When Laurie raised his head again, Alice had already stood up, and around her condensed countless golden ice thorns.

Standing like spears, like a golden ice throne!

If Laurie had been a bit slower just now, he would probably have been stabbed into a hedgehog now.

Alice's cold air was intimidating, she drew out the fine sword at her side.

"You what person?! I don't remember having offended any Saint-tier powerhouse in this dangerous city... "

Laurie had lingering fear, but still calmly said, "You don't need to know who I am, you only need to know that I want you to become a dead person, little Osvide! You are watching what! Don't move quickly! Single-handedly, I don't have a chance of winning!"

Laurie shouted loudly, and just as the words fell, two Saint-tier battle aura reinforced arrows pierced through the window, shooting out.

title: Chapter 36 — Pincer Attack (Bonus Update for Monthly Votes)
content:
Chapter 36 — Pincer Attack (Bonus Update for Monthly Votes)

Volume 13 · Chapter 36

The sound of tearing air rang out, but the sudden ambush arrived far too swiftly for anyone to react.

The enemy's target was Alice's nape, clearly aiming to pierce straight through it — ruthless to the core!

Both arrows were reinforced with fighting energy, their tips shimmering with a golden glow, their destructive power far beyond the ordinary!

These were arrows that could slice through thick castle walls as easily as tofu, proof of long-premeditated aggression — they had been waiting for a moment of Alice's distraction to strike!

Alice was startled by the hidden ambush, but she hadn't yet lost her composure enough to falter, though she didn't yet know how to counter.

Though the arrows flew impossibly fast, she was not entirely without means.

Dense blue-white scales rapidly appeared across Alice's nape, visible to the naked eye, forming a defensive layer.

In the blink of an eye—

The two arrows struck Alice's nape, sparking brilliantly, the screech of metal colliding piercing to the ears!

The arrows were deflected, and Alice was knocked backward several steps by the force, but she avoided any fatal injury.

Osward lowered his bow outside, his face a mask of utter disbelief — was he seeing things?!

With an archer's innate long-range vision, he could clearly see what had happened at a distance, and every move Alice had made had fallen within his sight.

Scales growing on the neck? Is this woman even human?!

My two arrows were infused with fighting energy — the angles were perfect, the timing impeccable; it was impossible for nothing to have landed.

Even if she hadn't died, she should have suffered a fatal wound. How could they be completely deflected?!

Are those scales on her body really that hard?! Those arrows could effortlessly pierce a hundred layers of fine armor!

Osward was thoroughly shaken. This woman was indeed a formidable opponent — not someone to be dealt with easily.

It seemed the only option was to try killing her directly. If that failed, he would have to think of another plan.

"Hah! It didn't work...." Laurie's brows furrowed tightly. Facing the enemy so close at hand, he was under the greatest pressure. Now even Osward had missed, and he could only choose to fight head-on.

"There's someone outside too, it seems you came prepared. What exactly do you want by assassinating me?!" Alice pointed her slender sword at the Laurie opposite her, her attention still divided toward the outside, ever watchful for that mysterious archer's next attack.

"You have only yourselves to blame for taking a mission you shouldn't have. If our goals hadn't aligned, we wouldn't have bothered provoking you." Laurie secretly channeled fighting energy throughout his entire body, preparing for a swift, ferocious assault aimed at killing Alice on the spot.

"A mission I shouldn't have taken?" Alice looked puzzled, then realization dawned. "You must be...."

"That's right. I know your target is the blood clan relic map in Baron Barton's possession — but it is also something we desire..." Laurie paused, his tone laced with regret. "Unfortunately, once something catches my eye, I will never simply hand it over. You should give up and die quietly. For our smooth acquisition, you must be eliminated — that is the only way we can rest assured."

Alice gradually understood. So everyone had come for the map — conflict was unavoidable. "Who are you? What do you want with the map?"

"Words are useless. Die!" Laurie roared, golden fighting energy surging around him as he charged forward at astonishing speed!

At the same moment, countless fighting-energy-reinforced arrows thudded continuously through the walls, striking toward Alice relentlessly!

Alice's fighting energy and mana intertwined and merged as she was forced into a defensive posture, caught in an awkward pincer attack on two fronts....

Some time before the battle began, in Old John's study.

Merlin was still discussing that very question with the old man —

Is it true or false that a human claiming to be a demon has descended from the heavens?

As someone influenced by demon culture, Merlin believed that except for the demon race, whose historical records were remarkably genuine, other races all had some degree of exaggeration — inflating their own kind, making the credibility of certain matters rather questionable.

But Old John firmly believed that during that ancient Era of the Gods, a truly exceptional hero had indeed appeared, because so many historical versions recorded it — the possibility of it being real was quite high.

"Sir John, I find such a matter with absolutely no evidence to be rather unbelievable. While the probability of it having actually occurred may be higher, I'd rather believe it never happened at all." Merlin placed the ancient book on the table, clearly having lost interest in such unofficial histories.

"No, no, no, Mr. Merlin, you're still being far too extreme — clearly straying beyond the bounds of rational judgment. As you should know, I am far older than you and my knowledge is far richer. Analyzing from past historical experience, during the Era of the Gods, a strange hero similar to a demon truly did appear and ended the gods' rule." Old John shook his head emphatically, believing that although Merlin's strength was formidable, he was still somewhat inexperienced when it came to scholarship.

Merlin simply smiled without responding, thinking that Old John must be under eighty years old, which meant his own age was more than double.

If knowledge were measured by age alone, that would be truly laughable — and he was still at an overwhelming advantage.

Simply stating his age would terrify Old John, perhaps — better to keep a low profile.

"History itself is merely an epic written by victors to praise themselves. To paint their own glorious and great image, they dare say anything at all, so it cannot be trusted at all."

"I do not deny your point, but it still holds reference value. Although history has been distorted by later generations beyond recognition, we can still glimpse what major events occurred long ago from within its fragments." Old John's expression gradually grew grave.

"Come now, Sir John...." Merlin pointed at the ancient book on the desk and said with a helpless smile, "The author of this book must be an elf. The motif of praising one's own race is quite obvious — are you certain he didn't fabricate a story outright simply to make the elven race sound more glorious?"

"This.... does hold possibility, but then what of the similar accounts found across multiple historical texts?" Old John clasped his hands behind his back, eager to hear Merlin's explanation.

"Whenever similar events appear, it is always for some selfish motive." Merlin rested his cheek on his hand and recited what the demon race's historical records stated: "The destruction of the Era of the Gods was entirely because the World Tree, which nourishes all things, was severed — triggering the Twilight of the Fallen Gods. The culprit was the black dragon named Nidhogg, who dwelled at the base of the tree's roots."

Old John was about to continue arguing with Merlin when suddenly, two violent surges of Saint-tier pressure collided, and the entire mansion began to shake with a deep rumble.

"What's happening?! Who's fighting inside my house?!"

Merlin sprang to his feet, his brows furrowing. He could feel waves of dragon-like majesty — Alice must have run into trouble.

"It's Alice!"

"Isn't she supposed to be cultivating?!"

"Why has combat suddenly broken out?!"

title: Chapter 37 — Bedchamber Attendant
content:
Chapter 37 — Bedchamber Attendant

Volume 13 · Chapter 37

"Not good, it seems like bad guys have broken in!" Old John frowned, a flicker of shock and doubt in his eyes.

Besides the pressure emanating from Alice, he could sense another Saint-tier aura—clearly not just some petty thief.

As for the other archer, Oswald, he was too far away to be sensed.

Old John was puzzled. His home only had books and concentrated magic fluid—nothing valuable enough to attract a Saint-tier powerhouse.

"Tch!"

Merlin hurriedly stood up, wanting to check on Alice's condition.

He knew Alice should have been in meditation, and now that a fight had broken out, something must have gone wrong.

Merlin "sprang" up from his chair and rushed out the door toward Alice's room upstairs.

"Let me go see what happened, Old John. You wait here for me."

"How can that be? An uninvited guest has come to my home. It's my responsibility to protect it. Let's go together." Old John picked up his magic staff.

Merlin had seen that Old John was very old and wasn't sure if he could still fight. He was worried the old man would be a burden and wanted him to stay behind.

But Old John was completely young-at-heart and refused to just sit idle. Merlin was instantly at a loss.

"Fine."

When Merlin and Old John arrived at Alice's room, they found the wooden door had long been shattered by the rampant pressure.

Thick cold air slowly billowed out from the room, white and hazy, settling on the ground like clouds.

Looking up, they saw not the neat room before, but golden icicles scattered everywhere.

Alice held a slender sword, standing in the center of the room. She looked unhurt, her gaze fixed on the night sky outside.

At this point, the room had been blown open with a huge hole, like a missing corner. The entire wall had been pierced through, allowing a clear view of the outside...

Golden icelines stood all over the ground, emitting bone-chilling cold. One might mistake it for an ice cellar.

"What happened...?" Old John saw his house in shambles, not knowing what battle had taken place here. If he had arrived any later, his house would have been completely destroyed.

Merlin looked at the ruined room and felt the fight had been fierce. Otherwise it wouldn't have ended up like this. Who was it? Why attack Alice?

At this time, little Johnson woke up early from his sleep, rushing over in his pajamas with his sleep cap crooked.

When Johnson saw the scene inside the room, he immediately froze, staring blankly with wide eyes.

"...What have you done?! Did you think you were a demolition crew? Don't you know repairing a house is expensive?!"

Johnson cared about his home. Having a hole blown through it made him angry; the repair costs were no small amount.

"Sorry, I didn't mean to. It was completely forced by the situation." Alice turned back, feeling embarrassed by what she had done. She didn't want to ruin Johnson's home either, but the enemy had attacked with lethal intent, forcing her to counterattack with full force.

"What the heck?!" Johnson went crazy, already regretting letting Merlin and Alice stay here. "What did you do in the room?! You destroyed the house?! This is my home!"

"Alright, alright. The house doesn't matter as long as no one's hurt. We'll find a craftsman tomorrow and it'll be fixed in a week." Old John was quite generous and didn't push too hard.

"Father!" Johnson was somewhat dissatisfied, feeling his father was too easygoing. These were his family's properties, and seeing them destroyed made his heart bleed...

"Don't be so petty. The situation was special." Old John looked at his son, signaling him to calm down. "A Saint-tier thief broke in, and Alice's reaction was perfectly understandable."

"There was a thief?!" Johnson was full of question marks. He had been sleeping so deeply he didn't know anyone else was home, only waking up from the loud noise.

"You're too slow to react to what's happening outside. Thieves broke into Alice's room and fought—destroying the house was unavoidable. You can't just blame guests for lacking manners." Old John patted his waist and scolded his son a few times.

Johnson muttered and lowered his head, falling silent. He couldn't blame Alice anymore—when thieves break in, anyone would resist.

Merlin walked up to Alice and asked, "What exactly happened just now?"

"Two people wanted to kill us..." Alice answered with lingering fear. If she hadn't woken up from meditation in time, the consequences would have been unimaginable—they might have been ambushed successfully.

"What?! Someone wanted to kill us? Who?" Merlin was astonished, thinking they had only been in Highgate City for a few days and couldn't have made enemies with anyone.

"I don't know their identities either. One was a martial artist, and the other was a sinister archer lurking outside.

Alice was equally unclear about the invaders' appearances—their faces were hidden, making it hard to judge who they were.

She glanced at the John family father and son present and felt it inconvenient to say directly. Letting others know the mission details wasn't good, especially fellow adventurers.

So Alice thought for a moment, suspiciously hiding the treasure map matter, and tried to narrate using words both she and Merlin would understand.

"But it seems the other party had the same goal as us—both wanted to get whatever was in Baron Barton's hands... saying we blocked their..."

"Is that so..."

Merlin understood immediately, stroking his chin. He thought, so the enemies just now were two—one outside providing support. No wonder he hadn't sensed them immediately.

However, hearing Alice's words, Merlin felt some trouble coming. It seemed this journey wouldn't go smoothly—they would definitely encounter obstacles.

Since the enemy had already tried to kill them and failed, they would likely resort to even more unscrupulous retaliation later.

"It seems we're not the only ones interested in that. Now this is getting troublesome..."

"It seems your mission has caused trouble. If you need help, as president of the Highgate Adventurers Guild, I can greatly assist you." Old John said seriously. They were all adventurers and could help each other when necessary—no big deal.

"Thank you for your kindness, but this mission is special to us. It's inconvenient to say specifically." Alice politely declined.

Although Old John's help might make things more stable, before leaving, Earl Austin had repeatedly instructed Merlin and Alice not to tell outsiders about the family curse. There were people with ulterior motives watching. After all, the Austin family had enemies too—if the curse was exploited, the situation would be terrible...

"Alright, it seems your mission this time is no small matter. But if you encounter troubles you can't solve, come find me. I can give you appropriate help. In Highgate City, I still have some influence." Old John still left them some options, not making it absolute.

"Thanks."

Alice thought Old John was really nice to her and Merlin, wondering if he had other motives.

But right now, Alice couldn't think about that. She asked Merlin about next steps.

"Merlin, what now? Should we investigate the enemy's identity? We're both after the same thing—conflict is inevitable."

"We have no clues to investigate with? The priority is still to get the item first, but we need to patiently wait for Baron Barton to come. These few days we heighten vigilance against more enemy attacks. The rest...?" Merlin thought for a moment, spread his hands, and said, "Let's sleep to gather energy~"

"Please take this seriously! Don't be so negative!" Alice was somewhat dissatisfied, feeling Merlin decided things too casually.

"I am serious! But we have no clues about the enemy—should we search blindly like headless flies? That would only further alarm the snake. Please, do things efficiently. I won't waste energy on things I know won't yield much." Merlin turned and walked away, waving his hand. "I'm tired. Good night."

Alice hesitated, seeing Merlin showed no intention of digging deeper, so she had no choice but to give up.

But she thought about it and felt Merlin was right. For now, they could only wait for Baron Barton to return—getting the treasure map first was the priority.

Alice was also tired. Looking at the ruined surroundings, she realized she had nowhere to sleep, so she asked shyly...

"Old John, do you have any other rooms?"

"Really no more. We only have four empty rooms—my son and I each have one, the rest are book storage. It wouldn't be polite to put guests there." Old John said awkwardly, worried about Alice's accommodation. He thought to himself that Merlin and Alice were married, so why weren't they sleeping together? There might be hidden reasons, so he didn't dare ask more.

"No need, just give me a blanket. Anywhere that can block wind and rain is fine." Alice didn't really mind sleeping rough—it wasn't the first or second time—but she still muttered inwardly: why does such a big house only have four rooms? This father and son really love books!

"That won't do. If you sleep in the storage, it makes our family seem too rude. How about this...?" Old John thought seriously and said, "Let me and my son sleep together. You take his room?"

"That won't do! I can't do that. Staying here as guests is already enough. Making you give up your room would be too presumptuous." Alice shook her head repeatedly, thinking if she really accepted, it would be too much.

"No problem, go ahead. My father and I sleep the same anyway. The room will be repaired tomorrow anyway." Johnson crossed his arms, speaking in a condescending tone as if bestowing a favor on Alice.

Merlin stopped walking, noticing Alice's awkwardness. After thinking for a moment, he waved his hand carelessly and said...

"Alice, come here. Don't trouble the hosts anymore.

Sleep with me...

Tonight I'll reluctantly allow you to attend my bedchamber."

~Careful

title: Chapter 38 — Schemes (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 38 — Schemes (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 13 · Chapter 38

“Uh.

Alice’s expression froze on her face, as hard as if two pounds of cement had been smeared on it.

She didn’t hesitate to say she’d sleep with him?

Doesn’t he feel hesitant? Don’t act like it’s routine!

And... what does ‘serve’ mean? What the hell is this bastard thinking?

Although Alice didn’t say anything, she was already cursing Merlin in her heart.

“What are you standing there for? Come with me?” Merlin saw Alice staring at him without moving, thinking this guy’s brain must be broken.

“I...”

Alice was hesitant. If Merlin had said it casually, it wouldn’t be a big deal, but the word “serve” made her overthink — she felt Merlin’s room was a demon’s lair, and once she went in, she’d never come out.

“What do you want? Stay in the warehouse or have Mr. John clear out a room for you?” Merlin frowned, wondering why Alice was so scared — he wasn’t a tiger eating people.

“...Nothing, let’s go.” Alice thought it’d be better to put up with Merlin for a few days than to trouble others, so she stiffly followed him...

On the other side, the two members of Azure Flame escaped from the John family mansion.

Only after confirming they were safe did they stop to catch their breath and recover.

Laurie wiped the cold sweat from his forehead and cursed, “Damn, that’s crazy! That female adventurer is too tough — she even knows dragon magic and martial arts?”

Oswed hadn’t shown up during the fight — he only provided remote support, so his energy wasn’t as drained as Laurie’s; he was still in good shape.

But Oswed agreed with Laurie’s sentiment: Alice was indeed hard to deal with. He’d watched the whole battle and felt he wouldn’t have a high chance of winning if he fought her alone.

“Yeah, she’s tough. A swordmaster’s fighting style is already unpredictable, and now she grows super-strong scales — I’m useless against that. Meeting an enemy like this is just bad luck — really frustrating.”

“Don’t you have that expensive charged spear? Throw it and it’ll destroy a city — even the guild leader is wary of it. Why didn’t you use it? If you had, those scales would be pierced!” Laurie said angrily, implying Oswed held back and didn’t contribute much — he was doing all the fighting.

“Brother, I only have one. Using it here would be a waste. What if I miss? We’d lose our chance to get the vampire relic map. Can’t you think?!” Oswed frowned, annoyed by his simple-minded partner, and retorted sharply.

“...Sigh.” Laurie sighed heavily, feeling he missed a chance to kill the adventurer, but admitted Oswed had a point — the charged spear was too valuable to waste.

“Don’t be so down. We haven’t failed. Killing those adventurers isn’t strictly necessary — it just makes getting the map easier.” Oswed patted Laurie’s shoulder, speaking gently.

“You make it sound easy, but that female adventurer is a peak Saint-tier. We both struggled against her. This level of opponent should be left to the guild leader — only he can take her down.” Laurie recalled their leader, Humphrey, who was at the same level as the adventurer — he believed the leader could dominate her.

“We misjudged the enemy’s strength — that’s my fault. I didn’t expect her to have dragon powers. But whether she lives or dies isn’t critical. We’re still in a good position — we’ll get the map before them, and if we can’t fight, we can always run.” Oswed said confidently.

“What do you mean? Don’t beat around the bush — I hate people who act mysterious.” Laurie was impatient and wanted Oswed to explain.

“You’re so dumb. We have the baron’s butler on our side! Steve will help us get the map first. Don’t you see our advantage?” Oswed smiled slyly.

“But that man is obsessed with revenge — will he really help us?” Laurie was skeptical about trusting the butler.

“We don’t need Steve to sincerely help us. He wants to kill Baron Barton, and only we can help him — that’s enough. As long as the map isn’t in our hands, we won’t act, and he’ll be the one getting anxious.” Oswed knew he had Steve cornered.

“...Yeah, we don’t need to act — someone will bring the map to us.” Laurie finally understood Oswed’s plan.

“Exactly. We don’t have to kill the adventurer — it’ll just make the mission harder. But we must keep Steve obedient.” Oswed laughed.

“Right, I was overthinking it. But the fact that we two couldn’t beat her still bothers me.” Laurie frowned, still upset about the fight.

“Don’t worry. That adventurer is doomed. A few days ago, Steve told me the baron will attend a ball right after returning. That’s our perfect chance to get the map — a rich merchant at the ball is interested in it, so the baron will carry it. The adventurers will likely come too, and we can ambush them and kill them all.” Oswed grinned coldly.

“How will you do that?” Laurie asked, sensing Oswed had a plan.

“I’ll buy some black powder mixed with mana-blocking particles — it’s toxic to mages and disables magic instantly. We’ll plant it at the ball, then secretly kill the baron and take the map. Once we’re safe, I’ll throw my charged spear to detonate the powder. Even if the adventurer has strong magic, the particles will make her powerless — and the whole city can burn with her. Haha!” Oswed rubbed his chin, imagining the explosion.

“Brilliant!” Laurie gave Oswed a thumbs-up, praising him: “No wonder Vice Guild Leader Eden speaks so highly of you!”

“Everything is calculated.”

(/°V°)/

title: Chapter 39 — Sleeping posture
content:
Chapter 39 — Sleeping posture

Volume 13 · Chapter 39

Deep into the night.

Since Alice's room had been damaged, she had no choice but to share a few nights with Merlin.

As for the damaged room, Old John said Alice didn't need to compensate; tomorrow morning he'd find a craftsman to fix it.

Fortunately Alice had only demolished one room, not the whole house—enough to keep the John family from feeling devastated.

But Alice felt this matter was somehow tied to her; doing nothing would trouble her conscience.

So Alice gave the 1000 gold coins Merlin had extorted days ago to Old John, to help repair the house.

Old John wasn't keen to trouble guests, but little Johnson beside him accepted the money without ceremony, planning to find workers tomorrow.

Seeing the John family father and son accept the money, Alice felt slightly better; after all it was Merlin's ill-gotten money, used to repair the damage—quite fitting.

If Merlin knew what Alice did, he'd probably jump out of his skin—that was his money, yet Alice gave it away so generously!

At this point in Merlin's room, the two hadn't fallen asleep and had been in a standoff for a long time—

"Come on Alice, sleep with me." Merlin lay on the bed, patting the mattress like a holy perv trying to lure an underage girl into crime.

Alice's breath stalled, leaning only against the door, ready to flee, scared by Merlin's enthusiasm into having no sleepiness at all.

Actually Alice had stood there a long time, refusing to get on Merlin's bed and sleep with him.

It was all because of Merlin's earlier "attending the bed" that Alice felt unsettled and didn't want to approach him.

Always worrying that this guy Merlin would go wild at midnight and do beastly things; you can't have malicious intent, but you can't guard against others either.

"Tsk! What are you hesitating about? Shy? Haven't we slept together before? What's there to be shy about, come on~" Merlin kept patting the bed, signaling Alice to come up, leaving space for her.

"What do you mean not the first time?! Don't say things so ambiguously! Even if we're in the same room we sleep separately, okay?!"

Alice angrily rebutted Merlin.

"Tsk! What do you want? I've said all the nice things, do I have to coax you to sleep like a child?!"

Merlin sat up from the bed, looking somewhat impatient; it was already late night and Alice still wouldn't come up.

This made Merlin irritable. "Want to sleep? Come up. Don't want to? Leave my room. What's with standing there?"

Merlin was very sleepy but minded having someone standing and staring at him while he slept, feeling like a treacherous subject plotting against him.

"...Get down. I sleep on the bed, you sleep on the floor. I won't share a bed with you!" Alice made her demand, sounding quite harsh.

Merlin got angry, feeling Alice was bullying him. His own room, and this outsider made him sleep on the floor—completely unreasonable!

"Hey, have you any shame? Your room was damaged, I took you in out of kindness, and now you make me sleep on the floor—isn't that too much?"

"...What's so unreasonable? I'm a girl! Sleeping in the same bed with you is too dangerous!" Alice looked vigilant.

Merlin heard Alice's explanation, his expression becoming complex. "I won't do anything to you, don't think too much."

"You always lie. Who knows if you're saying this to lower my guard. Based on your past behavior, your credibility isn't high." Alice was extremely wary of Merlin.

"Please don't be so sensitive. Do you think you have something that tempts my desires?" Merlin frowned, scanning Alice's whole body, still seeing nothing particularly appealing.

"Don't joke around! If I sleep with you, who knows what'll happen—too late to regret it!" Alice glared at Merlin, feeling inexplicably annoyed.

"Fine, are you planning to stand here all night?" Merlin asked, as if giving Alice a final chance.

"I'm not forcing you to give up the bed. If worse comes to worst I'll... " Alice looked around, saw no better spot, threw the blanket on the floor. "I'll sleep on the ground. Anyway not with you!"

"Good idea." Merlin nodded, threw himself down and didn't care about Alice. This was his room—he definitely wouldn't give up the bed.

Seeing Merlin ignore her, Alice felt a stifled anger with nowhere to vent, wanting to kick his butt to relieve her resentment.

But after calming down slightly, Alice felt a twinge of guilt. Was her demand really too much? How was this different from a robber?

Alice sat on the carpet angrily, wondering how to survive the long night. The floor seemed cold, and one blanket probably wouldn't help.

Besides Alice was in pajamas, hard to resist the autumn night's low temperature. Even if she fell asleep she'd probably wake up freezing?

So Alice felt increasingly unbalanced, turning to look at Merlin on the bed, her gaze growing resentful.

"Ah~" Merlin rolled over, lying sprawled, sighing. "The bed is so big. Sleeping alone is great, much better than someone sleeping on the floor~"

Alice was indirectly mocked by Merlin, her face flushing with anger. Thinking: this bastard Merlin, after knowing each other so long, couldn't he care about her even a little?

Truly worthy of being a demon, heartless to a certain realm...

No! Can't let this guy be comfortable. I need to seize territory too!

Alice finally found an excuse, grabbed a pillow and climbed onto Merlin's bed, placing her rapier between them to draw a line.

Finally Alice lay down with relief, her back to Merlin, ready for a cold war to the end.

"What? You said you'd sleep on the floor?" Merlin glanced at Alice beside him. This guy's body was more honest than his mouth.

"I'm unhappy just seeing you happy. Taking your territory? As a Hero, suppressing demons is my duty. Hmph~!" Alice huffed, her reasoning convincing.

Merlin said nothing, thinking Alice's excuses all sounded lame. Couldn't she try harder?

"I warn you! Don't cross my sword, or I'll fight you!" Alice warned.

"Pfft! Do I want to cross over?" Merlin smirked, increasingly disdainful of Alice's sensitivity.

"Good. Don't break your promise, or your remaining credibility with me will vanish." Alice dropped a threat and slept soundly.

No words all night, until the next day....

Both still in bed. Alice slept deeply, but Merlin was sleepless all night.

Because Alice had just improved her strength, her body was still unaccustomed, so she slept very restlessly.

All night she kept moving, making Merlin unable to sleep, occasionally punching Merlin—whether intentional or not unknown.

At this point Alice's sleeping posture was awkward, turning 180°, lying sprawled, her feet on Merlin's face.

Congratulations, Alice fulfilled her dream in her sleep—truly a cause for celebration.

Merlin's face was deformed by Alice's foot, he looked sideways at this hateful woman.

Merlin found Alice slept soundly, probably from exhausting training, occasionally scratching her belly—quite the tomboy image.

"Holy crap! Said no crossing boundaries!"

"Wasn't this a unilateral breach of agreement?!"

"After falling asleep she becomes a completely different person!"

Come to think of it, I never noticed before...

"This stinky woman's sleeping posture is so ugly."

(∞ha)

title: Chapter 40 — Charge the Ball
content:
Chapter 40 — Charge the Ball

Volume 13 · Chapter 40

A few days later

Merlin once again came to Baron Barton's mansion, wanting to ask whether this guy had returned or not.

However, this time the one receiving Merlin was no longer the butler Steve, but a captain of the guards with high-level strength.

The guard captain looked to be nearly 40, with a stubbly beard and a slightly unkempt appearance, but his eyes were bright and spirited.

After carefully sizing Merlin up, he didn't seem to care much about this Black Iron adventurer.

"Your Excellency, what business do you have?"

"I want to ask if Baron Barton has returned; I have business to see him," Merlin said straight to the point.

The guard captain looked at Merlin with obvious disdain and continued, "Lord Baron has just returned, but not just anyone who wants to see him can see him."

"I was recommended by Count Austin; I have a very important matter. Recently I already handed the letter of recommendation to the mansion's butler, so could you please go and announce me?" Merlin spoke quite politely.

The guard captain sighed, clearly somewhat impatient, but still intended to go check. "You wait here; I'll go verify."

Merlin was helpless, thinking that he wasn't a bad person, so why be so guarded against him?

Actually, the baron's mansion wasn't very strict before; it was only after Baron Barton learned that the treasure map he had obtained while injured was a treasure that he became cautious, constantly worried about being targeted.

If it weren't for Steve publicizing everywhere that the baron had a vampire ruins treasure map, Baron Barton would have long since thrown the thing away as waste paper.

Merlin waited patiently at the door for a while, and the guard captain came out with an ugly expression, his tone carrying a hint of anger.

"Your Excellency, why are you lying?! Mr. Steve never received any letter of recommendation; what exactly are you plotting by trying to deceive me?!"

"Ah?! Didn't receive the letter of recommendation?" Merlin frowned and retorted, "Impossible! I handed it to your butler personally; how could he not have received it?"

"Would Mr. Steve's own words be false?" The guard captain looked at Merlin coldly and said lightly, "I advise you to put away your petty schemes and not do anything bad. Now everyone knows Lord Baron has a treasure; lowly types like you trying to exploit loopholes, I've seen far too many. Hurry up and leave, or I won't be polite."

"What are you saying? I just want to see Baron Barton; if that's not possible, letting me meet Mr. Steve for a face-to-face talk would also work; maybe there's a misunderstanding." Merlin tried his best to suppress his temper.

"It was Mr. Steve who told me to chase you away; your identity is definitely too suspicious!" The guard captain gripped the sword at his waist, feeling that dealing with a Black Iron adventurer was no problem. "I'm warning you one last time; get lost!"

Merlin narrowed his eyes, feeling a bit stifled anger, and his hand unconsciously moved to the sword hilt.

But after thinking for a moment, he put it down again, feeling that if he acted now things might become troublesome.

In case Barton was a miser, not only would he fail to get the treasure map, but he'd also botch the mission.

So Merlin planned to go back and discuss with Alice a bit before deciding.

However, Merlin hadn't gone far when he heard the guard captain shouting at his subordinates not far behind him.

"What are you standing around here for? Why haven't you gone to prepare the most splendid carriage?!"

"Lord Baron is about to go to Kathy Castle to attend a ball; that's a very high-class entertainment venue, only allowed for gentry and nobles."

"You lot are only able to enter thanks to Lord Baron's favor; all of you perk up and don't go out there and embarrass Lord Baron!"

"That's how it is......"

Merlin went back to find Alice and told her the whole story in detail, letting her understand the current situation.

"What did you say?!" Alice knitted her delicate brows. "That butler refused our request for a meeting and even denies receiving our letter of recommendation?!"

"Yeah." Merlin nodded, seeing people coming and going around them, and signaled to Alice. "Lower your voice, okay? Don't be so loud; afraid others won't know?"

Alice felt dissatisfied inside and couldn't help complaining, "Why is that person like this? What for? We have no deep hatred with him; why would he do us harm?"

"Who knows?" Merlin shrugged his shoulders, looking innocent. "Maybe we did something wrong?"

..... Alice lowered her head, thought carefully, and tentatively asked Merlin, "You said the people who came to assassinate us a few days ago—could they be related to this butler?"

"Not clear, but can't deny the possibility either." Merlin indicated he also found it hard to say for sure.

"That's strange. Why would they make things difficult for us? Most likely that butler also covets the vampire ruins treasure map." Alice speculated in her heart.

"Possible. We need to move fast; the sooner we see Baron Barton the better. So we'll also attend this ball; we can talk to Baron Barton face-to-face about the treasure map at the ball." Merlin nodded.

Alice looked at the brightly lit castle before her and murmured, "This...."

By now the two had already arrived at Kathy Castle in Gaowei City, standing in front of the main gate, preparing to attend this ball.

Kathy Castle is located in the center of Gaowei City; although its area isn't very large, its elegant style makes all surrounding buildings pale in comparison.

From the outside it looks extremely magnificent; compared to the capital's luxury hotels it's not inferior, and seems even more splendid.

Outside the wide entrance, two rows of neatly dressed servants stood, as if they had undergone special training, wearing polite and humble smiles.

Carriage after carriage stopped before Kathy Castle; servants hurried up to open doors and usher the distinguished guests into the castle interior.

Tonight's guests are all big shots who move in Gaowei City's high society; the men are exquisitely dressed, behave like gentlemen, and all have female companions.

From the attire of the ladies attending the ball, one can tell this is a formal ball; they wear custom-made puffy dresses, trying to cinch their waists as thin as bamboo poles, attempting to attract outstanding males at the ball.

However, Merlin doesn't like this world's morbid aesthetic, especially the thick white foundation on the girls' faces, which in the night look like ghosts

"However you look at it, this is a ball for nobles, right? We don't even have the qualifications to enter...." Although Alice didn't want to dampen Merlin's enthusiasm, she couldn't help stating the truth.

"Don't worry; as long as luck is good, we can sneak in." Merlin replied confidently, then looked at Alice beside him and said seriously.

"The situation is urgent now; we must see Baron Barton."

"Don't forget that besides us, there are others eyeing the treasure map on the baron...."

title: Chapter 41 — Identification
content:
Chapter 41 — Identification

Volume 13 · Chapter 41

Alice thought for a moment and felt that was right; now was not the time to hesitate, after all another force was eyeing the treasure map. If they hesitated in this race against time, big problems might arise. After Alice figured it out, she nodded at Merlin and said, “Let’s go; if it really doesn’t work we can think of another way, but we must see Baron Barton tonight.” The two arrived at the gate of Kathy Castle, initially planning to blend in by following a few nobles to slip in. However Merlin and Alice’s attire was really too plain— at a glance they didn’t look like they were coming to the ball. Everyone else around was wearing gorgeous, flamboyant evening gowns, making Merlin and Alice’s casual clothes stand out conspicuously. As a result, their plan of muddling through failed immediately; they were stopped right away by a few servants who had no intention of letting suspicious persons into the ball. A servant who seemed to be the head waiter approached Merlin and Alice, glanced at them a couple of times and said, “Sir and madam, what brings you here?” Alice saw that it wasn’t going to be easy to get in, so she tugged Merlin’s sleeve and said, “Look, I told you this ball has a threshold— sure enough we’re being stopped.” “Don’t panic, now is not the time to lose our composure,” Merlin replied in a low voice, then turned to the head waiter and said calmly, “Do we even need to ask? We’re obviously here to attend the ball.” “Do you have invitations?” the head waiter asked patiently, although he felt the two didn’t look like ball attendees, but if they had invitations he couldn’t slight them. “Can’t we get in without an invitation? I’m good at this sort of thing— wouldn’t more people be better?” Merlin retorted, trying to shamelessly bluff his way in. As soon as he said that, the nearby nobles burst into laughter; pale‑faced ladies hid behind their fans, shaking with laughter. In the nobles’ eyes, Merlin’s comment was utterly ridiculous; aside from country bumpkins from backwater towns, who would say something so out of place? This ball was hardly a place for ordinary commoners; it was a gathering for nobles to mingle, with an obvious class threshold. Even if you were a purple‑gold adventurer, these stiff old noble gentlemen wouldn’t accept you as one of their own; they’d merely see you as a mere warrior. In such an exclusive little circle, those lacking sufficient class standing are rejected to the extreme— letting a third‑rate adventurer in would probably just humiliate them. The head waiter gave an embarrassed laugh, considering his image and refraining from saying anything harsh, but he had already assumed Merlin and Alice were here to cause trouble. Alice, behind him, couldn’t help but tug Merlin’s sleeve again and whispered, “I told you, this ball isn’t simple; we should think of another way.” Merlin gave no reply; doubt began to creep in, and he started entertaining other twisted ideas, wondering whether he should knock out a few servants and impersonate them to sneak in. “Sir, it seems you still don’t understand what kind of gathering this is,” the head waiter paused, looked at Merlin and said, “This ball is organized entirely by the Rothschild family, a social exchange for the dignitaries of Highwind City, so your statuses still fall short of the qualification threshold, and besides we never sent you invitations, so regrettably you have no right to enter.” Upon hearing that it was the Rothschild family hosting the event, Alice gasped, recalling that this wasn’t that fabulously wealthy merchant family, the one said to be so rich they treat money like dirt. It seemed there was no chance left; they would have to think of something else. Alice then organized her thoughts in her mind and told Merlin, “Merlin, forget it, let’s think of another way; this is Rothschild territory, we’d better not cause any trouble.” “Wait.” Merlin responded with two words, seemingly already having made up his mind. If the other party hadn’t mentioned that this was Rothschild territory, it would have been fine. But now that they did, Merlin immediately recalled his own identity, and felt there was no reason to keep him away. “If ordinary people aren’t allowed in, then what if I’m a diamond member of the Rothschild family?” “Huh?” the head waiter was obviously taken aback; though flustered by Merlin’s remark, he still answered blandly, “If you are a diamond member, you may enter any venue set up by the Rothschild family without issue, but I advise you not to make such a boring joke, because whether you’re lying or not is obvious at a glance.” The surrounding nobles who were watching the spectacle began to whisper and chuckle, preparing to laugh at Merlin’s expense. “You actually claim to be a diamond member of the Rothschild family? How bold!” “Yeah, take a look at him— does he look like a rich and powerful person? He’s just a poor, shabby adventurer.” “It’s only because the empire lacks a law against bragging; otherwise this guy would surely be sentenced to life imprisonment.” Although Alice felt uncomfortable hearing the gossip around her, she also found it hard to believe Merlin’s words. Alice wasn’t very familiar with the Rothschild family, but she also knew that even becoming an ordinary member would require astronomical sums of money from the family’s enterprises. “Merlin, enough already— stop wasting time here; we could think of a better alternative. I know what you’re trying to do: you want to bluff your way in by deception, but the odds are minuscule.” “I haven’t bluffed my way in; I really am a diamond member, genuine~” Merlin shrugged his shoulders. Hearing Merlin’s words, Alice rolled her eyes, thinking, “Does this guy really need to get so into the act? Does he actually think he’s a distinguished guest of the Rothschild family? If I didn’t know his true worth, I’d easily be fooled by him— even a drama queen needs limits.” “Sir, I’ve been tolerating your nonsense; if you keep causing trouble here, I’ll have to call someone to remove you.” The head waiter’s implication was a threat; although he saw Alice was a mithril adventurer and not easy to provoke, there are plenty of strong men working for the Rothschild family, so he might not fear them. “Moreover, as far as I know, there has only ever been one diamond member in the family’s history, and that person must be a big shot; as for you, I think leaving now would still preserve the last shred of your dignity.” “Then please verify it— the matter dates back a while; if I remember correctly, my information should have been recorded by your family, so you should be able to look it up.” Merlin insisted on having them check. “Tsk!” the head waiter clicked his tongue impatiently; although he was sick of Merlin’s nagging, with so many people watching he still had to follow procedure. So the head waiter ordered his subordinates to fetch the crystal ball that contains all Rothschild members’ information; in real‑world terms it’s basically facial recognition. Alice covered her face, unable to bear looking at Merlin any longer, thinking, “Why is he so obsessed? How could there possibly be Merlin’s information in there? Now it’s all over—I don’t even know how to wrap this up…” The head waiter went and got a crystal ball, aimed it at Merlin and took a continuous shot; the sphere immediately emitted a faint green glow. Seeing the reaction of the crystal ball, the head waiter’s eyes widened, his eyeballs seemed to become bloodshot and red, his whole body trembling. “No— it can’t be…” z(°O°I)

title: Chapter 42 — Ritual (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 42 — Ritual (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 13 · Chapter 42

Some of the noble ladies watching from the sidelines couldn't help but start sneering under their breath at the head waiter's reaction.

"See? I told you it was fake. He's so angry his eyes are red."

"Really, some commoners always want to sit at the same table as us nobles. They should look at themselves first."

"This is going to be good. Provoking the Rothschild family is hardly a wise move."

Alice lowered her head, her heart in a frenzy. What was Merlin thinking? He knew it was fake, so why did it get this far!? Was it still too late to apologize now?

The head waiter wiped his eyes hard, then looked up at Merlin with an unusual expression, unable to believe the result. One crystal ball had shattered.

So he waved another crystal ball in front of Merlin. The result was exactly the same as before — a faint green glow appeared.

Actually, the people nearby were too foolish to understand the meaning of the crystal ball's colors. Red meant the identity didn't match, while green meant a complete pass, proving Merlin was truly a friend of the Rothschild family.

"What's the result?" Merlin asked curiously.

"..."

The head waiter stood frozen, his face visibly flushing red. He felt he had judged by appearances just now.

This person in front of him was a genuine diamond-tier member, of extremely noble status!

He had heard this gentleman had thrown around tens of millions of gold coins at the horse racing track!

But why did he dress so plainly, and why was he a lowly Iron-tier adventurer?

Good heavens! Great people really did like playing special games, disguising themselves as ordinary people to deceive others' eyes!

The head waiter did not hesitate for a moment, nor did he show any disrespect toward Merlin. A diamond-tier member had come to Highwind City and deserved the highest level of treatment.

Even if all the other envoys abandoned their guests, he would see this noble member off from Highwind City.

If the higher-ups of the Rothschild family found out they had slighted a diamond-tier member, they would surely be punished. Fortunately, his identity had been verified in time, or else there would have been trouble.

The head waiter completely changed his previous dismissive attitude, bowed deeply before Merlin, and said politely,

"I never expected you to truly be the Rothschild family's most尊贵 friend. I was blind and slighted you. I will report this to the higher-ups. The punishment I deserve will not be shirked. I hope you won't hold it against me. This is all my personal responsibility and has nothing to do with the family."

At these words, the group of noble ladies who had been muttering beside them erupted into chaos, their expressions filled with disbelief.

Their faces were extremely exaggerated, fans dropping from their hands to the ground, mouths gaping wide.

Some even changed their faces faster than flipping a book, silently sending flirtatious glances toward Merlin, completely forgetting how ugly they had looked just moments ago.

"Could it... really be a diamond-tier VIP?!"

"How is that possible!? Becoming a diamond-tier VIP requires tens of millions of gold coins, right?"

"I was saying it earlier — a handsome man like him, im... impossible to be completely useless..."

Alice's face went blank, then she covered her face with both hands and let out an incredulous sound. "Eh?!!"

"I told you so. Now you believe me, right?" Merlin turned his head and gave Alice a thumbs-up.

Alice's face turned dark in an instant. This couldn't be! How could Merlin possibly be a VIP of the richest family in the world!? What did he look like that he could associate with tycoons!? And a diamond-tier VIP — had this guy been that wealthy before!? No! Something must be wrong! This had to be a dream!

Still half-convinced, Alice noticed that Merlin had quite a few secrets, so she couldn't help but step forward and ask through gritted teeth,

"Merlin, what is going on?"

"Isn't it obvious? I'm a diamond-tier VIP~" Merlin spread his hands and put on an innocent expression.

"How is that possible? Becoming a VIP of the Rothschild family requires a lot of money, doesn't it? And diamond-tier — I've never even heard of such a level." Alice clung to Merlin, insisting he explain clearly.

"Well..." Merlin crossed his arms and stroked his chin, pondering. "Actually, I once threw tens of millions of gold coins at the Rothschild family's horse racing track."

"Tens of millions!?" Alice blurted out in shock, losing her composure. She wondered why Merlin, being so rich, hadn't paid off their debts. "Where did you get so much money? Did the demon race still give you a severance package after you got fired?"

"Cough, cough!" Merlin awkwardly coughed twice and said in a low voice, "It was from that inheritance armor of yours. I sold it for tens of millions of gold and immediately threw it into the horse racing track. Didn't I tell you about this half a year ago? You know the rest."

"Eeeek!!" Alice was so angry she forgot how to speak properly. Her chest heaved up and down, and she nearly fainted with her eyes rolling back.

"Hey, hey, hey!" Merlin quickly caught Alice as she was about to faint and comforted her, "Don't get so worked up. Relax."

Alice took several deep breaths, but the memory of the source of all her misery made her heart ache and go crazy. She couldn't maintain her composure at all.

"So that's how it is. The horse racing track was run by the Rothschild family, and you only became a high-tier VIP by using the money from selling my armor. I hate you."

"Umm..." A bead of cold sweat rolled down Merlin's forehead as he gave a dry laugh. "That's all in the past. Let's not bring it up again. Wouldn't it be better to look forward to a beautiful tomorrow?"

"Beautiful my foot! I've ended up in this mess because of you. I want to strangle you!" Alice could no longer hold back. Old grudges and new grievances surged together, and she grabbed Merlin by the neck and shook him wildly. "Eeeek eeeek eeeek!"

Merlin's expression remained blank. Shaken by Alice like a roly-poly toy, he showed absolutely no reaction.

Alice's frenzy skill dealt HP-1 to Merlin, but Merlin's thick-skinned skill instantly restored HP 10086.

Sigh, this annoying woman is such a trouble. From now on, I should avoid letting her remember the matter of the Hero's inheritance armor.

Otherwise, if she keeps fighting me every day, I won't have any peaceful life ahead.

Merlin pushed Alice's hands away and said with a very serious expression,

"Calm down. If I hadn't thrown around tens of millions of gold coins at the horse racing track back then, would the two of us be able to enter this ball tonight?"

Alice was speechless, unable to refute.

"So it's all fate. I threw around tens of millions of gold coins for today!" Merlin said confidently, not mentioning at all that he had done it for fun.

"Don't blame everything on fate! What did fate do wrong to cover for a despicable guy like you!" Alice retorted angrily.

"Cough! Don't worry about so many details. The point is, the result is good." Merlin turned to the head waiter. "Can we go in now?"

"Yes, but please wait ten seconds, sir and madam." The head waiter said respectfully to Merlin, then turned and ordered,

"Everyone, quickly prepare the highest-level welcome ceremony!"

"Welcome our Rothschild family's most尊贵 friend!"

"This is not a drill!"

"Repeat once more:"

"This is not a drill!!!"

title: Chapter 43 — Blessings
content:
Chapter 43 — Blessings

Volume 13 · Chapter 43

The squad leader's words had just fallen, and all the behind servants, as if trained specially, quickly sprang into action.

The splendid door before them was fully opened, no longer just half-open, but like a palace, fully opened.

The wide-open doors revealed the golden and splendid hall within, appearing extremely dazzling.

Immediately rushing out of the ancient castle of Kathy were a group of people dressed in black and white servant uniforms, standing neatly on both sides with solemn expressions.

Three cannon shots suddenly rang out, startling the observing noble ladies, catching them off guard with this sudden display.

Welcome music and dance commenced, and two servants pushed a bright red wool carpet forward, laying it all the way to Merlin's feet.

Watching the scene of nearly a hundred servants bowing simultaneously before them, Merlin and Alice were at a loss, obviously frightened by this imposing aura.

"Goodness, does it have to be so dramatic?" A cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead as he muttered a complaint. Originally, he had just wanted to attend the dance, never expecting such a grand spectacle. If one didn't know better, they'd think the queen was coming on an inspection tour.

...Perhaps this is just the most basic operation for the rich? Poverty limits our imagination... Alice quietly responded beside him, thinking that Merlin wasn't an ordinary member, so why were the welcome protocols so high?

"Damn capitalist class..." Merlin muttered with a dark face, reflecting that his diamond VIP identity was actually so impressive? He hadn't known before, but the Rothschild family apparently still had money, this carpet seems to be high-quality goods, what to do? A impulse of robbing the rich to help the poor suddenly surged in his heart.

"Alright, please go in." The squad leader made a gesture of invitation, signaling that Merlin could enter.

Merlin nodded, wanting to turn around for Alice, so he instructed, "That behind..."

"I understand, I understand, sir, don't worry. This silver-haired lady as your wife will also receive equal treatment." The squad leader responded tactfully.

"Not a wife..."... Merlin frowned and rebutted.

"This..." The squad leader's eyes turned, thinking himself clever, said, "Even if she's your mistress, it's the same."

"Who is his mistress?! ?" Alice glared at the squad leader, thinking that a mistress is not as good as a wife for one's enjoyment!

"Eh..." Cold sweat trickled down the squad leader's forehead, wondering what relationship it was if not a wife, and not a mistress either.

"Alright Alice, don't fuss. Let's go in first." Merlin waved at Alice, thinking that the task was on hand, don't waste time on such trivial matters.

After the two walked away, the squad leader wiped the cold sweat from his forehead. The sole diamond VIP arriving in High City was not a small matter and should be reported to the family head.

Many observing noble ladies, seeing the people go, began to enter the dance hall one after another, but were blocked by a row of servants.

"What are you doing? Why won't you let us in?" C

The squad leader expressionless, spoke in a calm tone—

"Sorry, this passage is the VIP passage. Everyone can enter from the side door."

QF SF Novel

Since it's a dance party, with Merlin and Alice's attire, it's very inappropriate.

Under the squad leader's suggestion, the two need to change into relatively splendid evening gowns.

Otherwise, randomly wandering about in the dance party, it would probably be extremely impolite behavior.

Merlin and Alice thought about it, feeling that they should follow local customs and change, otherwise they would appear out of place here.

So the two, under the lead of servants, each went to the fitting room to prepare to change into evening gowns and come out, agreeing to meet in the hall.

As a diamond-level VIP, Merlin has many privileges in the entertainment place opened by the Rothschild family.

Including playing freely, dispatching dedicated servants for full-process service, even those expensive custom-made evening gowns are free, just can't take them away; they must be returned after the dance ends.

Merlin feels that these VIP privileges which are simply chaotic are actually very useful, completely a green light all the way doing as one wishes, he believes it will greatly reduce the difficulty of obtaining the treasure map.

Usually male evening wear is not as complicated as ladies', so Merlin changed into his clothes early and came out. And behind him followed the squad leader.

Brilliantly sparkling crystal floor, reflecting the splendid lights of the dome, above were twelve crystal and gold chandeliers shining brilliantly, making the entire hall brightly lit, as if it were daytime.

Noble men and women clinked cups in the dance floor, laughter and merriment, completely different from previous scenes, harmonious and beautiful.

In fact, the lives of nobles won't be too hardship; they just control some power and can enjoy a lifetime.

Unlike Merlin and Alice whom he had encountered before, they are all ordinary folks, every day having to strive for a living.

So suddenly coming here today, it instantly made Merlin recall past feelings, surrounded by heavily made-up noble ladies, swallows and swallows.
