title: Chapter 44 — Meeting
content:
Chapter 44 — Meeting

Volume 13 · Chapter 44

"Uh, does your family also run these kinds of operations behind the scenes?" Merlin was speechless. He thought the Rothschilds were at least a major family, so even if they had some stains, they should have been whitewashed by now, right? How could they still offer slave services to VIP guests?

"This is also something we can't help with. Sometimes certain VIPs always have special requests, and we have to satisfy them," the head waiter said with an embarrassed expression.

Merlin nodded to show he understood. He figured everyone had their emotions and desires, and some shady transactions were normal.

But didn't they just mention female goblins?

Good heavens! What kind of taste is this? Aren't they afraid of being woken up in the middle of the night!?

Merlin's face darkened as he complained inwardly. He thought about how the Rothschild family had connections everywhere — why couldn't they get demons?

"Why can't you provide demons? Is there some difficulty?"

"Um..." The head waiter gave a troubled smile and said helplessly, "The demon race's territory is extremely dangerous. Almost no humans who go there ever return alive. Moreover, demons are hard to tame — unlike other races where there are many ways to handle them."

"I see..." Merlin thought about it and it made sense. The demon race was indeed a different race, but unlike the various non-human races in the United Kingdom, they completely refused to reason with humans and rarely had contact with the outside world.

"Has Mr. Merlin decided which one to choose?" the head waiter asked, rubbing his hands together with a sycophantic expression.

"Never mind, never mind."

Merlin waved his hand. He remembered that even normal interactions with other women usually earned Alice's death glare and accusations.

He was right under Alice's nose right now. If he dared to do anything reckless, she'd probably jump up and bite his neck off.

"Don't overthink it. I was just wondering if your family's VIPs have any more normal perks."

"Normal... normal?" The head waiter wiped the cold sweat from his forehead and thought for a moment before answering, "You have the right to freely hire two Saint-tier experts from the Rothschild family for one month. However, after the hiring contract ends, you cannot apply again within two years."

"Boring." Merlin shook his head, having no interest in the privilege of hiring Saint-tier experts.

Perhaps for others, being able to hire two Saint-tier experts was a very useful privilege, but for Merlin it was of little use.

Because with Merlin's strength, did he really need bodyguards? There was absolutely no need.

"Your level also qualifies you to directly meet the head of the Rothschild family. You only need to make an appointment one month in advance. This is an honor not available to ordinary people. Only rulers of various countries have the right to meet the family head," the head waiter said with a very serious expression. If you weren't of high status, there was simply no chance to meet the leader of the richest family in the world.

"Boring." Merlin had no interest in this either. He thought that since he had no intention of robbing the rich to help the poor, what use would meeting that family head be?

"..." The head waiter immediately felt immense pressure. After thinking for a moment, he added, "Oh, right — you can also use our family's intelligence network."

"Hmm?" Merlin became interested and looked at the head waiter. "Intelligence network?"

"That's right. As the wealthiest family, the Rothschilds certainly need to constantly guard against unknown risks, so our family's intelligence network is extensive and covers almost every corner of the Human Empire. If you need any help, our intelligence agents are obligated to assist you." The head waiter glanced around, secretly leaned closer to Merlin, and lowered his voice. "To be honest, our intelligence network is even more powerful than the royal family's. Even Queen Elizabeth recently sought our help."

Merlin frowned. He thought, no way — could a mere merchant family be that vast? He recalled that Elizabeth had previously investigated his background. Could she have asked the Rothschild family for help?

Seeing that Merlin finally showed some reaction, the head waiter secretly breathed a sigh of relief and continued, "With your Diamond VIP status, you will receive assistance anywhere within the Rothschild family's sphere of influence. I imagine your work as an adventurer requires a lot of information, right? Our intelligence network would be very useful."

Merlin nodded. He thought this perk was actually quite useful, though he wondered just how accurate the Rothschild family's intelligence network really was.

If it was truly spread across every corner of the Human Empire as the waiter said, then it would indeed be a very beneficial privilege.

Merlin was about to continue chatting with the head waiter when his peripheral vision caught a balding middle-aged man walking out from the other side.

Of course, it wasn't the bald head that caught Merlin's attention — it was the bodyguard accompanying the middle-aged man, who was precisely the guard captain who had been at the entrance of Baron Barton's mansion earlier that day.

Seeing the guard captain following so respectfully behind him, there was no need to guess — this balding middle-aged man must be Baron Barton himself.

Baron Barton's clothes were very vintage, but the expensive gold ornaments on him were dazzling and must have been worth a fortune.

Although his beard made him look dignified, his small eyes gave off a very cunning impression.

At this moment, Baron Barton's expression was not good. He seemed to be muttering curses as he just came out of a relatively secluded room, apparently having been thwarted over something.

Merlin felt this was a rare opportunity and said to the head waiter beside him, "You can go first. I'll explore on my own."

"Isn't that appropriate? As a VIP, Mr. Merlin, I'm supposed to serve you the entire time," the head waiter said hesitantly.

"It's fine. I have some matters to attend to. It would be inconvenient for you to stay by my side," Merlin replied tactfully.

"Then very well." The head waiter bowed slightly and added, "If you encounter any trouble, please call for me immediately."

In the rest area near the ballroom.

Baron Barton drained the glass of wine in front of him, then said irritably, "Damn merchant! Trying to buy my treasure map for five million gold — what a daydream! Unless it's twenty million gold, there's nothing to discuss!"

"...Indeed. You should see Baron Barton's status. Five million gold for armor is no different from robbery," the guard captain quickly flattered in agreement.

"I'm so angry. This buyer won't do. I'll have Steve find someone else next time. This time I need someone who understands the value of the treasure map, otherwise it's a complete waste of time," Baron Barton said in an agitated manner.

"Understood. I will relay this to Mr. Steve," the guard captain nodded and responded.

"Hey." Merlin walked over with a wine glass and sat down on the sofa opposite Baron Barton.

The guard captain was startled upon seeing Merlin, very puzzled about how this guy had gotten in. Wasn't this ball only for nobles and other important figures? How could a Iron-rank adventurer sneak in!? The Rothschild family's screening was too sloppy.

Since Baron Barton's group had arrived early, they hadn't witnessed the scene of Merlin being welcomed with the highest-level honors, which is why both of them now held Merlin in low regard.

"Baron Barton, correct?" Merlin said in a probing tone.

"Hmm?" Baron Barton looked up with a puzzled expression.

"Who are you, sir?"

title: Chapter 45 — Black Powder (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 45 — Black Powder (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 13 · Chapter 45

Merlin smiled, glanced around, saw no one paying attention, and calmly replied, “I was sent by Count Austin. I heard you have a treasure map of the vampire relics, so I’d like to take a look. In the Count’s name, I hope you’ll cooperate with me.”

“Oh? Count Austin?” Baron Batton was cautious and didn’t readily believe Merlin’s words, especially since he didn’t know the other’s identity.

At that moment, the captain of the guard, seeing Merlin still playing this game, whispered into Baron Batton’s ear, “Sir, don’t trust him. This man is a naked liar; this morning at the manor he used the same excuse to try to see you. I suspect he’s after the map on you. He claimed to have a letter of introduction from Count Austin to give to Mr. Steve, but I asked around—there’s no such thing.”

“Oh~ I see…” Baron Batton squinted, nodded, his gaze at Merlin turning unfriendly. He now possessed a treasure, and anyone would try any method to get it. Many swindlers had visited before using similar tactics, but none succeeded; he was still pondering how to sell the map for a good price!

“Chew!” Merlin clicked his tongue; seeing the baron’s expression, he knew this task wasn’t simple—there was a clear trust crisis.

“The Count Austin introduced you? I don’t bother checking whether that’s true or false. Of course I can look at the map~” Baron Batton’s expression turned sly, rubbing his fingers and whispering, “All I need is enough money, and I’ll let you see as much as you want.”

“Huh? What money? Count Austin’s intention is that you hand it over directly, with no other conditions.” Merlin paused, then continued seriously, “I heard you used to be a subordinate of Count Austin, right? So ignoring his words yourself is a bit excessive.”

“Haha, putting aside whether you’re some little swindler, even if Count Austin really sent you, what of it? To be frank, I only recognize money, not people. If you sincerely want the map, I can give you one chance…” Baron Batton tapped the table twice with his finger, “A flat price of twenty million gold, and the map is yours.”

Merlin’s face turned black, looking at the baron’s greedy mouth, feeling irritated. Indeed, Johnson hadn’t been wrong; this baron of Highway City had a problematic character, profit‑driven and completely oblivious to propriety. Whether or not he had Count Austin’s letter made no difference—this guy would still trouble himself for profit, trying to reason with a scoundrel, a real misstep.

Seeing Merlin stay silent, Baron Batton assumed the young man was frightened, so he rose shakily and sneered, “If you have no money, don’t covet my things, and don’t overestimate your own worth. I despise the poor most of all, especially those who are poor yet like to act like big wolves.”

After speaking, the baron didn’t linger; he left with the guard captain to rest elsewhere, still angry at Merlin, the scheming intruder.

Merlin sat on the sofa unmoving, his face gloomy and silent. He lowered his head slightly, propping his chin, thinking—

There’s no way out.

Dealing with this single‑cell creature, fists work better than words.

..

He wouldn’t give this bald fool any color—perhaps he thinks he can dominate Highway City single‑handedly?

Outside Kaisi Castle.

Oswid and Laurie arrived here according to plan.

Butler Steve knew Baron Batton was meeting a merchant buyer today, so the treasure map was likely on his person.

Having learned this crucial information early, Steve told Oswid and Laurie, so they could prepare.

Today’s ball was the perfect opportunity for Oswid and Laurie to act.

If everything went smoothly, snatching the vampire treasure map would be as easy as taking candy from a baby, and they could then turn around and destroy the entire Highway City, proclaiming the fame of the Azure Dark Flame!

According to Oswid’s speculation, those two adventurers should have entered the ball by some method, allowing old grudges and new ones to be settled together.

When the time came, they’d throw a charged spear; no one at the ball would survive. All the plans rested on Oswid’s calculations.

At this moment, Oswid and Laurie disguised themselves as wine‑carrying workers, bringing three barrels of red wine, each filled with black gunpowder laced with magical interference particles.

The main purpose was to deal with Alice, to disrupt her magical power so she couldn’t release it instantly.

In Oswid’s script, Alice would die in the first explosion, turning into a mangled corpse on the spot.

These interference particles are expensive; Oswid bought out every potion shop in Highway City to barely afford three barrels of the black gunpowder.

Although the quantity wasn’t huge, it was enough to handle Alice, and having too many barrels would raise suspicion; getting into Kaisi Castle was already a problem.

Oswid calculated that the explosion would engulf Kaisi Castle and its surroundings, and combined with the power of his charged spear, Alice’s chance of escape was negligible.

The two pushed a small cart carrying the three powder barrels to the gate of Kaisi Castle, only to be stopped by the servants.

“Gentlemen, what brings you here?”

“We’re here to deliver fine red wine,” Laurie said with a smile, his demeanor very friendly.

“Red wine?” The servant’s eyes flickered with doubt; normally, before a ball starts, such necessities are already stocked, making extra purchases almost impossible.

“Yes, it’s what your manager ordered. What’s the problem? Didn’t you know?” Oswid deliberately confused the servant, trying to lower his guard.

“This…” The servant furrowed his brow, internally puzzled, wondering whether the manager had placed a supplemental order that hadn’t been communicated yet, and whether he should verify…

“You’re not the professional servants trained by the Rothschild family? How can such a simple task go wrong? You can’t just send us on a wild goose chase! Bring out the person in charge here!” Laurie spoke harshly, his tone suddenly firm, aiming to make the other side lose composure.

Sure enough, under Laurie’s pressure the servant panicked, fearing he couldn’t handle even this small matter and might lose his job, so he quickly apologized, “I’m sorry, gentlemen, I overreacted. We’ll leave the three barrels of wine here; I’ll have them delivered right away.”

“That’s more like it....”

Seeing the task completed, Oswid and Laurie turned to leave, but they didn’t go far; they began patrolling around Kaisi Castle.

The two exchanged smiles, each seeing the other’s triumph; everything was indeed proceeding as they had expected.

“Didn’t expect it to be so easy to get those barrels of black gunpowder inside; now we can go all out,” Laurie said, his excitement barely contained.

“Of course. In my plan there is no such thing as failure,” Oswid said arrogantly.

“Now what should we do?” Laurie asked patiently.

“Isn’t it obvious?” Oswid smiled, looking up, “It’s time for us to slip inside…”

“Kill Baron Batton, seize the Dracula relic map.

title: Chapter 46 — Flirt
content:
Chapter 46 — Flirt

Volume 13 · Chapter 46

The ladies' evening gowns were extremely intricate, which caused Alice to take quite a while before finally emerging from the dressing room.

Now dressed in her evening gown—a blue-and-white off-shoulder princess dress—Alice looked especially radiant.

To make herself appear more curvaceous, Alice had stuffed two extra pads into her chest this time, giving her a notably fuller figure.

Upon arriving at the ball, Alice's graceful figure attracted many glances. If she weren't seemingly calling out for someone, a gentleman would likely have come forward to ask her to dance.

Alice scanned the crowd, searching for Merlin's silhouette—she had agreed to meet him here.

However, after looking around for some time, Alice still couldn't spot Merlin, which made her somewhat displeased.

Didn't we agree to meet here?

How strange. Where is he?

Could it be that I was too slow, so he left me behind?

But I'm a girl too! Can't you be a little more understanding?

Alice lifted her skirt and stamped her foot in frustration, nearly stumbling in the ballroom due to being unaccustomed to high heels.

Such parties generally come with dance partners, with men and women attending together. Now Alice stood alone, and she couldn't help but feel a bit awkward.

Fortunately, Alice soon spotted Merlin's whereabouts. It turned out she had simply missed him earlier because he was surrounded by a group of flashy socialites, being teased and flirted with.

Merlin had just entered the ball as an honored guest. Many socialites had spotted him, and these women, who considered themselves above others, found this seemingly ordinary man quite intriguing and wanted to flirt with him.

After all, those who become Rotschild family guests aren't ordinary people. Even if they aren't nobles, they're certainly extremely wealthy.

Moreover, looking at the level of the welcome ceremony earlier, many socialites could tell that Merlin wasn't just an ordinary guest—he was clearly someone of high status.

This was enough to make many socialites view Merlin with different eyes, and even casting shy glances wouldn't be excessive. After all, if they could successfully flirt with him, who knows what might happen?

Right after Count Batten left, Merlin sat alone on the couch. Somehow, two socialites walked over to flirt with him, and soon more joined until he was completely surrounded.

Although Merlin had little interest in these heavily made-up women, he still maintained gentlemanly decorum, chatting with them politely without rejecting them.

Merlin clearly understood what these noblewomen were thinking. This wasn't his first encounter—he had already experienced this in Manchester.

Generally, noblewomen are arranged into marriages by their families. Once they gain some say in matters, they often become dissatisfied with their marriages. Flirting with other men at balls is a common sight.

However, Merlin pretended not to notice these women's flirtatious advances and blatant teasing, simply engaging in casual conversation.

Merlin had previously experienced a situation where he was nearly driven out of Manchester by a group of ambiguous noblewomen and several noble lords ganging up on him. So he wasn't about to fall for it again.

Yet from Alice's perspective, the scene played out completely differently. To her, it looked as though Merlin was the one flirting shamelessly with a group of married women!

All sorts of rose-tinted special effects were playing behind Merlin, making him appear like a playboy strutting around in the dating scene.

Damn it, why does he look so happy chatting with those women?

As if I don't exist!

I'm still here, and he dares to act like this. If I weren't here, wouldn't this be a complete disaster!

Alice bit her teeth in frustration in her heart, and waves of jealousy surged up, making her dislike Merlin even more. She was angry that he didn't cherish her.

We're at the same party, yet he's flirting with other women. This is really going too far!

Alice's face turned red with anger as she adjusted her long skirt and strode directly toward Merlin, staring at him intently with a murderous gaze, trying to make him realize the severity of the situation.

"Ah, Alice, when did you come out?" Merlin's expression became slightly more reserved upon seeing Alice, no longer as carefree as before.

"I've been out for a while. I've been watching you flirting here for some time now." Alice replied in a suppressed voice, as if holding back her anger.

"......What flirting? I was just having a normal conversation. And what's with that deadly stare? I haven't done anything!"

"These ladies are all proper, you know. You two seem to be chatting so happily..." Alice tried to keep her voice calm, not wanting others besides Merlin to witness the scene.

"These sisters were just talking with me. It's your misunderstanding that we were having such a good time." Merlin attempted to explain, though it lacked persuasiveness.

"Oh really..." Alice's teeth ground softly in response, clearly not buying it. She wore a strained smile that seemed somewhat sinister. "Sisters, I have something to discuss with him privately. Could you all leave for now? Your presence nearby is somewhat inconvenient."

When Alice said this, she sounded very kind, but her tone was actually quite dark, clearly asserting her ownership over Merlin.

The subtext was clear: drive away these fluttering love-struck women and get lost! This is my man. What are you doing bothering Merlin?

These socialites had seen their share of storms and knew that Alice was Merlin's companion. Stealing another man's woman in such a setting wasn't a rational move.

So the socialites stood up one by one, bidding Merlin farewell. As they left, they didn't forget to cast flirtatious glances and drop hints about visiting his room later that night.

Since Alice had arrived, there was no way to continue the revelry. They could only politely wave goodbye to the departing socialites.

"Sisters, until we meet again."

Alice saw Merlin's waving gesture and her heart burned with anger. Until we meet again? Not a chance!

With a sharp slap, Alice struck Merlin's hand away, preventing him from having any further interaction with those women.

Above the two of them, a series of opposing buff effects floated—

Merlin's debuff: "Harem members -1 -1 -1 -1 -1..."

Alice's buff: "Wife status 11 1..-.."

Merlin rubbed his hand and looked at Alice with a bored expression. Now that no one else was around, there was no need to maintain his image.

"Why did you hit me?"

"Why? Because I can't stand how you're cozying up to those women! And you want to say 'until we meet again'? Give me a break! The fact that I saw you proves your fated connection is over!" Alice snapped through her teeth.

"What are you doing? We're at a ball right now. In such a setting, don't make a scene. You should always maintain your elegance~" Merlin adjusted his tie, fully embodying the role of upper-class society.

"What am I doing? I should be asking you!" Alice huffed, walking over to Merlin's side. She couldn't care less about her image anymore, sitting down right next to him with a heavy dose of jealousy.

"What were you doing just now?"

"Taking advantage of my absence to flirt with those women?"

title: Chapter 47 — Poor Ghost
content:
Chapter 47 — Poor Ghost

Volume 13 · Chapter 47

"Huh?" Merlin looked at Alice, extending a finger to emphasize, saying, "Pay attention, she's a fake wife; we're definitely not husband and wife, okay?"
"-..What's wrong with it being fake? Does being a fake wife mean I don't deserve face?" Alice turned her head away, huffing, saying, "After all, I'm your dance partner; ditching me to flirt with other women at this event is your fault!"
"...." Merlin clicked his tongue, gave Alice a complex glance, thinking, "Does that even count as flirting? At most it's just ordinary chatting, right?"
"Honestly, I just took a little longer to change clothes, and you can't help but flirt with others; even if it were assault, you wouldn't be this eager!" Alice puffed out her cheeks, like a hamster eating.
"Hiss~" Merlin sucked in a breath of cold air, retorting, "In your heart, have you already equated me with assault?"
"Wrong, you're even less patient than the assailants." Alice gave Merlin a white-eye.
"...." Merlin felt a bead of cold sweat trickle down his forehead, thinking, "Is my image in Alice's mind already hanging by a thread? It's just chatting with other women; making a big deal out of nothing. If I hadn't missed out on whatever stimulating perks, this woman would really jump up and bite me."
"You shameless guy, whenever you get a chance you pull some sneaky moves behind my back, completely disregarding my feelings." Alice paused, sounding aggrieved as she complained, "We clearly have an important mission at hand, yet you still have leisure to flirt around here—you're truly someone who doesn't know priorities, hum~!"
"Who says I don't know priorities?" Merlin immediately became displeased, continuing, "I've been properly carrying out the mission—I just met Baron Barton here a moment ago."
"Huh?" Alice looked at Merlin, astonished, asking, "Where?"
"Here." Merlin jerked his chin toward the back, indicating, "Right back there; at this very moment he's flirting with a young noblewoman."
Alice turned her gaze backward, where a bald old man was teasing a noblewoman, his expression so lecherous his features were all scrunched together.
Is that Baron Barton? He looks like a vacuous nouveau riche....
Alice glanced a few times then withdrew her sight.
"How did it go?"
"They don't believe we were introduced by Earl Austin, and even if we were sent by him, we still need to follow the game's rules." Merlin answered concisely.
"Huh? What rules? Isn't he supposed to assist us?" Alice asked matter-of-factly.
"That's just our assumption; Baron Barton is a miser who won't discuss any conditions. If you want the blood clan treasure map, you must fork out twenty million gold coins—not a single coin less." Merlin's tone was full of helplessness; running into such a money-obsessed fool is also unlucky.
"I never expected things to turn out like this; even if we wrote to Earl Austin to have him personally mediate, it would likely take over half a month. How are we supposed to get that treasure map? Surely we're not planning to scrounge up twenty million gold somewhere, are we?" Alice asked anxiously.
"We're not idiots; this obvious profiteering behavior—whoever pays to buy it would be wise." Merlin quickly dismissed Alice's thought, thinking even if he sold himself he couldn't scrape together ten million gold.
"What should we do? Should we...?" Alice lowered her head, her expression becoming hesitant, "Should we try to steal it?"
"Yo?" Merlin's eyes lit up with delight as he looked at Alice, teasing, "Even the great Hero is considering solving this by theft? How progressive~"
"...." Alice's face flushed a bit, she earnestly defended herself, "This isn't normal times, so we must take extraordinary measures? Besides, we just want to look at the information on the treasure map; we're not stealing and not returning it."
"You've now learned to mask your wickedness with hypocrisy; congratulations, Alice, you've evolved." Merlin said meaningfully.
"GUN!" Alice snapped angrily, thinking Merlin was truly a belly-full of wickedness—what the heck does that even mean?
"Cough cough, I've also considered stealing it, but do you know where Baron Barton hides the treasure map? Constantly probing wastes too much energy." Merlin countered Alice.
"What should we do then?" Alice felt a bit deflated, having thought everything would go smoothly, but instead encountered endless troubles.
"Don't be so stubborn; since Baron Barton doesn't listen to reason, we'll deal with him using unreasonable methods." Merlin clenched his fist in front of Alice, the implication clear.
"Wouldn't using force be inappropriate?" Alice hesitated, not endorsing Merlin's approach.
"I didn't say to use force, just appropriate threats; this place is full of mixed characters, so we'll be patient first. Once Baron Barton has no one around, we'll make him voluntarily hand over the hidden treasure map." Merlin already had a plan for what to do next, just lacking an opportunity.
"This.- ="
Alice and Merlin have completely opposite views, often leading to many disagreements.
Merlin is accustomed to doing bad deeds, using some rather underhanded tricks, feeling no guilt whatsoever.
But Alice is different; she has a feeling of living in the sunshine, and as a former Hero, she is naturally upright.
As for some of Merlin's wicked ideas, Alice's heart still resists them, and she doesn't want to be associated with him.
However, the situation is somewhat special now; facing the unreasonable Baron Barton, perhaps Merlin's method would be more effective.
Alice took a deep breath, decided to turn a blind eye, pretending she knew nothing.
"But don't go overboard, or else there'll be no way to wrap this up..."
"Don't worry, I know." Merlin patted his chest, thinking, "Will being moderate with this miser actually work?"
"Please enjoy, sir and madam." The waiter served Merlin and Alice a plate of layered cream cake.
"No wonder it's a misunderstanding among the nobles; even the dessert is made just like in the real world." Merlin looked at the cake before him and said.
"The real world? ..... what does that mean?" Alice asked puzzledly.
"Um, nothing, haha."
Merlin gave a dry laugh twice to cover up, picked up the fork and discovered it was gold-colored; the sheen didn't look like simple gold plating.
"Good grief, the Rothschild family can't possibly be that rich, right? Even the utensils at a local dance party are made of gold?!"
Maintaining skepticism, Merlin bit with his teeth, then widened his eyes, his expression turning incredulous.
"Wh... it's really made of gold?!"
"What's there to be shocked about? The Rothschild family seems to be the richest; gold utensils aren't surprising at all." Alice said expressionlessly, looking at Merlin as if he'd just crawled out of a refugee camp and had never seen gold in his life.
"Yeah, what's there to be shocked about...." Merlin rolled up his pant leg, bent the gold utensil, and clamped it onto his leg, preparing to sneak it away unnoticed.
"Hey!" Alice saw Merlin's action, felt inwardly embarrassed, her whole body as if struck by lightning.
"You really want to do this?!"
"Has your skin gotten this thick?!"
"You're greedy for every little advantage; could you be a reincarnated pauper?"

title: Chapter 48 — Arctic Princess
content:
Chapter 48 — Arctic Princess

Volume 13 · Chapter 48

“Tsk!” Merlin dismissed it with a tongue click, emphasizing, “I’m not a reincarnated pauper. This is just rational resource utilization. Gold, as a valuable item, being used as tableware is too wasteful. I think it’s more reasonable to convert it into other resources.”

“Gold is also mine, you know!” Alice completely ignored Merlin’s forced explanation, thinking this guy was just covering up his despicable actions with a veneer of reason.

“It’s just a golden fork. What’s the big deal?” Merlin leaned back on the sofa, carelessly saying, “As a diamond VIP, I’ve invested so much money. Isn’t it a bit excessive to expect me not to reclaim a little interest?”

“That was originally my money? No, that was the Church’s wealth. It has nothing to do with you!” Alice grew increasingly annoyed at Merlin’s brazen attitude.

“What do you mean it has nothing to do with me? The Church constantly organizes armies to attack my territory, causing many demons to die in battle. It’s only natural for me to rob the Church’s wealth.”

“This…” Alice was stunned into silence by Merlin’s rebuttal. Thinking about it, there was some logic to it, but the demons had also killed a lot of Church knights…

Just as Alice was about to counter Merlin, a classical and elegant melody began to play.

The melodious piano sound was graceful and moving, instantly calming the noisy ballroom and bringing the event to its main topic.

The pianist, dressed in a tuxedo and wearing white gloves, danced his fingers across the keys, like playing an overture.

As the most respected and powerful person in the entire Highwind City, Baron Barton naturally entered the dance floor with his recent dance partner.

Baron Barton first nodded and smiled at the guests, then held his partner’s waist and began to dance gracefully.

Subsequently, couples appeared in pairs, entering the dance floor and naturally starting the extremely traditional waltz—

Merlin watched for a while on the sofa, glanced at the side where Alice was, and extended his hand. “Miss Alice, may I have the pleasure of a dance?”

Alice looked at Merlin’s claws, her expression slightly disappointed. “Can’t you be a bit more formal? At least stand up to invite me. How could I possibly agree to this casual approach?”

“Alright then.” Merlin nodded, then stood up and looked around. “Then I’ll have to find someone else.”

“Wait!” Alice reached out and tightly gripped the tail of Merlin’s tuxedo, preventing him from leaving. “You’re going to find another dance partner just because I complained a little!?”

“You didn’t agree, did you?” Merlin frowned, confused by this person’s abnormal behavior.

“I… I never said I disagreed!” Alice said angrily, mentally cursing Merlin for being such a patient-less guy. The more she got to know him, the more she felt the soul beneath this skin was utterly hollow.

“Tsk…” Merlin撇ed his mouth, extended his hand again, thinking, What era is this? Does everyone still expect others to have the patience of three visits to the thatched cottage?

“Since you’re so honest in inviting me, I’ll reluctantly accompany you for a dance.” Alice blushed, placing her hand on Merlin’s, her expression clearly unwilling.

Merlin smiled politely but felt helpless inside—

This nagging woman…

Does she just like playing the game of verbal rejection but physical compliance?

◇

With the rhythmic piano music, the two entered the dance floor and danced like everyone else.

This kind of social dance naturally carried an ambiguous undertone, which became even more intense in this setting.

No wonder noble couples often had lovers. Attending such events daily, mutual betrayal seemed like no big deal.

Merlin held Alice’s hand and used his other hand to support her slender waist, moving to the slow rhythm of the music.

Alice similarly placed her hand in Merlin’s palm and supported his shoulder to maintain balance.

Their fingers were tightly interlocked. Although it was their first dance, their coordination seemed surprisingly harmonious.

One might think they must have danced together often, otherwise such an incredible level of coordination would be hard to explain.

“I thought you were dancing for the first time. Didn’t expect you to be so skilled,” Merlin whispered with a teasing tone.

In fact, when Merlin left the Death Marsh, he didn’t know how to dance in the style of human nobility. The demon race also didn’t have the leisure to spend time on such activities.

So even as a reincarnator, Merlin had never learned. Among demons, attracting the opposite sex often relied on the simplest method: violent conquest.

However, when he was a waiter in Manchester, Merlin had already learned most of it from those wealthy women, becoming a seasoned ballroom dancer, learning quickly.

Merlin recalled that Alice had always lived in the Great Snow Mountains and could dance in the noble circles? That was strange. Who taught her?

“Who’s a first-timer? I learned when I was very young. Don’t suddenly look down on me…” Alice frowned, feeling dissatisfied inside.

“Who taught you?” Merlin asked curiously.

“My teacher, of course…” Alice answered honestly.

“Didn’t you say your teacher was a hermit living in the Great Snow Mountains? How could she know the court-specific dance steps? Could she have come from a noble circle of a human empire?” Merlin became even more puzzled.

“This…” Alice recalled her difficult university life and found it hard to imagine her teacher had once been part of the upper class. “Impossible, right? But my teacher is always knowledgeable. It’s just a dance. It’s not difficult for her.”

Merlin didn’t press further and temporarily believed Alice’s words. Seeing her standard dance moves, he assumed that teacher must have formally studied.

However, Merlin wasn’t particularly interested in Alice’s teacher. Instead, his gaze lowered to Alice’s chest, and he suddenly smiled.

“You… where are you looking? Smiling so lewdly, you disgusting guy!” Alice, at such close proximity, could easily catch Merlin’s every move. Seeing his smile, she immediately blushed and scolded him, thinking this shameless guy had such impure eyes despite the many people around.

“Wait, don’t misunderstand. I just felt your chest tonight was unusually big, much bigger than usual. Did you stuff in a few more pads?” Merlin looked up and asked.

“Do I need you to tell me how many pads to stuff? This is my freedom!” Alice retorted confidently.

“I’m not telling you. I just felt you were really going all out. Stuffing so many pads, don’t you feel suffocated?” Merlin showed a playful expression, wondering how much Alice had looked forward to this ball.

“You!” Alice wanted to leave Merlin, but it seemed rude to abandon him, so she angrily stomped Merlin’s foot with her high heel. “You… talk… so… much…”

“Sigh~” Merlin’s smile froze on his face, stiffly saying, “Stepping on people while dancing? You’re really not a lady.”

“Why should I be a lady to someone like you? Hmph~!” Alice coldly huffed, thinking Merlin lacked gentlemanly manners and deserved such treatment.

Their awkward and unreasonable dance posture naturally caught others’ attention, drawing many questioning glances.

This was a noble circle’s ball, not a peasant’s torch dance. Making a scene here was truly impolite.

A bead of sweat rolled down Merlin’s forehead. He decided to stabilize Alice’s mood and said, “Well… even though you padded your chest, it still looks pretty good.”

“Huh?” Alice lifted her head in surprise, suspiciously asking, “Is that your sincere opinion?”

“Yes, for example, your princess dress tonight… it actually suits you quite well. It’s like the distant polar region, cold and elegant. If I hadn’t known you earlier, I might have thought you were a princess from the Polar Kingdom…” Merlin never said sweet nothings to Alice, but when he did, he was never hesitant.

“Is… is that so…” Alice shyly lowered her blushing face, her dance steps becoming slightly stiff, as if affected by this—

“Even… even if you praise me, I won’t feel happy…”

title: Chapter 49 — Blocked
content:
Chapter 49 — Blocked

Volume 13 · Chapter 49

Merlin saw Alice's reaction and finally quieted down, which made him feel a bit more at ease.

Whether Alice was happy or not didn't really matter; Merlin just hoped she wouldn't throw a tantrum in a situation like this.

However, just as Alice said she wouldn't be happy, she looked up and said, "So you can actually praise someone too? I thought you'd always say something annoying."

"Miss, I was once a rising star in the gigolo world. Don't look down on me so much, okay?" Merlin rolled his eyes, wondering if he had attacked Alice with words too many times, causing her to have some misunderstanding about him.

"Hmph, is that something to be proud of? It's just a smooth-talking liar," Alice coldly snorted.

Merlin smirked in disdain, feeling it was perfectly normal for Alice to dislike him. After all, they had once been on opposing sides, and having different values was only natural.

As for the sarcasm in Alice's words, Merlin didn't care at all. Instead, he斜ed his eyes to look at Baron Barton, who was dancing not far away.

Merlin hadn't forgotten the mission for this trip. Just as it happened, Baron Barton seemed to have had too much to drink and, after saying something to his dance partner, walked straight toward the restroom.

At this moment, Merlin narrowed his eyes, sensing an opportunity. Baron Barton was heading to a place with fewer people; it was time to act.

"Alice, that baron seems to be going to the restroom. Let's go now."

"Hmm?"

Alice suddenly paused, having originally thought the atmosphere was nice and wanted to stay with Merlin a while longer.

But the sudden interruption made Alice feel a bit bad, though the mission was still more important.

"Let's go..."

The restroom door.

The bodyguard captain was guarding here. For the safety of Baron Barton, no one else would be allowed in for now.

Merlin and Alice walked straight over. The ball was in full swing, so there was literally no one here.

Even if the two used some tricks, they wouldn't be noticed at all.

Merlin and Alice stood in front of the bodyguard captain, staring directly into his eyes.

The bodyguard captain looked at Merlin and the unfamiliar Alice beside him, completely dismissing the two of them.

It was normal for Merlin to be looked down upon, and Alice, not wearing her adventurer's credentials and having retracted her aura, made it impossible for the bodyguard captain to recognize her as a peak Saint-tier powerhouse.

"What do you want? The restroom is temporarily occupied by the baron. If you need to use it, just wait here patiently for a while."

"Move aside, I need to go in and talk to that bald monk, Barton," Merlin was already blunt, directly verbally insulting the captain's master.

The bodyguard captain, hearing Merlin insult his master, was instantly furious. "You, a lowly opportunist, actually want to see the baron? Don't you ever look at yourself in the mirror? I don't know how a mere iron-grade adventurer like you got in here, but I can assure you, you must have used underhanded methods!"

"Tsk!" Merlin was impatient and turned to Alice. "Give him a taste of his own medicine. This guy is too full of himself."

Alice's eyes widened, her pupils instantly turning into brilliant golden color, her sharp pupils exuding an intimidating aura. A powerful and terrifying dragon's威压 immediately pressed down on him.

The bodyguard captain "thudded" to the ground, yellow liquid leaking from his pants. He had actually been scared to urinate by Alice's dragon's威压! ?

His face was pale, his whole body trembling uncontrollably, his eyes filled with sheer terror, as if he had seen an unimaginable monster.

The bodyguard captain finally understood the situation somewhat. The woman in front of him wasn't simple at all; she was definitely someone you couldn't just惹.

"Hey, you should take a look at yourself while you're still wet, you stupid...," Merlin scoffed, saying to Alice, "I'll go in to find Baron Barton. It's not very convenient for a woman to go in there."

"Okay, I'll keep watch for you," Alice nodded.

Inside the restroom.

Baron Barton was sitting on the toilet, his face full of contemplation.

Even now, he was thinking about who would be the best to sell this treasure map to?

After thinking it over, he still couldn't find a good candidate.

However, Baron Barton thought selling it to the Rothschild family would be better, though he didn't know if they were interested in a blood族's treasure.

Thinking that two million gold coins wasn't a small amount, the Rothschild family definitely had the capability to buy it.

But the head of the Rothschild family wasn't someone you could just meet, and Baron Barton certainly didn't have the qualifications.

Baron Barton decided to find some connections to inquire. If the Rothschild family was interested, it would be a highly profitable deal.

This treasure map was obtained several years ago when Baron Barton was an officer in the Edinburgh garrison.

At the time, he had heard that there was a treasure deep in a certain mountain range. Long ago, countless adventurers had ventured into the mountains to seek treasure, but all had come back empty-handed, and some had even died inside.

Various legends had sparked strong curiosity and greed in later generations. Baron Barton, wanting to get rich overnight, had led a group into the deep mountains to seek treasure.

Originally, Baron Barton had gone with a try-it-out attitude, but by sheer luck, he had indeed encountered a mysterious cave guarded by vampires.

After a painful sacrifice, with only two people escaping, Baron Barton had only obtained a piece of parchment with strange writings.

At first, Baron Barton thought he had gotten a useless item, but after being coveted by many people, he realized the parchment was a treasure, hiding a big secret.

This was why Baron Barton was now seeking a buyer at an exorbitant price, though obviously the matter wasn't going smoothly.

"Hey, beauty..."

A sudden chat声 startled Baron Barton, almost making him urinate on his pants.

He had already instructed the bodyguard captain not to let anyone in, so how did someone get in?

Baron Barton looked up with some panic, seeing Merlin's half-smiling expression.

...Who allowed you to come in! ? This is temporarily occupied by me! "He roared.

"So what if I came in? You're really impressive, aren't you?" Merlin looked down at Baron Barton's below-the-belt size and showed a hint of disdain. "Could you pull up your pants? I'm a bit dizzy from the sight."

"...You..." Baron Barton turned red in the face, quickly pulled up his pants, and stood up. "Where is my guard! Why didn't he stop you! ?"

"Ah? He's already scared傻了. Don't expect anyone to come save you. It's just you and me here, understand?" Merlin extended his finger and poked Baron Barton's chest.

Baron Barton nervously swallowed and said in a weak voice, "I warn you! I'm the lord of the whole Gowei City. If you're disrespectful to me, wait for my punishment! If you can survive..."

A crisp "smack" echoed. Before Baron Barton could finish his sentence, Merlin generously gave him a slap.

A mere human lord trying to threaten the Great Demon Lord was truly unaware of the sky's height and the earth's depth. Merlin根本 didn't buy this.

"...What are you warning me about?"

"...Baron Barton, seeing that Merlin wasn't afraid of him, immediately started panicking, his fat body trembling and hugging the wall. "What do you want to do? What's your intention? Many things can be discussed."

"Ha..." Merlin crossed his arms, scrutinizing the shorter Baron Barton, and said in a teasing tone--

"Wanting to surrender now and talk?"

"Weren't you just very arrogant?"

"How powerful you are in Gowei City has nothing to do with me. In front of me, you need to stand properly."

title: Chapter 50 — Drowning (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 50 — Drowning (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 13 · Chapter 50

"Now now, let's talk this out properly. If you have any conditions, I'll do my best to meet them," Baron Barton said, uneasy.

"If you'd had this attitude earlier, would I have bothered coming to find you in person?" Merlin felt Baron Barton was just asking for a beating, unwilling to yield without being taught a lesson. "Hand over the treasure map to the vampire ruins."

"....."

Baron Barton had long guessed the other's purpose, but hadn't expected such directness.

Honestly, Baron Barton didn't want to give it up — after all, it was the key to his rise.

Just handing it over like this, getting zero benefit in return, would be a massive loss.

Baron Barton's miserly nature flared up. He lifted his head and said forcefully, "No! This is robbery!"

"What did you say?" Merlin casually turned on the faucet beside them. Water gushed into the washbasin with a splash.

"Your blatant extortion costs me too much. You've got to let me taste some sweetness at least. Even if—" Baron Barton took a fearful step back. "Even if you threaten me, I won't budge on this. Money in one hand, goods in the other. Fair trade."

"Ah~, fair trade. I like that. No, wait..." Merlin, having received a demon's education for hundreds of years, truly believed in fair trade. But deep down he was still a human steeped in sin. "Do you know fair trade often has a premise? That premise is equal strength — balanced power is the foundation of fair trade. If a genuine demon stood before you today, your wish for fair trade could be fulfilled. But I'm not one. I'm arrogant. If I'm displeased, I'll trample the rules."

"Wait, I think you have some... misunderstanding! I can sell you the map at a discount. Just need..." Baron Barton's shifty eyes rolled. He trembled as he held up a finger. "Just ten million gold coins. That's... not too much, right?"

Merlin's face darkened in a flash, his whole person turning ice-cold. He felt this baron was beyond saving — still trying to squeeze benefits at a time like this, completely failing to grasp how dangerous his situation was.

So Merlin didn't even respond to Baron Barton's proposal. He grabbed the man by the collar and shoved his head into the overflowing washbasin.

Merlin pressed Baron Barton's head down hard, not letting him struggle free to breathe, letting him get up close and personal with Death. Otherwise, this shameless hide would never cooperate.

"Mmph... ugh!!!"

Baron Barton thrashed wildly under Merlin's grip, his entire head submerged, experiencing wave after wave of suffocation.

With Baron Barton's strength, how could he resist Merlin? He was in danger of drowning any second.

Baron Barton flailed, water splashing everywhere, but under Merlin's suppression he was no different from a chick — utterly at the other's mercy.

When Merlin felt it was enough, he yanked Baron Barton out of the water and whispered, "Listen well. I won't give you a single copper. Hand over the map obediently, or the physical suffering coming next — you understand."

Baron Barton was soaked through, gasping in great gulps. His face was indistinguishable between cold sweat and water, pale as a sheet. "I... I was wrong. Fifty million. Fifty million at a friendship price — that's no problem, right? ...Really can't go lower!"

Merlin narrowed his eyes, murderous impulse surging. If not for the client Austin seemingly being on good terms with Barton, this guy would already be a corpse.

Truly beyond saving. Still thinking of extorting me at a time like this?

Merlin decided to be even more ruthless. He shoved Baron Barton's head back into the water. Today he'd make the man hand over the map willingly...

A while later.

The guard captain had already fainted from fright, or was conscious and playing dead.

Alice paced back and forth outside the door. Seeing Merlin not come out for so long, she grew restless, unsure what was happening inside.

She wasn't worried for Merlin's safety — only that he might take extreme measures against Baron Barton, making things messy afterward.

Thinking of Merlin's usual methods, Alice felt he had no bottom line when he turned evil. It made her deeply uneasy.

Alice kept feeling that behind the restroom door, Merlin was torturing Baron Barton, tormenting him into compliance.

From all of Merlin's past behavior, those who refused to learn and kept resisting — they'd seemingly all been killed by Merlin.

This Baron Barton would clearly leave a bad taste in Merlin's mouth. His personal safety was probably in dire straits.

Alice wanted to go in and check, but this was the men's restroom — she really couldn't just barge in.

However, Alice hadn't heard any pained screams from outside. She figured Merlin was probably keeping his word, handling it in a relatively gentle way.

In reality, Baron Barton was being held underwater, nearly drowned — how could he possibly scream?

Seems Alice was still too naive, not well-versed in torture techniques, judging everything by screams alone.

Merlin walked out of the restroom, expression unreadable, looking perfectly composed as if nothing untoward had happened.

He was wiping his hands with a towel. Looked like things had reached a conclusion.

"How'd it go?" Alice hurried over to ask.

"Mr. Barton has agreed to hand over the map to us. Only, that parchment isn't on him. He says after the misunderstanding is cleared up, he'll personally take us to retrieve it." Merlin replied coolly. Seems under threat, Baron Barton ultimately chose to yield.

"That smooth?" Alice found it hard to believe, felt it was too easy.

"Not smooth enough for you? Getting the vampire treasure map is what matters." Merlin dried his hands and tossed the towel into the trash bin.

Sh Light Novel

"You didn't use some cruel method to force him to submit, did you? That would be going too far." Alice questioned suspiciously.

"No way. I'm not that kind of person. Look at me — do I look like someone who uses violence? It was just verbal threats." Merlin refused to mention his torture methods, silently thinking—

Good thing I avoided Alice. Otherwise she'd probably lecture me.

Having a naive justice freak as a teammate is truly a headache...

In the corridors of Castle Casey.

Baron Barton didn't choose to return to the ball, instead heading for the lounge to hide, avoiding Merlin like the plague.

He was a soaked, bedraggled mess, face bruised — clearly nearly tortured to death by Merlin. He was currently berating his guard captain.

"You're a f*cking waste! Why didn't you stop him?!"

"Where were you when I was nearly drowned?! Taking my money but not doing your job — are you useless?!"

"I really raised a bunch of useless guards for nothing. I don't care — you find a way to fix this right now!"

"This grudge... I'll never swallow it. Whatever the cost..."

"I'll make that blond bastard die right here!!"

(+h n▲)

title: Chapter 51 — Claiming a Life
content:
Chapter 51 — Claiming a Life

Volume 13 · Chapter 51

Upon hearing the baron's words, the guard captain realized he was planning to fight those two adventurers to the death.

But the man looked ordinary, while the woman was genuinely a Saint-tier powerhouse!

This didn't seem like something that could be retaliated against easily—mess it up and he might bring disaster upon himself.

The guard captain thought Baron Barton was being stubborn, so he could only try to persuade him gently, hoping the matter would just be dropped.

If Barton insisted on retaliation, the guard captain would feel the same pressure.

"My lord baron, they have a Saint-tier expert? This grudge seems hard to avenge—even gathering all the guards in the manor, we still couldn't beat them."

"A Saint-tier expert?" Baron Barton looked confused, still unaware of what the guard captain had gone through.

"Yes, there were two of them—the woman was the blonde man's companion, and she's a Saint-tier expert." The guard captain said awkwardly, wanting to shift the blame to his own insufficient strength rather than deliberately failing to rescue Baron Barton.

Baron Barton clearly hesitated, feeling a hint of fear. This was becoming complicated—the point was that blonde bastard wasn't afraid of him because a Saint-tier expert was backing him up?

In all of Gaowei City there were only a handful of Saint-tier experts, and none at the barony mansion. What could he use to oppose them?

"My lord baron, it's truly not that I refused to save you—I was completely held back by that Saint-tier expert. Out there in confrontation, our odds were only fifty-fifty. I simply couldn't afford to be distracted." The guard captain said this shamelessly.

"Nonsense! You really think you can trade blows evenly with a Saint-tier expert? Don't flatter yourself—I know exactly what you're capable of!" Baron Barton's expression turned contemptuous, thinking the guard captain was boasting without considering his own weakness.

"Baron, please don't be angry. That's exactly what I mean—if I hadn't been held back by the Saint-tier expert, how could I possibly have failed to save you?" The guard captain forced a laugh and explained.

"Hmph!" Baron Barton was thoroughly displeased, still struggling to swallow his pride. He was the lord of Gaowei City, yet after being beaten he had to hold back. "This matter cannot be dropped! Two adventurers dared to assault an imperial official. They've gone too far!"

"Uh, but my lord baron, we don't have any Saint-tier experts here. We simply can't match them." The guard captain replied anxiously.

"We can seek protection from the Rothschild family! Don't forget whose territory this is. I was attacked here, so the Rothschild family should be held responsible!" Baron Barton declared with conviction.

"What are you getting at?" the guard captain asked cautiously.

"Summon the person in charge of Cathy Castle right away. Tell them we're under threat and seeking shelter. Tonight we won't be returning to the mansion—we'll stay here. Even if that Saint-tier adventurer is powerful, can they stand against the Rothschild family? Don't forget their guards include plenty of Saint-tier experts too." Baron Barton quickly changed his tune, seeking outside help. He was completely unwilling to hand over the vampire's treasure map to Merlin.

The guard captain suddenly understood, nearly having forgotten about this option entirely. "Understood, my lord baron. You go to the lounge and rest first. I'll go find the person in charge of Cathy Castle immediately."

Baron Barton nodded contentedly. Each time he wiped his facial wounds with a warm towel, it hurt so much he grimaced.

However, on the way to the lounge, someone was already waiting for them. It couldn't have been anyone other than the Dark Guild member who had infiltrated—could it?

Laurie stood in the middle of the corridor, blocking Baron Barton's path. He had been waiting for a long time.

He slowly raised his head, looked at Barton with a meaningful gaze, and spoke in a chilling voice.

"Baron Barton, we finally meet. This hasn't been easy."

......

Today Baron Barton had suffered considerable humiliation and was still trembling with residual fear.

Being stopped by a stranger now was hardly a good sign.

Perhaps another desperate opportunist who had his sights on his treasure map, and he looked like someone who wouldn't be reasoning with.

Baron Barton forced himself to stay calm but instinctively stepped behind the guard captain, then demanded loudly.

"Who are you!?"

"My identity doesn't matter. All you need to know is that you're about to die." Laurie donned his gauntlets, already planning to strike. He had been watching from the shadows for a long time, and this was truly a rare opportunity.

Baron Barton felt a trace of despair. He couldn't understand why so many people were jumping out today to cause him trouble. "I have no grudge against you. We've never even met. Why kill me? Are you also here for my treasure?"

"You're clever. That's right—I've come for the secret of the vampire ruins on your person." Laurie rubbed his fists together eagerly.

"...Protect me! I've kept you this long, and now is the time you're useful!" Baron Barton felt some fear. There was absolutely no one around right now, and he couldn't predict what would happen next, so he pushed the guard captain forward.

"....I—"

The guard captain instantly felt immense pressure. Unable to gauge the opponent's strength, he could only steel himself and draw the blade at his waist. "Where did you come from, you arrogant fool?! Baron Barton is the lord of all Gaowei City! This is Rothschild family territory—how dare you act so wildly? Aren't you afraid of being crushed by a united force!?"

"Just a city lord, nothing more. I've killed plenty of people with status higher than a baron. And as for the Rothschild family? Hah... laughter..." Laurie spread his hands, releasing his Saint-tier pressure. "I am a commander of the Dark Guild's Azure Blue Flame. Is that stinking rich family supposed to intimidate me? In my presence, the dead are all equal!"

"Urgh!" Baron Barton's face turned pale, his body went rigid, as if petrified. He never expected an actual Saint-tier assassin to show up.

Only now did Baron Barton truly realize the severity of the situation. His treasure had drawn the attention of so many Saint-tier experts—it must be extraordinary!

This wasn't about making money anymore; it was about carrying a miraculous treasure bringing death upon himself. But realizing this now was already too late.

"I'm sorry, Baron. A Saint-tier expert is truly beyond my ability to oppose!" Feeling the overwhelming Saint-tier pressure, the guard captain was so terrified he lost all will to resist. He turned and ran, not caring whether Baron Barton lived or died—he just needed to escape this place to survive.

However, at the moment the guard captain turned around, an arrow pierced straight through his skull, delivering a fatal blow.

The guard captain's face contorted in agony, his eyelids fluttered, and he collapsed to the ground, convulsing. Blood spread across the ground—he was beyond saving.

"Want to leave? That won't be so easy." Oswalt lowered his bow and arrow, blocking the escape route and ensuring no one could flee.

Baron Barton was so terrified his entire body stiffened, his breath caught in his throat. Staring at his guard captain's corpse on the ground, he was completely frozen in shock.

Laurie moved with shocking speed, grabbing Baron Barton by the neck and slamming him hard against the wall. His voice was cold and merciless:

"You think being the lord of Gaowei City makes you someone special?"

"In front of us, you're nothing more than a lamb waiting to be slaughtered."

title: Chapter 52 — Gunpowder (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 52 — Gunpowder (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 13 · Chapter 52

"How could this be?! I was willing to... hand over the treasure map, why won't you let me go?!"

Baron Barton was being choked by Laurie, his entire face turning purple, unable to catch his breath.

"What a pity. You'd better just die, because someone traded your life for clues from the treasure map. Although we dark guild members aren't exactly people who keep our promises, we're more than happy to kill, hahaha...." Laurie's Saint-tier pressure was immensely powerful, making it nearly impossible for Baron Barton to resist. He was far more ruthless than Merlin.

"Who?! Who wants to harm me?!" Baron Barton panicked, for his character had never been great and he had many enemies, so he couldn't recall who among them it might be.

"It's your butler Steve, poor Barton. You were actually betrayed by your own man." Laurie found it increasingly amusing; this was far more entertaining than squaring off against that female adventurer.

"Steve?! ...He actually dared to betray me! Wh-...why?!" Baron Barton's face was filled with disbelief. Steve had always been so respectful and deferential to him. He never expected that at such a critical moment, Steve would ruthlessly sell him out!

"How should we know about your grudges? You only have yourself to blame. If you hadn't been radiating the fragrance of treasure, how could hungry wolves have been attracted?" Laurie had already lost interest in Barton and spoke with killing intent, "Have a smooth journey to hell."

"......Spare my life!..."

Before Baron Barton could finish speaking, Laurie spread his fingers into a blade and drove them fiercely into Barton's chest, blood spraying in all directions!

A look of unwillingness still lingered on Baron Barton's face. After shivering a few times, his body went limp and lost all vitality.

Laurie tossed Barton's body to the ground like a pile of mud and turned to look at Oswald.

"It's really effortless, no effort needed at all."

"Just two greedy pigs. There's nothing to be proud of in killing them." Oswald replied calmly, continuing, "Check whether there's a map to the vampire ruins on this fat pig. If I'm not mistaken, it should be on him."

Laurie nodded, turned over Barton's corpse, and reached into his clothing to search.

After several moments of groping, a pleased expression crossed Laurie's face as he pulled out a rolled-up parchment from inside Baron Barton's clothes, its surface stained with dark yellow marks that clearly showed its age.

"This must be it, right?"

"Let me see."

Oswald took the parchment and unfolded it, studying it carefully. A satisfied smile appeared on his face as he nodded and said,

"That's correct. This is exactly what we've been searching for."

"Of course they kept it on their own person..."

"If Steve hadn't deduced it so accurately, we might have had to go through a great deal of trouble."

The bloody incident upstairs had not yet been discovered by those downstairs.

The ball was still in progress and had not ended; the atmosphere was only growing livelier.

The clamorous noises masked the screams from above, and everyone was oblivious to the faint scent of blood in the air.

Merlin and Alice hadn't kept their eyes fixed on Baron Barton, since there was only one passage in the entire Kathy Castle, leading toward the main entrance.

If Barton wanted to flee, he would inevitably have to pass right in front of Merlin and Alice.

Jumping out the window was even less likely, as it would cause a commotion and they would surely detect it.

So Merlin remained confident. Once the ball ended, he would have Barton lead them to retrieve the vampire ruin map.

Merlin felt Barton was reasonably compliant. After being beaten, he had finally accepted reality. He hadn't made a move to escape, suggesting he had abandoned the idea.

Now all he needed to do was wait for the ball to end, retrieve the treasure map, and find clues about Dracula.

"Merlin, do you think Baron Barton might try to sneak away? What if there are hidden doors or something..."

Alice felt somewhat suspicious.

"How far could he run? He's the lord of Highwind City." Merlin thought Barton was under his watch now; he could escape a monk but not a temple.

"That's true. We'll find him no matter where he runs to, but could he change his mind along the way?" Alice raised another concern.

"Change his mind? As long as he has even a shred of will to survive, there's no room for negotiation." Merlin frowned, wondering what would happen if this miser dared to renege — he wouldn't hesitate to be ruthless.

"Does it have to be so absolute? He's the lord of Highwind City. If you push too hard, even as an adventurer, you'll be wanted. Do you still want to continue in this profession?" Alice was irritated by Merlin's reaction; he was essentially forcing obedience through fear.

Moreover, if they truly killed a regional lord like Barton, neither Merlin nor Alice would enjoy easy days afterward, for the Britannia Empire held the highest authority, and one's actions had to comply with basic rules.

Most awkwardly, Baron Barton seemed quite familiar with Austin, the person who hired them. If Barton were killed, it would be difficult to explain things when they returned.

"Fear what? I know a wealthy lady in the imperial capital, and she owes me a favor. I'm just killing a lord — she'll sort it out for me." Merlin thought of Queen Elizabeth. She owed him an astronomical sum of money, so it seemed unrealistic for her to oppose him just because he had killed a minor city's lord.

"Huh?!" Upon hearing "wealthy lady," Alice immediately lost her composure, her expression turning cold. "Are you living in a dream? Have you lost touch with reality? Which wealthy lady would take a fancy to a lazy slug like you? Don't come here spouting nonsense with a straight face..."

"Tsk!" Merlin rolled his eyes and was too lazy to say anymore.

In Alice's eyes, someone glib like Merlin could only deceive young girls and schmooze wealthy ladies who could absorb vitality just by sitting.

Would any serious, talented wealthy lady really be interested in someone like Merlin, who was nothing but an empty vessel wrapped in a wretched shell?

Alice wouldn't easily believe Merlin's nonsense. After all, he had deceived her countless times, completely destroying any credibility he might have had.

Merlin and Alice fell silent, no longer speaking gibberish, and instead watched the nobles' graceful dancing and that decadent, wine-soaked, glittering lifestyle.

"Alice, do you like this kind of life?" Merlin asked suddenly.

"Which kind?" Alice was puzzled.

"This right before us — the lights and wine, men and women intermingling, seemingly beautiful, but underneath full of hidden currents. That's the life of the nobility." Merlin evaluated the noble class briefly.

"I don't." Alice answered simply.

"Why? Don't you know many people would break their heads just to squeeze into this circle?" Merlin was slightly surprised by Alice's answer.

"I simply don't like it. I dislike a life full of scheming and intrigue every day. What's the use of being magnificent on the surface? In the end, it's all the same. I used to think life on the Great Snow Mountain was the worst and longed for the outside world. But after spending a few years out here, I realized the isolated Great Snow Mountain was actually the most carefree life. Though very dull, it was peaceful and fulfilling." Alice spoke thoughtfully.

Hearing this answer, Merlin fell silent for a moment. He thought Alice's mindset was much like his own — both wanting to avoid this complicated world and hide in a place untouched by strife. Could it be... Buddhist-style detachment?

"If you miss the Great Snow Mountain so much, why not go back?"

"Pfft!" Alice shot Merlin a look, her tone resentful. "Isn't it all because of you? You're the reason I'm drowning in debt. Do you want me to live out my life in shame? Even troubling my teacher would give her a headache!"

"..." Merlin's face darkened, thinking how could this be traced back to the root of all sins? Was this really the butterfly effect triggered by his opportunistic mentality back then!?

"Besides, I don't feel mature enough right now. My desire to return to the Great Snow Mountain isn't that strong yet... Besides..." Alice glanced at Merlin, two inexplicable red clouds rising to her cheeks. She turned her face away and muttered, "Never mind..."

"Hmm?" Merlin furrowed his brow, wondering why Alice seemed so hesitant. Was she hiding some secret?

Just as the two were chatting, the servants nearby started arguing, their voices drifting over intermittently, sounding like reprimands.

"What are you doing?"

"The black powder is in the wine barrels!"

"Do you have any idea how dangerous it is to bring that into a ball!?"

title: Chapter 53 — Javelin
content:
Chapter 53 — Javelin

Volume 13 · Chapter 53

“Team leader, this is completely not my fault, isn’t it? These buckets of wine weren’t ordered by you, were they?” The waiter replied with a face full of grievance.

“Water and supplies were already prepared sufficiently before the dance even started—who would order again? And what’s inside? Is it gunpowder!” The team leader waiter harshly scolded his subordinate.

“...But just now those two people said it was you who ordered it.”

The waiter looked a bit embarrassed.

Listening to the intermittent discussion over there, Merlin couldn’t help but furrow his brow, feeling in his heart that something was amiss.

However, based on the information just obtained, it seems someone sent the wrong items.

Merlin couldn’t help but recall the night he assassinated Alice. After that incident, everything had been peaceful.

Did these people really calm down and no longer attract attention to the vampire treasure maps?

Merlin thought not necessarily. Before the storm comes, it is always so peaceful. They won’t let go of the treasure maps.

Time slowly passed. Under the host’s announcement, this dance party finally ended, and people applauded to express their gratitude to the organizers.

Then people began to disperse. The nobles left in an orderly manner; those who felt a connection, whether man and woman or same-sex, might choose to stay at Kassi 5 Castle and spend a wonderful night.

Merlin got up from the sofa and said to the dazed Alice beside him,

“Come on, let’s go check on Baron Barton. The dance is over....”

Night fell. The pale moonlight of the constellations flickered in and out under the cover of clouds.

The countless stars foretold peace; no one knew that danger was approaching.

On a certain mountaintop outside Gaowei City—

This was a place with a wide view, allowing one to take in the entirety of Gaowei City.

Osweid and Lori had already finished packing their luggage and came here, preparing to leave along the path.

Now, the vampire relic treasure map—its biggest task had already been completed.

The remaining plan was to destroy Gaowei City and announce the might of the Dark Guild, Azure Blue Eternal Flame.

It would be best to also bury those two hateful adventurers here, so as to understand the grievances from not long ago.

So far, Osweid’s plan had been proceeding steadily and smoothly, and completing all plans seemed within expectation.

Obstacles? It seems they simply don’t exist. Everything is water under the bridge, Osweid estimates that even now, no one knows that Gaowei City faces a threat of death.

The two looked at Gaowei City, where the lights were gradually dimming, and had already decided to deliver the final blow to this town.

“Didn’t expect the task to be completed so easily. I bet when we go back, the boss will reward us well~” Lori beamed with pride.

“Easy? You’d better look at who came up with the plan. We planned it, and we’ve never had a failed outcome.” Osweid smiled.

“That’s true. Anyway, now that the treasure map is in hand, you and I certainly don’t have to worry about the boss flying into a rage.” Lori stood up, looking at Osweid and asking, “How about it? Can you still see clearly the situation at Kassi Castle?”

“Of course I can see clearly. The dance has ended, and those nobles are heading toward the main gate. I can even see a kiss mark on a certain man’s neck.” Osweid said leisurely. Thanks to the archer’s keen eyesight, he could see a lot.

“No wonder the captain favors this archer so much. Even from nearly a hundred miles away, he can see so clearly. I can only see the city walls.” Lori had a drop of cold sweat on his forehead. Among all the archers he had seen, Osweid’s strength was undoubtedly the strongest. “So can we move now? For killing those two adventurers, I am really looking forward to it.”

“Alright, the opportunity is good now. The dance just ended, and it is precisely the time to set off fireworks for excitement!” Osweid also stood up, and a hint of slaughter intent flashed in his eyes.

“They say the power of the charged spear can destroy a city. I am already eager to see such a sight.” Lori felt that the black powder had already been injected. When the charged spear explodes the black powder, that female adventurer’s skin may be hard, but it will be useless; then all of Gaowei City will also become a burial offering in the explosion.

Osweid clapped his hands together, then slowly separated them. A golden light appeared.

He gripped the center of the light with his hand, and instantly a black spear appeared.

The appearance of this spear looked very simple, with pits and bumps on the surface, and faint red patterns carved like blood vessels.

Osweid took his stance, raised the spear, and locked his gaze on Gaowei City. To be precise, he locked onto the powder barrels inside Kassi Castle!

“Lori, hide far away.”

“Why?” Lori didn’t understand why Osweid was being so serious. Isn’t it just throwing it out?

“This thing is too strong. I find it hard to control the power. Even the shockwave produced when thrown will injure you, so it’s better to hide far away.” Osweid answered.

“Is it that dramatic?” Lori asked doubtfully.

“This thing can easily destroy a city. You don’t know? Even the boss might not come out unscathed when facing this; he might even face a threat of death.” Osweid said seriously.

“Er, well...” Lori nodded and hid very far away, but his gaze did not leave Osweid, preparing to see just how powerful this spear’s destructive power was.

Actually, Lori had only heard that Osweid had a secret weapon on him. This spear was forged by an unknown method.

This mysterious origin thing seems like Osweid himself doesn’t know much about it. He only knows that after infusing battle qi, it will produce extraordinary destructive power.

Even the boss of Azure Blue Eternal Flame would feel wary of this thing. If it were revealed, the power would probably be destructive!

Osweid held the spear, and the golden battle qi on his body began to surge.

Winds rose, blowing Osweid’s black robe to flutter, and the aura of the whole person changed!

Red battle qi frantically gathered toward the spear, almost to the point of sucking Osweid’s battle qi dry. This shows how harsh the usage conditions are.

The charged spear, after receiving the nourishment of battle qi and being stimulated, suddenly reacted. The entire gun body began to tremble non-stop, the faint red patterns like coming to life, starting to wriggle and spin, and emitting bursts of red light!

CE Xiao Ji

If Alice were present, she would probably feel a bit familiar with this spear, having a sense of déjà vu similar to the alchemy weapons made by Da Vinci.

Osweid roared angrily and viciously threw the charged spear. Instantly, the ground under his feet cracked, and a whirlwind swept around.

A powerful shockwave spread out and heavily impacted everything around. Trees were overturned and hard turned into “bow” shapes.

As for that spear? It had long turned into a stream of light, rushing into the clouds and disappearing into the night, shooting straight toward Gaowei City.

Lori furrowed his brow, covering his face. The shockwave came like a knife; he had to infuse battle qi to block it. Just the destructive power released was so astonishing!

No wonder Osweid told me to hide far away. The launching impact would injure me.

If not for Osweid’s special training, probably he wouldn’t be able to use this strange weapon!

No wonder it’s something the boss feels wary of. Indeed, one cannot make judgments based on common sense!

Cold sweat appeared on Lori’s forehead, feeling that if he were attacked, the death rate would be 100%! No power to parry!

Osweid rubbed his shoulders, his expression a bit fatigued, and his battle qi was nearly depleted. “Let’s go.”

“Huh! ? We’re leaving already! ? Don’t we need to check the situation?” Lori asked in surprise.

No.” Osweid looked at Lori, revealing a confident smile, turning his back toward the about-to-be-destroyed Gaowei City.

“At the moment I threw the spear, everyone in this city was already dead.”

“Then dead people, what is there to see? People”
