title: Chapter 54 — Collusion
content:
Chapter 54 — Collusion

Volume 13 · Chapter 54

In the period before that extremely destructive spear was thrown.
Merlin and Alice went straight upstairs to look for Baron Barton's whereabouts.
Now that the ball is over, it's time to fulfill the promise...
However, when the two arrived upstairs, they found something odd.
Many people were blocking the corridor, watching as if they had discovered something frightening.
People's faces were filled with panic, they chattered among themselves, pointing and commenting on the sudden situation.
Really? Is it true? The baron actually died?
Who did this? This is the Rothschild family's venue; safety should be guaranteed.
Exactly, who has the guts to do this without fearing a manhunt?
Merlin and Alice saw the scene before them, and simultaneously felt doubts rising in their hearts; the fragmented information still couldn't accurately judge the situation.
The two squeezed forward a bit and instantly saw a horrifying scene, pulling everyone back from joy to the naked cruel reality.
Just a moment ago, downstairs was still hosting a pleasant misunderstanding, but now a corpse suddenly appeared here! This will surely be hard to accept.
On the ground lay two corpses: one was the previous guard captain, his head pierced by an arrow; the other was Baron Barton, his chest brutally torn open, leaving a bloody hole.
From the still relatively orderly scene at the site, one can imagine the opponent being ruthless and decisive, killing without mercy.
Seeing that the people were already dead, Merlin and Alice felt the task's clues directly cut off, and facing this situation they couldn't help but feel their heads go a bit fuzzy.
"Who did this?" Alice asked instinctively.
"I'm not sure; the action was too fast— the ball just ended not long ago." Merlin frowned.
"Could it be the same group?" Alice looked at Merlin, having a premonition that these things should be connected, definitely not a coincidence.
"You mean..."
Merlin stroked his chin, wondering if Alice already had an answer.
"It's those two who came to assassinate us that night; could they have been constantly thinking about the blood clan relic's treasure map, so they chose to strike today?" Alice said seriously.
Merlin pondered for a moment, thinking it wasn't impossible: "Maybe it really was that group."
"Tsk!" Alice felt a bit annoyed, looking at Baron Barton's corpse dying miserably, feeling regret. "So... are we slower than the enemy by a step? Who are they? Why are they so obsessed with the blood clan relic? They wouldn't even spare lives....
"Alice, don't think too much; treasure like this naturally has endless allure, it drives people mad, countless will rush forward, even if they do extreme things, I think it's normal." Merlin replied lightly.
......Alice lowered her head, not speaking; obviously she was in a bad mood, now that all clues are cut off, she felt she had been busy for nothing lately.
However, Baron Barton said the blood clan relic's treasure map was at home; now he's suddenly killed, which seems illogical— if they really wanted the map, wouldn't it be better to sneak into his manor and steal it? Why come to the ball to kill him?" S I 6
Merlin frowned, uttering a string of his doubts, feeling that the situation before him was somewhat abnormal.
Baron Barton personally said the treasure map wasn't on him, but even so, he still suffered misfortune— this is...
"Flies don't bite seamless eggs; why would villains specially come to the ball to plot against Baron Barton?"
"It couldn't be that this guy deceived me from the start; that treasure map isn't at home but on his person!"
"If things are really like that, then everything would make sense— why would the enemy specially come to the ball to take out Baron Barton?"
"Perhaps someone else leaked the fact that the baron hid the treasure map on him, which is why the enemy's information is so accurate."
Merlin recalled: the original butler Steve, that kind and amiable appearance flashed in his mind, always feeling something wasn't quite right.
"Alice, we... seem to have been deceived"
"What do you mean?" Alice asked softly.
"The butler we first met might be colluding with the group that tried to assassinate us." Merlin whispered to Alice, sharing his thought.
"You can't just say that; do you have evidence?" Alice felt doubtful inside and didn't readily believe Merlin.
"Do we even need evidence? We have no grudge against that butler; why would he scheme against us in secret? This just doesn't make sense." Merlin said seriously.
Alice calmed down, thinking it wasn't impossible; that letter of introduction could easily get the blood clan relic's treasure map, after all it was guaranteed by Count Austin.
o了ζE42小治
Now this butler Steve has turned hostile and refuses to acknowledge; Merlin and Alice can't quickly prove their identities, so obtaining the treasure map will become much harder.
Who exactly benefits from all this? Surely besides the two who came to assassinate us that night, there is no second answer.
"Moreover, Baron Barton also said..." Merlin stared expressionlessly at the corpse on the ground and said quietly, "The blood clan relic's treasure map was just on him; it wasn't in the manor at all, and that's why it brought about his deadly disaster."
"Why would those villains know the treasure map was on Baron's body rather than hidden elsewhere?" Alice raised her question.
"This is also something I can't figure out, but I suspect that butler definitely has a problem." Merlin looked at Alice, lowering his voice, "You also feel something's off, right? Knowing the baron's movements and secrets so well, this couldn't happen without collusion from someone inside the manor; the prime suspect is the butler who's been causing us trouble, Steve."
Alice suddenly realized: the strongest force in the baron's manor is the high-ranking guard captain, who can have two Saint-tier powerhouses; the assassins that night were clearly not from the manor, yet they knew Baron Barton's secrets well, so the idea of the manor colluding with mysterious forces is quite credible.
Who would have thought that a simple task of borrowing to look at the treasure map would uncover so many complex relations and some mysterious forces, making Alice feel quite troubled.
Alice originally wanted to discuss with Merlin whether to confront the baron's butler Steve, but upon lowering her head she saw him push to the front and start touching Baron Barton's corpse, as if searching for something.
This rude behavior drew dissatisfaction from some onlookers, and whispers came and went, feeling that these two foreigners were desecrating a soul.
Alice felt the pressure of public opinion, couldn't help but step forward to stop Merlin in a low voice, "Hey! What are you doing? Roughly handling the corpse is a desecration; this should be left to the church and the city guards of Highwall."
"I'm looking for the treasure map; maybe Baron Barton hid it deep enough that those two scoundrels didn't find it— isn't this an opportunity for us?" Merlin replied seriously.
"......" Alice was at a loss for words, listening to the surrounding murmurs, she could only hold back; the treasure map is the next crucial clue, we can't give up any chance.
However, as Merlin just tore open Barton's blood-stained chest, he suddenly felt something and jerked his head up toward the north.
At the same moment, Alice and Merlin reacted the same— both lifted their heads to look through the glass at the calm northern sky, though her expression was more tense and shocked.
Merlin frowned, lowered Barton's coat, feeling the outside sky was off— though it was midnight, it was gradually becoming bright.
"What's coming over?"
"And it's moving fast."
"This destructive pressure...."
"Is it intending to destroy the whole Highwall city?"

title: Chapter 55 — Unstoppable
content:
Chapter 55 — Unstoppable

Volume 13 · Chapter 55

“What the hell? Why is there this level of pressure?” Alice muttered nervously, feeling the rapidly approaching immense pressure, a layer of cold sweat broke out on her forehead.
I don't know... Merlin furrowed his brows, a sense of unease in his heart, “It feels like an extremely strong magic is approaching...”
The surrounding nobles were puzzled by Merlin and Alice's reactions; these ordinary people had no idea danger was approaching, remaining oblivious.
It seems that unless they could personally see the danger approaching, ordinary people's vigilance is completely unaware that they are already on the brink of death.
The two raised their heads, looking through the back window at the outside scenery, feeling that this tranquil night was becoming restless and growing brighter.
Alice carefully examined this immense pressure, inwardly thinking things were bad, feeling that if the current situation wasn't handled well, the entire Highwei City could become ruins, with Keshic Castle being the primary danger zone!
So Alice didn't think long, first placing the defense of Highwei City as top priority, intending to go out and organize the sudden crisis!
Alice lifted her skirt, smashed the window glass in front of her, and leapt outside without looking back?
“Hey! Alice!” Merlin had wanted to call for Alice to calm down a bit, first clarify the situation, but he didn't expect this woman to be so impulsive, rushing out without a thought.
This headache-inducing action made Merlin wonder, are all Heroes like Alice? For the sake of protection, do they often not consider their own safety?
Merlin helplessly shook his head, intending to follow, but a sudden change occurred, causing him to momentarily lose his senses—
A sudden booming explosion rang out! The entire Keshic Castle trembled violently, as if a major explosion had occurred downstairs at this critical moment!?
Merlin turned his head toward the stairway entrance, saying, - - a tongue of fire surged up from below, the vicious flames nearly swallowing the surrounding nobles, just a hair's breadth away!
It seems the power of three barrels of gunpowder wasn't enough to level Keshic Castle; otherwise, at the moment of explosion, many would have died unaware.
The flames finally receded, leaving thick black residue flowing on the ground and ceiling; the entire staircase was blown apart, revealing that downstairs had become a sea of fire, with piercing screams clearly audible.
This group of superficially radiant nobles screamed and fainted from fright; the men barely retained consciousness, but looking at their ashen faces and trembling legs, they too were scared senseless.
What now?
Why are these situations happening one after another!?
Again dead people, and again an inexplicable explosion!
Wait! What is this smell? A sour, stinky odor like that emitted from a dead fish.....
Merlin rubbed his nose, took a sharp sniff, pondered for three seconds, and his expression turned to shock—
...the smell of magic hindrance particles?
Something made by grinding special crystals can suppress magic power.
Damn! Were all of these planned ahead!?
Alice jumped from Keshic Castle's window to the outside; as soon as she landed, she heard a deafening explosion!
The ground trembled slightly, and the walls of Keshic Castle swayed on the verge of collapse in the shockwave.
Alice stared back in shock, seeing Keshic Castle engulfed in flames, thick black smoke billowing skyward, the firelight filling a—layer!
She could see some silhouettes outside; many were being consumed by the flames, struggling incessantly, finally motionless, and those painful screams made people feel uneasy.
Alice was somewhat stretched thin; trying to rescue those in the flames was obviously too late, and now that immense pressure was approaching—any delay would mean the destruction of Highwei City.
Moreover, this explosion came out of nowhere; few could survive on the - - layer of Keshic Castle, and compared to the safety of the entire city, Alice unhesitatingly chose the majority.
Alice could only hope in her heart that Merlin would help her, to rescue the survivors, while she herself would have to stop the more dangerous presence.
However, just moments ago, Alice had already inhaled the magic hindrance particles diffusing in the air, but due to her extreme tension she noticed nothing.
Alice raised her head, looking toward the northern sky, wanting to see what entity could emit such immense pressure—
In the thick black night, several heavy bird clouds obscured the moonlight in the horizon.
Only then could one see in the horizon a very obvious dark red growing brighter, as if tearing a—gap in the gloomy sky!?
Alice gazed at the eerie sight before her, her heart somewhat astonished—what is this?
The blood-red in the horizon suddenly contracted, a jet-black spear, flashing with red patterns, came flying!
Its speed was so fast it made one gasp, like a dark-red comet plummeting from the sky, threatening to destroy everything in an instant—utterly terrifying!
Behind the charged spear trailed a long light tail X, like burning scorching red flames.
If it weren't for the overwhelming pressure, it would easily be mistaken for a meteor streaking across the night sky.
Alice's expression turned grave, instantly feeling like facing a formidable foe; every cell in her body sounded alarms, indicating this thing is not ordinary, and if not taken seriously she could very well be overturned.
This seemingly ordinary spear actually contains immense power; even Alice lacks full confidence she can block it.
Before the spear even hit the ground, Alice felt a tremendous wind pressure, and the entire Keshic Castle area began to tremble slightly.
A tremendous suppressive force made Alice's breathing constricted, her heart pounding rapidly.
Alice raised her hand; her magic and battle aura surged forth, Magic Warrior Glory and skill unleashed, icy air spreading—
A series of massive golden ice shields

title: Chapter 56 — Counter-Assassination
content:
Chapter 56 — Counter-Assassination

Volume 13 · Chapter 56

Alice stepped back in terror, never expecting that her fused ice crystals would appear so fragile at this moment—she had somehow managed to pierce through three layers of great ice shields in succession! ?

With the incredibly sharp spear closing in on Alice, the next moment would inevitably bring a violent explosion and a gruesome scene of flying flesh and blood.

At this critical moment, Merlin burst out of Cathy's castle, moving so fast that only a black afterimage could be seen.

Merlin had indeed just rescued some survivors from the explosion and led them to safety.

Only then did he realize Alice was in danger, so he quickly rushed out of the castle to stop that aggressively charging spear.

Just as quickly as it came—it happened in the blink of an eye—

"Alice! Move!"

Merlin arrived beside Alice, wrapped his arm around her waist, and pulled the dazed girl behind him.

Alice was startled by Merlin's sudden appearance. Her frail body was dragged backward, and after regaining her balance, she let out a startled cry.

"Merlin!"

In this emergency, Merlin the sister-con didn't bother responding to Alice. He frowned and looked up, seeing the ferocious spear already at point-blank range, merely a finger's distance from his forehead!

At that moment, Merlin could already feel that bone-chilling coldness. The crimson-red spiral seemed to possess the power to tear through everything!

Merlin's pupils contracted as he firmly grabbed the shaft of the spear with both hands, preventing it from continuing its thrust forward.

The charged spear, meeting resistance, seemed activated by some unknown force and grew even more ferocious, wanting to obliterate all obstacles before it!

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue, gritted his teeth, and increased his strength. Desperate to stop the moving spear, he wished he could simply snap it in half!

The crimson-red spiral exploded with tremendous force, driving Merlin back a step. The ground cracked loudly with massive fissures spreading like spiderwebs.

If this had hit an ordinary person—even a warrior at the peak of Saint-tier—they would have been torn to shreds on the spot. To think you could catch it with your bare hands? It was like a joke!

With surrounding stones splashing in all directions, Merlin's right sleeve was torn apart by the distorting power, revealing a solid forearm with clearly visible veins bulging out!

Looking at Merlin's annoyed expression, this spear's power was extraordinary. That subtle aggressiveness alone was enough to make him take it somewhat seriously.

Alice, watching from behind, struggled to even open her eyes against the chaotic shockwave. But inwardly she marveled—her enemies actually had something like this! ? Had they been holding back that night!? If they had deployed such a secret weapon back then, wouldn't she have been in grave danger! ?

The raging storm ultimately couldn't budge Merlin's physical strength and dispersed instantly, leaving devastation everywhere.

This long-planned attack was ultimately defused by Merlin, causing no catastrophic casualties.

The surrounding earth was shattered into pieces, forming an obvious large pit, and even nearby buildings were shaken into collapse.

Merlin had to step back a full pace to cushion the impact before stopping the spear—otherwise the consequences would have been unimaginable.

Merlin's once-neat evening礼服 was now torn and ragged, making him look as wretched as a beggar.

However, this wasn't much of a threat to Merlin—he was well within his ability to handle it.

The whole process unfolded in the flick of an eye, a rollercoaster ride from hell to heaven that left onlookers secretly stunned.

"Hmph!" Merlin tightly gripped the spear now calmed in his hand, rubbed his nose, and couldn't help but mutter, "What a troublesome thing..."

"……" Alice murmured to herself, her mind still not having recovered from the shock.

Merlin shifted his stance, raised the spear in his hand, looked upward toward the north, and took a deep breath—

"Haa!"

With a fierce shout, Merlin, without a second thought, directly threw the spear in his hand right back.

A "whoosh" of air-breaking sound echoed, and the tremendous throwing force created gale after gale, forcefully sending Alice tumbling backward.

The spear flew out again like a meteor shooting across the sky, tearing through the heavens in an instant before disappearing into the night.

Merlin looked at the night sky and finally breathed a sigh of relief, feeling that the crisis had reached a temporary lull. There was nothing else to worry about now, right?

"Hey! Why did you throw that spear away! ? That thing could've been a clue to help us figure out our opponent's identity!" Alice said somewhat anxiously, feeling that Merlin had acted too rashly.

"So what did you want me to do? They've caused us so much trouble—we can't just let them walk away cleanly, can we? Better to capture one if we can!" Merlin replied helplessly.

"……" Alice was speechless and could only sigh, "Sigh… We're being played like fools. What should we do?"

"Don't worry. If I'm not mistaken, as archers, what they need most is a broad field of view. They were probably on that hill outside Gao Wei City just now." Merlin paused, his expression calm. "Planning to manipulate us and still expect to escape unscathed? That's impossible."

"They'll have to pay for what they've done…"

"The moment I threw that spear, everyone in this city was already dead."

"Then what's there to see if they're dead?"

Osvald left without looking back, fully confident in his secret weapon.

Based on his speculation, that series of setups—no matter how insanely strong Alice was—wouldn't be able to withstand it. She would likely be instantly killed by his spear in the first strike.

Osvald picked up his luggage from the ground, preparing to leave. Although using the spear had drained most of his斗气, it didn't hinder his journey.

"You're really confident about it. You hardly ever use your secret weapons—isn't it worth staying to watch the destruction of Gao Wei City? It'd be a rare spectacle." Lawrence shrugged, feeling it would be a shame not to see it.

"If you want to watch, watch by yourself. I'm not interested." Osvald responded coldly and walked straight toward the path.

Lawrence glanced at Osvald and helplessly retorted, "What a boring guy…"

However, after just a few steps, Osvald sensed a whooshing wind sound from behind. It was strange.

"Hmm?" Osvald turned his head in confusion—and instantly that very same spear of his drove into his chest. "Kuh!"

"Osvald!" Lawrence's eyes widened in shock. He let out a cry and was dumbfounded by the sudden situation.

The spear that had been thrown only moments ago had somehow shot back in the opposite direction, striking Osvald directly in the heart.

What exactly had happened in that brief time!? Even between the two of them, their imaginations couldn't possibly piece it together in such a short time!

Osvald coughed up a mouthful of fresh blood on the spot, his expression filled with utter disbelief. His body was launched backward by the spear's force, his scream echoing through the air—

"Uaaaaaaaaaah! ! !"

title: Chapter 57 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 57 — Chapter Title: Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 13 · Chapter 57

Osmeros's body was pierced through by a javelin, and he flew backward like a cannonball.

He crashed into several thick trees, snapping them in two, and the ground was gouged out into long, shocking trenches.

The sand and dust rose up in a cloud, as if a tornado had just torn through.

Laurie hurried after him, stumbling and crashing along the way. This sudden, powerful strike made him feel uneasy.

When the dust settled, Laurie reached a large tree and found Osmeros nailed to it by his own javelin—completely motionless, his body limp and drained of all vitality.

Osmeros's eyes were glazed over, unseeing. Thin strands of blood trickled down the shaft as the javelin had already pierced straight through his heart—a fatal blow.

"Osmeros..."

Laurie's eyes widened in shock, his face twisted in horror. He was so overwhelmed that he couldn't even process what had just happened.

He nervously swallowed hard, called out his companion's name, and then had nothing more to say.

He had expected to witness the spectacular sight of Huowei City engulfed in flames—a perfect ending.

But the result was completely unexpected—Osmeros had been killed by his own secret weapon!

What exactly had happened in between was baffling and hard to figure out.

Laurie couldn't help but think about the black powder laced with magical particles he had arranged. That female adventurer must have had the ability to deflect such a powerful javelin back.

To deflect a javelin of such immense power, a mage would probably be unable to do it—only a strong warrior using their internal energy could manage it!

Yet this unimaginable thing had just occurred right before his eyes. Besides Huowei City, there didn't seem to be any other explanation.

Who would have thought this small city harbored such hidden power?

It seemed Osmeros had simply miscalculated by one move. He hadn't anticipated a stronger existence here, which was why he ended up falling flat on his face.

What a shame—Osmeros was an important official in the guild. To think he would meet such an end...

Laurie felt a pang of sorrow and sympathy, sighed deeply, and only wished Osmeros had turned back in time. Otherwise, he could have dodged that javelin.

Now that he knew there was a powerful presence in Huowei City, Laurie couldn't help but feel the urge to go back for revenge. If even Osmeros's secret weapon was useless, then he himself would probably just be courting death.

Laurie figured the powerful figure in Huowei City was someone not to be trifled with. Now that he had the map in hand, he should leave as quickly as possible—he might even be pursued by that powerful individual.

So Laurie reached out, gently closed Osmeros's lifeless eyes, and took the bloodline relic map from his chest.

"My friend, rest in peace..."

Not much time had passed.

Merlin and Alice did indeed leave Huowei City in a hurry, heading straight for the mountaintop.

Using the damaged mountaintop as a reference, they quickly found the exact location of the recent attack.

Merlin and Alice looked at the corpse nailed to the tree—Osmeros, dead. They fell silent.

That night, two people had been attacked, but only one had died here. That meant the other enemy had already fled.

And more importantly, the bloodline relic map was still missing. The situation was still far from optimistic, and the two of them were still confused, unable to find a clear direction.

"So... this is the guy who's been secretly working against us, right?" Alice said, looking at Osmeros's cold corpse.

"This late at night, showing up here—I'd say it's them, nine out of ten." Merlin replied with near-certainty.

The two of them stared at Osmeros's face, both feeling a bit uncomfortable inside. They recalled what had happened when they first arrived in Huowei City.

Isn't this the guy we gave a ride to the other day?

Who would have thought the enemy would be so close—just right beside them!

They had even sat in the car together, chatting amiably. It turns out the person who gave them a ride was their own enemy!

Now that this man was clearly the enemy, the identity of their companion was obvious too—certainly nothing good.

The two of them were in a complicated emotional state, feeling betrayed, and also regretting getting involved with a stranger's affairs.

"Ugh! So it was them—both of them going after us? This is insane..." Merlin's expression soured, and he was annoyed that he had let them hitchhike, making their mission so difficult. If he had just ignored those two, the map would probably have been secured long ago!

"I told you we shouldn't have picked them up. You only agreed to give them a ride for the money." Alice snapped.

"That's not right. At the beginning, I was against it. You were the first one who suggested giving them a ride." Merlin shot back, not wanting to take the blame.

"...Alice was left speechless, then forcefully retorted, 'You didn't listen to me either. In the end, it was you who welcomed them aboard for 1000 gold!'"

The two glared at each other, each refusing to take responsibility, and they started arguing.

Merlin figured his share of the blame was greater, so he quickly brushed it off and said, "Now isn't the time to shift blame. We should figure out who these people really are first."

"Hmph!" Alice rolled her eyes, pouting, "It's not like you didn't throw the first stone either."

Merlin sighed helplessly, shaking his head. He thought you just couldn't reason with a woman, so he decided to examine the body first.

So Merlin carefully lowered the body from the tree and examined it closely. Then he remembered a seemingly insignificant detail.

"Alice, I think Johnson mentioned that they looked like they were from the Dark Guild. Do you remember?"

"Did he say that? ...I can't recall..."

Alice couldn't remember. Maybe Johnson had already noticed something was off, but just couldn't confirm it.

"Yes, he did say that. Though even Johnson himself only said it 'seemed like' them, without a definitive answer." Merlin replied confidently.

"Then why don't we go ask Johnson's father to help identify them? That would clear up the enemy's identity." Alice suddenly became excited, as if she had grasped an important clue.

"That's true. Let's first check if there's anything else."

Merlin began searching the body for any useful information.

But just as Merlin lifted the collar of the victim's clothing, he suddenly noticed a strange tattoo.

It was a blue tattoo—a bundle of burning blue flames in the shape of a skull.

Merlin didn't know what this was, so he turned to ask Alice.

"This... Alice, come take a look."

"What is it?" Alice approached, curious about Merlin's discovery.

"Does this tattoo mean anything?" Merlin pointed at the tattoo on Osmeros's body.

"Let me see..." Alice looked closely, then her eyes widened as she covered her mouth in shock.

"Celestial Cannon!"

title: Chapter 58 — Interception
content:
Chapter 58 — Interception

Volume 13 · Chapter 58

"Cerulean幽焰?" Merlin was puzzled, not quite understanding what it meant.

"Didn't I tell you?" Alice replied helplessly. "Among the four most powerful dark guilds, Cerulean幽焰 is one of them."

"Oh~ I see..." Merlin nodded, stroking his chin as he pondered. "Does that mean... we've crossed paths with a dark guild?"

"I suppose so?" Alice looked down at Osborne's corpse and spoke softly. "So the dark guilds are also searching for the vampire treasure map. No wonder they were so hostile toward us, trying to kill us."

Merlin stood up, hands on his hips, and asked casually, "We need the vampire treasure map to find Dracula. What do the dark guilds want it for?"

"I don't know, but it's certainly not something good. Dark guilds usually act to satisfy their own selfish desires," Alice replied thoughtfully.

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue, feeling restless inside. "It looks like things won't be peaceful from here on out. Conflict with the dark guilds is inevitable."

"What should we do next?" Alice asked patiently.

"We'll take it one step at a time. Right now, the enemy is hidden while we're exposed, which puts us at a disadvantage," Merlin paused, then continued. "But since we now know their identity, we can be more careful. We were tricked repeatedly this time because we underestimated the situation."

"But we don't have any leads at all! Count Austin had such high expectations of us, and now we haven't even found a clue about the vampires. How are we supposed to investigate Dracula?" Alice voiced her greatest worry. With the only clue about the treasure map now in the dark guild's hands, what to do next was utterly confusing.

"Don't we have some clue at least?" Merlin looked at Alice and said meaningfully, "Don't forget the steward of the baron's manor, Mr. Steve..."

"What are you suggesting?" Alice seemed to guess what Merlin was planning.

"Now that the treasure map is lost, the steward is the most suspicious. He'll likely try to flee overnight. There are two roads out of Gowan City. If we split up and ambush along both, we might get an unexpected bounty," Merlin said with a knowing smile, planning to pry information out of the steward Steve.

"Then what are we waiting for? Let's split into two groups right now." Alice said eagerly.

Merlin nodded, then glanced back at the spear on the ground. It felt extraordinary—he should have someone appraise it.

At this moment, the spear had turned completely black, appearing extremely ordinary, but the power it had just unleashed was still vividly present.

So Merlin picked up the spear and took it with him, intending to investigate its origins...

◇

Late at night in Gowan City.

Because of the massive explosion at Kathy Castle, no one in the city slept that night.

Many residents carried torches toward Kathy Castle to see what was happening.

Even the Johnson father and son hadn't slept—they came here to see what had occurred.

The wounded from the explosion were carried away and taken to priests for healing.

All the guards of Gowan City were mobilized, surrounding Kathy Castle and handling the aftermath.

As for the death of Baron Barton, the news had not yet been released, which would have sparked even more unrest.

The incident had ignited heated discussion among the townspeople. Some blamed the Rothschild family, while others said they had been attacked by bandits.

Still others claimed it was caused by a meteorite fall, citing that they had seen a crimson-red meteor streak across the sky at midnight—it was very eerie.

Almost no one knew that just moments ago, they had experienced a transition from death to life. If not for Merlin, they would have died in their sleep without even realizing it.

On a secluded little road with few people, Baron Barton's steward, Mr. Steve, had indeed, as expected, fled with his belongings.

Steve wanted to leave through the south gate of Gowan City. The explosion incident in the city only made his escape easier.

His expression was slightly tense, his behavior sneaky, and he kept glancing over his shoulder, worried someone might be tailing him.

When Steve heard about the explosion at Kathy Castle, he immediately knew the plan had succeeded—Baron Barton was definitely dead.

It seemed that when it came to killing, the dark guilds were indeed more professional. Laurie and Osborne had not failed his expectations, fulfilling his long-held desire for vengeance.

Steve's heart was filled with mixed emotions—excitement and sorrow intertwined. He didn't know whether he should laugh or cry.

He was excited that the detestable Baron Barton was finally dead, that he had avenged his former comrades, and that his years of grief had been resolved!

But he was sad because his former comrades could not be brought back to life—they would never witness Baron Barton's demise.

Although the successful revenge filled Steve with immense joy, it was soon followed by an unbearable emptiness.

The vendetta was settled, but what good did it do? His comrades were still long dead...

Years ago, when Baron Barton served as an official in Edinburgh, he was seduced by rumors of a treasure hidden deep in the mountains.

When he ventured into the mountains, the guards he chose were Steve's squad. However, aside from Steve, all other members were callously betrayed and killed by Baron Barton.

That's right—the two survivors who had obtained the vampire treasure map and emerged from the mountains were Baron Barton and this very steward, Mr. Steve.

Most of the fallen guards were very young, inexperienced, and had been personally trained by Steve. Their bond was extraordinarily deep.

If anything, it was a bond akin to that between a father and his children, or a teacher and his students—a relationship极为 precious within the military.

But over a dozen vibrant lives were lost in the mountains solely because of Baron Barton's cowardice, his selfish decisions.

Afterward, Baron Barton covered up his abuse of power to hunt for treasure by branding those fallen soldiers as deserters, denying them even proper recognition!

This made Steve deeply resentful, birthing an intense hatred for Baron Barton. But fearing the baron's vast influence, he had to endure for several years, biding his time.

Now that his great revenge was accomplished, Steve had nothing significant left to tie him down. Moreover, his secret actions might soon be discovered, so it was safer to flee here and return to his hometown as soon as possible.

After all, he still had his wife and children at home. Steve hadn't returned in several years, writing letters only to say he was still serving in Edinburgh and asking his family not to worry.

Steve raised his head and saw the open south gate of Gowan City, as if seeing freedom before him—but—

"Where are you going?"

"Uh!"

The sudden voice made Steve's heart leap into his throat. He whirled around, only to have his neck grabbed roughly and pinned against the wall, unable to move.

Merlin gripped Steve's throat, shoving him hard against the wall, a smug grin spreading across his face—

"So you've been plotting against us behind our backs..."

"You really thought you could escape so easily?"

title: Chapter 59 — Steve
content:
Chapter 59 — Steve

Volume 13 · Chapter 59

Merlin and Alice divided their responsibilities clearly, each lying in wait at the southern and northern gates of Highwall City to prevent Steve from fleeing overnight.

If Steve were to escape through the northern gate, where Alice was hiding, then relying on his pitiful tears to win sympathy, it seemed he might actually have a chance.

Unfortunately, Steve's luck wasn't good—he rushed straight for the southern gate, only to crash into Merlin, making his chances of escape nearly zero.

Merlin grabbed Steve, pushing him against the wall with a mocking smile on his face, as if telling him he'd long anticipated Steve's actions.

Steve tried to struggle, but it was completely futile—his neck felt like it was being clamped in iron tongs, unable to move at all.

He was secretly amazed. After all, he was at least a mid-tier warrior, and more importantly, a trained soldier.

Yet now he couldn't even escape a black-iron adventurer—this was hard to swallow.

Steve was cornered and showed a resigned expression, giving up his struggles because he realized the other party was concealing his strength. Even a black-iron adventurer was likely above him in power.

Moreover, Merlin had his hand around Steve's neck—this was a vital spot, and all resistance was futile. Better to conserve his strength.

"Didn't expect this..." Steve lifted his head and gave a bitter smile. "In the end, I'm the one being caught. That's fine—I know I'm not as skilled as you. Being defeated by you is a reasonable outcome. Just do it."

"Tch!"

Merlin's brows knit tightly, and he clicked his tongue in displeasure. He thought, I haven't even asked him anything yet, and he's already resigned to death?

What's going on? Could it be that he's well aware of his own guilt in colluding with the Dark Guild? Or perhaps he's completely looking down on me, thinking I wouldn't dare to act?

So Merlin reached to his waist and slowly drew his wakizashi, bringing it down hard toward Steve's neck.

Steve closed his eyes and didn't resist at all, assuming the posture of someone waiting to die.

You're really not afraid of death?

Merlin's blade halted just above Steve's neck—not severing his head, but cutting the pendant around his neck.

The blade and Steve's neck skin were separated by barely a hair's breadth. With just a slight push from Merlin, the man's head would have been cleanly severed.

Given how naturally Steve sought death, Merlin felt deep suspicion—this didn't seem like the behavior of an evil person.

The pendant fell to the ground with a metallic clang, knocked away by the force. Inside was a circular photograph showing a family of three, with a background that looked like a crude rural tavern.

Merlin looked down and glanced at it curiously, then his expression changed to something strange, and his gaze toward Steve shifted.

In the photo, the man was naturally Steve, though younger. The woman and child, Merlin recognized well— they were Martha and young Henry from the village outside, who were struggling to run a tavern.

They looked so much like a family. Could it be that the Steve standing before him was actually young Henry's father—the man who had abandoned his wife for years?

Merlin recalled that Martha's husband was serving his military duty in Edinburgh and hadn't had time to return home. Yet the Steve before him looked just like Martha's husband.

If all this were true, then why was Martha's husband, who was supposedly serving his military duty, working as a butler at the Earl's mansion in Highwall City?

Merlin found this hard to understand, so he quietly pushed Steve aside and picked up the pendant from the ground, though his blade still pointed at him.

"What's your relationship with the people in this photo?"

"My wife and son. Is there a problem, sir?" Steve slowly opened his eyes and, seeing Merlin holding his pendant, felt a slight irritation in his heart.

Merlin said nothing, only looking slightly surprised. He hadn't expected it to actually be Martha's husband. But he was supposedly serving his military duty—why would he be working as a butler in Highwall City?

Given that the other party had tricked him before, Merlin didn't intend to directly ask, exposing that he knew Martha and young Henry. Instead, he began to probe indirectly.

"Why are you going after us? Do we have a grudge?"

"There's no grudge, but I want revenge. You can't help me anyway and will only become an obstacle." Steve, with the mindset of a dying man, didn't hide anything.

"Is that the reason you've been scheming behind our backs and colluding with the Dark Guild?" Merlin frowned, feeling that Steve was making excuses.

"As long as I can kill Earl Batten, I'm willing to pay any price—even if it means resorting to dark forces..." Steve's eyes carried a hint of determination.

"Why?" Merlin's expression turned cold, and his blade unconsciously moved closer to Steve. "Aren't you the earl's subordinate?"

"This all started three years ago with an incident I can't help but mention. I was foolish back then, and for some petty gains, I served Earl Batten to the death." Steve lifted his head, his eyes growing deep, as if recalling something from long ago.

"At that time, I was serving my military duty in Edinburgh, as an officer in a young squad..."

Three years ago.

In the most remote area within Edinburgh's borders, there were endless mountains.

It was said that a treasure of immense value was hidden here. Whoever found it would become wealthy.

Countless adventurers had come here before to seek the treasure, but all returned empty-handed, or never returned at all, forever sleeping in the depths of the mountains.

At this very moment, at night, a squad was camped here resting. More than ten people sat around a bonfire drinking and chatting, passing the long night.

They all wore the uniforms of the British Empire's soldiers, equipped with various gear, looking like an expeditionary force.

This was Steve's squad. They were currently being hired by Earl Batten to search for the legendary treasure.

Steve was the captain of the entire team, but in reality, orders were issued by Earl Batten, who wasn't present at the moment. He was thinking about tomorrow's route, looking for any clues.

The small path ahead.

The entire squad was quite young, with many soldiers still retaining a youthful appearance. The oldest was probably Steve himself.

Although Steve was over thirty, he easily blended in with these young people. Rather than being called a captain, it was more like he was an experienced senior in life.

The atmosphere of the chat was very harmonious. The firelight illuminated each person's face. Under the influence of alcohol, their faces were flushed red.

Despite being in the middle of nowhere, they didn't feel lonely at all.

"Lord Batten is really generous. As long as we accompany him, we get 1000 gold coins. If we find the treasure, it's five times that!" Steve made an exaggerated expression and held up five fingers. He seemed a bit drunk, his eyes filled with excitement. "This is a rare opportunity! In the military, there's nothing like this. Everyone must cherish this chance and try to find that damn treasure and make a fortune."

"Isn't this all thanks to Captain Steve's connections? We should be grateful. Otherwise, with the soldiers' meager pay, we'd struggle to even buy a cart." One soldier replied with a laugh.

"Don't mention it like that. You're all my subordinates. As long as I'm here, I'll make sure you live comfortably!" Steve swayed and said.

"...That's right. As long as Captain is here, we'll definitely get better and better..." A timid-looking soldier chimed in, his face showing strong inexperience, probably having joined the military not long ago.

"As long as we make enough money this time, I'll leave the military and return to my hometown."

"Then no one will look down on me anymore, and I can keep my promise to marry a girl from the town..."

title: Chapter 30 — Cave Vampire (Two-in-One)
content:
Chapter 30 — Cave Vampire (Two-in-One)

Volume 13 · Chapter 30

Hearing that the youngest soldier in the squad was already thinking about going home to find a wife and have children, the others immediately began to tease him.

"You really have no ambition at all. You make money and all you want to do is go home and raise a family."

"Yeah, Mary is the tomb of love. Being too eager about something like that isn't exactly a good thing, is it?"

"Don't say that. At his age, he's still a virgin. That should already be pitiful enough, shouldn't it?"

Gene realized that saying those words would get everyone to make fun of him, which made him feel a bit ashamed.

"You're the youngest member here. I bet seven or eight of us already have kids at home." Steve frowned and said, with a touch of the captain's authority, "You guys can joke around, but don't go too far. Saying things like this will make him afraid to get married."

"Captain, we're not being serious."

"That's right. We're just saying that since he's so young and hasn't experienced the pleasures of life yet, getting married so early would be such a pity."

The soldiers chimed in from all sides, each speaking with the tone of seasoned veterans despite their young ages.

Steve patted the youngest soldier on the shoulder and said with a deeply serious expression, "Work hard to make money so you can marry the woman you like—"

"No, no. His kind of thinking is what's truly foolish. As a man, you should fight for the woman you love. That's admirable. People like him who are still so pure and dedicated are rare these days. You lot—"

The youngest soldier was so moved he could barely hold it together, his eyes welling up with tears.

"Hmph. You still have the leisure to sit here daydreaming about the future. We've been here for over three months and only got 1,000 gold in subsistence pay. Get lost already!"

Baron Barton walked over with an expression clouded by frustration, clearly unhappy about having found nothing.

"Like we don't want to find the treasure either," Steve responded awkwardly.

"Sir, could it be that you don't actually want five times the payment?" Baron Barton asked sharply.

"I think you never put your heart into it."

Approaching the campfire, his gaze swept across the soldiers' faces.

"We also want to help you find the treasure, but finding this thing is really not easy. I heard that no one has found it in several hundred years. We've only been here for three months. How could it possibly be that easy?"

"You'd best give it your all, or don't blame me for deducting your pay." Baron Barton threatened.

"We'll do our absolute best, my lord. Please rest assured." Steve plastered a smile on his face, while cursing Baron Barton repeatedly in his heart.

These people made them work like oxen and horses, and they'd even resorted to the despicable tactic of threatening to dock wages.

"To get them moving, Steve quickly unfurled the map and pointed to a mountain peak. "Starting tomorrow, we head there."

"That's good." Baron Barton nodded satisfied.

"Is there anything strange about this place?" Steve looked at the map and found that the area behind Baron Barton showed no special markings.

"I've already investigated. Some exploration teams and adventurers have been to this place, and all of them disappeared without a trace."

"Such a mysterious place should hide something unknown. Perhaps the treasure we're looking for is hidden in this area," Baron Barton said confidently.

It did seem suspicious. Hearing that people who had gone there never returned was enough to make one feel afraid.

However, the squad's soldiers, motivated by the hefty reward, didn't say much.

But the commander of this expedition was Baron Barton. Hidden halfway up the mountain, they discovered a pitch-black cave.

After several days of trekking through mountains and rivers, the squad arrived here. Everyone was somewhat excited.

All members of the squad looked at the cave entrance, feeling this was the only place in three months that could possibly hide treasure.

"This looks suspicious," Baron Barton peered around. "Let's go in and take a look."

"Understood." Steve nodded and ordered the soldiers beside him, "Everyone, gear up and prepare to enter. There could be treasures here."

"Hmm!"

Everyone lit torches and entered the cave.

The group organized themselves and then lit their torches, relying solely on the flickering light to advance forward.

The pitch-black cave was so dark you couldn't see your five fingers. Leading the way, Steve could only explore bit by bit to stay safe.

In this unknown territory, no one dared to speak loudly, let alone rush forward recklessly.

They were eventually blocked by a massive boulder.

No one knew how long the squad had been walking, but they finally reached the end, which appeared to be a dead end.

"My lord baron, this seems to be a dead end?" Steve called out.

Baron Barton raised his torch and came close, examining it carefully. "Just move those stones aside. You several, work together to shift this rock!"

The soldiers exchanged glances, then sheathed their weapons and surrounded the boulder, pushing together slowly until they managed to move it aside, creating just enough space for a person to pass through.

While the soldiers were busy, Steve held up his torch and scanned around, trying to find something useful. Suddenly, he noticed a skeleton lying not far away.

This skeleton was wrapped in leather armor with a very ancient style, as if the owner had lived in a bygone era. The bones were grayish-black, but after Gene wiped away the dust, a shining luster was still visible. Resting on its knees was a peculiar brown beast-skin notebook, and its hands tightly gripped a pure silver sword.

He carefully flipped through the notebook,生怕 damaging the artifact.

Steve picked it up curiously. Due to its extreme age, he handled it very carefully. Obviously, it didn't belong to this era and resembled something like hieroglyphs.

What kind of nonsense is this?

Had someone been here long ago?

Steve was puzzled, but on the other side the stone had been moved aside, leaving him no time to think further.

Steve was very confused.

"Captain, we should go."

"Oh, right."

Steve nodded and tucked the notebook into his chest before following along.

The soldiers noticed that the passage widened as they went deeper, and the temperature gradually dropped. Strange noises occasionally echoed from above.

It was as if they had entered a bat cave. Illuminated by torches, they saw dense bats hanging upside down on the cave walls, resting.

To avoid disturbing them, they had to extinguish some torches and continue advancing using only the light from the large torches at the front.

When the team carefully made it to the bottom, the view suddenly opened up, and there were no more bat disturbances.

As the squad cautiously reached the end, they abruptly discovered a black coffin in the center.

Everyone relit their torches and observed their surroundings.

Baron Barton himself became extremely excited.

"The treasure must be inside that coffin! Quick! Open it!"

"Alright, just watch, my lord!"

Several soldiers worked together to pry open the coffin, and Baron Barton impatiently rushed forward, shoving the other soldiers aside.

"Get lost! This is mine!"

He gazed inside the coffin and found only a blackened mummy inside. Other than a dried sheepskin paper tightly gripped in its hands, there was nothing else.

Baron Barton took the sheepskin paper and slowly unrolled it.

He walked to one side to examine it and found it was filled with incomprehensible strange symbols, resembling a map. He immediately flew into a rage!

Baron Barton had come here for gold and jewels. Who wanted this junk of a sheepskin paper?

"Damn it! Another wasted effort! I want gold and jewels!!"

Gene wiped a cold sweat from his forehead and walked forward to say, "Please don't be discouraged, my lord. We can continue to search hard."

"Over three months! Not a single scrap of treasure! You're all a bunch of trash!" Baron Barton ranted at Steve.

"It's been over three freaking months!"

Suddenly, a corpse fell down right beside Steve and Baron Barton.

"What was that!?" Baron Barton was startled.

Steve shone his torch on it and immediately realized it was his squad mate, the youngest soldier!

The soldier's face still bore the terror of death, and his whole body was shriveled dry, as if all his blood had been drained.

"Captain! The mummy in the coffin is gone!"

"Huh!?"

The soldiers' faces turned pale, their hearts pounding wildly.

A string of disasters threw everyone into disarray, and they began to panic. Terrified to the extreme,

"You worthless commoners, what are you staring at for? Come protect me!" Baron Barton shrieked in anger.

"Everyone, gather together! Protect the baron! Don't stay apart!" Steve, at least somewhat experienced, knew that acting alone now

was very dangerous. Sticking together allowed them to better handle unknown threats.

They guarded their surroundings. In the darkness, the team looked like a small torch.

All the soldiers were very tense, cold sweat pouring down their bodies. They felt that in this pitch-black darkness where you couldn't see your five fingers...

Steve's face darkened. He wondered: Was the mummy杀人? Could this be some kind of undead magic?

Suddenly, a black shadow lunged out from the darkness, grabbing two soldiers by the head and dragging them into the darkness.

The speed was so fast that no one else could react. They could only hear desperate screams—

"Captain!"

"Captain, save us!"

Although it all happened in an instant, Steve勉强 made out what it was.

Blue-gray skin, crimson eyes and fangs, and large bat-like wings fluttering—it was none other than a legendary vampire!

This vampire, after feeding on the mummy's skeleton, had become very plump, and its skin was beginning to glow with vitality.

"You two bottom-feeders, hurry up and cover me while I escape!" Baron Barton had already lost his mind, his thoughts filled only with getting out of this cursed place.

Hearing the word "escape," everyone dropped their weapons and scrambled to flee ahead of each other.

"Hey! Don't run! If you run now, you'll become prey!"

Steve shouted, but at a time like this, his role as captain clearly had no effect whatsoever.

Hearing his teammates' agonizing screams in the darkness,

he was furious with himself, yet he lacked the courage to save them alone.

Moreover, morale had collapsed, leaving no chance to resist. Steve had no choice but to flee while blaming himself, constantly thinking...

The squad began to flee wildly, awakening swathes of vampire bats. Even if bitten, they didn't stop running, screaming as they fled.

Baron Barton followed behind, and one by one, lagging soldiers were caught and drained dry. Everyone was terrified to the extreme!

Yet in the distance, screams and the screeching of bat sonar could still be heard from deep within the cave.

Finally, Baron Barton and Steve managed to escape from the cave. Baron Barton pulled out a round earth bomb from his pack.

A cold sweat streamed down Baron Barton's forehead. Worrying that the monster might chase them out,

he intended to blow up the cave entrance and trap the monster inside.

Seeing the baron produce an earth bomb, Steve was utterly terrified. "My lord, what are you doing!?"

"I'm going to blow up this cave entrance! Otherwise, when the monster comes out, both you and I will die!" Baron Barton trembled as he lit the fuse in his hand.

"No! My lord! Steve tightly grabbed Baron Barton and said excitedly, "There are still people who can escape! Please wait—"

"If you throw the earth bomb now, you'll be a murderer!"

"You worthless dog! How dare you stop me! My life is tens of thousands of times more valuable than yours! Even if you bunch of

lowly commoners die, so what? I'm still alive! Your lives are worthless!"

Steve's expression went numb. His eyes filled with despair. He felt Baron Barton was at his most despicable. In his eyes,

Baron Barton fiercely threw the earth bomb into the cave. With a deafening "boom," the whole world fell silent.

Beneath the night sky, Baron Barton and Steve stood together.

The cave entrance had been destroyed by the explosion. Rubble sealed off the passage, and that vampire couldn't get out.

Of course, neither could those soldiers. It went without saying what blocking the entrance meant for them; they would likely become casualties of mutual devouring.

"Phew." Baron Barton exhaled heavily and collapsed onto the ground. "Finally safe. I thought we were dead for sure!"

Steve's face was grim. He clenched his fists, trembling with rage.

Originally, quite a few people could have escaped. But because of Baron Barton's cowardice, they all died!

He grabbed Baron Barton off the ground, wanting to beat that bastard to death.

"Barton, you despicable fellow! I'm going to—"

"Try it! I'll make sure your family is destroyed!"

"What are you doing!? Don't forget I'm nobility! You dare lay a hand on me?!"

Baron Barton glared at him, his attitude defiant. A mere captain daring to fight him—this was outrageous!

"Don't forget you also have a family. Offending me, do you think a lowly commoner like you can survive in the Britannia Empire?"

Steve's eyes turned bloodshot. His heart was filled with turmoil. Remembering his wife Martha and his son Henry, he simply couldn't bring himself to strike again!

"Hmph! Show some respect!" Baron Barton pushed Steve away and adjusted his collar. "You can't ruin your family's future for a moment of satisfaction."

Steve's breathing grew heavy, his teeth nearly biting through his own lip.

Steve glared at Baron Barton with furious eyes. His face was ashen with rage.

"Keep this quiet. Your soldiers didn't die seeking treasure; they deserted and couldn't bear military life anymore. Understood?"

Baron Barton approached Steve and patted his shoulder. "As a reward, after you finish your service, you can come work for me. Double pay. Work hard, my friend. Haha."

Finally, Steve fell to his knees, old tears streaming down his face.

After Baron Barton left, Steve stood there for a long time, eventually shedding tears.

He raised his fist and smashed it violently onto the ground, blood splattering everywhere. Sorrow and anger intertwined in his heart.

That Barton bastard...

title: Chapter 61 — Respect
content:
Chapter 61 — Respect

Volume 13 · Chapter 61

In a small alley of the night, Merlin held a knife at Steve, and upon hearing this story, his heart remained utterly unmoved.

To Merlin, these fellows were simply overestimating their own abilities. They were so weak yet wanted to get rich overnight through treasure hunting!

Steve gathered his thoughts. He wasn't particularly fond of events from many years ago.

"This is how it was. For countless nights, I was awakened by the cries of my subordinates. I wonder if they harbor resentment against me in hell as well.

Merlin pondered for a while and felt that Steve was merely a pitiful person whose eyes were blinded by hatred. To kill Baron Barton without drawing fire upon oneself was indeed more reliable by seeking help from the Dark Guild.

As members of a legitimate guild, Merlin and Alice certainly wouldn't agree to Steve's unreasonable request, nor would they kill someone so casually.

Merlin recalled that half a year ago, when he was working part-time in a village, Martha had taken good care of him. If he were to kill her husband, it would seem not quite right.

Thus, Merlin lowered his knife, sheathing it, intending to let Steve go on account of Martha and her son.

"Scram! Don't let me see...."

Steve was suddenly stunned. This time, he was doomed to die, but he hadn't expected the other party to let him go.

Thinking about how excessive his actions had been, he had torn up the introduction letters of Merlin and Alice, making things difficult for them.

Normally, even if Merlin had killed him, it wouldn't matter. Whoever had been calculated against would have a bad mood.

Moreover, with no one around, the moon dark and the wind high—even if he killed himself, no one would know, right?

Steve's heart was puzzled, nervously swallowing a mouthful of saliva, mustering the courage to show respect.

"T-Why did you let me go?! I stabbed you guys in the back!"

"How does that matter?" Merlin showed a disdainful expression, speaking calmly, "Your life isn't your own; it belongs to your wife and children. If I kill you, what about them? Don't even think about seeking death to be reunited, because you don't even have the qualification to commit suicide.

After saying this, Merlin turned and walked off, planning to head toward the north gate to meet Alice, who was lying in ambush there, and discuss the next course of action.

Although he hadn't obtained the treasure map, there might be other ways. The most direct method was probably to find the headquarters of the Azure Blue Hellfire and cause a commotion!

Merlin's brief words struck the softest part of Steve's heart, making him feel mixed emotions at this moment.

The only motivation Steve had to survive now was his wife and children, who he hadn't seen in a long time.

If there weren't such heavy ties in his heart, Steve might have died alongside Baron Barton a few years ago.

The moon was almost round like a silver plate, and the sky was completely bright.

Under the starry sky, although Merlin's clothes were messed up and tattered due to the conflict, making him look quite shabby, his departing silhouette seemed incredibly tall.

This might just be an illusion, but in Steve's eyes, Merlin was probably a giant. The originally desperate him had once again seen the future.

"Merlin, please wait!"

"Hmm?" Merlin stopped, frowning and asking, "Do you have other matters?"

"I have something I want to give you..." Steve reached into his pocket, fumbled for a while, and took out a thick brown leather book.

Merlin turned around, looking at the book in Steve's hand, as if it were something from long ago, the paper turning a waxy yellow color. "What is this?"

"A few years ago, when me and Baron Barton were searching for treasure, we found a cave. Outside the stone door, there was a skeleton, and this book was found beside the skeleton. It's a diary." Steve said seriously.

"What does a diary have to do with me? I have no interest in such things." Merlin impatiently waved his hand, intending to leave.

"Merlin, please let me finish!" Steve hurriedly stopped Merlin, summarizing concisely, "Aren't you wanting the vampire treasure map? Just to find vampires? The owner of this diary was a vampire hunter from long ago! I only kept the diary out of curiosity at the time, I didn't expect it would come in handy today."

"Hmm?" Merlin narrowed his eyes, suddenly interested. Although he wanted to find Dracula, the experience of a vampire hunter was also worth referencing, "What's written above?"

"Basically, it's about a hunter killing vampires everywhere, and some hearsay. The whole thing is written in extremely ancient characters, so with my learning, it's hard to understand; I can only understand some simple symbols." Steve paused and continued, "This diary was discovered together with the vampire treasure map in the same cave. I think if someone can understand the contents, maybe they'll discover connections, which should be useful for you."

"Hmm.... Merlin stroked his chin, slightly moved. If the diary had important things, one wouldn't need the treasure map to catch some clues.

"Merlin, I know I did something very overboard. You probably won't easily forgive me, ..." Steve handed the diary over with a very sincere expression, "I hope to use my own ability to reduce some of your losses, considering it my wa

Merlin looked at Steve's serious expression, then lowered his head to glance at this ancient and simple diary...

Highwealth City, north district.

It was late at night, and the whole city was still chaotic. Many people had gathered toward Keith Castle to watch the excitement.

Alice was hiding on the roof, scrutinizing every path with meticulous eyes, for fear that Steve would run away.

However, Alice had been lying in ambush for a long time, and no figure was seen, which made her very frustrated.

Damn! Where did the person go? Is it really from the south gate that he escaped?

Or maybe Merlin's guess was wrong, and the person never intended to escape in the middle of the night?

Alice couldn't help but mutter in her heart, beginning to doubt Merlin's guess, feeling that things weren't so simple.

A sudden shout made Alice jump, and her whole body leapt up from the ground.

Looking back, it was Merlin calling her. Alice suddenly felt a burst of anger, raising her small pink fist and attacking like a storm.

"You this rascal! Why didn't you call my name! ? Feinting so loudly to scare me! ?"

"Stop stop stop!" Merlin pulled Alice's hand away, sitting himself down on the roof tiles, doing as he pleased.

"Finish work? What work? The matter is already over?" Alice showed a puzzled expression.

"Yeah, it's over." Merlin nodded, letting out a breath.

"Wasn't it to capture that butler alive, then torture him to question the truth?" Alice was full of question marks, feeling Merlin hadn't proceeded according to the plan, but instead acted on his own accord.

"What truth is there to question? That butler knows nothing, his mind is just thinking about seeking help from the Dark Guild for revenge. We messed with the Dark Guild's cake, so this butler naturally has to make things difficult for us." Merlin casually responded.

"What on earth did you do? Don't so casually brush me off, okay? At the very least, you have to bring the person back!" Alice was somewhat going crazy.

"Sorry, I let him go." Merlin showed a helpless look, Alice's reaction was all within his expectations.

Eh? !" Alice's expression froze, then she was startled, "What?! You let him go! Why?! He's been playing tricks on us!"

"Why? ..... Merlin hesitated, looking up at the clear cold full moon in the sky, and said lowly

"I don't want a certain hardworking woman to cry every day.

"I don't want to see that little brat's admired person become a heartless killer.

"Total...

"I am that

"Respecting that man is a pretty good father."
