content:
Chapter 12 — Miranda (Moon Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 14 · Chapter 12

Arnold's words made Lilith jump, and she hurriedly knocked on his arm. "Don't say whatever you're thinking. It might not be what you imagine," she said sternly.

Arnold rubbed his temples and said with a huff, "What do you mean it's not what I imagine? That's Helen, the most beautiful woman in Rexrum."

"I think your eyes are on your ass. The most beautiful person in Rexrum is me!" Lilith pointed at herself without any courtesy.

"Forget it then. Even standing next to Helen, you wouldn't exist." Arnold waved his hands and couldn't help but say something that struck Lilith.

"Shut up, you jealous bitch. I'm the most beautiful woman in Rexrum, and I won't accept any arguments!" Lilith emphasized.

"Fine, fine. But Helen and Merlin's relationship definitely isn't normal. Have you ever seen Helen actively seek out any man? I think they must have some kind of intimate relationship~" Arnold stroked his chin, as if he had just thought of something. "It's a waste of Alice's pure heart, going around chasing after other women. Ugh, I'm so uncomfortable! Why can't a perfect person like me find true love?"

"Get lost. Maybe it's not as good as you think," Lilith rolled her eyes.

"Then tell me, why did Helen go looking for Merlin?" Arnold adopted an eager-to-hear-everything expression.

".... Lilith frowned, thought carefully, and answered, "I think Helen probably went to find Merlin to collect a debt?"

"A debt? What do you mean? It's not a debt of love, is it?" Arnold stroked his chin again.

"Love debt, my ass. What I mean is..." Lilith paused, then deliberately lowered her voice and whispered mysteriously, "Maybe Merlin's girlfriend didn't pay him?"

"What!?" Arnold's eyes widened. Suddenly he was deeply impressed with Lilith and wanted to kowtow to her. He thought, "Wow, Lilith's imagination is way richer than mine!"

So it seems Merlin is even more despicable than we thought!

In the basement of Helen's secret chamber.

Merlin met with Asmodeus through a long-distance connection using black technology.

Everything was prepared in advance, and they didn't waste much time.

Merlin sat in a chair, looking at Asmodeus on the magic screen, and asked casually, "Something happened again? First of all, I'm warning you—any troublesome things don't come to me. I'll definitely refuse."

"Coming straight out with the attitude of turning me away, you're really heartless~" Asmodeus said with a sly smile.

"It's not that I'm heartless. It's just that every time you come find me, it never brings good things, so I naturally have some wariness toward you." Merlin frowned, already not wanting to see Asmodeus's fake woman's face anymore.

"We're not old friends? You think I'd just go find someone else casually?" Asmodeus teased.

"Get lost, what old friends? Don't talk nonsense. If something gets misunderstood, I won't take any responsibility." Merlin said seriously, afraid someone might misunderstand, especially since Helen was respectfully standing behind him. If it got out, people might think he had some peculiar fetish~

2

"Many people have been dying to meet me in person. You, on the other hand, come find me with such an attitude. Don't you know how lucky you are?" Asmodeus asked with a seductive tone.

"Sorry, I really can't accept it!" Merlin stood up as if to leave. "If there's no real business, I'll just go now."

"Wait, I really do have something important to discuss with you this time." Asmodeus quickly called out to stop Merlin, hoping he could be more patient.

"Then say it quickly." Merlin sat down impatiently, waiting for Asmodeus to explain.

"But what I'm about to say might trouble..." Asmodeus added another sentence.

"Then I'm leaving. Goodbye." Merlin hadn't even sat down properly before he jumped up to run, completely unwilling to get entangled in troublesome affairs, especially now that his heart curse had already issued a warning. Any delay might cause problems.

"Merlin, why don't you listen first before deciding whether to leave or not?" Asmodeus was exasperated with Merlin's negative attitude. He had thought that as a friend, he could communicate with him properly, but it turned out to be disappointing.

"Fine, let's make it quick. Don't waste time." Merlin, constrained by Helen's presence, had to maintain Asmodeus's dignity as a ruler, so he gritted his teeth and decided to listen before leaving.

"Beelzebub's sister was kidnapped by humans. Since you're in the human empire, he wants you to help rescue his sister." Asmodeus stated it briefly, wrapping up the matter in a few sentences.

After hearing this, Merlin's face changed color, and his brows knit together as he tried to recall something.

Beelzebub's sister? Oh! That's the female demon who wanted to take me as her master back then. Right, wasn't she named Miranda? She's only about a hundred years old, younger than me. And she looks a bit naturally naive, always acting like a silly little kid.

Seems like Miranda used to admire me and took me as her role model, really hoping to become strong without relying on magic or combat spirit.

Because of this, Beelzebub had the audacity to beg me to be Miranda's teacher, hoping to impart some practical skills. But I refused.

I'm not being stingy. It's just that my power can't be passed on. Does Miranda have 9999 skill points built-in from birth? Impossible!

Moreover, no matter how you look at Miranda's personality, she's still childish, even more so than my sister Lilith. I'm the Great Demon Lord, not a babysitter! I'm not getting involved in this kind of childcare nonsense!

I didn't expect Miranda to actually get kidnapped by humans? Who did it? That's the beloved younger sister of the ultimate siscon gluttonous monarch!

No matter who did it, I really admire their courage. It's like they don't want to live anymore. Kidnapping the sister of a siscon, that's touching a sore spot—it'll be deadly serious!

Three black lines appeared on Merlin's forehead as he was shocked by the sudden news. He felt that some humans really don't know their limits, playing with fire. Miranda's sister being kidnapped—Beelzebub would definitely go crazy on the spot. Even starting a war against the outside world wouldn't be unreasonable.

"How did this happen? The demon race's territory has always been dangerous for humans. How could Beelzebub's sister possibly be kidnapped?"

S Novel

"Beelzebub and Miranda had some kind of conflict, causing Miranda's glass heart to break and she ran away from home. That's how she got kidnapped. It's really boring, just that simple. I was speechless when I heard about it." Asmodeus shrugged her ample shoulders, fully understanding Merlin's reaction to hearing this.

"No way? Why would this kind of troublesome thing happen to me? Can't Beelzebub just go find me himself?" Merlin's face turned black, clearly disliking this kind of mess.

"Lucifer, you should know that rulers can't just leave the Demon Lord Palace at will. And you're not just some idle person wandering around the human territory, are you? Who else would he ask?" Asmodeus said with a helpless expression.

"Who the hell said I'm an idle person?" Merlin's face darkened, and he began seriously explaining how busy he was.

"I'm busy every single day, okay? Besides eating, drinking, and shitting, I also have to find people to chat with and drink.

Before bed, I need to mock the previous Hero. I'm constantly suppressing the Holy Church lackeys' brazen momentum.

I also need to trim my beautiful nails, preparing enough to fight the Holy Church watchdogs.

Even when I fart, I need to deliberate for ten seconds. Say that honestly!"

"Am I really that busy?"

(+~m-)

title: Chapter 13 — The Fuse
content:
Chapter 13 — The Fuse

Volume 14 · Chapter 13

Asmodeus listened to Merlin's unconvincing explanation and helplessly said, "What the hell, you're practically turning into a vegetable from idleness? Just help out, it's only finding Miranda, you won't die."

"I will die, I'll die from exhaustion." Merlin responded with a completely serious face.

"You... why are you so afraid of trouble? You're lazy to the bone, even the Sloth Lord old man wouldn't be like you. Asmodeus really hopes Merlin changes his mind and helps Beelzebub a bit, otherwise this crazy- - sister-con will enter the human empire and cause trouble that won't be easy to clean up."

"I think that old guy who just sleeps to increase his magic power is far stronger than me; at least I can listen to you talking here, if it were Sloth, he wouldn't even pay attention to you." Merlin spread his hands.

"...Lin...." Asmodeus called his name directly, trying to get closer, "Among the Seven Lords, our relationship is pretty good. No matter what Beelzebub does, I hope you can help me with this; it's a good opportunity to win over the Gluttony Lord. If you ever return to the First Demon Lord Palace, having Beelzebub's help will make things go smoothly, and both I and Beelzebub will vouch for you; even if the demon council's opposition is loud, we can suppress it."

"Sorry, Asmodeus, but I really never planned to return to the First Demon Lord Palace..." Merlin replied embarrassedly.

"That's not for you to decide; demon blood flows in your veins, that can't be changed, you'll inevitably return someday." Asmodeus said sternly, wondering if Merlin already liked living in the human empire, which isn't a good thing.

Merlin didn't speak, but silently thought, what's the point of going back to the demon realm? Nothing at all, and besides, due to my heart curse, the demon realm is unsuitable for survival. nyf

CE's minor governance

"I am not Beelzebub's envoy; now I'm begging you as a friend, help find Miranda, otherwise this dead sister-con will go crazy, and then bigger chaos will ensue.... Asmodeus spoke sincerely, even if Helena were present, he would be willing to lower his stance."

"Pff.."

Merlin sighed, his face turned iron-blue; since it was an old friend persuading him, his heart began to waver a bit.

Thinking about it, I'm not a bad person either, and Beelzebub's sister Miranda gets along well with me.

She used to cling to me like a follower, taking me as a role model, constantly calling "Teacher! Teacher!" nonstop.

Because of this, Lilith found it unpleasant and often argued with Miranda, trying to drive her away.

It seems I also have some connection with Miranda; to protect my lofty and brilliant image in this girl's heart, I can only...

Merlin raised his head, his expression eased, as if he had made his decision, of course choosing to respect his true thoughts—

"Get lost!"

，

"I'm not going!"

"What does Beelzebub's sister being kidnapped have to do with me?!"

"Even though I was fried squid, I was at least a Great Demon Lord man; don't I deserve some face?"

"Are you really treating me as a babysitter for brats? Is Beelzebub looking down on me?!"

Originally Merlin had deep feelings brewing, yet he still chose not to go, indeed respecting his true thoughts.

Merlin truly felt that Beelzebub's sister had little relation to him, and he had never taken any disciples.

Whoever caused the trouble should solve it themselves; expecting me to handle everything is unrealistic.

Seeing Asmodeus silent, Merlin slowly rose from his chair and said calmly.

"If there's nothing else, I'll leave now."

"Why do you disagree? I've already spoken pleadingly." Asmodeus's eyes flashed with a hint of anger, dissatisfied with Merlin's indifferent attitude.

"Asmodeus, no reason, I just say one thing: Miranda is Beelzebub's sister, not my sister." Merlin's tone also became serious.

Actually the situation is special now; Merlin's heart curse flared up a few days ago, so time is precious for him—how could he waste it on the boring task of rescuing Miranda? His life is already hanging by a thread; if this matter were postponed, Asmodeus's request to Merlin would have a higher success rate.

"Our plastic sisterhood is really fragile."

Asmodeus sighed depressingly.

"Hey hey hey! Your statement is problematic!" Merlin's face turned black, he felt terrible.

"Oh, it's plastic brotherhood..." Asmodeus chuckled, continuing, "I'm actually asking you for the first time; you directly refused me, making me feel uncomfortable. Clearly, when you once confessed your love to me, I considered your feelings and never refused."

SF male small\say

"Huh?" Helena heard her master's words, jumped in fright, gave Merlin a strange look, probably thinking something weird?

"Cough cough!" Merlin quickly cleared his throat twice to cover his embarrassment, somewhat awkwardly saying, "Don't keep bringing up those old stories, it's so boring."

"I just think from a friend's standpoint, you shouldn't refuse me." Asmodeus puffed up his cheeks, seeming unbalanced inside.

"Asmodeus, you always treat me as a demon race member when considering things, which is wrong; the reality is..." Merlin pulled at the black iron adventurer's proof on his neck, self-mockingly saying—

"I am no longer a Great Demon Lord, and I've also been expelled from the demon race."

"Even if I say I have nothing to do with the demon race, it seems there's no big problem?"

"Now I'm just a novice adventurer scraping by at the bottom, struggling to live."

In the meeting.

Arnold and Lucya were still arguing about Helena actively seeking Merlin, almost about to fight.

Mutual verbal attacks continued, making surrounding adventurers reluctant to get close, fearing being dragged in.

However, at this moment Alice arrived; she woke up feeling fairly energetic, but didn't see Merlin, guessing this bastard must have gone to the guild to hang out with Hobbs again.

So Alice didn't think twice, tidied up a bit, and went out to find Merlin, wanting him to be her sparring partner to improve her skills.

Alice stood at the guild entrance, scanned around, still didn't see Merlin, and wondered inwardly—

"Where did that bastard go? And Hobbs isn't there either; they're not drinking here, where else could they go?"

Alice saw Arnold and Lucya arguing about something, thought a bit, then walked over, intending to ask if Merlin had come by.

Upon hearing Alice's voice, Arnold instantly looked as if injected with chicken blood, turned his head toward her, . Miss Alice, you've finally come.

"Um." Alice saw Arnold's fiery gaze, felt some resistance, kept a cold face and stayed silent.

"Come on, come on! Miss Alice, sit down, sit quickly! Standing is so tiring?" Arnold hurriedly offered his chair, pushing it toward Alice.

"I don't need it, I'll just ask a question and leave." Alice said irritably, feeling uncomfortable from Arnold's enthusiasm, then directly asked Lucya—

"Lucya, has Merlin been to the guild?"

"I checked a few horse betting shops and haven't seen his trace..."

title: Chapter 14 — Who understands men best?
content:
Chapter 14 — Who understands men best?

Volume 14 · Chapter 14

"Ah, are you looking for Merlin?"

Lucia's heart skipped a beat when Alice came straight to her, and she felt a wave of nervousness.

She hesitated about whether to tell the truth, since Helena and Merlin's relationship was somewhat murky.

But Lucia didn't know whether to speak up — she was afraid that if she said too much, she'd be the one blamed for ruining their marriage.

However, while Lucia struggled to find her words, Arnold sensed a major opportunity and didn't want to let it slip away.

If he added a little exaggeration to the fact that Helena had actively sought out Merlin, it might push Merlin and Alice apart — then wouldn't his chance finally come!?

Arnold nervously swallowed and felt his heart race. He quickly spoke up.

"Alice, Helena just主动 came looking for Merlin earlier — she probably took him to the secret cabin for some fun!"

"Eh!?" Alice froze on the spot. The Secret Cabin? Weren't those kinds of places inappropriate for minors? She'd warned Merlin countless times not to go there, and yet they still haven't cut ties!?

Lucia was startled when Arnold blurted it out without hesitation. If Merlin and Alice ended up having a huge fight over this, she'd be the one taking the blame for this idiot's recklessness.

She quickly clamped her hand over Arnold's mouth, her expression serious as she stared at him and whispered.

"Hey! What are you, stupid, talking nonsense like that!? Do you really want to see Merlin and Alice break up!? How can you just say something like that!?"

Alice watched the scene unfold. Although she was brimming with resentment toward Merlin and desperately wanted to storm the secret cabin right now and drag that guy out, she said,

"Lucia, don't stop him. Let him talk. I want to hear what exactly happened. If you keep secrets from me, that's not being a friend."

"I..." Lucia hesitated, but eventually gave in, releasing Arnold as she muttered under her breath, "Do whatever you want, then."

Arnold shrugged it off, straightened his clothes, and turned to Alice with a grin. "Alice, just now Helena主动 called Merlin away — their relationship is clearly not ordinary, is it? Merlin already has you by his side, yet he's still chasing after other women. Even I'm angry about this. It's like hogging the toilet and never using it!"

"You're the one on the toilet!" Alice's eyebrow twitched, irritated from the very first remark Arnold made.

"Uh, I just mean I couldn't put up with this if it were me. This Me... is too much!" Arnold said, enjoying the chaos. "Alice, don't worry — I'll definitely stand on your side on this!"

"That's not your concern." Alice replied coldly, thinking she couldn't let others make a fool of her, so she feigned calmness and said, "Merlin told me he needed to meet with Miss Helena recently to discuss some matters. I actually already knew about this — I just didn't expect it to be today."

"Eh!?" Lucia blinked in surprise. "Alice — you already knew!?"

"Yes." Alice nodded, wearing a composed smile on her face. To outsiders, there was no way they could tell how anxious she truly felt inside.

"Miss Alice, please don't be fooled by Merlin. Helena is the owner of the Secret Cabin. You know what kind of place that is, right!? Who would go there for legitimate reasons!?" Arnold wasn't ready to give up. Maybe this whole thing was just a misunderstanding — perhaps he and Lucia had been overthinking it.

"Merlin has important business to discuss. Lately we've been swamped with affairs, and there are certain matters we must seek Miss Helena's help with, so today's incident... doesn't surprise me at all." Alice turned and walked away, waving to them. "See you."

Watching Alice's retreating figure, Arnold and Lucia exchanged glances, each seeing confusion reflected in the other's eyes.

"Could it be that we overthought this? Maybe Merlin and Helena really do have serious business to discuss."

"It's only you who overthinks things. Stop talking nonsense when there's nothing to say!"

"You were the one saying earlier that Merlin gets free girlfriends and doesn't pay — and now the blame's landing on me!"

Alice walked toward the entrance of the Guild, her smile gradually fading, replaced by a dark expression. Her hand instinctively tightened around the slender sword at her waist.

Merlin...

You philandering bastard...

I'm going to get to the bottom of this today, or this isn't over!

Deep within the secret cabin's underground passage.

Merlin and Asmodeus's meeting had concluded — he had ultimately refused to help Beelzebub find his sister.

At this critical moment when the heart curse's warning was most pressing, how could Merlin possibly allow himself to be tied up by unrelated matters?

Regardless, this kind of request had to be decisively refused — otherwise, endless troubles like this could endanger Merlin's life.

What was most important to Merlin? Of course it was time. He needed to seize every opportunity to extend his own life.

So even though Asmodeus was Merlin's friend, coming to him for a favor at such a crucial moment — refusing was the only option.

Merlin now had to deal with the vampire clan's matters and also find a way to locate his prey. Between those two things, could he really spare the energy to help find Miranda? Impossible.

Helena respectfully followed behind Merlin, wanting to see him out, but her expression was a little curious as she occasionally stole glances up at him.

These small gestures were easily caught by Merlin — throughout the journey he'd felt Helena's strange gazes enough to make him uncomfortable.

"Helena, why keep staring at me?"

"I... I'm very sorry, Lord Lucifer..." Helena quickly lowered her head,不敢 look at Merlin anymore.

"Just say what's on your mind — stop beating around the bush." Merlin furrowed his brow, sensing that Helena had something on her mind. Otherwise, why would she keep looking at him?

Helena hesitated for a moment, then looked up and asked candidly, "Um... I'm just very puzzled. Did you really pursue our lord?"

...Merlin's expression stiffened. Being asked so directly was embarrassing. "...Well, I suppose I did pursue him, yes."

"Really...? Truly worthy of Lord Lucifer," Helena said, still finding it hard to understand but feeling deep admiration within. "As the ruler of the demon race, even your preferences are so unique!"

Merlin's features twisted together as he helplessly criticized inwardly: Shut up! This isn't something worth praising! It's a dark history!!

"Although I'm amazed by your unique tastes, our lord is a man, so there would never be any result between you two." Helena paused, lowered her head in thought, and muttered to herself,

"As expected, men truly understand men best.

(。・_・。)

title: Chapter 15 — Peeping at the Fallen Angel
content:
Chapter 15 — Peeping at the Fallen Angel

Volume 14 · Chapter 15

Merlin's face darkened, thinking "I'm not, I don't, who understands men? I don't."

"It seems I'm still too naive; I need more training." Helena said solemnly, feeling she still doesn't understand male desires. If there were Merlin accompanying the journey, perhaps they'd have already opened the secret cottage to the imperial capital.

Merlin, worried Helena might misunderstand, turned and said seriously to Helena, "That... don't misunderstand, I have no secrets with your master. I did pursue him before, but that was because I was young and completely unaware of the world's dangers, and didn't recognize Asmodeus as a man, so this joke happened. Please don't overthink it."

"Yes..... Helena suddenly understood, lowered her head and said, "I understand what's going on. Rest assured, Your Majesty, I won't tell anyone about this."

Merlin smiled, nodded satisfactorily, thinking Helena was truly understanding, knowing how to conceal his dark history, she would surely achieve great things in the future.

"Because those who sought love from our lord, Your Majesty Lucifer, you are not the first; there were originally many, and at first no one noticed that our lord was male." Helena added another sentence.

Merlin's expression instantly turned awkward, inwardly he wondered, "What does that mean? Is he mocking someone like me, a fool, and there are many more?"

"Actually.. I find it hard to understand our lord's behavior; clearly male, yet unusually fond of women's clothing, which has caused quite a few misunderstandings." Helena's expression showed some resentment; it seems she still has opinions about Asmodeus's cross-dressing habit.

"It seems that troublesome guy has caused quite a bit of trouble, huh?"

Merlin had also heard a bit about the misunderstandings caused by Asmodeus; initially everyone rejected and belittled them, but eventually everyone ended up bent, becoming supporters under Asmodeus's skirt.

As for Merlin himself, he's completely a wildcard, possibly a rare individual not conquered by Asmodeus's beauty; even Asmodeus himself might find it puzzling why he can't bewitch Merlin.

Little did they know Merlin comes from a civilized world where cross-dressing is the norm, and big-breasted moe girls are everywhere, so Merlin is naturally immune to Asmodeus.

"Although it causes many misunderstandings, after so long we subordinates have grown accustomed to it; we can tolerate our lord's quirks as long as they aren't too outrageous, we can just pretend we didn't see." Helena showed an exhausted expression.

Black lines streaked down Merlin's forehead as he thought in astonishment, "Has Asmodeus been completely abandoned by his subordinates?! How pitiful!"

"Although Asmodeus has a somewhat eccentric personality, he's still very responsible; following him won't lead you astray."

"I know, I just wish my master were a dashing demon rather than one who likes women's clothing..." Helena replied softly.

"A dashing demon?" Merlin frowned, rulers have the right to choose servants, but servants don't have the right to be picky.

"Yes, a dashing demon; I think such an owner would have more cohesion, just..." Helena lowered her head, covering her mouth as she whispered, "Even you- ..."

"......... Is that so? That's truly an honor." A bead of cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead as he thought, "What the hell am I like?!" How embarrassing.

Because of Helena's strange remark just now, the atmosphere between them instantly became subtly odd, always feeling weird, making one feel unnatural.

Helena kept her head down, silent; Merlin also remained silent as they walked through the narrow underground passage toward the outside.

Logically, even if Merlin is a former Demon Lord, his status is far nobler than Helena's; the two don't seem well matched.

Moreover, Helena has always believed Merlin to be a talented and ambitious monarch who, after enduring humiliation and relinquishing the Demon Lord throne, is plotting a grand scheme.

However, the real Merlin and Helena think completely differently; he's just a lazy bum with a mind full of idling, an unemployed vagabond.

Feeling the atmosphere between them strange, Merlin decided to find a topic to ease the awkwardness, so he recalled what the Rexhelm guard captain Price had said upon his return.

"Miss Helena."

"Huh? Your Majesty, what's the matter?" Helena asked, raising her head doubtfully.

"Recently I've heard outsiders spreading rumors about fallen angels; could your identity have been exposed?" Merlin turned his head to look at Helena.

Helena furrowed her brows, her face showing a hint of worry, hesitated a moment then replied, "My true form was indeed seen by a certain human."

"Really? How could you be so careless? Exposing your true form on human turf is no small matter; it could cause quite a panic." Merlin felt this was troublesome; after all, he too is a demon, and mishandling it could implicate innocent bystanders.

"Maintaining a human guise is quite exhausting for a demon, you should understand?" Helena paused, then continued, "So every night when I rest, I release my black wings to relax properly."

"Since it's in your own room, why would you be exposed?" Merlin asked, puzzled.

"When I was bathing.... Helena's face flushed slightly, she said embarrassedly, "It seems I was peeped at."

"Ah! ?"

Merlin's eyes widened, thinking "Damn, there's actually such a sneaky move?! And there are still people daring enough to peep at Helena bathing?!"

For demons, humans are lowly creatures; after being peeped at, their feelings are probably nothing but disgust.

Moreover, why would mere humans dare to peep at a female demon bathing? Aren't they afraid of death?

After calming down a bit, Merlin thought of the reason: who let her still flaunt such gorgeous looks? Being hailed as the most beautiful woman in Rexhelm, attracting some reckless wolves is understandable.

"After work that night, I returned to my room to rest; before sleep I released my true form to bathe, but at the time I felt something off, as if someone was watching, though the feeling vanished instantly—I thought it was an illusion, never expecting that night my fallen angel true form was indeed seen." Helena said, feeling stifled, her inner self not calm either.

"Do you know who did it?" Merlin inquired.

"The other party is a pickpocket, a member of a thief gang within Rexhelm." Helena looked at Merlin and said lowly, "Actually yesterday they already sent someone to look for me. They came to my door, saying they knew my secret, telling me to behave, otherwise they'd not let me stay in all of Britain, and also demanded I prepare five million gold coins to go to their hideout for a talk."

Merlin felt his ears must be malfunctioning; usually it's demons extorting humans, but today it's reversed—humans openly extorting a demon! ?

In Merlin's memory, demons always bully others, never having been oppressed themselves.

"Did you agree?"

"No, and I consistently denied being a fallen angel the whole time, acting like I knew nothing." Helena said truthfully.

"What are you going to do about it? Those who make a living by theft have no scruples; for profit they'll do anything." Merlin asked Helena, wanting to know if she had any idea to solve the present trouble.

"Isn't this simple? ....." Helena looked into Merlin's eyes, speaking without pressure, one by one.

"Lowly humans, just kill them all and it's settled, right?"

"Only the dead can keep the secret of life"

title: Chapter 16 — Monthly Ticket Bonus: The Kill Arrives
content:
Chapter 16 — Monthly Ticket Bonus: The Kill Arrives

Volume 14 · Chapter 16

"I plan to act tonight and kill this entire bandit gang. That way, no one will know my true identity," Helena said with a somewhat chilling smile.

Merlin felt this method was highly problematic and cautioned, "This is terrible. Not only will it not solve the problem, it will actually produce the opposite effect."

"Why?" Helena felt she had done nothing wrong. Those people were scum who had peeped at her bathing and then turned around to blackmail her. How could killing them be a problem?

"Your matter is already causing a huge stir in Lexham. Many people already harbor suspicions toward you. If you go and kill those bandits now, won't that simply confirm that you're a demon? People will surely think it was you, killing witnesses to cover up your true identity. There's both reason and motive—I would believe it myself." Merlin spread his hands.

"Is that so? I didn't realize it would cause such trouble. I haven't thought things through thoroughly enough..." Helena felt Merlin was right. Acting now would be like shouting "I have nothing to hide!" while holding a sign that said "I'm guilty"—there would be no explaining it away.

"Besides, this is human territory, not demon lands. Killing people recklessly could easily backfire and burn you. It's not the best option. Killing should only be a last resort." Merlin was somewhat worried that Helena might mishandle this, causing things to worsen and accidentally dragging him in as well.

"...As expected of Lord Lucifer, your thinking is truly comprehensive. It seems my rashness almost led to a grave mistake." Helena lowered her head, still feeling a shiver of fear.

"A grave mistake? Demon territories are scattered across the world, but they're all desolate wastelands. Some necessities need to be procured from the outside, so demons have always secretly done business within human empires. Your establishment falls under the Fourth Demon Lord Palace's assets. If it were discovered to be run by a demon, it would cause widespread panic among humans. They'd begin suspecting more and more things around them are demon-related. Ultimately, a chain reaction would occur, endangering all demon businesses within the human empire. Do you understand what I mean?" Merlin explained as clearly and simply as he could. A demon's identity was too special—it absolutely must not be exposed on human soil. This was the bottom line for continuing operations.

Helena's face went pale as she realized the seriousness of the matter. She never expected that her momentary carelessness would drag her entire race into the danger.

Such enormous responsibility was far beyond what Helena could bear. She was merely a cadre of the Fourth Demon Lord Palace, not someone of pivotal importance in the demon race.

"Most humans are timid and suspicious. For their own safety, they'd rather kill a thousand by mistake than let one slip through." Merlin summarized simply, finding that humans' survival instincts were remarkably strong.

"But if this continues, business will become even harder to conduct. Our Lord will surely be angry." Helena furrowed her brows tightly.

"You can play dumb and ignore the rumors about the Fallen Angel. Perhaps the bandits will lose interest when they see you won't hand over a single coin. Also, rumors are something no one remembers forever—they'll be quickly forgotten. If that still doesn't work, then spending money to avoid disaster may be the only choice. If they accept money and back down, the expenditure isn't entirely wasted. And if even that fails..." Merlin thought for a moment, his expression darkening. "Then we kill everyone connected to the bandits, leaving no survivors. Even with the danger of exposure, we absolutely cannot let them live. We'll figure out what to do afterward."

"Your words are well-reasoned, my Lord. I will keep them in mind." Helena said respectfully beside him. After all, Merlin was the former Demon Lord, and his considerations far exceeded those of a low-ranking subordinate like herself.

"This matter... does Asmodeus know about it?" Merlin asked curiously. After talking so much, he still didn't know whether Helena's master was aware of the situation.

"No. At first, I felt this was a trivial matter and saw no need to report it to our Lord. I thought I could handle it myself..." Helena frowned, her expression conflicted. "Now that I know how serious this is, I don't even have the courage to tell our Lord."

Merlin fell silent. He thought the First Demon Lord Palace also had assets, namely selling magic scrolls—but only at exorbitant prices on the black market, because they could only summon demons. Meanwhile, Asmodeus's Fourth Demon Lord Palace didn't seem to have particularly developed businesses, except for this adult entertainment industry, which was flourishing with venues spread across many places.

The fact that Helena herself served as the manager of one of these establishments showed she was still quite favored by Asmodeus.

But the greater his favor, the harder it would be for mistakes to be forgiven. Helena might very well be punished by Asmodeus because of this incident, and her standing in his heart would certainly decline as a result.

Merlin often pitied his seven former subordinates back then, because they were all misfits. Although he had heard Asmodeus's temper was generally good, he couldn't rule out the possibility that Asmodeus might punish Helena.

After much deliberation, Merlin felt Helena was a good girl, and since this incident happened right under his nose, it seemed not unacceptable to help her—much easier than seeking out Beelzebub's sister.

"Helena, you'd best do as I just said. From a ruler's perspective, the primary goal is to prevent matters from worsening or causing unnecessary losses. I imagine Asmodeus's thinking would be similar. As long as we handle this discreetly without committing a major offense, your master is unlikely to blame you severely."

"I understand, Lord Lu... I mean, Senior Helen." Helena bowed her head gratefully. Merlin was offering her advice. She was merely a demon cadre, yet she still felt deeply honored that a monarch would care for her.

"You don't need to tell Asmodeus about this. If you find yourself unable to handle it on your own, you may come to me for help." Merlin walked ahead without looking back, his tone appearing somewhat aloof.

Helena suddenly paused, her mind racing. Merlin had just rejected the Gluttony Monarch's plea for help, yet now he was extending an olive branch to her... Was she somehow special?

Overthinking things, Helena became somewhat nervous and awkwardly replied, "Thank you for your favor. I sincerely appreciate your kindness. However, I hope to handle this matter on my own. This is a test of my abilities. If I must trouble you even for something like this, then I am truly unworthy of our Lord's trust."

"Do as you please." Merlin silently sighed. Anyway, as long as it didn't affect him, he didn't care about anything else.

"...Helena silently followed behind Merlin, looking at his back. A faint smile suddenly appeared on her face."

The famous Lucifer the Third was unexpectedly gentle in person, and he was quite poor at expressing himself.

As expected, he was the youngest among the Seven Monarchs. His words and deeds were too different from the other几位...

Just as Merlin and Helena were about to leave the basement, Alice had already arrived at the secret house, marching in fury.

This place was hardly somewhere a woman ought to visit, but Alice didn't care about such things. She barged straight in, wanting to see Merlin.

Overflowing with jealousy, Alice's self-control had weakened, and the cold aura around her body erupted uncontrollably.

With sharp eyes and hands on her hips, she stood in the reception room. Her fierce demeanor was simply like someone coming to catch a cheating partner.

Where was that bastard Merlin?

Hurry up and come out!

Let me hear how you'll explain yourself this time. So you've finally been caught red-handed, huh?!

title: Chapter 17 — Shot While Lying Down
content:
Chapter 17 — Shot While Lying Down

Volume 14 · Chapter 17

Alice stood in the reception hall, pondering whether to rush further inside to look around; maybe she'd get an unexpected gain. However, before Alice could wait for Merlin, Hobbs came out holding a bottle, swaying drunkenly, looking very satisfied, apparently having a great time! Hobbs also came because recently the rumors about Helena being a fallen angel had caused an uproar; mainly he didn't want the secret cottage in Rexham to close down, so he specially took out his private money to come support Helena's business, but he certainly didn't expect to bump into Alice, this righteous little guard, here. Alice searched for Merlin to no avail, but then she suddenly saw Hobbs, that old rascal, and instantly her anger flared, feeling Merlin must be here! Because Merlin usually likes to hang out with Hobbs when he's free, and they've even come to this kind of place together before. With this precedent, Alice immediately deduced that Merlin and Hobbs must have come here together to mess around; there's no doubt about it. Alice's anger rose, she glared at Hobbs with an ugly expression, speaking in a cold voice. “Hobbs....” “Huh?” Hobbs was still immersed in his pleasure when he suddenly heard Alice's icy tone, and he was startled sober, the alcohol wearing off a bit. He rubbed his eyes, shook his head, trying to clear his head, and took a close look. “Ah... Alice! ? How did you come here? ! This isn't a place for a woman!” “I don't need you to tell me where I can go! Speak! Are you and Merlin together? ! Where is he? !” Alice angrily questioned, her overbearing attitude making people uncomfortable. “Ah? Merlin's little brother also came? How would I know?” Hobbs looked astonished, thinking Merlin came? He hadn't seen anyone at all. “Stop pretending to be dumb here, does it help? You two definitely came here to mess around, as if I didn't know! Thinking you can just breeze through? Dreaming!” Alice's face darkened, she pressed: “Quickly tell me, where is Merlin? Get him out to see me.” “I-I really don't know! I just came, I haven't seen Merlin's shadow at all!” Hobbs nervously sweated, feeling Alice was being unreasonable, this was just taking out her anger on him. “Hobbs, you're out here fooling around, does your wife know? I really want to talk to her.” Alice politely expressed her desire to tattle. If she hadn't said it, it'd be fine, but saying it shocked Hobbs so much he nearly fainted, his legs went weak, trembling. It seems Hobbs usually acts like an experienced guy, but actually he's quite afraid of his wife. “Oh dear little miss, don't go crazy; if you tattle, tomorrow you'll see my corpse! You know how hard it is for me to scrape together private money by pinching pennies?” “Then quickly tell me where Merlin is; if you come to this kind of place I could pretend I didn't see it.” Alice said sternly, knowing Hobbs is a blabbermouth, she must be firm. “I truly don't know.... Hobbs is almost being driven mad by Alice, his tone has turned pleading, hoping she'll let him go.” “Hobbs, are you trying to bring about mutual destruction?” Alice frowned, nearly bursting a blood vessel from anger. However, just as the atmosphere became extremely tense, Merlin and Helena walked out from inside, making the scene even more bewildering. “Alice!” Merlin exclaimed, astonished, never expecting Alice to find him here; he thought she'd be resting obediently at home. Alice glanced at Merlin, then gave Hobbs a sideways look without good intentions, thinking: “See? As I suspected, you're with Hobbs! Still pretending not to know? Who are you fooling?!” “......” Hobbs glanced at Merlin, not knowing how to explain, his face flushed red, thinking: “No way? Merlin's actually here! This makes it seem like I was just covering for Merlin, and now I can't explain it clearly!” Helena, upon hearing the name ‘Alice’, felt a stir; she had long known from Merlin's adventurer's proof that Alice was Merlin's human wife. Seeing the real person today surprised Helena greatly, but it wasn't entirely unexpected. The secret cottage is a place where men often come to relax; having a tigress suddenly show up to drag her husband home isn't the first time. So when Helena saw Alice arriving aggressively, she remained relatively composed, and couldn't help but scrutinize this human girl. “Is this the human wife of His Majesty Lucifer?” “Look.... she doesn't seem all that; at a glance you can see her chest is padded, presumably she's quite flat-chested.” “Even though her figure isn't as good as mine, why would His Majesty Lucifer like her and even marry her?” “Really strange, could it be that His Majesty Lucifer just likes flat-chested girls? It seems plausible.” “... As expected of someone who is the proud monarch, his taste is unique, not in line with mainstream aesthetics.” Helena felt she understood Merlin less and less; as a demon she had a sense of superiority, not thinking highly of Alice, feeling such a girl could never be worthy of a demon monarch; ! they're completely from different worlds. Moreover, demons are extremely xenophobic, forbidding demons from marrying outside the race; moreover, Merlin is the proud monarch, marrying a human is already somewhat treasonous. However, Helena could sense Alice's righteous and noble aura; if Merlin liked this kind of human girl, she'd really wonder if Merlin deep down favored humans. Helena was sizing up Alice, and Alice naturally also glanced over with a comparative eye, evaluating this woman who is publicly regarded as the most beautiful in Rexham. Is this the madam of the secret cottage, Helena? In person she looks even more beautiful than the rumors.... Wait! Now isn't the time to be impressed; if I admire her right off the bat, I'd already have lost, right? No! I need to calm down first; I definitely can't be outshone by this woman, otherwise I'd lose without fighting. Even if it's acting, I now have to put on the appearance of a dignified, virtuous, understanding model wife, and can't let some vixen find an opening at this time! By the way, how did Merlin hook up with Helena? She looks well-educated and reasonable; could it be that this scoundrel Merlin used sweet talk? Thinking of this, Alice's face darkened a bit, her inner anger flared; although she knew she needed to restrain herself, she still felt a surge of impulse to excel. Everyone in Merlin's household mutually eyed each other, saying nothing, but already felt the subtle tension, especially Alice, this little vinegar jar, obviously burning with jealousy, so she came up with a plan to divert disaster eastward: “Oh~, Hobbs, I was wondering why I couldn't see you anywhere, turns out you're here; you brought me to play but can't ditch me, leaving me so embarrassed~” “Shut up! You shameless old scoundrel!” Hobbs fumed, completely losing his mind-- “Not coming out early, not coming out late, but showing up just when I'm explaining.” “Why is it that every time I lie down I get shot?” “I think you're deliberately trying to kill me =” 山(。口。山)

title: Chapter 18 — Marital Trust
content:
Chapter 18 — Marital Trust

Volume 14 · Chapter 18

Hobbs couldn't figure out why his knee kept getting hit by an arrow every time. He hadn't done anything bad normally, yet he kept getting dragged into the vortex of the couple's quarrel. "I seriously suspect you two don't like me on purpose and are just messing with me!" Merlin's forehead dripped a big bead of sweat, thinking, "Forgive me, Hobbs; if brothers aren't for selling, then they're worthless." "Hobbs, stop acting, you said you didn't know anything, right?" Alice looked at Hobbs with a challenging gaze, as if saying, "Hmph! Still trying to fool me? I've never trusted a word that comes out of Hobbs' mouth." "I swear by the Goddess of Light!" Hobbs placed his hand on his chest, sincerely saying, "I really didn't bring Merlin here; this guy is always a tightwad, so I haven't come here with him in a long time." "You're not even a follower of the Light Church; what's the use of swearing?" Alice said expressionlessly, unmoved by Hobbs' mage. "Hobbs, what are you doing? Clearly I didn't want to come, yet you dragged me here and now flatly deny it—really not being a good friend." Merlin felt hurt, putting on the look of a friend betrayed. ".....You shameless wretch! You have no feelings at all!" Hobbs clutched his chest, looking like he was about to burst a blood vessel from anger. Merlin ignored the indignant Hobbs, turned to Alice, slightly nervous, and said, "Alice... why did you suddenly come here? Shouldn't you be resting at home?" "Dear, why can't I come here? Am I interrupting your good time?" Alice gave a meaningful glance at Helena beside Merlin, her hostility obvious. "Um, dear?" Merlin's face turned awkward, thinking Alice had taken the wrong medicine, suddenly calling him "dear"? Didn't she find that strange? Normally they called him "Hey!" "That guy!" "Damn!" and such; suddenly being called "dear" was hard to accept. Speaking of which, I'm feeling flustered now, a bit nervous—could it be that Alice showing up at my door made me tense? Calm down, me; Alice is just my little follower, and I haven't done anything shameful, so why be nervous? Merlin puzzled himself internally, coughed lightly to hide his embarrassment. "Cough cough, what's interfering with my good time? Nothing." "Really? Then how come you and this...." Alice's gaze turned to Helena, coldly saying, "Did this lady come out from inside? What are you doing?" Hobbs was so confused by Merlin's anger that he only then realized how Merlin ended up in the secret cabin with Helena together—could there be some sort of good fortune involving a person with insight? = Finished! Rexham's number one beauty, maybe she's going to sweep Merlin away! Heavens! What tricks is this kid using to continuously charm two women he doesn't deserve? Although Alice is flat-chested, her looks are still decent; as a mithril adventurer, seeing Merlin makes her unable to walk away. Now even the usually refined and wise-looking Miss Helena is entangled with Merlin! What love potion did Merlin give those two, that behind the scenes he's constantly enjoying the bliss of having arms around both sides! Hobbs furrowed his brows, feeling a heavy blow, extremely unbalanced, so he leaned close to Merlin and whispered, "Awesome, Merlin. Usually you don't show off, but turns out you're like an enterprise thinking the red flag never falls, with colorful flags fluttering high fur—even our number one beauty favors you, though this is very dangerous, is it that Chris can't move J, or are you just too flighty?" "Go away, it's not what you think." Merlin shoved the sour Hobbs aside and told Alice, "We're just chatting inside." "Talking alone man and woman in such a place..." Alice looked around, nodded, "Hmm, I believe you." Merlin grew impatient, feeling Alice's words said she believed him but her tone meant otherwise—clearly she would doubt. He thought Alice might be too into her role; even though they're just nominal spouses, each has their own life, coming to this place should still be his freedom, right? Merlin didn't want to over-explain; saying too much would seem like he cared about Alice's opinion, and as free people we shouldn't restrict anyone. "I came here for legitimate business, this... next to... Helena heard Merlin was about to bluntly say they'd meet Asmodeus in the basement, she jumped, face went pale, and secretly tugged Merlin's sleeve." Merlin glanced at Helena in surprise; seeing her shake her head slightly, signaling him not to speak, he finally understood. Oh no! Alice had confused him so much he almost blurted out that this place was a demon stronghold. That's not something to say casually; even Alice mustn't know, it's a secret shared by demons. Merlin suppressed the urge to argue with Alice and didn't plan to tell her about his connection to Asmodeus. After all, Alice is merely human, and there's no 100% guarantee she won't leak the secret; as one of the Seven Sovereigns, Merlin knows some things could let her understand. Moreover, in Alice's eyes, Merlin had been fried by demons and basically had no contact with that side, allowing her to not estimate... Three Merlin. If Alice learned Merlin still had ties with demons, she'd likely resist and even become wary of him. Seeing Merlin and Helena's little actions, Alice's anger flared: "What a big‑taled fox spirit! Am I dead? You're still pulling and tugging with Merlin in front of me! Who is Merlin's wife, unclear? Damn! Such a thick‑skirted fox spirit! Not putting me in your sights! No way! I won't give you any chance to act!" After Helena saw Merlin calm down, she looked at opposite Alice and gave a polite smile, "Miss Alice, there's no need to be angry; my relationship with Mr. Merlin is purely platonic, nothing secret happened—we were just talking inside. Please don't be jealous, trust Mr. Merlin." "When did I get angry? Jealous? No...." Alice put on an innocent look, feigning grievance, saying, "Why do you think I don't trust my own husband?" "...." Helena felt a cold sweat trickle down her forehead, thinking, "Clearly my suspicion is written on my face! Why is your mouth so hard that you won't admit it?" "I and our Merlin are very loving; normally our relationship is as close as can be, though we're married we still act like newlyweds, burning with passion—I don't trust him? Are you joking?" Alice stared at Helena with hostility, adding, "Trusting him is like trusting myself; it needs no reason." "Huh? !" Merlin's brows knit, his face darkened, he stared at Alice like looking at an alien, thinking, "One—I wipe! Has Alice become a trans? She didn't even cry, make a scene, or threaten suicide! This isn't the Alice I know! Fairy! Who exactly are you? Quickly give back our family's treasure!" 2(P° A°;)p The matter of the name really hopes everyone will understand; this is good for everyone. Everything is for the sake of later adaptation, long names aren't conducive to the book's spread. title: Chapter 19 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update (Targeted)
content:
Chapter 19 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Update (Targeted)

Volume 14 · Chapter 19

"That... I know you and Mr. Merlin are close, so I'm glad you understand."

Helena actually felt a trace of pressure facing the aggressive Alice. What was this woman's problem?

She said she trusted him, yet Helena could feel obvious resentment, and that hostility seemed vaguely directed at her.

You lowly humans, think being a Mithril adventurer makes you special?

Show some sense, would you? Does she really think I'm afraid of her?

Does she genuinely think she's the Demon Lord's wife? Who on earth would承认!

Helena maintained a polite smile on her face while growing increasingly annoyed at the human woman before her.

"I completely understand. I'm Merlin's wife. Do you really know him better than I do?"

Alice suppressed her inner anger and used cold words to subtly put Helena in her place, making it clear who the real wife was.

Heheh! I won't get angry here—that would only give this fox-spirit an opening.

Once Helena sees that my bond with Merlin is unbreakable, she'll surely back off and stop harassing him.

Looking at the fury hidden deep in her eyes, it was clear she was losing her composure because she couldn't find a way in. Trust really is the most important element in maintaining a marriage.

I'm so brilliant. Merlin must be shocked by my reaction—seeing how understanding I am, he'll surely feel ashamed and regret coming to this place.

Alice was very pleased with her strategy of winning through virtue, but over at Merlin's end, he wore a complicated expression and thought—

What the hell is this crazy woman babbling about?! She's claiming to be my wife, yet she won't explain that we're only married in name. Does she want people to misunderstand us?!

"That's not true, I certainly don't understand Mr. Merlin as well as you do," Helena replied with a forced smile, thinking—understand him? My lord Merlin is a demon monarch. This stupid human woman clearly has no idea. And here she is, smug in front of me. What's there to be proud of?

"As long as you know that for yourself. You keep saying I don't trust my husband, what exactly are you plotting? Are you trying to sow discord and destroy our relationship?" Alice said something full of hostility, as if testing the other woman's limits.

"Not at all, you're overthinking things." Helena's smile stiffened, and the muscle under her eye twitched—clearly a bit provoked by Alice's repeated taunts.

"I hope so. I trust my husband very much and rarely doubt him. When he just said he was chatting with you inside, I believed he didn't do anything strange. But don't explain things on his behalf, because explanations coming from your mouth would only make me suspect even more. After all, there's no room for a third person in the bond between Merlin and me." Alice spoke in a serious tone, clearly expressing her attitude—no one would come between her and Merlin.

Helena was also a woman, so she naturally understood the deeper meaning in Alice's words. She was clearly being rejected, which immediately annoyed her. She was just a lowly human, yet so possessive?! His Majesty Lucifer is one of the leaders of the demon race—how could he ever be willing to be restrained by a human woman!

Merlin, standing nearby, felt like he couldn't插话, but he吐槽ed internally—what is this woman talking nonsense about? When did our relationship become this good? Has she been living in a dream or what?

Hobbs, as an old hand, smelled the gunpowder in the air and sensed something was off. He couldn't resist walking over to Merlin and whispering, "Hey! Merlin! Aren't you going to say something to ease the atmosphere? It's getting too tense. If this continues, these two might actually fight over you."

"What does this have to do with me? Neither of them is someone close to me. They're suddenly at each other's throats, and even I find it weird!"

Merlin frowned and responded in a low voice, feeling a headache coming on.

Helena was Asmodeus's subordinate, a high-ranking great demon of the cadre level, and she held feelings of reverence toward Merlin.

Alice, as a former Hero, was Merlin's fake wife—she harbored romantic feelings for Merlin but had never expressed them outright.

In Merlin's eyes, these two fighting made no sense at all. There was absolutely no conflict of interest between them!

Hearing Merlin's indifferent remarks, Hobbs rolled his eyes. "Brother Merlin, you really are heartless. Haven't both of them fallen for your charms? Otherwise, why would they be competing here?"

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue, not wanting to explain. He thought—see, it'd be impossible to clarify anyway. In other people's eyes, I'm a heartless man who's playing both sides while sitting back and watching the show.

Both women stared at each other with cold expressions, and the atmosphere suddenly grew strange—creating a standoff with neither side willing to back down.

To pressure her opponent, Alice released a trace of her power, a demonstration of strength meant to let Helena know she was not someone to be trifled with.

Helena felt Alice's magical pressure at the peak of Saint-tier and paused for a moment, then was astonished by her strength.

Although Helena didn't believe she couldn't defeat Alice, that faint dragon aura did surprise her.

Because she was a fallen angel, Helena did not release pressure to counterattack and instead chose to endure it—all while thinking—

This woman... is she openly threatening me with force?

Showing me her strength through pressure, trying to make me back down?

Tch! If I weren't worried about exposing my identity, I'd tear this arrogant human to shreds!

Helena's expression darkened. She looked at Alice in silence, deciding it was best not to clash with this woman for now.

Alice secretly exhaled in relief, thinking the other woman had backed down and she had won. She happily walked over to Merlin and affectionately linked her arm with his.

"Darling, let's go home. It's already so late. There are all sorts of disreputable people here—you shouldn't hang around with them."

Hearing Alice's soft voice, Merlin immediately felt extremely uncomfortable, breaking out goosebumps all over. "...Act normal. Stop clinging to me."

"Let's go home together, do you hear me? I wondered when I woke up why you were gone. So you came here to mess around. You really are something. Our household is barely scraping by, and it doesn't stop you from enjoying yourself, does it?" Alice's expression darkened. Though she spoke quietly, her words were full of grievance.

"This..." Merlin felt tremendous pressure. He thought—he wasn't enjoying himself; it was Asmodeus's endless troubles. And at a time like this, he still managed to shift the blame. "It's all this old man Hobbs's fault. He always brings me to places like this. It's so indecent. We're not the same kind of people. I need to draw a clear line with him from now on!"

"Merlin..." Hobbs was so angry his nostrils smoked. He thought—Merlin is quick with his counter-accusations. Other people would cut themselves for their brothers, but this guy cuts his brothers for women!

"Enough. Let's go. I know you were persuaded by Hobbs, otherwise you wouldn't have come back here." Alice didn't want to stay any longer, so she pulled Merlin and led him away from the secret cabin.

Helena watched their retreating figures, and a deep sense of doubt rose in her heart. Something about the way Merlin treated his fake wife felt very wrong.

Why didn't Lord Merlin speak up for me just now?

Could a lowly human woman be more important to him than a fellow demon like me?

How strange... Could Lord Merlin have developed real feelings for this false wife?

This isn't a good sign...

Your Majesty Lucifer, please don't make a mistake on an issue of principle like this.

title: Chapter 20 — Dispute
content:
Chapter 20 — Dispute

Volume 14 · Chapter 20

At home.

Merlin and Alice had already returned, but the moment they walked through the door, they didn't look very close.

The atmosphere was as serious as a vice squad captain interrogating a suspect in an aborted prostitution case.

"Why did you go to a place like that? Can't you just tell me honestly now?" Alice sat on the couch, her expression stern and righteous.

".....," Merlin stood awkwardly on the opposite side, picking at his sword practice with his fingers, his mind racing on how to talk his way out of this.

Actually, Alice wasn't so dense that she couldn't see through things. She wasn't stupid enough to miss certain truths.

Earlier, in the secret room, the situation had been special, and Alice couldn't directly ask questions, so she had to keep her suspicions buried in her heart.

But now that they were back home, there was no need for such discomfort. Whatever needed to be said should be spoken face to face.

Alice felt this was much better. There wouldn't be any fox spirits helping Merlin talk his way out, or making excuses for him.

Merlin thought for a moment, putting on an awkward expression, "It was Hobbs, that guy forced me to go. You know that, I'm really not that interested in places like that."

"Come on, don't lie to me. Do you think I'm blind? I didn't notice you throwing dirt on Hobbs?" Alice pouted, growing more displeased as Merlin stubbornly stuck to his story.

"Am I the kind of person who throws dirt on others?" Merlin broke into a cold sweat, his guilt obvious.

"Looking at how angry Hobbs was, I know he didn't kidnap you. It was clearly you who went to the secret room on your own. Alice saw right through Merlin's mask without any courtesy."

".....," Merlin avoided her gaze, thinking to himself, Alice's tricks are getting more and more clever. Back outside, she was completely fine, but once home, she started making a scene.

"What reason do you have for going there? I've already warned you multiple times not to go to such places." Alice's face turned sulky, wanting to see how Merlin would react.

"Actually, I had something to discuss with Miss Helena." Merlin casually sat down next to Alice, not knowing what schemes were brewing in his mind.

"What is it?" Alice asked in an unfriendly tone.

"It's... well, there have been rumors lately that Miss Helena is a fallen angel, and she's been feeling troubled by it." Merlin deflected the topic.

Alice thought about it, and it did sound familiar, so she curiously asked, "Is Miss Helena really a fallen angel? You're a demon, you should be able to tell who your own kind is, right?"

Merlin glanced at Alice, thinking, Women are like that, you never know what they're thinking. If I admit the truth, who knows if Alice will take action against Helena.

"No, Miss Helena is a genuine human being. I'm a former Great Demon Lord, and I can't sense any demonic aura from her."

Alice withdrew her gaze.

"That's strange then. Who's been spreading rumors behind our backs?"

"I don't know." Merlin played dumb.

"Then why did Miss Helena go to you for her headache? You're not a priest, are you going to cure headaches?" Alice looked very skeptical.

"Headaches are mental issues, so I just chatted with her to relieve stress. It's that simple." Merlin waved his hands dismissively.

"There are so many people who admire her in secret, why is it only you who gets special treatment? I've never seen you and Helena interact before. When did you two get so close?" Alice's tone was dripping with jealousy, clearly her little jealous heart had been knocked over.

"Maybe Miss Helena was charmed by my handsome appearance? After all, she was very kind to me when we first met." Merlin stroked his chin.

"Just you? You don't even have a trace of masculinity. Who would look at you? Maybe she has some unspeakable secret and is just using you!" Alice couldn't stand seeing Merlin so self-satisfied, so she poured a bucket of cold water on him.

"Not really. Today, Miss Helena said she really likes my tall and strong figure~" Merlin raised his eyebrows provocatively.

"Huh? Did she really say that?" Alice was taken aback.

"Of course she did. Miss Helena really admires me." Merlin seemed to be deliberately provoking Alice, otherwise this annoying woman would always stand on her moral high ground and criticize him.

Alice's face gradually flushed red with anger. She suddenly felt a sense of crisis. She had never openly praised Merlin before, while Helena expressed her admiration without any restraint.

This kind of situation was bound to make Alice anxious. Even though she knew Merlin had his good points, she had never said it out loud, always picking at his flaws instead.

Compared to that, Alice was clearly at a disadvantage. Obviously, a girl like Helena who could praise others was more likable.

No wonder Merlin ignored her warnings and went to the secret room. It seemed she was partly to blame.

Alice thought this in her heart, but she wouldn't say it so honestly out loud.

"You! Don't you dare go to the secret room again, and don't you dare see that Helena!"

Merlin stuck out his tongue, leaning back against the couch with a provocative tone, "What? Am I not free to go wherever I want? Aren't you controlling me too much?"

"I don't care! If I say no, then it's a no!" Alice was so angry she stomped her feet, her cheeks puffed out like they were about to explode, "You go to such places, seeing unsavory people, have you thought about my feelings?"

"I've recently realized you're being a bit too much. We're just fake spouses, sticking together only to get through hard times, but you're controlling me too much, aren't you?" Merlin put on a serious face, trying to give Alice a good lecture. "For some trivial matters, I can compromise, but freedom is my bottom line. Don't push it too far."

"You!" Alice was so angry her body trembled, and she couldn't help but kick Merlin off the couch.

"What the hell! Are you rebelling?" Merlin scowled, feeling that Alice had been getting more and more unruly since she got close to that person.

"I'm hungry! Go cook! It's your turn today!" Alice tried various ways to suppress Merlin.

"I'm not going! What are you going to do?" Merlin stood up, putting on an air of stubborn determination.

Alice's eyes were red, looking like she was about to cry, and she stormed off to her room in a rage, "Hmph! Cheap bastard!"

"Come on!" Merlin grumbled in annoyance, watching Alice's tightly closed door, "Who are you calling cheap? Bitch!"

The two had argued and fallen into a cold war.

However, this kind of argument wasn't a big deal.

Because the frequency of Merlin and Alice's fights was as common as seeing flies every day.

Basically, there was one every day, and they had long since become used to it.

Approaching midnight, neither of them had eaten dinner. In their cold war state, neither was willing to take the initiative to lower their pride and cook.

This led to both of them going hungry, neither willing to give in to the other, stuck in a stalemate.

However, Merlin was still quite hungry. At midnight, driven by hunger, he walked to the kitchen to prepare something to eat.

Merlin had already prepared the ingredients, originally planning to make a single serving of late-night snacks. But seeing Alice's tightly closed door, he remembered this annoying woman still hadn't made up yet, and thought, SF light novel.

This woman is really hot-tempered. Can't she change a little?

I went to a brothel, and this is the big deal?

Is there a problem with me going to the secret room?

It's really overreacting. Although I'm a bit to blame, it's only a little.

Merlin thought about it, and silently prepared ingredients for two people, even though he cursed Alice a lot, his body was honest enough to prepare a two-person portion of late-night snacks.

"I really owed her in my previous life!"

Merlin placed the ingredients on the cutting board, about to turn around to get the knife, when he suddenly saw Alice in a white nightgown, holding a knife, standing in the kitchen doorway with a dark face.

It was deep night, with dim candlelight casting a gloomy glow. A disheveled woman holding a knife stood right in front of you. Would you be scared or not?

Merlin's heart pounded violently, recalling all sorts of terrifying scenes, and he stammered, "Y-You... what are you going to do? Don't seek death, you can't beat me!"

Alice said nothing, didn't respond to Merlin, and directly walked past him to start handling the ingredients.

The kitchen was silent, except for the dull thud of Alice cutting ingredients, very heavy and quiet.

Merlin couldn't understand Alice at all, wondering what she was up to. Suddenly coming out of the room, what was the meaning of this?

"Stop staring and get to work. Wash the vegetables." Alice pushed a basket of potatoes to Merlin, her face showing no emotion at all, cold and indifferent.

Merlin took the potatoes and looked at Alice curiously, "What's the meaning of coming out suddenly? Not angry anymore?"

"I'm just here to help you." Alice's hands never stopped cutting.

Merlin narrowed his eyes and made a judgment based on his own situation,

Is it that you're hungry too?

"I'm not hungry." As soon as Alice finished speaking, her stomach let out an embarrassingly loud rumble, grumbling...

"Ha, of course. Your stomach is rumbling, isn't it? Your body is much more honest than your mouth." Merlin wore a mocking smile.

"You're so annoying! I'm not hungry at all! It's just... I drank too much water!" Alice blushed, covering her stomach and desperately explaining, completely ignoring how weak her excuse was.

This little brat.

"Come on, come on. Drinking too much water makes your stomach rumble. Awesome~" Merlin gave a thumbs up.

"Hmph!" Alice rolled her eyes, not paying attention to Merlin's sarcasm.

The two fell silent, each busy with their own tasks. Since they were doing the same thing, the atmosphere gradually relaxed.

"Helena... what is it about her that attracts you?" Alice suddenly asked.

"Let me think..." Merlin crossed his arms and pondered for a moment, "Miss Helena is very gentle, speaks beautifully, is very understanding. In short, all feminine beauty is displayed on her."

Alice's chopping motion paused slightly, seeming not in a good mood, muttering, "What's so hard about that? I can do it too."

"Huh? What did you say?" Merlin frowned in surprise.

"...I said I can also be gentle. What's so hard about that? I don't want Helena to have such a thick face, pretending to act like what men like. It's really fake." Alice said angrily, then blushed and whispered,

"But if you like, I can change, become a little... slightly gentle, so you won't have to go to such places anymore?"

Merlin was stunned.

This woman would change herself for me. I can't believe my own ears!

Merlin felt a strange sensation inside, realizing he needed to say something.

"No need to change yourself. I think you're fine just the way you are. Miss Helena may be very attractive, but she's not very genuine. That mask of hers is too perfect."

"Is... is that so..." Alice's mood lightened, hearing Merlin's words and not feeling angry anymore.

"Besides, if you two are together, I would definitely choose you. Compared to her, I think you're more reliable." Merlin said seriously.

"Huh?" Alice was taken aback, almost dropping her knife in excitement, her face flushing red at an visible speed.

"Don't... don't think that just saying nice things will make me forgive you!"

"I'm not happy at all! Not in the slightest!"

title: Chapter 21 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter (Heading Straight for France)
content:
Chapter 21 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter (Heading Straight for France)

Volume 14 · Chapter 21

The three-day deadline had arrived.

According to the original agreement, Da Vinci should have had results by now.

Merlin and Alice were both eager to find information about Dracula in that ancient diary.

So the two of them came to the library in Wrexham full of anticipation, intending to hear the conclusions from Da Vinci's three-day investigation.

However, just as Merlin and Alice's expectations were at their highest, they received such a disappointing reply—

"I've already translated the entire diary. The conclusion is... there's very little information about Dracula. It does mention him, but only three times."

Upon hearing Da Vinci's somewhat pessimistic reply, Merlin and Alice's expectations instantly dropped by half. They felt that what Da Vinci meant was that there were almost no useful clues.

Merlin was feeling a bit irritable and anxious. He had waited so long, yet the result was so meager.

Had these past few days been nothing but wasted waiting, squandering his precious life!?

"Miss Da Vinci, does it not mention Dracula's whereabouts?"

"No," Da Vinci shook her head, not hiding anything. "This diary is the action log of a vampire hunter. From it, I learned about events from hundreds of years ago—the brutal struggle between the hunters and the vampire race, the entire ancient Francia was plunged into terror. The diary's owner hunted many vampires throughout his life and gave his life to save his kingdom, but he may not have fulfilled his wish, which is quite regrettable. The last page of the diary records his greatest regret in life: failing to completely eradicate the vampire threat."

Alice listened and it felt like a magnificent epic—a person with great ambitions, yet a tragic story of not meeting a good end.

Merlin wasn't as sentimental as Alice and pressed on with the practical matter. "Then what exactly were those three mentions of Dracula about?"

"The first mention says that hundreds of years ago, Francia was controlled by a man, and the royal family became puppets. That man was the legendary Dracula."

"The second mention describes a powerful hunter who successfully cornered Dracula and they perished together, but Dracula didn't die—instead, he fell into a deep slumber and was sealed away."

"The third mention says that other vampires hid Dracula's body and drew a map, hoping Dracula would recover and rebuild the vampire dynasty."

Da Vinci spoke fluently and concisely, laying out all three mentions of Dracula. Indeed, there was nothing explicitly stating Dracula's whereabouts, which put the matter in a stalemate.

That powerful hunter—there was no need to think about it, it was almost certainly Arnold's ancestor. The drawn map could basically be confirmed as the stolen relic treasure map.

Everything at this moment seemed to have returned to square one, making people feel extremely frustrated, as if all their efforts had been wasted for nothing.

Merlin rubbed his temples. Now all the clues had been completely severed—where was he supposed to find this Dracula?

They'd been busy for over a month, and this mission was probably going to come to naught—all their efforts would come to nothing!

Merlin was someone who intensely disliked having no results. One could imagine how terrible his mood was at this moment.

Alice looked at Merlin beside her, equally unwilling to accept this, feeling quite lost about what to do next.

Rosetti saw these two in such low spirits and felt somewhat unable to bear it. "Alright, no need to be so depressed. If worst comes to worst, just take on a different mission. Are you really going to stubbornly pursue this Dracula matter to the end?"

"Rosetti, don't speak so lightly. Since you're so open-minded about this, then lend me money—I need to pay rent, water bills, property fees, sanitation charges..." Alice muttered, sounding almost like she was chanting sutras.

"Stop, stop, stop! Let's talk about something practical—today's weather is quite nice." Rosetti quickly deflected, not wanting to get into these headache-inducing topics with Alice.

"Since you're so determined to continue with this mission, there actually is another way." Da Vinci suddenly changed direction, bringing a turning point to the whole situation.

"Wah... Miss Da Vinci still has a solution?!" Merlin suddenly sat up straight, thinking that this unassuming-looking girl was full of surprises!

"There is a way, but I can't guarantee my method will definitely lead you to the legendary Dracula. But it's worth trying," Da Vinci said noncommittally, seemingly not very confident in her own idea.

"Miss Da Vinci, please don't feel burdened. If there's a chance of finding Dracula, we're willing to try," Alice said eagerly.

"Then let me say—" Da Vinci paused, speaking seriously. "This diary records the catastrophe that ancient Francia suffered over a hundred years ago, with various vampires interspersed throughout. Almost all the events took place within the territory of the French Empire. So I'm thinking... shouldn't you go to France to have a look? A thorough investigation might yield new clues."

Merlin and Alice exchanged glances, both seeing doubt in each other's eyes—neither was particularly confident about this suggestion.

The reason was simple: France was such a vast place, and finding clues about Dracula there would be like searching for a needle in a haystack—the difficulty was beyond ordinary.

In a foreign land where they knew nothing of the circumstances, Merlin and Alice might become completely lost, having no idea where to even begin.

"Miss Da Vinci, isn't this approach somewhat impractical? France is also one of the leading nations in the human empire. Without any guidance, we'd need to find clues there, but the scope is too vast," Alice said honestly. This suggestion didn't really suit their situation.

"Although the difficulty is great, it is indeed worth attempting. The legendary vampire race possesses incredibly tenacious vitality. With their unparalleled self-healing abilities, their lifespan approaches immortality. A few hundred years to them might be merely a fleeting moment. If those legends are true, I believe the vampire race hasn't left the land of France—they exist in small numbers, living in shadows, waiting for Dracula's awakening. So going to France is not wrong," Da Vinci said with sound reasoning.

"But the scope of investigation is vast, and our energy is limited," Merlin emphasized.

"Actually, the scope can be narrowed. You should know that many legendary stories have real-world counterparts. If examined closely, you'll discover secrets that are deeply unsettling," Da Vinci paused, speaking in a didactic tone. "In France, there is an extremely traditional funeral custom where the deceased's family drives silver nails into the heart to prevent the dead from becoming vampires and harming the living. This is the earliest recorded method of dealing with vampires. However, this funeral tradition originated in France's Glen Plains, and they still maintain it to this day. I think when you arrive there, you will find something valuable."

After hearing Da Vinci's words, Merlin and Alice exchanged glances and secretly began discussing—

"Go to France?"

"We seem to have no other choice either."
