title: Chapter 22 — The True Strong
content:
Chapter 22 — The True Strong

Volume 14 · Chapter 22

The next day.

Alice was busy preparing her things at home; tomorrow she would set off for the unfamiliar country of France.

The two didn't really have many good options, so they could only listen to Da Vinci's advice and go to the Garon Plains in France to take a look.

This was the first time the two were heading to a relatively distant foreign land to carry out a mission, so they still lacked much experience in many matters.

Fortunately, Alice had consulted Mr. Karl about what to keep in mind when traveling, and had also worked out a series of plans to ensure this trip wouldn't cause any inexplicable trouble.

Mr. Karl was well-known and often left Britain to take on missions; he was truly experienced. When he heard that Alice and Merlin were heading to France, he was quite surprised in his heart.

As a senior, Mr. Karl didn't press for details. Instead, he specially pointed out some important things, to prevent Merlin and Alice from making mistakes, and urged them not to easily trust anyone while abroad—even when dealing with fellow adventurers, they should be cautious and maintain their own judgment, not blindly believing others.

Mr. Karl was being so careful for good reason, after all, people's hearts are hard to read, and one can't fully trust others.

Abroad, not being from that country, many local residents would resort to deception, hoping to get some money from foreigners.

As for traveling companions who were adventurers, there were even precedents of them coveting each other's rewards and killing or robbing one another—it was very unsafe.

Therefore, adventurers traveling together would never ask each other about their missions, which seemed extremely impolite; in severe cases, the other party might think you had ill intentions.

Although Mr. Karl's advice was somewhat clichéd, it was still very important for Merlin and Alice, especially since this was their first time handling affairs in a foreign land.

Novel (??ω?? ?)

Alice was busy preparing all sorts of things at home, while Merlin had nothing to do, so he dumped all the tasks onto Alice, and instead went off to chat with Hobbes.

"Hobbes, what a coincidence yesterday, didn't expect to run into you at the secret hideout~" Merlin said with a broad smile, instinctively reaching toward Hobbes's wine cup, trying to get a free drink.

"Isn't that right? The world is really small." Hobbes chuckled, pulling his wine cup close, not letting Merlin touch it at all.

Merlin felt very uncomfortable, sensing that Hobbes was on guard against him. "Ugh! Why are you so stingy? Let me have a sip, it won't—"

"No, no, no. My good friend Merlin is a distinguished figure, he wouldn't sully himself by drinking with someone like me. I understand." Hobbes said with a meaningful tone.

"Yesterday was a special case, wasn't it? If it weren't for Alice being there, I'd never have said those things." Merlin paused, feeling awkward, and continued, "Actually, Alice already knows, my trying to throw dirt on you is pointless."

"Oh~ So you mean throwing dirt was pointless, and I got shot for nothing?" Hobbes frowned, feeling that Merlin had sold out his teammate at a crucial moment. Although he himself had a habit of selling out teammates, Merlin's performance this time was truly beyond compare.

"It wasn't for nothing yesterday. I owe you one for being there, otherwise I wouldn't have known how to back down. I'll remember this favor." Merlin put on an act of being loyal and righteous. If there were a second time, he would definitely continue selling out Hobbes without hesitation.

"Cut the crap, Merlin. I see right through you. You talk big about brotherhood, but the moment you see a woman, you're done for. This is really shameless of you." Hobbes said with a face full of resentment.

"......Merlin was embarrassed, spreading his hands and sighing helplessly, "I don't have a choice either. You saw it yesterday—Alice suddenly rushed over, fierce and ready to chop heads. If I didn't act that way, what if she made a scene right there? It's not easy for me either, you should understand. If you ever get caught by your wife, I'm willing to take the blame for you."

"That's what you say, but I never forced you." Hobbes's attitude relaxed a bit, feeling this was acceptable, after all, he couldn't let himself suffer in vain.

"I said it, and I won't take it back." Merlin smiled and grabbed Hobbes's wine cup this time without any resistance.

"Honestly." Hobbes crossed his arms, his brow furrowed as he said, "You nearly drove me crazy yesterday. You didn't take me to the secret hideout, yet you accused me of kidnapping. Didn't you see Alice's expression? She looked like she wanted to tear me apart limb from limb."

"That's not true. Alice may have a bad temper, but she's not unreasonable." Merlin comforted Hobbes with a sentence.

"Yesterday you were cowering like a mouse, and now you're even helping Alice speak well of me. Does that mean something good happened last night?" Hobbes's expression turned sly, full of implication.

"What are you imagining? Nothing happened." Merlin explained with a sentence.

"Speaking of which, are you really together with Miss Helena?" Hobbes asked curiously, being very interested in such matters.

"No, we're just friends. Yesterday we only had a casual chat." Merlin answered with a hint of annoyance, having strong objections to the word "together" coming out of Hobbes's mouth.

"Don't pretend. I've never seen Miss Helena willing to be alone with anyone. You're the first." Hobbes looked around to make sure no one was nearby, then leaned close to Merlin and asked in a low voice, "To be honest, what underhanded trick did you use to make Miss Helena fall for you? Friends should be straightforward~"

Merlin pushed Hobbes away, speaking with righteous indignation, "Disgusting! Vulgar! In your eyes, there's no such thing as pure friendship between men and women?"

"That's exactly right." Hobbes said seriously with a full face.

Such a realistic response left Merlin speechless for a moment, and he suddenly didn't feel like chatting with Hobbes anymore. His values were too different.

Just then, Mr. Karl walked over, interrupting their whispered conversation.

"Merlin, I heard from Alice that you're setting off for France tomorrow?" Mr. Karl pulled up a chair and sat down at Merlin's table.

"Huh? Merlin, you're going to France? For what?" Hobbes was surprised, not even knowing about this yet.

"I need to go deal with a troublesome mission, so Alice and I have to make a trip." Merlin gave a brief explanation.

"I forgot to consider that yesterday. You two are going to a foreign land for the first time to carry out a mission, and you'll definitely encounter many things you don't understand. Being strangers in a strange land, if you don't have someone to guide you, it'll be really troublesome." Mr. Karl took out a letter from his pocket and placed it in front of Merlin. "This is a letter of introduction. Once you arrive in France, go directly to the Karswell Branch of the Guild and find Mr. Arcanum. He's a friend of mine. I once saved his life, and he's a trustworthy partner. If you encounter any problems, you can first go ask him."

"Mr. Arcanum?" Merlin took the letter of introduction, thinking it might be useful, and since it was someone's kindness, he smiled and accepted it. "Thank you, Mr. Karl."

"No need to thank me, this is nothing. If you two encounter any difficulties, just say the word. The guild will help as much as they can." Mr. Karl laughed heartily.

"Merlin, you're riding on Alice's coattails to take off~" Hobbes patted Merlin's shoulder.

"Shut up! Who's riding whose coattails?" Merlin rolled his eyes, feeling annoyed.

"Karl, this name Arcanum sounds somewhat familiar? Who is he?" Hobbes stroked his beard and thought.

"It's that French Iron Will Emperor! He completed 9,999,999 low-level commissions and at the age of 102 successfully advanced from Black Iron to Silver Adventurer!" Mr. Karl said with great admiration.

"Could it really be him?!"

Merlin exclaimed in surprise. He had heard about this legendary figure's glorious deeds since the very beginning—he was explosively powerful!

He looked at the Black Iron Adventurer's certificate hanging on his neck and suddenly felt ashamed of himself. Compared to Arcanum, he was incredibly weak!

So Merlin quickly took out the letter of introduction, his expression solemn, and in his heart, he worshiped and admired him.

MD, this Mr. Arcanum is the real strong one!

However, the facts weren't what the two imagined. France wasn't very beautiful, more like a malformed freak.

Except for the imperial capital Paris, which symbolized royal authority, everywhere else was dilapidated, as if washed by war, and hungry refugees were visible everywhere.

If Merlin and Alice hadn't seen all this with their own eyes, probably few would believe that across a sea strait, the gap between countries could be so large.

It seems many things need to be seen with one's own eyes, rather than just based on one's guesses....

After Merlin and Alice were ready, they could set off for France.

They departed from the Bristol port of Britain, boarding a trade ship crossing the strait, arriving at Montoir port in France and disembarking.

The two carried their luggage and walked straight ahead. The plan was first to find Mr. Akalón introduced by Karl as a guide, then proceed to investigate the Glenn Plains.

Merlin and Alice carried their luggage, looking at the scene before them. - Time and mood were a bit strange, and they didn't speak.

"Alice, don't people say France is a country that can compare with Britain? Why do I feel like I've arrived in a slum?" Merlin said expressionlessly, the gap between hope and reality making his mood not good.

"I don't know either. Logically, places with ports should be more prosperous, but here emmm.... Alice was speechless, feeling greatly deceived.

In front of the two of them wasn't particularly prosperous. Old, dilapidated houses were visible everywhere, intersecting in ugly ways, coupled with hungry refugees visible everywhere on the streets. It was truly a large slum.

"Perhaps only this place is particularly special? Other places might be a bit better." Alice concluded, thinking one shouldn't generalize just based on the scene before one's eyes.

As if, let's go, our first stop is Xiao Niu Town.

title: Chapter 2 — Hunger
content:
Chapter 2 — Hunger

Volume 15 · Chapter 2

Merlin stopped in his tracks, carrying Alice, who was looking back restlessly, wanting to find the person who had just brushed past him.

Here in a foreign land, running into a fellow demon was already quite rare.

However, just now, Merlin felt that the demon's strength was not weak; he belonged to the level of a Demon Lord.

This left Merlin quite puzzled. Powerful demons walking through human territory—no matter how one thought about it, it was a very dangerous thing.

However, after turning back and searching for a while, Merlin also didn't find the trace of the mysterious person in the brown robe who had just passed by him; it was as if he had vanished in the blink of an eye.

Alice had walked a long distance, muttering to herself, before she noticed that Merlin hadn't followed her, and she wondered if something had happened.

So Alice put away the map of France and ran back, asking Merlin.

"What's wrong, Merlin? Did something happen?"

"Just now, well... no, it's nothing, maybe it was my illusion."

Merlin looked like he wanted to say something but stopped, and ultimately didn't say what had just happened.

He suspected that he might have been mistaken; maybe he had wrongly taken someone for a demon?

Thinking about it—it was unlikely that a Demon Lord-level guy would be running around outside.

Merlin turned his head and, still carrying Alice, walked forward, muttering about what was to come.

"Let's go quickly, let's go rent a comfortable carriage to Xiao Niu Town."

"We need to save money; our funds aren't plenty, so renting one that's decent enough is fine."

"You guys are really stingy with yourselves; clearly, just now you almost gave all your belongings to the refugees...."...

In a certain alley where refugees were concentrated.

The mysterious person who had just brushed past Merlin arrived here, his steps unsteady.

He wore a brown robe that looked extremely worn, perfectly blending in with the surrounding refugees.

The mysterious person clutched his stomach, walking slowly and leisurely on the streets of the alley, looking extremely fatigued and hungry.

Under the low hood, there was a pale, thin, decadent face, like a skeleton.

It turned out that this mysterious person was the Demon Lord of Gluttony, Belial!

Belial, having learned from Asmodeus that Merlin was unwilling to help find the whereabouts of his sister, suddenly felt very disappointed.

So, having no other choice, Belial had to take matters into his own hands, leaving the Fifth Demon Lord Palace to search for the whereabouts of his sister, Miranda.

Belial and Merlin were about the same; both had just arrived at the port of this France.

The difference was that Merlin had come legally, but Belial, lacking identity, had stowed away across the sea.

Belial had drifted at sea for five days and five nights before successfully arriving in France; along the way, he suffered quite a bit. It was only after much difficulty that he arrived here.

So Belial made himself look like a refugee; it was all due to the hardships of the journey. Otherwise, how could a demon who was one of the Seven Main Lords end up mingling with refugees?

Belial currently had no clues at all about his sister's whereabouts, but he still had some ideas.

He planned to investigate the entire slave trade in France; after all, his sister had been kidnapped, and she would definitely be sold for profit. After all, his sister was so cute; anyone would find it hard to resist her charm.

However, there was yet another important problem troubling Belial right now; he was extremely hungry now, to the point where anyone looked like food.

Although Belial looked very thin, he was, after all, the Demon Lord of Gluttony; his appetite was incredibly huge. Even if he ate all the humans in an entire country, it probably wouldn't let him feel satisfied.

Belial was like a cursed demon; he always lived in hunger. No matter how much he ate, he would never feel satisfied; he would only get hungrier and become more and more crazy.

Sometimes, when Belial's hunger was unbearable, he would direct his gaze toward fellow demons, also wanting to eat them.

This was also why many demons were unwilling to go to the Fifth Demon Lord Palace; they were afraid that one day Belial would go crazy and eat them.

Up to now, many demons had been eaten; it was already impossible to count carefully.

Belial was the Demon Lord who liked his subordinates making mistakes the most, because that gave him a reason to eat the mistaken subordinates and fill his stomach.

Not only that, but the demon execution ground was set up in the Fifth Demon Lord Palace; all demons who made mistakes would be sent there, and at night they would become Belial's dinner.

However, Belial knew that eating fellow demons was not good, and he was very restrained; unless he was hungry to the point of unbearableness, he wouldn't eat fellow demons.

The fact that Belial always survives in hunger made all the demons feel fear, let alone the France in front of him, where such things were everywhere.

"So hungry.

"I can barely hold it anymore.

"What should we do? Should we just catch some lowly humans to eat...."...

Belial's eyes flickered with green light, looking around at the humans coming and going, inadvertently drooling.

This place is simply a heaven!

Meat everywhere on the move.

A few days later.

Merlin and Alice had already moved far from the port.

The two of them had rented a carriage and went directly to Xiao Niu Town.

After a few days of traveling, the two were not far from Xiao Niu Town; it was estimated that they would arrive soon.

However, there was one thing that made both of them puzzled; they had initially thought that only at the port would there be many such people.

But the result was not the case; it was all over France. Walking on the road, one could almost see them everywhere.

Many refugees were fleeing with their families toward more safe and affluent places.

So Merlin and Alice, sitting in the carriage, saw many refugees carrying their families heading north along the way.

This was obviously not a single case; it was indeed that France had some problems, otherwise how could so many refugees come out?

Just by chance, the carriage driver they hired was a local; they could ask about the situation.

Merlin patted the back of the driver in front, curiously asking, "Old brother, we heard that France is a good place; why does it feel a bit off after coming here? There are refugees everywhere, and they look very miserable."

"You don't know; recently in the south, a flood just happened; many farmlands were washed away, and these people are all farmers. With the farmlands destroyed, they can only leave their hometowns." The driver said helplessly.

"A flood?" Merlin touched his chin, thinking that made sense. No wonder there were so many refugees; it turned out that their homes were destroyed; that was truly pitiful.

"If a flood happened, so many refugees leaving their homes, does the King of France not manage it? At the very least, relief and resettlement for these people should be done," Alice suddenly asked in doubt, feeling that so many people wandering everywhere was a problem for public security, yet no one was managing it, which was very strange.

"Adventurer, you really don't know," the driver said, seeing the silver proof of adventurer on Alice's neck, and speaking very respectfully, quite different from his attitude toward Merlin.

"The King simply doesn't care about the life and death of these refugees; he would rather they all died."

"That way he can save a large sum of money to enjoy himself, instead of relieving those dirty refugees."

"I'll just put it plainly; actually, France is already finished now...."

title: Chapter 3 — Legend of Akaron (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 3 — Legend of Akaron (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 15 · Chapter 3

Hearing the driver make such blunt remarks, Merlin and Alice were both a bit stunned.

What had happened to France? A mere carriage driver was casually saying the Empire was already done for.

What terrible situation had pushed a commoner to blurt out words like that?

"Why do you say France is finished?" Alice said, slightly exasperated, not quite understanding.

"The old king of France is aged, his mind isn't clear anymore, and he's showing symptoms of dementia. He hasn't governed the country for a long time, handing it over to some outsider. The only heir to the Empire, Princess Margaret, spends her days wandering around doing nothing, never bothering to look at how chaotic the Empire has become. Adventurer, don't you think France has no hope?" The driver turned around to ask, his eyes full of sorrow and indignation.

"This..." Alice's expression turned awkward. It was pretty bad, but were the royal family of this country all weirdos?

"The old king only has one daughter. We all thought France would welcome its first queen, that Princess Margaret would inherit the throne. But now it seems almost impossible," the driver said, shaking his head helplessly.

Merlin stayed completely silent beside him, thinking so that was how it was. Then Alice and he had come to France at the worst possible time — right in the middle of political turmoil.

"Why has it become like this?" Alice asked, puzzled. She figured France was at least one of the major human nations. No matter what, surely they wouldn't just let things fall apart like this?

"Everything turned out this way after the new prime minister, Medes, took office." The driver guided the carriage and carefully chose his words. "Medes bribed officials with power and influence, and used sweet words on the old king, until he finally obtained the position of prime minister. But after he came to power, he revealed his greedy nature. He unauthorizedly seized a huge amount of the Empire's assets, causing the country to not even have money for disaster relief now. Refugees are leaving their homes in large numbers..."

"France is in such chaos now, doesn't the old king know about it?" Merlin asked lightly.

"He doesn't. The old king's health is poor. He contracted a serious illness long ago, and it's gotten worse in recent years. He hasn't appeared in public for a long time, remaining in the palace to recover." The driver answered with certainty.

"Huh? How could this be?" Alice was taken aback and found it hard to believe. Her own country was in this state, and the ruler of France didn't even know!?

"Medes, this cunning guy, taking advantage of the old king's illness, has been running rampant. He's blocked off all information so that no one except himself can see the old king — not even Princess Margaret has that right. He claims it's all for His Majesty's safety. Pfft! He obviously wants to become the ruler of the Empire indirectly, usurping power!" The driver grumbled discontentedly and continued, "Medes tells the old king every day how prosperous France is, how peaceful the Empire is, keeping the king living in the lies he's constructed. The king probably doesn't even know France has fallen into chaos right now."

"If it's like that, why hasn't anyone rebelled? That's so strange!" Alice felt that with so many refugees, couldn't they unite and resist? Were they really that easy to bully?!

"Some have rebelled. They even formed groups and went to the capital to march, demanding to see the king..." The driver said softly, his expression becoming unnatural.

"And then?" Alice pressed.

"They're all dead. Not a single rebel came back alive. They were all arrested and tortured to death in prison. Who would dare continue to resist?" the driver said without turning around, his heart full of bitterness.

Merlin raised an eyebrow, thinking what a violent approach. If you can't solve the problem, just eliminate the person raising it. How simple and crude.

"So I say, this country is already finished. Everyone with a bit of wealth is in a hurry to leave their homeland. No matter how bad a foreign land is, it's still better than staying here and perishing along with France." The driver said helplessly, filled with a sense of powerlessness.

Alice secretly glanced at Merlin, her expression somewhat complicated, as if she had something she wanted to say.

"What are you up to? I'm telling you not to meddle in other people's affairs. Whatever mess you get into has nothing to do with me," Merlin immediately put on an indifferent attitude,生怕 Alice was about to beg him to give her a ride the next moment.

"I haven't even said anything yet, what's with that attitude of yours?" Alice rolled her eyes.

"Is there a problem with my attitude? Compared to someone like you who goes looking for trouble everywhere, I'm clearly more reliable than you, right?" Merlin frowned, thinking sure enough his guess was correct — Alice was indeed planning to do something troubling, and she just wanted to pull him into it.

"You know I'm going to cause trouble before I even open my mouth? Can you read minds?" Alice glared at Merlin, puffed up with anger.

"Given you? The moment your mouth opens, I'll immediately know what kind of nonsense you're about to spout." Merlin said something particularly vulgar.

"Can you keep your language clean? You're so disgusting." Alice's forehead vein throbbed.

"Alright, alright, I'm just advising you to save your energy. Don't go meddling in this kind of business. The two of us aren't living in France anyway. No matter how big of an issue happens here, it has nothing to do with us. It can't affect either of us at all. So don't go looking for trouble, okay?" Merlin's tone was reasonably sincere.

"..." Alice fell silent, hesitating. "But we happened to run into this. If we don't do anything, I'll feel guilty."

Merlin paused, thinking Alice this girl... Could she be a reincarnation of the Goddess of Light?

She has to meddle in every unjust thing she sees? Can she calm down a little?

Merlin was at a loss for Alice's personality, suspecting maybe some wire in her brain was crossed.

"Alice, we still have other missions right now. Don't get卷入 into messy affairs. France is a major country. If there are problems, solutions will always be found. You and I are just adventurers, not saviors. Please be calm." Merlin said seriously, figuring he'd already received warnings about his Heart Curse, so it would be better to focus on scouting Saint-tier prey these days. What business did he have saving France? None whatsoever!

Merlin's words weren't without reason. Right now it was still...

"I understand..." Alice pouted and stopped talking. She looked at the pitiful sight of those refugees, and her heart still felt very uncomfortable.

But her own matters were more important. Still...

At sunset. In Ox Town, they were preparing to go to the guild to find Mr. Ackarlon.

Merlin and Alice finally arrived in the small town after getting off the carriage, looking at Ox Town before them.

After paying the driver, the two of them grabbed their luggage, far from the center of France.

Ox Town was actually not very large. It was a small town positioned somewhat centrally, appearing extremely harmonious.

It gave people a feeling of... "Let's go find that person named Ackarlon." Alice looked at Merlin beside her.

"This is the place. Let's go in first."

Merlin said with a face full of admiration, small stars twinkling in his eyes.

"Right, let's go see my idol first." Alice furrowed her delicate brows, unable to understand Merlin's peculiar behavior.

"Huh? What idol?" She was like a devout believer, gripping the black iron adventurer's certification around her neck.

"What do you know?" Merlin breathed out. "Ackarlon is the only adventurer who progressed from black iron to silver without relying on combat strength. Someone who can complete 9,999 low-level quests in a row — a person with such patience can't possibly be ordinary."

"With a weak physique, completing countless quests... He is the model and example for all of us black iron noobs~"

"Ah! The legendary Ackarlon~" (●°▼°●)+

title: Chapter 4 — Workshop-like Guild
content:
Chapter 4 — Workshop-like Guild

Volume 15 · Chapter 4

“Uh… Alice felt a strange sensation in her heart seeing [someone] so excited. ‘Is it really necessary? He’s just a Silver adventurer? I’m a Mithril adventurer, and I haven’t seen you worship me like this.’”

“Why would I worship you? Are you crazy?” Merlin looked at Alice beside him, his face filled with disdain. “Do you even deserve to be mentioned in the same breath as Mr. Alcaon? Please come to your senses.”

“...What did you say?!” Alice’s face flushed red with anger, feeling that Merlin was looking down on her. After all, she was a Mithril adventurer, far superior to the Silver rank! It was embarrassing for her to be compared to some nobody!

“Don’t you have any idea how you became a Mithril adventurer? Isn’t it all thanks to me?” Merlin said with a scornful glance. “Mr. Alcaon worked his way up from Black Iron to Silver through his own strength, completing over nine million quests. He has that kind of superhuman patience. Do you have that? And you expect me to worship you? Keep dreaming. Even if you become a Purple-Gold adventurer someday, there will always be suspicions of cheating.”

“You speak so harshly. Didn’t I work hard to become a Mithril adventurer? Why do you dismiss all my efforts with a single word—cheating?!” Alice retorted with an ugly expression, then changed her approach. “I also know that Mr. Alcaon’s patience is admirable, but it’s not as legendary as you吹捧 it! Find a better reason to justify looking down on me!”

Could she really let Merlin despise her for life over this matter? No, she couldn’t afford to give Merlin such ammunition, or her future would be miserable…

No, she had to…

That evening, as the sun set, the two had already returned home one after another.

Many street vendors were also packing up their goods, preparing to leave.

Even the refugees displaced by the recent flood were everywhere to be seen.

But since it was late at night, the refugees could only look for a place sheltered from wind and rain to spend the night.

Whenever it reached this time, probably only taverns and inns would still be open; even the Adventurers Guild was about to close.

Fortunately for Merlin and Alice, the guild in Cow Town had not yet been closed.

But luckily it was around this time and there were very few people. Still, the two planned to go in and inquire about Mr. Alcaon’s whereabouts.

“Finally… I’m so excited to meet Mr. Alcaon now.” Merlin pressed a hand to his chest, feeling overwhelmed with excitement.

Alice rolled her eyes.

“Even though I started as a Black Iron adventurer and it’s been so long, I still have no hope of promotion, yet Mr. Alcaon is like a great guiding light for me in my lost journey.” Merlin said, feeling as though a great prophet had pointed the way for him.

“Please, let’s stop this nonsense. Let’s go in quickly.” Alice covered her face and said.

After entering the Cow Town Adventurers Guild, they discovered that almost no one was inside.

The guild here was pitifully small. Compared to the Locksheim Guild, this was like a rural town versus a metropolis!

Moreover, this guild ranked very low, basically at the bottom tier, somewhat like a small workshop operation.

An old man with white hair, partially bald, was sitting at the counter wearing reading glasses and reading a newspaper. Dressed in slippers, legs crossed, sipping cheap black tea, he looked exceedingly comfortable.

When Alice first entered, she immediately felt something was wrong. This wasn’t a vigorous, energetic Adventurers Guild—it was an elderly care home!

Merlin and Alice also felt uneasy, secretly wondering if they had come to the wrong place.

“No mistake. The Cow Town Adventurers Guild is right here.” Alice answered with certainty.

“Then why do I feel like I’ve walked into a nursing home?” Merlin frowned, not understanding.

Alice hesitated for a moment, then seriously explained, “Not all guilds are thriving. Cow Town itself is just a remote, underdeveloped town. What could you expect from their Adventurers Guild?”

“This isn’t as bad as other remote towns, is it?” Merlin surveyed the surroundings, his face full of distaste.

“Locksheim is also a remote town, but their strength is not weak. In the last Adventurers Competition, Locksheim’s guild ranked in the top 28 among all the world’s Adventurers Guilds!”

“Did you know there are 6,489 Adventurers Guilds in the world?” Alice tried to make Merlin understand that Locksheim was no pushover.

Merlin thought for a moment and nodded. “Sounds impressive. So our guild was actually this excellent? Well, although luck played a big role in the last competition, I heard that Mr. Karl and Earl performed brilliantly. You basically dragged the Locksheim Guild into the top 128. That’s really amazing.”

Alice recalled with nostalgia. She hadn’t experienced the last competition herself, but she’d heard many stories from others.

“I understand. So this guild in Cow Town really doesn’t even have a ranking, right?” Merlin furrowed his brows.

“Alright, alright, stop dwelling on this. Let’s ask about Mr. Alcaon’s whereabouts.” Alice walked over to the front desk and directly asked the balding elderly man, “Excuse me, are you…”

The balding elderly man raised his head. Up close, he looked even older. “I am the front desk manager of this guild. If you have any questions, you can consult me.”

Merlin, standing behind, nearly spit blood, desperately complaining in his heart: *What the hell is a front desk manager! Didn’t they just hire some decrepit old man as the face of the guild? The fact that this guild hasn’t gone bankrupt is already a miracle! And why isn’t it a pretty girl? They should all kneel and apologize!*

There was an unwritten rule in the guilds: those standing at the front desk were usually called ‘front desk girls,’ young and beautiful, hired to attract more customers. In large guilds, the front desk girls were more beautiful than any other. However, the Cow Town guild had produced a ‘front desk manager’ instead, which made Merlin and Alice’s eyes widen in disbelief, utterly uncomfortable.

Alice ignored Merlin’s inner turmoil and asked politely, “Excuse me, do you know where Mr. Alcaon is? We have some matters to discuss.”

The balding elderly man adjusted his reading glasses and asked curiously, “You’re looking for me?”

Alice rolled her eyes and leaned close to whisper to Merlin, “Look at this wretched appearance—how could he possibly be that legendary figure, Mr. Alcaon? Probably just a namesake.”

Hearing Merlin’s words, the old man also felt puzzled inside and cautiously asked, “Then… are you really Mr. Alcaon?”

“There wouldn’t be a fake. There’s only one Alcaon in Cow Town.” Alcaon took out his Silver-rank adventurer certificate from his collar. All the information was clearly written on it—this was indeed the real person.

“What? It’s actually true?!”

Ignoring the stunned Alice beside him, Alcaon tightly grasped the wrinkled hands of Merlin, his expression filled with immense reverence. “I’ve long admired your noble bearing and extraordinary presence. Meeting you in person truly matches all the legends!”

“Today, from afar, I could already feel the kingly aura emanating from you—truly exceptional!”

“I’m Merlin. Nice to meet you.”

title: Chapter 5 — Serious Akaron
content:
Chapter 5 — Serious Akaron

Volume 15 · Chapter 5

Alice watched Merlin with an expression full of reverence on his face, a few black lines forming on her forehead as she wondered if something was wrong. Who was it that had just been mocking someone? Now he was changing his face so quickly—wasn't that a bit too realistic!

Merlin gripped Acaron's hands tightly, his eyes full of adoring stars, thinking how close he had come to injuring an ally. He never expected this unremarkable old man to be the legendary Liver Emperor. Indeed, one shouldn't judge a book by its cover.

Actually, in Merlin's fantasy, Old Man Acaron was a wise and courageous elder with bright, eagle-like eyes, like an experienced hunter.

However, Acaron's ordinary appearance—no different from a typical gatekeeper at a nursing home—left Merlin feeling a huge psychological gap, completely unable to reconcile with the image in his mind.

Still, Merlin's attitude toward Acaron remained highly respectful. No matter how ordinary Acaron looked, he would always be held in esteem by Merlin.

"...Acaron's reading glasses nearly fell off the ground. Startled by the enthusiastic Merlin, he said, 'Oh... Mr. Merlin...'"

Alice rolled her eyes and came over to Merlin's side, whispering, "Wow! You shameless guy. One second you were looking down on someone, and the next you're acting like a sycophant..."

Merlin gave a half-smile and whispered to Alice, "Everyone has moments of misjudgment. Who would have thought a man who patiently completes 9,999,999 low-level missions would be so ordinary?"

Alice furrowed her delicate brows and had to admit Merlin was right. Even she had momentarily doubted whether this was the infamous Acaron.

Old Acaron glanced at Merlin and Alice's adventurer credentials, then asked puzzledly, "Did you come all the way from Britain to find me for something?"

Alice nodded and got straight to the point, "We do have a matter we'd like your assistance with. Why don't we sit down and talk..."

The three found a small table right there in the guild to discuss matters.

Since Merlin had finally met the man he admired, his mood was still relatively excited.

Even Merlin's gaze toward old Acaron was filled with warmth; anyone who didn't know better might have thought he had special feelings for this elderly man.

Old Acaron felt uncomfortable being stared at by Merlin and wondered what he had done. Why did this man from Britain keep looking at him with such a naked gaze? Could it be that he was from Beibei Mountain?

Although old Acaron was well-known as the only ordinary person promoted from Black Iron to Silver, most of the chatter was mocking rather than commendable.

However, Merlin appreciated old Acaron, perhaps because he too was a Black Iron adventurer and could relate to Acaron's story.

"Merlin, pay attention to your behavior. Don't stare so openly; you'll be seen as a suspicious character." Alice kindly reminded Merlin.

"Oh right, I got a bit too excited." Merlin embarrassedly lowered his head, trying to appear normal.

"So... what do you two need from me?" Old Acaron asked.

"Our mission requires us to investigate something in France, so we'd like you to be our guide," Alice explained her purpose clearly.

"Guide?" Old Acaron was surprised, not expecting this kind of thing to come to him.

"Yes, after all, we're not locals of France and don't know many things. We need an experienced local to assist us," Alice explained.

"Need to find an experienced local? Can't we just find anyone? Why come to me, an elderly man with limited mobility?" Mr. Old Acaron asked, not understanding.

"Sir, you're being too modest. You're the only ordinary person in history to be promoted from Black Iron to Silver. In terms of experience, who can compare with you?" Merlin paused and showed a cunning smile. "To be honest, we're very interested in you. By the way, now get on the bus and enjoy two months of membership with a fifty percent discount!"

Alice's face darkened instantly, thinking to herself, Hey! What is this bastard talking nonsense about!? The topic had already been led to a strange place!

Old Acaron broke into a cold sweat, awkwardly thinking that these two were clearly adventurers, yet they seemed like unscrupulous peddlers hawking rotten fruit door to door!

"...But I usually have other work and can't leave the guild easily. You'd better find someone else. Of course, if you're here to peddle something, I suggest you go elsewhere. As you can see, I'm quite poor here."

"It's not like that. We're not here to peddle anything. Oh right!" Alice suddenly remembered something and hurriedly took out a letter of introduction from Karl Mr. and handed it to Acaron. "This is our letter of introduction. Mr. Karl introduced us here."

"Karl? The Karl from your guild?" Acaron's attitude immediately changed, and he had to take these two seriously.

"That's right. We're all adventurers from the Luxembourg Guild." Alice nodded.

Acaron quickly opened the envelope, adjusted his reading glasses, and read it word by word with narrowed eyes.

Merlin and Alice kept quiet and didn't make a sound to disturb old Acaron.

After finishing Karl's letter of introduction, old Acaron let out a long breath, removed his reading glasses to reveal his eyes, and suddenly his entire demeanor was different.

Those eyes were no longer listless and lethargic. Instead, they shone brightly, like a sleeping lion that had awakened.

"I understand. Brother Karl once saved my life, and I have always kept that kindness in my heart. Since he asked me to assist you, I will not refuse. From now on, I will accompany you throughout your actions in France."

"Oh!" Merlin clearly sensed old Acaron's aura had changed, as if a switch had been flipped and he had awakened. This was what an adventurer who had endured 9,999,999 hardships and possessed incomparable experience should look like! Indeed, I hadn't chosen the wrong person. Acaron was truly extraordinary!

"Thank you very much." Alice expressed her gratitude, but thought to herself, He suddenly becomes so reliable after taking off his reading glasses! With Acaron's help this time, we will surely be strengthened. It seems Merlin's judgment was correct. A person with great perseverance will not be ordinary. I'm truly looking forward to it.

"Can you tell me your goal for this trip? So I can prepare accordingly." Acaron asked patiently.

"We're going to Glen Plains to investigate some vampire matters." Alice answered.

"Oh? France indeed has many stories about the vampire race, and Glen Plains is even known as the homeland of vampire culture. Your investigation direction is correct." Acaron nodded in agreement, then suddenly changed the subject—

"But Glen Plains is located in southern France."

"That area recently suffered a flood and is in a state of chaos."

"We must be careful when we go there... hmm."

title: Chapter 6 — Transformation (Bonus Chapter with Voting Incentive)
content:
Chapter 6 — Transformation (Bonus Chapter with Voting Incentive)

Volume 15 · Chapter 6

Hearing old Acalon's words, Merlin's eyes lit up with little stars again, thinking that this was indeed a man full of legendary charm, and his suggestions were so stable!

Although Alice wasn't as excited as Merlin, she was still happy inside, after all, there's nothing more worthy of making someone happy than a reliable teammate.

"So when should we depart? Do we need to wait a while, let the flood crisis pass?"

"Not!" Old Acalon shook his head, speaking with a serious expression, "For adventurers, time is money and life. Useless waiting will only miss opportunities, so we depart immediately!"

"Wow~" Merlin showed an admiring look, feeling that old Acalon's every word was so imposing and heroic, not to mention he had completed 9,999,999 tasks, his understanding of the adventurer profession was beyond ordinary!

"... " Alice's expression hesitated, stuttering, "Your age is already quite advanced, shouldn't you rest a bit? You don't have to be so fierce for us."

"No problem, because the guild is severely short-staffed, I had to give up adventuring and stayed here as a guard all along. Suddenly a task found me, and I feel like I've instantly grown younger by 50 years." Old Acalon looked spirited, indeed full of vigor, "The adventurous soul hidden within me has been burning fiercely!"

"... Well." Alice saw Acalon so spirited, and it was inappropriate for her to say more.

It seems old Acalon has really been suppressing himself for too long. Every day staying in the guild doing elderly work indeed doesn't match his pursuits.

Old Acalon felt he was about to start a new adventure, and his whole body's fighting spirit began to burn fiercely.

Merlin: "I saw flames burning on old Mr. Acalon."

Alice: "Illusion, all illusions."

"Please wait, two of you, I'll go change into my battle attire. Without battle attire, I'll be weak by ten thousand times. Wait for me to change, and we'll depart together." Old Acalon said seriously.

"Okay, we aren't in a hurry. You old person, change slowly." Alice said with a bitter smile, worrying that if she was too eager, she might sprain Acalon's old waist.

"Thank you."

Old Acalon slowly stood up, walked to a relatively open place, and assumed a very strange pose, blurting out one after another:

"2! Sol

Only to see old Acalon's hunched body suddenly changed, golden light shining, as resplendent as the sun, making it impossible to look at directly.

Merlin's complexion instantly changed, feeling a faint oppressive force, "What?! Could this be the legendary..... Too bright to see clearly!"

Alice covered her eyes, some pain saying, "So blinding! My eyes are about to go blind!"

Merlin's expression was severe, his tone serious as he speculated, "This battle attire is probably a god-tier item! And the current glow should be the power after release!"

Alice was already speechless towards Merlin, quickly saying, "What nonsense are you talking about? This is already light pollution!"

Waiting for the ripples to dissipate, the guild restored its due tranquility, and Merlin and Alice couldn't help but stare intently....

Only to see! Old Acalon had no change at all, still the same old look, like a nursing home gatekeeper.

The two were simultaneously stunned, not understanding the situation in front of them. The momentum earlier was so huge, but the result was completely unchanged?

"Merlin, it's so strange, why is there no change at all? Just now wasn't very imposing?" Alice whispered to Merlin in doubt.

"Maybe the body had some change, like having superhuman strength inside, not to be underestimated." Merlin spoke seriously.

"... Is that so? It seems I worried too much. Being able to upgrade from iron to silver with an ordinary person's body, there must be two brushes." Alice felt Merlin's words made sense.

"Definitely so, I always believe old Mr. Acalon is a low-key powerhouse!" Merlin said affirmatively.

Old Acalon saw Merlin and Alice whispering, apparently having many doubts about themselves.

"Are the two of you puzzled by my behavior? Thinking I have no change? It's okay, you can ask directly, after all, people with such doubts, you aren't the first." Or rather, a novel...

"... We really can't see it, please enlighten us, senior." Alice said very honestly, truly couldn't see any change on old Acalon.

"Who said you can't see it? Old Mr. Acalon has already had obvious changes..." Merlin showed a look of understanding, "I suppose old Mr. Acalon has already completed the transformation now, having incredible power inside. Randomly punching can cause space to shake, but everything is hidden, impossible to easily discover, right?"

Alice furrowed her brows, wondering if it's true or false? Could she be of the same kind as Merlin, some kind of god descendant? Appearing ordinary on the outside, but having unbelievable power?

"Not at all, your changes are so obvious yet you didn't notice. These young people these days are really getting more and more careless. Look at my feet!" Old Acalon pointed at his feet with his finger, proudly saying, "Just now, I secretly used a magic scroll to release low-level Holy Light, and then took the opportunity to change the slippers into boots, after all, we're about to depart soon, slippers are really unsuitable for long journeys, but with these boots it's different, no matter how far the road, they won't break, how about it? Isn't my operation shocking enough? hiahiahiahia~!"

A crow flew over the heads of Merlin and Alice, the scene in front making the two fall into silence, unable to speak a word.

At this moment, old Acalon was wearing an old-fashioned vest, underneath was vibrant red underpants, and on his feet a pair of black long boots.

Such a mismatched outfit, unbinding making one doubt if this really is the "Country of Fashion" France?

The atmosphere of the combination of urban and rural areas, simply like coming out of the mountains from Malan Mountain!

Merlin and Alice both lowered their heads again, starting to whisper one after another:

"It's just changing a pair of shoes, why use such a pretentious special effect? Making it look like a killing blow..." Merlin muttered with a blank face, thinking about the promised transformation? About the body having incredible power? Ah, I feel my face hurts.

"I'll never believe old Mr. Acalon is a powerhouse again, he's just an old man with middle school syndrome who hasn't graduated!" Alice covered her face, already having lost all expectations of Acalon.

"Let's depart! Pull yourself together, new adventures await us, as adventurers symbolizing freedom, never stop challenging difficulties!" Old Acalon said seriously, unaware that in Merlin and Alice's eyes it was so middle school, still secretly pleased in his heart--

Finally said this sentence that had been brewing for 20 years, truly awesome!

I feel so cool now, like I've returned to my younger days, oh my~

(What country?)?

title: Chapter 7 — Going to Church
content:
Chapter 7 — Going to Church

Volume 15 · Chapter 7

Three people set out that very evening, heading toward the Glenn Plains in southern France.

It seems Mr. Akalon also knows that his attire affects the streetscape, and is not just doing as he pleases.

When traveling, Old Akalon still put on a convenient brown windbreaker, moving about with Merlin and Alice.

Old Akalon enthusiastically invited the two to ride in his vehicle to the Glenn Plains. Merlin and Alice were naturally delighted, as it would save them a sum of money.

However, what neither of them could have anticipated was that Old Akalon's vehicle... was a bullock cart.

Looking at this old yellow ox's docile horns, it should have been used for farming, and it's not young anymore, its movement speed extremely slow!

Originally, a regular carriage could reach the Glenn Plains in seven days, but now it's the twelfth day, and the bullock cart is still on the way...

Merlin and Alice sat in the back of the bullock cart, clutching their knees, wearing expressionless faces, looking at the happy Old Akalon in front.

Both had blank expressions, their gazes vacant, already exhausted in body and mind from Old Akalon's torment.

"Alice, how much longer until we reach the Glenn Plains? Isn't it supposed to be seven days? How many days has it been now?" Merlin's face instantly turned into that of an old man, filled with fatigue.

"You've already asked me that 867 times, I don't know, who knows how much longer it will take?" Alice's state is not much better than Merlin's.

"Does Master Karl have a grudge against us?" Merlin suddenly asked out of the blue.

"Why say that?" Alice looked at Merlin in confusion. "If there's no grudge, why introduce such a guide to us? Enmity of a father is no big deal, ah!" Merlin felt he just wanted a reliable person, why was it so hard?

"Don't say that, Master Karl is well-meaning, it's just that he... doesn't know... doesn't know that Mr. Akalon is such a swindler, ah?" Alice said with an awkward expression, then suddenly changed her train of thought. "Aren't you the one who praised Mr. Akalon so much before? Saying he's definitely a low-key powerhouse, now this setback has made you lose confidence?"

"Old man, I've been slapped in the face so many times, and still believed Mr. Akalon was a powerhouse, do I have a problem with my brain?" Merlin asked back, frowning.

"Hmph! Didn't someone previously have stars in their eyes, muttering about being especially excited to see an idol?" Alice coldly sarcastic from the side.

"You're going too far! I just think completing 999,999 low-level tasks, this patience of mine is remarkable, I just didn't expect Mr. Akalon to really be an ordinary person." Merlin said with a tone of weariness. He had thought that someone with such perseverance must be a person of outstanding talent, but in the end, he thought too much.

"Not everyone is like you, your kind wandering in the iron rank is an anomaly, and ordinary people are fine too, like Mr. Akalon becoming a silver-rank adventurer with an ordinary body, gaining the respect of many people." Alice said very seriously.

"Sorry, arranged to be the poster child, I don't see an ounce of respect." Merlin said with a dark face.

"....Alice was at a loss, indeed that was the case, in the adventurer industry, only useless people would go do clerical work.

"Say, can't we move faster? At this rate, it'll be the Year of the Monkey and the Horse Month before we arrive."

Merlin said with a fatigued demeanor.

"You ask the old yellow ox, whether it's willing to walk a few steps faster." Alice's voice sounded weak.

Old Akalon was briskly driving his bullock cart, although the speed was slow, he felt a sensation of wind flying and electricity rushing.

"Mr. Merlin, Miss Alice, you feel the speed of my bullock cart now? Is it fast?"

Merlin and Alice fell silent, no expression on their faces, not wanting to make any evaluation, wondering where Old Akalon's such confidence came from?

At this moment, a pig cart passed by ostentatiously, employing the skill of cutting corners, ruthlessly throwing the old ox cart behind...

Merlin instantly became restless, what horses, donkeys being understandable to be overtaken, but a pig cart too? What the hell! ? Too much of a slight!

"Impossible! I can't take it anymore, I'll chop this old yellow ox to death, and let's hire a carriage!"

"Hey! ? Calm down!" Alice pressed down on Merlin, not letting him stand up.

"Cough! That... maybe my ox is just in a bad state recently. Before it was faster than young thoroughbreds, though this is a good thing." Old Akalon said mysteriously and secretly.

"Originally a week-long journey took over ten days, what kind of good thing is this, ah?" Merlin's forehead veins jumped.

"Young man, don't be too impatient about everything. Now this situation is also a kind of cultivation, used to smooth out the edges of your character, greatly beneficial for your future." Old Akalon said solemnly.

Merlin and Alice had heard enough of Akalon's pretentious teachings, but since he was the guide for this journey, they endured it all the way.

NI 二<

Royal heavens don't disappoint those with intent, on the thirteenth day of the journey, a traveler finally arrived at the Glenn Plains.

This is not a particularly beautiful place, but is everywhere filled with decline and ruin, comparable to Merlin's hometown, the Death Marshes.

Due to having experienced a flood disaster, there are not many people living here now, the vast majority fleeing northward.

Merlin and Alice stared blankly into the distance, the horizon where the sun was just rising, the fiery red sunrise dyeing everything red.

"Not long ago, this was also a place with a thriving population, Glenn's people, even after leaving their own hometowns eventually, would all return here, making this the land they passed down through generations." Old Akalon said with deep meaning.

"Natural disasters and man-made calamities, no one can avoid." Merlin said with no emotion.

Alice said nothing at all, but instead clasped her hands together, assuming a prayer posture, perhaps she could only do this much.

"Where do you plan to start the investigation? This must have a direction, otherwise searching like a headless fly, although it's very energy-consuming." Old Akalon asked.

"Funeral culture, I heard that here, in order to prevent the dead from becoming vampires and harming people, there is a custom of nailing silver into the hearts of the dead, I think there might be gains, who knows." Merlin stated the goal of this trip.

"Starting the investigation from the local funeral culture, ah? I understood." Old Akalon nodded, quickly giving a plan, "Let's go investigate the nearest church? Asking the priests is the best choice for such things, after all, funeral matters are usually presided over by priests, they should be very familiar with local customs."

"Church ah..." Merlin's expression became unnatural, his heart a bit annoyed, not liking such places.

"What's wrong? Going to the church will make you uncomfortable?" Alice looked at Merlin in surprise, thinking it wasn't the first time, she had previously lived in a church, encountering an ice-frost holy dragon.

"Ah, how could I feel uncomfortable?"

Merlin pursed his lips, muttering a bit.

"I just seeing the ugly faces of those stinking priests makes me feel nauseous..."

title: Chapter 8 — Only Seven Days Left
content:
Chapter 8 — Only Seven Days Left

Volume 15 · Chapter 8

The three drove the ox cart straight to the nearest church.
This church is small in scale, and having suffered a disaster, it now shows utter dilapidation and decline.
A large flock of crows stands on the withered tree, cawing loudly.
Merlin and Alice got off the cart, surveyed the church, which looked quite ordinary, no different from a rural village chapel.
"This is the nearest church; I came here when I was young, the priest is a devout person, trustworthy.
'Let's go in.' Alice took the lead, heading toward the church, and Old Akaron followed."
Merlin was about to follow when suddenly waves of weakness swept through his body, and his heart began to throb with pain.
He instantly felt dizzy and nearly collapsed to the ground, as if struck by a serious illness.
Merlin barely managed to steady himself, realizing the gravity of the situation—his heart's curse crisis was imminent.
The heart curse usually gives a warning, roughly a month beforehand; the intense pain awakens Merlin, telling him it's time to seek prey.
However, more than twenty days have passed since the last curse warning, indicating a serious problem—
Merlin doesn't have much time left—he likely has only about a week of life!
If he does not use the demon sword Banri Garan in his hand to slay Saint-tier powerhouses, Merlin's heart will constrict and kill him.
Most of those twenty-plus days were spent rushing on the road, utterly wasted, leading Merlin now to face his survival crisis.
Merlin fell into extreme weakness, hastily gripping the withered tree beside him and panting heavily.
His face turned pale, cold sweat trickling down his forehead; he felt his curse worsening considerably, and the need to find prey had become urgent.
Damn it!
Has the curse unknowingly become this bad?
It seems too much time was wasted on the road, leading to the current situation....
If this mission continues, I don't know whether I'll encounter a Saint-tier foe who could alleviate my curse.
What can I do? The only Saint-tier powerhouse beside me is Alice; I can't possibly take her....
What am I thinking? Calm down.....
Merlin held his forehead; the urgent situation before him instantly made him irritable, wishing he could just find any Saint-tier powerhouse to slash first and talk later.
Alice noticed Merlin hadn't caught up, looked back puzzled, only to see he was in poor shape, weakly leaning on the withered tree, as if unwell.
Merlin?! What's wrong? Are you feeling unwell?
Alice jumped in fright, hurried over to check Merlin's condition; her eyes unconsciously showed concern, though she didn't speak, she was worried inside.
Seeing Merlin so weak, this was only the second time Alice had witnessed it; the first time was that night when Merlin's curse flared and he lay trembling on the floor.
Merlin glanced at Alice, then awkwardly shifted away; he could not bear her concerned gaze, being worried about by that damned old woman simply highlighted his own inadequacy!
I, who stand at the top of the food chain as a Demon Lord, when did I fall to the point where Alice needs to worry about me?
Thus Merlin gritted his teeth, swallowed his pain, put on an indifferent front, completely ignoring how dire his situation was—his life left only about a week.
"I'm fine, just my old ailment acting up; don't worry, I'll be better soon."
"....Alice showed dissatisfaction, recalling Merlin said he had an old ailment, she asked: 'Is your health always not good?'"
"Yeah, my body is just like that; I get sick from time to time, but it's nothing serious." Merlin said offhandedly, not wanting Alice to overthink.
"You should have told me this; why are you hiding it from me?" Alice frowned.
"What good would telling you do? You can't cure my old ailment anyway." Merlin curled his lip, smirking disdainfully.
"...You don't have to tough it out either; if you feel unwell, tell me and I'll take care of you." Alice said with a solemn expression.
"I don't need your pity; just look after yourself." Merlin, displeased, brushed off Alice and strode straight toward the church.
Old Akaron saw Merlin approaching and, also worried, inquired, 'Lord Merlin, are you alright?'
"'No, hurry inside.' Merlin replied coldly, his mood not wanting to say more.
Alice watched Merlin's retreating back, unease rising in her heart; why was his attitude so strange?
Recall that when Merlin's old ailment acted up last time, his attitude was similarly cold and aloof, not wanting anyone near.
Given Merlin's strength, no old ailment should remain unsolved to this day; could the situation be far worse than I imagined?
Alice thought for a moment, then hurried to catch up with Merlin, lowering her voice to speak secretly.
"To be frank, do you, as an evil creature, feel uncomfortable when near a church? If so, then wait outside for me."
Merlin rolled his eyes dramatically, sighed, and said, 'My lady, quit overthinking; this has nothing to do with it....
Despite Alice's repeated questioning, Merlin simply refused to speak.
The matter of the heart curse is Merlin's secret; casually telling others would be exposing his weakness.
Moreover, even now Merlin has not fully trusted Alice, finding it hard to regard her as one of his own.
The three entered the church; inside it was quite spacious, with rows of pews neatly arranged.
The walls depict the story of the Goddess of Light saving humanity; the figures are lifelike, showcasing the painter's superb skill.
Sunlight streams through the surrounding stained glass, filling the whole church with a mysterious aura.....
At the front stands a huge statue of the Goddess of Light, hands clasped in a prayer pose, looking quite solemn and dignified.
However, the statue's visage is blurry—this is a trait of the Goddess of Light; for the sake of religious mystery, her face is invariably indistinct.
The Holy Church calls this the Goddess of Light being sacred; mortals cannot perceive her true visage, only the most devout believers can see it.
This emperor's new clothes ruse works fairly well, so it has been kept; each time believers see the Goddess of Light's blurry face, they realize they are not pious enough and must continue to dispel stray thoughts.
Upon seeing Merlin and the others enter, a priest with white hair and a black robe immediately came forward, the wooden cross on his chest appearing exceedingly plain.
"'Sorry, travelers, today the church is not holding any blessing ceremony, so we are not receiving visitors.'"
"'Father, it's me, Akaron; you forgot me?' Old Akaron stepped forward, pointing at himself; it seemed they were old acquaintances.
"'Akaron! Good heavens, how did you come here? I recall seeing you twenty years ago; you weren't supposed to have stopped adventuring, were you? Have you taken up the old trade again?' The priest's aged face was full of astonishment.
"'As you can see, young people still need me, so for the sake of adventurous spirit, this old bone of mine must regain its vigor.' Old Akaron said earnestly, completely failing to notice the faint, insincere smiles on Merlin and Alice's faces.
The priest glanced at Alice and Merlin behind him, then turned to ask Akaron, 'What brings you to see me this time?'
"'It's not that I have business; rather, the two lords behind me have need...' Old Akaron pointed at Alice and Merlin behind him, continuing earnestly—
"'They want to learn about vampires.'
"'How about it, Father? We're old friends after all; please help us...'

title: Chapter 9 — Blood Clan Origin (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 9 — Blood Clan Origin (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 15 · Chapter 9

With Old Acaron's efforts, the priest still chose to receive Merlin and the group.

In a small room somewhere in the church, several people sat together.

"Are the two of you investigating vampires?" the priest asked in surprise.

"Yes, if you have any important information, please be sure to tell us." Alice's attitude was very sincere, hoping to gain something here.

"Father, just say whatever you know, this is very important to the two of them." Old Acaron helped by saying nice words on the side.

"Didn't expect the two of you to be interested in vampires; it's been a long time since anyone asked me about this." The priest paused, continuing, "Vampires as a creature did indeed exist, and once ruled all of France, but by now, the blood race may have long gone extinct, no trace of them anywhere, as if they vanished into thin air overnight. Now mentioning vampires, it's probably just a legendary creature."

"........" Alice heard the priest's words, her heart instantly turned cold, feeling the situation was still not optimistic.

"But Glen Plains here is hailed as the hometown of vampires; people always have a sense of awe towards vampires, many stories can find their source here, I don't know which aspect you want to consult?" the priest asked patiently.

"I heard Glen Plains has always had a strange tradition, the dead are buried only after their hearts are pierced with silver, what is this about?" Alice asked straight to the point.

"This is a very ancient tradition; ancestors once suffered indelible pain, in order not to let descendants be harassed, this burial ritual was passed down. Our family has lived here for generations, so we are relatively knowledgeable about this." The priest nodded and said.

"Piercing the dead with silver to prevent them from turning into vampires and harming people, is this true?" Alice continued to ask.

"That's right, it's true. The ancestors of the Glen people once suffered a blood race attack; many books have very clear and detailed records. This event is the oldest blood race attack event in existence now, and many subsequent processed stories spread out from this land, so Glen Plains being hailed as the hometown of vampires is not an exaggeration." The priest said slowly, as if telling an ancient story.

"Blood race attack? What is this about?" Alice was very curious about this matter; this is the first time in history that vampires attacked humans, she always felt something was suspicious.

The priest showed a look of recollection, organized his words, and said, "On a certain night more than 600 years ago, three monsters walked out of the great forest in the south of Glen Plains. Later we called the three of them the most ancient blood races. As soon as they walked out of the great forest, they began to crazily slaughter humans, sucking people's blood dry with their sharp fangs, like hungry wild wolves. Amazingly, those who died from having their blood sucked dry came back to life one by one, and began to slaughter their closest relatives around them. This hellish day lasted a full month. The disaster spread across the entire Glen Plains. Later, when the three ancient blood races disappeared, people were finally able to counterattack, burning those cruel subordinates to death, piercing their hearts with silver, which finally calmed the disaster."

Alice listened with mixed feelings; isn't this the same as those cruel vampires in the stories? She just didn't expect they would once threaten the safety of the entire Glen Plains.

"Who were those three most ancient blood races?" Merlin asked with great interest.

"Their names are Lamia, Bathory, and Dracula..." the priest said in a very flat tone.

However, after this sentence, Merlin and Alice found it hard to continue being calm, their spirits suddenly stirred!

The two both widened their eyes, looking at the priest with incomprehensible expressions, as if they had heard something incredible.

Because from the priest's mouth, they suddenly heard the name Dracula; this was the core of everything!

Merlin and Alice had worked hard for so long, and today finally had a harvest. The clue that was already broken now vaguely caught hold of some thread again!

For the two of them this was a huge good thing, proving things could continue; following this clue, perhaps they could perfectly complete the mission.

"Dracula!?" Merlin couldn't quite believe his ears.

"It is called Dracula, no mistake....." the priest nodded and said.

"Father, can you tell me in detail the causes and consequences of the blood race attack incident?" Alice wanted to dig out more useful things.

"Alright." The priest lowered his head, frowned and thought carefully, then said, "Most people think vampires are creatures that appear because of the Goddess of Light's curse, but here in Glen Plains there is a different story; vampires obtained evil power from the altar in the great forest, and were born only after being cursed. Very long ago, many people witnessed those three most ancient blood races walking out of the forest; that was the first time humans saw ageless, immortal, cruel bloodthirsty monsters. This story has many bases and records, obviously not groundless."

"The altar in the forest? What is that?" Merlin frowned, feeling the deeper the questions went, the more things were dragged out.

"This is a very ancient legend; right in the south of Glen Plains, there is a dense forest; its depths seal the most evil power, even the sun's light cannot reach the evil in the deepest part. Many brave people went to explore, and never came out again. It can be said to be the most dangerous and mysterious area of Glen Plains. However, the only three people who walked out of the depths of the forest became monsters that nearly destroyed Glen Plains." The priest said leisurely, making people more curious about what exactly is in the depths of this forest?

After listening, the three fell silent, feeling the priest had explained clearly enough; the depths of the southern forest had many suspicious points, but were full of unknown dangers.

However, Dracula, this legendary vampire great noble, was born from here, so there is really a necessity to explore, maybe can discover more valuable things.

"Listen... this forest is very dangerous, right?" Old Acaron had a drop of cold sweat trickling down his forehead; hearing the priest speak so terribly, he instinctively felt fear.

"More than dangerous? It's simply like it's cursed. Just that group of people who entered the forest's outer perimeter easily get lost; if not careful, they will be starved to death inside. Not to mention the depths are even more dangerous, very likely there are powerful creatures guarding it. Locals teach children from a young age, absolutely cannot step into the southern forest even half a step." The priest said with an extremely serious tone.

However, as soon as the priest finished speaking, which should have been the time to make people give up, Merlin suddenly stood up, black-faced, slapped the table, and said in an unquestionable tone--

"That mysterious forest, we are definitely going to go!"

"I'd really like to see the evil power in the depths."

"No matter how evil it is, is it more evil than me?"

title: Chapter 10 — Evil Altar
content:
Chapter 10 — Evil Altar

Volume 15 · Chapter 10

The priest's expression turned strange. He thought to himself, who would be willing to describe themselves with evil? Isn't that self-deprecation?

Alice lowered her voice and secretly reminded Merlin—sentence, "Hey! People are priests, they're very sensitive to evil, don't talk randomly."

"Cough!" Merlin lightly coughed to cover his embarrassment, then changed his meaning, "What I mean is, in the face of powerful evil forces, I'm not powerful either. We have to go deep into this forest to see."

Old Akarion looked at Merlin, thinking this man was just like him when he was young.

Clearly a black-iron adventurer, with the气势 of a calf not afraid of tigers, always liking to say laughable big words.

This isn't a good habit. When I was young, I suffered a lot because of this habit.

The strongest person in the current team is Lady Alice, and everyone's safety has to rely on her expression.

Shouldn't one ask Lady Alice's opinion about whether to go to the forest?

Old Akarion didn't quite understand Merlin's such a dominant attitude; it had a hint of "there's no old tiger in the mountains, the monkey claims to be the king."

He had originally thought that for a couple with such a large level difference, Merlin was the type who had to mind his wife's expression.

But through Old Akarion's observations along the way, he discovered that Merlin seemed to be in absolute control, and many times, the stronger silver-rank adventurer Alice listened to Merlin.

This made Old Akarion increasingly unable to understand how Merlin, who was less powerful, could make the stronger Alice listen to him. Was it merely because of love?

After Merlin made his decision, Alice didn't speak, nor did she have any urge to rebuke, because she also felt they should go to the forest where the three oldest blood clans were born.

It was not easy to find clues about Duke Dracula lately. No matter what dangers were in the depths of the forest, they should go and see; there was no more suitable choice.

"If it were before, I would definitely have discouraged you from going there, but now the situation is different; that forest can be entered." The priest paused and talked about the recent changes in the Southern Great Forest, "The Glenn Plain experienced this great flood, and the Southern Forest has been largely washed away by the water. If you observe from a distance, you can clearly see the deep altar. If you want to investigate the altar, this might be the best opportunity in history. Three days ago, a team also came here to inquire about the Great Forest. Calculating the time, they should have already entered the altar deep inside."

"Three days ago, there were already... " The beginning of Mei's head suddenly became dizzy, thinking that there were already many things taken away from the east, and the outskirts are not a good thing. If there was something important, it would be too much of a loss!

"Yeah, they were probably over a dozen people. After inquiring about the altar's matters, they set off overnight." The priest answered blankly, not knowing why Merlin and Alice's reactions were so large?

Merlin and Alice looked at each other, both feeling that the situation was a bit urgent, and time became somewhat urgent.....
