title: Chapter 11 — Altar Guardian
content:
Chapter 11 — Altar Guardian

Volume 15 · Chapter 11

The bandits were all frightened by the vice-captain's outburst and didn't dare neglect their duties anymore, continuing to pry open the stone door of the altar one after another—

"Our vice-captain is one of the top experts in the group, so what if there are evil spirits?"

"Exactly, our vice-captain is a Saint-tier powerhouse. Can he really not handle some evil spirits? Don't look down on people like that!"

"Shut up and work faster, or the vice-captain will throw you here when he gets angry."

The bandits muttered among themselves, but under the vice-captain's pressure, none dared to say anything reckless.

"Just work faster. If we find treasure, the captain will reward us. Everyone cheer up!" The vice-captain called out, giving a slight morale boost.

The bandits quickly smiled and nodded in agreement. Hearing about rewards, they all worked with great enthusiasm.

The vice-captain let out a slight sigh of relief, turned and walked to the side, then took out a cigarette from his chest, planning to rest for a moment.

He put the cigarette between his lips, raised his head, and looked into the distance—only to suddenly notice a massive tree far away.

This towering ancient tree wasn't just unusually large, it was incredibly enormous. From afar, it looked like a pillar holding up the sky, standing tall in the forest.

The vice-captain gazed at the towering ancient tree and couldn't help but think to himself: Good heavens, this tree must be at least a thousand years old.

"When we came in... was this ancient tree there too?"

"Vice-captain! We pried it open! Come quick and look!"

The bandit captain, who had been puzzling over things in his heart, heard his subordinates' calls, tucked away his cigarette, and immediately turned back.

He saw that the stone door that had been sealed shut was now being pried open by the bandits.

But since it was pitch black inside, the group huddled around and gazed into the depths, completely unable to see anything.

The vice-captain walked over, crouched at the altar entrance, and cautiously poked his head in to take a look.

"It looks pretty good..."

Before he could finish, a piercing screech rang out, and a huge flock of bats flew out, swooping over the bandits' heads.

For a moment, these hardened bandits, who lived on the edge of death, were so frightened that they panicked and kept retreating. It seemed their claim of not fearing evil spirits was false.

"What are you all scared of?! Get back here!" The vice-captain cursed angrily. "A bunch of bats and you're peeing your pants? Are you men or not?!"

The bandits looked at each other and slowly crept back, following the vice-captain to carefully inspect the altar's secret chamber.

"We need two people to go in and scout ahead. Who'll go?" The vice-captain surveyed everyone's eyes. He certainly wasn't going in himself, worried about dangerous traps.

The bandits all began to avoid his gaze, refusing to meet his eyes at all, afraid this unlucky assignment would fall on them.

The vice-captain's gaze landed on the bandit who had been so talkative earlier. He figured the guy could go. "You! Go!"

"Vice-captain, I was wrong. I shouldn't have said anything about evil spirits—"

"Cut the nonsense and get in! Do you want to die?"

Before the poor guy could finish explaining, the vice-captain's hand went to his sword, as if ready to strike at any moment.

"...Alright, I'll go."

The garrulous little bandit, face twisted in misery, looked at the pitch-black interior and steeling himself, stepped inside.

He held a torch, a layer of cold sweat beading on his forehead, keeping alert to his surroundings, worried some monster might attack.

Just as the little bandit hadn't walked many steps, he suddenly stopped and perked up his ears.

"What the hell are you doing? Keep moving!" The vice-captain cursed from behind, thinking the little bandit was just being cowardly.

"It's not that, vice-captain! Listen carefully..." The little bandit whispered mysteriously, "Can't you hear a girl singing from inside?"

"Are you out of your mind? This is an ancient altar. The stone door was sealed from the outside. How could there be any living person here?!" The vice-captain's forehead veins twitched with anger, feeling like his subordinate was playing with him.

"There really is a girl's singing voice! Maybe... maybe it's the legendary evil spirit..." The little bandit said with a deadpan expression.

At these words, every bandit present felt a chill run down their spines. Things were getting worse and worse—they came to find treasure but found evil spirits instead!

Just as the vice-captain gathered his qi in his dantian, preparing to thoroughly reprimand the little bandit, the entire ground began to shake.

"What the hell is going on now?!"

The vice-captain cursed Annoyed, panic rising within him as he looked around, and then saw a jaw-dropping scene.

The earth shook violently, making it hard to keep one's footing.

Far away, that towering ancient tree actually began to move right before everyone's eyes. Countless thick vines shot up toward the sky, blotting out the sun and enveloping the bandits in shadow.

On the thick trunk, a pair of pale yellow eyes suddenly opened, staring fixedly at this group of intruding bandits. Its mouth split wide, and it let out an angry roar.

"ROAAAAR!"

The roar stunned all the bandits, making their legs go weak. They fell to the ground one by one, faces pale, pointing at the revived ancient tree.

"A treant!? Why is there an异族 here!?" The vice-captain's lips moved as he muttered to himself, his eyes wide with shock.

Treants were a race of异族, long-lived and ancient, probably existing since the world was born.

But treants had all migrated to the Southern United Kingdom long ago. To see such a massive treant here was truly unbelievable!

What frightened the vice-captain, a Saint-tier powerhouse, was not the treant's appearance—it was its overwhelming pressure!

If the vice-captain was already fearful sensing just the pressure of a peak Saint-tier cultivator, then the pressure radiating from this treant would make him cry with terror!

Because it had already transcended the Saint-tier realm, reaching another entirely different level of power.

The treant's roots emerged from the soil, forming two legs. It didn't need to walk over; merely bending its body forward, its face was already level with the bandits.

All the bandits were completely despairing, soon dominated by fear, their will to live gone. Staring at the treant's enormous face, they felt certain they were doomed.

The vice-captain's hand rested on his sword at his waist, but he didn't even have the courage to draw it. He thought to himself: No way! This treant is far too strong. Even with all my strength, I have no chance of winning!

The treant's bell-like giant eyes regarded the bandits, then opened its mouth and spoke in a deep, thunderous, rough voice, filled with fury—

"Six hundred years ago, three rats broke in while I was dormant, and I failed to catch them."

"Now you barge in again. Are you deliberately mocking my existence?!"

"All of you will surely die! This is a sealing ground for evil!"

"I was commanded by the Goddess to guard this place. No one, under any circumstances, is allowed to touch the source of sin!!"

title: Chapter 12 — Under the Moon (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 12 — Under the Moon (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 15 · Chapter 12

The bandits were all frozen in terror by the treant, whose physique and prowess were exceedingly formidable, daring not so much as draw breath.

Fortunately, the vice-captain barely managed to remain composed. After long hesitation, he ultimately decided it was best not to resist.

Since the treant could speak human language, there must be some chance for communication.

The vice-captain withdrew his hand from his sword hilt and spoke in a casual, understated tone, ordering everyone to clear out from the祭坛.

"You all... we were merely curious. As you can see, we haven't touched anything. Is it still possible for us to leave in time?"

The treant's giant eye stared at the vice-captain. Upon hearing those words, it seemed to show not a single flicker of emotion.

Then came a roaring blast—violent winds erupted, gravel sprayed everywhere, and the ground was smashed deep into a large crater:

The vice-captain was instantly smashed into meat paste by the treant's vines.

It was like someone crushing a fly with their hand; his entire body was embedded into the wall opposite.

The vice-captain, who had just moments before been pleased with his Saint-tier strength, was eliminated in one stroke by the vines the next...

Late night fell, and the entire church became extraordinarily silent.

Due to his own curse being extremely urgent, only about a week remained.

This was a profoundly lethal matter for Merlin, making his entire mood tense and restless.

Although Merlin very much wanted to depart immediately and head straight for the great forest on Glenn Plain, the journey ahead would leave Alice and old Arkalon somewhat fatigued, so it would be best to rest and recuperate for one night before setting out.

So Merlin did not show any dissatisfaction. Instead, he coordinated for everyone to rest within the church for one night, and depart early the following morning for the祭坛 deep within the great forest.

Although they had caught a lead on Dracula, because the curse was pressing so urgently, Merlin still could not bring himself to feel joyful.

Merlin carefully pondered over the nature of vampires, creatures that needed to subsist by feeding on human blood, which seemed to share a remarkable parallel with himself.

He needed to continuously slay Saint-tier warriors and steal their life force in order to delay the curse's onset. What, exactly, was the difference between him and those vampires? Only his demands happened to be somewhat unusual.

Merlin's thoughts drifted back to events from long ago—that black-clothed figure he had encountered in the cave, who had driven a golden spike viciously into his heart. Ever since, the curse had accompanied him, but it had also unleashed his power.

He felt that mysterious figure seemed as though he had been deliberately waiting for him. Why not someone else? Why was it him who had endured such a terrifying experience?

As for that spike driven into his heart, Merlin had not removed it to this day, nor did he know what it was. Later it had simply vanished into thin air, leaving only a deeply unsettling scar.

Merlin felt that unless he resolved the curse, disaster would inevitably strike sooner or later. He might very well be forced onto the path of the Rakshasa, unable to cease his slaughter for the rest of his life, all just to survive.

The hour was already very late. Because of the paroxysmal pain in his chest, Merlin simply could not fall asleep. Within the remaining seven days, the suffering brought by the curse had already become continuous, revealing just how dire the situation was.

Unable to sleep, Merlin had no choice but to climb alone to the church roof, lean his back against the cross, and hide there alone, gazing at the moon.

He had decided: if he went to the祭坛 this time and could not find suitable prey, he would have no choice but to leave Alice behind and use his remaining time to kill someone, in order to relieve the pain inflicted by the curse.

Merlin would never kill Alice simply to ease the curse in his heart. That was something he found it impossible to do.

In the past, Merlin might have chosen to strike without hesitation.

But now, having grown close to her, Merlin simply could not bring himself to lay a hand on Alice.

Even the thought of leaving was, in Merlin's mind, for Alice's own good. During an outbreak of his curse, he would be like a ticking time bomb, dangerous to everyone around him.

Merlin could still control himself now, but what if, under the domination of an intense survival instinct, he lost control?

Merlin did not have much confidence in himself either, so at the final moment he chose to leave Alice—it would be better for both of them.

Quiet footsteps emerged from the stairway. Merlin turned his head and saw Alice climbing up the stairs, her face peeking around the edge like a marmot.

"Oh! You're actually here! I knew it—out in the middle of nowhere, if you weren't in your room, where else would you be wandering about?" Alice wore a triumphant expression, as though finding Merlin's hiding place were some great accomplishment.

"Why are you here? It's late at night—why not get some rest and come harass me? Don't you know we have to head for that祭坛 tomorrow?" Merlin frowned. He rarely enjoyed quiet solitude and did not welcome being disturbed.

"... " Alice hesitated for a moment, her face full of grievance as she said, "I was just... coming to check on you..."

"Why couldn't you look at any other time, but specifically choose the middle of the night? Is something wrong with your head?" Merlin frowned and shot back a sarcastic remark.

"How noisy you are! You have the nerve to scold me? Why aren't you going to rest obediently so late at night? What are you doing running off to a place like this all by yourself?" Alice asked curiously.

"Me? I just... wanted to be alone for a while," Merlin replied indifferently.

Alice knitted her delicate brows, climbed up from below, and came to the church roof, silently sitting beside Merlin.

In truth, when she had seen Merlin looking unwell during the day, Alice had already begun to worry about him and wanted to see what was wrong.

Her not sleeping so late was also due to Alice's inner concern for Merlin; she feared he would start feeling unwell again and wanted to take care of him.

As a result, Alice had searched Merlin's room thoroughly but found no trace of him, and instead had found him on the church roof.

Merlin cast a glance at Alice sitting beside him, noticing her silver hair stirring in the wind under the moonlight, looking extraordinarily enchanting.

"I told you I wanted to be alone—why are you coming over?"

"To keep you company," Alice responded in a deliberately nonchalant manner.

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue in dissatisfaction and said coldly, "If you're having another episode of your savior complex and want to take care of me, I advise you to drop that notion. I'm fine right now; you needn't worry yourself unnecessarily."

"If you weren't physically uncomfortable, would you be hiding out here all by yourself?" Alice turned her head and looked into Merlin's eyes, almost as if she were provoking him.

Merlin's gaze flickered, and feigning calmness, he said, "Even if I'm alone and physically uncomfortable, what kind of reasoning is that? Don't act as though you already understand me so well. Compared to me, you self-righteous do-gooder are worlds apart."

"Though I don't understand others very well, I... still understand you," Alice said confidently, continuing, "An demon with pride not commonly found—when you're unwell, you become irritable and short-tempered, snarling at everyone. Don't you dislike it when others sympathize with or pity you? You wish to always appear strong and unconquerable. Such an imperious heart—quite like a petulant child throwing a tantrum, really..."

"What nonsense are you spouting?" Merlin's face darkened, and the veins on his forehead twitched; in truth, Alice had struck a painful nerve, making him feel very much embarrassed.

Although Merlin kept a stern expression, inwardly he was very startled. Having spent too much time with Alice, this dreadful woman already understood his nature so well! ?

"Hah, angered?" Alice let out a cold laugh and continued to add, in a cooing tone—"

"You've hit the bullseye on my sore spot, so now you're flying into a rage out of humiliation, hmph~!"

(∞叮?

title: Chapter 13 — Stubborn Old Man
content:
Chapter 13 — Stubborn Old Man

Volume 15 · Chapter 13

"After all, I didn't want to take care of you, so don't overthink it. I just came outside to get some fresh air, and I happened to sit next to you." Alice said angrily.

Listening to Alice's lame excuse, Merlin had black lines streaking down his forehead. "Actually, you'd be better off staying farther away from me."

"Why?" Alice turned her head to look at Merlin, not knowing why he suddenly said such strange words.

"After all, I'm a demon and you're a human, so we're fundamentally different, right?" Merlin said meaningfully.

"What's the point of saying this now? If it was before, we were different, but now whether you're a demon or human doesn't matter. We..... Alice hesitated, her face flushed, she almost said 'husband and wife' but swallowed it back, afraid Merlin would retort, 'We are... partners, striving to live together, even if you're a demon, what does it matter?'"

"What I mean is, we used to be enemies, and our grudges haven't been resolved, right? Actually, do you especially hate me in your heart?" Merlin asked tentatively, recalling how he used to bully Alice; this grudge isn't so easily resolved.

"I'm a forgetful person; things have long passed, and I've pretty much forgotten them." Alice hugged her knees, expressionless, and said, "I'm no longer a Hero, and you're not some utterly wicked Great Demon Lord. Now we're just busy adventurers every day. Holding onto the past, am I really that narrow-minded?"

"You're too naive. If you believe me so much, what would you do if I, for some reason, drew my sword against you?" Merlin asked with interest, wanting to see how Alice would answer.

"Drawing swords against each other? Impossible." Alice laughed and shook her head, thinking Merlin was joking.

"Why are you so confident? I really would draw my sword against you." Merlin said with a stern face, thinking that if his own life couldn't be guaranteed, he might not care about anything else.

"Because I trust you, I believe you wouldn't do that to me." Alice looked at Merlin beside her and added, "After all, if you didn't have that demon exterior, you'd still be a decent person."

"A good person? I think there's something wrong with your eyes..."

Merlin gave Alice a light jab, but seeing how much she trusted him, he felt uneasy instead.

Turns out Alice never even considered the possibility that I would draw my sword against her.

Such a naive idiot; if I weren't by her side, Ken would probably be scammed to death.

Although Alice trusts me so much, I do feel a little happy.

But staying by her side is indeed dangerous, like a time bomb; who knows when something might go wrong....

Merlin felt guilty about Alice's trust in him; he had no confidence that, with the curse worsening, he wouldn't end up drawing his sword against her.

"And you? Will you draw your sword against me in the future? For example, when I'm extremely weak?"

"Of course! I'm a dreamer; someday I'll step on your face with my feet and humiliate you." Alice immediately showed a spirited fighting spirit, still not forgetting her unrealistic daydream.

Merlin's forehead veins twitched, his teeth itched angrily, and a phrase burst from his mouth--

"Go on dreaming, you damned girl...."

The next day.

At dawn, the three planned to board an ox cart heading to the southern great forest of Glen Plains, and the priest also got up to see them off.

Merlin and Alice hadn't rested much last night; their mental state wasn't fully refreshed, but it was still okay.

Alice, worried about Merlin's discomfort, stayed with him all night, sitting stiffly in the church's chamber, blowing the wind all night.

However, Old Akalon slept very comfortably last night; upon waking, he was full of vigor, and despite his age, his whole body brimmed with energy.

"Friends, let's embark on a new journey! I can't wait to unveil the mystery of the altar together with you!"

Merlin and Alice remained silent, expressionless, watching Old Akalon excitedly waving his arms and legs; they probably didn't expect bringing this old man to such a dangerous place as the altar.

"Why are you listless? Are youngsters nowadays all lacking vitality?" Old Akalon said doubtfully.

"Well... Mr. Akalon, are you also planning to come with us?" Alice asked hesitantly, thinking the altar was so dangerous that bringing the elderly Akalon along seemed like a bad idea.

"Of course, venturing into such dangerous territory, I couldn't rest easy if I didn't accompany you." Old Akalon showed the demeanor of a senior; in truth, he just didn't want to be left behind. It was rare for him to set out on an adventure, and it made him feel young again.

Merlin's expression grew complex; he thought that going to the altar might bring unknown dangers, and bringing Old Akalon would inevitably distract them, since although this old man is a Silver-ranked adventurer, he's essentially just an ordinary person, likely to be a burden.

"But the altar is very dangerous; if you come with us, I'm afraid I won't be able to look after you." Alice put it tactfully, without outright saying Akalon would hinder their progress.

"Yeah, you're 102 years old; you'd better stay in the church and wait for those two lords to return." The priest, noticing Alice's intent, chimed in to persuade.

"Although I'm old, I possess unparalleled adventuring experience. For this trip to the dangerous altar, I will surely use my experience to help them. Moreover, my adventuring spirit still burns fiercely; if I retreat out of fear of danger, that would be a blemish on my career." Old Akalon spoke with fervor, yet he gave others a somewhat chuuni feeling.

"Tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue impatiently, then dropped any pretense and said directly, "Mr. Akalon, I know you're a model worker in the adventurer industry, but you're just an ordinary person. If danger arises, we'll definitely have to protect your safety, which means we can't go all out against the enemy. Staying behind would be good for both me and you. Of course, I'm not saying you're a burden; it's just that your experience is valuable to the guild, and if something happened, I and Alice couldn't afford the responsibility."

"No need to worry about this old fool's safety; for an adventurer, dying in battle is honor." Old Akalon was especially stubborn, shifting the topic.

"Besides, couldn't Lord Merlin go as well? You're a lower-ranked adventurer than me, and you're not afraid, so what's there for a Silver-ranked adventurer like me to fear?"

"...... Merlin's face turned black, being shut down by that remark from Old Akalon—"

"He actually... actually looked down on me!?"

"This old guy is just a Silver-ranked adventurer; what's he getting all arrogant about?"

(叭叶)

title: Chapter 14 — Deep into the Secret Chamber
content:
Chapter 14 — Deep into the Secret Chamber

Volume 15 · Chapter 14

After two days of travel, Merlin and the others reached the outskirts of the Great Forest.

The road had been completely destroyed by floodwaters, and the central altar was clearly visible.

"That must be the altar the priest mentioned," Merlin stood up and gazed at the towering pillars.

"Shouldn't be wrong; we've arrived," Alice nodded, feeling it was relatively calm, with no seemingly dangerous threats nearby.

"The timing is good; let's push straight to the altar!" Old Akalaon said enthusiastically, completely oblivious to the fate of his carriage; "charging" was merely an illusion.

In the end, Merlin and Alice still couldn't persuade the stubborn Akalaon, so they brought him along, heading for the altar.

Although Old Akalaon was of little real use, he was a guide. Now, finding someone familiar with France was indeed not easy.

"Akalaon, if you encounter any danger, just hide behind me; I'll make sure you're safe," Merlin said, being cautious.

"Merlin, you're being too impetuous," Akalaon replied. "Although I'm already elderly and my body is past its prime, I'm still a higher-ranked adventurer than you. If danger arises, I should be the one protecting you."

Old Akalaon urged the carriage forward, his tone growing dissatisfied. He felt Merlin was just an iron-class adventurer, having no say in the team, yet daring to demand protection, making himself seem like a burden.

"Huh?" Merlin paused, thinking that in this world, those qualified to protect themselves probably haven't even been born. This old man has such a big mouth. "It seems you've misunderstood. What I mean is, if you hide behind me, it'll be safer, that way we can all fight with our full strength."

"Don't worry, I'll absolutely not cause you any trouble. But if danger truly arises, it's obviously safer to hide behind Lady Alice, wouldn't you agree?"

Old Akalaon didn't really believe in Merlin's strength; his words were emphasizing Alice's status in the team.

Even if an iron-class adventurer went mad, they couldn't compare to the silver-class elites.

Akalaon figured that even if he was a burden to the team, Alice was the one qualified for that, not Merlin, an iron-class adventurer.

Alice looked embarrassed, thinking that hiding behind her was useless. If they encountered a too-strong enemy, she wouldn't be able to handle it either, and in the end, she would have to ask Merlin for assistance. But Merlin willing to protect Old Akalaon was a good thing.

"Grandpa, trust me, I'm really strong." Merlin stepped forward and patted Akalaon's shoulder, speaking with a serious face.

Old Akalaon said nothing, but turned his head to look at Merlin, his eyes filled with confusion, as if saying "one more word..."

"Merlin, are you joking with me?"

"I'm a silver-class adventurer; do I need six iron-class adventurers to protect me?"

"If this continues, I might lose my reputation and become a laughingstock in the industry...."

The three of them arrived at the altar location smoothly. Along the way, they encountered no attacks, and it looked very calm.

They had originally thought they would face some unknown danger, but the reality was much safer than imagined.

However, just as they were thinking this, they discovered more than ten corpses with distorted faces hanging from the tree in the center of the altar. Some had been completely dismembered.

Blood had soaked the withered trunk, congealing into black, eerie things below. It looked quite bizarre.

Seeing such a bloody scene and smelling the decay in the air, Alice suddenly felt nauseous and retched instinctively.

"What's going on?" Merlin asked without changing his expression. The bloody scene before him had no effect.

"This group of people was probably the exploration team the priest mentioned. They arrived here first and suffered danger; it looks like no one survived," Old Akalaon said, his voice somewhat hoarse. He hadn't seen such a bloody scene in a long time, which reminded him of the cruelty of the adventurer's industry, always accompanied by danger.

"So... Alice forcibly suppressed her nausea, showing a worried face. "There is indeed something dangerous in the altar; we must be more vigilant."

"Let's first explore the surroundings and see if there's anything special; maybe we can figure out what happened to this exploration team?" Old Akalaon suggested.

Merlin didn't look around the altar like Alice and Akalaon, but surveyed everything around.

Finally, Merlin fixed his gaze on a towering giant tree in the distance. Internally, he marveled that there could be such ancient giant trees here, and also wondered—

Before entering the Great Forest, were there such tall trees here?

Merlin stared at the giant tree, very puzzled. If there had always been such a giant tree here, it should have been visible before entering the altar. However, it seemed there weren't such tall trees just now; where did it suddenly come from? He wondered.

But before Merlin could delve deeper into thought, a strange voice came from Akalaon's side.

"You guys come quick! There's a secret room door here; it looks like it's been opened!"

Hearing the news, Merlin and Alice quickly went to Old Akalaon's side and found a stone door that was half-concealed, clearly having been pried open.

"Perhaps this is the interior of the altar?" Akalaon guessed, then asked, "What should we do next? Now that we've found the path to the altar's core, it's best to go in and investigate. Maybe the three oldest vampires the priest mentioned have also been here."

Alice looked at the stone door of the secret room, undecided, and secretly asked Merlin, "What should we do? Should we go in and take a look?"

Merlin thought for a moment, feeling that since they've come this far, they definitely can't return empty-handed; they must investigate the mysterious altar thoroughly.

"Let's go in."

The three of them entered the altar's secret room.

Merlin and Alice walked in front, holding torches to guard against dangers rushing out of the darkness ahead.

In this narrow environment, Old Akalaon began to show a timid expression, silently hiding behind the two of them, glancing at everything around with sly eyes.

In fact, Old Akalaon had never experienced danger or high-difficulty tasks.

Those 999,999 tasks, without exception, were low-level tasks, basically helping neighbors find cats, or running errands to buy things.

Delving into the altar, this was probably the first time in Old Akalaon's life that he encountered a task with extremely high danger coefficients, and also the most dangerous place he had ever been.

Old Akalaon's heart was very contradictory; because for the first time undertaking a dangerous task, he felt incredibly excited, but his courage was small, fearing he would die here.

But Akalaon had always dreamed of experiencing a real adventure. Even knowing there was danger, he hard-muscled his way to follow behind.

The three of them walked along the dark corridor, not knowing how long it took, finally reaching the end of the secret room.

"What is this?" Alice asked in surprise.

Following the gaze of the three of them, they saw a beam of light shining down from the ceiling of the secret room, converging onto a high platform--

At the top was a dim sealed silver bottle.

White runes were attached to the bottle's mouth, and the black characters on it were very similar to the oldest doctrines.

Alice was somewhat familiar with this rune; it was a tool used by the Holy Church's heresy inquisitors to seal evil. However, the one in front was obviously much higher level.

Just as the three were about to step forward to examine it carefully, they heard a voice from the darkness beside them—

"Don't kill...."

"Please don't kill us..."

"We... we'll never dare again..."

title: Chapter 15 — Frenzied Tree Spirit
content:
Chapter 15 — Frenzied Tree Spirit

Volume 15 · Chapter 15

"Who's there?" Merlin was startled by the sudden voice.

"Could it be a survivor from the earlier expedition? The outer stone door clearly shows signs of having been pried open, so it's possible someone survived. Old Alcaston pondered.

"Is that so?" Merlin furrowed his brow, finding the whole situation rather suspicious. First there were corpses hanging outside, then a mysterious bottle in the hidden chamber, and now a survivor. No matter how you looked at it, this couldn't be anything simple.

Alice held her torch and slowly moved toward the sound, intending to investigate further.

Just then, a figure dressed similarly to the earlier expedition team was crouched in the corner, trembling and shaking. It was that talkative little rogue, who had somehow miraculously survived while all his companions were killed.

The little rogue realized something was wrong when he saw the deputy leader being slapped dead by a dryad.

With five escape routes available, the little rogue placed his hopes in the depths of the altar. Even though it was dangerous here, he had no choice but to hide in order to stay alive.

As it turned out, his choice was correct. After hiding inside, he wasn't threatened at all.

The little rogue clutched his head, his face pale and terrified, as if still in a daze.

"Hey, are you okay?" Alice shone her torchlight on the surviving thief.

The surviving rogue looked up at Alice with a blank expression, then suddenly bolted toward the outside, as if half out of his mind.

"Don't kill me! Please, don't kill me!"

"Huh? What the hell?"

Alice was frightened by the survivor's reaction. She wasn't a bad person, so why would she kill him?

"This guy is really weird," Old Alcaston furrowed his brow, wondering what this survivor had been through.

"Merlin, you stay here. I'm going to catch that guy—he probably knows something," Alice said and rushed out to grab the man and get to the bottom of things.

Merlin hadn't even finished his sentence before Alice had already dashed out of the chamber.

That person was clearly half out of his mind. Even if they caught him, what useful information could they get?

Merlin's original intention was to ignore the person who had just fled and let him die on his own. But Alice was simply too reckless.

Moving around in such a dangerous place and falling behind was obviously not a good thing.

"What should we do, Merlin? Miss Alice has already chased after him, so shouldn't we follow too? Without Miss Alice's protection, both you and I are in danger." Old Alcaston was feeling uneasy, thinking that two of the weakest people sticking together was really terrible.

"Isn't the more pressing concern the bottle over there?" Merlin's gaze shifted to the platform in the chamber, where the dim silver bottle sat quietly.

"But... without Miss Alice—"

"Don't worry. Alice won't be in any danger. Haven't we been safe the whole way?"

Originally, Old Alcaston was feeling uneasy and hesitating whether to chase after Alice, but Merlin cut him off.

Old Alcaston thought it over. Indeed, the journey had been peaceful so far, with no dangers encountered. Worrying about Alice's safety was less productive than worrying about himself.

"Merlin is right. I was being overly anxious..."

"Mr. Alcaston, do you recognize that bottle up there? It doesn't look like an ordinary object." Merlin tentatively asked.

"I don't know. I've never seen a bottle shaped like that before, but I think it's probably something very evil." Old Alcaston spoke cautiously, not daring to say anything reckless in this situation.

"Something very evil? On what basis?" Merlin asked in surprise.

Old Alcaston recalled his own experiences and slowly speculated, "There are talismans pasted on it. This is the kind of thing the Holy Church's inquisitors use to suppress evil. Did you see the text on it? Those should be ancient scriptures from the doctrine. This talisman is probably very old, so whatever's sealed inside that bottle is likely something very ominous. We're..."

"Is that so? This ordinary-looking paper is actually that amazing?" Merlin had already walked up to the bottle by now. With a "rustle," he tore off the talisman and held it up to examine.

"Huh?!?!" Old Alcaston was so startled by Merlin's action that he could barely form coherent sentences. "...Mr. Merlin! ...What are you—"

"What are you doing? You said it was so amazing, of course I have to study it carefully!" Merlin said with righteous indignation, glancing at the talisman in his hand and thinking it was just some old, worn-out scrap of paper. Aside from the faintly mysterious black text, it seemed to have nothing special about it.

"Mr. Merlin! Are you even listening to me? Why are you tearing off the talisman? This is so arbitrary!" Old Alcaston became agitated, his mustache bristling and eyes bulging, his voice rising in exasperation.

"Don't get so worked up. I just tore it off. I wasn't planning to open the bottle or anything." Merlin waved his hands dismissively, thinking it was no big deal.

"Come on, listen to me. Didn't I explain clearly enough? The talisman is meant to suppress evil. By tearing it off, you've broken its effect. You're going to release whatever evil was sealed in there!" Old Alcaston frantically clutched his head, complaining with a heavy sigh. Why were young people these days so impatient, never willing to listen to an elder's words?

Merlin broke into a cold sweat, feeling awkward as he said, "There's no need to make such a big deal out of this. Nothing has happened, right?"

No sooner had he finished speaking than a loud "clink-clink-clink" echoed through the chamber.

The silver stopper of the bottle on the platform was mysteriously knocked into the air and fell to the ground with a clatter.

"EEEEEE!!!" Old Alcaston screamed, thinking some terrible entity was about to appear, and immediately revealed his true nature by hiding.

Merlin only felt a wave of unease. He picked up the bottle and looked inside, only to find... nothing.

Apart from that brief moment when the stopper had inexplicably popped up, this bottle was just ordinary street vendor merchandise, with no special features at all. There was nothing sealed inside, no evil whatsoever. It was all nonsense!

"Mr. Merlin?!... Are you okay? Did you encounter some evil?" Old Alcaston peeked out from behind the rock, too afraid to show his face.

"Come out. There's nothing there. Stop scaring yourself." Merlin replied with a completely unconcerned expression, having lost interest in the bottle and putting it back.

"...No way?" Old Alcaston cautiously peered out.

...

But what followed was a tremendous rumbling. The entire chamber began to shake violently.

"...See? I told you something bad would happen! I said not to mess with that talisman. This is the end!" Old Alcaston crouched behind the rock, trembling with his backside sticking out, clearly inexperienced with dangerous expeditions.

Merlin remained calm and observed the situation, furrowing his brow.

This doesn't seem related to us.

"There are people fighting outside..."

"Cough!"

Alice coughed up a mouthful of blood, her body slammed hard to the ground by the vines, then sent flying like a cannonball!

Countless vines swirled through the air like a storm, writhing and twisting in all directions.

The ancient and powerful dryad was awakened once more, and its first target was to tear apart the intruding mouse that had dared to trespass.

The massive tree trunk slowly writhed, and its withered branches stretched out like tentacles, attacking Alice.

The dryad seemed to have gone completely berserk, splitting its enormous mouth open and roaring furiously.

"She's gone!"

"She's escaped from the place where she was sealed!"

"Look at what you've done! You've thrown everything into chaos!"

"Evil will plague this world. Even the almighty gods won't find peace!"

title: Chapter 16 — Monthly Ticket Bonus
content:
Chapter 16 — Monthly Ticket Bonus

Volume 15 · Chapter 16

Alice had been chasing after the sole survivor of the exploration team, but the moment they stepped out of the secret chamber, that person had vanished like they'd been vaporized into thin air.

Just as Alice was puzzling over this, the ground beneath the entire forest began to tremble. In the distance, the mighty ancient tree—seemingly summoned—stirred from its slumber and awoke.

Seeing Alice, the powerful treant flew into a rage and without hesitation launched an attack.

Vines lashed down like a raging tsunami, striking with merciless force.

Alice hadn't even figured out what was happening before she drew her sword in panic to fend off the assault, only to find that this treant's strength was extraordinary—truly beyond words.

The vines crashed down, sending Alice flying. She spat up blood, grievously wounded.

Alice, who had reached the pinnacle of Saint-tier strength, found herself up against this treant and was completely overwhelmed in a single exchange!

It seemed that compared to Alice, whose magical power stood at the peak of the Saint-tier, this treant's strength was overwhelmingly superior.

The treant had clearly sensed that someone had opened the bottle in the secret chamber. Countless time guardians had been stationed here, and it had finally reached its limit of patience!

Alice gripped her slender sword tightly and slowly pushed herself back to her feet.

That barrage of vines had clearly taken its toll. Her magical energy and internal qi were beginning to churn chaotically within her.

Alice had thought her strength was such that she needn't fear any dangerous enemy, but reality proved otherwise. The treant before her was clearly suppressing her.

The treant's emotions were out of control, its oppressive aura brimming with aggression, instilling a deep sense of dread.

Alice wiped the blood from her lips, roused her fighting spirit, and felt the crushing pressure of her opponent—an unfamiliar realm of power, a cultivation level.

This treant's strength had transcended the Saint-tier, reaching an even more powerful realm. No wonder Alice was struggling to hold her ground even in a single exchange.

This was an ancient forest of immense antiquity. When the ancestors of the Glen Plains migrated here, this forest may have already existed. It was no surprise that this treant was over 600 years old, and its cultivation-level strength was plausible.

Alice recalled what her master had once said on the snow-capped mountains: "Beyond the human world there are humans, beyond the heavens there are heavens. Never be complacent about your own strength."

Now she realized her master's words were true. This world was vast, filled with countless unknown things.

Alice felt as though her bones were about to dislocate. She gritted her teeth through the tearing pain, lifted her head, and gazed up at the massive treant.

"What nonsense are you babbling?"

"We haven't done anything, you know."

The treant heard Alice's words, bent down with its enormous eyes glaring at her, and roared with its mouth open.

"How dare you say you haven't done anything?!?"

"You opened the bottle!"

"Inside is sealed the source of evil."

"SF Light Novel"

"If the world falls into chaos because of this, you are criminals!!!"

The tremendous sound wave forced Alice to step back several paces, her eardrums aching from the treant's roar.

A heavy stench spewed from the treant's mouth, making Alice scrunch up her face.

A bottle? Could it be the one in the secret chamber?

No way—did Merlin and Arcanum open that thing?!

This was done without consulting me. What exactly is sealed inside?!

Alice's heart raced with anxiety. Perhaps her group had done something wrong, and the treant wasn't really an enemy—just that they had violated some taboo.

"I still don't know what's going on. Maybe our companions did something to anger you. I think there's been a misunderstanding. Can we calm down and talk this through?"

"Pointless words! You meager humans, time and again you come to disturb this forest, trampling what I protect. Now you've finally brought disaster upon us. Only with your lives can I quell my rage!"

The treant roared, raising its arm and forming a fist as large as a city gate. Its cultivation-level pressure surged, making it hard for Alice to breathe.

This punch wasn't a joke. In her current state, taking this blow would mean certain death.

A cold sweat trickled down Alice's forehead as she called out, "You're the guardian of this altar, right? We're not bad people—we just came here to investigate some things."

"Don't try to deceive me! I've seen too much of humanity's cunning. I won't believe a single word you say. Die!"

The treant roared and brought its massive fist crashing down toward Alice.

Don't let its appearance fool you—though it looked like ordinary black wood, its hardness was extraordinary, rivaling steel.

The force of the blow was like a massive iron hammer descending from the sky. Combined with the enhancement of cultivation-level energy, even a Saint-tier warrior would be reduced to meat paste under this single punch!

Facing this desperate suppression, Alice's spirit grew faint, and she was on the verge of being overwhelmed by fear.

Yet, having sparred with Merlin countless times and faced death threats repeatedly, she was already accustomed to it.

At this critical moment with no escape...

Alice bit through her own lip, using the pain to sharpen her awareness.

At a speed visible to the naked eye, sapphire dragon scales erupted across her body, quickly spreading over her entire form.

When Alice opened her eyes again, her irises shone with golden light, and two horns—identical to those of the Frost Saint Dragon—sprouted from her brow.

Then, draconic membranes burst forth from her back, unfurling into wings!

A chill spread everywhere. 50% of her draconic transformation power was unleashed...

"Paku"

In the corridor of the secret chamber.

Merlin realized a fight had broken out outside and immediately guessed that Alice, who had just rushed out alone, had encountered an enemy.

Since the journey up until now had been smooth and peaceful, Alice running into trouble the moment she stepped out meant he must have overlooked something.

Merlin quickened his pace as he hurried toward the exit of the secret chamber, all the while pondering what kind of opponent this could be.

Even in this deep corridor, he could feel that oppressive pressure—stronger than even the combined might of the Four Elemental Sword Saints.

Alice's draconic aura had even been suppressed. This opponent was clearly no easy target—a genuine cultivation-level powerhouse who had transcended the Saint-tier, not some scrub who merely brushed against the threshold like the Four Elemental Sword Saints.

Merlin's steps quickened instinctively, a mysterious smile playing on his lips as his heart soared with excitement.

With the curse manifesting in less than a week, encountering such a rare and formidable opponent was like rain on the parched earth for Merlin.

Merlin now desperately needed to steal life with the demon sword Banri Garan. This prey, exuding cultivation-level aura, had already caught his attention.

If he didn't devour this incoming meal, he was doomed.

Merlin felt like a madman fighting in an internet café, only to see the computer flash "five minutes remaining."

In such a desperate situation, he somehow managed to dig into his pocket and pull out five yuan!

At this very moment, Merlin wanted to shout from the bottom of his heart—

"Game master! Add five yuan to machine #30!"

"I feel like I can still be revived!"

title: Chapter 17 — Daredevil Squad
content:
Chapter 17 — Daredevil Squad

Volume 15 · Chapter 17

"Lord Merlin, you're running too fast... I can barely keep up with you."

Old Acalon was hot on Merlin's heels, but due to his advanced age, he was already panting after running for a while and his body could no longer keep up.

Merlin had no intention of slowing down; instead, he turned back to speak to old Acalon.

"Stay here first. It looks like there's a fierce battle going on outside, so it'll be safer to stay here."

"Miss Alice is in danger out there, how could I shrink away at the moment of crisis?!! Even if I can only share some of her burden, that would be a good thing. Shouldn't it be you, Lord Merlin, who stays here? What could a Black Iron adventurer do even if they went out?" old Acalon said incredulously, finding Merlin's excited state very unnatural.

"Ah,..." Merlin was too lazy to explain anything to Acalon. They were all low-level adventurers anyway; it was pointless when noobs fought noobs.

The two quickly ran out of the secret room, and as soon as they emerged, they began looking around. They had expected to see an intense battle, but instead—

Alice, with her horns and dragon wings, was slowly retracting her dragon transformation and sheathing her rapier.

That giant, formidable treant had its entire body frozen solid in golden ice, looking like a lifelike ice sculpture!

Alice had actually taken down a Domain-realm treant all by herself!? It was simply unbelievable!

"Wh-what was that just now?" old Acalon was utterly stunned, terrified by Alice's dragon-transformed form. "Is that really Miss Alice's true appearance?!! So terrifying, like a great dragon hiding among the crowd!"

Alice's 50% dragon transformation had indeed given her power a qualitative leap, and her appearance bore a close resemblance to the former Kingdom's Four Heroes, Carolna.

Back then, Carolna had devoured the inheritance crystal raw to awaken its power, becoming a half-human, half-dragon existence—and she had been quite inflated about it!

Now it appeared that Carolna back then hadn't been much different from Alice; she had only managed to awaken about 50% of her dragon race power.

Merlin was completely frozen in shock upon seeing this scene—not because he was amazed by Alice's growth, but because his life-extending little pill was ruined!

Damn it! How could this be!?

Alice actually took down that treant all by herself!?

He had finally encountered a strong enemy, only to be solo-killed by Alice!

What was he supposed to do!? He only had less than a week left!

Wait! How could a Domain-realm expert × be solo-killed by Alice?

This was obviously a fluke! Even if Alice's magic power had already reached the peak of Saint-tier, it was impossible to kill a higher-realm expert out of nowhere!

Merlin felt something was off. This treant wasn't some half-baked fighter like the Four Sword Saints; it was a genuine Domain-realm expert. It couldn't be so easily taken down by someone like Alice.

The truth was exactly as Merlin had thought. Just as Alice confidently turned around, thinking the battle was over—

The golden ice凝结 on the treant's body began to crack all over, then exploded with a tremendous force. It had only been frozen by Alice for about two seconds!

It seemed Alice's strength still couldn't compare to a Domain-realm treant. As expected, she couldn't defeat it.

Breaking free from the ice, the treant let out a roar and punched Alice hard, sending her flying backward. It showed no mercy toward the intruders in its forest.

Alice spat blood, her entire body blasted over a hundred meters by the treant before she finally came to a stop. She instantly lost her fighting ability.

Her body, which hadn't fully recovered from the dragon transformation, was struck again heavily, and Alice's injuries worsened even more than before.

The severe pain was unbearable for Alice, and she no longer had the strength to get back on her feet.

A Domain-realm treant had only needed two attacks to put Alice, at the peak of Saint-tier, in crisis.

"Miss Alice!" old Acalon, who had been hiding at a distance and watching, immediately cried out when he saw Alice getting hammered by the treant.

A bead of cold sweat ran down Merlin's forehead. He thought, as expected. Alice's current strength was quite decent among Saint-tier adventurers, but she was completely defenseless against a Domain-realm expert.

However, this situation was actually very good for Merlin. As long as the treant wasn't dead, Merlin could calmly collect his life-extending little pill.

Merlin reached for the long sword at his waist, ready to make his move. He wouldn't hesitate to slaughter this treant.

Although he still hadn't figured out its identity, Merlin's curse was about to erupt, and he could no longer suppress his killing intent.

"Old man, step back. Leave this to me. I'll go rescue Miss Alice."

"Don't be ridiculous, Lord Merlin..." old Acalon grabbed hold of Merlin, who was about to charge forward, and said with a serious expression, "You're just a Black Iron adventurer. You couldn't possibly defeat that powerful treant. I'm a higher rank than you and have more experience, so leave this to me. I will definitely rescue Miss Alice."

"Huh?" Merlin could barely hold back at this old man's nonsense and said helplessly, "Just go rest over there. I don't need to exert much effort to deal with an enemy like this."

"Enough, Lord Merlin! Don't talk big at a time like this!" old Acalon scolded. Sensing the urgency of the situation, his emotions became a bit agitated. "Miss Alice, our only hope, has already been defeated. If you don't follow my orders, none of the three of us will survive. Do you understand?!"

"..." Merlin was intimidated by the old man's aura and tentatively asked, "Then what do you plan to do?"

"I'll draw that treant away, and you'll take the heavily injured Miss Alice and escape." old Acalon nervously swallowed, his face ashen as he stared at the distant treant. Clearly, he was terrified inside, but it was the best plan he could come up with.

"We escape... and what about you?" Merlin looked at old Acalon in surprise.

"Lord Merlin, I'm already old. Even if I die here to save you two, it wouldn't be a waste at all. Consider it returning my life to Karl!" old Acalon's forehead veins bulged. After struggling bitterly within, he had made this decision. "If you think sacrificing this useless old man is worthwhile, then carry on my adventurer spirit and keep living! Sacrificing oneself for one's companions—that is the highest honor of an adventurer!"

"..." Merlin looked at old Acalon's passionate appearance and felt too embarrassed to pour cold water on him.

Compared to Acalon, this old man was a genuine, real adventurer, while Merlin's resolve was many miles behind.

It was said that adventurers lived for freedom, but that was completely absent from Merlin. Yet in old Acalon, it was profoundly genuine.

Merlin felt that throughout his life, he had been a fake adventurer, while old Acalon was the real deal.

"Lord Merlin! Follow my lead and charge together! Rescue Miss Alice!" old Acalon drew the hand crossbow at his waist and roared, charging toward the treant like a suicide squad.

"emmmmm..." Merlin remained silent, making no move to follow behind, watching Acalon's aged figure charging at the treant with twin crossbows—

Why does it have to be so tragic, like a suicide squad?

content:
Chapter 18 — One Encounter (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 15 · Chapter 18

Alice felt as if all the bones in her body were about to be broken by this treant. The intense pain made it very difficult for her to move again.

She had thought she had successfully sealed this powerful treant, but who would have thought the opponent would be so strong!

Alice realized that the oppressive might crushing her was not fake, but a real existence surpassing the Saint-tier!

"....Damn, why isn't my magic working?

The treant doesn't seem to have suffered much damage, it - - steps toward the fallen Alice, mocking with a sound like distant thunder.

"You, a mere human, actually have the power of a dragon? Did you eat something from a dragon's brain?"

Alice gritted her teeth. She had no strength left to speak, but she was still astonished to think that this treant knows about the inheritance crystal! How old is it exactly?

"Things like that only appear with very low probability. Getting one is truly lucky for a fellow, but even if you obtain the power of a dragon, you probably can't fully unleash it. After all, even true dragons - only one in ten thousand can fully unleash their power. Although the dragon race's power is formidable, even they themselves find it difficult to master, how laughable." The treant didn't step forward, and the ground would tremble. Its huge wooden body, though moving somewhat slowly, is as steady as a giant.

Alice couldn't help but frown. She didn't understand what the treant was saying. She felt the other party is an ancient treant, and its knowledge is beyond comparison. What do you mean dragons can't fully unleash their power? How is that possible?

"You dare to use stolen dragon race power to deal with me. For thousands of millions of years, humans haven't changed. Greedy nature is always hidden deep in the heart, coveting the power of other races, yet feeling inferior about being human. Boldly infiltrating the altar, isn't it just to covet the evil power within?" The treant walked up to Alice and slowly squatted down, looking down at the human like an ant.

......Alice gasped in pain, annoyed and said, "Who is coveting the evil power of the altar? We are. Just here to investigate the vampire race?" 2) Thistle Novel

"Oh? Vampire race? A completely unknown species..." The treant showed a look of confusion, completely unaware that vampires exist.

Alice suddenly realized, suddenly reacting to how long this treant has gone without leaving the forest? Not even knowing about the vampire race?

Could it be that the treant came to this forest at a time when vampires didn't exist yet? Thinking about it.....

The three vampires that came out from here are truly the first vampires in the world? ! !

Alice realized that the treant in front might know a lot of things. At the very least, those ancient legends might be verifiable.

....Are you the guardian of this forest?

"No, I am ordered to guard the altar." The treant's voice corrected like thunder.

"Whose order?" Alice gritted her teeth and asked, enduring the pain.

"Of course it is the great goddess.

The treant showed a pious look, as if having its own faith.

"Goddess? Maria?" Alice blurted out this name, as a believer of the Holy Church, she is most familiar with the name of the Goddess of Light.

In the classical records of the Church, it is recorded that only two deities are still alive in the whole world - one is the Goddess of Light representing justice, Maria. The other represents the evil ruler of hell, Satan.

They are both human-born, representing the deities of all humanity. As for the deities of other races, they perished during the gods' twilight. This is the fundamental reason why humans are prosperous now. Other race deities are dead, and they long ago lost their right to speak.

"How can a humble human dare to call out the name of our Lord? !" The treant angrily reprimanded. Although the Goddess of Light is human-born and has already become a high-and-mighty deity, it cannot be equated with humans.

Hearing the treant's answer, Alice's whole person fell into confusion and panic. The treant in front is dispatched by the Goddess of Light, so what exactly is sealed in the bottles in this altar? !

All kinds of conspiracy feelings surged into Alice's brain. At one point she felt a wave of dizziness, and many things started to become unclear.

Alice felt that the treant in front is worth talking to, maybe she can get more secrets. The appearance of the vampire race might be related to the deities!

Just as Alice was planning to ease the tense atmosphere, a series of bowstring oscillation sounds broke the silence one after another.

"Big fellow! Go to death

Old Akalron has arrived, running to the treant's feet, bravely raising his double crossbows in his hand, shooting at it - !

He doesn't know magic or martial skills. His only attack method is also using weapons and items. Although he cannot cause damage to the treant, he still attracts the opponent's attention.

The small-sized Akalron and the huge treant form a sharp contrast. Being able to attack the treant here is worthy of praise for his courage!

o了ζE2 Xiao Zhi

However, old Akalron is too weak. The crossbow arrows flew out with a whooshing sound, and in the end could only hit the treant's knee - that's already the limit!

Old Akalron's expression was crazy, the veins on his forehead stood out, constantly roaring at the treant, already having a resolve to die.

"Spit ah ah ah ah ah ah!

.-. Is this looking for death? - Old Akalron was originally some dragging the team back, now things have become more troublesome.

Alice doesn't know why Merlin didn't stop old Akalron, but let this old man come to such a dangerous place.

The treant slowly turned its body, looking down at old Kalron. It didn't expect such a thing to dare provoke itself, so it narrowed its eyes like copper bells, revealing killing intent.

Old Akalron feared, swallowing a mouthful of saliva, cold sweat flowing down his forehead. He ran away, while shouting while running.

"Come on big fellow! Come here! Let this old man have a good look at you!

"Thought... The treant uttered a sentence, slowly raising its giant leg, wanting to step on old Akalron directly.

Due to the treant's huge figure, no matter how fast the aging old Akalron runs, it is difficult to escape the attack.

The treant only needs to lift its leg, and easily envelop old Akalron's body in a huge shadow.

"...." Old Akalron's frightened expression froze on his face, feeling he can't escape, will be turned into meat paste "Merlin! Give me this! Quickly take Miss Alice and leave"

However, in this blink of an eye, Merlin must save old Akalron and must kill the treant, paying no heed to Alice's stop.

Seeing Merlin suddenly draw his sword, killing sword energy cutting everything, cold light flashing, accompanied by the crisp sound of drawing the sword, the battle ends one

title: Chapter 19 — Akalon, Convinced Heart and Soul
content:
Chapter 19 — Akalon, Convinced Heart and Soul

Volume 15 · Chapter 19

The towering treant was sliced in two by Merlin's blade, its two halves crashing to the ground with a tremendous crash, kicking up an enormous cloud of dust that rose up over a hundred feet into the air!

The earth beneath the forest trembled continuously, rumbling with a deep, rolling sound. The treant's fallen body directly destroyed a vast swath of trees, roughly estimated to be about one-third of the entire forest.

Merlin slowly emerged from the smoke, his face showing no dramatic fluctuations in expression—just a calm, composed demeanor.

However, Merlin's heart was genuinely feeling quite comfortable at the moment. The increasingly severe, nagging pain had dissipated like smoke, replaced by a sensation of relief after the pain—ah, so refreshing!

This particular realm-level treant had truly helped Merlin out. It had single-handedly pulled him back from the brink of death's seven-day countdown. What a relief.

For Merlin, this was the first time in his life that a curse had pushed him to such an almost explosive state. He couldn't help but secretly pat himself on the back.

Fortunately, the internal threat had now been resolved. He felt an unprecedented sense of relaxation, savoring the waves of comfort flowing through his heart.

Huh? The effect of lifting the curse this time was unexpectedly good!

Before, he had killed so many enemies, but none had felt this good.

It seems this treant's strength was no joke. Even among realm-level power tiers, it belonged to the higher echelon.

Too bad this treant had such terrible luck. It was incredibly unlucky to run into Merlin, the cursed one. It never even got to show off its true strength before being instantly killed. What a shame.

Merlin sheathed his sword, then turned toward the still-shocked old Arcan, shrugged his shoulders, and sighed helplessly.

"I'm really strong now, right? You should believe me by now. Taking down this tree spirit wasn't supposed to be such a big deal, yet you made it out like we were facing an existential threat..."

Alice's forehead broke into a cold sweat. She was no longer surprised by Merlin's overwhelming strength, but this tree spirit's power clearly surpassed the Saint-tier. Yet it still wasn't a match for Merlin?

That's truly terrifying. It can only mean one thing: Merlin's ceiling isn't at the realm level. It seems he's even stronger than that!

What kind of monster is this guy? Why isn't even a legendary existence like a realm-level being a match for Merlin?

Alice nervously swallowed, feeling not just amazement but also annoyance that Merlin hadn't listened to her advice to go easy on the tree spirit.

Now look what happened. The faint bloodline clues they'd managed to catch were all lost. They'd have to come up with another plan.

"...Really... killed it..."

Old Arcan stared at the treant's massive corpse, nearly fainting. His jaw twitched, his eyebrows jumped wildly as he stammered out his words.

The scene of Merlin effortlessly cutting the treant in half had deeply shocked this old man. He had never witnessed such lightning-fast combat.

No, no, no! Calling it a battle would be an insult to Merlin. A real battle requires both sides to be relatively evenly matched. Clearly, Merlin's power utterly crushed the tree spirit—this was nothing short of mindless slaughter!

Good grief! ...Am I dreaming?

Such a massive tree spirit was just cut down with a single slash?

SF light novel.

This was an enemy that even Alice couldn't defeat!

How did a Bronze-rank adventurer like Merlin manage to do this?!

Old Arcan's face turned pale, his eyes nearly falling out of their sockets. He was clearly terrified by Merlin's sudden display of power.

As an ordinary person, he naturally didn't have a good grasp of power levels. He could only judge strength based on the adventurer rank system, never imagining that the treant Merlin had just killed was so incredibly powerful.

Even so, Merlin had completely shattered Arcan's worldview. The Bronze-rank adventurer—known for being weak and just scraping by—had never seen him act as the team's main force before!

Arcan felt Merlin was practically not human. With such power, being a lowly adventurer was a complete waste.

"...Lord Merlin, you're a Bronze-rank adventurer, aren't you? How did you manage this?!"

"Huh?" Merlin looked at Arcan and replied calmly, "Nothing special, just normal operation."

"Normal... operation?" A bunch of question marks floated above Arcan's head. What kind of normal operation is this?! This is already beyond ridiculous!

"I told you to believe me. If you hadn't kept blocking me, insisting on following your plan, I would have taken down this tree spirit long ago." Merlin spread his hands, putting on an innocent act.

Arcan's face was covered in dark circles, thinking to himself, "If I had known Merlin was this reliable, I wouldn't have needed any of this damn plan."

Thinking back to his earlier grandiose speeches and self-important behavior, how foolish he had looked.

Arcan quickly walked up to Merlin, grabbed the adventurer badge hanging from his neck, and mumbled with a confused expression.

"Lord Merlin, is this badge really Bronze-rank? Maybe it was originally Silver but got too dirty with dust and turned black?"

"Tch!" Merlin snatched his badge back, sticking out his tongue, "What nonsense. I'm really a Bronze-rank adventurer."

"...Then how could you possibly have the strength to defeat this tree spirit? This is so unbelievable! I've been in the adventurer industry for so long, and I've never seen anyone like you!"

Arcan's expression was one of utter disbelief. He had never witnessed such an extraordinary existence as Merlin.

He had also clawed his way up from the bottom to become a Silver-rank adventurer, yet he had never heard of a powerhouse being stuck at this level.

Arcan had originally thought that in this three-person team, Merlin was the weakest link and he still had some say. But now, Merlin had just been holding back, and Arcan was the one dragging the team down!

"Old Arcan, isn't this world full of incredible things? I can defeat this tree spirit, and you can break the iron law of adventurer ranking to become Silver. We're not so different." Merlin casually adjusted his Bronze badge and said with a nonchalant tone, "Don't let this piece of junk blind your eyes. It has no right to declare that we must be weak, does it?"

"...Lord Merlin's eyes widened, and he felt as if he had suddenly been enlightened. 'Lord Merlin, I didn't think highly of you before, and I'm sorry for my attitude. I never expected your strength to be so formidable. If I had known, I wouldn't have acted like such an idiot, making grand plans and being self-important. How embarrassing!'

"Mr. Arcan, besides that slow carriage, you're an excellent guide. We need you..." Merlin patted Arcan's shoulder.

"Lord Merlin... Arcan's dry eyes suddenly filled with moving tears. No one had ever told him 'we need you' before—it felt like a validation of his very existence.

Merlin ignored Arcan and went to Alice's side, examining her injuries.

Although severe, they weren't life-threatening. With the power of her dragon lineage, this kind of external injury would heal on its own in about five days.

"Alice, are you okay? Do you need help?"

"Do I look like I need it?" Alice rolled her eyes.

Merlin picked Alice up from the ground, causing her to grimace in pain. She was clearly still in a lot of discomfort.

"Why didn't you listen to me and kill that tree spirit? It might have had bloodline clues!"

"Is that so?" Merlin finally realized, having no idea there was such a connection.

"Your reaction is strange. I've never seen you so excited when killing someone before..." Alice had already sensed something was off with Merlin.

"...". Merlin had no choice but to admit that he had been driven by survival instinct. He couldn't think of anything else—his entire mind was focused on killing the opponent to relieve his curse. Of course, he wouldn't tell Alice about this. "If I hadn't acted in time, Mr. Arcan would have been crushed to death. Is that not a problem?"

"Mmm... I suppose so. I'm not trying to blame you."

Alice leaned against Merlin, quietly lowering her head. She felt this had nothing to do with Merlin—it was all a matter of fate and coincidence. Compared to the mission clues, people's lives were clearly more important.

"Let's head back to the church. You need to rest and recover your injuries." Merlin said seriously. Alice's current condition wasn't suitable for continuing.

Alice suddenly remembered something, quickly lifting her head and grabbing Merlin's sleeve, her face full of urgency.

"The bottle!"

"The bottle in the hidden room!

"That thing was suspicious. We must take it back!"

title: Chapter 20 — Mysterious Bottle
content:
Chapter 20 — Mysterious Bottle

Volume 15 · Chapter 20

A few days later, in the small church.

Merlin and the others had returned from the depths of the altar, and had also brought back the mysterious silver bottle.

From the dead tree person's words, Alice felt the bottle should still have unsolved secrets. Perhaps it had some connection to the birth of the vampires—they'd need to investigate carefully.

Late at night, candlelight dim on the table, Merlin, Alice, Akaron, and the dead priest sat together, preparing to study the bottle carefully.

Since the priest couldn't cast healing magic, Alice could only apply some wound medicine, relying on the dragon race's self-healing ability to recover.

At this moment Alice looked like a severely injured patient, bandages wrapped around her arms, hanging on her neck, looking somewhat disheveled.

The priest glanced at the injured Alice and said with concern, "Alice-san, are you alright? It looks like you went through a very brutal battle..."

"It's nothing, just some superficial wounds. I'll recover after a few days' rest." Alice gave everyone a reassuring look, thinking thankfully that the tree person had been taken out by Merlin before it could show its true strength—if it had gone all out, she probably would have been crushed to death by now.

Old Akaron, seeing Alice's condition wasn't good, also asked, "Really nothing? Your injuries don't look light..."

"Don't worry, Alice's always been thick-skinned and tough. This kind of wound isn't anything, just a few painful nights at most." Merlin said casually beside her. Now that the life-threatening curse had stabilized, his mood was fairly good—this stretch of time could finally be used to relax properly.

"Tsks!" Alice furrowed her pretty small eyebrows and gave Merlin a harsh elbow strike to the chest, protesting that this guy had zero sympathy—she was injured and he couldn't even say something nice to cheer her up?

"What are you doing?" Merlin rubbed his chest, muttering with a displeased face.

"You're thick-skinned? Your whole family's thick-skinned." Alice scolded angrily.

A cold sweat trickled down the priest's forehead. He awkwardly interjected, "This time seems to have been no easy feat, right? Was the altar really that dangerous, with strong—"

"Not just strong—extremely strong. There was a tree person, so huge! It was almost touching the clouds!" Old Akaron waved his hands excitedly, his expression exaggerated.

"...Is that so? There are tree spirits in that forest? I've never heard of that." The priest's face changed, finding it unbelievable.

"You don't know how strong that tree person was. Alice-san couldn't even beat it. If it weren't for Merlin-sama stepping in at the most dangerous moment, we'd all have died there." Old Akaron sighed with emotion.

"Eh?"

The priest froze, his expression one of disbelief, as if his ears had deceived him.

Alice-san couldn't beat it, and Merlin-sama could?

And Alice-san was the one covered in wounds—clearly the one who did the most fighting.

Merlin and Akaron were completely unscathed—probably just standing by shouting "666" like dead weight?

The priest coughed lightly to hide his embarrassment and didn't intend to dwell on it, chalking it up to Old Akaron's senility.

"So this is the mysterious bottle you brought back from the altar's secret room? It looks quite old."

"There was no treasure in that secret room at all, but this bottle was suspicious. Alice-san insisted on bringing it back," Old Akaron explained.

The priest picked up the silver bottle on the table, opened the cap, and looked inside—nothing was there at all. It was completely an ordinary object.

"Does this bottle have anything suspicious about it? I checked before and didn't feel anything odd," Merlin asked Alice.

"That tree person said it existed to guard this bottle, that something evil was sealed inside, and releasing it would plague the world." Alice said succinctly.

"That can't be that exaggerated, right?" Merlin's forehead slid a few black lines. "Evil source? Nonsensical. I opened it and there was nothing inside. Ask Old Akaron if you don't believe me."

"Yes, nothing at all. I can vouch for that." Old Akaron nodded seriously.

"Oh~ So that's you behind my back screwing me over? If you hadn't opened the bottle, that tree person wouldn't have attacked me!" Alice glared at Merlin angrily, feeling that in the secret room, Merlin and Old Akaron must have done something to provoke the tree person. Sure enough, it turned out that way. "You family... almost got me killed..."

"Er..." Merlin frowned, explaining awkwardly, "I didn't know you'd be attacked outside. Blaming me entirely like that is a bit much, isn't it?"

"Bah! Great at making excuses. We should discuss things before acting instead of making decisions on your own and causing trouble. Look at my hand!" Alice held up her bandaged hand and complained, "Can't move for another three or four days."

"Had nothing to do with me. Even if I hadn't opened the bottle, the tree person would've attacked you—you and I were invaders in its eyes." Merlin emphasized that it had little to do with him.

"Hmph, nothing good ever happens when I'm with you. I always get hurt." Alice puffed her cheeks, sullen.

"That's my—" Merlin rebutted without mercy, not giving Alice any leeway just because she was injured.

"Both of you, stop fighting. We're not here to figure out what this bottle is?" Old Akaron, seeing the tension, quickly jumped in to ease the mood, then turned to the priest. "Father, we've examined this bottle over and over on the way back and have no leads at all. You've lived on this land since childhood—can you see anything?"

"...From the outside it doesn't seem particularly special, but we have a tradition here on the Glenn Plains—bottles are often carved with information to record certain events. Also..."

The priest spoke while vigorously wiping the silver bottle with his sleeve, as if trying to remove the dullness on its surface.

The bottle, which had been somewhat blackened, grew brighter under the priest's rubbing, and faint patterns began to emerge.

"See? Just as I said. The bottle is too old—the carvings have faded, but after polishing they're still visible."

"Oh! So reliable, Father!"

All three exclaimed in unison, staring in astonishment as the priest kept wiping the bottle.

They'd been at a dead end the whole journey, and only here with the priest did they find a clue.

Apparently some things only locals would know—outsiders could never see through them.

As the priest wiped, the entire bottle gleamed like new, and the carved patterns grew clear.

Those weren't gorgeous patterns at all—they looked like crude murals, stick-figure versions with no aesthetic sense whatsoever.

The priest examined the bottle in his hands, deeply furrowing his brows, then widening his eyes in shock, speechless—

"This is!
