title: Chapter 21 — True Ancestor
content:
Chapter 21 — True Ancestor

Volume 15 · Chapter 21

Alice looked at the picture on the bottle, her expression gradually becoming bewildered. Why did she feel like she had seen it somewhere?

Merlin saw the priest's reaction, it seemed he had made a major discovery. He was just about to ask further when he was preempted by old Acaronon-

"What's wrong? Father, what does the picture on top mean?"

"The picture on top looks like... the story of Cain and Abel created by the Goddess of Light?" The priest said with a solemn expression, seeming not to be able to confirm completely, just feeling it was too similar. He had to be cautious, feeling that this matter was by no means trivial.

Hearing the priest's words, Alice suddenly realized, reacted, and the picture on the bottle seemed to indeed be the story of the Goddess of Light creating two lives!

Alice was once a Hero, belonging to the Holy Church. Naturally, she had seen the manuals that believers carried with her. This picture was in every manual!

". Holy... ah no! Mouth 0 mistake, the story of the Goddess of Light creating humans? What the hell?" Merlin asked with a look of confusion. He wouldn't idle away researching the history of the Holy Church, or reading the manuals. He couldn't understand the picture on the bottle at all.

The priest hurriedly took out thick manuals from his pocket, scaring Merlin a-

- Jump! This old man was so excited he wanted to pull himself into the club?

"You guys look, isn't it very similar?"

The priest opened a page of his manual and placed it on the table, letting everyone look at the pictures above.

Behind the painting, a shining female should be the Supreme Goddess of Light.

As for the two stick figures kneeling on the ground below, they should be the ones created.

Merlin lifted his head and combined the pictures in the manual to look at the mysterious bottle. The contents had a high overlap, seeming to be narrating the same thing, which made one very puzzled.

"It can't be wrong, the story recorded on this bottle should be the story of the Goddess of Light creating Cain and Abel." Alice said with an affirmative tone.

"What. - . What is this story talking about?" Merlin curiously asked. Obviously, Alice knew much more than he did on this aspect.

"This story is recorded by the Holy Church. Legend has it that after the Twilight of the Gods, the Goddess of Light became the only god in the heavens. Feeling lonely, she decided to create two people to accompany herself, namely Cain and Abel, these brothers."

Alice paused slightly, recalling something. "Originally, the two brothers got along very well. To repay the Goddess of Light's act of creation, every autumn harvest season they would offer gifts to the so-called mother. Cain discovered that the Goddess of Light favored Abel's offering of cattle and sheep, but not his own fruits. Thus, Cain began to hate his younger brother Abel, thinking he was showing off his cleverness, and ultimately Cain killed Abel with his own hands, pushing his brother down from the heavens into the mortal world. And because he killed his own blood relative, the goddess punished him, sealing him in the Holy Bottle, and cursed him with immortality and a thirst for blood, forever tormented by hunger and desire."

"Alice lady knows the Holy Church's stories quite well?" The priest saw that Alice knew so much about the Light Church and was still very happy.

".... Yes, I only know a little." Alice concealed it, not wanting to admit that she was the 233rd Hero, and her reputation was already ruined.

"It's already impressive. I've never seen someone who isn't a believer know so much about the Light Church." The priest smiled kindly at Alice.

"Immortal and everlasting? Craving for blood? This, how is it so similar to the characteristics of a blood clan?" Merlin furrowed his brow and asked.

"It really is similar... Alice stared at the mysterious silver bottle," falling into silence.

"It's not strange. In the Light Church, we clergy call Cain the True Ancestor." The priest wiped the lampshade, making the surroundings brighter.

"True Ancestor? What kind of play is this?" Merlin was full of question marks and didn't understand this term.

"True Ancestor, meaning the ancestor of the blood race, the strongest, the first vampire. But Cain is not such a lowly existence as a vampire; he was created by the goddess personally, and is a wayward god!" The priest said very seriously, seeming not to like equating Cain with the blood race entirely.

"A god?" Merlin showed a face of utter contempt, seriously doubting the authenticity of it.

Anyway, Merlin had never seen any god. He had seen the servants of gods, though.

Like that hellish apostle who wanted to summon Merlin but was killed.

There was a barrier between the mortal world and the heavens, and between the heavens and hell. Unless special methods were used to open the roads, it was basically very difficult to interfere with each other. Even Merlin's draw-and-cut technique couldn't ignore this rule.

The previous kingdom's secret records combined with a magic circle were used for special methods, once instantly breaking through the barrier between hell and the mortal world, summoning the Hell Burning Legion, but it was destroyed by Merlin.

So Merlin wouldn't believe that gods would appear out of nowhere in this world, because after the Twilight of the Gods, most gods had died. What significance did this Cain have?

"Although Alice lady's story just now was roughly accurate, it's not completely so. After Cain was sealed in the Holy Bottle, he was thrown into the mortal world, and moreover, the Heavenly Giant Tree was guarding it, preventing humans from approaching the evil Cain..." The priest seemed to have a bit of old confusion. Just after saying this, he suddenly realized that something was wrong with the whole matter, so he hurriedly checked, "Acaron, you said you encountered tree spirits at your altar?"

"Exactly, a very big tree person, very fierce." Old Acaronon gestured dramatically.

"The sealed evil, the goddess throwing the Holy Bottle to the mortal world, the Heavenly Giant Tree guarding... The priest couldn't go on, his expression gradually becoming terrified.

The quiet night, several people staring at the silver-white bottle, not speaking, the atmosphere fell into dead silence, everyone sensing that something was wrong.

Because what Merlin and the others encountered had too high a coincidence with the legend, it was simply like finding the altar sealing Cain!

Merlin had no expression, thinking isn't this too coincidental? We found the sealing place of Cain?

Alice then had a heavy expression, suddenly recalling the words of the tree person. The evil source sealed in the bottle, could it be referring to Cain!

"Good heavens! We won't have found the place sealing the Goddess's son, right?" Old Acaronon stood up from the chair in fear.

"Joke? I personally opened the bottle, and there wasn't even a hair!" Merlin impatiently rebutted.

"Merlin, didn't you tear off the talisman stuck on the bottle at the beginning, and then have the bottle open itself in a strange event?" Old Acaronon didn't forget this matter.

"Alice, it seems like such a thing happened?" Alice narrowed her eyes, feeling that Merlin seemed to have poked a hornet's nest.

Several people's eyes were like searchlights, staring at Merlin in unison, hoping he could give an explanation.

Merlin, being stared at, felt uncomfortable, directly slamming the table and standing up, speaking in a calming tone—

"Acaron old gentleman, you are old, your brain really doesn't work, I completely don't remember this, and you guys calm down, okay? Don't scare yourselves. Let's go to the altar. It's just right to seal what True Ancestor? This is possible? The probability is very low, friends. Moreover, we saw no sign of Cain the whole way. He craves blood, right? If he were really released, he would definitely first suck our blood. However, there was none, so this is just many coincidences linked together. I'm tired, I'm going to sleep, bye~"

Several people felt Merlin's words had some logic. The bottle was empty, nothing was seen, and no vampire appeared. Perhaps they were really mistaken.

The priest stared at the bottle for a long while, hesitating and saying, "The matter is too strange. Perhaps we made a mistake. Although I've heard the altar has evil power, I've never heard it was such a terrifying existence as Cain.

"It's possible I was too anxious recently, too sensitive. Goodnight everyone." Alice also stood up, seeming to want to go to her room.

Old Acaronon furrowed his brow and thought for a long while, muttering, "My brain works well!"

The quiet church stairs.

Merlin alone, slowly walking up the stairs wanting to go back to his room, but his heart couldn't be calm one-

Isn't this too bad luck?

Could it be that I really released...

The monster that causes chaos in the world?

(u -●)?

Night, the moon covered by clouds.

The dilapidated southern forest outside, the ground was messy.

A girl wearing ragged clothes, barefoot, stepped out from the deep place....

title: Chapter 22 — New Method
content:
Chapter 22 — New Method

Volume 15 · Chapter 22

Or it wasn't just Merlin who came out of the altar - a completely forgotten minor character, the little thief first discovered in the depths of the altar.

Due to being scared silly by the treant, this little thief didn't communicate with Merlin and the others, but ran away directly.

After the little thief escaped the altar, he didn't leave the forest, because right after exiting the altar, he saw that terrifying treant awaken again, roaring to massacre the forest's intruders.

Instantly dominated by fear, the little thief didn't dare to run around anymore, so he hurriedly hid deep in the forest.

Until it was quiet outside, and it seemed there would be no danger, this little thief dared to walk out from inside.

A few days later, the little thief hadn't encountered danger again, and his mental state gradually stabilized.

He slowly walked out from the depths of the forest, gazing at the boundless black plain in the distance, and at the mess before him, unable to help but sigh in his heart -

...Is it all over?

It seems I'm safe now.

Now I should return to the mercenary group and report everything that happened here to the boss Dick.

But coming back empty-handed after such a big thing, the boss will definitely punish me, right?

What should I do?

The little thief scratched his head in frustration. His current situation made him dare not face Dick, and he might even be executed!

But just when the little thief had no idea what to do, he heard the sound of hurried footsteps coming from behind the forest.

-A young girl dressed in ragged clothes, looking like she was only three or four years old, stumbled out from the depths of the forest.

Her whole body gave people a dirty feeling, and she wasn't wearing shoes on her feet, making her chubby little legs covered in mud.

This appearance simply didn't look like a child with a home, but rather a stray beggar girl?

The little girl's expression was fearful, staring blankly at everything before her, and her eyes were even more filled with unease.

Where did this little girl come from?

How did she come to this forest?

The little thief watched the little girl, and many doubts arose in his heart, but soon he became resigned, feeling that there was nothing to it?

The entire Glenn Plain had suffered a great flood not long ago, and the people were displaced. Even if children and parents got separated, it wasn't strange.

So the little thief's gaze at the little girl gradually became greedy, and he thought of a way to avoid the boss's punishment!

If he brought this little girl back to the mercenary group, wouldn't he be able to greatly compensate for his own failure? !

Originally, the main source of income for the mercenary group was selling virgins, and the younger the age, the more expensive.

And the dirty little girl standing right in front of him K just perfectly met the requirements? Maybe if the boss is happy, he might even make up for the fault!

The little thief's heart became restless, and he slowly approached the little girl, revealing a seemingly "kind" smile one-

"Do you need my help?

A few days later.

Nothing happened in the little church.

Although that night's discussion brought out the existence of Cain, everyone still found it hard to believe such a heaven-defying coincidence, and felt it should just be too strong a sense of déjà vu.

So that mysterious bottle no longer attracted Merlin's attention, but was instead collected by the priest.

- The pedestrian now faced the problem of still not finding any valuable vampire clues.

Still like a headless fly, searching everywhere for information about Dracula.

Although the three oldest blood clans walked out of that forest, the secrets among them have become difficult to query.

In a certain room, Alice was unwrapping the bandages on her arm, slightly letting her hand on the table move.

After several days of recovery, Alice's injuries had recovered seven or eight points, and there would no longer be painful movements that were difficult to perform.

As long as she rests quietly for a few more days, she can fully recover.

"Knock knock knock!"

A knocking sound came from outside the door, Alice raised her head, and threw the bandages on the table into the trash can, "Who is it?

Merlin pushed open Alice's door, glanced at Alice a few times, "Just now Mr. Akalon said he thought of a way to find the blood clan and wanted us to come over and talk."

"Really?" Alice raised her head, her eyes still somewhat doubtful, and she didn't think old Akalon could have any method, after all this old man was very ordinary, compared to real adventure experience, she and Merlin were both more capable than Akalon.

"I don't think old man Akalon is joking, maybe he really has a way, who knows." Merlin also couldn't be sure, because throughout the journey, Akalon gave people an impression that was too slick, completely not like someone who could play a key role.

"Relying on Akalon old man is not as good as relying on ourselves." Alice didn't have much hope, feeling it was just a waste of time.

"Wow, are you looking down on Akalon old man? Discriminating against low-level adventurers?" Merlin frowned and opened his mouth to put a big hat on Alice.

".... I didn't, stop putting hats on me, I'm just saying Akalon old man's adventure experience isn't rich, we have to rely on him all the way, so I don't trust him much." Alice emphasized the tone and said.

"He has completed 99999....."

"You shut up okay;

; =

Before Merlin finished speaking, Alice dissatisfiedly glared at him, and said angrily.

"Low-level tasks no matter how many times they are completed won't accumulate any experience, it's like us eating every day, does that mean we'll be gourmets in the future? Akalon old man doesn't have any shining points, we should better not pin our hopes on him."

"Akalon old man is too ordinary - point, but as a local of France, he understands this empire better than us." Merlin said very objectively.

"You haven't woken up yet? Thinking there's something outstanding about Akalon old man? Please wake up, we've been delayed many times because of him on this road." Alice said tactfully, meaning that old Akalon was somewhat dragging his feet in the team and didn't play any role.

"I've been awake for a long time, good? Let me ask you, what do you have in your mind about the blood clan now?" Merlin pursued the question.

"None... none..." Alice hesitated, and honestly answered. 14

"That's not enough, both of us have no clue, why don't we go listen to Akalon old man's method, maybe we found a new breakthrough?" Merlin looked at Alice's eyes, feeling it was okay to go listen.

"This... Alice thought about it, feeling going to listen is fine, so she nodded, "I'll go past."

Merlin glanced at the trash can with the bandages, pretending not to care and asked, "That.... Is your injury better?"

"Hmm?" Alice raised her head and looked at Alice - it was the first time in these days he said something caring about her, ". Good much better, you don't need to worry about it."

"That's good, we might leave the church these few days and go find new clues, so.... Merlin paused, scratching his face with his finger, "I hope you recover quickly."

"Didn't you say my skin is thick and meat is thick and I don't need to worry? Looking at me so embarrassed, are you secretly happy inside?" Alice narrowed her eyes and probed.

"Being secretly happy is too much, isn't it? If you're injured, I'll also feel uncomfortable." Merlin said lightly, thinking of course this was said from the perspective of a companion.

"Is that so? If you care about me, you should be obvious, not always cold and ice-like, I thought this guy was a feelingless killer." Alice pouted, putting on an angry look and complaining one-

Originally when I was injured, this guy actually cares? Maybe this is a good omen.

Rarely hearing concern from him, perhaps this is a good sign.

Of course I definitely won't feel happy because of thisN trying to please me is not easy at all?

title: Chapter 24 — Beelzebub's Pet
content:
Chapter 24 — Beelzebub's Pet

Volume 15 · Chapter 24

Avignon.

This city, located in the south-central region of France, was known as the Empire's Slave Market.

People from all corners of the nation would come here to trade in slaves.

Some of these slaves were enemy combatants left over from wars, some were kidnapped from distant lands, and others had outright violated the laws of France and been reduced to slavery.

In the main city of Avignon, slave trading alone had brought prosperity, and the ruling Countess Carmilla was even praised as the most capable woman in all of France.

Due to a great flood in the south, many people had been displaced. As the ruling noble, Carmilla threw open the city gates and took it upon herself to house these homeless refugees.

However, the refugees' condition for entering Avignon was that each household must have at least one daughter; otherwise, Avignon would not accept them.

Carmilla's explanation for this was that women face greater threats during times of upheaval, and protecting the safety of women was her duty.

Nearly all of the refugees who were settled in Avignon were deeply grateful to Countess Carmilla, believing that while all other nobles were shirking their responsibilities, this remarkable woman was doing good deeds.

Especially the female refugees, who revered Carmilla almost to the point of worship. In no time at all, the countess had become a champion of women's rights throughout France, amassing many followers.

After taking in the massive influx of refugees, the city of Avignon became terribly overcrowded. Streets were filled with refugees who looked no better than beggars, their circumstances barely above those of the slaves.

Under the protection of Countess Carmilla, the refugees received some food each day and at the very least would not starve to death, making their situation far better than the refugees outside the city walls.

At the largest slave market in Avignon, slave traders dragged their merchandise out into the streets, lining them up or performing shows to draw attention.

These slaves had become commodities, constantly displaying themselves in the hopes that some master would purchase them, for under the slave traders' control, they would not eat well each day.

Of course, this bustling slave market also had its dark, unsavory side, such as the slave girls curled up in the corners, whose fate was obvious even without asking.

Among the people at the slave market, all manner of individuals could be found. Some customers needed cheap labor, while others sought to satisfy some other desire.

Thieves, swindling peddlers, and pimps—these unsavory types had all conspired together, making the slave market thick with filth and grime.

As the manager of the largest slave market in all of France, the guildmaster had to personally inspect the entire area each day to maintain order.

The guildmaster was a fat, greasy man who had originally been a commoner but, relying on his wealth and influence, had forced himself to dress as a petty noble.

Behind him followed a group of strong guards, all armed with sharp weapons and eyes that glared fiercely at everyone around them.

The peddlers, seeing the imposing guildmaster, quickly scrambled to pack up their wares. No one dared to block his path, and they bowed and scraped in greeting.

"Good morning, Guildmaster. You're up early today."

"Get lost! Want me to raise your rent?"

The guildmaster barked out a harsh shout, immediately silencing the peddler, who didn't even dare to fart. The others were equally confused—today the guildmaster seemed to have gunpowder in his ass, glaring at everyone with ill humor.

In truth, the slave market had recently become extremely chaotic, more difficult to manage than ever before, because the refugees were flooding in. Many had blended into the market, taking up a great deal of space.

Especially in the past few days, business had declined sharply. The guildmaster, who had always been greedy for money, could not possibly tolerate this. Today, he had come specifically to deal with these refugees.

Take a look at his guards behind him—about thirty-odd fierce-looking men who were not to be trifled with. They would serve as enforcers, driving the refugees out of the slave market!

"Sir, are you really going to do this? Won't this cause trouble?" One of the thugs asked with concern.

"What are you worried about?" The guildmaster puffed out his chest and glared, clearly in a terrible mood.

"But this was Countess Carmilla's direct order. If we suppress these refugees, won't we be offending the countess? I've heard she's ruthless and doesn't hesitate to use cruel methods." The thug's face was pale with fear as he spoke.

"Since when does the countess matter? Even the countess must obey the laws of the Empire! I am the master of this slave market—does that woman really think she can boss me around?" The guildmaster roared angrily, clearly holding a great grudge against Carmilla.

"...Yes, yes, I was being overly cautious, Guildmaster. Even the countess can't interfere with how you manage your own territory." The thug broke into a cold sweat, his face oozing flattery as he spoke.

"Carmilla, that self-righteous bitch, insists on opening Avignon's gates to take in these damn refugees. Doesn't she know that these refugees are like swarms of locusts, leaving nothing but devastation wherever they go? Originally, Avignon was already overcrowded. Now look at my slave market—it's become a temporary shelter. I've never seen such an idiot of a countess in my life!" The guildmaster vented his frustration, cursing the countess without any regard for the eyes around him. Even though she was the countess, the stability of the city still depended on the support of wealthy merchants.

"You're absolutely right, Guildmaster. This Carmilla is truly despicable, not considering anyone else at all. She's a worthless countess. And now there are still so many people praising her—how ridiculous!" The thug agreed with the guildmaster, which lifted his spirits considerably.

The fat, greasy guildmaster stopped in his tracks and scanned the refugees cowering in the corners with a fierce gaze, shouting loudly, "Move out! Let these locusts know who the real master here is! Drive all these outsiders away!"

Thirty-odd thugs sprang into action, grabbing the refugees hiding in the corners and beating them mercilessly, sending them fleeing in all directions.

In an instant, the entire slave market descended into chaos. Many refugees rolled on the ground and scrambled to escape, a sight that was heart-wrenching to behold. These were already homeless people, yet they had to suffer at the hands of local bullies.

The thugs showed no mercy as they beat the refugees, striking them with fists and feet, completely disregarding the countess's authority.

The guildmaster stroked his thin mustache and nodded with satisfaction. This was exactly the effect he wanted—killing a chicken to scare the monkeys, ensuring that none of the refugees would dare set foot on his territory again.

Just then, a figure in a brown robe slowly approached the guildmaster and asked in a deep voice, "It seems you're the biggest slave trader in all of France. Over 80% of the Empire's slave transactions pass through your hands, correct?"

The guildmaster sized up the stranger, who was dressed in tattered clothes and looked like just another refugee. "So what if you are? Who the hell are you? Dare to speak to me in such a lofty tone? Get him out of here!"

"Yes!" The thugs obeyed the order and roughly pushed the mysterious figure aside, cursing under their breath, "Get out! This isn't a place for you! Don't force me to beat you up!"

"How dare a mere human speak to me like that!"

The mysterious figure pulled back his hood, revealing a gaunt, skeletal face like a sickly child. It was none other than Beezle, the gluttonous demon.

In an instant, the gluttonous demon opened his enormous mouth, spewing forth an endless swarm of black flies that buzzed with the sound of their wings as they rose into the sky.

This massive swarm of flies, impossible to imagine coming from a human's mouth, fell like a dense storm of insects, instantly turning the slave market into a living hell.

title: Chapter 25 — French Saint Maiden
content:
Chapter 25 — French Saint Maiden

Volume 15 · Chapter 25

Countless man-eating flies blanketed the sky and instantly invaded the entire slave market, pouncing on any living creature without distinction to bite and tear.
The swarm of black flies, as soon as it landed on a person, would in the next second gnaw them down to bare bones.
In an instant, the crowded slave market turned into a hell on earth, with the flies like hungry ghosts incessantly devouring humans.
The president of the Slave Traders' Association, upon seeing this scene, was so frightened he could not speak, stunned by Beelzebub's act of spitting out flies.
Hearing the screams around him, his own enforcers had already turned into piles of white bones, completely devoured by the flies.
The association president fell to the ground in terror, pointing a trembling finger at Beelzebub and stammering.
"...Demons?" "That's right, I am a demon." Beelzebub revealed a ferocious smile, step by step approaching the fat man.
"...What... what do you want to do?!" The association president kept backing away, but seemed unable to escape Beelzebub's demonic grasp.
"As the manager of France's largest slave market, you must know a lot, right?" Beelzebub narrowed his eyes.
"Don't... don't kill me, what do you want to know? I'll tell you everything!" The association president immediately gave in, racking his brains to please Beelzebub.
"Very good, I like people who don't beat around the bush." Beelzebub pulled out a piece of parchment from his bosom, unfolded it to reveal a portrait of his sister Miranda, and asked, "Have you seen this girl? If you know, tell me clearly where she was sold to?"
"...Upon seeing Miranda's portrait, the association president's eyes clearly shifted, as if he had some reservation, 'I haven't seen her, I really haven't.'"
"Really? I hate liars the most." Beelzebub narrowed his eyes, his attitude turning vicious.
The buzzing swarm of flies instantly gathered, circling around the association president as if they would at any moment swarm and devour him.
The association president shrank back in terror, continually retreating, his face ashen, his lips trembling nonstop, reduced to a helpless wretch with no way out.
"You don't have much time to think; if you tell the truth, I might consider letting you go." Beelzebub glanced at his fingernails.
"I'll talk! I'll talk!" The association president broke out in a cold sweat, faced with the threat of the flies, he had no choice: "I've seen her! I've seen her! She was a female slave brought here a few months ago, but... she has already been bought."
"Who bought her?" Beelzebub asked, his face grim, having searched France for so long and finally found a clue to his sister's whereabouts.
"I... I really don't know! The buyer concealed his identity, but from his accent he seems to be a big shot from the imperial capital!" The association head replied in panic.
"The imperial capital of France? Hmm..." Beelzebub narrowed his eyes, turned and left, his expression looking extremely grim.
As an ultimate sister-con, Beelzebub could hardly tolerate his sister being treated like a slave, bought and sold—this is a grave disgrace!
Beelzebub's mood is now extremely terrible, as if he might go mad at any moment and launch a slaughter against those around him.
If it weren't for his urgency to find his sister and not wanting to waste time, Beelzebub might now start massacring the city on the spot.
Anyone who dares to buy and sell my sister, these vile humans must die!
Beelzebub swore inwardly in anger, now preparing to set off toward the imperial capital to continue searching for Miranda's whereabouts.
"Well... I've already confessed, can you let me go now?" The association president, still in the midst of the flies and not yet out of danger, said.
"Huh? When did I ever say I would let you go?" Beelzebub retorted, instantly changing his expression.
"No... just now..." The association president, panicked, started to speak but stopped.
"'Sorry, I was just considering it, but the result is... I don't want to let you go.' Beelzebub revealed an evil smile and turned to leave."
The flies that had been constantly swarming around the association president instantly surged forward, frenziedly gnawing at this poor wretch.
"No! Don't! Ahhhhh!"
In the blink of an eye, the fat association president turned into a skeleton, completely devoured by the flies, his limp body scattering helplessly on the ground.
Beelzebub put his hood back on, hid his true appearance, and swaggered toward the Avignon city gate, intending to leave this place.
Behind him lay a scene of chaotic bones, blood flowing like a river... little... Miranda, be patient, brother I will definitely come to save you.-factory
Not long after Beelzebub left the slave market, five people suddenly arrived here.
They wore armor engraved with crosses and cloaks adorned with golden cross flowers, looking mighty and valiant.
Such attire, at a glance, was not that of the French Empire's forces, but rather resembled warriors belonging to the Holy Church.
Indeed, these five were Inquisitors from the French branch of the Holy Church, specialized in eradicating evil forces within human territories.
Especially exterminating heretics, or undead and demons and other evil creatures—these are what the Inquisitors blame, and they consider slaying evil beings their most important task.
Just a month ago, Montoil port experienced an extremely severe bloody incident, with over a hundred refugees dying miserably in the small alleys of the port.
When the Holy Church's investigators arrived at the alley, they witnessed an extremely horrifying scene: the corpses looked as if they had been gnawed by beasts, limbs scattered everywhere, simply more terrifying than the hell described in doctrine.
This incident immediately alarmed the Cardinal residing in France, who suspected that evil creatures had already infiltrated the interior of the empire and that the truth must be investigated and the threat of evil forces eliminated, otherwise Montoil port would remain in a state of panic.
The French Cardinal dispatched Inquisitors to investigate this matter, among whom was the person known as the Saint of France, named Joan.
Joan was a native Frenchwoman; after mastering martial arts she joined the Holy Church and became a devout Holy Light Knight.
Two years ago, she had also competed with Alice for the position of the 233rd Hero, but unfortunately lost by a narrow margin due to her opponent's dual cultivation of magic and martial arts.
The defeated Joan resolved to improve, continually striving to enhance her strength; after two years of arduous training, her power rose from high-tier to the current Saint-tier intermediate level.
Now Joan is no longer an ordinary Holy Church knight, but is acclaimed as an excellent Inquisitor, remaining in France to eradicate evil and has earned the honor of Saint.
Joan accepted the investigation of the bloody incident at Montoil port, and along the way she followed Beelzebub's traces, arriving at Avignon.
However, the sight before her left Joan and her four subordinates feeling shocked—
The once prosperous slave market lay in utter ruin, countless bones picked clean littered the streets, as if they had reached the edge of hell.
The Inquisitor clad in holy cross armor, steeling himself, asked, "Lady Joan, what should we do now?"
"'Chase!' Joan shouted angrily, her grip on the spear already beginning to tremble slightly, showing how furious she was."
"The bloody smell in the air has not yet dissipated, that evil creature hasn't gone far!"
"This is human territory, not a breeding ground for evil!"
"Today we must eradicate this butcher who is wantonly slaughtering in France!"

title: Chapter 26 — Intercept Beelzebub
content:
Chapter 26 — Intercept Beelzebub

Volume 15 · Chapter 26

The turmoil at the slave market instantly spread throughout Avignon.

In a short span of time, the entire main city fell into panic as the populace fled about in confusion and bewilderment.

Someone claimed there was a vicious demon at the slave market, and that the devouring flies would consume all of Avignon's humans!

The rumor spread and mutated, fear infecting more and more people like a virus.

And the instigator of all this, Beelzebub, was striding nonchalantly toward the main city's outskirts, not even sparing a glance for the panicked humans around him.

Beelzebub looked utterly calm, as though he hadn't done anything wrong, his every thought consumed with his dear sister's safety.

The composed Beelzebub stood in sharp contrast to the chaotic town behind him, and just then—

A sharp whistle of air splitting rent through the space, and a spear radiating Saint-tier aura slammed point-first into the ground right in Beelzebub's path.

It was none other than Joan's weapon. Clearly, the Holy Church's pursuers had already caught up to him.

"Hmm?" Beelzebub raised his head and looked upward.

Four Inquisitors clad in Crusade armor, swords in hand, had appeared in the sky above him without warning.

The four of them didn't bother exchanging a single word with Beelzebub; instead, they let out a unified roar and descended from the heavens in a devastating combined strike!

An explosion erupted! Nearly a hundred feet of smoke and dust billowed upward, obscuring the center of the battle vortex.

The sudden fight immediately terrified the surrounding residents, who scattered in all directions, making the main city even more chaotic.

As the smoke cleared, the four Inquisitors' swords were pressed flat against the earth. This surprise attack had missed entirely, not even scratching Beelzebub.

Beelzebub had used some form of footwork—his figure hovered above, his feet planted on the blades of the four Inquisitors.

The four of them strained with all their might, trying to yank their weapons free from beneath his feet, but the gap in strength was too vast, and the pinned swords didn't budge an inch!

The Inquisitors were secretly startled within. They had assumed he was merely a common evil creature, but it seemed this one had some tricks up his sleeve.

Beelzebub cupped his hands behind his back, standing atop the four swords, and asked with mild interest, "What's this? So you're the Holy Church's dogs, huh? You so-called knights of justice really do love sneaking attacks, don't you?"

A bead of cold sweat trickled down the forehead of each Inquisitor. They found it strange that their opponent showed no fear. A normal evil creature would have been trembling with terror at the sight of Inquisitors long ago.

"Do you need something from me? I'm quite busy and have no time to entertain wild dogs raised by the Holy Church." Beelzebub's expression was cold as his gaze swept over the knights' faces.

"You ruthless, insignificant demon! How dare you act so arrogantly on land blessed by the Goddess of Light!? Today I'll make you witness the power of light!" Joan's figure flashed like lightning. She drew her spear from the ground, Saint-tier fighting spirit erupting in a straight line toward Beelzebub. "Let me deal with you myself!"

"Hmph." Beelzebub sneered. Facing the spear thrusting straight at him, he calmly extended a hand, gripped the shaft, and easily blocked the strike.

"Huh?!" Joan froze, surprised that he had defended so effortlessly. She had struck with all her strength, and yet he had neutralized it with one hand—somewhat astonishing. This demon was more complicated than she'd expected.

Beelzebub studied the woman before him. Her appearance gave away almost no feminine traits beyond a highly recognizable voice. Clad head to toe in gilded armor, she looked bold and formidable, her hair cropped close in a tomboyish cut. She was practically a tomboy through and through.

Where long hair on a woman usually lent beauty, Joan's short crop delivered a visual shock—in truth, she looked more like a man.

"You seem to be the strongest among these wild dogs, so you must be the leader, right? Saint-tier? Not bad." Beelzebub nodded, a teasing look on his lean face. "What's your name?"

"Inquisitor of the French branch of the Holy Church, Holy Maiden Joan!" she declared without an ounce of timidity, her eyes full of hostility.

"Oh? So you're Inquisitors, are you? Going around arresting heretics and burning them alive at the stake—you don't even show mercy to your own kind. I like that~" Beelzebub bared his teeth in a eerie smile. He himself was equally merciless toward his own kind, even going so far as to devour them.

"We slay evil creatures! Heretics are nothing but harmful sheep seduced by demons! Killing them is to protect justice!" Joan secretly gathered her fighting spirit, preparing to unleash a thunderous strike. "Don't make me sound like I'm any kindred spirit of yours. You're merely a demon that causes havoc everywhere. We are nothing alike!"

"Hah, not alike? I kill ten thousand people, and it makes no difference from you killing one person. We're all executioners—none of you should flatter yourselves. Just because you're the Holy Church's hounds, does that make you self-proclaimed warriors of justice? Wake up..." Beelzebub sneered, finding the Church loved draping itself in hypocritical finery, even wrapping its slaughter in the guise of a sacred mission.

"Nonsense!" Joan rebuked sharply. Golden fighting spirit surged outward from her body, and the grip on her spear suddenly tightened!

"Oh? She may be a woman, but she packs quite a lot of strength." Beelzebub narrowed his eyes. Though he still gripped the spear firmly, it was inching closer and closer toward his throat.

Just as Beelzebub was preoccupied dealing with Joan, the four Inquisitors beside him seized the rare opportunity, yanking their swords free from beneath his feet and suddenly attacking him!

Four razor-sharp blades encircled him in a pincer formation, coming down on Beelzebub's neck like whistling knives cutting through the biting wind!

Though they were only at a high-tier combat level, as Joan's supporting subordinates their coordination experience was rich. Their combined绞杀 tactic left the enemy with no room to escape!

Beelzebub's gaze shifted, and facing the dire situation of wolves ahead and tigers behind, he showed hardly any panic—instead letting out a furious roar—

"RAAAAGH!!!"

The colossal shout sent rippling sound waves outward, a powerful shockwave radiating from Beelzebub's position. For a moment, the humans were unable to withstand it.

Joan and the four Inquisitors were all blasted backward by the impact, crashing to the ground in utterly wretched states.

"You really think you can compete with me? Keep dreaming. Even if the Holy Knight Commander of your Church came personally, I wouldn't bother giving him a second glance. Of course, if he willingly walked into my mouth to be eaten, I'd be more than happy~" Beelzebub stuck out his tongue and licked his lips, his expression one of eager anticipation.

Joan and the four Inquisitors slowly rose to their feet. All had suffered varying degrees of minor injuries from the shockwave. It was without a doubt that their ambush plan had failed—they had vastly underestimated this demon's strength.

"Lord Joan, what should we do? His strength seems somewhat difficult to handle. Shall we request reinforcements?" one subordinate tentatively asked.

"We are the strongest Inquisitors stationed in France—who exactly would we ask for backup?" Joan retorted, then lowered her gaze toward Beelzebub and spoke quietly.

"Don't panic. I sense he's not unbeatable. We still have a chance."

"His level isn't that of a Demon Lord—it's more along the lines of a high-ranking officer within the demon race."

"As long as he's not Demon Lord-tier, we should have no trouble绞杀 this great demon through coordinated teamwork."

"Remember, we are warriors of the Goddess of Light, born to eradicate evil heretics!"

title: Chapter 27 — Saint
content:
Chapter 27 — Saint

Volume 15 · Chapter 27

Joan of Arc's fervent encouragement inspired the others; as a devout believer, her mood instantly infected her subordinates, and in the next second, scaling a blade mountain or plunging into a sea of fire was of no concern.
“Lady Joan of Arc is right.”
“Well, for the goddess, we shouldn't have any doubts.”
“Let's try once more.”
Several inquisitors encouraged each other; with this boost of faith, they might cast aside life and death and give their all.
In the Holy Church, inquisitors are generally fanatics who would not hesitate to commit suicide for the Goddess of Light.
This greatly enhanced the inquisitors' execution; they showed no mercy toward heretics, appearing as the Church's guardians but in reality serving as its executioner's blade.
“What are you whispering about? Are you hatching some plan?” Beelzebub's grin gradually turned hideous as he split his wide mouth, “Do you think I'll give you any chance?!!”
As his words fell, Beelzebub lifted his foot and then stomped down hard, instantly shattering the ground!
With the cracking sounds, the entire land of Avignon trembled, the vibrations spreading outward continuously.
The fissures spread like a spiderweb, causing the ground beneath the inquisitors' feet to collapse one after another, dropping them down.
“What the—?” Joan of Arc's body began to fall; she hadn't expected Beelzebub to act so outrageously, completely disregarding common sense!
“Hehehe! You lot of idiots, did you think I'd just stand there and let you hit me?!” Beelzebub bared his teeth in a cold laugh, his form gradually blurring and disappearing.
r」
The next second, Beelzebub's figure suddenly appeared among the inquisitors who were falling.
Beelzebub's fist looked weak, like a chicken's claw, but the power it held was far from trivial!
No matter how you say it, as a demon lord, Beelzebub is among the Seven Monarchs a type skilled in close-quarters grappling.
This group of inquisitors, as Beelzebub closed in, obviously faced defeat.
Beelzebub, smiling, unleashed a punch at the speed of sound, sending forth waves of black wind; all four inquisitors were beaten into cripples, their bodies like cannonballs slamming into the pit below!
“Ugh!” Joan of Arc widened her eyes in shock, for she hadn't even seen Beelzebub's punch; this seemingly playful attack stirred a huge sense of danger in her heart!
Still, Joan of Arc's ability was not bad; as the leader of these few, she quickly realized the danger and crossed her spear before her chest to defend.
Only a 'clang' was heard as Beelzebub's fist and Joan's spear collided, scattering sparks!
“Ha!” Joan of Arc was flung backward, barely managing to stabilize herself, while her subordinates had all lost their combat ability.
“Oh? Your reaction's not bad..." Beelzebub ceased his pursuit and rubbed his wrist.
“Don't be so arrogant, demon!”
Joan of Arc gripped her spear tightly, silently began chanting; the golden battle aura on her body surged, exuding a holy aura.
The spear technique she learned came from the Holy Church, specifically for dealing with various evil beings; she burned her own battle aura, converting it into holy power to inflict heavy damage on the enemy.
However, this step requires slow chanting; otherwise it's hard to achieve the desired effect, which is terrible for Joan of Arc.
Battles often occur in the blink of an eye; chanting leaves one open to having their weakness exploited by the enemy, which is also why mages find it troublesome when facing warriors in close combat.
The holy power gathering in Joan's spear grew more and more; it was about to be completed, but Beelzebub seized the opportunity.
In a single breath, Beelzebub instantaneously appeared before Joan, his face bearing a mocking smile.
“What are you concocting? Do you think I'll give you a chance? You foolish mutt!”
“Ugh!” Joan of Arc widened her eyes, a bead of cold sweat trickling down her forehead; she had thought she was far enough from the enemy to finish her incantation, but she had underestimated Beelzebub's burst speed!
Beelzebub grinned ferociously, showing no mercy, and slammed a fist into Joan's abdomen, instantly crushing the French Saint.
“Cough!” Joan of Arc's face turned pale, her throat sweet as she spat out blood; her body was blasted away, slamming heavily into the city wall and buried under rubble.
“Hmph, with just you few lot trying to take me on? Absolutely laughable; I advise you not to seek your own death.” Beelzebub snorted, feeling that diverting attention to deal with such enemies was simply a waste of time.
Suddenly, a chorus of footsteps sounded behind Beelzebub; troops in simple plate armor came running here in unison.
They were the private army of Countess Camilla, lord of the region; upon hearing that the city had fallen into chaos due to the attack, they rushed here immediately.
The countess's private troops were decently equipped; they appeared aggressive, their target straight for the chaos's center, Beelzebub.
Now Beelzebub didn't want to waste time before these shrimp soldiers and crab generals, so he smiled, turned, and left, vanishing on the spot.
Avignon became a mess, especially near the city gate, where the pits trampled by Beelzebub were a gruesome sight….
A week later, Merlin, as a pedestrian, sat in an ox cart and also arrived in the Avignon area.
“Lords and ladies, we should reach the main city of Avignon by tonight; keep your spirits up.” Old Akalon said cheerfully, having now accepted his role as the team’s logistics; still, he was glad to have two strong protectors beside him, for adventure was safer with security.
Upon hearing this, Alice snapped awake; she had just dozed off a moment earlier, and upon learning they were arriving, she said relieved, “Finally we’re here? Great, this ox cart is torture.”
“Really? I think it’s fine.” Merlin replied offhand.
“Tsk, why aren’t you complaining about the slow pace now? You were the loudest complainer before.” Alice frowned, not liking Merlin’s contrary stance.
“.... Merlin hesitated, thinking, “Now I don’t have to worry about wasting time, for the curse’s threat has been lifted and I’ve relapsed into late-stage laziness,” just as Old Akalon said, riding in an ox cart actually tempers the heart; look at you, you’re so impatient, and that’s not a good thing.”
“Lord Merlin truly understands me best; if we’d met earlier, we’d surely be friends.” Old Akalon, pleased with Merlin’s acknowledgment, said, “You’re right—overly impatient people can’t accomplish anything; Lady Alice ought to mend her temperament.”
Alice rolled her eyes, completely unable to get into the two of them singing in harmony; earlier Akalon had clearly been circling her for profit, but now it’s fine—every day he happily interacts with Merlin.
“Well, I don’t want to talk about this; let’s first think about where to investigate once we reach Avignon.”
“Of course we should ask someone familiar with the local situation.” Merlin said matter-of-factly.
“We still don’t know if we’ll be able to find any clues…” Alice said, feeling slightly worried.
At that moment, two refugees carrying luggage walked slowly by, and their conversation happened to be caught by Alice—
“Have you heard? The famed French Saint Joan of Arc has been gravely wounded by a demon.”
“I’ve heard; her injuries don’t look light, the Saint was defeated by a demon—today’s world really isn’t safe.”
Alice furrowed her delicate brows, a heavy doubt welling up inside her, “Joan of Arc? Which Joan of Arc?”
(n --●)?

title: Chapter 28 — Encounter (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 28 — Encounter (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 15 · Chapter 28

As the western sun slowly sank, night finally fell.

Merlin and the others finally arrived in Avignon, ready to begin a new investigation.

Under the crimson glow, the entire main city looked somewhat desolate.

"We're here." Old Acharon jumped down from the ox cart, intending to enter the city directly.

"Is this Avignon? Finally seeing a city that looks somewhat decent." Merlin followed suit, jumping down from the cart with a sigh.

"What are you thinking? If not for the great flood that hit all of Frankland, the places we've been weren't bad either." Alice also climbed down from the ox cart.

"Although what Lady Alice said is correct, it has something to do with the great flood, but the reason this place remained prosperous after the disaster is mainly thanks to the local lord." Old Acharon led the old ox over to Merlin's side.

"Oh? The local lord is formidable?" Merlin asked curiously, noting from Acharon's tone that he seemed to hold this lord in high regard.

"The lord of Avignon is named Camilla, a rare female noble in the Frankish Empire." Acharon paused, then continued, "Camilla is very skilled at management. Avignon used to be a chaotic city with no rules whatsoever. After Camilla took over, she revitalized it in three years, making it one of the more prosperous cities in the empire. After this flood, Avignon is also one of the few main cities willing to accept the refugee wave—this countess is truly a representative of both sharp wit and kindness."

"Is that so? If all that is true, then this lord Camilla is indeed quite impressive." Merlin nodded beside her.

"Merlin-sama, now is not the time to be stingy with praise. Camilla is a great woman of the new era! A role model for all women!" Acharon praised loudly, seemingly very reverent toward the countess.

"This..." Merlin hesitated, thinking that while the female lord's actions were commendable, calling her a role model for the new era seemed a bit exaggerated.

Beside him, Alice had been silent for a while. Seeing these two stinky men praising another woman, she suddenly felt a pang of sourness in her heart.

What? Role model for all women? Can you tone down the flattery?

Good at management? That only proves this female lord is manipulative!

Taking in refugees—maybe that's just putting on a show for others!

Alice felt very unbalanced, thinking maliciously in her heart, and inexplicably demonized this countess.

Actually, even if Alice was being sour, she couldn't stand Merlin praising other girls, as if she herself was inferior.

If Acharon said it himself, it would be fine, but praising another woman right in front of Merlin—this was hard for Alice to bear.

"What nonsense? She's just a female lord with a bit of cunning. Why praise her so much?"

"Oh, you're angry?" Merlin looked at Alice meaningfully, thinking she could smell jealousy even from here—strong stuff~

"I'm not." Alice emphasized, huffing, then changed the subject. "Hurry up and go in, find a place to stay. If it's too late, everything will be closed."

When Merlin and the others entered Avignon, they witnessed a scene completely different from the prosperity Acharon had described.

Large swaths of damaged houses awaiting reconstruction; the city wall had a huge hole shaped like a human figure.

The ground had shocking deep pits, now roped off to prevent anyone from accidentally falling in.

The scene before their eyes didn't seem to match the so-called prosperity at all; it looked more like a ruined town that had been through the crucible of war.

"...Really a prosperous town?" Merlin's tone was full of doubt, looking at Acharon beside him.

"...How strange! Why did it become like this? It was fine before, but now it looks like it suffered a terrorist attack..." Acharon led the ox cart, his mind also very puzzled, especially by the deep pits in the ground, which made one feel fear.

Alice frowned, looking around. Everywhere she looked she could find traces of fighting; it didn't feel like a natural disaster—it seemed someone had battled here.

"Looks like there are some pretty strong guys in this town..." Merlin looked down at the deep pit, feeling the destruction might have been caused by a single strike—the opponent's power was impressive.

"Seems nothing to be surprised about. Maybe there was just a conflict here before we arrived?" Alice thought nothing of it; no need to be surprised.

After leaving the messy area near the city gate and entering the center of Avignon, things looked much better. They finally saw the prosperity Acharon had described, and it was indeed impressive.

Passersby, seeing it was getting late, had as their primary goal not to find someone to ask about the mysterious disappearances, but to find a place to rest.

Soon Merlin and the others found a decent inn, still brightly lit at this hour. It looked fine, and the group had no objections, choosing it directly.

After entering the inn, there weren't many people, so they easily got three rooms. Just as Alice was pulling out her small money pouch to pay, someone started muttering in the distance.

"Heard that this time the Holy Church sent five Inquisitors to chase the demon responsible for the bloody incident in Montoir, and guess what?"

"What happened?"

"Two Inquisitors were heavily injured, three died."

"That bad?"

"This time it was the team of the Frankish Saint—truly humiliating for the Church's branch!"

"Good grief! If such a strong demon infiltrated the empire, we're in terrible danger!"

Alice frowned, her heart filled with confusion. Joan again? Could it be a different person with the same name? Could it be the Joan who competed with her for the Hero's seat in the Church back then? She was her junior, after all. She wondered how she was doing now—maybe after failing to become Hero, she became an Inquisitor?

"France... a demon infiltrated?" Merlin frowned, then lowered his voice to say to Alice with a strange expression, "Hey, has my cover been blown?"

"Impossible. No one in Britannia could tell—you're just a demon? Besides, you've been with me the whole time. When did you ever fight Inquisitors?" Alice was uneasy inside but didn't think Merlin had been identified.

"Other demons? That shouldn't be. Demons rarely appear in human lands. Even exiled demons have their powers sealed—they couldn't defeat humans..." Merlin rubbed his chin, feeling the situation was very strange.

At that moment, Joan, covered in wounds and bandages, slowly descended the stairs. She looked very battered—Beelzebub had hit her hard.

Behind her, of the four subordinates, only one remained, completely lacking the momentum they had at first.

Joan lowered her head like a defeated general, her entire demeanor very low.

But just as she descended, Joan saw Alice about to pay. Their eyes met and they cried out simultaneously—

"Joan?"

"Alice?"

title: Chapter 29 — Old Rival
content:
Chapter 29 — Old Rival

Volume 15 · Chapter 29

Alice and Joan of Arc faced each other, and both looked thoroughly astonished.

Estimating that neither of them expected to meet here, the last time they saw each other was when Alice served as the Hero and set out for the First Demon Lord Palace.

After the 233rd crusade failed, Alice never saw Joan of Arc again. She heard that Joan had gone into seclusion for rigorous training. She never expected that now Joan had become a heretic inquisitor!

Joan of Arc's mood was equally astonished. She heard that Alice's crusade this time had suffered heavy losses, and even the Holy Church's secret weapon developed over ten years failed to capture the First Demon Lord Palace.

After that, there was never any news about Alice again. She could only hear all sorts of messy rumors. Rumors said Alice was ravaged to death by Lucifer the Third, and chose suicide because she couldn't bear the humiliation.

After Joan of Arc came out of seclusion, she once tried to inquire about Alice's whereabouts, but it was as if she had evaporated. There was a high probability that she had died in the 233rd crusade against the demons.

Who would have thought that, Alice had become a silver-ranked adventurer wandering about everywhere. This made Joan of Arc feel extremely shocked. So Alice was still alive!

Both of them had complex moods. After two years apart, they met again. The competition for the position of Hero back then is still vivid in their minds.

For a moment, both sides didn't know what to say. Their brains were completely blank—one character, out.

Alice was surprised to see Joan of Arc in France. The people gossiping on the streets and alleys were her—

Joan of Arc was astonished that Alice was still alive, and had left the Holy Church to become an adventurer.

Merlin was standing to the side, somewhat bewildered. Looking at Joan of Arc, then at Alice, "You two know each other?"

Alice looked embarrassed, lowered her voice, and secretly said to Merlin, "She's called Joan of Arc. We were both Hero candidates before. She's my junior. I never expected to meet her here here."

"Is that so?" Merlin felt a slight shock, looking at Joan of Arc opposite. If one didn't listen to the voice, with such short hair, she's definitely a pure guy, "Speaking of initially— she became the Hero, now the person standing beside me— seems like it's not you anymore."

"Seems like it is... Alice nodded, internally sighing. If she hadn't competed for the 233rd Hero position, she probably wouldn't have met Merlin. But immediately afterward, she felt something was wrong, "Wait! What do you mean? You're disparaging me? Wanting her to be your partner?"

"I'm not meaning that. I mean, almost my partner was a fake young boy. To be honest, I don't like her appearance much." Merlin whispered, evaluating Joan of Arc's appearance.

"You shouldn't talk nonsense. She used to have golden long hair. I don't know why it became like this now." Although Alice said this on the surface, inside she was equally surprised by Joan of Arc's appearance. Before, Joan of Arc was also a very pretty girl. Now, it seems stimulated, she cut off her beautiful golden hair. —Little Yuan

Since Old Acaron was relatively close to Merlin and Alice, hearing them discussing him, he got scared and interjected, "You two shouldn't talk randomly! The other party is a heretic inquisitor. If she's not pleased, defining us as heretics would be terrible. We'd be miserable, being burned at the stake."

"Ah?! Is it really that exaggerated?" Merlin furrowed her brow, feeling Old Acaron was too sensitive.

"How could it not be exaggerated? Heretic inquisitors are called the executioners of the Holy Light, specially dealing with heretics. How many people burned to death? The Holy Church's power spans the whole world. Don't provoke them lightly." Old Acaron said with a face full of fear.

Merlin furrowed her brow, listening to Old Acaron say that, heretic inquisitors are like emotionless killers. Do you have to be so exaggerated?

Alice's mood gradually stabilized from the shock, and she was the first to break the silence, asking—

"Joan of Arc, why are you here?

"This question is for me, right? Alice..."

Joan of Arc slightly recovered her calm. She had many questions she wanted to ask Alice, but in the short term, she didn't know where to start.

The atmosphere of the dialogue between the two couldn't be called friendly at all. It was completely a stranger state. After all, they were originally competitors. Estimating like old friends catching up and asking about cold and heat was probably not possible.

"Long time no see. I didn't expect you to have become a heretic inquisitor. Looks like... Alice looked at Joan of Arc's arm wrapped in white bandages, "You've had a hard time..."

"You don't seem very relaxed either. Leaving the Holy Church and becoming an adventurer. Silver rank? You're doing quite well." Joan of Arc nodded, looking at Alice's adventurer proof, then looking at Merlin beside her, "You even married a husband? That's really surprising. You actually found a lover to marry. I thought you would devote your whole life to the cause of justice, and wouldn't care about worldly affection.

A black line slid down Alice's forehead. She thought to herself that she and Merlin aren't real husband and wife?

In Joan of Arc's eyes, wouldn't she get married? What's the point of struggling for the justice cause!

Not... That sentence of marrying a husband sounds quite good. I don't mind it, hehe...

Alice's face inexplicably flushed two red spots. Embarrassedly explaining to Joan of Arc.

"I'm not an emotionless robot. After leaving the Holy Church, I certainly wouldn't be so naive as to hang justice on my lips...".

"Is that so? Before, you weren't like that. In terms of devotion to the goddess, you're more outstanding than me." Joan of Arc had an indescribable taste in her heart. The opponent from back then, now had become a wife. More or less, it still made her a bit hard to accept.

Alice looked embarrassed, thinking, the old yellow calendar shouldn't be flipped out. Who wants to be the Hero? It's not because I just came down the mountain and need money!

CF Novel

Seeing that Alice was twisting and not speaking, completely lacking the aura of becoming a Hero, but more like a homebound little woman, Joan of Arc suddenly felt some anger in her heart.

Thus Joan of Arc looked at Merlin with a gaze containing a bit of hostility, and tentatively inquired.

"Leaving the Holy Church, giving up continuing to be the Hero, was all for this man who looks extremely ordinary?"

"Wait a minute, you seem to have some misunderstanding about us. We really don't.....

Merlin hadn't finished speaking when Alice secretly gave him an elbow, stopping him from making any explanation.

Merlin was elbowed by Alice and retreated a step, clutching her chest in astonishment, thinking, damn it! What does this old woman mean? Obviously the other party misunderstood! Why not let me speak!

Alice ignored Merlin's complexion. In front of her was Joan of Arc, her original opponent. She couldn't let the other party laugh at her.

So let the misunderstanding be a misunderstanding. She felt that even if she married, it also meant she was ahead of Joan of Arc in life.

Anyway, Alice definitely wouldn't admit that the title of the 233rd Hero had become stinky. Continuing on would be too shameful.

"I left, of course, not simply for a man."

"Actually is.

"Because of love[  =

title: Chapter 30 — Dispute
content:
Chapter 30 — Dispute

Volume 15 · Chapter 30

Ni Ma! Alice, are you playing with snakes?

What, because of love? How the hell can this stinky woman say something like that with a straight face!

Aren't we bound together because of debt? What kind of love is that?

The man beside him, Merlin, was seething with rage, his face darkening and his muscles twitching. He couldn't figure out what to say to Alice.

Merlin didn't know what Alice was thinking, but he could sense that she and Jeanne weren't exactly friends.

But that didn't give this stinky woman the right to spout nonsense! Get lost! I hate women the most!

Jeanne's expression grew even more unnatural. Her opponent had now become a housewife, which was a significant blow to her.

Why had she really been practicing so hard in seclusion, finally becoming a Saint-tier warrior, just to surpass Alice?

And now Alice had given up midway, running off to play house. Jeanne suddenly used her target, and the sense of loss she felt was probably something only she herself could understand.

The injured subordinate of the heretical inquisitor standing beside Jeanne had been quietly listening, and upon learning that Alice had apparently once been a Hero, his curiosity finally got the better of him.

"Jeanne-sama, is this your friend? You said she doesn't serve as a... what's going on?"

"Friend? Ah, I suppose you could say that..." Jeanne shrugged her shoulder like a man and said casually, "This is the 233rd Hero. Two years ago, she led a hundred thousand troops to attack the First Demon Lord Palace, but was defeated by Lucifer III with total annihilation of her army. Now it seems only she survived alone. How ironic."

"...Alice broke into a cold sweat, thinking, What tone is Jeanne using? Is she mocking me? I know it's embarrassing to be the sole survivor of the Hero, but Lucifer III's strength is on a completely different level! The person standing next to me is Lucifer III himself—who can defeat him? The Church had already invested massive military force against the First Demon Lord Palace before me, and still suffered total defeat! And that secret weapon, the giant whale that took ten years of research, had no effect on this freak either! Why do they always keep picking on my failure? Why target me?"

Merlin glanced at Alice with a resentful eye and thought, When I let her go, wasn't that a good thing? Could it be that she's being used as a negative example of a former Hero, getting dissed right in front of everyone?

"Although your failure in the campaign can't be blamed on you, there's no doubt that you've become a stain on the Church, known as... the weakest Hero in history." Jeanne said expressionlessly, secretly mocking Alice's lack of ambition and her decision to marry and abandon her righteous cause.

"Weakest Hero in history?!" Alice's face turned dark with rage, her whole body trembling. She thought, Who wouldn't look weak standing in front of Merlin! Why is it only me who gets labeled the weakest? What about the previous few Heroes who were killed?

"The Church currently has no intention of launching another attack on the First Demon Lord Palace. Lucifer III, this new arrogant ruler, is undeniably powerful and not someone to be trifled with. Your failure isn't entirely unjustified." Jeanne said, looking directly into Alice's eyes with a meaningful tone.

Merlin, hearing Jeanne praise his strength as unquestionable, nodded satisfactorily. He thought, That's right! I've already repelled so many of the Church's invasions. If they still haven't realized the gap in strength, the Church would have already perished long ago.

Alice glared at Merlin furiously, muttering under her breath, "What are you nodding about? What's there to be happy about?"

"Wow, are you done talking sense? Even my nodding gets you angry?" Merlin's face broke into a string of black lines as he thought, Alice is like a cactus now—no matter who, she stabs first.

"Miss Alice, you were actually a Hero?" Old Arcanum suddenly interjected in shock. No wonder Alice knew so much about Cain's story—she used to be a Hero!

"...That's... not really something to be proud of..." Alice awkwardly turned her face away, not wanting to acknowledge it at all.

"To think you're really the 233rd Hero-sama, please forgive my rudeness!" The heretical inquisitor's subordinate bowed slightly, feeling respectful toward Alice. Although the 233rd Hero's reputation wasn't great and she had no honors, she was still a Hero—this was the highest honor bestowed by the Church, said to be attainable only by those chosen as saviors of humanity.

Since the founding of the Church of Light, only 233 people in history had become Heroes. Though Alice didn't want to admit it, the title of Hero was indeed extremely precious.

"No, no, no—I'm not a Hero anymore. I've already left the Church. Don't call me that!" Alice's emotions grew more urgent, afraid of drawing further attention.

"No, no, no—the title of Hero is an honor that accompanies one for life. Although you ended in defeat, you once wielded your sword for the Goddess. That alone is worthy of our respect." The heretical inquisitor looked quite rigid and formal.

"I don't want it! I really don't want to be acknowledged as a Hero!" Alice explained, on the verge of tears.

"Miss Alice, I often hear the bards singing about your story with Lucifer III—how you and Lucifer III locked eyes and fell in love, then defied everything to be together. If that's true, is Lucifer III still in the Dead Marsh? Old Arcanum, curious about such gossip, asked directly.

"...Alice's face turned green. Of course something like this would come up! If it weren't for these bards making things up, would I really have to leave the Church and refuse to acknowledge myself as the 233rd Hero?

"This elderly gentleman, please don't make things up and slander the Hero, which is the same as slandering the great Church of Light!" The heretical inquisitor's subordinate argued with Old Arcanum, explaining, "The rumors I've heard are completely different from what you're saying. It's clearly that Lucifer III corrupted the 233rd Hero's will, forcibly took over her body, and killed her. But now Alice-sama is fine, which proves that the 233rd Hero chose to endure in silence and escape from the Dead Marsh! Regardless, that kind of will is definitely worthy of admiration!"

"That's not right, is it? What I heard was that the 233rd Hero fell in love with Lucifer III first. There's no such thing as corrupted will—it's purely love at first sight, then they defied everything to be together, achieving a great love that transcends race." Old Arcanum patted Merlin's shoulder sympathetically and said, "Miss Alice was the 233rd Hero, so Merlin-sama, you got cuckolded?"

"...You're making things up as you go!" The heretical inquisitor was truly furious now, veins bulging on his forehead. "The Hero is a glorious warrior personally appointed by the Pope. How could they possibly fall in love with an evil Demon Lord? You're spreading rumors and misleading people. Don't blame me for treating you as a heretic!"

The argument between the two made the tavern even more chaotic, with many people turning to look.

As for Merlin and Alice? They both wore dark expressions and stayed silent.

Merlin: What's this about corrupted will and forcibly taking over the body? What's this about love making things happen? It's all fake, alright! Those bards have no bottom! I didn't get cuckolded!

Alice: I'm so fed up! It's because of people like you spreading rumors that my Hero reputation has been completely ruined! Give me back my dignity! I never slept with Merlin!

Seeing the argument escalating further and more and more people gathering, to prevent things from getting worse, everyone knowing the identity of the 233rd Hero, Alice had no choice but to shout loudly.

"Enough!!!"

That cry of anger immediately silenced everyone, and all eyes turned to Alice in unison.

On Alice's sorrowful face, she managed to force out a faint smile and said in a complicated tone,

"Can we find a place to sit down first?"

"Please don't... keep using the bards' stories to insult me..."

title: Chapter 31 — Demonized Lucifer III
content:
Chapter 31 — Demonized Lucifer III

Volume 15 · Chapter 31

At the table in the corner of the inn, where few people came, even if we talked, no one would overhear.
Merlin, the wanderer, sat together with the two Inquisitors, and Alice slowly recounted what had happened two years ago when she subjugated the First Demon Lord Palace.
“That’s how it is. I picked up my life in the Death Marsh, escaped on a bamboo raft, and along the way I accidentally lost my armor, so I owe the Holy Church a lot of money. On top of that, news of my defeat spread everywhere, and through rumors people said that this 233rd‑generation Hero had been defiled. To protect my reputation, I had no choice but to leave the Holy Church and live a low‑key life.”
When Alice was recounting to the others, she deliberately concealed everything about Merlin, doing her best to cover for him.
She also didn't say that Lucifer III had left the Death Marsh with her, and that the person sitting beside her was the infamous Great Demon Lord spoken of in rumors.
After all, Jeanne and her subordinates are Inquisitors, and Alice had served as a Hero in the Holy Church, so she wasn't completely unfamiliar with that profession.
The duty of the Inquisitors is to eradicate evil, sweep away evil beings walking in human lands, and ensure the safety of the human world.
Therefore, Merlin's identity as a demon makes him the enemy of the Inquisitors, a dangerous element that must be eliminated.
Given Alice's understanding of Jeanne, her devotion to the Goddess borders on fanaticism; if Merlin's identity were exposed, it would surely bring endless pursuit.
To avoid trouble and prevent Merlin from becoming the world's public enemy, Alice voluntarily helped him conceal his identity, keeping him from being exposed.
Hearing Alice not mention him at all, Merlin instantly understood, realizing he was quite special, and thus remained completely silent beside her.
“In that case, Hero, you didn't accidentally suffer any humiliation, did you?” said the Inquisitor’s subordinate, surprised.
“Of course! Why would I be… be ravaged by Lucifer III?” Alice gave Merlin a meaningful glance, “You’ve heard those versions; they’re just random fabrications by those bards for popularity. Nowadays, don’t people love cross‑species romance stories?”
Merlin nodded in agreement beside her, thinking, “Exactly, who would go ravage Alice? At most it’s just bullying her. Those damned bards, I’m not a cuckold!”
“…Really? Since the Hero hasn’t suffered anything terrible, it shows the Goddess of Light is protecting you. Leaving the Holy Church is indeed a pity.” The Inquisitor wore a wistful expression, still full of respect for the Hero.
“There’s nothing I can do about it either—my image has already become like that; if I kept being a Hero, I’d inevitably be mocked. Plus, my defeat in the subjugation has sidelined me. Jeanne was right; I really am the weakest Hero.” Alice forced a bitter, self‑deprecating smile.
“The rumors are all false—what a pity. So many people thought the 233rd‑generation Hero was together with Lucifer III.” Old Akalon sighed beside them.
“Sir, please watch your words; don’t spread slander against the Hero.” The Inquisitor’s subordinate said sternly.
Old Akalon ignored that rigid Inquisitor and pressed on, saying, “Miss Alice, since you’ve seen Lucifer III, what does this great demon look like? I’ve heard this young monarch has a blue‑fanged, ferocious face.”
Merlin’s face darkened, and he thought, swearing, “Who the hell is spreading this nonsense about me? At least I can be called handsome. What’s with the blue‑fanged monster? Don’t think of demons as ugly just because I’m one!”
“Lucifer III—”
Alice put on a pensive look and said with malice, “He’s a completely despicable scoundrel—looks like a pig’s head, heart even more foul, lazy and gluttonous, constantly chasing respectable women, a total disgrace.”
“Huh?” Merlin stared at Alice, wide‑eyed, thinking, “Damn! Is that how she sees me? Don’t smear me while I can’t reveal my identity—this is settling personal scores with public funds!”
“I knew it—although I’ve never seen Lucifer III, a demon’s ugliness comes from inside out, and that’s no lie.” The Inquisitor’s subordinate chimed in, nodding with satisfaction.
“…Really? Then Lucifer III is a scoundrel—has he ever reached his evil claws toward you?” Old Akalon continued his questioning.
“Well… of course he has. That bastard couldn’t stop drooling when he saw me, like he’d never seen a woman before, insisting he wanted to marry me and such. Just thinking about it now gives me the chills.” Alice looked shaken, as if Merlin had truly once wanted to do something to her.
Merlin lowered his head, his hands trembling from anger at Alice, and he thought, “Who’s seen Alice drooling? And yet she yaps about marrying her? Bullshit! A woman with an airfield at home is just daydreaming!”
“Wow, Lucifer III really isn’t anything good—his mind is pure filth, it seems demons have nothing decent about them; Merlin almost got cuckolded.” Old Akalon said solemnly.
“Yeah, if I hadn’t run fast enough, I might have… …hummed… Alice let out a manly voice, like a real‑life victim.”
Ahhhhh!!!
I’ve had enough of this slutty woman?
What? Surely it’s something not suitable for minors!
I’ve never laid a hand on her!
Why go to such lengths to smear me—what’s in it for her?!
Merlin could barely hold back; he tugged at Alice, suppressing his inner fire, and gave her a serious, covert questioning.
“What are you doing? Is there no end to this? Do you really think I’m a creature that thinks with its lower half?”
“Don’t misunderstand, I have no choice either. You see those two Inquisitors across from us—they love to grab any handle, then exaggerate it into a conviction. My doing this is also to pick a side; otherwise they’d keep grilling us.” Alice looked helpless, not that she enjoyed blackening Merlin, though inside she felt a secret satisfaction.
Merlin thought it over, realized Alice had no other option, and sighed, “Just this once—don’t make a habit of it. Go easy on the smearing, don’t overdo it. When have I ever wanted to do something evil to you?”
“In Holy Church culture, demons are portrayed exactly like that—rape, pillage, all manner of evil.” A large bead of sweat rolled down Alice’s forehead.
“Shout!” Merlin curled his lip, his mood beginning to turn irritable.
“I see now—during that subjugation of the First Demon Lord Palace, you ran into so many bizarre things; I even thought you were dead.” After Jeanne roughly understood Alice’s situation, she let out a slight sigh of relief.
“How could that be? My life’s prospects are huge.” Alice laughed triumphantly, then turned to question Jeanne—
“And you?”
“Why did you cut your hair into this style now?”
“If it weren’t for your uniquely distinctive eyes, I’d have thought you were a man at first glance.”
“You used to keep long hair, which was actually quite pretty—”
