title: Chapter 32 — The Contest for the Candidacy
content:
Chapter 32 — The Contest for the Candidacy

Volume 15 · Chapter 32

"What's this?" Jeanne tugged at her own hair nonchalantly, answering, "Long hair is too inconvenient, short hair is easier to manage. Even in battle, it's more convenient."

"Really? Won't having short hair feel strange?" Alice showed a puzzled expression.

"It's convenient, but that's just one reason. I shaved my head mostly to show my awakening, to become stronger than you."

Jeanne didn't hide the fact that shaving her head was largely because of Alice.

"Ah? It has something to do with me."

Alice stood there, completely forgetting she had done anything to provoke Jeanne.

Jeanne looked into Alice's eyes and realized her gaze hadn't changed much from before, still full of innocence.

Though Alice was now an adventurer, compared to two years ago, her mood seemed to have changed not at all.

Two years ago, in the review grounds of the Holy Roman Empire.

Among the many hero candidates gathered from around the world, two emerged by today.

One was a girl from the great Alpine snow mountains, Alice.

The other came from a remote village in the Kingdom of France, Jeanne.

The two would settle their fate in the review grounds, the victor receiving the hero title from the Pope's wife, becoming the 233rd Hero.

Leading the Crusade Army of ten thousand Holy Church knights, they would march north to suppress the Demon Lord Palace situated in the Death Marsh.

It was a lucrative venture, becoming the human race's hope as the Hero, everyone's greatest wish, enjoying cheers and admiration.

Alice's strength was high-ranked; she left the great snow mountains not long after, but because she was too excited to go out, she didn't bring money, leading to a rather impoverished life.

Coincidentally, the Holy Church had been waging continuous wars against the demon race, suffering heavy losses, many strong ones dying in the suppression battles, and internally, talent was scarce.

In such a situation, when selecting the 233rd Hero, the Holy Church chose to hold the selection across all human empire territories, picking the best.

But the number of people who came to participate was few, because the Holy Church's wars against demons kept failing, too many people died, no one dared to become a hero anymore.

However, Alice, the greenhorn on her first outing, was unafraid, and upon hearing the news of the hero selection, she was actually quite excited, and immediately participated.

Thanks to her years of hard training in the great snow mountains, Alice felt the fruits of her labor in her body, and with her own strength, she fought her way to the final match.

Her final opponent was a girl named Jeanne, who joined the Holy Church later than Alice, but her strength was no joke, passing through the preliminary rounds, entering the final match.

Alice's expression was serious, silently gripping her thin sword at her waist, staring at the opposite Jeanne with golden long hair and a spear in hand, not daring to underestimate her.

Unlike Alice, who wanted to earn money, Jeanne's family was devoted to the Goddess of Light, raised in the light church's culture, a truly devoted follower.

Despite Jeanne's humble origins, she couldn't be stopped by her dream of becoming a Hero to fight injustice. For her, the hero title was something she desperately yearned for.

However, Jeanne didn't dare to underestimate Alice, knowing that since the selection began, she hadn't lost a single match. Though everyone was high-ranked, the opponent was a dual master of magic and combat, giving her an advantage in battle.

The cardinal in bright red robes was the final match's referee. He slowly walked into the center of the review grounds, loudly declaring:

"After two months of selection, today we finally arrive at the final match."

"Alice from the great snow mountains, and Jeanne from France."

"The 233rd Hero will be born between the two of you."

"Regardless of the outcome, both of you are the Holy Church's finest warriors. You two, begin..."

After finishing his speech, the cardinal silently opened the review grounds, handing it over to Alice and Jeanne.

Alice didn't hesitate, drawing her thin sword, pointing at Jeanne, "Let's go."

"Senior, I have a question I'd like to ask..." Jeanne didn't assume an attacking stance, but suddenly had something to say.

"Huh? What? Alice was stunned, "What's going on? Ask away."

"Why do you want to become a Hero? You don't look like someone who worships the goddess, nor a devoted follower. That's strange..."

Jeanne showed a confused expression.

"...Is that so? I never said only those who worship the light church can become heroes, right?" Alice said with a sweat drop, thinking her situation was a bit awkward, like a traitor among the faithful.

"Well, the people who came to the selection were all devoted light followers, yet you're not. I came to become the goddess's sword to purge evil and fight injustice, what exactly are you, the senior, doing here?" Jeanne lowered her head, this doubt had been tormenting her for a while, "You're different from me and all of us. You don't daily confess your sins to the goddess, nor attend the blessing ceremony, it's basically a disgrace..."

"Well, you're right. I'm not a devoted follower. I just came here to become a hero to get the reward for defeating the demons." Alice awkwardly scratched her face with her finger.

"Huh... Jeanne's eyes widened, surprised that Alice had come here for such a trivial reason, just for money?"

"That's... I guess so." Alice said with a slight awkwardness, his tone a bit embarrassed.

Jeanne's face darkened, swinging her spear, assuming a stance, "Without grand ambitions, just for money, you don't deserve to become a Hero. If you became the 233rd Hero, it would be a disgrace to the heroic spirits of past generations. I absolutely won't allow it!"

Alice frowned her brows, thinking, "Is this really such a big deal? Do I have to be as devout as a follower to become a Hero? That's so strange."

The two fell silent, staring intently at each other. With the sound of the clock striking, the duel began.

Jeanne launched the first attack, holding her spear fiercely, raising her spiritual pressure to the extreme.

Her wrist flicked, and a hail of spear strikes like raindrops rushed toward Alice, so dense that even a fly couldn't fly past!

Facing the tough attack, Alice wasn't backing down either, seamlessly switching between magic and spiritual pressure, raising her sword to counterattack.

At that moment, the two clashed with sparks flying, the sound of metal hitting metal was very intense, neither dared to retreat as they exchanged blows.

The two fought without pause, in a short time, they had already exchanged over a hundred rounds without a winner.

Jeanne's spear technique was fierce, and she looked down on Alice, so her attacks left no room for mercy, actually pushing Alice into a corner.

Alice's forehead dripped cold sweat, her thin sword swung in a large arc, launching a volley of ice spears, the ice thorns emerged from the ground, catching Jeanne off guard.

Seeing an opportunity, Alice took a deep breath to counterattack, her thin sword fused with ice crystals, cleaved Jeanne to the ground.

Jeanne tried to get up to fight again, but was held back by the icy sword pressing against her neck, daring not to move a muscle.

Alice's chest rose and fell, breathing heavily, clearly exhausted, but she managed to squeeze out a slight smile:

"I won.

The 233rd Hero is me!"

(???)

title: Chapter 33 — Provocation (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 33 — Provocation (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 15 · Chapter 33

In the two months after the Hero selection ended, the Crusade Army of one hundred thousand set out.
The residents of the entire Holy Roman Empire came out to cheer, scattering flower petals like in the sky, blessing the new Hero.
The scene was grand and solemn, comparable to a major festival held once every four years.
The knights held their heads high, leaving the Holy Capital, looking as if heroes were setting out on a campaign.
Leading them was the trusted Hero Alice, wearing the inherited mithril armor symbolizing her status, riding a white steed, gradually departing amidst countless cheers.
As for the defeated Jeanne, she could only hide in the church’s bell tower, gazing from afar at Alice departing from the Holy Capital.
Watching Alice gain everything—the inherited mithril armor, the highest‑ranking farewell ceremony, the adoration of countless people.
These should not have belonged to Alice; she was just a low‑spec money‑grubber!
As the Goddess’s sword, Alice obviously lacked the qualifications in faith.
Jeanne felt that all of this should have been hers; she believed she was the one most worthy to become Hero and march out to subjugate the evil Demon Lord.
Yet what should have been hers was ruthlessly taken by Alice.
Jeanne felt unwilling inside, thinking that if she just tried a little harder, she could have become Hero and won!
Damn! Why? !
Why wasn’t I the one who became Hero? !
Having someone like Senior Alice become Hero is clearly an insult to the Goddess!
Has the Holy Church already fallen to this state? Even those without faith can become glorious Heroes!
Jeanne’s eyes filled with anger; she silently clenched her fists, harboring extremely complex feelings toward Alice.
On one hand, Jeanne respected her senior Alice, who was strong.
On the other hand, she envied Alice for becoming Hero, and felt some hatred toward her.
Jeanne drew a dagger from her waist, gathered her long hair, and cut it off directly!?
She did this to strengthen her inner resolve, no longer seeing herself as a woman.
Jeanne watched the direction Alice disappeared, silently swearing in her heart—
One day……
One day I will take back everything!
Merlin stood quietly beside them, watching Alice and Jeanne, thinking these two seem to have deep grudges—you can tell from their eyes; it looks like running into them today isn’t a good thing,
Jeanne collected her thoughts, returned to reality, and looked at Alice, speaking bluntly: “Senior Alice, I hate you; everything I did before was to become Hero, yet you took it all away.”
Alice’s expression turned awkward; she hesitated and said, “This isn’t my fault, right? The selection was fair, and I won the duel, wasn’t it?”
“You’re right, Senior Alice did win, but I still haven’t changed my view—you are not worthy to be Hero.” Jeanne said in a serious tone.
“Well… Alice broke out in a slight sweat, never expecting Jeanne to still hate her after all this time. “Whether worthy or not, I’m no longer a Hero now; I’m just an adventurer in debt. The past has little to do with me.”
“Saying ‘it’s fine’ and completely ignoring the past—truly your style, Senior.” Jeanne’s eyes held deep meaning, as if mocking Alice.
Alice furrowed her brows, feeling Jeanne had no intention of catching up, her tone full of cold sarcasm: “What do you want? Are you going to use the Inquisitor’s authority to arrest me as a heretic?”
Upon saying that, the conversation’s atmosphere suddenly grew tense, as if a single disagreement could spark a fight.
Merlin narrowed his eyes, thinking, No way? Are we going to fight? What’s there to argue over a broken Hero? You might as well just obediently come to me for death.
Old Akalon, very timid, muttered quietly, “Miss Alice, calm down; a strong dragon doesn’t crush the local snake—don’t cross the Inquisitor.”
Jeanne’s Inquisitor subordinates nearby felt something was off, and asked tentatively, “Lady Jeanne, you don’t have to do this, right? The other party is at least a former Hero who once fought for the Light.”
Jeanne looked into Alice’s eyes, suddenly smiled, and said calmly, “Senior, what do you think I am? I’m not a petty person; back in the Holy Capital, you, as my senior, once looked after me, for which I’m still grateful. How could I abuse my authority to label you a heretic? That would be repaying kindness with hatred.”
Alice remained silent, thinking that meeting Jeanne today was a mistake; she wasn’t a petty person? Jeanne only knew she was extremely jealous.
“Speaking of which, all that is already in the past; I no longer care that Senior took my Hero position. After calming down, it’s still just that my skill was inferior.” Jeanne adopted a resigned look, then turned fiery: “But since our duel two years ago, we’ve hardly crossed swords; I wonder if Senior would be interested in trying…?”
That sounded rather polite, not aggressive, but said in this atmosphere it was essentially a challenge—Merlin even caught a whiff of gunpowder.
When they met again two years later, Jeanne’s heart burned to prove she was now stronger than Alice, eager to defeat her, to erase her past shame!
“A spar? Just a simple spar?” Old Akalon muttered dubiously, seeing Jeanne’s belligerent tomboyish demeanor, which didn’t look like someone who just wanted a friendly match.
The subordinates of the Inquisitor also felt this was improper; Jeanne is a clergy member, Alice a former Hero—private combat is clearly wrong.
“Lady Jeanne, this isn’t right; private fighting already violates the precepts.”
“Don’t speak; didn’t you hear me say it’s a spar? Does that count as combat?—
Jeanne glanced at the subordinate, gave him a blunt retort, and told him to stay quiet and not meddle.
In a calm state, Merlin could barely sense Jeanne’s— a faint pressure, not matching Alice’s, so he whispered while watching the spectacle, not minding the trouble—
“Alice, don’t hold back, smash her!”
“I’ve seen plenty of troublemakers like this; if you don’t smash her, she’ll just get itchy.”
“Smash her hard, guarantee she’ll behave from now on.”
“Go ahead; I’ll support you with my gaze…”
“Tch! Get lost!” Alice shoved the approaching Merlin aside, examined Jeanne, and said, “This probably won’t work; your injuries seem serious, and you haven’t healed yet—sparring… I think it’s unnecessary.”
“Hah, this injury isn’t anything…” Jeanne let out a cold laugh, her expression turning scornful, unabashedly saying
“How?”
“Senior Alice, are you worrying about pitying me?”
“No need; it’s just a spar. If you don’t dare to accept…”
“Could it be that Senior TT is afraid of me? =二

title: Chapter 34 — Guessing the Great Demon
content:
Chapter 34 — Guessing the Great Demon

Volume 15 · Chapter 34

The provocation in Jadwiga's words was obvious, and the idea of fighting Alice had probably been there from the start.

The atmosphere grew tense, and besides, Alice wasn't the type to just take insults lying down. Perhaps after ten or twenty years apart, this reunion would turn into a fight.

Alice looked into Jadwiga's eyes, thought carefully, then lowered her head and forced out a thin smile.

"Forget it. I'm just a small-time adventurer. How could I dare lay hands on the Inquisitor of Heresy?"

"I don't want to duel you at all. In the past, I just let you off easy."

"Besides, there's no reason to fight you. Maybe you're still nursing old grudges, but I've left the Holy Church. You and I are no longer from the same world."

Merlin involuntarily raised an eyebrow, thinking, "No way? Alice actually held back? This bitch never tolerated me before!"

Jadwiga's face instantly turned ugly, like plaster hardened into a fierce scowl, looking very stiff.

She had assumed Alice was still the same as before—bold and unyielding, with a low tolerance for humiliation.

But she hadn't expected her own belittlement to be so obvious, yet Alice remained unmoved, as if she hadn't heard at all.

Jadwiga felt deeply disappointed in Alice, slowly stood up from her chair, and spoke with a cold tone.

"Senior, you've truly disappointed me. Compared to before, you've completely lost your former passion, becoming cautious and looking back."

"Not even standing up to others' provocations—this is what the Hero is like?"

"Why have you changed so much? Is it because of the man beside you?"

"Huh?!" Merlin was obviously taken aback, suddenly finding the battle flames burning right in front of him. Damn.

"It looks pretty ordinary, like someone trailing behind you eating soft rice. So Senior likes this kind of man? Hard to understand." Jadwiga showed a disdainful expression. If it weren't for the Adventurers Guild registration listing Alice's husband as Merlin, she might have completely overlooked Merlin's insignificant companion.

"....Merlin's face went black, his brows knitted in irritation. Are you kidding me? Alice refuses to duel and takes it out on me? Where's the logic? And now I'm being called a soft rice eater—how infuriating!"

"....Say what, Lord Merlin isn't a soft rice eater. He's a man of real talent!" Old Arcanum couldn't help but speak up for Merlin.

"How laughable." Jadwiga sneered with a mocking expression.

"If you have grievances, Jadwiga, direct them at me. Don't drag others into it." Alice's expression grew stern.

"I don't have any ill feelings. Senior, please don't misunderstand. I'm just disappointed in you." Jadwiga sighed, apparently intending to leave. "I thought Senior was still the same as before. Seems I expected too much. Goodbye. I hope I never see you again. Just live a stable life with that useless man. A mediocre life like that suits you."

"Tch!" Merlin looked unnatural, muttering under his breath, "Honestly, I want to beat her up."

"Don't be like that. She's really scolding me." Alice comforted Merlin, knowing he was annoyed at being unjustly targeted.

"I know, but can she stop using me as a punching bag when she insults you? That really hurts." Merlin's brows were tightly knitted.

"Calm down. She doesn't mean you any harm." Alice sighed helplessly, feeling that Jadwiga was still nursing old grudges.

Recalling the past, Alice felt that becoming the Hero had indeed been somewhat unfair.

Jadwiga had worked so hard serving the Goddess, dreaming of becoming the Hero, yet Alice had trampled all over her.

Compared to Jadwiga's devout faith, Alice became the Hero for the sake of bounties, which seemed quite infuriating.

Even Alice herself felt she had stolen Jadwiga's rightful place.

"Let's go." Jadwiga told her subordinates, then turned around and left with another inquisitor.

Alice watched Jadwiga's retreating back and called out loudly, "Where are you going? Don't you need to rest and recover before leaving? Your injuries aren't minor."

Jadwiga stopped, turned back to look at Alice. "I'm different from you. As a devout follower of the Goddess, I must fight evil at all times. I'm now going to continue hunting the Great Demon Lord who has infiltrated France. Since you've left the Holy Church, don't pry into my affairs. Just spend your days peacefully with that worthless man."

"Huh?" Merlin looked puzzled, thinking, "A Great Demon Lord infiltrating France? That doesn't sound right. Wouldn't that demon be idle, coming to the human empire?"

"They say you suffered heavy losses in the demon battle, and you're still unhealed yet pressing on with the hunt. That's not wise, is it?" Alice hesitated to advise, feeling that Jadwiga's recklessness was excessive.

"Heavy losses? That's an exaggeration. Only three people died. For an inquisitor, dying in the fight against evil is glorious." Jadwiga was very serious, then continued explaining. "I admit I underestimated them. I didn't get to use my trump card in time. If I encounter them again, I'll definitely behead that Great Demon Lord."

"But you're still in this condition... shouldn't you take a break to recover?" Alice's pretty brows were knitted together, thinking, "You've been beaten this badly and still chase demons without resting? Isn't this a vicious cycle?"

"The forces of evil must be eradicated before we can rest. This is the creed of the inquisitors." Jadwiga rejected Alice's good intentions, leaving behind one final sentence as she departed.

"By the way, Senior, that Great Demon Lord is extremely powerful."

"If you happen to encounter it, I advise you not to hesitate—just run."

"Otherwise, your injuries will be worse than mine..."

After Jadwiga and her subordinates left, the tavern fell quiet.

"These inquisitors are like a bunch of madmen." Old Arcanum commented calmly.

"Who says they're not? Like rabid dogs, biting everyone in sight." Merlin agreed expressionlessly.

Alice couldn't help pulling Merlin aside and demanding, "Merlin, didn't you say demons rarely appear in human territory? What's going on here? This is completely different from what you told me."

"Miss, I said 'rarely,' not 'never.'" Merlin shrugged, patiently explaining, "Only demons who have been exiled can linger in human territory for long. Leaving the demon race is their punishment, and they lose all their power. But even so, they could still beat Jadwiga like that. I suspect it's a demon officer-level Great Demon Lord, sent to handle affairs. They won't stay long."

"Is that so? A demon officer... coming to France for what purpose?" Alice asked curiously.

"I'm not deeply involved, so how could I possibly..."

Merlin's sentence was cut short as a flash of insight struck him, remembering recent events.

He touched his chin, thinking, "Wait a minute! Didn't Baphomet's sister get kidnapped recently?"

"Could that demon officer be Baphomet's subordinate, coming to France to search for Miranda?"

"Sss~ Could it be that Baphomet's sister was kidnapped to France?!"

"This guy Asmodeus never mentioned anything to me about this!"

"It must be something like that. It can't be wrong. Otherwise, why would a demon be wandering around human territory?"

"Besides, it's definitely not Baphomet himself coming."

"That guy is a super siscon. He'd kill anyone who threatens his sister!"

"Thinking about it, if it really were Baphomet coming, it wouldn't be as simple as leaving a big pit at Avignon's city gate."

"Baphomet's strength isn't limited to that. If he got serious, he could reduce the capital to ashes in an instant..."

title: Chapter 35 — Dirkett Plain Mercenary Band
content:
Chapter 35 — Dirkett Plain Mercenary Band

Volume 15 · Chapter 35

Alice saw Merlin as if he had lost his soul, completely silent and not speaking, with no idea what he was thinking about. She waved her hand in front of him, asking.

"What's on your mind? Why aren't you talking?"

Merlin shook his head, thinking about how to explain the situation to Alice. "I don't know...this has nothing to do with you or the demon lord's affairs. I'm not even sure what the demon lord is doing in France."

Alice looked down, thinking that Merlin wouldn't know anything about it. "Forget it, let's go back to Arcanum. We need to discuss the disappearance of Avignon's people."

The two returned to Arcanum, preparing to discuss the investigation into Avignon's population disappearance.

Old Arcanum saw Merlin and Alice whispering to each other, but didn't approach them, as they were a couple and had their own secrets.

"We should discuss how to investigate Avignon. Do you have any ideas?"

Alice looked at Merlin and Old Arcanum. "This...I think we should ask the locals. We don't know much about Avignon."

Old Arcanum quickly offered to investigate, thinking this was his chance to show off his skills.

"Really, it's not a problem at all. I'll dig up information and find out what's going on in Avignon."

Alice looked at Old Arcanum, hesitant. "Are you sure? If not, maybe I should go?"

Old Arcanum assured her, "Don't worry, Alice. I'll get to the bottom of it. I've been in tough situations before, and I know how to survive."

Merlin and Alice exchanged a look, and it seemed like they didn't have many good ideas either. Giving Old Arcanum the task was a good choice.

Night began to fall.

In the old city of Avignon, which was once the seat of the baron.

This was the center of the city, bustling with people in the past.

However, since the baroness Camilla took over, the city has been abandoned and left to decay, becoming a desolate and eerie place.

No matter the time of day, the old city was never crowded, and it was said to be a haven for evil spirits.

The people who lived in the old city were usually people who were not welcome in society, such as thieves, gamblers, and bandits.

They lived in the shadows, making a living by day and resting at night.

The old city was ruled by a figure named Dickert, who had a group of mercenaries at his disposal, always stationed in the city.

Dickert's power and influence were unmatched in the city, and even the baroness Camilla was afraid to cross him.

He was like a king in the old city, and even if he looked at the entire city of Avignon, he was still a small tyrant.

Even if Dickert did something bad, no one dared to intervene, as the baroness Camilla seemed to be letting him do as he pleased.

At this moment, in a hidden underground room in the old city, a group of mercenaries were fully armed and ready to fight.

The room was decorated with luxurious furnishings, including red carpets, crystal chandeliers, and a throne.

This setup was almost regal, and it showed Dickert's ambition to establish his own power in the old city.

Recently, Dickert had learned about a great flood in the south, and as someone from the Glen Plains, he immediately realized that the forest might have been destroyed.

Dickert had heard stories about the evil altar in the forest, where it was said that there was a treasure worth a fortune.

He decided to send his deputy to search for the treasure, hoping to be the first to get it.

However, the deputy and his team of ten people went in, and only one person returned alive.

Dickert sat on his throne, looking at the trembling thief.

"How did you come back alone? What happened to the others?"

The thief looked down, afraid to meet Dickert's gaze. "I...I came back, but the others...they all died. I'm the only one left."

Dickert's face turned red with anger. "What about your deputy? How did he die?"

The thief hesitated, knowing that Dickert respected his deputy. "He...he was killed by a tree spirit. We thought it was just a normal tree, but...but it turned out to be a guardian of the forest. I managed to hide in the altar and escape, but...but I don't know how to explain it."

Dickert's eyes narrowed, feeling uneasy. He couldn't believe that his deputy, a saint-tier warrior, had been defeated by a tree spirit.

"What did you find in the altar?"

The thief shook his head. "There was just a broken bottle. It didn't seem to be worth anything."

Dickert's anger grew. "You spent so much time searching, and you didn't find anything? And you lost so many people? How can you come back here and expect me to believe you?"

The thief pointed to a small girl standing beside him. "I...I didn't have a choice. I found her on the road, and she was just a lost child. I brought her back."

Dickert looked at the girl, who was dirty and barefoot, and a hint of a smile appeared on his face. "Ah, I see. Well, in that case, we'll just have to find a buyer for her. She's worth a pretty penny, after all."

The girl cowered, her eyes cast down, and her hands clutched her torn dress. She was terrified of being hurt or sold.

title: Chapter 36 — New Discovery
content:
Chapter 36 — New Discovery

Volume 15 · Chapter 36

The middle of the night.

Something was wrong with Merlin's room - wanting to pee, he found the toilet was broken, which irritated him on this late night.

Damn! This cheap crappy inn, even the toilets are broken!

After cursing fiercely in his heart, Merlin decided to go outside to take care of it - he didn't want to sleep in the smell of urine.

After going downstairs, he saw Alice hadn't slept yet, sitting alone at the counter drinking something.

Merlin knew Alice's problem - she couldn't touch alcohol at all, she'd go crazy immediately. What she was drinking must be ice and milk.

But Alice was alone drinking so late at night - clearly she had something bothering her.

So Merlin gritted his teeth and held back his urge, going to Alice's side.

"What are you doing? Still not sleeping this late."

"Can't sleep."

Alice glanced at Merlin, responding calmly. The dim candlelight illuminated her profile, looking even more sorrowful.

"What? Having troubles?" Merlin leaned his chin on his hand, looking at Alice, not expecting this energetic guy to have times when he wasn't spirited.

"....Nothing..." Alice mumbled in response, clearly not wanting to talk much with Merlin.

"Let me guess...." Merlin feigned thought, asking tentatively, "Is it because of that tomboy Joan?"

"....Alice shivered all over - obviously Merlin hit the mark directly.

"Looks like I guessed right." Merlin smiled, continuing, "She just belittled you a few times - why so down about it?"

"You don't understand." Alice frowned, speaking in low spirits, "Before, in the Holy Capital, Joan was my junior, very respectful of me. Who knew now she's like an enemy - how can this not be disappointing? What exactly did I do wrong?"

"You took away the Hero she dreamed of..." Merlin said bluntly, showing Joan was very jealous - that Alice wasn't a devout enough believer to be the Hero, those were just excuses. It was purely because she lost what she pursued that she was so hostile to Alice.

"I made a mistake becoming the Hero? It was a fair duel, winner takes all - what did I do wrong?" Alice puffed her cheeks, angry - probably Joan had been holding a grudge since leaving.

"You're so straightforward. I killed a demon noble to keep the arrogant monarch's throne - it was already my thing, what did I do wrong?" Merlin shrugged, continuing, "But some people still took dislike to me, thinking I was too young to be a monarch."

"What do you mean?" Alice looked up at Merlin.

"My meaning is, neither of us is wrong, we just happened to become stumbling blocks for others chasing interests." Merlin showed a teasing expression, adding, "This world is like this - people die for wealth, birds die for food. As long as there are conflicting interests, someone inevitably becomes the loser."

Alice thought Merlin made some sense - wasn't she the stumbling block for Joan?

Joan had trained so hard, purely to become the Hero, just wanting to fight for the Goddess.

That beautiful hope in her heart was torn apart by her own greed for money.

If she were Joan, she'd probably be dissatisfied too... meeting again with a bad face was only natural....

Alice sighed, although she knew it wasn't her fault, her kind heart still felt some guilt.

"Don't feel guilty. You can't make everyone like you - if someone has no enemies, that's abnormal. Besides, even the Goddess of Light has Satan as her mortal enemy." Merlin paused, smiling, "If you hadn't become the Hero then, you might never have met me. I might never have met you. This is truly fate's arrangement!"

"....Fate's arrangement?" Alice froze, then her face flushed, seemingly thinking of something else, "....Don't talk nonsense....

"Now I think meeting you isn't a bad thing, actually quite lucky..." Merlin's lips curled slightly, speaking meaningfully.

"....Really? You think so?" Alice's face turned slightly red, becoming somewhat restrained, thinking this bastard finally had feelings for her?

"I robbed your treasure, but thankfully you're a holy maiden. If it were Joan, she'd probably fight me to the death, never willing to cooperate like you." Merlin said in a certain tone.

"Uh,...." Alice's blush gradually faded - this wasn't what she wanted to hear.

"What? This isn't what I imagined he'd say at all!

Meeting me is lucky, just because I didn't hold grudges?

I thought this Merlin guy finally realized I was a good girl!

Result: nothing changed at all. So annoying, I'll never let him flirt with me easily again!

Then at noon.

Old Acalon left before dawn to gather information, very enthusiastic.

This was his own mission - a good chance to prove himself, so he was excited.

Result: Old Acalon returned at noon, apparently it wasn't as hard as imagined.

At this point in Alice's room, several people gathered -

"Have you figured out the cause of the missing persons?" Alice asked with a blank face.

"Not yet." Old Acalon said awkwardly.

"You've been out all morning - what did you find?" Merlin asked anxiously, feeling his expectations would be disappointed again.

"I was surrounded by refugees, I didn't manage to..." Old Acalon replied, embarrassed.

Alice lowered her head, whispering to Merlin, "See? I told you not to give this to Old Acalon, he can't figure it out."

Merlin had black lines on his forehead, saying helplessly, "But Old Acalon is French after all, he knows some things better than us."

Alice slapped her forehead, worried, "It's been so long, and you still trust him? We've been wandering France aimlessly too long."

Merlin had no reply - he'd defended Acalon, but he wasn't pulling his weight, and Alice was about to explode.

"Stop whispering! I haven't finished!" Old Acalon saw the couple starting their meeting, probably thinking he'd failed again -

"Although I didn't figure out why people keep disappearing in Avignon -

"But I have a newer major discovery -

"Recently, many daughters of the refugees who came to Avignon have disappeared mysteriously."

title: Chapter 37 — Alice, the Pawn
content:
Chapter 37 — Alice, the Pawn

Volume 15 · Chapter 37

"Huh?" Alice froze in surprise, asking in astonishment, "Is that really true?"

"Absolutely. The families that entered Avignon to take refuge mostly had daughters, and many women have mysteriously disappeared during this period." To dispel Merlin and Alice's doubts, Old Araklon added, "I'm not making this up; those refugees told me themselves."

"If that's the case? If their daughters have disappeared, didn't those refugee parents look for them? Or report it to the local guards or something?"

Merlin felt something was off. With so many people missing, the incident should have caused a huge uproar. Yet, when they first arrived, they hadn't heard of any such events. It was only after Old Araklon went out to inquire that they learned of it.

"How could they not react? Many of them stood at the gate of the Guard Corps and refused to leave, questioning the matter. But those people are refugees with no one to rely on. Even if they reported it to the local guards, there was no response at all. The guards of Avignon acted as if they hadn't heard a thing, and would even arrest a few who reacted too strongly, seemingly trying to suppress the matter..." Old Araklon spread his hands, wearing an expression of incomprehension.

"Hiss~" Merlin drew a sharp breath, stroking his chin as he thought in confusion. This was truly strange. People were disappearing mysteriously, and the local guards just ignored it? Wasn't the duty of the guards to maintain the safety of the residents?

"Damn it! How outrageous! So many people have gone missing, and the guards have no right to ignore it!" Alice slammed the table and stood up in anger, having witnessed oppression and unfairness.

"Perhaps... they just don't want to meddle in others' affairs? There are plenty of people who take their salaries without doing their jobs..." Old Araklon mused.

"Old Master Araklon, didn't you say that the lord of Avignon is a shrewd and capable manager? With so many people protesting at the Guard Corps, can she not see it?" Alice voiced her doubts, feeling that as an administrator, not being fully aware of the local situation was a dereliction of duty. Moreover, the local lord, Countess Camilla, was praised as an excellent ruler, so it was strange that she would turn a blind eye to the disappearance of people.

"Poors are not allowed to enter the area of the Count's Manor. Perhaps Countess Camilla simply doesn't know about this?" Old Araklon speculated, noting that the female count seemed to rarely go out and thus couldn't experience the life of the lowest strata.

Merlin frowned, feeling an increasingly strong sense of dissonance. This Avignon, which appeared prosperous on the surface, seemed to harbor some unspeakable secrets.

"Since the local guards won't handle it, we will! We must catch that human trafficker!" Alice declared passionately.

A large drop of sweat rolled down Merlin's forehead. He thought, Sure enough, here we go again. Has this woman forgotten that investigating the Blood Clan is the most important thing?

"Miss Alice is right. We adventurers must uphold the spirit of acting bravely for justice. This matter... we should get involved!" Old Araklon's chuunibyou soul began to burn brightly again.

"Wait, can you two calm down? Our primary goal is to investigate the whereabouts of the Blood Clan, not to meddle in this, okay?" Merlin couldn't hold back anymore and spoke up to emphasize their objective.

"Lord Merlin, the recent disappearances of girls in Avignon may be related to past disappearance incidents. What if they are being sold to vampires as food? So it is still worth investigating," Old Araklon said seriously.

"Yes, Merlin. You need to be flexible. It's the same kind of mysterious disappearance of people. Perhaps the Blood Clan is acting in the shadows? We just happened to stumble upon it. This is a rare opportunity." Alice agreed with Old Araklon's opinion for the first time.

"You..." Merlin looked at Alice, then at Old Araklon, and spread his hands, saying, "Heh, what can I say? Whatever you say is fine..."

Merlin had given up resisting. It was obvious that Alice and Old Araklon shared the same view, and he himself was simply the odd one out.

No matter what Merlin said now, it was always a two-against-one situation, making it difficult to change Alice's and Old Araklon's minds.

"But where should we go to find those human traffickers? Do you have any leads, Mr. Araklon?" Alice asked tentatively, as she knew nothing about human traffickers yet.

"I naturally inquired about that. Combining the statements of several refugee families, I found that the missing women are all young and pure," Old Araklon said very seriously.

"Young and pure?" Alice looked thoughtful, finding this commonality strange.

Merlin raised his eyebrows, and his gaze inexplicably shifted to Alice, as if he had come up with an idea.

"...Why are you looking at me like that?" Alice felt uncomfortable under Merlin's stare.

"Alice, you're a virgin, right?" Merlin suddenly asked an extremely awkward question.

"Ah!?" Alice froze for a moment, her face turning red at a visible speed. She stammered in a panic, "Wh-why... why are you asking that!? ...I I... I am a... virgin, and... what does that have to do with you!"

"Judging by that reaction, it's definitely 'yes'..." Merlin wore a meaningful smile, looking very like he deserved a beating.

"What is that expression on your face!? Don't laugh! Be careful or I'll beat you to death!" Alice waved her small fists threateningly, but it had absolutely no intimidation. Being asked such a question by Merlin suddenly made her extremely embarrassed; she wished she could find a crack in the ground and crawl into it.

"I don't mean anything by it. I just thought of a plan. If a pure woman goes out walking late at night, the human traffickers might come to us on their own."

"That's right, Miss Alice perfectly fits the description of a young and pure woman. Isn't she the prime target for human traffickers!"

Merlin and Old Araklon both turned their gazes toward the isolated Alice. Both of their faces showed approval, as if they were selling out their teammate.

"You... what are you thinking? Are you trying to make me, a girl, go be the bait!?" Alice was not willing, feeling as if she had been abandoned. Going alone to be bait was not a good thing! If there was any danger, wouldn't she be the first to suffer? For such a dangerous task, it would be more reasonable for the tough-skinned Merlin to go.

"Miss Alice, aren't you a glorious little guardian of justice?" Merlin put on the expression of a veteran cadre who wouldn't let go of a point, speaking to Alice with a heavy tone.

"Now is the time when the organization needs you. Even if some sacrifices must be made, it is worth it."

"I see you love meddling in others' affairs every day. You can't have that little sense of duty, can you?"

title: Chapter 38 — God-damn Kidnapping
content:
Chapter 38 — God-damn Kidnapping

Volume 15 · Chapter 38

Here's a translation that follows all the rules:

Night fell.

Alice had no choice; she was selected as the bait for this plan, and absolutely no objections were allowed.

In such a quiet black night, Alice—just by herself—walked out, wandering the somewhat obscure streets of Avignon.

To dress like a homeless refugee, Alice put on dirty clothes and smeared a bit of dust on her face; she really looked like a refugee wandering the night, perfectly blending in with the refugee group.

Alice's clothes were bought by Merlin from the refugees a few copper coins at a time; the refugees had taken Merlin for a fool, after all, who would use money to buy broken, tattered clothes?

Since Alice had to pretend to be a homeless refugee, she couldn't bring her own sword; she had to go hands-on.

If Alice wore a slender sword on her person, it would look utterly out of place with a refugee's identity, and might even scare off the human traffickers.

This left Alice, weaponless, feeling a bit anxious inside; not having her sword at hand was quite unsettling.

However, according to the plan, Merlin and Old Akarion would secretly keep watch from the shadows, following Alice the whole way until they discovered the human traffickers' hideout.

Though Alice felt unsettled without a weapon in hand, she figured Merlin would definitely protect her in secret; yet the reality was...

On a rather tall building in Avignon, Merlin and Old Akarion looked down from above, observing the streets Alice was moving through.

The view was quite open, allowing one to see farther; Alice's expression could barely be made out, but the night was too dark; if one wasn't careful, the view would be lost.

But to avoid startling the snake and making the human traffickers wary, Merlin and Old Akarion couldn't get close to Alice; they could only watch from afar.

Old Akarion held a rather crude monocular, keeping his gaze fixed on Alice in the distance.

He was already very old, his eyesight was getting bad, and staring at Alice was very taxing on him.

"Merlin, you're also helping to watch over Miss Alice, aren't you? My eyesight is getting blurrier in the night..."

"Don't worry, old man, Alice won't be in danger. Is she a match for some small thieves? Besides, you'd do better to worry about the safety of those small thieves."

Merlin lay on the roof, closing his eyes for a small rest; he didn't seem very concerned about Alice's safety at all.

"Though that's what's said, one must still prepare for the worst, right?" Old Akarion was timid, cautious about everything.

"It's fine, I'm watching Alice. /A Merlin's calm response; as a demon, his night vision is far superior to humans', and he can lock onto Alice's silhouette with just a casual glance."

"Then I can relax." Old Akarion set down his monocular and let out a breath. "Say, Merlin..."

"What is it?" Merlin lifted his eyelids slightly.

"You and Miss Alice are supposedly a couple, why don't you honestly express your love for her?" Old Akarion suddenly asked a question that felt utterly nonsensical. T SE Light Novel

"Ah!?" Merlin was scared out of his wits, his mouth twitching as he asked, "W-why are you asking this?"

"Because I can tell, you like Miss Alice, don't you? But whenever you're together, you're often so cold; many times you want to care for her, but your behavior isn't very positive, ah?" Old Akarion slowly sat down, continuing to ask, you two are clearly a couple, why can't you be straightforward? It's truly strange; is there some hidden reason?"

"Old man, stop talking nonsense; the situation isn't what you think..." A drop of cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead; his look was somehow giving off a sense of guilt.

"With just one glance, I can see through you, Merlin. I think Miss Alice is quite proactive, actually; sometimes she hopes you'd give some reaction, but it's always been unsuccessful, resulting in unnecessary anger..." Old Akarion paused, continuing, "I've seen many couples, and yours and Miss Alice's, I've only seen once before—it's too strange, always giving a sense of disharmony..."

..... Merlin's eyes darted about, not wanting to tightly lock his forehead in answer to Old Akarion's question one after another.

We aren't truly a couple, so the lack of harmony is quite normal, isn't it?

Alice is mostly being unreasonable, that's why she's so proactive.

And I like this old bitch? Impossible, impossible, impossible...

On the other side.

Alice, to look more like a refugee, walked with a somewhat fatigued appearance.

Her eyes would occasionally look around warily, raising her senses to the maximum; even the slightest wind or grass movement could be anticipated in advance.

That fellow Merlin... is he really watching me well?

Alice couldn't help but wonder internally, thinking about Merlin's usual attitude, she always felt unreliable.

After Alice passed through three small alleys, she arrived at an area particularly sparse in pedestrians; there was almost no light nearby, incredibly dim.

.

Just then, Alice suddenly sensed something amiss; earlier, when people were coming and going, she hadn't noticed, but now, with few people around, she discovered something strange.

Two people had been trailing her from beginning to end, secretly following Alice, and seemed to have been watching her for a long time.

But now that it was suddenly empty all around, the two of them following behind looked particularly conspicuous, easy for Alice to capture.

Alice moved slowly, secretly glancing backward; she saw two men behind her, dressed simply in armor, looking like mercenaries from there?

To infiltrate the enemy camp, Alice needed to lure the traffickers to her base, and then pull off a complete sweep.

So Alice went where there were fewer people, and finally arrived at a pitch-black alley; here, there was no one.

Alice stopped, thinking about how to be lured smoothly by the other party without raising suspicion.

She began to stew her emotions, planning to pretend to be a innocent girl, making the two suspicious guys lower their guard.

Who would have thought that after Alice stewed her emotions for a while, preparing to turn around and act pitiful, she directly and inexplicably got hit on the head with a club! ?

... Yeah.

Alice received HP-1 damage, and instantly fell into a faint, lying on the ground motionless.

This, of course, is impossible! How could Alice, who is a Saint-tier powerhouse, be knocked out by a club? Unless Merlin personally made a move, there's drama.

Alice was hit on the head just to dispel the suspicion of the two suspicious guys behind her; the other party naturally had to faint weakly, being a powerless refugee girl!

Would she have to turn around and curse MMP, raise her little fist, and hammer the chests of these two suspects into crushing fractures? ! That doesn't fit the refugee girl's setting!

Though even so, after Alice fell to the ground, she still furrowed her brows, unable to help but internally harshly criticize

Isn't the point to kidnap! What kind of kidnapping is this! ?

Straight up a club! Clearly it's abduction, okay! ?

Indeed, being a bait is really dangerous. ●° (>_ <0)°●o

title: Chapter 39 — Mercenary Corps Headquarters
content:
Chapter 39 — Mercenary Corps Headquarters

Volume 15 · Chapter 39

The Mercenary Group's Headquarters

SOURCE TEXT:
<<<BEGIN SOURCE>>>
Alice feigned unconsciousness, lying motionless on the ground, thinking she would soon be tied up and taken back to their lair.

Although things weren't quite as Alice had imagined, it seemed that overall they were still proceeding as normal.

Two mercenaries wearing simple protective gear approached Alice. After carefully inspecting her, they found that she had already fainted and breathed a sigh of relief.

"It's done, she's already unconscious," said the long-haired mercenary, dropping his stick.

"That's really steady and accurate," exclaimed the short-haired mercenary.

"I've done it so many times, no exaggeration, I can knock anyone unconscious with one blow without causing serious injury," said the long-haired mercenary, confident in his stealth skills.

"That's great, we're so lucky that we can find such a perfect prey just by wandering around," exclaimed the short-haired mercenary, feeling very happy.

"That's right, we're so lucky today, we can rescue a woman so easily. Now those refugees are so protective of their daughters that it's almost impossible to get to them. It seems like our business is getting harder and harder," said the long-haired mercenary, sighing deeply.

"But... isn't it too easy? Could there be a trap?" asked the short-haired mercenary, suspicious that this kidnapping was too easy and something was wrong.

"No, this woman is alone, I've carefully observed the surroundings and there are no other people," replied the long-haired mercenary confidently.

0) y F's Xiaozhi

"That's good, we'll take her back and I'm sure the boss will be happy," said the short-haired mercenary with a greedy smile.

"Of course, even though the deputy leader died unexpectedly, the boss has been in a bad mood lately, but yesterday we caught a three or four year old girl, and if we add today's catch, our mercenary group won't have to live in poverty anymore," explained the long-haired mercenary.

Alice, lying on the ground, frowned slightly, thinking, "A three or four year old girl? These people are definitely human traffickers! That girl must be someone's daughter! These scum... not one of them can be spared!"

"This is good news, but she's a bit old for us today. Usually we prefer little lolitas. I wonder if the boss will be satisfied," said the short-haired mercenary, looking at Alice on the ground.

Alice felt a surge of anger in her heart, thinking, "What the hell! Who is old! You are old! Your whole family is old!"

The two mercenaries had inadvertently touched the pain points of all the girls. If it weren't for the mission at hand, Alice might have immediately stood up and hammered these two bastards to death!

In fact, Alice was not very old, but compared to three or four year old lolitas, being called an aunt didn't seem so bad, right?

"She's definitely a bit old, but we'll make do for now. We can't find better prey," replied the long-haired mercenary helplessly.

Alice felt like crying, thinking that even though she was kidnapped voluntarily, it was only because she was a good enough bait, and the failure of being an诱饵 had reached a certain level...

"That's true, but at her age, can she still be a virgin? If she's not pure, she won't fetch a high price," asked the short-haired mercenary again.

"Of course she is, trust my eyes, you can tell from her walking posture," said the long-haired mercenary, pointing to his eyes.

"Is that so? She's an old virgin, I guess she's not very likable and no man would want her," speculated the short-haired mercenary.

"Alright, stop talking nonsense, quickly lift her onto the cart and take her back home," urged the long-haired mercenary.

Alice's forehead was throbbing with veins, her small pride was being stabbed to pieces by these two thieves.

Old virgin! ? Who are they talking about! ?

That's the name I use every day to irritate my teacher! ?

I never thought that today, this humiliating title would be placed on my head!

Damn you! Wait for me, I'll definitely kill you when I have the chance!

On the other side, Merlin and Old Acalon were both a bit distracted.

Especially Old Acalon, who was too old and his mental state couldn't keep up, he was very sleepy.

Merlin glanced over and was about to check if there was any trouble with Alice.

However, upon looking, Merlin's eyebrows frowned, because Alice had disappeared!

Merlin quickly rolled over and stood up, using his superior night vision to search the streets where Alice had been active, but found not a single shadow!

This could only mean one thing: Alice had been kidnapped, which proved that the plan had worked and successfully lured out the human traffickers! Following the trail might lead to a big haul.

"She's gone!"

"What? What's gone?" The confused Old Acalon was suddenly awakened and asked in astonishment.

"Alice is gone, she seems to have been kidnapped," said Merlin, frowning slightly.

"What! ? It worked!" Old Acalon was like he had been injected with chicken blood, suddenly becoming energetic.

"Go! Chase! We must find these human traffickers' lair," said Merlin, throwing one sentence and then jumping onto the ground, his body flying up like a cat, his shadow speeding across the rooftops.

"Okay," said Old Acalon, nodding, his expression serious, knowing that this wasn't the time to nap, but his skills weren't comparable to Merlin's, and he had just taken a step when he fell off the roof, letting out a cry of pain, "Ouch!"

Merlin had to stop and look down from the building, finding that Old Acalon had luckily fallen into a pile of grass, "Old man, are you okay?"

"I... I'm fine, you go after Miss Alice, don't worry about me!" said Old Acalon, supporting his old waist with his hand, slowly standing up and not wanting to be a burden.

"Fine," said Merlin, seeing that Old Acalon wasn't seriously hurt, so he nodded and quickly started chasing, disappearing into the night.

The two mercenaries got into the driver's seat of the carriage and arrived at the deserted old town of Avignon.

After arriving at a relatively secret ruin, they stopped the carriage.

Dictoplin's mercenary group headquarters was located underground in this ruin.

It was originally the ruins of a church, with a spacious basement underneath.

After being occupied by Dictoplin, it was turned into a secret headquarters, making it difficult for people to find and providing excellent concealment.

"We're here, let's lift this woman inside and show her to the boss."

"Got it, come and help."

The two mercenaries got off the carriage and walked directly to the back, planning to lift Alice inside.

Alice's eyes were tightly closed, with a small gap showing, observing the surroundings, and her heart couldn't help but stir, thinking...

Is this the place?

The carriage hasn't been here for long, it should still be in Avignon city, right?

I never expected that the human traffickers' lair would be in the main city! That's really surprising...
