title: Chapter 50 — The Bloodshed Caused by Stealing a Man
content:
Chapter 50 — The Bloodshed Caused by Stealing a Man

Volume 15 · Chapter 50

Alice, like a pet guarding its food, shielded Merlin behind her, preventing Ophelia from getting any closer. Although Alice didn't say it out loud, seeing Ophelia touch Merlin here and there made her feel sour inside, and she was really unhappy!
Alice's action somewhat annoyed Ophelia; the originally joyful reunion atmosphere was abruptly shattered.
Especially with Alice standing between Ophelia and Merlin, it felt like a stumbling block.
"Hey Alice, what are you doing? I just need to talk to her, don't cause trouble." Merlin poked Alice's shoulder with his finger.
"What are you talking about? This woman is clearly getting handsy, she must have bad intentions. What's your relationship?" Alice's tone was full of jealousy, she was practically dying of sourness.
"Didn't I already say? She's the maid who specifically takes care of me and Lilith; if you insist on labeling her, she's like a sister." Merlin spread his hands, explaining, feeling that Alice had misunderstood something.
Originally, demons don't really like humans, Merlin planned to chat with Ophelia and then send her back.
But Alice, for some unknown reason, jumped out directly, making things even more complicated.
Ophelia's mood is probably not good right now; she might even lash out in anger.
"Sister? You don't look like one at all. Who has a sister who acts all lovey-dovey over her brother? That's just perverted." Alice muttered under her breath.
"I don't know what to say about Merlin, but Alice really guessed right—Ophelia is a pervert." "Where did this maggot come from, daring to interrupt my reunion with Your Majesty? Get lost! A mere livestock coming within five meters of Your Majesty is nothing but an insult!" Ophelia shouted angrily, her attitude instantly changing; just moments ago she had been all coquettish toward Merlin.
"Don't misunderstand, I'm not interrupting you; could you please keep your hands to yourself? Please show some restraint." Alice said seriously.
"Your Majesty hasn't even said anything, what are you to meddle?" Ophelia looked at Alice jumping out, as if seeing a fly—utterly disgusted, wishing she could crush this human outright. However, Alice still maintained her dragonified state, exuding an aura mixed with dragon's might. Although Ophelia wasn't afraid of Alice, her intuition told her this human woman wasn't easy to deal with. "Besides, I've watched Your Majesty grow up smiling; even being affectionate is normal." Merlin had a series of black lines slide down his forehead, thinking, "Normal my ass!" Secretly fantasizing about his master—what kind of normal is that?!
"Sorry, even if you take good care of Merlin, I won't allow such casualness." "Human, are you confused about the situation? If you don't get lost, don't blame me for being impolite." Ophelia's eyes gradually turned vicious, wanting to kill the human woman before her.
"Ophelia-sister, calm down, this guy is my companion, not an enemy." Seeing the atmosphere grow increasingly tense, Merlin hurriedly spoke up to explain for Alice, as he didn't want to see Ophelia and Alice fight—both women had a good relationship with him, and truly fighting would make it hard to know whom to help.
"Companion? Your Majesty isn't joking, right? How could you possibly stoop to having livestock as a companion?" Ophelia furrowed her brows, not really believing Merlin's words.
"Really, we truly are companions; we've been together for a long time." Merlin replied embarrassedly, thinking, "This zero— a beast of burden, indeed demons treat humans terribly."
.会
Ophelia was half-believing, half-doubting, she re-examined Merlin and noticed something like a small metal tag necklace on his neck—that was the black iron adventurer's proof—
Region: Rexerum.
Name: Merlin Lucifer.
Wife: Alice Claudya.
Occupation: just a villager with no magic or fighting spirit, by the way his wife is even more impressive—she eats soft rice~
After seeing the information on the black iron adventurer's proof, Ophelia stood there stunned, completely speechless. Lucifer? This refers to the Lucifer family, the information is Merlin's true details!
What's going on?
Your Majesty working as an adventurer in Rexerum? When did that happen? I have no recollection at all!
And it's still the lowest rank black iron; with Your Majesty's strength, how could you possibly be ranked so low?!
Even if you fought with your feet the whole time, you should be the highest existence!
Why does it describe Your Majesty as a soft‑rice‑eating coward? That's disrespect to the Demon Lord!
Could it be that Your Majesty has been out here for so long, doing terribly, and has fallen to this point?!
Wait a minute! This isn't the point! What's with the wife column?! I've never heard that Your Majesty got married!
Who the hell is Alice Claudya?! How dare she steal my man!, i
Ophelia's mind went crazy ranting; just the information on the adventurer's proof alone gave her a huge shock.
"Ah" Merlin grabbed the adventurer's proof on his neck, wanting to speak but hesitating, "This... to say..."
Ophelia subconsciously glanced at Alice's adventurer's proof; if she hadn't looked, it would've been fine, but after looking she completely lost her mind—
Region: Rexerum.
Name: Alicia Claudya<
Husband: Merlin Lucifer.
Occupation: Swordswoman of the demon sword.
Ophelia was struck as if by lightning, her spirit taking 9999 points of trauma; combining the two pieces of information, she uncovered an unbelievable secret!
The fly that disturbed my intimacy with Your Majesty is none other than Alice Claudya, Your Majesty's wife! ?
No! ! ! Impossible! How could Your Majesty secretly marry behind everyone's back!
Your Majesty, whom I raised myself, I've watched you since childhood—why would some nameless woman suddenly appear and steal him away!?
Ophelia's delicate body trembled, her face instantly drained of blood turning pale; her slender fingers, trembling, pointed at Merlin and Alice.
"Don't misunderstand, we're just..." Merlin frowned, seeing Ophelia about to break down, he instantly knew what she was misunderstanding.
After all, Merlin knows Ophelia appears as a caring sister on the surface, but deep down she harbors romantic fantasies about him; just the mistaken information on the adventurer's proof is enough to cause a huge mix‑up.
Alice said nothing beside him, seeing Ophelia's agitated reaction, she understood—surely this female demon likes Merlin, right? Seeing our marital introduction, did she start losing her mind?
Ophelia lowered her head, her face darkened to gloom, her eyes turned empty and dazed, murderous intent stirring.
"Companion? That's not all there is to being a companion!"
Would Your Majesty rather marry a human beast of burden and not even consider me?
No! —It must be that this fox spirit used some trick to bewitch my little Merlin, unforgivable!
To use such despicable means to win Your Majesty's favor—she truly is a despicable and shameless human!
Suddenly her body erupted with a massive amount of poisonous gas, as if green flames were burning on her, rage sky‑high!
Ophelia lifted her ashen‑gray face, wearing a smile that didn't reach her eyes, and spoke in a cold, icy tone:
"Your Majesty, please stay far away—I fear I might accidentally hurt you."
"According to the contract rules, I must obey the summoner's orders."
"But to strike at you, I truly cannot; however, that woman named Alice, the fox spirit, will surely die."
"Now I will fulfill the contract rules and tear this despicable woman into ten thousand pieces!"

title: Chapter 51 — War of Two Women
content:
Chapter 51 — War of Two Women

Volume 15 · Chapter 51

“Wait,”
Merlin had just wanted to stop Ophelia from attacking Alice, but before he could finish his sentence, the battle suddenly began.
Ophelia could not suppress her inner anger, she first broke the peace and launched a fatal poison gas strike at Alice!
Alice was caught off guard by Ophelia's sudden attack, she didn't have time to react and was forced back.
Merlin widened his eyes, thinking, “Just attack without a word?!” Completely ignoring self
Ophelia came to Merlin's side, with a cold face, seriously said, “Next I will carry out my mission; I hope Your Majesty does not interfere. For the wicked one who bewitched His Majesty, I have the duty to eradicate her!”
“It's not what you think; calm down and talk properly.” Merlin said with a dark face, seriously, trying to ease the atmosphere.
However, Ophelia now couldn't listen at all, directly ignored Merlin and walked toward Alice.

Chapter 52 — Merlin's Choice (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 15 · Chapter 52

**Merlin's Choice? (Monthly Ticket Bonus)**

<<<BEGIN SOURCE>>>
"Shout!

Alice clutched her left arm, feeling a searing pain that threatened to render it useless. The slow corrosion of the poison on her flesh was even more agonizing than a knife wound.

She was a fiercely independent person by nature, not one to yield easily to bullying. If Ophelia was taking advantage of her, she would never stand idly by and let it happen!

Moreover, Ophelia always spoke with a tone of contempt, looking down on Alice and demanding that she leave Merlin on her own.

Alice would never agree to this. She had never thought the demon race was noble, and she was even less polite than the elves!

Furthermore, Alice thought that even if she married Merlin and became his wife, what difference would it make? Would others still interfere? !

Enraged and ashamed, Alice angrily pointed her short sword at Ophelia, and the blade immediately emitted a golden glow.

This was the move Alice had used in the British capital to kill the Thorn Knight: the Frost Lance, a long-range killing technique.

Starting with the short sword, a golden ice spear appeared out of thin air, taking the shape of a long spear, and shot towards Ophelia's abdomen, as if to pierce through the enemy!

Ophelia was still in a state of triumph, feeling that Alice's strength was not great. Although her dragon-transformed appearance was intimidating, fighting her was not a big pressure.

But Ophelia didn't expect that Alice had a very strong will and immediately started counterattacking!

"Oh!"

The frost lance stabbed deeply into Ophelia's abdomen, and her entire body was pushed out, crashing into the end of the underground hall before stopping.

Thick smoke rose, and a golden ice spear pierced through the entire underground chamber, looking quite spectacular.

Alice used facts to prove that she was not a soft target either, and not to look down on the entry.

....You bastard!

Ophelia, who was nailed to the wall by the ice spear, glared angrily at Alice, her voice trembling with anger.

Her abdomen was pierced by the ice spear, and bright red blood dripped down her body onto the ground, but she was not seriously injured. The demon's vitality was still very strong.

The ice spear brought a fierce coldness into her body, and Ophelia felt that her movements were becoming slower, unable to keep up with her thoughts.

Ophelia smashed the ice spear with her hand, sliding down the wall, and then pulled out the ice spike embedded in her abdomen, causing blood to fly everywhere. The scene suddenly became violent.

"Now you understand what respect means, right? If you don't, I can continue to teach you!" Alice said calmly, enduring her injuries, with cold sweat streaming down her forehead.

"Don't get too complacent, human! This injury is nothing to me! I'm not as fragile as you!" Ophelia covered her pierced wound with her hand, feeling that it was not a fatal injury, and the problem was not serious.

Merlin's expression was very ugly. Alice and Ophelia were fighting too fiercely, and he felt uncomfortable being caught in the middle. He couldn't help but think,

Damn it! They've already drawn blood. Are they really going to keep fighting like this?

For the first time, he discovered that women are such scary creatures, especially when their jealousy is triggered, they become like lunatics!

Merlin had underestimated them too much. In front of him were two jealous women who had started a war over a man, and their attacks were particularly vicious.

Even Alice, who was usually like a little angel, became very fierce in this situation, giving Ophelia no mercy, absolutely unwilling to lose.

Hey! You two stop fighting and calm down and talk properly! There are big misunderstandings here!

"No more talk, Your Majesty. For your future, I must eliminate this human woman. If you cannot bring yourself to do it, leave it to me. You just need to stay out of it." Ophelia said seriously.

"That's right, Merlin. Don't interfere. This is between us two, and has nothing to do with you. I haven't reached the point where I need to ask for help yet." Alice said seriously, also not wanting Merlin to interfere at this time.

Although both were in a state of jealousy, they were still competing secretly, as if admitting to asking for help would mean losing.

Merlin's expression became awkward. He thought, Am I redundant? They've completely ignored me!

"You are not allowed to call the name under the 'Your Majesty' title! You have no right to do so!" Ophelia couldn't even call Merlin by his name casually, so why should a human be allowed to do so! ?

"I usually call him that, and I don't think there's anything strange about it." Alice said provocatively.

"How dare you!" Ophelia's face contorted, her mouth stretched all the way to her ears, looking very large and losing its original beauty.

Then, poisonous gas spewed out from Ophelia's mouth, and the thick poison instantly filled the entire hall.

It seemed that Ophelia was going to get serious and paralyze Alice, then slowly devour her.

Alice wouldn't just sit there and wait to die. She kicked hard, and her body instantly approached Ophelia.

Each time she swung her short sword, a golden ice spear accompanied it, launching a fierce attack on Ophelia.

The two women didn't have much time to catch their breath before they were fighting again, with no possibility of reconciliation.

Merlin was in a bad state. He was struggling internally, thinking that he was a man after all, and it was useless to stand by while they fought.

If he wanted to stop this meaningless fight, Merlin would have to choose a side and clearly show who he wanted to protect.

One was his sister, Ophelia, who had taken care of him since he was a child.

The other was his current teammate, who also served as a mascot in his home, Alice.

This put Merlin in a difficult choice, as he didn't want to offend either of them. If he upset one of them, he would have trouble.

Alice and Ophelia fought for a long time, and the entire underground chamber was almost destroyed by them.

However, after so much time had passed, Ophelia's poison began to take effect, and the outcome became very clear.

Alice burst out of the poison fog, kneeling on one knee and breathing heavily. Cold sweat streamed down her forehead, and she felt her whole body was in a state of paralysis, unable to move.

Even Alice's magic and fighting spirit were out of control due to the paralysis, and she couldn't control them.

"Hmph, this is an underground chamber, not the outside. You can't avoid my poison."

Ophelia slowly walked out of the poison fog, her body covered in many sword wounds, but her movements were slow, obviously affected by Alice's coldness.

Don't look at Ophelia's expression, which seems very composed. In fact, she wasn't doing well either.

.........Alice was breathing heavily, and her dragon-transformed state had to be removed. She couldn't help but feel anxious. What should she do? Her body was completely powerless!

Ophelia came in front of Alice, in a victorious posture, corroding the kneeling Alice, and slowly lifted her skirt!

"Oh!" Alice was stunned, not knowing what Ophelia was going to do! ? Was she going to show her precious treasure! ? No..... Impossible! How could such an outrageous thing happen in such a serious situation!

After Ophelia lifted her maid's skirt, eight black and strong spider legs extended from underneath. These were part of her true form.

The eight black spider legs were all aimed at Alice, covered with green poison, looking very deformed and terrifying.

Ophelia revealed a hideous smile, laughing and wanting to deliver the final blow to Alice.

"Die! You despicable human woman!"

Looking at the eight spider legs attacking her, Alice's face turned pale, her pupils contracted, and she felt the threat of death.

However, Ophelia's attack stopped halfway, and the spider legs hovered in the air, not daring to advance an inch.

Because Merlin stood in front of Alice, after much consideration, he chose his home's precious treasure.

"Ophelia, I told you she's my companion. Don't go too far...."

Merlin's tone became cold and full of authority, and he no longer called Ophelia "sister," creating distance between them.

This look was clearly that of a superior using a commanding tone, expecting the subordinate to obey.

"Your Majesty......" Ophelia revealed an expression of surprise, feeling very uneasy, and instinctively took two steps back.

"You actually protected that human!"

title: Chapter 53 — The Buried Root of Disaster
content:
Chapter 53 — The Buried Root of Disaster

Volume 15 · Chapter 53

"No! Impossible! How could His Majesty protect a human woman?!" Ophelia stepped back repeatedly, finding Merlin's actions too abnormal. As a Great Demon Lord of the demon race, how could he protect a human woman?! This was way too unnatural!

Alice saw Merlin protecting her. Though happy inside, she was still competing with Ophelia, so she stubbornly said, "Merlin, I—"

"Stop talking first. What was originally a simple matter became troublesome because you jumped in." Merlin complained softly, annoyed by Alice's habit of always sticking her nose in.

"Ah? ... Blame me?" Alice felt accused by Merlin, utterly unwilling to accept it, wanting to stand up and argue, but her body was paralyzed and she couldn't move at all.

Merlin didn't want to deal with Alice for now, turning to Ophelia instead. "After fighting so long, shouldn't your anger have subsided? I don't care about your quarrel, but I won't allow murderous intent."

"Your Majesty, what are you thinking? Mixing with a human—have you already betrayed us?" Ophelia looked hurt, seriously suspecting Merlin had lost his mind.

"I haven't betrayed the demon race. It's just that this woman is special to me; I can't let others hurt her." Merlin said seriously, trying to make Ophelia understand.

"... Alice's face flushed red, her heart pounding from Merlin's words... It sounded like a husband protecting his wife, didn't it?

Just now Merlin had thought a lot—still, standing on Alice's side was the more reliable choice. He had already left the Demon Lord Palace; it would be strange if he couldn't cut ties with the past.

Bound by enormous debt, Merlin felt he'd have to stay with Alice for a long time. As for the Demon Lord Palace... that was all in the past.

Future or past—which to choose? Merlin would obviously look forward. How could he be nostalgic for his past as Demon Lord? That would be throwing away a watermelon to pick up a sesame seed.

Alice might accompany him for a long time in the future, while Ophelia was someone who had owed him kindness in the past, but not someone who'd always be by his side.

Besides, Merlin didn't like Ophelia. He truly couldn't do the thing of bullying Alice together with Ophelia.

Though Merlin said nothing, he had actually favored Alice a bit—comparing the two, he leaned more toward Alice.

"Your Majesty, you've..." Ophelia looked disappointed. Seeing Merlin so openly protecting Alice, jealousy burned fiercely in her heart. She strode forward aggressively, wanting to kill Alice first. "Your Majesty, you've gone abnormal. I don't know what this human bitch drugged you with, but you've abandoned the底线 of being a demon. Please step aside. For the future of the Demon Lord Palace, this woman must die!"

Seeing Ophelia charge over, Merlin got annoyed. Looks like he really wasn't the Demon Lord anymore—he couldn't even control people.

"Ophelia, step back!" Merlin said.

Ophelia's anger was instantly suppressed by Merlin's majesty. Though he had left the Demon Lord Palace, the lingering prestige of an arrogant monarch remained.

Merlin's tone was extremely serious, as if scolding Ophelia, making her too angry to dare act rashly.

Seeing Merlin so serious, Ophelia dared not lay hands on Alice anymore, held back everywhere.

"Your Maje... You!"

Ophelia hadn't finished speaking when the teleportation magic circle on the other side began to spin, black smoke gathering like a whale sucking water.

This was a sign that the summoning time had arrived. Ophelia had to return to the Demon Lord Palace through the magic circle and couldn't stay any longer.

Ophelia showed a regretful expression, knowing it was time to leave, but her heart was still very unwilling.

She retracted her spider legs, returning to her original elegant and gentle demeanor, pinching her maid skirt and bowing to Merlin.

"Your Majesty, my time is up, I must return. Please take care of your health. If possible, I hope you can return too."

"As for you secretly marrying a human and protecting this bitch, I will report to Princess Lilith..."

Ophelia felt she couldn't say more to Merlin, but Lilith, as his sister, was different—she had full reason to interfere.

Given Lilith's personality, upon learning Merlin had secretly married, she would surely explode on the spot! She would definitely fight to the death with this human woman.

After all, Lilith liked Merlin very much as her older brother, even planning to marry him later. Having her fruit stolen by someone else—how could she bear that?

Dropping this sentence had clear warning意味—she couldn't handle it, but Merlin's sister could.

Merlin jumped in fright upon hearing this. It was already a misunderstanding; if it spread to his sister by word of mouth, what then?!

She might come killing without regard for anything to cause chaos. Dealing with Lilith every day would be enough to make him suffer!

"Ophelia, don't do this! You're mistaken! We—"

Ophelia didn't listen to Merlin's explanation at all. Before he finished speaking, she turned into a wisp of black smoke, sucked into the magic circle and disappeared, returning directly to the Demon Lord Palace.

Merlin's expression was astonished, his whole body stiff like he'd been hit by a petrification spell, feeling something big was wrong!

It's over! After Ophelia returns, she'll definitely add fuel to the fire.届时Lilith won't be able to contain herself, jumping in place?!

Moreover, Ophelia had seen his adventurer's badge and already knew he was in Lexham. Now even his hiding place would be exposed!

What to do now? The trouble ahead would probably keep him sleepless all night!

No! I don't want to see Lilith! I'm an adult now! I don't need a little tail following me every day!

Merlin's heart ached terribly. Today's events might cause big trouble—the fuse of the powder keg had already been lit.

"Merlin, what's wrong?" Alice saw Merlin's state was weird.

"My sister will find out about this." Merlin turned to look at Alice, face ashen.

"So what? We're not really married either." Alice found Merlin's loss inexplicable.

"The problem is my sister won't believe it, and even Ophelia would twist the truth." Merlin said meaningfully.

"So what? A straight body fears no shadow. What's there to fear? Your sister's strength... I can take on 10 of her." Alice was full of confidence. She wasn't the filler Hero anymore. Even if they were really married, so what? What could Lilith do? Just stare blankly?

"She might leave the Demon Lord Palace without regard for anything to come find me. Then my sister wouldn't just bother me—she'd abuse you daily, always plotting to poison you. Is that okay?" Merlin listed the potential misfortunes, given his sister's crazy personality, she seemed capable of anything.

"Er... Alice's face instantly darkened, hearing Merlin's words and immediately feeling the severity of the situation.

If there was someone at home who opposed her every day...

That would really be unlucky!

What to do? Seems like he'd provoked trouble he shouldn't have.

title: Chapter 55 — Interrogating the Mercenary
content:
Chapter 55 — Interrogating the Mercenary

Volume 15 · Chapter 55

Merlin tied up the knocked-out mercenaries, preparing to interrogate them to see if he could get any information.

"Don't go overboard, just scare them a bit." Alice reminded him from the side, recalling how Merlin had tortured Baron Barton to a pulp, worrying he wouldn't know his own strength.

"Don't worry, I don't need to torture them. When I came, I tortured them to tears. Seeing my face, they might tremble and foam at the mouth." Merlin smiled meaningfully.

Earlier, Merlin had stormed into the mercenaries' stronghold, asking everyone he saw where Alice was, and she was actually next door.

Surely these mercenaries should know his methods and wouldn't dare try to bluff their way through with smooth talk.

Merlin fetched a basin of cold water and ruthlessly splashed it on their faces, jolting the unconscious awake.

The mercenaries all shivered, looking around dazedly. Seeing Merlin's evil grin, they instantly turned ashen, showing terror.

"We don't know where Alice is!"

"Really, we don't know, let us go!"

"Don't hit us! If we knew, we'd definitely tell you!"

It seems these mercenaries lack any sense; after being beaten by Merlin, they've become extremely honest and obedient, ready to spill any secret to save their lives.

Seeing the mercenaries in this state, Merlin nodded satisfied and said with a smile, "Earlier I misunderstood; you really don't know where the person I'm looking for is. Actually, they're just next door—I didn't even notice, haha."

The newly awakened mercenaries showed complex expressions, thinking that this beating was for nothing, and the blond man before them was utterly unreasonable.

"We have some questions we want to ask; you better answer honestly, or else...."

Alice cooperated with Merlin, putting on a fierce look, intending to use force to make these mercenaries submit.

She didn't finish her sentence; instead, she expressed her meaning through action, which is more persuasive than words.

Alice flicked her fingers twice, and suddenly a dozen golden ice swords condensed beside her, swoosh swoosh swoosh, all nailed into the floor in front of the mercenaries' crotches. Move forward just a little more, and these poor fellows' manhood would be gone!

The mercenaries were terrified to the point of their livers and guts bursting; their little brothers trembled violently, feeling the chill emanating from the golden ice swords.

"Hmph! If you don't cooperate actively, you don't need me to spell out the consequences. Your attitude determines your fate." Alice struck a cold, imposing pose, full of dignity.

The mercenaries dared not breathe, nodding like chickens pecking grain, appearing very obedient. For the sake of their manhood, they had completely submitted.

Merlin said nothing, but black lines streamed down his forehead like a waterfall. He thought, "Didn't I say not to go overboard? Isn't Alice being even more excessive? Using someone's manhood as leverage is cruel—I could never do something like that."

"Cough! That..."

"You must have seen that woman is not easy to provoke; don't try to deceive us."

"Think about it—my beating you compared to her, isn't it actually quite merciful?"

On the other side, Alice frowned, her expression unpleasant, thinking, "Merlin merciful? Pfft! I'm just cooperating with his carrot-and-stick approach; I wouldn't really go berserk and attack someone's manhood!"

Without any communication between them, they naturally formed a good-cop/bad-cop act to make these people confess; otherwise, their manhood wouldn't be safe.

The mercenaries basically dared not speak, looking at Merlin and thinking, "This guy's ruthless—he doesn't just break fingers or ribs; cutting off manhood isn't much better! Are they demons?!"

"Your leader is seriously injured and has fled, abandoning you lot here with no care whatsoever—no loyalty at all." Merlin said in a strange tone, as if sympathizing with them.

Sure enough, as soon as Merlin said that, the mercenaries became even more panicked, their hearts wavering, losing their backbone.

"Now I give you a chance to live—do you know where your leader fled to?" Merlin probed, his eyes flickering, watching each person's gaze.

The atmosphere fell silent; they seemed hesitant, but after a few breaths, the first defector appeared.

"I don't know!"

"Tsk! Are you looking for death? What are you yelling about?" Merlin glared menacingly, gripping his sword hilt as a warning.

"But I heard that your leader seems to have been exchanging letters with Countess Camilla; they seem to be friends. If he fled, he's likely seeking her protection." A thin-built mercenary shouted, spilling everything he knew to save his life—quite the savvy one.

"Oh? Really?" Merlin stroked his chin, feeling the situation getting complicated. This information involves the Countess of Avignon; one is a high-ranking noble, the other a mercenary living in a basement—what connection could there be between such disparate identities?

Even Alice wondered inwardly, "Isn't Countess Camilla a benevolent lord who takes in refugees? How could she be linked to an evil mercenary leader? This seems utterly unfathomable."

However, the mercenary said, "Dickent Ping is very likely to seek the Countess's protection; if true, then the collusion between a lord and bandits is confirmed."

After the first mercenary defected, several others quickly followed, eagerly answering Merlin's questions—

"Yeah! We've seen the leader exchange letters with Countess Camilla more than once; I even thought our mercenary group had quite a background, actually having a lord's backing!"

"Me too; that night I helped deliver the letters—the guards all looked gloomy, like sickly individuals."

"Our leader couldn't possibly leave the city; all his business is in Avignon, so he must have gone to seek help there."

Merlin nodded; with so many saying so, it seems Dickent Ping and Countess Camilla indeed have a close relationship.

He turned his head to look at Alice behind him, raised his eyebrows, asking, "How about it? Any progress?"

Seeing Merlin's gesture, Alice nodded satisfactorily, hoping to continue questioning; although these mercenaries are small fry, the information they provide is still valuable.

"So, you kidnapped all these young women—what exactly are you planning to do with them?" Merlin inquired.

"Obviously to sell them, of course! A young virgin is worth 200,000 gold!" a mercenary hastily replied.

Merlin narrowed his eyes, thinking, "That valuable? Impressive—Alice is still a treasure."

"Sell to whom? Are you the ones purchasing the kidnapped young women? What do you need so many young women for?"

"We don't know either; each delivery is shrouded in mystery, we never see what the buyer looks like, but they're a regular customer of our mercenary band. The women we capture are sold there; as for what they're used for... I guess big shots probably enjoy youthful, vigorous flesh..." a mercenary speculated, apparently still unclear on this point.

Upon hearing that, Alice's eyes widened, as if she suddenly recalled something important, almost forgetting—

When we came, weren't we listening to them...

Just now we brought back a little girl—are we supposed to sell her together with Liangji?

(-"-)

title: Chapter 56 — Mysterious Little Girl
content:
Chapter 56 — Mysterious Little Girl

Volume 15 · Chapter 56

Beneath the mercenary group's headquarters, below the underground hall, there was actually another level.

It was a prison dedicated to holding people, where nearly all the kidnapped women were kept, waiting to be sold off.

But now, Merlin and Alice had arrived in the pitch-black dungeon with torches in hand, slowly advancing with the faint flicker of flame as they searched for something.

Just a moment ago, Alice had suddenly remembered the initial conversations among the mercenaries. They said another young girl had been kidnapped, and the day after tomorrow she was supposed to be sold together with Alice to an old customer.

Now that the leader Dickton had fled into hiding, the entire mercenary group was falling apart and facing the danger of dissolution, so that kidnapped young girl should also be freed.

So Alice had decided to take that young girl away — she absolutely couldn't stay in such a dangerous place; she might end up coming to harm.

Alice had assumed there would be many kidnapped women in the dungeon, but after searching for quite a while, she couldn't see a single soul — it looked more like an empty dungeon.

This situation made Alice's heart tighten. She wondered if they had already been moved away in advance. I hope not, she thought. She's just a young girl; how pitiful to be sold back and forth!

Merlin followed close behind Alice, looking around, but the empty dungeon only deepened his suspicion. "Alice, are you sure you didn't mishear? Where's this young girl? I can't even see a shadow."

"I didn't mishear," Alice shot back at Merlin. "They definitely kidnapped a young girl to be sold together with me. That's what the mercenary leader himself said — how could it be false?" She thought that they'd only been looking for a little while and the guy was already getting impatient. He really had no patience.

"Where is anyone? This whole area is as empty as an abandoned factory, and I don't sense any sign of living creatures. Not a trace." Merlin answered with certainty, clearly not keen on wasting time.

"Have a little patience. This dungeon is so huge — how could we possibly find everything just by chance?" Alice pressed.

"Is anybody there? If someone's there, make a sound!" Merlin called out loudly, and his voice echoed throughout the dark dungeon. Even the reverberation showed just how vast and empty it was.

"Tch! If you find it troublesome, go ahead and climb back up yourself. I'll search on my own." Alice shot Merlin a side-eye, complaining in a way that soured her own mood.

"Don't get so worked up. I was just joking, did you actually take it seriously?" Merlin shrugged.

"Pfft!" Alice pursed her lips and looked at the dungeon before her, unable to help but remark, "By the way, this dungeon is really huge. What was this place used for before?"

"Old man Aralon told me that this used to be the count's mansion, but it fell into disuse after they moved away," Merlin answered idly, resting his arms behind his head.

"That's strange. Why would a count's residence have such a large dungeon underground? Who was it meant to hold?" Alice couldn't help but wonder. It was hard to understand — generally, noble mansions were for living in. Building such a massive dungeon was baffling.

"I don't know, but judging by the scale, it could easily hold a thousand people," Merlin observed around them.

Alice furrowed her brows, a string of questions rising in her mind, especially regarding the enormous size of this dungeon.

This should have been the residence of the local countess. There was no doubt that the construction of this dungeon was connected to her.

A bright and virtuous ruler on the surface, yet it seemed she had many unspeakable secrets.

If she were a decent person, why would she need such a vast dungeon? Who was it meant to hold?

Combining the clues from the mercenaries, this female ruler appeared to have a very close connection with the mercenary leader.

It was hard not to speculate — were these rows and rows of cells meant to imprison missing women?!

Why imprison so many people? Could it be that...

Alice's chain of conjectures startled herself. She felt there was a possibility, but lacking evidence, she kept it to herself and didn't tell Merlin.

"Merlin, what do you think about the clues the mercenaries provided earlier?"

"About that..."

Merlin stroked his chin and, after thinking for a moment, said, "Countess Camilla of Avignon is suspicious. We need to investigate. The correspondence between her and the leader of the kidnapping ring just doesn't add up. A kind and wise ruler would avoid contact with evil forces."

"That's true, but we seem to lack the authority to investigate nobles. Besides, she's the ruler of all Avignon and is deeply beloved. If we provoke her, it doesn't seem like a good idea, does it?" Alice was somewhat worried. They were only adventurers; they didn't have much power anyway.

"Alice, your flaw is that you're too rigid. You always like following rules. If we don't have the authority to investigate, won't we just do it secretly? Infiltrate the countess's mansion, turn everything upside down, and see what secrets she's hiding." Merlin said bluntly, cutting through the Gordian knot. Straight to the point.

"...Isn't that a crime?" A drop of cold sweat ran down Alice's forehead.

"You can wait outside if you want. It's fine if you don't join in." Merlin said indifferently.

"Huh?" Alice felt that Merlin was looking down on her and quickly said, "Don't underestimate people! I never said I wouldn't go!" Merlin shrugged, acting completely nonchalant, which only increased Alice's dissatisfaction.

Both of them had nearly reached the end of the dungeon, yet still found nothing. They were preparing to go back up and find a mercenary to question further.

But just as they were about to leave, Alice sensed a faint sobbing sound from the most remote corner of the dungeon.

"Merlin, wait. I think someone's over there." Alice pointed toward a direction, holding her torch.

"That's probably an illusion. I don't sense any living human presence," Merlin frowned, puzzled.

"Come with me quickly. I really heard a sound." Alice waved her hand, summoning Merlin to follow.

The two of them pushed through some obstacles and arrived at that very remote cell. They smashed open the door lock and walked straight in.

Alice raised her torch and slowly searched deeper inside. Sure enough, she found a young girl curled up in the corner.

She had glossy black hair, was filthy all over, and wore a tattered little dress. She looked about three or four years old, quite petite.

The little girl had her head buried in her knees, shivering and sobbing. Her chubby little hands tightly hugged her legs, as if she lacked a sense of security entirely, and only in this posture could she barely endure.

Merlin paused, genuinely surprised. So there really was someone here? But why can't I sense any living aura from this girl? She feels lifeless. Could it be because she's so young that her presence is too faint?

Alice saw the pitiful appearance of the little girl and was immediately consumed with rage, cursing silently at the cruel mercenaries outside. She wanted to kill them all to vent her fury!

The young girl seemed lost in her own world and hadn't noticed Alice and Merlin's arrival at all.

Alice composed herself, squatted down, and approached using a gentle, big-sister tone.

"Little sister, we've come to rescue you. Let's leave with us first. We'll take you to a safe place, okay?"

The little girl didn't react at all. Alice had no choice but to try touching her. The moment she made contact with the girl's skin, she felt an overwhelming chill!

The little girl's small body shuddered and shrank back slightly, then cautiously lifted her face and peeked at Alice.

Her face was streaked with tears, her eyes somewhat red and swollen. Although her head of black hair covered half her face, her chubby cheeks were still quite cute.

The little girl looked at Alice with an expressionless face at first, then her eyes lit up with delight. She gave a pure, innocent smile and immediately threw herself into Alice's embrace.

"Mama!"

"Huh?! " Alice froze completely. Looking at the little girl who had thrown herself into her arms, she suddenly turned pale. "Eh?! "

Merlin raised an eyebrow slightly and, enjoying the show, said, "Impressive, Alice. Congratulations. You're a mom now."

"It's not — this — ah!" Alice's face flushed red. Her heart was in such disarray that she couldn't explain coherently, so she just turned around and yelled at Merlin.

"You bastard, don't talk nonsense!"

"Quick, come help out! Stop just standing there like an idiot!"

"Seriously, what in the world is going on?!"

"I haven't even gotten married! Where would I get a kid from?!" ⊥!

title: Chapter 1 — The Blood-Bathed Countess
content:
Chapter 1 — The Blood-Bathed Countess

Volume 16 · Chapter 1

Avignon, the estate of Countess Camilla.
A splendid castle was built here, covering a vast area.
Situated on high ground of the whole region, from the watchtower one can overlook the entire main city.
High walls were erected around it, appearing especially oppressive, giving the feeling of a ruler looking down on mortals.
The estate is far from the bustling downtown of the main city, utterly silent, eerily quiet in the night.
This castle is clearly isolated from the outside world, forming a city within a city, completely two different worlds.
Within the castle grounds, many plants have been planted, forming a lush garden that looks refined.
However, at this moment, a scene of pursuit and hunt is unfolding in the manor—
Large numbers of bats hang upside down from tree trunks, their membranous wings wrapped around themselves as they rest, scarlet eyes fixed on the fleeing girl below.
The girl looks panicked, her eyes filled with fear, barefoot, wearing a pure white dress.
On her leg are wounds torn by thorns, slowly oozing blood.
She pays no heed to her injuries, as if something even more terrifying is chasing her, constantly looking back while she runs.
She seems to want to escape this castle, but the dense thickets block her steps.
A branch trips the girl, causing her to fall to the ground, scraping her knee and blood pours out.
She winces in pain, already unable to move, yet still looks back in terror—
A cold moonlight filters through the layers of leaves and shines down.
A near-human monster slowly emerges from the shadows, revealing sharp fangs, smiling at the girl.
She is covered in black fur, her nails gleam with cold light, in the darkness resembling a huge black cat! ?
“Run? Why aren't you running anymore? You like this, I'm quite bored.”
“The girl, terrified, looks at the monster, her lips moving as she says, ‘Lady Camilla, please spare me, I still have family.’”
This seemingly cat-like humanoid monster is actually the lord of Avignon, Countess Camilla herself! ?
Seeing her thirsty, bloodthirsty appearance, it is clearly the vampire that Merlin and Alice have been searching for everywhere.
“You have seen my true form; letting you go would cause great trouble, and I am already hungry, so just let me drain you dry. After all, I am also your lifesaver—if I hadn't ordered the admission of this group of refugees, you might have starved to death already, right?”
Camilla said leisurely, this beloved and supported enlightened female leader is indeed not simple, far from the kind and benevolent image on the surface.
Everything is to satisfy her own desires, prioritizing refugee families with young daughters to enter first—doesn't that make it easier for the blood clan to hunt food?
In fact, the whole of Avignon has become an enticing trap, continuously drawing in homeless refugees; the young women who enter the main city are especially doomed to never escape!
Camilla had long planned how to lure pure young women, crafting her own radiant and great image, while also hunting more food to fill her underground dungeons.
But such deeds certainly cannot be done by Camilla herself or her people, as it would easily expose her and ruin her persona; the dirty work needs others to do.
At this moment, the greedy Dickteping walked into Camilla's sight, becoming the best pawn to use, and they established a very subtle cooperative relationship.
Dickteping is responsible for kidnapping pure women from Avignon and delivering them to Camilla for a large reward; this transaction has lasted a long time and remains stable.
Camilla is the old customer Dickteping speaks of, already his greatest protection, allowing him to thrive in Avignon thanks to the lord's patronage.
“For the lord's benevolence, I am deeply grateful; as for you being a monster, I swear I will not tell anyone!” The girl kneels on the ground, pleading desperately.
“Sorry, only the dead can keep secrets.”
Camilla moves as swift as a ghost, - - leaps up and pounces on the girl, mouth - - splits to reveal ghastly fangs, mercilessly piercing her slender neck, biting through her entire neck.
The girl stares wide-eyed, feeling no strength in her whole body, blood surges wildly toward her neck, sucked completely dry!
The power disparity is huge; the girl cannot resist Camilla, her limbs flail desperately, her skin quickly shrivels, the plump young skin instantly becomes withered and wrinkled.
Finally, the girl's eyes turn hollow, her body goes limp and collapses in Camilla's arms, having expended all her vitality.
Camilla throws the girl's corpse to the ground, her mouth still stained with the fresh blood she just sucked, showing a satisfied expression, as if she is full.
At this moment, a servant-like man with a pale face approaches, holding a tray with a napkin, seemingly one of Camilla's subordinates—
“Countess—”
“I have just finished eating; do not disturb me casually, have you forgotten the rules?” Camilla shows displeasure, her black fur recedes, turning into— a lady in an elegant long dress.
“My lady, Dickteping came late at night, saying he has urgent business and wishes to see you.” The subordinate says softly.
“What does he want?” Camilla picks up the napkin, wipes the blood from her lips.
“I don't know.” The subordinate replies.
Camilla thinks for a moment, throws the napkin into the tray, and says indifferently, ‘Let him keep waiting; he's just a human pawn, no need to worry too much.’
“Yes.” The subordinate bows slightly in response.
“Recently you go to the dungeon and select a hundred pure women, secretly send them to the capital, and personally hand them over to Chancellor Madess.” Camilla suddenly issues this command.
“Why? Those are the ones we painstakingly collected.” The subordinate does not understand.
“For the prosperity of the blood clan, what is this sacrifice? Madess is an ancient bloodline that once served our father, called the First Clan; after our father fell into eternal slumber, he has never been idle, trying various methods to awaken him.” Camilla says lightly.
“Could it be… Father?” The subordinate widens his eyes, seeming to have realized something; “Father” refers to Dracula, the oldest vampire on this land!
Because vampires can create their own kin as subordinates, with strict hierarchy, Dracula is thus called Father by the French bloodlines.
And Madess, personally created by Dracula, is the foremost kin, of extremely noble stature, above all others.
“You are right; Madess's efforts have not been in vain. The father lying in the coffin, long asleep, is about to awaken and rule this land again; the plan has now reached its final stage.” Camilla pauses, lifts her head to gaze at the full moon, her red lips part slightly—
“For thousands of years, our clan has hidden in darkness, barely surviving; those days are about to end.”
“What awaits us is endless frenzy bathed in blood”—

title: Chapter 2 — Midnight Lament
content:
Chapter 2 — Midnight Lament

Volume 16 · Chapter 2

The subordinate looked up, unable to hold back his question. "But Father died alongside a vampire hunter thousands of years ago, didn't he?"

"Do not forget, we are the most powerful of the blood races in terms of resurrection ability—vampires of the First Generation. We can essentially fear silverware not at all; at most, we are merely restricted. Our true natural enemy is sunlight. Even First Generation vampires exposed to sunlight can only meet one fate: total annihilation." Camilla turned her head and showed a faint smile. "Our father is one of the Three Great First Generations. How could he possibly be killed so easily by a vampire hunter?"

"Is that so? Father didn't actually die, but instead entered a long slumber?" The subordinate lowered his head and muttered to himself.

"In fact, thousands of years ago, that vampire hunter with werewolf bloodline was indeed no easy opponent. On the night of the full moon, he transformed into a werewolf, and his power was no small matter, dealing irreversible重创 to our father and forcing him into a long slumber to recuperate." Camilla paused, then continued with a smile. "As for that vampire hunter? He suffered miserably. Not only was he killed by Father, but his bloodline was also cursed. Isn't it true that werewolves have now vanished from existence?"

"Werewolf bloodline? Is it the kind of monster that can rival the vampire race in legend?" the subordinate asked curiously.

"Yes, werewolves can indeed rival the vampire race, but their numbers are pitifully scarce." Cam tilised her head and gazed at the cold moonlight in the sky. "In the ancient Era of Gods, there was a group of rebellious humans who served Fenrir, the Giant Wolf that devours heaven and earth. They sacrificed countless infants to Fenrir and thereby obtained divine power—in other words, werewolf bloodline. Every night of the full moon, they would transform into two-legged wolves, possessing immense strength, ruthlessly slaughtering every living creature before them. But these are all legends. After the gods fell, the wolf-blooded tribe that served Fenrir had long disappeared from history. They are probably already extinct. That vampire hunter who severely wounded Father was likely the very last werewolf."

"I see. But after Father awakens, will he be able to recover to his peak strength from back then?" The subordinate looked at her with a doubtful expression. Since Dracula had slept for thousands of years, causing the vampire race to hide and survive in darkness, he must have suffered extremely severe injuries to end up like this.

"Of course. Lord Methuselah had long prepared everything. How could he not have considered this aspect?" Cam ila slowly turned around and said softly, "Our vampire race can drink blood to strengthen ourselves. The degree of strengthening depends on the prey's species. The higher the species, the stronger the power we gain after drinking their blood. Recently I heard that Lord Methuselah acquired a female demon from somewhere. The demon race has the best compatibility with us, and they belong to high-tier species. When Father awakens, the first thing he will do is drain this female demon dry. At that point, it won't be a matter of simply recovering to full strength—he will possess the power of a demon and become even stronger."

The subordinate's eyes widened. He seemed frightened by Cam ila's words. Dracula was already powerful enough thousands of years ago and had ruled this land for a long time. If he became even stronger, wouldn't the vampire race reach an unprecedented prosperity?!

"Lord Methuselah's plan is nearly complete now, but it still requires many human blood offerings for the ritual. What we give today will be returned to us multiplied times over in the future." Cam ila said coldly. "Compared to our race ruling this land again, the lives of those one hundred girls are utterly worthless."

At the Count's mansion, in the reception hall.

Dick Top came running in, covered in dust and grime, seeking refuge. He still dared not return to his old stronghold.

He had already guessed that his subordinates, in order to save their own lives, would very likely betray him. After all, he had always been selfish and had no real感情 for his subordinates; it was all mutual exploitation.

If Countess Camila refused to protect Dick Top and decided to sacrifice him to save herself, then he would be truly finished—no career, hunted, exactly like his old days as a pirate living with his head strapped to his belt!

Dick Top's mind was now filled with the thought that the Great Demon Lord Lucifer the Third had set his sights on him, and his life was likely in grave danger.

He had never felt such terror. Merely recalling those rumors about the arrogant monarch made him shudder with fear!

A man who single-handedly defeated countless crusades and pushed the Holy Church, with its vast holdings, back by decades—how could someone like him possibly be dealt with by himself?!

In the underground great hall, he had even thought about counterattacking? Hehe, what nonsense. Things that weren't realistic should just remain fantasies.

Dick Top had arrived quite a while ago, begging the Count to see him, but after waiting a long time, he was the only one pacing back and forth in the reception hall. He couldn't catch a glimpse of Cam ila anywhere.

How humiliating, like a tiger misplaced in the plains being bullied by dogs.

This emotion welled up in Dick Top's heart. In the past, he had delivered young women to the count's mansion every day, and Countess Cam ila's attitude had been nothing short of wonderful.

Now that his stronghold had been destroyed by two adventurers, and he had fallen to the point of having no home to return to, he was met with cold treatment here?

Dick Top had never known that Cam ila was a vampire. He had never thought about it. He had simply noticed that the people living in this castle had excessively pale skin, as if suffering from anemia.

He had assumed that Cam ila, on the surface a lofty lord, was actually a human trafficker secretly engaged in unsavory dealings.

After quite a while, Countess Cam ila finally strolled in leisurely and took her seat at the head.

Seeing Cam ila arrive, Dick Top was过joyful and could barely contain himself from dropping to his knees and crying out "Mom!"

As long as this lord was willing to see him, there was still a chance!

Dick Top quickly lowered his posture, removed his hat, and transformed into an obsequious flatterer.

"Good evening, oh beautiful and breathtaking Cam ila-sama~"

Cam ila wore an elegant black dress and sat in her chair, inquiring in a flat tone, "I wonder what has brought Mr. Dick Top to my residence at such a late hour?"

"Terrible things have happened! My mercenary company was destroyed!" Dick Top showed a bitter expression, his heart full of grievances with nowhere to vent them.

"Oh? I never gave any order for such a thing to happen. Haven't your guards always turned a blind eye to your operations?" Cam ila frowned slightly. She still needed to use Dick Top to kidnap young women. If he had problems, it would not be good for her or for Dracula's awakening plan.

"It wasn't the guards. It was two adventurers from Britain!" Dick Top quickly explained.

"Two outsiders? Haven't I told you to keep a low profile? Were you not targeted because of your own carelessness?" Cam ila frowned, her mood far from pleasant.

"It's not like that! Those two adventurers came specifically for me! They disguised themselves as prey and infiltrated my territory, throwing my stronghold into complete chaos!" Dick Top said with agitated emotions.

"Came specifically for you?"

Confusion rose within Cam ila. A premeditated action—what was the other party thinking? Why make things difficult for a mercenary company? Were they just meddling in matters that didn't concern them?

Still, Dick Top was somewhat capable among humans. A large mercenary company destroyed by just two adventurers—what a worthless fellow!

Cam ila looked at Dick Top coldly, wanting to kill him on the spot, but also feeling that he still had some use to her.

"Those two adventurers are very powerful? They reduced you to this state, coming crying in the middle of the night to pour out your woes."

"Powerful! Very powerful! Of course, the blond man in there was even more outrageous!" Dick Top nervously swallowed, saying fearfully, "He is the Great Demon Lord from the Dead Swamp."

title: Chapter 3 — Shift Target
content:
Chapter 3 — Shift Target

Volume 16 · Chapter 3

What? That young Demon Lord who lives deep in the Death Swamp and has repeatedly repelled the Holy Church's crusades, Lucifer III?
Camilla jumped up from her chair with a start, her expression extremely shocked, a hint of wariness flashing in her eyes.
This female countess obviously knows something about this legendary great demon, although it's just hearsay, but it still feels frightening.
I've heard that although this young ruler now possesses extraordinary strength, he used to be a useless good-for-nothing who only played around every day, lacking ambition.
A hundred years ago, a certain legendary Hero successfully slew Lucifer II, dealing a heavy blow to the First Demon Lord Palace, nearly wiping out the demons.
Fortunately, at the critical moment, other Demon Lords came to assist, barely managing to defend the First Demon Lord Palace, and this young ruler also vanished without a trace.
He reappeared a hundred years later; after returning from training, this young ruler underwent a complete transformation, becoming like a different person, decisive in battle and retaking control of the First Demon Lord Palace.
The Holy Church thought this newly appointed young ruler was unsteady on his feet and saw it as a good opportunity to topple the Demon Lord Palace, thus sending countless strong ones to subjugate him.
As a result, within three years Heroes died one after another, countless strong ones fell, being beheaded by this young ruler and suffering a crushing defeat at the First Demon Lord Palace, with hardly anyone returning alive!
Three years of consecutive defeats left the Holy Church in an embarrassing situation with no usable forces, its strength regressed by ten years, and in the short term it no longer had the capacity to launch a large-scale crusade.
By sheer force of will, he single-handedly made the mighty Holy Church submit? Such a formidable Demon Lord looming right under one's nose—how could one feel at ease? Not being afraid would be abnormal.
"Exactly! That's the legendary harbinger of death! With a wave of his hand he slaughtered a hundred thousand Holy Church knights!" Dicteping answered affirmatively.
"Listen
Camilla's first reaction was to avoid conflict and hide, but then she thought that if the other party came looking for trouble, hiding would be useless!
Moreover, now is the critical juncture when Dracula is about to awaken; we cannot cause a big problem, otherwise we would be sinners of the blood clan.
"A strong dragon does not overwhelm the local snake; this is my turf, so I might not necessarily lose to this young Demon Lord."
"I will try to avoid direct confrontation with this Demon Lord; it seems there is still a chance to survive by maneuvering."
"You say this young Demon Lord is an adventurer? As the lord of the demon race, how could he come to human territory and still be an insignificant adventurer?"
"He's still a bronze-rank adventurer," Dicteping added.
"What? To intimidate a demon race overlord and become the lowest-rank adventurer?" Camilla felt it was fake, such a thing couldn't possibly happen—maybe something went wrong somewhere.
"Absolutely certain—I used a scroll to summon the great demon of the First Demon Lord Palace, and that great demon actually addressed him as 'Your Majesty.' Besides Lucifer III, who else could be called that by a great demon?" Dicteping recalled the previous events and felt summoning the demon was a mistake.
"Tsk!" Camilla clicked her tongue in annoyance, showing an irritated expression, and said with a headache, "It's really nauseating—why have there been so many troubles lately? A few days ago a demon ran into Avignon and badly wounded the Inquisition interrogator; fortunately I left afterward, and now another of the Seven Demon Kings has appeared?! This is human territory! How can we live in peace? Could it be because the Holy Church is recovering its strength, and these demons are now recklessly scheming against humans?"
"It's possible; the Holy Church's weaklings, after being beaten by demons and losing their spirit, aren't they just emboldening the demon race's arrogance?" Dicteping agreed.
Camilla actually didn't care at all about the lives and deaths of the Avignon people; these words were just her putting on a human facade, saying them for Dicteping to hear.
"So what if demons appear? I'm just afraid that at this critical juncture, a powerful enemy will oppose me!"
"The ritual to awaken Dracula requires a large amount of human blood; the refugees I've taken in are mainly kidnapped and sent to Chancellor Mades."
If Lucifer III opposes me, it will definitely affect the progress of the plan to awaken Dracula.
"Your business being sabotaged is a troublesome matter; since the other party is one of the Seven Demon Kings, they're absolutely not someone to provoke lightly. I think we should avoid conflict and let this blow over—please stay here with me for now and don't go out."
"Lady Camilla, this can't just be forgotten! That's my lifeblood! Moreover, the other party is clearly here to investigate the kidnapping; I feel they'll surely find you sooner or later!" Dicteping was extremely unwilling; his mercenary group had been his life's work for over twenty years, now it's all for naught—if we just let it go, who could bear it?
Camilla furrowed her brows and said helplessly, "What else can we do? Do you have confidence in taking on Lucifer III? Anyway, I have no confidence I could defeat that monster-level guy."
"Dicteping was at a loss, then suddenly recalled those two are a married couple—'Lady Camilla, there is still a way!'"
"Oh? Do tell." Camilla smiled, wanting to hear what wicked idea Dicteping could have.
"Those two are a married couple! Since we can't handle Lucifer III, we can strike at his wife!" Dicteping thought he couldn't beat Merlin, but beating his wife would also work!
"Did Lucifer III find a human wife?" Camilla's expression turned strange.
"Uh, that's right—I personally saw it, and it's a human!" Dicteping nodded repeatedly.
Camilla's brows knotted tightly; according to her knowledge, demons are forbidden from intermarrying with other races, and Lucifer III being a Demon Lord makes it even more impossible for him to marry a human.
"If Dicteping isn't lying, this is hard to comprehend, yet it's an important breakthrough for taking down Lucifer III!"
"Because once a person has ties, that becomes a deadly weakness that can be exploited!"
"Even if we can't beat Lucifer III, it's fine as long as we can beat his wife~"
Camilla burst out laughing, her mood suddenly enlightened, having already thought of a way to deal with Lucifer III.
"Hahaha, I see now—the mighty Demon Lord who shakes the world actually fell in love with a human girl and married her? This is a perfect opportunity!"
That
Dicteping saw Camilla's smile, felt a little nervous, and probed, "What... what opportunity?"
Camilla had already thought of a way to deal with Lucifer III; even if he came looking for trouble, she had confidence to keep the Great Demon Lord forever in Avignon.
Only saw Camilla put away her smile, and with a very serious tone say to Dicteping—
"You're right, we can't beat Lucifer III."
"Then we'll strike hard at his wife—"

title: Chapter 4 — Courtesy Before Force
content:
Chapter 4 — Courtesy Before Force

Volume 16 · Chapter 4

“Have you already decided?!” Dickteping exclaimed, delighted, as long as Camilla is willing to help, after all she is the lord of Avignon, and only she has the ability to contend with Lucifer III, this outsider.

“In terms of strength, I am indeed no match for Lucifer III, and I have no confidence in defeating him.” Camilla paused, then continued, “But the great Demon Lord falling in love with a human girl changes things; excess emotion is a weakness that can be exploited. If we control that girl, would this young Demon Lord still dare act rashly?”

“Exactly! Lady Camilla, you're absolutely right! That's exactly what I thought!!” Dickteping was overjoyed, besides being excited, he volunteered, saying, “Now what should we do? Should I go kidnap Lucifer III's wife?”

“This matter is dangerous; if mishandled, it could easily backfire, so just leave it all to me to handle—I'll get our business back up and running.” Camilla slowly rose and approached Dickteping.

“Then I'll trouble you.” Dickteping, upon hearing Camilla would take charge, had no complaints; he was eager to find someone to help him get revenge.

“Your injuries are not light; just stay and recuperate in my manor for now.” Camilla patted Dickteping's shoulder, saying lightly, “It's getting late; go on, my servants will arrange everything for you.”

“Yes.” Dickteping nodded and followed the deathly pale maid out of the reception hall.

Just as Dickteping had just left, Camilla's subordinate couldn't sit still, stepped forward and objected, “My lord, this probably isn't appropriate.”

“Huh?” Camilla turned to look at her subordinate.

“That's the arrogant monarch of legend; with our strength it's hard to oppose him, provoking such a being would likely end in a disastrous defeat like striking a stone with an egg.” The subordinate said very sincerely.

“I understand your concern, but they are here to investigate the strange disappearances, and we've already been targeted; I doubt those two will give up easily.” Camilla paused, then added, “Now is a critical period; the awakening of our father's ritual requires a large amount of human blood, and we are the main supplier of sacrifices. Whether we fight or avoid, as long as Lucifer III remains in Avignon, we will be hesitant and restrained, affecting the revival of our entire clan, possibly even causing a stall.”

“The subordinate was at a loss for words, thinking that indeed, whether it's a brave confrontation or a cowardly hiding, neither is easy to handle.”

“Avignon, because of Lucifer III's presence, still came regarding the missing persons issue; this made the vampire clan suddenly dare not act rashly, and they dare not go out to seize people for sacrifices at this time.”

“However, during the critical period of Dracula's awakening, delay equals slow death; both confrontation and avoidance risk facing Lucifer III's wrath upon our doorstep.”

“But now we know Lucifer III has a lover—this is his deadliest weakness. As long as we subdue the Demon Lord's beloved, won't this young ruler obediently comply?” Camilla narrowed her eyes; her expression was no longer as tense as before.

“But Lucifer III is said to be a feelingless killing machine; can controlling his wife really indirectly control him?” The subordinate still harbored doubts.

“It depends on how deep Lucifer III's love for his wife is, but I think a great Demon Lord marrying a human across species is likely true love. As far as I know, demons forbid interracial marriage, let alone a high-ranking monarch; Lucifer III's marriage to a human entails pressures only he himself knows.”

“Camilla wore a half-smile, already convinced that capturing Lucifer III's wife would likely allow her to control that dread-inducing great Demon Lord; then she could indirectly command the demon monarch to do her bidding—how satisfying!”

“I see, but isn't the risk of provoking Lucifer III too high?” The subordinate's attitude remained cautious.

“They've already come killing at our door; we're completely on the defensive. For our father to return to this land, even if there's risk, we can only try.” Camilla's tone was firm and unquestionable.

“Then what should we do? Should we just go straight to their door and abduct Lucifer III's wife? They should still be in Avignon; their lodging isn't hard to find.” The subordinate said seriously.

“No, tearing faces apart is a last resort; we'll observe propriety before force—invite Lucifer III and his wife to dinner, see if we can peacefully persuade them to leave.” Camilla thought, then continued, “After all, their status is that of adventurers, a bunch of people just in it for money; we can test them—if they insist on opposing us to the end, then we'll have no choice but to fight to the death.”

“Yes, Lady Camilla's idea is still fairly reasonable; if they refuse to reconcile, we'll have to resort to arms.” The subordinate nodded, seeming to understand Camilla's thought, still hoping for a peaceful resolution; mutual loss is merely an unfortunate necessity. “What about Dickteping? His mercenary band has disbanded; he's now of no use.”

“Who says he has no use? If the current matter is resolved, we'll still need Dickteping to do our dirty work.” Camilla chuckled, turned, and walked toward the outside of the reception hall.

“This pawn can't be discarded yet.”

“When our father returns to France, everything we've invested in him will make him spit it all out!”

“The next morning.”

“Merlin and Alice brought the little girl back to the inn.”

“The two hadn't returned after being out all night, which made Old Akalon very worried.”

“He had thrown out his back yesterday, leaving him unable to fight on the front lines with Merlin and Alice.”

“Old Akalon had intended to help, but Merlin vanished in a puff of smoke!”

“Left with no choice and unable to find anyone, Old Akalon reluctantly returned to the inn alone, didn't sleep well all night, and suffered from his back pain.”

“It seems Old Akalon is truly old; a twinge in his back saps his fighting spirit, leaving him completely lacking the burning zeal for adventure.”

“After the little girl inexplicably called her 'mom,' Alice was completely bewildered—how could an unmarried woman like her have a child that people would mistake for hers?”

“However, seeing the poor little girl, who had been locked in the mercenaries' dungeon, Alice softened and discussed with Merlin bringing her back.”

“Merlin had no objection either, since that was mercenary territory; leaving a small child there would indeed be dangerous, so he agreed.”

“At this moment, in Alice's room, everyone had gathered here—”

“Alice was gently wiping the dirty little face of the young girl with a warm, damp cloth, hoping to make her look a bit cleaner; otherwise her splotchy face would obscure what she actually looks like.”

“Old Akalon frowned, watching the young girl brought back by Merlin and Alice, his face showing puzzlement, as black lines streaked down his wrinkled forehead.”

“Aren't pregnancies ten months?”

“How did you go out and— at night— just make a baby?”

“I've never heard of such magic before—”

“(u -_.)y?”

title: Chapter 5 — The Mysterious Child
content:
Chapter 5 — The Mysterious Child

Volume 16 · Chapter 5

Old Arkalon was very puzzled, because he had heard the little girl call Alice "Mom" more than once already.

If Alice and Merlin were "couple" then Merlin is the dad?

Creating a child overnight, and one that's 3-4 years old at that—Old Arkalon had never seen anything like it in his half-century of life!

However, Old Arkalon noticed that the little girl only seemed close to Alice, showing little interaction with Merlin and appearing very cold toward him.

This only made Old Arkalon more and more confused, feeling that this suddenly appeared child was very unnatural—at the very least, their relationship was off.

"Eh!" Alice heard Old Arkalon's words and immediately grew embarrassed, hastily explaining, "No! That's not how it is at all! We don't know this child! She was found in the mercenary group's dungeon."

"But..." Old Arkalon frowned slightly, looking at the little girl whom Alice was gradually wiping clean, remaining silent.

"Mom!" The little girl seemed very clingy, pouncing on Alice and refusing to let go.

Since she was too short, she could only hug Alice's ankles, her little face rubbing against them constantly.

Alice had already wiped the little girl's dirty appearance clean; though her black hair looked slightly eerie, her chubby, baby-faced cheeks were undeniably cute.

"No... no no no... that's not true! I'm not your Mom! Don't... don't call me that!" Alice became flustered when the girl clung to her, her embarrassed look making one unable to help but laugh.

Actually, Alice's heart was very helpless—she had been called Mom by a child out of nowhere, and having never married, this careless calling inevitably caused misunderstandings!?

But Alice, with her soft heart, didn't want to adopt a harsh attitude toward a little girl, telling her in a very serious tone that she wasn't her mother!

After all, the little girl looked too young; Alice couldn't bear to hurt her, so she could only force herself to maintain a maternal facade.

As a result, the little girl was now completely clingy to Alice, convinced she was her mother, constantly throwing tantrums to get her way, leaving Alice very helpless!

"See, the child already called Mom—that's not a title you just blurt out casually. A child remembers their parents most clearly." Old Arkalon said very seriously, thinking: Indeed there must be a secret here? Children are innocent and don't lie; if she calls Alice Mom, then maybe she really is...

"She... she's not my child! You old man, stop talking nonsense! She's just a little kid we accidentally rescued—maybe she was kidnapped from her parents by those mercenaries!" Alice's expression turned serious, seemingly not wanting to become a mother by accident, and mentally unprepared as well.

"R-really? A child can mistake her mother? I've never heard of such a thing." Old Arkalon was still skeptical inside.

"Mom, you... you're not going to abandon me again, are you? I'll be good, I won't bully my sister anymore..." The little girl lowered her head, her eyes red and swollen, her eyes seemingly full of tears, her two fingers fiddling back and forth like a child who had done something wrong.

Alice was suddenly stunned, thinking: Abandon me again? What does "again" mean? Was this child abandoned by her parents?

How pitiful, only 3-4 years old and already abandoned—what kind of mother could do such a thing?

Seeing the little girl look so aggrieved on the verge of crying, Alice's heart softened instantly; she no longer wanted to explain anything and could only temporarily cheer her up.

So Alice slowly squatted down, wiped the little girl's tears with her hand, and decided to play the mother role for now.

"Mom was joking, Mom wouldn't abandon you. Don't scare yourself, okay?"

Alice's tone softened, her expression becoming gentle; as she stroked the little girl's head, she really did look like a mother.

From the moment she saw the little girl last night, Alice had been desperately explaining that she wasn't the child's mother!

But the little girl was somewhat weak-willed; whenever Alice explained she wasn't Mom, the girl would cry sadly.

That aggrieved appearance made Alice feel deeply pained—on one hand she was embarrassed to be called Mom by a child, on the other she didn't want to see the child crying sadly.

Alice had been torn about this for a long time, but now she thought she'd temporarily pretend to be the child's mother, then find a way to locate her real parents,

Merlin leaned against the wall, watching Alice interact with the little girl, saying nothing the whole time, remaining silent throughout, thinking: She was just desperately insisting last night that she wasn't married! No kids! How could she crumble to tears so quickly and start playing the mother role? And this kid is so close to Alice, wishing she could stick to her every second of every minute.

"Really?" The little girl looked up, her eyes sparkling like lightning, seeming to doubt Alice's comfort.

"Of course it's true, silly child, how could I lie to you?" Alice stroked the little girl's face and smiled.

The little girl immediately stopped crying and smiled, throwing herself into Alice's arms happily and saying, "Mom is the best."

Alice holding the little girl in her arms gave people the illusion of a real mother, causing quite a bit of surprise.

Old Arkalon frowned, no longer able to figure out the little girl's origins, and couldn't help asking Merlin beside him, "Merlin, what exactly is going on? The child isn't yours, is it?"

"Ah~" Merlin yawned hugely, looking very tired from a busy night, "Of course not. Look, is this little girl close to me? She's only close to Alice, right?"

"Really rescued from the dungeon?" Old Arkalon asked.

"Yeah, pulled out from the dungeon. Saw Alice and called Mom, couldn't stop her." Merlin shrugged, feeling this matter was also helpless. Now there was the mission to investigate vampires on his hands, yet he'd inexplicably gotten a small trouble; if he didn't handle it, it seemed he couldn't proceed either?

And Alice was too soft-hearted; she definitely wouldn't easily abandon this little girl, leaving him completely unsure what to do next.

"Probably kidnapped, forcibly separated from her parents. This child is still so pitiful." Old Arkalon also showed a sympathetic expression, "But for a 3-4 year old to mistake her real mother, that really is strange, isn't it?"

"What's strange about it? The child is so young, memory is limited." Merlin looked at the little girl, speaking in a flat tone—

"Besides, she was kidnapped; she's probably scared stupid."

"Seeing Alice and thinking she's her mom, no big deal."
