title: Chapter 8 — Temporary Care
content:
Chapter 8 — Temporary Care

Volume 16 · Chapter 8

Seeing Alice doting on the little baby so affectionately stirred something deep within Merlin's heart.

He wasn't a man driven by grand ambitions; he simply wanted to break his own heart curse and then retire to live out a quiet life.

The scene before him was exactly what Merlin yearned for, so naturally he felt a pang of longing.

Fortunately, Alice was busy doting on the little girl and didn't notice Merlin's unusual expression.

Old Arcanum glanced at Alice, then at Merlin, thought for a moment, and tentatively asked in a low voice, "Merlin, do you really want a child that badly?"

"No, don't get the wrong idea. I hate bratty kids the most—how could I possibly like them?" Merlin explained awkwardly, not wanting Old Arcanum to jump to conclusions.

"Is that so?" Old Arcanum frowned, and couldn't help but wonder inwardly.

Was the longing in Merlin's eyes just my imagination?

The whole day passed without any sudden incidents, seeming quite peaceful.

Old Arcanum's waist injury hadn't fully healed, and upon learning there would be no operations today, he returned to his room early to rest.

Merlin seemed equally exhausted, so after leaving Alice's room with Old Arcanum, he also went to get some sleep.

However, Alice couldn't rest at all. She was constantly attending to the clingy little one, finding it hard to separate from the child, and never managed to rest.

All day long she kept the baby company, trying to extract useful information to help find the child's biological parents.

But despite Alice's best efforts, the results were discouraging—the little girl's memory loss was thorough, and she couldn't recall anything, not even her own name.

Alice couldn't help feeling a headache coming on. She had no idea how to handle this child—should she send her to an orphanage?

That idea was completely unrealistic. The little girl was so attached to Alice, having already completely taken her as her mother.

Sending her to an orphanage now would likely make the child think she was being abandoned again, crying herself blind.

Alice didn't doubt it at all. If she abandoned the child now, the girl would be heartbroken beyond hope.

So Alice had no choice—even if it was just for a day, she had to do her best to play the role of mother. Perhaps the child's memory loss was temporary, and one day she might recover her memories, resolving everything.

The little girl liked to say childish things, constantly calling "Mom," which made Alice both laugh and feel helpless.

Alice thought this little one was very sensible and well-behaved. How could any cold-hearted parent abandon such a cute baby? It was simply beyond comprehension.

By evening, Alice had given the little girl a warm bath and lulled her to sleep, finally managing to relax.

Though it had only been a day, Alice had come to understand how difficult it was to be a mother—taking care of a baby truly required a great deal of effort.

After tucking the sleeping girl in with a blanket, Alice gently touched her chubby little face.

"Mom."

The little girl clutched Alice's finger in her sleep, murmuring in her dreams, as if feeling insecure, worried she might be abandoned again.

Alice stood frozen, lowered her head, and whispered softly by the child's ear, "Mommy is here, I won't leave you."

The sleeping child was soothed and gradually grew quiet, no longer restless, sleeping peacefully.

Alice watched the girl, letting out a slight sigh of relief, thinking, "This child probably treasures maternal love so much because she was abandoned. It always makes people feel pity."

After taking care of the little girl, Alice quietly withdrew from the room, preparing to take a walk, her head spinning from the day's exhaustion.

But right as Alice stepped out, she saw Merlin standing outside, having not left.

"You're here? Didn't you go to rest?" Alice was startled upon seeing Merlin, thinking he had already fallen fast asleep and wouldn't ask about anything.

"Cough!" Merlin cleared his throat and said casually, "I took a brief nap and am no longer tired. Aren't you still not rested? I came to check on your side."

"Oh? Checking on me?" Alice raised an eyebrow, finding it hard to believe Merlin would care about her.

"Well, not exactly. I just want to ask what you plan to do with this child." Merlin changed the subject, wanting to know Alice's thoughts on how to handle the child.

Alice lowered her head, her expression suggesting she didn't quite know what to do, "I don't know either, but this child is so pitiful—abandoned by her parents, it even makes me feel sorry for her."

Merlin's forehead was etched with frown lines as he continued, "So you don't want to just abandon her casually, and instead want to take good care of her and help find her biological parents?"

"That's right. How could we just abandon her? She's so young, she can't even recognize her own mother." Alice sighed, her sympathy overflowing.

Merlin's expression turned strange as he pressed further, "And then? If you can't find her biological parents, do you plan to send her to an orphanage?"

"How could that be right? That's too much! If we send this child to an orphanage, she'll refuse food and starve herself." Alice paused, her tone awkward, "Besides, I'm already being called 'Mom' by her. What does it mean to send her to an orphanage? She'll definitely think she's been abandoned by her parents again."

Merlin was completely baffled by Alice's reasoning, pressing, "So what do you actually want to do?"

Alice sighed, showing signs of frustration and irritation, "I'm not entirely sure myself."

Merlin narrowed his eyes, looking at Alice who was hesitating and indecisive, and guessed, "You don't want to adopt this little brat, do you?"

OB SE this novel

"Ah?! What did you say?!" Alice reacted like a cat whose tail had been stepped on, startled and flustered, "W-What? How could I adopt a child out of nowhere? On what grounds are you saying that?"

"I think you're really into being a mother, interacting so well with that child, as if she were your own." Merlin wore a sly smile, as if teasing Alice.

"Impossible! Which eye of mine makes it look like I'm obsessed with being a mother? Please don't say such things." Alice shot Merlin a glance, still very sensitive, "If I don't tell her I'm her mom, the child will cry and cry. What can I do about it?"

"Is that so?" Merlin said with a hint of disbelief, clearly seeing through Alice's pretense, "The maternal aura you exuded while holding the child earlier wasn't fake, was it?"

"I never thought about adopting her. Our situation isn't suitable for adopting a child." Alice furrowed her brow and spoke seriously, "It's just that this child has lost her memory and can't remember her biological parents. I can't just watch her wander around.

I plan to temporarily take care of this child for now, and once she remembers who her biological parents are, we'll send her back.

Besides, I've never been married. Being called 'Mom' out of nowhere is already embarrassing enough for me!"

"It's just like—being played around and then abandoned by a heartless man, ending up as a single mother. So embarrassing.

title: Chapter 9 — Banquet Invitation
content:
Chapter 9 — Banquet Invitation

Volume 16 · Chapter 9

"If that child can't recover her memories?" Merlin pressed on, his expression unreadable.

"Then... then..." Alice hesitated, clearly unable to come up with a proper answer.

"Then take care of her forever." Merlin supplied the answer for Alice.

"..." Alice looked at Merlin in surprise, wondering if Merlin also wanted to adopt this child. If so... wouldn't that make them a family of three?

"Do you take me for a fool?" Merlin narrowed his eyes and said seriously, "How is that any different from adoption? Are you bullying me for being uneducated?"

A bead of cold sweat trickled down Alice's forehead, and she said awkwardly, "Then what do you want to do? Abandon her and leave her to her fate? Are you a demon or something?"

"I am one, actually." Merlin shrugged.

"Ugh, I don't care. I won't just abandon this child. My conscience won't allow it." Alice said in an irrefutable tone, as if she had already made up her mind to adopt the girl.

"Alice, please be realistic, okay?" Merlin was at a loss for words at Alice's stubbornness. She wasn't reading the situation at all. We're not in Britain right now; we're in France. What's our mission? Have you forgotten?"

"To find Dracula and kill it to lift the short-lived curse on the Arnold family." Alice remembered clearly; she hadn't forgotten why they were here.

"Exactly, that's our original mission. Now you want to bring this child along, which is extremely inconvenient. We'll face all sorts of dangers. Do you think we'll have the energy to take care of a child? If not, aren't you变相 harming her?" Merlin tried to persuade Alice, hoping she wouldn't be so kind-hearted. Bringing a child around in a foreign land was really troublesome.

It wasn't that Merlin was too cold-blooded; after weighing the pros and cons, he felt it would be better to leave the little girl alone for now.

If they really brought such a young child along, who would take care of her? Alice? Then Merlin would be left to complete the mission alone.

"....." Alice hesitated, thought for a moment, and could only choose a compromise. "How about we find the girl's parents after we finish the mission? I can't bear to just abandon her."

Merlin had already given up on persuading Alice. This stubborn woman had clearly been conquered by the little girl's adorable cuteness.

But finishing the mission first, then helping find the parents—this approach wasn't impossible. It was still better than carrying the child around throughout the mission.

"So... where do you plan to temporarily leave this child? An orphanage?"

"An orphanage definitely won't work. That child was abandoned before; if we send her there, she'll overthink it." Alice rejected the suggestion.

"Then we need to find someone to take care of her for now..." Merlin rubbed his forehead. He couldn't think of a good solution in the short term. Besides old Archelon in France, he had no acquaintances.

Just as the two were at a loss, dense footsteps echoed from the tavern's lower floor, and it sounded like quite a few people.

Camilla's subordinate, leading a group of the count's private soldiers, had arrived. They had originally been looking for which room Merlin and Alice were staying in, but upon going upstairs, they spotted them standing in the corridor chatting.

Merlin and Alice both wore Adventurers Guild identification badges, which sufficiently proved their identities.

So Camilla's subordinate stepped forward, forced a faint smile onto his pale face, bowed to the two of them, and said very politely,

"You two are the adventurers from Britain, correct?"

"What do you want?" Merlin looked at the man before him. He looked extremely frail, the kind who could be blown around by a single gust of wind.

Camilla's subordinate raised his head. Knowing Merlin's true identity, especially being gazed at by those ruby-red eyes, a wave of fear rose from deep within his heart.

Could this really be the Great Demon Lord who struck terror into everyone? He didn't seem to have an overwhelmingly fierce aura at all. He looked almost like an ordinary human.

But those eyes were utterly intimidating, showing no trace of any emotion. How many people had he killed to have such a cold gaze?

Camilla's subordinate lowered his head, instinctively avoiding eye contact with Merlin, even feeling an urge to distance himself from danger.

"Hey, I'm talking to you. What are you spacing out for?" Merlin frowned, not having a good impression of these uninvited guests.

"Ah, sorry, sir, I was distracted." Camilla's subordinate quickly apologized, forcing himself to suppress his nervousness. "The lord of Avignon would like to invite you both to dinner. Would you honor us by visiting the count's mansion?"

"Inviting us? Why?" Alice pointed at herself in surprise. They were already suspicious of Countess Camilla, and now these people showed up uninvited and wanted to share a meal? What was their game?

"Yes, it's you two. As for why... you'll know once you go." Camilla's subordinate responded politely.

Merlin and Alice exchanged glances, both deeply puzzled. They had been planning to cause trouble for the lord, and now the lord came to them instead.

The two stepped aside and huddled together, whispering quietly, debating whether or not to go. It felt like a trap—a banquet from which none would return.

"Merlin, why would the lord of Avignon invite us to dinner?" Alice asked quietly.

"I don't know, but didn't the mercenary company leader likely flee to the count's mansion for refuge? It might be about that." Merlin glanced at the group, all of them carrying weapons. At first glance, this didn't look like a pleasant dinner. If they refused, there would likely be violence.

Actually, Merlin was overthinking it. So many people had come just to put on a show. The other side already knew his identity as the Demon Lord and had long abandoned any plans to use force against him—it wouldn't work.

"What is this countess plotting? Why show up at a time like this? Is it because we interfered with her interests?" Alice furrowed her delicate brows.

"Possible. These people are not here with good intentions, so it's better to be careful. Our lodging was easily found, which clearly means they've been investigating us." Merlin deduced that this group had come straight for him and Alice.

"What should we do? Go or not?" Alice was seeking Merlin's opinion.

"Let's go. Free dinner, why not?" Merlin said matter-of-factly.

"Hey! Are you serious?" Alice stomped her foot in anger, shooting Merlin furious glares.

"Cough! This is a rare opportunity. Aren't you curious what kind of person this female lord is?" Merlin countered.

Alice thought about it and nodded. "Fine, we'll go to the banquet. Should we bring the baby? She didn't seem to have eaten enough for dinner."

"Tch!" Merlin rolled his eyes and said in an exasperated tone,

"You've really taken on the role of her real mother, haven't you?"

title: Chapter 10 — Banquet of Treachery?
content:
Chapter 10 — Banquet of Treachery?

Volume 16 · Chapter 10

"...It's not like that!" Alice's face flushed red, and she glared at Merlin with puffed cheeks. "I was just worried that the child would wake up hungry at night. Besides, for some reason, that kid eats very little and seems to really dislike meals."

"We'll just come back earlier, won't we? We can just ask old Acalon to help look after her for a bit, right?" Merlin figured it was fine to have old Acalon help watch over the little girl while he and Alice went to meet the countess.

Alice hesitated for a moment, thinking it wasn't a bad idea—as long as they came back early. Still, she felt a bit worried about the child.

If the little girl suddenly woke up and couldn't find her mother, she would surely cry and throw a fit.

"...Alright."

Although Alice and Merlin's conversation was kept very low, Camilla's subordinates still caught fragments of it. The information they gathered was incomplete and piecemeal.

They have a child too? This news should be reported to Lady Camilla at once.

That human woman was a Mithril-ranked adventurer—not exactly easy to deal with.

But a weak child would be very easy to handle. Perhaps by kidnapping the child, they could control both of them…

That night, Merlin and Alice arrived at the count's mansion.

Before leaving, they had already entrusted old Acalon with watching over the little girl.

When old Acalon learned that Alice and Merlin had been invited to dinner by Countess Camilla, he was very surprised inside, but he still urged them to be careful.

If Merlin and Alice didn't return for a long time, old Acalon said he would go to the count's mansion to look for them.

The dim candlelight cast a yellowish glow. At the long dining table, only three people sat—Merlin, Alice, and Countess Camilla.

The table was laden with a sumptuous feast. Merlin's eyes grew fixed on the spread, pondering whether to start with the roast chicken or the large steak beside it.

The room was lavishly decorated and quite refined, making the strict old castle feel solemn and stately. In such a private setting, it seemed as though something confidential would be discussed.

Camilla smiled and observed both Merlin and Alice. She didn't speak first but was considering how to broach the subject—how to ask these two troublesomest entities to leave without revealing she was a member of the Blood Clan.

*Are those two? They don't look particularly well-matched. How did this human woman manage to seduce a Demon Lord? Those fake breasts—surely a joke.*

*If it were just this woman alone, I could probably hold my own or even gain the upper hand. But with that one beside her…*

Camilla gave Merlin a closer look, her expression growing slightly more serious. *So this is the First Demon Lord? There's absolutely no trace of demonic aura—it's as if he's just an ordinary human.*

*If I hadn't already received definite intelligence, I wouldn't have even bothered to glance at someone so ordinary.*

*Still, to remain so calm here—I suppose being one of the Seven Demon Lords earns that much respect. He keeps his composure in any situation.*

*Unlike that human woman beside him, who came in with openly hostile eyes fixed on me. Such an obvious display of antagonism—isn't she practically shouting her thoughts for everyone to hear?*

*It seems she's already figured out how suspicious I am. Even if I hadn't invited them to dinner tonight, she must have already planned to deal with me, hasn't she?*

Meanwhile, Camilla was speculating about various scenarios in her mind, viewing both Merlin and Alice as deeply hostile. However, the truth was quite different.

*Merlin: Chicken leg first, or steak first? I want both—the chicken leg looks delicious, but there's only one steak. I guess I'll go for the steak first; otherwise, Alice will steal it. That terrible woman never lets me have my way.*

*Alice: Are you kidding me?! Why the hell are this lady lord's boobs so enormous?! They're about to burst out of her bra, right? I hate women with bigger breasts than mine the most! Fortunately, Merlin's busy staring at that chicken leg, so I'm relieved.*

"Hmm!" Camilla gave a light cough and put on a polite smile. "I welcome you to my castle. I wonder if the two of you are satisfied?"

"Satisfied, satisfied." Merlin nodded repeatedly. Regardless, the table full of dishes greatly pleased him.

"Tch!" Alice nudged Merlin with her elbow, signaling him not to forget what they were there for.

"Ah…" Merlin looked up, thought for a moment, and said, "We are satisfied, but I wonder what business Lordess has to summon us here."

"This is… of course to thank you for your outstanding contributions to Avignon. Otherwise, what do you think I invited you here for?" Camilla smiled.

"Our outstanding contributions to Avignon?" Merlin was full of question marks. He didn't recall having done anything particularly good.

"Lordess, perhaps there's some misunderstanding. We've never done anything like that," Alice responded seriously.

"The two adventurers who wiped out the Dict Plains mercenary band—aren't those precisely the two of you?" Camilla said meaningfully, closely observing Merlin and Alice's reactions.

Merlin and Alice glanced at each other but said nothing. They had originally suspected Camilla was colluding with the mercenary band, and now the other party not only brought it up proactively but also credited them with the功劳. This left the two puzzled. Could it be that Camilla wasn't colluding with the band but merely had some kind of connection to them?

"This merit is no small thing. The Dict Plains mercenary band has always been a destabilizing factor in Avignon, frequently engaging in kidnapping and human trafficking. I've long wanted to eliminate them, but I never found a suitable opportunity." Camilla painted the mercenaries as dirty and distanced herself from any involvement. "You've inadvertently done me a great favor. This dinner invitation is my way of showing gratitude."

Merlin furrowed his brows, wondering if Countess Camilla truly had no connection to those mercenaries. It couldn't be—so many people had said she frequently exchanged letters with the mercenary commander. Would someone who wanted to eliminate them act like this?

"The merit hardly counts. We were after the people who kept mysteriously disappearing in Avignon, and wiping out the mercenary band was just an附带 benefit. No need to make a fuss about it," Alice responded coolly, feeling the other party was being far too enthusiastic.

"You two needn't be modest. Even though it was by chance, you've done me a great favor and removed a thorn from my side. I ought to thank you properly."

After Camilla finished speaking, she clapped her hands. Her subordinates outside entered, each taking out a crystal card from their chest and placing it directly in front of Alice and Merlin.

Such crystal cards were generally issued by major merchant guilds. As long as one visited the guild's branches, they could be exchanged for a considerable sum of money, though the exact amount varied.

Carrying large quantities of gold coins was too inconvenient, but with these crystal cards, much of the burden was relieved. They were mostly used for large-sum payments.

Merlin and Alice stared at the crystal cards on the table without speaking, thinking in surprise: *What exactly does this countess want? Not only is she treating us to a meal, but she's also giving away money for free?!*

"There is 500,000 gold coins inside, considered my token of gratitude." Camilla paused and added with a smile, "Once you accept it, you may return to Britain."

"Anything after this, I will handle entirely on my own. There's no need for you to interfere further. How does that sound?"

title: Chapter 11 — Unappreciated
content:
Chapter 11 — Unappreciated

Volume 16 · Chapter 11

After hearing Camilla's words, Alice immediately narrowed her eyes, wondering what this meant? After paying them off, she wanted them to leave and take over everything? Was this a roundabout way of bribing them?

What on earth could make this countess want them gone so badly?

So her warmth was just a facade; her real intention was to keep them out of her business, right?

There must be something suspicious about this countess; otherwise, why would she be so worried about Merlin and Alice investigating the disappearances?

Alice frowned, realizing today wasn't just about a meal—it was likely to be very troublesome. Something was definitely wrong here.

Although Camilla's attitude was pleasant, she was already becoming an obstacle for them.

Merlin stared at the crystal card. This tiny crystal card was worth 500,000 gold coins? That was a considerable sum. Even if they helped Lord Austin lift his family's curse, they wouldn't get nearly that much.

Comparing the two, Merlin felt a flicker of wavering—this offer was clearly more profitable.

So he leaned closer to Alice and whispered, "Alice, this offer is quite generous—500,000 gold. How about we stop poking our noses in and just leave France?"

"Huh?" Alice was taken aback, then said discontentedly, "What are you thinking? You'd betray your mission for money? If we just leave Britain, how will we explain to Lord Austin? We'll lose our credibility."

"Credibility doesn't pay the bills, does it? Lord Austin can't offer 500,000 gold. Weighing the benefits, this is clearly the better choice." Merlin didn't let emotions cloud his judgment; choosing the most profitable option was only natural.

"No, you can't have no principles at all! We're adventurers—if we take a job, we see it through. What kind of professional ethics is it to be talked out of it?" Alice said sternly.

"Tsk." Merlin clicked his tongue, unable to understand Alice's stubbornness. The main reason for taking a job was to earn money. Once the money was in hand, why keep working?

"Your Excellencies, how did your discussion go? If you've decided, please accept the payment. I'll have someone prepare a carriage first thing tomorrow to take you to the port and out of France." Camilla thought her offer was generous. What else did adventurers want besides money? With enough money, why would they keep investigating?

"Sorry, we..."

"We'll take the payment—as a reward for eliminating the mercenary band. But regarding the disappearances, we still need to investigate."

Alice had intended to refuse, but Merlin beat her to it, slipping the crystal card into his pocket under the guise of it being the reward for "wiping out the mercenaries," completely ignoring the displeasure on Camilla's face.

Merlin's shamelessness had reached near-human levels. Though he accepted the money, he wasn't entirely ignoring Alice's wishes.

Alice watched Merlin tuck the crystal card away, her expression turning peculiar. She thought, *Whenever this guy gets a chance to profit, his IQ shoots up by 200%, coming up with a thousand excuses to claim the prize.*

Camilla's face darkened instantly. Her deeper meaning was: *Take the money and get lost; don't be a nuisance in Avignon.* But Merlin's thick skin had completely shattered her worldview. The money was gone, and nothing had been accomplished.

Camilla knew Merlin was the Great Demon Lord. She had no confidence in confronting him directly—she'd probably lose. Stuck in a dilemma, she had no choice but to force herself to speak.

"Ah... yes, this is well-deserved reward for both of you. You must have made a fortune on this trip. You can go back now, right?"

"Huh? Why should we leave Avignon? Our mission isn't even finished." Merlin thought for a moment, then said, copying what he'd just heard, "We have no professional ethics..."

Camilla was nearly spitting blood from rage. In her mind, she was cursing, *You Great Demon Lord, putting on this fake act! We're all the same here—no one's better! Who cares about professional ethics? If you really cared about ethics, you'd go conquer all the human empires!*

"Aren't you adventurers? Then don't meddle in things beyond your control. Tell me, what was the bounty for this mission? To compensate you, I'll double it."

"Lord Countess, this isn't about the money. Why do you want us to leave so badly? Is there a reason?" Alice asked, her expression unreadable.

"To be honest, there are officials within the empire secretly supporting the mercenary band. The human trafficking trade is rampant behind the scenes. This involves political maneuvering. You're just adventurers—you shouldn't get involved. Moreover, as the ruler of Avignon, dealing with the Dictat Mercenary Band is my responsibility. You have no right to interfere, do you? If you insist, I'll have to use imperial law against you and report your unprofessional behavior to the Adventurers Guild headquarters in Denmark." Though Camilla spoke tactfully, her threat was unmistakable.

Adventurers couldn't act without restraint. They had to follow local rules, or the headquarters would sanction them—ranging from expulsion to demotion.

Though adventurers belonged to different regions, the headquarters in Denmark was their true governing body.

This reporting system was similar to complaints in the civilized world. If they didn't want demotion or a hit to their income, it was best not to make mistakes.

"Oh? Is the Lord Countess threatening us now?" Alice regarded Camilla coldly.

"It's not a threat. You're from Great Britain; this is France. If you want things to go smoothly, I suggest you behave yourselves," Camilla said earnestly.

"Are you worried we'll uncover something damaging to you? Or are you hiding something?" Alice studied Camilla, but the countess was a seasoned fox—her cover-up showed no cracks.

"Hiding what?" Camilla smiled, putting on a calm, open face.

"We interrogated those mercenaries. They said you've been in frequent contact with the mercenary band's leader. Is that leader hiding here with you?" Alice asked pointedly, her eyes scanning the room as if searching for clues.

"Nonsense! Those mercenaries will say anything to save their lives. Do you really think they're trustworthy?" Camilla spread her hands dismissively.

Alice had no more options. They hadn't found anything unusual about the castle upon arrival, and now Camilla had cleared herself of all suspicion. There was no point in continuing.

"Apologies, but we won't leave until we've properly investigated this. Thank you for your hospitality. Merlin, let's go."

As Alice spoke, she grabbed Merlin's arm. He, however, conveniently snagged a roast chicken leg, pointing it at Camilla like a weapon.

"We're not leaving. If you offer us ten times the bounty, we might reconsider. Just think about it—ten times isn't much!"

After Merlin and Alice left, only Camilla and her subordinates remained at the table, the atmosphere now cold and empty.

The dishes on the table were barely touched, except for the chicken leg Merlin had dragged away.

Camilla's face was grim. She kept her head down, an aura of dead silence radiating from her.

One of her subordinates approached and whispered, "Lord Countess, what should we do next?"

Camilla's expression turned savage. She slammed her fist on the table, shattering the long wooden surface into powder.

"You ungrateful pair! After all my kindness, you dare reject me?!"

title: Chapter 12 — Time is Pressing
content:
Chapter 12 — Time is Pressing

Volume 16 · Chapter 12

Seeing Camilla fly into such a rage, the subordinates dared not speak, not even daring to breathe.
It seemed that Merlin and Alice's unyielding attitude made Camilla especially furious.
The veins on Camilla's forehead were throbbing, her expression twisted with anger, completely lacking the previous poise of a noble lady.
"What the hell is that human woman?! If Lucifer III weren't sitting beside me, I'd tear her mouth apart right now!"
"My lord, since they won't back off, should we think of another way?" the subordinate asked timidly, his meek demeanor for fear that the lord would vent his anger on him.
"Other ways? What other ways? If we keep letting them investigate, they'll surely drag our whole clan into it, and since they're in Avignon we can't just go kidnapping humans anymore; if Lord Madess still needs human sacrifices next month, what would we give him?" Camilla said grimly, half-pushed into a dead end; if it weren't for her fear of Lucifer III, she would have already cut through the mess with a swift blade, sending all obstacles to the grave.
"If we were to go head-to-head with that Great Demon Lord, what are our chances of winning? If not, we could ask Lord Madess to come personally and deal with Lucifer III; with Lord Madess's strength he could still contend with the demon monarch, and besides we could assist from the side." The subordinate thought that seeking external aid would be safer in this situation; rashly provoking a dispute would likely make victory impossible.
Camilla lowered her head, thought for a moment, then shook her head to reject that answer: "At this critical juncture, when our father is about to awaken, Lord Madess is surely busy with the sacrificial rites and won't have time to deal with Lucifer III; if we insist on having him help us, it will inevitably affect our father's awakening plan—and if that's the case, we'd be utterly useless."
"But Lucifer III..." the subordinate wanted to speak but held back, thinking that dealing with Lucifer III was the top priority.
"Who said we have to go head-to-head with him? I'm not an idiot—yesterday didn't I say we'd strike at his wife? Given the situation we can't just sit and wait for doom; we must find a way to subdue them." Camilla corrected the misunderstanding; she had never even considered fighting the Great Demon Lord directly.
"But how could we separate them? Obviously that human woman isn't easy to deal with either; for some reason I sense a pressure from a superior species about her." the subordinate said, frowning.
"What do you mean? Do you think I can't beat that human woman?" Camilla's eyes flashed with a fierce light, as if questioning.
"No, my lord, you've misunderstood; I mean dealing with this woman is troublesome, so we should pick a better hostage?" the subordinate hastily explained.
"A better hostage?" Camilla furrowed her brows, unsure what he meant.
"My lord, just now when I went to invite them to dinner, I inadvertently heard they need to look after a child; compared to the trouble of dealing with that female adventurer, I think taking their child would be more appropriate—even a demon wouldn't be indifferent to their own flesh and blood." The subordinate relayed this information to Camilla.
"There's a child too?" Camilla's eyes widened in disbelief; hearing this she was greatly surprised—Lucifer III not only married a human but also had a child!
"Yeah, although I didn't hear it clearly, I did catch that they have a child to look after; initially they were unwilling to come to the banquet." The subordinate said with a sly glance, guessing Camilla already knew what to do.
"I see, going out adventuring while bringing a child—what a foolish couple..." Camilla stroked her pointed chin, pondering how to instantly subdue the two.
It seemed that making Lucifer III and his wife submit wasn't really that difficult.
It just needed a slight adjustment in strategy....
In the late night, inside the room, the little girl was still sound asleep.
Merlin and Alice returned quickly, and they hadn't eaten either.
So the little girl didn't make any fuss; she probably still thought her mother was nearby.
Old Akalon lit an oil lamp, wrapped himself in his coat, walked in, saw Merlin and Alice discussing matters, and hurried over.
"How was it? Did you gain anything from the late-night banquet?" Old Akalon asked curiously.
Merlin spat out the chicken bone in his mouth and said lightly, "Here, this is the gain."
"Tsk, don't joke—I'm asking seriously." Old Akalon said helplessly.
"We haven't really found anything worthwhile; the lord indeed seems quite proper, we saw no evidence of collusion with the mercenary corps, and aside from the castle lighting being too dim, there doesn't appear to be anything else suspicious." Alice answered quite seriously.
"Is that so?" Old Akalon stroked his chin, probing, "Did the lord give you any trouble?"
"That's not the case." Alice replied softly, afraid to wake the sleeping baby.
"I told you, the lord of Avignon is very conscientious and kind—how could he be a bad person? You must have been mistaken earlier." Old Akalon showed a relieved expression.
"I haven't finished speaking yet; we can't jump to conclusions about right or wrong too early. The lord of Avignon said the mercenary corps is involved in many things, hopes we won't interfere, and wants us to leave France as soon as possible—isn't that just blatantly kicking us out?" Alice said seriously; the situation isn't clear yet, and she definitely won't leave the French Empire.
"'....Is it just a misunderstanding?' Old Akalon thought it wasn't a big deal; if we wipe out the mercenary corps of Dikteping and offend imperial bigwigs, it really wouldn't be easy to handle."
"What misunderstanding? She wants us to leave? There must be some deeper reason..." Alice paused, hesitant, and said, "Maybe our actions disturbed her cake, she started feeling anxious, so she invited us to dinner late at night, trying every means to get us to leave Avignon and stop meddling."
"Hiss!" Old Akalon sucked in a breath of cold air, nodded, and agreed, "Indeed that's possible."
"Besides, that wasn't really a request for us to leave; the words inside and out are full of threats. If we don't go, they might cause us trouble—I'm increasingly suspecting that this female lord is always putting on a false front, that she has something on her mind which makes her eager for us to leave. But we have no evidence, so we can't openly contend with her." Alice wore a gloomy expression, presently at a loss.
"We can't leave yet—the mission isn't finished, and we still hope to investigate the missing persons and root out the hidden blood clan." Old Akalon also didn't agree to just leave like that; it feels rather humiliating.
"Exactly, we never agreed to leave." Alice dispelled Akalon's doubts.
said
"But the lord of Avignon wields tremendous local power; taking action would be difficult, don't you have a way?" Old Akalon glanced at Merlin and Alice.
Merlin leaned back in his chair, thinking over the past two days, feeling that Avignon had frequent mysterious disappearances; this female lord is definitely implicated.
"Let's investigate this lady's background; her castle is huge, there's no way there wouldn't be any clues."
"If we search carefully, we should uncover some secret."
"If possible, we'll take action tomorrow."
"Before we're restricted by the opponent's authority, we ought to get everything cleared up...."

title: Chapter 13 — Being Watched
content:
Chapter 13 — Being Watched

Volume 16 · Chapter 13

“Check it? This might be difficult, right? You went to the lord's castle and found nothing.” Old Akalon frowned, thinking Merlin's words were unrealistic.

“That castle is huge; we can't possibly see everywhere—those guards behind us on the road are staring us down, giving us no chance.” Merlin spread his hands helplessly.

“Yeah, we can't find any evidence now; if we rashly oppose Countess Camilla, we could easily be labeled as rioters. With evidence, it would be a completely different story.” Alice nodded.

“What do you plan to do?” Old Karron looked at Merlin and Alice, unsure what they were thinking.

“Tonight, I'll sneak into the count's castle to have a look; maybe I can find some useful clues.” Merlin intended to go himself, hoping to find evidence of Countess Camilla colluding with the mercenary band.

“Oh? Tonight? What a good opportunity!” Old Akalon's eyes lit up.

“A good opportunity?” Alice furrowed her brows, not understanding Old Akalon's meaning.

“I heard that tomorrow night there will be a parade in the main city of Avignon, and Countess Camilla will leave the castle to meet the populace and give a speech, to stabilize the current tense emotions.” Old Akalon said seriously, having heard this from drinkers downstairs.

“Stabilize the current tense emotions in the main city?” Alice wondered.

“Exactly, because of the lord's decision, Avignon's main city has taken in a large number of flood refugees, already causing many conflicts and bloodshed; if not handled promptly, it could lead to riots.” Old Akalon said solemnly.

Alice said nothing, lowering her head in thought: “Sure enough, people who rely on others are rejected wherever they go—here is no different. If the empire still doesn't step in to handle the massive number of refugees, this group might end up—only homeless?”

“But it's strange to hold it at night—aren't such things usually during the day?” Merlin showed a thoughtful expression, finding it odd.

“I'm not entirely sure either, but I heard that Countess Camilla only meets the populace at night and never leaves the castle during the day.” Old Akalon was equally puzzled.

Merlin furrowed his brows, thinking carefully about everything: vampires cannot walk in sunlight or they'd be burned to death; Countess Camilla never goes out during the day, only becomes active at night; the castle's layout is overly dark, surrounded by dense jungle that blocks almost all light—_.... could it be that Countess Camilla cannot stand the light?

A series of oddities forced Merlin to think more; it seemed he had caught some clues, but they weren't quite solid, and he still needed to look further.

“So... tonight really is a good opportunity, Countess Camilla leaves the castle—there's no better time to sneak in. Alice thought we could give it a try, so she turned to Merlin and said, ‘You go?’”

“Sure, I'll go. Actually, I'm quite interested in sneaking into Countess Camilla's bedroom and maybe taking a few pieces of underwear—her breasts are really...” Merlin gave a half‑smile, as if he'd been wanting to complain for a while.

“Ugh!” Alice felt as if struck by lightning, jabbing Merlin's cheeks with her fingers, deforming them but not stopping, “Can't you focus on something decent, you jerk? Seeing big breasts and you can't walk straight, you don't even spare middle‑aged women—wow, you're disgusting…”.

“…” Merlin glanced sideways at Alice, thinking, “I'm just commenting on her figure—where does this old woman get her attitude? She's exposing her own inferiority complex.”

“Wait, I think I should handle this—let me infiltrate the count's manor to investigate; it would be more suitable.” Old Akalon volunteered.

“…Suitable?” Alice had wanted to say Old Akalon wasn't reliable, but she didn't feel like saying it outright.

“You two are now on bad terms with the countess; I estimate your every move will be watched, while I, a nobody, will be relatively safe.” Old Akalon paused, wearing a reminiscent expression, “To be honest, before I became an adventurer, I was a thief with consummate skill—I'm quite good at stealing things.”

“...Really? I don't think that's something worth bragging about.” A bead of cold sweat trickled down Alice's forehead.

“I'm just saying I have plenty of experience in sneaking in to steal things; this can totally be left to me, especially since I'm always under your two's protection—I can't just do nothing.” Old Akalon said confidently.

Alice still doubted Old Akalon, looking at Merlin, trying to get him to refuse.

However, Merlin thought it over and felt Old Akalon was indeed safer—this low‑profile guy would be safer infiltrating the castle than I would. “Alright, I think handing it over to Old Akalon is fine—who knows whether our every move is under the countess's surveillance?”

“But… Alice still feels uneasy.

“There's no ‘but’—the organization has already decided to appoint Old Akalon as the best infiltrator. But please don't forget that if we find Countess Camilla's underwear, remember to bring back a piece; we need to study this thoroughly, and if we succeed, it will be a boon for countless washboards.” Merlin said seriously; among all the women he'd seen, Countess Camilla's breasts were unusually large, which naturally piqued his curiosity.

Old Akalon's face was grave as he said solemnly, “Please rest assured, organization—I guarantee I will complete the mission.”

Alice darkened her face, covered Merlin's smelly mouth, and said coldly:

“Please shut your stinking mouth—no one wants to hear you talk.”

The next day, the sun was about to sink below the horizon, entering evening.

The number of pedestrians on the street became very large, starting to become crowded.

They are presumably all participating in Countess Camilla's parade, wanting to hear the lord's speech.

Although the number of participants is large, they are basically divided into two groups: the native residents of Avignon and the incoming refugees.

Due to the influx of refugees, the main city is overcrowded, and the number of people resentful of Countess Camilla's decisions is countless.

Moreover, the refugees' children keep disappearing; many problems have piled up, causing many to complain bitterly, forcing Countess Camilla to come out and give a response.

Even so, this female lord remains in most people's eyes as a wise figure, enjoying great respect and affection.

Merlin pulled back the room's curtains, gazing outside; although many people had gathered outside, he had already noticed some issues.

Right in the alley outside the inn, two people had been staring there all day, sneaking glances at this place, never leaving.

Merlin cocked the corner of his mouth, gave a helpless laugh—indeed, as expected, he and Alice had been under the countess's all‑day surveillance—

“Alice, there are two people outside watching us all day.

“It seems our every move cannot escape the lord's eyes.

“How is Old Akalon's preparation? It's time for him to set out....

title: Chapter 14 — Stay Calm (Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets)
content:
Chapter 14 — Stay Calm (Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets)

Volume 16 · Chapter 14

"He's long gone," Alice said, holding the little girl in the house. The two of them looked particularly affectionate.

"Is that so?" Merlin nodded, pulling the curtains closed, and said helplessly, "Looks like this female lord is determined to make things difficult for us. Being watched so closely, we can't do anything. We can only rely on Old Akalon to bring back some gains."

"However, Old Akalon is usually unreliable. I'm afraid this time will be no different," Alice thought with some worry.

"Now we're like prisoners. Only leaving Avignon can remove Camilla's targeting. If we want to resist, we can only rely on Old Akalon obtaining evidence. By then, even if we kill the lord of Avignon, nothing will happen. We can even beautify it as ridding the world of a villain~"

Merlin sighed, turning to sit on the chair, thinking that if they were in Great Britain, it would probably be fine to chop off the lord's head, since the queen still owed him a favor.

In Great Britain, Merlin is a great hero, but in France he's nothing. Acting recklessly would bring all sorts of trouble.

He came to France to solve the Austin family's short lifespan curse, not to cause trouble randomly.

"Hope so," Alice nodded, but she also hoped Old Akalon would have some gains tonight.

"Is Mom going to beat up bad guys?" the little girl asked in a childish voice.

"Possibly, but don't worry too much. Mom is still pretty formidable," Alice said, holding the girl and pinching her nose.

"But Mom, when fighting bad guys, you always encounter danger. I don't want Mom to be in danger," the little girl said with a dejected expression.

Seeing the worried look on the little girl's face, Alice was suddenly melted by cuteness, her heart overflowing with love. Such a small baby already knew how to care for her, much better than that ungrateful one.

So Alice hugged the girl tightly, pressing her against her chest, and said in a gentle tone.

"Good baby, Mom won't be in danger. I'll stay with you, okay?"

"....." The little girl stopped talking, seeming very clingy toward Alice.

Merlin watched coldly from the side, getting goosebumps all over. He was very unaccustomed to Alice showing a maternal side, so different from her usual image.

"Hey, enough already. You've been sticking together for a long time. Have you considered others' feelings?"

"What? It's none of your business. Jealous?" Alice rolled her eyes dramatically.

"What!?" Merlin froze suddenly, pointing at himself. "Me? Jealous?"

"Why would I be jealous of you meddling so much?" Alice said irritably.

"I..."

Merlin thought. He wasn't jealous. It was just that since the little girl arrived, Alice had been ignoring him, always coaxing this mysterious baby.

He just found it a bit annoying. He wasn't her real mom. Was there a need to spoil her like this? Was that what jealousy was!?

Merlin couldn't find a suitable reason to respond, and since the child was present, he couldn't say it outright.

"Clearing his throat, don't forget what we said last night."

Alice froze, remembering she promised to help the girl find her mom. She said huffily, "I won't forget. No need for you to butt in—"

"Hey!" Merlin grinned, not wanting to meddle further. He thought that if this continued, Alice might treat the girl as her own. Whether she'd help find the biological parents was uncertain. This bitch was so willful; he couldn't pull her back either.

Alice glanced at Merlin, thinking if she had neglected him too much these past two days, making him feel like a lonely old man?

But it was strange that the girl was only close to her and not willing to approach Merlin. Did Merlin look nothing like the girl's father?

Alice thought for a moment, her face suddenly turning red. She thought of a method, though it was a bit embarrassing. So she whispered to the little girl.

"Baby, can you call that smelly man sitting on the chair 'Dad'?"

"Dad? But I don't have a dad..." The little girl showed a troubled expression.

Alice's face changed. No dad? The child was from a single-parent family! Abandoned by mom, no dad—this child was too pitiful, right?

Alice, overflowing with sympathy, felt even more pity for the little girl. She hugged her tightly and patted her back gently.

"So that's it. Forget it, don't call then. It's fine."

"If Mom lets me call like that, I'll listen." The little girl said hesitantly.

Alice thought for a moment, whispered something to the little girl with a smile, then put her on the ground and acted.

The little girl nodded, scampered over to Merlin, looking very obedient to Alice's words.

Merlin was thinking about Old Akalon, wondering if something unexpected would happen, when he felt someone shaking his calf. Looking down, he saw the little girl looking at him with puppy eyes.

"What?"

Facing Merlin's question, the girl seemed a bit scared, her eyes darting. After hesitating, she said, "Da... Dad!"

"Pu!" Merlin almost choked on his spit, nearly falling off the chair. He never expected this brat to start randomly claiming parents. Before it was just Alice, now the target shifted to him.

Seeing Merlin's reaction, Alice almost burst out laughing. It was no different from when she was first called Mom. She was shocked to the extreme. Ha, she was actually so happy she jumped up?

"Shut up! It's definitely you, this bitch, who instigated it?! What do you want?" Merlin's face darkened. Honestly, he wasn't that happy. He just felt 100,000 grass mud horses trampling his chest. He had no kids and never would!

"Who said I instigated it? She's willing to call you Dad. Aren't you secretly happy right now?" Alice showed an expression of seeing right through Merlin.

"I don't. Right now I just feel a headache," Merlin emphasized, frowning.

"Dad." The little girl was small; Merlin's knees were at her nose level. To get attention, she could only shake his leg.

"Stop, don't call randomly! I'm not your dad. That's your real mom. Go find her." Merlin said with a very serious expression.

Alice frowned slightly, thinking why was this guy so cold? Wouldn't he be happy if such a cute kid called him Dad?

"Uh, Dad, wah..." The little girl felt her eyes tighten, with an urge to cry. She held Merlin's leg and wouldn't let go, looking very aggrieved.

"......." Merlin's eyebrows rose helplessly. He really couldn't stand the kid crying like this—

"Don't do this. It makes me look like a bad guy, deliberately bullying a child—"

But this kid was so clingy, and when she threw tantrums she was fearless. She seemed kinda cute though....

Wait!

Calm down! Don't let a few calls of "Dad" make you forget who you are! Hey!

title: Chapter 15 — Merlin's Attitude
content:
Chapter 15 — Merlin's Attitude

Volume 16 · Chapter 15

Merlin thought about it. Seeing the little girl's aggrieved expression, he wanted to comfort her, but then he remembered he wasn't her biological father, so why should he treat her so gently?

Besides, he couldn't show too gentle a side, or else this little girl would keep clinging to him. He should let her know his scary side.

"Don't cry! Swallow it! ...Or I'll hit you if you keep crying?"

Merlin put on a stern face and scolded her sharply, hoping to scare her straight and stop her from pestering him.

"Guh..." The little girl let out a whimper like a small animal from her throat, and covering her eyes with both tiny hands, she burst into tears, sobbing loudly.

"Uh!" Merlin's expression darkened. He didn't know how to handle it. He hadn't expected this brat to be so fragile—was he really supposed to cry just because he said a few harsh words?

The little girl, who hadn't been crying for a long time, now had tears streaming down like a stream. She kept wiping at them with her hands but refused to look up, bowing her head and sobbing without speaking. Her petite body trembled slightly, making her look just like a child who had done something wrong.

"Hey! Merlin! What are you doing? Why so fierce?! How can you be so cold-hearted toward such a little kid?!" Alice saw Merlin being harsh with the little girl and was immediately furious, giving him a good scolding.

"...I didn't say anything..." Merlin felt rather wronged. He wasn't deliberately bullying a child, and he certainly wasn't the type to do such a thing.

Seeing the little girl frightened, Alice felt heartbroken and rushed over to comfort her. "Baby, don't cry, baby don't cry, be a good girl~"

With Alice's comfort, the little girl felt a little better and tried hard to hold her tears back, putting on a brave face as if she were trying desperately to stay strong.

"Don't just stand there stunned. You made her cry, so at least make it up to her?" Alice glared at Merlin poutily. Was this guy really not fond of children?

"How am I supposed to compensate? It's not even my fault..." Merlin shrugged, feeling like he was the most wronged person here.

"Stinking Merlin, hopeless." Alice shot back an accusation.

"Me!?"

Although Merlin felt a bit of guilt, it wasn't enough to warrant an apology.

Being scolded by Alice like this left him quite annoyed.

Actually, Merlin had panicked inside when called "Dad," which is why he'd scolded her so harshly. He had zero experience being a father and had no idea how to make a little kid happy.

Merlin had grown up in the Demon Lord Palace. As the royal heir, he'd naturally lived a life where everything was done for him—servants dressed him and fed him. Who would have bothered to coax a child when he was growing up?

"Cough! Stop crying. Crying nonstop is embarrassing."

"She's a kid. Crying is normal. Didn't you ever cry when you were little?" Alice rolled her eyes so hard it was painful.

"No."

Merlin shook his head. He wanted to coax the little girl, but he had nothing on him that could make a child happy, except...

He pulled out the crystal card worth 500,000 gold coins from his coat and placed it in the little girl's hand.

In Merlin's mind, kids surely liked money too, right? They could buy lots of toys and such.

Merlin, with absolutely no experience coaxing children, had racked his brains and could only come up with this awkward method.

So, suppressing the sting of parting with such a costly item, he struck a cool pose and spoke in a stern, fatherly tone:

"Take this and buy something to eat. Buy whatever you like, but don't go crying the moment something goes wrong. Someone's wiping your tears now, but later no one will feel sorry for you, got it?"

"..." The little girl looked at the crystal card in her hand with a puzzled expression. She didn't seem to understand what it was at all.

......

Alice gave an awkward laugh. She was at a loss for Merlin's actions. What kind of three- or four-year-old could understand the concept of money?

This guy really couldn't coax anyone happy. Even if he did become a dad, he'd surely be the clueless type. So someone who always acted so nonchalant had this呆 (dense) side too?

If this child was truly hers and Merlin's, he'd probably show his affection in his own eccentric way, wouldn't he?

Alice let her imagination run wild, and her face inexplicably flushed red. If the child called Merlin "Dad," then wouldn't they be a real couple? That actually didn't sound bad—

"Alice, what are you imagining in your head again? Still thinking about how to screw me over? Is that what's making you blush?" Merlin noticed Alice zoning out and couldn't resist teasing her.

"...I'm not! Don't say nonsense!" Alice woke from her daydream and explained timidly.

Merlin scrutinized Alice for a moment. He figured the little girl calling him Dad was八成 (likely) instigated by this rotten woman. What exactly was she planning?

Alice saw the crystal card in the little girl's hand and got an idea. "Baby, this card in your hand can be exchanged for a lot of money. How about you give it to Mommy? Mommy will keep it safe for you for now, okay?"

The little girl trusted Alice completely and held up the crystal card with both hands, saying in a milky voice, "Mommy takes care of it. Here, Mommy~"

"You're such a good girl." Alice patted the little girl's head and took the crystal card. After all, a kid wouldn't know how to spend money anyway, so she might as well keep it for her.

The little girl seemed to enjoy the head pats very much and threw herself into Alice's arms, acting spoiled.

Watching all this from the side, Merlin's face turned dark. Keep it safe his ass! This was nothing but embezzlement in disguise! Using adult lies on a child—did she have any conscience at all?!

Merlin felt a bit resentful. This crystal card was meant to coax the little girl happy, and now this little brat just handed it over to her mom in an instant. Was innocence supposed to have no limits?

Alice deliberately waved the crystal card in front of her eyes as if to taunt, This is mine~

Merlin frowned. This money should have been his in the first place. Last night Alice hadn't wanted it, but he'd grabbed it anyway. But now that the kid was here, and he'd just given it away... going back on it now would be embarrassing.

So seething quietly, Merlin stood up. He felt he'd been played and wanted to go for a walk.

"What are you doing? Going out?" Alice saw Merlin get up, seeming ready to leave, and wondered if she'd annoyed him.

"I'll go take a look. Since the lord personally gave a speech, it'd be worth listening to. There might be other gains. Besides, there's nothing to do here anyway." Merlin headed straight for the door, but stopped suddenly as he reached it, looked at the little girl who was all cuddly with Alice, and said, "Then... take good care of this brat. I won't be long."

"......" Alice nodded blankly. Only after Merlin had left did she snap out of it, her mind wondering—

Was Merlin... actually caring about this kid?

He always mocked me about being a mom, yet he wasn't exactly great at it either?

This guy was so full of contradictions, showing a gentle side at the most random times.

If he liked the kid, just come hug her. Suffering in silence—who would ever know?

title: Chapter 16 — Wanted
content:
Chapter 16 — Wanted

Volume 16 · Chapter 16

Merlin stepped out of the inn, rattled by a child suddenly calling him "Dad," and clumsily got scolded by Alice.

Stepping outside, Merlin felt much lighter. He had absolutely no idea how to deal with children. It was always others catering to him. When had he ever catered to others?

Merlin decided to check out Countess Camilla's speech. Since it had become such a spectacle, it would be a pity not to go see it.

He was genuinely curious what this countess would say. If she was loved by so many people, she must have something admirable about her.

Old Alcaron had already started his mission and should have reached the lord's castle by now. Wonder if there would be any unexpected gains tonight?

Merlin blended into the crowd. Before walking a few steps, he felt someone tailing him from behind. They were continuing to watch him.

However, Merlin didn't care. Let them follow. He had no intention of doing anything wrong. As long as Old Alcaron wasn't being targeted, the plan was proceeding smoothly enough.

But shortly after Merlin left the inn, about a dozen people emerged from an alley, all wearing black robes.

"The target has left, boss. Should we make our move?" one robed figure asked.

Camilla's subordinate slowly walked from behind to the front, gazing at the inn ahead. "Go in and subdue that female adventurer. If that doesn't work, then kidnap the child at all costs. Remember, Lady Camilla wants them alive."

"Understood!" The dozens of black-robed figures knelt on one knee in unison.

"Move out. For the restoration of my race, we will not hesitate to sacrifice our lives." Camilla's subordinate issued the command. It was time to make a move against Alice and the little girl.

On the other side, Merlin followed the crowd and slowly arrived at the central area of Avignon.

There stood a majestic guillotine, a place built specifically for executing criminals.

Whenever something important happened in Avignon, announcements would be made here, not far from the chaotic slave market.

Merlin weaved through the crowd and felt like almost the entire population of Avignon had come. It showed just how influential this female lord was.

Among them were大量 homeless refugees, looking completely out of place compared to everyone else.

Although the sun had already set, the sky dark and dim, the torches carried by the common folk lit the area bright as day.

A sharp horse neigh rang out, and several knights clad in armor and red cloaks galloped toward them on their magnificent steeds, constantly shouting:

"Make way! Make way! Do not block the lord's convoy!"

Several knights dispersed the crowd. Their fierce tone made the citizens fearful, and the dense throng automatically parted to create a passage for Camilla's personal guards.

These were merely the vanguard knights. To ensure the route was clear, they needed everyone off the procession path.

Merlin, blending into the crowd, glanced around and thought: the lord's procession was so grand. It was almost comparable to a royal parade!

With the shrill blast of a horn, a vast and stately procession slowly emerged. Their neat formation showed disciplined training.

Armored cavalry riding at the front led the way. Though pale-faced, their eyes were fierce, like elites who had survived countless battles.

An ornate carriage drawn by eight horses entered everyone's field of view. Camilla, wearing a long dress, stood at the topmost position, waving to the crowds on both sides.

"Lord Camilla!"

"Camilla!"

"Our wise lord!"

The moment Camilla appeared, the crowd fell into a frenzy, endlessly chanting her name. If the guards hadn't been holding them back, many people would have gone forward to kneel and worship.

Merlin frowned slightly. From deep within the crowd, he felt the fervent emotion surging. He had never imagined so many people would revere this female lord so intensely. It was like a cult leader at a massive pyramid scheme.

The gorgeous carriage stopped at the center. After Camilla stepped down, she climbed onto the raised platform. The sea of people continued chanting her name.

"Camilla! Camilla! Camilla!"

The waves of sound grew louder and louder. Everyone was swept up in the emotion, supporting and adoring the mistress of Avignon.

Camilla raised her hand, signaling for everyone to quiet down. Seeing the people settle down, she slowly began to speak.

Through the amplification barrier built into the venue, every word Camilla spoke was heard by all.

"Good evening, citizens of Avignon. We haven't met in quite a while, have we? Recent matters have kept me busy, and I couldn't address the problems troubling Avignon immediately. But today, I will give everyone a satisfactory answer."

No sooner had Camilla finished speaking than protest voices erupted from below. This resentment had been building for a long time; many people harbored anger.

"Drive the refugees out!"

"Yeah, drive them out! This is our city!"

"Avignon doesn't welcome refugees!!!"

For a moment, the crowd was in an uproar. There were no shortage of people who resented Camilla's decision to accept refugees, especially the slave owners.

As the largest slave exchange in France, Avignon naturally needed massive resources to sustain the slaves. The arrival of refugees was equivalent to occupying living space.

Every slave was worth a considerable sum of money, so it was only natural that this would spark such strong opposition.

Camilla coldly watched the protesters below. Bringing in refugees was merely to increase the vampires' prey; it was in no way an act of compassion.

But these slave owners' protests were effectively interfering with the blood clan's restoration, so Camilla's mood certainly wasn't good.

"Everyone, be quiet!" Camilla rebuked sharply. She looked at the protesting crowd below and said coldly, "This wasn't some bad deed done for ulterior motives, but rather an act of compassion. The Goddess of Light said we should treat the world with mercy. Turning a blind eye to those in dire hardship would be a betrayal of our faith! Besides, one day we too may suffer hardship. Do you also wish others to ignore you when you're in distress?"

At these words, the protests were instantly suppressed, because the vast majority of the people were followers of the Church of Light. Once the doctrine was invoked, they would乖乖ly comply.

Furthermore, Camilla's words were reasonable and emotionally compelling, leaving no room for rebuttal. Many people actually strongly agreed with her charitable act, so these protest voices could be easily ignored.

Below, Merlin saw the initial protest voices weaken considerably and couldn't help but think: this female lord sure knew how to whitewash herself. Was she portraying herself as a savior?

At that moment, an elderly man from among the refugees walked forward. He slowly approached the base of the platform, knelt on both knees, and pitifully said, "My lord, please have mercy on me. My granddaughter has gone missing. I've already reported it to the guards, but they wouldn't help. I beg you, my lord, show some compassion and help me find her."

"Yes! My own child has been missing for a long time too. No one cares whether we live or die!"

"My lord! Please help us!"

Chaotic voices erupted from among the refugee crowd. It seemed many people had children who had gone missing, and everyone began questioning Camilla about how she planned to handle this.

Camilla certainly knew where the missing children had gone. They had all been captured to her castle. Otherwise, who would let these refugees in for shelter?

"Regarding this matter, I know it very well. I've been secretly investigating the child abduction incidents recently, and today I finally have results. I know who abducted your children! Today, I am here to expose the mastermind behind all of this, issue a wanted order, and use every resource to hunt down the criminal!"

Merlin raised his eyebrows, feeling an inexplicable sense of foreboding. He caught a whiff of danger being drawn in.

Two guards carrying parchment scrolls stepped onto the platform and unfurled them. On the scrolls were portraits, and they were unmistakably Merlin and Alice!

"I have thoroughly investigated. They are human traffickers from Britannia who have been in Avignon for some time. The frequently missing children are all their doing. They are the criminals who abducted your children!" Camilla declared firmly, announcing to everyone that Merlin and Alice were wanted criminals.

Standing in the crowd, Merlin's eyes widened. He instinctively lowered his head, unable to believe what he was hearing.

What the hell! Why are they framing us?!

Those were clearly the mercenary guild's dirty deeds!

This was an attempt to incite the masses, to use the commoners against them!

Once the two portraits were released, they would quickly spread across all of France. By then, everyone would know Alice and Merlin were wanted criminals.

Moving around in France would surely become extremely difficult. They couldn't even hope to get through this period peacefully.

The refugees, having waited a long time without seeing the lord appear, originally thought she was privately investigating the children's disappearances. They were overwhelmingly moved and their admiration for Camilla had sunk into their bones.

"They should be hanged!"

"Yeah! Kill them!"

"Give back our children!!!"

Curses and denunciations erupted from the crowd, piling filth upon Merlin and Alice. Many undoubtedly felt an urge to grab a hoe and go settle this themselves.

"These two openly present themselves as adventurers, but in secret they engage in despicable dealings. In just a few months, they have trafficked hundreds of children. They are truly irredeemable!" Camilla said mournfully and sternly. "I have already issued a nationwide wanted order. Whoever captures these two fugitives, or provides important clues, will be rewarded with 200,000 gold coins! So act now! Take revenge for your children! Unless they die, our rage cannot be appeased!"

"Lord Camilla is wise and just!"

Someone shouted, instantly igniting the fury in everyone's hearts. They fell into a state of excited irrationality.

The pain of losing loved ones transformed into boundless motivation. Every refugee wanted to kill Merlin and Alice, having lost the ability to think clearly.

Merlin, bowing his head, gritted his teeth and thought: because we didn't comply with Camilla's wishes, they're targeting us like this? And using the people's trust as well. What a cunning bastard.

On the raised platform, Camilla glanced at Merlin below. She had actually spotted him arriving long ago but had simply pretended not to notice.

Camilla wore a contemptuous smile, slowly turned around, and prepared to leave. The crowd's fury had already been ignited. That was more than enough.

Lucifer III. Still too young, after all.

Sometimes force alone can accomplish nothing.

It was like quicksand; the more you struggle, the deeper you sink.

Since you refuse to leave, then I'll play along with you properly——

7

title: Chapter 17 — Both Fall
content:
Chapter 17 — Both Fall

Volume 16 · Chapter 17

Merlin originally wanted to turn and leave, but now the two of them have inexplicably become wanted criminals, and the angry populace, their heads clouded with fury, will surely rush to tear them apart.
Although Merlin doesn't care about the lives of the populace, having him carry out a massacre and slaughter the weak and innocent goes against his original intention.
Moreover, even if Alice is now framed as a criminal who abducted children, she would absolutely not vent her anger on ordinary civilians; she would surely choose
Merlin, considering Alice's feelings, had no choice but to avoid trouble and leave; in such a critical time, it's better to avoid causing problems.
Camilla, you bastard, actually framed us?
Do you really think that just because you're a lord, I wouldn't dare to act?
Merlin's brows knotted tightly; he involuntarily grew irritable, feeling he needed to go back and briefly discuss with Alice what to do.
If possible, Merlin would really like to just kill that female lord—pouring dirty water on him for no reason—this already counts as bullying him.
Now, if they continue to stay in Avignon, it's already very dangerous; if Merlin and Alice's residence is exposed, it will surely draw a large crowd of pursuers wielding torches to burn them.
After all, the populace's thinking ability is limited; they are easily provoked and used, truly shrewd people are few, and one cannot control everyone's thoughts.
Hearing the angry curses of the surrounding populace, Merlin's face darkened; he lowered his head, wanting to leave, but after just a few steps he was recognized.
"You look like a wanted criminal?"
"Seems like just... ah"
"It's him! The wanted criminal is here!"
I don't know who shouted, but instantly everyone in the square heard it; a dark crowd surged here, blocking Merlin's path.
Countless people surrounded Merlin, sizing him up with their eyes, and within a few seconds they recognized him as the person from the recent wanted notice!
In an instant the crowd exploded, the suppressed anger fully erupting; many surged forward to grab Merlin's clothes, lamentingly questioning.
"Give my child back!"
"You laid hands on a child—are you still human?!"
"You British pig, you should be shoved onto the stake! ! !"
Merlin was being pulled this way and that by many people, yet he kept his head down and stayed silent, waves of anger rising inside him.
These idiots, just because of a few slanderous words from Camilla, have decided I'm the mastermind behind abducting their children!
Indeed, the populace easily becomes a tool for others, completely unaware they're becoming accomplices.
Camilla's ploy of using a knife to kill is quite good—does she want to make it impossible for me and Alice to stay in Avignon?
Merlin's face gradually darkened; his clothes were about to be ripped apart by the angry crowd, and he could no longer hold back.
"All of you, get lost!"
Merlin flipped the katana at his waist 180°, drew it out slightly, and instantly released a non-lethal killing sword aura!
The sudden shockwave sent the civilians near Merlin flying; it created a safety zone where no one dared to step.
This draw‑slash is a blade‑back strike; it won't kill, but serious injury is unavoidable.
The civilians blown away by the shock spat blood, rolling on the ground in agony.
Seeing this, the other civilians became much more subdued, not daring to step forward and provoke Merlin; seeing his grim face, they felt he might unleash a massacre at any moment.
Merlin held the katana horizontally before his chest, lifted his darkened face, looked around, and spoke in a very solemn tone—
"You guys are really annoying"
"If you dare to come forward and harass me again, I won't be polite."
"You might lose your life; I won't take responsibility."
"I'll say this once: I have never abducted children; your enemy is not me!"
On the other side.
Alice had no idea what was happening outside; she was still happily interacting with the little girl.
"Mommy! Mommy! Hug me!" the little girl said, coquettishly.
"What a clingy little
Alice laughed as she picked up the little girl and tentatively asked, "What would you like for dinner?"
"Anything Mom makes, I like." the little girl said in a very pleasant voice.
"Let's go out and buy something to eat today—do you like cake?" Seeing the little baby so obedient and cute, Alice decided to buy some sweets for her today, and wondered if, when she herself had a child in the future, she could be this obedient.
"Like!" the little girl cheered happily; indeed, she still loves sweets in her heart.
"Mommy will take you to eat the best cream strawberry cake." Alice held the little girl and walked toward the door, not intending to stay inside; after all, it was mealtime and the child was also hungry.
However, just as Alice was holding the child and quickly walking to the door, the room's door was suddenly forced open with brute force, making a loud "bang".
Dozens of black‑clad people appeared outside the door, blocking the exit; everyone's eyes turned toward Alice, especially the child she was holding.
Alice didn't react properly; she instinctively stepped back, moving toward the slender sword she had placed on the table, ready to draw and counterattack if things went wrong.
Faced with the sudden black‑clad men, Alice was full of vigilance; using such violent means to break in, no matter how you look at it they aren't good people—she didn't know who sent them or what their purpose was.
"Who are you?! You barged in without permission—has nobody taught you manners?! ?"
Seeing so many strangers outside the door, the little girl shrank back into Alice's arms, feeling that this group was very dangerous.
The black‑clad men said nothing; they surged forward, flipped back their black robes, and drew dual crescent‑moon curved blades.
They didn't waste words; drawing their weapons already showed they weren't good sorts, and they immediately launched a surround attack.
The black‑clad men's bodies flared with high‑rank battle aura; they weren't terribly strong individually, but their great numbers and coordination made them very troublesome—
Each sharp crescent‑moon blade lunged straight at Alice, the sound of tearing air—*shila‑shila*—shaking the surroundings!
Alice widened her eyes, her pupils contracting; she hadn't expected this group to say nothing and launch straight into attack.
She bent low at lightning speed while holding the child, dodging the two half‑cuts aimed at her neck, quickly retreated, and pulled the slender sword from the table.
Alice's eyes flashed with anger; having no choice but to fight while holding the child, she unleashed a barrage of golden ice shards with a backhand!
"Don't go too far!‘
*Chomp chomp chomp!* The golden ice shards were like bullets, wildly shooting at the black‑clad men, forcing them to frantically block with their blades.
However, the gap in strength between them and Alice was noticeable; several of the ice shards pierced their bodies, yet it seemed to have little effect—they stood up as if unharmed.
"Mommy!" the little girl cried out in fear, clinging tightly and not letting go; trembling from terror, her petite body shook.
Alice lowered her head to look at the little baby; seeing her frightened look made her feel a pang of pity, so she patted her back and said—
"Don't cry, don't cry, Mommy's here."
"Mommy will protect you."
S■
