title: Chapter 21 — Straight to the Castle
content:
Chapter 21 — Straight to the Castle

Volume 16 · Chapter 21

"You really can talk."

Alice responded coolly, and a cold wind surged around her, with ice shards swirling in the snowstorm. In an instant, the room was covered in a thick layer of frost, as if they were inside an ice cellar.

"You just said that I would be distracted taking care of the child and could only use a fraction of my strength. Well, let me tell you the truth—only thirty percent."

"But now I’m going all out to kill you. Do you think you can still land those sneaky attacks like before?"

"Then let’s see about that. The number of adventurers dying by my hand today might just increase by one!" The subordinate of Camilla, whose face was already twisted, now smiled even more sinisterly.

The shadow beneath Camilla’s subordinate came to life, spreading across the entire floor of the room. Countless shadowy spikes erupted from the ground, dense and inescapable. It was clear that Camilla’s subordinate intended to pierce Alice through like a honeycomb, and the sheer number made evasion impossible!

However, though Camilla’s subordinate was a Saint-tier powerhouse, they clearly hadn’t reached the peak of that tier. Without the little girl holding her back, the vast gap in strength between them became immediately apparent.

Alice moved at least ten times faster than before. The moment the shadowy spikes struck, she vanished from sight.

"Huh?!" Camilla’s subordinate’s eyes widened, cold sweat beading on their forehead. *So fast!* They couldn’t sense her presence at all. This woman’s strength was extraordinary—if the child hadn’t been a burden earlier, they might have already been wiped out!

"Where are you looking?" Alice appeared behind Camilla’s subordinate, her silver-white holy sword already piercing through their chest.

"Ugh—! You—" Camilla’s subordinate stared in horror at the blade protruding from their chest, their mind reeling. They had thought they could capture Alice and earn great merit, but now they realized they had overestimated themselves. Their opponent was far stronger, no weaker than Lady Camilla herself!

"Since we’ve come to France, we won’t allow you and your kind to continue your evil deeds in the shadows!" Alice channeled more magic and fighting spirit through her rapier, pouring it directly into Camilla’s subordinate’s body.

"AAAAAAAAH—!!!" The subordinate let out a bloodcurdling scream as flames erupted from the wound in their chest, quickly spreading across their entire body.

Alice’s rapier, *Hymn of Light*, was the bane of dark creatures. Against bloodline beings, it was as effective as silver, its divine power overwhelming even the vampires’ unnatural regenerative abilities.

In moments, Camilla’s subordinate was burned alive, reduced to a pile of black ash scattered on the ground, as if they had never existed at all.

◆

Alice let out a long breath, sheathed her rapier, and immediately rushed out, her face filled with worry. She feared the little girl might be in danger.

*Hopefully they haven’t gone far. Hopefully I can still catch up...*

Meanwhile, in the plaza.

In the darkness, eerie flames flickered continuously, and beast-like howls echoed endlessly.

The over 300 vampires, who had been ferocious moments ago, were soon "educated" by Merlin’s own hand.

The iaijutsu strikes from Merlin’s holy silver greatsword were lethally effective against these bloodline beings with their extraordinary regenerative abilities.

The snarling vampires, flapping their membranous wings, were cut in half at the waist one after another, turning to ash and disappearing.

Merlin’s iaijutsu was not only swift but also executed with incredible frequency, repeatedly drawing and sheathing his blade.

The relentless iaijutsu strikes caught the vampires completely off guard. One by one, they fell from the sky, their fate sealed without a shred of suspense.

One vampire, severely wounded by an iaijutsu strike, crawled slowly on the ground, leaving a shocking trail of blood as it clutched its chest, where flames were spreading. It was desperate to survive.

Merlin, however, walked over at a leisurely pace, stepped on its head with one foot, and plunged the holy silver greatsword into its back with a *thunk*.

"Disappear, you filthy pest."

"AAAAAAAAH—!!!"

The poor vampire’s eyes widened in terror. The holy silver greatsword was far too brutal against its kind—it couldn’t resist the divine power at all. Its entire body burst into flames, and with a *whoosh*, it turned to ash. The entire knightly order of 300 vampires met its end in total annihilation.

As the last embers faded, Merlin sheathed his holy silver greatsword. *Thank goodness I brought this silver weapon.* Without it, dealing with the bloodline’s world-class regenerative abilities would have been quite troublesome.

The regenerative abilities of the bloodline were undeniable. Among all the races Merlin had encountered, none could compare. As long as they weren’t completely exterminated, a single drop of blood could restore them entirely—truly monstrous.

Even if Merlin unleashed his full-power iaijutsu, he wouldn’t have been able to reduce the vampires to nothing. The holy silver weapon made things much easier.

In the past, when Merlin faced enemies with regenerative abilities, he had always used overwhelmingly brutal methods to shatter their limits of recovery.

Merlin wiped the blood splattered on his face and surveyed the empty surroundings before locking his gaze on the ominous castle towering over Avignon.

Since the guards sent here were all vampires, that Countess Camilla was probably no saint either. If that was the case, then he could strike without hesitation. Even if he killed this noblewoman, it didn’t seem like it would be a problem.

Merlin was rubbing his chin in thought, considering his next move, when Alice suddenly rushed over, her face flushed with panic.

"Merlin! Something’s happened!" Alice had been searching for a long time but found no trace of the black-clad figures. She had no idea where they had gone. Now the child was missing, and she was nearly frantic with worry.

"Huh?! What?" Merlin didn’t know the situation, but seeing Alice so distressed, he realized it must be serious. She rarely ever looked this panicked.

"The child! The child was taken by vampires!" Alice ran up to Merlin, panting heavily, her chest heaving.

"Hmm? You encountered vampires too?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"Eh?! Wait—did you—" Alice froze for a moment, as if realizing something.

Merlin lowered his head, frowning. *Both of us encountered bloodline beings? That’s no coincidence.* It was all a setup!

They were clearly trying to separate us. Their goal must have been the child. Did they know how strong I am?

If that’s true, then we’ve fallen for a classic diversion. Those vampire knights were just sent to tie me down.

Merlin grew agitated, his mood no better than Alice’s. The child’s abduction added another layer of concern.

"Merlin, what do we do? The child’s been taken! She’s already had such a hard life, and now this... She’ll definitely be treated cruelly. How pitiful..." Alice’s voice grew more emotional as she spoke, her eyes beginning to glisten, a glassy sheen forming over them as her lashes fluttered rapidly.

"Tch! What’s with the panic? Aren’t you her stand-in mother? Why are you falling apart like this?" Merlin chided, hoping to calm her down.

"Sorry... I’m just so worried about her. It’s all my fault for being too cautious and letting the enemy—" Alice forced herself to suppress her grief, trying to regain her composure.

"What good does it do to talk about that now?" Merlin lifted his head, gazing at the dark castle under the moonlight, his killing intent surging. "Come on. We’re going to the castle. Let’s kill that bitch Camilla!"

"We can’t afford to waste any time. Every second that passes, the child is in more danger."

title: Chapter 22 — Adventurer's Courage
content:
Chapter 22 — Adventurer's Courage

Volume 16 · Chapter 22

Before the time reversal.

Old Aralon, who had not appeared until now, had sneaked into the castle long before Camilla led her personal guard away, clad in a pitch-black night suit.

With Camilla and her guards gone, the castle's defenses were exceedingly thin, and Old Aralon faced no obstacles, his youthful skills as a thief serving him well.

He threw the grappling hook directly at the second floor of the castle. Due to his advanced age, he exerted all his strength just to climb up, but managed to successfully enter the castle interior.

The moment Old Aralon landed, he warily scanned his surroundings, looking as though he was holding back a sneeze.

After confirming no one was around, he secretly exhaled. This was a room piled high with books, with a desk—it had to be Camilla's study.

Old Aralon speculated to himself, thinking it was worth investigating. After all, a lord's study should hold fairly useful information.

So Old Aralon began rummaging through drawers and cabinets, searching everywhere for anything useful. He even looked over documents.

If something important were written on them, that would be a find—but after searching for a long time, he got nothing.

The documents were all about Avignon's development, nothing worth noting.

Old Aralon straightened his aging back, his forehead drenched in sweat, utterly exhausted.

Where is it? This lord seems perfectly normal—nothing suspicious at all.

She appeared to be nothing but a wise ruler, wholeheartedly busied with Avignon's development.

Could Merlin and Alice have been wrong?

Old Aralon told himself he couldn't waver, otherwise this trip would've been a complete waste.

He shifted his target to the drawers beneath the desk, beginning to search without restraint.

Countess Camilla was likely leading a procession outside with her guard, and there wasn't much in the castle.

Even if he made some noise, he wouldn't worry—no one would bother coming upstairs for no reason.

When he pulled open the bottom drawer, Old Aralon found a black box, locked and looking very mysterious.

"Hmm..."

Old Aralon puzzled, looked at the desk, picked up the quill dipped in ink, shook off the excess ink, and jammed it into the lock, fiddling with it repeatedly.

He pressed his ear close to the lock, listening to the faint sounds inside, his expression shifting continuously.

"Click." Everything sprang open. Old Aralon truly was a veteran of petty theft in his youth; he could open a lock with a quill pen.

He carefully pried the lid open and discovered letters inside, so he picked one up and roughly skimmed through it—

"Camilla, our father is about to awaken, but the ritual still requires a large number of humans as sacrifices. I hope you'll assist me further. This is a critical moment for the revival of our clan. Please take it seriously..."

Old Aralon's heart sank as he read it, starting to catch on. Though he couldn't fully grasp it, the need for a large number of human sacrifices was highly suspicious!

Combined with the rumors of bizarre disappearances in Avignon—if those kidnapped people didn't go to some sort of ritual sacrifice, then where did they go?

Old Aralon pondered, a cold sweat breaking out across his back. Things were looking dire. This letter was from France, involving Medes—the implications were enormous.

If the Empire's chancellor were secretly connected to the bizarre disappearances, wouldn't all of France be trapped in some kind of conspiracy?

It seemed Merlin and Alice hadn't misjudged. It wasn't just Camilla—Medes was also deeply abnormal. He had to go back and discuss this!

Realizing the gravity of the situation, Old Aralon quickly stuffed the letter into his chest and stealthily tried to slip back out the way he came.

He had already obtained fairly convincing evidence. There was no need to keep risking his life in the castle. If he ran into any patrolling guards, it would be disastrous. Besides, according to his calculations, Camilla would be back soon.

Old Aralon sprang up in a hurry, intending to escape through the window using the grappling hook. But the moment he poked his head out, he spotted a patrol guard below.

Old Aralon was terrified. He hastily pulled the grappling hook back up to avoid detection, closed the window, and hid, trying not to be discovered.

Old Aralon sweated profusely, his little heart pounding erratically. He felt there was no way to escape for now. But Camilla was about to return. Could he choose to hide in the castle and wait for an opportunity to flee?

No choice. Better to hide in the castle first and see if there's another exit.

The castle gates burst open as Camilla had already returned with her procession.

She went straight to the main hall. Dozens of figures in black had already come back.

The little girl had been subdued by the men in black, her mouth covered so she couldn't speak, her tearful eyes pitiful. She was surely devastated from being forcibly separated from her mother.

"Is everything ready?" Camilla asked directly.

"Yes, my lord. The entire castle has been sealed with barriers. Lucifer III will surely fall into the trap if he follows us," one of the men in black said respectfully.

"Very good." Camilla nodded, then looked at the little girl and asked with a smile, "So this is their child?"

"Yes, we grabbed her with our own hands," the man in black replied.

"Good work. The plan is proceeding smoothly, and the initiative is in our hands." Camilla smiled, very satisfied with the current situation. Nothing unexpected had gone wrong.

The little girl felt abject terror at the sight of Camilla. Her tiny body trembled uncontrollably, too afraid to even lift her head.

Camilla pulled the little girl into her arms, lifted her chin, and displayed a greedy expression. "What a lovely child. I bet her blood tastes delicious~"

"Why are you crying? That look breaks my heart. Don't worry, your mother will be here soon. You just need to be obedient," Camilla said meaningfully, not showing her ruthless side.

The little girl sensed Camilla was no good person. Overcome with fear, she dared not speak much, only struggling frantically with her small hands, clearly resisting the strange woman holding her.

All of this was witnessed by Old Aralon, who had been hiding in the shadows. He had intended to find a way to escape, but once he left the study, he discovered Camilla had already returned. All his misfortunes had converged at once.

The castle was inexplicably surrounded by guards, protecting the place like an iron bucket. There was simply no escape, as if someone were expected to storm the castle?

With no other option, Old Aralon could only patiently hide. But then he heard the familiar sound of a child crying from the main hall, so he偷偷 stole a glance.

Wasn't this the child Merlin and Alice had brought back? How did she end up captured here?

It's over. Things have only grown more complicated. Not only was he taking action, but Camilla was no pushover either—she had already set things in motion!

Old Aralon's face twisted in sheer terror. He desperately wanted to rescue the hostage girl. Who knew what Cartel Camilla would do to the child, having colluded with human traffickers?

But his strength as a Black Iron adventurer was far too weak. The dozens of men in black were all elites, and Camilla was present as well. If he went out, he would certainly die!

However, though Old Aralon was very cowardly and an inconspicuous nobody, and had been a thief in his youth, his character was absolutely not that of a bad person. His passion for adventure had always been unwavering...

"Do you want to be a coward for the rest of your life, or do you want to be a hero? Even if only for a few minutes?"

That was Old Aralon's final thought. He drew the hand crossbow at his waist and, steeling his nerves, charged bravely forward.

Though the old man's figure was clumsy, his form radiated a light that even Merlin had never possessed—the shining brilliance belonging to all adventurers....

title: Chapter 23 — Hostage
content:
Chapter 23 — Hostage

Volume 16 · Chapter 23

Old Akaron raised his crossbow and immediately began firing at the distant Camilla, attempting to pin down the lord.

With the sound of the crossbow bolts whizzing, eight arrows accurately shot toward Camilla's eyes.

"Who?" Camilla wasn't some weak vampire; her strength was genuinely Saint-tier and very powerful.

She merely turned her head slightly, and with just a glance, all the arrows suspended in the air in front of her, unable to advance even an inch.

Old Akaron stood firm, bearing the pressure and loudly scolding, "Return the child! You despicable bastard!"

Camilla examined Old Akaron, his all-black nightclothes clearly indicating he was a thief.

"Haha, what was I thinking? So you're the mouse that sneaked in? Invading my territory, are you unaware of death?"

"Shut up! You幕后 mastermind, conspiring with Prime Minister Medes to kidnap humans for evil rituals, I will definitely expose your crimes to the public!" Old Akaron angrily scolded, appearing very tough on the surface, but in reality, he was terrified inside because the crossbow had already run out of bolts, only eight had been fired.

"Oh? You old geezer know quite a lot, so it's even more impossible for you to leave alive. But it's really a pity, your aged body doesn't even qualify to be food. Disappear, don't be a nuisance here."

As soon as Camilla finished speaking, the arrows suspended in front of her all turned around, pointing directly at Old Akaron, the intention was very clear.

With the sound of the arrows piercing the air, all eight bolts returned, shooting out toward Old Akaron's body.

Puh puh puh, the arrows pierced the flesh, Old Akaron let out a painful and凄厉 scream, his aged body flying backward, his fate unknown.

It was a completely one-sided battle, just a single exchange, Old Akaron had already lost. Having just气势 is not enough to solve problems.

The little girl saw how惨 Old Akaron was, her heart became even more afraid, she couldn't even breathe, her small body shook even more violently.

After dealing with the little mouse Old Akaron, Camilla originally wanted to prepare more, watching Merlin and Alice come to their own doom.

But unexpectedly, the other party was so fast, the two had already killed into the castle--

The sound of fighting and various beast-like screams echoed outside, followed by the heavy door being kicked open with one foot.

Merlin and Alice had both arrived, standing menacingly outside the door, clearly not intending to let this go.

Some vampire corpses lay beside them, slowly burning and turning into ashes.

Almost all enemies in the castle who dared to block their path had been killed clean!

Camilla wasn't at all panicky, instead she was happily welcoming them, everything was exactly as she had expected.

"Coming to my castle so late, should I welcome you or drive you away?"

"Mommy! Mommy!" The little girl held in Camilla's embrace saw Alice and immediately became excited, continuously calling out "Mommy."

"Baby...." Alice heard the little girl call her mommy, the fire in her heart instantly turned into infinite tenderness, wanting to take the child back.

Merlin saw Alice so unsteady, quickly stopped her and said seriously, "Stay calm, we've killed our way here, but the other party isn't the least bit panicky, still looking confident, probably already well-prepared. Don't easily fall into the trap."

"But... but the child is still in her hands." Alice glared at Camilla with hatred, wanting to fight this wicked woman to the death.

"What good is being in a hurry? It will only make you sink deeper into the mud." Merlin said earnestly, hoping Alice wouldn't be emotional at this time, otherwise she would be exploited by others.

Alice suppressed the fire in her heart, feeling Merlin was right, the other party was so confident, clearly not afraid at all.

"What are the two of you whispering about? Are you discussing how to deal with me?" Camilla asked with interest.

"Shut up! Return the child!" Alice angrily pointed her sword at Camilla, the fire in her chest boiling.

"Want to get your child back? Of course, come and try, Miss Alice,......" Camilla looked at Merlin with profound meaning and said,

"The Demon Lord's arrogant king, Lucifer......"

"Er!" Alice was shocked, her eyes widening, for a moment she thought she had heard wrong, why would the female lord of Avignon know Merlin's true identity? And prepared to call out his name!

Merlin chuckled dryly, looking up and saying, "Indeed, you know my true identity, from the beginning I felt suspicious, it was like intentionally leading me away from Alice's side, just to catch that child and blackmail us? Normally no one would consider me a threat, yet they were trying their best to avoid me, if they didn't understand my extraordinary strength, they wouldn't go through so much trouble."

"Exactly so, I wouldn't be foolish enough to confront a monster who could easily cut down the Church's ten thousand Crusade Army head-on. Since my strength is inferior to yours, suppressing you from other aspects is the same." Camilla pinched the little girl's cheek, sneering, "Now the trump card is in my hands, your child is the soft underbelly, I will make full use of it, making you obediently become my puppets!"

"......" Merlin sighed, helplessly thinking, what was this woman thinking? This child wasn't his and Alice's, he and her wouldn't have a biological child, they were different races after all.

"Delusional! You bunch of evil vampires, we came to France to definitely eradicate you completely!" Alice heard the other party wanted to use the child to blackmail her and Merlin, instantly angry to the point of trembling shoulders, feeling the other party was truly despicable, it was the first time she encountered such a troublesome enemy using psychological warfare.

"Haha, what a joke, our great bloodline has been rooted in France for thousands of years, do you really think you can eradicate us? Even one of the seven main leaders of the demon race would have to bow to us!" Camilla, with the little girl in hand, was no longer afraid of Merlin at all.

"Talking with such confidence? I hope you don't regret it......" Merlin frowned, gripping the holy silver greatsword, thinking whether to draw it and kill this female lord now.

"Aren't you very eager to save this cute child? Then come and try, in my territory, no one has ever left unscathed, you are no exception." Camilla boasted arrogantly.

"Kill! Die!" Alice could no longer hold back, she forcefully kicked the marble floor, shattering it, her whole body like an arrow shot from the bow, shooting out and raising a storm below zero degrees!

Dozens of black-cloaked men behind Camilla instantly rushed out to attack, their curved swords flashing with cold light, all jointly attacking Alice!

"Get out of the way!" Alice cursed, her fine sword unstoppable, fiercely swinging, beheading the dozens of black-cloaked men!

The sacred aura made these vampires suffer immensely, they self-ignited and turned into ashes.

Such high-level enemies were like a mantis trying to block the path of Alice at the peak of Saint-tier, it was nothing but a death wish!

Earlier, Alice had to suppress her strength due to worrying about the cold air harming the little girl, but now she was firing at full power without any reservations, could these little shrimps possibly block her?

"Really dared to attack? Are you not afraid I'll kill this child? Is it really okay?" Camilla quickly grabbed the little girl's neck, threatening Alice.

"Er!......" Alice felt very angry, but had to stop, daring not to get any closer to Camilla, fearing she would kill the little baby in a rage.

"Umm, Mommy......" The little girl shed tears, looking very scared, Camilla's nails had already scratched her neck skin, a trickle of blood flowed out.

"Hahahaha......" Camilla laughed wantonly, kidnapping the little girl was indeed very useful, so she proudly said,

"If you're still worried about this child's life, then obey me!"

"Because of your momentary impulse, if I twist this child's neck......"

"That's your parental responsibility, no matter how much you atone, you can never make up for the guilt in your heart!"

"You will struggle with regret until death, never forgetting the pain of indirectly burying your own flesh and blood!

title: Chapter 24 — Transfer
content:
Chapter 24 — Transfer

Volume 16 · Chapter 24

“Shout!” Alice had to control her emotions. Every word Camilla said was like a pearl of wisdom, all of it things that made her feel worried. If she insisted on causing a conflict and the little girl died because of it, that would be a sin she could never wash away.

Merlin, seeing the standoff had reached an impasse, was also getting a bit anxious. He wanted to spit at Camilla. Although the aphrodisiac effect could temporarily make her lose her senses, it couldn’t control her thoughts.

The enemy might twist the little girl’s neck the moment they sensed something was wrong. That move was dangerous and a bit of a loss.

Merlin thought for a moment and could only choose to make the other side panic. He had to clarify that this child wasn’t his or Alice’s biological daughter. The threat was useless.

“Give it up. This child isn’t ours at all. We found her in the dungeon of a mercenary group. Trying to use her to hold us back, I think you should save your breath.”

“Oh? Is that so?”

Camilla looked at the little girl she was holding, and it seemed she really didn’t look like them. She suddenly felt a bit anxious.

Could it be true? This child wasn’t their biological daughter? She was adopted?

If that were really the case, then wasn’t she just wasting her efforts for nothing!?

If it wasn’t their blood, then even if she died, they wouldn’t be worried, right?

Camilla’s eyes flickered with a hint of tension. She was worried the child in her arms wouldn’t be enough to restrain the other side. If that were the case, her own fate would probably be terrible.

“I won’t easily believe what others say. You, Lucifer III, aren’t you very strong? Then try it. Cut me and this child down together.”

“Mom…” The little girl was suffocating from Camilla’s grip but dared not move, looking very passive.

“If you want to die, don’t drag others down with you!” Alice scolded in a fit of rage.

Merlin narrowed his eyes, gripping the sacred silver tachi, and asked tentatively, “Do you think I won’t?”

“Exactly. Don’t hesitate. Draw your sword. Let me see how cold-blooded a demon can really be. Haha… Camilla appeared very relaxed on the surface, mocking coldly, but in her heart, she wasn’t very confident. But now she was on a tiger she couldn’t get off, so she had to take a gamble. She bet that this child was very important to them. As long as the other side had even a slight wish not to see the little girl die, she would have an opportunity to take advantage!

“I hate it when others provoke me…”

Merlin said coldly, his eyes gradually turning cold, and a desire to draw his sword surged within him.

Would he dare to cut down both the little girl and Camilla together? Of course he would. He wouldn’t hesitate too much.

But Merlin didn’t really want this child to die for no reason. However, if the situation became too tense, he would become cold-blooded.

Merlin could recall the expression on the child’s face when she called him “Dad,” timid and nervous. But it was just a joke, and he hadn’t taken it seriously.

If Camilla created too much of a threat and the little girl became an obstacle, he would kill both of them together.

Although Merlin would also feel very guilty, someone had to play the villain, and he would do it.

“If you want to die so much, I’ll send you on your way!”

The sacred silver tachi unsheathed slightly, and a deadly sword qi immediately erupted. The surrounding walls were cut with dense notches and grooves.

The sword qi stirred up a wind as sharp as a knife, like a howling demon, ready to kill both Camilla and the little girl!

“Er!? Are you crazy? This child will die too!” Camilla’s eyes widened, sweat beaded on her forehead, and she panicked, thinking, No way? Lucifer III is really cold-blooded to this extent? This child isn’t even their biological daughter. Now is he going to kill me at all costs?!

“Mommy!” The little girl struggled in fear but was held tightly in Camilla’s arms.

The deadly sword qi ravaged the area. As soon as Merlin drew his sword, the destructive power would destroy everything in front of him.

Even if Camilla had an amazing self-healing ability, she couldn’t withstand the draw slash of the sacred silver tachi.

However, just as the atmosphere became extremely tense, the fierce sword qi suddenly retracted and returned to calmness.

“Alice! What are you doing? Are you not in your right mind?” Merlin’s eyes widened as he looked at Alice, thinking this person didn’t know how dangerous it was to stand in front of him when he was about to draw his sword.

Alice had somehow stood in front of Merlin. If he unleashed the draw slash, it would cut Alice as well. “You’re the one who’s not in your right mind. Do you really want to kill that child together?”

“What other options are there? Rather than being held back by this贱 woman, it’s better to cut through the mess quickly. If you’re not willing to do it, then let me do it.” Merlin shrugged his shoulders, appearing indifferent on the surface, but in reality, he was under a lot of psychological pressure.

“Merlin! That child didn’t do anything wrong. Do you think that’s reasonable? To achieve your goal at any cost? That’s too much, isn’t it?”

Alice seriously stopped Merlin.

“We are different. You are human, and I am a demon. Don’t impose your thoughts on me.” Merlin frowned, not very happy about Alice’s interference.

“Yes, we are different. No matter what you did in the past, I can accept it and won’t ask questions. But things are different now…” Alice turned her head to look at Camilla, her back to Merlin. “Promise me, don’t be forced into becoming a bad person.”

“Tsk!”

Merlin furrowed his brows. Hearing Alice’s meaning, she didn’t want him to get involved and wanted him to let her handle it. Saying more was useless, so he could only sheathe the half-drawn blade.

“What exactly do you want? What do we have to do to let that child go?” Alice stood alone in front of Camilla.

“Hahaha…”

Camilla laughed wildly, her mouth stretching to her ears, overjoyed.

For a moment just now, she really thought she was doomed and couldn’t escape!

Unbelievably, this female adventurer had finally stepped forward. No wonder she was the woman who married magic. Lucifer III valued her more than the child.

Camilla exhaled in relief. Since the other side still cared about the child’s safety, she could make good use of that.

“I thought you were really cold-blooded and didn’t care about the child at all. Turns out you’re still very worried about this little cutie’s safety?”

“Since you care about her, then just obey my orders. I’ll let her go…”

“Speak, what do you want?” Alice’s emotions were much more stable now, deciding to prioritize rescuing the little girl.

“Take a few steps forward. I’ve set up a teleportation magic array here. You and I will leave here.” Camilla grabbed the little girl’s neck and looked at Merlin, saying, “As for Lucifer III? You’re not allowed to follow. Otherwise, you know what will happen.”

“Hey! Don’t go alone into such an obvious trap.” Alice wasn’t very willing for Alice to go alone; it was too dangerous.

“Merlin, I’ll leave with her. You don’t follow.” Alice said and directly walked into Camilla, stepping into the teleportation magic array.

“Are you serious?!” Merlin’s expression was surprised. Was Alice really going to save the child at the cost of her own life?

“Don’t worry, I’ll be fine.” Alice turned her head and smiled at Merlin.

“Good.”

As soon as Camilla’s words fell, the pre-arranged teleportation magic array lit up, ready to teleport her and Alice to another place, completely cutting off contact with Merlin.

In the second before being teleported away, Camilla looked at the shocked Merlin and said in an extremely sinister tone—

“Lucifer III, although you are very powerful, what does that matter? You’re still being led by the nose by me.”

“Just stay here nicely. I’ve specially prepared a gift for you!”

“I’ll be kind and give you a warning. Be serious. If you’re a little careless, you’ll lose your life.”

“Hahaha”

(V')ψ

title: Chapter 25 — Miranda's Whereabouts
content:
Chapter 25 — Miranda's Whereabouts

Volume 16 · Chapter 25

“Alice!!!”

Merlin shouted, but suddenly a fierce gust of wind rose inside the castle, making it impossible to open his eyes.

After the wind subsided, Alice and Camilla had vanished from the spot, and even the little girl had disappeared.

The teleportation magic circle had been set up in advance; Merlin had no idea where they had been sent, which inevitably made him anxious!

Merlin clicked his tongue, just about to leave, when the whole castle began to shake, with rumbling sounds like it could collapse at any moment—apparently after Camilla left, some trap had been triggered.

Recalling Camilla’s last words, it seemed she had prepared something unpleasant for him; could she intend to bury him alive here? That was too naïve.

Just as Merlin was about to turn around and take out the castle, he noticed something off—several drops of liquid fell on his face; he touched them and found they were bright red.

Immediately, with a “puff”-like boom, Camilla’s castle began to melt, turning into a surging river of blood that swept Merlin in, sending him drifting with the flow.

He didn’t know whether Camilla knew his weakness or it was just a blind cat hitting a dead rat, but the surging blood river instantly robbed Merlin of his combat ability, leaving him only able to struggle desperately to avoid drowning.

Merlin was swept away by the torrent of blood, rushing toward the castle’s extension; he covered his mouth and gulped several large mouthfuls of the water, which carried an extremely strong fishy stench!

Suddenly appearing, the turbulent blood river placed Merlin in an extremely passive state; unable to swim, he could not resist and could only go with the current.

Merlin exerted all his strength to surface, gasping heavily, feeling as if he were about to die, seeing the blood water carrying him to some unknown place—apparently the deepest part of the castle.

In the center of the blood river was a vortex-like thing, frantically swallowing the water; he didn’t know what device Camilla had prepared, but it gave him an ominous feeling, as all the water converged toward it.

Merlin quickly realized something was wrong and tried to break free from the blood river’s control, but unable to swim, he had no means in the water and was directly swallowed by the vortex...

Midnight, the capital of France.

The residence of Chancellor Mades, located in the most prosperous part of the imperial capital.

Now the old king is bedridden, and the true ruler of the empire is precisely this chancellor.

Mades manages both major and minor mistakes, almost having taken control of the entire empire, moving toward the position of regent.

Yet there remain many obstacles: Princess Margaret is the old king’s sole heir and likewise holds considerable power.

If the old king encounters any trouble, this land of France will welcome its first queen in history.

From any angle, Margaret is the most reasonable, universally supported heir.

But Margaret’s personality is very eccentric, causing the entire empire’s populace to worry, doubting her ability to bear such a great task and to control all of France.

Margaret loves to play, a fact known throughout France; she constantly says astonishing things and is utterly careless, bearing no semblance of an imperial heir.

The most famous farce is the martial arts marriage contest: whoever can defeat France’s first warrior, Margaret will break tradition and marry him, directly ennobling him as a consort of the empire.

This matter caused a huge uproar; everyone in the streets and alleys of other human empires knows about it, and many have come hoping to become royalty overnight, only to be sent back defeated.

That France’s first warrior is precisely one of the empire’s three great knights, dedicated to serving Princess Margaret, and the match will certainly involve no holding back.

Countless suitors have come and gone in disgrace; to this day the farce continues, every Sunday the first warrior sits alone in the arena, awaiting challengers.

Many people find this puzzling: if Princess Margaret truly wants to marry, why must someone promise to the empire’s first warrior? Isn’t that forcing someone?

The strength of France’s first warrior is extraordinary; only a handful can defeat him, clearly Margaret is just amusing herself with others and never intended to marry.

Don’t look at Princess Margaret appearing foolish, but her entourage is formidable, second only to the old king, showing how beloved this sole daughter of the king is.

Now the old king has fallen into a coma, unable to govern the empire—this is Mades’ perfect opportunity to seize power, yet Princess Margaret has become his greatest stumbling block, secretly opposing him at every turn.

This makes Mades’ dream of becoming the new master of France difficult to achieve in the short term; even though his current authority rivals that of a regent, he still cannot shake the foundation of the royal family.

Mades’ ambition certainly does not stop there; he wishes to establish a nation for the blood race, with all humans as domesticated livestock.

By means of a celestial ritual, he would move a massive planet from outer space to permanently block the sun, plunging all of France into darkness, an empire he would call the Eternal Night Empire.

Then all blood clans would no longer be limited to nighttime activity, but would enjoy eternal freedom in France.

Without the threat of sunlight, the power of the blood race would greatly increase, easily becoming the masters of this land.

However, activating the celestial ritual requires an enormous amount of power, something ordinary people simply cannot possess—unless the most ancient blood clan, Dracula, awakens and personally wields unmatched power to carry it out.

This is the great undertaking of the entire blood race, and also Mades’ ultimate dream: to build a blissful pure land for vampires.

Trying to take France through politics is too difficult, far less direct and effective than seizing it by force.

As the saying goes, throughout history victors and vanquished are common; Mades, who originally followed Dracula’s retinue, knows this well....

To successfully establish the Eternal Night Empire, Dracula’s power is indispensable, and Mades has been striving all along to awaken his father.

However, Dracula was once severely wounded by the ancestors of the Austin family; the werewolves’ power is no joke, directly inflicting grave injuries on Dracula and casting him into a slumber lasting thousands of years.

To this day, Count Dracula’s body remains damaged, as if torn by beasts, requiring a vast amount of human blood to heal.

Through Mades’ millennia of offerings, Dracula’s body has gradually been repaired, and now it has reached a critical point—the day of his awakening is not far off.

In the basement of the chancellor’s residence, there is a man and a woman—

The girl wears the tattered prison garb, covered in whip lashes, even exposing crimson blood; she hangs there, exhausted and in pain.

She has several very obvious features: on her head grow black horns like a goat’s, and on her back hang a pair of deep black membranous wings, unmistakably demonic traits.

It seems this girl is Beelzebub’s younger sister, Miranda; after being captured here she has never escaped, and has been treated like a slave.

Mades is dressed in a silk white shirt with lace‑trimmed cuffs that look very elegant, his wavy black hair revealing a refined, cultured demeanor.

He throws his whip to one side, looks at the hanging Miranda, and speaks in a sympathetic tone:

“How many times have I told you, don’t try to escape?”

“How then can I treat you politely?.”

“Beautiful demon lady?”

title: Chapter 26 — Blood Moon Swamp
content:
Chapter 26 — Blood Moon Swamp

Volume 16 · Chapter 26

“Please... please don't do this, I beg you, let me go.” Miranda, who was hung up, pleaded desperately.
“Sorry, you are the demon I bought at great expense, destined to become our father's sacrifice; letting you go does not serve our interests.” Mades lifted Miranda's chin, speaking seriously, “Actually I don't want to use violence against women; if you obediently listen, you can treat this place as your home and be treated courteously.
“If this continues, it will summon my brother; if he doesn't see me, he will surely go mad.
Miranda showed a sorrowful expression, worriedly saying, “By then, surely many people will die; even so, does it not matter?
“Who is your brother?” Mades probed.
“It's you... absolutely unbeatable exis...
Miranda hesitated and said.
“Oh?” Mades' face turned cold, he slapped Miranda's ear with a “pa” sound, “An unbeatable existence, you dare say that? Do you think I would feel fear because of that? Don't be naive; you will spend the last of your life in this dungeon.
Having said that, Mades left without looking back, locking Miranda alone in the basement.
Miranda lowered her head; sorrowful emotions surged in her heart, tears streamed uncontrollably.
“Brother, where are you?
.
Just as Mades left the basement, a subordinate stepped forward and handed him his coat. 1所
“Keep a close watch on this female demon; starve her for three days, and if she still doesn't behave, break her legs.”
“Yes, sir.
The subordinate's name is Ram; he is Mades' capable steward, handling all affairs of the manor, including overseeing the captured slaves.
“How is Camilla's side? Have the agreed-upon 100 slaves been delivered?” Mades inquired about recent matters.
“Not yet; we have already demanded too many slaves, even on Camilla's side they are probably stretched thin.” Ram answered seriously.
“Push forward—now father is about to awaken; we absolutely cannot have trouble at this time. Didn't Avignon take in many refugees? Round them all up; if anything happens, I will help suppress it here, and no matter what happens to Avignon, it won't reach the king or princess's ears.” Mades' eyes flashed with a hint of anxiety; the awakening consciousness requires many sacrifices, still not
NI 二多.
“Afterwards I will contact Lady Camilla, but the situation is dire now; her side may not be able to help.” Ram said hesitantly.
“Rest assured, that Camilla guy is more capable than you imagine; as a high-ranking officer of the blood clan, his strength is second only to mine, and in some aspects even I feel inferior.” Mades said lightly, seeming to greatly admire Camilla.
“No way, you're such an outstanding person, yet there are aspects where you fall short of Lady Camilla?” Ram exclaimed in surprise.
“Camilla's magical attainment is very high; she is a lord I cannot even reach. You should know that magic is a miraculous power, one of the two great systems of the world; upon reaching a certain realm, it is even possible to create a new world.” Mades said with deep meaning.
“Creating a world? Is that really possible? I've never heard of anyone who could do that.” A bead of cold sweat trickled down Ram's forehead.
“Not having heard of it doesn't mean it's impossible; magicians who have reached the peak of Saint-tier will comprehend the essence of some world, and using magic power to create a world of their own is also feasible; Camilla has always specialized in this aspect.” Mades paused, looked at Ram, and asked, “Have you heard of the Blood Moon Swamp?
“I have heard of it; it is a gathering place of magic beasts on par with the northern forests of Great Britain, a very dangerous place, but a thousand years ago it mysteriously disappeared, and it has become an endless desert.” Ram replied, he does have some knowledge.
“That mysterious disappearance there is directly related to Camilla.” Mades smiled.
“Ah?!” Ram widened his eyes, feeling somewhat unbelievable; such a vast place as the Blood Moon Swamp disappearing out of thin air—could it be man-made?
“Actually, the entire Blood Moon Swamp has been refined by Camilla into a world constructed of magic power; this is also her strongest magic. If one must put it in words, it is like a person cultivating a lifetime's secret, condensing a lifetime's martial arts essence.” Mades glanced at Ram beside him and continued, “As far as I know, nobody whom Camilla has imprisoned in the Blood Moon Swamp has ever managed to come out alive; it is truly a formidable sealing magic.”
“It's that strong?” Ram felt tremendous shock inside; imprisoning people in a self-created world—such magic he had never heard of.
“A few hundred years ago, the renowned Wind Holy Dragon, one of the Six Holy Dragons, once attacked Avignon from the south; the whole empire was troubled dealing with it, requiring the strength of three knight orders, yet Camilla alone resolved it.” Mades thought, recalling, “If I remember correctly, the Wind Holy Dragon was imprisoned by Camilla in the Blood Moon Swamp; to this day it has not escaped, likely it died inside.
“...That exaggerated? The Six Holy Dragons, like the Light Holy Dragon hovering over the Vatican's skies—how could such an existence be defeated by a single person?!” Ram showed an expression of disbelief.
“Don't forget, the Blood Moon Swamp is named together with Great Britain's magic forest; inside there are millions of magic beasts, and they have been starving for thousands of years, among them are monsters even stronger than the Wind Holy Dragon; if a living creature is suddenly thrown in, what else do I need to say about the outcome?” Mades gave a half-smile, clearly expressing the danger of the Blood Moon Swamp.
“Um... Ram stared, already understood; even a lofty Holy Dragon facing millions of starving wolves would feel fear, let alone the formidable monsters inside; ‘So it turns out Lady Camilla is this strong, usually unseen; if imprisoned in the Blood Moon Swamp, is there really a way to get out?’”
“Of course, as long as you are strong enough to break the magic-constructed world, everything is fine; however, I cannot do this, perhaps only our father has a slight chance.” Mades gave a mysterious smile.
“..... Ram's inner shock is hard to calm, updating his perception of Camilla; he had always thought her status was not inferior to Mades, a woman scheming, but he didn't expect her strength to also rank among the blood clan as second...
Being imprisoned in the Blood Moon Swamp, it should be impossible for anyone to get out, right?
After all, the Wind Holy Dragon died inside; facing hundreds of thousands of starving magic beasts, one would likely be completely helpless.
As the top-tier dragon race's Six Holy Dragons, strength is unquestionable; even against opponents of equal rank, they would submit to dragon might and be defeated.
It seems that if the Eternal Night Empire is established, the only one who could share autumn colors with Lord Mades would be this Camilla....

title: Chapter 27 — Blood Moon Swamp
content:
Chapter 27 — Blood Moon Swamp

Volume 16 · Chapter 27

Outside the main city of Avignon, there was a continuous mountain range. This place was isolated from the world, with few people, and was very far from the main city. In the distant past, this was the location of a garrison, with the characteristic of being easy to defend and difficult to attack. A beam of light shot up into the sky, tearing through the night air. Camilla's transfer magic array had transported herself and Alice to this remote and inaccessible place. She planned to defeat and coerce Alice, gaining more leverage to negotiate with Lucifer III. Camilla's ambition was not small, wanting to use the child and Alice's life to indirectly control Merlin. Being able to make a demon lord's monarch do her bidding was an exciting thing to think about. Camilla had already seen from the previous events that it was unclear whether the child was their biological child, after all, killing one's own kin was not unheard of in the demon race. Additionally, Alice had stopped Merlin, which fully demonstrated that in Lucifer III's eyes, this woman was more important than the child. Only by controlling the woman in front of her could she truly make Lucifer III surrender and become her greatest aid. Camilla felt that her current plan was going smoothly, as long as she defeated Alice, she would be fine, and now that she was holding the little girl hostage, what was there to lose. Alice opened her eyes to find herself surrounded by mountains, with the full moon hanging high in the starry sky, and she had no idea where she was. "Where am I? Could this be a trap set by the countess for me? I wonder what method she will use to deal with me." Alice slightly suppressed her anxious heart and looked at Camilla with hostile eyes. "Mom..." The little girl, being held tightly in Camilla's arms, stretched out her small hand, wanting to return to her mother's side, which made Alice's heart ache. However, with the great enemy in front of her, Alice couldn't comfort the little girl and could only say irritably, "I've done what you said, now should you return the child to me?" "Haha... Camilla laughed twice, looking at Alice with a playful gaze, "Did I say I would return the child to you? I only said I wouldn't kill her if you listened to me." "Tch! What else do you want? I've come with you, do you have any other demands?" Alice frowned, feeling annoyed, thinking that it wasn't going to be that easy after all. "What do I want? Can't you see? Camilla narrowed her eyes, seemingly teasing Alice, and since they were far from Avignon, she wasn't afraid that Merlin would come, and she was unscrupulously manipulating Alice. Moreover, she had prepared a "gift" for Lucifer III, and it was impossible to escape so easily, and she might be detained for a long time. What Camilla feared most was Lucifer III, but since he wasn't here, what was there to fear? Alice calmed down and thought for a moment before saying, "You want to subdue me and then negotiate with Merlin, right? I can see that you're afraid of dealing with him." "Haha, since you can see that, yet you still dare to follow me to this wilderness, I must admire your courage." Camilla didn't hide it, instead, she frankly admitted it. Alice took a deep breath, feeling that a fierce battle was unavoidable, "I advise you to give up this idea, if Merlin becomes ruthless, he won't care about my life or death, and he will destroy everything that stands in his way." "Oh? Is that so? But earlier, you didn't do that, did you? You were going to kill me directly, but you gave up because you might hit Alice." Camilla paused, speaking in a firm tone, "In Lucifer III's eyes, you must be a very important woman, at the very least, you can influence his decisions, and a Great Demon Lord marrying a human is not a fake emotion!" Alice was stunned for a moment, her heart slightly moved, but she still spoke seriously, "Although what you said makes me happy, I must tell you that I and Lucifer III are not truly husband and wife, we're just nominal." "What's the difference?" Camilla didn't believe Alice's words, thinking that she was trying to downplay her relationship with Lucifer III, and that she had miscalculated. "Even if you subdue me, you won't be able to restrict Merlin, he won't give up killing you because of me." Alice said in a very serious tone. "At this point, do you think I would believe what you say? Lucifer III's actions earlier, stopping his sword for you, have already made it clear, and any explanation is useless!" Camilla's smile became more arrogant. Alice's anger rose, and she raised her slender sword, "Then there's only one way left!" "Haha, do you not understand your situation?" Camilla once again grasped the little girl's neck, threatening, "The initiative is in my hands, if you don't want this lovely baby to die, then throw away your sword, that holy aura is nauseating!" Alice's chest began to heave with anger, wanting to fight Camilla to the death, but considering the little girl's safety, she had to compromise, and so she threw away her sword, empty-handed, saying, "Are you satisfied now?" "Not bad, you're obedient..." Camilla smiled, her elegant appearance slowly changing, as black, long-haired wings unfolded wildly. Alice looked at Camilla's transformation, her heart becoming more serious, this was a vampire, but why did its appearance differ greatly from the specimens in the Austin Earl's collection, looking more like a black cat, but she couldn't underestimate her opponent, whose oppressive power was almost at the peak of the Saint-tier, not much different from her own. Camilla's appearance became somewhat ferocious, and although she was indeed a vampire, she was a variant, having merged with the habits of a beast. She stretched out her sharp, hair-covered tail, which looked like a sharp whip, and intentionally swung it in front of Alice. "Next, you'll be crying out in agony, I love it when you're so serious, showing a painful expression..." As soon as she finished speaking, Camilla controlled her sharp tail, shooting it out like a whip, striking Alice. The sound of the tail whipping through the air was like lightning flashing across the night sky, and Camilla's tail easily tore through Alice's flesh, crazily piercing her internal organs. Camilla's methods were ruthless, clearly wanting to torture Alice to the brink of death, she wouldn't kill Alice, or else she would lose her leverage to coerce Lucifer III. "Ahhhhhh!" Alice covered her head, forcibly enduring the pain of the tail whipping her, and her mournful cries echoed through the mountains, but no one could hear her. Merlin let out a painful cry, feeling like he had been washed away by a river of blood, his whole body feeling like it had been soaked for months, his limbs weak, and his head dizzy. When he opened his eyes again, in front of him was a huge, crimson moon, and all around him was a vast, swampy wetland. Merlin quickly got up, his body drenched, and soon his stomach started to churn with nausea, and he vomited twice before feeling slightly better. Earlier, when he had fallen into the water, he had drunk a belly full of water, and had almost passed out, his whole body feeling extremely fatigued. After vomiting, Merlin tried to suppress his bodily discomfort, and with great effort, he lifted his head, and what entered his vision was a gigantic, pale dragon skeleton, its enormous bones covering the crimson moon in the sky. "Where am I?"

title: Chapter 28 — Merlin Trapped
content:
Chapter 28 — Merlin Trapped

Volume 16 · Chapter 28

Merlin looked around at the unfamiliar world before him, the scarlet-red moon particularly eye-catching.

The ground beneath his feet was a muddy swamp, not far from the Death Swamp of his homeland, sharing the same quiet yet menacing atmosphere.

Merlin bent down, wringing out his clothes slightly, then turned to look at the massive dragon skeleton lying quietly behind him.

The skeleton bore very obvious scratch marks and a grey-black patina, looking old — as if it had been dead for over a hundred years.

And it seemed to have been attacked by a horde of monsters. Its flesh had been devoured completely; the bone-deep claw marks were the best proof.

This skeleton was extraordinarily large, suggesting its owner had once been an apex predator of the skies, a being that once dominated its domain.

Merlin felt this skeleton was no ordinary thing. Even in death, he could still sense faint traces of wind element emanating from it.

It seemed there was no need for further guessing. This was the world constructed by Camilla using her magic, her ultimate spell — the Blood Moon Swamp.

It served to trap living things inside, restricting their movement. Once someone entered this Blood Moon Swamp, escaping would be extremely difficult.

And the dragon skeleton before his eyes was most likely the remains of one of the Six Great Holy Dragons — the Storm Holy Dragon.

The ravaged bones made it easy to imagine what kind of attack this Holy Dragon had suffered, being devoured completely by magical beasts.

If the skeleton hadn't contained indelible magic, it would have long been gnawed down to nothing.

If even the famously renowned Six Great Holy Dragons could fall within the Blood Moon Swamp, there was no need to prove how dangerous this place was.

What is this? Such a huge dragon skeleton.

Merlin knew well whose remains these were, but he had no idea where he stood. This felt like a place fraught with danger at every turn.

He recalled the "gift" Camilla had said she left for him. Could this be it?

Was it some kind of teleportation mechanism? Had she dragged him somewhere completely different? To some remote corner of the world?

Several black lines of exasperation slid down Merlin's forehead. This was troublesome. If this were really the case, how much time would it take him to get back to France?

Just as Merlin stood there, at a loss, he suddenly heard a few weary coughs from behind him.

"Cough! Cough cough!"

Merlin was startled. He hadn't expected anyone else alive in this place. Maybe he could ask them where they were.

He quickly turned around and followed the sound of coughing, only to find old Acaron painfully lying in a puddle, several arrows pierced into his body, badly wounded.

"Mr. Acaron?" Merlin's eyes widened. He couldn't believe he'd see the half-dead old man here. Had he been dragged in just now too?

"...Lord Merlin?"

Old Acaron had briefly clashed with Camilla only moments ago and had been instantly struck by his own reflected arrows, leaving him grievously injured and unable to move. He had been struggling to stay conscious in a corner ever since.

When his consciousness had begun to fade and he was unaware of what was happening outside, the river of blood left by Camilla had swept him directly into the Blood Moon Swamp.

Old Acaron felt unbearably unlucky to keep getting caught in the crossfire. But at least he had run into Merlin now, giving him someone to rely on. He had thought he was going to die.

"Hey, are you alright? You don't look good..." Merlin looked at the arrows sticking out of old Acaron's body, from which dark red blood was slowly seeping.

"...I'm fine. It's not fatal. If... if they had hit my heart, I would have died already." Old Acaron endured the pain and answered.

"Get up quickly. Lying in the water will only make your injuries worse."

Merlin held out his hand and pulled old Acaron out of the puddle, dragging him onto dry land.

Looking at the arrows piercing through the old man's body, Merlin reached out to help, but was stopped.

"No no! Lord Merlin, don't touch them. One of the arrows seems to have pierced a blood vessel. If you pull it out now, I'll lose too much blood. Let it stay for now."

"Peh!" Merlin clicked his tongue, feeling helpless. His saliva had healing properties, but it wouldn't work on males. "What should we do? There don't seem to be any healing items here either. Things will only get worse like this."

Old Acaron lifted his head and looked around. "...Where is this? Just a moment ago we were still in Avignon."

"I don't know. A flood came and swept me into a whirlpool. When I woke up, I was here. Aren't you French? Is this still within imperial territory?" Merlin asked tentatively. With Alice having been taken away and himself not even knowing where he was, plus a wounded companion at his side, the situation was far from optimistic.

Old Acaron also wore a puzzled expression. As a Frenchman, he should recognize this place, but when he tilted his head up and saw the crimson moon hanging high in the night sky, he was visibly shaken.

Although old Acaron had never seen the Blood Moon Swamp in person, as a native he had heard plenty of stories about it.

A swamp filled with a foul stench, teeming with extremely dangerous magical beasts, numbering in the millions — it was the final resting place for countless adventurers. Countless people had died here!

There were many such stories, still passed down among common folk today. The most conspicuous feature of the Blood Moon Swamp was undoubtedly its eerily scarlet-red moon.

Old Acaron's eyes widened, his face growing paler and paler. He could hardly believe he had somehow ended up in a death zone that had vanished hundreds of years ago. His mind struggled to process it.

"N-no... no way! This is... this is..."

"Hmm?" Merlin noticed old Acaron's strange state and quickly crouched down to ask, "Mr. Acaron, do you know where this is?"

"Although... I'm not entirely sure, this should be the Blood Moon Swamp that vanished hundreds of years ago..." Old Acaron said hesitantly. Although he felt this was indeed the legendary gathering place of magical beasts, he dared not speak too confidently.

"The Blood Moon Swamp?" Merlin looked confused. He had never heard of such a place.

"That's right. Every French person has heard of the Blood Moon Swamp. Hundreds of years ago, this area was known as the Death Zone. Millions of magical beasts gathered here, and not a single person who entered ever made it out alive. It was an incredibly perilous place. Even the former King of France once tried to conquer this land and failed. No matter how powerful the army, they could not clear this region. Until one day, this Blood Moon Swamp seemed to be erased by the gods, disappearing overnight and turning into a vast desert." Old Acaron recounted, momentarily forgetting his pain.

"Something like that actually happened?" Merlin looked up at the blood-red moon in the sky, feeling a strange sensation.

This sounded like a very dangerous place. I need to be careful.

But why was I dragged here?

If Camilla was behind this, her power is truly unfathomable.

It's pointless to think too much now. How exactly can I get out of here?

(u --●)?

title: Chapter 29 — Magical Beasts Attack
content:
Chapter 29 — Magical Beasts Attack

Volume 16 · Chapter 29

“Mr. Akaron, are we still in France?” Merlin asked patiently.
“...I’m not entirely sure either. The Blood Moon Swamp is indeed within France, but this place has long disappeared; our sudden appearance here is completely baffling.” Old Akaron was clearly a bit muddle-headed.
Merlin furrowed his brows. A place that has long disappeared? Does that mean we are now in another space?
Does Camilla have that kind of power, able to create space?
Merlin found it hard to believe; creating a world and space is something only a god could do.
“Tsk! This is getting troublesome; we have no idea where we are....
Old Akaron glanced at his wounds, feeling somewhat guilty, thinking Merlin still had the strength to return, while he himself had become a burden, and the intense pain was steadily eroding his will. “Lord Merlin, why don’t… why don’t you just go on your own? I’m already in this state; I probably can’t hold on much longer. Rather than drag you down, I’d rather die here.”
“Huh?” Merlin turned to look at Akaron, not expecting this old man to have given up, planning to die here without burdening anyone.
Old Akaron tugged his silver adventurer’s certificate from his neck, trembling as he offered it to Merlin. “Please deliver my proof to the Adventurers’ Cemetery of the Kingdom of Denmark. I wish to hang my sole keepsake on the holy tree alongside countless fallen adventurers, basking in the morning sun each day—this is my final request…”.
“Go!” Merlin flung open Old Akaron’s adventurer’s certificate, speaking earnestly. “We haven’t reached a dead end yet; don’t say that. I despise hearing defeatist talk. Hold on a little longer, and we’ll find a way out of here.”
“.....” Old Akaron stared blankly, then sucked in a breath of cold air; several arrows were deeply embedded in his body, and any movement would trigger excruciating pain. “Sorry, I might be too weak; I’m not as strong as you, but we really might die here. You seem fine—if you can run, then run.”
“Really? Is it truly that dangerous?” Merlin chuckled, still showing no tension. “To be frank, my hometown is a swamp, so this place feels rather familiar to me.”
“Which… which swamp?” Akaron exclaimed, thinking, Who would live in a swamp? Generally, this place is extremely dangerous—no one would reside here.
“There’s a Death Swamp on the islands across from Great Britain; have you heard of it?” Merlin gave a mysterious smile.
“....” Akaron looked flustered and quickly said, “Lord Merlin, don’t joke—Death Swamp is demon territory; who would have humans living there?”
“Really, I’m not lying,” Merlin emphasized with a straight face.
“I know you’re strong, Lord Merlin, but don’t joke at a time like this—you need to assess the situation. This place is truly dangerous; I’ve heard since childhood that many powerhouses have perished in the Blood Moon Swamp. Our chances here are slim.” Akaron thought Merlin was a weirdo, never showing any tension.
“Oh?” Merlin spread his arms and spun around in place. “A place where powerhouses fall—doesn’t that sound interesting?”
“Um… can you defeat hundreds of thousands of magical beasts?” Akaron asked tentatively, feeling his question was foolish, like asking someone if they could go a lifetime without eating—impossible!
“I haven’t tried, but maybe I could manage…” Merlin mused, adding that he had no experience slaughtering hundreds of thousands of magical beasts.
“I_…” Old Akaron couldn’t find words; he admired Merlin’s strength despite being only a low-rank black iron, but now he felt Merlin was a lunatic!
One person taking on hundreds of thousands of magical beasts is akin to wiping out an entire region’s monsters—no matter how you look at it, it’s a massive siege, something a single person couldn’t accomplish.
Moreover, the Blood Moon Swamp is a place even the Frankish Empire couldn’t develop; countless imperial powerhouses have failed, so for Merlin alone to think he could pull it off is as unrealistic as a tale from the Arabian Nights!
Although Old Akaron had personally witnessed Merlin’s blade power—cutting down a Sacred Boundary Tree Spirit—he was just a small figure, lacking detailed knowledge of powerhouses; he couldn’t distinguish between Sacred Boundary and Saint-tier, only knowing that golden magic and battle aura were incredibly strong.
However, according to rumors, many magical beasts in the Blood Moon Swamp possess strength surpassing Saint-tier powerhouses, and their numbers are not small—this is why Old Akaron thought Merlin was just spouting nonsense.
“What? Are you worried we’ll be eaten by magical beasts?” Merlin raised his eyebrows.
As Merlin’s words fell, a pitch-black double-headed snake sprang from the swamp, coiling tightly around him.
The double-headed snake’s four eyes glowed red, flicking its tongue and emitting a “hiss” sound; it seemed nearly mad with hunger, and upon seeing Merlin and Old Akaron, it could no longer suppress its craving.
Magical beasts aren’t a single species; they lack intelligence, knowing only to hunt and reproduce. Moreover, having been imprisoned here by Camilla for a long time, they’ve starved to the point of losing all instinct.
“Huh?” Merlin lifted his head, gazing at the hungry double-headed snake.
NEES,
“....” Lord Merlin!” Old Akaron panicked, eyes wide as he stared at the double-headed snake, guessing it had silently swum up from underwater, making no sound.
Bound Merlin remained utterly calm, feeling no pressure at all.
This double-headed snake magical beast was merely a tiny shrimp among the hundreds of thousands.
Merlin sensed a faint tremor in the ground; turning slightly, he saw the horde of magical beasts had caught the scent of living people and was surging forward in a mighty wave.
Gazing at the vast, dark mass of magical beasts, Merlin narrowed his eyes slightly; he couldn’t make out their forms clearly—they all looked bizarre, as if radiation had caused genetic mutations.
Snake-tailed beasts running on land, three-eyed giant crocodiles swimming in water, human-faced birds flying in the sky, and so on—varieties abounded, making it impossible to distinguish them.
The magical beasts bellowed hungrily; seeing two living humans with eyes glowing green, they surged forward in a frenzy, utterly unaware of what kind of foe they faced.
One can imagine that centuries ago, the Storm Holy Dragon faced these fearless magical beasts and perished— they were not only tough to deal with, but impossible to slay completely.
“Oh wow, there are quite a few…” Merlin said blandly, watching the beast horde.
“Lord Merlin! Run! I told you to go first! Now look—we can’t escape!” Old Akaron’s emotions flared; seeing the tide of countless magical beasts, he was utterly terrified.
“What’s there to panic about?” Merlin effortlessly broke free of the double-headed snake’s coils with sheer physical strength, tearing the surrounding beasts apart limb from limb, then assumed a sword-drawing stance. “Old man, don’t stray too far from me; otherwise, I won’t be responsible for any mishaps!”
Having said that, he unleashed his draw-cut; the killing sword aura burst forth like a demon manifesting, emitting a shrill, wild howl!
Merlin swept sideways—slash—frantically clearing the beasts before him; countless magical beasts were reduced to bloody pulp by the sword aura’s vortex, not even his toe tips touched!
The draw-cut fanned out in a wide arc, slaughtering the magical beasts; every mindless monster was annihilated!
“....” Old Akaron stared blankly at it all, his heart trembling as he thought— Compared to the horde of hundreds of thousands of magical beasts, Merlin seemed even more frightening….

title: Chapter 30 — Bloodline Suppression
content:
Chapter 30 — Bloodline Suppression

Volume 16 · Chapter 30

The mournful screams echoed through the valley.
Alice suffered considerable injuries all over her body, being whipped by Camilla's tail until her skin split and flesh tore.
Camilla's spiked tail was like a torture instrument; when swung, it was no different from a blade.
The dense tail lashes struck Alice, producing crisp sounds, accompanied by Camilla's exaggerated laughter, as if this place were a prison dedicated to torture.
Alice knelt on the ground; the dense lashing was already unbearable, and after such a prolonged whipping, even an iron man would be deformed.
“Hahahaha……” Camilla, seeing Alice's pained expression, felt an indescribable pleasure, “How is it? Comfortable? Weren't you still arrogant yesterday, talking back to me? Have you learned what submission means now?”
“Don't hit Mom! You wicked woman! Don't hit Mom!”
The little girl held hostage by Camilla could do nothing; she raised her tiny fists and cried as she pounded the wicked woman's chest, but it had no effect at all.
Alice endured the searing pain of the lashes, slowly lifted her head, and glared at Camilla with hatred, like a starving wolf waiting for an opportunity.
“Oh? Your gaze isn’t bad; it seems I haven’t broken you completely yet…” Camilla, seeing Alice's stubborn nature, instantly sparked her desire to torment, and she extended her claws, each nail flashing with a cold light as magic surged, “I’ll increase the force, so you can truly feel what it’s like to wish for death! Go ahead and scream your heart out, then please me!”
“……” Alice could barely speak, her whole body feeling numb, likely because the pain had dulled her senses; if this continued, she wouldn’t die but would be crippled by Camilla’s blows.
Camilla's sharp claws swung, releasing a cutting force imbued with magic from afar; the shockwave struck Alice's body directly.
“Ahhhhh!!!”
Alice let out a miserable cry; her whole body was flung into the air by the shockwave, her clothes torn apart, her chest, waist, and thighs savagely gouged, dark red blood spraying into the air.
This vampire variant of Camilla already possessed beast-like strength; her magic-infused long-range claw swipe would cause massive harm, and Alice felt as if a tiger's claw had raked her chest.
“Hahahaha! Exactly! Keep screaming! Don’t stop! Your anguished wails are the source of my pleasure! Indeed, tormenting a solemn woman like you gives me a sense of achievement! Keep going, keep going, keep going! Hahahaha!”
Camilla laughed like a madman, hysterically, watching Alice's pained state, feeling an unprecedented joy, far greater than the thrill of hunting young girls.
Alice was repeatedly struck by Camilla's long-range claw attacks, each blow a razor-sharp impact that relentlessly harmed her body, worsening her condition.
The stone wall behind Alice was already covered in beast-like claw marks, a shocking sight!
“Mom!” the little girl cried, seeing Alice being bullied by Camilla, her sobs growing more heartbroken, fury welling up, she instinctively shouted back, “Don’t hurt her! You wretch!”
“Ugh!”
Camilla's movements suddenly halted, as if she had been frozen; she swore she had no intention to stop, yet her body oddly refused to budge, as if some force were controlling her!
She slightly lowered her head, looking at the little girl she held hostage; those eyes glowed deep crimson in the moonlight, as if some power were compelling her to obey?
Why? This kid is a bit strange; why should I listen to a little girl?
No……
I am being restrained by this child’s words; even the mere power of calm speech binds me!
Such a thing could never happen to a human; only… only a bloodline superior to mine among our kind could do this!
Until now, the only one who could control me with words was my father; no other vampire has ever managed it!
Just who is this little brat?! Could it be one of the two progenitors who lived alongside my father?!
No… impossible! Those progenitors are thousands of years old; they couldn’t possibly maintain the appearance of a little girl!
Camilla’s mind was in turmoil; for a moment she couldn’t figure out the girl’s background, feeling she was an extremely dangerous presence.
The blood clan is a strictly hierarchical race, with very clear class divisions; Camilla’s worry is not without reason.
After all, the blood clan’s propagation requires the Embrace to create new members; the purer a vampire’s bloodline, the stronger its control over lower-blood kin.
Words also wield inconceivable power; if Dracula commanded Camilla to die, her instinct would be unable to resist.
Now, a single rebuke from this little girl actually left Camilla unable to move, forcing obedience; her identity is thus quite thought-provoking.
“Drop dead!”
Alice let out an angry shout, then punched Camilla’s face hard; golden battle aura surged from her, knocking the wicked woman back!
Camilla was still cowed by the little girl’s pressure, failing to notice Alice’s dying counterattack from the other side, and thus suffered the loss.
Camilla slammed hard into the rock wall, showing how enraged Alice was—she wished she could punch Camilla to death.
“Mom!” the little girl, having broken free, sobbed as she threw herself into Alice’s embrace, her frail shoulders shuddering.
“Don’t cry, don’t cry, baby, Mom’s okay…” Alice held the little girl, continually comforting her, though she herself was also badly hurt.
“Tch!” Camilla burst out of the rock wall, her black fur trembling, she said angrily, “It seems this child really isn’t your biological offspring—how astonishing…”
Alice lifted her head, glaring at Camilla, and patted the little girl’s back, “Hide, Mom’s going to deal with this wicked woman.”
“No, I… I don’t want to leave Mom…” the little girl clung tighter, fearing Alice might be in danger.
“Silly child, Mom won’t abandon you; I just want you to hide for a bit, okay?” Alice said patiently.
“Ugh…” the little girl nodded, then had to hide behind a stone, peeking out with her head, looking very worried about Alice.
“Where did that kid come from? Mind telling me?” Camilla, now very interested in the little girl, felt she must be of her own kind, and a superior one at that.
“Cut the nonsense! This is your burial ground!”
Alice, having endured brutal abuse, her body swayed on the verge of collapse, yet her fighting spirit remained fervent, like an enraged valkyrie!
She then activated her dragon transformation, becoming a half-dragon, half-human being; her dragon wings unfurled, disdainful of the freezing, bone-chilling wind!
Alice gestured, and the “Hymn of Light” lying on the ground flew back into her hand, readying herself for a fight to the death.
“Oh? Dragon power? Rather interesting…” Camilla felt the draconic aura emanating from Alice, not feeling fear but rather a hint of contempt—
“But what does that matter?”
“You think having dragon power lets you beat me?”
“Hahaha, I advise you not to be so naïve…”
