title: Chapter 31 — Swamp Food Chain
content:
Chapter 31 — Swamp Food Chain

Volume 16 · Chapter 31

"Hope your attitude later is still as tough as it is now." Alice glared at Camilla, her magic and battle aura churning like boiling water, rolling around her body.

"How many times do I have to beat you before you learn to behave? Ten? A hundred?" Camilla placed her hands on her hips, showing no respect for Alice.

"Shut up!" Alice leaped from where she stood, her slender sword blooming with glistening golden icicles that shot toward Camilla!

"It's useless. I don't know where you got that dragon power, but it's still far inferior to a true Saint Dragon!" Camilla's tail lashed about, its rapid swings forming a barrier that shattered all the incoming icicles to pieces.

Hundreds of years ago, Camilla had indeed confronted the Storm Saint Dragon face-to-face, and she had been at a disadvantage, forced to use the Blood Moon Swamp against the Storm Saint Dragon to escape disaster.

Although Camilla's magic was powerful, her overall strength still lagged behind that of a dragon. However, Alice was still far from matching a Saint Dragon, and she didn't feel the slightest pressure.

Alice charged at Camilla, her slender sword delivering frequent thrusts, the flashing silver light resembling falling meteors. By eye, even a single fly would be poked into a honeycomb under such attacks.

Although Camilla was a mage, her movement speed was extraordinarily swift. Facing the dense barrage of sword edges, she showed no panic at all, dodging repeatedly. Each thrust grazed the edge of her skin.

It seemed Camilla genuinely looked down on Alice, clearly not fighting at full strength, still effortlessly mocking her.

"What? Is this your sword technique? So slow. Aren't you the Demon Lord's wife? This level of strength is nowhere near your husband's. Could it be that you're just a vase relying on Lucifer the Third? Haha~"

"Shut up! Be quiet!"

Alice flew into a rage, her mental state exploding from Camilla's taunts. She strongly resented the word "vase," feeling deeply insulted.

She knew Camilla was a vampire. The best way to kill her was in close combat — only by piercing the blood clan's chest with a slender sword could they be killed. Otherwise, even if severely wounded, they would heal quickly.

This ultra-fast healing ability was fatal to any adventurer. When their magic and battle aura were exhausted, that was when vampires could run rampant.

As Alice grew angry, her attacks became somewhat sluggish, losing all cohesion, and Camilla seized the opening.

Camilla reached out midair, her immense magic surging with tearing force, forcing Alice to retreat. The scale-like armor on her chest was torn apart by the overwhelming power.

"Urgh!" Alice was forcibly driven back. Even with her dragon transformation, she couldn't gain the upper hand against Camilla. The dragon scales she had generated had good defensive properties, but against the claws of this little wild cat, they proved somewhat fragile.

"Heh heh, I advise you not to get close to me. Although I'm a mage, tearing you apart is still not difficult..."

Camilla said triumphantly. She glanced toward the direction of Avignon's main city. There had been no sign of movement at all until now. Indeed, the Blood Moon Swamp restricted Lucifer the Third effectively, giving her ample time to torment the woman before her.

A creepy smile appeared on Camilla's face. She thought Lucifer the Third's strength was merely average — not as powerful as the legends claimed.

Otherwise, with her own power, she wouldn't have been able to restrict this young Demon Lord at all. Don't let him die inexplicably in the Blood Moon Swamp, that would be terribly boring.

I suppose now my countless millions of little darlings are hungrily charging toward Lucifer the Third, wanting to tear off a piece from him.

Hah, wants to tear me apart? In your dreams!" Alice gripped her slender sword tightly, the pain from her chest wound extremely intense.

"Don't get too carried away. I just want to torture you half to death. After all, if you die, you'll be completely worthless..."

"That depends on whether you have the chance!" Alice unleashed her full power, swinging left and right. Golden ice thorns erupted from the ground one after another, reaching toward Camilla!

Looking at those densely packed ice thorns, like vines infused with life, they encircled Camilla from 360 degrees with no blind spots, then crashed down—

The Blood Moon Swamp.

Merlin's sudden blade-drawing slash caught the sudden surge of magical beasts completely off guard.

Before they could even reach Merlin's heels, more than half fell. A single sweep cleared countless magical beasts.

The once ferocious beasts suddenly showed signs of weakening, their arrogant momentum suppressed.

Although they lacked intelligence and were very hungry, they still retained some instincts about strength.

After teaching these beasts a lesson, Merlin slowly returned his katana to its sheath. Aside from noting the enemy's large numbers, he didn't feel as though he were in a death zone.

This wasn't entirely Merlin's arrogance either. In the past, strong figures who came here, even the Storm Saint Dragon, lacked the ability to clear a large area with a single strike.

If they had, they wouldn't have fallen here. Merlin simply felt no pressure because he was too strong.

The Blood Moon Swamp lay in ruins, the ground covered with the dissected corpses of magical beasts. The blood curdling stench hit the face, making one feel as though transported straight into hell.

Old Arcalon, watching from behind Merlin, was dumbfounded. Such a massive, dark horde of magical beasts, and one blade-drawing slash cleared them all.

This efficiency... wasn't this too exaggerated?! And among them were quite a few powerful beasts. Couldn't even one wave hold him back?

How much limit does Merlin's strength have? It seems he's never taken things seriously! He feels stronger than any strong figure I've encountered in my entire life!

Although he's currently just a Black Iron-ranked adventurer, who knows what he'll become in the future! He'll surely shake the world one day!

Old Arcalon nervously swallowed. He felt that nothing, not even a death zone, was a problem for Merlin. It seemed there was hope for successfully escaping — all he needed to do was cling to Merlin's leg.

Unnoticed by the two, the scarlet moon in the sky began developing hairline cracks, seeming unable to withstand the force of Merlin's blade-drawing slash, already beginning to collapse!

If a few more slashes came, or if Merlin fought seriously, this Blood Moon Swamp constructed by Camilla's magic would likely be completely wiped out in an instant.

"That... wha..., is there s... still..." Merlin frowned. He had wanted to finish this after clearing them, but saw a second wave of magical beasts attacking from the distance, apparently even stronger than before.

The characteristics of the Blood Moon Swamp manifested — the magical beasts attacked wave after wave. Even if they couldn't defeat the prey let in, they could slowly wear it down.

"Tch!" Merlin felt a trace of annoyance. He had just finished clearing one wave, and immediately a second one came. Who knew how many more waves of beasts were behind! If he couldn't kill them all, wouldn't he exhaust himself to death?

The second wave of magical beasts was even larger and just as ferocious, charging straight for Merlin and Old Arcalon.

"Lord Merlin?! These magical beasts are too numerous,恐怕it won't be easy to kill them all!" Old Arcalon said nervously.

"So what?" The moment Merlin finished speaking, his second blade-drawing slash was unleashed. A majestic sword aura swept across the entire battlefield, further fracturing the entire Blood Moon Swamp, which had grown somewhat unstable.

Old Arcalon felt a bead of cold sweat roll down his forehead. He thought, oh heavens, such a powerful killing move? Doesn't it even have a cooldown? Can it be released continuously without limit? ...So terrifying!

Merlin had barely drawn his sword. The ferocious killing intent paralyzed all directions, slaughtering the unsuspecting horde of magical beasts before him down to the last one.

The sword aura continuously battered the horde of magical beasts. It was almost impossible for any monster to escape under such a massive attack — most were smashed into paste!

However, at this critical moment, a pitch-black giant crocodile nearly ten meters long burst from beneath the swamp, radiating Saint-tier aura.

It crashed into Merlin's chest, sending the unguarded him flying!

Merlin's blade-drawing slash was interrupted. Surprised by the sudden ambush, he hadn't expected the swamp to be so dangerous, with strange magical beasts launching surprise attacks at any time — that was the most dangerous part!

Powerful beasts inside the Blood Moon Swamp appeared like bamboo shoots after rain. There were no fewer than twelve Saint-tier magical beasts, all launching fierce attacks on Merlin!

The magical beasts seemed to have realized as well — Merlin was the truly powerful one. Old Arcalon was completely irrelevant, just background decoration. As long as they eliminated Merlin, they could enjoy fresh flesh and blood.

Each of the twelve Saint-tier beasts could have been dominant rulers elsewhere. Although their appearances were bizarre, their attacks were exceptionally vicious.

Merlin, surrounded by twelve Saint-tier beasts, was被打 like a tennis ball, looking somewhat undignified. Sharp claws repeatedly struck Merlin, tearing his clothes.

"Lord Merlin!!!" Old Arcalon, severely wounded, saw Merlin in such a disadvantageous position and felt extreme anxiety inside.

A Saint-tier three-legged vulture took to the sky, diving from above, wanting to deliver a fatal blow with its hard beak!

The three-legged vulture's enormous wings blocked out the sky and sun, its feathers trembling like steel!

Merlin staggered to his feet, seemingly not badly hurt. He raised one hand to block the unstoppable vulture, stopping its rampage.

Then he turned and slashed with his free hand, cleaving the fierce beast in two. Its entire body was severed, blood spraying in all directions!

The three-legged vulture cawed twice, then collapsed lifelessly to the ground, completely dead.

Bathed in blood, Merlin's eyes gradually took on a gem-like crimson hue, making him appear eerie.

After absorbing the life force of the three-legged vulture, Merlin's heart sent waves of comfort throughout his body, and the curse was healed to a certain extent.

The remaining eleven beasts felt a trace of fear, baring their sharp teeth in anger at Merlin from where they stood, yet none dared approach!

Merlin felt a hint of anger well up inside him and wanted to begin counterattacking. These Saint-tier beasts were likely the top predators of the swamp...

"Come on! Keep going!"

"Is this all the strength you have?"

"Don't ruin the fun, keep hitting me!"

With a "boom," a three-headed, six-armed chimpanzee wreathed in flames suddenly descended behind Merlin, radiating an awe-inspiring pressure.

It was the true ruler of the entire Blood Moon Swamp — the king of magical beasts, the existence at the top of the food chain!

Without saying a word, this three-headed, six-armed chimpanzee raised six massive clubs of unknown material and rained down a furious barrage of hammer strikes on Merlin.

Bang bang bang! The extremely fast frequency of heavy hammer blows caused the entire death swamp to tremble, while the other magical beasts dared not approach, cowering in place.

Merlin appeared even more disheveled, his entire body driven underground by the chimpanzee's hammering. Moreover, the creature didn't stop, continuing its furious assault!

The three-headed, six-armed chimpanzee kicked Merlin upward, gathered all its strength, and its flames blazed even more fiercely.

One club swing sent Merlin flying, launching him tens of thousands of meters into the air, becoming a small star against the scarlet night sky. The chimpanzee's movements were as standard as a professional baseball player.

This invincible power seemed intent on sending Merlin circling the earth a hundred times before finishing. It appeared its sole purpose was to kill Merlin.

After launching Merlin into the sky, the three-headed, six-armed chimpanzee fell into a state of wild ecstasy, continuously pounding its own chest with all six arms and letting out excited roars.

"Urgh! Lord Merlin?!" Old Arcalon watched, cold sweat streaming down his face, terror gripping his heart—

Are you kidding me?!

What is the background of this chimpanzee!

Was Lord Merlin being careless?

title: Chapter 32 — Break Out of the Blood Moon Illusion
content:
Chapter 32 — Break Out of the Blood Moon Illusion

Volume 16 · Chapter 32

The gorilla that suddenly jumped out caught Merlin off guard, seemingly gaining a dominant advantage from the start.

After hitting Merlin flying, the three-headed, six-armed chimpanzee danced excitedly in place, flames jumping along its body.

As the strongest existence in the entire Blood Moon Swamp, other magical beasts dared not approach; even the several Saint-tier beasts knelt on the ground, looking terrified.

Saint-tier magical beasts are each a local overlord; this Zong-realm chimpanzee had already reached the top of the beast hierarchy, capable of destroying a royal city.

But magical beasts have low intelligence; just look at how the chimpanzee comically scratches its belly—you know its brains aren't anywhere near sharp.

Old Arcalon was stunned. Just now Merlin had been seconds-heaven, seconds-earth, seconds-air, but in a blink he was beaten silly by the monster. This sudden reversal left his mind blank.

And the monster chose the perfect timing—striking just as Merlin's sword slash was released and hadn't been retracted yet. At that moment Merlin couldn't release another slash unless he quickly sheathed the blade early.

Damn, Merlin-sama doesn't even know where he got hit.

What should I do? Can only obediently let this ugly group of monsters eat me?

Old Arcalon swallowed nervously, feeling his prospects were grim—countless magical beasts had locked onto him simultaneously.

Dense red eyes revealed hungry desires, making one's flesh crawl just looking at them.

"Ugh!" Arcalon dragged his heavily wounded body, backing away slowly, showing fear, his face growing paler.

The magical beasts slowly approached Arcalon, knowing their hunger was hard to restrain, then surged forward together.

Seeing this, Arcalon could only helplessly close his eyes, his mind full of "my life is over."

But at that moment, a thunder-like sound rang through the sky, as if the entire world had been split open!

The earth trembled, the dark red sky already swaying, forcibly torn open a crack!

Above the entire Blood Moon Swamp, it was like shattered glass, fragments rustling down.

The three-headed, six-armed chimpanzee slowly raised its head, looking at the heaven-collapse earth-shatter spectacle, confusion flashing in its eyes—completely unaware of what happened?

The next second, destructive killing sword energy descended from the sky, crashing down with the might of splitting Mount Hua!

The wind howled desperately, the sword energy sweeping everything directly plunged into the dense crowd of magical beasts below, beginning to rampage.

For a moment, the magical beasts' miserable screams rang out. The flesh that was搅碎 scattered everywhere, and in the center of destructive power, unknown numbers of beasts' severed limbs were mixed within.

The three-headed gorilla and that group of Saint-tier magical beasts were almost mercilessly slaughtered in the very first moment of the destructive force's impact.

They probably didn't even know how they died, just like divine punishment from angry gods!

The violent storm blew Old Arcalon a somersault, fortunately he was far away, otherwise he would have been caught in the crossfire.

Looking at the dark mass of torn-apart magical beasts, Old Arcalon's heart was only fear—if this had hit Avignon, that city would surely be completely erased from the map!

The destructive power ravaged this space, the Blood Moon Swamp already unable to bear the burden, couldn't withstand this force, beginning to collapse. Sky and earth split into pieces, like a mirror dropped on the ground, cracking at a visible speed.

This world constructed by Camilla's magic still had its own endurance limit—it couldn't withstand everything. If hit by this level of power from the start, it would have completely collapsed in the first moment.

"....What's going on? ! What happened! ?"

Old Arcalon covered his heart, afraid his weak heart couldn't accept the massive change before his eyes—his old age illness acted up instead.

In his eyes, the Blood Moon Swamp was collapsing mountains and splitting earth, with almost no perfect spot left—calling it the end of the world wasn't an exaggeration.

As a dazzling white light struck, Old Arcalon had to close his eyes. When he opened them again, the scenery before him had changed completely--

All around were dead walls and broken ruins, but from the carving style one could feel the elegance.

Washed by the blood river, the walls revealed a dark red hue, all of them stained.

Outside was a thick layer of bushes, the cold moonlight projecting through layer after layer of bushes.

Although before his eyes was a ruin, Old Arcalon could still vaguely recognize this as Camilla's mansion.

"....Back? !" Arcalon muttered to himself. Although arrows in his body made movement difficult, he still struggled to stand and survey the surroundings.

Just a while ago the count's mansion was still very magnificent, but now for some reason it had become a ruin washed away by floodwaters, looking a complete mess.

With a "bang," Merlin suddenly fell from the sky. Although his clothes were hammered to tatters by the magical beasts, his body seemed unharmed.

Looks like these beasts were fierce, but after hitting for a long time, Merlin was just HP-1, no real effect.

Mere Zong-realm magical beasts wanting to effectively kill Merlin—still a bit unrealistic.

Merlin looked at the dozen or so Saint-tier beasts, plus this Zong-realm chimpanzee—his heart curse was greatly relieved, considered the greatest harvest of this trip.

Just after landing, Merlin put the太刀 back in its sheath, glanced around, felt safe enough to relax slightly, rubbed his neck and said.

"You hit me the moment I said hit, not giving me any face at all, really..."

Old Arcalon stared with wide eyes at Merlin, feeling like he'd seen a ghost. After enduring such fierce attacks, he was still acting like nothing happened—was this guy made of iron!?

"Merlin-sama! ? You're okay!3" E-zhi-xiaozhi

"Huh? What could happen to me? At most I played dead and ascended to heaven in place...". Merlin spread his hands and said lightly.

"Uh...

Old Arcalon's expression became weird, his heart began to doubt life itself. This strength is Black Iron adventurer level? Which ** rank? Can't come see for himself! This is truly rare talent!

"Speaking of which, this is Camilla's residence, right? We were probably just in a false world constructed by some method, not the real one, we were tricked." Merlin looked around, feeling it was okay, not dragged to some godforsaken place.

"R...right, we're still in Avignon." Arcalon suddenly remembered something and asked, "Merlin-sama, where is Alice? Why haven't I seen her?"

"This... Merlin hesitated, looked at the cold round moon in the sky, his heart slightly worried—

Who knows where Alice is right now?

The location of the transfer formation is completely unclear.

Don't get transferred to some weird place?

Hope it's not too far away, otherwise if something happens there's no time to rush over....

title: Chapter 33 — Malygos Returns!
content:
Chapter 33 — Malygos Returns!

Volume 16 · Chapter 33

On the other side, in a valley far from the main city of Avignon, Alice and Camilla were fighting fiercely, their forces constantly colliding, occasionally causing the entire space to tremble. The originally flat ground was now covered with golden icicles and shocking beast claw marks, making one feel as if they were in an ice cellar somewhere in the extreme cold. The two figures crossed and intertwined, their fierce entanglement making the scene look somewhat stalemate. Camilla was clearly not using her full strength, because she wanted to capture Alice alive, which left her somewhat hesitant. Moreover, Camilla's strongest magic, the Blood Moon Swamp, had already been used on Merlin, so naturally she couldn't use it on Alice. This greatly discounted Camilla's strength; her state in fighting Alice was far from perfect, yet she could still faintly maintain the upper hand and suppress her opponent. In contrast, Alice had no reservations; without the hostage restriction, she could go all out, her strikes especially vicious, wishing to seal Camilla's throat with her sword! Alice's chilling aura continually swept the valley; her flashing blade assault was unstoppable, frequently entangling with Camilla's claws. The little girl hid behind a distant stone, shivering as she watched everything outside, her troubled eyes showing concern: 'Mom...' Alice had somewhat given up on close combat, because she realized that fighting Camilla up close yielded no benefit. If she could restrain the agile Camilla, Alice felt she still had a chance to kill this troublesome foe in one strike. 'You must be feeling tired too, right? It's time to obediently become my hostage, then go threaten Lucifer....' Camilla revealed a mysterious smile, her two sharp claws slashing through the air, a tremendous rending force instantly bursting forth, viciously raking across Alice's body. In terms of speed, Alice was indeed considerably inferior to Camilla, which was also her greatest weakness. 'Ahhh!' Alice screamed, her abdomen torn open by Camilla's claws, forcing her to retreat repeatedly. 'What gave you the illusion that you could defeat me? Stop dreaming, okay? As long as you obey, you'll suffer a little less fleshly pain.' The membrane wings behind Camilla slowly unfurled, like she was stretching. 'You're dreaming!' Alice glared with furious golden eyes, clutching her wounded abdomen; her dragon scales were brutally torn by Camilla, oozing crimson blood. Hmph, then don't blame me. Camilla didn't say a word, but her face suddenly changed, as if she had just learned something terrible, her expression revealing tension. What! ? My Blood Moon Swamp has been destroyed! ? This means Lucifer the Third has already escaped his restraint! No wonder he's the Great Demon Lord that makes the Holy Church tremble; a world created by magic has no effect on him at all! Clearly the Blood Moon Swamp imprisons countless magical beasts, and powerful monsters are as numerous as cows' hair! Could it be that even these cannot defeat this young Demon Lord? What a terrifying fellow..0 Camilla sighed inwardly, her face turning deathly pale as she gazed toward the direction of Avignon's main city. At this moment, Camilla realized Merlin had regained his freedom; finding him here was probably just a matter of time. If Lucifer the Third comes here, I might face a situation of being attacked from both front and rear, which would be truly disastrous. Camilla decided to increase her offensive power, to make Alice submit quickly; dragging things out would be deadly for her. Alice saw Camilla zoning out, raised her slender sword, seized the opportunity, and directly unleashed a Frost Lance. With its incredible speed and range, it left the somewhat dazed Camilla off‑guard, the golden ice spear piercing her heart! The Frost Lance kept shooting out, its distance continually increasing, like a golden spear running through the entire valley! 'Damn it!' Camilla was directly stabbed by Alice's Frost Lance onto the opposite rock wall, her whole body pinned there. Alice felt delighted inside; this strike should have pierced Camilla's heart, so it ought to be effective, right? Camilla showed a hint of pain, used her claws to sever the ice spear, fell from the rock wall, and then slowly pulled out the half‑ice shard embedded in her heart, blood still spraying during the process. ...Alice saw Camilla acting as if nothing had happened, couldn't help but frown heavily, thinking 'Even though the heart was pierced, it still didn't work? Indeed only direct damage from silver can kill.' 'Don't push your luck, you bitch!' Camilla's features twisted into a grotesque grimace, obviously enraged by Alice; her pierced heart was healing at a visible speed, 'Since you refuse to compromise, if you'd rather be dead than alive, I'll grant you that!' No sooner had the words fallen than Camilla, like a black cat, sprang into action with incredible speed. That agile black shadow fell into Alice's sight; she could only see a dark shape darting back and forth before her eyes. Camilla brandished her sharp claws, launching a peerless ferocious assault against Alice! Alice had just raised her slender sword to block when she was struck heavily from behind by the claws! Because Camilla's speed was astonishing, aside from the continual swooshing sounds, it was nearly impossible to catch her silhouette! This allowed Camilla to attack from all 360 degrees, more lethal than a sneak attack, making it hard to defend against. Alice suffered Camilla's consecutive heavy grabs; the shards on her body shattered one after another, blood continuously splattering, her screams echoing throughout the tranquil valley. 'Haha, how's that? Since you won't obey, now you know my power, huh? Scream! Cry! You have absolutely no chance of winning!' Camilla literally made Alice shed a layer of skin; even her dragon form was about to be torn apart alive, showing Camilla's brutality. 'Mom!' the little girl cried, seeing Alice beaten into this state, her heart aching immensely, even having the urge to rush out. After enduring a series of heavy blows, Alice's flesh and blood became a blur, almost entirely torn open by Camilla's attacks! Although the dragon form greatly increased her defenses, those defenses seemed useless under Camilla's claws. Alice swayed her body, collapsed powerlessly to the ground, her consciousness beginning to blur.... 'Anyone who tries to resist me ends up badly; this is your fate.' Camilla slowly approached Alice, grabbed her neck and lifted her off the ground, 'Although I don't want to kill you, I'm quite happy to torture you.' Alice was lifted by Camilla, unable to muster any strength, her whole body limp as if she'd lost her soul; this wave of devastation truly harmed her core. 'Should I chop off your arms, or your legs? Or maybe cut them all off, turning you into a useless puppet, then keep you in a little jar to raise—how nice! Let's do just that! Don't call me a pervert; I just like seeing people mutilated, hahaha....' Camilla raised her sharp claws, her inner urge stirring, her eyes blazing with fervor. But who would have thought Alice would suddenly lift her head slowly, her golden pupils blazing like flames, her aura surging as if injected with chicken blood, using her remaining strength to twist Camilla's arm, 'Get lost!' -A gust of icy cold wind centered on Alice swept up, its mighty force directly blowing Camilla away! Zero‑degree wind and snow intertwined, causing the valley's weather to change abruptly, bringing heavy snowfall like goose feathers. The pallid storm resembled a scythe, scraping nonstop; this sudden blizzard truly left one bewildered. Camilla furrowed her brows and slowly crawled up from the ground, clutching her twisted arm as she looked ahead. In the midst of the blizzard, a solitary shadow resembling a dragon flickered in and out, appearing extraordinarily solemn and beautiful. 'What is that?' (正_工)

title: Chapter 34 — The Ice River Reappears
content:
Chapter 34 — The Ice River Reappears

Volume 16 · Chapter 34

Kamila set her dislocated bones back in place, staring intently at the center of the blizzard.

Since the blizzard kept gathering toward the center, Kamila had no idea what was happening inside.

Only a massive dragon shadow flickered in and out, seeming to materialize out of thin air—a dragon of enormous size.

Based on the towering silhouette, Kamila deduced the monster wasn't small, nearly filling the entire valley.

What was going on?

This sudden surge of power...

Kamila's face turned ugly as she beheld the overwhelming draconic aura. She had to raise her guard.

Because she sensed this pressure was unusual, and far too powerful.

Only the Blizzard Sacred Dragon had ever exerted such pressure on Kamila, fighting for three days and three nights without being able to defeat the dragon king.

Yet now Kamila felt the same pressure from Alice, as if facing a truly formidable sacred dragon.

No way?

This human woman actually wielded such immense pressure.

Having draconic power isn't enough—could she even transform into a real dragon?

Kamila narrowed her eyes, staring into the depths of the blizzard, suspecting Alice might be a transformed dragon.

She had never heard of inheritance crystals before—usually only found in very ancient texts.

With a deafening roar that shook heaven and earth, the sky and ground trembled, and the falling snow began to flow upward!

The tremendous shockwave rippled outward, scattering the converging blizzard and finally revealing what was happening at the center of the storm!

A massive white dragon with blue scales slowly emerged, powerful limbs, wings that blotted out the sky, and horns like precious gems.

This form was almost identical to the Frost Sacred Dragon Malthus—seemingly reborn and returned once more.

The Frost Sacred Dragon slowly lifted its massive head, golden eyes burning with flames, spreading its strong wings, and instantly scoffed at the fierce cold wind!

A cold sweat dripped down Kamila's forehead as she raised her arm to block the chill, her whole body beginning to stiffen.

What the hell is this?!

Why can this human woman transform into such a powerful dragon?!

This is too abnormal—has she been suppressing this power from the very beginning?!

A dragon with such strength would be top-tier even among dragons!

Kamila recalled the Six Sacred Dragons. Among them, only the Frost Sacred Dragon Malthus was ice-attribute—the legendary beast that once froze the entire Greenland Sea in a single night.

The little girl hid behind a rock, peeking out her head to look at the Frost Sacred Dragon that had appeared out of nowhere, her expression confused, seemingly not understanding where her mother had gone.

The Frost Sacred Dragon stopped flapping its wings, its golden pupils fixed on the tiny Kamila below, its expression growing increasingly vicious.

Kamila, enduring the intense draconic pressure, dared to mock, "Oh? You actually transformed into a dragon? Are you really human? Honestly, I'm starting to lose track of your identity. This overwhelming pressure... it's probably only comparable to a sacred dragon..."

The Frost Sacred Dragon narrowed its eyes, shook its wings, and suddenly struck—condensing its combat aura into a single massive dragon fist that slammed hard into the tiny Kamila.

A punch launched by a dragon's body carried tremendous force and speed, striking Kamila in the blink of an eye.

Kamila took the full brunt of the dragon fist head-on, the immense power sending her flying, crashing through several massive stone pillars in a row, spewing blood.

The Frost Sacred Dragon soared into the air, descending upon the ground below Kamila, seemingly preparing to press its advantage.

Kamila wiped the blood from her lips, hatred burning in her eyes as she glared up at the Frost Sacred Dragon in the sky, "Don't get too cocky! Even if you've turned into a dragon, so what?!"

The Frost Sacred Dragon spread its wings, and the wind and snow across the horizon stilled for a moment, then erupted into a fierce golden snowstorm that battered Kamila.

The golden snowstorm was devastatingly destructive, raging across the vast area below, accompanied by Kamila's pained screams—

"AAAAAHHHH!"

The Frost Sacred Dragon kept flapping its wings, the storm growing more intense and powerful.

The snowstorm seemed to be Alice's secret technique from the Great Snow Mountain, fusing magic and combat aura into one, displaying a dazzling color. Even its offensive capability had leveled up—the golden snowflakes were sharper than blades. One could imagine the torment awaiting the center of the storm, possibly getting torn apart into pieces.

Kamila strained with all her might to break through the snowstorm, her body bloodied and battered, her eyes filled with killing intent, revealing her sharp claws.

She had come to regret it—she shouldn't have toyed with Alice like that. Now she was clearly losing ground and struggling to keep up.

Originally, Kamila wasn't afraid of any sacred dragon. Even her peer, the Blizzard Sacred Dragon, had been killed by her. The Frost Sacred Dragon naturally wouldn't pose much threat.

But Kamila's strongest magic was constructing a false world—a fake realm that had sealed away countless magical beasts, the Blood Moon Marsh.

Unfortunately, that secret weapon had been used against Merlin and then destroyed. There was no way she could recreate a false world to trap the Frost Sacred Dragon in such a short time.

So now Kamila's power had suffered a major setback. Facing the Frost Sacred Dragon, she could only be suppressed, unable to gain the upper hand.

Yet Kamila's heart burned with indignation. Leaping from the spot, she aimed to tear the Frost Sacred Dragon right out of the sky!

Unknown to her, the Frost Sacred Dragon was even more shameless. It opened its jaws and unleashed a stream of dragon's breath at the approaching Kamila, giving her no chance to resist.

The dragon's breath erupted from the Frost Sacred Dragon's mouth like a massive laser beam, sweeping everything in its path.

The temperature of this breath was so low it instantly froze the entire valley and surrounding area, coating it in a layer of white frost.

"AAAAAHHHHHHHH!"

Kamila screamed in agony as the dragon's breath struck her. Though it wouldn't kill her, the pain was unavoidable.

Before long, half her body was frozen solid, shattering into countless ice fragments with the slightest movement, her left side completely destroyed.

But a vampire's vitality was formidable. Lilman regenerated from her half-dead state, proving harder to kill than even a cockroach.

"You bastard! You dare reduce me to such humiliation! Even if I kill you ten thousand times, it won't quench my hatred!"

The Frost Sacred Dragon's expression shifted several times, circling the valley in the air before swooping down and grabbing the little girl hiding behind the rocks, tossing her onto its back.

"YAAAH!" The little girl shrieked, completely at a loss, landing on the Frost Sacred Dragon's mane at its neck.

"Hold on tight, baby." The Frost Sacred Dragon suddenly spoke in Alice's voice.

"Mommy?" The little girl stared with wide, blank eyes at the towering dragon before her, completely baffled as to why this blue-and-white dragon was speaking in Alice's voice.

The Frost Sacred Dragon didn't waste words, immediately soaring into the sky, flying higher, seemingly preparing to flee.

"YAAAAAAHHHH!" The little girl screamed under the intense acceleration, her tiny hands barely clinging to the Frost Sacred Dragon's fur, nearly falling from the sky!

"Trying to run? Useless!" Kamila followed, launching herself into the air, flapping her membrane wings in pursuit of the Frost Sacred Dragon.

Kamila's magic surged wildly, gathering all her power into her sharp claws before swinging them out, unleashing her strongest tearing slash.

The powerful tearing wave sliced through the air with a "swoosh swoosh swoosh," its range and destructive force both terrifying!

The previously calm space began to distort slightly, and this tearing wave was now surging forward with overwhelming force, nearly devouring the Frost Sacred Dragon that had taken to the sky.

This time, Kamila was like a madwoman, determined to tear the Frost Sacred Dragon apart with her bare hands!

The Frost Sacred Dragon glanced back once, conjuring up an imposing great iceberg to block the tearing slash.

But this time, Kamila's attack was no ordinary strike—comparable to the great iceberg of the Avignon main city being instantly shredded.

If that great iceberg were hurled at Avignon, it could probably destroy the entire main city!

"You think you're so clever?!" Kamila roared, shaking her wings and pressing on.

The Frost Sacred Dragon's attack only managed to block Kamila, but that was enough—it bought time to unleash its ultimate magic.

When the Frost Sacred Dragon reached a certain altitude, it began to dance slowly in the sky and let out a primordial, low chant.

The Frost Sacred Dragon unfurled its sky-obscuring wings, emitting a dazzling light that bathed the entire mountain range in daylight.

After hundreds of years, the dragon's glorious presence still awed the former kingdom. The ultra-powerful magic that froze the entire Greenland Sea was about to reappear—

"Ice Age Descension!"

title: Chapter 35 — Thoughts of Retreat
content:
Chapter 35 — Thoughts of Retreat

Volume 16 · Chapter 35

Merlin was tending to old Akarone's wounds; there were still more than a dozen arrows protruding from his body.

Fortunately, there was no danger at the moment, and the surroundings were safe — unlike the Blood Moon Swamp, which had been fraught with peril at every turn.

Akarone's backpack contained healing potions, and applying some to his wounds had a good stopping-blood effect.

Merlin helped Akarone apply the medicine and felt that, at the very least, there would no longer be a life-threatening situation; he could hold out for a while.

"Feeling better?"

"Much better. Sorry for causing you so much trouble."

Akarone winced in pain as he spoke, lying obediently on the ground, having barely escaped with his life.

He felt that he and Merlin and Alice did not belong in the same world — he was always slowing them down.

This dealt a considerable blow to the old man's pride, and he felt deeply guilty about it.

Akarone had already begun thinking about returning to Little Cow Town; he was not the type to shamelessly hang around.

He knew he was constantly getting in everyone's way, and staying in the party like this was wrong.

Moreover, Merlin and Alice had already found clues about the blood kin, and they essentially didn't need Akarone's help anymore.

"It's fine. You're older after all, and there are many things you can't handle as well as you used to." Merlin said lightly, as though he didn't mind it much. Although Akarone always seemed to mess things up, he was still somewhat useful. But the enemies Merlin and Alice encountered were often far too powerful for him, so having Akarone by their side was indeed dangerous.

Akarone was only supposed to be their guide in France, yet he kept running into dangers far beyond his level. The old man was already emotionally and physically exhausted.

He knew exactly what he was capable of and couldn't be an equal companion to Merlin and Alice. Rather than getting in their way here, it would be better for him to return to his retirement in Little Cow Town.

Adventuring was the sort of thrilling pursuit clearly meant for young people, and it no longer suited old Akarone. During this journey, he had seen many things he had never even dared to dream of before, and his heart was deeply satisfied.

Slowly, Akarone reached into his chest and handed Merlin the letter he had stolen from Camilla's study. Although some of it had been dampened by water, he could still make out the writing.

"What's this?" Merlin's expression turned puzzled; he had no idea what this was.

"These are letters exchanged between Camilla and Chancellor Mades. I found them in the study. It's obvious from the correspondence that the two of them were secretly colluding, and they are closely linked to the bizarre, frequent disappearances of the Avignon refugees. The Empire's chancellor and Camilla share a deep relationship — perhaps the blood kin you are looking for could very well be him." Akarone said in a hoarse voice.

"Is that so?"

Merlin took the letter and glanced at it. This could very well be an important clue going forward. Since Camilla was a member of the blood kin, this Empire chancellor's identity was equally suspicious.

Perhaps they could follow the trail and uncover an even greater secret?

Merlin stroked his chin. The contents of the letter were roughly what Akarone had described — it seemed Camilla was merely a pawn, and this chancellor, Mades, was the one behind the scenes.

"I see. So many kidnapped people were smuggled to the imperial capital. It seems we'll need to pay a visit there...."

Akarone lowered his head and said with deep self-reproach, "Lord Merlin, I am terribly sorry for my incompetence. I always mess things up at critical moments. Therefore, I intend to return to Little Cow Town once my injuries have healed. From then on, I leave everything in your hands."

"Huh? Why?" Merlin didn't quite understand. Weren't they doing just fine? Although Akarone often blundered, a guide was still very necessary. Otherwise, he and Alice would be like headless flies in France, unable to find their bearings at all.

"Weren't you came to France to find the hidden blood kin? Now that the clues have been found, my job is over." Akarone sighed and said helplessly, "Besides, my abilities are limited, and I can't be of any help to you. I'll only ever slow you down. For a useless old man like me, it's better to go back and retire early."

"Who says you're useless? You've already helped us a great deal!" Merlin waved the letter in his hand. For someone like Akarone, this was already quite something.

"What is this? Lord Merlin, please don't comfort me. I know perfectly well what I'm capable of." Akarone wore a resigned expression. "The enemies you encounter are terrifyingly strong — I've witnessed that firsthand. We don't live in the same world. Rather than staying behind and forcing you to split your energy to look after an old codger like me, it's better if I leave. That would be a good thing for me; I wouldn't have to live in constant fear anymore."

Merlin fell silent for a moment and felt that Akarone wasn't entirely wrong. They had already found traces of the blood kin.

Since bringing Akarone along would surely expose him to many dangers, perhaps it was better to rely solely on himself and Alice from here on and let the old man rest.

"Well then, thank you for everything throughout this journey."

"I should be the one thanking you. Although it was only a month, I've experienced more in that time than in my entire life — so it hasn't been in vain." Akarone sighed and said with emotion, "The truth is, I'm not a capable person, nor am I an experienced adventurer. I'm a complete and utter failure. I've never truly adventured in my life — I don't even know what a goblin looks like. As for a silver-rank adventurer? That's just me shamelessly blagging my way up, doing pointless low-grade quests day after day just to accumulate rank points."

Merlin didn't say anything. He felt that Akarone's tone was filled with bitterness, like a insignificant person at the bottom of society letting out a cry.

He had long noticed that Akarone was completely ordinary, without a single noteworthy quality.

Although Akarone was one rank higher than Merlin, he was weak to the point of being unbearable to watch....

Merlin found it hard to empathize with Akarone's feelings; he himself was powerful and lived a colorful life.

But the vast majority of people were much like Akarone — burning with passion yet never able to experience true adventure.

Merlin had dwelt at the pinnacle for so long that he rarely noticed the pitiful worms at the very bottom anymore.

"Still, following you, I finally got to experience what a real adventurer's life is like. That has fulfilled a wish of mine. Even if I die, I'll have no regrets." Akarone seemed to have aged significantly.

"Weren't you always saying your adventurer's soul was blazing fiercely? And now it's gone?" Merlin said in an amused tone.

"Gone, gone. Witnessing the life of a true adventurer is far more dangerous than I ever imagined." Akarone didn't shy away and continued, "At first I wanted to follow you to experience an adventurer's life because the opportunity was rare, but reality is cruel. An old guy like me will never become as strong as you."

"I see...." Merlin sat down on the ground beside Akarone and said mildly, "Actually, aren't you stronger than me?"

"Eh?!" Akarone was suddenly stunned, not understanding what Merlin meant.

"Compared to me, you're the one who looks more like a true adventurer." Merlin patted Akarone on the shoulder. "You are the role model for all of us black iron-rank adventurers."

"Don't tease me, Lord Merlin." Akarone managed a bitter smile.

"I'm not teasing you. In a certain sense, you really are a kind of strong person." Merlin said seriously.

"As expected of Lord Merlin, even your jokes come across so seriously...."

Akarone smiled helplessly, raised his head, and looked toward the distance — only to see a shining starlight streaking straight toward the heavens above the mountains outside Avignon's main city!

Because Akarone's eyesight was poor, he couldn't make out what it was at all; he could only vaguely perceive the object emitting brilliant light.

"Hm?" Merlin followed Akarone's gaze. His vision was far superior, and at first glance, he was greatly startled.

Bg!?

Malygos!?

Wait, the Frost Holy Dragon died long ago. This...

Alice?

~o~;)

title: Chapter 36 — The End (Extra Update)
content:
Chapter 36 — The End (Extra Update)

Volume 16 · Chapter 36

Merlin could see it quite clearly; despite the distance, he could still make out the figure of the Frost Holy Dragon soaring straight into the sky! Why would I encounter the already-dead Frost Holy Dragon here? Could it have inexplicably risen from the dead? Merlin didn't react at first, but after a moment he figured it out. It's likely that Alice has already mastered most of the power of the inheritance crystals, beginning to take on a humanoid dragon form, able to be compared with the true Frost Holy Dragon. This is the proper use of the inheritance crystals; forcing them like the four heroes of the former kingdom, Carolona, did is wrong—not only can one not become a humanoid dragon, but one also loses sanity. Merlin furrowed his brows, thinking: to what extent has Alice been pushed to raise her strength another level? Now it's likely that her magic and battle aura have reached great perfection, both at their peak. "Merlin, what is that? Can you see it clearly?" Old Akalon asked curiously beside him. "It's Alice, there should be no mistake." Merlin answered affirmatively, standing up and gazing at the distant mountains; it seemed Alice hadn't been moved too far, just outside the main city of Avignon. "Ah?! It's actually Miss Alice, what on earth happened over there?!" Old Akalon exclaimed in surprise, sensing something was amiss. "I don't know.... Merlin doesn't know the exact details, but surely she encountered a strong enemy; otherwise why would she suddenly turn into the Frost Holy Dragon. The previously tranquil night sky began to slowly drizzle snow, the temperature suddenly turned cold, each breath visible as white vapor. Suddenly, a strong blast of cold air surged in, causing the temperature to drop as if winter had arrived instantly; the whole of Avignon was shrouded in winter! "Hiss hiss hiss hiss..... Old Akalon shivered uncontrollably, a layer of frost forming on his eyebrows—what's wrong?" "Tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue once, feeling that Alice's location was rather far; Avignon's main city was merely affected by the spillover, otherwise the entire region would surely be frozen solid, casualties uncountable... From above, after the baptism of the ice river's descent. The entire mountain range was draped in silver, everywhere white snow. Translucent golden ice crystals were interspersed like pillars propping up the snow mountains. The ice river's descent covered a vast area; the mountain range was almost completely frozen; even if there were living beings, if not strong enough they would have frozen to death outright. Just a few minutes ago this place was a vibrant mountain, but the assassins have turned into lifeless ice mountains, as if sealed in ice for over ten years. Actually the Frost Holy Dragon's strength is not weak; most people would feel fear facing it, but against Merlin even the strongest foe would be struck down with no power to retaliate, so its strength cannot be judged. After the terrifying ice river's descent, that beautiful and dignified dragon also vanished, Alice returned to her human form. In the valley, Camilla had turned into an ice block, her entire body encased in golden ice; even a heavenly-skilled assassin couldn't move. But Camilla wasn't dead yet; her eyes darted around, revealing panic—she probably didn't expect to be counter-killed in desperation. What the hell! How could this happen?! Why did the final move become so perverse?! A wide-area indiscriminate freeze—this is basically impossible to escape, right?! Damn! If only there were a Blood Marsh Swamp, a mere Frost Holy Dragon couldn't hold me! ! What now? I feel I can hardly break free of the icy seal..... Camilla felt remorseful; she had thought tormenting Alice would be easy, but she hadn't expected it to be no pushover, secretly suffering a loss. Alice held a slender sword, slowly walking from afar, her dragonization already undone, and her wounds had healed considerably. Now Alice's strength has indeed advanced a step; her battle aura keeps pace with her magic, reaching the Saint-tier peak. Alice's next target is likely the higher realm that only a few can reach—the Ancestral Realm. Alice has almost mastered most of the dragon race's martial arts and magic, barely distinguishable from a true Frost Holy Dragon; combined with the secret technique of fusing with the great snow mountain, she surpasses her teacher, the title of humanoid dragon truly deserved. Upon activating dragonization, she can still become a Frost Holy Dragon—not just a partial dragonization, but truly achieving free switching. However, only 75% of Alice's inheritance crystals have been utilized; the remaining 25% is unresponsive, completely ignoring her commands. Even though Alice now matches the true Frost Holy Dragon in every way, even slightly stronger, she still cannot draw out 100% of the inheritance crystals' power. This likely indicates only one thing: the true Frost Holy Dragon, Marilegus, probably also cannot unleash the full power of the dragon race. The dragon race seems to have some secret preventing it from exerting 100% of its own power, only able to use a portion. Alice can't figure out what she's lacking; even the true Frost Holy Dragon Marilegus can't do it, so she seems even less likely to achieve 100% of the dragon race's power. But at this moment Alice doesn't care about these problems; her eyes are only on Camilla, her mind filled with killing this wicked woman. Camilla saw Alice approaching her, her expression instantly showing obvious panic; her state was extremely passive, like a lamb awaiting slaughter, unable to move. Alice stood before Camilla, her gaze piercing, "I've won—what do you feel now? Who really is the prey?" Camilla, encased in ice, even if her mind was full of regret, couldn't utter a word; she could only stare blankly. "Are you thinking that a mere vassal of Lucifer the Third dares to show off in front of you? Right?" Alice looked at Camilla's eyes. Camilla's eyes flickered a few times; her thoughts matched what Alice said—she thought Alice was merely a plaything of the Great Demon Lord, what right did she have to act so arrogantly before her? "I want to tell you, I am not Lucifer's vassal; without him I would still live, and perhaps even better; moreover I despise the despicable tactic of taking hostages!" Alice raised her slender sword and viciously stabbed it into the ice-encased Camilla's chest, ending the woman's life. The ice-encased Camilla's eyes glazed over; she received a fatal blow and was completely dead. "The Hymn of Light" originally is the bane of dark creatures; Alice also pierced Camilla's heart. Even though Camilla is a vampire with strong self-healing ability, she cannot withstand this blow. Only see Camilla within the golden ice beginning to burn, her face covered with red blood vessels, her body gradually disintegrating. At the brink of death, Camilla gave Alice an eerie smile, her heart still filled with contempt, using her last strength to let out a cry: "The Eternal Night Empire is coming; none can escape!" "Humans, you are only fit to be our slaves!!!"

title: Chapter 37 — Farewells
content:
Chapter 37 — Farewells

Volume 16 · Chapter 37

A few days later.

The unrest in Avignon had gradually subsided, but the city was still in a state of chaos, with people on edge and anxious.

This was because the lord’s manor had been attacked in the night several days ago, and Camilla had mysteriously vanished—like she’d simply evaporated.

The people assumed that Avignon had been infiltrated by a brutal criminal, who had destroyed the count’s manor and killed the lord.

The most likely suspects were Merlin and Alice, those British adventurers who had just been put on the wanted list. They were now irrevocably linked to the murderous spree.

With Camilla dead, Avignon was taken over by the garrison, barely maintaining order in the city.

But now that Merlin and Alice were wanted criminals, their movements in France would face significant obstacles.

Over these days, the two hadn’t gone out much, fearing unwanted attention and trouble, instead packing their belongings to prepare for their journey to the imperial capital.

Old Akalon’s injuries had recovered well enough that he could move on his own, though his legs still needed rest, and he now relied on a cane.

Alice had been spending her days with the little girl, their bond growing increasingly close. Every time Merlin saw them together, he couldn’t bear to interrupt.

The little girl was very attached to Alice and obedient, though Alice never said as much—she likely cared for the child deeply.

Merlin’s emotions were still complicated. He had no real desire to become a father, partly because the little girl didn’t seem to like him at all, making it hard for him to appreciate her charm.

The real problem was how to handle the little girl—she was clearly a danger. Merlin had already realized that bringing her along would be risky.

They were already constantly in danger, and adding a child to the mix would only make things harder. Just look at this time—the little girl had been kidnapped, causing them no small amount of trouble.

Late at night, Alice tucked the little girl into bed and soothed her gently, saying, “Go to sleep now, or the Great Demon Lord will come and eat you.”

“Why would he eat me?” the little girl asked, looking pitifully innocent.

“Because you’re not being good,” Alice said seriously, scaring the child. “The First Demon Lord especially likes to eat children who don’t listen and don’t go to sleep early.”

“...Mommy, I’ll be good,” the little girl whispered, closing her eyes obediently.

Alice smiled, stroking the little girl’s black hair before standing up and leaving the room—only to find Merlin leaning against the wall.

“Ugh! You always drag me into this,” Merlin raised his head, his tone slightly grumbling. “I’d never eat a little kid—I don’t have that habit! Honestly, scaring children is always your job, not mine. Who did I offend?”

“Where do you get off saying that?” Alice defended herself. “You’re the villain—how else would you scare a child?”

“...I have nothing to say.” Merlin spread his hands, realizing that as the Demon Lord, he was always the one used to frighten children. His image was only getting worse, and it seemed he’d forever be stuck in the role of the villain.

But these were trivial matters, and Merlin didn’t really care. He just found it annoying to be constantly portrayed as a monster that eats people.

“Did you come to see me about something?” Alice cut to the chase, assuming Merlin wouldn’t be standing around idly.

“Yeah, I’ve almost finished packing. Tomorrow morning, we’ll leave Avignon and head straight for the imperial capital in France.”

“Leave tomorrow? That’s fast.”

Alice lowered her head, knowing she’d already learned about Camilla’s correspondence with the imperial chancellor. “Is the imperial chancellor really the mastermind?”

“There’s no doubt about it,” Merlin said after a pause, his tone heavy with meaning. “The letters were clear—Camilla’s kidnapped victims were all sent to the imperial chancellor. Even if he’s not the true mastermind, he’s definitely a big fish. If we expose the bloodline here, we might drag out the entire French demon race. Then the secrets of the Dracula ruins would surface.”

That makes sense. So many people were kidnapped and sent to the capital—there must be some secret going on in the background... Alice furrowed her brows, looking puzzled.

“Once we reach the capital, we’ll investigate. There should be some results,” Merlin said, though he still had no clear plan. He then changed the subject. “After we leave tomorrow, we’ll temporarily leave the little girl with Old Akalon.”

“What?!” Alice gasped, startled by Merlin’s words.

“Our mission is too dangerous, and Old Akalon can’t continue as our guide anymore,” Merlin explained. “He’s decided to return to Cow Town, which is perfect—we can temporarily entrust the little girl to him. Once everything is over, we’ll figure out what to do with her.”

“Yeah, he feels like he’s holding us back,” Merlin continued. “Even if there’s trouble, he can’t help much. Now that we’ve found a lead on the bloodline, he should go rest.”

Alice didn’t think it was right to leave the little girl with Old Akalon. She might get upset, thinking Alice had abandoned her.

“But...leaving her with Old Akalon isn’t right,” Alice hesitated. “She’ll probably be heartbroken, thinking I’ve abandoned her.”

“Alice, this is for her own good,” Merlin said seriously. “You’ve seen how dangerous it is—if we’re not careful, she’ll be kidnapped again. Can you guarantee she’ll never be in danger again? Think about it—kids don’t have the sense to understand.”

“...” Alice lowered her head, torn by indecision. Merlin was right—the little girl was too much of a risk to keep around while they were still on the mission.

It seemed they had no choice but to temporarily leave her with Old Akalon.

---

The next morning.

Merlin and Alice arranged for a carriage and left Avignon in secret, avoiding attention.

Now that they were wanted criminals, suspected of assassinating the French lord, they had to stay low.

Old Akalon, carrying the little girl, said goodbye to Merlin and Alice.

“Are you really leaving?” Old Akalon asked.

“Yes,” Merlin said calmly. “With Camilla dead, the imperial chancellor might escalate things, so we should go to the capital as soon as possible, in case something changes.”

“Old Akalon, please take care of the little girl for us,” Alice said seriously. “We’ll return to Cow Town once we’re done, and we won’t bother you.”

Old Akalon patted the little girl’s head, scratching his head. “Don’t be so formal. Whatever Alice asks, I’ll do my best. You can trust me—I’ll take care of her like my own granddaughter.”

“Thank you,” Alice bowed slightly, grateful. But she still felt a pang of reluctance, knowing she was leaving the little girl behind.

“Mommy, don’t leave! Don’t abandon me!” The little girl threw herself into Alice’s arms, tears streaming down her face, her eyes red and swollen.

Alice sighed, kneeling down to look into the little girl’s eyes. “Mommy has to go to a very dangerous place. I’ll come back after finishing my work—I’m not abandoning you. You have to be good, okay?”

“But...what if I never see you again?” the little girl cried, heartbroken.

“Don’t be silly,” Alice smiled, holding out her little finger. “I promise I’ll come back for you. If you don’t believe me, we can make a promise.”

The little girl hesitated for a moment before hooking her little finger with Alice’s. “Mommy, I’ll wait for you.”

“Then you have to be very good,” Alice said, her eyes slightly red. “Mommy doesn’t like naughty children. You have to listen to Old Akalon, okay?”

“Yes, Mommy,” the little girl nodded firmly, her eyes still red and sad.

Merlin watched from afar as Alice and the little girl linked their little fingers, sighing deeply.

What will happen after this?

Alice...

Is she really pretending to be serious now?

title: Chapter 1 — Margaret
content:
Chapter 1 — Margaret

Volume 17 · Chapter 1

The French capital, the arena.

"Ahhhhhhhhhh!!!"

A young man screamed in agony, being knocked to the ground.

He was a swordsman from a foreign land, who had come specifically to marry Princess Margaret.

According to the rules of the duel for marriage, only someone who could defeat the first hero of France could have a chance.

Many people from other countries had been blocked by this obstacle, and so far, no one had succeeded.

The middle-aged man with a muscular upper body standing in the distance was the first hero of France, Blaze.

Blaze was a loyal fighter serving the royal family, becoming a Saint-tier strong warrior at a young age and serving as the commander of the royal knights.

Although he was already 38 years old, an undeniable middle-aged man, his strength had not declined at all, and had even become stronger.

Now Blaze was the commander of the elite troops, responsible for protecting the safety of the royal family, and was recognized as the first hero of France, along with the other two, known as the Three Knights of France.

Blaze was very muscular, with a solid body like a steel plate that could make a sound when hit, and just from his appearance, people felt fear.

Soldiers said he was a tank, and as long as he stood on the battlefield, France was invincible.

Unlike those with family lineage, Blaze had climbed step by step on his own.

His fighting style was called a "wild path" by the orthodox knights, and was completely like fighting in a tavern, using any low-down tricks to win.

Although he had no fighting style and often made sudden attacks, his character was not bad, and he was respected by the knights.

Blaze slowly put the heavy sword on his shoulder, which was three meters long and made of black mountain copper.

Black mountain copper was a very hard metal with excellent toughness, and was very suitable for Blaze, who was strong in brute force.

Rather than saying the giant sword was Blaze's weapon, it was more like his trophy, with the many obvious scratches on it being the best proof.

Every time Blaze defeated a Saint-tier strong warrior, he would carve a scratch on his heavy sword as a memorial.

Looking at the heavy sword with countless scratches, it was unknown how many Saint-tier strong warriors Blaze had defeated.

Blaze carried the giant sword and stood with it across his waist, looking down on the young man who had come to challenge him for the marriage.

"You don't have the qualifications to marry the princess, and you dare to challenge me as a high-tier warrior, is that suicide?"

"Uh..." The young man looked at the strong Blaze and trembled with fear.

"You are such a weak opponent that you will only waste my time. To be honest, I can defeat you with one finger." Blaze waved his hand and said arrogantly, "Please leave here quickly, you don't have the right to leave a mark on my heavy sword."

The young man was relieved and quickly left, already regretting his foolishness in coming to France, which was a disgrace to himself.

To have the first hero of France as an opponent, who could defeat him?

The duel for marriage was just a joke, and the princess of France, it seems, didn't even want to get married!

The arena was left with only Blaze, and he sighed as he looked around.

At the beginning of the duel for marriage, there were still many challengers.

However, because Blaze was too strong, he had repelled too many people, and gradually, fewer and fewer people wanted to challenge him.

A soldier entered the arena and knelt with one knee.

"Blaze, the princess has something to summon you."

◇

The royal palace, a luxurious bedroom.

A young and beautiful girl lay on the bed, with maids carefully trimming her nails.

She had long, auburn hair, and a face like a white jade sculpture, with a smooth, translucent complexion that radiated a captivating glow.

This was the infamous incompetent princess, Princess Margaret.

As the only child of the old king, she not only lacked any sense of responsibility but also ignored the people of the country who were in a state of crisis.

Now, after the great flood in the south, refugees were wandering everywhere, with no hope, while Margaret was busy playing, trimming her nails.

This was obviously not the attitude of an imperial heir, but rather that of a spoiled princess who was out of touch with the world.

That's why the people of France were worried about the future of the country, fearing that if Princess Margaret became queen, the country would be in eternal chaos.

A princess who treats her marriage as a joke and holds a duel for marriage, how could she possibly take on the responsibility of reviving France?

Not only the people of the empire, but even the nobles and ministers in the royal palace, were not pleased with Princess Margaret, considering her to be nothing more than a decorative item.

In fact, although Margaret was incompetent, her beauty was known throughout all the human empires, and the title of decorative item was not inappropriate, as almost everyone came to challenge her for marriage.

Blaze walked in directly from outside and knelt with one knee, "Your Majesty, I have come."

"Hmm?" Margaret slightly raised her head and waved her hand, "You can all go now."

The maids quickly stood up, bowed, and slowly left.

Blaze saw that the door was closed and asked in confusion, "Your Majesty, what do you need me for?"

"Did you drive away the flies today?" Margaret pointed to those who were reckless in seeking her affection, in her eyes, those men who sought her were like flies.

"Yes, the young men who came to participate in the duel for marriage were very weak, and the level of those who came to challenge has greatly declined. At the beginning, there were still a few decent Saint-tier warriors, but Your Majesty, you didn't even look at them..." Blaze said in a helpless tone.

"If you can't even beat me, how can I look at you? If I want to ally with someone, it must be someone who is invincible and unstoppable, otherwise, I would be at a disadvantage." Margaret said in a calm tone.

Blaze's expression became gloomy, he understood what Princess Margaret wanted to do, and needed strong allies to help her eliminate the power of the prime minister, Medes.

Actually, many people misunderstood this princess. Although she seemed crazy and never serious, in reality, Margaret was a girl with great ambition.

Margaret, of course, knew that as the imperial heir, she should strive to improve herself, but the current situation did not allow her to do so.

After all, Medes controls the eyes and ears in the capital, and Margaret is in a very disadvantageous position, and it is not suitable for her to show her abilities, and being foolish is safer.

Now Medes has been house arresting the old king, who is seriously ill, and often issues orders in the name of the king, acting like a regent.

In addition, he holds great power and has strong warriors under his command, and Medes has already become the actual ruler of the empire, and most nobles are flattering him.

Margaret? Just a foolish princess, without royal blood, she is nothing.

Moreover, only Medes can see the old king, and even Margaret does not have the right to see her father, and she has been completely marginalized.

"But Your Majesty, treating your marriage as a joke, the King will be angry. If possible, please consider the face of the royal family."

"The face of the royal family? When the empire falls into the hands of Medes, the royal family will have no face at all." Margaret stood up and walked to the window, saying coldly, "It's all my stupid father who fell into the trap of others and ended up in this situation. I haven't seen him for a long time."

"Your Majesty, please don't say that." Blaze saw Margaret mocking the old king and thought it was a bit disrespectful, "Even if it's not for the face of the royal family, please consider your own happiness. To marry, you must use marriage as a bargaining chip, otherwise, you can only attract a group of greedy and lustful trash."

"For my happiness? You're joking, I don't have the right to choose. I'm being watched by Medes' spies all day, with no freedom at all." Margaret paused and said in a emotionless tone, "To get everything back, I'm willing to pay any price. Except for this body that still looks good, I have nothing left. If you can kill Medes, I can sleep with you too..."

"Uh!" Blaze lowered his head and dared not look at Margaret, his heart was shocked by her words:

Your Majesty...

Has she...

Gone crazy?
