title: Chapter 2 — Deceiving Superiors and Concealing from Subordinates
content:
Chapter 2 — Deceiving Superiors and Concealing from Subordinates

Volume 17 · Chapter 2

"Your Highness, please don't joke like that." Blaise frowned, not looking directly at Marguerite at all. "Even if Your Highness is eager to kill Medes, there's no need to do something so vile. Besides, true elites are never swayed by beauty; most of them have severed their worldly desires and reached another level of mental cultivation."

"If not like this? What capital do I have to recruit powerful people? If you could defeat Medes, I wouldn't have to stoop to this, would I?" Marguerite glanced at Blaise.

"It's that I'm incompetent. Medes dominates the capital single-handedly; I alone truly cannot shake him, and his own strength surpasses mine." Blaise said with a reluctant expression.

In fact, Marguerite had already been secretly opposing Chancellor Medes and had once sent Blaise to assassinate him. The result was not only a failure but Blaise also suffered serious injuries, showing just how formidable an enemy Medes was.

After that, Medes began secretly surveilling Marguerite, knowing her every move. Now Marguerite had become a puppet, possessing only the title of imperial heir with absolutely no power.

"This is why I'm humiliating myself, isn't it? If I could help it, who would willingly use such a ridiculous matchmaking tournament?" Marguerite smiled, adding, "Someone you can't even defeat is completely worthless. What we need is someone who can kill Medes."

"But Your Highness really doesn't need to use your marriage as a bargaining chip. If His Majesty weren't critically ill, he definitely wouldn't allow you to do this."

Blaise was truly disgusted by Marguerite's actions; it disgraced the royal family's honor.

"This is my own choice and has nothing to do with anyone else. Besides, marrying a peerless elite is also a good choice—it can help us eliminate Medes, and in the future they'll become a pillar of the empire. Isn't this a win-win? You just need to do your own duties." Princess Marguerite said seriously.

"Yes, since Your Highness has decided, this subordinate will definitely do my utmost."

Blaise no longer said anything else, choosing silence instead. He felt the princess had completely become a pawn in the game of interests, which was undoubtedly cruel for such a young girl.

But right now, Chancellor Medes was deceiving superiors and hiding from subordinates, surveilling Princess Marguerite, deceiving the old king, and had completely taken over the entire Frankish Empire.

From this perspective, Marguerite indeed had no other choice except to become a sacrifice in a political marriage; there was no other path.

"Recently, scouts reported that things don't seem to be going well for Medes. Someone killed Carmilla, the Countess of Avignon. That woman was Medes' right-hand aide; her sudden death must be a significant blow to him." Marguerite revealed a meaningful smile.

"...Blaise widened his eyes, finding it hard to believe. Medes' faction had immense power in the empire; normally no one would dare to touch them." "Someone killed Carmilla? That powerful magician? Who did it?"

"They say it was two adventurers. They've already been wanted. Medes was furious, threw a tantrum in the parliament, and ordered all imperial guards to hunt down the two of them." Marguerite revealed a meaningful smile.

"No way, adventurers dare to kill imperial nobles?" Blaise was confused. A city lord's status is high; how could adventurers dare to strike against imperial elites?

"It's true. Now Medes has lost one arm, so to speak. After all, the enemy's enemy is a friend. This is a good thing for us." Marguerite paused and continued—

"Someone is secretly opposing Medes. We can try to make use of these two wanted criminals."

"Those who can kill the Lord of Avignon—their strength must be quite close..."

The old king's bedchamber.
Since falling ill, the King of Frank had been resting here, not leaving the room for a long time.

Because his whole body was paralyzed and weak, the old king was now like a useless person, needing others to care for his every need—eating, drinking, urinating, defecating.

The old king knew nothing of the outside world; all information came from Medes' mouth. The entire empire still seemed prosperous, having suffered no disasters.

This kept the old king living in a false reality woven by Medes' lies, completely unaware of the chaotic situation outside.

Medes was the old king's most trusted person—young and talented, deeply valued by him.

Before falling seriously ill, the old king had noticed Medes' talent and his very excellent leadership abilities. After falling ill, he promoted him to chancellor to manage the empire's affairs great and small.

In truth, the old king didn't know that his serious illness and bedridden state were entirely a conspiracy orchestrated by Medes.

Every day, Medes had someone feed the old king a slow-acting poison that not only worsened the king's condition but also indirectly affected his sanity.

At this time, Medes came as usual to visit the old king and fed him the chronic poison, worsening his condition.

The old king lay weak in bed. His white-haired appearance looked very lackluster, especially his sunken cheeks, wasting away to skin and bones.

"Cough! Cough cough! This medicine is so bitter!" The old king coughed, unable to bear it after just one sip.

Medes placed the decoction on the table and wiped the old king's mouth with a handkerchief. "Your Majesty, this medicine can treat your strange illness. To recover soon and govern the empire, you should drink it."

"Medes, you are truly loyal to me. Back then I didn't misjudge you; leaving the empire to you temporarily was the right choice," the old king said slowly, his body very weak.

"Your Majesty overestimates me. I'm merely doing my duty." Medes said humbly.

"Although this medicine should cure me, after taking it so long, I see no improvement at all. I also hope to take over the empire soon and not let all the pressure rest on your shoulders alone." The old king sighed.

"Your Majesty's illness is very peculiar. This medicine must be taken continuously to work. I hope Your Majesty understands." Medes said hypocritically.

"Put it aside for now; I'll drink it later." The old king showed a worried expression and continued asking, "How is the empire lately? Has anything happened?"

"Your Majesty, rest assured. Under my governance, the empire remains stable, the people live in peace and contentment, and everyone prays for your early recovery."

Medes smiled, showing absolutely no sign of being a villain.

"That's good. With you here, I'm at ease. I haven't wasted my effort promoting you to chancellor." The old king nodded with satisfaction, then asked about the princess's condition. "How is Marguerite lately? Even lying ill in bed, she doesn't come to visit me."

"Her Highness..." Medes wanted to speak but stopped, not knowing what to say.

"What's wrong? Could something have happened to her?" The old king couldn't help but worry.

"No, Her Highness is still the same—playful and irresponsible. Many people are dissatisfied with her." Medes shook his head, adding fuel to the fire.

"After all, Her Highness is the empire's only heir, yet she has absolutely no sense of responsibility."

"You've been critically ill for so long, yet you're still thinking about fun and refuse to come visit."

"If this continues, the empire's future is worrying."

"I think it would be better to send Princess Marguerite to the frontier to gain experience."

"Thus she can experience the people's suffering and her identity as heir, gaining new understanding."

"What does Your Majesty think?"

title: Chapter 3 — The Imperial Capital in Peril
content:
Chapter 3 — The Imperial Capital in Peril

Volume 17 · Chapter 3

Facing Medes' proposal, the old king fell into hesitation and did not give a clear answer. "This matter... allow me to consider it. Margaret has never endured much hardship since she was young, but I believe her nature is not bad."

Medes' expression turned slightly ugly. He had originally wanted to drive away this troublesome princess, but failed. Even after consuming the mind-altering drug for so long, the old king was still cautious when it came to Margaret.

"I am already quite tired, Lord Medes. You may withdraw for now," the old king said weakly.

"Yes." Although Medes was reluctant, he did not want to push too hard, so he carefully retreated.

After leaving the king's bedchamber, Medes emerged with a dark expression.

His mood had been foul lately, especially after receiving the news of Camilla's death not long ago.

This left Medes feeling a little caught off guard. After all, Camilla was a pillar of the blood clan.

The sudden news of her death shocked him. It was hard to imagine who would dare do such a thing!

A sense of unease grew in Medes' heart. Camilla's death revealed one problem: someone had begun targeting the blood clan in secret.

This was a critical period for Dracula's awakening. No mistakes could be allowed. Medes worried that this might provoke a siege by many powerful forces.

However, he had heard that the ones who killed Camilla were two adventurers from Great Britain. That didn't seem like a massive organization.

Medes felt a glimmer of relief. He thought that as long as they captured these two adventurers, everything would still be under his control.

Lam, the assistant to the chancellor, saw Medes come out and immediately approached him.

Medes did not even glance at Lam and directly ordered, "Make sure that old man drinks the medicine. If he refuses, find a way to force it down his throat. Also, apart from me, absolutely no one is allowed to see the king. Or else, death."

"Yes. I will increase the guards here recently to ensure the old king takes his medicine on time," Lam replied respectfully.

"How is the search for those two adventurers going? Any news?" Medes was not at ease about this matter. Only by killing these two adventurers could he ensure the success of his plans.

"I have ordered the men to guard all checkpoints. Even the ports are filled with our people. No matter how skilled they are, they cannot easily leave France. However... there has been no progress yet. Since being wanted, those two adventurers seem to have gone into hiding and have not appeared since," Lam said awkwardly.

"Send out the garrison to search. No matter what, find these two. Do not let them run amok outside," Medes said sternly.

"Yes, my lord. But since they were able to kill Camilla, their strength must not be weak, right?" Lam voiced his concern.

"I know. Anyone who can kill Camilla is definitely not weak. As soon as we confirm their location, I will personally lead the army to subdue them," Medes declared decisively, planning to take action himself.

"If Lord Medes takes the field personally, victory will be assured," Lam flattered.

"Camilla's death caught us off guard. Perhaps someone is secretly launching an extermination campaign against us. We must take this seriously and strangle all unstable factors in the cradle," Medes said seriously, his expression grave. Camilla's death had touched a raw nerve, making him vigilant against any slight disturbance.

"Who exactly is targeting us? Could it be Princess Margaret acting in secret? She once sent assassins to attack you," Lam suggested, feeling that Margaret could not be absolved of suspicion in Camilla's death.

"It's unlikely. Margaret has been completely sidelined. She is nothing but an empty shell of a princess. Every move she makes is under our surveillance. Where would she get such power?" Medes felt it was unlikely, but what worried him was the possibility that a new force was targeting the blood clan.

Having another powerful enemy was not good news...

His greatest cathedral stood tall, with the magnificent statue of the Goddess of Light at its peak, gazing into the distance.

The capital's cathedral, named O'Brien, was ancient and the oldest stronghold of the Holy Church in France.

This cathedral had been built since the founding of the country and served as a landmark in the capital.

It was even named after the legendary Ten Great Heroes, which showed the cathedral's high status. Even among the entire Holy Church, it was considered quite prestigious.

Cathedrals named after the Ten Great Heroes were extremely important strongholds. Ordinary cathedrals did not have this honor.

Inside the cathedral, Cardinal Scott, dressed in red robes, was leading a prayer session. Standing beneath the statue of the Goddess of Light, his expression was solemn and devout.

This was something every believer had to do. Even a high-ranking cardinal like him had to do it twice a day.

Cardinals controlled the believers in their entire region and held a position second only to the Pope.

In the hearts of the red-robed believers, aside from the Pope, the cardinals held the highest position. The Pope was the spiritual leader of all.

The entire Holy Church had only 12 cardinals, scattered across various human empires, controlling all believers worldwide.

Each cardinal held great power, with the authority over life and death. They took eliminating heretics and spreading the gospel as their lifelong mission. Each and every one of them was a fanatical believer.

Another inquisitor had returned here with Joan. Both knelt on one knee before the red-robed cardinal to apologize.

Joan's failure to kill the demon that had infiltrated France was an insult to the Holy Church. The responsibility for the failure was not small.

After finishing his prayers, the cardinal slowly turned around and looked at Joan, who stood with her head lowered. "You have failed?"

"That demon was no ordinary foe. We could not resist its evil power at all. The losses were severe..." Joan's expression showed frustration.

"You are the cream of the crop among the inquisitors. If even you cannot handle that evil demon, the Holy Church will be extremely disappointed in you." Cardinal Scott showed a pitying expression.

"I am ashamed of my incompetence before the Goddess. But that demon was truly extraordinary. Its power was not like that of an ordinary being. It emanated an unstoppable aura, like a tyrant standing at the pinnacle. We fought with all our might, but the evil creature defeated us in just a few moves. However, that demon seemed to have urgent business. It appeared very anxious..." Joan slowly recounted.

A demon of such strength had infiltrated the empire? They would have to request the Pope to send reinforcements. They also needed to contact the royal family to protect the empire's safety and coordinate their efforts. However, doing so would only reveal their incompetence. The status of O'Brien Cathedral in the Vatican would drop to an unbearable level. Do you think that would be good, Joan?" Cardinal Scott asked.

Joan showed a hesitant expression, gritted her teeth, and said reluctantly, "Please give me one more chance, Your Eminence. I have already devoted my soul to the Goddess of Light. Even if I die in battle, I will not live in disgrace!"

"Even if you have devoted your soul, you have already been reduced to this state. What can another chance change, Joan? You must remember that sometimes brute force is not the solution. To deal with that demon, you need to use your brain more." Cardinal Scott used his wrinkled hand to tap his forehead.

"I don't understand, Your Eminence. What do you mean?" Joan asked, confused.

"Do you know the whereabouts of the demon?" Cardinal Scott suddenly changed the subject.

"No, I lost track of it." Joan felt embarrassed but then speculated, "However, I saw that demon heading straight for the capital. Perhaps it is hiding within the royal city right now!"

"What did you say?" Cardinal Scott was stunned and said in shock, "Such a dangerous demon has come right under our noses, hidden in the bustling crowd."

In the midst of the bustling crowd in the capital, a ragged Beelzebub stood in the center, slowly lifting his head.

His clothes were tattered, and he looked frail and sickly, like a common vagrant.

"My sister... Where is Milan? I have searched for days without a clue. Why..."

Volume 17 · Chapter 4

Balthazar arrived in the capital far earlier than Joan of Arc, yet after several days, he had found no trace of his sister at all.

Counting carefully, Balthazar had already killed countless slave masters, but without exception, no one knew where Miranda was.

This made him suspicious—was his sister even in the capital?

Balthazar grew increasingly agitated, deeply worried about his pure-hearted sister.

Miranda had never left his side before, and this time, she had run away—unlucky enough to be kidnapped.

As a sister-obsessed man, Balthazar’s mind was tormented. He feared his innocent sister would suffer violence.

Would she be tormented by hunger?

Would she be tortured?

Was she curled up in a corner, crying silently?

All these worries tormented Balthazar, making him unable to calm down. Now, he could no longer suppress his rage and was preparing to unleash a massacre.

If he couldn’t find Miranda, he would slaughter every living soul in the capital to vent his fury—regardless of guilt, they would all pay a terrible price.

Balthazar valued his sister’s life more than his own, willing to kill innocents rather than let her suffer.

Around him, the bustling crowd never noticed the ragged Balthazar—how dangerous he truly was. They assumed he was just another homeless wanderer.

With cold eyes, Balthazar watched the passing people, his mouth twitching slightly as he imagined feasting on them at will.

A fly crawled out of his mouth and slowly moved across his cheek, buzzing its wings.

Blazer had just stepped out of the royal palace after a long conversation with Princess Margaret, but her mind hadn’t changed.

As the empire’s only princess, she was using her marriage as leverage to secure stronger allies...

Blazer instinctively disliked this behavior, but as her guard, he had no choice but to endure it.

He was constantly forced to fight in the arena, defeating one suitor after another—when would this farce ever end?

Blazer felt the capital was growing more chaotic by the day. Madis was acting like a tyrant, and Princess Margaret, cornered, had no choice but to sell herself.

Meanwhile, two unknown adventurers had begun secretly targeting Madis’ followers.

As Margaret had said, their appearance was an opportunity—proof that Madis had many enemies. If used wisely, they might even turn the tide of the war?

Margaret had already given Blazer orders: find those two adventurers and bring them under her banner.

Blazer decided to dispatch his informants to search for them. Anyone who could kill Camilla’s family wasn’t weak.

There had always been a rumor in the empire that a hundred years ago, a Storm Saint Dragon had attacked, destroying countless towns before vanishing without a trace.

Some said Camilla was responsible, but given human lifespans, the rumor had never been substantiated.

Still, Blazer had seen this elegant woman—though she was a refined noble, her power was no joke. She was one of the few nobles in the empire who could use magic.

If these two mysterious adventurers could kill Camilla, their strength must be formidable—worth recruiting.

Blazer rubbed his temples, realizing he had a lot to do. To kill Madis, this traitorous rebel, he had to act.

But just as he stepped out of the palace gates, a squad of soldiers rushed toward him in panic. Their faces were pale, clearly shaken.

“Lord Blazer! Something terrible has happened! Someone attacked the capital! Our brothers are half dead!”

“What?! Who did this?” Blazer’s eyes widened in disbelief. Though the empire was plagued by internal and external threats, who dared strike the capital?

“Uh... we don’t know. Suddenly, swarms of bloodthirsty flies appeared in the city. In just a short time, so many people were left with nothing but bones!”

The captain’s trembling report sent a chill down Blazer’s spine. He had never seen anything so terrifying.

“Cannibal...” Blazer frowned, utterly confused. “We must go see—who has the nerve to attack the capital like this?”

Buzzing, countless flies ravaged the capital.

Who knew how many people died in this catastrophe, their bodies reduced to bones by the swarms.

Even the soldiers who dared approach were helpless—many were struggling in the flies, leaving behind only tattered armor and white bones.

The massive swarm of flies, like starving beasts, blocked out the sun, casting the city in darkness.

People fled in terror, their screams and cries filling the air. The capital, littered with corpses, seemed like a living hell.

Balthazar removed his hood, waiting until the flies were thick enough before opening his mouth wide. The swarm surged in like a whale drinking water, all of them swallowed at once.

With a *gurgle*, every cannibal fly was gone from his stomach. A deep satisfaction washed over him.

The Feast Sovereign had many ways to eat—this was one of them. Let the flies devour their prey, then he would consume them indirectly.

Balthazar wiped his mouth, looking at the city littered with corpses. A smug smile curled his lips.

“Hmm, let’s make it a little more exciting.”

He spread his arms, and black energy began to rise from his body, spreading across the entire city instantly.

A chorus of ghostly wails rose from the depths of the abyss, and the city was enveloped in a thick, violet-black smoke—something monstrous was about to emerge.

Blazer hurried toward the chaos, but along the way, he saw too many dead civilians and soldiers.

Bones littered the capital in every corner, their surfaces chewed away. Rivers of blood flowed slowly across the ground.

Blazer’s gaze was dazed. Was this the end of the world? He heard desperate, heart-wrenching screams—an old woman clutching her dead son, soldiers holding their gutted comrades.

What happened? The city had been fine moments ago—why was it now in ruins?

Who was this enemy? How could they cause such devastation in such a short time? Half the capital’s population was likely dead!

Blazer’s face paled, sweat dripping down his cheeks. His instincts told him this foe was no ordinary threat—attacking the imperial capital directly meant they were no mere commoner.

With a low, spine-chilling growl, a monstrous creature burst from the violet-black smoke, towering over everything.

Its size was unmatched—no one knew what it looked like, because they were already inside its gaping maw!

No one knew where it came from. All they knew was that death was near.

The creature hadn’t even fully emerged—only its head was visible, its body seemingly trapped in another space.

Yet even so, the entire capital was already inside its mouth. The towering city walls couldn’t even reach its teeth, proving just how vast it was—it wanted to devour the entire region.

From the outside, the creature’s eyes were tiny, but their crimson glow was blinding. Its body was covered in black tendrils, and its low, terrifying growls made people shudder.

The creature’s jaws began to close slowly. The people of the capital watched as the sunlight faded, plunging into endless darkness—this was true *daylight-blocking*.

“Ugh!”

Blazer froze, tilting his head to stare at the creature’s pale-red jaws, its teeth like tiny mountains.

At that moment, everyone was inside its mouth—no one was spared.

Blazer’s body trembled, his fear rising from his core. This was the rhythm of total annihilation—

What... is that?

No—France’s capital was doomed.

(;° Ai!)

title: Chapter 5 — Holy War Declaration
content:
Chapter 5 — Holy War Declaration

Volume 17 · Chapter 5

Amidst waves of purple‑black smoke, a huge monster suddenly appeared, about to devour the entire royal capital. Its enormous, terrifying head made the whole capital look tiny, held within its gaping, blood‑filled maw. Beelzebub’s appetite was no ordinary size—since he couldn’t find his sister, he wanted to drag the whole capital down with him as a burial offering. This posture suggested he intended to wipe out the capital in one strike, showing no mercy toward humans at all. As the Demon Lord King, Beelzebub was the opposite of Merlin, truly treating humans like livestock. In fact, Beelzebub hadn’t even gotten serious yet; don’t be fooled by the massive size and formidable aura of the summoned monster, which could swallow the whole capital. It was merely a pet he kept, not a powerful monster at all—just like feeding a dog leftover bones. Even if you compared sheer size, this monster wasn’t even enough to stuff between the teeth of the jealous monarch Leviathan. Legend says Leviathan’s true form is an eternally gigantic sea beast; a single sneeze could stir up a world‑shaking tsunami. The monster let out low growls, its blood‑filled maw slowly closing, and everyone in the capital froze, watching the light gradually fade.

No! If this continues, the capital will become the monster’s snack! Blaize felt he had to do something; he suppressed his inner fear, mustered courage, and gripped the heavy sword on his back. As the first warrior of Francia, he was quite experienced, yet he had never seen such a huge monster before! Even before fighting, he felt endless pressure, constantly doubting himself. However, Blaize’s strength was not weak; although he had never faced such a colossal monster, he still had confidence. After all, Blaize’s swordsmanship had no fixed form—against any enemy, he just charged in. “Haah!” Blaize roared, leaping from the ground into the sky, his golden Saint‑Tier battle aura blazing like a flying fireball. Reaching the highest point, he gathered all his strength into his heavy sword and unleashed an angry horizontal slash! A golden shockwave burst forth, spreading outward with a thunderous roar like rolling drums, almost drowning out the monster’s low growl. The sharp sword aura, carrying the force of splitting Mount Hua, swept through the air toward the monster’s mouth walls and pierced through with a “swish”! Blaize fell from the sky, gripping his heavy sword and lifting his head to see how things stood. If this couldn’t stop the monster, he had no better ideas. How about it? Surely there must be some effect, right? Blaize broke out in a cold sweat on his forehead, eyeing the slowly closing blood‑filled maw. The monster seemed to have been hit by a paralysis spell—it didn’t twitch at all. Sunlight streamed through its sharp teeth, the only light left in the capital. “Boom!” a huge blast! The monster’s head was cleaved sideways; the massive outflow of blood surged like a flood, pouring over the capital’s surroundings. The monster wailed, presumably gravely wounded by Blaize, and slowly sank into the purple‑black smoke. “Qin…… Blaize muttered dazedly, as if he himself hadn’t expected to succeed in driving back the monster. As the purple smoke that had engulfed the capital dissipated, light returned, bathing everyone in a brief moment of relief. Blaize rested his heavy sword on his shoulder, his thick brows knotted, thinking that this seemingly mighty monster was actually so fragile—just one hit and he’d been on edge……

On the other side, Beelzebub saw his pet defeated and felt somewhat annoyed; he had been thinking of giving his pet a snack. “Huh? You actually killed my little cutie—worth praising…” Beelzebub stroked his chin and gave a light evaluation: “No wonder it’s the human empire’s capital—there really are some genuine talents here.” Having his pet defeated was something Beelzebub truly hadn’t anticipated; he had always regarded humans as extremely weak, believing that sending out just his pet was enough to handle any foe. It seemed the situation wasn’t as simple as Beelzebub thought; if he wanted to easily annihilate the whole capital, he’d still need to put in some work. However, after venting his frustration, Beelzebub gradually calmed down, realizing that finding his sister was the top priority. Causing destruction around here was useless; it wouldn’t help him locate his sister at all. b's o Beelzebub pondered and decided to threaten everyone in the capital, forcing the culprit to hand over Miranda. So Beelzebub soared into the sky, arriving above the capital, looking down at the chaotic scene, and issued his threat to all: “I am the lord from the Fifth Demon Lord Palace, Beelzebub!” “Now I declare: the capital may only be entered, not left—you are all my hostages!” “I give you three days to surrender my sister; otherwise, whether man, woman, old or young, I will personally send you all to hell!” “Of course, you can try to resist me—three days is plenty of time to make full preparations.” “But I will prove with facts how laughable it is for humans to think they can oppose the demon race!” “You will struggle like ants, and after three days, the imperial capital of Francia will cease to exist! Hahaha….” After finishing his words, Beelzebub turned and vanished, leaving only a capital riddled with holes, as if he had never been there. His meaning was clear—no hidden agenda: hand over my sister, spare everyone’s lives, or else I will unleash a slaughter. Such a straightforward, brutal approach truly fits Beelzebub’s style—he’d rather kill than negotiate any terms. The chaotic capital gradually returned to calm, with many people emerging from corners, dazedly surveying their surroundings. Just now Beelzebub’s voice had been loud enough for everyone in the capital to hear; that one of the Seven Demon Lords had attacked the empire was the first thing each person realized.

At this moment, whether they were low‑born commoners or high‑ranking palace nobles, everyone’s faces turned pale, feeling that death was already creeping step by step, with no safety to be found. In fact, the vast majority felt utterly bewildered, having no idea how they had provoked the Gluttony Lord Beelzebub, who his sister was, or which scoundrel had brought this calamity upon them. — The fear of time gripped the capital; three days later would be their doom, and everyone was overcome with despair, sitting on the ground as if they had lost their souls. Beelzebub needed only to say a few words, and the capital’s people lost all will to fight; no matter how they struggled, they could not escape the doom of death. “Is… that the legendary Gluttony Lord, Beelzebub?” Blaize swallowed nervously, his eyes downcast. He’s incredibly strong—no wonder the Holy Church warns that the demon race is a threat to humanity. If all seven Demon Lords possessed such power, it would be truly terrifying! Only an extraordinarily powerful empire could hope to resist a demon invasion; smaller nations would face only annihilation. Now that the empire has caught the eye of the Gluttony Lord, no one can stay uninvolved; we must unite to survive this catastrophe. Saint 5--- is about to break out on this cow field? z(°△° I)

title: Chapter 6 — Fearless Mades
content:
Chapter 6 — Fearless Mades

Volume 17 · Chapter 6

After Bisby left, the entire royal capital was sleepless all night, with almost everyone beginning to panic.

The deadline was three days; if Miranda wasn’t handed over, the entire royal capital would be doomed.

The problem was, aside from Prime Minister Mads, almost no one knew where Bisby’s sister was—and even less knew what had offended this bloodthirsty demon race king.

Everyone became at a loss, their minds filled with the desire to flee the royal capital, to leave this cursed place.

However, Bisby had already sealed off the entire royal capital and surrounded it in secret, allowing no one to enter or leave.

Anyone who dared to leave the royal capital now would inevitably invite death upon themselves.

The once-glorious royal capital had now become a prison, from which no one could escape, and they could only quietly await the coming of death.

However, after Bisby threatened France, many people began to act in secret, even if it was just a last-ditch resistance, they absolutely couldn’t just sit and wait for death.

In the basement of the Prime Minister’s mansion, the root cause of everything, Mads, felt very surprised—

“You are actually the Gluttonous Monarch’s sister?”

He hadn’t expected that randomly kidnapping a single demon would turn out to be the sister of the Gluttonous Monarch, and he’d inadvertently stirred up a great deal of trouble.

Even if Mads was an idiot, he could realize the seriousness of this matter—it had already threatened the survival of the empire.

However, as a vampire, Mads didn’t really care about the fate of the empire; he was merely surprised that he had accidentally kidnapped Bisby’s sister.

Mads felt he could fully utilize Bisby’s sister to indirectly serve his own plans.

“Since you already know, why don’t you let me leave!?” Miranda huddled in a corner of her cell, having just heard her brother’s voice—besides being overjoyed, she also saw a glimmer of hope for survival.

“Leave? Do you think I would let you leave?” Mads asked expressionlessly.

“You heard what my brother said, right? If you don’t let me go, none of you will end well!” Miranda, knowing her brother had come for her, began to speak with more confidence.

“Oh? Miss, you have quite the big tone, you really scared me.” Mads’ expression became smug, saying playfully, “But I’m sorry, even if your brother comes, I have no intention of letting you go. Rather, knowing your brother is the Gluttonous Monarch has made me feel excited.”

.“.....Miranda was stunned for a moment, feeling Mads was like a madman. Her brother was one of the Seven Demon Kings, a normal person would have been terrified out of their wits, but the man before her was completely different.

“I advise you to give up your childish ideas.” Mads spread his hands, saying decisively, “No matter who your brother is, I have no intention of letting you leave.”

“Lord Mads, Bisby’s sudden attack has caused considerable damage to the royal capital. Everyone is already panicking. The nobles are outside requesting to see you, hoping you can give an explanation…” Lamb followed closely behind Mads, simply explaining the current situation.

“Hmph, let those nobles shout outside, ignore them. They all lived comfortably in the past, but now that danger comes, they rush to seek my protection—where is there such a good thing? Tomorrow there will definitely be a council meeting to discuss dealing with Bisby. There’s no need for me to come forward personally now.” Mads said with a dismissive tone.

“Yes, I’ll ask them to leave in a moment.” Lamb nodded, then asked with a worried expression, “But Lord, Bisby’s attack has also had a considerable impact on us. That female demon keeps talking about her brother every day, and it turns out he’s the Gluttonous Monarch. This time we… seem to have caused quite a bit of trouble.”

“I didn’t expect that a demon I bought casually would be Bisby’s sister. It really is like catching a big fish.” Mads revealed a mysterious smile.

“......Lamb saw that Mads didn’t show the slightest bit of nervousness, and felt very puzzled. With Bisby about to destroy the royal capital, this was also unfavorable for the vampires in the royal capital. “Lord, what are you saying? We are also in danger, how can you say you’ve caught a big fish?”

“You’re wrong, Lamb. We are in an absolutely safe position. The humans are the ones truly in danger.” Mads didn’t show any panic at all, but said very calmly, “Now the entire royal capital is sealed off by Bisby. If they want to move everyone away, they will inevitably have to launch a large-scale transfer magic, but this method isn’t reliable—it will alert Bisby and provoke retaliation. But we have a secret passage leading outside the royal capital, which Bisby won’t easily detect. Even if the royal capital is destroyed, we won’t be affected by the danger, and we could have escaped long ago.”

“So that’s how it is. When did Lord Mads dig the secret passage? You actually left a way out.” Lamb widened his eyes, completely unaware of this.

“This is called being prepared for a rainy day. Lamb, you should study more.” Mads responded indifferently, continuing, “This passage was built long ago, originally intended as a secret route for transporting slaves, but it was never used. But today, this passage is our vampire’s escape route, putting us in an absolutely safe position.”

“As expected of Lord Mads, so we can escape at any time?” Lamb asked in astonishment. Since there was a secret passage that could be used to escape at any time, Bisby naturally wasn’t a major threat.

“Escape? Ha, unless absolutely necessary, we will definitely not escape. This time we will lead the humans to resist to the end.” Mads said, acting contrary to his usual manner.

“Why? Humans aren’t our race.” Lamb looked puzzled, not understanding Mads’ intentions.

“Look further ahead. We want to establish the Eternal Night Empire and conquer all of France. At that time, humans will be our enemies. Now, the more fiercely they fight with the Gluttonous Monarch, the more beneficial it will be for our future conquest of the empire. It would be best if all the strong humans died.” Mads revealed a treacherous smile.

“Is that so? As expected, Lord Mads thinks long-term…”.

Lamb nodded, understanding Mads’ intentions—it was a case of the jackal profiting from the fight between the tiger and the crocodile.

By using Bisby’s hand, the more human strongmen who died, the smoother the plan to establish the Eternal Night Empire would be.

“But Lord Mads, we kidnapped Bisby’s sister. If he finds out, we might… not escape death? Should we send this female demon back?”

“Don’t be naive, Lamb. You can’t believe what demons say. Even if we send Bisby’s sister back, we definitely won’t be forgiven.” Mads dismissed his subordinate’s foolish idea.

“But… this female demon is like a time bomb, it’s always unsettling to have her here.” Lamb was somewhat worried. Now, these people were already the main culprits.

“Don’t worry, Lamb. Vampires aren’t necessarily weaker than demon monarchs. If there’s a chance, I’d very much like to compete with this Gluttonous Monarch.” Mads paused, smiling mysteriously—

“As for Bisby’s sister?”

“We’ll keep a close watch on her, and she’ll never be able to find him.”

Volume 17 · Chapter 7

In the royal palace.

Margaret was supposed to be sleeping at this hour, but because Asmodeus had suddenly issued a three-day death countdown, she couldn’t rest at all, her mind in turmoil.

The empire was already in chaos from Medes’ internal strife and external threats, and now the gluttonous monarch had suddenly attacked the capital city—adding insult to injury, making the entire kingdom’s situation even worse.

Unlike Medes, the bloodline traitor, Margaret was the empire’s heir, the only princess, and couldn’t ignore the safety of the empire.

Asmodeus’ sudden assault had her thoroughly frustrated. Dealing with Medes was already difficult enough, but now there was an even more troublesome gluttonous monarch to contend with?

Margaret was in a foul mood, feeling the situation was utterly chaotic—she had to eliminate Medes and drive Asmodeus out of the capital.

But for now, she couldn’t afford to focus on Medes; she had to figure out how to deal with the gluttonous Demon Lord’s threat first.

After all, Asmodeus’ deadline was short—just three days. If she didn’t surrender his sister, he would slaughter the entire capital city.

Although Medes wasn’t a good man, protecting the capital’s safety was the most important thing.

Margaret just had no idea how to deal with Asmodeus, the demon king. She couldn’t think of any good way to drive him back.

She sat in her chair, resting her face as if pretending to sleep, while the dim yellow light flickered softly beside her.

Blaze knelt on one knee, having waited there for a long time. The princess’ silence made him uneasy.

“My... Lord?”

Hearing Blaze’s voice, Margaret opened her eyes slightly and asked, her tone indifferent, “What is it?”

“Asmodeus has already reached the capital. The imperial capital is now in a state of imminent peril...” Blaze hesitated, clearly very anxious about the current situation, but Margaret didn’t seem the least bit concerned.

“Speak plainly, don’t beat around the bush,” Margaret smiled faintly, showing no sign of the impending doom of the empire.

“My Lord, the situation is already critical. If we don’t do something, in three days the entire capital will be turned into a slaughterhouse!” Blaze’s voice grew agitated, hoping that at this moment, Margaret would step forward as the empire’s heir. “I have no doubt that the demons are ruthless. Look today—half the capital’s forces have already been injured. If this happens again, I fear the imperial capital... will become nothing but dust in history.”

“What can we do about it? Do you think you can defeat the demon king?” Margaret asked with mild curiosity.

“...I don’t have absolute confidence, but as your subject, I am willing to sacrifice my life for the empire!” Blaze’s heart pounded. After seeing Asmodeus’ tactics today, he wasn’t sure he could defeat him with certainty.

“What good is a heart full of passion if it can’t feed you? We need to be realistic,” Margaret said calmly.

“But My Lord, the capital is in chaos right now. As the empire’s heir, you can’t just sit there and do nothing!” Blaze’s expression showed his confusion.

“Do you think I have any say in the Council? The Council is already controlled by Medes. Now I’m just a hollow princess,” Margaret sighed.

“That’s not true. The Three Knights of the Empire are all willing to remain loyal to you and uphold the empire’s legitimacy,” Blaze replied firmly, hoping the princess would show some confidence.

“Blaze, I’m touched by your words, but the only one who can truly help the empire survive this crisis is Medes—not me,” Margaret said seriously.

“Why?” Blaze stared at her in bewilderment.

“Because Medes has great ambition. The capital has already become his territory, and he won’t allow anyone else to destroy it,” Margaret paused, then continued, “I suspect tomorrow’s Council will be called. All the nobles of the capital will attend, and Medes will rally the entire city’s forces to strike back against Asmodeus. Everyone will unite in this crisis.”

“How is that possible? Medes can already mobilize the entire capital’s forces?” Blaze found it hard to believe.

“Don’t underestimate him. Many people may publicly respect my father, but in private, they probably bow to Medes,” Margaret seemed to have guessed most of tomorrow’s events. “And those idiots in the Council, desperate to survive, will unanimously pass Medes’ demands, even electing him as their leader. Even deploying the legendary magic cannons isn’t impossible.”

“Legendary magic cannons? Those aren’t our empire’s secret weapons? Only the king can order their use!”

Blaze was shocked. The twelve legendary magic cannons were sacred relics of the empire’s founding, used by the first emperor to unify the seven kingdoms during the age of warlords. They were legendary for their power.

It was said that the twelve cannons were incredibly destructive, and after the empire was founded, they had never been used again. Only the royal family had the right to enter the secret chamber and activate this imperial relic.

As the first Hero, Blaze didn’t even know what the legendary magic cannons looked like—he’d only heard rumors. Some said they were artifacts from ancient civilization, capable of unleashing primordial power to destroy everything in sight.

Ancient civilization was from the age of gods, when humans faced divine threats and created formidable civilizations—magic, martial arts, alchemy—all with terrifying power.

But with the end of the age of gods, humanity’s ancient civilization collapsed, leaving behind only fragments.

Now, those who could master ancient magic or martial arts were far more powerful than ordinary warriors, even if their strength was similar. The difference in combat ability was immense—ancient magic and martial arts far surpassed ordinary magic and martial arts.

The twelve legendary magic cannons of France were no less powerful than ancient magic or martial arts. Their destructive potential might even be greater, after all, they were treasures that helped the first emperor unify the empire.

“My father is too ill to care about governance. Do you think these rules can stop Medes?” Margaret smirked, already certain that tomorrow’s Council would support Medes. Even if they ignored the royal family, who would care? As long as everyone wanted to survive, they’d all rally behind Medes.

“But the legendary magic cannons are the empire’s secret weapon. Letting Medes use them is too reckless, My Lord—you must refuse!” Blaze felt this was unacceptable. Medes was just a chancellor; now he could deploy the empire’s secret weapons? That was seizing control of everything. It was the emperor’s legendary weapon used to crush all rivals—letting outsiders use it was completely against protocol.

“No, I intend to support Medes in using the legendary magic cannons. Not only that, this time, the Three Knights must fully cooperate with Medes to help the empire resist Asmodeus’ invasion,” Margaret said seriously.

“Why, My Lord? You want me to cooperate with Medes, that traitorous rebel? Kill me instead!” Blaze stood up in anger, thinking the princess was utterly foolish.

“Blaze, calm down. This isn’t about...” Margaret looked into his eyes, speaking sincerely.

“It’s about the future of the empire.”

title: Chapter 8 — O'Brien Cathedral
content:
Chapter 8 — O'Brien Cathedral

Volume 17 · Chapter 8

Hearing Margaret speak with such seriousness, Blaze was momentarily speechless.

After regaining some composure, he more or less understood the princess’s meaning.

The current situation was special; the greatest enemy was no longer Mads, but the Gluttony Monarch who had suddenly attacked.

To protect the entire royal capital, it was necessary to unite with even enemies to jointly resist the powerful foe.

“I will obey your orders, but I absolutely will not associate with someone like Mads. Cooperation is only temporary.”

“Who said you’d have to cooperate with him forever?” Margaret smiled faintly and said in a low voice, “Once we repel the Gluttony Monarch, we’ll be enemies again. I won’t let this guy continue to control the empire.”

“Hearing the princess say that puts my mind at ease.” Blaze felt reassured, thinking Margaret was the empire’s last hope. Whether France could return to the right path depended entirely on this sole imperial princess.

“We and Mads are like hounds fighting over food. Now a lion has suddenly appeared, wanting to take the food for itself. Naturally, we must unite. Isn’t it common for the weak to band together?” Margaret felt there was no other choice. Even if Mads was a treacherous man, they had to unite in this situation, or no one would want to see the royal city destroyed.

“But even if we unite, do we really have confidence in defeating Besib, that Great Demon Lord? I’ve heard that the demon race are all eccentric. Although their numbers are small, their power is extremely strong.” Blaze’s heart pounded with anxiety. Despite the empire having many hidden cards, he still felt nervous after witnessing Besib’s abilities.

“It’s not just our forces and Mads’s, but also Bishop Scott of the O’Brien Cathedral.” Margaret paused, speaking meaningfully.

“Dealing with demons is what these religious fanatics are best at.”

a.sF light novel

The O’Brien Cathedral at night.

Superficially, it was incredibly quiet, but in reality, it was brightly lit.

This was strangely unsettling. In the past, the cathedral would close its doors at night, but tonight it was completely open to worshippers.

After Besib’s rampage through the royal capital, many citizens felt their lives were numbered, with death arriving in just three days.

This caused widespread panic, a complete loss of morale, and a descent into despair.

However, in such times of crisis, the power of faith could exert an unparalleled force, calming the anxious people.

The O’Brien Cathedral had gathered the entire city’s worshippers, who knelt before the statue of the Goddess of Light, praying devoutly for deliverance from this crisis.

Seeing this, Red Cardinal Scott ordered the O’Brien Cathedral to remain open 24 hours a day, allowing worshippers to pray in peace.

However, Scott, as Red Cardinal, wasn’t foolish. Could praying really save them? That seemed unlikely.

Upon learning that Besib had attacked the royal capital today, Scott’s first reaction was to defeat this Great Demon Lord—it was instinct.

The demon race and the Holy Church had always been at odds. Now that a demon dared to run rampant in human territory, it was a disrespect to the Goddess of Light.

Scott was the highest-ranking cleric in all of France and would not stand idly by, watching demons wreak havoc under his nose.

Beneath the O’Brien Cathedral, there was a very deep cellar, seemingly hiding a secret.

On the spiral staircase, Scott held a torch and slowly descended, Joan of Arc following closely behind, not daring to breathe.

Joan of Arc felt that today was unusual. She had always heard that the cathedral’s cellar was used to store grain, but after entering, she found it excessively spacious—it was clearly not just for storing grain.

Despite her inner doubts, she didn’t dare ask directly. Scott was, after all, a noble Red Cardinal, and she, a minor inquisitor, had no right to inquire too deeply.

“Joan of Arc.” Scott, walking ahead, suddenly asked, “When did you begin to believe in the Light Church?”

“Hm?” Joan of Arc paused, answering honestly, “My parents are devout believers. I received the baptismal rite at the age of three and became a servant of the Goddess of Light.”

“Three years old? So that’s how it is. It’s rare to see such devotion at such a young age. Your piety towards the Goddess is admirable. Great Maria will surely see it, fulfill all your wishes, and save you from suffering, sparing you from any further torment.” Scott spoke in a rambling manner.

“I hope so.” Joan of Arc replied calmly, inexplicably thinking of Alice. If piety was truly important, she should have been chosen as the Hero, not Alice, that false believer.

“My child, your tone suggests you don’t quite believe my words?” Scott didn’t turn back, but continued to lead the way slowly.

“...” Joan of Arc offered an embarrassed excuse.

“I know you’ve experienced many misfortunes, but these hardships are trials given to humanity by the Goddess.” Scott spoke mysteriously.

“Trials?” Joan of Arc was confused.

“That’s right, trials. Legend has it that Goddess Maria once had a twin sister named Teresa, the Goddess of Fortune, who died during the war of the gods because of a demon.” Scott paused, continuing in a low voice, “Grief-stricken by the loss of her kin, our Goddess of Light once considered ending her own life, but ultimately persevered, ascended to the pinnacle of the gods, and became the ruler of all living things.”

“There’s such a story?” Joan of Arc was slightly surprised, having never heard it before.

“These are hidden parts of the doctrine, only visible in the Pope’s library.” Scott replied indifferently.

Joan of Arc was stunned, thinking she simply lacked the necessary rank. “But what does this have to do with trials?”

“The Goddess herself rose from a human state step by step, fully understanding human sin. Pride, gluttony, greed, sloth, lust, envy, and wrath—these vices always prevent humanity from escaping the fate of flesh and blood. Only by constantly undergoing trials can the human soul be elevated. Therefore, Maria has set up numerous trials, simply to purify sinful humanity. Compared to the Goddess’s pain at losing her only kin, your misfortunes are nothing.” Scott spoke like a wise elder, a Red Cardinal with MAX brainwashing ability, a true sales elite of another world.

“So that’s how it is. It seems my thinking is too shallow. I apologize, Bishop…” Joan of Arc felt a bit ashamed.

“No need to apologize, my child. As long as you understand the Goddess of Light’s good intentions, all suffering is a purification of the soul. I noticed you’ve been silent. Do you have something on your mind?” Scott asked curiously.

“It’s not that I have something on my mind… just…” Joan of Arc hesitated, then voiced her confusion, “I just don’t understand why Your Eminence suddenly brought me here?”

“You’re worried about that? I’m getting old and forgetful.” Scott patted his head, answering mysteriously, “I want to represent the merciful Goddess and give you a gift, one that only a pious child like you deserves.”

“A gift?” Joan of Arc frowned, becoming even more puzzled.

“Do you know the history of the O’Brien Cathedral?” Scott abruptly changed the subject.

“I apologize. Although I was born in France, I spent my early years training in the Vatican and am not very familiar with this cathedral. I only know that it’s one of the few holy sites directly under the Pope.” Joan of Arc replied apologetically, direct holy sites under the Pope were rare, mostly the hometowns of great figures who had made significant contributions to the Church.

“It doesn’t matter if you don’t know. Having trained in the Vatican, you must have heard of the legend of the Hero of the Lance, right?” Scott asked meaningfully.

“Eh!?” Joan of Arc’s eyes widened, instantly recognizing the name. “Of course. The ten heroes of the Holy Church’s legends, each an extremely great figure, said to be able to influence the world. The Hero of the Lance is one of them, the youngest but with achievements that inspire awe—killing the powerful Lucifer II and nearly annihilating the First Demon Lord Palace!”

“Haha, you’re quite knowledgeable about that.” Scott smiled and turned back, speaking in a low voice to Joan of Arc.

“The O’Brien Cathedral is named after the Hero of the Lance.”

“He lived here as a child, raised by the church…”

title: Chapter 9 — Scarlet Enchantress
content:
Chapter 9 — Scarlet Enchantress

Volume 17 · Chapter 9

“O'Brien is a warrior who grew up on this land and is renowned for his prowess with a spear. He is known as the Spear Hero and is a source of pride for our church.

Scott, the Archdeacon, spoke with a touch of sentimentality, as if considering the Spear Hero a form of honor.

Indeed, the radiant Spear Hero O'Brien, who grew up in this church and was named after it, is a significant memorial.

The legendary Ten Heroes are those who have made great contributions to the Church and whose abilities are admired by the world.

They are the foundation of the Church's standing and are noble warriors comparable to saints.

O'Brien's achievements, such as slaying Lucifer II and attacking the demon race's headquarters, are sufficient to place him among the Ten.

“Is the Spear Hero's real name O'Brien? Did he live here as a child?” Joan of Arc felt a slight surprise.

“Yes, it's said that O'Brien was silent as a child but was very passionate about martial arts. He showed exceptional talent at the age of seven and was cultivated by the Church. No one expected his later achievements to surpass anyone's expectations.” Scott sighed, filled with pride for the Spear Hero O'Brien.

“That makes sense. I can understand why this is a holy land directly under the Pope's authority.

Joan of Arc nodded, amazed that she had assumed this was just a large church, but the Spear Hero emerged from here, which is why it is a holy land.

The Ten Heroes are the most outstanding representatives selected from the time the Church was established until now.

The Spear Hero is likely the youngest among them and has naturally become an idol for many believers.

However, the Spear Hero has disappeared, and no one knows where this talent has gone, leaving behind countless legends.

“I want to give you a gift related to this legendary hero.” Scott said mysteriously.

“Eh! ?” Joan of Arc was stunned, her mind filled with doubt. “Is it related to the Spear Hero?”

What exactly is it?

They walked for a long time before reaching the deepest part of the cellar.

Joan of Arc peeked inside, and the exit of the cellar was glowing with a dim light, about 100 meters deep!

It's a very deep cellar, not just for storing grain....

Joan of Arc marveled in her mind, feeling that the Red Robed Archbishop's gift to her was extraordinary, otherwise, it wouldn't be so secretive.

“This is it... Scott stood in front of the heavy stone door, looking at Joan of Arc behind him.

“What is this?” Joan of Arc looked at the thick stone door, her instincts telling her this was a place for storing valuable items.

“This is the treasure vault of the cathedral, a place for storing valuable items. Normally, only I am allowed to enter, but under special circumstances, you can come in with me.” Scott said seriously.

“...Joan of Arc felt a sense of tension, becoming even more curious about what was inside? Why is it stored in the treasure vault? Is it something extremely rare?

“Come on, my child....” Scott activated the mechanism on the stone door, and the two stone doors opened slowly.

Joan of Arc hesitated before following the Archbishop's footsteps into the room. When she reached the far end, a cold blade of light flashed into her eyes.

That was a spear with a crimson body, and just looking at it, one could feel the soul-draining killing intent.

Joan of Arc was somewhat overwhelmed, although the spear looked simple, its intimidation was real.

Especially at the tip of the spear, the cold light shimmered, and if one stared at it for too long, it could damage one's eyes.

“Archdeacon, what is this spear?” Joan of Arc slightly averted her eyes, as staring directly at it might harm her spirit.

“Crimson Banshee, the holy spear used by O'Brien. He used this weapon to kill Lucifer II and establish his legendary status.” Scott introduced it.

“Crimson Banshee....” Joan of Arc looked at the spear on the pedestal, finding the name quite eerie, not like a weapon used by a righteous hero.

“This holy spear is unique. It is said to have been found in the depths of a meteorite crater and forged after being tempered with the blood of millions of demons. It is a powerful weapon of slaughter.” Scott explained simply.

Joan of Arc slightly frowned, although it was created by sacrificing many demons, the act was too bloody, and calling it a holy weapon seems inappropriate.

“There are two levels of weapons: common and rare. Rare weapons are considered treasures, with high quality and limited in number. The Crimson Banshee used by the Spear Hero is indeed far beyond a rare weapon.” Scott said seriously.

“Beyond rare.... Could it be.... Joan of Arc widened her eyes, thinking of something beyond common sense, and said with a trembling voice, “Is it an artifact?”

Artifacts are items belonging to the gods. Based on the legends from the era of the gods, these artifacts that surpass human understanding have the power to control the world.

The gods used artifacts to change the rules of the world, control the power of nature, and even transcend life and death or time, completely reversing fate.

Artifacts are often only found in people's imaginations and have never been seen in reality, existing only as stories passed down through generations.

“No, this spear is far from the artifacts in stories. It has not yet earned the title of artifact.” Scott dismissed Joan of Arc's fantasy.

“Then what exactly is it.... Joan of Arc raised her eyebrows, her mind beginning to doubt, since it is beyond rare but not yet an artifact, what is its status?

“Pseudo-artifact.” Scott revealed the quality of the Crimson Banshee and explained, “The Church has been trying to create artificial artifacts, but they have never succeeded. This spear is one of the more successful works among artificial artifacts, and we call it a pseudo-artifact, meaning it has some of the power of an artifact but is a fake.

“Pseudo-artifact.... Joan of Arc looked at the crimson spear, wondering if this was the result of countless experiments conducted in secret by the Church.

“The Crimson Banshee was initially modeled after the legendary artifacts and has qualities that other weapons cannot surpass. Any defense is like paper in front of this spear, and it has a very special ability.” Scott said mysteriously.

“What is the special ability?” Joan of Arc asked curiously.

“The ability of the Crimson Banshee is blood sacrifice. It can sacrifice up to two humans, and for a certain period, the two people's strength will be transferred to you, allowing you to temporarily increase your power.” Scott looked at Joan of Arc and said meaningfully, “You are already a Saint-tier warrior. If you can sacrifice two people, your power may surpass the Saint-tier limit and reach a higher level. At that time, even the Gluttony Monarch would not be invincible in a single battle.

“...Joan of Arc's forehead dripped with cold sweat, thinking that the blood sacrifice ability is equivalent to temporarily consuming others. It is indeed very useful, but it feels quite eerie....

“This pseudo-artifact filled with legendary colors, I will give it to you in the name of the Goddess today.” Scott intended to give Joan of Arc the Spear Hero's weapon to use.

“Ah? ! Me?” Joan of Arc pointed at herself and then shook her head. “My abilities are limited, and I know I am not as good as its owner. I do not deserve to hold it.

“My child, you need to have confidence.” Scott smiled and personally took down the Crimson Banshee, holding it out to Joan of Arc.

“O'Brien once used it to kill the previous Gluttony Monarch and became a hero praised by all.

“Now the Gluttony Monarch is without evil....”

“I believe you can also accomplish this seemingly impossible task, defeating Beelzebub with it!”

title: Chapter 10 — Parliament Mobilization
content:
Chapter 10 — Parliament Mobilization

Volume 17 · Chapter 10

Bael's attack on the royal city was his eighth, and there were still two days left before the deadline.

Nowadays, not only the former bitter enemies but also the forces that had been mutually hostile had almost all united together.

Many scenes that had not appeared in the capital for many years appeared in the capital, everyone was happy and peaceful, and it seemed very peaceful.

All this was thanks to Bael, who forced everyone to stand on the same line of unity and fight against the enemy.

Everyone abandoned hostility and enmity, and regarded the violent tyrant as the most important thing at present.

The royal city had been blocked by Bael, and almost no one could escape, so everyone had only one way to resist.

In order to arrange the defense more reasonably, as the prime minister, Mads early issued a notice to convene an emergency meeting to discuss the plan to resist Bael together.

At present, all the nobles in the royal city were present in the imperial parliament, including the Margret princess, who was Mads' enemy.

On the podium, Mads talked about the current situation with a powerful tone, as if the world was at the end of the world and humanity would die if they did not unite.

However, Mads' dress was very strange, he was all wrapped in a black cloak, and only his eyes could be seen.

Because Mads was a vampire, he could not face the sun, and he would wrap himself tightly every day when he went out, so that no sunlight would hit him.

Sunlight was the greatest enemy of the blood race, and if it was exposed to the light for a while, it would be burned to ashes, and even the gods could not save it.

Although Mads' appearance was very strange, few people could think of him as a vampire. He claimed that he had a skin disease that was afraid of sunlight, so he would not show his head in the daytime.

"We have been driven to the brink of extinction by the bloody tyrant! We have completely cut off contact with the outside world!"

"There is only one road in front of us! That is to give full play to our strength to resist the pressure of the Great Demon Lord!"

"For our future! For the tomorrow of the empire! Even if we sacrifice our lives! We must defeat Bael!"

The nobles in the royal palace clapped their hands, and their emotions were mobilized by Mads' passionate speech, and they all wanted to fight against evil to the end.

Bryce sat beside Margret and whispered, "Your Highness, although Mads is a wolfish and ambitious man, I didn't expect him to fully protect the royal city at this time. I thought he would let the empire fall into a state of no return."

"It doesn't make sense for the royal city to be destroyed by the tyrant, and it is completely reasonable for him to do so. Now he doesn't have the title of regent, but his power is no different from the controller of the empire. Look at that...." Margret gave Bryce a look, and there were several army commanders and many nobles with private armies sitting there, and they all served Mads. Except for him, no one could bring the forces in the royal city together.

"Ah, Mads is really a hand to cover the sky...." Bryce sighed, and he was ashamed of himself, thinking that Mads' power had grown again, and more than half of the people in the parliament were his followers. It seemed that he didn't need to vote for anything, and Mads' words were enough.

Although Bael, as one of the seven kings of the demon race, had natural strength, it was not easy for us to defeat it. However, the situation is urgent, and we only have three days left. In order to let us continue to live and pass this crisis, we must unite all our strength and fight against the tyrant together!

Mads established a common enemy and wanted to integrate all the forces in the royal city.

The members of the parliament stood up and cheered, and they highly praised the prime minister Mads, and many people were very respectful of him.

Now the royal city is under the threat of Bael, and the old king is still ill and cannot get up. It seems that only Mads can take the initiative to bear the flag of resistance.

"Mads, I am willing to put all the forces of my family into the ranks of the resistance against the tyrant.

"I am also willing to it! If the tyrant dares to challenge us, we should let him have no way back!"

"The demon race is always arrogant and arrogant, but we have Mads' leadership, and we believe that it will not be difficult to pass this difficult period."

Margret watched Mads being supported by so many people, and she was not very happy inside, and she thought that this man was only for his own interests, not for the future of the empire.

In short, Mads was only a thief, who stole what belonged to Margret. She, Margret, the legitimate heir of France, had no right to speak in the parliament. The novel

"Everyone be quiet for a while!" Mads nodded and was very happy with everyone's reaction, which was very easy for him to use. "I have seen your loyalty to the empire, and if the emperor knows that everyone here is willing to go forward and backward with the empire, I believe he will also be very happy. Although I have limited talent, I am willing to make every effort to guard the empire. Yesterday, I contacted the commander of the royal city's defense army and the various knight teams, and everyone will unite in this period of time to repel the tyrant. All the troops will be temporarily under my command.

The members of the parliament began to whisper among themselves and nodded frequently, and most people had no objections and were very confident in Mads.

Now Mads seems to be the savior of the kingdom, and everyone treats him as the last straw to save their lives, and they think he is very capable.

It seems that only Margret princess's face is bad, because the right to manage the army is usually the right of the royal family, and now all the rights are given to Mads to manage, which leads to the further decline of the status of the royal family, and it is marginalized in the parliament.

The right to use the army is the right of life and death, and this is to be used by Mads? Only the royal family of France can say that it has completely become a small transparent.

If we really defeat Bael, will Mads give up the military power? Obviously not.

Margret looked at Mads with anger, thinking that this man was seizing the opportunity, but the supporting voice was getting louder and louder, and this princess of the empire could not dare to act.

The parliament has become Mads' personal toy, and he is completely controlled by him, and no one considers the feelings of the royal family.

"Of course, relying on the army alone is not enough to defeat the tyrant, we need the support of the church, because the best way to deal with demons is to ally with the enemies of demons!" Mads looked at Scott below and said seriously, "So I have invited the bishop of the O'brien Cathedral as the strategist for this defense, and he will make it easier for us to deal with the tyrant.

"Your Excellency, you are welcome, I am the cardinal Scott, who manages all the affairs of France." Scott stood up with a thick book of doctrine and greeted the nobles in the hall.

"I have already known about the attack of the tyrant on the royal city, and I am very angry about it!"

"The Goddess of Light loves this world, and all human beings are her most intimate children."

"But now the evil forces are invading the land protected by God, which is an insult to God!"

"I, as a servant of God, absolutely do not allow evil creatures to act at will on the land protected by God!"

"Don't worry, and don't think that the demon lord is invincible...."

"We have sufficient experience in the church to deal with demons, and we have even killed arrogant kings!"

"So please believe in the church, please believe that the merciful Goddess Mary will protect them...."

"This time the tyrant dared to attack the royal city alone, so he will definitely have no way back!"

title: Chapter 11 — Joan of Arc Receives Orders
content:
Chapter 11 — Joan of Arc Receives Orders

Volume 17 · Chapter 11

From the Red-Clothed Archbishop’s mouth, such words carried a convincing weight, immediately swaying many to believe.

Many began to consider that the arrival of Beelzebub wasn’t a hopeless situation, and there was still a chance to turn defeat into victory.

As a high-ranking cleric of the French region, Scott’s words held considerable weight, giving everyone present confidence.

However, Margaret listened to so many people filled with fighting spirit, their heads clouded, clearly intent on fighting the Gluttonous Monarch to the bitter end.

This didn’t align with the interests of the royal family. The losses from fighting the Demon Lord would ultimately be borne by the entire empire, causing its strength to regress.

Margaret could no longer bear it, and slowly stood up to ask, “Bishop Scott, your words have restored our confidence, but to directly confront the Gluttonous Monarch, bloodshed is inevitable. Do you have a good way to avoid conflict? After all, peace is most precious. Isn’t this conflict between the empire and the demon race rather inexplicable? If we insist on conflict, it will ultimately lead to mutual destruction, which benefits the empire in no way.”

“Tsk!” Madess secretly clicked his tongue, finding Margaret long-winded. He had finally managed to incite everyone’s hatred, only to have someone interrupt at this crucial moment, which was sure to be irritating.

“Hmm? What is it? Isn’t this Her Royal Highness, who only knows how to enjoy herself, making countless jokes and bringing shame to the French royal family? You usually don’t care about the empire at all. Why are you suddenly talking about the empire’s interests now?” Scott’s tone was full of sarcasm. He had long heard of this untalented princess.

Margaret, in this situation, jumped out wanting to reconcile with the Gluttonous Monarch, touching on many people’s sensitivities. This was going against everyone, so naturally no one would give her a good look.

Moreover, Scott, as the Red-Clothed Archbishop, was a religious leader controlling a vast area, and he wasn’t afraid of just one princess.

Blaze, standing nearby, heard Scott’s sarcastic tone and immediately stood up angrily. “Your Excellency Bishop, what did you just say!? Her Highness is the empire’s only heir. Please speak respectfully!”

This remark immediately caused the councilors to burst into laughter, clearly scoffing at Margaret’s status as the heir apparent. The royal family’s power was now dwindling, far less influential than Madess’s words.

Blaze, hearing the laughter around him, became even more enraged. “What’s so funny? Don’t you acknowledge Her Highness as the legitimate heir?”

Madess, fearing Blaze would disrupt things, said, “Blaze, calm down. The Bishop doesn’t mean anything by it. Let’s just listen to his response, okay?”

“Hmph!” Blaze snorted, very disgusted with the bureaucrats in the council. They had no real ability, only using their mouths to show off. Now they were mocking the princess, wouldn’t they become even more arrogant later?

book.SEA

;

“Since Her Royal Highness wants to seek peace with the Gluttonous Demon Lord, I would like to hear your plan?” Scott said from the stage, adopting a listening posture.

“The Gluttonous Monarch is searching for his sister. In that case, someone in the royal city is holding the Demon Lord’s sister hostage. If we find her and hand her over, all problems will be solved. Therefore, I suggest that instead of preparing for war, we conduct a carpet search of the entire royal city to find the Gluttonous Monarch’s sister…” Margaret didn’t quite agree with fighting Beelzebub to the death. Fighting the Demon Lord was a last resort.

Madess’s face immediately darkened. He had to admit Margaret was calm, not like others who wanted to fight the Gluttonous Demon Lord to the death.

However, aside from Madess himself, no one dared to be certain that Beelzebub’s sister was even in the royal city, nor could they bear the consequences of not finding her.

“Your Highness, please abandon your naive ideas. If we don’t find the Gluttonous Monarch’s sister, can you take responsibility for that? In three days, we will all be in danger. Can a simple ‘not found’ make the Gluttonous Demon Lord leave? Wake up, Your Highness! As the sole heir to the throne, haven’t you heard that only strength is the capital to reason with?! ” Madess scolded harshly, fearing Margaret would disrupt his plans.

“The demon race has never proactively invaded human territory. I don’t believe the Seven Kings of the demon race would attack human territory for no reason. Ultimately, someone in the royal city provoked the Gluttonous Monarch and harmed his sister. If we don’t find the real culprit, how many people will die in vain?” Margaret raised her voice, making herself sound more confident.

The council fell silent. Some people began to waver, feeling that finding Beelzebub’s sister was the correct solution, a more gentle approach.

After all, going to war with the Gluttonous Monarch meant sacrifice, and countless people would die in the conflict, which wasn’t beneficial to the empire.

Madess’s face turned black. He remained silent, unable to believe that Margaret, who usually didn’t dare to fart, was so bold today, openly expressing a different opinion from his own.

“Your Highness, I advise you not to naively think of negotiating peace with the Gluttonous Demon Lord, because demons are not trustworthy.” Scott expressed his firm opposition, then turned to the councilors and said, “Our Church has been studying demons for thousands of years and is very familiar with their race. Beelzebub’s sister is named Miranda. Although she has no combat ability, her bloodline is very noble. This time, Beelzebub claimed that he would spare us if we handed over his sister. This is just a trick demons are best at! Everyone must not easily believe it!”

“A lie? Your Excellency Bishop, what evidence do you have?” Margaret frowned, clearly sensing resistance.

“This doesn’t need evidence. Our Church has dealt with demons for thousands of years. Can’t we even see their nature? The Gluttonous Monarch is definitely aiming to destroy the royal city, and finding his sister is just an excuse.” Scott retorted, then said, “Although you are a princess, this concerns the fate of the entire empire. I hope you don’t continue to fantasize that demons can be reasoned with peacefully.”

Madess heard the Archbishop’s words and was overjoyed, quickly seizing the opportunity to say, “Yes, Your Highness, I know you’re used to playing around, but this is not the time for foolishness. If you continue to babble, you’ll be misleading the country…”

Margaret’s face was cold. She didn’t speak, feeling she had no voice in the council, and few people would listen to her.

“Everyone, do not easily believe the words of demons. They are a despicable race and will fabricate any lie for their own benefit! All we can do is fight back!” Scott urged everyone to take up arms and announced, “In the name of the Red-Clothed Archbishop, I announce that the Church will fully assist the empire in fighting the Gluttonous Demon Lord. I will appoint Joan of Arc, renowned as the Saint of France, as the main force in this crusade. She was born in France, has deep affection for this land, and has been trained in fighting demons in the Vatican since childhood. She is considered the best substitute for the Hero! ”

Below, in the audience seats of the council, Joan of Arc slowly stood up. To avoid attracting attention, the Crimson Witch, a pseudo-artifact, was wrapped in white cloth. Her eyes were firm, and she responded with a resounding voice:

“233rd Hero Candidate, Joan of Arc, will not fail in her mission!”

title: Chapter 12 — The Knight in Prison (Apologies for the late update)
content:
Chapter 12 — The Knight in Prison (Apologies for the late update)

Volume 17 · Chapter 12

The assembled senators turned their gaze toward Joan, many of them seemingly familiar with the name of the French Saint.

After all, Joan was the strongest inquisitor of the Holy Church’s Inquisition, often operating at the forefront of battles against evil forces.

As a result, she was often called the French Saint by many, praised for her resistance to evil and her efforts to save the people.

Seeing Joan take the lead in this confrontation with the gluttonous Demon Lord instantly put people at ease.

The senators below whispered among themselves, praising Joan’s involvement, feeling that the situation was becoming more stable.

Joan had obtained the pseudo-divine weapon Crimson Witch, and with this holy lance’s blessing, she felt she had the strength to fight the Demon Lord!

Like the legendary Lancer Hero, she would slay Lucifer II and achieve greatness.

Joan thought to herself that as the new owner of Crimson Witch, she absolutely could not let this divine weapon bring shame upon her.

*"I didn’t expect the Chief Inquisitor would join as well,"* Blaze frowned, realizing the Church was taking the fight against the demons seriously.

*"You seem very familiar with this androgynous person,"* Margaret, the imperial princess who held high status, questioned, not knowing much about the French Saint.

*"Your Highness, calling someone androgynous always feels like an insult..."* Blaze stammered awkwardly.

*"Oh? If she didn’t speak, I would’ve thought she was a man?"* Margaret said with a hint of meaning.

*"I actually admire Joan’s personality—she’s decisive and never hesitates."* Blaze didn’t see anything wrong with her short hair and masculine appearance.
