*"Hmm? So you like this type?"* Margaret asked with interest, having always thought Blaze was a tough man—she hadn’t expected him to have a preference for androgynous women.

*"...Not like that, Your Highness, please don’t misunderstand..."* Blaze’s face turned red, and he hesitated, unable to continue speaking.

Margaret didn’t bother teasing Blaze further and pressed on, *"Is this Joan well-known? Why haven’t I ever heard of her?"*

*"She’s very famous among the common people—she fights tirelessly against evil, earning the title of the French Saint. She’s an admirable woman."* Blaze evaluated, continuing, *"Her strength is decent; she’s the strongest inquisitor of the Church, slaughtering countless evil creatures. She’s defeated many hidden demons within the human empire. But compared to her strength, I’m still superior."*

*"So that’s how it is..."* Margaret studied Joan’s expression, which was meticulous and composed, thinking that this young woman had already achieved so much. The Church must be full of talent—if she’s just a Hero-in-training, then the real Hero must be even stronger.

Seeing that the Church was fully supporting the resistance, Medes nodded in satisfaction, *"Thank you, Bishop Scott, for your support of the empire. But to defeat the gluttonous Demon Lord, it’s still not enough. We need more strong warriors to join us. I’m sure everyone has heard of the Empire’s Three Knights—Blaze, Battiloka, and Robert. Each is mighty, possessing invincible strength. Their power is indispensable in this fight against the Demon Lord!"*

Blaze slightly furrowed his brow, thinking that Medes was indeed as predicted by the princess—he was now trying to rally all forces, including the Three Knights.

Below, a group of people began discussing the fame of the French Three Knights, which was as well-known as thunder striking the earth.

*"Will the Three Knights even participate in the crusade against the gluttonous Demon Lord this time? That’s definitely a good sign!"*

*"Yes, the Three Knights are the face of the empire—there’s no doubt about their strength. Even if the opponent is a Demon Lord, they might not fear them!"*

*"Especially Blaze—no one has ever seen him lose! So many young men who came to compete for my hand in marriage were all sent away by him!"*

*"Although Blaze is the first knight of the empire, Robert isn’t far behind. As the Grand Master of the martial arts, he opened his own dojo, teaching his own techniques. Now, his students are everywhere."*

*"Exactly! Robert’s martial arts are unmatched, a representative figure of the empire’s martial traditions. And he’s also very humble—no less than Blaze!"*

*"No matter what, the Three Knights together will surely turn the tide. Don’t worry about that gluttonous king."*

Listening to the senators’ praise of the Three Knights, Blaze’s expression remained unchanged, showing his unshakable composure—evidence of their status in the empire.

Medes turned to Blaze below and asked cautiously, *"I wonder, Blaze, are you willing to help the empire resolve this crisis?"*

Blaze recalled Margaret’s words—now the enemy was the gluttonous Demon Lord, and he needed to cooperate with Medes. So he spoke firmly, *"As a knight, I naturally wish to risk my life for the empire. But I oppose Battiloka joining—he doesn’t deserve to be called a knight; he’s nothing but a prisoner!"*

Among the French Three Knights, Battiloka was the most peculiar—he had no trace of a knight’s conscience, instead acting like a wicked criminal.

Although Battiloka’s character was extremely questionable, his strength was undeniable—he ranked among the Three Knights, proving he had real talent.

Battiloka was a rare warrior-mage—a dual-class of combat and magic. He combined martial arts with magic, unleashing destruction beyond imagination!

Though he shared the same dual-class as Alice, the warrior-mage’s fighting style differed from that of a mage-swordswoman. They fought with nothing but their bare hands, making their difficulty far greater than that of a mage-swordswoman.

Warrior-mages often had the agility of a brawler and the explosive power of magic, making them extremely formidable opponents.

Despite Battiloka’s status as one of the Three Knights, Blaze saw him as a disgrace and rarely mentioned him.

Because Battiloka was a prisoner—three years ago, he had killed the son of an imperial duke and was sentenced to life imprisonment.

A murderer, yet one of the Three Knights—this made Blaze feel ashamed. Now, Medes wanted to bring him out to fight the Demon Lord, and he was unwilling.

*"Blaze, this is a critical time. No matter what Battiloka did in the past, we can temporarily overlook it. The empire needs his strength."* Medes spoke sternly, trying to make Blaze understand how urgent the situation was.

*"But Battiloka is a murderer! Such a person isn’t worthy of my trust—just thinking about fighting beside him makes me ashamed!"* Blaze snapped back angrily.

*"Mind your place, Blaze! I’m not asking for your opinion—this is an order!"* Medes stood firm in his role as chancellor, pressuring Blaze, *"I am the empire’s chancellor, and the Emperor himself said that all matters are temporarily under my management. Everyone here heard that—do you think I can’t command you?"* Now the empire is at a life-or-death crossroads—don’t let your personal emotions ruin the bigger picture. You can’t afford this responsibility! I give you two days—if the Three Knights aren’t assembled, you’ll be considered a traitor to the empire!"*

*"Hah!"* Blaze’s face twisted in anger, his resentment toward Medes growing even stronger.

Would Medes really release Battiloka from the empire’s most secure prison?

He was a madman—no one could control him!

My scar on the eye is his doing—I still remember the pain then!

Though I despise him, I can’t deny his strength...

In my entire life, the only one who could leave a scar on me was this man—Battiloka!

title: Chapter 13 — Qi Gong Master Robert
content:
Chapter 13 — Qi Gong Master Robert

Volume 17 · Chapter 13

Mades looked at Blaze below, whose face had darkened and who remained silent, too lazy to pursue anything. After all, his orders had already been issued; even if it were the Empire’s foremost warrior, failure to comply would bring punishment.
“There is one last matter: in this confrontation with the Gluttony Lord, we will deploy the twelve legendary magic cannons stored in the imperial secret chamber.” Upon saying this, the councilors below erupted in an uproar, beginning to discuss heatedly— “To deploy the legendary magic cannons! ?That superweapon containing ancient power? “Good heavens! That is the treasure that founded the Empire; are we really going to use it directly against the Demon Lord? ?” “Now there’s a show to watch: theoretically, no one could survive a bombardment from twelve legendary magic cannons.”
Margaret furrowed her brows; the situation was exactly as she had anticipated, and Mades had mobilized everything usable, not even sparing the empire’s treasured heirlooms. “However, using the legendary magic cannons requires the emperor’s verbal edict, but His Majesty is now in poor health and unable to handle this matter. Therefore, as his deputy during his illness, I have decided to adopt a council vote: if the majority agrees to use the legendary magic cannons, we will not seek the emperor’s approval and will directly deploy them in this confrontation.” Mades surveyed everyone and added, “Recently, His Majesty’s condition is not optimistic; I suggest we not disturb him. With the royal capital plunged into crisis, some cumbersome old rules should be discarded for everyone’s survival—employing the legendary magic cannons is urgent.”
Mades made his intention clear: the old king’s health is poor, and it would be unwise to bother him now, especially with war imminent; his tone implied the king should decide, but it would be better for us to act first and report later.
Sure enough, as soon as Mades finished speaking, he received an immediate response; most of the councilors raised their hands in approval of his proposal, directly bypassing the royal family to employ the legendary magic cannons.
Mades nodded satisfactorily, having secured an overwhelming majority vote; he believed the empire had staked much of its wealth, and losses in the confrontation with Beelzebub would not be small, ultimately leaving him to profit. As long as the empire suffers grave injury in its battle against the Gluttony Lord, the blood clan’s plan to establish an Eternal Night Empire would proceed all the more smoothly, wouldn’t it?
“Mades, this guy is utterly arrogant—even though Your Highness is right here, he ignores your presence and dares to use the legendary magic cannons!” Blaze said lowly, indignant, feeling that Margaret, as an imperial princess, should at least be consulted; instead, he completely disregarded others. “The council has become Mades’ tool, letting him do as he pleases.... Margaret shows no concern on the surface, but inside she is deeply unsettled. Damnable Mades, we’ll see what happens. Sooner or later you’ll pay for what you’ve done today. Using the legendary magic cannons without my consent, acting as if the royal family were all dead?”
After the emergency council concluded, most of the forces in the royal capital had already been mobilized. All strength gathered together to resist Beelzebub’s assault to the death. Several well-equipped legions, the Three Knights, Joan wielding a pseudo-divine artifact, and the twelve legendary magic cannons—these constituted essentially all the power the capital could muster, all heeding Chancellor Mades’ wisdom and destined to fight Beelzebub to the end. Although the empire still possessed considerable strength elsewhere, the royal capital was now sealed off by Beelzebub, leaving most regions unaware of the capital’s plight. From this moment on, the sound of swords being sharpened never ceased within the capital; the air was thick with the scent of pre‑battle gunpowder, and a desperate resistance against the Demon Lord’s oppression had become inevitable. Margaret’s feeble voice of negotiation was long since drowned by the fury Mades had stirred, rendering her utterly insignificant; no one paid any heed to this incompetent princess.
In the west of the royal capital, nestled against towering mountains, the martial arts hall of Robert, one of the Three Knights, is located here; he frequently imparts to his students the essence of battle aura. Robert is considered the finest fighter in all of France, the object of admiration for many youths, and his mastery of battle aura has reached a state of profound subtlety and relentless refinement. While many believe a fighter must engage in close‑quarters grappling, Robert is different—he can unleash battle aura as a long‑range attack, earning him the title of qigong master. Robert is also a Saint‑tier powerhouse, yet far surpasses his peers of the same tier; this stems from his technique: his defense is like an impregnable shield, his offense like a blade that cuts iron as easily as mud. Among the Three Knights, Robert’s strength is not much inferior to Blaze’s; the two are very close, but owing to his low‑key disposition, his fame is not great. Although Robert is a member of the Three Knights, he hardly ever appears in the knightly order; at barely thirty he lives like a retired old man, cultivating himself and nurturing his vitality.
At that moment, in the open‑air dojo, the sturdy Robert wore his training uniform and assumed an attacking stance, with a circle of straw dummies set up beside him. A crowd of young on

title: Chapter 14 — Boya Prison
content:
Chapter 14 — Boya Prison

Volume 17 · Chapter 14

The students all showed expressions of reverence, as if Robert were the strongest fighter in the world, worthy of their following.

Robert didn’t feel he’d exaggerated, because he was full of confidence in his martial arts; as long as the Gluttony Demon Lord wasn’t overwhelmingly powerful, he stood a chance!

“Yo! Robert, long time no see…”

Blaze’s voice suddenly rang out from behind Robert, appearing there without anyone noticing when.

Although Blaze disliked Prime Minister Mads immensely, he still had to prioritize the bigger picture and put confronting the Gluttony Demon Lord first.

So Blaze could only temporarily follow Mads’s orders and find the other two of the Three Knights.

The first, of course, was his friend Robert, and the easiest to locate.

Blaze and Robert were good friends, with a deep connection and no grudges between them.

The students, seeing Imperial First Hero Blaze, all lit up, whispering amongst themselves below.

“Th-That… is First Hero Blaze-dono! He actually came to the dojo!?”

“What a robust physique, and that heavy sword… so cool!”

“He’s no weaker than the teacher, it’s rude to comment on someone like him based on appearance alone!”

Blaze was the most famous of the Three Knights, almost like an idol, so it wasn’t surprising the students were so adoring.

Robert turned to see his old friend, giving him a bear hug with a smile. “Long time no see, Blaze.”

“Indeed, it feels like a long time since we last drank together. How have you been?” Blaze asked with a smile.

“Still the same as always, drinking tea every day, teaching martial arts to students, and striving to cultivate more talent.” Robert scratched his head, laughing heartily.

“You’re really diligent. What you do is more meaningful than my work running errands for Princess-dono.” Blaze said with a helpless tone.

“Being able to serve Princess-dono is an honor. I, a semi-retired man, can’t compare to you.” Robert said awkwardly.

“Speaking of which, your skills have improved considerably. I’m afraid I wouldn’t be your match in a fight now.” Blaze said meaningfully.

“Don’t tease me. A guy like you would never willingly fall behind me?” Robert retorted, very familiar with Blaze’s personality—he absolutely wouldn’t stagnate.

“Haha, you know me best.” Blaze burst out laughing.

Although they were friends, their relationship was more like healthy competition; neither was willing to lose to the other.

“You suddenly came to find me, there must be something wrong, right?” Robert’s expression became serious, feeling that Blaze coming to him now must be an extremely urgent matter.

“Yes.” Blaze nodded, speaking in a very serious tone. “The Gluttony Demon Lord is ravaging the royal capital. All available forces have been mobilized to fight the Demon Lord to the death. We need your strength.”

Robert’s eyes changed instantly upon hearing this, immediately understanding the situation—the Empire needed him.

“As a loyal knight of the Empire, I have no choice but to answer the call!”

After finding Robert, Blaze didn’t stop.

Instead, he headed directly to the Empire’s most secure prison—

Boya Prison.

This prison was like a world apart, located in the most remote corner of the royal capital.

From its inception, Boya Prison was built to hold the most heinous criminals, and was the place all evildoers feared most.

If a person was imprisoned in Boya Prison, it meant their life was ruined, and they would spend the rest of their days suffering torment within its walls.

To this day, no one had ever escaped from Boya Prison. Once you went in, you’d never come out, forever losing your status as a human being.

A terrifying aspect of Boya Prison was that no one treated the prisoners as human beings, but rather as livestock to be beaten, abused, and humiliated at will.

Prisoners lived a life of darkness, subjected to inhumane treatment every day, and many eventually went insane and committed suicide.

If agonizing screams came from Boya Prison, it shouldn’t be surprising, as it was the most common occurrence.

Although Blaze deeply disliked Bartilocca, the man was still one of the Three Knights, and his assistance was needed in the current situation.

Blaze absolutely had to temporarily put aside his prejudice against Bartilocca and join forces with him to fight the Gluttony Demon Lord—that was the correct choice.

The two were on their way to Boya Prison, passing many soldiers standing ready in the streets and alleys of the royal capital.

Every soldier’s expression was grim, knowing that war was imminent, and whether they could resolve the crisis in the royal capital depended entirely on the upcoming battle.

Robert looked at the damaged streets and couldn’t help but ask, “What’s the situation like now?”

“Not optimistic. Almost all available forces have been deployed, but I’ve witnessed the Gluttony Demon Lord’s methods, and I’m not confident we can defeat him.” Blaze replied seriously, despite the powerful lineup they now had, he still felt uneasy.

“Really? Has the Gluttony Demon Lord’s power become so overwhelming that it makes you lose confidence?” Robert was a little surprised.

“Perhaps. But the Gluttony Lord absolutely cannot be underestimated. I’ve never seen him take things seriously.” Blaze cautioned Robert not to underestimate him.

“Until we fight him, no one can guarantee who’s stronger. I think the Gluttony Lord isn’t invincible.” Robert felt Blaze was exaggerating.

“That’s because you’ve never seen a Demon Lord with your own eyes. When you have, I believe you’ll change your mind.” Blaze didn’t say much more, understanding Robert’s pride.

“Hearing you say that, I’ve become very interested in this strong enemy….” Robert said meaningfully, wondering what the Gluttony Lord was like, and how he could shake his rival’s fighting spirit.

Unknowingly, the two had arrived at the infamous Boya Prison.

The towering prison walls made the entire prison look incredibly solid and ominous.

After reporting their identities, the heavy prison gates slowly opened, allowing them to enter.

As Three Knights, Blaze and Robert had the right to enter and exit this most secure prison freely, without being obstructed.

But the massive statue that came into view after the gates opened completely stunned them both.

“Uh!”

The huge statue appeared to be painstakingly carved by hand, lacking any aesthetic appeal.

It was vaguely visible as a man wearing a collar, striking a libertine pose, appearing very dignified and imposing.

“…..” Blaze widened his eyes. Although the statue’s craftsmanship wasn’t great, the man’s features were very distinct—it was clearly sculpted after Bartilocca!

What the hell!

Isn’t this a prison for holding prisoners!?

Why is there a statue of Bartilocca here!?

He’s a murderer! Not a worthy figure to be celebrated!

Boya Prison is the Empire’s most secure prison, yet it has a statue of a prisoner erected within it?

This is outrageous! What on earth is going on….

title: Chapter 15 — Batiloka
content:
Chapter 15 — Batiloka

Volume 17 · Chapter 15

Blaze and Robert entered the Bota Prison, with a guard leading them from the front.

On both sides were densely packed cells, from which occasional groans of pain could be heard.

Although torches lit both sides, the place still seemed far too dim.

"Forgive me, honored guests, for not greeting you properly at a distance. I have no money to do so." The warden, standing beside them, forced a smile. His pockmarked face was unpleasant to look at.

"Don't worry about it." Blaze waved his hand, but he was still deeply puzzled by the statue of Bartiloka erected in the prison. "Warden, I have a question for you."

"Please, go ahead." The warden rubbed his hands together, his attitude extremely enthusiastic.

"Why is there a statue of Bartiloka standing in the prison? He is a prisoner, after all. This clearly violates the rules, doesn't it?" Blaze frowned as he asked, his mood souring. This was the empire's most secure prison, yet they had built a statue for a convict? How absurd!

"This... this isn't our fault! It's Bartiloka who—"

"Barti... sir?" The warden couldn't even finish his sentence before Blaze cut him off. He was extremely displeased by the sight of imperial soldiers showing respect to a criminal.

Even though Bartiloka was indeed one of the Three Knights, his current status was that of a prisoner. Even ordinary people held a higher position than him. Yet here was the warden addressing Bartiloka as "sir," which infuriated Blaze.

"Warden, watch your words. Bartiloka is a prisoner. You should not address him as 'sir.'"

"N-No... I sincerely apologize, Lord Blaze, but no one can restrain Bartiloka. Even here in Bota Prison, he wields power like a local tyrant. We guards don't dare provoke him. As for the statue outside... it was actually built by the prisoners on his orders. We... we couldn't stop it..." The warden wore a troubled expression, his face turning pale at the mere thought of Bartiloka. Fear filled his heart.

"You, as the prison's administrator, actually let a prisoner run amok like this?!" Blaze's temper flared, as if he were interrogating the warden for his crimes.

"Lord, I had no choice!" The warden quickly dropped to one knee, explaining, "Bartiloka is one of the Three Knights, a man of immense power. Even locked in prison, we have no way to control him. Though we appear to be in charge, ever since Bartiloka arrived, he has been the true master here. As long as he doesn't escape or cause a major disturbance, we consider ourselves lucky..."

"Are you making excuses for yourself?" Blaze was not convinced. Building a statue for a prisoner was preposterous!

"Enough, Blaze. Don't make things difficult for him. Clearly, we understand better than anyone what kind of monster Bartiloka is..." Robert suddenly spoke, his words heavy with meaning.

"But this is going too far. Bartiloka is a murderer, yet he lives in comfort here." Blaze was deeply displeased.

"For Bartiloka, not causing trouble everywhere is already considered serving his sentence. His power is too overwhelming, to the point where even he can't control it. You should know that, right?" Robert paused before continuing, "Three years ago, Bartiloka killed the duke's son. Perhaps that incident truly wasn't his fault. Maybe it was because he couldn't control his own strength. What he considers a light push would be a devastating attack to an ordinary person. Even if you and I joined forces against Bartiloka, we wouldn't have a hundred percent chance of taking him down, would we?"

Blaze furrowed his brows, hesitating. He had personally experienced Bartiloka's strength—the man was the only one who had left a scar on his body.

"And don't forget, Bartiloka has been wearing chains that seal his magic and aura. A normal person wearing them wouldn't be able to exert even the slightest bit of power, no different from an ordinary man. Yet he moves about as if they were nothing, still capable of unleashing astonishing strength. If Bartiloka were to break those chains, his power would likely surge to an unimaginable level." Robert spoke gravely.

Blaze fell silent, realizing that pressuring the warden served no purpose. If even sealing chains couldn't restrain him, how could a mere prison possibly do so?

It seemed that as long as Bartiloka didn't leave the prison, he was already being remarkably well-behaved...

Following the warden, they arrived at Bartiloka's cell.

Blaze and Robert's expressions immediately darkened. What they saw before them was utterly unacceptable.

Though this was a prison, the cell before them was entirely different from the others—excessively luxurious, like a high-end VIP suite. A warm fireplace flickered with light, and the room was furnished with all manner of high-quality items.

Prisoners in striped uniforms surrounded a man, massaging his legs and shoulders with more care than they would show their own fathers.

It seemed this man, attended to by so many inmates, was Bartiloka. He truly lived a life of unparalleled comfort in prison.

Bartiloka appeared much younger than Blaze and Robert, though his appearance was unkempt and disheveled. Dark circles under his eyes made him look like a panda, and the sealing collar around his neck was highly visible.

Though Bartiloka also wore the striped uniform of a prisoner, seated at the center of the crowd, he looked more like the king of the entire prison, basking in everyone's service.

"Bartiloka, what do you think you're doing?" Blaze demanded, his face dark.

So comfortable was Bartiloka that he hadn't even noticed the two familiar faces in his cell. He lazily opened his eyes, took a good look, and said, "Huh? It's you two. Why are you here all of a sudden? Don't tell me you've done something wrong and are here to be my cellmates?"

"You're talking nonsense!" Robert scolded, wanting him to watch his tone.

"Do you really think I'd believe you'd come here just to visit me out of boredom?" Bartiloka looked at them with keen interest.

"All of you, get out! Robert and I have business to discuss with Bartiloka in private!" Blaze ordered.

Everyone in the cell trembled and quickly left, leaving only Blaze, Robert, and Bartiloka.

Though Blaze found Bartiloka insufferable, considering the threat of the Gluttonous Demon Lord, they needed this man's strength.

So without hesitation, Blaze got straight to the point. "Bartiloka, listen carefully. The empire is currently under the threat of the Demon Lord. In three days, it will face the danger of annihilation. So we need you to redeem yourself by joining us in repelling the Gluttonous Demon Lord. Do you understand?"

"Hah, so you want my help to take down the Demon Lord? I knew it wasn't going to be anything good..." Bartiloka grumbled, responding in a mocking tone. "Three years ago, I accidentally killed the duke's little brat, and for that, I've been locked up here for three whole years. Now you come asking me to save the empire? Do you take me for a dog that'll wag its tail in gratitude for a bone?"

title: Chapter 16 — Madman
content:
Chapter 16 — Madman

Volume 17 · Chapter 16

Hearing Batiloka’s response, Blaze’s brows knitted tightly, his forehead darkening with swirling storm clouds—clearly, his mood had taken a sharp turn for the worse.

“Batiloka,” Robert tried to reason with him, “no matter what, you *are* one of the Three Knights—now the Empire needs your strength.” Though he wasn’t entirely confident whether Batiloka would listen.

“What nonsense about the Three Knights?” Batiloka stood slowly from the soft sofa, rubbing his shoulders as if loosening his muscles. “That title was just shoved on me by others.”

“Don’t act like that,” Robert frowned, thinking that even after three years in prison, Batiloka seemed to have no remorse at all. “You *did* kill the Duke’s son. If you’d followed the rules, how could you have ended up in prison?”

“It’s not my fault!” Batiloka spread his hands, dismissing it casually. “That little brat was so frail—all I did was scratch him, and he died.”

“Those things are in the past, Batiloka,” Robert coaxed. “If you just help the Empire weather this crisis, all your past mistakes can be wiped clean. I and Blaze will both intercede for you, and you can regain your freedom.”

“Freedom?” Robert, you’re still the same old you, always so perceptive. Batiloka smirked. “If I wanted to leave, no one could stop me. This prison, so famous for its security, has already become my backyard.”

“This is your chance to redeem yourself!” Blaze couldn’t hold back, snapping. “If you don’t seize it, you’ll never deserve to be a knight!”

“Redeem? I’ve never had any guilt, Blaze,” Batiloka scoffed, turning his nose up at the Empire’s first Hero. “Don’t force your naivety on me—it’s disgusting.”

“You—!” Blaze’s anger flared, ready to strike.

Fortunately, Robert pulled him back, whispering, “Stay calm, Blaze. Batiloka is proud to the bone—you keep calling him a criminal, and he’ll never join us.”

“What then? Can’t we just keep dragging this out?” Blaze gritted his teeth. “This man doesn’t deserve to be one of the Three Knights. Just being near him makes me sick.”

“Be patient,” Robert soothed Blaze, then turned back to Batiloka. “What would it take for you to help the Empire? I won’t believe you don’t want to leave this prison.”

“Robert, you’re still the same old you, always so good at reading people,” Batiloka raised an eyebrow, pondering for a moment. “Helping the Empire isn’t impossible, though.”

“How?” Robert pressed.

“Fight me,” Batiloka said, glancing at both of them, his eyes flickering with a hint of heat. “If you win, I’ll listen to you.”

Blaze didn’t hesitate—he drew his massive sword, his pent-up rage finally finding an outlet.

“So simple?” Robert raised an eyebrow, rubbing his fists together in anticipation.

“Simple?” Batiloka made no move, his tone scornful. “I just want to beat up both of you. There’s no one here to fight in this prison—truth be told, I’ve been itching to do this for three years.”

“Hey!”

Blaze’s eyes widened as golden battle energy erupted from him like a volcanic eruption, surging forward.

He swung his heavy sword across at Batiloka with full force—clearly intending to cleave him in two.

“Hahaha, you really hate me, Blaze!”

Batiloka reacted instantly, laughing recklessly as his form dissolved into a blur, vanishing.

In the next instant, he stood upright on Blaze’s towering sword—unharmed.

Batiloka slowly crouched on the blade, grinning triumphantly at Blaze, taunting him.

“You’re the Empire’s first Hero, aren’t you? But you don’t seem so great. Your reputation and strength don’t match at all.”

“You—you *madman*—!” Blaze’s eyes bulged with fury, his jaw twitching.

“Hey!” Robert shouted, unleashing his attack—a lightning-fast kick aimed straight at Batiloka.

Batiloka stood his ground, blocking the strike with his hand, then flipped through the air before landing smoothly on the ground.

Robert assumed his stance, golden battle energy crackling from his fingertips like flickering flames, all his energy focused into his fingers.

Unlike Blaze, Robert wasn’t a brute—he was a killer, restrained but always ready to strike the deadliest blow.

He didn’t stop. With the speed of lightning, he pressed his attack, slashing at Batiloka with his hands formed into blades, his movements sharp and relentless—truly the Empire’s fighting authority.

Yet Batiloka remained undeterred, grinning like a madman, dodging every strike and pulling back.

“Hmm, not bad, Robert,” he chuckled. “Three years apart, and you’ve improved a lot. I can feel the heat—worth praising.”

Robert narrowed his eyes, not replying, sensing the challenge was harder than expected. “Blaze, let’s go!”

“Oh, give this madman a taste of his own medicine,” Blaze raised his heavy sword, preparing to charge.

“You think I’m the shame of the Three Knights?” Batiloka spread his arms, his body erupting in scorching flames, turning him into a living inferno. The prison’s temperature skyrocketed, as if they were standing in a furnace.

Overwhelming pressure radiated from him, making Blaze and Robert struggle to breathe—like facing a monster.

A bead of cold sweat trickled down Blaze’s forehead. Though they felt the pressure, they pressed forward, launching a combined assault on Batiloka.

Their figures clashed violently, thunderous explosions ringing out. The massive prison trembled, as if ready to collapse at any moment.

Different forces clashed—flames filled the air. Blaze and Robert roared, attacking with everything they had, determined to crush the arrogant madman.

Blaze’s strength was formidable, his battle energy like a roaring tiger, unleashing every trick. His massive sword slashed with terrifying force, as if he could cleave through a mountain.

Robert’s techniques were exquisite, his mastery of battle energy flawless. His entire body seemed to be a weapon—even the strongest foes would be beheaded with a single misstep.

But under their combined assault, Batiloka moved with effortless ease. His flaming fists struck them back, each blow unstoppable.

After dozens of exchanges, Blaze and Robert were both stunned—this madman was *too* strong.

We’re fighting together, and it’s having *no* effect!

And this is with his power sealed—can you imagine what would happen if his seal were broken? The sheer scale of his strength is unimaginable.

title: Chapter 17 — The Death Limit Has Arrived
content:
Chapter 17 — The Death Limit Has Arrived

Volume 17 · Chapter 17

Blaze and Robert joined forces to suppress Bartiloka, unleashing a barrage of highly destructive attacks that shook the prison to its foundations, threatening to collapse it at any moment.

The three figures clashed and grappled in close combat, their battle fierce and intense, neither side gaining the upper hand in the short exchange!

Yet Bartiloka maintained his usual grinning, carefree demeanor. It had been so long since he last fought someone—today’s rare chance to stretch his limbs filled him with excitement.

"You two team up and this is the best you can do? How disappointing. I was hoping you’d bring me some fun..."

Bartiloka’s body blazed with flames, perfectly merging magic and martial arts into one.

Even surrounded by Blaze and Robert working together, he seemed to handle the pressure without the slightest strain?

What was even more terrifying was that Bartiloka was still in a state of sealed power, yet he could dominate the fight against their combined assault.

It seemed Bartiloka truly was the anomaly among the Three Knights—his character might be neither good nor evil, but his strength was undeniably the greatest.

"Don’t underestimate us, you lunatic!"

Blaze roared, gathering power into his greatsword. A golden radiance erupted, illuminating the entire dark prison.

With the momentum of a mountain-splitting strike, he swung the greatsword down at Bartiloka. The searing blade energy surged forward like a devastating flood, unstoppable!

Robert, of course, did not stand idle. He suddenly appeared beside Bartiloka, his hands moving so fast they left afterimages.

He condensed his battle aura into a single point on his palm, aiming to break through with a precise strike—without hesitation, he unleashed his ultimate killing move!

Robert had completely cut off Bartiloka’s retreat. The only options left were to either take Robert’s fatal blow or face Blaze’s brutal sword energy head-on.

"Hah, I’ve had my fun. Three years apart, and you two haven’t improved much."

Bartiloka remained calm, opening his left hand. Suddenly, flames erupted from his palm, surging upward endlessly.

Even the stone walls around them were scorched red, as if on the verge of melting.

With the two knights’ attacks closing in, Bartiloka let out a mighty shout and slammed his flaming left hand into the ground.

The earth trembled violently, and boundless infernos burst from beneath the prison floor, engulfing the entire cell and incinerating everything within range!

From outside the Boya Prison, a towering pillar of fire shot into the sky, punching a massive hole through the ceiling.

The spectacle was so grand that nothing short of a volcanic eruption could compare to the scene unfolding now!

To unleash such overwhelming flames in an instant proved Bartiloka’s magic was profound beyond ordinary comprehension!

Once the flames subsided, the Boya Prison returned to silence.

But the guards and prisoners inside had already been terrified out of their wits, kneeling on the ground and trembling in fear.

Inside the cell, Blaze and Robert lay weakly on the floor, their bodies wreathed in black smoke from burns, clearly injured.

Bartiloka, still in his school uniform, stood over the two defeated men with his hands in his pockets, looking down at them with disdain.

"Tch, so this is all you’ve got? Get lost already. I never want to see either of you again. What a letdown—can’t even find a worthy opponent to make me go all out."

Blaze and Robert slowly picked themselves up from the ground, glaring at the arrogant Bartiloka, their hearts heavy with helplessness.

Though they hadn’t used their full strength against him, the brief exchange was enough to unsettle them deeply.

Bartiloka could suppress them even with his power sealed. If that seal were ever removed, wouldn’t they stand absolutely no chance?

Blaze, simple-minded and quick to anger, was infuriated by Bartiloka’s taunts. He picked up his heavy sword from the ground, ready to fight the madman to the death!

But Robert was calmer. Bartiloka’s words had struck a chord with him, so he quickly stepped in to stop the enraged Blaze.

"Wait, don’t attack."

"Don’t stop me! If this lunatic won’t serve the Empire, we might as well kill him. He’s nothing but a ticking time bomb!" Blaze snapped furiously, as if he wanted to behead Bartiloka himself.

"Bartiloka can still be useful to the Empire. Calm down for a moment." Robert said seriously.

"Do you have a plan?" Blaze suppressed his rage, forcing himself to ask patiently.

Robert didn’t answer. Instead, he looked at the haughty Bartiloka, recalling the past.

Ever since he had known Bartiloka, he had never once seen anyone force this madman to go all out!

The sealing collar around his neck had never been removed—no enemy had ever pushed him to the point of unleashing his full power.

It seemed Bartiloka truly longed for a powerful foe, one worthy of his absolute effort!

Robert knew that although Bartiloka was human, the Empire had always treated him as a weapon. And a weapon unused was a weapon without value.

"You said you want to find a strong enemy, to go all out in a real fight?"

"Huh? What’s wrong with that?" Bartiloka tilted his head.

"Well, you’ll get your wish soon enough. Without a doubt, the Seven Demon Lords of the demon race are each monsters in their own right. Legend says they stand at the peak of this world. Why not go test yourself against them? You’d redeem your crimes and satisfy your desires at the same time, wouldn’t you?" Robert spoke with calm certainty.

"Are those Demon Lords really that strong? Worth me going all out for a good, hard fight?" Bartiloka sounded skeptical.

"Of course. Blaze himself said so. He once saw the Demon Lord of Gluttony, and just one glance from that demon filled him with terror." Robert said meaningfully.

Bartiloka lifted his eyelids, pondered for a few seconds, then revealed a mysterious smile. "Now that’s interesting."

Three days later...

Today was the day the deadline arrived. The Demon Lord of Gluttony would descend once more, bathing the capital of the Franks Empire in blood!

Margaret stood on the city walls, dressed in a long gown and a red cloak against the cold, gazing out at the entire royal capital shrouded in dark clouds. The sky and earth were filled with oppressive gloom.

Below, the empire’s knights stood in formation. A rough estimate put their numbers at 50,000 heavily armored cavalry and 100,000 imperial guards—every last soldier the capital had to offer had been deployed for this battle.

They were armed to the teeth, their swords polished to a mirror shine, showing just how seriously they took this fight.

The wind howled, stirring the banners of the Franks Empire, forming a forest of spears and flags.

Every soldier in the capital stood ready, determined to defend their land and never allow evil to run rampant here.

Margaret slightly raised her head, looking beyond the city walls. Thick, rolling black smoke surged toward them from all directions, as if concealing demons within.

"...So it’s finally here."

Outside the capital, the black smoke pressed closer, completely surrounding the isolated imperial city.

The guards on the walls could hear the ear-piercing wails and howls, like calls from the depths of hell.

Many soldiers unconsciously began to tremble, their faces pale with fear, their grip on their weapons faltering.

The black smoke slowly dispersed, revealing the skin-and-bones Beelzebub emerging from within. He seemed harmless at first glance, but no one dared underestimate this ruler of the demon race.

Beelzebub raised his head, looking at the heavily fortified capital before him, and couldn’t help but twist his mouth into a contemptuous smirk.

"Three days have passed, and you still haven’t handed over my sister?"

"Fine. Since you’re so unafraid of death, then prepare to meet it."

"Old or young, I won’t spare a single one."

"If I slaughter everyone in the capital, I’ll find my precious sister eventually."

"Then—"

"Begin."

title: Chapter 18 — Gluttonous Quirk
content:
Chapter 18 — Gluttonous Quirk

Volume 17 · Chapter 18

The guards on the city walls, upon seeing Beelzebub suddenly appear, were filled with deep terror, their faces turning pale.

Fortunately, everyone had mentally prepared themselves and wasn’t instantly scared out of their wits by the Gluttony Demon Lord.

At a command, the guards on the city walls set up bows and fired arrows, while the mages raised their staffs, launching scorching fireballs.

A dense volley of arrows and a barrage of fireballs rained down from the sky!

Such a concentrated assault would turn an ordinary person into a porcupine—there’d be no way to dodge!

Yet this pathetic attack seemed to have no effect on the king of the demon race?

"Pathetic."

Beelzebub casually muttered the two words. Then, raising his palm toward the distant royal capital, he clenched his fist—suddenly, a terrifying shockwave erupted!

The rain of arrows and fireballs was scattered by the shockwave. Even the sturdy city walls of the imperial capital were instantly blasted apart!

The soldiers on the walls screamed as they died—some were turned to pulp by the shockwave, others buried under the rubble!

The once-impenetrable defense was now torn open by Beelzebub’s single strike, leaving the royal capital completely exposed.

The shockwave showed no sign of stopping after destroying the east gate. With a crackling sound like thunder, it tore through the earth, surging forward with unstoppable force, heading straight for the magnificent royal palace!

The elderly king, already gravely ill, had been put to sleep by Mades’ magic and knew nothing of the catastrophe unfolding in his empire.

The royal capital was filled with prepared troops, but Beelzebub’s devastating shockwave caught them completely off guard, throwing their initial formations into chaos. Many began to panic.

Countless soldiers died, and a towering column of dust rose nearly a hundred meters into the sky, shrouding the entire royal capital in a storm of sand and debris.

From her vantage point on the high platform, Margaret’s face turned ashen. She couldn’t help but feel a surge of fear as she watched the shockwave about to destroy the royal palace—a disaster in the making.

This demon’s power was unstoppable—was he going to destroy the palace right from the start?!

Her father was still inside! If he was caught in this, it would be a huge problem!

Margaret didn’t dare think further. She was extremely anxious, but there was nothing she could do. Blaize wasn’t by her side—he had gone to prepare to confront the Gluttony Demon Lord.

Whether intentionally or not, Beelzebub had torn open the city gates and immediately targeted the royal palace, the symbolic seat of power, throwing the enemy’s carefully laid plans into disarray!

At the critical moment, the short-haired, tomboyish Saint Joan descended from the sky. Clad in silver armor and holding a wrapped, mysterious object, she stood before the royal palace, as if ready to confront Beelzebub’s force head-on!

Joan unwrapped the black cloth covering the Crimson Demon Queen, revealing the bizarre pseudo-divine artifact, the long spear. She pointed it at the oncoming shockwave—

"Hah!"

With a shout, the Crimson Demon Queen in Joan’s hands blazed with radiant light, as if excited by the demonic presence, humming with a deep resonance.

Beelzebub’s devastating strike was instantly nullified by the spear’s radiance, completely averting the crisis of the palace’s destruction!

Standing at the center of the battlefield, Joan wielded the holy spear, battling the Demon Lord like a goddess of war, filling everyone present with immense confidence and inspiration.

Many knights even cheered, some shouting Joan’s name—anyone who didn’t know better might think they had already won!

The shockwave left a horrifying trench in the earth, the path behind it a scene of utter devastation, as if trampled by a monster.

Though the destructive power of the attack was staggering, this was merely the force Beelzebub had unleashed with a flick of his hand—not his true strength. The real terror was yet to come!

Margaret on the high platform let out a sigh of relief, her suspended heart finally settling. She had feared her father might have perished in that disaster.

She couldn’t help but glance curiously at the distant, stern-faced Joan, especially the strange crimson spear in her hands...

What was that weapon? Why did it give off such an eerie feeling? Could it be a secret weapon the Holy Church had developed specifically to counter demons?

Margaret was puzzled, but judging by the spear’s color and its earlier performance, it was clearly no ordinary weapon—not even a rare one could compare. It had to be some kind of divine artifact!

With Joan blocking the Gluttony Demon Lord’s attack, the knights in the royal capital were filled with renewed morale!

As the dust slowly settled, Beelzebub stepped over the corpses of imperial soldiers, leisurely walking into the royal capital from outside the walls.

The way he moved with such ease was as if he were mocking all of humanity, treating the human empire’s capital as his own territory.

Beelzebub slowly lifted his head and saw the royal palace standing unscathed. He was slightly surprised inside.

"Hmm? They actually blocked my attack... Even though they’re just a bunch of livestock, they’re not entirely useless..."

"Shut up, you vile fiend! Let me take you on!"

A sudden curse rang out. Blaize, who had been waiting in ambush for a long time, leapt from the shadows, landing on Beelzebub’s head to launch a surprise attack!

Blaize had been lying in wait for the perfect moment—when the Gluttony Demon Lord had just entered the royal capital.

If he could land a heavy blow on the Demon Lord, it would be a huge gain!

Blaize gripped his massive sword, his entire body burning with golden Saint-tier aura, and swung down with the force of a mountain-cleaving strike!

"Where did this rat come from?" Beelzebub indifferently lifted his eyelids and caught the blade of the massive sword barehanded.

Blaize froze. No matter how hard he pushed, he couldn’t budge the Gluttony Demon Lord’s single hand. The power gap was simply too vast!

Looking at Blaize’s grimacing, red-faced expression, it was clear he was exerting every last ounce of strength—yet it was completely useless.

"Human, are you in such a hurry to die? Just scram to the side and wait your turn. There’s no need to rush, is there?" Beelzebub said in a playful tone, tightening his grip slightly.

To his horror, Blaize saw his massive sword cracking under Beelzebub’s grip. Fine fissures spread like a spiderweb across the blade!

In a panic, Blaize quickly retreated, staring at the weapon that had accompanied him for years. The sword already bore the clear imprint of Beelzebub’s hand.

This sword was forged from Black Mountain copper—hard as rock—and had never been in danger of breaking before. Yet it couldn’t withstand the Demon Lord’s physical strength!

Blaize was shocked. The skin-and-bones figure before him possessed an unimaginable strength. Were all Seven Demon Lords monsters like this?!

At that moment, Blaize began to understand why the Holy Church was so determined to oppose the demon race. Demons wielded such overwhelming power—they were an eternal source of instability, capable of plunging the world into crisis.

It made sense that the Holy Church had spent so much time and effort trying to eradicate the demon race, only to fail. After all, the Demon Lords were just too strong.

Still, Blaize suppressed his fear. His Saint-tier aura blazed as he prepared to continue his desperate struggle against the Gluttony Demon Lord, if only to buy time for his comrades!

"Now do you understand the gap between us? Then behave and wash your neck while you wait..." Beelzebub lowered his head, examining his nails with cold indifference.

"Though I do have a peculiar habit..."

"And that is, the best things must be saved for last."

"So there’s no need to rush. Everyone will have the honor of being consumed by me... one by one."

title: Chapter 19 — Knight's Defeat
content:
Chapter 19 — Knight's Defeat

Volume 17 · Chapter 19

"Hmph! Stop talking nonsense. If you want to run amok in the royal capital, step over my corpse first!"

Blaze roared, charging forward despite Beelzebub's pressure, having long since thrown his life to the wind.

Blaze wielded his heavy sword at breakneck speed, raising wave after wave of torrential force, charging forward without hesitation.

Blaze's sword techniques had no form or discipline; they existed solely to chop enemies into paste.

With such a heavy weapon, Blaze wielded it like a toy, flipping it up and down, transforming into a human meat grinder in an instant.

"Hehehe, you're just like a clown. Your strength is only fit to contend with my subordinates. Fighting me? You're not even close."

Beelzebub laughed coldly. Despite his skinny, bony frame, Blaze's speed was extraordinary—utterly unfathomable!

To hit the Gluttony Demon Lord and deal him a fatal blow? Easier said than done!

Beelzebub mocked Blaze; this man hailed as France's strongest warrior was no different from a novice who had just learned to swing a sword.

Facing Blaze's torrential onslaught, Beelzebub dodged effortlessly—the enemy couldn't even touch him!

Yet not far away, Robert had been lying in wait for a long time, watching the arrogant Beelzebub from the shadows.

According to the original plan, Blaze hadn't expected to defeat the Gluttony Demon Lord; his task was merely to tie up the enemy and attract the demon lord's attention.

The real killing blow lay with Robert. As soon as Beelzebub faltered, he would strike like a leopard, delivering a fatal attack!

Now Blaze's desperate, death-defying struggle was precisely to create that opportunity for Robert.

With Beelzebub's full attention locked on Blaze, the hidden Robert realized the chance had come. He had to attempt to subdue the demon lord in one move!

Now Robert dared not underestimate Beelzebub anymore. The initial devastating attack had shaken him profoundly; he had to take the Gluttony seriously.

Watching Blaze and Beelzebub fight fiercely, Robert's eyes changed. Suddenly he burst out from the shadows.

He summoned all his combat qi, concentrating it into one finger, letting his fingertip contain nearly terrifying destructive force!

All his power focused on a single point. If it struck the enemy successfully, it would be nearly impossible to withstand such devastating force—it would pierce straight through!

Robert's mastery of combat qi techniques was no bluff. Even though Beelzebub was powerful, against such concentrated force, he couldn't remain unharmed!

"Die, demon!"

Robert roared, surging forward at incredible speed behind Beelzebub. His finger, brimming with piercing power, stabbed straight toward the demon lord's heart.

He had calculated well in his mind, intending to pierce straight through Beelzebub's back and hit his heart.

Robert held his breath, gritted his teeth, and stared at the undefended demon lord, striking Beelzebub with all his might!

Beelzebub's expression changed to shock, freezing in place, seemingly unprepared for another enemy to suddenly emerge from the shadows.

"Success?" Blaze froze, seeing Beelzebub stop moving, thinking their plan had worked!

"Hah! What a demon lord, he's just—" Robert was about to say "not worth a single thought," but when he looked up, his eyes widened in disbelief, "Uh—"

Robert's finger, carrying all his power, tore through Beelzebub's clothes and caused some damage.

But the damage was negligible—merely causing Beelzebub's flesh to turn slightly red and swollen, completely ignorable!

Beelzebub slowly turned his head, gazing at the dead-eyed Robert. Being touched by livestock made him feel nauseated and furious. "You idiot, you're playing with fire."

Robert's face turned pale, cold sweat streaming down his forehead. This was his proudest attack—enemies before could never resist it, torn apart by the concentrated combat qi blade, yet against the Gluttony Demon Lord, the damage was negligible!

Faced with this unbelievable situation, Robert felt a chill in his heart, even beginning to doubt himself. Beelzebub's power far exceeded his imagination!

"...Impossible!"

In the distance, Blaze was stunned. In his impression, Robert's martial arts were invincible, his control over combat qi unrivaled.

Until now, Blaze had never seen anything that could withstand Robert's full-powered attack unscathed. They had severely underestimated Beelzebub's strength.

"You insect, die! Hurting my body, your life cannot repay it!" Beelzebub, enraged, stabbed his hand into Robert's chest, ripping out his heart alive!

"Robert!!!" Blaze shouted loudly, running toward his comrade whose eyes had lost their focus.

Robert staggered back two steps, a huge hole in his chest gushing blood wildly!

He never expected to die here. The demon lord's power—his entire life's effort couldn't move it a fraction!

Robert's face was ashen. Without his heart, death was certain. He fell straight to the ground, completely lifeless.

"No!" Blaze picked up the dead Robert. Losing a teammate so suddenly was hard for him to accept.

Beelzebub pinched Robert's heart with two fingers, swallowed it in one gulp, then licked his lips. "Hmm, truly delicious."

Blaze's eyes were bloodshot. Inside him, a volcano surged toward the sky; he wanted to grind Beelzebub to dust and scatter him to the winds!

To Blaze, Robert was his comrade-in-arms. Among the three knights, only Robert shared his views. Now he had been murdered by the evil demon lord!

"Oh? Good eyes. Are you hating me?" Beelzebub's words corroded Blaze, his tone full of amusement. He had no interest in the emotions of humble humans. "Humans are so fragile. Why is it your era now, this livestock? I'm a bit confused. I heard anger makes you stronger—is that true?"

"Demon lord! I'll take you with me!"

Blaze stood up holding his heavy sword, caked in blood and tears. His golden combat qi surged wildly. With only the thought of killing Beelzebub left, his mind had completely lost its ability to think.

In his rage, Blaze unleashed his Saint-tier ultimate technique—Mountain-Splitting Cross Slash!

This technique was the strongest move Blaze could use. As the name implied, it could destroy everything in its path; even the earth would tremble.

Blaze swung his great sword, releasing all his combat qi in a massive golden cross slash, attacking Beelzebub with a mountain-crumbling, earth-shaking momentum!

"Aaaaaaaaaaaaaah!!!"

"Oh? With your upper Saint-tier strength, using such a technique is already pretty good... Beelzebub moved, evading the Mountain-Splitting Cross Slash in a bizarre manner, appearing before Blaze and piercing through his abdomen.

"Loss of reason makes you like a mad dog. You're just a brute."

"Compared to before, you've become easier to deal with. Hehehe..."

title: Chapter 20 — Irritable Flames (Two More Episodes to Follow)
content:
Chapter 20 — Irritable Flames (Two More Episodes to Follow)

Volume 17 · Chapter 20

Blaze’s stomach was pierced through, his body collapsing weakly to the ground as his life force vanished into silence.

Besideb had ruthlessly carved a gaping wound into the knight’s chest, blood trickling slowly from the gap.

Blaze’s consciousness faded, his strength utterly drained, plunging him into a deep unconsciousness.

The three knights of France had already lost two men in a single encounter—Besideb’s slaughter was far from ordinary. If this kept up, the Demon Lord would easily breach the capital with just one person.

Margaret stood on the high platform, watching everything unfold. Blaze was dying, and Robert had suffered even worse—his heart had been torn out and eaten by the Gluttonous Demon Lord.

The situation was dire. Two knights lost before the fight even began meant a severe drop in combat power. Clearly, everyone had underestimated the Demon Lord’s strength—it was beyond mortal comprehension.

“Three days of preparation, and we’re facing opponents like this? This is... ridiculous.”

Besideb kicked the barely breathing Blaze aside, his gaze fixed on the distant royal palace.

If he wanted to destroy the entire city, the royal palace—symbol of supreme authority—was the obvious target. This would crush human willpower, making them docile, ready-to-be-slaughter sheep.

Besideb made up his mind and strode toward the grand imperial palace. But after only a few steps, he felt a scorching breath behind him.

“Hmm? No wonder the Demon Lord calls himself that—he’s already taken down two of them so effortlessly. I’m actually a little impressed.” Batiloka stood behind Besideb, muttering with interest.

Besideb turned, eyeing Batiloka, who was dressed in prison stripes. He raised an eyebrow. “Who are you?”

“I? Just a freshly escaped convict looking for excitement.” Batiloka shrugged, showing no fear at all in the face of such a brutal demon.

“An escaped convict? Interesting.” Besideb glanced at Blaze and Robert lying on the ground, his voice flat. “Are you with them?”

“No, do you really think a murderer like me would side with noble knights?” Batiloka retorted.

“So you’re not here to fight me? But I won’t spare a single human in the capital—even the most wicked criminals.” Besideb shook his head.

“How convenient. I also won’t let you go. After all, it’s rare to meet someone this strong—if I don’t kill you now, I’ll always regret it.” Batiloka’s expression brightened, as if he’d found his prey.

Seeing Blaze and Robert defeated, this madman seemed to see hope. He’d finally found a worthy opponent—if he didn’t challenge him now, he’d never get another chance.

“Hmph! I thought you were a sensible person, but you’re just a reckless lunatic.” Besideb turned slowly, deciding to eliminate this annoying nuisance first.

“Not necessarily. You’ll know if I’m reckless or not after I hit you. What if *you’re* the one lying on the ground, unknown to you, in front of me?” Batiloka said with interest.

Besideb didn’t respond, but his frustration grew. He found the convict’s mouth repulsive.

On the high platform, Margaret saw Batiloka and was surprised. She had assumed he wouldn’t appear, but here he was, showing up at the critical moment.

Though Batiloka was one of the Three Knights, he wasn’t Margaret’s subordinate, so she wasn’t very familiar with him. She only knew he was the most powerful but also the most unruly among them—disobedient, impossible to control.

Three years ago, after Batiloka murdered the Duke’s son and was imprisoned in the Boiya Prison, he faded from public view. Now, he was standing up for the Empire he had once despised—it was truly unexpected!

Margaret had heard rumors about Batiloka. From birth, he possessed strength far beyond ordinary humans, once causing a major stir and chaos within the Empire.

Later, under the Empire’s surveillance, he was raised as an outcast, studied like an experiment. From childhood, he was trained as a weapon.

Even the collar around his neck was a specially designed product—otherwise, he couldn’t have controlled his explosive inner power, threatening the Empire’s safety.

Just as Batiloka’s excitement peaked, fully armored knights surrounded Besideb, ready to help in the crusade against the demon.

But Batiloka’s expression suddenly darkened. He coldly snapped, “All of you, get out of here. Who gave you permission to interfere?”

A knight commander awkwardly replied, “Sir Batiloka, we came to help you.”

Besideb looked at the knights surrounding him, unable to hold back a mocking laugh. These pawns would all die soon.

“No need. Don’t get in my way.”

Batiloka snapped his fingers, and flames suddenly erupted from thin air, engulfing the knights who tried to help. Many didn’t even have time to react before they were consumed, their screams filling the air.

“Hmph!” Margaret furrowed her brows, wondering what this madman was thinking—didn’t he care about friend or foe?

Besideb glanced around at the knights struggling in the flames, sighing. “If you were a demon, I’d actually admire someone like you.”

“Hmph!” Batiloka scoffed, his body ablaze as he charged toward Besideb, slamming a heavy punch into his stomach.

“Hah!” Besideb’s eyes widened slightly, surprised. “Saint-tier peak? Not bad—better than those two idiots. But still—”

“Hah!”

Before Besideb could finish, Batiloka struck again. Scorching flames erupted from his body, roaring upward as his fists unleashed a combined blast of martial energy and magic.

The inferno and heat wave crashed into Besideb’s face, sending him flying backward.

“Ugh!” Besideb was stunned, realizing he had underestimated this man. He crashed to the ground.

Batiloka’s flames created an immense shockwave, consuming everything around them like a meteor striking the city center.

Margaret’s eyes widened in shock. From her high platform, she witnessed everything—this was impossible.

Batiloka alone had knocked down the Gluttonous Demon Lord!

The gap between the Three Knights’ strength had never been this vast.

title: Chapter 21 — Flame Demon
content:
Chapter 21 — Flame Demon

Volume 17 · Chapter 21

Bartiloka's hands burned with flames, hissing and emitting black smoke, his arms covered in crimson patterns like lava spreading across the earth.
Beshebu slowly rose from the ground, using his hand to straighten his twisted neck, his expressionless gaze fixed on Bartiloka.
“Pretty strong, huh—I really underestimated you. Knocking me down is enough for you to brag about for a lifetime....”
“This is just a greeting—I only used a third of my strength. Don’t collapse before I go all out.” Bartiloka sneered.
“If you can, go all out—my time is precious, mutual probing is pointless.” Beshebu spread his hands, seemingly provoking.
“Hah, as you wish, I couldn’t wait any longer.” Bartiloka grinned wickedly, crushing the collar around his neck to pieces.
This empire‑made collar was specially designed to limit Bartiloka’s power; now that it’s been undone, he’s likely to become even more reckless.
Towering flames surged forth, lighting the originally gloomy, oppressive sky.
The flames writhed like a monster, tearing through the heavy black clouds.
Bartiloka was completely engulfed in the raging fire, no human shape visible anymore.
The air grew scorching, temperature skyrocketing to an unbelievable degree, making the whole royal capital feel like a furnace.
Margaret up high couldn’t help but tense, the sky‑high flames reflecting on her face as she instinctively clenched her fists.
Margaret never expected Bartiloka to suddenly go berserk—this was the rhythm of burning both enemy and royal capital to ashes.
Bartiloka already struggled to control his power; now falling into a frenzy, he might have lost all reason.
Only then did one see Bartiloka at the city’s center utterly consumed by flames, yet immediately from that spot rose a colossal Wrath Flame Demon!
Once human, Bartiloka suddenly transformed into a flame‑spewing demon, terrifying everyone present.
This flame demon was massive—its height twice the city walls, its fangs and claws seeming able to touch the rolling clouds on the horizon.
As for its appearance? Though somewhat demon‑like, its body was entirely a polymer of molten lava and fire.
“So that’s it—you’re just a possessed puppet; the real power lies in this guy....” Beshebu, facing the scorching firelight, narrowed his eyes and muttered to himself, “A pure elemental conglomerate, possessing a certain divinity and wisdom as a magical beast—I never imagined I’d encounter such a thing after leaving the Demon Lord’s Palace....”
It seemed Beshebu was well‑versed; at a glance he recognized the flame demon’s nature—though an elemental conglomerate, it belonged to the magical beast category.
This was very similar to the lake fairies of the British Empire; the flame demon, too, was an elemental conglomerate with its own wisdom and divinity.
Though both are the same kind of existence, the lake fairy represents the water element while the flame demon represents fire, so there are still differences.
Since the beginning of creation, four ages have passed; such a long span has given birth to countless novel species.
Wisdom‑ and divinity‑endowed elemental conglomerates are merely one of them.
They possess the purest power, able to freely command the elements, their destructive force astonishing, their magic never depleted.
Those like the lake fairy that can form contracts with humans are exceedingly rare; most are like the flame demon, refusing any control—Bartiloka is merely its host.
Beshebu calmly watched the raging flame demon’s roar, his strength having surged directly to the Ancestral Realm after Bartiloka broke the seal, faintly residing in a higher tier.

This monster is no weaker than the divine tree spirit Merlin encountered in the forest, and it seems to have an even greater aura of dread, making it a terrifying presence.
No wonder Bartiloka is monitored as a dangerous weapon; a slight loss of control could put the royal capital in danger, making him an extremely unstable factor.
The overwhelming aura accompanied by waves of scorching heat made it hard to breathe; Jeanne d'Arc, accompanied by two heresy inquisitors, rushed over, only to be stunned by the sight before her—
9.... What the hell is that? Is the empire secretly hiding something like this?!
The enraged flame demon gnashed and clawed, burning everything, while Beshebu showed no expression and no reaction, making it hard to tell who was the real demon at this point.
The flame demon lowered its molten rock body, gazing at the tiny Beshebu, slightly opening its mouth to emit a terrifying heat wave that scorched the surrounding rocks to a glowing red.
“Huh, what? You wanna fight me?” Beshebu jeered.
The flame demon roared, raised its massive fist, and slammed it down, blasting Beshebu underground for a close encounter with the earth.
Beshebu was already nothing but skin and bones, and being slapped by the flame demon like a mosquito made one wonder if he could even withstand it.
The flame demon grabbed Beshebu from the ground, swung him around twice, and hurled him away with full force, showing no intention of letting him go easily.
With a whoosh, Beshebu couldn't control his stop, smashing through numerous pillars and walls along the way, even blasting a hole through the Imperial Council and causing it to collapse.
“Ugh!” Jeanne d'Arc saw this, her mind went blank, feeling utterly useless, and the flame demon's ferocity made her dare not approach at all.
Beshebu, looking somewhat disheveled, pushed himself up from the ground, shouting, “Damn it, don’t get in—uh!”
Just as Beshebu, at a disadvantage, had climbed to his feet, he saw himself engulfed in a huge shadow.
Looking up, Beshebu saw the flame demon's molten lava foot stomping down fiercely, once again driving him deep into the ground.
As the flame demon's stomp landed, the entire royal capital's surface rolled like waves, kicking up a mighty gust that flattened all structures within a hundred‑meter radius.
This monster showed no restraint, pressing the attack to try to kill Beshebu outright, raising its massive fists and beginning to pummel the Gem Demon Lord lying on the ground.
Oh oh oh oh oh oh oh oh!
Don’t be fooled by the flame demon’s huge size—its punch speed is relentless, like a machine gun, bang bang bang striking Beshebu in rapid succession.
The earth kept trembling, the wind kept howling, and everyone was

title: Chapter 22 — Holy Lance
content:
Chapter 22 — Holy Lance

Volume 17 · Chapter 22

The demon lord let out a pained wail, a large hole torn in his chest by Besiege’s attack, his massive body disintegrating.

Soon, the lava body composed of fire element vanished without a trace, leaving only a devastated area around them.

“Haa~” Besiege blew on his fingers, having sustained some minor injuries but nothing serious, and said meaningfully, “So this is the Empire’s strongest trump card? It seems humans are no more than this. If it weren’t for needing to guard the Demon Lord Palace, it wouldn’t be impossible to let the world regress to the age of demons.”

Margaret, in the distance, was a little dazed. Unable to deal with Besiege at all, growing stronger the more they fought? What kind of battle was this where absorbing attacks to strengthen oneself was possible?

Besiege’s ability actually had limitations. Although he could absorb all attacks to enhance his power, his body’s capacity had its limits. He didn’t have the healing ability of a vampire.

If Besiege’s body couldn’t withstand the attacks—increasing his power would be pointless.

Joan of Arc felt fear rising in her heart. If such a terrifying demon lord could fall, was it even necessary for her to fight? It seemed there really wasn’t a need!

However, Joan of Arc held a pseudo-artifact spear in her hand. O’Brien had once used it to defeat a Demon Lord. To show cowardice now would be a disgrace to her predecessors?

And the Crimson Succubus was originally a weapon to deal with demons. It wouldn’t hurt to try—treat a dead horse like a live one and give it a shot!

Joan of Arc focused her gaze. She was a Hero candidate, always preparing to conquer demons.

“Please lend me your strength!”

“op SF light novel”

Joan of Arc held the crimson spear horizontally across her chest, issuing an order to her two Inquisitor companions.

“Good, we are willing to sacrifice our lives to eliminate the demon race!”

The two male Inquisitors answered in unison, like brainwashed individuals, completely disregarding life and death.

For these devotees of the Goddess, death was merely a return to her side—nothing to fear.

The Crimson Succubus emitted waves of eerie red light, enveloping the two Inquisitors. Immediately, their bodies began to dissolve and vanish without a trace!

Accompanied by agonizing screams of exhaustion and pain, Joan of Arc gritted her teeth, enduring the immense psychological pressure and continuing the ritual.

Although the two companions had volunteered, Joan of Arc still felt a sense of murder, a huge wave of guilt rising in her heart.

But thinking that this was to eliminate the Gluttony Demon Lord, Joan of Arc’s heart felt slightly more at ease. To drive out evil, she was also willing to sacrifice her life.

The two Inquisitors weren’t Saint-tier powerhouses—they were high-tier—but the short-term enhancement to Joan of Arc was obvious.

The red light dissipated, the ritual ended, and the two companions had been sacrificed.

Joan of Arc slowly opened her eyes, her fighting spirit no longer a vibrant color, but a strange crimson.

She had leaped from Saint-tier to the early-stage of the Zong Realm. Although this enhancement effect was only temporary, it was enough.

Joan of Arc knew her strength was no match for the previous demon lord, hoping this pseudo-artifact spear would bring her a surprise.

“I won’t let your sacrifices be in vain…”

Joan of Arc finished speaking and quickly approached Besiege in the center of the fire pit, prepared to fight to the death.

Besiege was now completely unlike a frail, bony figure. Instead, he was very robust, his muscles clearly defined. It seemed the demon lord’s beating had greatly strengthened him.

“Demon, die!” Joan of Arc shouted, unwilling to waste time due to the limited enhancement time, launching an attack, the crimson spear thrust straight at Besiege.

“Tsk! You troublesome woman again…” Besiege rolled his eyes impatiently, dodging to the side.

In the past, Joan of Arc would definitely have missed Besiege, but with her enhanced strength and years of honed skill, she managed to land the blow, the edge of the spear grazing the demon.

Besiege lowered his head to look at the red line slashed across his chest, which didn’t seem to be a serious injury?

The next second, however, the small wound on his chest expanded tenfold, spurting blood—clearly showing the crimson flesh!

Besiege froze, his expression puzzled. It was just a small wound, inexplicably becoming a severe injury. If it had been pierced deeper, it might have threatened his safety.

Joan of Arc stabilized her form, seeing Besiege injured, her confidence in the pseudo-artifact growing. It could inflict serious damage on demons. Although her strength was inferior to the Gluttony Demon Lord, she still had a chance with the pseudo-artifact!牡小“吮

Besiege instinctively looked at the weapon in Joan of Arc’s hand, becoming slightly wary. “Although your strength isn’t much, that spear looks pretty good?”

“This spear can kill Lucifer II, and it can kill you too!” Joan of Arc scolded, gripping the spear tightly.

“A weapon that killed Lucifer II? Oh~” Besiege feigned enlightenment, understanding the situation. “So it’s the Spear of the Hero, a famous weapon indeed. He is one of the few men feared by the demon race, worthy of respect. Do you want to learn from the Spear Hero, kill the Demon Lord and become famous?”

“Hmph! So what?” Joan of Arc’s gaze was stern, not denying it.

“Haha, laughable. Unfortunately, you can’t do it. Whether a weapon can exert its full power depends entirely on the user’s strength. If the Spear Hero were standing before me, I might take it seriously. You? You’re just like a clown performing tricks.” Besiege waved his fingers dismissively, genuinely looking down on the tomboy.

“Haa!” Joan of Arc’s crimson fighting spirit surged, the spear in her hand seeming to come alive, writhing like a dragon emerging from the sea, launching frequent attacks at Besiege.

Besiege had already begun to pay attention to the holy spear, not easily letting Joan of Arc succeed. Although he could absorb attacks to enhance his power, taking risks wasn’t worth it.

SE4 novel

Joan of Arc, relying on her demon-suppressing pseudo-artifact, launched frequent attacks, seemingly with the resolve to die alongside the Gluttony Lord.

The two powers collided violently. With the pseudo-artifact’s boost, Joan of Arc was actually fighting Besiege on equal footing?!

In a corner of the royal capital, a very safe place used for command.

Mades lowered his telescope, calling his subordinate, Ram, over, his expression slightly disappointed.

“Sir?” Ram quickly walked over.

“Issue the order, fire the cannons directly.” Mades said decisively.

“But Saint Joan of Arc is fighting fiercely with the Gluttony Demon Lord. Using the legendary magic cannons might not be wise?” Ram hesitated.

“Fighting fiercely? Nonsense, they can’t win. Joan of Arc is too weak, unable to unleash the power of that spear. The Gluttony Demon Lord can completely crush her with brute force.” Mades thought for a moment, speaking coldly—

“Now that these two are fighting so fiercely, isn’t this the perfect opportunity to fire?”

“Not only can we severely injure the Gluttony Demon Lord and drive him away, but we can also eliminate the French Saint Joan of Arc, weakening the Holy Church. Don’t forget, the Holy Church is also our blood race’s enemy.”

“Fire at these two directly. I don’t believe that under the power of the legendary magic cannons, this arrogant demon can remain so composed…”

title: Chapter 23 — Legendary Magic Cannon
content:
Chapter 23 — Legendary Magic Cannon

Volume 17 · Chapter 23

Barbatos drove the wounded Jeanne away, realizing that this fake divine artifact was indeed troublesome—once touched, it caused serious injuries.

Now Barbatos understood why Lucifer II had been defeated. The despicable Holy Church constantly researched weapons specifically designed against demons, making up for the gap in their strength.

Although Barbatos didn't think Jeanne was particularly powerful, she kept pestering him like a fly, making him increasingly irritated.

Jeanne steadied herself, her strange crimson aura surging and overflowing, not giving Barbatos any chance to breathe as she pressed her attack.

Suddenly, Jeanne's momentum surged, wielding her holy spear and thrusting it at Barbatos. A powerful piercing red light shot out!

Barbatos furrowed his brow and swung his hand to scatter Jeanne's attack, but he still suffered the severe injury effect from the crimson temptress—his entire arm was covered in wounds.

"Tch! The despicable Holy Church, resorting to cheap tricks!"

Jeanne completely ignored Barbatos's complaints. As long as she could kill a demon, any method was fine. Seeing the Gluttony Demon Lord being suppressed, her confidence gradually grew.

Margaret noticed Barbatos was at a disadvantage and couldn't help but think: Indeed, when dealing with demons, the Holy Church people are more professional. Ordinary humans like us are completely helpless.

Just as Margaret was lamenting, the earth beneath the castle keep trembled again, and a massive magic cannon slowly rose from underground—twelve of them.

This was the weapon that France had swept everything before it—the Legendary Magic Cannon, which no one had ever survived its tremendous power!

The enormous cannon barrels shot up into the sky, so thick that twenty people would need to surround them to embrace. Ancient scriptures were carved on them, looking like twelve pillars holding up the sky, turning the entire castle keep into an altar.

No way? Firing before the battle was decided?

What on earth is Mads thinking? Trying to kill both of them at once?

Margaret's eyes widened in shock, not expecting Mads to make such a decision, treating the Holy Church people as mere discards.

As the ancient scriptures on the twelve Legendary Magic Cannons began to glow, the muzzle of each cannon started brewing unparalleled power. The magical elements in the sky and earth were instantly drained dry.

Margaret wanted to stop it but was too late. She could only watch helplessly as the massive beam of light shot up into the sky. The Legendary Magic Cannon activated directly, with no warning whatsoever!

On the other side, Jeanne launched another attack, her holy spear turning into a series of illusions, all rushing to tear apart Barbatos!

The density of the holy spear shadows was like raindrops, real and illusory, making it hard to discern which was the actual attack.

Jeanne wielded her long spear, drawing out brilliant crimson light and shadow. Her skillful spear technique left onlookers gaping in amazement.

Barbatos didn't want to struggle with Jeanne, so he opened his mouth and spat out a swarm of man-eating flies that surrounded and broke up her attack.

The buzzing swarm of flies fearlessly bit Jeanne, forcing her to retreat.

Surrounded by the man-eating flies, Jeanne was unwilling to give up. She swung her holy spear to slash at the annoying insects, but there were too many of them—she couldn't shake them off no matter what.

"Hmph!" Barbatos sneered, extending his finger toward the chaotic Jeanne, preparing to blast this annoying Holy Church traitor from afar.

But with a rumbling boom, like lightning flashing across the sky, it made everyone feel ominous.

Barbatos instinctively lifted his head, sensing a tremendous energy gathering above. He couldn't underestimate it!

The magical elements in the sky and earth were all drained dry. Something extremely powerful was about to arrive, and the air grew tense.

After the twelve Legendary Magic Cannons fired, the concentrated ancient power and light streams suddenly gathered above Barbatos, gradually forming a massive ball.
