The originally dark and oppressive sky was illuminated by this light ball, turning everything into a sea of white, like the last remaining troops on the day of doomsday!

"What... the hell?" Barbatos furrowed his brow, his sixth sense issuing a warning—this thing was not to be trifled with!

Suddenly, the light ball changed, shrinking to half its size. In a flash of lightning, a beam of destructive light descended from the sky and struck Barbatos directly!

This was the attack of the twelve Legendary Magic Cannons. Although the method was strange, it was very hard to evade, as the range was enormous—half the castle keep was engulfed within it!

The magic cannon beam, infused with ancient power, produced a tremendous thunderous sound that shook the heavens and earth, like the wrath of gods, ready to punish everyone.

Barbatos's eyes widened, and before he could react, he was swallowed by the pale light, unable to determine life or death.

Jeanne was even worse off, struck directly by the unstoppable Legendary Magic Cannon shockwave, coughing up blood as she was blown far away.

Fortunately, the holy spear of the crimson temptress flashed, suddenly forming a protective barrier that wrapped around Jeanne. Otherwise, she might have been caught in the Legendary Magic Cannon's power and shattered into pieces right then.

As a fake divine artifact, the crimson temptress's function wasn't limited to just sacrificing and strengthening. It also had the ability to protect its wielder. Jeanne's strength was far inferior to the spear-wielding Hero O'Brien, unable to fully unleash the fake divine artifact's power.

Jeanne flew backward through the air, moving farther and farther from the center of the Legendary Magic Cannon's strike. She watched as the devastating light column destroyed everything in its path, even buildings seemed to be decomposed into dust and vanished, with the destruction spreading outward.

The Legendary Magic Cannon truly deserved to be the empire's strongest weapon. Its tremendous destructive power was only one aspect—most terrifying was the ancient civilization's power that decomposed everything it touched. Even rare defensive equipment would struggle against this overwhelming decomposition ability.

Jeanne felt dizzy and confused, her bones feeling as if they had all been broken. She wondered why they suddenly fired—wasn't this different from the plan? If the fake divine artifact wasn't protecting her, she would probably be dead already. This magic cannon was so powerful—under such tremendous destructive force, everything would be reduced to nothing. It seemed like everything was over. Even the Gluttony Demon Lord, no matter how strong, couldn't shake the ancient civilization!

The massive light column struck the ground, continuously spreading toward the edges, devastating the general area of the castle keep, flattening it into a plain.

The destructive shockwave swept across the entire castle keep, even the sturdy castle walls crumbling down, the earth constantly trembling.

This kind of attack that destroyed the enemy while causing massive self-damage was typical of Mads's style. After all, it wouldn't harm the vampire's interests.

Margaret, with her brows tightly knitted, had long since fallen from the high platform, kneeling on the ground, watching the Legendary Magic Cannon mercilessly bombard.

Surely the Gluttony Demon Lord would die this time? But we've paid such a heavy price...

Margaret worried, and when the light column faded and the magic cannon's power dissipated, a grotesque shadow appeared in the swirling sand...

...No way?

How could he survive such a fierce attack!

title: Chapter 24 — A Stopgap Measure
content:
Chapter 24 — A Stopgap Measure

Volume 17 · Chapter 24

The legendary magic cannon's aftermath faded. Once-prosperous capital city lay in ruins, nearly half destroyed by the bombardment, forming a horrifyingly massive crater.

Even the heavy clouds in the sky were torn open by the cannon's immense power, revealing the azure sky beneath.

Margaret's face was etched with disbelief. Watching the huge shadow emerge after the smoke cleared, even the empire's proud ancient weapon hadn't killed Beelzebub!

At that moment, Beelzebub stood motionless in the field, his form no longer human but undergoing an earth-shattering transformation—

His entire body turned jet black, massive demon horns symbolizing his noble status, his mouth stretched to his ears, teeth sharpened to points. Ancient scales covered his sturdy form, crawling in the scale gaps and breeding countless white flies that made one's scalp go numb. His lower half was even more repulsive—thin, fly-like legs, as if fly legs had been enlarged. Even his scarlet eyes resembled flies, occupying half his face entirely, composed of dense tiny particles. Behind him, huge semi-transparent cicada wings trembled, fully six pairs, their patterns clearly visible. This was the true form of the Gluttony Lord Beelzebub, called the "Fly King" by the world—no wonder, a monster seemingly spawned from rotting corpses.

Jeanne, severely wounded, supported herself with the Holy Lance and stood up, gazing at Beelzebub in the distance. The revolting sight made her nauseous. How could this be? Taking that world-destroying attack head-on and still not killing the thing! Were Demon Lords made of iron? If it were a human, it would have died a hundred times over! Jeanne widened her eyes in shock, feeling doomed—the empire's trump card spent, still unable to defeat the Gluttony Demon Lord. No one could stop him now.

Swarms of flies surrounded Beelzebub, fluttering about in apparent anxiety for their injured master. Having taken the direct hit from twelve legendary magic cannons, Beelzebub wasn't unscathed—he had indeed suffered considerable damage, though not fatal. It seemed Demon Lords had their limits too, not invincible. At the very least, destroying the capital alone would cost Beelzebub something.

Beelzebub's two fly-like eyes rolled around, examining his body where bone was visible through torn flesh, meat writhing. The swirling flies seemed to receive an order, all descending upon his wounds to heal their master, repairing the damaged body.

After a few seconds, the flesh flies scattered, and Beelzebub's wounds instantly healed, restored to peak condition. Beelzebub clenched his fists several times, feeling nothing wrong, slightly relieved. "Unexpectedly, as a Demon Lord, I've been forced to reveal my true form by you lot—livestock!" His voice was magnetic. Hearing this, the injured Jeanne felt a cold sweat drip from her forehead. Things looked grim. From far away, she already felt the Gluttony Demon Lord's oppressive pressure was several times stronger than before. This wasn't about whether she could win anymore, but the contempt and absolute suppression of a higher existence over inferior creatures!

"But to deal with you, I still need to reveal my demon true form—what shame!" Beelzebub's killing intent surged. He vibrated his twelve fly-wings behind him, emitting a deafening buzz and stirring up violent gusts. He darted upward, soaring to the sky above the capital, looking down at the pitiful survivors below. Raising one hand, he unleashed an unparalleled force fluctuation. A circular energy cannon resembling the sun appeared out of nowhere, its massive volume covering the entire capital! Everyone was shrouded in shadow. With such a vast bombardment area, escape was useless. This energy cannon combined the power of the twelve magic cannons with Beelzebub's own strength. If it dropped, the capital would be annihilated in an instant, erased from this world forever!

"An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth!" Jeanne's face was ashen, staring at the endless energy cannon, despair in her heart. Beelzebub had never shown his true power from the start—if he'd used such force earlier, what reason did they have to resist? Laughable... The wind was like knives, the fierce tornado lifting stones and debris toward the energy in the sky. What a spectacular sight of doom! Just as Beelzebub prepared to hurl the energy cannon down to destroy the entire capital, a voice called out to stop him—

"Wait!" Margaret, without warning, left the safe zone and walked through the violent gusts alone, approaching Beelzebub.

Her hair was disheveled, forcing her to shield her face with her arms to advance slowly. As the empire's heir, Margaret was certainly unwilling to see the capital destroyed. With no other options, she had to try stopping this.

"Hmm?" Beelzebub's eyes rolled, showing no intention of withdrawing the energy cannon, only sizing up this tiny human princess.

"Please wait! Don't destroy this place!" Margaret shouted hoarsely, her clothes torn by the fierce wind.

"Hmph, why should I listen to you?" Beelzebub was somewhat lazy to bother with this little ant.

"Don't you want to find your sister? I have a way!" Margaret's words struck right at Beelzebub's soft spot.

"You?" Beelzebub's interest was piqued. "Speak."

"Your sister might have been kidnapped by someone in the capital. If you want to save her, then bind me instead! I'm willing to trade my life for your sister!" Margaret shouted loudly. With no options left, she could only sacrifice herself to stall Beelzebub, or the capital would become dust today. "Destroying the capital is meaningless. Don't you want to save your sister? Killing everyone might mean you never find another clue!"

Beelzebub narrowed his eyes, still channeling the destructive attack, but his thoughts loosened. The human woman made sense—killing countless people without finding his sister would be for nothing.

"Who are you? How dare you stand equal to my sister?" Margaret removed her red cloak against the cold, her expression grave like a challenger facing a powerful foe. "I am the princess of France, the empire's sole heir to the throne. If you kidnap me, you control France's future!"

Beelzebub looked at Margaret, thinking the empire's sole heir—such weight made a suitable exchange for his sister. "Hmph, interesting!" Seeing the energy cannon about to destroy the capital dissipate, Margaret realized the Demon Lord truly cared about his sister; persuasion had worked. Beelzebub unleashed a demonic wind, lifting Margaret from the ground and clutching her throat.

"If I don't see my sister, you cunning human will die!" Margaret felt her breath growing difficult; even struggling couldn't free her from his grip. She had no confidence in her heart—using herself as hostage was merely a stopgap measure. What came next was completely uncertain.

Jeanne showed a helpless, existential expression, looking at her trembling hands—defeated! Completely defeated! Indeed, she was never worthy of being a Hero. Days later. Merlin and Alice had entered the imperial capital's territory and would soon reach the capital. The arrogant one and the overbearing Gluttony Demon Lord—what sparks would these two long-unseen Demon Lords create?

title: Chapter 25 — A Party of Three?
content:
Chapter 25 — A Party of Three?

Volume 17 · Chapter 25

Merlin and Alice were riding in a carriage, already very close to the royal capital. They should arrive before nightfall.

Their goal was to investigate Imperial Chancellor Mades. Judging from the letters exchanged between Camilla and Mades, their relationship was far from ordinary.

So Merlin and Alice felt something was off. This imperial chancellor likely had serious issues, and might even lead them to more clues about the blood clan.

Originally, their mission was to kill Dracula and lift the curse on the Austin family. But for now, they had no choice but to take this indirect approach, following the trail wherever it led.

Merlin drove the carriage and glanced at Alice beside him. She seemed distracted, her head lowered, lost in thought.

"Alice, what's wrong? Something on your mind?"

"Huh?" Alice lifted her head, looking around as if caught off guard. "No, what could I possibly be worried about?"

Merlin raised an eyebrow, pondered for a moment, and guessed most of it. "Is it about that little brat? Relax, Old Man Akaron will take good care of her."

"...I wasn't thinking about that..." Alice's face flushed red, and she turned her head away in embarrassment.

"Cut it out. It's written all over your face. You're not even her real mother, so why are you so concerned?" Merlin curled his lip, not quite understanding Alice's attachment to that little girl.

"I feel like it, and it's none of your business!" Alice huffed, looking defiant.

"Fine, fine, I’ll mind my own business." Merlin twisted his mouth and decided not to pry further.

Alice was surprised that Merlin, for once, didn’t argue back. In truth, she had been thinking about the little girl they had left behind. In the short time they spent together, she had grown quite fond of the child.

But with their mission weighing on them, they couldn’t bring her along for safety reasons. Alice felt an empty ache in her heart.

Could she adapt to living with Old Akaron? Would she eat enough? Would she go to bed on time? These questions kept popping into her mind.

Alice was still an unmarried woman, yet here she was, worrying like a mother. It was absurd.

"Ahem, Merlin... do you think we could adopt that child?"

After much hesitation, Alice asked tentatively, wanting to know Merlin's true feelings—whether he had any thoughts about adopting the baby.

But Merlin was struck as if by lightning. He stared at Alice in shock. "You... have you lost your mind?"

"W-What?" A cold sweat dripped down Alice's forehead as she felt a pang of anxiety.

"Do we even have the energy to raise a child? We're already exhausted, and you want to add a burden? That's just asking for trouble." Merlin frowned, clearly opposed to the idea.

"How can you call her a burden? That's so harsh! Don't you have any sympathy for that child?" Alice's expression turned angry.

"Miss, sympathy doesn't put food on the table. I only agreed to help her find her real parents, but I absolutely do not agree to adopting her." Merlin made his stance clear, adding, "Besides, she's not your child, nor is she mine. Raising someone else's kid... sorry, I can't accept that."

Alice, seeing Merlin's practical stance, refused to give up. She maliciously speculated, "Are you just upset because the baby only likes me and ignores you? Is that why you're feeling unbalanced?"

"What's there to feel unbalanced about? What does it have to do with me?" Merlin said bluntly.

"You—!" Alice pointed at Merlin and tried to ask, "What if the baby calls you 'Daddy'? Wouldn't you feel... something?"

"Not at all, thanks. We demons care about bloodlines." Merlin replied coldly.

"Hmph!" Alice let out a cold snort, muttering, "What's the big deal? Raising a child would be so joyful. Besides, that kid is well-behaved and won't cause trouble."

"Joyful, my foot. We're already being mistaken for a married couple. If we adopt a child, won't that just confirm the relationship? We'd never be able to clear our names!" Merlin said seriously, then suddenly looked as if he had a revelation. "Oh~ I see, you scheming woman. Are you trying to turn this pretend relationship into a real one and marry me?"

"Ugh!" Alice's face slowly turned red, and she quickly retorted, "Pfft! You're shameless! Who would want to marry a guy like you?"

"Good, then I can rest easy. Drop the idea of adopting a child. As a self-respecting, refined man, I do care about my reputation." Merlin said this with a straight face, utterly without shame.

Alice glared at Merlin, silent. She thought, *What kind of reputation does a stinking demon have? Does Merlin not like children?*

Deep down, Alice still wanted to adopt that baby. Apart from feeling sympathy for the orphan, she also thought that having a child between her and Merlin seemed like a very romantic idea.

But Alice would never voice her true thoughts, especially not after seeing Merlin's attitude.

This left Alice feeling extremely frustrated. After living with Merlin for so long, it turned out he didn't have the slightest romantic feeling for her. She had been harboring one-sided feelings all along.

Merlin didn’t want to discuss adopting a child anymore, so he changed the subject. "Your strength has improved. You can even transform into a giant dragon. I suppose you're not far off from a true Frost Saint Dragon now."

"No, I'm at the peak of both magic and battle aura at Saint-tier. I'm actually a bit stronger than a true Frost Saint Dragon." Alice replied, still annoyed.

"So, you've digested all the inheritance crystals?" Merlin asked curiously.

"No, there's still some left. No matter what I do, they won't budge. It's like they're missing some conditions." Alice muttered in confusion. Currently, 75% of the inheritance crystals in her body had been utilized, but a quarter remained unused.

"Hmm? Even though you've surpassed a true dragon, the inheritance crystals still haven't been fully absorbed. That's strange." Merlin furrowed his brows, equally puzzled.

"Do you have any ideas?" Alice asked.

Merlin wasn't very familiar with inheritance crystals. He had only come across rough records in demon race texts. The details were unclear to him. However, dragons, being creatures that had existed since the beginning of creation, certainly held many secrets beyond ordinary comprehension.

"Is that so?" Alice knitted her delicate brows, sensing the lingering chilling aura within her. The remaining inheritance crystals were still slowly circulating. She wondered what method could unlock 100% of the dragon's power.

"Your situation only points to one possibility." Merlin said expressionlessly, speculating, "Perhaps even the dragons themselves cannot fully utilize all their strength. Maybe they've been sealed by some mysterious force all this time..."

Behind Merlin and Alice's carriage, Dickter Ping was cautiously following.

The mercenary leader hadn't died. Instead, he had been lucky enough to survive.

And in this time, he had learned many secrets that completely shattered his worldview.

Dickter Ping had never imagined that the lord of Avignon was a vampire. Had he been working for the blood clan in the shadows all along?

This was something Dickter Ping couldn't accept. He refused to be a pawn used by others and wanted to uncover more secrets.

So, as soon as Merlin and Alice left Avignon, he secretly followed behind.

His instincts told him that these two adventurers were connected to a huge secret, and there might be profits to be made.

Dickter Ping was a man driven by greed. He knew it was extremely dangerous, but he still wanted to take a gamble for a chance to turn his life around.

Hmph! Blood clan? A party of adventurers consisting of a Demon Lord and a giant dragon?

Things were getting more and more interesting.

(工邛)?

title: Chapter 26 — The Fallen Saintess
content:
Chapter 26 — The Fallen Saintess

Volume 17 · Chapter 26

On the road, Merlin and Alice were still wondering why they hadn't seen a single person.

They were already near the capital, which was the empire's political center, so it should have been bustling.

But the desolate road made them very confused, feeling inconsistent with the prosperous capital image.

Until they reached the foot of France's capital, they realized something was wrong—

They saw the solemn city wall had a large hole torn open, and everywhere were ruins, like a devastated wasteland after a catastrophe.

"What the hell? Is this the capital?" Merlin frowned, jumped off the carriage to look around, wondering if he and Alice had taken a wrong turn.

"...Yeah, this is the capital, but what exactly happened?" Alice was equally puzzled, seeing several injured soldiers sitting listlessly at the city gate, like defeated losers who had lost all morale—

"Could there have been a battle before we arrived?" Merlin speculated, seeing many signs of destruction even from below the city gate.

"Let's go in and take a look?" Alice suggested, gesturing for Merlin to hitch up the carriage and follow.

When they entered the capital, they understood what "devastation" meant—everywhere were destroyed houses.

Especially in the far distance, under the power of the legendary magic cannons, the ground formed a huge pit, and half the capital had completely disappeared.

There were few pedestrians on the road, hardly resembling a prosperous imperial capital—almost no different from a refugee port, both were desolate and bleak.

After the empire's defeat, the prime minister's mansion had long been emptied.

Medes chose to abandon the capital without courtesy, having long secretly slipped away with his subordinates through an absolutely secret passage. Of course, Beelzebub's sister Miranda had also been taken captive.

In the end, after witnessing Beelzebub's terrifying power, Medes still had no intention of letting Miranda go, choosing to contend with this Demon Lord to the end.

After all, demon blood was precious, and moreover Miranda was the Demon Lord's sister, making her even more noble by bloodline.

If Dracula successfully awakened and drank demon blood, he would surely quickly recover to his prime state, perhaps becoming even stronger than before with demonic power.

Thus Miranda was an important link in the vampire revival plan, naturally impossible to hand over easily.

Although compared to Miranda, Beelzebub's blood as the Demon Lord would be even better—if the vampires could control the Gluttony Demon Lord, that would be like heaven's work!

However, after seeing Beelzebub's methods, Medes could only choose to give up on targeting Beelzebub, opting instead for the safest approach—controlling Miranda.

Because Medes had no confidence in defeating Beelzebub; several rounds of fierce attacks hadn't knocked down this demon, and if he fought personally, it would be risky.

Especially the final salvo of 12 legendary magic cannons had only forced the Demon Lord's true body out, failing to cause fatal damage.

This made Medes sweat with shame; he felt he couldn't even remain calm under the legendary magic cannons' attack, and despite his powerful self-healing ability, he dared not take risks.

Anyway, the empire's losses were huge—two powerful figures fallen, the capital destroyed beyond recognition.

Even the proud legendary magic cannons, after use, entered a year-long cooldown and couldn't be used consecutively.

The once-glorious France was now rapidly declining; Medes' goal had been achieved. Though Beelzebub rampaged and weakened the empire, in the end it would serve as the wedding dress for the vampires lurking in the shadows.

The next day, news of Medes' escape spread quickly throughout the capital's streets, instantly causing panic among everyone.

To the survivors, Medes was their savior and backbone—if even he sneaked away, didn't that prove the capital was completely doomed?

In a moment, people were in a panic. Nobles fled the capital with their wealth, believing all of France was unsafe, causing the imperial capital to become a ghost city overnight. What remained were old, weak, sick, and disabled—pitiful people unable to escape.

As for the empire's sole heir, Margaret, kidnapped by Beelzebub?

Who cared about the fate of this stupid princess? They were busy saving their own lives!

Maybe Beelzebub would destroy the entire empire—running a step late meant death!

But someone still cared about Margaret—the loyal knight Blaze.

Blaze had thick skin and flesh; though pierced through the belly by Beelzebub, he had luckily survived.

But he suffered significant injuries and probably wouldn't recover for a year and a half—he could no longer be called combat-effective.

After Blaze awoke, he was besieged with affairs. Hearing the princess had been kidnapped, he was anxious, dragging his severely injured and exhausted body—

tending to the unconscious old king in the palace.

maintaining the chaotic order of the capital.

and searching everywhere for Beelzebub's sister to save Margaret from danger.

However, Blaze had ordered his subordinates to search the main city thoroughly, finding absolutely no clues about Beelzebub's sister.

As nearly a week passed, Beelzebub's patience was limited, and Margaret's chances of survival grew increasingly slim....

Merlin and Alice walked along the ruined capital avenues, looking around constantly.

Having just arrived and witnessed this, the two found it inexplicable.

"Has this place been robbed by bandits? Not a single person in sight..." Merlin led the carriage, completely confused about the current situation.

"Rather than bandits, it looks more like a monster attack not long ago?" Alice thought it looked like the place had experienced fierce battle not long ago.

"Well, that's good too." Merlin said unexpectedly.

"What's good about it? You're gloating?" Alice raised her delicate eyebrows, disagreeing.

"No, don't forget you and I are imperial fugitives. If the capital hadn't suffered this disaster, you and I probably couldn't get in." Merlin scouted the surroundings sneakily; though he occasionally saw a few guards, they were spiritless and paid no attention to them.

Alice was speechless, thinking it seemed true—she and Merlin were fugitives for assassinating imperial nobles, so entering the capital required keeping a low profile.

"Eh?" Merlin suddenly saw a person in the

title: Chapter 27 — The Capital's Predicament
content:
Chapter 27 — The Capital's Predicament

Volume 17 · Chapter 27

Since her defeat, Jeanne had been wandering alone through the ruined capital, never once returning to O'Brien Cathedral.

Bishop Scott had held Jeanne in extremely high expectations, yet she had failed to deliver.

Though Jeanne wasn't certain what the bishop thought of her now, she herself lacked the courage to return.

Jeanne hadn't expected Belial to still be hiding his strength, fully capable of instantly razing the capital, yet this demon was toying with everyone for his own amusement.

She now felt the enormous gap in power between humans and demons, and realized that eradicating the demons would likely be an extremely difficult and arduous task.

Jeanne berated herself, growing increasingly dispirited, feeling too weak to stand against the Demon Lords, let alone dream of becoming the Hero.

In the end, Jeanne was deeply discouraged—not only had she lost to Alice back then, but now she had been utterly defeated by Belial. She truly was a complete failure.

Just as Jeanne was alone in a corner, questioning her existence, she heard Alice's voice, which gave her a slight jolt of surprise.

Alice stood before Jeanne, noticing her disheveled state—covered in wounds, clothes tattered, looking as though she had suffered a great setback. She asked with concern, "...What happened to you?"

"Ugh!" Jeanne snapped back to her senses, her expression shifting rapidly before she looked down and fell silent, seemingly unwilling to speak with Alice.

As a fellow Hero candidate who had once trained together, Alice had always been far more successful than Jeanne, consistently surpassing her.

This filled Jeanne with quiet envy in her heart. To be seen by Alice in such a wretched state was a deep shame.

Now, having just been defeated, she was caught by Alice—how could she not feel miserable? She wished she could crawl into a crack in the ground and hide.

Alice noticed Jeanne's strange reaction and pressed further, "Why won't you speak? What exactly happened?"

"What's it to you? Stop blocking my sunlight, you're in the way!" Jeanne snapped, her tone completely unfriendly.

"You?!" Alice's eyebrows knit together as she grew angry, "What kind of attitude is that? I was just asking if you were alright!"

"Alright?" Merlin approached, pulling up in a carriage, noticing the atmosphere wasn't exactly harmonious.

"Hmph!" Alice, irritated, clenched her fists and glared at Merlin, using her as an outlet for her frustration whenever she was in a bad mood.

"Tch!"

Merlin rolled her eyes. She thought, This woman is really something—she didn't do anything to me, yet she's glaring at me?

So Merlin looked down at Jeanne, who was sitting on the ground, and upon seeing her pitiful state, couldn't help but tease her a bit.

However, when she noticed the holy spear Jeanne was clutching, her expression changed, recalling the nightmares from her childhood caused by the Gun Hero.

Without hesitation, Merlin stepped forward and snatched the crimson holy spear from Jeanne's grasp, examining it closely in her hands.

"Merlin, what are you doing?" Alice suddenly realized, confused as to why Merlin was suddenly grabbing someone else's weapon.

Merlin said nothing, inspecting it a few times before recognizing it as the Gun Hero's weapon—the very one that had once pointed at her and nearly killed her.

Even now, Merlin could vividly recall that scene—waking up screaming from a dream in the marketplace, the Gun Hero pointing his weapon at her. That was the moment she had come closest to death in her entire life.

The Gun Hero was a lingering wound for Merlin, something she had to overcome, much like how a child bitten by a snake in youth might grow up fearing ropes.

Merlin was no different. Though the Gun Hero had disappeared long ago and she had grown older, deep down she still harbored fear toward him.

"Give it back!" Jeanne suddenly sprang to her feet, snatching the holy spear back, glaring at Merlin with disgust and wariness.

Merlin shot Jeanne a glance, a wave of confusion rising within her. Where had this girl gotten such a weapon? It clearly wasn't the Gun Hero's, was it? How strange...

"Merlin, what are you doing grabbing someone else's stuff?" Alice muttered disapprovingly.

"Nothing much, just... something caught my eye." Merlin gave a vague explanation, unwilling to elaborate on her past, and turned her attention back to Jeanne, "Where did you get that weapon?"

"Is there a problem with that?" Jeanne replied with hostility, clutching the holy spear tightly as if afraid Merlin would try to take it again.

In truth, Merlin had no interest in the crimson spear—she was only fixated on the Gun Hero. "That long spear should belong to the Gun Hero O'Brien, right? It's his most treasured weapon—how did it end up in your hands?"

"Huh?! Really?" Alice's interest was piqued upon hearing the name of the Gun Hero O'Brien, and she began scrutinizing the holy spear in Jeanne's arms.

After all, Alice had once been a Hero herself, and she had heard some tales about the legendary Gun Hero.

In the Church's history, the Gun Hero was a figure of legend, especially known for slaying the Demon Lord Lucifer II, a deed widely celebrated.

Naturally, Alice was curious to see the legendary Hero's weapon in person. However, Lucifer II was Merlin's mother, and she was uncomfortable discussing it.

After all, Alice wasn't foolish. She had been living with Merlin for so long, and the past was too sensitive a topic to bring up.

Jeanne looked into Merlin's eyes and said calmly, "I didn't expect you to be just a low-ranking adventurer, yet you know so much. This spear was bestowed upon me by Bishop Scott, specifically for slaying demons."

Merlin felt awkward inside but said nothing, continuing her questioning, "How would a bishop come into possession of the Gun Hero's weapon?"

"How should I know? O'Brien Cathedral was where the Gun Hero grew up. This weapon might have been left behind by him himself." Jeanne replied tersely, clearly not wanting to discuss it further with Merlin.

Merlin was taken aback. O'Brien Cathedral? Named after the Gun Hero, and the place where he grew up? It seemed worth a visit.

Because of the childhood trauma inflicted by the Gun Hero, Merlin longed to face that man in battle, but unfortunately, he had mysteriously vanished thirty years ago after the appearance of the Great Sea Demon of the North.

"Jeanne, what happened? How did you end up like this?" Alice wasn't concerned about the holy spear at all—she was more worried about what had happened to Jeanne.

Jeanne furrowed her brow and once again looked down, falling silent, embarrassed to be seen by Alice in such a state.

"Is it really that hard to talk about? We just want to know what happened in the capital." Alice pressed urgently.

"...Jeanne hesitated for a moment, and despite herself, gave in to Alice's persistence, speaking evasively, 'A few days ago, Belial attacked the capital in search of his sister. Everyone fought back desperately, but the outcome was grim—Princess Marguerite was taken hostage by Belial. If we don't find his sister, she'll definitely die.'"

"Huh?! ...Belial!" Merlin was startled upon hearing Jeanne's account of the capital's situation, her heart beginning to race.

Belial had actually left the Demon Lord Palace in search of Miranda?!

This means we might run into him at any time...

To think he would so brazenly destroy the human empire's capital like this...

(??ω?? ?)

title: Chapter 28 — Knight's Plea for Help
content:
Chapter 28 — Knight's Plea for Help

Volume 17 · Chapter 28

Merlin recalled the words Asmodeus had once spoken to him back in Rex Muth, and piecing that together with the current situation, he suddenly understood what was going on.

It seemed that after Miranda was kidnapped, she had ended up in the royal capital of France—otherwise Belial wouldn't have attacked this place.

He hadn't expected Miranda to be right here in France, in the same place as himself?

If he had known that, he should have agreed to help Belial find Miranda and hand her over in the process.

But now things had turned out this way, and there was no easy resolution anymore.

Damn, who was stupid enough to provoke this demon-molester? Miranda was Belial's lifeline...

Merlin suddenly felt immense pressure, feeling somewhat responsible—if he had agreed to help from the start, things wouldn't have ended up like this.

What was Belial's excuse for slaughtering an entire royal capital for his sister? Even fellow demons dared not touch his sister, and this madman tore them apart without hesitation!

As a fellow Demon Lord, Merlin felt awkward. Both he and Belial were Demon Lords, yet this madman was causing chaos, leaving him with a sense of guilt.

"Belial attacked the royal capital?!"

Alice's eyes widened. She had never imagined that besides the discarded Merlin, there were other Demon Lords roaming around freely.

It was her first time hearing about Demon Lords actively launching attacks on human territories—truly rare.

Thinking of Merlin beside her, Alice narrowed her eyes and gave him a meaningful look.

Merlin's eyebrows twitched as he felt uncomfortable under her gaze.

Alice's expression was one of reproach toward Merlin, as if saying, "See? Demons are really all bad—this confirms it! They're running around causing destruction with impunity!"

"Cough!" Merlin cleared his throat and lowered his voice, "What are you staring at? It's not like I did it—this blame isn't mine to bear."

Alice also lowered her voice and whispered, "But you're a Demon Lord too. What do you have to say about your companion's actions?"

"I'm just a discarded piece of trash who got fired. Besides, isn't it Belial who started this? If his sister hadn't gone missing, would he have attacked the royal capital for no reason?" Merlin deflected the blame entirely.

"That's no way to handle it either, is it? Killing more people won't solve the root problem, will it?" Alice thought Belial was simply a destroyer, and it even made her begin to doubt Merlin.

"Not all demons are like me. Do you think I can chat with you politely every day? Are all the other demons reasonable?" Merlin countered, raising his fist to show Alice, "In the demon race, fists are the ultimate truth. Without fists, no one will acknowledge you."

05 SE this little cure

"You two are whispering behind my back?" Judith interjected, annoyed, thinking Alice and Merlin were gossiping about her.

"Nothing much." Merlin mumbled evasively, then asked, "Speaking of which, have you still not found Belial's sister?"

"If you could find her, would the royal capital have been reduced to this state? Would the princess have been forced to become a hostage to buy time?" Judith's expression was grim as she looked down, "Just great, everything's ruined. This empire has been destroyed by Belial, and I can do nothing but watch helplessly..."

"So who's managing the royal capital now? Is it Chancellor Meads?" Merlin pressed, having learned from the coachman that the old king was ill and that Meads was the one running the empire. But now this chancellor seemed suspicious.

"For now, it's being managed by Lord Blaise. As for Meads? Ha, he was terrified by the Gluttony Demon Lord and fled overnight. Now the royal capital is filled with only the elderly, the weak, and the sick. They've all been abandoned by Meads." Judith said bitterly, having spoken grandly in the council but fled faster than anyone.

Hearing Judith's words, Merlin's head swam. Not only had they not found Miranda, but Belial would surely not stop—unless he beat this demon-molester senseless and made him behave.

However, Merlin wasn't particularly eager to meet Belial. Though they were both Demon Lords, they weren't especially close.

But if Belial continued to run amok in France, it would likely interfere with Merlin's own interests.

Merlin was investigating the vampire clan, but with everything in such chaos, how could he possibly conduct his investigation? The people in the royal capital had scattered.

Even the key informant Meads had disappeared—wasn't this whole trip in vain?

Alice was equally disappointed, but right now she was more concerned about the kidnapped princess. Who knew what horrors the princess might be subjected to after being taken by a Demon Lord.

"Where is the kidnapped princess being held?"

"I don't know. The princess's whereabouts are probably known only by Blaise and the High Priest. I haven't set foot in the church in several days." Judith answered with deep shame.

"Huh?!" Alice was taken aback and asked curiously, "Why haven't you gone back?"

"Why do you ask? I was defeated. I failed the High Priest's expectations. I... I even brought shame to the master of the sacred spear." Judith sank into deep self-reproach, not even looking at Alice.

"The Hero of the Spear is such a big deal?" Merlin frowned, his tone mocking.

"What do you know?" Judith looked up and glared at Merlin, "A black-iron adventurer dares to judge the Hero?"

Merlin tugged at his mouth and smiled without speaking, thinking, I've killed nearly 100 heroes—Alice, the so-called lucky goddess's daughter, can't be counted. So many heroes, and only this stinky woman managed to survive under my blade—of course, thanks to the inherited Hero's Silver Armor.

"What's that supposed to mean? Because you were defeated, you don't dare go back? When I was defeated, I still had the face to return!" Alice thought it was no big deal, and being unable to beat Merlin was just a fact.

05 SE small play

"I'm not the same as you. I am a devout believer, while you are a greedy impostor!" Judith solemnly distinguished herself from Alice.

"It has nothing to do with that. Defeating Demon Lords is not something you should be doing—it's the Hero's job. I am the Hero!" Alice pointed at herself, then awkwardly laughed, "Of course, I used to be, and among all the past Heroes, I was the most unremarkable with no achievements at all, hehe."

"You're surprisingly self-aware?" Merlin couldn't help but mutter inappropriately.

"G-U-N!" Alice gave Merlin a fierce look, her gaze sharp enough to kill.

"What do you mean? Are you mocking me for losing to you back then?" Judith's face turned black. Alice said she was useless, so wasn't she saying she was even more useless?

"No, what I mean is, although I'm a useless Hero, I have more experience dealing with Demon Lords than you. Can you take us to the Grand Cathedral of Oublaan? The princess might be in grave danger." Alice said seriously.

The Grand Cathedral of Oublaan.

Wrapped in bandages from head to toe and leaning on a cane, Blaise approached Bishop Scott.

"I beg the Holy Church to dispatch its elite forces and save Princess Marguerite!"

"Besides you, we have no other options..."

title: Chapter 29 — The Hero Who Can Get By
content:
Chapter 29 — The Hero Who Can Get By

Volume 17 · Chapter 29

The great cathedral of Oublain had grown far quieter than usual, with only Scott, the cardinal, standing as its lone guardian.

Blaze had given it his all, yet he still hadn't found Belshazzar's sister.

He didn't even know how Margaret was faring now. He just sensed that the situation was dangerous.

The empire's strength had suffered considerable damage, and few forces remained that could be of use.

With no other choice, Blaze dragged his wounded body to beg the Holy Church for help.

After all, the Holy Church was the demon race's sworn enemy. Even if it was in decline, a skeleton camel was still mightier than a healthy horse.

Blaze hoped Cardinal Scott would contact the Vatican and send over some strong reinforcements—perhaps Margaret could still be saved.

But upon hearing Blaze's request, the old man wore a troubled expression. "Lord Blaze, I understand your urgency, but having the Vatican send rescue troops—that's not realistic."

"Why!? Don't you guys go on and on about exterminating demons every day? Now the Demon Lord is all alone—doesn't this give you the perfect opportunity to ambush him? Hurry up and summon a Hero or something and kill this demon bastard!" Blaze, hot-tempered, snapped. If he weren't leaning on his cane, he'd probably have already hauled the cardinal up by his collar and forced him.

"There is no Hero," Cardinal Scott emphasized. "Since the 233rd generation, my church has never chosen a new Hero."

"That doesn't mean you can just stand by and watch the prince die! He volunteered to become a hostage to save everyone! The reason we're still standing here alive is because of the favor he's done us!" Blaze, furious, shouted back. He was on the verge of losing his mind, and the bandages wrapped around his abdomen were turning a deep red.

"No—we're alive because of the Goddess Maria's blessing. Everything is predestined..." Cardinal Scott said with great presumption.

—Moushi small novel

"Cut the crap! What does the goddess have to do with anything!? I despise you priests most of all! When it comes to good fortune, you're the first to jump at the chance, but when it comes to bad deeds, you're the fastest to run away!" Blaze, enraged, grabbed Scott by his collar and yanked him forward.

"Lord Blaze, please calm down," Scott, sweating coldly, quickly explained, "I deeply admire Princess Margaret's courage. She is a kind-hearted princess, not a useless person. I apologize for my earlier lack of respect. But our Church is also struggling to spare any additional personnel for a rescue. These days aren't like before—we suffered heavy losses in the war against the First Demon Lord Palace."

"Even without a Hero, doesn't your Church still have a Saint Knight Commander? Can't you send one over?" Blaze pressed on.

"That's... that's difficult. The Saint Knight Commander answers directly to the Pope. I have no authority to command them. Moreover, they exist solely to protect the Vatican, so they may not come to Princess Margaret's aid." Scott said nervously.

"Are you going to just stand by and watch? You're supposed to be experts at dealing with demons! What use are you now!" Blaze, beside himself, was so angry he wanted to punch the old man senseless if his wounds hadn't still not healed.

"...This might not be such a bad thing. Someone as kind as Princess Margaret will surely be summoned by the goddess after death, living the rest of her days in bliss." Blaze reluctantly said, having already concluded that Margaret was doomed and had ascended to heaven.

"I...fuck..."

SF2 small

Blaze's rage surged straight to his temples. He couldn't hold back any longer—he had to beat this old priest senseless. It seemed the Holy Church was no help after all.

But suddenly, the doors of the Oublain Cathedral swung open, interrupting the argument inside.

Jill walked in directly, approaching Cardinal Scott, then kneeling on one knee. "Cardinal, I have returned."

"Jill?" Scott pushed Blaze aside and stepped forward to help Jill up. "My child, where have you been? Why have you returned so late?"

"I apologize, Cardinal. I... I have been defeated in battle. I failed to meet Your Eminence's expectations, and I am deeply ashamed of my incompetence..."

Jill slowly stood, speaking with a tone full of self-reproach.

"It's fine. We all underestimated the Demon Lord's power. It's only natural that you couldn't win. You needn't blame yourself." Scott had no intention of blaming Jill.

"...I can't forgive myself. If my strength were just a little greater, I would have succeeded." Jill frowned, feeling that the pseudo-divine artifact was already quite powerful, and it was all because she was too weak to unleash the spear's full power.

"You've done your best, my child. We've been fighting demons for countless ages and have never been able to eradicate them. How much more could you, on your own, hope to defeat the Demon Lord?" Scott said seriously.

Though Jill was unwilling to admit it, she couldn't deny the truth. So she brought Merlin and Alice along.

After all, rescuing Margaret was the priority now. Grudges would have to wait.

"Cardinal, I've brought back two..."

Merlin and Alice walked in from outside, looking around like tourists.

Especially Merlin, who was quite curious about everything here. He wondered, is this where the Gun Hero grows up? It's so ordinary. He'd imagined it would be some hellish training ground.

Merlin couldn't fathom how such a mundane cathedral could produce a cold-blooded warrior like the Gun Hero, let alone one who could spar evenly with the Demon Lords.

Alice spotted Cardinal Scott and walked straight over. "It's been a long time, Cardinal Scott. I believe the last time we met was when I left the Vatican."

As a former Hero, Alice naturally knew Scott. After all, there were only twelve red-robed cardinals, and their status was second only to the Pope. During her time as Hero, she had met nearly all of them.

"You..." Scott furrowed his brow, not immediately recognizing her, only feeling that she was very familiar.

"Already forgotten me? What a terrible memory you have..." Alice sighed with a wry smile.

"Alice! You still owe me tens of millions!" Scott finally recognized her and exclaimed in surprise.

"Ugh, why do you have to bring that up right away?" Alice awkwardly laughed, not expecting to be reminded of her debt the moment they met.

Scott was extremely surprised inwardly. He hadn't expected to see the former Hero again.

He remembered that when Alice had failed in her quest to defeat the First Demon Lord Palace, she had returned alone, disheveled and ashamed.

She had even lost the mithril armor worn by all the Heroes throughout history, racked up a massive debt, and then simply quit and left the Church.

But now, seeing Alice become a mithril adventurer, he had to admit his respect for her.

The title of mithril adventurer symbolized strength. The weak could never achieve such a rank. Scott realized that Alice had grown significantly stronger since leaving the Church.

"It's been a long time. I never expected the weakest and most failed Hero in history to become a mithril adventurer. But when will you finally pay back what you owe?"

"Right, you bring up money the moment you see me! Shouldn't you be more polite and catch up first? I'll pay you back, so stop nagging me, you old man!" Alice, annoyed, her mood soured instantly.

"Fine, let's set the debt aside for now. You've long since cut ties with the Church. Why are you here?" Scott asked, puzzled.

"We just happened to pass by. We heard there was some trouble here. I heard the empire's princess was kidnapped?" Alice countered.

"Yes, Margaret... wait, what?" Cardinal Scott suddenly had a flash of insight and turned to Blaze beside him.

"Lord Blaze, you wanted the Church to send a Hero to rescue the princess, didn't you?"

"The person standing before you is our Church's final Hero!"

"She once participated in the campaign against the First Demon Lord Palace and survived!"

"She may lack other talents, but she's especially good at clinging to life. Do you think she's suitable?"

title: Chapter 30 — Expedition Against Gluttony
content:
Chapter 30 — Expedition Against Gluttony

Volume 17 · Chapter 30

“What Hero? Aren’t those two the wanted criminals who assassinated nobles?”

Blaze stared at Merlin and Alice with a very serious expression, his heart full of wariness, unable to tell whether they were friend or foe.

Just moments ago, when Merlin and Alice had walked in, Blaze had felt a familiar flutter in his eyes, certain he’d seen them somewhere before.

After carefully examining the two of their adventurer IDs, Blaze suddenly realized the truth—weren’t these two the wanted criminals who killed Avignon’s lord, Camilla?! And not long ago, they’d even spoken with Princess Marguerite!

Blaze hadn’t expected to run into them so soon. Although the enemy of his enemy was his friend, now that Desmond had fled, who knew what Merlin and Alice’s true intentions were?

"...What wanted criminals?" Scott asked in surprise, finding it hard to accept. After all, Alice was a Hero of impeccable character—how could she possibly become a wanted criminal?

"Alice, you..." Judith’s expression turned odd, hesitating, unwilling to believe what Blaze was saying.

"Ugh, we’ve been spotted..." Alice broke out in an awkward expression, a bead of cold sweat trickling down her forehead, glancing over at Merlin beside her as if seeking help.

"Well, we did kill Avignon’s female lord. But doesn’t killing a non-human not violate imperial law?" Merlin reasoned, thinking no human nation would make it illegal to kill evil creatures.

"Non-human? What do you mean?" Blaze frowned, though Merlin and Alice had eliminated Desmond’s faction, which was beneficial to his side. Still, attacking nobles was a different matter entirely.

"That female lord was a vampire. Honestly, I don’t get why your empire would appoint a bloodline as a lord. Doesn’t that seem strange?" Merlin said with a shrug.

"A vampire! Avignon’s lord is a bloodline?!" Scott the bishop’s eyes widened, and he found it hard to believe. As someone who frequently dealt with evil creatures, he had some knowledge of bloodlines.

"...No way. The legendary immortal beings that fear sunlight and silver weapons—do they really exist?" Judith was stunned, probably having never faced a bloodline before.

Blaze was shocked to hear such an outrageous claim from Merlin—it was truly horrifying to think about!

If Avignon’s female lord was an evil creature, then her ally Desmond was even more suspicious!

Blaze tried to keep himself looking calm, unwilling to believe Merlin’s words so easily.

"You dare say that—do you have any evidence? Slandering nobles is a serious crime!"

"Pfft! Do I need proof when I’ve seen it with my own eyes?" Merlin said with a smirk.

"That female lord was a bloodline. We saw it with our own eyes—when we killed them with silver weapons, they burned to ashes with no bodies left." Alice agreed seriously.

Judith hesitated, then looked at Blaze beside her. "I’ve lived with Alice. She doesn’t lie."

"Right. Besides, she’s a former Hero. Her character doesn’t need questioning." Scott still trusted Alice deeply.

"..."

Blaze hesitated. If Desmond’s faction were all bloodlines, then who had he and the princess been fighting all along? Monsters?

"This is the correspondence between Avignon’s female lord and your chancellor. Take a look yourself—the secret dirty dealings are already obvious." Merlin pulled out the letter from his sleeve and tossed it directly to Blaze, letting this slow-witted knight read it for himself.

Blaze caught it quickly, tore open the envelope in three moves, and began reading. His expression turned blank, his face extremely grim.

A flood of information rushed into his mind all at once, far too much to process in the moment.

Desmond was probably like Camilla—both bloodlines, secretly running a human trafficking business. What did they need so many people for?

If Desmond wasn’t human, then everything he’d done so far should be questioned. Was there some other hidden purpose?

Why had the old king suddenly fallen ill, and why hadn’t he recovered despite treatment, with no outsiders allowed to visit?

To deceive and hide things, making the empire increasingly chaotic, ignoring the voices of commoners?

Why hadn’t he lifted a finger against Belial, letting loyal knights go die in his place?

As the empire’s chancellor and temporary ruler, noticing something was wrong and fleeing first?

All of this... seemed like the work of a spy!

Blaze’s head spun, overwhelmed by so many thoughts. It felt like he was being played like a fool, his mind couldn’t keep up.

And the situation involved too many people. As a minor knight, he didn’t have the authority to handle this. The old king was in a coma, Princess Marguerite had been kidnapped and held hostage, and everything was at a stalemate.

"Actually, we were heading for Chancellor Desmond. But we heard he already fled. What a shame. Do you know where this guy ran off to?" Merlin asked.

"...I don’t know." Blaze shook his head blankly, still unable to calm down. "But Princess Marguerite has long wanted to take down Desmond. She’s more familiar with his affairs. Perhaps she might guess where Desmond fled?"

"That’s right, then we really need to rescue the princess," Merlin said, raising an eyebrow and muttering, "Looks like we can’t do without this princess."

"Where’s the princess? We’ll go rescue her!" Alice stepped forward.

"..."

Blaze eyed Alice a few times, feeling her strength was quite formidable, with a faint aura of the dragon, stronger than himself. "Although Miss Alice’s strength is no small feat... compared to Belial, she’s still far behind. Going would just be suicide."

"That’s true. The Demon Lord grows stronger with each battle, very strange." Judith seriously reminded, still somewhat surprised that Alice had grown stronger since their last meeting.

"You two have both suffered heavy injuries. You can’t fight anymore, can you? If I don’t go, the princess is surely doomed. Do you have any other powerful reinforcements? Besides, I have experience dealing with Demon Lords. I don’t think the Gluttonous Demon Lord would be any harder than the Prideful one." Alice countered, casting a glance at Merlin.

"..."

Blaze’s face darkened. He had to admit that, for now, besides Alice, there was no one else who could stand against the Gluttonous Demon Lord.

"It’s just Belial, right? Don’t worry. I’ll make this guy behave." Merlin suddenly said casually. Facing Belial wasn’t that much pressure. It would only be truly stressful if he were up against the Envious Demon Lord, Leviathan.

Blaze, Judith, and Scott all turned to look at Merlin, their expressions like they’d just heard something bizarre.

Probably, the three of them would rather treat a dead horse as a living one and let Alice try her luck than believe that this unassuming guy could defeat Belial.

In perfect unison, the three of them automatically filtered out Merlin, instead turning even more enthusiastic toward Alice...

"Alice, are you skilled with firearms? This holy spear here, you can try it out. It works well against demons."

"Miss Alice, do you need people? I can dispatch knights to guard you."

"Alice, I’ll pray to the goddess for your safe return. Don’t worry, just go!"

"..."

Merlin broke into a cold sweat, his eye twitching furiously, seething with frustration inside.

Hey! Am I being completely ignored?!

Do you really think Alice can beat Belial?!

(??ω?? ?)

title: Chapter 31 — Deadline Approaching
content:
Chapter 31 — Deadline Approaching

Volume 17 · Chapter 31

Outside the royal city, the sun had already begun to set slowly.

The crimson sunset dyed the earth red.

Blaze had sent people to search for Margaret's location, but due to insufficient ability, could only worry anxiously.

However, the arrival of Alice and Merlin still gave him a glimmer of hope, and he told them the location.

In the end, Blaze chose to trust the two of them once; to be precise, he was willing to gamble on Alice.

This female adventurer's strength was not inferior to his own, and moreover, she was a former Hero who had challenged the Demon Lord—maybe she could truly create a miracle.

If she could really rescue Margaret, that would certainly be a happy outcome for everyone.

As for Merlin? It seemed Blaze and the others regarded him as a prop, like a free gift with purchase, and didn't have high expectations for him.

Standing next to Alice, unremarkable Merlin looked like a sidekick or assistant in every way, completely unlike a powerful figure capable of making waves.

"Lady Alice, may you have a safe journey. Although I'm still recovering from severe injuries and can't help, I still hope you return victorious." Blaze said seriously.

"Alice, be careful. Beelzebub is hard to deal with; don't underestimate him." Joan warned seriously. Although she didn't particularly like Alice, as a comrade-in-arms she still had to remind her.

"I know." Alice nodded, thinking to herself that if she couldn't win, she'd just let Merlin loose on him—after all, both were Demon Lords, so one would come out on top.

"Nobody's blessing me or anything..." Merlin muttered sourly nearby, feeling marginalized.

"....Blaze glanced at Merlin several times, really seeing nothing special about the guy. After holding it in for a long time, he said, 'Don't cause trouble for Lady Alice. Just pull Beelzebub's aggro and cheer for your teammates with "666." For other things, you probably can't help anyway.'"

"...Merlin was speechless, looking at Blaze's difficult expression, estimating that even if he racked his brains he couldn't say anything good. Besides, when had he become a freeloader who just shouts "666"?"

"Don't worry too much. Alice is after all a former Hero, and she's so good at surviving. Back then, ten thousand armies perished in the Death Marsh, but only she survived. That speaks for itself. If you can't beat her, you can always run~" Scott was optimistic and still had confidence in Alice's will to survive.

"Shut up." Alice's face darkened. She always felt like the bishop was calling her a deserter. "I'm not some Hero anymore. I'm helping you out of duty. Don't use the past to slander me."

"Clearing his throat!" Grand Bishop Scott lightly coughed, making a cross shape with one hand to mask his embarrassment, saying, "May the Goddess of Light protect you."

After Merlin and Alice left, Joan couldn't help but show worry on her face. She felt this trip was fraught with danger, after all, she had fought Beelzebub personally and knew how formidable the demon was.

"Alice, can you really beat Beelzebub? I feel really uneasy..."

"The difficulty is very high," Scott the Grand Bishop said bluntly. "We've invested so much force against Gluttony, yet we haven't even seen the bottom of his strength. Although Alice is much stronger than before, to stand on equal footing with a true Demon Lord, there's still a long way to go. I've seen previous Heroes, and they were all stronger than current Alice."

"Although I also think Miss Alice can't win against Beelzebub, as long as Princess Margaret can be rescued, that's fine. Luck is something you can't count on..." Blaze said, wanting to speak but stopping. He no longer expected Alice to defeat Beelzebub; if she could rescue the princess by sheer luck, he'd thank heaven.

The two drove the carriage toward the north of the royal city, where there was a remote mountain ravine—that was where Beelzebub was temporarily staying.

"Merlin, if I kill Beelzebub, would you feel uncomfortable? After all, you're both demons." Alice asked tentatively.

"Don't dream about it. You can't beat that guy. Only I can suppress him." Merlin replied calmly.

"How would I know if I don't try?" Alice asked back unwillingly.

"Demon Lords are very special existences; saying they're near the pinnacle of the world wouldn't be an exaggeration. Your current strength is at the peak of Saint-tier, and above that there's the Zong realm that suppresses you. Yet I've never seen a Demon Lord lose to an enemy from the Zong realm. Do you think you can beat a Demon Lord?" Merlin's realistic response made Alice give up this naive idea early.

"Then... Alice thought of Merlin's mother and asked hesitantly, 'Your mother wasn't defeated by the Spear Hero, right? So does that mean the Spear Hero is stronger than Demon Lords?'"

"Unclear." Merlin frowned, seemingly unwilling to talk about it. "I also don't understand why she was defeated by humans? And there were many suspicious things back then; now I can't make sense of it either."

"...Is that so..." Alice saw Merlin's face wasn't very good and tactfully stopped mentioning Merlin's mother.

"Anyway, stop thinking about unrealistic things.

If you meet Beelzebub later, don't interfere. I'll reason with him to behave." Merlin paused and added, "Besides, this is demon business. A human like you shouldn't meddle; you'll only make things worse."

"Oh." Alice nodded obediently, thinking to herself that reasoning would calm Beelzebub? That was impossible.

"Come to think of it, defeating the Demon Lord to rescue a princess—this is exactly the Hero's classic plot. I didn't expect I'd get to indulge in it too~" Merlin suddenly revealed a meaningful smile.

"Uh!" Alice frowned, reaching out to cover Merlin's mouth, emphasizing—

"Shut up, you shameless guy. I'm the Hero.

"You're clearly a villain role. Have some self-awareness!

In the deep, dark mountain ravine.

Margaret was locked in a cage, looking very disheveled. For these past few days she had only been able to drink stream water and chew bread to barely survive; her body was already extremely weak.

Every time she woke, she would look around like a white mouse, trying to find a way out. But the cage was made by Beelzebub from a single piece of stone—hard as rock—making escape almost impossible.

After several days with no one daring to rescue her, Margaret had figured out the situation. They definitely hadn't found Beelzebub's sister, and hope was growing dimmer.

Margaret hadn't expected to find Beelzebub's sister anyway. After all, France was so big—who knew where this female demon could be?

The reason she had willingly become a hostage was merely to delay time, to see if she could negotiate a turning point.

But Margaret had given up. Seeing Beelzebub's patience running out, she could only rely on herself instead of others.

Below, Beelzebub sat on a rock, looking up at the sky, then glancing at Margaret in the cage far away—already panic-stricken—

"Princess, it's been almost a week, and no one has sent my sister back. This isn't what you said!"

title: Chapter 32 — Sword Drawn, Bow Bent
content:
Chapter 32 — Sword Drawn, Bow Bent

Volume 17 · Chapter 32

Suddenly being questioned by Bael, Margaret was startled, as this demon was only the second time she had communicated with him in days.

This made Margaret's heart stir, as if there was still a glimmer of hope if the Demon Lord could speak and communicate.

"That... perhaps, perhaps your sister is very far from the royal city, and it may not be possible to reach her within a week."

"That's so?" Bael looked at Margaret, saying without expression, "But after the sun has completely set today, I plan to kill you."

"No... no way? I am the only heir to the empire, and my knights will definitely find your sister and rescue me." Margaret pretended to be calm, but her heart was not at ease.

"But it's been so long, and no one has helped you, I even doubt if you are a discard?" Bael leaned on his chin, looking at Margaret, and thought this woman was a bit cunning. Without the noble status of a princess, she would not be worth trusting.

"Believe me, I am the legitimate heir to the royal family. If I die, who will inherit the empire?" Margaret said very seriously.

"Okay, I believe you, but after the sun sets today, you still won't escape death, my patience is gone." Bael said indifferently, as if he no longer intended to continue discussing Margaret.

Margaret bit her lips, thinking that today might be her last day, and if things did not turn around, she would die without a chance.

It had been so many years, and there was no movement from the royal capital, "It seems I can no longer rely on them."

Margaret thought for a moment, staring at her chest, and decided to try to continue negotiating, to block everything.

"That... Mr. Demon Lord, do you have an interest in human women?"

"What do you mean?" Bael's face was as blank as a playing card, completely unaffected.

"If you wish,.... I am willing to marry you." Margaret's expression was very serious, but she was not truly heartfelt. As long as Bael agreed, she could still live, which was better than dying.

"Ah?" Bael showed disgust, even as a demon, he found such words out of place.

"I heard that your homeland is very barren and difficult to survive in. If you marry me, France would be your second homeland, and you would need to provide protection for us. This seems like a good deal, right? Demons also have desires, and I believe any male would not mind having multiple wives around." Margaret made an offer, of course, all of which were false, and she would not fulfill any of them.

"You are in such a state, and you still dare to negotiate with me? Are you drunk? You need to calm down." Bael raised his arm, pointing at Margaret in the cage, and released a black shock wave of moderate power.

"Ah!" Margaret screamed, and her whole body slammed hard against the prison bars, causing intense pain that left her on the verge of fainting.

"Are you trying to seduce me, you pathetic human? Foolish!" Bael stood up, completely unashamed, and shouted loudly, "There is no one in this world more beautiful than my sister, you worm are not even a fraction of her, humans are lowly beasts dreaming of climbing onto the noble demon race, how ridiculous!"

Margaret still did not understand Bael, as seduction might work on ordinary males, but it would be completely ineffective on a sister complex.

In Bael's eyes, only his sister was the most beautiful, and the rest... were ugly!

Added to the demon race's inherent disdain for humans, this only made Bael angry, thinking that Margaret was ignorant of her status.

After Bael shouted loudly, he found that Margaret had already passed out, and he muttered to himself, "Humans are really fragile, just a bump and they pass out...."

Outside, the sky was gradually darkening, and it seemed that Margaret's death was approaching, as the sun was gradually sinking below the horizon.

Bael was about to act, and after killing Margaret, he would continue on his journey to find his sister, but he saw a stranger walk in.

Alice had no defense, and she simply stepped into Bael's territory, looking at this gaunt-skinned Demon Lord.

"Hmm? Who are you?" Bael looked at Alice.

Alice spoke bluntly, "Release Margaret Princess!"

"Ha ha, what? Originally, it was to save this cunning woman, but I don't see my sister?" Bael was suspicious and did not see his beloved sister, which made him wary.

"If you don't cooperate, then we will have to take her by force." Alice spoke with confidence.

"Just you? You are coming to die." Bael raised his corner of his mouth, and Alice was really not worth mentioning.

"Not me, but him." Alice looked back.

Only then did Merlin step forward from behind Alice, his eyes fixed on Bael, "Long time no see, Bael."

"...Bael narrowed his eyes, although he was surprised to see Merlin, he still maintained his composure, "Lucifer..."

"What do you have to say to me?" Merlin spread his hands and smiled.

"I have nothing to say to a failed ruler who was fired by the council." Bael sneered.

"Oh, that's a pity, ha... Merlin chuckled, thinking that Bael was not very friendly, which would make things more complicated.

"Why are you in France? I heard that you refused to help me find Miranda." Bael's tone was full of reproach.

"I was just passing through, if I had known that Miranda was in France, I would have helped you." Merlin said seriously.

"What's the use of talking about it now? I have already come out, and I can find her myself." Bael thought that Merlin was being a hypocrite, which made him very resentful.

"Don't the council allow you to go out on your own? You sneaked out of the Demon Lord Palace, who is maintaining the blood pool seal? Are you trying to cause the demon race to go extinct?" Merlin raised his eyebrows.

"I'm sorry, I am not the same as you, a pathetic dog, the council dare not do anything to me. Besides, compared to my sister, the survival of the demon race is trivial to me." Bael grinned, full of superiority.

"Just like your style." Merlin nodded, saying bluntly, "You have been too reckless, Bael, this is human territory, not your backyard, you need to follow certain rules."

"Are you still a demon? You are dissatisfied with me and complain, it's a pity that you were once a ruler equal to me, the humans kidnapped my sister, and this sin should be borne by all humans, they all deserve to die!" Bael resented Merlin, and he would rather kill a few livestock than miss one, right?

"I'm sorry, this is not a complaint, but a requirement imposed on you." Merlin's expression was cold, and he spoke in a commanding tone, "Release that human princess, from now on, you need to be obedient and follow my arrangements, and we will help find your sister. If you don't listen, then I can only use force."

"Hey hey hey~, did I hear you wrong, you little greenhorn, also dare to tell me to obey you?" Bael was not afraid of Merlin, but rather like hearing a joke, and became even more reckless.

"You have only been the Demon Lord for a few years, when I was just starting to rule the Fifth Demon Lord Palace, you had not even been born yet."

"If your mother were still alive, she would not dare to speak to me in such a tone..."

title: Chapter 33 — Hand-to-Hand Combat
content:
Chapter 33 — Hand-to-Hand Combat

Volume 17 · Chapter 33

Alice looked at Merlin, noticing his calm expression showed no signs of anger.

It seemed Merlin had been Demon Lord for a very short time. Even Beelzebub, who was also a Demon Lord, referred to him as "little brat."

Although Merlin was over 200 years old, he was considered very young among the demon race, similar to a human who had just reached adulthood.

Beelzebub was from the same era as Merlin's mother, Lucifer II, and naturally looked down on this young Demon Lord.

"Stop using your age to show off your superiority. I'm not buying it," Merlin scoffed, then asked, "I've made my stance clear. Will you agree or not?"

"I refuse," Beelzebub replied bluntly, showing no intention of giving up his idea.

"Then there's no way around it..." Merlin rubbed his shoulders and sighed, "It seems we have to settle this the demon way."

"Right, neither of us wants to compromise, so there's only one path forward," Beelzebub said with a calm smile.

A cold sweat dripped down Alice's forehead as she felt the thick tension in the air. She thought, What is the demon way? What does that even mean?

"If I win, you'll listen to me. If I lose, I'll leave immediately and won't bother you again. Is that acceptable?" Merlin asked.

"Sure, I agree," Beelzebub nodded, flexing his muscles.

Merlin unfastened the Banri Garan and the sacred silver longsword from his back and casually threw them on the ground. "I won't use the draw cut, in case anyone says I'm bullying you."

"Ha, what a big mouth. Isn't your strongest technique the draw cut? When I saw you demonstrate it before, I was actually scared. Who would have thought someone could master the draw cut to such a terrifying level? If you don't use the draw cut, you're essentially a weakling with no fighting ability. What do you plan to use to beat me?" Beelzebub spoke with a teasing tone, thinking Merlin was an idiot. Cutting off his own arm like that, if Merlin didn't use the draw cut, he'd be a negligible threat.

"That's none of your business. If I defeat you with the draw cut, you probably won't be convinced. After all, you'd be on your knees in an instant," Merlin said seriously. He wasn't joking. The destructive power of the draw cut was too strong. It wasn't something Beelzebub could withstand. He might not even know how he died. This clearly wasn't conducive to resolving the current dispute.

"Hmph, you're really young and hot-headed. Fine then, I'll also take a step back," Beelzebub paused and said in a low voice, "I won't use magic anyway. I know it's useless against you, ha ha."

"Then don't waste time. Let's begin!" Merlin took off his gloves and threw them on the ground, launching a fierce attack and delivering a powerful punch directly to Beelzebub's smiling face.

"Erk!" Alice stood frozen in shock, her face slightly pale. She thought, So this is how demons resolve disputes? Just fight it out? Who has the stronger punch wins!

Beelzebub's entire body shifted backward, his waist seeming to break, and his face twisted from the impact of Merlin's punch.

However, Beelzebub still managed to stabilize himself. That was his nature. He didn't feel comfortable unless he was being hit.

This bastard has quite a bit of strength. Even without using the draw cut, his physical power was already on par with other Demon Lords...

Beelzebub's eyes darted around. He had never fought Merlin before, but just from that single punch, he realized the danger.

"Is that all you've got? Put more effort into it, little brat. You're not going to... puff!"

Before Beelzebub could finish his taunt, Merlin delivered another punch without expression, landing it squarely on Beelzebub's stomach.

Merlin didn't hold back against Beelzebub, who was also a Demon Lord. Because Demon Lords weren't made of glass, he knew his limits.

Beelzebub's eyes bulged. The immense impact on his abdomen made him feel like he was going to vomit his stomach out.

His body was blasted away like a cannonball, crashing into the rock wall. A sudden gust of wind erupted, stones flew everywhere, and the entire mountain valley shook.

"Did he win?!" Alice gasped, struggling against the fierce wind. She thought, This is how Demon Lords fight? It looks like Merlin can maintain an absolute advantage even without using the draw cut!

"This is just the beginning. Demon Lords don't lose that easily," Merlin said indifferently, walking directly toward Beelzebub, who was buried under the rubble. He knew Beelzebub would be fine even after two punches.

The ruins suddenly exploded. Beelzebub, with a grim expression, looked at the approaching Merlin with cold eyes. He brushed the dust off himself. "Stupid brat, you actually have some skill."

"You still have time to take this seriously," Merlin stepped closer to Beelzebub.

"Is that so!" Beelzebub sneered, appearing in front of Merlin in an instant, his right leg lifting like a whip. The speed was so fast that only a blur could be seen.

Merlin was caught off guard and was kicked in the shoulder by Beelzebub. A sudden surge of power sent him face-first sliding several meters across the ground!

"Idiot, don't think just because you're a Demon Lord you have the right to boss me around," Beelzebub's thin frame gradually became stronger. "Among the demon race's rulers, you're an outlier. Your behavior is completely un-demonic. You always pity humans and were even stripped of your Demon Lord status, yet you still don't know what you did wrong? Associating with such a卑微 species as humans, you're a disgrace to the demon race. I've always disliked you, and today I'll finally teach you a lesson on behalf of your mother!"

Alice didn't go to help because Merlin had told her not to interfere. However, the sudden appearance of an opponent who could fight back and forth was surprising.

Merlin usually obliterated his opponents instantly. Even without the draw cut, his punches were enough to make enemies suffer.

But this time, Merlin wasn't able to subdue Beelzebub even without using the draw cut.

Alice was a bit confused about why Merlin didn't just draw his sword and finish Beelzebub off. She assumed Merlin had his reasons. Perhaps he didn't want to kill a fellow demon.

Margaret in the cage heard the loud fighting sounds and gradually woke up from her faint. She was dazed and saw two new people here, which startled her.

Two adventurers? Could they be here to save me?

But could they defeat Beelzebub? Their strength probably wasn't enough.

And... why is that mithril adventurer standing there watching? Is he sending his iron-tier companion to die?!

Since Margaret was far away, she couldn't hear their conversation and could only guess based on what she saw with her eyes.

Merlin got up from the ground and had to admit that Beelzebub was much more difficult to handle than previous enemies. "Stop trying to lecture me with your seniority. It's not your place."

"You're just talking big!" Beelzebub roared, shattering the ground and charging toward Merlin.

Merlin remained calm, sidestepped, and grabbed Beelzebub's back of the head with a reverse hand,狠狠 pressing him into the ground.

A loud "boom" echoed as Beelzebub hit the ground headfirst.

A massive crack suddenly appeared, sand and stones flew everywhere, and the once-flat ground was transformed into a landscape of jagged rocks!

"....." Margaret's eyes widened, and an odd blush spread across her face. Seeing the handsome Merlin subduing Beelzebub and not letting the enemy gain any advantage, her heart couldn't help but race...

Although he was just an iron-tier adventurer, his strength was unexpectedly strong.

And... he's so handsome =N/w/Y

title: Chapter 34 — Bloodshed
content:
Chapter 34 — Bloodshed

Volume 17 · Chapter 34

Merlin's full attention was on Beelzebub, so he wouldn't have imagined the little princess far away was daydreaming about him.

As for Alice? She felt a bit worried about Merlin, after all, it was the first time she saw this guy give up using his draw-cut slash and choose hand-to-hand combat instead.

Although Alice thought Merlin's physical strength was strong enough, this opponent was also a Demon Lord, and his physical strength might not be weaker!

Beelzebub was pinned to the ground by Merlin and couldn't move, gritting his teeth in anger, "You this bastard..."

Merlin didn't stop, taking the opportunity to unleash a series of heavy blows on Beelzebub, each punch landing on flesh.

Each punch was like hundreds of volcanoes erupting, containing extremely overwhelming power, making the ground "boom boom boom"响!

The earth trembled with the frequency of the punches, startling and terrifying, as if an ancient giant was trampling the earth.

The cracks on the ground spread further, making a "crackling" sound of breaking, as if it would collapse at any moment.

Even with Beelzebub's amazing defensive capabilities, he couldn't hold out against Merlin's continuous heavy blows, and he actually spat out a mouthful of blood!

Although he could indeed absorb the power of the attack for his own use, there were limits, and his body couldn't absorb the power of the blows infinitely.

Beelzebub was both shocked and angry. Don't look at Merlin's youth, but in terms of strength, he was no worse than the other Demon Lords, and could even suppress these old guys.
