At this moment, Beelzebub felt he was immobile, only to be beaten by Merlin on the ground.

"Can you behave a little?" Merlin asked, his fists continuously hammering Beelzebub's back.

"Stop it already!" Beelzebub's eyes were about to pop out, shouting loudly.

Merlin felt Beelzebub's whole body turn black, a dark power surrounded Beelzebub, forcing him to retreat a few steps.

The angry storm howled, like an omen of demons descending, sweeping away everything around it.

Merlin frowned, he knew what was happening, it was definitely Beelzebub using his true form, a common ability among demons.

High-level demons would transform themselves into a form with demon horns on their heads and resembling humans, although their power would be greatly limited, it would allow them to move more easily.

When they revealed their ugly true forms, that was when they were at full strength, meaning the demons were going to go all out.

Beelzebub transformed back into his original form, all black, with huge demon horns on his head, and six pairs of fly wings grew from his back, his huge eyes spinning wildly.

"Hmph, you can't help but go all out..." Merlin coldly smiled.

"I'll see how long you can laugh," Beelzebub's voice became magnetic, making people feel uncomfortable and get goosebumps, "After all, you're just a contemptible creature born from your mother's succubus power, your bloodline is impure, you don't even have demon horns, compared to your sister, she's more like a pure demon race, as for you? I doubt you're even a foundling!"

"Who said demons must have horns?" Merlin frowned, he used to care about this issue, but now he was grateful for not having demon features to wander around in human countries.

"Your mother is of a noble royal bloodline, but as her child, you don't even look like a demon? Indeed, you're a failure born from succubus power," Beelzebub looked down on Merlin, as a demon, he was too similar to humans, and could even become one of the Seven Sovereigns? What a disgrace!

"Failure? If I beat you to the ground, who is the failure?" Merlin paused, retorting, "All demons are second-generation products, if we're talking about who is the real demon, it should be the monster sealed under the blood pool, that creature is the ancestor of all demons?"

"Tch! You're just making excuses, it's been several epochs, demons and that monster have nothing to do with each other!" Beelzebub shook the fly wings behind his head, immediately making a sharp "buzzing" sound, and disappeared from the original place in an instant.

Merlin's eyes changed, the current Beelzebub was in full release state, his power and speed were incomparable to before, much stronger!

Beelzebub's black body silently appeared behind Merlin, the moment he noticed and turned around, he was hit by a devastating sky-piercing punch.

Merlin felt his jaw was about to dislocate, his body flew into the air involuntarily, it was indeed no longer easy to deal with.

Beelzebub laughed wildly, his wings vibrated at high frequency and he soared into the sky, launching a pursuit attack on Merlin who couldn't defend himself.

"Hahaha! I'll let you experience the fear of a real demon firsthand!"

"You, your draw-cut slash was impressive back then, we several sovereigns agreed to let you become the new Demon Lord because we saw you had some real talent!

"But I've been looking down on you for a long time, why would we have someone like you among us? Are you really worthy of this arrogant throne?!"

"You're nothing without this technique! How about it? Do you want to backtrack and use it to save face? Hahaha!"

Beelzebub unleashed ruthless attacks on Merlin in the air, using all kinds of ruthless techniques, punching and kicking.

Merlin was hit back and forth like a ping-pong ball, often as soon as one side was hit, Beelzebub was already on the other side.

This super-fast speed was terrifying, giving the illusion of being invincible, how could one fight such a powerful demon?

Beelzebub flew up and down, fighting with increasing vigor, like he was kicking Merlin like a ball, unbeatable!

The frequent heavy blows hit Merlin's body, making him emit muffled groans one after another, this Beelzebub was really hard to deal with.

The fierce battle stirred up a storm like a knife, combined with a huge noise, as fierce as a typhoon landing, the mountain gorge began to collapse and disintegrate with a "rumbling" sound!

"Merlin!" Alice shouted, gripping the rapier at her waist, hesitating whether to go up and help, but what would Merlin think if she interfered?

Margaret in the cage was full of shock, although she knew Beelzebub was very powerful, she didn't expect his seriousness to exceed her imagination.

At first, she was very happy to see Merlin could suppress Beelzebub, but now her heart was lifted, worried that if these two adventurers lost, she would definitely die!

Margaret looked at Alice, who was far away and hadn't moved, and couldn't help but think anxiously, what was this woman thinking? Go up and help quickly!

"I hope you reflect on it properly, you're not qualified to boss me around!"

Beelzebub thought it was enough, he kicked Merlin down with a foot, and then fell from the sky, wanting to use his knee to cripple Merlin directly.

Sharp whistling sounds echoed, Beelzebub's attack was extremely brutal, as soon as it touched the ground, it raised waves of shock, the earth followed suit and rolled!

The destructive power of this sky-falling knee strike was comparable to a comet hitting the ground, the entire mountain gorge was instantly flattened.

"Hey!" Alice drew her rapier, ready to intervene, but she stopped after taking a few steps forward, her expression shocked.

In the deep pit where the two were, Merlin was dirty and disheveled, his clothes torn to pieces, his hands tightly protecting his chest, and he had actually withstood Beelzebub's comet strike!

Alice stopped, a layer of cold sweat appeared on her forehead, thinking that after taking so many attacks, he could still block? Looking at his clear eyes, he should be fine.

Beelzebub's pair of crimson fly eyes were full of horror, his knee was blocked by Merlin's arms, making it difficult to attack again--

...Is that possible?

He clearly took so many direct heavy blows from me!

How could he still have the strength to defend against my final killing move!?

...Is this guy really a demon!?

He feels like his physical strength and durability have already surpassed other demons!

title: Chapter 35 — Counterattack in the Death Trap
content:
Chapter 35 — Counterattack in the Death Trap

Volume 17 · Chapter 35

A normal demon would have been half-dead by now after taking such direct attacks. Why does this guy still have the strength to fight back?

Aren't you already past your limit? A defective product relying on a succubus's power, how can your physical strength be so formidable?

Belial didn't expect Merlin to still have the strength to resist. He thought the final blow would end the fight, but he had underestimated Merlin's endurance.

"Enough of this? Isn't it my turn now?" Merlin smiled, kicking Belial away with one foot.

Belial flapped his fly wings and floated in the air. "You're more durable than I expected. It's rare for a Demon Lord to remain calm under such intense attacks. I'm truly surprised."

Merlin slowly stood up from the deep pit, his clothes torn and looking somewhat disheveled, with some minor injuries on his face from the beating. "You're surprised by this? You're underestimating me."

Margaret in the cage watched Merlin from afar. Though she didn't understand what they were saying, the fact that he could stand up after such a brutal beating already shocked her.

After all, just a few days ago, the empire's elite forces weren't a match for Belial, and the legendary magic cannon could only force out his demon true body.

What's the background of this black iron adventurer? To last this long under Belial's full firepower, is he too strong?

And to stand up to him directly without showing any signs of weakness, this strength... seems to be on par with a true Demon Lord...

Margaret looked at Merlin from afar, her heart pounding. She found herself thinking Merlin was the prince charming she was waiting for.

Handsome, powerful, determined, he completely outshone all her previous suitors! A rare man in a hundred years!

Margaret had set a rule that only someone who could defeat Blaze could marry her. Merlin clearly could do it easily, and even exceeded the requirement!

Even as an imperial princess, Margaret found herself a little out of control when facing Merlin. Even his flaw of being a low-level black iron adventurer was ignored with style.

Alice saw Merlin stand up and let out a slight sigh of relief, thinking she didn't need to help for now. Defeating Belial should be no problem, right?

"I have to admit, you have the potential to become a Demon Lord, but it's still far from enough!"

Belial was不甘 (reluctant), and immediately charged forward with lightning speed, kicking Merlin's neck with a whip-like leg!

The sharp attack brought a whooshing sound, and the powerful surprise attack left the enemy unable to react. Even Alice, from afar, couldn't catch Belial's figure with her eyes.

"Don't think the same trick will work on me again,哼!"

Merlin coldly scoffed, directly grabbing Belial's ankle by the back, putting him in a passive position.

Merlin then didn't hold back, spinning Belial around twice before throwing him heavily to the ground!

A loud "boom" echoed, the ground cracked, creating a depression where Belial's figure had been.

"Cough! Ah!" Belial's eyes widened, his whole body shook, and he immediately coughed up blood, clearly suffering a major injury.

Merlin grabbed Belial's terrified ankle, pulled him into the air, and then followed, shattering the ground as he chased after him.

"啧!"

Belial's mouth was full of blood, he flapped his fly wings to stabilize himself in the air, but Merlin's pursuit was immediate.

Merlin's fist was like an angry lion, roaring as it slammed into Belial's face. In an instant, Belial lost count of how many teeth he had lost.

Belial's nose bled profusely, but Merlin, like a madman, pressed the attack—

One punch, two punches, three punches...

Merlin became increasingly fierce, while Belial was beaten to the point of being unable to fight back, his body continuously flying higher and higher into the sky!

The two's entangled figures grew increasingly distant, only the heavy impact sounds echoing, like rolling thunder.

Alice was speechless, looking up at the sky, unable to estimate how high Merlin had beaten Belial. She only knew their figures looked like tiny ants, with only sharp gusts of wind indicating the intense battle between the two demons.

"...." Margaret was already stunned, seeing Merlin display his divine power and completely suppress Belial. She began to admire him. If this man became the imperial son-in-law, he might be more useful than 100 legendary magic cannons. What method could she use to make him fall for her?

If Alice knew the little princess she was rescuing was having a crush from afar, she would regret coming to save her and be so angry she would turn white. She came to save people, not to create a love rival for herself.

"Er ah ah ah ah ah!"

Belial clumsily fell from the sky, "Plop" landing on the ground, as if he had sunk into the earth.

After being thoroughly beaten by Merlin, Belial was indeed seriously injured, his bones seemed to have broken several, twisted into a mess.

Excluding Merlin this anomaly, Belial's physical strength was already very good among Demon Lords, and he could even absorb attacks to replenish himself.

But he still couldn't withstand Merlin's relentless attacks, his body was really struggling.

Merlin followed from the sky, looking at Belial who was motionless in the ground, slowly walking up to him. "Satisfied? Now can you listen to me?"

"...Cough cough!" Belial coughed a few times, dragging his somewhat crippled body up, wiping the blood from his mouth. "You... this... are really a monster..."

"Aren't you the one who said I was a failure? So now? Do you understand the gap between us, you so-called true demon?" Merlin smiled ambiguously, as if mocking Belial.

"I still think you're a failure, foolish..." Belial suddenly stood up, placing his hand on Merlin's chest, a massive power gathering. "Do you know I can absorb the enemy's attack power? Why are you still fighting me so hard? You're digging your own grave! I'll return your power plus mine to you!"

The massive power suddenly erupted, emitting a dazzling destructive white light, directly blasting Merlin away!

The fierce white light was rapidly expanding, destroying the mountain gorge in an instant, swallowing everyone present with this power.

From a distance, the originally unstable mountain gorge instantly turned to powder, a huge mushroom cloud rising into the sky, the ground shaking, and the incomparable impact force flipping the earth upside down!

The capital city, the Cathedral of O'Brien.

With the force of Belial's final attack reaching here, it began to shake violently as well.

The Cathedral of O'Brien swayed left and right, the survivors felt the oppressive power and couldn't help but kneel on the ground, unable to stand up!

Blaze, Joan, and Archbishop Scott all knelt on the ground, overwhelmed by this unstoppable pressure, their hearts filled with fear.

Archbishop Scott was already old, rolling around on the ground comically, truly believing the end of the world and the sky collapsing.

"What... what's happening!? "

"Why is there such a big commotion! "

"Is the goddess angry?*"

(( A)))

title: Chapter 36 — The Unkillable Weirdo
content:
Chapter 36 — The Unkillable Weirdo

Volume 17 · Chapter 36

The mountain ravine had been leveled to flat ground, and the dust that filled the sky was scattered by the howling wind.

From above, the terrain had completely changed, and the enormous crater inspired awe and dread.

"...Beelzebub coughed once, then slowly dragged himself up from the ground. Seeing that Merlin had vanished, he secretly rejoiced, thinking he had blown his enemy to bits. 'Hahaha, you fool! Serves you right for daring to challenge me. How does it feel?'"

Margaret had been thrown far away, and it was only thanks to the cage’s protection that she hadn’t been crushed by falling rocks. Now, she crouched inside it, trembling nonstop, terrified by Beelzebub’s monstrous power.

...What kind of monster is this?

In the distance, the rubble shifted. Alice struggled to crawl out from beneath the debris, scanning the area for any sign of Merlin.

Fortunately, she had been far enough away to only suffer minor injuries from the aftermath.

Alice couldn’t find Merlin anywhere, and her heart immediately leapt into her throat, filled with worry.

Where is Merlin...?

...He couldn’t have been defeated, could he...?

Alice refused to believe Merlin would lose, but the sheer power of Beelzebub’s final outburst had been overwhelming. Even she couldn’t help but doubt—though Merlin’s body was incredibly resilient, could he really have survived that last strike?

Panic set in, and Alice spun in place, her heart burning as if scorched by flames. She was terrified something had happened to him.

That idiot—why didn’t he just use Draw Slash? Why did he have to fight Gluttony up close? What if something went wrong?

Alice’s lips trembled, but no words came out. Tears welled in her eyes.

*Whoosh!* Stones flew as Merlin suddenly shot up from beneath the rubble, standing tall but with his head lowered, his expression grim.

His upper clothes were reduced to a few tattered strips, the rest utterly destroyed, revealing his solid torso. Merlin’s muscles weren’t exaggerated, but they were well-defined. The scar over his heart and chest was shocking, the mark spreading toward his arms.

After taking Beelzebub’s counterattack head-on, Merlin had sustained injuries. His front was riddled with wounds, as if slashed by countless blades, slowly oozing dark red blood.

"Merlin?!" Alice’s eyes widened. It was the first time she had ever seen him injured. Though the wounds weren’t fatal, the sight of blood was unprecedented.

This could only mean one thing—other Demon Lords *could* harm Merlin. His body wasn’t invincible; it had its limits.

"...!"

Margaret pressed her lips tightly together and hurried to the front of the cage, staring at the distant figure of Merlin standing once more. Her mind was in turmoil.

...This has to be a joke.

How could he still stand after taking such a devastating blow?!

Was this man really just a Black Iron-ranked adventurer? Just who in the world was he?!

Margaret’s heart pounded wildly. She was increasingly convinced that Merlin was the man she had been waiting for, and she couldn’t escape the thought.

"...Impossible!" Beelzebub staggered back half a step, utterly stunned by Merlin’s revival. "You took a double strike—you shouldn’t be able to stand! ...Are you a monster?!"

"Tch!" Merlin gritted his teeth against the pain, lifted his defiant head, and forced out a smirk of unmatched arrogance. "A monster? Maybe."

"Ugh!" Beelzebub finally felt the pressure. His full-force counterattack hadn’t killed Merlin—it was unthinkable. "With this kind of resilience, how could you possibly be something Lucifer the Second birthed using succubus power?! You’re some kind of freakish mutant!"

"Don’t drag my mom into this. You gonna fight or not?" Merlin rubbed his aching neck and taunted, "Is that all you’ve got? Disappointing..."

Beelzebub’s face flushed red. That was *his* line! And now Merlin was throwing it back at him.

His body was already at its limit. If he kept fighting, there would be no good outcome.

What the hell was going on? Why was this brat’s body so damn tough? It was impossible to take him down!

That cunning woman, Lucifer the Second—what exactly had she done? Could it be that from the very beginning, she had planned to gestate a monster in her womb?

During her pregnancy, she had rambled on about how her child would be the hero of the Age of Gods, that he would correct the world...

Beelzebub’s mind raced, forcing himself to recall Lucifer the Second’s ravings. Could the thing she had birthed truly be a monster that even the gods would fear?

Seeing Beelzebub’s lack of response, Merlin assumed he had given up and charged forward. "Don’t think playing dumb will save you!"

"Wai—"

Before Beelzebub could even call for a stop, Merlin’s fist crashed into him, sending him flying. He spat out a mouthful of blood.

Beelzebub’s body soared backward, embedding into the earth like an ostrich, his bones snapping in countless places, his form twisted.

"...!" Merlin lifted his head, gazing at the dark sky, and let out a long breath. Finally, he had taken down the troublesome Beelzebub. Without using Draw Slash, it had taken far more effort than he’d expected.

Margaret’s face was frozen in shock. She had thought being rescued would be enough, but the golden-haired man in the distance had actually defeated Beelzebub—far exceeding her expectations.

This man... she *had* to bring him to her side. Someone capable of defeating a Demon Lord alone? His strength was comparable to that of a powerful empire!

If he could be made to serve France, the empire would face no threats for a hundred years!

But... how could she seduce him? It seemed like an impossible task...

Just because he saved me, does that mean I should offer myself to him? That’s far too cliché...

Margaret’s mind raced, already scheming ways to marry Merlin and make him the empire’s son-in-law. It would be the perfect solution.

Alice rushed over and carefully examined Merlin’s injuries. "How are you? Are you okay?"

Merlin turned to see Alice’s worried and anxious expression, and a warmth he couldn’t explain spread through him. He casually replied, "No problem. I’m fine. Though dealing with other Demon Lords will take a bit more effort."

"...You don’t *look* fine at all!" Alice stared at his wounds, her voice laced with distress. "These don’t seem minor..."

"They’re just superficial. Nothing serious. I’ll be better after a few days of rest." Merlin waved her off, signaling her not to worry.

In the distance, Margaret, still trapped in her cage, wore a sour expression. Watching Merlin and Alice’s somewhat intimate exchange, her heart churned as if a bottle of mixed emotions had been overturned.

Who *was* that woman? She had just stood by the whole time, watching like an extra, refusing to help, and now she had the nerve to rush over and act concerned? She was even more hypocritical than Margaret herself!

Ahhh, could it be that man had already been taken by someone else?!

No way... This was making her anxious...

That woman was in the way. She had to find a way to drive her off, or it would be nearly impossible to win that man over.

title: Chapter 37 — Schemes Upon Schemes
content:
Chapter 37 — Schemes Upon Schemes

Volume 17 · Chapter 37

"Honestly, don’t do such dangerous things next time." Alice said in a reproachful tone.

"What? Are you worried about me?" Merlin looked at her strangely.

...No! Alice’s face turned red as she covered up, "It’s just that you’re being ridiculous. You could’ve just drawn your sword and slashed, but instead you chose to brawl with the enemy. Are you out of your mind...?"

"You’re human, you don’t understand the rules of the demon race. We demons are few in number, so when conflicts arise, we settle them with a fight—there’s no need to kill each other." Merlin explained. Compared to the human population, the number of demons was indeed minuscule. Coupled with their low reproductive capacity, demons generally avoided fighting to the death.

"...Is that so..." Alice somewhat understood. She glanced at Beelzebub, who was sprawled on the ground, and suddenly said, "Now that the Gluttony Demon Lord is defenseless, this is a perfect opportunity!"

"What kind of opportunity?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"We can easily kill Beelzebub, right? If we act now, it’s still not too late. Once he recovers, he’ll be much harder to deal with." Alice itched to act, her words carrying a hint of taking advantage of someone in distress. Besides, Beelzebub was a notorious evildoer—there was no need for sympathy.

"Don’t do that. I’ve already defeated him; there’s no need to kill him." Merlin shook his head, not particularly eager to take action.

Alice glanced at Merlin, her heart fluttering with unease. Was Merlin reluctant to eliminate Beelzebub because they were both demons? Did he still feel a sense of kinship with demons? If so, wouldn’t her own position be awkward?

Alice felt a pang of anxiety, suddenly realizing that even after living with Merlin for so long, they still weren’t truly on the same path.

"Why won’t you kill him? Is it because he’s also a demon?" So that’s why you refuse?

"What nonsense are you spouting?" Merlin shot Alice a sidelong glance and explained helplessly, "Beelzebub and I are both monarchs, each commanding vast demon legions. He snuck out this time. If he dies out here, the demon race will fall into chaos. The situation might become uncontrollable, even leading to war."

"...I see..." Alice nodded in understanding. Though she still had doubts about Merlin, for the sake of stability, Beelzebub couldn’t be killed.

"Alright, let’s not waste time here. Let’s take that princess back." Merlin walked straight toward Margaret, who was locked in a cage.

"And... what about Beelzebub? Just leave him here?" Alice asked curiously.

"Don’t worry about him. I won, so he won’t cause any more trouble. Rest assured." Merlin had triumphed in their struggle, so Beelzebub had to obey. Though it was a bit heavy-handed and unreasonable, this was the rule among demons—even Demon Lords followed it.

Alice turned back to look at the motionless Beelzebub. Was it really fine to leave him here? Once he recovered, wouldn’t he start wreaking havoc again?

Inside the cage, Margaret saw Merlin and Alice approaching. She quickly straightened her clothes to appear more dignified, her mind racing.

Here they come! How should I get close to this man? First, I need to find ways to have more physical contact.

If this man isn’t completely dense, he’ll surely be captivated by my charm. Heh heh...

Margaret was lost in her fantasies, but when Merlin and Alice stepped closer, she noticed their Adventurer’s Guild cards—marked with "married"!

Margaret felt as if she’d been struck by lightning. Instantly, she was overwhelmed, her heart churning with frustration, as if she’d swallowed a fly. Disgusting.

...So someone had beaten her to it! They were actually married! How was she supposed to interfere now?

Was she, the empire’s one and only princess, supposed to shamelessly become a third wheel and break them up? That wouldn’t be right, would it?

Merlin broke the bars of Margaret’s cage and reached out a hand to pull her up. "Princess, we’re here to rescue you. Let’s return to the royal capital together."

Margaret lifted her head, glancing at Merlin, then at Alice beside him. She made up her mind—so what if they were married?

This man was so powerful; she absolutely had to win him over. Besides, wasn’t it common for men to be tempted by new women? She’d just have to steal him away.

So Margaret squeezed out a few crocodile tears, putting on an act of being utterly terrified and helpless.

"Princess? What’s wrong?" Alice saw Margaret acting strangely, cowering in the cage and refusing to come out. She couldn’t help but ask in confusion.

But then, Margaret suddenly stood up and threw herself into Merlin’s arms, clinging to him and sobbing as if she’d suffered a great injustice.

"Uh! Wh—" Merlin furrowed his brows. Truthfully, he wasn’t very fond of women, but kicking her away would make him seem ungentlemanly. Besides, she was the empire’s princess—he had to give her some face.

Margaret was full of schemes. Playing the victim, she shamelessly sought sympathy, pretending to be deeply traumatized. She cried with pearl-like tears, burrowing herself into Merlin’s chest.

But that wasn’t all. The most unbearable part was Margaret’s ample chest pressing directly against Merlin, bumping into him as she clung tightly.

At that moment, Merlin’s upper body was bare, and the softness against his chest left him utterly speechless, the awkwardness overwhelming.

"Finally, someone has come to save me... I was so scared. That demon was always so fierce with me, wahhh..." Margaret buried her face in Merlin’s chest and began to pour out her grievances in a whimpering voice.

Seeing this, Alice was furious. Her eyes burned with rage as she glared at Merlin, her cheeks puffed up as if she might explode at any moment, silently screaming:

*Die, die, die! Stay away from Merlin! Don’t think you can do whatever you want just because you’re a princess! Don’t you understand first come, first served?! Have some self-respect, can’t you?!*

"Ahhh... I’m so scared... If you hadn’t appeared, I might have died here. Only your warm chest can comfort me... Please, don’t push me away..." Margaret sniffled, her words so pitiful that anyone who heard would think she’d been terrified out of her wits.

Alice’s face darkened to an extreme degree, her anger surging. She then turned her furious gaze onto Merlin, venting her frustration. Merlin felt the heat of her glare and became flustered. *What does this have to do with me?* It was *this woman* who threw herself at him—why was Alice mad at *him*?

Merlin sighed, "You’re safe now. Beelzebub has already been defeated by me."

"But whenever I recall Beelzebub’s fierce expression, I’m still terrified. Please, let me hold on for just a little while longer..."

"No!" Alice snapped.

Margaret looked up at Alice, feigning difficulty. "It seems the princess is truly shaken. Shouldn’t we let her be for now?"

Merlin glanced between Alice and Margaret. The latter’s trembling appearance didn’t seem like an act, so he had to suppress his own jealousy. "Do as you please."

Margaret secretly opened her eyes, a subtle, triumphant smile creeping across her face. Being able to cling to Merlin like this made her heart bloom with joy.

*Heh heh heh, winning this man over seems very promising!*

*If I keep pressing my body against his like this, I refuse to believe he won’t be moved.*

*And this man’s body is so warm... Holding him gives me such a sense of security. I wish I could stay like this forever...*

But—

title: Chapter 38 — Strife on the Carriage
content:
Chapter 38 — Strife on the Carriage

Volume 17 · Chapter 38

Merlin and Alice drove the carriage they had arrived in, taking Margaret back to the royal capital with them.

Yet along the way, Margaret completely ignored Alice’s presence and instead clung to Merlin relentlessly.

This left Alice feeling unbalanced—her expression had been sour the entire journey, but she couldn’t exactly lash out. After all, Margaret was supposedly still in shock.

Normally, the seat beside Merlin was always Alice’s. Now, Margaret had shamelessly taken it for herself, leaving Alice stuck at the back of the carriage.

No matter how you looked at it, Alice seemed to be getting bullied by Margaret, unable to even defend her own spot.

Alice suppressed the jealousy rising in her heart, nearly at her boiling point, hoping Margaret would have some self-awareness and stop clinging to Merlin.

“Lord Merlin, you’re not wearing a shirt right now. Would holding you make me feel warm?” Margaret, now knowing their names, addressed him with growing intimacy.

“No.” Merlin replied coldly, then added, “And could you stop pressing your chest against my arm? It’s making it itch.”

“Haha, Lord Merlin, you’re so funny…” Margaret’s face flushed as she leaned close to his ear. “Doesn’t this feel nice?”

“If I had the chance, I’d kick you out of this carriage in a heartbeat.” Merlin rolled his eyes, thoroughly annoyed by her clinginess.

Margaret froze, her expression stiffening. *What? Did I misread the situation? Am I not pretty enough? I’m at least better than that flat-chested girl in the back who stuffs her bra, right? How can I be the one making the first move and still get rejected? Is this guy some kind of steel-straight man?*

Alice, listening from the back, heard Margaret shamelessly flirting with Merlin. The fuse to her powder keg of rage was instantly lit. Furious, she snapped, “Princess, have some dignity! Stop rubbing your vulgar chest against him! As royalty, you should at least know basic shame!”

“Huh?” Margaret knitted her delicate brows, glancing at Alice with a dismissive look. “What does it have to do with you? Mind your own business, would you?”

“H-How does it *not* have to do with me?! I’m right here! Don’t be so shameless!”

Alice’s voice dripped with hostility. From the start, she had felt this princess was like a vixen seducing Merlin. Now, she wasn’t even bothering to hide it—brazenly tempting him right in front of her.

Fortunately, Merlin had never been particularly interested in women, and his unmoved, mountain-like demeanor pleased Alice greatly. If he had succumbed to the temptation, she might have exploded on the spot.

“Hehe~” Margaret wore a smug expression, as if she had seen through everything. “I think you’re just jealous of me.”

“....”

Alice felt overpowered, stammering, “J-Jealous of *you*?!”

“Jealous of my figure, of course. I don’t need to stuff my bra to feel satisfied.” Margaret’s words were laced with implication, and she didn’t forget to thrust out her impressive chest in a provocative gesture. She knew her advantages—she couldn’t compare in strength, but in looks? The other woman was nothing.

“Y-You—?!”

Alice’s face darkened as if struck by lightning, her heart taking a brutal hit.

She was, at the very least, the original wife! How could she tolerate this vixen flaunting herself in front of her? And to have the audacity to look down on her! If Margaret weren’t an imperial princess, Alice would have lost her patience long ago!

Alice’s entire body tensed, her pupils flickering with occasional flashes of gold. She itched to unleash her dragon’s might and scare this little princess to death.

“...So what if your figure is good? What’s so great about that?”

“A good figure, a gentle personality—it means I can do whatever I want. Men all love girls like me.” Margaret didn’t forget to shoot frequent glances at Merlin. “Isn’t that right, Lord Merlin…?”

Merlin’s face remained blank, a bead of sweat sliding down his forehead. *What the hell are these two idiots doing? Did they eat too much and have nothing better to do? There are far more important things to deal with right now, and they’re just bickering like this?*

“...Lies! Merlin would *never* like a lowly woman like you, reeking of male hormones!” Alice viciously insulted Margaret, boasting, “Merlin and I have been together for ages. I know him best, hmph~!”

Margaret felt a pang of frustration. It was true—she couldn’t compare to Alice.

After all, she had been so “enthusiastic” this whole time, yet Merlin hadn’t reacted at all. It seemed his eyes were only for this flat-chested wife of his.

But Margaret refused to give up. She had finally met a powerful and handsome man, someone capable of protecting the empire. How could she let him slip away so easily?

Even if he was another woman’s husband, if she could steal him away, it would just prove her charm was overwhelming.

Margaret, a princess, was actually willing to stoop to such despicable acts—proof of how highly she valued Merlin.

“So what? As long as Lord Merlin belongs to me in the future, that’s all that matters. I should even thank you for taking care of him for me~”

“....” Alice was left speechless. She wasn’t afraid of unreasonable people, but she *was* afraid of shameless ones. This was the first time she had ever met a princess this brazen—it made her grind her teeth in fury.

“Ah~, Lord Merlin, why not consider kicking that pitiful woman to the curb and marrying me instead? My father the emperor would certainly approve.”

Margaret rested her head on Merlin’s shoulder, sending him every possible hint.

“Hey! Are you ever going to stop?! How much longer are you going to cling to him?! Your emotions are stable now, right?! Let go and get away from Merlin!” Alice was seething, the veins on her forehead bulging.

“Lord Merlin hasn’t said anything. What’s the point of you shouting over there?” Margaret had no intention of letting go.

Alice suddenly stood up, her fists clenched tight. This was the first time she had encountered someone so thick-skinned, openly seducing Merlin right in front of her. It was torture.

“....What are you going to do?” Margaret broke out in a cold sweat, wondering if Alice had lost control and was about to hit her. She hesitated, considering whether to ask Merlin for protection.

But to her surprise, Alice simply sat down on Merlin’s other side, immediately wrapping her arms around his, yanking him toward her. “You little vixen, get your hands off him! Merlin and I are this close—there’s no room for you!”

“What gives you the right to tell me what to do? The choice is Lord Merlin’s…” Margaret refused to back down, pulling Merlin back into her own embrace.

Sandwiched between the two women, Merlin looked utterly exasperated, rolling his eyes in frustration. The carriage even began to swerve, weaving in an S-shaped path.

“You two are so annoying. Can you just shut up for a second?”

Alice: “Did you hear that? I said get lost! You’re the annoying one!”

Margaret: “She’s clearly talking about *you*—stop causing trouble!”

Merlin turned to Margaret, his expression serious. “Your Highness, your emotions are stable now, right? Then please stop clinging to me. I’m begging you.”

“Okay.” Margaret immediately let go, putting on an obedient front. But in her mind, she thought, *What the hell? Why does he want me to leave? Does Lord Merlin have zero attraction to me? Is he… not into women at all?*

“Alice…” Merlin turned to the other side, looking at Alice.

“Sniff…” Alice lifted her head, her eyes glistening with tears, looking pitiful, weak, and wronged.

“....” Merlin’s expression froze, and a waterfall of black lines cascaded down his forehead. He hesitated, thinking, *Alice… maybe I should just let this go.*

If he told her to leave too, she’d definitely throw a tantrum.

Besides, he didn’t *hate* having this annoying woman next to him. Whatever. Let her be.

title: Chapter 39 — Long-Term Planning
content:
Chapter 39 — Long-Term Planning

Volume 17 · Chapter 39

Merlin hesitated for a moment before deciding not to say anything to Alice. After all, to avoid trouble, it was better to stay out of Alice's way... However, Merlin still didn't like being held by others, so he had to speak in a softened tone. Alice's hair... Merlin kept quiet, too lazy to argue with Alice, having long gotten used to her temperament. Gret, seeing how lenient Merlin was with Alice, immediately felt unhappy. It seemed she had acted too hastily. Indeed, he still preferred his wife. Despite her good figure, she had no advantage in matters of the heart. She would have to think of another way. "My lord, do you know who we are?" Merlin turned to Margaret and asked. With no one around, this was a good opportunity to gather information. "Aren't you the reinforcements sent to save me?" Margaret replied tentatively. In a sense, that was true. But the two of us are wanted criminals. Didn't you notice?" Merlin tried to remind Margaret. "Eh..." Margaret suddenly stopped, thinking carefully about recent events and gradually piecing things together. "You... are the adventurers from the Viscount of Vignyong, right?" "The assassination? Yes, what are your thoughts, my lord?" Merlin observed Margaret, still unsure of the imperial princess's attitude toward wanted criminals. "Thoughts? I have no thoughts. I now pardon your sins in the name of the French princess." Margaret spoke without any intention of pursuing the matter, instead wanting to collaborate with Merlin, a powerful individual. "So easily? That's too straightforward?" Merlin found Margaret surprisingly easy to deal with. "What else? You just saved my life, so I must repay you properly. With me, you can be assured of safety within the empire." Margaret looked down and said softly, "It's not like you killed a noble. Moreover, he was a hound of Mades. There's nothing to it. In a way, you even helped me." "I heard you have a very poor relationship with the imperial prime minister Mades? What's the reason?" Merlin pressed. "That Mades is a wolf in sheep's clothing. He has imprisoned my father and acts as the temporary administrator of the empire, brutally suppressing others. I am the only heir to the empire, the future queen of France. Do I need a reason to hate Mades?" "Of course not..." Margaret looked at Merlin, as if seeing a lifeline. "Lord Merlin, would you stand with me, help me kill Mades, and reclaim the throne?" "Control of the kingdom?!" Merlin was stunned, not expecting Margaret to be so direct, immediately trying to recruit him to eliminate Mades. It was a perfect match. He also needed to investigate the bloodline! Margaret highly valued Merlin, not only admiring him but also believing his strength could help her turn the situation around. A person who could single-handedly defeat the Gluttony Demon Lord would surely have no difficulty eliminating Mades. If she didn't seize this opportunity to maximize her benefits, Margaret would have wasted heaven's favor. "Of course, I won't let Lord Merlin work for nothing..." Seeing Merlin unmoved, Margaret moved closer again, deliberately pulling open her chest to flirt. "If Lord Merlin is willing to help me eliminate Mades's forces, I will grant you any wish... oh~" "Any wish?" Merlin frowned, glancing at Margaret's full chest, awkwardly thinking this woman's mind was full of pornography. What was she thinking? She was no different from a cheap woman in a tavern, thinking he would fall for such a trick so easily? "Little princess!" Alice, seeing Merlin's hesitation, secretly pinched his arm to warn him, almost giving him a debuff. "Huh?!" Merlin winced, turning to look at Alice, who had a dark face and a warning gaze. Though she didn't speak, he could feel her anger simmering. "What is this woman doing? I haven't done anything yet, and she's already angry. Where did this much jealousy come from?" Merlin rolled his eyes, helplessly pushing Margaret away and saying in a serious tone. "I'm sorry, my lady. I'm a man of principle. To be honest, we came here specifically for Mades." Pushed away by Merlin, Margaret felt a bit disappointed but still inquired. "What business do you have with Mades? My lady, have you heard of vampires?" Merlin changed the subject and asked. "Of course. As a child, I heard similar horror stories every night—immortal monsters that feed on human blood." Margaret answered calmly. "We have been investigating vampires along the way. Not long ago, we unexpectedly discovered that the lord of Avignon, Camilla, is a vampire. She is closely connected to Mades and likely holds a significant position, which is why we came to the capital..." Merlin briefly explained the essentials to let Margaret understand the situation. "Camilla is a vampire? Is that true?" Margaret showed a look of disbelief. After all, such creatures had always existed in stories. "It's true. We saw it with our own eyes. Camilla is very afraid of silverware and has secretly abducted many innocent humans. We can testify. However, the evidence is temporarily in the custody of your knight, Lord Blaze." Merlin said seriously. "Vampires..." Margaret frowned, feeling overwhelmed by the sudden influx of information, her mind a bit confused. A man who had almost taken over the entire empire was a terrifying monster? It was hard to believe. All this time, who had she been fighting against? Her opponent wasn't even human! Still having some doubts, Margaret couldn't promise Merlin anything yet and only replied. "Lord Merlin, let's discuss this properly once we return to the capital." Light Novel City, O'Brien Cathedral. Bishop Scott looked outside at the pitch-black night, completely unaware of Merlin and Alice's situation, and became increasingly pessimistic. "Sigh, the sun has set and they haven't returned yet. It's likely... more bad than good..." "You old fraud, what are you saying! The princess is absolutely safe!" Blaze was furious, grabbing Bishop Scott's collar and wanting to beat the old man. "With no news at all, the result is obvious, isn't it? Why are you angry at me?" Bishop Scott sweated coldly. "And what about the earlier tremor? It must have been intense fighting!" Blaze refused to believe in failure, which would mean Margaret's certain death. "It could also be the Gluttony Demon Lord getting angry and using absolute power to kill them." Scott muttered, sweating coldly. "You said Lady Alice was the former Hero, very resilient? How could she possibly be in trouble!" Blaze questioned. "Blaze, you can also see the gap between Lady Alice and the Gem Demon King. No matter how resilient she is, she can't be resilient forever! This time's luck might have run out, and Lady Alice and her little follower might already..." Bishop Scott looked hurt and sighed heavily. There was no Alice.贞德 looked up, gazing at the pitch-black sky outside the cathedral, her heart filled with worry—so long without returning: Alice had likely already died for her faith. Even if she was the former Hero, she couldn't defeat a true demon...

title: Chapter 40 — No Such Luck This Time?
content:
Chapter 40 — No Such Luck This Time?

Volume 17 · Chapter 40

Joan sighed deeply, feeling that her group had placed too much hope in Alice, leading to their current profound disappointment.

How could a hero who had been utterly defeated in the initial assault on the First Demon Lord Palace possibly defeat a true Demon Lord?

Although Joan disliked Alice, this false believer who had stolen her position as the Hero, recalling their days as Hero candidates together still brought a pang of sadness.

"Her Highness will definitely be fine! You old fraud, stop talking nonsense!" Blaze grabbed the collar of Bishop Scott's robe and yelled.

"Lord Blaze! Can't you just accept reality?!" Bishop Scott broke out in cold sweat, nearly collapsing under the stubbornness of this man.

"What are you doing?!" A soft but sharp voice cut through their argument. Joan and Bishop Scott turned to the classroom door, where Margaret had just appeared, running in with a group of students.

"I thought you were all so calm, but it turns out you're all in a complete mess." Joan was genuinely stunned, her heart trembling uncontrollably. Margaret had returned!? This meant... Alice had succeeded? It was unbelievable!

"Wha—? No way! She actually... she really came back! Are you a ghost or something?!" Scott couldn't believe his eyes. He had already convinced himself that Margaret was surely dead.

"Your Grace," Margaret coldly smiled, seemingly not forgetting the old man's opposition to her at the council. "You've only been away for a few days, yet you can't even recognize me now?"

"Ah—!" Scott, the bishop, became incoherent, pinching his own thigh hard, realizing it wasn't a dream. His heart was filled with shock—she had actually done it! They had truly rescued Margaret from the clutches of the gluttonous demon Belial! This was clearly an impossible mission. Although Alice's strength had increased significantly compared to before, it wasn't certain she could defeat the gluttonous demon Belial.

I've seen Belial's power with my own eyes. That was a monster that even the near-total forces of the capital city couldn't defeat. How could they have defeated a true Demon Lord in just about two years? Perhaps Alice had used some special technique to defeat the Demon Lord? Or maybe she had an incredible stroke of luck, barely surviving and managing to rescue someone? No wonder she was the one who had survived the First Demon Lord Palace. Her luck was truly exceptional... Bishop Scott was filled with doubts and couldn't fathom how Alice had accomplished this. He couldn't have guessed it was all her doing.

"Your Highness!" Blaze, seeing Margaret return alive, was overjoyed and immediately limped forward to bow. "...Blaze, you're still alive, that's truly fortunate." Margaret looked at the thick bandages around Blaze's abdomen. "When I saw you pierced through the stomach by Belial, I thought you were surely dead. Now seeing you standing before me alive is something worth celebrating."

"Your Highness..." Blaze was tearful, having countless words in his heart but now not knowing what to say. "You've finally come. If anything happened to you, how could I explain it to the unconscious King?"

Margaret found this somewhat odd and asked, "Can you see my father now? Didn't Medes's subordinates stop you?"

"We can see the King now, though he hasn't awakened yet. As for that bastard Medes? He fled with his subordinates the very moment he lost! Now you are our only pillar of support." Blaze said with indignation.

"Fled!?!" Margaret was internally shocked. Combined with Merlin's revelations about the vampire clan, she began to suspect Medes had left out of fear. "Yes, I went to Medes's residence at the Prime Minister's office immediately after waking up, but it was already empty. No one knew where he had gone from the capital city. It seemed he left through a very secret passage," Blaze said seriously.

"..." Margaret furrowed her brows, feeling the situation was full of questions. "I heard Medes's identity was suspicious. Is that true?"

"Ah, forgive me, I almost forgot an important matter." Blaze took out the temporarily保管ed letters from his chest and handed them to Margaret. "Your Highness, these are from two adventurers from Britannia. They are letters between Medes and Camilla. The content is very suspicious and might be related to the legendary blood monsters. Please have a careful look."

Margaret opened the envelope and read carefully. Her face grew increasingly grim, and she was so angry she trembled all over. Until now, Margaret had simply thought Medes wanted to rebel and seize France for himself. Now it seemed the matter wasn't so simple. This prime minister seemed to be secretly working on many things. Medes fleeing the capital city at night didn't align with the interests of seizing France. He should have fought Belial to the death. Perhaps seizing France wasn't the ultimate goal, but something like "for the revival of my clan" as mentioned in the letter. Moreover, the letter mentioned a large number of human trafficking activities. What did Medes need so many slaves for? If Merlin was right and Medes was a vampire, then everything made sense, after all, they needed to "feed." While Medes fleeing might be due to fear of Belial's power, it could also be because he was guilty. Why would a demon lord attack the capital city and claim someone had kidnapped his sister? No way... Margaret quietly folded the letter, her face full of anger, and gritted her teeth, "We... have been played by that bastard Medes. Not just us, even Belial was played... What does that mean?" Blaze scratched his head and said seriously, "Medes is really a vampire?"

"Not certain, but definitely has close ties to vampires. Our struggle with the gluttonous demon might have been orchestrated by Medes to make us both lose. However, he probably didn't expect us to be so useless, so he fled at night. Medes is afraid of Belial..." Margaret speculated, though she wasn't sure either.

"Damn it! So many knights died in vain! Even Robert! It was all because of this bastard! I'll definitely kill him!" Blaze clenched his fists, his veins bulging on his forehead from anger.

"It seems Medes isn't human after all. He abandoned so many innocent people so easily. The Goddess will punish him. The Holy Church will not tolerate such an evil man causing chaos!" Bishop Scott said seriously.

Just as Margaret was about to say something, Joan suddenly stepped forward and asked, "Your Highness, how did you escape?"

"Escape? That demon locked me in a cage. How could I escape? I was rescued after defeating the gluttonous demon." Margaret smiled.

"What?!" Joan's eyes widened, finding it utterly unbelievable. Defeating the gluttonous demon? Had Alice's strength reached such a level?! Indeed, there was an insurmountable gap between them!

"Cough cough! I told you, Alice, as the former Hero, has an incomparable strength that ordinary people don't have. She surely lived up to expectations. I actually admire her!" Bishop Scott quickly changed his face, instantly forgetting how he had previously belittled Alice—

Oh my! This is truly unbelievable! This time, Alice didn't rely on luck to get through. She actually rescued Margaret! So it seems Alice does have some skills, capable of defeating the gluttonous demon... No, I need to find a way to bring her back and make her the Hero again! Then our O'Brien Cathedral would have two Heroes who defeated Demon Lords in a row. That would be wonderful! I'm sure the Pope would look at me differently and send us a lot of money. Hehehe... (??ω??)

title: Chapter 41 — Stars Embrace the Moon
content:
Chapter 41 — Stars Embrace the Moon

Volume 17 · Chapter 41

"Did... did you really pull it off?" Blaise's eyes widened in shock. He felt his strength was on par with Alice's, yet while he had been instantly killed by Beelzebub, Alice had somehow won. It was unimaginable.

"Alice?"

Margaret furrowed her brows. Everyone kept talking about Alice, but no one mentioned Merlin at all. It left her utterly confused.

After all, during the fight against Beelzebub, Merlin had done all the work. Alice had just stood by and watched...

Margaret felt she had to set the record straight. Otherwise, everyone would think Merlin was just some irrelevant bystander.

"What does Alice have to do with it? It was Lord Merlin who defeated Beelzebub and rescued me."

At these words, the expressions of the three froze on their faces, as if they had seen a ghost.

"Th-that... that black iron adventurer by Alice's side?" Jeanne's expression turned odd, a cold sweat trickling down her forehead. *Did I hear that wrong?* How could a black iron adventurer have the power to defeat a Demon Lord? This had to be a joke, right?

"That's impossible! Beelzebub is one of the seven sovereigns at the peak of the demon race. That black iron adventurer absolutely couldn't have done it!" Blaise thought Margaret was joking. He could believe Alice might have exchanged a few blows with Beelzebub, but as for Merlin... probably a single sneeze from Beelzebub would have scared the guy into wetting himself!

"Your Highness, if this is a joke, you should consider the occasion. A black iron adventurer defeating the Demon Lord of Gluttony? Who would believe that?" Archbishop Scott gave a dry chuckle, feeling that Margaret's joke was in poor taste.

"Why don't you believe me?"

Margaret furrowed her brows. It seemed these people had all been deceived by Merlin's appearance. He was the real powerhouse in the adventuring duo.

Just then, Merlin and Alice entered from outside, preparing to discuss their next steps.

Merlin had just been outside tying up his horse, with Alice following closely behind him.

Now, a fox spirit had suddenly appeared beside Merlin. Alice, ever vigilant, kept her eyes fixed on Merlin, refusing to take a single step away.

"Alice, could you stop staring at me like I'm a criminal..." Merlin muttered, feeling the pressure.

"No way. You look all proper on the outside, but who knows what you're really thinking?" Alice responded seriously in a hushed tone.

"...Merlin sighed, wondering what he had done to deserve this. He hadn't even made a mistake!

Jeanne rushed forward as soon as she saw Alice return. "Alice, did you really defeat Beelzebub?! How did you do it?"

Blaise, also puzzled, asked bluntly, "Yeah, Lord Alice, how did you manage it? Beelzebub is so powerful. Your strength clearly isn't enough to beat him!"

"This... Alice felt immense pressure. Sweat beaded on her forehead as she thought, *It wasn't me at all! It was all Merlin fighting Beelzebub...*

"Ahem!" Merlin cleared his throat, pointing at himself. "Don't be so surprised. I was the one who defeated Beelzebub."

Jeanne and Blaise turned to look at Merlin, who stood there with a slightly smug expression, his clothes tattered and bearing minor injuries. They immediately assumed he was boasting.

In their eyes, if Merlin had truly fought Beelzebub, he wouldn't have just minor injuries—he'd be a bloody, lifeless corpse!

So Jeanne and Blaise both turned away, ignoring Merlin completely, determined to get the truth from Alice.

"Alice, just tell us!"

"Yeah, Lord Alice, if possible, I'd really like to learn from you."

Merlin stood there, disheveled by the wind, feeling a deep sense of gloom. *I've been ignored again!* Why did these people only swarm around Alice? Couldn't they come fawn over him for once, let him experience what it felt like to be the center of attention?

"It wasn't me, it really was Merlin—" Alice started to point at Merlin, but she was immediately cut off.

"Don't be modest, Alice. It must be some incredibly powerful secret technique your teacher from the Great Snow Mountain passed down to you, right? Am I correct?" Jeanne thought this was highly plausible. After all, even back when she was a Hero candidate, Alice had boasted more than once about her teacher from the Great Snow Mountain.

"That makes sense! Lord Alice, you've been hiding your true strength! So you possess some kind of ultimate skill!" Blaise was utterly convinced. He thought it no wonder she could defeat Beelzebub. There were many powerful magics and martial arts in the world—perhaps Alice really did wield some terrifying power!

"...Alice was at a loss for words. She felt like nothing she said would make a difference. These people's imaginations were too wild. That wasn't what had happened at all!

From a distance, Margaret observed Merlin and Alice, and suddenly understood why no one had believed her when she said Merlin had defeated the Demon Lord of Gluttony.

Alice was sharp and capable, exuding an elite aura, and was a rare Mythril-ranked adventurer.

Merlin, on the other hand, seemed completely unmotivated, giving off the vibe of someone who despised the lower classes of society. He was just an unremarkable Black Iron adventurer.

When the two stood together, Merlin instantly became overshadowed, his presence dimmed by Alice's radiant light.

Who would believe he was the once-in-a-lifetime prodigy capable of defeating a Demon Lord? To anyone looking, such a feat had to be Alice's doing!

It seemed that because his wife was too dazzling, Lord Merlin had a tough time as well...

Margaret's gaze toward Merlin carried a hint of sympathy. Others might not understand Merlin's strengths, but she knew the truth.

Archbishop Scott saw a rare opportunity and quickly stepped forward, wearing a fawning smile. "Congratulations, Alice! This truly washes away past humiliations! You're the second person in history, after O'Brien, to have defeated a Demon Lord! This is a tremendous honor. You can now cast off all past disgrace and become a great figure recorded in the annals of the Holy Church! The Church will be proud of you. You've revitalized our morale!"

"Ah..."

Alice's face flushed, her expression awkward. She wasn't used to such praise from the red-robed Archbishop. Normally, Scott's words were laced with barbs, belittling her at every turn. Now he was suddenly showering her with flattery?

Alice averted her gaze, feeling as if she had inexplicably turned her fate around. She mumbled in an attempt to clarify, "It's not what you think. I really didn't do anything. How could I have defeated Beelzebub with my strength?"

"Alice, I could always tell you were a modest child. I never expected you to still have this virtue. Truly admirable..." Archbishop Scott nodded in satisfaction, his mind racing with calculations. "Rest assured, I will definitely report this to His Holiness the Pope. All your past mistakes will be wiped clean! And with you included, the legendary Ten Heroes might very well become eleven..."

"Eh?" Alice blinked, her heart stirring slightly. She asked tentatively, "I'm not interested in the Ten Heroes, but... will all my past mistakes be wiped clean? Including the debt from losing the inherited Hero armor?"

"Well..." Archbishop Scott hesitated. He truly didn't have the authority to decide that, but he was no stranger to making grand promises. "I think His Holiness the Pope values talent greatly, especially someone like you who can stand against the Demon Lords."

"As long as you're willing to return to the Holy Church and resume your role as the Hero guarding the Vatican..."

"I believe His Holiness the Pope won't be inflexible. It's not impossible for your debt to be wiped clean~"

title: Chapter 42 — Fiancé Merlin?
content:
Chapter 42 — Fiancé Merlin?

Volume 17 · Chapter 42

Seeing Archbishop Scott's elated expression, Alice immediately abandoned the idea.

She had originally thought there was a chance to clear the debt on her back, but in the end, it turned out they wanted her to go back and be a Hero?

Alice was definitely not willing. In the past, she would have been more than happy to return.

But now? She really wanted to be with Merlin and had no intention of being a Hero again, even if the astronomical debt made her scalp tingle.

Archbishop Scott thought the conditions he offered were great. With the Pope's approval, the money wasn't a big deal, and it would also allow the Church to once again have a Hero capable of defeating the Demon Lord. It was a win-win!

While Alice wasn't very willing, Merlin thought for a moment and said in a low voice, "Alice, I think it's okay."

"Okay your big head!" Alice glared at Merlin in anger, thinking this guy had no heart, wanting to get rid of her so badly?

"Think about it, we owe so much money, I don't know when we'll be able to pay it back. If you go back to be a Hero, I'll be free."

"You'll be free, but I'll be tied to the Church's war chariot. How selfish can you be? I've been good to you..." Alice frowned, full of resentment inside.

"I didn't finish. You go be a Hero, and I'll go to Vatican City and tie you back, so you'll be free too," Merlin rubbed his hands together, eager to try.

"Then won't I be unable to live in the open? Once exposed, I'll be pulled back to be a Hero again?"

Alice didn't like Merlin's bad idea. It seemed to benefit him the most.

"Didn't you always have a spirit of dedication? Can't you just help me out now?" Merlin was very eager for freedom.

"G, U, N! Don't even think about it. I'm going to watch you for the rest of my life and make sure you never do anything bad." Alice said grandly, not wanting to deal with Merlin. He could go back to his hometown and cause trouble, but she couldn't. It was completely unequal.

"... Merlin pouted, hands outstretched, thinking why was Alice so stubborn? It wouldn't be a problem to be a Hero for a while and then tie her back. It wasn't like he was leaving her alone.

"Hehe, Alice, what's your decision?" Archbishop Scott asked expectantly, seeing them whispering, thinking they had already discussed it.

"No, I don't want to go back to be a Hero." Alice answered firmly, having completely given up on returning to the Church. In the past, when she was alone, she could go anywhere, but now she was more concerned about Merlin and preferred to stay by the side of the person she liked. Fame and fortune weren't that important anymore.

"W...why?" Archbishop Scott's eyes widened in disbelief. He thought being a Hero wasn't something anyone could do; it was the highest honor, something many people would kill for! Although the quality of the later Heroes had declined sharply, they were still top-tier people with talent and character. He hadn't expected Alice to be so indifferent to the position of Hero now!

Even Joan beside him didn't understand, asking, "Alice, this is a rare opportunity to return to the Church. As long as you agree, you can become a Hero again and be revered by countless believers. Isn't that good?"

"No." Alice shook her head, completely unmoved.

"Alice, why!?" Joan frowned, seemingly hoping she would return instead of being a wandering adventurer.

"Do you know what it means to become a Hero again? If you refuse, you might never have the chance again."

"If it were before, I should have returned to the Church to be a Hero, but now..." Alice looked at Merlin and muttered, "It's better to give it up. I have other pursuits."

"Huh? ? ?" Merlin was full of questions, thinking why was this woman looking at him? Was it because of him that she didn't want to go back? Shouldn't... no way...

Seeing Alice looking at Merlin, Archbishop Scott thought he understood something and said, "Oh~, I see. Alice, don't worry, we'll also invite your husband into the Church. It should be no problem for him to be a cat servant in Vatican City. You can still be together."

"Ah? Stupid old man, what are you saying? I'll kill you..." Merlin's face darkened, thinking that as a Great Demon Lord, they dared to invite him into the Church. It was already a miracle they hadn't torn the Church apart. Cat servant? I'll beat you to death!

"Archbishop, Alice doesn't mean that. You've misunderstood." Joan looked at Alice's blushing face and was very puzzled inside. Could love change a person so easily? And this man called Merlin wasn't even that good! Black Iron Rank... where did he match Alice?

"Alice, what exactly are you dissatisfied with? Let's talk it over. Your strength is so strong now, it's a pity you're not working for the Church." Archbishop Scott said earnestly.

"There's nothing to talk about. Everyone has their own aspirations. I was driven out before, and now you want me to go back? I'm not that cheap..." Alice said seriously, but inside she thought, if Merlin didn't go back to be the Demon Lord, she definitely wouldn't go back to be a Hero. That would be fair.

"... Archbishop Scott sighed, regretting deeply that his little plan wasn't working.

"It's so much better to go back and be a Hero. Then I can finally be with Lord Merlin..." Margaret leaned in, looking at Merlin with stars in her eyes, as if she wanted to eat him.

"Your Highness?" Blaze frowned, thinking he had never seen the Princess be so enthusiastic about anyone before. Why was she being so nice to this Black Iron adventurer? Was she bewitched by his appearance?

"You don't stand a chance!" Alice stood in front of Merlin, preventing Margaret this little bitch from getting any closer!

"Hmph!" Margaret looked at Alice and thought this woman was really in the way. She changed her tone and said, "Since you saved me, I should reward you."

"... What do you want to do?" Alice had a bad feeling.

"In the name of the French Princess, I declare that Lord Merlin is my fiancé from today on. I will marry him!" Margaret didn't hide anything and immediately declared Merlin as the imperial son-in-law.

"What the hell!?" Archbishop Scott exclaimed, his wrinkles cracking.

"Your Highness! ... Isn't this too childish!?" Blaze's expression was like he had seen a ghost.

Joan remained calm on the surface, but inside she was shocked. What was going on? Why was even the imperial princess competing for this man? What kind of charm did he have?

"... Merlin had a numb expression, looking at Margaret like she was a monster. What was going on! ? I randomly became a fiancé! ? Was this princess's brain full of shit! ? Pr...丁“吮

"Invalid! What right do you have!?" Alice was so angry she was stomping her feet, ready to fight Margaret!

"Lord Merlin..."

Margaret hugged Merlin, rubbing her face against him, "We can become husband and wife in the future. You have to love me well~"

Merlin's face was dark, his body like it was petrified, feeling the situation was getting more complicated. What kind of karma had he accumulated!

"Shut up! We are the couple, you fox spirit, where did you come from!?" Alice started to emphasize their fake marital relationship.

"Wait, Alice, we aren't fake... Ugh! ?"

Merlin didn't even finish his sentence before Alice covered his mouth, not letting him explain. She was getting more and more excited instead.

"We have a 3-year-old child! He's very cute, and he's in Little Cow Town! Give up and die, you have no chance..."

"So what? I'm willing to be a concubine~" Margaret had already known Alice would have a strong reaction and was completely all in.

"You! ?"

Alice's face immediately darkened. She had never seen someone so shameless. She couldn't control her jealousy anymore.

She could see her magical aura fluctuating, and in the next second, the entire church was instantly frozen, as if it had entered deep winter.

"Fox spirit! Let go of Merlin!"

"If you dare to say he's your fiancé again..."

"I have nothing to do with you[  =

title: Chapter 1 — Dangerous Thought
content:
Chapter 1 — Dangerous Thought

Volume 18 · Chapter 1

Alice released a massive burst of cold air in her emotionally unstable state, freezing the entire O'Brien Cathedral as if it had suddenly been plunged into an icy wasteland. Except for Alice and Merlin, everyone else was covered in a layer of frost, making the atmosphere instantly awkward and the temperature unbearable.

Archbishop Scott, Joan, Margaret, and Blaze all shivered uncontrollably, feeling as though they had been transported to Siberia within mere seconds, freezing to death.

"... Margaret hugged herself, her eyebrows white with frost, too frozen to speak.

"Alice,... quickly retract your power!" Archbishop Scott's body couldn't withstand the cold for even a few seconds.

Merlin, being immune to magic, remained unaffected. However, seeing everyone shivering, he couldn't help but push Alice's hand away and say, "Alice, what are you doing?"

Alice retracted the cold air back into her body and huffed angrily, "Who let her talk nonsense? Hmph!"

"Tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue, saying helplessly, "About fiancés... it was definitely a joke. Why did you take it seriously?"

Joke... Alice thought about it for a moment, then puffed up her cheeks indignantly, refusing to admit her mistake.

"But I feel uncomfortable too!"

"I don't care about others, but it's unacceptable to joke about you!"

After defeating Beelzebub, the capital city temporarily returned to safety, no longer living in constant fear.

After all, Merlin had made a deal with Beelzebub that as long as he could defeat him, the demon would behave.

Although Beelzebub was a demon, he at least had some sense of honor and wouldn't cause trouble randomly anymore.

Moreover, as long as Merlin stayed in the capital, it might be the safest place in the world, with a very low probability of being attacked.

Even if Beelzebub intended to keep causing trouble, he would have to consider whether he could defeat Merlin.

Currently, France was in a semi-paralyzed state of chaos, unable to handle many issues, lacking any opportunity to restore the empire.

The old king remained unconscious, and Margaret had just returned, facing a difficult situation without a chance to stabilize the empire.

Medes had thrown the empire into turmoil, leaving behind a mess for everyone. He hoped that the more chaotic France became, the smoother his plan to establish the Eternal Night Empire would proceed, with no one able to stop him!

Margaret now began to suspect Medes' true identity, thinking he might not be human but a malevolent dark creature.

She realized that the empire's greatest enemy wasn't Beelzebub but the hidden Medes who manipulated everyone from the shadows, possibly even the vampires behind him.

Margaret had clashed with Medes several times and even organized assassination attempts, so she knew something about the man.

Given Medes' character, he wouldn't stir up trouble for no reason. The chaos in the empire wasn't his ultimate goal but a cover for his grand ambitions.

What did he want by kidnapping so many humans? Even daring to target the sister of the Demon Lord, what did "the revival of our race" mean?

Margaret couldn't figure it out, but her intuition told her that things weren't over yet. Perhaps greater chaos was brewing in the darkness, ready to engulf France completely.

Although Medes was currently the biggest threat to the empire's security, as long as this man lived, there would be unease.

But Margaret planned to think long-term, stabilizing the capital first. Given the current chaotic state, any attack would leave them defenseless. Fortunately, she had witnessed Merlin's strength. As long as he stayed in the capital, the empire would remain stable, with no one threatening royal authority.

So Margaret decided to stabilize this adventurer from Britannia, seeing him as a temporary lifeline to stabilize the empire.

In the pitch-black night, hoofbeats echoed, stopping near a mansion close to the palace.

The capital was still in chaos, with poor security.

Taking advantage of the empire's vulnerability after the Demon Lord's attack, many thieves emerged to wreak havoc, like wild dogs gnawing on corpses in ruins.

Even this mansion, used to host distinguished guests, now had its doors tightly shut, unlit, resembling a black inn in the dead of night.

"Gentlemen, will you rest here tonight? The capital has been devastated by the Gluttony Demon Lord, and this mansion is one of the few habitable places. Please don't mind," Blaze said awkwardly.

"It doesn't matter where we stay." Merlin glanced at the mansion outside, thinking it was better than sleeping on the streets.

"... Sir Merlin, why don't... I invite you to stay at the palace? ... It's much more comfortable there," Margaret said meaningfully, her body still trembling from Alice's cold air.

Merlin was about to decline when Alice angrily interrupted, "Thank you for your kindness, Your Highness, but no need! Let's go, Merlin."

"Humph!" Margaret pursed her lips, growing increasingly discontent, feeling that this woman was a stumbling block in her pursuit of Merlin, utterly annoying!

Merlin hesitated, seeing Alice step down from the carriage first, and followed suit. But he suddenly remembered something important and turned back to ask.

"Your Highness, how do you plan to handle Medes?"

"This guy must die. As long as he lives, the kingdom won't be safe. It's likely he kidnapped Beelzebub's sister, triggering this disaster..."

Margaret made her stance clear, but to confront Medes, she needed to seize control of the kingdom first.

Merlin frowned. Was Miranda kidnapped by Medes? It seemed finding this prime minister was becoming increasingly urgent. "Do you know where Medes fled to now? We also need to find him."

"This..." Margaret's heart skipped a beat, suddenly flashing a sweet smile. "Sir Merlin, don't worry. Stay here for now. Give me some time, and I'll find out where Medes went and give you a satisfactory answer."

"... Really?" Merlin looked at Margaret's smile, feeling that this woman wasn't someone to be underestimated, her words seeming frivolous and unreliable.

"Merlin, let's go!"

Seeing Merlin hesitate in the carriage, Alice assumed he was flirting with Margaret and angrily pulled him away.

The luxurious carriage started moving again. Once far from the mansion, Margaret finally spoke.

"Blaze, lend me your robe. It's too cold."

"Eh! Of course, Your Highness!" Blaze quickly took off his robe and draped it over Margaret.

"Phew, finally warm..."

Margaret sighed in relief, complaining, "That flat-chested weirdo, small chest, bad temper. If she didn't get in the way, I would have seduced Merlin already. How hateful!"

"That..." Blaze smiled awkwardly, unsure why Margaret liked Merlin, feeling it was inexplicable. "Your Highness, can you really find Medes?"

"No, I'm not a god. How could I know where that bastard fled?" Margaret said confidently.

"Why did you lie to them? Isn't that wrong?" Blaze felt that if Alice, who defeated the Demon Lord, got angry, it wouldn't be good.

"The empire is in chaos and can't afford another blow. We need them to stay and stabilize the situation, protect the kingdom. You're severely injured and useless right now," Margaret glanced at Blaze.

"... I see. Your Highness thinks deeply."

Blaze laughed foolishly, feeling embarrassed. The empire's strength was severely weakened, lacking protection.

If Alice could defeat the Gluttony Demon Lord, her power was undoubtedly immense.

If she stayed in the kingdom, it would be a great blessing!

But Blaze couldn't understand why, while wanting them to protect the kingdom, Margaret pursued Merlin's husband. What was she thinking? Wouldn't that make people hate her?

"Your Highness, when you said you wanted Merlin as a fiancé, it was a joke, right? Ha ha."

"Huh?" Margaret turned around, responding seriously without much thought, "Who's joking? I'm serious..."

"Eh?!!" Blaze was startled, not expecting Margaret to be serious. He inwardly criticized her for trying to keep Alice in the capital while pursuing her husband. Who would want to help? Alice must hate her! Speaking of which, what kind of love potion did Merlin give her to make her like such an unremarkable man? Even he felt it was like putting a flower in cow dung!

"Don't hold another tournament. I've decided to marry Merlin. He's my fiancé now." Although Margaret said it casually, she was sincere inside, feeling Merlin met all her requirements and was handsome, making him the perfect choice for a husband!

"Marry a Black Iron adventurer? The emperor will never agree!" Blaze felt Margaret and Merlin were mismatched, thinking her choice of fiancé was too casual!

"So what if he's a Black Iron adventurer? Merlin is much better than you think," Margaret said meaningfully. "This is my marriage. Even Father can't interfere."

"Your Highness, think carefully. Any young man who came to propose before was better than Merlin! As the heir of France, marrying an ordinary adventurer is a joke," Blaze said seriously, feeling Merlin was far beneath Margaret, and their relationship was doomed.

"Blaze, mind your own business. My affairs don't need your interference. You should think about how to make that woman leave Merlin instead," Margaret raised her eyelids, still not giving up on seducing Merlin.

Sigh, with that flat-chested woman around, I have no chance. She's truly annoying and hard to deal with.

How can I get closer to Sir Merlin and make him fall for me completely?

Should I take the initiative and reverse-seduce him?

title: Chapter 2 — Midnight Visitor
content:
Chapter 2 — Midnight Visitor

Volume 18 · Chapter 2

Blaze watched Margaret's infatuated state and couldn't help but sigh in exasperation.

This was bad. The usually calm princess had clearly lost her mind.

He had always thought the princess was too proud to easily favor anyone...

But now she had fallen for a lowly adventurer? It was simply unbelievable!

After all, the princess was the sole heir to the empire, her status immeasurably high, yet she had hesitated not at all to target another man's wife?

If the Emperor awoke and learned of this, he would probably faint from anger again!

Blaze felt the little princess he had been taking care of was getting crazier by the day. If Merlin were the prince of some small country, he wouldn't have let out so much as a fart.

The key was that Merlin was just a nameless, passing married adventurer. Margaret, as the future leader of the French royal family, how could they possibly be on the same level?

Margaret seemed uninterested in discussing Merlin with Blaze, but suddenly remembered another important matter. "Blaze, are Robert and Batiloka really dead?"

"Huh?" Blaze snapped out of his thoughts and replied with a somewhat sorrowful tone. "Yes, they're both dead."

Margaret looked away and comforted him. "You don't need to dwell on it too much. Becoming a knight always carries the risk of sacrifice. Medes, the mastermind behind this, will surely pay for his actions."

"Your Highness, I understand. Robert was my friend and a loyal warrior. To sacrifice himself for the kingdom's protection, I think he wouldn't regret it. But..." Blaze hesitated, thinking of Batiloka, whose mind had been consumed by madness.

"What is it?" Margaret glanced at Blaze.

Blaze paused for a moment, feeling that since the people were dead, holding onto past grudges wasn't worth it. He then sincerely said, "I think Batiloka should be cleared of his name. Although this guy was impulsive and disobedient, his nature wasn't entirely evil. That noble's son was causing trouble everywhere, and even the Emperor turned a blind eye. If it weren't for Batiloka killing him, more people might have been oppressed. Putting him in prison wasn't really fair."

Margaret closed her eyes and thought for a while before seriously replying, "It's not impossible. Now that power is being reshuffled, if I can take control of the empire, I will pardon Batiloka's crimes and bestow him with the honor of a martyr."

"Thank you for your grace, Your Highness." Blaze bowed slightly. Although he didn't have a good relationship with Batiloka, as a fellow officer, he had done his part in the end.

"But is the fire demon still inside Batiloka? That's a very rare魔兽 with intelligence, and it's important to the entire kingdom." Margaret was quite concerned about this creature.
