title: Chapter 10 — I'll Bring This Stick Down
content:
Chapter 10 — I'll Bring This Stick Down

Volume 18 · Chapter 10

Merlin and his group came out just to have a bite to eat; it wasn't anything particularly important.
Several days have passed, and there's still no word from Margaret's side; she probably hasn't found Mads's whereabouts yet.
Although Merlin was also a bit anxious, he decided to wait patiently.
Alice also came out, but hearing that Margaret had issued a notice, she went to check it out of curiosity and is temporarily not here.
Merlin ate melon while spitting out seeds, and glanced at Beelzebub.
Beelzebub has been relatively well-behaved these days; Merlin keeps an eye on him the whole time, so he couldn't possibly harm a single hair of Alice.
Beelzebub's face looked grim, as if everyone owed him eight hundred ten thousand, and seeing Merlin content with the status quo filled him with resentment.
“It's been days already, and that little princess still hasn't given any news—when exactly are we supposed to wait until?” “Don't be impatient, what's the use of rushing? The little princess is probably tied up with affairs; just wait a bit longer.” Merlin said, shaking his head, utterly lacking any sense of urgency.
“You're not in a hurry, but my sister has always been in danger—I can't wait much longer!” Beelzebub said, slamming the table in anger.
“What do you intend to do?” Merlin said, lifting his eyelids to size up Beelzebub.
“I think it'd be better to slaughter all the humans in France than to sit here doing nothing!” Beelzebub said fiercely.
“Would killing them all help find Miranda? Cut it out.” Merlin frowned, speaking solemnly, “She should be fine; if those people wanted to harm her, they'd have acted already. They must be waiting for something… or have another use?”
“I'm waiting for the last stretch; if there's still no clue, I'll first make that lying bitch bleed.” Beelzebub was referring to Margaret, a despicable human who has lied from the start and never told the truth.
“I'll go ask the princess myself; don't worry, come, have some melon.” Merlin handed Beelzebub a slice of watermelon.
“I eat meat, not vegetables, you bastard…” Beelzebub said through gritted teeth, clenching his fists silently.
“I recall you're never full, right? You must be starving now—make do for now. This royal city's been wrecked by you; where would you find meat to eat?” Merlin shrugged helplessly.
“Don't you have a prime prey right beside you? That should be enough…” Beelzebub said lowly with a meaningful tone, licking his lips, apparently eyeing Alice for days.
“Oh, then you can stay hungry; Alice is off-limits, she's not food.” Merlin's expression turned much colder, disliking Beelzebub always treating Alice as food.
“Hmph, I know—she's your wife, liking humans, that lowly species; the whole demon race only…” Beelzebub said sarcastically.
“Say what you will…” Merlin didn't bother explaining; as long as Beelzebub behaved, any trash talk was fine.
Beelzebub had been planning to insult Merlin a few more times, but then he saw a strange male wielding a staff approach from behind Merlin.
Who is that? Does Merlin know him? He looks weird… not a good guy…
Humphrey arrived behind Merlin under the gaze of his many subordinates, preparing to strike directly; his plan was as follows…
To take out Merlin with lightning speed, make a big commotion, and see if they could lure the swordsman who killed Oswald to join in the killing.
As for the ragged Beelzebub opposite him? He's likely just a smelly beggar come for scraps, skin and bones, whom Humphrey outright ignored.
Humphrey's grim face broke into a sinister grin as he raised his staff, golden magical power swirling around it, preparing to unleash a thunder strike!
Even if Beelzebub saw Merlin about to be hit, he remained silent, calmly raising his cup to sip tea, thinking, “Is this human crazy? Trying to ambush Lucifer? This pressure is pathetically weak—it couldn't possibly do anything, especially since he's just a mage…”
Humphrey's murderous grin grew more grotesque; at this moment he played out in his mind, over and over, the scene of blasting this black‑iron adventurer into mincemeat—
I have gathered 100% of my magical power into this staff; its destructive force is something no one could withstand!
Of course, this pitch‑black staff is no ordinary item; it's a rare treasure that would be worth over ten million gold coins even on the market!
This staff is forged from naturally formed black crystal, the toughest material, then tempered in hellfire for forty‑nine years, giving it a hardness surpassing that of mithril ore and doubling my magical power!
When I bring this staff down, it will surely shatter the heavens and rend the earth, making the whole royal city tremble! It must draw blood and claim a life!
Even if the three knights of France took this blow, they'd certainly not come away unscathed—they'd vomit three liters of blood and lose more than half their lives!
Though it's overkill to deal with a mere black‑iron novice, we have to do this to draw out that swordsman.
As the Azure Abyssal Flame, one of the four great dark guilds, we command respect on the road; anyone who dares kill my subordinates will not get off lightly!
Today you'll learn just how terrifying it is to provoke my guild! Wahahaha!
Humphrey laughed loudly, blue flames already igniting on his staff—a sign of highly condensed magical power—and then he brought it down hard!
Not far off, the members of Azure Abyssal Flame watched, holding their breath; this was a rare sight of the guildmaster's tentacles, and the next second could become a bloody scene.
As guildmaster, Humphrey could not easily let Merlin go; his subordinates were watching, and he wanted everyone to know that Azure Abyssal Flame is a terrifying organization not to be provoked.
Dong—
A muffled crack, like a wooden stick hitting a wooden fish.
No scene of heaven‑shattering, earth‑rending carnage appeared.
The magical staff, charged with power, had its energy completely dispelled as it neared Merlin.
In reality it was just a tiny staff that tapped Merlin on the back of the head.
A mage's destructive power comes from magic, yet none of it works against Merlin.
So mages in front of Merlin are essentially useless; would getting tapped hurt?
Merlin: HP‑1
“???” Eden.
“???” Laurie.
“???” Yuna and Vina sisters.
Everyone was full of question marks, unable to make sense of the situation; it felt like a joke, all that buildup for a dud.
Humphrey, as guildmaster, never unleashes an attack without shattering heavens and flooding rivers with blood—yet this time the result was completely unexpected.
Hmm? Wait, why isn't my magic working on this guy? It's just being mysteriously dispelled—what the hell…
Beelzebub calmly sipped his tea, thinking, “What an idiot—trying to take down Merlin with this? He'd need a million years' head start and the power of gods to even hurt him with magic.”
Merlin stiffened, not knowing whom he'd provoked while snacking on the street; he dropped the watermelon rind, stood up, and turned to stare at Humphrey.
Humphrey looked at his staff, then at Merlin, feeling deep confusion and panic; it was the first time his magic had failed him, and though his strength wasn't weak, even with magical defenses he couldn't possibly come away unscathed!
Merlin spat a watermelon seed at Humphrey's forehead with a “pah,” speaking in an accusatory tone—
“What gives you the right to hit my head?”
“Are you looking to die?”
(??◣ω◢)??
On that website's Moe Battle Grand Prix, everyone should vote for Alice alone, not for Merlin.
Don't rush the daughter; whenever everyone urges her, I get anxious.
It's not that she only appears at the end; don't bring this pacing, the daughter will account for over half the story.
Actually, the daughter's backstory is already written; it's just that few people can think to discover it.
The earlier talk of Cain and Abel, the Luck Goddess and the Light Goddess sisters, the god‑slayers of the Divine Era, etc.—the outlines I think should be pretty clear.

title: Chapter 11 — The Demon Lord's Might
content:
Chapter 11 — The Demon Lord's Might

Volume 18 · Chapter 11

Bebelifted his eyelids, unable to suppress a secret laugh, thinking how shameful this was—the mage probably didn't know that Lucifer was renowned as a mage slayer.

Hankfully had just barely regained consciousness from the shock, and he couldn't comprehend why his attack had no effect on Merlin. It was simply like a natural insulation against magic.

".... You

"What me?! " Merlin snatched the magic wand from Hankfully's hand and rained blows on Hankfully's forehead. "Am I hitting you?! Am I knocking your head?! Did I eat melon and get in your way?!"

Thump thump thump, Hankfully retreated continuously after being hit by Merlin's magic wand, a lump forming on his head, and soon his nose and face swelled up.

The leader of the four great dark guilds, who was supposed to be formidable, actually had no brains in front of Merlin, as if he were a chick being slaughtered.

How dare you hit me? I... Hankfully covered the lump on his head, trying to intimidate Merlin.

"What! What's it to you if I hit you?! " With a "thwack," Merlin added another blow to Hankfully's head, hammering him into continuous retreat.

Hankfully had become a bit cowardly. He had always bullied others, and this was the first time he had been bullied. His heart was incredibly aggrieved.

"Hmph! Who do you think you are? Have I provoked you?" Merlin callously snapped the magic wand in half and threw it at Hankfully's feet like trash.

"Urgh!"

Hankfully widened his eyes, his small heart uncontrollably trembling, agitated with distress.

My thousand-gold cup magic wand was just broken like that!

Although its hardness was comparable to mithril essence, it's hard to find a material harder than this!

Why is it so fragile in the hands of this black-iron adventurer? Like tofu residue breaking apart!

Could it be that this guy's physical strength has become terrifyingly formidable! A mere one-in-a-million treatment

If even a black-iron adventurer has such power, how much stronger would the higher-level swordmasters be?

Hankfully picked up the two pieces of the magic wand from the ground, his heart bleeding, feeling that Oswell's being反杀 (killed unexpectedly) was unjustly wrong.

These two adventurers seem to have extraordinary origins, and their strength is not weak. Even facing this black-iron adventurer, I feel considerable pressure.

"Speak, who are you? Did you come here deliberately to find trouble?" Merlin grabbed Hankfully's collar, questioning him with a face full of anger.

"This... it's a misunderstanding."

A layer of crystalline sweat appeared on Hankfully's forehead. Internally, he was extremely panicked. Since his magic of level 2 wasn't effective, it was simply like an ordinary person. With what could he fight Merlin?

Although Merlin looked ordinary on the outside, from the just now effortless breaking of the black crystal magic wand, he had completely pinned Hankfully down, making him dare not move lightly.

Hankfully asked himself that his body wasn't as hard as black crystal, so in such a close distance, if the other party moved, he could have his neck twisted!

"Misunderstanding?" Merlin furrowed his brows, not very believing this explanation. The guy who randomly knocked on his head was probably intentional!

"Yeah brother, it's... all a misunderstanding. I'm apologizing! I just mistakenly recognized the person... your back shadow and my... a rival are too alike... Hankfully spoke nonsense from his mouth, his mind full of how to get away from Merlin's control.

"Has an apology been useful? Do we still need laws?" Merlin let out a cold snort. Just as he was eating, he was disturbed. Need I say how bad his mood is now?

"Release the Guild Master! ! !" Eden saw Hankfully being restrained and directly brandished his magic wand, preparing for a big fight.

Everyone looked at Eden taking the lead, and thousands of azure blue flame disciples brandished their weapons without regard for this being the Imperial Royal City, forming a momentum of a decisive battle with Merlin to rescue the Guild Master.

For a moment, the street suddenly had so many people holding weapons, each looking like a guy who didn't care about their life. Their cold gazes surrounded Merlin and Bebeli.

This group of disciples couldn't see Merlin's BUG-like magic immunity, nor could they feel Hankfully's terror at the moment. They only saw the Guild Master's power mysteriously dissipating, as if deliberately holding back.

In the past, every time Hankfully made a move, he was unstoppable, and it was rare to meet an opponent. This time, however, he ate a loss in front of a black-iron adventurer, which really made people drop their jaws.

Everyone had already realized that this black-iron adventurer was not simple. The person who could easily subdue Hankfully must have formidable strength, so they must be cautious.

People on the street let out many screams and fled the scene. Every household closed their doors, fearing they would be harmed. Even the watermelon seller lifted his cart and fled, daring not to take Merlin's money.

In the end, only those holding weapons and desperate disciples remained. They surrounded Merlin and Bebeli, forming an impenetrable human wall, making it impossible for the enemy to fly!

Only Lorei, this Saint-tier fighter, didn't move, hiding at the very end of the crowd. Merlin couldn't even see him.

Lorei's brain was short-circuited right now. He had never thought that this black-iron adventurer was so powerful, able to subdue the Guild Master!

He had always thought he was just a filler! A follower so awesome! That silver-level swordmaster's strength... how terrifying!

Lorei didn't dare to think about it anymore. He had never seen such a perverted pair of adventurers. Even the Guild Master was pressed to the ground by their follower, so what grudge was there to report?

"You didn't hear me?! Release our Guild Master, otherwise don't blame us for being impolite!" Eden held up his magic wand and threatened, trying to save Hankfully from the predicament. He didn't believe the Guild Master had just been holding back; something must have happened, otherwise with the Guild Master's Saint-tier peak strength, how could he be pressured by a mere black-iron adventurer?

Merlin swept a circle around this group of disciples, still holding Hankfully's neck, suddenly smiling, "Yo, what a big scene. So it's a group coming in. Just now mixed in the crowd, I didn't notice. What organization are you all?"

"Downplaying the situation, we... we are just a traveling mercenary group." Hankfully's life was controlled by Merlin, so he had to smile and lie, daring not to say he came to seek trouble.

At this moment, Hankfully's intestines were regretful X. He really shouldn't have come to take revenge on his subordinates. He didn't expect to hit an iron board. Magic was ineffective against this guy, so what use did he have? Cool cool!

Hankfully abandoned the idea of revenge. Now he just wanted to leave the royal city quickly and not provoke this pair of adventurers. He would obediently take his subordinates to find the Dracula ruins, which would be the most stable.

It's just that the atmosphere was full of gunpowder right now, and it might break out. Hankfully didn't think there were any disciples among his subordinates who could break a black crystal with their bare hands. Obviously, defeating Merlin was very difficult, and the loss would be heavy.

"Traveling mercenary group?" Merlin looked at these people a few times. Their dusty look really looked like travelers, so he didn't think much. "If you let me release the person, I will release. Am I not losing face then?"

"I think you're looking for death! Attack!" Eden's voice turned cold. Everyone started to move restlessly, wanting to tear Merlin into pieces.

"Let my two sisters go meet this man?" Vena curled her fingers and stretched out, her nails instantly becoming much longer and extremely sharp.

"If the Guild Master is completely at a loss, I'm very interested in him~" Una narrowed her fox-seductive eyes, thinking about how to kill Merlin the fastest.

"Two beautiful ladies, I'm not someone who likes fighting and killing. I just don't want to be beaten for nothing. Perhaps we can sit down and talk." Merlin's original intention was not to fight, just to swindle some money.

"You have a really sweet mouth. If you're interested in my sister, why not wait until midnight alone to visit me? However... I'm actually more interested in cutting your throat!" The voice had just fallen, and almost all the azure blue flame disciples launched an attack. Magic power and battle aura wildly intertwined, forming a net of slaughter covering the sky, as if a meat grinder, tearing any enemy into pieces.

Over 1300 people jointly besieged Merlin, the momentum was grand, each disciple like a hungry wolf rushing at the enemy.

"Don't move."

A personal voice sounded, and everyone moved as if they had been hit by a immobilization spell, unable to move, not knowing if this moment's time had stopped.

Una and the two sisters' eyes were filled with fear, each wanting to imagine that aragbeg who was ignored at the beginning. A feeling of great trouble arose spontaneously.

Bebel put down his teacup calmly, lifted his eyelids, "Kneel down, humble humans.

Overwhelmingly powerful pressure was released from Bebel, comparable to a giant beast devouring the earth waking up. No one could escape the fate of being eaten.

In a short instant, Bebel's pressure swept through the entire process. Over 1300 azure blue flame disciples knelt on the ground in succession, making a "thump thump thump" sound" -=

They weren't willingly kneeling, but couldn't withstand that terrifying pressure!

title: Chapter 12 — Misunderstanding Deepens
content:
Chapter 12 — Misunderstanding Deepens

Volume 18 · Chapter 12

Belphegor's pressure raged like a towering mountain crashing down, and the people around fell to the ground, unable to resist it!
The obvious demonic aura surged like a flood beast, continually striking the nerves of these disciples, making them feel the fear of a superior race!
Thousands knelt on the ground, faces pressed to the dirt, even their heads could barely lift to stare at Belphegor!
The scene looked spectacular; those who didn't know might think a king was on patrol!

As one of the four great dark guilds, Azure Blue Abyssal Flame is not weak at all—far stronger than the small guild Merlin belongs to in Rexham.
There are five Saint‑tier experts, over three hundred high‑rank disciples, and the rest are mid‑tier masters; low‑tier strength doesn't even qualify to join Azure Blue Abyssal Flame.
Yet they still couldn't directly withstand the pressure emanating from the Demon Lord—only those few Saint‑tier experts could lift their heads before the bland Belphegor.
They never imagined that this guy who looks like a street beggar would have such terrifying power! Not even a shred of a chance to resist!

Eden's face turned deathly pale, cold sweat dripping from his cheeks as his whole body shuddered involuntarily.
He lifted his head against the pressure, staring at Belphegor with shocked eyes, suddenly realizing the gravity of the situation—
A ferocious demonic aura, an unmatchable pressure!
The only thing I can think of… is probably the Gluttony Demon Lord who recently attacked the Empire!
Wasn't it defeated? Why is it still unharmed here?!
Eden's mind raced, feeling impending doom; he had only wanted to avenge Osweid, but ended up provoking an enemy he couldn't afford.
Now the whole guild is in a hostage situation; escaping seems like a problem.

“A mere flock of livestock, dare to brandish weapons before us? Deserve to die!” Belphexor shouted, and the pressure he released increased further.
In an instant, wails rose everywhere; many weak disciples couldn't withstand the pressure and fainted on the spot.
It's estimated that if Belphegor got serious, he wouldn't need to lift a finger—just releasing his pressure could kill a large group of people.

Merlin saw the situation escalating, likely to draw guards, and he wouldn't be able to explain to Margaret, so he said, “Alright, don't go overboard; we agreed not to cause trouble.”
Belphegor glanced at Merlin, speaking with slight contempt: “You really suck at mixing around out there; you dare to follow any monster or ghost.”
“What's strange about that? Didn't you say I'm a defective product?” Merlin laughed indifferently.
“Hmph!” Belphegor didn't say more, thinking he shouldn't have called Merlin a defective product; that's basically insulting himself for not even being as good as a defective product.

Humphrey stared blankly, not daring to move even as Merlin choked his neck; he was scared stupid, even feeling like he might lose bladder/bowel control.
He personally felt Belphegor's pressure, asking himself he'd never seen anything so formidable in his life.
Indeed, the Demon Lord's strength is so great it brings despair, even more terrifying than the rumors!
What's the relation between this Iron Adventurer and the Gluttony Demon Lord? They look quite familiar......
Humphrey's mind was full of “can't afford to provoke”; he completely gave up resistance, only hoping for a peaceful resolution.

“Hey, still planning to make a move?” Merlin looked at Humphrey, who put on a “kind” smile.
“No no no! How could I possibly cross you?” Humphrey came to his senses, nervously begging.
“But how does hitting my head count? My head is very valuable…. Merlin thought about the bounty the Holy Church had on him, then exaggerated, saying, “It's worth tens of billions!”
“Pff!”
Humphrey spat out old blood, thinking “Damn, worth tens of billions! You just spout that out of nowhere! Is your forehead studded with diamonds?! Even the world's richest Rothschild family isn't that wealthy!”
Although Humphrey thought Merlin's nonsense was unreliable, he still put on a smile, though it looked worse than crying.
“....This is too much; I can't come up with that. Can you make it less?”

The street returned to calm, just appearing very deserted.
Apart from Merlin and Belphegor, there was no one left; everyone had been scared away by that show of force.
Merlin chose to release Humphrey's horse, and didn't go for a massacre; it wasn't necessary for a travel.
Moreover, Merlin didn't know Humphrey and his companions were from a dark guild; he genuinely thought it was just a misunderstanding, that he'd been misidentified.
If Merlin could see Laurie among the crowd, he might recall what happened earlier in Ireland.
Of course, Humphrey paid a hefty price: his magic wand worth millions was broken by Merlin, and he also lost 500,000 gold!
To Humphrey, this was nothing short of a disgrace, like being slapped and still grinning while giving a thumbs-up, saying “Nice hit!”
But Humphrey had no choice; Merlin and Belphegor are both people he can't afford to offend; losing money to avoid disaster is already the lightest outcome.
Just the Azure Blue Abyssal Flame guild wasn't wealthy to begin with; now they still haven't found the losses, and they've poured in even more money, making the guild's situation worse and worse.
Merlin fiddled with a crystal card worth 500,000 in his hand; this could be exchanged for a large sum at any merchant association.

“Is it really okay to just let them go like that? You got your head knocked by them.” Belphegor frowned, not understanding why Merlin wasn't angry.
“Isn't this too trivial to quibble over? What do you want me to do?” Merlin retorted to Belphegor.
“Slaughter the city, ambush hundreds of thousands—no need to be polite with these lowly livestock; kill until I'm satisfied.” Belphegor said with a ferocious gaze.
“I'm not that extreme; frankly, I can't bring myself to do something like killing someone's whole family…” Merlin gave a faint smile.
“Pathetic…” Belphegor rolled his eyes, thinking Merlin was too unpromising, no wonder the council drove him out.
“Here, take this.” Merlin tossed the crystal card worth 500,000 gold to Belphegor.
“What do you mean?” Belphegor looked at the crystal card but didn't reach out.
“The demon race is poor and short on money, right? Your territory isn't easy either; take it back to subsidize a bit.” Merlin said nonchalantly.
“...Are you bribing me?” Belphegor's breathing grew shallow, saying insincerely, “Don't think a bribe will make me yield; I'll still sue you before the council.”
“Never mind.” Merlin said, reaching to take the crystal card back.
But Belphegor was quicker, snatched the card, silently slipped it into his pocket, and covered his embarrassment with a cough: “Even if I don't sue, you marrying a human breaks the taboo; the council will find out sooner or later—just wait for the punishment!” Hmph!
“Poor is fine, but your mouth is still hard.” Merlin rolled his eyes. 三之7人治
Actually, the demon race as a whole is impoverished; Belphegor is no exception—resources need to be obtained via trade with humans.
500,000 gold isn't little; it could let the Fifth Demon Lord Palace live comfortably for a while.
As a Demon Lord, Belphegor needs to manage his domain well; otherwise he couldn't support his brood of hungry demons.
“Is it really okay to just give me this so easily? Are you that kind-hearted?”
“Otherwise, if I kept it, I'd only be able to give it to Alice, and I wouldn't get any benefit at all.” Merlin sighed helplessly, showing a henpecked expression.
“You mean— you usually put in all that effort, earn money, then hand it over to that flat‑chested woman?” Belphegor's expression turned weird.
“Pretty much.” Merlin didn't hide it; he indeed had some issues, habitually throwing money into the horse‑racing gambling, hoping luck would turn things around, which naturally provoked Alice's anger!
“...You used to be the Demon Lord, your power could crush that woman several blocks over, yet you're controlled like this? What's the difference from slavery!” Belphegor slammed the table, thinking humans are lowly creatures, yet they can ride on a demon's head—damn it!
“Are you trying to say I'm really pathetic?” Merlin gave a half‑smile.
“No.” Belphegor shook his head seriously, “Love is like poison; you love her so deeply you've completely lost…”
“???” Merlin frowned, his head full of question marks-
What the heck is all this nonsense =
(°∞叭)

title: Chapter 13 — Visitor from the Homeland
content:
Chapter 13 — Visitor from the Homeland

Volume 18 · Chapter 13

“Then… I think you might have misunderstood something?” Merlin felt like he and Beelzebub were on completely different wavelengths.

“I can somewhat understand you. After all, Miranda is my everything. As long as it’s not a principle issue, I’ll go along with her. I suppose it’s similar for you. But…” Beelzebub hesitated, his expression conflicted. “Why would you be infatuated with a human? I can’t wrap my head around it. We demons are a far superior species. Even though this era belongs to humans, our lowly status can’t be changed.”

“Why do you think I’m infatuated with a human?” Merlin raised a brow, realizing the misunderstanding was deep.

“Do I need to ask? You’re defending this woman to the death, and you’re working for her like a slave? Is that something a former Demon Lord would do? You have no dignity left as a high-ranking species.” Beelzebub lowered his head, stubbornly insisting. “Don’t think I’ll say nice things just because I’ve taken your bribes. You and a human won’t have a happy ending, and your fate won’t be any better. I suggest you leave this human woman early and find a noble demon female as a partner. It’s better than being with a lowly human.”

“I…”

Merlin wanted to explain, but he couldn’t think of a good way. His actions seemed irredeemable.

“I’m back!”

Just as Merlin and Beelzebub were arguing, Alice returned after reading the empire’s posted notice.

Merlin and Beelzebub fell silent in unison, stopping their discussion and pretending to be leisurely.

Some things weren’t suitable for Alice to hear, after all, humans were a different race in front of two demons.

After returning, Alice looked around and felt something was off. “Earlier, this place was bustling with people. Now it’s unusually quiet, and I can’t even see a single person. Even the watermelon vendor is gone?”

So Alice sat beside Merlin, looking suspiciously and asked, “Did something happen here just now?”

“No, everything is peaceful,” Merlin shrugged, trying to ease Alice’s concerns. If she found out he had extorted a travel军团 and given some of the money to Beelzebub, she’d definitely think he had betrayed the revolution!

“Really? It just feels much quieter than before,” Alice was puzzled. The capital city had already returned to normal operations these past few days.

“Did this demon cause trouble?”

Beelzebub’s wife narrowed her eyes and said with an unpleasant tone, “Although I promised Lucifer to behave, do you have the right to question me?”

“Cough! No, just… just now, a circus troupe passed by, and a lot of people chased after them to watch,” Merlin made up a lie on the spot.

“Circus? How come I didn’t see it?” Alice thought to herself, she wasn’t blind or deaf, and she hadn’t seen any circus at all.

“Don’t… don’t talk about that. What did the notice say? Is it about Medes’ whereabouts…” Merlin changed the subject.

“No, it’s about the old king being poisoned and falling into a coma. The empire is recruiting alchemists who are proficient in pharmacology nationwide, probably to find a cure for the king,” Alice recalled the notice Margaret had posted a few days ago.

“The old king is poisoned?” Merlin thought this wasn’t good news, meaning Margaret would focus most of her energy on it.

“Yes, I think Medes poisoned the old king before he left, not wanting the empire to be peaceful. If the old king dies, it will definitely cause more chaos,” Alice speculated.

“Is anyone responding?” Merlin asked further.

“I saw a lot of people gathering around, and many alchemists with bottles and jars, but no one dared to step forward,” Alice’s呆毛 on her head twitched.

“Why?” Merlin frowned in confusion.

“Because the conditions are quite harsh. It says to prove the alchemist’s own ability, they need to drink a poison themselves and solve it to be allowed to treat the king. Otherwise, they’re not permitted,” Merlin answered.

“What! Treating the king requires the alchemist to drink the poison and solve it themselves? That’s not asking for suicide?” Merlin found it unbelievable. He thought this Margaret princess was too strict. Searching the nation for alchemists, yet setting such a high threshold, how many alchemists would dare take the job? Drinking poison themselves? If they couldn’t solve it… they’d be dead, and it would be their own fault!

“Yes, I also think this condition is too harsh. If alchemists don’t have enough confidence, drinking the poison is essentially suicide, so many are hesitant. It’s been a long time, and no one has dared to try treating the old king,” Alice paused and added, “But I think the princess is just being cautious. After all, treating the king is a major matter, and they can’t let a group of alchemists who can’t even solve their own poisoning take over. This eliminates a lot of unqualified people.”

“It seems… understandable,” Merlin thought to himself,勉强 able to understand Margaret. Besides, no one was forced to drink the poison. If they wanted to treat the king, they at least had to have confidence in their own alchemical skills.

“Hmph! What caution? This princess is clearly a heartless woman, the kind who won’t kill people with her own hands. I advise you to stay far away from her,” Beelzebub thought Margaret was too cunning, truly not worth trusting.

“You’re not much better. Do you know how much damage you caused by attacking the capital? Compared to Margaret, more people died at your hands,” Alice retorted with hostility.

“Shut up! Do you even have the right to judge me? If it weren’t for Lucifer’s deep love for you, I’d have eaten you up by now!” Beelzebub showed his fangs in a threat.

“Eh?” Alice’s face turned red, her heart pounding as she looked uncertainly at Merlin beside her, “…”

“No, no, he’s just talking nonsense. You don’t have to believe… I didn’t say that, haha…” Merlin hurriedly explained, laughing awkwardly to cover up the embarrassment, thinking to himself—

What is this Beelzebub talking about? How will I face Alice later?

By the way, why is this woman blushing? Is she angry and embarrassed?

The capital city’s notice board had the recruitment notice for alchemists posted on it.

If one wanted to accept this task, they just needed to go up and tear down the notice.

Two imperial guards stood in front of the notice board, preventing anyone from causing trouble here.

At this moment, a large crowd had gathered, pointing and discussing. Many were alchemists who had come upon hearing the news.

“To cure the king’s poison, they also require the alchemist to drink the poison and solve it themselves? That’s not nonsense?”

“Exactly, you can’t just eat random poison. What if they can’t solve it?”

“I think the princess hasn’t changed at all, still likes to play around. I bet she doesn’t even know much about pharmacology.”

The alchemists criticized Margaret, and no one dared to step forward to tear down the notice and accept this arduous task.

At this moment, a short figure in a brown long robe pushed to the front. His small stature easily led people to mistake him for a dwarf.

He wore a hood, his face obscured. The wooden magic staff in his hand was long enough to be used as a cane.

The short figure read the notice, then suddenly smiled. The purple荆花 knight团’s emblem on his chest gleamed—

“Margaret:

“A truly clever princess.”(‘心)

title: Chapter 14 — The Phoenix: First Under the Gods
content:
Chapter 14 — The Phoenix: First Under the Gods

Volume 18 · Chapter 14

The Azure Flame team left the capital city in a massive procession, not daring to look back even once.

Wagon after wagon raced southward, heading toward the location of the ruins.

In the lead wagon, the guildmaster Humphrey sat in the darkest corner, his face ashen and his head bowed in silence, looking as if he had suffered a severe blow.

His disciples followed Humphrey in silence, their moods no better. Many were still recalling the terrifying aura of Beelzebub just moments ago.

Azure Flame was, after all, one of the four major dark guilds, notorious for its cruelty. Usually, they were the ones bullying others. Today, however, they had been taught a lesson.

This greatly damaged the confidence of the many disciples, some even beginning to doubt the capabilities of their guildmaster Humphrey.

What kind of guildmaster was one who submitted to another's strength? What right did he have to lead the guild?

Fortunately, Eden remained relatively calm. Being able to escape safely from under the nose of the Demon Lord was already a great fortune. Just moments ago, he had thought he wouldn't be able to leave the capital city alive.

However, he was becoming increasingly confused about Merlin, the iron-black adventurer. The gluttony Demon Lord seemed to have a good relationship with Merlin and was also obedient to him.

The attack on the capital had left the entire empire in a state of near paralysis. Countless people had likely perished in the chaos. Yet this tyrant, who had caused such destruction, would obey the words of a human? It was truly shocking.

He even began to suspect that Merlin was not human. Otherwise, how could the lofty demon race possibly associate with a human?

Eden glanced around at his companions and noticed their morale was somewhat low. They had definitely been shaken, especially Humphrey, who had remained sullen from start to finish.

A thin layer of cold sweat beaded on Humphrey's forehead, his body trembling slightly. He hadn't yet recovered from his fear, his mind filled with questions:

Why was my magic ineffective against that iron-black adventurer?

Why was the opponent's physical strength so formidable, able to easily snap the hard black crystal?

Why was the gluttony Demon Lord, who had caused such chaos in the empire, present there, and seemingly on good terms with this iron-black adventurer?

What kind of crazy killer was I, a murderer, who in front of a Demon Lord was nothing more than an ant!

Humphrey was full of questions, unable to understand why this adventurer from Britannia had such power, even being able to connect with the Demon Lord King. As for the female demon swordswoman who hadn't appeared, he didn't dare to think about her.

"Guildmaster? Guildmaster?" Eden called out a few times, trying to stabilize his guildmaster's low spirits.

"Ah... yes!" Humphrey was jolted out of his daze, startled.

"Guildmaster, what's wrong?" Eden asked. If Humphrey didn't recover, the guild might fall apart.

"...Nothing much," Humphrey tried to calm his emotions. "I just didn't expect one of the Seven Demon Lords to be there..."

That was truly surprising.

"Yes, although we had long heard that the Demon Lords' power was terrifying, experiencing it at such close range, it's indeed even more terrifying than imagined," Eden nodded in agreement.

"The gluttony Demon Lord is so powerful. How did the empire defeat this monster? I've never heard of any strong figures in France who could defeat a Demon Lord King. It's fortunate for us that Eden was there, otherwise, if we had provoked the empire on our own, the outcome would have been obvious!" Laurence said, still shaken.

The twin sisters Yuna and Vina remained silent, feeling they had been too naive. The power of the gluttony Demon Lord was already terrifying enough, and to provoke the empire that had defeated the Demon Lord was nothing short of suicide.

"Exactly. Any empire of significant scale must possess a mysterious power capable of deterring enemies. Unless absolutely necessary, one should never provoke them. The Hōki Raisan was also one of the four major dark guilds, but in the end, it still declined. This is a lesson for us, don't walk the same old path," Eden said with a cautious tone.

"Eden is right. Although our guild is not weak, we should still be more low-key when we go out," Humphrey nodded, feeling Eden's words were very reasonable.

"But Guildmaster, why did your ambush on that iron-black adventurer fail?" Eden asked in confusion.

"Yes, Guildmaster, why were you subdued by an iron-black adventurer?" Yuna couldn't help but ask.

"Guildmaster, are you deliberately holding back?" Vina became suspicious, feeling today's Humphrey was strange.

"Haven't you realized? That iron-black adventurer is not someone you can easily provoke. Do you know how hard this black crystal staff is? Even if burned with the hottest flames for years, it wouldn't change, yet he snapped it easily. How many people can possess such formidable physical strength? Can you?" Humphrey asked everyone, holding up the two broken pieces of the staff to show them.

Everyone fell silent. After hearing the guildmaster's words, they had to reassess Merlin's strength. Could someone who could easily destroy black crystal be an iron-black adventurer? It was impossible!

"This iron-black adventurer is very strange. Have you noticed? Even the gluttony Demon Lord respects his opinions. That Demon Lord is a monster capable of single-handedly breaking through the entire empire, yet he is so close to a human adventurer?" Eden boldly stated his doubts.

"It seems to be true. At the time, I always thought this iron-black adventurer was just a pretty face. How could his wife, a mithril-level adventurer, be willing to marry a low-level iron-black adventurer? Today, it seems the situation isn't so simple," Laurence suddenly realized, thinking he had been tricked all along.

"Perhaps the wife of this iron-black adventurer is even more terrifying?" Eden asked curiously.

"Impossible. I and Osward tried to assassinate that demon swordswoman in Gao Wei City. Although she was strong, she was definitely not an unbeatable existence. She certainly couldn't easily destroy black crystal," Laurence answered with certainty.

...Eden's eyes widened in confusion as he lowered his head, thinking to himself. Where did this iron-black adventurer come from? Was he deliberately hiding his strength? When had Britannia produced such a powerful figure!

"What's strange isn't the fact that he can easily destroy black crystal, but that my magic was ineffective against him, rendering me completely useless as a magician... Humphrey believed this was the most formidable aspect of the opponent.

"Maybe... the adventurer is wearing magical armor?" Laurence speculated.

"Are you an idiot? Even with magical defensive items, the guildmaster's strength would have been impossible to completely block. The opponent barely had any injuries!" Yuna gave Laurence a cold look.

"Laurence is probably scared傻 by the Demon Lord, thinking the guildmaster is as useless as him. Haha," Vina gave Laurence a cold look and mocked.

"....I wasn't scared傻!" Laurence turned red and argued.

"Enough, now is not the time for arguing. Although we suffered a setback here, we will eventually get our revenge. Osward is our companion, and we must avenge his death. As for now? We must prioritize obtaining the treasure from the Dracula ruins. Other matters can be set aside for now," Humphrey said seriously.

"The guildmaster is right. Although that iron-black adventurer is extremely mysterious and powerful, we don't need to fear him. We should first make our guild stronger so we have a voice, and then find an opportunity to eliminate this pair of adventurers, letting them know the consequences of offending us," Eden sighed in relief, seeming that Humphrey was still calm and knew what was important.

"But... the boy seems to have a good relationship with the gluttony Demon Lord. Can we...?" Laurence hesitated to speak.

"Even if we can't defeat the Demon Lord, we can still involve other dark guilds. Don't forget, Phoenix is currently at an unprecedented peak. Even the demon race has the capital to confront them head-on. Their guildmaster is even known as the Phoenix," Eden paused and said slowly.

"If even that man can't defeat the Demon Lord, perhaps only a god can?"

"I have always believed that the guildmaster of Phoenix is the strongest human..."

title: Chapter 15 — A Single Swallow
content:
Chapter 15 — A Single Swallow

Volume 18 · Chapter 15

At the bulletin board in front of the royal palace, the many alchemists were still gathered here arguing among themselves, privately having already torn Margaret's reputation to shreds.

Margaret's reputation had never been good to begin with—she had done many puzzling, outrageous-seeming things.

And now she was making alchemists test poisons on themselves? That was beyond absurd!

Conspiracy theories had even started circulating, claiming that Margaret never actually wanted the king to wake up, so that she could take the throne directly and become the new queen of the empire!

But thinking about it carefully, that conspiracy theory fell apart. Margaret was the sole heir—she had no siblings. The empire would be hers sooner or later regardless.

Just as nobody had the guts to accept the task, that short fellow with the Judas Flower Knight Order badge pinned to his chest stepped forward, tore down the notice, and thoroughly startled everyone—

"Oh my god! Someone accepted the mission! What's he thinking?!"

"There's really someone who isn't afraid of death? Poison isn't something you can just casually counteract. One tiny mistake and you'll have poison upon poison!"

"Hey there, lad, I advise you to just give up. Don't end up dead without even knowing how. The princess is clearly just messing with people!"

"It's fine, I'm willing to try." The little man rolled up the notice and smiled. "Also, don't call me lad—I'm actually in my sixties already. It's just that this baby face of mine is terribly deceptive."

Hearing the short man say that, quite a few people were secretly amazed. He looked more like a young man in his early twenties, his face so youthful it seemed like you could squeeze water out of it. He looked fairly immature, with seemingly little social experience—anyone would find it hard to believe he was already over fifty.

The two guards on duty beside the notice board, seeing someone had accepted the task, stepped forward to ask, "Sir, are you willing to cure His Majesty the King? Don't forget you'll need to drink the poison we prepare yourself."

"Of course, I'm willing to give it a try," the short man replied affably.

The guards couldn't help but frown. The man looked far too young to be over fifty, and even less like an experienced alchemist. "Are you sure? This isn't a joke. Do you actually understand pharmacology?"

"A little." The short man nodded, without bragging.

"Fine. State your identity clearly, and I'll report to Her Highness the Princess." The guards stopped talking and instead began probing the short man's background.

"My name is Clady, and I come from Great Britain." The short man paused, then added, "Oh right, I'm affiliated with the Judas Flower Knight Order, ranked as the Twelfth-Thorned Knight."

In the sleeping chambers, the light was somewhat dim.

The aging king lay on the luxurious bed, fading from life. His condition worsened day by day.

His aged face was covered in wrinkles, his complexion a dark purplish hue—clearly beyond hope.

Margaret stayed by the bedside, watching over her father, occasionally dabbing his cheeks with a warm cloth.

Seeing her father's body growing weaker and weaker, Margaret couldn't help but sigh, feeling truly powerless.

That cursed Medes—what exactly did he do to my father?! I'll tear him to pieces!

Margaret viciously cursed in her heart, but at that moment Blaize burst in, startling the maids into gasps.

"Your Highness! Your Highness!"

"Shh!" Margaret turned her head and made a silencing gesture, not wanting to disturb the aging king. "Keep it down. Do you think this is someplace else?"

"Uh—I'm sorry, Your Highness." Blaize scratched his head foolishly, forgetting the king needed quiet.

"So reckless—where's your decorum? Why did you suddenly come here?" Margaret asked.

"Outside..." Blaize swallowed, gathering his words before speaking, "Someone tore down the notice. They're going to cure the king!"

Margaret raised her willow-leaf eyebrows, slightly surprised. "Someone still dares to try under those harsh conditions?"

"Yes." Blaize nodded repeatedly.

"Seems this person has some courage—and likely some skill as well. Perhaps he can truly bring father back." Margaret nodded, feeling her elaborate conditions hadn't been in vain. The reason she set such strict conditions was entirely to keep mediocre alchemists away. The king's situation was dire and couldn't withstand any further折腾. Only a truly talented alchemist would do. If even she couldn't save him, who had the qualification to treat the king?

"Not only does he have courage—this guy has considerable backing as well." Blaize emphasized.

"What do you mean?" Margaret frowned.

"The guards reported that the guy is a Thorned Knight from Britannia named Clady." Blaize said seriously.

"From Great Britain again?" Margaret thought of Merlin and Alice. That country across the sea certainly had no shortage of talent. An instinctive sense of crisis crept over her. "Do you know this person?"

"I don't know him well, but I've heard of him. Ranked as the Twelfth-Thorned Knight, he's a scholar who travels far and wide researching ancient magic. It's said the Thorned Knights all respect him." Blaize gave a rough introduction—though he himself had only heard it through rumor.

"Bring the prepared poison. Let's go meet this..."

Outside the royal palace, Clady waited quietly, while quite a few people behind him gathered to watch and refused to leave.

Most of them had their hearts set on treating Clady as a fool, ready to enjoy the show.

If Clady died, it would prove Margaret was truly pulling nonsense—and they'd escaped disaster.

The great doors of the royal palace slowly opened, and a grand procession emerged—

At the forefront was the dignified Margaret, who eyed Clady from a distance and asked in a low voice, "Why so young? Is this what a scholar looks like? Could he be a fake?"

"As for this... surely no one would dare impersonate a Thorned Knight so easily. The Judas Flower Knight Order badge on his chest is absolutely genuine." Blaize explained awkwardly, but his heart was pounding. Too young, wasn't he? Why would Thorned Knights respect someone so young?

Seeing Margaret arrive, Clady leaned on his staff and bowed slightly, paying respect to the imperial princess.

"Then you must be the renowned Princess Margaret? As beautiful and radiant as the rumors describe."

Margaret looked over Clady several times, her doubts mounting. She didn't believe someone so young had the ability to cure the king. "Stop flattering me. I'm the one known for my terrible reputation."

"You jest, Your Highness." Clady straightened. "I've often heard you're the most beautiful woman in France. Meeting you today confirms it. No wonder those nobles and lords are breaking their heads trying to marry you."

"Are you really a Thorned Knight?" Margaret looked into Clady's eyes.

"As genuine as it gets. Though my reputation isn't great, I sit at number twelve." Clady said humbly.

"Then do you have the ability to cure His Majesty's illness?" Margaret pressed again.

"This humble one may not be talented, but having traveled the world, I've seen many strange poisons and diseases. I'm willing to try." Clady didn't over-promise.

"Very well." Margaret mulled it over—"willing to try" wasn't enough; the king had to be cured. Despite her doubts, she was still willing to give it a go. "As expected of a Thorned Knight from Great Britain—truly admirable. I'll trust you once. But you must prove your ability. Someone, bring up the poison!"

At her command, the guards dragged forward a long table, placing seven bowls of poison on it in the colors of red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, and violet.

A bizarre smell wafted out, turning the faces of the onlookers pale. They纷纷 backed away and covered their noses, terrified that even a whiff would cost them their lives.

"These seven bowls of poison were all brewed by the palace alchemists."

Margaret didn't dare approach, instead introducing from afar,

"The seven bowls each have different properties, and all are fantastically lethal. A single touch will turn your entire body to liquid—no bones left behind."

"Even one drop spilling outside could bring catastrophic disaster."

"I wonder if you have the courage to choose one bowl, and drink it all down right here before everyone?"

title: Chapter 16 — Cladi
content:
Chapter 16 — Cladi

Volume 18 · Chapter 16

Margaret's words had barely faded when the onlookers erupted into gasps.

"This is plainly barefaced murder!"

"With such a pungent odor, the poison must be too potent to mask. Who in their right mind would dare drink it down? Only someone completely out of their mind."

"Exactly. If you drank it, not even your remains would be left. The sight of death would be unbearable!"

Merlin, Alice, and Beelzebub all noticed the commotion and slowly drifted closer, though they stopped short of getting too near.

"No way? Someone actually accepted this task?!" Alice looked surprised. She had assumed such苛刻 terms would deter anyone, yet here was someone truly reckless.

Merlin studied the short figure of Clady from behind, a sense of doubt rising within him. Was this guy for real? One mistake and he was dead. Still, having the courage to drink poison to prove himself—whether he was a genius or a fool remained to be seen.

Beelzebub, hiding discreetly beneath his cloak, sniffed the air and murmured softly, "This guy isn't simple."

"Hmm? What do you mean?" Merlin glanced at Beelzebub beside him, having to admire his nose for picking up so much with just a single sniff.

"He's not weak. Clearly not some random passerby. And his magical power is unusually domineering—that kind of trait only appears in those who've cultivated ancient magic."

Beelzebub recalled the bombardment of the twelve magical cannons. The domineering power bore a striking resemblance, as if crafted specifically to counter enemies several times their own strength.

The ancient forebears had faced mighty monstrous beasts and even tyrannical gods. The magic and martial arts of that era were simply incomparable to what existed now.

"Is that so... " Merlin nodded, genuinely surprised to find someone like this among the British Thorn Knights. He had never encountered anyone of this caliber before.

"Still, drinking poison is no joke. One slight misstep and it costs you your life. Strength and poison resistance are entirely unrelated. No matter how formidable your power, you could still be felled by poison." Beelzebub paused, casting a few glances at the seven bowls of poison on the table. "These poisons clearly aren't ordinary stuff. They were probably prepared quite some time ago."

"Do you have confidence in drinking these poisons yourself?" Merlin asked tentatively.

"You think I'm human? I'm the Gluttony who devours heaven and earth. I've eaten toxic food more times than you've eaten salt. I'm confident I can handle three bowls without being affected, but after that—I can't guarantee anything." Beelzebub wasn't completely immune to all poisons, but his resistance was far beyond that of an ordinary person. "This human may have decent strength, but his end will surely be grim. I guess he'd be poisoned to death after just one bowl. After all, poison isn't something just anyone can drink like water."

"What if he somehow manages to brew an antidote for himself?" Merlin felt he could hold out a sliver of hope.

"Unless the sun rises from the west, this human would need to identify his symptoms within an extremely short timeframe after drinking the poison and then formulate an antidote. The difficulty is far too high. Eight out of ten chances he'd be dead before he even finished brewing it." Beelzebub shifted his tone and flashed a amused smile. "But occasionally watching a suicide farce like this is rather entertaining, don't you think?"

Alice found this test absurd upon hearing this, so she said, "Merlin, shall we go stop him?"

"Hey! Disgusting holy maiden. Did he ask for your interference?" Beelzebub shot Alice a sidelong glance. He found this human woman to be nothing but trouble. What on earth had caught Merlin's interest in her?

"You—!" Alice was indignant. How had she meddled in someone else's affairs? She retorted angrily, "Demons are demons. Surely none of you are decent people!"

"... Merlin furrowed his brows and looked at Alice with an innocent expression, having been caught in the crossfire for no reason.

"N—no, that's not what I meant. Don't misunderstand. I was just saying... Alice waved her hands frantically and quickly added, "All demons except for you are villains..."

Meanwhile, Clady glanced at the seven bowls of poison before him, raised his head with a smile, and asked, "It seems Your Highness doesn't trust me? I've already presented my credentials as a British Thorn Knight. Do you really think I would deceive King His Majesty?"

"It's not that I don't trust you, sir, it's simply that we aren't familiar with each other. After all, you're a knight of Britain, not of France. I've heard His Majesty Elizabeth is extremely shrewd, with numerous capable generals under her command. She recently recruited a valiant warrior named Elgin the Great Swordmaster, who single-handedly crushed a rebel army. This greatly bolstered our nation's strength. So it's best to remain somewhat vigilant in certain matters. I'd rather not become someone's pawn." Margaret's words were diplomatic, but her meaning was clear. Clady, as a knight from another kingdom, needed to be watched. Only when everything was guaranteed to succeed could they attempt to treat the king.

"Very well, I understand your concerns. Then, to demonstrate my sincerity in coming here, I'll drink all seven bowls of poison." Clady wore a helpless expression.

His words sent ripples of shock through the crowd. People whispered amongst themselves, believing Clady had lost his mind. One bowl was enough to kill him hundreds of times over, and he wanted to drink seven?!

"This guy actually... he actually wants to commit suicide, doesn't he... " Alice's expression grew complicated, wondering whether Clady found his own life too long and wanted it ended.

Merlin fell silent, thinking that this little shortie was becoming even more unreadable. Could he truly be a genius?

"Fascinating. Drinking seven bowls of lethal poison? Planning to use his own life as the antidote?" Beelzebub widened his eyes, treating everything before him as mere after-dinner entertainment.

"Very well, sir. If you can truly accomplish this, I'm willing to consider you France's most loyal friend." Margaret made no move to stop Clady's reckless act.

"Your Highness, surely this isn't appropriate. He's a Thorn Knight of Britain with noble standing. If he dies here... it seems ill-advised to explain this to Queen Elizabeth." Blaise felt something was off.

"What's there to fear? He did this of his own accord. We've suffered no loss. If he's truly a genius, he'll naturally have the ability to cure the king. If he lacks the ability, his death will effectively weaken Britain without any cost to us. Where else can we find such a profitable deal?" Margaret's eyes turned cruel, signaling Blaise to shut up.

"... Blaise dared not speak further.

Clady swept aside his oversized sleeves, removing his tattered robe to reveal plain white garments underneath.

Without any more words, he picked up a bowl and drank down all seven bowls of poison on the table in one go.

Hearing the gurgle-gurgle-gurgle sounds, the onlookers stood dumbfounded. Was he treating poison like plain water? Had suicide become this bold?

The moment he finished the seventh bowl, Clady felt discomfort. His body swayed unsteadily as he leaned against a chair, and the bowls clattered and shattered across the floor.

"....This guy is a madman...." Merlin's gaze never wavered, his heart nearly leaping from his chest. Whether Clady was truly brilliant or utterly foolish would be revealed soon!

The poison began to take effect rapidly. Clady's body began to rot and dissolve as if bathed in sulfuric acid, growing soft and lifeless as his flesh peeled away into thick liquid.

This sight drew screams from the crowd. Many covered their eyes, unable to bear watching further, secretly marveling at the ferocity of the poison. It had begun taking effect within mere seconds of ingestion, leaving no time to prepare an antidote. Margaret was indeed committing barefaced murder!

Clady watched as his own hands appeared to shed their skin and fall away, leaving only stark white bones behind. Not daring to delay any longer, he opened his travel bag and pulled out mysterious vials and jars, roughly mixing potions without concern for precise measurements.

Many alchemists could see at once that Clady had lost his composure, abandoning all methodical principles and resorting to chaos. There was no way such a mixture could produce an antidote, especially not after consuming seven different types of lethal poison in one go. The complexity of breaking down such a combination was beyond imagination!

"....." Alice's slender frame trembled. She covered her eyes but couldn't resist peeking through her fingers. Clady's body was a bloody mess, reduced to bare bones with organs still pulsing inside. It seemed as though a skeleton itself was brewing the antidote—utterly bizarre and grotesque!

The rotting Clady mixed a bottle of transparent liquid at an unbelievable speed. He managed only two drops into his mouth before the bottle shattered on the ground. It seemed he hadn't had enough time...!

Under everyone's gaze, Clady had melted into a pool of foul-smelling thick liquid, dead beyond any possibility of revival. Only the transparent antidote slowly spreading on the ground confirmed that a living person had once stood there.

"???" Alice.

"???" Merlin.

"Hah, just as I thought...." Beelzebub chuckled darkly, watching Clady's remains—no bones, no flesh—and teased, "With abilities that paltry, why pretend otherwise? Wouldn't it be better to stay alive?"
