title: Chapter 17 — Ruins
content:
Chapter 17 — Ruins

Volume 18 · Chapter 17

Blitz stared blankly, his wide eyes like cowbells, gazing at the foul-smelling puddle of thick liquid on the ground as doubt swelled in his heart—

....Is that really dead!? S-Shouldn't it be a bit more difficult than this!?

He had looked so confident before, like a master of alchemy.

And yet... he surprisingly drank the poison and died right in front of everyone!

Blitz could think of nothing better than "pathetic" to describe this, and even began to wonder if the man was truly a Thorn Knight at all.

The onlookers, seeing that Cladi was quite definitely dead, couldn't help but whisper among themselves, regarding Cladi as a textbook example of someone whose equipment far exceeded his actual abilities.

"..." Margaret sighed, looking utterly disappointed, and said coldly, "Handle it. He was all talk. If someone with capabilities like his can become a Thorn Knight, then Great Britain is hardly something to fear."

"Wait, Your Highness! Look!" Blitz suddenly called out in an exaggerated tone, as if witnessing something truly unbelievable.

"Hm?" Margaret turned around and her eyes immediately widened in shock.

Right there, from that stinking puddle, a skeleton slowly rose up, its flesh reconstructing itself before everyone's eyes at a visibly rapid pace.

Bone grew muscle, tendons connected flesh to bone and skin, and even the newly regenerated pink organs began to pulse.

Cladi, who had been dead a moment ago, was now alive before their eyes, completely unchanged from how he had been bustling about earlier, as reborn like a newborn infant.

No wonder Cladi claimed to be in his sixties but still looked like a young man. This technique resembling molting and rebirth truly amazed everyone present—

"He really came back to life!? Is this some ghostly trick!?"

"He's left not even a shred behind and he's still alive!? I've spent most of my life studying alchemy and never seen anything like this!"

"Can alchemy really bring the dead back to life? ...This has to be cheating!"

"How could that be!?" Beelzebub frowned. For all his vast experience, he had never seen anyone resurrected after being reduced to a puddle of blood.

"Is there really an alchemical concoction that can revive the dead...

Alice awkwardly averted her gaze, for Cladi had just regenerated and was completely naked, his backside facing the onlookers.

Merlin remained silent, harboring suspicions in his heart. Magic that could resurrect the dead was exceedingly rare, and most of those who awakened did so as undead, remaining under the control of hell—hardly true resurrection in any meaningful sense.

But what Cladi had just done left Merlin incredibly astonished. To be reduced to a pool of blood and yet regenerate again—it was as if he had broken the very rules of nature.

Cladi, half-naked and rather indecent, picked up his discarded robe and wrapped it around himself, smiling as he asked, "Are you satisfied, Your Highness?"

"Incredible skill! Truly divine, Your Highness!" Blitz was extremely excited, utterly impressed by Cladi's techniques.

"Be quiet." Margaret shot Blitz a disapproving look before turning to Cladi. "You certainly have remarkable abilities. I wonder how you managed it?"

"I have traveled the world researching ancient civilizations and witnessed many wondrous things. The potion I just used was merely the simplest application of the art of false death." Cladi answered briefly.

"What is the art of false death?" Margaret asked curiously. She had never heard of such a thing.

"As everyone knows, ancient peoples had to contend with many powerful monsters, and even the oppression of gods... To prevent their vitality from declining and maintain a youthful state, the ancestors developed the art of false death, which allows one to remain at their peak forever. I merely understand a fraction of it. Gregory of our Great Britain is the true master of this art." Cladi explained meaningfully.

"Gregory?!" Blitz gasped, feeling as though he had heard a thunderous name. Rumor had it that the old man was already several hundred years old. In his youth, he served as a court mage and campaigned alongside Great Britain's founding emperor. Later he became a Purple Gold adventurer and faded completely from public view, though it was recently reported that he was struck down by the great swordsman Elgin and still has not awakened.

"Your Highness, might I ask if I now qualify to treat His Majesty the King?" Cladi inquired.

"Of course. You are now a distinguished guest of France." Margaret stepped aside. "Please." Soldiers formed neat ranks and interlocked their spears, presenting a simple welcoming ceremony—the highest honor extended to foreign dignitaries. The crowd, unable to contain their curiosity, buzzed privately with enthusiastic remarks about Cladi, especially regarding the wondrous art of false death.

"This human is no ordinary person. He appears frail on the surface, but is actually quite dangerous...." Beelzebub murmured.

"Why do you say that?" Merlin asked in confusion.

"Ancient magic and martial techniques have always been overbearing, far more powerful than what we use. Anyone who can wield that kind of power is by no means a pushover."

In the Nil Desert, sandstorms swirled in every direction, and the heavily weathered mountains resembled hornets' nests riddled with holes. Yet these very formations made for excellent hiding places. Although the entrances were densely scattered, an ordinary person who entered would never find their way out and would surely lose their bearings. This was the mysterious site of the Dracula Ruins, located deep within the mountain's core region, with a labyrinthine interior.

It was pitch black inside, yet the sound of an underground river surging could be heard. Venturing deeper revealed a breathtaking spectacle—sharp formations like fangs ringed the center, a massive cruciform altar stretched across the cavern, and beneath it flowed a churning river of blood. The entire space was suffused with the scent of blood. This altar-like structure appeared to be a resting place crafted specially for Dracula himself. The dark coffin at the center radiated an aura of solemn grandeur, exuding an eerie, unapproachable feeling.

One had to admit that the wealth accumulated by the blood clan over several centuries could rival multiple empires. Mountains of dazzling gold glittered brilliantly, countless precious jewels were piled high, and even legendary weapons lay scattered among them. Any person witnessing such an opulent scene would likely find their feet rooted to the spot, captivated beyond measure by such incomparable treasure.

At the edge of the altar, Miranda was imprisoned in a cage, restless and anxious. She repeatedly poked at the lock mechanism with a small wooden stick, trying to figure out how to escape, but without any thief's skill, her futile efforts were useless.

"Stop wasting your strength. You can't escape. You'd be better off eating well and sleeping soundly until you're plump and fat..."

"You—" Miranda glared furiously at the suddenly appearing Medes and cursed, "My brother will never let you off!"

"Hah, how terrifying. Perhaps your brother is out there slaughtering people as we speak, but so what? He still can't find you." Medes found Miranda's naivete thoroughly laughable. Beelzebub was hardly invincible or unconquerable.

"Our father sleeps within that coffin. When he awakens, it will be the end of us all."

"Even your brother Beelzebub will not stand a chance against the Blood King...."

title: Chapter 18 — The Vampire's Poison
content:
Chapter 18 — The Vampire's Poison

Volume 18 · Chapter 18

“You're lying! My brother is one of the greatest Demon Lords, how dare you speak to him like this... you'll surely face a terrible end...”

Miranda mustered her courage to counter Medes, still believing Beselius would come to save her.

Although Miranda was a demon, she lacked the ferocity demons were supposed to have. Her weak personality was the complete opposite of Beselius.

To those who didn't know them, it would be impossible to imagine these two were siblings, with a ruthless older brother and a weak younger sister behind him.

“Hmph, look at your pitiful state. I almost feel sorry for crushing your last hope,” Medes sneered, speaking calmly. “If you're lucky, you might get to see your brother defeated. But you won't even get to see him one last time.”

Miranda gritted her teeth, but due to her timid nature, she couldn't lash out. She could only hope her brother would find her.

“Lord Medes,” Lamb entered from outside, looking worn out, as if he had been gathering information. Although Medes had no intention of returning to the capital, he still needed to understand the external situation. Once Dracula awoke, they could immediately begin the bloodline's path to dominance.

Medes ignored Miranda and walked up to Lamb, asking in a low voice, “What's the situation outside? Has Beselius started a massacre because he can't find his sister?”

“No,” Lamb shook his head.

“Huh? What's going on?” Medes frowned, disliking unexpected events.

“Beselius has been defeated. Margaret has taken control of the empire again, and the chaos is gradually being quelled,” Lamb said seriously.

“What? Beselius was defeated? Who did it! Where in the empire is there still a powerful enough figure to rival a Demon Lord?” Medes looked utterly stunned.

“I don't know. It's said to be an adventurer from Britannia, possibly the same one who killed Lady Camilla,” Lamb speculated.

“Ugh! I thought Beselius would cause chaos in the empire, and we could benefit from the chaos. Now it seems things have become much more complicated,” Medes frowned, his mind growing irritated.

“Lord, should we return now and suppress Margaret? Otherwise, the empire will truly fall into her hands. With your status as a prime minister, you should be able to command widespread support upon your return,” Lamb thought they could return and suppress Margaret again, not allowing the empire to be handed over so easily.

“No, the situation now is that our father is about to awaken. We need to stay here to welcome him. Even if that little girl regains control of the empire, what difference does it make? Once our father goes on campaign, all of France will still become my paradise,” Medes remained calm, believing Margaret was not a threat and the situation was still under control. “Besides, we left Margaret with many troubles. It won't be resolved in a day or two. This gives us enough time to focus on maintaining the altar. Just the poison we gave the old king is enough to give them a headache. Imagine the respected old king turning into a terrifying night monster. Isn't that a very ironic thing?”

“I see. No matter how hard Margaret tries, she probably can't change the outcome of us ruling France,” Lamb's eyes burned with excitement, slightly easing his mind. He then shifted the topic, “But Lord, the human sacrificial offerings we brought are running low. If we continue like this, even if we kill them all, it might still not be enough to awaken our father. I still need a large amount of blood.”

“This...” Medes thought for a moment, realizing this was indeed a serious problem. If they couldn't resolve it, the plan would fail. “You take some people and go to the villages near our father's location. Capture all the humans there.”

“But that... wouldn't our hiding place be easily exposed?” Lamb hesitated.

“If our father awakens, do we still need to hide here?” Medes said meaningfully.

In the sleeping chamber, everyone was observing Claudius.

Margaret and Blaise looked tense, unsure of the old king's condition, hoping Claudius could find a solution.

Claudius changed into a new set of clothes and sat beside the old king, occasionally opening the king's mouth and flipping his eyelids, speculating on various possibilities.

“How is it?” Margaret couldn't help but ask.

“The situation is very bad, Your Highness. I'm afraid I'm also powerless. The Emperor has been poisoned deeply... Claudius showed a troubled expression. Even someone who could regenerate in snowwater was helpless against the old king in front of him.

“Are you joking? I brought you here for what! If you're powerless, why did you accept this task! Are you mocking me?!” Margaret became furious, her hope turning into disappointment, and she vented her anger on Claudius. “Bring him! Lock him up!”

“Hey, hey, hey, Your Highness, please calm down. Mr. Claudius came here to treat the Emperor. You can't lock someone up just because they have limited abilities,” Blaise quickly stepped in to stop the guards who were already stirring outside, saying in a low voice, “Besides, the other party is a Thorn Knight from Britannia. It would be inappropriate for Your Highness to arbitrarily punish them. It might turn a small issue into a diplomatic one.”

Margaret was so angry she was shaking, forcing herself to suppress her anger and taking a deep breath before saying, “I apologize, Lord Claudius. I was a bit impulsive earlier. Please don't mind.”

“It's fine. I can understand Your Highness's anxious mood. It's normal to be emotionally volatile. I'm glad you have such high expectations for me,” Claudius helplessly smiled.

“Do you know what kind of poison my father was bitten with? Why are you completely helpless?” Margaret asked politely.

“The Emperor's face is pale, his teeth have become sharp, his pupils are completely black, and even his blood is beginning to dry up. This is the poison of a vampire,” Claudius declared.

“Indeed...” Margaret recalled the news Merlin and Alice brought, feeling dizzy. “Medes isn't human at all. He's the legendary night monster.”

Blaise frowned, thinking that everything was now irrefutable. The empire had been harmed by dark creatures all along. No wonder Medes was so powerful. It turned out he wasn't human after all!

“If the Emperor was poisoned only slightly, I might still have a method. But now...”

Claudius shook his head, walked to the window, and suddenly pulled the curtains open, letting sunlight pour in. “The Emperor's condition has slightly improved,” he said. “But the Emperor has already begun to fear sunlight. Although he might be able to move around again in a short while, that won't be the original Emperor anymore. He'll become a vampire who craves blood and the night.”

title: Chapter 19 — World-Changing Star-Shattering Cannon
content:
Chapter 19 — World-Changing Star-Shattering Cannon

Volume 18 · Chapter 19

Margaret's heart skipped a beat upon hearing Claudius's words, instinctively glancing at the old king lying on the bed, feeling it was a time bomb left behind by Medes for her.

A mighty empire's monarch turning into a bloodthirsty monster—this would surely cause great turmoil if it got out.

Margaret clenched her teeth, her mind in a mess. Medes had left, but he hadn't stopped digging fatal pits for her.

Even Blaise, who was usually slow-witted, realized the gravity of the situation. "My lady, this can't go on. If the king becomes a bloodthirsty monster, it might cause panic among the people nationwide."

Margaret said nothing, knowing the consequences of the old king becoming a vampire. She would be suspected of being a dark creature, leading to a kingdom revolution and her being burned at the stake. The Church, those wolves in sheep's clothing, would also take the opportunity to stoke the flames, promote their faith, and lead a rebellion. At that time, France would become the pope's land. After all, alliances were fragile in the face of利益.

"Your ladyship need not be alarmed. If you are willing to use silverware now..." Claudius spoke with a meaningful tone, hinting that Margaret should kill the old king to eliminate any future troubles.

"Stop it. That is the one thing I cannot do." Margaret cut off Claudius's words, unwilling to commit patricide. Although it could ensure the kingdom's stability, she would become a criminal. "Sir, you are so learned. Is there no other way?"

Claudius thought for a moment and said in a very uncertain tone, "In my understanding, the poison of the bloodline cannot be cured. However, I believe there is a strange person who can find another way to resolve it."

"Who!?" Blaise asked impatiently.

"A purple-gold adventurer who lives in seclusion in the French Forest of Vincennes, named Thetis. Her mastery of potions has reached an unparalleled level. She can use elixirs to bring flesh to white bones and poisons to wither all things. It is said that as long as a person has a breath of life, she can revive them there." Claudius recalled.

"Is this purple-gold adventurer that miraculous? How come I've never heard of her?" Blaise scratched his head, having never heard of such a person in France.

"That's because you don't know much about the purple-gold adventurers. They are all a few people at the peak, with eccentric temperaments and never showing their faces. Most live alone in sparsely populated areas. As far as I know, there are only five of them." Claudius explained, thinking it was normal for many people not to know about them, as there was no one else like Gregory, who also served as the guild master.

"How can we get this strange person to treat my father?" Margaret asked, grasping at the last straw.

"This is also something I can't be sure of. Purple-gold adventurers have very eccentric temperaments and are very different from normal people. Whether they are willing to act depends entirely on their mood." Claudius couldn't guarantee that Thetis would save the king, as adventurers were generally reluctant to work for nobles.

"Ugh!" Margaret became frustrated, wanting to drag the purple-gold adventurer out of the Forest of Vincennes and beat her up.

"Even if she doesn't help, she has to help! If she resists, I'll set the Forest of Vincennes on fire!" Blaise, with a hot head, said a foolish thing.

"Haha, with your strength, you might not even get to light the fire before you die in the forest..." Claudius couldn't help but pour a bucket of cold water on Blaise to calm him down.

"...Blaise was embarrassed, thinking that the purple-gold adventurers were that strong?

"However, although adventurers don't like serving nobles, they also know that imperial stability is good for everyone. Perhaps if the princess personally writes a letter of earnest request, she might be willing to help you." Claudius comforted, thinking that how could you know without trying? Although adventurers were used to being free and散漫, they also understood what it meant to stand up for justice.

"Then I will write a letter later and send someone to the Forest of Vincennes." Margaret nodded, feeling a little relieved. "Thank you, sir, for helping us this time. I will surely repay you when the opportunity arises."

"Your ladyship doesn't need to be so polite. It's just a small favor. Queen Elizabeth has a high opinion of you. After hearing about the attack on France, she ordered me to come here immediately." Claudius had been traveling around, but upon receiving the queen's order, he came to France. "However, I'm a bit puzzled. Only one Demon Lord attacked, yet why was the capital city destroyed like this? As far as I know, the capital of France itself was built on an ancient ruin. Only you could use the power of the ancient civilization. Did you not use your pride and joy, the magic cannons?"

"Of course we did, but Beelzebub's power was too strong. Even thirteen legendary magic cannons couldn't deal with it." Margaret explained.

"Your ladyship might have a misunderstanding. I was not referring to these sidekicks, but the Star-Shattering Cannon located at the very center of the empire. If you had used this weapon, wouldn't you have been able to completely destroy even the Seven Demon Lords?"

Claudius asked with deep meaning.

"Er..."

Margaret's eyes widened in confusion. This was a state secret. Only the royal family would know about it.

Did that woman Elizabeth have spies who had already uncovered the empire's secrets?

So Margaret tried to calm her shocked feelings and asked with a trembling voice.

"Why would you know about the Star-Shattering Cannon?"

"Your ladyship need not be nervous. I am just deeply interested in ancient civilizations and know many stories from long ago. France was a gathering place for the ancients during the age of the gods. It's not strange that they have such things." Claudius smiled, letting Margaret relax her guard.

Margaret sighed in relief. It seemed she was too sensitive. "This thing absolutely cannot be used casually. After using it, the land of France might no longer exist and would completely disappear from this world."

"Your ladyship, please don't joke. I have no intention of coveting your country's treasures. I am just very interested in ancient civilizations. If your ladyship knows some secrets, I would be grateful if you could tell me." Claudius thought Margaret was talking nonsense. France was a large country. For such an empire to completely disappear, only a god's anger could do that.

"Sir, do you think I'm joking? You know so much about ancient civilizations, yet you don't know how terrifying their power is?" Margaret narrowed her eyes and asked.

"Although I know the Star-Shattering Cannon is definitely not an ordinary weapon, making France... disappear is a bit too exaggerated." Claudius sweated a cold sweat on his forehead.

"Believe it or not is up to you. I heard this from my father when I was a child." Margaret paused and whispered in a small voice.

"The Star-Shattering Cannon can only be used one last time now. It is so precious that no one can use it without permission."

"The first time the Star-Shattering Cannon was fired was during the age of the gods. The hero who killed the gods used it to shatter the gates of Asgard."

"The second time the Star-Shattering Cannon was fired was during the age of the elves. The elf king used it to tear apart the continental map, seizing a large area of land to establish the United Kingdom."

"Every time the Star-Shattering Cannon is used, it changes the world's格局 and history. Is it really appropriate to use it against the Demon Lord of Gluttony?"

title: Chapter 20 — Deification Stone
content:
Chapter 20 — Deification Stone

Volume 18 · Chapter 20

After hearing Margaret's counter-question, Clady fell silent, his expression turning contemplative.

He had never seen the Shattering Star Cannon's true power with his own eyes, but from their description alone, he could sense it was something terrifying indeed!

Against a weapon capable of tearing apart continents and blasting open the gates of the Divine Realm, what was the Gluttony Demon Lord? Perhaps no different from a mere fly.

But the Shattering Star Cannon's destructive power was so immense that it could already rival legendary divine artifacts. In anyone's hands, it would pose a tremendous threat.

Divine artifacts were things that could turn even a fool into a regional overlord — beings capable of freely manipulating the forces of nature, even altering the world's固有 rules.

Clady felt that France was not a kingdom to be trifled with. That dreadfully terrifying Shattering Star Cannon alone was more than enough to keep them unshaken — a colossal deterrent.

Though Britain was hardly some small human nation either, its overall strength was overshadowed by France's cannon. In any conflict, the only outcome would be mutual destruction.

"If the Shattering Star Cannon has this kind of power, it would be a waste to use it against the Gluttony Demon Lord. Saying ancient sages would describe it as crystallized destruction wouldn't be an exaggeration. Your Highness, might I request a glimpse of the cannon?"

"I know you've been of great help to us, but that is our empire's highest classified secret. As a knight of Britain, I'm afraid it wouldn't be appropriate..." Margaret declined tactfully.

"That's true, then let it drop." Clady let out a dry laugh, somewhat disappointed. "I came at Her Majesty's orders to assist. Might I ask if Your Highness needs anything else?"

"If possible, I would like you to stay for a while and help us defend the empire. That bastard Mades is an evil vampire; his turmoil has left many lingering dangers. I need to stabilize the situation." Margaret thought for a moment before continuing. "That guy is ambitious — he will never give up easily. I guess he'll come back."

"Since you know the enemy won't give up, why not gather all your current forces and wipe them out?" Clady was puzzled.

"An old knight told me Mades fled westward with his men, but the west is endless desert — sparsely populated and hostile. Finding that bastard would be far too difficult. Do you think I don't want to kill him?" Margaret paused, then went on. "Mades is extremely powerful. We just suffered heavy losses from the Gluttony Demon Lord's attack. If he returns again, I'm afraid I'll be forced to choose mutual destruction."

"Uh, I hope Your Highness will calm down." Clady's eyebrow twitched. He understood Margaret meant to use the Shattering Star Cannon, taking the lives of the entire empire as collateral. "If the enemy is a vampire... then that's good..."

"What do you mean?" Margaret asked, confused.

Clady didn't answer. Instead, he opened his backpack, took out a small box, and when he opened it, a nail-sized silver ore gleamed inside. "With this, any vampire can be killed. Your Highness needn't bet the entire kingdom."

"...What is this thing?" Blaise casually picked up the tiny silver ore, speaking with a tone of slight disdain. "I once fought Mades and nearly died. You expect this nail-sized little stone to take him down? I don't think so."

"You don't understand, Lord Blaise. This ore is extraordinarily rare — even all of France would not be enough to exchange for it," Clady said proudly.

"What!?" Blaise was utterly baffled, unable to see anything unusual about the little ore. "What's so special about this thing?"

"This ore is called a God-Sealing Stone. It has the power to strangle souls and negate all regeneration, healing, and resurrection. I've spent half my life traveling every corner of the world, and only by chance did I find such a small fragment." Clady paused, falling into his habitual teacher's manner as he continued. "In the ancient era of gods, that Hero who slew the gods carried two swords. One was called Banri Garan — unremarkable on the surface, but capable of stealing vitality. It is said to now be in the demon race's possession. The other is the legendary God-Slaying Sword, Mistilteinn — the divine artifact that led the gods to destruction — forged from this very small stone you see here. Now can you understand how precious this metal ore truly is? It's a sacred relic capable of even killing gods!"

"Good heavens!" Blaise shuddered, suddenly taking the unremarkable stone seriously. An ore used to forge divine artifacts — utterly unheard of!

"I understand something about vampires. Their most difficult trait is their overwhelmingly powerful healing ability. Aside from sunlight, there's almost nothing that can truly kill them," Clady said calmly.

"Doesn't the gentleman not know about silver?" Margaret asked.

"From what I understand, silver only works on lower-ranked vampires. For example, Dracula — one of the three founder vampires who once ruled France hundreds of years ago — isn't particularly afraid of silver." Clady looked at the small stone. "This God-Sealing Stone is too small to forge into a proper weapon, but it can be embedded into the head of a blade. Once pierced into an enemy's body, even gods would struggle — let alone mere vampires."

"In that case, this is truly a precious treasure..." Blaise gazed entranced at the nail-sized God-Sealing Stone.

"Naturally. I'm willing to lend the God-Sealing Stone to you, but after the crisis passes, please return it to me." Clady wasn't a philanthropist — he couldn't just give away something this precious.

"Thank you, sir. With this, Mades is nothing to fear." Margaret stole a glance, secretly wanting to keep it for herself.

"Someone!" Blaise closed the lid and called over a guard, handing the God-Sealing Stone to him. "Take this to the Highness's bedroom and keep it well-guarded."

The guard nodded respectfully and withdrew without raising his head the entire way.

"It's getting late. Shall I have someone see you to your quarters?" Margaret planned to arrange for Clady and Merlin to stay together.

"Not urgent. I'm not the only one who came to reinforce Your Highness this time. Another Thorn Knight will be arriving shortly. Let me calculate the timing..." Clady put on a thoughtful expression. "Should be arriving now."

On the palace walls, two guards were dozing when a piercing cold wind suddenly woke them.

They panicked and sprang to alertness, only to find themselves engulfed by a massive dark shadow. Looking up, they were nearly scared to death —

"That... what is that!?"

"Enemy attack!? It's an enemy attack, right!... Go notify the Highness immediately!"

A colossal black mountain eagle — a giant hawk with steel-like black wings — battered the air with thunderous wingbeats. The wind it raised was so fierce it was impossible to keep one's eyes open, as if it were looking down contemptuously at the insignificant humans below.

The Black Mountain Eagle swept lazily across the palace sky. A graceful figure dropped from the heights, landing directly at the center of the palace courtyard.

She was striking and magnificent, yet undeniably beautiful, clad head to toe in exquisite silver-white armor, a purple-blossom-embroidered cape fluttering behind her...

None other than Mesfield, hailed as Britain's number one knight!

title: Chapter 21 — Third Wheel Beelzebub
content:
Chapter 21 — Third Wheel Beelzebub

Volume 18 · Chapter 21

Messfield's sudden arrival scared the guards patrolling the palace; given the repeated attacks on France, even the slightest rustle could put everyone on edge.

Rustling footsteps came frequently as the guards gathered, armed weapons at the ready, treating Messfield as an intruder who had breached the royal palace.

A guard captain stumbled toward Margaret, his voice still shaky as he reported, "Your Highness! There is an intruder!"

"Dismissed. A guest is here." Margaret replied coolly.

"Huh!?" The guard captain froze. If this were truly a guest, wouldn't they simply walk in?

"What are you standing around for!? Dismissed!" Blaise roared loudly.

Hearing Blaise's lion-like shout, the guards obediently retreated like a receding tide, restoring peace to the palace courtyard.

Cradle walked down the steps to meet Messfield, greeting her with a smile. "Windsor, you're finally here."

Seeing Cradle, Messfield's eyes naturally revealed a trace of respect. "Long time no see, Teacher Cradle. Where have you been?"

"Many places. Wherever there's news of ancient civilizations, I go to investigate. I wonder how the Empire is doing?" Cradle asked.

"Although there was much chaos before, ever since Her Majesty the Queen took the throne things have improved greatly. Everything is normal now." Messfield answered seriously.

"I heard rumors of the earlier chaos while I was away. It's a pity that I myself was tied up with my own affairs and couldn't return. I feel truly guilty." Cradle showed an apologetic expression.

"Teacher, there is no need to blame yourself. All of that is in the past." Messfield reassured Cradle.

"Yes, it's all in the past. Her Majesty must have been blessed by the gods — she always manages to turn danger into safety at critical moments. This time I heard it was thanks to that mysterious swordswoman who turned the tide with nothing but her own strength. I wonder where that hero is now?"

Even while abroad, Cradle had heard of Grandmaster Elgin's exploits. Those things nearly impossible for ordinary people — the man seemed capable of accomplishing them all, with nothing able to stop him.

Eliminating the Red Beard Pirate Fleet, saving the entire city of Elgin and the coastal regions.

Crushing the Hellfire Legion summoned by the former kingdom, foiling the former kingdom's schemes.

Destroying the elf's lamentation of the Three Taboo Magics, preventing the return of the dark elf king Arthedore.

Severely striking the once world-shaking Phantom Flame Demon General with his anger, quenching the Dark Guild's ambitions.

Punching the Orichalcum-tier adventurer Gregory so severely that he lies comatose to this day.

Crushing the Over Family rebels and executing the powerful figure from the mysterious seas...

Cradle found Grandmaster Elgin's deeds utterly unbelievable. These were absolutely not something an ordinary powerhouse could accomplish — just any one of them alone was sufficient.

Cradle had studied many ancient civilizations and was somewhat familiar with the legendary god-slayer who slew the pantheon. Grandmaster Elgin bore a striking resemblance to that mythical slayer — both had an untamed arrogance and an air of looking down on everything!

Even counting back a thousand years, Cradle felt almost no one could stand against Grandmaster Elgin in battle. The only exception might be O'Brien, the Hero of the Spear hailed by the Holy Church as humanity's genius — he alone might possess the ability to contend with Grandmaster Elgin.

"That man... after the parade held in the capital, he simply never appeared again. Her Majesty once tried to persuade him to stay, but he refused." Messfield furrowed her brows, seemingly unwilling to recall that detestable man. "Hmph, what an ungrateful bastard!"

Though Messfield boasted bravado, wishing she could cleave Grandmaster Elgin in half with her sword, deep down she acknowledged that his strength was indeed invincible.

Messfield would never admit, even to herself, that she was inferior to Grandmaster Elgin — she often belittled him verbally.

Fortunately, Grandmaster Elgin seemed to have evaporated after the parade, and she hadn't heard any news of his activities since. Messfield had enjoyed a rare stretch of peaceful days.

Still, Messfield sometimes thought back to that man who spat on the ground. Though his personality was foul, on the whole he seemed like a decent sort. It was a bit regrettable that he had simply vanished like this.

"It's such a waste that someone with his abilities cannot serve the Empire. I was actually thinking of recommending that Her Majesty confer upon him the title of Thorns Knight." Cradle sighed.

"Huh!? Absolutely not!" Messfield shook her head frantically as if shocked by electricity.

"Why? That swordswoman's strength is formidable. If we could recruit her, it would be a tremendous boon for the kingdom." Cradle looked puzzled.

"J-just... no! That bastard has a terrible personality — he's hardly a proper person! How could he possibly qualify to be a knight!? Working alongside him would be an insult to me!" Messfield resisted with her whole being.

"Windsor, I admire your knightly spirit, but sometimes you must be realistic." Cradle spoke in a didactic tone.

"... " Messfield was left speechless, thinking it would be best if that bastard never appeared again!

"Is this the famed First Knight of Britannia? Truly a person of outstanding bearing." Margaret stepped forward to observe her, sensing that Messfield's aura was comparable to Blaise's, though slightly weaker than that mithril-rank adventurer, Alice.

Seeing Margaret, Messfield bowed slightly. "Greetings, Your Highness. I have come to your aid under the orders of Queen Elizabeth. Should you need any assistance, please do not hesitate to ask."

"No need for such formality. Britannia and France shall enjoy everlasting friendship. I shall always remember your kindness." Margaret nodded politely, then introduced the subordinate beside her. "This is my knight, Blaise — the First Warrior of France. You happen to be Britannia's number one as well. Both of you are at the peak of your kingdoms' strength, so you likely share much in common."

"Oh, hello." Messfield straightforwardly extended her hand in friendliness, but Blaise did not move for a long time.

Margaret, displeased at the sight, glared upward —

And saw that Blaise looked like he had lost his soul, his gaze fixed motionlessly on Messfield, who was shorter than him. A strange flush rose on his bronzed face. So the humble First Warrior fancied this type!?

Though Messfield was a girl, she was a knight brimming with heroic vigor — a combination that completely overwhelmed Blaise, a simple-minded muscle man.

Tch!

Margaret felt somewhat embarrassed. Her knight had been won over at first sight, wearing the most obnoxious foolish grin. Unbearable!

So Margaret secretly and viciously stomped on Blaise's foot, signaling him to mind his manners and not make her lose face.

"Hiss!" Blaise drew in a sharp breath and finally came to his senses. He quickly grasped Messfield's hand. "Senior — er, hello! I am the First Strong Man of France. When you have time, we can exchange ideas properly."

"... " Messfield wore a blank expression, finding the towering knight before her utterly silly.

"Sigh, what a disappointment..." Margaret thought that Blaise, who spent every day by her side, should have long been immune to beauties. Yet here he was, conquered so easily — what a disgrace!

Inside the mansion, the three of Merlin's party were idly lounging about.

"Was that the Thorns Knight just now? She looked refined and gentle, but her skills are actually quite formidable," Alice told Merlin.

"Pfft, what's so great about that? A total noob." Beelzebub pouted disdainfully.

"Tch! Merlin, let's get rid of that eyesore, okay?" Alice had long been annoyed by Beelzebub. She and Merlin were enjoying their sweet couple time, and here came a third wheel ruining it!

"Ah..." Merlin responded awkwardly.

"Why drive me away? Are you two trying to have some private moment, and I'm just in the way?" Beelzebub sneered coldly. "Go ahead, just pretend I don't exist."

"You... what are you talking about!?" Alice abruptly stood up, angry enough to draw the slender sword at her waist, though her words betrayed her true feelings.

"... I never once thought about anything so dastardly... phew..."

title: Chapter 22 — Joan of Arc's Visit
content:
Chapter 22 — Joan of Arc's Visit

Volume 18 · Chapter 22

Alice, being a pure girl, naturally wouldn't feel good after being slandered like that by Beelzebub.
But thinking about cheering for love, Alice's face flushed red and her tone became uncertain.
"Humans are all... their minds are only about reproduction, no different from livestock. Maybe this is your humans' way of survival? After all, you're so weak, you can only win by numbers." Beelzebub sneered, showing disdain.
"...You're nonsense!" Alice, furious, protested, "I just can't stand you being here!"
"Hah, fine~" Beelzebub snorted, continuing, "I'd actually like to leave, but Merlin would never agree."
"Shout!" Alice, unwilling to yield, started urging the cold-faced Merlin, "Get him to leave quickly! I've never met such an annoying guy; I can say anything and he'll belittle me!"
"But if Beelzebub leaves, whatever he does outside will be completely out of control. What if he causes an attack on the royal capital?" Merlin countered Alice.
"...Alice really had no good way to handle this Beelzebub trouble, so she angrily said, "How annoying, causing trouble everywhere still needs us to clean up...."
"Ah?!" Beelzebub startled, baring his fangs angrily, said, "What does it have to do with you? You're just Lucifer's pet; don't think too highly of yourself, foolish human."
"Who are you calling a pet!" Alice's anger flared, she wanted to stab him with a sword.
"Who else could I say?" Beelzebub smirked, "This is already demon territory, you filthy bug, get lost as far as you can."
"Shut up! Demon territory? What a joke, this is clearly my and Merlin's temporary base!" Alice thought she shouldn't shelter Beelzebub, couldn't help but be unsettled, and he was so annoying.
"Can you guys quiet down?" Merlin glanced at Beelzebub, "I asked you to stay so we could look for Miranda together; you may not respect humans, but don't hurl insults."
"Isn't it this guy causing trouble?" Beelzebub coldly glared at Alice, muttering, "Flirting, sending autumn waves, like a *...."
"You!" Alice, embarrassed and angry, her face flashing red then white, a chill burst from her body, "Come out! Let's duel!"
"Heh, you're not strong enough." Beelzebub grimaced, licked his lips with his tongue, "If Merlin hadn't stopped me last night, you'd already be a pile of dung~"
"...Alice recalled Merlin guarding her last night, feeling an inexplicable surge of courage and warmth, complaining, "It's not your fault; otherwise Merlin would have to waste energy on you? Hurry up and find your sister and get lost, this isn't your territory."
"Fine, when I return to the Demon Lord's Palace, I'll definitely find a way to restore him to the Demon Lord's throne." Beelzebub stared at Alice's eyes, mocking, "In any case, I will absolutely not let you, a human, have your way."
"Nonsense! Merlin... Alice's face spread with layers of dragon scales, her eyes blazing with golden fire, "Merlin will never go back!"
"Tsk!" Merlin, somewhat annoyed by Beelzebub's foul mouth, "Don't say more things to provoke her; after all, we're fine, you're the trouble."
"Being in the same house with lowly humans is already my limit; you should thank me for not tearing the house down in anger." Beelzebub said arrogantly.
Merlin sighed, thinking it was too hard to change this old stubborn Beelzebub's mind, so he only could pull Alice aside.
"Alice, calm down, don't listen to Beelzebub's nonsense; he's always been like that."
Alice's dragon scales on her body slowly receded, she lifted her head and stared into Merlin's eyes, "Will you really return to the demon race?"
"Why are you suddenly so serious?" Merlin felt bewildered.
"Actually I didn't sleep last night, I heard some of your conversation." Alice lowered her head, hesitating for a while, then said, "It seems you can't completely sever ties with the demon race, right? Some things still have restrictions."
"Indeed." Merlin didn't hide it, demons mixing with humans is inherently strange, let alone the fact that the two sides are opposing camps.
"If... if my presence pressures you, then... then you should leave." Alice said without lifting her head; she had been thinking for a long time since last night, feeling that if she truly caused trouble for Merlin, it'd be better to give him freedom.
"Huh? Why?" Merlin's expression turned astonished, feeling Alice was acting strange; normally he wouldn't let himself leave, and would even worry she'd run away.
"Being by your side will only deepen misunderstandings; violating taboos etc., the demon race is your homeland, you might face many accusations." Alice didn't really want Merlin to leave, but she said, "I think this is unfair; if you want to return to your homeland, then... then go ahead..."
"If I leave, will you have to pay those astronomical debts alone?" Merlin glanced at Alice, unable to see her expression at the moment.
"I can manage on my own," Alice stubbornly said.
Merlin's expression was strange; even if he wanted to run away, he couldn't go to the demon race, the curse not lifted, he could only wait to die.
However, seeing Alice's shoulders slightly tremble, Merlin felt somewhat moved.
Clearly, at first I feared you'd sneak away, but now you're not thinking of causing me trouble, but rather wanting to give me freedom?
Really can't understand this woman; sometimes she's stone-hearted, sometimes overly kind.
"Before we finish what we're doing together, I definitely won't leave."
"Really?!" Alice suddenly lifted her head, tears glimmering at the corners of her eyes, recalling Merlin and Beelzebub's conversation last night, which didn't seem like a joke; maybe if this continues, Merlin will face pressure from the entire demon race.
"You're crying?" Merlin frowned, seeing Alice's eyes a bit red, thinking her words were surely spoken unwillingly.
...No, it's just... this is getting into sand... Alice hurriedly lowered her head, pretending to be upset about something hard to bear.
"Don't be hard on yourself; just pretend last night's words never happened, Beelzebub just doesn't like me." Merlin smiled, his tone relaxed, he handed Alice the red apple he'd taken a bite of, "Eat an apple and you'll feel better; no one in this world can twist my will, not even the demon race...."
Alice saw the apple, noticed the neat tooth marks, and embarrassingly pushed it back, "I don't want what you've bitten, it's gross..."
"Uh... Merlin rolled his eyes, thinking this guy was just pitiful a moment ago, now he starts finding himself disgusting? Can't figure it out...."
Beelzebub expressionless, watching this pair of lovebirds release their flashbang, thinking, "Damn! Is Lucifer planning to go down this road to the end? Even if I don't snitch to the council, it won't stay hidden long; the demon race will use all its power to suppress."
At that moment, a knocking sound "dong dong dong" rang out—
"Alice, I'm Joan of Arc, here to see you."
Merlin—upon hearing it was that Holy Church's saint—was instantly frightened, his face instantly turning pale!
Not long ago, Beelzebub had almost beaten Joan of Arc to death, yet here he sits openly!
Something's going to happen =

title: Chapter 23 — Joan's Interrogation
content:
Chapter 23 — Joan's Interrogation

Volume 18 · Chapter 23

Alice looked at Merlin in confusion, completely caught off guard by the sudden visit from Joan.

Beelzebub was still in the house, and if he was discovered, it would be a nightmare to explain.

Given Joan's reputation as an Inquisitor, she was almost certain to see both Alice and Merlin as accomplices of the demon race and sentence them to the stake.

Alice fully understood the Holy Church and the demon race were natural enemies, and if they met, they would definitely fight to the death.

"Merlin, what should we do?"

"I..."

Merlin was also flustered, finding Beelzebub to be a hot potato.

"Who is it? Joan?" Beelzebub blinked, as if he had already forgotten about the saint. "Oh~... that guy I beat up until he was crying?"

"Beelzebub, you should find a way to hide," Merlin suggested, thinking that if this guy was discovered, it would be a real problem to explain.

"What for!?!" Beelzebub's temper flared, his nose in the air. "The other person is just a defeated opponent. There's nothing to be afraid of. She should kneel before me and show submission, or I'll kill her!"

Merlin's head immediately swelled with frustration. Communicating with this old stubborn demon was so difficult. "Don't always threaten to kill people. Didn't we agree not to cause trouble? You just need to hide for a while!"

"No way! I'm a demon lord, why should I hide from a human?" Beelzebub said with righteous indignation.

"I'm worried you'll get me into trouble. Do you understand? I don't want to have to clean up your mess later!" Merlin's expression was anxious, and he had a sudden urge to kick Beelzebub out.

"Hmph, you're so weak. You were the former Demon Lord, yet you're so scared of the Church's dogs. How embarrassing!" Beelzebub smirked, unable to resist mocking Merlin.

"...I've had enough of you..." Merlin's vein throbbed on his forehead. He forcibly put the hat back on Beelzebub's head and狠狠 pressed his head down onto the table, making a loud "thud" sound. This would at least hide his face from view.

Although Merlin really wanted to kick Beelzebub away, he was afraid the noise would be too loud and hard to explain. Plus, with Beelzebub's stubborn personality, there was no way to persuade him. He could only deal with it this way for now.

"Lucifer! You bastard!" Beelzebub's head was pressed firmly onto the table, and he was still trying to struggle up.

"Cooperate with us. Don't make a scene, or you can forget about me helping you find Miranda." Merlin threatened in a low voice.

Beelzebub's whole body stiffened. Thinking of his sister, he deflated like a punctured balloon. "You'll regret this... just wait..."

Merlin felt it was about time to get through this. He nodded to Alice, signaling that they could open the door. As long as Beelzebub didn't cause trouble, everything would be fine.

Alice understood. She walked over and opened the door. "Joan? Why... why did you come suddenly?"

"I just had some things to ask you." Joan gave a simple explanation, then asked with suspicion, "You look flustered. What happened?"

"....Nothing, I'm fine..." Alice sweated coldly on her forehead, her eyes darting around nervously, giving off the impression of a thief caught in the act.

"Is that so?" Joan didn't think much of it, but she still felt something was off about Alice, as if she had done something wrong. "Why did it take so long to open the door just now? What were you doing?"

"I wasn't doing anything. The house was a bit messy... I just tidied it up a little."

Alice feigned calmness, thinking to herself, what should I do? If Beelzebub is discovered, wouldn't I be guilty of harboring a demon? How would I deal with the Church's pursuit then?

It seemed Alice hadn't realized she was a habitual harborer of demons, and had even hidden two great demon lords in her house. If this got out, it might scare a lot of people.

"Why go through so much trouble? You don't need to treat me like a guest." Joan was unbothered by small things. She wanted to sit inside but was stopped by Alice. "What? Are you not going to invite me in to sit for a while?"

Alice's nervous behavior was abnormal, and her speech was stammering. "....It's not necessary... um... there's not much... to sit in there, ha...."

"Why are you so strange?" Joan's alertness as an Inquisitor rose. The reactions of humans who had hidden dark creatures were exactly like Alice's!

"I am? It must be your imagination." Alice laughed nervously, not daring to meet Joan's gaze.

Joan's intuition told her there was definitely something hidden in the house. So instead of playing games with Alice, she forcefully pushed her aside and entered the house.

"Joan!?" Alice was completely stunned, not expecting Joan to be so unreasonable.

Joan's eyes were like a hunting dog's, quickly scanning the entire room and finally locking onto the suspicious figure pressed under the table by Merlin.

Normally, only Merlin and Alice lived here. The sudden appearance of a third person was highly suspicious.

Combined with Alice's guilty behavior just now, Joan couldn't help but become alert.

Seeing Joan's suspicious gaze fixed on Beelzebub, Merlin's heart tightened. He quickly covered for him. "Miss Joan, what a surprise to see you. You're a rare guest."

Joan glanced at Merlin, then automatically ignored him. In her eyes, this useless man was just a pretty face. She couldn't understand why Alice was so devoted to him.

"Who is this person? I definitely didn't see him yesterday."

"He...." A bead of sweat rolled down Merlin's forehead. He was thinking of making up an identity for Beelzebub to get through this, but it had to be convincing.

Beelzebub, who had been pressed on the back of his head by Merlin all along, was already in a bad mood. Now, being questioned by Joan, this weakling, from a position of superiority, made him furious.

"Hmph! Defeated opponent, I'm your father!"

"! ! ?" Joan's eyes widened. She hadn't expected the other person to be so disrespectful right away. She suddenly reached for the pseudo-sacred spear on her back and angrily asked, "Where did you come from, you arrogant fool? How dare you openly insult a clergyman! You should be locked in the dungeon to listen to the Goddess's teachings!"

"Phlegm!" Beelzebub grumbled, spitting out a mouthful of words. "Do I need to listen to the teachings of a stinking whore? The sky is vast, the earth is vast, but I am the biggest! You bunch of holy dogs! One day, you'll all die!"

"Despicable heretic, spewing filth! Your soul has already been corrupted by demons. Come out and accept your punishment! You need to purify your sins. Disrespecting a clergyman is an insult to the Goddess!" Joan's cheeks twitched with anger. She directly took the sacred spear from her back and pointed it at Beelzebub, filled with killing intent.

"Absurd, I'm originally.... Puh! ! !"

Before Beelzebub could admit he was a demon, he was狠狠 punched in the stomach by Merlin, silencing him immediately.

Beelzebub was hit so hard his stomach churned, and his thin, bony body trembled slightly. He spat out a string of sour water, almost vomiting up his intestines.

"Knock... knock the duck's ass, you x traitor=."

title: Chapter 24 — Persuading a Return
content:
Chapter 24 — Persuading a Return

Volume 18 · Chapter 24

Belial was slumped over the table, completely dejected, his whole body twitching uncontrollably. He hadn't expected Merlin to be so ruthless.

Merlin's smile was all teeth and no warmth. He didn't bother explaining away the "traitor" label Belial had thrown at him. After all, it was Belial's own fault for not reading the room and trying to expose him.

Belial had nothing to fear and no reason to worry. If he got into trouble, he could just return to the Demon Lord Palace.

But Merlin couldn't do that. If his demon identity was exposed, he'd definitely be unable to continue living in the human world.

Merlin wouldn't let Belial cause chaos and ruin his own livelihood by accident.

Jeanne slightly furrowed her brow, not understanding what Merlin and this mysterious man slumped over the table were doing.

"Miss Jeanne, don't worry about it. This guy isn't very bright and often says nonsense. You don't need to pay attention to him," Merlin explained with a dry laugh.

"Is that so..." Jeanne's eyes were suspicious. She thought this mysterious man's words were very radical and didn't seem like a good person.

Alice, who had been holding her breath quietly beside them, quickly added, "Yes, this guy... he's a madman. He must have been through some kind of trauma?"

Belial was so angry he bared his teeth, wanting to lift his head and curse them out, but Merlin had him pinned down, so he could only mutter, "You two lovebirds..."

When Jeanne heard Alice say this man was a madman, she immediately believed it somewhat.

After all, although Alice was a fake believer, she was still someone who served the goddess.

If this madman was some evil character, Alice wouldn't have lied to her.

It seemed Jeanne, who was simple, still overestimated Alice. After hiding Merlin, could she not also be hiding another Great Demon Lord?

"So he's a madman. Do you know him?"

"We..." Alice was at a loss for words, looking at Merlin for help.

"We know him. This madman is a vagrant from Leicester, and we didn't expect him to end up in France. We plan to send him back home," Merlin made up a story on the spot.

"Is that so..." Jeanne relaxed, looking at Belial who was motionless on the seat. "This madman's nonsense will definitely cause a lot of trouble. Why not hand him over to our church? Many monasteries keep some mentally unstable people."

"This... this isn't necessary, is it?" Merlin broke out in a sweat. He thought if he handed Belial over, he'd definitely be considered a traitor of the demon race. "He still has a sister at home. He's not alone. Although his sister really hates him and thinks he's a pervert, always wanting to stay as far away from him as possible..."

Jeanne's eyes showed a hint of sympathy as she sighed, "What a lonely orphan."

"Er..." Alice felt awkward. She thought this was Belial, the Demon Lord who had almost killed Jeanne, and now he was being called an orphan. In a way, it was also his karma.

"Nonsense! My sister loves me the most! We're going to be together forever! You're the orphan! Your whole family are orphans!" Belial was so angry he unilaterally believed he was the most important person in his sister's heart.

Merlin frowned, thinking this idiot was saying what nonsense? Miranda had been so angry she ran away from home. What face did he have to say his sister loved him the most?

"What... what kind of perverted statement!?" Jeanne's face darkened, clearly shocked.

"Kurayami! You're just a defeated underling... Ugh!!!" Belial wanted to defend himself against being called a pervert, but suddenly Merlin covered his mouth, so he could only make muffled "Mmm" sounds.

"I'm warning you not to cause trouble. We're all on the same boat now. If you cause chaos, we'll all be finished," Merlin's expression turned serious as he leaned close to Belial's ear and spoke softly.

Belial rolled his eyes. He had never been so humiliated. He was full of contempt for Merlin. He shouldn't be so soft-hearted towards humans!

Jeanne sighed, having already considered Belial a mentally disabled person. She made the sign of the cross on her chest and sympathetically blessed him, "Poor soul. May the goddess protect you. I also hope your sister can find liberation."

Merlin and Belial both had strange expressions. They both felt extremely uncomfortable with the ritualistic blessing of making the sign of the cross.

"Alice, about yesterday's matter, I hope you can reconsider," Jeanne then turned to Alice and said, her tone very serious.

"What? What matter?" Alice blinked in confusion.

"I hope you can return to the church to serve as a Hero again and make contributions to spreading the goddess's glory," Jeanne got straight to the point. Yesterday, Alice had refused Archbishop Scott's invitation, and she wasn't very willing to give up.

"Let's not talk about this anymore. I've already decided not to return to the church," Alice helplessly smiled, thinking she didn't have any faith anyway. She had just been a temporary Hero back then. There was no reason to serve the church for life.

"What's so good about wandering around outside? Adventurers are just a bunch of insignificant people. If you return to the church, you'll definitely be treated well. Your status, reputation, and wealth will all increase. Aren't these exactly what you're pursuing?" Jeanne tried to persuade Alice.

"Didn't you always hate me, a fake believer? Why would you suddenly change your attitude?" Alice felt very strange. She knew Jeanne disliked her from the bottom of her heart.

"The situation is different. The church now desperately needs a Hero to inspire the entire church, and you are the best candidate. Your strength has improved rapidly and has already attracted the attention of the church's high-ranking officials. As long as you're willing, you can become a Hero again at any time. Isn't it a good thing to be admired and respected?" Jeanne paused, then looked down and said, "Although I despise you for being a fake believer, I'm very clear that I don't have the ability to become a Hero. Only you, who can stand on equal footing with the Demon Lord, can carry the goddess's banner! Defeating Belial is the best proof!"

"???" Belial was full of question marks. He thought when had this human woman defeated him!? He had clearly lost to Lucifer!

Merlin remained silent, looking at Alice and thinking that if she continued like this, it was only a matter of time before she became the center of attention. It was normal for the church to try to recruit her. However, being able to stand on equal footing with the Demon Lords was still far from reality.

"I used to really like status, reputation, and wealth, but now these things aren't important to me anymore," Alice shook her head.

"Oh?" Jeanne frowned, her gaze locking onto Merlin. "Because of this humble little lover? To be honest, I can't see what kind of charm he has that makes you so attached. You're even indifferent to the glory of being a Hero."

Merlin frowned, thinking what did he have to do with it? Wasn't it Alice herself who didn't want to go back? Why was it being brought up to him!

"This... has nothing to do with him. I just don't want to go back to the church anymore, hehe..." Alice explained with a slightly red face, completely unconvincing—

Who would want to go back to the church and be with those smelly priests!?

Merlin wouldn't even go back to be a Demon Lord. Why would I go back to be a Hero?

Besides, it was hard enough to get this cheap husband, I can't let him run off~

title: Chapter 24 — Righteous Faith
content:
Chapter 24 — Righteous Faith

Volume 18 · Chapter 24

"Alice, don't harbor any naive thoughts at a time like this. The Holy Church doesn't open its doors to a person again and again. If you refuse, I'm afraid there really won't be another chance to return to the Church." Jeanne's expression was serious as she spoke earnestly. "Besides, does a wandering adventurer who sleeps in the wind and dew possess the nobility of the Church's Hero?"

"Forget it, Jeanne. I won't change my mind on this matter." Alice responded with an equally serious tone, leaving Jeanne absolutely no room to maneuver.

Jeanne's brows knitted tightly together. She found Alice's stubborn temperament somewhat unbearable; in her view, this was simply failing to recognize a good thing.

Countless people like Jeanne could strive for an entire lifetime and never be granted the title of "Hero," yet Alice — she didn't want it at all!

No matter how powerful an adventurer might be, they were merely a bunch of brutes with nothing but martial strength, their status neither high nor low.

But a Hero was entirely different. In the hearts of the faithful, they were outstanding humans who could converse directly with the Holy Spirits, their status in no way inferior to the monarchs of the various empires.

Alice had repeatedly refused the Holy Church's cage — it was simply incomprehensible!

Jeanne was seething inside, but she couldn't vent it on Alice, so she could only look toward Merlin across from her, his face a picture of innocence.

"Is it worth it for this pretty boy? Honestly, aside from his skin, there's nothing praiseworthy about a guy like him. Even I could knock him down so he couldn't get up with a single hand."

"It's not like that... you've misunderstood..." Black lines cascaded down Alice's forehead like a waterfall.

"Hahaha, you've really hit rock bottom, being treated like a useless gigolo who lives off a woman. She even says she can knock you down so you can't get up with just one hand!"

Beelzebub burst into laughter. Merlin had once been a sovereign of equal standing to himself, yet after leaving the Demon Lord Palace he had become this miserable? It was unexpectedly hilarious.

In truth, in Beelzebub's eyes Merlin was still the First Demon Lord, the king who commanded the seven great Demon Lord legions, majestic and awe-inspiring.

But now he was suddenly being disparaged so by a lowly human, and Beelzebub truly found it hard to adapt in a short time — he himself wouldn't dare speak so arrogantly, yet his own defeated subordinate dared to?

"Shut your mouth."

Merlin's face darkened, and he secretly drove a fist into Beelzebub's abdomen.

"Pfft!" Beelzebub rolled his eyes continuously from the blow. "Bastard... I didn't say you were a pretty boy..."

"Miss Jeanne, which of your eyes sees me as a pretty boy?" Merlin's demeanor shifted as he retorted with a sneer. "Besides, you're not much yourself — a total tomboy. Calling you 'Miss' is out of respect; otherwise I'd have called you 'Big Bro' long ago..."

"....What did you say?" Jeanne raised an eyebrow, glaring at Merlin with displeasure. "A servant of the Goddess has no gender. My appearance has nothing to do with anyone."

"Aah~ Is that so? Then even if I really were a pretty boy, what would it have to do with you? You clearly have no right to disparage me, do you?" Merlin frowned, speaking in an impatient tone. "You Holy Church types are all the same — mouths full of high principles, yet your actions constantly contradict your words. Isn't that a double standard?"

"Well said! God-botherers are all the same!" Beelzebub agreed with Merlin for the first time, thinking that although this guy differed from other Demon Lords, his personality leaning human, in essence he was still a demon, right? A natural aversion to the Holy Church.

"Raving nonsense, daring to slander the Holy Church's purity!" Anger flared in Jeanne's eyes. She considered Merlin's words a grave insult to the Goddess, enough to take him back for a thorough interrogation.

"Stop fighting, stop fighting... they... they're just joking, hah...." Alice forced a laugh, trying to ease the tension between the two sides. As expected, a demon and the Holy Church sharing a room would come to blows within a few sentences — they were fundamentally incompatible as fire and water.

"Alice, why do all the people you know spout such evil rhetoric? To so easily speak disrespectfully of the Goddess — even wearing human skin, their hearts are black!" As an Inquisitor, Jeanne was extremely sensitive to this sort of thing. Under normal circumstances, both Merlin and Beelzebub would be guilty. "You hang around with these people day in and day out — how could you have a good end? No wonder you don't want to return to the Church. You've been bewitched and deceived, corrupted by these lot!"

"Jeanne, you've misunderstood. They're just speaking offhand — you're the one being oversensitive!" Alice knitted her delicate brows, feeling that Jeanne was the one who had been severely brainwashed, overcorrecting in every matter.

"The Goddess is forever just! Those who slander the Holy Church are undoubtedly villains!" Jeanne's eyes gradually filled with hostility.

"....Are you crazy?" Alice felt that both Jeanne and Beelzebub were extreme, impossible to understand.

"I'm crazy?" Jeanne's composed face instantly turned a pale gray, her eyes widening in horror. "Alice, you really have been influenced by evil. I truly regret coming to find you."

With that, Jeanne turned and walked away, her steps quick, clearly with a bellyful of fire she had nowhere to vent.

Alice did not stop her, merely watching quietly as Jeanne left. She had thought they could communicate properly, but the result was an unhappy parting.

After Jeanne left, Beelzebub regained his freedom and let out a long breath. "She's clearly just a defeated subordinate, yet her temper's not small. I somewhat regret not spending a bit more effort to finish her off back then."

"That's neither here nor there. Just the claim that the Goddess is forever just — I find it rather funny. Justice and such is far too cheap; any random person can claim it for themselves." Merlin spread his hands.

"Exactly. You can only say those old foxes of the Holy Church are too good at brainwashing. How many fools have perished in the campaigns against the Demon Lord Palace? To their dying breath they never knew they were merely pawns being used by others." Beelzebub spoke lightly.

"That's also why I loathe the Holy Church. They only know how to bewitch hearts with faith — such despicable means. Just who is the evil one?" Merlin sighed, wearing a look of not wanting to bother.

"When it comes down to it, all humanity is merely sacrificial lambs in the conflict between the Goddess and the demons. If the Holy Spirits could easily cross the barrier between the mortal world and the heavens, would they need to cultivate followers in the mortal world to deal with us? Obviously it would be better if the Goddess acted personally, no?" Beelzebub smiled, continuing, "The enmity between the demon race and the Goddess of Light runs deep, said to trace back to the Era of the Gods. That self-proclaimed demon, the God-Slaying Hero, killed her sister — otherwise she wouldn't be racking her brains trying to exterminate us."

"There's such a thing?" Merlin wore a puzzled expression, seemingly never having heard this history before. But from the sound of it, the demon race is the scapegoat!

"Yeah. Could it be your mother Vivian never told you?" Beelzebub asked in surprise.

"No." Merlin shook his head.

"You might be too young. This story was something Sloth happened to tell me once. He's the only first-generation Demon Lord, older than even the Elven King." Beelzebub said casually.

"Sloth, huh...." Merlin recalled slightly. There seemed to be some impression — a contemporary of the first Lucifer, an ancient monster, an elegant and noble old gentleman.

"Why did you have to say such nasty things just now? You clearly knew Jeanne is an Inquisitor who roots out evil, yet you kept trampling on her bottom line." Alice was unhappy, turning to question Merlin and Beelzebub.

"Does this need a reason?" Merlin looked at Alice.

"Yeah, no reason needed." Beelzebub curled his lip, speaking with contempt.

"Because... we're demons."

title: Chapter 26 — The Judgment Plan
content:
Chapter 26 — The Judgment Plan

Volume 18 · Chapter 26

Hearing Merlin and Belial's casual explanations, Alice was at a loss for words.

Of course they were demons, naturally inclined to despise the Holy Church.

But Alice felt it was a bit much to denigrate the Church entirely, even bordering on demonizing them.

Jeanne was a devout believer through and through, and to the faithful, faith in the Goddess of Light meant everything, more important than life itself.

"Don't you think that's going too far?"

"What? Do we have to grit our teeth and praise the Goddess's lackeys?" Belial raised an eyebrow.

"Even if the Church has its flaws, surely it's still more trustworthy than the demons who slaughter without restraint?" Alice argued, unwilling to back down.

"Oh really...?" Belial nodded with a sneer, "You used to be one of the Church's dogs yourself, your mind already twisted, using honeyed words to manipulate foolish humans—that's their standard tactic."

"You're lying! Many in the Church just want peace, they're not like you, a brute who constantly threatens humanity!" Alice furrowed her brows, recalling Belial's various deeds, and suddenly felt the Church's campaign against demons wasn't entirely wrong.

"How laughable, are we threatening humanity? Do you humans enjoy crushing ants beneath your feet for fun? That's just being gluttons!" Belial's eyes turned sharp, his voice growing heavier, "So we threaten humanity? Show me your evidence!"

"...Alice was speechless, thinking it over, she didn't have very convincing evidence. Though the demons were powerful and posed a threat, there was no record of them actively starting conflicts.

"In our era of great strength, at most we enslaved you, never sought to exterminate you. After the Demon Era, we retreated to remote places, almost never leaving the Demon Lord Palace to interfere with human lives. But you? You keep launching crusades, aiming to wipe out the demons entirely. So I ask you, who is truly evil to the bone?" Belial shot back with conviction.

Alice was left speechless by Belial's words, because the facts were undeniable—the Church always struck first, trying to hunt down the demons.

Each time under the banner of "eradicating evil and protecting humanity," it had become the norm.

The demons were evil and cunning, and the righteous Church, heirs to the Goddess of Light's will, were simply eliminating evil—there was no reason not to.

"The Church has killed countless demons in every war, and what I've killed... is nothing more than a drop in the ocean." Belial paused, waved his hand, "In the end, it's because humans are too stupid, becoming the Goddess's lapdogs. The root of all this is the conflict between demons and the heavens. Humans? At most, they're just the Goddess's front-line soldiers."

"...Alice's eyes still refused to agree, and she turned to Merlin, "You think the same?"

"Of course, Alice. You should know that history is written by the victors, no one records things fairly. Though I don't know what you saw in the Church, it's not necessarily the truth." Merlin was fairly supportive of Belial's words.

"So does that mean whatever the demons say is the truth?" Alice shot back at Merlin.

"That's..."

Merlin hesitated, because he couldn't guarantee that either.

The air fell silent. Belial glanced at Merlin, then at Alice, and suddenly realized something.

Oh~ So these two dogs weren't as harmonious as they seemed on the surface. Their relationship was fragile and full of distrust.

Just stir up some factional conflicts, and they'd fall apart easily.

Unless they completely abandoned their past, they couldn't walk forward together.

Thinking this way, he felt at ease. Lucifer's return was just a matter of time...

The night at O'Brien Cathedral reignited with lights, and many believers sought refuge here, receiving relief supplies from the priests.

Bishop Scott stood in the cathedral's upper gallery, looking down through the windows at the refugees below.

"Knock knock knock." Three knocks echoed, and Jeanne entered with a troubled expression.

"Bishop Scott, I'm back."

"Welcome back, my child." Bishop Scott slowly turned around, wearing a gentle smile, "What are the results? Has Alice had a change of heart and agreed to serve the Church?"

Jeanne shook her head, speaking with resignation, "She doesn't want to come back. I've tried my best to persuade her, but... it didn't work."

"Is it because the conditions I offered aren't good enough? His Holiness is kind-hearted, perhaps the debt she owes could be forgiven, and there's no need for her to remain a worn-out adventurer." Bishop Scott sighed, feeling his offer was already quite generous, certainly better than being an adventurer.

"I think... it's not about the conditions being good or not. Bishop Scott, you might be misunderstanding something?" Jeanne hesitated.

"Oh? What might I be misunderstanding?" Bishop Scott asked curiously.

"I think Alice doesn't want to return because of love." Jeanne furrowed her brows and slowly said, "She's quite fond of that black iron adventurer beside her, to the point of being willing to give up everything for this useless man. So no matter what conditions Bishop Scott offers, the real obstacle is still that black iron adventurer."

"Black iron adventurer? What charm does he have that makes Alice fall for him so completely? ...That's not normal. Even with Alice's current status as a mithril adventurer, she's far beyond him, it's clearly not likely... Bishop Scott's head spun trying to figure it out."

"I'm not entirely sure either. That useless man seems to be living off Alice, and I can't understand why Alice would like such a person?" Jeanne's expression carried clear disgust.

"This is getting complicated... Bishop Scott felt a headache coming on, grinding his teeth.

"Not only that, Alice herself has been influenced by that black iron adventurer, becoming somewhat strange?" Jeanne recalled the conversation, feeling Alice had already gone astray.

"What do you mean?" Bishop Scott asked with confusion.

"Alice's companions are outright criminals, openly spouting slanders against the Church and the Goddess, and Alice is even making excuses for them? Clearly her soul has been corrupted!" Jeanne said angrily, her teeth grinding with frustration.

Bishop Scott's face darkened, and after a moment of silence, he said, "Could this be true? To slander the great Goddess is to invite punishment, let alone seducing our Hero. It seems Alice's refusal to return must be due to being deceived."

"That's right, I think so too!" Jeanne's tone grew more intense, "That black iron adventurer spouts nonsense, he's nothing but the worst kind of heretic. If he weren't around, how could Alice refuse to resume her role as Hero?"

"If he weren't... that's well said, my child." Bishop Scott nodded, turned around, and said with meaning, "No one in this world can slander the Church, let alone the great Goddess. We are the ones executing divine justice. Everything that opposes the Church is evil heresy, and we shall purify them, letting the entire world bathe in light."

"What do you mean, Bishop Scott?" Jeanne asked in confusion.

"Take the opportunity, catch that black iron adventurer off guard." Bishop Scott made the decision to eliminate Merlin—this was the most effective and direct approach.

"I believe, as long as that heretic isn't there to mislead Alice, she'll surely return to the Goddess's embrace..."
