title: Chapter 26 — The Straightforward Fellow (One More Update Before Midnight)
content:
Chapter 26 — The Straightforward Fellow (One More Update Before Midnight)

Volume 18 · Chapter 26

Jeanne was truly taken aback, harboring doubts about the bishop's idea and momentarily at a loss.

Wouldn't it be going too far to simply eliminate that Black Iron-rank adventurer outright?

Although this man did have a significant influence on Alice, assassinating him didn't align with the Holy Church's proper image — it came off more like cowardly thugs.

Jeanne frowned, quite unwilling to engage in such underhanded deeds, her heart strongly resistant.

"Remember to handle this quietly, and preferably don't let anyone discover it, let alone suspect that our Church is behind it." Archbishop Scott, not noticing Jeanne's expression, continued talking to himself. "If Alice finds out we were the ones behind this, not only would we fail to win her over, but we might also awaken her rebellious side. It's not impossible for her to come to hate the Church and become an enemy."

"But Archbishop..." Jeanne raised her head, unable to hold back her objection. "Isn't this despicable? We are all servants serving the Goddess. We ought to treat everyone with goodwill, even if the other party is a wicked criminal."

"What you say is correct. We truly should not use such despicable means as assassination, which goes against the Goddess's teachings. But wicked criminals are not human — they can become clutches of evil at any moment. There's nothing wrong with strangling all dangers in their cradle." Scott looked at Jeanne and said gently, "Besides, Alice was once our companion. Now she has been influenced by people with twisted values. If we continue like this, Alice will fall deep into the muck of evil and be unable to extricate herself."

Jeanne lowered her head and fell into thought. She felt Archbishop Scott wasn't wrong. Assassinating wicked individuals, no matter how despicable the methods, was all in the name of promoting justice. Besides, Alice could roughly be considered her friend. She absolutely couldn't watch her continue to be bewitched.

"Don't feel doubtful. We are all doing this to save Alice's soul." Archbishop Scott kindly patted Jeanne's shoulder.

A few dark clouds obscured the moonlight, making the entire royal capital seem ever more gloomy.

Although the empire had initially returned to normal, it was still in a precarious state.

Places outside the royal capital began sending armies here one after another to further reinforce the royal city's defenses.

But right now, it must be said that the royal city's guards were quite lax — anyone could easily come and go.

Even Dicktep had disguised himself as a guard for so long without being discovered.

At the city gate, an exhausted guard lay on the ground fast asleep, clutching a spear in his arms.

Dicktep had long since shed his disguise and crouched down with great interest, using a brush to draw a turtle on the guard's face as mockery.

After looking at the work he'd left behind, Dicktep nodded satisfactorily, then casually took the guard's horse.

Mades fled toward the west? Then let's go try our luck in the desert. Perhaps there will be unexpected harvests...

I worked for those vampires for so long for nothing. Isn't it a bit excessive to just ask for some interest?

Besides, Mades had been a chancellor for so long — he must possess wealth rivaling a nation.

If I don't take a little something along the way, I wouldn't be Dicktep!

After leaving the city, Dicktep mounted his warhorse and, using the cover of night, galloped wildly toward the west.

He slowly took out from his chest a fingernail-sized stone that gleamed faintly in the darkness — it was exactly the God-Sealing Stone that Clardy had lent to Margaret.

With this thing, the vampires seemed to have nothing to fear...

Wealth, treasures, and even this empire — I want a share of everything!

In the mansion.

Clardy and the two Knights of Thorns, Mesfield, decided to stay in the royal capital for the time being and leave only after France was completely out of danger.

For some reason, Blaise was especially proactive today. Without Margaret having to ask personally, he volunteered to see the two of them off to the mansion.

Margaret didn't say anything. She pretended not to notice Blaise's frequent groveling, thinking he should know his place and wouldn't be seduced by the First Knight of Britain.

Still, Margaret couldn't help but feel uneasy. Before leaving, she reminded Blaise not to get too close to Mesfield and to always remember that he was a knight of France.

As for Mesfield? She was straightforward by nature. She thought that France treated foreign guests warmly this way. With Blaise's honest appearance, she clearly regarded this burly man as a comrade in the united front.

Mesfield and Clardy stepped down from the carriage. For the next period of time, the two of them would live here with Merlin and the others.

"Please rest here. If there's anything you need, I will personally notify you." Blaise said honestly. Normally such small matters could be handled by guards, but to see more of Mesfield, this honest guy became exceptionally diligent.

"Thank you for your care, sir. With Her Highness Margaret's abilities, the kingdom will soon return to normal. If there's any difficulty that needs help, please don't hesitate to ask." Clardy said gratefully.

"Good. Sir, you are kind-hearted and willing to help us in our time of crisis. We will certainly repay this kindness in the future." Blaise said very humbly, his words and actions showing great respect toward Clardy.

"This is all for the friendship between our two empires." Clardy smiled.

"Yes, yes, yes! Long live friendship!" Blaise scratched his head, unable to resist glancing at Mesfield beside Clardy. "Um... Miss Windsor, I wonder if you have time tomorrow? We... we could perhaps have a chat or something..."

Seeing Blaise's awkward speech, Clardy couldn't help but smile. Reading between the lines but saying nothing, he chose to stand silently aside.

"A chat?" Mesfield was even more direct than Blaise. After thinking for a moment, she said seriously, "You mean you want to spar with me? I'm willing to have an intense match with you, but you still have injuries. I think we should wait until you've recovered. I don't want to take advantage of someone's weakness — that would make victory seem undeserved."

......That's not what I meant...... Blaise became embarrassed, sweat dripping down his forehead from anxiety. Unfortunately, he was too clumsy with words and didn't know how to委婉ly invite a girl on a date.

"Sir Blaise, there's no need to be anxious. I know you really want to spar, but if it's not at full strength, then sparring would be meaningless." Mesfield placed her hand on her chest and said solemnly, "We are all knights serving royalty, representing our respective empires. For honor, we must give it our all."

Hearing this, Blaise looked at Mesfield with deep respect. His own resolve wasn't as high as hers, and he instantly felt ashamed of himself. "Miss Windsor is right."

After Blaise left, Clardy recalled his pitiful appearance and felt somewhat unwilling to let it be. He offered a hint to Mesfield.

"Mesfield, this Sir Blaise really admires you."

"I've noticed that too." Mesfield nodded, indicating she understood.

"You actually realized it?!" Clardy was very surprised. He and Mesfield were fairly familiar, and this young girl had an EQ in the negatives since childhood. How could she possibly realize Blaise's affections?

"I saw an immense intensity in Sir Blaise's eyes. This is a common trait among martial artists — a fanaticism for climbing to the peak of martial skills. When encountering an opponent of similar strength, you feel itchy hands. Not sparring would leave considerable regret." Mesfield nodded seriously. "Yes, I understand very well, because I'm the same. Blaise is much stronger than that lazy guy Morrison."

"......" Clardy slapped his own forehead. He felt whatever he said was like casting pearls before swine.

Two straightforward folks stuck together were destined to achieve nothing.

Looking at it, Windsor wasn't getting any younger. Hadn't she encountered any men worth appreciating?

If things continued like this, she might be destined to die alone.

title: Chapter 28 — Midnight Kitchen (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 28 — Midnight Kitchen (Extra Chapter)

Volume 18 · Chapter 28

Klaudi saw that Mesfield had no thoughts of romance at all, so she stopped bringing it up and asked about other things.

"Your Majesty didn't give you any other instructions when you came rushing over this time?"

"No, she only said that France will become our ally in the future, and we must pay attention to maintaining the relationship."

"High-sighted as always, Your Majesty. This world has many unpredictable evil forces. If humans cannot unite, they probably won't be able to withstand them." Klaudi nodded in agreement, thinking Elizabeth's decision was quite good.

"Klaudi teacher, you've been traveling outside all this time, you must have seen many novel things. Could it be that there is now a group capable of rivaling all of humanity?" Mesfield asked curiously.

"Of course. Although the current era belongs to humans, a small mistake and it's truly hard to say." Klaudi paused, giving examples. The demon race, this group, although legend says they suffered heavy damage from the Spirit a long time ago, resulting in their current decline, but their strength is still terrifying. I find it very hard to find an force that can confront them head-on, especially the seven Demon Lords. Saying they are the seven strongest monsters in the world is no exaggeration. If they can luckily recover their vitality, the era might possibly regress back to the demon age.

"So terrifying?" Mesfield looked coldly surprised. Although she had long known the demon race's power was formidable, it still exceeded her imagination.

"Yeah, I've seen many ancient texts. The demon race's civilization is in no way inferior to ours, even more powerful. They have high wisdom and strength comparable to dragons. Even in the age of gods, they were the only group capable of contending with deities." Klaudi paused, then suddenly relaxed and said, "However, for some reason, they can almost leave the Demon Lord Palace. The Gluttony Demon Lord appearing in France this time is truly anomalous.

"Klaudi teacher, you say the demon race is so strong, but I heard the Gluttony Demon Lord was repelled, and we humans don't seem weak either..." Mesfield had heard some rumors before coming.

"Repelled is not the same as defeated. There's a big difference in essence. Perhaps after the Demon Lords leave the Demon Lord Palace, their strength may greatly weaken." Klaudi analyzed. "I heard the person who repelled the Demon Lord this time is an adventurer from Britain, who lives in this mansion. Their power to fight a Demon Lord is probably a platinum-ranked adventurer. It's too late now, we shouldn't disturb them. Tomorrow we need to visit—."

"Platinum adventurer..." Mesfield's expression turned serious. The other party should be by no means inferior to that Gregory fellow. A second platinum adventurer has been discovered in the empire; this to some extent is good news.

"Windsor, you can try leaving Britain and taking a walk. You'll find our class is still under threat. Although the Church is gradually declining, its foundation is deep, and it can always transcend royal power with divine rule. The Southern United Kingdom led by the Elf King has enough power to flatten any place." Klaudi spoke like a teacher, telling Mesfield many unknown things.

Even excluding these, humans themselves face threats. The divided nations are too many, hostile to each other, making peace difficult. Even in some ancient texts recorded far-off mysterious East, there are existences called cultivators. They wear strange clothes, step on weapons and fly...

Mesfield felt very curious. In front of Klaudi, she was simply a child who had never left home. Every conversation impacted her worldview.

Under the guidance of the servants, both Mesfield and Klaudi were arranged to live in the mansion.

Both are noble guests from foreign lands, naturally enjoying the highest treatment.

But in the silent second half of the night, Mesfield actually walked out of her room.

Mesfield was so hungry she couldn't sleep. Her stomach was gurgling, very uncomfortable.

Actually, as a warrior, her appetite was large, about five times that of an ordinary person.

Others only need one piece of bread to suffice, she might need five or six, plus dessert.

Mesfield had always had a large appetite since childhood, related to the family's training method. She needs a large amount of food supplementation, otherwise she has no strength when fighting.

Although she had dined with Margaret before, Mesfield ate very little to avoid frightening the other party due to etiquette, which led to her not being able to sleep now.

"So hungry, where is the mansion's kitchen? Downstairs?"

Mesfield weakly leaned against the wall, walking downstairs. It was easy to find the mansion's kitchen by the smell of cooking oil, but although it was so late, there was already someone inside.

Merlin was sitting on a small stool, in front of a vigorously burning stove. On it leaned various foods, looking quite abundant.

Beelzebub was not being polite, greedily gnawing on the roasted chicken, eating it ugly, like a starving ghost reincarnated, not even sparing the chicken bones and swallowing them down.

"You this guy is so strong! So you can make things this delicious?! I never would have thought you have a chef's talent! Beautiful... rare delicacy!"

Hey, what's this... Merlin rolled his eyes, not taking Beelzebub's compliment to heart. This bastard only knows how to compliment when eating.

Just now, this big eater Beelzebub was woken up by hunger. He hasn't eaten for several days, almost going crazy from hunger.

His stomach made a sound as if it were thunder, his eyes glowing with green light, wanting to eat everything alive in front of him.

Beelzebub couldn't help but want to eat people. His gaze inadvertently fell on the sleeping Alice nearby.

Fortunately, Merlin did not relax his vigilance. All along staring at this guy. Out of necessity, he could only bring him to the mansion's kitchen to get something to eat.

Otherwise, if this Gluttony Demon Lord wasn't fake, and really lost his mind due to hunger, then trouble would be caused again.

"I've decided!" Beelzebub, while gnawing on the roasted chicken, mumbled.

"Huh?" Merlin tilted his head, not knowing what he was thinking?

"If you can't return to your original position, I can graciously allow you to be my chef. Then you at least won't end up homeless. Remember to feel grateful to me in your heart." Beelzebub spoke big words, in his heart he had already placed Merlin as his private chef position.

"Dream on, old man will never mix with you. If you want to eat in the future, you should kneel down and beg for a nest, and call me Merlin dad..."

Merlin starts collecting sons-in-law at this opportunity.

"....". Mesfield frowned outside, secretly observing the two people in the kitchen, her heart inexplicably puzzled.

Who are these two guys?

Coming to the kitchen to eat so deep in the night?

Saying that little yellow毛...

Why does it feel so familiar?

title: Chapter 29 — Criticism and Judgment
content:
Chapter 29 — Criticism and Judgment

Volume 18 · Chapter 29

Beelzebub was gnawing on a roasted chicken while sucking her fingers; anyone seeing such a wolfing-down display would feel hungry.

"By the way, does that woman by your side not get to eat this kind of stuff every day?"

"Hmm..." Merlin thought for a moment. He and Alice divided household chores; it wasn't as if he did them all alone. "Not necessarily. Sometimes she cooks, sometimes me."

"That guy really is fortunate. Now I somewhat understand why she always clings to you." Beelzebub paused, then added jokingly, "If I were a girl, I might develop a soft spot for you too, hehe~"

"Pfft! Don't say such disgusting things, I'm almost gonna—!" Merlin rolled his eyes, constantly stuffing firewood into the stove and turning the rotisserie so the chicken cooked evenly.

As a transmigrator, Merlin's understanding of cooking far surpassed that of most people. The simple trick of stuffing herbs inside the chicken didn't even exist in this world.

Food in this world was actually quite backward and monotonous. Even an amateur like Merlin could call himself a god of cookery here.

The fragrance of the roasting chicken slowly drifted from the kitchen to the outside, subtly tempting Maisfeld standing beyond the door and making her hunger grow worse.

So... so fragrant. What are they eating? It doesn't seem like ordinary food...

Maisfeld peered secretly through the door crack, unable to resist swallowing hard. Though she really wanted to go in and eat, she felt a bit too embarrassed.

However, no matter how much Maisfeld restrained herself, her stomach had already started protesting, emitting faint "gugu" rumbling sounds.

"Who!?" Beelzebub sensed the strange noise outside and abruptly raised her head, her fierce eyes looking as if she were guarding against an enemy.

"Hmm?" Merlin also looked up toward the door, wondering if Alice had noticed that he and Beelzebub were gone and had come downstairs specifically to find them.

"...Maisfeld felt an invisible pressure, feeling that her current state was somewhat humiliating. Here she was, the First Thorn Knight, her stomach growling in the middle of the night just searching for food."

"Who's out there? Alice?" Merlin called out tentatively, thinking that Alice's straightforward personality would surely kick the door open and come in to eat together. When had she become so reserved?

Maisfeld, caught in the act, pushed open the kitchen door and walked in boldly, her cheeks flushed as she sized up Merlin and Beelzebub with a somewhat拘谨 demeanor.

Beelzebub was still wearing her low-profile, tattered robe, her oversized hood covering her head, making it hard to see her face clearly—mysterious and secretive.

As for Merlin?... Maisfeld's gaze grew strange. The more she looked, the more familiar he seemed, especially the name on his adventurer credential. It felt like she had seen it somewhere before.

But she didn't recall knowing any iron-rank adventurer. She certainly wouldn't initiate conversation with someone of that level.

Just as Maisfeld was racking her brains trying to remember, Merlin had already recognized the knight he had frequently spat on, and blurted out instinctively—

"The First Thorn Knight?"

"Hmm?"

Maisfeld suddenly froze, thinking that indeed they had met before. How did he know who she was?

At this moment, Maisfeld wasn't wearing her conspicuous armor; she was dressed in silk sleepwear.

The glossy fabric wrapped around her body, outlining her voluptuous curves. In the dead of night, she looked quite alluring.

"You know me?"

"What, haha, and you actually forgot me?" Merlin displayed a slightly mischievous smile, thinking that a few months ago he had marched alongside her in the capital of Britannia. But back then he was wearing a mask, so she definitely couldn't recognize him as the Great Sword Master Elgin.

"You forgot me...."

Maisfeld noticed Merlin's voice suddenly trailing off, filling her with confusion.

"Never mind...."

A few drops of cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead. He thought that was close—he almost slipped and revealed that he had spat on this personage!

If that happened, the other party would surely realize his true identity. In Britannia, besides himself, who else would dare to boldly spit at the First Knight?

Merlin quickly organized his thoughts and calmed himself down. Anything he shouldn't say, he absolutely wouldn't say.

"Cough cough...."

"Eh!?"

Hearing Merlin's light cough, Maisfeld instantly felt as though she had been struck by lightning.

Every hair on her body bristled with tension, and she pressed her legs tightly together.

She even assumed a stance as if drawing her sword, clearly in full defensive mode against a predator. Unfortunately, her sword was left in the room, so she drew at empty air.

What the—! Why does this man's cough... sound like that despicable person!? Don't tell me...

Maisfeld's eyes turned wary, her heart full of suspicion and unease. If Merlin dared to open his mouth and spit anything right now, she swore she would beat him until his teeth were scattered everywhere!

"Haha, do you really need to be this tense? I was just clearing my throat..." Merlin shrugged helplessly, speechless at Maisfeld's huge reaction.

In fact, Merlin knew very well that his saliva acted as a powerful aphrodisiac on the opposite sex, leaving indelible memories in both body and mind.

Moreover, the vile Merlin had targeted a girl and spat several times. Maisfeld would hardly forget this jerk; killing him a thousand times wouldn't even satisfy her hatred!

As a pure woman, Maisfeld had been inexplicably aroused by Merlin's advances multiple times, only to be cruelly stood up and tormented. Only she herself knew this pain.

Merlin observed Maisfeld with interest. Seeing her face flushed and her behavior bizarre, he said meaningfully, "My lady, why are you blushing? Is it because it's too hot?"

"I... it's just nervousness—" Maisfeld hardly believed the First Knight herself could feel nervous. It was just that Merlin hadn't spoken incorrectly; she truly did feel a burning heat. It was most likely a aftereffect left by the Great Sword Master Elgin. Just thinking about how she felt after being spat on made her whole body uncomfortable.

"Nervous about what? Relax a bit. We're not bad...." Merlin smiled, seeing through it all but not stating it directly. "Looks like your memory isn't so good. Didn't we meet when we saw off the little princess Shelly of the Southern United Kingdom at the dock?"

"Oh! So it was...." Maisfeld pretended to suddenly remember, immediately recalling the Samuel cholera incident in the capital. She had originally thought Merlin and Alice were disorderly elements, but didn't expect them to be the meritorious有功 who found the Elf King's youngest daughter.

Merlin smiled without responding. He wasn't foolish enough to reveal all his secrets. If he denied being the Great Sword Master Elgin, his encounter with Maisfeld would remain limited to the time he saw Shelly off and left Britannia.

Beelzebub crushed the chicken bones, studied Maisfeld carefully, and then asked Merlin, "Someone you know?"

"Not very familiar. Just crossed paths a few times. She's Britannia's First Knight, the favorite by Queen Elizabeth~" Merlin said in a teasing tone.

"Is that so? Another random 'first' someone. Their strength isn't that impressive either, huh?" Beelzebub's gaze lewdly scanned Maisfeld a few times, then nodded. "But the figure isn't bad. Big breasts, nice round butt."

"Waaaay better than the flat-chested lady upstairs!" xN

title: Chapter 30 — The Knight and the Demon Lord
content:
Chapter 30 — The Knight and the Demon Lord

Volume 18 · Chapter 30

Mesfield's expression showed a hint of distaste, finding the sloppy fellow in front of her speaking in a rather frivolous manner.

"Don't talk nonsense. If Alice finds out, I'm definitely not going to have a good time." Merlin frowned and warned Beelzebub.

"Who is he?" Mesfield glared at Beelzebub, not sensing any threat from this guy.

"...That—"

Merlin thought for a moment, speaking half-true and half-joking, "He's my countryman."

"Countryman?" Mesfield didn't overthink it, but still warned sternly, "I hope he keeps his mouth shut next time, or I won't be polite."

"Haha, --ungh!!!"

Beelzebub was just about to make a scene when Merlin covered his mouth and stopped him. He laughed awkwardly.

"Say less, can't even keep your mouth shut while eating? Please excuse him, sir, this guy's mouth is never still."

Beelzebub rolled his eyes and snorted coldly, ignoring Mesfield. He stubbornly continued gnawing on his food, since food seemed to appeal to him more than arguing with others.

Seeing Beelzebub hadn't continued disparaging her, Mesfield's anger subsided somewhat, but her stomach let out another untimely rumble.

"Gurgle gurgle."

Mesfield's face flushed red, and she awkwardly bowed her head, secretly hating that her stomach had rumbled at such an inconvenient moment.

Merlin understood with a smile, pulled up a small stool from nearby, and said, "Would you like to join us, sir?"

Mesfield, breathing in the aroma of roasted chicken, could barely walk. Her hungry stomach had long since begun its revolt, yet she was still somewhat hesitant, surprised to receive such a warm invitation. "Is this really okay?"

"What's the harm? There's plenty more anyway. Wouldn't it be nice to eat together?" Merlin gestured for her to sit.

"Pfft!" Beelzebub stopped eating and showed his extreme displeasure. "Why should we eat with lowly humans? This is an insult! I refuse to share a late-night meal with humans!"

"Lowly... humans?" Mesfield showed some confusion. Could those words really come from a human's mouth? Was he not a human after all?

"What, got a problem?" Beelzebub gave a sneering smile, spat a chicken bone onto the ground, and said contemptuously, "Just squat over there and gnaw on the bones I've finished — that's what's meant for you."

Mesfield's expression suddenly changed. She felt insulted, her fists clenched tightly, and an oppressive aura radiated from her uncontrollably.

Make her squat beside him and gnaw on leftover bones? Was he treating her like a dog?!

She was at least a knight of high standing. When had she ever suffered such an insult!

Mesfield's eyes turned cold, and the veins on her forehead began to throbs faintly. If this were Britain, she would have already动手 to teach him a lesson.

"If you don't know how to respect others, then I'll make you understand... in my own way."

"Wanna fight?" Beelzebub was completely unfazed. Mesfield's oppressive aura simply couldn't affect him.

Mesfield fell silent, wondering if the opponent truly wasn't afraid of her. Judging by his appearance, he didn't seem like a strong individual either. Why was his attitude so aggressively overbearing?

"Shut up!" Merlin raised the roasting stick and smacked Beelzebub on the head hard. "If you can't behave yourself, I'll make you eat dirt!"

"You bastard..." Beelzebub was furious, glaring resentfully at Merlin.

"What, wanna fight?" Merlin said with full confidence.

"Hmph!" Beelzebub rolled his eyes, unwilling to burn bridges with Merlin, and silently continued gnawing on his roasted chicken.

"Miss Mesfield, please sit." Seeing Beelzebub no longer causing trouble, Merlin finally relaxed.

Mesfield saw that Merlin could calm down this sloppy man so easily, and her inner suspicions vanished.

It seemed he wasn't some powerful figure at all — he could be subdued by an Iron-rank adventurer. She had really overthought things just now...

Mesfield composed herself and, not being overly polite, sat down quietly beside them.

"Thank you for your generous hospitality. First, give me five roasted chickens."

"Huh..." Merlin was taken aback, looking at Mesfield with a somewhat strange expression. *So this guy is a huge eater!*

Beelzebub alertly lifted his head, looked at the five roasted chickens on the烤炉, and immediately became discontented.

Damn it! Why was this human woman so thick-skinned?! Grabbed everything right away — she really doesn't treat me as an outsider!

I've been dominating this world for years, and this is the first time I've seen someone openly snatch food from a Demon Lord's mouth!

Beelzebub was so angry he bared his teeth. If not for Merlin being here, he would have devoured this bold and reckless woman first before going after his chicken.

"Get lost, damn it! A woman with such a huge appetite — don't you feel ashamed!?"

"..." Mesfield's cheeks flushed red. Being mocked like this made her feel somewhat humiliated, so she compromised. "Then... two will do..."

"￥#%￥#@&..." Beelzebub cursed under his breath, lowered his head, and continued eating, giving up on further bothering Mesfield. He could barely accept this.

"I didn't expect you to have quite the appetite," Merlin couldn't resist teasing, then cut the roasted chicken into small pieces, placed them on a plate, and handed it to Mesfield.

Mesfield knew she had lost her composure, gritted her teeth, took the plate, and started eating immediately.

In just one bite, her eyes lit up, and her expression showed some disbelief.

So delicious! She had been curious about that unique fragrance before, but she never expected it to be even more amazing in her mouth.

This man might be weak in combat, but his cooking skills seem pretty impressive...

Mesfield glanced at Merlin and had to admit she was seeing him in a new light.

"Well?" Merlin asked tentatively.

"...." Mesfield cleared her throat and said in a very serious tone, "It's delicious. Even better than the royal chef. I think you shouldn't be an adventurer — you should apply to be a cook instead."

"Haha..." Beelzebub suddenly burst out laughing, patted Merlin on the shoulder, and said, "Hear that? You should become a cook. I'll take you in. Consider it."

"Get lost!" Merlin swatted Beelzebub's hand away. *My dream has nothing to do with being a cook! Don't look down on people!*

"I'm serious. I can introduce you to Her Majesty the Queen as a court chef." Mesfield was actually taking this seriously.

"What are you talking about..." Merlin furrowed his brows and said meaningfully, "That Elizabeth wouldn't dare to hire me..."

"Uh, please don't refer to the Queen by her full name, that's disrespectful." Mesfield became serious.

Merlin kept a straight face, thinking *What's the harm in being disrespectful? I'm the man who teased the Queen!*

Even if he became a court chef, Elizabeth would still deeply fear this grand swordsman of Elgin.

"Sorry, I'm used to it. By the way, aren't you responsible for Britain's security? Why did you suddenly come to France?"

"This area was attacked by the Gluttony Demon Lord, plunging the kingdom into chaos. I was ordered by the Queen to come here for支援, to prevent evil forces from invading again." Mesfield explained briefly.

"Oh~ I see..." Merlin nodded, thinking this must be the spirit of the human alliance.

"The Gluttony Demon Lord has committed countless evils, causing panic in France. He might return. We absolutely cannot let our guard down. I came here to protect this land, and I will not allow the demon race's claws to trample upon this soil." Mesfield said resolutely, unaware that—

She would never know that she had once calmly eaten a late-night snack with two Great Demon Lords~

title: Chapter 31 — Seeking Information
content:
Chapter 31 — Seeking Information

Volume 18 · Chapter 31

Beelzebub rolled his eyes, not thinking he had done anything particularly wicked, and couldn't resist sneering, "Hah hah, what do you mean 'riddled with evil deeds'? We haven't even gotten to the good stuff yet."

"What do you mean?" Messfield's gaze turned sharp. If wantonly slaughtering humans didn't count as riddled with evil deeds, then what did?

"Eat your food, shut up..." Merlin stuffed a chicken leg right into Beelzebub's mouth. This guy's comments would expose the demon's identity sooner or later; it was better to keep a low profile.

"Mmph mmph!!!" Beelzebub protested dissatisfiedly. This person was slandering him to his face and wouldn't even let him defend himself?

"So you've come to support France, I thought there was something special." Merlin smiled and said tactfully, "Actually, you don't need to worry about that Gluttony Demon Lord. He won't be causing trouble anymore."

"We absolutely cannot let our guard down. He's not an ordinary demon; he's a ruler of the demon race. Look at how chaotic France is right now, and this is only one ruler attacking. It's hard to imagine how dangerous it would be if there are six more..." Messfield said gravely.

"..." Merlin's expression grew odd, and inexplicably he thought of... the Calabash Brothers.

"So it's impossible not to be on guard. Maybe your strength is too weak for you to understand how dangerous a Demon Lord's arrival truly is, isn't it?" Messfield felt that Merlin speaking so casually was understandable. After all, how could a Black Iron adventurer possibly comprehend the power of a Demon Lord?

"Hah..." Merlin gave a dry laugh and didn't defend himself. Instead, he agreed, "True. A jerk like the Gluttony Demon Lord should be guarded against more. Perverted personality, eats too much—he doesn't look like a good person at all."

"???" Beelzebub was covered in question marks. He thought Merlin was really not polite in rubbing salt into wounds! Taking the opportunity to smear his own reputation!

"That's right. Not just the Gluttony Demon Lord, no demon is any good. They are inherently an ideologically extreme race. Who knows when they'll launch large-scale invasions of human territory?" Messfield emphasized.

"..." Merlin's expression grew awkward. It seemed the impression that the demon race was evil was deeply rooted in people's minds and hard to change. Thinking about what Beelzebub had done since arriving in France, no wonder humans classified him as a demon lord.

"Hmph!" Beelzebub let out a cold laugh, not forgetting to shoot a provoking glance at Merlin, as if to say, See! You worship humans, yet in humans' eyes you're no good either, and yet you lecture me~

"Actually, France is now suffering both internal strife and external threats. Besides the Gluttony Demon Lord incident not being fully resolved, I also heard that the escaped imperial chancellor is a dark creature with considerable power. This is also a hidden danger not to be underestimated." Messfield looked up at Merlin and said in a kindly manner.

"The two of you don't have strong abilities. You'll likely struggle to protect yourselves in the chaos. I advise you to leave the royal city as soon as possible. If evil forces attack on a large scale again, your lives will be in danger."

"Hahaha, that's hilarious. Our lives in danger? That's the funniest joke I've ever heard." Beelzebub slowly pulled his lips back into a teasing curve. He thought this knight woman was quite interesting. Two Great Demon Lords couldn't protect themselves in the chaos? Clearly, it was these insignificant humans whose lives were in danger. He and Merlin were the true hunters; the rest... were all prey!

"Is there anything funny about it? France has been destroyed by the Gluttony Demon Lord to this extent, which already shows how dire France's situation is. If the warfare starts again, the first to die will often be people like you, the lower classes..." Messfield's tone didn't sound like a joke in the slightest.

"Is that so? Then let the warfare come faster. I'd really like to know what in this world can threaten our lives." There was arrogance in Beelzebub's words. Aside from a few of his own kind among the demon race, he didn't care about anyone else.

Messfield stared at the unkempt man who refused to show his face, thinking his words were no different from a madman's. "You will pay for your arrogance."

Merlin felt a gunpowder-like tension between the two; perhaps they simply couldn't stand each other. So he took the initiative to interrupt, "Uh... Lady Knight, she means well. Don't argue with her."

Noticing Merlin signal him, Beelzebub could only let out a cold snort, silently bowing his head to gnaw on a chicken neck, muttering, "What a bunch of nonsense First Knight. Long hair, short sight..."

...Messfield's face darkened. Her hungry stomach was already nearly full from this Contrarian, and she had genuinely hoped the two would flee to safety before danger arrived. Yet they didn't appreciate it at all; they seemed to find her meddlesome instead.

"Don't mind this guy, he's just..." Merlin pointed to his own temple and joked, "There's a problem up here."

"Yep, can see that." Messfield agreed.

Beelzebub frowned, staring resentfully at Merlin. His patience had limits too; constantly joking at his expense wasn't a good thing.

"Cough cough!" Merlin awkwardly cleared his throat and changed the subject. "Miss Messfield, I know you're suggesting we leave as soon as possible out of goodwill, but when actual warfare breaks out, we'll actually be the safest."

"Oh?" Messfield curiously lifted her head and guessed, "Someone is protecting you?"

"Huh? Protecting?" Merlin was puzzled. Did he and Beelzebub need someone else to protect them?

"I've heard about it. An adventurer from Britannia repelled the Gluttony Demon Lord. It's precisely because of this adventurer's existence that the royal city was spared disaster." Messfield didn't think Merlin was the adventurer who drove off Beelzebub; instead she suspected he might know that adventurer.

"That's right, an adventurer from Britannia." Merlin briskly flicked his hair, looking like he was going to promote himself while he had the chance.

"With the strength to repel the Gluttony Demon Lord, even throughout the entire Adventurers Guild, he'd be among the outstanding ones, or one of the top-tier Purple-Gold ranks. I wonder who this adventurer is?" Messfield thought it over and asked Merlin in a probing manner, "This adventurer seems to live in this mansion too. Do you know his name?"

"You don't need to search for it. The adventurer who drove off Beelzebub is far away in the sky, yet close right before your eyes." Merlin said without any disguise. Although he couldn't admit it was Earl the Great Sword Master, this didn't seem to matter. Besides, he could enjoy feeling worshipped. It felt wonderful~

"Your meaning..." Messfield's gaze turned strange, half suspicious and half astonished.

"Tch! It's me. I repelled Beelzebub not long ago." Merlin puffed out his chest and stood tall, pride all over his face.

"Then..." Messfield furrowed her pretty brows, her gaze重新 evaluating Merlin from head to toe—

"Please be honest. This joke isn't funny at all." _(:з)∠)_

title: Chapter 32 — The Audiobook Is Out—Hope Everyone Will Give It Their Support
content:
Chapter 32 — The Audiobook Is Out—Hope Everyone Will Give It Their Support

Volume 18 · Chapter 32

Mesfield wore a blank expression. No matter how you looked at it, Merlin the adventurer did not appear to be anyone capable of opposing a Demon Lord; he came across as more of a jokester.

"Don't struggle. You look like a weakling. Nobody will be—""

Beelzebub hadn't finished his snark before Merlin clamped a hand over his mouth. He really didn't want to hear him speak.

Merlin knew well enough in his heart that no matter how much he did alongside Alice, he would always end up as the supporting character. He was just a bit unhappy about it.

"Well, I was kidding, hah..."

Mesfield withdrew her gaze, thinking Merlin probably had no idea about the adventurer who had driven back the Gluttony Demon Lord.

Teacher Kraldy had said the对方 must be Purple-Gold tier; there was no way someone that high-ranking would ever cross paths with the lowest-tier Black Iron.

It didn't matter if Merlin didn't know. He would be paying a visit tomorrow anyway and would learn the person's identity sooner or later.

"What do you want from that adventurer who drove back the Demon Lord?" Merlin asked cautiously.

"That adventurer should be Purple-Gold tier. Those types are often hard to pin down, so we need to make their acquaintance and build some trust. We hope they'll lend a hand when Britain faces crisis," Mesfield said concisely.

Merlin frowned slightly and spoke as if he half-understood. "Does that mean, like that Purple-Gold guild master in the capital, we need to follow the queen's every command?"

"...He doesn't look like much, but he knows quite a bit." Mesfield eyed Merlin.

"I'm just a farmer, but I've heard of the great sword hero Elgin. I heard you once asked Master Gregory for help hunting him down..."

Mesfield's face darkened instantly. "Don't you dare mention that Elgin Great Sword Master. If I get the chance, I'll cut out his tongue myself."

A bead of sweat rolled down Merlin's forehead. He asked awkwardly, "Why... do you hate him so much? Did he do something unspeakable to you?"

"It's worse than unspeakable. If it weren't for Her Majesty the Queen's ambiguous attitude toward him, I wouldn't let him off!" Mesfield said angrily, twisting the neck off her roasted chicken—she was probably imagining the food as the hateful Elgin Great Sword Master.

Merlin swallowed nervously, feeling an inexplicable chill on his neck. He thought, I've only spit a few times, right? Is that really worth this much hatred?

"You have a misunderstanding about old Mr. Gregory. He wasn't following the nobility's orders—he did it entirely on his own volition," Mesfield said as if discussing something casual. "Gregory once served as the court magician for the British Emperor and has deep affection for the kingdom."

"Eh? Is that so..." Merlin barely understood.

"As for this adventurer who rivals the Demon Lord? We intend to recruit her and make her a new Thistle Knight." Mesfield didn't hide it.

"Huh? A Thistle Knight?!" Merlin's expression turned peculiar.

"What? Do you have an issue with our knights?" Mesfield noticed Merlin's look; it seemed like he didn't hold the Thistle Knights in high regard.

"No, no, are you guys really that short-staffed?" Merlin felt the Purple-Gold Flower Knight Order was starting to look a bit desperate, when in the past only Britain's elite could join. And Alice's prestige wasn't even sufficient, let alone the fact that suppressing Beelzebub was entirely his own doing.

"After Britain's civil unrest, six Thistle Knights were sacrificed. We urgently need to replenish our forces." Mesfield sighed.

"What if the person refuses?" Merlin found this unlikely—Alice wouldn't even become a Hero, so why would she become a Thistle Knight?

"Aside from being less free, the benefits of a Thistle Knight are no inferior to a Purple-Gold adventurer. They may even be better..." Mesfield didn't think the person would refuse.

Merlin fell silent, feeling increasingly unfair in his heart. Has this stinking woman Alice become a hot commodity now? Why does everyone want to win her over? Here he is, still struggling at the bottom!

At this point, Merlin began to doubt himself. Back then he truly had hoped Alice's fame would grow larger; building her up to the altar would have earned him lots of pocket money.

But with this... Merlin felt like he was getting the short end of the stick. Wouldn't he completely become Alice's little sidekick?

However, Merlin felt Mesfield and the others would be wasting their effort. Alice probably wouldn't willingly accept being restricted.

Beelzebub suddenly stood up, spat the chicken bone from his mouth, and stretched lazily.

"What are you doing?" Merlin became wary, wondering if this bastard was up to something again.

"I'm going to release fertilizer. Want to come along?" Beelzebub looked at Merlin.

"Tch! Go by yourself." Merlin rolled his eyes, thinking in his heart: eat and then immediately poop. What a straightforward idiot!

Beelzebub pointed at the roasted chicken on the stove and said bluntly, "These are all mine. Don't touch them. I expect them to be intact when I get back."

"Hurry back," Merlin said indifferently.

After Beelzebub left, only Merlin and Mesfield remained in the kitchen.

This female knight enjoyed her meal to the fullest, beginning to devour it as if no one were around.

Merlin watched Mesfield's eating manner and thought she was far superior to Beelzebub—

She also ate like a wolf, but kept some decorum. She didn't display any embarrassing behavior; on the contrary, she could arouse others' appetite.

It was just that Mesfield, as a woman, eating so uninhibitedly would still surprise quite a few people.

As for Beelzebub? Merlin couldn't be bothered to comment. He was simply indescribable, like a dog gnawing at bones.

Mesfield finished two roasted chickens and didn't forget to lick her fingers, not particularly caring about her image as a woman.

"The spices from the East are very rich. The taste is oily but not cloying. You'd really suit being a chef."

"That's not my ambition. I'm used to being free and unbound. Adventurer suits me better." Noticing Mesfield's gaze still fixed on the roasted chicken on the stove, Merlin added, ".. Haven't you had enough?"

"......" Mesfield's face flushed red, looking slightly constrained.

Merlin thought for a moment, tore off a chicken leg and held it to Mesfield's lips. "Eat. Don't be polite."

"But..." Mesfield hesitated, not wanting to cause trouble for others.

"Don't worry about that guy." Merlin waved his hand, thinking: I've bullied you several times before anyway. Consider this compensation. Just don't hold such a grudge against me.

"...." Mesfield hesitated for a moment, then boldly took a big bite of the chicken leg.

In Mesfield's eyes, this appearance was nothing inappropriate. It was simply normal social interaction between a man and a woman.

But to onlookers, this looked rather like Merlin actively feeding the knight lady, unbearably ambiguous.

Outside the door, Alice, who had come here to eavesdrop at some unknown time, sucked in a sharp breath, her face filled with shock, her little heart leaping into her throat—

Hmm?!!

Merlin...

You big pig trotter, what are you doing?!

title: Chapter 33 — Can't Understand This Couple
content:
Chapter 33 — Can't Understand This Couple

Volume 18 · Chapter 33

Merlin had not noticed Alice outside the door, and at the same time felt that his actions were not particularly inappropriate.

But to an onlooker like Alice, who was just there for the drama, the meaning of it all was completely different—

Damn it! What is Merlin that bastard doing?

He... he has never fed me anything before!

To actually cook personally for another woman in the middle of the night and feed her food!?

I have never received such treatment! Usually, I have to beg him to make something delicious, only to be met with a glare!

Alice instantly became indignant, her heart burning with jealousy and extreme imbalance.

It was the first time she had ever seen Merlin treat another girl so well, or been this attentive toward her!

Originally, Alice had woken up in the middle of the night, seeing that Merlin and Baelzebub were gone, and assumed they had gone out for some business.

But then she went downstairs and stumbled upon Merlin sharing a room with a female knight late at night, the scene so ambiguous it nearly blinded her eyes!

Alice’s delicate body trembled with anger, her face looking very ugly, and her frequent deep breaths made her flat chest rise and fall.

“I’ll do it myself,” Mestfield was not used to this, so she took the chicken leg from Merlin’s hand and ate it noisily.

Merlin forced a smile that didn’t reach his eyes, thinking that this female knight had an astonishing appetite; wasn’t she a reincarnated hungry ghost?

Alice could no longer bear it, took a deep breath, and pushed the door open, walking straight in.

“Merlin! You-- what are you d-”

“Eh!?” Merlin suddenly froze, seeing Alice standing outside the door in her pajamas with a terrible expression. “What? You’re awake?”

“Is it really necessary for you to be so surprised just because I’m awake?”

Alice gripped the doorframe, making creaking sounds, like a female ghost scratching walls late at night, which was creepy.

The thick kitchen door had been scratched by Alice, leaving dark, shocking grooves.

“Uh...”

A bead of cold sweat slid down Merlin’s forehead. Looking at the scratches on the door, his strong survival instinct told him things were bad; Alice now was like a powder keg, where even a tiny spark could cause an explosion!

“Did my sudden appearance... ruin your good deed?” Alice narrowed her eyes, trying to get Merlin to give her a reasonable explanation.

“What nonsense are you talking about? Where is any good deed? We are just eating normally....” Merlin explained helplessly, thinking that Alice must have crossed wires in her brain again.

“Normal... eating? Are you sure?”

Alice felt Merlin’s trustworthiness in her heart dropping rapidly. Just now, he had personally fed someone else, yet he claimed it was normal? He had never personally fed her! The difference in treatment was so obvious; did he really think she was stupid?!

Alice’s imagination concluded that Merlin came to secretly meet the female knight in the dead of night, and that she had been too careless sleeping so soundly as usual!

“Isn’t it....” Merlin winked and nodded, hinting that he was with Baelzebub, “That guy was starving, so I fed him something.”

“Where is that guy? Why don’t I see him? I think you are making up lies, and in reality, while I was asleep...”

“Knock! Knock! Knock!”

Alice’s words were unfinished when Merlin, with a blank expression, tapped the table with his fingers. There piled up a mountain of chicken bones, all created by Baelzebub.

“Tsk tsk tsk, say I am lying? Show evidence.”

“A....”

Alice’s expression softened slightly. She was not blind, and naturally could see the chicken bones spat out by Baelzebub; she had been so angry earlier that she hadn’t seen them at all.

Since the three of them were eating together in the middle of the night, there was no issue of a man and woman meeting privately, and she seemed to have misunderstood something?

Feeling guilty, Alice retracted her aggressive attitude and muttered questions.

“Where is that guy? Why are only the two of you here?”

“He went out to relieve himself,” Merlin spread his hands and said.

“.....” Alice became embarrassed, thinking she had come at exactly the right time, just seeing Merlin ambiguously feeding someone. It seemed she really had misunderstood. “You... just now... um, were you feeding her?”

“No, I just handed her the food normally,” Merlin said in a casual tone.

“How was that normal?” Alice sat next to Merlin, puffed out her cheeks, stared at him angrily, full of resentment.

“Hmm?” Merlin’s expression was strange, and he asked tentatively, “Do you think I would do something disgusting like feeding others?”

“.....” Alice’s face turned red, thinking that Merlin really wouldn’t lower his status to please others, so she turned her little face aside. “Hmph.”

Mestfield had not spoken at all, but silently observed Merlin and Alice.

This girl was his wife, ...Alice, right? A Gold-rank adventurer.

Previously, they had delivered the United Kingdom’s little princess together at the dock; apparently, both were kind people.

Unexpectedly, they met again here. Thinking about it, it was also a kind of fate.

This guy with decent cooking skills actually managed to marry such a cute wife; he was truly lucky....

Because Alice was wearing pajamas and had no adventurer certification, Mestfield thought she was Gold-rank.

If she knew that Alice had directly become a Mithril-rank adventurer in a short period, this Thorn Knight would surely be startled.

Mestfield thought Alice was very cute; she spoke like she was acting coquettishly toward her husband, and ate like a child.

“You couple seem to have a good relationship....”

“Huh? Where do we look like we have a good relationship?” Merlin glanced at Alice, unable to resist complaining, “Small breasts, big temper, and always complaining about others inexplicably.”

“Ha! Who would want a relationship with a loser like that who is full of delusions?” Alice pursed her lips and couldn’t resist retorting, “Lazy and gluttonous every day, throwing money into horse races if he has any, fantasizing about turning his life around through luck. Dream on!”

“You have the nerve to belittle me? You yourself aren’t great, okay?” Merlin frowned, the veins on his forehead throbbing. What was wrong with wanting to turn his life around through luck! Luck was also a form of strength!

“I am much stronger than you, okay? Face reality quickly; without me, you would have been sleeping on the streets long ago!” Alice responded confidently, refusing to yield an inch, feeling that if she weren’t by Merlin’s side, this guy would still be that male host wandering around taverns, “Little Chrysanthemum.”

“Emmmmmm...”

Mestfield raised her eyebrows, watching the two people in front of her clash head-on, spitting saliva everywhere, wishing to fight each other directly, which made her fall silent.

Why did they get jealous over a small matter just now, but then immediately start arguing like enemies?

This couple... really can’t be understood. := =
