title: Chapter 34 — Clash Between the Dark Guild and the Vampire Clan
content:
Chapter 34 — Clash Between the Dark Guild and the Vampire Clan

Volume 18 · Chapter 34

In the deep night of the northwestern great desert of the Empire, a handful of villages were clustered together.

Far from towns, they had little chance of calling for help or resisting if danger struck.

At that moment, a village in the desert was engulfed in roaring flames, thick black smoke rolling skyward as screams and cries echoed across the heavens.

Meades' adjutant, Lamb, was here carrying out his master's orders—abducting the humans of the desert villages to be offered as sacrifices to Dracula.

Working diligently, Lamb had already seized fourteen villages and taken hundreds of lives, drawing dangerously close to completing the plan.

Bold in their isolation within the great desert, the vampires grew recklessly brazen, free from any interference. It was nothing short of a paradise of freedom.

A line of humans, heads bowed like slaves, were bound together on a single rope, marching toward a mysterious vampire ruin.

The villagers knew death awaited them. One after another, they wept and sobbed, but none could resist the powerful vampire soldiers around them.

Lamb stood like a foreman, hands clasped behind his back, supervising the operation and wondering whether they had gathered enough offerings yet.

"Move it! We need to be back at the ruin before dawn!"

A vampire soldier stepped forward and bowed slightly. "Lord Lamb, there are still some elderly and infirm in the village who cannot walk on their own. How should we handle them?"

"Kill them all. Leave no one alive," Lamb said expressionlessly, then added with a suggestive tone, "Haven't you all been working hard for me for a long time? I bet you're hungry. Why not drain them dry to satisfy your hunger in the meantime?"

"...Are you serious?" The vampire soldier's face lit up with excitement, eyes burning with fanaticism. "But Lord Meades specifically forbade us from feeding on humans at will. If he finds out, we'll be punished."

"What's there to fear? Lord Meades isn't here. I won't tell… who would know?" Lamb said haughtily with his hands behind his back. "Consider this a reward for all your hard work. Letting you vent appropriately is only right—but you only have five minutes. Hurry up."

"Hehehe, thank you, kind Lord Lamb." The vampire soldier bowed and called out to the other vampires. "Brothers, follow me into the village for a feast!"

Lamb watched placidly as the horde of vampire soldiers streamed into the village, leaving only a few guards to watch over the captured slaves…

Dozens of vampires poured into the village, draining the blood of surviving humans wherever they found them. The place quickly became worse than hell.

Even survivors who had hidden and escaped the first wave of plundering would soon fall into danger.

Blazing flames shot up to the sky, and collapsing houses crackled and popped in their death throes…

Inside a remote thatched hut, two elderly people protected their seventeen-year-old granddaughter, huddled beneath the bed.

Hearing the howls of murder and destruction outside, they dared not breathe a sound, trembling violently as they tried to stay hidden.

The firelight seeped through the window, and the wooden slats made it feel like a prison.

Every now and then, terrifying shadows swept past the ground, letting out hair-raising shrieks—the dreadful silhouettes of vampires.

"Grandma… are we… are we going to die?" the young girl asked in terror.

"Don't be afraid. We can hide through this," the old grandmother whispered reassuringly.

"…" The old grandfather's face was pale, his eyes wide with fear. "Don't you two speak. Those monsters have sharp ears…"

No sooner had he finished speaking than the door was kicked open by a vampire in armor, his face hideous and twisted.

It growled hungrily, smashing everything in the room as it searched for any trace of surviving humans.

The vampire twitched its knife-sliced nose and slowly approached the bed, sensing something suspicious.

The three huddled beneath the bed were extremely tense, cold sweat pouring down their faces like a bursting dam, on the verge of tears from fright.

They could clearly see the vampire's feet, and for the first time, felt Death so near.

After a moment, the vampire seemed to find nothing and walked away.

After a while, the three beneath the bed slowly exhaled in relief, their panic gradually subsiding…

"I-it seems… we're okay?" the grandmother said nervously.

"See? I told you hiding under the bed was fine. Unlike you old woman—if we'd been in the closet, we'd be dead for sure," the grandfather grumbled.

Suddenly, before the young granddaughter could say anything, an unknown creature grabbed her ankle and yanked her out with force, drawing forth a string of screams.

"AAAAAAHHHHH!"

The vampire hadn't left at all—it had circled around behind the three and launched a surprise attack, catching them completely off guard.

Seeing their granddaughter captured, the two elderly people were terrified. Forgetting the danger, they burst out from under the bed, only to see the vampire gripping their granddaughter's throat, its mouth opening to reveal sharp fangs as it prepared to feed.

The young girl struggled desperately, but what could a normal human do against a vampire? She could only watch helplessly as her breathing grew weaker.

"You monster! Let her go!" The old grandfather grabbed a nearby hoe and shouted, his whole body shaking.

"We'll fight you to the death!" Even the old grandmother picked up a pair of scissors, showing just how dearly she loved her granddaughter—willing to risk her life without hesitation.

The vampire ignored the two old people entirely. Encountering such a young human was a stroke of luck, and it intended to savor every moment.

Just as the starving vampire was about to sink its fangs into the girl's fragile neck, the roof suddenly collapsed as someone dropped down.

The figure was powerfully built, wearing silver gauntlets, with an aura that felt dark and sinister. None other than Laurie, the Saint-tier fighter from the Azure Phantom Flame, had arrived.

In an instant, Laurie grabbed the girl's arm, kicked out with his leg, and sent the vampire flying into the wall with a brutal impact.

The girl was panicked and pale-faced, completely unable to comprehend what was happening.

The vampire quickly got to its feet. Having its prey stolen made it furious, and it roared, charging at Laurie!

"Hmph! Ridiculous!" Laurie's eyebrows narrowed. In a flash, he delivered a single punch that slammed into the vampire's grotesque face.

"ROOOOOAR!" The vampire screamed in agony. Unable to withstand the silver attack, it immediately began crumbling into ash.

A few seconds later, the two elderly people were still shaken, but seeing their granddaughter saved, they began to bow in gratitude.

"Brave warrior from afar, we thank you for saving us!"

"Yes, if you hadn't stepped in, our granddaughter would have…"

"Hahaha… did you perhaps misunderstand something?" Laurie's smile turned wicked. He yanked the young girl closer and mercilessly tore open the clothes on her chest, exposing a vast expanse of snow-white skin, her beauty laid bare without reservation…

"This great one is no righteous hero."

"I'm a complete and utter scoundrel! ! !"

title: Chapter 35 — Night Battle
content:
Chapter 35 — Night Battle

Volume 18 · Chapter 35

The girl's face went pale with terror as she let out a piercing scream. Laurie tore apart her clothes until nothing remained, her body laid bare for all to see.

No one could have guessed that after barely escaping the vampire's fangs, she would so quickly fall into the clutches of a different monster.

Laurie held the young girl in his arms, greedily extending his tongue to lick her cheek.

"How amusing. Did you really take me for some decent person? We're deep in the heart of the desert here. Most people who wander in are fugitives who've never faced justice."

"Please, spare our granddaughter! Show us mercy and pity!"

The two elderly people wept blood tears, falling to their knees before Laurie in unison, begging him to let their granddaughter go.

"Oh? Spare her?" Laurie pinched the young girl's throat, pausing for a moment before saying, "Well, I guess that's not... completely out of the question..."

"Thank you—"

"Don't thank me yet. I have conditions."

Laurie's smile carried a meaning far too deep, as if he wanted to toy with these three pitiful souls.

"I can't save your granddaughter for nothing. How about this, then—a life for a life. Which one of you old wretches is willing to die, and I'll let her go."

The two elderly people froze at those words, looking at each other in bewildered silence, as if the very air had been sucked from the world.

"Don't... don't trust him..." The young girl felt Laurie was untrustworthy and tried to speak up.

"Tch!" Laurie curled his lip, then grabbed the young girl by the throat and lifted her up, forcing her to experience suffocation and near-death, "Hurry up and decide. My patience is limited."

The two elderly people's faces turned deathly pale, their hearts burning with desperation. Watching Laurie about to strangle their granddaughter to death, they had no means of rescuing her at all.

Within the old woman's heart, despair overwhelmed her. Unable to bear Laurie's pressure, and determined to save her granddaughter, she did not hesitate to take her own life.

With a resolute heart, she raised the scissors in her hand and stabbed it deeply into her own neck. Blood sprayed everywhere.

"Wife!" The old man let out a startled cry, watching his aged wife's body convulse, then grow cold.

"Hahaha! You actually went ahead and killed yourselves! You fools! Even if you sacrifice your lives, I still won't spare your granddaughter! Serves you right!" Laurie's expression was exaggerated, mockingly ridiculing them with疯狂 laughter.

"...I'll fight you to the death!" The old man roared with uncontrollable rage and charged forward with his hoe.

"Tch!" Annoyed, Laurie clicked his tongue and ignited golden battle energy around his fist, blasting the old man into bloody paste.

"You monster!" The young girl's sorrow transformed into boundless fury, and she weakly clawed at Laurie's arms, leaving crimson marks.

"Hmph. Now it's just you and me. I suggest you behave yourself." The lustful glint in Laurie's eyes was unmistakable as he forcefully pressed the girl onto the table and began unfastening his belt.

"Let me go! Let me go!" The young girl struggled desperately, writhing her body, large areas of bare skin provoking Laurie's baser instincts. As a Saint-tier powerhouse, suppressing an ordinary person was trivially easy.

However, at that very moment, Eden suddenly appeared on the scene wielding his magic staff, asking softly, "What are you doing? The others outside are waiting for you."

"...Laurie stiffened, awkwardly scratching his head. "...Just messing around, that's all."

"I didn't expect you to still be in the mood at a time like this." Eden waved his staff, and a dark-elemental arrow shot forth, piercing right through the young girl's head. "Come out quickly, or the Guild Master won't be pleased."

"...Laurie glanced at the girl whose eyes remained open in death. He didn't really have a taste for such things anyway, so he merely sighed and fastened his belt. "Such a buzzkill."

Outside the burning village.

Lam furrowed his brows anxiously, feeling that his subordinates had been inside far too long—with not a single person returning.

"Why is it taking so long—"

Lam completely failed to notice that danger was quietly creeping closer. Right behind him, Yuna and Vena, cadres of the Azure Blue Netherflame, were approaching without a sound.

The twin sisters were skilled assassins, as nimble as night cats. They moved silently, and even though vampires' senses far surpassed humans', they still failed to detect the sisters' movements.

Yuna and Vena's crimson fingernails shimmered, coated in a layer of sacred silver. To vampires, this was akin to a potent poison that stripped away their healing ability.

Taking advantage of the night, the twins moved continuously, severing vampire soldiers' heads one after another. Those dead monsters never even sensed the danger lurking, turning to ash without a sound.

The ignorant villagers thought some brave hero had come to save them and didn't dare make a peep, watching helplessly as vampire after vampire had its throat slit.

After clearing out the lower-level troops, Yuna and Vena silently closed in on Lam, lunging to strike his neck from both sides!

"Hmm!?" A chill ran down Lam's spine. He felt a chilling killing intent, as though two agile beasts had locked onto him. He abruptly drew the sharp sword at his waist!

A sharp ringing sound rang out as Yuna and Vena's claws struck the blade. Lam barely saved his life!

Seeing their ambush had failed, the twin sisters sneered and did not pursue relentlessly, instead retreating two steps to face off against Lam.

"We were actually discovered. I underestimated you, really."

Vena chuckled softly.

"Wouldn't it have been easier if you just let us kill you? Why bother struggling?" Yuna said indignantly, having originally planned to pierce Lam's neck with her nails.

Lam was still shaken. Looking back, he saw the ground littered with the ashes of dead vampires, and his heart grew tense.

To silently eliminate so many vampires without anyone noticing—and making sure to use silver as well—clearly, these opponents had come prepared!

Lam couldn't identify the two glamorous women before him. If they were vampire hunters from somewhere, this was going to be very troublesome.

"You—Who are you? Why are you attacking us?"

"We're good people. Seeing you lot committing evils here, naturally we had to step in. Can you believe that?" Vena teased.

"Are you kidding me?" Lam eyed the twin sisters warily. "Looking at you two, you're certainly not good people. Speak—what do you want?"

"Haha, you're harder to fool than I thought. Have you ever heard of the Azure Blue Netherflame?" Vena smiled uncontrollably, trying to make Lam let his guard down.

"The Azure Blue Netherflame?" Lam furrowed his brow, thought for a moment, then looked stunned. "That dark guild made up of criminals? I don't recall having crossed paths with you."

"You haven't crossed us, not exactly..." Vena smiled meaningfully and said, "Fresh flesh and blood will inevitably attract hungry wolves, wouldn't you agree?"

"Hmph! What tremendous gall—to even think of laying hands on us, the vampire race! Aren't you afraid of suffering the consequences yourself?" Lam tightened his grip on his sword and threatened with feigned calm, though inside he was alarmed. Although he too was a Saint-tier powerhouse, clearly, neither of those two opponents would be easy to deal with.

"Enough talking. We came for the vampires—" Yuna curled her lips into a fanatical smile—"in their entirety—"

"—we'll take everything!"

title: Chapter 36 — Pathfinder
content:
Chapter 36 — Pathfinder

Volume 18 · Chapter 36

The air of arrogance was thick. "You think you're something with that mouth? Our bloodline runs deep—what makes you think this rabble can shake us?" Lamu slowly raised his blade to his chest, adopting a battle-ready stance.

"You really have the guts to say that," Vina laughed lightly. "You'll regret those reckless words before long."

"Give him a taste of his own medicine, sister," Yuna said, and the pressure emanating from her body surged outward.

The night grew darker, the frigid desert wind biting through the air.

In the next instant, golden battle energy flared around Vina and Yuna, the two sisters moving like spectral assassins, their attacks weaving together in a deadly dance.

Lamu’s gaze narrowed—then he revealed his true form. His skin was a sickly green, his face twisted with jagged fangs glinting in the moonlight, his membranous wings unfurling as a howling gale tore through the air.

"You humans don’t know when to die! Today, you’ll pay the price!"

Lamu was no weakling—he was a Saint-tier powerhouse. With a roar, he drove his blade deep into the ground, sending shockwaves rippling through the earth. *Boom! Boom! Boom!* Explosions erupted, sharp shards of rock hovering like blades before him, sealing off every possible escape route.

At Lamu’s command, the stone fragments shot forward in a relentless barrage, forcing Vina and Yuna back. The sisters, known for their speed, found themselves struggling against the sheer volume of the attack.

"Come on," Lamu sneered, his wings vibrating as he hovered into the air, his maw splitting into a grin. "You killed my kin—you won’t leave this desert alive. My standing may not match Madess’s, but I’m no weakling in our bloodline. Few dare threaten me, and even with silver weapons, you won’t kill me unless it’s a fatal blow. My resistance is too high!"

Vina and Yuna slowly rose from the ground, wiping dust from their faces with cryptic smiles.

Silence settled over the ruins. A faint desert wind stirred the sand, and the village burned behind them, its smoke curling into the night sky.

The disciples of the Blue Flame Sect gathered outside the smoldering remains, their silence heavy with tension. They had just annihilated Lamu’s entire vampire squad.

The Blue Flame Sect had been heading toward the Dracula Ruins when they stumbled upon Lamu’s raid. Humphrey had given the order without hesitation—no survivors. Not because of mercy, but because letting even one vampire escape could mean warning the ruins of their approach.

If the vampires inside were prepared, the mission would become far more dangerous.

"Are they all dead?" Humphrey switched to a new staff, forged from holy silver, its purpose clear.

This time, every member of the Blue Flame Sect had been equipped with silver weapons—and now they’d finally faced their first real test.

"I’ve checked. All the vampires are dead..." Eden lowered her head, staring at Lamu, who lay broken on the ground, his breath shallow. "Except this one—the leader."

Lamu was in terrible shape. Blood loss had drained his face to a ghastly pallor, his hollow eyes fixed on the night sky. His limbs had been severed by Vina and Yuna, leaving him a mangled, twitching corpse—unable even to struggle.

Though Lamu could resist some silver’s effects, it had crippled his regeneration. Without his limbs, they wouldn’t regrow quickly. He was nothing but a helpless wreck.

He had underestimated the sisters. Now, defeated in moments, he had no illusions left.

"Oh, little pretty boy," Vina prodded him with a stick, sneering. "You were just bragging about making us pay, weren’t you? Now look at you—still alive, but not moving. We’re all here. Show us how you’ll make us suffer."

"Cut off the limbs, bled you dry, and you’re still alive? Vampires are just cockroaches, aren’t you?" Yuna licked her nails suggestively. "Wonder if we chop off your head, you’ll still keep breathing?"

Lamu said nothing. He was their prisoner now—no hope of escape.

"Tsk tsk," Laurie shook her head. "This guy really picked the wrong sisters to mess with. He’s not dying easy."

"Don’t kill him," Humphrey said, rolling up the Dracula Ruins map and tucking it away. "He’s useful. We need him to guide us straight to the deepest layer."

Vina smirked. "You heard the boss. You get to live—for now."

"Why not just kill him?" Yuna frowned. "What good is a cripple?"

"Even if the map shows the ruins’ location, the caves inside are a maze. We need someone who knows the way," Humphrey said, eyeing Lamu. "And this vampire probably came from there. Might as well use him."

Lamu remained expressionless, as if he hadn’t heard. *What kind of people are these?* he thought. *Not hunters—they’re after our wealth. What should I do?*

"Eden was right," Humphrey mused. "The ruins aren’t empty. There *are* vampires inside. Lucky we brought silver."

He paused, then added, "And we’ll need to be even more careful. We’re dealing with something that once ruled France for centuries. Can’t afford to let our guard down."

Humphrey stepped closer to Lamu, his voice low. "You heard me. You’ll take us to the deepest layer. Understood?"

Lamu swallowed hard. The pressure from this hawk-faced man was overwhelming—stronger than any of the others. *Traitor.* He didn’t want to betray his own kind, but what choice did he have?

Silence was his only answer.

Humphrey didn’t press further. "No need to talk. If you want to live, you’ll do as we say. We’re here for treasure, not to wipe out your bloodline."

He turned to his disciples. "Move. Wrap him in black cloth—don’t let the sun burn him to ash."

"Boss," Eden stepped forward, "what about the villagers?"

Humphrey glanced at the bound survivors—the very people Lamu’s kind had attacked. Now they were in *his* hands.

He met their desperate eyes, then smirked coldly.

"Kill them all."

"If we hadn’t shown up, they’d already be dead."

"We’re not heroes. No obligation to save anyone."

"This is just restoring fate. They were doomed from the start."

title: Chapter 37 — The Qualification to Ascend to Purple Gold
content:
Chapter 37 — The Qualification to Ascend to Purple Gold

Volume 18 · Chapter 37

The next day, inside the mansion.

Despite the rather large misunderstanding the day before, things between Merlin and Alice were still relatively peaceful.

"I'm hungry, go get me something to eat." Beelzebub was acting like a lord, giving orders to Merlin.

After tasting Merlin's cooking the day before, Beelzebub had grown somewhat attached to it and kept wanting him to make food for her.

"Tch! Endure it, aren't you just a glutton? You ate so much last night and you're already hungry the next day." Merlin rolled his eyes.

"If you won't do it, then let that woman make it. I'll condescendingly try it," Beelzebub said, unable to order Merlin around, so he shifted his target to Alice.

"G、U、N!" Alice responded with a supposedly "kind" reply.

"Tsk!" Beelzebub pouted and said arrogantly, "You've lost your only chance to curry favor with me. Don't regret it."

"Who wants to curry favor with you? A manure-producing machi—," Alice completely looked down on Beelzebub, thinking this woman not only had a foul mouth but also a terribly nasty personality that made her very repulsive.

"Hm? Who are you calling a manure-producing machine? A mere human dares to speak so disrespectfully to me." Beelzebub's brows furrowed. She wondered if this lowly human thought they had grown close enough to start insulting her. Ugh! It was all because of Lucifer, that bastard, who spoiled her!

Alice歪ed her lips and懒得 bothered to respond to Beelzebub. If it weren't for Merlin, she wouldn't even want to live under the same roof as her.

"Knock knock knock." Someone knocked on the door.

Merlin walked over to open it and was greeted by three unexpected guests.

Blitz, wearing a foolish grin, Crady, who looked young but was actually quite mature, and Mesfield, whom Merlin had had midnight snacks with the night before.

"Sir, we would like to meet the hero who drove off Beelzebub. Would that be convenient?" Crady asked bluntly.

"Hah." Merlin let out a dry laugh, thinking, So it was inevitable that you'd come.

Mesfield seemed a bit surprised to see Merlin. She wondered, Didn't this guy live with the Hero who drove off the Gluttony Demon Lord? Why didn't he say so directly last night?

"Um..."

"Do you two know each other?" Blitz, noticing Mesfield's strange reaction, asked in confusion.

"That... we ate together last night," Mesfield explained simply.

"Huh?! You... you had dinner together?!" Blitz felt awkward inside and anxiously said, "You could have come to me for that! No matter when, I would have gladly accompanied you."

"Sir Blitz, I am not a child. I don't need someone else's companionship." Mesfield replied seriously. Recalling the taste of the roast chicken from last night, she couldn't help but be impressed by Merlin's culinary skills. "Besides, Sir Merlin is someone no one can replace."

"Huh?!"

Blitz's face turned pale. He felt deeply hurt inside. He had worked so hard to try to gain favor, yet he was beaten to the punch by an ordinary Iron-rank adventurer. He really felt like a failure.

*She meant Sir Mesfield said Sir Merlin is irreplaceable, right? That's probably what she meant.*

*Ah, what's so good about this guy? Why do both Princess and Sir Mesfield favor him so much? And he even managed to snag a free wife. Could my emotional intelligence be the problem?*

"Sir Mesfield, you and... you two are... secretly developing feelings..."

"What?!" Mesfield was startled, her face turning red as she shook her head repeatedly. "No no no! That's not what it is!"

"Hmph!" Alice puffed out her cheeks, glaring at Mesfield with eyes that basically said, *Watch yourself*.

"I meant that Sir Merlin's cooking is superb and can't be replaced by just anyone! Don't misinterpret what I'm saying!" Mesfield explained in a flustered hurry.

"...Is that so...?"

Blitz scratched his head foolishly, wondering if he had misunderstood.

Crady's expression was peculiar. Mesfield's flustered behavior seemed very unusual to him. "Windsor, it seems like you have a special relationship with this Sir Merlin, don't you?"

"Huh???" Blitz's little heart skipped a beat again, feeling extremely nervous.

"It's simply that we had a chance encounter with them long ago. The Elven King's daughter was imprisoned in Britain, and it was Sir Merlin and the others who found her. Speaking of which, they helped us greatly." Mesfield explained, thinking it best to say less, otherwise she'd only dig the hole deeper. He was already a married man, so he definitely didn't want any scandals affecting his reputation as the Empire's First Knight.

"Oh~" Crady nodded understandingly and took a look at Merlin, but he didn't feel that there was anything particularly noteworthy about him. He seemed very ordinary. "Thank you for the contributions you've made to the Empire, sir."

"Let's skip the polite pleasantries. Please come in." Merlin stepped aside and let the three people in.

Crady looked around the room at the three people: Merlin, an Iron-rank adventurer; Alice, a Mithril-rank adventurer; and that mysterious faceless Beelzebub.

He guessed that whoever could defeat the Gluttony Monarch would at least be a Platinum-rank adventurer. Merlin and Alice didn't seem to fit that description, so this mysterious faceless person was very suspicious.

Platinum-rank adventurers tended to keep a low profile and act strangely. Beelzebub's outfit did indeed resemble that quite closely.

In order not to cause any misunderstanding, Crady asked Blitz instead. He only knew that the one who drove off the Gluttony Demon Lord was an adventurer from Britain, but he didn't know specifically who it was.

"May I ask which of you is the valiant one who drove off the Gluttony Demon Lord?"

Blitz quickly stepped forward, standing beside Alice, and introduced, "It's this Sir Alice. She successfully drove off the Gluttony Demon Lord."

"...Is that so?"

Crady's expression became somewhat unnatural. Although Alice carried a very distinctive pressure, with a draconic intimidation factor, her strength as a Mithril-rank adventurer wouldn't be weak either.

But this was still far from Crady's expectations. The combat power of a Demon Lord was monstrous — a Mithril-rank adventurer defeating a Demon Lord? That seemed rather unlikely just from imagining it.

Even Platinum-rank adventurers could only be said to have some possibility of defeating a Demon Lord.

Mesfield also looked very puzzled. However, seeing the Mithril-rank adventurer's certification on Alice, she internally gulped.

*She was only a Gold-rank adventurer half a year ago. Has she really promoted to Mithril this quickly?*

*A Mithril-rank adventurer's实力 is at least Saint-tier. This girl's growth in strength... is almost godlike!*

A trace of admiration appeared in Mesfield's eyes. If this person truly was the hero who drove off the Demon Lord, her实力 must be immeasurable.

"Cough!" Crady awkwardly gave a light cough, finding it hard to believe this fact. "Sir Blitz, are you sure there hasn't been a mistake?"

"Of course. The two of you went together to rescue Her Highness. Aside from Sir Alice, who else would have the ability to drive off a Demon Lord?" Blitz said earnestly.

"I see..." Crady calmly observed Merlin and Alice. Between the two of them, it really was only Alice who had the qualifications to clash with a Demon Lord.

*Could it really have been this Mithril-rank adventurer?*

*Then her实力...*

*Wouldn't she already have the qualifications to be promoted to Platinum? =D*

title: Chapter 38 — The Exalted Status of a Knight
content:
Chapter 38 — The Exalted Status of a Knight

Volume 18 · Chapter 38

Clady carefully examined Alice, thinking that on the surface this young lady didn't seem to have the ability to defeat the Gluttony Demon Lord—perhaps she had some hidden trump card.

Alice could tell from their few words that they surely thought she had driven away the Demon Lord, so she could only explain, "Don't misunderstand. I'm not the one who defeated Beelzebub..."

"Oh come on~" Blaise grinned broadly. "Lady Alice, there's no need for modesty. We all understand."

Alice rolled her eyes. *Understand your foot! There's no way my strength can face the Demon Lords head-on!*

"Esteemed warrior, I am Clady, the Twelfth Thistle Knight of Britain. It's a pleasure to meet you." Clady bowed slightly, fully expressing his sincerity in coming here.

"Uh, you..." Alice replied stiffly.

"Your feat of driving away the Gluttony Demon Lord fills us with sincere admiration." Clady lowered his manner, offering appropriate flattery toward Alice.

"Yes, when I last saw you you were a Gold-rank adventurer. To advance to Mithril so quickly—truly astonishing speed." Mesfield remarked, thinking Alice's talent was extremely strong, not inferior to his own at all; she was more than qualified as a member of the Thistle Knights!

"Oh? Is that so? Lady Alice is indeed extraordinary, truly a role model for our generation." Clady nodded with a smile, growing ever more satisfied with Alice. If she could join the Thistle Knights, Queen Elizabeth would surely be very pleased.

...A bead of sweat slipped down Alice's forehead. *Heartlessly*, she wondered if these guys had some misunderstanding about her?

"May I ask what kind of training method you use? Could you share it casually? Your training speed is truly astonishing, even surpassing Britain's little prodigy Johnson." From what Mesfield knew, Johnson might have the fastest training speed in all of Britain. He had achieved superhuman feats at a very young age. But Alice was merely a high-rank adventurer before—now she's shot straight to the peak of Saint-tier!?

"Th...then..." Alice was extremely guilty. She had a heritage crystal inside her continuously supplying magic power to transform her body—how could her training speed not be fast? All she had to do was lie around and train every day. But it wasn't convenient to tell the truth right now. "Ahem, it's just going to bed early and waking up early every day, drinking tea, reading newspapers... and whenever I have free time I go help the landlady cross the street, so... so I train... go..."

Clady:
Mesfield:
Merlin looked at Alice, this foolishly cute brute of a woman, and couldn't resist mentally throwing shade: *What the hell is she saying!? For others, training is agonizing—why does it sound like playing around coming out of her mouth!? Even if you're lying, at least make it believable!*

Mesfield wore a strange expression. *What kind of training method is that? Could someone really break through to the peak of Saint-tier in a short time like this? ...You've got to be kidding me!*

Clady felt somewhat embarrassed. He had come here for a serious conversation, but Alice had turned it into something he didn't know how to continue discussing.

Fortunately, the honest Blaise actually bought it and said in full astonishment, "What!? There's such an easy training method!? Lady Alice truly is no ordinary person! I'm impressed!"

"Cough...haha, no wonder you have the strength to repel Demon Lords. You really surprised us. The emergence of outstanding talent like you is truly Britain's fortune!" Clady said with a smile that didn't reach his eyes, though in his heart he was thinking: *Yeah right, sure. You brat are way too cunning.*

"...Is that so? I think it's not that big a deal, haha."

Alice laughed awkwardly, getting a bit carried away by everyone's flattery. She'd spout nonsense and people still believed her—sure enough, whatever a strong person says is right. This feeling was thrilling~ She felt like her brain was about to hemorrhage, constantly rolling her eyes beside them while muttering inwardly: *Wow! This wicked woman is actually getting conceited!*

"The ones who know how to get themselves inflated with pride are always impressive. Right now, even a brute like me is thoroughly convinced." Blaise deeply admired Alice in his heart. After all, she had once been a Hero—a true one in ten thousand. That instantly made him feel relieved.

Clady's expression shifted. He now looked at Alice with new respect, thinking that having served as a Hero before and possessing such a mysterious background—perhaps there really were countless bizarre events stacked together. Clady found himself unable to fully read Alice. Little did he know, Alice back then had merely been a fill-in-the-ranks Hero.

"You were also a Hero of the Holy Church?" Mesfield asked curiously.

"That was a long time ago." Alice put on the expression of a tough guy who doesn't talk about past glories.

"What generation Hero were you?" Mesfield pressed on.

"Don't know~" Alice, still a bit carried away, blurted it out without thinking.

"233rd generation?" Mesfield furrowed his pretty brows and said in surprise, "You mean that most failed Hero in the Holy Church's history—who led 100,000 Saint Knights to the destruction of the Demon Lord Palace and was utterly defeated by the evil Lucifer!?"

Alice snapped back to reality like someone revived from a dream, her face turning bright red as she frantically tried to change the subject. "No, no—!"

"Eh!? Stop talking about that! What are you guys even here for today!?"

"Since you're a person of action, we'll skip the pleasantries." Clady collected his thoughts and spoke earnestly. "We've already witnessed your bravery. Someone like you is exactly what the Empire is missing. It would be a great pity if you didn't pledge yourself to the Empire and do your part to protect the people. Therefore, we wish to invite you to join the Crimson Flower Knight Order and become an honored Thistle Knight. Would you have any interest...?"

*Hmm... Crimson Flower Knight Order?*

Alice frowned, torn and conflicted. *Why is every major faction inviting me lately? It must be because I've been drawing too much attention.* Thanks to Merlin's exploits, the troubles always ended up landing on her doorstep. While being fawned over felt pretty good, always being someone's target was quite uncomfortable.

*Thinking about it, I don't really have any lofty ambitions. Pledging loyalty to the Empire—don't even mention it. That's impossible. Joining the Crimson Flower Knights...*

Alice considered it. *Rising to Crimson-rank adventurer would be fine, but I don't want to join any knight order. Thank you for your kindness.*

"Let's pass on that..."

Clady paused abruptly, genuinely baffled that such an olive branch was being refused. Only a fool would reject an invitation to join a knight order that belonged directly to Her Majesty the Queen, with authority answerable to no one but the sovereign herself.

The Crimson Flower Knights were top-tier existence—they bent the knee only to Her Majesty, ranking above tens of thousands yet below only one. Although the Thistle Knights held no personal territories or factions, their status was equal to that of the various dukes.

Such an opportunity to become a Thistle Knight, and she's just casually letting it slip away... *Does this girl's brain... truly malfunction?*

(一"-)

title: Chapter 39 — Suicidal Investigation
content:
Chapter 39 — Suicidal Investigation

Volume 18 · Chapter 39

Claudia and Mesfield were both taken aback by Alice’s outright refusal.

This was an incredibly rare and precious opportunity—one that could elevate a commoner to rival the nobility. If Queen Elizabeth issued a decree to recruit new Thorn Knights nationwide, countless people would fight to the death for the chance.

Merlin remained expressionless. Alice’s refusal was entirely within his expectations. While Thorn Knights enjoyed excellent status and treatment, the key drawback was their obligation to obey the queen’s commands, which left little room for freedom.

“Hmm,” Claudia thought for a moment before deciding to press further. “Miss Alice, is there anything in particular about the Thorn Knights that you find unsatisfactory?”

“Not unsatisfactory, exactly,” Alice replied cryptically, glancing at Merlin. “It’s just that we owe tens of millions of gold coins. Do you think the Empire will repay that for us?”

“What?! Tens of millions of gold coins?!” Claudia was stunned. The sheer scale of debt was unimaginable—it could bankrupt a kingdom.

He had been considering recruiting Alice into the Thorn Knights, but now he abandoned the idea entirely. If Alice joined, she would become the queen’s subject and would be expected to help repay the debt.

But the amount was absurd! Even Britain wouldn’t dare take on such a burden, let alone any other empire. No nation would willingly accept this hot potato.

“Hahaha—so much debt, huh?” Merlin chuckled, though his tone was strained. “That’s quite the sum.”

Mesfield’s forehead broke out in cold sweat, his heart pounding. *What kind of reckless spending could lead to a debt that would take generations to repay?*

“My goodness,” he muttered, wiping his brow. “Alice… she’s truly unlike anyone else.”

Blaze trembled as he dabbed at his forehead, his mind racing. *I’ve been pushing Princess Elizabeth to recruit Alice this whole time—what if we’d dragged an entire empire into ruin? I’ll never suggest it again.*

“Exactly,” Alice sighed, shrugging helplessly. “I *could* be a Thorn Knight, but the conditions don’t allow it. And honestly, joining the Thorn Knights would mean less freedom, which isn’t something I enjoy. So, I’m sorry.”

Claudia and Mesfield exchanged glances, silently communicating their disappointment.

They had hoped to recruit a powerful figure into the Thorn Knights, but now it seemed like a losing deal—the queen wouldn’t be pleased.

Mesfield lowered his head, speaking in a hushed voice. “Master Claudia… perhaps we should drop it. I *do* want her to join, but we can’t take on that kind of trouble.”

“We’ll think it over,” Claudia replied quietly. “If we can find a compromise, that would be best. If we just give up on this opportunity, where else will we find someone as suitable for the Thorn Knights?”

“…Fine,” Mesfield nodded, having no objections.

Claudia had been in the Thorn Knights for over forty years, making him a veteran among them. Compared to him, the other knights were all youngsters. His experience and prestige had elevated him to the status of an elder.

Many Thorn Knights had been promoted or mentored by him, and even Mesfield respected his judgment.

Claudia turned to Alice, hesitating before speaking. “We can’t help with your debt, but… freedom? We can still discuss that.”

“Do you mean I wouldn’t have to follow the queen’s orders?” Alice asked, confused.

“Something like that,” Claudia clarified. “You wouldn’t have to obey commands, but you’d still need to act in the Empire’s best interests.”

“Oh?” Alice’s interest piqued slightly.

“When the Thorn Knights were first established, their primary goal was to protect the Empire’s security. Besides the usual ranks—two Thorn Knights and three Knight Commanders—there’s a lesser-known position: the Foreign Thorn Knight. It’s designed for talented individuals who dislike military life but still want to contribute.”

Alice blinked. “Foreign Thorn Knight?”

“Exactly,” Claudia explained. “Foreign Thorn Knights have no real authority and can’t participate in the order’s management. But their status is equal to that of regular Thorn Knights—they’re respected, essentially becoming a noble class without actual power.”

Alice considered it. *A noble title without real power is just a title, but even that has its uses—no local nobles would dare bully me, and I wouldn’t have to worry about soldiers harassing me.*

Still, she hesitated. “So… I’d still be free?”

“Absolutely,” Claudia assured her. “You can do whatever you want—even continue as an adventurer. You won’t have to follow the queen’s orders, and you’ll receive a monthly stipend of 10,000 gold coins.”

Alice raised an eyebrow. “A long-term meal ticket?”

Merlin chimed in dryly, “Indeed. A noble title with no strings attached, a monthly paycheck, and no restrictions—sounds like a sweet deal.”

“Merlin,” Mesfield corrected, “Foreign Thorn Knights *are* Thorn Knights. They do have obligations.”

“Tsk,” Merlin smirked. “No such thing as a free lunch, I suppose.”

“What obligations?” Alice frowned, her interest waning after the cold splash.

“Foreign Thorn Knights enjoy all the benefits of a Thorn Knight—except the authority,” Claudia said, gesturing as if painting a picture for her. “In exchange for these perks, you’d assist the Empire in times of crisis. Otherwise, you’re free to do as you please.”

Alice nodded slowly. “I see.”

Claudia locked eyes with her. “What do you think?”

Alice hesitated. “I’ll… consider it.”

Claudia stifled a sigh. *After all these concessions, she still isn’t decided? This is frustrating.*

He composed himself, forcing a smile. “We won’t pressure you. If you change your mind, come find me anytime. For now, we’ll take our leave.”

As Claudia turned to leave, his peripheral vision caught Asmodeus, who had been silent in the corner this whole time. Something about him felt off.

“Who is that gentleman over there?” he asked casually. “Part of your group?”

“Ah… yeah! Fellow countryman!” Merlin blurted out.

“Huh? Earlier, there were only the two of you,” Blaze scratched his head. “When did a third person appear?”

“Hahaha—uh, we ran into them nearby,” Merlin said stiffly, forcing a laugh. “They’re in quite a panic, actually. We’re just helping this ‘crazy’ person get back home.”

Claudia’s expression remained neutral, but something felt *wrong*. He subtly channeled his magic toward the mysterious figure—

And in the next instant, he caught a glimpse of something so terrifying that he nearly collapsed from shock.

title: Chapter 40 — Doubt
content:
Chapter 40 — Doubt

Volume 18 · Chapter 40

Cladwell had deep knowledge of ancient civilizations, so he naturally knew some of those mystical magics.

Ordinary divination could only gauge the level of one's oppressive pressure and determine what tier a person belonged to.

But Cladwell's divination was different. With his knowledge of ancient civilization, his scan would instantly reveal a person's true essence.

The moment he directed his divination toward the mysterious Beelzebub in the corner, Cladwell witnessed a scene that chilled him to the bone—

An endless dark space with no visible boundaries, every surface made of pulsating fleshy walls. The sky and the earth were both flesh, as if he were inside some monster's body.

Countless tentacles blanketed the world, each as thick as a millennium-old ancient tree, covered with suction cups resembling an octopus's, spewing yellowish-green fluid.

Only upon closer inspection would one realize that those suction cups dotting the tentacles were actually human mouths—except their teeth were jagged, razor-sharp saw blades.

Countless tentacles danced through the air like ravenous monsters, desperately devouring the ferocious man-eating flies hovering midair.

Cladwell saw this infernal scene, and his consciousness was gradually being devoured, as though escape had become impossible.

But fortunately, at that moment Beelzebub let out a series of cold sneers, his attitude full of contempt: "Hmph hmph hmph... Don't play with fire..."

Cladwell's consciousness snapped back to normal. He felt excruciating pain in his head, as though he'd suffered a psychic attack.

The people around him had no idea what had happened. They only saw Cladwell in obvious agony, clutching his forehead as though enduring something unbearable.

"Teacher Cladwell? Teacher Cladwell!" Maisfield noticed Cladwell's strange reaction and called out repeatedly, also supporting his body.

"What's wrong, Mr. Cladwell? What happened?" Blaise was thrown into chaos, not knowing what to do.

"Hmm?" Alice grew puzzled and looked at Merlin, assuming he knew the answer.

But Merlin's expression remained flat. After a moment's thought, he shot a suspicious glance at the silent Beelzebub, wondering if that guy had orchestrated this.

Cladwell's suffering was only brief. Within a few seconds, he returned to normal, and the headache vanished completely.

He gasped for air in large ragged breaths, cold sweat soaking through the white undershirt on his chest.

Cladwell silently stared at that mysterious figure, thinking to himself: damn it! Why was I the one corrupted? Anyone capable of such means is definitely no ordinary person.

"Teacher Cladwell! Are you okay?" Maisfield asked worriedly.

"...Nothing. Just a headache. Probably too tired and need to rest."

Cladwell managed a smile, but his eyes kept drifting toward the mysterious Beelzebub, clouds of suspicion forming in his heart.

He wasn't entirely sure whether that mysterious figure had actually cast any spell. After all, the other party hadn't made any discernible movements.

Ancient magic involved many secrets, and a common trait was side effects. The human body wasn't a magic cannon machine; it would suffer backlash.

Cladwell himself couldn't claim complete mastery over ancient magic. Perhaps what he'd just experienced was indeed a side effect of wielding it, causing his consciousness to be rejected.

"My apologies for the inconvenience. We'll take our leave now."

"Safe travels." Alice responded politely.

Once Cladwell and the other two departed, the room returned to calm, as though nothing had happened at all.

"What was that about Mr. Cladwell? It was somewhat....." Alice couldn't help but ask Merlin directly.

Merlin thought for a moment, then turned to look at the silent Beelzebub and demanded, "You bastard, you were behind that just now, weren't you?"

"Lucifer, don't pin this on me. That arrogant human was the one courting death. If I hadn't spoken up, he would've already been dead. Not only did I not harm him, I saved his life. Is there anything wrong with that?" Beelzebub, seeing no outsiders in the room, lifted his heavy hood and exhaled heavily.

"What do you mean? What happened just now?" Merlin didn't quite understand. Whatever had occurred, only Cladwell and Beelzebub—the two parties directly involved—would know best.

"He used some method to try probing my soul, but his own soul was so weak that he nearly got consumed by me. You should understand the Demon Lord's strength. Our souls have already acquired a divine nature. How could a mortal be allowed to peer into them?" Beelzebub sneered back.

Merlin stayed silent. He felt this counted as Cladwell nearly burning himself through curiosity. Demon Lords were indeed the pinnacle of this world, after all—not something to be trifled with.

"Hmph! It all boils down to those pitiful humans not knowing their own worth. They always do things born of curiosity that end up killing them. If I hadn't been honoring our agreement, swallowing that fool's soul would've been fine by me." Beelzebub sniffed dismissively.

"What's with the arrogance? If that had caused any trouble, none of us would've escaped unscathed!" Alice couldn't help but reprimand Beelzebub.

"Not my problem~" Beelzebub spread his hands.

"You!"

"Alright, alright. Didn't any trouble happen, did it?"

Merlin signaled Alice not to argue and directly asked her about the foreign Thorn Knight matter.

"So, what do you think of the conditions they offered?"

"...What do you suggest?" Alice glanced sideways at Merlin.

"I think they're fine. The key point is freedom—you'd only need to help out a little. A permanent meal ticket, how wonderful~" Merlin looked genuinely tempted.

"...I'll think about it." Alice lowered her head, looking indecisive.

Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue, then shamelessly said, "If you're not willing, then pass the opportunity to me. I'm actually quite interested, hehe~"

"Don't dream," Alice retorted, rolling her eyes at him. "They're recruiting me, not extending an olive branch to you."

"Behind every successful woman is a....."

"What are you doing?!" Alice suddenly grew alert, her eyes flashing like a lecherous wolf.

"...A man who handles the practical work!" Merlin barely recovered. He'd originally been going to say "a man who works until he pukes," but being too vulgar, he'd swallowed those words. "You're being courted by all major factions right now—whose credit is that? When you drink water, don't forget the one who dug the well, brother~"

"Oh~" Alice rolled her eyes and nodded. "Rest assured. Once I become a Thorn Knight, I'll designate you as my servant. No one will compete with you for foot massages and shoulder rubs."

"???" Merlin's expression grew complicated. He thought to himself: that rotten woman thinks pretty well for herself. Foot massages and shoulder rubs? If only I could kick her into outer space and let her travel the world!<

Along the manor's corridor, Blaise had taken some prior matter and left. Cladwell and Maisfield were preparing to return to their respective rooms.

"Teacher Cladwell, are you really going to grant Miss Alice the title of Thorn Knight as well? From the nation's founding to now, this position has never been granted to anyone. Isn't Miss Alice's ability somewhat insufficient? I....feel a bit uneasy....." Maisfield said hesitantly.

"How is it insufficient? She's the former Hero, and she has the means to repel the Demon Lord. That's enough." Cladwell was much more composed now, having recovered his usual calm demeanor.

"Although Miss Alice's cultivation speed is astonishing, the foreign Thorn Knight position involves the nation's first case. Doesn't this require notifying Her Majesty the Queen?" Maisfield spoke cautiously.

"As long as Miss Alice agrees, I will personally return to the capital to explain to Her Majesty. The Bauhinia Knight Order has suffered heavy losses. Continuing to replenish with fresh blood—Her Majesty will agree." Cladwell said with confidence.

"......" Maisfield didn't press further, thinking to himself: a foreign Thorn Knight. Is such a special position really appropriate for the former Hero?

"Then.....about the mysterious figure in the corner of the room today.....do you understand anything?" Cladwell was still somewhat bothered. He had a feeling that person was no ordinary individual.

"Not really. Though we chatted briefly last night, that person has an extremely nasty and extreme personality, frequently spouting arrogance. And also....." Maisfield's eyes took on a strange quality. He pointed awkwardly at his own temple. "They say there's something wrong with his brain. He's a lunatic who randomly came all the way from Britannia to here....."

title: Chapter 42 — Mades' Power
content:
Chapter 42 — Mades' Power

Volume 18 · Chapter 42

Humphrey, upon seeing the mountain of treasures, was overjoyed. All the effort spent searching for this ruin was clearly worth it!

If they could take all these treasures, the overall strength of the Black Flame would increase significantly, giving them the capital to stand toe-to-toe with other dark guilds.

"Black Flame?" Medes furrowed his brow, finding the situation increasingly troublesome. "A dark guild made up of outcasts? Do we have any grudges with you?"

"Your Excellency, you might be misunderstanding. We specialize in burning, killing, and looting. It has nothing to do with whether we have a grudge or not," Eden replied calmly.

"If it's about money, we can negotiate. Why go through all this trouble?" Medes didn't want to escalate the conflict and hoped for a peaceful resolution.

"Good!" Humphrey nodded, his sinister eyes seemingly appreciating Medes. "That coffin looks very valuable. Leave it for me, and you can disappear right now. I guarantee your safety."

"Tch!" Medes' expression instantly turned extremely grim. He didn't care about the money, but the coffin behind him was more important than his own life. "The coffin is out of the question. Everything else is yours."

"Hmm? You place such importance on that coffin. There must be something extraordinary inside. We're taking it today!" Humphrey's eyes lit up with excitement, convinced this was a huge harvest!

"Seems... there's no room for negotiation. Do you really think you can take anything from me?" Medes was furious, slowly drawing the noble sword from his waist...

"You pathetic vampires are already surrounded. What right do you have to negotiate with us?" Humphrey coldly said, giving Eden a signal behind him.

With a dragging sound, Lamb, bound in five directions, was dragged out and fell to the ground, covered in injuries.

Lamb, who had been cut into a human stick earlier, had now healed his limbs. To recover so completely in just a few days showcased the blood族's formidable regenerative abilities.

"Lamb..." Medes looked at his trembling subordinate below and already had a rough idea.

"Medes-sama, save me! I didn't bring them here on purpose! I was forced!..." Lamb looked up at Medes, stretching his neck to plead for help, his helpless eyes full of fear.

Eden pulled out a silver dagger and drove it through Lamb's heart from behind, without the slightest hesitation, as if slaughtering a chicken to warn others.

Lamb's plea for help ceased instantly. In the blink of an eye, his entire body was engulfed in flames, turning to ash that scattered into the air.

A silver weapon piercing the vampire's vital point meant even regenerative abilities couldn't save him. Lamb, the guide, had no more value to Humphrey.

Medes watched helplessly as his subordinate was burned to ashes, his veins bulging on his forehead. He realized these despicable humans had come prepared.

Miranda in the distant cage, watching the two sides confront each other, didn't dare breathe a word, wondering if this was the moment she was rescued.

"See? You won't obey us... this is what happens! Hahaha..." Humphrey grinned, mocking them.

Medes narrowed his eyes at Humphrey, so angry he was almost biting his teeth to pieces, his face extremely grim.

He released his realm-level aura, pale golden battle气 swirling around him, making people dare not approach.

The obvious golden magic and battle气 were the symbol of a Saint-tier. After breaking through to Saint-tier, the color of magic and battle气 actually became lighter, somewhat returning to its original simplicity.

In just a breath, Medes vanished from his original position, suddenly appearing at the center of the enemy's encirclement, ready to launch an attack with the speed of a thunderclap!

Speed was also a racial talent of the vampires, and it was now fully displayed on Medes, almost making everyone's eyes fail to follow his steps!

Medes charged straight toward the leader Humphrey, smoothly cutting down anyone who blocked his path, his sharp royal swordsmanship unstoppable!

Every time the sword flashed, it meant another disciple of the Black Flame lost their head. It seemed impossible to stop Medes' attack?!

The other vampires, seeing Medes start the attack, immediately picked up their weapons and engaged the human invaders, the ruins instantly filled with shouts of battle!

Don't underestimate the vampires just because they were few in number. Each one could rival an elite warrior, and one could easily take on ten humans.

They didn't hide their beastly nature at all, pouncing on humans, biting necks, and drinking blood.

Medes had a cold gaze, his magnificent swordsmanship stunned everyone. A guild of over a thousand people was actually getting chaotic!?

"Try to get close to the leader!"

Eden suddenly roared, gathering golden magic on his staff and violently swinging it, releasing hundreds of dark light swords!

The sound of piercing air echoed, the dark light swords shining like meteors, shooting forward at incredible speed.

Medes' eyes flickered, his figure disappearing again. The hundreds of light swords missed completely.

The next second, Medes was already beside Eden, delivering a powerful elbow strike to his face.

Eden's expression twisted, his jaw almost shattered, spitting out a mouthful of blood before crashing into the rock wall.

Medes' gaze once again locked onto Humphrey, but the sisters Vina and Yuna rushed over to interfere again.

"Come play with us! What's the point of staring at our leader?"

The sisters' sharp attacks forced Medes to be cautious. Being hit in a weak spot would be disastrous.

But Vina and Yuna were no match for Medes. A single sweeping kick sent both of them flying, defeated.

"Watch me blow you to bits!" Humphrey roared, his magic causing the air to heat up, instantly turning the ruins into a furnace.

A blue fireball rapidly expanded above Medes' head, as if it would explode and flatten the ruins.

Humphrey was a peak Saint-tier强者, the strongest in the guild. His magic's destructive power was no joke.

Although his staff had been broken by Merlin, reducing his strength somewhat, he was still a murderer!

The prepared magic was called Scorching Inferno, its power almost indistinguishable from a meteor impact. Everything within the attack range would be reduced to ashes, no living thing could survive!

Even though this magic would affect many of his own people, Humphrey didn't care at all. He just wanted to kill the troublesome Medes first.

"Hmph, in front of my speed, mages are just trash."

Medes coldly said. Escaping the Scorching Inferno's attack was easy, but just as he was about to move, someone grabbed him from behind.

"Tired of dodging around? I want to see what you'll do now?"

Lauri had somehow secretly approached Medes and grabbed him from behind, completely restricting his freedom.

"Good job, Lauri! Don't let go of him! Let this bastard taste our strength!" Humphrey laughed wildly with excitement.

The blue fireball in the sky grew larger and larger, the Scorching Inferno was already formed and would soon crash down to destroy everything.

"We'll die together. Aren't you afraid?" Medes asked calmly.

"To die together with the esteemed Imperial Chancellor is an honor for me. Are you afraid? Hahaha... Ugh!" Lauri's voice suddenly stopped, his eyes widening in disbelief!

Medes had used his sword to pierce his own abdomen, simultaneously piercing Lauri's body. How decisive was his move in this critical moment!

Lauri's body went limp, forcing him to release Medes. Blood gushed from the wound, his eyes staring in disbelief at Medes.

"Idiot, trying to die with me? You're not worthy!" Medes slowly pulled the sword from his abdomen. The wound healed at an incredible speed, visible to the naked eye, with no effect whatsoever...

No sooner had he finished speaking than the Scorching Inferno was unleashed!

A magnificent blue fireball crashed down from the sky...

title: Chapter 43 — Scorching Infernal Flame
content:
Chapter 43 — Scorching Infernal Flame

Volume 18 · Chapter 43

The intense heat burned the ruins, and the Scorching Inferno rained down, causing the entire area to tremble violently.

Even at the last moment, it was hard to tell if Medes had escaped or not.

What was known was that Humphrey's Saint-tier magic had a vast range, covering nearly a third of the ruins, encompassing both enemies and his own subordinates.

The blood of vampires and humans mixed together, blending with the gold melted by the high temperatures, slowly flowing toward the center of the altar, where that black coffin emitted a faint, dark glow once more.

The shattered ground formed a shocking crater, with幽blue flames spreading to every corner of the pit, truly resembling the scene of a meteorite impact.

The disciples thought that in such a situation, Medes must have been hit directly by the attack, and now might have been burned to nothing.

But as the heat waves quietly dissipated, the situation was vastly different from what the disciples had imagined—the one who had been subdued was Humphrey.

Medes remained as noble as ever, his suit spotless, his long silver hair fluttering with the heat waves.

His crimson eyes flickered, and with one hand, he grabbed Humphrey's throat, lifting the madman off the ground.

"Earlier, you showed me the consequences of disobedience. Now, I'll show you the consequences of meddling with vampires. Isn't that fair?"

"Th... then, let's talk this over calmly, okay?" Humphrey, with his throat gripped, struggled to speak.

"Sorry, it's too late." Medes curled his lips, revealing sharp teeth like straws.

"So, no talking? Perfect! Hehehe!" Humphrey laughed maniacally, then surprisingly turned around and grabbed Medes's neck with his own hands, as if afraid he would escape.

Medes was taken aback, sensing something unusual about Humphrey. Suddenly, a wave of heat hit him. "Fake!?"

Humphrey's entire body ignited with幽blue flames, turning him into a fireball in an instant, his body swelling as if about to explode!

The fireball clung tightly to Medes, and the magical elements grew wildly chaotic. It all seemed like a carefully designed trap.

Just as Medes tried to break free, the ground beneath him lit up with a dark purple magic array. One by one, black chains made of magic shot out, binding him tightly in place.

From afar, Eden, whose jaw had been broken, slowly stood up with his staff, controlling the chains to wrap around Medes, preventing him from moving. "I won't let you escape."

Medes felt as if his body was about to be torn apart by the chains, his composure shattered, even showing a hint of panic. He hadn't expected the enemy to anticipate his relentless pursuit of Humphrey.

A gray-robed figure calmly stepped out from among the many disciples. He pulled down his hood, revealing Humphrey's old and cunning face. "This is the real one!"

"I knew you'd go after me, so I set up the binding array and the explosive decoy in advance. I didn't expect you to fall for it so easily... it saved me a lot of trouble..."

"Deceitful humans..." Medes narrowed his eyes, the chains nearly binding him like a mummy.

"Enough talk. Disappear!" Humphrey's magic surged, and after waving his staff, he unleashed a second Scorching Inferno!

A blue fireball filled with intense heat appeared above Medes' head, rapidly expanding and almost draining all the magical elements from the air!

The illusion was about to explode, a meteor was about to fall from above, and he was bound in place by the chains, unable to move.

Faced with such a desperate situation, a cold sweat dripped from Medes' forehead. Although these humans were weaker than him, their cunning had given them the upper hand.

Boom—

A massive explosion shook the entire ruins as the explosive decoy and the Scorching Inferno erupted simultaneously!

Heat waves and flames engulfed the sky, as if trying to melt the entire mountain.

Lava fell into the dark river, hissing as steam filled the air, making it so thick that one couldn't see their own hand.

The ground rolled, the wind howled. Humphrey, in his effort to defeat Medes, had no regard for his disciples' lives. More than half of his subordinates had perished in the flames.

The altar, which had nearly run dry of blood, was replenished again, with a blood river surging toward the center.

As the chaos subsided, Humphrey's eyes widened with excitement. He thought this time he must have killed Medes. A double blow was impossible to survive unscathed.

But as a set of footsteps echoed, Humphrey was pulled back to reality.

A skeleton emerged from the幽blue flames, its noble sword glowing red-hot in its hands.

Fine nerves and blood vessels began to缠绕 the skeleton. Within just a few breaths, Medes' body was restored to its original state.

Medes' powerful healing ability was far superior to that of ordinary vampires. Even after being burned to a skeleton, he could recover instantly.

The participating disciples stared at Medes in disbelief, their hearts filled with awe at the vampires' formidable power.

Under normal circumstances, who could stand up unharmed after such a猛烈 attack? It was as if he was an existence that could never be killed.

"...," Humphrey frowned, thinking maybe the attack had been too weak. If his black crystal staff hadn't broken, perhaps he could have...

Medes moved in a flash, teleporting from a hundred paces away to Humphrey's side, his sword piercing Humphrey's heart. "Are your trump cards all used up? Or is that all you have?"

"...," Humphrey spat blood, his face still showing a mocking smile. "I... will tear that arrogant face of yours to pieces!"

The幽blue flames erupted again, forcing Medes to retreat. Humphrey's aura surged in a short time, breaking through the peak of the Saint-tier!

Humphrey continuously burned himself with flames, his body gradually merging with the fire, transforming into a being similar to an elemental spirit.

A stronger aura than before swept over Medes, who had to take the situation seriously. To increase his power so dramatically in such a short time must have been some kind of forbidden magic.

Lauri clutched his abdominal wound, watching as the会长 turned into a fireball, his heart filled with horror—

Is... is he going all out?!

He actually used a dangerous magic of self-sacrifice, sacrificing half his life for a temporary power boost!

This was the first time Lauri had ever seen the会长 go this far! Was he willing to pay any price to kill this guy?!

Lauri felt the others couldn't help much. The battle between Humphrey and Medes was too intense for them to intervene.

The幽blue fireball Humphrey didn't hesitate, raising his hand to fire a concentrated flame, shooting it out like a beam of light.

The scorching heat wave and flames made Medes feel a moment of fear, forcing him to quickly dodge.

The concentrated flame hit the rock wall, instantly melting a large hole. A single shot of flame had power comparable to the Scorching Inferno? Its destructive power was even stronger!

A cold sweat dripped from Medes' forehead. His gaze toward Humphrey changed significantly. He had to reassess this man.

A temporary power surge to this level... his strength was now almost equal to mine...

If I were to be hit directly by that scorching magic again, there might really be danger.

title: Chapter 44 — I'm Back
content:
Chapter 44 — I'm Back

Volume 18 · Chapter 44

Medes couldn't delay, though Humphry's strength had greatly increased, it was also apparent that he seemingly couldn't master the power proficiently.

Medes leapt into the air, and the noble sword in his hand flashed instantly, instantly cutting Humphry in half at the waist!

Surely this should be the end, after all, he's just a human...

Medes turned his head slightly in the air, but saw that Humphry's severed body was healing, reconnecting as if it were liquid that wouldn't stop flowing.

Damn it? This guy's body isn't human anymore?

Humphry let out a mocking laugh, and shot focused flames from his palm again, not giving Medes any chance.

The ejected sapphire flames instantly engulfed Medes. The flames were like cutting blades, melting and cutting into the ruins' mountain body, leaving traces of lava oozing.

Hot wind storms swept through the stones, making the remaining disciples dare not act rashly; a slight mishap would see them burned to death by the splashing flames.

Eden covered his face with his hands to block the coming storm, looking at Humphry in the air and wondering, Has the club president gone mad? Willing to sacrifice half his life just to kill this guy; though the benefits would be greater, the guild's loss would also be significant.

Humphry had no choice either; surrounding Medes had no effect, so it had to be this temporary leader personally stepping in. Although this was his first time using taboo magic that exchanges life for a temporary power surge, the effect was strikingly immediate.

Just as the flames dispersed, a burnt arm burst from the ruins, and black-red thick water continuously oozed out, like rotten mud.

Within just a few breaths, Medes's body recovered completely. No matter how severe the injury, as long as even a tiny bit remains, he can revive again.

Medes slowly stood up, twisted his just-regenerated neck, and said with a tone of helplessness.

"It's useless, I admit your flames are very powerful, but how long can that power last?"

Eden saw that Medes could still stand up again, and felt secretly anxious in his heart. The club president won't be able to hold on like this. Indeed, directly causing fatal damage with silverware is useless, isn't it?

"Hahaha!" Humphry said nothing; his palms aimed at Medes, and more violent spiral focused flames assailed. The roar of the flame waves was comparable to a fire dragon's breath!

"Hmph!" Medes coldly snorted, quickly leapt to dodge, and in the air revealed his vampire posture. His skin turned brownish-red, his limbs began to grow claws, his fangs protruded, his ears became pointed, and huge membranous wings suddenly opened behind him.

The spiral focused flames began to move, constantly chasing Medes in the air, as if using a stick to swat the biggest mosquito?

Seeing that Medes was about to be swallowed by the flames again, he suddenly spun and flew, and his noble sword suddenly swung, sending out a half-moon slash that dispersed the flames!

Medes flapped his membranous wings to pursue, and with a roar, he collided with Humphry, who had turned into a person of fire. The two began to fight up close.

Humphry himself was a mage. In close combat with Medes, who was a swordsman, he didn't have the advantage. But both possessed strong healing capabilities at this moment, making it hard to tell who was better for a while.

Medes proficiently unleashed court swordsmanship, the clear sword sounds dispersed the flames, forcing Humphry to dodge continuously, and soon revealed a declining situation.

It seems that compared to the vampire race, Humphry knows his regeneration ability can't compare, and there's no advantage in a head-on hard hit, so he can only look for good opportunities.

"Shouldn't we go help the club president?" Una looked at her sister and sought her opinion.

"Not like this, we can't get involved. If the club president goes mad, he won't care about our lives at all." Vina whispered, watching the two peak powerhouses fighting on the sky.

Eden saw the club president was at a disadvantage, and felt anxious in his heart, but he saw a silver dagger among the ashes not far away. That was the weapon that had just killed Lamm.

He thought for a moment, then dragged his fatigued body over, splashing the dagger, and frantically poured magic power into it.

Eden lifted his head, aimed at Medes's flight trajectory, and without hesitation threw the dagger infused with magic power!

The silver dagger flew at extreme speed in the air, trailing black shadows, like a meteor fiercely stabbing into Medes's membranous wing's palm bone.

"You despicable human!" Medes roared, his body lost balance and fell heavily to the ground.

"Die for me!" Humphry seized the opportunity, and the spiral focused flames fell from the sky, ruthlessly striking the fallen Medes.

The violent impact made the ground tremble. Everyone couldn't help but keep their eyes open, especially the surging flames, which almost submerged the entire ruin.

The blue幽焰 disciples died in heaps, many not killed by the vampire, but by Humphry's indiscriminate attacks.

It seems Vina and the two sisters are still quite clever. Humphry this madman killed red-eyed and simply doesn't care about his own people's lives.

After the violent attack ended, Medes knelt on the ground. His body had become charcoal, but he still hadn't died, his crimson eyeballs rolling around everywhere, and new tender meat growing on the burnt flesh.

"Last strike, I don't believe you can still... ". Humphry raised both hands over his head. The time of his power was almost at its limit, and he must speed up the battle. Terrifying magic power crazily gathered, instantly forming a fire element aggregate covering the entire attack. At first glance, it was simply a sapphire sun!

Medes's eyes showed some fear. He himself wasn't in any trouble, but the Dracula on the altar might also be affected.

"Club president... Eden took a breath, feeling this trip was full of danger.

Qi ya

A series of discordant sounds came out, like an old door shaking.

Medes's expression changed from loss to ecstasy, and he suddenly looked at the black coffin on the altar. For some reason, a crack had been opened!

"Hahaha! My lord! Finally... finally waited for this day!"

Accompanied by Medes's laughter, the altar strangely lit up, and the heavy black coffin slowly opened under everyone's gaze.

A pair of withered hands like rotten tree branches hooked onto the glowing edge, and then a black figure sat up, looking silly like just woke up and doesn't know how to think!

Its whole body was rotten, its body seemed to have no trace of moisture, black, and a few white hairs on its head floated with the wind.

"That's?!" Eden felt things were a bit bad, and an ominous feeling surged in his heart.

"What ghost thing?" Laurie covered his abdominal wound, and a layer of cold sweat appeared on his forehead.

"Sister, what is this?" Una asked, not understanding.

"I don't know, it seems like... Vina also couldn't figure it out.

A "Qi qi qi" roaring sound came, and countless bats flew from all directions, circling around this withered old man.

Such a shocking scene, as if a king in the night was waving hands at his subjects.

Medes dragged his burnt body and prostrated five-body worship towards the person in the coffin, "My lord! Congratulations on finally waking up!"

The other vampires also performed prostrations towards the top of the altar, their expressions extremely devout. Some cheered, some shed old tears.

This corpse-like fellow is Dracula, who has awakened again after a few hundred years.

Originally, the blood needed for the ritual was not enough, but Humphry's indiscriminate killing, and the blood of those disciples indirectly helped Dracula complete his awakening, which can be considered doing something good by mistake.

Hearing the calls of the vampires, Dracula's consciousness gradually recovered, and he began to learn to think.

He swayed and barely managed to stand up in the coffin. His thin body seemed like it could be blown over by a wind.

Dracula looked at the同族 below, and then looked at Humphry above who was brewing fire magic, his dull red eyes started to have some spirit.

"Who are you?" Humphry questioned.

Dracula opened his mouth, and all his teeth had fallen out.

"Not speaking... then go die!" Humphry gathered his magic power, and the most powerful spiral focused flames blasted past!

Sapphire flames rose to the sky, as if the last attack of a dragon that destroys the world. The intense light made it impossible to open one's eyes, and one could only see a white mist.

Seeing that the skyrocketing spiral flames were about to flatten everything, Dracula slowly raised his arm, and with difficulty stretched out a finger. The movement was stiff and slow, like a zombie.

Just when the skyrocketing spiral flames were about to flatten everything, they strangely dissipated completely?

Humphry fell from the sky, his flames receded, revealing a human body.

He seemed to be poisoned, desperately pinching his own throat, his expression terrified, constantly rolling his eyes, sticking out his tongue.

".......... or J玩

"Club president! What's wrong with you?" Eden called out, barely walking over to try to support Humphry, feeling his state was very strange, like being strangled by an invisible throat?

"What situation... Laurie's face turned pale, seeing the club president like this, an urge to retreat arose in his heart, a bit wanting to run away.

Dracula silently flipped his arm, and Humphry, like a puppet, obediently pushed Eden away, turned over, and knelt down towards the enemy.

Dracula narrowed his dried eyes, and slightly flicked a finger towards Humphry, and a bloody scene appeared.

Only to see all of Humphry's blood seemed to boil, gurgling continuously, spurting out from his seven orifices, flowing in the air!

"Uh ah. Ah ah ah ah ah.

In the blink of an eye, Humphry's blood was drained by Dracula in the air, turning into a foul-tasting dead body without a peaceful death, powerlessly falling to the ground.

"What... Eden was bloodless, an incredible scene. The club president, who was also a strong person, was actually easily drained by this unknown monster, and didn't even have a chance to resist!

...Laurie's cold sweat streamed, and his heart was incredibly incredible. The club president is also a strong person, how did the other party do it!

As for Vina and the two sisters, they were already frightened silly by Dracula's method of draining human blood in the air, and didn't even have the courage to resist.

"My lord is mighty! ! !" Medes admired repeatedly, his inner joy already showing on his face.

Humphry's blood slowly gathered on Dracula's hand, forming a round blood ball.

His hungry gaze kept flashing, and he opened his mouth without a single tooth, his voice sounding like a broken bellows--

"Come back"
