title: Chapter 1 — Sunset (Part 1)
content:
Chapter 1 — Sunset (Part 1)

Volume 19 · Chapter 1

Half a month had hurriedly passed in the French Royal City, and the empire seemed to have returned to its usual calm.

The walls of the entire main city had already been constructed, and soldiers from other places had also moved in here to strengthen the royal city's defenses.

Even the private armies of many nobles had been requisitioned, all gathering near the royal city, only to face unknown risks.

Margaret dared not relax her vigilance at all, because there was still not a shred of news about the escaped Mades.

As long as this traitor did not die, there was a thorn in Margaret's heart, making it hard for her to sleep peacefully.

The well-ordered imperial order allowed Margaret to finally take a slight breath and rest for a while.

As the saying goes, when food and drink are full, lustful desires arise~

With Margaret free, she couldn't help but keep thinking of Merlin, and her mind began to scheme about this married man.

Margaret was not at all willing to let Merlin go; this man who could defeat the Demon Lord must be controlled in her own hands by any means necessary.

As a result, last night Margaret sent someone to invite Merlin to the palace for lunch today, obviously her true intention was not the meal; she couldn't wait to eat Merlin alive!

Of course, Margaret only invited Merlin himself, not anyone else, in order to create a private space between herself and Merlin, a romantic scene similar to a world of just the two of them.

Margaret felt she found it hard to approach Merlin, all because there was an annoying third wheel, Alice, interfering on his side!

If she could get this annoying woman out of the way, then she could lure him more, and she didn't believe Merlin wouldn't take the bait!

On the night she sent the invitation, Margaret was so excited she couldn't sleep, as if she had already seen the Merlin she admired in her heart fall for her and obediently climb onto her bed.

However, Alice was exceptionally shrewd when it came to matters involving Merlin; her keen nose rivaled that of Holmes, who lived by the Thames, and any little sign would make her very sensitive.

Upon learning that Margaret was going to have lunch with Merlin today, Alice immediately sensed something was wrong.....

This princess has sinister intentions; judging by how she always shamelessly approaches Merlin, she must not have good intentions, right?

And she only invited Merlin alone? That's a bit too obvious, isn't it!

No! Absolutely cannot let this scheming woman have an opportunity!

After some scheming and intrigue, the scene of today appeared--

The midday sun shone brightly, yet it was somewhat chilly, with the cold wind gently brushing past.

Merlin left the manor alone, following the arrangement Margaret had made to go to the palace, preparing to have a meal there together.

What he was thinking was, would suddenly inviting him mean there was something important? Like news about Mades or something?

So Merlin didn't think much, too innocent for his own good, without hesitation he went alone to the banquet, but....

"Alice, why are you staring at me like I'm guarding against a thief? Have I done something wrong?"

"I haven't done anything wrong, I'm not staring at you, okay?"

"Still saying you're not staring? You've followed me all the way, I feel like I'm being watched openly!" Merlin complained resentfully, stopping in his tracks and turning back to look at Alice, who wasn't far from him.

"...." Alice hesitated, responding with an awkward expression, "I just need to be on guard against a thief about to appear."

"Huh? What thief? Would they dare to go after me? I don't have any money on me..." Merlin helplessly spread his hands.

"N-no, not that kind of thief..." Alice hesitated, unwilling to speak, wanting to say Margaret was a love thief, wanting to steal Merlin away, "Anyway, I'm just going to follow you, you heartless fellow, someone might steal your soul with sweet talk, I must watch from the side, hmph~!"

"What nonsense...." Three black lines slid down Merlin's forehead; looking at Alice's unreasonable, pouting-with-arms-crossed look, he really had no way, "Didn't we agree I'd go to the palace to see Margaret, and you stay at the manor to watch Beelzebub? That guy is a time bomb; without anyone watching him, who knows what he'd do? If he causes trouble later, we'll all be in for it."

"Who wants to watch that stinking-mouthed guy!? I won't! If you want to watch Beelzebub, you do it yourself!" Alice didn't want to separate from Merlin, especially in a situation where Margaret invited Merlin alone, so she couldn't relax her vigilance at all, "I guess that princess doesn't have anything important either, why not just not go?"

"How can that be? Margaret suddenly looking for me might have something important; what if she found Mades' whereabouts?" Merlin emphasized.

"...Then I won't go back either, I can't watch Beelzebub, he's so strong, I can't win against him, better to go to the palace with you." Alice unhesitatingly found a reason for herself.

"But Margaret only invited me, not you? If we force our way over, isn't that too rude?" Merlin felt bringing Alice along was inappropriate.

"What's rude about it? Don't worry about such a small matter, let's go!" Alice pushed Merlin's back forward.

"....Today is really strange, by the way, is it really okay to just leave Beelzebub?" Merlin was pushed by Alice, moving forward passively.

"It's fine, that eternal old monster isn't a child...."

In the palace dining hall, a lavish banquet was already prepared, with the busy figures of servants shuttling back and forth.

Plates of carefully cooked dishes were arranged neatly, almost employing all the palace chefs.

To create a romantic and ambiguous atmosphere, the servants also brought fresh roses, arranged in the center of the dining table.

Winter had arrived, and almost all flowers had withered, so being able to get fresh roses was also the result of the gardeners carefully nurturing and cultivating them.

It seemed Margaret had also put in quite a lot of effort for her secret meeting with Merlin.

Margaret was like a reviewing general, examining the dishes, paying extra attention to details.

The honest Blaise followed behind Margaret, asking with a smile, "Is Your Highness satisfied?"

"Not bad, has Lord Merlin arrived?" Margaret had dressed herself up carefully; her elegant long dress made her look radiant.

"He should be here soon, right? I made it clear last night." Blaise responded, then whispered, "But Your Highness, is what you're doing really worth it? That Merlin isn't much, and that couple owes a buttload of debt; I think you shouldn't try to win them over, you should be dodging them."

Margaret lifted her skirt hem, stopped, and said, "As long as Lord Merlin is willing to be with me, there is nothing I cannot accept."

"...." Blaise's expression revealed regret; he wondered in his heart, "It's over, has Your Highness been dazed by love, caring about nothing anymore?!"

The doors of the palace dining hall slowly opened, and the servants stood on both sides, bowing to welcome the guests.

Margaret's face immediately showed joy; lifting her skirt hem, she walked quickly toward the door, wanting to welcome Merlin.

Merlin walked in blankly, looking around; Alice followed behind him, her eyes looking triumphantly at the quickly approaching Margaret, seemingly with a hint of provocation.

"Merlin...!" Margaret's originally joyful expression instantly turned into an unhappy one upon seeing Alice, hating until her teeth itched.

Damn it!

Why did this woman follow along too!?

I prepared all this for Lord Merlin for nothing, what a mood-killer!

......

title: Chapter 2 — Sun Extinguished (Middle)
content:
Chapter 2 — Sun Extinguished (Middle)

Volume 19 · Chapter 2

Merlin looked at the lavish banquet and said politely, "This is truly extravagant. I'm grateful for your trouble, Your Highness."

Margaret, upon hearing Merlin speak, immediately concealed her dissatisfaction and replied with a smile, "Since I'm dining with Grandmaster Merlin, of course I wouldn't be negligent."

"Good thing I didn't eat anything this morning, so I can join too," Alice said with a smile, unceremoniously including herself as a guest.

"..." Margaret's face darkened, her anger barely restrained. Everything today had been prepared for her and Merlin, not including Alice at all!

"What's wrong? Your Highness, your expression seems a bit off..." Merlin asked in confusion.

"..."

Margaret was at a loss, unsure if Merlin was genuinely foolish or pretending. Was he bringing Alice here to cause trouble?

Fortunately, Margaret had a high tolerance for restraint. As a princess, she understood the importance of etiquette and wouldn't lose her temper here, damaging her image as a lady.

Margaret forced a faint smile, nodded, and gestured politely. "Nothing, I just didn't sleep well last night. Grandmaster Merlin, please come in."

"Then I'll trouble you."

Merlin walked in directly, and Alice followed, only to be suddenly stopped by Margaret.

Margaret's face showed a stiff smile as she spoke in a very polite tone, "Miss Alice, if I'm not mistaken, I didn't invite you to this banquet, did I?"

"Is that so!? I thought we were both invited. Oh well~★" Alice feigned surprise, looking pitifully clueless, as if she had genuinely misunderstood and followed along foolishly.

Merlin remained expressionless, but seeing Alice's act, he couldn't help but mentally吐槽, Oh well you mother! Can your acting be any more fake!? You clearly knew you had to follow along!

Margaret, being sharp-minded, immediately saw through Alice's lie. She had deliberately followed.

But she couldn't openly drive Alice away—it would be too impolite and damage her reputation.

After thinking for a moment, Margaret decided to express her meaning indirectly and began blaming Blaze for his poor communication.

"Blaze! How did you relay the message? Didn't you clearly state I was only inviting Grandmaster Merlin?"

"..." Blaze became慌张, feeling very wronged. He had been clear last night, and Alice had heard it herself.

"What do you mean 'you'!? Margaret's gaze turned sharp as she glared at Blaze. "It's all because of your carelessness that Miss Alice misunderstood! What do you have to say for yourself?"

"Well..." Blaze was at a loss, looking very embarrassed.

"Standing there doing nothing!? Don't you go and personally send Miss Alice back!?" Margaret desperately gave him a meaningful look, urging him to act quickly.

Alice watched with a smile, thinking this vixen must want to be alone with Merlin, using every means to get rid of her. How cunning!

"Ah... okay!" Blaze, after pondering for a while, finally understood and hurried forward. "Miss Alice, I'm very sorry. Let me take you back?"

"Wait." Merlin suddenly spoke up, feeling Alice had already come, so there was no need to leave. "Your Highness, I see this banquet is so lavish. One more person won't matter. As a princess, I'm sure you wouldn't mind?"

Alice looked at Merlin excitedly, her heart blooming with joy. NICE Merlin! I knew he wouldn't leave me behind in a situation like this...

"..." Margaret looked at Merlin, realizing that refusing would make her seem petty. Reluctantly, she forced a dry, gritted-toothed smile. "Of course I wouldn't mind. Since Grandmaster Merlin requested it, please, Miss Alice."

"Thank you."

Alice walked in gracefully, brushing past Margaret.

The two women's eyes met, and faintly, sparks seemed to fly in the air.

This invisible war was probably only clear to them, while Merlin remained oblivious.

Margaret frowned, her mood very poor—

Ugh! I'm so angry! How do I get rid of this woman!?

At the banquet, Margaret had only prepared two seats.

book.SFA.

Moreover, she had cunningly placed the two seats close together, making it easy for her to exchange glances with Merlin.

However, there was a gap between the two seats, just enough to fit two chairs.

Alice immediately felt dissatisfied. As the host, shouldn't Margaret be sitting across from them? What was the point of sitting so close!?

So Alice picked up her chair and moved to Merlin's other side, forming a natural barrier like a lightbulb.

This ensured that besides conversation, Merlin and Margaret had no other means of communication, not even a chance to exchange glances.

Margaret's veins throbbed with anger. Her carefully prepared plan had been ruined by Alice. "Miss Alice, what do you mean by this?"

"I just don't like sitting that way. I prefer sitting to Merlin's left," Alice said with an apologetic expression.

"Y-ou..." Margaret maintained a polite smile, but it looked very strained. She then ordered the servants to bring out fresh steak.

"Alice, you're acting strange today. When did you start sitting to my left?" Merlin asked in confusion, lowering his voice.

"I'm not strange at all."

"..."

"I'm not strange at all."

"Then..."

"I. A. M. N. O. T. S. T. R. A. N. G. E." Alice leaned closer to Merlin and said each word with a smile.

"???" A bead of sweat slid down Merlin's forehead as he felt a faint sense of aggression.

Margaret's face was cold as she quietly told Blaze, "Watch my signals."

"Understood." Blaze nodded, thinking to himself that the princess and Miss Alice clearly disliked each other. Indeed, trying to steal someone's husband was a despicable act. Miss Alice watching the princess like a thief was also not surprising...

After the tender steak was served, the delicious aroma filled the air. Blaze secretly sniffed and couldn't help but swallow hard.

"Your Highness, I can eat anything. Preparing all this was a bit of a waste of effort," Merlin thought this was just a normal meal, but now it felt like something more.

"Please don't say that, Grandmaster Merlin. You are my savior. To repay you, even if it takes all my effort to make you satisfied, it's worth it," Margaret felt she was back in her rhythm, launching a gentle offensive to try and emotionally connect with Merlin.

"..." Alice made a disapproving noise, secretly rolling her eyes, her face smiling but her mind repulsed—

It was just that Merlin had saved her life once. Now she was shamelessly clinging to him!?

Hmph! Merlin is mine! <3

title: Chapter 3 — Sun Extinguished (Part 2)
content:
Chapter 3 — Sun Extinguished (Part 2)

Volume 19 · Chapter 3

"That...." Merlin's expression was strange; he felt Margaret was being a bit too enthusiastic toward him. "Your Highness's enthusiasm flatters me, but let's forget about the 'lifesaver' business. It was merely a trivial effort, not worth such gratitude from the Princess."

The standing Blaze nodded inwardly, thinking Merlin still had some self-awareness and no greedy intentions. Her Highness should clearly be focusing on building a good relationship with Miss Alice.

"I quite like Lord Merlin's modest appearance; it's very captivating...." Margaret's face flushed red as she spoke softly.

"....." Merlin froze abruptly, thinking: Has this princess lost her mind? I just happened to save her, and now she's latched onto me? What a troublemaker.

"Lord Merlin needn't feel pressured. Even if you weren't my lifesaver, you should receive this kind of treatment." Margaret said seriously.

"Wh.... why?" Merlin asked curiously.

"Lord Merlin, really, you still need to ask why? You're making me feel shy." Margaret held her slightly red cheeks with both hands. "You are my personally designated fiancé."

Blue veins throbbed continuously on Alice's head. She clenched her fists, her hair bristling with anger--

This woman! Why did she unilaterally decide Merlin was her fiancé!? I really shouldn't have saved her back then!

"Your Highness, don't be like this. Miss Alice is still here...." Blaze reminded Margaret in a low voice, afraid Alice might explode and start a fight on the spot.

Light novel.

"Mind your own business." Margaret said displeased, incidentally shooting Blaze a glare.

"Your Highness truly knows how to joke, haha...." Merlin laughed dryly, thinking Margaret couldn't be serious, right? If he really became her fiancé, wouldn't that be too much of a farce?

'Yeah, Your Highness, you're so humorous, you're killing me with laughter." Alice tilted her head, racking her brain to stop Margaret.

Margaret kept a cold face and said nothing. Originally the plan was just her and Merlin.

Now look, Alice wedged herself in the middle, making many things inconvenient to say.

Damn it, with this woman here, there's simply no way to make a move on Lord Merlin. All my careful preparations these past days have gone to waste.

Margaret forced a smile and had to change the subject.

"Let's eat, Lord Merlin. Please have a good taste. This is what I specially prepared for you."

Several people began dining, but Alice was rather awkward. It looked like no cutlery had been prepared for her at all.

This meal was for two people, but Alice's sudden addition caused the servants to overlook it; they hadn't prepared a third set of utensils.

Seeing Alice's situation, Blaze, not wanting to lose royal courtesy, hurriedly said, "Miss Alice, please wait a moment. I'll go fetch you a set of gold cutlery right away."

But just then, Margaret suddenly lifted her head and glared fiercely at Blaze, as if saying, "You dare move an inch and see what happens?"

"...." Blaze's breath caught. He immediately stopped in his tracks, blinking frantically, as if saying, "I wouldn't dare move, I wouldn't dare move."

Margaret lowered her head, her gaze sweeping toward Alice. Seeing her somewhat embarrassed look, her depressed mood vanished, and she finally felt happy.

Hahaha, that was specially prepared by me for Lord Merlin. I just won't let you eat it!

Serves you right for insisting on tagging along. Not giving you a taste of your own medicine — do you really think I'm a pushover!?

Seeing Alice make a fool of herself, Margaret couldn't help revealing a little devil's smile, not forgetting to provoke her.

"It's so delicious, tender and smooth, melts in the mouth~"

"Hmph. Boring." Alice muttered, too lazy to look at Margaret's petty triumph.

"Here." After cutting the steak, Merlin brought a forkful to Alice's mouth. Seeing she had no utensils, he could only feed her himself.

"Mmph!?" Alice instantly perked up like she'd been injected with chicken blood, her face slowly flushing red.

"Mmph what mph? No appetite? This steak's not bad." Merlin saw Alice reacting like a block of wood.

"........" Alice shook her head with a red face, ate the steak Merlin fed her, and thought: This guy actually took the initiative to feed me? First time ever. Feels a bit subtle, but so happy~

Seeing Alice's expression brighten considerably, Merlin asked quietly, "You've been so weird today. Are you still mad about that female knight from before? You really hold a grudge."

"Absolutely not." Alice lowered her head, hands restrained between her legs. "That kind of trivial thing.... I never took it to heart!"

I- 牡」\玩

"Good. Like now, me feeding you — do you think this kind of thing is special?" Merlin looked at Alice curiously.

".... Nothing special. I'm definitely not secretly happy in my heart! Hmph~!" Alice's pretty face was slightly flushed. She turned her head away, thinking: It's only special when the one being fed is me, you idiot!

Margaret had been fed up. She really couldn't stand watching this dog couple, so she slammed the table hard, venting her anger on her subordinate. "Blaze, what are you eating? Didn't you see Miss Alice has no cutlery? Do you want the guest to grab food with her hands?"

"..--.." Blaze cried out at the injustice, thinking: Their marital relationship is super good. Your Highness, just give up on butting in. No chance!

"What 'what'? Standing there in a daze — still not going to fetch cutlery!" Margaret felt her plan had backfired. Seeing Merlin so considerate as to personally feed Alice, she was dying of envy inside.

Blaze hurriedly nodded. A helpless tear trickled from the corner of his eye. He thought: What did I do wrong? What more do you want? Want me to die? Sob.

"No need to trouble yourself. I don't need cutlery now, hehe~" Alice said with a smile.

Margaret rolled her eyes, feeling like she was about to get a cerebral hemorrhage.

Da-mn-it!

In the mansion's garden, Mesfield hid sneakily behind a pillar, secretly monitoring Beelzebub's every move, puzzled.

What's with this guy today? Why does he look so down? So suspicious....

Merlin and Alice ran off to eat good food, leaving Beelzebub alone at home. This orphan's resentment was huge!

Beelzebub wrapped in a gray robe, still not readily showing his face, crouched alone in the garden drawing circles on the ground with a twig, as if cursing Merlin and Alice.

"Human Era Year XXXX, Month XX, Day XX. Sunny. Today Lucifer took his wife out to eat good things and didn't bring me along. Damn dog couple! This grudge, I'm writing it down first."

After writing, Beelzebub threw away the twig, felt extremely empty, raised his head to look at the sun in the sky, and sighed.

"So boring. Little sister, where are you? Big brother wants...."

The cold winter sun, its light not very dazzling, appeared very gentle.

But at this moment a black shadow suddenly appeared, beginning to slowly devour the sun, making the sunlight gradually disappear.

"...." Beelzebub frowned, feeling something wasn't right, and murmured:

"What the hell is that?"

"A solar eclipse?"

title: Chapter 4 — The Limit of the Draw Slash?
content:
Chapter 4 — The Limit of the Draw Slash?

Volume 19 · Chapter 4

The sun hanging in the sky gradually lost its light, as if being slowly swallowed by a shadow, falling into darkness.
Bie Xibu furrowed his brows as he observed the sky, initially thinking it was just a normal eclipse that would soon return to normal.
But seeing the sun being devoured halfway, Bie Xibu realized something was off.
The speed of this eclipse was faster than imagined, and it seemed more like being covered by something special; faintly, one could feel an elusive magical fluctuation, clearly man-made!
Bie Xibu's tightly knit brows grew heavier, unable to fathom who was behind this, controlling celestial bodies to block the sun?
One who possessed such power was definitely not an ordinary existence; his strength was surely not to be underestimated.
'Who did this? Why would they do such a thing?'
Although Bie Xibu couldn't figure it out, he was clear that if the sun remained obscured, France would likely become an uninhabitable bitter cold wasteland.

Meisifield raised his head, blankly watching the sun completely obscured, his heart filled with astonishment.....
What happened? I must inform Teacher Kladi!
Meisifield had just taken a few steps when he heard Bie Xibu leisurely say from that side, 'You're not going to keep watching me, huh?'
'Ugh!' Meisifield jerked to a halt, stopping his steps and looking at the turned-around Bie Xibu, his thick hat obscuring his face, 'When did you find out? . . . SE light novel'
'I've known for a while; every time I come out, I feel eyes watching me from behind—it's you, right?' Bie Xibu gave a cold laugh, demanding, 'What evil scheme are you plotting?'
Meisifield fell silent for a moment, then frankly said, 'Your identity is suspicious; you don't seem human.'
'If I'm not human, what do you want to do? Kill me?' Bie Xibu spread his hands, showing no fear.
Meisifield fell silent, gave no answer, and left directly; after a while, echoes came—
'As long as you are an evil foreign race, no one will spare you; we'll see how this plays out.'

In the royal palace, the disappearance of the sun caused everyone to fall into chaos.
At this moment, the sun had been completely extinguished, not a shred of light remained, like a huge black disk, with red flames burning around it.
Although it was noon, it felt like deep night; the guards had no choice but to raise torches for illumination, anxiously watching the eclipse in the sky.
'..-. What's going on? ! Why did an eclipse suddenly appear? The astronomers seemingly didn't notice at all!' Blaze broke out in a cold sweat on his forehead, feeling inexplicably tense.
Margaret gazed at the ominous sign for a long time, then lowered her head and angrily said, 'Mades! It must be him! He really isn't willing to stay away!'
orJ U
'Mades? ...Really?' Blaze widened his eyes, thinking maybe he was mistaken.
'The sun has vanished; Mades and his blood clan will become even more reckless; he will surely return!' Margaret hurriedly turned toward the palace, shouting nonstop, 'Prepare for battle! Mobilize all the kingdom's knight orders, and meanwhile contact Archbishop Scott—we must secure the Holy Church's support this time, and...'
Blaze wore a solemn expression, silently following Margaret, attentively receiving every order.
Seeing Margaret so tense, Blaze felt the situation was grave, likely another war.
Margaret had thought Mades and the blood clan could only operate in the shadows, but never imagined they could make the sun completely disappear!?
Now it's really troublesome; the blood clan, a race that can only survive at night and in darkness, no longer needs to hide timidly—they can act at any time.

Alice lowered her head, no longer looking at the solar eclipse, and asked Merlin beside her, 'Do you know what's going on?'
'I don't know.' Merlin shook his head, then continued, 'But this is obviously not a natural phenomenon; someone deliberately did this—probably a massive celestial body blocking the sun. I fear the whole of France and neighboring countries are now plunged into total darkness.'
'Can you move a massive celestial body?!' Alice gasped, her mouth unable to close, 'Is that even possible? It's practically something only a god could do...C )F little play'
'Yeah, it's practically godlike; even the demon race lacks this ability.' Merlin nodded with a sigh, feeling the situation troublesome; the opponent's power seemed terrifying to the point of speechlessness, capable of doing what only a god could.
Alice, hearing Merlin say the demon race lacks this ability, couldn't help but grow tense.
Although the demon race is few in number, they have endured for several epochs, showing their deep foundation.
Yet Merlin's words made Alice feel apprehensive, fearing this enemy truly is extraordinary—even Merlin finds it troublesome.
'What can we do? If this continues, even if the blood clan doesn't attack here, France will become a place devoid of any life.'
Merlin watched the eclipse, fell silent for a moment, then stretched out his hand, gesturing at the sun, 'Since the sun is blocked by a massive celestial body, wouldn't chopping it in half solve the problem?'
'...?' Alice nearly fainted, her face turning pale from Merlin's words, '.-. What are you saying?'
'I said let's try chopping that massive celestial body...' Merlin repeated expressionlessly.
'....' Alice nervously swallowed, pointing at the blackened sun, asking, 'You're not joking, right? This... this kind of Arabian Nights fantasy—can you actually do it?' SEZ novel
'How would I know without trying? But I think it's about right; it should be possible to chop it.'
Merlin subconsciously touched the katana at his waist, his heart inexplicably excited to the point of restless eagerness!?
But Merlin has never actually performed a draw-cut to slash a planet; he only knows his draw-cut is strong, almost always instant kills, and who knows what the limit of this 9999 trash skill truly is?
'....Alice lowered her head, face pale, thinking this lunatic really could chop a massive celestial body... wouldn't the ground beneath my feet also be unsafe?'
'I really want to give it a try, but I can't jump that far, and my draw-cut's range isn't enough—what a pity.' Merlin sighed regretfully, restrained by the distance.
Alice breathed a sigh of relief, rolled her eyes, and said,
'Then what are you spouting nonsense here? Aren't you just daydreaming?'
'.....Merlin stroked his chin, eyes gleaming with excitement, 'How about we try on the moon tonight? ! What if we really can chop it?'
'Don't do that!' Alice exclaimed, nearly frightened silly, she grabbed Merlin's collar, shaking him desperately to stop, saying,
'If you really destroy the moon, you'll be the culprit who destroys the world!'
'Calm down, let's think of another solution!'

title: Chapter 5 — Origin of the True Ancestor (Part 1)
content:
Chapter 5 — Origin of the True Ancestor (Part 1)

Volume 19 · Chapter 5

Margaret assigned a bunch of tasks for Blaze to handle, then hurried back to her own bedroom.
She was convinced that Mades was secretly up to something, and the sudden massive solar eclipse was likely preparation for a more fierce invasion.
If the sun disappeared, there was no doubt that the blood clans, who could only be active at night, would benefit greatly.
Without sunlight as a weakness, France would likely become a playground for these vampire monsters, able to run rampant.
Moreover, Margaret understood Mades well enough to know he couldn't possibly have the power to cause an eclipse; she suspected escaping the capital wouldn't be simple, and that he must have some important matter requiring him to leave.
Margaret recalled all the previous events and instantly felt that the bastard Mades was disgustingly—
Mades had originally planned to leave the capital, and even mobilized everyone to oppose Beelzebub, causing the empire to suffer heavy losses and a shortage of troops, allowing him to clear many obstacles without lifting a finger—wasn't that profitable?
Now the empire is unprecedentedly weak, the perfect moment for a counterattack to seize it; Margaret thought that if she were Mades, she would definitely not let this opportunity slip.
Although Margaret felt very tense, she wasn't completely at a loss, mobilizing her limited strength to prepare resistance.
If France seemed doomed to destruction, Margaret would consider using the underground mysterious star‑annihilating cannon, to drag the empire and all those bastards down together!
Margaret came to her dressing table, opened the lowest drawer, and took out a small box.
This was a treasure Cladi had lent her not long ago, called the God‑Sealing Stone.
Although it was only the size of a fingernail, it was said to be one of the materials used by Mistelin in legend, possessing the ability to nullify regeneration, resurrection, and so on.
Margaret hadn't studied this tiny piece of metal much, but it was about to be put to great use; she planned to turn the God‑Sealing Stone into an arrow, hoping to kill Mades with a single shot.
After opening the box, a single silver‑white stone lay quietly inside, though it seemed rather ordinary, lacking any luster.
What's going on? When Cladi took it out earlier.... was it really this ordinary?
Margaret picked up the small stone, held it before her eyes and examined it closely; the precious God‑Sealing Stone turned silver‑white right before her.
“Fake! ?
“...Who did this! ?”
“Now how am I supposed to explain this to Cladi X.+ =
At the same time, in a distant desert.
Dickteping, who had stolen the God‑Sealing Stone, followed the traces of the Canglan Youyan all the way and actually managed to locate the vampire relic.
At this moment, the sneaky him was hiding in a concealed corner, peeking at the vampires' every move below.
On the road he discovered traces left by a large group of people, and, thinking to give it a try, he followed them—unexpectedly he succeeded in finding this mysterious relic!
Oh~, look who I see? Isn't that the famous chancellor? I've used him for so long, it's time to collect some interest, right? Hehehe....
Dickteping sneered inwardly, his gaze fixed on Mades below, though he didn't know who the young man beside Mades was.
From the start, Mades treated that young man with utmost respect, constantly calling him 'master'.
At the center of the relic stood an altar, a huge red light shooting straight into the sky, like a blade plunged into the heavens.
The suddenly appearing eclipse was precisely caused by this altar, resonating with a distant massive celestial body.
The vampires' plan had nearly reached its end, using a massive celestial body to permanently block France's sun, establishing a dark domain for the vampires.
Mades led the dense throng of vampires, who knelt silently on the ground, utterly revering the master atop the altar.
In just half a month, Dracula had recovered, transforming from a withered corpse into a handsome young man.
The sight of ten thousand people worshiping truly resembled a cult gathering, feeling eerily strange....
Dracula slit his own wrist, letting blood continuously flow onto the altar, making the red light shooting to the heavens even more turbulent.
Only after the massive celestial body stabilized and completely blocked the sun did Dracula turn around, his wrist wound healing in an instant.
Mades excitedly shouted, “Long live the master! Our clan's long‑held wish has been fulfilled; from now on it’s our era!
The vampires followed with chants of “Long live!”, continuously kowtowing to Mades, essentially treating Dracula as a deity.
“From now on, we needn’t hide; we too shall live under the sun!” Dracula’s voice rang out, his black‑red robe fluttering, “If others see us as monsters, we’ll turn all humans into our kind; any place shrouded in darkness will be the land of our Eternal Night Empire!”
The vampires below erupted in unprecedented cheers, many beginning to dance and frolic, having claimed their own territories—enough to excite those who had been hiding in the night, barely surviving.
“For the prosperity of the blood clan, we are willing to offer our humble lives.” Mades bowed his head.
Dracula looked at Mades and said calmly, “Mades, during the time I fell into long slumber, you still managed everything and didn’t forget to wake me—truly your hard work; choosing you as my servant, I certainly didn’t misjudge you.”
“Please don’t say that; serving my master is my highest honor.” Mades said humbly, feeling deeply moved.
Dracula nodded and said leisurely, “We should have long since established our own nation; if it weren’t for that vampire hunter from a century ago appearing, our banner might already have covered this continent.”
“Yeah, that despicable hunter actually wounded the master’s body—unforgivable!” Mades’ eyes flashed with angry fire.
“That hunter, though strong, inherited part of the giant wolf totem’s power, but he never truly killed me; he merely delayed my steps, postponing my wish by a few hundred years.” Dracula paused, then coldly smiled, “But he’s the one who’s miserable—my curse remains effective; I’d wager the remnants of the ancient tribes that still worship Fenrir have been completely wiped out....
“Master’s martial might, divine power overwhelming!” Mades shouted, exclaiming, “I thought the master would still be wounded after waking, but I never expected him to recover so quickly, and even control a celestial body as huge as the moon—this is practically a miracle!
“Is that considered a miracle?” Dracula replied with a calm smile, “True gods are far more terrifying than I.”
“Has the master ever seen a true god?” Mades asked, his expression odd, curious.
“I really have seen one—it was a long, long time ago, when I was still a human treasure hunter.” Dracula lifted his head, trying to recall—
“Back then I heard that in the southern great forest of the Glen Plains, there was a mysterious altar.
“To seek the treasure, I and two companions decided to go in; fortunately we discovered the tomb beneath the altar.
“Inside, there was a genuine deity, but unfortunately she had been sealed inside a holy vial...

title: Chapter 6 — True Ancestor Origin (Middle)
content:
Chapter 6 — True Ancestor Origin (Middle)

Volume 19 · Chapter 6

Several hundred years ago, Dracula was not the progenitor of the vampire race, but rather a young man who traveled far and wide seeking treasure.

Dracula was born into an aristocratic family in the Holy Roman Empire, where he trained in martial arts from childhood; his father was also a renowned general.

Thus, he was not poor, and treasure hunting was one of his few interests.

With his keen mind, Dracula had gained some fame among treasure hunters, allowing him to smoothly assemble his own treasure-hunting team.

Dracula’s team consisted of only three people; the other two companions were both beautiful women.

One was Bathory from the Austro-Hungarian Empire, and the other was Lamia from the desert nation of Ptolemy.

All three possessed high-tier strength, making them a relatively powerful team among treasure hunters.

Based on various legends, Dracula set his sights on the Glenn Plains located within France.

It was rumored that deep within the dark forest in the southern part of the Glenn Plains lay a mysterious altar, which sealed away an evil deity.

Whoever could find that altar would have the opportunity to speak directly with the deity and gain unexpected benefits!

However, that dark forest rarely saw sunlight, and its complex terrain made it easy to get lost; no human who entered ever emerged alive....

Dracula’s keen mind immediately sensed that there must be something extraordinary here. Although dangerous, it was very much worth trying.

And so, Dracula led his small team directly to the Glenn Plains in France, settling down at a certain tavern—

“This is definitely the place. As long as we head south, we will surely discover that forest.” Dracula put down the map, a strong passion flashing in his eyes; every treasure hunt excited him immensely.

“Is the information accurate? Don’t take the wrong path and end up wasting our time again.” Lamia complained. Having grown up living in the desert, her skin was somewhat tanned, but her eyes were very bright, making her undoubtedly a beauty full of exotic charm.

“Yes, last time you took a wrong turn, and we wandered aimlessly in cold Greenland for half a month. On the way, we even encountered an Ice Frost Sacred Dragon and nearly froze to death under its ice.” Bathory also complained endlessly, sporting long brown hair, while the freckles on her face looked quite cute.

The three wore simple clothing, adorned with numerous weapons on their bodies, clearly looking like weary treasure hunters.

The tavern owner was long accustomed to such people; every few years, a group of these treasure hunters would arrive, all having heard rumors of the mysterious altar. Yet, after entering the forest, not a single person had walked out.

“Trust me! This time is definitely correct. If I’m wrong, I’ll eat shit right in front of you!” Dracula clenched his fist, speaking with great confidence.

“Please, don’t say that. You already owe tons of money; when are you going to pay it back?” Lamia rolled her eyes as she said this.

“Hehehe, I’m the captain, shouldn’t you trust me?” Dracula smiled awkwardly.

“We really had bad judgment back then, actually getting on your pirate ship? I didn’t expect your deductive abilities to be so poor...” Lamia couldn’t help but complain, revealing how bitter she truly felt inside.

“This time will definitely not go wrong. I’ve gathered a lot of intelligence; this time it’s certainly a huge treasure, possibly containing a god!” Dracula spoke very seriously. “Just like... just like a magic lamp, rub it twice and it grants us three wishes or something. Just thinking about it is thrilling~”

“But... but I heard that forest is very dangerous. No one who enters comes out. Shouldn’t we think it over more carefully?” Bathory hesitated slightly, feeling it was too risky.

“What are you afraid of? We are a famously renowned treasure-hunting team. Retreating before treasure is not our pursuit. This time, let’s do something big!” Fire burned fiercely in Dracula’s eyes. “That’s a god! Don’t you want to see it?”

“But that god... seems to be evil, doesn’t it? Meeting him won’t yield any good results for us.” Lamia frowned.

“That doesn’t matter at all. We’ll just take the benefits and leave immediately; we probably won’t fall into trouble.” Dracula patted his chest confidently. “This time has the potential for immense profit. Didn’t Bathory want to make money and return home to do business? And didn’t Lamia want to infiltrate the noble circles? Then don’t hesitate.”

Bathory remained silent, deeply tempted.

Lamia thought for a moment, finding no reason to refuse, and instead asked, “By the way, you don’t lack money, do you? After all, you’re the son of a general.”

Dracula smiled and replied, “It’s an interest. Treasure hunting makes me happy.”

A few days later, the three successfully entered the dark forest.

Like those who came before them, they got lost, running out of food and ammunition.

Yet, as if destined by fate, they stumbled upon the altar and discovered a mysterious entrance.

Unable to exit the forest, they had no choice but to press forward until they reached the deepest point—

There stood a sealed silver bottle, its patterns resembling written stories, emitting a holy aura.

“It’s empty here, except for that bottle? Did we come all this way for nothing?” Lamia said angrily, her face turning ugly with frustration.

“Th-that... shiny thing should be valuable,” Bathory deduced.

“No, I’m afraid this... Dracula stood at the front, staring entranced at the patterns on the bottle, seemingly able to decipher their meaning! ?

Suddenly, a crisp voice, like that of a young girl, rang out, echoing through the pitch-black tomb chamber—

“Who? Who entered?”

The three were startled, retreating repeatedly, as if they had seen a ghost. Where did this voice come from?

“Oh? How rare. It turns out to be weak humans. How did you get in? Were you not beaten to death by the dryads outside?”

“Who’s talking? Could it be a ghost?” Lamia broke into a cold sweat.

“Could it really be as the legends say, that an evil deity resides here?” Bathory held her magic staff, guarding against the surroundings.

“Why don’t you answer me? Are you deaf? It’s rare for humans to enter here; talk to me!”

Dracula nervously swallowed, unsure of where the voice came from. It might be hidden somewhere in the shadows; he felt himself being stared at by terrifying eyes.

However, Dracula had some experience; he forcibly suppressed the panic in his heart and began communicating with this mystery.

“I... what dryad?! We haven’t seen anything!”

“Didn’t you encounter that dryad from the divine realm? Haha, you lucky ones. That dryad must have been asleep; normally, you’d be dead!”

Chills ran down their spines. Hearing about a dryad from the divine realm, they believed seven or eight parts of the rumor: the entity speaking here might truly be a god!

Dracula continued recalling the pictures on the bottle, forming a vague guess in his mind, “...Are you a god?”

“Of course. I am a genuine deity, created personally by the Goddess of Light, Maria. Because I made a slight mistake, I was sealed in this hateful bottle.” The bottle placed on the high platform shook twice, attracting the trio’s attention.

“Normally, beings like me are unreachable in a lifetime, but you three lucky exceptions are different.”

“Congratulations. My mood is currently good, so I can grant you divine blessings.”

“As long as you help me open this bottle, I will fulfill any wish of yours~”

title: Chapter 7 — Origin of the True Ancestor (Lower)
content:
Chapter 7 — Origin of the True Ancestor (Lower)

Volume 19 · Chapter 7

“Genuine... God?” Bartoli stared wide-eyed, somewhat incredulous.

“How... how could this be...?” Lamia felt as if she were dreaming; gods and such... aren’t they only existent in stories?

Suddenly, the holy bottle rose with black smoke, gradually forming a stunning girl clad in holy robes.

This girl seemed not to be a physical body but a light‑shadow illusion; she had black long hair covering half her eyes, the other eye exposed was a celestial‑like red, as eerie as a blood moon in the sky.

The girl floated in the air, as white and tender as lotus root, captivating to behold; aside from being hand‑crafted by a god, no one could produce such a beautiful human.

“I am the daughter of the Goddess Mary, possessing divine power beyond mortal reach; I can easily grant any of your wishes,” the girl said, floating mid‑air, looking down, “Come, face your inner desires bravely and open the bottle.”

“Can you give us endless wealth?” Dracula asked.

“Cannot.” The girl replied.

“Then can you grant us exalted status?” Dracula continued.

“Also cannot.” The girl replied.

“You can’t do anything at all... Are you not deceiving us?” Dracula rolled his eyes, thinking this god was useless.

“I can make you my followers and inherit my power.” The girl smiled, a hint of malice flashing in her eyes, “As long as you have divine power, wealth and status are merely trivial things; they’ll be easily within your grasp.”

“Hmm... not bad...” Lamia felt a bit excited, stepping forward, but Bartoli stopped her, “What’s wrong?”

“Don’t act rashly...” Bartoli felt the situation was delicate; obtaining this divine power seemed too easy.

“What are you hesitating for? Such an opportunity to gain divine power isn’t something everyone can have; you are one in a million lucky ones—seize the chance, otherwise you’ll never get such a boon again.” The girl kept tempting them.

“I’ve heard that an evil god is sealed here...” Bartoli’s expression wavered, wondering if opening the bottle might bring something bad.

“Shut up, Bartoli! What does that have to do with an evil god? We’re about to gain divine power—isn’t that exciting? Good and evil are trivial!” Dracula’s eyes burned with fervor; he seemed very moved by this opportunity.

“Yeah, if she’s telling the truth, then we... could become world‑changing overlords overnight! She’s right—once we have invincible power, money and authority are child’s play!” Lamia, who originally lived at the bottom of society, felt tremendously excited by this chance.

“...” Bartoli felt unable to persuade them, so she closed her mouth; deep down she too was greedy for that power, yet worried about unforeseen consequences.

“Enough talk, we agree!” Dracula stepped forward, gazing at the ethereal figure, “First grant us power, then we’ll rescue you! Regardless of your nature, we only want what we desire—no trivial concerns.”

“Hahaha, I like your straightforward personality, but you’d better open the bottle first, then I’ll bestow power upon you.” The girl suddenly objected.

“Although you’re a great god, you seem unclear about the situation; you’re asking us to save you—shouldn’t you show some sincerity by giving us power first? If this is all real, we will surely open the bottle for you to emerge.” Dracula rested his head on his arms, adopting a nonchalant pose, “What if you deceive me? Who knows if what you say is true?”

The girl looked down on Dracula, her eyes flashing with disgust, contempt, and irritation—like a superior observing ants, full of cold indifference.

However, only a moment later, the girl revealed a meaningful smile and spoke in a resigned tone.

“You’ve got guts, daring to negotiate with me? I admire your courage—very well, let you have a taste of sweetness first, but you must let me out.”

“Of course, I swear on my soul, I will absolutely not deceive you.” Dracula bowed, making a noble gesture, appearing very sincere.

On the holy bottle, a black‑red liquid slowly welled up, like viscous blood or a living eel, writhing in mid‑air.

The blood split into three portions; with a “whoosh” as swift as lightning, it shot straight into each of their mouths.

The three let out choked groans, collapsing to their knees as their veins bulged and continued to swell, threatening to burst at any moment.

Following a long howl, the three treasure hunters emitted a powerful shock that made the entire tomb chamber rumble.

Their bodies seemed to blaze with blood‑colored flames; slowly they rose from the ground, their eyes now closely resembling the girl’s, and immense power continually emanated from within them.

“...This is divine power!?” Dracula’s bones crackled, his fangs protruded, and he was utterly enamored with his new existence.

“Unbelievable!” Lamia stared at her hands, feeling as if she stood atop the world.

“Truly....” Bartoli’s mind went blank, somewhat at a loss.

“Now you are my followers; each of you inherits one‑third of my power. I’m sure you can already feel this wonderful sensation—come, it’s time to fulfill your promises.” The girl’s smile gradually turned grotesque.

“Sorry, we’re not opening that bottle.” Dracula suddenly smirked, beginning to burn his bridges.

“What did you say...?” The girl’s face instantly turned ugly.

“Our power is your gift; who knows what will happen if you’re released? In your presence we’re merely lucky ants.” Dracula bared his fangs, mocking, “I’ve lived in the Holy Roman Empire since childhood, a follower of the Light Church

title: Chapter 8 — The Girl of Little Bull Town
content:
Chapter 8 — The Girl of Little Bull Town

Volume 19 · Chapter 8

Once Dracula recognized that the bottle contained the mythical Cain, he would never again believe the other's nonsense.
As a follower of the Holy Light, Dracula was well aware of Cain's story: this child created by God was extremely jealous and a villain who slaughtered his own kin.
However, Dracula was after all a treasure hunter, disliking coming away empty-handed; if he could profit from the famous Cain, that would also be highly beneficial!
As a result, he succeeded, obtaining power beyond imagination through deceit, and abandoned Cain at that altar.
As long as no one opened that bottle, they had nothing to fear; Cain could not possibly escape the goddess's seal on his own.
The three stumbled out of the dark forest, thinking that after gaining power they would achieve great things, but the result was not so.
Cain himself was an evil deity cursed by the goddess; the power the three obtained through deceit was certainly not that simple—
In the pitch‑black night, firelight illuminated the clouds over the heavens.
The small town outside the dark forest was now blazing fiercely, thick smoke rolling straight up to the sky.
The town that had been thriving in daylight was now utterly silent, corpses littering the fields.
Blood gathered into rivers, flowing through the town's streets and alleys, as if it had just endured a catastrophe—
At the town's center, the flickering flames illuminated Dracula and his two companions; beneath their long shadows lay human corpses.
"What have we done?!" Bathory, stunned, suddenly covered her face and wept.
Lamia wiped the corner of her mouth, looking at the bright red blood on her hands, "Why did we just lose our reason? Like monsters we attacked others, as if not drinking blood would leave us thirsting...."
"Definitely...." Bathory, feeling very guilty, said in a trembling voice, "It must be the evil god in the forest! The power she bestowed turned us into monsters!"
Lamia's face turned pale, she felt a bit nauseous, this was nothing like what she had hoped for, "Hey! Dracula! What do we do now?! Don't play mute! It's all because of your greed that we ended up like this!"
Dracula said nothing; he had not expected this outcome, he had greedily wanted to steal the god's power, but he did not want to become a monster contrary to his wishes!
He licked the blood at the corner of his mouth with his tongue; the blood originally had a rusty metallic smell, but now it tasted sweet, his taste buds altered.
Seeing Dracula absent‑minded, Bathory wanted to take initiative: "Why don’t we have that evil god take back his power? If that’s impossible, we could just smash the bottle...."
"No!" Dracula suddenly shouted, "If we let her out, we will surely all die!"
"Why do you dare...?" Lamia stared at Dracula.
"She dares to bestow her power upon us, naturally she has the ability to kill us; the reason we are still alive now is entirely because that monster cannot escape the seal's control!" Dracula glared at Bathory, urging her to abandon her naive idea early, "You haven’t seen the way she looks at us, like we look at ants that can be stepped on at any time— it’s contempt! Utter contempt without any concealment! I don’t know how long she’s been sealed, but she desperately wants freedom; as a child of the god, she doesn’t hesitate to give us power in order to break the seal’s shackles. If we really open the bottle, then she will indeed succeed! I! You! And you! will all be slain by her own hand!"
"Could it be... that we have to keep going like this, as a monster?!" Lamia felt unwilling, not wanting to live like this.
"No, we are not monsters." Dracula lowered his head, his eyes hollow, speaking extremely extreme words, "If we just turn everyone into our kind, wouldn’t that be fine? Then humans would be the monsters, right?"
"Dracula,... have you gone mad?" Lamia widened her eyes, face full of shock.
Bathory’s expression was terrified, she stepped back a few paces, "I don’t agree with you doing this...."
"Do we have any other choice? Rather than bow to Cain and be killed, it’s better to keep living." Dracula lifted his head, looking at his two companions--
"We now have this ability; since we cannot change ourselves, we might as well change others."
"It doesn’t matter if you disagree, as long as you don’t disturb me, I proclaim.... A circumstance"
"Our treasure-hunting team is disbanded."
Dracula withdrew his thoughts and roughly told McDees about his past.
McDees had not betrayed Dracula even during his slumber, thus earning full trust.
So Dracula had no qualms about sharing his past with his subordinates, and could let McDees bear greater responsibility together.
"I never imagined that, as a human, my master had experienced so much and actually seen a genuine god!" McDees knelt on the ground, sighing.
"Moving celestial bodies and such... is nothing; I am able to do it because I inherited the power of the true ancestor Cain; otherwise it would be impossible." Dracula shook his head.
"What does she look like?" McDees asked curiously; the gods he imagined were all bizarre in appearance.
"Ha, you’re actually interested in that?" Dracula smiled faintly, recalling, "Back then I didn’t see her true form, only an illusion; I don’t know about other gods, but Cain’s appearance is no different from a human’s—she had long black hair, a frail build, her eyes were distinctive, like a bottomless blood‑red abyss; staring too long felt as if one’s soul would be sucked in. If I hadn’t been sharp‑eyed enough to recognize the meaning of the pattern on the bottle back then, I might have thought the seal held a harmless girl."
"So she’s actually like a human....." McDees muttered to himself, feeling very astonished, then shifted the conversation: "Master, I heard you say that the true ancestor isn’t an evil existence at all; on the contrary, she is very pure, after all she truly bestowed divine power upon you, while you and the other two ancestors deceived her...."
"McDees, I originally thought your abilities were outstanding, but now it seems you’re still a bit foolish." Dracula frowned and continued, "As for Cain, she has been sealed for countless ages; her deepest desire is freedom. Our appearance gave her hope, so the Cain sealed in the bottle has little room for choice; the initiative lies in our hands. If we don’t satisfy her, she will remain sealed forever; satisfying her only offers a chance to gain freedom, but even that is merely a possibility—yet it’s worth the risk compared to having no hope at all."
"..." McDees stared blankly, realizing this was a choice between despair and a slim hope; no one wants to sit and wait for death, even a faint hope is worth trying. "It’s my shortcoming for not thinking things through; I originally thought I could communicate with the true ancestor and make her one of us."
"You’re overthinking it, McDees; remember, gods and humans are different—we will always be lowly creatures in their eyes, not worthy of comparison." Dracula looked at McDees seriously and said, "Fortunately Cain cannot free herself by herself; otherwise, once she breaks free, her first goal would be to kill us three deceivers and reclaim her power...."
At the same time, the small town where Old Mr. Akalon lived.
At the entrance of the Adventurers’ Guild, the little girl rescued by Merlin and Alice was lonely and curiously gazing at the sky.
Her black hair hung down her slender shoulders, as if the blood‑red abyss of her eyes reflected a pitch‑black solar eclipse....

title: Chapter 9 — Missed Opportunity
content:
Chapter 9 — Missed Opportunity

Volume 19 · Chapter 9

The little girl quietly gazed at the sky, her eyes full of doubt and childish innocence; it seemed to be her first time seeing a solar eclipse, and she found it very remarkable.
Old Akalon walked out of the guild and came to the little girl's side. After looking at the dark sky, he asked in a kind tone, "What are you looking at?"
"Akalon Grandpa!" the little girl pointed at the sky and said in a childish voice,
"The sky suddenly went dark?"
"Oh~" Old Akalon didn't notice anything strange, treating it as quite ordinary, "It's just a solar eclipse, no need to make a fuss."
"A solar eclipse? Will Mr. Sun come out again?" the little girl showed a bit of worry.
"Yes, it's only temporary; the sun will come out soon." Old Akalon squatted down, trying to be at eye level with the little girl.
"That's wonderful; if the sky stays dark, Mom might not be able to find me..." the little girl said innocently.
".... Old Akalon stared, feeling a bit sad inside; it hasn't been long, yet this child has already started missing Miss Alice, coming every day to sit blankly at the guild's entrance, probably hoping to see her mother sooner. But strangely, this child doesn't miss Merlin at all."
The little girl's eyes were sad as she murmured, "I miss Mom."
"Don't worry, your mother will be back soon." Old Akalon stroked the girl's hair, trying to comfort her.

"Of course, Miss Alice won't abandon you; you just need to be patient and wait." Old Akalon said with a smile.

Old Akalon secretly wiped the cold sweat from his forehead, thinking, "Indeed, just a little kid, really good...."
In the ruins of the blood clan.
"Will the True Ancestor kill the master and the other two progenitors?" Medes frowned, not understanding; the True Ancestor's power was supposedly divided among three people, so logically the True Ancestor now should be powerless.
"Yeah, our power came from deception, and besides, the gods are high above; how could they share power with humans?" Dracula sighed helplessly.
"But you said the True Ancestor's power was given to us; she couldn't possibly have the ability to defeat the master now, right?" Medes voiced his doubt. =
"Medes, kneel down and bark twice like a dog." Dracula suddenly issued the command, his scarlet eyes flashing eerily.
Medes stiffened all over, 'plop' knelt on the ground, and immediately barked 'Woof! Woof!'
The lower blood clan members below all lifted their heads, looking at Medes with strange eyes, thinking he might have lost his mind.
Medes broke out in a cold sweat; only he himself knew what just happened, his body uncontrollable, he was carrying out Dracula's order.
"You should have felt it, right? Our blood clan is a strictly hierarchical group, with absolute bloodline suppression; higher bloodlines need no martial action, just a word can kill lower blood clan members—it's that extreme. You are my followers, and I am your master; this is an irresistible ruling power." Dracula paused, then continued, "In the blood clan's pyramid, the one at the top is not me, but the True Ancestor Cain. Even though her power was tricked away by us, she only needs to say one word, and we will walk into the light to kill ourselves, and we will act like fools...."
".... This is just too terrifying.... Medes trembled all over, a chill ran down his spine, 'If the True Ancestor gains freedom, wouldn't we become slaves?'"
"That's right; initially I didn't understand the absolute bloodline suppression, but later I learned why Cain could fearlessly grant us her power. Now, looking back, I still feel a lingering dread." Dracula lowered his head silently, thinking, 'Thank goodness I didn't trust Cain back then and stayed wary of the gods; otherwise the consequences would be unimaginable.'
"Master need not worry; since the True Ancestor has been unable to gain freedom for so long, she likely will remain the same and pose no threat to us." Medes abandoned his naive idea of winning over Cain, continuing, "However, to let the Eternal Night Empire gain a foothold, we still need more strong warriors to join; I wonder if you have any suitable candidates?"
"If there were, I wouldn't have been badly wounded by that despicable vampire hunter back then." Dracula gritted his teeth, recalling how he and the ancestors of the Austin family fought alone, and even now he bears intense hatred.
"Master, where are the other two progenitors now? Weren't we originally a team? Now, pushing the blood clan toward prosperity would also benefit those two progenitors; why not try contacting them?" Medes paused, full of expectation, saying, "I believe that if the three progenitors gather, they will surely make the Eternal Night Empire stand firm!"
"Forget it; we went our separate ways because our ideas didn't match. Bathory is innocent and kind, Lamia very pragmatic; they both think I'm crazy." Dracula shook his head, speaking in a low tone, "As for where they are now, I'm not sure either, but I guess they certainly wouldn't be like me, fighting for the ideals in their hearts; instead, they silently eat and work, living low-key lives."
Mmm, truly a pity..." Medes showed a disappointed expression, thinking that although the first step of establishing the Eternal Night Empire had been completed, they were just lacking manpower, and as a result, all those strong warriors were unusable.
"If we need more manpower, I suddenly thought of something." Dracula stroked his chin, considering other ideas; weren't all those intruders locked up? I saw a few inside whose strength is barely usable, ....
"Master's meaning.... . Medes raised his head, looking into Dracula's eyes, instantly understood; 'Alright, I understand, let them become our kind.'
Dickteping, hiding behind the high cliff, heard many things; his originally calm mood was now stirred up into huge waves-
The gloomy forest in the south of Glen Plains? A sacred bottle exists in the mysterious altar? Keeping black long hair and scarlet eyes, that urgent?
Damn! Why do I feel like I missed something? Or maybe I did something huge? Could it be a coincidence?
Dickteping carefully recalled recent events; his subordinates entered the forest and were wiped out, only one person came back alive, and he even brought back a young girl?
That subordinate also said the altar had a mysterious bottle, and the little brat's appearance closely resembles Cain's visage—good heavens!
Dickteping stared wide-eyed in terror, cold sweat trickling down his forehead, feeling he had missed a certain--soaring opportunity.
What refugee orphan?! That little girl is clearly Cain!
What the heck have I actually done?! I actually kidnapped a god!
If I could control Cain, then I would be on par with a god!
Damn! Actually brushing past Cain, this is more precious than any treasure!
No way! I'm not resigned; where is that child? I must snatch her back!

title: Chapter 10 — Overstepping
content:
Chapter 10 — Overstepping

Volume 19 · Chapter 10

What does it feel like to be angrily stared at by countless hungry eyes?
In the past, Dickteping never 'enjoyed' such treatment, but today he finally truly felt it—how terrifying it is to be stared down by a pack of hungry wolves!
The vampires' pairs of bloodthirsty eyes, in the dim light, were extraordinarily kind; Dickteping only felt a chill down his spine, as if countless ants were gnawing at him—
....It's over! No......I need to get out of this damned place quickly!
Dickteping's face turned deathly pale; he turned to flee, only to suddenly realize his legs had gone weak! ?
What's frightening isn't the wolf pack, but being in the wolves' den—escaping has become a luxury.
Dracula narrowed his eyes; he truly hadn't expected a mouse to barge in—truly a clueless act.
All I saw was Dracula wave his hand and raise a blood-red whip, lashing out with lightning speed!
This whip seemed forged from blood, able to lengthen or shorten, and when swung it actually mixed with thunderous explosions!
Dracula had no intention of killing this mouse, Dickteping; instead he chose to wrap the whip around his bare foot and forcibly drag him down from the high cliff.
"Ahhhhh!" Dickteping screamed, thudding to the ground; when he lifted his head again, several sharp weapons were already pressed against his throat, leaving him no room for rash movement: "Misunderstanding! Misunderstanding! Don't do this... I'm just... hehe, passing by, everyone, don't be nervous."
The vampires' faces were grim; having recently suffered a human invasion, they were now even more vigilant—any order and Dickteping would lose his head instantly!
"Who are you! ? Dare to barge in, aren't you an imperial spy? !" Mades angrily demanded.
Dickteping broke into a cold sweat, his fear reaching its peak, his hand instinctively moving to the revolver at his lower back resembling a mini magic cannon.
The revolver's chamber held the God-sealing Stone that Kladi gave to Princess Margaret, a holy relic capable of sealing all regeneration and resurrection abilities, able to take out any vampire present!
Even Dracula could be killed with a single shot! That's the power of the God-sealing Stone, as the material for the God-slaying Sword—far from being an empty reputation!
However, Dickteping was timid and nervous, full of worries—the God-sealing Stone is only one, while vampires surround us on all sides!
Even if he managed to kill the strongest Dracula, the other vampires would overwhelm him, getting him killed on the spot—drawing the gun is just a dead end.
Damn it! I can't resort to violence! If I move, I'll surely die—this losing deal I won't take!
So Dickteping put on a goofy grin, started rolling on the ground, licking his hand and said.
"I'm just a dog, woof woof woof! I know nothing, just kick me out! ! Hehe!"
"Seek death!" Mades snorted coldly, raising his palm.
The vampires understood, inching their weapons closer; when Mades lowered his hand, it would be the moment for Dickteping's head armor!
"Ah ah ah! Don't don't don't! Don't do this! I'm not an imperial spy," you've misunderstood me; logically I'm still an enemy of the empire, we have deep ties, you.... are all- partners, please don't friendly fire!" Dickteping's will to survive was extreme, practically like a dog—just short of wagging his tail.
"Hmph! Truly laughable, spouting nonsense without checking the situation? A mere human actually dares to claim he's one of us? Mades' lips curled, his eyes full of mockery, not even regarding Dickteping, thinking this guy is just a clown!
"I haven't lied; I've done many things for you, working like an ox and horse!" Dickteping hurriedly said, and he truly hadn't lied.
"Oh? Then go on—if you lie, you'll be tonight's meal... Mades wanted to see what ivory this weak fool could spit out?"
Dickteping swallowed silently, looking at the hungry eyes around him, and said, "I... I once worked for Countess Camilla of the Avignon main city!"
"Hmm? Camilla?" Mades showed a slight reaction.
"Yeah, actually I know I've been serving the great blood clan, my heart full of admiration for you!" Dickteping embellished, wishing to portray himself as a loyal slave: "Doesn't Countess Camilla often send you slaves? Those slaves were all captured by me! So I've made great contributions to the blood clan too! If you kill me, isn't that like unloading the mill and killing the donkey?"
Mades had indeed heard of this; the slaves Camilla sent were all bought from the mercenary group—'Could you be the leader of the mercenary group?'
"Hehehe, fellow, fellow in..." Dickteping gently pushed aside the surrounding sharp weapons, took off his cowboy hat, bowed and said, "I am the leader of the mercenary group, Dickteping, but... I'm now just a bare-bones commander; the mercenary group was scattered by two adventurers from Britain.
Mades heard Dickteping's words matched his own information, immediately believed seventy to eighty percent, and waved his hand for the vampires to step aside.
"So that's it, it's you..."
"Mades, who is he? Not an enemy? A Dracula asked from on high.
"Master, this guy counts as our assistant; to wake you from slumber we need many human sacrifices, this person is the one who helped me provide many slaves." Mades replied with a bow.
Dracula thought it over, then retracted his blood-red whip, nodded and said, "You're smart, you can see the situation clearly—I admire you."
"Whoa whoa whoa! Amazing! You must be the master of the blood clan, right? ! I've heard of your fame since I was young; my admiration for you is higher than the heavens, deeper than the sea!" Dickteping knelt on the ground and began a fervent licking.
"Heh heh, your mouth is quite eloquent—how did you know about this place?" Dracula inquired.
".....The petty one was following a troop, never expecting to meet you—truly fortunate!" Mades feigned a delighted expression.
"Why were you just hiding and sneaking around? Could there be something on your mind?" Dracula was very cautious.业
"That's not it; I'm just timid and fearful, seeing you all discussing things, I didn't dare to interrupt." Dickteping showed a cowardly demeanor.
"Look: your loyalty to my blood clan is indeed commendable; what do you wish to receive? I can bestow rewards upon you." Dracula looked down on Dickteping and said.
".....Dickteping really wanted to obtain the gold and treasures here, but he dare not say so now, fearing he'd be killed here; thus, getting too into his role, he said, 'I seek no riches or glory, only admiring the great master in my heart, so I wish to join you in accomplishing hegemony; since Countess Camilla's death, I've been neither human nor ghost, and today I finally found an organization!'
"Good, I..." Dracula's eyes turned sinister.
".....Dickteping had a bad premonition.....'What does that mean?"
"You aren't admiring us? From now on you'll be our kind—how about it, happy or not?" Mades said with deep meaning.
".....Dickteping held his breath, stared, his heart pounding, his face instantly turned eggplant-colored, purple to black—
"No way?
"I--I actually messed up =
