title: Chapter 11 — Neurotic (Couldn't Load the Website Earlier, Updating Late)
content:
Chapter 11 — Neurotic (Couldn't Load the Website Earlier, Updating Late)

Volume 19 · Chapter 11

Several days later, the capital of France was in a tremendous flurry, with new regiments arriving every day.

Margaret had issued a summons decree, and nearly all the armies across the empire had gathered, preparing to face the coming crisis.

The royal castle had been very desolate because of Beelzebub's messing around, but within just a few short days, the city had become incredibly lively.

Everywhere were imperial soldiers in red uniforms, belonging to nobles from various regions.

Of course, it wasn't only that—there were also many knights in exquisite armor with serious expressions. This portion was an extremely elite force, private armies secretly cultivated by the nobility.

If the French Empire fell, these interest groups would be the first to suffer, so the nobles were generously opening their coffers at such a time, helping the royal family weather this crisis.

The bustling capital became a temporary resting place for the soldiers, and all the taverns were busy as ever, constantly supplying alcohol. Even the women who made a living on their beauty became extraordinarily busy.

However, the sun in the sky still had not appeared, and the duration of the solar eclipse had exceeded everyone's understanding.

Many people even began to worry that the sun would disappear from France from now on, and that this land would become eternal darkness.

Rumors spread everywhere, causing widespread panic. Fortunately, after Margaret communicated with Bishop Scott, they fabricated a lie and spread it abroad—

"Meads cast wicked magic and turned our empire into darkness. As long as we defeat this evil man, the sunlight will shine upon France once again!"

The uneasy emotions immediately turned into shared indignation and anger, and everyone started sharpening their swords, preparing to kill Meads and save France!

Both soldiers and knights wanted to distinguish themselves in this war. Whoever killed Meads would be the great hero who saved the kingdom, becoming renowned forever—perhaps even able to marry the beautiful Princess Margaret!

Indeed, controlling people's hearts was the Light Church's signature skill. Even a lie could stir the crowd to fervor; one had to admire that.

In a room of the mansion, Messfield and Clady were secretly discussing recent events. The two of them were responsible for assisting France but did not need to obey Margaret's orders.

"Is it true that the former prime minister who fled is planning to counterattack?" Messfield asked.

"It should be. That prime minister is a bloodthirsty monster in the darkness. The disappearance of the sun benefits them enormously. Attacking right after the empire just suffered the gluttony Demon Lord's assault—a truly perfect opportunity. Your Highness didn't guess wrong; this struggle will determine who rules this land in the future," Clady responded in a low voice.

"Your Highness publicly ordered us to assist the French royal family, but she also said we should observe the situation and act accordingly." Messfield paused, then continued, "If Margaret can't win, should we instead support that prime minister? That way, Britain would still reap benefits, and we'd have fulfilled His Majesty's mission as well."

"It's best not to cooperate with that prime minister. He is not human at all; he's an evil vampire. Just like the Southern United Kingdom, where various non-human races have gathered, we must always stay vigilant. We cannot fully trust them." Clady lowered his head and said thoughtfully, "If possible, we should establish an alliance of humans. We must never allow any non-human race to join. In the future, the war may very well be between races. Grievances between nations are not important. To maintain the prosperous era that belongs to humanity, we still need to fully support Margaret."

"But what if Margaret loses? Wouldn't our support be completely wasted?" Messfield said hesitantly.

"Windsor, don't worry too much. In terms of military strength, we surpass France, but when it comes to hardcore power, France is even more formidable. We needn't yet worry about France's fate." Clady smiled calmly.

"Teacher, what do you mean...." Messfield was extremely puzzled. It felt like the house was already on fire; by all appearances, Margaret seemed more anxious.

"I predict this war will have only two outcomes: France wins overwhelmingly, or mutual destruction occurs, with France vanishing from the world map entirely, and neighboring Germania also losing a third of its territory. France's empire being utterly destroyed is impossible." Clady said seriously.

"Hearing you say this... France seems to still be in a strong position...." Messfield frowned.

"France has many trump cards. The famous twelve legendary magitech cannons apparently only suffered a setback against the gluttony Demon Lord. The intelligent elemental demon beast Flame Demon, renowned alongside our Britain's Lake Fairy—that, although I heard the host died, must have been well preserved. And most terrifying of all is the Planet Annihilator Cannon..." Clady closed his eyes and said leisurely, "Few people know about this thing, but its destructive power rivals the mythic artifact that split heaven and earth. Unfortunately, it's hard to use—it would engulf the entire continent. With so many powerful trump cards in hand, France's complete defeat is impossible."

"Uh, this is the first time I've heard of this. So France's trump cards are each more terrifying than the last...." Messfield's eyes widened. After hearing Clady's words, he重新-recognized the nation across the sea from Britain. No wonder Queen Elizabeth had requested proactive assistance—France was simply an ally with enormous resources!

"Unfortunately, our Britain only has the Lake Fairy as something relatively rare. It completely can't compare to France's; there is still a gap in hardcore strength." Clady sighed, then suddenly remembered something and asked, "By the way, recently you've been keeping a close eye on that mysterious figure around Miss Alice. Any leads?"

"No. The person is very cautious and seems to have known I was monitoring them from the start...." Messfield answered dejectedly.

"So vigilant...." Clady furrowed his brows, recalling the moments dominated by fear. "Then have you noticed anything abnormal?"

"No. That person often mutters about a sister or something, appearing rather unhinged." Messfield recalled.

"Could there really be no problem...." Doubt lingered heavily in Clady's heart; he remained suspicious.

"Teacher, why don't I directly attack him to test him? Perhaps we can discover something..." Messfield suggested.

"Only as a last resort. We need to win over Miss Alice, so let's try to avoid using force." After careful consideration, Clady continued, "Keep watching. Don't relax your vigilance. By the way, what was he doing today?"

"He seemed to have gone out partying with that black-iron adventurer Merlin. When they left, they were all arms-around-shoulders, very buddy-buddy..."

In another room of the mansion, a faint humming sound came.

On closer listening, it appeared to be a nursery rhyme circulated in the great snow mountain region.

Alice carefully wiped her slender sword with a silk handkerchief until it could serve as a mirror, then nodded in satisfaction.

Today she was left here alone, and she couldn't help but enjoy the free space, breathing the free air—and had actually started going a bit crazy?

Recently, Alice had been courted by all sorts of factions. She didn't say it aloud, but deep down she was very happy, and even... a little giddy?

To put it this way, Alice now had at least partially wiped away the past shame. She had originally been the Light Church's most failed Hero, with all sorts of rumors and jokes circulating among the common folk.

But now, Alice had transformed into a rising star. Refreshing! A sense of triumph! This was the true reflection of her inner feelings.

France seemed to be in chaos. If she were lucky enough to defeat Meads, wouldn't she suddenly skyrocket to fame?

At that time, admirers would come visiting one after another, fans would number in the tens of millions—she wouldn't even have time for interviews, and counting money from endorsements would tire her hands. Thinking about it made her feel a little excited!

Alice's expressions were rich, and she took advantage of Merlin being absent to direct and act out a one-person show in her room—

"You must be the great hero who saved France!"

"No no, you've got the wrong person...."

Impossible. You exude the aura of a hero; I could tell at a glance!

"Oh my, I've been recognized. How embarrassing. Yes, that's right—it's me!"

May I ask, what exactly did you feel when you saved France?

"It was nothing special, just...." (in Merlin's tone)

Truly France's savior; as expected, extraordinary. Now that you're also becoming a popular adventurer, may I ask if you've considered giving yourself a domineering title?

"I prefer to keep a low profile, so nothing too flashy. How about... Ice Dragon Empress!"

Alice raised her slender sword, then silently placed it back into its scabbard. Suddenly her face flushed red, and she covered both cheeks with her hands, feeling like a lunatic.

"Ugh! So embarrassing, so chuunibyou!"

"But something like Ice Dragon Empress isn't bad...."

(●'' ') *° *

title: Chapter 12 — Holy Church Knights
content:
Chapter 12 — Holy Church Knights

Volume 19 · Chapter 12

So this is how Alice behaves when she's home alone? If Merlin saw it, he'd probably be disgusted!

Alice had already tasted the sweetness of growing stronger. The girl who used to be looked down upon by the Church had finally won a spectacular comeback!

Various forces kept flattering her, letting her feel needed. She was feeling pretty great~

Now Alice felt she lacked an opportunity to instantly become a famous adventurer, a superstar shining like a star.

But right now, preparations against Medes were in full swing. Alice thought this was a perfect chance. If she could achieve military merit, maybe the Adventurers Guild would notice her and give her a chance to promote to Purple Gold.

Although Alice said she didn't pursue fame and fortune, she still hoped to be famous worldwide and admired, just not wanting to be purely a pawn of the Church.

Recalling the heroic figure of Elgin the Great Swordsman, Alice used to admire him greatly. But now she thought she could reach that height, maybe even more famous and hotter than him!

If lucky, she might meet the real Elgin the Great Swordsman, establish pure revolutionary friendship, and thank him for saving her life on the Redbeard Pirate Ship back then!

Half a year had passed, making Alice much more mature. She could already distinguish between admiration and liking. Now she just wanted to be with Merlin. As for that mysterious swordsman, she probably only had respect left in her heart.

Alice laughed to herself in her room for a while, then suddenly felt bored.

She remembered Merlin said he'd take Beelzebub out for some fresh air, come back soon, wouldn't go far.

But they still hadn't come back, making Alice a bit worried. Who knows what those two demons went out to do?

Alice walked to the window, looking around, trying to find Merlin and make them come back.

A low horn suddenly sounded, catching Alice's attention. She said

Although the sound was low, it carried a solemn majesty that made her feel very familiar.

It was an instrument exclusive to the Church. Those who heard it felt reverence, as if seeing a deity descend.

As the city gates opened, a Church procession in formal attire walked in. Leading them was a choir in Church robes with gentle faces, chanting--

"Great Mother Maria of the World, shining with light and love upon the earth, all living creatures bathe in it, enjoying God's care."

"Every believer is Maria's child, should be converted by devout love, letting light be sown into every corner."

"God's sister wanders in the mortal world, hoping she returns soon to the pure land, embracing the merciful Maria, the twins reunited.'"

"Demons killed God's sister, they will never be redeemed. Poor demons will eventually be destroyed by light and receive due punishment."

Alice widened her eyes slightly. It sounded familiar. Two years ago when she served as Hero and marched from Vatican, everyone sang this song.

The tone was solemn, the melody pleasant, as if holy spirits were singing, calling a wandering soul back to the goddess's side...

Alice didn't particularly like hymns. They sounded uncomfortable to her, always accompanied by a vague sense of sadness.

"A procession of this scale... isn't it the Holy Knights?"

Just as she finished speaking, the sound of orderly footsteps and hoofbeats rang out. A team wearing holy silver armor, with pure white capes imprinted with golden crosses, marched in grandly.

Their expressions were serious, eyes firm and devout, like a war machine. Every step made the earth tremble.

With the glowing Church flags waving, the momentum was imposing. Their strict discipline was even better than the Violet Knights!

Every member of the Holy Knights is a devout believer, selected through layers of screening, each with high-tier power. Just this alone makes them elite forces of the human faction.

This formation appeared two years ago too, when Alice led the Holy Knights to assault the First Demon Lord Palace.

The Holy Knights are large in scale and divided into branches. I bet today's grand procession is one of them.

The backbone protecting the Church are the Holy Knight Captains. They are the leaders of the Holy Knights.

Alice had seen those Holy Knight Captains before. She scanned carefully but saw no familiar faces. It seems the Church supports the French Empire against evil invasion, but only sent the knights, not the Captains.

The Holy Knights stopped. Many wandering soldiers gathered around, watching the Church's elite forces, frequently expressing admiration. A well-trained knight order is incomparable to these riffraff.

Bishop Scott slowly walked onto the platform under everyone's gaze. As a Cardinal, his status is no worse than a Holy Knight Captain, so he naturally receives respect.

"Brave knights! Thank you for coming from Vatican day and night across thousands of miles to France!"

"You are all warriors serving the Goddess. Repelling evil and spreading light to every corner is our lifelong mission!"

"Now the Empire faces the threat of evil vampires. To protect the land blessed by the Goddess, we will fight to the death!"

"Your deeds today will be recorded in the Church's history. Amen!!!"

Scott shouted. The Holy Knights showed intense fanaticism, raising fists to their chests, shouting "Amen" in response. The cohesion brought by shared faith was evident.

At this moment, a loud "boom" caused a commotion. Sand and dust filled the air. Soldiers screamed, flying into the air!? Looks like someone started fighting!

"What happened!?" Alice suddenly froze, widening her eyes. "What's going on!?"

Before the commotion, everything was peaceful.

Because the capital gathered many Imperial soldiers, everyone had nothing to do in their spare time.

What to do? Most soldiers liked to gamble to kill time, a must-have entertainment.

In the corner near the mansion, a group of soldiers gathered back with excited faces, shouting about big or small numbers.

"Big big big!"

Merlin's face turned red and neck thick, banging the table constantly, wishing his eyes could shoot lasers!

Originally he couldn't stand being idle, came to gamble with these idle soldiers.

If Alice found out, she'd drag him back by the neck with a sword in a minute and give him a thorough scolding!

The lid opened, three dice showed 9 points, small. Merlin lost once again!

Merlin covered his forehead, showing a painful expression. The pain of always losing at gambling is worse than being beaten!

"No! These dice are cursed! Why do they always pick on me!?"

"Haha! Sorry brother, your luck is just too bad"

Laughing sounds came from the idle soldiers around, thinking Merlin was simply an unlucky wretch who liked to gamble and ended up benefiting others.

"Why are your hands so stinky? Lost 127 times in a row! Even an idiot could win once!?" Beside him, Beelzebub couldn't bear to watch anymore. Merlin was like cursed; Lady Luck would never visit him.

"...So uncomfortable. Why... why can't I win once..."

Merlin looked at his empty money pouch, expression wanting to die. The private savings he'd secretly accumulated, 1270 gold coins total, were all lost in an instant, becoming penniless.

It seems the unlucky Merlin is always misunderstood as a man who lives off women. Maybe it's understandable. Nothing strange. When he has no money, he can only rely on Alice to get by.

"It's the Holy Knights! The Church's team is here too! Come look!"

Someone shouted, and surrounding soldiers left one after another, wanting to see the Holy Knights' prowess.

"Who came?" Merlin didn't hear clearly, suddenly uncomfortable with so many people leaving.

"Hey, the Holy Knights. Elite forces under the Church, vanguard against the demon race. Everyone's talented, power not to be underestimated. Probably the strongest team in this capital." The soldier handling the dice answered casually.

"Oh~ So those experience babies? What crap. My little finger can beat ten thousand. Super easy~" Beelzebub said with disdain, showing her little finger.

"Hey, what's that supposed to be? Two years ago I cut down ten thousand Holy Knights with one stroke." Merlin suddenly remembered something, said awkwardly. "Oh right, only one escaped..."

"...People..." The soldier handling the dice looked up, several black lines slid down his forehead, mocking with a crooked mouth.

"Amazing, didn't see that coming~"

"Two brothers, each better at bragging than five!"

(.∞●1川)

title: Chapter 13 — Turmoil
content:
Chapter 13 — Turmoil

Volume 19 · Chapter 13

Even though these idle soldiers had called him a bluffer, Merlin and Beelzebub didn't mind — after all, they came from completely different worlds.

"Hey guys, still want to play?" the soldier asked with a toothy grin. Having encountered such incredibly unlucky opponents, he didn't want to let this chance to fleece them slip away so easily.

"Well…" Merlin frowned, looking at his completely empty pouch with a pained expression. "I'm out of money. Looks like I can't keep playing."

"Huh? Are you really this broke?" Beelzebub said, his expression strange. As a demon race monarch, how could he possibly be this poor?

"This is all I had stashed away. I'd barely scraped together some savings, and today they all got lost gambling. Looks like I'll have to tighten my belt again from here on out…"

Merlin sighed and tossed the empty pouch aside.

"Oh~" Beelzebub suddenly understood, remembering that most of Merlin's money had to be handed over to someone else. It was embarrassing. "Hmph, actually handing over your hard-earned money to a woman? Pathetic! I feel so ashamed walking beside you now. Get away from me."

"There's nothing I can do about it. Gold coins never stay with me. Alice stopped trusting me long ago. If I couldn't squeeze a few feathers from this iron hen, I doubt I could even afford a plain bread roll." Merlin shrugged helplessly. Constantly throwing his money into the horse racing tracks had long since exhausted Alice's patience, and now she kept a very strict grip on his finances.

"Can't you just ask for it directly? As a lofty and powerful existence, how can you tolerate a human woman riding roughshod over you? If worst comes to worst…" Beelzebub thought for a moment, "couldn't you just take it? I don't think she'd be able to resist you."

"Forget it. I definitely would've done that in the past, but now that we're close, it's really not something I can just go and do. Besides, if Alice finds out I'm gambling and messing around again, she'll absolutely stand on the moral high ground and come down on me like a ton of bricks. The scolding won't end for days. I'm not going to look for trouble." Merlin gave up. He definitely wouldn't go to Alice — it would only put the cart before the horse.

"Tch! Absolutely infuriating. We two reigning monarchs actually have to watch a human woman's mood just to go out and have fun?" Beelzebub pounded his chest and stamped his feet, extremely vexed inside. If not for Merlin holding him back, he'd be more than happy to get rid of Alice, that cumbersome obstacle.

"By the way, didn't I give you an expensive crystal card a while back?" Merlin suddenly remembered that碰瓷 fellow Humphrey. Realizing Beelzebub was currently carrying a large sum, he stretched out his hand without any hesitation. "Hand it over! Let's play something big! Don't worry, I'm confident this time! My luck's back! I guarantee a hundredfold return!"

"You?!" Beelzebub shot Merlin a scornful glance and shook his head. "No way. You've lost 127 times in a row — what luck do you have? Besides, that's my money now. Better not even think about it."

"What's the harm? Pull it out and let's play a few rounds together — it'll be so much fun~" Merlin slung an arm around Beelzebub's shoulders and kept urging him to hand over the crystal card. "You know, it's the brave who get fed and the timid who starve. We're here for the thrill of it. Don't be so stingy~"

Beelzebub kept a stern expression, already thoroughly frightened by Merlin's rock-bottom luck. How could he possibly let his money go down the drain?

"Hey, two brothers? What's wrong? Got some difficulty?" the opposing soldier spoke up. He'd noticed the two of them acting all mysterious, unable to figure out what they were arguing about.

"We're not playing anymore. No money for now." Merlin released Beelzebub, stood up, and patted his pants, preparing to leave.

The opposing soldier's eyeballs spun, and an idea came to him. Driven by greed, he wanted to trick the pair. "Don't go! No money's no problem — you can play on credit!"

"Oh? You can do that?" Merlin perked up immediately and sat back down.

"You move aside. Let me play this round." Beelzebub considered Merlin a bottomless pit — no matter how they played, he'd lose. Better to let himself take a turn.

"Alright, you go ahead, you go ahead." Merlin resignedly made room for Beelzebub.

"How big are we playing?" the opposing soldier asked with a meaningful smile.

"100,000 gold." Beelzebub blurted out the enormous sum without hesitation.

"100,000?" The opposing soldier's eyes went wide. "100,000? If you lose, you're really paying up?"

"Save the chatter. I can afford it!" Beelzebub was blunt.

"Alright! Brother's straightforward — I'll play with you!" The opposing soldier loaded the dice, his face brimming with excitement. "Big or small?"

"Big!" Beelzebub bellowed, full of confidence.

Merlin raised his eyebrows. Beelzebub seemed quite assured — could he actually pull off a hundredfold profit this time?

"Alright then!"

The opposing soldier began shaking the dice cup. The clacking sound was intense.

When the cup was finally lifted, the three dice totaled 8 points. Small!

"Haha, sorry, you lost. Hand over the money."

"Heaven…!" Merlin wailed to the sky, thinking that perhaps not just himself, but the entire demon race was cursed? Everyone's luck was equally terrible!

"128…" Beelzebub furrowed his brow, sensing something was off. "Losing 128 times in a row — no matter how you look at it, that's too strange."

"Hey hey hey, what's so strange about that? You just don't want to pay, do you? Refusing to accept a loss after gambling isn't a good habit…" The opposing soldier grinned.

"One person losing 128 consecutive times is practically impossible. You…." Beelzebub raised his head, his eyes turning cold. "You're cheating, aren't you?"

"What cheating? Can't even afford to play? If you can't play, don't play!" The opposing soldier suddenly grew angry and slammed the table.

"But since you lost, you pay. 100,000 gold. Act sensible and hand it over. Don't make us rough about it — we wouldn't want to break your limbs."

Contemptuous laughter rose from all sides. Dozens of soldiers closed in, rubbing their fists as if to threaten Merlin and Beelzebub. Some had already drawn their weapons.

It looked like if Merlin and Beelzebub didn't pay up today, they wouldn't be leaving — they'd have to settle the debt with their limbs?

Beelzebub refused to believe it. He picked up the three dice and crushed them hard, only to discover—

"Hollow?!" Merlin leaned in for a look. There really was a trick. With someone as "lucky" as him, how could he possibly have lost 127 times in a row?

Normally, dice are solid. Hollow dice could have their weight adjusted to control the landing numbers. These idle soldiers really were cheating.

"Hahaha, so what if they're hollow? You didn't notice before, did you? That's on you for not being sharp enough. According to the rules, whoever loses pays. You still have to hand over the money, or else…" The opposing soldier drew his sword, pointing it at Merlin and Beelzebub. "Do you want to leave here alive?"

"I really hate cheating bastards. This game is unfair."

Merlin stood up, his eyes cold, his expression dark.

"Indeed. Those who break the rules should pay the price." Beelzebub also stood, his expression no different from Merlin's.

"Hey hey hey, you two rotten ne'er-do-wells, looking to die? Right now is a very sensitive period. We're the soldiers, you know. Killing the two of you would be no trouble at all. I suggest you just hand over the money obediently, otherwise…" The opposing soldier stroked his sharp blade and drawled, "We're also the empire's elite troops. We've campaigned against powerful magic beasts and even killed dragons' sub-species. You two? Don't even think about resisting. Without anyone else's help, I can beat the two of you so badly you won't even recognize your own mother. Hehe~"

With a loud bang from the corner of the Royal City Avenue, dust and debris erupted in every direction.

Dozens of soldiers were sent flying out, all bruised and battered, some even with their clothes torn to shreds — utterly wretched!

This sudden commotion made everyone on the avenue tense up. Did war begin all of a sudden?!!

The Holy Church knighthood's knights immediately went on high alert, assuming an imminent battle stance and keeping watch on all sides.

Archbishop Scalder, who had been delivering a passionate speech, furrowed his brows slightly, suspicion rising in his mind.

Could Jeanne have started making her move already?

Why is there such a huge disturbance?

Didn't I tell her to eliminate them quietly?

title: Chapter 14 — Assassination in the Shadows
content:
Chapter 14 — Assassination in the Shadows

Volume 19 · Chapter 14

After the commotion caused by Merlin and Belial, the entire capital city went on high alert.

Knowing that violent elements were causing trouble within the city, the guards raised their weapons and began searching everywhere.

It seemed the guards didn't know Merlin was Margaret's esteemed guest; they just wanted to save face after seeing their comrades beaten up.

"Find those two guys! Someone just saw them running that way!"

A guard captain shouted, and a large group of soldiers followed him, chasing after them in that direction.

Not long after the guards left, a wooden barrel in the corner of the alley suddenly wobbled, as if someone was hiding inside.

"Seems like they're gone? Looks like we're safe now."

"Damn it! Why are we hiding? This is so pathetic!"

The lid of the barrel opened, and Merlin and Belial crawled out. After causing the commotion, they had slipped away and hidden here to avoid being found by the guards.

After they emerged, they brushed off the dust on their clothes and sneakily looked around. Once they confirmed the alley was empty, they relaxed a little.

"We're not afraid of them. You have to understand, these kinds of troubles will keep bothering us. Sometimes hiding is easier than facing them head-on," Merlin said, shrugging his shoulders.

"Come on! Kill as many as come! I don't believe there's anyone who wouldn't be afraid!" Belial scoffed, clearly dismissing Merlin's words.

"You'll just create more problems. Human resistance is stronger than you think. They might submit to you on the surface, but behind your back, they'll always find ways to kill you. That's way more troublesome than those stupid fools who openly resist," Merlin explained.

"What's the big deal? Just kill all the humans! There's no problem that can't be solved with violence," Belial didn't want to be as low-key as Merlin, being chased around the streets by human soldiers was a huge blow to the dignity of a Demon Lord.

"Are you going to destroy all of humanity just because the other side is being stubborn? Never mind if you have the ability or not, just that statement proves you're really something. How did you even become one of the Seven Princes?" Merlin said with a meaningful tone, teasing him.

"Tsk!" Belial clicked his tongue in annoyance, knowing Merlin was speaking sarcastically.

"Alright, those fools won't find us. It's getting late. Let's go back?" Merlin ran his hands through his slightly messy hair and turned to leave the alley.

"What? Are you missing that human woman? No way! You look absolutely pathetic. I advise you not to get too attached to your human wife. You're not from the same world," Belial quietly warned Merlin, thinking this wasn't a good situation to be in.

"Cut it out. I'm just tired and want to go home to rest," Merlin waved his hand carelessly.

"Hmph!" Belial coldly huffed and silently followed Merlin, thinking to himself how this guy was being so ambiguous about that human woman. But after all, Lucifer III was universally recognized as the heir to the First Demon Lord Palace. He should know his own limits. If he continued to be stubborn, the demon race wouldn't tolerate such a disgraceful violation of taboos. The other princes would surely go to war with him. Just Leviathan, that giant beast, would put immense pressure on him.

Qian Xiaozhi

"Then... I heard that the escaped prime minister, Medes, is returning. Maybe your sister Miranda has a high chance of being found. After all, she's very likely been taken by that prime minister," Merlin suddenly said.

"Are you sure about that?" Belial perked up at the mention of his sister.

"Everyone's been saying that recently. It's probably very likely. Didn't you notice that there are more soldiers on the streets lately? Today, even the Holy Church's knights..."

"If I still don't get any results this time, I won't keep my promise to you. I'll find Miranda my own way," Belial said seriously.

"Alright," Merlin nodded, thinking he had no reason to interfere with Belial anymore. "But if it's really that prime minister who kidnapped Miranda, what are you going to do?"

"Need I even ask?" Belial's expression turned ferocious, his jagged teeth showing. "I'll eat him until not a single bone or scrap is left. If anyone dares to hurt a single hair on my sister's head, they'll have to pay with their blood!"

"I see..." Merlin nodded, somewhat understanding Belial's restless mood.

"What about you? If your sister was kidnapped, what would you do?" Belial asked curiously.

"Of course, I'd make them pay. But I wouldn't be as reckless as you. I might be a bit more rational," Merlin thought for a moment before answering. If it was Lilith who was kidnapped, as her older brother, he couldn't just sit idly by.

"You still have a bit of a conscience. After you left, your sister is now the acting Demon Lord. She's been busy as hell every day," Belial chuckled dryly.

"Haha, that's a good thing. If she wasn't busy enough, she might have already come out to bother me," Merlin shrugged his shoulders.

"If your sister finds out you've been fooling around with some other woman, she might get really angry. I'm really looking forward to seeing how you explain it to your sister," Belial's words were laced with malice.

"This..." Merlin frowned. It seemed his situation had already been discovered by the head maid, Ophelia. And before she left, she had clearly said she would tell Lilith about his affairs. His happy days might be coming to an end...

As the two were about to leave the alley, they didn't notice someone on the rooftop above them, a figure wearing a black robe.

This mysterious attire was just as unidentifiable as Belial's, completely concealing the face.

This person was Joan, disguised, who had been sent by Bishop Scott to secretly assassinate Merlin and Belial.

Joan felt her actions were quite dishonorable, but every time she thought about how Alice was becoming increasingly indifferent toward the goddess, the devout believer in her felt an immense anger.

Although Joan knew Alice wasn't particularly devout, the Alice of the past still showed respect to the goddess. But now she had fallen to such a level?

Joan believed Alice's change was greatly influenced by these two people. She couldn't just stand by and watch Alice be corrupted.

In Joan's heart, she still wanted to see Alice as a friend. So killing these two villains was also a form of redemption for her friend!

Wol Short Play

Joan had been observing them in secret for a long time, but hadn't found a suitable opportunity to strike.

However, today, these two annoying guys had actually come out, and Alice wasn't around. This was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity that couldn't be missed.

Joan switched to a regular steel spear to avoid being recognized. After all, a womanizing pretty boy and a crazy talker didn't need a pseudo-sacred artifact to be killed.

Joan leaped down and suddenly blocked Merlin and Belial's path. She slowly stood up, pointing the steel spear at them, her eyes narrowing.

Die! You two villains!

Scoundrels who insult the goddess are not worthy of mercy!

title: Chapter 15 — Battle to Wipe Away Shame
content:
Chapter 15 — Battle to Wipe Away Shame

Volume 19 · Chapter 15

Joan of Arc, in disguise, suddenly descended from the sky, blocking Merlin and Beelzebub's path, surprising both of them.
I originally thought some sharp guard had found them, but seeing the opponent's attire, I immediately felt it was not ordinary.
Joan covered her face with black gauze, wrapped even tighter than Beelzebub; at a glance she seemed to harbor some ulterior motive, unwilling to reveal her face easily.
Merlin and Beelzebub both stopped, watching the mysterious figure holding a fine steel spear; neither acted rashly, but the atmosphere felt very delicate.
"Huh? Where did this mouse come from? Brazenly blocking...." Beelzebub frowned, his tone threatening, "Do you want to die?"
"Who are you? For no reason blocking us? You're not here to cause trouble, are you?" Merlin sized up the mysterious person, feeling a sense of familiarity from the eyes and build.
Joan said nothing, already silently regarding the two as dead; a faint killing intent leaked out.
Merlin's eyes turned serious, as he discerned some clues; this person had come for him and Beelzebub, though the purpose remained unclear for now.
Although Joan remained silent, Merlin's hand had already rested on the holy silver katana at his back; if the opponent made a move, he could likely kill them instantly.
Recently France was in utter chaos; Merlin believed his enemies were hardly human, but rather a blood clan that had been hiding all along.
Perhaps this person had come to cause trouble as a vampire, so Merlin directly gripped the mithril katana, ready to take down the enemy at any moment.
Merlin had already tried; although his own sword slash could easily defeat a vampire, to completely kill the opponent he still needed the aid of a silver weapon.
"Oh? Looks like you don't intend to talk with us?"
"This guy.... has a fierce aura, probably wants to take us down." Beelzebub stood behind Merlin, smirking, "Interesting~"
Joan let out an angry snort, shaking the fine steel spear in her hand, a deep thrust that kicked up a tornado-like gale, aiming for Merlin's neck.
Her spear technique was overbearing; she deliberately did not use the holy church spear technique she had trained since childhood, but relied on her own strength, hoping to overwhelm Merlin and Beelzebub.
Seeing the vicious spear tip mixed with Saint-tier battle aura coming at him, Merlin remained calm, simply turned his head and easily dodged, raising his eyebrows, "Oh ho~, still a Saint-tier expert, huh?"
"Uh.... Joan was obviously--- stunned, not daring to claim her spear speed was unmatched, but it was comparable to lightning; how could a black iron adventurer possibly dodge that easily! ? Indeed something seems off....
"Hey hey, this guy really wants our lives? Hurry up and finish her off, don't waste time." Beelzebub muttered from behind,
book.S/"If you can't do it, I'll take over."
"I'm a bit curious about his identity," Merlin glanced at the mysterious figure; Joan, being a tomboy, though he felt familiar, judged the person to be male?
"Shout!"
Joan watched the two's nonchalant attitude, feeling deeply dissatisfied; she had come to kill them, not to play around.
Joan's Saint-tier battle aura surged again, her technique shifting as she raised the fine steel spear.
Accompanied by a howling sound, she used the spear to perform a cleaving slash; the fierce assault in the narrow alley left no room to evade.
Merlin felt the opponent was pushing too far, so he drew his sword, stepping back to assume a ready stance, "You bastard, don't get ahead of yourself, okay?"
Suddenly a graceful figure flashed across, positioning herself in front of Merlin; her slender sword was drawn and, in the blink of an eye, blocked the fierce spear slash.
"Clang"—a loud noise, huge cracks appeared on the ground, shards bouncing like bullets in the alley.
Joan widened her eyes; the one blocking her was none other than Alice, exceeding her expectations.
"Who are you? A lackey of the blood clan?" Alice furrowed her brows, using her slender sword to forcibly push the enemy back.
".... The masked Joan wanted to scold Alice for being crazy? Actually stopping herself? But the current situation didn't allow her to speak.
"Alice? How did you get here?" Merlin asked curiously, thinking Alice was still obediently staying at the manor.
"The commotion on the main street earlier was caused by you two, right?" Ashley turned back to question.
"That... Merlin scratched his cheek, embarrassed, saying, "We were just careless."
"Really, I guessed it was you two who came after us; why stir up trouble? Indeed, being with this ill‑natured fellow brings nothing good." Alice glanced resentfully at Beelzebub.
"What? Look at me? Who says I have a bad nature? Speak clearly!" Beelzebub felt he was taking the blame; gambling for fun was clearly Merlin's suggestion, and he himself never had that habit.
"Don't speak; I'll just say it to vent my frustration—who knows you're always causing trouble? It drags me in, damn~" Merlin shamelessly said, then covered Beelzebub's mouth, pinning the black pot firmly on him.
Beelzebub rolled his eyes, the veins on his forehead throbbing; he thought Merlin, this bastard, had shoved all responsibility onto him, leaving him clean—who exactly is stirring up trouble!
Alice temporarily didn't want to blame Merlin, but turned to the masked mysterious enemy, "Who are you? Are you here to assassinate us?"
..... The masked Joan's eyes flared with anger; seeing Alice protecting the two villains pained her deeply, feeling Alice had completely sided with the evildoers and was no longer the kind senior she once was.
"Don't ask; this person won't speak, better to capture him and interrogate properly." Merlin stroked his chin, still wanting to uncover who this masked individual is.
"Oh? Torture play? I like it." Beelzebub's tone carried a deep meaning.
A little activity
"Shut up." Merlin rolled his eyes, rolled up his sleeves, "I'll handle it myself."
"No, I'll do it; I can still handle an opponent of this level." Alice suddenly volunteered; after the brief exchange, she felt the opponent was comparable to her, and letting Merlin act personally might cause a huge uproar—after all, with his strength razing the royal capital would be easy.
Merlin glanced at Alice, thought it wasn't impossible, so nodded, "Sure, rare that you take the initiative."
Alice stepped forward, raised her slender sword, and said firmly, "Since you won't confess honestly, we'll have to resort to some means."
The masked Joan's forehead beaded with a drop of cold sweat; she gripped the fine steel spear tightly, constantly weighing the pros and cons--
What were they just saying? Probably they wanted to team up against me?
I thought I could come up with a good plan, but these two wastes are still hiding behind a woman?
Recalling my previous duel with Alice, it was still a few years ago at the Vatican Colosseum's hero selection.
Although Alice seemed to have repelled the Gluttony Demon Lord, I am certain that wasn't pure strength but some trick.
I can feel that the gap between me and Alice isn't large; I have a fighting chance, perhaps I can seize the opportunity to probe her odd stance--
Joan narrowed her eyes, gripped the fine steel spear, stepped forward with her left foot, planting the tip on the ground. The spear bore a strange--
Come on! I can't hold back any longer; I want to settle this once and for all!
After all these years, how far behind Alice am I still? Why not just duel now!
This time I will definitely not lose easily; I will reclaim my former honor....

title: Chapter 16 — The Three Swords’ Defeat
content:
Chapter 16 — The Three Swords’ Defeat

Volume 19 · Chapter 16

Alice saw the masked figure strike such a bizarre pose, her expression freezing for a moment as an inexplicable sense of familiarity washed over her.

Looking back carefully, the stance of touching the ground with the tips of her feet while holding a long spear — Joan of Arc was also very accustomed to that posture. Could it be...?

Alice felt perplexed. Aside from Joan of Arc, this was the second person she had ever seen using this stance.

Noticing Alice's distraction, Joan assumed the other was looking down on her and launched an attack in frustration.

After many years, the two were facing each other again. Joan fought with her life's conviction, determined to settle things with Alice once and for all.

Recalling the Colosseum in Vatican City from several years ago, her defeat had left Joan with the greatest regret of her life.

However, if she could defeat Alice today, she could prove that her strength was no inferior to Alice's — perhaps even superior and more suited to serving as Hero.

In the narrow alley, Joan chose not to use wide, sweeping techniques, opting instead for swifter attacks.

Consecutive thrusts formed a dense flurry of light and shadow, like a meteor shower, completely cutting off any area where Alice could dodge.

Facing such ferocious techniques, Alice instantly felt immense pressure and had to keep retreating, blocking the spear's strikes with her slender sword.

For a time, sparks flew in every direction within the narrow alley, the clash of weapons echoing constantly!

The originally intact walls on both sides, unbeknownst to when, became covered with nerve-wracking gashes, as though carved by sharp blades, their cut surfaces blackened.

Both fighters' strength was laid bare in the back-and-forth confrontation, their battle auras clashing furiously as swordplay and spear techniques each unleashed their fierce offensive within the cramped space.

"What's with this? Getting pushed back repeatedly? Might as well do it myself." Beelzebub couldn't help but mutter.

"Hmm?" Merlin furrowed his brow slightly, finding Alice acting strangely today, too cautious and hesitant. Was there something else bothering her?

Joan grew stronger with each exchange, highly aggressive and consumed by a single belief — she would defeat Alice. So her swinging spear was incredibly ferocious, holding nothing back.

In contrast, Alice was acting abnormally. Pressed by the enemy's follow-up attacks, she was forced to retreat while using her slender sword to parry and counter, appearing somewhat unable to keep up.

Alice had indeed underestimated her opponent. The other's spear technique was extraordinarily熟练, as though trained countless times, with each strike carrying a fierce offensive that brought considerable pressure.

Of course, that wasn't the root cause of Alice's distraction — rather, she felt the opponent's techniques were too similar to Joan's, making her mindset grow hesitant.

Having lived with Joan, Alice understood her well. Every familiar move before her eyes was exactly the same as when they had competed for the title of Hero several years ago, except the other had grown far, far stronger!

The sharp steel spear swung with terrifying force, its golden Saint-tier battle aura reinforcing every technique, bearing the momentum of an unstoppable surge straight toward the heart.

Joan grew ever more fierce in combat, her eyes growing fanatical as she repeatedly shouted within her heart:

It's working! I can defeat Alice! I will definitely reclaim the glory of Hero that was taken from me today!

Joan's golden battle aura surged暴涨 upon her body, and she shook her steel spear, kicking off the ground to unleash an ascending crescent strike, forcibly knocking Alice's parrying slender sword flying!

"Eh!" Alice's eyes widened in shock, and losing her defense, she could only watch helplessly as her slender sword spun through the air.

Without hesitation, Joan leaped into the air and brought her steel spear down with tremendous force, generating a sharp, biting gale that aimed to severely injure the undefended Alice outright.

In Joan's calculation, Alice couldn't possibly block her attack again and would definitely suffer heavy injuries, at which point she could easily dispose of the two useless men behind her!

With a tremendous crash, like a comet plummeting from the heavens, the steel spear struck a golden ice wall that had appeared out of nowhere — Joan had failed!

Alice's eyes gleamed with a golden hue as she instantly entered her half-dragon transformation, her unfurled dragon wings and hardened dragon scales exuding an incomparable aura.

The masked Joan stared in disbelief at Alice's dragon-embodied form, previously able to sense the dragon's pressure. Had she learned some kind of dragon race magic? Was this the secret to repelling the Demon Lord Gluttony? No! Although her intimidation had increased considerably, it was nowhere near that of the Demon Lord Gluttony!

"Oh? Reptilian transformation? Didn't expect you to get something like this. Did you teach her?" Beelzebub asked Merlin with interest upon seeing Alice's half-dragon appearance.

"How could I possibly have dragon race abilities? That's just an inheritance crystal." Merlin replied casually.

"An inheritance crystal? This woman is truly lucky. Such a rare item and she managed to acquire it — and successfully fused with it as well." Beelzebub seldom remarked with surprise. "Since she's now in control of dragon race power, the other party isn't even a match. Why is she struggling so much?"

Merlin didn't quite understand this either, so he urged, "Alice, what are you doing? If it's too much, let me handle it!"

Alice glanced back at Merlin, thinking perhaps she had overthought it? The opponent wasn't Joan — their techniques merely resembled each other. Regardless, she needed to find a way to capture the other first.

Settling on a decision, Alice retrieved her slender sword from midair, her golden eyes instantly sharpening as she began to counterattack.

Joan felt the overwhelming dragon pressure rushing toward her and subconsciously felt panic, as though facing a true great dragon! She appeared infinitesimally small before it.

Alice, already at the peak of Saint-tier in both battle aura and magic, had the two forces merge, suddenly unleashing power far exceeding any single power system.

Excluding Merlin, Alice was very likely the strongest adventurer in Rexham right now — the true flagship star, even surpassing Mr.卡尔 in strength.

Even across all of Great Britain, the knight celebrated as the number one knight, Mersfield, would probably pale in comparison to the current Alice.

Seeing Alice's demeanor, Merlin felt somewhat relieved, thinking she was finally getting serious? Hadn't she been deliberately holding back just now?

Alice shook her dragon wings behind her, moving with incredible speed. Her first strike flashed forth, emitting a biting cold aura!

Joan tried to resist, but couldn't withstand Alice's dragon race power at all, being knocked flying and crashing heavily into the wall within the alley, embedding herself deep inside!

Enduring the pain from the impact, she still involuntarily spat a mouthful of blood, looking thoroughly disheveled.

Alice pursued the advantage. Her second strike came down, the slender sword splitting downward with golden fused ice crystal power attached, greatly enhancing its attack.

Joan dragged her injured body to stand barely upright, but her steel spear was instantly severed in two, fragile as a dead branch before Alice's slender sword!

She stared blankly at her spear broken in half, suddenly feeling that things were not good — her earlier thought of defeating Alice had been nothing but an illusion!

Alice swung her slender sword, unleashing the third strike. Pointed ice spikes emerged, whizzing through the air one after another, leaving the enemy with no ability to resist.

Thud, thud, thud! A series of sounds echoed as ice spikes pierced into the body, Joann's joints all suffering damage simultaneously, losing her ability to fight back as her body collapsed limply to the ground.

Alice flapped her dragon wings and slowly halted before the masked Joan, pointing her slender sword at her and saying coldly, "It's over. I hope you'll cooperate with us."

The masked Joan leaned weakly against the wall, gazing at Alice's powerful figure, unable to help but show a bitter smile.

Several years have passed, and I haven't caught up to Alice at all — our gap has only grown wider.

In the past, there was still a chance I could defeat her. Now, in merely three strikes, I have no ability to fight back.

I really... can't match her.

title: Chapter 17 — Citywide Alert (Happy New Year!)
content:
Chapter 17 — Citywide Alert (Happy New Year!)

Volume 19 · Chapter 17

Joan of Arc felt extremely unwilling, but had no choice but to admit that there was a huge gap in strength between herself and Alice.
She could see that Alice had defeated her without using her true strength, because she was certain that the Gluttony Demon Lord was even more terrifying!
That kind of strength, which cannot be overcome by any method, is a chasm that even self2 cannot cross, completely not on the same level.
Although Alice couldn't beat Joan of Arc, relying on the bolstering of a pseudo-artifact, she truly wouldn't lose so easily.
It's a pity that Joan of Arc was worried about exposing her identity, so she didn't wear the pseudo-artifact belonging to the Hero of the Spear.
Joan of Arc covered the wound on her body injured by ice spikes, her eyes complex as she stared at Alice--
Alice probably didn't even use her true skills, right? This level still couldn't repel the Gluttony Demon Lord; she must be hiding some secret technique.
It's a shame that my strength is limited, so I can't see Alice's true power.
After so many years, I've worked so hard to improve myself, yet in the end I'm still no match for Alice—why is this?
Joan of Arc's confidence suffered a severe blow; she had thought she could avenge her past shame, but after fighting Alice, the pressure only grew greater.
“If you don't want to suffer fleshly pain, then be obedient; as long as you cooperate with us and tell us who sent you, you will gain freedom,” Alice said solemnly.
After hearing that, Joan of Arc's eyes flashed with a hint of a mocking smile; in fact, she had already prepared for the possibility that the assassination mission might go wrong.
Only see Joan of Arc's scarred body emitting a holy light, and in just a single breath she vanished from the spot!?
This is the teleportation scroll given to Joan of Arc by Archbishop Scott; it is a very rare and expensive magical item that can let one escape many dangers.
Such an ultra-rare item, the vast Holy Church only equips twelve cardinal archbishops with it, to prevent them from encountering mishaps.
Archbishop Scott, to ensure this assassination would be flawless, handed the teleportation scroll to Joan of Arc, telling her to teleport away if anything went wrong—little did he expect it would actually come in handy.
The archbishop's goal was to win Alice over to the Holy Church, without wanting to break face or cause conflict, which would be counterproductive; absolutely cannot reveal the Holy Church's identity.
“...Disappeared?” Alice stared in shock, eyes wide as she watched the enemy vanish right before her eyes, feeling somewhat incredulous.
“Ha, no wonder you're not afraid of death to come assassinate us—turns out you have a life-saving trick,” Beelzebub said with a cold smile.
“It should be a space-transfer type magical item,” Merlin frowned, recalling a few years ago when he brought Alice to subjugate his own bishop; that madman once used an item to dodge his Blade Draw Slash, apparently called the teleportation scroll, an ultra-rare item with price but no market. “That...just now that guy...couldn't be someone sent by the Holy Church, could he?”
“Oh? hearing you say that, those godmen really do often use such means,” Beelzebub nodded in strong agreement.
Alice: “Perhaps... but why would the Holy Church do such a thing? I once stayed in the Holy Church, and many people there consider assassination disgraceful.”
Narration: Alice's tone wasn't firm in her rebuttal, obviously lacking confidence.
“Hey! You're even making excuses for those heartless beasts of the Holy Church? Indeed, even if you left the Holy Church, your heart is still on their side,” Beelzebub said sarcastically with a hostile tone.
“Who said that? I—I just think it's not very likely!” Alice defended.
“Lucifer, you better keep an eye out—this woman... is not trustworthy, not of our kind, her heart must be different, you get that?” Beelzebub said from the side, trying to fan the flames.
“You're talking nonsense!” Alice's face flushed with anger, worried that Merlin would misunderstand her.
Merlin ignored Beelzebub, looked at Alice's eyes, felt the topic was sensitive, and thus casually said, “Maybe... just now it was my illusion?”
Beelzebub sighed, thinking Merlin trusted Alice too blindly, “woman's kindness.”
Alice lowered her head, said nothing more, her mind in turmoil--
The enemy's martial....
It's also a bit too similar to Joan of Arc.
Could it be?
Night fell, and many bonfires lit up in the royal capital.
That is the encampment of the soldiers and knights, where they rest.
Due to the large influx of troops into the royal capital, there was no way to provide lodging for everyone.
So many units camped on the streets of the royal capital, not staying in houses.
Today's disturbance caused by Merlin and Beelzebub did not cause too much chaos, but it was still reported to Margaret for handling.
At this moment, the palace was brightly lit; Margaret was busy in the study, acting as regent for the king, constantly approving documents from various places.
Since Madess could attack at any moment, Margaret needed to mobilize the empire's military forces as much as possible, busy to the point she hadn't slept well in a long time. But he, a rough warrior, truly couldn't help.
Blaize watched the exhausted Margaret, although these days he had been standing guard beside her
What help could he offer? He could only suggest that the princess get more rest.
“Your Highness, it's already late; you should rest first, then tomorrow you can attend to these matters throughout the empire's corners,” Margaret said.
“No, we must guard against Madess, considering every aspect; we can't let him find any opening.”
The quill kept writing and drawing: “No matter what method he uses to attack, we must respond; I feel that in such a situation I cannot
“Um, okay, Your Highness, but please take care of your health.” Blaize could only resign himself.
To relieve the princess's worries is practically a dereliction of duty for a knight.
Margaret: “Blaize, I heard today in the royal capital
Margaret did not heed Blaize's concern, but instead inquired about what happened today.
‘Did a disturbance occur? What's the situation? I'm not entirely clear yet.’
“Oh, yes, Your Highness, the royal capital indeed had a disturbance, but exactly what
Blaize hurried to answer. All matters within the city.
“What's going on? Tell me…… Margaret didn't lift her head, wanting to settle it, saying it was a vampire spy sneaking in.
“It seems there are two explanations: one says it was a fight caused by a gambling dispute, and another
Blaize said truthfully. How could a minor matter cause such a big commotion?
“Gambling dispute?” Margaret put down her quill, lifted her head, and said, “Such trivial matters, it's not impossible for spies to infiltrate the royal capital.” Margaret thought for a moment.
“It's possible; Madess wouldn't just sit and wait for death, while also ordering surveillance of the manor, not letting anyone in the manor…… at this time, the order says, ‘Instruct the guards to increase patrol strength.’
Waiting to leave the royal capital. Scratching his head, not really understanding why they need to monitor the manor, where Alice and
……‘Why is that?’ Blaize scratched his head.
Cladi's two factions only. These people are all our relied-upon external support; if they leave, we will fall into being
“Now is a very dangerous time; in the manor, they would perish together; this is the last resort—
“Action.” Margaret didn't want to use the stellar cannon against Madess; others didn't matter.
“Actually, just monitoring Lord Merlin would be enough; Lord Lin cannot---
“Anyone can leave the royal capital” — only Merlin
-~-;) .

title: Chapter 18 — Invisible Shackles
content:
Chapter 18 — Invisible Shackles

Volume 19 · Chapter 18

"Huh? Why?" Blaze scratched his head in confusion, thinking that there weren't many people in the mansion who could help France. Miss Alice and the two Thorn Knights were very useful, but as for Merlin? He probably couldn't help much either.

"Because as long as Merlin-sama is here, any crisis can be resolved."

Margaret answered lightly, not doubting Merlin's abilities at all. After all, she had witnessed him wrestling the Gluttony Demon Lord with her own eyes, and the scene was still fresh in her mind.

"If Merlin didn't have such high value himself, how could Margaret, as the heir of France, favor a mere Black Iron adventurer?"

"...Yes..." Blaze felt awkward, forcing himself to believe in his heart that perhaps the princess truly liked Merlin, so staying would make her feel at ease. It was just psychological comfort.

"We must rely on outside help to survive this crisis. If we fail, we... could choose to go down together rather than let that bastard Maides succeed easily." Margaret treated using the Star-Crusher Cannon as a last resort—even betting the entire empire, she wouldn't let Maides' vampires have an easy win.

"...Maides felt considerable pressure upon hearing Margaret's stern tone. 'Princess, has the situation become this dire?'"

"Yes. Among the three knights, Robert and Bartiloka have both perished. The fire demons that lost their hosts could dissipate at any moment. The twelve legendary magic cannons are cooling down and unusable. What do we have left? Without outside help, we can only choose to use our final trump card and go down together." Margaret's expression was worried. After the attack by Asmodeus, the empire had lost most of its fighting strength and was in a passive position.

"Good... That's true..." Blaze lowered his head, having to admit that the empire had been severely manipulated by Maides.

"So now we need to secure any force we can use. Those people in the mansion are all Saint-tier or above; they're very important to us." Margaret picked up her feather pen again and began busy work.

"Then... Blaze looked up, suddenly remembering something. 'Lord Claudi didn't give us a treasure, did he? Something that can seal any resurrection and regeneration abilities. Maides should be afraid of it too, right?'"

"....Margaret suddenly stopped writing, looked up, her eyes awkwardly avoiding eye contact. 'That treasure called the Sealing Stone... has been stolen...'"

Blaze's expression went blank for three seconds, then he panicked. "What?!

"Shh!" Margaret quickly put her finger to her lips, signaling Blaze to be quiet. "Keep your voice down, don't make a scene."

"...Stolen?! What are we going to do?! That... that was lent to us by Lord Claudi. How do we explain this to him?!" Blaze felt something terrible was wrong. No wonder Margaret had been so nervous lately; the treasure most likely to turn the tide had been stolen.

"Blaze, calm down. Things have already happened; it's too late to say anything now. As for how to explain this to Lord Claudi..." Margaret thought for a moment and whispered, "We can only try to calm him down and keep him from finding out."

"But... Lord Claudi treasures this Sealing Stone. We probably can't hide it from him for long," Blaze said hesitantly.

"We'll hide it as long as we can. If we really can't hide it, I'll find a suitable reason to make Lord Claudi accept it," Margaret said seriously.

Seeing that Margaret had made up her mind, Blaze knew better than to say more. "Alright, but who stole it? The servants..."

"No. I've already interrogated all the servants and the guards protecting the palace. None of them did it. But the guards mentioned a stranger wandering around the palace earlier. I guess it was a thief who slipped in during the empire's chaos..." Margaret showed an angry expression.

"Thieves?!'" Blaze widened his eyes, clenching his fists. "Please order the pursuit of thieves in the empire! We must get Lord Claudi's treasure back!"

"I know what to do, but right now we should prioritize dealing with Maides, right?" Margaret paused and warned, "Remember, don't let Lord Claudi know about the lost Sealing Stone."

In the mansion, Alice hadn't fallen asleep. Instead, she walked out of her room alone, looking at the pitch-black sky.

The moonlight was cold. Because a huge celestial body was blocking the sun, the night was now much brighter than day.

Alice couldn't sleep, still thinking about today's events. She felt there were many strange aspects--

Who exactly was the enemy that appeared in the alley during the day?

Why were the techniques so similar to Joan's?

Could the church really have ordered Joan to attack Merlin?

Although Alice had long left the church, her time as the Hero had been somewhat pleasant. She had met many kind priests.

So Alice instinctively refused to believe the church would use such dirty means as assassination to achieve its goals. She still had quite a bit of trust in the church.

"Why aren't you sleeping? What are you doing here in the middle of the night?" Merlin suddenly appeared, coming to Alice's side.

"Nothing, I just can't sleep," Alice said, looking down.

"Why can't you sleep? Even Asmodeus, the guy who lost his sister, can eat and sleep well every day. Are you more worried than him?" Merlin looked at Alice curiously.

"...I can't make sense of today's events..." Alice hesitated. "Is it really the church that wants to assassinate you?"

"Oh~ This matter?" Merlin smiled, seeming not to take it to heart. "These assassins are just small fries. If they wanted to kill me, the church would have to send opponents like the legendary Ten Heroes at minimum to give me a decent fight. I don't know for sure, but there are many who want me dead. The church is just one of them."

"But... Alice wanted to say she suspected the enemy might be Joan, but the words stuck in her throat. She thought about their hostile special identities—she couldn't just accuse the church outright. She was usually straightforward and quick-tempered, but at this moment she chose to hide some things.

"What do you mean 'actually'?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"...I...

Alice avoided eye contact, looking down as she spoke vaguely. "If... I mean, if the church wanted to assassinate you, why would they do it? In their eyes, you're just an ordinary little adventurer..."

Merlin stroked his chin and thought carefully. "Didn't the bishop of St. Brendan Cathedral come to invite you back to the church not long ago? You refused. Maybe they think you refused because of me, so if they eliminate me, you'll have no ties left, and returning to the church becomes inevitable. Of

title: Chapter 19 — Broken Flag
content:
Chapter 19 — Broken Flag

Volume 19 · Chapter 19

Alice said "if" with her mouth, but her face was full of seriousness, wanting to probe what Merlin was really thinking.

If Merlin said he was willing to be with Alice forever, she would be very happy and full of confidence in the future.

However, after listening, Merlin's expression flickered with a hint of bewilderment. He didn't really know how to answer, and he wasn't clear about what the future held. Whether he could be with Alice forever was an unknown.

Moreover, Merlin himself couldn't figure it out—was being with Alice forever really what he wanted, or was Alice just a temporary haven in his life?

Alice saw Merlin silent and speechless, feeling a little nervous inside. "Wh-Why aren't you saying anything? Is this question really that hard to answer?"

"It's hard to answer." Merlin replied honestly. "Being together forever... that's probably just a joke, right? We don't have any foresight, so who can say what the future holds? Your question is really childish..."

"..." Alice lowered her head, nervous to the point where her two fingers were intertwined, ...it's not childish at all. I'm just saying, hypothetically, we don't have to be like this forever.

"Oh~ if it's just a simple hypothetical, I can answer you." Merlin stroked his chin, lifted his eyelids to think carefully, then answered, "I don't want to."

"Huh?!?" Alice was taken aback, staring at Merlin in disbelief. "Wh-Why wouldn't you want to?! What about me don't you like?!"

"How dare you ask what I don't like about you? I don't like anything about you, you stinky woman..." Merlin wore a meaningful smile.

Alice's forehead showed bulging veins, wishing she could beat Merlin into panda eyes.

"Say that again and I'll have you! Don't think I won't beat you just because you're being cheeky!"

"How could I have ended up so pathetic that I had no choice but to be with you?" Merlin clasped his hands behind his back and began listing off her flaws one by one. "You're always nagging me, babbling endlessly like a mother hen. You grab onto every little trivial thing to criticize me. I just want to pee and read the newspaper in peace—looking at your reaction, it's like the sky is falling. Are you going to die if you hold it in outside? It really disrupts my leisure time, and besides..."

Alice, hearing Merlin continuously point out her flaws, couldn't help but roll her eyes. "Enough! You're not so great yourself! Every morning you'd rather die than get up! You don't know what you're thinking, do you? Your luck is terrible, always trying to gamble your way out of poverty—that's just daydreaming! And besides, you snore every night. I can hear it through the door. It sounds like a dragon flying overhead! If I didn't wear earplugs, I'd have gone crazy from your torture long ago! And there are so many other things I can't even be bothered to mention!"

CCZ Novel

As the two began exchanging barbs, it was clear they knew each other very well. Unfortunately, they both thought the other was deliberately picking a fight, and the argument was becoming increasingly heated.

"Damn it... Merlin frowned, glaring at the furious Alice. "You're defaming my innocence. I don't have a snoring habit!"

"You sleep like the dead, so how could you hear your own snoring? It's me who's being tortured!" Alice bared her canines, trying to look aggressive.

"Is... is that so?" Merlin broke into a cold sweat, changing the subject. "Look at this, you can't let go of even such trivial things. I hate it when you're like this."

"It's your fault first! Hmph!" Alice sniffed disdainfully.

"Sigh, if I have to be with someone forever in the future, I hope she's kind, understanding, empathetic, shares common interests with me, and preferably has a pair of ample breasts to make her feel feminine. ...you're not that person."

Merlin gave Alice a provocative glance.

Alice heard the first half of Merlin's statement and felt she barely matched the description, but when he mentioned having ample breasts, she sensed something was off—this was clearly provoking herself.

"Bullshit! You're shameless! Don't you look at yourself? Who would be so brain-dead as to want to be with you? It's a curse!"

"Pfft, I bet you're just angry because you're flat-chested!" Merlin wore a sly grin. "So let me ask you, if there are no major complications in the future and we still haven't paid off our debts, would you want to be with me forever?"

"I don't want to! Get lost! You're destined to be alone forever, a dog for life!" Alice, furious, kicked Merlin and turned to leave back to her room.

"Hey! You stinky woman, wait up!" Merlin rubbed his knee and chased after her. "I was being serious just now, you need to take it seriously too. What's with the attitude? You start acting unreasonable when you can't win an argument, right? Heh heh, I know you too well."

Far away, Mesfilth, who was keeping watch, secretly poked his head out, looking strange and wondering in his heart:

What are these two spouses up to? Are they on good terms or bad? It's really hard to figure them out...

In the grand cathedral of O'Brien, in Bishop Scott's chamber.

Jeanne was bandaged, and it was clear she had suffered significant injuries from fighting Alice.

At this moment, she knelt on one knee, apologizing to Bishop Scott. This time, she hadn't expected Alice to suddenly return, resulting in mission failure.

"Bishop Scott, I sincerely apologize. It was supposed to succeed, but Alice suddenly came back..."

"No need to say more, my child. Seeing you return so heavily wounded, I know what happened." Bishop Scott slowly turned around, looking at Jeanne with a mixture of resignation and disappointment in his eyes.

After all, Jeanne had once been an excellent inquisitor of heresy. Whatever task was given to her, she could handle it well.

But recently, Jeanne had failed repeatedly, proving to be quite useless. As the Scarlet Bishop, Scott was bound to be dissatisfied.

"Ugh, I'm so sorry..." Jeanne didn't lift her head, feeling extremely guilty for betraying the bishop's trust.

"No need to apologize, Jeanne. Lift your head." Bishop Scott paused, then asked, "The last time you faced each other was during the struggle for the Hero's position. Do you know how much Alice has grown now? How was this fight with her?"

"I didn't push her to her full strength. Compared to two years ago, she's become stronger and has even gained the power of a dragon. Without the aid of a pseudo-divine artifact, I can't possibly defeat her." Jeanne lifted her head and said honestly.

"If I had brought the pseudo-divine artifact this time, the outcome would probably be different."

"Even if I can't defeat Alice, I can still witness the mysterious power that repels the Demon Lord..."

title: Chapter 20 — Assimilation
content:
Chapter 20 — Assimilation

Volume 19 · Chapter 20

Is that so? Even with that fake holy artifact, you can only force Alice to reveal her full strength?" Archbishop Scott sighed, "It seems we were mistaken back then. If we had realized how great Alice's potential was, we shouldn't have pushed her out of the Holy Church. Now we truly regret it.... ....Jeanne feels uneasy, thinking she can't compare to Alice, and even Archbishop Scott's attitude toward her is different—he seems to value his senior more.

"If we hadn't blamed Alice for the failure to conquer the First Demon Lord Palace back then, she could have continued growing in the Holy Church and eventually become an outstanding Hero of the Holy Church, and we wouldn't be at a disadvantage in our conflict with the demon race now." Archbishop Scott lowered his head and said regretfully, "Just think, back then we were short-sighted, watching Alice leave the Holy Church helplessly—this is a huge loss for us."

"Bishop...." Jeanne couldn't help but emphasize, "No matter how much you admire Alice, she is no longer the same as before; she might never be able to become a...."

"Oh? How so?" Archbishop Scott asked curiously.

"Alice is so protective of those two slanderers of the Goddess; obviously, she is no longer the kind-hearted person she once was...." Jeanne bluntly spoke her mind.

"That's possible, but the Holy Church needs Alice's abilities; even if she is now bewitched, she will eventually realize that the great Goddess is her refuge—even the most devout believer can make a mistake, and Alice is no exception." Archbishop Scott mused.

"Your Grace, are you still unwilling to give up on bringing Alice back to the Holy Church?" Jeanne asked doubtfully, feeling that even if Alice returned now, she would likely be a liability.

"Jeanne, you must understand that the Holy Church now needs a strong Hero, and Alice might be the most suitable candidate." Archbishop Scott looked at Jeanne with sympathetic eyes.

"...." Jeanne lowered her head, feeling deeply unwilling; in the end she remained a failure, no matter how hard she tried she had no qualifications to become a Hero, while fortunate Alice always receives favor.

"I know you feel unbalanced, but I believe that if you just try a little harder, you will also gain the qualifications to become a Hero, after all, your devotion to the Goddess is something everyone knows." Archbishop Scott patted Jeanne's shoulder, speaking in a comforting tone.

"I understand." Jeanne suppressed her dissatisfaction and countered, "Was this mission's failure because Alice suddenly showed up? Should we continue trying to eliminate those two villains afterward?"

"Since we've been discovered, we shouldn't use the same method again—that would be foolish; they'll surely increase their vigilance." Archbishop Scott thought for a moment and said, "Perhaps we should adopt a milder approach? I will write a letter to His Holiness the Pope explaining the situation; if the Pope himself persuades her, Alice might change her mind."

Jeanne felt extremely surprised; she never imagined that to win over Alice, the Pope himself would need to intervene—the Pope is the Goddess's voice in the mortal world, the supreme commander of the Holy Church, QE之, i治

Archbishop Scott handed Jeanne a scroll: "This is a healing scroll; it can quickly restore your injuries. To avoid suspicion, don't let Alice see you wounded."

Jeanne suppressed her shock and took the healing scroll from Archbishop Scott, saying, "Thank you, Your Grace."

Archbishop Scott showed a pained expression, silently thinking to himself,

This time we lost two rare items: the teleportation scroll and the healing scroll.

As a result, the effort to lure Alice back to the Holy Church has made no progress at all?

What a loss.... .

Three days later, the vampire ruins in western France's desert.

The black sun still hasn't dissipated; darkness continues to shroud the entire empire.

Yet outside the ruins, many vampires wear sturdy armor from their ships and wield sharp weapons.

Such a scene of sharpening weapons and training troops clearly indicates that Dracula has begun preparing for his campaign to conquer France.

Originally this should be a time of blazing sunshine, but because the sun is blocked, these vampires can move freely without needing to shield themselves to avoid being burned by the sun.

This is clearly the ideal environment for vampires to live; they wish to conquer this land and establish their own nation.

As long as most of France's humans are turned into vampires, they will no longer be monsters lurking in darkness but a new species distinct from humanity.

The warhorses' neighing echoes across the desert; the vampires' numbers are not large, but including those assimilated disciples of the Azure Blue Abyss Flame, they total fifty thousand troops.

Although compared to the empire's massive legions this is nothing, the vampires' immortality and swift speed will turn these fifty thousand into an elite force capable of battling tens of thousands of humans!

Now France's trump cards have been exhausted, placing it in a perilous situation; Mades clearly understands this point and will certainly not let this opportunity slip.

As long as the French royal family is exterminated and the capital seized, this empire, trembling in wind and rain, will soon change hands and become Dracula's territory.

In the ruins' prison cell, the unfortunate Diketeping curls up in the corner, his skin deathly pale, his eyes indistinguishable from the bloodshot eyes of a vampire.

It seems this profit-driven fellow ultimately messed up, dragging himself in as well, becoming a member of the blood clan.

Diketeping, numb-faced, slashes his arm artery with a small knife; "hiss" blood spurts out, yet merely a few wounds heal instantly.

This powerful self-healing ability clearly shows Diketeping can no longer call himself human.

For several days Diketeping has repeatedly used this method to pass time, yet still finds it hard to accept the reality of having become a vampire.

Although he has gained new power, Diketeping dislikes it, feeling he has shifted from human to a despised monster.

"Damn it! Why did I become like this? I was only after wealth!"

Diketeping—neither human nor ghost—constantly scratches his intensely itchy neck; where the vampire bit him, two small holes remain, continually emitting an itchy sensation.

"Damn vampires, if I get the chance, I'll definitely kill you all."

"Don't be foolish; if you still think you can take on vampires, if you had the ability you wouldn't have been captured like us."

A mocking voice suddenly sounded from the opposite cell, where four listless individuals sat—turns out they are the four officers of the Azure Blue Abyss Flame: Eden, Laurie, Vina, and Yuna.

They apparently suffered the same fate as Diketeping—those who died were bitten by vampires, and under the toxin's corrosion they completely turned into vampires.

Diketeping lifted his head, furrowed his brows at the listless four opposite him, and couldn't help but burst out laughing—

"What the heck, you four idiots can actually talk? I thought you were mute."

"By the way, you guys are really something—how did you end up locked up here?"

"Heh heh, you're just like a stray dog....".

title: Chapter 21 — Boost
content:
Chapter 21 — Boost

Volume 19 · Chapter 21

"What did you say?!" Rauri looked up, his face pale, devoid of any color.

"I said you all look like stray dogs? What? Problem?" Dickteplin couldn't help but mock.

"Hah, why don't you look at yourself? We're all stray dogs, why mock each other?" Vina looked up, spiritless.

"Exactly, we're all prisoners now, who's higher than who?" Yuna agreed coldly, following her sister.
