"This bastard has been restless since being locked up, always making a scene, I've wanted to scold him for a long time." Rauri's brows furrowed with anger, seemingly having been annoyed by Dickteplin's muttering for a while.

"Shout! I like it! What can you do? Shut up?!" Dickteplin played with the dagger in his hand, feeling an impulse to throw it at Rauri's face.

"Hmph! Where did you little thief come from, daring to make such a racket in front of us? If not for the cage protecting you, I'd have beaten you to death!" Rauri stood up, patting his own muscular arm.

"Come on! Hit me!" Dickteplin made a grimace, constantly provoking the other.

"You!?" Rauri was furious, wanting to rush out of the prison, but as soon as he touched the silver bars, it felt like touching a high-voltage wire, and he was immediately thrown back!

This prison was specially made of silver, possessing the effect of suppressing vampire powers, originally used to punish disobedient vampires, and happened to be used to imprison those assimilated into the blood race.

"Ha ha! You deserve it!" Dickteplin laughed heartily, as if he had finally found some entertainment in this pitch-dark prison.

"You bastard..." Rauri got up from the ground, covering his silver-burned hand, glaring fiercely at Dickteplin.

"Could you please be quiet? At a time like this, what's the point of quarreling?" Eden, leaning in the corner by the wall, suddenly said.

"Damn! Being a slave to the blood race is bad enough, now I have to take it from a little thief too!" Rauri's forehead veins bulged.

"Hehe~" Dickteplin was in much better spirits, continuing to ask, "Hey, I was talking to you, who are you? Why are you locked up here too?"

"Someone like you little thief wouldn't have the chance to talk to us anyway, why should we tell you?" Rauri's eyes were full of disdain.

"Don't call me a little thief every time, can you even speak human language? Oh right, we're all not human anymore." Dickteplin showed a self-deprecating smile, continuing, "My name is Dickteplin, leader of the underground mercenary group in Avignon City. I'm someone with a face in the slave trading industry. Have you heard of me? ="

"Haha... Vina let out a string of bell-like laughter, "What? Just a human trafficker?"

"Now anyone dares to call themselves a big shot, not realizing they're just a lowlife." Yuna curled her lips, full of disdain for such a third-rate character like Dickteplin.

"Underground mercenary group leader? What nonsense? Never heard of it." Rauri laughed until his shoulders shook.

"Let it go, don't argue with him. He's just a small shrimp who hasn't seen the world, but he's somewhat interesting." Vina said with a smile.

"... Dickteplin clicked his tongue, his face ugly, "Ah really? I'm indeed not some widely celebrated big shot, but what are you guys then?"

"If we say it, you might be scared to death. Have you heard of Azure Blue Flame, one of the four dark guilds?" Rauri said proudly.

"Azure Blue Flame?"

Dickteplin thought for a moment, and indeed had heard of it - a criminal group that roamed freely, burning, killing, and plundering, wandering outside the law.

Their mad leader was a prolific killer, even by French standards he was a high-level wanted criminal.

Dickteplin suddenly understood - he had been chasing the traces left by dark guilds all along, which was why he came here.

"So that's how famous you are. But how did you end up locked up here?"

The four fell silent, clearly not wanting to mention the incident at the Humphrey Exhibition where Dracula annihilated them, resulting in the entire guild being enslaved by vampires.

Dickteplin looked at their dejected expressions and instantly guessed most of it, "Oh~ So you were taught a lesson by those vampires outside? Did the leader die too? That guy was hailed as the crazy butcher, a fire mage, and he just easily killed you? You're really useless~ Still have the face to look down on me?"

"We're not like you. We still have the ability to fight the blood race, while you can only survive by groveling at their feet!" Rauri frowned, not rebutting.

"We would have definitely exterminated the vampires here and taken the huge wealth for ourselves, we just didn't expect the guy in the coffin would wake up again. The root of all failure was thinking things were too simple." Eden sighed helplessly.

"Yeah, the progenitor in the coffin is way too strong, the leader and it are completely not on the same level." Vina nodded.

"Not everyone thought Dracula was dead? Turns out he was just heavily injured and fell into a long sleep." Yuna clenched her fists in frustration.

"Hah, you guys? You're not exactly strong yourselves, yet you like making excuses for your failure, acting like you could turn the tide~" Dickteplin shrugged.

"We're stronger than you too. You wag your tail and beg for mercy the moment you see a vampire. I really doubt if you're born with a cheap bone." Rauri recalled how Dickteplin acted when first locked up, acting like a grandchild of vampires, kneeling everywhere begging for forgiveness.

"...Want to die?" Dickteplin's eyes changed, fury surging to his forehead, immediately throwing the dagger in his hand straight at Rauri's forehead.

"Hmph, weak." Rauri waved his hand and deflected the incoming dagger back, aiming for Dickteplin's forehead.

Dickteplin widened his eyes and fell flat on the ground, groaning in pain.

Dickteplin sat up, pulling the dagger out of his forehead, the wound healing rapidly.

"With that little strength you dare provoke us? Don't even look at your own dog behavior..." Rauri said disdainfully.

Dickteplin's forehead veins bulged, murderous intent arising, he put his hand on the revolver behind his back.

He was inherently weak, relying heavily on this weapon forged by the dwarf race.

Now with the Fengshen Stone on his body, without exaggeration, if he wanted to, he could kill any vampire, including Dracula.

Dickteplin was somewhat provoked. One strong gunshot could take Rauri down, but he wanted to live, so he couldn't have no trump card.

At this moment, the prison door was slowly pushed open, and Medes led in four vampire knights clad in black armor.

"This is quite lively. I didn't expect you'd find entertainment in hardship, chatting like this."

"Damn it! What do you want?! We've already surrendered! What do you need to do to let us go?!" Rauri stood up angrily, shouting at Medes.

"Mr. Medes, you turned us into this in-between state of not-human and not-monster, what exactly do you want?" Eden calmly looked at Medes.

"Everyone don't be nervous, we're now the same... clan." Medes smiled, standing with hands behind his back, speaking in a low voice.

"The great blood race is about to embark on a campaign, bringing all of France under father's control, establishing a kingdom belonging to our clan.

"A kingdom forever shrouded in night, we will continue to exist as a new species..."

"So I hope you will all do your best and contribute your own value to the prosperity of the blood race."

"This isn't for me, but for all our compatriots, and also for your own future..."

title: Chapter 22 — Dickter Ping's Goal
content:
Chapter 22 — Dickter Ping's Goal

Volume 19 · Chapter 22

With the door opened, Mardes got straight to the point, expressing his intention to recruit everyone and asking them to contribute to the establishment of the Eternal Night Empire.

Duke Ping and the four members of Azure Phantom Flame had already been turned into vampires by Mardes, so there was no problem calling them kin.

Conquering France and establishing a homeland for the vampire race on this land was well in their interests at this time.

After all, once they went outside, they would either be treated as monsters or killed by the Holy Church using silver. It was better to join the vampire race for their own future.

However, after Mardes finished speaking, silence reigned in the dungeon. No one paid any attention to him, and the atmosphere grew awkward.

Cough, cough! You are no longer human, gentlemen. My proposal benefits you all. In the future, humans will become the lowest existence — food for our survival. Our great vampire race will lead the era and create the Vampire Epoch!

Mardes expressed his意思clearly and concisely: we're all in the same boat. Stick with me and there will be meat to eat; refuse and face the consequences yourselves.

The dungeon remained dead silent. The Azure Phantom Flame members still seemed to hold deep resentment toward Mardes, completely unmoved by the olive branch he had thrown their way.

We only want to obtain freedom. We don't want to do anything related to your blood-drinking business... Eden responded coldly.

That's right. You killed our boss. You forcibly turned us into blood-thirsty monsters. We should be the ones killing you, not the other way around. Laurie ground his teeth as he spoke.

Hahaha, I advise you to see the situation clearly. It is your honor to join our vampire race. You must have already realized by now that you possess new powers, right? Immortality, superhuman speed, and strength far beyond that of a human body. Don't these changes make you ecstatic? Mardes asked in surprise.

You really know how to joke. What is there to be ecstatic about when you become a monster everyone chases and stones? Vena said with a contemptuous smile.

Exactly. We're just a species that lingers on in the dark. Where does the sense of superiority come from? Yuna's lips curled slightly upward.

Mardes' expression turned cold, but thinking of how he would need them later, he had to suppress the urge to kill these people. I admire your backbone. You want freedom? Very well. I can grant you freedom, but you need to help us win the war against the French royal family first.

Can we trust your words? Eden looked up and asked cautiously, not entirely convinced by Mardes.

The others also stood up. Hearing that they would gain freedom after winning the war, some of them felt tempted.

Duke Ping didn't say a word. He thought: this is the chancellor of France, renowned for his cunning all along. If you believe him, you'd better prepare to be scammed to death!

Of course. I always keep my word. As long as you give it your all, even if you don't join our vampire race, I can grant you freedom. Mardes paused, then shifted the subject. To prevent betrayal, you need to voluntarily wear collars forged from sacred silver. If you play tricks during the conquest of France, I can control the collar at any time to kill you. It contains fifty silver spikes that will pierce your throat. So... you had better think carefully.

The four armored vampires each carried a silver-white collar and stepped forward, tossing them into the dungeon before retreating behind Mardes.

Eden, Laurie, Vena, and Yuna looked at the collars in silence. Putting one on meant handing their lives over to Mardes — the risks were enormous.

Eden, what should we do? Vena looked up and whispered.

Yeah, you're always the cautious one. Should we wear them or not? Laurie looked at Eden.

In the distance, Duke Ping remained silent, watching the four people in the opposite cell. He thought: this group doesn't have many choices, does it? If they refuse to wear the collar, given Mardes' ruthless nature, he might kill them on the spot. If it were me, I would definitely compromise temporarily, serve the vampire race wholeheartedly for now, and protect my life — that would be the best choice.

Eden pondered for a moment, then furrowed his brows and said, If we refuse, we might die immediately. Wear them. As long as we still have value to the vampire race, as long as we behave obediently, we can ensure our safety. Then wait patiently and find an opportunity to escape.

Makes sense. This guy clearly came with bad intentions today. He's giving us an ultimatum. Yuna nodded and picked up the sacred silver collar first, placing it around her neck.

After the collar was put on, it strangely contracted automatically, fitting the wearer's neck perfectly. Moreover, silver spikes protruded outward, as if ready to pierce the wearer's throat at any moment.

The remaining few didn't hesitate much either. They picked up the sacred silver collars from the ground and put them on, making a compromise to Mardes.

Very good~ Mardes clapped his hands and nodded approvingly. I hope you'll all perform brilliantly in the battles ahead. After the war is victorious, not only will I grant you freedom, but I will also bestow upon you considerable wealth.

Eden looked up and said coldly, I hope you can keep your word.

Don't worry. Mardes waved his hand with a smile. The vampire knights took out four bags filled with blood and handed them to the people in the dungeon. Eat your fill. A fierce battle is coming soon. Our vampire race's power is greatly diminished without drinking blood. I'm sure you've all been hungry for a long time, right? That feeling of thirst must be unbearable — as if ants are devouring your insides, making you want to rip open your own body...

The four members of Azure Phantom Flame took the bags and tore them open with their teeth, beginning to drink the blood inside frantically. Their eyes emitted an eerie red glow, clearly nearly driven mad by hunger.

Duke Ping was also very hungry. He pitifully approached the bars and watched the others drinking blood, subconsciously swallowing, his throat itching unbearably.

"Lord Duke Ping?" Mardes walked over and looked at him with a smile.

Yes, sir! Duke Ping said with a flattering expression.

Didn't you recently stay in the royal city? Mardes asked.

Yes, I set out from the royal city and then found my way here. Duke Ping rubbed his hands together, eager to ask for food.

Then you must be quite familiar with recent events in France? Mardes pressed.

Quite well. I can't say I know everything, but I'm clear on most of it! Duke Ping said proudly.

Good. Father needs to understand the recent situation in France. You'll come with me and tell him in person. Mardes raised a finger and emphasized, Remember to tell the truth. Lies cannot hide from us.

Chancellor, what are you saying? I'm utterly loyal to the vampire race! Duke Ping patted his chest to show his devotion.

Mardes nodded and ordered his subordinates to open the dungeon, temporarily restoring Duke Ping's freedom.

Duke Ping emerged nervously and timidly from the cell, then asked tentatively, Uh... Chancellor, don't I need to wear that... colored collar?

You don't. You're different from them. You came of your own accord to join us, so we consider you one of our own. Mardes patted Duke Ping on the shoulder. Congratulations on becoming one of us. How does it feel? Moved?

...Wow... truly moved to death... Duke Ping grinned without warmth, cursing Mardes viciously in his heart.

Moved my ass! Damn thing!

I'm neither human nor ghost anymore. How am I supposed to survive out there?

Just wait. Once I get the chance, I'll kill you all, and then...

I'll find that sealed god and gain even greater power!

title: Chapter 23 — Winning Over (First Update)
content:
Chapter 23 — Winning Over (First Update)

Volume 19 · Chapter 23

Mades led the extremely nervous Dicteping to the center of the altar and bowed deeply.

"Father, I have brought Dicteping."

"Are those people willing to serve our vampire race?" Dracula asked with his back to them.

"They don't want to. They want freedom. I've temporarily kept them in check by putting holy silver collars on them and telling them they'll be granted freedom once we win this war." Mades related truthfully.

"Hmph. Disgraceful creatures. Just kill them after the war ends. We don't need loyal subjects among our own kind." Dracula said coldly.

"This subordinate had the same plan." Mades revealed a cunning smile.

Dicteping kept his head down, trembling with fear, thinking: As expected. Fortunately I acted very loyal, otherwise I would have followed the fate of those stray dogs.

Dracula nodded and turned around to look at Dicteping, who was kneeling before him. "You have joined our vampire race as you wished. I wonder how you feel now?"

Dicteping shivered and knelt deeply, saying, "This humble one is overjoyed. I feel my strength has improved considerably. That power of immortality is truly wonderful."

"That's right. The bodies of our vampire race are far more powerful than humans. Especially that immortal body, which allows you to endure even more intense training. Even if you are in a lava flow, it won't completely kill you." Dracula explained.

"Is that so? Thank you for your favor, my lord." Dicteping quickly knelt, but his mind began to race. He remembered the fire demon in the secret room of the royal city. Before, he hadn't been capable of seizing that treasure, but now it seemed he could rely on a vampire's immortal body to obtain it! It seemed he needed to make proper plans.

"No need to thank me. This is what you deserve. I will not mistreat any member of our vampire race." Dracula smiled faintly and changed the subject. "I heard you came from the royal city, so you must be well informed about the recent movements of the royal family, correct?"

"Yes, please ask freely. This humble one will say everything without reserve!" Dicteping answered respectfully.

"Very good. I heard from Mades that the royal city was about to be breached under Beelzebub's attack. How was that situation resolved?" Dracula asked.

Dicteping nodded, recalling as he spoke, "It was repelled by two adventurers from Great Britain."

"How is that even possible? Hundreds of years ago I saw Lucifer II Vivian. That overwhelming aura still gives me a sense of pressure. Demon Lords are among the few top-tier强者 in the world. They were defeated by two adventurers? Haha, if that's true, then the Holy Church, which has fought against the demon race for a thousand years, must be utterly incompetent." Dracula sneered.

"My lord, those two adventurers are no ordinary people. One is a demon swordsman wielding dragon bloodline power, and the other is even more formidable—she is Lucifer III, the one who continuously defeated the Holy Church's Crusade Army!" Dicteping said hurriedly.

"Lucifer III? Vivian's child?" Dracula frowned. Although he had slept for a long time, before being mortally wounded and entering deep slumber, Vivian had not yet borne children.

"So it really is that man who single-handedly beat the Holy Church into submission?! " Mades showed astonishment. Seeing Dracula's confused expression, he elaborated, "This Lucifer III is indeed Vivian's eldest son. It is rumored that his strength is overwhelmingly formidable, undefeated to this day. Some even say he surpasses his mother in power. To deal with him, the Holy Church nearly deployed all its elite forces, yet still couldn't handle him. They themselves were dragged into a quagmire, falling a decade behind in progress."

"Oh? Vivian's son.... seems to be someone remarkable. Far more arrogant than his mother...." Dracula narrowed his eyes and asked suspiciously, "But why does he, as the new Demon Lord, help France repel Beelzebub?"

"This Demon Lord is currently an Iron Black adventurer. His mission this time seems to be to eliminate you, rescue Princess Margaret from Beelzebub, and apparently also to investigate the vampire race's hiding place." Dicteping said concisely.

"The great Demon Lord serving as a wandering adventurer?.... And at the Iron Black rank? Pfft...." Dracula couldn't help but laugh aloud, as if seeing a king reduced to a beggar—that absurd image.

"What's going on? With the strength rumored to belong to Lucifer III, he should have easily qualified for Purple Gold at the very least, maybe even higher. Why is he faring so poorly?" Mades was extremely puzzled in his heart.

"This...this humble one doesn't know, but everything I've said is the truth." A cold sweat dripped down Dicteping's forehead. He thought: Even if he's an Iron Black adventurer, one shouldn't underestimate him.

"There are quite a few suspicious matters here. As far as I know, the demon race wouldn't lightly kill one of their own. They resolve disputes through force of arms. That Demon Lord of Gluttony must not be dead; he is likely hiding somewhere. Perhaps...he's currently together with Lucifer III." Pressure flickered in Dracula's eyes.

"Can't be...if it's really as... " Mades didn't dare to continue thinking.

"That's right. Currently the empire is outwardly strong but inwardly weak. It cannot possibly stop our vampire cavalry's advance. Our true enemies may well be those two demon monarchs. If we can defeat them, then seizing France will be half accomplished." Dracula paused and said with self-mockery, "The empire wants to eliminate us, and those two Demon Lords also want to get rid of us. Given identical interests, it's not surprising they've aligned together."

"Father, what should we do? The strength of those Demon Lords is so terrifying. Can we still win?" Mades asked anxiously, knowing from personal experience how difficult Beelzebub's power was to handle.

"To deal with one Demon Lord, I have that ability. But with two, I'm not sure. Wait...." Dracula paused and looked meaningfully at Mades. "We still have one card left to play, don't we?"

"The meaning of my father.... " Mades thought for a moment, then suddenly understood and quickly clapped his hands.

Two vampire knights dragged Miranda to the front of the altar and threw this pitiful girl roughly onto the ground.

Miranda was covered in wounds. Supporting herself on her arms, she timidly surveyed everyone, her heart full of unease.

Dicteping's eyes lit up upon seeing Miranda, especially the clearly visible demonic horns on her head. He instantly understood many things. So it really was Mades who had kidnapped Beelzebub's sister, yet he pretended not to know, letting so many people be used as his pawns. That damn dog!

"Father, I originally bought this demon to be your feast, to further boost your strength. I never expected that at this crucial moment, she would become our trump card." Mades looked at Miranda with a smile.

"Our vampire race can inherit all the abilities of our prey by drinking their blood, but the prey will inevitably die from the blood poison's corrosion. Eating Beelzebub's sister won't maximize the benefit, so she cannot die. Otherwise, she would truly be worthless."

"I understand my father's intention...."

Dracula and Mades exchanged a knowing smile, as if they had secretly made up their minds about the plan.

Miranda saw those two vampires' sinister smiles and instinctively curled up her body, completely unaware of what she would face.

Dicteping's eyes flickered, a layer of cold sweat forming on his forehead. He lowered his head and thought uneasily:

Looking at their confident demeanor....

Could the vampire race really be manipulating those two Great Demon Lords with ease?

S■

I only just saw today that this work ranked fourth in the annual rankings. My sister's work "Sister Doesn't Call Me Brother" ranked seventh last year.

Being among the website's top ten authors for two consecutive years—I owe it all to everyone's strong support.

Some people say I don't deserve this? Is it because I didn't add extra chapters that I don't deserve it?

This isn't preordained. It's calculated based on an entire year's data. I'm in fourth place. Despite adding fewer chapters in the later months, I maintained a steady 2000 words daily and even had 7-8 missed updates within a single month, yet the problem isn't big.

Think about early 2018—this book's data was astonishing. Old readers know well. It several times competed for the top of the rankings, and there was even a record of 13,000 monthly tickets in a single month. Right?

Whether one deserves it or not.... it depends on the person, I suppose. As a useless salted fish, I wouldn't dare argue with readers. Honestly, I'm afraid now. I barely dare to reply to reader comments.

First, I'm afraid of arguments. Second, I'm quite busy in real life, helping my family with everything, so I rarely have time to read comments. Third, I've come to accept the relationship between authors and readers—I won't stubbornly keep arguing. I've become more laid-back.

So I'm not sure what to say. I'll just thank everyone here for their continued love and support. Counting this chapter, I'm doing three updates today to celebrate the fourth-place annual ranking.

This book is better than "Sister Doesn't Call Me Brother." It can still rank fourth despite taking a break and having fewer updates in the latter months, while my sister's work required me to add chapters throughout the entire year just to reach seventh.

Every day I look at my hair falling off the keyboard, and my heart turns cold. I really don't want to go bald! I guess my hairline has receded another centimeter!

Finally, today I'll think of a new bonus chapter rule to increase my update volume, and it'll be a reasonable one too.

The previous bonus chapter rules actually became invalid back in November when I dropped out of the monthly ticket rankings, which is why I didn't respond to all the criticism—I genuinely had no bonus rule in place. So it was just updating whenever fate allowed.

There will be two more chapters coming, and then I'll introduce a new bonus chapter rule. Stay tuned!

title: Chapter 24 — Gathering
content:
Chapter 24 — Gathering

Volume 19 · Chapter 24

A week later, almost all the forces the empire could mobilize had gathered at the Royal City. The weapons of the legions and knight orders were honed to mirror-like sharpness.

And on the Church's side, not only had the Holy Knight Order been dispatched to station themselves there, but they had also brought many silver-plated equipments to counter the blood arrows that could strike at any moment.

In the mansion, Beelzebub sat alone by the window, gazing at the pitch-black sun outside, his heart still weighed down by concern for his sister. Over the past few days, he had grown increasingly impatient.

As for Merlin and Alice? They were temporarily in a cold war with each other, and the two hadn't spoken in days.

Alice was deeply bothered by Merlin's answer that night and had thrown a tantrum over it. No matter how Merlin grinned and tried to coax her, she refused to pay him any mind.

"Alice~" Merlin sauntered over with a grin.

"Hmph~!" Alice turned her head away, putting on an air of wanting nothing to do with him.

"Ugh..."

Several dark veins popped on Merlin's forehead. He thought to himself: Does this shrew really hold grudges like this? I just told the truth. Isn't that supposed to be okay?

"What exactly do you want from me? What did I do to offend you? I just called you a flat-chest. I won't say it again next time, okay?"

"...It's not about that!" Alice's cheeks flushed slightly, and she glared at Merlin through puffed-out cheeks.

"Tch!" Merlin massaged his temples, thinking: Ugh, women are such a hassle! They're like cacti—there's no way to approach them!

"...Can't you figure out what you said wrong yourself?" Alice couldn't help but retort, hoping he would notice his own mistake.

"Miss, I can't read minds. You keep making me guess? Guess what, then!" Merlin's scalp went numb. He really couldn't stand Alice's stubborn temperament anymore.

"Then don't talk to me. I hate you. Hmph~!" Alice grew even more vexed, spouting angry words one after another. In truth, she just wanted Merlin to think seriously about the matter of staying together forever—rather than using it as an excuse to pick on her and start a huge argument.

"Fine, I won't talk to you then. Who's afraid of whom? Pfft!" Merlin refused to bow down either. As a result, the two stubborn souls locked horns, evenly matched.

"You!!" Alice knitted her delicate brows, her face flushing red with anger. Her shoulders trembled as she glared at Merlin. "Heartless ingrate!"

"Oh, you're not much better yourself, a nagging board-scourer..." Merlin rolled his eyes as he retorted.

"I--..." Alice's hand instinctively went to the slender sword at her waist. She was deeply hurt inside. She couldn't beat Merlin in a fight, and honestly, she didn't quite have the heart to. So she just stewed in her own anger, becoming even more withdrawn.

Noticing this, Beelzebub curiously scooted over and nudged Merlin, lowering his voice to ask, "What happened? Had a fight?"

"No. Someone's looking for trouble for no reason." Merlin answered with a stern expression.

"Fighting is good. If you're gonna do it, do it properly. Just kick this human woman to the curb, wouldn't that be great?" Beelzebub couldn't help but eggn Merlin on. Seeing Merlin—the Demon Lord like himself—always stuck with Alice, he really couldn't stand it.

"Hm?!" Alice had extremely sharp ears. Hearing Beelzebub's words, anger surged from somewhere deep within her. She slammed her palm hard onto the table, signaling the other party to stop meddling. This was a private matter between her and Merlin!

"Tch! Why so fierce? I said kick her, so what if it's you?" Beelzebub's face was full of provocation as he continued to nudge Merlin. "The worst case scenario is you just return to the demon race. You know how it works, right? As long as you're willing to go back, your subordinates will welcome you with open arms. Then what beautiful woman won't be available to you? I remember your head maid was a real beauty, wasn't she? Haven't you been keeping score of her for a while now? Consider it~"

Merlin remained silent, thinking: Should I go back to the Demon Lord Palace and wait to die? As long as the heart-stealing curse isn't removed, I can't have a moment of peace.

"You devil, don't bully people too much!" Alice suddenly stood up, glaring at Beelzebub with hostility. Not only was he egging Merlin on to leave her, but he was also helping him find another woman! This was unbearable!

"Hey, hey, hey! What are you doing? Want to throw a fight with me? Are you even worthy?" Beelzebub said dismissively. "If Lucifer weren't here protecting you, do you really think you'd have the chance to raise your voice at me?"

"..." Alice was speechless, but she was still deeply worried that Merlin might believe Beelzebub's nonsense. So with reddened cheeks, she secretly reached out and tugged at the hem of Merlin's clothes, silently expressing her dissatisfaction.

Merlin looked down, then raised his head and gazed at Alice with a look of helplessness, thinking—

If you're unhappy, just say it. Using this kind of method to express yourself—are you a child?

Sigh. In a way, this might be the greatest compromise she could offer...

The next morning, the sky was still incredibly dim.

The three of them were still resting, not yet awake.

Alice slept alone in the bed, while Merlin leaned against the bed frame, resting on the ground.

As for Beelzebub? He was like a solitary, aloof swordsman, sleeping all by himself on the windowsill.

He had thought today would pass without incident, but suddenly Beelzebub's eyes snapped wide open, jolting awake from his sleep.

Beelzebub swiftly jumped down from the windowsill, his gaze wary as he looked out the window, murmuring to himself—

"So they've finally tracked us down?"

Beelzebub glanced back at the sleeping Merlin and Alice, pondered for a moment, then turned and jumped out the window.

Merlin, whose head was hanging low, slowly lifted it to look at the now-empty windowsill. His gaze flickered, falling into confusion.

Outside Jiuyi's earthen city walls, a large number of vampire forces had gathered. They were clad in black armor, riding tall horses in formation. Dracula's fang banner waved atop the mountain peak. Clearly, the vampire army had silently arrived here. Every vampire was comparable to a knight who had undergone special training—swift in action, never hesitant or sloppy. Combined with the enhancements of their vampiric abilities, they felt no fatigue after drinking blood, and their combat power far exceeded that of humans. Although they were outnumbered, they could absolutely crush the legions within the Royal City. The dense black legion was awe-inspiring to behold. Judging purely by quality, the imperial legion had already lost.

"What exactly was our mission again?" Lauri asked.

"Take out the strong ones in the Royal City." Vena shrugged.

"What kind of brain do you have? You forgot already?" Yuna jeered.

"I'm not Lord President. Who would keep that kind of thing in mind?" Lauri spread his hands. "I hope we don't run into those two monster Demon Lords. If we bump into them, we're definitely dead meat."

"If we can't win, we just run~" Vena smiled.

"Will we really be granted freedom once the war ends?" Lauri asked again.

"Probably. Don't forget we have no choice. We can only risk everything and try once." Eden responded faintly.

"Cut the crap. I'm hungry again. This bloodthirst is torture. Right now I just want to bite through a human's throat." Yuna's eyes flashed red as the hunger pang struck again.

Mades noticed that Deidra, who was mounted on his horse, had a peculiar expression, his fists clenched as if burdened by thoughts. "Father, what's wrong?"

"Hmm... Seems we've already been discovered." Dracula opened his clenched fist, revealing a housefly that had just been crushed inside.

"Excellent reconnaissance skills. As expected of the Fly King who is never satisfied." "I never thought I'd one day face the monarchs of the demon race head-on... How thrilling. I can hardly wait to see the Demon Lords bowing and scraping before me."

One more chapter coming, and I'll release the new bonus chapter rules.

title: Chapter 25 — Eyes Everywhere (Third Update)
content:
Chapter 25 — Eyes Everywhere (Third Update)

Volume 19 · Chapter 25

Outside the manor, Mesphield had not relaxed her vigilance at all and continued to monitor every move in Merlin's room from the outside.

She had been drowsy all night due to her surveillance, but when she saw the mysterious Belphegor standing by the window, unwilling to show his face, her spirit perked up!

Mesphield, having monitored for so long, was very clear in her mind that the people inside the room usually wouldn't wake up so early.

It was very abnormal for someone to wake up like today, which couldn't help but make her pay attention.

Especially Belphegor's behavior was abnormal, as if he was thinking about something, yet also hesitating.

Recalling Claris's instructions, Mesphield immediately felt that something might be about to happen, otherwise it would be impossible to cause this mysterious man's strange actions.

Mesphield carefully hid in the corner, revealing half her face to observe Belphegor by the window carefully.

She saw Belphegor jump down from the window, start stepping on the roof tiles, and move toward the outside of the capital.

Mesphield became even more convinced of her speculation. The fact that the other party refused to go through the door and instead came out secretly from the window clearly indicated that he was going to do something secretive.

So Mesphield didn't think twice and quietly followed Belphegor behind, ready to find out the truth.

But not long after Mesphield secretly followed Belphegor away, Merlin also came out of the window secretly--

"Belphegor this guy, has he already lost patience and wants to act on his own? No wonder he's been distracted these days...

Merlin had long noticed that Belphegor had been quiet these days. He was probably too worried about Miranda and didn't want to follow him anymore.

Fortunately, Merlin had long been cautious. Otherwise, Belphegor might have sneaked away on his own tonight, and who knows what kind of trouble would have been caused.

The three left one after another, and Merlin, who was at the back, had a feeling of the mantis catching the cicada while the oriole is waiting behind. Only the simple Alice didn't notice anything.

Merlin had two katana on his waist. He had just chased a few steps when he discovered Mesphield secretly following Belphegor-

That female knight? Why was she chasing Belphegor so persistently?

Wasn't she already aware of Belphegor's identity?

No good, she can't follow Belphegor, otherwise we'll have a lot of trouble.

After making up his mind, Merlin sped up and quickly approached the pursuing Mesphield, starting to prepare a wad of phlegm in his mouth.

"Acetylneuraminic acid helical cannon!"

With Merlin's loud shout, he revealed his position. Mesphield was very alert and swiftly drew her sword, turning around to start blocking.

Hearing Merlin utter a jumble of names, she instinctively thought it was some kind of magical attack, so it was reasonable for her to turn around and use her sword to block.

However, the situation wasn't that simple. Could a sword defend against liquid? It was like a fishing net couldn't hold water; it was simply impossible.

Merlin's saliva mixed with phlegm, and the speed and range from his mouth were much farther than usual, and it was fast, which in a way could also be considered a water cannon.

Mesphield had just turned around and hadn't even seen what kind of projectile was flying towards her when she saw this spit split into two in front of her sword.

Then, against her will, it shot into her eyes!

"Ah!" Mesphield covered her eyes and fell from the half-air, sitting down on the ground.

Merlin resisted the urge to laugh and flew past her in the half-air, not even looking at Mesphield. He somehow felt a little sympathy for the female knight.

Sigh, why is it always this poor guy every time?

I don't want to spit on women, but she always appears at the right time and in the right place, making it impossible for me to refuse.

Off I go, off I go, don't care about her...

Merlin shook his head in helplessness, didn't say anything, and directly chased after the front Belphegor, obviously considering it more important to bring this bastard back.

"Who! ? Dammit! Who ambushed me?

Mesphield quickly got up, feeling her eyes burn painfully, and for a short time, she couldn't see clearly.

She rubbed her eyes vigorously, and only after they started to redden did she feel a bit better and could see things clearly.

Mesphield wiped the sticky liquid from the corner of her eye and saw the yellowish vomit on her hand, feeling extremely nauseated.

"...What is this?"

No sooner had she spoken than Mesphield's body suddenly felt uncomfortable, her whole body turned red, rushing to her forehead, and her body became hot and restless.

...This familiar feeling, this shameful reaction...

It is... it must be! That damn great swordsman Elkin, he's also in France!

What bad luck, I met him again, why am I so unlucky, always being ambushed!

Mesphield instinctively clamped her legs together around her sword and couldn't help but let out a loud curse that echoed through the capital.

"You damn bastard! I will definitely kill you!"

Merlin, who had溜ed away, heard the roar from behind and couldn't help but stumble, almost twisting his own foot, and felt a little guilty.

Can't blame me, since you know you can't resist, better to just enjoy it.

Although it's a kind of torture, doesn't she still have her fingers?

Merlin put aside his messy thoughts and quickly caught up with Belphegor, directly pulling him down from the half-air.

Belphegor originally wanted to violently resist, but upon seeing Merlin, he silently put down his fists. "You usually sleep like a dead pig, but today you're unexpectedly alert?"

"You've been too quiet these days, which made me suspicious." Merlin grabbed Belphegor's collar and asked, "What are you going to do? Have you forgotten our agreed matter? You want to escape when I'm not paying attention and cause trouble?"

"Why do you see me as a troublemaker?" Belphegor pushed away Merlin's hand that was grabbing his clothes.

"Stay calm, you'll find Miranda, but if you cause chaos like this, you won't only fail to find Miranda, you'll also cause a lot of trouble and make it even harder to find your sister." Merlin said seriously.

"I know where Miranda is, I just saw her. A group of pale-faced guys brought her here, on the mountain top outside the city." Belphegor pointed in a direction and said seriously, "I must go save her now, no matter the cost, and use that bunch of trash's blood to quell my anger."

"You haven't left the capital at all, what do you know?" Merlin frowned, thinking Belphegor was looking for an excuse to leave and search on his own.

Belphegor tilted his mouth, and a small but strong fly flew out from inside, buzzing around Merlin's head.

"This fly is my familiar, it can breed offspring by itself, and I can't even count how many there are.

"These things are all over the capital and the vast areas around it, they're my eyes.

"Do you think I would just sit around and do nothing?"

"Do you think I would be content to be kept in the dark?"

"...The person who knows the capital best is that cunning little princess?"

"Wrong! It's me.

"I know everything about everyone in the capital, from the imperial royal family to the two or three-year-old children.

"I have the ability to have the flies kill everyone instantly, but I haven't done that, I'm just collecting information.

"Don't think you're controlling me, it's me who has kidnapped everyone's lives.

"Do you think I would be docile just because you hit me a few times? No, I'm not that weak.

"I'm monitoring you all the time, even when you went to the palace with that human woman, I clearly remember every word you said."

Congratulations, you did a good job, indeed trying to help me find Miranda, so I choose to temporarily spare their lives.

"Now I've found Miranda's location, so I don't need your help anymore, I'm going to save my sister, and if you dare to stop me, I swear I'll kill you.

"Oh, before I go, give you a little福利, do you know what color underpants that cunning little princess wore today? I can assure you you'll never guess.

"This slut didn't wear anything under her skirt today, if she were a demon, she would definitely be that kind of particularly seductive hot girl, hahaha..
