2019 additional update rules, using an immediate system.

According to the daily monthly vote ranking, adjust the daily additional update amount.

Top 20 (including 20th) monthly votes

Monday ~ Friday, basic update one more, additional updates at will

Saturday ~ Sunday, basic update one more

Top 15 (including 15th) monthly votes

Monday ~ Friday, basic update one more, additional updates

Saturday ~ Sunday, basic update one more

Top 5 (including 5th) monthly votes

Monday ~ Friday, basic update one more, additional updates

Saturday ~ Sunday, basic update one more, additional updates

The above is the new additional update system for 2019, because excluding my daily time is a more reasonable way to add updates.

Additional updates at will are not guaranteed, depending on how tight the time is, if not busy there will be additional updates, if a bit busy there will be at least one update.

Additional updates are unlimited, if I'm in a good mood I can write three updates a day, but I will definitely add one update.

On Saturday and Sunday I usually need to adjust, maybe rest, but if my monthly vote ranking is high I won't rest and will add updates.

For top 20 and top 15 monthly votes, Saturday and Sunday updates will be slower, focusing on adjusting, so only the basic one update.

For top 5 monthly votes, there's basically no rest, regardless of weekends, at least two updates, I hope everyone understands.

title: Chapter 26 — Game (Part 1)
content:
Chapter 26 — Game (Part 1)

Volume 19 · Chapter 26

Merlin furrowed his brows; usually he thought Beelzebub's mind was simple, but it turned out to be surprisingly shrewd.
Without his knowledge, he secretly did all these things, monitoring every move in the royal capital.
Merlin really underestimated Beelzebub; just from being able to clearly know the scenery under Margaret's skirt, it made one firmly believe.
"If you hadn't helped me find Miranda, what would you have done?"
"It's really a pity, everyone in this royal capital will die; if you hadn't suddenly come here, I was originally going to turn this land into ruins." Beelzebub answered expressionlessly.
"...He really likes to vent his resentment on others.... Merlin said indifferently, and didn't think Beelzebub was wrong, because he clearly knew that demons' personalities are all violent."
"So what? You won't still try to stop me now, will you?" Beelzebub paused, emphasized, "I don't want to fight you now, but you're blocking my way to Miranda; I guarantee the upcoming struggle won't be as simple as our previous fight, but a real life-or-death battle."
"You might have some misunderstanding about me? I won't stop you; my mission is to kill Dracula, the blood clan also counts as my enemy." Merlin spread his hands.
"That's really lucky; outside there's a guy called father by a group of vampires, I think that's your prey~" Beelzebub revealed a meaningful smile.
"It seems we can cooperate." Merlin proposed.
"No, demon lords never like to cooperate, and neither do I." Beelzebub curled the corner of his mouth, turned and walked away, "You little brat apparently still don't know the rules, Vivian didn't teach you well.... of牡小A 玩"
"Tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue displeased, silently followed up, couldn't help but mutter in his heart—
I really want to beat this guy up.....
After finding his sister, he started acting recklessly?
The blood clan's troops were strictly waiting on the mountain peak, while the royal capital appeared windy and calm.
This is obviously a premeditated surprise attack, aiming to catch the royal family off guard and quickly end the war.
Madoc looked down, feeling the army pressing the border, yet the empire had no reaction at all, he slightly breathed a sigh of relief.
"Father, we seem to have only been discovered by the Gluttony Demon Lord; the empire hasn't noticed us."
"That's probably the case; those two demon lords haven't formed an alliance with the empire, which is good news." Dracula narrowed his eyes, gave the order, "The demon lords will surely come to find us; we'll wait here to deal with those two, split the army into two routes—one route waiting to meet"

title: Chapter 27 — Game Theory (Part 2)
content:
Chapter 27 — Game Theory (Part 2)

Volume 19 · Chapter 27

On the mountain peak outside the royal capital, the first wave of the surprise attack troops had already driven siege catapults straight to the city's core area, paving the way for the subsequent invasion.
But the originally silent royal capital, when the blood clan's heavy-armored knights approached within a certain range, suddenly bright red lights flared on the city walls, and the piercing alarm echoed throughout the area.
".5...？” Mades widened his eyes, feeling somewhat incredulous; normally the enemy wouldn't expect us to carry out an aerial surprise attack!
Dracula silently watched the flashing alarm lights and questioned, "Mades, what's going on?"
.... Mades broke out in a cold sweat, never expecting to have been outmaneuvered by Margaret, "The enemy got lucky, they guessed our attack route; this little princess really walked into dogshit luck!"
"Luck?" Dracula did not blame Mades for being slapped in the face right away; after all, the big battle was imminent, blaming was useless, "Continue the attack, don't panic...."
The four of the Azure Blue Nether Flame flew in mid‑air, hearing the piercing alarm, their hearts involuntarily tightened with panic--
"Oh no! We've been discovered!" Laurie tensed up.
"It looks like the enemy had already set a trap, waiting for us." Vina furrowed her brows.
"We are immortal now, what's there to fear?" Yuna felt indifferent.
"Don't take chances; the enemy definitely prepared silver weapons—if we get hit in a vital spot we're dead, so descend quickly, otherwise we'll become targets!" Eden said with a very serious expression.
As his words fell, countless lights suddenly blazed in the pitch‑black city, brilliant as stars.
That was the magical cannon Margaret had prepared in advance, and the gleam of silver arrows in the night.
The twang of bowstrings sounded, a dense rain of silver arrows came down like madness! J《死
The magical cannons roared one after another, fierce tongues of flame shot straight into the sky!
The blood clan's heavy‑armored knights and the four of the Azure Blue Nether Flame were instantly submerged in the attack....
Dickte Ping stood silently behind Dracula, seeing this scene he couldn't help but break out in a cold sweat, thinking, "What kind of surprise attack is this? Are the vanguard just cannon fodder? !Please don't send me up there."
Damn Margaret! She actually made me lose face in front of my father; I will certainly not let you off lightly!
Mades gritted his teeth, thinking, "Right off the bat I hit a snag, which really pissed me off," and then he loudly told all the blood clan's knights:
"Don't worry, this firepower still can't wipe out the vanguard completely; I have served as the empire's chancellor for many years, cultivating many trusted confidants hidden in every corner of the empire, they will sabotage the empire's defenses at this crucial moment...."
In the alley, Mesfield felt his whole body burning hot, his reactions grew increasingly strange, ** kneeling on the ground.
Because Merlin's saliva had an outstanding aphrodisiac effect, she now could not fight at all, and her mind was also a bit dazed.
"........".
Mesfield kept panting, barely supporting his body with his sword, his eyes glazed and unfocused.
Elgin the Sword Master, you bastard! May you die a horrible death! I swear... -.... I will personally kill him!
Mesfield gritted his teeth, having already cursed Merlin's ancestors eighteen times over in his heart.
Waves of lust surged into Mesfield's forehead, causing her to unconsciously start fantasizing about various men, her spirit becoming perilously unstable.
Fortunately, Mesfield had experience; her willpower was not ordinary strong, continually suppressing her desires.
If this continues, after Merlin spits a few more times, Mesfield will definitely acquire immunity.
Mesfield lifted his head, seeing the red alarm light and the fierce anti‑air firepower, he couldn't help but worry—
It looks like the war has already begun? It's actually so sudden!
And just when I'm in bad shape, what can I do?
Given my current state, I'm afraid--- I can't cope with the enemy..
Mesfield's brows knit tight, suddenly a 'bang' echoed, a dark, mysterious object fell before him.
With a crackling unfold, two heavily armored knights nearly ten feet tall suddenly appeared!
Their faces were hideous and ugly, red light flickered in their eyes, sharp teeth jutted out of their mouths.
Wielding huge shields and battle axes, their heavy armor could deflect most arrows, very similar to elite orc soldiers!
"Ugh!" Mesfield felt a "thud" in his heart, seeing the two heavy‑armored knights' arms thicker than a human waist, he instantly felt immense pressure.
If it were normal times, Mesfield wouldn't be afraid at all, but now she ** is burning up, almost losing her combat ability, she can barely draw her sword.
The two heavy‑armored vampires lowered their heads, looking at Mesfield's flushed face, and emitted a series of muffled, evil laughs from their noses.
Mesfield's whole body broke out in goosebumps, he nervously shrank back, his eyes flickering continuously--
In the palace, Margaret and Blaze walked one after another on the scarlet carpet:
The two prepared to go out to fight; along the way the soldiers saluted the princess respectfully.
"Your Highness, you truly have foresight; I bet Mades is already furious and confused, huh? Hehe~" Blaze scratched his head and gave a simple smile.
"What's this? It's merely the initial mutual probing." Margaret paused, then slipped on leather gloves, "The thing we should most guard against is our own people."
"Huh? Our own people? With Mades' army at the city gates, we should trust our own people, why guard against them?" Mades frowned deeply, | not really understanding Margaret's idea.
"Should we just completely trust our own people? In a crisis, no one can be fully trusted; if we trust anyone, we should trust ourselves." Margaret said offhandedly.
"..... Blaze felt Margaret's words were too hurtful, and he cautiously rebutted, "Your Highness, you can't do this, otherwise it will be heard by other subordinates, and they will be dissatisfied."
"What's there to fear? Besides you, I have no subordinates I can fully trust; everyone is suspicious." Margaret lifted her gaze and looked at the tall, big Blaze.
"No.... Although Your Highness saying that makes me happy, . . . . Blaze felt embarrassed, wanting to speak but stopping.
"When Mades was chancellor he held great power, his faction spread across all imperial domains; even though he left the capital, it doesn't mean we lack his lackeys around us—they still exist and are deeply hidden." Margaret looked serious and continued, "For this defense I have indeed mobilized most of the legions; among them are mixed good and bad, it's very likely that Mades' people are hidden here, I estimate they will stab us in the back at a crucial moment—we must definitely guard against it."
"... Is that so? !" Blaze suddenly understood, finding it very reasonable., up
Margaret had just opened her mouth to speak when she suddenly felt killing intent from behind; a guard wielding a spear lunged like lightning, aiming at her throat.
Blaze's body surged with golden fighting spirit; he shouted angrily, drew the silver‑common weapon at his waist, and instantly cleaved the ambush attacker's head off!
To deal with the blood clan, Blaze swapped out his heavy sword and chose a new weapon.
The ambushed guard let out a mournful cry, rolled twice on the ground, and then turned to ash in the flickering flames—actually it was only a vampire?
"Your Highness! Are you alright?" Blaze hurriedly turned back to ask.
"It's fine, just gave me a start." Margaret looked at the ashes on the ground, smiled and said, "Indeed, they're everywhere— Mades' lackeys"
"Your Highness, what should we do? We have so many spies inside; this might cause serious trouble!" Blaze anxiously inquired.
"Don't worry, I've already prepared; I've handed this matter over to the Holy Church." Margaret waved her hand, letting Blaze follow her—
"I will make Mades truly feel the taste of humiliation..."
Wait a moment, there's still another chapter.

title: Chapter 28 — Gambit (Part 2)
content:
Chapter 28 — Gambit (Part 2)

Volume 19 · Chapter 28

The situation seemed to have unfolded exactly as Margaret had anticipated—rebellion had indeed broken out in the capital.

Many of the soldiers and knights guarding the city were McDess’s loyal henchmen.

At this critical moment when the blood race was launching a full-scale assault on the capital, they had chosen to betray the empire and were now attacking humans with reckless abandon. Coordinating with the blood race’s main forces outside the city, they relentlessly slaughtered archers and mages wielding magic cannons.

They were also incredibly cunning, exploiting the weakened defenses to allow even more vampires to parachute into the capital.

The once-formidable anti-air firepower was now overwhelmed by the invasion from above and the internal uprising, leaving the imperial guards physically and mentally exhausted.

The battle grew increasingly intense, and Xing’s movements were swift—he was nearly out of the capital by now.

Merlin followed closely behind Beelzebub, their crimson and white flashes catching his eye, but he had no time to spare for these distractions.

The chaotic fighting, the piercing alarms—his priority was still to eliminate Dracula. The imperial guards were fighting desperately, which only deepened Merlin’s confusion, forcing him to pause and observe.

But along the way, Merlin spotted something.

“You... you traitors!” The guards shrieked in terror, stumbling backward as if struck by lightning, their movements eerily swift.

The opposing guards acted strangely—four of them lunged forward, biting through the guards’ throats in an instant and greedily feeding.

They pounced on the terrified imperial soldiers, and Merlin suddenly understood. The situation had grown far more complicated—the empire was now under attack from both sides.

“Vampires?” Merlin frowned, his anger flaring as he stopped. “Don’t interfere! If we delay any longer, we might miss the chance to save my sister!”

“Hey! What are you doing?” Beelzebub snapped, his voice sharp. “I’ll fight you to the death!”

“How could there be so many vampires disguised as soldiers?” Merlin muttered his confusion aloud.

“I wasn’t interfering,” Beelzebub shrugged. “Most of them were summoned recently by that little princess. The day we fought, remember?”

“What’s strange about that?” Beelzebub continued, “I know every detail about the capital’s inhabitants. Soldiers like these? They’re all vampires.”

Merlin frowned, finding Beelzebub’s lack of scruples infuriating.

“Why didn’t you say anything earlier? Was the little princess purging her enemies? I don’t care about these humans’ fate!”

“Why should I?” Beelzebub retorted, crouching on the rooftop and emphasizing his stance. “Blame me if you want—I’m just being true to myself. I have no obligation to help France.”

Merlin rolled his eyes, though he had to admit Beelzebub was an interesting character. He smirked, baring his teeth.

“Speaking of blood race spies...” Beelzebub’s demon lord horns swayed above his head, clearly amused by something worth noting.

“What?” Merlin pressed.

After battling three decently strong opponents earlier, he had no patience for this.

“During the initial assault on the capital, I encountered three knights who were barely worth mentioning. The France Three Knights?”

Merlin thought for a moment, then asked, “You mean the France Three Knights?”

“Exactly,” Beelzebub chuckled darkly. “And yes, there were vampires among them.”

Merlin was stunned. “You’re saying the France Three Knights—those absolutely loyal knights—were spies?”

“That’s right,” Beelzebub smirked. “Isn’t that fascinating?”

“Wait—you’re talking about the France Three Knights? The ones who swore absolute loyalty to the empire?”

“Correct,” Beelzebub’s voice was low and amused.

“Not that brute, the one with the simple mind and strong limbs?” Merlin shook his head. “He couldn’t handle something as clever as espionage.”

“Blaise?” Beelzebub’s voice rose slightly.

“That’s the one,” Merlin confirmed. “He’s too much of a brute.”

“...” Merlin fell silent, then remembered the knight who could turn his battle energy into blades. “Wait—you ate his heart?”

Beelzebub spoke meaningfully. Vampires had powerful regenerative abilities, so if he was a blood race spy, he could have been resurrected...

Merlin finally realized. “You’re sure it was him?”

“Of course,” Beelzebub licked his lips, evaluating. “Human flesh... but that heart was *really* hard to swallow.”

Merlin felt the capital was in grave danger. “We need to hurry! That little princess is smarter than we thought—she must have prepared a contingency. You said she—”

“Let’s go kill Dracula first!” Beelzebub urged.

Merlin hesitated, still puzzled. In terms of gathering information, even he couldn’t match Beelzebub’s abilities.

“Contingency? What contingency?” Merlin asked. “The Holy Church’s sacred bell has been moved to the cathedral—it suppresses dark creatures.”

“That bitch brought the Vatican’s sacred bell here,” Beelzebub explained. “Once it rings—*dong dong dong*—the sound echoes, pure and clear, making you feel like kneeling in worship. Under the Goddess of Light’s gaze, its divine pressure suppresses and intimidates dark beings.”

The sacred bell was a holy relic of the Church. After securing the support of the Holy Knights, Margaret had brought it along.

This time, Margaret and Scott had—

Dark creatures would be instantly suppressed, unable to resist. McDess’s minions would reveal their true forms.

As the bell rang, the vampires in the capital immediately knelt, their howls of pain echoing.

Merlin and Beelzebub suddenly felt a sharp discomfort, a throbbing pain in their heads. Since demon lords were affected, lesser dark creatures would likely suffer even more.

Far away, the vampires scattered, gathering near the knights.

At the front of the cathedral, the Holy Knights remained unshaken, their gazes firm despite the chaos.

Even in the midst of war, they were the most resolute fighting force in the capital.

The knights from the Church raised their voices in unison:

“The sacred bell has rung! Driving out darkness is our lifelong mission!”

“As warriors of the Goddess, we will exterminate all evil creatures!”

“Let us take up our weapons and slaughter that demoness!”

Joan of Arc raised her fake holy relic, declaring her willingness to die for the Church. The knights followed, raising their weapons and shouting in thunderous unison:

“Forward! Our formation is like a pure white blade, born to destroy dark creatures!”

The Holy Knights marched out, their disciplined ranks cutting through the blood race’s minions, quickly restoring order. These were all tasks Margaret had arranged in advance.

Their mission was to clear the capital of the blood race’s infiltrators.

Joan watched the golden sacred bell, its carvings depicting the Goddess of Light sending holy spirits to slay demons.

After the main force departed, Joan remained to guard the bell. As long as it kept ringing, the blood race entering the capital would be suppressed, ensuring the empire’s victory.

Her task was simple: protect the bell.

A man in tattered clothes lay on the road, barely breathing.

“Thump!” Joan rushed forward and lifted him up. “Are you alright? It’s extremely dangerous out here—don’t move!”

Joan froze in shock as the man’s fingernails pierced her abdomen. It was an ambush! The “civilian” disguise was just a trick.

The pain was excruciating. She looked down—blood, thick and sticky, was pouring from her wound.

Joan stared blankly, her face pale.

The man peeled off his ragged clothes, revealing his true form—a vampire. He licked the blood from his lips, savoring it, and sneered.

Vina stretched out her long tongue, wiping Joan’s blood from her face, then smirked.

“Hello, Inquisitor.”

title: Chapter 29 — No Way Out (One More Chapter Coming)
content:
Chapter 29 — No Way Out (One More Chapter Coming)

Volume 19 · Chapter 29

On the mountaintop, Medes observed the battle in the royal capital, seeing the fierce anti-air firepower dwindle, the Imperial Legion showing signs of decline.
“Hahaha! Even if I betrayed the kingdom, many still follow me; at this moment it has become the key point for us to breach the defenses
Dracula, riding on the horse, nodded satisfactorily; the situation is still very advantageous, we can take the royal capital without great cost.” “Very good, Medes, you are indeed my most trusted vassal; it seems I have done many things during my slumber. Once we breach the royal capital, I will surely reward you well.”
“Thank you, father, I actually don’t need any reward; everything is for the prosperity of the blood clan!” Medes knelt on one knee, openly expressing his loyalty.
Dickteping, standing behind, had a changing complexion; he had already seen the trend of the Imperial defeat, which was not good news for him.
If the blood clan wins, Dickteping will likely find it hard to escape, to break free from Dracula’s control; only if the Imperial side wins could he possibly gain freedom.
The current situation is very disadvantageous for Dickteping, making him restless, his hand gripping the revolver at his back, itching to act--
Damn it! Is the blood clan going to win?
This is truly a terrible situation!
Should we act now, first take down Dracula and then turn the tide?
Dickteping’s gaze was strange; after thinking, he put his hand back down from the revolver, feeling that now is not the best moment.
If he were to kill Dracula, he himself would have no good ending either, unable to escape the vampires’ encirclement.
Dickteping let out a breath, deciding to wait patiently; see if there might be an excellent opportunity for him to retreat unscathed.
The melodious holy bell rang out, coming from the Oberlin Cathedral in the royal capital, echoing over the heads of the vampire legion.
Many vampires hearing this holy bell showed extreme discomfort—some vomited, some had headaches, and some even lay on the ground unwilling to get up.....
“What the hell! What is this sound?” Medes’ face turned grim as he held his throbbing forehead.
Dracula narrowed his eyes; the holy bell’s effect on his image wasn’t too great. “Holy bell? The Holy Church has already joined the fight; it seems your trusted aides can’t stir up any big waves.”
“.” How... how is this possible....
Medes broke out in a cold sweat on his forehead, feeling utterly undignified in front of Dracula—this was the second time he’d been slapped in the face.
He had originally planned to take the royal capital with minimal losses, to show his ability before his father, but ended up being repeatedly outwitted by that little girl Margaret.
Medes knew very well the capabilities of the Oberlin Cathedral in the royal capital; it was obvious that Margaret had sought the Holy Church’s aid during this period.
“Medes, compared to that Imperial heir, you are still somewhat lacking,” Dracula said, his tone unfriendly, clearly admonishing him.
“No... very sorry, father,” Medes lowered his head, feeling extremely unwilling; the detestable Margaret, who usually acts crazy, where does she have the demeanor of an Imperial heir? I never expected that when she gets serious she’d be this hard to deal with! It seems I underestimated this bitch; her past madness was all an act.
“Trying to breach the royal capital with minimal losses is probably impossible; pass the order, full army advance, spare no expense to take the royal capital!” Dracula commanded.
“Father, what if those two Demon Lords come? Do we not need to leave any backup?” Medes asked in surprise.
“As long as that female demon remains under our control, the Demon Lords are nothing to fear; moreover, my strength is not inferior to theirs, and I might even have a slight advantage.” Dracula replied calmly.
“..... Medes wanted to speak but stopped, feeling it wasn’t thorough enough.”
“No need, but if we really fight, that level of battle you can’t help with.” Dracula waved his hand.
Dickteping’s heart stirred; if the vampires all go to attack the city, wouldn’t it be easier for me to escape? Hehe, great, it seems the opportunity is coming soon.
“Alright, then I’ll stay with Dickteping.” Medes nodded, yet noticed Dickteping was absent‑minded, “Dickteping, what are you thinking? !”
“Ah? Oh!” Dickteping quickly dropped to one knee, putting on a fawning smile and said, “I will surely do my utmost, willing to lay down my life to protect you, sir!”
On the other side of the summit, countless vampires wearing light armor and with membrane wings on their backs clung to the cliff face.
Dense black figures, from afar looking like an ant colony preparing to march out at any moment.
With the sound of a horn, the vampires shook their membrane wings and soared into the sky!
They howled, like a swarm of locusts

title: Chapter 30 — Kladi's Power (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 30 — Kladi's Power (Bonus)

Volume 19 · Chapter 30

Mesfield's eyes were filled with terror as she kept backing away. The effects of Merlin's saliva continued to exert their aphrodisiac influence, making it hard for her to lift her sword and resist the two heavy-armor vampires.

Thankfully, as the sound of the holy bells rang out, the two vampire knights were significantly affected, both clutching their heads and showing painful expressions.

Although the holy bells were very effective at suppressing dark creatures, the two heavy-armor knights were incredibly strong, far stronger than ordinary vampires...

So they were only affected, not suppressed, and could still barely maintain their actions.

.-.Where did that bell sound come from? A church?

I didn't expect it would be so effective against the blood race. Maybe I can try to escape!

Mesfield desperately suppressed her desires, stood up and staggered to try to escape, otherwise with her current state she would absolutely be unable to resist the two evil vampires.

However, a tingling sensation spread through Mesfield's body, making her movements sluggish and hard to move quickly. Every step she took brought intense stimulation.

The two heavy-armor knights were also very shrewd; seeing Mesfield try to run from the corner of their eyes, they grabbed her ankle and lifted her up.

"Ah! ... Put me down!" Mesfield panicked, constantly holding down her skirt, her feet kicking at the heavy-armor vampire's face.

However, at this moment Mesfield's strength was greatly diminished by the aphrodisiac effect. This powerless resistance was obviously useless, like scratching an itch against the strong vampires.

The two heavy-armor vampires gradually endured the pain from the holy bells' sound, looking at the embarrassed and furious Mesfield in their hands, they grinned with mocking laughter.

"Damn it! Die! Die!" Mesfield was furious, kicking harder and harder until her heel stabbed into the heavy-armor vampire's eye.

"Uaaaaah!" The heavy-armor vampire let out a pained cry, angry, shook Mesfield in his hand a few times, and threw her hard!

Mesfield was like a cannonball, crashing through several walls with thuds before stopping.

She dragged her aching body up slowly, a sweetness in her throat as she spat out large mouthfuls of blood.

The heavy-armor vampire knight covered his eyes, and after a moment the damage healed as if new, he could roll around completely unaffected by any substantive harm.

Their powerful healing ability made vampires an undead army. Such terrifying combat power, how could ordinary human armies compare?

The two heavy-armor vampires were clearly enraged by Mesfield, lifting their huge axes and walking over, as if they wanted to tear her alive!

After taking a heavy hit, Mesfield seemed to have sobered up somewhat from the aphrodisiac effect, but the weakness throughout her body still couldn't support her...

Could she... die like this?

So unwilling to die!

In the end, she was killed by that bastard Elgin the Great Swordsman!

Mesfield still thought of the man who had insulted her many times at this moment. Not only had she failed to settle old scores, but she was going to be killed by him instead.

The two heavy-armor vampire knights came before the gasping Mesfield, raising their huge axes to chop this human knight into minced meat!

Mesfield sighed deeply, closed her eyes silently, and gave up resisting.

At this critical moment, a stone was thrown at the middle vampire's helmet, making a crisp "dong" sound.

Mesfield looked up in astonishment, seeing Clardi had arrived somehow, standing alone behind the two heavy-armor vampires.

"Clardi-sensei!?"

"Windsor, what are you doing? Why were you beaten so miserably by two mere fish?!" Clardi frowned, unable to understand how the First Knight Mesfield could be handled by enemies of this level.

"...Mesfield lowered her head in shame and anger, really didn't want to say it. She couldn't say she was currently ** and couldn't fight at full power, could she?

"Don't be afraid! I'll deal with these two minions, let them see the might of the Thorn Knights!" Clardi waved his wand, standing in a battle pose with it across his chest.

"But teacher you...-"

"Come on then! You bunch of evil creatures, bullying a little girl, what kind of skill is that! If you've got guts, come at me! Soldiers like you, I can annihilate you in an instant!"

Before Mesfield could finish speaking, Clardi on the opposite side began loudly taunting, as if deliberately provoking the enemies to transfer their hatred onto himself =

The two heavy-armor vampires were indeed enraged, baring their teeth and roaring at Clardi, swinging their axes and running over!

They coordinated with each other to form a pincer attack. Their massive bodies stamped the ground each time, causing vibrations, their offensive unstoppable!

"...Clardi's expression was serious, his eyes firm yet bloodshot, but his breathing became rapid?

Although he was the twelfth Thorn Knight, showing such nervousness in the face of two blood race vanguard soldiers was indeed amazing!

Mesfield widened her eyes, not daring to blink, as if worried... afraid Clardi would have a problem.

Boom boom boom, the huge vampires stamped the ground, suddenly swinging their giant axes to slash at the short Clardi.

Clardi's cold sweat poured down, brilliant white light began emanating from his wand, and he shouted loudly-

"Iieeee! Come on you minions!"

Only then did Clardi bend down, extending his hand to touch the bodies of the two heavy-armor vampires, a series of extremely dangerous movements!

Unfortunately, Clardi was short in stature, completely unable to reach the enemy's body.

Although Clardi successfully avoided the two deadly axes, he was still kicked flying by the heavy-armor vampires' thick thighs?!

This scene was just like an adult bullying a kindergarten kid, completely without suspense!

"Teacher!!!" Mesfield shouted worriedly, watching Clardi fall to the ground like a kite with a cut string.

The twelfth Thorn Knight, Clardi whom many respected as teacher, was actually so weak in the face of two blood race vanguard soldiers?

If others saw this bizarre scene, they would surely find it unbelievable, suspecting Clardi's Thorn Knight position was gotten through back doors or bought?

"...Clardi felt all his bones were scattered, half-kneeling and coughing nonstop. He slowly raised his head and wiped the blood from his mouth, "...I really am not good at fighting..."

"What to do... Mesfield muttered nervously to herself, seeing Clardi injured she felt even more self-reproach, but the aphrodisiac effect made her unable to struggle...

Clardi-sensei saved me, not hesitating to use himself as bait to lure the enemies away...

Why would he do such a dangerous thing?

He's just a support class!

title: Chapter 31 — Supporting Double Kill
content:
Chapter 31 — Supporting Double Kill

Volume 19 · Chapter 31

Melsfield saw Caddy in crisis, her heart filled with anxiety, wanting to help Caddy.

Unfortunately, the duration of Merlin's saliva effect was quite long, and Melsfield could barely grip her sword firmly until now, while the fighting energy in her body remained in chaotic disarray—

What should she do? Although Teacher Caddy was extremely powerful in support, his own combat ability was very low, unable to even defeat a strong ordinary person.

Wanting to defeat two tall, heavily armored vampires? For Teacher Caddy, it was clearly hell-level difficulty.

Going on like this, Teacher Caddy would probably be killed.....

Melsfield was sweating nervously, looking at Caddy who was kneeling on one knee, seemingly injured quite badly.

"Teacher Caddy!"

".....Tea...." Caddy gritted his teeth, enduring the severe pain throughout his body, finding it difficult to even stand up.

Melsfield's expression grew grave, thinking — are you really okay? You're already bleeding.....

The heavy-armored vampire saw that Caddy was still conscious, so he sneered and kicked him again, sending the short-statured man flying once more.

"Cough!" Caddy spewed blood — this time his internal organs were probably shattered from the impact, his entire body crashing heavily against the wall.

"Teacher Caddy! ! !" Melsfield saw the situation becoming increasingly desperate, she had no choice but to stand up, wanting to use the last bit of strength to resist, but even slight movements brought unbearable stimulating sensations, making her whole body feel feverish.

The two heavy-armored vampires approached Caddy, who looked like a dead fish, their mocking laughter seemingly belittling this man for being overconfident.

But who would have known that the apparently lifeless Caddy reached out with trembling hands and touched the big feet of the two heavy-armored vampires.

The strong vampire showed a puzzled expression, not understanding what Caddy meant, and they looked at each other.

Caddy raised his blood-covered face and said with a miserable smile, "I finally got my hands on you? You will pay for what you just did! Equipment weight increased by 1000%! ! !"

"Eh! ?" Melsfield widened her eyes, watching Caddy's hands emitting brilliant white light, releasing a strengthening magic spell toward the two heavy-armored vampires!

With Caddy's roar, the two strong heavy-armored vampires fell into the ground, making a loud "bang!" sound!

Their expressions were terrified, their huge bodies becoming incredibly heavy, forcing them to constantly sink, the solid earth cracking open with shocking fissures that continued to spread around.

The heavy-armored vampires wailed as if they were about to be crushed by the enormous weight — even with their strong physiques, they couldn't bear the equipment with increased tenfold weight.

Caddy was a support master, although he knew many powerful support magic spells that could make teammates several times stronger, he couldn't fight at all, not knowing a single attacking magic.

Although Caddy didn't understand what happened to Melsfield, in order to save her, this knight had no choice but to take a desperate risk — unexpectedly producing miraculous results at the critical moment!

The equipment weight increase makes the equipment on the target's body incredibly heavy, usually released against the target's weapons, enhancing the weapon's destructive power!

But this time Caddy used it against the heavy armor on the two vampires, amplifying the pressure by exactly 10 times — immediately exceeding their bearing capacity, pinning them to the ground under the heavy armor, unable to move!

"You two lowly dark creatures — were you mocking my short stature? I indeed can't reach your heads even when jumping, but as long as I smash your knees, you'll just have to lie on the ground obediently, right?" Caddy stood up unsteadily, drew the silver dagger at his waist, and coldly looked down at the two terrified vampires, "Disappear! Filthy creatures!"

Caddy used stiff movements to slash the throats of the two heavy-armored vampires — flames instantly consumed them, turning them to ashes, leaving only empty armor behind.

Melsfield let out a long breath, her worried heart finally at ease. Although two heavy-armored vampires weren't much, it was truly incredible that Teacher Caddy, as a support class, could defeat them.

Caddy panted heavily, trembling as he approached Melsfield, asking with concern, "Windsor, what's wrong with you? Why were you suppressed by two grunt enemies to this extent?"

"...I had some issues—" Melsfield's face flushed red — she was completely too embarrassed to say it.

"Hmm?" Caddy covered his chest that was still having periodic effects, asking patiently, "What happened? Didn't I ask you to keep an eye on that mysterious man?"

"That man suddenly left the mansion alone in a sneaky manner, and then I don't know where he went. I was following closely behind, but on the way I encountered...." Melsfield's voice stopped suddenly, not wanting to admit she was insulted by being spit on, and her body was abnormally sensitive, so she spoke in a very implicit way, "But on the way I was ambushed, causing my mental state to become very unstable."

"He left sneakily? It seems this mysterious guy isn't simple, having some secret he doesn't want others to discover...." Caddy muttered to himself, increasingly suspecting the mysterious man beside Merlin. After thinking for a moment, he changed the subject, "The situation is urgent — we'll talk about this later. Right now we need to help Princess Margaret repel the incoming vampires!"

"Ah, but...."

Caddy was feeling quite anxious, not finishing listening to Melsfield's words, he wanted to reach out his hand to help her up.

But the moment he touched Melsfield, she made a sound like a comfortable moan—

"Ahh~="

Melsfield's body was very sensitive now — when touched by a male, she instinctively made this suggestive sound, a bodily instinct under the aphrodisiac effect, almost impossible to resist.

Hearing this strange cry, Caddy was obviously startled, no longer daring to touch Melsfield, his eyes as if seeing a ghost, "Windsor, ...what kind of reaction is this?"

"...."

Melsfield covered her mouth, her face crimson, as if a red-hot branding iron, glowing and radiating heat—

Oh no! Oh no!

Why did I make such a shameful sound! ?

And in front of a respected teacher....

Good heavens! I can't face living anymore — just let me die!

Teacher Caddy must think I'm a very improper person!

Melsfield couldn't bear to raise her head, her body becoming increasingly拘谨, wishing she could find a crack in the ground to crawl into!

Usually Melsfield's image was heroic and imposing, but today she became somewhat girl-like, which puzzled Caddy greatly.

After a brief moment of thought, Caddy suddenly showed an expression of realization, looking at Melsfield and saying in a very serious tone,

"Windsor, ...."

"Actually, you just want to be convenient, right?"

(-_-)

title: Chapter 32 — The Fall of the Sacred Bell (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 32 — The Fall of the Sacred Bell (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 19 · Chapter 32

Meesfeld suddenly raised his head, seeing that Krad's expression wasn't some joke — she genuinely thought he was holding in his urine!

Happiness came a bit too suddenly. Though Meesfeld felt incredibly embarrassed, he still nodded like a chicken pecking at rice.

.....Yes, I need to use the facilities...

"I see. I wondered why you'd be making such strange sounds," Krad nodded, turned around and walked away. "Hurry up a little. We have a lot to do next. There are no absolutely safe places within the royal city. Vampire sympathizers are everywhere. Stay alert."

.....Meesfeld awkwardly responded, thinking that Elk the Great Sword Master was such a jerk! How could he make me lose face like this!? If I get the chance, I'll never let him off!

Krad stepped aside and waited for Meesfeld to take care of his personal needs. But dense, continuous howls came down from above.

His heart pounded with alarm as he quickly looked up at the sky crisscrossed with cannon fire......

A swarm of grotesque vampires descended from the heavens. Their numbers were so vast they couldn't be counted by sight alone!

They brandished their claws and fangs, flapping the membrane wings on their backs, like a swarm of hungry locusts leaving not a blade of grass standing in their path!

Anti-aircraft fire obviously had become insignificant against so many vampires!

Krad gazed at the apocalyptic scene, cold sweat dripping down his forehead as he sighed:

"It's just like... someone said before..."

" Satan in Hell blows the horn of attack."

The Holy Knights' participation in the battle somewhat salvaged the Empire's deteriorating situation.

Those weaker vampires couldn't move under the sacred bell's toll, and were quickly counter-killed.

The resolute Holy Knights almost wiped out the large contingent of vampire traitors within the royal city, restoring its defenses.

However, the Saint-Denis Cathedral — the Holy Knights' headquarters — faced an unprecedented crisis.

Joan, who was responsible for guarding the Sacred Bell, fell victim to an ambush by Vina, a cadre of the Pale Blue Flames, and was grievously wounded on the spot.

"Hello there, Inquisitor-sama~" Vina flashed a mocking smile. Her slender, fair arm sliced through like a razor, piercing straight through Joan's abdomen.

.....Joan felt her body falling into waves of numbness. Looking down, she saw her slightly viscous blood flowing down her enemy's arm.

"You really are foolish. In a moment like this when vampire forces are at the city gates, who would dare wander the streets?" Vina smiled broadly and taunted in a low voice. "So~ pur~e~."

"You shameless wretch!" Joan glared fiercely, steeled her spirit, and unleashed the Saint-tier fighting energy within her body. She wielded her pseudartifact spear, its deadly tip aimed straight at Vina's throat!

"So fierce~" Vina's figure was lithe. She pulled her arm from Joan's abdomen, dodged the vicious spear thrust like a cat, and kept retreating to maintain a safe distance.

Vina and Yuna were very skilled at assassination. Swift movements and unexpected attacks were their specialties.

Facing an opponent like Joan, who was almost ferocious in battle, the two sisters entangling her would clearly be irrational.

Still, Vina's younger sister Yuna was nowhere to be found. The two sisters rarely parted ways.

"I will....."

As Joan was about to launch a fierce counterattack, her abdominal wound tore open once more. Blood gushed forth. She only felt a wave of dizziness, and without control, fell to her knees.

"I'd advise you not to move around carelessly. Such wounds will worsen with your struggles. We excel at crippling our enemies. Those we wound suffer tears that continue to ripen until they become fatal. If you want to live, it would be best to find someone to heal you now~" Vina extended her long tongue, her crimson eyes gleaming with greed as she constantly licked the blood on her arm.

"You sing quite deliciously. It would be a pity to simply kill you off."

"Against evil, I will not retreat!" Joan tore the cloak behind her, using scraps of cloth to roughly bandage the bleeding wound on her abdomen. Being ambushed had put her at a disadvantage. If she delayed until her injuries worsened, she'd stand no chance!

"It's useless. Before long, your abdominal wound will deteriorate, and you'll lose your life because of it~" Vina seemed to offer well-meaning advice, but she actually wanted Joan to flee — she had no information that would allow her to win a direct fight against this heretic Inquisitor.

"To die defending justice is my honor!" After roughly treating her wound, Joan tapped into her fighting energy again. A golden phantom coiled around her entire body, gradually merging with the scarlet spear in her hands!

Joan's power was no different from usual. Although she wielded the razor-sharp pseudartifact Scarlet Bride, she hadn't used the ability to sacrifice two teammates, and her cultivation hadn't yet reached the Grandmaster realm.

Even so, Joan wielding a pseudartifact against a despicable assassin was clearly more than enough!

Joan stomped the ground violently. The pseudartifact's terrifying power generated a mighty gust of wind with a single swing, putting considerable pressure on Vina.

Vina frowned and was forced to keep retreating. Numerous small wounds suddenly appeared on her body, surprising her deeply——

Such a formidable weapon! It actually enhances the user's strength by several tiers!?

This utterly real intimidating power. If it pierced her, it would surely be tragic!

While Vina was pondering a strategy, Joan's speed surged. In the blink of an eye, she appeared right before her.

"Damn it! So fast!"

With the pseudartifact's加持, Joan could rival top-tier Saint-level experts. Even with Vina having the advantage of initiative, she still couldn't win!

Joan flicked her spear sideways in a flash, generating surging golden afterimages that cascaded down like a waterfall!

Caught off guard, Vina could only raise her arms to block, and they were immediately shattered by the scarlet spear!

Joan danced with her spear skillfully. With the pseudartifact in hand, her momentum was truly extraordinary.

"Evil abomination! Die!"

"Ughhh...."

Vina's hair was disheveled. She glared at Joan with malicious eyes, her broken arms dangling limply, looking thoroughly wretched.

She suddenly let out a bizarre laugh. She shook her hands, and the severed arms regenerated instantly. The Vampire Race's power was remarkably convenient.

"Hahaha. Did you really think I'd fight you here so simply? I've prepared a surprise for you~"

"What do you mean?" Joan's expression grew grim.

"Look~ over there~" Vina tilted her chin, gesturing toward behind Joan.

The Sacred Bell's toll became disordered. Joan turned her head anxiously and her eyes widened in sheer horror, her face turning deathly pale.

The Sacred Bell that suppressed all dark creatures within the royal city had been cut down and thrown from the tall bell tower!

Without the Sacred Bell's suppression, the vampires would be unrestrained, and the Empire's chances of victory were becoming increasingly slim.

Her sister Yuna's figure descended from the bell tower, dusting off her hands with a provocative smile——

"I really went through quite a bit of trouble for this~"

"This damn bell was making my head about to explode."

"Inquisitor-sama. Now it's time to deal with you...."

title: Chapter 33 — The Senior Arrives
content:
Chapter 33 — The Senior Arrives

Volume 19 · Chapter 33

Joan stood in a daze, gazing down at the Holy Bell that had fallen to the ground, her spirits utterly crushed.

Her duty was to protect the Holy Bell and continuously pressure the dark creatures.

But that very mission had been ruined by the twin sisters, turning what had been a steadily favorable situation into instant collapse.

The vampires within the main city, now restored to normal, began to roar in fury, echoing the large forces in the sky above as they launched their furious counterattack.

The Imperial Legion started to retreat steadily, forced to shrink their defensive perimeter, clustering together to resist the blood swarm pressing in like locusts.

But facing vampires so numerous and so difficult to kill, even with silver weapons equipped, they were already like arrows spent from a broken bow.

Joan was consumed by deep self-reproach. Without the Holy Bell, the empire had lost its shield, and danger would only intensify!

"We will not let you go!"

Fire roared in Joan's eyes, and she wished with all her might to bite the despicable twin sisters alive. The Crimson Damsel in her hand trembled violently.

"You should blame yourself for being too foolish, focusing all your attention on me," Vina sneered, covering her mouth with a hand as she laughed.

"Once this Holy Bell is destroyed, the vampire armies will be unstoppable, and the empire's defeat will be certain." Yuna slowly joined her sister at her side.

"Shut up! As a warrior of the Goddess, I will not let you run rampant!" Joan stamped the ground and swung her spear, its strike utterly incomparable!

Vina and Yuna sneered, their figures flickering like ghosts as they scattered in different directions. Their nimble movements and swift speeds gave them the upper hand against the straightforward Joan.

To top it all, Joan's abdominal wound continued to worsen, her attacks clearly becoming sluggish. Her fierce spear techniques came in rapid succession, yet she could not catch the twin sisters.

"Hahaha, Lord Inquisitor, do you hate us terribly? But as long as we sisters fight together, what does it matter if you're strong?" Vina let out mocking laughter.

"Sister, let's just finish her off quickly and keep looking for our next prey!" Yuna stirred restlessly, her eyes brimming with killing intent.

The twin sisters counterattacked, their razor-sharp nails proving no less deadly than edged blades. Every vicious strike came from a treacherous angle, and the slightest mistake would cost their lives.

Sweat dripped from Joan's forehead. She sensed that handling one sister was not difficult, but together they became incredibly thorny, far surpassing ordinary Saint-tier experts!

Facing the twin sisters' bullet-like claw strikes, Joan was forced to shift from offense to defense, constantly retreating while searching for an opening. The pseudo-divine artifact in her hands seemed to come alive, repeatedly deflecting lethal blows.

"Do you think just blocking continuously will keep you safe? How naive!" Vina's smile turned grotesque, golden light and shadows swirling around her sharp nails.

"Sister, let this tomboy taste our power!" Yuna shouted, her figure mirroring Vina's from a distance, their assault growing ever sharper!

The twin sisters' figures resembled swallows returning to their nest, enveloping the disadvantaged Joan, then swinging their razor claws to strangle her in an instant!

"Ughhhhhhh!"

Joan let out a piercing scream, her body spinning like a kite with a cut string in midair before crashing heavily to the ground.

In that single moment, Joan had taken countless strikes from the sisters, her body covered in wounds, dark crimson blood flowing slowly.

"Hmph, truly thick-skinned and tough..." Vina looked down at the motionless Joan.

"She took a severe abdominal wound yet still holds herself up. How silly~" Yuna licked her nails.

"Stop bothering with her. Let's go find our next prey."

Vina turned and walked away. Yuna glanced down at the lifeless Joan, snorted coldly, and followed her sister.

The two grew farther and farther away, yet the blood-soaked Joan, lying prone on the ground, rose again. Golden battle aura surged continuously, her unyielding will still burning fiercely!

Joan's expression was completely unreadable now. All that could be seen was the spreading blood, which beneath the aura's influence seemed to bubble as if boiling!

Joan's eyes held the defiance of an unyielding warrior, with not even the smallest trace of retreat—

She vibrated her crimson spear, pouring her battle aura into the pseudo-divine artifact, which immediately blazed with crimson radiance!

Joan cultivated traditional Temple Knight lance techniques, renowned for their ferocity and brute strength, and now those qualities shone through her perfectly!

With a thunderous horizontal thrust from Joan, a fierce red beam erupted forth, like a crimson tiger descending the mountain, unstoppable in its path.

Wherever the red beast passed, the earth cracked entirely, and every obstacle in its way was flattened, an unstoppable killing move in full display!

Vina and Yuna's faces went pale with terror. The red beast came with overwhelming momentum, its power leaving both sisters speechless; they feared they could neither resist nor evade it!

Joan's strength was still no small matter. If she had fought at full capacity, the twin sisters恐怕 would not have stood a chance!

Vina and Yuna's eyes widened, their faces drained of color, watching as the red beast was about to tear them apart—but suddenly, an unexpected change occurred!

This raging killing strike weakened before their eyes, dissipating silently!

"...What happened?" Yuna asked, still trembling with lingering fear.

"...Chu..." Vina was so scared she seemed to have lost her soul, staring blankly into space.

Joan stood like a commander on the battlefield, still bowing her head, maintaining her horizontal thrust posture, her spirit completely dead.

The next moment, Joan's previously roughly treated abdominal wound erupted with a massive gush of blood, the critical injury deteriorating into a fatal wound!

Joan's eyes grew hollow, gradually losing their luster as she entered a precarious, near-death state, and she collapsed to the ground.

Never expecting that at this most critical moment, the initial abdominal wound would become Joan's weakness, allowing Vina and Yuna to barely escape with their lives.

"If we hadn't secretly struck and critically wounded her at the start, we'd both be dead for sure," Vina swallowed hard, still shaken.

"If she had been at full health, we really would have had no winning chance..." Yuna nodded, her expression extremely grim.

"She doesn't seem fully dead yet. Still clinging to one breath... Truly a tough one." Vina frowned.

"Let me go finish her off! Leaving her alive is a danger!" Yuna revealed her sharp nails and slowly walked toward the unconscious Joan.

Whoosh! Three chilling golden ice swords shot through the air with piercing sound, their target directly aimed at Yuna approaching Joan!

Yuna's heart raced as she dodged the attack, and the three golden ice swords clattered into the ground, preventing anyone from approaching the unconscious Joan.

"Who?!"

The twin sisters looked up simultaneously, gazing toward an unknown direction, sensing that a far more powerful opponent was arriving!

Alice plummeted from the sky like a meteor. The piercing cold wind made it hard for Vina and Yuna to keep their eyes open, and the frigid temperature made them feel as though they had wandered into icy Greenland.

"I am her senior, come here to test your skills!"

title: Chapter 34 — Sword Slash All Around (Extra)
content:
Chapter 34 — Sword Slash All Around (Extra)

Volume 19 · Chapter 34

Originally Alice was sleeping very deeply, but the chaotic artillery fire outside still woke her from her sleep.
She looked around but didn't see Merlin and Beelzebub, and her heart suddenly jumped—she didn't know what those two were secretly doing with their grandmother?
So Alice hurriedly left the mansion, and after killing many vampires along the way she realized that the vampire army had assaulted the royal capital, the whole city was in peril, and the streets were in a state of melee.
As for Merlin and Beelzebub? Alice guessed they had gone straight to look for Madès, after all this minister was very important, concerning Miranda's whereabouts and the clues to the Austin family curse.
Alice wanted to leave the royal capital to find Merlin and the others, but on the way passing through O'Brien Cathedral, she saw Joan of Arc in dire straits and had to come to her rescue.
In Alice's eyes, Joan of Arc also counted as a friend; she couldn't just stand by and watch her die. Back when she was a hero candidate, Joan had been her rear support, pure like a little child.
Alice's eyes turned icy; she drew her slender sword from her waist, gave a sudden shake, and a chilling aura burst forth, accompanied by dragon pressure and a faint roar.
As the wind and snow swept over, Alice entered a half-dragon state, her body covered in hard sapphire-like dragon scales, and when her dragon wings unfurled they instantly froze the ground—

I am her senior; come and learn your betters, you two!
QCZ Xiao Pa
'What the heck, someone actually using dragon power? How rare....' Yuna's forehead beaded with cold sweat, under that terrifying dragon pressure she felt immense pressure.
'Senior of the Inquisition? Aren't you just a mithril adventurer?' Vina showed a doubtful expression, unable to guess Alice's identity.
If Laurie were here now, seeing Alice would surely make her jump, give her second thoughts, and she wouldn't choose to fight.
After all Laurie has seen Alice and Merlin, and has always thought Alice was an invincible powerhouse, capable of killing Osweid and even suppressing the chairman with her little lackeys.
But Vina and Yuna, the two sisters, have never seen Alice, so they can't associate this half-dragon, half-human person before them with that invincible powerhouse; they don't know if they're of the same ilk!
'Come on!' Alice, with a flourish, pointed her slender sword at the two, speaking sternly, 'Bullying my juniors—what skill is that? You can attack all you want; I want to see what you're capable of!'
'Um...
Vina's smile froze on her face—although Alice's pressure was strong, not much less than Joan's.
But Alice's arrogant attitude completely enraged Vina, making her think the other was utterly full of herself.
Even though one-on-one she couldn't be a match, Vina felt that teaming up with her sister would make even a Saint-tier peak have to yield three paces!
'What an arrogant adventurer~—just a mithril rank, huh? The mithril adventurers I've killed with my own hands, counting them, are more than ten fingers; what are you?
'Yeah, that disgusting arrogance really pisses me off~' Yuna said with intense hostility, provoking, 'Having dragon power is rare, but when it comes to life-and-death combat, my sister and I have never feared anyone. Someone like you, when we sisters join forces, will probably not last three rounds before dying on the spot!
'This silver-haired miss clearly doesn't understand the situation, thinking she can beat us—little does she know.... Vina raised her chin, her face grim, speaking contemptuously, 'Your attitude of looking down on others has already landed on our kill list; we'll slash open your belly with our claws and drag out your entrails to feed the wild dogs!
'Hehe.... Yuna's expression turned frenzied, like a madwoman muttering, 'Sis, don't say anymore—I'm getting so excited I might die! Do it! Now! Kill this bitch!'
Alice remained expressionless, her icy eyes revealing no emotion, calmly replying, 'Sounds fun, then let's go.'
Vina's expression went blank; Alice's indifferent attitude disgusted her, making her lose her composure, 'I want to see what your arrogance is based on—just a cock-eyed adventurer from Rexham, don't get too full of yourself!'
'Kill her! Kill her! Kill her....' Yuna's face twisted with murderous intent, killing intent washing over them.
The two sisters' forms crossed, releasing a tremendous oppressive force, striking with the exact same motion they'd just used to take down Joan, another hard-to-defend joint strangling maneuver!
Alice pressed her legs together, one hand behind her back, the other holding her slender sword upright before her, her golden eyes narrowing to slits—
'Judging by your looks, you must be speed-specialized assassins, right? But I get to witness the pinnacle of speed every day—drawing and sheathing the blade, that man interprets killing technique with such simple moves; what you pride yourselves on is worth nothing before him, and I certainly won't take it seriously either. Let's see whose speed is faster—yours or my sword?'
'Big talk! Die, bitch!!!'
Vina and Yuna instantly turned into two red lightning bolts, displaying the perfect curve of a swallow's return, surrounding the unmoving Alice in the center!
The biting wind was severed by their incredible speed; the two red lightning bolts, like obviously crazy meteors, easily sliced the ground....
—Time fragments scattered, the wind and snow froze, killing intent lurked between motion and stillness, almost impossible to defend against this—
Alice's face sank, her silver hair dancing, caught between the two red lightning bolts, she withstood the piercing howl of the wind.
Die, die, die! Slash the throat! L—fatal strike! Broad Mare" play
Vina and Yuna suddenly attacked from an extremely tricky angle; their sharp nails seemed to lock Alice's throat, as if a light slide could sever her head.
Alice's eyes changed; she swung her slender sword, bringing up golden ice shards, her silver hair flowing like a waterfall, her posture as if dancing in the wind and snow—she slashed her sword all around, leaving no trace.
'No... no... impossible....
Vina and Yuna's bodies stiffened and halted, they each let out a 'chi' sound and spurted blood, which condensed in the air into blood‑colored cherry blossoms!
The slender sword's radiant chant is equipment that counters dark creatures, no different from silverware.
After the two sisters became vampires, they suffered a lethal blow from the radiant chant and began to combust spontaneously.
Vina and Yuna turned to ash before Alice's eyes, their gazes still lingering with shock and unwillingness—they never expected to be felled by a single sword from her; the speed they prided themselves on was useless before Alice and was easily shattered—
Alice rose, her half‑dragon form receding, she slipped her slender sword back into its sheath, lowered her head to look at the ashes left by the twin sisters, and with a wave of her hand scattered them with a cold wind.
'Truly a pity—looks like my sword is just a bit faster.'

title: Chapter 35 — The One Who Truly Decides Victory or Defeat
content:
Chapter 35 — The One Who Truly Decides Victory or Defeat

Volume 19 · Chapter 35

After killing Vivian and Luna, Alice immediately turned around and went to the side of Percival, who had fallen into a coma from unconsciousness.

Percival was gravely wounded by the two sisters, entering a near-death state, especially his abdominal wound, which was quite horrifying to behold.

Alice frowned, carefully examined Percival's injuries, and found that he still had breath left; he hadn't actually died, only fallen into a coma due to the severity of his wounds.

This eased Alice's tense heart slightly, and she let out a quiet sigh of relief. She couldn't just stand by and watch Percival die in front of her, leaving behind a great regret and guilt.

Alice discovered that Percival's abdominal wound was very serious; if not treated promptly, it might really threaten his life.

So Alice used her cold magic to form a layer of golden ice crystals over Percival's abdominal wound, which immediately took him out of the life-threatening danger.

After completing this treatment, Alice stood up and prepared to leave, intending to find Merlin. After all, the chaos within the capital wasn't the source of evil; the true culprit was outside the city walls.

But just as Alice was about to stand up, Percival's unconscious hand grabbed hers. Her uneasy reaction seemed like she was having a bad dream.

Alice stood frozen, knelt down, and placed her hand on Percival's forehead.

A gentle, cold breeze seeped into his body, calming Percival's unease, and he gradually relaxed, letting go of Alice.

Alice quietly stared at the unconscious Percival, recalling the assassin she had fought in the alley earlier—

It was really him, the one who was supposed to attack Merlin. Was that person actually Percival?

After all, his build and techniques were very similar...

If the enemy from that day was indeed Percival, would saving him be right or wrong?

Regardless of who it was, whoever attacked Merlin I would not forgive, even if they were a close acquaintance...

Alice's eyes sharpened, and she felt a strong suspicion that the enemy she had fought earlier was Percival, though she had no concrete evidence.

After staring at Percival for a while, Alice averted her gaze, deciding not to dwell on this issue any longer. Finding Merlin was more urgent.

So Alice stood up and walked away from the Archbishop's Cathedral, heading straight for outside the capital.

It was only after Alice left that Percival slowly opened his eyes, looking at the golden ice crystal attached to his abdominal wound, and fell into silence...

Outside the capital, the vampire army poured out en masse, ruthlessly wiping out humanity, constantly gnawing at the remaining defensive formations.

Once the holy bell at the Archbishop's Cathedral ceased ringing, the human forces within the city fell into a losing battle.

Without the bell's suppression, the vampires surged in power, maximizing their advantages and defeating the human army step by step!

OP SE This novel

Dracula and Matthias observed the situation, seeing the vampires gaining the upper hand, and slightly relaxed their posture.

"It seems the situation is settled. The capital will be ours soon." Dracula smiled confidently.

"Congratulations, Father, the first step toward establishing the Eternal Night Empire has succeeded! We've won this war!" Matthias excitedly said, his eyes wide open.

"Winning this war is still too early. The decisive factor isn't about capturing the capital; it's the game between me and those two demons that determines the outcome." Dracula gazed far away, feeling that the real enemy was approaching, "We are the players on the board, while others are merely pieces that can be moved around."

"Indeed... Matthias's expression grew serious, acknowledging that Dracula was right. This war's conflict between races was unimportant; the result of victory or defeat would be determined between Dracula and the two demon lords.

"Let's calculate the time. Those two honored guests should be arriving soon?" Dracula squinted, hearing a buzzing sound in the air.

In the sky, a vast cloud of flies was approaching at a speed visible to the naked eye. Looking closely, it was a dense swarm of man-eating flies!

Groups of flies, appearing as if gone mad, charged at the small remaining vampire forces—

"...What's this!?"

"Flies..."

"...Man-eating creatures!"

2F SF Light Novel

A torrent of man-eating flies crashed down on the vampires defending the location, drowning them all in the deluge.

At that moment, the vampires suffered heavy casualties, their pitiful wailing screams echoing like those of someone in hell!

Even though vampires have extremely strong regeneration abilities, they were overwhelmed by countless man-eating flies, their bones being completely devoured, their regeneration suppressed!

"Mommy, please don't... don't bite me!" Dickie Patrick lay trembling on the ground, too terrified to even breathe as the flies swarmed.

"Father, what should we do? The insects' numbers are too many; we can't hold back some of them!" Matthias drew his sword and swung it, but to little effect, the flies were too many.

"Don't make things worse, become the enemy's target." Dracula sat on his horse, expression resolute, feeling that the two demons had arrived. This ferocious swarm of flies was merely Gorgon's greeting, "Ha, this gluttonous demon lord sure has a big appetite. Just showing off with a preemptive strike."

As soon as his words fell, Dracula's expression changed. Vast magical power surged from his body into the sky, such overwhelming pressure and magic seemed comparable to that of the demon lords?

Under Dracula's feet, a deep, swirling blood pool appeared, forming a wave of fresh blood rushing in all directions after just a single breath!

The blood wave surged up, its momentum no different from a real tsunami, scattering the dense swarm of flies to the ground or drowning them in the flood.

The blood wave dissipated, staining the mountain peak crimson. The previously frantic swarm of flies had been driven away.

The surviving vampires were wounded from head to foot, but in an instant, they recovered as if nothing happened, not being devoured by the flies, which was very fortunate.

"Come," Dracula squinted, staring ahead.

The flies gathered, beginning to enter the mouth of Albus in an organized, disciplined manner, swallowing countless flies, as if consuming the land and sea.

After Albus finished swallowing the flies, he wiped his mouth corner and looked at Dracula and Matthias with a disdainful expression, "You blood monsters are really hard to eat! My fly babies are about to throw up..."

"Are you Dracula?" Merlin stepped out from behind Albus, staring at the young man on the horse, feeling his status was very high, even the chancellor Matthias was extremely respectful.

"Right, it's me. You're the son of Vivian?" Dracula examined Merlin, finding that despite rumors of his genius, upon meeting him, he felt he was ordinary, too common. "His appearance is indeed similar to Vivian, but he lacks his mother's commanding presence over all the kings."

"Stop wasting time. We're not acquainted." Merlin placed his hand on the holy silver scimitar behind his back, saying meaningfully, "I'll cut off your head and behead you."

"My task is to kill you!"

title: Chapter 36 — Instigation (Extra)
content:
Chapter 36 — Instigation (Extra)

Volume 19 · Chapter 36

"The short-life curse you placed on the Austin family ends today." Merlin hid nothing, coming straight to the point by declaring his intention to kill Dracula.

"Oh? So the descendant of that vampire hunter from centuries ago is still alive? Your vitality is truly extraordinary. I thought their bloodline had gone extinct. Looks like I underestimated human will to survive." Dracula smiled strangely, understanding why Lucifer III had come back to cause him trouble—it was because of the curse he had released long ago.

"I spent a long time looking for you, but who knew you'd come to me on your own. How lucky of me~" Merlin cracked his knuckles, eager to get rid of Dracula.

"Lucky? I hope you'll still say that. You've probably not been Demon Lord for long, have you? Young and impulsive, you're nowhere near your mother Vivian. No wonder you're doing so poorly—struggling at the bottom of the adventurer industry. How pitiful~" Dracula said mockingly.

"I haven't sunk to the point where you can pity me, you bastard. Are you that eager to die?" Merlin gripped the holy silver katana at his waist, as if ready to draw it at any moment.

"If I could, I wouldn't want to conflict with either of you, but that seems impossible. Your eyes are both flashing with murderous intent. Do you hate me that much?" Dracula calmly sized up Merlin and Beelzebub.

"This is a stupid question! I'm dying to drink your blood and eat your flesh right now! And release my sister! Otherwise your end will be terrible!" Beelzebub shouted angrily, no longer hiding his face, his huge demon horns symbolizing his noble royal status.

Merlin said nothing. The target of this trip was to kill Dracula; otherwise the task Arnold's father assigned couldn't be completed. To end the Austin family's short-life curse, Dracula had to die.

Dickteplin saw Merlin and instinctively shrunk his head. After the big fight in Avignon before, encountering the murder-famous Lucifer III now still made him feel quite nervous.

However, Dickteplin had expected the blood race to win big in this war, but now there were variables. Whether they could achieve final victory was unknown. He could continue watching and find the opportunity most beneficial to him.

Maides stood obediently by Dracula's side, looking at Merlin and Beelzebub, feeling very surprised. It was the first time he had seen the Seven Demon Lords in person.

Were these two the demon race's kings? They didn't look that terrifying.

Especially that Lucifer III. Rumors said he was ugly and merciless, but his actual appearance was no different from a human's. He didn't even have the horns symbolizing demons!

Maides commented in his heart but didn't speak, because at this moment he had no right to participate. This was a conversation between Dracula, one of the three blood race ancestors, and the Seven Demon Kings of the demon race.

"Oh~, your sister? We never hurt her." Dracula said meaningfully.

"Stop talking nonsense, return Miranda!" Beelzebub stepped forward abruptly. His overwhelming pressure made everyone present stop breathing and feel fear!

Maides's face turned pale. He froze, then sweat slid down his forehead, shocked in his heart. Although he had seen Beelzebub's power before, experiencing it at such close range was truly terrifying!

"Lord Gluttony, please calm down. I never said I kept your sister imprisoned." Dracula turned his head slightly, signaling to Maides.

Maides understood, nodded, and went behind to push out the frightened Miranda, his hand always gripping her throat.

If Miranda dared make any drastic move, Maides would instantly break her neck, fool.

Seeing Miranda brought out, Beelzebub was overjoyed. The Demon Lord who was brutal in front of others showed a tender side at this moment.

"Miranda! It's brother! Brother's here to take you home!

Merlin's eyes stared at Dracula's face. Something seemed off. His group wanted to tear Dracula apart, yet Dracula was so obediently handing over Miranda. It was too cooperative, making one suspicious.

Dracula's face showed no emotional fluctuations. He was constantly calculating proportions, preparing to play with the two powerful Demon Lords in the palm of his hand!

Hearing Beelzebub's call, Miranda was like someone injected with a stimulant. She went from listless to energetic, tears in her eyes, probably having suffered quite a bit.

"That's natural. You're my most important sister. No matter what danger you're in, as your brother I'll risk my life to save you!

Miranda's eyes were tearful, her nose a bit stuffy. After so much suffering, she finally saw her brother and wouldn't have to worry anymore.

She blamed herself for not listening to her brother, running away and causing so much trouble. She dared not do it again.

Miranda wanted to say some apologetic words, but her peripheral vision saw Merlin's cold face. Her complexion strangely flushed red.

"...Teacher,...why are you here? Did you come specially to save me?"

Merlin didn't want to deal with Miranda and kept staring at Dracula. His hand never dared let go of the holy silver katana. "Don't call me teacher. I'm not."

Seeing Miranda's enthusiasm for Merlin over himself, the older brother, Beelzebub felt unbalanced and stepped forward. "Miranda, it was brother who kept looking for you. This Lucifer guy didn't do anything. You should be grateful to me..."

"Don't come near!" Maides saw Beelzebub approaching, extremely nervous, immediately grabbing Miranda and pressing hard on her throat pulse. This was a blatant threat!

"Brother... Miranda had no combat ability now, could only be controlled by Maides, choked and unable to breathe, showing a painful expression.

"Miranda!"

Beelzebub felt like needles piercing his whole body, worried about Miranda's safety, and had no courage to take another step forward.

The flame of rage was支配ing Beelzebub. His face became hideous, hatred glaring at Dracula, voice hoarse.

"You cunning dog! What do you want! ? Release my sister quickly!"

"Sorry Lord Gluttony, interrupting your touching reunion. But I wonder if you have a misunderstanding? When did I say I'd release your sister?" Dracula's face changed instantly, starting to manipulate the situation. As long as he had Miranda in hand, the two Demon Lords didn't seem fearsome.

"What do you want?" Beelzebub narrowed his eyes, clenched his fists, veins popping on his arms!

"I don't want to trouble you. Just now seeing you siblings reunited touched me deeply. But there's no free lunch in this world. To gain something you must pay. So if you're willing to do one thing for me, I'll release your sister, guaranteeing not to harm a single hair on her. Are you interested?" Dracula asked tentatively.

Beelzebub trembled with anger. He wanted to tear the enemy apart, but thinking of Miranda being held captive, he had to calm down. "Say it!"

"You two are top-tier Demon Race powerhouses, two of the Seven Lords: Pride and Gluttony. Hearing your titles, it's hard to say who's stronger." Dracula turned around, stood with hands behind his back, smiling slyly.

"Lucifer III, the young Demon Lord, successor to Vivian.

"Single-handedly fighting the Church's large-scale crusades multiple times, countless holy spirits perished in the swamps.

"Never defeated, fame spread far and wide!"

"How to describe it... one word..."

"Strong!"
