title: Chapter 37 — Beelzebub's Dead End
content:
Chapter 37 — Beelzebub's Dead End

Volume 19 · Chapter 37

Merlin fell silent, his guard rising sharply when Dracula suddenly gushed about him with suspicious praise, sensing something far more sinister unfolding.

Dracula slowly turned, his eerie gaze fixed on Merlin. "What a perfect man—inheriting your mother’s throne so soon and already carving out such legendary achievements. I’m genuinely curious… how exactly would one defeat you?"

Merlin’s face darkened. "What do you mean?"

Dracula didn’t answer, instead smirking at Beelzebub. "You’re a demon king too. Surely you can shatter his unbeaten legend? Want to challenge him?"

Dicket Plain, standing behind them, nearly jumped out of his skin in shock. *So that’s what Dracula’s scheming about!* No wonder it’s so bold, controlling the Demon Lord’s sister like that—using one Demon Lord against another? Does it really think it can just sit back and profit from their mutual destruction?

Held captive, Miranda’s heart raced at Dracula’s manipulative words.

She was overjoyed her brother had traveled so far to rescue her, but if because of her, her brother had to fight Lucifer—

No matter what, Miranda refused to see that happen. She didn’t want to be the chain dragging others down.

Her bond with Beelzebub as siblings needed no explanation. As for Merlin, she held nothing but reverence for the young king, deeply admiring him.

As a powerless demon—ordinary among royalty—she’d faced endless scorn in the demon race. But long ago, she’d witnessed Merlin, equally unremarkable, unleash a force that made every demon bow. After that, she’d been utterly obsessed.

Miranda had relentlessly begged Merlin to teach her his unstoppable sword-drawing technique, even getting Beelzebub to plead on her behalf. But Merlin had flatly refused, showing no interest in taking disciples.

Though she still called him *Teacher*, the two had no actual master-disciple relationship.

"Brother! Don’t listen to their lies! These deceitful humans aren’t worth trusting! ...Ugh! ! !"

Miranda’s protest died in her throat as Medusa clamped a hand over her mouth, her icy glare warning her. "Be quiet—or you and your brother will regret it."

Miranda’s face twisted in terror, on the verge of tears, silently praying Beelzebub wouldn’t fight Lucifer to the death. She didn’t want to see either of them destroyed.

Beelzebub’s gaze locked onto Dracula’s, flames of fury burning in his eyes. "You pathetic creatures, think a few words can manipulate me? You dare tempt me to strike my own kin? Do you even have the right to bargain with me?"

"Don’t we?" Dracula waved a hand, his smile laced with meaning.

"Violent, you’d better obey—or your sister..." Medusa suddenly tightened her grip on Miranda’s throat, pressing a dagger to her neck. "One wrong move from me, and her head rolls."

"...These bastards..." Beelzebub gritted his teeth, veins bulging in his forehead. He wanted to slaughter every vampire in front of him, but his sister’s safety held him back.

"This is your only way out. Kill Lucifer before we breach the capital, or..." Medusa’s voice dropped, adding a deadline. "If you fail, your sister dies."

Beelzebub’s expression darkened, his head bowed as he grappled with the choice. Dracula had backed him into a corner.

Merlin sensed something off in Beelzebub’s demeanor and quickly spoke up. "Don’t listen to them. Attack together—we’ll protect Miranda."

"You don’t have a 100% guarantee either, do you?" Beelzebub lifted his head, his eyes no longer so simple.

"You wouldn’t really—" Merlin stumbled back half a step, suddenly treating Beelzebub as an enemy.

"You wretched bloodsuckers, think threatening my sister makes me bend? Fine. For her, I’ll do anything—even kill my own allies!" Beelzebub twisted his body and lunged, his fist flashing toward Merlin’s face. "Sorry!"

Merlin, caught completely off guard, took the full force of the strike. His features twisted under the impact, his body hurled backward in a violent arc.

"Beelzebub! You traitorous bastard at a time like this?!"

"For my sister! There’s nothing I wouldn’t betray!" Beelzebub roared, sending Merlin crashing into the ground before vanishing from sight.

The collision sent a shockwave rippling outward, the sheer force pressing down on everyone present.

Dicket Plain tumbled across the ground, eyes wide with terror. *Holy hell...* That’s the power of Demon Lords! One punch like that—terrifying strength, nearly matching Lucifer’s! If they fight... if it’s truly to the death, who knows who’d win?

"Ugh! ! !" Miranda screamed in protest, but only muffled sounds escaped as she glared at her brother’s betrayal.

Beelzebub ignored her, fixing Dracula with a glare. "I’m going to kill him. Don’t you dare harm a hair on my sister’s head—or I’ll make you regret it!"

"Of course not. I said we wouldn’t hurt your sister, didn’t I?" Dracula looked down at the burning capital, smirking. "But time’s running out. My army’s about to crush the empire’s last defenses. Make it quick."

"Wait for me!" Beelzebub sneered, sprinting after the stunned Merlin, their clash igniting in a frenzy.

After Beelzebub left, Medusa let out a low, triumphant laugh. "Father, just as expected. The two Demon Lords will tear each other apart—leaving us untouchable."

"Nothing to it. Extra emotions are just baggage. Beelzebub’s strong, but his weakness is just as obvious." Dracula’s tone was detached as he watched the capital burn. "The empire won’t last much longer. We can announce the fall of the B Dynasty soon."

Dicket Plain stayed silent, his eyes darting wildly. *What now?* The vampires have all the advantage! How can I turn this around and survive?

Meanwhile, Merlin hit the ground hard, springing up to curse. "Are you insane?! You can’t trust those people! Even if you obey, they’ll still kill Miranda!"

Beelzebub landed beside him, his expression eerily calm. "How else can I guarantee her safety? What would *you* do?"

"Cut losses! Crush them all! Worrying about Miranda will only hold us back!" Merlin’s voice rose, veins throbbing in his forehead.

"You’re just standing there judging me! It’s not your loved one being held hostage!" Beelzebub’s voice was cold. "If it were your human wife, you’d react the same way, wouldn’t you?"

Merlin fell silent, his expression twisting. *Alice’s...*

Yeah. If it were Alice being threatened, would I really choose to cut losses so coldly?

title: Chapter 38 — Showdown
content:
Chapter 38 — Showdown

Volume 19 · Chapter 38

Merlin was left speechless by Beelzebub's sudden questioning, not knowing how to respond.
If Alice's life were being held hostage, could I really easily say something that disregards her safety? No matter the cost, eliminating the enemy must be the top priority.
After thinking for a moment, Merlin truly couldn't give a precise answer, finding himself in a similar dead end with Beelzebub, unable to devise a perfect solution.
Because deep down, Merlin truly does not want Alice to be harmed; if he could, he would proactively eliminate any danger that could hurt her before it even arises.
Of course, Merlin does not think Alice holds a particularly high place in his heart; rather, it is a normal reaction that arises solely from protecting his comrades.
Merlin remained silent, somewhat understanding that Beelzebub would, for Miranda's sake, not hesitate to be used by others and fight him fiercely; he realized he had spoken too lightly, failing to consider things from the perspective of Beelzebub as an elder brother.
Seeing Merlin say nothing, Beelzebub smirked and said, "What? Do you think I'm right? Now you can at least somewhat understand my predicament, right?"
"No..." Merlin furrowed his brows, speaking firmly, "Even if Alice were taken hostage, I would still prioritize eliminating the enemy. Being hostageable is solely due to one's own weakness; even if it's an accident, it's merely because my skills are lacking."
"You... are you serious?" Beelzebub's eyes grew strange, feeling Merlin's words were utterly insincere; he didn't believe Merlin could be so cold-blooded toward that human woman, after all, having spent these eight with him, from various small matters one can see that Alice's position in Merlin's heart is absolutely not ordinary, even surpassing that of his own sister Lilith; this is clearly abnormal!
"Of course I'm serious; constant compromise and yielding to others solves nothing—it's merely weakness." Merlin said solemnly.
"Anyone has the right to call me weak, but you don't!" Beelzebub frowned and retorted, "You're willing to become my enemy for that human woman, and I could likewise harden my heart to strike you down for Miranda's sake, so we're the same—both would betray our kind for someone; what qualifications do you have to point fingers at me?"
"Nonsense, choosing to fight me for Miranda's safety is a foolish decision; rest assured, even if I were defeated, those beasts wouldn't release Miranda—they'd continue to use her life as leverage to make you do more for them; greed is endless"
Merlin speculated, feeling that the blood clan side acted with impunity, relying on holding Miranda to manipulate Beelzebub and thus exert pressure on himself.
As fellow demon monarchs, a genuine clash of blades would hardly be a simple brawl; it could easily lead to the fall of a demon lord.
Merlin did not want to kill Beelzebub, for it would easily make him a reviled sinner among the demon race—not only mingling with humans but also slaying his own kin, which would cement the crime of betraying the demon race, a stain impossible to wash away. i上名
Having lived over two hundred years from birth to adulthood in the demon realm, it is impossible for Merlin to have no special feelings toward the demon race and his homeland.
"I know exactly what they want: nothing more than to use me to restrain you, then securely win this war and capture the royal city; but my sister's life is in their hands, and though I know certain actions are wrong, I must still carry them out."
Beelzebub paused, his eyes suddenly enlarging into dense clusters like a fly's, his body transforming into a dark, sturdy form, six pairs of translucent cicada wings unfurling from his back, and his horns becoming even sharper.
"The reason you can stand here and lecture me is simply because you don't know how much pain I feel inside; you cannot stand in my position. If you still wish to help me, then offer up your own head!"
Merlin, seeing Beelzebub reveal his true demonic form, could not help but grow furious.....
This sis-con! — Coming out with full force right away?
Looks like he's serious; can the conflict no longer be resolved peacefully?
I fear this isn't a simple brawl that can settle things; mishandled, it could end in mutual destruction, only concluding when one side is completely defeated.
Merlin wanted to go straight for Dracula, but Beelzebub, to protect Miranda's safety, stopped him; perhaps only a true victor can be decided.
Thus Merlin's eyes blazed like torches; the proud him would never deliberately yield to another as a compromise. He gripped the demon sword Banri Garan at his back, pressed down, adopting an iaido stance, determined to see it through to the end— SF4Z novel
"Beelzebub, since you're obstinate and unrepentant, then I won't hold back either—I'll say it plainly: you might die by my blade."
"Don't speak too soon, or you'll bite your tongue!"
Beelzebub let out a furious roar, his cicada wings vibrating to emit a terrifying soundwave; his swift figure flashed through midair, his speed already exceeding the speed of sound.
The two demon lords' powers collided violently, instantly producing a destructive force akin to heaven and earth being torn apart.
In the brief clash, each displayed their strength, both aiming to overwhelm the other; judging by such fierce combat, neither held back.
Beelzebub's balanced yet formidable physical attacks, with their N techniques continuously shifting, left Merlin unable to discern real from feint; various invisible killing skills were unleashed in an instant!
Merlin's gaze was sharp, flashing with ruby‑like light; without flashy martial aura or stunning techniques, he relied only on the rudimentary skill of returning to basics—an iaido slash.
Boom—
The earth shook and mountains trembled; the impact's shockwave ripped through every obstacle, even creating a spatial distortion that made the passage of a breath freeze in stillness!
The hostage Miranda widened her eyes at what unfolded before her, her inner turmoil becoming intense anxiety.
She could sense that Merlin and her brother Beelzebub were not merely sparring; a conflict of this level almost always carries the intent to kill the opponent, and if mishandled, could result in death!
Miranda felt useless, having become a pawn exploited by others; the fact that Merlin and her brother were forced to fight with their lives on the line only made her angrier, tears slipping down like broken pearls.
A violent storm surged forth like a tsunami; Dickter Platt fell to the ground, trembling with fear, thinking, "My goodness! Demon lords clashing is terrifying—it feels as if the heavens and earth could be torn apart at any moment!"
"…Good heavens! The clash between demon lords… is actually this terrifying?! It almost seems as if the combatants aren't beings of this world, giving me the feeling they are gods!" Mades, merely watching from the side, felt his heart pound, cold sweat pouring forth, relieved he didn't have to face the demon monarchs.
"God? I'm afraid it's still far from the true God.... Dracula's expression... as someone who has personally seen God, he evaluated the two demon lords saying"
"The Gluttony Demon Lord is formidable, and I too fear him three parts, but he falls far short of the oppressive might of the true God."
"As for that young Pride, the Demon Lord?"
"From start to now, I simply cannot gauge his strength—where does his limit lie?"

title: Chapter 39 — Blitz's Old Friend (and More to Come)
content:
Chapter 39 — Blitz's Old Friend (and More to Come)

Volume 19 · Chapter 39

Within the royal city, flames of war raged everywhere!

The battle between the imperial army and the vampires had reached a white-hot intensity, and the empire was already showing an irrecoverable decline.

Although the vampires far outnumbered the imperial soldiers in combat effectiveness, their strength far exceeded what many had anticipated.

Even the royal guard wielding powerful silver weapons couldn't gain the upper hand, unless they dealt fatal blows to these swift vampires.

This meant imperial soldiers had little advantage when fighting the vampires, relying entirely on their overwhelming numbers to push the vampires into a desperate corner.

Margaret led the participating imperial forces, shrinking their defensive perimeter and focusing their efforts on the royal palace!

They had to defend the palace to the last man, or the swarming vampires would seize the opportunity to smash through and destroy the imperial core that symbolized supreme royal authority in a single blow!

If they truly reached such a desperate situation, Margaret might find herself with no choice but to activate the Star Annihilator Cannon — the weapon that had shaped so much of history — and perish alongside the vampires on this land!

Silver spears stood erect like towering brambles, forming a natural thorn barrier. Any vampire foolish enough to charge in would suffer grievous injuries. Relying on this rock-solid defense, the imperial soldiers could still hold out, and the fierce vampires had no answer for now.

Arrows rained toward the sky like dense hail. The soldiers hadn't given up on counterattacking; each one treated killing a vampire as an honor!

The vast swarm of vampires blotted out the sky. The sun had already been invisible, and now not even its shadow could be seen.

Those grotesque faces in the sky constantly bared their needle-like fangs and roared, as if taunting the humans below.

Margaret wasn't hiding complacently within the palace — she took personal responsibility, fighting alongside her soldiers!

She skillfully handled the gold-inlaid flintlock pistol in her hand, constantly firing at the vampires in the sky. A silver bullet striking a vital point could take down an enemy.

Though Margaret was the old king's beloved daughter, she hadn't grown up the way her father expected — as an elegant, gentle little princess. Naturally restless since childhood, she had followed the old king hunting, honing her instincts into second nature. Especially her marksmanship: she could hit exactly where she aimed, to a level that made even professional musketeers feel ashamed.

One vampire luckily dodged the arrow storm and charged into the center of the defense. It dove down furiously, heading straight for that graceful figure on the battlefield.

"Your Highness!" Blaze cried out. He was busy defending another sector and couldn't reach Margaret in time. Watching this stray vampire head straight for the princess, panic welled up inside him!

"Ugh!" Margaret sensed the danger, her fair face turning pale. She immediately crouched and rolled, successfully dodging the vampire's diving attack!

Margaret was in an extremely central position. Even if the vampires didn't know her noble status, they could still deduce she was their commander.

This vampire came in with fierce momentum, flipping the soldiers who tried to block its path aside and letting out an excited roar—

"Fall back, fall back!" someone shouted.

"Hmph!" Margaret sniffed coldly. In this critical moment, she directly chose to crouch, raise her flintlock, and aim the dark barrel at her enemy. "Disappear!"

With a thunderous "bang," blazing flame erupted from the muzzle. The silver bullet instantly pierced through the vampire's forehead!

The vampire let out a shriek and turned to ash right before everyone's eyes...

Margaret's display greatly bolstered the soldiers' morale, and many of them cheered.

Even the noble princess had taken to the battlefield — what was there to fear for soldiers like them, born for war?

Many had heard the gossip about Margaret, that she was a mischievous, idle dummy of a princess.

But seeing her with their own eyes today, the soldiers couldn't help but look at the empire's sole heir with new respect. Seeing was believing!

Blaze exhaled deeply. Seeing that Margaret was unharmed, he felt somewhat relieved — his heart had been in his throat just moments ago.

Her marksmanship was no joke. A weapon with such poor accuracy seemed to come alive in her hands. Even in that panicked situation, she'd managed to turn the tables on her enemy. Impressive!

Blaze quickly ran over, watching Margaret with concern as he asked.

"Your Highness, are you alright?"

"I'm fine..." Margaret frowned, climbed to her feet, picked up her feathered hat, brushed off the dust, and put it back on.

"That was really dangerous just now. Please don't act on your own — stay by my side. I can fully protect your safety!" Blaze said earnestly.

"Do I look that fragile? Can you stop treating me like some noble lady who faints at the slightest thing?" Margaret熟练ly loaded a round, poured in silver pellets, and slung the flintlock over her slender shoulder. "I may not match you, but whatever the soldiers can do, I can do too!"

"Well..." Blaze felt particularly torn. Recalling how terrifying the situation had just been, he truly didn't dare let Margaret continue acting recklessly. After all, the entire imperial legion needed Margaret's command. If anything happened to her, the imperial defense would crumble without a fight!

"Alright, don't nag at me like an old mother. In a situation like this, even I can be useful." Margaret walked to the front, gazing at the vampire horde blotting out the sky, with not a trace of fear on her face.

Blaze wore a grimacing expression and didn't dare say much more. Margaret's behavior felt like she was causing more trouble, making it impossible for him to focus fully on the battle.

"Do you know where Lord Merlin went? I told you to send people to find him — why is there still no news?" Margaret asked.

"I've already sent people looking, but the manor was empty. It seems they disappeared somewhere as soon as the fighting started. I'm quite anxious too — if they don't return to assist us soon, I fear we won't be able to hold out long..." Blaze showed a worried expression.

"Pfft! Where on earth did they go?" Margaret grew restless. Were they fighting someone else, or... had we been abandoned?

"Your Highness, at a time like this, please don't dwell on that dull-faced iron-skinned rookie. We need true strength, like Lord Melfield and Alice..." Blaze said seriously.

"It's not what you think..." Margaret lowered her head, longing to see that man right now. "I never had much confidence in this war to begin with. Only with Lord Merlin by my side do I have the courage to persist in resisting. I believe he possesses the power to spark miracles!"

"You really..." Blaze sighed. He just couldn't understand — why would someone with such high standards like Her Highness be fascinated by an iron-rank adventurer?

Suddenly, commotion erupted from the defensive line—

A silk-thread-like aura slash descended. Without close inspection, it was utterly invisible!

This thread of aura seemed soft but was actually incredibly sharp. With a light flick, dozens of knights were sliced apart on the spot.

The scene descended into chaos — limbs and blood sprayed everywhere. Clearly, the enemy was no pushover. A strong force had attacked!

"Your Highness, be careful! This is likely something serious! You must stand behind me!" Blaze gripped his silver greatsword, positioning himself in front of Margaret, his attention fixed on all sides. But he could see nothing except the severed limbs around him.

"Who's there? Seems unusual... this fighting style is..." Margaret's expression grew tense as she saw someone breaking through!

A black shadow descended from the sky. Golden aura threads slowly faded from his fingertips, his silhouette appearing mature and composed.

"...You're?!" Blaze's eyes widened in utter disbelief.

Robert, one of the Three Knights of France, slowly turned around and looked at Blaze with a meaningful gaze.

"Long time no see, my friend."

title: Chapter 40 — The First Hero (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 40 — The First Hero (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 19 · Chapter 40

The person who suddenly appeared was indeed Robert, one of the Three Knights of France, a man who taught by example and had mastered the techniques of aura usage to a supernatural degree!

Blaize had personally witnessed Robert being killed by the Demon Lord Gluttony, his heart dug out and eaten — so how could he possibly be standing alive before everyone? It was like seeing a ghost with your own eyes!

Normally speaking, no human could survive having their heart excavated, so Robert's sudden appearance left everyone utterly stunned!

"Robert!? ...Weren't you already..." Blaize's eyeballs nearly popped out of his head, his words stumbling and incoherent.

Margaret wore an odd expression, unable to regard Robert with any normal attitude. A strong sense of wrongness washed over her, yet she couldn't quite put her finger on it.

"My old friend, what's wrong with you? Don't you rejoice at seeing me?" Robert's smile was peculiar. "I remember you were very sad after I died. Wasn't that all faked?"

"...No! I'm just shocked!" Blaize was simple and honest at heart, and couldn't process it in time. He truly believed his good friend had come back from the dead. "...Weren't you killed by the Demon Lord Gluttony? I saw my own eyes as it devoured your heart! Why are you standing before me alive!?"

"Yes, I was killed by that monster, the Demon Lord Gltony. It was impossible for me to appear again..." Robert sighed, then went on to explain, "But in order to protect the Empire, my powerful willpower drove me to climb out of the grave once more."

"...Margaret shuffled behind Blaize, thinking there was no way anyone would believe such nonsense. He had just been mercilessly slaughtering Imperial soldiers, and resurrection through sheer willpower was... far too ridiculous!

"...Is that really true?" Blaize's eyes widened, and such a straightforward man actually felt a hint of admiration. "Your loyalty... impresses me!"

A vein pulsed on Margaret's forehead. She raised her flintlock pistol and smacked him on the head, irritated. "Use your brain! Don't believe such nonsense so easily! How could someone whose heart was eaten still be alive? And he was attacking Imperial knights just now!"

Blaize shuddered and snapped to his senses, adopting a wary posture. "Right! Stop lying to me! The fact that you massacred Imperial knights just now proves you're no longer my friend!"

"Hahaha. Blaize, worthy as ever of your title — so defenseless toward others, so easily deceived." Robert mocked.

"What loyalty to the Empire? You've betrayed us! You threw yourself under the vile Mades, becoming his humble lackey!"

Blaize gripped his greatsword tightly, his heart churning with mixed emotions.

Robert had always been Blaize's closest friend. They had survived life and death together for many years, only to discover he was Mades's informant.

No wonder Princess Margaret's countless schemes to eliminate Mades never succeeded. It must have been this rat Robert leaking information!

Blaize hated Robert to the point of gritting his teeth. He longed to kill this traitor without delay. Regardless of whether Robert was his friend or not, anyone who betrayed the Empire was an unforgivable enemy!

" accusing me of betrayal... that's a bit much. I have never betrayed the Empire, because I have always been Lord Mades's subordinate, serving the great Vampire Clan." Robert had no interest in loyalty or righteousness. He was a member of the Vampire Clan himself.

"Ha, no wonder you could survive after Gluttony ate your heart. You're a vampire too, right? That kind of fatal wound to ordinary people means nothing to you. You'll quickly grow a new heart, won't you?" Margaret sneered.

"That's right, I am also a vampire..." Mades split his mouth, revealing sharp fangs. "Her Highness's intelligence, I've felt it for a long time. Those plans of hers could indeed have killed Lord Mades. But with me here, you would never succeed. Every plan Her Highness made, Lord Mades knew intimately."

"Accursed thing, I should have suspected you scum from the start..." Margaret frowned tightly. She never expected a traitor to emerge among the Three Knights.

"To be hated by Her Highness is my honor. Hmph hmph hmph..." Robert bowed deeply, full of sarcasm.

"You ungrateful worm! Even Bat洛ka, tormented by the炎demon parasite, was willing to sacrifice herself for the kingdom. You not only betrayed the King's trust but stabbed us in the back. Unforgivable!" Blaize raised his silver broadsword, Saint-tier aura surging forth!

"Getting angry? That's wonderful. In the past, I had to conceal my vampire identity and couldn't fight at full power, making you the Empire's First Warrior. Now I have no need for restraint and can crush you beneath my feet!" Robert spread his arms, golden aura erupting from his body and condensing into blades. An overwhelmingly sharp killing intent exploded outward!

Blaize sensed an inexplicable pressure. Robert was stronger than usual by more than a little, not inferior to himself. "Your Highness, please step back. I'll deal with this lackey of Mades myself!"

"You no longer regard this fellow as a friend?" Margaret asked tentatively, worried that he might still cling to the false camaraderie of the past.

"That's right. I truly wish he had really been killed by Gluttony. Then I could have still respected him." Blaize said, his words heavy with meaning.

Margaret was finally at ease and stepped back. Since she couldn't help, she'd leave it to Blaize.

The other soldiers and knights who had been on alert and watching also dispersed, clearly sensing they couldn't well intervene in a clash between Saints.

"Hehehe! I'll ruin your reputation as the Empire's First Warrior!"

Robert struck first. As a fighter, his techniques were ruthless, aura manifesting as invisible sharp weapons, invincible!

Blaize showed no weakness, swinging his great sword and cleaving downward, generating gale-force winds that drove those nearby back two steps.

The two's attacks collided, golden aura wreaking havoc in all directions. The clash between two of the Empire's strongest was like dragons and tigers contending, neither able to gain the upper hand!

But Robert possessed the加持of vampire power. His speed, strength, and perception all crushed Blaize's. Under the assault of aura-forged blades, he was extremely rapid, splitting the earth into long trenches!

Blaize was terrified, his arms numb, driven to a desperate position. He had no choice but to resort to hand-to-hand combat—

What the hell! Robert's power increased so much?! Slightly surpassing my own!

Outside the royal city, this battle was the one truly determining the Empire's fate.

A terrifying killing intent erupted, leaving the scene in ruins.

Several mountains were blasted to powder, the earth split and fissured, leaving behind a deep abyss resembling a trench.

Merlin was unharmed, his katana already drawn, seemingly having just experienced a fight worthy of his drawing blade.

His expression blank, he stared down at his feet. Beelzebub lay motionless in a pool of blood, as if no longer alive—

"Beelzebub, you forced my hand..."

title: Chapter 41 — Heavy Blow to the Blade's Back
content:
Chapter 41 — Heavy Blow to the Blade's Back

Volume 19 · Chapter 41

It seemed the worst-case scenario had already occurred; a firefight had broken out between Merlin and Beelzebub.

Merlin's face showed no emotion as he stood there like a rigid puppet.

Beelzebub was beaten until his head was shattered and blood poured from his wounds; he lay motionless in a pool of his own blood.

The onlookers in the distance were all frozen in shock at this sight—

"Brother! No..." Miranda saw her brother Beelzebub lying lifeless on the ground and immediately feared the worst; overwhelmed by the blow, she collapsed and lost consciousness.

Meades caught her falling body, his inner shock refusing to settle. One strike! He had assumed it would be a contest of evenly matched forces, yet the outcome ended in a crushing finish. Beelzebub had been slain by Lucifer III's single blow. There were no other superfluous moves—victory was already decided when the blade's edge came to rest...

Dickteping, who had been hiding at the rear, trembled uncontrollably. A battle between Demon Lords—was already over with a single strike. He refused to believe his own eyes.

Truly a monster who had driven the Holy Church to surrender on his own strength alone! Truly overwhelming power!

Even among the lords of the demon race, he must be an extremely powerful presence!

Good heavens! Does this freak have any weaknesses? He could think of no one capable of toppling him!

Dickteping felt his opportunity approaching. Lucifer III had defeated Beelzebub; next, he would surely target Dracula. At that point, he might have a chance to escape unharmed!

"Hmph. As expected of the son born to Demon Lord Vivian—so young yet so terrifying. Not in the least inferior to his mother back then; in fact, his strength has reached an unfathomable degree..." Dracula narrowed his eyes, studying the silent Merlin below. "To defeat Beelzebub with a single move—what does this mean for you?"

"...I understand..." Meades stammered in response.

"It means this young Demon Lord has long since surpassed his demon kin. He may well be the demon race's greatest representative." Dracula paused, then continued seriously, "What we face is no ordinary Demon Lord—it is a monster who crushes the entire demon race."

"...What should we do? How should we respond?" Meades grew flustered. He had never imagined such a situation; Lucifer III's power had far exceeded his expectations.

"Do not panic. Regardless of how powerful he is, there remains a way to deal with him." Dracula spoke calmly, confidently. "What is the blood clan's pride? Of course, it is our immortality. In a war of attrition, we will not lose to anyone. Even if Lucifer III can devastate the heavens and earth, his strength is by no means infinite. When he grows exhausted, that will be our opportunity..."

"Oh! So that's how it is. Father, your wisdom is truly divine!" Meades praised sycantically.

Dickteping furrowed his brow. He felt the situation had not clarified and remained fraught with anxiety...

Over there, Alice arrived and saw Merlin standing still in the middle of everything, utterly bewildered.

Upon seeing Beelzebub collapsed in a pool of blood, Alice was visibly shaken; she was unwilling to believe Merlin was the one who had done this.

After all, during the time they had spent together, Merlin and Beelzebub had gotten along reasonably well. For weapons to suddenly turn against each other meant something serious had undoubtedly occurred!

Alice stopped beside Merlin, her expression dazed, her voice trembling as she asked, "What have you done... Merlin?"

"That bunch of bastards threatened his sister with harm to force him to attack me. I had no choice but to act. There was no other way." Merlin answered calmly.

Alice lowered her head. She did not reproach Merlin. Considering the enemy had used Merlin's life as leverage and forced the issue, a counterattack was only natural.

Yet Merlin's cold-blooded approach made her uneasy.

Alice did not particularly enjoy Merlin being so emotionless. Rather, she wished he had a touch more warmth. In plain terms, she hoped Merlin would become more human rather than purely a demon.

"You can only blame Beelzebub for being so unlucky—and for caring too much about his sister. Why didn't he just team up with me to handle Dracula? Miranda has already become the vampire's protective umbrella. They will not harm her, for doing so would cost them their last lifeline." Merlin sighed and pointed his blade upward, returning the katana to its scabbard.

This subtle movement immediately caught Alice's attention. Ordinarily, after killing an enemy, Merlin would lower the blade's edge when sheathing it.

By sheathing with the blade facing upward, he had almost certainly not attacked with the cutting edge but with the flat of the blade—the刀背!

Alice hurriedly knelt down to inspect Beelzebub's injuries. His head had taken the main blow, and blood continued to pour unabated, leaving him critically wounded and unconscious.

Merlin had indeed shown mercy! Using the flat of the blade could only injure gravely, without delivering a lethal strike...

Alice raised her head, wanting to ask Merlin what he intended to do—but he cut her off.

"Merlin..."

"Shh!" Merlin held up a silencing gesture, speaking with deliberate meaning. "The enemy's ears are sharp. Do not speak carelessly."

Alice suddenly stilled. She thought Merlin must be feigning Beelzebub's death to make the enemy abandon using Miranda as a shield.

"I am going to kill Dracula. You stay here and watch over him." Merlin turned to seek out Dracula and settle the score.

"Who wants to stay and watch over him? I won't do it. I'm coming with you!" Alice persisted, absolutely unwilling to remain behind.

"If you come with me, you'll only get in the way and be of no help at all." Merlin said helplessly.

"How do you know I'll get in the way? Don't look down on people. I'm now a rising new star among adventurers. You're merely my little sidekick. Hmph!" Alice said resentfully.

"Tch! Do as you please—as long as you don't get in the way. Otherwise, I'll kick you off..." Merlin clicked his tongue, unable to control Alice at all.

"Fine. We'll see! We'll definitely be of help. When the time comes, you'll be kneeling to beg me!" Alice said defiantly.

Merlin had taken only a few steps when he was stopped by Beelzebub, who lay in the pool of blood and grabbed his ankle, still unwilling to let Merlin come to harm Milanoda.

In such a situation, Merlin could do nothing but stop and turn to look at the utterly狼狈 Beelzebub. Feeling pity, he said,

"Are you not yet fully unconscious? I advise you to stop struggling. At times like this, it's best to listen to me."

Beelzebub showed no response, still gripping Merlin's ankle tightly. He looked profoundly unwilling to accept defeat—afraid Merlin would bring harm to his sister.

Merlin sighed and, having no choice, knelt down and spoke in a voice only the two of them could hear:

"Don't worry. I will not abandon Milanoda to her fate."

"I pledge upon the identity of the Third-generation Arrogant Lord—your sister will surely survive..."

title: Chapter 42 — Turnaround (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 42 — Turnaround (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 19 · Chapter 42

Medes saw Merlin drop Beelzebub, who was lying in a pool of blood, and come over with another woman. He asked in confusion, "Did a companion just arrive?"

"Oh? Not worth fearing. That woman's strength is about the same as yours; she poses no real threat. The true threat is still..."

Dracula's eyes stared at Merlin as he approached, his mind focused on how to eliminate this stumbling block.

Just moments ago he had thought to give Beelzebub a time limit, letting him kill Lucifer III within that time.

But it was completely unnecessary—the clash between the two Demon Lords ended in an instant, with none of the evenly matched bloodbath he had imagined.

"Thank goodness it wasn't some ruthless character, or things might have been difficult to handle..." Medes wiped the cold sweat from his forehead, clearly still intimidated by Merlin and beginning to hesitate.

Dickteplin's eyes darted around; he sensed an opportunity. He placed his hand on the revolver behind his back, loaded with the Fengming Stone, ready to fire the decisive shot at the perfect moment!

Merlin stood before Dracula again. Seeing Miranda unconscious, he felt a pang of guilt—

"Sigh, Miranda must think she killed Beelzebub, right? She probably can't accept the reality yet, so she fainted..."

"Still, it's for the best. Otherwise explaining things would be a hassle. I need to focus on taking down Dracula!"

Merlin averted his gaze, his eyes cold as he stared at Dracula, provoking him.

"Now let me see what tricks you can pull next?"

*Patter patter patter*—Dracula's meaningful chuckle was heavy with meaning. He watched Merlin with interest. "Wonderful. I didn't expect someone so young to be this powerful. You defeated the Gluttony Demon Lord of equal rank in an instant. Clearly, you've surpassed your mother Vivian—First Demon Lord Palace... you deserve it!"

"Stop talking. You're holding Beelzebub's sister hostage and inciting it to kill me—how despicable!" Merlin's face turned extremely ugly.

"We're enemies. If it can defeat the opponent, it's a good method—there's no such thing as despicable or not." Dracula spread his arms, teasing. "We're all creatures of the dark faction. To be called despicable by the Great Demon Lord—how subtle~"

"Hmph! Let's see how long you can keep your composure. Beelzebub is dead, and you have no more pawns to use. Wait for death..." Merlin's eyes revealed killing intent without concealment.

"Sorry, but the Gluttony Demon Lord's sister is still in my hands. Dare to move even a hair, and she dies instantly!" Dracula glanced behind him. Although Miranda was unconscious, she was still being held by Medes.

Alice looked behind and saw Miranda's long hair flowing like a waterfall. Even with demon horns on her head, she was still clearly a beauty.

"This girl is Miranda? Beelzebub's sister, whom he searched everywhere for—she doesn't look vicious at all..."

Alice frowned. Demons she had seen before were all fierce and astonishingly powerful, but this sister of Beelzebub seemed too weak.

"Miranda isn't my sister. Who cares if she lives or dies? This won't work on me. Give up." Merlin wore a fearless smile.

"Oh~ really?" Dracula pretended to be surprised, sneering.

"If you're so cold-blooded, just swing your sword! Use the same move you used to behead Beelzebub. I'd love to experience it. Of course, I'll also have my subordinates twist this female demon's neck, hehehe~"

"No... right! Try it if you dare!" Medes saw Dracula was so brazen, his morale rose instantly. He grabbed Miranda's unconscious neck, eager to try.

Alice found the situation very tricky. No wonder Beelzebub had been forced into fighting Merlin.

"Merlin, we..."

"Alice, don't speak. Just act as you see fit. I'll handle Dracula."

Seeing the seriousness in Merlin's eyes, Alice obediently shut up and stopped interfering with his plans.

Alice had thought Merlin would continue talking, but the next second, Merlin's sword slash had already been unleashed!

Merlin's terrifying burst speed was astonishing. In an instant he became a bolt of lightning, decisively drawing his blade without hesitation. The Holy Silver Longsword slashed straight at Dracula's forehead!

"No talking at all! You really don't care about his sister's life?!" Alice screamed in shock, criticizing Merlin's reckless behavior.

"Ugh!" Medes was shocked. He hadn't expected Merlin to strike so decisively. His brain short-circuited for a moment, but his hand still instinctively reached for Miranda's neck, intending to kill her.

Dracula widened his eyes, not blinking at all. Facing Merlin's killing move, he showed no fear at all, appearing completely calm.

"Die!"

Merlin saw that Dracula was serious and didn't buy his act of indifference, so he had to hover the Holy Silver Longsword above Dracula's forehead.

Actually, Merlin did care about Miranda's life. He just acted too much like he did, lest Dracula exploit that weakness, just like with Beelzebub.

If he could, Merlin would really want to save Miranda. After all, in his impression this demon girl wasn't bad. Even though he refused to teach her skills, she still kept calling him "teacher, teacher"—it was impossible for him to have no mercy at all.

Seeing Merlin suddenly stop, Dracula laughed happily, revealing a mocking face that deserved a beating.

"Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha..."

"What, do you want me to die? You're just talking big, aren't you?"

"Saying you feel nothing, but you're still worried about this female demon, aren't you?!"

"Sorry, I won the bet in the end. You're worried about Beelzebub's sister's safety. Good~"

"Come on, cut me! Cut me! You're useless even with the chance!"

Dracula kept slapping his own neck, shouting, and used his hand to push aside the Holy Silver Longsword hovering above his forehead.

"Hehehe, this female demon is quite the treasure. She has two Demon Lords manipulated—we should make good use of her!" Medes laughed, his morale rising instantly. He shouted, "Lucifer III, obey, or this female demon is dead for sure!"

Merlin lowered his head, his face gloomy, recalling that he had just promised to keep Miranda alive. He hesitated whether to destroy his opponent at all costs.

...Alice furrowed her brows, sensing Merlin's inner struggle. She couldn't help feeling a pang of sorrow. Why was he hesitating for this female demon? Considering the hostage's safety was good, but why did she feel so uneasy?

Dickteplin slowly raised his head and suddenly drew the revolver from his lower back, aiming at Dracula and Medes ahead.

The opportunity is here! I've been waiting for this moment!

There's only one Fengming Stone. I can only eliminate either Dracula or Medes!

I need to ensure the vampires are completely annihilated, so I won't have to worry about future troubles.

And I must ensure my own safe escape. I can't die under imperial or Demon Lord pursuit!

Thinking this way, the outcome was already obvious!

Heh heh heh, controlling the whole situation feels so good!

The ones controlling the war aren't the imperial royal family, nor the Demon Lord ancestor...

But it's me!

title: Chapter 43 — Forged a Thousand Times (I caught a cold today, my head hurts off and on)
content:
Chapter 43 — Forged a Thousand Times (I caught a cold today, my head hurts off and on)

Volume 19 · Chapter 43

Dickte Ping's expression became frenzied. After waiting for his grandson so long, he finally had the chance to turn over and become the master, no longer having to endure being bullied. He wanted to maximize the value of the stolen God-Seal Stone, not only to gain freedom but also to obtain great profit! If he killed Dracula, the blood clan would surely be defeated, but he himself would probably not escape being killed by Lucifer the Third! In that case, it would be most appropriate to kill Mades, who was holding Miranda hostage; Lucifer the Third merely couldn't act because of the hostage. So as long as he rescued Miranda, Lucifer the Third would become entangled with Dracula, and then he would have the chance to flee! Dickte Ping revealed a ferocious grin and ruthlessly pulled the trigger of the revolver crafted by the dwarves- With a 'bang' gunshot, the God-Seal Stone flashing with scorching light shot out like a meteor! The gunshot stunned everyone present; by the time they reacted, the God-Seal Stone had already pierced Mades' heart! '......Despicable villain!' Mades, powerless, dropped the unconscious Miranda, watching his heart being devoured by the tiny stone flashing with brilliant light, and in rage lunged at Dickte Ping. 'Don't-..don't come closer!' Dickte Ping fled backward in terror, collapsing onto the ground. Dickte Ping's seven orifices bled, his expression full of hatred; his powerful regenerative ability was completely sealed. After just a few steps he turned into a mixture, leaving behind the God-Seal Stone and a mysterious 'small bottle' on the ground. 'Is it you!?' Alice exclaimed in disbelief, having never noticed this former mercenary captain before. Merlin stared, equally surprised. He wasn't supposed to be helping the blood clan with underground slave trade? Why would he suddenly attack Mades? 'Why... Dracula's eyes were bloodshot, furious to the point of his face turning bluish-black. He never expected Dickte Ping, who had willingly allied himself with him, to betray him, especially at such a critical moment by stabbing him in the back. 'Why would you do this?' 'Hehehe... A bead of cold sweat trickled down Dickte Ping's forehead as he gathered his courage and said, 'This great lord has always only considered his own interests. Who would willingly be your dog? What are you still standing there for? Hurry up and kill that teasing monster! That demon woman is already safe!' No sooner had he spoken than Dracula's power surged, his form turning into layers of shadows as he furiously charged toward Dickte Ping. 'Eee! ! !' Dickte Ping turned pale with fright, momentarily at a loss. But Dracula was merely feinting; there was no need to dwell on Dickte Ping's betrayal now. Instead, seizing Miranda again to indirectly control Lucifer the Third was the most important thing! However, Alice's eyes were sharp and her hands quick; she noticed Dracula's intent, instantly stepped in front of the unconscious Miranda, drew her slender sword from her waist, and swung it fiercely! 'Hiss~!' Dracula sucked in a breath of cold air; his hands were sliced by the holy hymn, sending tingling sensations through them, and his advance was blocked. 'You won't succeed!' Alice shouted, and golden ice spears instantly condensed in mid-air! 'Get lost!' Dracula roared, his hair flying wildly as he turned his fingers into blades and viciously stabbed toward Alice's throat! Alice showed a hint of panic; with her current strength, she was no match for Dracula! 'Your opponent is me, don't treat me like thin air!' Merlin roared, flashing to Dracula's side, pressing his hand on Dracula's head and shoving him aside to protect Alice's safety. 'Damn it!' Dracula's expression twisted as he cursed loudly. 'Alice! Protect Beelzebub's sister!' Merlin shouted after saying that, then shoved Dracula away to prevent the fight from spreading to others. Alice hadn't even had time to respond when Merlin vanished, leaving her feeling somewhat unsettled. She lowered her gaze to Miranda, checked her over, and found that she had merely suffered a bit of emotional distress—she had fainted due to a mental blow. Alice secretly breathed a sigh of relief, then suddenly remembered there was still another enemy present; she raised her slender sword, wary, and fixed her stare on Dickte Ping. 'Hey hey, dragon girl, isn't it a bit too wary of me? After all, I did help you guys a lot, didn't I?' Dickte Ping said with a smile. 'Who knows what evil scheme you're hatching? You were never anything good to begin with!' Alice replied in a hostile tone. 'Seeing your attitude now, I really shouldn't have done that...' Dickte Ping snorted coldly. 'I don't mind killing you; trash like you doesn't deserve to live!' Alice's fighting spirit and magical power surged. 'Okay okay, I'm scared, alright...' Dickte Ping was a little afraid, knowing he couldn't beat Alice, so he turned and started to leave— Who would just run away that easily? In the underground laboratory of the royal capital, there still exists that flame demon treasure. 1KX> Previously I couldn't endure the Nine Amounts of Demon Slaying, but now I have obtained the blood clan's immortality, plucked from the void by Merlin and landed heavily on the ground. Not far away, Dracula snorted coldly and said, 'Now let's see what you can do.' Merlin followed closely as Dracula rose from the ground, letting out a low laugh, 'Indeed, I no longer have anything that can restrain you.' 'Huh huh huh...?' But what does that matter? You're doomed.... Merlin mocked Mades— 'Heh, how could you possibly beat me? Young.' Dracula's lips curled upward, showing no fear at all, 'Although your strength... 'You really think Vivian, but in observing others you're still far too inferior. 'Your power surpasses your mother Vivian; hearing my mother's name, could it be you've seen her?' Merlin frowned. 'Always hearing Vivian from your mouth, but even when I was still human I had heard of her; she is a mighty demon lord, the seven... 'I have not seen the demon lord palace at its peak, so you can tell your mother is an exceptionally capable demon, admirable.... Dracula implied deeply the demon lord palace, belongs to the first— The elder said. However, it's only hearsay; I have never personally seen my mother, what right do I have to judge?' Merlin sneered. 'Hmph, you too only—'Give me go to hell!' Then he drew the silver holy sword from his waist, which erupted with a tearing force, slashing downward vertically! The murderous sword qi descended like divine thunder, aiming to slaughter ignorant mortals! As if the gods beyond the heavens, Dracula stared wide-eyed, his astonished voice cut off abruptly; his entire body was instantly split in two by Merlin's slash, blood spraying— How swift the shadow and trajectory, just how many times must one have tempered to possess such power! A strong one who cannot see the blade's force, why can't even withstand a single strike of the opponent!? I possess divine power... yet I am about to die so simply... Damn! Could it be that I

title: Chapter 44 — Salt on the Wound (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 44 — Salt on the Wound (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 19 · Chapter 44

Dracula had witnessed Merlin's draw-and-slash; the sheer power of drawing the sword was so intense it seemed to want to tear and slash the enemy.
But when he actually felt it himself, he was still frightened; a surge of fear welled up—
...Why is this guy's power so strong? It pressed down like a mountain collapsing, a sea overturning! Impossible to block!
Even the divine child sealed in the bottle didn't give me this much pressure!
I feel that if this young Demon Lord were thrown into the age of the gods gathering, he could slay a god!
This is the second time in Dracula's life that he has felt an irresistible fear; the first time was the Cain sealed in the bottle, the second time is Merlin before him—both are powers beyond mortal reach.
Dracula felt his divinity slipping away, his body split into two halves, blood and flesh scattering in the air.
He saw Merlin, especially that icy gaze, as if his defeat were a matter of course.
Dracula's pupils contracted; his unwillingness and anger surged straight to his head, and a tenacious will to live began to dominate his body.
No! I cannot die! My great undertaking is not yet finished! I absolutely cannot fall!
In order to shed the monster's title, to live openly as a new species!
Dracula drew upon the divine power granted by Cain; it is an immortality far beyond that of ordinary vampires, and nothing can kill him except sunlight!
After inheriting one-third of the power of the divine child Cain, Dracula is no ordinary strongling; he is a being who can wield a portion of divine power, and his strength can fully rival the Demon Lords at the world's peak.
Such rare individuals who fortunately possess divine power are called false gods, pseudo‑gods, in ancient texts.
Only see Dracula's blood hanging in the air, beginning to spin wildly, forming a blood‑flesh vortex that engulfs his whole body, making him unapproachable.
"What?!" Merlin stared, dumbfounded, looking at the bloody chaos before him, finding it extremely bizarre; the vampire species is utterly different from any foe he has faced before, requiring extra caution.
A strong gust suddenly shattered the blood‑flesh storm, and Dracula turned into a monster all blood‑red, with a sharp mouth and cheekbones.
His long fangs protruded from his mouth, his hands and feet became sharp, and their size increased threefold!
His huge membranous wings quivered, raising a reeking gale, far more ferocious than an ordinary vampire!
Dracula, like **, floated in mid‑air looking down at Merlin, his voice turning muffled—
"You think you've killed me? Naive! I am a true immortal body; no attack can possibly kill me, and you will die unwillingly from exhaustion!"
Merlin stood stunned, instinctively glancing at his wounded weapon—this holy‑silver katana was a gift from Count Austin, forged from a vial of holy quicksilver, and has a suppressing effect on vampires and other dark creatures.
Obviously it is the Austin family ancestors' hunter's tool for fighting vampires; why is it useless against Dracula? I already used the holy katana to perform a draw‑and‑slash; logically Dracula should die for sure! 牡丁“吼
"Why... can't silver weapons kill you?"
"Hahaha, foolish, I am one of the original three vampire progenitors, a higher being; silver works on foot soldiers but... it simply won't work. Used...". Dracula said sarcastically, feeling Merlin was like wielding a useless toy to attack him and still thinking he could win.
Merlin furrowed his brow, feeling the situation a bit troublesome; his own strength is not weak at all, he could kill Dracula countless times, yet he cannot overcome the immortal body—no matter how he draws his sword, that monster could instantly recover; it's not that his power is lacking, but rather his ability has a hard time dealing with the opponent.
"I advise you to give up; why not cooperate with me and we split the wealth of all France? This would obviously be bad for you, right?" Dracula narrowed his eyes, sizing up Merlin with a tempting tone, "You, a noble lord of the demon race, why fight for humanity? That's really not normal."
Merlin raised his head, returned the holy‑silver katana to its sheath, and once again assumed the draw‑and‑slash stance, seemingly having no intention of accepting Dracula's suggestion, even thinking of killing him.
"I am now an adventurer from Rexhelm; completing my task is professional ethics!"
"Ha, that's truly a shame; clearly a great opportunity lies before you, yet you don't know how to cherish it." Dracula spread his hands, shook his head, and sighed.
"Sorry, I have no interest in the things you like; frankly, taking your life would excite me more." Merlin's eyes flashed with cold light, he gripped the hilt tightly.
"I know your power is terrifying; if I weren't immortal, you would have already killed me just now. I admit I haven't beaten you, but I said before....." Dracula spread his arms, speaking with deep meaning, "You cannot kill me; in the end you will only be exhausted and fall under my control."
"Hmph!" Merlin snorted coldly, launched another draw‑and‑slash, and a destructive, murderous sword aura burst forth.
In the royal capital, the battle between Blaze and Robert was extraordinarily tense, hard to separate.
Margaret stood behind, unable to stop herself from breaking into a sweat; she hadn't expected Robert's true strength to be so great, not inferior to Blaze at all, even secretly gaining the upper hand—it seems he could become the empire's first champion!
Robert's martial arts are extremely fierce and terrifying; his battle‑qi‑formed blades are sharp enough to cleave the earth, and he can even condense them into hard‑to‑defend battle‑qi filaments; a graze guarantees decapitation—truly a move‑by‑move lethal attack.
Conversely, Blaze, though fiercely counterattacking and wanting to personally slay Robert, that two‑timer, his mighty greatsword blows were still resolved by the formless.
Speaking of life‑and‑death combat, fighters who daily exchange punches and kicks actually gain the advantage here, not retreating but pressing forward, leaving Blaze overwhelmed.
Robert's battle‑qi filaments danced, their sharpness comparable to blades; as he swung, they nearly sliced off Blaze's head.
Blaze turned pale with fright, hastily stepped back a few paces, forced to catch his breath, feeling he wasn't gaining any advantage at all.
"What's wrong? O noble first champion of France, you couldn't possibly have only this much ability, could you? Truly disappointing~" Robert's smile was full of mockery.
"......Blaze leaned on his greatsword, panting heavily, "Don't get cocky, later when your head gets moved you won't be laughing."
Just as Blaze finished speaking, the ground suddenly lit up with a black magic circle, emitting strange sounds; it seems another enemy has joined, making the empire's already perilous situation even worse—snow on top of frost.
"I didn't expect someone to have already fought their way here?"
"Looks like we two arrived late..."
I am currently out of town; at this time the pharmacy is closed, so I can only take some medicine tomorrow and see.
If that doesn't work, I might go to the hospital for a check‑up; we'll talk about it then.

title: Chapter 45 — One Against Three (Part 2: Late Night)
content:
Chapter 45 — One Against Three (Part 2: Late Night)

Volume 19 · Chapter 45

The two remaining survivors of the Azure Flame, using teleportation magic to dodge the intense external defenses, burst straight into the central region where Margaret was located.

“Didn’t expect someone to have already reached here… looks like we’re too late.” Laurie equipped his own trap, his gaze fixed on the imperial knights surrounding him.

Eden glanced at Robert and whispered, “Someone’s already noticed. If we just take out that little princess named Margaret, the empire’s defenses will collapse instantly. I thought only I had realized that…”

Blaze’s body tensed suddenly, stepping in front of Margaret like a loyal hound protecting his master.

“Who are you? New recruits under Lord Medes?” Robert frowned, sensing that Laurie and Eden’s strength wasn’t weak—by rights, the blood race should have many capable subordinates, and he should know them well.

“Who’s his subordinate? We’re just here to help you vampires win this war.” Laurie retorted sharply, refusing to be anyone’s pawn.

Robert narrowed his eyes. If these two in front of him were vampires but denied it, that meant they were unlucky outsiders who’d stumbled in.

“Don’t waste time. We’ve finally made it inside—let’s finish this by killing that princess and ending the war. You came here for the same reason, didn’t you?” Eden asked Robert.

“Of course. I’m a subordinate of Lord Medes.” Robert thought, *Two reinforcements? Now I can take down Blaze and then personally kill the empire’s only heir.*

“Then let’s cooperate. The enemy only has one real threat, and three of us will overwhelm him. Once we control that princess Margaret, this war will be over.” Eden clenched his staff, eager for the fight.

“I agree…” Robert stepped forward, accepting Eden’s proposal.

“Just one person? Wonder if he’s tough enough?” Laurie cracked his knuckles, ignoring the knights glaring around them.

“Your Highness, retreat!” Blaze adopted a defensive stance, his expression grave. “I can barely handle Robert as it is. Now there are two more dangerous enemies—if I can’t protect you…”

Margaret heard Blaze’s words and felt a pang of unease. This usually straightforward knight had always been honest and fearless, never hesitating in battle. For him to say he couldn’t protect her was the first time.

Margaret understood Blaze’s tension and stepped back obediently, watching his back. “Give it your all. Survive.”

“Understood!” Blaze replied without turning around.

The three enemies moved at once, like starving wolves in the forest, surrounding the isolated Blaze, ready to feast.

The imperial knights watching couldn’t stand by any longer. If Margaret died, the empire’s defenses would crumble, leaving them leaderless and vulnerable to the vampires’ slaughter. They roared, drawing their weapons and charging forward, each becoming a gladiator who scorned death.

“Get out of my way!” Laurie’s golden battle energy surged into his fist, crushing a line of knights in a single strike.

The sheer power of that punch made the loyal knights realize the vast gap between Saint-tier warriors and ordinary foes.

“Guhhh!” Blaze roared, raising his greatsword’s blade. His massive frame, wrapped in battle energy, became a rolling war chariot.

Robert and Laurie struggled to shake Blaze’s strength, barely dodging his crushing sword strike.

“Hmph!” Eden coldly snorted, her staff blazing as dozens of black chains shot out, binding Blaze and restricting his wild sword attacks.

Seizing the chance, Laurie lunged, slamming a fist into Blaze’s abdomen, sending him crashing to the ground.

Robert didn’t lag behind, his battle energy forming a razor-sharp blade as he slashed toward Blaze’s neck, aiming to take his life.

But in that instant, Blaze unleashed an unimaginable surge of power. Golden battle energy erupted like a tsunami, soaring into the sky.

“You filthy bastards! All of you die!”

Blaze’s body glowed fiercely, as if transformed into a monstrous golden giant, unleashing his peak Saint-tier might. The sight was terrifying.

Eden’s face paled—this was no ordinary fight. The enemy was fighting desperately, and they couldn’t afford to provoke him.

Blaze howled, his massive sword whirling in devastating slashes—horizontal and vertical cuts, just like the Cross Slash he’d used against Beelzebub.

A colossal golden cross, radiating enough force to sweep through armies, pressed down on the three of them, aiming to finish them all at once.

This was Blaze’s signature move, one he’d used to defeat countless stubborn foes. If not backed into a corner, he’d never waste his energy on this exhausting technique—his battle energy was already dangerously depleted.

Eden and Laurie felt genuine fear. With their strength, they couldn’t block the golden Cross Slash, nor could they hope to—

At that moment, Robert boldly stood before the brutal attack, fingers forming a blade as he slashed downward.

Time seemed to freeze for a second as the oncoming golden cross shattered like glass.

Robert raised his arm, expressionless, staring at Blaze. “My strength isn’t weaker than yours. You think you can take out all three of us in one breath? I’ve said before—your battle energy usage is too crude, and you’re easily exploited, just like now…”

A sharp *snap*—Blaze’s arm was severed at the elbow, blood gushing from the clean wound.

Blaze’s face turned pale, staring at his stump. Sweat trickled down his forehead—he didn’t utter a word.

“Die!” Laurie charged, punching Blaze’s abdomen, shattering his ribs and spraying blood.

Eden swung her staff, and black thorns materialized, piercing Blaze’s back, making further resistance impossible.

“Ugh…” Blaze groaned in pain, collapsing to his knees, clearly defeated.

“Blaze!” Margaret screamed, her heart racing. Was she about to lose another loyal subordinate?

Robert approached the kneeling Blaze, raising his blade with a pitying tone. “It’s over…”

title: Chapter 46 — One Sword, Three Kills (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 46 — One Sword, Three Kills (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 19 · Chapter 46

As Robert's qi-infused blade was about to fall, Margaret hurried over in a panic, trying to stop it.

Before a Saint-tier powerhouse, Margaret was as weak as an ant; she could only frantically raise her firestone gun.

Yet against a powerhouse like Robert, the firestone gun was laughable—like a toy that could be ignored.

At the critical moment, a graceful shadow descended from the sky, her pale purple hair dancing as she forced Robert back with a sharp sword.

"Who?!" Robert hastily stepped back, irritated that someone had ruined his plans.

Mesfield resisted the duration of Merlin's saliva effect and recovered, coincidentally returning at this moment, once again radiating the radiance of the First Knight and boosting the morale of the empire's soldiers.

"Phew, I thought you'd actually be brave enough not to come back," Cladi exhaled, holding a tattered wand and walking slowly into the arena, his ragged clothes slightly disheveled.

"Hey! Lord Blaze! Are you alright?" Mesfield lowered her head to check Blaze's wounds.

...Blaze's injuries were no ordinary severity; his consciousness was already fading, unable to speak at all. In a daze, seeing Mesfield's face, he suddenly broke into a silly smile, probably thinking he had reached the Pure Land and could fulfill his dying regrets.

Robert steadied himself, saw two knights from Britain, and felt no great fear, even sneering, "Oh~ So it's Britain's First Knight lady, you're also butting in?"

"Humans are inherently allies, jointly resisting your kind of monsters—that's not butting in." Mesfield gently set down Blaze, stood up, and said seriously.

"Hmph! What a human alliance—it's all just trading for their own benefit!" Eden laughed coldly.

"Shh! Stop talking nonsense, it's just one more lamb to the slaughter. Kill her like before." Eden stepped forward.

"Better be a bit careful—the Thorn Knights both have some skill; don't capsize in the gutter." Robert felt that with two Thorn Knights here, they needed to be extra cautious.

"This female knight is about on par with that brute earlier—what's there to fear? You can take her down yourself, right?" Larry thought the warrior who could condense qi into a sword was formidable; at minimum he was at Saint-tier peak, equal to the Guild Master.

"Strength +1000%"

"Critical Damage +1000%"

"Attack Range +1000%"

"Defense Penetration +1000%"

"Pierce Effect +100%" =

"Adds special lightning attribute attack.

"Adds Storm Boots special domain.

"Adds special enchantment causing aftershock on attack.

Cladi kept "popping" his fingers, his wand flashing repeatedly as a string of ten-fold amplification buffs released, all stacked on Mesfield alone.

Margaret beside them was completely stunned, her mouth forming an "O" shape, unable to close it for a while. Though she sensed Cladi wasn't weak, she had never seen him display his power—he was actually a mighty support father?

Each BUFF had ten-fold amplification power—no ordinary small cleric could do that!

Clearly Cladi wasn't an ordinary support master, but a super support who could hard-lift a weakling into a powerhouse!

Of course, Mesfield wasn't a weakling either; for her, Cladi's support magic was the ultimate icing on the cake!

Don't look—Mesfield's power, even after all these amplifications, was still only Saint-tier peak, but her combat strength could fully rival a Zong-tier expert!

Mesfield held her sword in one hand, her eyes sharp as she felt explosive power surging through her whole body, radiating a peculiar brilliance.

No wonder the teacher's support magic was so powerful—she felt she could even defeat the Elgin Great Swordmaster now. Was that an illusion?

Mesfield loosely clenched her palms a few times; the feeling of fullness was wonderful, making her very happy.

"Sorry, what were you saying just now? I didn't catch it—could you repeat it?" Cladi revealed a meaningful smile.

"Larry didn't dare speak further. Before, he was confident of beating Mesfield, but now with so many BUFFs on her, who would dare say they could win?

Eden's expression turned grave; looking at Cladi, his eyes were tense. "That magician is extraordinary—possessing support magic of such immense amplification. He's definitely not to be trifled with. Look at that female knight... her pressure already rivals the Guild Master in life-burning state.

Robert felt a trace of fear; his intuition told him the buffed female knight was dangerous and couldn't be fought by force!

Seeing the opponents behave, Cladi lowered his voice, "Windsor, go take them down. Let them feel the depth of Britain's history—"

Mesfield's gaze was piercing; she instantly flashed before the enemies, too fast for all three to react.

"Damn! So fast!" Robert widened his eyes, wanting to flee, but it was too late!

"Farewell!" Mesfield roared, and her sword slashed down!

Boom—

A thunderous roar shook the entire royal city.

Sand and gravel blasted a hundred meters into the sky, lightning flashing toward the heavens!

Margaret stared at the wandering lightning, a trace of fear for Great Britain taking root in her heart.

The ripples dispersed; Eden and Larry's bodies turned to ash, while Robert's corpse was charred beyond recognition.

Mesfield slowly descended from the air, frowning as she looked at the vampires still howling in the sky. That powerful strike still couldn't wipe out the monsters—only kill nearby enemies.

Yet with just one sword, instantly killing three Saint-tier enemies, Mesfield was already satisfied—it was her personal best.

"Windsor, how do you feel? Recovered?" Cladi walked over to ask.

"Fine, I'm in great shape now." Mesfield's face flushed red, recalling her embarrassing state earlier; she was lucky Cladi hadn't noticed, or it would be humiliating.

After the small victory, Robert's charred corpse's mouth suddenly opened, and an ugly small vampire crawled out.

He was Robert's true form—a small vampire parasiting inside a human body.

Thanks to this ability to lurk in human flesh, he could live like a human under the sun.

After crawling out, the small vampire saw the knights cheering and no one noticing it, so he joyfully began to flee.

But he hadn't gone far when a gunshot rang out, a silver steel bead piercing his forehead.

The small vampire instantly widened his eyes in horror, turning to look at Margaret holding the firestone gun in surprise, before collapsing into ash.

"Phew..." Margaret put down her gilded firestone gun, elegantly blowing away the smoke from the muzzle.

"Hmph, dog, go to hell with Mesfield..."

title: Chapter 47 — Great Evolution Art
content:
Chapter 47 — Great Evolution Art

Volume 19 · Chapter 47

In the secret basement near the palace, the hesitant blood clan launched a massive assault on the city, causing the defenses here to be much weaker than usual.
At this moment, on the ground lay dozens of imperial soldiers' corpses, each killed instantly by a single gunshot to the head.
Obviously, this defensive force cannot stop Dickteping's invasion.
In the deepest secret chamber, the deceased host Bartirolka was sealed in a culture vessel, the flames burning on his body having weakened considerably, the remaining flame flickering constantly in the darkness.
Dickteping slowly walked up to the culture vessel, looking at Bartirolka's corpse, his eyes constantly flashing with fervor.
He hopes to obtain this power; as long as he becomes the new host of the flame demon, his strength will surely increase dramatically, and perhaps then he won't be so pathetic, being led around by others.
Seizing the flame demon is merely one link in Dickteping's plan; this selfish and self-interested man will never let go of anything that benefits him.
His greatest goal, however, is to control the deity sealed in the bottle that Dracula spoke of; then, by wielding this unique power, what could he not obtain? It would be an extraordinary might!
Therefore, Dickteping needs to find that black-haired girl with a suspicious identity and then do everything possible to control her.
Dickteping followed Merlin and Alice-lu, learning far more than he imagined; he knew the little girl was not with them, but was being looked after by an old adventurer, and as long as he found them, everything would be under his control.....
The greedy Dickteping, looking at Bartirolka in the culture vessel, suddenly chuckled and said:
"Your host is too weak; why not join me? SF light novel"
After saying that, Dickteping smashed the glass of the culture vessel, and the scalding liquid spilled out all over the place.
He carefully extended his hand and touched Bartirolka's corpse, which still burned with flame.
This weak flame seemed to have a life of its own; at the moment Dickteping touched it, it suddenly became extraordinarily vigorous, raising the temperature of the entire basement to an astonishing degree.
"Come on! I am your new master! Come devour me as you please! ?"
As Dickteping's mad roar rang out, the blazing flames separated from the lifeless Bartirolka and transferred onto Dickteping's body.
Faintly flickering with a crimson light, the flames instantly engulfed Dickteping, continually tormenting his body.
However, the vampires' formidable regenerative ability came into play at this critical moment.
One could see Dickteping constantly on the verge of death in the flames, his body scorched beyond recognition, yet he continually regenerated new flesh, maintaining the solemnity of his life—
"I can do it!"
"I am not weak!"
"I will completely control you!!"
At the palace, the crisis of the three powerful vampires launching a joint assault has passed, but the situation remains somewhat unfavorable.
The defensive line formed by the soldiers and knights has become precarious, increasingly unable to withstand the vampires' charges, the formation continually shrinking until they reached a predicament with no escape.
After Margaret killed the traitor Robert, she went to Blaize's side, saw his severe wound, and her heart couldn't help but become anxious.
Moreover, there is no priest to be found for help with treatment; what can we do?
If this continues, Blaize is very likely to die.
Margaret lifted her head to see the sky filled with countless vampires howling; her heart turned cold, and there was absolutely no chance to escape.
"Lord Cladi, do you know healing arts?"
"It's a pity; I am skilled at enhancing others' magic, but I cannot heal.... Cladi shook his head, his tone very regretful."
"Your Highness need not worry; Lord Blaize is physically strong, this level of injury can still be endured; as long as we deal with the immediate trouble and find a priest to treat Lord Blaize, there is still time." Mersfield said seriously.
Margaret gave a helpless smile and said, "Do you think we can easily handle... the trouble at hand?"
"..... Mersfield was at a loss for words; he also lacked confidence in defeating so many vampires, and it was very likely that his fighting spirit would be worn down,... "It's better than passive defense, right? If we resist, there is still a chance; but if we don't resist, we are surely doomed to a dead end...."
Margaret lowered her head, involuntarily thinking of Merlin; at this critical juncture, this man who alone possessed the power to turn the tide, yet no one knows where he ran off to—not even a shadow can be seen.
"Where did Miss Mersfield go before? Perhaps she saw Merlin and Alice......"
"...." Mersfield hesitated, glanced at Cladi, not wanting to say he had been spying on others, so he spoke vaguely: "We encountered a formidable enemy on the road; as for those two adventurers, we didn't see them."
"..." Margaret furrowed her brows, becoming worried; she thought that if she had known earlier, she should have done everything to keep Merlin in the palace and live together with him; it's all because that washboard interfered!
"Don't worry, with Teacher Cladi here; don't look at how the defense has become precarious—soon those weak knights and soldiers will become formidable individuals capable of standing on their own, even being called the strongest army on land would not be an exaggeration...." Mersfield said with deep meaning.
"What do you mean?" Margaret puzzled.
Mersfield did not answer, raised his head toward Cladi, and said, "Teacher, can we?"
"Pretty much; as long as we can tear through the vampires' encirclement, we can win." Cladi nodded in response.
"Leave it to me!" Mersfield said, pounding his chest.OF牡J

title: Chapter 48 — Perfect Fusion
content:
Chapter 48 — Perfect Fusion

Volume 19 · Chapter 48

A massive golden magic array slowly rotated beneath the blood-stained, darkened royal city, shining like a sun igniting hope, dazzlingly brilliant.

The magic of the ancient ancestors was created to resist the oppression of the gods, and even today, it remains immensely powerful.

From just a few scattered clues, one could glimpse the tip of the iceberg of that ancient civilization and their fear in the face of the gods.

What kind of enemy could have forced them to create such a magnificent magic?

The Great Evolution Technique was not permanent, nor could it continuously bestow power. It required Kladi to constantly supply magic to maintain the enhancement of everyone.

At this moment, Kladi's face was slightly pale, clearly showing the immense toll the ancient magic was taking on him. But to protect the last line of defense of France, he had to endure.

Marguerite was too shocked to speak, experiencing for the first time in her life the joy of being a Saint-tier warrior. Her fists could shake the sky, her legs could shatter the earth!

...This was the feeling of a Saint-tier warrior? !

It was amazing! It felt as if she had merged with the heavens and earth...

Even the slightest breeze in the air could detect the presence of enemies!

To enhance ordinary people into Saint-tier warriors—this was something most would find hard to believe unless they saw it with their own eyes.

Marguerite looked up, gazing at Kladi who was activating the Great Evolution Technique with an appreciative look, and gained a new understanding of the distant Britannia across the sea.

Although France had a strong foundation and was not afraid of any force, the number of talents had already been left far behind.

The soldiers and knights stood within the golden magic array, feeling an endless surge of power within them, transforming from mere commoners into formidable warriors!

Beginner Saint-tier, intermediate Saint-tier, advanced Saint-tier—there were countless of them!

Even the rare peak Saint-tier warriors numbered in the thousands!

As long as they stood within the Great Evolution Technique's magic array, everyone could become a capable general!

Mesfield's strength, already enhanced by the previous reinforcement magic, was now further assisted by the Great Evolution Technique, pushing his power to the peak of the Ultimate Realm. His martial aura was almost colorless, having faded significantly.
