At once, the soldiers and knights were filled with fighting spirit, raising their weapons high and shouting the empire's slogan in unison, their voices rolling like thunder toward the darkened sky!

Although Kladi's individual combat ability was mediocre, with teammates, he became terrifyingly powerful.

Creating an army composed of Saint-tier warriors—such strength could probably rival the Burning Legion of Hell, showing how rare a strategic talent Kladi was.

"Winshia, end this quickly. My magic is limited, and the Great Evolution Technique can't last long. The rest is up to you!" Kladi said with a serious expression, his head beginning to throb and his vision filled with illusions. This was the side effect of using ancient magic, severely harming the caster's body.

"Leave it to me, teacher!"

Mesfield said seriously, leaping into the air and drawing her silver sword, engaging the fierce vampires in battle.

At this moment, the Britannian knight seemed to transform into an invincible goddess, charging into the center of the vampire encirclement.

With every swing of her sword, entire groups of vampires turned to ash, as easy as cutting melons and vegetables.

The Mesfield family's sword techniques were fierce, and her radiant sword was imbued with lightning attributes. This power... was almost tearing the sky apart!

The imperial soldiers were no less formidable, bursting with unprecedented combat power and launching a counterattack against the invading vampire legion, their swords cutting through their throats without hesitation.

What had been a dire situation was suddenly reversed by Kladi's efforts, turning into a one-sided massacre of humans against vampires. Victory was within reach!

"...So powerful, a support mage changed everyone! So powerful!" Marguerite's mind was blank, her mouth only uttering praises!

But suddenly, a deafening roar of "Boom!" echoed, and the ground beneath the royal city trembled.

A fierce blaze shot up into the sky, like a waking demon stretching its claws, roaring angrily at the heavens!

Marguerite's face paled as she looked toward the direction of the flames, "There... Oh no! Someone has stolen the Fire Demon!"

"What happened!? " Kladi was startled, watching the direction of the flames, and the Great Evolution Technique's magic array began to become unstable.

Marguerite was silent. The Fire Demon was becoming active again, clearly indicating someone had擅自 fused with it. But who could it be?!

The war came to a brief halt, both sides staring intently at the towering flames, sensing something terrifying emerging.

Footsteps echoed from the flames, and Diketping appeared before everyone, swaying unsteadily.

At this point, Diketping no longer had a human form, looking like a monster emerging from hell!

He was completely enveloped in flames, his body covered in molten-like scales, his eyes spewing fire, and sparks flying around him.

He had fiery red horns resembling a demon on his head, and his tail behind him moved like a red-hot whip.

Looking at his new form, Diketping suddenly let out a heart-wrenching laugh—

"Hahahahaha! Success! I, the chosen one, am truly a lucky child blessed by heaven!"

"...Perfect fusion. He has perfectly merged with the Fire Demon, completely controlling its power! His strength must be several times greater than the previous host!" Marguerite gasped in shock. The empire had tried for centuries to subdue the Fire Demon to no avail, yet this mysterious figure had somehow done it with his own willpower alone. It was incredible!

"So powerful a pressure. Winshia, even after multiple enhancements, is very strong, but her pressure is still not as great as his!" Kladi immediately felt the immense pressure of a mountain. The opponent's strength was beyond imagination!

Diketping had successfully suppressed the fierce Fire Demon. After the perfect fusion, he was no longer that mediocre Saint-tier warrior, but had directly upgraded to become a true peak Ultimate Realm boss, without relying on any enhancements!

Diketping pulled out his beloved revolver from behind, using his flames to boldly modify it, completely enhancing its quality, elevating it from rare to pseudo-legendary, greatly increasing his combat ability!

The originally ordinary revolver, after Diketping's modifications, became extremely exaggerated, resembling a demon's roaring head, crimson and spewing flames.

"I, Diketping, from this moment on, will begin a new life!

"Hey! Who are you, you arrogant fool! Die!" Mesfield roared, her pale golden swordlight piercing the sky, fiercely劈ing toward the dancing Diketping!

"Winshia! Don't be impulsive!" Kladi tried to stop her, the danger level was extremely high, but it was already too late.

Faced with the ferocious swordlight, Diketping smirked, raising his hand and firing a single shot at Mesfield—

The small gun barrel suddenly unleashed an unimaginably powerful firepower output!

The喷射ing flames, like hellfire, erupted with a loud炮-like sound!

Unparalleled firepower!

Unparalleled range!

Unparalleled爆发!

Even though Mesfield was very strong, she still seemed insignificant under Diketping's gun barrel, instantly engulfed by the flames and killed in one shot.

When the flames dissipated, Diketping moved his revolver to his mouth, blowing away the lingering smoke and sparks.

"I am the new master of the Fire Demon. I'm not the pitiful wimp who could be bullied by you before."

"Could... could you show me a little more respect, please?"

title: Chapter 49 — Springboard Plan
content:
Chapter 49 — Springboard Plan

Volume 19 · Chapter 49

Meisifelde, despite so many enhancements, was still no match for Diketeping after his perfect fusion with the Flame Demon.

Diketeping merely fired one shot, stripping Meisifelde of the ability to resist, then turned back as the scorched body fell from the sky!

At this moment, Diketeping's power surged; whether it was Medesi or Humphrey, the president of the Blue Ghost Flame, neither could be mentioned in the same breath as him.

Meisifelde fell like a meteorite, crashing heavily into the ground and sinking in, his body charred and gravely injured, his consciousness fading as he lost consciousness.

"Windsor!" Kaledi cried out, but he was maintaining the magic circle for the Great Evolution Technique and couldn't go check Meisifelde's injuries.

Marguerite stood there stunned, unable to speak. Meisifelde was already so powerful, yet he was defeated by a single shot. Was the enemy's power truly this terrifying? Even the previous host, Batiloka, couldn't achieve this level!

Diketeping seemed to have transformed into a flame demon, even containing the vampire's undead body. The fusion of the two powers gave him...

He stood alone under the pitch-black sun, a mocking smile on his face, as if everything happening was within his expectations.

"Originally I didn't want to bother with you all, but before I leave, I'll give you a gift."

Diketeping raised the Flame Demon Great Spear again, aiming at the sturdy defensive line composed of countless soldiers and knights. Terrifying Zongjing power was infused into it.

"Feel it well, and die slowly in despair!"

As soon as he finished speaking, "Boom!" The Flame Demon Great Spear fired again, shooting out a tongue of flame with terrifying heat; wherever it reached, not a blade of grass survived!

Apocalyptic flames swept across the battlefield; the empire's defense line, as solid as a rock, collapsed in an instant. The soldiers and knights who counterattacked were pierced through, casualties mounting...

These knights, empowered by Kaledi's Great Evolution Technique to become Saint-tier powerhouses, were utterly unable to withstand Diketeping's attack!

Kaledi's magic was broken, falling from a great height. Magic exhaustion left his body extremely weak; the counterattack rhythm he had barely established was instantly severed.

Without Kaledi's Great Evolution Technique, the empire's soldiers and knights were knocked back to their original forms, unable to resist the vampires' surprise attack, becoming fish to be slaughtered!

"Hehe... Diketeping put down the Flame Demon Great Spear, turned around and vanished, preparing to find Cain, sealed in the bottle, and enslave the true god."

"Lose...?" Marguerite's expression was blank, as if she had lost her soul, plopping down to her knees and lifting her pale face to look at the pitch-black sun—

"Must we really use the star-destroyer cannon and perish together with these monsters?"

"If... if we could tear open a huge star and see..."

Countless vampires blocked out the sky and sun, blocking Marguerite's view. They shrieked, flapping their membrane wings excitedly as they surrounded them.

Murderous sword qi destroyed heaven and earth; the solid ground was forcibly split open, revealing a bottomless abyss.

Under the devastation of Merlin's Sword Draw Slash, the terrain had changed drastically; within a hundred-li radius, not a single mountain remained, all flattened.

The ground beneath them turned into a web-like pattern of gullies; if one fell in, they might never reach the bottom, as if the world had undergone an apocalyptic baptism!

A single hair in the air began to regenerate—cells, muscles, nerve tissue, organs, systems—until Dracula's body, killed countless times, restored itself to pristine condition once more.

The entire regeneration process took only three breaths, comparable to a dead man regenerating and reviving at the speed of light; the efficiency was so fast it made one stare in astonishment!

Dracula inherited one-third of Cain's divine power; his undead body was very close to the level of a god, and would not be easily killed.

"Hehehe, the seventh slash. I told you, it's useless. You can't kill me!"

Merlin panted several times, feeling a trace of exhaustion, and dropped the Holy Silver Greatsword he was holding.

Although this weapon, gifted by Count Austin, was of average quality and couldn't withstand Merlin's power, it broke after a few uses.

Merlin had already unleashed seven Sword Draw Slashes in a row. Although he could kill this cockroach-like monster over and over, the enemy would always regenerate and revive each time.

Although Dracula couldn't beat Merlin, if this continued, Merlin would show signs of fatigue first, making it easy for the enemy to seize the opportunity.

"The seventh slash..."

Alice protected the unconscious Miranda, watching Merlin from over there and murmuring to herself.

An enemy that couldn't be killed completely with seven slashes—this was the first time!

No, to be precise, Dracula had died many times already, but what's with that pesky undead body?

Merlin had clearly torn the enemy into powder, yet the enemy always regenerated from nowhere, as if there were no limit...

Alice felt it was getting tough—the enemy was immune to silver, the sunlight was blocked, and all the key factors that could kill Dracula seemed to have been erased.

Although Alice really wanted to rush over and help, seeing how brutally Merlin and Dracula were fighting, she gave up on that thought; she probably couldn't provide any help.

Plus, Beelzebub's sister Miranda had fallen into a coma. Alice needed to take care of her here, so she could only watch from afar.

Merlin became annoyed, reaching for his Banri Garan again, looking like he didn't believe in evil, still wanting to attack Dracula.

"Hey hey hey, still not giving up? Silver weapons don't work on me; do you think other materials will?" Dracula flapped his membrane wings, hovering in the sky to mock Merlin for being unable to do anything about him.

"You're not strong, but your vitality is like a cockroach's—really annoying!" Merlin frowned, his disgust for Dracula had reached a new height.

"Anyway, you can't kill me. The royal city is about to be breached by me. You're blocking me now? Not even a shred of meaning..." Dracula said in a low voice.

"Shout! France doesn't concern me; I want your life!" Merlin made a face.

"That's a real pity..." Dracula burst out laughing; fighting Merlin gave him endless joy.

Merlin's windbreaker fluttered in the wind as he prepared to unleash another Sword Draw Slash, but suddenly someone patted his shoulder.

"Lucifer, move aside, I'll deal with it."

"...Beelzebub! You're awake?!"

Merlin was full of astonishment; he didn't expect that Beelzebub, whom he had knocked out, could still come over at such a time.

"You bastard, you hit really hard. My head almost got opened up." Beelzebub tore off his gray robe and bound it to the wound on his forehead to stop the bleeding.

"It's all your own fault. If you listened to me, there wouldn't have been so much trouble." Merlin replied calmly.

"Protecting my sister's safety is the top priority. Fortunately, she's safe now, so I can settle accounts with this bunch of bastards." Beelzebub paused and said seriously, "This boss leaves it to me to deal with. You've already slashed seven times with no obvious effect, so stop wasting time. If you don't target the enemy's undead body, you can never win."

"What do you mean 'leave it to you'? Looking down on me?" Merlin's brows furrowed.

"No, I'm just better at dealing with this vampire. You have more important things to do?" Beelzebub looked at Merlin and said, "We need the sun. Go chop that planet blocking the sun into pieces."

"What do you mean?" Merlin asked in confusion.

"Vampires fear silver and sunlight. This one before us is immune to silver, so the only way to kill him thoroughly is probably sunlight." Beelzebub lowered his head and whispered, "My attacks don't have moves that powerful, but you can—back then I saw the power of your full-force attack; destroying a star the size of a monthly ticket should be no problem."

"Too far. I can't reach it at all. Don't daydream." Merlin shook his head helplessly.

Beelzebub glanced at Merlin and tentatively asked, "If I give you a springboard..."

title: Chapter 50 — Journey to the Unknown
content:
Chapter 50 — Journey to the Unknown

Volume 19 · Chapter 50

A blue-white dragon shot up into the sky, flying straight toward the dark sun, and each tremor of its wings stirred up a fierce cold wind.

Alice transformed into the Frost Holy Dragon, carrying Merlin up to tens of thousands of feet in the air, like a blue-white meteor bursting with vitality from the ground!

At this point, Alice could freely transform into a dragon at will; her majestic body and beating dragon wings were awe-inspiring.

Beelzebub told Merlin that a “stepping stone” meant carrying him to fly to the maximum height that living beings can reach.

Then, using a flying object as a stepping stone, Merlin would leap again, reaching a distance unattainable under normal circumstances, possibly allowing his draw‑and‑slash attack to strike the huge celestial body blocking the sun.

Beelzebub needed to stall Juddracula, so the only one who could serve as the stepping stone was likely Alice, naturally taking on this heavy responsibility.

But Merlin had never done anything so crazy before; who knows what mysterious things lie beyond the maximum height that living beings can reach?

Therefore, this stepping‑stone plan carries great risk; Merlin might face something he has never seen before, and this unknown mystery always inspires fear.

The altitude at which normal creatures can fly is limited; once they reach the limit, any creature will feel dizzy, weak, etc., and eventually fall into a coma.

Merlin also didn’t know if he could stay conscious, but using Alice’s Frost Holy Dragon form as a stepping stone would surely let him reach an unimaginable height.

As Alice flew higher and higher, the land below became infinitesimally small; she could clearly see the world’s continental map, showing an oval shape, the land adsorbed onto the ocean, with France merely a tiny patch on it, and the surroundings began to plunge into pitch‑black darkness where one could not see their hand in front of their face.

With the rise in altitude, the temperature dropped to an unimaginable degree; if the Frost Holy Dragon itself did not possess extremely strong resistance to cold, she would have already passed out from freezing.

Even so, Alice in her Holy Dragon form still felt waves of discomfort, dizziness, and slight difficulty breathing, suggesting she could not ascend much further before reaching her limit.

Merlin stood on the dragon’s head, gripping its thick horn with one hand, joking, “I never imagined that one day you would become my mount.”

“Shut up, you bastard!” the Holy Dragon‑formed Alice rolled her eyes, angry enough to fling Merlin from her head, yet she still had the mind to joke, “If it weren’t for clearing out the vicious blood clan, I wouldn’t let you ride on my head at all! Hmph~!”

“Wow~!” Merlin said with a strange expression, teasing, “After you turn into a dragon, your voice automatically carries a reverb effect; it’s quite amusing.”

“G、U、N!” the Holy Dragon‑formed Alice bared her teeth, explaining, “Humans and dragons have different vocal organs; dragons produce sound from their abdomen, making their voices much richer than humans’.”

“By the way, are you clothed right now? Would turning into the Frost Holy Dragon leave you only able to be bare‑assed…?” Merlin stroked his chin, voicing his curiosity.

“....” Alice’s Holy Dragon form flushed red, thinking that dragons don’t wear clothes, so after her dragon transformation… according to human aesthetics toward dragons, she seemed indeed to be naked!

Merlin, seeing Alice silent, exclaimed in astonishment, “Could it really be that you’re bare‑assed? Even though your dragon form looks mighty, wouldn’t you feel embarrassed if the wind blew on your backside?”

“Oh ah! You filthy bastard, can’t you think of something normal?” the Holy Dragon‑formed Alice fumed, defending herself, “My mindset is human; I see dragons as not needing clothes, and besides, with thick scales, nobody can see anything, right? In this state, could you even see my breasts?”

“Well… even if you didn’t turn into the Frost Holy Dragon, you still couldn’t see any breasts at all…. Merlin furrowed his brows, completely unable to notice any change in Alice before and after.”

“Eeeee!!!” the Holy Dragon‑formed Alice, furious to the point of vomiting blood, spun wildly at high altitude, already regretting having carried Merlin on her flight.

“Don’t… don’t do this! Falling from this height is no joke!” Merlin clung tightly to the Holy Dragon Alice’s horn; under the strong centrifugal force, his features became distorted.

“Hmph! If destroying the huge celestial body weren’t so important, I would definitely have tossed you down!” the Holy Dragon‑formed Alice fumed, no longer continuing to act up.

“It’s just a flying lizard, what’s the big deal? The mount is still so…. Merlin rubbed his nose, wearing a look of disdain.”

“What did you say?! I’ll bite you to death! Even if you grovel with a thick‑skinned plea for mercy, I won’t let you go!” the Holy Dragon‑formed Alice bared her sharp dragon teeth; Merlin’s loud laughter could barely match her teeth.

“...” Merlin let out a laugh, patting the head of the Frost Holy Dragon beneath his feet, “All right, Alice, don’t push yourself further; you’ve already far exceeded your flight altitude limit, and if you keep going, your body could be torn apart by the forces between celestial bodies.”

“.....” The Holy Dragon‑formed Alice’s gaze shifted; her constant fussing was merely to distract Merlin’s attention, wanting to help him more by carrying him~ to fly higher.

But Merlin had already noticed Alice’s intention and stopped her from risking herself, which could possibly cause her to suffer as well.

At this height, one could see a sky thick with stars, as dark as a stage curtain, with meteors of various sizes drifting about.

Obviously, the Frost Holy Dragon’s altitude limit had been reached; her gem‑like sturdy scales were beginning to show a tendency to crack, and if Merlin hadn’t stopped her, Alice would truly have been prepared to shatter into pieces.

The Holy Dragon‑formed Alice had no choice but to stop flying; her attitude eased a bit, her eyes darting about, she fell silent for a moment and said.

“What? You noticed?”

“Of course, I’m not an idiot; I’ll handle this dangerous matter myself—you don’t need to come along. Getting me this far is enough.” Merlin sighed.

“I can still fly higher.” the Holy Dragon‑formed Alice said.

“No need; if you keep going you’ll be in danger, so let’s stop here. Next…. Merlin tightened the katana at his back, slowly lowered his body, assumed a jumping stance, “This is something I have to do alone!”

As soon as he finished speaking, Merlin used the Frost Holy Dragon as a springboard, took off from the spot, and flew toward the enormous celestial body at great speed.

The powerful impact caused space to tremble slightly; Alice felt as if she might faint from Merlin’s blow, and her body began to fall toward the earth.

Merlin then did something he had never done before; his heart held no anxiety, only a deep curiosity and excitement for the unknown.

He turned his gaze toward the falling Alice; her beautiful dragon body curled into a ball, and her eyes were fixed on him.

“Alice! Wait down there for me, don’t worry, I’ll be fine!”

“I know, I’ll wait for you, always waiting for you!”

title: Chapter 51 — Beelzebub's Stomach (Plus an Extra Update)
content:
Chapter 51 — Beelzebub's Stomach (Plus an Extra Update)

Volume 19 · Chapter 51

After transforming into a holy dragon, Alice slowly descended, her dragon wings folding together, preparing to withstand the impact of hitting the ground.
At such an altitude, even though Alice's body after dragon transformation is extremely hard, she would still suffer considerable injury.
Alice's golden eyes fixed on the ever-retreating Merlin, and she couldn't help but feel uneasy.
This plan is actually extremely dangerous; perhaps no one has ever ventured into the realm beyond the sky.
Just this altitude alone, Alice already felt a mysterious, powerful force emanating from the celestial bodies, almost tearing her body apart.
Who knows what terrifying tearing force Merlin will face if he continues deeper; I don't know if he can withstand it.
Only after Merlin's silhouette completely disappeared did Alice close her eyes, silently murmuring—
“Be careful, …”
Using the last foothold's power, Merlin shuttled through the silent meteor shower of stars, continually approaching the enormous celestial body.
But that tearing force from beyond the sky began to strengthen; even though Merlin's body was extremely tough, his nose still slowly trickled blood.
It seems even Merlin, wandering beyond the sky, cannot emerge unscathed; he is clearly affected significantly.
On the ground it felt nothing, but upon approaching, one could realize how enormous this sun‑blocking celestial body is.
Merlin before this celestial body…
He is merely dust, too tiny to be seen.
On the ground, Dracula and Beelzebub were locked in combat, each move deadly, the battle somewhat stalemated.
Dracula drew his long blood‑colored whip, and with a fierce swing it split the earth open like a thunderbolt, leaving horrifying fissures!
This vampire progenitor not only possesses formidable immortality, but his combat ability is equally strong, able to match the demon lords!
Like thunder, his blood‑red whip easily shattered mountains into rubble, hurtling straight toward Beelzebub!
Revealing his true Demon Lord form, Beelzebub's combat power surged; he flapped his cicada wings, not retreating but advancing, withstanding Dracula's frontal assault head‑on, then shot a black‑red beam from his fingertips!
Dracula's eyes widened as Beelzebub's counter‑blast pierced his chest, creating a black hole the size of a head.
A normal person receiving such grave injury would surely die, but Dracula merely smiled calmly, and the wound began to heal in the blink of an eye.
“Not bad for a demon lord; you're truly not ordinary strong, though your power compared to that just‑mentioned… seems to have a considerable gap.”
Beelzebub's two fly‑like huge eyes flickered repeatedly; he personally felt how troublesome the opponent was—not that he couldn't win, but that he couldn't kill him!
“Hmph! Your mouth is far stronger than your actual ability…”
“Is that really the case?” Dracula narrowed his eyes, probing, “You came alone to face me? Where did that young Demon Lord go? Did you know you were bound to lose, so you sent him fleeing first? I don’t recall demons having a habit of protecting their young…”
“How laughable! We are the demon kings; do we need to flee to deal with you? For countless ages we have faced the heavenly gods’ suppression, yet we have always resisted without retreating a step—you, a mere cockroach, are not worth mentioning!” Beelzebub spoke haughtily, clearly not taking Dracula seriously.
“What’s there to be proud of for a group that hides in its homeland?” Dracula chuckled, shaking his head, pointing at the sky, “Even if you don’t say it, I can guess: that young Demon Lord intends to destroy the celestial body blocking the sun, right?”
……Beelzebub gave no answer.
“Anyone could figure that out with a little thought, but let me tell you…” Dracula cracked his grotesque grin and sneered, “All your efforts are futile! This celestial body is moved by means of an ancient altar and divine power pulling it; for the young Demon Lord to destroy it, he would need world‑destroying power, otherwise he couldn’t budge it even a fraction. If it were a god, I’d believe he could accomplish such an unthinkable feat, but sadly it isn’t, so your actions are utterly worthless.”
“Who knows…” Beelzebub said expressionlessly, “Even if he can’t do it, I have the ability to kill you completely.”
“Oh? Then give it a try!”
Dracula soared into the air, swinging his blood‑colored whip, and a spectacular pool of blood surged up from his feet! s
The blood pool shot up to the heavens, forming a massive blood tsunami, momentum incomparable!沉
Suddenly, the blood tsunami transformed, morphing into countless blood‑colored giant drills, as if alive, they surged toward Beelzebub and began to grind!
Beelzebub relied on his tremendous speed to dodge repeatedly, but the blood drifts were too numerous and their attack range too wide to avoid.
Imagine a tiny fly trying to escape a raging tsunami—obviously impossible; Beelzebub was slammed onto the rock, countless blood‑colored drills striking him head‑on.
“Urrrraaaah!” Beelzebub’s blackened body became riddled with wounds under the assault, pierced in several large spots.
“Hahaha, what demon lord? Your strength is nothing more than this!” Dracula burst into wild laughter.
Beelzebub gave a bitter smile, lying on the ground and said with deep meaning, “Do you think only you possess divine power? In ages past, divine power could be obtained through cultivation; it so happens that for us demons to become lords, having divine power is merely a threshold!”
“Are you joking? Divine power can only be granted; how could one achieve it through self‑cultivation?” A bead of cold sweat trickled down Dracula’s forehead.
“Thank me! Let you witness the capital of demons versus the heavens—I haven’t used it in ages; I originally intended to use it against Lucifer, but I never imagined I’d use it on you, this cockroach.” Magical power surged over Beelzebub, not gold, not pale gold, but pure white—“Don’t blink.”
Buzz buzz buzz, a dense swarm of flies erupted explosively from Beelzebub’s body, spreading outward and engulfing everything—even Dracula couldn’t escape.
When Dracula opened his eyes again, what lay before him was no longer the original world, but the interior of some monster’s body, the walls pulsing with flesh, seemingly still alive?!
Countless tentacles extended from all directions, appearing extremely strong and powerful, covered with countless hideous mouths, continuously spewing caustic acid.
White insect eggs and maggots clung to the flesh walls, slowly crawling; ferocious man‑eating flies swarmed the sky like a plague, as if we had entered the nest of the man‑eating flies.
“This…”
Dracula froze, his face pale with fright, constantly looking around, sensing that something terrible was about to happen.
“What kind of… place is this?”
( A°))

title: Chapter 52 — Escape (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 52 — Escape (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 19 · Chapter 52

The independent small world before them was inside Beelzebub's body, capable of swallowing anything and melting it away.
This was not merely Beelzebub's body, but a pseudo-divine secret technique he unleashed using divine power.
Beelzebub had trained his body into an independent space capable of annihilating any enemy; in this place filled with acid-spewing man-eating flies, no one could possibly survive.
Even someone as well-traveled as Dracula, upon being suddenly swallowed into Beelzebub's stomach, was stunned by the hellish sight before him.
Beelzebub's intention to use this pseudo-divine secret technique against Merlin was no joke; he had genuinely planned to kill Merlin with this move.
Although Merlin is immune to magic, the magic born of divine power can no longer be easily resisted.
The world's two major power systems are battle aura and magical power, while divine power transcends both, residing at a higher level.
Although Alice's fusion of battle aura and magical power counts as independent of the two systems and can break Merlin's magic immunity, it is still far inferior to divine power.
Recall the Dark Elf King's Eye atop the London clock tower; it indeed used magic to wound Merlin's flesh, confirming the rumor that the Dark Elf King inherited the power of the elven god Corellon.
In ancient times, those who wielded divine power were called pseudo-gods; even after several epochs, they still exist as a rare few.
As an ancient race, the demons have faced the heavenly gods head-on and have not been utterly annihilated; how could they be a bunch of weaklings? They must have their own outstanding qualities.
For demons aspiring to become Demon Lords, mastering divine power is the basic threshold; otherwise they have no qualification to oversee a Demon Lord's palace.
Beelzebub differs from Dracula and the Dark Elf King; he became a pseudo-god through his own cultivation, step by step, not by inheritance or prayer.
In terms of experience, foundation, basics, and even the application of divine power, Beelzebub far surpasses Dracula and the Dark Elf King, who are akin to 'beggar-type' powerhouses!
“What the hell is this place?!?” Dracula cried, his legs going weak as the acid vapors filled the air with deadly poison; he could already see his own body slowly melting and rotting, white bones beginning to show.
“You’re inside my belly now—how is it? Isn’t it beautiful?” Beelzebub's voice echoed faintly, his true form nowhere to be seen.
“My flesh has only melted five… what have you done?!” Dracula's flesh was falling off in chunks onto the ground.
“This is my proud space magic, called Meat Purgatory, originally prepared to deal with heavenly spirits; I wouldn’t easily unleash it on humans. Lucifer III was the first little brat to make me want to kill, and I once thought letting him die in Meat Purgatory would not disgrace the title of the first king, but I never imagined… it would end up being used on you?” Beelzebub spoke with a tinge of disappointment, feeling Dracula unworthy of his own Meat Purgatory.
Dracula stared, his hands turning to white bone, yet still speaking firmly: “So what? I’m immortal! You can’t kill me!”
“Even if I can’t kill you, it doesn’t matter—you can never escape from here; you’ll be trapped in an endless cycle of corrosion, revival, and re‑corrosion. As long as you can’t get out, what’s the difference between that and death?” Beelzebub said with a mocking laugh.
“Impossible!” Dracula refused to believe, swinging his hand to create a huge blood‑colored blade; after slashing around, it could not harm the pulsing flesh wall—instead the blood‑colored blade shattered.
“Useless—this place was designed to kill heavenly spirits; how could it let them escape? Your power is nowhere near that of the legendary heavenly spirits, so don’t waste your effort.” Beelzebub said leisurely.
“You’ll never kill me!” Dracula repeatedly unleashed blood magic, assaulting the surrounding flesh walls, hoping to blast a breakthrough.
“Hmph, disappear, you insignificant wretch
As soon as Beelzebub finished speaking, the whole space seemed to receive a command and instantly became incredibly active.
Tentacles with mouths, spewing acid, frenziedly wrapped around Dracula’s body, hungrily gnawing at him.
The buzzing man‑eating flies were not to be outdone, swarming down from the sky in droves, bombarding Dracula and beginning to tear at him.
“Your corpse will be dissolved by the acid into nutrients, continually feeding my minions—this is probably your last worth.
Dracula, engulfed by the hungry tentacles, endless swarms of man‑eating flies, and the strong acid, gradually vanished from sight—
“No!!!”
Outside, Beelzebub patted his own belly, gazing at the pitch‑black sun in the sky, and sighed.
“It seems I don’t need that Lucifer fellow after all—I can handle this myself; truly an unnecessary extra step.”
At this moment Dracula had already disappeared—perhaps, as Beelzebub said, he was forever sealed inside the belly, enduring countless deaths’ agony.
Beelzebub never imagined his prized technique would be used on an opponent of Dracula’s caliber; it even felt like using a cattle‑slaughtering knife to kill a chicken.
But the fact was not as simple as Beelzebub thought; Dracula was not an easy foe to handle, and he was clever, always leaving himself a retreat.
In a corner behind Beelzebub, not long ago the ashes of Mades had been left with a small bottle.
With a bang, a strand of bright red blood shot out of the bottle, gradually forming organs and bones…
Dracula, who should have died in Meat Purgatory, eerily regenerated at this very moment!
Dracula unfurled his huge membrane wings on his back, came back to life, and launched a surprise attack from behind, lashing Beelzebub’s back with a vicious whip!
“…?” Beelzebub was shocked; his back was torn open by Dracula’s strike, his body nearly split in half—he never imagined this cockroach‑like vitality‑filled foe could actually escape from his Meat Purgatory!
In fact, Dracula had prepared beforehand; the vampire race possesses a bug‑like vitality—any single drop of blood can revive and regenerate.
So before the war began, Dracula had infused his blood into the bottle and given it to Mades, just in case he met with mishap, allowing him to instantly come back to life.
Although the divine power bestowed by Cain is extremely potent, and immortality puts one in an invincible position, Dracula was not foolish enough to place complete trust in it.
Having just been locked inside Meat Purgatory, Dracula was in a death‑certain state, yet he still used his prior preparation, employing the blood in the bottle outside to revive and regenerate, thereby evading the killing move.
Beelzebub lay on the ground, the spot on his back where he’d been struck exposing white bones—clearly bearing Dracula’s attack was taxing him.
Dracula lunged onto Beelzebub’s back, grabbed the demon lord’s proud head and slammed it hard onto the ground, speaking in a triumphant tone—
“You thought I was dead?
“Huh?
“I’m here to tell you—I’m not dead, and I’m doing just fine!”
“Heheheheh…”

title: Chapter 53 — Extreme (Update: More Chapters Coming)
content:
Chapter 53 — Extreme (Update: More Chapters Coming)

Volume 19 · Chapter 53

Beelzebub widened his eyes, having suffered considerable injury; that Dracula could escape from his own pseudo-divine secret art truly shocked him.
"Hahaha, what's wrong? Can't you believe your own eyes?" Dracula revealed a ferocious smile, firmly pressing Beelzebub's head so he couldn't move.
"Shout!" Beelzebub flared up in anger, "You're really astonishing—actually managing to escape from my body; I have to praise you for that."
"Did you think I wouldn't anticipate possibly falling into a desperate situation? I haven't become so arrogant that my mind is addled." Dracula said in a teasing tone.
Beelzebub furrowed his brow, veins bulging all over his body, trying to break free from Dracula's control.
"Stop meaningless resistance!" Dracula roared, using great power to ruthlessly suppress Beelzebub, "You've lost. Take a good look at the royal city below, completely surrounded—France has fallen, and the empire of our bloodline is about to be established. What deep grudge do you demons have against me that you'd go to such lengths to stop me?"
"An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth—that is the creed of us demons. Because you dared to kidnap my sister, you won't get off easily."
Beelzebub angrily retorted.
"Isn't your sister still alive? We haven't done anything to her; at most we gave her some superficial wounds. You could just take her and leave, letting us not interfere with each other, alright?" Dracula hoped Beelzebub would abandon his resistance, otherwise the fight might never end.

"Just letting her suffer some superficial wounds, I should have killed you countless times!" Beelzebub turned his head, glaring at Dracula, "I've never laid a hand on her, yet you treat her as a slave; if you don't die, my hatred will never fade."
"You're like a never-ending plaster, we've already won, you can't possibly defeat me completely, what else do you want? That powerful move you just used—surely you can't unleash it twice in a row?" Dracula's smile turned contemptuous.
"You really think you've already won?" Beelzebub narrowed his eyes, speaking with deep meaning, "I feel your doom has arrived. That brat Lucifer III may be young, but his power is enough to destroy that troublesome celestial body; your dream of building a new kingdom will ultimately come to nothing."
"Hahaha..." Dracula laughed, covering his forehead, sneering, "What? So you've placed your hope on that young arrogant demon lord? Let me tell you, daydreaming! That celestial body will permanently block the sun over France; no one can destroy it. Before it, humans are mere insignificant specks, not worth mentioning."
"Hmph!" Beelzebub snorted coldly, speaking calmly—
"Have you ever seen that guy's limit? Actually, his usual power can only unleash a tiny fraction."
"This world simply lacks a stage capable of bearing his power; he's constantly suppressing himself."
"If that little brat were to go all out, probably everything would cease to exist."

Many years ago, Merlin had just slain the demon great noble, reclaiming his mother Vivian's demon lord throne to avenge past humiliation.
He also successfully drew the demon sword Banri Garan, the symbol of authority for successive arrogant demon kings, proving his legitimate status.
Immediately, Merlin used iron-fisted methods to suppress the rebels of the First Demon Lord Palace, even beheading several elders and commanders from Vivian's era.
After retaking command of the First Demon Lord Palace, leading the seven demon legions, and promoting seven trusted aides to great generals, young Merlin momentarily outshone all in the demon race!
Many demons knew that the First Demon Lord Palace had undergone a tremendous change—Vivian's son, who lacked demonic traits and was considered a defective product, had returned alive from the Despair Grand Canyon of the Death Marshes!
The Despair Grand Canyon of the Death Marshes is famed as a place of certain death, a demon's graveyard, filled with unknown secrets and dangers; demons who enter to challenge themselves have never emerged alive.
In the demon era, the original Lucifer and the holy spirits, although they barely won, also suffered severe injuries. To secure a path to survival, he alone ventured into the Despair Grand Canyon, and never came out again.
From then on, unless a demon was desperate enough to seek death, no one would dare approach that place; even as mighty as the original Lucifer couldn't get out, and who knows what lies inside?
And Merlin!

This prince, mocked as a good-for-nothing who only eats and waits to die, was created by Vivian using succubus power—a male infant lacking demonic traits. From the very beginning he faced criticism, and many demons privately called him a defective product.
Yet this unlucky fellow actually walked out alive from the Despair Grand Canyon where even the original Lucifer perished, and gained unstoppable power!
Although the draw‑and‑slash skill is showy but insubstantial, in Merlin's hands it was reborn; with a single draw‑and‑slash, no one survives, defeating each obstacle in turn.
This matter quickly caused a sensation among the demons; even the council composed of elders had to take notice, beginning to acknowledge Merlin as the new master of the First Demon Lord Palace.
However, for Merlin to officially become Lucifer III and inherit the title of the Arrogant Demon Lord, he still needs the acknowledgment of the other six demon lords—namely, to demonstrate his strength and make the other demon lords submit.
The Death Marshes, far from the seaside of the First Demon Lord Palace—
Waves of sea breeze blew in, under a cloudless sky, gulls skimmed the sea surface, their claws tracing ripples.
Merlin stood alone on the beach, silently fingering the katana at his waist, his back to everyone, unknown what he was thinking.
"All six monarchs have already gathered; I wonder if the young master can win their hearts and minds?" Ophelia, slender and dressed in a maid outfit, looked around, finally fixing her gaze on Merlin's back, showing a hint of infatuation. "If the young master fails to satisfy the six monarchs, the council might not recognize him as the legitimate heir; that would be troublesome..."
"Ophelia sister, what are you saying again? My brother is the only demon in history who has walked out alive from the Despair Grand Canyon; his strength is undoubtedly the greatest, perhaps even surpassing that old man, the original Lucifer." Lilith furrowed her small brows, unconvinced, saying, "Since my brother returned, how many old‑fashioned buffoons has he defeated? Isn't that enough to prove he has awakened?"
"Your Majesty's bearing is indeed admirable; I'm just a little worried...." Ophelia lowered her head slightly.
"Don't worry, these demon lords are all proud, but Merlin brother will make them submit." Lilith proudly lifted her head.
"I hope so; since the young master aims to become the new demon lord, he surely needs a queen, right? I wonder who he'll choose?" Ophelia's face flushed red, she thought bluntly—
"This isn't nonsense! Of course I should be chosen! The young master was raised by me from infancy to adulthood; if he doesn't pick me as his queen, it would be against heavenly principle!"
"...Yeah, I also don't know who Merlin brother will pick as his other half; I guess it'll be someone close to him?" Lilith's cheeks flushed, her heart likewise fluttering—
"Need to ask? Of course it's me!"
"Could my brother have someone closer than me? I am absolutely the best candidate to become his queen!"
"Can a blood‑related sister not be allowed, just because we're fated to be a pair and monsters still dare to oppose?"

title: Chapter 54 — Strange Demon Lords (Extra)
content:
Chapter 54 — Strange Demon Lords (Extra)

Volume 19 · Chapter 54

Six demon lords gathered here to witness Merlin's power.
It's truly a rare sight for several top-tier demons to gather together.
After all, demon lords cannot easily leave the Demon Lord Palace, and their relations are so-so; it's almost impossible for them to gather.
But this time, to observe the new demon lord's strength, even those who usually refuse to move have come here, breaking their habits.
The demon lords need to carefully observe Merlin, to see if he has the ability to become the master of the First Demon Lord Palace; the main point is whether his strength passes the test.
If his strength is lacking, the Holy Church's paladins could easily breach it, and then Merlin would not be worthy of protecting a demon lord's palace.
The demon lords vary greatly in form, all looking like weirdos, seemingly none of them normal—
The beautiful cross-dressing lust demon king Mesphild, and the bone-thin gluttony demon king Beelzebub, both wore blank expressions, intently staring at Merlin ahead.
On the left is a little dwarf, wearing expensive silk clothes, a small vest over it, the tie on it neat and proper, looking like some young master from a wealthy family.
But don't underestimate this young, petite shota; he is the largest-bodied demon lord, a monstrous beast capable of overturning rivers and seas, the envy demon king Leviathan.
Leviathan is the sea beast that connects heaven and earth; with each breath he can move the oceans, causing massive tsunamis. In a sense, his control over water elements makes him Merlin's nemesis.
On the right is a fat man, his bulky body making movement look laborious; he dresses exquisitely, his body covered in gold and jewels, his hair neatly combed, resembling a country gentleman.
He is also a remarkable figure among the demon lords, possessing many treasures and being a greedy demon merchant, the avarice demon king Mammon.
Mammon is the wealthiest among the demon lords, his power not to be underestimated; most importantly, his treasures—he intends to collect the legendary divine weapons, and it's said he even holds a true artifact in hand!
The two demon lords behind are much more low-key; they hardly speak at all, just quietly observing.
The most obvious one is a burly man wearing heavy, rust-streaked armor, his limbs bound with shackles, his face hidden, and he wears a helmet resembling a beer keg.
Such a bizarre outfit, plus his height like a twenty-foot small giant, makes the demons look over curiously, their eyes filled with respect.
This big guy represents the wrath demon king Samael, a rare fallen angel among the demon race; in power, perhaps only Leviathan could match him a little.
As for the low-key old man at the back, he is likely the demon race's living fossil, an ancient monster existence, the sloth demon king Belial.
Belial has white hair, yet wears a suit; a bright rose on his chest makes him look like an old gentleman, with no hint of sloth or laziness, but rather full of vigor.
Dooksta
As the Sloth Demon King, the sole surviving first-generation demon lord after the heavenly holy war, his status among demons is exalted; even the council of elders would give him respect.
Belial is very old, having been born in the age of gods, surviving across several epochs to the present; it's a pity he knows little about that era, for back then he was merely an infant in swaddling clothes.
It's hard to imagine just how strong this old monster's power has become; perhaps his usual low profile hides it, but faintly there is the voice of the strongest among the demon race.
"What the hell? That young brat is Vivian's son?" Mammon said, his eyes strange, staring at Merlin's distant back.
"That's right." Asmodeus nodded in response.
"He doesn't look like much, huh? I heard he's a defective product born from Vivian's succubus power, his demon blood thin; seeing him in person, it's really like that—I initially thought a human had mixed in." Mammon's chubby face twitched, he looked down on Merlin.
"I think the same; although he's Vivian's son, what power did he inherit? I see none at all—how can such trash be qualified to be the new master of the Demon Lord Palace?" Beelzebub closed his eyes, refusing to watch Merlin's display.
"Just look, even this sis-con pervert thinks so; I think we came here for nothing today." Mammon twirled the golden decree in his hand.
"Tch! Are you insulting me? You fat bastard, wanna die?" Beelzebub's eyes narrowed, he glared at Mammon.
"Hmph, foolish; I'm well-built, unlike your skinny, ugly self—you wouldn't understand this beauty." Mammon lifted his belly, almost popping his buttons.
"You fat bastard, you came here to fight, right?" Beelzebub's eyebrows furrowed.
"Why do you two always argue when you meet? Can't you be a little more patient?" Leviathan, this young shota, idly glanced at his nails, saying, ""Vivian values her son so much; he must have something extraordinary. This brat becoming a demon lord at such a young age truly makes me feel... jealous...."
"That's right; I actually think highly of him. A few days ago in the garden, he even brought me flowers to express his affection—if I weren't a guy, I might have not been able to resist accepting them." Asmodeus, holding a fan, gently stroked his peerless beauty, "Another young demon has fallen for my irresistible beauty, my sin deepens another layer, sigh...."
Beelzebub, Mammon, and Leviathan's faces all turned strange, looking at Asmodeus' eyes with a hint of chill.
Probably they feel deep regret for a fine young man being led astray by Asmodeus onto a no-return path.
"My lord... expressing affection to His Majesty Asmodeus? Impossible!?" Ophelia whispered in shock, feeling her queen's dream slipping away; Merlin would rather choose a man than her? Is there still royal law?!
"Exactly! How could my brother possibly like a man? It must be this disgusting guy making things up." Lilith flared up, hostile toward Asmodeus; originally many female demons had been eager for Merlin, now another male appears—damn it!
The two girls whispered and discussed, pressured by Asmodeus, they had to stay on guard, but they couldn't let the new master of the Demon Lord Palace take a strange path.
"Disgusting!" Samael muttered, his bulky frame matching his blunt, straight-to-the-point nature.
"Shout!" Asmodeus flicked his gaze, dissatisfiedly staring at Samael, "You coarse brute, how could you understand women's delicate beauty? You probably don't even know what elegance is. Don't you feel any stir for my beauty? If you feel even a little, you can express it—no shame, since countless demons have bowed under my pomegranate skirt, I myself can't even keep track...."
Samael remained unmoving like a mountain, his huge body seated cross-legged on the ground; compared to Asmodeus's refined elegance, he indeed seemed rather crude.
This wrath demon king seems not good with words; his speech is short and cold, yet each word is precious.
"Sorry."
"I don't understand."
"I vomit...."

title: Chapter 55 — Reappearance (Extra Chapter After 0:00)
content:
Chapter 55 — Reappearance (Extra Chapter After 0:00)

Volume 19 · Chapter 55

"Huh...?" Asmodeus's face was grim, and with nothing to say in response to Semel's scolding, he could only think to himself that no matter how he explained it, the concepts of beauty and elegance would be lost on this burly giant—like talking to a cow about music.

"....Beliel let out several yawns in a row, looking extremely tired. "I have to say, you youngsters are always messing around with all sorts of nonsense. With so much free time, why not try to improve your own strength? When the Goddess of Light sends the Holy Spirits to attack again, your current level... is simply not enough."

Upon hearing the lazy king speak, the other Demon Lords all fell silent, none daring to retort. Even though Beliel addressed all the Demon Lords as "young people," no one objected.

After all, Beliel was the eldest and had every right to speak. He was the sole original among the Demon Lords, and his status and authority were naturally the highest.

As the most senior Demon Lord, Beliel's words about the other Demon Lords being too weak to resist the Holy Spirits were probably not just idle boasts.

"...Asmodeus coughed lightly, turned his head toward Merlin, who was standing with his back to all the Demon Lords, and said, "He seems to have been preparing for this..."

"Hmph, I bet he's going to make a fool of himself." Mammon said with his jowls quivering.

"I don't think so. He's the one who can draw the demon sword Banri Garan. This blade was once wielded by our demons' prophet in slaughtering the gods—a sacred relic. Since this young man has been acknowledged, he's clearly no ordinary person." Asmodeus fanned himself with his fan, the breeze fluttering continuously.

"Shh, I think you're infatuated with this pretty boy! From the start, you've been on his side, praising him. No matter how much you flatter him, if his strength isn't up to par, he doesn't deserve to be the new master of the First Demon Lord Palace. Being acknowledged by Banri Garan has nothing to do with it." Belial stressed the rules of the demon race.

"I agree. According to legend, that blade in the hands of the prophet could undergo transformations, absorbing the life force of enemies to replenish itself, with the ability to sustain itself in battle. But after the prophet, Banri Garan never underwent any changes. Perhaps it's just that this defective blade got lucky." Mammon said with disdain.

"He's the only demon who managed to walk out of the Despair Grand Canyon alive. You talk big, but who among you dares to go in alone and try?"

Asmodeus shot back at the other Demon Lords, but everyone fell silent, pretending to look around at the scenery, probably because they had no confidence in entering the Despair Grand Canyon.

Merlin stood silently on the beach for a long time, listening to the sound of the waves crashing. Each time the seagulls in the sky passed over the surface, he could easily perceive them.

He was carefully controlling the power within his body, worried that if he lost control with full force, he would destroy the island beneath his feet.

Merlin had only just released the power of the draw-sword slash, and he couldn't control it perfectly yet. It was easy to go too light or too heavy.

Then, Merlin slowly opened his eyes, raised his right hand holding the long sword, lowered his stance, and assumed the posture for the draw-sword slash.

"Slash!"

bookSEACGo

With a furious shout from Merlin, the Banri Garan rang out of its sheath, its sharp sword energy like a wild beast breaking free from its cage, rushing forward with unstoppable force.

Merlin's gaze focused, gripped the sword tightly, and with firm suppression controlled the power. He lifted it high, then brought it down in a mighty slash!

The overwhelming slashing force began to rage, the shockwave spread across the sea, and the sky trembled with violent spatial distortion!

This slash wasn't simply cutting through the sea—it plunged straight toward the seabed, tearing into the deeper mysteries below.

The wind rushed past, the seawater split apart on both sides, flowing away in neat grooves. Suddenly, a stream of scorching magma erupted from the dark depths of the ocean!

Merlin held the sword against his shoulder, turned around gracefully, and looked at the other six Demon Lords, saying calmly,

"How's that? Still satisfied? This is only about one-tenth of my full power. If I don't hold back, I think I could destroy the continent on the other side of the Occult Strait..."

The six Demon Lords fell into silence, the air filled with a deathly stillness and awkwardness. It seemed they were all quite intimidated by Merlin.

Belial nervously swallowed, thinking, "One-tenth of his power? If he goes all out, he'll split the world in two! What a joke!"

Back then, Merlin was still young, and his control over the draw-sword slash was still immature. Yet the sea area before him was marked with a bold stroke on the navigators' maps.

The Occult Trench, later known as Lucifer's Abyss, lies 96,700 meters beneath the sea. It directly carved out a deep-sea cliff between the Dead Marshes and Great Britain.

This magnificent scar was left behind by Merlin's draw-sword slash. It's been plagued by storms and whirlpools year-round, and to this day, it remains uncalmed...

"Heh heh heh, you're really good at pretending to be calm," Dracula suppressed Belial, "Because your power is too strong, if you go all out, the world might collapse at any moment, so you've been holding back. That's... really taking it to a new level. Though that young Demon Lord is indeed awe-inspiring, hearing it from your mouth still sounds a bit too exaggerated!"

"Hmph, if you don't believe me, that's fine. It's not just you—I've never seen that guy go all out either..." Belial lay on the ground, speaking casually.

Dracula's expression darkened. He instinctively lifted his head and looked up at the sky, where a pitch-black sun remained motionless in place.

He couldn't believe anyone could destroy a celestial body the size of the moon in an instant. The sun of France had already completely disappeared...

It must be exaggeration, trying to throw me off balance.

If I believed such nonsense, I'd be completely out of my mind!

Destroying that massive star would surely be something only a god could do.

The age of gods has passed, and now there are probably very few who could be called gods still around...

Dracula's expression slightly softened, thinking the situation was still under control. But the next moment, he saw something that made his hair stand on end!

On the pitch-black sun, a thin line appeared, stretching at a visible speed, forming a clear crack!

"...What just happened? What's going on with that crack?!"

The pitch-black sun was split in two, and the massive star blocking the sunlight was truly being destroyed, breaking apart on both sides!

The sun, long hidden from view, finally shone its warm light again, bathing the dark and cold land in its radiance!

After a month without the sun in France, the land finally welcomed the warmth of sunlight. The evil vampires, exposed to the light, turned to ash with nowhere to hide!

Dracula's face twisted in rage, facing the sunlight, his undead body ignited with scorching flames, and he let out a cry of wonder from his soul,

"This can't be!

That guy......"

title: Chapter 56 — Ice Dragon Fall
content:
Chapter 56 — Ice Dragon Fall

Volume 19 · Chapter 56

The pitch-black celestial body that had blocked out the sun was split in two, cracking apart toward either side!

Brilliant sunlight poured through the gap, illuminating all of France.

Dracula wailed in agony, never having expected that Merlin would truly be able to destroy the massive celestial body and accomplish something nearly impossible!

Its body burned in the sunlight. Despite its immortality, it still couldn't escape the ancient fate of vampires under the sun, turning into ashes that scattered on the wind...

Bael slowly picked himself up from the ground, clutching his arm, and looked up at the spectacular sight of the giant celestial body being split open—

"I told you..."

"If he's really going all out, he'll definitely pull it off."

Within the royal castle, both Mersfield and Blaise were critically injured and near death.

The mass reinforcement spell, Grand Evolution, had also lost its effect, leaving the soldiers who had become vampires to the mercy of their own kind.

Clady's magical power was depleted, and the side effects of using ancient magic began to surface—severe headaches constantly pounding in his head, accompanied by frequent hallucinations.

Still, Clady struggled to crawl over to Mersfield's side and saw that his companion's burns were severe; he had already fallen into unconsciousness.

The legion guarding the royal palace was thrown into chaos. The counterattack momentum they had barely mustered was thoroughly shattered by the sudden appearance of the Dictator.

Soldiers and knights began dropping their weapons and armor, scattering in every direction, but they couldn't break through. They were repeatedly torn apart by vampires diving at them from the sky.

The Empire's defeat appeared to be irreversible, the declining tide becoming all too obvious—

Margaret looked at the utter devastation before her and felt a profound sense of powerlessness and exhaustion.

She felt that against such absolutely overwhelming strength, all her careful preparations had been useless. She seemed utterly fragile.

Unable to reverse the inevitably losing situation, Margaret simply raised her head and blankly gazed at the pitch-black sun in the sky.

"Merlin..."

Even in this despairing moment, Margaret thought of Merlin's figure, though she had no idea where he was at this very moment.

Even in a situation like this, she still believed Merlin would be the most likely hope to turn the tide. Perhaps right at the final moment?

Margaret silently clenched her fists and stared directly at the bloodsuckers shrieking wildly across the sky. This horde of monsters had grown bold and unrestrained as they dove down from above.

Such a vast swarm of vampires blocked Margaret's line of sight, making her feel a chill deep in her heart brought on by despair. There seemed to be absolutely no possibility of turning this around.

"Hmmmm..." Several vampires snarled and swooped down from the sky, heading straight for the dazed Margaret.

"Your Highness!" Clady cried out loudly, but the excruciating headache nearly made him faint.

"I suppose... I was thinking too much after all." Margaret closed her eyes, accepting her fate of death.

At this final moment, Margaret didn't have the heart to use the mysterious Star Destroyer and take the vicious vampires down with her.

While it would preserve the kingdom's dignity and spare them the humiliation of defeat, it would also reduce everyone on this land to a lifeless wasteland.

In the end, Margaret showed mercy and refused the massive sacrifice, choosing instead to accept defeat so that more people could survive.

The vampires fell upon her like a surging flood from the heavens, all jostling to be the first to sink their fangs into her throat.

However, just as those monstrous claws were about to touch Margaret, they inexplicably—all at once—turned to ash!

Scorching heat washed over her. Margaret opened her eyes wide in curiosity and beheld the breathtaking spectacle unfolding before her—

The pitch-black celestial body in the sky had cracked open and was slowly dissipating, and the brilliant, warm sun was gradually emerging.

Golden sunlight streamed through the gaps, and the vampires seemed to be standing in a sea of fire and blades. Nearly all of them turned to ash in an instant!

For a time, what lay before Margaret was a vampire hell. Their anguished howls rose as they burned to nothingness in the sunlight like mosquitoes caught in flame!

Margaret stood speechless before the tragic scene of ash and fire, most especially at the spectacular sight of the cracked-open giant celestial body.

"The... the star blocking the sun has disappeared—"

The kingdom's soldiers and knights stopped their fleeing in their tracks and stared dumbfounded at the sky.

For these mortals, to have witnessed such an apocalyptic scene in their lifetime was already to have lived meaningfully.

"H-How is this possible!? Is there really... someone who can actually do something like this!?" Clady was nearly struck dumb with fear, his mouth twitching uncontrollably. He almost thought he was dreaming!

The sky-full of vicious vampires had vanished in an instant. Margaret found it hard to believe her own eyes. Everything had happened so suddenly and yet so dreamlike.

She dropped her golden-fire flint pistol and stepped down from the platform, looking around at the cloudless expanse. Not a single vampire was in sight.

"Lord Merlin... Could it be that Lord Merlin did this?"

Margaret reasoned in her heart. She believed that Merlin had disappeared from the beginning because he went straight to the point—figuring out how to destroy that troublesome massive celestial body!

Since destroying a star was essentially impossible, such a crazy scheme had been dismissed from the start. But she never expected this unbelievable method to actually succeed!

"I-Impossible..." Clady leaned on his magic staff and slowly rose to his feet. "What kind of power could accomplish such a miraculous feat—"

The soldiers were completely bewildered by what was happening, but it seemed from the situation that they had won.

Those vicious vampires had disappeared in an instant under the sunlight, and everyone had seemingly gotten lucky and saved their lives.

Cheers rose one after another. Soldiers raised their weapons, tears in their eyes, shouting the name of their kingdom.

But just then, a flash of cold light streaked across the sky, and a massive blue-white dragon encrusted with ice plunged from the heavens, plummeting rapidly toward them.

"...What is that?" Margaret frowned, bewildered as to why a high-ranking dragon race would suddenly appear in the Empire.

"Frost Dragon Marigos!?" Clady, well-traveled and knowledgeable, recognized the Frost Dragon at a glance. This was the former kingdom's holy protector dragon, sealed away in the mountains by the court magicians of Great Britain! How could it suddenly appear in a place like this!

Returning from beyond the skies, the Frost Dragon crashed onto the ground with a tremendous "Boom," sending forth waves of cold wind and shards of ice.

This magnificent dragon slowly shrank down until it transformed into Alice's human form, curled up pitifully on the ground.

Having been stepped on by Merlin from such a great height, Alice had clearly taken significant damage as well. She was now unconscious and would likely need a long recovery.

The soldiers' eyes bulged with shock as they silently gathered around this silver-haired girl, their gazes unconsciously filled with adoration and reverence.

That look—

It was precisely the reverent stare one reserves for a savior hero.

It seemed Alice... was about to become inexplicably famous again...

title: Chapter 57 — Eerie Oil Painting (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 57 — Eerie Oil Painting (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 19 · Chapter 57

Margaret looked at Alice curled up on the ground and couldn't help but fall silent, yet waves of confusion still rose within her heart—

Why did she suddenly fall from the sky? Was it because she destroyed the massive celestial body blocking out the sun?

...No! She couldn't even intervene in battles between Demon Lords, how could she possibly destroy a celestial body?!

It must be Lord Merlin! That was the only explanation—she was fighting side by side with Lord Merlin....

But... why does my heart feel so unbalanced?

Margaret's expression darkened somewhat; even at a time like this, she felt a trace of clear jealousy.

Claridy didn't know as much information as Margaret, so she found it hard to realize the truth of the matter.

The celestial body had only just been destroyed not long ago when Alice fell from the sky. If one said this was a coincidence? He certainly wouldn't believe it.

It was probably this adventurer from Larksworth before him who had saved France from crisis, since Claridy could hardly find any other reasonable explanation.

In Claridy's eyes, Merlin was merely a follower of Alice and naturally wouldn't play a decisive role in influencing the situation.

Claridy's expression grew serious; she felt more and more the importance of recruiting Alice to join the Red Oak Knight Order, which concerned the future of the entire Britannia kingdom—

...Miss Alice was beyond imagination!

Her strength was about the same as Windsor's, only slightly stronger, yet she was able to do things far exceeding her own capabilities.....

Too strong! Far too powerful! This adventurer possessed strength far beyond what her level should allow! Impossible to explain with common sense!

I must have a good talk with Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth. No matter the cost, I must make her a member of the Knight Order!

Meanwhile, over in Oxville.

Old Akallon looked up, watching the sun slowly reappear, and the warm sunlight made many people secretly breathe a sigh of relief.

Because Oxville was located in a remote area with limited information, most people didn't know much about the recent events in the kingdom, let alone that the kingdom had nearly fallen apart.

They only knew the sun hadn't appeared for a long time and assumed something had happened, and only now did they finally put their minds at ease.

Old Akallon was exactly like that, no different from the countless ordinary people living in superficial calm, perhaps even more thick-skinned.

He wiped the sweat from his forehead and exhaled, muttering to himself—

The sun is finally out. These past few days I've been on edge, wondering if some evil force had appeared.

But it's fine now, time to go back and cook dinner for the kid.

I wonder when Merlin and Alice will be back. They should be almost here, otherwise that child keeps missing them, doesn't she?

Old Akallon's residence was a wooden cabin. Although crude, it was still cozy enough for one child and one elder to live in.

The little girl who had been rescued by Alice still obediently stayed here, but she asked once a day, "When is Mommy coming back?"

One or two times, coaxing worked, but later she couldn't keep it hidden. Old Akallon felt tremendous pressure, so he bought a paintbrush and an easel.

Old Akallon figured kids weren't hard to please; just give them something to play with and distract them.

Sure enough, the little girl became fascinated by painting and had been doodling away day after day without putting it down, much better than her previous crying state.

Right now, this little black-haired girl sat before the easel, using oil paints to draw what was in her heart.

Because of her young age, her painting skills were very poor, basically no different from random scribbling, but still barely discernible as human figures—

A beautifully dignified blonde woman?

A black-haired child?

A silver-haired child?

The two children seemed to be showing something before the woman, or perhaps presenting something to her?

The little girl painted messily, and from these tangled lines, only these shallow bits of information could be interpreted.

"....."

The little girl put down her brush, her expression growing puzzled, as if she didn't understand what she had painted.

She stared intently at the silver-haired figure she had drawn, and the younger her face got, the angrier she became, even a little twisted?

A sharp, ferocious light flashed in the little girl's eyes, and she suddenly stood up from her chair with a "fwoosh."

Her hair began to fly about like a demon's, pulled by some inexplicable power, and she dipped her brush into crimson dye, stabbing it fiercely into the silver-haired figure's head on the painting, instantly making the oil painting eerie.

"I... why am I here?"

When Old Akallon returned from outside, he discovered the black-haired little girl had vanished, simply not at home.

Old Akallon kept calling out loudly several times, but still no one answered, and he couldn't help but grow anxious.

He was only responsible for taking care of the little girl. What if she got lost—how would he explain himself to Merlin and Alice?

Old Akallon searched many places but couldn't find her, and in the end, he only saw on the easel at home a drawing left by the little girl—

By then, the painting skills were no longer mere scribbling, but sharp and precise brushwork at a level surpassing even professional painters.

The figures in the painting became vivid and lifelike, so realistic it was as though they could step out of the canvas—

This was clearly beyond the ability of any brat, sending a wave of inexplicable eeriness through Old Akallon.

The blonde woman radiating holy light and looking exquisitely dignified dressed identically to the Holy Church's Goddess of Light, Maria!

The black-haired girl knelt on the ground, looking at the goddess with hope in her eyes, holding out a dirty potato in her hands.

Beside her, the silver-haired girl held a young, adorable lamb with both hands, but you couldn't make out her face, because it had been struck with a red "X" by the paintbrush, completely obscuring her features and expression!

The two girls together presented offerings to the goddess, and obviously the silver-haired girl's offering was superior, yet her head was gone, directly crossed out by the red paintbrush. The entire painting carried a terrifying quality....

Old Akallon felt a deep chill; the more he examined the painting, the more terrifying it became! His whole body couldn't stop trembling, every hair standing on end—

The story depicted in this painting was exactly the same as the tale of the Goddess's twins he had heard at the church not long ago!

The realistic expressive power of the oil painting far exceeded the carvings on the holy vase; it looked so lifelike that this story might have actually happened!

Of course, none of this was enough to terrify Old Akallon. What truly shocked him was the facial resemblance of the figures in the painting!

The black-haired girl's face bore an eight or nine-tenths resemblance to the adopted little girl; you could say it was her grown-up self, completely replicated!

What Old Akallon found most incomprehensible was that exquisitely dignified blonde goddess, because the goddess's face was far too familiar—recognizable at a single glance.

Old Akallon touched his chin, his pale eyebrows tightly knit, and stared fixedly at the blonde Goddess of Light, muttering to himself—

"Strange!"

"Why does Miss Alice's face...."

"Appears on the face of the Goddess of Light?"

I owe a bonus chapter from yesterday, I remember it. I'll make it up with three chapters tomorrow.

The bonus chapter pace is reasonable now, unlike before where I could never catch up. I can still pay this back.....

title: Chapter 58 — Seeing Off
content:
Chapter 58 — Seeing Off

Volume 19 · Chapter 58

In the extraterritorial region, a huge celestial body whose edge cannot be seen is slowly splitting apart.
Countless objects that could turn into meteors at any moment float in midair, continually falling toward the earth.
Merlin also slowly descended, sheathing his katana, wiping his nosebleed, admiring his handiwork.
Without the celestial body blocking it, the scorching sun appeared; those seemingly gentle rays of sunlight were actually extremely hot!
Merlin felt as if he were inside an oven, and his clothes instantly caught fire.
The heat from the flames caused him a slight pain, which he had to endure.
Merlin's gaze was firm as he stared at the sun, and after a while he couldn't help but stare blankly.
This might be the closest Merlin has ever been to the sun in his life, that huge fireball placed at the center of all things.
Before it, Merlin estimated he wasn't even worth a speck of dust; he could not possibly see the sun's full appearance.
But just then, Merlin vaguely saw a rather strange building, as if it had always been here—
A crystal gate flowing with colorful light, continuously emitting a mysterious glow, appearing very sacred and solemn......
Merlin couldn't help but frown, desperately trying to see the crystal gate clearly, but the flames obstructed his view, making it hard to see.
“What was that just now?”
“In this mysterious realm that no one has ever reached, there actually exists a unique building?”
“Water gate.... what the heck is this”
Although Merlin was very puzzled, that majestic crystal gate just now seemed unrelated to him.
Even if he set foot in this region, there would be no reaction at all; perhaps it's just a purely peculiar structure.
Unfortunately, Merlin can only fall now; he cannot go over to investigate, so he can only silently......
Half a month later, the blood clan's invasion war ended in a complete victory for the kingdom.
The turbulent France finally regained peace, temporarily no danger, everything gradually returned to normal.
Mercedesfield and Blaze, though seriously injured, fortunately found a priest for treatment in time; recently they have mostly recovered and can act on their own.
Although Joan of Arc failed to guard the holy bell, she fortunately survived; however, during this period she didn't go see Alice, as if deliberately avoiding her.
Of course, the good news doesn't stop there; Margaret's handwritten letter to the purple-gold adventurer Chris received a reply, the messenger returned from White Dew Forest, also bringing medicine that can cure the old king.
According to reliable rumors from the palace, after the old king took Chris's medicine, he was successfully rescued from the brink of death, and appears to have become ten years younger, full of vigor!!
This made many people marvel inwardly; the purple-gold adventurer living in White Dew Forest became more admired and respected, and many now want to go seek treatment.
Margaret hasn't been bothering Merlin lately; she's probably guarding her newly awakened father's side, and she seems busy as well.
As for Miranda and the Sebupu siblings who were found, they now stand before the port of Wangcheng—
A huge cruise ship is docked here, making a 'woo-woo' sound as it prepares to depart; passengers with suitcases hurriedly board.
We... want to go.... Sebupu wearing a long robe, a small hat, dressed as a merchant.
“Sorry for all the trouble!” Miranda bowed apologetically; she changed into a long dress, used a sun hat to cover her horns, this outfit looks like a girl-next-door.
“Get lost already, the earlier you leave the quieter it'll be; it's annoying that you even know you're causing trouble, barely any self-awareness.... Merlin said impatiently, rolling his eyes, not to mention how annoyed he was.”
“Ah? What did you say?! What's with that high-and-mighty attitude? Do you think I'll meekly thank you for your help? You little brat! Your mother's manners aren't inherited at all!” Sebupu snarled, baring his teeth, raising his luggage to hit Merlin.
“Hey... Alice still has some bandages on her, her wounds apparently not fully healed, so she tapped Merlin's arm and whispered, emphasizing: 'They're about to leave; can't you just say something nice? Why cause such a fuss?’”
“If it weren't for those two, our affairs would have been finished long ago; do we really need this trouble?” Merlin sighed helplessly.
“It's clearly because you refused to help at first; otherwise how would it have turned out like this.... Sebupu curled his lip, looking down on Merlin.”
“Ah? It's my fault, I think we need to have a good talk.” Merlin frowned.
“Heh, nowadays youngsters' tempers are getting... Sebupu's expression stiff.”
“Brother, please say less; I really caused the teacher a lot of trouble; if I don't apologize properly, it won't do.” Miranda said earnestly.
“...” Sebupu's anger instantly dissipated, he muttered: “That kind of home... really isn't necessary....”
“Sorry, teacher, this is all my fault; if I hadn't run away from home on a whim, we wouldn't have caused so much trouble.” Miranda apologized nervously.
Alice saw Miranda's frightened look, thought this female demon was both sensitive and timid, overturning her fixed impression of demons as ferocious.
After getting along for a few days, Alice thought Miranda was very kind, simply like an angel who took the wrong womb.
Compared to the unpleasant-smelling Sebupu, Miranda this sister is very likable, making one doubt whether they are really siblings.
Alice didn't want Merlin to embarrass Miranda, so she turned and glared at him, signaling him to react.
“啧!” Merlin's expression softened; although Sebupu's temper is foul and stubborn, his sister is still nice, so he said, “You know you were wrong, that's good; next time don't run away from home on a whim; you're just an ordinary demon, without this sis-con looking after you, you'll definitely get bullied outside, you understand?”
“Yes... understood, teacher!” Miranda nodded like a pecking chick.
