title: Chapter 69 — Celebration Banquet
content:
Chapter 69 — Celebration Banquet

Volume 19 · Chapter 69

Alice stared down Margaret with neither deference nor arrogance, acting as if she were Merlin’s wife by right—like she was staking her claim.

Margaret’s expression darkened instantly. She knew Alice had an innate advantage she couldn’t compete with, but when Alice insisted on attending the banquet as Merlin’s wife, it still rubbed her the wrong way.

Merlin’s expression twisted awkwardly, wanting to clarify the misunderstanding—Alice wasn’t his wife, and attending as his spouse was clearly inappropriate.

“What? Is there something wrong with that? Or do you want to go alone?” Alice turned her head to ask.

“That’s not the point,” Merlin frowned, feeling like he’d been arbitrarily assigned a role.

“I know, I know—I’ll definitely go with you. No need to ask me.” Alice cut him off before he could explain himself to Margaret.

Merlin’s eyebrows twitched. *Who asked you? I didn’t even say anything!*

“Fine, if Alice insists on coming, then let her come.” Margaret turned away in a huff, tossing over her shoulder, “I’ll give you a surprise.”

Once Margaret left, Alice let out a quiet sigh of relief. She’d finally fended off that little imp’s advances.

If she stayed any longer, Margaret would keep harassing her day and night, and Alice knew she’d end up exhausted.

But since she’d already agreed to the victory banquet, there was no way out now. She hadn’t expected Margaret to suddenly swoop in like that.

Alice felt a pang of regret—she should’ve packed her things and left last night.

“Guess I’ll have to go then.”

“Wait—you were planning to sneak away, but now you’re not leaving?” Merlin asked, confused.

“After the banquet, okay? We already won, so we can’t just skip the celebration.” Alice sighed.

“You could’ve just refused in the first place. Why agree to go?” Merlin tilted his mouth, thinking Alice was being insincere—always doing things she didn’t want to.

“I *have* to go! Otherwise, it’d look like I’m scared of that fox spirit!” Alice huffed. “I can’t show weakness in front of her!”

Merlin rolled his eyes. *She’s torturing herself over this. It’s just pride.*

“Besides, I’ll stay by your side. Otherwise, who knows what kind of trouble might come crawling over.” Alice spoke seriously.

“Wait—what did you mean by calling yourself my wife?” Merlin hesitated, unsure how to ask.

Alice’s face flushed crimson, her expression torn. “You—you don’t actually think I’m your wife, do you?”

Merlin’s forehead broke out in a cold sweat. “How—how could you even think that?!”

“N-no way!” Alice stammered, her body trembling, her cheeks burning. “You—you misunderstood! I’ve never thought that! I just… I just didn’t want you to go alone to the banquet, that’s all. Yes, that’s it!”

Merlin narrowed his eyes, studying her like a suspect. *Is she telling the truth?*

But earlier, when she’d called herself Merlin’s wife…

She’d sounded so proud.

---

Night fell, and the palace glowed with lanterns, fireworks bursting across the sky in dazzling displays.

A grand symphony drifted from the halls, its melody sweet and intoxicating.

The victory banquet had begun. Noble officers mingled, their laughter and clinking glasses filling the air.

Some conversed eagerly, boasting about the defense war.

Others led young women into the dance floor, twirling in joyful steps.

Servants weaved through the crowd, offering fine wine and delicacies to the guests.

Blaise had hoped to use this night to draw closer to Mesfield, inviting her to dance.

He knew the kingdom was safe now, and both Mesfield and Kladi—the Thorned Knights—would soon leave France. After that, he’d rarely see the beautiful Windsor again.

Unfortunately, Mesfield wasn’t attending tonight. Kladi had said she was unwell, declining the banquet, and that the two would leave France soon.

Blaise sighed, forcing himself to enjoy the moment. He regaled the younger women around him with exaggerated tales of his heroics in the defense war, earning their shrieks and applause. When he reached the part where his life hung in the balance, the ladies nearly fainted from shock.

Merlin and Alice arrived early, only to spot many familiar faces—those who had fought against the vampires. This banquet was to honor them.

Kladi was deep in conversation with a mage, but his gaze flickered when he saw Merlin and Alice.

He’d heard from Mesfield about that night’s events. The mysterious figure, disguised as Belzebub, had slipped out of the manor late at night—only to be ambushed by Elgin, the legendary swordsman, on the road.

Kladi found it hard to believe this was all coincidence, that Merlin and Alice had nothing to do with it. Too many things didn’t add up.

So he excused himself from his conversation, apologized, and walked straight toward Merlin and Alice, hoping to subtly pry for answers.

“Alice, it’s been a few days. How’s your recovery?”

Merlin saw Kladi alone and thought, *Where’s the female knight? Every time I see him, it’s just the two of us. Doesn’t it feel wrong to keep staring at one sheep like that, even if you’re shearing wool?*

Alice greeted Kladi with a polite smile. “Thank you for asking. I’m much better now.”

“Good to hear. That night, seeing you descend from the sky like that—so majestic—it was truly shocking. I never expected you could transform into a Holy Dragon. Such a rare ability… absolutely breathtaking.” Kladi spoke with genuine admiration.

Alice felt awkward inside. She’d only flown high with Merlin—nothing extraordinary had happened. She couldn’t take all the praise.

“This isn’t something worth praising,” she muttered.

“Not worth praising?” Kladi smirked, clearing his throat. “I’ve seen plenty of shameless people, but someone as modest as you? That’s a first.”

Alice’s heart sank. *Shameless? He’s talking about me, right?*

*Sob. I’m not trying to steal Merlin’s glory.*

title: Chapter 70 — Dragon Duelist
content:
Chapter 70 — Dragon Duelist

Volume 19 · Chapter 70

Chris was lavishing praise on Alice, his eyes brimming with admiration. “You actually shattered an entire celestial body—one that could plunge all of France into eternal darkness. Its roar must have been as vast as the moon at night. Without world-shaking power, how could anyone achieve something so unimaginable?” Chris had lived half a life, and in his eyes, Alice was the only one—just one—who possessed such terrifying strength.

Alice felt utterly flustered. She was already being hailed as the world’s strongest, yet now that she’d been lifted so high, she couldn’t find a way down. If the truth ever came out, how would she ever face the world again?

Alice no longer dared to accept compliments. Though she wanted her name to echo across the world, she refused to rely on Merlin—she had to do it herself.

“You’re being too modest,” Chris chuckled, pressing on. “Everyone saw it with their own eyes. How could it be a lie? Your true strength must have long since broken free of the Saint-tier shackles, venturing into realms far more mysterious. Serving as a silver-ranked adventurer is a waste of your talent. I won’t be surprised if a new gold-ranked adventurer emerges soon—and when that happens, I hope you won’t forget this old friend who fought beside you.”

Alice groaned, rubbing her forehead. Her so-called strength was all for show—hollow inside.

Merlin smirked, nudging Alice with his elbow. “Oh-ho, now you’re about to become a big shot. Don’t forget where you came from, especially not your little lackey who’s always by your side. I’m still waiting to drink the soup from your backside!”

Alice jabbed Merlin in the ribs. “Shut up! I don’t want to hear you mock me when I’m already in this mess. It’s bad enough you’re here—now you’ve got the nerve to joke about it?”

Chris cleared his throat, shifting to a more formal tone. “I’m honored that the Thistle Knights will soon welcome you. I’ll sing your praises to Queen Elizabeth, ensuring your deeds are properly recognized so you can become an honorary member of our order.”

Alice covered her face. “Please don’t. I don’t deserve any of that.”

Chris forced a dry laugh. “You saw the dragon form you took that day—pure blue-white, dripping with frost. Was that the legendary Frost Saint Dragon?”

Alice nodded. “That’s right.”

Merlin confirmed it for her. “It’s the Frost Saint Dragon.”

Chris hesitated, his curiosity piqued. “How did you do it? The Frost Saint Dragon was the guardian of the old kingdom. When Britain was founded, countless royal mages barely managed to seal it away. Did you…” He trailed off, suspicion flickering in his eyes. Was Alice somehow connected to the old kingdom? Had she been a dragon transformed into human form? After all, the old kingdom and Britain had been bitter enemies, and rumors still swirled about remnants of the old regime resurfacing.

Merlin gave a vague explanation. “There’s a crystal that sometimes forms in a dragon’s mind. If you consume it, you can evolve into a humanoid dragon. Alice just happened to get lucky and obtain one.”

Chris probed further. “So… a legacy crystal?”

Merlin’s eyes widened slightly. “You know about this?”

Chris smirked. “I’ve studied dragon lore. Long ago, our ancestors, dissatisfied with being human, sought ways to enhance their bodies. That’s when they discovered legacy crystals. Only a rare few could merge with them—people with human hearts but dragon-like power, known as Dragon Warriors.”

Alice stared at Chris in disbelief. She could transform into a dragon, but she hadn’t fully absorbed the crystal’s power. It seemed some force was holding back that last bit—something that refused to recognize her.

Chris nodded solemnly. “Exactly. The power you’ve tapped into is just the surface. The true essence—the part that even dragons can’t fully unlock—lies in that stubborn fragment. If you master it, you’ll transcend even the Saint Dragons.”

Alice blinked. “So… the core of dragon power isn’t about becoming a dragon at all?”

Chris leaned in, his voice dropping to a conspiratorial tone. “No. The legends say that when a human fully awakens dragon power, they don’t turn into a dragon—they become armored in steel wings, their bodies forged into an unstoppable suit. Strong enough to tear apart Valkyries with bare hands, to roar defiance at the gods themselves.”

Alice blinked. “…What?”

The two exchanged confused glances. Clearly, they hadn’t grasped what Chris was saying. He clarified with simpler words.

“From the description, you can tell that mastering dragon power isn’t about becoming a dragon—it’s about transforming into a warrior clad in steel wings. That armor is so powerful it could rend ancient divine messengers apart with its bare hands.”

Alice’s eyes widened. “That sounds… incredible. Mr. Chris, do you know how to unlock that power?”

Chris hesitated. “I’ve heard rumors. Only those who can fully awaken dragon potential are called Dragon Warriors. I once found records in an ancient ruin about them—they were called *Dragonheart Warriors*, souls pledged to the supreme Black Dragon, leading the rebellion against the old gods. Their armor was unbreakable, their steel wings soaring through the skies, their claws tearing Valkyries apart as they howled at the gods’ twilight.”

Alice: “???”

The two stared at each other, clearly lost. Chris repeated himself in plainer terms.

“From what I’ve read, mastering dragon power doesn’t mean becoming a dragon—it means becoming a warrior encased in steel-winged armor. Powerful enough to kill divine messengers with their bare hands.”

Alice’s eyes gleamed. “Mr. Chris, you know so much about ancient secrets… Do you also know how to fully awaken dragon power?”

title: Chapter 71 — A Chance for Solitude
content:
Chapter 71 — A Chance for Solitude

Volume 19 · Chapter 71

"I only know some clues," Claudi said mysteriously. "What I just said already revealed them."

"Eh?" Alice froze, then after a moment's thought asked tentatively, "Offer one's soul to the supreme black dragon?"

"That's right. This is the key to completely controlling the dragon race's power," Claudi nodded with a smile, thinking Alice had good comprehension and could quickly grasp the key point.

"Offer one's soul? That doesn't sound like a good thing. It's like some kind of contract," Merlin frowned.

"No no no, Lord Merlin only saw the literal meaning. The true meaning here is to drink the black dragon's blood. As long as one can drink the black dragon's fresh blood, the dragon race can evolve into a perfect form," Claudi explained.

"Drink the black dragon's blood? What is this black dragon?" Alice asked in confusion.

"Legend says in ancient times there was a giant tree supporting the world. Gods and other races lived in the same system. At the roots of the world tree leading to the land of the dead, Nibelheim, lurked the dragon ancestor Nidhogg." Claudi paused, then continued, "This black dragon's mission was to bite through the world tree's roots, leading the world to destruction. However, its mission was completed by a hero of the mythological era. That hero personally severed the world tree's roots, announcing the end of the gods' era, and the world was destroyed. According to stories passed down by the Church of Light, our current world was reconstructed, governed by the Goddess of Light from the heavens and the God of Death from the underworld. This also explains why the world tree no longer exists in our era—it perished along with the age of the gods."

"Uh, this means there's absolutely no chance then," Alice's face fell, thinking. Such a distant creature—where would she even find it? Even if she found it, she couldn't win, let alone drink its blood.

"Who said there's no chance? According to various ancient texts, the black dragon Nidhogg might still be alive. It's one of the few survivors who escaped the Twilight of the Gods," Claudi said leisurely. "Perhaps it's now lurking in some abyss."

"..." Alice lowered her head, thinking. After all this effort, it turned out there were still no clues at all. Whether they could meet it was purely luck. Who knows if this great black dragon that feeds on tree roots is good or evil?

"Alice-san was able to obtain the Frost Holy Dragon's crystal. Clearly your luck is not something ordinary people can match. You still have a chance to become a Dragon Buster in your lifetime," Claudi said with a smile.

"In your lifetime..."

Merlin let out a cold sweat from his forehead, thinking: 'In your lifetime' equals a distant prospect. Isn't that industry consensus?

"By the way, where is the other gentleman who was with you two?" Claudi asked casually, pretending to be inquiring inadvertently.

Merlin and Alice shivered simultaneously, like mice stepped on their tails, feeling guilty.

The two knew Claudi meant Beelzebub, but didn't expect him to pay attention to a madman like that.

Merlin's gaze dodged, stammering, "His sister came looking for him, so he was picked up a few days ago. Yeah, that's it."

"Oh~ He's gone already," Claudi nodded, saying intentionally or unintentionally. "That gentleman's identity is suspicious. The first time I saw him I felt something was off. He's somewhat like a demon. Do you think he might be the Gluttony Demon Lord who attacked France?"

Merlin:

Their expressions both became tense simultaneously, completely failing to reveal whether Claudi was joking casually or had already discovered the truth.

"What's with those expressions? Did I discover a real secret?" Claudi's eyes swept back and forth between Merlin and Alice's faces.

"How could that be? Mr. Claudi is just joking around," Merlin said, forcing a laugh to muddle through.

"Exactly, he's just a madman. How could he be the Gluttony Demon Lord? Haha," Alice said with a dry laugh.

"I see, then it was probably my imagination. You two are busy, I won't disturb you." Claudi smiled, but his face changed as he turned to leave, thinking as he looked at their reactions: did he feel they had something to hide? Could that mysterious man earlier really be an evil creature?

After Claudi left, Merlin and Alice both let out sighs of relief, having been so nervous their hearts were in their throats.

"Merlin wiped the cold sweat from his forehead and said in a low voice, 'This Thorn Knight is no simple person. Not only is he well-read, but his alertness is exceptionally high. Truly, a young exterior with the soul of an old fox.'"

"Yes, I feel like Mr. Claudi knows a lot of things. I'm somewhat impressed by such a person," Alice said seriously.

"I hope he doesn't dig deeper, or else I feel my secrets will be exposed," Merlin frowned, having to face this Thorn Knight at the very end.

Jeanne, wearing a male evening suit, walked through the crowd, seemingly wanting to leave the lively venue to get some air on the balcony outside.

Seeing the figure of an acquaintance, Alice couldn't help recalling her recent doubts. She became increasingly concerned and turned to Merlin to speak.

"I'm going over there alone. Wait for me here. Don't wander around."

"Hmm? What are you going to do?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"I saw Jeanne. I want to go chat with her." Alice said truthfully.

Merlin nodded meaningfully, recalling the previous assassin, understanding what Alice wanted to do.

"Wait here for me. I'll be back soon. Don't wander around," Alice warned.

"Okay." Merlin nodded.

Alice turned and left, but after not going far, she came back, worried, and said seriously, "You better not go flirt with the young girls here while I'm gone, or get flirted away by them. I came with you, so I'm your companion tonight. You know what I mean."

Merlin sighed impatiently, rolling his eyes, thinking: When will this end? She's so meddlesome! I didn't ask Alice to be my dance partner; she insisted herself!

After Alice hurried away, Merlin stood around with nothing to do, intending to find a quiet place to drink, and ended up running into Marguerite dressed in fancy attire.

Marguerite attended the ball dressed to the nines, wearing a gorgeous dance gown that sparkled in the dance floor

title: Chapter 73 — Coexisting in One Room
content:
Chapter 73 — Coexisting in One Room

Volume 19 · Chapter 73

"...".

Joan's heart trembled uncontrollably. She had thought she was being very discreet, yet still someone saw through it.

Does that mean Alice already knew the truth when she saved me back then?

Joan lowered her head, clenched her fists in embarrassment, and felt a sense of guilt for repaying kindness with hostility.

"How did you recognize me?"

Alice looked at Joan, having expected her to deny it, but instead she admitted it so plainly. "When you were a Hero candidate, we lived together for a long time. As soon as you threw out a move, I could guess it was you. There was no way to hide it."

...Joan fell silent. No wonder Alice hesitated slightly and wasn't fully focused when they fought before. So I was already exposed from that moment on.

"I've seen many strong spear-wielders. You're quite special — the only one who can make spear techniques look like swordsmanship," Alice added.

"You must hate me right now, correct? Since you already figured it out, don't suppress your emotions. Feel free to rage at me. I can accept whatever you say." Joan showed an expression of accepting it all calmly.

"That's right. At first when I realized you would resort to such despicable methods, I despised you. Merlin is a very important person to me, and I didn't want him to fall into danger because of me." Alice frowned, her tone carrying suppressed anger. "But when I calmed down, I wasn't so angry anymore. I thought maybe you were acting against your own will, right?"

"Why?" Joan raised her head and looked at Alice.

"Because I know you. You've always been straightforward — you'd never use despicable means to solve problems. I think it must have been Archbishop Scott's idea. Because you refused to return to the Holy Church, he wanted to destroy everything you currently have, forcing you into a situation where returning to the Church would be your only option..." Alice paused, then continued. "Am I right? You don't agree with Bishop Scott's methods, but as an Inquisitor you had to follow orders. There was no way to resist, right?"

"You're wrong. I agree with Lord Scott's methods. The Church using some means to bring you back is not wrong. The bishop is trying to save you, not murder you..." Joan's tone suddenly grew resolute.

"Save me? When did I need anyone to save me? I'm very..." Alice emphasized.

"The old you wouldn't have been like this. You've been corrupted by those scoundrels around you, and your reverence for the Goddess of Light is completely gone!" Joan stared into Alice's eyes and shouted loudly. "You can so easily speak words belittling the Goddess! What difference is there between you and those heretics?! You should be sent to the pyre! Turn back while it's still not too late — stay away from those sketchy people!"

"I'm not a follower of the Holy Light Church! I never was from the start. Don't apply believers' rules to me..." Alice said seriously.

"I know you're not a devout believer. But you once wielded a sword for the Goddess and fought in her name. As the Goddess's former warrior, shouldn't you at least retain a shred of reverence?" Joan frowned tightly and spoke with an imposing air. "Look at how you are now — hanging around with scoundrels. Before long you'll become a sinner who has lost all faith!"

"What's past is past. I have no more ties with the Holy Church. I may have once been the Hero who fought for the Goddess, but regrettably, I am no longer that person. I'm simply an adventurer running around everywhere. No matter what despicable means you use to try to make me return, I will never serve as a Hero again..." Alice spoke seriously, as though expressing her attitude to Joan.

"This isn't despicable. We're saving you." Joan frowned and said earnestly. "As someone who was once your comrade, I can't just stand by and watch you be seduced by scoundrels. I must bring you back onto the right path."

"I don't need to be saved by anyone. I chose my own path, and I'll walk it without regret." Although Alice spoke calmly, her words left no room for others to question her.

"...Joan's eyelid twitched violently, her mouth twitching uncontrollably, as though steam were rising from her head. "Is that useless man worth all this for? Do you really love him?"

"Guess." Alice said enigmatically, turned, and left. "I won't return to the Holy Church. Don't waste your efforts. I'll pretend what happened before never occurred. But if there's a next time, sorry, I won't hold back at all!"

Joan watched Alice's departing figure, silently clenching her fists. Her heart filled with unwillingness —

Why can some idiot become the Hero when I can't?

Is my devotion not worth even a single coin?

In the princess's bedroom, Margaret eagerly pulled Merlin inside.

The room was lavishly decorated yet carried a touch of girlish heart.

That pink-colored large bed seemed... somewhat incongruous with Margaret.

To think this little princess full of wicked schemes was actually like this in private?

After Merlin entered, he curiously looked around. Compared to Queen Elizabeth's room, Margaret's room was evidently a bit more childish. It was probably because she was still young.

Margaret walked behind Merlin and asked with a smile, "Lord Merlin, what are you looking at? So curious about my room?"

"N-nothing..." Merlin cleared his throat, covering his awkwardness.

"Now that Lord Merlin has seen my bedroom, do you have any thoughts?" Margaret asked curiously.

"It's... pretty nice. Like a child's room," Merlin said with a calm smile. It was similar to his sister Lilith's room — always filled with cuter items.

"Hmph!" Margaret puffed up her cheeks angrily and insisted, "For goodness' sake, I'm already an adult now. The way you talk makes you sound like an old grandpa. That's not good."

"Old grandpa..." Merlin looked awkward and thought that although he was considered young among demons, he could easily serve as Margaret's grandfather by human standards.

"That's right. I think Lord Merlin should be more lively. That's what a young person should be like. Always so aged and solemn — even I find you a bit boring now." Margaret said earnestly.

"..." Several black lines slid down Merlin's forehead. He changed the subject. "Aren't we here to drink and chat? Why is there absolutely no alcohol in your room?"

"Hehe."

Margaret chuckled twice, then directly pushed the defenseless Merlin onto the bed. She lifted her long skirt and straddled him. "Lord Merlin, are you truly foolish or pretending? Why are you so dense? Drinking and chatting is so boring~"

Margaret rode on top of Merlin with a big grin, her hands resting on his chest — not behaving properly at all. The atmosphere suddenly became constrained and ambiguous.

Merlin was frightened. His eyes bulged wide, and he gasped in horror, "WTF! What are you doing!?"

"What am I doing? Don't you understand, Lord Merlin? How adorable — such an innocent man. He's exactly my type..." Margaret gently stroked Merlin's cheek. A faint blush appeared on her pretty face, her eyes overflowing with unmistakable desire —

"It's just you and me here. No one else is around."

"When a man and a woman are alone in a room, of course they should do pleasurable things..."

▼(@><)▼

title: Chapter 74 — The Princess of Temptation
content:
Chapter 74 — The Princess of Temptation

Volume 19 · Chapter 74

Merlin was so startled when Margaret pinned him down that he nearly jumped out of his skin. *What the hell?* He thought to himself. *This is supposed to be a casual drink and chat, but this little princess wants to sleep with me?*

“What’s so surprising about that?” Margaret laughed lightly, finding Merlin’s reaction utterly amusing. “Don’t you know what I mean, Merlin?”

“...That’s not appropriate,” Merlin said sternly, trying to push her off. He had no intention of doing anything improper—he rarely even thought about such things himself.

“Why wait until we’re *having fun* to talk?” Margaret’s hands slid up Merlin’s firm chest, her excitement growing with every touch.

“...” Merlin frowned, completely flustered. *This little princess is so bold,* he thought. *What kind of things does she dare say?*

“Pfft, Merlin,” Margaret bit her lip, her face flushed as she whispered, “Didn’t expect you to be such a pure man, did I? Your reaction is so adorable~”

“That’s not it,” Merlin stammered, his mind racing. *Sure, I’ve worked as a male escort before, but they pay for it. This princess clearly wants a freebie—that’s unacceptable. I won’t let my value drop like that.*

“...Your Highness, please step down,” Merlin said, trying to clear up the misunderstanding. “I think there’s been some—”

“What misunderstanding?” Margaret pressed her full breasts against Merlin’s chest, her voice sincere. “I love you, Merlin. I’m serious. Can’t you accept me?”

Merlin’s forehead creased with confusion. *What kind of ridiculous country love talk is this?* He thought. *It’s like I’m in some cheesy village drama.*

“Merlin...” Margaret’s cheeks burned red as she looked into his eyes, clearly lost in the moment. “It’s just you and me here. We can do whatever we want. Don’t you want to be intimate with me? If you’re a man, I don’t believe you’d have no reaction!”

Just as Margaret reached for his belt, Merlin panicked. “Wait!”

“What’s wrong?” she asked, smiling sweetly. “Or did Merlin finally change his mind and wants to cooperate? Then hurry up—we don’t know what might interrupt us.”

“...Not like that,” Merlin said stiffly, his voice trembling. “You—you love me? What exactly do you love about me?”

Margaret hesitated, then quickly found a reason. “I love your aura,” she said seriously, locking eyes with him. “That extreme strength, that untouchable pride. I know you destroyed the celestial body—not that woman out there. No matter how many men there are in this world, only you could ever be worthy of me.”

Merlin rolled his eyes. *Unbelievable.* “Your Highness, stop joking,” he said. “You don’t even know me. You’re in love with a hollow puppet, not the real me. We’ll never work.”

“No!” Margaret tried to protest, but Merlin cut her off with a stern tone.

“Your Highness, stop acting childish,” he said, avoiding her gaze. His mind flashed with Alice’s image. “I’m not the kind of man who thinks with his lower half. What I want...” He trailed off, embarrassed. “I want a woman who understands me, someone to share a simple life with until the end—not just some base desire.”

Margaret froze, her anger rising. *So... so that woman outside is the one you actually want to spend your life with?*

Merlin’s brow furrowed. “You guessed it.”

“...” Margaret’s expression turned cold. “I’ll change your mind. I’ll make you fall in love with me.”

“...What are you planning?” Merlin’s eyes sharpened, sensing something extreme.

Margaret clenched her dress and tore it apart, revealing her tempting body. The room filled with her allure—her fiery figure was enough to make any man lose control.

“Nnn!” Merlin’s eyes bulged as Margaret straddled him, her bare upper body writhing like a seductive serpent. Her intoxicating scent made his blood boil.

There was no denying it—Margaret was France’s most beautiful woman. Not just young and vibrant, but so stunning that even other women felt inferior beside her. No wonder so many princes chased after her.

She leaned in slowly, her hands wrapping around Merlin like vines as she licked his neck with her tongue. Her voice dripped with temptation.

“Merlin, let’s forget everything. Let’s follow our instincts and indulge.”

“Just leave your seed with me,” she whispered. “I swear I won’t bother you after.”

---

Outside, Alice searched the entire hall but couldn’t find Merlin anywhere. A cold dread settled in her chest.

*Damn it!* She had told him to wait for her—why was he gone?

Alice’s instincts kicked in. She noticed Margaret, as a royal representative, was also missing from the banquet. That was suspicious.

Recalling how Margaret had always flirted with Merlin, and now both were gone at the same time—Alice’s suspicions deepened.

She found Blazes and didn’t ask directly about Merlin. Instead, she probed carefully.

“Blazes,” she said, her voice icy, “where is Margaret? Isn’t she the guest of honor tonight?”

“Oh! The princess and Merlin—” Blazes, ever honest, clapped his hand over his mouth in horror, realizing he’d said too much.

Alice’s eyes narrowed. She already knew something was wrong.

“So,” she said, her voice dangerously calm, “Merlin left with the princess?”

“Blazes,” she continued, her fury barely contained, “I can’t pretend I didn’t hear that.”

“And I expect a *detailed* explanation of what happened.”

title: Chapter 75 — Guilt (Extra chapter today, will be late, sorry)
content:
Chapter 75 — Guilt (Extra chapter today, will be late, sorry)

Volume 19 · Chapter 75

In the corridor of Margaret's bedroom, Alice's face was grim as she hurriedly walked quickly.
Blaze really couldn't withstand the actually blazing Alice, fearing that if she got angry she would demolish the palace, so he honestly told the truth.
After knowing what just happened, Alice didn't say a word and rushed straight to Margaret's bedroom, wanting to see what Merlin was doing.
Margaret had been thinking of Merlin for a long time; suddenly she pulled Merlin away alone, and even an idiot knows there's nothing good about that!
But Alice felt a bit angry in her heart—why was Merlin so easily taken away? Didn't I tell him to wait for me?
Alice suppressed her anger, thinking of many possibilities, very worried that something bad might happen.
“Miss Alice, don't be so impulsive; there's nothing between Your Highness and Merlin, they just want to have a private chat, so please don't disturb them.” Blaze said with a smile, worrying himself sick for his master.
“What can't be said directly? Why do you need a private chat? Hmph!” Alice said coldly, giving Blaze a fierce look and lumping him into the camp of bad people.
“Please, can't you just wait a bit?” Blaze stepped in front of Alice, blocking her way forward—if Margaret really is doing something shameful, the royal face would be lost completely; it's still banquet time, causing a joke would be awful. “This is the French royal palace; outsiders are not allowed to enter the princess's chambers. Although you are a hero who repelled the blood clan, you still can't trample on the kingdom's laws at will!”
“.....Outsiders?” Alice gave Blaze a strange look, glaring at him and said, “I just want to find Merlin; I'm not a terrorist!”
“No… that's also not allowed! Without Your Highness's permission, no one is permitted to enter the bedroom…” Blaze smiled more ugly than crying, using all his strength to cover for Margaret, facing Alice's pressure which was enormous, “Your Highness Alice, please don't act rashly; I believe Your Highness and Merlin have a pure friendship; don't overthink it.”
Alice furrowed her brows; hearing Blaze's feeble explanation, she directly drew her slender sword, and a chill swept through the corridor.
“Ugh!” Blaze broke out in cold sweat, stepping back—he truly had no confidence to defeat Alice, or stop her from barging into Margaret's bedroom, especially after hearing that Alice destroyed the huge celestial body blocking the sun; her mighty image had clearly taken root in people's minds!
“Scram!” Alice coldly cursed, a naked threat of force.
“Okay okay, I'm leaving, I'm leaving…” Blaze nodded like a chick pecking at rice, silently making way, not daring to resist, only able to pray in his heart—Your Highness, I've done my best; you're on your own, just please don't have any ambiguous behavior with Merlin…
“Hmph!” Alice sheathed her slender sword, coldly saying, “Pure friendship? I don't believe a word of it! You and Margaret are wearing the same pants!”
When Alice reached Margaret's bedroom door, without hesitation she kicked it open without knocking.
“Merlin! You bastard, what are you doing?!”
Alice came in shouting loudly, first overwhelming Merlin with momentum, then intending to talk about his mistake.
But as soon as she entered, she saw an inhuman scene that made one lament the decline of morals and the corruption of ethics.
Margaret was wrapped in a blanket, bound five ways, then hung from the gorgeous chandelier on the ceiling.
And Merlin was even more shameless, constantly rotating the chandelier, making Margaret spin like a top, going crazy.
Merlin used to say he would turn people into spinning tops, and today he actually did it— and to the French princess!
“Rumble rumble rumble…”
Margaret's speech was slurred; she only felt the world spinning, about to vomit, she never imagined…
…that she, the pearl of France, would be rejected at the door by Merlin, and still be tortured while bound five ways!
A nameless sense of shame welled up in her heart; her dignity was trampled by Merlin, this unromantic man.
How did Merlin ever find a wife? Someone like him should be single for ten thousand years!
Hearing Alice's shout, Merlin turned his head in surprise, face full of confusion, asking, “How did you come here?”
“……Alice was frightened by Merlin's torment of Margaret, her mind went blank for a moment, “I came… just to have a look…”
Blaze's face darkened; he muttered inwardly, “Damn it, just to have a look? Earlier you clearly wanted to fight to the death! …Seeing nothing happened, you instantly went mute!”
“It's you! Didn't you tell me to wait for you? Why did you leave on your own?!” Alice complained angrily.
“Your Highness said she wanted to drink and chat with me…” Merlin glanced at Margaret hanging from the chandelier, speaking meaningfully, “…she actually wanted to play games with me…”
A bead of cold sweat trickled down Alice's forehead; she thought, what kind of game is this? Is she a masochist?
Merlin thought that after tormenting Margaret like this, the wild girl might hold a grudge, so he hastily grabbed Alice's hand and said, “It's getting late; let's hurry and leave.”
Being led by the hand, Alice's face turned slightly red, flustered she said, “Ah! Why are you acting like you're fleeing?”
“Your Highness!” Blaze rushed forward, pulling Margaret down from the chandelier, “You… you alright?”
Margaret couldn't move, feeling dizzy, the whole world seemed like tiny stars, she whimpered, “…”
“Why….”
“Why did Merlin do this to me?”
“Damn it, where am I lacking compared to that flat-chested woman?”
Late at night, the stars speckled across the sky like ink.
A carriage rushed out of the royal city, speeding away from here.
Merlin drove the carriage in silence, as if nothing had happened.
Alice sat beside him, eyes suspicious, staring at Merlin, feeling something was off.
“Stare”
Black lines like a waterfall fell on Merlin's forehead; helplessly he asked, “Why do you keep staring at me?”
“Why are you in such a hurry to leave the capital?” Alice retorted.
“Aren't you the one who wanted to leave in a hurry? Now you're dissatisfied again?” Merlin rolled his eyes.
“I don't mean that; it's just that you're even more eager than I am, as if you have something on your mind…” Alice acted like a little detective, searching for clues on Merlin.
“You're being too suspicious…” Merlin said nervously.
“Hmph! Tell me the truth…” Alice leaned in, locking eyes with Merlin and asked,
“Did you do something guilty?”
“Don't worry, speak boldly; I won't get angry.”

title: Chapter 76 — In the Way (Bonus Update)
content:
Chapter 76 — In the Way (Bonus Update)

Volume 19 · Chapter 76

Time reversal, and Margaret was topless, about to do something scandalous.

Merlin watched Margaret eagerly offer up news, then sharply turned his head away.

"Wait!"

"What is it now?" Margaret asked, bewildered, thinking Merlin always interrupted at the worst times, making her so flustered.

"...I can't just... Merlin said in a grave tone.

"Why not? Or is it only I that you're talking about?" Margaret pressed.

"Weren't you just asking me if the woman I wanted to grow old with was Alice? I'm going to answer... Merlin took a deep breath and said earnestly, "Yes, she's the ideal person in my heart."

"For... why?" Margaret couldn't understand. She thought Merlin had gone blind. "What's so good about her? Willful, bad-tempered... and she's flat-chested! Does she even have half my beauty?"

"Sunlight, wet sheets, a beautiful silhouette wearing an apron, and her hair dancing in the wind..." Merlin closed his eyes and recalled.

"...What are you talking about?" Margaret didn't understand.

"On a sunny afternoon, I saw Alice wearing an apron, hanging laundry like a housewife. When the breeze swept through her hair... it was so graceful and peaceful. That's the life I want. I admit I've fallen for her." Facing the pressure of Margaret leaning on him, Merlin had no choice but to confess his true feelings, hoping it would discourage her. "If one day I have no worries, I want the person living by my side to be her."

"Lord Merlin,..." Margaret became incoherent. She was being intimate with Merlin right now, but he was thinking of another woman. The blow was greater than she could bear.

"Yes, Alice isn't as beautiful as Your Highness. But that's not what matters to me. I want my future wife to understand me, and unfortunately, Your Highness, you don't understand me at all." Merlin shook his head.

"..." Margaret couldn't tell whether she felt sad or happy. She felt as though her internal organs were churning inside her. Finally, her gaze hardened. "I'll come to understand you slowly! I won't be inferior to that annoying woman!"

"Your Highness, please calm down. If you continue to be rude, I will use force to resolve this." Merlin suddenly grew serious.

"..." Margaret felt a hint of fear, but still forced herself to appear calm. "I don't believe Lord Merlin, who's always gentle, would lay a hand on me, do I?"

"I'm not gentle. You've seen me wrong. Which is why you don't understand me at all, Your Highness..."

Before he finished speaking, Merlin grabbed the blanket beneath them, forcefully wrapped it around Margaret, then bound her tight with the ropes from the bed curtains.

The little princess who had moments ago been radiating beauty was now a wrapped-up bundle, hanging from the grand chandelier on the ceiling, looking utterly狼狈.

"Me—Lord Merlin!?"

"Sorry, I'm a demon!"

---

At Alice's questioning, Merlin couldn't help but cover his face in embarrassment. What had he been saying in bed? Such an awkward thing couldn't let Alice know.

"...I haven't done anything wrong. I only spoke a few words to Margaret, and now I'm feeling a bit... uncomfortable thinking about it."

"Huh!? What did you say!?" Alice immediately grew excited, determined to get to the bottom of it.

Merlin was embarrassed. How could he say he wanted to kidnap Alice and make her his bandit wife? He could only give a vague explanation. "Nothing happened between me and Margaret. Stop being so suspicious."

Alice wasn't entirely convinced by Merlin's explanation, but she couldn't press further, so she suppressed her doubts.

Still, Alice lowered her head and stared blankly at her own hands, recalling how Merlin had taken her hand proactively. Her heart swelled with delight.

To hold hands proactively in front of Margaret—was that Merlin's way of showing his attitude? He always leaned toward her, after all.

"Hmph... I'll let it go this time. Next time, remember to communicate with me first. Don't let yourself get kidnapped without reason."

"Kidnapped? Do you take me for a child..." Merlin grumbled不满.

"Seriously, if it weren't for me, you'd definitely get tricked by a bunch of bad women until you had nothing left to your name. Remember to thank me properly~" Alice said proudly.

"All right, all right, I thank you. I'm moved to tears," Merlin replied perfunctorily, thinking Alice always liked to make excuses for herself. Well, if she wasn't like that, she wouldn't be her.

"Sigh, completely lacking emotion..." Alice pouted in dissatisfaction. Looking at the brilliant night sky in a foreign land, she couldn't help but stare blankly. "So... how long have we been living together?"

"How long?" Merlin tugged the reins and thought for a moment before answering, "Almost a year..."

"A year? Time flies so fast. Before I knew it, we've been living together like this for... so long." Alice suddenly sighed.

"Why are you suddenly sounding like an old woman? Snap out of it and go back to your normal silly self!" Merlin frowned, unable to tolerate Alice's current demeanor.

Alice didn't speak. Instead, she made a more intimate gesture, silently resting her shoulder against Merlin's, using him as her soft cushion.

......Merlin paused, glanced over, but could only see the silver hair atop Alice's head. "What are you doing? Does it make you uncomfortable not arguing with me?"

"That's not it!" Alice rolled her eyes. A faint blush appeared on both cheeks as she stammered, "I'm just... just a little tired. I want to lean on something."

"..." Merlin's face flushed. Looking down, he said seriously, "Then rest if you're tired. I'll protect you."

Alice slightly widened her eyes. Today's Merlin seemed a bit strange. He seemed to have suddenly become more... sensible.

So Alice's face grew hot, and she couldn't help saying something with deeper meaning.

"Then... if I keep resting, will you keep protecting me?"

"Are you trying to die and leave this world?!" Merlin's mind was filled with question marks. He complained, "A little while is fine, but if my shoulder goes numb, I'll definitely kick you off the carriage."

"You!?"

Alice's face flushed red with anger. She had thought Merlin was being nice to her—how naive!

So Alice, like a punching bag, quickly sat upright. No longer leaning on Merlin, she angrily glared at him.

"Do you think anyone wants to lean on you!? You smell like some other princess's perfume! I'm about to throw up from the stench! Disgusting!"

"Huh?!" Merlin's brows knitted together. Looking at Alice beside him, he said, "I'm disgusting? Where am I disgusting? I think you just need to keep your mouth busy since we're not arguing, and you're deliberately picking a fight!?"

The two glared at each other, ready to argue further, when suddenly a massive black mountain eagle swooped past overhead, letting out a terrifying shriek!

The giant eagle's shadow engulfed Merlin and Alice. The lead horses immediately panicked and refused to move further, emitting frightened whinnies!

Melsfield descended from the sky fully armed, with some minor injuries on his body. Apparently, he had pursued them out before fully recovering.

"Why the rush to leave, Lord Merlin?"

"That's not right..."

"I should still address you as the much-admired Great Swordmaster Earl of Elgin!"

title: Chapter 77 — True Ancestor (Part 2: End of the Volume)
content:
Chapter 77 — True Ancestor (Part 2: End of the Volume)

Volume 19 · Chapter 77

Mesfield suddenly blocked Merlin and Alice's path, his eyes filled with hostility, as if he was about to attack with his sword at any moment. In reality, Mesfield was just testing Merlin, and he was extremely suspicious of his identity, trying to let the other person reveal his true self.

Over the past few days, Mesfield had carefully thought about everything, and he found it very suspicious, Merlin's identity was not as simple as a normal adventurer. He had been following that mysterious man, and suddenly he was ambushed by Elgin, the great sword master, from behind. This series of events made Mesfield think deeply.

Merlin's relationship with that mysterious man was not superficial, and he had a motive to stop Mesfield from following him. Moreover, just like Elgin, they were both from Britain. At that time, there were not many men from Britain in the mansion, and Merlin, who was an unremarkable adventurer, seemed very suspicious! Maybe Merlin was actually Elgin, hiding his true strength and identity!

Mesfield pretended to understand the truth, took a step forward, and stared at Merlin's every move. "Great Sword Master, why don't you speak up? Didn't you think your identity would be exposed?" Merlin looked at Mesfield, then lowered his head and took a deep breath, as if he had been caught.

Oh no, did he really get caught? He shouldn't have gotten involved that night. There was no choice, so he might as well admit it. Merlin lifted his head, although his eyes became serious, but his face still had a hint of a smile. "I didn't expect it, I've been hiding... or playing a role."

"What? This guy is Elgin, the great sword master? Lady Knight, are you sure you're not mistaken?" Alice suddenly interrupted Merlin, thinking it was ridiculous that he was suspected of being Elgin.

"...I'm not mistaken!" Mesfield refused to admit that he was just speculating, and he continued to say, "He's the one who's been insulting me, and he's the one who's been hiding his true identity!"

"Don't be ridiculous, the great sword master is a man of excellent character, not only is he strong, but he also has a sense of responsibility that is worthy of respect. As for Merlin?" Alice glanced at Merlin, with a personal tone, "He's just a guy who's afraid of trouble and wants to live a carefree life, he has no sense of purpose to save the world, and he's far inferior to Elgin."

"Hmph... Merlin took a deep breath, his eyes became strange, and he thought to himself, "What's wrong with me? I'm actually Elgin, the great sword master, but why don't I feel like I have a sense of responsibility?" "What are you looking at? Didn't I say anything wrong?" Alice responded challengingly.

"...No... Merlin's expression became complex, and he couldn't say what was going on in his mind.

Since Mesfield was just speculating, he couldn't be sure that the ordinary Merlin was actually the man who shook the British Empire, and Alice's analysis made him doubt his own thoughts. With no choice, Mesfield could only let Merlin and Alice leave, and she watched their figures disappear, her mind becoming more and more puzzled and suspicious.

Maybe I was just overthinking it, that Merlin was just an ordinary black iron adventurer, and Elgin was someone else? But why did he attack me when I was following the mysterious man? We had already made amends... Could Elgin be a pervert? Seeing Mesfield's back, a flash of light appeared, and Claddia appeared beside him, looking at the already distant Merlin and Alice.

"It's not him, is it? I told you, you're just overthinking it, I don't see anything special about this Merlin, he's just an ordinary person, but he seems to be a fan of Elgin, even his sword is similar, I've seen it many times before."

"Actually, his personality is also similar." Mesfield said calmly.

"What?" Claddia was surprised.

"They both have a bit of a carefree attitude, and they look down on others..." Mesfield said seriously.

"This... can't determine that Merlin is actually Elgin..." Claddia shook her head, laughing.

"If I kissed that man, I could determine whether he's actually Elgin or not, his saliva is very unique, it can stimulate human emotions..." Mesfield suddenly said.

"Oh? That's similar to the demon's saliva..." Claddia sighed, and then her face turned pale, a large sweat droplet appeared on her forehead.

"Ah! Windsor, what did you just say? Are you joking?" Claddia wiped the sweat from her forehead, unable to understand why Mesfield was so disgusted with Elgin.

"If his wife was not by his side, I wouldn't mind trying..." Mesfield said seriously.

"...Claddia wiped her forehead again, unable to understand Mesfield's hatred for Elgin, "You said the queen knew Elgin's identity, so why do you want to know who he is? Why not ask the queen?"

"I've already asked... Mesfield raised an eyebrow, speaking in a very dissatisfied tone.

"But the queen seems to have made some kind of agreement with Elgin?" "I feel like they have a connection, the queen's attitude towards that man is a bit strange."

A few days later, Merlin and Alice sat on a horse-drawn carriage, and they were about to enter the town of Little Cow. "Merlin, do you think that child will be crying because she thinks of me? I suddenly want to go back and get her, I feel a bit excited..." Alice said to herself.

"Hmph!" Merlin rolled his eyes, muttering, "It's not like she's your own child, what's there to be excited about? If you really find her parents, you'll be... "

"I don't want to hear what you have to say, you're heartless and practical." Alice said, her face stern.

"I'm just saying the truth, you should try to find the girl's biological parents, you're not her biological mother." Merlin said seriously.

"Speaking of which, she even called you 'daddy' before, don't you have any special feelings?" Alice asked tentatively.

"It's because of you, isn't it? She's too young to understand anything." Merlin shrugged.

"Hmph, you have no compassion." Alice said, her voice full of anger.

Just as they were talking, Merlin suddenly felt a shock, and he looked ahead, seeing a familiar figure, it was the black-haired little girl they had rescued before, smiling at them.

"Halt! Halt!" Alice shouted, making Merlin stop the carriage, and she got down, squatting down in front of the little girl, opening her arms, "Come here, baby, let momma hug you."

The little girl smiled, and then looked at Alice, but instead of running to her, she walked straight to Merlin, without saying a word to Alice.

"What?!" Alice's eyes widened in surprise, feeling that it was unbelievable, she had been very attached to the little girl before, but now she just ignored her and went to Merlin instead? Children are really vengeful!

The little girl didn't say a word, but instead looked at Merlin with a smile, her eyes seemed to be thinking about something. "What's wrong? Do I have a flower on my face?" Merlin looked at the little girl, feeling puzzled, this little girl had been cold to him before, but now she suddenly came to him?

Maybe it's just a child's tantrum? Merlin thought to himself, and then he bent down, reaching out to touch the little girl's head, showing a caring attitude, but his mind was still puzzled.

Weird, this kid seems to have grown taller? Do children develop that quickly? Merlin thought to himself, and then he suddenly felt a sharp pain in his arm, looking down, he saw the little girl biting his arm, sucking his blood!

"Ah!" Merlin's eyes widened in shock, and he felt a chill run down his spine.

title: Chapter 78 — The Heir (Bonus Update)
content:
Chapter 78 — The Heir (Bonus Update)

Volume 19 · Chapter 78

Merlin’s heart trembled uncontrollably as he stared at the young girl drinking his blood. Those needle-like fangs, like straws, made her identity clear—she was a vampire!

Alice also saw this eerie scene, her eyes glowing as she grew feverish with bloodlust.

Merlin’s heart pounded violently, his life force draining rapidly, triggering the heart curse to shrink and throb with agonizing pain.

The life energy absorbed from slaughtering countless demons was being drained by Cain in such a short time, causing the stable curse to become restless.

Merlin knew this couldn’t go on—his gaze sharpened, and without hesitation, he drew his sword and severed the girl’s head in one strike.

This... thing wasn’t human! It was a ferocious vampire!

Judging by how it moved freely in sunlight, its bloodline far surpassed Dracula’s!

No wonder I couldn’t sense its presence in the dungeon back then!

It was an extremely dangerous existence—how could I have been fooled by that innocent appearance? Now I’ve been tricked into this!

“Ah!” Alice gasped, watching the child—who had just called her “mom”—have her head chopped off, her body tumbling through the air in a spray of blood.

Cain’s tiny body swayed backward before tendrils shot from the neck stump, instantly reconnecting with her flying head. She pulled it back, reattaching it to her body—but with her face turned away. It looked grotesque.

“Oh my God!” Alice turned pale, pressing her hand to her mouth as if she’d seen a ghost.

Cain twisted her head 360 degrees, the wound sealing instantly. A satisfied smile spread across her face as she licked the last traces of blood from her lips.

“Delicious... I’ve always suspected you were different. And indeed... your power far exceeds my expectations!”

“You—you damned bastard! You took advantage of our kindness!” Merlin’s cold sweat dripped as he knelt, using his sword to prop himself up. The heart curse tormented him with every beat, each pulse sending waves of unbearable pain. His vision blurred, his mind growing hazy.

“Took advantage? No. The law of the jungle is survival of the fittest. You trapped me the moment you freed me from that bottle.” Cain spoke with deliberate meaning.

“No way...” Merlin’s eyes widened in shock as he recalled the silver bottle on the altar and Cain’s story. The truth hit him like a storm—this seemingly harmless girl was a godchild, the true heir of the bloodline.

“What have you done?!” Alice’s body chilled as she summoned a violent blizzard, drawing her slender sword and lunging at Cain with overwhelming pressure, like a dragon’s roar.

Cain picked up a wooden stick from the ground, gripping it like Merlin’s sword, and attacked with the same stance.

Blood splattered everywhere as Alice was slashed open, her eyes filled with disbelief. Impossible! Besides Merlin, who else could—

“Alice!” Merlin shouted, his usual composure shattered for the first time. That attack... it was my *Blade Draw Cut*! That technique is supposed to be mine alone—almost impossible to replicate! Why?!

Alice collapsed to the ground, blood gushing from her wounds. Her face twisted in shock, her lips frothing with blood as Cain’s single strike left her on the brink of death.

Merlin, enduring the heart curse’s agony, crawled to Alice’s side. His frantic examination revealed she was barely alive, teetering on the edge of death.

Years ago, Alice had barely survived Merlin’s *Blade Draw Cut* thanks to the Hero’s legacy silver armor. But Cain had just replicated it with a wooden stick—

“Oh? Still alive? Looks like mastering what I just learned isn’t as easy as I thought.” Cain smirked, then explained, “Don’t be so surprised. This is a unique ability of our bloodline—absorbing blood allows us to perfectly replicate the victim’s abilities. I’m the true ancestor Cain, so permanent replication isn’t difficult. Like this.”

He licked the wooden stick, now stained with Alice’s blood, and suddenly cold energy mixed with dragon-like aura erupted. Golden ice shards formed behind him.

Alice’s years of hard work and power were instantly absorbed by Cain, becoming his own—an unbelievable replication ability!

“Hmm, her power isn’t as strong as yours, but it’s still excellent.” Cain nodded in evaluation. “You’re truly extraordinary—beneath that ordinary appearance lies terrifying strength. Ruthless, brutal, and fierce—unmatched. I even think... you’re more dangerous than my mother.”

Merlin cradled the near-dead Alice, his eyes burning with fury. He gripped his sword, but the heart’s pain paralyzed him. Keeping consciousness was all he could manage.

Cain studied Alice’s pale face, his gaze turning sinister. “Funny... her face is almost identical to my mother’s. If I met her in the heavens, I’d never tell them apart. Too bad she’s not my real mother—just a resemblance.”

Dickter stepped out of the shadows, his movements slow. Unlike Cain, he feared sunlight and had to hide beneath his black cloak, even in daylight.

Worthy of being a godchild—he instantly suppressed the legendary Great Demon Lord...

The ambush was shocking enough!

Dickter wiped cold sweat, approaching Cain respectfully. “Master, are we done?”

“Mm, I’ve no further use for them. Their power is mine now—I’ll make good use of it.” Cain spoke coldly.

“Then... why not just kill them here and now? Eliminate the threat entirely!” Dickter drew his flame demon spear, aiming it at Merlin’s forehead.

“Don’t point weapons at me, or you’ll regret it.” Merlin’s gaze burned with killing intent. This scheming rat, Dickter, dared to threaten him? It reminded him of the humiliation he suffered as a child at the hands of the Hero with the gun!

“Uh...” Dickter’s eyes flickered with fear. Even in his weakened state, Merlin’s aura was enough to terrify him.

“Forget it. They’re as good as dead anyway. They’re the ones who freed me—let them enjoy their last moments. That’s my final mercy.” Cain turned and left without another word. “Come on.”

“...” Dickter hesitated but obeyed, sheathing his weapon and following.

“You’re the second bastard in my life I want to kill with my own hands!” Merlin clutched Alice, his teeth grinding from the heart’s agony. His entire body radiated icy killing intent. “I swear, I’ll slaughter you, you little bastard! Next time we meet, I’ll make you taste the despair of falling into the abyss! Hide as much as you want—when you die, you’ll realize how lucky you were that I didn’t kill you today...”

“Ah~ is that so? I hope so.” Cain stopped, turning back with a childlike, innocent smile. “Merlin Papa, Alice Mama, I love you from the bottom of my heart.”

“But...”

“Still, farewell. I’ll use your power to fulfill my dreams.”

---

**Afterword**

Many people think this chapter is long, but it’s actually two volumes combined.

Originally, I planned to have Dracula’s defeat in one volume, with Cain’s foreshadowing and twist in another. But since the two storylines are too close, merging them keeps the flow better.

Merlin being ambushed was part of the original design, especially with his curse triggered.

Vampires gaining their prey’s abilities through blood absorption was mentioned early on, though Cain’s power is exaggerated here.

The bloodline storyline’s final Cain is the true Big Boss, inheriting Merlin and Alice’s power—both stats and intelligence at their peak.

I’ve mentioned before that the bloodline story will adjust some details, focusing more on side characters and villains, as many readers requested.

Cain’s design is closely tied to Merlin and Alice, and he has his own goals. Later, many of the things you care about will connect. Most of what I’ve shared in background stories isn’t filler—it’s foreshadowing for future events.

Many clues can be found in the background stories I’ve told. I’ve seen some readers’ guesses, and only one came close—like they’d seen the outline.

As for the *Blade Draw Cut* being replicated, it’s not a major issue. Alice didn’t die, so Cain couldn’t fully unleash its power, but his strength is still terrifying.

The book hints that the *Godslayer Misttin* can seal resurrection abilities—you should understand that.

The next volume will fill in the gaps, with Merlin regrouping. Stay tuned, and goodnight...

title: Chapter 1 — Imminent Danger
content:
Chapter 1 — Imminent Danger

Volume 20 · Chapter 1

In the wooden house of Little Cow Town, this was the residence of the old Mr. Arcalon. At this time, the weather had already entered early winter, although it had not yet snowed, the temperature had dropped sharply. Merlin was wrapped in a blanket, white breath slowly exhaled from his nostrils, he hid in the corner of the room, deliberately avoiding the sunlight that shone in. Not far from the fireplace, the firewood was burning fiercely, occasionally producing a "crack" explosion, constantly alleviating the low temperature. Alice was quietly lying on the bed, without any vitality, deathly pale, her face was so white that it seemed like she was a corpse. Merlin's curse was gradually calming down, this was only temporary, it would frequently occur later. Gadiel not only replicated Merlin's abilities, but also absorbed almost all of his collected life force, leaving him in a precarious situation where the curse could strike at any moment. Merlin carried the dying Alice and directly went to the nearest residence of the old Mr. Arcalon, temporarily only able to choose to stay here. Over the past two days, Merlin had thought a lot, although Gadiel had not said too much, carefully recalling all the events, he discovered numerous clues. Gadiel was the one who had inadvertently opened the bottle and released him, and then lost his memory for some reason, was caught by the human traffickers. Coincidentally, he met himself and Alice again, recovered his memory, and chose to steal their powers. Merlin could not understand more details, and could only guess the general situation, combining the legend of the Holy Church's twin gods and Gadiel's words, he knew that - Gadiel was sealed by his mother for countless years, his hatred for his mother had reached an irreconcilable point, he wanted to connect the mortal world and the heavens, and to revenge against his mother. Merlin looked at the Banri Garan in his hand, he felt that he was not unbeatable by Gadiel, but was restrained by the troublesome revival and regeneration ability. He realized that relying solely on the Banri Garan was not enough to handle various situations, he needed a more special weapon that could suppress the troublesome revival and regeneration ability. The Banri Garan was similar to a blood-drinking sword, it could constantly absorb life force for Merlin, but it was of little use against an enemy with infinite revival. Merlin would need a second weapon to completely eliminate the revival and regeneration ability that restrained him, a weapon similar to a death sentence that could suppress or even kill healing-type abilities. However, equipment with unique abilities only appeared in rare quality or above, such equipment was not easily obtained, and required a certain amount of luck. It seemed that to kill Gadiel, a troublesome enemy, he needed to prepare carefully. Merlin sighed, looked at his arm, which had been bitten by Gadiel, leaving two small holes, his physical body was already beginning to deteriorate, his skin was showing purple-black color, and his blood vessels were exposed. He hesitated for a moment, placed his arm in the sunlight that shone through the window, and immediately sparks flew, white smoke rose, and his arm was burned by the sunlight. Merlin had been bitten by Gadiel, the blood of the vampire had already begun to invade his body, constantly eroding it, which was also the reason why he avoided sunlight. The speed of erosion was so fast, it was terrifying, in just two days, Merlin's entire arm had deteriorated. After all, Gadiel was the true ancestor, not a small fry like Medus, the toxin was enhanced, far exceeding the erosion speed of the old king. Now, Merlin's life was only about a month left, and eventually, his consciousness would be eroded, and he would become a bloodthirsty undead. Merlin's current situation was already very miserable, with the curse, the vampire's toxin, and the current situation, it was the most miserable situation he had experienced in a long time, the last time was when he faced the Gun Hero, Obrien. Alice's situation was also not optimistic, although she was often severely injured, this time was the closest to complete death. Merlin had already tested it with his saliva, Alice's injuries were too severe, and the saliva was no longer effective, if the injuries were lighter, he could still raise Alice. In the past two days, there had been over a dozen priests who came, looked at Alice's situation, and all shook their heads, unable to do anything, because treatment was only for the living, and was ineffective for the dead, in the eyes of these professional priests, Alice was actually already dead, and the last breath was likely to be a return to life. If Gadiel had not been unable to completely grasp Merlin's slash, it was likely that even if he used a wooden stick, Alice would have died on the spot, and would have left a hint of breath? It was clearly impossible. Gadiel said "let the two enjoy their last moments", it seemed that he was not joking, the current situation was indeed difficult to solve, and saving Alice was an urgent matter. Merlin raised his head, saw the old Mr. Arcalon rushing in from outside, and immediately asked, "What did the most experienced priest say?" The old Mr. Arcalon looked embarrassed, hesitated, and said, "That... Merlin stood up, speaking seriously, "Don't have any pressure, say it." The most experienced priest said that Alice was still alive, it was a miracle, this kind of situation was impossible to save, it was better to prepare for the worst." The old Mr. Arcalon spoke with a sorrowful tone. Merlin was stunned, turned around, and came to Alice's side, looking at her pale face, "What kind of joke is this, even if Alice's soul falls into hell, I still want to pull her back..." The old Mr. Arcalon lowered his head, understanding Merlin's current feelings. However, bringing a living person back from hell was clearly impossible, only a few special magic could do it. It was still a matter of reviving as a ghost, no longer a human, and would be controlled by the ruler of hell forever. "We have already found many priests, they all cannot do anything, Merlin, you should face reality." "What reality?" Merlin turned his head, speaking seriously, "I see with my own eyes, that is reality, Alice still has a breath left, she is not dead, this is reality!" The old Mr. Arcalon did not say anything else, thinking about Merlin and Alice's husband-and-wife situation, suddenly suffered this calamity, no one could accept it, "Actually, I also have a bit of responsibility, if I could have discovered that girl's abnormality earlier, maybe Alice would not have encountered this situation." "It's not your fault, don't blame yourself, we were completely deceived by Gadiel's innocent appearance, from the human traffickers' dungeon, who would have thought that the rescued child was a dangerous existence?" Merlin thought that if he had discovered this child on the altar, he would have been more cautious, but he was rescued from the human traffickers' dungeon, it became too normal, and various coincidences avoided all warnings. "Yes, it's too coincidental, who would believe that the rescued child from the dungeon was a dangerous monster?" The old Mr. Arcalon shook his head helplessly, turned around, and rummaged through the boxes, finding the oil painting left by Gadiel, "This is the thing left by that monster, when I first saw it, I felt something was off, the painting skill and technique... how could a child with no teeth yet paint like this?" "Ah..." Merlin carefully observed, the outstanding painting skill, the lifelike figures, made people feel like the painted people were alive. Two children offered gifts to the goddess, Gadiel was filled with expectation, while the one that should be marked with a red "X" was Abel, and he could sense Gadiel's jealousy and hatred. The goddess's face, with Alice's appearance, was particularly striking, looked at Abel with affection, but completely ignored the dirty Gadiel. Merlin furrowed his brow, his attention was drawn to the goddess, if Gadiel had not said otherwise, the goddess's appearance was too similar to Alice, it was like one mold carved out. Why was Alice's appearance so similar to the demon race's archenemy? Could a human's appearance really be similar to the goddess in the heavens? Was there some unknown secret, or was it just a simple coincidence? The old Mr. Arcalon looked at Merlin's changing expression, couldn't help but try to probe, "Gadiel's oil painting may contain some deeper meaning, Alice may not be...". Merlin's face turned pale, grasped the oil painting roughly, and directly threw it into the fireplace, the flames instantly engulfed the painting, turning it into black ash. "Alice is Alice." Absolutely not something mysterious.

title: Chapter 2 — Searching for the Great Potion Wizard (Extra)
content:
Chapter 2 — Searching for the Great Potion Wizard (Extra)

Volume 20 · Chapter 2

“......Is that so!” Old Akalon embarrassedly scratched his head, agreeing, “Miss Alice is Miss Alice, how could she possibly be connected to some inexplicable heavenly thing, haha... I must be getting old, liking to overthink.... ....Merlin didn’t speak, just stared at Alice lying quietly on the bed. It wasn’t that he had no doubts, but he was unwilling to believe that the lively girl he’d lived with for so long had any connection to heavenly deities. This wasn’t a sign that everything about him had been arranged; in the eyes of that bitch Goddess of Light, he was nothing but an ant she could crush in her palm.... Old Akalon watched Merlin’s silent demeanor and couldn’t help but sigh, “Lord Merlin, I understand how you feel now, but some things cannot be changed. Miss Alice this time... might not be so lucky.... “There must be a way. I don’t believe someone as fortunate as her would die so easily.” Merlin said firmly, never having imagined Alice would die. After all, the guy who escaped death from his own sword slash still hasn’t used up his lifetime luck—how could he be defeated by his own counterfeit? “But many... have already confirmed Miss Alice has no hope.” Old Akalon said cautiously. “If a person’s life is held in someone else’s mouth, that’s just too pitiful.” Merlin sat, staring at the lifeless Alice. “...Yes...” Seeing Merlin so insistent, Old Akalon felt that saying more was useless. “Actually, I had a bit of doubt at first—you and Miss Alice don’t look like a married couple; you seem more like people forced together. But... I’ve dismissed that idea now. Surely you really like Miss Alice, right?” Merlin’s face showed no ripple; he murmured calmly, “I just enjoy watching this guy get furious and angry, and seeing my own helpless, foolish self.” ) Little Mao said “Ah... like that...” Old Akalon’s expression turned strange, thinking, What is this? Lord Merlin just likes to torment Alice? Doesn’t seem like it. “Old Mr. Akalon, besides finding a priest, do you have any other options? In terms of experience, you’re far more seasoned than us....” Merlin turned to Old Akalon, facing this helpless situation, he could only consult an experienced elder. Although Merlin is old enough, his knowledge of the demon race is deep, but regarding the human world, he truly can’t compare to the experience of human elders. After all, this shut‑in Demon Lord had hardly ever left the Death Swamp before, and hasn’t been away long; his understanding of the human world is shallow. Old Akalon suddenly felt immense pressure, vaguely sensing that the burden of saving Alice rested on his shoulders. Seeing Merlin’s expectant eyes, he couldn’t think of anything, nor could he bring himself to speak. This guy, who became a silver‑rank adventurer thanks to superhuman patience, has limited abilities, and is likewise experiencing for the first time this desperate situation that makes people despair. But Old Akalon is also quite experienced; though he can’t claim to be widely knowledgeable, he’s heard plenty of rumors. “Since Lord Merlin asked me, I’ll tell you everything I know. Miss Alice’s condition is now extremely dangerous. According to the rumors I’ve heard, the only person capable of pulling her back from the brink of death is likely just one, though I don’t know if it will succeed.” Merlin’s eyes widened, as if he’d grabbed a lifeline, he urgently asked, “Who? Who exactly can save Alice?” “Lord Merlin hasn’t been in the adventurer business long, so he knows little about those mysterious purple‑gold adventurers....” Old Akalon frowned. “Purple‑gold adventurers?” Merlin thought he wasn’t that ignorant—wasn’t the Gregory he hammered away one of them? I heard he’s still unconscious. “Yeah, among adventurers we always say: as long as a soul hasn’t scattered, if you meet an old witch carrying bottles and jars, there’s still hope to survive.” Old Akalon said seriously. “Old... witch... who is it?” Merlin pressed. “This old witch refers to a specific mysterious purple‑gold adventurer, famed as the greatest healing master, the savior of adventurers....” Old Akalon could only rely on memory to recount this mysterious adventurer to Merlin: “Rumor has it she’s masterful in potion‑craft; any potion she makes becomes a family heirloom, priceless no matter the cost. She has many methods—her poison can leave a kingdom littered with corpses, her elixir can turn a dead land into a spring‑filled paradise—truly miraculous.” The more Merlin listened, the more it rang a bell, though Old Akalon’s account sounded almost divine, possibly exaggerated. Still, the name of this purple‑gold adventurer? “Her name is Seysi, the Grand Potion Witch Seysi.” Old Akalon spoke the name circulated among adventurers, “But she appears and disappears unpredictably; few have seen her. In my half‑life I’ve never met this potion master; I hear she’s very low‑key, prefers to stay home.” Merlin lowered his head, recalling that he’d heard this name not long ago in the royal capital. Margaret had obtained a miraculous potion from her, reviving the dying old king, solving a situation that left many helpless—indeed she had real skill. If I remember correctly, this mysterious purple‑gold adventurer should be living in the White Dew Forest of France? Margaret had once sent a messenger there.... Merlin felt the matter was nine‑tenths certain; he thought the urgent thing now was to save Alice, and this purple‑gold adventurer Seysi was probably the only hope, with no other choice. “Tomorrow I’ll carry Alice and set out to find this Grand Potion Witch!” The next day, at the exit of Little Ox Town, Old Akalon saw Merlin off. Merlin hoisted Alice onto his back, tying her to himself for stability. Yesterday, seeing how quickly Akalon had made a decision, Merlin felt a flutter of panic. He had only passed along the rumors to Merlin and couldn’t guarantee that the Grand Potion Witch could save Alice. If something went wrong, he feared he couldn’t bear that responsibility. “Lord Merlin, I’ve only told you rumors; I don’t know whether this Grand Potion Witch can actually save Miss Alice.” “Besides this, is there any other way to save Alice?” Merlin countered. “...I really can’t think of anything....” Old Akalon scratched his head, feeling sorry. “Then we have no choice; no matter what, it’s better than sitting here waiting to die—worth a try!” Merlin’s gaze turned resolute. “Terribly sorry... I really can’t help much; I can only pray for you in my heart.” Old Akalon sighed. “This is enough. In fact, you’ve already helped us a lot. Thank you for your care, and thanks to Mr. Karl for introducing us.” Merlin smiled, turned with the lifeless Alice on his back, and said, “We’ll meet again if fate allows.” “Safe travels!” Old Akalon waved, watching them fade into the distance. Just this.... Merlin carried Alice onto the road to seek a cure. And Merlin himself, eroded by the blood‑clan toxin, has only about a month left. Both of their situations are grim.

title: Chapter 3 — Pharmaceutical Apprentice
content:
Chapter 3 — Pharmaceutical Apprentice

Volume 20 · Chapter 3

A week after that, in a valley somewhere in France, this place was desolate, with not even a single blade of grass to be seen, and all over the place were the bones of beasts that had been weathered by the wind. But on this land that was as still as death, there was a dense forest in the central area, looking incredibly resplendent. Because the trees that towered above were unlike any others, they were pure white all over, and even their leaves shone with a metallic luster, looking like knives. Even though it was already autumn, these leaves didn't wither at all, and they swayed gently in the wind, producing a sound similar to that of a bell. Merlin stood outside this mysterious forest, carrying the barely-alive Alice on his back, and looked around at everything in sight. "This is... the White Forest, right? It doesn't look like a peaceful place at all... Merlin furrowed his brow, and a sense of unease rose up inside him, feeling that this forest was hiding some sort of secret, like it was a massive mechanism itself. In fact, this White Forest was located in a very secluded area, and Merlin had only been able to find it after searching for a long time. If it weren't for the fact that he had heard about it from Margaret when he was in the castle, Merlin wouldn't have been able to find the White Forest where the great wizard lived. Merlin swallowed hard, his heart racing, and tightened his grip on Alice, before forcing himself to step into the forest, looking up at the countless metallic leaves above him, which made him feel even more fearful, like he was about to face a storm of knives. Curious Merlin tentatively reached out to touch these pure white trees, and found that they weren't just cold, but also incredibly hard, like iron. How amazing, these trees had no life at all, and were completely cultivated using some special method. Being able to cultivate iron trees, and creating a massive forest, the owner's idea was truly astonishing... Merlin's heart filled with admiration, and the iron tree forest in front of him was a natural defense barrier, and anyone who entered had to be careful. Suddenly, a loud shout echoed out, and it seemed that someone had already discovered Merlin, the unwelcome guest. "Who's there?!" "Huh?!" Merlin stopped in his tracks, only hearing the voice, but not seeing anyone. "This is private property, and outsiders are not allowed to enter. If you know what's good for you, you'd better leave quickly!" A warning came from the shadows, and it seemed that this place wasn't welcoming to outsiders.
