"Captain Dennis?"

"Hah, it’s been a long time..."

"How’s your family’s eldest miss, Cecilia?"

title: Chapter 15 — Ships
content:
Chapter 15 — Ships

Volume 20 · Chapter 15

"Merlin, sir! ?" Dennis saw Merlin's expression, which was a mix of a smile and a frown, and his mind immediately turned upside down, scaring him not a little.

He couldn't help but think back to their last meeting, when Merlin and his people were on the William, heading to the island of the evil alchemist, and in the end, they had to split the island in two with brute force! Such a powerful ability would naturally leave a lasting impression, and Merlin's strong presence would be hard to forget.

Dennis' brain went blank, unsure of what to say, only feeling that his two subordinates had gotten themselves into a bit of trouble. In fact, Merlin hadn't expected to run into Dennis, the captain of the William, a merchant ship that often sailed the seas for the sake of the Rose family's business, and yet, here they were, meeting in the port of France.

Merlin looked at Dennis, the captain, pointing a gun at his head, and his mood was a bit off, "Can you please not point a gun at me? I think we don't need to be so tense, do we?"

"Ah! Sorry... Dennis, the captain, woke up from his dream, quickly putting away his gun and taking off his tattered captain's hat to bow to Merlin, "It's been a long time, Merlin, sir."

"Yes, it's been a long time since we defeated that evil alchemist," Merlin smiled, impressed by Dennis' bravery.

"How did you end up here alone? Is Alice not with you?" Dennis asked.

"...Merlin's expression turned gloomy, Alice was suddenly not by his side, and he felt a bit uneasy, but he didn't need to tell anyone about her injuries, that was between the two of them, "She's... dealing with some issues, and for now, I'm... handling it myself."

"...Dennis, the captain, noticed that Merlin's expression wasn't quite right, and he sensed that something was amiss, but Merlin didn't want to talk about it, so he didn't pry further.

"How are Cecilia and Kel doing?" Merlin asked, changing the subject.

"The duke thinks Cecilia is disobedient, so she's been sent to the Royal Academy for further education, and Kel is accompanying her," Dennis replied with a hint of resignation, "To be honest, I spend most of my time at sea, so I don't know much about what's going on with the young lady."

"That's... Merlin nodded, thinking that the Royal Academy was a place where nobles went to learn magic and martial arts, founded by the royal family themselves, and inviting many famous teachers to teach.

In the distance, two burly sailors looked at their captain, who was not only not defending them, but also chatting with Merlin like an old friend, and they didn't quite understand.

So, the two of them walked up, trying to stir up trouble, hoping that Dennis would teach this young upstart a lesson and regain some face.

"Captain! That's him! He's the one who just beat us up! Why are you chatting with him so happily?"

"Yes, this good-for-nothing, he's been bullying our sailors on the William, and now he's looking for trouble! "

...Merlin's cold laughter echoed, his eyes gleaming with meaning as he looked at Dennis, "What? You two are my subordinates? You were just extorting money from me, weren't you?"

Dennis, the captain, heard Merlin's words, and his face turned dark, realizing that his two subordinates were not as good as he thought, and they were taking advantage of his position to bully people.

He believed in Merlin's character, and in this situation, there was no need to lie, he was completely at the mercy of his two subordinates, and he almost made a fatal mistake.

So, Dennis, the captain, turned around, slapping the two sailors with a loud slap, and speaking in a menacing tone, "Shut up! You two, don't dare say another word without permission... I'll cut out your tongues!"

The two sailors were shocked, covering their swollen faces, still trying to figure out what was going on.

Seeing Dennis, the captain, looking terrified, maybe this ordinary-looking guy was actually someone to be reckoned with?

"Get down and apologize to Merlin, sir! If you don't satisfy him, you'll be dinner for the sharks tonight!"

The two sailors paled, looking at each other, finally realizing they had made a mistake, and they cowered, bowing their heads and apologizing loudly, "Sir, we were wrong, we won't do it again, we won't... "

"Oh, you know you were wrong?" Merlin's mouth twisted into a smile, his voice low, "Which one of you is refusing to apologize and making me bite him?"

One of the sailors quickly pointed to his companion, trying to show their fake brotherhood, "He is! He is!"

...The other sailor quickly slapped himself in the face, making a loud slapping sound, and crying, "I'm sorry! I won't dare! Please, sir, spare me!"

"Merlin, sir, you want to do what you want with them, they may have joined the William recently, but they are still my subordinates, and offending you is unforgivable, all you need to do is say the word, and I'll make them disappear from this world..."

Dennis, the captain, spoke seriously, his piercing eyes not joking.

Merlin thought for a moment, thinking that he didn't want to deal with the two insignificant sailors, and besides, they were Dennis' subordinates, and he could still show some mercy.

Moreover, Dennis, the captain, was too good at handling people, and he had clearly expressed his stance, leaving the decision to Merlin, which was a sign of respect.

"No need, I'm not interested in dealing with these two insignificant people..."

"Not bad, Merlin, sir, your character is so kind that it's an insult to these two scoundrels... Dennis, the captain, looked at Merlin, secretly relieved, it's not easy to find a good sailor, "Hear that? The kind Merlin, sir, has forgiven you, and you'd better get out of here quickly!"

The two sailors, like they had been pardoned, bowed deeply, thanking Merlin, and then, in terror, they scrambled to get out of the tavern, afraid that Merlin would change his mind and take their lives.

"My people have caused you trouble, and I'm truly sorry."

Dennis, the captain, sat down beside Merlin.

"No need to be so polite, I've seen my share of chaos in the port, and it's nothing to worry about..."

Merlin's expression was as calm as ever, "I want to go to the mysterious sea, but I've been here for days, and I still can't find a ship willing to take me, can you help me arrange something? Even if it's just getting me to the area near the mysterious sea..."

"Unknowable mysterious sea?!" Dennis, the captain, was shocked, his mouth wide open, "Merlin, sir, are you... "

"Merlin, sir, you're not joking, are you?"

title: Chapter 16 — Join the Fleet (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 16 — Join the Fleet (Extra Chapter)

Volume 20 · Chapter 16

“Of course, I wasn't joking. If I could find a ship, why would I be stuck here drinking alone?” Merlin chuckled to himself.

“Merlin, I must confess, my journey this time is to the unknown mysterious sea,” said Dennis, the captain, with a serious expression.

“Ah?” Merlin was taken aback, his mind racing. Dennis was also going? He was the one who had been searching for a ship for days, and now someone had come to him? “Is this really... Dennis, you're looking around, lowering your voice, “I heard that the previous Duke of Overre's rebellion was manipulated by a mysterious alien tribe in secret. This is the Queen's heart disease, wanting to know who is behind the plot to control the empire. So, not long ago, the Queen requisitioned the Duke's warships and sent a trusted general to investigate the mysterious sea. Unfortunately, at the time, I was just returning from delivering goods to England, and the William was chosen by the Duke, and was incorporated into the investigation team of the mysterious sea.”

Merlin furrowed his brow, looking at Dennis's gloomy expression, thinking that this was just bad luck. He had just returned and was chosen to enter the death zone, “Why didn't Elizabeth have any available naval forces? Did she need to ask the Duke of Rose to requisition them?”

“There are only two countries that have the power to compete for ocean control, Britain and Spain. The Royal Navy is mostly stationed in the southern islands to defend against Spanish aggression, and there are no easily deployable fleets,” Dennis said, shaking his head, “After the rebellion, the Duke took over many of the Overre family's businesses and became much richer than before. Now, the Queen needs ships, and the Duke has no reason to refuse. Besides, our Duke is very loyal, and won't easily refuse the Queen's request.”

Merlin thought that this was just the result of eating too much, and now it was time to spit it out, “So, you're saying that your William is not a commercial ship? Putting it in a warship is too weak, right?”

“Commercial ship?” Dennis smiled strangely, speaking in a low voice, “I think Merlin knows that the William is a legitimate warship. I've been a pirate, and I know that the Empire's open sea permit is just a piece of paper in certain situations. The big sea is all about fists, my ship is more solid, more stable, and more powerful than ordinary warships.”

Merlin looked at Dennis's smile, thinking that people who had been pirates had a bit of a violent tendency, “Merlin, I'll be honest with you, I'm glad you're here. I was looking for a ship, and you just happened to come to me. I hope you can join my crew.”

Dennis extended his right hand, speaking sincerely, “This time, we're going to a place where all sailors are afraid of, the Death Sea. The more strong people we have, the better our chances. I've seen your abilities, and I believe you can create another miracle. We'll be the first crew to ever leave the mysterious sea alive.”

Merlin looked at Dennis's eyes, knowing that the other was hoping he would join him, and there was a sense of security. However, Merlin was in need of a ship, and Dennis's request made the two of them click into place immediately.

Dennis led Merlin to the William's anchorage, saying that he wanted to introduce him to some people, including the Queen's trusted advisors. Since Merlin was joining the crew mid-journey, he needed to get to know the others to avoid any misunderstandings during the voyage.

“I've sailed the William around the edge of the mysterious sea before. It's not bragging, but as long as I have a compass, I can navigate the ship to the exact location with my eyes closed. However, it's extremely dangerous, with numerous reefs, strong underwater currents, and a thick fog that makes it impossible to see more than a few feet in front of you. It's like a portal to another dimension...”

“Oh,” Merlin listened to Dennis's words, not showing much interest. He only wanted to enter the mysterious sea to find the deep-sea clam and get the pearl inside.

“Hey, Dennis! What are you doing? We've already been delayed for an hour...”

A sturdy young man approached, speaking in a slow, complaining tone. Merlin slightly raised his eyelids to look at this person, and his expression changed to one of surprise. It was Morrison, the sixth-ranked Thistle Knight? He was the Queen's trusted advisor.

Morrison was not wearing any conspicuous armor, but a casual-looking jacket, which made him look like he was on a secret mission. “I went to do some things, but I met an old friend on the way, who also wanted to go to the mysterious sea, so I brought him back.”

Dennis gestured to the side, introducing, “This is Merlin, a very powerful person. He's joining our crew this time, and with him on board, we'll be safer.”

Morrison furrowed his brow, carefully examining Merlin, thinking that he looked very familiar. “Huh? Oh? Um?”

Merlin's forehead broke out in a cold sweat, thinking that he looked at him? Didn't he see how handsome he was? “Oh! Oh! Oh!”

Morrison's eyes lit up, and he exclaimed, “I remember! We had a man-to-man competition in the castle, a battle of muscles and muscles! I still remember it vividly!”

“That was just a wrist-wrestling match, right? Please don't make it sound so meaningful, thank you,” Merlin rolled his eyes.

“What? Don't be so cold! Don't you like this simple test of strength? It's a romantic thing for men, isn't it?”

Morrison walked up to Merlin, patting him on the shoulder, “It's a way to unleash one's physical potential, to splash with crystal-clear sweat...”

Merlin pushed Morrison's hand away, suppressing his urge to spit out angry words, and thought that working with someone as simple-minded as him was always a headache.

“Since you two know each other, it's okay for Merlin to join the crew, right? Morrison, what do you think?”

Dennis asked, looking at Morrison, who had the final say in this matter. “This...”

Morrison looked at Merlin, and suddenly, he had a disagreement, “We object! Two people walked up, a man and a woman, both wearing shining silver adventurer badges, from London, the capital of Britain. They seemed to be hired adventurers.

The man, Adam, was slender, with half his face hidden by his hair, and he had a lute on his back, dressed like a bohemian poet. The woman, Renée, was fiery, with long, auburn hair tied up in a high ponytail, wearing futuristic glasses, and a simple leather jacket and shirt, looking like an engineer.

They heard the conversation about Merlin joining the crew, and they couldn't help but interrupt, “This journey is extremely dangerous, and we can't afford to add any more burdens. This guy from Recksemm is clearly useless.”

“Yes, safety is our top priority. If we encounter danger, we won't have the energy to protect unnecessary...”

Merlin's face turned red, his eyebrows deeply furrowed, looking at the two silver adventurers from London, “I'm not useless! I don't need anyone to protect me! Are these words meant for me?”

(-_-)

title: Chapter 17 — Captain’s Cabin
content:
Chapter 17 — Captain’s Cabin

Volume 20 · Chapter 17

Merlin gazed at the two adventurers from London, a sense of resignation washing over him. Was he really a burden that needed to be protected? The person who said that must be incredibly confident.

"Please, gentlemen, don't speak carelessly. Merlin's abilities are far from ordinary, and he will undoubtedly be a valuable asset to our journey, not a burden. I hope you can retract your previous statements." Dennis, the captain, spoke seriously, his expression stern. He had deliberately brought Merlin on board, and now that he was being rejected, he was determined to help him out.

"Far from ordinary?" Adam's gaze flicked to Merlin, his lip curling in disdain. "Captain, are you joking? We're not children. We're adventurers from the city of London."

"Yes, the adventurers from London are all quite skilled, with the exception of Chris, the fighter. And as for this young man...he's clearly just starting out, only capable of doing low-level tasks like helping old ladies cross the street. Far from ordinary? It's not possible." Rene laughed, her eyes fixed on Merlin.

Dennis was taken aback, his eyebrows furrowed in surprise. He had never encountered adventurers from the capital who were so sharp-tongued and arrogant.

However, Adam and Rene did have reason to be proud. The London Adventurers' Guild was a prestigious organization, renowned for its exceptional members. In past competitions, the guild's members had consistently achieved impressive results, earning them a reputation as a force to be reckoned with.

Not to mention their guildmaster, a legendary purple-grade adventurer, who had been defeated by Merlin with a single punch and was still recovering to this day...

"If you two can take Merlin seriously, I think you'll change your minds. I've had the privilege of traveling with Merlin to a remote island, where I witnessed him single-handedly turn the tide of battle and even split the island in two. Based on that alone, he has the qualifications to join our team."

"Is being able to split an island something to be proud of?" Adam scoffed, even suspecting that Dennis was exaggerating.

"If we two were to put our all into it, we could probably do the same thing. That island was probably just a small hill, right?" Rene chuckled.

Dennis's face darkened, and he wondered if his words had been so ineffective. The island was indeed large, and Merlin had likely held back during the battle.

Adam and Rene's reactions were like they were trivializing something that was truly awe-inspiring. It was clear that they were from the capital, but they seemed to be lacking in some way.

"Please, gentlemen..."

"Good, don't bother explaining." Merlin patted Dennis on the shoulder, stopping him from continuing. "I assure you, I won't be a burden, and I don't need your protection. Is that satisfactory?"

"Flattery is cheap. You're not even in our league, and we're going to a very dangerous place. You understand, don't you?" Rene said seriously.

"That's right. I think you should have some self-awareness before you decide to take on a challenge. If you want to join us, you should at least have the ability to keep up." Adam didn't bother looking at Merlin.

"If I had to, I'd like to know if you two could stop me?" Merlin furrowed his brow, his hand tightening around the hilt of his sword.

"Ah? You've got a lot of nerve..." Adam narrowed his eyes, seemingly uninterested in teaching Merlin a lesson.

"Low-level adventurers these days are really lacking in respect... " Rene's expression flashed with a cold, mocking smile.

Morrison, who had been silent until then, suddenly spoke up: "Fine, I agree to let Merlin join the team, but this mission is extremely dangerous, so you'd better take care of yourself."

"This is something I can return to you verbatim." Merlin's expression softened.

"Hey, what's going on? You're just going to let a weakling join us and cause trouble?" Rene complained.

"You're just a hired hand, and you don't have the right to interfere with my decisions. You're not part of the Adventurers' Guild." Morrison said bluntly.

Adam and Rene might be unhappy, but they didn't argue further. Morrison was in charge of the ship, and they were just hired hands.

"Oh, by the way, Merlin's physical strength is quite impressive. He once beat me once, and it's not like you said, he's not completely useless. Of course, I wasn't exactly trying my best at the time..." Morrison said nonchalantly.

Merlin couldn't help but roll his eyes, thinking that Morrison was implying that he would win if he tried harder. In a way, this simple-minded person was even more detestable than Adam and Rene.

Adam and Rene exchanged skeptical glances, wondering if Morrison was telling the truth. Had he really beaten the Seventh Thorn Knight in a physical contest? It was unlikely that Morrison would make up such a story just to get Merlin to join the team...

A full moon hung in the dark sky, and the sound of waves and wind filled the air. The heavily armed William was sailing across the sea, followed by several warships.

This time, the number of soldiers sent by Queen Elizabeth was not large, with fewer than a thousand soldiers in the team.

Their mission was to enter the mysterious sea, gather as much information as possible, and figure out the danger that threatened the kingdom's security.

As long as Morrison's team didn't lose contact, the queen would find another way to deal with the danger, trying to eliminate it before it was too late.

Inside the captain's quarters on the William, Dennis warmly invited Merlin to drink with him, thanking him for joining the team.

Dennis pulled out a bottle of fine red wine that he had kept for a long time and shared it with Merlin.

Merlin took a sip and was immediately impressed, his eyes widening. The flavor was rich and smooth, with a sweet aftertaste, a high-end wine that was likely from a famous winery.

Unfortunately, Merlin had no idea about wine, and he couldn't tell just by the taste where it came from. That was a skill that only wine connoisseurs possessed.

"Merlin, how is it?" Dennis asked, his face beaming with pride, holding up his wine glass.

"Two thousand?" Merlin's eyes widened in surprise, staring at the transparent red liquid in his glass. He thought that just a small sip would cost hundreds of gold coins, and this was just pure extravagance!

However, Dennis was a capable person, and enjoying fine wine was nothing out of the ordinary for him. It was just the price that made him hesitate...

"Yes, it's expensive, but it's worth it. Every time I taste this familiar flavor, I feel like I'm back in my hometown, reminiscing about my carefree youth, wandering around with my trusty sword, Blayke..." Dennis said wistfully, his eyes gazing into the past.

As a former high-ranking naval commander, he still couldn't shake off his love for his hometown.

Merlin looked at this unyielding sea eagle, suddenly realizing that he didn't know much about this strong-willed old man.

However, as he glanced around the captain's quarters, he noticed the many antique decorations, filled with the patina of age, revealing that Dennis was not as straightforward as he seemed.

Suddenly, Merlin's attention was drawn to a painting on the wall, a beautiful woman wearing a long dress, her head adorned with a crystal crown, sitting elegantly in a chair.

The blue pendant around the woman's neck looked eerily similar to the one worn by Alice...

title: Chapter 18 — Dark Clouds Gather (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 18 — Dark Clouds Gather (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 20 · Chapter 18

Merlin's interest suddenly piqued, he couldn't help but walk up to the painting, holding his wine cup, and take a close look at it. As he got closer, he could see the painting more clearly, and suddenly he discovered that the woman in the painting was extremely beautiful - her long, flowing hair like a waterfall, freely and loosely falling on her slender shoulders. Although she couldn't escape the ravages of time, her face still left people in awe of her beauty. The intricately designed long skirt and the crystal crown on her head seemed to be in harmony with each other, giving off a sense of wholeness. The beautiful woman was lovingly gazing at the silver-haired infant in her arms, radiating the brilliant light of motherhood to the extreme! The painting was incredibly skillful, with bold brushstrokes, far surpassing the works left behind by Cain, it was a very lively oil painting... Of course, Merlin's focus wasn't on the beautiful woman radiating motherly love in the painting, nor was it on the silver-haired infant shouting in the painting, but rather on the blue pendant around her neck. Under Merlin's intense observation, he discovered that the pendant in the painting was not just similar to Alice's pendant, but seemed to be carved from the same mold. The same color, the same craftsmanship, the same carving, even if it was said to be made by a craftsman, it wouldn't arouse any suspicion. This was the first time Merlin had seen a painting in the captain's quarters of the tavern, and he hadn't had the chance to see it last time, he didn't expect that there would be a painting that would make him think of Alice. Merlin furrowed his brow, the woman with a crown on her head, the silver-haired infant in her arms, and the pendant that was almost identical... Connecting these three things together, Merlin suddenly fell silent - was it just a coincidence? He remembered that last time, Dennis had mistakenly thought Alice was a member of the Spanish royal family. Was Alice not trying to appear simple on the surface, but was actually a princess from some kingdom? No way? Alice said she was an orphan, raised by her teacher. Although the pendant had the Spanish royal crest carved on the back, Alice's parents could also have been palace guards or maids who worked in the palace. To let their child grow up with money, they would steal something from the palace and hope that the adoptive family would help raise Alice. Merlin thought back to Alice's carefree nature, and he thought it was more likely that she was, after all, a palace maid who had stolen some small items to sell and make a living. "What's wrong?" Merlin hesitated and said, "I'm a bit interested in this painting..." Dennis, the captain, walked over curiously, looked at the painting, and said, "You're interested in this painting?" "A bit, yeah..." Merlin said, his mind not at ease. "Ha, I didn't expect you to be interested in art, you're a refined person... Dennis, the captain, seemed to have found a kindred spirit, and he was even more enthusiastic about talking to Merlin, who shared his love for art. "Who is this in the painting?" Merlin asked curiously. "This painting is called 'The Beautiful Consort', it was painted by the great painter Michelangelo during his trip to Spain, and it's a portrait of Queen Josephine," Dennis, the captain, pointed to the woman in the painting, introducing, "This is Queen Josephine, and the infant in her arms is the only princess in the kingdom, Diana. When this painting was auctioned off, it sold for 500,000 gold coins, and I, a poor old man, had to spend all my wealth to buy it..." Merlin nodded, looking at the woman in the painting, "This is the woman you mentioned earlier, the queen who was assassinated in the palace?" "That's right, it's her," Dennis, the captain, paused, remembering, "I was just a small officer, I never saw Queen Josephine in person, but I heard she was so beautiful that she would make the stars in the sky dim, and she was kind and charitable, often helping the poor..." "Huh?" Merlin replied, but his mind was thinking, "What a saint! " Queen Josephine was a devout believer, and when she first married into the Spanish royal family, she was met with opposition from many sides. Dennis, the captain, gazed at the painting, speaking deeply, "If she had refused to marry the king from the beginning, that virtuous woman might not have died in the palace intrigue..." "Really?" Merlin nodded, thinking that a devout believer was a product of the Church's brainwashing, and being assassinated wasn't just a coincidence. "Oh, by the way, there's something else about Queen Josephine that's interesting..." Dennis, the captain, suddenly thought of something, and a mysterious smile appeared on his face. "What?" Merlin asked. "Queen Josephine said that when she was pregnant with Diana, she had a dream that she was blessed by the great goddess, and she would give birth to a divine being..." Dennis, the captain, furrowed his brow, remembering, but it seemed he wasn't quite sure, "Anyway, it was just some crazy talk, and at the time, they even called in the red-robed archbishop to exorcise the evil spirits, it was really laughable..." Suddenly, Merlin's eyes widened in terror, and he instinctively lowered his head, recent events had filled him with doubts about Alice - he discovered that he was starting to lose his grip on Alice, the woman who was always by his side, laughing and joking. Was she really a normal human being, or was he just a small pawn in a grand game? Why was the pendant in Cain's painting identical to Alice's? Why was the pendant Alice's mother left behind similar to the one worn by the devout believer, Queen Josephine? Why did Alice become a hero? Why did Queen Josephine claim she would give birth to a divine being? Why did Alice and Diana, the princess, both have silver hair? Was it all just a coincidence? Why did it seem as if someone was manipulating and arranging everything from behind the scenes? Since he had traveled to this world, he wouldn't always be just a pawn in someone's game... "Merlin, the captain!" Dennis, the captain, suddenly shouted loudly. Merlin felt dizzy and his ears were ringing, "What?!" "You're not responding, and I've been calling you several times, are you feeling unwell?" Dennis, the captain, looked worried. "No, I'm fine, I might be a bit tired..." Merlin forced a smile and replied. "You should take care to rest more often... Dennis, the captain, reminded him, his heart full of joy that Merlin was interested in his homeland, "It seems that you're interested in the Spanish royal family, huh?" "Yeah, it's okay..." Merlin smiled and nodded, asking, "You said last time that you mistakenly thought Alice was a member of the Spanish royal family, is there any evidence?" Dennis, the captain, looked straight into Merlin's eyes, speaking seriously, "Alice's situation is indeed similar to that of the lost Princess Diana, and the pendant she wears is almost identical to Queen Josephine's pendant, but the pendant is not rare, it's a cheap trinket that can be bought by anyone in Spain, it's just that the back has the Spanish royal crest, which is quite intriguing... but Alice has said she's just a normal person, maybe I'm just an old man with a homesick heart, thinking too much, haha..." "Is that so? Thanks for telling me so much, my captain. Goodnight." Merlin finished his wine, turned his head back to his room to go to bed, and glanced at the painting one last time, "Queen Josephine... is a poor woman..."

title: Chapter 19 — The Missing Ralph
content:
Chapter 19 — The Missing Ralph

Volume 20 · Chapter 19

Merlin had been assigned his own cabin aboard the *William*.

He sat by the window, facing the salty sea breeze, watching the endless ocean dotted with stars.

Though Merlin wanted to believe Alice had ties to the heavens and was just an ordinary person, recent events had shaken his doubts about her true identity.

The demon race and the heavens had always been bitter enemies, and he was the master of the First Demon Lord Palace. Could Alice be a spy sent by the Goddess of Light to infiltrate them?

Merlin sighed deeply. Had he risked his life for Alice only to realize everything was part of someone else’s scheme?

Captain Dennis had suggested that Alice’s mother’s heirloom wasn’t particularly rare—even if it bore the royal crest of Spain, it didn’t prove she was the lost princess Diana of the Spanish kingdom.

After all, even Merlin himself could carve a bull emblem to claim something belonged to the Spanish royal family—wasn’t that absurd?

But one thing was certain: Alice’s real parents were likely from Spain.

Merlin lowered his head, suddenly remembering Alice often mentioned her teacher in the Snowy Mountains—perhaps only that person could know the truth.

A numb, stinging pain spread through his right arm. He loosened his clothes and saw the bloodline poison creeping toward his heart, corroding half his body—

Damn it. My time… seems to be running out.

In the unknown, storm-wracked seas, where monstrous waves and violent currents raged, a lone island stood at the center of the chaos.

Countless wrecked ships were scattered across the jagged rocks, their hulls splintered by the storm. The island itself was littered with sharp, jagged stones, like teeth erupting from the earth.

Most unsettling of all was the crimson vortex swirling above the island, devouring anything that dared cross the sky. Lightning occasionally split the air, making one wonder if it was a secret passage to another dimension.

The Chaos Clan—mutated beings twisted by otherworldly forces—inhabited this desolate island. With no fixed appearance, their forms were grotesque and shifting; only a few retained any trace of humanity, while most were covered in sea creatures.

Struggling to survive on this barren land, they rarely left, and food was their greatest enemy. Even a floating tin of meat could spark brutal fights to the death. Cannibalism among their own kind was common—anything to fill their empty stomachs.

Though these starving creatures would lose all reason for food, they still maintained a rigid hierarchy. At the top of the food chain in these cursed waters stood the Chaos King.

This ruler, thriving in such a brutal environment, was undeniably powerful, dominating the entire sea.

Now, the Chaos Clan faced extinction. Their island could no longer protect them, and their leader was conferring with his subordinates.

“This sea has grown increasingly unstable. The seal on the otherworld could shatter at any moment, and the Northern Sea Leviathan will swallow our homeland whole.” The Chaos King, his face obscured by an eye mask, his body covered in scales, coiled around a pillar. His hair was a nest of venomous snakes, his upper body still vaguely human, but his lower half was a massive serpent’s tail. “We must find a way out, seek richer lands to build a new territory—otherwise, we’ll either be slaughtered by otherworldly monsters or crushed in Kraken’s belly!”

Endless statues lined the damp, shadowed depths of the underground palace, lifelike in their detail—even the finest sculptors couldn’t replicate such realism. Sailors, merchants, soldiers, pirates, knights—though their faces varied, their expressions were eerily identical: terror and despair, as if they’d glimpsed something horrific before their final screams.

They weren’t statues at all. Once living men, their life and strength had been drained by the Chaos King, leaving only hollow stone. Their frozen faces spoke of the monstrous thing they’d seen before death.

Every lost soul in these cursed waters became the Chaos King’s feast. Among them were countless strong warriors, their power fueling his own.

How much magic and martial energy had he absorbed? Over the centuries, at least tens of thousands of Saint-tier warriors had been drained—conservative estimates. With such reserves, the Chaos King’s own strength was terrifying, his magic and martial energy vast. That such a being could exist on this barren island was nothing short of monstrous.

“Master, don’t worry. Lahman has been gone for a long time now. Maybe he’s already found the target and begun building our new territory,” said a creature with an octopus-like face—Ocot, one of the Chaos Clan’s three great leaders, equal in power to the Lahman Merlin had killed.

“But he hasn’t sent word in so long… Could something have happened?” The Chaos King’s serpent tail slithered slowly along the pillar. His suspicious nature made him doubt the simplicity of the situation. Lahman’s disappearance for this long likely meant trouble.

“If Master is uneasy, I can leave the island to scout the situation outside,” Ocot’s beady eyes gleamed with mischief as his tentacles twitched.

“Getting people out of this island is harder than bringing them in. Sending Lahman out already cost me a great deal of energy. Now, I must focus on absorbing the otherworld’s power. When the time is right, I’ll tear open the deep-sea vortex and let all our people escape this cursed place. I have no extra energy to waste on sending others out.” The Chaos King’s voice was androgynous, stern. “But be careful—if we disturb something truly terrible in the otherworld, the entire world becomes dangerous, and we’ll have nowhere to stand.”

“What are we supposed to do then? That bastard Lahman is missing, and we don’t even know how the plan’s progressing! It’s infuriating!” Ocot’s tentacles lashed in frustration.

“I don’t see the need to worry so much. Lahman’s strength is formidable. I know the power of the British Empire well—few could defeat him. Besides, the Chaos Clan can absorb magic and martial energy. Even a single one of us could crush a local powerhouse. Perhaps Lahman is too busy establishing Master’s new territory to send word.” Suddenly, another spoke up—a being whose left side still bore traces of humanity, with black hair and brown eyes, but whose right was covered in coral and starfish.

“Are you sure about that?” The Chaos King’s suspicion lingered. Then, a thought struck him, and he bared his jagged teeth in a grin.

“Ah, I remember now.

“Before you pledged to me, you were a secret-silver adventurer from Britain.”

“Did I forget?” the creature replied.

“Lahman…”

title: Chapter 20 — Trapped (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 20 — Trapped (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 20 · Chapter 20

The man before them, half his body already corrupted by otherworldly forces, was none other than the long-missing silver-rank adventurer of the Rekserum region—Ralf!

The man who had once fought side by side with Karl now appeared here out of nowhere, leaving no doubt that something strange had transpired.

Not only had Ralf arrived in the mysterious seas, but he had also joined the Chaos Clan and become one of their Three Pillars.

"That’s right. After serving my master, I nearly forgot my own name," Ralf said, lowering his head with a self-deprecating chuckle.

"To have Lahman attack the Kingdom of Britain after his departure—you were the one who suggested that," the Chaos King spoke with heavy implication.

"Yes. The British lands are fertile and vast, and their naval power is formidable. If Lord Lahman could control Britain, it would pave a smooth path for the master’s future conquest of the world," Ralf replied earnestly.

"Your idea isn’t bad. Though you’ve only been with us for a short time, you’ve proven yourself loyal. I’m glad I didn’t drain you dry when I had the chance—that was the right decision," the Chaos King sneered, his grotesque face twisting into a grin.

"Thank you, master, for your mercy," Ralf bowed respectfully.

"But Lahman has always reported back regularly. After successfully turning the royal duke, he never rested again—until now, when he’s vanished without a trace. I suspect things aren’t as you’ve described," the Chaos King had already sensed the faintest clues. Even without external news, he had pieced together enough.

"The master means..." Ralf lifted his head.

"Lahman is dead," the Chaos King said with certainty.

"...What? Lahman was one of the Three Pillars—how could he die so easily in a human kingdom?!" Okote was stunned, though he still hoped Lahman’s plan had succeeded. Yet the Chaos King was certain of Lahman’s failure.

"We must have underestimated Britain’s strength. Even if we can absorb magic and martial energy, rendering human power useless, we still need to be wary. There may be something we fear lurking there," the Chaos King speculated.

"Hey!" Okote glared at Ralf with vicious intent, suspicion in his voice. "You’re the one who suggested we strike Britain. Now Lahman is dead there—could you have planned this all along?"

"What do you mean?" Ralf frowned, staring at the octopus-faced figure across from him.

"You haven’t fully submitted to the master. Your heart still belongs to humanity, so you set a trap—letting our people die outside while you played along," Okote’s beady eyes darted wildly. "You’re a traitorous bastard. I’ve always known you weren’t trustworthy. Maybe you’re a human spy sent to deceive us!"

"I am loyal to the master! How could I set a trap to harm you?" Ralf lowered his head, his expression stern. "Lord Okote, please don’t slander me without cause—or I’ll be forced to take offense."

"Oh? And what will you do about it?" Okote’s massive tentacles coiled beneath him, his gaze burning with malice.

"You two... *both* shut up!" The Chaos King exhaled an aura of authority, pinning both subordinates to the ground, unable to rise.

The invisible pressure was eerie yet overwhelming, filling them with an unstoppable dread. Both men trembled, crawling on the ground in submission.

Not just Ralf and Okote—every Chaos Clan member on the island felt their leader’s might, collapsing to their knees and bowing toward the underground palace.

In the distance, the towering waves, stirred by the pressure, dissolved into frothy spray. The usually turbulent sea fell eerily still for a moment.

The Chaos King’s casual display of power was so terrifying that even tearing through the deep-sea currents seemed effortless.

"...This man is deceitful. We can’t fully trust him. Maybe Lahman’s failure is his doing..."

"...I’ve always suspected him," Okote huffed, still distrustful of Ralf.

"I trust Mr. Ralf is sincere. Compared to those Four Saint-Swordsmen—human opportunists who only seek power—he chose to join us of his own will, proving his allegiance. So Mr. Ralf can serve as my capable subordinate, but the Four Saint-Swordsmen cannot," the Chaos King didn’t doubt his subordinate’s loyalty but instead praised him. "Besides, Mr. Ralf has brought me invaluable intelligence. Lahman’s failure was his own doing, unrelated to Mr. Ralf."

Okote said nothing, his tentacles twitching nervously as he dared not contradict the Chaos King.

"The master is wise. My choice was never wrong. Serving you is the only right path," Ralf bowed deeply, a smug smile on his face.

"I’m rather tired. Mr. Ralf, you may return and rest. Our departure isn’t far off," the Chaos King said wearily.

"Please take care of your health, then. I’ll withdraw for now," Ralf turned and left.

Once they were alone, Okote could no longer contain himself. "Master, do you *really* trust this man? He’s different from us. Lahman’s failure is tied to him—he must be hiding something, leading Lahman into danger."

"How could I trust a human?" the Chaos King scoffed. "But for now, he’s still useful. Whether he’s a Three Pillar or not, it’s only to make him willingly serve us. I’ll squeeze every last drop of value from him."

Okote’s expression relaxed. "I knew the master wouldn’t trust some mere human. You’re just maximizing his use."

"But Lahman’s failure is a warning. This Ralf isn’t honest. He claims humans have absolute superiority, yet Lahman still died. We can’t rule out that he’s leading us into a dead end. So I won’t believe a word he says anymore. Once I tear through the deep-sea currents and absorb their power, I’ll crush this pathetic man like a bug—effortlessly," the Chaos King paused, speaking softly.

Outside, Ralf stood on the rocks, gazing at the sea toward Britain.

A year ago, he had accepted a commission to travel near the mysterious seas.

Unfortunately, he was swept into a storm and washed ashore here. When he woke, he was trapped on this island.

His once-respectable strength meant nothing against the Chaos Clan—they drained his martial energy and magic. A powerless man had no chance against these monsters. He was doomed to be eaten alive at any moment.

So Ralf had no choice but to submit, offering no resistance.

Thanks to his human elite status, the Chaos King had taken notice, elevating him to the rank of Three Pillar.

After living here for over a year, his body had gradually been corrupted by the otherworldly forces, growing more monstrous by the day.

Ralf stared at the endless ocean, gripping his silver-rank adventurer’s proof in his fist. His heart burned with restless ambition—

To return to Rekserum alive?

He’d have to learn to play the game...

Tomorrow is a double holiday. Extra chapter coming soon—looking forward to seeing everyone!

title: Chapter 21 — Preparing for Battle
content:
Chapter 21 — Preparing for Battle

Volume 20 · Chapter 21

Ralf had no choice but to become the henchman of the Chaos King to survive on this cursed island.

This hellish place was filled with monsters that thrived by devouring magic and martial energy—even human warriors might be stripped to nothing but bones if they wandered in unprotected.

Fortunately, Ralf was smart enough to pledge allegiance to the Chaos King, barely scraping by in this wretched environment.

He constantly schemed for the Chaos King, even suggesting they strike against the Kingdom of Britain. His goal was to escape this nightmare, and for that, nothing was off-limits.

Ralf needed the Chaos King for more than just shelter—only this enigmatic apex predator of the cursed seas could disrupt the storms encircling the island and grant him freedom from this barren land.

Yet Ralf wasn’t entirely without gains. Corrupted by the alien energies, he had gradually lost his humanity, but his power had skyrocketed in just a few years.

He was no longer an ordinary adventurer—his magic had surpassed the Saint-tier, reaching the rare and cold-shouldered Realm of the Patriarchs, a peak only a handful of prodigies could touch.

As a half-man, half-monster, he could wield magic infused with alien energies and absorb his enemies’ attacks to strengthen himself.

Frankly, if time could be rewound a few years, on the world’s most watched adventurer tournament stage—

Ralf would have been the brightest star, crushing all challengers without hesitation. With absolute dominance in absorbing magic and martial energy, claiming the title of the world’s strongest adventurer would have been effortless.

---

“Ralf, you’re always staring at the sea like that… Missing your homeland?” Okoto slithered forward, its body undulating.

“What’s it to you?” Ralf tucked away his adventurer’s credentials, his gaze sharp with hostility.

“It’s none of my business, but you’ve sworn loyalty to the master. I suggest you bury your little schemes and work wholeheartedly for your people’s survival—or else…”

Okoto’s beady eyes narrowed. “You’ll regret it.”

“You threatening me?” Ralf’s stare turned lethal. This octopus monster had insulted him enough—one wrong move could ruin his escape plans.

“Oh-ho-ho, such a fierce glare! You’re just a stray dog the master picked up. Remember when you were wagging your tail? Now you dare defy me?” Okoto’s thick tentacles lunged toward Ralf, venom dripping. “I should’ve killed you back then, spared you the chance to stand beside me!”

Ralf didn’t flinch. Calmly, he extended his hand. The magic ring on it flared, unleashing a devouring alien power that formed an invisible barrier.

Okoto’s poisoned tentacles struck the shield—useless. They shattered like glass, blood spraying everywhere.

“Sorry, but now you can’t beat me,” Ralf said coolly. “Your strength comes from draining magic and martial energy, but I’ve absorbed alien forces. My power isn’t something you can touch anymore.”

“Tsk!” Okoto retracted its tentacles, sneering. “The same coward who used to grovel now dares show his fangs? Don’t get cocky. You won’t last long.”

Ralf turned his back, standing tall. “I’ll return the favor with those words. My patience isn’t infinite.”

“Hmph! You’d better watch yourself. Lahman’s death isn’t without your involvement. If I find any leverage, even if I don’t act, the master will tear you apart.” Okoto vanished into the darkness. This pathetic human’s growth was faster than he’d imagined.

Ralf stared at the raging storm and waves before him, his face twisted in fury. He clenched his fists—

Just a little longer. Once he left this hellhole…

He’d be free.

---

Days later, the *William* had reached the edge of the mysterious cursed seas.

Before them lay a thick, ominous fog—dangerous waters known as the Sailors’ Graveyard, where ships vanished without a trace, and whispers of horror kept crews on edge.

In the ship’s meeting hall, Captain Dennis gathered everyone, outlining the dangers ahead to prevent chaos.

“The fleet has reached the threshold of the cursed seas. Are you all prepared for what lies beyond?” Dennis scanned the room.

“Captain, what threats will we face inside?” Morrison asked.

“Rumors speak of monstrous storms that can capsize ships, and fog so thick it erases day and night—even compasses fail.” Dennis’s expression darkened. “We’ll be like headless flies in there.”

“Then how do we even—?” Adams, the musician, frowned.

“No need to panic. I’ve prepared for this. Every ship is loaded with chains—we’ll link them all together, leaving one vessel outside the cursed seas as a scout.” Dennis paused, then added seriously, “The *William* will lead the way, but our exploration range will be limited by the chain’s length. If we lose the anchor, we risk being lost forever.”

Morrison nodded. “So we won’t get turned around…”

“But this method requires perfect coordination,” Dennis warned. “If the chains break, we’re truly in danger.”

Morrison swallowed hard but stood firm. “We’ve come this far. We must explore—maybe we’ll uncover why ships keep disappearing.”

Dennis smirked grimly. “If we die here, at least it’ll be a sailor’s honorable end.” He sobered. “Beyond the storms and fog, there may be worse monsters. That’s where you come in. The *William* will provide fire support as needed.”

Merlin, wrapped in rags, lowered his head slightly. He clutched his tachi, leaning silently in the corner—

Finally.

He had no idea where the lost pearl had washed ashore.

Guess he’d have to search for it the old-fashioned way.

title: Chapter 22 — Lost (Late Bonus Chapter, Sorry)
content:
Chapter 22 — Lost (Late Bonus Chapter, Sorry)

Volume 20 · Chapter 22

"Don't worry, leave this to us!" Morrison said with high fighting spirit, cracking his knuckles. "Last time that ugly freak caught us off guard, this time we'll definitely return the favor!"

"Morrison-sama, you said there are monsters in the mysterious sea zone that can absorb magic and aura, is that true?" Adams suddenly asked.

"That's right. Those monsters are very strange. Our attacks don't work on them. As soon as we touch them, our power gets swallowed up quickly." Morrison nodded, lowering his head to recall. "I remember during the London Defense Battle, I attacked that monster with all my strength but felt my power being swallowed bit by bit, rendering our attacks completely useless. I still remember clearly... it called itself something like the 'Three Chaos Titans'..."

"It seems that after we enter the mysterious sea zone, the special monsters are what we should guard against most. The mysterious disappearances of so many ships are probably related to them." Adams speculated.

"That's right. We need to be extremely careful, or we'll easily trip and fall." Morrison said seriously.

"Extreme caution is unnecessary, just need to pay a bit more attention. Don't forget, we are London's elite adventurers. Dealing with special monsters, we have more experience than you knights." Adams paused meaningfully. "You told me about this last time, so I've already made some preparations. Rainey, everything ready?"

"Of course. I always prepare for things like this in advance." Rainey waved her hand, causing a slight spatial fluctuation. Immediately, several bizarre red-and-black weapons appeared on the table. It seemed this girl was skilled in spatial magic and could summon various equipment at any time.

"What are these?" Morrison picked up the fist gloves on the table. The black, cold metal was covered with strange patterns, as if alive, constantly pulsating.

"These are magic tools made using alchemy. They significantly boost magic and martial arts. To deal with monsters that can absorb magic and aura, we need these." Rainey said confidently.

"Oh? Do these have special effects?" Morrison asked curiously.

"Simply put, it changes the output target of magic and aura. In usual battles, we need to direct our power straight at the enemy. But this time the enemies can absorb magic and aura, so we must make corresponding changes. We direct magic and aura into the alchemical magic tools and attack the enemy with the tools' power, so the enemy probably won't be able to absorb it..." Rainey adjusted her laser glasses on her head and said seriously.

"Oh! So that's how it is~" Morrison stroked the alchemical fist gloves on his hands. "So it means fighting using props? I get it."

"If you insist on understanding it that way, it's not wrong." Rainey picked up her weapon, an alchemical hunting rifle. Looking at the thick muzzle, calling it a mini magic cannon would be fine too.

"Then... let's get serious and enter alert status? After entering the mysterious sea zone, we might encounter unknown dangers at any time." Adams picked up the alchemical lute, plucked the strings slightly, producing a pleasant sound.

Merlin watched the three alchemical magic tools being distributed and couldn't help thinking. Could this woman also use alchemy to create magic weapons besides spatial magic? Leonardo da Vinci seems to know too. I wonder who's better between the two?

Captain Dennis saw Merlin's gaze turning this way, thinking he was envious of others' alchemical weapons, so he couldn't help but ask, "Miss Rainey, are there any extra alchemical magic tools? Merlin-sama doesn't have one either. This time facing unknown monsters, he should need this kind of weapon too."

"Ahh? What did you say?" Rainey frowned. She didn't regard Merlin, this guy who joined midway, as combat power at all. How could she prepare custom weapons for him?

"Right, are there any extras? Let him use one temporarily." Morrison suddenly thought of Merlin and felt that if he had a handy weapon, he could help out.

"Don't joke around like that!" Adams's face looked bad, saying seriously, "That kind of guy is completely useless in battle. He just needs to shout '666' beside us. Even if we give him custom weapons, it's just wasting resources. Morrison-sama, please be serious. The three of us are the main force of this operation."

"That's right. Moreover, these weapons are made using alchemy. The material requirements are strict; they can't be just pulled out randomly. I only prepared three weapons, with no extras." Rainey explained the situation. Actually, she thought low-level adventurers didn't need custom weapons at all because they couldn't help much anyway.

"...Morrison hesitated, feeling this was unfair to Merlin?"

"Forget it. I don't need such things." Merlin suddenly spoke. In fact, he really didn't need any alchemical magic tools.

"Hmph. Although you're a low-level adventurer, you've got unexpected backbone." Adams snorted, mocking Merlin. "I'm somewhat impressed."

"Whatever you say, I'm tired. Good night." Merlin turned and walked away, not wanting to deal with these two guys at all.

"What attitude is that? He's just a black iron adventurer but has such a big temper." Rainey muttered dissatisfiedly.

"He's weak. We didn't involve him for his own good, at least so he wouldn't die in vain. But this guy doesn't seem to appreciate it." Adams sighed, feeling his good intentions were treated as meddling.

The next day, ships were connected by chains. The William plunged straight into the fog-shrouded mysterious sea zone.

Suddenly the sunlight disappeared, replaced by thick fog behind them where fingers couldn't be seen. They could barely see a meter ahead.

Lightning ravaged, storms howled—

The lonely William was like a dagger, piercing into the heart of the mysterious sea zone, bravely advancing on the surging waves.

In the room, Merlin staggered, frequently bumping into walls, like a kite with a severed string losing control.

His heart curse activated at this moment, and the pain was more intense than ever. Every twitch of his heart caused agony deep into his soul.

When this curse first activated, it was a reminder. If within a month he didn't use Banri Garan to devour life, then facing him would be death by heart tearing.

It had been over half a month since the last activation. Merlin hadn't found a suitable target during this time, causing this curse to be abnormally fierce.

"...Cough cough!"

Merlin supported his body with both hands, trembling all over, feeling he was almost tortured to the point of suffocation.

Nosebleed slowly flowed from his nostrils. Merlin's eyes rolled back, falling into heavy unconsciousness...

Outside, the situation was worse. A lightning bolt suddenly struck the William's chains, cutting off its only connection to the outside world.

Losing this chain, the William would be completely lost in the mysterious sea zone. Wanting to find a way back? Probably harder than ascending to heaven!

The pitch-black sea rolled with waves, suddenly raising monstrous waves that struck the William head-on like a drifting duckweed.

"Careful!!!" Captain Dennis gripped the helm in the wind and rain, letting out a final shout—

Under the power of nature, everything is as insignificant as ants.

The William was capsized by waves, sinking into the deep sea vortex...

title: Chapter 23 — Loss of Consciousness
content:
Chapter 23 — Loss of Consciousness

Volume 20 · Chapter 23

When morning came, the William was washed ashore on a mysterious island by the storm.

The surrounding air was filled with chaotic currents, and the spectacular sight of waterspouts was visible at any moment.

A huge crimson vortex hung in the sky, with lightning flashing over it from time to time!

In the end, the William was still swept into the center of the sea.

On the deck, Captain Dennis lay unconscious, yet still clung tightly to the helm. Several small fish swept up by the storm were jumping wildly on his captain's hat.

A sea breeze carrying a faint fishy smell blew past, and Captain Dennis suddenly jolted awake, opening his mouth to spit out the seawater he had swallowed. His face was pale, his whole body seemingly on the verge of collapse.

Captain Dennis raised his head in great surprise and looked around. The unfamiliar scene before him filled him with deep confusion, and a profound unease gradually began to take hold.

"...W-here... where is this?"

Captain Dennis walked unsteadily forward, pulled out the telescope from his waist, and what met his eyes were countless strange rocks, the storm raging ceaselessly, and of course the vortex in the sky.

Such a scene,仿佛 an otherworldly realm, shocked him. He immediately realized this was some corner of the Mysterious Sea, absolutely not a safe place!

Captain Dennis hurriedly took out the compass. The needle was spinning disordered, circling around? This navigational tool had clearly malfunctioned!

Despite having planned so much, they had still lost contact with the outside world and stumbled into this place known as "Sailors' Graveyard." This journey would likely become very dangerous!

Captain Dennis looked around, seeing his subordinates unconscious on the deck in scattered numbers, some even hanging high on the masts.

Looking carefully, he had lost many subordinates. Roughly estimating, only half remained, which made the old captain feel very heartbroken.

However, there was something more urgent. Captain Dennis hurried into the William and entered the room where Morrison, Adams, and Renee were.

"Everyone, wake up! Wake up!"

The three slowly got up; by now their heads were still dizzy. The William had been tortured by the storm, and their conditions were not much better.

Morrison rubbed his slightly aching head. "...What happened? How did it suddenly..."

Renee stood up unsteadily. "We seem to have encountered a fierce storm, and then the world started spinning..."

"...Adams vomited directly, clearly exhausted from the torment."

"We've lost contact with the outside world! The chains were severed by lightning in the storm!" Captain Dennis said seriously.

"What?!" Morrison widened his eyes in surprise. "So we've gotten lost in the Mysterious Sea?!"

"...Yes. We underestimated the storms here. They're too powerful. The William was caught in turbulent currents and dragged deeper. Now I can't even determine where we are." Captain Dennis briefly explained the situation.

"That's terrible. We only came to explore; now we might never get out." Adams' face looked extremely grim.

"How could it be like this..." Renee's gaze stagnated; she hadn't expected the situation of losing contact with the outside world.

"Don't panic. Since we've already come here, we should go out and investigate. How can we know if we can leave the Mysterious Sea without careful investigation?"

Morrison said calmly, but his heart was a bit nervous. Innumerable people had entered this area and failed to get out; could he successfully escape?

"Captain Dennis, what's the situation outside?"

"It looks quiet, but it's very strange here. I feel like I've come to another world; it doesn't look like a place where humans can survive..." Captain Dennis said nervously.

The several of them came outside and saw unimaginable scenes, falling silent, unable to speak. They felt the environment here had exceeded their understanding.

"Goodness! This ground covered in thorn-like rocks... what kind of place is this?" Adams frowned.

"Looking at the storms around, wanting to leave here, probably..." Renee hesitated to speak, having already thought of the worst case.

"What's there to panic about? Let's go down and explore now; there might be unexpected gains." Morrison made a decision, not wanting to stay on the ship and wait to die.

"Go now? We just woke up, we haven't stabilized yet." Renee didn't quite agree.

"This isn't a safe place. We're in unfamiliar territory. The longer we stay, the worse our situation might become..."

"Morrison spoke with reason and evidence: rather than staying here and waiting for danger to find them, they should take the initiative to nip various dangers in the bud."

"Captain Morrison is right. We need to take the initiative." Adams agreed more with Morrison.

"...Renee had no choice but to take out her alchemy magic device."

Watching the three leave the William, Captain Dennis felt he needed to do something too. At the very least, he had to handle the ship's affairs in order and try to find a way to break through the storm and leave the Mysterious Sea.

So Captain Dennis woke up the surviving sailors and ordered everyone to start organizing the weapons on the William, preparing for any danger that might appear.

But he hadn't been busy for long when he suddenly remembered something important and slapped his forehead—

"Right! Merlin..."

"Why hasn't he reacted at all by now?"

Due to the onset of the heart curse, Merlin had fallen into a deep coma before the William was sucked into the vortex, lifeless.

This situation was more serious than ever before. The threat lurking in Merlin's body had gradually begun to endanger his life.

"Boom—"

The door was kicked open, and Captain Dennis rushed in, seeing Merlin lying motionless on the ground.

"Merlin! Are you alright!"

Captain Dennis kept shaking the unconscious Merlin, feeling his body ice-cold, like a dead person!

Thump-thump! Stimulated by the outside world, Merlin's heart beat violently twice, and he suddenly opened his eyes; the blood throughout his body began to flow!

If Captain Dennis hadn't come to try to wake him, Merlin might really have died!

Clearly, under the torment of the curse, Merlin's heart had gradually lost its vitality and could stop beating at any moment, causing his death.

Merlin's violent reaction scared Captain Dennis. "...My lord, ..."

Merlin scrambled up from the ground as if electrocuted, his face pale, leaning against the wall, constantly clutching his heart and breathing heavily.

"Did I lose consciousness for a while? How long has it been? It's no different from being dead!"

He hadn't expected it to be this serious, beyond his expectations...

Merlin wiped the dried blood from his nose, and he looked completely dazed and in terrible shape.

"Merlin, are you alright?" Captain Dennis walked up to check Merlin's injuries.

"Don't come closer! I'm fine..." Merlin's eyes changed drastically; he stopped Dennis from approaching, because he found that under the stimulation of the vampire toxin, he had become increasingly sensitive to human aura...

"How long was I unconscious?"

Extra update before 1:30 AM, no debts. Tomorrow's update proceeds as usual according to the monthly ticket rankings.

title: Chapter 24 — Ignoring It (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 24 — Ignoring It (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 20 · Chapter 24

“.... I'm not really sure, I just woke up myself...." Captain Dennis's embarrassed recollection.
"How.... Merlin rubbed his aching forehead, 'Where are we now?'"
"We were swept by the storm into the depths of the mysterious sea, and we docked on an unnamed island somewhere." Captain Dennis answered succinctly.
"Tsk!" Merlin forced himself up despite the discomfort, "What about Morrison and the others?"
"They three have already left first, heading to the island to explore...." Captain Dennis said.
Merlin lowered his head, recalling that he still had an important task, needing to find the deep-sea clam, "I also need to go to the island."
"But.... Captain Dennis saw Merlin's pale, bloodless face and couldn't help advising, 'Your condition doesn't seem good right now; you should rest here.'"
"No, since we've come to the mysterious sea, I have something I must do."
Merlin ignored Dennis's advice, directly took his katana and walked out of the cabin. When he saw the outside situation, he was slightly startled.
The blood-red vortex in the sky looked extremely eerie, as if a monster from another dimension was greedily peeking at this place.
"Be careful, Lord Merlin, Morrison and the others haven't been gone long; maybe you can catch up with them." Captain Dennis suggested.
"No need, what we have to do is different." Merlin didn't look back, stepped off the William, wading through shallow seawater, stepping on sharp reefs, resolutely leaving.
"See you, Captain first...."

At the moment Morrison and the three stepped onto the island, the chaos tribe already knew of the intruders' arrival.
They showed no panic at all, instead becoming unusually excited!
The humans brought by the storm were like a gift from the sea; the chaos tribe were already starving and wanted to devour the intruders.
Countless humans washed ashore had almost all become food for the chaos tribe's bellies; lucky ones like Lei Fu were extremely rare.
Strange monsters came from all directions, frenziedly attacking Morrison's trio, hoping to get a share of fresh flesh and blood.
Previously, humans who came to the island relied on their own trait of devouring magic power and battle aura, and thus had almost no natural enemies.
Heaven, this group of chaos monsters, however, unexpectedly ran into a tough nut—
"Hah!"
Morrison let out a shout, after equipping his alchemical weapon, he easily killed the last incoming chaos monster, its head split into quarters, plasma splattering!
"This should be the last— one, right?"
"Not sure, I don't know how many of these monsters are on this island; they are indeed quite troublesome." Adams felt a hint of pressure.
"Don't get close to them; even a slight touch will drain your power." Renee's alchemical hunting gun glowed red and hot, unknown how many consecutive shots she had fired, "If we hadn't prepared in advance, encountering them would probably get us killed here!"
"Thinking back, when we were beaten helplessly by similar monsters before, today it feels like no big deal, really satisfying!" Morrison kicked aside the corpse in front of him; the monsters back then weren't actually hard to deal with, just their abilities were too tricky, so they were easily suppressed.
"Still need to be careful; we just entered the island and already ran into so many monsters; if we go deeper, it's hard to imagine what we might encounter." Adams said cautiously.
"Could there be something terrifying on this island?" Renee felt a hint of nervousness inside; this place is a no-return zone, maybe there really is something extremely terrifying, after all the mysterious sea holds many unknowns; even an ordinary-looking small island needs to be taken seriously.
"It's possible; with so many monsters here, there must be some leader-type monster; perhaps what we just encountered is only a small part of this group." Adams said softly.
"Don't scare yourself; let's keep moving forward to explore." Morrison put his hands on his waist, turned back and said, "Now that we're trapped here, maybe we can find a way to leave this damned place on the island?"

Just as Morrison's words fell, a gloomy voice sounded—
"Leaving? Hehehe, nice dream."
"Who are you?!"
Morrison was shocked, the surroundings were empty, not knowing where the voice came from; it felt like they were being watched all the time.
The three quickly gathered together, forming a defensive stance, each staring in a direction, to guard against ambush from the dark!
Bang bang bang, the sound of the ground trembling continuously rang out; three thick tentacles suddenly burst from the earth, fiercely smashing toward the three!
These three tentacles were not only thick and strong, but also sprayed poison; splashing on the ground gave off intense black smoke!
Adams narrowed his eyes, quickly strummed his alchemical lute, and instantly a metallic clashing killing sound rang out!
The sharp cutting sound wave instantly swept the surroundings, directly slicing the attacking tentacles into pieces!
"Hehehe, you've got some skill; it seems I really underestimated this prey that delivered itself to my door—I need to properly toy with you."
A series of cold laughter rang out; Okote, with an octopus face, slowly wriggled out from the darkness, his murky eyes trembling.
"Being able to launch an effective attack against our chaos tribe shows you found a way to counter the devouring magic power and battle aura, but so what? As soon as you set foot on this island, your fate is already sealed; any resistance is just pointless struggle."
"Who are you?" Morrison kept his combat stance, fists clenched, as if he would explode at any moment to blast the enemy!
"Since you're doomed anyway, I'll tell you." Okote writhed his tentacles, speaking gloomily, "I am Okote, one of the three great heads of the chaos tribe, serving the supreme ruler, managing all big and small affairs on this island."
"Ah... Morrison suddenly realized, somewhat understanding the enemy's identity," "So it's the same level as the mastermind behind that rebellion; finally I've met an opponent I can play with—I'm almost itching to smash you into mincemeat with my fists."
"Foolish humans, everything on this island belongs only to our tribe's king; I advise you to give up resistance, willingly offer your lives for us to feast upon—that is your worth." Okote's murky eyes narrowed, as if mocking.
"Nonsense..." Morrison frowned.
"Even if you could free yourselves from the suppression of devouring magic power and battle aura, it wouldn't change anything; even in a pure strength comparison, you would be like ants before me!"
Okote roared, spread his arms and lifted a huge black curtain, shadow enveloping the humble humans.
Morrison's trio also refused to yield, each erupting with their own Saint-tier power, pushing the alchemical mage device's power to the limit!

In the distance, Merlin hid behind a rock, silently watching the intense battle before him; the next moment—
He turned and left, alone heading deeper into danger....
Did he really not care about Morrison and the others' lives at all? =

title: Chapter 25 — Fellow Townsman (Extra Update Later)
content:
Chapter 25 — Fellow Townsman (Extra Update Later)

Volume 20 · Chapter 25

In the dim, damp underground palace, the Chaos King hovered above the pillars, drifting in an unknown direction.

Though it wore an eye mask, it seemed to see far into the distance.

Relf knelt on one knee, summoned here with a heart full of uncertainty. He had heard that intruders had arrived on the island.

But this time was different. The enemy possessed resistance, rendering the Chaos race’s abilities useless.

Since they could absorb magic and martial energy, mages and warriors’ attacks were nearly ineffective against them.

Yet once deprived of this advantage, they faced humans with far greater pressure—easy victory was no longer guaranteed.

“Three human warriors have arrived on the island,” the Chaos King’s deep voice echoed through the palace. “I’ve already sent Okot out to hunt them down. It seems some reckless fools have dared to intrude into the Mysterious Sea. Why not capture them alive for our master to enjoy?”

Relf suggested, “This time might not be so simple. Though their strength isn’t yet enough to threaten us, they’ve somehow neutralized our abilities. Okot will face considerable pressure against three of them. You should go help him. There’s no need to capture these humans—just kill them all.”

Relf remained unmoved. “Okot seems fully capable of handling three human warriors. I don’t think I’m needed.”

The Chaos King looked down at this human who only cared about survival, his voice growing colder. “Are you defying my order? Do you think your wings have grown too hard?”

“No, it’s just… I don’t have a good relationship with Okot. Even if I went to help, I’d likely be rejected.”

A bead of cold sweat trickled down Relf’s forehead as he explained, “Besides, Okot’s strength is undeniable. Even without relying on the Chaos race’s abilities, few humans could rival it.”

“Right now, I must focus entirely on absorbing extradimensional energy. Whether you leave this dangerous place depends on my last effort. I can’t be disturbed. For safety’s sake, you should go help. Put an end to the chaos as quickly as possible.”

Relf, desperate to escape this cursed place, bowed his head obediently. “Very well. If it’s your command, I’ll go at once.”

Leaving the underground palace, Relf walked down the long corridor.

In truth, he resisted the Chaos King’s order not because of his poor relationship with Okot.

It was because he didn’t want to become a mindless hound of the Chaos race, freely slaughtering humans.

But Relf had no other choice. “To survive and leave here, even killing a few humans is unavoidable.”

As he lowered his head, nearly stepping out of the corridor, he suddenly felt someone blocking the sunlight. A shadow enveloped him.

He slowly lifted his head—and saw that someone had already broken in. They had reached the very entrance of the underground palace.

The figure wore a filthy robe, wrapped tightly around them, stained with rust and blood dripping down the blade.

Behind this person was a mountain of Chaos race corpses, clearly slaughtered on their way here. Every obstacle had been cut down, now part of the pile of dead.

Relf was stunned, his eyes wide as if facing a bloodthirsty demon. The stench of decaying flesh made him want to vomit.

Merlin wiped the blood from his sword and sheathed it, ignoring the three Morisons. Alone, he had slaughtered his way to the island’s depths.

He found a cave guarded by countless monsters—clearly a place of great importance.

The Chaos race saw the intruder and lunged wildly, only to be hacked down one by one by Merlin’s blade.

Merlin turned slowly, locking eyes with Relf in stunned silence. His expression remained cold. “Are there any survivors left? After seeing so many strange monsters, you’re the one who looks most human.”

Merlin studied Relf, noting that though half his body had grown coral-like, his human form was still recognizable. A flicker of surprise passed through him.

Relf snapped back to reality, sizing up the young man before him. “I never expected someone to kill their way here so quickly. The usual prey has finally become the predator.”

“You seem smarter than those mindless monsters,” Merlin wiped the blood from his face with his sleeve, asking bluntly, “Your leader is deep inside this cave, right? I haven’t come to the wrong place.”

Relf frowned, unsure whether the young man was arrogant or just foolish.

Alone, he had ventured into danger—and now he was charging straight toward the Chaos King…

Was he suicidal?

“What if I am? Do you think you can single-handedly defeat the island’s master?” Relf scoffed. “You’re delusional. Even if you killed a bunch of lesser monsters, you’re still just an ant before that thing.”

“Am I joking?” Merlin stepped forward, entering the cave. Without the sun’s threat, he removed his heavy hood.

“Ah, a young calf not afraid of the tiger,” Relf sighed. “I advise you to leave quietly. Pretend you never came here.”

Relf still didn’t want to kill a human easily. “I suspect you were caught in a storm after entering the Mysterious Sea and washed up here. If you want to live, hide on the island’s west side. There are few monsters there.”

“You actually want to let me go?” Merlin rubbed his neck, speaking without restraint. “Thanks for the advice, but it’s useless. I came to kill the leader here and see if there’s anything I need.”

“Truly hopeless!” Relf’s words had barely left his mouth when he vanished in an instant, reappearing beside Merlin. His hands clamped around the young man’s head, ready to drain his energy.

Merlin’s eyes widened in shock—he hadn’t expected such swift action.

But the next second, Relf’s face paled, his forehead slick with cold sweat.

Damn it! There’s no magic or martial energy at all!

How could someone without magic or martial energy slaughter so many Chaos race members?

“Having fun?”

Merlin’s gaze turned as cold as a wild beast’s. He seized Relf’s wrist and twisted it 360 degrees, snapping his arm clean off.

Blood sprayed as Relf’s limb twisted into a grotesque shape, the pale bones piercing his skin—clearly ruined.

But at such close range, Relf suddenly noticed something familiar beneath Merlin’s robes—an Adventurer’s Proof.

He and I… we’re both from Rexam’s Adventurers Guild?!

title: Chapter 26 — Don't Block My Way
content:
Chapter 26 — Don't Block My Way

Volume 20 · Chapter 26

Merlin stared at Raelf’s stunned expression. The guy didn’t look like some chaotic monster—letting him go would have been surprising enough in itself.

Raelf quickly glanced at Merlin’s adventurer’s certificate and found that the young man before him belonged to the same guild as him. In a way, that counted as fate.

But he had never seen Merlin before, likely a new recruit who had joined recently.

The searing pain in his arm made Raelf frown slightly. Merlin seemed odd—how could a lone warrior have broken into the underground palace and snap his arm so easily?

Though Merlin didn’t seem to have any magic or martial energy, he was definitely more than just a black-iron ranked adventurer.

Raelf decisively abandoned his ruined arm, quickly breaking free from Merlin’s control, and pressed his bleeding wound, his gaze fixed uncertainly on him.

"...You’ve got some skill, new guild recruit."

Merlin shook Raelf’s arm like trash and tossed it aside. “You know the Adventurers Guild?”

“If the situation allows, you should respectfully address me as senior...” Raelf, with one arm, fished out his silver adventurer’s certificate from his robes and showed it to Merlin.

Region: Rekserum
Name: Raelf
Occupation: Mage

Merlin frowned after seeing the information. He remembered Alice mentioning once that there were three Saint-tier figures in the guild.

Besides the Guildmaster and Mr. Karl, there was also a mage who had gone on a mission around a year ago and never returned—like something had gone wrong and he’d vanished.

He never expected to encounter him in this no-exit mysterious sea domain. It was highly possible that he had been dragged into this place years ago and never left.

But seeing Raelf’s half-body already leaning toward the inhuman, still fighting for the chaotic monsters, was very strange.

“I said your behavior didn’t match those crude monsters—turns out you’re human, actually siding with them...”

“I was swept in by the storm. Fighting for the monsters wasn’t my intention—I just wanted to survive and leave this place. Compromising with reality isn’t something to be ashamed of.” Raelf said with a resigned tone.

“I’ve heard rumors about you in the guild. You were Mr. Karl’s comrade, fighting side by side in the Adventurers Tournament.”

Merlin searched through scattered memories.

“Such things aren’t worth mentioning.” Raelf lowered his head and couldn’t help but ask, “Are those weirdos in the guild okay?”

“They thought you were in trouble, but no one expected you to be dragged into the mysterious sea domain, and...” Merlin looked at Raelf’s half-body made of coral, “...turned into one of the monsters.”
