“I just wanted to use the monsters’ power to escape this cursed place. As for this body...” Raelf paused, looking at his ruined form, “No matter who lives here, they’ll all be infected by some unknown force, turning into creatures that live by devouring energy...”

Merlin was confused and didn’t understand what Raelf was talking about. “Unknown force? You mean the red vortex in the sky?”

“Probably.” Raelf said slowly. “This sea domain is a gap between two worlds, a place abandoned by the gods. Living creatures here for too long will all have... shadows...”

Merlin’s heart skipped a beat. “A gap between two worlds”—that was exactly where he was headed. The deep-sea clam had a good chance here.

“Why didn’t you stay in Rekserum? What are you doing here?” Raelf asked curiously.

“I’m here to find the deep-sea clam and get the Pearl of Ebb to save someone.” Merlin said seriously.

“The deep-sea clam? That creature doesn’t belong to our world. They come from other planes, occasionally wandering into this one, but they’re almost never seen.” Raelf thought Merlin’s target was hard to come by. “But the Pearl of Ebb—the Chaos King does have one stored away...”

Merlin’s heart raced twice, feeling even more certain he was in the right place. No matter what, he’d just snatch the pearl first—at least he wouldn’t come here for nothing.

Seeing Merlin’s eager expression, Raelf couldn’t help but warn him, “You want that thing? I advise you not to overestimate yourself. The Chaos King’s power is terrifying. If it weren’t for the chaotic currents around the island restraining it, it might have enslaved all of humanity. I’m not killing you, but while I’m still hungry and haven’t changed my mind, you should run. As fellow adventurers from Rekserum, that’s all I can do.”

“What if I don’t leave?” Merlin said expressionlessly, stepping forward. “The treasure the monster king collects—I’ll just take it. Whoever blocks me, I’ll cut down!”

“The Chaos King is planning to leave this island, and only it has the ability to do so. I won’t allow you to interfere.” Raelf’s gaze darkened with hostility. He never expected Merlin to be so stubborn.

“To put it bluntly, you’re just a dog that fights for monsters to survive. Don’t use that ‘senior’ tone with me. Since we’re already on opposite sides, I won’t hold back.” Merlin paused, coldly saying, “Move, or prepare to die.”

“I gave you a chance, young man.” Raelf narrowed his eyes, and his magic ring pulsed with magic energy.

Merlin didn’t understand Raelf’s intentions. To leave this cursed place, he needed the Chaos King’s power.

Right now, the Chaos King was at a critical moment of absorbing energy from another world, and Raelf wouldn’t allow Merlin to interfere.

The conflict between them became irreconcilable. Raelf wanted to teach this arrogant new recruit a lesson.

Raelf’s body radiated the oppressive aura of a peak Saint-tier, and the surrounding space began to warp terrifyingly.

“Disappear, you arrogant fool!”

The moment the words left his mouth, the air erupted with a powerful cutting current, crisscrossing like a dense fishing net.

Raelf’s magic turned the air into destructive blades, so dense that even a dragon would be sliced into fragments if caught in them!

“Boom!” A deafening explosion shook the ground as the powerful area magic cut through everything in its path, leaving deep, horrifying trenches in the earth.

The cutting currents flattened everything around them, and when the storm passed, only scorched, desolate land remained.

The wind died down, and Raelf lowered his single arm, looking at the empty space before him. Merlin was likely reduced to dust.

“I didn’t want to do this. You forced my hand, young...”

“Hey!”

Raelf heard a greeting from behind him, and someone even patted his shoulder?!

He froze in shock, instinctively thinking—there’s more than one enemy, and another hiding in the shadows?!

Raelf spun around and saw Merlin’s smirking expression, who knew when had appeared behind him!

Merlin drew his sword in a flash, striking Raelf down in the blink of an eye before the enemy could react, killing him instantly!

Blood sprayed into the air, hanging suspended as Raelf’s eyes widened in disbelief. The battle ended in a flash—he hadn’t even had time to react.

How... how was that possible?!

That sword draw was too fast!

My magic didn’t even scratch him....

I was wrong. I’m guilty. I fell asleep last night.

title: Chapter 26 — The Dungeon Gate
content:
Chapter 26 — The Dungeon Gate

Volume 20 · Chapter 26

Ralf had severely underestimated the strength of this new recruit from the Reksem Guild. After engaging in serious combat, he finally realized just what kind of monster he was dealing with!

Unmatched destructive power, extraordinary speed, razor-sharp insight—

These traits in a single person made him a natural-born combat genius!

Even on the bloodiest battlefields, he would be a creature that made one’s hair stand on end!

Rather than being an unremarkable new adventurer from the Reksem Guild, he was more like a stroke of luck.

Ralf’s face turned pale, blood gushing like a fountain, his body collapsing weakly to the ground, his severe wounds leaving him unable to fight.

“Cough!... I warned you,” Merlin sheathed his katana, looking down at Ralf from above. “I *must* obtain the Flowing Pearl. Anyone who blocks me will—definitely die.”

Ralf leaned against the cold wall, black blood spurting from his mouth and pooling on his chest, his organs exposed by Merlin’s blade.

He had to admit he was old. The new generation surpassed the old. After leaving the guild over a year ago, he had joined such a powerful newcomer.

"...Very strong. Beyond... my expectations. If... you continue, the future... will let Reksem... shine brightly..."

Merlin remained silent, listening to Ralf’s faltering words. Clearly, he wouldn’t last much longer, but he could still speak—likely the dying light’s effect.

Ralf fumbled weakly in his chest for his silver adventurer’s proof, his voice barely audible. “...Take it back. Please.”

Merlin took the silver adventurer’s proof from Ralf’s hand—the two gleaming silver iron plates engraved with the adventurer’s information.

Adventurers were a profession where survival was never guaranteed. Countless would meet unfortunate deaths on missions.

Though many were talented, in their pursuit of freedom, they left nothing behind, and no one remembered them.

Only the adventurer’s proof—a seemingly humble iron pendant—was the sole mark of their existence.

Adventurers would return their fallen comrades’ proofs to the Adventurers Guild headquarters in Denmark, hanging them on the massive maple tree in the cemetery, where they greeted the morning sun every day.

Though Merlin had been an adventurer for only a short time, he knew the custom. Ralf handing over his proof was likely hoping it would return to where it belonged.

Ralf’s eyes grew bloodshot, his consciousness fading, yet he refused to close them, as if there was something he wanted to say.

Merlin’s heart stirred. He knelt down, gently closing Ralf’s eyes with his hand, and whispered, “Don’t worry. I’ll return your proof to Reksem. You died honorably in an adventure, not as a monster’s pawn.”

Ralf’s standing in the guild had been on par with Mr. Karl—many respected him.

In the eyes of countless others, he was a steadfast, powerful, and excellent adventurer.

So Ralf didn’t want anyone to know that after being dragged into the mysterious seas, he had become a monster’s tool, only to be despised in the end.

Sure enough, after hearing Merlin’s final promise, Ralf’s body trembled, growing colder by the second, as if he had no regrets left.

Merlin understood Ralf’s feelings. For a dying man, wanting to leave a good impression behind was nothing wrong.

Merlin tucked Ralf’s silver adventurer’s proof into his chest and turned toward the depths of the underground palace, intending to meet the ruler of this sea.

He planned to keep this secret buried, pretending Ralf had died in an adventure long ago.

But Merlin hadn’t taken more than a few steps when he heard a faint voice murmuring behind him, as if speaking directly to him.

"...Can’t... beat that monster. You still have time to turn back.

“If... she *has* to go, watch out for... those eyes.”

Ralf’s life force had been absorbed by Merlin’s Banri Garan, waves of pleasant warmth nourishing his heart like spring rain on parched earth.

The curse had eased, meaning Ralf was truly dead—his life force fully consumed by the demon sword.

Merlin stopped, looking at the lone corpse slumped against the cold wall, muttering to himself.

“It’s not that you *can’t* beat him—it’s that—”

Time passed slowly. The Morrisons were still locked in a desperate battle with Okot, the fighting reaching a fever pitch, yet they still hadn’t managed to kill this Chaos Triumvirate member.

They had thought finding a way to resist the devouring magic qi through alchemical weapons would make victory easy.

Now, it seemed Adams and Renée had overestimated themselves. Even without relying on that godlike ability, the monster’s underboss was still nearly impossible to handle—one careless moment, and the poisonous spray would corrode them to nothing but bones.

Captain Dennis wasn’t idle either, directing the crew to prepare weapons and push the magic cannons forward to assist.

The *William*, damaged in the storm, had been quickly repaired and was ready to set sail.

But the powerful storm surrounding the island made escape impossible—the *William* would be torn apart by the sea’s fury!

Captain Dennis could only place his hopes in Morrison and Merlin, praying they would find a way to break free on the island.

“Faster! Faster! Push out all the cannons—if we can still fire, we can help!”

Sailor: “Captain, the gunpowder’s been soaked by seawater—it won’t ignite!”

“Blow it dry with your mouth until it’ll light!”

Sailor: “Reporting, Captain! The magic cannons are too heavy—we can’t lift them!”

“Are you idiots?! Roll some logs under them and push them out slowly!”

Sailor: “Captain! The tide’s receded a lot—the sea’s revealed... lifelike statues over there!”

“Shut up! If you slack off again, I’ll shoot you dead! Get to work—what’s so interesting about statues?!”

Sailor: “It’s not just statues, Captain—there are *so many*, countless ones....”

Hmm? Captain Dennis frowned, sensing something off. He quickly followed the sailor to the shore, took out his telescope, and looked toward the horizon.

The seawater around the island rose and fell in cycles. Now, near midnight, the tide had receded significantly, exposing vast stretches of beach and reef.

Rather than strange rocks, they were more like corroded, grotesque statues—scattered haphazardly across the shore.

There were so many, impossible to count. Many were still submerged, their terrified expressions and twisted postures as if they had witnessed something horrific!

These were the unfortunate souls drained of their power by the Chaos King. Not just humans—elves, beastmen, lovers, and even dragon statues were among them!

Merlin had thought the number of statues in the underground palace was already shocking, but the reality far exceeded his imagination.

Why were there so many strange rocks on the island? Because the entire small island was made up of petrified human corpses!

The Chaos King’s power—absorbing the strength of so many mighty beings—was beyond imagination. Even guessing at its true strength was impossible.

Captain Dennis lowered his telescope, his expression growing uneasy, a chill running down his spine.

“This little... island is *weird*.”

In the underground palace, Merlin now stood before the massive stone door, gazing at the thick, mysterious entrance. He couldn’t help but furrow his brow.

“Is this it?”

title: Chapter 28 — Lord of the Waters (Extra Chapters Coming)
content:
Chapter 28 — Lord of the Waters (Extra Chapters Coming)

Volume 20 · Chapter 28

Merlin looked at the heavy stone door, lightly touching it with his hand. Besides feeling a cold breeze emanating from it, it seemed there were no other dangers.

Recalling the words left to him by Ralph before his death, he had to be a bit more cautious, in case of encountering troublesome enemies.

After confirming it was safe, Merlin used both hands with force to push open the mysterious, heavy door. A creaking sound accompanied it, and the sour-smelling odor spread throughout the area.

It smelled like old, rotten mouse meat, and even a slight whiff would make one sick to the stomach. Merlin frowned, covering his nose and mouth as he walked inside.

After entering the core of the underground palace, the light was dim, and he could barely feel his way, only vaguely seeing countless lifelike statues scattered across the ground.

The sheer number of them made Merlin think he had entered a stone forest, or perhaps a graveyard?

These stone statues varied in appearance, all displaying terrified expressions directed upward, as if they had seen something terrifying, and then instantly died.

The island beneath his feet had existed for an unknown length of time, conservatively estimated to be over ten thousand years. From their attire, one could tell there was a strong ancient-era aura.

Merlin navigated through the dense forest of stone statues, constantly examining them, feeling as though he was looking at the original bronze soldiers of the old world.

"...What kind of ghosts are these?"

Merlin muttered to himself, when suddenly something cold and slimy dripped onto his forehead.

He instinctively felt a startle, touching his head where the cold substance was. After careful observation, he discovered it was a dark yellowish viscous liquid.

Merlin looked up and saw a massive stone pillar with the sticky substance coating it, as if some monster had recently nested there.

"How dare you intrude... just a tiny little mouse? This truly surprises me."

Suddenly, a voice that was neither male nor female echoed out. Merlin felt a chill, something had evaded his perception, hiding in the shadows!

So Merlin quickly assumed a defensive stance. In the blink of an eye, he was struck on the back with a heavy blow!

Merlin hadn't seen what kind of ghost it was, but a giant serpent-like tail struck his chest with force!

A loud "BOOM" echoed as the massive impact shook the space, and the statues shattered, flying in all directions!

Merlin huffed a low sound, like a cannonball, smashing through all the giant rocks and crashing into the rock wall, with dust filling the palace.

Quietly, the King of Chaos descended from above, its hair growing poisonous serpent heads, emitting a "hiss" sound, feeling extremely sinister.

Merlin slowly emerged from the smoke, appearing a bit disheveled but with no significant injuries.

After examining the King of Chaos, Merlin couldn't help but slightly frown, thinking how this form resembled the mythological Medusa from the old world.

Ralph had last cautioned him to be careful of enemies with petrification abilities. If that were the case, it would indeed be quite difficult.

"Hmm? A rough-skinned, meaty little mouse?" The King of Chaos coldly muttered.

"Hey!" Merlin brushed off his shoulder, "You dare not prove your strength, attacking me head-on like a coward, you're afraid of me, aren't you?"

"Fearful? Not yet to the point of making me nervous." The King of Chaos smiled with his mouth open, calmly saying, "Though you've reached here alone, I'm sure you've killed many of my subordinates. Even if you're a mouse, I must take you seriously. Perhaps this is what humans call the lion's fight with the rabbit, using all their strength?"

"Ha, a surprising individual. This is the first time I've encountered someone this cautious. If all villains were like you, I'd be frustrated..." Merlin chuckled dryly.

"I've lived on this island for countless years, and this is the first time I've seen a human. You're far stronger than those previous useless ones. Defeating my powerful subordinates and facing my direct blows without a scratch." The King of Chaos, though wearing a blindfold, was still carefully observing Merlin, "Your strength and appearance don't match. I always thought those who fell into my domain were all prey, but this time... you're a hunter."

"I came here originally to find the lost pearl, but my mind has changed now." Merlin looked at the King of Chaos, seriously saying, "I want to eliminate..."

"HAHAHA..." The King of Chaos laughed wildly, cracking his lips, revealing jagged teeth, "Excellent. Let me see what you're proud of, and consider it a pleasure to amuse me."

Merlin slowly approached the King of Chaos, gripping his tanto at his waist, his gaze steadily fixed on him, then suddenly speeding up, disappearing from the spot.

"Little skills!" The King of Chaos grinned with his teeth bared, extending his hand, and a strange dark purple energy flickered abnormally in his palm.

Merlin unexpectedly crashed into an invisible wall, his attack being blocked instantly, unable to approach the King of Chaos.

What the hell is this? It's blocked me!

It seems the opponent's techniques don't rely on magic. My magical immunity won't help here..."

Merlin realized the problem. The enemy's techniques didn't rely on magic, so it wouldn't be so easy to win.

The people of the Chaos Clan on this island were a new species born from the invasion of foreign energy. Their source of power came from another world, naturally not part of the magic and qi systems.

The King of Chaos, as the ruler at the top of the food chain in the Mysterious Seas, wasn't comparable to the little demons Merlin had previously slain. Its methods were far more varied.

"You're surprised? Perhaps you underestimate me? A foolish little mouse..."

Merlin had somewhat underestimated the King of Chaos, the enemy not using magic, which made him feel a bit unexpected.

"Your surprise is just the beginning!" The King of Chaos swung his hands continuously, creating more invisible walls, enclosing Merlin within them, then pressing in, making the space shrink.

"Damn it!"

Merlin was trapped by several invisible walls, the space around him being squeezed under the King of Chaos's influence, his bones nearly being crushed, even the space to draw his sword was nonexistent!

Although Merlin's sword-drawing technique was strong, it required a certain amount of space to execute. If he couldn't even draw his blade, it was a very frustrating situation.

"How are you? Where did your arrogant flame go? Hahaha..." The King of Chaos looked at Merlin being squeezed by the invisible walls, feeling very pleased.

"Don't be too happy too soon, bastard..." Merlin's eyes burned like coals. Though the invisible walls trapped him, it wasn't enough to kill him; cracks were slowly forming...

"Oh~, you can't kill me? Your life is quite tough..."

The King of Chaos noticed the cracks in the invisible walls, knowing how long Merlin could be trapped. He should quickly use an attack with extremely destructive power to deal a heavy blow to the enemy!

Suddenly, it extended its hand, pointing its finger to the ceiling of the underground palace, which echoed with the red vortex outside the sky.

Dark purple foreign energy suddenly began to converge, surging mysterious power filling the entire palace, clearly a powerful destructive technique with a wide area of effect!

The King of Chaos suddenly smiled with his mouth open, pointing his finger at the trapped Merlin, and a dazzling dark purple light suddenly flashed, seeming to symbolize the coming of the apocalypse.

"Give me your head!"

"How dare you, you ignorant human mouse!"

title: Chapter 29 — Sanction (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 29 — Sanction (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 20 · Chapter 29

Morrison, Adams, and Reni were still locked in fierce combat with the Chaos Trio's third member, Okot.

Admittedly, Okot's strength was extraordinary. Even against three Saint-tier powerhouses, he showed no signs of losing and was subtly pushing the upper hand.

Okot's tentacles seemed to grow infinitely, constantly erupting from the ground and catching the three off guard.

Furthermore, those tentacles were coated in venom. Morrison and the others had to be careful when dealing with them, which added considerable pressure without anyone saying a word.

Adams channeled his Saint-tier magical power surging around him, dodging back and forth while clutching his alchemy lute. Whenever he plucked the strings, a piercing sound rang out.

The sound waves acted like sharp blades, slicing through the surrounding tentacles. The destructive power was truly shocking!

Although Adams's defenses were watertight, venom still splashed onto his body, immediately producing thick white smoke and making him gasp sharply in pain—

"Hisss…"

At that moment of distraction, four thick tentacles suddenly burst from underground, pressing their advantage, aiming to kill the team's mage Adams outright!

Morrison abruptly appeared in front of Adams, having already shifted into Rakshasa state, doubling his strength. His body turned crimson red, and the horns on his head grew extraordinarily sharp.

"Huh!"

Morrison let out a mighty roar, his fist generating a ferocious storm that scattered all the tentacles targeting Adams.

Meanwhile, Reni in the distance wasn't idle either. She continuously pulled the trigger, her alchemy hunting rifle spitting flames straight at Okot's face.

"Heh heh heh…" Okot let out a grotesque laugh. With a wave of his hand, a massive number of tentacles emerged, weaving together into a shield that made the alchemy rifle struggle to pierce through. "It's useless. Is that really all you've got? I thought you'd be troublesome enemies, but your strength is just so-so. Before me, you're nothing but clowns, good only for passing the time…"

Adams's expression darkened. He never expected the monsters on this island to be so stubborn—completely different from the grunts they'd fought before. "If this keeps up, we'll be forced onto the defensive. We have to find a way to get close and tear through its defenses!"

"Yeah, once our strength is exhausted, this monster will grind us to death…" Reni frowned deeply. She found the octopus-faced monster ahead extremely difficult to deal with. Moreover, fighting three against one showed not a hint of fatigue. This clearly wasn't suitable for a war of attrition.

"No other choice then. Watch this…" Morrison clenched his fists, the alchemy gauntlets creaking under the pressure.

"You have a plan?" Adams asked in surprise.

"When it comes to fighting to the death, I've got quite a bit of experience…" Morrison slowly stepped forward, preparing for one all-out desperate strike.

Adams fell silent, thinking that Morrison was at least the Seventh Knight of Thorns, so he must have some unique ability.

"I'll provide remote support for you." Reni offered to assist.

"Oh ho ho~ What? Neither of you three can match me alone, and now you're thinking about fighting one-on-one?" Okot sneered mockingly.

"I'm going to cut off the tentacles on your face and roast them for snacks!" Morrison's speed suddenly surged, charging straight at Okot.

"Heh heh heh…" Okot spread his arms wide. A swarm of tentacles erupted from the ground, aiming to strangle the reckless Morrison!

Bang bang bang! Continuous gunshots rang out. Reni's alchemy rifle constantly spat flames, shooting through the tentacles targeting Morrison.

Morrison's body surged with crimson battle aura, his entire figure seeming to descend into madness. He leapt into the air and struck down at Okot with tremendous force.

Tentacles crisscrossed instantly, forming a protective net. But under Rakshasa state, Morrison's destructive power was astonishing—it was clearly unable to block him!

A ferocious storm swept through the surroundings, crushing even the rocks into powder. Morrison's attack caused the ground to collapse, forming terrifying cracks!

"Ugh!" Morrison felt a flicker of surprise. His most powerful strike still hadn't managed to break through Okot's defense. Those individual tentacles had changed, now shining with a metallic luster!

"How is this possible? Even that didn't work?!" Adams's eyes widened, finding it unbelievable.

"Those tentacles… have been reinforced…" Reni adjusted her radar glasses. The enemy had been hiding their true strength all along!

"Hmph hmph hmph, foolish creature. Can't beat me, so you want to risk your life against me?" Dark purple energy surged around Okot—that was power from another world. "Want to defeat me? How about you measure yourself properly first!?"

The metallic-luster tentacles suddenly vibrated and counterattacked Morrison, piercing straight through his abdomen!

Morrison coughed up a mouthful of blood, quickly clutching his bleeding abdomen as he retreated. If not for the Rakshasa state, this strike would have cost him his life!

"Lord Morrison!" Adams moved forward to help support him.

"I'm fine…" Morrison pressed his hands against his gushing wound. The toxin had entered his bloodstream, making his spirit fuzzy. He felt extremely sleepy, his entire body slipping into a numb paralysis.

"Fine?" Okot let out a sinister chuckle. "You say that so lightly. You've already been poisoned by my toxin. Before long, you'll be numb, unable to move a single muscle—just like a dead man."

"Tch!" Morrison ground his teeth in anger, but his gradually paralyzing body proved Okot was right.

"Disappear neatly for me!" Okot's eyes bulged with rage. Clearly, he had finished playing, and began wielding his metal-reinforced tentacles toward the trio, aiming to strangle them all here!

But just then, the earth began to tremble with a deep rumbling sound—

"W-what's happening!?" A bead of cold sweat rolled down Adams's forehead.

"You don't think it's…" Reni suspected enemy reinforcements.

Only then did they see from the depths of the island, a dark purple beam of light shooting straight into the sky!

Like a laser, it tore through the heavens from the ground, connecting to the giant crimson vortex swirling above!

The entire island was trembling, as if experiencing a magnitude 10 earthquake, the earth sinking into the deep sea!

Morrison and the others could barely stand, collapsing to their knees on the ground as they gazed at the furious sword of light cleaving the sky!

"What… what is this? What an overwhelming pressure… my heart… it feels like it's about to stop beating…" Reni shivered, her face drained of all color.

"Is there such a terrifying existence on this island?! Where on earth… have we ended up…?" Adams stammered, utterly terrified to the point of despair. With such a powerful existence on this island, what was the point of fighting? Might as well surrender!

As for Morrison? He was completely frozen in fear, watching as the dark purple light pillar was about to pierce through the island.

Was this incomparable pressure real? The monsters on this island actually possessed such terrifying power!

The Lahmann who had previously disrupted the kingdom was nothing more than a small fry compared to this power!

In a direct confrontation, Britannia wouldn't stand a chance!

Morrison lowered his head. The fear in his heart couldn't be hidden—the unsteady, trembling look in his eyes revealed everything.

Okot's gaze fixed on the dark purple light beam, narrowing his eyes slightly as he thought—

Did an enemy enter the underground palace and disturb Master?

That bastard Ralf, was he busy eating shit? He couldn't even stop a single mouse…

But since it forced Master to use otherworldly energy for punishment, the enemy's strength must not be underestimated!

Σ( ° △ °|||)

I haven't forgotten that I owe a chapter update—I'll definitely make it up!

title: Chapter 30 — Decision!
content:
Chapter 30 — Decision!

Volume 20 · Chapter 30

Morison and the other two stood dumbfounded as the dark purple pillar of light erupted into the sky, accompanied by a terrifying oppressive pressure.

They fell silent, no words coming out, suddenly realizing how naive their plan to sweep across the island's monsters had been.

Forget about finding a way to leave the island; with such a powerful existence, merely surviving seemed like an enormous problem.

Ocot turned his gaze away, thinking that since the Chaos King was now serious, his enemies must have already been dealt with.

No one in all his memory had ever survived the Chaos King's full-force strike, and this time would be no exception.

"I didn't expect quite so many rats to have climbed onto this island. I truly underestimated you..."

Morison frowned, feeling that the current situation was extremely dangerous. If they continued exploring the island, death was certain. The best course was to leave immediately, but the octopus monster before them was a vicious opponent, and they needed some way to kill the bastard.

"But what's the point? Stupid enough to anger my master, and you won't even be granted the chance to beg for mercy." The tentacle beside Ocot writhed slowly as it spoke with ominous significance. "Your fate is only death. Not a single one of you will escape!"

Morison and his companions had no idea what had happened, but one thing was certain—

Only by defeating Ocot could they hope to survive...

Dust filled the air, rubble lay everywhere; the underground palace had been nearly reduced to ruins.

The Chaos King had delivered a final blow to Merlin, flattening the entire area.

The dome ceiling had been completely pierced through, revealing the outside world. In the sky above, the crimson vortex continued its slow rotation.

The Chaos King gazed at the devastation before him, his expression darkening as he spoke in a low voice—

"You can't even die from this? As expected, compared to me, you are the real monster..."

Rustling sounds echoed as Merlin slowly climbed out from the rubble. He had suffered several minor wounds, blood trickling from them, making him look thoroughly disheveled.

His clothes had been torn apart, exposing his bare upper body, his right arm corroded by vampire toxins, and the gruesome wounds across his chest all laid bare.

This scarred steel-like physique was no medal of honor for Merlin—it was a mark left by past humiliations.

"A monster? Ah~, yes, many people have called me that. But it's not because my power is too great to be called a monster; it's simply because your strength is too weak."

"Oh? Is that so?" The Chaos King silently clenched his fists, gazing at Merlin's battered body. "What's with that scarred body of yours? You look like someone who has struggled at the edge of death countless times."

"I have indeed come close to death more than once, but I endured every time. Those bastards who humiliated me—I remember all of them. One day, I will personally kill them all, one by one."

Merlin stood bare-chested, gripping the tachi in his hand. The recent attack had left his entire body feeling numb and tingling.

Clearly, the energy from another world was different from mana—it not only bypassed Merlin's magical immunity but also exerted a suppressive effect on his body.

He wondered what kind of existence this otherworldly civilization truly was. Even though the Chaos King had only absorbed some of this energy, it had made him this powerful!

If there truly were a powerhouse from another world, just how formidable could they possibly be? It was hard to imagine!

"How unfortunate. You won't have the chance..."

The Chaos King wasn't foolish either. The powerful blast earlier had had negligible effect on Merlin—he hadn't been able to kill the man before him.

This alone demonstrated the enemy's formidable strength. If he didn't take this seriously and give it his all, he could very well suffer a humiliating defeat!

Then all that remained was to use his final trump card. He had to unleash his signature technique and eliminate this mysterious human right here in one stroke!

The Chaos King reached up to his face, grasping the black eye patch covering his eye, and slowly removed the seal that had been restricting his power.

"Because you will never walk out of here alive. This place will be your tomb. I will make you rest eternal—

"Tch!"

Merlin clicked his tongue. Seeing the Chaos King about to remove his eye patch, his expression instantly turned grim, and he remembered Ralf's final warning.

"You can't beat that monster. Turn back while you still can. If you insist on going, watch out for those eyes!"

The enemy could ignore his magical immunity, so regardless of whether Ralf was exaggerating, he needed to be careful. It was best to nip every danger in the bud!

Merlin suddenly assumed a draw-ready stance, stomped hard against the ground, and launched himself into the air, attempting a flying strike to sever the Chaos King's head before he could remove his eye patch.

However, Merlin seemed to have forgotten that his body, corroded by vampire毒素, was extremely vulnerable to sunlight.

Just moments before, the dome of the underground palace had been pierced and collapsed, and the outside sunlight streamed in unimpeded.

The moment Merlin leaped out of the shadow and into the sunlight—

The sunlight instantly transformed into lethal rays, triggering the curse that caused vampires to combust and die upon exposure to sun!

"Urgh!"

Merlin's face contorted in shock. He saw sparks rising from his corroded right arm, which instantly burst into flames!

He gritted his teeth, enduring the excruciating pain of spontaneous combustion. If he persisted with his attack, he would surely be consumed by the flames!

The situation was critical. Forced to abandon his initiative strike, he quickly pulled back mid-air and retreated into the shadows.

Merlin fell to the ground, rolling and slapping himself to quickly extinguish the burning right arm.

Upon closer inspection, after merely seconds of contact with sunlight, his entire right arm had been burned down to bare bone!

If Merlin had hesitated just a moment longer, he likely would have been killed by the sun before he could even slay the Chaos King!

The隐患 left by Cain was gradually manifesting—not only tormenting Merlin's body and mind, but also costing him the optimal moment to eliminate the Chaos King at this critical juncture!

"What? A human who fears sunlight? So you're just like us... a monster!" The Chaos King had removed his eye patch. His dark purple pupils gleamed like gems as he stared down at Merlin below. "We are both abnormalities!"

Instinctively, Merlin raised his head and caught sight of the Chaos King's eerie eyes. It felt as though his very soul was being sucked away.

His entire body trembled, and his mind suffered an unparalleled blow in that instant.

"Damn it..."

Starting from Merlin's left arm, petrification was visibly spreading, devouring his flesh by the second.

His petrified body grew incredibly heavy, severely limiting his movement. It would only take a few seconds before he became a vivid statue, identical to the stone figures throughout this place!

The sheer terror of the Chaos King's power was evident in Merlin's panicked expression—few enemies ever managed to fluster him.

This monster wielding otherworldly energy was absolutely nothing like his previous foes; its suppressive capabilities far exceeded anything he had faced before!

Merlin watched in horror as the petrification was about to spread from his left arm to the rest of his body. Cold sweat poured down his frame in a desperate situation.

So Merlin gritted his teeth, steeled his heart, and made a shocking decision that stunned everyone—

He drew his tachi and wedged it under his armpit...

Then, with eyes wide and roaring in fury, he ruthlessly severed his own left arm!

"Uaaaaaaaaaah!"

title: Chapter 31 — Boundary Mind's Eye (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 31 — Boundary Mind's Eye (Extra Chapter)

Volume 20 · Chapter 31

Merlin's petrified left arm was flailing through the air before it finally crashed onto the ground and shattered into pieces.

Merlin's rapid decision to sever his own left arm with his own hands had spared him the danger of being entirely turned to stone.

If he hadn't been decisive enough to cut off his own arm, he might well have found himself in an even more dire situation.

But as a result, his entire body had fallen into a severely weakened state, having lost an arm.

At the cleanly-cut stump of Merlin's left shoulder, blood surged and then erupted forth like volcanic lava gushing from an eruption.

For a moment, it was as if a crimson blood rain were falling within the underground palace, dripping relentlessly onto the statues and dyeing them a vivid red.

Merlin knelt on one knee, propping himself up with his katana, gasping for breath in great heaves, his head bowed so that he would never again look up to meet the chaotic king's demonic eyes.

The power from another world was so bizarre, as if completely unstoppable, making one wonder what kind of existence the other world truly was.

The King of Chaos looked down at Merlin from above, particularly at his left shoulder which was bleeding profusely, and couldn't help but utter an exclamation of admiration. "A wise decision. You're ruthless even toward yourself. In countless ages, I've seen many people who couldn't bear to harm their own bodies, and in the end they were drained completely dry of their life force and became lifelike statues. You are utterly different from those people, and this is the first time I've encountered such a one. If circumstances allowed, I would very much like you to join us."

"What the hell...." Merlin said coldly with his head bowed, vowing never to fall for the King of Chaos's technique a second time. As long as he didn't look directly into his enemy's eyes, there wouldn't be any problems.

"What a pity. I value talented individuals, but alas, you won't get along with us. Then there's nothing to be done...." The King of Chaos, confident that Merlin wouldn't dare meet his gaze, strode fearlessly toward Merlin. "I'll just have to kill you. Someone like you surviving would be a threat to everyone—"

Merlin took a deep breath and slowly closed his eyes, his entire being becoming incredibly calm, his panicked heart quickly settling into a state as still as unmoving water.

It looked as though Merlin had resigned himself to waiting for death, but that wasn't the case at all.

He simply needed quiet, to make himself even more "still," so that he could perceive more of reality with ease.

Since he couldn't look into his enemy's eyes, Merlin needed to be extremely careful. He decided that throughout this battle, until the very last moment, he would not open his eyes.

He intended to win by utilizing the supreme level of swordsmanship known as "Mind's Eye." To explain it plainly, it meant closing your eyes, plunging yourself into darkness, and drawing your blade to attack relying solely on your senses!

This special skill wasn't anything rare, but rather an transcendent state that only a handful of swordsmen could comprehend after reaching a certain level in their sword techniques!

Anything practiced to its absolute极限 will eventually lead one to understand what ordinary people cannot——that is the instinct deeply embedded in the soul...

Many swordsmanship masters had once described the feeling of the "Mind's Eye." Though their eyes were tightly shut, they saw more than before, clearer than ever——everything slowed down, to the point where one could even sever a rushing current of water!

Merlin rarely fought with his eyes closed, but facing such a troublesome opponent this time, it seemed he had no choice but to employ this elusive art.

Merlin slowly returned his katana to its scabbard, the crisp vibration echoing endlessly in his ears——

The sound of wind, the sound of water, his enemy's mocking laughter...

All these sounds converged in Merlin's ears and ultimately归于 silence, nothing audible remaining.

Within Merlin's heart, everything around him formed a vivid picture, and even the slightest roll of a stone couldn't escape the range of his "Mind's Eye." Everything was within his掌控.

"Hehehe...."

The King of Chaos laughed arrogantly, rapidly wriggling around Merlin to disrupt him. Though Merlin was at a disadvantage, he lay in wait like a venomous snake ready to strike at the slightest opening.

It still dared not underestimate this man and was searching for a way to deliver a fatal blow.

Merlin's body was covered in wounds, but the scar on his chest was the most gruesome of them all.

The King of Chaos fixated on that spot, preparing to pierce straight through Merlin's heart and personally send this man to hell.

"Die, you stubborn fool! Submitting to me would have let you live. Since you refuse, then there's nothing I can do..."

Merlin maintained his iai stance, motionless as still water where he stood, his mind empty, desiring only to merge with the wind and the earth.

Suddenly, he felt time become incredibly slow, his heart beating once every so often.

A strand of icy cold energy penetrated through his heart, shattering the quiet and dark picture.

Merlin suddenly opened his eyes, his expression commanding respect without a trace of anger. Before anyone could realize it, his blade was already drawn——a single-handed iai slash wielded with his right hand alone!

"The blade cuts the body, the heart slays the soul!"

The air filled with a coppery stench, a crimson glow flashing suddenly, flowing and surging like a vibrant haori fluttering in the wind.

Merlin's posture was fierce and sharp, his katana seeming eager to cleave through everything around him.

Due to the impossibly fast speed of his draw, not a single drop of blood stained the blade of Banri Garan.

Merlin slightly raised his eyelids and could no longer see the ugly face of the King of Chaos, nor those dazzling eyes.

What he saw instead was a gushing fountain of blood, splashing and spraying in all directions.

The King of Chaos had already become a headless corpse——its head had flown off like a soccer ball, rolling across the ground, death's disbelief still lingering in its eyes!

Merlin had originally been driven to a desperate situation by his enemy; had the King of Chaos managed to pierce his heart, he would have won.

But to everyone's surprise, Merlin launched a counterattack at the critical final moment. His strength had exceeded the King of Chaos's imagination——he was almost like a perfect creature with no weaknesses whatsoever.

To accurately kill an enemy relying solely on perception while blind——swordsmen capable of reaching such a level could be counted on only a few fingers across all the continents!

The neat incision on that neck showcased Merlin's masterful iaijutsu, and the spraying blood was like celebratory cannon fire marking victory.

The headless corpse of the King of Chaos thrashed and staggered, apparently unwilling to die so easily, but in the end it fell heavily to the ground, twitching uncontrollably.

The battle ended in an instant. Though Merlin's face was pale, he finally exhaled a long breath, returned his katana to the scabbard at his waist, and looked down at the headless corpse of the King of Chaos.

Merlin cupped his aching right shoulder, tore off a strip of cloth from his pants, and used his teeth alongside his right hand to apply a simple bandage and stop the bleeding.

Then he placed his foot on the headless corpse of the King of Chaos and spoke in a loaded tone——

"Sorry. You made a mistake just now."

"This is clearly your own graveyard."

title: Chapter 32 — Returning with a Bounty
content:
Chapter 32 — Returning with a Bounty

Volume 20 · Chapter 32

Merlin kicked the headless corpse of the Chaos King aside and, taking advantage of the motion, picked up the head rolling on the ground.
Although the Chaos King was already dead, its head full of snake hair still emitted a 'hiss' sound.
Those eyes are still pretty formidable; I might as well take it back—couldn't it be a rare treasure....
Merlin thought to himself, found a piece of black cloth, wrapped the Chaos King's head in it, and slung it onto his back.
He wouldn't look at those eerie eyes again, but he could show them to enemies—instant petrification is still quite useful.
Merlin looked around and saw, deep in the underground palace, an inconspicuous door that might be the Chaos King's treasure chamber.
Just thinking he might obtain something like the flowing pearls treasure made Merlin's heart jump twice, a bit excited; after all this effort he was finally about to get the precious materials he'd been seeking.
So Merlin stepped forward without hesitation, pushed open the door with his only remaining right hand, and saw a pitch-black interior.
Merlin walked in, and suddenly red flames flared on both sides, bathing the place in crimson light while also letting him see the interior clearly.
Before him stood three stone pedestals, each bearing—well, three strange items—.
On them were placed an old piece of parchment, a withered white arm emitting a faint glow, and a strange stone.
This empty room only held these three items, which looked extremely precious.
Merlin approached with a nervous heart to examine these things, which might all be rare treasures.
First was the old parchment; Merlin unfolded it and found it was an ancient map, similar to a nautical chart.
Unfortunately the edges were uneven, obviously torn; only half remained, on which some sea area markings could be clearly seen.
Merlin examined it closely and found the information limited and partly illegible because the script was twisted and very ancient; experts could still make out some of it.
"Tsk! Is this a treasure map? Only... 'mi' left...."
Merlin scratched his head, feeling a bit annoyed; he guessed this parchment was a treasure map, but half of it was missing—really disgusting.
Although Merlin felt unhappy, he obediently put the treasure map into his bosom; when he had time he could have someone else look at it—maybe there would be some clues.
Approaching the second prize, the withered white arm emitting a faint glow, Merlin curiously touched it with his hand, and suddenly his whole body shuddered; an expression of hostility and disgust unconsciously appeared on his face.
Being able to make a demon produce such an instinctive reaction shows it's clearly a dangerous enemy, a natural foe of the opposing side!
Merlin furrowed his brows, carefully examining the arm: pure white all over, with... feathers?
Having read many demon race tomes, he knew that a body pure white, feathered, and glowing was exactly like the celestial spirit warriors recorded in the texts—could even be called angels without issue.
Four hundred thousand years ago, in the demon era, countless demons perished together with the celestial spirits, their bodies turning to ash; who would have thought that an angel's arm would have fallen into the mysterious sea and been picked up by the Chaos King?
Merlin felt deeply moved; as the youngest monarch of the demon race, he had never witnessed that bloody holy war, but from the few fragments in the books he could still imagine its cruelty.
Being able to see a celestial spirit's arm today is also a considerable gain, after all such beings from other planes are very rare, especially when they come from the heavenly realm.
On the hand of this celestial spirit's arm was worn a— a dazzling silver ring, antiquely styled, looking like nothing ordinary.
Merlin hesitated a moment, then took off the ring; immediately the celestial spirit's arm, as if deprived of nourishment, quickly withered and turned into feathers that scattered in the air.
After playing with it for a while, Merlin searched his memory, showing a mocking, suddenly enlightened expression; he could basically confirm what this ring was—.
Ancient records state that the celestial spirits' combat power was astonishing; each wore a ring forged by the archangel Uriel with hellfire, named 'Anjier'.
Wearing it grants two lives; upon death, one can trigger the power of 'Anjier' to resurrect on the spot!
That's why celestial spirits are so hard to deal with—not only are they strong and well-equipped, but they can also... trust Spring Brother to resurrect on the spot!
A hundred thousand celestial spirits can easily handle twenty thousand demon legions; their combat power is twice that of demons, precisely because they possess a—second life.
Holding this ring in hand one can feel the gentle aura of the heavenly realm, and while gathering magical elements from the air, besides instant resurrection it likely also aids cultivation and repels evil creatures....
Although Merlin liked the instant-resurrection ability, the heavenly aura made him feel disgusted; looking at the explanation of 'Anjier', it should undoubtedly be a pseudo-artifact.
Exactly, even the most ordinary celestial spirit warrior can wear a rare pseudo-artifact, showing how terrifying the heavenly realm's strength truly is.
Actually, the demon race's strength in the demon era is not weak either; being called the overlord of the mortal world is not an exaggeration, and they had the capability to stand against the angels, but after suffering heavy losses in the holy war, they never recovered.
Even now, the demon race still squanders its foundation, huddled in a corner of the world, barely surviving....
Merlin thought of the 'Anjier' ring as a sort of exchange; even if he didn't like it, it was still a rare pseudo-artifact that he could give to someone else.
The third prize was a plain, unremarkable stone, looking utterly ordinary with nothing special about it.
If it weren't placed in such a lofty location, anyone could glance at it twice and just toss it away.
Merlin fiddled with the stone, lightly tapping it with his finger, producing a 'dong dong dong' sound—.
Suddenly, the whole stone trembled, 'pfft' and opened countless eyes on its surface, staring at Merlin in astonishment.
Merlin was startled by the stone's many eyes staring at him, jumping back; thinking of the Chaos King's eerie eyes, he felt a lingering dread.
But Merlin quickly recalled what that old woman Seysi had told him: the abyssal sea clam's body is covered in eyes—couldn't this be exactly the same?
Merlin turned his surprise into joy, hurled the abyssal sea clam to the ground, drew his blade and slashed!
"Squeak!!!"
The abyssal sea clam screamed continuously, its shell mostly shattered, plasma gushing nonstop.
Merlin watched the cold abyssal sea clam and thought that such a rare creature actually had no resistance at all—how weak....
So

title: Chapter 33 — Noob Passing By (Extra)
content:
Chapter 33 — Noob Passing By (Extra)

Volume 20 · Chapter 33

Fingering the flowing pearl in his hand, it seemed to contain a considerable amount of otherworldly energy.
No wonder, as a creature living in the gap between two worlds, it looked quite different.
Merlin was in a good mood; after all those twists and turns, he finally hadn't come for nothing, obtaining something crucial.
At the very least, this would save Alice; if he had returned empty-handed after all that effort, Merlin would probably be so angry he'd roll his eyes.
Merlin intended to leave, but the instant he turned back, he saw strange lights flickering intermittently deep within the treasure chamber.
Merlin stopped his steps, curiously venturing deeper to explore, only to witness an astonishing sight—
Red flames blazed on the ground, forming an eerie altar that appeared to have existed for quite some time.
At the center of the flame altar lay a pitch-black small box, inlaid with a red gemstone.
...What the heck?
Merlin curiously walked over, picked up the black lacquered box and tapped it, his face lighting up with keen interest.
Could it be another good thing? Good heavens! My luck today is off the charts.....
Merlin rolled up his sleeves, exerting all his strength to pry open the box, eager to see what lay hidden in the deepest part of the treasure chamber.
Since Merlin temporarily had only one arm left, he had to clamp the box with his foot, repeatedly trying to pry it open with his sole hand.
As a result, Merlin's face flushed red, veins bulging on his arm, yet the mysterious black box remained utterly unmoved!
Merlin panted, unwilling to accept defeat, drew his katana and began to lever it, but the result was the same.
No way?
Merlin's two eyebrows knit together on his forehead, feeling somewhat incredulous—what treasure could be inside a box he couldn't open even with all his strength?
So Merlin lifted the box, shook it near his ear, but heard nothing at all—utterly silent—
Empty! ?
Really unlucky!
However, the box's design is antiquated, and the gemstone on it is quite nice; it's probably worth some money.
Forget it, I'll just take it back with me....
At the same moment Merlin picked up the box from the ground, the outside of the underground palace underwent a noticeable change.
The scarlet vortex in the sky vanished, the storm surrounding the island dissipated, and the weather cleared to cloudless skies.
Captain Dennis of the William personally witnessed all of this, the storm subsiding at a speed visible to the naked eye.
The captain's crew stirred into action; just moments ago the area around the island had been enduring apocalyptic storms, and in the blink of an eye it turned into clear blue skies.
A certain sailor muttered doubtfully: '...What's happening?'
Although Captain Dennis didn't know what had happened, he realized something even more important—
"Never mind what happened! Quickly prepare the sails—we must seize this chance to escape here!"
Captain Dennis issued the order; the disappearance of the storm before his eyes was a good omen, and he couldn't let this opportunity slip—if the storm returned, there would be no hope at all!
Merlin, inside the underground palace, remained oblivious to the outside situation, still believing everything stemmed from the death of the Chaos King, unaware that the outside events had any direct connection to the box he had taken.
Morrison and his two companions were panting heavily; after Octec became serious, the three were beaten back relentlessly, the situation turning very passive.
Octec noticed the change in the island's environment, especially the disappearance of the vortex in the sky; his face instantly darkened, cold sweat trickling down his forehead—
How—how could this be! Someone moved the box in the secret chamber!?
So... the master is already dead!? ! !
...Who did it! The master's power is so immense—how could anyone possibly accomplish this!?
And they even moved the box in the flame altar—killing people and cutting off their hearts! Is this meant to annihilate our entire clan!?
Octec's face turned ashen, his whole body trembling, his eyes filled with bewilderment—he never imagined the Chaos King would die, and that the evil box had been tampered with.
"...What the hell have these bastards done!? Are they trying to drag us down with them!?"
"Huh?" Morrison frowned, not understanding why Octec had suddenly lost control of his emotions and was shouting loudly.
Adams and Rene exchanged glances; neither really understood what had happened—the enemy who had just been calm and composed suddenly descended into madness.
"Doomed, doomed, doomed...." Octec clutched his head with both hands, repeatedly saying, "Why did you move that box!? We'll all—die!"
The raving Octec brimmed with resentment, furious as if he'd become another person, continually roaring at the three humans Morrison, Adams, and Rene.
"What are you saying?" Adams asked, steeling himself.
"It's all you—you lot who brought in that ominous filth!" Octec's eyes bloodshot, he roared angrily, "That box is an extremely dangerous object; whoever opens it will unleash an unprecedented catastrophe of silver hair! No one can escape it unscathed, and moreover—......"
Morrison noticed Octec losing control, hearing only gibberish, completely unaware of what he was saying, so he whispered to his companions behind him, "This guy seems to have gone mad....
"I think so too." Adams nodded.
"Now the opportunity is rare—should we... strike while it's sick, take its life?" Rene's eyes grew deep, feeling that Octec's loss of control would make him easier to deal with.
"Good idea, let's move!" Morrison bellowed, swinging his fists and charging forward; although his body was nearly numb, the state of the yaksha ghost greatly increased his resistance, allowing him to withstand Octec's paralyzing toxin—whereas an ordinary person would already be immobilized.
"Let's quickly take down this monster and then return to the William; I always have a bad feeling." Adams plucked his lute, ultra‑high‑speed sound blades shooting out, slicing past with a swish‑swish‑swish.
"Let's take care of this monster first...." Rene set up her alchemical fire gun, aiming at Octec's forehead and firing repeatedly!
"You've destroyed my kin; I'll leave you all here to be buried with me!" Octec flung his arms wide, and instantly countless thick tentacles erupted from the earth below, covered in gleaming metallic scales, smashing fiercely at the three clueless humans—"Die, die, go die! You bunch of despicable humans!"
For a moment, dust filled the air, the island trembled slightly, and the ground pounded with a thunderous roar as the tentacles hammered it.
Although Morrison and his companions had the upper hand, they still dared not underestimate Octec's corpse; if struck continuously by those metallic tentacles, they would surely be smashed to pieces!
At this moment, a friend with no money, no power, no influence—the "weakest" member of the fleet—happened to pass by here......
Merlin, returning laden with spoils, the black cloth bag on his back holding the Chaos King's head, once again saw Morrison and his trio battling the octopus‑faced foe.
Seeing them fighting so intensely, Merlin instantly wore an incomprehensible expression, thinking to himself—
What are they up to?
Has the novice‑versus‑novice pecking not ended yet?
Come on, I've already blown up the enemy base's crystals—what are you still doing here showing off those elementary‑school‑level fancy moves?
(∞0)

title: Chapter 34 — Level Gap
content:
Chapter 34 — Level Gap

Volume 20 · Chapter 34

Merlin completely ignored the few people squabbling like chickens, turned around, and directly returned to the William.
He saw the sailors were busy, as if they were preparing to set sail.
Captain Dennis kept shouting, urging the sailors to work faster.
Now the storm around the island has subsided; if we don't leave this damned place now, when will we?
Merlin looked at Captain Dennis and couldn't help asking—
“Captain Dennis, are you ready to leave?”
“Lord Merlin!? You’re back? Yeah, the fog and storm have temporarily cleared, we… uh!” Captain Dennis was about to explain, but seeing Merlin covered in wounds, he sucked in a cold breath, “Hiss… you… what happened to you?”
Merlin glanced at his missing left arm, sighed helplessly, and thought he’d need to figure something out, “It’s nothing serious, I just ran into a somewhat troublesome opponent.”
“A bit troublesome…” Captain Dennis broke into a cold sweat, thinking, “Is it really that simple to be a bit troublesome?” “You didn’t go explore the island alone, did you? How did you come back looking like this?”
“I went to the island to find a material, and casually took out whatever ruler was there…” Merlin shrugged helplessly, “So I ended up like this.”
“Uh…”
Captain Dennis wore an incredulous expression—had Merlin single-handedly killed the island’s monster leader?
Could the storm’s dissipation be directly related to him? This can’t be true, right? Obviously Lord Morrison and the others haven’t returned yet, yet Merlin, who left the William last, already finished the job?!
Although Captain Dennis knew Merlin was strong, saying so casually that the enemy boss was already dead still seemed hard to believe.
And how long has it been? The task is already done in hardly any time—this efficiency… is too fast!
“Are you really that surprised?” Merlin asked expressionlessly.
“No… no, please tell me you’re alright? Your arm… your arm…” Captain Dennis’s face kept changing as he looked at Merlin’s severed arm, feeling pain himself.
“Ah…” Merlin furrowed his brow, shook his head, “No problem, the bleeding has stopped.”
“My ship has medicine for treating blade wounds; do you need some?” Captain Dennis thought Merlin’s injury was actually quite severe, estimating the enemy’s strength was formidable, unaware that Merlin had actually cut himself.
“I need a highly skilled priest to regenerate my arm; ordinary medicine won’t help.” Merlin thought treating his arm should wait until after leaving this damned place.
“Alright… alright…” Captain Dennis stopped pressing and instinctively asked, “May I ask if you’ve seen Lord Morrison and the others? Why have you returned while they haven’t?”
“Oh, them…” Merlin glanced in a direction, said calmly, “I saw them still fighting the monsters; the battle was quite intense, so I came back first.”
“What???” Captain Dennis was instantly dumbfounded, thinking, “Lord Merlin already killed the boss and came back, while Morrison and the others are still fighting the small fry back and forth?”
“I’m a bit tired; I’ll go rest now. If there’s nothing particularly important, please don’t disturb me.” Merlin waved his hand and headed straight for the cabin.
“Understood, Lord Merlin; if you need anything, please let me know anytime.” Captain Dennis’s eyes filled with admiration as he watched Merlin leave—
If “iron-blooded tough guy” were used to describe a person, it would probably refer to Lord Merlin, right?
I don’t know if it’s true that he single-handedly killed the boss.
If it’s true, then Lord Merlin’s strength…
Tsk, looking at it now, Morrison and his two companions are just a bunch of loser brothers; compared to Merlin, what do they have to be proud of?
However, just as Merlin returned to his room, he collapsed with a “thud,” his face pale, looking extremely weak.
Fighting the King of Chaos in such a poor state drained him considerably; it’s impossible that losing his left arm had no effect on him.
Slaying Relf eased the heart curse, but having suffered so many heavy blows still left Merlin with serious injuries.
The vampire toxin left by Cain has a major impact; if not resolved quickly, it will likely impose more restrictions later—
“MMP, I never expected the poison to interfere with me this much…”
◇
“Hrahhh!!”
Morrison let out a earth-shaking roar, crimson battle aura flaring as he exerted all his strength to deliver a fatal blow to Ocot.
One punch pierced the chest of this Chaos Triad leader, ending the monster’s life.
Ocot collapsed with a crash, his face still bearing an unwilling expression, gasping—
“You cannot leave alive; you will all… die here as sacrifices, it… it’s coming right away…”
The three panted heavily, sweat soaking their clothes; fighting Ocot left them utterly exhausted.
They fought three against one for a long time before finally subduing the monster, and they almost got counter-killed?
They felt the island’s monsters were strong; they had just witnessed the terrifying pressure of the purple radiance, and truly powerful monsters they hadn’t encountered yet?
If they continued to linger on the island, it would be extremely dangerous; escaping the island has become an urgent matter.
“Finally… finally dead…” Adams wiped the sweat from his forehead, his magic nearly depleted.
“I’m dead tired…” Rene sat on the ground.
“Don’t rest; there are even more terrifying enemies on this island. We must hurry and take the ship away from here.” Morrison gazed into the distance, continuing, “Although we don’t know why the storm cleared, it’s a good opportunity for us.”
Morrison and his companions were unaware that the island’s strongest Chaos King had already been knocked down by Merlin; in truth, there wasn’t much danger, but they had been frightened by a single Ocot.
After reaching a unanimous decision, the three returned to the William, where Captain Dennis had already prepared everything, eager to leave this dangerous place.
“You’ve finally made it back; we’ll set sail immediately, lest the storm return and trap us here!”
“Sorry, we ran into a very powerful monster and got held up.” Morrison said, still shaken.
“This island is dangerous; we should leave as soon as possible.” Adams frowned.
“Captain Dennis, you don’t know this from the ship, but the island is full of terrifying monsters; a little carelessness would wipe us out, and we struggled hard to escape danger…” Rene said with an unpleasant expression.
“???” Captain Dennis wore a strange expression, his forehead full of question marks, left bewildered by the three—
“What are you talking about?”
“Lord Merlin already smashed the boss and called it a day.”
“You three fought ordinary monsters until you were exhausted, yet you act as if you’d accomplished some incredibly difficult feat…”
(?-_??)
The monthly votes are currently #6; tonight I’ll add an extra chapter to make up for Monday’s, so I won’t owe anyone, and tomorrow I can rest a bit, hehe~☆

title: Chapter 35 — Deep Sea Monster (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 35 — Deep Sea Monster (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 20 · Chapter 35

Given the current situation was extremely urgent, Captain Dennis did not mention Merlin's matter, but hurriedly went to take control of the helm.
The repaired William set sail again, full speed away from the island.
Everyone on the bed did not want to linger here, fearing that the terrible storm would return.
Morrison and the three others did not return to the cabin, but tidied up on the deck, still feeling some lingering fear from this encounter--
“I never expected the enemy to be such a terrifying monster; I must report the situation here truthfully to Her Majesty the Queen.” Morrison’s cheeks kept twitching, his speech somewhat stiff, obviously Octot’s poison was taking effect, though this temporary paralysis was not fatal.
“If only our guild leader could come this time, we wouldn’t need to fear anything, just…. Adams sat on the deck, helplessly saying, “The guild leader last time clashed with Elgin the Great Swordsman, causing his consciousness to be injured, and he remains unconscious to this day.”
“That Elgin the Great Swordsman is clearly a scoundrel, yet the Queen actually pardons this outlaw—it’s utterly incomprehensible…” Rene said, full of resentment.
“Well…. Morrison had a few black lines on his forehead, “Elgin the Great Swordsman hasn’t done anything heinous, has he? I actually quite admire him.”
“He injured our guild leader; just based on that, we won’t forgive him.” Adams said solemnly.
“Exactly, although Her Majesty the Queen is willing to forgive this man, we certainly won’t…” Rene echoed.
Morrison didn’t want to say more, feeling deep sympathy for Gregory’s ordeal, so he changed the subject: “I believe Lord Gregory will wake up.”
“What should we do next? After Her Majesty learns of the situation, will she send the Royal Navy to sweep this place clean?” Adams asked curiously.
“I don’t know the Queen’s thoughts, but this place is very dangerous; even if the Royal Navy attacked here, they’d likely suffer heavy losses, so I guess the Queen would choose to blockade this place.” Morrison speculated, having seen the powerful monsters on the island, it’s clearly unrealistic to completely eliminate the kingdom’s potential threat.
“Could it be a blockade of the entire sea area?” Rene couldn’t help but ask further.
Morrison glanced at Adams and Rene, speaking meaningfully: “These matters aren’t convenient to discuss with you, after all they involve royal family decision secrets.”
Adams and Rene gave an embarrassed laugh; they were merely hired adventurers, many things not suitable to inquire about.
Captain Dennis carefully piloted the William; with his experience, based on the current season and wind direction, he could roughly determine the course.
As long as they left the range of the mysterious sea, everyone could completely escape danger; before that, they still needed to be extremely cautious.
Suddenly, the originally blue seawater gradually deepened, turning into a pitch‑black expanse—this was clearly not a good omen—
Sailor: “Captain, quick look! The water’s col…”.
Captain Dennis’s face darkened; he said nothing, merely increasing the William’s speed—his vast experience told him clearly that a massive creature was approaching!
Adams came to the deck’s edge, staring at the pitch‑black sea: “What’s happening? Why has the sea turned black!”
Rene felt a sinister aura: “Is… what monster?”
Morrison gazed at the astonishing sight, cold sweat beading on his forehead: “There’s a monster… an incredibly huge monster, right beneath our ship!”
The reason the blue seawater turned pitch‑black is that an incredibly huge sea monster has appeared in this waters; its black color is exactly the monster’s hue!
Morrison felt at a loss; for the first time he sensed the sailors’ despair and helplessness on the sea—when faced with an unstoppable danger, only death awaited.
The black sea stretched endlessly; it’s hard to imagine just how gigantic the monster lurking beneath the depths truly is……
Morrison recalled Octot’s final ravings, somewhat understanding why he said nobody could escape, and they would stay behind to be buried together.
“Everyone hold on! We’re going full speed ahead! If anyone falls overboard now, no one can save you!” Captain Dennis turned the helm, his powerful command reaching every ear; the monster lurking below might already have locked onto the William, and the only option is to go full speed ahead!
The sails bulged from the wind, the William cut through the calm black sea, speed already at its maximum, yet escaping still felt a bit beyond their strength.
Pop pop pop—
A sound similar to an explosion suddenly rang out, seawater shot up several hundred feet into the air, causing the sailors aboard to become terrified.
Only then did they see several dozen huge, thick, powerful tentacles surge from the deep seabed, writhing in this sea area.
These enormously large tentacles were pitch‑black, covered with rocks and moss; the tiny suckers on them repeatedly contracted and expanded, as if breathing.
When these tentacles appeared, the clear sky instantly turned to night; the sun was completely blocked by the swaying tentacles, plunging everyone into darkness!
The sea churned violently, raising towering waves; in the distance a massive whirlpool gradually formed, frantically swallowing seawater!
We still couldn’t see the monster’s true form; just these dozen tentacles alone made tiny humans look up in awe, even feeling the urge to kneel and worship.
The William appeared incredibly tiny before those gigantic tentacles, like a grain of rice in a human hand that could easily be crushed!
“...What is this?” Adams stared wide‑eyed, already bereft of speech in his terror.
“.Object‑genuine monster!” Rene’s face turned deathly pale as she screamed.
Morrison trembled all over; he had never seen such a colossal sea monster in this world.
However, he had once heard from Leonard, the Knight Commander of the Thorn‑Rose Knights, that the legendary North Sea Giant Monster is a creature so horrifying that merely looking at it would cause one to faint!
Morrison now felt his consciousness clouding, gradually overtaken by fear, unable to tell—could what he saw before him really be the legendary…?
Captain Dennis gazed at the awe‑inspiring sight behind him, his chapped lips trembling; those dozens of tentacles seemed like pillars holding up the sky.
This old man, having sailed the seas for many years and witnessed countless strange phenomena, upon seeing this apocalyptic scene, immediately had an answer—
.....0.司.....
“It’s the Kraken..”..
“Exactly! It’s the North Sea Giant Monster, the Kraken!”
Captain Dennis’s exclamation had just ended, the sailors hadn’t yet had time to react, when the North Sea Giant Monster seemingly noticed the tiny humans aboard the William and lashed out with its thick, massive tentacle—
A slight movement of the North Sea Giant Monster’s tentacle stirred up a terrifying tsunami, carving a huge, hard‑to‑heal gash into the sea!
The people aboard the William watched as a tentacle like a looming mountain came down, all of them shrouded in the shadow of death….
Alright, I’ve just exceeded a monthly ticket, reaching the fifth, which also counts toward fulfilling the extra chapter condition.
After this chapter is done, I’ll do a makeup chapter, then I truly won’t owe anyone anything.

title: Chapter 36 — Petrifying Eye (Extra Update)
content:
Chapter 36 — Petrifying Eye (Extra Update)

Volume 20 · Chapter 36

“Complete……complete disaster?” Morrison watched the towering waves, with no thought of resistance, estimating that a single tentacle of the North Sea Giant Demon could kill everyone on a ship in an instant. As for Adams and Rene? The two were completely dumbfounded, terrified by the Kraken as soon as they appeared. Seeing the sweeping tentacles accompanied by the huge wave slamming over, if hit, the William would surely be smashed to pieces! Captain Dennis now faced the most dangerous moment of his life: alive, he would achieve fame and glory; dead, he would suffer disgrace and ruin! For any sailor who lives by the sea, doing everything possible to survive is the ultimate test! “Hold on tight!!!” Captain Dennis was unwilling to die here; he wanted to challenge that legendary sea monster, not by force but by courage and determination to survive. He roared in the face of the towering waves, his aged body revitalized by the crisis, he spun the wheel with all his strength, the “creak” sounds as if it might snap at any moment. The William’s tiny hull, before the raging seas, was almost twisted, a frantic hard left turn, nearly a 90‑degree drift, trying with all his might to dodge the North Sea Giant Demon’s crushing blow! The hull of this legitimate warship kept trembling, the side planks beginning to split! Who would have thought that this merchant ship carrying rotten fish and shrimp would dare to challenge the Kraken that everyone fears!? On the surging ocean, the tiny William frantically evaded the North Sea Giant Demon’s claws, like a stinky sardine trying to escape a fishing net—slim chances. The Kraken’s tentacles slammed down, sending up a 500‑foot tidal wave, nearly submerging everything in the area under seawater! Yet under Captain Dennis’s handling, the William miraculously avoided that deadly strike, only grazing the edge of the hull. But even just scraping the edge of the North Sea Giant Demon’s tentacle still gave the William a massive jolt, nearly tearing it apart on the sea. Sea water gushed into the cabin, and the William instantly sank six feet! The crew on the William were thrown to and fro; some were even knocked unconscious, and even Captain Dennis, who was at the helm, felt dizzy and blurred. Morrison, Adams, and Rene all slammed into the walls, unable to keep their footing on the ship; even a glancing blow had this destructive power, let alone a direct hit from the North Sea Giant Demon—what would happen then?! The North Sea Giant Demon seemingly hadn’t expected this tiny ship to evade its attack, so a second massive tentacle followed, determined to smash the obstructive William to pieces! This time the Kraken seemed a bit more serious, its tentacles aimed straight at overturning the William, and the waves were twice as fierce as before. The splashing seawater came in waves, making one hear the thunder of a god, though it was merely because the waves were too violent. “……” Morrison lifted his head, watching the Kraken’s tentacles slowly descend, his heart filled with ashes—was this… really the end? Adams and Rene curled up in a corner, covering their heads, their bodies trembling like sieves, facing the Kraken they had lost all their previous arrogance. “Ugh… cough cough cough!!!” Captain Dennis repeatedly vomited seawater with a fishy smell, his whole body drenched, looking older than before, utterly miserable. He dragged his exhausted frame, gripping the William’s wheel with a death grip, vowing to share fate with his beloved ship. The old man tried to turn the wheel with his remaining strength, hoping to dodge the North Sea Giant Demon’s attack again. But a wave of weakness overcame him, and he collapsed onto the wheel, exhausted after just one clash with the Kraken. Captain Dennis would watch as a tentacle like a pillar of heaven pressed down, revealing a resigned smile— The North Sea Giant Demon already controlled this sea; wanting to escape really was a pipe dream. It’s said that over thirty years ago many powerful beings coveted the Gods’ relics, yet all died at the Kraken’s hands. I’m just a former officer‑turned‑pirate merchant captain; challenging the North Sea Giant Demon is nothing but a joke… Faced with an unbeatable North Sea Giant Demon, the life‑seeking tentacles had already struck, and almost everyone on board had despaired—except for one “person.” “Bang!” The cabin door was kicked open; Merlin stepped out, pallid, staggering like a drunk. Merlin wasn’t wearing his demon sword Banri Garan; instead he carried a black sack holding the head of the Chaos King, and he knew exactly what had happened outside— Along the way, Merlin had been tormented beyond human shape, his mind and body in terrible condition. Especially after the battle with the Chaos King, he had been forced to cut off his own arm, which only worsened his dire state. To slay such a colossal sea monster as the North Sea Giant Demon, a large‑scale sweeping sword strike would surely be needed. But Merlin’s current condition does not allow it; his body and spirit are both in terrible shape, making a large‑scale sweep difficult. Moreover, Merlin himself is unsuited for sea combat, with many restrictions; if he mishandles the sweep, he could destroy the William along with himself. If Merlin unfortunately fell into the sea, unable to swim, he would practically be digging his own grave. At this moment Merlin felt like a spent arrow, yet he had not given up, for someone important was waiting for his return. “Mer…Merlin‑sir…” Captain Dennis watched Merlin emerge, his eyes unconsciously flashing a hint of hope. Merlin wearily walked to the front of the deck, staring straight at the tentacle bearing the terrifying waves as it approached; while everyone else’s legs turned to jelly, only this constantly mocked fellow remained standing. The North Sea Giant Demon never revealed its true form; with just its tentacles it could annihilate everything, mocking humanity, disdainful of placing anything in its sight. The biting wind and spray lashed the William’s deck like knives cutting Merlin’s face— Is this… the legendary North Sea Giant Demon? The Gun Hero O’Brien vanished after his campaign against it. If I recall correctly, this monster guards the Gods’ relics. Yet on the island just now, aside from the deformed monster, there was nothing at all!? Why would this sea‑borne nightmare suddenly appear here… But speaking of which, this octopus‑like body seems even larger than that stinky younger brother Leviathan? “Merlin‑sir! What are you doing!?” Morrison shouted in astonishment. “You’re just a black‑iron adventurer; you can’t change anything! Give up!” Adams thought everyone was going to die, so what’s the point of showing off? Merlin smirked, turned his head, and said meaningfully, “Huh, can you all shut up? You’re really noisy…” “Eh!
