title: Chapter 44 — Serf Who Stood Up (Extra Update)
content:
Chapter 44 — Serf Who Stood Up (Extra Update)

Volume 20 · Chapter 44

"Of course, I'm Merlin. You actually didn't recognize me?"

Little Merlin was held high in the air by Alice, his expression meaningful and somewhat dissatisfied that Alice hadn't recognized him at first glance.

It's not like he had just a little baby fat? The difference between this and his adult self was huge? That didn't make sense~

The scene became a bit awkward. Alice had never imagined that Merlin would one day become so small that she could easily lift him.

Oh my god! What exactly happened?

How could the tall and imposing Merlin suddenly become a little kid?!

What should I do? How can we get married now? Won't I be mistaken for a pedophile?!

But... he looked pretty cute, with his round, plump face...

Alice stared at little Merlin. While she wasn't satisfied with his current appearance, Merlin had always been tall and handsome. Suddenly becoming a brat was really hard to adjust to.

Looking at young Merlin, Alice found him quite adorable and couldn't help but feel an urge to pinch his little cheeks.

"Why... why did you become like this? What did you do?"

"This is a long story..." Little Merlin struggled, his face darkening. "Can you put me down first? You're holding me... to be honest, it's very embarrassing. I'm the Great Demon Lord, please show me some respect, thank you."

"...Okay..." Alice obediently put Merlin down. Her inner self was restless. Even though he had become a little kid, his attitude was just as arrogant as before. But he looked like he had no fighting ability now. Did that mean... I could take this opportunity to kick his butt wildly and vent all the anger I've been holding in?

"I've encountered a lot of things along the way..."

Little Merlin briefly recounted the events of his journey: Cain's conspiracy, entering the mysterious sea alone, killing the King of Chaos Medusa, encountering the北海 giant kraken Kraken...

He told Alice almost all the important things, as Merlin trusted her and didn't need to hide much.

However, Merlin didn't mention his own situation, like nearly dying on the road or losing an arm, because he thought these weren't big problems and would only lead to Alice's endless questioning.

Alice's eyes flickered, nodding repeatedly in response. She found Merlin's solo journey incredibly unbelievable, almost like an epic, making her heart race with tension.

"Anyway, that's how it is. I drank too much time potion, so I became like this. But it's not a big deal. That old hag Circe said she could make an antidote. I can still return to normal. This state is only temporary. You don't think I became a kid so you can ride me, right? Yeah, that's right! That's how it is~" Little Merlin sat cross-legged on the bed, rubbing his chin like a little adult, not forgetting to emphasize that he could recover, fearing Alice might think he was easy to bully.

Oh~ So many things happened... Alice looked down, saying thoughtfully, feeling that during her coma, Merlin had been very busy.

"Of course! I was exhausted to death." Little Merlin stood up on the bed, hands on his hips. "You should thank me for waking up. Give me a massage, rub my shoulders, stuff like that~"

"No way, I'm not your servant. Don't try that on me..." Alice pouted, completely unimpressed.

..... Little Merlin's tongue flicked out in disgust, thinking to himself that after all he had done, wasn't it reasonable to enjoy a bit of premium treatment?

"Um... Alice poked little Merlin, sticking her finger in his face, "Can you really recover? It looks really difficult..."

"Of course I can. Our injuries were all treated by that old hag Circe, so there's definitely no problem." Little Merlin, annoyed by Alice's poking, opened her hand and said with great arrogance, "Don't touch my face! I'm the first of the seven demon kings, treating me like a little kid is a complete humiliation!"

"Ah...?" Alice said expressionlessly, her tone indifferent. "What first of the seven demon kings? You're still so arrogant even as a little kid?"

"What's the problem? You won't think you can take advantage of me now, will you? Dream on!" Little Merlin said with his head held high.

Alice's vein on her forehead twitched. She thought, Well then, it's not my fault anymore. We'll have to settle this later.

So Alice slowly stood up and kicked little Merlin's butt with a "plopp," looking down at him with a dark face.

"Hey?! Little Merlin turned to look at Alice, his face full of shock. "What are you doing?! Are you rebelling?!"

"For always bullying me! For always looking down on me! For always using your power to oppress me! Go die, go die, go die... hahaha!"

Dada dada dada, Alice kicked little Merlin's butt wildly, venting her long-suppressed anger.

As a result, Alice's mood became increasingly pleasant, feeling like a freed serf singing a song of triumph, emitting a queen-like laugh.

"Hey! Alice... you're crazy, daring to treat me like this?!" Little Merlin was stunned, thinking to himself that it was truly a case of a tiger falling into a flatland being bullied by a dog!

"Ah? You're not much better yourself. Tell me how many times you've bullied me by relying on the fact that I couldn't fight you?" Alice felt extremely pleased.

"Those don't count!" Little Merlin struggled.

Suddenly, the door to the room was pushed open, and Circe entered with her apprentice Susan. "I said inside was so noisy, it's because you woke up, right?"

"Hmm?" Alice looked up, seeing the two strangers in front of her. She thought these two must be the alchemists Merlin mentioned? The purple-gold adventurer Circe and her apprentice?

Merlin took this opportunity to sneak away, running outside. "Alice, you crazy woman, wait, when I recover, I'll definitely teach you a lesson!"

"You?!" Alice was about to retort when she saw Merlin sneak away.

"Your two's relationship is really good, isn't it?" Circe said meaningfully.

"..." Alice blushed and denied it, saying it wasn't good, but her heart was secretly happy.

Circe chuckled dryly, sitting by the bedside. "How is your body? Any other discomfort?"

"No, I feel fine, and my strength has somehow become much stronger..." Alice muttered.

Circe's expression stiffened, her eyebrows twitching. She thought, what was with that casual tone? Was he boasting about leveling up while lying down? You drank a whole pool of my potential-boosting potions! Not bad for Clovidia's student, a bit problematic in personality~

"Thank you for your help. If it weren't for you, Alice and Merlin might have had serious problems." Alice sincerely thanked her.

"No need to be so polite," Circe said. "I saved you for a reason. How is your teacher Clovidia?"

Alice was very surprised. "You... know my teacher?"

"Didn't she tell you about me?" Circe was also surprised.

Alice shook her head helplessly. Her teacher had always been on the snowy mountain and had never mentioned the name "Circe." Instead, she had often cursed her dead enemy for stealing men back then, but never mentioned the name, just calling her a "bitch."

"Oh, if she didn't say it, it's fine. We can say we were... acquaintances." Circe smiled falsely, gritting her teeth. She thought,

Clovidia this country girl, she never mentioned me to her students at all?

She didn't care about me at all. It seems that compared to coldness, Clovidia is still better. I lost, I lost...

title: Chapter 45 — Payment
content:
Chapter 45 — Payment

Volume 20 · Chapter 45

"Friend?" Alice blinked, having never heard that her teacher had any friends; the teacher had always been alone.
"Not that we're close, but we've seen each other many times, so we're not completely strangers," Chris said, masking her embarrassment.

"Oh... Alice nodded dazedly, barely believing Chris, and replied, 'My teacher has been training nonstop on the Alps' great snow mountain; she never leaves easily. I guess she's immersed in her training every day and rarely asks about outside affairs.'"

"Indeed, she's just like her..." Chris nodded, thinking, 'Is this country girl really that hardworking? Could her strength have already advanced to a terrifying level?'

Alice sized up Chris and asked tentatively, "Senior, you seem quite concerned about my teacher. Could it be that you're close?"

"Who would care about that... *cough cough*" Chris coughed twice to hide her embarrassment, then continued, "Who would care? I'm just curious. Is she still alone? Hasn't she found another half of her life?"

"My teacher would never look for a man; she never interacts with anyone normally." Alice chuckled, recalling her teacher, that old maid with a weird temperament who never actively approached strangers. Moreover, the snowy mountain is a bitterly cold place, rarely visited, and daily necessities are bought from passing caravans.

"Oh~, turns out it's still that miserable, hah..." Chris couldn't help laughing out loud upon hearing that her nemesis Claudia was still an old maid, her life apparently just as miserable, instantly making her feel much better—compared to Claudia, she was obviously much better off.

"I feel... you and my teacher..." Alice furrowed her brows.

"No, no, it's a misunderstanding. I have no grudge against your teacher. By the way, why is she still alone?" Chris asked curiously.

"Because my teacher... apparently suffered a setback when she was young, so she doesn't really trust others. Every day she curses some 'bitch,' saying things like 'they dug a hole in my wall'..." Alice recalled.

"Hehehe~" Chris's smile grew wider; she thought to herself, 'Exactly, that bitch is definitely me. I didn't expect Claudia still holds a grudge against me.' She felt relieved.

Alice watched Chris, who looked pleased in body and mind, growing more suspicious whether the two had some grudge. However, since the other was willing to help her, she probably wasn't a bad person.

"You... seem quite familiar with my teacher. Did you know each other long ago?"

"Probably. We once served together as knights in the Spanish Royal Guard; we could be considered former colleagues," Chris said with a meaningful tone.

"Eh? The Spanish Royal Guard?" Alice showed a doubtful expression, thinking her teacher had never mentioned it, assuming she'd always lived on the snowy mountain; she hadn't expected her teacher to have once been a knight guarding the Spanish kingdom.

"That's all from long ago; better not mention it. However, Claudia seems never to have told you about the past, right?" Chris said with a smile.

"Yes, my teacher... seems not to like talking about her past affairs." Alice nodded, recalling her teacher; indeed, she had never spoken of her past, leading Alice to think her teacher had lived on the snowy mountain since childhood.

"She definitely doesn't want to recall those embarrassing things..."

Chris nodded understandingly, thinking that Claudia still keeps cursing her as a "bitch" to this day, surely unwilling to recall those wretched years.

Seeing that her nemesis wasn't doing so well, the old lady's mood instantly brightened; she slowly rose and advised Alice.

"I won't disturb you; rest well for a few days. Although you're out of danger, you still need to pay close attention to your health."

"Thank you for your concern," Alice said, lowering her head slightly to express her gratitude.

"But I still have one thing I'd like to ask; I hope you don't mind," Chris said, shifting the topic.

Alice froze, then said, "Eh? Please, it's fine."

"Are you and Merlin really husband and wife?" Chris asked abruptly. These days she's been doubtful; although the adventurer's certificate lists them as a married couple, their behavior hardly resembles a true marriage—more like two people who are just familiar with each other, disliking sleeping together, constantly bickering, and lacking any marital intimacy.

"Well..." Alice's face turned red as she lowered her head, tugging at the corner of the blanket, speaking somewhat hesitantly, "We're actually just a fake couple. The information on the adventurer's certificate is a mix-up caused by our guild leader; it's not easy to amend, so it's been left as is."

"Exactly as I thought. I said you two don't look like a married couple at all." Chris nodded in understanding. "If it's a fake marriage due to a misunderstanding, then there's nothing strange about it."

"Not really married?!" Susan, who had been watching nearby, jumped upon hearing Alice admit the fact. "If you're not truly married, why is Mr. Merlin pushing himself so hard? Adventurers' mindset is self-centered; even as companions, they wouldn't go to such lengths!"

"Huh? ... What do you mean?" Alice asked, turning her head in surprise.

"...... Susan was startled by Alice's reaction and stammered, 'Mr. Merlin carried you here; his body is already terrible from poisoning, and he could die at any moment. Moreover, he had to venture into the inescapable mysterious sea to gather medicine ingredients for you, returning covered in wounds, his arm even broken. My master and I all thought he should have died on the road by now. As for his current state? That's from him testing medicines on you, so... I think you...'"

Chris reached out to cover Susan's mouth, sternly saying, "What nonsense are you spouting? You're just too talkative."

"???" Susan raised her brows, not understanding why she wasn't allowed to speak.

Alice's mind went blank, her expression shifting, her face blank as she clenched the blanket with both hands, wrinkling it.

Is it really true?

During the time I was unconscious, did Merlin do all this for me?

He usually acts all carefree, not caring about anything...

Honestly, why didn't he tell me earlier, saying it so lightly? Turns out this period was actually dangerous.

My attitude toward Merlin just now was kinda awful; I...

...am I feeling ashamed?

Outside, little Merlin lay against the fence, picking up small stones to throw at the piglets Chris was raising.

"Nom nom nom! All you know is to eat! Once you're full, you get eaten! Worthless!"

Since Alice can now bully Merlin, he's in a terrible mood and can only vent his anger on this litter of piglets.

Alice, you jerk, actually taking revenge on me when I couldn't fight back—just wait, I'll remember this grudge!

Little Merlin fumed, continuously throwing stones at the piglets to keep them from eating.

Suddenly hearing Alice's expression, little Merlin was so frightened his whole body shook violently, leaning against the fence and trembling.

"...What are you trying to do?! I'm the proud Demon Lord! Even if I'm now a child, you can't provoke me—don't come over!"

Seeing little Merlin's reaction, Alice couldn't help but lower her head in embarrassment, feeling somewhat awkward.

At that moment she was wearing a loose long dress, barefoot, walking out of the pumpkin hut, wanting to say something.

Alice clasped her hands behind her back; her silver hair trembled as she swayed in a dance, biting her lip, blushing as she whispered softly.

".Lin...."

"That I"

title: Chapter 46 — Angela (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 46 — Angela (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 20 · Chapter 46

"...."

Little Merlin was terrified, convinced Alice was going to take advantage of the situation to bully him. He grabbed the pig-feeding ladle beside him and brandished it, shouting, "Don’t come any closer! I’m warning you! Don’t think I can’t fight back just because I’m weak right now—I’m just… a gentleman who doesn’t hit women! Don’t push your luck!"

"...."

Alice’s expression turned awkward. She hadn’t expected Merlin to be so guarded. It seemed she *had* gone too far earlier.

"Hmph! Scared now, huh? It’s not too late to admit you’re wrong!" Little Merlin tucked the ladle into his waist like a sword, striking a drawing-cut pose—though in reality, he couldn’t even use Drawing Slash right now. He just didn’t want to be bullied by Alice.

Alice hesitated, then slowly approached Merlin. She crouched down in front of him so she wouldn’t have to look down at him.

"Eek!" Little Merlin covered his face in terror. "Don’t come closer!"

Still crouching, Alice pulled little Merlin into her arms, gently stroking his back to ease his hostility.

"Mmm?!" Little Merlin, held tightly by Alice, felt his face inexplicably flush red. His heart raced with confusion. *What is this woman up to?* Wasn’t she supposed to take this chance to bully him mercilessly? What was she doing?

"Merlin, thank you for everything you’ve done for me these past days. It’s been a lot." Alice held his small body, a blush rising to her cheeks as she whispered, "You’ve worked hard."

....

Little Merlin’s eyes widened. His tense body gradually relaxed, and the only weapon he had—the pig-feeding ladle—nearly slipped from his grip.

His expression softened. He lowered his head, resting his chin on Alice’s shoulder, his emotions growing complicated...

These past days *had* been exhausting for Merlin, both physically and mentally. But hearing those words of acknowledgment from Alice—"You’ve worked hard"—made it all feel worth it.

Little Merlin stayed silent. Why *had* he gone all out for Alice, the person who bickered with him every day? In the end, it was because he didn’t want her to leave him.

"I always thought you were someone who didn’t care about anything. I never expected... you’d care so much about me, or do so much for me." Alice averted her gaze, pretending to mutter casually, "I’m really happy. From the bottom of my heart."

"Ah....... Oh....." Little Merlin felt a little embarrassed.

Neither of them were good at sweet talk. Their interactions were clumsy, and the atmosphere was subtly awkward.

But then Alice suddenly realized the perfect opportunity. Maybe she could try expressing her feelings.

"Uh... Merlin... I, uh... actually like you... a little..."

Alice’s face flushed crimson in an instant. A flicker of panic shot through her dark eyes, and her heart began to race.

Even if her words were vague, for Alice, this was already a huge step forward.

*—I said it... I actually said it!* Her mind was in chaos. *What does Merlin think? Is he happy? Angry? Or does he not care at all?*

Alice was so nervous she couldn’t let go of little Merlin, afraid he’d see how flustered she was.

"Hmm???"

Little Merlin’s eyes widened in disbelief. His heart skipped a beat. *This can’t be real...*

*Alice... likes me? A little?* Since when? She’d been arguing with him every day, acting like she couldn’t stand the sight of him. This didn’t make sense.

He had to stay calm. After all, he was over two hundred years old. He could see through this kind of childish trick meant to embarrass him.

Little Merlin suppressed his racing emotions and put on a composed, world-weary front. "Don’t be ridiculous. I didn’t do much. Saving you was just saving myself—I wanted to live, too. I just took you along for the ride, that’s all~"

"Eh?"

Alice froze. *Wasn’t it obvious enough?* Did he really not take her seriously? Was he treating her confession like a joke?

And what did he mean by "just took you along"? Was there really no other feeling behind it?

Alice felt a surge of frustration, but seeing Merlin’s haughty attitude, she refused to back down. She wouldn’t lower herself either.

"....It’s not like there’s any other meaning. I like you... just as a friend. You didn’t misunderstand, did you? Heh..."

"Oh? Did I misunderstand?" Little Merlin scratched his head, secretly relieved. *So that’s how it is. Good thing I didn’t take it seriously. Otherwise, this stinking woman would’ve laughed at me to death. Dodged a bullet there.* "Then... can you let go of me? It’s uncomfortable. Even if I look like a kid now, I don’t like being treated like one..."

"...." Alice released little Merlin, her eyes lingering with reluctance. *I actually said I liked him... so why is Merlin so indifferent?* Was the problem with *her*?

Little Merlin, now free, stretched his shoulders with a satisfied groan. Alice had been holding him too tightly.

*Could it be that now that I’m a cute little boy, I can’t contain my primal, overwhelming power?* The thought sent a chill down his spine. *Does Alice have such a strong maternal aura that she can’t control herself around children?*

"Cough, cough. Actually, I *have* been exhausted these past days. But it’s fine. You don’t need to feel guilty. What happened with Cain—it’s my responsibility, too. If I’d noticed his true nature sooner, we wouldn’t have ended up in such danger."

"It’s not like that..." Alice lowered her head, looking apologetic. "I’m the one who should take responsibility. If I hadn’t taken pity on that child and tried to take him in, you wouldn’t have gone through so much danger. It’s my fault. I need to be more careful in the future."

Little Merlin hopped onto a stool, swinging the pig-feeding ladle in circles as he spoke carelessly, "There’s no need for self-blame. The future is long. We should look ahead. Isn’t everything fine now? We’re both alive. Sure, turning into a kid sucks, but it’s only temporary. I’ll get back to normal eventually. Then I’ll be a real man again!"

"Heh..." Alice found Merlin’s behavior amusing. Here he was, a little kid, spouting such over-the-top, middle-school-level lines. He was like a genuine bratty child.

"What’s so funny? I’m serious..." Little Merlin emphasized sternly, then suddenly remembered something. He patted his chest. "Oh right, I have something to give you..."

"What is it?" Alice crouched down to talk to little Merlin, looking patient.

"This!" Little Merlin pulled out the treasure he’d obtained from the Mysterious Seas—a ring called "Anjel" (Angel). "Uh... Alice, I..."

"...Oh my God... No way..."

Alice’s eyes locked onto the ring glowing with sacred light in little Merlin’s hand. She clapped a hand over her mouth, afraid she might scream.

The scene was surreal: little Merlin, in his childish form, held the ring high and offered it to Alice.

Alice had seen this exact scenario play out in stories countless times. She never thought it would happen to *her* one day.

*Merlin...*

*Is this... a proposal?*

(ﾟωﾟ;

title: Chapter 47 — Frequency Hop (Update at Midnight)
content:
Chapter 47 — Frequency Hop (Update at Midnight)

Volume 20 · Chapter 47

"Take it, Alice. I think this suits you better." Little Merlin said this with a straight face, believing Alice was more likely to encounter danger than he was. With the angel ring "Anjel," it would surely play a crucial role.

"V-Very... suitable for me?" Alice's cheeks flushed a light pink, as if she were dreaming. He had ignored all her hints before, so why was he suddenly presenting a ring like a proposal? Was this meant to be a surprise?

Their thoughts were on completely different wavelengths, yet they had managed to get along for so long—it was nothing short of a miracle.

Alice lowered her head, stammering as she spoke, wondering if Merlin was hinting at something. After all, this was the first time he had seriously given her a gift. It was a day worth remembering.

As for the Frost Dragon’s legacy crystal? He had only given it to her because he didn’t like her holding him back, right? His attitude had been terrible then.

So, this radiant ring in her hand... did that mean she was Merlin’s fiancée?

What should she do? This was so sudden, she had no idea what to say...

A proposal was such a formal occasion. She needed to take it seriously and not say the wrong thing.

Alice’s mind raced, her heart pounding so hard it felt like it might leap out of her chest.

"I... I wasn’t mentally prepared, Merlin. This is... too sudden..."

"Huh???" Little Merlin’s mind was filled with question marks. He had just meant to give her a piece of equipment—why was Alice reacting so strangely?

"I-I don’t know what to say right now either..."

Alice, embarrassed, clutched the ring tightly, her heart racing. Since she wasn’t good with words, she decided to respond with actions instead.

Still crouching, she closed her eyes, puckered her lips, and slowly leaned in, intending to answer Merlin’s "proposal" with a kiss.

No words were needed. This intimate act proved she would accept Merlin’s proposal without hesitation.

Alice inched closer, her whole body leaning toward him, about to press her lips to his...

"Eek?!" Little Merlin was startled. What was this stinking woman doing?! He had never noticed before—was she really this desperate?!

Alice hesitated internally. Merlin was currently defenseless—was it too sneaky of her to take advantage of him like this? It almost felt like she was exploiting his vulnerability.

But after a moment’s thought, she threw caution to the wind and kissed him anyway—only to be met with a cold, hard surface. It wasn’t soft lips at all. Instead, she tasted something foul, like pig manure. *Ugh...*

Alice’s mind jolted awake. She opened her eyes and, to her horror, realized she had kissed the pig-feeding ladle in Merlin’s hand!

"Uuuuugh!!!"

Alice’s eyes widened in shock, her mind going blank. A wave of nausea rolled through her stomach, instantly shattering the romantic atmosphere.

"Tsk tsk tsk~" Little Merlin clicked his tongue, pressing the ladle against Alice’s face to keep her at bay. "Don’t try such cheap tricks. Do you think I’m stupid enough not to see through your little schemes? You were trying to take advantage of me, weren’t you? How dare you! Back off!"

Hearing Merlin’s self-righteous words, Alice rolled her eyes so hard she nearly saw stars. A surge of unnamed rage welled up inside her. She turned her head and started dry-heaving, utterly disgusted by the taste of pig manure—especially since she had just kissed it.

"Ptooey! ...Ptooey! ...Ptooey!"

"Trying to outsmart me? You’re still far from it~" Little Merlin said smugly.

Alice was furious at Merlin’s complete lack of romantic sense. She abruptly spun around, snatched the ladle from his hand, and her face darkened instantly.

"...What are you doing?" Merlin warily took a step back, sensing the icy aura radiating from Alice. "Are you so frustrated that your IQ’s been suppressed that you’re resorting to brute force?"

"Merlin! Just die already!" Alice raised the ladle and, in a fit of rage, brought it down hard on Merlin’s head with a *thunk*, like the sound of a wooden fish being struck.

"Oof!" Merlin clutched his head, seeing stars as he collapsed to the ground, barely conscious. "A-Alice..."

Alice dropped the ladle, turned on her heel, and marched toward the pumpkin house, furiously wiping her mouth. In her mind, she cursed Merlin the idiot. *I’ll never fall for his tricks again! Damn it!*

Inside the pumpkin house, Circe and Susan, master and apprentice, had been pressed against the window the whole time, spying on the scene outside. When they saw the two part on such bad terms—

"That Alice... she’s so violent..." Susan’s mouth formed a perfect "O," too stunned to close it.

"Children shouldn’t watch things like this." Circe covered Susan’s eyes, wondering to herself why the two of them, who were already so close, hadn’t just gotten married yet.

Evening fell, and a faint candlelight flickered inside the pumpkin house.

Alice lay on the sickbed, staring at the ring on her finger, not just unhappy but disappointed.

"So it was just equipment after all? He should’ve said so earlier. He made me misunderstand everything."

"Wasn’t I clear enough? Honestly, if you’re unhappy, just hit me. I’m just a kid, my body’s weak—I can’t take your brute strength. Be careful..." Little Merlin winced as the throbbing lump on his head ached. He absentmindedly sorted through his belongings. After all, once Alice recovered, they’d be leaving White Dew Forest soon.

"Hah! Now you’re acting like a kid again? You weren’t saying that when you were being all high and mighty earlier..." Alice huffed, puffing out her cheeks in protest.

"I don’t want to argue with you right now. I was perfectly clear. What was *that* about, suddenly coming at me?" Little Merlin shot Alice a sidelong glance and muttered, "Puckering your lips like that—I should’ve shoved the pig ladle into your mouth."

"You—?! ..." Alice clapped a hand over her mouth, the memory alone still making her feel sick.

"That ring belongs to the Holy Spirits. It has the power to bring the wearer back to life. Don’t take it off carelessly—next time you’re in a situation like today, it could save your life." Merlin said seriously.

"Holy Spirits?" Alice examined the ring on her finger, sensing its dense divine energy. It was even automatically gathering magic and aura from the air. Clearly, if she trained while wearing this, her progress would be twice as fast!

"Yeah, Holy Spirits. You could call them angels, too. A long time ago, they fought against our demon race. Both sides were devastated. I have no idea how this thing ended up in the Mystic Sea... It’s pretty strange, if you think about it." Merlin commented.

Alice rubbed the ring, feeling its value. Not only would it aid her cultivation, but it could also revive her on the spot. It felt almost wasteful for her to use it. "Something this precious... why didn’t you keep it for yourself?"

Merlin froze, silent for a moment before saying, "You need it more than I do. I don’t want you to go through something like today again. Your life is more important than anything... If you weren’t around, I’d probably just get bored."

Alice’s pretty face flushed pink against her will. She lowered her head, tangled in her thoughts.

*What is he even talking about? This guy always says the weirdest things...*

*...Is he actually concerned about me?*

*Ugh, what does he even mean by that?*

title: Chapter 48 — Leaving White Dew Forest (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 48 — Leaving White Dew Forest (Bonus)

Volume 20 · Chapter 48

"Besides, the sacred aura on it makes me sick. I won’t wear that thing." Little Merlin said seriously.

Alice examined the angelic ring, wondering—was the sacred aura really that unpleasant? Merlin had no problem entering churches, after all.

"Actually, I gained quite a lot from this trip, and then there’s this..." Merlin waved an old, worn parchment in his hand.

"What’s that?" Alice took it and studied it carefully. It was a nautical chart, though clearly incomplete—no one could tell what it was supposed to record.

"I’m not entirely sure either. I can’t read the text on it, but since it was kept in a secret chamber, it must be a treasure map. When we get back, we can ask Miss da Vinci—she might have some clues." Little Merlin recalled his colleague from Lexham; whenever they encountered an unsolvable problem, da Vinci always managed to uncover a lead or two.

Alice said nothing, carefully examining the sea chart. She could see the lands of France and Britain—it seemed to be a map of the world’s oceans, but what did that red line mark? If they could find the other half, it might reveal something useful.

"But the greatest gain from this trip is this!" Little Merlin pulled out the head of the King of Chaos, unwrapping the black cloth and turning his back to Alice as he showed it to her.

"Ugh!" Alice set down the half-map, her attention drawn to the severed head in Merlin’s hands. The snakelike hair writhed menacingly, hissing as it swayed. "...What *is* that? What kind of bizarre thing have you gotten yourself into now?"

"This is the head of the King of Chaos—the leader of that island. Its eyes are terrifying. I nearly got myself killed by them. If you meet its gaze, you’ll be petrified in no time." Little Merlin said earnestly, then stuffed Medusa’s head into a bag and tied it shut with a dead knot. "My current situation is a bit awkward. If I run into trouble, I’ll have to rely on this."

Alice stared at the bag in Merlin’s hands. If it had nearly done him in, it must be extremely dangerous. Turning people to stone just by looking at them—was that even possible? It sounded like... something out of folklore, like a cursed evil eye.

"These are my gains from this trip. I’m pretty satisfied. I’ve earned a good sum of money too. That ring of yours is high-quality—probably a quasi-divine artifact." Little Merlin stood up and stretched.

"A quasi-divine artifact?!" Alice’s eyes widened in disbelief. The ring’s function was impressive, but she never expected it to be *that* rare. "I thought it was just... a fancy-looking ring. I didn’t realize it was something so extraordinary..."

"These are worn by the Holy Spirits. They can’t be low-tier. Our demon race’s ancient texts say they were forged by Uriel herself, one of the Seven Great Archangels. The Holy Spirits wear these resurrection rings, and they’ve caused us demons no end of trouble." Little Merlin explained.

Alice knew some stories of the Holy Church. Uriel was one of the seven eminent Holy Spirits created by the Goddess of Light, the keeper of the Eternal Flame, who punished sinners and heretics. She never imagined she’d one day obtain such a thing.

Driven by curiosity, Alice sent a wisp of her will into the ring, wanting to investigate what made this "Angel" ring so special.

Suddenly, her consciousness was transported to another space—completely empty, with nothing inside. The ring actually contained its own independent space?!

Alice opened her eyes, amazed. She turned to Merlin and said, "Merlin, this ring has an independent space inside! It seems like I can store things in it!"

"Huh? Really?" Merlin looked over in surprise. An independent space meant it could be used for storage. Such rare items were nearly impossible to obtain—even royal families didn’t necessarily possess one. It just went to show how uncommon equipment with independent spaces was!

Alice decided to demonstrate. She waved the half-map in her hand, then channeled her will into the spatial ring—*whoosh*, and it vanished.

When she reversed the flow of her will, *whoosh*, the half-map reappeared in her hand.

"See? The independent space inside can hold things!"

"I see, so it works like that. We won’t have to carry so many gifts on our backs anymore." Little Merlin nodded thoughtfully, growing even more convinced of the accuracy of the demon race’s ancient records. Creating an independent space within equipment—this had to be a power unique to the Supreme Holy Spirits! No wonder it was a quasi-divine artifact. Not only did it have resurrection and cultivation-assisting abilities, but it also possessed this rare storage function!

"What an amazing item. This is the first time I’ve ever seen something so incredible—it can actually hold things inside?" Alice rubbed the angelic ring, growing more and more fond of it.

Little Merlin watched Alice’s delighted expression and smiled along, but his mood suddenly turned strange.

Because he had been recalling a recent string of events—all of them hinting at Alice’s extraordinary nature, even suggesting she might be connected to the Heavenly Faction.

Cain’s hand-painted oil painting, the assassination of Queen Josefine of Spain—these incidents all seemed tied to the Holy Church, the shadow of the demon race’s greatest enemy, faintly lingering behind Alice.

Alice noticed Merlin’s gaze and asked, puzzled, "What’s wrong, Merlin? Why are you staring at me like that?"

"...Nothing." Merlin hesitated, then forced an awkward smile. "..."

I shouldn’t doubt Alice. Even if this silly woman has some inexplicable connection to the Holy Church...

If Alice *is* some kind of puppet controlled by a powerful deity, then I’ll cut those strings too...

A few days later, the two packed their bags. With all dangers resolved, it was time to leave White Dew Forest.

Merlin and Alice had completed their mission and should return to Lexham. Earl Austin would reward them handsomely for their efforts.

Since they’d discovered the angelic ring’s spatial storage function, Merlin handed all their belongings to Alice for safekeeping. Traveling light made the journey far easier.

"Are you leaving already? Won’t you stay a few more days?" Circe asked with a grin.

"Pfft, last night you couldn’t wait to kick them out, complaining they were freeloading. What a hypocrite~" Susan muttered under her breath, mocking her own master’s false politeness.

Circe reached out and flicked Susan’s forehead, silencing her.

"Ow!" Susan rubbed her head, pouting, not daring to badmouth her master again.

"We’re no longer in danger, so of course we’re leaving. Thank you for taking care of us these past days." Alice gave a slight bow to Circe. After all, she *was* their lifesaving benefactor.

"No need to be so formal. If you get the chance, give my regards to your teacher." Circe’s tone was meaningful.

Alice hesitated—she had no intention of returning to the Great Snow Mountain. So she changed the subject, pulling a crystal card worth 500,000 gold coins from her embrace. "This is a small token of our gratitude. Please accept it, Senior."

The two of them had unexpectedly gained a considerable sum on this trip. They’d embezzled a crystal card from Countess Camilla and extorted another from President Humphrey, totaling a million gold coins—a truly impressive haul.

Since Circe had helped them resolve their crisis, Alice naturally wouldn’t accept such a favor for free. She took half of their earnings and offered it to Circe.

Though Circe was a powerful Purple Gold-ranked adventurer, she still needed money to live, so she wouldn’t refuse such a kind gesture.

"How could I accept this? I don’t need it at all, hahaha..." Circe laughed, but her hands moved faster than her words. She swiftly snatched the crystal card from Alice’s hands and, with a teasing motion, tucked it into the valley between her ample breasts.

Alice had already consumed a pool’s worth of Circe’s special potential-awakening potions, so this crystal card was just compensation for the loss.

Alice’s expression turned awkward as she stared at the crystal card nestled between Circe’s breasts, a hint of envy in her eyes.

"Tsk tsk tsk~" Little Merlin shook his head and muttered, "That’s a move you’ll never be able to pull off~"

"Shut up." Alice grumbled under her breath, feeling a little defeated.

Huh? Was that really so impressive?

If I push hard enough, I can probably fit a card in there too=

title: Chapter 49 — Guest from Afar
content:
Chapter 49 — Guest from Afar

Volume 20 · Chapter 49

Hey! Old lady, where's the antidote you promised? Did you make it or not? Little Merlin jumped up, he was about to leave, couldn't even see a trace of the antidote, can't keep going like this.
During this time, Seysi wasn't idle either; she really thought a lot and helped Merlin create an antidote to restore adulthood.
However, Seysi lacks experience with time potions, so this antidote is merely an experimental attempt, seemingly without any guarantee.
"I certainly haven't forgotten about you." Seysi took out a string of potion bottles from behind her, colorful, about a dozen or so,
"Here, these are the antidotes that can restore you...."
Little Merlin eagerly took them, as if he'd found treasure, "If I just drink them, I can immediately return to adulthood, right?"
"These potions need to be taken once every three days; they won't instantly restore you, since you drank a large amount of time potion causing you to regress too much. To regain your adult form, you still need to be extra careful." Seysi emphasized, advising Merlin not to rush, otherwise new problems could easily arise.
"Tsk! One bottle every three days? So it's not an instant recovery? I've been looking forward to this for nothing..." Little Merlin muttered dissatisfiedly, looking at the dozen bottles, feeling very disappointed, guessing that finishing them all would take about a month.
"You could try gulping them all down at once, if you're not afraid of dying."
Seysi gave a harmless smile.
"Ugh... never mind." Little Merlin thought about his current state, caused by drinking too much medicine; he wouldn't make the same mistake again, so he'd better obey Seysi honestly. "If I follow your instructions and honestly finish these potions, I'll definitely be able to change back, right?"
Seysi smiled without speaking, thinking theoretically these potions could neutralize the effects of the time potion, but that's only theory; as for whether it'll succeed, how would I know? Hehe~
Little Merlin looked at Seysi's meaningful smile, a chill ran down his spine, he carefully stored the potions, "I'll trust you this once, old lady; if it doesn't work, I'll surely drag you down with me."
"Don't worry, in potion-making I'm still quite confident." Seysi waved her hand, comforting him verbally, but inside she thought, if he can't regain adulthood, what deterrent power does he have?
Little Merlin remained silent, inwardly still very doubtful of Seysi; this old lady never takes things seriously, and I don't know if what she says is true.
"Oh right, I still have something I need your help with." Seysi took out another bottle of pitch-black potion, looking quite familiar, "Since you're heading back to Britain, please deliver this time potion to the head of the London Guild, Gregory. I heard he suffered a heavy blow from some strong individual and remains unconscious; I've received a commission from their guild to wake Gregory, so you should deliver this time potion."
Little Merlin took the time potion Seysi handed over, recalling that purple-gold adventurer he'd blown up with a fist—
Tsk tsk tsk,
Has that old geezer not woken up yet? Did I go too far?
"Mr. Gregory... Alice still remembers that this old guild master once saved her, but unfortunately she was educated by the great swordsman Elgin, [if it weren't for being taken advantage of, it wouldn't have turned out like this..."
"Old sir? Haha..." Seysi suddenly let out a light chuckle, teasing, "Although the number of purple-gold adventurers is very scarce, Gregory here is also quite young among us, because he's basically an ageless monster...."
"An ageless monster? No way?" Alice recalled carefully, his white hair, stooped back, withered hands—all clearly that of an old man.
"Don't be fooled by him; his usual self and his serious self are completely different people." Seysi gave a meaningful glance, then brushed it off, "Alright, it's getting late, you should head out. How's the work going?"
"Then, Seysi before... Alice slightly bowed, formally bidding farewell, "Well then, we'll be taking our leave."
After Merlin and Alice left, Susan finally couldn't help but ask— "Master, the potions you gave Mr. Merlin are clearly unfinished products, right?"
"This.... Seysi's eyes darted embarrassedly, she whispered, "Although they're unfinished, they still have some effect; if luck is good, maybe they can restore him."
"Your attitude is quite irresponsible.... Susan's expression complex, "What if Mr. Merlin has bad luck?"
"Then just keep him as a child, or wait for him to grow up slowly..." Seysi said with a giggle, not taking this matter to heart at all.
"...This is so pitiful!" Susan was quite startled.
"You should know, since I started creating the time potion, I never thought about an antidote; expecting me to find a perfect solution in just a few days is impossible—I'm not an omnipotent god." Seysi felt she'd done her best; now it's up to Merlin's fate—if things go well, he'll recover soon.
"Mr. Merlin will definitely come back, right? He surely won't just let it go." Susan said worriedly.
"Don't worry about these useless things; you should figure out how to train properly—you're already this old and still just a high-level mage, you've made me lose face." Seysi tapped Susan's head with her wand, saying bitterly, "I'll give you six months; you must reach the Saint tier, or else see how I deal with you."
"Wuwuwu! Master, did you take the wrong medicine? Before you didn't care, but now you seem to have become strict..." Susan buried her head and cried, feeling she'll suffer endless torment.
After seeing Alice, Seysi indeed received quite a stimulus; Claudia's students have already reached the sect's threshold, while her own foolish disciple is still wandering around in the high level—
No way! My disciple absolutely cannot be inferior to Claudia's!
After leaving the Bai Lu Forest, little Merlin wore a serious expression, thinking, "I can recover, right? That old lady better not deceive me! Otherwise, how will I survive in this dangerous otherworld with my current conduct?"
Alice lowered her head, watching little Merlin—now turned into a little brat—walking unsteadily, as if he might fall over at any moment? worrying.
Little Merlin can no longer wear the demon sword Banri Garan; this katana is obviously taller than him, slung on his back, as he walks it often drags on the ground, making a "clatter clatter" sound.
The two—one big, one small—little Merlin's appearance makes it believable that he's Alice's son; looks rather comical—
Alice: "Merlin, let me hold the sword for you?" Merlin: "No need!" Alice: "How about I hold you instead? Walking will be much faster." Merlin: "I don't need that! Don't treat me like a kid, my legs are long enough!!"
"...Alice furrowed her beautiful brows, feeling that even if Merlin becomes a child, his pride remains as high as before," "You don't need to worry too much; during this time I can protect you, you can try relying on me more."
"Damn.... Little Merlin showed a look as if he were about to spit blood, kneeling on the ground, utterly unwilling to think—
I actually ended up needing Alice's protection?!
I never imagined I'd have a day like this, sniveling...."
At the same time, in the adventurers' guild of Rexhelm, a stranger arrived.
This person wore a black robe, making it hard to see their face, walked straight into the guild and stood before Lukiya.
"Miss, please..."
Lukiya lifted her head, temporarily setting aside her work, feeling the person before her was unfamiliar, "Sir, what do you need help with? If you have a task to commission us, please fill out a form next to it and post it on the request board; then adventurers will contact you voluntarily. Of course, if the situation is special, I can also recommend some excellent adventurers."
"I'm not here to commission a task; I want to inquire about something." The mysterious person lowered their voice.
"...May I ask what it is?" Lukiya became serious.
"Do you have anyone named Merlin here? Cough—no, I mean, is there a human adventurer named Merlin?" The mysterious person got straight to the point.
"Merlin? You're looking for Mr. Merlin?" Lukiya chuckled slightly, instinctively asking, "May I ask who you are?"
"Me? .... The mysterious person stiffened, fell silent for a moment, then said—
"I and Merlin come from the same place...
"Let's just say we're fellow townsmen."
■T oBeued
Afterword
Today is a double day off; according to the rankings, today is a single update.
Merlin's brat state won't last long; soon he'll enter the United Kingdom elf storyline.
I think some readers know what that means, so I won't elaborate.
Overall I'm quite satisfied with this volume; at least the ending is full of many unknowns.
This book starts with an overpowered, max-level invincible flow, hardly any upgrade elements.
It's not the kind where you need to layer power upgrades for invincibility; I removed the upgrade system right at the start.
That's why many think level distinctions aren't obvious, since I've positioned this as a plot-driven novel, and upgrade-like plots have mostly been cut.
However, writing after the opening invincible gets harder and harder, my pressure is also considerable.
This book is a long novel; without an upgrade system to propel the plot, and without several heroines to add content.
The further I write, the more I feel the difficulty; without an upgrade system, the bottleneck of a single heroine pure love story is obvious, like the feeling of writing a book while severing one's own arm.
Although I can guarantee this book is a single heroine pure love throughout, future new books might rarely touch single heroine pure love long novels unless there's a solid system framework to build on.
Alright, that's it; see you in the next volume!

title: Chapter 1 — Blackmail
content:
Chapter 1 — Blackmail

Volume 21 · Chapter 1

Under the night, Rexham was silent, with occasional dog barks breaking the stillness.
As the town's well-known 'entertainment' venue, the Secret Cottage had already closed for the night.
However, the lights inside were not extinguished; the weak candlelight flickered repeatedly—
“Sister, can't we just fly there?”
“Yes, it's too dangerous for you to go alone; why don't we accompany you?”
Dozens of the Secret Cottage's barmaids gathered at the door, calling Helena 'sister,' living together like family.
They are all female demons belonging to the Fourth Demon Lord Palace, continually deceiving men to come here and spend money in order to obtain external resources.
Such establishments run by demons are scattered throughout many human nations, and Helena is the overseer of this entire region.
However, something terrible has happened now, making all the female demons uneasy, living in constant anxiety every day.
Helena's demon identity was discovered by the bandits of Rexham, who not only weren't afraid but openly began to extort
They demanded Helena produce a large sum of money as hush money, otherwise she would bear the consequences!
During this period, rumors spread throughout Rexham, all concerning the most beautiful woman in town, speculating about Helena's identity.
This is clearly the bandits applying pressure, trying to intimidate Helena, hoping she will obediently comply and not resort to extreme measures.
Business at the Secret Cottage has become increasingly difficult; if this isn't resolved soon, Asmodeus' side will likely notice the abnormality soon.
Helena had been dealing with the bandits for over a month, but under the ultimatum she was defeated.
The bandits no longer wanted to play games with Helena; they clearly stated that if they didn't see the money soon, they would bring clergy from the church to publicly expose her demon identity.
No matter how Helena negotiated, they refused to budge, so she had to compromise, preparing an expensive crystal card.
Helena absolutely does not want her demon identity exposed; that is her bottom line.
Humans and demons have always been opposing camps; only a rare few humans can accept demons as evil beings.
Moreover, as the overseer of this region, if her demon identity were exposed, it would cause a major incident, affecting all her sisters, who would be subjected to the angry humans' punishment of being placed on a wooden horse.
Thus Helena hesitated repeatedly; to ensure everyone's safety, she had no choice but to obediently hand over the hush money, hoping the matter would be settled.
“'No, they demand I go alone; you stay behind and guard this place's safety.' Helena said sternly.”
“'But what if those bandits give you trouble?' the barmaid demon asked worriedly.”
“'Don't worry too much; I can handle them.' Helena donned a black windbreaker, preparing to leave secretly.”
“'Sister, why don't we go together and slaughter those bandits? Only the dead won't spill secrets.' Another barmaid suggested.”
Helena smiled helplessly; she had considered that idea before, but it's utterly unrealistic and would only bring trouble upon herself.
“'We absolutely cannot expose our demon identity; many people already suspect us. If we killed those bandits spreading rumors, wouldn't that confirm the rumor that this place is a demon stronghold? Moreover, if suddenly so many humans died overnight in the main city, the imperial authorities would certainly not ignore it; if they investigated, our troubles would only grow.'”
The female demons fell silent, feeling Helena's words made sense; the more dangerous the situation, the less they could act rashly.
Moreover, we are now in a very passive state, being led by the nose by those hateful bandits; reconciliation is probably the best outcome.
“'....Should we really not inform the master? Given the master's favor toward you, he would surely secretly lend a hand to help us overcome this difficulty.' The barmaid demon thought they should tell Asmodeus; maybe it could be easily resolved.”
“'Exposing our demon identity is my carelessness; if His Majesty knew, he would certainly impose punishment.' Helena hesitated because, having been favored by Asmodeus, she was unwilling to confess after making a mistake, fearing it would shake her position: 'His Majesty always distinguishes rewards and punishments; by then.....we will all have nothing good to eat....'”
Several beautiful female demons lowered their heads; if Asmodeus learned of this, it wouldn't be just Helena punished but everyone would face punishment.
The situation is indeed very tricky; if the hush money can keep the demons' secret hidden, it would be a win-win for everyone.
“'I'll go and come back quickly.'”
Helena put on the hood of her black windbreaker behind her, went alone to the dangerous place; her heart was equally anxious.
Although in a small place like Rexham, few could defeat her, she still needed to be vigilant, for the opponents were a gang of cunning thieves.
However, Helena had prepared a backup plan; although she couldn't inform Asmodeus, Merlin knew of this and said he could come to her aid if needed.
With Merlin, that arrogant sovereign, behind her, she obviously had more confidence and would not feel very panicked.
However, Merlin's identity is a secret; even though the sisters here are demons, some things are not convenient to speak openly.
Before leaving, Helena to reassure her companions, only left behind this sentence:
“'If....if I don't return within three days, then something must have happened; you can go inform Mr. Merlin of the local Adventurers Guild; he will find a way.'”
The full moon hung high, though some clouds obscured its light.
In a remote corner of Rexham stood a dilapidated two-story house.
Located in a secluded part of the main city, the area is full of pickpockets, and few people come here.
However, precisely because there are few people, it has become a haunt for bandits.
Bandits usually have a vast underground network; information spreads extremely quickly, and many shady deals are carried out in secret.
Two bandits guarded the door, seemingly waiting for someone.
“'Are they coming or not? Won't they be a tough nut to crack?' the bald big guy muttered, rubbing his shiny oily head.”
“'Ooh ooh ooh....' his companion yawned, listlessly saying, 'Who knows? The boss said if that woman doesn't behave, we'll make her wish she were dead.'”
“'I never expected such a beautiful woman to actually be a female demon? Do you think all demon women are that beautiful? If I had the chance to keep one as a pet, hehehe....' The bald big guy leered.”
“'What are you thinking? With your disposition, you'd probably be drained in a few rounds.' His companion replied meaningfully.”
At that moment, a person in a black windbreaker with a slender figure slowly approached, seeming to intend to force entry.
“'Hold on! No outsiders allowed inside!' the bald big guy shouted sternly, stepping in front of them.”
“'Outsiders? Are you talking about me?' Helena removed her hat, revealing her beautiful visage.”
The bald big guy was left breathless by Helena's beauty before him, quickly putting on a smile and saying, 'Yo! Isn't this Rexham's most beautiful woman, Miss Helena? Please come in; we've been waiting for you a long time.'
Helena stared at the pitch-black house before her, hesitated a moment, then strode inside--
---- Time awakened countless greedy eyes, their gazes roaming wantonly over Helena's alluring figure.....
What awaits Helena in the ferocious bandits' den?
Tomorrow seems like it can have an extra update; please pay more attention.

title: Chapter 2 — Deeply Trapped
content:
Chapter 2 — Deeply Trapped

Volume 21 · Chapter 2

In a remote wooden cabin, dim yellow lights were lit, and dozens of bandits gathered here.
Inside, smoke swirled, the heavy smoke was very pungent...
The bandits looked like hungry wolves, constantly gazing at this beautiful female demon who visited at night with their unrestrained greedy eyes.
Helena looked around, finding that this group of bandits had little strength, so she didn't need to worry too much; although she despised their naked gazes, she could only endure for now.
"Hehehe, you finally came over? I thought Miss Helena, so proud, would resist us to the end." The bandit leader sat opposite, supporting the table with his hands and resting his chin on them; his mouth and eyes were askew, his appearance ugly enough to provoke disgust, revealing an obvious lecherous nature.
Helena stopped, staring at that disgusting man, and took out a crystal card from her bosom, worth hundreds of thousands of gold coins or more, "I've brought what you wanted; as agreed, everything will be settled, and you will forever forget my true identity."
"You're really straightforward?" the bandit leader laughed, his shoulders shaking, his voice hoarse, "Very good, I like your temperament; doing business with straightforward people is most pleasant."
"I hope you keep your promise and don't do anything like playing with fire and burning yourself; otherwise, after we turn hostile, the demon race's wrath is not something you can bear." Helena placed the crystal card on the table and pushed it straight toward the bandit leader.
"Hmph..." The bandit leader coldly smiled, taking the valuable crystal card, a hint of cunning flashing in his eyes.
"Since the deal is done, I have no need to stay; I hope we won't have any further dealings." Helena said coldly, turning to leave.
"Miss Helena, you think we'll let you go that easily? How naive..." The bandit leader said meaningfully.
Two bandits revealed evil smiles, blocking Helena's path. She turned to stare at the bandit leader, Saint-tier golden magic power surging silently, "What do you mean? I've already made an exception and conceded; you still want to push further? Who gave you the nerve to act against us"
"Sorry, people die for wealth, birds die for food; we're just doing this for money!"
As soon as he finished speaking, the bandit leader suddenly leapt up, grabbed a bottle filled with water, and smashed it hard at Helena.
Normally it would shatter, splashing water everywhere, spraying onto Helena's body, instantly like boiling hot water, sending up rolling white steam over the demon's form.
"Holy Church's holy water?!" Helena exclaimed in shock; although this looks like ordinary water, it's actually a product processed by the Holy Church, extremely toxic to demons, with a very obvious suppressive effect!
Seeing the boss act, the bandits all took out their prepared holy water bottles and smashed them hard at Helena, hoping to suppress this female demon before she could retaliate.
Although holy water is an exclusive tool of clergy, for the bandits who run the black market, obtaining such things is not particularly difficult.
Helena's body gradually became soaked with holy water; if she didn't find a way to resist, her power would be significantly suppressed, and dangerous mishaps could easily occur.
In desperation, Helena erupted with terrifying Saint-tier magical power, blasting away all the holy water on her body!
Helena's face turned pale, she clutched her chest and panted; having only been corroded by the holy water (maybe a typo), her whole body was already covered in wounds, her power greatly weakened, likely unable to exert her full strength.
She glared angrily at the bandit leader, considering these humans dangerous; to ensure her safety, she could only choose to go all out and kill everyone.
As for the trouble that might arise afterward? We'll deal with it later.
"Ugh!" The bandit leader shrank his neck, thinking he could suppress Helena, but didn't expect her to break free; facing a Saint-tier powerhouse, he obviously lacked confidence!
"Despicable humans!" Helena gritted her teeth, lowly shouting, and with a backhand condensed a concentrated water droplet spinning at high speed, "You will pay for your rudeness!"
The concentrated water droplet suddenly shot out like a sharp arrow, unstoppable, aiming straight at the bandit leader, intending to pierce this scoundrel.
Helena's Saint-tier magic power was formidable; the sharp water arrow undulated in the air, creating layers of ripples, the piercing sonic boom startling.
This is while Helena was suppressed by the holy water; under normal circumstances, its power would probably be even greater than now.
"Mr. Brett, save me!" The bandit leader desperately retreated, still calling for help!
Suddenly, a black shadow descended from the sky, wearing a black eyepatch over one eye, holding a round shield and a naval sword, Saint-tier battle aura surging continuously, pressure pressing directly at Helena.
The one-eyed man named Brett raised his black round shield, firmly blocking Helena's water arrow magic; the splashing water overturned all the nearby tables and chairs.
"Tsk! You called for reinforcements?" Helena frowned, originally dealing with these bandits wasn't difficult, but now, after being corroded by holy water, she had to face an opponent of the same Saint-tier, inevitably feeling great pressure.
The water arrow left a clear dent on Brett's black small shield, nearly piercing through it.
He slowly lifted his head, his single eye scanning Helena, and muttered hoarsely—
"As expected of the demon race's elite; my shield is forged from black gold and inscribed with defensive spells. As a Saint-tier opponent, it's hard to leave a mark on it. Indeed, demons are extremely dangerous monsters; we must be extra careful."
"Who are you? Dare to interfere with our..." Helena felt the man holding a white sword and black shield before her was a true enemy; the other bandit lackeys, as long as they lacked holy water, could be ignored.
"I'm merely a subordinate following orders; I find it hard to answer you, but I heard that a certain superior wants only a living demon; unfortunately, you are our best target." Brett said muffledly, placing the white sword on the black shield, assuming a gladiator's stance; from his flawless posture one could tell he is a warrior who has endured countless battles.
"Capture me alive? What audacity!" Helena thought the matter simple; these bandits not fearing demons was strange—turns out someone had been watching her all along.
"If you agree to stop resisting, maybe things could go better; if you don't cooperate, I can only use force to make you submit." Brett's eyes showed no ripples, no emotion at all.
"You used holy water to scheme against me, thinking I'd be so easily defeated? You've overthought it!"
Helena took off her black robe, raised her arms high, revealing her slender, graceful figure.
In an instant, black feathers appeared; she revealed her fallen angel form, demon horns sprouting on her head, a pair of black wings unfurling fiercely.
Holy magical power formed a ceaseless flow of water; a giant serpent made entirely of water coiled around Helena, protecting her, and roared at all the vile humans, spewing forth—
"Hiss!"
There is an extra update before midnight.

title: Chapter 3 — Lord of the Black Market
content:
Chapter 3 — Lord of the Black Market

Volume 21 · Chapter 3

The two Saint-tier powerhouses began clashing inside the cramped house, while the surrounding band of petty thieves either bolted for the door or cowered in the corners, trembling.

“I was raised as a gladiator from childhood, surviving countless deadly battles. If my master hadn’t purchased me, my name would have been carved into the Champion’s Pillar of the Holy Roman Arena, immortalized as a glorious gladiator hero. But I’ve never fought a demon before—my long-dormant blood is finally burning again. Come!” Burey tapped his white blade against his black shield, a classic gladiatorial taunt.

“Hah!” Helena summoned her magic, and the colossal serpent coiling around her seemed to come alive, hissing as it lunged at Burey with gaping jaws.

Despite his hulking frame, Burey moved like a nimble monkey in the confined space, flipping and dodging the Great Water Serpent’s strikes.

The serpent was terrifying—its entire body a churning mass of water, each movement sending violent waves crashing through the room, shaking the house as if it might collapse at any moment.

Helena stood motionless, fully focused, her fingers twitching slightly. The water serpent responded with eerie precision, striking exactly where she directed.

But Burey, a gladiator tempered by battle since youth, was swift. Every time the serpent swallowed him, he barely escaped its maw.

Helena’s expression darkened. The Holy Water’s corrosion made her body ache, and her anxiety grew. She shifted tactics—

The serpent suddenly split midair into a two-headed beast, launching a pincer attack. This time, it succeeded in swallowing Burey whole.

Trapped in the thick, suffocating water, Burey endured crushing pressure, as if submerged in the deep sea. His bones groaned under the strain, on the verge of snapping.

Worse, he couldn’t break free. Once inside the serpent, he was sealed as if by a binding spell, unable to move.

Oxygen deprivation set in. Burey’s vision blurred, and he exhaled a string of bubbles, on the brink of suffocation.

“In the end, you humans are nothing special—just thieves who stole the fruits of our demon race…”

Helena sneered, spreading her arms as she activated another Saint-tier spell. A high-pressure water spear, surging with violent currents, materialized before her.

The immense power warped the air around the spear, accompanied by a deafening roar, as if it could tear space itself apart.

“Disappear, human!”

Helena gripped the water spear like a javelin, took aim at Burey—now encased in water, a perfect target—and hurled it.

With a piercing *whoosh*, the terrifying spear shot forward, piercing the serpent. The water column exploded outward.

The impact shook the earth, and the roof collapsed under the slicing force of the water.

Helena exhaled deeply, her face pale. Already weakened by the Holy Water, the battle with Burey had drained her further, leaving her lightheaded.

But just as she caught her breath, a deep voice rang out again—

“Just as I expected. Are all demons as strong as you?”

“Wha—!”

Helena froze, eyes widening in horror as she looked up. The man she thought she had killed—Burey—still stood before her, unyielding.

What the hell is going on?!

This man… there’s something off about him!

No one should survive that attack… it’s impossible…

Her gaze trembled slightly, disbelief clouding her mind.

In truth, Burey’s injuries were severe—a fist-sized hole in his abdomen, carved by the high-pressure water spear. Blood still gushed from the wound, yet he stood there like an unfeeling iron statue, not even flinching.

Burey loomed over Helena, drenched and disheveled, yet utterly indifferent to his own wounds.

Helena snapped back to her senses, summoning a fresh current of water to deliver another lethal strike.

But mages were always vulnerable at close range, and this time was no exception. The enemy wouldn’t give her a chance to counter.

Burey took a sudden step forward, his Saint-tier battle aura erupting. His muscles rippled as he swung his left hand’s small black shield, slamming it into Helena’s petite frame.

“Cough—ah!” Helena spat blood, her eyes wide with shock.

With a single word from Burey, she was hammered into the ground by the shield. The impact detonated with a *bang*, blasting apart the house and carving a massive crater into the earth, the ground splitting with cracks.

Burey slowly stood, looking down at the severely wounded and unconscious Helena. Calmly, he said, “Without the Holy Water’s help, you’d have been a troublesome opponent… Just what kind of ancient tribe are the demons, anyway?”

Seeing the fight was over, the thief leader crept out from his hiding spot, trembling. “I-is it… safe now?”

“She’s unconscious. Later, she’ll be shackled with magic-sealing and battle aura-suppressing manacles, then delivered to that lord. She won’t be a threat anymore.” Burey grunted, tearing off part of his shirt to roughly bind his wound.

The thief leader gasped at the sight of the gaping hole in Burey’s flesh. A normal person would be screaming in agony, but this hulk of a man showed no reaction at all.

“Th-then… Mr. Burey, we did good this time, right?”

“Not bad.” Burey nodded, pulling a pouch of gold coins from his pocket and tossing it to the thief leader. “This is a reward from the family head for your assistance.”

“Hehehe, no, no, it’s our honor to serve the family head~” The thief leader grinned as he pocketed the coins, thrilled by the windfall.

To operate in the gray markets of a major city like Rexham, these thief gangs clearly had powerful backers.

The entire black market trade of Britannia was controlled by these thieves, and their master was none other than the infamous Morgan family.

The empire’s underground dealings generated staggering daily profits, all flowing into the Morgan family’s coffers, making them practically the underground emperors of Britannia.

Unlike the Rothschild family, whose industries spanned the world, the Morgans were deeply rooted in Britannia itself, dominating the empire’s shipbuilding business.

The empire’s prized warships were all products of the Morgan family. Their ability to straddle both political and commercial spheres was what made them so formidable.

As for the thieves before him, no matter how fierce they seemed, they were nothing more than the lowest of the Morgan family’s attack dogs.

Burey hoisted the unconscious Helena over his shoulder like a bandit, seemingly preparing to leave.

The thief leader glanced at Helena’s face, wondering which important figure would get to enjoy such a beautiful demoness. Lucky bastard…

“Mr. Burey, do you know… who’s taking Helena? What do they plan to do with her?”

“You’re just the family’s leashed dogs. You don’t deserve to know that much. Remember your place and stop prying into things that don’t concern you.” Burey shot the thief leader a cold glare, a clear warning.

“Y-yes, yes, my bad…” The thief leader wiped his cold sweat, forcing a smile. But once Burey was out of sight, his expression twisted. He spat on the ground.

“You’re no better than the rest of us—just a bought-and-paid-for slave.”

Tch. What a joke.

title: Chapter 4 — London Guild
content:
Chapter 4 — London Guild

Volume 21 · Chapter 4

After several days of travel, Alice and Little Merlin returned to Great Britain.

However, the two of them did not return to Rheghem immediately, but came directly to the royal capital, London.

Before leaving, they were commissioned by Circe and needed to send the time potion to the president of the London Adventurers Guild, Gregory.

This task was obviously not difficult; it was just delivering some items along the way.

Since Alice obtained new equipment, the "Angelique" angel space ring, the two of them traveled much more lightly, and many things could be stored inside it.

Little Merlin had already drunk three bottles of the antidote given by Circe, but there was completely no effect, except making him feel extremely nauseous, with no signs of recovering his adult form at all.

"Tch! Really hateful, how much do I have to drink to recover?"

Little Merlin showed a nauseous expression, constantly spitting out his blackened tongue stained by the potion, shaking the empty potion bottle in his hand.

"Didn't I tell you to take it on time, until you finish drinking it? The effect might not manifest until you finish it all."

Alice surmised

"Before I recover my adult form, I might be poisoned to death by the smell of this potion... Little Merlin frowned, complaining continuously.

"...You've never had much patience since you were young... Alice shrugged helplessly, there's no use being anxious, it's not like there's anything we can do but take it slow.

"Who said that?! " Little Merlin turned his head and said seriously, "I just don't want to remain a little kid. I endured over 200 years to become an adult, and now look, it was all for nothing.

"What's so bad about that? Your current appearance is much better than before, at least I think it's pretty fun. Just now taking the boat back home gave you a child's ticket, you didn't even need to spend money~ I Alice poked Little Merlin's face with her finger.

"Don't touch you, you really talk big without worrying about your back, who would want that child's ticket?! ?" Little Merlin dodged Alice's teasing, irritatedly stomping his feet.

Although Merlin's body had become a child, his heart was the same as before, a thoroughly grown-up demon.

A third-generation monarch of the demon race, and yet he was given a free child's ticket on a boat, this was simply a great shame and humiliation!

Little Merlin followed beside Alice, and many people took him for the son of a single mother, irritating him to the point of wanting to roll his eyes!

"Be quiet, we've already arrived at the London Adventurers Guild..." Alice pulled back the curtain of the carriage, looking outside.

After the two got off the carriage, they saw the largest, strongest, and most prosperous Adventurers Guild in Great Britain.

Led by the Gold-ranked adventurer Gregory, this group ranked among the top even in the entire human world as an adventurer organization.

Little Merlin looked up at the magnificent building before him, " ...Such a magnificent building, compared to our guild in Rheghem... it's simply like a countryside roadside tavern.....

"..... Alice had a drop of cold sweat roll down her forehead, powerless to refute, "Is... is that so, but after all, the reputation of London's guild is out there, the overall strength of adventurers is indeed stronger than Rheghem's.

"A tall five-story building, looking very imposing, making it hard to find anything more eye-catching along the street than this guild's attic.

"The gorgeous facade seems to have been crafted with heavy gold; just standing in front of it one can feel some pressure, as well as the extraordinary nature of the London Guild.

Little Merlin felt an insurmountable gap, not just in momentum, but more so that the London Adventurers Guild looks more professional.

"Shall I go in with you?" Alice asked tentatively, feeling that Little Merlin's state wasn't good, it was safer to stay by her side.

"Since we've come, not going in would seem too wasteful." Little Merlin nodded.

Continuing the novel

Entering the London Adventurers Guild, the first thing that came into view was a spacious hall, fully equipped.

Huge chandeliers could be called works of art of unparalleled beauty; even the floor was carefully polished tiles, on which one could faintly see one's own reflection.

This was simply not like an Adventurers Guild, but rather a huge high-end talent market.

Busy adventurers came and went in large numbers, roughly ten times the number of the Rheghem Guild!

They gathered before the rolling quest boards, carefully selecting their tasks.

Just glancing a few times, Little Merlin secretly ate in surprise, because he saw quite a few S-class, SS-class quests with generous rewards!

Such high-level quests are rarely encountered even over several months in Rheghem, yet here several were seen consecutively?!

It seems the overall strength of London's adventurers completely crushes Rheghem's, possibly having double-digit Saint-tier powerhouses!

And not only adventurers gathered here, but also many well-dressed gentlemen with refined manners, and minor nobles, contacting suitable adventurers.

Regardless of scale, level, or proficiency, your guild is far inferior to the London Adventurers Guild, truly cannot be compared.

Little Merlin secretly sighed, quietly saying, "Alice, this place is so formidable? I didn't expect business to be so bustling.

"After all, they are the top adventurer organization in the empire... Alice replied in a low voice.

"Let's rebel? How about leaving Rheghem and joining here? What do you think?" Little Merlin's eyes lit up, saying that if one wants to rebel, one should rebel immediately, not mentioning the old President Taylor's kindness at all.

Ten thousand novel

"Wow, you're really.... " Alice rolled her eyes, being made very speechless by Little Merlin's such an uncertain stance, "Can't you have some backbone?'

"People go where the high ground is, water flows to the low ground, isn't that very normal?" Little Merlin spread his hands.

"You think too beautifully, the problem is that changing guilds isn't so easy, it requires many assessments, do you think they'd be willing to accept useless trash?" Alice answered softly.

"? You're finding new ways to scold me?" Little Merlin frowned tightly.

"I didn't mean that, I mean changing guilds is a difficult thing, unless Rheghem's Adventurers Guild really can't be run anymore, then it might be possible." Alice explained.

"Tch! Really troublesome... Little Merlin pouted,

Although the London Adventurers Guild has many strong experts, Silver-ranked adventurers are still not many.

Alice had just entered the door and attracted quite a few people's attention, a middle-aged man with short hair and a delicate beard walked over.

This middle-aged man looked mature on the outside, wearing light armor, with a military sword embedded with rubies at his waist, appearing to be a beautiful swordsman.

When he stepped inside, an overwhelming pressure emanated from his body, yet he was ferocious like a lion or tiger, not weaker than Alice in the slightest!

"I am the guild's vice president, Weland Motam." Weland gave a slight bow, politely asking, "Unknown to you, coming from Rheghem all the way here, what is the matter?"

" We previously operated in France, and encountered the Gold-ranked adventurer Circe, who said your president's spirit was injured and he is in a coma, so she asked me to deliver the potion." Alice said concisely and briefly.

"Circe..." As a vice president, Weland knew quite a few secrets, upon hearing this name he instantly showed respect, knowing the matter was important, so he put out a please gesture, "Please follow me to a quiet place to talk, there are too many people and eyes here, it's not suitable for discussing important matters.

"Very well." Alice nodded, wanting to take Little Merlin along.

However, Weland's expression became strange, his eyes fixed on Little Merlin, who was shorter than most people's knees; if not for Alice leading the way, he might easily be overlooked—

"May I ask... this child..."

"Is he your son?"
