title: Chapter 5 — A Look of Arrogance (Extra)
content:
Chapter 5 — A Look of Arrogance (Extra)

Volume 21 · Chapter 5

Weland also considers himself well-traveled, but he thinks Alice as a mother is still a bit too young— the kid is already this big? !
He couldn't help but deeply suspect that he might be out of touch with the times, unable to keep up with most people's thinking.

“Even if it's your lordship's son, it's better not to follow along— some things are rather secret, not suitable for children to know”

“No......... Alice is embarrassed, wanting to speak but stopping, not knowing how to explain to the other party.”

“. .-. What are you saying? !” Little Merlin was so angry he jumped up and down, wanting to smash Weland's knee— how could I look like Alice's son? ! Isn't it just that your guild leader got knocked out and is still unconscious? What secret is that! It was me who did it!

Alice stopped the angrily jumping little Merlin, awkwardly asking, "The kid's... not related, right?"

“My lord, I hope you understand that the guild leader's unconsciousness is known only to a few; if it spreads, it will have a considerable impact on our guild.” Weland said seriously, although the London Adventurers Guild is full of strong warriors, as a platinum adventurer Gregory remains the guild's flagship.

...... Alice hesitated, looking at Merlin, as if seeking his opinion.

Little Merlin crossed his arms, suppressed his displeasure, feeling that business comes first, so he nodded, "Go ahead, I'll wait a bit."

Alice let out a breath, followed Weland away, planning to secretly hand over the time potion.

Little Merlin helplessly stayed behind, after looking around, he saw two somewhat familiar figures—

Adams and Renee had returned long ago; because Merlin stole the spotlight on the island in the Mystic Sea, the two have been feeling downcast ever since, to the point that their bonuses and such have gone to waste. or 工」“吼

The two are also considered frontline strength of the London Adventurers Guild, yet in the mission they were suppressed by a mid-way joining black-iron adventurer— how frustrating that is.

“What's wrong with Adams and Renee? After returning from France they've been listless— did they suffer some blow?”

“Not sure, but I heard they were carrying out a secret mission with the Seventh Thorn Knight Morrison, and... it ended up like this....”

Several adventurers observed Adams and Renee from afar, whispering among themselves, completely unaware of what happened in the Mystic Sea.

“Tsk tsk.... Little Merlin clicked his tongue and shook his head, sympathizing with their mindset; he had wanted to go over and say something, but thinking of his own brat-like appearance he immediately gave up the idea— after all, even Alice doesn't recognize her own childhood self, let alone Adams and Renee.”

“What background does that black-iron adventurer have? Why could he do something so unimaginable?” Adams drank his bitter ale, almost doubting his life.

“Not sure, but the monster head he's holding is indeed formidable— that... the North Sea Giant Kraken, a monster that once sent countless strong warriors to their deaths in the sea, actually got petrified? Even if we said it, few would believe us, since we ourselves had a close encounter with the North Sea Giant Kraken not long ago.” Renee furrowed her brows, muttering, "Vice Guild Leader Weland even said we might have been seeing hallucinations— how ridiculous.”

“. Say--. Did that guy really, while we were locked in fierce combat with the tentacle monster, charge in alone and take down the island's strongest monster? Thinking back, during our fight we witnessed a terrifyingly oppressive light shooting up to the sky— we wouldn't..... Adams wanted to speak but stopped, already a bit afraid to think about it.”

“Impossible! He must have gotten some treasure from somewhere, which is why he dared join our crew; we can't do such things, how could a black-iron adventurer manage? Could the centuries-old adventurer rating system be flawed? Thinking about it, it's unlikely.” Renee still couldn't believe Merlin's unfathomable strength; she was certain that the power of that skull itself was immense.

“That's true, but we've put in so much to get where we are today, and yet the effect isn't even close to that of a single black-iron adventurer— how infuriating!” Adams resentfully slammed the table.

“Such things... try to take it in stride; maybe we don't have that guy's luck, but if we also possessed the weapons of the ancient gods from myth, we could surely destroy heaven and earth without breaking a sweat.”

Renee said sourly, having already judged Merlin's own strength as mediocre.

She felt someone staring at her from behind, so she turned in surprise and saw little Merlin.

Looking at that brat's half-smiling expression, Renee whispered to Adams.

“Do you see that kid behind us always staring? Do you know him?”

Adams curiously turned back to look at little Merlin, shook his head, "I don't know— whose spoiled brat is this? What's he doing at the guild?"

“Don't know, maybe he's just come to play; looking at that gaze, he might want us to play with him— why don't you play a tune on your instrument to cheer him up?” Renee said teasingly with a smile. py S F this little cure

“Who wants to deal with a little brat?” Adams had a few black lines on his forehead, turned back and shouted, "What are you looking at? Stupid brat, go play somewhere else!"

“Shout!” Little Merlin pursed his lips, walked away arrogantly, not bothering with those two guys, thinking they were defeated underlings— who would want to look at you

“Tsk? What does that mean? Are kids nowadays all so arrogant? ..- Too impolite!” Adams' face fell—not only had he suffered setbacks in the Mystic Sea, now even kids look down on him!

“..... Maybe his parents didn't teach him well? Forget it, forget it— no point getting angry at a kid, it's not worth it.” Renee awkwardly comforted Adams, not expecting a little brat to be so smug.

“I don't know why... Adams had a complex expression, watching little Merlin's back, he muttered an evaluation:”

“This brat's look of having no regard for others is exactly like that jerk named Merlin.”

- In a quiet room, Deputy Guild Leader Weland and Alice sat facing each other.

“Did you really bring the potion crafted by Master Seysi from the White Dew Forest?” Weland asked with a serious expression.

“Of course.” Alice flipped her hand under the table, the Angel's Ring emitted a faint glow, and the time potion appeared in her hand; she carefully placed this precious item on the table— “This is it.”

“..... Weland held the time potion in both hands, examined it carefully, then asked, “Did Master Seysi say this could heal our guild leader's mental injury? Although she is a highly respected strong adventurer among adventurers, she lacks responsibility; some things should be confirmed, for I fear the guild leader might not be saved but instead poisoned.”

“Such a sigh.... Alice's forehead beaded with large drops of sweat, thinking Seysi really isn't all that proper, Merlin got screwed over badly— “This potion is fine; I myself took it not long ago and escaped danger.”

“Have you taken it yourself? That's wonderful.” Weland breathed a sigh of relief, stored the time potion, couldn't help smiling— now Gregory will recover quickly— “Thank you for sending such a precious item; I don't know how to thank you enough.”

“No need to be polite; we're just passing by to deliver things.” Alice said politely.

“You have a hint of dragon's aura, and it's not weaker than mine; at such a young age to achieve this— truly impressive.” Weland, after close contact with Alice, already had a rough grasp of her strength, exceeding the Saint tier.

“Where, where...” Alice replied modestly, thinking lately everyone's been praising her.

“Someone like you, a genius, has limitless future prospects; staying in the Lackserm guild would be rather shabby.” Weland clasped his hands together, probing with a question.

“If I give your lordship one opportunity....”

“Would you be willing to become a member of the London Adventurers Guild?”

“To be frank, the guild leader already wants to retire; I will become the guild leader here.”

“And with such a bright future ahead of you, young as you are, I'm very interested in grooming you as the successor to the next guild leader.”

title: Chapter 6 — Rampage
content:
Chapter 6 — Rampage

Volume 21 · Chapter 6

After hearing Weilan's words, Alice couldn't help but feel embarrassed, estimating that the other party wanted to recruit her because, despite her young age, her strength had already made her one of the few who could surpass Saint-tier, so they wanted to win her over.

Then, as a successor to be trained, the Adventurers Guild of London would remain steadfast, as long as she wasn't utterly hopeless.

In fact, many adventurers' guilds adopt this approach, selecting a successor before the guild master retires, hoping to continue and flourish the guild.

If Alice could join the great guild based in London, her future would surely be bright, becoming an existence admired by countless people.

Although Alice thought the London Adventurers Guild was indeed impressive, with high scale and prestige, it was also among the top adventurer organizations in the entire human world.

But just because they were willing to recruit and accept her didn't mean Merlin would receive the same treatment.

After all, no matter how strong Merlin became, he was merely a black iron adventurer, unlikely to draw the attention of major powers, and the threshold was low enough to be easily overlooked.

It's like a great job: even if one's personal ability is strong, without a degree they wouldn't even qualify for an interview.

Considering Merlin's situation, Alice didn't want to just leave him casually, so she shook her head and responded—

"Thank you for your kindness, but I think I'll pass. Although our guild is far inferior to yours, we won't necessarily stay beneath you forever; one day, the adventurers of Rexham will be known throughout the world and become the strongest adventurer organization...."

Alice spoke quite seriously, believing that Rexham's current slump was only temporary, and once the next Adventurers' Tournament began, it would be the moment for all guilds to reshuffle.

"Uh.."

Weilan was stunned by Alice's words, seeing that despite her young age, her strength was comparable to his own, perhaps it wasn't a joke?

In Weilan's eyes, Alice was a rare genius who had already surpassed Saint-tier at a young age, and it would be hard to find another person with such heaven-defying potential across the entire empire.

It's a pity that she seemed uninterested in joining the London Adventurers Guild, which left Weilan quite surprised.

"That's truly a shame, you possess such outstanding talent yet are willing to stay in that rustic Rexham guild; I must say it's a waste of resources."

"Mr. Weilan, you are the designated successor to the guild master, surely you are also full of potential and have already earned much admiration, but I want to say...." Alice paused, her eyes turning serious, "It's not only the great guilds that can produce excellent adventurers; those obscure small guilds can too, they just need an opportunity."

"Weilan was speechless; in fact, many fine adventurers in the London guild came from small guilds, and Alice's hint was not wrong." "Since you remain unmoved, I won't press further, but if you ever change your mind, our guild's doors will always be open for you—you should know that among the empire's many adventurer guilds, only ours is called the strongest, and thus possesses an unshakable advantage."

Alice let out a sigh, stood up to leave, and said, "If there's nothing else, then I'll take my leave."

Merlin and Alice completed the task entrusted by Seysi and left the London Adventurers Guild.

They planned to head straight back to Rexham to rest for a while, and would not accept any other tasks in the short term.

After all, their journey through France had been fraught with twists and turns, leaving both of them somewhat exhausted.

Moreover, Merlin's current condition was not optimistic; he still needed proper rest, and would only resume adventuring after recovering his adult state.

"We've talked for a long time—what were you discussing? Wasn't it just about delivering the time potion to them and then ending?" Little Merlin walked ahead of Alice, curiously asking.

"It's not really important; I just wanted to join the London Adventurers Guild, but I've already turned them down." Alice said nonchalantly, thinking that if they recruited Merlin instead, she might truly follow in his footsteps and leave.

"What?!" Little Merlin exclaimed in disbelief, pressing further, "You've been recruited by someone else again?"

"Of course, they seem to have taken notice of my strength and hope to train me as the next guild master." Alice explained concisely.

"...Damn it, no one has ever tried to recruit me, yet you've suddenly turned the tables, becoming a coveted prize everyone's fighting over.."

Little Merlin stomped his feet in anger, feeling deeply unbalanced; Alice's side kept experiencing unexpected joys, while his side kept suffering misfortunes—if this continued, he'd really become a pretty boy who buys meals for Alice. It seemed the goddess of fortune had never smiled upon him; not killing him was already the greatest mercy.

"...." Alice let out a zero sigh, feigning distress, "Actually, this isn't a good thing either; lately people keep throwing olive branches at me, I'm about to get sick of it—what should I do? I really miss the days when I was a salted fish."

"You've had enough! Don't act superior in front of me; you're surely smiling inside." Little Merlin rolled his eyes in anger, arms crossed, muttering,

"You're making me furious...."

"Alright, alright, don't be angry; this is unavoidable. I promise, if I have something to eat, you'll definitely have soup and drink!" Alice said shamelessly.

Little Merlin's face darkened; if this continued, he'd truly become Alice's lackey—damn it, this can't go on, that troublemaker Alice is plotting a rebellion! I absolutely won't let her ride on my head! It's simply a disgrace!

Previously, Alice had always followed behind him as a novice, needing Herculean effort to deal with any foe, but now she was gradually gaining control over Merlin—how could he keep his mind balanced?

Because Little Merlin kept thinking in his heart and didn't watch the road, a splendid carriage came rushing by, galloping with great force.

Eight tall steeds neighed continuously, charging wildly across the central continent, passersby showing fear, seemingly aware that the carriage's owner was not to be trifled with.

Little Merlin caught sight of the carriage heading straight for him in his peripheral vision, his face instantly paling; his two short legs could hardly dodge.

"You damned little brat, get out of the way! Want to die?" The coachman didn't stop the carriage; instead, he swung his long whip and cursed.

"Merlin!" Alice instantly flashed to Little Merlin's front, shielding him behind her, her pupils instantly turning brilliant gold, dragon's might pressing forward—

In an instant, the mighty carriage was overturned, people and horses thrown to the ground!

The eight steeds neighed in terror, spewing white foam under the fearsome dragon's might.....

title: Chapter 7 — The Morgan Family
content:
Chapter 7 — The Morgan Family

Volume 21 · Chapter 7

Alice’s dragon blood surged within her, and the overwhelming might of her draconic presence sent waves of terror through every lesser creature nearby.

The horses, as if mice spotting a cat, shrieked in panic, stamping their hooves and refusing to move forward.

Even the coachman tumbled to the ground, utterly bewildered, with no idea what had just happened—only the fleeting sensation that some monstrous horror had streaked past him.

The oppressive aura radiating from Alice, a humanoid dragon, caused quite a commotion. She hurried to Merlin’s side, worriedly checking his condition.

"Are you alright? Did anything happen?"

"...Merlin muttered in a daze, thinking to himself that he had almost forgotten he wasn’t in his adult form anymore—no longer the indestructible body he once had.

The coachman staggered to his feet, rubbing his forehead. Seeing the panicked horses, he flew into a rage and started cursing under his breath.

"Blind, are you?! If you want to die, just say so!"

"What did you say?" Alice spun around abruptly, her furious glare locking onto him.

"Ah!" The coachman was so terrified he didn’t dare breathe, instinctively taking a step back. Noticing she was a Mithril-ranked adventurer, he instantly dropped his earlier arrogance, abandoning any thought of provoking her.

"What’s going on? What happened out there..." A lazy voice drifted from the ornate carriage.

The coachman jolted upright, quickly scurrying to the carriage with forced reverence, squeezing out a smile as he whispered, "My lord, we almost hit a child. The horses got spooked."

[OP SE: Chris turns small]

"So what if we hit a child? Just plow through! In this royal capital, who wouldn’t show *me* some respect—except Her Majesty the Queen?" the man inside said with pride.

"...The child’s mother is a Mithril-ranked adventurer. She... doesn’t look like someone to trifle with." The coachman spoke cautiously.

The man in the carriage fell silent for a moment. Upon hearing Alice’s status, his tone shifted immediately. "If she’s a Mithril-ranked adventurer, then yes, it’s best not to provoke her. Drive away—no need to interact with them. If I get the chance, I’ll make sure adventurers are driven out of London."

"Understood, my lord." The coachman nodded, climbing onto the carriage and taking the reins. Not forgetting to flaunt his borrowed authority, he shouted, "Hmph! Consider yourselves lucky today—our lord doesn’t deign to acknowledge you. Next time, you won’t be so fortunate!"

"You—!" Alice blinked in stunned disbelief, never expecting to be framed like this.

Ignoring her displeasure, the coachman cracked his whip and swiftly drove the carriage away.

Yet, as it passed by Alice and Merlin, a gap in the curtains briefly revealed the man inside—a greasy-haired, portly figure draped in expensive jewelry. His mouth split into a grin, the glint of a gold tooth flashing as if to ensure no one missed his wealth. He looked down at little Merlin with a mocking smile, his eyes brimming with the disdainful pride of a plantation owner surveying his slaves.

...Merlin frowned, thoroughly annoyed by the man’s attitude.

"Who *is* that?" Alice muttered, having no interest in causing a scene here.

"Wasn’t that the head of the Morgan family? The one who monopolizes the kingdom’s shipbuilding business?" Merlin said.

"Must be. Who else in the royal capital would dare barrel through the streets like that?"

The earlier disturbance had drawn a crowd. Several onlookers were still discussing the carriage.

"The Morgan family?" Little Merlin knitted his brows, thinking in surprise—

So arrogant...

Back in the royal palace, the Thorn Knights who had been dispatched abroad had already returned.

Clarke and Melfield recounted in detail to Elizabeth their encounters in France.

The two nations, separated by the sea, had reached a consensus, subtly forming an alliance to jointly resist the invasions of other races.

Apart from the conflict with the bloodline race, Elizabeth also learned of Alice—especially her terrifying rate of growth.

This girl had first caught Elizabeth’s attention as the wife of Elgin, the Great Swordsman.

But now, Elizabeth had a completely new understanding of Alice, and she couldn’t help feeling a jolt of shock.

Clarke seemed quite taken with her, praising Alice’s outstanding performance against the vampires and strongly recommending her as a foreign Thorn Knight to bolster the Purple Thorn Knights’ ranks.

As someone who knew many hidden truths—including Elgin the Great Swordsman’s true identity—Elizabeth listened to Clarke and Melfield’s report and felt a headache coming on.

Especially the part about Alice furiously cleaving a massive celestial body, allowing sunlight to annihilate countless bloodline monsters.

No matter how Elizabeth thought about it, this didn’t seem like something Alice would do—it sounded more like Elgin the Great Swordsman, i.e., Merlin. After all, that man had a history of large-scale destruction, and obliterating a massive celestial body wasn’t impossible for him.

Though Elizabeth knew Merlin was Elgin the Great Swordsman, she had kept this secret to herself from start to finish, a private understanding between her and Merlin.

As long as Merlin didn’t stir up trouble within the kingdom, Elizabeth would be grateful.

But she did notice Alice’s power was soaring at an alarming rate, and she suspected Merlin had something to do with it—perhaps some kind of secret training?

As for Clarke’s strong recommendation of Alice as a foreign Thorn Knight...

After deep consideration, Elizabeth decided it was worth a try.

Merlin had said he disliked trouble, and Elizabeth had no compelling reason to make him do anything.

His immense power was a valuable asset—if left unused, wouldn’t that be a waste of resources?

So Elizabeth decided to accept Clarke’s suggestion: recruit Alice as a foreign Thorn Knight, indirectly establishing a connection with Merlin. Perhaps this way, she could find a way to enlist his aid.

It seemed Alice’s smooth path to becoming a foreign Thorn Knight owed much to Merlin’s influence.

At this moment, in the palace conference room, Morrison had returned from abroad and was reporting to Elizabeth about the mysterious sea region.

"Lord Morrison, you’ve had a hard journey. What did you uncover in the mysterious sea region?" Elizabeth asked.

"Your Majesty, I have two matters to report." Morrison knelt on one knee, speaking earnestly. "First, the mastermind behind the previous rebellion was indeed creatures from the mysterious sea region. They have a strict hierarchy, vast numbers, and are extremely difficult to deal with. Our party barely escaped the island with our lives."

"How could this be?" Elizabeth massaged her temples, feeling a headache coming on. "Have we been targeted by those creatures? Apart from settling the foreign Thorn Knight candidate, there hasn’t been a single piece of good news."

"Eh?!" Morrison froze, caught off guard by something unexpected.

"Lord Morrison, what’s the second matter?" Elizabeth pressed.

"The second matter... ..." Morrison responded woodenly, his mind reeling—

The foreign Thorn Knight has already been decided?

When?!

I was going to recommend Big Brother Merlin...

I’ve been attending the annual conference lately, so updates might be a bit unstable.

Hope everyone understands. I’ll make up for it when I get back!

title: Chapter 8 — Pirate Successor
content:
Chapter 8 — Pirate Successor

Volume 21 · Chapter 8

Merlin and Alice rode in a carriage leaving the London royal capital, preparing to return to Rexham as quickly as possible to rest.
"Hey! Alice, that... I want to tell you something." Little Merlin said mysteriously.
"What's the matter?" Alice asked, surprised, as she rarely saw Merlin being so serious.
"After we get back, please don't say I turned into a child." Little Merlin emphasized seriously.
"Huh? Why? Is there something hard to say about this?" Alice asked, not understanding.
"I.... As the mighty Demon Lord, ending up as a little brat is super embarrassing. I don't want anyone to know that I could have such an unlucky day!" Little Merlin said very seriously.
"Really? So that's it...." Alice's expression turned weird; she reluctantly agreed, "...Well, but if others ask, how should I answer? I can't just go out and mysteriously bring back a child, can I?"
"....." Little Merlin furrowed his brows, stroking his chin as he thought for a long time, "Just say I'm Merlin's little nephew, needing to stay in Rexham for a few days."
"....." Alice felt inexplicably weird inside, wondering what she was—was she an "aunt"?
The carriage Merlin and Alice were riding rushed straight to Rexham, brushing past a speeding carriage.
Brei's face was grim as he drove his carriage, crossing paths with Merlin and Alice's carriage and departing.
And in that carriage filled with weeds lay the unconscious Helena—
The two groups happened to brush past each other by coincidence.
The Kingdom of Britannia, Bristol port.
A merchant ship that appeared basically non-threatening was slowly approaching the port.
The flag bearing a crowned lion indicated that this was a ship from the Nawé Kingdom's merchants' association, and it had not undergone overly strict inspection or interception, steadily sailing into the port.
The sailors on board had rugged faces, deliberately showing off their scars like medals.
If it weren't for the merchants' association flag fluttering, this group of seemingly fierce sailors brandishing longswords and firearms would likely be mistaken for disguised pirates by many.
In fact, this dilapidated merchant ship truly is a pirate that has been rampaging on the seas; not long ago, they merely replaced the skull pirate flag with the merchants' association flag, sneaking carefully into Britannia's port.
However, this pirate gang had no significant power; they were merely remnants of the Red Beard Pirate Crew, personally wiped out by the Great Swordsman Elgin.
These Red Beard brothers, who once dominated the seas, had the ambition to become pirate kings; their terrifying reputation once made all port cities of Britannia tremble.
But this ill-fated duo kicked an iron plate in Elgin City, encountering the Great Swordsman Elgin, after which their legend came to an end.
However, this swarm of locusts on the sea did not perish just like that; their successors still lurk in the darkness, eager to act.
Locchi, the adopted son of the Red Beard pirates, is also the inheritor of the pirate crew's spirit.
However, he is weak in strength and lacks any cultivation talent, thus being collectively ostracized by the pirates.
To protect this adopted son, the Red Beard pirates expelled him from the crew early on, leaving him to scrape by in a remote icy sea.
Although the Red Beard pirate crew's legend had long since ended, Locchi only recently learned that his two fathers had been slain by the Great Swordsman Elgin.
Locchi's hatred burned ever fiercer; he swore to kill the Great Swordsman Elgin, avenge his fathers' blood, and raise the Red Beard pirate flag once more, letting fear dominate the coastal ports again.
At this moment, inside the fishy-smelling ship's cabin, two people were plotting something?
One is a young captain wearing old leather clothes, the adopted son of the Red Beard pirates, Locchi.
The other is a black-clad person hiding their appearance, whose mysterious attire is highly suspicious.
The two, relying on the faint candlelight, whispered about some kind of deal.
"I have already ordered one of my subordinates to capture a high-ranking demon; I have fulfilled your request," Locchi said.
"Words aren’t proof; I need you to personally deliver that high-ranking demon alive to me," the black-clad person said softly.
"What do you need the demon for? In some sense we are allies; why won’t you tell me?" Locchi asked earnestly.
"You just need to obediently work for us, and we will fulfill your wish; that was the original agreement we made." The mysterious person emphasized, unwilling to say more.
"Enough!" Locchi slammed the table, angrily saying, "I have already shown my sincerity, yet in cooperating with you I am treated like a puppet being manipulated—don’t you think you should reflect on this?"
"We are the strongest dark guild, Phoenix; promises are our most valuable asset, needing no other guarantees. We can help you accomplish unimaginable feats—even the homage to the Oni from a hundred years ago pales before our might. Even if you wanted to kill the Britannia queen, such a trifling matter...." The mysterious person spoke with deep meaning, their words treating a king's life as dust: "As long as you obediently complete the tasks we assign, as repayment we will give you your enemy’s head—"
"I have no interest in killing the Britannia queen; what I want.... is Elgin the Great Swordsman’s head!" Locchi’s eyes blazed, he said earnestly.
"The mysterious person remained completely calm, spreading their hands and saying, "Sure, as long as you can deliver a high-bloodline demon to me, Elgin the Great Swordsman’s life is just a word away for you."
"You... really can take down that bastard? My father couldn’t even withstand a single move from him." Locchi asked, deeply doubtful; he knew dealing with the dark guild Phoenix was like dealing with a tiger for its skin—few could profit from such a dark organization.
But Locchi had no choice; being weak himself, he could not avenge his father, and no one would dare provoke a being like Elgin the Great Swordsman.
Only the powerful, unregulated dark guild Phoenix dares to take down Elgin the Great Swordsman; if one pays the appropriate price, unimaginable gains might be reaped.
"Elgin the Great Swordsman? I’ve heard of this man, a mysterious hero risen in Britannia; even the royal family willingly bows their proud heads to coexist with such a formidable figure. His strength is unfathomable; against all enemies he defeats them in a single move, never dragging his feet. Dealing with such a dangerous individual is indeed not easy...." The mysterious person knows quite a bit about Elgin the Great Swordsman.
"How about it? Even outlaws like you are left helpless?" Locchi felt a drop of cold sweat slide down his forehead.
"No, there is no enemy in this world that can leave our guild Phoenix helpless. Our organization has many warriors wielding extraordinary skills; pulling out any one of them would frighten many." The mysterious person paused, then added—
"Of course, our guild master is the strongest."
"He is a former Purple Gold Adventurer, acclaimed as the human closest to god."
"Elgin the Great Swordsman? Hehe, there is no enemy our guild master cannot defeat...."

title: Chapter 9 — Merlin's Little Nephew
content:
Chapter 9 — Merlin's Little Nephew

Volume 21 · Chapter 9

"So, if I help you capture a high-ranking demon, you will definitely help me kill Elgin the Great Swordsman?" Lochrinn's heart stirred with temptation.

"Are you doubting the strongest dark guild?" the mysterious man asked meaningfully.

"No, I'm asking for your promise." Lochrinn emphasized.

The mysterious man fell silent for a moment, then said leisurely, "Trust us. We have the ability to take Elgin the Great Swordsman's life."

"Good, we have a deal." Lochrinn slowly stood up, adjusting the travel bag made of sad cowhide. "Britain strictly prohibits slave smuggling. I need to grease the palms of the imperial guards to bring that high-ranking demon out. You’ll have to be patient..."

Several days later, Alice and little Merlin’s carriage entered the main city of Rexham.

Captain Prices, the guard captain who protected the town, was on duty but slacking off, constantly dozing off. His thick stubble looked like it hadn’t been trimmed in days.

But upon seeing Alice, whom he hadn’t seen in a long time, Prices instantly became much more alert. A lecherous grin spread across his face as he couldn’t resist the urge to tease her.

"Oh my! Isn’t this Rexham’s most beautiful flower, Miss Alice? It’s been a while. Did you just return from a mission?"

Alice, sitting in the carriage, glanced at Prices and coldly huffed, "You old lecher, shut your mouth."

"Miss Alice, why do you have such a bias against me? Calling me an old lecher is an insult to my character." Prices was scolded fiercely by Alice, but his heart was still secretly thrilled.

"Do you believe I’ll tear your mouth apart so you can never speak again?" Alice, harassed, grew even more annoyed.

"Ah..." Prices’ face flushed with excitement. He turned around, lifted his butt, and said, "I hope you’ll kick my ass!"

Little Merlin was speechless inside. Seeing that Prices was still such a shameless pervert, he instantly felt a lot more at ease.

Prices noticed little Merlin beside Alice and asked curiously, "Who’s this kid? Miss Alice, you didn’t adopt an orphan and decide to live as a widow, did you? Where’s Merlin? He still owes me a lot of drinking money..."

Little Merlin’s whole body jolted, and he couldn’t help but feel a bit more awake. Being a little kid had its perks—at least he didn’t have to pay back the debt.

Alice’s face was covered in frost, her cold aura pressing down as she drew her slender sword and pressed it against Prices’ neck.

"Shut up."

"..." Prices shivered, "...Welcome back, Miss Alice."

After escaping Prices’ harassment, the two didn’t return home directly. Instead, they headed straight for Rexham’s Adventurers Guild.

Little Merlin hadn’t forgotten—he still had an important matter to attend to.

It was a man’s request on the mysterious island at sea...

Little Merlin took out a chain from his bosom. The iron plate on it was engraved with the information of Mithril Adventurer Ralf.

This adventurer’s proof had been handed to Merlin by the desperate Ralf, who hoped it would be brought back to Rexham and hung on the towering tree in the cemetery.

Little Merlin lightly touched the weathered marks on the iron plate, as if they were recounting countless adventures.

Merlin didn’t have any particular feelings for Ralf, his senior. Choosing to surrender by any means necessary to survive seemed somewhat understandable.

But Merlin knew clearly that this would only bring temporary peace—it wouldn’t solve the root problem.

Just like the Holy Light Dragon that had submitted to him, Merlin had never intended to let it go. Instead, he planned to keep it by the gate of the Blood Pool Seal for its entire life as a guard dog.

Alice glanced at the Mithril Adventurer’s proof in little Merlin’s hand. She had already heard about these matters from him.

"I never expected Mr. Ralf to be trapped in the mysterious sea, and even become a pawn for the monsters. If Mr. Karl knew, he would definitely be very disappointed. After all, the two of them have known each other for a long time, fought side by side countless times, and together built up the guild..."

Little Merlin looked at Ralf’s adventurer’s proof and remained silent for a long time.

"Hey, Alice, there’s something I want to say..."

The guild was much quieter than usual.

But the idle loafers were still there.

Hobbes, his face flushed, looked at Arnold, muttering, "Arnold, you useless noble’s son. Your drinking capacity is terrible—it’s not even half of Merlin’s."

"Miss Alice... Alice... When will she come back? I’m about to die..." Arnold slurred drunkenly, his consciousness already dulled from drinking too much.

Because Alice had been away for so long, Arnold, her suitor, had grown increasingly depressed and started drowning his sorrows in alcohol every day.

"Tch! These two good-for-nothings..." From a distance, Lucia rolled her eyes, really wanting to kick these two drunks out.

Alice walked into the guild and immediately saw the two drunkards, frowning.

"Hobbes, you..." As soon as little Merlin entered and saw Hobbes, this old rascal, a sense of familiarity surged, but he quickly remembered his current state and immediately shut his mouth.

Hobbes turned his head and saw Alice, his eyebrows jumping. "Oh! Alice, you’re back!"

Arnold, who had been listless, suddenly perked up as if injected with adrenaline. He jumped up from his chair and rushed toward Alice, overjoyed. "Miss Alice! I missed you!"

Alice knitted her delicate brows and instinctively took a step back, then casually punched Arnold, sending him flying into the wall as if swatting a fly.

"Stay away from me. Your alcohol stench is suffocating."

"Ah... Miss... Alice..." Arnold slowly slid down the wall and passed out.

Hobbes, grinning, walked over with a bottle of wine in hand. "Hahaha, Alice~"

"Stop. You stay away from me too." Alice’s expression was serious as she shook her fist.

"Hehehe, got it, got it~" Hobbes staggered back a step, worried he’d receive the same treatment as Arnold. "It’s been so long since you left, Alice. I’ve already seen your outstanding performance in France on the screen. You’re a celebrity now. Many people are saying you’re Rexham’s biggest star."

"Oh..." Alice, overwhelmed by the strong smell of alcohol, had no desire to talk to Hobbes and was nearly knocked out by the fumes.

"Huh?" Hobbes noticed the child next to Alice. He bent down and stared at him. "Who’s this little brat?"

"...He’s Merlin’s nephew. I need to look after him for a while." Alice said nervously.

"Hello, Uncle!" Little Merlin, to keep up the lie, forced himself to act like a child, blinking his bright, innocent Kajiran eyes.

"Yo~, so well-behaved. If you hadn’t said, I wouldn’t have noticed. This kid’s eyes really look like Merlin’s. He’s definitely from the same family." Hobbes, drunk, pinched little Merlin’s cheek without restraint.

Little Merlin’s face darkened. His face was being deformed by Hobbes’ grip. *Damn it! You old drunk! Now you even dare to pinch my face?! Unforgivable!*

Unable to keep up the act any longer, little Merlin furiously pried open Hobbes’ calloused hand, baring his little fangs and snarling fiercely.

"Don’t touch me! You old drunk! I’ll hit you!"

"Oi, oi?" Hobbes froze, bewildered. "What a fiery temper..."

"...Just like Merlin, huh?"

title: Chapter 10 — Return to the Adventurers Guild
content:
Chapter 10 — Return to the Adventurers Guild

Volume 21 · Chapter 10

Little Merlin gnashed his teeth and glaringly stared at Hobbs, the old drunk.

However, since Little Merlin was too small, barely reaching Hobbs' knees, he had absolutely no threatening presence.

"He's just a kid, but has such a temper..." Hobbs wanted to reach out and pat Little Merlin's head, but was afraid of getting bitten.

Alice's face looked strange; she imagined Merlin's psychological shadow area must be huge right now? He had been completely stunned by Hobbs treating him like a brat.

"Alice?!" Lucia saw Alice return and hurriedly put down her work to run over.

"Ah... good... not..." Alice forced a smile, finally seeing something normal.

"Did you really shatter a giant celestial body in France not long ago? I saw a special interview about you on the magic TV! Super handsome!" Lucia asked excitedly, feeling Alice had taken an extraordinary trip.

Alice felt awkward, not knowing how to answer.

"How did you manage that? Has your strength gotten stronger recently?" Lucia blinked her large eyes, full of curiosity.

"......" Alice's smile stiffened, feeling pressured by the rapid-fire questioning.

"Did you see the little princess of France? I heard her beauty has obsessed many nobles. Is she really that pretty?" Lucia asked like a curious child, asking question after question.

Alice frowned, thinking: That wasn't me, it was Merlin! But even if I said it, they'd hardly believe me, right?

"Although many dangerous things happened, overall there weren't any major problems."

"Then..."

"You ask so many questions! Alice is tired from traveling, she needs rest. Don't act like a census guard, asking question after question..."

Lucia had intended to keep pressing, but was shut down by Hobbs, the old drunk.

"What's it to you? Alice and I are good friends~" Lucia gave Hobbs a side-eye. "Fine, I won't pry further. But Alice, you're famous now. Don't judge people by their wealth in the future~"

"What are you talking about..." Alice's forehead dripped a cold sweat, thinking: Is he afraid I'll leave without saying goodbye?

"Hmm?!" Lucia noticed Little Merlin, looked down and asked, "This child... who is he?"

"Ah... oh! He's Merlin's nephew. I need to help take care of him for a while..." Alice smiled.

"Really? Looks so cute..." Lucia bent her body down, her cleavage barely hidden, the deep cleavage seemed able to suck the soul out of a human. She pinched Little Merlin's cheek, thinking this brat had smooth, tender skin and was adorable.

"...Don't..." Little Merlin showed displeasure, thinking: Damn! Why does she want to pinch my cheek, it's almost swollen! But... Lucia's figure is amazing! Her chest is unexpectedly well-endowed...

"Merlin-sama's nephew, looks like he's somewhat similar to him..." Lucia picked up Little Merlin, hugging him and stroking him. "Hurry, call me sister."

......Little Merlin's face turned red. His head was pressed into Lucia's chest, feeling the fullness and softness before him. For a moment he realized that even if he was a brat taking advantage, he wouldn't be blamed.

"Tsk tsk tsk!" Hobbs, half-asleep, clicked his tongue repeatedly. "This kid and Merlin are both lecherous. What will happen when they grow up?"

"......" Alice's face changed, quickly snatching Little Merlin away and hugging him to her chest, acting like she was protecting her son. "You old drunk, what nonsense are you talking about? How could you have such dirty thoughts?"

"Can't say that? I've seen this since they were young. My eyes have never failed me." Hobbs pointed at himself. Though his eyes were bleary from wine, they still gleamed.

Alice looked down at Little Merlin, thinking: This bastard's heart is still that of an adult demon even as a brat. Looks like she still couldn't let her guard down, deceived by his appearance.

So Alice reached out and slapped Little Merlin's butt, then gave a side-glance warning in a low voice.

"Behave. Don't try to take advantage of others just because you're a brat now."

"Me??" Little Merlin frowned. He had actually been scolded by Alice? This made him very unhappy.

"By the way, where's Merlin-sama? Didn't he come back with you?" Lucia asked curiously.

"Yeah, I was thinking something was missing. Where did Merlin go?" Hobbs touched his stubbly chin and recalled. "To be honest, this guy still owes me a lot of bar tabs..."

"Mmmmm..." Little Merlin lowered his head, thinking: Hobbs is really stingy, still remembering I owe him money. Looks like becoming a brat isn't so bad either? At least I won't get chased for debt. Hehe, unexpected freedom~

....He had things back home, wouldn't be returning recently. Alice spoke with hesitation. She who never lied had to grit her teeth and help Merlin cover.

"Yo~ Living alone? Can you withstand loneliness?" Hobbs glanced at Arnold, who was unconscious against the corner wall. "The landlord's silly son might have a chance to steal the wife?"

"You want to die?" Alice frowned, thinking Hobbs was mouthy. Was she that kind of person who loved every person she saw?

"I see..." Lucia nodded, understanding the situation, and asked, "Then you didn't go home first, but returned to the guild for a reason?"

"That's right, this..."

Alice took out Ralph's mithril adventurer's proof. Everything spoke for itself.

"......" Lucia looked carefully, then her expression froze.

Ralph was also a core adventurer in the guild. Bringing back an adventurer's proof could only mean one thing...

This man was dead.

In the guild room, Mr. Carl tightly held Ralph's adventurer's proof, his expression very low. He was silent for a long time.

"I didn't expect my old friend disappeared for so long, only to be dead."

"Ralph-senpai was caught in mysterious seas during a mission, unable to escape. Such things... are unavoidable. I hope Mr. Carl can find solace."

Alice said seriously, knowing a bit about Carl and Ralph. The two were trusting partners who had together shouldered the entire Rexham guild, with a deep bond.

For Ralph's sudden death, Carl felt very depressed inside. This meant he had lost a trustworthy friend.

Carl lowered his head and asked in a deep voice, "How did he die?"

Alice glanced at Little Merlin beside her, who said nothing, then raised her expression and said seriously...

"Ralph-senpai was surrounded by monsters in the sea and fought bravely until the very end, dying in battle."

"......"

"A hero."

The worst part is I also lost my phone. I had no data to post an update, could only return to the hotel.

But after I go back, I still have to find time for a hospital checkup. I'm only 25, I don't want to die.

title: Chapter 10 — Fellow Townspeople
content:
Chapter 10 — Fellow Townspeople

Volume 21 · Chapter 10

"Fought bravely to the very end..." Carl frowned, tightly holding Ralph's adventurer's certificate. "I thought this guy who always compromised would do everything possible to survive, but I never expected him to become so brave in the end?"

"Yes, Ralph-senpai... He gave it his all, but the enemies in the Mystic Sea truly... exceeded many people's expectations."

Alice narrated these dramatically; these were all things Merlin said.

However, the real Ralph did whatever it took to survive, even selling information to terrifying monsters, which was already considered a complete betrayal of his human identity.

But Merlin felt Ralph was also helpless, and decided to protect this pitiful man's last dignity.

"We adventurers are like this—a group of people who stick their necks out for a living. For that pitifully humble freedom, we're willing to shatter our bodies. Many who were drinking yesterday could disappear today. How foolish..." Carl looked at Ralph's adventurer's certificate in his hand, his emotions having hit rock bottom.

"Carl, please don't be sad. Ralph-senpai's death was just an accident." Alice emphasized seriously.

"I'm not sad, just feeling very regretful." Carl paused and said in a low voice, "When the guild was at its lowest, Ralph and I fought side by side, resisting enormous pressure to pull the guild out of the mud. But the result is that he left first—I'll never see that man who fought beside me again."

Little Merlin hid behind Alice, listening to Carl's sentiments, thinking to himself that killing Ralph was also a matter of necessity. The other party wanted to use the Chaos King's power to escape the Mystic Sea, blocking his advance, and he didn't have many choices either.

"Alice, I know you've shown brilliantly in France. I should have congratulated you, congratulations on becoming the hottest adventurer recently. But..." Carl lowered his head, gazing at Ralph's remains, "I'm feeling a bit tired now. Let me be alone for a while, okay?"

Alice held little Merlin and walked out; she could see that Carl was very depressed after learning of Ralph's death, with no desire to chat with anyone.

Alice, holding a child as big as little Merlin, could just pretend not to see?

Merlin not returning yet—she forgot to ask about such a strange thing?

It was clear how terrible Carl's mood was; besides accepting the reality of his dear friend's death, there seemed to be no other way.

Lucy sent Alice and little Merlin out of the guild, then said in a low voice—

"Alice, I hope you don't mind my father's coldness. He's someone who cherishes feelings deeply. Uncle Ralph's death hit him hard; even I found it hard to believe."

Alice held the silent little Merlin and nodded, "It's okay. I understand Carl's feelings. If my dear friend died, I'd be devastated too."

"I still remember when I was little, Uncle Ralph held me and said I was lucky to look like Mom, otherwise I'd definitely be ugly." Lucy stood there, showing a wry smile. "My father was so angry he fought with him. Now thinking about it, it feels like yesterday."

"That... Alice wanted to offer comfort, but was suddenly interrupted."

"If you want to comfort me, save it. I've been the guild's poster girl since I was very young, watching one familiar face after another leave. What can I say? I'm numb now." Lucy paused and added, "Uncle Ralph was my father's most trusted partner. His sudden death is truly a heavy blow, but I believe it's temporary. Father isn't the type to be obsessed with the past."

"Then...". Alice felt slightly relieved.

"Alice, promise me you'll live well and stop pushing yourself so hard. I don't want to hear about your death someday." Lucy's eyes suddenly turned serious.

"No, why do you say that?" Alice felt pressured.

"Your progress is visible to the naked eye, and now you're even slightly surpassing my father. You'll face more pressure and challenges. If you're not careful... you might follow in Uncle Ralph's footsteps." Lucy warned seriously.

A drop of cold sweat rolled down Alice's forehead. She forced a smile and said, "Don't worry, I've always been very careful."

"That's good. It's late already. Go rest early." Lucy bent down and looked at little Merlin, "Little brother, if you have time, come play with me sometime."

"Meow!" Little Merlin shrank back; he didn't like being treated like a toy.

"...Lucy's expression became awkward. She thought, 'What a damn brat.'"

"Then we'll leave first." Alice let out a dry laugh, holding little Merlin as she left, and asked in a low voice, "Merlin, did you have to kill Ralph? Did you have other thoughts at the time?"

Held in Alice's arms, little Merlin frowned and wiggled his two short legs. "That guy wanted to use the monsters' power to escape the Mystic Sea, while I had to kill the monster leader. At that time, it was either you die or I die—no room for compromise."

"I see..." Alice fell silent, thinking that Merlin had also深入 the Mystic Sea to save her. Whatever he did, she had no right to blame him. It was just that Ralph's death made her feel guilty.

"Of course, I gave him a chance, but he didn't cherish it. Relying on others means being used by others." Little Merlin crossed his arms and said in an old-man tone, "Besides, this pitiful guy sold his hometown to monsters just to survive. Not revealing the truth and exposing this human traitor was already being benevolent and righteous enough..."

Alice fell silent, recalling Carl's depressed mood. If he knew his friend had long become a monster's lapdog, he'd probably feel humiliated, right?

"Alice!" Lucy suddenly called out, as if there was something important.

Alice held little Merlin and stopped, turning around. "Lucy, what is it?"

"I almost forgot! A few days ago, a very strange person came looking for Mr. Merlin, saying he was Merlin's fellow townsman. I told him you were out on a mission, but he insisted on waiting for you..." Lucy recalled.

"Merlin..." Alice showed a puzzled expression, instinctively looking at little Merlin in her arms.

"..." Little Merlin frowned tightly, trembling with fear, thinking—

Fellow townsman? Could it be a demon from the Death Swamp?

Damn! What happened with Ophelia before...

Sure enough, it exposed me now?

I just got off the plane. Things have been relatively stable these past two days. I'll add more tomorrow. Recently I'll prepare some activities for everyone.

title: Chapter 11 — Subordinates
content:
Chapter 11 — Subordinates

Volume 21 · Chapter 11

In front of Merlin and Alice's home, a burly man sat on the ground, his forehead nearly touching the doorframe.

The suddenly appearing strong man attracted attention; everyone pointed at this unexpected guest.

The man's image was too imposing; many townsfolk of Lexem thought he was a soldier or knight.

The white-haired landlady, learning there was a suspicious person in her house, came out of curiosity to look.

However, seeing the man had sat for three days without water or food and hadn't done anything bad, she relaxed slightly—maybe he just had business with Alice and Merlin and meant no harm.

The landlady brought a bowl of water and bread, placing them before the man. "Have something to eat? They should be back soon. Going three days without food is a problem."

The man on the ground bowed deeply. "Thank you, madam, but three days without food is nothing for me. I need to focus on waiting for Lord Merlin to return."

".... The landlady, seeing his persistence, didn't push further. "Alright, if you can, rest at my place. As a guest from afar, you deserve proper hospitality."

"You're such a kind human. In all this time out, I've never met someone so hospitable. But I have an important mission and can't leave easily. I need to see Lord Merlin immediately." The man politely declined the landlady's kindness.

"Then I won't insist. The food is here; eat when you're hungry." The landlady turned and left slowly, thinking whether he was a fellow townsman of Mr. Merlin. He seemed to have something very important.

She thought he was a man of principle, but once she walked away, he grabbed the bread and wolfed it down. Looks like three days of hunger had taken quite a toll on him.

The landlady smiled knowingly and left with peace of mind. After a few steps, she saw Alice and young Merlin walking toward her.

"Landlady, long time no see!" Alice waved. "We're back. We'll pay the rent right away."

"That doesn't matter. Someone wanted to see Mr. Merlin and has been sitting at the door for three days..." The landlady looked around but didn't see Merlin. "Mr. Merlin? Didn't he come back with you?"

Young Merlin frowned slightly. He had waited three days—this was the rhythm of someone who couldn't afford to miss seeing him. He felt things were getting complicated.

"This... something came up and I couldn't return yet..." Alice covered.

"That's troublesome. That person seems to have something urgent..." The landlady looked at young Merlin in Alice's arms and asked differently,

"Who is this?"

"Ah... he's Merlin's little nephew. I'll take care of him for a while." Alice explained with a dry laugh.

"Oh? So he's Mr. Merlin's nephew. Come to think of it, he has similar eyes. Such a cute child..." The landlady patted young Merlin's head, looking very doting.

"Let's go check on that person first. We'll talk about the rent later."

When Alice and young Merlin squeezed through the crowd and approached the man from behind, they happened to see him wolfing down bread. He looked somewhat disheveled.

"Merlin, do you know him?" Alice asked quietly, setting young Merlin down.

"That build... no way?" Young Merlin frowned, his face darkening. His intuition told him this guy was his subordinate.

Merlin was the master of the First Demon Lord Palace, commanding seven Demon Lord Legions. Their leaders were called Grand Generals—essentially trusted confidants.

Head maid Ophelia and Merlin's sister Lilith were among the seven generals, along with five others.

As for the demon before him, Merlin deduced he was the strongest of the seven generals, known for his ferocious strength—Blackman.

Blackman was simple-minded among the seven generals. He had no close relationship with Merlin, but he was obedient and believed Merlin's words implicitly—a good-natured old soul in the First Demon Lord Palace.

Blackman seemed to sense the gaze behind him, turned to look at Alice, then lowered his eyes to look at young Merlin, whose height didn't reach his chest.

"Eh, it's really you? How did you end up here?" Black lines slid down young Merlin's forehead as he gripped his head in disbelief.

"Who is this man?" Alice asked curiously.

"Blackman, one of my subordinates." Young Merlin paused. "This person is intersex. Calling him 'man' isn't entirely accurate."

"Ah?! ... Intersex?!" Alice was startled, looking at Blackman with a strange expression.

"Yeah, he's different in battle than in normal times. I suggest you prepare yourself." Young Merlin said quietly, afraid Alice would see something unexpected.

"...Merlin-sama?!" Blackman had seen Merlin as a child. The moment he saw young Merlin, he felt a sense of familiarity. Thinking carefully, wasn't this the Demon Lord he had been searching for bitterly?!

"...." Young Merlin felt Blackman had found him, so there was no point hiding. He nodded. "Long time no see, Blackman. How is the Demon Lord Palace?"

Blackman's mouth fell open in shock. Half-chewed bread flew out as he immediately gave Merlin a bear hug, crying, "Your Majesty! I missed you so much! Do you know how hard the journey was? Don't you care about me at all?!"

"Crack!" Young Merlin, hugged by Blackman, felt his bones being crushed. He kept rolling his eyes upward.

Young Merlin no longer had his former powerful body. Being hugged by someone so strong caused him considerable pain.

"I'm dying! I'm dying! I'm dying!"

Alice thought Blackman was attacking the master and drew her short sword from her waist. The chilling cold caused frost to crystallize around them.

"Let go of Merlin, you bastard!"

In the room, young Merlin lay weak against the sofa, on the verge of collapse, looking at the ceiling with utter despair.

If Alice hadn't stopped him in time, Merlin the Great Demon Lord might have been hugged to death by his subordinate—a scandalous end.

Young Merlin was full of resentment. Even the lackeys who used to follow him could now hurt him. How embarrassing!

Blackman knelt on the ground, a swollen lump on his head from Alice's hammer, glowing red with pain.

Blackman crawled on the ground, prostrating himself fully. He said in a muffled voice—

"I'm so sorry, Your Majesty!"

"I was just so happy to see you. I didn't expect it to turn out like this?"

title: Chapter 12 — Underground Blood Pool
content:
Chapter 12 — Underground Blood Pool

Volume 21 · Chapter 12

Xiao Xiaomei slumped onto the sofa. Having been messed around by this idiot Blake, she had nothing to say, "You get lost..."

...Cold sweat was trickling down Blake's forehead. He embarrassedly explained, "I don't know either, Your Majesty's body is so fragile now. Although you used to come to the lava pools together..."

"...?" Alice had question marks all in her head, unable to imagine what silly operations Merlin had when he was Demon Lord.

"Don't talk, I'm in a bad mood because of you right now. Your burly build, if you use a bit of force to hug someone, their bones will be crushed. I almost got choked to death by you, you know?" Xiaomei said with a hopeless expression.

"I was wrong. I just haven't seen Your Majesty for a long time, so my brain suddenly went... Blake knelt on the ground, respectfully asking, "By the way, why did Your Majesty suddenly become a childlike appearance? If I hadn't seen you grow up, I probably wouldn't recognize you."

"This... it's a long story. I apparently ate some kind of medicine, temporarily becoming this form..." Xiaomei hesitated to speak, feeling that too many things had happened recently, making it hard to explain the situation clearly in a few words.

"But Your Majesty in this state is clearly unbeatable by anyone, right? I bet encountering many dangers outside." Blake hesitated to say.

"You know it all without me saying it, don't you? Look, I'm being very low-key now." Xiaomei sighed, thinking that for this period of having become a child, she could probably only tuck her tail and be a person.

"In the subordinate's opinion, Her Majesty is in a very dangerous period. Some elite soldiers and strong warriors from the Demon Lord Palace should be dispatched to ensure Her Majesty's absolute safety." Blake said with a serious tone.

...Factory nonsense...

...This... Xiaomei hesitated, feeling that since returning to childhood, there's no threat of the heart curse anymore. The Demon Lord Palace is indeed much safer than outside.

Alice raised her elegant eyebrows, looking at the demon named Blake in front of him, who appeared very simple-minded, but the huge horns on his forehead fully demonstrated his high-ranking demon identity.

Fortunately, Blake knew how to hide his demon identity, using a wide cloak to cover his appearance. Otherwise, those two huge horns would have caused chaos in a small town like Rekham.

Hearing Blake's urge to rush more demons, from Alice's human standpoint, she could never agree. Moreover, at this time, Merlin's subordinates might not many be her opponents.

"No, having me beside Merlin is enough. I don't need other demons to protect him. Having me here, no one will harm him. Besides, you aren't my opponent. Calling more helpers, what use is it?"

"... Xiaomei seems to have objections.

"What? You have any other opinions? I'm much more reliable than your chaotic subordinates, right?" Alice raised her eyebrows, she didn't want her home to become a demon stronghold.

"... Xiaomei flowed with cold sweat, thinking damn it! Alice has already started controlling her freedom! This isn't a good sign, wouldn't it become a real wife-dominated husband? Factory small pit

"Do not interfere in our demon race's affairs, after all, you are just a human." Blake's expression turned serious.

"Just a human?" Alice's eyes shone with gold, dragon might surged, "Your high-and-mighty tone is when speaking to me."

......... Blake shivered, lowering his head. He was just a Saint-tier powerhouse. Just now outside, he got hammered by Alice one punch, and now the lump on his forehead still aches faintly. The strength gap was very obvious. Even if he wanted to be tough, it wasn't very possible.

"Hmph, be honest in front of me, otherwise I'll blast you out." Alice coldly hummed, having already stepped into the threshold of the sect realm, she completely had the capability to press Merlin's subordinates to the ground and rub them.

The great Demon Lord and his elite subordinates, under Alice's hand, all fell silent, like two naughty children who made mistakes.

"Cough cough!" Xiaomei, to cover his own embarrassment, turned the topic, "That Blake... why did you suddenly come find me if you didn't guard well in the Demon Lord Palace?"

"Olivia that big mouth has already told Lilith about your mischief outside, and marrying a human..." Blake said leisurely.

"Tch! So it was Olivia's small report after all?" Xiaomei wiped his forehead, feeling his peaceful life was running out.

Alice was silent, thinking why the Demon Lord Palace side couldn't accept reality? Herself and Merlin reacted so much, and specially sent people to confirm.

"Lilith and Olivia have already exploded on the spot, almost going crazy. Now the entire Demon Lord Palace is in chaos..."

Blake sighed, recalling that day's scene, still feeling very scary...

More than a month ago, the Demon Lord Palace was still in a calm state.

After Lilith, because her brother Merlin was fired by the parliament, temporarily became the proxy arrogant Demon Lord, controlling the big and small matters of the First Demon Lord Palace.

Because the Demon Lord Lord has a dangerous blood pool seal, related to the life and death of the entire demon race, it needs to be maintained regularly with royal blood.

This led Lilith, no matter how much she missed this brother Merlin, could not easily leave the Demon Lord Palace. Not knowing Merlin's whereabouts, leaving too long would cause the blood pool seal to collapse.

In the dim underground corridor, torches flickered with dim light. Blake followed Lilith, escorting her to the blood pool to maintain the seal.

"Your Highness, you look a bit fatigued, seems to need more rest." Blake suggested.

"No, if I slack off a bit, the blood pool seal will have problems. The seven Demon Lord Palaces' blood pools together form a huge seal. If any one has a problem, it will be a catastrophic disaster." Lilith walked silently in front, lowing, "Before such things were always handled by my brother, suddenly having to do it myself, didn't expect the pressure to be so large.

"If the First Demon Lord Palace still can't find a new monarch, the parliament might make an exception to summon the Majesty back. You don't need to worry, we won't acknowledge any demon other than Merlin as the owner of the Demon Lord Palace." Blake said seriously.

"I hope so..." Lilith said with deep meaning, she knew Merlin's leaving wasn't because the parliament fired him, but because of his own heart curse. Continuing to stay in the Demon Lord Palace would only be waiting to die. It's better to leave his hometown and go outside to seek a way to lift the curse. Who knows, after so long, maybe he has gained something. Then he can be together with his brother forever.

The two came to the underground depths. Here, a giant dragon was lying, radiating light and sacred aura. Unfortunately, it had no wings.

This holy dragon, whose wings were personally cut off by Merlin, the Temple's Holy Dragon Avis, was here serving as the guard for the blood pool seal.

The slumbering Holy Dragon sensed the arrival of demons, lifted its proud head, looking down at Lilith and Blake...

"Another group of magic race old..."

title: Chapter 13 — Location Exposed (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 13 — Location Exposed (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 21 · Chapter 13

"You're talking about who? A big lizard who's fallen to being a loser dog, Wangcai?" Lilith's face looked terrible, staring at the Holy Dragon Avis without fear.

"Despicable demon, slandering the great dragon race will cost you..." Holy Dragon Avis bared his fangs, wanting to intimidate Lilith. Even if he had fallen to guarding the door now, he still wanted to maintain his dignity.

"Avis, watch your words. Lilith is the proxy Demon Lord, and disrespect will be punished!" Blackman's tone was serious, as if ready to defend Lilith and lecture the giant reptile.

"You want to teach me a lesson? Don't overestimate your strength. When I used to soar above the Roman temple, I wouldn't even look at you demons!" Holy Dragon Avis trembled his claws.

"Hmph, big temper. If you're just a dog we keep, what qualification do you have to talk about your past glory? Can't you face reality and recognize your situation?" Lilith showed a mocking smile. "If not for my brother thinking you still had some use, it wouldn't have been as simple as cutting off your wings. You probably would have died with those reckless knights who came to hunt you..."

"Shut up!" Holy Dragon Avis roared, feeling insulted.

The fierce dragon aura made Blackman feel significant pressure. Even if Holy Dragon Avis was now a prisoner of the demon race, a dead camel is still bigger than a horse.

Looking at Lilith, her frail body stood firm in the dragon aura storm, pink hair fluttering, seemingly not afraid of the powerful dragon aura at all.

"So you're furious because I hit the nail on the head? Such a glass heart, Avis..."

"Close your mouth!" Holy Dragon Avis's eyes seemed to spit fire, roaring, "What are you? Just a counterfeit demon, relying on your brother's power to bully others here. You're just a clown!"

"Hehe, everything brother has is mine, and you are also my defeated subordinate!" Lilith breathed roughly, knitting her brows, constantly stimulating the dragon's pitiful pride.

"What did you say!?" Holy Dragon Avis snarled in anger, the chains behind him ringing loudly. "I was defeated by the third-generation arrogant king. Though I submitted to his strength, I won't easily lose to clowns like you! You have no qualification to trample on my dignity!"

Seeing the chains that seemed about to be broken by Holy Dragon Avis, Lilith turned away with a blank face. "Don't bother with this guard dog. Let's go."

"Yes." Blackman nodded and silently followed behind Lilith.

"Despicable demon. If one day the three kings lose that strange power, I will definitely return all this humiliation to you..." The low roar of Holy Dragon Avis came slowly, then he closed his eyes, recovering his calm.

Lilith didn't turn back, cold sweat slowly flowing from her forehead. She seemed calm on the surface, but her heart was actually panicking. She had just been pretending to be calm...

The Holy Dragon was still not to be messed with?

SE3 /

The dragon aura just released seemed to have recovered much from his injured state. Xiao Wan...

Better not provoke this big lizard. With brother away, no one can restrain him...

In the secret room beneath the First Demon Lord Palace, the bright red blood river surged endlessly, intertwining like underground rivers, connecting somewhere...

The large-scale magic array emitted strange light, forming symbols that others found hard to understand.

Under the Demon Lord Palace, there was actually architecture of such scale. Anyone seeing it would marvel at the godly craftsmanship. That mysterious demon prophet from the ancient times who thought of this method to continue the demon race... must be a brilliant genius!

Like the grand sealing array before them, there were seven in total, all built beneath the Demon Lord Palace, connected to each other, forming an unprecedented sealing array. It was just like strange symbols drawn with the whole world as the blueprint!

On the high platform, Lilith used a knife to cut her wrist, letting blood spray into the air, finally immersing in the surging blood river.

The blood pool seemed stimulated, emitting a strange roaring sound, the surging river becoming even more turbulent.

Suddenly! A giant hand made of blood river water shot out, with imposing momentum, seemingly trying to struggle out of the seal?!

But finally it let out a powerless low roar, collapsing with a crash, splashing up a hundred-foot giant wave! L

Lilith staggered, her body seeming weak. Seeing this, Blackman rushed over to support her. "Your Highness, are you alright? There's no need to push yourself so hard."

"With brother gone, I am the main pillar of the Demon Lord Palace. Absolutely cannot have any problems. This should... bring peace for a while." Lilith took a deep breath, the wound on her wrist slowly healing.

"If His Majesty were here, Your Highness could relax." Blackman said softly, then changed the subject. "Just now someone used a scroll to summon Ophelia. After returning, something seemed to have happened, and she urgently wanted to see you."

"Ophelia-sshi?" Lilith felt something important. Ophelia was their mother's trusted aide, having watched over Merlin and Lilith siblings since childhood, their relationship had always been good.

Just as Lilith hesitated, the head maid Ophelia hurriedly rushed in from outside, immediately bowing deeply.

"Your Highness."

"Ophelia, what are you doing? Don't you know this is a forbidden area, you can't enter without permission?!" Blackman scolded seriously.

"Tsk! Shut up, you bisexual freak. If you dare talk more, I'll tear your mouth open." Ophelia's face was cold, disgusted by Blackman's nonsense.

"...." Blackman swallowed his anger, but Ophelia was very senior, being the trusted aide of the second-generation Demon Lord Vivian, he clearly dared not argue more.

"If it weren't very important, would I rush here to see Lilith-dera?" Ophelia said seriously.

"Ophelia-sshi, what happened? I heard you were just summoned by a scroll?" Lilith asked in surprise.

"Correct. I just made a major discovery and want to report to you." Ophelia looked up, staring into Lilith's eyes.

"What... matter?" Lilith felt a bit of pressure, unusual.

"I discovered the whereabouts of His Majesty." Ophelia said.

"Brother?! Is he okay?!" Lilith suddenly became excited, eagerly asking.

"His Majesty... looks fine now, no problems, just..." Ophelia hesitated to speak.

"What's wrong? Just...?" Lilith's expression became serious.

"It's just that His Majesty is working as an adventurer, not only associating with humans, but also married to a human woman." Ophelia said with a grievance.

"Eh? What are you saying?" Lilith's face stiffened, her soul seemed to receive a fatal blow...

Brother married a human woman?

My brother, who should belong to me, is being flirted with by a fox spirit outside, and he's a lowly human?!
