title: Chapter 14 — Blackman's Misunderstanding
content:
Chapter 14 — Blackman's Misunderstanding

Volume 21 · Chapter 14

"Ah?! Is this for real?! His Majesty is outside... and he actually took a human wife?!" Blackmann gasped in shock, as if he had misheard. In the eyes of demons, humans were nothing more than lowly creatures like livestock—how could any demon possibly marry one?

"It's absolutely true. I saw it with my own eyes just now. His Majesty treats that human woman very well. He even stopped me from killing her. They seem to have been together for a long time already." Ophelia spoke gravely, but behind the scenes, she was already embellishing the story, hoping to provoke Lilith and thus break up Merlin and Alice. Since Merlin refused to listen to her kind advice, perhaps his own sister Lilith wouldn’t ignore it so easily?

Lilith’s face darkened instantly. She lowered her head, her eyes brewing with endless fury. "That good-for-nothing brother of mine, not only did he break our agreement, but he also secretly found himself a human vixen behind my back?!"

"Exactly! We demons have no shortage of beautiful women, yet he was seduced by a despicable human. If it were me, I’d never tolerate it!" Ophelia fanned the flames, hoping Lilith would come up with a way to bring Merlin back.

Lilith’s vision blurred, her slender body swaying unsteadily as if she might faint at any moment.

"Princess Lilith!" Blackmann quickly stepped forward to support her.

"Your Highness, are you alright?" Ophelia asked with feigned concern, wondering if she had pushed too hard—she only wanted to provoke Lilith, not make her pass out from anger.

"I’m so furious I could die!" Lilith rolled her eyes, her heart brimming with resentment. "I’ve been working so hard to manage the Demon Lord Palace, hoping my brother would come back soon, and yet that heartless bastard is out there cavorting with some human vixen?!"

"I bet His Majesty must have been deceived or has some kind of leverage held over him by that human woman. Otherwise, he would never lower himself to be with a human!" Ophelia said with false conviction.

"But with His Majesty’s power, who could possibly have anything on him? That doesn’t seem likely..." Blackmann interjected doubtfully.

"Shut up! No one asked you!" Ophelia shot Blackmann a fierce glare, not wanting this blunt "man" to ruin her plans.

"No! I can’t just sit here and do nothing. I have to bring my brother back. I can’t let him keep gallivanting around out there!" Lilith steeled herself again, though her face still wore a troubled expression. "But... I can’t leave the Demon Lord Palace right now. If I’m not here, there’ll be no one to maintain the Blood Pool Seal."

"Your Highness!" Ophelia had been waiting for this exact moment. She immediately volunteered, "To be honest, I’ve already prepared everything! I can set out for the human kingdom of Britain at any moment to bring His Majesty back directly!"

"Tch! You clearly planned this a long time ago!" Blackmann frowned, unable to stop himself from retorting.

"Sister Ophelia, you’re so eager..." Lilith gave her a strange look, sensing something off.

Ophelia stiffened. In truth, she just wanted to snatch Merlin back for herself, but she would never admit it. "His Majesty is someone I watched grow up. This is his first time leaving home, and he’s already been tricked by a wretched human woman. I absolutely cannot stand by and do nothing!"

Lilith was no fool. She could see right through Ophelia’s little schemes. After all, she had long understood that this "Sister Ophelia" didn’t exactly have *pure* sisterly feelings for her.

Lilith wasn’t stupid enough to set up another rival in love. She wouldn’t easily give Ophelia the chance.

"Sister Ophelia is the chief steward of the Demon Lord Palace. She’s always so busy. I don’t think we should trouble you with this."

"But aside from me, who else can bring His Majesty back?" Ophelia replied with full confidence.

Lilith hesitated for a moment, her gaze flicking to Blackmann beside her. "Then *you* go."

Ophelia’s scheme failed, and she glared at Blackmann in furious frustration, cursing him silently. *Die! Die! Die!*

"Huh? Me?" Blackmann pointed at himself, his eyes lighting up with excitement. "To be honest, I—"

"Calm down. My brother doesn’t like your kind—neither man nor woman. If you make any inappropriate advances, you’ll get chopped up." Lilith’s judgment was precise. Anyone could potentially spark a romance with Merlin, except Blackmann, who was the least likely.

Blackmann’s heart sank, and he even felt a little intimidated.

"This mission is yours. You *must* bring my brother back to see me. Understood..." Lilith paused, her expression suddenly turning vicious. "And kill that shameless human woman who dared to seduce my brother!"

---

Back in their room, after listening to Blackmann’s concise report, the two of them basically understood the situation at the Demon Lord Palace.

"So that’s how it is..." Merlin sat on the sofa, nodding. Lilith was probably so angry her lungs were about to explode. He recalled how, when they parted, she had said she would kill all the vixens who got close to him. Truly a mentally unstable little sister.

Blackmann knelt on the floor, sneaking glances at Alice beside him. The large bump on his forehead throbbed painfully. *Kill this human woman?* That didn’t seem feasible. He couldn’t even beat her in a fight!

It seemed Blackmann hadn’t prepared thoroughly enough. He had assumed, based on Ophelia’s casual words, that this would be an easy task, but Alice’s strength was unexpectedly formidable.

"So, does that mean Princess Lilith wants to bring him back?" Alice recalled her battle with Lilith long ago. The other’s strength was ordinary—nothing to fear.

"...Yes..." Blackmann averted his gaze and muttered, "His Majesty’s... *extracurricular activities* outside have been exposed. If he doesn’t return to handle this, the Demon Lord Palace might descend into chaos."

Alice furrowed her brows, looking as if she wanted to say something but held back. She didn’t want to let Merlin leave, afraid he might never return. "Merlin, what do you think? I’ll be blunt—your condition is terrible right now. You’re not fit to go anywhere dangerous. It’s much safer by my side. Even if you’re usually insufferable, I’ll still reluctantly consider protecting you."

Merlin stayed silent. *Tch. A tiger in decline, bullied by dogs.* Even Alice was speaking to him in that superior tone now.

Returning to the Demon Lord Palace would be safer, but it would also mean losing his freedom. That lunatic Lilith would definitely confine him, treating him like a toy to manipulate.

All things considered, it was better not to go back. After all, he couldn’t even suppress Alice in his current state—let alone deal with his maniacal sister.

"Blackmann, I’m not going back in this state. Go tell Lilith that I’m doing just fine out here. She doesn’t need to worry about me."

Hearing Merlin’s answer, Alice secretly let out a breath of relief and said triumphantly, "See? Merlin doesn’t want to go back. You might as well stop wasting your effort."

Blackmann knit his brows, rubbing his forehead as he pondered the possibilities.

*Why did His Majesty refuse so decisively?*

*Could it be, as Ophelia said...*

*Does His Majesty have some kind of leverage held over him by this human woman?*

*These despicable humans, using underhanded methods to control His Majesty’s thoughts!*

*As His Majesty’s loyal subordinate, I must find a way to save him!*

◆

I read the manga—it was pretty good. At the very least, the plot and paneling were solid. Everyone should go check it out and show some support.

It’s hard to judge the quality of a manga adaptation from just a prologue. I think if it can convey the original story’s plot, then it’s already a successful work.

Earlier, I took a five-hour train ride home and finally ended my offline life, so I’ll talk about recent updates here.

Next month, there will be a monthly vote giveaway. I’ve already privately ordered figures of Merlin and Alice to use as prizes.

Also, starting tomorrow until the end of next month—May 31st—there will be daily 6,000-word updates. This will be a *crunch month*, and the plot will progress quickly. Everyone, stay tuned!

title: Chapter 15 — A Frank Meeting
content:
Chapter 15 — A Frank Meeting

Volume 21 · Chapter 15

Blackman wore a conflicted expression. Princess Lilith had given him a direct order—if he didn’t bring Merlin back, he’d have no way to answer to her. But the human woman before him was far too powerful; if he fought her head-on, he had no chance of winning.

"Your Majesty, you took it upon yourself to marry a human. That violates the demon race’s taboos. I believe you need to return and explain yourself properly."

"This is all a misunderstanding. We didn’t actually get married. You don’t need to make such a big deal out of it." Little Merlin sighed. He hadn’t expected this misunderstanding to cause so much trouble, to the point that even Princess Lilith had found out.

"That’s right, we’re not really married. What exactly are the demons worried about?" Alice said, her expression serious.

Blackman hesitated, his gaze darting between Little Merlin and Alice. *This is obviously a lie, right?* They were so in sync they were even living together—there was no way they could fool Princess Lilith.

"In any case, you’ve come all the way from the Death Swamp. It wasn’t easy, so rest here for a few days. Then you can truthfully report the situation to Lilith. I don’t plan on returning to the demon race for now." Little Merlin paused before continuing, "After all, there are plenty of demons back there who don’t like me. It might even be safer here in the human world."

"Your Majesty, there’s no need to worry. We are all your loyal subordinates. We would stake our lives to protect you. We would never—" Blackman glanced at Alice with a meaningful look. "—be like *that* human woman, radiating such lewd dominance..."

"Who are you talking about?!" Alice knitted her brows and stepped forward. She could feel the strong hostility from Merlin’s demon subordinate!

"Don’t be like this. I’ve already decided. I won’t be returning to the Death Swamp for now, not until my condition recovers." Little Merlin said sternly. He thought to himself that if Alice could already bully him a little, then if that little lunatic Lilith got her hands on him, she might even keep him as a pet. That would be even worse for his freedom. "Alice, is that alright? Let this guy rest at our place for a while. Afterward, I’ll make sure he leaves obediently."

"It’s not that I—" Alice saw that Blackman was still polite, so for Merlin’s sake, she decided to let it slide. "But he must follow human rules. No causing trouble everywhere, or else..."

Blackman saw Alice cracking her knuckles, her eyes filled with an unspoken threat. He couldn’t help but shiver internally. *Did she threaten His Majesty the same way?*

This wouldn’t do. He needed to find an opportunity to rescue His Majesty from this dire situation...

Evening, in the bathroom.

Little Merlin looked at his body in the mirror, occasionally pinching his emaciated frame.

*Was I really this frail as a child?* If I hadn’t grown up under Mother’s protection, I might have been swarmed and devoured by demons long ago.

He had no idea if Circe’s, that old hag’s, antidote was even working. He’d already drunk several bottles, and yet there was no effect at all.

Little Merlin tilted his head back and downed the pitch-black antidote in one gulp, then rolled his eyes and let out a loud burp.

"Burp~ Why does it taste like pig manure? Who knows what that old crone used to make this antidote?"

Little Merlin grumbled nonstop. To finish all the antidotes Circe had prepared, he’d probably need a while.

Now that he’d turned into a child, he had to be extra careful. He couldn’t afford any mishaps at such a critical time.

Little Merlin sighed, wrapped a towel around his lower body, and prepared to leave the bathroom. But the tightly shut door suddenly swung open.

"Huh?! Alice?"

"No, Your Majesty, it’s—" Blackman poked his head in, lurking suspiciously outside the door.

"Oh, it’s you. It’s so late, why aren’t you resting? I don’t like having others around while I bathe." Little Merlin said awkwardly.

"I believe Your Majesty’s current physical condition is poor and requires close protection. Though I am unworthy, I am willing to share your burden." Blackman walked straight in, his clothes already completely removed. The dense, powerful muscles on his body seemed to pulse with every breath. "Let’s bathe together, Your Majesty!"

Little Merlin’s gaze drifted downward, and he saw Blackman’s *massive* thing. His face turned deathly pale, utterly shocked. "Get out! Don’t point your filthy thing at me!"

"Your Majesty, you can’t call it filthy just because you’ve shrunk. I can faintly smell a sour scent..." Blackman said meaningfully.

"Shut up! You shameless bastard!" Little Merlin felt immense pressure. Right now, he wasn’t the Great Demon Lord who could crush heavens and earth. In front of his subordinate Blackman, he truly had no power to resist.

"Your Majesty need not worry. Are you afraid of eavesdroppers? It’s just you and me here. I just saw that human woman return to her room. Now, all you need to do is tell me your true thoughts, and I can immediately take you away from this dire situation. Even if I can’t beat that woman, slipping away won’t be a problem." Blackman patted his chest.

"Which eye of yours sees me living in dire straits? I *really* don’t want to return to the Demon Lord Palace! That neurotic Lilith would take advantage of my weakened state and treat me like a toy. Who knows what disgusting desires she’d satisfy? And don’t even get me started on that pervert Ophelia lurking nearby, waiting for her chance!" Little Merlin had an unusually clear understanding of his situation. Returning wouldn’t necessarily be better than staying with Alice.

"Your Majesty, we are all your loyal subordinates. Why do you speak of us as if we were vicious enemies?" Blackman asked, confused.

"Loyal subordinates my ass! You’re all just waiting for me to be weak so you can control me! Especially the women in the Demon Lord Palace! Including you!" Little Merlin pressed himself against the corner, trembling. He was terrified that this neither-man-nor-woman Blackman had some *unusual* preferences.

Blackman hesitated for a moment before asking tentatively, "Does Your Majesty find my male body too aggressive? Is that why you can’t communicate with me calmly?"

"...What are you planning to do? Don’t act recklessly, or I’ll scream." Little Merlin’s face darkened. He felt something was very wrong. He had realized long ago that Blackman’s sexual orientation was a bit... *off*.

If he remembered correctly, Blackman appeared honest and simple on the outside, but his mind was filthy. He had a peculiar taste for handsome young men.

Back when Merlin had been the Demon Lord, Blackman had served as his personal guard. As a result, his entire personal guard had become *extremely* gay, and their relationships had turned bizarrely complicated!

After all that, it turned out this seemingly honest Blackman had treated the young demons in Merlin’s personal guard as his own personal harem! Who knew what he’d done!

"Hehehe, I mean no harm. Come to think of it, Your Majesty, it’s been a long time since you’ve seen my female form. Such a candid moment is truly rare..." Blackman grinned innocently, gripping his *massive* thing with both hands—

Then, with a sudden *yank*!

A brilliant white light, as radiant as a magical girl’s, burst forth!

---

I caught a cold and fever. I didn’t expect a trip to the south to be so full of hardships.

I’ve been taking medicine for a day, but the fever still hasn’t broken. I plan to go to the hospital for an injection tomorrow.

Hopefully, I’ll recover soon and can start adding more chapters.

title: Chapter 16 — A Beautiful Girl in the Bath (With Bonus Extra Content)
content:
Chapter 16 — A Beautiful Girl in the Bath (With Bonus Extra Content)

Volume 21 · Chapter 16

Blackman's expression shifted abruptly amid the dazzling brilliance, and in an instant his entire appearance and gender transformed.

The hulking, oversized brute became a woman with a toned, slender figure overflowing with youthful vitality.

Her form was perfectly curvaceous, her skin as delicate as if it could be burst by a touch, seeming to radiate a luminous sheen. Long sky-blue hair was tied back in a ponytail, and a large pink butterfly bow revealed a playful charm.

It was hard to reconcile such a beautiful maiden's image with the fierce warrior over two meters tall from moments before — it was as though he had become an entirely different person of a different gender.

Little Merlin's face went pale. Overwhelmed by the person before him, he could barely breathe. He had witnessed the entire process of Blackman removing his own member and transforming into a beautiful girl!

Though Merlin had not seen Blackman's unique ability for the first time, he was still shocked every single time, his mind going completely blank.

Just moments ago, he was a burly man sporting a massive member, but now — suddenly — there was just an empty little girl instead.

"...You...!"

"How is it? Your Majesty, are you satisfied now? If I'm in a female form, I probably won't seem quite so intimidating, right?"

Blackman spoke with firm, forceful tones, swinging the massive iron hammer that had been transformed from his former member, standing in a bold, wide-legged stance in the bathroom.

It seemed that even with her body transformed into a beautiful woman, her personality was still that of a粗犷 man — her sexual orientation was just a bit... off.

Although Blackman's ability was rather vulgar — plucking out his own member and turning it into a weapon, while also changing his gender — his strength was still not something to be underestimated.

This pitch-black great hammer, forged from that member, weighed three tons. A grazing touch would injure, a solid hit would kill. Up close it could shatter mountains and tear apart the earth; from afar it could overturn rivers and seas.

Its design was ancient and primitive, the hammerhead shaped like a ferocious demon's skull. It seemed as though some kind of restriction sealed upon it, tendrils of electric light crawling across its surface.

That Blackman could lift a three-ton warhammer with her maiden body showed her strength was far beyond ordinary — enough to make even typical powerful warriors step back in trepidation.

"Come on, Your Majesty. At a time like this, there's no need to be shy, is there? Without that human woman watching over us, we can discuss some more private matters. Do you wish to return to the Demon Lord Palace or not? I can assist you in escaping from here!"

Hearing Blackman's pleasant yet slightly rough and bizarre voice, little Merlin's eyes rolled back into his head. What made matters even worse was that the other party was completely naked, looking like a female exhibitionist running wild on the street. "Don't come any closer! ! !"

Blackman furrowed her slender eyebrows, wondering if she hadn't already done enough. Why did His Majesty still guard against her so heavily? Could there be some secret behind it?

Simple-minded Blackman couldn't fathom that Merlin was merely someone who simply disliked having a gender-swapped powerhouse getting too close to him — not to mention the rumors about Blackman's own sexual orientation.

After pondering for a moment without finding an answer, Blackman's old face flushed red, and she exhaled hot breath through her nostrils.

"Your Majesty must simply be someone who hasn't seen my beautiful form in a long time, which is why you're so shy you can't speak. Let us have some intimate contact — it will surely dispel your prejudices!"

"Are you deaf or what?! Can you actually hear what people are saying?! It's not what you think!" Little Merlin shrank against the wall, feeling as though he were being targeted by a tigress so desperate for release that she'd sit and suck the earth dry — he felt like he would suffocate under the relentless assault!

"Your Majesty! I'm coming! Let us perform our long-overdue ritual of friendship!" Blackman's pretty face turned wicked, and like a famished tiger pouncing on its prey, she threw herself onto little Merlin, pinning him to the bathroom floor.

"Don't, don't, don't! Stop messing around, you... are you trying to rebel?!" Little Merlin's eyes widened in terror. His hands were restrained by Blackman and he couldn't move at all, but he still didn't forget to use his noble status to intimidate this subordinate who was daring to defy his superior!

"At a time like this, why are you still being so fake-principled? Those handsome demons in your personal guard — I've already tasted them all~"

Blackman's expression gradually grew more unrestrained. Even wearing a maiden's face, she still managed to send chills down one's spine — her grinning mouth and demonic horns looked as though an insatiable devil had stepped out of a painting.

"Indeed... Ah!" Little Merlin's face contorted in horror. Just as he was about to rebuke Blackman, he was smothered by two soft mounds, instantly experiencing that familiar sensation of suffocation!

"Hehehe, although I greatly enjoy Your Majesty's youthful and vigorous body, even in a young boy's form, it still holds a different kind of charm~" A pink tint flashed in Blackman's eyes as desire slowly took over her mind. She rubbed herself against Merlin's body, completely bare.

"...Ngh ngh!"

Little Merlin struggled fruitlessly. Blackman's female body felt like a vast, rolling ocean, steadily dissolving his consciousness. The suffocating sensation repeatedly surged to the top of his skull.

It proved once again that breasts that were far too large were not necessarily a good thing — they could become the most fatal of weapons, smothering a person to death!

Feeling that a great disaster was upon him, little Merlin began to hope for Alice's appearance. At the very least, she could make this intersex demon stay away from him.

With a loud crash, the tightly shut bathroom door was forcibly kicked open.

Alice had sensed something wrong at home — Merlin and his retinue had vanished — causing her heart to tighten. She wondered if they had secretly escaped back to the Demon Lord Palace.

Suddenly, she had heard strange sounds coming from the bathroom, as though some wanton woman were laughing wildly, which only made one's imagination run wild.

In a fit of rage, Alice kicked open the bathroom door and saw the naked, feminized Blackman shamelessly pinning down little Merlin and rubbing against him.

The obscene and shameful scene, the unbearable-to-watch actions, and the two's unfathomable positions — every detail was triggering Alice's sensitive nerves.

Her face turned completely black in an instant. Fury burned within her chest, and the cold aura mixed with dragon might slowly began to spill outward. It seemed as though a river of blood would flow the next second.

"What in the world are you two doing in here?!"

"We..." Blackman stood frozen, utterly astonished that Alice would barge in so unexpectedly. She had been so careful!

"This is my home. How can you two be so shameless? By the way, where did you, you vixen, come from?!" Alice's silver hair flew about as she instantly transformed into a witch, looking as though she wanted to slash at anyone who crossed her path.

"I am... I..." Blackman felt explaining was too much trouble. The fact that she was an intersex demon was difficult enough to understand. Under the pressure of a strong survival instinct, she instead hugged little Merlin beneath her tighter. "We are genuinely in love with each other! Don't just stand here like a lightbulb — get lost!"

"Huh?!" Alice's brows knitted together. What nonsense was this random woman spouting?

"Ahhh!" Little Merlin finally managed to pry open a tiny gap and cried out, "Alice, save me! This bastard... ngh!!"

"???" Alice tilted her head, her expression easing slightly. Though she didn't fully understand the situation, Merlin's cry for help meant this wasn't anything underhanded — he was likely being forced down against his will. "I see..."

"Ah... O powerful one of humanity, please listen to me. I am His Majesty's loyal guard. This manner is merely a way of expressing closeness..." Blackman said, cold sweat streaming down her forehead.

"Is this your last words? Very well..." Alice narrowed her eyes, her silent authority radiating. "Cling..." With a sound, she drew her sword from its scabbard.

The narrow bathroom was immediately swept by a fierce cold wind.

Blackman, this intersex demon, was sealed within a coffin of ice...

title: Chapter 17 — Thunder Demon Warhammer (Extra)

Volume 21 · Chapter 17

In the living room, little Merlin collapsed again on the sofa, his small face blankly staring at the ceiling.
He swore that in this life he had never been so fearful of women, as if they were all wolves and tigers, and a slight mistake would send him to an eternal sleep in the gentle countryside.
Thanks to Blackman this damn idiot, Little Merlin increasingly didn't want to return to the Demon Lord's Palace; who knows what bizarre treatment awaits him, powerless as he is, if he goes back?
Blackman was wrapped in a towel, kneeling on the ground shivering nonstop; just rescued from the ice coffin not long ago, the cold had seeped in, frost condensing on his hair and eyebrows.
This bisexual demon pervert once again felt Alice's ferocity; it would probably take several demon generals ganging up on him, as solo combat would be quite difficult.
"Ah-choo!" Blackman suddenly sneezed, breaking the quiet atmosphere; his teeth kept chattering, he even wondered if Alice was a monster from the North Pole.
Alice had already heard the whole story; she felt there were many misunderstandings, but no matter what, she couldn't change the fact that Blackman had sneak-attacked Merlin at night.
Just based on that, Alice was already sufficiently wary of this demon visitor.
I thought he was just a tough subordinate, but he turned out to be bisexual; any feminine aura approaching Merlin should be met with extra caution.
Alice supported the electrified warhammer transformed from Blackman's J-ding; she wasn't sure what this "thing" was, only knowing it was a weapon of the bisexual demon.
o牡」玩

title: Chapter 18 — Rare Temperature
content:
Chapter 18 — Rare Temperature

Volume 21 · Chapter 18

Alice suddenly learned the true form of the Thunder Demon Warhammer and was badly frightened; she no longer dared to touch this weapon that weighed three tons, feeling as if she had touched some filthy, creepy thing.

The Thunder Demon Warhammer descended slowly, looking rather gentle, but the moment it actually hit the ground —

Boom — a huge roar, the earth trembled a few times, like thunder sweeping past.

A large pit was smashed into the middle of the room, and even the roof was blown open with a hole by the shockwave!

All three of them were dumbfounded, looking at the mess at the scene; a perfectly good house had turned into an open-air observation deck.

The weight of the Thunder Demon Warhammer is not to be underestimated; even a light landing causes terrifying destruction.

Because of the huge commotion here, all the stray dogs in Rexxam were startled awake, barking non-stop, provoking a chorus of curses.

"N-no... don't just throw my precious baby on the ground!" Blackman turned pale with fright, hurriedly squatted down to pick up the Thunder Demon Warhammer, rubbing it affectionately without stop.

"This hammer..."

Alice's expression was awkward, a bit hard to voice, and she asked Merlin in a low voice, "What kind of weirdos are you demons anyway?"

"You should know, in every race there are a few idiots... Little Merlin tilted his mouth, suddenly asking with deep meaning, "Hehe, this hammer — it's thick, long, and hard; how does it feel to the touch?"

".... Shut up! Why didn't you tell me this earlier? I just... Alice's face flushed red; she wanted to find a crack in the ground to crawl into, or kill someone to silence them and cover up her dark history.

"Don't overthink it; it's just a weapon, you absolutely have to look at it with a normal mind, otherwise when you get a chance to see Blackman fight, that's when it'll be truly messy — you won't be able to look straight at it... Little Merlin covered his own eyes, adding in a strange tone, "This bastard swings his own big ding-ding, hammering one enemy after another into pulp, holy shit! Eye-searing..."

"...." Alice looked at this hermaphrodite demon before her, really unable to imagine the scene Merlin described, "Don't say anymore."

"Hm?" Blackman slung the Thunder Demon Warhammer on his back, stood up, and asked curiously, the butterfly knot on his single ponytail trembling, "What are you two talking about? Is it about me?"

"No, no, can you put your hammer away? I can't look at it directly anymore..." Alice covered her face, thinking: since the Thunder Demon Warhammer is formed from a ding-ding, doesn't that mean Blackman is shamelessly swinging his big ding-ding in broad daylight!?

"Easy enough."

Blackman twisted his waist, aimed the end of the Thunder Demon Warhammer at his own crotch, and thrust it in hard, "Ah~●"

"Oh ho~" Little Merlin's face was calm, as if long used to the sight, even observing with great interest.

But Alice received quite a shock, feeling Blackman was committing suicide; she hurriedly covered Little Merlin's eyes, "What?! What is this thing? Children shouldn't look at such filthy scenes!"

"Who's a child?!" Little Merlin protested dissatisfied.

Suddenly, electricity crackled, accompanied by Blackman's alluring cries, making one suspect what on earth was happening in the middle of the night.

The light dispersed; Blackman's appearance changed, returning to the look of a simple, burly man. He scratched the back of his head and asked with a bitter smile, "Miss, is this okay now?"

".... Fine." A drop of cold sweat rolled down Alice's forehead; she thought speechlessly, this guy can switch genders at any time, but the process... isn't it a bit too erotic!?

"Phew~" Blackman let out a long breath, thinking this human woman finally stopped making things difficult for him; sure enough, his simpleton appearance is more deceptive~

"Remember not to randomly show your hammer, especially in my house, got it?" Alice admonished, already not wanting to see that shameful thing a second time.

"Rest assured, beautiful miss." Blackman bowed slightly, performing a gentleman's salute toward Alice; after becoming male he looked much more normal.

Alice looked at the wrecked room and sighed, "Made into this state; how do I explain to the landlady tomorrow? We won't be kicked out, will we?"

"Just pay some money; the landlady won't make things difficult for us. Count Austin's reward hasn't been paid yet~" Little Merlin said extremely lightly.

"Don't make it sound so easy; it was your subordinate who caused the trouble, can't even manage your own underlings — what kind of Demon Lord are you?" Alice knitted her brows, unable to hold back a complaint.

"Tsk!" Little Merlin clicked his tongue, poked his own cheek, and acted cute, "I'm a child, I don't know anything~"

"You little..."

Alice looked at Little Merlin gnashing his teeth, thinking: this old bastard Merlin; when it's time to wipe his hands clean and shirk responsibility, he'll obediently admit he's a little brat — too cunning!

"Forget it. I'll personally apologize to the landlady tomorrow, then find craftsmen to repair the house. It's already very late; since you're a child, just behave and go to sleep with me."

"Sleep with you?" Little Merlin's expression was strange, as if full of deep meaning.

"... What's with that look?! I have no other meaning; it's just that I need someone to protect me right now, isn't it safe sleeping next to me?" Alice's face was red as she explained, completely refusing to admit she had ulterior motives; if Merlin really recovered, there probably wouldn't be another chance. "Don't tell me you want to sleep with your own subordinate?"

"...." Little Merlin glanced at Blackman beside him.

"I'm looking forward to it, Your Majesty~" Blackman's muscles twitched all over, as if seducing.

"Pass!" Little Merlin refused with a pale face, afraid Blackman might do something unspeakable to him in the dead of night.

"The moonlight is really..."

Blackman sat on the sofa that originally belonged to Merlin, raised his head through the hole in the roof, and gazed at the night outside —

Damn it, looks like His Majesty is playing around outside, simply doesn't want to return to the Demon Lord Palace with me.

How do I report back now? Can't exactly use force to kidnap His Majesty back, right?

That human woman is hard to deal with; even going all out in a head-on clash, I probably only have a 40% chance of winning...

But His Majesty seems to have a very good relationship with this woman; they can even sleep together — I'm afraid they've already consummated the marriage.

Such an important matter — should I really report it truthfully?

Blackman couldn't sleep for a long time, feeling he must use some method; bringing Merlin back first is the priority.

"Sigh, so difficult..."

However, at this very moment, in Alice's room, Little Merlin was held in Alice's arms, the two embracing in sleep.

Alice had long since settled her mindset, treating Little Merlin like a child to take care of; her heart held none of those messy thoughts.

But Little Merlin was like he'd discovered a new world, squirming non-stop, tense and unable to sleep...

Wow! Alice fell asleep so easily; looks like she really has no ill intentions toward me?

Come to think of it, this is the first time sleeping so openly with Alice; why can she be so calm...

Little Merlin turned on his side, looking at Alice's cute face; her faint breathing puffed over, carrying a hint of lavender scent.

His heart stirred; his old face flushed red. He glanced sideways at Alice's washboard chest, and involuntarily stretched out his demon claws...

Only to see Little Merlin's pair of small hands, "puji," through the thin pajamas, touch that flat expanse of mystery, inexplicably feeling a sense of peace.

In this crisis-ridden world, human hearts are cold and ruthless; only this pair of washboards lets me feel a trace of warmth.

I won't admit it's because it's too flat, so there's no danger of being smothered to death, making it feel very safe...

If Alice found out about this, I'd be ****ed, right?

(lol)

Adjusting status

I went to get an injection today, came back and took a lot of medicine, my head is dizzy, feeling a kind of... out-of-body sensation?

Probably like that. I'll rest for now; if my condition improves tomorrow morning, I'll start updating during the day.

title: Chapter 19 — Stake
content:
Chapter 19 — Stake

Volume 21 · Chapter 19

The night was deep, little Merlin really fell asleep holding Alice's flat chest, without the previous tension and unease.
In fact, Alice hadn't fallen asleep at all; she was completely awake, merely using a calm exterior to hide her inner nervousness.
This was the first time Alice actively slept with Merlin, although she used protecting little Merlin's safety as an excuse, but for her it was already exciting enough.
Normally, Alice would never have the chance to sleep with Merlin; suddenly she thought that Merlin turning into a child wasn't such a bad thing?
Alice's tightly closed eyes narrowed into a slit as she watched Merlin's youthful face, her expression turning inexplicably embarrassed and shy.
Does this guy really have to be touching something to fall asleep? What a strange habit....
Besides, even if his appearance turned into a child, his mindset wouldn't be any different from before, right?
So... what's his motive for taking advantage of me now? Could it just be that the child lacks a sense of security?
This time... I'll let it slide, but not again, hum~!
I'm doing this purely out of concern for a minor, not for any other reason!
In the royal capital of London, Morgan Trading Company's mansion was brightly lit, as if awaiting someone's late-night return.
The adopted son of the Red Beard Pirates, Lochiri, arrived at the gate carrying a large bag of luggage.
The heavy doors slowly creaked open with a squeaky sound, and a bald old man in luxurious silk robes stood inside, hands clasped behind his back.
This old man was the head of the Morgan Trading Company, Mr. Morgan, and standing beside him with a blank expression was the gladiator Brett, humbly bowing his head.
Around them stood guards wearing light armor and weapons, each holding torches that illuminated the mansion as brightly as daylight.
Even in the entire royal capital, places with defenses as tight as Morgan Trading Company's are few, comparable to a simple fortress.
Queen Elizabeth permits such armed forces to exist within the capital also out of respect for Morgan Trading Company's outstanding contributions to the imperial navy.
"Morgan Uncle, long time no see." Lochiri said with a smile.
"Please come in, Young Master Lochiri; I've been waiting for you for a while." Mr. Morgan's cheeks squeezed out a smile, his mouth splitting to reveal a dazzling gold tooth.
Inside the mansion, Lochiri and Mr. Morgan entered the parlor, ordering the guards to tighten surveillance around, not allowing any idle persons to approach; it seemed they intended to discuss some secret matters.
"Young Master Lochiri, I've already taken care of what you asked: I've brought that high-ranking demon away, so you should leave quickly." Mr. Morgan pulled out a handkerchief to wipe his chubby face, seeming to fear something.
"What? You're driving me away? I haven't even put down my luggage, and I haven't had a chance to drink any water." Lochiri tossed his dirty luggage onto the chair, his gaze deep as he looked at Morgan Old Sir, "My fathers were killed by the Sword Master Elgin; now we lowly pirates can't possibly afford to associate with a big shot like you from the merchant guild. It's not like before when you fawned over us..."
"Young Master Lochiri, you can't just say things randomly; didn't we agree? As long as I help you find a living high-ranking demon, we won't bring up the past again, right?" Mr. Morgan frowned, bringing up their recent transaction.
"Hmph, that's right; as long as you get me a living high-ranking demon, I'll pretend that your past act of selling intelligence to our Red Beard Pirates—which caused the British Royal Navy to suffer repeated defeats at sea—never happened. Morgan Uncle, you remain the esteemed merchant guild magnate, a pillar of the empire~" Lochiri's words were laced with sarcasm, though not easily detected.
The Red Beard Pirates were able to sweep the Dalian sea area before, each time escaping unscathed from clashes with the Royal Navy and even gaining some advantages.
This wasn't because the Royal Navy were incompetent, but because this Mr. Morgan, an important figure in imperial warship manufacturing, had sold a lot of intelligence to the Red Beard Pirates.
Although the Red Beard brothers were slain by Sword Master Elgin, their adopted son Lochiri knows all the details, which he can use as leverage to manipulate Mr. Morgan.
If Mr. Morgan's betrayal of the Royal Navy were exposed, it would surely provoke the queen's wrath, and he would lose his head the next day—this is also why he fears Lochiri.
"As long as Young Master Lochiri you keep your promise and don't speak of the past, we remain partners."
"Morgan Uncle, I've had many transactions with your two fathers; I understand the rules—when one is desperate, the most valuable thing is integrity, which my fathers taught me." Lochiri said sincerely.
"With your words, I feel at ease." Mr. Morgan rubbed his hands like a merchant, turned and called outward: "Brett, bring the demon captured from Rexham in, so Young Master Lochiri can have a good look."
The door swung open, and the sturdy Brett entered expressionlessly, carrying Helena, whose hands and feet were bound, on his shoulder.
This poor female demon had shackles sealing her magic and fighting spirit; she now had not a shred of resistance left.
Brett threw Helena from his shoulder onto the carpet, then stood guard behind Mr. Morgan, like a robot.
Helena felt waves of pain throughout her body; she lifted her head and angrily glared at everyone present.
Where is this?
An old fat man, a young man reeking of fish, and that emotionless gladiator?
What exactly happened?
Helena felt that since she fainted, she had left the familiar Rexham and arrived in an unfamiliar place.
She didn't know how much time had passed, nor whether Merlin had learned of her misfortune.
Helena's heart welled with worry; she hadn't expected the other party to want her personally, not just money!
"Young Master Lochiri, look, this is the female demon who runs a small tavern in Rexham." Mr. Morgan bared his gold tooth and introduced: "If it weren't for my company's dominance in the black market, such secret information would be hard for outsiders to know. This demoness is not only beautiful, but also said to be immensely powerful. To capture her, I specially prepared holy water to suppress her, and sent my capable aides, which allowed me to subdue her—though it cost me dearly...."
Lochiri excitedly approached Helena, seeing the horns on her head and the messy black wings on her back, his eyes instantly blazing with fervor.
"Very good, very good!"
"Just look—it's a comparable high-grade item; from afar you can sense the magical power fluctuations of a superior species."
"I've finally obtained it—an important bargaining chip for killing Sword Master Elgin...."
Tomorrow I'll continue to the hospital for an EEG and CT; there will be an extra update before midnight.

title: Chapter 20 — Swapping the Bird in the Cage (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 20 — Swapping the Bird in the Cage (Extra Chapter)

Volume 21 · Chapter 20

"I didn't expect you'd snatch up such high-grade merchandise. You've got skill, Uncle Morgan...." Lockley revealed a meaningful smile.

"Our guild's influence in the black market allows us to easily uncover things even Her Majesty the Queen doesn't know. If you want to find clues as to where the demon race has strongholds in Britain, we can certainly trace them." Mr. Morgan wore the characteristic smile of a crafty merchant.

"I see. Finding you, Uncle Morgan, was indeed the wisest choice I could have made." Lockley looked down at Helena, reached out and twirled a few strands of her hair around his finger, bringing them to his nose to sniff. "My father once said that you are a straightforward merchant who sees only profit and nothing else intertwined, and that doing business with you is a truly pleasant experience."

"That goes without saying. I was also deeply grieved by the deaths of the Redbeard pirate brothers. It caused me to lose a great deal of business at sea, but all that is in the past now. These days I only wish to live peacefully in retirement in Britain." Morgan paused, then added in a low voice, "The reason I'm willing to help you, a son of pirates, is largely out of respect for the friendship I shared with your fathers long ago. You understand, right?"

"Yes, yes, I understand," Lockley nodded, giving a perfunctory reply, though his attention was drawn to Helena's beauty. "It's a pity such a beautiful demon is about to fall into the hands of wicked men for whatever purpose. I really am quite the scoundrel myself."

"Pah!" Helena raised her head and spat a mouthful of saliva all over Lockley's face, glaring fiercely. "Don't touch me, you stinking kid who reeks of fish! You dare lay eyes on me? All of you despicable humans will pay the price!"

"Hmm hmm hmm..." Lockley let out a cold laugh a few times, carelessly wiped the saliva from his face with his hand, and wore an expression of appreciation before backhanding Helena across the face. "What a fine temper. A tiger in disgrace is no better than a dog, Miss Demon. Do you still think you're some higher being who looks down on humans as livestock? How pitiful, that ridiculous dignity of yours...."

"You—!?" Helena clutched her swollen cheek, glaring ferociously at Lockley, completely devoid of any elegance or refinement.

Lockley sneered and stepped on Helena's neck with his foot, pinning her to the ground so she couldn't move. "Put away that pride of yours belonging to a demon. You're nothing more than a stray beast now, lacking any offensive capability whatsoever. If it weren't for them wanting her alive over there, I wouldn't hesitate at all to pour molten holy silver over your body and turn you into a piece of art for everyone to admire."

..... Helena struggled in vain. With her magic sealed, her combat ability amounted to little more than just being able to talk trash, perhaps marginally better than Beelzebub's younger sister Miranda.

"Then...." Mr. Morgan, seeing that Lockley had already obtained what he wanted, couldn't resist but interject and ask.

"This female demon is yours now. Our transaction is complete. Don't forget our agreement—I have nothing further to do with you pirates."

"Alright, it's been a pleasure working with you, Uncle Morg—" Lockley smiled, then continued, "When a person is completely cornered, the most valuable thing is integrity. What nonsense—any fool who believes that is a damn fool. My fathers always promised me I'd stay in the pirate crew forever, yet the next day they tied me to the mast of a small boat and let me drift with the current, nearly getting eaten by sharks. I understand very well never to trust anyone."

"..-. What do you mean?" Mr. Morgan instinctively took a step back.

"You want me to keep a secret, but only dead men can truly keep secrets. I haven't taken out Great Swordmaster Elgin yet, so I can't afford to die...." Lockley explained with a straight face.

No sooner had he finished speaking than Bray drew his naval saber and drove it straight into Mr. Morgan's chest. Blood gushed forth like a fountain. "Forgive me, Mr. Morgan. I was originally a slave purchased by Young Master Lockley and have always been ordered to lie in wait beside you as your bodyguard. In truth, Young Master Lockley has known everything you've done and every move you've made all along."

"Bray,..." Mr. Morgan desperately gripped Bray's sleeve, blood spurting from his mouth as he fell to the ground, his eyes rolling back.

"Two years ago, your intelligence indicated that Elgin City was easily plunderable, yet you never told my two fathers that the place was full of danger, that a man of terrifying strength had taken up residence there, resulting in their tragic deaths at the hands of that bastard. You deserve to pay the price." Lockley looked down coldly at Mr. Morgan, having long wanted to kill this fat man.

Mr. Morgan glared at Lockley with不甘, but in the end his gaze lost its luster—it was as simple as slaughtering a pig.

"Good work. Thank you for your trouble, Bray. I wasn't mistaken when I chose you back then—spending all my savings to buy you was the right decision." Lockley nodded at Bray, very satisfied with this loyal slave.

"It is my honor to serve the Young Master. Even now I remain grateful for your favor." Bray, with his naval saber strapped to his back, offered a slight bow.

"Has everything been arranged?" Lockley pressed.

"It was all ready the day before you arrived, but..." Bray hesitated, and at that moment shouts and clashing sounds erupted from outside, as though a massive purge was underway.

Helena's eyes widened in bewilderment as she stared at the scene before her. Blood splattered against the glass nonstop, and only then did she realize what scheme this young human reeking of fish was plotting—switching the bird inside the cage?

"Excellent. We'll temporarily take control of this place. Given your current position, can you bluff your way through and hold things together for a while?" Lockley nodded approvingly, feeling that everything was proceeding exactly as he'd predicted.

"After lurking beside Mr. Morgan for so many years, I've already earned his trust. Many matters have been relayed through my words, so things can basically remain normal. But a month from now, people will easily spot the discrepancies." Bray said in his usual gruff tone. As the guild's head of guards, he still held some authority, sufficient to handle things for about a month after Mr. Morgan's death.

"Very good." Lockley walked to the doorway and caught the heavy stench of blood in the air outside—the purge seemed to have concluded. "Clean up the scene and throw all the corpses into the well in the back. Tell anyone who asks that Mr. Morgan is critically ill in bed and cannot receive visitors. And you... handle things according to my instructions."

"Understood." Bray knelt on one knee, showing his loyalty.

"You haven't had it easy either. Following me for so long and still maintaining your loyalty—this truly pleases me." Lockley came up to Bray and pulled a scroll from his chest. "Actually, I did consider what I'd do if you betrayed me: I would have torn up this slave contract and we would have perished together, master and servant. Fortunately, I won't need to do that. Rest assured, after this matter is settled, I'll release you from this slave contract and grant you your freedom."

Bray raised his head, his single eye fixed on the slave contract in Lockley's hand, his gaze burning with fanaticism.

That was the one thing this dour man desired most—the freedom he still dreamed of, no longer having to hand his life over to someone else's will.

A slave contract was a voluntarily signed fetter of law, wherein one surrendered everything and placed the right of domination into the master's hands. With merely a single thought from the master, the slave would die instantly under the force of the contract.

When Bray was first purchased by Lockley, he meekly signed such a slave contract. To survive, he had no choice but to obey.

"You won't have to wait long. I need to deliver this female demon safely to the docks and hand her off to another..." Lockley put away the slave contract, gazing at the moon obscured by clouds outside the window, and spoke softly—

"Pity that the royal city's guards have grown increasingly strict lately. Doing something like this is easily discovered by others."

"But I've heard that the enfeoffment ceremony for foreign Thorn Knights has been causing quite a stir recently. I think Queen Elizabeth will be leaving the royal city in the near future."

"At that time, the defenses will surely weaken. This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for us...."

title: Chapter 21 — Sensing a Hint
content:
Chapter 21 — Sensing a Hint

Volume 21 · Chapter 21

Early in the morning, Blackman was left alone at home, becoming a pitiful child left behind.

Little Merlin and Alice had both gone out for business without taking him along.

And here was Blackman, the Great Demon General, now stirring cement and patching up the roof he had destroyed the day before.

The reason? Of course, it was because the thrifty homemaker Alice refused to waste money on hiring a craftsman.

"We really shouldn't tell the landlady about the damaged house," little Merlin said worriedly. "We've been behind on rent for so long—what if she doesn't let us stay anymore?"

"That does make sense," Alice mused, stroking her chin. "Even if the landlady has been tolerating our antics, a broken house isn't a small matter..."

"Hmm?" Alice frowned, turning to the well-built Blackman. "And why do you, the one who caused all this damage, have zero guilt? Hiring a craftsman? Do you think money grows on trees? Whoever breaks it fixes it. Repairing a house isn't that hard, so you can do it yourself!"

"Me?!" Blackman's eyes widened, his right hand pointing at himself in disbelief, as if he had never done manual labor before.

"Got a problem with that?" Alice said sternly, every inch the formidable mistress of the household. "I'm going to meet Count Austin this morning and pay the landlady our rent. You two stay here. Merlin, don't wander off—it's dangerous for you out there right now."

"Hmph hmph~" Little Merlin hummed twice, barely counting as a response.

But the moment Alice left, little Merlin turned to Blackman and said, "You stay here and behave. When I get back, I expect that roof to be fixed. Understood?"

"Eh?! Won't Your Majesty stay and help me a little?" Blackman's eyes widened.

"You made the mess, so you clean it up. Don't expect others to do everything for you. Do I really need to teach you that?" Little Merlin said with the wisdom of an old man, hands behind his back as he walked off to who-knows-where. "Blackman, you still have a lot to learn~"

And so, Blackman was left alone, lonely, brushing cement onto the hollow roof. He sighed deeply, head drooping.

"What am I even doing here?"

"...What do I have to do for Your Majesty to be willing to go back with me..."

At the Adventurers Guild, things were as usual, though Alice's recent return had given people more to talk about.

Little Merlin, of course, didn't much like being cooped up with the gloomy Blackman. Every other sentence out of his mouth was about Demon Lord Palace business, which was extremely annoying.

He probably knew full well that Blackman was under Lilith's orders to bring him back.

But Merlin had been away from the Demon Lord Palace for so long—getting him to give up his freedom outside and return willingly was clearly going to be difficult.

Little Merlin brought along the half of the treasure map he had obtained from the Chaos Sea islands, intending to see if Da Vinci and Rossetti had returned.

If Da Vinci was in Lexham, handing these puzzles to that bookworm would likely yield results.

Unfortunately, the alchemist dedicated to researching the Philosopher's Stone had not returned, and today, there weren't many familiar faces in the guild.

"Have Relf's remains been taken to the Adventurers' Cemetery yet?" Old President Taylor asked quietly.

"Not yet. I plan to take them myself," Mr. Karl said as he packed his bags, seemingly preparing to leave.

"Don't be too disheartened. Death is a normal part of life for us. Relf's remains will bask in the dawn of adventure, and his soul will find solace." Old President Taylor patted his son on the shoulder.

"I understand. This is the only thing I can do for him. I feel like Relf and I—old fogeys like us—are out of touch with the times. The young ones in the guild are growing up. I look forward to their future." Mr. Karl said meaningfully.

"What are you talking about, losing your drive? You're still young..." Old President Taylor blew on his white beard.

"Alice came back yesterday. I feel her strength has grown a lot from this trip. Her potential is enormous, far beyond what I expected. I always thought Merlin was the dark horse among the newcomers, the one who would shine in the Adventurers' Tournament... but now, I'm not so sure." Mr. Karl hesitated.

Old Taylor, seeing his son's expression, worried he was losing confidence in his martial skills. "Cough! It's good for the guild to have more strong members. But don't just focus on them—learn from their strengths to make up for your weaknesses. Recently, I've gained some new insights from Merlin that could perfect our family's Thunderclap Grappling Art. When you get back, let's spar and exchange pointers."

"Well, it's rare for the old man to be so refined..." Mr. Karl smiled.

"By the way, Merlin didn't come back this time?" Old President Taylor asked, stroking his beard.

"No, but Alice brought back Merlin's little nephew. I heard he's a foul-tempered brat... Oh, there he is, standing by the door." Mr. Karl noticed little Merlin.

"What's this kid doing at the guild?" Old President Taylor asked in surprise.

"Probably his first time in a place like this. He doesn't have many friends, so maybe he's just here to play?" Mr. Karl speculated.

Little Merlin averted his gaze, suddenly feeling out of place. Now that he was a child, no one recognized him. It was far more boring than before.

Over there, Hobbs was harassing Lucia. With nowhere else to go, little Merlin had to join them.

"Lucia, take my advice—meet with the owner of the second-hand shop next door. Even if you don't accept his confession, I can still get a little commission." Hobbs rubbed his fingers together.

"...Lucia gave Hobbs a cold stare, rolling her eyes at him.

"Huh? Isn't this... Merlin's nephew?" Hobbs looked down at the tiny little Merlin. "What are you doing here? The guild isn't a place for kids..."

"Tsk!" Little Merlin clicked his tongue and struggled to climb onto a chair.

"You can't stand me, Hobbs?"

"Huh? Who are you?" Hobbs frowned, not understanding what the little brat was babbling about.

"I'm Merlin!" Little Merlin pointed at himself seriously.

"Pfft! Don't joke around. Are you some kid who idolizes your uncle?" Hobbs laughed, not taking little Merlin's words seriously at all. "That bastard Merlin? He's not someone worth idolizing. He's just like me, loafing around the guild all day, but he's luckier—he latched onto Alice, a promising rookie. Probably won't have to worry about food or clothes in the future. Oh, and he still owes me a ton of bar tabs. I've got to find a way to get that back~"

Little Merlin's face flushed red. He lowered his head, thinking, *Because I'm a child, no one believes me!*

*And in Hobbs' eyes, was I really that pathetic? Tsk, just a drinking buddy...*

Little Merlin, annoyed, unconsciously picked up Hobbs' wine glass, intending to drown his sorrows.

But Hobbs immediately snatched the glass back and said seriously, "I don't know where you learned this, kid, but children aren't allowed to drink. Understand?"

"...Little Merlin knitted his brows, left speechless for a moment.

"If you're thirsty, drink this instead. It might help you grow taller. Their favorite stuff isn't good for you." Lucia placed a cup of warm milk in front of little Merlin, not forgetting to wink at him. "Finish it and leave. If Alice can't find you, she'll probably worry. There are a lot of bad people in the guild—don't learn from them."

"Ah..." Little Merlin's heart trembled uncontrollably. *I'm the Demon Lord who strikes fear into others' hearts... and now I'm reduced to meekly hiding here, drinking milk! Completely looked down on as a child!*

"Lucia, don't make it sound so bad. Who's a bad person?" Hobbs forced a smile, not letting it go. "Think about it— the owner of the second-hand shop next door is a good guy. He's just a little face-blind. He says he wants to talk to you not because you're pretty, but because he doesn't even know if you are or not..."

"Hobbs, I'm going to call my dad. You'd better watch your mouth..." Lucia sighed and warned seriously.

"Don't be like that. I'm just trying to make some extra cash..." Hobbs broke into a cold sweat, afraid Karl might jump over and smash him.

"Honestly, stop bothering me. Like always, why don't you go harass Miss Helena in the Mysterious Hut? Aren't you always saying she's Lexham's number one beauty, that no one can compare to her?" Lucia rolled her eyes, her tone sour.

"Hehehe~" Hobbs scratched his head awkwardly. "The rumors have been flying lately. I don't really dare to go. Besides, Miss Helena hasn't shown up these past few days. I don't know if she's given in to the suspicion around her. The Mysterious Hut has been closed for business for days now."

"Hmm?" Little Merlin looked up, his expression turning surprised as he carefully recalled.

Last time he left Lexham, Lucia had mentioned something about his identity being investigated?

But he hadn't taken it seriously. Helena had said she could handle it...

Now this situation—could something have gone wrong?

Back at home, Blackman, the burly man, was diligently repairing the roof.

He had even, with a touch of girly flair, painted a pink rabbit in one of the holes.

This was completely at odds with Blackman's tough-guy image—utterly out of place.

*Bang bang bang—*

A knock at the door made Blackman's whole body jolt. He thought Merlin had returned early.

He hurried to open the door, but standing outside was a young girl in a long dress, dressed alluringly.

"Are you Mer—" The young girl's voice cut off abruptly. She had heard that Alice and Merlin were husband and wife, and that Alice had just returned yesterday. So today, she had come to fulfill the task Sister Helena had given her. She hadn't expected that the moment she opened the door, she'd be faced with a towering demon!

Blackman realized his mistake and tried to cover the horns on his head, but it was useless. His demon form was exposed!

With no way out, Blackman's expression turned cold. His muscles swelled, crackling with lightning, his killing intent sharp and frosty.

"There's nothing to be done, beautiful miss. You've seen what you shouldn't have."

"Wait!" The young girl's eyes suddenly turned crimson, and she deliberately revealed her own demonic aura. "Are you affiliated with that Demon Lord Palace?"

"Eh?!" Blackman was taken aback, retracting his killing intent. He stepped aside slightly, his expression grave. "Seems things are more complicated than I thought. Please, come in and talk."

title: Chapter 22 — No One There
content:
Chapter 22 — No One There

Volume 21 · Chapter 22

The atmosphere at Rexham Lord's Manor was as tranquil as usual, with several maids sweeping the courtyard with brooms.
Recently, Count Austen has been in exceptionally high spirits, feeling rejuvenated as if he had grown several years younger.
This is likely due to the resolution of the family's hereditary short-life curse, so there's no need to worry about the family's continuation anymore.
Because their ancestors were powerful vampire hunters who clashed with Dracula and incurred a short-life curse, the Austen family has few descendants and is gradually dying out.
However, this century-old problem troubling the family was entrusted by Count Austen to Rexham's newly promoted excellent adventurers, Alice and Merlin.
The two of them killed the newly awakened Dracula in France, successfully lifting the Austen family's long-standing heart ailment and completing an almost impossible task.
Thus Alice visited today to claim her rightful reward, receiving a warm welcome from Count Austen, who treated her as a lifesaver.
"Miss Alice, thank you for dispelling the cloud that has loomed over our family for a century. On behalf of everyone in the family, I express my heartfelt gratitude." Count Austen bowed, as the lord of Rexham he showed great humility, even using honorifics—clearly a sincere respect for Alice, with no arrogance whatsoever.
"This is what I should have done; there's no need for such courtesy." Alice replied awkwardly, thinking she hadn't really done anything—it was all Merlin's effort, though there were hardly any witnesses.
"There's no need for modesty; you are our family's benefactor, a great kindness we cannot repay." Count Austen's face glowed red as he signaled a maid to open a small chest, taking out a crystal card worth 500,000 gold coins: "These are some of our family's savings. Although I know money can hardly repay your help to our family, I know the adventurers' custom—this is also a token of my heart; please accept it."
"How could I possibly accept this..." Alice said she felt embarrassed, yet her hand moved unusually fast, directly taking the crystal card. She mentally calculated that during this period she had gained quite a bit; even after handing over most to the Holy Church and repaying the debt for inheriting the Hero's mithril armor, she could still save a considerable amount. What once felt like an unattainable debt now hinted at the possibility of one day clearing it entirely.
"This is what you deserve." Count Austen nodded and continued, "Miss Alice, you're now a celebrity in Rexham as well. I've heard of your outstanding performance in the Kingdom of France—truly, heroes emerge young. I suppose you've already replaced Mr. Karl as the highest-priced, hottest adventurer in the area?"
"Well..." Alice hesitated, wanting to speak but stopping, thinking she hadn't yet had time to consider these matters. Not long ago she was just an ordinary mithril adventurer; after her trip to France, her fame rose and her hiring price increased accordingly, making it unlikely that just anyone could afford her services now.
It seems that, in some sense, Merlin and Alice's original plan has completed its first step—
They worked together to build momentum: Merlin provided the effort, Alice accumulated prestige and raised her status, earning a more substantial reward.
Thus the astronomical debt binding the two of them, which once seemed hopeless, now holds a faint possibility of regaining their freedom.
"Don't be too modest, Miss Alice; you're also a star of Rexham. Be a bit more confident—become the spokesperson for our town..." Count Austen stroked his beard, full of expectations for Alice.
"I don't have the ability to represent Rexham, my lord; you've misunderstood me." Alice replied nervously, thinking she was just a paper tiger that would break at a poke.
"Hah, if Miss Alice lacks that ability, then there's no one in Rexham capable of shouldering important responsibilities~" Count Austen shook his head and sighed meaningfully, "I've recently heard a rumor spreading among the nobles that Her Majesty intends to bestow the title of foreign knight of the Thorns upon someone, and an internal candidate has already been chosen—likely someone from Rexham. Who do you think it will be?"
"..." Alice's expression turned embarrassed as she recalled seeing the twelfth-ranked Thorn Knight, Cladi, in France and discussing the foreign Thorn Knight—no need to think; there's an eighty percent chance it's her.
"If Miss Alice becomes the first-ever foreign Thorn Knight in history, it would also be an honor for all of Rexham, and I would have to tip my hat to you then." Count Austen said in a joking tone.
After bidding farewell to Count Austen, Alice left his study, stepping outside and letting out a breath, feeling a tremendous weight on her shoulders.
Foreign Thorn Knight? According to Mr. Cladi, it's quite good—just an honorary title.
But who knows what might happen? It could possibly cause some trouble.
Alice thought to herself, if the foreign Thorn Knight is merely a simple title, taking it on wouldn't be bad, after all the benefits are plentiful.
"Oh~, beautiful Miss Alice, I didn't expect you to come straight to my house?" Arnold, having heard Alice was visiting, rushed over to see, "What did you and my father discuss? Could it be that you've had a change of heart, concerning our future?"
"Ah!" Alice furrowed her brows, suddenly encountering the very Arnold she least wanted to see, her mood instantly worsening: "What nonsense are you spouting? I'm merely here to complete the lord's task."
"I see, Alice. It's been a while; I don't know if you're free, but could we have dinner together?" Arnold's eyes brimmed with anticipation and excitement, as if he wanted to write his confession on his forehead.
"No need, I'm quite busy and have no time to waste." Alice turned and walked away, waving her hand, "Sorry, Young Master Arnold."
"Don't go!" Arnold quickly blocked Alice's path, excitedly saying, "Since Merlin hasn't returned, won't you feel lonely? Making a lady feel lonely is a gentleman's greatest failure; though I'm not great at jokes, I can still be a listener."
Alice's expression remained blank, thinking, "Will Arnold ever quit? When will he finally give up? Besides, Merlin's basically turned into a child now."
"If you stay silent, does that mean you consent?" Arnold's excited eyes glittered, believing he'd finally gotten his chance, "Then let's set a meeting place."
Just as his words fell, a shout suddenly rang out—a slender figure flew and pounced onto Arnold, beginning to scratch and claw.
"You idiot brother, I asked you to find out why Lord Merlin hasn't returned—not to hit on my wife!"
Jenna had a little wildcat, riding on Arnold's body, scratching and clawing at this disobedient older brother.
"...." "Cut it out! I wasn't planning to ask you about that later, was I? Merlin might have other matters; his little nephew is temporarily staying in Rexham!" Arnold lamented.
"I don't care! I want to see Lord Merlin! You figure out a way!" Jenna insisted.
"Hmph~!" Alice, now freed, turned and left the lord's manor directly.
Arnold's unwilling voice trailed off faintly.
"Don't go! Miss Alice!"
After Alice had repaid part of her debt and paid her rent, returning home,
she unexpectedly found little Merlin and Blackman missing, the house empty.
Only half-repaired roof remained, the ground a mess, as if they had left in a hurry—
"Damn it! Where did Merlin and his subordinates go?"

title: Chapter 23 — Visit
content:
Chapter 23 — Visit

Volume 21 · Chapter 23

Alice stood in the empty room, her heart filled with unease and sinking into deep thought.

Had Merlin suddenly changed his mind and wanted to return to the Demon Lord Palace with his subordinates?

That was unlikely. She hadn't restricted Merlin's freedom at all, so if he wanted to go back, he could have simply told her openly.

Could it be...

Alice lowered her head, her gaze flickering as she looked at the half-repaired ceiling, and suddenly a possibility occurred to her.

Could it be that that Blackman saw Merlin didn't want to return to the Demon Lord Palace, but for the sake of completing the mission, forcibly took Merlin and escaped?

You had to understand that the current Merlin was different from before, so weak that he couldn't even defeat an ordinary adult.

If Blackman forcibly went against Merlin's will, he presumably wouldn't face any punishment either.

Alice was deeply worried, turned around and left her home immediately. She felt she hadn't been gone long, and even if Blackman had kidnapped Merlin, he couldn't have gotten far.

Trusting demons too much, I should have known better...

The vast majority of demons were extremely cunning creatures.

Meanwhile, Alice was burning with anxiety, but the reality was nothing like what she imagined.

In the remote two-story wooden house of Lethcum, this thieves' hideout was doing its usual shady business as always.

Recently, the thieves had made quite a lot of money, their wallets gradually swelling, everyone in high spirits, including the guards at the door.

"Hey hey, the boss has been making a lot lately, huh? But he's being too stingy with us, giving us too little. This isn't even enough to pay for our lives." The bald giant patted his head.

"Be content. Just having something to share is already good. This time we did a big score. Usually we'd be thankful just to have black bread to fill our stomachs," his companion said, rolling his eyes.

"Tch! How can you be content with even that tiny amount of meat on a toothpick? You really have no ambition. Going out to rob merchant caravans would be better than this..." the bald giant complained endlessly.

"Hey! You two idiots, is your boss around?"

Little Merlin suddenly appeared, stepping into this dangerous territory with a carefree expression on his cute little face. One might think he was some young master from a wealthy family.

Although Little Merlin had temporarily lost all his power, he wasn't foolish enough to put himself in danger. Behind him, a black bag contained the head of Medusa, the Chaos King.

If any dangerous situation arose, relying on this monster's head, Little Merlin could handle the vast majority of strong enemies. After all, this was an item capable of briefly petrifying even a Kraken.

The two thieves thought a rival gang was looking for trouble, but then looked down and saw the short Little Merlin, immediately bursting into mocking laughter.

"Hahaha, where did this little brat come from? Tired of living? Go home and drink your mama's milk!"

"You haven't even grown hair yet and you're still bold enough to make threats here. Don't you know what we do? Want to voluntarily increase our extra income?"

"Tch!" Little Merlin crossed his arms and asked sternly, "Why so much nonsense? I'm asking if your boss is here. Can't you understand human speech?"

"Hehehe, this little brat has a pretty big temper, huh?" The bald giant pointed at Little Merlin. "Seems like he hasn't been beaten by the harsh world yet?"

"You little kid, scram while we're in a good mood today! Otherwise you'll suffer." The thief companion growled.

"I was thinking about staying polite, but it seems unnecessary now. Using fists to reason seems to be the simplest and most direct approach," Little Merlin muttered, frowning.

"...The bald giant rolled up his sleeves and strode forward, looking down at Little Merlin from above. "Kid, are you tired of living and looking for death? I swear one punch could explode your little head—"

"Oh~" Little Merlin raised his eyelids in response, even dragging out the trailing tone.

Before he finished speaking, a whoosh of breaking air echoed, and the three-meter-tall giant Blackman descended from above, landing behind Little Merlin.

The powerful body stirred up a fierce wind, blowing Little Merlin side to side until his hair was a mess like a bird's nest. He couldn't help but complain inwardly: *This bastard Blackman, couldn't you be a little quieter?*

Blackman straightened up, creating the illusion of blocking out the sky. He clenched his fists and looked down at the "short" bald giant.

"Hey, human kid, are you tired of living and looking for death? I swear one punch could explode your little noggin."

"Uh—"

The bald giant's head roared, feeling that锐利 killing intent, shuddered violently, every inch of his body breaking out in goosebumps.

The other person had turned his own words right back at him, and that monstrous fist was three times the size of his head!

"..Sorry."

"Kill him." Little Merlin took out a comb and tidied his messy hairstyle.

"At once!" Blackman suddenly raised his massive fist, laced with the power of thunder, and struck directly.

With a loud bang, the ground was smashed into a large pit. The bald giant was crushed into paste, not even having time to let out a scream.

Blackman raised his head and slowly removed his cloak hood, revealing sharp demonic horns, his gaze coldly fixed on the other terrified thief.

"Eeeeek! D-demon! The demon is coming! A demon is coming!!" The thief companion wet himself and scrambled on hands and knees, crawling into the hideout to cry for help.

"This is the right place, correct?" Little Merlin asked.

"That female demon just now said so. After Miss Helena came here, she never returned. Something unfortunate must have happened," Blackman rumbled in response.

After hearing the secrets from the female demon at the secret hut, Blackman had immediately gone to find Merlin and relayed everything.

After thinking it over, Little Merlin decided to fulfill what he had promised Helena, intervening in this matter, and charged straight to this place.

"As long as we're in the right place, follow me in and let's have a talk." Little Merlin waved his hand, signaling Blackman behind him to follow.

"Wait, Your Majesty. Shouldn't we notify Miss Alice before taking action? Slaughter without warning isn't appropriate, after all... this isn't our territory," Blackman said hesitantly.

"There's no need for that. Do I need to ask my little follower's permission for whatever I do? Besides, this is our demon race's affair; outsiders aren't suited to interfere," Little Merlin said seriously.

"Understood, Your Majesty. Wherever your sword points, this subordinate will march through fire and water." Blackman responded respectfully.

Little Merlin narrowed his eyes and whispered meaningfully, "Let these guys feel the terror of being dominated by demons..."

On the second floor of the wooden house, the thieves' leader had no idea what had happened outside, still counting gold coins on the table with a grin spreading across his face.

"Hehehe, mine, all mine..."

The door shattered as a thief came flying in like a cannonball, knocking over the gold coins on the table, scattering them everywhere in a glittering pile!

His corpse was gruesome, his head smashed deformed, having crashed through the wall, his body hanging lifelessly against it.

"Huh!?" The thieves' leader was startled, his sly eyes darting around frantically. Grabbing his long sword, he thought rivals had come to steal their loot!

As the dust settled, Little Merlin led Blackman behind him, stepping over the corpses of numerous thieves as he walked in.

"So you're the leader here?"

"I heard you lack basic manners toward our kind, demons?"

"I've decided to personally teach you today."

"What the f— manners!?"

title: Chapter 24 — Interrogation
content:
Chapter 24 — Interrogation

Volume 21 · Chapter 24

.-- you all
The bandit leader's teeth chattered with fear, making a giggling sound, especially when he saw Blackman behind little Merlin, those huge horns were terrifying.
This bandit chief never dreamed that Helena would have a demon companion show up at his door in broad daylight, and immediately start a slaughter!
Seeing countless subordinates lying in pools of blood outside, the bandit leader secretly regretted taking the Morgan family's business, which had now brought fiery trouble upon himself.
This time the bandits didn't have the holy water prepared by the Morgan family, so dealing with Blackman obviously wouldn't be as easy as when they dealt with Helena before.
-A group of lowly human bandits, could they possibly defeat an elite officer of the Demon Lord Palace head-on? The odds are about the same as winning the lottery.
Merlin stepped forward and asked, 'I don't want to waste words either—where is Helena?'
....What are you....
Originally the bandit leader instinctively wanted to scold little Merlin, but after being glared at by Blackman, he didn't dare to even fart.
The bandit leader didn't take little Merlin seriously at all, thinking he was just some wild kid who had come here to throw his weight around.
What was truly frightening was the demonic brute behind him, reeking of blood that made anyone who saw him tremble in the legs.
'My boss is asking you, where is Miss Helena!' Blackman's voice thundered as he roared at the bandit leader.
The bandit leader stammered, so scared he was about to wet himself, trembling all over, thinking this demonic brute was being called the 'big boss' by some human brat? What the hell!
The bewildered bandit leader couldn't be bothered to figure it out, just treating little Merlin as a clown; the real threat was that strong demon!
So the bandit leader drew his long sword, suppressed his fear, and forced himself to stare into Blackman's eyes.
'Don't ask me, I don't know anything!'
'You don't know?' Merlin raised his head, speaking meaningfully, 'I advise you to be honest—you don't have many chances left to live.'
'No matter how you ask, I know nothing—stop pressing me! You won't get anything from my mouth! Get off my turf, or you won't like what comes next!' The bandit leader brandished his sword, but his tough exterior was utterly unconvincing.
'Oh~' Merlin stepped aside, clapped his hands, and said, 'Blackman, let him see what our demons can do.'
'Yes sir!' Blackman clasped his fists together, and tiny currents of electricity crackled in the air.
