'Don't... don't come over! If you trespass on my private property, I'll have the guards arrest you!' The bandit leader, obviously scared stupid, was actually citing imperial law to a demon.
'Sorry, dead people can't notify the guards...' Merlin shrugged, giving the bandit leader no chance to call the authorities.
'Ugh!' The bandit leader's face turned pale as he wondered whether they intended to leave him no way out today.
Blackman moved— in an instant he was before the bandit leader, lowering his head with icy eyes to look down on this despicable human.
Don't let his bulky frame fool you—though he looks slow and clumsy, his swift movements are fast enough to make your scalp tingle!
The bandit leader looked up in terror at Blackman; before him he was like a chick, and his long sword instantly became a child's toy.
Blackman's huge fist slammed into the bandit leader's face, sending him flying backward like a cannonball into the hard wall, wood chips and stone fragments scattering everywhere.
'Cough!' The bandit leader went limp, spitting a mouthful of blood onto the ground, his features distorted—likely even his own mother wouldn't recognize him.
Blackman walked toward the bandit leader lying on the ground, each step heavy as if the Grim Reaper were slowly approaching the poor man.
Blackman grabbed the bandit leader's neck and lifted him off the ground, his voice icy as he demanded.
'Helena, where is she? Speak!'
'....Cough cough!' The bandit leader felt he'd lost half his life, so he reluctantly said, '...She's no longer here. Please spare me—I'm just a pawn, I really know very little.'
'You know so little? Are your eyes and ears just for show?' Merlin frowned, thinking the guy's mouth was tight, guessing the mastermind behind him was someone not to be provoked, 'Blackman, gouge out his eyes.'
'Yes sir!' Blackman shouted back, raising two fingers and stabbing them into the bandit leader's eyes, tearing out the eyeballs.
'Ahhhhhh!!!' The bandit leader screamed in agony, blood streaming from his eyes, his whole body shuddering with pain, his hands frantically scratching Blackman's arm to no avail.
'You don't need your ears either—rip them off.' Merlin said in a flat tone, listing these horrible methods, straight-up chilling to the bone.
Blackman raised his demon claw again, and the bandit leader could no longer endure, bellowing for mercy--
'Wait! I'll talk! I'm willing to speak!'
'You should have done this sooner...' Merlin twisted the corner of his mouth.
'......It's the Morgan family in London; they want to capture a live elite demon, and I merely gave them a clue...' The bandit leader's face went pale as he stammered.
'The Morgan family? That shipbuilding guild?' Merlin had heard a bit about them—after all, Britain's famed warships are all built by this family—'What do they want with demons?'
'I really don't know; I just sold them the news that Rexum has high-ranking demons, and as for the rest... I truly don't know...' the bandit leader said, trembling.
'I see.' Merlin nodded, feeling he'd pressed enough that the guy wouldn't dare lie anymore—probably this bandit gang really was just a pawn.
'I've told you everything I know, but... can you spare my life?' the bandit leader pleaded.
'Too bad, I never considered letting you live.' Merlin shook his head.
'Hey!' The bandit leader's whole body jerked, obviously startled by Merlin's shamelessness, 'You think killing me ends it? No! Not at all! All of Rexum is whispering that the secret cottage is a demon lair, and it's not just Helena— I know every gorgeous woman inside is a demon! If I die here today, without a doubt everyone will suspect we were killed by demons, and all the women in the secret cottage will die with me! But if you spare me, I swear this won't be brought up again—what do you say to this deal?'
'You think you're clever?' Merlin tilted his head, walked over, and whispered in the bandit leader's ear—
'We demons value fair exchange—'
'but we never do business with rude people...'

title: Chapter 25 — Rebellion (Update Soon)
content:
Chapter 25 — Rebellion (Update Soon)

Volume 21 · Chapter 25

Darkness filled the room, thick with the heavy stench of blood. The headless corpse of the thief gang leader lay on the ground, his head kicked off to one side.

"What now, Your Majesty?" Blake asked, looking down at little Merlin with concern. "That thief just said something reasonable. We run rampant on human territory, and we'll definitely attract a large-scale pursuit. Of course, that's not the worst situation. What about the demon ladies living in the secret huts? They belong to the Fourth Demon Lord Palace. We might bring disaster upon them."

"Hmm..." Merlin frowned, touching his chin. "I only thought of killing this rude fellow. I never thought of such a thing. Now it's really troublesome..."

Although the beautiful female demons in the secret hut aren't Merlin's subordinates, but Asmodeus's people.

But Merlin has a good relationship with Asmodeus. They are bound by duty, so he can't just stand by.

Moreover, Merlin just wanted to destroy this thief's hideout. He never really thought about how to deal with the messy situation afterward.

As the thief gang leader just said, many suspect the secret hut is a demon base. With so many humans dying suddenly in the main city of Recksen, anyone would recall the recent rumors, threatening the safety of those demon ladies.

"Eh?! ? !" Blake widened his eyes, surprised like a cow bell, exclaiming, "So Your Majesty didn't think about the aftermath? I thought you had a plan, so you acted so decisively! ? ... How should we do this? Even if we can escape with those demon ladies..."

"Tch! Why are you panicking? Something tall will prop up the sky." Merlin rolled his eyes.

"....I'm just a tall one..." Blake looked dejected. He trusted Merlin too much, so he didn't think much earlier, and now he's in a tight spot.

"You're just a tall one..."

Merlin seemed to be suddenly reminded of something. His gaze at Blake kept flashing strange looks, as if eating tofu with a beauty?

"Blake, you... what do you mean? Your gaze feels very strange..." Blake subconsciously took a half step back, shyly saying, "If you have any private requirements, you can just tell me directly. Hinting like this... I find it rather unclear..."

"Pull in your disgusting delusions!" Merlin's face turned black, kicking Blake's calf. "Be quiet, let me think properly."

"......" Blake nodded, closing his mouth obediently. He looked around at the corpses lying in pools of blood, about twenty in total. Placed in Recksen town, it's a major case that would alarm the lord.

Merlin fell silent, frowning and lowering his head, constantly rubbing his chin, his eyes flashing, wondering what evil idea he was plotting in his head?

After a few breaths, Merlin's troubled expression relaxed, as if he thought of a method. He lifted his head, looking up at the silly big guy Blake beside him.

"Blake!"

"At your service!" Blake shivered all over, adopting a serious posture ready to accept orders.

"You've followed me for a long time, haven't you?" Merlin circled around Blake with interest, constantly turning in circles.

"....Yes, though not as tall as Ophelia and you who grew up together, but I've followed you for many years, witnessing you reclaim the throne of your predecessors, pulling out Banri Garan, gaining all the subjects'...." Blake spoke seriously.

"Um~, good!" Merlin nodded. Due to being too short, he had to stand on tiptoes, patting Blake's knee. "You haven't followed me in vain. In my seven subordinates, you are the most loyal to me, always doing your best, strictly executing all my orders. I'm glad, Blake, you are as precious as my two hands."

"Land... Blake's eyes were filled with tears. He knelt on one knee immediately, as if all his hardships were recognized. "Did you finally discover that only I am loyal to you? The other few executives either want to cage you and castrate you to death, or want to pounce on you and mess you up..."

Merlin's face turned black, thinking what garbage? Those idiots' brains are full of shit!

Well, let's not talk about other subordinates now. Let's get to the point!

So Merlin coughed lightly, disguising his embarrassment.

"Cough cough! ...I've long been aware of your loyalty. Now I want to give you an important task. Do you have the confidence to complete it?"

Certainly! I... huh?! !" Blake suddenly froze, feeling something amiss, as if he'd fallen into a trap. "I have a bad feeling, suddenly feeling unwell, fearing.

"What are you afraid of, Blake?" Merlin stood on tiptoes, touching Blake's forehead, showing a harmless smile. "Scapegoat for me..."

Blake's gaze was blank, lost in thought for three seconds. He slightly opened his mouth, uttering the sound of "obeying orders"—

"Ah, huh?

Outside the thief's hideout, Blake wore a fierce and terrible expression, not concealing his demon identity at all, exposing his horns in the air.

This demon warrior was holding the small-sized Merlin in his hand, looking like he was picking up a chick?

Little Merlin's face was pale and panicked, trembling in Blake's hand, indistinguishable from a hostage.

In front of the two of them, a group of Recksen guards surrounded Blake, long spears in hand, sealing off the demon that had infiltrated human territory.

Leading them was the guard captain Price, who had just finished drinking. His mind was a bit muddled now. He nervously looked at the tall demon before him, not daring to move lightly.

Damn it, when did a demon sneak into the city? I didn't notice at all!

Being able to slip in under my "sharp" eyelids, hmm! Worth praising! A real tough character!

Saying the small kid in the demon's hand... seems to be Merlin's little nephew brought in by Alice?

How did it become confused being caught by a demon as a hostage? Tsk! This is a bit troublesome now. Can't save them, Alice's side won't be easy to handle...

Price was highly tense, holding a real sword, gritting his teeth and shouting loudly—

"Lowly demon!"

"Huh?" Blake's breath stagnated, feeling Blake's voice was loud, like a valiant warrior!

"....". Under great pressure, Price's face couldn't hold up, falling into the professional disease of a sycophant. Instantly lowering his identity, he said with a servile smile, "Can you put down the bear child in your hand? If we have something, let's sit down and talk nicely. On the wine table, you one cup, I one cup, drinking until dawn, everyone becomes good brothers. To be honest, is there any problem in the world that a round of drinking can't solve? If there is, then two rounds, hahaha~"

"....Little Merlin rolled his eyes, being messed around by this unreliable cheapskate Price, feeling speechless and embarrassed—

I'm being abducted by Blake! The guard captain of the city still has the mood to clink glasses with a bandit?

Beg the demon opposite is an enemy! Show some momentum, you guard captain!

Too embarrassing! Buuut Price 5

Mountain (∩°山)

title: Chapter 26 — Attracting Hatred (Extra)
content:
Chapter 26 — Attracting Hatred (Extra)

Volume 21 · Chapter 26

Blackman had expected the guards to charge at him furiously and fight to the death, but to his surprise, no one dared to move.

On top of that, the guy who seemed to be the captain was overly familiar, grinning foolishly in a way that made it hard for Blackman to act vicious.

Blackman lowered his head and asked Merlin in a very soft voice, "Your Majesty, are you really going to do this? It's not right..."

Little Merlin maintained a terrified expression, his lips trembling as he whispered back, "Why so much talk? I told you to do it, so just do it. Do you not loyal to me?"

"...I..." Blackman grew nervous because what Merlin had asked him to do was somewhat insubordinate; he didn't dare do it.

"Come on, Blackman, you're my most loyal subordinate. If you don't carry out my orders, I'll never trust you again." Little Merlin frowned and said in a serious tone.

"Alright..." Blackman's brows knit tightly together, and he bared his fangs at all the guards, showing off the vicious appearance of a demon!

"Eh! Don't kill me! Don't kill me!" Price, this cowardly fellow, immediately turned pale with fright and hid behind the other guards, terrified that the demonic strong man in front of him might tear him apart in a fit of rage.

Rexium's guard unit's overall strength was truly mediocre. Blackman didn't even need to make any attacks; merely baring his teeth was enough to make them tremble all over. They had zero fighting spirit.

Blackman held up little Merlin high in the air and struck a pose as if he were going to dash him to the ground, "Waaaaaa!"

Little Merlin struggled, craning his neck and shouting for help loudly, "Help!!!"

Blackman let out a roar. Golden Saint-tier battle aura rose up, and blue lightning crackled and popped in the air, gradually gathering into a huge sphere of electricity.

With a mighty shout, the blue lightning flew out like an electromagnetic cannon, carrying the fury of wind and thunder, and directly blasted Rexium's city gate to smithereens!

A massive column of electric current shot up into the sky, thunder cracking like daylight bolts. The earth was scorched with traces of charred marks, and the obstacles on the road leading outside were all swept away clean!

Alice had left home and was searching everywhere for little Merlin's whereabouts. She was very worried about Merlin's safety now.

She had a terrible feeling that something bad was about to happen; whenever she wasn't keeping an eye on little Merlin for even a moment, something major would go wrong!

Now Merlin was so weak that he definitely couldn't resist his strong subordinate Blackman.

Perhaps this Blackman, in order to bring Merlin back to the Demon Lord Palace, would dare to defy Merlin's wishes and forcibly take him back by brute force.

But in such a short amount of time, Blackman probably wouldn't be able to leave Rexium with little Merlin. Even getting out of the city would trigger scrutiny.

So Alice was convinced that Merlin hadn't left Rexium yet. Perhaps Blackman was plotting how to escape from within the city!

Alice's forehead was covered in fragrant perspiration. She'd been to everywhere she should go and found not a trace of Merlin.

She'd checked every horse race betting booth, every popular tavern that was always packed with customers, and even Helena's secret cabin.

Just because these were all places Merlin liked to go didn't mean they were safe—they were actually the easiest places to hide in all of Rexium.

If Blackman had kidnapped Merlin, the safest place for him to hide would be somewhere crowded with lots of people around.

However, the secret cabin was different from usual. Business was extremely slow, and even the front door was closed.

Alice paced around aimlessly like a headless fly, her heart boiling with frustration as she weighed various possibilities.

But just then, Hobbs came stumbling over, swaying with a bottle in hand. He probably found the guild boring and was heading home to rest.

The moment Hobbs saw Alice standing there, he sobered up instantly. He walked over with a grin and asked, "Yo~ Alice, what are you doing here?"

"Get lost! I don't have time for you!" Alice turned her head and gave him a vicious glare. Right now she was like a barrel of gunpowder—just one spark and she'd explode. Being harassed by Hobbs like this, how could she possibly be in a good mood?

"Huh? What's wrong? Did I offend you somehow?" Hobbs was utterly confused. He felt like he hadn't bothered Alice lately at all, so her glare, which looked like she wanted to kill him, was very abnormal.

"Stay away from me. I have something urgent to do!" Alice emphasized in a cold tone, unwilling to waste any more time on a drunkard like Hobbs.

Hobbs shook his head, sensing that something had happened, and for once showed a trace of seriousness. "Eh, don't rush. Tell me what's going on. You know I'm usually very well informed. Maybe I know something that could help you~"

"Hm?" Alice's expression slightly softened, realizing there was some logic to his words. Hobbs's intelligence-gathering ability was incredibly strong; maybe she could ask him. "Merlin..."

"Huh? Merlin? What's wrong with Brother Merlin? Does he have some random woman outside and won't come back? Hahaha~" Hobbs fell back into his old habit of making jokes regardless of the atmosphere.

"Hobbs, if you don't want to help, disappear from my sight right now." Alice's anger boiled over and her hand gripped her sword hilt, her aura fierce.

"No joking, I was wrong, I was wrong." A bead of cold sweat trickled down Hobbs's forehead as he covered his mouth, afraid to speak carelessly.

"It's Merlin's little nephew. He suddenly went missing. I've looked in many places but haven't seen him anywhere." Alice spoke concisely. She didn't dare reveal Blackman's identity as a demonic subordinate. After all, Merlin was also a demon, and saying too much could easily bring trouble down on herself.

"Huh? That little brat? He was just at the guild playing for a bit, wanted to drink. I was wondering how you could be so careless letting such a small kid run around alone." Hobbs narrowed his eyes and thought for a moment. "Looks like something really did happen..."

"Do you know something?" Alice pressed eagerly.

"Rexium hasn't been peaceful lately. Kids going missing nowadays... well, that's a big problem..." Hobbs paused and said solemnly, "Merlin's little nephew might have been kidnapped and eaten by a demon."

"Huh!" Alice's eyes widened in sheer disbelief, her face full of astonishment. *Is this guy Hobbs really human? His predictions are eerily accurate!* She hadn't said a thing, and he already guessed that Merlin had been taken by a demon!?

"You haven't been back for a while, so you probably don't know. Lately a lot of people in Rexium have been talking about how Miss Helena is a demon, and that little secret cabin of hers is a demon stronghold. Demons, you know what those are, right? They especially like to eat human children..." Hobbs said with a grim expression and quickly took a swig of beer to calm his nerves.

"???" Alice's head was full of question marks. *What kind of nonsense is this? Does this have anything to do with Merlin being kidnapped by Blackman? The secret cabin is a demon stronghold, for real? Could the reason business is so冷清 that they had to close the door be because of this?*

Crash—

Thunderbolt struck on a clear day!

The entire city of Rexium heard the massive explosion, and spectacular blue lightning surged toward the sky!

The central continent leading out of Rexium was filled with dust and smoke, as if it had come under attack!

Alice's current strength was astonishing, and her perception far exceeded her previous abilities. Even from this far away, she could detect the subtle demonic aura within the lightning.

Alice stared at the brilliant lightning, and suddenly her expression turned dark, her eyes filled with heavy hostility.

She tightened her grip on her slender sword, her entire body's battle aura exploding outward, and she shot toward the center of the thunderstorm like a meteor—

Merlin, wait for me!

That damn bastard dares to lay his hands on a child!

I will definitely tear that androgynous demon to pieces!

title: Chapter 27 — Thunder and Lightning Turmoil
content:
Chapter 27 — Thunder and Lightning Turmoil

Volume 21 · Chapter 27

A bolt from the blue stirred up a fierce impact, putting the whole of Rexham into a state of panic.
Dozens of guards lay on the ground, eyes rolled back, foaming at the mouth, obviously knocked out by electricity.
Only a timid mouse-like Price remained standing before Blackman, gripping a sword, trembling all over.
Don't look at Blackman's fearsome appearance; these things are all Merlin's instructions, otherwise no demon would be foolish enough to run amok on human territory.
Blackman lowered his head, looking down at this short guard captain, with electricity wandering over his body, crackling.
Price nervously swallowed, trembling as he put down his sword and raised both hands in a surrender pose.
"You won, you won...
....Blackman snorted, raised his large palm, electricity gathering, wanting to knock out this coward Price."
"No no no! I'll do it myself!" Price, afraid of pain, quickly sat by the roadside, grabbed a handful of dirt and smeared it on his face, then collapsed stiffly, "Ah~! I'm dead, I really died...."
....Blackman had a strange expression, wondering what this human was up to, which made him lose all will to fight; forget it, as long as he doesn't meddle.
"This useless fellow....Little Merlin rubbed his forehead, rendered speechless by Price's poor acting, thinking how such a person could still be a guard captain? Who is he protecting? It's a miracle that Rexham's townsfolk have survived to now! Even just shouting would do, scare him and he'd surrender his weapons."
Death novel
"Your Majesty, is it alright? The commotion should be big enough, so the rumor that the secret cottage is a demon stronghold will stop, right?" Blackman asked softly.
"Yeah, pretty much. We've killed so many bandits; we can only protect those female demons this way. Since everyone suspects the secret cottage is a demon lair, just jump out openly and launch an attack, then those rumors will mostly disappear, and everyone will think the bad deeds were done by you, the demon who attacked Rexham."
Little Merlin said while thinking, after a long while he felt this plan was relatively suitable—
Helena, who suspects the secret cottage, and Blackman's self-exposure, will draw all hatred.
Although Blackman can no longer stay in Rexham, the rumors unfavorable to Helena will also gradually fade.
After all, the rumor that Helena is a demon is just hearsay; Blackman's self-exposure confirms the rumor that Rexham has demons, but it clears Helena's stain.
"At the end of the day, I'm just taking all the blame, right? I feel it's a bit unfair...." Blackman muttered resentfully.
"Don't worry, you can always go back to the Demon Lord Palace; I don't believe anyone besides the Holy Church would dare invade there." Little Merlin said in a comforting tone.
....Blackman frowned tightly, always feeling Merlin was trying to drive him away.
"Stop the nonsense, hurry up; although few in Rexham could beat you, the commotion just now.... Little Merlin looked around and issued the order: 'Let's quickly flee Rexham and head straight to the capital of Britain to find Helena......"
"Before leaving, shouldn't we say hello to Miss Alice?" Blackman felt it was a bit improper.
"Damn it! You still want to greet Alice? I swear, with you kidnapping me like this, she'll cut you down directly; we went to great lengths to clear the secret cottage's stigma, and speaking the truth would ruin all that!" Little Merlin emphasized seriously, thinking Blackman too naive; this secret must absolutely not be spoken!
"Eh? Then I'd be terribly unlucky, now I'm like a street rat, everyone shouting to beat me, even Miss Alice would hunt me down... but... I probed Miss Alice's aura, it's a bit terrifying, I can't beat...." Blackman panicked, feeling he shouldn't have accepted Merlin's task.
"Can't beat him, won't you run? Hurry up and flee; once Alice arrives you won't be able to leave.... Little Merlin really wanted to jump up and knock Blackman's head, but being a hostage he shouldn't be too arrogant."
....
Blackman responded with a sound, grabbed Little Merlin's neck, and took off running.
Although he is tall, his running speed is extremely fast, kicking up gusts of wind, making people dare not approach lightly.
Blackman regretted deeply; he had come out fine, but ended up bringing trouble upon himself.
"Help! Help!" Little Merlin swung in Blackman's grip, still remembering his hostage status, shouting for help a couple times, thinking no one would come after him.
But reality slapped him in the face; the rescue was faster than Merlin imagined, already cutting through in a flash—
"Don't be scared, kid! I'm here!!!" Uncle Karl, his whole body clad in golden thunder armor, famed for his swift thunder fighting style, arrived with astonishing speed.
"Pfft!" Little Merlin widened his eyes, never expecting someone to chase so quickly; if Blackman were slowed down, that would be no joke!
"Put down the child! Vile demon K<Uncle Karl clenched his black-gold gauntlets, mixed with thunder's might, launched a flying kick, fiercely assaulting Blackman!"
"Huh?!" Blackman startled, raised his arm to block. Squeak
After the loud bang, Blackman's heart filled with astonishment; his arm was kicked and deformed, the opponent's strength not to be underestimated!
Uncle Karl's heart was equally astonished; although he roughly knew this demon's strength, he didn't expect that even with his full-force kick, the demon's body barely moved; this physical power qualifies as a formidable foe!
The center of the commotion is very close to the Taylor residence; when the disturbance occurred, Mr. Karl headed this way and caught up to Blackman without much effort!
Uncle Karl gave the demon no chance to catch its breath, flipping in midair to unleash a second barrage of strikes!
The storm-like kicks struck Blackman's body, leaving him little spare attention for Little Merlin's safety.
Thunder and lightning like a storm blew Little Merlin, making his eyes roll white, nearly knocking him unconscious.
Blackman worried about Merlin's condition, tucked him under his arm for protection, fell onto Uncle Karl, yet stubbornly refused to release the hostage.
This made Uncle Karl inwardly furious; his attacks grew ever more fierce, wishing to kick and break Blackman's bones!
"Release the child! Do you demons only have such despicable tactics?!"
"Get lost, human!"
Blackman, feeling somewhat aggrieved from the blows, angrily retaliated, his fist wrapped in blue lightning, hammering hard at Karl.
Uncle Karl was greatly startled, raising his hands to guard his chest, wanting to clash head-on with the demon, refusing to retreat even an inch.
Their Saint-tier battle qi violently collided, yellow and blue lightning intertwining in opposition, instantly causing tremors all around!
Uncle Karl stepped back two steps, his arms numb, astonished at the opponent's strength: 'I really underestimated you, what tremendous power....
"Disappear, or I'll twist your neck." Blackman's gaze cold, revealing sharp teeth in a hostile glare.
"Sorry, my dictionary has no 'retreat in the face of battle'.... Uncle Karl rubbed his wrist, inquiring tentatively"
"Recently there have been rumors of demons lurking in Rexham, boiling over...."
"Could it be that you're the one they're talking about?"

title: Chapter 28 — Hand Chop (Extra)
content:
Chapter 28 — Hand Chop (Extra)

Volume 21 · Chapter 28

"He! I didn't even...!"

"Cough, cough!"

Blackmann instinctively wanted to deny it, but at the sound of little Merlin's light cough, he remembered and was left with no choice but to admit it.

"That's right! It's me! I never expected to be discovered after coming here — I really let my guard down."

"I don't know what you're doing here, but you're running amok through Rexam. Don't think you can walk away from this unscathed. You'll pay for your actions!" Uncle Carl clenched his black-gold gauntlets, signaling he wouldn't let Blackmann leave easily. "If you still have even a shred of honor as a warrior, then release the child, and we'll fight this fair."

"..." Blackmann hesitated for a moment, then shook his head. "I'm not letting this child go. Don't you humans all think of us demons as despicable beings? Fine — I'll show you despicable."

Little Merlin pretended to be too scared to speak, thinking to himself: *hurry up and end this quickly. If Alice comes, something bad is definitely going to happen.*

"Hopeless!" A raging aura of battle energy swirled around Uncle Carl, and the Thunder Armor seemed to come alive at that very moment, gradually transforming into a vivid, multicolored fierce tiger that roared ferociously at Blackmann.

Blackmann frowned, looking at the battle-hungry human before him. *This guy's hand-to-hand skills are brutal. He seems like someone who isn't afraid of dying at all — a bit troublesome, actually.* But His Majesty had ordered him to flee Rexam quickly. *I guess I'll have to end this fast.*

"Raaarh!" Uncle Carl let out a deafening roar and launched himself forward like a tiger descending the mountain, his fists swinging with thunderous force.

"Your Majesty, hold onto me tightly. We can't afford to go easy on this guy." Blackmann spoke in a low voice, the dangerous gap between them palpable.

"..." Little Merlin instinctively gripped Blackmann tightly, watching the imposing Uncle Carl and thinking: *It's been a long time since I've felt this kind of thrill. Everyone seems more powerful than me now. Before, I looked down on nobody; I never paid much attention to people.* *So this guy is actually this dangerous? For Blackmann to take him seriously, he must be quite strong...*

Blackmann clenched his teeth, and every muscle in his body swelled as if provoked!

Nearly three meters tall, he resembled a stone giant.

Blue lightning surged forth from Blackmann's body, and the ground beneath his feet crumbled to dust!

His gaze sharpened, and he swung his massive fists, summoning a torrential storm of thunder as he clashed with Uncle Carl.

Thunder continuously exploded around them, blue and yellow lightning colliding and even merging into devastating bursts!

The two fought like beasts in a forest, never dodging each other's attacks, trading blow after blow, each determined to knock the other down immediately!

"What the hell..." Little Merlin almost fainted. This feeble body of his truly couldn't handle it anymore.

Even though Blackmann had to protect little Merlin and could only use one arm, he wasn't at all at a disadvantage in terms of power — he could even knock Uncle Carl back.

Uncle Carl grew anxious in his heart. He knew the child caught in their clash wouldn't be able to endure much longer, so he could only choose to end this quickly with a more powerful attack.

Little Merlin's presence had become a shackle in their fierce battle — neither dared to hurt him, both suppressing their strength accordingly.

With such overwhelming electrical forces clashing, one wrong move and the child would explode on the spot!

"Drop that kid!" Uncle Carl roared, pressing his palms together into a hammer fist and smashing down fiercely!

Golden lightning surged toward the sky. Uncle Carl's thunder-multicolored tiger form suddenly extended its razor-sharp claws!

Lightning streaks charged with tearing force sliced toward Blackmann like claws, leaving him nowhere to dodge!

This attack was devastating — with thunderbolts and lightning crackling, it seemed determined to crush the demon before him into pieces!

Blackmann bared his fangs and reacted quickly, slamming a fist hard into the ground. Blue radiance erupted from the earth beneath him, turning the ground into an ocean of lightning that surged upward to confront the tearing thunder of the multicolored tiger in the sky!

Boom —!

The deafening roar and intense flash caused the entire Rexam to tremble. The lightning storm upended the earth, scorching everything around to charcoal!

Uncle Carl was knocked backward, his whole body numb, clutching his chest to ease the searing pain. *What kind of demon is this?! So tough to deal with, and his hide is rock-solid!*

In the fierce exchange, Blackmann clearly had the upper hand. But he knew his opponent was worried about hurting Merlin and was fighting with one hand tied behind his back. *What would he look like if he fought with full power?*

"Are you satisfied? If you don't want to die, get lost."

"Pah!"

Uncle Carl stood up and spat on the ground, deeply unconvinced.

But just then, someone tapped his shoulder. Startled, he turned around to see a hunched, ancient-looking old man — the guild master of the Rexam Adventurers Guild!

Old Taylor had actually followed closely behind. Seeing his son knocked back by the demon without gaining any advantage, he had been about to step in himself.

"Kid, I told you you weren't good enough — you lack training. Leave this kind of thing to me. You just stand back and watch..."

"Father?!" Uncle Carl was taken aback. He hadn't expected his father to return, and seeing his own embarrassed situation, his face flushed red. He figured this would be teased about for years to come.

"Your family's Thunder Shock Fighting Technique is being used so timidly. You fight with no momentum at all — truly disgraceful. If your heart holds reservations, you'll never unleash your advantage." Guild Master Taylor slowly walked forward, bowing slightly with his hands behind his back, a smile on his face as he looked at Blackmann.

"If you want to take your enemy's life, your enemy can also take yours. Whoever fears death has already lost. Your training is incomplete, Carl. Learn from this..."

"..." Uncle Carl was speechless and could only sigh. "Be careful. This guy is hard to deal with. That body of yours... probably won't last long..."

"Even though I'm old, your dad is still your dad..." Guild Master Taylor smiled meaningfully.

A bead of cold sweat rolled down little Merlin's forehead. *Why is this old man here too? What a headache. Why is it so hard to escape Rexam? What should I do? I can faintly feel the cold wind in the air — is Alice coming?*

"Blackmann, end this quickly..."

"Don't worry, Your Majesty. He's just an old man. If I can't beat someone like him, what kind of good-for-nothing am I?" Blackmann looked down at the even shorter old Taylor and sensed no threat — he appeared easier to handle than Carl.

Merlin didn't think much of it. Rumor had it that Old Taylor and his son were about equally matched. If Carl couldn't beat Blackmann, then certainly Guild Master Taylor couldn't. *From what I remember, this guy was originally quite ordinary — a single drawing slash was enough to make him retreat.*

"Old man, give it up. Don't come looking for death on your own." Blackmann rumbled gruffly.

"Oh?" An armor of lightning wrapped around Guild Master Taylor, his aura even stronger than Carl's!

"Hmph!" Blackmann let out an angry snort, his surrounding lightning erupting as he threw a punch straight at Old Taylor!

But Guild Master Taylor's frail, aged figure suddenly vanished mid-air, causing Blackmann to punch only empty space!

"So fast!" Blackmann was greatly alarmed. The opponent's strength was beyond his imagination!

In the blink of an eye, Guild Master Taylor appeared before Blackmann's chest, his fingers extended in a blade stance, carrying the unmistakable momentum of a drawn sword strike.

Thunder crackled in all directions as Guild Master Taylor's palm blade slashed downward, piercing through Blackmann's hardened body.

The battle ended in an instant. One palm strike from Guild Master Taylor had秒杀 Blackmann, sending him into defeat!

"Ah?!" Little Merlin's eyes widened in horror, his little mouth hanging open, his mind completely blank. He was terrified by a guild master who supposedly spent his days just lounging around!

Blackmann... lost in a single exchange?!

This decrepit old man actually had this much strength?!!!

Wait! That palm strike just now...

Why did it feel a bit like my Drawn Sword Slash! =_=

title: Chapter 29 — Escape
content:
Chapter 29 — Escape

Volume 21 · Chapter 29

Little Merlin found it rather unbelievable. Blackman was his subordinate, and he knew best how strong she was. Even human powerhouses with far-reaching reputations would have a hard time breaking through her defenses!

Old Tyler managed to pierce Blackman's defense in a single strike, which was clearly unbelievable!

What surprised Merlin even more was Old Tyler's technique. Using his hand as a blade, each swing carried a hint of the same spirit as Merlin's iaijutsu draw-cut, exuding a very familiar, grim aura!

Little Merlin couldn't help but take another good look at Old Tyler. The old man rarely appeared at the guild, living a life like a retired pensioner day in and day out. Who would have thought that when he got serious, he'd be so difficult to deal with?

It seemed that contrary to his appearance of being half-buried in yellow earth, Old Tyler truly had his own unique strengths to serve as guild master. At the very least, his ability to put knowledge into practice was truly astonishing!

"Huh!?" Uncle Carl stared blankly, his heart thundering as he thought: A single strike broke her defense!? What technique was that? He'd never seen the old man use it before!

"Though I am advanced in years, I wonder if I still have the qualification to fight you," Old Tyler said with a serious expression, electricity coursing through his body. Unlike Carl's flashy锋芒, his power was restrained yet razor-sharp!

"Uh!"

Blackman's face went pale, cold sweat dripping from her forehead. She clearly hadn't expected this unassuming old man to be such a tough opponent.

Dammit! Why is this guy's attack so fierce!? He broke through my defense so easily!

And that move... it had a bit of the Demon Lord's draw-cut about it. He was trying to kill me in one strike!

Enduring severe pain in her abdomen, Blackman realized that although Old Tyler had broken her defense, it wasn't fatal. With a formidable enemy before her, she had to find a way to escape.

After all, Blackman had already delayed them for no small amount of time. If this continued, Alice would catch up, making it nearly impossible to get away.

"Old man, I'll remember this injury. If there's a chance, I'll definitely carve a hole in your body!"

Before the words had fully left her mouth, Blackman's entire body trembled, instantly summoning a terrifying torrent of lightning that swept around her, attempting to force Old Tyler back so she could slip away.

"Leave the child!" Old Tyler roared, trying to rescue little Merlin. But the lightning torrent was so fearsome that it literally flung him backward!

Lightning crossed and cracked like depth charges, exploding with thunderous force!

The powerful shockwave forced both Old Tyler and Carl to retreat!

When the fierce electric light finally dissipated, both Blackman and little Merlin had vanished from the spot, nowhere to be seen.

"He got away, and we couldn't even save Merlin's nephew..." Uncle Carl frowned, feeling that the situation was becoming more troublesome.

"I never expected them to still have the strength to resist at the end. This demon is no ordinary one," Old Tyler said, hands behind his back, stroking his beard.

"That demon seemed to have some kind of hesitation, never using full force throughout the fight," Uncle Carl said seriously.

"Yes, I have a feeling something is suspicious about the demon suddenly attacking Rexem. There might be a conspiracy behind it..." Old Tyler, the guild master, muttered meaningfully.

"Old man, what technique did you just use? You broke through the demon's defense with a single strike. Was that also the Thunder Strike Combat Art?" Carl recalled the hand-blade strike from earlier and couldn't help but ask.

"Hmph, so the brat is finally willing to ask humbly? I wonder how much you picked up just now..." Old Tyler paused, then leisurely said, "That was inspired by Merlin's draw-cut technique. I spent a long time carefully studying it and improved upon our family's Thunder Strike Combat Art, using the hand as a blade to create a new martial art. It's faster, more ferocious, and more lethal than before. For now, let's call it the Thunder Palm combat art."

"Thunder Palm combat art?..." Uncle Carl fell silent, secretly admiring his father. The hand-blade strike he'd just used was indeed somewhat similar to Merlin's draw-cut. He never would have imagined that the old man, who was usually quiet and low-key, secretly studied so many things. Drawing inspiration from Merlin to improve the family combat art — in that regard, he could never compare to his father.

A burst of cold wind swept past. Alice rushed desperately toward this location, but she was still one step too late.

Her expression was panicked and distraught. Upon reaching Old Tyler, she immediately asked anxiously, "Did a fight just happen here with a demon?"

"That's correct." Old Tyler nodded, adding, "Unfortunately, it got away."

"What!?" Alice felt dizzy, as though her main support had suddenly been ripped away. Her slender frame swayed unsteadily. Merlin... had been taken away by that bastard demon....

"Alice!" Uncle Carl caught her, looking at her seriously and saying, "Calm down. Panicking isn't going to help anything. Merlin's nephew probably won't face a life-threatening danger. When the demon fought me, it still cared about the child's safety. I think they definitely need him alive. That child won't die. Don't worry too much."

Alice steadied herself, calming her anxious mind. She reasoned that the other party certainly wouldn't kill Merlin, but would forcibly take him back to the Demon Lord Palace.

If things developed to the worst possible scenario, she might have to go to the Demon Lord Palace alone, facing countless vicious demons. Whether she could rescue Merlin was far from certain!

"I know that. I have to go save that child. I can't waste time here...."

"....You're in bad condition. Are you really okay?" Uncle Carl saw Alice's state and felt slightly worried in his heart. Ralf's death was a huge loss to the guild. If something happened to Alice too, the guild probably truly couldn't bear it.

"Alice, wait a moment. How about I help you post a bounty task among the adventurers? As long as this demon hasn't left human territory, we should get news soon," Old Tyler suggested, recommending mobilizing adventurers spread across the world. In that case, the demon probably couldn't run far.

"No! No need!" Alice suddenly raised her head in alarm, firmly rejecting Old Tyler's suggestion.

"Why? Posting a bounty task would still be quite useful..." Old Tyler didn't quite understand Alice's big reaction.

"....I still want to find him myself. Please don't get involved. I can handle this alone," Alice said hesitantly, thinking: Merlin and Blackman are both demons. Post a bounty task? Were they afraid people wouldn't know Merlin's background? The safest approach this time was to rely on herself!

It was then that Hobbs and Price, two brothers in hardship, finally arrived, panting heavily from exhaustion.

"Is it over? So fast! Didn't you say there was a demon? We can't even see a shadow of it..." Hobbs scratched his head.

"It already escaped," Uncle Carl answered helplessly.

"It escaped!?」 Upon hearing this, Price instantly became excited, puffing out his chest and boasting nonstop:

"Curse it! I guess it ran fast enough. Otherwise, I definitely would've let it taste the might of the Rexem Guard Captain!"

"You don't know, I just fought this demon for three hundred rounds. If I hadn't drunk so much wine today, I definitely would've taken it down!"

"Someone dares to cause trouble in my territory without even doing some reconnaissance first. Let me tell you, back in my mercenary days, I was also a notorious figure~"

title: Chapter 30 — Swordpoint Morgan
content:
Chapter 30 — Swordpoint Morgan

Volume 21 · Chapter 30

“You're pretty awesome...” Karl chuckled nervously, thinking to himself that Price was a different person when he wasn't drunk.

“I need to report this to the Baron. The damage is significant — over 20 people in one house were killed...” Price muttered under his breath.

“? ? ?” Alice was shocked, sensing something was off. “Twenty people were killed?”

“Yeah, they were all local thugs who hung around doing nothing. I don't know why the demon killed them?” Price replied, even he felt the demon was targeting specific people.

Alice lowered her head, her expression shifting rapidly. Based on what she knew of Merlin, he wasn't the type to kill indiscriminately — he was actually quite restrained.

And since Merlin couldn't even beat a kid his own age right now, it had to be Blackman who did it!

...But Blackman only wanted to bring Merlin back to the Demon Lord's Palace. What could have driven him to kill?

Alice couldn't figure it out. The sudden death of twenty humans seemed random, unless demons are inherently violent and driven by a killing instinct.

“So there really is a demon hiding in Rexham? That means the rumors about Lady Helena being a demon are false — the real demon is someone else. It's highly likely this attacker.” Hobbs rubbed his chin, recalling the gossip he'd collected.

“...Do you have evidence?” Price asked cautiously.

“I heard the rumor that the Secret Room is a demon's lair originally came from those idle thieves. Maybe the demon killed them to cover it up. Today's attack on Rexham fits — they killed to silence, then accidentally ran into your guard team.” Hobbs nodded, thinking this made sense.

Alice listened and felt more uneasy. This didn't match the insider information she had — it sounded like someone was setting things up.

Blackman only arrived in Rexham recently, so he couldn't be connected to the old rumors about the Secret Room. That's a separate issue.

But why would Blackman stir up trouble and kill twenty people? That requires deeper investigation.

Alice fell silent, pondering. It seemed strange that Blackman would do something unrelated to his goal — like a key piece of information was missing.

Everyone else agreed with Hobbs, especially since there was a pretty lady involved.

“Right! I've been saying it — Lady Helena, with her curves and charm, couldn't possibly be a demon!” Price, a regular at the Secret Room, didn't want it to close. “Now I see it was just slander. The real demon is out there. I'll put up a notice to clear Lady Helena's name!”

“Exactly!” Hobbs agreed, missing the sight of Helena. “I don't care about curves — I hate seeing good people slandered. Who's going to pay for the loss of business?”

“Wait... you two are only focused on curves and charm...” Karl couldn't help but comment.

“No! As the captain of Rexham's guards, I must be fair and truthful. Justice is my motto. Don't insult my profession, Karl!” Price insisted seriously.

“That's right! I'm full of justice. I can't stand to see the weak get hurt, so I'll save the fallen women of the Secret Room!” Hobbs declared passionately.

“You two jerks... don't make visiting brothels sound so noble...” Karl frowned, speechless.

Alice rubbed her forehead, feeling a headache. She worried about Merlin —

These unreliable old lechers are only defending Helena because she's pretty, right?

I wanted to ask Hobbs for a way to easily catch Blackman, but now...

Forget it.

Far from Rexham, Blackman struggled to carry the young Merlin.

The distance was so great that even if Alice tried to follow, it would take a while. They were temporarily safe.

“...Blackman gasped for breath, sweat pouring down his face, his hand still clutching the wound from Taylor's blow.

Young Merlin looked at Blackman's state and remembered Taylor's hand strike — it was still impressive.

If he wasn't mistaken, Taylor was imitating his own draw-cut technique, and had developed something unique.

Merlin had always been too strong, ignoring the growth of those around him.

Now, as a child, he saw everyone as rare strong fighters.

“Are you okay, Blackman?”

“I'm fine, just a scratch. Not fatal.” Blackman's color improved as the wound began to scab.

“You're my subordinate, and you got beaten by a human old man? That's embarrassing. Your training isn't good enough...” Young Merlin said with an air of authority, just like a boss scolding an employee.

“No, Your Majesty!” Blackman blushed, embarrassed. “I underestimated him for a moment and got caught off guard. That hand-blade technique is strong — if he'd been more skilled, he might have killed me.

“What are you trying to say?” Young Merlin frowned.

“The power of that strike reminded me of you. I admit I panicked... but the real issue is I was protecting you. It's hard to fight two enemies with one hand, and I couldn't even transform. If I had my hammer, I'd crush their heads.”

“So... I'm your burden?” Young Merlin's face darkened.

“In a way, yes.” Blackman said sadly. Without needing to care for Merlin, he wouldn't have been so vulnerable.

Young Merlin thought hard. He realized he should stay hidden to avoid interfering with Blackman.

To cover his embarrassment, Merlin cleared his throat and walked north, calling his subordinate.

“Let's not talk about this. We're out of Rexham. Our goal is the Morgan family. Let's go!”

“...Blackman followed, picking up the young Merlin and putting him on his shoulder. “Your Majesty, I have a bad feeling. If we don't tell Lady Alice, will she kill me?”

“Don't worry, Black... this is just your imagination...” Young Merlin patted his head, sitting on his shoulder.

“It's just a feeling.”

(*><)/)★

title: Chapter 31 — Opportunity Arrives
content:
Chapter 31 — Opportunity Arrives

Volume 21 · Chapter 31

A week later, boom boom—one

Two saluting guns boomed across the sky of London, signaling that a grand event was about to take place.

The Thistle Knights, dressed in finely crafted armor, formed a parade over a hundred meters long, marching toward the distant Lixian.

The Queen herself led the charge and issued a proclamation, designating the first foreign Thistle Knight in British history.

Alice, the young mithril adventurer from Lixian, had first shown her prowess in suppressing the undead of the former kingdom.

She then carved her way through countless trials and tribulations, emerging into the public eye during the pacification of the French internal strife, becoming a renowned adventurer.

Now, personally titled by Elizabeth as a Foreign Thistle Knight, this was expected by many, though objections still lingered.

On this journey, three Thistle Knights accompanied Elizabeth to Lixian: Morrison, Katherine, and Cladi.

Mesfillet stayed behind to guard the capital, and as for the Second Thistle Knight Seth, he had long since left the capital.

"Is it really okay to appoint this adventurer as a Foreign Thistle Knight? This position carries great authority, and many times we can't treat them as our equals. I'm skeptical." Katherine whispered, clearly not pleased about the Queen's decision to title an adventurer as a Foreign Thistle Knight.

"Don't worry. I've met Alice-sama, and she is a noble, righteous person. I believe making her a Foreign Thistle Knight is the correct choice." Cladi said seriously.

Morrison hesitated and couldn't help but interject, "Actually, besides Alice-sama, there's a more suitable candidate. Recently, there's been quite a bit of support for them, and perhaps the Crown hasn't considered things thoroughly enough."

"A more suitable candidate? Who?" Cladi turned around to ask.

"Just... Elkin the Great Swordsman. This guy is equally prestigious, and many people hope he'll take on the role of Foreign Thistle Knight."

"This absolutely won't do." Cladi frowned and waved his hand to reject Morrison's suggestion.

"Why? Could it be that Cladi-sensei has his own thoughts on this?" Morrison asked curiously.

"Elkin the Great Swordsman's identity remains unclear, always elusive like a dragon. How can someone whose background we don't even know be made a Foreign Thistle Knight?" Cladi voiced his opinion.

"..." Morrison was left speechless. If a reliable person was needed for the Foreign Thistle Knight position, then Elkin the Great Swordsman was definitely out of the question.

"Whether it's the adventurer Alice or Elkin the Great Swordsman, neither is suitable for the role of Foreign Thistle Knight. Simply put, we shouldn't be bringing outsiders from the knightly order into the inner circle." Katherine insisted stubbornly.

"Katherine, I know you don't want to add uncertainty to the knightly order, but all twelve Thistle Knights have lost half of their members. We need fresh blood injected into our ranks." Cladi countered.

The three of them arguing caught the attention of Elizabeth in the royal carriage. She pulled back the curtain and leaned her head out to look at the three below.

"What are you talking about? Do you have any interesting stories to share with me?"

SE /

Katherine and Morrison both fell silent, pretending nothing had happened.

Although they had reservations about Elizabeth's decision, they were just engaging in idle chatter, not planning to actually protest.

"..." Elizabeth looked at Morrison and Katherine's reactions and asked in confusion, "What's wrong with you two?"

"Your Majesty, you're overthinking it. They were just arguing about whether to eat white bread or black bread today." Cladi smiled warmly, bowed, and said, "This journey is tiring. Please rest more, Your Majesty. When we arrive at Lixian and meet the new knight, there's no way to do it without being in top condition."

"I know. After this, the rest is up to you, Cladi." Elizabeth smiled brightly.

"Yes sir." Cladi nodded, straightened his back, and signaled the group to set off.

Elizabeth pulled up the carriage curtain and sat back inside. Her smile gradually faded, replaced by an inexplicable sense of panic.

She clutched her skirt, and dark lines trickled down her temples like waterfalls, seemingly inexplicably afraid of this journey.

Based on the information gathered, Alice is Elkin the Great Swordsman's wife...

What should I do? We're about to go to Lixian. Maybe I'll easily run into that man.

Thinking back to what happened in the wooden hut, she still felt deeply ashamed!

She really didn't want to see that rogue Merlin again, hoping this time she wouldn't be forced into doing something strange...

As the solemn horns sounded, the Queen's entourage began to depart, grandly leaving London.

Many children ran along the banks of the Thames, waving the fluttering British flag.

Blake Man hid his horns under his hat, and his tall figure stood out sharply in the crowd.

He gazed at the slowly departing knightly procession, beginning to flex his muscles and wait for nightfall.

Little Merlin sat on Blake Man's shoulder, giving her a better view.

The royal carriage and familiar-looking knights rode off one after another.

Little Merlin realized that with this force leaving, the capital would be rid of many troublesome characters, and it seemed like the time for unchecked chaos was about to begin.

"Oh~ With that ** bitch gone, appointing Alice as a Foreign Thistle Knight is a great opportunity. Let's just strike tonight and tear down the Morgan family estate!"

"** bitch? What do you mean?" Blake Man asked in confusion.

"That's Queen Elizabeth's... breasts are huge, roughly like this..." Little Merlin held up his hands in front of Blake Man, with a meaningful expression, "The kind that can't be contained by both hands. I once grabbed a handful so hard~"

"..."

"...What exactly... Blake Man's eyes widened, caught up in the serious atmosphere, and with a conspiratorial tone said, "Could it be that there's some grand secret here? Does this mean you and Queen Elizabeth have an extremely intimate relationship? Has the entire British Empire broken free from the Church's control and joined our demon race's camp? Truly a wise ruler, adding a strong piece for our clan and restoring our former glory—it won't be long now!"

"Wrong! It's not like that..." Little Merlin furrowed his brow, glanced at his own hands, and said seriously, "My hands once attacked the chest of the most noble woman in Britain, meaning the entire empire has been tainted by our demons. That soft touch... mmm, yes, it's so wonderful..."

"By conquering Queen Elizabeth, you're indirectly conquering this land? Truly a wise ruler..." Blake Man looked at Little Merlin with admiration, then suddenly exclaimed, "Bullshit!"

"You're just bragging about grabbing Queen Elizabeth's breasts!"

title: Chapter 32 — Eyes Meet (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 32 — Eyes Meet (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 21 · Chapter 32

In the evening, the Morgan family's manor was brightly lit, with guards holding torches to illuminate the courtyard.
After Lei killed the Morgan patriarch, he temporarily took over all matters of the merchant guild, becoming the de facto ruler.
However, this situation could not last long, as Morgan merchants continuously shipped gold coins to Bristol Port, this abnormal movement drew the attention of the city guard.
Recently, outside the merchant guild, guards would patrol from time to time, as if to prevent anyone from leaving the manor in large numbers—?
During the day, Elizabeth and several important Thorn Knight squadrons had just left the London Royal City.
In the evening, the Morgan family's manor immediately took action; Luoqili decided to act tonight, secretly sending Helena out of the royal city to Bristol Port to conduct the final transaction with the members of the dark guild, Phoenix.
“Lei, is everything ready?” Luoqili asked.
“Everything is ready; the last few bags of gold coins and valuable items are already on your carriage, all that's left is to load that demon woman.”
Lei responded with a bow, adding, “But that woman is resisting fiercely; she’s not obedient.”
“It’s no problem; give her a shot of the drug, and she’ll calm down soon.” Luoqili paused, taking out Lei’s slave contract from his bosom, “You’ve done well; I’m satisfied. When tomorrow’s sun rises, I will tear up this slave contract, and you’ll be free, Lei.”
“Thank you for your mercy, young master.” Lei lowered his head, his eyes showing a hint of fervor.
“After regaining your freedom, what do you plan to do?” Luoqili asked meaningfully.
“..-. I want to return to my hometown, Rome, to see the vast fields of sunflowers.” Lei raised his head and said softly, “Countless nights, I have dreamed only of these things; I think this is what I need most.”1.
“You will return to your hometown; I wish you well.” Luoqili patted Lei’s shoulder.
In the secret dungeon beneath the Morgan family's manor, ding! ding! ding!
Constantly, the sound of hammering came, echoing in the deep, confined space.
Helena repeatedly struck the shackles that limited her magic and battle energy against the hard walls.
Trying to break free with brute force, as long as she could use magic, escaping from here would not be difficult.
However, this self‑harm‑like action persisted for a long time; her hands were covered in wounds, yet the shackles remained unmoved.
. Huff..... Helena sighed, mentally exhausted as she sat down, “Damn it!”
Helena felt despondent inside; she never imagined she would fall to such a state, and could only hope for rescue from outside.
But so much time has passed, and there hasn’t been a whisper from the outside world; perhaps now no one even knows she’s imprisoned here.
“You haven’t given up yet, Miss Demon?” Luoqili appeared outside the dungeon, the flickering torchlight illuminating this pirate’s son.
“What are you doing here?! Don’t show up in front of me, you make me sick!” Helena’s eyes were full of hostility.
“You’ve already been reduced to a prisoner, yet your temper is still awful; you’d be better off improving your attitude to lessen the physical suffering.” Luoqili opened the dungeon door and slowly approached Helena.
Although Luoqili is an ordinary person who cannot use magic or martial arts, the sealed Helena is no different from an ordinary person.
Luoqili obviously would not fear a tiger with its teeth pulled out; otherwise he would run faster than anyone. Sink
“What are you planning to do? Better stay away from me, or you’ll regret it.” Seeing Luoqili enter the cell, Helena instantly became alert, “Don’t think you can imprison me now; if my demon companions track you down, you will surely die!”
“Do you think I’d fear any demon if I laid hands on you?” Luoqili violently grabbed Helena’s throat and shoved her hard against the cold wall, “I’ll tell you, there’s nothing in this world I fear; I’ve crawled out of the abyss of death countless times and have long forgotten what fear is.”
“......... Helena struggled to her feet, feeling difficulty breathing.
. Come on..... Luoqili took out a syringe filled with the incapacitating agent, a few drops of the liquid surfacing on the sharp needle, “Let’s go to the final stop; someone very much wants you.
Helena stared wide‑eyed in terror, watching the needle approach her inch by inch, “...Don’t!”
Luoqili showed no expression, driving the syringe’s needle into Helena’s neck and injecting the full dose of the incapacitating agent, enough to keep her unconscious for a long time.
Helena wearily closed her eyes, her body went limp and collapsed on the ground, twitching for a moment before becoming completely still.
Luoqili exhaled, just about to lift Helena up, when suddenly—
Boom!
—a thunderclap exploded, shattering the night’s silence; the entire dungeon trembled nonstop.
Luoqili’s face darkened; he lifted his head, sweating, thinking..
What happened?
According to plan, as soon as night fell, Blakeman launched a sudden assault on the Morgan manor, catching everyone off guard.
Blue lightning kept arcing, turning night into day; the guards holding torches were repeatedly electrocuted to the ground, twitching uncontrollably.
This time, Blakeman did not bring little Merlin with him, to avoid being overly distracted should he face a strong opponent and find it hard to unleash his powers.
Little Merlin hid in a corner of the manor, near the back door, watching Blakeman battle this group of humans.
Anyway, little Merlin couldn’t help much at this point; it would be better to try to find Helena’s location.
“Where is Miss Helena? You bunch of despicable humans!” Blakeman roared, —punching a guard, it was just like a cat falling into a mouse hole.
Suddenly, Lei’s body surged with golden battle energy, attacking from an extremely tricky angle, he raised his white blade and fiercely chopped at Blakeman.
Blakeman’s heart jolted; he retaliated with a thunder‑charged heavy punch, deflecting the vicious white blade, “You despicable villain!”
Lei slightly furrowed his brow, striking Blakeman’s chest with his other hand’s black small shield!
However, Blakeman’s physical strength was truly formidable; his body — ~ shook, sending Lei retreating several meters!
Lei slowly lifted his head, his expression grim, thinking, “What tremendous strength; not easy to deal with.”
“Are you the leader here? Tell me! Where is Helena?!” Blakeman’s body crackled with lightning.
Lei bent slightly, tapping his shield’s edge with his naval knife, taunting, “If I win, I’ll tell you.”
“Courting death!” Blakeman surged with furious thunder and launched a fierce strike— “Listen
In the distance, little Merlin saw the two entangled in combat and decided to sneak off to look for Helena; as a result, he discovered a rather conspicuous carriage at the back door, loaded with sack after sack.
What’s going on? Why is a fully loaded carriage parked at the back door?
Little Merlin laboriously climbed into the carriage, untied a sack, and instantly golden light flashed, nearly blinding his eyes.
“Money! So much money! I’m going to get rich! Has the goddess of fortune finally favored me? Or am I dreaming....”.
Little Merlin dove into the sack, frantically grabbing coins and stuffing them into his pants pockets, thinking a pie had fallen from the sky, laughing until he couldn’t close his mouth.
At that moment, Luoqili walked out of the manor, Helena slung over his shoulder; he already knew what had happened—the demons had truly come to rescue Helena, and if they didn’t escape now, it would be too late.
Thus, Luoqili hurried to the carriage, tossed the unconscious Helena aboard, preparing to flee immediately, but who knew a cry of pain came from the carriage.
“Ouch! Who is it?!”
Little Merlin crawled out of the pile of gold coins, saw the panicked Luoqili, and the two locked eyes, falling into a heavy silence—
Luoqili:
Little Merlin:

title: Chapter 33 — Expressing Respect (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 33 — Expressing Respect (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 21 · Chapter 33

The two stared at each other wide-eyed for a full three seconds, both unable to determine the other's identity.

Little Merlin thought: Who is this guy? Could he be a merchant guild guard?

Loghry thought: Who the hell is this? Where did this brat come from, climbing onto my carriage?

"Who are you?" Loghry spoke first.

"..."

Little Merlin felt a surge of panic inside. He glanced down at what he'd just tossed onto the carriage, and what he saw made his blood run cold — it was Helena, the very person he was searching for!

The unconscious Helena lay limp on the carriage, surrounded by full sacks of gold coins, completely unaware of what was happening outside.

These were the ones who held Helena hostage? I just handed myself over!

Little Merlin looked up anxiously at Loghry, then quickly unslung the black bag from his back, intending to pull out the head of Medusa, the Lord of Chaos, and finish him off right there.

Merlin no longer dared to underestimate anyone. A child's body had poor combat capability, and even an ordinary adult was a formidable opponent for him.

"You damn—"

His curse cut short. Loghry had already sensed something was wrong. He suspected that even if this was just a brat, it could be an accomplice who had snuck in to rescue Helena.

Without giving Little Merlin any chance to resist, Loghry lightning-fast struck the black bag out of his hand, sending it flying to the ground and robbing him of any means to fight back.

"Ugh!" Inside, Little Merlin immediately bent to grab Medusa's head, but Loghry's fingers clamped around his throat before he could reach it.

"Brat!? Where did you come from!? Wanting to save someone? Then die with her!" Loghry grabbed Little Merlin by the neck with both hands, squeezing harder and harder, determined to choke him to death.

"Cough! Cough!" Little Merlin's eyes rolled back as his consciousness blurred. He struggled desperately, raking his nails at Loghry's face, gouging at his nose and eyes.

"You little—! Seeking death!"

Loghry screamed in agony as his eyes were clawed, and he grappled with Little Merlin.

Just how weak was he, to find it so difficult to strangle a mere child?

Loghry pinned Little Merlin against the edge of the well, pouring all his strength into his grip, cursing through gritted teeth.

"Die for me!"

"...Ghk...ghk..." Little Merlin's eyes bulged, his breathing weakening. Just as he was about to lose consciousness, he suddenly kicked out with his short legs, driving his foot hard into Loghry's chin!

"Gah!" Loghry's jaw throbbed with pain, forcing him to let go. But in that moment, Little Merlin fell into an even more dangerous situation — he plummeted straight into the well! Splash!

Water splashed everywhere as Little Merlin thrashed frantically in the water. He couldn't swim anyway; falling into a well meant he'd have no room to resist at all, only to meekly wait for death.

"Neewa! Cough! Spit!"

"Haha..." Loghry peered into the well and saw Little Merlin's wretched state, mocking him. "So you're a landlubber? Wasted all that effort on you. Don't be so reckless next life, kid. Kids should just behave~"

Little Merlin glared hatefully at Loghry as his body gradually sank, until finally only bubbling air rose to the surface.

Loghry felt relieved, turned around, and sat back on the carriage. He yanked the reins hard and sped away through the back gate.

He didn't know if Bre would win on his end, but the frequent flashes of lightning made him uneasy. Better to leave early — that was safer.

Inside the bubbling well, Little Merlin used his last reserves of strength to thrash around, grabbing hold of a floating object on the surface and dragging himself up with all his might.

"Haa... haa..."

Little Merlin was soaked from head to toe, gasping heavily. He felt as though he'd almost drowned, and his terrified eyes still trembled with lingering fear.

He slowly came to his senses and gnashed his teeth in rage. If he hadn't taken the wrong medicine, he'd have slashed that bastard to pieces!

Little Merlin looked down. He had assumed he'd grabbed a piece of floating wood, but to his surprise, it was a bloated corpse.

His body, already fat, had grown even more swollen from soaking in water for so long — pale all over, with an extremely grotesque appearance. It was that man Morgan.

This unlucky shady merchant had been killed by Bre and dumped straight into the well, not knowing he'd accidentally saved Merlin's life!

Little Merlin gazed at Morgan's twisted face and recalled the wealthy merchant who had looked down on him at the London Guild. It all suddenly clicked.

"...Aren't you the head of the Morgan family? You've already died here? But those guards outside—"

Little Merlin frowned, thinking of a series of possibilities. Before he arrived, a rebellion must have already occurred at the Morgan Merchant Guild. The real master was no longer the wealthy man beneath him?

Good heavens! Why did he feel like he was being set up? Was he about to be framed by the mastermind?

Rallying his spirits, Little Merlin stood up on the corpse and scanned around. He noticed a ladder on the well wall?

When Little Merlin climbed out of the well, he found that Loghry had long since disappeared. And Helena, who had been right there, was gone again—

"Darn it!"

Meanwhile, the two warriors Blackman and Bre were locked in fierce combat, nearly tearing the Morgan Guild apart.

Blackman's moves were broad and powerful, accompanied by devastating lightning attacks that frequently sent Bre crashing to the ground.

Yet Bre was like a man without a sense of pain — even with several broken bones, he kept getting back up.

Such a powerful fighting will made Blackman startled. How many times did he need to knock the man down before he couldn't get up again?

Bre held his round shield and wielded a navy knife in reverse grip, his sharp blade techniques targeting Blackman's weaknesses. One careless moment and he'd be dead.

Blackman's clothes were slashed open, and his body bore several bleeding knife wounds. Dodging the enemy's wild slashes, he countered with a thunderous punch.

Bre widened his eyes, raising his round shield to block. A deafening boom erupted, lightning surging skyward!

Bre's figure twisted as he took Blackman's attack head-on. His arm bones were shattered, the shield was dented and deformed, and a gruesome fist mark remained.

Blackman roared, adding a lightning upcross to slam directly into Bre's chest, the overwhelming power of the lightning unleashing a fierce gale!

"Die!"

"Cough!"

Blood sprayed from Bre's mouth as he was slammed into the ground, creating spiderweb-like cracks.

Yet the next second, Bre got up again, propping himself up with the navy knife on one knee, staring blankly at Blackman.

"...You can still get up? Are you a cockroach? No matter how much I hit you, you won't die." Blackman bared his teeth with hostility.

"Compared to the heavy injuries I suffered in the Roman Colosseum..." Bre narrowed his eyes and commented, "...it's still a bit lacking."

"What a big mouth. Hope you can stay this tough." Blackman suddenly reached his hand down into his pants.

"Hm? What are you doing?" Bre froze, confused. "Are you scratching an itch somewhere at a time like this?"

"No!" Blackman grinned wickedly and said solemnly—"

"You're pretty good. I acknowledge you—"

"So let me give you a handjob first, as a sign of my respect!"

title: Chapter 34 — Pain Perception
content:
Chapter 34 — Pain Perception

Volume 21 · Chapter 34

Blackman bathed in blue lightning, dazzling, causing everyone around to open their eyes. Threads of electricity like jumping sprites continuously surged from Blackman's sturdy body. "What is this?" Bray's usually calm face finally showed a hint of astonishment, as if he had seen something unbelievable. The electricity faded, Blackman's strong, tall physique disappeared, replaced by a shapely girl's figure, a bow on her ponytail fluttering in the wind. Blackman wielded the three‑ton thunder demon war hammer in his hand, casually set it on the ground, and with a "bang" smashed a huge pit into the earth! She pushed aside the hair covering her eyes; her muffled voice had completely changed, as if she had become another person— "From now on, I will hammer you until you regret being born into this world—prepare yourself, human!" Bray frowned, still a hint of doubt in his heart: how did this sturdy man suddenly turn into a frail woman? However, from the way she casually set down the war hammer just now, one could tell the weapon wasn't light; this woman's strength was extraordinarily great! "Are you a female demon?" "What? Is there anything surprising about that?" Blackman bared his tiger teeth, unable to resist mocking, "Could it be that you're dazzled by my splendid appearance? A true warrior knows no gender, only victory or defeat." "You're right..." Bray raised his battered round shield, hiding his naval sword behind him, "No matter if you're male or female, even if you're a neutral monster, I will erect a tombstone for you here." "Hmph! As you wish!" Blackman let out a low roar, seized the thunder demon war hammer and leapt up, bringing the force of splitting Mount Hua, and swung down! The sound of thunderous time exploded, lightning shot up into the sky! Under the hammer's blows, the earth rolled like waves! Sand and debris, along with the lightning storm, swept up to 300 feet above London! On the distant, brightly lit palace terrace, Mesfield stood alone, not knowing what he was tinkering with, muttering to himself. "Go die, hurry up and die—choked on water, choked on food, struck by lightning on a rainy day—no matter what, I want you dead." Two guards stood behind Mesfield, watching what seemed like a mentally unstable first‑knight, and couldn't help whispering below. "Hey, Lord Mesfield, what's wrong with you? Why do you look like a resentful spirit..." "I don't know; ever since he came back from the Kingdom of France, he's been like this, cursing someone every day." "This... is exactly like an abandoned, pitiful woman—could he have been screwed over by some man?" "Who knows? Don't look at Lord Mesfield being young; now he shows signs of hormonal imbalance, an early trend of menopause." "I think so too," said one, "Should we advise Lord Mesfield to drink more hot water? I've heard it can solve most women's problems." "...I think if you say that, Lord Mesfield will hit you—you should know that menopausal women are moody." The two nobodies whispered among themselves; Mesfield seemed to sense something, suddenly turned his head and shot a murderous gaze: "What are you whispering down there?" "No, no, no!!!" The two guards dared not move, shaking their heads like rattles, fearful that the moody menopausal woman would redirect her anger. "Hmph!" Mesfield snorted coldly, turned his head away, and continued what he had been doing. In Mesfield's hand was a small doll resembling the masked swordsman Elgin, now pierced with many needles. One could tell without thinking that this was some kind of witchcraft, used to help losers vent their resentment. Not long ago, Mesfield learned this method from Catherine; it is a curse commonly used by some cannibal criminals on the southern sea islands. One makes a doll of the hated enemy, stabs it with needles a hundred times each day; once a certain level is reached, the target will be punished. However, Catherine didn't say this method is basically useless; she just saw Mesfield was in a terrible mood and told him to use the voodoo doll to relieve his gloom. "Mmm-hmm..." Mesfield gazed at the hedgehog‑like Elgin swordsman doll; though he didn't know whether that bastard had been punished, his mood became extremely pleased: "I stabbed that despicable man a hundred times again today—he must be wishing he were dead by now. Let you always insult me; this is retribution!" The two guards listened to Mesfield's mutterings, not daring to breathe, now seriously suspecting that the empire's chief knight's mind has gone wrong, that he is mentally abnormal. Boom boom boom— A shocking roar, the earth trembled slightly. Dazzling and terrifying lightning truly shot up to the heavens, (in a daze illuminating the night like day!) In the city, sand and debris sprayed into the air; the magnificent sight awed everyone! "Eh?!" Mesfield jumped in fright, the doll in his hand fell to the ground, as he looked at the distant commotion— "That... is the direction of the Morgan Guild? What happened!" The terrifying electricity faded; little Merlin hid far away, watching, his eyes barely able to stay open. Helena had already been moved; he had intended to call Blackman to pursue Lochiri. But the fight between Blackman and Bray was intense; little Merlin couldn't get close at all. Blackman lifted the thunder demon heavy hammer from Bray's chest, took a breath, thinking these were finally over— even if matched against an equally strong opponent, they probably couldn't withstand this hammer strike. Bray lay powerless on the ground, expression dull, eyes rolled back, limbs almost twisted as if boneless, chest caved in—this body was dead beyond death. Blackman hoisted the thunder demon heavy hammer onto his shoulder, turned to look for little Merlin, but after just two steps his eyes widened in shock as he heard a strange sound coming from behind! Bray, this seemingly undead monster, despite suffering consecutive lethal blows from Blackman, somehow rose again like a war god, standing firm! "This guy... really human?" Little Merlin's face turned pale with shock, looking at Bray's scar‑covered body, showing no fear of death—Blackman lowered the thunder demon hammer from his shoulder, his eyes filled with disbelief: "What exactly is supporting..." "No way? What terrifying..." "You stand up again? Your head, the dull gaze from beginning to end never changed, as if indifferent to everything." Bray slowly raised his blood‑soaked body, which teetered on the brink, still posing a danger. He bathed in his own hand's broken round shield, abandoning defense, and raised that naval sword once more— Bray threw away himself "Demon, not bad—I finally feel what pain is for the first time?" "Since birth," PS■Just late, thanks for the monthly ticket support. Still three chapters today.

title: Chapter 35 — Encounter (Bonus Update)
