Chapter 35 — Encounter (Bonus Update)

Volume 21 · Chapter 35

"What nonsense are you spouting?" Blake Man's thunder demon war hammer suddenly flashed with fierce lightning.

"I was born without pain sensation, my body is numb to the outside world." Blake's expression was wooden, he didn't care about his own injuries at all, "Because of this, when I was little my parents sold me to the arena, I was trained as a gladiator to entertain countless nobles and officials, day and night I faced not a warm bed and tasty food, but the slave traders' whips and pig slop, at age twelve I stepped onto the arena, when the lion tore open my chest I felt nothing, numb I plunged the dagger into its throat, from that moment I realized that any pain that could drive a normal person mad meant nothing to me, this flesh is like an icy coffin locking my soul, what I yearn for in my heart is..

"....Merlin frowned, thinking it's no wonder he can always get up, suffering attacks without even a scream, turns out he's completely insensate, such a person even if alive is just a walking corpse, right?

"I have no interest in your story, if you want to survive just lie down and don't get up.... Blake Man's maiden honor exudes might without anger, pressure begins to climb steadily.

"I have countless times walked the edge of death, honing my combat skills, all to one day cast off the slave's yoke; tonight is the chance that decides my fate, to walk out alive... only me." Blake's tone was flat yet decisive.

"Oh? I admire you as an unyielding warrior, I've already given you a choice.... Blake Man's demon horns on his head flickered with lightning, behind him unfurled black demon membranes, then his whole body bathed in blue lightning, revealing his true demonic form, like a thunder demon descending from the heavens, 'You're foolish! Humans!!!'"

Lightning frequently flashed in the air as if gone mad, storms erupted, surrounding buildings were instantly flattened!

Blake Man's demonic form was terrifyingly abnormal, his whole body bathed in lightning, his war hammer constantly trembling!

"Fighting you excites me, you're the first opponent who made me feel pain, you've successfully provoked me." Blake gripped his navy blade, golden fighting spirit grew more terrifying, he stepped forward and the earth shattered!

Boom boom boom, a sudden thunderclap—

The two acted simultaneously, charging at each other face to face, neither willing to yield!

Blake Man bathed in lightning, raised his war hammer with both hands, struck out violently, unleashing his destructive power to the extreme!

Blake was like a jungle warrior, dragging his broken body, spinning his navy blade to slash through the lightning, straight for the enemy's throat!

"Damn! The commotion is too big, if this continues.... it'll draw the knights guarding the royal capital!" Merlin felt the wind like a blade, his face went numb, thinking he'd probably just keep letting Blake Man take the blame.

The two were about to decide victory with their final blow, but at this crucial moment—

Blake suddenly stopped, his aura dissipated, his expression filled with disbelief as he kept scratching his throat, as if an invisible hand were choking him.

Blake Man didn't take advantage of his peril to blast Blake into mincemeat; instead, sensing the anomaly, he let the lightning fade and suspended the thunder demon hammer above Blake's head.

What's wrong with this guy? Why did he suddenly stop? Could he have suddenly seen the light... maybe he wants to beg for mercy?

Blake Man looked puzzled at Blake's strange reaction, like a mentally abnormal person flailing about.

"....uh.... Blake scratched his neck, exposing shocking flesh, rolled his eyes and collapsed to the ground, twitching nonstop, "......"

"???" Blake Man's head was full of question marks, completely unable to understand what happened; just moments ago he was full of battle spirit, now he's suddenly cold.

Merlin saw the battle end, stood up confused and shouted, "Hey! Blake Man! When did you learn to kill with the Force?"

"No... no, he's faking it, I didn't even touch him!" Blake Man put on an innocent look, pouted his little mouth and said, "It wasn't me, believe me~"

"Speak normally, stop being cute!" Black lines slid down Merlin's forehead, he would never forget Blake Man's sturdy physique.

"Nauseous, vomit!"

Outside the royal capital of London, Lochiri had already fled far away, sitting in a carriage loaded with gold and Helena, lonely heading for Bristol Port.

Lochiri held Blake's slave contract in his hand, slowly burning in the night, turning to ash drifting in midair.

After ensuring his own safety, he decisively discarded Blake as a useless tool, directly using a single thought as master to kill this gladiator.

"What a pity, Blake...."

"If you didn't chase after some illusory freedom, even if you were willing to follow me just to shake off slave status, you could have lived."

"I fulfilled the promise, returned your freedom, hoping that in hell you can get to see Rome's sunflower as you wish?"

The slave contract is merely a means of coercion, it cannot control the slave's actions.

If the slave isn't even afraid of death, then the slave contract is just a worthless piece of paper.

Lochiri knew Blake wouldn't wholeheartedly follow him, so he could only use the lure of doubtful freedom to tempt him.

If he truly wanted to give Blake freedom, the most direct method would be to personally dispose of this poor soul who knows too much.

Lochiri watched the ash in his hand dissipate, exhaled, gazing at the vast continent under the night sky far away, thinking—

Next, as long as I hand over the demon on the carriage to the people of Phoenix, I will win over the strongest evil organization.

By then I'll have an extra card to oppose the great swordsman Elgin, maybe even enough to kill that mysterious figure.

Father, you really raised a bunch of good-for-nothings back then; the only one who would avenge you is me....

Lochiri will never know that he just brushed past the great swordsman Elgin, missing his lifelong wish by a hair; if he had known, he probably would have jumped into a well to die together with little Merlin!

Late at night, the surroundings were silent wilderness, the road originally empty of people suddenly had someone walking.

A silver-haired girl riding a small donkey approached from the opposite direction, a silver-glinting fine sword at her waist, indeed it was Alice searching everywhere for Merlin! ?

Alice had almost been following Blake Man and Merlin's footsteps, though there was no information along the way, she relied on Merlin's appearance to inquire around, got the right direction, and was about to head for the royal capital of London!

"Damn, why is there still someone coming to the royal capital at this time... Lochiri lowered his

Lochri heard Alice calling him from behind, and he instantly felt flustered, lowering his head even more and silently speeding up the carriage.
Oh no, did this adventurer actually see something? In this wilderness, the chances of slipping away from a mithril-ranked adventurer are very low...
No way! Play dead! Absolutely cannot respond.....
Lochri had no intention of dealing with Alice behind him; he planned to pretend he hadn't heard and slip past.
"Huh?"
Alice furrowed her delicate brows, sensing a hint of strangeness; the other's reaction was like that of someone who'd done something wrong.
I didn't intend to do anything; I just wanted to inquire about Merlin's whereabouts, asking if anyone had seen a burly man with a blond little boy.
At this late hour, running into someone leaving the royal capital here is rather strange....
Alice unwilling to give up, raised her volume again and shouted loudly at Lochri.
"Sir! Please wait a moment! I have something I want to ask!"
"... Lochri shuddered all over, feeling guilty, so the carriage sped up even more; in Alice's eyes it looked like he was fleeing.
"... Alice dismounted her little donkey, magical power surging through her, she waved her hand and constructed a pale gold ice wall in front of Lochri's carriage, blocking his path!
The startled horse neighed several times, nearly throwing Lochri off; a layer of cold sweat trickled down his forehead, his inner fear growing.
Damn it! Is this adventurer not going to let me go?
What should I do? Should I just dismount and run away now?
But after great effort I finally got that demon woman out; if I flee now, all my work would be wasted.
Lochri lowered his head, his eyes darting nervously; he decided to grit his teeth and communicate with Alice, after all most adventurers aren't meddlesome—they're in it for the money.
Alice slowly approached, holding a stick with a carrot tied to it, looking at Lochri who refused to lift his head, "Sir, why are you so nervous seeing me? Do you need any help?"
"No.... Lochri lifted his head, forcing out a faint smile, 'I'm a merchant from the Morgan Consortium, I need to deliver goods overnight to the port, so... I'm in a hurry; could you, Adventurer, not block my way? I have three kids to support at home; if I'm delayed, I won't be able to explain it.'
"Ah... sorry." Alice waved her hand to dispel the massive ice wall, then continued, "You misunderstood, sir; I harbor no ill intent, I just have a few questions for you< =
Lochri's eyes rolled, his heart eased; he had really been close to being scared to death, it was all his overthinking, "May I ask..."
"Have you seen a tall, burly man and a blond little boy together? The boy is about seven or eight, with a bad temper—he gets arrogant to the heavens at the slightest disagreement." Alice gestured with her hands, hoping he'd understand.
Lochri's eyes shifted instantly, because he had indeed just seen those two fellows. Two
A fierce blond little boy, and a hulking demonic brute who attacked the merchant guild.0
Huh? What's going on? They couldn't be working together, could they?
Lochri's face looked grim, his heart leapt up again.
"Huh?" Alice noticed Lochri's tense expression; unlike ordinary people, her female intuition made her sense something increasingly off, "Do you know something?"
Lochri quickly hid his tension, putting on a smile, "Sorry, Adventurer, I haven't seen them; as a merchant I've seen all sorts of fish and dragons mixed together, but I truly haven't seen a burly man paired with a little boy."
"........ Alice stared into Lochri's eyes, feeling a bit disappointed.
"Can I leave now? The cargo behind me can't be delayed.
Lochri showed a troubled expression, his tone pleading.
"Sorry for the trouble." Alice stepped aside, no longer blocking the path, after all she said she had three kids to support; hindering someone's business would be a big guilt.
"...." Lochri secretly breathed a sigh of relief, his back soaked in cold sweat—don't even mention the pressure Alice put on him; fortunately this adventurer isn't overly sharp, otherwise things would have gone wrong. Alice watched Lochri's carriage recede, various feelings of unease making it hard for her to calm down. Just as Alice was about to look away, she suddenly noticed on Lochri's horse, from a gap in the stacked sacks, a slender, pale white arm darting out! ?
Alice's heart gave a start; she hurriedly rubbed her eyes, but saw nothing—nightfall somewhat limited her vision.
Just now... what was that? A human arm?
Could it be because it's getting late and I misread things.... Alice stood in place for a moment, unable to let go, so she turned back, mounted her little donkey, turned the carrot on the stick 180°, gave up going to the royal capital of London, and instead followed the suspicious carriage ahead—this merchant seemed off! The Morgan Consortium's smoke cleared, and little Merlin and Blackman calmed down.
"Helena was just taken away by a young man; we missed our chance." Little Merlin said quietly, having earlier picked up the head of the Chaos King Medusa and now carrying it again on his back.
"What should we do? Should we chase now?" Blackman, having resumed his male form at Merlin's request, indeed still had a strong posture that looked normal.
"We can't catch up; it's been too long, that bastard might have already run far off..." Little Merlin rubbed his forehead in a headache.
"So... we don't know where Helena was taken; we've just been busy for nothing?" Blackman sighed, having again taken the blame and put in effort for nothing.
"This really is a problem.... Little Merlin worried, who knows where that vicious brat is taking Helena? But at this moment, an unexpected person burst in—Mershield darted forward like lightning, scooping up little Merlin from the ground, brandishing his sword at Blackman, 'Damned demon! What gall! To dare set foot on British soil! Still wreaking havoc and slaughter here! Today I shall execute you on the spot in the name of the First Thorn Knight!'
"Eh? ? ?" Blackman startled, inexplicably having taken another blame, but seeing little Merlin in someone else's arms, he reflexively said, "Give that kid back to me!"
"Dream on! As a knight, I have the duty to protect every citizen of the kingdom; you lot of vicious demons, are you trying to eat the child's innards?" Mershield's battle aura surged, his powerful reply: "Unforgivable!"
"Shout!" Blackman felt a bit tricky; he'd just finished a battle, his aura depleted, and now another comes? This is the rhythm of a war of attrition!
Little Merlin was held in Mershield's embrace, he lifted his head and looked, feeling depressed, thinking, "Why does this female knight appear everywhere?" Please just let me go!
"Don't be scared, kid! I, Mershield, want to soothe Merlin by tucking him into my chest for a sense of safety. But Mershield has never cared for a child, his control over strength is poor. So he pressed down on Merlin's head and slammed it hard against his own unyielding knight's breastplate, making a 'puh' sound!"
"... not a benefit.... Little Merlin saw stars, his eyes and mouth skewed, shaking as he stuck out his tongue and fainted, 'Hoo~ more~ oh~~'
For a moment the atmosphere turned awkward; the two stared at the unconscious little Merlin, unable to speak—Mershield: Blackman:卜°(; 0n0)

title: Chapter 38 — Female Knight (Extra Update)
content:
Chapter 38 — Female Knight (Extra Update)

Volume 21 · Chapter 38

After hearing Mesfield's conclusion, the knights whispered among themselves, unsure whether what she said was the truth. After all, no matter how you look at it, the demon attacked the Morgan Merchant Guild, and saying it's two completely unrelated things is still hard to understand. A knight said, "The demon's attack on the merchant guild and the death of Guild President Morgan are two separate matters? Lord Mesfield, you're not just spouting nonsense, are you?" Mesfield replied, "How would I be spouting nonsense?" She turned, earnestly explaining, "You just said that Guild President Morgan has been dead for a long time—who's been running the guild?" Then—it must be a familiar face. If it's not someone from inside the guild, the president would have been suspected long ago after disappearing for so many days. The answer is obvious: Morgan died in an internal disturbance within the guild; the killer is one of their own. As for that demon? Its true target might not be Morgan, nor the entire guild, but rather the killer. I never expected that internal strife had already happened here; the master of this place is no longer Morgan.... Little Merlin narrowed his eyes, staying silent, thinking, "Indeed, that's the case. Blackman and I came just to find Helena—who knows how that fat rich merchant died?" This matter is very suspicious. Although the demon's intrusion into our territory is truly hateful, the real enemy... probably still lurks in the shadows.... Mesfield lowered her head, thinking, constantly considering possibilities. The knights whispered privately; Chapman, the knight captain holding Little Merlin, heard Mesfield's words and suddenly remembered something, raising his hand. Chapman, a squad leader in the Purple Orchid Knights, had been doing fairly well; secretly he was a supporter of the great swordsman Elgin. "My lord, I have something to report." "Speak." Mesfield replied. "I've received some news: there are signs of pirate activity at Bristol Port, and recently the Morgan Merchant Guild has been secretly transporting treasure to that port. These two things... could there be some connection?" Chapman reported an important piece of information. "Pirate activity traces..." Mesfield widened her eyes slightly, looked at the corpse of old Mr. Morgan on the ground, a flash of insight: "It's pirates, pirates looted this place, raiding the guild... they probably planned this for a long time, though it's still unclear why they provoked the demon...." Little Merlin perked up his ears, becoming agitated, because he'd obtained an important piece of information: Bristol Port. He had no doubt that the bastard who tried to choke him was a pirate; the fishy stench was almost making him faint. Little Merlin thought, Bristol Port? It seems to be in Manchestercity? He once worked there as a male PR, meeting many upper-class ladies. "Little buddy, you awake?" Chapman noticed Little Merlin opening his eyes, smiling at him. ".....Let go of me! Let go of me!" Little Merlin struggled, breaking free from Chapman's arms. Mesfield slowly approached, half-kneeling in front of Little Merlin, trying to communicate with the little child: "Are you feeling better? You just fainted from the demon's fright...." "Ah? !" Little Merlin rubbed his forehead, rolled his eyes, and said, "Clearly it's your chest that's too hard—what does that have to do with the demon?" "Hahaha, kids really talk nonsense...." Mesfield gave a dry laugh; surrounded by so many knights being blamed by a child, it was still awkward: "You were frightened into unconsciousness by the demon." "No, it's your chest that's hard...." Little Merlin said firmly. Mesfield clicked her tongue disapprovingly, thinking this brat doesn't listen; who raised such a nasty temperament? Thus Mesfield's face darkened, she stared into Little Merlin's eyes, speaking with a hint of threat: "You, are, you, were, frightened, by, the, demon, right?" "Eh!" Little Merlin sucked in a breath of cold air, feeling a hint of killing intent, so nervously he swallowed, trembling, nodded: "Yes... yes, I was frightened...." Mesfield didn't notice Little Merlin's double entendre reply, continuing to ask: "What's your name?" "I... I..." Little Merlin paused, then answered with mischievous glee: "I am Elgin the Great Swordsman! How's that? Aren't you scared?" 口r牡」 玩 The surrounding knights burst into snickers, finding it hilarious that such words came from a little brat who hasn't even grown hair yet. After all, many knights in the royal capital have seen the figure of Elgin the Great Swordsman; he's a grown man. Even if Little Merlin revealed his identity, no one thought much of it, because Elgin the Great Swordsman has many admirers in Britain, mostly kids, and toy swords and mask memorabilia are hot. ".....Mesfield gave a dry laugh, the veins on her forehead twitched; hearing the name Elgin the Great Swordsman made her disgusted, she felt like sending Little Merlin to a mental hospital for a couple of shocks." "Little buddy, don't joke, okay? We're just trying to send you home." "...I don't remember my name..." Little Merlin planned to sneak away, opening his mouth to spout nonsense. "What about your parents? Where do they live? You should at least know that." Mesfield frowned, asking. "I... I can't remember, my head still feels dizzy..." Little Merlin pretended to be in pain, indicating amnesia: don't ask, answer is I don't know. "...." Mesfield sighed, got up with a headache, feeling she couldn't abandon this child, but right now the child's mind isn't clear, and she doesn't know if the parents are reliable; seems like he really was scared silly. "Lord Mesfield, what should we do next?" Chapman lowered his head to look at Little Merlin, full of worry: "Such a small child can't just be abandoned, but it's too late now; I don't know which orphanage could temporarily take him in? Maybe once his emotions settle he'll remember his parents..." "I'm perfectly fine! I don't need looking after! Just let me go!" Little Merlin said in an old-fashioned tone: "You knights, stop meddling, alright? I'm not an orphan at all!!" "...Probably his brain still has issues; what he's saying now isn't from his heart...." Chapman looked at Little Merlin with sympathy: "When my daughter gets angry, she also says she'll run away from home..." "When do I need your pity? You forgot that you secretly asked Elgin the Great Swordsman for an autograph to give your daughter as a birthday gift, didn't you?" Little Merlin retorted angrily. Upon hearing that, Chapman's whole body shuddered; he looked at the little Merlin with disbelief, as if suddenly struck by some small secret? Mesfield thought for a long time, sighed silently, then squatted again, placing her hands on Little Merlin's shoulders, speaking earnestly one by one: "Tonight come home with me: we'll just go to sleep~ (o.w则)"

title: Chapter 39 — Two-Faced (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 39 — Two-Faced (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 21 · Chapter 39

"But there's one thing: you need to behave, okay?" Mersfield advised.
Little Merlin shuddered upon hearing it, not wanting to go home with Mersfield, lest he couldn't escape later, shouting, "No! I don't want to sleep together with you! I want to leave! I have more important things to do!"
The surrounding knights burst into laughter, and even several close friends showed expressions of regret and envy, feeling that Little Merlin was wasting an opportunity.
Even if we disregard the identity of the empire's foremost knight whom everyone admires, Mersfield is still a handsome and graceful beauty.
The chance to sleep together—who knows how many people have secretly thought about it, but they fear they wouldn't survive doing so.
The Mersfield family has served the royal lineage for generations, holding a lofty status; everyone in the family is a knight, and some have even sacrificed their lives to protect the royalty.
"What a blockhead this melon-headed kid is, Miss Windsor invited him to spend a lovely evening together, yet he's not even willing?"
"Young and ignorant—when I was a kid I was just as foolish; an older sister who sold pastries once invited me to her home for tea, but all I remember is eating~"
"I guarantee that in ten years this lad will definitely regret his intestines turning green, missing the peak of his own life!"
The knights whispered among themselves, shaking their heads at Little Merlin, unaware that his inner self was fairly mature and he wanted to rescue Helena as soon as possible.
"More important things? Are you planning to learn all sorts of mischief from Elgin the Great Swordsman?" Mersfield couldn't help but sneer.
Little Merlin felt a few black lines drop onto his forehead, thinking he was being treated like a brat, and that saying anything would be useless.
"You'll stay at my place tonight; tomorrow I'll help you find your parents and send someone to take you home." Mersfield picked up Little Merlin.
"Damn it! Let go of me! I don't want to go back with you!" Little Merlin struggled, but to no avail.
"I understand, since you were seized by demons your emotions are unstable; after a night's rest it might improve considerably.... Mersfield tried to soothe Little Merlin, holding his head, with a 'thud' it struck his own hard chest armor again, 'ah...'"
"I hate~the chest~armor~~" Little Merlin felt dizzy and fainted.
Captain Chapman behind him stared at Little Merlin for a while, couldn't help scratching his head, pondering strangely: It's really ghostly—why would the matter of me asking Elgin the Great Swordsman for an autograph... be known by a little kid? At that time, clearly only I and Elgin the Great Swordsman were around the others? At an altitude of several hundred feet above the royal city, Blackman's demon wings trembled behind him, continually hovering secretly over the heads of the Purple Gold Flower Knights, refusing to leave. Blackman looked anguished, a surge of daring fear rose in his heart, thinking he was too incompetent, failing to protect Merlin— that despicable female knight, she's started tormenting His Majesty again.. )0K. P5ACgcoI Hang in there, I will surely rescue you!
That night, Little Merlin woke up to find himself lying on a large bed.
The furnishings were simple, just a few pieces of furniture and a piece symbolizing femininity, with nothing else.
Nevertheless, that faint, soul-soothing fragrance was still refreshing, and one couldn't help but admire the owner's taste.
Little Merlin sat up on the large bed, anxiously looking around; after two consecutive hits to his chest armor, he narrowly avoided real amnesia, his mind still clear.
"This is Mersfield's room, right?"
Little Merlin calmed down, thinking he must sneak out of here, otherwise Helena would be in danger.
Blackman, as my most loyal subordinate, would never abandon me and flee.
Perhaps he is still circling nearby; as long as I escape, I can meet up with him!
Little Merlin made up his mind, fixed his gaze on the window, deciding to slip out from here—good thing the room is empty now.
However, after Little Merlin laboriously dragged over a chair and looked out the window, he finally understood his situation.
In the distance, the clock tower glittered with lights; this was a seven-story villa on the outskirts away from the bustling market, with his own manor below.
Seven stories? If I jump down now, wouldn't I break my legs in this condition? 24
What should I do? Do I have to stay trapped here forever? This is hopeless! !元
Little Merlin silently got off the chair, stood there blankly, and began to think again—
"Rope... Is there any rope in this room? Anything that could be made into a rope would be good..."
Little Merlin's gaze fixed on the curtains, hesitating a bit, his inner urge began to stir.
Time was pressing; Little Merlin worried that Mersfield might return at any moment, so without further thought he sprang into action.
The curtains and sheets were forcibly pulled down and tied together, but the length wasn't enough, so he then fixed his gaze on the wardrobe.
When Little Merlin opened the wardrobe, he was instantly stunned....
A normal girl's wardrobe is like a treasure chest, surely filled with various bright and splendid outfits, and even Alice is no exception.
But Mersfield is abnormal; his wardrobe contains only a few everyday clothes, and they look quite monotonous.
However, after thinking it over, Little Merlin felt relieved, for Mersfield is a proper knight who usually wears armor, and there's no memory of him ever dressing too flamboyantly.
But the next second, Little Merlin was slapped in the face by his own madness, forcing him to reevaluate this lady knight.
"Huh! ? Heavens, no way... actually.... Little Merlin's eyeballs almost popped out, as if he'd seen something unbelievable, his breathing quickened considerably."
Just above the wardrobe hung several pieces of brightly colored lace thong underwear!?
Amid the few plain everyday garments, these sexy and alluring undergarments stood out strikingly!
Little Merlin, with a strange expression, took the lace thong in his hand and examined it closely.
Among the women he knows, nobody would dare wear such bold underwear, not even his succubus sister would wear something so revealing!
Alice is even more childish, often wearing panties with little bear prints; every time he sees himself, he's left speechless, rolling his eyes.
Come on! Alice, you're an adult—can't you be a bit more mature? A man seeing such boring underwear would turn cold and indifferent!
But really, who would have thought? The stern-browed, big-eyed chief knight of the kingdom, beneath that valiant armor, actually wears such *.*. stimulating underwear, hehe~
Little Merlin revealed a meaningful smile, feeling he had uncovered the secret of a new continent, and reacquainted himself with Windsor. Mersfield this lady knight—turns out she is someone who appears righteous and upright on the outside, yet inside burns with fiery passion—
"I never expected—normally she looks proper and dignified, but I never imagined in private... - tsk tsk..."

title: Chapter 40 — Never Be a Slave
content:
Chapter 40 — Never Be a Slave

Volume 21 · Chapter 40

The rope made from curtains, bedsheets, and a few pieces of clothing was lowered from the window by little Merlin.

At the end of this rope were a few lace thongs fluttering in the wind, looking flimsy and even a bit lewd?

Little Merlin hurriedly poked his head out the window to look, but then, feeling disheartened, he glumly climbed down.

Damn....

I've used everything I could, why is it still not long enough?

Little Merlin tiptoed out of Mersefield's room, pricking up his ears to listen to all kinds of sounds, afraid of being caught and taken back.

He carried a black bag containing Medusa's head, and he would never discard such an important item.

Fortunately, Mersefield had no interest in the brat's parcel, thinking it contained only childish toys.

If Mersefield, out of curiosity, opened the black bag, he would very likely be stared to death by the petrifying gaze!

The narrow corridor was empty, with portraits of men and women hanging on the walls.

They all wore armor, as if telling outsiders the family's glorious history.

The Mersefield family has always been knights guarding the royal lineage; these portraits of ancestors might well have been famous knights of their time.

Little Merlin had given up on weaving his own rope to escape, instead choosing to take a risk and sneak downstairs to slip out the main door.

Looking at the valiant portraits on the wall, little Merlin couldn't help but stare; the Thorn Knights alone in Mersefield's history numbered over ten.

For a family to produce so many high-status knights, it could be considered a prestigious noble house...

Little Merlin sighed, and going downstairs he found a spacious banquet hall.

After evading several servants' patrols, little Merlin reached the second floor, where a faint, aged man's voice came through.

Little Merlin looked toward the source of the voice; at this late hour, a room's light was still on, seemingly a study.

Driven by curiosity, little Merlin sneaked over and pressed his ear to the wall to eavesdrop on what they were discussing so late at night.

In the study, there was an old man whose face was gaunt, yet his eyes sparkled with shrewdness.

He sat in a wheelchair, his legs covered with a blanket; by the faint candlelight beside him, his emaciated frame could be seen.

You say... recently there have been pirates appearing at Bristol Port, directly linked to tonight's attack on the Morgan Merchant Guild? Are you sure? My child..

Believe me.... Mersefield paused, speaking seriously: 'That demon's target is the pirates; the Morgan Merchant Guild's guards are all sacrificial pawns, internal strife has long erupted within the guild, and the guild chief met a miserable death, his body thrown into the well....'

This old man is the current head of the Mersefield family, but his frail appearance in a wheelchair makes it hard to associate him with the radiant knightly lineage.

Your guess is not impossible; the Morgan Merchant Guild has built countless warships for the empire, appearing formidable, yet in actual naval encounters their victory rate is pitifully low, especially when exterminating pirates, where ships mysteriously sink...

What do you mean, Father?" Mersefield started, feeling he had just heard an earth-shattering secret from his father's mouth.

I've long suspected that the warships built by the Morgan family are flawed, and I've even suspected they collude with pirates..." the old man said in a low voice.

.... Mersefield's delicate frame trembled; she had never dared imagine that the empire's warships could also have problems.

Windsor, what do you plan to do next?" the old man asked patiently.

I intend to inform Her Majesty the Queen tomorrow that the kingdom is under threat from pirates; this is very dangerous." Mersefield said seriously.

However, the matter of conferring the title of foreign Thorn Knight is equally important; it concerns the kingdom's future development, perhaps allowing the kingdom's strength to surge unprecedentedly, breaking the tradition of selecting Thorn Knights solely from knightly families—an epochal significance; perhaps future Thorn Knights will be outstanding individuals from all strata, not merely a pastime of noble houses." The old man said leisurely, appearing frail and detached from worldly affairs yet knowing everything about the outside world.

But.... the situation at Bristol Port.... cannot be ignored.... Mersefield furrowed her brows, feeling short-staffed nearby, thinking she should have Catherine stay behind.

Why don't you personally lead a few squads of knights to the port for investigation tomorrow? Sharing the royal family's worries is our family's long-standing tradition; even if we act first and report later, it's completely fine. You've accompanied Queen Elizabeth since childhood; this feeling.... she will understand you." The old man offered this advice, not wishing Elizabeth's side to be troubled.

But if I leave, there will be no one to guard the royal capital; if a surprise attack occurs, the consequences would be unimaginable!" Mersefield did not fully agree with his father's idea.

Don't worry, I'm still here.... The old man paused, forcing a smile: 'Although I'm an old bone, having never left the manor for decades, if the kingdom needs me, I can still wield a sword.'

But Father, your...." Mersefield showed a worried expression.

It's fine; old Leonard hasn't died yet, how could I precede him? We retired from the Thorn Knights together, so we'll naturally go together as well." The old man chuckled indifferently.

Mersefield lowered his head, not responding to his father's optimistic words, feeling a bit uneasy inside.

By the way, what's the deal with that little friend you brought back?" the old man suddenly asked.

Ah.. he was demon-possessed; unfortunately he suffered a great fright, his mind still not entirely clear, so I brought him back, planning to help him find his parents tomorrow." Mersefield said helplessly.

This manor hasn't seen children in a long time; it has brought a lot of cheer here..." the old man nodded, then added meaningfully: "However, the little friend you brought back seems to have a habit of listening to stories before bed, huh?"

Huh!?" Mersefield blinked, turning his head toward the door.

Er!" little Merlin exclaimed, thinking, "What's this old guy's background?! Such keen perception!"

Mersefield spotted little Merlin outside, walked over and looked down at him, 'You've even packed your luggage; where are you headed?'

I'm leaving!" little Merlin said sternly.

.... Mersefield, lacking experience with children, felt a headache over little Merlin: 'It's not okay to stay up this late; come, let's go back.'

Don't touch me! I will never submit to your lewd.威! Don't try to taint my free soul!" little Merlin bared his teeth, continually giving off a prickly aura, "Demons! Never be slaves!"

Oh ho~ here we go again with the nonsense.... Mersefield's face darkened, looking down at little Merlin from above.

Didn't I tell you? Behave here, don't cause trouble.... Mersefield grabbed little Merlin's collar, lifting him like a chick and taking him back to his own room.

Little Merlin's head swelled with a big bump, as if Mersefield had hammered him; being lifted, his short legs couldn't touch the ground, still acting arrogant?

.. sorry....

There's still another chapter; I've been busy today, delayed a lot, the third update might be difficult to produce.

title: Chapter 41 — Disgrace and Ruin (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 41 — Disgrace and Ruin (Extra Chapter)

Volume 21 · Chapter 41

Mersfield carried little Merlin back to the house price, seeing not neat and tidy, but... a mess!
The cabinets were all turned out, the bed. was a mess, the floor covered with torn rags, even the curtains had disappeared?
Even if you kept a Siberian Husky at home, it probably wouldn't cause this much destruction.
Mersfield's mood instantly turned sour, his face grim as he said nothing and set little Merlin down.
Little Merlin broke out in a cold sweat on his forehead, thinking he was done for, that a fist would KO him?!
"What did you do in the room?" Mersfield stared at little Merlin, expressionless, asked.
"...." Little Merlin shivered, not knowing how to explain; after thinking, he lifted his head and stuck out his tongue, "Heh-heh~★"
"You're still acting cute!" Mersfield grabbed little Merlin and shook him wildly, gritting his teeth, "Do you act like this even at your own home? No manners at all! I'm not your mother, otherwise I'd have spanked you raw!"
"Wait... wait a minute!" Little Merlin, dizzy from being shaken, quickly put on a pitiful act, "I didn't... do it on purpose; it's just that this place is too unfamiliar, I feel so panicked, waa waa~"
"...."
Mersfield furrowed his brows, barely believing little Merlin's crocodile tears; after all, he's just a kid, you can't just lay hands on him to discipline.
Thus, the helpless Mersfield had no choice but to set little Merlin down and tidy the room himself, still muttering complaints.
"Honestly, why would you mess up someone else's room? This isn't your own home; you ought to know what politeness is—did your parents never teach you that?"
". . ." Little Merlin wiped the cold sweat from his forehead, feeling he had snatched back a life from the female knight's hands.
While Mersfield was cleaning his room, he unexpectedly discovered a long rope on the floor made from curtains, bedsheets, and clothes.
"...." Little Merlin's heart leapt again, thinking he was done for—would she explode in rage just because he touched her private underwear? If he'd known, he wouldn't have touched her lingerie.
As Mersfield expected, he found the rope's end tied to a few of his embarrassing underwear, and the atmosphere instantly turned eerie.
One could see Mersfield's face reddening at a visible pace, as if discovering his little secret was terribly embarrassing.
"Whoo-whoo-whoo~" Little Merlin, desperate to survive, pretended to whistle innocently, looking utterly naive and clueless, unaware that this old foggy knew more than anyone.
"...." Mersfield clenched his underwear in his hand, suppressing the immense shame welling up inside, "You little... why did you... touch my underwear? Don't play innocent here!"
"That.... Little Merlin's forehead dripped large beads of sweat; thinking on his feet, he feigned idiocy, "Eh? Is that your sister's underwear? I didn't notice at all, uh... it's just a... nicely patterned mask..."
"Mask?" Mersfield stared, looked down, aside from the lace thong having little fabric, there didn't seem to be anything resembling a mask, but since the kid said it's a mask, he must be completely clueless—good thing he's totally ignorant, otherwise this embarrassment would be huge. Dead text small
"Sister...." Little Merlin revealed a triumphant smile, looking very evil, "Why aren't you speaking? Could it be... this isn't a mask?"
"Cough cough!" Mersfield panicked, using a cough to hide his embarrassment, "Right, that... you're correct, it's just a mask, I misspoke earlier."
"Oh~" Little Merlin nodded, his smile growing more brazen, "If it's a mask, can you put it on and show me? I've never seen such a nearly transparent mask before~"
"Ah! ?" Mersfield's body stiffened; the flush that had been like boiling water rapidly faded, replaced by an eggplant purple, "..-.I"
"Hey? What are you afraid of? Didn't you just trick me?" Little Merlin's inner laughter had him doubling over; the imperial knight putting his own underwear on his face—what a sight! Indeed, I am a thoroughgoing demon! Come on, let's truly feel the fear of being dominated by a demon! Who would be so brain‑damaged as to use a thong as a mask?! All of this is her contemptuously treating me as a child and getting her comeuppance! This great lord will use the advantage of a brat to toy with him between applause, hiahiahiahia (baboon‑like laughter)~
Mersfield remained silent, feeling that facing a mere brat he was experiencing unprecedented pressure—truly humiliating.
Having calmed down, the opponent is just a wet‑nosed brat; we can't go along with his whims!
A brat who doesn't even understand trivial matters, trying to deceive is as easy as flipping a palm!
Mersfield slowly turned around, squeezing out a smile that was hard to fathom; it seemed he had already escaped the immense embarrassment.
"Sister, why are you lying to me? This really is a mask, but I won't wear it—how about you personally put it on me so I can feel its merits: ultra‑thin, breathable, with a faint fragrance..."
"Uh! What!?"
Little Merlin's stare went blank, his expression instantly turning to terror—scarier than seeing a ghost; the lace thong in Mersfield's hand is the evil implement that will ruin his reputation!
Flirting dangerously on the edge, Merlin never imagined he'd mess up; he seems to have forgotten that the weak have no rights and must obey the strong—an ironclad fact!
"No.. I don't need to, right? ... I don't want to wear it."
"Don't be polite; treat my sister's house as your own—are you shy?" Mersfield, usually serious, never imagined he'd have a hint of scheming in private.
"You weren't saying that just now!" Little Merlin kept retreating, being forced hard against the wall.
Mersfield's shadow loomed over the little Merlin, who trembled helplessly, unable to resist, watching the evil implement slowly approach.
"Come on, come on, let sister put it on you—I won't eat you, don't be scared.
"NO!!"
"Merlin, disgraced and ruined....."
Downstairs, Mersfield's father nearly fell from his wheelchair from little Merlin's scream, he slightly furrowed his brows—
Although the old house has gained a bit of a cheerful atmosphere, isn't this going a bit too far?
Little Merlin's voice echoed over the Mersfield family manor; Blackman's oscillating membranes had long been circling here.
Faintly hearing Little Merlin's voice, Blackman nearly fell from the sky—- time, worried and anxious—
"Ooh ooh ooh, poor Your Majesty, that hateful female knight still hasn't let him go?"
"I'm so useless; at this time I actually can't free His Majesty from suffering...."
"Pfft! His Majesty must be feeling secretly delighted because he can share a bed with that lovely female knight!"
"According to His Majesty's logic, having seized the British queen's breasts is tantamount to the whole empire being tainted by demons."
"Now he's started to go after the kingdom's chief... no need to think further—this is surely for the demon race's future!"
"Before long, under His Majesty's efforts, the demon race's flags will be planted all over Britain; then this fertile land will be ours!"
"Hmm! Truly worthy of a wise Majesty, I admire you from the bottom of my heart....."

title: Chapter 42 — I'm Still a Child
content:
Chapter 42 — I'm Still a Child

Volume 21 · Chapter 42

The room echoed with the dripping sound of water from the bathroom.... "Hehehe~ little hum~ J" Mesfield was bathing, having tormented little Merlin earlier, he seemed in a good mood and could even hum a tune. Little Merlin, however, was not so happy; he sat on the floor with his head down, a blank stare, wondering what to think with his hands. Yet from his miserable little face it was easy to see what had just happened—the humiliation after being ravaged still lingered. Utter ruin and disgrace—this was the best description of Merlin, the former great Demon Lord reduced to being toyed with by a female knight? Though Merlin had once felt a twinge of guilt for always tormenting Mesfield, that guilt had vanished, leaving only a chest full of frustration. "This shouldn't be like this!" he thought. "What am I even doing here? Why am I being humiliated by a female knight like this? I'm the Demon Lord, the supreme villain ruling the First Demon Lord Palace! No! I can't stay here any longer; who knows what torment I'll face—I have to escape!" "What the heck is that idiot Blackman doing? Why isn't he trying to save himself? Has he rebelled because he's been blamed too much?" Little Merlin grew uneasy, shifting nervously on the carpet, looking for a way out. When he saw the hot water placed on the table, an idea struck him; his throat instinctively began to move, saliva gathering. Although Merlin had become a child, his succubus nature remained unchanged, and the alluring power of his saliva still existed. Even if its effect was weaker than in adulthood, it could still be useful now. If Mesfield fell under its spell, that would be the perfect chance for little Merlin to slip away. Having made up his mind, little Merlin fidgeted, approached the table, and picked up the lovely cup. He glanced furtively toward the bathroom, the steam‑clouded glass revealing Mesfield's naked, slender figure. He had no mood to admire it, lowered his head, and muttered a few times— "Cough! Pah!" Little Merlin watched his saliva float in the water, frowned, and thought to himself, "Why does this feel a bit gross?" To make it more convincing, he didn't forget to shake the cup, letting his saliva disperse completely in the water. After finishing, little Merlin returned to the corner; his previously dejected expression instantly turned a bit sinister. Hehehe! This should work now. As long as she drinks this cup, the succubus power will activate. Even a giant woman won't be able to resist the force of desire—I guarantee she'll lose all will to fight and her ability to think! Mesfield hummed a little tune as he stepped out of the bath, already changed into a nightgown, continually toweling off his damp hair. Perhaps because he had just bathed, he was thirsty, so he headed straight for the table where the warm water waited, unaware that it had already been 'poisoned.' "Hehe!" Little Merlin, seeing his plan go so smoothly, couldn't help but let out a strange laugh, thinking, "Hurry up and drink! Once the effect kicks in, I can swagger right out of here!" "What are you laughing at?" Mesfield held the water cup in his hand, a towel lazily draped over his head. "...Nothing..." Little Merlin darted his gaze away, nervous that Mesfield might notice something. "Huh?" Mesfield didn't think much of it, a hint of doubt in his voice as he downed the warm water in one gulp. "Muhahaha..." Little Merlin's grin grew wilder; he couldn't help cheering in his mind, "He drank it! I finally succeeded! Let him enjoy the torment of burning desire! If his spirit weren't strong enough, escaping under a succubus's control would be impossible! Indeed, my own saliva is this female knight's nemesis!" Mesfield wiped his mouth after drinking, felt nothing odd, and climbed straight into bed, apparently ready to rest. Little Merlin stared at Mesfield with a strange expression; that curvaceous figure was truly tempting, even in a loose nightgown her sexiness seemed ready to burst forth. Yet little Merlin wondered, "Why hasn't the saliva's effect kicked in yet? Could it be that because I've shrunk, my saliva isn't as strong as before, and being diluted in water means it will take longer to work?" Mesfield saw little Merlin sitting in the corner staring at him and couldn't help but wave, "What are you staring at? Hurry up and come to sleep—it's late, kids like you need plenty of rest." Little Merlin's old face flushed; he turned his head away, sweating, thinking, "Who would want to sleep with this muscular woman? If the saliva's effect does kick in, I'll be in big trouble! A person under the thrall of succubus saliva loses reason, becomes lust‑crazed, ready to devour anything—if his will isn't firm, he might even attack the males nearby; my tiny frame couldn't possibly withstand that, so staying far away is safer." "What are you hesitating about? Aren't you tired? Come on up to sleep." Mesfield kept patting the big bed, like a tempting older sister to a little shota, "Come on, the lights are going out." "No... no..." Little Merlin shook his head frantically, afraid Mesfield would lose his reason and drain him, "...Sleeping on the floor is fine; I don't want to sleep with a stranger..." "Huh?" Mesfield looked at the nervous little Merlin, gave a kind smile, "You look young, but you sure think a lot—are you shy, maybe?" A bead of cold sweat trickled down little Merlin's forehead; he thought, "Grade? I could be your grandfather, shyness is impossible—I can only refuse to sleep with an older leftover woman to barely avoid being drained." "Here you don't need to be shy; what could a little kid like you understand? Come on up to sleep, tomorrow early we still have to look for your parents." "......" Little Merlin wanted to speak but dared not tell the truth. "What are you afraid of? Do you think I'll eat you?" Mesfield wondered, puzzled at how a little boy could have so many thoughts—what's filling his head? Little Merlin lowered his head, his face grim, thinking, "This really isn't certain." "Don't sit there day‑dreaming; come up now, otherwise I'll have to use..." Mesfield cracked his fingers with a meaningful smile, saying, "Special means~" "Go to sleep, don't wet the bed." Mesfield gave a warning, then reached out to turn off the light, thinking, "Reason doesn't work with kids; force is the only way." Little Merlin stared blankly at the unfamiliar ceiling, expression lifeless, thinking, "What should I do? This woman beside me will probably turn into a hungry tigress; how can I survive?" They shared the same blanket, the room pitch black except for the faint moonlight seeping through the window. Time ticked by, and little Merlin sensed danger drawing near— Beside him, Mesfield had already fallen asleep, yet his breathing was odd, restless and uneasy, his chest rising and falling. Little Merlin shivered, his body constantly shifting, trying to slip under the bed so that even if Mesfield lost his reason in lust and couldn't find him, he'd only be left to be played with. Then, just as little Merlin was about to escape the hot covers, a slender but scorching hot hand grabbed him. Little Merlin's face turned pale, his whole body trembling; he looked fearfully behind him, already eyed by a starving wolf. Mesfield lay wantonly on the bed, cheeks flushed, his grip locked on little Merlin's small hand, his sharp eyes filled with... Little Merlin's face turned ashen, almost revealing it, his throat working for a long time before he weakly squeaked out, "I'm still a giant baby, please let me go." (φ_ 时)

title: Chapter 43 — The Civet Cat Exchanges the Prince (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 43 — The Civet Cat Exchanges the Prince (Extra Chapter)

Volume 21 · Chapter 43

Little Merlin wanted to cry but had no tears, thinking the effect of saliva had long worn off, yet it chose to act just when he was trying to sneak away—wasn't this just playing with himself? He could feel Mesfield's hand extremely hot, as if all the blood in his body were boiling, this was the reaction after accumulating how much pressure? Mesfield held Little Merlin tight, his delicate body instantly turning into a soft poisonous snake, lightly rubbing against him. '...Get away! Don't get aroused by me! I'm not a wire....' After round after round of mental impact, Mesfield couldn't hold back, he flipped over and pressed Little Merlin down, grabbing his arms so he couldn't move. 'What are you doing? Didn't we agree to just sleep?' Little Merlin said with a sobbing tone, tonight not only would he lose face and reputation, but also his later years would be ruined. The strap of the off-shoulder nightgown slipped, revealing half of his bosom, Mesfield's face wore a dreamy, intoxicated smile, oblivious to Little Merlin's words. Seeing Little Merlin do nothing but give it his all, using his slender frame, he mustered all his strength to pull his hands out, then with the momentum of holding up the world, he grabbed the two mounds on Mesfield's chest. 'Damn bastard! Make me feel ecstatic! I'll let you know what... calling... ecstasy and death!' You awful knight who doesn't even spare a child! Wahaha!' Little Merlin's actions looked obscene yet somehow felt ignited? To escape the older sisters' **, desperately guarding his later years, he resembled... a desperate struggle for survival. "???"

Xiao Merlin looked odd, thinking, "What on earth is Blackman saying? Still going after all the male knights of Britain?"

The little Merlin, who was mistaken as having dedicated herself, had a terrible mood. She pulled open Blackman's two legs and said seriously, "What nonsense? Nothing happened at all!"

"I understand, Ar.... Blackman sighed deeply, sympathizing, 'Your late-life affairs, I won't tell anyone. If Lilith-sama finds out, she'll definitely perish with this female knight.'

'Don't conceal your inner pain, be strong!' Blackman clenched his fist, saying leisurely, 'In political matters, you've already hooked up with the British Queen. In military matters, you successfully slept with the kingdom's chief knight. Now you just lack a wealthy woman. The difficulty seems large; I suggest you start training with a steel wool ball first, otherwise it'll be hard to please those incredibly rich women...'

'Black....' Xiao Merlin looked ugly, exasperated, 'Wait until I recover, I'll definitely stuff your head into a toilet...'

'Huh? ? ?' Blackman showed a wronged expression, innocently saying, 'Your Majesty, you can't do that. Just because I guessed your small thoughts, you won't kill me to silence me, right?'

'....' Xiao Merlin, headache, pressing her forehead, thinking she really had enough of this guy. Why not send a slightly cleverer subordinate to find me?

When the sun rose from the horizon, welcoming the next day - SE4 Zhi

Although Mesfield was so diligent, she didn't wake up. It was strange that she fell asleep in the room.

Her posture was coquettish; her sexy legs were clamping the pillow, and she was holding it tightly in her arms. Drool was even flowing onto it.

Mesfield was unaware of what she did last night. Until now, she still thought she met a white horse prince in her dream last night.

Thump thump thump, knocking sounds continued outside the door. Mesfield slowly woke up, opened her eyes after taking off her glasses, and got up from the bed in a drowsy state.

"Who is it? I haven't slept enough..."...

Mesfield rubbed her eyes, yawned, and went to open the door. To her surprise, it was her father? Looking at her with a serious face.

"Father? You... what's wrong?"

The old man looked exhausted, staring at her dark circles under the eyes, speaking in a slightly complaining tone, "You finally woke up? What were you doing in your room last night? And calling so loudly....."

"Eh? !" Mesfield was stunned, turning her head to look at the messy big bed, as if she had experienced a big battle last night, - I seem to have done nothing at all -

"Calling so loudly and saying you did nothing at all? Really embarrassing for our family..." The old man lowered his head, speaking gently, "Windsor, I know you're not a child anymore. Also will... such needs, but you should pay attention to the influence. Doing it secretly is good. Calling so loudly... are you afraid others don't know?"

"? ? ?" Mesfield's face turned red, completely unaware of what happened. She always felt it wasn't a good thing! What did she do last night that was shameful? To the point that her father didn't sleep all night!

"...." The old man sighed, meaningfully saying, "Unknowingly, you've reached this age. If the situation allows, you should find a good man. Come... M SF Light J' said

'You... You... You... What are you saying?!'"

Mesfield's face instantly turned red like an apple. Her heart was panicked, not understanding why her father suddenly said such things!

However, Mesfield soon noticed something was wrong. Looking around the room anxiously, she said,

"Father, that child... that child is missing! He was there last night!"

"That child... last night was taken away by a demon. I saw it with my own eyes from the attic." The old man said calmly.

"Ah! ? Why didn't you save him?! " Mesfield's tone was slightly resentful.

"I saw that the child was willing." The old man paused, speaking seriously, "You misunderstood Windsor. That child was originally from the demon side, not a demon's prey. I saw the demon clothe this child. This clearly wasn't the treatment a prey should have. Obviously, you did something redundant..."

".... This is really how it happened..." Mesfield had a numb expression.

"Windsor..." The old man's expression became serious, and he advised one-

"Regardless of the situation, don't get involved with demons."

"If they aren't producing a threat to the kingdom, - don't meddle in other people's business..."

The grand royal procession, after several days of long travel, finally arrived at Reckham.

The Lord Earl Austin and the local nobles organized a long queue to welcome the arrival of Queen Elizabeth.

Beautiful purple wisteria flags fluttered, accompanied by classical celebration music, and the knight team entered the city.

The residents threw the prepared flowers towards the knights, welcoming the bravest warriors of the kingdom.

Elder Taylor and his granddaughter Lucya stood in the crowd, whispering to each other--

"Queen Elizabeth is actually coming to such a small town in the countryside? I don't know what she wants to do?" Lucya murmured in confusion.

"Cough!" Elder Taylor lightly coughed, "I heard from the Earl that it's to confer the foreign Thorn Knight... "

"Ah! ?" Lucya was startled, unbelievable, "Foreign Thorn Knight? Such a high-ranking knight of the kingdom, aren't they all selected from noble descendants or the Royal Institute? This time it's an exception."

"The Earl said this is the first Thorn Knight in history who is a commoner, representing the Queen's determination to break tradition. Maybe in the future, Thorn Knights will be selected from elites of all classes." Elder Taylor said softly.

"Really? It sounds good. I don't know who this lucky... Lucya showed a puzzled expression.

'It's not clear, but it must be someone from our Reckham.' Elder Taylor smiled kindly.

'Does Reckham have the qualification to serve as Thorn Knight...' Hopkins, holding a wine bottle, stroked his chin in thought at the side, "Karl and Alice should both fit, unfortunately their experience isn't enough~"

"What experience and experience? This time it's looking at ability!" Lucya rolled her eyes at Hopkins, her heart still hoping her father could become Thorn Knight, so she wouldn't have to live in constant fear of adventure. Having a Thorn Knight dad is also an honor; it would make others envious!

"Hehe~" Hopkins laughed silently, showing a lewd smile. "I've only seen Queen Elizabeth in newspapers and on screen before. I didn't expect to have the chance to see the real person this time. I must take a good look. I heard she's more beautiful in person, a woman with lingering charm, prprpr.. ."

o)YCE Zhi Xiao Zhi

'You old lecher, don't forget you have a child and are a married man...' Lucya was very contemptuous of this unscrupulous guy Hopkins.

'Meddling in other people's business, is fantasizing a crime?' Tsk~' Hopkins pursed his mouth, and beside him started drinking wine, ton ton ton ton ton...

Elder Taylor remained silent beside him, his heart was drumming. The foreign Thorn Knight wasn't revealed by Earl Austin, just as Hopkins said. Karl's experience wasn't enough now, and his fame wasn't as big as Alice's.

Even if it was truly Karl, today would probably have problems. Two days ago, Karl took Ralph's adventurer group, proving that going to Denmark alone to a ruined country, preparing to send his old friend on the last journey.

Applause and cheers never stopped. Queen Elizabeth received a warm welcome from the people of Reckham. Down below, people kept shouting the Queen's name.

However, this Queen of Britain, at this moment, was trembling in her own carriage, her face pale, legs together, slightly rubbing restlessly.

What to do?

Do I need to see Merlin?

That terrible man, who had an evil smile on his face... .

Wow! I'm so nervous! I'm going to die! I want to go back!

title: Chapter 45 — Final Deal (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 45 — Final Deal (Extra Chapter)

Volume 21 · Chapter 45

Outside the Earl Austin's manor, a large group of minor nobles and merchants had gathered. Earl Austin today wore especially splendid attire, his hair neatly combed, standing straight and stiff at the very front. Behind him, his siblings Arnold and Jenna, at their father's request, had dressed up carefully to welcome the Queen of Britain. "Ah..." Jenna furrowed her brows, dissatisfiedly muttering, "Why do I also have to stand here to welcome? What does it have to do with me?" "This is a chance to show off like royalty, you girl, behave yourself—later you must present your best self before the Queen." Arnold whispered a reminder. "I want to see Merlin... Jenna stomped her feet in anger, muttering, "I don't even know what he's up to? Why hasn't he come back yet? That hateful woman stuffing her chest pads refuses to say anything—she surely wants to monopolize Merlin all for herself, how wicked!" "Merlin must be busy—didn't you see Alice bringing his little nephew back?" Arnold sighed, saying absentmindedly, "I suppose taking care of a brat alone must be exhausting? Maybe Alice should also consider me..." "Go dream on, you idiot brother..." Jenna rolled her eyes, directly splashing a basin of cold water. "Ugh!" Arnold's forehead veins twitched, "What do you mean? Stink...." "It's not that I'm putting you down, brother; as a woman I simply look down on your type—utterly uncompetitive, you might as well give up." Jenna shrugged her shoulders, looking down on her own brother from the heart. "Me? What's wrong with me?" Arnold gazed at the sky at a 45-degree angle, entering a sparkling mode, "I too am the hope of the whole village, within ten miles: the most handsome guy." "Ugh~" Jenna gagged, unable to hold back, "A simp deserves no good death, big brother." "You two keep quiet, stop whispering behind." Earl Austin didn't even turn his head, scolding the two. Arnold and Jenna immediately fell silent, not uttering a word, maintaining their composure as they prepared to welcome. The knight troop halted before the Earl Austin's manor, with Cladi stepping forward as representative, getting straight to the point: "Earl Austin, long time no see..." "Mr. Cladi, hahaha." They shook hands, appearing to have known each other for a long time, not strangers at all. "You're quite a busy person, eh? The last time we met was at the national founding anniversary celebration; your erudite demeanor left a fresh impression on me." Earl Austin beamed. "Flattery aside, is everything ready for the reception?" Cladi inquired about the welcoming ceremony. "Of course, we stand ready at any moment to greet Her Majesty the Queen." Earl Austin nodded, his little mustache twitching. Cladi waved his hand, and then the two knights laid out a long scarlet carpet on the ground, extending all the way to the Queen's carriage, preparing to receive her.

Catherine stepped forward, lowering her voice to the carriage where Elizabeth was inside, saying, "Your Majesty, please alight." The carriage showed no response, as if Elizabeth hadn't heard, unnervingly calm? "Your Majesty, we have arrived, you may disembark." Catherine said again. Yet Elizabeth still showed no reaction, and those waiting began to whisper, wondering what had happened? "Huh?" Catherine felt a hint of strangeness, thinking she couldn't have fallen asleep—no way, she had just been talking to me. As Catherine was about to enter the Queen's carriage to check, Elizabeth cautiously lifted the curtain, sneaking a peek at the surrounding people, looking like a thief? Elizabeth was just timid inside, truly not wanting to see that ruffian Merlin, so she wanted to confirm whether he was present; if not, she would dare to step down. Seeing the lofty Queen acting like a thief, Catherine couldn't help but remind, "Your Majesty, what are you doing? Mind your demeanor." ".-.plan-...." Elizabeth secretly breathed a sigh of relief, not having seen Merlin; to her this was wonderful news. She then descended from the carriage openly and confidently, her steps steady, faintly revealing dignity, walking along the red carpet to Earl Austin. Elizabeth looked down at the bowing Earl Austin, extending her hand wearing white silk gloves, showing no trace of her earlier timidity. "Your Majesty's greetings." Earl Austin respectfully lowered his head, kissing the back of Elizabeth's hand with a "peck". "Earl Austin, there's no need for such a grand reception; just keep it simple." Elizabeth glanced at everyone, her gaze sweeping over as all present bowed. "Your Majesty honoring my domain with your presence is my honor; etiquette absolutely cannot be neglected." Earl Austin flushed with pride. "Well, you must have received my message already, knowing why I'm here today—so let's not waste time...." Elizabeth paused, thinking to act swiftly, appointing Alice as a foreign Thorn Knight, then slipping away quickly to possibly avoid that man perfectly, "Is Miss Alice here? Please let her come to receive the knighthood." "Alice... she left Wrexham some time ago and hasn't returned; I had already informed her of her impending appointment as a Thorn Knight..." Earl Austin answered awkwardly. "???" Elizabeth's expression went blank, thinking she had misheard— A thousand-strong knight corps had painstakingly made it to Wrexham, only to be stood up like that? Even if you're the wife of the Elgin Great Swordsman, don't be so arrogant! I am the Queen of Britain—don't I deserve face? ? ?

At the same time, in Manchester, Bristol Port. Alice had been secretly following Lochiri's carriage all the way, tracking it to this port. She hid behind crates at the port, her gaze fixed on the distance, thinking this guy definitely wasn't just a merchant; his sneaky behavior might hide some secret? Alice was somewhat familiar with this port—two years ago, she had set out from here with the Templar Knights, marching all the way to the First Demon Lord Palace! Back then Alice had still wanted to use this campaign to prove herself, to achieve something that would make her teacher look at her anew. Unfortunately she ran into Merlin, that scoundrel, got beaten down, losing her armor and weapons, the first batch of debts, plunging into life's low point. However, these old stories Alice didn't bother to recall; she still needed to determine what eerie thing was hidden in that fake merchant's carriage, and whether it had anything to do with little Merlin. Lochiri came to a hidden corner of the port, after getting off the carriage and checking around to ensure nothing was amiss, he pulled out a red flag from his bosom and waved it at the distant pirate-disguised merchant ship. Not long after, a small boat carrying a group of people rowed over; the leader was a mysterious figure clad in black robes, from the strongest dark guild, the rest being pirates. Lochiri first ordered the pirates to move the gold and jewels onto his ship, then went to negotiate with the Phoenix people. "Did you pull it off?" the black-clad person's tone held a hint of suspicion. Lochiri walked up to the carriage, hoisting the unconscious Helena onto his shoulder, "Of course, I said I could do it." "Hehehe, I like capable people," the black-clad person said meaningfully. The final transaction quietly began at Bristol Port.
