title: Chapter 55 — Letter from Afar
content:
Chapter 55 — Letter from Afar

Volume 21 · Chapter 55

"Do not speak of my past. I am no longer the Beast King—I am merely an exile, a sinner cast out by my own kind." Saret lowered his head, as if unwilling to recall the time he had held the title.

"You still haven't explained why you were exiled," Heshi said meaningfully, her gaze flickering with suspicion toward the feline beastman. "You chose to leave your tribe and joined the infamous Dark Guild. Something doesn't add up."

"The United Kingdom is an alliance of non-human races. There are nine major races—other smaller groups we can ignore. The nine great races each elect a leader, forming a Nine-Member Council that shapes the kingdom's destiny…" Saret spoke slowly.

"Sounds fair. Weren't you one of those nine yourself?" Heshi looked at him.

"Fair? There is no such thing. Everyone is fighting for their own clan's interests. Whoever has the stronger fist gets to speak, and the rest listen. Among the nine rulers, the Elf King holds the most authority. Even without the Elf God's blessing, he is still deeply fearsome…" Saret paused, then added with a self-deprecating laugh, "The last sanctuary of non-humans? Sounds beautiful, but in truth it belongs entirely to the Elf King. With nothing but words, he controls the fate of every other race, feeding on their strength while the elf bloodline grows ever stronger."

"Why don't you leave? Are all your people fools?" Heshi teased.

"I warned them. But they refused to believe me. They'd rather cling to the false dream the Elf King spun. That's how I ended up exiled—as a traitor to unity, a wanderer with no home…" Saret said bitterly, glancing at his black-furred claws.

"Poor thing. Hah…" Heshi covered her mouth and laughed, then asked curiously, "At least your beastmen are a proud and ancient race. How could you let one old man lead you by the nose? Why didn't the other races unite and rebel?"

"The Elf King is an ancient monster. He does not age—he was born during the Age of Gods. He may have even seen the gods fall from the sky while still in his swaddling clothes." Saret closed his eyes. "His power is bottomless. No one can shake his position. More crucially, he holds the lives of every non-human race in his hands. He could sink the entire kingdom into the abyss beneath the sea at any moment. I even suspect the alliance itself was his scheme from the beginning—a web of sweet lies to bind the other races to his will."

"I see. If you hand your lives over to another, you've already lost everything. You're all just vassals of the Elf King—"

Heshi nodded, beginning to understand why Saret had been driven out. He had once been a fighter for freedom, only to be branded a madman by his own kin. "But from what you're saying, the Elf King's strength is so terrifying that none of the other leaders dare move against him? Is he really that frightening?"

"The entire territory of the United Kingdom was ripped away from the human continent and built atop an abyss. It hangs like a floating city with no supports, requiring constant, massive magical reinforcement just to keep the land above the sea…" Saret lifted his head. "And the one who has sustained the kingdom for millions of years without collapse—that is the Elf King. He has endured, constantly battling the terrible gravitational pull from the abyss below. In a way, I genuinely respect his willingness to sacrifice himself to protect the kingdom. But it is also true that, in doing so, he has grown ever more autocratic, tightening his grip on everyone's fate."

"Heshi felt a chill. Sweat dripped down her temple. She thought, Can one person really hold up an entire kingdom's land for millions of years without it falling into the abyss? The magic required must be beyond imagination. Even an elf who never ages or dies must have limits. Could this Elf King be a living god? It was too shocking to comprehend."

"I pray for freedom and equality. I do not hate the Elf King. I simply cannot bear to watch my people unable to control their own destinies. It is pitiful…" Saret said in a deep voice. He did not seem to be a vicious monster.

"Do you think our Guild Master or the Elf King is stronger?" Heshi asked softly, clearly thinking of something else.

"I cannot compare them. Both the Guild Master and the Elf King possess power beyond my ability to measure." Saret shook his head, then changed the subject. "But the reason I followed Phoenix is that I agree with his ideal—to transform the world and push all races toward evolution. In that process, the weak will perish. Those who survive will be strong enough to shape their own fates."

"Even if it means doing evil things?" Heshi pressed with a half-smile.

"Revolution inevitably brings blood and sacrifice. It cannot be avoided. Those who survive—the lucky ones—in the end will understand."

Saret brushed past Heshi and walked straight toward the spire rising from the endless yellow sands, off to meet the human closest to godhood.

Heshi watched him disappear, murmuring to herself,

"Hmph. Stubborn cat…"

—

At the southernmost edge of the world, almost completely cut off from the outside, lay the United Kingdom of the South.

This was a gathering place for non-human races, far removed from the central continents, undisturbed by any human kingdom.

Beyond ordinary trade, there was little contact with the outside world. Yet some would sing praise of its paradise-like beauty.

Long, long ago, the continents were all joined together as one massive landmass.

With the end of the Demon Era came the Age of Humans, and the non-human races faced discrimination and suppression at every turn.

Facing the overwhelming numbers of humans, non-humans were dwarfed and unable to resist the rapidly rising human power. They had no choice but to flee their homeland and migrate.

The Elf King, unwilling to let the non-human races perish completely, persuaded the various tribes and used Star Annihilator Cannons to split the continental plates, establishing the United Kingdom of the South far from the central world.

At this moment, on a clear afternoon when the human world had already entered winter, the United Kingdom remained spring all year round.

—

Shelly, the Elf King's only child, paced back and forth in her study, apparently waiting anxiously for something.

Tap tap tap. A light knocking sounded—like some prearranged signal. Shelly's pointed ears twitched, and she approached the door with a bright expression, opening it.

A handsome elven knight in male attire stepped inside. His demeanor was furtive, as though he had done something wrong and feared discovery.

"Did you bring it?" Shelly could not help asking.

"Yes, I brought it…" The elven knight looked embarrassed. He pulled a rolled newspaper from his chest and handed it to Shelly.

"Haha! Mwah~" Shelly kissed the newspaper, her little face flushed with excitement. "Finally, I can find out what's happening outside the kingdom!"

"Then… Your Highness, could you not make me do this next time?" The elven knight frowned. "Human-world items are contraband. If I'm discovered, I'll be punished…"

"Don't worry. Only you and I know about this—it's our secret. They won't easily find out." Shelly smiled brightly. "You're my knight after all. If I want to know what's happening in the human world, I have no choice but to ask for your help…"

The elven knight blushed shyly. "I hope you won't ask me to do this again. It's far too dangerous. By the way, why do you want to know about human affairs?"

"After all, I lived in exile in the human world for a long time. I'm curious about it—there are so many things I've never seen." Shelly walked to her desk and unrolled the newspaper.

"Humans are all evil, despicable sinners! They're selfish and lazy—why learn about them? Those filthy creatures kidnapped you once…" The elven knight furrowed his delicate brows. Even in male clothing, he carried a certain feminine air.

"Don't say that. There are good humans and bad humans. Not everyone is like you say. Perhaps you should try seeing for yourself with your own eyes." Shelly said warmly.

"Hmph. I won't seek out humans on my own. The humans hanging around the port are more cunning than any—I've seen it. For profit, they'll use all manner of underhanded tricks…" The elven knight spoke seriously.

"All merchants talk like that. It's their nature…" Shelly said gravely.

"—" The elven knight's expression darkened. "I think you're in danger of—-"

Shelly did not respond. Instead, she focused intently on the newspaper before her—the London Post, which mostly covered affairs in Britain.

Since elves and humans wrote differently, Shelly was not very familiar with human script. She read far slower than others. This newspaper had been brought by traveling merchants; the news was not fresh, but covered events that had happened some time ago.

Still, it held immense appeal for Shelly. It was her only channel for learning about the human world.

[SHOCKING! The powerful adventurer who saved the Kingdom of France secretly keeps a man living off his wealth! ?!]

A headline quickly caught Shelly's eye, along with a blurry illustration. The two figures looked somewhat familiar.

"Huh?!" Shelly studied it closely, her eyes widening. Isn't that Miss Alice and Mr. Merlin? They made the newspaper! I didn't realize they were already celebrities…

"Your Highness, what's wrong?" the elven knight asked curiously.

"These… they're adventurers who once helped me. I lived with Miss Alice for several days. She's gentle and kind…" Shelly pointed excitedly at Alice in the photo. She had become a hero without Shelly knowing.

"—So…" The elven knight glanced at the silver-haired girl in the picture. She didn't look like a bad person, but the man beside her certainly didn't appear trustworthy—he looked shrewd and his gaze was lecherous.

Shelly stared at the newspaper, lost in thought.

It had been a long time since she last saw Miss Alice and Mr. Merlin.

They rescued me, and I have nothing to repay them with.

If I recall correctly, Miss Alice has never visited the United Kingdom. She's curious about it. Perhaps—

Shelly nodded, having made up her mind. To the elven knight she said,

"I'd like to invite them both as guests. Please deliver this letter to the Kingdom of Britain for me!"

"Huh?! No way!" The elven knight was startled. Secretly bringing human newspapers for the princess was already a mistake—now she wanted to invite humans over too?

"Don't worry. I pledge my honor—they're not bad people. It's decided." Shelly cheerfully took out letter paper, dipped her quill in ink, and sent long-overdue correspondence to Alice and Merlin—

[Dear Miss Alice and Mr. Merlin, it's been too long.]

[So much time has passed since we last parted. You haven't forgotten me, have you?]

—

Afterword

The next volume will focus on the United Kingdom story arc, filling in a hole I left open long ago.

Some longtime readers will remember what I said: the daughter will appear very soon in the United Kingdom storyline.

The story will shift tone, focusing on the warmth of a family of three—the main selling point will be the couple raising their cute daughter together.

As for everyone's interest in Merlin's recovery—feel free to look forward to the next volume.

But I'll design the recovery method carefully.

Will Merlin truly recover?

Will Helena become a female slave?

Can the dwarves forge Mistilteinn?

What stories unfold in the non-human kingdom?

Will the daughter actually be born?

Find out next time!

—

Why did I write over 3,000 words today? Because there's a lot of information to process. Tomorrow morning I'll wake up early, review the outline, and organize everything. I'll make up three chapters tomorrow to catch up!

title: Chapter 1 — The Name of a Knight
content:
Chapter 1 — The Name of a Knight

Volume 22 · Chapter 1

The ceremony was in full swing in the central fountain square of Leicester, where almost the entire town had gathered.

Yet under the grandeur of this grand event, little Merlin had secretly led Blackman out of the city.

Blackman was now a wanted demon, accused of attacking people everywhere, and had been portrayed as a villain beyond redemption.

Little Merlin felt that Blackman could not stay by his side any longer. If discovered one day, it might cause a fire that would spread to himself, making it impossible for him to continue living in the human kingdom.

"Come on, Blackman, let's go—take the road less traveled." Little Merlin waved his hand.

"Are you sure about this? Your Majesty, I'm not really keen on leaving..." Blackman, with his backpack on, looked very reluctant. After all the effort it took to meet Merlin, he would have to return to the Demon Lord Palace so soon.

"You're a wanted man now, everyone's out to get you. You can't stay here. The Demon Lord Palace is safer." Little Merlin shrugged.

"If it weren't for Your Majesty letting me take the blame, how could I have ended up like this..."

Blackman couldn't help but complain, feeling that if he hadn't helped Helena take the fall, he could have stayed here for a long time.

"...Enough talk. Get lost quietly. If the guards catch you, you'll be in trouble. When you get back, tell Lilith I said hello and tell her not to worry—I'm living quite well out here."

Blackman, with a wistful expression, knelt on one knee and said sincerely, "Your Majesty, please take care of yourself. After I return, I will report your situation honestly—that you're living in the human world in disgrace, that everyone looks down on you, that you're just a useless adventurer eating off human women, that you have no status living off others, and that you're being ordered around every day, very pitiful."

"Huh?!" Little Merlin was taken aback, quickly saying, "Don't be so honest!"

"What's wrong?" Blackman looked up curiously, wondering if he had said something wrong.

A swarm of dark lines slid down Little Merlin's forehead. He thought, Lilith always treats me like a good-for-nothing older brother who's never left the house!

If this embarrassing situation were known, wouldn't that just confirm the reputation of being a useless older brother?

He had always told Lilith that he was doing great outside, living in luxury every day, with everyone praising him to the skies.

If the lies he had carefully constructed were exposed... that would be so embarrassing.

Just then, he had transformed into a child, no longer under any curse that threatened his life. Lilith would definitely take him back to the Demon Lord Palace by force.

Little Merlin pondered, he absolutely could not let Blackman report the truth. He had to find a way to keep it hidden.

"Heh heh, Blackman, you're so naive..."

"What?" Blackman widened his eyes, hearing Merlin's theatrical laugh, as if the reclusive Demon Lord had returned. Master... what do you mean?

"You think I'm really as pathetic as I seem? Foolish!" Little Merlin cursed, revealing the evil grin that only a great villain could muster, "You should think carefully about this. I am Merlin, the Third Ruler of the First Demon Lord Palace, a super-strong warrior who is both respected and feared by all. Why would I end up in this situation?"

"Right, why?" Blackman, simple-minded as ever, asked directly.

"..."

Little Merlin was caught off guard by Blackman's counter-question, awkwardly lowering his head. Why? Why indeed?

How would he know why? He used to be lofty and fearless, but now he spends his days with Alice, that stupid woman.

His domineering and unmatchable demeanor has been worn down by the trivial daily quarrels, turning him into someone who is completely unremarkable in the eyes of others—a mere househusband.

Little Merlin covered his face, feeling increasingly unable to fit into demon society. Even if he truly returned to the Demon Lord Palace, he would struggle to adapt.

"Oh! I get it now. So that's what Your Majesty means..." Blackman narrowed his eyes, putting on a look of profound understanding.

"...What do you know?" Little Merlin's forehead was drenched in cold sweat.

"Your Majesty is living at the bottom of the human world, where everyone looks down on you, basically just a useless waste. But that's not really the case!" Blackman's imagination was running wild again, speaking with a conspiratorial tone, "Your Majesty must be secretly planning the great revival of the demon race. If you attracted too much attention, it would jeopardize the plan. To rise again as the master of the world, you must act discreetly. So being a man who eats off human women is the perfect disguise. Am I right, Your Majesty?"

"Uh... Right. That's exactly it. Blackman, I didn't expect you to be so wise. You're truly my right-hand man. When you get back, tell Lilith just that!"

"Understood! I'll head back to the Demon Lord Palace right away. Farewell, Your Majesty." Blackman stood up, nodded to Little Merlin, turned around, and set off with a spring in his step. Seeing the master so diligent and determined made him feel at ease.

Watching Blackman's sturdy back gradually disappear from view, Little Merlin secretly let out a sigh of relief, worrying in his heart.

At least I managed to send Blackman away. I should be able to fool Lilith, right?

But what if that crazy woman comes looking for me herself... how would I explain it then?

The central fountain square of Leicester was bustling with people.

Everyone was watching the two figures on the red carpet—the Queen Elizabeth and the recently famous adventurer Alice.

The knights, dressed in formal attire, lined both sides with stern expressions, their spears adorned with flags bearing the thistle.

Morrison, Catherine, and Cladius, the three Thistle Knights, stood behind Queen Elizabeth.

The crowd witnessed this unprecedented ceremony, marking the first time in British history that a foreign Thistle Knight was born.

"Ugh, it's Alice? Why not my dad?" Lyuria muttered resentfully in the crowd, a bit disappointed.

"Alice becoming a Thistle Knight isn't surprising. Karl may have enough strength, but his experience is lacking. Alice just saved France and returned as a hero..." Old Taylor, the guildmaster, stroked his beard. Although it wasn't his own son who would be honored, Alice becoming a Thistle Knight was also a great achievement for the guild.

Although Queen Elizabeth had been stood up by Alice, she wasn't angry. Instead, she stayed in Leicester for a few days until Alice returned.

Learning that Alice had returned to Leicester the previous night by carriage, Queen Elizabeth immediately held the ceremony for the foreign Thistle Knight at the crack of dawn.

Queen Elizabeth's haste was simply because she didn't want to encounter Merlin, hoping to finish the task quickly and rush back to the palace. After all, Merlin had left her with a significant psychological scar.

On the red carpet, Queen Elizabeth held the ceremonial sword, placing it on Alice's shoulder as Alice knelt on one knee.

Under everyone's held breath and intense gaze, Queen Elizabeth's expression was solemn, looking into Alice's eyes, and softly spoke:

"I command you, by the name of the Queen of Britain, to be brave!"

"I command you, by the name of the Goddess of Light!"

"By the name of all living things, I command you to protect the innocent and the weak..."

The crowd, who had been whispering moments ago, fell silent as Elizabeth began the ritual, each person gazing intently at Alice. This was the first foreign Thorn Knight in history, not from an aristocratic family, nor a noble-born, but born into the common class.

The enfeoffment of a foreign Thorn Knight was extraordinary, meaning the kingdom's highest honor, not a small circle's self-amusement, but giving everyone an opportunity.

Elizabeth wore a solemn expression, speaking brief sentences that sounded like an ancient ballad. She touched Alice's left shoulder, then right shoulder with her sword, finally touching her forehead.

Morrison, Katherine, and Claud had serious expressions; they had experienced what was before them, swearing loyalty to the royal family, guarding every inch of the kingdom's land.

Yet Elizabeth's admonition to Alice was different—she requested greater leniency, not making her swear loyalty to the royal family, merely making her a kind and just knight.

The ritual ended, Elizabeth set down her sword, and kindly said, "Rise, Alice. Claud, the kingdom's first foreign Thorn Knight."

Alice slowly opened her eyes, then stood up, thinking it was over, simpler than she'd imagined. The Hero's enfeoffment ceremony was far more complex.

From now on, you're one of us," Elizabeth paused, adding, "Although you're a foreign Thorn Knight, you enjoy the same treatment and status as Thorn Knights. title: Chapter 3 — The Top Dog of Lei Feng Primary School (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 3 — The Top Dog of Lei Feng Primary School (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 22 · Chapter 3

The ceremony ended, and the knights led the procession back to town.

However, the excitement of the celebration had not dissipated, and people were talking and laughing.

Merlin didn't want to go home yet, and while playing on the street, he happened to grab a piece of candy.

Tsk tsk! The fish had turned; although he had met the adventurer years ago, who would have thought he would become like this?

It really wasn't easy. Merlin grumbled in his heart, suddenly feeling a sense of de vu as he watched an adult.

"This is mine! I'm not giving it to you!"

Suddenly, a childish voice rang out from the nearby alley, carrying a hint of fear.

Merlin stopped his footsteps and frowned slightly. After hesitating for a moment, he hid the candy behind his back and walked toward the alley.

What was it? It seemed to be a little girl.

In the alley, a boy slightly older than her surrounded her.

"Hand it over quickly, don't make me use force," the boy reached out his hand.

"It's just a candy? Don't be so stingy," the girl with the hood said.

The girl was clearly taller than the boy, and she was quite strong as well.

"No! I won't give it to you! You bad thing!" Millie was full of hostility, hiding the candy behind her.

"Tsk! Since you're being unreasonable, then don't blame me for being polite!"

As soon as the words fell, the boy charged and began to snatch it. The girl was naturally smaller, and she lacked strength, so she quickly lost the struggle.

"Hehe, I got it!" The boy waved the candy in his hand.

"Remember this," the boy said greedily as he licked his lips.

"Give it back to me!" Millie's face turned red with anger as she lunged forward for her original candy.

"Go away! Are you crazy?" The boy frowned. "Let go!"

"Let go! You shrew!" The girl lunged forward, pulling at him.

In her desperation, Millie opened her mouth and bit the boy's arm. As a result, the candy in his hand fell to the ground.

Seeing her thing broken, Millie bit her lip, and tears welled up in her eyes as she began to cry.

"Gu..." The boy rubbed his arm, seeing the red tooth marks. He became instantly enraged and raised his fist. "You brat, I'll kill you!"

But just as the boy's fist was about to hit Millie's face, a stone "whooshed" hit him.

"Ah!" The boy clutched his face and looked around. "Who is?"

Merlin stood at the exit of the alley, weighing another stone in his hand. "Wanting to meddle in other people's business?" The boy was annoyed. "Kids nowadays are so annoying~"

"Go away! Don't you understand English?" The boy with the hood pursed his lips.

"Tsk! You little brat, you're quite loud," Merlin said playfully.

"You're just a brat yourself, why are you talking back?" The boy frowned.

"Don't talk to him, hit him!" The boy refused to give up and charged.

"To be honest, I haven't fought anyone in a long time..." Merlin shrugged, and another stone "whooshed" out, hitting the head.

The boy clutched his head and cried in pain, finally realizing that Merlin was not someone to mess with.

Holding back tears, he turned and ran, disappearing into the alley, not forgetting to leave a classic line: "You just wait!"

"If you have the guts, don't run away!"

"Are you crazy? Are you waiting for your dad to come?" Merlin unfurled both hands, finding it nonsensical. As he left the school gate, someone wanted to hit him, but speaking of which, ah! It feels good! It has been a long time since I felt the thrill of fighting someone... at this rate, won't I become a complete loser?

Merlin put away his pride and walked over to Millie, who was still staring at her broken candy.

"Hey, kid, how much do you care about food? You almost got hit..."

"My candy..." Millie's tears burst. She wiped her nose, making the freckles on her face more prominent.

"..." Merlin frowned, thinking that as expected, kids are so troublesome.

Merlin and Millie sat on the alley wall as the sky gradually grew dark.

Millie still held a grudge over her broken candy. Even after Merlin gave her the candy he had snatched, she continued to chatter.

"Those hateful Charlie and Duke, actually stealing my candy, I'll definitely settle score with them!" Millie complained while licking Merlin's candy.

"Who are Charlie and Duke?" Merlin asked in confusion.

"The two bad things who just stole my candy. And their drunk dad is the same crap, wandering around the streets every day. They are the bullies among the children in town!" Millie's mouth was quite sharp.

"Ah..." Merlin was stunned, suddenly realizing that adults have their world and children have their rules; he had never understood the worldview of little kids before.

"I'm going to form a resistance army, unite the children of town, and teach those bullies Charlie and Duke a lesson!" Millie said seriously, but the act of constantly liking the candy was very childish.

"I don't think a kid who cries without stopping over a broken candy can accomplish anything..." Merlin shook his head.

"What are you saying? Aren't you a kid too? I think you're about the same as me..." Millie argued in confusion.

"Tsk! Go home and find your mom quickly, I don't have time to accompany you..." Merlin jumped down from the box and turned to walk out.

"Wait! My name is Millie, what is your name? It feels like you just moved to Rokesham, I haven't seen you before." Millie chased Merlin, asking.

"What's your damn business?" Merlin crossed his arms, not wanting to communicate much with this child.

"Millie! Millie! Where are you?"

A familiar voice came over, sounding like a father looking for his child, very anxious.

"My dad is here, I hope I can see you again!" Millie ducked past Merlin and ran straight out of the alley. "Dad! I'm here!"

"Millie? Haha, let me find you~" Hobbes came to hug Millie, his face filled with a smile rarely seen in daily life.

"..." Merlin widened his eyes, not having expected that Millie was Hobbes' daughter.

title: Chapter 4 — Turning the Tables
content:
Chapter 4 — Turning the Tables

Volume 22 · Chapter 4

At home, Alice sat on the sofa with a serious expression, looking as though she were weighed down by thoughts.

Elizabeth had casually brought up Merlin, and it had left Alice still on edge, suspecting that Merlin's relationship with the Queen of Britannia was far from ordinary.

By rights, Merlin was just an adventurer in the eyes of ordinary people. How could a queen sitting high above have ever heard of him?

To top it off, Alice recalled the ridiculous incident where Merlin had once put a stocking over his head, making her even more suspicious that he and Elizabeth were up to something. Her little jar of jealousy had been knocked over, spilling everywhere.

Just then, Little Merlin pushed the door open and saw Alice on the sofa with such a stern expression, as if she were brewing up anger. He couldn't help but shiver privately.

Hmm? What's going on? Who pissed her off again?

Looking at that darkened face, it seemed she had a belly full of resentment with nowhere to vent it. It would surely fester into internal injuries sooner or later~

But I've been out causing trouble all day. Whoever pissed her off probably wasn't me, right?

Although Little Merlin didn't think he was the one who angered Alice, seeing her unpleasant expression still made him a bit timid.

After all, a woman's mood changed faster than anyone else's. Don't let her take her resentment out on him just because she didn't like the look of him.

So Little Merlin gently closed the door and carefully followed along the wall, wanting to climb onto the dining table, grab a bite to eat, and then go to sleep.

Merlin could already smell the aroma of freshly baked bread. Alice must have finished baking and had been waiting for him to come back the whole time.

"Merlin..."

Alice was wearing a house dress, barefoot on the sofa, not even turning around. She had assumed Merlin would come back and voluntarily say something. But instead, as soon as he returned, he bolted toward the dining table like a thief.

"! ! !"

Little Merlin stopped in his tracks, as if struck by lightning, his whole body going rigid as he turned to look at the back of Alice's head.

Crap! Has this woman already focused her attention on me?

There was no one else in the room. If she needed to vent her resentment... the only target could be me!

Darn it! Do I have to play the child again? This old master doesn't want to act cute...

Little Merlin's thoughts raced. He decided to take the initiative and unload a barrage of flattery first.

"Ahaha~ Could this possibly be Miss Alice Cloudia, the first foreign Thorn Knight in the history of the kingdom? My apologies, my apologies. I didn't notice you were here just now, otherwise I definitely would have greeted you~"

"Tch!" Alice furrowed her brows slightly. Merlin's words always sounded so grating, carrying a hint of sarcasm. "What's with that tone? Are you mocking me?"

"Not at all! Haha..." Little Merlin laughed awkwardly, thinking that sure enough, this had to be a sign of early menopause. Starting to overthink and pick fights for no reason.

Alice turned her head, looked at Little Merlin, and asked with deep meaning, "Now that I've become one of the supreme knights of Britannia, are you particularly unbalanced inside?"

"Don't talk nonsense. How could I be unbalanced? Wasn't this what we agreed on from the start? Your glory is my glory. A mutually beneficial cooperation. We're working together to clear our massive debts and restore our freedom. You're now adorned with glory, and I imagine those employers will pay a higher price to hire us. Isn't that great?" Little Merlin said earnestly.

"Do you really think that way? I stepped on your shoulders all the way up. I didn't put in much effort at all. Can you really accept this reality?" Alice asked tentatively.

"Of course. Today's honor also includes your efforts..." Little Merlin nodded, but in his heart he thought, what else can I do but accept it? I put in 99.9% effort, and it still can't compare to your 0.1% luck!

Alice narrowed her eyes and asked suspiciously, "Did you take the wrong medicine today? Your little mouth is as sweet as honey..."

"No, hah..." Little Merlin chuckled nervously, thinking, I have a will to survive too! You come back with a long face. Shouldn't I say something nice? Once I recover, I won't need to read your moods! Tsk!

"Then... there was something quite strange at today's investiture ceremony..." Alice paused, staring into Merlin's eyes. "Queen Elizabeth actually mentioned you?"

"Huh!?" Little Merlin suddenly froze, thinking that Elizabeth still owed him quite a bit of money. She should be the most afraid of seeing her creditor. So why would she mention him? That's weird... What did she say?"

"What were you expecting? Do you have a good personal relationship with the queen?" Alice suddenly transformed into a detective, observing all of Merlin's reactions.

"... Ah..." Cold sweat streamed down Merlin's back. "Why are you asking that?"

"During today's investiture ceremony, Her Majesty the Queen specifically asked whether you were in L Rexem. Your relationship is obviously quite close, isn't it? I remember you once got your hands on a stocking from somewhere and said it belonged to the Queen of Britannia..." Alice's tone was rather peculiar.

"..." Little Merlin was drenched in cold sweat, thinking, oh my god! Alice usually seems scatterbrained, but why does she become so sharp at times like this! She can remember some trivial matter from so long ago so clearly!

"Merlin, be honest. Stop beating around the bush. Did you and Queen Elizabeth... have some kind of inappropriate affair?" Alice's tone was full of implication. Although she phrased it委婉, she was clearly asking whether Merlin and Elizabeth had something going on behind her back.

Little Merlin recalled the拘泥 scene with Elizabeth in the little wooden cabin, and his heart suddenly turned into inexplicable panic.

No way! If this continues, Alice will figure something out!

Right now I'm powerless. I can't let this vinegar jar explode on the spot. I need to turn the tables!

"Enough! Alice, I never expected you to be the type of person like this!?"

"Me!?" Alice was stunned, pointing at herself and asking in return, "What about me?"

"With someone as... as... ah, damn it! With someone as upright as me, you actually suspect I did something lewd to the queen! I'm so disappointed!" Little Merlin spoke with forceful tone, making it seem like Alice was the one in the wrong.

"No... no..." Alice stood up, her face showing reluctance, "... I didn't say anything..."

"By your side, the whole world knows there's a man living off a woman next to you. Would it be strange if Her Majesty the Queen knew my name? You actually have the nerve to say my relationship with Elizabeth is deep!" Little Merlin feigned a pained expression, looking into Alice's eyes and saying, "I'm a demon. The only human who has a deep relationship with me... is you."

"Uh!"

Alice's breath hitched. It felt as if she had been shot straight in the heart by a shotgun. Her cheeks flushed red for no apparent reason, and she lowered her head, unable to say anything.

The only human who has a deep relationship with me? This guy can casually say things so embarrassing.

In a way, isn't this describing that my position in Merlin's heart is unique?

What is this? It made my heartbeat speed up a bit. N-no... I can't let him lead me by the nose...

Although Alice was very resistant inside, her body was unexpectedly honest. She waved at Merlin.

"Let's not mention this anymore. Come eat quickly. I made some of your favorite dishes specially."

"..." Little Merlin looked at Alice's graceful back, and suddenly a wicked smile appeared behind his back.

Heh~ nice

Alice's attitude changed from before, becoming much gentler, and she began to actively take care of little Merlin, treating him like a child. Little Merlin didn't refuse, enjoying Alice's care openly, even getting a bit pushy. "Alice, my shoulders are a bit sore, help me rub them." …………… Alice frowned, rubbing Merlin's small shoulders from behind, thinking that since he's not feeling well, a little care is appropriate? But why does it always feel like someone is being treated like a servant? Don't go overboard, I'm not a maid!" Alice angrily sat opposite Merlin, her face displeased, having been dazed by Merlin's sweet talk, now calm she realized it was just a routine. "I'm still a child, you radiate motherly light, you should take care of me attentively~" Little Merlin said righteously, at this moment he also knew how to use his advantage as a child. "Huh? I have to use motherly radiance to protect you? Disgusting! Humph!" Alice turned her head away angrily. Absolutely not! Humph!" "Helen… is our demon race's fallen angel, not a good woman…" Little Merlin broke out in big sweat on his forehead. "I don't care! It's not allowed, male slaves are fine." Little Merlin frowned, awkwardly explaining, "I already can't eat anymore, and I still haven't thought about detox…" "Really? Let me help you...." Alice at this moment was wearing home pajamas, without any padding, her chest looked unusually flat, yet she still reached into her own chest, pulled out a bean, "Use croton bean!" "You airport, don't learn the special move of those busty characters! It doesn't suit you!" Little Merlin rolled his eyes, his face full of disdain. At the same time, in the distant United Kingdom lands. The elves' palace is built upon a towering tree. They yearn for peace, perfectly blending with nature. Although the elves also have a few ordinary folks, the vast majority possess extremely high magical talent. Moreover, they are beautiful and dignified, with an otherworldly demeanor, possessing nearly eternal lifespans and ageless bodies. title: Chapter 6 — Beset by Misfortune
content:
Chapter 6 — Beset by Misfortune

Volume 22 · Chapter 6

"If it weren't for this desperate situation, I wouldn't have involved Sherry. If possible, I hope she can continue to live carefree." The Elf King said wearily.

"If you insist on that, who will lead the clan forward? This last land belonging to our race will also disappear completely. Must we fight to the death with humans to fight for a place to live?" Hillph lowered her head, silently clenching her fists.

"Don't be so pessimistic, Hillph..." The Elf King slowly raised his head, speaking seriously,

"We still have a chance..."

"Your power has retreated to this extent, where is the chance?" Hillph raised her head in astonishment.

"Whatever I say next, don't tell anyone. This is a secret of our race. You are my most trusted subordinate and have the right to know this. If something happens to me, I hope you can lead the people to survive..." The Elf King's tone became serious, like a dying entrustment.

"...Hillph was startled, her gaze serious as she responded, 'Although I don't know if I have the ability to inherit your legacy, I am willing to do my utmost, even offer my life.'"

"In fact, most of the gods of this world have fallen, and the Elf God Corellon is no exception. However, his remains and divine artifact were left behind, preserved in the Secret Realm." The Elf King panted and continued, "If my orthodox bloodline can be poured onto the Elf God's remains, it could trigger a miracle, and with the artifact's power, the kingdom will no longer face the threat of the abyss beneath the sea."

"I'm willing to enter the Secret Realm for you!" Hillph immediately knelt on one knee, requesting to complete this task.

"No. The condition to enter the Secret Realm requires strength to break the shackles of the Saint-tier, otherwise you will be shattered by the lingering might of the Elf God once inside." The Elf King said calmly.

"If there is such a way to solve the kingdom's hidden danger, why didn't you enter the Secret Realm long ago?" Hillph asked puzzledly. Although the Elf King's power had retreated greatly now, it was once terrifying; he probably had long broken through the Saint-tier shackles.

"If it only required matching strength, that would be too simple. The most stringent condition is that entering the Secret Realm requires two people, and they must deeply love each other. Because of this, I have been unable to enter the Secret Realm." The Elf King said distressedly.

"How could this be? Breaking through the Saint-tier shackles is already hard enough, yet both must reach this realm and must be in love?... It's like a joke!" Hillph found it hard to understand these harsh conditions.

"The earliest records show that the Secret Realm had no condition of the two being in love. But a long, long time ago, before the land beneath our feet separated from the main continent, a giant rock fell from the sky, directly shattering the Secret Realm's gate and merging with it, changing the rules of entry. To enter the depths of the Secret Realm, one must find a way to move that rock." The Elf King's tone revealed...

"What exactly is this rock of unknown origin? Can't you move it?" Hillph asked puzzledly.

"I don't know. It looks no different from an ordinary meteorite, but during my prime, I couldn't move it even a bit." The Elf King explained.

"...Hillph lowered her head, astonished in her heart. Something even the Elf King couldn't move in his prime? It feels extraordinary!"

"The person I loved most in my life is Andiya, but from when I don't know, her disposition changed drastically - she was taciturn and ignored me. The Elf King thought of his princess consort and said with melancholy, 'Sometimes I see hatred and loathing deep in her eyes. I don't know what I did wrong?'"

"Her Highness... perhaps... she's just in a bad mood..."

Hillph dared not make rash judgments.

"No, that hostility is sincere. That look... I've only seen it in my younger brother's eyes." The Elf King paused, suspiciously saying, "When Sherry returned from exile abroad, I thought Andiya would become happier, but it wasn't like that. Her eyes revealed disappointment and resentment, as if she didn't want to see Sherry return at all, wishing she had died out there..."

"Your Majesty, you... you're joking, right? Maybe you're just too tired..." Hillph widened her eyes, feeling incredibly shocked. Although she had long known the Elf King and princess consort had a poor relationship, she never expected it to be this bad!

"Why do you think I never let Sherry out of my sight? Because I'm worried about her safety. The person who nearly killed her is her own biological mother." The Elf King's gaze grew heavy; he had long sensed danger.

"......." Hillph's heart couldn't calm down, as if she heard something unbelievable. Perhaps because the Elf King's body could barely hold on anymore, that was why he said so much as if slightly insane.

"Perhaps I made the wrong choice back then, trying my life to kill my younger brother Asmodeus, and the curse descended upon me. My retribution has come..." The Elf King's eyes went hollow, his whole body beginning to tremble uncontrollably. Killing his own brother was like a nightmare deep in his heart.

"Your Majesty! Calm down. The Dark Elf King died because he brought it on himself. He was just a scoundrel who tried to split the alliance!" Hillph shouted.

"...The Elf King gradually came back to his senses, sighing, "Sorry, my head isn't clear anymore."

"So it seems, if you can't hold on, this place... will inevitably become dust of history..." Hillph's expression was lost.

"No, Hillph..." The Elf King's gaze flickered, like stars in the distant sky, "You know I have some precognitive ability. Last night I dreamed of vague omens - two mysterious people are coming. One born from the land of darkness and fire, the other bathed in divine light. Two completely opposite people, they will end my...misfortune..."

"Dark and... bathed in divine light...?" Hillph muttered to herself, completely unable to guess the identities of these two people. She knew the Elf King's precognitive ability was limited, and could only guess what was coming based on vague things.

In the corner of the top-floor palace, a pair of scarlet eyes suddenly lit up.

Black skin, ranger's low-key attire, pointed ears - unmistakably a black elf.

Black elves also belong to the elf race, serving Asmodeus as king.

Until the Dark Elf King died, they lost their leader, yet they still operated in the shadows.

The Elf King's power had retreated so severely that even a black elf sneaking into the palace was hard to detect, showing he was no longer a fearsome existence.

The black elf lowered his hat, carefully sneaking out of the palace, glancing at the Elf King who was full of tubes, revealing a look of disdain.

The Elf King's era is about to pass; it's time to welcome Asmodeus's return...

title: Chapter 7 — Ashmodor (Extra)
content:
Chapter 7 — Ashmodor (Extra)

Volume 22 · Chapter 7

The Elf King just said these things; his power has weakened to an unimaginable degree, and his spirit is gradually becoming unable to bear the burden. In a certain room of the palace, the returning dark elf knelt on one knee, nervously gazing at the graceful figure before him. A beautiful woman with wavy blond hair stood before the mirror in a white nightgown, examining herself. Her skin was pale and could emit a faint glow even in the night, and her pointed ears added a touch of nobility. This is the Elf King's queen, Andiya; at some point her temperament changed drastically, turning her into a woman whom everyone respects and keeps their distance from. If one carefully observes the mirror before Andiya, it's easy to see that the reflection is not herself, but a handsome man who looks exactly like the Elf King. An elf who could possess the same appearance as the Elf King—aside from Ashmodor, there is probably no one else in the world. Although Ashmodor was personally killed by the Elf King long ago, he did not die completely; a wisp of his soul devoured Andiya, becoming the person closest to her brother. However, the mighty Elf King's appearance in the mirror is that of a woman's thin nightgown, making the scene look extremely eerie. "Is that so? He finally can't hold on anymore?" "Indeed, I infiltrated the palace this time on an adventure and didn't even notice; it's far off from when my perception was extremely strong." The dark elf raised his head, speaking confidently, "If it weren't for Silf being present, I think I would have the confidence to kill the Elf King." "Ha... Andiya chuckled lightly, 'Even you have the confidence to take down my brother; it seems he truly is at the end of his rope.' "But the Elf King gave a prophecy that two people would be able to save the entire kingdom and end his..." The dark elf said doubtfully. "Oh? Please tell me in detail?" Andiya furrowed her brows, deeply aware of the Elf King's precognitive ability; although vague, it could still see many future events. "One born in a land of darkness and fire, another bathed in divine..." The dark elf recalled. "Darkness and fire? Bathed in divine light?" Andiya's brows knit together; after thinking, she suddenly understood, "Darkness and fire means a barren and evil land, hinting at the demons' territory, bathed in divine... refers to those who believe in deities, possibly the clergy of the human Holy Church..." "Demons and clergy?" The dark elf's expression instantly turned strange, for the Elf King's prophecy said only two people who love each other would enter the secret realm; this pair is obviously mortal enemies, how could they possibly love each other? "Recently, we have strictly monitored any outsiders who have entered, especially demons and clergy; if possible, we will secretly close the port and recently prohibit all contact with the outside world." Andiya gave a serious command, since it is the Elf King's prophecy, we need to guard against it. "Yes, sir, I will convey the master's order to others overnight." The dark elf lowered his head in response. Although the dark elf has always found it hard to be valued by the Elf King, doing only manual labor, he is at the lowest stratum of the elf race. Nevertheless, many dark elves serve as guards and soldiers; controlling the kingdom's communication with the outside is not difficult. Many dark elves still believe deep down that Ashmodor will return and then change the situation of the dark elves being oppressed. "I absolutely will not allow the prophecy to come true; the Elf King's misfortune is his deserved retribution." Andiya paused, then said optimistically, "As long as we forbid demons and Holy Church personnel from entering here, the prophecy cannot come true. When I return from the cleft of hell, nothing will be able to stop me; I am the successor of the Elf God and ought to become the leader of the elf race." "That's right, we all believe in your talent, but those foolish idiots are willing to believe the Elf King's honeyed words and support him..." The dark elf echoed ruefully. "These are not problems; I will use my own means to let all elves know that I am the trustworthy one." Andiya glanced at her slender hand, her face showing flashes of displeasure, "Our plan can begin now; the Elf King is so weak, this is a good opportunity for my return. Give the order, start preparing the Elf Lamentation ritual." The dark elf lifted his head, his eyes showing excitement; this means Ashmodor will return to this land again. "Master, have you made up your mind?" "Of course, I have always dreamed of this day; last time in the Britannia Kingdom, I was clearly just a little short, but a sudden blond adventurer disrupted my plans; if it weren't for him, I would have returned already!" Andiya's face twisted with anger as she looked at the dark-skinned male elf in the mirror, "After I kill the Elf King, I will definitely find that adventurer and tear him apart alive!" "No... Even if the Elf King is now insignificant, there are still leaders of other races who might... disrupt the Elf Lamentation ritual?" The dark elf said worriedly. "Although the chiefs of the nine great clans in the council possess extraordinary strength, they are basically disunited; they will not rush to save the Elf King at first. As long as I return to my own body, they are all ants!" Andiya clenched her fist, adding, "Not long ago I offered the Cave King wine mixed with hallucinogenic drugs; as long as I speak, it will regard me as mother and obey my commands!" "Cave King? Chief of the stone clan... The dark elf stared, his heart greatly startled; the Cave King is a stone giant, though not as huge as a true giant, but comparable, possessing terrifying defensive and destructive power; even the Elf King at his peak would not lightly confront it head-on!" "We are in an absolute advantage; this time I will definitely succeed!" Andiya is full of confidence; the Elf King's decline has given her hope, and she has finally risen to prominence. The more she looked at herself in the mirror wearing a woman's skirt, the more displeased she became; she simply took off all her clothes, revealing a sexy, alluring body. She is young and beautiful, with long brows and delicate shoulders, a slender figure, her eyes like shifting stars; under the moonlight she is gorgeous. Even the dark elf behind her felt his heart race, blushing and lowering his head, not daring to look directly, for the woman before him seemed to be Andiya but was actually the body occupied by Ashmodor! Andiya's mood improved; she did not admire her sexy, alluring body, but instead looked at the handsome, sturdy dark elf youth in the mirror—that was her original appearance. "It's a pity that Shirley did not become my resurrection sacrifice; if she had died, my brother would have suffered even more." "But it's fine; this time I will use this body as the sacrifice for the Elf Lamentation~" "The Elf King's beloved woman, Andiya? 'I clearly she is still our cousin, yet she dares to lay hands on her own sister; brother, he is so disgusting, ah...'." In the morning of Rexham, the celebration of the foreign thorn knights ended, and everyone returned to their usual lives. In the house, Alice paced back and forth outside the bathroom door, occasionally glancing at the closed door. This scene is just like a man waiting outside the delivery room for a child's birth; she was anxious and unable to settle. Creak— The bathroom door opened, and Little Merlin emerged from inside with a refreshed face, having expelled toxins, feeling light! "How is it? Have you come out yet?" Alice asked eagerly. "Huh?" Little Merlin blinked, then said meaningfully, "Don't worry, mother and child are safe; it's a girl." Alice stared blankly, then her face flushed red, raising her voice to express her dissatisfaction, 'Merlin!!!' "Of course...." Little Merlin's face showed a smile, then gradually froze as he spread his hands and said, "I didn't pull it out!" "I've done my best; I estimate that the slave contract has already merged with my body." .It's not that I tried, but it's all up to fate+ (的叭 (

title: Chapter 8 — TITLE: Double Encirclement
content:
Chapter 8 — TITLE: Double Encirclement

Volume 22 · Chapter 8

Alice gasped, her eyes nearly closing, her mouth twitching, and her eyebrows jumping wildly.

"I don't know what's happening... According to logic, things that shouldn't be digestible should be able to be expelled, right? Merlin is thinking deeply, but he can't figure out why Helenna's slave contract isn't coming out. Maybe it's a problem with my stomach?"

"If this continues, it's definitely not a good sign..."

Alice lowered her head, her face shifting between gloom and light, and as someone who excels at imagination, she began to unleash her unique imagination--

Merlin lounged lazily on the sofa, cradling Helenna, who was dressed in a maid outfit, in his arms, looking thoroughly enjoying himself.

Helenna, in turn, peeled grapes with her hands and fed them to Merlin affectionately, looking completely submissive.

Both looked over at each other, filled with challenge and mockery.

Alice gasped, holding her head in horror, feeling like hell itself was waiting for her.

"No! No! No!"

Merlin jumped in surprise, looking at Alice in shock. "What's wrong with you? You're acting so strange."

"Merlin..." Alice crouched down, looking at Merlin and saying, "We have to find a way to get Helenna's contract out."

"That... Isn't that forcing you to do something you don't want to do?" Merlin's forehead dripped with cold sweat, shaking his hands and saying, "And besides, Helenna's slave contract being in my body is fine, right?"

"You're saying that's fine?" Alice stopped abruptly, then said unhappily, "I see! Are you trying to be sneaky? Do you want to use the slave contract to command Helenna to do some indecent things?"

"I? No!" Merlin frowned, saying awkwardly, "What do you think I am? Why would I want to do indecent things to Helenna? What's going on in your head..."

"Hmph! Don't deny it, you're thinking it, right?" Alice, as if she had been wronged, puffed up her cheeks, looking like a hamster stuffed full of food, "I won't agree to it. I'm the only female owner in the house, and I won't allow a second one."

Merlin looked at Alice with a strange expression, wondering what "the only female owner in the house" meant. It was a bit ambiguous.

"Alright, I understand. If Helenna's slave contract can't be taken out of my body, then I won't use this contract to do anything strange. Okay?"

"Are you telling the truth? You really won't do anything indecent to a female slave, right..." Alice narrowed her eyes skeptically.

"Of course!" Merlin nodded, then raised his hand, "I swear!"

"...I'll believe you five times," Alice said, but her heart was still pounding.

"Five times? Haven't I done anything indecent to you? Why do you always think of me as a weak-willed, automatic cannon when it comes to women? I don't get it..."

Merlin shook his head in frustration.

"Because... because you're a...." Alice muttered.

Merlin was speechless, waving his hands awkwardly. "Alright, I don't care. I'll go find Helenna and clear things up. Okay?"

"You have to clear things up, I can't have Merlin surrounded by a tangled mess of relationships," Alice said seriously, fearing that Helenna would become a troublesome rival.

Merlin frowned, his mouth twisted, wondering why Alice was so wary of Helenna.

Was it because she was jealous of her figure? Pfft~

Outside the secret room, Merlin stood hesitantly at the door, looking at people passing by and pointing and laughing.

He suddenly realized an embarrassing problem: two kids like him shouldn't be in such a place. They should be playing in the mud instead.

What should I do? If I go in directly, won't the female demons come out? Saying I haven't grown yet...

Just as Merlin was struggling to make a decision, he was suddenly surrounded by two shadows, and he looked back in surprise.

Hobbes and Pleas stood behind Merlin, looking at him in surprise.

"...You two" Merlin's eyes widened, not expecting to see these two old perverts here.

"This isn't Merlin's nephew, right? What are you doing standing here?" Hobbes muttered.

"Hehehe, don't you understand?" Pleas smiled wickedly, saying enthusiastically, "Standing in front of the secret room and not daring to go in, is it because you want to go in and play, but don't have the courage? No wonder, you're Merlin's nephew, and you're just like him, having a lecherous heart but no lecherous courage."

"It's true that it's similar to Merlin, the same lecherousness, haha..." Hobbes's smile grew more and more boastful.

"...No, you're misunderstanding!" Merlin frowned, being teased by the two old perverts, feeling his image was so bad in their eyes?

"Come on, don't be shy, today uncles will take you to see the world of adults." Hobbes grabbed Merlin.

"Yes, pick any big sister you like, it's on Merlin's account!" Pleas said cheerfully.

"...I'm still a child! Where are you taking me? Please, have some responsibility? You're publicly teaching minors to be bad!" Merlin struggled, feeling that he would have no good time being taken in by these two old perverts.

"No!" Pleas crouched down, patting Merlin's shoulder, "This is called releasing your nature, don't suppress yourself, explore the unknown freely! Your Merlin uncle will understand!"

"Wait... Wait!"

Merlin's resistance was ineffective, and he was hard to pull into the secret room by Hobbes and Pleas...

Inside the secret room, the flickering colored lights shimmered, and a series of seductive music played continuously.

The demon ladies came out one by one, using sweet words to cheer up the human patrons.

"Cheers!"

The ladies and gentlemen entered, feeling like they had entered their own home, and were happy beyond words, with wrinkles on their faces smiling like flowers.

The demon ladies threw themselves into the human patrons' arms, laughing softly, making people even more immersed in the intoxicating atmosphere.

Their hands became unruly, causing the demon ladies to laugh softly.

"We can reopen our shop thanks to the trust of the guard captain, who helped us solve many problems." A demon lady threw a seductive glance at Pleas.

"Indeed!" Pleas suddenly felt like he had been injected with adrenaline, "You don't know, I fought that demon who attacked the town for three hundred rounds. If I weren't strong enough, I would have seen none of you beautiful girls, hehehe~"

"That's right, I said it, Helenna is so kind, how could she be a demon? It's all because of some people's envy, jealousy, and hatred." Hobbes said, nodding in agreement.

The demon ladies laughed in a silver bell-like sound, and Merlin, who knew everything, felt like all the female demons were starving to eat him.

Merlin missed his steel body more and more, otherwise, how would he feel terrified of older women now?

The demon ladies on both sides, with their hot bodies, seemed to be deliberately using their breasts to press against his small face, as if they were openly teasing him--

Damn it!

Am I wrong?

I didn't come here for this.
