title: Chapter 33 — Great Merlin (Extra)
content:
Chapter 33 — Great Merlin (Extra)

Volume 22 · Chapter 33

"You are too naive..." The Elf King's gaze was cold as he began to rotate the golden magic wand in his hand.

This pseudo-divine artifact suddenly began rapidly draining power back into its user, and the Elf King's oppressive pressure was rising steadily!

Light of Corelon was named after the elves' sole deity, to commemorate the great figure who led his race through the dark era of the gods, and it also symbolized the supreme commander of the elf race.

This noble pseudo-divine artifact wand could continuously store the user's magic power, accumulating over years.

In moments of crisis, it could instantly return all that stored power to its master, granting them strength far beyond their own!

The Elf King held Corelon's Light horizontally before his chest, and extremely dim golden magic power erupted forth like a monstrous flood!

Its terrifying pressure no longer merely made the space tremble slightly—it produced distortions visible to the naked eye!

"So...!" Alice involuntarily gasped, every pore on her body trembling in fear before the Elf King's terror. He was the strongest creature she had ever seen aside from Merlin! Beelzebub seemed somewhat lacking in comparison standing before the Elf King!

"That is our king. As I said, he is magnificent. No one is stronger than Your Majesty." Sylph's tone was quite proud, feeling that Arcturus would repeat his past mistakes.

Arcturus's smile grew ever more excited and fanatical. In his eyes, the Elf King was like a roaring lion. "Hahaha! I knew it—he truly is my eldest brother! Of course he was hiding trump cards. This is much more interesting! Defeating you with zero ability to resist would be utterly meaningless!"

"Arcturus, this is not your place. A madman like you should remain in hell forever!" The Elf King raised the golden wand high in his hand, and ancient elven magic descended once more—

Boom, boom, boom! The earth quaked, the wind and clouds changed color, and the sky above grew dense with dark clouds as if the gods themselves were wrathful!

Endless thorns shot up from beneath the ground, instantly turning this place into a thorned hell!

Each thorn tangled together and converged, forming an earth-shaking tidal wave that swept toward Arcturus in a杀ing onslaught!

Arcturus sneered coldly. Even as sky-filling thorns engulfed him, completely obscuring even his shadow, such ferocious magic should have reduced a normal person to shreds in that thorn forest.

But the next moment, black streaks flashed across the sky, slicing those whistling thorns to pieces. Arcturus was unharmed, his body radiating only slightly dimmer golden magic power.

"Terror-inducing! This guy's strength... exceeds even the Elf King's!" Alice's face went pale; the collision of two such powerful pressures made it hard for her to breathe.

"That wand is truly useful. You spent several eras灌注ing magic into it, all just to try and kill me at this moment?"

Arcturus strolled forward carelessly.

"You were ambitious, so I had no choice but to keep a trump card to counter you." The Elf King replied coldly.

"Last time you schemed behind my back and took me down. This time, I won't give you the chance." Arcturus looked up at the Elf King in the sky. "That isn't your own strength. How long can that power of accumulated strength and deferred release actually last? After all this trouble, you can only barely catch up to my pace!"

"Is that really the case?"

The Elf King narrowed his eyes, swung Corelon's Light, and the dark clouds in the sky were instantly blown apart, revealing small orbs of light.

If one looked closely, these light orbs were a flock of winged light element spirits, and under the Elf King's call, they had actually gained physical form!

"Children of light, dance!"

The small light orbs filling the sky suddenly grew intense and began frantically firing beams of light arrows at Arcturus!

The formation of ten thousand arrows fired simultaneously was scalp-tingling, and the terrifying magic power within was even more staggering—as if each arrow could kill a Saint-tier powerhouse!

Countless light arrows hammered the earth, turning land already in ruins into a desolate wasteland, with dust and smoke rising everywhere!

"Hahaha..." Arcturus let out a mocking manic laugh from within the dust and smoke, then formed his fingers into a blade. Suddenly, a gigantic pitch-black sword芒 appeared, and with one swing he destroyed all the light element spirits. "You haven't improved at all, brother!"

"It is...!" Suddenly behind the Elf King appeared a extraordinarily beautiful woman, her snow-white luminous body and pointed ears with light wings on her back radiating pure holiness! The utterly terrifying magic power was converging upon the golden wand!

"Huh!" A drop of cold sweat trickled down Arcturus's forehead as he smiled. "You're finally getting serious..."

Although the Elf King had temporarily broken through to the pseudo-divine realm, just like Beelzebub he could use Divine Power only a limited number of times,

and now the woman formed from light elements behind him was a manifestation appearing under the blessing of Divine Power, already possessing a trace of divinity.

Yet Arcturus, who was no weaker than the Elf King, had inherited part of the Elf God Corelon's power—and of course he could also use Divine Power as well!

"Not only can you use it, so can I! If Divine Power clashes with Divine Power, who knows if the entire land of the elf race won't be reduced to scorched earth?!"

Arcturus raised both hands, aimed at the Elf King, and click-clack-click! A huge golden magic array suddenly flared to life above him, bearing the insignia of the elf race.

Dots of light were converging.

Destructive aura continuously emerged, and the space around Arcturus distorted more and more severely.

"Don't forget, I inherited part of the Elf God's power. He once taught me the second of the three elven forbidden magic spells—but he didn't teach it to you. I will crush you utterly beneath my feet to prove that I alone deserve to lead the elves toward prosperity!"

"Vanish, you mad..."

The beautiful goddess behind the Elf King merged into the golden wand, and instantly brilliant light erupted, launching a light cannon hotter than the sun!

A spell cast with Divine Power had astonishing destructive power. Where the light cannon passed, the land turned to scorched earth, and even the space itself faced the danger of being torn apart!

Alice and Sylph, hiding in the shadows, didn't even dare to breathe. It was their first time witnessing such a clash of terrifying powers, and their palms were drenched in cold sweat.

"Come!" Arcturus bore immense pressure, preparing to strike back—only for that terrifying light cannon to dissipate before it reached him. "Huh?!"

The Elf King, holding the golden wand, suddenly spat blood and fell狼狈ly from the sky to the ground.

The time for Corelon's Light to recharge magic had run out. The Elf King had been knocked back to his true state, his body appearing extremely weakened.

Arcturus approached the Elf King with a desolate expression. "Brother, look at yourself now. So fragile. Is this land worth so much from you?"

"..." The Elf King couldn't stop coughing, too weak to speak.

"I'm so disappointed! Defeating you now would be meaningless to me!" Angered, Arcturus kicked the Elf King far away with one foot, black light flaring in his hand.

"But still, farewell, foolish brother..."

"..." The Elf King, his body extremely weak, looked at Arcturus with despair in his expression.

"Your Majesty... lost?" Sylph displayed an incredulous expression. In her heart, the Elf King would never lose. Indeed, to prevent the kingdom's silence, the Elf King's strength had long since declined from its former glory—the situation was worse than imagined!

Alice clenched her fists, furrowed her delicate brows and lowered her head, still worrying about little Merlin. But the other party was far too powerful. Then she heard a familiar voice.

"Alice!"

"Merlin!?" Alice suddenly raised her head, a delighted smile spreading across her face.

Little Merlin had arrived here, wanting to find Alice, but couldn't see her anywhere.

"Alice, where are you?!"

Little Merlin didn't find the hiding Alice; instead, he inadvertently disturbed the Cave King who had been searching for the two of them!

Still under control, executing "Mother" Andy's orders, it sought to kill Alice and Sylph—but encountered little Merlin!

The Cave King's gigantic body abruptly turned, the earth constantly shaking. It looked down at the "human" below like an ant.

"Uh!" Little Merlin's face went deathly pale, and he fell backward onto the ground in fright. He simply couldn't see the head of this rock giant!

The Cave King, frustrated and unable to find Alice and Sylph, grew exceptionally agitated. It unceremoniously hurled a fist straight at little Merlin!

..."Little Merlin's legs went somewhat soft. He stumbled and scrabbled, trying to flee, but the opponent's range was enormous—he couldn't escape. All he could see were shadows looming over him.

"Me—rlin! !!"

Alice panicked, instinctively rushing from her hiding spot straight toward little Merlin, forgetting her own battered and bruised body.

She quickly reached little Merlin and scooped him into her arms—but then the Cave King's fist came crashing down, striking her back.

"Eaaaaah! !!"

Alice screamed, holding little Merlin tightly as she rolled across the ground. She slid fully a hundred meters before stopping, falling into a deep unconsciousness.

Even though Alice had lost consciousness, little Merlin remained securely cradled in her arms, perfectly protected beneath her body, which served as a living shield.

Drip, drip. Warm blood trickled from Alice's head, dripping onto little Merlin's face and leaving him completely stunned.

Little Merlin saw Alice limply lying on top of him, her eyes tightly closed, her breathing faint. "...Hey... Alice, Alice! Wake up!"

"....Finally... arrived..." The Cave King slowly approached, raising its enormously huge fist and smashing down with even greater power than before. "Die!"

"Miss Alice! !!"

Sylph cried out in alarm. Her aura defense wall was like tofu against the Cave King's attacks—it provided almost no protection at all.

She bit her lip and had no choice but to close her eyes, unable to bear watching further. Yet in the darkness she heard a childish yet unwilling roar—

"What kind of joke is this? !!"

Sylph's eyes snapped open in amazement, discovering that the situation had undergone an unimaginable transformation.

That blond-haired child was gone, replaced by a blond-haired adult man!

His clothes were shredded and burst apart, hanging in tattered strips, and his children's pants had become shorts! !

Especially the scar on his chest at the heart location—it looked startlingly gruesome! !

Little Merlin was gone forever. That arrogant and rude but overwhelmingly powerful Merlin had returned! ! !

Merlin was now tightly cradling the heavily injured and unconscious Alice with one hand, while his other hand was clenched into a fist, clashing directly against the Cave King—a hundred times his size!

Two powerful presences locked fists against fists, and the earth beneath them cracked instantly, turning to powder. The air surged like waves in a violent storm.

The Cave King's hollow eyes showed confusion, seemingly unable to comprehend why a渺小 human could block its fist, why it couldn't suppress the opponent!

"Ho—how is this possible?! A human body so渺小! It actually withstood the Cave King's attack! Matching the stone giant blow for blow!"

Sylph's beautiful eyes widened, her mouth agape.

"GRAAAH!!!"

Merlin roared, suddenly increasing his strength and blasting the Cave King's gigantic body away like a cannonball with a single punch!

The Cave King, renowned for its defense, shattered its arm on the spot during the power struggle with Merlin, letting out a hysterical scream of agony!

Merlin's punch unleashed fierce shockwaves, and the earth exploded in continuous circular bursts, rolling like ocean waves as fierce winds and dust storms swept the sky!

"Ah..." Sylph's little heart was utterly stunned. She felt like her eyes might be malfunctioning. The entire area was in chaos from flying sand and stones—

Matching blow for blow?

Heh heh!

I was truly too naive.

title: Chapter 34 — Return in Kind
content:
Chapter 34 — Return in Kind

Volume 22 · Chapter 34

After blasting the Rock Cave King away with his fist, Merlin held Alice in his arms and flexed his palm a few times, a dazed look on his face.

It seemed that after being in a child's body for so long, his sudden restoration to an adult form left him struggling to adjust.

Damn it. I drank all of the antidote—why did it take so long for me to recover?

Was it because I took the antidote half a day earlier than planned that this happened?

Still, it was a relief that that old hag Circe hadn't given me a fake potion. At least I'd recovered, even if the effects were a bit unstable...

Merlin frowned and looked down at Alice in his arms. Her eyes were tightly shut, and she was in critical condition, unconscious from her injuries.

The Rock Cave King's earlier attack on Alice had been severe. Fortunately, the creature had only thrown a casual punch—if it had fought seriously, Alice's condition would have been far worse than mere critical injuries and unconsciousness.

Moreover, the ring named "Angel" had not activated, which proved Alice was still alive. Merlin secretly breathed a sigh of relief.

"Alic..."

Merlin brushed Alice's messy hair aside and lifted her up from the ground.

He glanced around and noticed Sylph in the distance, staring blankly in his direction as though her soul had left her body.

Merlin decided to have her help take care of the unconscious Alice and slowly walked over.

"What are you spacing out for?"

"Huh!?" Sylph jolted as though waking from a dream, stammering in confusion, "W-w-who are you!?"

"What? I've returned to my adult form and you can't recognize me?" Merlin gave her a meaningful smile.

"...Sylph fell stunned. The disheveled blonde man before her was none other than that smug brat. Recalling what had just happened, she wondered if everything Sherry had exaggerated about was actually true? To have repelled the Rock Cave King—his strength was undeniable!

"Please take care of Alice for me..." Merlin set Alice down in his arms and appeared to be going off to do something else.

"What are you going to do? It's dangerous everywhere right now!" Sylph couldn't help but remind him.

"Then..." Merlin gazed toward the distant Dark Elf King and said calmly, "I have some scores to settle with that guy."

"Huh?! " Sylph suddenly furrowed her brows, "You're not joking, right?"

"Of course not." Merlin took Banri Garan off Alice's body.

"But... that's Dark Elf King Ashador!" Sylph paused and said seriously, "I know you can repel the Rock Cave King and you're very strong, but Ashador is completely different from the leaders of the other races. He inherited a portion of divine power, and he also knows the Elf Race's second forbidden magic—

"The second forbidden magic?" Merlin looked puzzled.

"That's right. That magic has devastating destructive power. In the past, Ashador was the strongest presence in our clan. Relying on that forbidden magic, he swept through countless powerful enemies and built the elves' current prestige. Back then, if anyone dared to resist Ashador, their kingdom would have vanished overnight. Do you understand?" Sylph hoped Merlin wouldn't act recklessly. Even if he had repelled the Rock Cave King, Ashador was on an entirely different level!

"Is that so? The elf race's forbidden magic? Sounds kind of interesti— Merlin lifted his eyelids.

"Even if you go, you'll just be throwing your life away. Why not take Miss Alice and leave while you still can? You two don't belong to this land anyway—there's no need to get involved in this conflict." Sylph suggested. The current situation was an internal crisis of the elf race, which had nothing to do with two humans.

"Can't do that. I'm someone who holds grudges," Merlin smiled, grabbed Banri Garan, and turned to leave. "An eye for an eye, a tooth for a—"

"Hey! Don't you understand what I'm saying?" Sylph widened her eyes, unable to comprehend his actions.

Merlin waved his hand without looking back at Sylph and headed toward the distant Ashador—

"Take care of Alice for me. I'll be right back—"

"Goodbye forever, older brother."

Black light surged from Ashador's palm, intending to bring this drawn-out conflict to a close.

The counter-magic of Coirland's Light had expired, and the Elf King's power was instantly depleted, leaving him abnormally weak.

To put it bluntly, in his current state, Ashador could kill the Elf King as easily as crushing an ant.

"Cough..." The Elf King lay weakly on the ground, lifting his head to look at Ashador. "The prophecy... will ultimately come true."

"At a time like this, you still believe in your own prophecy? ... Heh..." Ashador's expression turned dark and sinister. "Go to hell, brother. Watch closely from below as I revive our race."

The sound of tearing air rang out. The Rock Cave King's massive body blotted out the sun, its right arm completely shattered.

The rock giant flew past Ashador's head at extreme speed, shouting in its mouth.

"... ... Latin... You—"

The Rock Cave King vanished into the horizon, turning into a star, with only echoes lingering behind.

"What happened?" Ashador turned around in confusion and saw a shirtless blonde man carrying a ōdachi slowly walking toward him. "Who is that?"

"!!!" The Elf King looked puzzled, gazing at the approaching figure from afar.

Ashador narrowed his eyes. The more he looked, the more familiar the man seemed. Suddenly, an image flashed through his mind, making his eyes widen—

This... I've seen him before! When I was in the human kingdom, this bastard ruined my plans! And he killed my beloved subordinate Samuel!

I never expected fate to narrow our paths like this. It's a miracle we could meet here. Very well—today I'll settle all old scores and let him know the consequences of angering me!

"Brother, could it be that... the one who ends your destiny in the prophecy is this person?"

The Elf King said nothing, his heart filled with turmoil. He had no knowledge of Merlin and was seeing him for the first time.

"You watch here carefully. I will shatter your prophecy with my strength and show you with facts how ridiculous those vague dreams are." Ashador主动 walked toward Merlin.

The two approached each other and stopped simultaneously when they were quite close.

Face to face, the atmosphere became overwhelmingly oppressive, making it hard to breathe—

"It's you—" Ashador said, his voice filled with hatred.

"Oh? You recognize me? How unusual." Merlin curled his lips.

"We've met before. Back in Britain, I saw you. You ruined my plans..." Ashador narrowed his eyes.

"Oh~ So it's you. Perfect. Then everything can be settled once and for all..." Merlin gave a mysterious smile, recalling the giant eyeball in the sky and remembering he'd sustained minor injuries himself?

"Heh heh..." Ashador let out a string of cold laughs, his expression contorted. "It should be me who settles with you. Last time you barely escaped with your life, and now you dare to walk right into my hands? My strength now is not the half-baked power of back then. Killing you is simply— Pfft!"

Before Ashador could finish, Merlin looked up and slapped him across the face with a crisp sound.

"..." Ashador's eyes widened, his gaze blank as he clutched his left cheek. "...You actually hit me? You audacious adventurer, how dare you harm my body! I am the great— Pfft!"

Merlin increased his force and delivered a second slap with his other hand, striking Ashador's right cheek!

Ashador's body spun uncontrollably through the air like a spinning top, crashing through several thick walls before coming to a halt.

Merlin looked at Ashador lying on the ground in the distance, silently lowered his arm, and said seriously—

"I told you long ago—"

"That slap would be returned to you double."

title: Chapter 35 — Forbidden Magic (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 35 — Forbidden Magic (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 22 · Chapter 35

The Elf King gazed into the distance and saw Ashtodur being thrown to the ground, feeling astonished; who was that guy—human?

However, Sylph saw Ashtodur being humiliated by Merlin, and her heart grew increasingly panicked—it's over! No one has ever humiliated Ashtodur before; he will surely retaliate a hundredfold!

Lying on the ground, Ashtodur suddenly rose into the air, hovering mid‑air, his face swollen and reddened from Merlin's strike.

He opened his mouth and spat, spitting the fallen tooth onto the ground; the pressure around his body raged, warping space, his murderous gaze unhidden—

"This is the first time in my life I've been slapped and humiliated; you have some nerve."

"Likewise, it was my first time too. How does it feel?" Merlin grinned.

"I swear, you will pay a terrible price for this!"

Ashtodur's eyes sharpened, and with a "whoosh" he vanished from his spot and appeared behind Merlin.

He laughed arrogantly, snapping a whip‑like kick that tore through the air, aiming to kick Merlin's head clean off!

"Are you looking down on me?" Merlin's pupils suddenly turned to his back, staring at Ashtodur.

"Uh!"

Ashtodur halted his movement, thinking that this adventurer's perception seemed extremely sharp—could it be that none of his actions could escape his eyes?

Merlin reached back, grabbed Ashtodur's ankle, and slammed him hard in front of him!

Ashtodur's face hit the ground, sliding across it and carving a shocking trench, his butt stuck up in a pitiful, disheveled pose.

"Back in Britannia you did wound me. Could you show me that move again?" Merlin said expressionlessly.

Ashtodur rolled over, his eyes full of hostility, "You don't deserve it. Dealing with you doesn't even require my full strength..."

"Is that so? You'll change your mind..." Merlin strode forward, calmly approaching Ashtodur.

Ashtodur's gaze showed doubt as he saw flaws all over Merlin's body—obviously a death trap?

Or perhaps the other side doesn't consider me worth noticing, so he dares to walk forward unguarded!

Damn it! No matter how much I think about it, since you are offering yourself to die, don't blame me for being ruthless!

Ashtodur swung his arms, conjuring a dense swarm of magical light projectiles out of thin air, raining down like a meteor shower, bombarding Merlin from every direction with no blind spot—

"Disappear for me!"

Countless black magical bolts surged, blasting everything before them into ruin; shockwaves of wind and flame erupted continuously.

NI VJKX = :

The already devastated land, under the storm of magical light bolts, turned into a cratered surface like that of the moon!

"Hehehe..." Ashtodur laughed triumphantly, his internal magic seeming endless, tirelessly bombarding the scene, but the next second his smile froze, "How could this be?"

Merlin emerged from the flames and explosions; the incoming magical bolts seemed to fear Merlin, veering away and detonating behind him.

Without invoking Divine Power, ordinary magic has no effect on Merlin!

"Impossible!" Ashtodur increased his output, refusing to believe it, as if he wanted to blow the entire kingdom into the sky!

Merlin's sword flashed in an instant to Ashtodur's left side, its uncanny speed sending chills down the spine.

"Are you setting off fireworks to liven the atmosphere?"

.....

Ashtodur's expression was blank; he had not anticipated this at all, the opponent's actions surpassing his perception!

He glanced sideways at Merlin's smiling yet ominously grim face, his mind going blank...

Merlin's fist struck Ashtodur's face, distorting his features and sending him flying backward!

Stunned, Ashtodur rose into the air, forming a blade with his hand; dim golden magic burst forth, creating a magical blade aura.

He roared, swinging the magical blade down, tearing the ground beneath him cleanly.

A thunderous rumble shook the area, accompanied by a massive crash; the earth split into a black chasm, its bottom invisible.

Breathing heavily, Ashtodur thought that such a powerful attack should have killed that guy, right?

"Hahaha! Serves you right! This is the fate of those who oppose me!"

"You're celebrating too early!"

Merlin's whereabouts were unpredictable; he suddenly appeared above Ashtodur, descended swiftly, and kicked Ashtodur's back hard, stomping him down!

Because Merlin's speed was so great, Ashtodur couldn't discern his position, suffering constantly in the clash.

"Boom!" Ashtodur fell from the sky, his face hitting the ground again, carving a crater over 300 feet in diameter, riddled with fissures.

Merlin landed on the ground, looking at Ashtodur's disheveled state, "You're weak. With that kind of strength you still brag about ruling the world? Did you underestimate what's out there..."

"....."

Ashtodur trembled all over, blood oozing from the gaps between his teeth.

He clenched his fists, lifted his head, his expression twisted, eyes full of hatred, his mind fixed on one thought—

To slice the adventurer before him to pieces!

The Elf King furrowed his brows, watching Merlin in the distance, a wave of doubt rising in his heart. Who was that blond man? Though humans have short lifespans, have they already produced someone so powerful? A terrifying figure, yet even though he easily suppressed Ashtodur, he hadn't given his all—could this human withstand the forbidden magic unleashed by Divine Power?

"....." Sylph kept an eye on Alice, swallowing nervously, recalling how she had boasted about sparring with Merlin—now it seemed she had escaped a disaster.

"Adventurer, you are the strongest opponent I've ever faced in my life, but it's over now..." Ashtodur raised both hands toward the monument forest, the Divine Power hidden deep within him awakening, the space around him warping, a unique pressure making it hard to breathe. "You will face the first forbidden magic of our race, its power enough to destroy a thriving empire in a single night, never before defeated! Dying in this Demon Lord's realm is a lifelong honor. You are, aside from my brother, one of the few who forced me to use forbidden magic! I admit you are a peerless champion, equal to me!"

Merlin grew slightly more serious, for he sensed a hint of danger; Ashtodur's pressure underwent a qualitative change, like a deity high above, now gazing down upon him!

The Elf King closed his eyes, a trace of despair in his expression, lowered his head and let out a deep sigh.

As the leader of the elf race, he was well‑versed in the three great forbidden magics of the elves, each capable of reshaping the world.

The first forbidden magic, Soul‑Weeping, can reverse life and death, bringing the dead back to the world of the living; it is one of the few spells that lets the deceased return as a living being.

As for the second forbidden magic? With the Elf King's innate talent, he simply has no right to learn it—

"So it still has to be used?"

"Under that magic, no one can survive."

"After all, it was created by the elven god Koreilon himself, a divine technique that once slew the gods of the old age!"

title: Chapter 36 — Elven Judgment
content:
Chapter 36 — Elven Judgment

Volume 22 · Chapter 36

The ancient gods of bygone eras fell one by one, and the world teetered on the brink of collapse, desperately needing new deities to arise and construct a fresh order.

Under Corealon's leadership, the elven race seized control of the world凭借 their extraordinary magical gifts, ruling for no less than ten thousand years.

Yet the elves' golden age did not endure. As Corealon's body grew increasingly frail, their downfall approached.

In a radiant palace, the ancient elven god Corealon sat upon the throne, weary-eyed, looking down at two young elves — one dark, one light.

Having exhausted himself in the war against the gods of the old era, Corealon was now running on fumes, unable to hold on much longer. He had no choice but to choose his successor to lead the elven race onward.

Both young men knelt on one knee, their expressions diverging — each harboring private thoughts.

Arthoir's eyes barely concealed his excitement. He had already caught wind that Corealon intended to name an heir. He considered his magical talent far superior to his older brother's and saw no one else fit to bear the weight of the elven king. Who else but him?

Kneeling beside Arthoir was his elder brother, Sindael. Calmer and more composed than his younger sibling, his magical talent may have lagged behind, but he could foresee certain fragments of the future.

"My days are numbered, yet the elven race must endure, spreading our glory to every corner of the world. Therefore..."

Corealon's voice was faint, his gaze resting on the two elves below. "You two are the most outstanding among our youth. The elven king will be chosen from between you."

"Heh!" Arthoir lifted his head, his heart racing with excitement. It had to be him!

Sindael, however, reacted with平澹, showing no strong attachment to the matter — a stark contrast to his brother.

"Then... tell me," Corealon asked with pointed meaning, "if you were to become elven king, what qualities would you bring?"

"I'll go first!" Arthoir stood up, eager to declare his merits. "Among the young elves, my power is the greatest and my talent the finest. If we are choosing a leader for our people, strength alone is not enough — how else could we lead the race to resist invaders and protect every elf? Clearly, I am the most suited to be elven king!"

"Well said..." Corealon nodded, turning his gaze to the silent Sindael. "And you, Sindael? Do you not wish to be leader?"

"I do want to, but this responsibility is too heavy for me to take lightly. Still, if I were to become elven king, I would give everything to lead our people to survive." Sindael answered briefly.

"Very well..." Corealon nodded again, signaling approval, then fell into quiet thought before speaking. "I am satisfied with both your answers. The one to inherit my mantle—"

Arthoir could hardly mask his joy, certain Corealon would speak his name next. Compared to his brother's answer, he was clearly the superior choice!

Corealon studied Arthoir for a moment, then shifted his gaze to the side. "Sindael. It is you. You are the one capable of inheriting my legacy."

Sindael lifted his head in bewilderment, wondering why he — who fell short of Arthoir in every way — had been chosen as elven king.

"What!?" Arthoir's eyes widened as though struck by a massive hammer, unable to accept reality. He could not help but cry out in protest. "Why!? Why not me!? Am I not strong enough!? In what way am I inferior to my brother!?"

"Calm yourself, Arthoir..." Corealon paused, his voice aged and measured. "Your talent is exceptional and you are already powerful enough. It is not that you are insufficient."

"Then why!?" Arthoir was devastated, his disappointment palpable. "I trained day and night, preparing to succeed you, and in the end I receive nothing! For what purpose did I exhaust myself!?"

"You must understand — being a leader requires more than sheer power. A calm mind and far-sighted wisdom are more important than raw strength. These two qualities are what a leader must possess, ensuring our race never makes catastrophic errors that could lead to total destruction in the future..." Corealon explained his reasoning for choosing Sindael.

"How can this be..." Arthoir lowered his head, fists clenched, his heart churning with resentment. Why Sindael? He was superior in every way! Yet Corealon chose someone who lacked anything he possessed!? Was he truly not worthy of such a重任!

"Sindael, will you bear the future of our race?" Corealon paused, gazing at the future elven king before him. "You are a child I watched grow. Your mind is sharp and calm, adept at observing the whole picture and making sound judgments. No one is more suited to lead the elves than you."

"If you trust me, I will give my all." Sindael replied with unwavering conviction.

"Arthoir, do not lose heart. I deeply appreciate your talent and strength — your future is immeasurable." Corealon paused, then raised a finger. Golden elven runes erupted in dense clusters before Arthoir's eyes.

"...Arthoir froze, staring at the ancient script and sensing threads of terrifying, destructive aura radiating from it.

"This is one of our race's three forbidden magics. I once used it to slay a god of the old era — its power is no trivial matter." Corealon closed his eyes, speaking with solemn weight. "Your talent is outstanding, and you have the capacity to learn it. I bestow this magic upon you today. Though you cannot become elven king, you shall be our race's sharpest blade, aiding your elder brother in elevating the elven race to new heights. If you can cooperate with honesty, great achievements await."

Arthoir gazed at the golden script floating before him, silently clenching his fists. He had never considered supporting his elder brother.

Corealon would never have imagined that Arthuir would become the most unstable threat to the elven race's safety...

On the battlefield, wind and sand swirled in all directions.

After unleashing Divine Power, Arthoir seemed like a different person — his pressure descending like a god looking down in contempt upon the lowly mortals of the mortal realm!

Arthoir's power had grown so overwhelmingly greater than before that spatial distortions became increasingly apparent, as though space itself might tear apart at any moment.

Divine Power was no longer mere magic or battle energy — it was a unique force achieved after transcendence. Even Merlin's magic defenses could not ward it off!

Thud, thud, thud! A massive golden magic circle ignited before Arthoir, bearing the crest of the elven race. He glared furiously at Merlin in the distance.

"Forbidden magic — Elf Judgment."

All of heaven and earth seemed to freeze for a single second, then a doomsday-level aura of destruction surged forth, like monstrous demons roaring at the heavens!

From within the golden magic circle, a colossal pillar of light erupted — like a blade that split sky and earth, unstoppable!

This devastating power swept through everything like rotting wood, reducing all in its path to yellow sand. Even the strongest would be reduced to a handful of dust under the judgment of the elves!

"So this was the power that wounded me back then. I've gained a new appreciation today — the power of this magic is truly formidable!" Merlin took a step back, gripping the hilt of Banri Garan, adopting a drawing stance. Facing a Divine Power strike several times stronger than what he had endured in Britain, a faint smile of excitement flickered across his face.

"You may have the qualification to stand against demon lords, but to me—"

"—it's nothing but so-so!"

title: Chapter 37 — Shatter the Legend
content:
Chapter 37 — Shatter the Legend

Volume 22 · Chapter 37

When Arthur was nearly revived in Britain, he had once used Elven Judgment enhanced with Divine Power against Merlin, injuring him.

But this time, Arthur had unleashed this forbidden magic at the peak of his power, and its strength was incomparable to what it had been back then!

As one of the three forbidden magics of the elf race that had slain gods, anyone who witnessed this绝望ful light would feel terror deep within their hearts.

The elf prince sighed, silently closing his eyes. He had originally thought that this shirtless man was the savior foretold in his prophecy, but now it seemed that was not the case. Since Arthur had already mobilized a forbidden magic, no one would survive under judgment.

The light of Elven Judgment illuminated the entire land, and the central area was completely erased, reduced to scorched earth where nothing could grow, burned alive by scorching heat waves!

The blade of judgment was like a divine sword that split heaven and earth. Space was torn apart by its tremendous power, bringing forth an apocalyptic scene as it bombed straight toward Merlin below!

The previously violent great winds had now transformed into indestructible razor blades. Merlin's eyes were unknowingly carved with tiny cuts.

Faced with Arthur's forbidden judgment, Merlin felt not a trace of fear, only marveling at the profound底蕴 of the elf race, and was still laughing heartily.

The elf king suddenly opened his eyes wide, gazing at Merlin from a great distance. A bead of cold sweat unconsciously trickled down his forehead. He thought: Is this guy a madman? He can still laugh in a situation like this?

"Vanish!!!" Arthur roared, and the light blade of Elven Judgment had already reached Merlin's face, within arm's reach.

Merlin's gaze sharpened, his expression somewhat twisted in the piercing wind like knives.

He gripped the sword hilt tightly. With a ringing sound, the heavens and earth fell silent, and he drew his blade, charging straight toward the light of judgment—

"Slash!!!"

The Iai strike erupted instantly, carrying an overwhelming aura of slaughter like overturning seas and mountains, fearlessly cutting toward Elven Judgment!

The violent great wind, the rolling dark clouds in the sky, and everyone's heartbeat—all fell into stillness!

Everyone's eyes could only see two unbelievable forces clashing: a seemingly useless Iai technique against a legendary god-slaying Elven Judgment.

This was Merlin's first time directly confronting an enemy with Divine Power; in a sense, he was battling a god!

The menacing sword light was invincible, crashing head-on into the light blade of Elven Judgment—

There was no fierce contest, no evenly matched struggle, only sheer碾压!

The murderous Iai strike forcibly tore the light blade of Elven Judgment apart, and bearing down through the oppressive pressure of the forbidden magic, it even split Arthur's body in two!

The forbidden magic that had once slain the gods of the old era, the pinnacle of elf civilization, was ruthlessly shattered by Merlin's Iai technique!

The ever-victorious, undefeated legendary record came to an end at this moment!

"Impossible!! I—" Arthur babbled incoherently, his body split in two, barely managing to emit a trace of unwilling wail from deep within his throat.

His gaze was vacant and unbelieving, his mind went blank, and even he couldn't figure out why he had lost to this adventurer.

I am a genius of the elf race, with outstanding magical talent, having inherited Corellon's Divine Power, and even mastering the super-strong forbidden magic that my brother wasn't qualified to learn!

How could someone so powerful be killed by an ordinary Iai technique from this adventurer before my eyes? This is impossible!

What was the point of all my hard training all these years? In the end, even a mere human adventurer could take me down with a simple draw cut!

Arthur fell from the sky, his mind in chaos, and his consciousness dissipated directly. His body did not bleed but instead erupted with countless souls from within.

These souls had been trapped during the Elf Mourning Ritual. They had not truly died; they had simply been devoured into his body by Arthur.

When Arthur died, these innocent souls would scatter and return to their bodies.

However, Queen Consort Andyia, who had been killed by Arthur, had served as the ritual's sacrifice and could not be resurrected. This would likely be a significant blow to the elf king and Sherry.

Far away, Sylph was speechless. Having witnessed Merlin's strength with her own eyes, she found her heart restless. She had never seen a human as powerful as Merlin. Even Arthur had been defeated in an overwhelming manner. Had the gap between elves and humans truly grown this large? Perhaps Princess Sherry was right; she should go see the outside world.

"Did we win?"

The elf king endured the excruciating pain coursing through his body and slowly rose to his feet. Watching the innocent souls scatter, he could hardly believe his eyes.

Against Arthur's forbidden magic, they had actually won?

How could this be! What was that Iai strike just now? Wasn't that a technique that even swordsmen would disdain to learn, mere showy filler moves?

Wait. That sword.

The elf king came to a sudden standstill, his attention captivated by the nodachi in Merlin's hand. The blade was rust-stained and full of notches, a dull piece of aged scrap metal.

"That demon race's royal artifact, the signet of authority worn by Lucifer..."

The elf king, a creature who had lived countless ages, may not have been the strongest in terms of power or talent, but his experience and knowledge were unmatched by almost anyone.

He had once seen the two monarchs of the First Demon Lord Palace, the first Lucifer and the second Lucifer Vivian. He naturally knew intimately the signets of authority they wore.

This nodachi looked extremely antique, almost like a worn-out broken blade, yet the unique power radiating from it was irreplaceable by any ordinary weapon. It possessed the power to steal life for its wielder.

The elf king, a living fossil, had heard the legend of the demon sword Banri Garan, the weapon of the Demon Lord's prophet and the hero who ended the age of the gods.

It was not originally in this humble appearance but was a bona fide divine artifact, its blade entirely black and accompanied by surging flaming fire.

According to legend, the power of Banri Garan was so tremendous that when fully unleashed, it could cause the world's waters to evaporate instantly. A certain divine fire was said to dwell within it; if the wielder was not powerful enough, the blade's flames would backlash and turn them to ashes.

As for why this artifact, once so oppressive even to the gods, had become what it was now—the elf king did not know. This was a secret of the demon race.

Merlin took a deep breath. Banri Garan returned the freshly stolen life force to him, bringing waves of comfort to his heart.

Arthur's power was indeed formidable. His cursed heart beat noticeably stronger, a phenomenon he had never experienced before.

Merlin sheathed Banri Garan and turned to check on Alice's condition. She would likely need him to look after her for some time.

Countless faintly glowing souls drifted throughout the sky, returning to their bodies. Countless elves awoke, their faces filled with bewilderment, unsure of what had happened.

"Why has the Demon Lord appeared here?" The elf king wondered, watching Merlin disappear from his sight. He then lowered his head silently, thinking—

Since he held Banri Garan, that royal artifact, he must be the third-generation master of the First Demon Lord Palace. He looks so young.

Time passes so quickly. Has that domineering fellow Vivian already retired?

title: Chapter 38 — Guilty Conscience (Extra)
content:
Chapter 38 — Guilty Conscience (Extra)

Volume 22 · Chapter 38

Three days later, the turmoil gradually subsided, and most of the elves awoke after the howling of Ashudor.
Although they didn't know what had happened, they still heard some clues from the survivors, couldn't help but feel uneasy, and muddledly managed to save their lives.
The leaders of the other major clans also heard about Ashudor's return, and couldn't help but panic; only after hearing that the turmoil had subsided did they put their minds at ease.
While the Elf King was busy handling the aftermath, Ashudor's remnants were captured and imprisoned, and the elf clan carried out a major purge internally.
As for Shirley? Merlin heard from Shirley that Shirley, having lost her mother Andiya, fell into grief and hid in her room, refusing to come out.
Merlin expressed sympathy; Andiya's body had been possessed by Ashudor, and he really couldn't help, so he feared only Shirley could pull herself out of the shadow on her own.
The elves' territory suffered heavy damage—ruined streets, collapsed houses—and while the elves busied themselves rebuilding their homes, only two guys looked idle—
Dwarf Barry walked down the street, watching the elves busy and sweating profusely, "I heard Ashudor has returned? Fortunately, its ambition wasn't fulfilled, otherwise we dwarves would also be in danger."
"You dwarves just like digging for gold every day—what danger could there be? Just hide in your caves and you'll be fine," Fairy Firi sat on Barry's head.
"My family has produced many master craftsmen, many works from my ancestors, and now they're priceless but unsellable. Ashudor once asked my great-grandfather to forge a weapon for it, but my great-grandfather refused. If Ashudor ruled the alliance, our family wouldn't have a good ending," Barry said, a little afraid.
"Oh~, then you're also a little young master of an artisan family," Fairy Firi teased.
"Of course! Not that I'm bragging—Barry blew on his own big beard, proudly saying, 'The Kerelon Light in the Elf King's hand was personally forged by my great-grandfather.'"
"How did you end up like this?" Fairy Firi didn't think Barry was a young master of a big family; he seemed more like a destitute blacksmith.
"Barry gave an embarrassed smile and said softly, 'Forging also depends on talent. After my great-grandfather passed, the talent in the family declined generation after generation; many techniques weren't passed down, so our skill is not what it used to be.'"
"Tch! What are you bragging about here?" Fairy Firi rolled her eyes.
"But Barry's face flushed and his neck thickened, unwilling to concede, he retorted, 'Even if our family's forging skill has declined, if we go out we're still first-rate forging masters; our family claims second place—who dares claim first?'"
"I believe you, haha!" Fairy Firi thought Barry was a little drunkard, and she had never seen him demonstrate his forging skills; probably most of his boasting is just hot air.
"If you get the chance, you'll definitely see our family's forging secret arts passed down through generations; legend says we can even forge divine artifacts!" Barry said unwillingly, wanting to show Firi.
Fairy Firi rolled her eyes and comforted, "I believe you, I believe—we're friends, how could I not believe you?"
Barry's mood improved a bit; he thought he hadn't even dared to mention his family's long history yet.
His great-grandfather once said their ancestor's lifetime masterpiece was the god-slaying sword Mistetin, which he personally handed over to the demon forefather.
Without their ancestor's help, how could the hero acclaimed as the ender of gods and savior of all races have achieved such greatness? Where would that demon forefather's great accomplishment come from?
"By the way, is that human kid already dead? I clearly told him not to go to such a dangerous place, yet he still wouldn't be persuaded." Fairy Firi showed a hint of regret.
"I don't think so," Barry said seriously.
"Huh? Really? Could that kid survive?" Fairy Firi wondered, thinking such a small child would definitely die in the chaos.
"Pretty much—clearly, so many elves collapsed back then, but now most are lively and vigorous; that kid probably didn't suffer anything," Barry speculated.
"Really? Then I can relax," Fairy Firi secretly let out a breath, her guilt lessening a lot, "What are you going to do next?"
Barry thought for a moment, then headed toward the palace on the Sacred Tree, "I heard the Elf King has already appeared; I'm going to ask for medicine to treat my father's waist<"
In a side chamber of the palace, Alice lay quietly on the bed, showing no discomfort, as if in a deep slumber.
Alice still hadn't woken up, but her condition was already stable; it would likely take some time before she could awaken.
After Merlin brought Alice back, he directly used the universal healing potion, the succubus's saliva.
After all, she was only punched casually by the Cave King; her injury wasn't as severe as Cain's last time, so the succubus's saliva still worked.
Besides its aphrodisiac effect, it has a remarkably effective healing action on external wounds.
However, Alice this time had clearly fainted, and there was nothing unsightly about it.
While Merlin was helping with the treatment, Alice was lethargic and showed no reaction at all.
Sylph had already come several times; after checking Alice's condition, she hurriedly left, seemingly avoiding Merlin?
She now feared this terrifyingly powerful 'human' in her heart, worried that if she suddenly suggested going out to spar, ...
After personally witnessing Merlin's power, Sylph would no longer look down on him; her heart now held only respect for the strong.
Merlin sat beside Alice's bed, using a damp towel to wipe her face, and after pulling the blanket up a bit, he finally breathed a little easier.
These past few days, Merlin has been constantly attending to Alice, not leaving her side until the situation became clear, at which point he could finally relax.
Merlin gazed at Alice's closed-eyed face, recalling the situation, and couldn't help but think—
In such a dangerous situation, she was willing to use her body to protect me; it feels a bit delicate?
This guy usually relies on me for protection, but this time it's reversed—kind of awkward.
Although Merlin's expression was complex, warmth welled up in his heart, and he couldn't resist reaching out to gently stroke Alice's cheek, starting to indulge in random thoughts—
This guy is willing to stake his life to guard me—could it be because he likes me?
If he regarded me as just an ordinary friend, there would be absolutely no need to go to such lengths.
Since he likes me, why does he put on a sour face toward me every day and boss me around?
Damn it! I can't possibly understand a woman's thoughts at all!
Merlin withdrew his hand, furrowed his brow, unable to figure out what Alice really meant, wondering if he was now basically living with her—doesn't seem like it.
He glanced at Alice sideways, and his gaze suddenly locked onto her full, tempting lips—his little heart began to flutter uncontrollably.
Merlin, possessed by some impulse, gulped down a mouthful of saliva, his old face turning red; he nervously looked around, afraid a third person might be in the soup, basically like a thief.
Eh! What am I thinking? Want to go kiss Alice?!
No no no! How could I have such a boring thought?
Could it be because I haven't been intimate with a girl in a long time, so I'm getting a bit involuntarily excited?
But it seems there's no one else here now; Alice is still asleep, so it would be fine if I sneak a kiss—she wouldn't know.
But why does it feel a bit lewd? , not good, huh?_

title: Chapter 39 — Verification
content:
Chapter 39 — Verification

Volume 22 · Chapter 39

Merlin sat beside Alice's bed, becoming hesitant and restrained, oddly feeling a bit embarrassed.
He thought to himself that, no matter how you look at it, he was an upright guy—was it okay to take advantage while Alice was asleep?
Although Merlin felt it was wrong, seeing Alice's lips made his heart itch, stirring with desire, even producing a demon-and-angel hallucination—.
Little demon: "It's no big deal! Go kiss her! Anyway, Alice won't know, and when she wakes up we can pretend nothing happened."
Little angel: "No way! That's so filthy! Merlin, you're a transmigrator, not a real demon—don't do this!"
Little demon: "What nonsense! Just kiss! Merlin, you grew up with demons since childhood—learn to do what demons do! This is 'when in Rome.'"
Little angel: "You damn liar! Alice trusts Merlin so much, yet Merlin would go against her wishes and do this? Isn't that betraying her trust?"
Little demon: "What's there to fear? Besides, it's not the first time—when Alice was drunk, didn't she ask Merlin about his willingness? Believe me, a man just goes for the kiss; Alice is into you."
Little angel: "Merlin, don't believe that jerk! Believe me, you absolutely need a girl's consent for this kind of thing!"
"Tsk! Good"
Merlin patted his own head, the demon-and-angel fantasy vanished, ending the struggle between desire and morality.
He glanced at Alice, made his decision, and desire ultimately prevailed.
I'm a demon, after all! What's there to fear? Not doing something bad would be embarrassing, and besides, I'm doing it secretly.
Merlin swallowed, propped himself up with his hands over Alice, gazing at her face, and unconsciously leaned in slowly.
Thump thump thump
Three knocks suddenly sounded, and Hilf flung the door open, bringing the busy Elf King with her.
"Mr. Merlin, His Majesty wants to have a chat with you."
The Elf King had already stabilized the situation and immediately wanted to talk with Merlin, the young Demon Lord.
As soon as they stepped inside, they saw this embarrassing scene, leaving them thunderstruck—outside charred, inside tender—and they couldn't make sense of what was happening in the room.
Merlin was leaning over Alice, his mouth close to hers, giving the impression he was about to do something nasty, and a faint sleazy scent filled the air.
If the Elf King and Hilf hadn't burst in suddenly, Merlin would have succeeded in the next second.
Ah, Merlin froze on the spot, not knowing what to do, feeling caught between a rock and a hard place, wondering how to explain sneaking a kiss on Alice.
"Cough!" the Elf King gave a light cough, breaking the silence first, and said embarrassedly, "It seems we came at a bad time—sorry to disturb you, Hilf; let's come back tonight."
"Yes! Mr. Merlin, we disturbed you." Hilf followed the Elf King as they hastily exited the room, preparing to close the door.
Even if Merlin had thick skin, his face began to flush now, feeling he was losing his dignity.
So he sprang off the bed in a flash and hurriedly called out to the Elf King and Hilf.
"Come back! It's not what you think!"
Merlin sat on the bed with a stern face, facing Hilf and the Elf King, the atmosphere in the room somewhat subtle.
"Mr. Merlin, what were you just doing?" Hilf asked, puzzled.
Merlin lifted his head, speaking solemnly, "I was just doing push-ups to exercise."
"Doing push-ups to exercise requires you to lie over Miss Alice?" Hilf fired a deadly question.
"A bead of cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead; he couldn't help but mentally retort, 'Shut up! You talk too much!'"
"And Mr. Merlin, you're acting sneaky—you wouldn't be trying to secretly kiss Miss Alice, would you?" Hilf, looking rather lewd, wore a complex expression, clearly not buying the push-up excuse, which sounded like a melodramatic lie; although she knew from the newspaper that they were a married couple, sneaking around like this was still too underhanded.
Faced with this relentless barrage of deadly questioning, Merlin inevitably grew a bit nervous, saying, "Really, it's push-ups—this is a special exercise method: doing push-ups over a beautiful girl versus over the floor, the motivation is completely different, so the answer should be obvious, right?"
Hilf furrowed her brows, about to speak but stopping, saying, "At the end of the day, you just want to do something naughty to Miss Alice in broad daylight, right?)"
"Pa—", Merlin covered his face, gritting his teeth, and said, "Don't say any more."
"Hilf, stop dwelling on this—they're a married couple, and you're being rude by probing so deeply." The Elf King suddenly interjected.
Thus Hilf obediently closed her mouth.
Merlin secretly let out a sigh of relief, inwardly grateful that the Elf King was willing to help him out of this predicament; this time, he would not deny his and Alice's "married" relationship.
"Hello, Lord Merlin, I am Sindadiel, chief of the Elf race." The Elf King nodded and smiled at Merlin.
"Hello, I am an adventurer from Rexhelm, Merlin." Merlin gave a brief self-introduction.
The Elf King was startled, thinking Merlin would frankly admit he was a Demon Lord, so he chuckled and said, "Lord Merlin, here you needn't hide yourself—we're all non-human races."
"Huh?" Merlin stared, astonished, at the Elf King and said, "You can tell I'm a demon?!"
"Of course, I knew when you drew that sword." The Elf King nodded.
"Wow!" Merlin instantly felt the relief of taking off his mask and being himself; he'd said it several times before with no one believing him, but finally there was someone who just knew he was a demon without explanation, so he relaxed, saying, "If you knew I was a demon you should have said so earlier—saved me from all this hiding and nervousness—yeah, I am a demon, we're all non-human races!"
"Merlin's a demon?!" Hilf glanced at Merlin, then at the Elf King, suspicion rising in her heart.
"Exactly, I said it before—I'm a demon, not human, and you all refused to believe me; now you believe me, right?" Merlin gave a meaningful smile.
Hilf fell silent, never imagining that this man, indistinguishable from a human, could truly be a demon! Now she would believe whatever Merlin said, after witnessing so many unbelievable things.
The Elf King could almost confirm that even if Merlin appeared human, he was absolutely a demon, though he still harbored a slight doubt.
To be safe, the Elf King still wanted to further confirm his suspicion; all it would take is a simple method to settle everything.
"Lord Merlin, may I borrow the sword at your waist for a look?"
"This," Merlin hesitated, thinking he wasn't a child anymore and needn't fear the Elf King, so he handed over the demon sword Banri Garan, saying, "Sure, go ahead and look."
The Elf King held the demon sword Banri Garan across his chest, took a deep breath, gripped the hilt, and his gaze turned serious.
Pale golden magic seeped out, concentrating in the Elf King's hand, and he began to exert all his strength to draw the blade.
The whole room trembled slightly, under the Elf King's overwhelming pressure his face turned red from strain—clearly he'd given it his all, yet the demon sword Banri Garan remained eerily unmoving.
Hilf stood behind with her mouth tightly shut, her eyes filled with disbelief, thinking in horror—
"What on earth is the origin of this sword?"
"Even the Elf King can't pull it out."
"I remember Mr. Merlin could draw it easily before."
