title: Chapter 40 — Demon Race Prophet
content:
Chapter 40 — Demon Race Prophet

Volume 22 · Chapter 40

Merlin let out a light snort and decided it wasn't worth wasting effort on. Even the first Lucifer and his own mother Vivian couldn't draw Banri Garan, and the Elf King wouldn't be acknowledged no matter what tricks he tried. If that weren't the case, how had Merlin managed to override all objections and become the master of the Demon Lord Palace? It was precisely because he had drawn Banri Garan, proving the legend that he was the legitimate heir to the First Demon Lord Palace.

In a sense, neither the first Lucifer nor Vivian truly qualified as orthodox proud lords, since they couldn't draw Banri Garan. But their overwhelming power still warranted the title of Demon Lord. The Elf King let out a long breath, his expression returning to normal as he gave up trying to draw Banri Garan, his doubts completely dissipated. He returned the katana to Merlin. "It really is a sacred artifact of the First Demon Lord Palace after all, Banri Garan. Only a recognized legitimate demon can draw it. It seems it doesn't favor me, does it?"

"You talk all fancy, yet you actually know quite a lot." Merlin took Banri Garan and fastened it at his waist.

"I haven't suffered through the tribulations of the Gods' Era, but I've personally witnessed the rise and fall of every age." The Elf King gave a self-mocking laugh, then changed the subject. "Lord Merlin, which generation of proud lords are you?"

"The third. My mother is Vivian." Merlin answered calmly, not at all worried about being endlessly harassed by those religious zealots wielding doctrine there.

Shirufu had completely lost the nerve to interject. So Merlin wasn't just any ordinary demon—he was a Demon Lord! Given such formidable power, it made perfect sense. After all, the demon race had outright rejected the Elf King's alliance proposal, showing utter disdain for associating with any non-human races.

"You're Vivian's child?!" The Elf King was secretly startled and said in surprise, "I've seen your mother. She extremely despises men. How could she bear children? Which tough guy managed to win over the Rose of the Death Swamp?"

"Ah…" Merlin became awkward, black lines sliding down his forehead. His mother, the Rose of the Death Swamp? What kind of name is that? It was the first time he'd ever heard it. "Mother does indeed despise men. I also have a younger sister. We were both born using Mother's succubus power, so there is no father."

"I see. Using succubus power to unilaterally give birth to you—Vivian would very likely use this method to continue her bloodline." The Elf King raised his head, a look of confusion on his face. "But even children born through succubus power inherit traits from their mother or the succubus. Why do you not have a single horn?"

Merlin clicked his tongue and explained dejectedly, "My sister inherited them perfectly, but I did not. My demon bloodline is very thin, with only a trace of succubus power."

"Wouldn't you be shunned among the demon race like that? As far as I know, the demon race values bloodlines highly. Even if you're Vivian's child…" The Elf King frowned, thinking a demon with such diluted blood should have been strangled to death in childhood.

"That is indeed the case. The fact that I can wander around freely now has more than a little to do with my bloodline. I was fired by the council elders and I'm no longer the Demon Lord—I'm now a free-wandering demon." Merlin shrugged.

"You drew Banri Garan and were expelled by the council? That makes no sense. Your mother was a domineering woman; how could she allow such a thing to happen?" The Elf King asked, puzzled. In his impression, Vivian was a tyrant who would never permit anyone to encroach on her interests.

"She's dead. Killed by the Holy Church's Spear Hero, O'Brien." Merlin answered. In truth, he also had doubts about his mother's death, but until he could confirm them, he would answer as though she were truly dead.

The Elf King froze, then said sympathetically, "I apologize. I didn't mean to bring it up intentionally."

"It's fine. A long time has passed." Merlin paused and said calmly, "Being expelled was probably for the best. I had already grown tired of staying in the Demon Lord Palace, spending every day playing wits with those old fossils on the council was exhausting."

"Expelling you is absolutely a tremendous loss to the demon race. You are extraordinary." The Elf King paused and said seriously, "Besides your mother Vivian, I also personally saw the first Lucifer. That was before the Holy War began. He was the greatest swordsman I have ever seen in my life. Perhaps your swordsmanship cannot match his, but he could not draw Banri Garan, while you can. This alone proves you are extraordinary. You are the second demon, after that Demon Prophet, to receive Banri Garan's recognition."

"The Demon Prophet? Oh." Merlin bowed his head and thought hard. There didn't seem to be much information about this person—even in demon race documents, he was merely brushed over. But Merlin knew the Blood Pool seal beneath the Demon Lord Palace was created by this Prophet, and all the ancestors of the demon race were sealed below it. "I was only Demon Lord for a century, so I don't know much about him."

The Elf King wore a patriarchal smile. "I don't know much about this great man either, but I once heard about him from Father God Corelon. He was somewhat similar to you—both wearing human faces yet calling themselves demons, leading the entire demon race to be the first to rebel against the suppression of the Old Gods' era. He cut down the World Tree and brought about the twilight of those evil gods. He is a world-overturning hero, and Banri Garan was one of his former swords."

Merlin looked down at his Banri Garan. He had rarely delved deeply into the origin of this blade, and he never would have guessed it was once the佩刀 of the Demon Prophet.

No wonder everyone was shocked when he drew Banri Garan. It turned out the reaction had little to do with him and was almost entirely due to the profound influence of that ancient Demon Prophet!

Wait! A human who calls himself a demon? Hadn't he heard something like that at Old John's house in GaoWei City?

The human who ended the gods by calling himself a demon became the hero who saved the world—in the end, he was the same person as the Demon Prophet!

But how did the demon race, a族群 that once produced a hero, end up looking like rats crossing the street, with everyone shouting to beat them? He had to admire the Holy Church's brainwashing through propaganda.

Merlin felt deeply within his heart, growing ever more curious about this Demon Prophet. Yet he had grown up in the demon race and had never heard much about this Prophet, nor had Vivian ever mentioned him.

"How is Miss Alice doing?" The Elf King suddenly asked.

"There's no major issue now. She simply hasn't woken up. I've already healed her with succubus saliva." Merlin frowned and answered.

"Succubus saliva?" The Elf King's expression turned peculiar.

"Is there a problem with that?" Merlin was confused, noticing the Elf King didn't seem to approve.

"Succubus saliva does have healing properties for the opposite sex, but only for superficial wounds at most. It has little effect on serious injuries, and the most awkward part—" The Elf King pursed his lips and added, "using it too much causes addiction."

"Huh?!" Merlin was genuinely stunned, his expression becoming rather unnatural. He thought of another person—

Succubus saliva causes the opposite sex to become addicted!

How many times had he spit saliva on that female knight named Messfield?!

Was she… right now… T_T...

title: Chapter 41 — Peering at Fate
content:
Chapter 41 — Peering at Fate

Volume 22 · Chapter 41

Merlin lowered his head and fell into contemplation, feeling like he had done something terrible.

Was Mesfield's intense hatred toward him due to addiction?

Merlin realized he could no longer look directly at that female knight. It seemed demonic saliva shouldn't be used carelessly either.

"Alice-san has taken a direct attack from the Rock-Cave King. Aside from physical damage, her consciousness must have also suffered some damage. Simple treatment will be very slow." The Elf King turned to Sylph and said, "Sylph, bring the medicine."

"Yes." Sylph took out a small green potion from the bag at her waist and carefully handed it to the Elf King.

"What's this?" Merlin asked with confusion.

"This is a spirit medicine our clan prepared. It can heal injuries—even damage to consciousness will be repaired quickly. Just now, the son of dwarf master Balin came to ask for medicine. There's some left here, enough to let Alice-san wake up quickly." The Elf King removed the cork and dripped two drops onto Alice's forehead, where they quickly dissolved.

"Oh~" Merlin sniffed carefully. A refreshing scent filled the air, making him feel alert. It must be a precious magic potion.

The Elf King nodded satisfactorily and screwed the cap back on. "Fortunately, the Rock-Cave King was controlled by Axious and didn't kill her outright. Alice-san's injuries aren't serious; otherwise, the consequences would have been severe."

"That's good. If that stone person had hurt Alice, I would have dismantled it." Merlin sighed in relief.

The Elf King looked strange, unable to understand why Merlin, the third monarch, was together with a human.

But this was clearly Merlin's privacy, and the Elf King didn't pry further, showing discretion.

"Is Alice-san a member of the Holy Church of Light?"

"Once." Merlin nodded, embarrassed. "She was the Hero who hunted me."

The Elf King looked peculiar. Even though it had lived for a long time and was a living fossil of history, this was the first time it had seen such a situation.

Those who can become Heroes are deadly enemies of demons—mortal foes. Yet these two before it overturned its impression completely.

Moreover, according to its prophecy, these two were mutually in love—a pair that could enter the Elf Clan's secret realm. This was even more scandalous!

The Elf King lowered its head, wondering how these two completely opposite-faction guys had gotten together? Besides, didn't the demon race prohibit love across species?

"What's wrong?" Merlin noticed the Elf King's strange reaction.

"Clearing throat! N-nothing." The Elf King coughed twice to hide its embarrassment and continued, "As I suspected, you are the vague figures I saw in my dream. Merlin-sama comes from the demon land of darkness and fire, and Alice-san is the one bathed in divine light."

"You have the power to foresee the future?" Merlin was slightly surprised. He had never met anyone who could see the future!

"Correct, but what I can see is very limited and vague. I can only guess the future based on vague content." The Elf King paused and continued, "What I have foreseen will definitely happen. Wen Bazhi..."

"So creepy?" Merlin felt somewhat surprised. Usually, even when meeting guys who claimed to foresee the future, most were just frauds making a living. But the Elf King taking it so seriously was the first time.

"I once saw in a dream that the different races were engulfed in raging fire and all perished. All I could do was try every means to avoid this fate." The Elf King said seriously.

Merlin was startled and asked in confusion, "You said the prophecy would definitely happen, right? Obviously it can't be avoided?"

"Indeed unavoidable, but one cannot stop fighting. Every revelation of the future I hold in awe." The Elf King looked at Merlin and smiled. "If you know you're doomed and don't try to struggle, what's the difference between you and a creature raised in a pigsty? Even if the result cannot change, I can make the end of the races in the prophecy come sooner. This is also why Father God Coreron chose me instead of Axious to become the Elf King."

Merlin fell silent. Honestly, he somewhat admired this old Elf King, but he wasn't fond of the claim that prophecies would definitely happen, nor did he believe in it. It was like the blind fortune-tellers at the market—everyone just went for psychological comfort.

"Merlin-sama, actually I came to see you today not to talk about those things, but to request help from both of you." The Elf King's gaze became earnest.

"Oh? Go ahead." Merlin pulled over a chair and sat down. "Speak."

"Initially, to prevent the different races from being swallowed by humans, I chose to use the Star-Splitting Cannon to split the continent. But something unexpected happened—the United Kingdom's continent floated above a huge underwater abyss, ready to sink into the sea at any moment." The Elf King lowered its head and simply stated the kingdom's greatest threat. "To prevent the worst case, I constantly fought the underwater abyss with my own power for tens of thousands of years. Now my strength has declined severely; I probably can't hold out much longer. Only you two, bringing my blood into the secret realm and activating the divine artifact of Father God Coreron, can calm this threat."

"Why must it be us? We're not elves—" Merlin frowned.

"You are the people from the prophecy. That's why I trust you unconditionally." The Elf King's gaze was sincere as it silently lowered its head and spoke in a humble tone. "Merlin-sama, you are also a non-human race. If we perish, that's not something the demon race would want to see, right? If you fail in your battle against humans, this place will become the demon race's next homeland. Please help us."

Sylph's eyes flashed with complex emotions. In its impression, the Elf King had never bowed to anyone before. This was the first time, but it understood the Elf King's willingness to lower its姿态, as this concerned the survival of the entire kingdom.

"Sounding nice doesn't work. Saying this to me, a wandering demon, is useless. I'm an adventurer now; we only recognize rewards." Merlin rubbed his fingers, crazily hinting, "If I can't fleece Sherry, I'll fleece her dad instead."

The Elf King was stunned, then relieved. "I see. In our clan's secret realm, there are some treasures. Besides the only divine artifact, I can let you and Alice-san each pick one as a thank-you gift."

Merlin's expression moved. Thinking that since the Elf Clan had passed down treasures for so long, there must be plenty of good items. Picking one randomly would probably be priceless.

"Sounds pretty good."

Merlin sent the Elf King and Sylph out the door. He had already promised that after Alice woke up, he would go to the Elf Clan's secret realm.

However, Merlin was quite interested in the Elf King's precognitive ability and couldn't help but say as he was leaving:

"Your prophecy is really that powerful? Then take a look at me, can you see anything?"

"Merlin-sama, such trivial matters don't require using your Highness's precognitive power. Please don't do this." Sylph frowned, feeling Merlin was impolite.

"No problem. Since Merlin-sama is in the mood, I can take a look then."

The Elf King interrupted Sylph's protest with a gentle attitude and did not refuse Merlin's rude action.

Actually, it was also curious itself, especially after witnessing Merlin crush the Elf Clan's genius Axious.

Such a powerful and young demon lord—what would the future look like? Even a little bit would make one curious.

The Elf King drew two fingers from deep within and wiped them on Merlin's forehead, its consciousness diving into the deepest part of his spirit, beginning to peer into his fate.

What exactly was Merlin's future?

No one knew.

But at this moment, the Elf King's face was ugly, its eyebrows tightly furrowed on its forehead.

title: Chapter 42 — Unknown Fate (Extra)
content:
Chapter 42 — Unknown Fate (Extra)

Volume 22 · Chapter 42

Mist, a fog where you can't see your own fingers.
There was no light, before me was a blank white world.
The air was filled with an oppressive pressure, making breathing difficult.
Heaven and earth overturned, the laws changed drastically—
Ding ding ding, crisp sounds broke the silence of the entire fog world.
The katana fell to the ground, its light dimmed, as if mourning the loss of its master.
Merlin, his body suddenly collapsed, his eyes empty and lifeless, not a trace of spirit flickered.
His lifeless body lay motionless, like a soulless piece of wood.
From afar came mournful cries, continuously calling Merlin's name, the piercing voice moving one's heart.
In this white world, suddenly a huge pair of eyes lit up, emitting a dangerous purple light.
The bloodthirsty gaze rolled about, fixed on Merlin's fallen body, revealing delight; those narrow pupils resembled a cunning snake, or perhaps a ferocious dragon?<
The Elf King suddenly opened his eyes, withdrew his hand, lowered his head, his expression wanting to speak but stopping.
All the hints were already obvious; the result was—
Merlin had died, he would die someday in the future.
The fallen katana must have been destroyed in battle, so he surely faced a powerful foe!
But Merlin's strength was already formidable—just who could kill him?
Anyone capable of such a feat would likely be stronger than Merlin!z
My prophecy will surely come true, perhaps delayed a bit, but it will eventually arrive.
The Elf King unknowingly broke into a cold sweat on his forehead, unsure how to tell Merlin his prophecy.

“What’s wrong?” Merlin frowned, looking at the Elf King’s tense expression.
The Elf King lifted his head and glanced at Merlin, thinking that if he told him he would someday be killed, it might put psychological pressure on him.
After much hesitation, to let Merlin continue living without pressure, without suspicion, the Elf King decided to conceal his prophecy.
“Nothing? You’re special, I couldn’t see anything at all.
“? It seems your prophecy isn’t all‑powerful. Ah, Merlin twisted the corner of his mouth, wondering if it’s because I’m a transmigrator, too special, so the Elf King can’t see my future? Indeed, prophecies that are certain to come true are just exaggerations, right?
“Huh?” Hilf showed an incomprehending expression, thinking the Elf King can’t see the future of a person? Impossible, this has never happened before.
The Elf King didn’t explain further. He nodded at Merlin.
“Lord Merlin, “Wishing you a good night.” =

Night fell, warm wind lifting the curtains.
In the southernmost kingdom, spring lingered all year; even here, everything was warm.
Merlin sat in a chair, his head drooping, breathing evenly, as if already asleep.
“

The unconscious Alice let out a few soft groans, furrowed her brows and opened her eyes.
Looking at the relatively unfamiliar ceiling, she felt a bit uneasy, and hastily endured the body‑wide ache as she sat up on the bed—
Where am I? Since I’m not seriously injured, things have already settled down.
Wah! Merlin! Has this guy recovered? The antidote Senior Se Xi gave has all been drunk!
Alice saw Merlin slumped on the chair beside the bed, his head drooping, and felt a bit surprised.
She had thought Merlin was like a child, never expecting that during her coma he had already recovered.
She didn’t know how long had passed; seeing Merlin’s somewhat weary appearance, could it be because he was taking care of me?
How strange, this guy willingly takes care of me? Hard to imagine.
Alice’s face turned slightly red as she let her mind wander, thinking that Merlin not throwing her out was already good, and he even attentively looked after her, which surprised her.
Yet Alice still felt waves of warmth in her heart, so she quietly went barefoot, picked up her coat, and gently draped it over Merlin—
Really, if you’re tired, why not rest a bit? Just sit in the chair and fall asleep.
Alice bent over, intrigued, secretly watching Merlin sleep; for a moment she found it quite interesting, rarely having the chance to quietly stare at him.
Heh heh, this guy is unusually quiet when asleep, much more likable than his usual nose‑in‑the‑air demeanor~
The room was empty of people, the atmosphere somewhat private, easily prompting mischievous thoughts; even Alice’s gaze toward Merlin had shifted a little.

Alice straightened her back, warily looking around—just like Merlin’s earlier demeanor—
Is it just me and Merlin in this room? Sneaking a kiss on Merlin seems fine; I won’t be caught—
I definitely don’t have any thoughts of taking advantage; I merely—just want to repay Merlin for his careful care these past few days!
After all, I dislike owing people; I absolutely won’t have any rogue thoughts!
Huh! Right!
Alice frenziedly gave herself a pep talk, seemingly finding a justified reason.

Thus Alice quietly bent down, secretly gazing at Merlin’s side profile, then gently kissed his cheek.
Ding ling ling
The evening breeze softly blew in, bringing pleasant wind chime sounds; the room was silent, as if isolated from the world.
Alice hurriedly lowered her head, her face reddening at a visible speed, like a ripe red apple—
What am I doing? This is no different from those casual girls— !
No way, absolutely not! It’s all Merlin’s fault for being so clueless!
I clearly care about him so much, yet he gives no response at all.
Alice grew angrier and angrier, and with lightning speed she darted back into the blanket, wrapping herself up like a zongzi.
“Stupid.”

Hearing the murmurs of complaint, Merlin slowly woke up, instantly furrowing his brow; what came into view was Alice wrapped in the blanket, like a little angry package muttering something.
Merlin was about to speak, but noticed he was covered with a coat—needless to say, it was Alice who had covered him—and a strange feeling welled up in his heart.
“Are you awake? Alice
“Eh, Alice stared wide‑eyed; her complaining voice cut off, but she still replied angrily, “I was already awake, you woke me
“Huh?” Merlin sensed Alice’s tone was a bit unhappy, thinking he hadn’t provoked her, so he asked without much thought, “Didn’t wake you, how are you feeling? Anywhere still uncomfortable?
“No, I’m fine. Alice, wrapped in the blanket, had her back to Merlin, her pretty face—red, realizing this was Merlin caring for her.
“But, I can finally rest easy.” Merlin breathed a sigh of relief, then felt the cool saliva left by Alice on his face, touched his cheek, “Why is my face all wet and sticky?
“!!!” Alice’s eyes widened, guilty as a thief, her whole body shivered, her face instantly flushed, as if steaming.
Merlin’s brow twitched, feeling the saliva on his face, as if he’d discovered something?
“It’s nothing, I’m fine!” Alice nervously jumped ahead of Merlin to rebut, “No silver three hundred li here” as she defended herself—
“That. That must be your own saliva!
“Don’t suspect me! I
“I would never indulge in sleeping and secretly kissing you! Hmph~⊥”

title: Chapter 43 — The Moment to Test True Feelings
content:
Chapter 43 — The Moment to Test True Feelings

Volume 22 · Chapter 43

"You're so nervous." Merlin frowned and asked in confusion.

"It's just your imagination!" Alice retorted with a blush.

Merlin suspiciously wiped the dampness off his face, wondering if he had been drooling while sleeping. It was so strange—

"You seem to be fine. You were too reckless. Don't do that next time. You need to know that no matter how lucky you are—"

Alice was taken aback for a moment. Hearing Merlin's lecturing tone, she felt annoyed inside, so she turned over and sat up. "What did you say? I was—"

"Ah?" Alice obediently listened to his advice. "I told you to stay by my side, but you kept running around everywhere. If you had just listened, there wouldn't have been so many dangerous situations!"

Merlin nervously broke out in a cold sweat and explained, "I was kidnapped. Who knew someone would try to take advantage when I just went to the restroom?"

Alice glared at Merlin angrily and said in a serious tone, "You need to listen to me! Whatever you want to do, you should discuss it with me first. Do you understand?"

"Tch!" Merlin clicked his tongue in dissatisfaction, flexed his fingers, and said meaningfully, "Cut it out a little, Alice. Do you think you can keep riding on my head? Don't forget you're just my little follower."

"Hmph, don't flatter yourself. I only happened to drink the Time Potion and turn into a kid—that doesn't mean you get to dominate me forever. Occasionally let me have my fun, that's enough." Alice's face turned red and then pale. She opened her mouth as if to say something, then stopped.

Merlin frowned.

"Just what?"

"Idiot! Might as well have died earlier!" Alice angrily turned her back to Merlin and lay down, wrapping herself up like a burrito again.

"Idiot! Big—"

"Uh!" Merlin furrowed his brows, his face darkening, the veins on his forehead pulsing faintly.

Had he provoked this grandma again? Why did every few sentences turn into her yelling at him? This anger was completely baffling!

He felt increasingly unable to understand women's thoughts, so he couldn't help but poke Alice's back with his finger.

"Hey, are you really angry? Are you a pufferfish? One touch and you explode!"

Alice hugged the pillow and didn't say a word, expressing her displeasure through a snort. "Hmph~!"

The current Alice was full of thorns, hard to handle. "Then why are you angry? Is it just because I didn't listen to your words?"

Alice bit her lip, blushing, and whispered softly, "You won't discuss anything with me. It makes me feel like I'm useless."

"Just—"

Merlin's old face turned red, his heart racing. "I see... I wouldn't harm you, yet you keep avoiding me. Clearly, apart from me, no one would be willing to protect you when you're weak."

"I've never—when danger strikes, I'm not watching over you like a prisoner." Alice was facing away from Merlin, so he couldn't see her expression. She continued her own complaints. Merlin felt a bit embarrassed and couldn't bring himself to refute, so he said softly, "That's enough. I was wrong. I apologize. I know—since I turned into a child, I've been causing you nothing but trouble. You've worked hard."

"Hmph, you scared me this time." Merlin awkwardly scratched his cheek and said softly, "When the danger came, you charged over without hesitation. I should thank you."

"Don't mention it." Alice interrupted with a blush, speaking in a reluctant tone, "Any ordinary person would have done the same. Don't misunderstand that I did it only for you or anything."

"Uh..." Merlin's expression grew complicated. Thinking carefully about Alice's personality, she really might have done something like that.

Alice pursed her delicate brows, thinking that she had only said it half-heartedly because she couldn't bring herself to say it properly, yet Merlin actually believed it? Ugh, she was so frustrated!

"Get some rest. Tomorrow we'll go to the elves' secret realm. The Elf King came to ask for our help today." Merlin walked over to Alice's side and pulled the blanket for her.

"The elves' secret realm?" Alice asked in confusion.

"The burial place of the Elven God Corelon. There shouldn't be any dangers." Merlin turned to go back to his room, waving his hand, "If anything comes up, come find me. I'll rest first."

Alice saw Merlin about to leave and her mood instantly dropped. She covered half her flushed face with the blanket. "Will you stay with me? Hurry up and roll over here."

"I don't need anyone staying with me," Merlin gritted his teeth in response, turned, and walked away. But suddenly his hand was grabbed—gripped extremely tightly—from inside the blanket.

"What are you doing?"

Alice bit into the blanket pitifully, holding onto Merlin tightly and refusing to let him leave, saying one thing while meaning another: "I definitely don't need you to stay!"

"Hmph..." Merlin furrowed his brows, black lines sliding down his forehead. What was she thinking? What exactly was going on in that head of yours?

The next day, the Elf King led Merlin and Alice toward the elves' sacred ground. The corridor was exceptionally long, and unknown gems were glowing, illuminating the passage like daylight.

"The long resting place of the Elf King Corelon is built at the very top of the Holy Tree. We still need some assistance to get up there," the Elf King said.

"After you enter the secret realm, don't worry about dangers. Our elf race isn't vicious enough to set various life-taking traps. Being able to see Corelon's remains is destiny. You only need to pour my blood on Corelon's remains, and the artifact's power will be triggered. At that point, the United Kingdom will no longer be threatened by the abyss below the sea. You haven't forgotten about pouring my blood on Corelon's remains, have you?" Merlin showed a merchant-like expression.

"Fulfill our promise," the Elf King smiled and looked back at Merlin. "After you complete the mission, you can choose two treasures from inside."

"Hah, of course. Aside from the artifact, there are still some good items inside. I think you can put them to use." Merlin rubbed his hands together, growing eager.

"Hey hey, Your Majesty the Elf King, why do we have to be the ones to enter the secret realm?" Alice was very puzzled about this.

The Elf King paused, adding, "The prophecy says—"

"You are the chosen ones foretold in the prophecy. Only two people who love each other can make that mysterious giant stone disappear."

Merlin: "Ah?"

Alice: *glanced sideways*

The atmosphere became extraordinarily awkward. Both of them simultaneously thought—

What the hell is this situation?!

Only two people who love each other?!

Does that mean him or—

title: Chapter 44 — The Sole Survivor (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 44 — The Sole Survivor (Bonus)

Volume 22 · Chapter 44

"Wait a moment!" Merlin couldn't help but interrupt the Elf King, saying in astonishment, "We also need the two to be in love? You didn't tell me about this condition yesterday!"

"What's the problem with that? It's not too late to say it now," the Elf King frowned slightly, not knowing what Merlin was bothered by.

Merlin licked his slightly dry lips. "That's a completely different matter!"

"Yes, Your Majesty, Elf King. Are you misunderstanding us?" Alice couldn't help but interject.

"Misunderstanding? What misunderstanding?" the Elf King asked with confusion.

"How did you conclude?" Alice looked at Merlin awkwardly, lowered her voice, and said, "That we are in love? We're not what you think."

The Elf King chuckled dryly, saying with deep meaning, "Do I need to ascertain that? To collapse that giant rock, it definitely requires the blood of two powerful, loving couples."

"After all, what the hell is that mysterious stone?" Merlin couldn't help but ask, frowning.

"I don't know either. On a certain day long ago, it suddenly fell from the sky, striking the barrier of the secret realm. Since then, the barrier has been in chaos. Even to enter the secret realm, I must move that mysterious giant stone. As for my situation, you know a little something." The Elf King recalled his late wife, and his expression turned sorrowful.

Alice felt deep sympathy, but still couldn't help explaining, "But we are not a loving couple."

"Ah?" The Elf King was suddenly stunned, then laughed, "This doesn't count as being in love? What counts as being in love? Alice-san is willing to use her body to protect Lord Merlin, and Lord Merlin is willing to get furious for you. This isn't...!"

Before the Elf King could speak, Merlin and Alice pushed him against the wall, a broadsword and a rapier simultaneously pressed against his neck, and his mouth was tightly covered by both of them.

Alice: "Please don't talk nonsense. It's completely not like that."

Merlin: "My sword is fast. You watch your tongue."

Cold sweat seeped from the Elf King's forehead. Scared by their murderous expressions, he trembled and thought:

What did I say wrong?

Why do they look like they want to silence us forever?

At the end of the corridor, Sylph had been waiting early, ready to see if she could help with anything.

In the distance were the massive branches of the Sacred Tree. Up close like this, they still looked magnificent and imposing.

The top of the tree couldn't be seen at all; it had pierced through the clouds, reaching an unknown height.

Seeing the three of them arrive, Sylph went to meet them, but seeing the Elf King's unpleasant expression and his frightened look, she asked, "Your Majesty, what's wrong?"

"Clearing his throat!" The Elf King waved his hand, forcing a smile. "Nothing, just feeling a bit unwell."

"Please, Your Majesty, make sure to rest." Sylph said worriedly, looking at the recovered Alice. "Alice-san, how is your body? You've been unconscious for three or four days."

"Don't worry, I'm completely fine. I feel great now." Alice said, looking spirited.

"That's good. The secret realm has strength requirements for entrants, so be careful." Sylph nodded, then looked at Merlin with a strange expression and asked, "Last night, you didn't do anything strange to Alice-san, did you?"

"Ah?" Merlin was like a mouse with its tail stepped on, nearly jumping in place, so he quickly scratched his head and acted innocent. "What are you talking about? I completely don't understand, haha."

"Hmm?" Alice looked at Merlin confusedly, completely unaware of what they were talking about.

"The secret realm is on the other side of the Sacred Tree." The Elf King looked up, gazing at the branches sweeping through the clouds. "There are powerful turbulent currents above; flying up would easily get swept away. So we need a friend's help. It can take us up there."

"Who?" Merlin wondered in his heart. The Elf race's secret realm—even the Elf King wanted to go and found it so difficult?

That wasn't the case. Rather, the Elf King's strength had regressed severely, making it difficult for him to deal with the turbulent currents at high altitudes.

Moreover, the stored magical power of Corelon Light had been depleted in the battle against Axiodier, making it hard to activate again.

So it was only natural that the Elf King found it extremely difficult to even approach the secret realm and needed to ask for help.

Should be arriving soon...

No sooner had the Elf King finished speaking than deep, rumbling roars echoed from above, and fierce gusts began to sweep the ground.

A towering figure comparable to a mountain suddenly descended from the sky, crashing down before everyone, stirring up flying sand and stones.

Cave King slowly raised his head, supporting his body with his remaining single arm, and looked down at the several people below.

"Elf King, after receiving your message, I came running through the night. Looks like I'm not late, right?"

"Hard work, my friend," the Elf King smiled, deliberately bringing Cave King here.

However, the reactions of the latter two were completely different from the Elf King's; they both immediately became alert.

Merlin pressed his hand down on the great sword at his waist, and Alice also gripped the hilt of her rapier, as if they were about to fight at any moment.

"Please calm down, both of you. Cave King is not an enemy; it came to help us." the Elf King explained.

Alice frowned, recalling what had happened earlier, feeling that this giant was not to be provoked.

"Before, it didn't mean to hurt you; it was corrupted by Axiodier and its spirit was controlled. It wasn't deliberately targeting you." The Elf King paused and continued, "Cave King is a gentle creature that hates fighting most; its only hobby is sleeping."

"Is that so..." Merlin relaxed slightly, temporarily letting his guard down.

"Regarding what happened before, I'm sorry. I didn't want to hurt you. Even though you're humans, I have no hostility toward any creature." Cave King paused, then actively bent down, placing his huge palm on the ground. "To express my sincerity, please come up. I'll take you to the top of the Sacred Tree."

Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh—fierce wind whipped past their ears.

Don't let Cave King's massive stature fool you; it moved with surprising agility, relying on its remaining single arm to climb the majestic Sacred Tree, constantly approaching the summit.

Several people stood on Cave King's shoulders, grabbing the protruding rocks around them to avoid falling accidentally.

"This guy moves pretty fast," Merlin remarked.

"Not all Rock Tribe members are slow. They are spirits of the earth and can run just as fast. Moreover, Cave King is the elite among them. The fight was unconscious, so it couldn't show its true strength," the Elf King evaluated.

"Oh?" Merlin turned to look at Cave King, seeing only its huge ears. "You said its only hobby was sleeping? How did a creature like this become the chief of its tribe?"

"The Rock Tribe has only it left alive, so it is the chief." the Elf King said meaningfully.

"? ? ?" Merlin's mind was full of question marks, but the Elf King's answer was logical and irrefutable—

The only survivor of the entire tribe, so is it the King of Nine...?

It's just like a joke—pulling the tallest out of a group of dwarves.

(∞ Kiss)

title: Chapter 45 — Everyone Has Their Own Ulterior Motives
content:
Chapter 45 — Everyone Has Their Own Ulterior Motives

Volume 22 · Chapter 45

Elf King seemingly saw the doubt in Merlin's eyes and explained, "The Cave King being able to become the sole survivor is exactly a symbol of great strength; don't misunderstand, the truly weak would have been eliminated long ago." "Is... is that so?" Merlin said with a complex expression, thinking that because he is the sole survivor of the clan, he could become leader, which seems like a joke no matter how you look at it. "No, compared to Lord Merlin, I am still far behind... The Cave King keeps climbing toward the top of the Holy Tree, and he doesn't forget to communicate with a few people, 'I heard the Elf King say you are the third-generation monarch of the demon race, possessing such strength at such a young age; indeed, the waves behind push forward the waves, we old folks, since being cut off from the human world, have fallen further behind the times.'" "That's that, you overpraise me... Merlin replied a bit embarrassed." "...." Alice glanced at Merlin, thinking that after coming to the United Kingdom, this guy seems even more at ease. "My proudest thing is my extremely hard body; frankly speaking, only a very few strong warriors can harm me, and you are one of them." The Cave King paused, then continued, "When I learned that I lost my arm in our confrontation, I was utterly incredulous; it seems the demon race had a reason for not joining the alliance with other races—you don't need to form alliances to deal with various dangers." Merlin remained silent, thinking the reason the demon race doesn't ally isn't because they're too strong, but because of the blood pool seal in the Demon Lord Palace; if this hidden danger isn't cleared, demons can never leave their homeland. "I won't repair my broken arm; it will become a memorial of my defeat to the third-generation demon monarch, something worth remembering." The Cave King muttered. Elf King understood and smiled faintly, lowering his voice to Merlin, "My old friend here is very pleased; so far, hardly anyone could injure his body, and he thinks you are a worthy opponent." "This... Merlin scratched his head, thinking this big guy, is he a martial arts enthusiast?" After an unknown amount of time, the Cave King finally reached the very top of the Holy Tree. At that moment, a huge altar came into view, surrounded by surging seas of clouds, with distant sunlight shining down in brilliant rays. The Cave King bent down, placed the few people down with his hands, and said, "Everyone, we have arrived." After Merlin and Alice got down and looked around, they felt everything before them was quite strange, basically there was no elf realm secret, just emptiness. Only that abrupt huge stone stood in the center of the altar, seeming out of place compared to the surroundings. The stone was entirely white and translucent, faintly glowing, with red threads like veins continuously pulsing on its surface. "Is this... the stone you mentioned?" Alice asked doubtfully. "Yes." The Elf King stepped forward, nodded, and said, "It's this stone that suddenly fell from the sky, disrupting the secret realm's barrier; besides the blood of two lovers, nothing else can move it even a bit. If you want to enter the secret realm smoothly, this stone is the biggest obstacle." "Maybe we should...?" Alice's face turned red, wanting to speak but hesitating. "Or... Merlin stepped forward, eager to try, 'Let's see if we can split it?'" "Please stop! Merlin first..." Hilf was genuinely startled, hurriedly stopping him, "The secret realm is our clan's important heritage; if you lose control and damage it, the loss would be irrecoverable for us." "Not allowing a direct split... really troublesome." Merlin furrowed his brows; he indeed lacked confidence that he could draw his sword without damaging the secret realm—on the ship he only drew his sword out of necessity, and now the situation demands even more caution. "Since you're both here, why not give it a try?" The Elf King looked at Merlin and Alice, "You are the people foretold in my prophecy; logically, moving this huge stone should pose no problem—let's see the result with a try." The two instinctively glanced at each other, then simultaneously looked away, their eyes darting as they stood before the stone, clearly feeling guilty. "Maybe we should just forget it?" Alice said, her cheeks flushed with two red spots, fearing her secret crush on Merlin would be exposed. "...Yeah! This stone doesn't look strange at all; insisting on using the blood of two lovers to move it is utterly ridiculous!" Merlin lowered his head nervously, feeling guilty. The Elf King watched their resistance, growing more puzzled, "Do you two have some unspeakable difficulty? Why are you so resistant to this stone? Could there be a secret you don't want to expose?" "I... I really have no secret..." Alice said, blushing, fidgeting with her two fingers. "Me too... I have no secret." Merlin said he had no secret, but his eyes darted nervously. "Then please both put your blood on the stone; if you are the foretold ones, you will surely be able to move it." The Elf King gradually lost patience. "After all, why can a single stone judge whether we are in love? That's too fake." Merlin frowned. "Exactly, we..." Alice glanced at Merlin, her voice getting softer, "It's impossible for us to love each other; clearly it's just me..." "Mr. Merlin, Miss Alice, what are you hesitating about?" Hilf couldn't hold back, speaking directly, "Are you afraid this stone will reveal your inner feelings? If you dare not try, then there must be disloyalty toward the other in your hearts!" Upon hearing this, the two instinctively glanced at each other, unable to stop themselves from beginning to suspect each other. Alice: Merlin's resistance to this stone—could it be because he's fickle? Damn it, I care so much! Merlin: Yeah, why is Alice such a coward? Could she be hiding some little secret? Damn it, I really want to know! "Cough!" Alice coughed lightly, pretending to be relaxed, "Trying might be okay, Merlin." "I have no problem at all, let's go." Merlin forced a stiff smile, pondering various possibilities. Black lines like a waterfall slid down the Elf King's forehead; he thought that mentioning disloyalty made him want to try, and indeed, between intimate couples, such things are hard to tolerate. Seeing Merlin and Alice both draw their weapons, cut their fingers, and press their hands simultaneously onto the mysterious stone, remaining silent for a full three seconds, yet nothing happened. "Hahaha, I said we couldn't do it! Indeed it's just a joke!" Merlin laughed bitterly, thinking Alice truly dislikes me—I already knew that. "Yes... yes! No matter how we think, we're impossible..." Alice forced a smile, thinking Merlin never liked her at all; it was all her own wishful thinking. But the next second, a series of cracking sounds rang out! The mysterious giant stone emitted bursts of white light, then suddenly shattered and collapsed— Merlin: Alice: =

title: Chapter 46 — Hieroglyphs (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 46 — Hieroglyphs (Extra Chapter)

Volume 22 · Chapter 46

The mysterious boulder suddenly developed fine cracks upon contact with Merlin and Alice's blood!
It then shattered into countless fragments, crashing down with a clatter!
This mysterious stone that had restrained the elf race for countless ages turned out to be as fragile as tofu under their blood!
Before everyone's eyes, a golden radiance shot up into the sky, as if a golden gate had been constructed—
The secret realm of the Elf God Koreuron appeared, hovering in midair like a magnificent mirage in a desert sea!
Merlin and Alice stared wide-eyed at everything before them—not frightened, but feeling immensely embarrassed at the confirmation of the prophecy, their minds instantly going blank.
...The elves started joking, inopportunely delivering a sharp retort: "Sure enough, I didn't misjudge; you two are exactly the ones foretold, without a doubt—this stone was shattered by the power of your love!"
"Mr. Merlin, Miss Alice, you needn't beat around the bush; the result is already obvious." Hiluf added another jab.
The two suddenly came to their senses, unable to help but glance at each other—eyes wide with shock, as if they'd discovered an earth-shattering secret.
"Well..." Merlin's gaze was complex; he unconsciously licked his dry lips, "You... when did it start?"
"Um!"
Alice's face flushed red; she lowered her head in panic, "No no no! Obviously it's you..."
"I..." Merlin swore he had never been this nervous before, feeling as if his last fig leaf had been ripped away, leaving him completely exposed in the street.
The atmosphere suddenly became excruciatingly awkward, as if a window paper had been poked through, leaving both of them feeling suffocated.
The two lowered their heads in silence, their thoughts in turmoil, completely unsure what to say.
The Elf King furrowed his brow, full of question marks, wondering what kind of reaction this was—weren't they a married couple? Why did they act like they'd just started dating?
Hiluf, quick-hearted, fanned the flames from the side, saying, "When such deep emotions surface, one should embrace and kiss to let the feelings further sublimate."
"Um!" Alice trembled nervously, her mind filled with thoughts of kissing, very worried about what to do next—she had no experience! Moreover, she had no idea what attitude Merlin, as a demon, held toward human girls; would he dislike her?
Merlin's expression kept shifting, silently cursing Hiluf for meddling.
If Alice knew he liked her, how would they live under the same roof?
Wasn't this a sign of harboring ulterior motives, having long schemed against Alice?
After all, where did this broken stone even come from? Even the Elf King doesn't know—on what basis could it possibly reveal their thoughts?!
Merlin couldn't help but suspect the mysterious stone, even beginning to think the Elf King was playing him.
"Well... even if this stone shatters, it can't prove—"
"!!!" Alice lifted her head, as if grasping a lifeline, quickly agreeing, "Exactly! A mere stone reading our hearts? That's absurd, utterly impossible!"
"Right, this stone can't read minds—how could it know what we're thinking? I guess... we just happened to coincide?" Merlin voiced his doubts repeatedly.
"Exactly!" Alice nodded repeatedly, agreeing, "Letting a stone decide our relationship is ridiculous!"
"Your Majesty Elf King, your joke is in poor taste; we won't fall for it!" Merlin turned back, smugly.
"???" The Elf King's expression showed a hint of despair, letting out a helpless cry in his heart: What are you two hiding?!
Both secretly let out a sigh of relief, each harboring similar thoughts—
Merlin: Seeing her shy reaction just now, could she really like me? I need to observe carefully.
Alice: Seeing his nervous reaction just now, could he be interested in me? I need to find a chance to test him.
Within the Elf race's secret realm, entering here is utterly different from the outside world—a desolate expanse where storms rage!
This is an independent small world; being able to create such a vast, stable small world makes one marvel at Koreuron's magical prowess.
Terrifying pressure constantly ravages this small world, making breathing difficult; even Merlin feels some of it.
As for Alice? If not for her adequate strength, she would likely have been suppressed by this divine might to the point of vomiting blood and dying—ordinary folk entering here would only meet death.
"........." Alice frowned, following behind Merlin, laboring to breathe; even with her sect-level strength, entering the secret realm still taxes her.
Walking against the storm, Merlin stopped, reaching back toward Alice: "Alice, give me your hand."
"......" Alice blinked, instinctively taking Merlin's hand, her face flushed as she recalled the recent events, feeling Merlin had become gentler toward her—though she wondered if it was just an illusion.
Actually, Merlin merely noticed Alice struggling to withstand the secret realm's divine pressure, fearing she might suddenly lag behind and faint; he needed to look after her.
The two slowly advanced through the storm, steadily approaching the place the Elf King had designated—a hidden, mysterious cave.
"Have we arrived?" Alice felt the pressure ease somewhat, not as terrifying as outside.
"This is it...." Merlin exhaled in relief, shaking dust from his body, "That Elf King guy said there's no danger inside, but the pressure out here is enormous—most who come in probably die."
"This secret realm is shrouded in unparalleled pressure; I've never seen such extensive pressure before." Alice couldn't help but sigh.
"What we've seen are the remains of true gods; a dead camel is bigger than a horse—even if it's a corpse, its power likely far exceeds our comprehension." Merlin said solemnly.
"Really? Looks like we need to be more careful." Alice nodded.
The two passed through the pitch-black corridor, aided by the faint glimmers of light within the cave, they could barely make out ancient murals on the walls, resembling—individual pictographs.
One mural caught Merlin's attention: a stick figure holding two sticks, with curved horns on its head—clearly symbolizing a demon.
Above the stick figure, a large wave-like band resembling clouds was painted, depicting various strange creatures; a few lightning-like symbols seemed to be casting a spell?
Merlin stared at the ancient mural, as if it held a mysterious allure that blurred his consciousness; when he opened his eyes again—
On the mountaintop, dark clouds roiled, red lightning flashing continuously.
Above those clouds stood countless gods of tremendous power!
They roared in anger, mocking and scorning—those who dare challenge divine authority will meet a dead end!
A man gripped twin blades, gritted his teeth, his cape fluttering wildly behind him, facing the gods alone...

title: Chapter 47 — Eternal Sleep Secret Realm
content:
Chapter 47 — Eternal Sleep Secret Realm

Volume 22 · Chapter 47

“Merlin?!”

Hearing that call, Merlin came to as if from a dream, his head throbbing with a dull pain. He had the lingering sense he’d just seen something terrible, though he couldn’t quite recall what.

“Merlin, what’s wrong?” Alice walked over, concern in her voice.

“I was just...” Merlin felt a flicker of surprise within himself. It was as if he’d glimpsed a man facing countless enemies, yet now he could remember nothing—only some vague, indistinct images.

“You suddenly started staring blankly at these murals, and when I called to you several times you didn’t answer. I thought something was wrong…” Alice frowned slightly, wondering if Merlin was feeling unwell. He hadn’t been back in his normal state for long, and he might have some aftereffects.

“I’m fine, it’s just… these crude murals look a bit strange.” Merlin looked again at the stick-figure murals before him, but this time he saw no more inexplicable illusions. They simply appeared to record stories from ancient times.

Alice followed his gaze and murmured, “Maybe they record part of the elf race’s history? Since this is the resting place of the Elven God, naturally they would depict His life’s deeds.”

“That’s right…” Merlin nodded. Most of the murals before him depicted the greatness of Corellon, yet his eyes remained fixed on the horned stick figure, a growing mystery settling in his chest.

At the very center of the maze, things become exceptionally terrifying!? SF轻 Novel

This was a spacious chamber. Fireflies drifted through the air, casting a soft glow.

Warm white light poured down from the ceiling, shining directly upon a throne built of stone.

A skeleton sat upon it, draped in a tattered, ragged robe. Even in death, it radiated a palpable majesty.

Countless fireflies clustered upon the bones, seeming intimately familiar with this corpse, causing the entire skeleton to emit a faint fluorescence.

Elven God Corellon died alone, with nothing but a dust-covered ring on one finger still gleaming faintly. It gave no indication that its owner had once been a great figure who led the elves into an age of prosperity.

Even if supremely glorious in life, after death there remained only a pile of bones.

“Is this Corellon’s remains?” Alice asked, looking at the skeleton upon the throne.

“There’s no doubt about it.” Merlin nodded. The skeleton appeared slightly taller than a human’s, clearly that of an elf.

“Then…” Alice took a small vial from her bosom, inside which flowed the blood of the Elven King. “We just need to pour this blood upon the skull, correct?”

Merlin held out his hand and said solemnly, “Let me handle this. If any danger arises, it would be to your detriment.”

“Hmph?” Alice frowned stubbornly. “If there’s danger, you going won’t help either. Shouldn’t I be the one to do it?”

“Even if danger exists, I’m safer than you, aren’t I?” Merlin countered. Then, feigning impatience, he said, “Leave it to me. If anything were to happen to you, I’d end up having to take care of you anyway.”

“…” Alice blushed, hesitated for a moment, and then meekly handed the vial of Elven King’s blood to Merlin. She reasoned that Merlin was indeed more reliable than she when facing danger.

Merlin took the small vial and cautiously stepped onto the stairs, approaching the skeleton step by step.

After all, this had once been the deity of the entire elven race, and Merlin took no chances.

Even if the Elven King had said there were no deadly traps here, it was better to be safe than sorry.

Alice rested her hand on the hilt of her slender sword, her eyes revealing worry. If Merlin encountered danger, she would move immediately to rescue him.

Seeing strangers approach the remains, the fireflies scattered in alarm, swirling in the air like scattered starlight.

Merlin arrived before Corellon’s bones, removed the vial’s stopper, and slowly poured the Elven King’s blood over the skull.

The blood flowed over the skull and gradually seeped into the empty eye sockets. In that profound darkness, a soul that had slumbered for countless ages seemed to awaken.

Merlin drained the vial completely, yet Corellon’s remains remained still. “Well… nothing happened, did it?”

“Did we misunderstand?” Alice asked, puzzled.

“It can’t be. We followed exactly what the Elven King instructed. Did He forget something crucial?” Merlin frowned inwardly.

Suddenly, the ring upon Corellon’s skeletal finger erupted in brilliant light, fierce as the sun, blinding enough to force one’s eyes shut!

The dust-covered ring seemed to have been stimulated into extreme instability. Its dazzling radiance shot straight into the sky, and one could feel the overwhelming pressure belonging to a god!

“So this is… a Divine Artifact!?” Merlin blurted out in involuntary astonishment.

This ring was the sole Divine Artifact in the secret realm spoken of by the Elven King. The moment it activated, it unleashed power beyond imagination!

Terrifying divine might surged outward. Even Merlin’s eyes widened in genuine shock.

This was no counterfeit artifact; it was the real thing. Even a utterly useless waste could become a regional overlord merely by wearing a Divine Artifact, capable of establishing his own era!

Merlin’s brows knit. This was the first time in his life he had witnessed a true Divine Artifact. The mere divine pressure made his former enemies seem like novices, utterly insignificant, like ants.

This was only the pressure exerted by a single Divine Artifact ring. If Corellon, the Elven God, had still been alive, combining His innate power with the ring’s strength… who knew how formidable He would have been!

It seemed that after the gods fell, the elves’ age did not come from mere luck. Rather, it was because Elven God Corellon’s strength was sufficient to establish the Elven Era.

“Merlin!” Alice grew worried for his safety. The artifact’s pressure filled her with fear. If anything went wrong, she feared the entire secret realm might not withstand its power!

“Alice, calm down. It’s fine!” Merlin turned back and shouted loudly. Though the aura of the Divine Artifact ring was surging, he felt no threat.

The intense golden light emitted by the artifact ring gradually dimmed, though it did not disappear completely. It stabilized, as if continuously radiating its power outward.

“Is it over?” Alice relaxed somewhat. The terrifying divine pressure softened, becoming less threatening.

Merlin exhaled in relief, feeling that they had successfully awakened the artifact’s power. “The mission’s complete. It went rather smoothly.”

“Then let’s leave this place quickly,” Alice suggested, glancing around cautiously. “I don’t know why, but I feel something odd here.”

“What’s the rush? We haven’t claimed our rewards yet. Don’t forget what the Elven King promised—we can choose any two items here as compensation.” Merlin planted his hands on his hips and surveyed the surroundings, but soon frowned.

*Damn it. Is this old fox playing word games with us!?*

The place was utterly empty. Aside from that Divine Artifact ring, what else was there!?

Wait… wait! Beneath Corellon’s skeleton, isn’t that something—?

title: Chapter 48 — Scroll
content:
Chapter 48 — Scroll

Volume 22 · Chapter 48

Merlin walked forward curiously, reached under Corelon's skeleton, felt around for a moment, and took out two old scrolls covered in dust.

The two scrolls looked very old, with damaged edges and corners, the paper was somewhat yellowed.

"Merlin, what are you holding?" Alice asked curiously.

"...Don't know either."

Merlin walked slowly down from the high platform, blew the dust off the two scrolls, looked at the weird hieroglyphs on them, and couldn't recognize them at all.

"I see..." Alice took the two scrolls, then frowned, "They... are ancient elf script."

Merlin looked around, couldn't help but say in disappointment, "Damn elf king, said there were good things here. Besides that artifact ring, just give us two, bullshit! Besides these two scrolls, absolutely nothing!"

"Well... not coming back empty-handed then? Maybe these scrolls record something valuable. How about letting the elf king check them for us?" Alice wasn't obsessed with getting treasures from here, but the scrolls under Corelon's butt must be something unusual.

"...Merlin sighed, his mood wasn't good, his eyes fixed on the artifact ring in Corelon's hand, 'That artifact looks powerful, I really want to take it directly...'"

"Don't do that. The other races rely on that artifact to survive. If we take it, those races will likely be destroyed." Alice stopped Merlin's dangerous thought.

"Forget it. Let's go ask the elf king what these scrolls are. If they're not rare treasures, we'll settle accounts later."

Merlin frowned and walked outside; Alice followed closely behind.

But just as Merlin was about to disappear into the secret room, a mysterious voice suddenly sounded in his ear—

"Is it you? This is impossible..."

Merlin was struck like by lightning, stood frozen, incredibly shocked, he couldn't sense anyone else inside besides himself and Alice. Who exactly was speaking?

This situation where Merlin couldn't sense anything wasn't the first time. Last time it was saving Cain locked in the dungeon, same thing—no aura at all.

This could only mean two things: either the hidden guy was too weak, or like Cain, powerful beyond measure!

Merlin's gaze was alert, a drop of cold sweat slowly slid down his forehead, he became uneasy, looking around.

"What's wrong?" Alice asked confusedly, looking at Merlin.

"...Did you hear a voice?" Merlin asked in a low voice.

"What voice?" Alice looked left and right, suspecting Merlin had mental issues?

"Just... an old man's voice..." Merlin felt he hadn't misheard.

Alice froze, then suddenly laughed, "You're talking nonsense. Where is there an old man's voice? If anything, here only you're an old man."

Merlin wanted to speak but stopped, beginning to doubt himself, thinking Alice couldn't hear anything either—was he hallucinating?

Merlin...

Alice frowned, stood on tiptoe and touched Merlin's forehead, worried, "Are you sick?"

"........." Merlin's expression awkward, turned his head to scan the room again, gaze fixed on Corelon's skeleton on the throne—

Just now, who was speaking?

Merlin and Alice used the elf king's blood to activate the artifact's power in the secret realm.

Colored light penetrated the clouds, spreading endlessly outward, gradually covering the entire United Kingdom!

The artifact powers intertwined, forming a huge protective shield that completely enveloped the land under the other races.

The huge abyss in the sea kept releasing gravity, but couldn't do anything about the golden shield—it was like an unpoppable bubble?

"Did they succeed?" Sylph looked at the strange sight before her.

"Should have succeeded. With the artifact's power supporting it, the abyss underwater can't swallow this land."

The elf king felt the ancestors' divine power, couldn't help but smile, feeling freed from destiny.

The artifact's power would continuously protect the United Kingdom, no need to worry about most threats.

That prophecy of the other races' extinction might change because of this?

The elf king wouldn't need to keep contributing his magic; if he cultivated quietly for a while, his strength might recover to its peak.

"Moreover, the artifact's power forms a shield that can defend against many powerful magic attacks. One could say, with the artifact's support, the United Kingdom is the safest place in the world."

"That's great." Sylph's eyes sparkled, full of longing for the future.

"They activated Corelon's ring power?" Rock Cave King asked from behind, grumbling.

"Correct. That ring has infinite potential. Back then, father god relied on it to establish the elves' era." Elf king answered with a smile.

"No wonder it's an artifact, this power is indeed terrifying..." Rock Cave King looked up at the light blooming in the sky, "But what's the origin of that ring?"

"I'm not clear either. Father god never said." Elf king looked troubled.

At this moment, Alice and Merlin's figures slowly appeared from the secret realm's entrance, returning from that barren small world.

"Welcome back! My friends..." Elf king stepped forward, acting extremely enthusiastic, after all they helped quite a bit.

"Stop! Don't..." Merlin put on a cold expression, "You said there were good things in the secret realm?"

"Correct, there were indeed many treasures of our clan." Elf king nodded sincerely.

"Bullshit!" Merlin frowned, looking elf king up and down, "You big eyebrows, you're a thorough merchant! Besides that artifact, clearly no other

title: Chapter 49 — Fatal Blade
content:
Chapter 49 — Fatal Blade

Volume 22 · Chapter 49

The Elf King unrolled a scroll and glanced at it, his astonished expression gradually freezing on his face, his hands trembling slightly—

"This is truly... amazing..."

"What is it?" Alice asked curiously.

"The third forbidden magic of our race..." The Elf King spoke seriously, swallowing nervously, "Elf Blood Sacrifice."

"No way?!" Sylph exclaimed, as if hearing something incredible, "That's the forbidden magic the father god refused to teach even until his death?"

"That's right..." The Elf King nodded, speaking solemnly, "Every forbidden magic demands a painful price; it must be used with extreme caution. Elf Lament can revive the dead, but it costs countless souls. Elf Judgment takes vitality as its price—if one wishes to use it, the elf must give up immortality. Even as mighty as the father god, after using Elf Judgment to slay the old-era gods, he could not escape the ravages of time and died. As for this third forbidden..."

"The third... price... could it be...?" Sylph started to speak but stopped.

"Elf Blood Sacrifice is a forbidden magic of mutual annihilation, erasing both the user's and the enemy's souls simultaneously, leaving no chance for either to survive."

The Elf King frowned and said.

"How domineering... No wonder the father god preferred to take this forbidden magic to the grave rather than teach it to you..." Sylph somewhat grasped the horror of this magic. Normally after death one falls into hell, but those killed by Elf Blood Sacrifice have their souls obliterated outright, not even given a chance to enter hell.

"I..." The Elf King paused, thinking, then said, "The father god's intention is... he does not want me or Axiudiel to learn this forbidden magic, for the end result would be mutual annihilation, which is not what he wishes to see. I and Axiudiel are destined that one of us will continue to lead the race..."

"Huh? By the way, can we learn your forbidden magic?" Merlin felt intrigued, sensing that each forbidden magic was more overpowering than the last; if they could learn it, it would seem pretty good.

"If you were an elf, Lord Merlin, I would teach you, but our clan's forbidden magic cannot be used by anyone outside the elves." The Elf King smiled helplessly.

"That's really no fun, all that work for nothing...." Merlin rolled his eyes, thinking that after finally finding something good in the secret realm, it has nothing to do with him—isn't this just like being a wage laborer?

"You two have found our clan's lost forbidden magic; this is extremely precious to me, I don't even know how to thank you." The Elf King smiled, unceremoniously slipping the scroll of forbidden magic into his bosom; this item is vital to the elf race, and might turn the tide at a critical moment.

"Are you really going to thank us, you old coot? Or are you just laughing inside at us working for nothing?" Merlin's veins bulged on his forehead; he felt that his collaborations with the elves had never been beneficial, and they were all terribly sly!

"No, no, no—I'm not a stingy person. If you come away empty-handed, I'll give you extra compensation; that shouldn't be a problem, right?" A bead of sweat the size of a fist rolled down the Elf King's forehead; he felt misunderstood.

"Cut the nonsense, what's written on the other scroll?" Merlin demanded, irritated.

"Just a moment..." The Elf King opened another mysterious scroll, his expression shifting continuously—sometimes deep in thought, then suddenly enlightened— "This... is amazing, amazing..."

"Huh?" Alice couldn't help but prick up her ears; being praised as amazing by the Elf King must mean it's something truly astonishing, right?

"What exactly is it? Are you bullying us because we can't read your clan's writing?" Merlin frowned, obviously out of patience.

"Lord Merlin, don't rush; let me explain slowly..." The Elf King took a deep breath and said slowly, "Our father god was born in the Age of Gods; he once experienced the destruction of the old era and understands all matters, great and small. This records the forging method of the Godslayer Sword Mistilteinn; I believe the father god must have witnessed the entire forging of this divine artifact...."

"Godslayer Sword... Mistilteinn?" Merlin showed a hint of doubt.

"Ha, Lord Merlin seems not very familiar with this divine artifact..." The Elf King paused, then explained, "The ancestor of your demon race, the Prophet, possesses not only the demon sword Banri Garan at your waist, but also the Godslayer Sword Mistilteinn. Legend says it was forged by the finest dwarf master; this weapon holds the power of certain death—any regenerative, healing, or resurrection power is useless before it. It can be called the ultimate killing edge among divine artifacts...."

"!!!" Merlin's eyes widened; Cain's face flashed in his mind, thinking he desperately needed this divine artifact! When facing those who endlessly regenerate like chewing gum, wouldn't it be a sure kill?!

"I never expected..." The Elf King gazed at the scroll and sighed, "The forging method of Mistilteinn was already attempted by the dwarves long ago, yet to find another copy in the father god's resting place? Perhaps this is heaven's will—fate does not allow this legendary divine weapon to vanish into the currents of history."

"Well... this is mine now." Merlin took the scroll from the Elf King's hand, revealing a satisfied smile.

"Ha, of course—I won't go back on my word. If you bring out something usable from the secret realm, I'll give it to you." The Elf King said generously, thinking that Mistilteinn was made from primordial materials; now wanting to forge this divine artifact, the difficulty would surely be enormous.

Merlin excitedly clenched the scroll, feeling this thing could at any moment become an awesome divine artifact. "Can you make the weapon described above?"

"As for forging, we elves have no talent for it; even a random dwarf friend could likely outperform us. Moreover, legend says Mistilteinn was forged by the dwarves; if Lord Merlin wants this sword, he still needs to seek out the dwarves—probably only they can make this primordial divine artifact reappear." The Elf King said seriously.

"Dwarves?" Merlin furrowed his brow, feeling he needs to go through some ordeal—"Who among the dwarves has the best skill nowadays?"

"As far as I know, it's Master Balin..." The Elf King replied.

"Master Balin... huh!?"

Merlin suddenly recalled a familiar short figure—the cross-eyed dwarf who had saved him—hadn't he been shouting that he was Balin's son?!!

Tch! Do I have to see those two idiots again?

Merlin furrowed his brow, looking at the scroll in his hand, feeling a bit irritated, but to obtain this killing blade he would surely have to put in some thought.

The Elf King glanced at Alice, embarrassed, and said, "Miss Alice, you didn't get anything useful, huh."

"...I don't need it, ha..." Alice gave an embarrassed laugh; inside she still felt a little disappointed.

"If you're willing, I can introduce you to a hot-tempered friend; if he's willing to give you pointers, it would surely help you greatly." The Elf King said meaningfully.

"Who?" Alice asked curiously.

"..." The Elf King smiled and lowered his voice, saying—

"The sovereign of the entire dragon race—"

"The Blazing Flame Dragon King."

title: Chapter 50 — Tempered by a Thousand Hammers
content:
Chapter 50 — Tempered by a Thousand Hammers

Volume 22 · Chapter 50

The Rock Cave King led Merlin and Alice away from the summit of the Sacred Tree, while the Elf King and Sylph remained behind.

The Elf King gazed at the Mystic Gate, which continued to radiate the power of divine artifacts. He no longer needed to pour his own strength into maintaining the kingdom, and a wave of emotion washed over him.

In the end, did he still need to rely on the Father God's power for his people to survive?

Were his own abilities truly limited? Had he failed the Father God's trust?

Perhaps Asmodeus was better suited to lead the elf race...

The Elf King lowered his head, overwhelmed with self-reproach. He was desperate to recover his strength now.

But having long since surpassed the Saint tier, regaining his peak condition shouldn't take too long.

"Your Majesty, directly giving Merlin-sama that scroll for forging Mistilteinn... isn't that a bit risky?" Sylph couldn't help voicing her concern. "That's the method for forging a divine artifact—the very blade that once slew a god. We could have the dwarves forge it for us, strengthening our race."

"We can't be too petty. They did help us enormously. If we gave nothing in return, that would look bad." The Elf King lifted his head, pondering. "I don't know why Merlin-sama was exiled from the demon race, but as one of the former Seven Monarchs, I hope to build a deep friendship with him. That would benefit us both greatly."

Sylph lowered her head, recalling how Merlin had crushed Asmodeus with overwhelming force. She somewhat understood the Elf King's desire for a powerful ally.

"Besides... we also found the third forbidden magic..." The Elf King silently gripped the scroll. With this forbidden magic in hand, if they faced extreme danger, they'd at least have a mutual destruction option.

"Your Majesty, you intend to learn this forbidden magic? That's... far too dangerous." Sylph disapproved.

"Sylph, you must understand—this forbidden magic could bring a turning point in a moment of life and death." The Elf King paused, flashing a seemingly relaxed smile. "The moment I was chosen by the Father God as leader, I made my peace with death. If the doom of the alien race is unavoidable, I need you to take care of Shirley. Only this child—I don't want her to bear the heavy burden of..."

"Your M—" Sylph wanted to speak but stopped, not knowing how to respond. The prophecy that the alien race would eventually perish felt like a mountain pressing down on her.

Among the rubble of the ruins, strange things began to rise—pure white, round and plump, emitting startled cries.

The Elf King frowned, his expression unsettled.

"This..." He said nothing, his mind racing with how to get his hands on Mistilteinn.

Late at night, Merlin stared at the scroll before him. Forging it would be extremely difficult—especially since it was made in the primordial era. Could anything comparable to that age even be recreated now? As for the dwarves' forging technology in this era...

He couldn't even obtain the materials needed to forge Mistilteinn. Like a child eyeing a desired toy, dreaming of it every night.

Yet Merlin couldn't let go of this weapon—who could stand against his blade? He absolutely had to get this armament. And afterward, Mistilteinn would remain intact!

He didn't believe that Cain, that ungrateful wretch, could get close to it.

"Merlin, what are you thinking?" Alice, noticing his preoccupied expression, asked curiously.

"I want to go find Balin-sama of the dwarf race and see if he can forge this."

"...Since you're going to find the dwarf master Balin, shall I come with you?" Alice said enthusiastically.

"Never mind, I'll go alone this time. The Elf King invited you to meet the Blaze Holy Dragon for guidance—that's a rare opportunity. You might learn more secrets about the inheritance crystals. Don't forget, your training is still important." Merlin planned to visit the dwarf lands alone.

"......" Alice frowned, feeling uncomfortable at the sudden separation from Merlin. "But why? Is there a problem...?"

Merlin looked at Alice in confusion.

"......" Alice puffed out her cheeks like a hamster eating, her eyes filled with resentment, as if Merlin couldn't wait to be rid of her.

"What's that look for...?" A cold sweat formed on Merlin's forehead. "You wouldn't sneak back home while I'm gone, would you?"

Alice suspected him. "What are you thinking???"

Merlin frowned, explaining, "I'm fine out here. Why would I go back?"

"Really? Don't lie to me, or I won't let you off~!" Alice's tone was full of warning.

"You... don't trust me at all?" Merlin sighed. "I'll be back soon." He added, "By the way, the Holy Dragons are supposedly brothers. We took Maelstrom's power—that Blaze Dragon King might get angry. The Elf King said he'd introduce you, but you should be careful. Who knows if this dragon king would seek revenge for his brother."

"Is that so? Sounds a bit dangerous..." Alice frowned.

"With the Elf King there, it should be fine." Merlin recalled his battle with Maelstrom—even provoking the Light Holy Dragon, that guy hadn't gotten too angry. The Holy Dragons, though brothers, didn't seem particularly close.

Alice nodded, accepting the temporary separation. She glanced at the scroll for forging Mistilteinn in Merlin's hand, lost in thought.

Novel text: "You're so eager to get Mistilteinn... isn't it because of Cain?"

"That bastard almost got us killed. We can't just let it go—an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. That's my creed." Mentioning Cain put Merlin in a bad mood. He said with a helpless tone—

"Speaking of which, we don't even know where she's hiding now." The pitch-black night, the deserted wilderness, occasional wolf howls breaking the silence—yet a humming tune shattered the darkness, completely out of place.

"Hmm~ Humming~" Dickte, draped in a black robe, carried a gagged and bound girl on his shoulder. The girl struggled and squirmed, tears soaking her cheeks.

"Stop struggling. You'll be food for the Great Lord. It's your honor~" Dickte cooed falsely, humming as he led her to a deep cave. He roughly threw her inside. Beast-like roars and the girl's piercing screams echoed, then silence fell.

"Master, are you full?" Dickte knelt, asking quietly.

"Not nearly enough. Catch more young girls." Cain's voice drifted from the darkness.

"Yes." Dickte lowered his head, peeking up. "When will the Master finish digesting Dracula's power?"

"That废物's power was already fully absorbed by me... But that couple's power is harder to control—especially the sword-drawing technique. It's extremely unstable. I need time." Irritation crept into Cain's voice.

"Lucifer III's sword-drawing technique is indeed formidable, but as the Son of God, controlling demonic power must be difficult too," Dickte ventured cautiously.

"What do you mean, Dickte? Are you doubting me?" Cain's tone turned annoyed. "As your most loyal servant, how could I question your supreme power? Just curious, that's all."

Dickte let out a cold snort.

"Hmph!" Cain snorted, casual. "This sword-drawing technique is unique—my talents can't fully驾驭 it. But I can sense its unfathomable destructive power. If I could wield it, facing my mother, I'd have no fear. To hone basic sword techniques to such terror—magic and combat power have become burdens. Returning to simplicity is true strength. My Merlin Father... he's truly remarkable..."

"Dickte unconsciously gasped. Could it be that Cain, the Son of God, held such high regard for Lucifer III? Did that mean...

A guy without any magic or combat power, relying solely on tempered sword techniques, could rival a god? Unbelievable—sounded like a fairy tale for children.

"Dickte, be patient. I will soon surpass everything in this mortal realm." Cain paused, excitement in his voice. "Once I eliminate the two treacherous humans who deceived me and reclaim all my power, I'll open the passage between the mortal world and the celestial realm."

"I'll tread on countless corpses, return to the celestial realm, and complete my divine transformation. You'll receive generous rewards."

"Thank you for your generosity, Master. I'll serve you faithfully..." Dickte smiled humbly, silently gripping the stone in his hand, thinking—

Ignoring all lives to return to the celestial realm? Why not seize the chance to kill him and become god myself? But... there was no reason to refuse.
