title: Chapter 2 — Master's Level (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 2 — Master's Level (Extra Chapter)

Volume 23 · Chapter 2

“? ? ?” Merlin widened his eyes, instantly recognizing this foul‑mouthed little imp, couldn’t help but chuckle, thinking what a small world—back then he tormented me for so long, is revenge coming this fast?

“Dwarves are really stupid, stealing dozens of times in a row and still not noticing, hehe.... Fairy Phil holding a wine bottle three times the size of a notebook, looking very bizarre; if you don’t pay attention you’d think the bottle is flying by itself?”

Merlin grabbed the wine bottle in one hand, pulled it to his side, and stared at Fairy Phil with a meaningful gaze.

Fairy Phil suddenly felt unable to fly, puzzled, lifted his head, and saw Merlin’s chin, looking at him with ill intent.

“Who is this guy? I haven’t provoked him, why is he snatching the wine I stole?”

Fairy Phil didn’t recognize the little Merlin from before, but seeing someone trying to take something from him, he suddenly became tough.

“Where did this bandit come from? Get lost! Don’t make me angry, otherwise the consequences will be dire!”

Merlin’s face darkened, thinking puzzledly, “How can a tiny thing that could be slapped to death with a palm have such audacity? I’ve seen a ghost.”

Seeing Merlin silent, Fairy Phil instantly became a bit timid, thinking, “What’s wrong with this bastard? Does he have a grudge against me?”

Thus, having no choice, it merely stirred the surprise behind it, using all its suckling strength to tug, trying to get its wine back.

Alas, fairies have always been trash with combat power 5; how could they possibly snatch something from the hands of a mighty Demon Lord?

“.... Merlin let out a cold chuckle, reflecting that not long ago he had been driven to distraction by such explosively weak little things—it felt like a dream.

“Bastard! What are you laughing at? Looking down on me?!” Fairy Phil flew up to Merlin’s face, bared his teeth, “Tell you you’ve caused big trouble! I’ll kick your ass to pieces!

“Still so arrogant?” Merlin— grabbed Fairy Phil in his hand and said meaningfully.

“What? ? ?” Fairy Phil scrutinized Merlin suspiciously and asked, “Who are you? Have we met before?”

“You forgot your dad so quickly?” Merlin paused, then reminded, “Forget that you went to the Elf King’s palace to steal wine, got caught by me?”

“Huh?!” Fairy Phil widened his eyes, continually sizing up Merlin, finding it utterly unbelievable, “It’s you! That little brat?! You really didn’t die!

“Tsk!” Merlin furrowed his brows, dissatisfied, “From your tone, you actually wish I were dead?”

“No no no.” Fairy Phil flew out of Merlin’s palm, intrigued, circling him curiously without cease, “Back when I saw you foolishly going to your death, I thought fools have fool’s luck—you’d surely not die!”

“Watch your words, thinking I was helpless against you back then and still can’t deal with you this little thing?” Merlin’s face turned black, thinking whether this brat had gotten chummy with him.

“How did you suddenly get so big? Did you eat fertilizer? Hahaha....” Fairy Phil giggled nonstop.

“Don’t push me, I don’t want to argue with you little thing, I’m here for an important matter.” Merlin’s forehead veins twitched as he suppressed his anger. 915

title: Chapter 3 — Infinitely Close
content:
Chapter 3 — Infinitely Close

Volume 23 · Chapter 3

“Demon?” Old dwarf Balin furrowed his brows, sizing up Merlin from head to toe, completely unable to see anything demonic about him.
“Don’t joke, you’re clearly human, right?” Dwarf Barli couldn’t help emphasizing, it’s a rule that the smithy won’t forge equipment for criminals, after all humans once iron‑fistedly suppressed other races, not something easily forgotten.
“....Merlin scratched his head, thinking not having horns is really a hassle, should I stick a carrot on my head to fake one?
Fairy Ferri flew out from behind Merlin, landing on the table, pointing at him and saying to Barli, “Barli, it’s him! The little brat we rescued!
“Eh?!” Dwarf Barli jerked—stunned, he stepped up to Merlin, looking up at him, “Really that ill‑tempered criminal kid
“What does ‘ill‑tempered’ mean... Merlin’s eyebrows twitched involuntarily.
“Exactly, this is his true appearance; before, for some unknown reason he turned into that little brat.” Fairy Ferri landed on Barli’s head to explain.
“Surviving the internal strife among the elves is really lucky?” Dwarf Barli showed a simple smile, baring his teeth as he tried to punch Merlin’s body, “Turns out he’s such a strong guy, just with an unpleasant villain’s face, not likable at all, far from cute like when he was a child.
“....Veins faintly appeared on Merlin’s forehead, he thought, Damn! What does he mean? Could it be that I’ve become crippled?!
“Barli, do you know this young man?” Old dwarf Balin asked doubtfully.” i T
“Sort of, when I went to the Elf King for medicine, there was an internal disturbance; he was imprisoned by the dark elves, and I together with Ferri rescued him.” Dwarf Barli chuckled, using his hands to gauge Merlin’s height, “I didn’t expect him to grow this tall in just a few days—it startled me; clearly he was just a little brat before…
“I’m not a brat; it’s just that I took the wrong medicine, causing my body to degenerate.” Merlin emphasized with a serious expression.
“Criminal…….” Old dwarf Balin showed a hesitant expression, wary of any human.
“Father, rest assured, he’s not a bad person; if he were ill‑intentioned, Ferri wouldn’t get close to him.” Dwarf Barli pointed to Ferri on his head, “The fairy race’s talent is still trustworthy; they can easily sense good and evil.
“Indeed, don’t look at my demeanor—I can still tell right from wrong.” Fairy Ferri crossed her arms, saying proudly.
“Since he’s Barli’s friend, I can relax.” Old dwarf Balin nodded, his expression softening, “I don’t know what business Master Merlin has with me; if you want to buy weapons, you can look around yourself—though you’re a criminal, I can make an exception and sell to you… =
Merlin didn’t bother explaining his identity; as long as the other party trusts him, that’s fine. “I’m not here to sell weapons, but rather another item; I hope Master Balin can help me forge it.
“What item?” Dwarf Barli asked curiously, “You came all the way from the human world—surely it’s not just to have my father forge something?
Merlin took out the Mistral scroll from his bosom and handed it to Barli, “This is something I happened to obtain; the scroll records a—I want to obtain that blade.
“Let me see…” Dwarf Barli took the Mistral scroll and examined it carefully; although it’s ancient elf script, he can still understand much of it.
“I’ve heard that worldwide, dwarven forging is top‑notch, and Master Balin is among the best of them, so…” Merlin paused, looking at the aged dwarf, “Besides Master Balin, I doubt anyone could reforge this divine weapon.
“Ugh… what is this? ?” Dwarf Barli trembled all over, as if he’d seen something unbelievable, his eyes almost popping out, “Father, quickly look—what’s recorded here…
Old dwarf Balin rarely saw his son so shocked; he hurriedly looked at the scroll as well, instantly turned pale with shock, nearly fainting.
Dwarf Barli quickly supported his father, worriedly saying, “Father, …”.
“I’m fine; I never imagined I’d get to see my ancestors’ peerless forging technique in my lifetime—it’s not like I lived for nothing.
Old dwarf Balin’s hands trembled, as if the scroll in his grasp were a priceless treasure.
“But Father, I can’t understand much of what’s written here.” Dwarf Barli said doubtfully.
“Your skills are insufficient, so of course it’s hard to understand; every sentence on the scroll is supreme forging essence, and many ancient techniques have already been lost—even I need to study it thoroughly.” Old dwarf Balin paused, then said solemnly, “Our ancestors in the primordial age could forge this perfect divine artifact, the Mistral, relying not only on experience and skill but also other factors.
“Is Mistral… something your ancestors forged personally?” Merlin asked doubtfully, because the Balin family supposedly has poor eyesight, making it hard to swing a hammer accurately.
“Of course, our family has been blacksmiths for generations; our ancestors were the greatest forgers in history, Mistral is the crystallization of dwarven forging art, capable of becoming a god‑slaying sword passed down through the ages—its excellence needs no further explanation.” Old dwarf Balin said sternly.
Merlin was about to ask further when he saw Balin and Barli father and son place the Mistral scroll on the ground, murmuring incantations nonstop, then began to kowtow.
This left Merlin puzzled—isn’t the scroll just a design diagram? Why the need for such solemnity?
Merlin didn’t know what forging process was recorded on the scroll, but to any blacksmith it’s a priceless treasure.
It means Master Balin can learn the primordial ancestors’ forging experience, elevating his skill to a higher level.
Every blacksmith’s dream is to forge a legendary divine weapon; this is recognition of their skill and a supremely glorious achievement.
“Hey, what are you doing? Kowtowing to a sheet of paper is ridiculous.” Fairy Ferri couldn’t help muttering.
“Ferri, you don’t understand; Mistral is my ancestors’ supreme masterpiece, and my father and I are paying respect to them by kowtowing.” Dwarf Barli said seriously.
“Master Balin, can you forge this Mistral?” Merlin asked tentatively.
“Forging it is no problem, only…” Old dwarf Balin showed a troubled expression.
“Only what?” Merlin tilted his head.
“Only wanting to match the primordial Mistral’s quality—it’s extremely difficult; although my forging skill is decent, trying to stand beside the ancestors… is basically impossible, the gap isn’t just a little.” Old dwarf Balin shook his head; compared to the ancestors, what he forges is like a child’s toy.
“Like that….”.
Merlin furrowed his brows; although he had some expectation, he still felt a bit disappointed, unable to perfectly forge Mistral.
He wondered, since the demon race’s prophet left behind Banri Garan, why not also leave Mistral? Instead, he took that divine artifact and let it disappear from history.
“Then what level can Master Balin achieve?
“To be frank…” Old dwarf Balin lifted his head, his gaze turning serious, speaking honestly one by one
“Although my memory doesn’t match the ancestors’, it’s not bad either.
“If I thoroughly study the primordial forging techniques on the scroll, I might be lucky.
“The Mistral I forge could infinitely approach the primordial god‑slaying blade!”

title: Chapter 4 — Three Super Rare Materials
content:
Chapter 4 — Three Super Rare Materials

Volume 23 · Chapter 4

"Infinitely close, is it?"

Merlin pondered for a moment. He figured there was no other way. After all, it was clearly unrealistic to expect Master Bardin to perfectly recreate a divine artifact forged in the primordial era.

Besides, apart from Master Bardin, if he left the dwarf race, Merlin really couldn't find another smith with such exquisite skill.

Merlin nodded, but his expression showed a touch of financial embarrassment, and he said with a hint of awkwardness, "Very well. I'll leave it to you, Master Bardin. As for payment... I'll do my best..."

"Payment isn't really an issue," the old dwarf Bardin said. "You bringing me this scroll is the best payment. It records many forging techniques from the primordial era — something money can't buy." The old dwarf Bardin had no intention of demanding any reward. After all, the scroll for forging Mistilteinn was already priceless. "However, the materials listed on it for forging the God-killer Blade are each more difficult to obtain than the last..."

"What materials? Tell me. I can go find them." Merlin had long been mentally prepared. Divine artifacts weren't something you could just casually forge. Finding a suitable blacksmith was the first hurdle, but the truly death-defying part would be acquiring the required materials. Precious things from the primordial era — he suspected it would take considerable effort to get his hands on them.

"To forge a divine artifact like Mistilteinn, you need three..." The old dwarf Bardin paused, then slowly began introducing the three required materials to Merlin.

"The first is the rare treasure from the primordial era — the God-Sealing Stone. It has the ability to suppress all resurrection and regeneration. It is the very foundation that allows Mistilteinn to slay gods."

"The second is called Golden Essence. It usually exists deep within gold mines, taking tens of thousands of years to form even a tiny bit. It can make forged weapons incomparably sharp, capable of splitting heaven and cracking the earth."

"The final one is a god's soul. No matter how卓越 of forging skill and how excellent the materials, it remains difficult to forge a divine artifact — the highest achievable quality is a pseudo-divine artifact. That barrier is hard to break, which makes a god's soul crucial. It determines the final quality of Mistilteinn. If you want a weapon to have a chance of becoming a divine artifact, a god's soul is indispensable."

Merlin's brows tightened. After hearing Master Bardin's explanation, he felt a chill run down his scalp. He'd never heard of any of these things. Who knew where to find them?

And some of them were rare treasures from the primordial era. In the present day, hundreds of thousands of years later, they must be exceedingly scarce — finding them would be harder than climbing to the heavens!

Not to mention a god's soul. He'd never seen a god in his life...

Merlin immediately felt his head spinning. He'd expected forging Mistilteinn wouldn't be easy, but he hadn't imagined it would be this difficult.

"Then... do you know where I can obtain these things, Master Bardin?"

"I'm not very clear about the God-Sealing Stone and the god's soul. These are too secretive, and they're things that only existed in the primordial era. Even with shocking luck, finding them in the present day would be nearly impossible." The old dwarf Bardin shook his head. "But Golden Essence — a century ago, our clan once discovered a piece at the entrance of a gold mine. It was only the size of a fingernail and was regarded as our clan's supreme treasure. However, this rare treasure is usually guarded by powerful demonic beasts. To this day, we've only managed to seal off the Golden Essence but haven't succeeded in retrieving and using it."

"I see..." Merlin nodded in understanding. Though forging Mistilteinn was full of difficulties, he would take it step by step. Since he could get the Golden Essence now, he wouldn't let it slip away. "Where is the Golden Essence sealed? I'll figure out a way to get it right away."

"That won't do!" The old dwarf Bardin waved his hands frantically and said hesitantly, "Golden Essence is our clan's ultimate treasure. We won't allow anyone else to lay hands on it. Moreover, King Dwarf is selfish and stingy. That Golden Essence is his lifeblood. If it's taken, he'll fight to the death."

"Tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue in mild annoyance. He wondered if he should just snatch it. That didn't seem right. If he weren't completely backed into a corner, he wouldn't want to rob people openly. Even stealing would require more finesse than that.

"Lord Merlin, thank you for trusting me and willing to entrust the forging of Mistilteinn to me." The old dwarf Bardin sighed. "But even if you find all the materials, I'm afraid I won't have the chance to help you..."

"What do you mean?" Merlin frowned, his expression darkening. This Master Bardin had been talking all this time, and it turned out he didn't want to help forge Mistilteinn for him at all? Then why chat with him for so long? Was it because he looked too much like a criminal?

"Our clan's great general, Holly, ordered me to forge a set of Blackgold Armor. Tomorrow is the final deadline. But my lower back condition has flared up again, and I simply can't complete the general's order. I'm afraid by tomorrow morning, I'll be dragged out by General Holly to be punished."

"Father, no... let's fight them!" the dwarf Bardi said angrily, teeth clenched.

"Forget it. I'm already old, and my body is growing weaker by the day." The old dwarf Bardin looked up at his shop. "This place will be yours from now on, Bardi. I hope you'll diligently study the family's forging techniques. Perhaps you'll become an even better smith than I am someday..."

"Dad..." Dwarf Bardi clenched his fists helplessly. Facing the oppression from above, there was nothing he could do. Fighting wasn't his forte.

"What's there to fear? They're being so unreasonable, so we shouldn't hold back either. Watch me kick that so-called general's ass!" The fairy Phoebe floated in the air, brandishing her limbs and claws, utterly lacking any威慑.

"This... General Holly is acting so arbitrarily. Doesn't the Dwarf King care about such things?" Merlin asked in confusion.

"Lord Merlin, you don't know. The Dwarf King King only cares about gold and doesn't care about anything else. So General Holly is effectively the most powerful voice in Gold City. No one dares to offend him." The old dwarf Bardin shook his head and sighed, giving up on struggling.

"Only cares about gold? Finally, I've seen someone worse at leadership than me..." Dark lines dropped from Merlin's forehead. He took a deep breath and said, "Don't worry, Master Bardin. Since I'm here, you won't face any danger. No one can act so recklessly right under my nose."

"No... Lord Merlin, this has nothing to do with you. I don't want to drag you into this. If you anger General Holly, I'm afraid you won't be able to leave Gold City alive..." The old dwarf Bardin said worriedly.

"Oh? I won't be able to leave Gold City alive? Then I'm all the more curious about this dwarf general." Merlin gave a meaningful smile. He wanted to see how much trouble this dwarf general could cause him.

"Lord Merlin..." The dwarf Bardi thought this was dangerous and spoke hesitantly, "Stop joking. Although you look pretty strong, when it comes to facing a whole group of dwarf knights, you'd only have the option to run."

"Exactly. Now is not the time to show off. Even though you've turned into an adult, you can still only bully me. Face off against so many well-trained dwarf knights? I'd advise you to be sensible." The fairy Phoebe said seriously.

Both of them couldn't shake the impression of Merlin's childish weakness. Even though he'd turned into an adult now, they suspected nothing would change much.

They couldn't understand that Merlin and Little Merlin were two completely different beings, incapable of being compared.

"Whatever. I'll just stay here and wait for those guys to deliver themselves tomorrow morning..." Merlin sat down without hesitation, striking a pose as though he intended to stay.

"You don't need to meddle in this. Just watch from the sidelines tomorrow."

"Any food? I'm hungry..."

title: Chapter 5 — Blazing Holy Dragon (Extra)
content:
Chapter 5 — Blazing Holy Dragon (Extra)

Volume 23 · Chapter 5

On the other side, Alice followed the Elf King to the territory belonging to the dragon race.

The pitch-black land seemed cursed. Everything that came into view was barren and desolate, as though it were a forsaken place.

The towering black peaks in the distance gave off a faint sense of ill omen, like scorched earth after being consumed by flames.

The sun in the sky appeared to be larger and more blistering here than anywhere else, its fierce rays constantly baking the land.....

"Uh...."

Alice was drenched in sweat. She stopped and took deep breaths of the scorching air, gazing toward the peak of the distant black mountain where several giant dragons circled overhead.

She felt her saliva nearly dried up. Every swallow felt like someone was dragging a blade across her throat. This damn place was simply not fit for humans to survive in...

Alice lowered her head and quietly regretted having come here. A wave of dizziness began to wash over her.

The Elf King stopped and turned around to see Alice's exhausted state. "Miss Alice, are you alright? We're almost at—"

"I'm fine. It's just that the environment here is far harsher than I expected..." Alice sighed.

"There used to be dense forests here, but the dragons didn't like them, so they burned them all away," the Elf King explained.

"I see..." Alice frowned, recalling that dragons seemed to prefer open areas with wide视野, so they all made their homes in caves high in the mountains.

"As for why it's so hot? It's because of the influence of the Explosive Flame Sacred Dragon. Wherever it is, it feels like being inside a furnace. Miss Alice, it seems you haven't adapted yet," the Elf King said with a helpless smile. It appeared Alice wasn't the first person to feel uncomfortable here.

"Why is the range of influence so vast? We haven't even reached the foot of the mountain yet, and it's already this hot. If we were to face the Explosive Flame Sacred Dragon head-on, wouldn't we get roasted alive?" Alice furrowed her brow. Based on her experience, she had almost never seen a creature capable of affecting such a vast area!

"Sacred Dragons are the royalty among dragon race. The Explosive Flame Sacred Dragon is the most powerful and terrifying among them — and may be the only dragon capable of transforming into a human form. Wherever it goes, flames invade and turn everything into scorched earth," the Elf King paused, then looked at Alice. "In my prime, with the Light of Corellon, I indeed could have fought it. But now.... I'm no match for it. So let's not provoke that hot-tempered fellow."

"...I know," Alice nodded, realizing there might be considerable pressure when facing the Explosive Flame Dragon King. A Sacred Dragon that can transform into a human form? She'd never even heard of such a thing!

"Sir Sylph mentioned that Miss Alice can also transform into a Sacred Dragon? I wonder where you obtained this power? As far as I know, for a non-dragon race being to become part of the dragon race, one must have consumed an inheritance crystal," the Elf King, well-traveled and knowledgeable, guessed that Alice might have eaten an inheritance crystal born within the brain of a great dragon.

"That's right. I consumed the inheritance crystal of a deceased Frost Sacred Dragon, which is how I inherited the power of the dragon race...." Alice didn't hide it and admitted it openly.

"Then it makes sense. In the dragon race, there is the closest of kin bonds among siblings. You ate the inheritance crystal of a Frost Sacred Dragon, so you'll need to be careful. I'm not sure what the Explosive Flame Dragon King will think — if he seeks revenge for his sibling, it would be quite troublesome for both you and me."

Alice felt a thread of tension, her heart growing uneasy. Could he seek revenge against me because I consumed the Frost Sacred Dragon's inheritance crystal?

She resolved to stay alert around the Explosive Flame Sacred Dragon. She didn't know just how terrifying the strongest creature of the dragon race truly was. She should be able to handle it...

title: Chapter 7 — The Dragon Clan's Creed
content:
Chapter 7 — The Dragon Clan's Creed

Volume 23 · Chapter 7

The Blazing Flame Dragon King took on a human form, exuding a dragon's might that made one's heart tremble, and the magma behind him, as if summoned, grew even more boiling.
Alice grew wary, thinking, “So the Elf King and the Blazing Flame Holy Dragon have such a bad relationship? Then my hope of getting guidance is surely dashed.”
“Don’t be so hot‑headed, okay?” The Elf King faced the pressure of the Blazing Flame Dragon King, still keeping a harmless smile, “Even if you don’t welcome me, you shouldn’t hold such great hostility toward me, right?”
“You old fox, every time you come you bring nothing good, your head full of how to use me.” The Blazing Flame Dragon King’s face was full of anger; if he were a barrel of gunpowder, the Elf King would definitely be a spark, capable of making this strongest dragon’s mindset explode at any moment.
“No way I think that badly; at most I’m just asking you for a small favor, using…. This is a groundless slander against me.”
The Elf King helplessly shook his head.
“Slandering me? Hmph!” The Blazing Flame Dragon King snorted coldly, speaking in an unfriendly tone, “You once promised that if I agreed to ally with the Elf Clan Journalists’ Alliance, I could gain dominion over the entire inter‑racial alliance, but you never kept your promise; up to now it’s been you, that old fox, directing and manipulating everything inside the alliance! You deceived me and my kin with such despicable means, and still want respect from me? Do…”
“I did all this solely so that all other races could survive; if the non‑human peoples keep fighting each other, future catastrophe is inevitable, and only by uniting can there be a glimmer of hope.” The Elf King explained earnestly.
“I’ve heard enough of your excuses, that unfathomable prophecy—tens of thousands of years have passed, we’re still doing fine, your prophecy never came to pass!” The Blazing Flame Dragon King paused, narrowed his eyes, and speculated, “After all, you just want to exploit the other races’ interests to feed your own elf populace.”
“I never thought of exploiting anyone’s interests; with so many races forming an alliance, we inevitably need a visionary leader, and I will take responsibility without shirking.” The Elf King emphasized solemnly, not wanting to be misunderstood as a dictator.
“Such flowery words, proclaiming yourself a natural leader, your brain‑washing tactics are getting ever more proficient.” The Blazing Flame Dragon King bought none of it, speaking sarcastically, “No wonder the leaders of the other great races are increasingly dissatisfied with you; even the Orc King Sarat chose to exile himself, unwilling to stay—you really need to reflect on yourself, Elf King…”
“Sarat was exiled for trying to dismantle the alliance; anyone who wishes harm upon the alliance is undoubtedly an enemy of the non‑human races.” The Elf King recalled the former Orc King, his face turning somewhat grim.
“...The Blazing Flame Dragon King gave a cold laugh, turned his back, and said, ‘It’s precisely because of your arrogant attitude that people find you repulsive; get out of my sight at once—I don’t want to see you.’"or牡J玩
The Elf King furrowed his brows, feeling he could never get along with this hot‑tempered fellow, “I didn’t come today to explain all this; this Miss Alice is my friend, I hope you can give her some guidance.”
“You’ve really sunk so low as to ally with humans?!” The Blazing Flame Dragon King turned his head, eyes full of hostility, “I’m terribly disappointed in you…”
“You must have heard that my territory recently suffered a disturbance, right?” The Elf King probed.
“Exactly, I heard Ashmodor nearly destroyed you guys; it’s lucky you survived…” The Blazing Flame Dragon King said mockingly.
“This Miss Alice helped me a great deal; she possesses the power of the Holy Frost Dragon…” The Elf King introduced briefly.
“Huh?!” The Blazing Flame Dragon King suddenly frowned, instantly drawing his attention, “Really?”
“.....Alice took a step back, feeling extremely nervous; the pressure from the Blazing Flame Holy Dragon was overwhelming!
“Sinner, I’m asking if it’s true?!” The Blazing Flame Dragon King’s temper flared; he raised his hand and unleashed an attack, vicious flames roaring forth.
Facing the onrushing flame assault, Alice felt scorching breath wash over her, as if she’d be roasted in the next instant!
Left with no choice, Alice’s eyes turned into golden, narrow pupils; dragon’s might erupted, she lifted her hand and forged an impregnable ice wall!
The scorching flame surge surged madly, slamming into the ice wall; the clash of ice and fire instantly made the air tense!
Alice’s ice wall, built from fused ice crystals, under the Blazing Flame Dragon King’s flames, actually began to melt despite being unable to resist?!
The Elf King felt considerable pressure; although he knew the Blazing Flame Dragon King had a bad temper, he hadn’t expected the other to suddenly strike, “Stop! What are you doing?! =”
The terrifying flames slowly dissipated; the Blazing Flame Dragon King, expressionless, lowered his palm, “I was just testing you; if I really went all out, I’d burn you together with….” The Elf King relaxed a bit, seeing that the Blazing Flame Dragon King still had some restraint and had no intention of killing Alice.
Alice placed her hand on the hilt of her slender sword at her waist, cold sweat continually trickling down her forehead; from that clash she had already pretty much gauged the Blazing Flame Holy Dragon’s fearsome power—indeed worthy of being the dragon race’s leader! Even if she gave her all, she probably wouldn’t be a match for him!
“Your aura… indeed exudes Malygos’s power…” The Blazing Flame Dragon King’s face shifted between light and dark; suddenly a mighty dragon’s might accompanied a heat wave, as if he were on the brink of rage, “Did you kill my brother and devour his inheritance crystal?”
SF牡」说
“Yes… so what?” Alice gritted her teeth and replied, having prepared herself to fight the Blazing Flame Holy Dragon to the death.
“Our dragon race’s great power has been illicitly used by you sinners…” The Blazing Flame Dragon King bared his sharp teeth, veins bulging on his forehead, as if he would slay Alice in the next second.
Sensing the Blazing Flame Dragon King’s unstable mood, the Elf King stepped forward and hurriedly said, “Miss Alice is my friend; calm down, I won’t allow her to be harmed.”
“Shut your mouth; I never feel proud for crushing an ant.”
The Blazing Flame Dragon King’s expression remained angry, but that oppressive dragon’s aura that made breathing difficult gradually faded.
He carefully examined Alice a few times, thinking her strength sufficient to kill Malygos, so he had no doubts.
The Blazing Flame Dragon King suddenly gave a cold snort; his eyes lost a few traces of hostility and gained a hint of admiration.
“Our dragon race’s creed is survival of the fittest; the strong reign, the weak should be discarded like trash.”
“Although I utterly despise sinners inheriting our race’s power, you managed to slay Malygos and even take his place…”
“This proves that Malygos is utterly unworthy of being a great dragon!”

title: Chapter 8 — The Hour Has Come
content:
Chapter 8 — The Hour Has Come

Volume 23 · Chapter 8

"???"

Alice's mind was full of questions; she didn't understand the situation, nor did she comprehend how dragons felt.

In her view, brothers naturally needed to support each other and survive together.

Not like the Blazing Flame Sacred Dragon, who believed that his brother's death was simply because the brother was weak, making him trash that deserved to be eliminated.

But dragon thinking was indeed this simple, without any extra emotional entanglements, adhering to the iron-blooded rule of survival of the fittest where the strong are supreme.

In the eyes of great dragons, the weak were born to become food for the strong; this was an irreversible destiny.

"Marigot was a stupid and despicable creature who took pleasure in bullying the weak. A few praises from humans made him lose sight of himself, becoming some kind of Kingdom-Protecting Sacred Dragon? How ridiculous~" The Blazing Flame Dragon King showed no concealment of his disdain as he continued, "I warned him long ago, but he indulged in humans' sweet words, so it's not surprising he ended up like this."

"This..." Alice hesitated, unsure how to respond, since it was Merlin who had killed Marigot, not her.

"You defeated Marigot and consumed his inheritance crystal; this is what you deserve. Even as a sinner, you have the qualifications to inherit our race's power. This conforms to the law of the strong devouring the weak." The Blazing Flame Dragon King paused, then said sternly, "The weak do not deserve to possess the power of our great ancestors, nor do they have the right to call themselves Sacred Dragons. Marigot's death proves you qualify to replace him."

The Elf King noticed the Blazing Flame Dragon King had no intention of avenging his brother; instead, he mocked Marigot coldly. He finally felt relieved — it seemed Alice would not be in danger. Such a ruthless and cold-blooded outlook was indeed every dragon's way of thinking.

"We dragons are all descendants of Nidhogg. Sacred Dragons, especially, are the exceptional ones who have survived after being tested by time. We once fantasized about imitating the elves and establishing a world belonging only to the dragon race (but this dream never came to pass)." The Blazing Flame Dragon King became much calmer as he spoke slowly.

"After the era of sinners arrived, I realized this trend was unstoppable. All other races would fall into danger, slowly being devoured by the rising humans. At that time, I kindly invited my other brothers to come to this land, but not a single one was willing to follow me. They were proud, short-sighted, and overly self-assured. From that moment on, I knew they would definitely end their miserable fates in the overwhelming surge of sinners' rise."

The Elf King suddenly smiled and couldn't help saying, "Joining an alliance composed of other races — you are wise."

"Shut up! Hearing your voice irritates me. I won't deny that this land allowed the dragon race to continue繁衍, but that doesn't give you the right to dominate the kingdom's destiny." The Blazing Flame Dragon King's face darkened with anger again.

"..." The Elf King awkwardly cleared his throat, feeling it best to keep quiet to avoid provoking this short-tempered guy.

"So, are you willing to guide me in further learning dragon race power?" Alice asked tentatively.

"If you can perfectly fuse with Marigot's inheritance crystal and replace him, then you are the new Frost Sacred Dragon. I can barely consider you kin, and I have no reason to obstruct my own people from growing stronger." The Blazing Flame Dragon King said deeply. Although he didn't particularly like Alice as a sinner, in principle she was indeed more suitable to become a Sacred Dragon than Marigot.

"I see..." Alice secretly exhaled in relief; the trip hadn't been in vain.

"Although you consumed the inheritance crystal and can obtain some inherited memories, Marigot himself was someone with incomplete skills. You won't find the essence of dragon race power in his memories." The Blazing Flame Dragon King paused, then shifted direction. "If you want to learn the true power of great dragons, then you must enter the Ancestral Dragon's Sanctuary, where the souls of many primordial dragons are enshrined. You can receive certain training there."

"The Ancestral Dragon's Sanctuary..." Alice thought for a moment. Since that was where orthodox dragon race power was inherited, she definitely had to go there once, otherwise she might not get another chance in the future. "How do I reach that place?"

"Are you sure you want to go?" The Blazing Flame Dragon King's gaze suddenly became meaningful.

"Of course!" Alice answered firmly.

The Blazing Flame Dragon King suddenly pointed at the rolling lava behind him and said expressionlessly, "Jump down from here. This is the only path to the Ancestral Dragon's Sanctuary."

"..." Alice was momentarily stunned. Looking at the scalding lava waterfall ahead, suspicion arose in her heart — wasn't the Blazing Flame Dragon King finding ways to get her killed?

"Aren't you joking? Jumping into lava is no trivial matter. Even some geniuses who can surpass Saint-tier can easily die in there. Not everyone has your extraordinary resistance to flames, just like you." The Elf King frowned, feeling this was far too frivolous.

Alice approached the edge of the lava waterfall and looked down. The scalding lava flowed slowly, bubbling continuously.

Her face went pale, and a trace of hesitation stirred in her heart. To obtain orthodox dragon race power, she still couldn't joke away her own life.

"The inside of the Ancestral Dragon's Sanctuary is far more dangerous than this scalding lava. If you don't even have this much courage, then leave now. The dragon race's ancestors dislike cowards." The Blazing Flame Dragon King said with a solemn expression.

"..."

Alice hesitated, then suddenly looked at the ring Merlin had given her. Besides spatial storage, it also possessed the power to revive the wearer once.

Even if she couldn't resist the lava, she could rely on "Angela" to escape danger again.

Maybe I should try relying on this ring...

Alice, taking advantage of having a second life, decided to gamble. She stepped forward and resolutely plunged into the lava waterfall.

"Miss Alice! Wait!"

The Elf King cried out, but it was already too late. He could only watch helplessly as Alice fell into the rolling lava.

This is bad! They hadn't even figured out whether the Blazing Flame Dragon King was talking nonsense, and Miss Alice trusted that old fellow too much!

Magic power surfaced in the Elf King's palms. Before things became uncontrollable, perhaps he could stir up the lava and pull Alice out.

However, the Blazing Flame Dragon King suddenly blocked the Elf King, his expression dark as he said, "Don't interfere. Shouldn't you respect her choice?"

"..." A bead of cold sweat slid down the Elf King's forehead. His current strength couldn't defeat the Blazing Flame Sacred Dragon, so he could only calm himself down. "What you said about the Ancestral Dragon's Sanctuary... is it all true?"

"Do you think I'd lie to you like that?!" The Blazing Flame Dragon King stared at the Elf King, gritting his teeth. "The Ancestral Dragon's Sanctuary is the holy land in our hearts. There, you can see the souls of dragon race ancestors. Although you'll suffer unprecedented torment, there are far greater benefits."

"Wouldn't there be any danger?" The Elf King was deeply worried inside.

"I don't know. It all depends on that human's own fortune. Back then, Marigot gave up after one night inside, and..." The Blazing Flame Dragon King looked at the lava waterfall before him and said casually, "...he only lasted three days and nights."

The next morning, Master Balin's blacksmith shop had its door tightly shut; they weren't open for business.

Today was the deadline; General Holly would come to claim his black mirror armor, but Master Balin hadn't made it at all.

The dwarf father-son pair, Balin and Bahli, had already given up and could only pin their final hopes on Merlin.

Meanwhile, Merlin was sitting on a chair, whittling a wooden stick with a small knife, leaving wood shavings all over the ground. He had actually taken some effort to craft a rough wooden sword.

By the count of time, they should be arriving soon, right?

title: Chapter 9 — A Beating (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 9 — A Beating (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 23 · Chapter 9

Merlin didn't bother lifting his head, going about whittling the wooden sword as if the troublemakers about to show up weren't worth his attention.

But this left the dwarf father and son, Balin and Bari, feeling tense and deeply uneasy, wondering if Merlin had already given up on resistance.

"N... Nether Merlin..." Old dwarf Balin could no longer sit still and ventured a tentative inquiry, "Are you really okay?"

"What problem?" Merlin raised his eyelids, puzzled inside.

...... Old dwarf Balin immediately grew nervous again, wondering if Merlin had forgotten yesterday's solemn promises.

"Merlin-sama, have you forgotten? It's about General Horli coming today to demand the black gold armor..." Dwarf Bari frowned tightly, feeling increasingly that Merlin was unreliable.

"Oh~" Merlin suddenly understood and said calmly, "Is this even considered a problem? I haven't taken it to heart at all."

"Don't be like this! We all believe in you. If you can't produce the finished black gold armor today, those bastards will drag my father out and whip him!" Dwarf Bari said anxiously.

"I'm not even panicked, so why are you panicking?" Merlin didn't look up, continuing to whittle the wooden stick. "Just leave everything to me. Whatever you normally do, keep doing it now. Don't let this weigh on your minds."

"But looking at you like this makes us feel so unsettled..." Dwarf Bari's face turned red with anxiety, looking as if his rear end were on fire.

"What's wrong? Is there something strange about me?" Merlin glanced at the wooden sword in his hands, feeling it was about ready.

"What are you doing? Those bastards will be at our doorstep any moment now, and you don't need to prepare at all?" Dwarf Bari saw Merlin's indifferent attitude and felt a bit angry inside; his father's peace of mind depended entirely on him.

"Are you talking about that?" Merlin waved the wooden sword in his hand and smiled. "This is prepared for that dwarf general. In a moment, I'll use this thing to educate him."

Balin and Bari's faces darkened at once, feeling that Merlin was joking and had no intention of actually helping them.

General Horli at least had an impressive record of merit and was considered a strong figure among the dwarf race. Was Merlin going to take a small wooden stick to teach him a lesson? It was hard to believe.

The two wondered if Merlin didn't realize the seriousness of the situation. General Horli wasn't some childish brat who would admit defeat after getting a few whacks on the rear with a small stick.

"Merlin-sama, please don't make jokes like this." Dwarf Bari couldn't help but stand up. "General Horli is at least a fierce general serving His Majesty the Dwarf King. A wooden sword in your hands is completely useless. Just pick any weapon from our shop — any of them would be a hundred times better than this wooden sword!"

"Is that so? Against a mere dwarf general, a wooden sword is more than enough. Don't worry." Merlin gave a half-smile expression.

Dwarf Bari's face turned dark, finally realizing that Merlin hadn't grasped the situation at all, thinking the illustrious dwarf general was some weakling. Where did he get his confidence from?

Just then, the fairy Phiree flew in from outside in a panic, an anxious expression on her face.

Phiree had run out early that morning to scout the situation outside. Only after learning that General Horli was leading a large force of heavily armored dwarf knights toward them did she return to report.

"They're coming! There are so many dwarf knights heading this way!"

"Father!" Dwarf Bari hurriedly supported the ailing Master Balin and volunteered, "Don't worry, I'll go out and fight them to the death! These bastards who disrespect a blacksmith deserve to die!"

"Don't do that, my child..." Old dwarf Balin sighed and said helplessly, "You'd better stay here obediently. Let me, this old bone, go meet General Horli. I hope Lord Horli will show some mercy and understand my difficulties."

"Tsk." Merlin clicked his tongue, furrowed his brows and blew the wood shavings off the wooden sword. He stood up, swung it twice and nodded with satisfaction, then turned to the dwarf father and son and said—

"Don't make it sound like the end of the world. You stay here obediently."

"I'll go out alone to meet that illustrious dwarf general."

The mighty General Horli, high-ranking and powerful. Relying on his own hard-earned merits, he was second only to the Dwarf King in authority within the Golden City.

His subordinates included 30,000 heavily armored knights, each having undergone rigorous training, well-equipped, and hailed as the elite among foreign military forces.

The dwarf knights were responsible for guarding the safety of the Golden City, and their direct superior was this very General Horli — which also explained why his word carried such weight in the Golden City.

Of course, besides all the praise for Horli, there were also many private criticisms. For instance, Horli took advantage of his brother-in-law being the Dwarf King to commit numerous foolish acts, becoming arrogant and disrespectful throughout the Golden City.

He was also extremely glory-seeking, paying excessive attention to his own reputation, constantly promoting his former days of dominance.

Demanding a complete set of magnificent black gold armor from the finest blacksmith in the Golden City, Master Balin, was precisely for that pitiful vanity — he hoped to appear more impressive in his clansmen's eyes rather than having reached his position solely through nepotistic relationships.

However, yesterday when General Horli heard his subordinates' report and learned that Master Balin had not yet begun forging the black gold armor he demanded after three months —

This made General Horli feel an unprecedented sense of shame. Clearly, Master Balin, relying on being the Golden City's most outstanding blacksmith, hadn't taken him seriously at all!

Throughout the entire Golden City, Master Balin was the first one bold enough to treat General Horli's orders as wind past their ears!

Enraged and shamed, General Horli arrived at dawn with 300 heavily armored dwarf knights to demand answers. If Master Balin couldn't produce the black gold armor, then this proud old man would need to be properly taught a lesson —

Hmph! Damn old Balin! Thinking he's the greatest forging master in the Golden City, so he doesn't put me in his eyes?

This old fellow must learn my methods. I need to make him know my status in the Golden City!

General Horli fumed inwardly, but when he led his knight company to the blacksmith's shop entrance, he found the doors tightly shut, and even the surroundings were desolate and quiet. As the liveliest district in the Golden City, this was clearly abnormal...

General Horli was by nature suspicious. He wondered if old Balin knew he was about to be punished and wanted to ambush him — had he risen in rebellion?

At that moment, with a "creak," the blacksmith shop door opened, and Merlin walked out from inside without a hint of panic, looking at the heavily armored dwarf knights before him who bore down upon them aggressively.

"Hmm?" General Horli frowned atop his earth dragon mount. Looking at Merlin's appearance, he muttered perplexedly, "A commoner? Why is he here? Could it be that old Balin has secretly colluded with commoners behind my back..."

Merlin swept his gaze across the dwarf knights before him. Since dwarves all liked to grow big beards, he felt every dwarf looked the same, so he couldn't help but speak up —

"Who's Horli?"

"I don't like beating around the bush. Whoever is named Horli, step forward and take the beating."

(w --●)?

title: Chapter 9 — Unshakable
content:
Chapter 9 — Unshakable

Volume 23 · Chapter 9

The dwarf knights stared at each other; in the Golden City, it was the first time they had seen such a stubborn fellow.
Even if the knights were dissatisfied, they only muttered complaints in private and absolutely dared not belittle General Holly to his face.
However, seeing Merlin's human appearance, it was obvious he did not belong to the United Kingdom, and it was normal that General Holly's temperament was unknown.
Feeling insulted by Merlin, General Holly's face turned red with anger; he dismounted and stepped out of the crowd, shouting, "Where did this criminal wild dog come from, spouting nonsense here?! How bold!"
Merlin lowered his gaze, looking at the sturdy yet extremely short General Holly, and asked, "You're Holly?"
With a loud "bang," General Holly planted his spiked club firmly on the ground, spreading his hands in an overbearing pose.
Seeing the spiked club smash the ground and crack it, apparently heavy, it was clear this General Holly was a dwarf with some skill.
"That's me!"
"Not hiding in fear shows some spine.... Merlin smiled and continued, 'Master Barin won't forge that black-gold armor for you; give up.'"
"Who said that?" General Holly frowned.
"I did. Master Barin is going to make a weapon for me; you should just step aside." Merlin tried to drive General Holly away.
".... General Holly gave a cold snort, thinking this human's brain might have a problem, 'What are you, an outsider criminal? Tell that old brat Barin to come out and see me! Ignoring my orders is one thing, but you dare to secretly collude with criminals? He should be given a good reflection!'"
"Sorry, Master Barin won't see you; as long as I'm here, I won't let a single hair of Master Barin be harmed." Merlin tapped his shoulder with his wooden sword.
"Hmph! Such a big mouth! A petty criminal dares to run amok in the Golden City?" General Holly blew his beard and glared, not seeing Merlin's strength, instead thinking him a tiresome lunatic.
Although most humans couldn't discern the adventurers' ranks, at least they could sense the pressure.
To General Holly, Merlin seemed weak; his body looked sturdy, but he had no pressure at all.
Combined with Merlin's arrogant words on his lips, General Holly assumed the opponent was just bluffing.
"Since you won't retreat knowing the difficulty, then come and get beaten." Merlin pointed his finger at General Holly, hooking it, openly provoking.
"Damn it! Don't interfere, let me teach this ignorant criminal a lesson!"
General Holly ordered the dwarf knights behind him, intending to duel Merlin and beat him into a pig's head, to show off in front of all the dwarves.
The dwarf knights glanced at each other, then stepped back, clearing space for the duel, ready to watch the general display his might.
General Holly spat on his hands, picked up the spiked club from the ground, and said while cracking his knuckles, "You foreigner probably don't know my glorious exploits—I followed the dwarf king at fourteen, always the bravest vanguard; countless enemies have died by my hand! I've seen plenty of weaklings who only attack with their mouths!"
"Really?" Merlin raised his eyebrows.
"Tch!"
General Holly sank his body, sank his body, expression furious, golden Saint-tier battle aura radiating from within!
Suddenly, he leapt from the ground, using his proud battle technique that had torn through countless legion defenses, invincible!
General Holly wanted to kill Merlin to establish his authority, naturally giving it his all without reservation.
"Die!!!"
"Laughable, on the battlefield you might be like a fish in water, but in a one-on-one you show too many openings!" Merlin bared his teeth in a triumphant grin, swung his wooden sword with lightning speed, and slammed it hard onto General Holly's forehead!
With a sound like knocking a wooden fish, the furious General Holly suddenly sputtered out, painfully shouting as he was flung backward.
"General! General! Are you alright?"
The dwarf knights gathered around, seeing a large bump on General Holly's forehead, it seemed Merlin had not gone easy on him.
General Holly stuck out his tongue, feeling dizzy, everything before him was little stars; he barely regained consciousness.
"Damn! That sword draw was so fast I couldn't see clearly, this criminal... actually played dirty!"
He didn't look that weak at all; he deliberately lured me forward to expose an opening, a cunning human!
General Holly's forehead throbbed painfully; he kept sucking in cold air, heart still racing, he no longer dared to rise— that blow almost took his life! =
"Can you be honest now, General?" Merlin looked at the fallen General Holly with a half-smile.
General Holly, ashamed and angry, trembling all over, shouted at the knights, "What are you standing there for? This criminal threatens Golden City's safety— all together! Kill him!"
"Yes sir!" The dwarf knights lined up, took up their weapons, raised their heavy shields, and roared as they pushed toward Merlin holding his wooden sword, clearly treating him as a formidable foe!
Faced with the swarm of brave dwarf knights charging, the surrounded Merlin let out a soft hum.
Merlin's wooden sword seemed to have eyes; relying on his lightning-fast draw speed, he frequently attacked from extremely tricky angles.
The dwarf knights' armor was extremely sturdy, far surpassing the Purple Orchid Knight Corps, yet under Merlin's blade it seemed as if they wore no armor at all.
The wooden sword made a "whoosh" as it split the air, slipping through the gaps in the dwarf knights' armor and striking their bodies.
At that moment, the charging dwarf knights continually screamed, struck by the wooden sword they fell unconscious one after another!
Merlin became an impregnable fortress; he never moved his feet from start to finish, each dwarf knight that rushed in would inevitably be knocked out by his wooden sword.
……this
General Holly stared, speechless, eyes wide as he watched the knights continually fall, thinking "This... this guy is a monster?!"
Soon, hundreds of dwarf knights collapsed, unconscious, lying in a circle around Merlin.
Yet within a one-meter radius around Merlin, the ground was spotless; the charge of hundreds of dwarf knights could not move him even a step.
The blacksmith's door was secretly opened a crack; the few inside saw the outside scene and were stunned, not knowing what to say to express their feelings at the moment—
Old dwarf Barin: "...What happened? Only a short while and so many have collapsed...."
Dwarf Bari: "So Master Merlin is... this strong?! He's completely different from when he was a kid!"
Fairy Ferri: divination—I feel lucky I didn't die...

title: Chapter 9 — The Dwarf King (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 9 — The Dwarf King (Bonus)

Volume 23 · Chapter 9

Just as the dwarf knights were initially ferocious, in the end they were left with only a dozen after being beaten by Merlin.

They were all frightened by Merlin, and for a moment stood in place, too afraid to advance, looking at their unconscious dwarf companions around them, feeling very panicked.

Merlin lifted his head, looked at the remaining dozen or so dwarves, and tapped his shoulder with a wooden sword, speaking with deep meaning, "How about it? Do you want to continue?"

The remaining dwarf knights couldn't withstand the pressure Merlin exuded, discarded their weapons and shields, and turned in fear to run away— not even wanting to stay a moment longer.

"Come back!" General Holly was furious; his orders had clearly had no effect.

Merlin slowly approached General Holly, pointing the wooden sword at it, "Hey, ..."

"Ah!" General Holly's face turned pale; terrified, he sat on the ground, his whole body trembling, afraid that Merlin would kill him in a fit of anger.

Looking at General Holly, who had been immensely arrogant before but now appeared very embarrassed, Merlin couldn't help but smile, putting away his wooden sword.

"You!" General Holly had never suffered such humiliation? His face flushed red, and he had an air of facing death bravely, "You dare humiliate me like this! Do you know who I am? The Dwarf King is my brother-in-law! You, an outsider, dare to lay hands on me, and you'd better not think of leaving Golden City alive, I won't let you go!"

"Hmm?" Merlin tilted his head, looking down at General Holly with cold eyes.

"Wah! ..... Just go then!" General Holly was terrified by Merlin's gaze, his soul nearly leaving his body; he scrambled up and fled in a sorry state, no longer estimating his tall image.

"Hmph..."

Merlin let out a light hum, turned his head to prepare to return to the smithy.

As for the mixed-up dwarf knights on the ground? They certainly wouldn't dare cause trouble after waking up, being no different from General Holly's sorry state of discarding armor and fleeing.

After seeing that there was no danger outside, Master Barin of the smithy came out, and his gaze at Merlin was no longer the same—it was genuine respect from the heart.

"Mr. Merlin, ..." Old dwarf Barin hesitated to speak but couldn't help asking, "So you are actually a strong person?"

"I never said I was weak. It's entirely your one-sided recognition..." Merlin shrugged his shoulders.

"Mr. Merlin Big Brother! Teach me martial arts!" Dwarf Barin suddenly hugged Merlin's leg, his eyes full of little stars, and directly changed the address. He had always admired strong people, but no one had ever paid attention to this half-baked smith. He never expected that the child saved earlier was actually a terrifyingly powerful expert!

"Get away!" Merlin's face turned dark, and he shoved Barin away, "Be good and inherit your father's business, don't think of random things!"

"Please, Mr. Merlin Big Brother! I also want to learn the sword technique you just used! Steady, accurate, and ruthless, simply flawless!" Dwarf Barin insisted.

"Relax, as long as you chop firewood a hundred million times, persist for ten years, you'll also be strong..." Merlin answered casually.

"???" Dwarf Barin had question marks all over his brain, feeling that Merlin was brushing him off, like a joke?

"You're too amazing, huh?" Fairy Fai flew to Merlin's front, excitedly talking non-stop, "This is completely different from when you were a child! Your child state was really useless!"

"Shut up."

A vein pulsed on Merlin's forehead; he had an urge to crush this fairy to death.

"Mr. Merlin, what are you going to do next? Insulting General Holly, he won't let it rest." Old dwarf Barin showed a worried expression, "And you are an outsider, attacking dwarves in Golden City, it might anger the Dwarf King..."

"What is there to fear?" Merlin paused, speaking nonchalantly, "Before the Dwarf King gets angry with me, I'll go see him first."

"!!!" Old dwarf Barin stared wide-eyed in shock, surprisedly asking, "Why do you want to see Dwarf King...?"

"Why else?" Merlin spread his hand, seriously saying, "To forge Mistint, I need your clan's treasure."

Golden City, the Dwarf King's Palace.

The spacious hall was the work of a renowned craftsman, with a rather imposing shape.

Outside, there were many sculptures of great dwarves, vivid and lifelike.

It was hard to imagine that the short-statured dwarf race would build such a magnificent palace.

At this moment, the Dwarf King was extremely comfortable, indifferent to things outside, and didn't care at all.

The Dwarf King loved treasures, especially the golden crafts he collected; each one was glittering and valuable.

So this dwarf race leader appeared very decadent, never managing Golden City, and had no desire to make the dwarf race prosperous.

To the Dwarf King, collecting all sorts of treasures was much more interesting than anything else; who would want to worry about the affairs of citizens every day?

This led to General Holly doing as he pleased in Golden City, almost reaching the point of almost having heaven under one hand.

At this moment, the Dwarf King had an unkempt beard, wearing a lazy pajama, sitting on his golden throne, holding a gold cup inlaid with precious stones in his hand, carefully wiping the dust on it with a handkerchief.

His eyes were greedy, as if the golden cup in his hand was more important than his own life; he kept breathing on it to wipe it, until he could see his unkempt face, then he nodded in satisfaction.

The Dwarf King felt he was busy every day, almost having no time to rest, similar to the golden cup in his hand, there were many things; he almost had to carefully wipe each one every day to be satisfied.

A dwarf knight walked in from the palace entrance, kneeling on one knee and reporting, "Your Majesty! General Holly requests an audience!"

"Tsk!" The Dwarf King showed a impatient expression; he hated being disturbed while wiping his treasures, so he waved his hand, "Drive him away! Let him come another day!"

"..... The dwarf knight paused, embarrassed, saying, "General Holly seems to have been beaten, his nose swollen and face bruised, and he's still outside crying and making a fuss, saying he won't leave if Your Majesty doesn't see him."

"Despicable! Truly a man's home..." The Dwarf King was angered to roll his eyes; unable to resist the soft and hard tactics, he had to put away his golden cup, "Let him in."

"Yes!"

Not long after, a humiliated General Holly, who had been beaten by Merlin, walked in crying and sobbing, a large bump on his forehead from being hit with a wooden sword.

Seeing the high-and-mighty Dwarf King, General Holly instantly looked like he had seen a relative, "Pfft" knelt on the ground, crying even more miserably.

"Brother-in-law! I was beaten outside, you must avenge me!"

"Shut up!" The Dwarf King frowned, his face ugly, and hurriedly descended from the throne, speaking in a very serious tone—

"I've said it several times, don't call me brother-in-law."

"You look like this weak state, makes me feel ashamed."
