title: Chapter 11 — Initiate a Duel
content:
Chapter 11 — Initiate a Duel

Volume 23 · Chapter 11

“.....General Holly nervously swallowed, nodding like a pecking chicken, 'Yes, brother-in-law, no problem, brother-in-law.'

'Hmph!' The Dwarf King blew on his beard impatiently, 'Always causing trouble and then running to me to clean up the mess. What happened this time?'

'Ahem! Your Majesty, I was beaten outside...' General Holly looked aggrieved, appearing very pitiful.

'In Golden City, someone dared to attack you?' General Holly's tone was skeptical.

'Not our people, but an outsider, a criminal!' General Holly wanted the Dwarf King to vent for him, adding fuel to the fire, 'That bastard is arrogant on our turf. I went to teach him a lesson, and as a result... he narrowly won and almost cracked my skull. Hundreds of knights were also beaten to a pulp. He even claimed that no one in Golden City is his match...'

'Hmm?' The Dwarf King's brows furrowed, 'Is that so?'

'Look at the bump on my head, just got hit!' General Holly pointed to the swelling on his forehead, crying, 'His attitude is so arrogant, he doesn't put our Dwarves in his eyes! No, he clearly doesn't respect you, Your Majesty! A foreign criminal dares to act recklessly in Golden City. If it were me, I'd fight him to the death!'

'Where did this arrogant fool come from, daring to run wild in my Golden City?' The Dwarf King's face darkened, clearly upset by Holly's words.

'I'm not sure, I guess he must be a spy sent by the criminals to gather information about us Dwarves!' General Holly paused, trying to make the situation more serious to get the leaders of other races to unite against Merlin, 'I think other major races are also in danger. Your Majesty, why not unite the nine leaders to exterminate this arrogant criminal spy?'

'His strength is already so terrifying that it requires all leaders to unite to defeat him?' The Dwarf King looked at General Holly, finding it hard to believe.

'Well... I'm just being cautious. That criminal is quite strong, we're on par, but if I were serious, I could definitely crush him. Unfortunately, he's too cunning, hiding his strength and letting me relax, which is why I suffered.' General Holly didn't forget to save face, insisting they were on par, not wanting to look too weak in front of the Dwarf King.

'Is that so?' The Dwarf King pondered, thinking that according to Holly, the criminal's strength wasn't that terrifying, just slightly better than Holly, so he could still handle it.

The glory-seeking General Holly never imagined that his vanity would convey false information to the Dwarf King, nearly ruining his brother-in-law.

'If I fight that criminal, who do you think will win?' The Dwarf King asked cautiously.

General Holly's eyes lit up, unable to hide his joy, thinking his brother-in-law was going to avenge him! He quickly said, 'Who else? Of course, you, brother-in-law!'

'Tsk!' The Dwarf King frowned.

'Ah, no! Of course, Your Majesty!' General Holly corrected himself, flattering, 'Your Majesty's strength is unmatched. You fought on par with the Orc King back then. Which leader in the United Kingdom doesn't respect you? Even the Elf King wouldn't dare to look down on you lightly.'

'Hmm, well said.'

The Dwarf King nodded with satisfaction, feeling flattered by General Holly's praise, becoming a bit overconfident.

He had an idea to use this incident to re-establish his authority as the King of the Dwarves!

He had heard that his subjects privately called him incompetent, unworthy of being the Dwarf King.

Why not take this opportunity to defeat and humiliate a strong criminal, showing all Dwarves...

That he is unworthy, but who is?

Only he has the ability to protect the people from danger!

The Dwarf King smiled, planning to make a big show of it, with all Dwarves watching.

'Where is that criminal? Take me to him. I will issue a challenge in the name of the Dwarf King! Tell him the dignity of the Dwarves is sacred and inviolable!'

'I've been waiting for this! He's at Master Balin's forge.'

General Holly was eager to go with him for revenge, 'Your Majesty, please change into your armor and follow me...'

But before he finished, a voice suddenly echoed in the empty palace —

'Are you looking for me?'

The Dwarf King and General Holly were shocked. The sudden voice meant someone had sneaked into the palace!

e) CEz小 治

On the golden throne of the Dwarf King, Merlin sat casually, with a half-smile on his face.

With Merlin's abilities, even if the palace defenses were impenetrable, he could easily bypass them and sneak in undetected.

'Ah?!' General Holly almost fainted, shouting in panic, 'It's him! Guards! Guards! There's an intruder!'

The doors burst open, and a group of spear-wielding Dwarf knights rushed in, protecting the Dwarf King.

Seeing the intruder sitting on the golden throne — a sign of disrespect and contempt for the leader — they were enraged and ready to kill him.

'Wait!'

The Dwarf King stopped them, not allowing the knights to attack.

Though he looked calm, he was seething inside.

The golden throne was his treasure, and he hated others touching it...

But to use this criminal to re-establish his authority, he needed to show leadership.

The Dwarf King glared at Merlin, saying in a low voice,

'Are you the criminal running wild in Golden City?'

Merlin thought for a moment and replied, 'Yeah... I guess?'

'What do you mean "I guess"?' General Holly, emboldened by the Dwarf King's presence, spoke more confidently, 'It's you, you bastard! Daring to cause trouble on our turf? You're dead!'

'Tsk! I should have cut your tongue out earlier...' Merlin frowned, finding General Holly too noisy.

'Uh!' General Holly quickly shut up, trembling behind the Dwarf King, not daring to breathe.

'Hmph!' The Dwarf King snorted angrily, 'Since you dare appear before me, I admit you have courage, but you're too confident. Golden City is not your backyard, you can't come and go as you please!'

'Oh? What do you want to do then...' Merlin rested his head, asking lazily. He came to get the golden essence, but the Dwarf King seemed to hate him.

'This is my territory. I could call my army to kill you here, but I won't use numbers to bully you — that would tarnish my reputation!' The Dwarf King raised his head proudly, 'You injured my people in my city. I can't let that go. I challenge you to a one-on-one duel in the name of the Dwarf King!'

'???' Merlin paused, raising his eyebrows, 'Wait! A one-on-one duel with me? Are you serious?'

(正_工)

title: Chapter 12 — Hall of the Ancestral Dragon (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 12 — Hall of the Ancestral Dragon (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 23 · Chapter 12

Can't blame Merlin for thinking the dwarf king was joking; issuing such a formal duel challenge to himself was the first time.
This left Merlin feeling quite conflicted, with a vague impression that the opponent's courage was commendable—as if they could fight until the sky darkened and the earth grew dim?
“Do you think I'm joking? To protect my people, I will defeat you with my own hands!” the dwarf king said passionately, though inside he was feeling quite smug, thinking, “Cool! I’ve wanted to say this line for a long time but never had the chance. Surely what happened in the palace today will soon spread through every street and alley of Golden City? Then all the dwarves will surely feel proud to have such an excellent king as me! Feeling fresh and clean~”
“.....Merlin wiped off his grin, thinking that since the opponent was so serious, he couldn't be too playful, so he rose from the golden throne and said, “Sure, I accept your challenge!”
“Good! Then”
“Wait a moment!”
The dwarf king had intended to say where the duel would take place, but Merlin interrupted him, asking, “What are you doing? You're not scared, are you? Really just all show and no substance....”
“I'm not afraid; it's just that a duel with no stake is meaningless, and I have no interest in it.” Merlin lowered his gaze at the dwarf king, speaking seriously, “If I lose this duel, I will personally cut off my head and offer it to you—so... what will you wager?”
“I..... The dwarf king hesitated, then suddenly recalled Holly saying that this criminal's strength was comparable to his own, and winning with his own strength would be absurdly easy, so he burst into loud laughter, “Hahaha! Good! If I lose, I'll also cut off my head and give it to you”
5 SE this little news.
“Hmph, you're really overestimating your own head~” Merlin couldn't help teasing, having absolutely no interest in the dwarf king's head.
“What do you mean!?” the dwarf king glared at Merlin, gritting his teeth.
“My head could fetch a good sum at the Holy Church, while yours isn't worth a penny—this is utterly unequal.” Merlin shook his head.
“Then what do you want? I'll bet with you!” the dwarf king said angrily.
“I've heard that your dwarf race possesses a supreme treasure, the golden essence, and I want that... Merlin revealed his ulterior motive, entirely aimed at obtaining that rare material.”
“How did you know that?!” the dwarf king exclaimed in shock, “Few people know about the golden essence, and you've figured it out?!”
“Don't worry about that—just tell me whether you're willing to wager the golden essence in this duel; my life for your people's treasure, and you'd definitely profit~” Merlin very much hoped the dwarf king would agree, so he could justifiably obtain the first material for forging Mistartin.
The dwarf king lowered his head, hesitating for a moment, not answering quickly, because the golden essence is a treasure encountered once in ten thousand years, more precious than the entire Golden City.
Using it as a wager seems a bit frivolous; the dwarf king was a bit worried about slipping up in the gutter—if something went wrong, wouldn't he be handing over his treasure?
“The Holly general sitting behind couldn't stay still; his mind was full of hoping the dwarf king would avenge him, so he couldn't help stepping forward and whispering, “Your Majesty, bet with him! This guy's strength.... is just about that; who are you? You are the wise and mighty dwarf king! How could you fear a mere criminal? This is your chance to display your divine might!”’”
“....The dwarf king furrowed his brows in deep thought, carefully sizing up Merlin, feeling that this duel was a sure win for him, impossible to lose; even if he verbally wagered the golden essence as a stake, what of it? Since the opponent couldn't possibly beat him anyway, “Good! I agree—if I lose, I'll give you the golden essence!”
“Excellent!” Merlin felt secretly delighted, clapped his hands, and said, “I have a bit of admiration for you....”
“Cut the nonsense! Tomorrow at the duel arena in Golden City, all the dwarves will come to watch; I'll make you lose face in front of everyone!” The dwarf king clenched his fists, already itching to try.
“? ? ?” Merlin stared blankly, thinking he'd have to duel in front of everyone's eyes—this little dwarf isn't giving him any way out.
The dwarf king watched Merlin's dazed, foolish expression, thinking his aura would overwhelm him, and thought—
“Hmph! Just wait to commit suicide in front of all the dwarves, you foolish criminal....”
At the Ancestral Dragon Temple, when Alice resolutely jumped into the magma waterfall, she thought she would soon endure the pain of being burned by flames.
But the result was completely unlike her imagination; when Alice opened her eyes again, the scene before her had entirely changed into something else.
The rolling scorching magma vanished, replaced by a pitch-black world, with only one point of light—a blazing torch tower!
In the darkness, the continually swaying firelight appeared especially warm, drawing people constantly toward it....
Alice realized that the terrifying magma outside, like hell, was merely an illusion, causing the timid to shrink back and dare not enter.
Those who dare to leap into the magma all possess a certain amount of courage and bravery; the simple illusion directly screens out those truly

title: Chapter 13 — White Dragon
content:
Chapter 13 — White Dragon

Volume 23 · Chapter 13

The torch's flames burned fiercely, yet they couldn't illuminate this place at all!

In the distance, countless eyes suddenly lit up, looking extremely eerie, and an ominous aura rushed forth.

Alice instinctively took a step back, her back against the icy wall of the torch tower, vigilantly observing her surroundings.

"Who?!"

Alice tried to figure out who was in the darkness, but there was no response. Instead, she heard waves of chilling, mocking laughter.

The flames atop the torch tower suddenly changed, replaced by eerie blue ghostly flames, as if she had instantly been transported to the entrance of hell.

What's happening?! Why is the dragon tribe's sacred site so terrifying?! It's more like a place where the undead reside.....

Alice's cheeks were illuminated by the ghostly flames, her anxious emotions written all over her face. She felt like there was something terrifying present here.

After the flames turned into blue ghostly flames, the terrifying existences in the distance seemed to no longer hold back, gradually revealing their forms.

They had varied shapes, soaring through the sky, constantly flapping their illusory dragon wings.

Countless sharp, crimson pupils stared greedily at Alice below, accurately speaking, they were craving fresh flesh.

Innumerable souls of ancient dragons, they weren't artificial ancient dragons created by necromancers, but the purest of souls!

The dragon tribe's ancestors didn't fall into hell after death. Instead, thanks to the power of the Ancestral Dragon Temple, their souls achieved immortality!

The ancient dragons' souls had been trapped in this temple for countless years, they were frantic, in pain, and enraged, having long since lost patience with the dull years, hoping to seize a living body to escape this hellhole, even if it wasn't a giant dragon's body!

"........" Alice's face turned pale as she watched the ancient dragon souls swirling in the sky, feeling unprecedented fear from the bottom of her heart!

The ancient dragon souls seemed gigantic, yet they were like wisps of blue smoke, without any physical form. Their overwhelming pressure intersected, like a god gazing down at all living things, no one would dare to resist.

No way! These guys aren't benevolent! Staying here any longer... is certain death!

Alice realized the danger before her and made up her mind to escape immediately.

In the blink of an eye, Alice transformed into the Frost Saint Dragon amidst the blizzard, flapping her dragon wings to take to the sky!

Alice used all her strength, trying to break through the ancient dragon souls above, escaping this terrifying temple.

However, the ancient dragon souls let out mocking laughter, as if they had anticipated Alice's reaction.

"She thinks she can leave?

"Impossible!"

"Leave this young body behind!"

"Give it to me! I've been trapped here until I'm about to go mad! Eight equals two!"

The ancient dragon souls swarmed out, diving down to form a massive net, blocking any escape.

They rushed towards the Frost Saint Dragon like starving ghosts who hadn't eaten in years!

"Ah!"

The Frost Saint Dragon was startled by the terrifying ancient dragon souls charging towards her.

So she gritted her teeth, her dragon wings flapping wildly as she unleashed her strongest dragon skill, Ice River Descent!

A brilliant white light burst forth, the Frost Saint Dragon becoming like a sun in this dark world, dazzlingly bright!

Everything in the light's path was frozen, transformed into beautiful golden ice sculptures.

No matter how agile one's movements, it would be impossible to fly under such a large-scale magic spell!

However, these ancient dragon souls without physical form weren't afraid of the Frost Saint Dragon's attack, completely unaffected.

Souls are mysterious substances, usually unaffected by magic. Even the Holy Church's priests' simple exorcism spells would be more effective than "Ice River Descent."

The ancient dragon souls took this opportunity to crazily burrow into the Frost Saint Dragon's body, all wanting to seize this body for themselves.

The Frost Saint Dragon's mind fell into chaos, suddenly hearing countless voices in her head, their quarreling almost making her brain explode.

"She's mine!

"No! Mine! Get out of my way!

"I want out! This body is mine!

"Don't even think about it! This is my possession!"

The quarreling voices echoed in her mind, the Frost Saint Dragon suffering terribly, letting out a mournful cry as she plummeted from the sky.

"Ahhhhhh!"

The Frost Saint Dragon crashed to the ground, her dragon skeleton shattering everywhere. She rolled in agony, eventually transforming back into Alice's form and fainting.

SF lost small play

However, the ancient dragon souls still hadn't stopped quarreling, none willing to yield, unable to occupy this body.

At this moment, a warm white light suddenly appeared in the distant darkness, spreading outward, trying to dispel the evil spirits.

The ancient dragon souls seemed unable to endure the warm white light, beginning to wail and complain.

"Damn it! It's here!"

"It's ruining my plans again!"

"That bastard should be killed!"

The wailing continued as the ancient dragon souls transformed into wisps of blue smoke, constantly escaping from Alice's body, fearing the warm white light would reduce them to ashes.

Ignoring the escaping souls, they continued to curse, expressing their anger, yet were helpless, not daring to approach.

The warm white light gradually dissipated, revealing a massive dragon that could only emit light in the darkness, its gaze gentler than the other ancient dragons.

Its body was enormous, its golden dragon horns extremely eye-catching, its pale dragon whiskers dangling to the ground, looking like an old grandfather.

This white dragon's wings were very special, not like normal dragon membranes, but pure light wings, as if composed entirely of elements. It was probably the light from these wings that had just dispersed the ancient dragon souls.

The white dragon lowered its head to examine the unconscious Alice, drawn to the pendant around her neck.

It couldn't help but reach out, using its claw tips to pull the pendant from Alice's neck....

The white dragon looked at the pendant in its palm, especially the Spanish royal crest on the back, its calm gaze changing slightly.

"Nidhöggr's ritual....

In the center of the Golden City, the dueling arena was bustling with people, colorful flags fluttering!

A series of polite, thunderous sounds echoed, white smoke lingering in the air.

This place was usually used to select the dwarf tribe's warriors, but today was different from usual.

Yesterday, a criminal had rewarded the dwarf tribe with three hundred knights. The usually incompetent Dwarf King, unexpectedly wanting to protect his people, had decided to duel this criminal who was running amok in the Golden City!

The dwarves all thought the sun was rising in the west, the Dwarf King wasn't completely useless after all. At a critical moment, he was willing to stand up and protect his people.

A prodigal son returning is worth more than gold, although the Dwarf King usually seemed foolish, this time, the vast majority of dwarves hoped their leader would win, defeating the despicable criminal and letting the dwarf tribe regain some dignity!

The Dwarf King had spent the entire night preparing for this duel, proclaiming everywhere that he was fighting to protect the dwarf tribe, showing himself to be a responsible leader.

In just one night, the Golden City was like a grand festival, dwarves spreading the word about the Dwarf King's virtue of not bullying the weak in the palace, and his intention to duel the criminal fairly.

The entire Golden City was jubilant, almost all dwarves gathering at the dueling arena, cheering for their leader.

They all hoped to see the arrogant criminal being beaten into a pulp by the Dwarf King.....

title: Chapter 14 — High Spirits (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 14 — High Spirits (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 23 · Chapter 14

The dueling arena was packed to capacity, with dwarves constantly cheering for their king and rallying behind their leader!

In truth, the dwarf race was a brave and formidable people, and most of them were粗犷 fellows with fiery tempers.

The dwarf king was going to engage in a fair one-on-one duel against a sinner, without using his authority to suppress the outcome.

To many dwarves, this made the dwarf king seem like a righteous and battle-hungry leader.

In the audience stands of the dueling arena, the dwarf blacksmith father and son had also come to watch. Although Merlin had defeated General Holly, neither of them had any certainty about whether he could defeat the even more powerful dwarf king.

Last night, after Merlin returned, he told Baly and Balin about his upcoming duel with the dwarf king, explaining that if he lost, he would offer his head to the dwarf king as compensation.

This terrified the father-son pair, making them feel that Merlin was playing with fire — agreeing to such a dangerous duel?

The two couldn't make heads or tails of Merlin anymore, unable to tell whether he truly had the ability or was simply overconfident to the point of recklessness.

General Holly was not even on the same level as the dwarf king. While not every one of the nine great clan leaders was skilled in combat, the dwarf king was still one of the more capable fighters among the nine.

General Holly? He was nothing compared to the leaders of the great clans — barely worthy of a minor command.

Balin even had doubts about whether Merlin's confidence had inflated because Holly was weak, to the point that he no longer regarded the dwarf king as a threat.

"Father, do you think Brother Merlin can defeat His Majesty the dwarf king?" the young dwarf Bal asked worriedly.

"....." The old dwarf Balin lowered his head, thought for a moment, and said, "It's difficult. Although Merlin's strength is no small feat, defeating His Majesty the dwarf king will be very hard. How strong was the orc king?"

"Of course!" Bal answered without hesitation. "Especially the former orc king Sarit, who dared to challenge the elf king head-on! That was terrifying...."

"I once heard that our dwarf king once had a dispute with Sarit and they fought once. Although His Majesty lost, Sarit didn't win easily, which shows that His Majesty is no less formidable than Sarit...." The old dwarf Balin looked at his son. "What do you think? Can Mr. Merlin win?"

"........" After hearing his father's words, Bal's resolve began to waver, feeling that winning this duel would be extremely difficult for Merlin, and he might very well lose his life in the process.

"His Majesty could easily use his army to crush Mr. Merlin, yet he chose open duel instead. I have a feeling this is a trap designed by His Majesty, perhaps to demonstrate his martial prowess to the tribe and suppress the negative opinions that have persisted for a long time...." Having dealt with the dwarf king before, the old dwarf Balin felt this was quite possible.

"Isn't Brother Merlin in great danger then? In a way, if it weren't to help us punish General Holly, why would Brother Merlin anger the dwarf king in the first place?" Bal felt guilty, wondering whether they should try to stop this duel. But looking around at the highly energized dwarves, he sensed that preventing it might be nearly impossible.

"I don't know what Mr. Merlin is thinking. I persuaded him for a long time last night, but he insisted on participating in this duel."

The old dwarf Balin sighed deeply, feeling as though he himself had led Merlin into danger. Initially, he had only agreed to accept Merlin's help so that he wouldn't suffer General Holly's punishment, but he never expected things to escalate to this uncontrollable point.

"What's there to worry about? This guy said himself he's fine with it, so he must be! " the fairy Phairy perched on Bal's head, believing that Merlin must have some trump card if he wasn't afraid of anything — otherwise, what difference would there be from a dumb goose marching to its death? After getting to know him for so long, Phairy felt Merlin wasn't a fool.

"Really? Don't you know how formidable our clan leader is?" Bal frowned.

"I trust my instincts!" Phairy said with nose held high.

On the eastern side of the dueling arena stood the dwarf king's exclusive viewing platform, where he could watch the duel.

At this moment, the dwarf king sat in his chair, looking out over the bustling arena where everyone was cheering his name, unable to hold back a smile of smug satisfaction.

He was very pleased with the current situation — almost all the dwarves had come to watch him display his might. He felt his entire sleepless night of planning had been worth it.

For the first time, the dwarf king felt truly loved and admired by his people. He began wondering whether he should hold more duels in the future to showcase his strength.

"Brother-in-law?" General Holly approached with a grin.

"Hmm?" The dwarf king rolled his eyes.

"Ah! Forgive me, Your Majesty." Holly quickly corrected himself, rubbing his hands together. "How is Your Majesty feeling?"

"Excellent! I can hardly wait to twist that sinner's head off!" the dwarf king said in his gruff temperament.

"The arrangements for the duel are complete. We can begin shortly...." Holly said seriously.

"Let's go, I'm already impatient...." The dwarf king stood up and spread his arms wide.

Then a group of dwarf knights walked up from behind carrying heavy armor forged from orichalcum, to dress the dwarf king.

Orichalcum was a rarer metal than black gold, possessing strong defensive properties — it was difficult to melt even under dragon breath.

It was clear the dwarf king had spared no effort for this duel against Merlin.

Clad in the magnificent orichalcum heavy armor, the dwarf king appeared radiant, like a seasoned general who had ridden across battlefields for years.

Immediately after, a burly dwarf knight staggered forward carrying a pitch-black warhammer. He was panting heavily and drenched in sweat, each step a struggle — it was hard to imagine just how heavy the hammer was.

This warhammer was so heavy that even a strong dwarf could barely lift it, yet it was the dwarf king's beloved treasure, forged from a single piece of meteoric iron that could split mountains and shatter boulders with ease!

Although the meteoric iron hammer hadn't yet reached the level of a pseudo-divine artifact, it was very close. A single strike from it would be instantly fatal!

The dwarf king lifted the meteoric iron warhammer with one hand and leaped down from the platform, landing in the dueling arena.

Clad in golden armor, wielding the black hammer, he looked every bit the god of war confident of victory — the center of all attention in the arena!

The dwarf king, full of vigor, raised his meteoric warhammer high and let out a earth-shaking roar!

The dwarves in the stands seemed to feel some kind of summons, rising to their feet one by one, raising their arms and stomping heavily, emitting rhythmic guttural sounds from their throats in response —

"Ho! Ho! Ho! Ho! Du...."

This was the dwarven ritual for expressing excitement, practiced since ancient times. Being a warlike people, they loved to shout in triumph when roused!

Hearing everyone cheering, the dwarf king's excitement reached its peak. He shook his thick beard and roared to his people —

"That sinner dared to come onto our land and run wild, injuring our knights!

"As your leader, I will never let him go! I will make that arrogant sinner learn the power of the dwarf race!"

"Soon I will use this hammer in my hand to smash his skull to bits!"

"My people, are you excited?!?"

title: Chapter 15 — Serious Duel
content:
Chapter 15 — Serious Duel

Volume 23 · Chapter 15

"Ho! Ho! Ho! Ho! Ho..."

The dwarves continuously let out thunderous cheers, demonstrating their excitement through their actions.

They kept stomping their feet on the ground, causing the entire arena to tremble, and the atmosphere reached its peak.

The Dwarf King spread his arms wide, listening to his people's cheers, and seemed to be thoroughly enjoying himself, thinking to himself—

Great! As long as I defeat that criminal next, my prestige will soar to unprecedented heights!

Who will still dare to call me incompetent behind my back then?

Rumble, rumble, the thick stone gate opposite the Dwarf King slowly opened, and Merlin walked into the arena with a wooden sword in hand.

Merlin looked around and found that the spectator seats were packed, with the dwarves appearing extremely excited, far exceeding his expectations.

Hmm? I didn't expect the Dwarf King to make such a big show of this? Is he planning to use me as a stepping stone?

Merlin wore a composed smile on his face and, mimicking the dwarves, waved to them—

"I'm the guy who beat up 300 dwarf knights. If any of you have placed bets, remember to bet on me winning, or you'll lose badly. I'm about to beat the Dwarf King so badly he'll be picking his teeth off the ground. Are you excited?"

Looking at Merlin's demeanor, he didn't seem the least bit nervous and appeared to be enjoying the heated atmosphere of the arena, frequently interacting with the audience.

It seems this show-off Merlin, if he didn't become an adventurer, might be more suited to being a star gladiator in the Holy Roman Colosseum.

"Tch!" The Dwarf King's face instantly darkened, gnashing his teeth as he glared at Merlin, thinking, What an arrogant bastard, just wait and see how you'll be begging for mercy later, it'll be useless!

The dwarves in the spectator seats heard Merlin's words and immediately erupted into a chorus of boos, with some even giving him the thumbs down, shouting out contemptuous remarks—

"Wait for your death, criminal!"

"Kill him! See how arrogant he'll be then!"

"Your Majesty, go out and conquer! Leave nothing standing!"

The dwarves were not friendly towards Merlin, hoping from the bottom of their hearts that the Dwarf King would teach this criminal a good lesson and greatly boost the prestige of the dwarf tribe!

Wave after wave of contemptuous voices made Merlin frown, and he felt somewhat disappointed after preparing for so long.

"Sigh, is there no one welcoming me?"

At this moment, Bali and Fairy in the spectator seats couldn't sit still anymore and stood up, shouting encouragement to Merlin at the top of their lungs!

In the midst of the overwhelming majority of dwarves hoping for Merlin's defeat, the voices of these two small figures stood out awkwardly.

"Take down the Dwarf King! If you lose, I'll look down on you!!!" The fairy Fairy shouted with all her might, her voice surprisingly loud despite her small size.

"Brother Merlin, go all out and show everyone!" The dwarf Bali cheered with raised arms.

"... " Old dwarf Balin wasn't so impulsive, and in his heart, he still had some concerns about Merlin.

Merlin heard Bali and Fairy's voices and waved towards their direction, "Don't worry!"

"Hmph! Where does your confidence come from? Don't tell me you still think you can win?" The Dwarf King couldn't help but mock Merlin's confident appearance.

"It's not confidence, it's certainty that I will win." Merlin replied with a faint smile.

"Ridiculous! Do you think I'm like Holly? I am the Dwarf King, one of the nine leaders of the United Kingdom! You may have easily defeated Holly, but you won't have it easy against me!" The Dwarf King sneered.

"Whether I can gain an advantage or not will be clear after we fight, won't it?" Merlin retorted.

"Then come on!" The Dwarf King stomped his foot fiercely, assuming an attacking stance, "I'll make you understand how foolish it is to be my enemy!"

"Wait a minute!" Merlin suddenly stopped him.

"What? Scared? It's too late to beg for mercy now..." The Dwarf King sneered.

"I'm not begging for mercy, I just think our wager should be announced publicly, don't you think? It's a rare opportunity to have so many people bear witness..." Merlin said meaningfully, worried that the Dwarf King wouldn't acknowledge the debt, planning to push this stubborn fool into a corner where he couldn't back down. If all these dwarves knew about the wager, it would be difficult for the Dwarf King to welch on the bet, making him appear untrustworthy in the eyes of his people.

"Hah! Do you want to be utterly humiliated? Fine! I'll grant your wish!" The Dwarf King, confident in his victory, felt he had nothing to lose and wouldn't possibly give away the Golden Essence, so he loudly declared, "My people! This duel concerns the dignity of the dwarf tribe! If I lose, I'll give this criminal our tribe's treasure, the Golden Essence! I'll abide by the wager, no regrets!"

As soon as he spoke, the dwarves in the spectator seats began to buzz with discussion. They had thought it was just an ordinary duel, but they didn't expect the stakes to be so high!

The Golden Essence was the treasure of the dwarf tribe, something ordinary people might not see in their entire lives!

It was something the dwarves had discovered by chance while mining for gold, and using it as a wager seemed a bit too casual.

However, most dwarves were merely shocked and didn't react too strongly, as they believed the Dwarf King could easily win.

"No wonder Mr. Merlin insisted on participating in this duel, it turns out he was after the Golden Essence..." Old dwarf Balin suddenly understood why Merlin was so persistent.

"Brother Merlin really wants to forge that Mistiltein, Father, can you do it?" Dwarf Bali asked.

"Don't make it sound so easy, the materials for forging Mistiltein are a huge obstacle. Even if Mr. Merlin gets the Golden Essence, there are still two other materials, and getting them will be even more difficult..." Old dwarf Balin frowned with worry.

"Are you satisfied now?" The Dwarf King looked at Merlin.

"Mm, not bad. Then if I lose, I'll give you my head." Merlin nodded in satisfaction.

"No need, because during the duel, I'll smash your head to pieces!" The Dwarf King revealed an excited expression.

"You're quite eager to kill, Dwarf King..." Merlin swung the wooden sword in his hand, pointing it at the Dwarf King, "Make your move."

The Dwarf King saw the wooden sword in Merlin's hand and was taken aback for a moment before flying into a rage, "A wooden sword? Are you mocking me? Bring out your real weapon!"

"This wooden sword is enough to deal with you." Merlin tilted his head.

"You bastard!"

The Dwarf King's eyes blazed with anger, feeling his dignity had been challenged like never before!

The opponent was using a wooden sword, and even if he won, it would be a hollow victory, with the suspicion of bullying the weak.

What would his people think of him then? They'd say he only won against a human wielding a wooden sword, something he couldn't even boast about, and he wouldn't be able to refute it!

He absolutely couldn't give this criminal any excuses! He had to win convincingly!

The Dwarf King slammed his meteoric iron hammer into the ground, causing a deafening boom that shattered the earth of the arena, with magma visibly churning beneath the surface!

All the dwarves swayed with the shock, barely managing to steady themselves before staring at the terrifying cracks in the ground in stunned silence.

The Dwarf King gripped his meteoric iron hammer tightly, letting out an angry roar towards Merlin.

"Bring out your real weapon, criminal!!"

"... "

Merlin's expression turned cold as he looked at the Dwarf King's serious demeanor, took a deep breath, and closed his eyes.

He casually tossed the wooden sword aside, drew the demon sword Banri Garan from his waist, and held it across his chest. When he opened his eyes again, they were equally serious—

"This is what you asked for, don't blame me..."
