title: Chapter 16 — Drawing the Sword to Shave
content:
Chapter 16 — Drawing the Sword to Shave

Volume 23 · Chapter 16

"Hmph!" the Dwarf King snorted coldly, seeing Merlin become much more serious, he felt satisfied inside, his whole body itching to try, "One move! - - one move and I will end this duel!"
"This.... Merlin slowly gripped the hilt of the demon sword Banri Garan, replying, "I will return it to you exactly as it was."
"At this point, still spouting nonsense? Go to hell and reflect well, criminal!!!"
The Dwarf King roared angrily, the ground beneath his feet cracked, stones flew, the pale gold battle aura of the sect burst forth like a floodgate opened from his small stature!
Wielding a meteoric iron hammer and clad in orichalcum armor, he resembled a war god on earth!
One cannot help but admire the dwarves' excellent equipment; at this moment the Dwarf King seemed to have no weakness whatsoever!
Even though the formerly brave and warlike dwarves have become history, one can still glimpse the ancient era on the Dwarf King, showing how valiant the dwarven race is!
The Dwarf King's face full of anger, his short legs stomped the ground, actually erupting with unimaginable huge force! The earth split apart, as if a carpet were being pulled behind him!
Merlin watched the Dwarf King's fierce assault with a blank expression; before the attack even arrived, the terrifying gust like a blade swooshed past, slicing off a few strands of his hair.
The Dwarf King came back with overwhelming momentum, the meteoric iron hammer dragging behind him, scattering scorching sparks!
"Hya!!!"
All that could be heard was the Dwarf King's earth‑shaking roar as he lifted the already friction‑reddened meteoric iron hammer from below upward....
Boom! Flames shot up instantly! The tremendous explosion deafened!
The flames and shockwave thrown up by the explosion made the dwarves watching on either side hold their breath; the Dwarf King's attack terrified them to the point of scalp numbness.
The dwarves trembled all over; although they usually gossiped about the Dwarf King in private, no one would doubt his strength!
The entire dueling field was shrouded in the fire and heat from the explosion; the Dwarf King wished he could tear the whole arena apart!
General Holly watched the Dwarf King from afar, flashing a hint of smug smile: "Brother‑in‑law is invincible! Haha! You wretched criminal, now you know you were wrong, huh?!"
...The elf Feyri stared agape, unable to speak.
"Merlin big brother!" Dwarf Barl leapt to his feet, anxiously gazing at the center of the dueling field.
"...Old Dwarf Barin sighed deeply, feeling great pity for Merlin.
The flames of the explosion dissipated; before the Dwarf King lay a scene of utter devastation, only a huge pit with rising sparks remained.
Merlin? He had long since vanished without a trace, likely shattered into fragments by the Dwarf King's attack, not even leaving bone fragments.
"Hahaha!" The Dwarf King gazed at the huge pit before him, laughing unrestrainedly, raising his meteoric iron hammer high to express his present delight: "Woo‑ho!!!"
In the stands, the dwarves awoke as from a dream, rising to cheer their leader, with rhythmic stomping sounds echoing again.
They were subdued by the Dwarf King's mighty strength; although this leader always had many flaws, possessing the power to protect the tribe made him a trustworthy chief—
"Ho! Ho! Ho! Ho!..
"Ha ha! Woo‑ho! Woo‑ho‑ho!" The Dwarf King beamed with joy, basking in the cheers and praise of his people, immersed in the happiness of victory, thinking everything went according to plan—that this criminal paid the price for his arrogance!
However, just when everyone thought the duel was over, a mocking voice suddenly rang out—
"You're getting happy a bit too early, Dwarf King! Heart Sr ...?"
"What!?"
The Dwarf King turned pale with shock, never expecting Merlin to dodge his previous attack!
By rights he should already be dead; with the opponent's strength, how could he manage this?!
Unprepared, the Dwarf King didn't turn back; the first thing he saw wasn't Merlin, but a long blade covered in rust and nicks!
Merlin's eyes flashed with ruby‑like fiery light, without the slightest hesitation he stepped forward and delivered a draw‑cut slash!
The demon sword Banri Garan unleashed an unstoppable killing aura, its overwhelming force aiming straight at the Dwarf King's head as it came down.
The Dwarf King's mind went blank; his whole being was dazed by Merlin's lightning counterattack, forgetting to defend.
He swore this was the strongest sword aura he had ever felt in this life, as if he were being torn apart countless times!
At that moment, fear welled up from the depths of his heart, taking over....
"Eeeeeeeeeeeee!!!"
The Dwarf King involuntarily let out a cry unbefitting a leader from his throat, his eyeballs nearly popping out of their sockets, as if he might be scared to death at any moment?
He realized he was surely doomed, impossible to survive such a terrifying draw‑cut.
The Dwarf King felt a twinge of regret, only wanting to prove himself to his people by picking a soft persimmon to crush, but instead he kicked an iron plate; the opponent's strength was undoubtedly superior to his own!
In that flash of lightning and stone, Merlin oddly curled the corner of his mouth, while the demon sword Banri Garan hovered above the Dwarf King's head.
At that moment, the nick‑filled blade was only about two centimeters from the Dwarf King's forehead!
Merlin needed only to twitch his wrist slightly, and the Dwarf King would be cleaved in two, dying on the spot!
But Merlin did not do so; looking at the Dwarf King's dazed expression, he teased meaningfully: "I won't kill you, for if I did, who would fulfill our wager? You were lucky to snatch back a life—feel genuine joy from the depths of your heart..."
.... The Dwarf King's astonished expression froze on his face, bloodless, lips trembling unable to speak, gazing at the sword hanging over his head like the Sword of Damocles, feeling as if he had brushed past death.
A crisp sound—
—a crisp crack, the orichalcum‑forged helmet on the Dwarf King's head shattered instantly, splitting in half and falling to the ground.
His formerly thick hair also blew away in the wind, turning into a comical Mediterranean‑style bald look!
"I gave you a new haircut, Your Majesty Dwarf King—do you like it?" Merlin smiled, having used the draw‑cut to shave his head; the Dwarf King was the first in history to receive such a treatment.
.... The Dwarf King came to his senses, the wind blowing over his scalp felt chilly, he sensed he had suffered a great humiliation: "You cheated! I didn't lose! I refuse to accept it! ..."
Rumble—
The dueling field shook violently, a thunder‑like roar causing all the dwarves to panic.
Outside Golden City, that towering mine was sliced through the waist and then collapsed with a roar!
No need to guess—it must be the aftershock of Merlin's draw‑cut that destroyed the distant mine!
In the dueling field, not a sound was heard; the dwarves' gazes all turned to Merlin, eyes showing awe and bewilderment—no one imagined this criminal's power could be so terrifying!
They had no choice but to accept the reality that their leader had been crushed by the criminal, utterly defeated!
"Good heavens, this..." The elf Feyri's expression went blank, her words incoherent.
"Merlin big brother, this is simply too terrifying..." Dwarf Barl prostrated himself in admiration of Merlin.
"No wonder there's no flaw..." Old Dwarf Barin sighed, growing ever more curious about Merlin.
"See... far off, General Holly sat on his butt on the ground, muttering blankly, 'Brother‑in‑law lost, so... is it too late to beg for mercy now?'"
Merlin remained expressionless, coldly tapping the Dwarf King's face with his blade, "Anything else you want to say?"
".I"
The Dwarf King shuddered, his expression turning sorrowful and indignant, tears welling in his eyes.
Seeing the towering mine sliced in half, he had already been utterly convinced by Merlin!
He could never achieve such a feat himself; the opponent was clearly holding back, sparing his life!
One move to end the duel? Indeed just one move—but the loser is me!
If I had known it would turn out like this, why would I have made such a fuss over the duel? I've lost all face....
The Dwarf King lost all face before his people, suffering heavy loss; his legs went weak and he knelt on the ground, tears streaming down, gnashing his teeth as he said:
"I lost!"
Already after 48 hours I will sleep for hours
Tonight I will try taking half a sleeping pill to see if I can sleep....

title: Chapter 17 — The Time-Tested Dragonblood Fighter
content:
Chapter 17 — The Time-Tested Dragonblood Fighter

Volume 23 · Chapter 17

In the pitch-black Ancestral Dragon Temple, the ancient white dragon did not leave; instead, it radiated a warm light, staying behind and keeping watch.

"Hmm..."

Alice let out a soft hum and awakened from her unconsciousness. She didn't know how long she'd been out, only that her head throbbed with a dull ache.

She could still recall countless evil dragon souls invading her mind, attempting to take over her body.

Alice rubbed her temples and slowly pushed herself up. The moment she lifted her head, she spotted the ancient white dragon.

"You're awake? You seem rather lucky; your soul wasn't devoured by that group." The white dragon spoke in an ethereal voice, its mouth not moving at all, as though it were using ventriloquism.

"Eh!" A cold sweat bead slipped down Alice's forehead. In her panic, she drew her slender sword. "Who's there!?"

The white dragon looked down on Alice as if viewing a tiny ant. After a moment of silence, it leisurely responded, "There's no need to be so tense, human. I'm different from that group of mad souls."

"...Huh?" Alice froze, hardly able to believe it, yet she maintained her警戒 stance. But she was startled—where had those ancient dragon souls gone?

"My name is Alphard, the first patriarch of the dragon race and the guardian of this entire temple."

The white dragon replied in a deep voice, hoping Alice would lower her guard.

"The first patriarch of the dragon race?" Alice hesitated, then slowly returned her slender sword to its scabbard. This towering giant dragon didn't seem like a bad person.

"Something like that. In a certain sense, I'm also not the real Alphard." The white dragon's words were full of contradiction.

"What do you mean?" Alice frowned.

"I am merely a remnant soul. The real Alphard died a long, long time ago." The white dragon paused, speaking in a low tone, "But I inherited some of Alphard's memories and aspirations, remaining here to select outstanding descendants and teach them how to wield their race's power."

"Oh... I see." Alice suddenly understood, thinking this white dragon was the existence she had been searching for. "Did you save me?"

The white dragon stared into Alice's eyes and said calmly, "You could say that. Originally, I had no intention of saving a human who consumed the dragon race's inheritance crystal... Yet seeing you, I felt inexplicably familiar..."

"Huh? I've never been here before. You must have mistaken me for someone else, right?" Alice's mind was full of questions. Could a remnant soul from the ancient era find her familiar? It must be some mistake.

"My memories are incomplete. It's just that seeing you gives me a sense of déjà vu..." The white dragon closed its eyes.

"That must be wrong. How could I possibly be familiar with you? I'm not even old..." Alice replied awkwardly.

"You're right. Let's just say it was a fleeting impulse of kindness." The white dragon lowered its head, not wanting to dwell on the matter, and extended a massive claw to return Alice's pendant. "This is yours. I took a curious look at it. Please forgive my rudeness."

Alice instinctively touched her neck, feeling the empty space there, and quickly retrieved the pendant.

She gently blew away the dust on it, secretly feeling relieved.

This pendant had been given to her by her teacher and was very likely the only relic left by her mother. Losing it would have been far too regrettable.

"This thing is very important to you?" The white dragon's tone was filled with incomprehension.

"Of course it is..." Alice nodded and responded with a smile.

"But it's not anything good. It carries meanings of all sorts of misfortunes."

The white dragon said seriously.

"Misfortune? It's just a pendant. How does that relate to misfortune?" Alice was confused.

"That sun-and-bull pattern on the back foreshadows it being an offering dedicated to Nidhogg, the Black Dragon. In the ancient era, humans were the most miserable species at the bottom of society. They held the same status as cattle and sheep. The Black Dragon would regularly feast upon them, forcing the insignificant ones to offer tribute—three thousand young bulls, three thousand milk-producing ewes, and three thousand humans..." The white dragon explained in a low voice.

"...Huh?" Alice barely understood and responded, "This sun-and-bull pattern... is simply the heraldry of the Spanish Kingdom. It doesn't mean anything like an offering."

"The Spanish Kingdom? What country is that? I've never heard of it. Still, using such a pattern as a kingdom's crest is far too foolish; it would attract the hungry Black Dragon." The white dragon found what it heard unbelievable.

"Hmm?" Alice seemed to realize something and asked tentatively, "How long has it been since you last left here?"

"I'm merely a remnant soul. Leaving the temple would mean immediate death. But when I entered, those detestable ancient gods had already perished, and the elves had begun to flourish." The white dragon raised its head, as if searching through its distant memories.

"...Huh." Alice gave an awkward smile, thinking no wonder they couldn't communicate properly—this white dragon's memories were completely stuck in the ancient era. Not knowing about Spain was natural. "A long time has passed outside. The world is now dominated by humans, and other races are no longer as prosperous as they once were."

"Dominated by humans?" The white dragon lowered its head and said in disbelief, "How is that possible?! Humans were the lowest of all beings, with not even a single god. How could they possibly dominate the world? No matter how you look at it, that's impossible. Ants devouring a giant to become the rulers—this is too madness!"

"That's just the reality. You simply haven't learned about the outside world for too long." Alice responded understandingly.

The white dragon fell silent for a long time, apparently still digesting this information. After its emotions stabilized, it said, "People have told me these things before, but it's hard for me to accept it all at once. I never thought those utterly weak humans would one day rise above all other races. But thinking about it carefully, such a possibility isn't impossible. After all, the once-arrogant ancient gods were also wiped out in a short time."

Alice remained silent, unsure how to communicate with a living fossil. Though this white dragon was a remnant soul, it seemed even more ancient than the elven king—a genuinely authentic creature that had witnessed the ancient era.

"By the way, as a weak human, why did you come to my race's temple? What is your purpose?" The white dragon asked without disguise. It had no idea what a human was doing risking its life to enter the dragon race's holy land.

"I came to learn the true power of the dragon race!" Alice answered frankly.

"Oh?" The white dragon's eyes reflected Alice's figure. It fell silent, unable to tell what it was thinking.

"C-Can't I?" Alice grew nervous, wondering if she had been too reckless.

"Although you can fuse with the unique crystal within a dragon's mind and even surpass the original in power, no matter what, you cannot change the fact that you are human. Will the dragon race pass on its power to an outsider? No." The white dragon refused without any leniency.

"Hmm..." Alice sighed. She had thought things were too simple. How could the other party just casually teach her?

However, granting the dragon race's power to humans was not something that had never happened before... The white dragon paused, lifting its enormous head as it recalled.

"In those turbulent times, in order to resist the oppression of the ancient gods, the weak creatures united."

"Although the dragon race was extremely few in number, their combat prowess far exceeded many other kinds."

"So we gave the inheritance crystals of dead dragons to humans. Combined with the black dragon's blood, warriors were born who were no less than dragons themselves."

"These warriors feared neither hardship nor death, defeating the ancient gods' henchmen several times. They were called..."

"The Dragon Fighters."

title: Chapter 18 — One-Shot Deal (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 18 — One-Shot Deal (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 23 · Chapter 18

"Dragon...," Alice frowned, suddenly recalling this group from what Clady, the 12th Thorn Knight, had told her.

"The Dragon Warriors were born from those chaotic times, a huge concession our clan made for freedom." The White Dragon paused, its eyes seemingly welling up with murky tears. "I personally dug up the corpses of my kin, burned them to ashes, and extracted the crystals that held their power. The evil dragon souls you see here are the pitiful remnants of my people, whose bodies I destroyed, leaving their souls without a place to rest. They made a great sacrifice for the continuation of the dragon race..."

"That... could you tell me more about the Dragon Warriors?" Alice asked curiously, very interested in this topic.

The White Dragon looked at Alice, perhaps not having spoken to anyone in a long time, and began to narrate simply.

"The source of everything must be traced back to a prophet who suddenly appeared among the demon race. In that era, the old gods were the rulers, and we were merely their vassals."

"We were born from the blood of the Black Dragon Nidhogg, so we have a close relationship with this evil dragon, calling it our supreme father."

"This is similar to the demon race; demons are just servants created by the demon gods, and we were all slaves without freedom, our bodies, minds, and souls belonging to the old gods."

"The world was under the oppression of the old gods, with no resistance, as if everyone had grown accustomed to it. But one day, this changed when someone dared to resist - that prophet of the demon race."

"The news of Nidhogg's death still feels like a dream to this day. It made us realize that the old gods could bleed, suffer, and die, just like us!"

"That demon prophet changed my impression of demons. At the time, most demons were deceitful and cunning, but he was eager to climb to the top of the World Tree to confront those terrifying old gods, even sealing away the demons' supreme father - something we dared not imagine."

"The demon prophet united the lower classes and sparked the largest rebellion I remember. He demanded that I hand over the legacy crystals of my deceased kin to the weakest of humans - the greatest insult to our clan!"

"But I admit, I feared this prophet and yet hoped he could bring us freedom, so I complied."

"Those Dragon Warriors, born from Nidhogg's blood, now possess power far surpassing that of giant dragons, making us question who the true dragons are."

"In my eyes, those Dragon Warriors are just strange hybrid creatures, yet they can tear apart the old gods' minions, the Valkyries..."

Alice saw that the White Dragon didn't want to speak anymore, probably recalling unhappy memories, but what it had said was already shocking enough.

Though the White Dragon hadn't said much, it was enough for Alice to understand that the Dragon Warriors were created as warriors to fight against the old gods.

"...Is that so? That demon prophet sounds quite unreasonable..."

"Indeed, but I admire him. He single-handedly climbed the World Tree and triggered the gods' downfall. If not for him, we would still be living in the dark era under those gods' rule." The White Dragon spoke in a low voice.

Alice lowered her head, feeling this was hopeless. She didn't have the power to threaten the White Dragon into teaching her dragon powers. It was unlikely she could make it submit.

"Although there's precedent for teaching power to humans, the situation is different now. I have no reason to teach you." The White Dragon paused for a few seconds before continuing, "However, our clan values strength above all. If you can surpass my kin, you must have something even better. If you consider yourself one of us, I can teach you some practical things..."

"Consider myself one of you?" Alice was puzzled, not understanding the White Dragon's meaning.

"Accepting that you're one of us means inheriting my will, not Alphard's, the first clan leader's wish. This is something every dragon must strive to fulfill."

The White Dragon hesitated, clearly appreciating Alice's courage in coming to the sanctuary and her talent, but humans were ultimately untrustworthy.

This remnant of Alphard gazed intently at Alice, seemingly wanting her to acknowledge herself as part of the dragon clan for some purpose.

"Alphard's wish... what is it?" Alice asked hesitantly.

"To kill our father, the Black Dragon Nidhogg." The White Dragon said seriously.

"Ah?... Isn't it already dead?" Alice was startled.

"It's not dead. Nidhogg is one of the old gods. The dragon clan's bloodline connection has become very weak over generations. Don't forget, dragons were born from Nidhogg's blood, and its death would mean the extinction of our entire clan. My remnant surviving to this day proves it's still alive. That demon prophet sealed away the terrifying demon god but didn't choose to kill it, probably to allow the demons to survive and thrive." The White Dragon lifted its head, gazing into the distance. "I am Nidhogg's first giant dragon creation. I believe that if there are still living first-generation demons among the demon race, they would feel their father's presence just like I do..."

"...But didn't you say Nidhogg's death would mean the dragon clan's extinction? Is this really Alphard's wish?" Alice grew more confused. Killing their creator seemed like a path to mutual destruction.

"In reality, our situation is very similar to the demon race. The giant dragons of today have almost no relation to our ancestors, having become an independent species. Killing the father who created us would only mean the death of us first-generation old dragons." The White Dragon lowered its head, looking at Alice as it explained slowly. "As long as Nidhogg lives, it will remain a huge threat to our clan. We betrayed it, and it will surely not forgive us, eventually slaughtering us traitors."

"I see...," Alice forced herself to understand. The current giant dragons had little blood connection to their ancestors, so even if Nidhogg were killed, only the original ancient dragons would die.

"If you accept this condition, then don't think of yourself as human. We can accept you..." The White Dragon's gaze turned serious. "But you must fulfill Alphard's wish and make killing Nidhogg your lifelong pursuit."

Alice hesitated. She wasn't like Merlin, full of malice, and didn't want to lie to deceive this White Dragon that had saved her, just to gain the chance to learn dragon powers.

She wasn't willing to deny her humanity and become a dragon just to become stronger, which completely went against her original intentions.

Although Alice often used giant dragon magic and martial techniques, she hadn't forgotten that she was the sole successor of the Great Snow Mountain—

"No! I am human!"

"But I am an adventurer! We have our own rules!"

"If you're willing to teach me the true power of the dragon clan?"

"I can make killing Nidhogg my mission goal and use its corpse as the reward."

"Rather than having your kin challenge the dangerous Nidhogg, why not let me, a human, become the Black Dragon Slayer!"

"What was the meaning of Alphard leaving you in this sanctuary..."

"Isn't it to cultivate an enemy capable of threatening Nidhogg's life?"

title: Chapter 19 — The Ultimate Cold
content:
Chapter 19 — The Ultimate Cold

Volume 23 · Chapter 19

After hearing Alice's words, the white dragon remained impassive, showing not even a flicker of reaction, simply staring at the diminutive figure before it.

The atmosphere grew strangely tense, and an invisible pressure pressed down heavily on Alice.

Wh- why isn't it saying anything? Did I say something wrong?

"Ha ha ha ha!" The white dragon suddenly erupted into laughter that echoed through the entire sanctuary, the ground rumbling beneath its voice.

"Hrrk!" Alice barely steadied herself, confusion washing over her. She hadn't told any jokes—what was this dragon laughing about?

"Truly befitting one destined to replace my descendants, you are extraordinary!" The white dragon lowered its head, and a hint of approval now gleamed in its gaze toward Alice.

...Alice froze mid-step.

"I don't know how long I've lingered within this sanctuary. I am but a remnant soul of Alphard, unsure of the meaning of my own existence. I simply continued teaching magic and martial techniques to young dragons, relaying Alphard's dying wishes and urging them to fulfill them...." The white dragon paused and bowed its head. "I always considered myself nothing more than a machine. But it seems that Alphard did not leave me here merely to breed more enemies capable of rivaling Nidhogg and fulfill his wish to slay that black dragon. Rather, as long as Nidhogg can be killed, what does it matter whether one is a dragon or not?"

"...Alice gazed at the white dragon, thinking that this creature wasn't truly the first patriarch Alphard himself, but rather a lingering remnant soul, making it considerably simpler in disposition.

"What you say is correct. Cultivating you into a black dragon to kill would not be harmful to our clan—it actually serves our interests. I myself failed to realize this for so long, yet you, a human, have enlightened me. I do not exist to bestow power upon young dragons, but to create more enemies capable of opposing Nidhogg...." The white dragon's eyes flickered repeatedly. This remnant soul of Alphard seemed to have gained a deeper understanding of itself.

"Then... will you let me learn the true power of the dragon race?" Alice asked tentatively.

"That you can merge with the crystallization bearing our clan's power proves you possess the qualification." The white dragon's demeanor softened considerably, resembling an elder. "I admire your courage to risk your life and come to this sanctuary, and even more so, your sincerity—you do not deny yourself in pursuit of power. If you had just admitted you were no longer human, I would have instead held you in contempt...."

"Eh? Why?" Alice stood dumbfounded, wondering if she had nearly stepped into a trap. This dragon was actually laying a snare for her!

"Because those who deny themselves are nothing but opportunists—greedy, despicable, and lacking self-confidence. Without firm convictions to sustain them, even if they learn our dragon race's true power, they will gradually lose themselves." The white dragon said heavily.

"I see..." Alice sighed.

"We sense the power surging within your body, filled with the aura of cold. I have magic and martial techniques here that can make you stronger, but you must answer one question for me." The white dragon closed its eyes in thought, then asked softly, "You are a human who wields the power of ice. Tell me—what is the ultimate extreme of cold?"

"T-this..." Alice hesitated. No one had ever taught her this; even her master on the Great Snow Mountain had never asked such a bizarre question. "Perhaps... it can freeze a person to death instantly, and seal the earth under ice, turning many regions into bitterly cold wastelands or... something like that."

"So that is the ultimate extreme of cold as you conceive it? Expand your imagination further." The white dragon's expression grew strange, clearly unsatisfied with Alice's answer.

"The most I can imagine... is probably already all there is..." Alice said awkwardly, thinking that if this was already the limit, what else could possibly be done?

The white dragon fell silent for a moment, seemingly at a loss for how to respond to Alice.

"Are you considered a strong figure out there?"

"......I suppose so..." Alice awkwardly scratched her cheek.

"Then that is truly disappointing..." The white dragon sighed and spoke slowly. "A strength of your level is considered impressive outside—truly, this is the sorrow of the age. It seems the demise of the gods of the old era did not bring about the world's evolution, but rather a severe regression."

"What do you mean?" Alice furrowed her delicate brows, feeling as though she were being looked down upon.

"Freezing enemies to death? Sealing the earth under ice? These are the most basic forms of power—insignificant even in the primordial era." The white dragon raised its head and spoke earnestly. "The ultimate extreme of cold is not some superficial display like that. When your power reaches a certain level, you can achieve even the freezing of time and space, and control phenomena far more profound and unfathomable...."

"Time and space?" Alice blinked in confusion, somewhat doubtful she could accomplish such things.

"To contend with the black dragon, your current level falls far short. You cannot even scratch its scales...." The white dragon spread its luminous wings behind its back, a spectacular sight, as the entire sanctuary was bathed in its radiance. "You will witness the secrets of our clan. How much you can learn depends on your innate talent!"

The moment those words left its mouth, a colossal pillar of light descended from the heavens, engulfing Alice!

Within the radiance, every single cell in Alice's body suddenly screamed with tears as though being ripped apart!

The residual inheritance crystallization within her body, as though summoned, began to stir restlessly.

Alice felt her blood boiling, as if it were on the verge of bursting forth from within her at any moment!

She endured the pain, opened her eyes, and saw ancient dragon script hidden within the light—

"...What is this?!"

Outside the Golden City, deep within the mines, tunnels crisscrossed and had long since been hollowed out by the dwarves.

Gazing at the pitch-black rock walls around her and the marks left by axes and chisels, it was not hard to imagine the dwarves extracting no small quantity of hard ores from here.

During that duel, the dwarf king had brought ruin upon himself by hoisting his own stone, suffering a crushing defeat. He now couldn't even lift his head, having lost all face before his clan.

Even now, the dwarf king was racked with worry over what he could do to salvage his utterly ruined reputation. If things continued like this, the clan members would only grow more openly disdainful of their leader behind his back.

Merlin had no interest in the dwarf king's predicament—that was his own problem. Who told him to insist on dueling Merlin and spread word everywhere until even the dwarf children in Golden City knew their chief had been defeated by a criminal?

Per the original bet, the dwarf king was to present Merlin with his clan's supreme treasure—the Golden Essence.

Though the dwarf king was deeply reluctant, even wanting to renege, he was now caught with his tail between his legs, unable to break the agreement.

Because every dwarf knew the dwarf king had lost the supreme treasure—if he reneged now, his situation would become even more dire. Not only would he have lost to a criminal, but he'd also be branded a man without honor.

At this moment, within the mine tunnels, Merlin and the dwarf king walked side by side, preparing to retrieve the Golden Essence, with rows of dwarf knights escorting them behind.

Up front, General Holly shamelessly took on the role of guide, repeatedly sending friendly signals toward Merlin and grinning obsequiously.

"Right this way, Lord Merlin~"

"Oh! Careful! There's a pebble ahead—don't injure your foot~"

"What, a puddle? Lord Merlin! Step across upon my body!"

title: Chapter 20 — Deep Within the Mine
content:
Chapter 20 — Deep Within the Mine

Volume 23 · Chapter 20

General Holly didn't mind the dirt and lay down directly in the puddle, waiting for Merlin to step over him.

This wind-vane turncoat had shown his sycophantic nature to the fullest after witnessing Merlin's terrifying power!

After all, the Dwarf King had already been defeated. If he didn't submit, wouldn't he be an incurable fool?

General Holly was terrified that Merlin would hold a grudge and settle scores with him. If he could please Merlin thoroughly now, perhaps he could avoid a beating.

"..." Merlin wore a blank expression, unmoved by General Holly's enthusiasm, and even found it a bit uncomfortable. He said with embarrassment, "There's no need for this. I'm not so fragile that I need someone to take care of me."

"How can that be? Lord Merlin, a noble guest of the Golden City, getting his boots dirty is a matter of the utmost importance!" General Holly scrambled up, panicked that Merlin wasn't appreciating his efforts.

"You don't need to do this. I know what you're thinking, General. Isn't it just that you're afraid I'll cause trouble for you?" Merlin snorted coldly and said casually, "My magnanimity isn't so narrow as that. You don't need to worry too much."

"Hehe... I always knew Lord Merlin had a broad mind and wouldn't hold a grudge against someone like me, ha..." General Holly gave an awkward laugh, feeling much more at ease after hearing Merlin say that. "Please, Lord Merlin. We're almost there."

"..." The Dwarf King, watching from behind, saw General Holly's despicable face and ground his teeth in fury. If it weren't for this bastard causing trouble, would he have been reduced to gambling away his clan's greatest treasure? He had dug his own grave and now still had the face to bow and scrape before a sinner! Once this was over, he would definitely deal with him properly!

A chill suddenly ran down General Holly's back. Sensing something was wrong, he quickly scurried over to the Dwarf King and said with a grinning face, "Brother-in-law, the road ahead is rough. Let me support you?"

"Get lost!" The Dwarf King barked angrily and strode after Merlin in irritation.

General Holly's expression darkened. He thought, this is bad. If my brother-in-law is this cold toward me, it can't be a good sign. I'll need to ask my sister to plead on my behalf later.

"Your Majesty the Dwarf King, we made a deal. This golden essence already counts as mine..." Merlin said suddenly from ahead.

"You don't need to keep emphasizing this. Although the golden essence is our clan's treasure, priceless in value, I agreed to accept defeat in a wager. I'm not so low as to be a man without credit." The Dwarf King snorted coldly, his mood already at its worst, and he was still being provoked by Merlin.

Merlin glanced back at the Dwarf King and felt a bit strange. The golden essence was the dwarf race's greatest treasure, yet he was handing it over so casually. Wasn't that a bit too easy?

According to Merlin's thinking, since it was a supreme treasure, the Dwarf King wouldn't hand it over easily, even if Merlin won the wager. But he quickly remembered some things Master Balin had mentioned.

"I heard... you discovered this golden essence, but couldn't make use of it because a terrifying magical beast was guarding it? Is that true?"

"Hmm? You actually know about that..." The Dwarf King was slightly surprised. He was cooperating with Merlin precisely because a magical beast guarded the golden essence. Even he couldn't retrieve it himself. Even if Merlin wanted the golden essence, he'd need to survive to take it.

"I can't not know anything, right? I would definitely do some advance research." Merlin smiled.

"Hmph! There is a troublesome big guy. You'll know once you go inside. If you want the golden essence, fine, but you'll need to have the life to take it. If you can't take it? Sorry, our wager ends there."

"Oh?" Merlin stopped and stared at the Dwarf King. "You think I can't take it?"

"That magical beast is no ordinary monster. Even using all the power of our clan, it would be difficult to defeat it. Do you think you can rely on your own strength to take the golden essence right under its nose?" The Dwarf King said confidently, thinking that if Merlin couldn't take the golden essence, it would remain dwarf property.

"Hiss~! I see..." Merlin frowned and suddenly said meaningfully, "How about we make another wager? If I retrieve the golden essence, you'll give me something else of value, how about that?"

"You—!" The Dwarf King's face went pale, his big beard trembling with anger. He already had psychological trauma from gambling and couldn't help but curse:

"You despicable, greedy, shameless sinner!

"I'll bet my grandma's foot!

"Do you want to plunder all the treasures of our clan?!"

Nobody knew how long they walked, but they finally reached the deepest part of the mine tunnel.

The space here was clearly much larger than the mining areas. To protect the golden essence inside, a crude hall had been specially constructed.

A massive sealed stone door appeared before everyone, carved with dwarf ancestors on both sides holding giant axes, looking extremely majestic.

"This is it." The Dwarf King stopped and said nonchalantly, "Go get the golden essence yourself. We don't want to provoke the monster inside."

"Is that so?" Merlin walked up to the stone door and examined it carefully, but didn't sense any danger.

"Let me give you some advice..." The Dwarf King paused and said with a wicked smile, "Don't lose your life trying to get the golden essence. Being too greedy will cost you your life."

Merlin frowned slightly and turned his head. "Can you be more specific? What exactly does the monster inside look like? Why are you all so reluctant to approach this place?"

"Lord Merlin may not know, but the thing inside..."

General Holly wanted to explain the situation in detail, but the Dwarf King shot him a vicious glare, resentful of his meddling.

General Holly awkwardly shut his mouth and retreated sullenly, not daring to say more.

The Dwarf King withdrew his murderous gaze and said to Merlin with a mocking expression, "Why should we tell you what the monster inside is? Do you need me to personally deliver the golden essence to your hands to be satisfied? If you want it, go in and get it yourself. If not, leave the Golden City. You're not welcome!"

"Ha..."

Merlin gave a dry laugh. He didn't care about the Dwarf King's hostility and could even understand the other's attitude.

After all, anyone would be very unhappy if their family's most prized treasure was about to be taken away.

The fact that the Dwarf King had brought Merlin here was already maximum assistance. The rest depended on himself.

"Then wait for my good news..."

"Hmph!" The Dwarf King sneered. Although he couldn't defeat Merlin himself, the monster inside could definitely tear him to pieces. Overestimating himself. I'll wait to see you...

...Merlin stood before the ancient stone door, took a deep breath, and extended both hands, slowly forcing the heavy door open with a rumbling vibration—

The moment a small gap opened, brilliant golden light poured out!

Inside were rare treasures, but also unknown dangers...

title: Chapter 21 — The Third Elemental Beast
content:
Chapter 21 — The Third Elemental Beast

Volume 23 · Chapter 21

Outside the ancient stone gate, Merlin had already entered the chamber storing the Golden Essence.

The Dwarf King and General Holly remained behind, refusing to accompany Merlin.

The dwarf knights behind them felt a thread of unease, seemingly instinctively fearful of the monster within the stone gate.

General Holly pondered for a long time before finally asking in a low voice, "She...cough! Your Majesty, the monster inside is no trivial matter. Is it really alright not to tell him anything?"

The Dwarf King's forehead bulged with veins, glaring at Holly in annoyance, "Whose side are you on?! Still worrying about a criminal?"

"...General Holly's face turned pale as he realized his mistake, hastily correcting himself, "No, no, no! How could I worry about a criminal? I'd rather see him die in there..."

"Hmph! That's more like it..." The Dwarf King's expression slightly eased, speaking with ill intent, "If he wants our clan's treasure, he'll have to be lucky enough to take it out alive. If he dies inside, the bet will be null and void, which would be a great fortune for me! Why would I tell him about the situation inside? The door isn't even open!"

"Right, right, right! Your Majesty is wise..." General Holly quickly forced a flattering smile, sycophantically agreeing, "Why should we help him obtain the Golden Essence? It would be better if he died here! He's humiliated our dwarves, he must pay a painful price."

"Exactly, that's how it should be~" The Dwarf King nodded in satisfaction, his mood greatly improved by General Holly's flattery.

"But this criminal's strength isn't weak. What if the monster inside isn't his match? We'll definitely suffer heavy losses..." General Holly said with concern.

"What's there to fear? If I didn't have complete confidence, would I have brought this criminal here?" The Dwarf King glanced at Holly, coldly sneering, "In my estimation, this criminal absolutely cannot take the Golden Essence. The monster inside is no ordinary creature..."

"Shh~" General Holly gasped, cautiously asking, "Could it be that Your Majesty has some understanding of that monster?"

"Of course! Do you think I don't want to take out that Golden Essence? I've mobilized all our clan's power, yet we still can't retrieve it. This criminal from afar, although not weak, wanting to take our treasure is almost impossible." The Dwarf King was full of confidence, having brought Merlin here precisely because he was certain Merlin couldn't take the Golden Essence, "You know that magic beasts are generally low in intelligence, right?"

"I know. Although they're very aggressive, they're not much different from ordinary beasts." General Holly nodded.

"But they can cultivate like us, and the longer they live, the stronger they become, and eventually..." The Dwarf King pointed to his own head, speaking meaningfully, "they can develop wisdom."

"Ah?! Magic beasts can have wisdom?!" General Holly had never heard of this before.

"The monster inside once communicated with me, warning me not to enter, or it would kill me." The Dwarf King's expression turned serious, still fearful, "It's a magic beast born alongside the Golden Essence, conservatively estimated to have lived for over a hundred thousand years, with a body composed purely of earth elements, already possessing considerable divinity. If it becomes enraged, it's no joke. Even the Elf King and the Blazing Dragon King combined might not be its match."

"So terrifying?" General Holly's face turned pale, despite knowing the monster inside was fearsome, the Dwarf King's words far exceeded his imagination.

"This kind of magic beast, composed purely of elements, with considerable wisdom and divinity, can control natural forces. In a sense, its power can approach that of a god..." The Dwarf King explained seriously, then asked, "Do you think this criminal can kill the monster inside?"

"Impossible!" General Holly said decisively, "Originally, my brother-in-law had already made preparations. We won't suffer any losses and can even use the monster inside to get rid of this troublesome guy."

"Exactly." The Dwarf King smiled and nodded, then suddenly gritted his teeth, "Call me Your Majesty, not brother-in-law!"

Inside the ancient stone gate, the surroundings were dark rock walls, not as gloomy as imagined.

In the distance, faint golden glows continuously lit up, as if beckoning outsiders to proceed deeper.

Merlin became cautious, advancing forward until he reached the end, where he saw a massive cliff.

He leaned forward to look down, and what entered his vision was a magnificent deep pit, roughly 500 feet deep.

Is this the dwarves' doing? Why dig such a deep pit? It looks like a monster's lair...

Merlin wondered to himself, suddenly noticing that at the center of the pit, a simple platform had been formed from piled stones.

On it, a half-transparent golden crystal floated!

This golden crystal was only half the size of a hand, and if not for the light emanating from it, it would be hard to see.

Flying gold? It must be the Golden Essence...

Merlin's heart stirred, and without hesitation, he leaped down into the depths of the pit.

Boom!

Merlin's landing produced a considerable sound that echoed through the mine for a long time.

At that moment, it seemed this outsider had awakened something. The stones on the ground began to float and tremble.

Merlin retreated half a step, lowering the long sword at his waist to draw it easily, vigilantly observing his surroundings, muttering to himself.

Getting the Golden Essence isn't that simple, as expected...

Those floating stones seemed to have gained life, continuously gathering together!

In just an instant, they formed three massive stone giants. Although not as imposing as the Rock King, they still possessed sufficient intimidation.

The three stone giants opened their mouths with a "crack crack crack" sound, as if roaring at the intruder, trampling the earth as they charged towards Merlin, intent on tearing him apart.

Merlin's eyebrows twitched, and with a swift motion, he drew his sword. The sharp blade flashed, and the killing intent sliced the three stone giants into powder without any suspense.

"This is the monster the Dwarf King mentioned? It feels much weaker than I imagined..."

Merlin muttered in puzzlement, sheathing his sword and preparing to directly take the Golden Essence. However, the sound of falling stones came from behind him once more.

The originally shattered stones reassembled into three stone giants, appearing completely unharmed despite Merlin's attack.

"Tch! Not..."

Merlin furrowed his brows, feeling a sense of entanglement. He made up his mind to swiftly grab the Golden Essence and leave.

Facing monsters that couldn't be killed, Merlin currently had no good solution. Continuing to entangle would only waste time, and he increasingly yearned for Misty.

The stone giants roared, raising their fists to heavily strike Merlin, "Boom!" The massive impact sent shattered stones flying, and the ground was smashed into a large crater.

Merlin used a ghostly movement to dodge, continuously evading the three stone giants' encirclement, slipping away like an eel.

After dodging the stone giants' attacks, Merlin's gaze locked onto the Golden Essence on the platform. The dwarves' treasure was within reach!

Just as Merlin was about to succeed, a strange power suddenly struck!

Merlin felt as if a massive mountain had been pressed onto him, pinning him to the ground, his face intimately meeting the earth.

"Crack crack crack," the ground beneath him split open, revealing the terror of this mysterious pressure, as if wanting to merge him with the earth.

Merlin gritted his teeth, unable to move under the pressure. The gravity around him was extraordinary, at least ten times stronger than usual!

It seemed only he was struggling against this terrifying gravity, while the stone giants showed no abnormalities.

"...Who's ambushing me?!"

Two points added for the update

title: Chapter 22 — Spirit of the Earth (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 22 — Spirit of the Earth (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 23 · Chapter 22

Merlin felt the terrifying gravity pressing down on him as though a majestic mountain were perched on his back, pinning him to the ground and making it hard to move.

He caught a whiff of danger—these three stone giants were merely puppets, and the real enemy hadn't even revealed itself yet!

And that despicable guy was definitely no weakling. Merlin was immune to magic, and ordinary spells had no effect on him.

For an enemy to apply this kind of gravity technique directly to Merlin, the power being used couldn't be magical energy—it had to be something far higher, such as the elusive Divine Power!

Crack—

The gravity intensified tenfold once more. Merlin's face darkened as his entire body sank into the earth, much like a fly mercilessly crushed flat.

An endless pressure assaulted him, and Merlin felt as though every bone in his body was on the verge of shattering. The ground before his eyes cracked open and shattered into countless fragments.

The three stone giants charged again, hoping to take advantage of Merlin's inability to move and kill this intruder!

"Hah—"

Merlin gritted his teeth in frustration. Plating his courage, he forced himself to rise against the terrifying gravity bearing down upon him, his body trembling as he stood up unsteadily.

He clenched his jaw, his face grim. The overwhelming gravity constantly pressed down on his shoulders, causing his body to tremble slightly.

A fierce light flashed in Merlin's eyes, and with a vicious expression, he executed another Rising Slash, once again shattering the three charging stone giants.

From the darkness, a faint "oh?" echoed, as if deeply surprised by Merlin's actions.

Merlin returned his katana to its scabbard and, enduring the extraordinary gravity, shouted loudly, "Who's there?!"

Long silence filled the air, and then a somewhat ethereal voice rang out, "You're also here to grab the Golden Essence, aren't you? Many have come before you. You're the strongest among them. Being able to hold out under my gravity space—now that's some real skill."

Merlin frowned tightly. A magical beast capable of speech made him somewhat taken aback. "Stop lurking around sneakily! Have the guts to show yourself! Let's fight openly!"

"Hahaha, what an interesting guy~"

Laughter rang out, and the earth elements in the air suddenly grew denser, shimmering with brown light.

Soon the earth elements converged and transformed into something very similar to a human...

Or more accurately, a half-human being with a human-like form, because the entire body radiated a faint brown glow, composed completely of pure elements, much like a wandering soul.

Lake Sprites and Balore were both magical beasts composed of pure elements, carrying traces of divinity, and could each serve as treasures protecting a nation!

But compared to the entity appearing before him, the差距 wasn't just great—it was enormous. This being's body had almost entirely broken free from the form of a magical beast, becoming a half-human. Who was stronger? Just look and you'd know!

".....Human or ghost?" Merlin felt the elemental power before him was extraordinarily pure. Any ordinary person facing such an existence would feel terror. Especially given the oppressive pressure emanating from this half-human—it far surpassed the terrifying presence of Azhudor he had killed earlier. No wonder the gravity technique affected him; the opponent's power had already transcended the realm of magical energy.

"I am not human. I am the Earth Spirit born of this land, a supreme elemental magical beast born of nature itself. That Golden Essence belongs to me. If you leave peacefully right now, I can spare your life—" the Earth Spirit said calmly, wanting to轰 Merlin away from this place.

"Elemental magical beast..."

Merlin paused for a moment, recalling the Lake Sprite, which also seemed to belong to this category. In simple terms, their elemental power had attained sentience, gaining its own physical form.

However, the Lake Sprite still resembled a water monster, while the Earth Spirit before him had begun to take on a more human appearance, easily mistaken for a glowing ghost.

During their earlier clash, Merlin hadn't been particularly afraid of this being. Instead, a strange smile had appeared on his face. He wouldn't mind his opponent being strong—the stronger, the better.

"Sorry about this, but that thing is mine now. If you leave peacefully, I can spare your life too. It's not easy to cultivate into a form resembling a human, is it?"

"It seems there's no need to negotiate. You seem unaware of just how dangerous you are? What you're doing now is like—" the Earth Spirit's gaze gradually turned cold.

"Dangerous? Where's the danger? Seeing you makes me feel incredibly lucky. Prey coming to me one after another has left me rather flattered. Beings like you are always hiding, impossible to even find." Merlin rested his hand on Banri Garan at his waist.

"I haven't seen anyone this rude in a long time..." The Earth Spirit slowly raised both hands, and the shattered stone giants stood up once more.

This time there were twenty of them, nearly filling the entire crater, and their bodies were no longer black—but a dazzling golden color. They had clearly been reinforced!

It seemed this intelligent magical beast was truly angry now and had decided to play for real. These golden stone giants were even more ferocious and harder than before!

To put it plainly, a single golden stone giant could fight three or four Saint-tier experts without any problem—and might not even get injured!

Upon seeing the Earth Spirit's true form, Merlin was overjoyed inwardly, because as long as it wasn't an unkillable creature, this would be manageable.

These stone giants were merely puppets, able to rise continuously only because of the Earth Spirit's power. As long as the main body was killed, the stone giants would be nothing to fear!

Merlin changed tactics and went on the offensive, rushing straight toward the Earth Spirit. Relying on his extremely swift speed, he attempted to avoid being caught by the opponent's daunting gravity magic.

Although the Earth Spirit's power surpassed Azhudor's, it was still in the pseudo-god stage.

From Merlin's estimation, Azhudor had fought him cautiously, only resorting to Divine Power at the very end. That meant this power must have a limit on how many times it could be used—otherwise Azhudor would have gone all out from the start.

Twenty golden stone giants closed in, surrounding Merlin completely. They raised their hardened fists and repeatedly smashed into the ground, causing the earth to rumble continuously!

These reinforced stone giants had indeed grown significantly stronger and became somewhat troublesome. Plus, supported by the Earth Spirit's power, they wouldn't die, making it easy to toy with their enemies!

Merlin drew his blade in a wrist flick, chopping the two nearest stone giants in front of him into碎屑, and seized the opportunity to quickly close the distance toward the Earth Spirit behind them!

"Skulking around like a rat. Stop right there—" the Earth Spirit raised a finger and directly unleashed Divine Power at Merlin.

The gravity space was released. An area centered on the Earth Spirit was heavily affected, and the entire space became distorted, constantly quivering!

An utterly terrifying pressure descended. The earth seemed to be compressed and collapsing. Merlin finally understood why this place had a 500-foot-deep crater—half of it must have been formed under the Earth Spirit's gravity magic!

This time, the Earth Spirit didn't release the gravity space only at Merlin. Instead, in anger, it released it across the entire area before him. Those golden stone giants were instantly crushed into powder!

Even though Merlin moved swiftly, he was still affected by the wide-range attack. His body bent under the pressure, his steps suddenly faltered, as though ten mountains were burdened on his shoulders! The pressure was even more terrifying than before! His feet had already sunk deep into the earth.

"One hundred times the gravity. How does it feel? With just a single thought from me, you'll be crushed to death..." Seeing Merlin immobilized, the Earth Spirit became smug.

"Oh? Is that so?"

Merlin gritted his teeth, his forehead veins bulging, enduring the incomparable gravity as he forcibly took a step closer to the Earth Spirit.

With every step forward, the gravity increased further, fracturing the earth beneath him!

It wasn't that Merlin's strength was too great and he crushed the ground—it was that the pressure on his body was so immense he seemed to be walking while carrying a mountain on his back.

"Continue... keep going! What is this level?!"

".." The Earth Spirit suddenly froze, an uncontrollable tremor running through its mind—

What kind of monster is this guy?!

Under normal circumstances, one hundred times the gravity would have already reduced a person to碎屑!

title: Chapter 23 — Gravity Magic
content:
Chapter 23 — Gravity Magic

Volume 23 · Chapter 23

Under the 100-fold gravity of the Earth Spirit, Merlin gritted his teeth, the veins on his forehead bulging, the terrifying pressure making it hard for him to endure.

"...The Earth Spirit felt a slight astonishment, encountering Merlin for the first time, its gravity magic unable to crush him!"

Merlin gripped the hilt tightly, slowly approaching the Earth Spirit under the 100-fold gravity, finding it extremely difficult to even hold his knife under such pressure.

With each step, the ground beneath his feet would shake and shatter into countless fragments!

Originally a mine, the ground here was several times harder than outside, yet Merlin felt as if he was walking through a muddy swamp, needing to exert great effort to move forward.

As the distance closed, Merlin's gaze turned sharp, using all his strength to draw his sword and slash straight at the Earth Spirit, "Die!"

"Huh?!" The Earth Spirit was startled, finally feeling fear towards this intruder, raising its hands to use Divine Power again, "Disappear!"

This time, the gravity space was even more terrifying, its power suddenly increasing tenfold, forcefully suppressing Merlin with 1000-fold gravity.

The space visibly distorted, the 1000-fold gravity causing the ground beneath him to sink, sending sand and rocks flying towards the sky.

Merlin's barely drawn sword began to curve under the 1000-fold gravity, as if it might snap at any moment!

He looked at the constantly trembling blade of Banri Garan, a cold sweat forming on his forehead, thinking this intelligent magical beast was far more difficult to deal with than the lake spirit from Great Britain!

Merlin felt the crushing gravity assault him, as if he was carrying a continental map, his bones crackling with each movement, as if they might break under the pressure.

Just as Merlin spoke, a loud "Boom" sounded, and he indeed couldn't withstand the 1000-fold gravity, crashing down and sinking into the ground, cracks spreading out in all directions.

The Earth Spirit didn't stop, pressing its advantage. With a light wave of its hands, the ground rumbled, and countless rock spikes appeared in mid-air!

Immediately, the dense rock spikes fell like a heavy rain, attacking the immobile Merlin with "Boom, boom, boom" sounds.

Dust rose, filling the mine, the rock spike rain lasting a full minute before stopping...

The Earth Spirit panted heavily, clearly exhausted from fighting Merlin, its Divine Power depleted.

Looking at the forest of rock spikes, it felt satisfied, thinking this troublesome enemy would either be crushed by gravity or pierced to death.

"That detestable thing, finally dead..."

Suddenly! A sword light flashed through the dense rock forest, striking with unstoppable momentum!

"No!" The Earth Spirit's voice cut off as the sword light pierced its neck, its eyes widening in shock, unable to comprehend how Merlin was still alive.

The dense rock forest shattered, revealing Merlin's figure, though he had survived the attacks, he was clearly injured.

Merlin's clothes were tattered, his body pierced by several rock spikes. He ripped off cloth strips to roughly bandage his wounds.

"I knew you couldn't keep pressing down on me."

The enemy's life force, absorbed by Banri Garan, nourished Merlin's heart, alleviating some of the pressure on his body.

Just as Merlin prepared to turn and take the golden essence, he saw the Earth Spirit's corpse dissolve into light, leaving behind a small brown light orb floating in place.

Merlin wondered, since the life force had been absorbed and it was clearly dead, why was something like a soul left behind?

He approached cautiously, examining the brown orb, which didn't seem aggressive, only emitting exceptionally pure and dense earth elements.

Driven by curiosity, Merlin tentatively reached out to touch it, extremely careful, unsure what it was.

The moment his fingertips made contact, the mysterious brown orb surged into Merlin's body as if finding its host!

"Ah!"

Merlin was shocked, his butt landing on the ground, worried it might be poison or a curse!

But upon checking his body, he found no discomfort or abnormal status.

What the hell just entered my body?

Merlin calmed down, closing his eyes to focus his consciousness inward, unexpectedly discovering the brown orb emitting dense earth elements.

Could this be the magical beast's crystallized core, absorbed by accident?

Merlin had heard that magical beasts of sufficient strength could form cores within their bodies, though not as rare as dragon cores, they greatly benefited warriors and mages.

As the Earth Spirit was a high-level magical beast born from natural elements, with near-human intelligence and divinity, its crystallized core was naturally extraordinary.

Merlin had unknowingly stumbled upon a great fortune. He slowly opened his eyes, clearly feeling the Earth Spirit enhancing his spiritual and physical strength.

Though Merlin was immune to magic, most spells had no effect on him, and he didn't fear spiritual magic. However, if he encountered spiritual attacks independent of magic and qi, he would have high resistance.

His wounds also healed rapidly, his body feeling light and powerful, likely to increase in strength several levels, becoming as tough as steel under the Earth Spirit's nourishment.

"Good stuff..."

Merlin felt joyful, thinking this trip wasn't wasted. Besides the physical changes, there was an even more exciting transformation.

He discovered he could manipulate earth elements in the air, meaning...

Merlin slowly raised his hand, freely manipulating the dense earth elements in the air, trying to guide the Earth Spirit's power.

Rumble! The gravity in the space suddenly increased! The entire mine trembled as if it might collapse at any moment!

Merlin quickly withdrew the earth element's power, clearly not as skilled at controlling gravity as the Earth Spirit, fearing he might collapse the mine.

He hadn't been mistaken; he was using the same gravity space magic as the Earth Spirit!

"Heh heh..." Merlin's expression was incredulous as he stared at his hands, laughing foolishly.

"I can..."

"Use magic now."
