title: Chapter 24 — Got It
content:
Chapter 24 — Got It

Volume 23 · Chapter 24

Countless tiny stones floated in the air, Merlin closed his eyes tightly, carefully studying his newly acquired ability, and he discovered he could freely control the stones to form any shape.
However, controlling earth elements was obviously less practical than gravity control; the Earth Spirit's gravity field could at least be considered a wide-area control, and many enemies wouldn't even reach Merlin before being pressed to the ground by overwhelming gravity, unable to move.
Merlin opened his eyes, roughly understood the situation, and the Earth Spirit had not altered his magic-immune constitution.
Therefore, what he used was not magic at all, but directly drew power from the Earth Spirit's crystal core deep within his spirit, which is why he could wield the same magic as the Earth Spirit.
In a sense, this thing could be considered a tool, able to parasitize within Merlin's body and share its power with him.
After gaining the Earth Spirit's power, Merlin felt he had secured a considerable advantage; although he didn't expect the gravity field to kill strong foes, even resisting gave him a headache, so the enemy must feel even worse.
“No wonder the mercenaries could sell the crystal cores they got from killing magic beasts at a high price; turns out this is such a good thing……
“I just don’t know whether the Earth Spirit’s crystal core will continue to evolve?”
Outside, the Dwarf King and General Holly waited here, wanting to find out whether Merlin had died inside.
But after waiting half a day, there was no movement at all inside, making it hard for them to judge the situation.
“Your Majesty, it’s been so long—has that guy died?” General Holly asked tentatively.
“Logically speaking, if someone tried to take the golden essence, that monster would surely fly into a rage, but”
The Dwarf King paused, frowned in confusion, and said, “It’s too quiet—really, I can’t tell whether a fight broke out in there.”
“Well… ” General Holly thought for a moment, then said obsequiously, “Your Majesty needn’t worry too much; if nothing unexpected happens, that criminal definitely won’t walk out alive—we might as well head back.”
“No way—I can’t rest easy until I’m sure he’s dead.” The Dwarf King remained worried, thinking the monster inside shouldn’t be so calm.
At this moment one
The whole mine rumbled, terrifying gravity as if it could collapse the place at any moment.
The dwarves waiting outside turned pale, feeling the strong pressure descend, and were all slammed to the ground instantly!
“. . What is this!?” General Holly winced, gritting his teeth, feeling as if his bones were about to be torn apart.
“Hahaha!” The Dwarf King let out an eerie laugh, proudly saying, “Here it is! Here it is! The monster inside has gone berserk! That criminal is as good as dead! It’s this overwhelming force—I nearly got crushed to death by it last time!”
Because Merlin had just obtained the Earth Spirit’s power and his control wasn’t yet proficient, the outside was affected, leading the Dwarf King to a considerable misunderstanding.
Just now, the Earth Spirit’s gravity field could be well controlled within a certain range, even acting on a single person—his control of power was something Merlin couldn’t match.
Fortunately, this terrifying gravity passed in an instant; the mine returned to calm, the dwarves rose to their feet, still a bit shaken.
“Congratulations, Your Majesty—the monster’s fury subsided quickly; surely that despicable criminal was instantly wiped out!” General Holly beamed, convinced Merlin had definitely died inside, even though he had just been fawning like a sycophant, he hadn’t forgotten Merlin’s humiliation of him.
“Hmph! I knew it!” The Dwarf King brushed off the dust, blew his beard, and said, “Our treasure—could a mere criminal even dare to covet it? He deserved it! Good riddance! This is what he gets!”
“Exactly! Right, hahaha…” General Holly’s smile grew wider, “Wanting to take the golden essence without checking your own strength? Such an arrogant fool—dying a hundred times wouldn’t be a problem!”
“Let’s head back and spread the word—we’ll say that criminal was seriously injured by me in the duel, but ended up dying at the hands of the monster deep in the mine.” The Dwarf King hadn’t forgotten to save face, crafting an illusion that his strength was on par with Merlin’s to cover the embarrassment he suffered in the duel.
But just as the Dwarf King and General Holly turned around, the heavy stone door behind them rumbled and began to open slowly—
“Wait, aren’t you going to wait for me to come out together?” Merlin stepped out from inside, his expression carrying a hint of teasing; aside from his tattered clothes, he appeared unharmed, having been nourished and healed by the Earth Spirit.
“Ah!?” General Holly jerked his head back in shock, his eyeballs almost popping out—“You came out alive, proving…… the monster inside was defeated?! How is that possible!”
Seeing Merlin walk out alive, the Dwarf King felt as if struck by lightning, and his words came out incoherent.
“What’s it to you? You didn’t think I’d die in there, did you?” Merlin paused, held up two fingers deep inside to compare, “The monster inside was indeed a bit troublesome, but only just a little bit. In zh”
“Ah….” The Dwarf King stared wide-eyed, pointing at Merlin, unable to speak, his heart unable to believe—“Did that beast capable of cultivating

title: Chapter 25 — Farewell
content:
Chapter 25 — Farewell

Volume 23 · Chapter 25

Merlin furrowed his brows, thinking where he could find clues for the other two rare materials. If Mistystin isn't forged quickly, not only will he be unable to deal with that troublesome Cain, any undead enemy could jump around in front of him.

"Merlin big brother! You actually did it! The Dwarf King Majesty must be regretting to death, haha.... Dwarf Barli rushes over, his heart full of admiration for Merlin."

"It's quite regrettable.... Merlin recalls the Dwarf King passing out from anger, and finds it funny."

"What about that Dwarf general? Won't he come looking for trouble again?" Fairy Feyri flies over, worriedly asking.

"I already warned him, so he probably won't come cause trouble for Master Barlin again. If he still dares to strongly demand Master Barlin, then I'll accuse him." Merlin pats his chest, intending to protect this blacksmith father-son pair.

"Merlin... Elder Dwarf Barlean walks over with a cane, gratefully saying, "You helped us a great deal, I don't know how to thank you!"

"I don't need thanks; you just need to help me forge Mistystin." Merlin says seriously.

"I will do my best with all my effort." Elder Dwarf Barlean promises Merlin.

"Alright, hide this gold essence, don't let the Dwarf King see it, otherwise this stingy fellow will surely try to take it back." Merlin emphasizes.

"I will definitely keep it safe. Once the materials are gathered, I'll start forging Mistystin, but the remaining two materials are even more precious and rare. Your Excellency, can you really find them?" Elder Dwarf Barlean says doubtfully, although he very much hopes to forge a masterpiece in his lifetime, upon careful thought it seems unrealistic.

"I'm not sure either—Divine Forge Ore? Soul of the gods? I've never heard of those before, but I can only try my best to look." Merlin frowns and asks back, "Master Barlean, with your abundant forging experience, surely you have some clues?"

"No, I only heard it from my grandfather: the souls of gods, whether dead or alive, never perish and can serve as the finest forging material. As for Divine Forge Ore?" Elder Dwarf Barlean recalls, speaking uncertainly, "Perhaps it exists at the roots of the World Tree, but the World Tree perished along with the gods of the old era; whether we can find it remains unknown."

"The roots of the World Tree.... Merlin mutters to himself, suddenly recalling something from long ago: I heard the guardian of the North Sea Kraken protects the relics of the gods—could there be what I need inside? But who knows where the gods' relics actually are?"

"Merlin big brother, don't rush; this kind of thing cannot be hurried." Dwarf Barlean comforts.

"I understand; for this god-slaying blade, I've long been mentally prepared, but the forging difficulty exceeds my imagination." Merlin turns around, looking at them, "Tomorrow morning I'll head back, and afterward I'll try to find the last two materials."

"Leaving so soon? Aren't you planning to stay a few more days?" Dwarf Barli startles.

"I have an appointment to meet with my companions; timing is about up, and besides, the Dwarf King probably harbors a grudge against me, so there's no need to stay." Merlin shrugs helplessly.

"Merlin big brother! I don't want you to go!" Dwarf Barli rushes over and hugs Merlin's thigh.

"You this...... just simply want to learn sword techniques from me?" A few embarrassed black lines slip down Merlin's forehead.

"Definitely, these days Barli has been practicing draw-cut technique, but it still has no power.... Fairy Feyri mutters—"

"... Dwarf Barli's face turns red, he puffs his beard angrily, 'I'm still at the beginner stage; as long as I train hard, I'll eventually have power—who just learns martial arts and becomes that strong?'"

Merlin looks at Barli's appearance and can't help but smile, "Barli, don't you want to become a master blacksmith?"

"Who wants to stand by the furnace all day? If I'm not careful, I'll spend my whole life stuck in this smithy; going out wandering, defeating the strong and helping the weak—how fun is that!" Dwarf Barli's eyes blaze with passion, it seems he already harbors the thought of wandering the world with a sword.

"..... Elder Dwarf Barlean sees his son like this, lets out a deep sigh; he already knows Barli's little thoughts, and worries that the family's blacksmithing craft cannot be passed down."

Merlin squats down to make himself appear as tall as the dwarves, and says earnestly, "Don't think things are too simple, Barli—not everyone who wanders outside achieves something; many people envy your stable life."

"But I've had enough of being a blacksmith." Dwarf Barli's tone is full of gloom.

"Haha, Barli, your skills are at most apprentice level, yet you dare to boast that you've had enough of being a blacksmith. When you become a renowned master far and wide, saying that won't be too late!" Fairy Feyri mocks.

"... Don't talk nonsense!" Dwarf Barli, being teased by Feyri, blows his beard and glares.

"Feyri is right; if you become a renowned far-and-wide blacksmith master, saying that later won't be too late." Merlin pauses, then speaks seriously, "Don't look at my surface glamorous appearance—actually we adventurers live with our heads constantly at risk, worrying about the future. For instance, right now I'm not even begging your father Master Barlean to help me forge a weapon? No matter which profession reaches its peak, achievements have no hierarchy."

"..... Dwarf Barli sighs, lowers his head, feeling he still sees things too simply; being a blacksmith is already confusing, what qualification does he have to become a warrior?"

Elder Dwarf Barlean pats his son's shoulder to comfort him, "Don't lose heart, Barli; if you can integrate the family's blacksmithing skills, even if you can't become a warrior, you can still be friends with someone as strong as Lord Merlin."

"Exactly." Merlin nods, thinking Barli lacks talent for magic or martial arts; at his age, a breakthrough is unlikely; it's more practical to inherit his father's trade and become a generation of blacksmith master.

"Merlin! Since you're leaving, I'll give you something.... Fairy Feyri pats her small hand, instantly conjuring a little bell and handing it to Merlin."

"What is this?" Merlin looks at the golden little bell in his hand.

"This is my bell; as long as you shake it, no matter how far away I can hear it." Fairy Feyri flutters her cicada wings behind her, "If you find the remaining materials, shake this bell, and I'll bring the materials back to Master Barlean for you, and by the way I'll give you a hard kick on the butt! Hehe...."

Merlin looks at the little bell in his hand, unexpectedly realizing that this foul-mouthed fairy actually has good intentions—she's basically offering a doorstep delivery service.

"Before you kick my butt hard, I swear I'll sit on you until you become a pancake...."

The dragon race's territory, atop Black Mountain.

The Blazing Dragon King stands with hands behind his back, expressionless, gazing at the rolling lava before him, completely unaware what this guy is thinking in his heart?

Behind him, the Elf King paces back and forth, looking anxious as if burning inside, somewhat worried, unable to help but speak in an irritated tone.

"Three days have passed, already three days! Miss Alice still hasn't come out—what exactly happened inside?!"

"Hmph, this is the first time I've seen you flustered like that—is that human really that important?" The Blazing Dragon King replies nonchalantly.

"..... The Elf King is at a loss for words; it's not that Alice is important, but if something goes wrong, I can't explain it to Merlin."

"Three days have passed, that sinner's time in the sanctuary has already exceeded....." The Blazing Dragon King pauses, closes his eyes and says.

"I advise you not to wait any longer; that human woman must be dead."

"I thought she had something special about her, but it turns out she's only this much...."

title: Chapter 26 — The Power of Probing the Laws (Additional Update)
content:
Chapter 26 — The Power of Probing the Laws (Additional Update)

Volume 23 · Chapter 26

In the Ancestral Dragon Temple, the lingering remnant soul of the White Dragon Alphard lifted its head to gaze at the human bathed in light.

Alice had been immersed in the Dragon Clan's power for three days, still deep in study, constantly absorbing the precious experience of the ancient dragons.

Within the radiance, she witnessed the birth and decline of colossal dragons, saw the civilizations they endlessly constructed, evoking a profound sense of admiration.

Alice's strength steadily grew as she learned the Dragon Clan's premier powers. Only now did she understand—

Marcgon was merely an amateur, failing to grasp the essence of dragon power. He'd only learned the tip of the iceberg, yet could rampage unchecked outside. How terrifying must the true might of dragons be!

Alice had always considered "Glacial Descent" to be an immensely powerful magic, but that was merely the outermost layer of dragon power?

True dragon power far exceeded Alice's imagination, and even with her current abilities, she simply couldn't use it!

The white dragon narrowed its eyes slightly. It hadn't originally believed Alice could learn much, yet after a full three days, she was still immersed in study, as if having forgotten the torment of bathing in the radiance?

It secretly admired this human's indomitable soul. Looking at it now, her talent was not poor—in fact, it surpassed the current clan leader, the Blazing Flame Holy Dragon.

It remembered how the Blazing Flame Holy Dragon had merely endured three days and nights within the radiance before breaking down, yet Alice was still progressing after three days and nights.

Sigh, it seems our Dragon Clan truly has declined—our talent has been surpassed by humans...

The white dragon sighed silently in its heart, forced to admit the changing times. The Dragon Clan no longer possessed the splendor of days past.

Suddenly, the entire Dragon Temple trembled, as if something had been triggered—

The white dragon snapped its head up, gazing at Alice bathed in radiance, its eyes carrying an undercurrent of disbelief.

"She..has already comprehended it?! The extreme of cold... the power of the Law..."

The light gradually dissipated, and Alice slowly descended. The previously violent pressure had become far more condensed, like a calm lake without a ripple.

Alice's strength had increased once again. She was no longer at the stage of just stepping across the threshold of the Sect Realm.

Though not yet matching the Blazing Flame Dragon King, she had closed the gap by a significant stride.

Alice slowly opened her eyes, recalling the immense piercing pain that had struck her spirit at its deepest point while within the radiance. Her heart still trembled slightly at the thought.

But all of it had been worthwhile. She had successfully glimpsed the essence of dragon power. The extreme of cold was the Law governing time and space.

"How was it? Did you gain a great deal?" the white dragon asked softly.

"Yes, I never expected pure power to be so terrifying—capable of even twisting the world's very rules."

Alice glanced at her own hands.

"Indeed, you've already glimpsed the tip of Divine Power," the white dragon paused, then spoke leisurely. "To become an unmatched powerhouse, one inevitably must come into contact with the power of Laws— the flow of time, the falling of objects, the dimensions of space, and so on, all stem from the power of Laws. If one can thoroughly integrate them, then they can rival true gods."

"...Alice nodded, partway understanding."

"Although you have witnessed the power of Laws, do not grow arrogant. Merely comprehending the power of Laws grants only the qualification to position oneself alongside gods. Truly powerful gods are those who alter them, constructing the very rules of the world!" The white dragon, like a teacher, explained the subtleties within the power of Laws to Alice.

"Constructing the world's rules..." Alice thought of the Goddess of Light worshipped by the Holy Church and the Lord of Hell who was its enemy, both having completely transformed the once-divine-and-human shared world. Those two were probably what the white dragon meant by truly powerful gods. "The power of Laws is indeed formidable, but unfortunately, I currently lack the ability to use it at all. I can only dream of it."

"Your talent is quite good. You may have the opportunity to comprehend Divine Power. When that time comes, you will naturally be able to wield the power of world Laws," the white dragon said slowly.

"An enemy's enemy is a friend—that's what you taught me. Perhaps I am the seed you planted, one day to grow into the greatest enemy of Nidhogg. Then your purpose will have been achieved," the white dragon had not forgotten Alice's agreement, still treating the slaying of the black dragon as a mission objective.

"Don't worry, I haven't forgotten your commission. If I learn of the vicious dragon's whereabouts, I will find a way to eliminate it," Alice responded earnestly.

"Your soul is pure and kind. I trust you," the white dragon nodded.

"Then I must take my leave. I've made plans with my companions. Perhaps we shall meet again someday."

The white dragon watched as Alice flew away from the Ancestral Dragon Temple, using its warm, gentle light to illuminate her path and dispel the mad evil spirits in the darkness.

The temple returned to its usual deathlike silence, with nothing but the curses of the ancient dragon souls.

This place was filled with resentment and anger, yet it was only this remnant soul of Alphard that remained stationed here, as lonely as ever, waiting for one dragon kin after another.

The white dragon lowered its head, its cloudy eyes devoid of any emotional fluctuation. It wearily lay upon the cold ground, as if about to enter a deep slumber—

This human... she feels strangely familiar. Doesn't it feel like I've seen her somewhere before?

Right, I'm just a remnant soul. Most of my memories have already been lost, and even the countenance of that Prophet among the demon race is quite blurred...

The white dragon didn't know how long it lay on the ground before a sudden image flashed through its mind, sending a chill down its spine!

It sharply lifted its head, gazing toward the direction where Alice had departed, its expression shifting from shock to dread, before finally settling into calm—

"This déjà vu feeling...

"I see... So it was like this!?"

"The leader of humanity, the despised witch humiliated by the gods of the old era, Mary...

"Hah, fate seems to have played a joke. No matter how powerful, no one can escape its palm..."

Outside, the Blazing Flame Holy Dragon maintained its usual detached air, as if Alice's life or death had nothing whatsoever to do with it.

If Alice survived, it proved this sinner was indeed superior to the great dragons.

But if she had died, it would simply be because she was too weak, unqualified to learn dragon power.

Yet the usually calm elven king's patience was gradually wearing thin. He turned and said coldly,

"Do you or do you not have schemes involving Miss Alice?"

"You're saying..." the Blazing Flame Dragon King responded in a nonchalant tone.

"If anything happens to Miss Alice, then I..." the elven king left his sentence unfinished, constantly striving to control his emotions.

"What of it? You old fox, don't shout at me. Look at your current state—you're no longer as powerful as you once were. To be frank, I could crush you with a finger." The Blazing Flame Dragon King pinched two fingers together, immediately unleashing layers of sparks.

"...The elven king's brows furrowed tightly, his expression grim. He wasn't afraid of the Blazing Flame Dragon King, but was deeply worried about Merlin. What would happen if he himself, having brought Alice here, died? That梅林, despite being fired, was still the youngest ruler among the demon race. Whether Merlin would even listen to his explanation was questionable.

Suddenly, the magma began to churn, forming a spectacular vortex, the entire black mountain trembling with a low rumbling sound.

"...The elven king sharply turned his head, fixating on the magma waterfall before him.

Half-dragon-transformed Alice burst forth from the magma, landing before the Blazing Flame Dragon King and the elven king.

"Miss Alice!? Are you alright?" the elven king asked concerningly.

"I'm fine." Alice reverted her dragon transformation, appearing largely unharmed.

"...The Blazing Flame Dragon King sensed the pressure on Alice's body, its expression flickering. The return of this sinner had apparently taken it quite by surprise—

Her strength had grown considerably in such a short time! I thought she had a high probability of dying inside!

Damn it! It seems the primordial clan leader's remnant soul has recognized her. How could something like this happen!?

Could it be... this human truly surpasses the great dragons?

title: Chapter 27 — Leave
content:
Chapter 27 — Leave

Volume 23 · Chapter 27

Blazing Dragon King felt suspicious and hesitant in his heart, and asked tentatively, "....I saw that old...."

"Hmm?" Alice was stunned, realizing the old fellow was referring to the white dragon, and nodded, saying, "I saw it.

"Is it willing to teach us the power of our clan to you?" Blazing Dragon King pressed further.

"If it wasn't willing to teach me, how could I possibly have lived to leave the Ancestral Dragon Sanctuary?" Alice asked rhetorically with deep meaning.

....Blazing Dragon King's complexion continuously fluctuated. If even Alphaard's remnant soul approved of Alice, then she—must know many secrets of the dragon race, "So you know what you should do, don't you?"

"Of course, we have a common goal." Alice looked into Blazing Dragon King's eyes.

"......" Blazing Dragon King suddenly froze. Looking at Alice's reaction, it was obvious she knew that the dragon clan's descendants were all burdened with the mission to kill Nidhogg.

"What are you saying?" The Elf King felt that the two of them were talking nonsense.

"It has nothing to do with you." Blazing Dragon King suddenly laughed, praising, "Good, since that old fellow is willing to acknowledge you, you must certainly have something extraordinary about you. Congratulations, I am willing to accept you as a member of the dragon race."

"No, I won't become yours." Alice replied seriously.

"What?!" Blazing Dragon King furrowed his brows, his face turning extremely ugly, and a fierce aura erupted, the temperature in the air rising straight up, "Getting benefits yet wanting to leave clean and tidy? Do you think there's such a good thing in the world?"

"Please don't misunderstand, me not wanting to become your clansman doesn't mean I won't complete our common goal. I know I've received the dragon race's favor, so as an adventurer, I am willing to take killing our common enemy as a task that must be completed, just as a return of favor. But making me a member of the dragon race is absolutely impossible!" Alice firmly rejected.

"Silver-tongued sinner, unchangeable nature! Do you think I would believe your sweet words?!"

Blazing Dragon King's body instantly erupted with terrifying flames, shooting straight up into the sky. The surrounding rock walls melted at a visible speed, turning into molten magma!

It had already viewed Alice as an traitor, taking benefits but not doing things, wanting to destroy this untrustworthy mixed-race creature!

Blazing Dragon King's aura surged, raising the temperature in the air straight up, as if standing in a furnace.

"You calm down a...." The Elf King had a slight cold sweat on his forehead, hoping everyone could talk things over properly.

"This is something I agreed upon with that senior from the Ancestral Dragon Sanctuary. There is absolutely no suspicion of deception in it." Alice answered expressionlessly.

"! ! !" Blazing Dragon King was shocked, exclaiming, "You're telling the truth? That old fellow actually agreed to you doing this? !"

'Correct, the enemy of my enemy is my friend, you wouldn't not know this principle, would you?" Alice retorted.

"...."

Blazing Dragon King's heart became suspicious again. Thinking that Alice had learned the true power of the dragon race and was enemies with Nidhogg, this was naturally a good thing.

But teaching the essence of dragon clan inheritance to a human, and not pulling the other party over—this was very difficult for it to understand. Isn't this flowing wealth outwards?

However, Blazing Dragon King gradually calmed down. The remnant soul of the first clan leader Alphaard had a high status, and the decisions it made might have some deep meaning.

S Broad Web Novel

"Hope you don't forget the things you promised. If you deceive us, you will surely pay a painful price!"

"I am absolutely not an untrustworthy person, and I don't need you to question me." After Alice finished speaking, she turned her head and walked out, planning to leave this black mountain full of rolling magma.

Blazing Dragon King's complexion alternated between green and red, his fists tightly clenched causing his knuckles to turn white, obviously suppressing his anger, "After all, humans cannot be easily believed, they are all damned things good at playing tricks and deception!"

"Are you okay?" The Elf King felt Blazing Dragon King's mood was very bad.

Blazing Dragon King angrily shouted, and the magma in front of him began to boil, surging crazily straight up into the sky, illuminating the black mountain's sky red.

It very much wanted to kill Alice, but Alphaard's remnant soul had made some kind of agreement with this human, making it unable to lay a hand on her—

"Quickly disappear from my eye!

"You this old fox, if you dare come to my territory....".

"I swear, I will definitely kill you!"

A few days later, Merlin and Alice gathered under the Elf tribe's sacred tree.

The two had handled all matters, organized their gear, and prepared to leave the United Kingdom, returning to Retham.

Although they only understood a small part of the allied races' coalition, this mysterious country still had many secrets.

But now both of them had their own goals to accomplish, and there was no need to stay here any longer.

At the port, the Elf King, carrying his daughter and a group of Elf knights, saw Merlin and Alice off.

Snowy, having suddenly learned of her mother's death, fell into a low mood and locked herself in her room for several days.

However, under the careful guidance of Knight Sylph and her father the Elf King's encouragement, Snowy's condition had improved somewhat, although she would still think of her mother Andia, but she would no longer lock herself in the room and despair.

Today was the day Merlin and Alice were leaving, and Snowy also got up early, to send off two old friends.

Seeing Snowy with red eyes, Alice thought she might not have completely come out of the shadow, so she walked forward and pulled her hand, saying, "Snowy, be strong, don't always be so sad. If your mother knew, she would definitely be in more pain, you understand, right?"

"I understand.... Snowy nodded, wiping the tears from the corner of her eyes, "Thank you, Alice Miss. You are truly a gentle...."

Looking at Snowy, Merlin also wanted to go forward and say some encouraging words, but suddenly realized this sort of thing wasn't suitable for him to do.

He wasn't as gentle as Alice, words coming from his mouth, more or less were prickly, similar to one—

Cry all you want, cry! Useless! Your mother seeing you like this, probably would have died of anger already!

Merlin forced this hardcore comfort back into his stomach, after holding it in for a while, he said one sentence.

"The dead are already dead, the living must live well. People always have to look forward. With you like this, how will you inherit the position of the Elf King? Such weakness might not harm your own clansmen, right? One more novel

"Wuuu wuuu, I am guilty.... Snowy, who had barely held back her tears, once again started flowing, being made to cry by Merlin.

"Merlin! What are you saying..." Alice's face turned dark, turning back to rebuke Merlin.

"Yeah, Miss Alice, Her Highness has always been sensitive, you shouldn't speak randomly." Sylph furrowed her brows, having comforted Snowy for many days, almost being ruined by a few words from Merlin.

"Cough cough!" Merlin embarrassedly coughed once, lowering his head, "Okay okay okay, I won't speak."

"Then we will go, take care." Alice beamed with a brilliant smile.

"Alice sister also...." Snowy's gaze revealed reluctance, looking as if she very much liked being with Alice.

The two stepped onto the ship back home, standing on the deck waving goodbye to the Elves.

"Don't send any further, just here, alright, Your Majesty, I dare not trouble you to come personally to see us off..." Merlin waved his hand, teasing.

"Hmph, really a person who can't speak...." The Elf King let out a light hum, his deep gaze looking at Merlin, recalling this man's deathly vague prophecy, "Merlin! I give you one last advice!"

"Ah? What? I'm all ears!" Merlin smiled casually.

The Elf King lowered his head in silence for a moment, hesitating whether to give Merlin some hint, but finally still raised his head and said loudly,

"Beware of snakes!

"It might take your... ."

Chris, she will land the day after tomorrow, delicious~

title: Chapter 28 — The Egg in Captivity
content:
Chapter 28 — The Egg in Captivity

Volume 23 · Chapter 28

Merchant ships traveling between the human world and the other races' alliance set sail, gradually moving away from the mysterious United Kingdom.

Alice knit her brows, not understanding at all, and couldn't help but ask, "What did the Elf King mean? Have you been communicating privately about something?"

Merlin withdrew his gaze and smirked indifferently, "Pfft! This old mystic is spouting nonsense again. 'Be careful or the snake will cost you your life'? What kind of joke…"

"…?" Alice grew even more bewildered, her brows tightly furrowed.

Merlin shot Alice a glance, waved his hand, and answered carelessly, "I don't know what it meant either. Maybe it's parting advice, or just babbling nonsense. That's all."

"Is that really so?" Alice felt somewhat worried. Was the Elf King trying to warn them about something important?

"Definitely. This guy is always so cryptic. You believe anything he says?" Merlin反问.

Alice fell silent, recalling that the Elf King often prophesied events that would certainly come to pass — he really did seem rather like a mystic.

Merlin narrowed his eyes and warned with deep meaning, "He said we two are in love with each other. Do you believe that?"

Alice's face flushed crimson in an instant. She stammered, "I… I… Of course I don't believe it! Who would believe such nonsense!?"

"Hah, there you go?" Merlin let out a dry chuckle. "Don't worry about his words. He's just pretending to be mysterious."

Alice lowered her head. The doubts in her heart were hard to dispel. Although the Elf King was always so cryptic, he wasn't some street swindler, and his actions were very reliable. Perhaps Merlin being cautious about the snake wasn't entirely useless nonsense.

"By the way…" Merlin looked Alice up and down, "you've grown considerably stronger. Going to see the Blazing Saint Dragon must have benefited you quite a bit, right?"

"Of course. I saw Alpha's remain…" Alice said with a meaningful look.

"Alpha? Who is that?" Merlin asked in confusion.

"He was the founding patriarch of the Dragon Clan, a figure from the ancient era. He showed me the true power of the dragon race," Alice said proudly.

"Is that so? Looks like you made a big harvest." Merlin nodded, then changed the subject, "Actually, I also acquired quite a few good things~"

"What? Let me see!" Alice said eagerly.

Merlin extended his hand and snapped his fingers. The pressure within the space immediately increased significantly.

Suddenly, Alice bent over sharply, nearly stumbling on the ground.

Merlin had only slightly drawn out the power of the Earth Spirit; otherwise, he might have crushed the ship beneath them to pieces!

Alice felt a bead of cold sweat trickle down her forehead, her heart filled with unease and bewilderment. She didn't understand why just Merlin snapping his fingers made her feel such crushing pressure. "You this…"

"How about it? Pretty impressive, right? Back then, that monster gave me a hard time. Manipulating gravity is really tough to deal with." Merlin smiled proudly.

"You… you can actually use magic now?!" Alice's eyes widened in shock. She found it utterly inconceivable. In her understanding, Merlin possessed a constitution that granted him magic immunity — he absolutely couldn't use magic. That would create a massive contradiction with his innate physique!

"What? Does that mean you're allowed to set fires but I'm not allowed to light a lamp?" Merlin shrugged.

"That's not what I meant. I mean, how did you manage to do it!?" Alice was practically vibrating with curiosity.

"Heh~" Merlin hummed twice, "Actually, I still can't use magic. I just obtained a rare magical beast core. I can channel the power within it to create the illusion of using magic, but…"

"A Supreme Magical Beast Core?" Alice was puzzled. From her experience, many people swallowed magical beast cores to enhance their strength, but it often led to unstable foundations and forced growth as side effects. Moreover, it would completely merge with the host. She had never heard of someone like Merlin drawing out the core's power — it was the first time.

"That magical beast was unexpectedly powerful. It already possessed a certain divinity and no small amount of intelligence. Dealing with it… cost me considerable effort," Merlin sighed.

Alice fell silent. A magical beast that even Merlin had to exert himself to defeat — its strength could only be described as terrifying. After death, the core existing independently without being absorbed… that might actually be possible.

Damn it! This guy was already ridiculously strong, and just a few days alone, his power grew again. Was he leaving anyone else any room to play?!

"…Aren't you supposed to be figuring out how to forge Mistilteinn?"

"Right. Master Balmung said forging Mistilteinn requires three materials: refined gold essence, god-sealing ore, and a god's soul. I ran into that monster while searching for the refined gold essence." Merlin paused, then sighed, "Mistilteinn is extremely difficult to forge. Although I found the refined gold essence, I have no leads on the other two materials. I don't even know if I can successfully make it."

Alice fell silent, then offered comfortingly, "No need to rush too much. I can accompany you to search together."

"Thanks~" Merlin smiled, then turned and walked toward the cabin. "But needing your help to forge even a single weapon — I've truly become hopeless."

Alice's kind gesture was rebuffed. Puffing out her cheeks in anger, she chased after him, "What do you mean by that? Explain yourself!"

Late at night, with the world quiet and still, everything remained as usual after Merlin and Alice had departed.

However, the Sacred Tree Palace, normally brightly lit, was eerily silent.

It was as if the higher-ups of the elf race had suddenly had some urgent matter and temporarily vacated.

In some hidden underground secret chamber, a white egg floated in the air, continuously radiating mysterious power in all directions!

A group of elf elders stood in a circle around the white egg, gathering everyone's magic power to form a restriction that suppressed the mysterious energy.

This pure white egg had been discovered in the ruins shortly after Merlin and Alice's blood shattered the mysterious giant stone. It had been emitting mysterious power from the start, causing the entire elf hierarchy to grow vigilant and forcing them to use their magic to suppress it to prevent it from escaping.

A bead of cold sweat trickled down Sylph's forehead as she whispered to the Elf King, "Your Majesty, what exactly is this egg?"

"It appeared within the stone that disrupted the secret realm's barrier. It must be something extraordinary. The secret realm's barrier was personally established by Father God Corellon himself. How could it alter it? Only a very few can achieve such power," the Elf King said cautiously.

"I see. We've been suppressing it with magic for several days now. Its power has somewhat weakened. We can investigate more carefully now," Sylph whispered.

"I'll handle this personally."

"Your Majesty, be careful."

The Elf King took a deep breath, strode forward toward the pure white egg, and placed his hand upon it. In that instant, he saw—

Merlin and Alice standing before him. Their blood had merged within the mysterious giant stone, instantly creating new life!

She slowly opened her eyes, and the time gears behind her back began to turn!

Suddenly, the egg, which had been suppressed by the numerous elf elders, exploded with overwhelmingly powerful force!

It sent all the surrounding elf elders flying unconscious, and even the Elf King was launched backward like a cannonball, crashing heavily against the wall!

This unknown egg ascended into the sky, smashing through the dome, flying toward the unknown distance…

"Your Majesty!" Sylph hurriedly caught and supported the Elf King.

"That… that was… Merlin and Alice's child!"

"Ah?!" Sylph's eyes widened in shock, unable to believe her own ears.

"This is of grave importance!" The Elf King possessed a unique precognitive ability. It seemed he had already glimpsed something. His voice was hoarse as he said—"

"She was originally supposed to belong to us, but… alas…"

"I miscalculated. We must find a way to bring her back!"

■ToBeContinued

title: Chapter 1 — The Egg Flies a Little Longer
content:
Chapter 1 — The Egg Flies a Little Longer

Volume 24 · Chapter 1

The mysterious white egg, long suppressed, smashed through the Spirit Tree Palace in the dead of night and fled toward unknown territory.

This incident shocked the elven leadership, and the Elf King convened an emergency meeting overnight to discuss the matter.

A group of elven elders stood below, having been knocked unconscious by the mysterious power radiating from the white egg not long ago.

They whispered among themselves privately, endlessly speculating about the egg's origins, each offering different theories but no one able to give an accurate answer.

Sylph stood at the very front with her head bowed, her brows tightly furrowed. Although she herself didn't understand the situation either, she had heard the elves say that egg was the child of Merlin and Alice?

This was extremely hard for Sylph to comprehend. Wasn't that pure white egg born from within the mysterious giant stone? What did it have to do with those two humans?

The atmosphere in the great hall was somewhat oppressive, everyone waiting for the Elf King, hoping he would provide a reasonable explanation.

Creak, the great hall's doors were slowly pushed open. The elders fell silent as the Elf King entered with an unpleasant expression and took his seat on the high throne.

"What has happened, I assume everyone already knows?"

An elderly elf elder with white hair stepped forward, speaking on behalf of all the elders. "Your Majesty, that white egg is rather strange, constantly radiating mysterious power. What exactly is its origin?"

"I cannot determine its origin either, but since it was able to interfere with the barrier left by the Father God, it is likely not something a low-tier species could accomplish." The Elf King pondered for a moment before slowly continuing. "That egg was found beneath the ruins of the mysterious giant stone. I now somewhat suspect that what fell from the sky was not something from our world."

The elven elders immediately erupted into heated discussion, endlessly speculating about the origin of the mysterious giant stone, each offering different theories.

The mysterious giant stone was able to interfere with the barrier left by the Elf God Corelon. If it came from a higher plane, that would seem to make sense.

Sylph suddenly stepped forward one pace, unable to hold back any longer. "Your Majesty, you mentioned not long ago that it was the child of Merlin and Alice? What exactly does that mean..."

"The child inside the egg belongs to those two, and this information is absolutely true." The Elf King paused and said solemnly, "When I was attempting to investigate the secrets within the egg, I witnessed the process of a new life being born. After the blood of those two merged inside, an independent consciousness emerged..."

Sylph hesitated, feeling as though her brain couldn't process this. She had never heard of anything like this!

"This is impossible!" The white-haired elder frowned tightly and countered, "The creation of life... even our Father God Corelon cannot do it. Most life forms created through magic or alchemy are extremely low-tier species, useless for any significant purpose. They could never possibly possess the power to interfere with the divine."

"This is also why I say that giant stone is not from our world. Anything capable of affecting the barrier left by the Father God, and the life born within it, must be extraordinary." The Elf King sighed and said with regret, "I deeply regret it. Back then, I should not have borrowed the power of Merlin and Alice to resolve the crisis of the kingdom's land sinking into the sea. I should have thought of another method. Now the new life inside has formed an unbreakable bond with those two. It could have become a priceless treasure of our race, used by us. But the result... Sigh! I miscalculated!"

Hearing the Elf King say this, the elven elders below all began to suffer headaches, feeling the enormous loss!

That mysterious giant stone was capable of birthing a life form that could interfere with divine power — undoubtedly a rare treasure. And it had been carelessly given away to two outsiders...

"How can something like this be casually handed over!? We must retrieve it!" The white-haired elder suddenly spoke loudly. "Although those two helped us greatly, we have already given generous compensation. Some things can be given away, but there are treasures that must never, ever be given — they could affect the continuation of our race! Your Majesty must cut through this quickly!"

The Elf King's face darkened and he remained silent, deeply conflicted inside. When he had sensed the new life within the egg, his guts were already regretting it. If the elven race's blood had been used to activate that mysterious giant stone, perhaps the life inside would have been of elven bloodline, and careful cultivation might have produced someone capable of changing elven history. But now it was too late no matter what was said.

"Wouldn't this be inappropriate? The life inside the egg was born from the merged blood of Merlin and Alice, clearly making them the child of those two. Wouldn't it be wrong for us to forcibly take it back?" Sylph hesitated, feeling it was like breaking up a family.

"Sylph, haven't you been so absorbed in your cultivation that you've damaged your brain as well?" the white-haired elder said righteously. "That mysterious giant stone landed within our territory, so it should belong to us. No matter what is born inside that egg, it should belong to our elven race! Isn't it only natural to retrieve it?"

The other elders all nodded in agreement, finding the reasoning sound, and immediately began chiming in.

"Exactly, that is our property. Retrieving it is beyond reproach!"

"That egg inside the mysterious giant stone is of great importance. It absolutely cannot be handed over!"

"Since it can interfere with the Father God's barrier, the new life inside must also be a genius comparable to the Father God. We cannot let it go!"

Sylph remained silent, still holding her opposition in her heart. Did they really have to go snatch someone else's child?

She raised her head and looked at the Elf King, who was bowing his head, completely unable to guess what was going through the King's mind.

After a long while, the Elf King, after deep deliberation, seemed to have found a solution and finally deigned to speak.

"All newborn children will seek out their parents. If I am not mistaken, that egg must have followed Merlin and them back to the human kingdom."

"Your meaning is..." Sylph asked tentatively.

"Sylph, you and Shelly will lead one hundred elite knights and secretly travel to the Britannia Empire to find Merlin and Alice. Bring that newborn back. If possible, avoid conflict. Best to persuade them with reason and emotion, convince those two to hand over the child." The Elf King ultimately refused to yield, ordering Shelly and Sylph to serve as envoys and resolve this matter peacefully.

Sylph's brows furrowed tightly as she recalled Merlin's terrifying strength, and she grew somewhat timid. "Your Majesty, you know Merlin's temper. What if he refuses?"

The Elf King fell silent. This scenario was quite likely to occur; he had to think carefully.

One was the enormous wealth of the elven race, the other was offending the former Demon Lord...

The Elf King's gaze grew profound, his eyes shifting constantly, before finally settling on Sylph's eyes.

"If Merlin obstructs us, then..."

Over a month passed. Merlin and Alice had returned to Lexham in Britannia, and life seemed to have returned to calm.

Early in the morning, Hobbs covered his daughter Little Minnie with the blanket she had kicked off in the middle of the night, left breakfast on the table, and then headed out.

Hobbs pushed open the front door, took a deep breath, stretched his waist, and gazed at the sun that had just risen above the horizon.

Then in a daze, a white egg streaked across the sky and vanished from view in a flash.

"What the hell! What was that?" Hobbs rubbed his eyes, his face full of astonishment, but he could see nothing. He smacked his lips, still carrying the stench of last night's alcohol.

"A flying egg?"

"...I must still be half asleep. I'll go back and catch more sleep..."

title: Chapter 2 — Food Delivered to the Door?
content:
Chapter 2 — Food Delivered to the Door?

Volume 24 · Chapter 2

After returning from the United Kingdom, Merlin and Alice finally enjoyed a long-awaited peaceful life at home. However, it was normal for the two of them to argue when together, and today was no exception— "Ah, comfortable...." Merlin had already occupied the toilet in the bathroom early in the morning, carrying out his daily task. He slowly picked up the London Daily beside him and began to read it with great interest. Besides liking to use horse racing to salvage his miserable fate, Merlin's only seemingly normal hobby was sitting alone on the toilet, quietly reading something to help him understand the outside world. Since the two had been away from Britain for eight days, Merlin was curious about what interesting things had happened in the kingdom during his absence, so he bought the recent newspapers with the few remaining copper coins. "Let me see what fun things have happened lately." Merlin examined it carefully, sometimes frowning, sometimes smirking foolishly; it seemed that as long as Alice didn't lose her temper, he could stay in the bathroom all day— "Shocking! Someone actually escaped from the mysterious sea area said to be inescapable! ? This issue's personality interview features Dennis the captain of the Rose family!" Merlin raised his eyebrows, thinking Dennis the captain had also made the newspaper? It sounded like the same incident when they went together to the Chaotic Sea? Who would have thought, this old captain Dennis had also become a celebrity; surviving the Chaotic Sea, he could probably brag about it for a lifetime. "Recently the Pope proclaimed that the hero who saved France is the Church's Hero, the merciful Goddess of Light has not abandoned humanity, and announced that the Holy Church's secret plan has made a major breakthrough, the extermination of demons is imminent." Seeing this news, Merlin furrowed his brows, thinking the old Pope really knows how to gild his own image, and indeed won't miss any chance to boost his presence. After the failed crusade, Alice was expelled from the Holy Church, and now they're again acknowledging her as a Hero; they might as well just hand over the inherited mithril armor— However, the newspaper said the Holy Church's secret plan had a major breakthrough—what does that mean? The Church of Light, which has been quiet for so long, is probably about to make a big move against the demon race. Just as Merlin was filled with doubts, a 'bang bang bang' knocking sounded from outside the bathroom— "Merlin! Are you hiding in there again?" "What the hell are you doing knocking so loudly first thing in the morning? Do you want to scare me to death?" Merlin put down the newspaper, rolled his eyes, and instantly became irritated; he hated being disturbed while sitting on the toilet reading the newspaper, couldn't he just have a little dead-person space? He had finally managed to be quiet for a moment. "Are you sick? You hide in the bathroom every morning for two hours, it's really annoying..." Alice's tone revealed a hint of annoyance. "Can't I have a bad stomach? You're meddling too much, you're also annoying...." Merlin replied in a bad mood. "Huh? .... Alice outside furrowed her brows, instantly furious, 'You'd better come out quickly; today it's your turn to mop the floor, don't think you can get away with it!'" "Tsk!" Merlin clicked his tongue, impatiently saying, 'Such a trivial matter, can't you help me mop the floor? This small thing I didn't ask you to—'" "Merlin, do you still have any shame? I'm not your servant, there's no need for me to do things for you!" Alice said, emphasizing, "Don't forget you're the later arrival; I'm the owner of this house." ".... Merlin sighed, closing the newspaper in his hand, 'You've used that excuse eight hundred times; can't you change it? What exactly do you want to do?'" "'Out, come, mop, the, floor....' Alice said word by word." "All right, I'll go in a moment; please don't disturb me, okay? You annoying hag.... Merlin pursed his lips, responding nonchalantly." "Hmph!" Alice outside trembled with anger, her shoulders shaking, she angrily kicked the bathroom door, making a thudding 'dong' sound, 'I don't believe you won't come out, hum~!'" "Yell~" Merlin showed disdain, continuing to pick up the newspaper and read, his thoughtful look like a social commentator. But the peace didn't last long; only heard a 'clang' loud bang, the whole house shook! Dust fell from the ceiling in wisps, dirtying Merlin's hair; he angrily gritted his teeth and clenched his fist violently— "Alice! What are you doing? !" < Merlin stormed out of the bathroom, thinking Alice had eaten gunpowder, destined to not let him have a good time. It's because I didn't come out that she started wreaking havoc outside, destroying even my little bits of quiet time; her heart is terribly bad! After Merlin came out, he immediately saw the ceiling collapse: a big hole appeared, continuously dropping dust— Good heavens! Is Alice crazy? To deal with me she went all out, wrecking the house.... What's the point? I'm upset because my quiet was disturbed; in the end, isn't it her who will have to spend money to fix it? Alice stood there dazed, not knowing what had happened, as if she'd lost her soul; she had already tied on an apron, preparing to make breakfast. But Alice was busy in the kitchen, frazzled, while Merlin lounged in the bathroom slacking off, making her feel extremely unbalanced inside. Merlin stepped forward, patted Alice's shoulder, and said earnestly, 'What are you doing? To get me out, you demolished the house—is it worth it? Did your brain get kicked by the donkey you raised?' "'.' 'No, it's not like that! It's not me!' Alice exclaimed, turning her head to explain, her eyes doubtful." "'Huh?' Merlin froze, seeing Alice's expression didn't look like she was joking, 'What happened?'" "'Then....' Alice pulled Merlin, pointing ahead, 'Quickly look over there! Something suddenly fell down!'" Merlin walked over doubtfully, and immediately discovered that at the center of the cracked floor lay a pure white egg, strikingly out of place. Alice tugged Merlin and whispered, 'What is this thing? Do you know?' "'Don't panic, maybe a huge bird flew over our heads and laid an egg by the way?' Merlin scratched his head." "'How careless!' Alice flared up, complaining." Merlin stepped forward, hugged the egg, feeling it was rather large, so he examined it closely, shook it, and wore a puzzled expression, thinking, 'What exactly is this thing? There's nothing special about it; it just looks like an oversized goose egg.' "'How so? What exactly is it?' Alice couldn't help but ask; she herself couldn't judge." "'I don't know either, I can't tell at all.'" Merlin frowned in exasperation, then decided not to think too much; since it was delivered to our door, we might as well.... Only saw Merlin walk to the stove, light the fire, pour oil into the pan, and put the pure white egg inside. "'Although I don't know what this egg is, it must be a good omen; maybe someone knew we hadn't had breakfast, so they deliberately sent the egg for us to eat, uh!—definitely so! This is fate!'" "'Ugh!' Alice's face turned pale, startled by Merlin's action, she hurriedly tried to stop him—" "'We haven't figured out what it is yet; don't just eat it!'" "Quickly tell me to stop, ah 5 Mi'"

title: Chapter 3 — Love is a Ray of Light (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 3 — Love is a Ray of Light (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 24 · Chapter 3

Three hours later, Merlin and Alice sat on the ground, staring silently at this strange egg.

They couldn't figure out the origin of this thing, and in the short term they didn't know how to deal with it.

Of course, Merlin's suggestion to eat the egg was rejected by Alice; without knowing the situation, eating it randomly was also a dangerous thing.

"Ah!" Merlin scratched his hair, his patience gradually wearing thin, "What on earth is this thing? It suddenly smashed the house..."

Alice pressed her ear against the eggshell and tapped it with her hand, then shook her head and said, "Can't tell. It feels like there's nothing special. Maybe it was accidentally dropped here..."

The pure white egg had already become different from a few days ago. It had lost its obvious power, as if everything had fallen into silence, becoming an ordinary thing.

This greatly increased the difficulty of their investigation. Besides random guessing, they simply couldn't determine where this mysterious egg came from.

"So, how do you want to handle it? This egg has an unknown origin, and it might be dangerous. How about we eat it? Once it's in the stomach, who would think of any waves?" Merlin suggested a simple and crude solution.

"Does eating something of unknown origin have no danger? After all, you're just plainly wanting to eat, aren't you?" Alice watched Merlin warily.

"Actually... the size of this thing is about the same as a dragon's egg. Have you eaten dragon's egg before? The taste is quite good, especially the yolk, which is particularly delicious..." Merlin swallowed his saliva and encouraged her.

"Don't try to lure me. Your base thoughts are written all over your face..." Alice assumed a look of not wanting to talk to Merlin.

"It smashed our house, so it needs to make some compensation, doesn't it? If we don't eat it... we can sell it, can't we?" Merlin said seriously.

"But if we sell it and something happens, isn't that harming people?" Alice didn't understand.

"Tsk!" Merlin rolled his eyes wide, patting his thigh, "This won't work, that won't work, what exactly do you want?"

"I don't know..." Alice mumbled, feeling that handling this matter properly required good thought.

"Huff..." Merlin exhaled, as if making a decision, then slowly stood up, holding the pure white egg, "Since we can't eat it, and can't sell it? What do we do with it left? Why not just smash it directly? For something we can't figure out, the most direct approach is to destroy it before it causes harm."

"Stop!" Alice stood up and grabbed Merlin, stopping him, "This isn't our thing at all. Breaking it would be even worse."

"Get out of the way, Alice. I've had enough of your indecisiveness. Bad things I'll do, you just watch from the side, and it has nothing to do with you." Merlin said with a straight face.

"No!" Alice's expression also turned serious, "Since I saw it, I can't just sit by and do nothing. I won't let you make the decision on your own."

Their eyes met, and sparks of fire frequently burst forth in the gaze, making the atmosphere in the house confrontational.

Although Merlin and Alice could live together through mutual tolerance, their ideas were still fire and water!

But just when the two were at loggerheads, neither willing to give in, this egg of unknown origin suddenly moved--

"Huh?!!" Merlin suddenly became alert, lowering his head incredulously! He felt it clearly while holding the egg.

"What's wrong?" Alice asked in confusion.

"It... it just moved!" Merlin said with a face full of astonishment.

"Ah?!" Alice came closer and reached out to touch the egg, "Really? Is there something inside!"

"We... let's smash it quickly, who knows what's inside?!" Merlin said anxiously.

Crunch, crunch. Before Merlin could move his hand, this egg cracked open by itself, and the thing inside broke out of the shell--

A silver-haired little girl suddenly broke out of the shell, with a cracked half-egg shell on her head, her small body mostly curled up in the eggshell.

She had some baby fat, her face was quite cute, and with her eyes closed, it seemed as if she hadn't woken up yet?

"Achoo..." The silver-haired little girl sneezed, waking Merlin and Alice from their dreamlike state!

Merlin: ...

Alice: ...

The silver-haired little girl looked about one or two years old, and hadn't lost the innocence of a newborn. She continuously made soft sounds.

She rubbed her fat little hands over her eyes, and slowly opened them, only to reveal rubies that were extremely similar to Merlin's.

Watching the little girl who suddenly broke out of the shell, their minds went blank. The next second, they let out cries that would give the neighbors a headache--

"Ah!!!"

Hearing the two's exclamations, the silver-haired little girl raised her head in confusion, blinked her curious big eyes, and looked at daddy and mommy.

Because she had just spoken, the young daughter apparently didn't know how to speak well, and could only make a babyish "wah" sound from her throat.

"This... this this... what is this?!" Merlin, who was usually calm, unexpectedly became chaotic.

"I... I I I... I don't know either!" Alice's reaction was even more shocking, falling into a state of being at a loss.

Their chaotic looks were just like parents who had been found by a illegitimate child, except for surprise, they had no other thoughts.

This suddenly hatched little girl completely disrupted the two's peaceful life, making it hard for them to calm down.

"Uh... let's calm down..." Merlin suppressed the astonishment in his heart, intending to sort out his thoughts.

"Right, we need to calm down." Alice nodded, lightly patting her chest.

"Do you really not know what this child is?" Merlin looked at Alice with suspicion.

"Nonsense! How could I know?" Alice glared at Merlin in anger.

"Come, look carefully. Why does this child look so much like you, especially the face..." Merlin looked at the little girl's appearance, frequently hinting.

"Is that so? It really seems like that... No! Wait!" Alice suddenly had a major discovery, suspiciously hinting, "This child obviously looks like you! Look at the eyes, almost exactly the same!"

"Is that so? Er! It really is a bit like me..." Merlin was dumbfounded, his mind went blank.

"Merlin, are you... hiding something from me?" Alice suspected, feeling a faint greenish tinge on her head.

"What are you implying? I'm clean! Don't think wildly!" Merlin like a cat that had stepped on its tail, almost jumped up on the spot, quickly explaining to prove his innocence.

"..." Alice quietly stared at Merlin, obviously not believing his explanation.

At this time, the little girl nestled in the eggshell, curiously sticking out her small head, and came near Alice, sniffing with her nose, showing a look of surprise--

"Wah... wah... wooden horse... maybe... mommy..."

Although the silver-haired little girl's pronunciation was unclear, she could only speak according to instinct, she could still understand the meaning.

"!!!" Alice instantly froze on the spot, and quickly explained, "No... no. I'm not the mommy!"

"Alice, you... have something hidden from me, don't you?"

Merlin, with a dark face, wanted to say something but stopped, feeling that Alice's explanation was pale and powerless, because this child really looked like Alice.

He couldn't describe what was in his heart, only "bitter" could describe it, and a familiar melody echoed in his mind—

Love is a ray of light, so beautiful~?

title: Chapter 4 — Countermeasures
content:
Chapter 4 — Countermeasures

Volume 24 · Chapter 4

"No!" Alice frowned, hastily explaining, "It's not what you think! I'm not! I didn't!"

"No wonder the child looks like you, so that's how it is..." Merlin felt uneasy, as if there was a hint of green on his head, "When exactly did this happen? Could you tell me? I'm not angry, just quite surprised."

"What nonsense are you spouting?! I'm innocent, believe me!" Alice was almost crying from anxiety, not knowing how to explain to make Merlin believe her, so she approached the mysterious little girl, "You... can you understand what we're saying? Mommy isn't just shouting randomly, you got it wrong, right?"

The silver-haired toddler in the eggshell blinked her eyes, not quite understanding, curiously staring at Merlin and Alice, and called out in a babyish voice, "Mommy... ee-ya~"

"Alice, the child looks so much like you, don't bother explaining anymore, I understand. I'll leave on my own tomorrow..." Merlin sighed bitterly.

"Ugh!" Alice felt a bit dizzy, quickly rubbing her temples, thinking that even jumping into the Yellow River wouldn't wash this clean!

However, at that moment, the silver-haired toddler stared at Merlin for a while, then stretched out her chubby little hands and placed them on his chest.

The little girl suddenly broke into a goofy smile, showing her baby teeth, looking exceedingly cute and very close to Merlin.

"...What are you doing?" Merlin, unaccustomed, shrank back a bit, not knowing how to handle a small child.

.......... The silver-haired toddler, speaking in a babyish voice with unclear pronunciation, sneezed, "Ah-choo~!"

"She... she seems to want to say something?" Alice said based on her intuition.

"Daddy!" The silver-haired toddler, after holding it in for a while, finally said what she wanted to express.

Both of their faces darkened at once, overwhelmed by this child, feeling like this was a random claim of kinship!

The atmosphere in the room turned awkward, with Alice beside them already giving a murderous look, putting immense pressure on Merlin.

"Don't shout randomly! I'm not your dad!" Merlin quickly denied.

"Merlin,... Alice's face darkened as she coldly questioned, "Did you go out and find a fox spirit while I wasn't around?"

"Don't... don't spread dirty rumors, this child clearly resembles you more..." Merlin said, forcing himself to speak, feeling guilty.

"Nonsense! We just look alike; look at her eyes, they're practically a copy of yours!" Alice's veins bulged on her forehead, she clenched her fists, a violent chill surfaced, "Tell me! Who have you been sneaking around with?!"

"I didn't!" Merlin broke into a cold sweat, quickly shaking the silver-haired toddler in his arms, "Little ancestor! Don't talk nonsense, I really am not your dad, I'm still an older unmarried young man!"

"Guh-ma.-I The silver-haired toddler suddenly showed a wronged expression, as if she could see that Mom and Dad didn't like her, so she pitifully pressed her lips together, tears welling up in her eyes, this look of enduring injustice while trying to stay strong was exactly like Alice.

"Hey! .... Merlin felt this little kid was about to throw a tantrum.

"Don't be like that, we didn't say anything." Alice hurriedly suppressed her anger, realizing this child was unusually sensitive.

"Goo-goo...." The silver-haired toddler frequently made sad sounds from her throat, tears that had not flowed for a long time poured down like a stream, "Waa-waa.C)广牡J玩"

The two watched the toddler's expression turn awkward; it was the first time they'd encountered such a situation, and waves of guilt surged in their hearts--

Merlin: "It's all your fault."

Alice: "Nonsense, it's clearly you who scared her..."

After a few hours passed, the room seemed to have temporarily returned to calm.

The silver-haired little girl cried and fussed for a while, and the two kept soothing her until her emotions stabilized.

This made Merlin and Alice quite embarrassed, and they no longer dared to casually deny the "mommy and daddy" thing.

The peace they had barely maintained was shattered here, Merlin felt a headache, not knowing how to deal with it.

Alice brought a vegetable basket, placed many soft clothes inside, and made it into a makeshift crib.

Whether it was from crying herself tired or not, the little girl soon fell into a deep sleep in the basket, her mouth continuously making a "hiss-hiss" breathing sound.

"Finally.... quiet"

Alice rocked the basket, let out a breath, and was frazzled from the ordeal.

".Ah.... Merlin nodded, looking at the big hole in the roof, helplessly saying, "What kind of karma have we created? Why do we keep running into things like this...."

"Speaking of which, why does this child look so much like you? I need an explanation." Alice said with a cold face.

"I was saying it looks like you too!" Merlin exclaimed, rolling his eyes in anger.

"..... The silver-haired toddler let out a soft whimper from the basket, seemingly hearing the argument and feeling uncomfortable.

Alice furrowed her brows, made a shushing gesture, "Shh, keep it down..."

"..... Merlin sighed, gradually calming down, "Let's not jump to conclusions first; this child resembles both of you a bit, we both need an explanation.

"Indeed, there are some imaginative similarities with us...." Alice looked at the little girl in the basket, couldn't help but reach out and touch her cheek, "This kid.... really is adorable, tiny, and when asleep looks very peaceful.

"Hiss-hiss~" The silver-haired toddler made a comfortable sound, clearly enjoying Alice's caress, wondering what pleasant dream she was having.

"This has nothing to do with her being cute, right?" Merlin frowned seriously, saying, "She resembles us so much that there's bound to be something strange; shouldn't we be on guard? Thinking about how this child suddenly appeared beside us, it's all quite extraordinary—could someone be intending to harm us?"

"Harm?" Alice lowered her head to look at the little girl in the basket, feeling there was no hostility, "No way, she's just a one- or two-year-old baby...."

"Tsk! Alic... Merlin turned his head, reminding, "Did you forget how Cain almost got us killed?"

"Uh! This"

Alice immediately recalled the child rescued from the dungeon, who still left her with some lingering fear; that was their most dangerous moment!

She slowly lowered her head, gazing at the cute little life in the basket, her eyes shifting continuously, her heart becoming torn--

Although Merlin was right, no matter how cute this child is, we should still be cautious, after all we've suffered a loss before.

But such a tiny child who can't even speak clearly—could she really become as vicious as Cain?

Alice hesitated, unsure what attitude to take toward this suddenly appearing child; obviously the psychological shadow left by Cain was not small.

"Exactly, that Cain incident is a lesson from the past; we should keep an eye out, but her mental state is undoubtedly that of a child, so it's best not to neglect her just because Cain once harmed us."

Merlin thought it over, felt it wasn't excessive, nodded and said, "Sure, as long as we stay alert, I guess this kid won't cause any trouble... but what should we do afterward? This child can't stay with us forever, right?"

Their gazes locked onto the little girl's face in the basket; at this moment, they faced the primary problem—

Alice: "Right, we can't keep her with us forever, even though she looks somewhat like us, we aren't her biological parents."

Merlin: "Who knows who her parents really are? Abandoning a child like that is utterly irresponsible; they really deserve a good scolding..."

Their child arrived as expected, without breaking promises, right in the first half of the year.

Then onwards, we'll update according to the 19-year add-on immediate system; hope everyone gives enthusiastic support!

title: Chapter 5 — Chris
content:
Chapter 5 — Chris

Volume 24 · Chapter 5

Alice stretched out her finger, curiously poking the silver-haired little girl's cheek, and the touch was unexpectedly soft and springy.

The little girl seemed to feel the tickle, shrinking her neck in her sleep and kicking her small legs.

Alice was instantly infected, her heart overflowing with affection, and she became subtly entranced.

"This child is really so cute..."

"Hey, Alice, put away your maternal aura, didn't we agree to stay vigilant? You're surrendering too quickly, aren't you?" Merlin's face darkened, and the more he looked at Alice, the more he felt she was unreliable, clearly not someone to be counted on.

"What's the problem? I'm just teasing her a bit, why are you being so cautious?" Alice felt Merlin was being overly tense, and the child in the basket couldn't even speak clearly, obviously not as threatening as Cain.

"We just agreed to be on guard, did you ignore that?" Merlin's brows furrowed.

"I didn't... if we're too cold, this child will cry again, are you willing to comfort her?" Alice countered.

"...cough!" Merlin disliked trouble and was momentarily at a loss for words, changing the subject, "Then... let's discuss how to handle this child?"

"...Alice stared at the little girl in the basket, her heart stirring, then said seriously, "Let's raise her."

"Ah?!" Merlin was taken aback, incredulous, "Has your brain gone bad? You want to raise her? Think about Cain's situation, aren't you tired of trouble?"

"Don't keep bringing up Cain, must we avoid children for the rest of our lives? You're being too paranoid, Merlin..." Alice frowned slightly, with a hint of complaint.

"I'm just thinking of our safety," Merlin shrugged.

"But this child doesn't seem aggressive at all, even if she stays with us, it shouldn't be a problem?" Alice rebutted.

"Cain used to call you 'mom' nonstop, did she show any aggression?" Merlin said righteously.

"Show..." Alice suddenly said.

"Hmm?" Merlin was stunned, feeling Alice was hiding something.

"I saw Cain drive away Camilla, giving me a chance to counterattack, but at the time, I didn't pay attention, thinking Camilla was just careless. Looking back, I should have noticed Cain had issues... Alice paused, looking at the little girl in the basket, "This child is different from Cain, she hasn't shown any bad behavior, we saw her hatch, clearly just a baby. Treating her like Cain... isn't that too much?"

Merlin lowered his head, feeling Alice had some reason, and his tone softened, "I just don't agree with adopting someone with an unknown background, who knows what she'll do in the future?"

"I'm just saying we'll temporarily take care of her, if her real parents find her, we'll return her. What she does in the future isn't our responsibility," Alice said reasonably.

...Merlin stared into Alice's eyes for a while, seeing she wasn't joking, and nodded casually, "Do as you like, but don't be reluctant if her parents come looking."

"I won't," Alice vowed, continuing to stroke the silver-haired girl's cheek, finding it exceptionally interesting.

...The little girl in the basket slowly woke up, rubbing her eyes.

"Huh?" Alice hadn't expected to wake her, wondering if it was because she hadn't been rocking the basket.

The silver-haired girl lifted her head, saw Alice, and smiled brightly, "Mommy! Ga ga ga!"

"Ah..." Alice hesitated, reaching out to pat the little girl's head, "Good baby~"

...The silver-haired girl's face turned slightly red, not resisting, looking very content, and curiously glanced at Merlin, calling in a milky voice, "Daddy~"

"Eh!" Merlin felt as if he'd been struck in the chest, utterly unable to adapt, refusing to accept the reality of being a father, and turned away with a proud, cold demeanor, warning others to stay away.

Grrr... The silver-haired girl became sad again, making kitten-like and puppy-like sounds in her throat, pouting with tears welling up.

...Alice glared at Merlin, her eyes full of blame for his lack of cooperation.

"Cough cough!" Merlin lightly coughed to cover his embarrassment, unable to withstand the pressure, and responded, "I'm here..."

"Daddy! Daddy! Daddy!" The silver-haired girl was extremely happy, calling nonstop, her bright eyes smiling like crescent moons.

Merlin lowered his head, covering his face, thinking, don't call me that, it's super embarrassing!

I never thought I'd have a kid calling me daddy nonstop!

No... compared to that Cain, this child is clearly more affectionate, actually willing to get close to me?

The feeling is a bit complicated... is this what it's like to be a father? Hehehe~

Hehehe, damn it! Calm down! Calm down a bit!

Merlin forcefully suppressed his strange interest, which seemed at odds with his cold exterior, but he was secretly delighted.

"Come here, let mommy hold you..." Alice picked up the little girl from the basket, but her words caught in her throat as she sensed something off, and she turned to Merlin, "Why don't we give her a name?"

"What?!" Merlin's brows furrowed, "You want to give her a name? Wait a minute! Are you serious? What right do we have to name her?"

"Naming her temporarily is fine, isn't it? Otherwise, it's inconvenient to take care of her, we can't keep calling her 'baby'..." Alice felt it was somewhat troublesome, having just met the little girl and realizing she didn't even have a name.

"...It's not a big deal, but what name should we give her?" Merlin pondered.

"Do you have any good ideas?" Alice asked curiously.

"...Merlin hesitated, his mind filled with the tune of a shampoo commercial, thinking of a name? I'm not good at this! I can only try to come up with something, "Cough... let's call her Meigou Dan, 'Mei' represents her meeting me, 'gou' means easy to raise, and 'dan' is because she was born from an egg, how's that? It's quite memorable."

...The silver-haired girl looked disappointed, clearly not liking the name "Daddy" had given her, showing some rejection.

Alice's face was expressionless, thinking she had been too naive to expect anything beautiful from Merlin's mouth, just go die, even the baby is starting to dislike you...

"? ? ?" Merlin's mind was full of question marks, thinking, is my name that bad? It's just a temporary name, why be so serious?!

"That..." Alice thought carefully, then suddenly had an idea, "Chris, let's call her Chris..."

"Ga ga!" The silver-haired girl's eyes lit up, responding in a milky voice, clearly liking the name.

"Chris, from now on you'll be called Chris, mommy's precious Chris..." Alice smiled.

...Chris happily raised her chubby little hands, laughing as if accompanied by pink flower petal effects, infectious to all.

"Ga ga! ^
