".....Merlin let out a long sigh, realizing Chris being in the middle makes arguing inconvenient, so he prepared to get up and said, "Since Chris is already asleep, I'll go out; my broken sofa is more comfortable." Alice bit her lip, feeling Merlin cold, but deep down she didn't want him to leave. Before, she couldn't find an excuse to let Merlin come sleep over; now, thanks to Chris, she finally had a legitimate reason to let him stay. But Merlin seemed unmoved, planning to slip out as soon as Chris fell asleep? Alice felt both anxious and angry, watching Merlin rise to leave, and finally couldn't help but whisper, "No need to go back to the sofa to sleep; just stay here..." . "Huh?" Merlin's movement to get up stopped abruptly, and he became even more puzzled about what Alice meant. "Don't go, stay here, since you've come all this way..." Alice said, blushing, relieved that it was late and the light was dim; otherwise Merlin seeing her expression might make things even more awkward. "Forget it, actually I'm not used to sleeping in your bedroom; I'm no longer the little kid from before, and being this close to you—can you really relax?" Merlin said half-jokingly. ".... Alice wanted to speak but held back, thinking that Merlin turning into a kid earlier was also nice, holding him while sleeping was just an excuse; she just wanted to be close to Merlin. Just as Alice found a good reason to keep Merlin staying, she suddenly saw Chris's small hands tightly gripping both of their hands.... "You can't go." "Why?" "Chris is holding onto you; if you leave, she'll definitely wake up, so you'd better stay." Alice said seriously. "Pulling a ghost? When kids sleep, they basically have no reaction to the outside world." Merlin didn't believe it, gently moved his hand, trying to escape Chris's tiny palm? But the sleeping Chris immediately reacted, her expression turned tense, and she mumbled in her sleep, "...... Dad....." ".....A cold sweat trickled down Merlin's forehead, thinking he couldn't even move a bit? This little ghost is too sensitive? "Look." Alice proudly lifted her head, head, and said, "You'd better just stay put honestly; otherwise this kid will keep clamoring to sleep on the sofa with you." "Tch! Such a clingy little brat.... Merlin gave in, flopped down with his whole body, and gave up the idea of leaving. The two lay still on the bed, their hands linked by a small child's two hands, making it hard to separate. They stared blankly at the ceiling, never imagining they'd ever face such a situation? Suddenly appearing little baby, not knowing how to handle it, and even less knowing how to face the life ahead— Alice: "That.. is so awkward..." Merlin: "Yeah, because of this little brat, I feel like I've got insomnia..." The first ray of morning sunlight streamed through the curtains, turning the bedroom into a warm pale gold. Last night, because the two couldn't adapt to the new situation, they stayed up all night, both ending up with panda eyes. "Finally morning...." Alice said wearily. "How come you didn't sleep all night? Are you afraid I'm plotting something?" Merlin asked, staring at her dark circles. "GUN! Mind your own business? Why didn't you sleep?" Alice shot back. "...." Merlin paused, then said quietly, "I'm afraid you're plotting something against me." Alice's eyebrows immediately knotted, her teeth itching with anger, "Your face is too thick; I don't want to talk to you." "Each to their own." Merlin replied wearily. It seemed Chris was the one sleeping most comfortably; she smacked her lips, swallowed her saliva. Then she turned sideways, placed her two small hands on Merlin's chest, and muttered indistinct dream talk. "Is Dad....." Immediately after, Chris turned again, placed her two small hands on Alice's chest, and continued her dream talk. "Still Daddy" Then Chris panicked, started having a nightmare, became very uneasy, and muttered in her mouth— "Dad's not good, something big happened...". "Mom's gone, hurry go find Mom" 。.°(>_ _∞)°●。

content:
Chapter 19 — <<<BEGIN TRANSLATION>>> Not the slightest clue (bonus chapter) <<<END TRANSLATION>>>

Volume 24 · Chapter 19

"Find mom... Mom's gone."

Little Chris seemed to have had a nightmare, frightenedly speaking in her sleep, her two short legs kicking wildly.

In the dream, Chris felt extremely nervous because she couldn't find her mom, thinking mom didn't want her anymore?

Although Chris was very young and said things without thinking, not teasing her mom on purpose.

But after hearing Chris's sleep-talking, Alice's face turned ugly—

What does this mean? Even Chris is mocking my figure?

No! Why is this so? Just because I'm small, so they made me the second dad?

Alice lowered her head, feeling unprecedented pressure, being roasted by Chris at such a young age!

"Pu!" Merlin couldn't help it and actually laughed out loud.

"Laugh what?!" Alice was furious, her heart so ashamed she wanted to kill to silence herself.

"Ahh... sorry, ha... it was too hard to hold it in." Merlin's whole body trembled, almost injuring himself from holding it in.

"Get out! I don't want to see you!" Alice transferred her anger to the innocent Merlin.

"Don't be angry, what a kid says shouldn't be taken seriously, just said casually." Merlin held back his laugh to comfort Alice, actually agreeing with Chris's reaction in his heart—feeling male-like pectoral muscles, doesn't that mean mom ran away and there are two dads now?

"Really? She can't even recognize me anymore, actually thinking I'm dad too." Alice looked depressed, as if losing her lifelong goal, "Why do you treat me like this? Is it saying I'm not qualified to be a mother?"

Seeing Alice start to give up on herself, Merlin stopped smiling, "No no no, Chris is young, a bit confused about gender is normal, has nothing to do with your... figure."

"I'm already over twenty, really hopeless..." Alice looked at her own flat chest.

"...." Merlin looked weird, still couldn't help telling the truth, "Haha, definitely hopeless, can only barely get by with pads."

"You?!" Alice's face turned black, grinding her teeth in anger, jumping up to grab Merlin's neck and shake him, "Shut up! I won't listen! Forget it! Forget about this!"

Facing Alice's painless protest, Merlin rolled his eyes and sighed—

"Ahh, why bother?"

"Why won't you face reality?"

"Living in a daydream, is that fun?"

After Chris woke up, she didn't notice anything unusual, not knowing her sleep-talking made Alice feel so embarrassed.

Only knowing that both parents didn't look good this morning—dark circles, looking tired.

Chris couldn't figure out why both parents slept on the soft big bed, which should be more comfortable, but why did they look more tired?

And Chris noticed mom was in a bad mood this morning, looking ugly early on, seeming fierce, giving dad a cold shoulder.

Although Alice still looked like a kind mom, a child's sixth sense is sharp, Chris still sensed something?

So Chris didn't dare bother mom, just stuck to dad, watching the newspaper with him.

Chris sat on Merlin's lap with starry eyes, curiously looking at the newspaper in his hands, "Dad~, what's this? So many little ants on it, and colorful."

"This is a newspaper, many things happening outside are recorded on it, the little ants are text, the colorful parts are pictures, all scenes from outside." Merlin looked at Chris's back of the head, patiently explaining, feeling his temperament changed after being dad for two days, at least becoming much gentler.

"Wow~, newspaper!" Chris tried hard to learn new things, eyes shining at the pictures, "Scenes from outside..."

"What's wrong? It's actually just ordinary stuff." Merlin explained.

"Chris wants to see outside!" Chris suddenly turned around, looking at Merlin with eager hope, hoping dad would take her.

"Uh, this..."

Merlin immediately felt embarrassed, estimating that if outside Chris called him and Alice mom and dad, everyone would find it strange. Obviously realizing Chris wasn't biological, how would this kid look at him if the truth came out?

In the kitchen, busy Alice pricked up her ears. Making breakfast was their weekly rotation, so this week was her turn.

Alice quietly pricked up her ears, carefully listening to every word outside between father and daughter. Hearing Chris wanted to go see outside, she also felt embarrassed.

But Alice thought on her own, doubting if keeping Chris at home was right?

As Merlin said, if always staying home, wouldn't it be bad for Chris's growth? People would turn bad?

Alice didn't want Chris to develop the habit of staying home from young age, should go out more, so after growing up and seeing the world, wouldn't be scammed.

These were Alice's own experiences. She felt it was bad that the teacher always kept her on the snowy mountain, was tricked into becoming a Hero in one go, almost becoming a decoy!

Alice naturally didn't want Chris to follow her old path. If not for good luck, she might have died several times. The pits she encountered, she couldn't let her daughter encounter them again.

Merlin felt considerable pressure there, thinking hard and starting to talk nonsense, "Outside is not good at all, especially dangerous, everywhere are hungry bloodthirsty beasts."

"Beasts? What kind of thing?" Chris's fluffy hair turned into question marks.

"Just..." Facing Chris's many childish questions, Merlin felt a headache, "They'll eat you, you won't see mom and dad anymore, understand?"

"...." Chris's little face turned pale, showing panic, looking at the colorful newspaper, "I won't look outside then, I want to always see mom and dad..."

"Good~" Merlin patted Chris's little head, thinking: Sure enough still a child, easy to fool~

Chris sat on Merlin's lap, poking her head out to sneak a peek at Alice in the kitchen, "Dad..."

"Hmm? What again? Find the newspaper boring?" Merlin looked down at Chris.

"Not really, just..." Chris continued sneaking looks at Alice in the kitchen, "Mom seems to be in a bad mood early this morning? Always feel she's angry..."

"....." Merlin chuckled, couldn't help internally cursing, you little brat, shameless asking? Why angry? Isn't it because you talked nonsense hurting Alice's self-esteem?

"Dad knows why? I can go comfort mom..." Chris said very maturely.

"Why? This..." Merlin frowned, left right thought then secretly whispered to Chris—

"Your mom's menopause."

title: Chapter 20 — Little Spy
content:
Chapter 20 — Little Spy

Volume 24 · Chapter 20

"What do you mean by 'menopause'?" Chris asked, confused.

Merlin cleared his throat and glanced at Alice in the kitchen. Seeing that she wasn't looking, he whispered, "It's when some women get grumpy after a certain age, like your mom."

"....Mom is still young..." Chris frowned, her small eyebrows knitted together.

"It's early." Merlin replied with a smirk.

"? ? ?" Chris still didn't understand what Dad meant, thinking that Mom must have something on her mind to be so unhappy.

Alice was washing dishes in the kitchen last night, wiping her hands on her apron, and then said, "Chris, go eat. Stop clinging to Dad."

Merlin put the newspaper aside and picked up Chris, who was sitting on his lap, patting her bottom. "Hurry, go eat."

"Okay~" Chris responded, shaking her head with her silly hair, and ran to the dining table.

Merlin was also hungry, so he followed suit. Looking at Alice, he asked, "What did you make? Won't it be some discounted bread and jam that's about to expire? Please don't be so stingy...."

"Why do you think I always make these things for breakfast?" Alice frowned.

"Because you're so thrifty. Every time there's a big discount at the market, you rush out like you'll miss it if you're late." Merlin muttered.

SE novel

"....Alice's face turned red, and she said awkwardly, 'Saving a little isn't a bad thing. Don't you think you're being wasteful, like you are?'"

"Tsk! Do you need me to teach you the joy of living?" Merlin tilted his mouth.

"Just shut up. If you're like you, we'd be sleeping on the streets by now. Don't think I don't know you spend a little money on horse racing tickets. I've told you a hundred times that relying on luck to turn things around is a fairy tale."

"Okay, okay, you're right." Merlin replied reluctantly, wanting to go eat directly, but was stopped by Alice. "What's up? Is there something else?"

"Wait, let's talk about Chris first." Alice said seriously.

Merlin was stunned, scratching his head. "I don't see any problems with her?"

"Don't misunderstand. I thought carefully and realized that keeping Chris at home isn't good. She should go out and see the world.... Alice looked down, showing a thoughtful expression."

"Huh? You weren't afraid Chris would know things and oppose her going out, right? How did you change your mind?" Merlin looked at Alice in surprise.

"Chris needs to grow. She must experience the outside world, or... she might be too naive and get bullied." Alice looked like a concerned mother, worrying about her daughter's future.

"Yeah, but what if we run into someone familiar? Wouldn't that expose us? I'm worried that if we meet Hobbs, he'll spill the beans in a minute." Merlin was also concerned.

"We'll be careful and try to stay away from the Adventurers Guild. That way, it's hard to run into familiar people." Alice suggested.

Merlin thought carefully and nodded. "Okay."

At the dining table, Alice watched Chris beside her.

Meanwhile, Merlin sat across from them, chewing on bread that was about to go bad, thinking--

As I suspected, Alice is still so stingy, eating these things every day. I'm almost ready to give up!

Chris held up her bottle, sucking it happily, occasionally making happy humming sounds.

"Slow down, don't be so...." Alice wiped Chris's mouth.

Merlin looked at Chris and had an idea. He said persuasively, "Chris, do you want to eat something delicious?"

"What~" Chris was curious and put down her bottle.

"To be honest, Dad's cooking is very good. Do you want to try it?" Merlin smiled.

"Yes!" Chris was interested, even though she didn't know what Dad made, but something made by Dad must be good!

"Did you hear that, Alice? Let's improve the family's diet with our savings, and don't be so stingy. Even a little kid can't eat milk all the time, right?" Merlin said seriously.

"You stop trying to manipulate people. Chris is still young and can't eat random things. Drinking milk is enough for now." Alice rolled her eyes, thinking that even a child had to be used, and Merlin was still a decent person?

"Well, Chris wants to eat, right?" Merlin said with a righteous tone, but was actually thinking about having a big meal. "No one should cry over a crying baby, haha...."

Alice saw Merlin laughing and rolled her eyes. "Shut up. Using a crying child as a bargaining chip to satisfy your own desires, do you have any shame?"

"Mom, I also eat what Dad makes...." Chris bravely expressed her thoughts.

"See? She won't lie. Giving her some good food isn't a problem. You're such a bad mom~" Merlin showed an evil smile and put a big hat on Alice's head.

"...." Alice felt the pressure and recalled that Chris wasn't a real baby. She had teeth when she was born, so she could say, occasionally a few times, it's not a big deal....

"Yay~" Chris hugged her mom tightly, rubbing against her. "Mom is the best."

"......Alice's face turned red, very enjoyable. She changed the subject and asked, "Chris, do you want to go out and see the world? There are many things you haven't seen outside..."

Chris was stunned and showed a fearful expression. "No, I don't want to go out!"

"Why?" Alice was stunned. Just a moment ago, she was very happy to see the outside world, but now she was suddenly afraid.

"Dad said there are big monsters outside that will eat Chris, and I won't see Dad and Mom anymore."

Chris said with conviction.

Alice was filled with question marks and smiled calmly. "Don't listen to Dad. He just likes to talk nonsense, and most of what he says isn't true. There are many fun things outside, and there are no big monsters. At least not in the town."

"Really?" Chris's worldview was shaken and believed Alice. She looked at Merlin across from her and puffed out her cheeks, looking unhappy. "Dad is a bad person. Dad is lying."

Merlin hesitated, thinking that he was just trying to help Alice. Now, he was also his own fault?

Chris was deceived and became unhappy, so she decided to be a little spy. "Mom is not happy today. Dad also said Mom is in menopause because she's too old, which must be fake. Mom is so beautiful...."

"Hey, Merlin...." Alice looked up and glared at Merlin. "What were you telling her?"

"Cough cough!" Merlin's forehead dripped with cold sweat and explained. "You shouldn't believe it. Kids.... can't take it seriously."

"You just said that kids won't lie." Alice's face turned even more unpleasant.

"....Merlin was speechless, patted his head, and sighed. "This traitor..."

In the future, I can't say bad things about Chris's mom in front of her.

title: Chapter 21 — "Words and Deeds" <<<BEGIN SOURCE>>> SOURCE TEXT: <<<END SOURCE>>>
content:
Chapter 21 — "Words and Deeds" <<<BEGIN SOURCE>>> SOURCE TEXT: <<<END SOURCE>>>

Volume 24 · Chapter 21

The family of three arrived at the busiest market in Wrexham, letting Chris take a good look at the outside world.

The market bustled with people coming and going, vendors' cries rising and falling without end, a lively spectacle.

Alice held Chris in her arms. Everything around them filled her with boundless novelty; she let out constant exclamations of wonder, her little face written all over with excitement.

For the newly born Chris, anything could spark her interest. Like a curious baby, she kept asking what each thing before her was.

Watching Chris's adorably silly expression, Alice felt both exasperated and amused. She patiently explained everything to her, letting her learn as much new knowledge as possible.

As the family of three walked the streets, they drew curious glances from passersby from time to time. At the sight of the young, innocent Chris, everyone would break into kindly smiles.

Merlin walked beside the two of them, watching Alice ahead. Warm sunlight filtered through her hair tips, making her whole person radiate a light that soothed the soul.

At this moment Merlin suddenly felt he had aged a great deal. Not only because Chris's arrival had inexplicably made him a "dad,"

but because Merlin had always been struggling against his own curse, living aimlessly, which left his whole being restless.

Suddenly getting to enjoy a normal person's peaceful life — Merlin found it a little hard to adjust, yet he did not dislike such a boring existence.

If it could stay like this forever, that would be nice too. Is this the life I've been longing for?

Carefree, together with the person I like, able to hold my cute little daughter and stroll around every day.

I really have no ambition, thinking about retiring this quickly.

Merlin lowered his head, muttering in his heart, but he knew clearly that what lay before him was only temporary. As long as the curse was not lifted, he could never truly be at ease.

"Merlin!"

"Huh?"

"What are you thinking about? I called you several times." Alice, holding little Chris, turned her head back.

Merlin snapped back to reality, realizing he had just spaced out. "What is it?"

"Just now I saw you looking absent-minded. Are you worried about something again?" Alice asked tentatively.

"Does Daddy have worries?" Chris blinked her eyes curiously.

"No, no, no. What worries could I have? Just didn't sleep well last night, a bit tired is all." Merlin hid his embarrassment with a forced smile.

"Rare chance to bring Chris out once. Focus a little." Alice chided.

"Daddy~ cheer up!" Chris raised her tiny fist, as if cheering Merlin on.

"Good, no problem." Merlin chuckled, reaching out to poke Chris's little cheek. "Are you tired?"

"Chris!" Chris patted her nonexistent biceps, little face serious. "Full of energy~"

"Hah." Merlin gave a dry laugh. He supposed so — with so many novel things to see, how could Chris be tired?

"Mommy! What's that?" Chris curiously pointed at a stall ahead, hung with colorful masks, the kind that easily catch a child's attention.

"Those are masks. Once you put one on, others can't recognize you." Alice explained.

"That magical?" Chris bit her finger, staring at the masks hanging on the stall, eyes full of hope.

"Want one?" Alice asked with a smile.

Chris hesitated, then blurted out, "Daddy said Mommy's really stingy. I don't want to make Mommy angry."

"What!?" A vein pulsed on Alice's forehead. She whipped around and glared at Merlin. "You're so despicable, badmouthing me behind my back? Where am I stingy!?"

"Tsk!" Merlin covered his face, thinking this kid really tells Alice everything. Don't I have any dignity as a dad?

"Don't listen to your daddy's nonsense. Mommy isn't stingy at all." Alice looked at little Chris in her arms, serious. "Whatever you like, Mommy will buy it for you right now!"

"Kyaa~" Chris laughed happily. "Mommy's the best~"

Merlin's face darkened behind them. He thought Chris was a cunning little brat — was she using reverse psychology? So young, yet so crafty.

Alice approached the stall, looked around, then asked Chris, "Which one do you like?"

Chris bit her finger, looked them over, and pointed at a silver mask. "This one!"

"This one..." Alice looked at the silver mask, a nostalgic expression crossing her face.

"Good eye!" The vendor immediately started buttering them up, taking the mask down and boasting, "This is the same model as the Great Sword Saint Elgin! The hottest style right now! Kids nowadays all love this type, they can't put them down!"

"Huh? Mommy, who's the Great Sword Saint Elgin?" Chris asked curiously. He sounded pretty amazing.

Merlin laughed behind them and said bluntly, "It's your dad."

"???" Chris's eyes darted around. She felt like she'd just been scolded by her dad?

"Merlin! What are you saying? Why are you swearing?" Alice glared at Merlin with a cold face, feeling he'd gone too far.

"Me???" Merlin pointed at himself in surprise, then sighed helplessly in his heart. Who swore? The Great Sword Saint Elgin is Chris's dad. What's the problem?

"Don't listen to your daddy's wild talk." Alice looked at little Chris in her arms and explained seriously, "The Great Sword Saint Elgin is an ally of justice, a hero of Britannia. He selflessly saved many people many times. He's the person Mommy admires most~"

Merlin rolled his eyes behind them, too lazy to explain further. If Alice knew the fault-ridden Merlin was the Great Sword Saint Elgin, her worldview would probably shatter!

Now Merlin believed in the saying "distance makes the heart grow fonder." Clearly the same person, but because the Great Sword Saint Elgin had never interacted with Alice, in her impression he was just a good gu—

"Mommy's admired person? Wow~" Chris's eyes filled with little stars. "I want to become an ally of justice too, become the person Mommy expects!"

"Good. Mommy looks forward to it." Alice patted Chris's head, secretly adding, "As long as you don't end up like your dad."

"Oi, that's too much." Merlin muttered with a black face, not feeling he had any faults at all.

"Hmph!" Alice gave a cold snort, ignored Merlin, gently set Chris down, then bought the Great Sword Saint Elgin mask and put it on her.

Chris put on the silver mask, lifted her head, and asked happily, "Mommy, can you tell who I am?"

"It's the evil-punishing, justice-upholding Great Sword Saint Elgin! Good job!" Alice played along with her daughter, using a chuunibyou tone.

"Kyaa~" Chris spun around happily, walking forward with steps that recognized no kin, as if no one could see her.

Merlin glanced at Alice's beaming face and said quietly, "Cough! Don't take it too seriously. We're just pretend parents. This kid's a sharp one, learning ability far beyond normal children. We should stay vigilant."

"What's it to you? Mind your own business." Alice gave Merlin a sidelong glance.

"Huh?" Merlin froze for a moment, then said with a straight face, "I think you're too deep in character. Need some electrotherapy to wake you up?"

"Chris is such a well-behaved child. You don't like her? I don't believe it~" Alice gave him a suspicious look.

"Me?" Merlin pointed at himself, then suddenly said with a cold face, "What I hate most are brat kids. How could I possibly like Chris? Don't lump me together with you. Even if my line ends with me, I'd never like this little brat Chris!"

Chris, wearing the mask, strolled happily down the street. Having just learned to walk, her steps were unsteady, and she tripped on a small stone.

"Guwu?"

Watching Chris about to fall flat on her face, Merlin rushed over at eighty kilometers per hour.

Like a glider, he scraped wildly against the ground, kicking up clouds of dust and sand!

Finally, one second before Chris's face hit the ground, he caught her. Merlin let out a long breath and said helplessly.

"Be more careful, my little pri—"

Chris shook her little short legs, steadied herself, turned back to see Merlin's gloomy face, and immediately went up and *pacha* kissed his forehead. "Daddy~"

"Uh..." Merlin's expression turned strange, finally breaking into a foolish grin as he muttered, "You little crafty brat, hehehe~"

"Ah..." Alice had been watching from behind, stunned. Black lines like a waterfall streamed down her forehead. She thought—

Saying you don't like her with your mouth, but your body's honest to a fault?

A classic tsundere.

title: Chapter 22 — As Always (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 22 — As Always (Bonus)

Volume 24 · Chapter 22

The central square of Rexham featured gushing fountains and flocks of white doves.

This was the place where Alice had been knighted as an honorary knight, and also the spot Rexham residents loved most for relaxing.

When the family of three arrived here, Alice had just sat down with Chris in her arms, but this little one’s attention was immediately drawn to the distant pigeons.

“Mommy, I want to go down and look at those...” Chris said in a baby voice, pointing at the distant pigeons.

“You want to see the pigeons?” Alice hesitated, afraid something might happen.

“Let her go; nothing bad will happen if we stay here,” Merlin nodded and said.

“Alright, but don’t run too far,” Alice warned, taking off Chris’s mask to let her move around freely.

“Okay, Mommy~” As soon as Chris hit the ground, she excitedly ran toward the flock of pigeons.

“Slow down!” Alice admonished sternly.

“Hey! Looking at your current state, if Chris’s biological parents showed up, I doubt you’d even be willing to hand her over,” Merlin sneered.

“Shut up! You’re not much better yourself; you say you don’t like it, but what about that flying tackle you did earlier when you picked up Chris after falling?” Alice retorted with a cold face.

Merlin was speechless, his old face turning red as he stammered, “I-I was just afraid she’d fall and cry, and then I’d have to comfort her. It would be such a hassle~”

“You’re just bragging. If you like her, just say it openly instead of acting so contradictory. It’s truly ridiculous,” Alice mocked.

“You’re the one being contradictory; how dare you talk about me?” Merlin muttered with a dark expression.

The two found each other increasingly annoying, and merely because Chris disappeared for a moment, they started arguing.

Merlin: “Hey!”

Alice: ‘

Over there, Chris ran over excitedly on her own, startling the pigeons into taking flight, which made them unwilling to get close to her.

Chris stopped in her tracks, looking at the pigeons she had scared away with a depressed expression, unable to understand why these birds wouldn’t pay attention to her.

Unwilling to give up, Chris called out to the pigeons in mid-air, as if believing they could understand her words.

“Here, here! Come to me!”

The pigeons circled above Chris’s head, refusing to land. Chris looked like a deflated ball, tightly pursing her small lips on the ground, staring at them from afar.

*Crash*, a mysterious sound came from behind Chris, and an elderly grandmother stood behind her.

The landlady looked at little Chris with a look of utter disbelief; at her feet lay a paper bag that had fallen to the ground, its contents unknown.

The landlady stared fixedly at Chris, her cloudy eyes blinking not once, extending a trembling hand as if wanting to touch her.

“It’s you?! Am I not dreaming? I didn’t expect to see you again.”

“Eh?” Seeing the aged landlady, Chris felt a bit frightened and instinctively shrank back. Who is this??

“Hm?” The landlady suddenly paused, a glimmer passing through her cloudy eyes before she sighed deeply. “So that’s how it is. You don’t remember anymore, I suppose. That’s right; you were killed long ago. To appear before me now means you must have received love and achieved rebirth. You are ultimately not her, yet you still radiate the same warm glow as before.”

“...” Chris grew increasingly frightened and shrank away, saying, “I don’t understand...”

“Don’t be afraid. We come from the same place. Like that person, I too once deeply loved the past.”

The landlady smiled kindly, bent down, and slowly picked up the paper bag from the ground.

Upon opening the paper bag, it was filled with breadcrumbs, nothing mysterious.

Seeing the landlady grab a handful of breadcrumbs, the white doves in the sky were instantly attracted, gathering around to peck at the bread in her hands.

It seemed the aged landlady came to the square to feed the pigeons whenever she had free time, and this flock was already very familiar with her.

Little Chris watched the landlady with envy, feeling that while the birds亲近ed her, they did not亲近 her. The old lady was truly a magical person.

The landlady smiled at Chris, grabbing a handful of breadcrumbs to offer her. “Would you like to try?”

Chris hesitated, feeling a bit timid, but couldn’t help nodding and extending her chubby little hand.

Chris, who disliked the breadcrumbs, finally attracted many white doves, and these birds were finally willing to get close to her.

Watching countless pigeons flap their wings, looking exceptionally beautiful, Chris cheered up excitedly.

“Eat more! Eat more! Swish swish~!”

An old woman and a young girl were surrounded by white doves. The landlady looked down at Chris, whose face was full of smiles, continuously sprinkling breadcrumbs from the paper bag.

Nearby by the fountain, Merlin and Alice were still arguing, their situation becoming somewhat unmanageable.

“Look, you’ve gotten too deep into character, treating Chris as your own daughter. Save it; she’ll be taken away sooner or later.”

“Shut up! You’re no better either; you show a silly smile every time you see Chris. It’s disgusting!”

“What did you say?! Can’t I even smile?”

“Wait! Stop arguing, look over there! It looks like the landlady.”

Both turned their heads toward Chris, seeing the landlady feeding pigeons together with Chris, chatting happily?

“Oh no! It really is the landlady! Our cover is blown!” Merlin frowned.

Alice made a decisive decision; taking advantage of the fact that they hadn’t chatted for long, she quickly stood up and called out, “Chris!”

“Hm?” Chris looked back at her mother blankly, quickly patting her breadcrumb-covered hands. “Mommy is calling me back.”

“Is that so? Mommy.” The landlady smiled kindly.

Chris took short steps running toward Merlin and Alice, but suddenly remembered something, so she stopped. “Mommy said, if you take something from someone else, you should say thank you. Thank you, Grandma!” d” SF Light Novel

“Your mother is an outstanding person; she is correct.” The landlady nodded.

Chris returned to Alice’s side and said happily, “That grandma gave me breadcrumbs, and I said thank you.”

“You’re such a good girl~” Alice hugged Chris anxiously.

“The grandma also said many strange things; I didn’t understand them~” Chris said in a baby voice.

“Don’t believe it! They’re all tricks to fool you; don’t believe anything she says.” Merlin said seriously, thinking it was fortunate that she was just a child, otherwise trouble would have ensued.

Merlin and Alice looked toward the distant landlady, both nodding in greeting, considering it a casual hello.

The landlady similarly waved her aged hand with a smile; it seemed she had no intention of approaching the two to chat.

Merlin and Alice felt somewhat guilty, like thieves, and hurriedly carried Chris home, not wanting to accidentally encounter any more familiar people.

The landlady’s aged figure stood among the white doves, watching the family of three leave, feeling somewhat lonely in her heart—

Are those two your new relatives?

But even so... I still can’t forget

The way you used to look down upon the mortal world, humming sacred songs softly.

title: Chapter 23 — A Hostile Arrival
content:
Chapter 23 — A Hostile Arrival

Volume 24 · Chapter 23

A few days passed, and because they suddenly ran into the landlady, Merlin and Alice became a bit nervous.
Fortunately, the landlady didn't pry; otherwise, the two wouldn't know how to explain.
But Chris had been cooped up at home for several days, gradually feeling bored and really wanting to go out for a walk.
Alice understood Chris's feelings; after all, she herself had similar boundless energy as a child, and being confined to a small space was unbearable.
After all, not everyone is like that Merlin guy—staying in the Death Swamp for two hundred years.
Unable to resist Chris's pleading gaze, Alice decided to take her to see the little donkey she had raised, to pass the boring time.
Chris is just a naive little kid; any random novel animal can make her happy for a long time.
In the stable, the little donkey Mengmeng was chewing on old grass, expressionlessly watching its master and little master.
Held in Alice's arms, Chris looked at the donkey with delight, 'Mommy~, what is this? It feels different from the big horses outside.'
'This isn't a horse, it's a donkey. Although it's not as fast as a horse, its endurance is still very good,' Alice patiently explained.
'Really? Its ears are so long,' Chris, biting her finger, thought, 'Just like the rabbit I saw at the market that day!'
'Do you think it's cute?' Alice asked tentatively.
'' Chris thought for a moment, then innocently said, 'Not as cute as a little bunny~'
Alice stared, thinking, 'Kids are really pragmatic; they always speak straight to the point.'
The little donkey Mengmeng calmly looked at the two figures before it, bared its big teeth, as if smiling? It made a donkey's distinctive sound.
Chris's eyes lit up, pointing at the donkey, 'Mommy, it can laugh too!'
'Yes, it's called Mengmeng. Mom raised it from little; it's about two years old, a bit older than you,' Alice said softly.
'Mengmeng? Mommy, I want to get down!' Chris slipped from Alice's embrace, grabbed a handful of hay and handed it over, 'Mengmeng eats grass!'
The little donkey Mengmeng lowered its head, looking at this silly kid; faced with food, it didn't refuse, opened its big mouth and started eating the hay.
After eating, it didn't forget to stick out its tongue and lick Chris's face, as if expressing gratitude?
'Ah!' Chris was licked on the butt by the donkey, sat on the ground with her bottom, getting donkey saliva all over her face, 'I'm not food, you can't eat me!'
The little donkey Mengmeng made a 'hee-haw' sound, split its mouth to show big front teeth, as if mocking the foolish little master.
Alice couldn't help but chuckle a few times, lifted Chris from the ground, took out a handkerchief and wiped the donkey saliva off her face.
But just then, a call came from outside; it seemed an unwelcome visitor had arrived here——
'Mr. Merlin! Miss Alice! Are you home?'
Outside, Shirley had brought the elf squad and already arrived here, knocking on the two's door.
Shirley kept lightly knocking and calling Merlin and Alice's names, unsure if they were home.
Hilf guarded beside Shirley, her expression somewhat unnatural, constantly looking left and right.
It wasn't just the pressure of this mission that made her feel uneasy; it was also her first time coming to the human world.
Hilf had thought the sinners' world was filled with misery and sorrow, that they might not even have enough to eat, that beggars would be everywhere, but the reality was not like that.
All along the way in the Kingdom of Britain, what she saw and heard made this elf, born and raised in the United Kingdom, feel different—orderly governance, people living in peace and contentment.
This gave Hilf's worldview a jolt; it seemed she had indeed been full of prejudice before, and the human world was nothing like she imagined.
No wonder when she spoke of humanity's many flaws, Merlin and Alice's gazes were like looking at a frog at the bottom of a well.
Aside from Hilf, whom Merlin and Alice know fairly well, there were many unfamiliar faces behind Shirley——
+ several elf knights wearing swords, standing solemnly, young and strong; although they tried to suppress their aura, one could still sense a faint, elusive mighty presence.
These elf knights, like Hilf, are the most elite and loyal guards under the Elf King, each having undergone strict training; staff in hand, eyes closed, meditating, they look like the kind you definitely don't want to provoke.
In front of the knights, an elder in white robes held——
——his presence. An elder sent by the Temple Intent; for this mission Shirley only——
'This old man must be the Elf King, worried that Shirley's softness would hinder the mission,'
'He's merely a door knocker; the real decision likely rests with this elf elder, his pointed ears hidden, secretly come to Rex——'
People disguised as merchants, using hair or hats to hide those trained elf knights, who are somewhat conspicuous; occasionally they would attract—— this remote town, on the road they didn't draw much attention, at most only——
drawing the townsfolk's sideways glances. They knocked on the door, but the long-closed door didn't budge at all.
'Mr. Merlin? Miss Alice? Are you home?' Shirley lightly—— 'Have we hit a snag? Your Highness, are you sure this is——'
'Hmph!' The elf elder gave a light snort, opened his eyes dissatisfiedly, and said,
'Is that the right place for those two?' He knocked on the door, awaiting the city's response.
'Yes, this is the place. I've been here before; Shirley sensed something? Did you deliberately avoid us?'
The elf elder pondered, doubtful, muttering: 'Could it be they've already noticed and continued their adventure? Maybe they're just away for a few days.'
'Probably not? It's only been a short while; they wouldn't be that fast.'
'?' Shirley said doubtfully. The old man said gloomily.
'A few days? How long is that? Our time is not much.' The elf elder said? Shirley suddenly suggested.
'Let's find a place to stay temporarily and wait for them... [This place is full of the stench of sinners; we, as noble——'
'No!' The elf elder frowned, sternly said, 'We can't tolerate it, not just me, the knights probably don't want to either—elves, to stay a few days with these filthy sinners? Forgive me——'
Having too much contact with the sinners? Anyway, they don't like humans, nor do they want to stay in the human world.
The elf elder behind him, the dozen or so elf knights, all showed looks of disgust,
Staying a long time. The earlier reaction was just like before, toward the sinners——
Hilf looked at her kin, sighed silently in her heart, the whole novel——
The people are full of contempt.
JSh Qing Ling elder's pressure is somewhat unavoidable.
'What should we do?' Shirley had no idea, facing forward, 'It's just staying a few days, nothing——'
'Old' Hilf couldn't stand it, stepping in front of Shirley, 'Are we not as good as you? Please be humble, don't be so confrontational. It's not a big deal; besides, you haven't seen any human civilization on this trip, clearly humans aren't all filthy.'
Confrontational, and besides, His Majesty has acknowledged Miss Alice as our friend, this splendid little town, giving a passionate speech, 'This small——'
'Ha, the elf elder slowly turned, gazing at the abundant wealth before him, but the vile humans have slaughtered how many non-human kinds,'
Town, no! It's the entire human world's land, which once belonged to our—— clan.
Taken our wealth, it's not something time can easily erase; human sins can't be washed away. Under the elder's provocation, hearts——
The elf knights' expressions turned grim, having been educated since childhood——
The hatred flame rose. To reclaim our clan's wealth, we will fight to the death against humans.
Probably just need the elder to give a command, and the knights are ready to launch an attack; one side thinks they're still excellent, the other feels the elder isn't wrong.
Shirley remained silent, her heart became conflicted, one side thinks humans——
'You guys' Chris's little hand walked over.
Just as the elves stood at the door hesitating, Alice was leading a sheep yet still wearing weapons, suddenly realized——
She saw the elves before her, all solemn, dressed as merchants——
These guys:
Unwelcome guests!

title: Chapter 24 — Belonging
content:
Chapter 24 — Belonging

Volume 24 · Chapter 24

The elves all turned around and saw Alice behind them, especially the little child beside her.

Chris felt so many strangers staring at her, feeling frightened, she quietly hid behind Alice, poked her head out, curiously sizing up this group of uninvited guests.

"Miss Alice" Hilf froze for a moment, then showed a polite smile, "You're back?"

"Is this the sinner His Majesty praised a while ago?" the elf elder asked in a low voice.

"Yes." Hilf nodded and replied softly.

"Alice!" Shirley rushed forward, gave Alice a big hug, and pressed her cheek against Alice's cheek, showing intimacy.

The elf elder showed a hint of displeasure, thinking that as a princess, Shirley shouldn't be so intimate with humans, it was improper!

"Alice" laughed embarrassedly, patted Shirley's back, "I didn't expect to see you again so soon. Why did you suddenly come to Rexham?"

"Shirley released Alice, showed a somewhat embarrassed expression, lowered her head looking at the child hiding behind her, "This is a long story. We rarely come to Rexham, won't you invite us in to sit? We can talk slowly."

"Sure." Alice nodded, although she didn't understand what these elves wanted to do, but as the host, she shouldn't neglect her friends.

"Mom" little Chris tiptoed and tugged Alice's hand, nervously asking, "Who are they?"

Alice thought for a moment, lowered her head and smiled in reply.

"They are Mom and Dad's friends."

In the bedroom, Chris sat on the bed, surrounded by toys Alice bought, playing with them by herself.

Alice stood outside the bedroom door, looking at Chris and instructing, "Mom and Dad are talking with the outside friends, don't come out to cause trouble, you should behave well in the bedroom, okay?"

"I know, Mom~" Chris said in a childish voice.

Alice felt a bit relieved, closed the bedroom door, then sat down with Merlin outside, and gave him a look indicating that Chris's side was fine.

Merlin let out a breath; he had just been sleeping in, so he hadn't heard Shirley knocking outside, and still didn't know what was happening.

However, Merlin saw that these elves were dressed up and wore sharp weapons, obviously not a trivial matter.

Merlin had already faintly sensed the threat from the distant Elf King; this was a rhythm of first showing off his muscles, then putting on a suit to act refined.

"So what brings you all here?"

Opposite them were a group of elves, Shirley and the elf elder sitting together, while Hilf and other elf knights stood behind guarding.

They had solemn expressions; it seemed they weren't here just to visit, but had important matters to discuss.

"Mr. Merlin, Shirley was a bit hesitant, but recalling her father's entrustment, she gathered courage to speak frankly: "You called them Mom and Dad, but they aren't really your parents, right?"

Alice's eyes shifted, then she lowered her head blankly, thinking that what was bound to come would come, she didn't expect them to show up so quickly; has living with that child already come to an end?

Merlin leaned back on the sofa, stroking his chin stubble, "Is she really your biological child? How could you possibly know?"

"We certainly know, that child" Shirley paused, then said seriously, "She belongs to our elf race."

"Ha" Merlin laughed, as if hearing a joke, "What nonsense? The child looks like a human, and lacks elf features—how could she possibly be yours?"

"Yeah, if she were your elf child, why are her ears different from yours?" Alice likewise felt doubtful.

"Rayli" was at a loss for words, because she's inarticulate, worried she'd say too much and get it wrong, she didn't know how to explain this to Merlin.

Beside them, the elf elder glanced at Shirley, secretly shook his head, and interjected, "I suppose you must be the youngest monarch of the demon race? I recently heard His Majesty mention it."

"What? Do you have something to teach us?" Merlin's tone carried a hint of anger.

"No no no, how could I dare to instruct you?" The elf elder wanted to draw closer, but Merlin seemed impervious to flattery, "I am the great elder of the elf race; I have long heard the name of Lucifer the Third, and have repeatedly repelled the Holy Church's"

Merlin sighed, interrupted, saying, "Stop the flattery, let's talk about serious matters."

"The elf elder awkwardly cleared his throat, inwardly cursing the arrogant Merlin, glad that in the interracial alliance the demon race didn't join, all are rude folks," "That child is indeed ours; our father god Korolon once left an egg, inside which gestates a life bearing his supreme divine power; legend says the child born from it can lead our tribe to prosperity—I'm sure you both know, it's the one in the bedroom"

"???" Shirley stared at the elf elder with a face full of surprise; as a princess she had never heard of such a thing—are you just making up stories?!

Everything the elf elder said was just to emphasize Chris's legitimacy as belonging to the elf race, not something obtained by accident.

Describing Chris as a life created by Korolon makes taking her back to the United Kingdom justified and seizes the moral high ground.

Merlin and Alice glanced at each other; the elf elder's words basically match the facts, especially Chris being born from an egg—could she really be an elf child?

"That egg was originally enshrined in the secret chamber of the Sacred Tree Palace; recently it inexplicably flew to your place, truly helpless; if this child has caused you trouble, I apologize on her behalf." The elf elder stood up, bowed to Merlin and Alice, adopting the posture of a guardian.

Merlin furrowed his brows and countered, "Since it was enshrined on your territory, why would it come looking for us? Isn't that too strange?"

The elf elder gave a dry laugh and continued, "A newborn child is naturally curious and playful; you two are the first outsiders in history to enter the Sacred Tree Palace; that child, while still in the egg, was attracted by your aura, so it flew to you; moreover, its appearance imitates you two, which is why it lacks elf traits, but it is indeed a life created by our father god, an elf child"

Merlin and Alice fell silent, believing the elf elder's words, after all they match the facts.

Chris indeed resembles Merlin and Alice; if the life in the egg deliberately imitated them, that also makes sense.

The two lowered their heads without speaking; it seems Chris truly is an elf child, and her parents have come to the door.

The elf elder knew Merlin and Alice would have doubts; he had prepared everything in advance, and taking Chris back was inevitable!

"That child is the precious wealth left by our father god Korolon; all elves are its kin; we cannot let her wander outside; we hope you will allow us to take her back.".

"Alice obviously hesitated; half a month of getting along made her fond of the well-behaved Chris; now sending her away? She finds it hard to accept."

Merlin furrowed his brows, his feelings similar to Alice's, and couldn't help but tentatively say,

"Since you've come here, it's also fate; why not just stay with us?"

"Don't worry, we will definitely not let her suffer." _

"What do you all think?"

MKX

title: Chapter 25 — Departure
content:
Chapter 25 — Departure

Volume 24 · Chapter 25

When Merlin said this, the elves' faces suddenly turned ugly, because they felt the other side had no intention of handing it over. Even Shirley and Hilf showed troubled expressions; if Chris isn't taken back to the United Kingdom, the Elf King's side would also be hard to explain. The atmosphere in the room suddenly became oppressive, with both sides scheming. "What do you two mean? Are you going to openly rob us?" the elf elder jumped up. "Don't misunderstand, we aren't trying to steal your child; we just want to temporarily take care of her," Merlin emphasized. "Thank you for your kindness, but this child is better off being brought back by us to raise personally," the elf elder said solemnly. "What if we don't agree?" Merlin said with a meaningful look. "You two are friends of the elf race, you helped us through a crisis; I hope our relationship doesn't become too strained." The elf elder paused, then began to appeal to emotion, "Besides, Princess Shirley thinks you are her best friends; she risked punishment to repay your lifesaving grace. Now you want to openly seize our child—this is hardly moral." Seeing the elf elder's gaze, Shirley felt considerable pressure and thus said, "Yeah, that child is the legacy left by our Father God, tied to our clan's future. Mr. Merlin, Miss Alice, I've always thought you are kind and noble; abducting someone else's child is something you couldn't do." "It's just that you're strong; I've heard a bit, and I know even if I brought so many elf knights, they probably wouldn't be a match for you." The elf elder's expression softened, showing a pleading look as he played the moral card, "If you insist on possessing that child, we cannot take her away, but have you considered the pain of a young child leaving her kin? She would have to forever live in the lies you weave." Merlin and Alice, who usually yield to softness but not to hardness, suddenly faced a double blow of emotion and morality, and really found it hard to withstand. Alice, being an upright person, could not do something like stealing someone else's child. Merlin likewise had his limits and principles; he could not bring himself to harm a child. Without knowing the truth, they subconsciously thought Chris was an elf child. If they forcibly kept Chris, it would be no different from abduction, facing moral judgment and the rupture of their friendship with the elves. "Please return the legacy left by our Father God," the elf elder bowed deeply, lowering himself as much as possible. Shirley, Hilf, and several elf knights followed suit, bowing, hoping Merlin and Alice would return Chris. Merlin and Alice, faces dark, could not speak; they looked at the elves before them, feeling an unprecedented pressure.

Late at night, Alice walked out of the bedroom holding the asleep Chris; this little one had no idea what was happening outside. Alice held Chris, gently smoothing her messy bangs, showing a hint of sadness: "Really have to send her back?" Merlin stood at the doorway, gazing at the night outside, silent for a long while before saying, "She is someone else's child; we have no reason to keep her, right?" "This child is so well-behaved, even cares about us, happy every day, just sending her back like this." Alice pressed her lips, feeling indescribable distress: "What do you think? Don't you like her?" Merlin fell silent again, after a while he said without turning back, "You and I are both principled people; if we abandon our principles, we might as well become bandits." In the short half-month of getting along, the two gradually came to like Chris, infected by her innocent nature. Even if Merlin had a heart of stone, being clung to by Chris every day would make it impossible for him to have no feelings at all. However, the two could not change the fact that Chris comes from the elf race; forcibly keeping her would likely be impossible. "But Alice, looking at the sleeping Chris in her arms, was obviously very reluctant." "Alice, Merlin turned his head back, lowering his voice: 'I told you not to invest too much feeling; you'll be reluctant.'" "Alice glared angrily at Merlin, turning her head away: 'Who's reluctant? Just letting her return to her own family is a good thing.'" "You just need to know that." Merlin sighed silently in his heart. The two opened the door; the elves had been waiting outside for a long time. Seeing Merlin and Alice walk out holding Chris, they all came forward to greet. Merlin and Alice looked at the sleeping Chris, hesitating to hand her over, as if each glance would make her less. "Alice." Shirley watched their expressions, her heart secretly wavering, but in the end she suppressed the urge to speak the truth. "Mr. Merlin, Miss Alice, we will take good care of her." Hilf stepped forward and earnestly promised. Alice gritted her teeth and still handed Chris to Hilf, also handing over some luggage to the other elves: "Inside are clothes she can wear, plus some toys she really likes; if she can't find them she gets anxious; without us around she finds it hard to sleep, so before bed she must definitely be told a story; best not to eat random junk; just formula milk is enough, not too hot, and don't forget to add a spoonful of sugar—she likes sweet things; this child is curious about everything and very active, so she needs to be watched carefully to prevent her from contacting dangerous things, and also…" "Alice," Merlin reminded her in a sentence. Alice froze, realizing her lapse; finally she placed the little rattle on Chris's chest, then unable to hold back, she bit her lips, eyes red, turned and ran back to her own bedroom. Merlin remained silent for a moment, glanced at the sleeping Chris, and said, "Hope you take good care of her." "Don't worry, we will definitely manage," the elf elder bowed, smiling, and said, "Goodbye."

Night passed without incident; that night Merlin had a dream. Chris sat on Merlin's lap, father and daughter together looking at a newspaper. Light novel. Chris asked questions like a curious baby, while Merlin always patiently answered, teaching her new things. "Daddy~, what's in the photo?" "It's the Queen Mother giving gifts to the orphans at the welfare home." "What's a welfare home?" "It's a place that specifically takes in children without parents; there they are raised by the kingdom." "Will Chris be sent there in the future too?" Merlin suddenly woke from his dream; outside the sun was already high and blazing, the glaring light making him uncomfortable. Beneath him was still that old, hard plank of a battle bed; on the ground lay a small basket filled with soft clothing, still able to prove that Chris had once existed—everything seemed to have returned to the former dull, boring life? Merlin slowly sat up on the sofa, looking at the distant makeshift nest of Chris, the vegetable basket— Really leaving now. Why do I feel uneasy?

title: Chapter 26 — Unable to Adapt
content:
Chapter 26 — Unable to Adapt

Volume 24 · Chapter 26

The elf party has left Lexham behind, heading for the nearest port to sail back to the United Kingdom as quickly as possible.

In a sense, the mission was successfully completed—no conflict with Merlin and Alice, and Chris was brought back.

It seems the Elf King had long been prepared, accurately gauging Merlin and Alice's personalities; as long as they occupied the moral high ground, retrieving the child was not difficult.

Unaware of what had happened, Chris woke up groggily to an unfamiliar environment and all the elves with pointed ears—

"Huh?"

"You're awake?" Shirley looked down at Chris in her arms and spoke gently.

Little Chris grew tense, her eyes filled with unease, lips pressed tight, saying nothing.

She broke free from Shirley's embrace, apparently disliking being held by strangers?

Looking around, Chris saw she was in a moving carriage, with only a young miss, a female knight, and an old grandfather.

"What are you looking for?" Shirley asked with confusion.

"Mommy, Daddy—where are Mommy and Daddy? Who are you?" Chris asked in a childish voice, tilting her face stubbornly.

"Shirley hesitated, not knowing how to explain to the child, and looked at Sylph with a pleading gaze.

Sylph, having been entrusted with a desperate mission, could only steel herself and step forward, bowing slightly with a smile: "Alice-san and Merlin-san are not your parents; we are your relatives."

"Nonsense!" Chris grew sad, her eyes reddening as she retorted, "They are my parents! You aren't my relatives—I don't even know you!"

Sylph felt embarrassed, realizing Chris had already bonded with Merlin and Alice, making it hard to change her mind now.

"I want Mommy! I want Daddy!" Little Chris became dejected, lowering her head and choking up, her heart filled with extreme panic.

Shirley remained silent, looking at Chris with a sympathetic expression, guilt rising within her. This child had been born from the mingled blood of Merlin and Alice; now her own kin had taken her away. Indeed, they were the ones tearing apart families. In a sense, Father had used Merlin and Alice's kindness, making Shirley an accomplice as well.

"Hmph!" The elf elder snorted coldly, speaking sternly, "Stop crying, it's useless. Your parents abandoned you. From now on, you're one of us. We'll raise you well."

"You're lying! Mommy and Daddy would never abandon me! You're all bad guys!" Chris bit her lip, retorting, her crystal-clear eyes brimming with tears.

"Bad guys?" The elf elder curled his lips, speaking meaningfully, "You will receive personal training from the Elf King. Your future will surely shine brightly—our clan will make something of you."

"Elder, please say no more. She's still a child." Sylph couldn't bear it any longer and interjected.

"Precisely because she's a child does she need early cultivation. She should know her responsibility and strive toward it for life." The elf elder said sternly.

Sylph fell silent. She understood clearly—the Elf King and the elders intended to raise this child as a future weapon, especially one who could interfere with Father God Caelion's barrier before birth; such talent was destined to be extraordinary!

"Give it back!" Little Chris saw the rattle in Shirley's hand, recognized it, and began demanding it. "That's what Mommy gave me."

"This?" Shirley looked at the small rattle, saw Chris's pleading gaze, and her heart softened, so she returned it.

Chris took the rattle, hid in the corner of the carriage alone, wiping her tears, shaking it occasionally to emit "dong-dong-dong" sounds, hoping Mommy would hear and take her home.

Seeing this scene, Shirley's heart tightened. She began to hate her own profit-seeking father—Chris had been so happy with Merlin and Alice; why did they have to tear them apart?

"Your Highness, try to coax her. Make her happy. The journey back is long; don't let anything happen to her on the road." The elf elder said with eyes closed, resting.

"Okay." Shirley came to the sad Chris, squatting down to appear more approachable. "We're all friends of your parents, not bad guys. Your parents went somewhere far away and temporarily left you with us, so you'll see them again soon."

"Really?" Chris hugged the rattle, lifting her head to ask innocently, her eye circles already red.

"Really, they'll come back for you soon." Shirley reached out and patted Chris's head. She could no longer calm this child, so she could only use lies to coax Chris, to make her a little happier.

"Sister, you're a good person~" Chris said in a childish voice.

"Me? What?" Shirley pointed at herself, then felt ashamed inwardly.

Chris had been gone for days. Merlin and Alice's lives seemed to instantly return to before—the life of a family of three felt like a dream.

Yet for several days, Merlin and Alice hadn't spoken a word to each other, each busy with their own things. More bizarrely, they hadn't even argued once!

This abnormal phenomenon was probably inseparable from Chris's sudden departure.

Chris had unconsciously become the bond between them; her sudden departure left them as if they had lost their common language overnight.

Though they didn't say it aloud, both Merlin and Alice missed that little shadow-like child, hoping she'd reappear and ask many childish, naive questions.

Late at night, Merlin sat alone on the old sofa; the flickering candlelight illuminated his worry-lined cheeks.

The house hadn't been cleaned for days, looking very messy. Without Chris, they felt life could be more casual.

Merlin, who loved reading the newspaper alone, seemed to have lost his only pleasure; the newspaper was crumpled into a ball and tossed aside.

Merlin had recently become restless, unable to adapt to his former life, always remembering Chris, that little shadow clinging to him—

He could recall Chris sitting on his lap, asking questions everywhere while reading the newspaper, that naive appearance?

And following behind him, calling "Daddy, Daddy" nonstop, begging for hugs?

What he couldn't forget was Chris helping wipe the floor, making himself look like a little tiger cat, then proudly showing off and asking for rewards.

Merlin lowered his head, looking at the silver mask in his hand—the same style as Elgin the Great Sword Hero's toy he had bought for Chris that day.

It seemed because Chris had left in a hurry, Alice had forgotten to bring this thing for her, so it was left behind.

For days, Merlin had been secretly playing with this child's toy, recalling Chris's hero cosplay.

Merlin hesitated. Though he had done many bad things in his life, stealing another's child was something he had never done before.

He put the Elgin Great Sword Hero's mask into his chest, as if silently making some decision, then stood up and put on his coat to leave.

But just as Merlin was putting on his boots by the door, the bedroom door opened—

Alice walked out slowly in her pajamas, leaning on the doorframe staring at Merlin.

The two gazed at each other. Three seconds of silent stillness.

"So late, where are you going?"

title: Chapter 27 — Interception
content:
Chapter 27 — Interception

Volume 24 · Chapter 27

Merlin stopped in his tracks at the sound of Alice's voice, their first conversation in several days.

""

"Is it really just going out for a walk?" Alice asked, looking into Merlin's eyes.

Merlin was at a loss for words, thinking that with Alice's understanding of him, it would be hard to deceive her. He lowered his voice and answered honestly, "I'm going to bring Chris back."

Alice nodded, having already guessed that Merlin had lost his patience. "Aren't you the one who said we're people of principle and wouldn't do something like taking someone else's child?"

"That's right," Merlin paused, then changed his tone, "But this child is still willing to call us dad and mom. That makes us her parents, and that's enough. Can you watch her go to the distant United Kingdom? Who knows what's waiting for her there?"

Alice lowered her head in silence, then asked softly after a while, "But we're friends with the elves. If you bring Chris back, it will inevitably lead to a falling out with them. Are you prepared to become enemies with Snow and even the Elf King?"

"No, but I can secretly bring Chris back," Merlin said seriously.

Alice hesitated, then decided to stand by Merlin's side. "Do you need my help?"

"No, I can handle it alone," Merlin replied casually, turning to walk away.

Alice sighed, leaning her head against the doorframe, her gaze falling on the empty "basket" by the sofa.

"Be careful on the road."

The elven group, disguised as traveling merchants, traveled without obstruction.

After several days and nights of rushing, they were about to arrive at the nearest port.

A ship was already waiting there, ready to return to the United Kingdom at the fastest speed.

Chris, who had been feeling down about not seeing her parents, had cheered up after being deceived by Shirley's lies.

Chris thought she was only temporarily living with the elves, and her parents would soon come to take her back.

Unbeknownst to her, what awaited her was the Elf King's strict training, and she would soon lose her freedom, becoming a secret weapon of another race.

In the swaying carriage, the elven elder was resting with his eyes closed, while Shirley and Sylph focused their attention on little Chris.

"This was bought by mom, shake it and it makes a dong dong dong sound," Chris said proudly, playing with a rattle between Shirley and Sylph. "Mom is amazing, she can make beautiful sounds with it, but I just can't learn it."

Shirley forced a smile, having listened to Chris talk about her parents all along. She could feel the child's affection for Merlin and Alice, which made her feel increasingly guilty. Clearly, no matter how she was born, this child couldn't be separated from Merlin and Alice.

"Is that so? Miss Alice is amazing," Sylph said to keep Chris from getting bored.

"What about Mr. Merlin? What's he usually like?"

"Dad makes mom angry every day and always scares me like I'm a little kid~" Chris complained in a childish voice.

"But you are a little kid?" Sylph asked in confusion.

"Who says that? I'm not a little kid! Humph!" Chris pouted, then lowered her head and muttered, "Actually, dad is very gentle, and his temper isn't as bad as it seems. He always secretly pays attention to me, and when I fall, dad is always the first to rush over. Dad is the best!"

Sylph's understanding became complicated, thinking that in her impression, Mr. Merlin was a difficult person to communicate with, yet privately he was like this?

"But dad still has some small flaws, he's afraid of trouble and always tries to push household chores onto mom. He's always paying attention to the horse racing news in the newspaper, saying things like 'Richard will definitely lose,' but the next day he's very regretful," Chris muttered to herself, even she could see Merlin's flaws.

Shirley:

Sylph:

The carriage fell silent, and if it weren't for Chris's muttering, they might never have known why Alice had such a big opinion of Merlin.

No wonder Alice seemed so strict; it turned out Merlin was like this in private. If things went wrong, it might make the whole family sleep on the streets.

The moving carriage heard the sound of approaching horses. The elven elder, who had been resting with his eyes closed, opened them. "We've arrived, get down."

The elves disembarked, and outside, a huge merchant ship was already docked, waiting for them.

"Hurry up and board the ship," the elven elder led the elves toward the merchant ship.

Shirley took Chris's small hand, walking slowly toward the ship. She thought that soon they would leave this place, and this child might never return.

Little Chris looked up at the huge ship, feeling uneasy, and asked Shirley softly, "Sister, where are we going?"

"To a very far place, our hometown," Shirley said with a smile, hoping to ease Chris's anxiety.

Chris stopped in her tracks, refusing to take another step. "It's too far, I won't go. If I do, dad and mom won't be able to find me."

"They will," Shirley pretended to say.

"No, I don't want to be far from dad and mom. I won't go with you," Chris said tensely, sitting down on the ground and refusing to board the ship with the elves.

"Don't be afraid, be good," Shirley felt a bit embarrassed, not expecting Chris to start throwing a tantrum at the last moment.

"No! I won't go!" Chris sat stubbornly on the ground, worried that once she boarded the big ship, she would never see her parents again.

"At this point? Why can't you behave?" The elven elder was somewhat angry, directly picking up Chris, who was sitting on the ground. "Be honest and come aboard with us, we won't harm you."

"Let me go! Let me go! You're all bad people!" Chris began to struggle, crying and saying, "Bad people!"

"Don't do this, don't force her," Shirley couldn't help but stop the elven elder.

"Elder!" Sylph also couldn't bear to watch.

Just as the elves were about to conflict internally, a series of screams came from the huge merchant ship ahead.

One sailor after another was thrown into the sea, even the captain wasn't spared, kicked flying.

"What's happening?"

The elves looked up at the merchant ship, unsure what was happening. It seemed like some kind of disturbance?

Even the noisy Chris had quieted down, curiously looking at the ship above.

A man in a black windbreaker and silver mask appeared on the deck.

He looked down at the elves below, then jumped down, landing in front of them.

The elven knights immediately took action, drawing their swords and standing guard in front of the elder and the princess.

The elven elder furrowed his brow, sizing up the mysterious masked man with suspicion.

"Who are you?"

title: Chapter 28 — Power of the Earth Spirit (Extra)

Chapter 28 — Power of the Earth Spirit (Extra)

Volume 24 · Chapter 28

After Merlin left Lexurm, he deduced that the elves wouldn't stay in human lands for long, so they would definitely choose the nearest port to Lexurm to leave.

So he traveled through the night and arrived before the elf party did.

He had thought the elves had already boarded the ship, but found he had gotten there first; he simply threw the captain and sailors overboard, cutting off the elves' means of escape.

Facing the elf elder's questioning, Merlin said nothing, a bit worried that if he spoke, the other side would identify him by the difference in voice, so he didn't answer either, just staring quietly at the disguised elves.

Merlin had no intention of removing his mask; instead, he planned to hide his identity, kidnap Chris, and deny it afterward, letting Chris live secretly alongside him and Alice.

For this purpose, Merlin didn't even bring his sword, deciding to use the Earth Spirit's power to repel the elves, making it easier not to reveal his identity.

Sylph and over a dozen elf knights stood fully prepared, staring warily at the mysterious man before them; the atmosphere instantly became tense, as if a fight would break out the next second.

The elves' gazes were stern, hands resting on sword hilts; if the man opposite made any aggressive move, it would surely be a fight to the death.

The elf elder felt that being on human kingdom soil, it was unwise to create further trouble, hoping to clarify the situation, "Sir, why won't you speak?"

Merlin stood still, silent, seeing Chris in the elder's arms looking at him curiously, eyes red with tear stains, having cried not long ago.

This made Merlin silently clench his fists, anger rising in his heart; though he didn't know what happened, Chris crying clearly meant something bad had occurred.

Merlin's expression turned unfriendly, suddenly stepping forward, the gravity around him increasing suddenly, causing space to vibrate—

An elf knight noticed Merlin's subtle change and struck first, attempting to take the initiative.

The sharp sword gleamed with cold light, golden battle aura surging forth with imposing momentum!

These elite knights under the elf king, all starting from Saint-tier, prioritized their clan's interests above all and were fearless of death.

"Hmph!" Merlin snorted, drawing out the Earth Spirit's power from the depths of his mind, unleashing the Repulsion Space!

A powerful repulsive force spread rapidly outward from Merlin's body, forming an invisible defensive barrier!

The elf knight who had tried to strike first showed a trace of horror in his eyes, was instantly blasted away, crashing into the wall behind him, unable to even get close!

The Earth Spirit's power is near pseudo-divine, probing a trace of the earth's fundamental laws, how could these elf knights resist it?

The elf knights looked astonished; their companion's speed a hundred times that of light left them unable to react in time, not understanding what had just happened!

The elf elder let out an exclamation; he was well-traveled and recognized the Repulsion Space just now.

Being able to control similar gravity, attraction, repulsion—these are powers that earth element magicians can only master at very high levels!

The elf elder's expression turned serious, realizing the mysterious magician before him was no easy opponent, unaware that the other wasn't using magic at all but a tool.

"Be careful! This guy's strength is extraordinary! One slip and you'll lose your life!"

The elf knights reacted quickly, drawing their waist swords, pointing them at the masked mysterious man with hostility.

The oppressive pressure emanating from them gathered together, looking like a single entity, appearing especially terrifying.

Cold sweat dripped from the elf knights' foreheads; feeling immense pressure and seeing their companion's fate, they dared not rashly advance, instead protecting the elder and princess meticulously.

"Why did you attack us? Please explain the reason; we can talk!" Sylph shouted loudly, wondering if they had offended someone on the way and were being sniped here.

Sherry's gaze was uncertain, looking at the mysterious man's stature, which was close to Merlin's, but Merlin-sama couldn't use magic and carried a sword, so who exactly was the other party?

While all the elves were on high alert, little Chris was the most emotionally stable, seemingly having already recognized the person opposite as her father.

Chris bit her hand, blinking her big eyes at the mask on Merlin's face, feeling very familiar, "Hmm?"

Though Merlin was usually lazy, he hadn't been idle; after obtaining the Earth Spirit's power, he had studied it carefully in his spare time.

He discovered that the Earth Spirit controlled the essence of earth element power; earth elements attracted and repelled each other, and the power within could evolve into variants.

As long as one saw through the essence of elemental power, they could touch the ultimate of the earth, glimpse a corner of the world's fundamental laws, and control elemental power at will.

So Merlin tried to make changes; not only could he use the gravity space that pressed people to the ground, but he had also learned two variants of the gravity space.

The repulsion space that flung people away and the attraction space that pulled people in.

Seeing this, Merlin slowly raised his head, precisely directing the Earth Spirit's power onto Chris alone in the elf elder's arms.

The elf knights opposite thought

The earth spirit's power was unleashed, creating a space with 100 times the normal gravity. The pressure within the area suddenly increased, causing the ground to tremble slightly.

These fierce elf knights felt an indescribable, immense pressure in mid-air, as if a mountain were bearing down on them.

Boom, boom, boom! The elf knights hadn't had time to get close before they were crushed by the 100-times gravity and couldn't move, their faces making intimate contact with the ground.

Sylph was gritting her teeth in pain, sweating all over, and was frightened by the mysterious sorcerer's power. She lay on the ground unable to move, her bones in danger of breaking.

“....This is...

The elf elder was firmly suppressed, unable to even raise his head to glare at the enemy, and the crushing power made him feel incredulous!

The trembling ground began to slowly develop fine cracks as it struggled to bear the immense gravity.

The only one unaffected was Shirley. Merlin had applied the gravity space to the elves with combat abilities, but he didn't target Shirley.

Because compared to other elves, Shirley was too weak, so weak that she could be easily overlooked. If the gravity space had been applied to Shirley, she would probably have been crushed to death.

Shirley stood there blankly, watching her companions being crushed and unable to move, and took a step back in fear, her eyes full of suspicion as she looked at the mysterious man opposite her.

Merlin continued to release the gravity space, feeling that he had made these elf knights suffer enough and that it was time to take Chris and run away.

But little Chris was full of curiosity, reaching out her small hand to touch Merlin's beard, and giggling, "Dad!"

"Dad, dad! You're my dad! The smell and appearance are the same!" Chris showed her baby teeth and smiled happily.

“I knew dad would come looking for me soon, haha....” Chris's face turned bright red, for she had never given up hope and believed that her parents would come back to take her home.
