title: Chapter 30 — Solid Proof
content:
Chapter 30 — Solid Proof

Volume 24 · Chapter 30

"Give up..." Xieli lowered her head, clenching her fists and mumbling.

"Huh? What?" The elf elder was astonished, thinking he had misheard.

"I'm saying we stop bringing this child back to the United Kingdom." Xieli raised her head, speaking with a serious expression.

The elf knights all showed confused expressions. The child was of great importance, his future achievements might be extraordinary, he was the existence that Elf King — again emphasized — wanted brought back.
But now Xieli suddenly said to terminate this matter, which was no different from going against the Elf King, standing on the opposite side of all elves.

"Your Highness... Xifu wanted to speak but stopped, not knowing what Xieli was planning.
"Your Highness, please pay attention to your position. As the heir to the throne, how can you joke with the future of our race?" The elf elder said seriously.

"I haven't forgotten our stance. That's right, before this child was born she belonged to us, but now she has nothing to do with us. Her body flows with the blood of Mr. Merlin and Miss Alice!" Xieli frowned, constantly restraining the accumulated resentment, finally bursting out at this moment, "We are not the child's relatives... we are robbers!

Merlin was puzzled, somewhat unable to understand what Xieli was saying? He subconsciously looked down at Chris.
This little thing seemed to understand nothing either, sucking her fingers with a face full of curiosity.

"Your Highness, don't do this, we..." Xifu wanted to stop, but it was already too late.
Xieli knew well of Merlin's strength. If she continued to hide the truth, the elder, to complete the father's task, would order the elf knights to risk everything and fight Merlin to the death.
But Xieli didn't want to see a situation where both sides died. These elf knights couldn't defeat Merlin, and in the end would only be throwing their lives away.
To trick that child, was it worth sacrificing so many knights' lives?
Xieli's heart rippled with questions. Even her own elf father, she feared, wouldn't want to become enemies with Mr. Merlin.

"Mr. Merlin, do you remember the giant stone before the secret realm?"
"Remember... what happened?" Merlin asked in surprise, subconsciously feeling that something was being hidden from him.
"You and Miss Alice dripped blood on the stone... after... " Xieli's gaze fixed on Chris's innocent face, speaking seriously, "new life was born inside, this child is it.

"No way...?" Merlin looked at Chris in his arms, widening his eyes, seemingly noticing something?
"What about the father god's inheritance? What about the child imitating you out of curiosity? All lies." Xieli lowered her head, paused, then said, the reason she came from afar to be by your side, the reason she resembled your appearances, was all because of the blood connection between you...

"Aiyi?" Chris raised her head looking at Merlin, seemingly not understanding?
Merlin's expression became weird, immediately feeling quite a bit of psychological pressure, looking at the tiny Chris in his arms.
How could he not think that this little thing had both his and Alice's blood in her body? To some extent, it was the crystallization of his and Alice's feelings, right?
Bullshit! We never actually got married, we've always been sleeping in separate rooms, and suddenly a child, what a soap opera situation!
How did I suddenly become a dad?! I wasn't prepared at all! It's just like... in a dream...

Merlin's emotions were complex, as if the burden of fatherhood was on his shoulders. He had always been living a carefree, responsibility-free wandering life, but at this moment he couldn't express his feelings.

"Your Highness! What nonsense are you talking about?! Please don't speak randomly, distorting facts!" The elf elder was furious, turning the tables.
"If I don't say it, what do you plan to do? Let the knights fight Merlin to the death? That's just throwing their lives away!" Xieli rebuked, frowning her delicate eyebrows.
"Your Majesty's mission is supreme, and knights sacrificing their lives for it is beyond reproach!" The elf elder's white beard seemed to float up with anger.

Silence fell over Xieli as she looked at the elf elder, speaking seriously, "Elder, I have always respected you for your diligent service to our father, but I am the only heir to the throne. I hope you don't treat me like a child..."
The elf elder was speechless, noticing the elf knights' expressions were off?
Although the knights obeyed the elder, essentially they served the royal family.
Obviously, if someone disrespects the royal family, that touches the knights' bottom line.

The elf elder's face turned purple, under the pressure of his companions, he could only grit his teeth and say.
"I naturally wouldn't treat Your Highness like a child, but since you've hindered Your Majesty's mission, you should have prepared yourself to bear the consequences."
"Don't trouble yourself, I will personally apologize to Father, and won't evade responsibility." Xieli said in a low voice.
"Tch!" The elf elder was dissatisfied, pouting, closing his eyes and saying no more.
"Let's go back." Xieli used a commanding tone, unprecedentedly.
The elf knights hesitated a bit, looking at each other, finally choosing to obey the princess's order, putting away their weapons and walking toward the large ship at the harbor.

Xifu lowered her head, passing by Xieli's side, wanting to say something, but finally just shook her head and followed her companions.
Xieli walked slowly to Merlin's front, looking at the dazed Chris in his arms, returning the rattle to her, "Since it's something important Mom gave you, don't lose it easily.

Little Chris looked at the rattle in her hands, raised her head and asked curiously, "Sister, are we leaving?"
"You go home, sister also goes home. Remember, don't follow strangers easily. In this world, not everyone is like your mom and dad who would take care of you selflessly." Xieli warned in an elder's tone.
"Uh~" Chris nodded incomprehensibly.

"Mr. Merlin, goodbye. If there's a chance, I hope you can visit my hometown." Xieli paused, looking down, "I guarantee next time we meet, it won't be like this."
"Oh,.. have a safe journey?" Merlin tried to respond, watching the elves leave.
The merchant ship that had been docked for a long time slowly began to sail, heading toward the southern lands of the alien races. The elves returned empty-handed.

Merlin retracted his gaze, looking at Chris in his arms again, still having trouble accepting reality.
He put Chris down, slowly squatting down, trying to meet his daughter's eyes levelly.
"Chris..."
"Aiyi~?" Little Chris stepped up her feet to respond, the little hair strand on her head shaking happily.
"That..."
Merlin's old face turned red, his gaze dodging. Knowing that Chris flowed with his and Alice's blood, he could hardly look at this child anymore--
This little... is my child
No no no, is me and Alice's child.
Coming to this world for over two hundred years, I never thought I'd have an heir...
Am I... a dad now?
But speaking of which, what exactly must I do to become a qualified dad?

Merlin stared at the innocent-looking Chris, his heart feeling complicated. He had thought she was just a child he picked up, but he never expected they were related by blood!
Chris's appearance blended her parents' genes, so it's no wonder that from birth she could cause Merlin and Alice to misunderstand.
This left Merlin momentarily unsure how to face his little daughter, with various emotions tangled in his heart—aside from a hint of paternal joy, mostly shock and pressure.
What should I do? The child is mine and Alice's....
If I go back and tell Alice, she might be frightened silly on the spot, right?
Besides, neither I nor Alice have any parenting experience—can we really raise Chris into an outstanding person?
Merlin thought Alice, despite her minor flaws, could still be considered outstanding, whereas looking at his own shortcomings piled up, he feared he might leave a bad impression on little Chris.
Based on Alice's usual words and deeds, she will surely become an excellent mother, but Merlin is not so sure—he doesn't like that Chris has picked up a bunch of bad habits from elementary school.
“Dad?” Chris tilted her head in confusion, not knowing what Dad wanted to say to her.
“....Merlin gave a light cough to hide his embarrassment, speaking with a meaningful tone: “Chris, your birth.... is an....”
“Ah?” Chris blinked her eyes curiously, seemingly not understanding.
“Although it was an accident, but..” Merlin crouched on the ground, placing his hands on Chris's tiny ears and shoulders, speaking seriously: “I and your mother will do our utmost to raise you; we don’t need any repayment from you, we only hope you can become an outstanding person in the future, do you understand?”
“....Chris sucked her fingers, appearing not to grasp Merlin's thoughts.”
“I don’t care where you come from, what talents you have, or even if you don’t want to learn magic or martial arts and just be an ordinary person—none of that matters.” Merlin paused, speaking earnestly: “But you need to know, you are my Merlin’s daughter; never lightly harm others, nor meekly allow yourself to be harmed; follow the convictions in your heart and carry them through, just like your mother, to become an outstanding person.”
Chris is still young and couldn’t fully understand Merlin’s advice, but she smiled and replied, “Chris likes Mom~”
“That’s right...” Merlin patted Chris’s little head and lifted her up—
“Come on, let’s go home.”
The distant demon realm, the Swamp of Death’s First Demon Lord Palace.
This place is filled with an aura of desolation and death; the foul-smelling swamp makes one frown.
Since Merlin the monarch was fried squid, the demons have become idle, losing some vitality.
Although Lilith is Merlin’s younger sister and temporarily acting as the First Demon Lord’s position, her influence falls far short of her brother’s.
Sent out to seek Merlin’s Seven Generals—, Blake Man has recently returned—
In a certain secluded room of the Demon Lord’s Palace, a handsome man with long hair is loudly reading from a notebook.
“That day, I was strolling in the garden with my lord when his buttocks were unintentionally bitten by a poisonous snake. Out of concern for my lord, I said, ‘May I suck the poison blood out with my mouth?’ My lord replied, ‘Are you thinking about eating your own butt?’”
The long-haired man wore a look of enjoyment, as if receiving a double baptism of spirit and soul; each day reading through the sayings of spiritual leaders makes him feel redeemed.
His name is Pudom, one of the Seven Generals of the First Demon Lord’s Palace, an old subordinate of Merlin, who regards Merlin as his spiritual refuge.
Pudom differs from ordinary demons; he has a poet’s temperament, knows etiquette, speaks politely, and isn’t fond of killing—each time he engages in combat he needs a grand, righteous justification.
In childhood, when the monarch’s seat was seized by demon nobles, the young Merlin and Lilith fled, receiving much aid from the young Pudom.
Although Pudom is not a veteran like Ophelia who serves Vivian, he still shares a considerable bond and trust with Merlin.
Pudom slowly placed the notebook before him, its cover bearing “Merlin’s Quotations,” then turned his head to speak to the friend behind him.
“How about it, Dul? This is something that happened when I once strolled in the rear garden with His Majesty; isn’t it impressive? His Majesty always can utter golden lines—if we don’t record them properly, it would truly be a pity. Are you thinking about eating your own butt? Ah~, it’s wonderful—concise and striking the soul! What kind of talent must one possess to utter such splendid golden words?”
“Hehehe, truly the scholar’s dregs—thanks to you having idle mind to record these boring words, are you thinking about eating your own butt? This is scolding you, right? It’s entirely because you want to suck His Majesty’s buttocks, making him angry.,r 牡小
Dul laughed sinisterly, feeling no enthusiasm for Pudom’s creation of “Merlin’s Quotations”; instead he judged it boring.
He too is Merlin’s subordinate, one of the Seven Generals—short, ugly‑looking, with twisted horns on his head, and he sticks out a long tongue that droops to the ground; upon closer look, his tongue even has a row of nails driven into it.
Dul has a nasty disposition, enjoys tormenting enemies, and their screams make him ecstatic; although his bond with Merlin isn’t deep, he was nevertheless promoted by Merlin from the lowest ranks, hand‑lifting him five times—equals.
“Boring? That’s because you’re a coarse person lacking the talent to be a poet; His Majesty always can utter astonishing remarks, proving He is full of talent—no matter how many books I read, I can’t compare.” Pudom paused, opened “Merlin’s Quotations” and recited another passage: “After the Seven Kings’ banquet ended, His Majesty confessed his love to the Lust Monarch and failed; returning, His Majesty said, ‘Knock it?’ I almost got bent out of shape—though I’m a man, I dressed up so flirtatiously!”
Dul’s expression turned odd; he didn’t know how to evaluate.
“Listen carefully—this ‘knock it?’ in the sentence is literally the finishing touch; it expresses His Majesty’s regret after failing to succeed, the lingering anxiety of almost being trapped, and it warns all male demons not to approach the Lust Monarch lightly.” Pudom, face full of admiration, exclaimed.
“This is just His Majesty’s black history, right? If Bo knew you recorded this, he’d surely have you killed.” Dul said with an ugly expression.

Dul fell silent for a moment, then said in a gloomy tone, “Truly enviable—I haven’t had such luck; I’ve lived all my life as a slave at the bottom, once helped the demon nobles seize His Majesty’s throne, personally killing many rebels; after the demon nobles were defeated by His Majesty, I should have followed Bo to execution, but His Majesty pardoned our sins and made me an official; His Majesty’s breadth convinces me, and to earn his favor is my honor.”
“That’s natural—I could see His Majesty’s extraordinariness even as a child; He will surely become the leader of the entire demon race.” Pudom nodded in agreement and continued—

title: Chapter 32 — Merlin's Subordinates (Part 2)
content:
Chapter 32 — Merlin's Subordinates (Part 2)

Volume 24 · Chapter 32

“I envy that idiot Blackman, getting the chance to go out and see the world.” Duruth paused, his beady eyes showing a hint of longing. “He must have seen plenty of tasty humans out there — I wonder if he got to eat any? Ah, I can’t stand it — I want to go outside too.”

“You’d better not, you’d probably cause trouble. Lady Lilith sent Blackman because he’s more obedient,” said Podom, closing the Book of Merlin and tucking it carefully into his chest. “The peace we enjoy today is thanks to His Majesty’s efforts — otherwise those Church thugs would be harassing us nonstop.”

“What about you? Don’t you miss him? It’s been nearly two years since he left — don’t you long to see him?” Duruth asked in a low voice.

“Of course I miss him — the urge is like a flood breaking its banks. But I know my duty is to guard this place, to protect the legacy he built. I believe he’ll return someday, and those old fools in the council will regret their stupid decision.”

“I see...” Duruth replied without expression.

“My wish is to stay by His Majesty’s side, record his every word and deed, and compile the biography of the Third Prideful Monarch for future generations to admire his genius.” Podom said with hope, then turned to ask, “What about you, Duruth? What’s your wish? If it’s not about killing or torture, I might include it in the book.”

“Me?” Duruth fell silent, lost in thought. “...No, nothing. I have no wish. Just think of me as a mediocre, lifeless creature.”

“That’s odd — no wonder no other demons want to talk to you.” Podom said meaningfully.

“They don’t talk to me because of my background — I’m not just a low-level demon, I used to be His Majesty’s enemy. Even though he values me, others won’t change their minds.” Duruth raised his ugly face and whispered, “Podom, you and Blackman are good guys — in this quiet palace, you’re the only ones who chat with me.”

“Don’t misunderstand — I talk to you out of courtesy. As for Blackman, he’s a fool...” Podom replied with a smirk.

“Blackman wouldn’t agree with that assessment.” Duruth shook his head.

Just as they were talking about him, Blackman arrived — pushing open the door with a broad, excited smile.

“Hey, friends! I’m back!”

“Ha, we were just talking about you!” Duruth chuckled darkly.

“Oh? What were you saying? Not bad-mouthing me while I was gone, I hope?” Blackman scratched his head.

“Of course not! We were praising your intelligence — that’s why Lady Lilith sent you to visit His Majesty.” Podom smiled knowingly.

“Really? That’s embarrassing — you’re too kind, you fancy-talking jerk!” Blackman blushed.

“Did you see His Majesty?” Podom asked eagerly.

“Yeah, he’s doing well — except for taking the wrong medicine, no big issues.” Blackman said casually.

“Wrong medicine? He must need someone to look after him — he’s never left the swamp before.” Podom frowned.

“There’s a human woman taking care of him — no need to worry.” Blackman waved it off.

“A human woman? I didn’t expect His Majesty to keep a human slave — that’s unusual...” Duruth narrowed his eyes.

“It’s not just a slave — he’s using her as a kind of camouflage, to stay safe.” Blackman said mysteriously.

“What does that mean?” Podom looked confused.

“It’s a secret — only Lady Lilith should know. Best not to tell others.” Blackman hesitated.

“I see — a secret. We won’t ask then.” Podom dropped the topic and asked, “Did he say anything profound? Something that shook your soul? I need to write it down.”

“Profound? I don’t know — but we did bathe together...” Blackman grinned nostalgically, eyes drifting. “It was a sacred moment — skin on skin, merging souls. Ah, so wonderful...”

Podom and Duruth both turned pale, unsure what to make of that. The room filled with an awkward, slightly creepy vibe.

“Anyway, I got to see His Majesty again — it was worth the trip!” Blackman said proudly, arms crossed.

“Blackman! There you are!”

Ophelia, the palace maid, stormed in, looking annoyed. She’d been searching for him since he returned — and found him here chatting with Podom.

“Ophelia? What’s up?” Blackman asked innocently.

“Are you an idiot? Lady Lilith sent you to check on His Majesty — you’re supposed to report back immediately! What are you doing here?” Ophelia snapped, veins bulging. “Lady Lilith wants to see you — follow me.”

“Oh, right — I forgot!” Blackman laughed nervously.

As Ophelia turned to leave, she paused and glared at Podom. “And you — stop writing those stupid poems. They’re garbage. Spend more time thinking about how to grow the palace — you’re a general, not a poet. We need warriors, not poets.”

“Uh... okay...” Podom looked embarrassed.

“Hee hee — no wonder you’re close to His Majesty and Lady Lilith — you’re tough! But with that attitude, no male demon will like you. Aren’t you lonely, Ophelia?” Duruth leered, tongue flicking toward her skirt.

In a flash, Ophelia grabbed his tongue and sliced it off with her dagger.

“Aaaah!” Duruth screamed as blood poured from his mouth.

“Duruth, you filthy thing — behave yourself. I won’t be as kind as His Majesty. If you threaten the royal family, I’ll kill you myself.” Ophelia chewed the severed tongue, grinning with sharp teeth. “That was disgusting.”

The room fell silent — except for Duruth’s whimpering. Blackman and Podom exchanged glances, wondering what just happened.

And so, the Demon Lord’s palace remained a place of mystery and danger — even for its own inhabitants.

title: Chapter 33 — Merlin's Subordinates (Part 2)
content:
Chapter 33 — Merlin's Subordinates (Part 2)

Volume 24 · Chapter 33

In the main hall of the First Demon Lord Palace, Lilith, the acting Demon Lord, sat on Merlin’s original throne.

Ophelia stood respectfully beside her, watching Blackman kneel below.

Lilith had learned from Ophelia that Merlin had married a human, and that he had done all sorts of things with the human woman.

This made Lilith feel uneasy and disgusted, so she reluctantly sent Blackman to check on Merlin’s situation.

It was said to be a visit to Merlin, but in reality it was to find out whether Merlin had found a fox spirit outside for two years after marrying a human.

Lilith looked down at Blackman and slowly said, “Thank you for your hard work this time, Blackman.”

“It’s only right to serve Lady Lilith, so it’s not hard work,” Blackman replied, kneeling on one knee.

Lilith nodded in satisfaction and asked bluntly, “So, did you get anything out of your visit to my brother this time?”

“Of course, Your Majesty is still safe, please rest assured, Lady Lilith,” Blackman replied.

“That’s not the point. I want to know if my brother really married a human. Did he really find a wife outside?” Lilith’s face turned ugly.

“This…

” Blackman hesitated, and after organizing a prophecy, said, “Your Majesty did marry a human. It’s a fact.”

“See! What did I say? I never make mistakes!” Ophelia couldn’t help but interject, her face full of unhappiness. “Lady Lilith, we can’t just sit here and wait to die. Your Majesty has become arrogant, seeing one love one, leaving us here to fend for ourselves, going out to find human fox spirits, completely ignoring our feelings. It’s so disgusting!” Gongjiu

“How could this happen…

Lilith’s face turned black, and she scratched the throne with her nails, leaving scratches. She recalled Merlin’s sweet words when he left, and in just two years he had become a king! He didn’t care about his little sister at all!

The letters he sent from time to time always expressed his longing for her, but now it seems that it was just because he was having a good time outside and didn’t want to be disturbed!

Lilith clenched her teeth and vowed that if that fox spirit appeared in front of her, she would tear her apart no matter what.

“Given Your Majesty’s philandering nature, if left unchecked, he might soon be able to form a knight’s brigade of women. At that point, our position in his heart will definitely decline!” Ophelia looked evil and said quietly. “Lady Lilith, I think we should think of a way to kill that human woman who seduced Your Majesty, to eliminate the problem once and for all.”

“Is that so? This is indeed a solution…” Lilith nodded in agreement, thinking that Ophelia had spoken a lot of sense.

“We must never give up our man,” Ophelia said seriously, her face full of determination.

“He’s my man,” Lilith emphasized unhappily.

“What?” Ophelia showed a look of immense pain, covering her chest, turning away and wiping her tears. “Vivian, you left too early. I raised you from childhood to adulthood, and you still treat me as an outsider. I’m so sad, oh oh oh—

“Eh, don’t be like that, Ophelia, I didn’t mean that…” Lilith frowned, feeling a huge pressure. Ophelia had taken care of her and Merlin since childhood, almost like a second mother.

“Lady Lilith, please don’t be so hasty. Your Majesty did marry a human, but the reality is not that simple!” Blackman’s expression suddenly became serious.

“Hmm? So you mean there’s more to it?” Lilith asked curiously.

“Yes! Your Majesty has a grand plan to overthrow human rule and restore the demon race. He hasn’t forgotten his goal of reviving the demon race,” Blackman paused, speaking seriously. “Now Your Majesty is living a life of humiliation, working as the lowest-level adventurer in the human world, looked down upon by everyone, and having to scramble for a living every day. Even marrying a human woman, all of this is a cover to achieve the goal of reviving the demon race before that. The less noticeable Your Majesty is, the easier it is to achieve this goal. He’s waiting for an opportunity!”

“Is it true? Does my homebound brother have such a great ambition? It sounds like a different person,” Lilith became suspicious, recalling the letters Merlin had sent, which said he was so awesome he was about to establish a second base for the demon race. But the reality was the opposite, her brother wasn’t doing well outside. But thinking about it, her brother had never left the Death Swamp, so not begging for food was already good enough.

“It’s absolutely true. Your Majesty told me himself,” Blackman replied with a positive tone.

“That’s nonsense!” Ophelia glared and shouted in rebuttal. “Your Majesty was willing to fight with me to protect that woman, obviously being deeply enchanted by that human woman. The story about marrying a human woman as a cover to achieve the goal of reviving the demon race is all fake! Your Majesty is just using lies to lure you back! You fool! You shouldn’t have been sent out, you should have let Shu go to investigate!”

Lilith’s face turned ugly, feeling that her brother had always been full of lies.

In her little sister’s eyes, Merlin now had no credit at all.

He promised not to find a fox spirit, but turned around and violated the demon race’s taboo by marrying a human?

Lilith wanted to confront Merlin face to face and find out what he was thinking.

O’Brien was so stunned that he couldn’t speak, stammering in response, “T-That… was all Your Majesty said himself. How could he lie to me?”

“That’s your stupidity!” Ophelia was so angry that her teeth itched, and couldn’t help but step forward and volunteer. “Lady Lilith, please let me go and see Your Majesty. I will definitely find out what’s going on!

“No need, I’ll go myself,” Lilith said coldly, already distrusting her other subordinates.

“But… you can’t leave the Demon Lord Palace at will. If you leave, what about the Blood Pool seal?” Ophelia frowned and continued. “If you force yourself to leave the Demon Lord Palace, you can’t be gone for more than a month. But it’s not even to the land of the British Kingdom, it takes about half a month to sail there. You don’t have much time.

“I’ll ask Beelzebub’s sister Miranda to help me maintain the Blood Pool seal. She’s also a descendant of the first demon lords,” Lilith said calmly, preparing to go and see Merlin herself.

“But… Beelzebub loves his sister very much and may not agree to let Miranda help,” Ophelia thought that going to see Merlin herself would be a good idea too.

“I’ll think of a way to persuade Beelzebub,” Lilith slowly closed her eyes and sighed. “Look at that brother of his, look at my brother. It really pisses me off.

Poor Lilith didn’t know what she was going to see. When she met Merlin, she would be ‘surprised’ to find that her brother…

had even gotten…

a disease”

■ToBeued

Postscript

I see some people don’t know why I’ve suddenly written three episodes about the Demon Lord Palace.

I can’t possibly write out the outline of my thoughts for everything, that’s not meaningful.

First, the Demon Lord Palace side hasn’t been talked about for a long time, and a few subordinates need to say something, which will be used later.

Second, the little sister’s next move needs to be known, which involves Merlin’s conflict with the demon race and the struggle with the demon lords.

Third, we need to strengthen the presence of the supporting characters. It’s not good to always watch Merlin and Alice, the story needs to continue.

Now I need an extra story, which is the one I mentioned a long time ago, about Merlin and the little sister wandering around, but I haven’t written it yet, so I’ll find an opportunity to write it soon, preferably in one volume and release it directly. This kind of extra story is troublesome to watch one episode at a time, and it’s not the main storyline, but it can supplement character relationships and world-building.

That “Shu” is also one of Merlin’s subordinates, but I’m afraid of being criticized, so I’ll introduce him later due to space limitations.

I still remember how hard it was to write Beelzebub, and readers cross-referenced and criticized me. I’ve developed a psychological shadow about writing supporting characters.

Every time I see comments saying that supporting characters have no soul, I have to swallow my bitterness. With just a few lines of Zhang San’s handsome face, how can I write a good supporting character?

Also, in a few days, I’ll release a new version of the Three-Person Characters design, with some badge benefits.

Finally, everyone can go and watch the manga, which has been adapted quite well over ten episodes, basically close to the original work.

Combining the manga to imagine the characters’ images is still pretty good. I wonder how that drunkard Hobbes will be drawn?

title: Chapter 1 — The Long-Awaited Little Devil
content:
Chapter 1 — The Long-Awaited Little Devil

Volume 25 · Chapter 1

Merlin brought little Chris home, passing through a small town on the way to Rexham.
Merlin originally planned to travel all night back to Rexham, but considering Chris's age….
Merlin had to give up his idea and just head back peacefully, after all, a small child can't endure a long journey.
This is a small town north of London, near the dangerous Magic Beast Forest, so there are especially many mercenaries in town!
Just a few steps away you can see groups of mercenaries; some are sharpening their knives, preparing to hunt magic beasts for materials, while others are happily flaunting beautiful women in their arms, obviously having made a big profit not long ago.
But there are even more mercenaries with grimy faces and low spirits, hiding in corners sighing, likely to be sleeping on the streets for the next few months.
Mercenaries and adventurers operate similarly, both taking money to do jobs, but mercenaries are unrestricted and haven't formed an industry scale like adventurers, with everything orderly.
If you hire a mercenary to do a job and encounter a bad‑hearted guy, he’ll take the money and disappear, leaving no way to hold these people accountable.
But if an adventurer takes money and doesn’t do the job, the adventurers’ headquarters will investigate and strip their qualification; clearly adventurers are more formal and trustworthy than mercenaries.
However, mercenaries’ income isn’t from doing jobs for people but from hunting magic beasts; if they luckily slay a Saint‑tier magic beast, they could squander a year’s worth.
This town near the Magic Beast Forest was originally a territory managed by the Oberfre ducal family, but they were wiped out due to rebellion.
Now it’s controlled by other nobles, but obviously their management is lacking; the town is chaotic, with all sorts of people walking the streets, and a little carelessness will lead to pickpockets. or 检 J小玩
However, little Chris, being so young, can’t really tell good from evil; she just loves lively crowds. Merlin was very vigilant on the road, lest someone steal his travel money.
“Daddy! Daddy! Higher~” Chris sat on Merlin’s shoulder, the high view making him feel novel.
“Huh? You want it higher?” Merlin frowned in surprise, hesitating, thinking Chris sitting on his shoulder was unstable; if she went higher and fell, she’d become a fool—what then?
“Just a little higher, please Daddy....” Chris pouted her little lips, pleading.
Merlin sighed, unable to refuse Chris—after all, who made this little troublemaker his own dear daughter?
Upon learning that Chris’s veins carried blood like his own, Merlin became more patient with her than before.
Merlin didn’t know how to be a qualified father; now he only knows how to simply cheer his daughter up.
Only see Merlin picked up Chris, letting the little one ride on his neck while he held her two short legs; previously she would fall.
“Sit steady, if you fall your head will swell up.
“Mmm!” Chris instantly became alert, her two little hands instinctively grabbing Merlin’s hair.
“Hiss~” Merlin grimaced, saying with a bitter face, “Chris, don’t pull Daddy’s hair; if you use force Daddy will go bald.
5 SE2小治
“But... but, if I don’t pull Daddy’s hair, I feel like I’m about to fall....” Chris said embarrassedly.
“.....” Merlin furrowed his brow, thought a bit, then smiled: “Go ahead and hold on; actually becoming bald doesn’t matter—I’m already a dad, what’s there to worry about appearances?”
“Ah‑nee?” Chris didn’t quite understand Merlin’s words; she lifted her head and saw farther away, the crowd below like a sea of heads, feeling as if she had a god’s view: “Daddy! I feel like I’ve become a giant!”
“Don’t be silly, what kind of giant is that? A real giant is far taller than you imagine; you might not even reach the tip of a giant’s toe.” Merlin twisted the corner of his mouth.
“Really? I want to see a real giant.” Chris said in a childish voice.
“A real giant? Probably only visible in the United Kingdom; that long‑eared elf sister earlier came from there.” Merlin said softly.
“.....” Chris’s little face was full of shock, her eyes sparkling with tiny stars: “I really want to go see....”
“Uh.... Merlin froze, then quickly changed his tone: “Well... giants aren’t that interesting, just a bit bigger; if we go see giants, we won’t see Mom for a long time—can you accept that?”
“... Mom is nicer, so I won’t look at giants.” Chris answered with a giggle.
Merlin secretly breathed a sigh of relief, thinking a child’s curiosity is too strong; he mustn’t speak nonsense, lest it spark her wild fantasies and make her dare anything.
“Gurgle gurgle” Chris’s stomach suddenly growled inopportunely, as if she hadn’t eaten in a long time?
“Huh? You hungry?” Merlin lifted his eyelids to ask. oF 牡小'沉
“.....” Chris’s face blushed embarrassedly, she bit her finger, staring at the nearby red apple, saliva immediately flowing uncontrollably.
“Sure enough, she’s hungry.” Merlin had black lines sliding down his forehead, wondering where to get milk; his gaze fell on the auntie selling apples, which looked fresh, “Do you really want to eat it?”
“Mmm‑mmm!” Chris nodded like a pecking chick, unable to resist her craving.
“Having a bite shouldn’t be a problem, after all she’s not a baby who can’t even speak....” Merlin thought, walked over, looked at the pile of red apples, picked the freshest one, and asked, “How much for it?”
“Five copper coins each.” The auntie, seeing a customer, immediately put on a professional smile.
“Five copper coins! ?”
Merlin was shocked, pulling out the only two silver coins left in his pocket, looking embarrassed.
Having two silver coins left in his pocket, not having thrown them into the racetrack, was already a miracle for Merlin!
This was also thanks to not encountering any place along the way where he could buy a race ticket; otherwise he might not be able to walk when he reached the gate.
Merlin thought carefully; he’d need to stay at an inn, still have— -8 meals, maybe even hire a carriage; this amount of money seemed insufficient, even the five‑copper‑coin apples felt too pricey—
Ah~, Alice that iron‑rooster! Why won’t she give me a bit more money? She controls the purse so tightly I can’t even afford an apple!
*Well... can it be cheaper?
“You still think it’s expensive? Apples are scarce this season; it’s already cheap.” The auntie’s face immediately turned unpleasant.
“How about two copper coins?” Merlin stretched out two fingers with a grin.
“Buy it or don’t!” The auntie saw Merlin was a pauper, her attitude instantly turned unfriendly: “How can someone so poor have a kid? You can give birth but not raise them; look at this cute baby, she’ll suffer with you in the future, you scumbag!”
“? ? ?” Merlin’s face darkened, veins faintly visible on his forehead, “What did you say! ?”
“.....” Seeing Dad being blamed, Chris’s expression turned sad: “Daddy, let’s go, Chris isn’t hungry…”
At that moment, a gold coin struck the apple‑selling auntie’s face straight on, very abrupt—
“I’ll buy all your apples; he can take as much as he wants…”
The auntie picked up the shiny gold coin, bit it with her teeth, and instantly beamed: “Sure sure sure! No problem!”
“Huh?” Merlin didn’t know who was helping him; he turned his head, his face full of disbelief, “Eh! Little……
Standing beside Merlin was a fifteen‑ or sixteen‑year‑old youthful boy, namely the youngest mithril adventurer famed as a magic genius who controls multiple elemental forces, Little Johnson.
Little Johnson put away his money pouch, turned his head to look at Merlin, his expression becoming meaningful, he tilted the corner of his mouth and said—
“Long time no see, …….”
“You’re still as useless as ever\臧

title: Chapter 2 — Season of the Monster Tide
content:
Chapter 2 — Season of the Monster Tide

Volume 25 · Chapter 2

Little Johnson was short, though he resembled Merlin in appearance, his expression was extremely arrogant, “I never would have thought, Uncle, you’ve sunk so low you can’t even afford an apple~” “Ugh!” Merlin’s face fell, being looked down on by this snot‑nosed brat, he felt terrible inside, “...I just rushed out without bringing any money.” “Really? If you can’t even afford a meal, I can graciously help you out,” Little Johnson said with a haughty expression. “Who needs your help, you brat?” Merlin rolled his eyes. “Fine then, forget it~” Little Johnson shrugged, curiously asking, “At a time like this, you still have the leisure to wander around—don’t you know the Adventurers’ Tournament is about to start?” “Huh? What tournament?” Merlin exclaimed, hearing about this for the first time. “Ha, you don’t even know about this? It’s unbelievable, do you even count as an adventurer?” Little Johnson felt a slight headache, helplessly explaining, “The Adventurers’ Tournament is a grand event for adventurers, held every four years, the most convincing way to demonstrate a guild’s strength. If you achieve a good ranking, it brings unparalleled benefits to the guild’s development—take London’s guild, for example; they placed third last time, and you can see that London’s guild is packed with elites, its prestige and strength unmatched by any other guild.” “Really? So there are competitions between guilds.” Merlin remarked, thinking it’s no wonder the two London adventurers he’d met were so arrogant—turns out their guild backed them. “Now all the major guilds have begun preparations; many guilds’ outstanding adventurers are undergoing emergency training, all to secure good rankings in the tournament. How about you? You’re still idling around here?” Little Johnson frowned, thinking Merlin was taking things too lightly. “There’s such a thing? I’m hearing about it for the first time today.” Merlin gave an embarrassed laugh, thinking Guild Master Tyler never mentioned it to him. “With your strength, Uncle, you’ll definitely enter, right?” Little Johnson probed. “Me?” Merlin thought for a moment, then shook his head, “I’m not sure yet.” “At this time you shouldn’t desert before the battle; I still want to defeat you in the tournament.” Little Johnson declared firmly, pointing at Merlin as if issuing a challenge, his competitive spirit strong. “You’re serious?” Merlin raised his eyebrows. “Hmph! Don’t think I’ll stay stagnant; I’ve been doing secret training all along, my power has skyrocketed. Now I’m heading to the Magic Beast Forest to slay a powerful magic beast, using its crystal core to boost my strength!” Little Johnson said eagerly, his goal being to kill a ferocious magic beast in the Magic Beast Forest, using the beast’s crystal core to elevate his power, fully preparing for the upcoming tournament. “Oh, good luck then.” Merlin replied nonchalantly. “Your condescending attitude is really unpleasant…” Little Johnson put his hands on his hips, wearing a serious expression, “Remember this, at the Adventurers’ Tournament I will get my revenge!” Chris rode on Merlin’s neck, listening to their nonsensical talk, and couldn’t help but ask in a childish voice, “Dad, who is he?” “Ha, just a clueless little brat, your dad’s defeated underling.” Merlin gave a half‑smile. “Defeated underling, hee‑hee~” Chris showed an innocent smile, mercilessly teasing Johnson. “What?” Little Johnson jumped back a step, incredulous, “This … this … world … calls you” “Although you’re older than her, you’re clearly still a little brat yourself?” Merlin tilted his mouth, introducing, “Her name is Chris, my precious daughter, Chris, go say hello to this snot‑nosed little guy~” “Hehe~ 8” Chris chubby‑handed waved at Little Johnson. “Good heavens!” Little Johnson was startled, finding it hard to accept reality, “No way? Someone like you… can actually be a dad?” “What do you mean? What’s wrong with me being a dad?” Merlin’s forehead veins twitched, as if everyone doubted his ability to be a father. “You can be a dad… done, this world is too crazy…” Little Johnson covered his mouth, his mood unsettled for a long while. “Hey, I’m not that bad, am I?” Merlin lifted his eyelids, smiling, “Right, Chris?” “Hehe~密” Chris happily responded. “Never mind…” Little Johnson didn’t want to dwell on this, he was in a hurry, turned and headed south, “See you!” “If you’re going to the Magic Beast Forest, you need to go north…” Merlin kindly reminded. “North~” Chris echoed in her dad’s tone, voice sweet. As a direction‑challenged person, Little Johnson’s face flushed, his body stiffened as he turned, lowered his head, and strode northward. “I know!” — a certain novel “Do you still need to tell me?!” “Shh~, meddling…” In a quiet spot beside a certain tavern in town, unlike the rowdy mercenary‑filled tavern, this place looked more formal, receiving only passing merchant travelers. Still, a few idle mercenaries loitered around the tavern, chatting because they hadn’t managed to hunt their desired magic beasts and felt frustrated. Fat mercenary: “Damn, we haven’t harvested anything in over half a month; if this continues we won’t even be able to afford alcohol.” Skinny mercenary: “Yeah, seeing other mercenaries splash money on drink and women, I’m envious too.” Fat mercenary: “No, we need to find a way to make some money.” Skinny mercenary: “How? Recently the Magic Beast Forest isn’t safe; it’s the once‑a‑year magic beast surge season, the city guards are on high alert, and those beasts are even more ferocious than usual.” Fat mercenary: “It’s dangerous, but for us two brothers it’s also a chance to get rich. Don’t forget, many high‑level magic beasts normally lie dormant; when the magic beast surge season arrives they awaken and become active. If we pull off a job, we’ll earn enough to eat for three years.” Skinny mercenary: “That… sounds too risky? At night magic beasts appear frequently; if we’re unlucky we could run into a whole pack.” Fat mercenary: “What’s there to fear? With our experience we can easily avoid large groups of magic beasts; our target is a big score—directly hunt high‑level magic beasts.” Skinny mercenary: “Hunting high‑level… our strength isn’t enough, it would be dangerous.” Fat mercenary: “Yesterday I spent all my savings and bought a high‑level magic scroll.” Skinny mercenary: “What!? You bought a high‑level magic scroll? First time seeing you so willing to spend money.” Fat mercenary: “This time we’ll definitely succeed; killing a high‑level magic beast means guaranteed profit, though we need to figure out how to lure one out.” Skinny mercenary: “Ordinary bait has limited effect on magic beasts, but they love eating infants; they’ll show up once they smell it.” This is Merlin holding a bag of fresh apples in his left hand and Chris in his right hand, walking toward this quiet tavern. “Chris, what would you like to drink when we go in?” “I’ll have whatever you have, Dad!” “Mischievous, you can only drink milk, and no ice…” The fat and skinny mercenaries withdrew their glances, looked at each other… Both fell silent, the wicked thoughts in their hearts stirring…

title: Chapter 3 — Restless Night (Extra)
content:
Chapter 3 — Restless Night (Extra)

Volume 25 · Chapter 3

The inn where traveling merchants lodged looked exceptionally clean; the first floor was where customers drank and chatted, while the second floor had rooms for resting.
The innkeeper was a big-bearded uncle with a face full of fierce muscles, looking fierce and stern, clearly stating that his establishment did not allow mercenaries to enter, otherwise their legs would be broken.
Merlin first booked a room, then brought Chris downstairs to have a drink.
He gently set Chris on the stool beside him, snapped his fingers, and said, "One beer, one hot milk."
"Just a moment." The innkeeper busied himself, glanced at Merlin, noticed he was also bringing a two-year-old child, and instantly felt curious.
"Um... boss, why don't you accept mercenaries here?" Merlin asked curiously.
"I used to be a mercenary myself; I know exactly what kind of conduct mercenaries have." The innkeeper said fiercely, flexing his strong arms to prove he had once wielded a blade.
...... Merlin scratched his cheek, a few black lines appearing on his forehead, thinking that mercenaries were indeed a mixed bag and lacked management.
Little Chris blinked her big eyes at the innkeeper's big beard and said in a childish voice, "Uncle's big beard is scary!"
"Chris, don't talk nonsense." Merlin reminded her softly.
"It's really scary..." Chris, feeling wronged, poked up her two fingers.
"Oh? Really?" The innkeeper subconsciously touched his beard, then his old face turned red, and he said embarrassedly, "In a town full of mercenaries, if you don't act fierce, you can't survive."
"Please don't mind, she's still a child...." Merlin said embarrassedly, thinking he never imagined that one day he himself would use this phrase to morally blackmail someone.
"It's fine, children speak without restraint." The innkeeper handed Merlin a beer, gave Chris double the hot milk, and finally didn't forget to send a piece of cream cake with a cherry on top, saying, "Little one, this is for you."
"Isn't that inappropriate?" Merlin said in surprise, not liking to casually accept others' kindness.
"It's fine, this child is cute; I instinctively want to cheer her up, so I hope you won't refuse." The innkeeper said lightly.
Merlin glanced at Chris beside him, seeing her eyes light up; before eating, she was already captivated by the beautiful cream cake in front of her, and he said, "Why aren't you thanking them?"
Chris sensibly lifted her head, the cowlick on her head happily swaying, and said, "Thank you, uncle; I feel you're not so scary, you're kind..."
The innkeeper smiled, said nothing more, turned and continued with his work.
"You little clever ghost." Merlin rubbed Chris's head, thinking this child was really sly; before, she disliked people for being ugly, but give her a candy and she'd praise them as gentle; from a young age she showed the trait of changing faces extremely quickly, huh! Just like Alice!
Chris ate cream cake for the first time, feeling it melt in her mouth, incredibly sweet, her whole body delighted, and she exclaimed, "Good.... so good! Dad, can I eat this every day from now on?"
"Pfft!" Merlin spat out the beer he had just drunk, put on a serious face, and said, "No, this will make you fat like a piglet, and then Mom and Dad won't be able to hold you."
".... Chris froze, caught in hesitation, her heart struggling intensely, even at her young age revealing a dramatics nature."
"This sweet, fragrant thing is evil! Chris can't eat it, otherwise Mom and Dad won't be able to hold you!"
"But... it's really delicious, it'd be a shame to miss it; Mom said not to waste food!"
"Eating it will turn me into a piglet, not eating it wastes food; Chris is in agony, wuu..."
Merlin watched Chris with interest, this little one caught in self-contradiction, looking adorably silly.
Chris really wanted to listen to her parents, but couldn't resist the temptation of the food; in the end she sneakily glanced at Merlin once and blinked her eyes.
Merlin laughed, thinking this little one was still finding noble excuses for herself, so thick-skinned... huh! She's my child.
"Eat slowly; when you're done, go upstairs to sleep; we should be home in about two days."
Chris looked already quite hungry, having a bit of a wolfish devouring posture; to avoid worrying her dad, even if hungry she tried to endure it, but her stomach growled and she couldn't hide it.
Merlin looked at little Chris's hungry appearance, and a hint of sourness welled up in his heart.
I, as a father, am really inadequate; if it were Alice, she'd surely take better care of the child than I do.
Merlin began to notice the other patrons in the inn—altogether three people: two dust-covered merchants in attire, chatting; another drinking in the corner, looking very mysterious, wearing a windbreaker with the hat pressed low, making it impossible to see his face.
Tall merchant: "Sigh! Don't mention it; lately it's the season of frequent monster surges, business is

title: Chapter 4 — Anxiety Spreads
content:
Chapter 4 — Anxiety Spreads

Volume 25 · Chapter 4

"Doggie, doggie, wait for me~"

Chris chased after the little wild dog, leaving the remote tavern without Merlin's knowledge.

Still young, she had a playful nature and was completely defenseless against small animals like cats and dogs.

Suddenly, two mercenaries emerged from a dark corner, blocking Chris's path and eyeing her with malicious intent.

Chris immediately grew tense, fear rising within her as she was stared down by two menacing-looking adults.

"Heh heh, what did I say? Kids are so easy to trick, it's a breeze to lure them out."

The fat mercenary tossed a bone to the stray dog nearby as a reward.

The fat mercenary had been feeding the stray dog his leftover scraps for a long time, and over time the dog had come to see him as its master, obeying his commands without question.

The thin mercenary grinned and gave a thumbs-up to his companion, praising him.

"Amazing, that dog hasn't been raised in vain, haha..."

"..." Chris had a terrible premonition and bolted back toward the tavern, calling out, "Dad! Ugh!?"

The thin mercenary was quick on his feet, grabbing her and clamping his hand over her mouth before she could cry for help. "Run? We went to all this trouble to lure you little one out, do you really think we'd let you go back?"

"Ugh!!!" Chris struggled desperately, only able to make muffled sounds, her cries for help unable to reach Merlin's ears.

The thin mercenary looked up and asked, "What do we do now?"

"Need I ask? We slip out of town under cover of darkness and head straight for the Demon Beast Forest." The fat mercenary looked at his companion and said in a low voice, "We use this kid as bait, and pretty soon we'll draw out a high-tier demon beast. As long as we kill one, you and I can party it up for..."

Inside the tavern, two merchants were discussing the dangers of the Demon Beast Forest and expressing concern about the town's current safety.

Merlin listened with keen interest, secretly sighing that he had come at the worst possible time, right during the season when demon beasts ran rampant.

I should go to bed early and take Chris away from this place of trouble as soon as possible...

Merlin drained his remaining beer in one gulp, then turned and smiled at Chris beside him. "Chris, let's eat... huh?!"

Only now did Merlin realize that the seat beside him was empty—Chris was nowhere to be found. Where had that girl run off to?

He shot up from his chair and scanned the room, but couldn't find any sign of Chris, and his heart instantly filled with panic.

"Chris! Chris!? Where are you? Stop playing, come back right now!"

Merlin called out tentatively, thinking Chris was just playing hide-and-seek with him. But after calling several times, there was still no response.

The other patrons in the tavern noticed Merlin's strange behavior and looked at him in confusion, wondering what madness had taken him.

Merlin was burning with anxiety, cursing himself inwardly for letting his guard down even for a moment. Kids really knew how to cause trouble.

"Boss! Did you see that child who was sitting next to me?!"

"Huh? I didn't notice..." The tavern owner looked up, having been wiping tables the whole time.

"Did any of you see her?!" Merlin immediately turned and asked everyone in the tavern.

The two merchants glanced at each other and shook their heads at the same time. They had been too absorbed in their conversation to notice a child.

Only the trench coat man in the corner remained silent, showing no reaction at all, as if nothing had anything to do with him.

Merlin frowned, wondering if this mysterious guy knew something but was deliberately staying quiet.

Merlin was in a rush right now, and to find Chris, he couldn't afford to let any suspicious person go.

Merlin instinctively reached for his sword, only to remember he hadn't brought it, so he approached the trench coat man with empty hands.

"Hey, why aren't you saying anything? Did you see where that child next to me went?"

The trench coat man remained unmoved, as if he hadn't heard. He went on pouring himself a drink and stared blankly at the liquor.

This person seemed completely cut off from the world, indifferent to everything around him—truly an outlier.

Merlin gritted his teeth, clenching his fists in anger, feeling an urge to teach this weirdo a lesson...

What the hell is this bastard doing? A mute? Why won't he speak!

Merlin slammed his hand on the table with a bang, knocking over the trench coat man's cup. The liquor spilled and flowed across the table onto the floor.

"Speak!"

The trench coat man fiddled with his fingers, slowly raising his head. When he saw the black iron adventurer's badge on Merlin's chest, he finally reacted. "I've never once encountered a black iron adventurer with such a bad temper..."

"What did you say?" Merlin felt the other's condescension and his brows immediately knitted together.

"Has nobody ever told you what attitude you should use when asking someone for a favor?" the trench coat man said without looking up.

"You!" Merlin was about to lose his temper, but then remembered his lovely daughter was missing, and he had to suppress his anger, softening his tone. "If you know anything, please tell me. I'm in a hurry right now."

The trench coat man calmly poured himself another drink, took a sip, and said indifferently, "Two mercenaries were acting suspiciously outside the tavern just now. I think that child was probably kidnapped."

"Mercenaries? Were they one fat and one thin?" the tavern owner suddenly spoke up.

"Exactly." The trench coat man replied briefly.

"Damn it, those two are scoundrels. They've been lurking around my tavern for a while now. I should have broken their legs long ago!" The tavern owner gritted his teeth and said bitterly.

Merlin's expression darkened. Kidnapped by mercenaries? What would they want with a child?

But right now, Merlin was extremely disgusted with this trench coat man and deeply resented his inaction.

"Were you just going to stand by and watch them kidnap a child? Why didn't you speak up!"

The trench coat man was silent for a moment, then looked up and said something that stunned everyone:

"What does it have to do with me if that child was kidnapped by mercenaries? Why should I meddle in other people's affairs?"

Merlin froze, then the veins on his forehead began to throb. He really wanted to tear this guy apart with his bare hands.

The other patrons in the tavern looked at the trench coat man with strange expressions, wondering if this guy had any humanity at all.

Anyone with even a shred of justice would have stepped forward to stop thugs from kidnapping a child.

"Tell me, what reason do I have to stop that child from being taken?" the trench coat man looked up and demanded.

At this point, Merlin, who should have been furious, heard the mysterious man's question and his mind suddenly cooled down...

Right, what reason does this guy have to stop them? This self-centered, trouble-averse personality is just like mine...

Merlin lowered his head and realized that his own personality was the same as this guy's—both were annoying and detestable.

In the end, he had run into a kindred spirit of egoism, and only then did Merlin realize how detestable he himself could be. Not everyone was warm-hearted like Alice.

"What would they want with a kidnapped child?"

"Perhaps they're using her as bait..."

The tavern owner crossed his strong arms and answered thoughtfully. "I used to be a mercenary, so I know a thing or two about this. Those demon beasts really do like to eat tender-fleshed children. Some impatient types use infants as bait to lure high-tier demon beasts into traps. For money, these people will do anything. It's currently the demon beast tide season, and the demon beasts in the forest are very active. Those two bastards kidnapping a child might be trying to hunt down a big one for..."

After hearing this, Merlin could only feel restless and anxious. His heart felt as though it were on fire, filled with unease...

"The Demon Beast For..."

title: Chapter 5 — Qika Dilo (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 5 — Qika Dilo (Extra Chapter)

Volume 25 · Chapter 5

Thinking of Chris with the two dangerous mercenaries together, surrounded by countless hungry magic beasts….
Merlin instantly felt his head a bit dizzy, his heart unable to calm for a moment, and he walked straight out.
“What are you doing this late, sir?” the innkeeper suddenly asked.
“Sweep away the magic beasts…….” Merlin replied bluntly.
“???. ”
Everyone stared at Merlin in shock, as if looking at an idiot.
In their view, Merlin was joking; the magic beast forest existed before the Kingdom of Britain was established.
So many mercenaries and guards had once planned to exterminate the dangerous magic beasts, but ultimately could not.
Yet Merlin, who looks ordinary, declared he would sweep the magic beast forest, which is no different from joking.
“Don’t be so impulsive, sir; it’s the magic beast tide season, and fierce magic beasts often appear in groups outside the town. Going out now is dangerous; why not hire some guards and go by day?” the innkeeper kindly reminded.
“Daytime? I can’t wait for daytime.” Merlin put on his coat and headed straight for the magic beast forest.
Just as the innkeeper was at a loss, the man in the windcoat suddenly spoke:
“You, a mere black‑iron adventurer, what could you possibly do even if you went out?”
“This has nothing to do with my status; that’s my daughter, and I must find her back.” Merlin said solemnly.
“Well…. ” The windcoat‑clad man downed his drink, slowly stood, took off his heavy windcoat hat, revealing his face, “It just so happens I also need to go to the magic beast forest, so let’s—go together.”
Black skin, dark‑red eyes, fine scars on the face, pointed ears on both sides, and a mithril adventurer’s token on his chest shining brightly.
He had the appearance of a black elf, but with notable differences— not as handsome or tall as an elf, his nose sunken, as if elf ears were stuck onto a human head?
“An elf?!” Merlin was startled by the man’s appearance; it was unheard of for a foreign race to live in the human world and still work as an adventurer.
“Let me correct that—I am a half‑elf…” Zeqatilo emphasized.
“A half‑elf?” Merlin frowned, wondering if it was a mix of human and black elf; in elves’ eyes humans are the top race, yet he never imagined they’d engage in such affairs with humans.
The two merchants nearby, seeing Zeqatilo, were startled by his sudden elf‑like appearance and began whispering to each other.
Tall merchant: “Black elf?! How could there be a black elf here?”
Short merchant: “No, look—he’s carrying an adventurer’s token; he looks familiar.”
Tall merchant: “Zeqatilo… Good heavens! It’s Zeqatilo, the monster of the Manchester Adventurers Guild!”
Short merchant: “He’s Zeqatilo? The strongest among Manchester adventurers? He looks so young.”
Tall merchant: “Young? He could be older than your grandfather; rumor says he’s the offspring of a licentious mother and a black‑elf merchant, possessing elf blood and thus a long life.”
Short merchant: “Good heavens, this freak—I heard he once challenged the president of the London Guild, the purple‑gold adventurer Gregory. Is that true?”
Tall merchant: “True, though I don’t know if he won; everyone says his strength is close to that of a purple‑gold adventurer, very strong.”
Short merchant: “I never expected this *‑born mixed‑blood to have such talent; it seems the legend of elves’ superb magical talent is true—didn’t he inherit it well?”
Zeqatilo’s icy gaze snapped toward the two merchants, faint irritation flashing in his eyes.
The two merchants immediately shut up, pretending to admire the scenery, but inside they were terrified of this half‑elf adventurer.
Zeqatilo was abandoned by his parents at birth because, as a mixed‑blood half‑elf, he found no favor there.
Elves would despise him for having the filthy blood of sinners, deeming him unworthy of their kind.
And humans obviously would not accept a human bearing elf ears, considering him a freak.
Fortunately, Zeqatilo met a kind soul who was taken in by the Manchester Adventurers Guild and became the foster son of the old guild president.
Due to his ugly half‑elf appearance, nobody liked him; he was even called a monster, a ** mixed‑blood, and only the guild’s adventurers were willing to accept him.
Growing up in such an environment, Zeqatilo became solitary and odd, disliking contact with outsiders to the guild, and this also shaped him into a—
play
Each day he relied on studying magic to pass the time; at age seven Zeqatilo showed outstanding magical talent, gaining his foster father’s attention and beginning his training.
At seventeen, his kind foster father passed away, leaving Zeqatilo without his only relative; that year he had already become the strongest being in Manchester.
Because of his foster father, Zeqatilo had always considered himself human, yet he deeply disliked others gossiping about him, and hearing it naturally gave him a sour expression.
Zeqatilo withdrew his warning glare, lowered his head and said: “Don’t be so surprised; I am a half‑elf, but I hope you treat me as a person.”
Merlin had no interest in Zeqatilo’s identity and asked doubtfully: “You don’t like meddling, so why are you following me now?”
“Because you’re a fellow adventurer, I can help you; I was actually planning to go to the magic beast forest anyway, so early or late makes no difference—just on the way.” Zeqatilo put on his windcoat hat, covering his ears, “Besides… my father was an excellent adventurer who said adventurers are free‑spirited folk who dislike rules, and I like that, so even if you’re a lowly black‑iron, I won’t despise you.”
Merlin frowned as he watched Zeqatilo leave the tavern, unable to stop himself from muttering.
G.
What a strange fellow…
Merlin didn’t need Zeqatilo’s help, but since he was willing to come, Merlin wouldn’t refuse; besides, he was unfamiliar with the magic beast forest and needed a guide.
Zeqatilo, however, thought Merlin was a weak black‑iron adventurer; going to the magic beast forest at night would be suicide, so he desperately needed his assistance.
As a half‑elf raised by adventurers, Zeqatilo felt resistance toward anyone, yet he would never despise fellow adventurers.
This is also why the reclusive, solitary Zeqatilo is willing to lend Merlin a hand—under the influence of his deceased foster father and the old guild president of Manchester.
The two set off together toward the town gate, ready to head immediately for the magic beast forest—
Merlin: “Why do you have elf blood?”
Zeqatilo: “I refuse to answer.”
Merlin: “Is your father a black elf or your mother a black elf?”
Zeqatilo: “I refuse to answer.”
Merlin: “In your Manchester Guild, aside from you, are there any other mixed‑bloods?”
Zeqatilo: “I refuse to answer.”
Merlin: “You’re an idiot, right? Not answering just means…”

title: Chapter 6 — Monster Tide
content:
Chapter 6 — Monster Tide

Volume 25 · Chapter 6

The two hurried toward the city gate in the night, the distant wind howling continuously. I once worked as a part-timer in Mancest, and I've never heard of someone like you existing. After all, how did a half-breed like you become an adventurer?" Merlin looked at Qikatiluo, curiously asking, "Why don't you speak? Wouldn't it be good to introduce yourself a little?" "I beg you to say less; you don't seem worried about your daughter at all," Qikatiluo glanced at Merlin. "I do worry about her, but having a guy like you following me makes me uneasy," Merlin muttered suspiciously. Qikatiluo fell silent, then said calmly, "Please don't treat me as an outsider." Actually, Qikatiluo misunderstood; Merlin was simply wary of dark elves, for in the United Kingdom he had almost been killed by them. So even though Qikatiluo is a half-dark elf, Merlin still refuses to let his guard down, worried that this guy might betray him at a critical moment. The two went straight to the town's gate; because it was the season when magic beasts were active, the town's guards dared not sleep at night. At that moment, clusters of torches illuminated the top of the city wall, and the guards patrolled back and forth; if there was any movement outside the wall, the guards would start defending. Merlin stepped before the guard on duty and said solemnly, "Please open the gate and let us out!" The guard stared, then answered seriously, "What are you going out to do? It's very dangerous outside; unless it's an emergency, no one is allowed to open the gate without permission." "It's an emergency! My child was kidnapped by two bastards!" Merlin paused, then said anxiously, "They want to use my child as bait to lure the ferocious magic beasts in the forest! We must go to the Magic Beast Forest! Please open the gate!" "What the hell, why are there so many fearless people tonight?" the guard muttered, recalling that just a moment ago two mercenaries also rushed to leave the city, "The sky is completely dark now; if you had arrived earlier I could have let you out, but now... you can't, after dark no one is allowed to leave the town, and opening the gate is even more forbidden—who knows if there aren't hordes of magic beasts roaming in the darkness? If we open the gate and they rush in, what then? Can you bear that responsibility?" "Don't worry, with me here no magic beast will be able to rush into the town." Merlin said seriously. "You?" the guard looked Merlin up and down, gave a helpless smile, "Adventurer sir, please don't joke like that; in the face of a horde of magic beasts, you're not even enough to fill a tooth gap." "I'm not joking; believe me, you just need to open the gate and let us out." Merlin said with a furrowed brow, feeling an urge to smash the gate. "No, this is the rule; I hope you can understand, we're also considering the town's safety." The guard said with a half-smile. Just as Merlin was gritting his teeth about to explode, Qikatiluo stepped forward, pulled off his adventurer's proof from his neck and showed it to the guard, saying, "I need to go to the Magic Beast Forest to handle an important matter; please open the gate. The magic beasts you worry about charging into the town are nothing dangerous in my eyes." The guard looked dubiously at the adventurer's proof, then his eyes widened in shock, "Mithril Adventurer! .... Qikatiluo!" Other guards stationed not far away, hearing that name, all jumped in fright, their gazes snapping over. "What?! Qikatiluo?!" "Is that really Qikatiluo? The strongest adventurer from Mancest!" "How did he end up here? Unbelievable!" The guard held the Mithril Adventurer's proof with both hands, trembling as he lifted his head to look at Qikatiluo before him. Although Qikatiluo wore a heavy windbreaker and hat, by the torchlight one could faintly see his dark skin and scarlet eyes. The guard had obviously heard of Qikatiluo this oddball; instinctively he felt fear toward this eccentric, solitary adventurer, and immediately trembled as he returned the Mithril Adventurer's proof and ordered: "Open the gate!" With a rumbling, the heavy iron gate slowly opened; the guards stepped aside voluntarily, no one daring to provoke Qikatiluo. Qikatiluo walked ahead, then suddenly noticed Merlin lagging behind in a daze, not keeping up, and said, "What are you spacing out for? Hurry up and follow!" "Shout!" Merlin pouted sourly, couldn't help muttering lowly, "High-level adventurer proof sure is handy..." The two left the town; Qikatiluo looked around, pointed north, and said, "The Magic Beast Forest is that way; if we travel all night we can reach it before dawn." "I know even without you saying it." Merlin strode forward, but Qikatiluo suddenly grabbed his shoulder. "What are you doing?" "Our luck isn't great; as soon as we left the town we were spotted by those hungry fellows." Qikatiluo said lowly, his gaze toward the pitch-black darkness ahead where one couldn't see five fingers. The watchman on the town's tower sensed a slight movement and something unusual, lit a fire-arrow, and shot it with a "bang!" In the night, the flying fire-arrow was like a meteor, illuminating a farther place-- Where it passed, it revealed dense crowds of monsters! Their eyes flickered with a hungry red light, and the gaps between their sharp fangs constantly dripped saliva. Their bodies were covered in glossy black fur, with strange patterns running along it, similar to wild dogs but their size was several times that of a wild dog! Magic hounds, mid-tier magic beasts, have wolf-like habits, like to move in packs, and are something mercenaries greatly fear. A single magic hound isn't scary; the problem is that thousands of magic hounds acting together, with countless vicious eyes, is enough to make one's legs go weak. "M... it's magic hounds! Close the gate!" The guards were stunned, hastily shut the gate, and grabbed their bows, gathering atop the wall. The longbows and arrows are specially forged, "can easily pierce scales, and with magical enchantment, a single arrow can make a magic beast's skin split and flesh burst." Innumerable arrows lit up in the darkness, already nocked, just waiting for the magic hounds to enter range to loose! The guards were tense, cold sweat trickling down their foreheads; despite being prepared, they never expected to face a magic beast tide of such magnitude. Thousands of magic hounds swarmed, constantly growling, as if sensing the scent of living beings, they left the forest and surrounded this small town. Even though the town guards had ample ammunition, trying to block a massive assault of magic hounds was obviously no small difficulty. Though the magic hounds were somewhat helpless against the solid walls, seeing two living creatures emerge made the pack instantly become aggressive. These magic hounds are mid-tier magic beasts; they lack high intelligence, only following instinct—when hungry they must go eat living creatures! The dense mass of magic hounds moved, merging with the darkness, countless scarlet eyes fixed on Merlin and Qikatiluo. They opened their huge mouths, revealing terrifying fangs, tongues lolling as they sprinted madly, afraid that if they were slow they'd get no food. Merlin looked at the unstoppable tide of magic beasts before him; to him it wasn't frightening. In numbers and strength, they paled compared to the magic beasts he had faced in the blood-marsh swamps of Camilla.

title: Chapter 7 — Shadow Sickle
content:
Chapter 7 — Shadow Sickle

Volume 25 · Chapter 7

Merlin's repulsive space was about to be activated, but was suddenly stopped by Chikatilo.

Chikatilo pushed Merlin's hand down, walked to the front calmly, and spoke calmly.

"Beasts like this will hold hatred for those who attack them. You'd better not make a fool of yourself. Leave this to me..."

"A?" Merlin frowned, muttering discontentedly, "Don't look down on me, you guy."

Chikatilo ignored Merlin and walked toward the surging demon beast tide, his face showing not the slightest emotional fluctuation.

The demon dogs were extremely excited; their hunger instinct made them lose reason, opening their bloody mouths to rush toward Chikatilo one after another.

Chikatilo raised his arm, revealing the magic ring inlaid with jet-black Gluttony, which suddenly shone with deep purple light in the night. He narrowed his eyes—

"...Shadow Sickle....

The low sound fell, and the dark magic elements in the air moved with his will, appearing out of nowhere—a shadow sickle!

Chikatilo waved his wrist, and the shadow sickle danced, killing toward the fierce demon dogs before him.

The shadow sickle seemed to have life itself, growing as it faced the wind, becoming enormous by the time it reached the demon dogs!

A "whoosh" of cutting through the air suddenly sounded; the giant shadow sickle slashed the demon dogs, spraying blood and flesh, unstoppable!

The guards on the city wall watched in astonishment, instinctively lowering their longbows. Every swing of the shadow sickle made their hearts tighten.

The vicious demon dogs had no resistance under the giant shadow sickle, like cutting melons and vegetables, slaughtered one-sidedly!

In just a few seconds, thousands of mid-tier demon beasts were swept away by the shadow sickle. The demon dogs finally realized the danger; a small portion fled in panic in all directions, leaving their companions' corpses all over the ground.

The slaughter ended; the giant shadow sickle rapidly shrank, wrapping around Chikatilo's body and turning into a wisp of black smoke.

"Let's go, we're safe."

Merlin remained silent, looking at Chikatilo, thinking this guy had some skill. No wonder others feared him. Staring at the dark elf's appearance, with such strength, any human would be scared.

The guards on the city wall seemed stunned, standing motionless, looking at the pile of stinking demon beast corpses below—

"Is this the maniacal adventurer called a monster? Too terrifying..."

"Exactly, not even blinking in the face of demon beast tides..."

"Heard his strength is close to a Purple Gold adventurer, how terrifying would a true Purple Gold adventurer be?"

In the demon beast forest north of the town, the mercenaries relied on their rich experience to successfully avoid the dangerous demon beast tide and arrived deep in the forest.

At this moment, little Chris's mouth was sealed, only able to make weak "mm" sounds for help; her little face had long cried into a mess.

To use Chris as bait to attract high-tier demon beasts, the two mercenaries tied her up and hung her on a tall tree.

This way, if they encountered high-tier demon beasts that couldn't climb trees, they might smell the child's scent and come, but couldn't eat Chris, making them stay under the tree.

In the grass, the fat and thin mercenaries hid, staring intently at the tree, expecting high-tier demon beasts to come to them.

Thin mercenary: "Why aren't they coming? I'm bitten all over by bugs..."

Fat mercenary: "Wait a bit. This time we're going to make a big score, worth waiting three days and three nights!"

Thin mercenary: "If it really takes three days and three nights, we can't stand it either?"

Fat mercenary: "Don't worry, beasts' noses are sharp. They'll be here in a bit..."

The two crouched in the grass for an hour, finally hearing sounds from deep in the forest. As expected, a high-tier demon beast had smelled Chris's scent.

A beast strong like a war chariot slowly walked out, resembling a wild boar but covered in thorns, looking extremely sharp.

Two tusks protruded from its mouth, pig nose sniffing the ground constantly, approaching the Chris hanging on the tree in a few steps.

Fat mercenary: "Haha, what did I say? Sure enough, attracted a high-tier demon beast."

Thin mercenary: "A Giant Thorn Pig? A bit tricky. This thing has strong combat power, thick skin and meat. Can a high-tier magic scroll one-shot kill it?"

Fat mercenary: "Don't worry, I bought a fire-attribute single-target magic scroll. Destructive power is superb. Kill this thorn pig, and we can also have some roasted pork~"

Thin mercenary: "Then hurry up. The crystal core of this Giant Thorn Pig can sell for a lot of money~"

The Giant Thorn Pig's thorns looked particularly sharp; mercenaries didn't like encountering them—hard to hit and easy to be counter-killed.

This high-tier demon beast was full of lean meat, seemingly full of power, as tall as two adults, moving like a moving hill covered in thorns.

The Giant Thorn Pig came under the tree, raised its head, round eyes turning unevenly, lifted its front hoof to lean against the tree, tongue full of thorns deep inside, wanting to lick little Chris down from above.

"Ugh!!! Chris exclaimed, thinking the little pig below was not cute at all, struggling desperately, spinning in circles hanging from the rope.

But the tree was too tall; the Giant Thorn Pig fussed for a while without success, then got furious.

It started relying on its strong body, frequently colliding with the tree, wanting to break it, then eat the delicious little baby.

At this moment, the two mercenaries hiding in the grass seized the perfect opportunity when the Giant Thorn Pig was distracted, jumped out to attack.

"Flame Spear!"

The mercenary used the magic scroll bought at high price. A thin flame tore through the night sky, stabbing straight into the Giant Thorn Pig's brain.

A fire-element spear of burning flame pierced through the Giant Thorn Pig. Even with its extraordinary defense, it couldn't withstand the destructive power of a single-target high-tier magic!

"Awooo!!!"

The Giant Thorn Pig screamed in pain, the flame burning making it lose reason, starting to run around wildly, constantly colliding with surrounding giant trees!

In a moment, the second attack of Flame Spear released. With a "boom", the Giant Thorn Pig's head exploded!

For a moment the air was filled with the smell of burning and fragrant roasted pork smell...

"Done!" The thin mercenary cheered, running over eagerly.

"We're rich!"

The fat mercenary hurriedly followed behind the thin mercenary, secretly pulling out a small knife.

His gaze turned sinister, revealing a mocking smile, a knife stabbed through the thin mercenary's heart from behind!

Drip by drip, blood slowly flowed down the blade. The fat mercenary's smile grew even more rampant.

"You?! Ah..." The thin mercenary stiffened, showing an incredulous expression, trying to glance sideways at the comrade behind him, never expecting to be betrayed.

"Sorry, brother..." The fat mercenary skewed his mouth, leaning close to the companion's ear to say softly—

"Meals, can be eaten together.
Money, cannot be spent together.
Sharing hardships is possible, sharing happiness...
No!"

title: Chapter 8 — Letter from the Great Snow Mountain
content:
Chapter 8 — Letter from the Great Snow Mountain

Volume 25 · Chapter 8

“.... skinny mercenary's life quickly ebbed away, using his last strength to curse, “Not good....” “Hmph!” The fat mercenary threw his small island**, the skinny mercenary's corpse fell limp, blood spreading. He wiped the blood‑stained dagger with his sleeve and spat at his companion’s corpse. “Pah! You hide your good stuff yourself, do you think I don’t know? You bastard, you’re not even worthy to share loot with me?” “Ugh!” Little Chris, hanging from the tree, saw killing for the first time, almost fainted from fright, tears streaming nonstop, her mind filled with how scary the outside world was, as if she wanted to go home to find her parents. The fat mercenary lifted his eyelids, glared at Chris with one eye, and said coldly, “Cry! Cry hard!
