"Ptoo!" Rosetti spat out the tea in her mouth and quickly wiped her lips, explaining, "Hobbes is talking nonsense! I've never spread rumors. That drunkard is an information merchant — for money, he'd embellish anything!"

Merlin couldn't be bothered to argue with Rosetti. After all, in situations like this, no one would ever admit to anything. He hadn't even gone out for a few days, and already people were throwing dirt on him. What terrible luck.

"What's the child's name?" Rosetti asked.

"Chris," Alice answered.

"Oh~ Chris, come here. Come to big sister." Rosetti opened her arms.

"Chris hesitated and looked at her mother, as if seeking permission. Alice smiled and set her down. Chris walked over on her own.

"Yay~" Rosetti picked up Chris and pinched her chubby cheeks. "Kids' skin is always so good. Other than the eyes, she looks more like Alice."

Little Chris was somewhat shy around strangers. She kept staring at Rosetti's impressive chest, unable to look away. If she weren't a girl, people might easily mistake her for a little pervert.

*So huge~ Bigger than Sister Beluvia's!*

*How many beatings has she endured in her life? It's unbelievable!*

Chris remembered her mother forbidding her from speaking carelessly, so she tightly closed her mouth, though her eyes were filled with sympathy for Rosetti.

In this little one's eyes, Rosetti had become associated with a woman of tragic fate, and she had decided to make her parents save her.

"Then..." Rosetti furrowed her brows and asked suspiciously, "Alice, why do I feel like this child is looking at me with a strange gaze? Like she's pitying me."

"Who knows? Maybe it's uncomfortable being held by you." Alice's eyes darted evasively, guilty inside.

"Really??? " Rosetti looked down at little Chris in her arms, who was simply keeping her mouth tightly shut and saying nothing.

Seeing Da Vinci quietly remaining silent and staring at Chris for quite a long time, Merlin couldn't help but ask, "Miss Da Vinci, you are well-traveled and skilled in alchemy. When we encountered a stone in the United Kingdom, even the elves were unclear about its origins. Do you happen to know where that stone came from? I remember you once said that alchemy can create life itself."

"That's right. Alchemy can create life, but it absolutely cannot create a highly intelligent being. However, this child..." Da Vinci stared at Chris, her expression shifting unpredictably.

"Stare~" Chris curiously locked eyes with Da Vinci, not blinking at all, as if playing a childish game of who would blink first and lose.

"I'm very sorry, I'm not sure either." Da Vinci lowered her head, her eyes flickering repeatedly. She seemed to know something but hesitated to say it outright.

Could a highly intelligent life form be born from blood contact with a stone?

This was itself absurd, virtually impossible!

No matter the method, it would absolutely not create a highly intelligent life form.

Even with my vast reading, I can only find six stories of life creation.

[Story 1] The Holy Light Goddess Maria, lonely because she had no family, created two children — Cain and Abel.

title: Chapter 28 — Attempting Analysis
content:
Chapter 28 — Attempting Analysis

Volume 25 · Chapter 28

Is that so? Miss Da Vinci doesn't know either... Merlin muttered to himself, thinking that although Chris had inherited his and Alice's bloodline, her origins remained a mystery.
"Don't dwell on this issue; this child resembles you both, so it's fine to treat her as your own child." Rossetti lowered his gaze to little Chris, then lifted his head and said, "Besides, the world is vast, and even now there are many unexplained mysteries. Da Vinci is already quite knowledgeable, yet even she can't explain it—just consider this child a gift from the Gods, sent because they dislike your constant bickering."
"What are you talking about? That's not arguing; it's a fierce debate sparked by differing ideals." Alice said sternly.
"Exactly, just a debate." Merlin held Chris in his arms.
The two had reached some kind of agreement; if Chris were present, they would never admit to constantly arguing.
After all, Chris is still young and her thoughts are not mature; growing up in a discordant household could negatively affect her personality.
.....Rossetti let out a light snort; it was clear that Merlin and Alice, acting as mom and dad, were both trying to become more mature, shedding their former hot tempers.
"Alice, you came today... surely you have some serious business?" Da Vinci suddenly asked, feeling they weren't just here to introduce their baby.
"Yes!" Alice nodded, quickly pulling out the half-map Merlin had brought from the Chaos Sea, "What is this? Can you make sense of it?"
Da Vinci saw the map was very old, so he carefully picked it up, propping his monocle, and observed it intently.
Everyone else remained silent, waiting for Da Vinci; even the usually lively Chris sat obediently on Merlin's lap.
Da Vinci furrowed his brow; Merlin sensed a hint of unease—it was the first time he'd seen her expression like this, wondering if she still didn't know anything.
This half-map came from the treasure of the Chaos King Medusa, stored alongside other precious items; logically it couldn't be worthless junk.
Da Vinci let out a breath, his brows knitting together as he set down the half-map and said, "This map is far too ancient; I can't even determine when it was drawn, and moreover, the content on it makes me feel..."
"What does that mean? Have you seen it before?" Merlin asked curiously.
"I should have seen something similar." Da Vinci nodded, then countered, "Where did you get this?"
"From the unknown Mysterious Sea." Merlin replied.
"Huh?" Da Vinci stared in disbelief at the old half-map, "This... is it from the unknown Mysterious Sea? There, storms rage everywhere, cut off from the world—no one could possibly survive and emerge from there, Mr. Merlin..."
"Da Vinci, your information is outdated; the rumors of the Mysterious Sea being an inescapable death trap have been debunked—someone has entered and made it out alive." Rossetti reminded Da Vinci in a sentence.
"Who?" Da Vinci asked, puzzled.
"It's a captain named Dennis; after being trapped in the Mysterious Sea, he managed to return alive, and not long ago he was even featured in the newspaper." Rossetti said softly.
"Ah, I was the one who went with Captain Dennis." Merlin interjected.
"Eh?!" Rossetti widened his eyes, incredulous, "You were on the same ship as Captain Dennis?!"
"Yes, we had originally planned to enter the Mysterious Sea, but halfway through a storm grew too strong and swept us in; fortunately we managed to escape." Merlin said just enough, without revealing more.
"Oh, I see—that's incredibly lucky; throughout history, anyone swept into the Mysterious Sea has never survived. Rossetti didn't think much of it, assuming Merlin had merely clung to Captain Dennis's thigh and thus barely saved his own life."
Da Vinci re-examined the half-map and speculated, "The Mysterious Sea originated in the early days of human civilization, so this map might also be from that era..."
Alice looked at Da Vinci's deep gaze and asked curiously, "What have you figured out?"
"Wait for me, I need to look through some ancient texts." Da Vinci got up and left, heading to the library next to the lab.
Rossetti withdrew his gaze, speaking with a slight apology, "She takes a long time when she reads; you'd better be patient."
"No problem, we can wait a long time." Merlin leaned back in his chair, preparing to await Da Vinci's result.
But at that moment little Chris became restless, sliding off Daddy's lap and asking in a sweet voice, "Daddy, I want to help Ms. Glasses~"
"Huh? No, you can't... cough!"
Merlin hadn't finished speaking when Alice jabbed him in the side with her elbow.
Alice glared at Merlin with a resentful expression, then smiled at Chris and said, "Go ahead, just remember not to cause trouble for others and don't run too far, okay?"
"Got it~" Chris nodded repeatedly, toddling on her short legs to the library where Da Vinci was.
"What are you doing? This isn't home; can't you stop her from causing trouble? What help could a small child possibly offer?" Merlin complained dissatisfiedly.
"Chris means well and isn't doing anything bad; as her dad, can't you avoid discouraging her enthusiasm?" Alice said in an unfriendly tone.
Merlin: "If you keep indulging her like that, you're not fit to be a mother—spoiling a child will make her pampered and weak, and overindulgence will ruin her!"
Alice: "I can't? You're even worse! With your attitude, you'll only raise an idiot—I won't let you run wild!"
Rossetti calmly raised his eyebrows, thinking helplessly,
What the heck~
Once the child is out of sight, they immediately revert to their old selves...
The library—this is Rexum's largest archive, filled with piles of books.
The circular massive shelves are completely filled; the remaining books are scattered haphazardly on the floor.
Da Vinci stood on the ladder, searching for half a day, finally found a black-covered book; its pages were densely packed with strange script that ordinary people could hardly read.
This black book recounts some ancient matters, especially the end of the elven era, where the mysterious script shares much in common with Elvish.
Da Vinci stepped down from the ladder and saw Chris struggling to hold a few books, walking with a wobbly gait.
"Heave-ho, hey.... Chris arrived before Da Vinci, speaking in a sweet voice, 'Ms. Eyes, do you have the book you need here?'"
"No." Da Vinci, being a rational person, had no intention of helping, and replied sternly.
"..... Chris let out a mournful cry, silently set down a stack of books, exhausted and sitting on the floor, panting, 'huff... huff...'"
"I don't need your help; you should go find your parents." Da Vinci's tone was devoid of emotion, like a feelingless assassin.
"But there are so many books here; I want to help Ms. Glasses." Chris got up from the floor, showing a friendly smile.
"I'm Da Vinci, not Ms. Glasses." Da Vinci replied bluntly.
"Really? You're Da Vinci Sis~" little Chris thought she'd made a new friend and happily spun around in place.
Da Vinci looked at such a childish youngster, showing neither affection nor aversion, but instead recalled the doubt he'd just had outside.
Creating a high-intelligence lifeform is impossible; the only example is that the Goddess of Light created Cain and Abel...
Da Vinci thought it over, propped his monocle with his hand, and came up with a method to test his hypothesis.
Da Vinci's monocle, besides automatically analyzing material substances, also has a function to assess the strength of living beings, returning the result as a numerical value.
Last time, when analyzing Merlin, the monocle malfunctioned for no reason, so Da Vinci improved and upgraded it.
Da Vinci's single monocle suddenly lit up with a rotating magic circle, beginning to attempt an analysis of Chris-
She hypothesized that, if this child of unknown origin before her eyes was truly created by the Goddess of Light, even if only slightly connected...
then as a lifeform created by a god, its strength would certainly not be weak!

title: Chapter 29 — The Vast Territory Before the Human Era
content:
Chapter 29 — The Vast Territory Before the Human Era

Volume 25 · Chapter 29

达 Vinci used the analytical capabilities of her monocle, hoping to verify her own suspicions.

If Chris, despite her young age, had such high stats, then it was very likely that she was connected to the twins created by the Goddess of Light.

Da Vinci didn’t believe it—it was too bizarre that a mere stone could give birth to a highly intelligent lifeform.

In all the historical records, the only recorded event of life being created was the story of Maria giving birth to Cain and Abel.

No wonder Da Vinci was suspicious—she was linking the harmless little Chris before her with the deities of the Holy Church.

The swirling blue magic circle analyzed Chris thoroughly, and before long, it returned the results to Da Vinci.

Combat Power: 5

What did a Combat Power of 5 mean? It was almost on par with the combat power of a stray cat, even weaker than a stray dog—utterly lacking in deterrence.

Da Vinci frowned, baffled by the result, which was far from what she had expected.

Originally, Da Vinci had only considered two possibilities in her mind—

First, that Chris was truly connected to the Goddess of Light, and her combat power would be off the charts from birth.

Second, that Chris had no relation to the Goddess of Light, and her combat power would be about the same as a two- or three-year-old child.

Yet what appeared before her was an unexpected third scenario: Chris’s combat power was far too weak, far below that of a normal child.

Da Vinci was confused, finding this situation almost impossible. Even if Merlin was a useless ordinary person, Alice was definitely gifted beyond measure.

As Alice’s daughter, inheriting her bloodline, she shouldn’t have ended up so weak. Under normal circumstances, she should have been slightly stronger than an average child.

Da Vinci wore a perplexed expression, turning the possibilities over in her mind. The only explanation left was that the child simply lacked talent, inheriting most of it from Merlin.

Seeing Da Vinci lost in thought, little Chris couldn’t help but call out, “Sister Da Vinci?”

Da Vinci snapped back to reality and dismissed her doubts for the moment. “You don’t need to be here. You should go back to your parents.”

“Bu—but I’ve never seen so many books before! I want to stay a little longer.” Chris was clearly fascinated by the place and hadn’t had her fill, so she pouted pitifully and said, “Please, Sister? Just for a little while.”

Da Vinci hesitated, then sighed. “Fine. But don’t disturb me.”

“I know! I won’t disturb you!” Chris knocked her small fist against her own head. “Hiya~”

Da Vinci ignored her and walked to the desk, beginning to read the ancient black tome carefully.

Meanwhile, little Chris curiously examined her surroundings, crawling into the piles of books and trying to find something interesting.

Since Chris was so young, she couldn’t read at all—she pawed through the books like a bear flipping corn, picking one up, finding it boring, and tossing it aside.

But even though Chris couldn’t read, she could still understand the illustrations, and they easily piqued her interest.

Buried beneath the scattered books, she found a thick tome with a cover depicting a grand scene of demons and holy spirits clashing.

“Wa~” Chris picked up the book as if it were a treasure, her eyes sparkling with excitement.

The illustrations showed bizarrely shaped demons and holy spirits in stark contrast, which instantly captivated Chris.

Without caring about the dust, she lay on the floor and flipped through the pages, gasping in delight with each image she saw.

Da Vinci was deeply engrossed in the black tome when she happened to glance up and see Chris quietly lying on the floor, completely absorbed in her book.

Curious, Da Vinci quietly approached and glanced at the book Chris was reading—*The Holy War*.

It chronicled the Demon Era, when the great demons ruled the world and wreaked havoc, drawing divine punishment.

Countless righteous holy spirits descended from the heavens to wage a desperate war against the demons…

Da Vinci looked at Chris and asked softly, “Can you understand it?”

“No~” Chris answered honestly, pointing at the vivid illustrations and saying with sparkling eyes, “But the people in it… are so cool!”

Da Vinci felt a pang of awkwardness—*Of course she wouldn’t understand.* “This book tells a very exciting story. The start of the Holy War marked the dawn of the age of humanity.”

Chris stared at the dense text on the page, her head spinning. She couldn’t make heads or tails of it at all.

“This book is yours.” Da Vinci rarely smiled, and she didn’t dislike people with a strong thirst for knowledge. “When you go back, you can ask your mom and dad to read it to you.”

“Ee~ya~” Chris hugged the book to her chest, planning to have her mother tell her the story later.

Merlin had expected Da Vinci to come out of the library quickly, but the sky outside had already darkened.

*Is Miss Da Vinci really taking this long to look up information? What on earth is this half-map?*

Merlin stared at the half-map in his hands, his mind filled with confusion. He wondered if he’d solve this mystery today.

“Be patient, Mr. Merlin. When Miss Da Vinci gets into her books, it’s not uncommon for her to stay in the library for three days straight.” Rosetti kindly reminded him.

“Three days…” Merlin frowned, wondering when that would ever end.

“Does it really take that long?” Alice asked hesitantly.

“If you’re lucky, it won’t—” Rosetti smiled.

Just then, Da Vinci emerged from the library with Chris, and Merlin hurriedly stood up to ask, “Well? Any progress? Any clues?”

“Mr. Merlin, please let me look at the map again.” Da Vinci said seriously.

“Oh, sure.” Merlin handed the half-map to Da Vinci.

Little Chris toddled back to Alice’s side and held up *The Holy War* for her to see. “Mommy, look! Sister gave me this book!”

“Oh?” Alice picked up Chris and flipped through the book. “*The Holy War*?”

“The pictures are so pretty, but I can’t read the words.” Chris said grumpily.

“Is that so?” Alice thumbed through it briefly, thinking the stories were far too heavy for Chris’s age. She should be reading *Snow White* or *Little Red Riding Hood* instead…

Da Vinci’s brows were tightly furrowed as she studied the map for a long time before finally exhaling. “This is a map drawn before the Human Era.”

“Before the Human Era?” Merlin’s eyes widened slightly.

Da Vinci opened the ancient black tome and showed it to Merlin and Alice. “Our world once underwent a massive upheaval. Before the Human Era, all the continents were connected. When the Human Era began and the Holy War erupted, the continents were struck by immense divine power, shattering into many different regions and forming the many nations we see today. Look at the map in this book—it’s the world before the Human Era. Isn’t it almost identical to this half-map?”

Merlin let out a gasp of shock. The map in the black tome showed a single massive landmass, and the half-map he’d retrieved from the Sea of Chaos fit almost perfectly over it.

If the Holy War had caused such a massive shift in the world’s geography, what connection did the dead holy spirits in the Sea of Chaos have with this half-map?

title: Chapter 30 — Sword Saint on the Snow Mountain (Extra)
content:
Chapter 30 — Sword Saint on the Snow Mountain (Extra)

Volume 25 · Chapter 30

"Is this the map of the continent before it split apart?" Alice compared them carefully. Though there were some minor differences, the two maps were very similar. The half showing the Chaos Sea only contained half a continent.

That was right. In the distant Demon Epoch, the demon race ruled the world and was incredibly powerful. They only weakened after being sanctioned by the Heavenly Realm. That Holy War was extremely fierce — demons and holy spirits fought to a standstill. In the end, the Heavenly Realm unleashed some terrible power, annihilating a large number of demons with terrifying strength, and even the vast continental plates shattered... Da Vinci explained patiently.

"I can't believe something like that happened... This is Alice's first time hearing this history, and she couldn't help but偷偷 glance at Merlin beside her.

Merlin had heard a little about his own race's history, but this was the first time he'd heard that the continent used to be one unified landmass before the human era. "Miss Da Vinci, could it be that this half map is related to the Holy War between the demon race and the Heavenly Realm?"

"No, not in the slightest," Da Vinci answered lightly.

"Then... then what exactly is the information on this half map?" Merlin asked, completely baffled.

"This half map doesn't provide complete information, but I can try to make a guess." Da Vinci pointed with her finger at the faint, almost invisible lines on the half map. "Mr. Merlin, look carefully at the dashed lines on this map. They mark a sea area outside the continental shelf. This is clearly a very hidden waterway."

"Then where does this waterway lead to?" Alice showed some interest.

"Could it... lead to some kind of treasure!" Merlin's eyes immediately turned into gold coins — he hadn't forgotten his dream of turning his life around!

"Where it leads? I can't determine that, but I'm certain the destination of this hidden waterway is absolutely not as simple as just treasure." Da Vinci said firmly.

Merlin and Alice both shuddered. Hearing Da Vinci speak so seriously, it was clear this half map was absolutely not something ordinary.

Da Vinci pointed to the small text below the dashed waterway line. The blurry, distorted characters were still somewhat legible. "This is ancient human script. It says... the Burial Place of the Gods..."

"The Burial Place of the Gods? What does that refer to?" Merlin asked puzzled.

"In the old era, the ancient gods lived in Asgard, but they encountered demons whose prophet was bathed in flames and were brought to ruin. So the Burial Place of the Gods naturally refers to Asgard — what people still whisper about today as the ancient gods' ruins." Da Vinci said softly.

"The ancient gods' ruins? Wouldn't that be... the place guarded by the Kraken?" Alice remembered the old president Tyler recounting the Kraken's disturbance of the Norwegian kingdom thirty years ago.

"My goodness! This half map..." Rossetti stared at the tattered map in shock, eyes wide. She thought this item was far too precious — it was a shame it was only half.

"That's right, it's the same place. About ten-plus years ago, the Kraken sleeping within the ancient gods' ruins awoke and caused chaos in the Norwegian kingdom. At that time, many strong individuals appeared. On the surface they claimed to be there to protect Norway, but in reality the vast majority were fighting to find clues to the ancient gods' ruins. That mysterious ruin was simply too alluring." Da Vinci sighed, then pointed at the half map and said —

"So..."

"The mysterious waterway on this map is more than just treasure."

"It's far more likely marking the nest of an extremely dangerous... Kraken."

***

Far away on the snow-covered Alpine mountains, the environment was harsh, with constant blizzards year-round, making it unsuitable for human habitation.

However, caravans heading to the Holy Roman Empire often trekked across these great mountains on foot to save time and costs.

Even in such a harsh environment, several small wooden cabins sat here, adding a touch of warmth to the cold, snowy mountain.

Ding-a-ling~

The sound of bells echoed through the howling blizzard as a caravan led by a few yaks slowly advanced, gradually approaching these small wooden cabins.

A young merchant was so cold that snot was streaming from his nose. He gave a violent sneeze — he seemed to be visiting the snow mountain for the first time, extremely unaccustomed.

The old man beside him leading a yak, wrapped head to toe in a thick fur coat, couldn't help but bare his teeth in a grin. "Young man, first time coming to the big snow mountain, aren't you?"

"...Yeah. I didn't expect it to be so..." the young merchant stammered.

"Haha, there are frequent blizzards here. You're not dressed warmly enough. Never underestimate the bitter winds of the snow mountain — one careless moment and you'll freeze to death right here..." the yak-leading old man said with a smile.

"Th-thank you for the advice. Next time I'll definitely bring more clothes." The young merchant forced a smile, his feet sunk deep into the thick snow, his toes already numb.

"Hang in there a little longer. Up ahead there are several small wooden cabins. The owner is a very kind lady. As long as we give her some daily necessities, we can stay overnight there to shelter from the blizzard." The old man had plenty of experience.

"Huh?" The young merchant blinked in sudden surprise and said incredulously, "Someone actually lives in a place like this?"

"Why wouldn't they? I was born in a village at the foot of the snow mountain — I know it well." The old man paused, then continued. "Twenty years ago, a woman carrying a baby arrived here. She had a peculiar personality and refused to live among us villagers, so she came alone to the snow mountain, built a house, and settled down. That's why this place has become a temporary stopping point for traveling merchants. Although she avoids associating with us, she doesn't object when we stay overnight to shelter from blizzards. She's truly kind..."

"Someone could survive in such a harsh environment by themselves? That's truly..." The young merchant's astonished expression froze on his face.

"At first she wasn't alone. There was also a lovely baby girl who grew up here, named Alice. She was adorable as a child and always sneaked over to listen to our caravan folk tell stories. We brought her plenty of fun things, though her teacher always confiscated them. Such a pity." The old man sighed.

"Her... teacher? That lady must be quite strict, then?" the young merchant said with a dry laugh.

"She's indeed very strict. Every time I pass by, I can hear that child Alice complaining about her teacher. But two years ago she suddenly disappeared — she probably went down the mountain. It's such a shame. That child was so kind and pure. I even miss her a bit." The old man's face showed a hint of nostalgic smile.

"Teaching a student on the big snow mountain — what's this lady's background?" the young merchant asked curiously.

"We don't know. She simply appeared here one day twenty years ago. But this lady's swordsmanship is superb, and her strength is extraordinary — she's the strongest swordsman I've ever seen in my life. The blizzard she wields is a hundred times more terrifying than what we're enduring now! When her sword moves, I can barely follow it with my eyes! Truly amazing. Our village at the foot of the snow mountain has suffered several demonic beast attacks, and every time it was this lady who helped resolve the situation. All the villagers call her the Sword Saint of the Snow Mountain and deeply respect her. Every time I come here, I bring her lots of needed supplies..." the old man said with a smile.

"She sounds like someone worth respecting. I really wish I could meet her," the young merchant sighed.

"You might be able to see her at the cabin, but that lady has an odd personality." The old man, speaking from experience, kindly warned, "Remember, never ask things like whether she's lonely here or why she isn't married yet at her age. Most importantly, never mention words like leftover woman or old maid who can't find a match, or you'll be in for a rough time..."

However, the young merchant's wish was destined to remain unfulfilled, for the woman in the cabin had already packed her luggage.

Clothilde wore a mysterious Eastern-style long robe with a thick sable fur cloak draped over her shoulders, and beside her rested an ancient-looking weapon resembling a Longquan sword.

She excitedly held Alice's reply letter, while the white vulture beside her remained silent.

"That little Alice, such a contrary girl. Don't I know her well? She says she doesn't want me coming, but in truth she's probably missing me to tears by now!"

Clothilde picked up her sharp sword, slung her luggage over her shoulder, pushed open the door, and looked out at the raging blizzard with anticipation. The white vulture immediately flew onto her shoulder.

"My little darling, wait patiently for kisses, hugs, and being lifted high~!

■To Be Continued

title: Chapter 1 — The Demon's Perspective
content:
Chapter 1 — The Demon's Perspective

Volume 26 · Chapter 1

Several days passed, and Merlin and Alice's attention was all focused on Chris, with nothing special happening.

It was now nighttime. In the bedroom, Chris sat obediently on her mother's lap, while Alice was patiently telling stories to the little one.

Da Vinci had given that copy of "The Holy War" to Chris, and since returning, the girl had been pestering mother constantly, hoping to be told the contents inside.

Alice had been confused at first as to why Chris was so interested in holy spirits and demons. However, after looking at the strange illustrations inside, she understood.

Chris simply thought the drawings in the book were very beautiful, which was why she was interested in the stories depicted in them.

The oil lamp nearby emitted a dim yellow glow, illuminating the faces of the mother and daughter.

Chris sat on Alice's lap, listening raptly. At such a young age, she was actually quite engrossed in this kind of historical book?

Alice sat in the chair, holding the book, occasionally looking down at Chris, and then continuing to softly narrate the contents of "The Holy War"—

"The demons who committed countless evils finally met with their punishment. The gates of heaven were opened by Divine Power, and great miracles began to manifest. The Seven Virtues under the God of Light led countless holy spirits to set out in full force. The horn of the counterattack caused the humans oppressed by alien races to awaken one, beginning a century-long resistance to reclaim the fertile lands and drive out the alien races, leaving them to perish by their own devices..."

Reading to here, Alice paused for a moment, thinking to herself this book was definitely written by humans. It contained many disparagements of non-human races, while humans were portrayed as victims who rose in resistance after being oppressed.

Now Alice could more or less understand why the alien races in the United Kingdom had no goodwill toward humans when they were there; it turned out they were once the masters of this land.

However, Alice could not easily judge who was right or wrong. After all, it happened hundreds of thousands of years ago; who knew what exactly happened back then?

"Under the assistance of the great God of Light, humans who had been oppressed for countless eras welcomed their rise, becoming the leaders of a new epoch. Demons and holy spirits fought fierce battles for a long time, and eventually evil retreated. Six of the seven invincible Great Demon Lords perished, while the remaining demons guarded the Demon Lord Palace..."

"Mama?" Chris raised her head, revealing eyes full of curiosity.

"What is it?" Alice looked down at her daughter.

"Why are they always fighting? Can't they live together in peace?" Alice asked a very naive question.

"This..." Facing her daughter's question, Alice did not know how to answer for a moment. Killing was the instinct of all creatures, and the evolution of the world was always accompanied by war. "Because... because everyone wants to live better..."

"Live better?" The stray hair on Chris's head curled into a question mark shape.

"That's right. The world's resources are limited. Everyone wants their own race to continue reproducing, so they must fight for it. This leads to the appearance of exploitors and the oppressed. Any prosperity is built on draining the value of other races." Alice tried to make the young Chris understand the logic behind it, knowing that once she grew up, she would surely see more cruel realities.

"If resources are limited... can't everyone just share them equally? Why fight without end? If we share equally, everyone gets a part." Chris did not understand at all.

"It would be fine if we could truly share equally, but greed would never allow it." Alice smiled and gave an example, "Suppose you are very hungry now and there is only one small piece of cream cake in front of you, but other children are also very hungry. Are you willing to give it to others even if you remain hungry?"

"I am willing!" Chris said in her milky voice.

"Uh..." Alice's expression was awkward. She stroked Chris's hair, thinking this child was as simple and kind as herself, and she would only change after experiencing more things. "Even if you were willing, Mommy and Daddy wouldn't allow you to do that; instead, we would help you win that small piece of cake."

"Why?" Chris asked curiously.

"Because Mommy and Daddy love you~" Alice pinched Chris's little cheek.

"Ya~?" Chris patted her cheeks, smiling like a blooming flower.

"It's about time. Go to sleep nicely, okay?" Alice felt it was enough and intended to put the book down to urge Chris to go to bed early.

"No! No sleep-sleep!" Chris pouted her small lips, resisting.

"What? Haven't you heard enough?" Alice knitted her brows.

"I still have some things I don't understand. This book says demons are evil bad guys, but it doesn't say exactly what bad things they did? Why would things coming from the sky insisted on suppressing them?" Chris was a bit confused, but was also very curious.

"Ah..." Alice hesitated. She wasn't a historian nor had she read many books, so she couldn't answer Chris. She could only say mystically—

"Go ask your father. He knows a lot about demons."

◇

Outside the bedroom, Merlin was lying on the sofa, looking at the half-map he brought from the Chaotic Seas, lost in his own thoughts.

This thing has clues to the ruins of the ancient gods? It sounds like an unprecedented great treasure...

Merlin thought of artifacts as such extremely rare and powerful items; in the secret realm of the elf race, the power of Core's ring was indeed terrifying.

It was impossible to say Merlin wasn't moved, but considering that that artifact concerned the lives of too many alien races, he dispelled the evil thought.

However, now that he knew this half-map was connected to the ruins of the gods, Merlin's heart began to grow grass, having the idea of getting an artifact to play with.

However, realizing this idea was extremely difficult. The map was only half; where was the other half?

Only by joining the two maps would the correct path and the exact location of the ruins be found.

title: Chapter 2 — Worried
content:
Chapter 2 — Worried

Volume 26 · Chapter 2

Merlin feigned calm, forcing a smile as he said, “Why… why do you think demons are all evil villains?”
“Because… because the book says so…” Chris pointed to the Holy War that Merlin had thrown on the ground, which described demons as utterly evil, so they deserved punishment.
“Don’t just believe what’s written in books, is everything in books necessarily true? Many things can’t be discovered as truth unless you see them with your own eyes.” Merlin earnestly educated Chris.
“But if demons aren’t evil villains, why are they punished? Chased and beaten by so many people?” Chris sucked on her finger as she asked.
“Because… because the Goddess of Light sides with humanity; her position determines her thinking. Besides, it’s not only demons who are punished—all non‑human races are oppressed, though demons bear the brunt of it.” Merlin explained.
“Are all those demon gentlemen good people?” Chris asked innocently.
“This…”
Merlin suddenly felt his head swell a size; this “fake” demon who had transmigrated couldn’t possibly serve as a reference for Chris.
Among the demon race he was an oddball, utterly out of place with true demons; otherwise he wouldn’t have been mocked and ostracized by the remaining demon lords.
Merlin thought it wouldn’t do to paint demons too favorably; at the very least he had to let this little one understand that demons are dangerous, after all not every demon is like him.
“Chris, strictly speaking, demons really aren’t nice folks; their notions of class and race are extremely rigid, they’re brutal and bloodthirsty, unwilling to let humans stand equal with them, yet they are also intelligent beings capable of communicating with humans.”
“Well… are they good or bad then?” Chris tugged at her hair.
“It’s a mix of good and bad. Demons follow the truth, so there are few hypocrites among them, but they are also equally ferocious, having long grown accustomed to slaughter.” Merlin said seriously.
“Huh?” Chris simply didn’t get it; to a child there is only good and evil, no concept of half‑good, half‑evil.
“In short, you little temptress, if you ever run into a demon, try to stay away; quite a few demons still like tender, delicate prey.” Merlin paused, then flicked Chris’s little nose with his finger.
“But… but Chris’s legs are short, I can’t outrun them…” Chris said in a babyish voice, realizing her short legs weren’t much use.
“Ha ha…” Merlin chuckled, advising, “If you can’t get away, just loudly declare that you’re a child of the Lucifer family—it might scare the demons off.”
“The Lucifer family?” Chris’s ahoge swayed.
“Don’t ask so many questions; just remember that when you’re in danger from a demon, say that name—it could come in handy at a critical moment.” Merlin ruffled Chris’s hair.
“Okay~” Chris replied obediently, then curiously asked, “Dad knows a lot about demons, has he ever seen a real demon?”
“Of course~” Merlin looked at Chris, half‑joking, half‑serious, “Actually, Dad himself is a demon—aren’t you scared?”
“Dad’s lying to me again; earlier he even said he was a great demon who’d eat me, hehe!” Chris scrambled to the floor, picked up the book, and pointed at the frightening demon illustration, saying, “Real demons are scary—Dad doesn’t look like them at all, so he’s definitely not a demon~”
“Ha…” Merlin gave a dry laugh, black lines streaking down his forehead as he thought, I am a demon, after all—a renowned Great Demon Lord. I wonder how this little one will view me as her dad once she learns the truth?
Hiding in the bedroom, Alice silently watched the father‑daughter pair outside; she was fairly pleased with Merlin and hadn’t taught Chris anything strange—
Merlin, this guy…
Is he also afraid that his demon identity will frighten Chris?
◇
Ding dong! Ding dong! Ding ding ding dong!
“Who’s there…”
Alice was roused by the intermittent doorbell, she blinked awake and shuffled to the door.
In a daze, Alice felt the person outside seemed somewhat familiar, so she rubbed her eyes.
“Alice, it’s been ages—have you missed me, your teacher?”
“Uh…” Alice widened her eyes, staring at her teacher Claudia outside, instantly feeling a chill from head to toe.
“You left without my permission, went down the mountain, and haven’t come back in two years—do you think your wings have hardened?” Claudia flashed an evil grin, looming over Alice like a giant, “Come on, let’s have a good chat as master and disciple; I’ll make you relive that old fear! Hahaha…”
“No…” Alice shrank back, letting out a hysterical scream—
“Don’t!!!”
Alice jolted awake from her nightmare; it was already morning, and gentle sunlight streamed through the curtains.
Her nightgown was soaked with the cold sweat from the fright, she sat up on the bed, panting, her heart still pounding.
Oh… oh, it was just a dream—I nearly had a heart attack, thinking the teacher really showed up at the door…
Alice gently pressed her hand to her chest to calm herself, then glanced at the father‑daughter duo nearby.
“Whoosh~ whoosh~” Chris used Merlin as her mattress, lying on his belly and sleeping through the whole night.
Alice managed a faint smile; it seemed Chris preferred sticking to Merlin—could it be anything other than opposite‑sex attraction?
She sighed quietly, reflecting that her life was now peaceful and stable, and she didn’t want to be disturbed by that teacher.
Although Alice had already written to the teacher on Great Snow Mountain asking her not to come, who knows what the teacher is really thinking?
A wave of unease rose in Alice’s chest; whenever she imagined her life might be disrupted, she grew anxious and worried.
Merlin woke up, saw Alice sitting on the bed, her hands clasped around her knees, her nightgown damp with cold sweat.
“You… what’s wrong? You’re not still having nightmares at your age, are you?”
“I…” Alice furrowed her brows, irritated, “Don’t bother me, humph!”
“Huh???” Merlin slowly sat up, gently holding Chris so she could keep sleeping, “What happened? Your reaction is strange…”
“Nothing… nothing…” Alice trailed off, not wanting to let Merlin know about the teacher’s message.
Merlin pondered, then ventured, “I can tell you’re preoccupied; if you have any troubles, tell me—I might be able to help. Opportunities like this don’t come around often~”
“Well…”
Alice set her jaw and thought hard; she still wasn’t at ease about the teacher on Great Snow Mountain.
The teacher has always been strict with her; if she really showed up, she might take Alice back to the Great Snow Mountain.
Now that they have Chris, Alice can’t leave—otherwise the little girl would be motherless.
Moreover, Merlin makes Alice uneasy; if she left, this guy would probably go wild in no time.
Alice turned her head to look at Merlin, speaking with earnest sincerity—
“How about…”
“We move house with Chris?”
The Pineapple Circle held a lottery; a family‑of‑three, two‑version character standee set.

title: Chapter 3 — Disobedient Leg (Extra)
content:
Chapter 3 — Disobedient Leg (Extra)

Volume 26 · Chapter 3

"Ah? Moving? Why?" Merlin furrowed his brows, not knowing what weird idea had popped into Alice's head.
"Because..." Alice pressed her lips, embarrassed, saying, "Living in Rexham is a bit boring, I want to move somewhere else."
"? ? ?" Merlin's forehead was full of question marks, he said lowly, "Where is it boring? Isn't it pretty good?"
"Why so many questions? I just want to move, is that not allowed?" Alice retorted angrily.
"You always need a reason, right?" Merlin paused, teasingly said, "We are adventurers of Rexham; moving means changing jobs and renting a new house. You can't guarantee a landlady as easygoing as this one, and besides, the friends we've made here would be useless. Have you thought about all that?"
Alice fell silent, she only wanted to avoid the teacher, hadn't considered it would cause so many problems.

Merlin tilted his head, asking, "Why did you suddenly want to move?"
"A whim." Alice replied hesitantly.
Merlin suspected Alice was hiding something unwilling to say; the sudden urge to move looked like someone who owed a - - butt debt, afraid creditors would come knocking, a poor soul.

Alice turned to look at Merlin, changing the subject, "Today you take Chris to buy a few nice clothes?"
"Huh? Isn't there already some?" Merlin asked in surprise.
"Just one or two pieces of clothing isn't enough; Chris is a girl, she needs to live a bit more refined. Besides, last time she came back, her clothes were already a bit ragged; she really needs new clothes now." Alice said seriously.
"Alright then, I'll take her to look, I wonder what this little one likes?" Merlin gazed at the sleeping Chris, thinking—
Kids are great, carefree, and they get new clothes every day.

"We're setting off." Merlin stood at the door, holding Chris's small hand.
"Mom, we'll be back soon, don't think about us~" Chris waved her chubby little hand at Alice.
"What are you saying? It's just buying a few new clothes, not like we'll be gone long." Alice gave a helpless laugh.
"But I'm afraid Mom will feel uncomfortable alone at home." Chris said in a babyish voice.
Alice squatted down, patted Chris's head, and said kindly, "It's fine, you can go with Dad, remember to listen to Dad, don't run around everywhere, got it?"
"Don't worry, Mom, I'm obedient." Chris showed a smile, her baby teeth all showing.
"Young age, slick tongue, just like your dad." Alice sighed, stood up, and still reminded Merlin, "You must protect her well."
"Don't be so naggy, okay? With me here, how could she be in danger?" Merlin said confidently.
"Ha, I don't know who last time lost Chris, causing her feet to be covered in—" Alice sneered at Merlin.
"Cough cough!" Merlin coughed twice to hide his embarrassment, declaring firmly, "You shouldn't keep bringing up past things; this time I'll definitely watch Chris closely, won't let that happen again." "Roar"
"Hmph! I'll trust you once, go, come back soon." Alice relaxed a bit, seeing off the father and daughter.

But Merlin stood at the door holding Chris's hand, not moving, as if he had no intention to leave.
"What are you doing? Go buy clothes?" Alice frowned, puzzled.
"Tsk! Did you forget something?" Merlin, penniless, rubbed his fingers against Alice, hinting wildly.
"Huh?" Alice became especially wary whenever money was mentioned, eyeing Merlin suspiciously, "Did you run out of money?"
"I have no money! You took it all! And you still have the nerve to ask?!" Merlin's stomach filled with bitter thoughts, wondering how long Alice had been oblivious to how poor he is.
"It's impossible! You must have hidden private stash; take it out to buy clothes for the baby, isn't that better? Don't be so stingy!" Alice said righteously.
"Private stash? Where would I have that? Every time my pay goes to you; where would I get private money?" Merlin fumed, resentful of Alice's strict control over finances.
"Sigh, you're already this old and can't even afford clothes for your daughter—how embarrassing! Truly a useless..." Alice muttered sarcastically, then pulled out her own purse.
"I just noticed your face is thick enough; why not let me keep all future earnings from now on?" Merlin said with a fake smile, gritting his teeth in resentment.
"Hehe, you're doing"

FSF Light Novel
Alice smiled meaningfully, but she couldn't entrust the money to Merlin, the spendthrift.
The man who sold the inherited mithril armor for huge wealth and squandered it all in less than half a year—what credibility does he have?
Alice looked at her money pouch, hesitantly took out a gold coin and gave it to Merlin, her stinginess flaring up again, somewhat reluctant.
Merlin stared at the gleaming gold coin in his hand, a bit dazed; he hadn't touched such a large sum in a long time.

Thus Merlin happily pocketed the gold coin, took Chris's small hand, and prepared to go buy her clothes.
"We're off then."
"Wait!" Alice quickly grabbed Merlin's arm, stopping him, her face full of "vigilance."
"What are you doing?" Merlin turned his head in surprise.
Alice leaned close to Merlin, lowered her voice, whispering—
"You need to have a sense of proportion in your mind; I gave you money to buy pretty clothes for the baby, not for you to turn around and throw it into the horse betting arena. If you dare touch the baby's clothing money, you understand what I mean?"
Sweat beads the size of peas rolled down Merlin's forehead; it was the first time he felt such pressure from Alice.
He gulped nervously, nodded solemnly, and said seriously,
"Rest assured, I'm not that kind of person; I'm a responsible father, I will absolutely not do such a thing, I guarantee it with my own person."

Chris rarely got to go out with Merlin—this time she skillfully rode on his neck, looking around.
Whenever this little one saw something novel, she couldn't help but exclaim in surprise.
"Wow~ Dad, look, so many people!"
"Chris, do you perhaps like lively scenes?" Merlin asked with a smile.
"I like it! So many people, full of life!" Chris's cowlick bounced nonstop.
"Really? If you like it, Dad will often bring you out to stroll." Merlin said with a wry smile.
"Hey~" Chris patted Merlin's forehead with her tiny hand.
But as they walked, Merlin suddenly stopped, this sudden brake almost threw Chris off.
Before Merlin's eyes was a bustling scene: people constantly holding colorful little tickets, coming out of the horse betting ticket booth, eyebrows flying, discussing which horse to bet on this time.
Merlin's gaze at the horse betting shop was sharp, even exaggerated to the point of being bloodshot; his two legs seemed cursed, trembling uncontrollably—
Don't tempt me!
My legs, behave! Don't move, don't— A up=

title: Chapter 4 — Claudia
content:
Chapter 4 — Claudia

Volume 26 · Chapter 4

Merlin, carrying a huge sum of gold coins, passed by the horse‑ticket stall and suddenly found himself unable to control his steps.
The evil horse‑ticket stall seemed to possess some kind of magic that Merlin could not resist, constantly drawing him in.
Merlin had always thought his self‑control was strong, but now he realized how weak it was; as long as he had enough money in his pocket, he couldn’t help throwing it onto the racetrack.
Calm down a bit! I’m supposed to buy Chris new clothes, not throw my money at the racetrack dreaming of a rags‑to‑riches comeback!
If I can’t even resist buying a horse‑ticket with this one gold coin, Alice will surely look down on me when I get home!
Merlin was thinking this, sweat dripping from his forehead, when he suddenly took a heavy step forward toward the horse‑ticket stall.
“Huh? Dad?” Chris looked down at Merlin, noticing his father’s strange reaction—his whole body trembling, panting as he stared at the place selling horse‑tickets ahead.
“..... Merlin’s eyes were bloodshot, he lowered his gaze to his disobedient legs and thought, I’m a dad now! I won’t indulge in any more daydreams of striking it rich! Don’t tempt me! This money is for buying my dear daughter pretty clothes, not for horse‑tickets!
“Dad, what’s wrong? Are you feeling unwell?” Chris tilted her head in confusion, showing a worried expression.
“No…. Merlin stammered, but his other leg moved forward on its own, “…Stop, you bastard! I won’t throw the money meant for my daughter’s clothes into the racetrack!
“Huh?” Chris looked at Merlin curiously, thought it over, then somewhat understood and said with a hint of disappointment, “Dad is using Mom’s money to do what he likes, Chris doesn’t need new clothes…
“What? ? ?” Merlin was stunned, he set Chris down from his shoulders, squatted and asked in surprise, “What did you say?
Chris lowered her head, feeling wronged, she lowered her head again, two fingers tangled, poking back and forth, “Dad, don’t make yourself suffer like this; I’m fine as long as I have clothes to wear, just follow your own feelings…”
“Why? Don’t you like pretty new clothes?” Merlin asked, bewildered.
Dad is more important; if throwing money into the racetrack can make Dad happy, Chris can do without new clothes, as long as Dad can open yi ting yuan ke de si tian zhen de yan lun, hui bei shen ti = zhen, ying se “tu” de lan xia jie gai xia lai. Seeing the wronged Chris, I’d rather not have new clothes nor want myself unhappy..... Merlin this -toward feelings indifferent guy, heart actually will produce a faint stabbing feeling one-.--- after all also a dad ah = because a momentary interest, let Chris suffer委屈, really rotten through. Although throwing money into the racetrack will make me feel great, but compared to my innocent cute daughter, it’s trivial. Merlin took a deep breath -0, showed a kind smile, stroked Chris’s little head and said.
“You got it backwards; compared to my interests, of course my dear daughter’s feelings are more important.”
“Mmm~~~” Chris enjoyed her father’s warmth, the cowlick on her head becoming lively again.
“Throwing money into the racetrack is a bad habit; when you grow up, don’t be like Dad, be like your mom and become someone who can manage the household.”
Merlin instructed.
“I know~” Chris replied in a cute, childish voice.
“Good.” Merlin picked up Chris and walked toward the bustling clothing store, “Come on, my little princess, let’s see what cute skirt suits you.”
“Ee ya~ 8” at home. Alice paced back and forth, her expression very uneasy. Her heart raced; she always felt something bad was about to happen—good grief! Why does my eyelid keep twitching? Merlin’s side......should be fine, right? Wait! This bastard is completely untrustworthy!
A gambler who could lose tens of millions of gold coins, would he let a single gold coin for his daughter’s clothes slide? Isn’t it the case that when he passed the horse‑ticket stall he couldn’t move his legs and shamelessly threw his money into the racetrack? ! Alice thought more and more it was possible, she mused that if Merlin hadn’t bought new clothes for his daughter, they’d need to have a serious talk. Ding‑dong, ding‑dong, ding‑ding‑dong—
“Huh? You’re back so fast? Surely you didn’t buy Chris clothes and instead threw the money into the racetrack! Hearing the doorbell, Alice flared up, strode over angrily, ready to scold him properly once the door opened. Alice had her words ready—she would definitely take the moral high ground and blame Merlin, “How can you even call yourself a father?!?” With a creak, the door opened, but it wasn’t Merlin returning with Chris; instead...... a figure in classical robes, a fur stole draped over her shoulders, a snowy‑white vulture perched on her shoulder, her outfit utterly out of place, as if she’d come from some frigid realm—this person was none other than Alice’s teacher Claudia, who held her own sword and regarded Alice with interest.
“Indeed, this is the place; I haven’t mistaken it. Long time no see, Alice—you look well‑fed outside, you’ve gotten a bit chubby, huh? Seeing Claudia, Alice let out a piercing scream, slammed the door shut with a bang, and even locked it… Impossible! How could the teacher get here so fast? ! Didn

title: Chapter 5 — Katowice's Adventurer (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 5 — Katowice's Adventurer (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 26 · Chapter 5

Claudia opened her arms, the mother's radiance shining forth, "Come on, Alice, don't suppress yourself, you really want to hug me, don't you? No need to be polite."

"Don't treat me like a child!" Alice said angrily.

"Really, you child, why won't you change your stubbornness? Being a bit straightforward now and then won't kill you." Claudia said disappointedly.

"Why did you come? Didn't I reply to your letter?" Alice said helplessly, resentment building in her heart.

"Ha, the letter said not to let you come, but you actually want me to see you, right? Don't put on airs in front of your teacher; you've been under my watch since you were little." Claudia smiled.

"I'm serious! Teacher!" Alice said with a stern face, slowly, "I'm doing fine living outside, I don't need you to worry."

"Oh?" Claudia's expression suddenly turned grim, showing a hint of teacherly authority, "Dead girl, do you really think your wings have hardened? The outside is far more dangerous than the snowy mountain; I came out of goodwill to check on you, and you don't appreciate it?"

"My life is peaceful and warm; Teacher, by coming here you're completely disrupting my life!" Alice retorted.

Claudia's face darkened, she said sternly, "In my eyes you'll always be a little girl who never grows up; don't think that just because you've lived outside for two years you can stand on your own."

"Sorry, Teacher, I really can stand on my own—go back, staying in the snowy mountain isn't bad? If I'm not there, no one will fight you for chicken legs." Alice said with equal seriousness.

"You're still not mature enough; come back with me to the snowy mountain to continue training—that's what you should do." Claudia said with a dark face.

"I won't go back with you; I'm doing fine living outside, there's no need to return and suffer your torment again." Alice said with an unpleasant expression.

"You call that torment? It's clearly wholeheartedly nurturing you, so that one day you can become strong." Claudia said earnestly.

"You always eat the good stuff first? What happened to the rabbit I raised as a child that suddenly disappeared? When wolf packs chased me, you never saved me, just laughed happily nearby—how do you explain these things?" Alice demanded angrily.

"These things..." Claudia's eyes darted, she said embarrassedly, "They're all to temper your character; you know yourself, you were weak as a child."

"I've heard this excuse countless times; please go, Teacher. If I get the chance, I'll definitely return to the snowy mountain to see you, but I hope you won't disturb my life." Alice said coldly, slowly closing the door.

"Wait!" Claudia grabbed the door handle, preventing Alice from closing it, "Alice, I'm your teacher, after all this trouble to come here, aren't you going to let me come in and sit? Having a cup of tea would be nice."

Alice: "I don't see the need...."

Claudia: "I think it's very necessary."

The two stood deadlocked outside the door, both gripping it tightly, secretly testing their strength.

The frail door, under their tugging, could shatter at any moment, repeatedly making cracking sounds.

"Teacher, please let go." Alice said with an unpleasant look.

"You're becoming more and more disobedient; let me in, don't force me to use martial force." Claudia threatened silently.

"Don't joke, I'm no longer someone you can push around; if I remember correctly, your strength is only Saint-tier, right?" Alice retorted, refusing to back down.

"Only? What a big mouth—clearly you're a useless student, you wouldn't think you could ride on your teacher's head, would you?" Claudia let out a hint of mockery.

"Exactly, that's what I think...." Alice's eyes sharpened, she suddenly released her sect's dragon威, a fierce pressure that made the whole house tremble; though not as terrifying as the Blazing Holy Dragon, it was already powerful enough!

"...." Claudia was slightly stunned, then let out a dry laugh, "So that's it—I saw your news in the newspaper, thought it was exaggerated, didn't expect you to have grown to this extent, not bad, the power of the dragon clan..."

"Teacher, knowing that, please leave; I don't want to bully you." Alice said seriously.

"Ah?" Claudia felt insulted, her eyes gradually turning cold, "You really dare say that—today I need to make you understand what respect for teachers means."

Claudia showed no flashy tricks, nor any trace of pressure.

She simply pointed her fingers together like a sword, at a speed the eye couldn't catch, and poked Alice in the abdomen.

Instantly, Alice's fierce dragon威 vanished, her body went numb and she couldn't exert any strength.

"Cough!"

Alice widened her eyes, feeling utterly incredulous, never expecting to be instantly subdued by her teacher.

Logically, Alice's strength should be enough, yet she lost combat ability from a light touch by Claudia.

Knowing Claudia didn't use any magic or battle aura, it's clear this temperamental old woman's strength isn't as simple as Saint-tier.

Alice collapsed to the ground, coughing nonstop, her body weak, as if she'd become an ordinary useless person.

"I haven't been by your side for just two years, and your cultivation has already become this muddled? A stupid student remains stupid, nothing changed." Claudia looked at the fallen Alice and sighed softly.

"And you still want to stand on your own?" (SF Light Novel)

"It's practically a joke...."

"Please take your time, come again next time!" The clothing store boss waved goodbye to Merlin and Chris, estimating he'd made quite a profit.

The father and daughter had finished buying clothes and were preparing to head home.

Chris put on her new dress, a light blue princess dress, her shiny little leather boots tapping crisp sounds on the ground.

"Don't run too fast, slow down." Merlin reminded from behind.

Chris, delighted with her new clothes, hopped and skipped ahead, tugging at her skirt and asked, "Dad, does it look good?"

"Looks good, my daughter looks good in anything." Merlin replied offhand.

"Dad, you're being so perfunctory, huh!" Chris put her hands on her hips, puffed out her cheeks, expressing her dissatisfaction, just like Alice.

"Ha, so cute, a hundred times cuter than your mom." Merlin helplessly praised Chris again.

"No no, having half your mom's cuteness is enough, hehe~ 8" Chris made an OK sign and placed it in front of her eyes.

"Learning humility now... Merlin shook his head, thinking Chris learns quickly, should I let her try some martial arts and magic? At that moment, the surrounding crowd suddenly became restless, pointing and chatting in one direction, as if a big shot had arrived.

Merlin noticed the situation, picked up Chris from the ground, and together with others began to watch—

From the direction everyone was looking at, two men slowly walked over, wearing red checkered clothing, seemingly from the same place.

One man was much older, with a blue beard on his face, his eyes like a lion's, calm yet imposing, exuding a kingly aura.

The other looked very young, brown hair covering one eye, glancing around casually, revealing a hint of disdain.

Both shared a common trait: they were silver‑mine adventurers from the Austro‑Hungarian Empire.

Region: Katovice City

Name: Bozu Wanaqiaobei

Occupation: Gem Mage

Position: President of the Katovice Adventurers Guild

Region: Katovice City

Name: Sicily Noah

Occupation: Speed Sword

Seeing these two men, the crowd of Leikushem exploded, buzzing with discussion.

"...Are they the adventurers from Katovice?!"

"How? Are they that strong? How do they compare to our town's Karl?"

"Karl is just a younger brother; the Katovice Adventurers Guild ranks world‑number one!PS

Because I need to proofread for typos, the update will be a bit slower; each chapter takes over ten minutes, thanks for understanding.

title: Chapter 6 — Already Married
content:
Chapter 6 — Already Married

Volume 26 · Chapter 6

Listening to the murmurs around her, Merlin looked at the two adventurers from Katowice with a curious gaze.

Apart from the fact that their adventurer badges were very eye-catching, their behavior was very low-key, deliberately suppressing their presence.

"World's second-ranked adventurer guild?" Merlin frowned, thinking that it must be even stronger than London's. It's probably a guild full of hidden talents, but Katowice's guildmaster is only a secret silver, while London's Gregory is a widely admired imperial gold.

"Dad, who are those two people? Why are everyone looking at them?" Chris asked quietly.

"Ah, they're adventurers from other places, they're also my and your mom's..." Merlin answered softly.

The sudden appearance of off-site adventurers attracted the attention of the Rexum citizens, and many people were guessing in their minds what the strong adventurers from Katowice were doing in this remote small town.

"World's second-ranked guild? That's truly remarkable!"

"Of course, Katowice's guild wasn't very famous before, but it suddenly rose to prominence in the previous Adventurer Competition, defeating many strong teams and winning second place!"

"Are you familiar with Boz? He was the main force of Katowice's team in the previous competition, stepping on many veteran strong players and becoming famous. How long has it been since then? He has already become the guildmaster of Katowice."

"If Boz, such a powerful adventurer, retires to the background as guildmaster, it's a pity. The guildmaster is not eligible to participate in the competition, and I wonder if Katowice's guild can still achieve good results in the competition without him?"

"It should be able to. I heard that Katowice's guild is very good at cultivating new members, and there have been many talented newcomers recently. The one next to him, Noa, is said to be Boz's successor, and his swordsmanship has reached its peak."

Merlin listened to the frequent discussions around him and felt some curiosity about these two people. The guildmaster of a top-ranked guild, along with young members of the guild, coming to Rexum, what could they be doing?

As Boz and Noa walked away, the crowd of onlookers gradually dispersed. Merlin hugged Chris and walked home.

"Let's go home, it's not interesting..."

At home, Klodia sat quietly on the sofa, sipping Alice's brewed red tea, looking very comfortable.

The white bald eagle on her shoulder looked at her owner now and then, and then looked at Alice, who looked very miserable.

Alice, who had initially been stubborn, eventually chose to compromise and let Klodia come in as a guest.

On the surface, Alice was respecting her teacher, but in reality, it was all because she couldn't win and had no good way out.

Alice bit her lips tightly, looking at her teacher with full of resentment, like a child who had done something wrong, standing quietly on the side.

Ugh! Klodia is a Saint-tier, isn't she? I've already surpassed Saint-tier, so why can't I beat her?

It's so unlucky. I just had a few peaceful days, but I'm still being disturbed by Klodia...

Alice grumbled to herself in her heart, praying that Klodia would return to the Great Snow Mountain as soon as possible and give her peaceful life back.

"Hmm~ Klodia shook her head and sighed, putting down her teacup, and looked at Alice's living space. "Well, it seems like you've been living quite well outside, huh? I thought that with your straightforward and naive personality, you would be easily deceived by the bad guys and end up on the streets after coming down from the mountain."

".... Alice's forehead veins jumped twice, and she said unhappily, "Don't treat me like an idiot, okay? I'm not as bad as you think. I'm not a child anymore, I can take care of myself."

"Yes, you're not the little follower I was before, it seems my worries were unnecessary. You can take care of yourself completely." Klodia said with a sigh of relief, but her words were very restrained, and her heart was very pleased.

"That... that's of course, I'm not the puppet in your mouth, I'm not something that can be manipulated at will...." Alice blushed, turned her head away, and said angrily.

"But you've been out there for two years, and you're still not mature, you should listen to the advice of the elders more." Klodia said softly.

"In your eyes, I will always be a child, and I will never be able to mature, but have you ever thought about it? I am who I am, not a puppet that you can manipulate at will."

Klodia was speechless, lowered her head and sighed, "I discipline you strictly because I hope you can stand on your own feet as soon as possible. Why do you always think I'm deliberately bothering you?"

"Originally..." Alice grumbled in her heart.

"You're ungrateful." Klodia scolded Alice with a white eye, and asked curiously, "Where did the power of the dragon race come from?"

"I won't tell you~" Alice pouted her mouth, and contradicted her teacher.

"Alice!" Klodia scolded her seriously.

".... Alice was scared by Klodia's scolding tone and was afraid of being punished by her teacher, so she only answered seriously, ".... I ate a dragon race's inheritance crystal...."

"Dragon race's inheritance crystal?" Klodia frowned, thought carefully, and suddenly realized, "Oh~, it's that kind of thing, a crystal that appears in the brain of a giant dragon with a very small probability, which can give the user part of the dragon race's power..."

"Yes...."

Alice nodded.

"It's not bad that you have such good luck, you can get such a thing, and it's no wonder that you can reach Saint-tier so quickly, even surpass it. With your talent, I estimate that you would have to work hard until you're thirty to touch the door of Saint-tier...." Klodia said playfully, feeling that her student's talent is not good, but her luck is really excellent.

"I'm not that stupid!" Alice said indignantly.

"As your teacher, I know you too well." Klodia tilted her head and asked tentatively, "With the power of the dragon race, isn't your Great Snow Mountain swordsmanship abandoned? How long has it been since you've studied my teachings properly?"

"I have studied them properly, look!" Alice stretched out her hand, showing a small piece of pale gold ice, formed by the fusion of qi and magic.

Klodia looked at it and immediately looked unhappy, and said disapprovingly, "Your fusion ice crystal is not stable at all. You've studied for so long and can only construct such fragile ice. When you go out, don't say you're my student, people will think you're a joke."

".... Alice's anger burned fiercely in her heart, silently clenched her fists, and thought to herself, no matter what I do, I will never get the recognition of my teacher!"

Klodia didn't pay attention to Alice's mood, but instead, her peripheral vision caught something strange.

She stood up and went to Chris's small basket, and saw that there were many children's toys inside?

Klodia picked up a small surfboard and tried to "dong dong dong" hit it two times, then teased her.

"Alice, you, you're so old, do you still have time to play with children's toys? Don't you feel ashamed?"

"Not like that! ...."

Alice suddenly had a bright idea in her mind, thinking of a good way to make Klodia leave.

If Klodia wants to bring herself back to the Great Snow Mountain, then say that she has already married and has children.

After getting married, even if it's Klodia, she probably won't be able to force herself back to the Great Snow Mountain, right?

Alice cleared her throat, looked up, and said in a serious tone.

"Teacher, don't misunderstand, these are my daughter's toys...."

Klodia's eyes instantly widened, and her eyeballs almost fell out, and the surfboard in her hand also dropped to the ground unintentionally.

"What? ?"
