title: Chapter 7 — The Challenger
content:
Chapter 7 — The Challenger

Volume 26 · Chapter 7

Claudia almost fainted with her eyes open, her mouth twitching and eyebrows jumping wildly as she stared at Alice, unable to utter a word— These toys are my dear daughter's? No way! Has this girl already become a mother?! Claudia couldn't believe her ears, her mind filled with Alice's nonsense, not real. "I said these toys are my daughter's." Alice looked into Claudia's eyes, speaking seriously, "Actually I'm already married, my child is named Chris, and now she can even go out to buy soy sauce..." "What?!" Claudia's worldview shattered—so many words got stuck in her throat. "So, teacher, I can't go back to the Great Snow Mountain with you, otherwise my baby would have no mother. I hope you'll spare me for the child's sake." Alice pleaded earnestly. ......

Claudia suddenly felt considerable pressure; she was constantly called an old woman, yet her student had already married young and could even go out to buy soy sauce— a sense of frustration welled up, Claudia felt surpassed by her disciple, thinking Alice was the true winner in life compared to herself. She had thought Alice lacked feminine charm, destined to be forever single in this life, but unexpectedly Alice had gotten ahead of her! Claudia couldn't believe the reality before her, still hoping Alice would keep her company, so she tentatively said, "Alice, don't lie about this? You really... already married?" "Teacher, I have no need to lie about this; I really have started a family, I didn't inform you to attend the wedding, that's my fault." Alice said, feigning self-blame. "Huh?" Claudia's expression complex, she instinctively stepped back two steps, murmuring dazedly, "Really married? And you have a child?" "Yes, my daughter is very cute, named Chris, she just went out with her dad to buy new clothes, you'll be able to see her soon." Alice said solemnly. "Why didn't you consult me about getting married? You just randomly found a man and married him!" Claudia felt dissatisfied, thinking Alice acted on her own too disobedient. "Isn't my marriage my own decision? Why are you so angry, teacher?" Alice frowned. "I'm doing this for your own good! Out there it's a mixed bag, all kinds of people. How could you so lightly marry someone?" Claudia paused, expression serious, "Besides, you're naturally pure and kind, outsiders can easily deceive you, weren't you tricked by that jerk?" "I'm not a child, I have my own judgment of good and evil!" Alice retorted, then huffed, "He's a good person, he's saved me from danger several times, we live happily together." "Very... very happy?" Claudia almost choked, her tone sour, "It must be a man good at pretending, outwardly decent but inwardly filthy, I don't agree with you being together!" "No! Why do you always think the worst of people, teacher?" Alice turned away, huffing, "We already have a child; even if you disagree, it won't change anything. Do you really want me to be like you, almost fifty and still living alone? I don't want that...." "....Claudia was at a loss for words, her face gradually darkening, she asked in an unfriendly tone, 'What does he do?' Alice paused, thinking she couldn't say Merlin is a demon, otherwise the teacher would definitely look at him with colored glasses. Most people, due to the Holy Church's long-term propaganda, have no good feeling toward the demon race, even feel fear. Although the teacher has an eccentric personality, she might not necessarily accept the existence of demons.... So Alice cleared her throat, deliberately concealing Merlin's identity. "He and I are both adventurers...." "Huh~ Adventurer?" Claudia showed a bit of disdain, asking, "How? Could he be a rare violet-gold adventurer?" "No..." Alice's eyes darted away. "...And you- same, are both silver?" Claudia raised her eyebrows, thinking she could help Alice out of danger, couldn't be lower than silver? "...Not either" Alice lowered her head, feeling it inconvenient to say. "Couldn't he be a bronze adventurer?" Claudia frowned, lecturing, "You at least are a silver adventurer, how could you pick a man one rank lower as your husband? Are you brain-damaged? What love potion did he give you?" "Well... he's an iron adventurer." Alice answered honestly; she stood there modestly. Claudia, having experienced storms, was nonetheless stunned by Alice's answer. She had thought bronze adventurers were already low-ranking, but the fact exceeded her imagination! Claudia barely regained composure, putting on a stern face, looked at Alice, hesitated a moment and said, "Looks like your brain is really messed up again." "It's not what you think? He's actually very strong, otherwise how could he have saved me from danger several times?" Alice quickly explained. "At this point, you're still speaking up for him? Really, a woman grown up doesn't stay...." Claudia's eyelids twitched, she sighed repeatedly. "Soon he'll be back, right?" "I'd like to see what kind of person could bewitch you like this...."

In front of the Adventurers Guild in Rexheim, two outsiders stood. Boze lifted his head, lion-like eyes fixed on the guild's dilapidated door, letting out a disdainful 'huh' from his nose. Beside him, Noe occasionally yawned, showing how bored he felt in this remote town. 'Guild master, why did we come all this way to this backwater? It's even more boring than I imagined.' 'To test where your current strength stands, we need to challenge some strong opponents.' Boze's voice was thick, as if a megaphone were installed in his throat. 'What strong opponents could there be here? Isn't this just a waste of time?' Noe lowered his head and curled his lip. 'Don't underestimate them; the guild master here is called Taylor. Though his strength is merely average, his understanding of martial arts is extraordinary—if you underestimate that old guy, you'll suffer for it.' Boze said calmly. 'Oh, so we're here to challenge that old guy?' Noe raised his head in surprise. 'No, after becoming guild master you're ineligible to enter the tournament; you need to face adventurers who can appear in the competition, gaining prior knowledge of your opponents.' Boze lowered his voice. 'That's right... Noe scratched his messy hair, asking, 'Could this small town actually have strong adventurers worth the guild master squeezing time out of his busy schedule to bring me here?' 'Yes, according to various intel, the opponent's strength is close to yours, making them the ideal choice to test your power.' Boze paused, then said to the careless Noe, 'Silver-rank swordsman, Alice Claudia.'

title: Chapter 8 — Doorstep Mockery (Extra)
content:
Chapter 8 — Doorstep Mockery (Extra)

Volume 26 · Chapter 8

"Alice Claudio, when she thought carefully, felt it was familiar. 'I think I've heard that name before?'"

"Alice is someone who only recently became active in the adventurer world. I've investigated her thoroughly." Bozdon said slowly, "She first gained a bit of fame by solving an unexpected undead outbreak, then made a name for herself during the turmoil in France, and was even awarded by Queen Elizabeth of Britain, becoming a foreign thorn knight. You could say she went from unknown to highly sought-after in the shortest time possible. Even Carl of Rexthem can't compare to her."

"Ah, so that's how it is. Rexthem became a bit famous because of her, no wonder it all makes sense now."

"Your next opponent is this swordmaster. Defeat her and you'll prove your strength." Boz said seriously.

"Master, you know I really want to face Tanya, not some overrated has-been~" Noel shrugged, showing he wasn't very interested.

"It's too early to face Tanya now. You'll eventually meet her on the battlefield. Right now, the best person to test your strength against is that swordmaster." Boz said earnestly.

"Why can't I challenge Tanya now?" Noel frowned, feeling a bit discontent in his heart.

"Tanya is a true monster. Fighting her isn't sparring—it's a life-or-death struggle. The adventurer tournament is coming soon, and you'd best not get injured." Boz glanced at Noel and lowered his voice, "Don't underestimate this swordmaster. Beat her and you'll prove you have what it takes to face Tanya."

"Is that so? Then I'll have to take this seriously." Noel stretched lazily and asked curiously, "Master, did you come here because Rexthem's guild also has the strength to win the championship?"

Boz looked at the gate of the Rexthem Adventurers Guild and said flatly, "This time, our opponents are those traditional powers."

"Rexthem? Just a stepping stone on our way to the championship."

Lucia was busy with her own work, not even lifting her head, too occupied to even find time to drink water.

Hobbes seemed a bit drunk, leaning on the table and letting out a burp that made his whole body jump.

"Burp~ Lucia, how long has it been since your father left? Why hasn't he come back?"

"I don't know. Maybe his martial arts training isn't going well. He won't come back if there's no progress." Lucia answered without enthusiasm.

"Carl is really taking this tournament too seriously. With Alice around, we could make it into the top hundred just lying down. He doesn't need to work so hard anymore." Hobbes poured cold water.

"Who's the one acting like a drunkard here?" Lucia looked up, annoyed, "My father just doesn't want to put all the pressure on Alice alone. If you were like him, the guild would have been disowned by headquarters long ago."

"Heh heh heh, my bad. I shouldn't have said those things about Carl. I wish Carl well and hope he returns as champion, bringing us new heights in the tournament!" Hobbes said with exaggerated sincerity.

"Ugh." Lucia rolled her eyes, but inwardly she was a bit worried. Her father and grandfather had left to train, but where they went she didn't know. It had been a long time and they hadn't returned, which made her uneasy.

"That bastard Arnold, probably gave up this time. Alice and Merlin already have kids. If he keeps chasing after her like this, it just makes him look foolish." Hobbes suddenly brought up his "plastic" best friend.

"Who knows? Two years ago when that guy went to Elkin City, he was completely smitten with Alice. Who knows what happened on the road?" Lucia looked up with a puzzled expression, "Actually, Rosette is a good girl. She seems fiery on the surface but is very conservative inside. It's a shame she got stuck with Arnold."

"Hiss~" Hobbes squinted his eyes meaningfully, "Lucia, I didn't expect you to be so gossipy."

"What are you saying? If you keep talking nonsense, I'll tear your mouth apart!" Lucia immediately got serious, realizing she couldn't say too much in front of this loudmouth.

Just as Hobbes was about to tease Lucia further, he saw two people approaching from outside. When they showed their adventurer IDs, the surrounding adventurers were so intimidated they all made way.

End

Remember to bookmark and recommend this site to friends who enjoy reading.

Boz took Noel into the guild hall. Wherever they went, not a single person dared to meet their eyes.

Both of them came from the second-tier powerful guild. Boz was even more formidable, so the Rexthem adventurers naturally didn't dare provoke him—they could only look up at him.

Even drunk Hobbes sobered up a bit when he saw Boz and Noel, quickly grabbing his wine bottle and scurrying to the side.

Lucia put down her work and approached them, scrutinizing them carefully.

"Gentlemen, what brings you all the way from Cartowitz? If you need any help, please don't hesitate to ask."

Boz glanced at Lucia and gave a slight nod of greeting. "Hello, I'm the guildmaster of the Cartowitz Adventurers Guild. I have a request I'd like you to help with."

"Really?" Lucia forced a smile, embarrassed internally. The world's second-tier great guild needs our help? This doesn't sound like good news.

"This is Noel. He's heard that your Alice is exceptionally strong and holds her in high esteem, so he'd like to spar with her. Could you please notify Alice?" Boz said politely.

"This..." Lucia felt some pressure. Sparring? That sounds nice, but surely they're not trying to step on us before the tournament, are they?

"Miss, please don't misunderstand. We have no ill intentions. Sparring is a way for mutual learning and common progress. It's a good form of communication. I hope you'll give us a chance." Boz smiled, revealing his hypocritical kindness.

Lucia wore a professional smile but caught a whiff of something fishy. She didn't want to agree, "I'm sorry, Mr. Boz. The tournament is about to start. Private fights serve no purpose. Surely you understand this better than anyone."

Boz fell silent for a long time. His lion-like eyes revealed a hint of arrogance, and he said coldly, "Since you won't agree to spar, then it's a challenge. Please notify Alice that Noel from the Cartowitz Guild is challenging the renowned Alice."

"Sorry, we won't help relay the message." Lucia's expression also cooled, refusing outright.

"Haha." The usually silent Noel suddenly burst into loud laughter. "Of course Rexthem's guild is full of useless lackeys. I knew it the moment I walked in. You're raising a bunch of useless pests. I heard Alice is the strongest adventurer in your guild, but it seems like all bark and no bite."

Lucia's face turned red with anger, but she didn't dare to lash out. Noel's disparaging remarks made her furious.

Boz lowered his head and smiled slightly, as if giving Noel's behavior his silent approval.

"You bunch of people playing at being adventurers, isn't there a single one who's worth fighting?" Noel looked around at all the Rexthem adventurers present.

"I'm giving you one night to think about it."

"If tomorrow no one accepts the challenge, then I'll let everyone outside know."

"The joke of Rexthem's chicken-eyed adventurers, forever clowns in the sewer~"

title: Chapter 9 — Defining the Relationship
content:
Chapter 9 — Defining the Relationship

Volume 26 · Chapter 9

Hearing Noah's provocatively toned remarks, many adventurers flashed anger in their eyes, yet not a single one dared to act up.

That was the suppressing pressure of the major guild—before any match even began, they had already lost in momentum.

"It's not easy for a small guild like yours to raise a powerful adventurer. I hope tomorrow I can see Miss Alice, and that you won't let this trivial matter drag your entire guild's reputation through the mud." Noah strutted away, chin raised.

Boz, the guild master, had never once intervened; instead, he indulged Noah's rude behavior the whole time.

Boz gave a slight bow, apologizing to Lucy with a hypocritical expression.

"That guy has always been like this—short-tempered and rude. I apologize on his behalf."

"But I suppose he's not entirely wrong. Raising a talented adventurer really isn't easy."

"Having the reputation of a cowardly turtle isn't exactly pleasant to hear, though."

Boz smiled meaningfully, then turned and left with a flourish, leaving behind a roomful of furious faces.

Hobbs was terrified, trembling as he stepped forward. "Sure enough, these major guild types are no good~"

Lucy kept her face dark, silent, suppressing her rage. She didn't know what the other party was plotting, challenging Alice like that.

"Lucy, what should we do? Should we notify Alice?" Hobbs asked tentatively.

"The tournament isn't for a while. If possible, I don't want Alice to get into any duels. If something goes wrong, it'll be terrible." Lucy hesitated.

"Then we'd really just be a rabble..." Hobbs took a swig from his wine bottle. "Though what she said is the truth."

"Shut up." Lucy rolled her eyes, but her mind was racing.

Should she notify Alice or not?

If she didn't, the guild's reputation would be ruined...

At home, Claudria sat on the sofa like an authoritative elder, waiting for the despicable man who had seduced her student to return.

Alice stood nervously nearby, glancing at the clock from time to time, worried about what would happen when Merlin came back.

Who knew how her old-fashioned teacher viewed Merlin? She probably already thought he was a fraud!

Alice thought that to keep the fake marriage from being exposed, she'd have to be warm and welcoming when Merlin got home—like a real wife.

"Why isn't he back yet?" Claudria frowned; the tea on the table had gone cold.

"Soon..." Alice answered guiltily.

Ding-dong—

The doorbell rang. Alice jolted, nearly sitting down on the floor.

"Hm?" Claudria shot Alice a suspicious glance.

Alice forced a calm expression and walked to open the door, thinking: Finally here—please don't blow my cover!

The moment the door opened, Chris rushed in eagerly, clinging to Alice's leg and refusing to let go.

"Mommy! Mommy~ Is my new clothes pretty? Daddy picked them out for me!"

"Is that so? Very pretty..."

Alice's mind was a mess about how to bluff her way through—she had no interest in admiring her cute daughter at all.

She picked up Chris and immediately flashed a wife-like smile to welcome Merlin.

"Welcome back, dear. Are you tired?"

"Hm?" Chris's antenna-like hair tuft bent. Even she felt her mother was acting strange—usually Mom never gave Dad a good face and spoke in a rough manner. Why was she so gentle today?

Even a child could sense something off, let alone Merlin. Hearing Alice's affectionate greeting, goosebumps rose all over his body.

Merlin instinctively took a step back, unable to get used to Alice's mushy tone. He even had the eerie feeling that Alice was trying to harm him.

Claudria had been watching the doorway the whole time. Hearing Chris call her "Mommy," her heart sank halfway.

Called her Mommy? So there really is a kid!

She lost. She lost to her student. Her student already had a child. She was a complete loser in life.

Claudria felt emotionally crushed, but looking at Chris from afar, the child really was adorable—and it made this "elderly lady" feel quite fond.

"..." Seeing Alice so resistant, Alice felt displeased internally. Couldn't she just be gentle for once? Why was Merlin so resistant?

"Dear, what's wrong? Are you feeling unwell?"

"Don't fuss, Alice. Please act normal. Right now..." Merlin's face was dark, his voice low. "I feel a bit nauseous."

"Wha—!" Alice went rigid as if struck by lightning. Her pride shattered in an instant. She'd barely managed to be gentle, and Merlin already said he felt sick!

"Daddy's lying. Mommy's not gross. Mommy smells nice~" Chris pouted, arguing back.

"I didn't mean it that way." Merlin clarified. He wasn't insulting Alice—just that her behavior was too abnormal. She was usually hot-tempered, and suddenly speaking in a soft, sweet tone calling him "dear"—anyone would find the drastic contrast unsettling and nauseating.

"Why... why are you reacting so strangely? Am I not normal? Dear~" Alice swallowed her annoyance at Merlin and kept up the act, thinking: If it weren't to fool the teacher, I wouldn't be doing this either!

"You're the strange one, aren't you?" Merlin reached out and touched Alice's forehead, frowning. "You don't have a fever or anything, do you?"

"..." Claudria's gaze turned odd. She sensed a subtle dissonance between the two of them—nothing like a married couple. Hmph! Thinking that was the man Alice had picked—just some sleazy pretty boy!

"Ugh!" Alice was flustered. Tortured by Merlin's obtuseness beyond endurance, she grabbed his wrist, pressing harder to hint, gritting her teeth as she said, "I'm fine, dear."

Chris, held in Alice's arms, clearly sensed a killing intent and went silent with fear, trembling in her mother's embrace.

"? ? ?" Merlin noticed something off and turned to look around the room, finally spotting a stranger. "Th-that... who are you?"

"I forgot to introduce... Alice glanced at Claudria's stern face and whispered, "This is my teacher from the Great Snow Mountain. You mentioned her before, right?"

"Oh... oh!"

Merlin remembered. No wonder Alice was acting so strange—her teacher had arrived.

As Alice's roommate, Merlin felt it was only right to greet her properly.

So Merlin stepped up to Claudria and extended his hand warmly.

"Hello, I'm Merlin. I'm Alice's..."

"Husband!!!"

Merlin had wanted to say he was Alice's friend, but before he could finish, Alice shouted that single word, cementing their relationship right then and there.

That shout not only startled little Chris, widening her eyes, but left Merlin utterly bewildered, turning back to look at Alice with a confused expression.

That vile woman...

Is she crazy?

title: Chapter 10 — A Marriage Farce
content:
Chapter 10 — A Marriage Farce

Volume 26 · Chapter 10

Merlin looked at Alice with a strange expression, as if wondering if she had taken the wrong medicine today.

He pointed at himself and asked on impulse, "Alice, are you calling me?"

"Of course! I'm not calling you, who am I calling?" Alice's face broke into a mischievous smile, but it ended with her teeth gritted.

"???" Merlin's eyebrows knit together. He thought, This is Alice's teacher, right? Why does Alice seem so weird around her?

"Hmm, the first time I've heard Mommy call Daddy..." Chris said innocently, looking at Alice.

"Nonsense... nonsense! Don't say such things, kid, haha..." Alice laughed and covered Chris's mouth.

Chloria looked at Alice and Merlin with a suspicious eye and said with an air of superiority, "You're called Merlin, right?"

"Yes. Hello." Merlin extended his hand in friendship.

Chloria glanced at Merlin and turned her head away coldly, "Hmph!"

"Huh?" Merlin awkwardly withdrew his hand and looked at Alice, raising his eyebrows to ask what that was supposed to mean.

Alice, unable to withstand the pressure, could only scold Chloria, "Teacher, you really shouldn't... he hasn't done anything to you, has he?"

Chloria's temples twitched. She took a deep breath and demanded, "How did you lure away my student? What underhanded tactics did you use?"

"I... I don't understand. I'm a straightforward person. 'Lure away' is going too far. I didn't do anything."

"Didn't you?" Chloria's face darkened. She acted as though she knew everything and said, "Just looking at you, I can tell you're a smooth-talking pretty boy. I've seen plenty of people like you. One look and I know exactly what kind of person you are!"

"I... Alice, this is your teacher..." Merlin was insulted for no reason and felt annoyed. If it weren't for Alice's sake, he would have already thrown a punch.

Alice quickly tugged at Merlin's sleeve and gave him meaningful eye signals, hoping Merlin wouldn't say anything more.

Merlin held in his anger, but seeing Alice's pitiful expression, he couldn't figure out what was going on, so he held back.

"Ha..." Chloria sneered and said with a meaningful tone, "I remember about a year ago, you secretly wrote me a letter, saying you were dating a great swordsman who was strong and had a strong sense of justice, basically the perfect man in the world. I didn't expect that when we met, it turned out to be someone like you? Don't tell me this guy is the great swordsman from your letter, someone who can't even fool a child!"

Merlin heard Chloria's disdain and almost burst out laughing. He thought, So Alice used to be this infatuated? She even wrote me a letter like that!

He didn't even know who the Elkin Great Swordsman was, yet he was fantasizing about dating him every day.

I never expected Alice's imagination to be so rich when it came to her private thoughts.

What a coincidence, I'm actually the Elkin Great Swordsman.

Merlin cleared his throat and put on a smile that was both subtle and slightly smug.

"Cough, cough. Sorry, I..."

"Stop talking, teacher! Who is the Elkin Great Swordsman? I don't even know! I never wrote you any letter!"

Alice suddenly shouted, interrupting Merlin. Her face was red. She had long since treated those past events as dark history, and thinking about them now made her head hurt.

In the past, Alice had indeed admired the Elkin Great Swordsman, but back then she wasn't mature. She mistook her admiration for love and caused quite a few embarrassing incidents.

Later, Alice realized that every time she opened her eyes, it was this annoying guy Merlin by her side. She gradually grew to like him and found being together quite happy.

Alice didn't want to bring up those dark memories, fearing Merlin would look at her with disdain. Those were things she couldn't bear to recall.

Merlin was surprised by Alice's reaction. He thought, The Elkin Great Swordsman was Alice's idol, yet now she says she doesn't know him? Ha, women.

"You're hiding something. If it wasn't your letter, then whose letter was it? Did a ghost write it to me?" Chloria said sternly.

"N-no... no matter what, I never had any daydreams about dating the Elkin Great Swordsman..." Alice stubbornly denied, refusing to admit it.

"It doesn't matter if you admit it or not. If the man you chose is truly some legendary hero, I won't say anything. But... how on earth does he deserve you?" Chloria scrutinized Merlin from head to toe with a serious expression, "I don't approve of you two being together."

"Tch..." Merlin couldn't help but click his tongue in annoyance. He thought, Besides my reputation being a bit off, where else am I not worthy of Alice?

"Teacher! We're truly in love! You can't break up my family!" Alice said angrily, pulling out the emotional card, "My child is so young. How could I manage without Mommy? Can you bear to see that, teacher?"

"Uwaa..." Although Chris couldn't quite follow what the adults were talking about, she could vaguely sense that Mommy was about to leave. Tears welled up in her eyes, "Don't let Auntie bully Mommy. Auntie is mean... bully..."

"Huh? Auntie... Auntie?" Chloria's breath caught. Her heart struggled a bit. First called a leftover woman, and now already an auntie, "Don't use the kid as a shield. That's so shameless."

"Waaaahhh!!!" Chris suddenly broke down in tears, sobbing and wailing in Alice's arms, "Auntie is a bad guy! She bullies people! Bad guy, waaahhh..."

"N-no... that's not right..." Chloria suddenly felt an indescribable pressure, waves of guilt washing over her.

Why does this child cry so much?

Just like Alice when she was little, weak in character...

◇

After much effort, the three of them finally calmed little Chris down so she stopped crying and making a scene. Only then did the house fall quiet.

Chloria, having been in contact with Chris, revealed her fondness for children, chatting with Chris in a warm and gentle manner.

Little Chris clearly didn't dislike this suddenly visiting stranger auntie, cooing and communicating with her softly.

Seeing the opportunity, Alice quickly pulled Merlin aside and briefly explained what had happened.

After understanding the situation, Merlin sighed and smirked, "So that's what happened. I thought you said your teacher was coming, why did you act like a madwoman?"

"You're the madwoman!" Alice puffed out her cheeks and argued.

"Ha, you were calling me 'dear' and 'husband' just now. It made me sick to my stomach, ugh~" Merlin rolled his eyes.

"What did you say!?" Alice's face flushed red. She pointed her finger and blew hard on Merlin's chest, saying indignantly, "You think I want to do that?"

"So now, as long as your teacher doesn't leave, you'll keep calling me 'husband' and 'dear'?" Merlin said with a strange expression.

"That's right. We have no choice but to act like this. Not just me, you have to call me 'dear' too. Do you understand?" Alice said seriously.

"Huh?" Merlin's head spun. He was stunned by Alice's words, completely at a loss.

"I..."

"I'm sorry, I just can't bring myself to say it."

"And besides, I threw up..."

title: Chapter 11 — Aftermath
content:
Chapter 11 — Aftermath

Volume 26 · Chapter 11

"Wait, do you have any conscience at all?" Alice, though struggling to endure it herself, was willing to compromise on anything to avoid going back to the Great Snow Mountain with her teacher. "At a time like this, shouldn't you be cooperating with me a little more?"

"Cooperate, definitely cooperate..." Merlin swore solemnly, then couldn't hold back his laughter. "Hahaha, but this really is disgusting."

"Don't laugh, I'm serious." Alice glared at Merlin in dissatisfaction, whispering, "If you don't cooperate properly, I'll be taken back to the Great Snow Mountain by my teacher. Do you want me to go back there?"

Merlin's expression turned serious. After thinking carefully for a moment, he heartlessly said, "It's not like it's impossible. Just remember to leave your little treasure vault behind when you go. Consider it your final contribution."

Alice furrowed her delicate brows, her temples twitching with visible veins as she poured cold water on the idea. "If I'm not here, Chris will cry nonstop. Then you'll have to be the one to soothe her. And if I go back to the remote Great Snow Mountain, all the debts I owe will fall on you."

Merlin shuddered, his smile vanishing as he realized the gravity of the situation. He decided he needed to cooperate with Alice to get through this crisis. "Rest assured, I'll actively cooperate. I'll try my best to send your teacher away as soon as possible."

"That's more like it." Alice nodded in satisfaction, then a faint blush unexpectedly rose to her cheeks. "Then... then you try calling me 'dear.' Don't end up laughing and let my teacher find out we're faking."

"Huh? Do we really need to go that far?" Merlin found it hard to accept and didn't want to say anything too sappy.

"It's very necessary." Alice insisted stubbornly.

Merlin cleared his throat twice, straightening his posture before whispering, "D-dear..."

Alice's face slowly turned red, feeling a strange sensation. She lowered her head and stopped talking.

"How was that? Say something, we can't get caught, right?" Merlin asked tentatively.

"Then..." Alice kept her head down, hesitating as she said, "It really... is a bit disgusting..."

"What do you even want from me?" Merlin rolled his eyes in exasperation, thinking to himself—

We're not even a real couple. How are we supposed to act like one?

We're usually arguing fiercely. Now we're supposed to say "dear"? That's impossible, isn't it?

Meanwhile, Chris was playing with her crayons, happily scribbling on a piece of paper.

Claudia sat beside her, watching the child's doodles with interest.

Chris pressed down hard on the paper with her crayons, as if working on some "masterpiece."

Claudia lifted her head to examine Chris's face up close. The close observation made her secretly startled—

This child... really looks like Alice.

She resembles Alice when she was little, both of them mischievous little girls.

But this child has a much richer imagination than young Alice did. What is this? Three colorful monsters?

Claudia studied Chris's drawing, speculating about the possibilities, trying to see if the child had any innate talent.

Chris let out a long breath, wiping the sweat from her forehead. Drawing had exhausted her. She put down her crayon and looked at her multicolored hands, frowning as she thought she might get scolded by her mother later.

"What did you... draw?" Claudia asked curiously.

Chris proudly held up her freshly finished "masterpiece" for Claudia to see. "Grandma, look! This is Daddy, Mommy, and me!"

"Ah..." Claudia's mouth twitched. She wondered what kind of monstrosity this was supposed to be. None of them looked human. How was this supposed to resemble her parents?

"This is Daddy, and this is Mommy..." Chris pointed to a small figure with feathers on its back, then to another small figure with membranous wings and flames around it. Finally, she pointed to a plain little figure surrounded by small red flowers. "And this is me~"

"...Is that so?" Claudia forced a smile, asking, "Why do Daddy and Mommy have wings on their backs? They don't look anything like them..."

"That's not it! Daddy always teases me, saying he's a great demon who will eat me up. So Daddy is a demon. The flames around him are the sun. Even when Daddy teases me, he's as warm as the sun." Chris said in her childish voice.

"Oh~" Claudia felt a bit embarrassed, thinking that the pretty boy occasionally scared the child? He had absolutely no intimidating presence. What a failure of a father.

"The one with feathers is Mommy. Mommy is so good to me, so Mommy is an angel~" The ahoge on Chris's head wiggled as she pointed to the last figure in the middle of the red flowers. "And this is Chris, the cute little one taken care of by Daddy and Mommy~"

"Hahaha, so that's how it is..." Claudia laughed, barely managing to understand Chris's "masterpiece." It was quite a meaningful work, in its own way.

"We are a family, and we'll never be separated. Chris will be a good girl and stay with Daddy and Mommy..." Chris held up her drawing, happily spinning in place.

Claudia's eyebrows twitched. She wondered if the child was hinting at something—telling her not to take Alice away?

She rubbed her temples, feeling the pressure. With them having a child, it would be very difficult to take Alice away. What should she do?

"Chris, can Grandma ask you a few questions?"

"Eh?" Chris tilted her head curiously.

"Are your Daddy and Mommy... really a couple?" Claudia tried to use Chris as a breakthrough to gather some useful information.

"What's a couple?" Chris blinked innocently, tilting her head in confusion.

"Well..." Claudia felt awkward, realizing she had forgotten that the child was too young to understand the concept of "couple." She rephrased, "Are they really your Daddy and Mommy?"

"Daddy and Mommy are Daddy and Mommy! There's no such thing as fake..." Chris answered naively.

Claudia sighed, trying another approach. "Do your Daddy and Mommy... sleep together every night?"

"Yes! Daddy and Mommy sleep with me~" Chris answered with a smile.

"They sleep together..."

Claudia lowered her head, feeling lost. It seemed they were truly a couple. They must have been sleeping together for a long time.

Alice was too naive. The more Claudia looked at her, the more she felt that Alice had been deceived by a man with ulterior motives!

As her teacher, she couldn't just stand by and watch. She had to find a way to expose that pretty boy's true nature!

Meanwhile, the other two had finished discussing their strategy. Alice walked over and asked, "Teacher, what have you decided? Can you please not make me go back to the Great Snow Mountain?"

"Having a child does complicate things. I was considering taking you back, but now I'm reserving judgment. I plan to stay here for a while and then decide." Claudia said seriously.

"You... how long do you plan to stay?" Alice asked, feeling the pressure.

"Do you get to question how long your teacher stays? I'll leave when I'm happy." Claudia smiled meaningfully.

"Please, just leave quickly! Our lives are harmonious. We don't need you to worry about us!" Alice said, exasperated.

"You want me to leave? That can be arranged..." Claudia glanced at the absent-minded little Chris and whispered,

"I think this child is quite clever. If properly raised, she'll definitely be better than you, my dull student."

"How about..."

"Let me take Chris back to the Great Snow Mountain with me? That way, I'll have someone to keep me company."

title: Chapter 12 — Even Teachers Steal Men
content:
Chapter 12 — Even Teachers Steal Men

Volume 26 · Chapter 12

“What?!” Alice shrieked as she scooped Chris up, her voice laced with hostility. “You’re after my man now? And you want to take my child too? No way!”

“Why so resistant? I raised you, so of course I could raise Chris too. Why not trust me with her?” Claudine said with a helpless expression.

“No way!” Alice retorted firmly, thinking to herself that she knew exactly how Claudine took care of children. She wouldn’t let Chris suffer the same hardships she had endured as a child.

In truth, Alice’s worries weren’t unfounded. As a child, she had grown up under Claudine’s strict training, enduring countless hardships.

Little Chris couldn’t resist at all. If Claudine took her to the Snowy Mountains, she might end up being treated the same way.

“Pfft.” Claudine pouted and said indifferently, “If you won’t let me take Chris, then I’ll just stay for a while. I’ll leave when I feel like it.”

Merlin:

Alice:

The two fell silent, having no good way to deal with Claudine. As an elder, they couldn’t exactly force her out.

Still, both hoped Claudine would leave soon so things could return to normal.

“Grandma isn’t leaving?” Chris asked curiously, looking up.

“Nope. I’ll stay and play with you. How does that sound?” Claudine poked Chris’s little cheek.

Chris blinked her big eyes, her idle hair swaying as she happily replied—

“Yay~ Hi~”

As night fell, Merlin returned to his old den, collapsing onto the stiff, worn-out sofa.

Claudine had kicked him out of the bedroom under the pretense of “catching up with her student,” leaving him no choice but to sleep there.

Merlin rolled his eyes but didn’t argue with Claudine. After all, it had been ages since they’d seen each other, so chatting late into the night was reasonable.

So Merlin hugged his pillow and slept alone on the sofa, his mind already scheming about how to help Alice get rid of this “great deity.”

In the bedroom, without her father around, Chris’s mood turned gloomy. She kept muttering, “Daddy… I want Daddy. Why is Daddy sleeping outside?”

Alice lay beside Chris, seething at Claudine but unable to say anything. It was all her fault for kicking Merlin out, wasn’t it?

Claudine remained calm in the face of Chris’s complaints, gently asking, “Chris, do you like your daddy so much?”

“Mhm~” Chris said in her childish voice.

“Then… you don’t like Grandma?” Claudine asked with a smile.

“I like Daddy more if you don’t take Mommy away,” Chris pouted.

“Haha, don’t worry. I won’t take your mommy away,” Claudine said as she tucked the blanket around Chris, then asked, “So, what exactly do you like about your daddy?”

Chris pondered seriously for a moment before answering in all seriousness, “I like Daddy’s big chest muscles!”

“Chest… muscles?” Claudine blinked in confusion before realizing, “Oh~ I see. But Grandma’s chest muscles are way bigger than your daddy’s. Shouldn’t you like me more?”

“Mmm!” Chris peeked at Claudine’s figure before trembling in fear and falling silent, looking at her with pity.

Claudine had a mature, voluptuous figure, her ample chest practically bursting out of her clothes, easily overshadowing Alice by a hundredfold!

“Grandma, you’re so pitiful…”

Chris said in a voice full of sympathy.

“Pitiful? What do I have to be pitiful about?” Claudine asked, baffled.

“Your chest muscles are so big… you must’ve been hit a lot, right? That’s why they’re so swollen,” Chris said, still remembering her mother’s words—that only a flat chest was normal for a girl, and anything bigger was from being beaten.

“Huh? Who told you they were swollen from being hit?” Claudine asked, completely lost.

“Mommy did~” Chris said seriously. “Mommy said a flat chest is normal for a girl, and big ones are from being hit. It’s so pitiful…”

“Ugh!” Alice covered her blushing face in shame, feeling like she was about to be mocked by her teacher.

“Hahaha…” Claudine burst into laughter and patiently explained, “No, your mommy’s the one with the abnormal figure. Girls naturally have big chests—it’s not from being hit. Your mom just says that to avoid being looked down on and protect her self-esteem.”

“Mmm… really?” Chris puffed out her cheeks, looking upset. “Mommy lied to me too… I’m sad that Daddy and Mommy always trick me.”

“Teacher!!!” Alice shouted in frustration, wishing she could just crawl into a hole—

Sniff… my mom’s dignity is completely gone…

The next morning, Claudine had planned to expose Merlin’s true colors as a scumbag.

But she was completely disarmed by Merlin’s cooking. Spoon in hand, she stared blankly at the potato soup, at a loss for words.

Little Chris was lucky enough to taste her daddy’s cooking and drank it happily, nearly licking the plate clean.

Alice was used to it by now and didn’t react much, thinking that maybe this would make Claudine see Merlin’s good side.

In truth, Merlin had only made something simple for Chris since she was still a child, choosing the easiest dish to eat—potato soup.

If he’d made something else, Claudine might’ve been even more shocked.

Claudine stared at the last spoonful of soup, lost in thought, reluctant to drink it—because once it was gone, this heavenly taste would be gone too.

Why… why does a bowl of potato soup contain so many flavors?

It kept assaulting her taste buds, changing in countless ways.

Who would’ve thought ordinary ingredients could make something so delicious?

A man who could cook was truly endlessly charming. No wonder her silly student had fallen for him…

Claudine had a slight inkling of understanding Alice’s feelings, but she still stubbornly believed that good cooking was just another trick men used to seduce women.

Alice glanced at Claudine’s dazed expression and couldn’t help but smirk. “So, Teacher, what do you think?”

“…” Claudine snapped back to reality and forced a calm tone. “…It’s not bad. I’ve had better, though. This soup is inferior to that one…”

“Really?” Alice could tell Claudine was just being stubborn, so she added, “Actually, Merlin cooks often. We eat this kind of thing all the time. It’s gotten kind of boring.”

“…” Claudine’s face darkened. She forced herself to stay calm and said, “Is that so? Then I won’t take you and Chris back to the Snowy Mountains. Give me your man instead. How about that?”

“Huh?!” Alice froze in shock before angrily shouting—

“Teacher, you’re trying to steal my man?! R”

title: Chapter 13 — Challenger (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 13 — Challenger (Bonus)

Volume 26 · Chapter 13

"What? Not allowed? Even as your teacher, I still have my charm, far better than you~" Claudia shot Alice a challenging look. "Besides, life in the Great Snow Mountain is harsh, and I never get to eat good food. Bringing a chef back with me wouldn’t be bad~"

"You didn’t come here to see me at all—you’re just here to stir up trouble! You can’t stand seeing me happy!" Alice slammed her hands on the table, fuming. She thought to herself that her teacher was trying to take her and Chris back to the Great Snow Mountain, and now she was even eyeing Merlin—wasn’t this clearly an attempt to break up their family?

Merlin, having finished in the kitchen, took off his apron and came out to join them for breakfast.

He noticed Alice standing up, seething with anger, while Claudia across from her calmly finished the last of her soup...

An odd tension hung in the air. Curious, Merlin asked, "What’s going on?"

"Nothing!" Alice huffed as she sat back down, glaring at her teacher with hostility.

"Hmm?" Merlin had no idea what had happened and couldn’t be bothered to ask. Instead, he turned to Claudia. "Senior Claudia, I hope the food I made suits your taste?"

"It’s... passable." Claudia spoke dismissively, but her bowl was licked clean.

"Ha, as long as you’re happy." Merlin chuckled, then looked down at little Chris. "Chris, how was it? Good?"

"Delicious! Dad’s cooking is amazing! I could drink more~" Chris put down her bowl and answered without hesitation. Kids were always the most honest.

"No, no, overeating isn’t a good habit." Merlin wiped Chris’s mouth with a napkin, then asked, "Compared to your favorite cream cake, which do you like better?"

"..." Chris hesitated, measuring with her little fingers before innocently saying, "The cream cake is a tiny bit better, hehe~"

...Merlin sighed inwardly. This child really had a sweet tooth.

"But Dad’s cooking is way better than Mom’s! His food is... tastier than hers!" Chris said earnestly.

"Ugh!" Alice frowned, feeling overshadowed by Merlin. If this kept up, wouldn’t her precious daughter cling to Merlin every day, begging for food?

"Of course~" Merlin grinned, pinching Chris’s cheek. "Dad likes honest kids..."

"...My cooking isn’t bad either. It won’t kill anyone." Alice paused, putting on her strict mother face. "Children shouldn’t be so picky. Eat what’s given to you..."

Chris pressed her lips together, staying silent. She thought, *Mom always tells me to be honest, but when I am, I get scolded. I really don’t understand adults...*

Claudia remained silent across from them, watching Merlin act like a doting father. A sense of unease grew in her. She shook her head repeatedly.

*Fake! All of it’s fake! They’re just putting on an act for me!*

Trying to fool me with this "good father" persona to lower my guard!

I won’t be so easily deceived! I’ll definitely find proof that you’re tricking my disciple!

Claudia muttered to herself internally, still refusing to give up. Her mind was consumed with ways to expose this hypocritical man’s true nature.

*Ding-dong!* The doorbell rang, breaking the morning calm.

"Who is it at this hour...?" Alice got up to answer the door.

Seeing Alice leave, Claudia’s expression darkened. She leaned toward Merlin, her voice low and threatening. "Boy, don’t think that putting on a good guy act to win me over will make me trust you. I know your type—men who pretend to be perfect family men to deceive girls. Alice’s trust in you is temporary. Just you wait, I *will* find your weakness and expose your true, ugly self..."

Merlin blinked, then gave a meaningful smile. "As you wish..."

Alice opened the door to find Lucia standing outside, looking anxious. "Lucia? What brings you here?"

"Alice, something’s happened." Lucia looked worried. Boz and Noe had shown up at the Adventurers Guild, demanding Alice come out to face them. In no time, a crowd had gathered to watch the spectacle.

"Don’t panic. What’s going on?" Alice straightened up. She figured Lucia wouldn’t come without a good reason. With the Guild Master and Mr. Karl away, she had a responsibility to help.

"Boz, the Guild Master of Katowice, has arrived with one of their adventurers, a man named Noe. They’ve come specifically to challenge you." Lucia explained concisely.

"Ah? Katowice? That second-largest guild in the world?" Alice’s brows furrowed sharply.

"That’s right. They came here just to challenge you." Lucia nodded.

"Why challenge me?" Alice was puzzled. The Katowice Guild was famously powerful, even stronger than London’s. Why would they come all this way to challenge her?

"Alice, your reputation has been spreading beyond the Kingdom of Britain lately." Lucia wore a worried expression. "I suspect they’re unsettled by the sudden rise of a powerful adventurer like you in a remote town like Rexham. They’ve traveled all this way to challenge you, probably to stomp on us before our guild can truly rise."

"I see..." Alice pondered for a moment, then looked up. "Where are they now?"

"They’re at the guild. They said if you refuse the challenge, you’re a coward, and they’ll spread the word to ruin the reputation of every adventurer in Rexham." Lucia lowered her head, looking somewhat apologetic. "I didn’t want to bother you so close to the tournament—if you got hurt, it’d be trouble. But they’re being so aggressive, even slandering all of Rexham’s adventurers. I had no choice..."

"Say no more. I accept their challenge." Alice declared firmly, turning to go inside and fetch her weapon.

At the table, Merlin and Claudia were still locked in a silent stare-down when they saw Alice return, grab her rapier, and rush out in a hurry.

"Alice, where are you going?" Merlin asked.

"Someone’s come to challenge me. I’m going to greet them."

Both of them were stunned—neither had expected such a sudden turn of events.

Claudia: "???"

Behind the Rexham Guild stood the training arena, once the old Guild Master Taylor’s place of cultivation. Merlin had even dueled here before.

But today, it had become a stage of honor for Rexham. Alice and Noe would settle their rivalry here!

Alice gripped her rapier, her sharp gaze fixed on the challenger from Katowice.

Noe wore a contemptuous smile, cradling his own rapier, eyeing the currently famous demon swordswoman with keen interest.

The two stood silently within the white circle, a dangerous duel about to erupt at any moment...

title: Chapter 14 — Swift Sword Duel
content:
Chapter 14 — Swift Sword Duel

Volume 26 · Chapter 14

In the training hall behind the Rexheim Guild, adventurers with nothing to do had almost all gathered here, preparing to watch Alice and Noah's duel.
This was no longer just a duel between the two adventurers Noah and Alice; it was also a wager on the honor of both guilds—
“You think Alice can win? The opponent is from Cattowiz…”
“Pretty much? Alice is now strong enough to even startle the Queen herself.”
“Not necessarily; the Cattowiz Guild is second in the world, filled with strong individuals, so they wouldn’t send a weakling to challenge Alice.”
“Exactly; the opponent isn’t a pushover—they might be trying to use this opportunity to suppress our guild, so we hope Alice can win.”
The Rexheim adventurers voiced many opinions; public sentiment was not unanimously in favor of Alice’s victory, but rather everyone had their own take.
Besides Alice standing in the arena, Merlin, Chris, and Clodia also came, standing in the crowded crowd.
Merlin glanced at Noah opposite Alice, then looked at Boaz standing in the rear—‘So it’s those two…’
“How? Do you know those two guys from Cattowiz?” Hobbs stepped over and patted Merlin’s shoulder.
“I don’t know them; I just glanced at them from afar yesterday on the street, and a lot of people were watching them.” Merlin said calmly.
“It’s normal; they’re a major guild, and besides, Boaz is a division leader.” Hobbs chuckled.
“…Do you know them well?” Merlin asked curiously.
“I wouldn’t say I know them well, but I definitely know more than the average person.” Hobbs paused, then glanced sideways at the relaxed Boaz and said, “Boaz, in the previous tournament he breezed through, trampling London Guild’s top seed underfoot, securing second place for the Cattowiz Guild, then retired abruptly to become a division leader. His ambition and drive are terrifying; even four years ago his strength was enough to look down on all heroes. After becoming guild master he rarely shows his power, but I estimate he’s far stronger now—though it’s hard to gauge precisely. As for Noah? He’s even more remarkable…”
“Oh? How so?” Merlin showed a bit of interest.
“Noah has completed zero missions so far, meaning he’s never done any adventurer work yet still earned headquarters’ recognition through sheer strength—a rare occurrence that shows how terrifying his power is.” Hobbs glanced at Merlin and whispered, “Moreover, I suspect Noah has remained obscure all along, yet Boaz has looked after him in every way; he’s likely being groomed as a secret weapon for the Adventurers’ Tournament. Now that the tournament is near, that honed blade of his should finally be drawn and shown.”
“Really?” Merlin nodded, unfazed, and asked, “What do you think Alice’s chances of winning are?”
“Hehe, hard to say, I…” Hobbs raised a finger, expressing it vaguely.
“One percent? You’re joking?” Merlin was a bit surprised, thinking that although he wouldn’t say Alice could walk sideways across the world, among humans she is absolutely a top-tier talent, or something.
“The Cattowiz Guild is second in the world, possessing vast resources; the adventurers they train…” Hobbs shook his head, speaking mysteriously, “I can’t even imagine how strong they are.”
Merlin fell silent, gazing at Noah in the arena, thinking that this seemingly ordinary fellow might truly possess terrifying strength.
Clodia held little Chris, so she could better see her mother.
Clodia’s gaze first rested on Boaz’s face, then shifted to Noah’s contemptuous expression—
“I haven’t left the snow mountains for decades; have the adventurers’ overall abilities really progressed this much?”
“Even though they’ve been strong for decades, adventurers are merely a rabble hired for money.”
Although Boaz and Noah were suppressing their auras, Clodia still caught faint traces, discerning a hint of their true strength.
“Huh?” Chris sucked her finger, looking around curiously, then fixed her gaze on Alice standing in the center, “Mom, what are we going to do?”
“Your mom is in a duel; she needs to defeat the challenger who came to her door.” Clodia answered softly.
“Why fight?” Chris asked, puzzled.
“Because your mom is defending her honor; only by defeating the challenger can she earn more respect.” Clodia explained simply.
“Oh~!” Chris widened her eyes, half-understanding, then loudly began cheering for Alice, “Go, Mom! Mom will win! Mom is the strongest!”
Inside the white circle at the center of the training hall, Alice heard Chris’s cheering, lifted her head to look at her daughter, and waved happily.
Alice’s heart warmed; hearing her beloved daughter’s cheers filled her with confidence—she cannot lose this duel! She must set an example for her daughter!
“…Noah opposite her suddenly gave a dry laugh, ‘So Miss Alice is a mother, huh?’”
“What? Do you have any advice?” Alice asked expressionlessly.
“Nothing much; I’ll just defeat you in front of your child later, which will make you look even more foolish.” Noah’s gaze gradually turned sympathetic.
“Isn’t it a bit early to say that? Why not think about who will be slinking away from here in disgrace—maybe it’ll be you?” Alice retorted.
“No, I cannot lose; I’m destined to win.” Noah set down the slender sword he was holding, saying meaningfully, “My sword is fast; Miss Alice, you’d better be careful.”
“How fast?” Alice likewise gripped her Light Chant tightly.
“Before you even finish speaking, I’ll have already defeated you and sheathed my sword.” Noah said, half-serious, half-joking.
Alice furrowed her brows, wondering whether the opponent was serious or just boasting, which made her feel pressured.
At that moment, Lukia slowly stepped between them, cleared her throat, and said—
“This isn’t a duel; it’s merely a sparring match between Alice and Mr. Noah, where they learn from each other through combat.”
“Therefore, this match will stop at the point of contact; no one may be injured.”
“The rule is that both must stay within the white circle; whoever steps out loses.”
“Mr. Boaz, is this acceptable? We don’t want an ordinary sp

title: Chapter 15 — Itchy Hands
content:
Chapter 15 — Itchy Hands

Volume 26 · Chapter 15

The two struggled within the small white circle, power poured into their swords constantly colliding.
Alice's eyes flickered with a faint gold, the dragon's might pressing forward strongly, the surface of her thin sword blending with faint ice shards.
Just from the momentum of her strike, Alice was enough to overwhelm Noah!
Yet in the clash, Noah showed no sign of weakness; facing Alice's pressure, his momentum was even greater!
At this moment, Noah finally stopped suppressing his aura, releasing a terrifying sect-bound pressure that was in no way inferior to Alice's.
“Eh!” Alice inwardly gasped, not expecting that beneath Noah's ordinary appearance lay such formidable strength!
“What did I say again…” Hobbs said calmly.
Merlin didn't speak, thinking the opponent's strength was on par with Alice's; this was troublesome.
Claudia held Chris, carefully observing Noah; seeing him suddenly step back, she realized he was gathering momentum before an attack.
“Alice! Be careful!
The words had barely left her mouth when it was already too late—
“…. ” Noah bowed, raised his sword, and struck suddenly; in an instant his whole body twisted, “I won!
A piercing whistle rang out; Noah's sword seemed to turn into a beast, his battle aura continuously letting out deafening roars.
At that moment, Noah's sword and arm seemed to vanish; due to the extreme speed, most people's eyes couldn't keep up!
A single thrust shot out, Alice was directly knocked out of the white circle, defeated in an instant!” “Ah
The crowd below instantly fell into silent stupor, finding it hard to believe their eyes; only after a few seconds did they react.
“Lost? ! Alice actually lost?，
“- ….. just lost?”
“As expected of the adventurers of the great guild, no matter how hard we try, the opponent is far too strong for us.”..
The Rexum adventurers, due to Alice's defeat, had their confidence greatly shaken, becoming self‑critical.
The opponent is a newcomer nurtured by the world's second guild; without some skill, they wouldn't have earned Boz's attention.
“One strike and she lost? Merlin, what do you think?” Hobbs glanced at Merlin beside him.
Merlin remained silent, his eyes turning grim, thinking “One strike? Far more than one—because the sword speed was too fast, many couldn't see clearly, thinking it was a single strike, but in that instant he actually unleashed three thousand six hundred seventy‑four blows; the inconceivable attack speed left Alice unable to parry, knocking her senseless.
“Mom…” Chris, seeing Alice defeated, felt uneasy, her little face turning pouty.
“Hmph!” Claudia snorted in dissatisfaction, her heart full of anger, being beaten so helplessly—does this even qualify as my student? What an embarrassment!
It seemed Claudia thought the loss was Alice's own fault and had no intention of going out to vent for her student.
After all, it was a sparring match between Alice and Noah; as a teacher, Claudia really wasn't suited to step in and help Alice.
Alice stood dazed on the spot; suddenly countless tiny wounds on her body burst open, pain making her drop to her knees—
What a swift thrust—my eyes can't keep up at all!
Compared to when Merlin draws his sword, the pressure it gives me is even greater!
Alice lifted her head and glared at Noah, unwilling to accept the loss; it wasn't because he was stronger, but because he hid his strength and took full advantage!
“Again! Let's have another match!
“I don't see the need for that,” Noah said, slowly sheathing his sword with a meaningful tone, “No matter how many times we fight, you'll never be my opponent; my sword exceeds the speed of sound, and at equal strength there is no rival!
“You!?” Alice tried to rise to block Noah as he turned to leave, but sharp pain shot through her body, making her repeatedly suck in cold air.
“Alice!” Lucya rushed to Alice's side, worriedly asking, “How are you? Any serious injury…”
“No… no problem, just superficial wounds…” Alice answered through gritted teeth.
Noah stopped, turned back, and said to Alice with deep meaning, “I originally wondered how strong you could be, but now it seems… just this much; I’ve wasted my expectations—tonight, indeed the outstanding adventurers nurtured by this small place Rexum are nothing but empty names; you’d better pray in your heart not to meet me in the tournament, otherwise you’ll become a stepping stone on my path to success.
Boz watched the departing Noah, put on a fake smile, and stepped forward saying, “It looks like the outcome is decided; our guild's Noah has the edge, though Miss Alice's strength is not bad either. I hope we get a chance to spar again in the future. Actually, in four years I've trained three newcomers; Noah is the weakest among them. It's just that your guild's weakness exceeded my imagination. Had I known, I would have sent a substitute to spar. Sorry I overestimated you all. Farewell.
The onlookers glanced sideways, angry but silent; even Alice lost, so them going up would be pointless.
Alice's face flushed then paled; she angrily pounded the floor with her fists, “Damn it!”
“Alice, calm down; this isn't a match, just a spar. Giving that guy a bit of color on the battlefield isn't too late.” Lucya comforted Alice, worried her confidence would suffer.
“I… uh…” Hobbs wiped the sweat from his forehead, sighing, “This Noah is already strong enough to… take off, and he's the weakest of the three newcomers Boz trained? What about the other two—just how terrifying are they?”
This duel was like a warning shot, making all Rexum adventurers wake up.
Lucya had thought the guild had been developing well these past years and was already capable of vying for higher ranks.
Only now did Lucya realize that the traditional powerhouses remain strong, with insurmountable aspects.
Boz, as the president of the world's second‑strongest guild, not only possesses overwhelming personal strength but also harbors grand ambitions.
Many thought that if Boz stepped back to the second line as president, the Cattowitz guild would collapse, with no one capable of fighting—who could have imagined…..
Under Boz's leadership, how terrifying is the Cattowitz guild's blood‑line production! In just four years it has filled the guild with powerhouses!
The three newcomers Boz cultivated, including Noah, are all aces prepared for the tournament; they've stayed hidden all along, only revealing their sharp fangs when the competition approaches, catching other rivals off guard.
Who would have thought that old ginger is still spicy? In terms of patience, the old guild head Taylor surpasses even more, likewise hiding Merlin as his ace, and until now refuses to leak even a bit of information,
Merlin had remained silent all along, but he couldn't help calling out to the departing Noah and Boz, “Wait!”
Noah stopped, turned with puzzlement, “Is there anything else? If it's just for an autograph, forget it—I'm busy….”
“Tsk!” Merlin's mouth twitched twice, thinking, “Who would even want your autograph…”
“Since you came here to spar, I happen to be itching for a fight.
“No—
“Shall we also have a spar?

title: Chapter 16 — Vesteriev
content:
Chapter 16 — Vesteriev

Volume 26 · Chapter 16

When Merlin's words came out, the entire field was shocked.

Everyone stared at Merlin as if he were a lunatic, wondering if he had drunk too much to say such things.

Even the widely-recognized strongest adventurer of the guild, Alice, had not been his match and had been defeated.

How could Merlin, who had been obscure in the guild all along, have the courage to say such words?

Claudia held Chris with a confused look, wondering if this guy was extremely stupid or truly possessed extraordinary talent? Surely he wasn't just trying to play hero?

On the other side, Lucia couldn't watch any longer and shouted loudly, "Mr. Merlin, please calm down!"

Hobbes, on the other hand, loved stirring trouble and poked Merlin in the back. "Getting revenge for your wife? Man enough! I support you, beat that arrogant bastard to death, he he~"

Merlin ignored the idle chatter and instead said in an expectant tone, "How about it? I will be your opponent. If that's not enough, both of you can come at me together."

"Hahahaha!"

Boz suddenly burst out laughing and nodded to Merlin. "I've often heard that the adventurers of Lexhem are all cross-eyed and possess an uncommon talent for comedy; today I have seen for myself."

"Yes, Chairman, I really didn't expect the adventurers of Lexhem to all be comedians." Noel also couldn't help but laugh, then looked at Merlin and said in a contemptuous tone, "Sparring with me?"

"Sorry, you aren't qualified enough."

In the snowy Kingdom of Shasha, there was the small town of Vestyev in the west.

Originally, this was just a remote town in the kingdom, possessing no fame whatsoever apart from producing strong liquor.

But in the past three years, because of the rise of an adventurer, it rapidly attracted the attention of countless people.

Even the Tsar had gone through the trouble of coming here specifically, extending friendly olive branches to recruit her, only to be ruthlessly rejected?

But this did not affect the adventurer's fame at all; she had clearly become a hot figure in the Kingdom of Ice. She was Tanya.

Tanya was originally the daughter of a hunter; her mother had passed away when she was very young.

At age seven, she took up a bow and arrow and followed her father into the forest to hunt, using wits and bravery against wolves and brown bears.

As a girl, she was unexpectedly born with natural divine strength. At a young age, she could pierce through towering trees with a single punch and could even make ferocious brown bears scream repeatedly in pain.

As Tanya grew up, her strength increased eightfold. Without any guidance, she realized the power of battle qi on her own, and at age fourteen, she even taught herself magic without a teacher, fusing two different powers for use.

The peaceful life of hunting with her father every day did not last long. While Tanya and her father were hunting on the mountain, they offended that "Mountain God."

That "Mountain God" was a wind elemental beast that had occupied the mountains for an unknown eternity. It could speak human tongues and communicate with people, but was temperamental, occasionally raising terrifying storms to attack the surrounding villages.

The surrounding villagers were all terrified of that beast, the "Mountain God," and revered it more respectfully as the "Apostle of the Gale."

Tanya and her father accidentally disturbed the sleep of the "Apostle of the Gale." This existence at the peak of the beast hierarchy became immediately enraged, raising a heavenly storm that leveled the forest.

To protect her, Tanya's father died in the storm. From then on, the still underage Tanya was greatly shocked. Her temperament changed completely; she never smiled again, and she became icy cold.

The surviving Tanya began to cultivate bitterly. By the age of eighteen, her strength could only be described as terrifying. She ascended the mountain peak again, tore the "Apostle of the Gale" known as the Mountain God to pieces, and consumed its crystal core.

Because of this battle, Tanya shocked the entire kingdom. The Chairman of Vestyev, Ligachev, took the initiative and went to accept the homeless Tanya, allowing her to start a new life...

After several days of travel, Tanya and her attendant returned to Vestyev City. The city guards saw the hero's return and quickly became excited.

"It's Tanya! Tanya has returned victorious after eliminating the Dark Guild!"

The cries quickly spread throughout the entire town, and a large number of residents rushed to the city gates with prepared gifts.

Naughty children, taking advantage of their size, didn't mind the cold snow and ducked between the adults' legs wanting to see Tanya up close.

Rumble rumble, the heavy city gates were slowly opened. A group of guards lined up in two rows, using spears adorned with flags to form a passage for the nobility; the flags were printed with vivid double-headed griffins.

This was the Tsar's instruction and also respect for Tanya. As long as Tanya appeared on the kingdom's land, she was to be received with noble etiquette.

However, Tanya seemed used to this, walking slowly into the city with her attendant.

The residents became excited seeing Tanya, giving her prepared small gifts: fresh fruit, woven scarves, fine wine, and so on.

The children were even more excited, circling Tanya and calling her name.

Tanya had clearly become the guardian god here, deeply respected, but her gaze was cold, and she ignored everyone, leaving directly.

"Thank you, no need, we don't need it."

The attendant accompanied with a smile, constantly thanking the care of the elders and neighbors, tactfully declining the kindness, then ran a few steps to catch up with Tanya. "Tanya, don't be so cold. At least respond to the people welcoming you so warmly?"

"Why?" Tanya said without looking back.

"Does one even need to ask why? They like you. As the big star of Vestyev, you should get along with the people here," the attendant said lowly.

"I don't think there's any necessity. I haven't done anything for them; why would they like me?" Tanya said expressionlessly and indiffer.

"But in such cold weather, they are willing to come out to welcome you; more or less, you should be more enthusiastic?" The attendant forced a smile, not daring to criticize Tanya much.

"It was their own choice. I never asked them to welcome me; it has nothing to do with me," Tanya said bluntly.

"..." The attendant was full of embarrassment and could only sigh, saying no more.

Just before reaching the guild, Chairman Ligachev had long brought many adventurers to welcome Tanya home.

Ligachev was in his sixties, his hair had gone bald a long time ago, and his curved white beard looked somewhat comical.

He was red-faced, swaying like a bloated barrel, his eyes glazed.

"Welcome back, Tanya of Vestyev, you must have returned victorious after beating those bastards of the Dark Guild into the ground, hic!"

A burp sounded, and a strong smell of alcohol hit everyone. "So smelly, Chairman, how much did you drink?" The attendant rolled their eyes, nearly vomiting, while pinching their nose.

"Not much, not much, he he. In a few days apart, Tanya has become even more beautiful," Ligachev swayed, falling falling into Tanya's bosom after tripping over a stone. His face flushed. "He he~"

"Chairman, don't be like this, I beg you watch your body..." The attendant was full of contempt, seemingly used to Ligachev's personality as a drunk and a lecher.

title: Chapter 17 — Whispers of a Nightmare (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 17 — Whispers of a Nightmare (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 26 · Chapter 17

Viestejef's Adventurers Guild was in an uproar, with Guildmaster Lijagov lying in a wheelchair, his head swollen from a recent beating. The poor old man had been "blasted" by Tanya, and was now half-dead. "Waaaah, I'm so miserable, I didn't do anything wrong, I just... " Lijagov's words were interrupted by his attendant, who sighed in exasperation. Tanya, however, was uninterested in Lijagov's complaints, and instead got straight to the point. "Guildmaster, you called me back here in such a hurry, is it because of the Adventurers' Competition?" Lijagov struggled to sit up, his face apologetic. "Yes, that's right. This time, you need to take it seriously, so I called you back early to prepare." Tanya let out a sigh, her tone unenthusiastic. "Is it really that important?" "Important? Of course it is!" Lijagov exclaimed. "Our guild has been around for over 50 years, and we really need to win this time. You have to try your best, Tanya... " Lijagov's eyes shone with high expectations. "If there aren't any strong opponents, I don't have any interest in participating." Tanya's tone was nonchalant, as if participating was a waste of time. "Don't worry, there will be opponents who will make you happy, I've already heard that many guilds are pulling out all the stops this time. Winning the championship won't be easy for you." Lijagov puffed out his chest, his eyes gleaming with excitement. Tanya rarely heard Lijagov question her abilities, and this was the first time. She looked up, her interest piqued. "Guildmaster, are you trying to motivate me?" "No, I'm serious," Lijagov said, his tone sincere. "The headquarters has been looking for a new Purple-ranked Adventurer this time, and I think you have a good chance of getting it." Lijagov's eyes sparkled with excitement. "That's the Purple-ranked Adventurer, the ultimate goal that many adventurers strive for, but never achieve. You've been an adventurer for several years now, don't you know what it means?" Tanya fell silent, of course she knew what it meant - it meant unparalleled glory, a high social status, and a vast fortune. Even a small guild like theirs could use it to rise to fame. But Tanya didn't want any of that. She wanted to face strong opponents and test her limits. "It seems like you've done a lot of work, Guildmaster, for someone who's always been so laid-back." Lijagov chuckled, patting his bald head. "Don't underestimate me, I'm not as lazy as you think. I was the one who recognized your potential and kept you around." Tanya asked, her curiosity piqued. "Guildmaster, can you tell me more about the opponents I'll be facing in the competition? I want to know what to expect." "Besides the usual suspects, like the new stars and traditional powerhouses, I've also found out about a special opponent." Lijagov's tone was mysterious. "A special opponent?" Tanya raised an eyebrow, her interest piqued. "His name is Merlin. Lucifer. You should keep an eye on him." Lijagov's expression turned serious. "Merlin. Lucifer?" Tanya thought for a moment, but the name meant nothing to her. "The Emperor recently visited the rebuilding France Kingdom and talked to Princess Margaret about the Adventurers' Competition. The Emperor asked Princess Margaret, who would be the strongest adventurer to win the championship?" Lijagov paused, his tone dramatic. "And Princess Margaret said a name that no one had ever heard of before - Merlin. Lucifer, from the city of Rexem. "Oh?" Tanya narrowed her eyes, her voice low. "He must have some extraordinary abilities to catch the attention of the princess." "That's what I think too," Lijagov said, his tone serious. "He's not a strong adventurer at all, in fact, he's just a low-ranking Black-iron. But his wife is a famous Magician, Alice, and she's been making waves lately. He's been relying on her to survive, what a useless... " Lijagov's expression was strange. "Guildmaster, are you sure you're not just joking?" The attendant beside him laughed in exasperation. "I'm not joking!" Lijagov said, his face stern. "Think about it, why would a low-ranking adventurer catch the attention of the princess? Maybe he really does have some extraordinary abilities." "Guildmaster, are you sure it's not just that the princess was charmed by him?" The attendant suggested. "You know, he's got a famous Magician wife, maybe he's just using her to charm the princess." Lijagov furrowed his brow, rubbing his head. "Anyway, that Merlin. Lucifer is a strange one, be careful around him." Tanya snorted in derision. "Guildmaster, don't worry too much." "A clown like him, there's no need to worry about him... " Tanya returned to her home late at night. Her room was unlike any normal girl's, with a single, worn-out bed, a large mirror, and no other furniture. The space was empty, simple to the point of being unsettling. As a 20-something-year-old girl, she had no vanity table, no beautiful wardrobe, and no pretty dresses. Everything was unconventional, unlike her age. The only thing that made the room slightly more lively was the bear skull on the wall, a reminder of her childhood. Tanya had killed the bear in the forest, and her father had praised her, making a keepsake out of it. After her father's death, Tanya had carried it with her everywhere, it was the only thing that reminded her of her childhood. Her clothes and luggage were scattered on the floor, and Tanya sat on the bed, her hands nervously clasped together, her eyes empty. She couldn't sleep, afraid of having nightmares. Tanya had been having the same nightmare every night for seven years since her father's death. A desolate world, a faint voice whispering in her ear, "My child, you are the embodiment of loyalty, you must protect the crown, no one can use it, everything is for the balance..." Every night, Tanya could hear the woman's whisper, making her feel like she was going crazy, even doubting her own humanity. She always thought it was just her own mental health issues, her father's death had left her without a purpose, leading to these strange hallucinations. Tanya still remembered the day she was 14, carrying a bow and arrow, following her father on a hunting trip. The terrifying storm had destroyed everything. Her father had protected her, but was torn apart by the wind, while she had received only minor injuries. From that moment on, Tanya realized her father was weak, fragile, and could be easily injured. She, on the other hand, was like a monster, born with incredible strength, invincible in battle, and it was hard to find opponents who could match her. It was not just a doubt about her humanity, but also a realization that came after her father's death. Tanya's only way to cope with the nightmares was to keep fighting, using the intense fear of death to distract herself from the mysterious woman's whispers. Tanya got up from the bed and walked to the large mirror, taking off her nightgown, staring blankly at her reflection. Her golden hair hung limply on her shoulders. From behind, her shoulder blades were covered in fine, white feathers, like they were just starting to grow, and would eventually become full wings. Tanya's expression twisted in disgust, and she began to scratch at her back, tearing off the tender feathers. A large amount of blood-soaked feathers fell to the ground, piling up at her feet. Maybe she didn't even realize it, but who was she, really?

title: Chapter 18 — Trial
content:
Chapter 18 — Trial

Volume 26 · Chapter 18

Alice lost to the adventurer Nöe from Katowice in the sparring match.

But what really infuriated her was not Alice herself—it was her teacher, Claudia.

Seeing her student lose, Claudia’s lungs nearly burst with rage, her mind more convinced than ever that Alice lacked skill, having no combat experience at all despite her raw power. She didn’t think Alice could handle whatever challenges lay ahead.

Claudia didn’t rush to intervene, instead letting Alice reclaim her dignity. She believed this was the fairest way to settle it—she, as a teacher, shouldn’t interfere, and her impulsive "motherly" protection wasn’t her style.

Second, Alice’s defeat wasn’t entirely her teacher’s fault; most of it was Alice’s own recklessness, taking on an opponent who was far too strong.

Claudia thought letting Alice endure a little suffering wouldn’t be wrong—it would help ease her inflated ego.

Later, Claudia, while Chris was clinging to Merlin in their bedroom, gave Alice a thorough dressing-down alone.

She scolded her for being overconfident, for forgetting everything she’d been taught as a child, for lacking skill, and for even descending into the mountains to share experience with others!

Alice felt like a petty person, deeply hurt—she hadn’t meant to, and it wasn’t because the opponent had an advantage.

Nöe’s strength wasn’t inferior to Alice’s, but he played like a lion, suddenly unleashing attacks that left Alice completely unprepared, losing in confusion. The rules of their duel were confined to a small white circle—a deliberate restriction. She couldn’t fully wield her Saint-tier power, let alone transform into a dragon.

Even drawing a small circle for combat was like restricting the battlefield to a narrow alley, where Alice’s fighting style—open and fluid—wouldn’t adapt well to confined spaces.

Yet for someone like Nöe, who thrived in tight spaces with blistering speed, this was a massive advantage, perfectly letting his power shine.

In that narrow alley, Alice’s mediocre third-tier swordplay clashed against Nöe’s refined, forged-in-a-thousand-battles speedblade—how could she possibly win?

This was just a non-lethal sparring match. If it had been a life-or-death fight, their duel might have been another story entirely.

Alice stormed back, kneeling on the ground, defiant as she faced her teacher’s scolding. "I don’t accept this! Let’s fight again! That tiny circle—where I have no place to dodge! Where could I possibly lose? It’s clearly their plot!"

"Still finding excuses?" Claudia raised her fan and smacked Alice’s head hard.

Alice groaned, covering her head in protest. "You lost, that’s it. No excuses."

Claudia’s face turned dark with fury, feeling her reputation as a teacher ruined by her student’s failure. "You were raised in the Great Snow Mountain under my guidance, and now you’ve become this? My face is ruined by you!"

"I don’t want to be your student anymore," Alice muttered, her tone bitter. "You forced me to learn these things anyway."
