"What did you say?" Claudia scowled, her presence radiating menace.

"...Nothing," Alice muttered, lowering her head under Claudia’s pressure and backing down.

"You gave me so many sword techniques when you were young, yet you forgot everything when facing an enemy. What’s in your head?" Claudia’s frustration was almost palpable. "Tomorrow, let’s find a place. I’ll teach you properly."

"Ah?" Alice froze, stammering, "Don’t need to... I’ve already mastered all the sword techniques from the Great Snow Mountain."

"No, you haven’t," Claudia said sternly, her expression unyielding. "I want you to truly understand the essence of swordplay as a teacher."

Alice’s face paled instantly, trembling in place.

She relived the fear of being controlled by her teacher as a child—

Don’t do this!

Outside, Merlin had sliced an apple, sitting on the couch to play with little Chris.

Little Chris, leaning on her tiny legs beneath the couch, bounced around, trying to reach the apple Merlin had cut.

"Want one?"

"Want~"

Merlin looked at the apple in her hand, then at the child, "Call Daddy."

"Daddy~!" Chris giggled and called.

"Good girl, come here. My little princess." Merlin picked Chris up, placing her on her lap.

Chris held the apple in her tiny hands and began eating, her cheeks puffing up like a store rat. "Daddy, Mommy..."

"...Did we talk about a lot of things?" Merlin smiled awkwardly, knowing Alice had been scolded.

"I always thought Mommy was strong, but today I was defeated. I feel so uncomfortable..." Chris’s mood had darkened.

"Stupid kid," Merlin gently patted Chris’s head. "Sparring is just practice—it’s not real combat. You shouldn’t have accepted the challenge today. The opponent was clearly better prepared than you."

"But... why didn’t you help Mommy?" Chris raised her head, curious.

"Sparring is for one-on-one. Interfering would break the rules. Do you think I didn’t want to help her?" Merlin paused, then continued, "If it were a different match, I’d step in."

"Really?" Chris nodded, though still sulking. "But Mommy was treated unfairly. Chris doesn’t like it."

"You’re too young to worry about this."

Merlin smiled, stroking Chris’s hair softly. "If there’s an opportunity, I’ll teach that person who hurt your mommy a lesson."

The next day, Claudia brought Alice to a mountain top near Recklesham.

Claudia stood facing away from Alice, gazing down at the tiny Recklesham village below.

Alice watched her teacher’s back, feeling a biting cold wind.

Was it the mountain’s chill or the cold radiating from her teacher?

Alice hesitated, shivering slightly. "Teacher! I’ve already mastered all the sword techniques from the Great Snow Mountain. No need to teach me anymore. It’s too cold here—I’ll go back?"

"You’ve come this far—why retreat now? You’re a useless student."

Claudia turned to face her, slowly drawing her sword—a blade about three feet long, its surface gleaming like autumn water, though its material was unknown, yet far from common. "Come, draw it."

"I want to show you how reckless it is to descend into the mountains."

title: Chapter 19 — The Mysterious East Asian Swordcraft
content:
Chapter 19 — The Mysterious East Asian Swordcraft

Volume 26 · Chapter 19

Alice coughed up a mouthful of blood, sent flying backward, her slender sword clattering to the ground.

She glanced back, seeing the sheer cliff face behind her, a few stones tumbling down without even an echo.

Alice's face turned deathly pale, her eyes flashing with resentment as she glared at her teacher, Clodia. Is this what you call training? You're trying to kill me!

In just a few rounds, Alice had been beaten to a pulp by Clodia, who spoke of training but inflicted wounds far worse than those from Noe.

Alice had to focus completely; the slightest lapse in attention could mean death under her teacher's sword.

This pressure made Alice feel like her teacher disliked her, wanted her dead.

"Teacher... enough! Is this... training? What kind of teacher are you?!"

"Go easy on you? Hmph!" Clodia approached, sword in hand, her voice cold. "I think I was too lenient with you before, letting you neglect the sword techniques of the Great Snow Mountain. You're not a child anymore; I won't be soft on you!"

.....

Alice struggled to her feet, her body covered in wounds, unwilling to accept her teacher's special training.

But Alice's mind worked quickly, her eyes turning serious as she spoke with righteous indignation.

"It's getting late, Chris must be hungry, I need to go feed her. Teacher, you can stay here if you want."

"Don't make me laugh. That barren land of yours wouldn't have milk even in dreams..." Clodia retorted, dashing cold water on Alice's words.

"Teacher!!!" Alice gritted her teeth, feeling this was the greatest insult to her as a mother.

"Angry? Still just a little girl..." Clodia sneered, picking up the sword Hikari Elegy from the ground, her tone meaningful. "I have many swords hidden under my bed, yet you chose this one? It seems to suit you well..."

"Huh?" Alice furrowed her brow, not understanding her teacher's words.

Clodia tossed the slender sword Hikari Elegy at Alice's feet, assuming a stance again. "Pick up the sword, Alice! You're complaining about just a few surface wounds? After two years outside, this is all you've got?"

Alice seethed at Clodia's "surface wounds" comment. This is what you call surface wounds? I feel like my bones are about to break!

She couldn't understand why, despite surpassing the Saint-tier, she couldn't defeat Clodia.

Alice picked up the sword, forcing herself to speak under the pressure.

"Teacher, I don't want to fight you anymore. I obviously can't win! Do you enjoy bullying me like this?"

"Ha, finally admitting the truth? My foolish student." Clodia laughed dryly. "Weren't you confident earlier, wanting to force me away with your strength?"

"Evil..." Alice bit her lip, feeling her teacher was destroying not just her body but her spirit too.

"Alice, do you know why you can't defeat me?" Clodia's expression suddenly turned serious.

"You... you've been hiding your true strength, right? You're not just at the Saint-tier level!"

"No... my strength is genuinely at the Saint-tier, and it's true that I'm not as strong as you." Clodia said with a hint of a smile.

"Huh?" Alice was confused. So after surpassing the Saint-tier, I'm actually weaker than someone at the Saint-tier? What kind of logic is this?

"You made a serious mistake in your training, Alice. If you had stayed on the Great Snow Mountain, I would have never let you break through the Saint-tier. I would have kept you at that level."

"...What do you mean? I've been getting stronger, is that wrong?" Alice asked, unable to understand.

"The Saint-tier is the lifelong goal for many, and the Realm of Saints is a domain only a few lucky ones can enter. Many people call the process from Saint-tier to Realm of Saints a restrictive shackle, but that's wrong." Clodia explained gently, hoping Alice would understand the magnitude of her mistake.

"...Really?" Alice was astonished, feeling like she was hearing about an unknown realm.

"The process from Saint-tier to Realm of Saints, though extremely difficult, is not a shackle. If utilized properly, it becomes a help on the path of cultivation." Clodia paused, explaining seriously, "Cultivation is about accumulating power, like blowing up a balloon. The more power accumulated, the more the balloon expands, and at a certain point, it will burst – that's the breakthrough of power limits."

"...". Alice furrowed her brow, feeling like she was hearing a new interpretation of cultivation.

"Power limits are like the balloon itself. Without accumulating enough power and forcing a breakthrough, it's like a deflated balloon – there won't be much of an impact." Clodia looked at Alice, speaking patiently. "Think about it, if during the breakthrough from Saint-tier to Realm of Saints, you suppressed and accumulated your power, making the balloon of power limits burst, would the power you gain now compare to a careless breakthrough?"

"Ah!" Alice had an epiphany, her mind filled with the image of a balloon exploding with multiplied force, shattering her understanding of cultivation.

"Someone who accumulates great power to break through to the Realm of Saints will have a solid foundation, with magic and qi as firm as a rock, and be stronger than ordinary Realm of Saints cultivators. You wasted a chance to build a good foundation, Alice." Clodia paused, smiling. "To be honest, I had the ability to break through the Saint-tier at twenty-seven, but I didn't rush. I suppressed my power and accumulated it until today."

"I see...". Alice finally understood, realizing she had made a mistake in her cultivation. Many people struggled to break through the Saint-tier's shackles to enter the Realm of Saints, never realizing this shackle was an opportunity to build a solid foundation.

"Now you should understand why your Realm of Saints power can't defeat me. If I were to break through the Saint-tier's shackles now and unleash decades of accumulated power, you would be even more desperate." Clodia said with a hint of a smile.

"...". Alice felt defeated inside, finally acknowledging that despite surpassing her teacher, she was still inferior.

"Alice, lift your head. Don't be discouraged. Even though you missed the chance to build a foundation, you can still make up for it." Clodia looked at Alice, speaking slowly.

"The sword techniques of the Great Snow Mountain originated from the mysterious East.

"When I was young, I met an old man with white hair but a youthful face, and I learned a unique sword technique from him.

"That old man had extraordinary knowledge about tempering the body, allowing one to build a strong foundation and become one with heaven and earth.

"In his words, the world's two great power systems, magic and qi, weren't called that. Instead, he called them 'qi' and 'shin'."

title: Chapter 20 — Another Humanoid Dragon (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 20 — Another Humanoid Dragon (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 26 · Chapter 20

"Qi and Shen?" Alice heard this nonsensical phrase for the first time.

"Qi-tempered body, Shen-tempered soul—all things are the shocking power of heaven and earth used to strengthen oneself. That old gentleman taught me this, completely overturning my childhood understanding of cultivation." Claudia paused, emphasizing, "We usually train only to break through our limits and increase our strength, but have we ever considered making good use of the suppression those limits place on us? If I hadn’t met that old gentleman, I might never have discovered this secret. Though... there are those who uncover it without guidance—one can only call that true genius..."

"Uh... are you telling the truth?" Alice asked doubtfully. After all, encountering a mysterious old man as a child sounded too fantastical.

"Of course. I will teach you the true Great Snow Mountain Extreme Frost Sword Style and help you improve your fundamentals through sparring." Claudia raised the three-foot sword in her hand and said seriously, "You are human, Alice, not a dragon. Don’t always rely on the power of the dragon race to crush your opponents—that will make you lose yourself. The profound art of swordsmanship has been a martial art shared by gods and men since creation, far surpassing brute force in..."

After listening to Claudia’s teachings, Alice finally chose not to retreat any longer. She too raised her sword.

"Please, Teacher!"

---

Far from the densely populated towns, deep within the mountains, lay the great waterfall of Maghermo.

The area was sparsely populated, with almost no towns nearby—only a few small villages.

It was said that most who came here did so for hunting, and few ever approached the waterfall in the mountains.

Yet it was here, in this secluded place, that the long-missing old Guild President Taylor had brought his son Karl for secret training.

Old Taylor had drawn inspiration from Merlin’s Iaijutsu, integrating it into his family’s Thunderclap Close Combat Style to refine and create the Thunderclap Hand Blade Technique.

With its overwhelming lethal power, it had shone in battles against Merlin’s subordinates, filling Old Taylor with pride. He decided to continue refining it and teach it to his son Karl.

The Taylor family’s Thunderclap Close Combat Style was already renowned for its "swift ferocity," but after evolving into the Thunderclap Hand Blade Technique, its destructive power had increased tenfold—surpassing even Saint-tier martial arts.

Thus, Old Taylor placed great importance on this new technique. With the Adventurers Guild Tournament approaching, he hoped Karl would master it and use it to defeat strong opponents in the competition.

The waterfall’s water roared down from the sky, crashing with earth-shaking force—

Karl, bare-chested, stood beneath the waterfall, enduring the immense pressure of the cascading water without budging an inch.

His eyes were closed, his blood surging beneath his skin, turning it red, as if he had entered some special state.

Old Taylor, leaning on his cane, stood on a rock below the waterfall, his gaze fixed deeply on Karl, as if waiting for something.

Suddenly, Karl’s eyes snapped open in fury, his golden fighting spirit surging. He pressed his fingers together and swung with all his might at the waterfall before him—

"HAAAAH!!!"

With a mighty shout, the waterfall seemed to be sliced by a blade, splitting cleanly in half as if severed at the waist!

This bizarre spectacle, though magnificent, lasted only a second before vanishing.

Karl was overjoyed. He swept back his soaking wet hair and proudly shouted to his father, "How’s that? I’ve mastered it! Doesn’t seem that hard!"

"Hmph, you’re still far off..." Old Taylor shook his head, feeling Karl’s ability to sever the waterfall was insufficient. "You only held it for a second. At least three seconds would be passing. Otherwise, how will you fight against other guild members?"

"That’s a bit much, isn’t it? I know my old rivals well—with my current strength, I can definitely beat them!" Karl said confidently.

"Don’t get cocky. Our goal isn’t just the top 100—it’s the championship." Old Taylor paused, lowering his voice. "Four years ago, only you and Relf participated. Though Relf has passed, our guild has since gained two powerful allies—Merlin and Alice. We’re stronger now than ever before. If we only manage the top 100 again, wouldn’t that waste their contributions?"

Karl fell silent, his mood darkening as he thought of his fallen comrade, Relf.

"Karl, you are my son. Whether our family’s combat style thrives in the future depends on you." Old Taylor spoke with gravity.

"I know, I know. You’ve said that countless times already." Karl replied impatiently.

"I’ve experienced Merlin’s power firsthand. To be honest, it’s terrifyingly overwhelming. I’ve never seen such deadly killing intent in my life. I can’t even imagine anyone surviving that kind of attack. There’s much to learn from him." Old Taylor said seriously.

"Yeah, I used to think Iaijutsu was all show and no substance, but Merlin completely shattered that notion. How did he manage to train it to such perfection?" Karl couldn’t help but exclaim.

"And then there’s Alice. She’s improved at an astonishing speed in such a short time. I think... she’s already reached a realm I could never hope to attain in my lifetime." Old Taylor sighed deeply.

"Really?" Karl froze, looking at his own hands. "Actually, I’ve been feeling lately like I’ve hit a wall. It’s as if something is blocking my progress."

"Karl, you’re not old yet. There’s still time. Who knows? Maybe in this lifetime, you’ll even surpass Saint-tier. That would make you the first in our family’s history." Old Taylor encouraged him.

"Don’t worry, old man. I’ll do my best." Karl smiled, then changed the subject. "Merlin and Alice are so strong. I can’t fall behind. If I let them steal all the spotlight, it’ll be embarrassing for me as their senior."

"Hahaha, Merlin will surely make a stunning debut in this tournament. It might even shock the judges from headquarters, forcing them to reconsider the current adventurer ranking system. It won’t have been in vain that I kept Merlin hidden for so long. It’s time for everyone to see what Rektham is truly capable of." Old Taylor paused before continuing, "Judging adventurers solely by magic and fighting spirit strength is far too one-dimensional. It creates unfair situations like Merlin’s. I used to think no one would waste time on useless techniques, but now it seems some do—and they’ve even mastered them to an unimaginable degree."

Karl sighed quietly to himself. "With Merlin around, the championship is practically in the bag. All my hard work feels pointless."

"Don’t think like that. This tournament won’t be as easy as you imagine. To be safe, we can’t rely entirely on Merlin and Alice." Old Taylor said with concern.

"What? Do you mean there’s a worrying opponent in this tournament?" Karl asked in surprise.

"I’ve known Gregory, the Guild President of London, for a long time. He’s extremely confident this time—he’s only sending one participant..." Old Taylor raised his head and spoke slowly.

"A Secret Silver-ranked adventurer named Aeria. She’s Gregory’s carefully cultivated successor for the guild."

"I’ve heard..."

"Like Alice, she’s also a humanoid dragon. Her strength is not to be underestimated."

title: Chapter 21 — Dragon-Transforming Warrior Aelia
content:
Chapter 21 — Dragon-Transforming Warrior Aelia

Volume 26 · Chapter 21

“Human-shaped dragon?” Karl blinked, surprised, asking, “Isn’t it like Alice—able to transform into a fierce dragon?”

“Yeah, that’s right. It’s said that way, but I don’t know how old Grégory the old coot managed to raise it.”

Old Taylor lowered his head, speaking seriously, “That old bastard has a deep city mind and full confidence to send a newbie to compete—definitely someone who’s hard to handle. You’d better be careful.”

“Sounds interesting. I wonder who between this human-shaped dragon and Alice is stronger? I’m kind of looking forward to seeing them compete.” Karl rubbed his chin.

“Can’t say for sure,” Old Taylor said thoughtfully, “Since it’s Grégory’s personal protégé, it’s bound to have impressive strength—otherwise, the other adventurers in the London Guild wouldn’t be bothered.”

---

In the borderlands of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, surrounded by mountains, the area was poorly connected but had a few villages resting there.

Though nearly cut off from the outside world, merchants still came from dangerous mountain paths to trade with villagers for essentials, exchanging them for crops and animal furs.

But during the season when monsters from across the world were unusually active, this village became extremely dangerous, constantly facing monster attacks.

Especially since it sat on the borderlands with no large number of guards stationed there to defend against monsters, if the attacks were fierce enough, every villager would become a meal for the monsters.

The village elder refused to wait passively, so he had assembled a militia of young and strong men in the village. During the monster-active season, the entire village would be on high alert, constantly vigilant against monster attacks.

The militia would train every morning at the village’s church center, but these farmers—who lacked magic and martial skills—were ordinary people. They could handle small-scale monster raids, but if a monster tide or a powerful monster came, they’d have no choice but to die.

Fortunately, this border village had a good relationship with the London Adventurers Guild. As long as they paid roughly the same amount, the Guild would send strong adventurers to assist the villagers in protecting the village, allowing them to survive.

Yet, the elder’s request for aid had been sent for over a month, and no support from the London adventurers had arrived yet—no one knew what had gone wrong.

The villagers, fearing the delay, had been living in constant anxiety for days, worrying about frequent and increasingly fierce monster attacks. From Grégory’s reply, it was revealed that the sent adventurers were newbies, their first mission, with little experience, hoping the elder would take good care of them.

This made the elder furious. They’d already paid, handing over the lives of dozens of households to a single new adventurer—wasn’t this just a joke?

---

Great Britain’s second-ranked Knight of Thorns, Sith.

A few months ago, Sith had participated in the campaign to suppress the rebellion in the Kingdom, then took a rest before leaving London on his own to continue his travels, hoping to further improve his strength.

Sith hadn’t listened to Eldrick the Great Blade’s advice to return the demon armor he’d stolen from the Mermore Treasure, instead stubbornly keeping it. He showed no intention of giving it back.

It wasn’t that Sith didn’t want to return it—he needed that power as a Knight of Thorns!

Without the demon armor’s strength, his own abilities would be severely weakened, barely making it into the ranks of the Knight of Thorns.

As a Knight of Thorns, Sith had the duty to protect the Kingdom and safeguard Queen Elizabeth.

So even if he’d heard Eldrick’s advice, he wouldn’t willingly give up the demon’s power.

Recently, the demon armor’s appetite had grown worse, demanding more blood and meat to feed. If it weren’t careful, it might even devour its "owner"—Sith himself.

Sith had originally planned to continue his journey south, but by chance, he passed through this border village on his way. He carried a heavy box with the armor on his back, gasping for breath as he approached the guards at the checkpoint, who were blocking a small, short girl.

The guard said, “Sorry, it’s a restricted period. Suspicious individuals aren’t allowed inside the village.”

The girl said, “I’m the adventurer you hired from London, here to assist you in protecting the village.”

The guard said, “Please show us your adventurer credentials so we can verify your identity.”

The girl said, “I lost them on the way.”

The guard said, “Then important things can be lost? We can’t confirm your identity, so we can’t let suspicious individuals enter.”

The girl repeated the same words over and over, making the guards feel like she had a low IQ.

Not just because she looked suspicious, but also because she was short and a bit childish, seeming like she couldn’t possibly be a powerful adventurer. Usually, the adventurers sent to assist had been tall and imposing, but now a tiny girl claimed to be the one—making the villagers doubt her.

Sith watched from behind as the situation unfolded. Hearing “London adventurer,” his interest piqued.

Though Sith rarely communicated with adventurers, he knew some of the well-known ones from London.

So he walked forward, carrying his black box, and took a closer look at the tiny girl.

She didn’t seem to have lost her childishness, her bright eyes sharp, her short green hair neat, and she wore a windbreaker. Her outfit looked like that of a weary traveler, but two small brown horns sprouted from her head in the springtime hair.

Sith froze when he saw the girl’s horns. He thought, *Of course the guards wouldn’t let her in—what kind of monster with horns would they let through?* Was this a human child?

The girl noticed a filthy man staring at her and, without fear, lifted her head to meet his gaze. “Staring—”

“Hmph!” Sith coughed to cover his shock and asked softly, “Little sister…”

“I’m already an adult, older than your mother,” the girl said without expression.

“...Sith felt uneasy inside and forced a weak smile. “Big sister, aren’t you human?”

“No, I’m human,” the girl said, tapping her horns. “These are dragon horns. Because I’m too strong, they’ve been eroded.”

“Huh?”

Sith’s face grew awkward, thinking, *What nonsense is she spouting here? Did she just boast about being so strong that her horns were eaten away?*

Was this some kind of mentally ill child?

Sith tried to steady his emotions and spoke in a childlike tone. “You say you’re a London adventurer? No joke, right? What’s your name?”

The girl stared at Sith’s eyes for a moment, giving a blank response.

“Alice.”

“Silver-haired adventurer Alice.”

“Dragonborn warrior Alice.”

“London Guild’s Transparent Alice.”

title: Chapter 22 — Rice Bucket
content:
Chapter 22 — Rice Bucket

Volume 26 · Chapter 22

“…Alice?” Sace tried hard to think, never having heard of a person like this in the Adventurers Guild of London. “Lying isn’t a good habit.”

“I’m not lying, I’m an adventurer from London.” Alice kept a straight face and said seriously.

Sace’s expression turned strange, wondering if the little dwarf in front of him had a mental problem, or if he was a lost child of the other race.

“You’re not trustworthy at all. I’m also from London, among the silver‑mined adventurers, I’ve never heard your name. If you truly are a powerful adventurer from London, I would have at least a hint of an impression.”

“Oh! A fellow countryman!” Alice lifted her head, eyes full of tiny stars, staring at Sace as if she had found a lifeline.

“What kind of fellow countryman? You’re actually a lost child of the other race, right? Hurry up and find your own parents. The human kingdom isn’t a place where little other‑race scoundrels can just wander in.” Sace said seriously.

“Don’t treat me like a child. I’m the successor designated by Professor Gregory!” Alice said seriously.

“Ah? You know Gregory?” Sace stared, feeling the little kid with horns on his head even more mysterious.

“That’s right, I’m the only student of Professor Gregory.” Alice kept a straight face, asked in a cold voice, “You talk to me with a lofty attitude, what are you?”

“Me?” Sace’s face turned black, feeling the little devil in front of him was a bit arrogant, speaking in a harsh tone, so he replied, “I am the second‑ranked Sace of the Twelve Thorns Knights of Britain. If you’re an adventurer from London, you must have heard of me.”

D factory small…

Alice stared at Sace for a while, then turned her head away, “Sorry, I haven’t heard of you. I never remember the names of cats and dogs.”

“…What did you say!?” Sace gritted his teeth, thinking, why is this little devil so arrogant! He’s often away from the capital, but he’s not that unknown, right?

“Although I haven’t heard of a Sace in the Thorns Knights, I’ve heard a little about the Violet Thorns Knights.” Alice said without expression.

“…” Sace secretly breathed a sigh of relief, thinking that the Violet Thorns Knights had no presence, but he still knew something.

But Sace’s heart was still not at ease. Alice, on the other hand, added an inappropriate comment, “The Violet Thorns Knights are all a bunch of vegetables gathering together, forming a useless group. Most of them are just cannon fodder. As for the Thorns Knights? They’re the big ones chosen from the dwarves, they’re useless.”

“Phew!” Sace almost spat out old blood, the veins on his forehead pounding, “You’re full of nonsense, little devil. I see you’re full of lies, no truth at all. Since you’re a student of Master Gregory, do you know what he used to do?”

“Wasn’t he a court mage? The master told me…” Alice answered casually.

“Uh!” Sace was startled, his heart could not calm down.

Does he know this?

In theory, Master Gregory was a court mage of the kingdom, and only a few would know this.

Could this little devil not be lying…

Since Alice had some knowledge of Gregory’s past, her claim of being a London adventurer and Gregory’s student became more credible, even Sace’s mind believed it about seven or eight percent.

So Sace showed the Thorns Knight medal, proving his identity, and then brought Alice in.

The militia guarding the checkpoint saw that the man in front of them was a noble Thorns Knight of Britain, and they were overjoyed, rushing to report to the village chief.

Because the monster beasts were frequently invading, the arrival of a well‑known strongman was great news for all villagers. Even if the hired adventurer didn’t arrive, as long as Sace was there, they could ask for his help to guard the village.

Moreover, Gregory’s reply said the dispatched adventurer was a newcomer, even needing the villagers’ care. Compared to the famous Thorns Knight, most people preferred to trust Sace, because no one wanted to give their name to a brand‑new, inexperienced adventurer.

E novel

Sace led Alice into the village, his heart not fully trusting this guy, because he had lost an important adventurer’s proof for the first time, seeing such a careless adventurer.

“You’re telling the truth, right? You’re a student of Master Gregory. If you lie to me, I won’t let you go easily.”

“What? You brought me in, but you still doubt me? Wouldn’t you go back to Britain and ask my teacher? Alice glanced at Sace’s face, silently saying, “You look like a shrewd guy, but your words are so foolish.”

“Uh…

Sace held back his inner dissatisfaction, looking at Alice’s short stature like a child, but when she spoke, she was old‑fashioned.

Every sentence was sharp, making communication uncomfortable.

But Sace thought that Alice’s relaxed response would let him verify with Master Gregory, so there should be no problem, right?

“How did you lose such an important adventurer’s proof? That thing represents the honor of adventurers, comparable to one’s own life, doesn’t it?”

“I lied. My silver‑mined adventurer’s proof wasn’t lost, it was sold by me…” Alice suddenly answered sincerely.

“Ah! You sold it!” Sace stared in shock, as if hearing something incredible.

“Yes, I ran out of money halfway, I was so hungry. The adventurer’s proof was made of silver, it had some value, right? You understand….” Alice paused, expressionless, said, “What honor? It’s not important, it didn’t fill my stomach.”

Sace’s gaze on Alice became increasingly strange, thinking that because his stomach was hungry, he sold the important silver adventurer’s proof without hesitation. Other adventurers see the proof as honor, but this little devil treats it as dung! How clueless an adventurer! Never heard of such a thing!

“The silver‑mined adventurer’s proof isn’t as valuable as imagined. The rare magic bracelet, the hidden cloak, the instant teleportation scroll that the master gave me… all are worth much more than that broken card.” Alice’s expression was calm, as if saying it was a trivial matter, everything that could be sold was sold, exchanged for food, but it wasn’t enough to fill my teeth, I was still hungry, I want to eat enough…

“Ah…” Sace stared in disbelief, not knowing how to communicate with this freak, his mind could not calm down for a long time.

Rare magic bracelet, hidden cloak, instant teleportation scroll…

These are super rare, valuable magic items!

To fill his stomach; he sold everything, but still didn’t eat enough?

What was Master Gregory thinking? He clearly raised a “food bucket”!

!!( n°))

title: Chapter 23 — Glutton
content:
Chapter 23 — Glutton

Volume 26 · Chapter 23

Seth's expression grew increasingly strange as he stared at Alice with a complex mix of emotions, unable to discern any unique qualities about her, but clearly recognizing her as a worthless person who would sell her adventurer's proof just because she was hungry. A person who was so clueless that they would sell their proof and become a haphazard adventurer. It was almost laughable that she was a student of Gregory the Master. Seth began to wonder if Gregory's eyes were blind, as he couldn't see any exceptional qualities in this little brat. “.....Alice let out a deep sigh, looking at her completely undeveloped and childish body, “I'm envious of those girls at the tavern, chatting and drinking, and just lying down to earn money, next time when I'm hungry, I don't know if I can sell myself..... “Shut up! You scum! Stop talking or it's a crime!” Seth was frightened, his face pale, thinking that this little brat's brain was indeed problematic, and she could even sell herself to fill her stomach? Gregory the Master would take in such a confused person as a student? It was unbelievable! “Hey, hey~” Alice pulled on Seth's pant leg, looking at him with a serious face, “Go get some food, I'm hungry... Seth's face turned black, speaking seriously, “Figure it out yourself, I don't owe you anything. “But after I sold my adventurer's proof, these villagers don't believe me anymore, originally, when I came here, they could treat me well, and I could eat to my heart's content. Alice showed a pitiful expression, looking down at her small stomach. “Now it's too late... Seth's forehead had a few black lines slide down, and he was speechless, thinking that the person who was revered as the secret silver adventurer, had fallen to such a state? “Why don't you help me out? Prove to the villagers that I'm the adventurer they hired, then they'll treat me well... Alice spoke expressionlessly, lifting her head, her eyes filled with longing for food, already determined to live off the villagers for free. “Just relying on a single word, how can these villagers easily believe it?” Seth said, his face flushed with embarrassment. “You're the Thorn Knight, aren't you? They'll believe you, and then you'll obediently bring back the good food from your home?” Alice spoke seriously. “You're... Seth furrowed his brow, “Not to protect the village, but to go after the villagers' food? Those villagers are unlucky, why did they have to encounter you, such an adventurer? “Eat your fill, and live a good life, that's the natural order.” Alice grabbed Seth's pant leg, speaking expressionlessly, “You brought me here, so you have to take responsibility... “....” Seth suddenly felt a significant amount of pressure, thinking that he shouldn't have gotten involved, now this little troublemaker was stuck to him. - - Gregory the Master, why would he send out such an immature adventurer to execute the task? Wouldn't... it be because he couldn't afford to keep them, so he intentionally let them fend for themselves? Just then, a group of militiamen, armed with simple armor and farming tools, surrounded an elderly man. This elderly man was the village elder of the border village, who had heard that the Thorn Knight had arrived, and hurried over to greet him. Because the adventurers hired from London were late, the village elder had given up waiting, and instead sought help from the suddenly arrived Thorn Knight. The militiamen who had been guarding the checkpoint pointed at Seth and said, “Village elder, that's him.” The elderly village elder looked at Seth, his face filled with tears, and approached him, asking, “Sir, are you the Thorn Knight from the British Kingdom?” “I am.” Seth hesitated, nodding his head. “Good! The Goddess of Light hasn't abandoned us!” The village elder prayed devoutly, thinking that the benevolent goddess had sent a strong warrior to this border village, giving everyone hope to live. After praying, the village elder “thud” fell to his knees, his expression sincere, and begged Seth, even the militiamen behind him also knelt down. “Knight, please, save us! “Ah!” Seth saw this scene, and was startled, “What's going on? Get up quickly. The village elder, with the militiamen's help, slowly stood up, speaking sorrowfully, “Knight, I must confess, our village has been attacked by the monsters, and we've suffered dozens of casualties, the villagers are anxious, and some have even written their wills, preparing to meet their end with the monsters, now the monsters still won't give up, and if we continue like this, we... might become the monsters' food.” Seth secretly glanced at Alice beside him, thinking that this little brat... was just eating and drinking on the road, and hadn't taken the task of protecting the border village seriously? Look at how she had driven the villagers to the point of writing their wills. “Knight, please save us, help us protect our home, if you're here, our entire village, men and women, old and young, will...” The village elder's emotions were intense, and he regarded Seth as the savior of the village, “Actually, we had already hired adventurers from London, but they haven't arrived yet, they completely disregarded us, I'll definitely complain to the Adventurer's Guild about the London Guild's evil deeds!” “Then...” Seth's forehead had a few black lines slide down, speaking awkwardly, “Actually, the adventurers who are supporting you have already arrived.” “Ah? ? ?” The village elder was suddenly stunned, looking at Seth with a puzzled expression, “Where? I haven't received any news at all?” “That one.” Seth pointed at Alice, who was holding onto his pant leg. The village elder looked down, and saw the small Alice, who was blinking her big eyes at him, her expressionless face like a proud little devil. “This... this is the adventurer sent by the London Guild to support us? ! A child who hasn't even grown teeth, and yet they want to come and help us fight against the monsters? What a joke! Just because we offered them a lower reward, they look down on us? Sending a child to support us, it's just a way to humiliate us! The village elder's face turned black, his heart filled with disappointment towards the London Adventurer's Guild, and he even thought that they were playing a trick on him. “This... oSE2 small thing, Alice didn't know what the village elder was thinking? She only knew that she had proven her identity, and could now eat her fill. She looked up, her mouth wide open, and said, “I'm Alice! I'm strong! Feed me quickly! The village elder, at his home, learned that Alice was the adventurer sent to support them, although he didn't want to, but he still treated her with courtesy. However, at the dinner table, the village elder's face turned into a tomato, his old body shaking, and he was frightened by the sight before him. Even Seth was in a state of stunned silence, from start to finish, he hadn't eaten a single bite, and was staring at Alice with an incredulous expression. The bowls on the table were overflowing, and the bowls on the ground were stacked up like skyscrapers, the originally spacious room was even unable to accommodate anyone to stand. Alice, although young, had a shocking appetite that stunned everyone. She ate alone, and consumed half a year's worth of food for the entire village! Watching her, the village elder and Seth were shocked, thinking that this... this was a worthless person! ! ! Don't eat anymore, leave some food for others!

title: Chapter 24 — Demon Training (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 24 — Demon Training (Extra Chapter)

Volume 26 · Chapter 24

Aria devoured her food with reckless abandon, transforming the once-peaceful dining table into a battlefield. She didn't chew her food, instead swallowing it whole as if afraid someone would snatch it away. The table quickly became a mess of empty bowls, and Aria's small stomach swelled noticeably. Her tiny frame seemed disproportionate to the massive amount of food she had consumed, leaving everyone wondering where it all went.

Aria let out a satisfied belch, patted her bloated belly, and smiled contentedly. She had no idea how long she had been hungry, but she had eaten enough of the villagers' food to last half a year before finally stopping.

"...This is..." Seth's face contorted in shock as he stared at Aria, who was now incoherent. Was she here to help protect the village, or to add fuel to the fire? The village was already in a dire situation, and now she had consumed half a year's worth of food. How were the villagers supposed to survive?

The elderly village chief was terrified, having initially thought Aria wouldn't eat much. But this small girl had an enormous appetite, unlike anything he had ever seen before.

Aria spotted the untouched steak on Seth's plate and, standing on her chair, snatched it with her small hand and swallowed it whole before Seth could react. After finishing the last of the food on the table, Aria collapsed onto her chair, limp and motionless.

"You...?" Seth's eyes widened in disbelief as he asked sternly, "Are you a food bucket?"

"My teacher says that too," Aria replied proudly, "but being able to eat my fill every meal is the ultimate goal of a food bucket!"

Aria suddenly yawned, jumped down from the chair, and mumbled, "I'm full, so I'll take a nap. Don't disturb me tomorrow; I have a terrible temper when I wake up."

"You eat and then sleep? You're a pig!" Seth exclaimed, his stomach growling with hunger while Aria had eaten her fill. "Shouldn't you be discussing how to protect the village? That's your mission!"

"Who cares about that? Don't bother me," Aria waved her hand dismissively and left to find a room to sleep in.

"...This scoundrel..." Seth's forehead throbbed with frustration, wondering if Aria had any sense of responsibility at all. She had eaten the villagers' food and then left without a care, like a bandit.

After Aria left, the elderly village chief finally broke down, kneeling with a thud. "Sir Knight, please save us! Our village is not only surrounded by monsters, but we're also running out of food! It's not just the monsters eating our crops; we might all starve to death!"

"Uh..."

Seth wiped the sweat from his brow, feeling the weight of responsibility. "It wasn't me who ate it..."

"Didn't you bring her here?" the village chief asked, tears streaming down his face.

Seth's face darkened, regretting his decision to get involved. The village chief's words made sense – Aria's appetite was unsustainable, and it was possible that Master Gregory had sent her away because he couldn't afford to feed her.

"Sir Knight, we can only rely on your kindness to protect us now. If you abandon us, we're doomed. The adventurer from London has made things worse, and we can't even defend the village..." The village chief pleaded.

Seth remained silent, thinking deeply. As a knight, he couldn't ignore the situation, especially since he had brought Aria into the village, leading to their potential famine.

Taking a deep breath, Seth declared, "Don't worry, I'll stay in the village until the monster tide passes."

Meanwhile, on a distant mountain peak far from Rexham, the landscape had transformed into a frozen wasteland. The summit had been plagued by relentless snowstorms and thunderous roars for days.

Claudia and Alice clashed swords, their figures weaving in and out of the blizzard. Alice collapsed, exhausted, her body covered in wounds that, while severe, were not life-threatening. This showcased the intensity of Claudia's training, which far surpassed Merlin's methods.

Although Claudia was strict, she knew exactly how far to push Alice, making her endure pain without risking her life.

Claudia turned slowly, raising her sword again. "Get up, Alice! This isn't enough to give up! You must learn the true Snow Mountain swordsmanship, and suffering is necessary. Keep pushing yourself, and you'll reach new heights!"

Alice's stubborn nature refused to let her give up, despite the countless times she had been knocked down. She struggled to her feet, determined to face her unbeatable teacher and not let her efforts go to waste.

"Good, Alice," Claudia said, standing amidst the howling storm. "Though you're a bit foolish, diligence can make up for it. If others can do something once, you should put in ten times the effort to achieve the same result!"

Alice had been training relentlessly for days, leaving her daughter Chris at home, who missed her mother dearly. Even Merlin found it hard to resist Chris's pleas and came to the mountain to check on Alice.

Upon seeing Alice's battered state, Merlin frowned, thinking the training was too intense. For someone of Alice's abilities, this pace was unsustainable and seemed like a reckless attempt to force growth.

Only someone with a death wish could endure such torment. It reminded Merlin of his own desperate journey into the Valley of Despair after Vivian's death, where he had suffered unimaginable pain.

Seeing Alice in a similar situation, Merlin couldn't bear it and shouted, "Claudia, what are you doing?!"

(-“-)

(Note: The last line appears to be incomplete or corrupted in the source text.)

title: Chapter 25 — Devotion
content:
Chapter 25 — Devotion

Volume 26 · Chapter 25

Alice turned her head in surprise, not expecting Merlin to find her here, which left her feeling astonished.

"Merlin?!"

"Although I knew you and your teacher were training, I didn't expect you to be in such a sorry state..."

Merlin walked to Alice's side, looking down at her injuries, and felt that Claudia's severity was excessive.

"...how did you find me?" Alice asked in puzzlement.

"It's because you haven't returned for several days, and Chris has been clamoring to see you," Merlin said helplessly.

"......" Alice lowered her head, unable to help but ask, "Chris, how has she been lately?"

"Besides shouting about wanting to find her mother every day, she seems pretty normal." Merlin shrugged. In reality, he had been busy taking care of the child himself these past few days, and with no end in sight, he had no choice but to come see Alice.

"That...that's good, thank you, Merlin." Alice said with her head down.

"Instead of saying that, you'd better return sooner." Merlin sighed, looking at Claudia who stood sternly before them, "Senior, I know your special training for Alice is a good thing, but isn't this intensity a bit too much?"

"Too much? Where is it too much?" Claudia paused, her gaze sharp as she stared at Merlin. "All the strong ones in history were forged in blood and sweat. Easy training is completely useless."

"But the training intensity has already exceeded Alice's endurance. If you're not careful, it could be fatal." Merlin said seriously.

Alice pulled at Merlin's sleeve, wanting to say something.

"Do you think I would let Alice die during training? Don't underestimate me, foolish man!" Claudia's expression turned unpleasant, feeling insulted. "At the end of the day, you're just a useless guy. What qualifications do you have to point fingers at my training methods?"

"Mer...Alice pulled at Merlin's sleeve, wanting to say something.

"I...I really do have the qualifications to point fingers..." Merlin suddenly took a step forward, feeling somewhat dissatisfied with Claudia.

"Hah, your confidence is admirable, but your outwardly strong yet inwardly weak appearance is laughable." Claudia curled the corner of her mouth, naturally looking down on Merlin. "I am Alice's teacher, and this special training is between us as master and disciple. What does it have to do with you? You'd better leave quickly and not disturb us."

"What does it have to do with me?" Merlin furrowed his brow, looking at Alice beside him with a strange expression.

"...what are you doing?" Alice felt a sense of foreboding and subconsciously took a step back.

Merlin gritted his teeth and stretched out his hand, embracing Alice's waist in front of Claudia.

"Ah?!" Alice's eyes widened in shock, her mind going blank as she was suddenly pulled into Merlin's embrace.

Merlin held Alice, looking at Claudia across from him, and said with a serious tone, "Alice is my woman!"

"Ah?!"

Alice's body stiffened, as if petrified, her face slowly turning red with shame. In her heart, she felt an overwhelming sense of embarrassment.

Merlin...what is he saying?! And in front of my teacher!

Why can he say such embarrassing things so easily?! His woman...what's that supposed to mean?!

Alice lowered her head, her face still red, though she had heard the words she had longed for, the current situation was inappropriate.

Claudia's veins bulged on her forehead, seeing the detestable man embracing her beloved student in front of her, making her furious.

How infuriating! What are these two doing?! Are they intentionally provoking me?!

Is it impressive that they're a couple?! Do they look down on us single women?!

Claudia gritted her teeth, seeing Merlin and Alice embracing before her, exuding a nauseatingly sweet atmosphere that was unbearable to look at.

"Now can you acknowledge my relationship with her? I won't allow you to continue torturing Alice like this." Merlin held Alice's waist, his tone serious, determined to stop this hellish training no matter what.

"......" Alice's face was red as she remained silent, thinking that Merlin rarely showed such boyfriend-like behavior.

"Shh~" Merlin frequently blinked his eyes, whispering, "If you continue training like this, you'll be in danger. How can I face Chris if something happens to you?"

"......" Alice was speechless, thinking she had thought Merlin was being considerate of her, but it turned out he was only stopping her for Chris's sake. This was completely different from what she had imagined!

"You're a shortsighted man." Claudia frowned, speaking seriously. "Temporary pain for a bright future is a sure thing. Don't forget, Alice lost to Katorwitz's adventurer because her foundation was unstable and she lacked experience. We must make up for this weakness, otherwise, it will become a big problem in the future. I am Alice's teacher and will never harm her. How long have you known her? You dare to speak so boldly here!"

Merlin raised an eyebrow, thinking this old woman was truly unreasonable. She wanted to train Alice into an invincible strong person overnight, which was simply forcing things too much.

Alice lowered her head, recalling her defeat against Noa and her efforts over the past few days. If she gave up now, wouldn't all her hard work be for nothing?

Although Claudia had beaten Alice mercilessly these past few days, she had also constantly imparted new knowledge and corrected Alice's past mistakes during their confrontations.

Although Merlin didn't have ill intentions, as a teacher, Claudia wasn't simply tormenting Alice for her own amusement.

Alice gently pushed away Merlin's chest, thinking carefully before saying, "Merlin, I know Teacher's training methods are dangerous, but I need to become stronger. Not just to protect myself, I'm Chris's mother, and I need to protect her too."

"Al...Alice..." Merlin wanted to speak but stopped, thinking that Alice was an independent and strong-willed person. Whatever he said now would be useless.

Claudia saw Alice stand before her again, sword in hand, and felt a surge of admiration for her student.

"Come on, Alice. Don't relax at all. I'll show you the strongest move in the Extreme Ice Sword Technique!"

At the border village of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, the villagers finally felt at ease with the arrival of the Second Thorn Knight, Seth, and could finally get a good night's sleep.

However, the militia didn't dare to slack off. At the village gate checkpoint, torches burned brightly, illuminating the surroundings. The militiamen took turns patrolling, and at the slightest movement, they would alert the entire village to be on guard.

Yet in the darkness, three powerful Saint-tier magical beasts led a dense swarm of starving magical beasts, silently approaching the border village...

title: Chapter 26 — Insects Attack at Night
content:
Chapter 26 — Insects Attack at Night

Volume 26 · Chapter 26

At the border village's gate, two militiamen were on guard duty, keeping watch around the perimeter. If any demons were to attack from afar, they would be the first to sound the alarm, warning everyone to be on their guard. However, as the night wore on and the hours crept closer to dawn, fatigue and drowsiness began to creep in, and the two militiamen couldn't help but start chatting. "Rest for a bit, it's almost dawn, and I don't think any demons will attack tonight." "Still, we can't be too careful, we're the last shift, and the village elder said demons don't follow any rules, so we can't let our guard down." "What's there to be afraid of? You don't know that a big shot came to the village today?" "You mean that knight from Britain?" "Yeah, that's the one, the Thistle Knight, the British queen's personal bodyguard, he's quite the big deal. As long as he's in the village, demons like that... aren't worth worrying about." "......" "Hey, don't worry, sit down and rest for a bit, we've been on edge for over a month now, and it's not easy to get a chance to relax, don't be so tense..." The militiamen were also tired, so they put down the sickles they were using as weapons, but suddenly, they noticed a dark shadow floating in mid-air, "Huh?" Using the faint light from the nearby torches, they managed to make out the shape of the thing floating towards them - a small, palm-sized meatball floating in mid-air, its body covered in writhing tendrils, like a magnified bacteria. "No good!" The militiamen's eyes widened in terror as they realized this was a demon attack, but this time, it was different. In the past, demons would charge in with a loud roar, making a big commotion, but this time, it was floating in mid-air, using the darkness to sneak up on them, and even when they discovered it, it was too late! The militiamen had just picked up their sickles to defend themselves when the meatball suddenly opened its mouth, revealing a row of neat, white teeth, and bit down on the militiaman's head! "Aaaaahhh!" The militiaman felt his face being torn apart by the meatball, and his cries of pain echoed through the night, his hand holding the sickle began to flail wildly out of control. "Hey!" The militiaman's companion also realized the situation was dire, and frantically stood up to help. At this point, the meatball, with its writhing tendrils, let out a "pffft" sound as it stabbed into the militiaman's brain, and this poor human being lost his life, slumping to the ground. The militiaman's companion was frozen in shock, his heart filled with fear, his hand holding the axe he used to chop wood, trembling with fear. The militiaman who was supposed to be dead suddenly stood up again, his movements stiff and jerky, like a rusty robot? Seeing his companion still standing, the militiaman's face lit up with joy, and he mustered up the courage to grab the axe and walk towards his companion, "Are you still alive? Hold on, I'll come and save you!" However, in the blink of an eye, a bizarre scene unfolded - the militiaman who was supposed to be dead suddenly raised his sickle, his face twisted with malice, and attacked his companion who had come to rescue him. The militiaman's companion's face was filled with shock, and before he could even let out a scream, he was struck by the sickle, his head split open, and he fell to the ground, lifeless. At this point, the militiaman who had been possessed by the demon had lost control of his brain, and his body had become a puppet, controlled by the monster, and was being manipulated by the demon's whims. The moment the tendrils stabbed into his brain, he was already dead. The demon that had attacked the village was not just a simple meatball, and in the darkness of the night, a large group of demons was slowly approaching the border village. Three spherical creatures, their bodies covered in scales and razor-sharp tendrils, their blood-red eyes rolling wildly, were drawn to the scent of living creatures, and were slowly closing in on the border village. They were demons with rare psychic control abilities, and their strength was at the peak of the Saint-tier, making them powerful predators among demons. Three demon-like creatures, massive in size, like a flying castle, opened their mouths, revealing rows of teeth covered in green moss, and constantly produced smaller meatball demons from their mouths. The three demons were like motherships, surrounded by countless smaller meatball demons, like a swarm of terrifying locusts, blocking out the sun... In the border village, Seth was summoned by the old village elder, and had no choice but to stay behind to help guard the village until the demon threat was gone. Seth was exhausted from his long journey, and soon fell asleep. However, before dawn, he was suddenly woken up by the old village elder, frantic and panicked, "Knight, wake up! Knight, wake up!" The old village elder's face was filled with terror, and he kept shaking Seth's strong body, outside, something big was happening! Seth felt a headache, and was woken up by the old village elder, slowly sitting up, "What...what's going on? Is it dawn already?" "No, Seth, it's not that. Something big is happening outside! Three demons have attacked us!" The old village elder's eyes were wide with fear, and he kept banging his staff on the ground. "What?!" Seth's eyes widened in shock, and he thought to himself, this is too fast, he had just arrived, and now demons were attacking the village? Seth quickly got up and walked to the window, just as he opened it, a pungent smell of smoke wafted in. Seth's face contorted in disgust, and he looked out the window, and was shocked by what he saw. Outside, the village was engulfed in flames, smoke billowing into the sky, the entrance to the village was destroyed, and many houses were badly damaged, and villagers were running out of their homes, wearing their nightclothes, and fleeing in panic, amidst the raging flames. Three demon-like creatures, their eyes like balls, were hovering above the village, shooting out powerful beams of light from their eyes, destroying everything in their path, causing massive explosions and towering flames! The smaller meatball demons, like a swarm of locusts, were surrounding the village, attacking villagers, and controlling human bodies to attack defenseless villagers. Seth saw the situation outside was dire, and half the village was already destroyed, "What's going on? Why didn't the militiamen sound the alarm first?" "It's not that we didn't want to, but this time, the demons were different, they were quiet and stealthy, and hard to detect, especially at night. And we set up many traps and obstacles, but they were useless against flying demons!" The old village elder was on the verge of tears, his heart aching for Seth's pain tenfold. "Those monsters have already reached our village... Seth's face was grim, and he felt that these demons were quite formidable. "Now, what should we do? Knight, please save us!" The old village elder had no choice but to put all his hopes on Seth. Seth looked at the village church, which seemed to be the most solid building, and thought for a moment, then turned to the old village elder, his face stern, "Village elder, you go and lead everyone to that church, now!" "It's not safe to run around, it's better for everyone to gather in the church, it's safer!"

title: Chapter 27 — Chivalry (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 27 — Chivalry (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 26 · Chapter 27

Bang!

Seth kicked open the door to Elyria's room in a frantic rush. Outside, monsters were rampaging, continuously slaughtering innocent villagers - the situation was dire, and Seth couldn't afford to be picky!

Moreover, Seth judged that the three monsters outside were too difficult to handle alone, so he needed help. As Gregori's student, Elyria must have some exceptional abilities, perhaps she could help stop the monsters' rampage!

So Seth didn't care about Elyria's temper now; he just wanted to wake her up and have her go out to exterminate the monsters - it was her job. Besides, she had already eaten half a year's worth of the village's provisions, so she couldn't just idle around!

"Elyria! Wake up quickly! Stop sleeping!"

Seth rushed to Elyria's side, shouting her name loudly, hoping she would get up quickly to work. But Elyria showed no reaction to Seth's loud calls, sleeping so soundly it was as if she hadn't heard anything. She even drooled and scratched her little belly with her hand, who knows what delicious thing she was dreaming of?

"Elyria!!"

Seth, growing anxious, shouted again, but this little horned creature remained completely unresponsive - how could she sleep like a dead person? How could shouting not wake her up? She even claimed to have morning temper, but a normal person couldn't wake her up at all!

Seth was getting impatient and decided to use violent means to stimulate Elyria awake, so he stretched out his palm and gave her two loud slaps.

"Wake up!!!"

@SF Light Novel

"Huh... Elyria slept even more soundly, blowing bubbles with her nose, changing size with each breath.

"My god..."

Seth's face turned black, his heart speechless towards Elyria. Not waking up even now? He had never seen anyone sleep so soundly! He wondered, this person sleeps after eating and is only clear-headed when hungry - shouldn't they not be fed?

What kind of adventurer is this? Doesn't she harm people? He couldn't understand what Gregori saw in her to take her as a student...

Seth grew more bewildered, having no way to deal with Elyria who slept like a dead pig. He even felt that this border village and Gregori must have some grudge, otherwise why would they send such a foolish adventurer?

At this time, the village elder rushed in from outside, wiping the sweat from his forehead. "Knight, I've done as you said and led the villagers to the church for shelter. That church was once a place to train orphans into temple knights, so it's very sturdy and should be able to withstand the monsters' attacks for a while."

"Is that so? As I guessed, you people can't help against those monsters. Charging in would be suicidal. Don't step out of the church until the monsters are eliminated."

"Yes, I will follow your instructions." The village elder nodded seriously, then asked, "Then what? Are you going to face the monsters outside alone?"

"That's right. The situation is urgent. If we delay, the entire village might be doomed. I must go out to stop them." Seth frowned, looking at Elyria who was still fast asleep on the bed, and handed her to the village elder. "Take her to the church for shelter too. She sleeps so soundly she can't be woken up, and she's of no use..."

The village elder took Elyria, looking at this adventurer sent to support them who had the body of a child, and couldn't help but complain, "We spent so much money to hire an adventurer, what's the use?"

"Alas! What did we do wrong to deserve such suffering?"

On the streets of the border village, a large group of villagers controlled by the meatball monsters had become the monsters' pawns, starting to slaughter humans. These controlled people all had one characteristic - a terrifying tumor-like growth on their foreheads where the meatball monsters had parasitized them.

The parasitized humans had lost their humanity and reason, using their teeth to tear at human flesh, almost indistinguishable from ghouls except for their single-minded desire to kill.

Some villagers who hadn't made it to the church in time fled in terror, with the ferocious parasitized villagers behind them. Former friendly neighbors had now become the monsters' accomplices.

The fleeing villagers cried out for help, scrambling to escape, but they couldn't outrun the relentless parasitized villagers. Several unlucky ones were bitten to pieces!

The villagers were terrified, facing the relentless "monsters." Some even gave up on survival, kneeling on the ground with ashen faces.

But then, Seth arrived with a black box containing the demon armor on his back, holding his beloved weapon, an ancient bronze long spear. He descended from the sky.

Seth's eyes blazed as he danced with his spear, instantly transforming his golden fighting spirit into a sharp spiral.

He smashed the parasitized humans in front of him into a bloody pulp, splattering it everywhere!

The surviving villagers, who had given up all hope, saw Seth arrive and were overjoyed, crying tears of gratitude. Their eyes were filled with worship for the strong savior.

Seth turned to the surviving villagers and shouted, "Leave quickly and head to the church for shelter! Don't come out until the monsters are eliminated!"

The lucky survivors nodded repeatedly, taking the opportunity to escape towards the safe church.

Seth let out a sigh of relief, looking up at the three monster mothers rampaging in the sky, their large eyes seemingly wanting to burn the entire village to ashes.

"Dealing with three... is a bit difficult..."

Seth felt considerable pressure, but he resolutely marched towards the three powerful monsters. He wouldn't forget his duty as a knight - protecting the weak was a knight's responsibility.

As the only living being in the area, he immediately attracted a large group of parasitized villagers. They howled, rushing towards Seth in a frenzy.

However, Seth didn't even furrow his brow. With a sweep of his spear, the parasitized villagers fell into a pool of blood, exuding an unstoppable aura.

As the Second Thorn Knight of the Kingdom of Britain, Seth was considered a strong warrior. Killing low-level monsters was as easy as chopping vegetables.

Seth kicked the tumor monsters and the parasitized villagers' heads, exploding them into a bloody mess. The numerous small tumor monsters in the sky seemed to sense something and noticed the approaching human.

A swarm of small meatball monsters circled twice in the sky before diving towards Seth, like a torrent of water pouring down from the heavens!

Seth's face turned cold as he opened the black box on his back. The demon armor, which had been starving, immediately attached itself to Seth, enveloping him in evil power.

But the meatball monster swarm descended like a waterfall, burying the tiny Seth in a flood. Countless meatball monsters crawled over him, constantly seeking weak points to control him.

Inside the demon armor, Seth looked at the hellish scene outside and felt the armor itself growing excited.

"Have a feast!

"Turn their blood and flesh into your power!"

title: Chapter 28 — Crisis Situation
content:
Chapter 28 — Crisis Situation

Volume 26 · Chapter 28

The dense, tumor-like demonic beasts swarmed around Seth, who was clad in the devilish armor, like a flood. They crawled over the armor, seeking a weak point to control Seth. However, the devilish armor was a treasure of the Greedy Sovereign, crafted with exquisite precision, boasting 360-degree defense without any blind spots. The demonic beasts bit and clawed for half a day but couldn't do anything to Seth, who was protected by the armor, and could only pressure him with their numbers. Suddenly, the devilish armor emitted a dazzling red glow, and demonic energy surged as towering demonic flames began to spread. Countless small tumor-like demonic beasts, as if drained of their flesh and blood, withered at a visible speed and fell from Seth's body. Blood flowed out of the demonic beasts' bodies, gathered in mid-air, and was then absorbed by the devilish armor like a whale drinking water. Seth, inside the armor, could clearly feel the armor's excitement for battle; it was eager to fight after being fed. Indulging in slaughter and combat could rapidly strengthen the living devilish armor. Dark red patterns appeared on the armor, emitting an ominous aura and light in the darkness, like an evil spirit slowly awakening from its slumber. Seth knew this was a sign that the armor had been satiated. After a long-awaited feast, the armor was awakening, about to unleash part of its true power. Only intense combat could vent its raging fury. Crimson demonic flames shot up from the armor, illuminating the dark night like daylight, casting the entire border village in a red glow. The three eyeball demonic beasts destroying the village noticed the man in black armor below, surrounded by their fallen "children," and slowly encircled him in anger. Seth wielded his ancient long spear, assuming a battle stance, his Saint-tier aura surging as he roared, "Come on, monsters!!!" A piercing sound tore through the air, causing ear pain. Three powerful beams of light shot from the eyeball demonic beasts' single eyes! The blue beams were scorching hot, and the air seemed to burn before they even hit Seth. The three beams converged on Seth, exploding with a deafening "boom!" The blast sent flames and heat soaring over a thousand feet high, reducing the fragile village houses to rubble. Only the sturdy church remained standing, swaying in the heat waves. Amidst the rolling smoke, before the flames had dissipated, Seth charged out of the inferno. The black-armored knight, his true nature obscured, left onlookers wondering if he was human or a ferocious demon. The satiated devilish armor, with its incredible defense, effortlessly withstood the three powerful attacks, and its enhancement of Seth's strength was evident. Seth leapt into the air, his spear trembling with Saint-tier aura, and pierced the nearest eyeball demonic beast with a single strike. The massive beast let out a deafening scream as Seth killed it, and even its flesh was devoured by the armor. The armor fed on the beast's flesh, nourishing Seth and increasing his power. Seth was surprised to find the armor felt so light, perhaps becoming its slave was the correct way to use it. The lifeless eyeball demonic beast fell to the ground, and Seth pursued the second one, using the corpse as a stepping stone to launch a fierce attack. The second beast retaliated, its sharp tentacles shooting towards Seth like a thousand arrows. The sound of metal clashing echoed as the tentacles struck Seth's heart, attempting to pierce his defense. However, the devilish armor protected him, rendering the attacks ineffective. The beast's immense strength sent Seth crashing to the ground, kicking up a cloud of dust. With a whoosh, Seth's spear, wrapped in golden aura, shot through the dust and pierced the second beast's eye, causing it to collapse with a pained shriek. Seth flicked his cloak, dispersing the dust, and recalled his spear. He looked up at the third eyeball demonic beast amidst the flames. "You're the last one. Have you made a will? Otherwise, you won't have the chance..." The third beast realized its predicament, its massive eye rolling wildly, clearly not planning to flee. It extended its tentacles to its fallen companions, and a bizarre transformation occurred. The two corpses dissolved into black blood, flowing through the tentacles into the last beast's body. A fierce gale erupted, its howling like a monster awakening from the night. The blood, seemingly alive, merged into the beast's body... "What's going on?" Seth frowned, sensing a qualitative change in the monster's pressure. The last beast had devoured its companions, evolving into a gigantic one-eyed giant with enhanced strength. The giant's body was covered in exaggerated muscles, its size rivaling three castles stacked together. Before it, Seth appeared as small as an ant. "...Seth was stunned, gazing up at the giant, feeling its terrifying pressure. The giant crouched, its single eye fixed on Seth. Seth could see nothing but the giant's white sclera. Magical elements in the air agitated, forming countless light points that converged into the giant's eye. A blue-black laser shot out, its intense light making the villagers in the church think dawn had broken. The destructive beam ravaged everything in its path, reducing it to dust. Seth, bathed in the beam, felt his consciousness blur, his body like it was being torn apart by countless monsters. Without the devilish armor's protection, he would have been pulverized instantly. Seth's body flew backward uncontrollably, his mind clouded by the powerful attack. "Ahhhh!" Inside the precarious church, the villagers felt the earth shake from the battle outside. Dust and debris fell from the ceiling as they huddled in corners, some praying to the Goddess, others crying, and a few had gone mad. Only the adventurer Aria, who had come to assist, slept peacefully, oblivious to the chaos. A stray tumor-like demonic beast had infiltrated the church, observing the humans below, planning to control a host and slaughter everyone. Aria's deep sleep had caught its attention...

title: Chapter 29 — The Most Useless Adventurer
content:
Chapter 29 — The Most Useless Adventurer

Volume 26 · Chapter 29

The battle raged outside, intermittent flashes of firelight piercing the darkness like daylight.

The constant tremors shook the sturdy church, built for training the Holy Church’s knights, as waves of heat and shockwaves sent it shuddering—so close to collapsing, burying everyone beneath its ruins.

The villagers of the border settlement, gripped by terror, huddled inside the small chapel, shivering uncontrollably.

In the face of certain death, nearly everyone revealed their true selves—some sobbed, others laughed hysterically, and some erupted in fury, shouting at those around them.

Even those who had once rejected the Goddess of Light now knelt before the broken idol, praying fervently.

Even as Sith fought desperately outside, the villagers still refused to fully trust the knight, their survival now uncertain.

Cowering in the cramped chapel, despairing negativity spread, leaving them clueless about the outside world and eroding their last shreds of hope.

“Oh, mighty Mother of Humanity, Goddess of Light Maria, I beg you to spare us these useless fools and grant us safe passage.”

The old village elder knelt before the idol, his expression devout, repeatedly bowing, hoping his voice would reach the gods.

He hoped Sith would triumph outside, but the repeated explosions and tremors proved the fight was far from over.

The old village elder watched as his daughter, Alice, slept soundly beside him, sighing deeply. This hired adventurer was useless—she ate half the village’s grain while doing nothing, a lazy burden!

This made the kind old man wonder if he’d done something wrong or if he’d been underpaid, sending a useless adventurer to scam the entire border village.

With no other choice, he prayed that Goddess Maria would not abandon this place, hoping Sith could defeat the monsters outside.

Suddenly, the villagers grew restless—

“There’s a monster!”

“This isn’t safe! How did it get in?”

“Village Elder! There’s a demon in the church!”

The small, lurking meatball demon—originally cautiously approaching the sleeping Alice—had been spotted, sparking further panic.

The old village elder saw the villagers scatter like startled birds, their terror escalating even for a creature no larger than an adult’s palm.

The tiny demon waved its tentacles defiantly, scaring off nearby villagers as if they were unoccupied territory.

The old village elder lost his temper entirely. With no escape left, a creature that could be crushed with a foot still acted so arrogantly—

“What’s the matter? We have nowhere left to run—what’s the point?”

“It’s just a little thing! How did it scare you so much?”

“We’re a whole group—how can we not be able to handle even a palm-sized demon? Are you all cowards?”

The old village elder roared at the villagers, knowing chaos would only worsen things. He hoped to snap them out of their panic and steady them.

And it worked—villagers stopped in their tracks, turning to glare at the bragging little demon, their expressions shifting from confusion to fury.

One villager, finally finding courage, raised a pitchfork and roared, slashing at the meatball demon—

“Die! Die, you vile monster!”

The demon shrieked, then was impaled like a bee swarm, collapsing lifelessly.

The villagers stared at the corpse, some even showing sadness, but others let out a laugh—like they’d finally been released from years of oppression.

The brief disturbance settled, and someone suggested, “Village Elder! This church isn’t safe anymore! Let’s go out and fight those monsters!”

“No!” the old man said firmly. “Those monsters are too troublesome. We’re farmers—we’re not trained to fight them. If we go out, we’ll only be a burden to Sith, who’s already struggling to handle them alone. Why should he have to worry about us?”

The villagers fell silent at his words, their excitement fading. They saw the hired adventurer Alice still sleeping peacefully, and many grew furious.

“Wasting our money on this useless adventurer? Why not buy weapons to strengthen our militia?”

“Exactly! This lazy adventurer just eats and sleeps—why hire her at all?”

“At least she could’ve helped!”

The old village elder watched as more villagers turned against Alice, sighing in frustration. He regretted even asking the Adventurers Guild in London for help.

Suddenly, the meatball demon—still impaled—twitched, proving it hadn’t truly died. It dragged itself forward, lunging at Alice’s face as she slept.

“—Didn’t die!” the villagers gasped, terrified by the sudden resurrection.

The demon aimed to control Alice, then use her body to slaughter everyone. It extended its tentacles, stabbing Alice’s skull with reckless force.

Everyone assumed Alice would become their slave, but the woman—who’d been sleeping like a dead pig—suddenly bolted upright, snatching the demon from her face.

“Ow! How dare you disturb my rest?”

Alice glared at the dazed demon in her hands, her jaw clenched in fury.

She squeezed it hard, crushing it completely, spraying green ichor everywhere.

Alice tossed the demon’s corpse aside, looking around in confusion. She didn’t remember anything—she’d been sleeping cozily in her room.

“What happened? Why am I here?”

“You’re asking me?” the old village elder snapped, his anger finally erupting. “Didn’t you know? You came here to protect our village! You didn’t even do your job—you ate half the village’s grain while doing nothing!”

The old man raged, “I’ve lived half my life, and you’re the most useless adventurer I’ve ever seen!”

“Useless adventurer…?”

“You’re the one being called useless?”

(u--.)

title: Chapter 30 — Holy Dragon's Breath (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 30 — Holy Dragon's Breath (Extra Chapter)

Volume 26 · Chapter 30

"Who else could it be?" The old village chief huffed, his mustache bristling as he glared at Aria, who had reduced him to tears of frustration.

"Oh~," Aria scratched her disheveled hair, "still the first time someone's... "

The villagers, already resentful of Aria's inaction, couldn't help but join in the criticism upon seeing the village chief's accusations.

"You're the adventurer we hired to protect us, yet you didn't help and now you want us to return the money and leave? We don't welcome you here!"

"Exactly! You're just a parasite who eats without working. We don't welcome you, get out of the village!"

"Get out! Foolish adventurer! We placed our hopes in you, but you toyed with our trust! Leave! We don't need you!"

As Aria listened to the surrounding doubts and curses, she furrowed her brow and spoke expressionlessly, "You want me to leave? Are you sure?"

"What, should we keep supporting you? You don't work but eat so much, who can afford that? I'll definitely report your evil deeds to the Adventurers Guild headquarters in London!" The old village chief angrily pounded the ground with his cane, his belly burning with rage.

Just as he finished speaking, a sudden situation arose on the other side—

A fierce white light suddenly illuminated the church window, a beam of light that was blue to the point of blackness shot out, blasting straight towards them!

The sturdy church dome quickly collapsed under the giant cyclops's beam, exposing all the villagers who had been hiding inside!

The giant cyclops's beam had a wide attack range, originally intended for Seth, but it accidentally pierced the church roof, allowing the monster to discover more humans hiding there.

Seth, who had been fighting outside, was blown away and landed before everyone.
