His demonic armor was partially charred red, and even with the armor's protection, he was seriously injured. Without the armor's defense, he might have died on the spot!

"...This monster."

Seth's bones felt like they were broken, and even slight movements caused piercing pain, making him frequently gasp for breath.

"Knight!" the old village chief exclaimed, seeing Seth defeated. Wasn't this the end for everyone?

"...Run!" Seth shouted with all his might. He couldn't block the giant cyclops, and these villagers would likely become its food!

The villagers panicked, and since even Seth had been defeated, who could save them?

People lost their last psychological defense and began rushing towards the church door in a frenzy.

Staying in the church meant certain death, while escaping might allow them to survive by luck!

Suddenly, a massive figure blocked the church door, cutting off everyone's escape route.

The giant cyclops looked down at the tiny humans, its rolling eyeballs gleaming with mockery.

The villagers gazed up at the giant cyclops, stunned by a single glance, their minds blank and hearts filled with despair.

The magic elements in the air became agitated, transforming into countless light points that converged towards the giant cyclops's eyes.

The giant cyclops intended to annihilate all life here, leaving no survivors!

As the air exploded, the temperature soared, and a blue-black beam shot out from the cyclops's eye, carrying a destructive aura that blasted towards everyone.

Aria watched the incoming beam, her lazy eyes suddenly sharpening as she unleashed a terrifying dragon roar from her small body!

Her body grew gem-like scales, her small curved horns lengthened, and massive brown dragon wings sprouted from her back, disproportionate to her size...

Half-dragon transformation! A power similar to Alice's, where a human body approached that of a giant dragon!

Aria took a deep breath, her small belly swelling, then unleashed her full power!

Holy Dragon's Breath!

Aria and Alice had both consumed the Saint Dragon's inheritance crystal, gaining the dragon tribe's power.

Decades ago, Gregory had somehow obtained an Earth Saint Dragon's inheritance crystal. Such a precious item filled him with joy.

Since Gregory couldn't fuse with the inheritance crystal, he didn't consume it himself but instead searched for a human who could resonate with the dragon tribe's power.

Finally, in a remote orphanage in the Kingdom of Britain, he found a highly talented child—Aria, who suffered from dwarfism.

Gregory treated Aria like his own, training her as his student, intending for her to eventually take over the entire London Adventurers Guild. He secretly cultivated Aria until her strength was sufficient, gradually letting her emerge into the public eye.

As an existence equal to the Frost Saint Dragon, the Earth Saint Dragon proved that Aria's talent and strength wouldn't be inferior to Alice's. Under Gregory's meticulous guidance, she would only grow stronger!

Aria used the Earth Saint Dragon's breath to counter the giant cyclops's beam. The two forces collided, triggering a massive explosion.

In the midst of the fiery scene, all villagers were stunned, even the old village chief felt dazed, as if dreaming, because Aria's Holy Dragon's Breath had dispersed the destructive beam that even Seth couldn't block!

The Earth Saint Dragon's breath shot out countless powerful earth element crystals, each crystal like a massive bullet. Under Aria's furious outburst, they poured out like a Gatling gun with 60 times increased firing speed, unleashing 3 million bullets in an instant to annihilate the enemy!

The giant cyclops's attack was powerless against the Earth Saint Dragon's Breath, instantly shattered.

Even the giant cyclops itself was engulfed in the breath, its body turning into a sieve, leaving only a giant, riddled skeleton before collapsing with a loud "boom"!

The enemy that Seth had struggled to defeat was felled by Aria's single angry roar, the overwhelming power difference leaving everyone ashamed!

"Aria..." Seth looked dazed, thinking, "No wonder she's Master Gregory's student, just as I suspected, she's truly exceptional!"

At this moment, no one dared to complain about Aria. The old village chief's gaze towards her was filled with reverence and fear, feeling his previous doubts were too rash.

Aria wiped her mouth and muttered expressionlessly, "I have a bad temper when I wake up, don't provoke me..."

Days later, the border village regained its safety and peace, with most surrounding magical beasts eradicated. The villagers returned to their daily lives.

At the village entrance, Seth saw Aria off.

"Goodbye, useless knight," Aria said expressionlessly.

"You're so rude..." Seth, with his arm bandaged, was still recovering in the village. "Are you in such a hurry to return to London?"

"Correct. My teacher is urging me to return because the Adventurers' Tournament is about to begin. I can't wander around outside," Aria replied calmly.

"Oh~," Seth sighed, glancing at his injuries. "I won't be able to cheer for you. I need to stay in the village to recover. Good luck in the tournament, bring glory to London."

"I don't need to worry about you. You Thorn Knights should worry about yourselves. You're so weak it's embarrassing. The royal family's talent cultivation is truly terrible..." Aria said bluntly.

"...Seth's forehead veins bulged as he gritted his teeth, "Then I hope you crash in the tournament. Even if you win the championship, others will be infuriated."

"Sorry, I was born for the championship. Thirty years of training were for today. To be honest, the championship is mine for the taking," Aria said nonchalantly, turning to leave.

"This..."

Seth frowned, watching Aria's back as he shook his head and turned back to the village. He felt like someone was staring at him from the direction of the church ruins.

Seth suddenly turned around but saw nothing, only the setting sun casting a red glow over the ruined church.

"Was it just my imagination? Am I too tense..."

After Seth left, a demon with horns on its head and membrane wings on its back appeared atop the church ruins, its crimson eyes fixed on Seth's departing figure—

"I've found you, foolish human..."

"Lord Mammon's things aren't for anyone to take."

title: Chapter 31 — The Last Chapter—Plus Updates
content:
Chapter 31 — The Last Chapter—Plus Updates

Volume 26 · Chapter 31

A month later, the Adventurers' Grand Tournament was about to begin.

At the John family's estate in Ireland.

This old mansion seemed ordinary, but the books it contained were comparable to a national library.

The John family was renowned for producing exceptional mages, as could be inferred from their illustrious history.

However, with the passage of time, the John family gradually declined, and it became rare for a genius mage to emerge. Until today, young Johnson became the family's only hope.

Recently, Zikatile had snatched young Johnson's prey in the Beast Forest, directly disrupting his plan to rapidly increase his strength.

This enraged young Johnson, who began subjecting himself to cruel emergency hell training.

However, young Johnson's cultivation had already hit a bottleneck, and without the aid of a powerful external force, it was difficult to achieve significant improvement.

This was also why young Johnson had gone alone to the Beast Forest to hunt Parn. Unfortunately, his carefully laid plans were ruined by Zikatile.

After Zikatile absorbed Parn's beast core, his strength would likely soar, making him an even more formidable opponent for young Johnson.

However, young Johnson's efforts had not gone unnoticed by his father, old John. Seeing his son torment himself to revive the family, he felt a strong urge to help.

Thus, just yesterday, old John mysteriously told his son to follow him to their ancestors' graves at night.

The gentle evening breeze rustling through the graveyard made young Johnson shiver involuntarily, feeling the eerie atmosphere.

Buried here were all of young Johnson's ancestors. Every year, he would accompany his father to clean the graves and pay respects.

However, young Johnson disliked coming to such places. Since childhood, he had been afraid of the dead, and even though these were his own ancestors, he still felt countless eyes watching him.

Young Johnson tightened his clothes, clutched the white flowers in his hand, and walked quickly with his head down, his mind racing with fears of ghosts suddenly appearing.

The surrounding tombstones bore famous names from the past, all of whom were once renowned mages whose power and achievements had reached extraordinary heights.

Yet, despite their remarkable accomplishments, they were now nothing more than a handful of yellow earth.

Young Johnson arrived at his grandfather's tombstone and found his father already waiting there, silently gazing at the stone.

"...".

"Here?" Old John turned to his son with a warm smile.

Young Johnson placed the flowers on his grandfather's tombstone and asked curiously, "Why choose this time to pay respects? We usually do it at fixed times."

"You've been training too intensely lately. I know you want to revive the family, but don't push yourself too hard. I've never asked anything of you, just worried you're under too much pressure." Old John looked at his father's tombstone and said softly, "Your grandfather instructed me to take good care of you before he passed away, but it seems I haven't done well enough..."

Young Johnson lowered his head, his emotions complex. "I just want you to be proud of me. I want to revive our family; it's my dream..."

"I'm already proud of your current achievements, my child..." Old John's aged body slowly turned around. "Even if you don't revive the family, it's fine. What's most important is living."

"I'm different from you, Father. I won't live a carefree life; I must do something meaningful." Young Johnson said stubbornly.

Old John sighed, "Many of our ancestors created numerous spells, but after death, they were forgotten, their contributions unknown. You don't need to force yourself; living happily is what matters. Your grandfather probably understood this, which is why he gave me so much freedom since childhood."

"Father, look at these tombstones. They all tell the story of our family's former glory. I grew up listening to stories of our ancestors and feel sorrow for them. The family must be revived! We must return to our former glory and show everyone that heroes still emerge from our family!" Young Johnson exclaimed passionately.

"Are you certain you want to walk this path?" Old John's expression turned sorrowful.

"Yes! Father, you don't have to support me, but please don't stop me!" Young Johnson said seriously.

"As your father, how could I not support your dreams? If possible, I'd like to help you and reduce your suffering."

Old John shook his head, raised his staff, and began drawing circles in the air.

Instantly, the magical elements in the air surged, forming a massive sphere of magical energy.

This energy orb pulsed with violent power, its radiance rivaling the sun, and its presence made young Johnson's body tremble uncontrollably.

Creating such a colossal magical aggregation was impossible in young Johnson's understanding!

"This is our family's secret." Old John lowered his staff, speaking in a teacher-like tone. "Our ancestors, in their quest to create the strongest mage, devoted themselves to crafting a container that could hold magical energy. Every ancestor's magic is stored within it after death, including your grandfather's..."

"A container holding all our ancestors' magic?" Young Johnson's eyes widened in astonishment, clearly sensing the vast magical energy.

"That's right. Your grandfather said that if you ever hit a training bottleneck and still wished to revive the family, I should give this to you. It will become your second source of magical power."

Old John paused, gazing at the terrifying energy sphere. "This container can aid your training, allowing you to instantly unleash power far beyond your own."

"But promise me, don't use it lightly."

"The price of using this container's power..."

"...is the loss of lifespan."

In Manchesters Bottom City.

Zikatile packed his bags, preparing to head to the tournament venue. This time, he wanted the world to know his name, no longer living as a half-breed.

Having absorbed Parn's beast core, his strength was already formidable, and now it was likely to become unimaginable.

Zikatile shouldered his bag and glanced at an old photo on the bedside table – a kind old man and a young black elf. Though they looked different, they seemed like father and son.

This was taken when Zikatile was five, and the old man was his foster father, the former guildmaster of Manchesters Bottom Adventurers Guild.

Five-year-old Zikatile looked shy and timid, unable to look at the camera and needing his foster father's hand for courage.

Looking at the old photo, Zikatile couldn't help but smile, murmuring to his foster father's image, "I've trained to this point, and I feel the time is ripe. I have the ability to bring the championship to Manchesters Bottom's adventurers, fulfilling your wish..."

"I am a half-breed of black elf and human, and you are human. Thank you for not rejecting me and raising me."

"I will complete your wish. If you can see from heaven, please be proud of me!"

Zikatile left the room, where many were already waiting to see him off. Almost all of Manchesters Bottom's adventurers had gathered to bid him farewell.

Among them was a woman with a smoking pipe, sporting red wavy hair that exuded mature, intellectual charm.

Her name was Jennifer, the current guildmaster of Manchesters Bottom, a renowned mage known as the Flame Witch.

Jennifer exhaled smoke from her red lips, her dense red hair covering one eye, and asked as she saw Zikatile emerge, "Ready?"

"Yes." Zikatile nodded.

"Bertram, Bishel." Jennifer called out, and two men immediately stepped forward from the crowd – a tall and short duo, both powerful adventurers who would accompany Zikatile to the tournament.

"They'll go with you. Remember to bring back a good result, okay?"

"Are we just here for show?" Bertram, the tall one, chuckled.

"Yeah, this time it's all up to you. We're just along for the ride." Bishel, the short one, smiled.

"Don't joke around. You're my comrades. Let's bring the championship back to Manchesters Bottom together!" Zikatile smiled.

The adventurers all smiled, unlike outsiders who disliked Zikatile. Here, they were all old acquaintances who treated him kindly and had full confidence in his ability to win.

Jennifer approached Zikatile and said softly, "You're older than me, so I shouldn't speak to you like an elder, but I still hope you won't feel inferior because of your black elf blood. Not everyone despises you. Today, you are Manchesters Bottom's pride. Go and let everyone see you anew."

Zikatile smiled, looking at Jennifer. "I know. Guildmaster, I've been waiting for this day."

In the Adventurers Guild of Katowice City.

Guildmaster Boz was hosting a dinner party with three participating adventurers.

They too had made their preparations and were ready to battle on the tournament grounds.

"Are you all ready to depart tomorrow?" Boz scanned the faces of the three young people.

"I'm completely relaxed, no pressure at all." Noah leaned lazily on his arm, thinking that since even the tournament favorite Alice had been defeated by his injury, the tournament would be a mere formality.

"If even Noah is this casual, I might be able to win the championship just by showing up?" Gabriel smirked, another of Boz's talented adventurers who excelled with dual swords, his strength in no way inferior to Noah's.

"Since they're both so confident, I suppose the tournament will be a boring game?" Shawn sneered, Boz's direct disciple who used the same magic as his master, his true strength likely the deepest among the three.

"Seeing you all so relaxed puts me at ease, but we should still take this tournament seriously." Boz said sternly.

"There's no need for that, is there? That famous demon sword user was defeated by Noah, and if I were to face him, it would probably end even faster. Now anyone can be hyped as a championship favorite. How boring~" Gabriel looked down on Noah, thinking that if the favorite could be easily defeated, he himself would surely soar.

Noah's face darkened, his voice cold. "Why are you being so casual? That demon sword user had some strength, don't think everyone I've beaten is trash."

"Oh? Isn't that the case?" Gabriel provoked.

"Don't get arrogant just because you defeated a favorite. Noah..." Shawn sneered.

"Do you think you're stronger than me? If we really fought, I could slit your throats in an instant." Noah's veins bulged on his forehead, his hand resting on the sword at his waist.

"Everyone, calm down!" Boz shouted, looking at the three. "Having confidence is good, but don't be arrogant."

"You all have the potential to win the championship, so focus on the tournament."

"This championship will definitely belong to us!"

title: Chapter 32 — Selection
content:
Chapter 32 — Selection

Volume 26 · Chapter 32

Sand Kingdom, the remote town of Visterev. "Tanya! You have to do your best in the competition!" "Let the people of Visterev see how strong our adventurers are! Tanya, you have to win the championship! You're the strongest adventurer!" The residents and adventurers of Visterev all came to see Tanya off, hoping that this hero from their small town could win the championship and show everyone that the strongest adventurer was from Visterev. "Go back! Don't bother sending me off! Winning the championship isn't easy for Tanya, is it? I'll be going with her too, to witness this historic moment!" As the guild master, Ligajov was drunk and shouting, this time he was going with Tanya to the competition venue, not to participate, but just to watch the excitement. Ligajov chased away the people who came to send Tanya off, grabbed a bottle and got on the carriage, muttering to himself. "These people are just worrying for nothing, Tanya has agreed to participate, and the championship is as good as won, isn't it?" "Don't say that, guild master, they're all hoping for Tanya's success," Tanya's attendant said awkwardly. "But if they're too enthusiastic, Tanya might get overwhelmed, right?" Ligajov smiled and said. "Tanya, how are you feeling now? You're about to face the strongest adventurers from all over the world..." Ligajov said with a fluttering brow. "Normal," Tanya replied with two words, without any signs of nervousness, and instead seemed to be treating it like a trip to relax. "Ha ha, that's a good attitude, don't get nervous, I think only a few adventurers can beat you," Ligajov said, stroking his bald head. Tanya turned back to look at him, her tone slightly displeased, "What am I supposed to do? It's boring..." "But if you meet an opponent you like, wouldn't that be even better? Trust me, you'll find a great opponent at the competition!" Tanya looked out the window again, her tone a bit distant, "If there's no one worth fighting for..." "I'll give up the championship, I don't want it..." Tanya's voice trailed off, her eyes fixed on the horizon. Great Britain, London Adventurer's Guild. Gregory had his vice-guild master, Verlan, buy a new dress for Alice, she couldn't participate in the adventurer's competition looking shabby. Gregory paid the witch, Seresh, for the potion, and only then did he wake up, he didn't know how long he would have been asleep otherwise. Elgin's swordsmanship had hit Gregory's spirit, leaving him with a lingering fear. However, Gregory heard about what happened after he fell into a coma, that the queen was actually Elizabeth's sister, Isabella, in disguise, and that Elgin had established a peaceful relationship with the royal family, which made him slightly more at ease, and he didn't pursue the matter further. Because Gregory knew that the mysterious guy was not someone to be trifled with, and that maintaining peace was the best outcome. Although adventurers shouldn't interfere with internal affairs of the kingdom, Gregory, as a former court magician, would still help the royal family if they were in trouble, using his personal name. Gregory helped Alice adjust her new dress, almost treating her like a daughter, "Do you like the new dress, Alice?" "Buying something like this is like hanging a bunch of sausages on my neck..." Alice said expressionlessly. "Cough, cough!" Verlan coughed twice, looking awkward, "You shouldn't think about food all the time, Alice, we have to represent the guild's dignity..." "....." Verlan's face turned dark, thinking that Alice was treating the competition like a snack to be devoured. "Ha ha, I'll buy you a bunch of food on the way to the competition," Gregory said, his old voice trembling with laughter. "Wow~" Alice's eyes sparkled, and she helplessly drooled. "Did you have any thoughts after your first task as an adventurer last month?" Gregory asked. "Thoughts?" Alice thought for a moment, "I should have eaten all the villagers' food for a year, that would have been better... I ate too much..." "Shut up! The old village elder wrote to us about your opinion, you should reflect on your actions..." Verlan was furious, London Adventurer's Guild had a good reputation, and they had produced an adventurer like Alice, who was a complete anomaly. "I met the Thorn Knight, Sess, and I thought he was so weak, why do the royal family invest so much in him? Don't they know that quantity is more important than quality?" Alice tilted her head, puzzled. "You should respect people, don't underestimate others!" Verlan frowned. "I understand, but I don't understand why the royal family would invest so much in one person, but not dare to take risks, and the power they gain often comes with a great cost, don't you understand?" Gregory explained patiently. "I understand, but I just don't get it..." Alice said softly. "Elizabeth the Queen just has her own considerations, we shouldn't overthink it," Gregory said patiently. "Okay," Alice nodded. "You need to focus on the competition now, and take back the championship that belongs to us, do you have any pressure?" Gregory asked, concerned. "Not at all, I just hope the opponents are strong, so I can eat more food..." Alice said, biting her finger. "This house..." Verlan's face turned dark, thinking that Alice was treating the competition like a snack to be devoured. "Ha ha, I'll buy you a bunch of food on the way to the competition," Gregory said, his old voice trembling with laughter. "Wow~" Alice's eyes sparkled, and she helplessly drooled. Gregory's old body shook with laughter, "Very good, after all, you're the only Dragon Fighter in this world. You have the capital to be arrogant." "Drink up!" One loud shout, a golden battle aura cut through the waterfall like a lightning bolt, and the young warrior's swordsmanship became more mature. The thunderous waterfall was cut off by the powerful destructive force of the lightning bolt, lasting for eight seconds! This achievement far exceeded the old guild master, Taylor's, expectations, proving that Carl was still a talented fighter. Eight seconds later, the strange scene of the broken waterfall disappeared, and the majestic waterfall merged back together, returning to its peaceful state. "Success!" Carl shouted, his arms raised in triumph, unable to hide his joy, he had finally mastered the Lightning Bolt Sword Technique. Old Taylor saw his son succeed, and couldn't help but smile, thinking that he hadn't wasted his time training this young scoundrel. "Old man! I succeeded, ha ha!" Carl walked over to share his joy with his father. "Don't get too excited, you've only learned a superficial technique, that's not the attitude of a true fighter," Old Taylor said, trying to bring Carl back down to earth. "I think I've done well, this time I'll let those old opponents taste their own medicine!" Carl said, excited. "Ha, you'd better calm down, don't let yourself get hurt," Old Taylor said, his voice cold. "Father, don't always discourage me, you should encourage me more," Carl sighed. "If I encouraged you too much, you'd become arrogant," Old Taylor said, smiling. "Time's up, let's head back, I don't know how the guild is doing, my granddaughter must be worried sick about me." "Ah, yes, Lulcia must be cursing me in her heart," Carl thought of his daughter, and his heart immediately returned to his hometown. The storm in the distance had stopped, and the sun was shining through the clouds, slowly melting the snow that had accumulated for a month. "Alice, have you learned it? This is the strongest sword technique in the Great Snow Mountain..." Clodia thought that Alice had almost grasped the technique, and her foundation had become more solid after a month of hellish training, and her strength had also increased. She slowly put away her long sword, looking at Alice, and began to explain the technique. "This sword technique is divided into three parts, one part is to control the sword, the second part is to move mountains, and the third part is to open heaven, all three parts are powerful, and the owner has great killing power, but to master it, you need to be flexible." "The third part, opening heaven, is the most special, and its power is the strongest, but it requires great caution, it can be used to make a desperate counterattack, or to kill an opponent stronger than yourself, but under no circumstances should you use the third part unless absolutely necessary..." "Because the third part, opening heaven, will instantly drain all your magical power and battle aura, and you won't be able to recover for a short time, and it will also put a huge burden on your body, if your physical strength is not enough, you'll easily get hurt, and you'll lose to your enemies, but you'll suffer a thousand times more damage yourself..." Alice breathed heavily, her body exhausted from learning the technique. Luckily, Merlin was watching over her, or she would have died from exhaustion. Alice was covered in wounds, her head spinning, and she seemed to be about to faint, she looked at the small sword in her hand, her heart filled with mixed emotions. Merlin looked at Clodia and Alice in the distance, and his brow suddenly broke out in a cold sweat. He looked around, and the swords stuck in the ground seemed to be radiating a terrifying chill. What kind of mysterious sword technique was this? It had created a forest of swords, and even Merlin couldn't help but exclaim in his heart, "Wow, this sword technique is so powerful!" Several days later, the group returned to Reksem. Since the Adventurer's Competition was about to be held, Guild Master Old Taylor gathered all the adventurers at the guild, announcing the participants. "We've been in existence for a long time, and our best achievement in the competition has been to rank among the top 100, but now it's different, we have strong adventurers joining us, so this time we'll definitely get a better ranking!" "This competition is very important, it's related to the guild's reputation, and the three people who will participate are the ones I've carefully selected, they'll represent us all and fight on the competition stage." "First, Carl Taylor!" Carl walked out of the crowd, waving at his friends, he was happy to be going to the competition again. The adventurers laughed and joked with Carl, because he was an old face, and he had always been the red flag, going to the competition was a given. Only Lulcia rolled her eyes, not wanting to cheer for her father, and didn't even look at Carl. "Second, Alice Clodia!" Alice walked out of the crowd, her injuries had healed, although her body was still a bit weak, but she was determined to participate. The adventurers started cheering, thinking that Alice was the main attraction, because her growth over the past two years was evident, and everyone had seen her progress, and they were all excited to see her perform. Lulcia saw Alice, and shouted loudly, "Alice, go! It's all up to you!" ...Alice looked embarrassed, thinking about how she had lost to Noah, and everyone still believed in her, she felt a sense of guilt. Old Taylor looked at the crowd's reaction, cleared his throat, and announced the third participant with a serious tone. "And finally, the third adventurer representing Reksem Guild at the competition is... 4T" "Merlin Lucifer!" Old Taylor announced the third participant, and the crowd was stunned, everyone's expression was one of confusion, unable to understand why the guild master would choose a mysterious and unknown adventurer like Merlin. The crowd looked at Old Taylor, and there was a stunned silence, lasting for three seconds, before the crowd erupted in shock. "What?!!" "Cough, cough! Quiet down!" Old Taylor's face turned red, knowing that the other adventurers would react this way. "Why? Guild Master seems to have always liked Merlin, but this competition is no joke, choosing Merlin to participate... the crowd's Da Vinci, Chu, raised an eyebrow, "I don't understand." "I also don't understand, logically speaking, choosing me would be more suitable, I've been training my skills in vain," Rosetti felt a sense of disappointment, not knowing what he had done wrong, and not knowing why Merlin, who relied on Alice, was stronger than him. Lulcia thought that her grandfather was senile, and couldn't help but walk up to him, and ask quietly, "Grandfather, are you okay? You're not confused, are you? The competition is held once every four years, and we need to send our strongest three people to participate." "I know, I'm not confused, Carl, Alice, and Merlin, are all my carefully considered choices, there won't be any problems, this is indeed the optimal configuration." Old Taylor explained seriously. "Grandfather, you're joking, right? The optimal configuration would be Rosetti, he should be the one to participate, not Merlin... what were you thinking?" Lulcia stomped her foot, not understanding her grandfather's thoughts. "Lulcia, don't say that, I've already made up my mind, and I won't change it," Old Taylor said seriously, his face stern. The adventurers in Reksem Guild were already in an uproar, discussing and speculating about Merlin's participation. "Guild Master must be crazy, choosing Merlin to participate, what a waste!" "Yeah, Merlin and Hobbs, that drunkard, are both black iron adventurers, what can they do to compete?" "I think Guild Master is just making a random choice, if he's going to choose someone, why not choose me, I'll just lose anyway, so I might as well participate too..." Hobbs, drunk and disheveled, leaned on Merlin's shoulder, and said with a smile, "Wow, you're going to make a name for yourself, if you become famous, don't forget to pay me back for the drinks..." Merlin pushed Hobbs away, and walked out of the crowd, coming to stand in front of Old Taylor, and smiling meaningfully. "Guild Master, you have good eyesight!" "Choosing me is indeed a wise decision."

title: Chapter 1 — Another Half of the Ruins Chart
content:
Chapter 1 — Another Half of the Ruins Chart

Volume 27 · Chapter 1

In Copenhagen, the capital of the Kingdom of Denmark, the Adventurers Guild Headquarters is located.

This organization has existed for several hundred years and possesses a unique adventurer culture.

Adventurers define themselves as a profession that champions freedom, loves adventure, and is eager to help others.

This characteristic has continued to this day, constantly spreading the free-spirited adventurous ethos.

Several centuries ago, someone suddenly raised their arm in a rallying cry and established the world’s first Adventurers Guild in Copenhagen, earning remuneration by helping those in need. This business model became the foundation for adventurers, attracting countless like-minded individuals to join.

Thus was born the prototype of the Adventurers Guild Headquarters. From its inception, it aimed to gather scattered forces, break free from state control, and become a unique power in the world.

As the ranks of adventurers grew stronger and expanded across the globe, the Adventurers Guild Headquarters gradually shifted away from undertaking adventures itself, instead fully assuming the role of an administrator.

The Adventurers Guild Headquarters is responsible for managing and evaluating Adventurers Guilds around the world. At the top level lies the Arbitrators Association, composed of five arbitrator members, with the leader known as the Chairman.

Entering the Arbitrators Association does not require immense strength, but rather leadership and management skills, as well as foresight to steer the development of the adventurer industry.

To prevent unequal resource distribution, no adventurer is allowed to hold a position on the Arbitration Committee. Although the Arbitrators Association operates independently from adventurers, it remains closely tied to them.

The operational status of Adventurers Guilds, mission success rates, and member strength levels are all evaluated by the Arbitration Committee, which ultimately determines their appropriate rank.

At this moment, within the Arbitration Committee of the Copenhagen Adventurers Guild Headquarters, the five members were discussing preparations for the quadrennial Adventurer Competition.

Mr. Dawson, the Chairman, sat at the head of the five-person meeting table, his expression deep and troubled, as if stumped by some difficult problem.

Mr. Dawson had once been an adventurer himself, but due to insufficient strength, he was slowly eliminated from active duty before joining the Adventurers Guild Headquarters. He climbed step by step to reach the position of Chairman of the Arbitrators Association, becoming one of the managers of adventurers.

The other four arbitrator committee members—tall, short, fat, and thin—were different from Dawson; they did not come from backgrounds as adventurers but hailed from other professions: a banker, a merchant, a sailor, and a fallen noble. These individuals ended up managing adventurers through various coincidences.

Mr. Dawson looked at his four colleagues, cleared his throat, and said seriously, “This year’s competition will be held in Budapest, the capital of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. There lies the magnificent Arminius Colosseum, covering an area of 260,000 square meters, making it very suitable for hosting the event. By my calculations, adventurers from around the world have already begun arriving there.”

The other four members nodded in agreement. They had no objections to the choice of venue. Past competitions had been held in various locations worldwide; the last time was in the Holy Roman Empire, where even the Pope came to observe the matches. It was only natural for it to be hosted in the Austro-Hungarian Empire this time.

“I have invited many guests to watch the competition,” the tall member said, nodding to the others. “There is Sindadir, the Elf King of the United Kingdom; Princess Margaret of the Kingdom of France; and Alfonso, the State Preceptor of the Kingdom of Spain. They represent their respective factions and wish to acknowledge the achievements made since the establishment of adventurers.”

“The Elf King? It is good news that a leader of another race is willing to attend,” the tall member added. “It proves our efforts have been recognized by non-human races.”

The thin member smiled. “Perhaps we can expand the adventurer industry into the United Kingdom, where other races gather.”

“The Elf King showing goodwill toward us for the first time is a good omen. Perhaps we can take this opportunity to discuss matters further,” Mr. Dawson said, somewhat proudly, believing that under his management, the adventurer industry was thriving.

Little did he know, the Elf King’s willingness to visit a human nation was entirely to meet Merlin and to adopt Chris as his adopted daughter.

“Then... are we really going to increase the number of Purple-Gold adventurers this time? Dawson, do you perhaps have someone in mind?” The fat member looked at Dawson. Rumor had it that suitable candidates would be selected to advance to Purple-Gold adventurer status, but he didn’t know if the news was true or false.

“I do have such plans,” Mr. Dawson paused before continuing. “Currently, there are only five existing Purple-Gold adventurers. The number is indeed too small.” He went on, “With many powerful adventurers emerging recently, injecting fresh blood into the ranks of Purple-Gold adventurers is something I truly intend to do.”

“Then who would be suitable? It feels like the overall gap between candidates isn’t very large...” asked the short member tentatively.

“That depends on their performance,” Mr. Dawson said cryptically. “Our headquarters will prepare a unique prize for the champion this time.”

“Oh? I wonder what it could be?” asked the short member.

“A half-route map to the Ancient Gods’ Ruins, Asgard,” Mr. Dawson said, with a hint of pride.

Upon hearing this, the other four members were instantly shocked. Such a rare treasure was extraordinary.

Almost everyone familiar with history knew that the Ancient Gods were incredibly powerful and possessed various legendary artifacts renowned throughout the world!

If one could find the ruins of Asgard and locate the artifacts inside, it would be wealth beyond estimation!

“Dawson... this is a treasure that money cannot buy!” exclaimed the fat member, his eyes wide with horror.

“This is no small matter! The ruins of Asgard... a place dreamed of by countless people!” sighed the tall member.

“Although this half-route map is precious, without the other half, it is merely an old, useless piece of paper,” Mr. Dawson shook his head and said slowly, “but using it as a prize for the competition is sufficient enough.”

“Where did you obtain this half-route map?” asked the thin member curiously.

“Thirty years ago, the Kraken, a sea monster of the North Sea, suddenly appeared in Norwegian waters, attracting numerous strong experts from all over the world to the Kingdom of Norway. Many people knew that the Kraken guarded the ruins of Asgard. Back then, everyone tried every trick to enter the ruins, but almost no one succeeded. At that time, I was just a minor adventurer trailing behind a treasure-hunting team,” Mr. Dawson paused and spoke in a low voice, “However, our former Guild Master was very clever. He used magic to secretly dive into the deep sea to search directly for the Kraken...”

“What!? Someone actually dared to dive into the deep sea and come into close contact with the North Sea Kraken!?” The short member displayed an expression of disbelief.

“That shows our former Guild Master was skilled and courageous, having the guts to do things others wouldn’t dare,” Mr. Dawson said, showing a bit of...

“But he also paid the price for his recklessness. A week later, our Guild Master’s body washed ashore, his hand tightly clutching half of the route map to the Asgard ruins.”

Everyone sighed, feeling that Dawson’s former Guild Master was somewhat lucky, though unfortunately, he paid with his life for just half a route map.

“This half-map seems precious, but its actual utility is limited. Who knows where the other half is? Unless the complete route map is pieced together, it is nothing more than worthless waste paper...” Mr. Dawson said helplessly.

Was reality truly as he thought?

Mr. Dawson probably never dreamed...

The other half of the Asgard route map was in Merlin’s hands.

title: Chapter 2 — There's an Extra Update
content:
Chapter 2 — There's an Extra Update

Volume 27 · Chapter 2

Today, the adventurers of Rexham also officially set out, heading to Budapest to participate in the Adventurers' Competition.

Chairman Old Taylor will accompany them, helping to handle various miscellaneous tasks so the three competitors can focus on the tournament.

Since Alice is participating in the Adventurers' Competition, Clodia won't stay in Rexham either, following Alice as part of her support group.

Although Clodia has been busy training Alice recently, she hasn't forgotten her mission and still harbors dissatisfaction towards Merlin, not forgetting her plan to expose this man's "hypocritical" mask.

However, during Alice's hellish training, Merlin has been by her side, showing concern for his wife's progress, leaving Clodia without a good excuse and forcing her to endure.

Clodia doesn't believe Merlin can wear his "hypocritical" mask for long; he'll definitely slip up on the road, and when that happens, she'll separate them and bring Alice and Chris back to the Snowy Mountains - isn't that a natural course of events?

As someone who's been through this, Clodia thinks Alice is currently blinded by "love," and once she sees the true nature of this bad man, she'll definitely come to her senses and obediently follow Clodia back to the Snowy Mountains.

Outside Rexham town, the residents spontaneously came to see them off, led by Lord Austin, the town lord.

"Mr. Taylor, this time it's up to you. I hope you can achieve new heights in the competition. Every person in Rexham will be proud of you."

"Don't worry, Lord Austin. This is our shared glory. We won't disappoint everyone's expectations." Old Taylor replied politely.

"You can charge all your expenses to me. As the lord of Rexham, I want to contribute what little I can."

"No need to be so extravagant. If possible, Lord Austin, just bring out some of your private collection of fine wine." Old Taylor said with a hint of a smile.

"Those are my family treasures! You old man have been eyeing them for a long time?" Lord Austin laughed, pointing at Old Taylor, and generously said, "Alright, if you can enter the top three, I'll definitely bring out my private collection."

The two exchanged smiles, being old acquaintances who naturally wouldn't engage in too much formal talk, instead joking around on the spot.

Not far away, Chris, held in Alice's arms, gazed at her mother with curious eyes.

Chris occasionally stroked Alice's hair, occasionally touched her face with small hands, as if searching for something.

Alice will bring Chris along on this trip, as there's no one at home to take care of her, and she doesn't trust leaving this little one with others.

Alice noticed Chris's strange behavior and asked in puzzlement, "Chris, what's wrong? Why are you staring at Mommy nonstop today? Is it... because..."

"It's not..." Chris looked like she wanted to say something but hesitated.

"Then why?" Alice thought for a moment, suddenly realizing, "Could it be because Mommy was away for a few days, so you can't recognize Mommy anymore?"

"Chris isn't a foolish child, she can recognize Mommy. Mommy smells nice, just sniff and you'll know." Chris said in a childish tone.

"Then... why..." Alice furrowed her brows, not believing Chris, so young, could have any worries.

"Because when Mommy came back, she had many injuries. I don't know if she's better now, I'm so worried..." Chris fidgeted with her small fingers.

Alice was suddenly touched, her emotions stirred by her adorable daughter.

She realized Chris was still young, and for a child, Daddy and Mommy might be the whole world.

If something happened between her and Merlin? Chris might feel like the sky was falling, feeling very uneasy...

Alice smiled understandingly, stroking Chris's small nose, and said affectionately, "Don't worry, Mommy has already recovered. Those were just superficial wounds, nothing serious. Now Mommy is fine and can even lift you high~"

Chris was lifted high, her hair fluttering happily, "Yay~"

"My little darling~" Alice hugged Chris tightly, rubbing her cheek against her daughter's face.

Behind them, Clodia couldn't help but feel displeased, her heart involuntarily turning sour. Her student had become a mother, and she was forced to endure the mother-daughter sparkle, a truly unpleasant feeling.

"Don't be so embarrassing. Can't you have some dignity as a mother? How can you teach this child properly like this?" Clodia forced herself to say.

"Huh?" Alice heard her teacher's words and paused, speaking seriously, "I won't be like you, Teacher. I want my child to have more freedom."

"You're saying what? Children won't grow up properly without strict training. Don't you understand this principle?" Clodia argued strongly, her views differing greatly from Alice's. She felt Chris, though young, was clever, and with proper cultivation, might surpass Alice's expectations.

"I know what I experienced when I was young. You, Teacher, don't know how to take care of children; you only know how to impose your own will on others," Alice said, holding Chris, stubbornly.

"I can listen to you on other matters, but not this."

"You're not doing this motherhood thing right, you'll raise a useless child." Clodia said, frowning.

"That's my choice, so don't worry about it, Teacher." Alice said stubbornly.

"Shouldn't you ask Chris her own wishes? Your current method is no different from mine," Clodia sneered, then smiled kindly at Chris, "Little darling, do you want to learn magic with Grandma?"

"Magic?" Chris's big eyes sparkled with curiosity.

Alice forced a smile, trying to guide Chris's choice, "Learning that is very tiring, and it's not necessary, right?"

Clodia's forehead showed faint signs of anger, and she said slyly, "After learning, you can protect Daddy and Mommy so they won't get hurt~"

"Really?" Chris's eyes lit up, successfully piqued her interest. Being able to protect Daddy and Mommy was very tempting.

"I want to learn! Magic!!!" Chris exclaimed.

Clodia's face showed a smug expression, challengingly saying to Alice, "Did you hear that? She wants to learn herself. Let's see her talent!"

"Teacher!!!" Alice was furious, glaring at Clodia.

"Using me as bait to trick the child into learning magic is too despicable!"

title: Chapter 3 — Chris's Talent (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 3 — Chris's Talent (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 27 · Chapter 3

I want to learn magic so I can protect Mama and never get hurt again! *8* Chris smiled happily, completely unaware of how hard it was to practice magic.

“Chris is such a good kid!” Clodia praised her—then, coldly turning to Alice, “Did you hear? This child is willing to endure hardship for you, so let her down and let me see her talent!”

“I—”

Alice hesitated, her gaze lingering on Chris, who looked so adoringly at her, making her reluctant to let her suffer.

But Alice thought carefully—Chris seemed to have never shown any innate talent for magic or spellcasting? Maybe Chris was just an ordinary child, and Clodia would have to give up.

Alice hesitated for a moment before finally lowering little Chris to the ground, praying silently that she was just an ordinary child.

Clodia casually pulled the already withered wildflower from the ground and approached Chris—

“Chris, try focusing on this withered wildflower?”

“Focus?” Chris chewed her fingernail, not quite understanding.

“Focus means...” Clodia thought for a moment, recalling how she’d taught Alice when she was young, “letting your mind drift into imagination, like dreaming.”

“Dreaming?” Chris giggled. “I dream about so many delicious things!”

“Exactly like that. Now look at the withered wildflower in my hand, and enter your focus—try to make it move.”

“Oh! I...” Chris stared at the withered wildflower in Clodia’s hand, then closed her eyes and began imagining her favorite buttercream cake. *oF* full-on playing

Clodia watched the withered wildflower in her hand. If Chris were a child with innate magic talent, she should have had extraordinary focus power even as a child, capable of moving small objects.

Now, with no wind around, even a slight movement of Clodia’s withered wildflower would prove Chris’s success.

But little Chris seemed to be straining hard—her tiny body trembling repeatedly—

“Keep going, Chris! You can do it!” Clodia focused intently, still encouraging her.

“Uh-uh-uh-uh-uh!” Chris’s shoulders shook violently before suddenly opening her eyes.

“What’s going on?” Alice gasped, thinking Chris couldn’t possibly have such surprising talent—

“Gurgle...” Chris’s stomach made a noise, already protesting hunger. “Papa, I’m sorry—I was just thinking about the cake and got hungry!”

“???”

Alice watched her precious daughter—of course, she was just an ordinary child with no magic or martial talent.

Though a little disappointed, it was fine. Chris wouldn’t have to suffer so much for training.

Alice picked up Chris from the ground without scolding her, instead asking gently, “Did you get hungry so fast?”

“Yeah...” Chris lifted her head, smiling. “Just thinking about the cake made me hungry.”

“You’re such a greedy little thing,” Alice tapped Chris’s forehead with her forehead.

A light autumn wind brushed past, and Clodia’s withered wildflower finally moved—though not due to Chris’s focus.

Clodia scowled at the withered wildflower, thinking, *What nonsense!* Chris was Alice’s child, after all? Why couldn’t she even do something so simple?

Alice had learned focus at two years old—though she hadn’t developed magic or spellcasting, she could still move small objects. Why couldn’t Chris even do this? Was she just an ordinary child, lacking her mother’s talents?

*Damn!* It was all the fault of that useless man! Let him go to hell! If I had a student like this, I’d have a prodigy!

Clodia tossed the withered wildflower to the ground, her glare fixed on Merlin in the distance, adding more resentment to her anger.

In the distance, Merlin felt an overwhelming negative energy toward himself. Seeing Clodia glare at him—

What the hell? Why was this old woman looking at me like that? Had I done something wrong?

Merlin was confused, not knowing what he’d done wrong. Just then, the guard captain Pless approached, walking over excitedly.

“Merlin! I heard Hobbs says you’re also entering the competition? Really?”

“Yes, I did.” Merlin, seeing this scruffy fellow, responded coolly.

“Merlin, are you planning a one-day trip to Budapest?” Pless laughed heartily.

“What do you mean?” Merlin arched an eyebrow.

“Well, since you’re going up anyway, why not take the chance to visit Budapest? *~” Pless jabbed his elbow into Merlin’s chest, his eyes subtly hinting at the beauty of Budapest’s women.

“Who says I’m going for a vacation? I’m the main player!” Merlin said proudly, convinced that Old Master Taylor had made a wise choice by selecting him—he’d easily reclaim the title.

“Come on, everyone knows you’re just a placeholder for this competition. You’ll need to show up for your wife and Karl to get some presence anyway,” Pless laughed, assuming Merlin’s participation was just for a three-person team.

“Whatever you say.” Merlin shrugged, not bothering to explain. He thought, *If the competition is live-streamed worldwide, this could be my chance to rise from the ashes! This is the perfect opportunity to make a name for myself!*

In front of them, Old Master Taylor was preparing to bid farewell to Austin, Duke of Osmund.

“Then let’s go now. Lucian, I’ll need you to take care of the guild while I’m away.”

“Don’t worry, Grandpa, the guild is always under my management,” Lucian said with a sigh, still not understanding why he’d chosen Merlin to enter the competition, but since it was his grandfather’s decision, he had no choice.

“Lucian, Dad will do well this time—don’t you give me any trouble?” Karl scratched his head, hoping his daughter would cheer him up.

“Just don’t embarrass Reckserum,” Lucian said coldly.

“Hmph...” Karl sighed in disappointment.

Old Taylor smiled at Austin, Duke of Osmund. “Then—”

“Wait! Guildmaster!” Rosetti, clutching the Da Vinci, burst out of the city gates.

“Rosetti? What are you doing here?” Karl asked, confused.

Rosetti panted, lifting her head and smiling. “We’re also going to Budapest!”

“You’re going too?” Old Taylor looked at Da Vinci.

Rosetti lowered the Da Vinci back into her waist. “Yes, Da Vinci wants to see Budapest’s library, and I... also want to watch your performance live. *~”

“Yes, Budapest’s library has many books,” Da Vinci said without expression.

Old Taylor nodded at them. “Alright, then let’s go.”

Austin watched the carriage disappear from sight, recalling how his weak son Arnold had been in a bad mood lately and needed a good scolding.

When everyone had left, no one noticed—

The withered wildflower Clodia had discarded on the ground had miraculously revived.

In this season of withered things, a single blooming wildflower stood out.

title: Chapter 4 — Alchemist and the First Blood Clan
content:
Chapter 4 — Alchemist and the First Blood Clan

Volume 27 · Chapter 4

Austro-Hungarian Empire, Budapest.

Elite adventurers from all over the world flocked here, preparing to participate in the quadrennial grand festival.

The one in charge of this tournament was not the Austro-Hungarian royal family, but rather the socialite of Budapest’s noble circles, Countess Bathory—also praised by many as the most beautiful widow among the nobility.

This woman, Bathory, was none other than the infamous figure: one of the three original vampires of the bloodline.

Due to a disagreement with the mad Dracula over their ideals, she had parted ways with him long ago, choosing not to follow Dracula’s path of founding a nation.

After becoming a vampire, Bathory had chosen to live in extreme secrecy, constantly migrating from place to place.

Because of her eternal, undying life and the violent bloodlust that plagued her, Bathory could not stay in one place for long. She had to be extremely careful to avoid others discovering her true identity.

Unlike Dracula, who was extreme and harbored grand ambitions, Bathory had no such aspirations. In fact, among the three original vampires, she was likely the weakest in terms of power.

This woman had walked through a thousand years of time, witnessing the rise and fall of civilizations, the ebb and flow of history, and the collapse of once-great dynasties into the river of time.

Bathory knew full well that she was a bloodthirsty monster, incompatible with humanity. She could never return to her former self and could only survive by constantly changing identities and hiding among humans, which gave her a semblance of peace.

A thousand years had taught Bathory one truth: Dracula’s vision was impossible. In an era dominated by humans, it was better to become one of them than to enslave them—this way, survival would be far easier.

Bathory had assumed many identities. Relying on her ageless beauty, she had gained numerous advantages.

She had once been a dancer in a tavern, a queen consort of a declining kingdom, and even disguised herself as a withered old farmer...

And now, Bathory was a countess, the most beautiful widow in Budapest’s noble circles.

Thirty years ago, Bathory had wandered into Budapest and caught the eye of an old count. They quickly fell in love and married.

But when the old count accidentally discovered Bathory’s secret, he was silently killed, and his death was announced to the public as a heart attack.

Freed from the old count’s constraints, Bathory thrived in Budapest. Countless young and promising noble sons sought her favor, hoping for a taste of her charm. She even exchanged flirtatious glances with the Austro-Hungarian emperor, securing the rights to host the Adventurers’ Tournament.

Though she claimed to be in her fifties, Bathory retained the youthful appearance she had had a thousand years ago when she first met Cain. Many believed she possessed the secret to eternal youth, unaware that she held a fraction of Cain’s divine power, granting her immortality.

At this moment, in the basement of the countess’s mansion, Bathory’s bloodlust had unexpectedly flared up in the dead of night. Like an addict, she knelt on the ground, her delicate body trembling as if her flesh and spirit were being torn apart by countless ants.

*...Why is it so slow?!*

Furious, Bathory swept a vase off the table, her slender neck now marked with red scratches from her own claws. Her long hair flew wildly, making her look like a demon in the flesh.

Unlike Dracula, who had sired countless vampires as his minions to conquer cities and lands, Bathory had only created a single thrall to fetch her food when it was inconvenient for her to do so.

Moreover, Bathory never caused too much of a disturbance. She would never prey on the humans in her own territory. Instead, she chose a safer method: secretly purchasing slaves to feed on, making it difficult for anyone to detect the presence of a bloodthirsty monster in Budapest.

But now, Bathory had ordered her thrall to find prey long ago, and yet there was still no sign of it.

This abnormal situation infuriated her. The waves of bloodlust tormented her to the point where she was neither human nor demon, and she even felt the urge to go on a killing spree in Budapest.

Bathory had no desire to kill humans, let alone drink their blood. But the cursed bloodlust made it impossible for her to control her bestial urges.

*Thump, thump, thump—*

A knock echoed from the cellar door. Bathory’s head snapped up, her face twisting into a feral snarl as she bared her sharp fangs.

If anyone outside saw her like this, those young and promising noble sons would not just flee—they’d be too terrified to even think of running.

“Did you bring it back? You useless thing! Why does it take you so long to buy a single slave?! Get in here!” Bathory roared in fury.

The cellar door swung open, and a blackened corpse was thrown at her feet.

The corpse had a ghastly face, its leathery wings drooping—clearly not a slave, but a dead vampire!

*...Huh?*

Bathory was like a bucket of cold water had been dumped over her. She rapidly calmed down, staring at the lifeless body on the floor. Her unease grew, for this was her one and only thrall!

*What happened? It was supposed to go buy a slave for me to feed on... Why is it dead out there?*

Bathory’s mind raced, unable to settle. She suddenly lifted her head, glaring at the cellar doorway, where a strange figure stood watching her in disarray.

“Heh heh heh...” The mysterious figure outside let out a cold, mocking laugh. “Countess Bathory, a woman of fifty-plus years who maintains the appearance of an eighteen-year-old girl, the most radiant beauty in Budapest, known in noble circles as the ageless goddess. You’ve had affairs with many powerful nobles, even enchanting the Austro-Hungarian emperor to the point of madness...”

Bathory remained kneeling on the ground, her expression shifting to terror. She looked up at the figure in the doorway, realizing the situation had taken a dangerous turn. Her true form had been exposed—no matter who this person was, she could not let them leave alive!

“My information is flawless. You truly are a woman who brings ruin to nations,” the mysterious figure said, spreading his arms in a sarcastic tone. “But what a surprise! The real you locks yourself in a cellar every night, a wretched creature craving blood! Ha ha ha! How fascinating!”

Bathory forcibly suppressed her bloodlust, struggling to her feet. Her nails grew at a visible speed.

She glanced at the dead thrall on the floor, then fixed her predatory gaze on the mysterious figure at the cellar door, unleashing the overwhelming presence of an original vampire.

“Who are you?! How dare you barge in here and kill my loyal thrall!”

“Beautiful Countess Bathory, it’s only natural you don’t recognize me. After all, not everyone is qualified to know the darkness of this world.”

The mysterious figure slowly stepped into the cellar. By the flickering torchlight, his features became barely visible.

He appeared young and frail, with golden hair hanging limply by his ears. A red gemstone glowed brightly on his chest.

“Allow me to introduce myself. I am from the Dark Guild, Phoenix.”

“As for my name...”

The countess could call him Flamel.

title: Chapter 5 — No Other Choice
content:
Chapter 5 — No Other Choice

Volume 27 · Chapter 5

“Flamel...” Bathory had never heard the name, but she was vaguely aware of the Phoenix Society—an organization rumored to be the strongest and most mysterious of the dark powers.

“Good evening, Lady Bathory. I apologize for disturbing you so late.” Flamel’s words were apologetic, but his expression and tone held no sincerity.

“I have no dealings with the Phoenix Society whatsoever. Why did you kill my servant?” Bathory demanded, furious.

“Lack of dealings doesn’t mean we won’t approach you. We have a matter that requires your cooperation, and we hope you’ll assist us willingly.” Flamel glanced at the dead vampire food on the floor and sighed helplessly. “I didn’t originally intend to kill your servant. But it was too tight-lipped, refusing to reveal your location no matter what. So I may have been a bit too rough... I didn’t expect vampires to be so fragile. It was just a...”

Bathory’s veins bulged on her forehead. Flamel’s casual tone ignited a storm of rage within her.

Clearly, he felt not a shred of guilt for killing her loyal servant. Instead, he adopted a condescending attitude, ordering her to cooperate!

Bathory’s eyes were bloodshot, her expression ferocious, her mouth stretched into a grin revealing fangs as she roared, “Lies! You expect me to help you after killing my servant? Don’t think this will be swept under the rug!”

In an instant, a swarm of bats materialized before Bathory, their piercing shrieks threatening to shatter eardrums.

Though Bathory wasn’t a frontline fighter, as one of the three First-Generation vampires, her power was no joke.

The terrifying bat swarm could disorient enemies, and even among Saint-tier elites, blood would be drained in an instant.

Watching the ferocious bat assault, Flamel’s senses blurred, his body swaying with the sound waves, on the verge of collapse.

Suddenly! Bathory lunged from the bat swarm like lightning, using their cover to catch Flamel completely off guard.

“Die!”

She drove her sharp nails straight through Flamel’s heart, blood spraying everywhere, painting a gruesome picture on the cellar wall.

“Cough!” Flamel spat blood, his expression incredulous, never expecting Bathory to be so decisive.

“This is what you get for killing my loyal servant! You fool! Go to hell and repent for your recklessness!” Bathory’s arm remained embedded in Flamel’s chest as she cursed him savagely.

Flamel slowly raised his head, blood trickling from his lips. He gave Bathory an eerie smile, and the red gem on his chest suddenly blazed with blinding light!

“W-what is this?!” Bathory’s eyes temporarily blinded, unable to open, she could only feel the gem on Flamel’s chest shining impossibly bright.

The dazzling light faded, and the situation had taken a dramatic turn.

The near-death Flamel was fully restored, his pierced heart showing not a single wound.

But Bathory’s heart had been mysteriously pierced, leaving her gravely injured, blood splashing everywhere!

“Hahaha...” Flamel’s enigmatic smile revealed nothing of what he had just done.

“Y-you!” Bathory’s terror deepened, her finger trembling as she stared at him, speechless.

Her body tumbled down the steps, collapsing on the ground, barely breathing. For a First-Generation vampire, a heart wound was a serious danger.

Yet Bathory possessed one-third of Cain’s divine power; she wouldn’t die so easily. The shocking hole in her heart was slowly healing.

“Not bad for a First-Generation vampire who once plagued France a millennium ago. Your healing ability is indeed extraordinary—heart pierced and still alive? Impressive, truly impressive~” Flamel’s lips curled into a sinister smile, even clapping in admiration.

“Ah...” Bathory lay weakly on the ground, gasping for breath, waiting for her wounds to close. She trembled with fear at this man’s power, wondering what monsters made up the Phoenix Society.

Flamel calmly approached her, his gaze pitying, looking down as if she were an ant he could crush at any time.

“You don’t know much about our Phoenix Society, do you? Attacking us was a foolish choice. Any single member could deal with your kind of vampires as easily as playing house~.”

From his coat, Flamel produced two black cones, similar to the alchemical spears Merlin had captured, but each embedded with a small red gem.

He laughed loudly, driving the two alchemical weapons deep into Bathory’s wrists, pinning her to the ground.

“I wanted to talk to you properly, Lady Bathory. But you weren’t calm. I had no choice but to clear your head a bit~.”

Bathory looked at her hands nailed to the floor, a strange force suppressing her, leaving her powerless. Even her heart’s healing slowed dramatically.

She didn’t know what method this man used to inhibit Cain’s divine power. She only knew he was beyond her reach, able to play her like a toy.

At that moment, fear finally dominated Bathory. Her gaze trembled as she looked at Flamel, her lips quivering.

“...What do you want?”

“Good. Now you’re finally willing to listen~.” Flamel crouched down, smiling. “We understand you’re the organizer of this Adventurers’ Tournament. So we need you to do us a small favor.”

“...A favor?” Bathory asked nervously.

“We need you to rig the tournament arena. You’re in a perfect position to make it happen, right?” Flamel chuckled.

“Why do this? Are you planning to kill all the adventurers here?” Bathory’s mind raced with dark possibilities.

“Do you take our great Phoenix Society for senseless butchers? Don’t underestimate us. Our dream is to bring transformation to the entire world! Senseless slaughter is the last thing we’d do~.” Flamel tilted his head, slightly annoyed by being misunderstood.

“...” Bathory felt this was too dangerous for her. With a forced tone, she said, “I won’t do this for you.”

“Tsk tsk tsk~” Flamel clicked his tongue, wagging a finger as he lifted Bathory’s chin, studying her beautiful face. “Lady, you have no right to refuse.”

“If you refuse, I’ll expose your identity to the world.”

“Think about it—a monster that feeds on humans. Where would you possibly find a place to live then?”

“Hahaha...”

title: Chapter 7 — Slip of the Tongue (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 7 — Slip of the Tongue (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 27 · Chapter 7

Half a month later, Rexham Alton's carriage was about to arrive at Budapest.

Da Vinci didn't like crowds, so she hid alone in the carriage, reading a book with earplugs in—nothing from the outside world concerned her.

Karl claimed he was resting up for the tournament, but in reality he passed out immediately, snoring so loudly it echoed throughout the carriage.

Old Taylor and Karl had already heard about Chris, and while they were startled to learn Merlin and Alice had a child, they didn't press for details.

After all, Chris looked very much like Merlin and Alice. If not for the timing being off, they would have thought the child was theirs.

But Old Taylor felt somewhat guilty. Ever since he'd filled in the wrong information back then, which made Merlin and Alice husband and wife in name only, he had been hoping to find an opportunity to correct this error at the Adventurers Guild headquarters.

Now that the two of them had a child with inherited bloodline, Old Taylor felt quite pressured, unsure of how to handle this matter.

Seeing how much Merlin and Alice both liked Chris, this situation was tricky. Having a child out of wedlock—was that good or bad?

The Adventurer Arena Tournament was about to open, and there would be a chance to meet Chairman Dawson of the Arbitration Committee. Old Taylor planned to take this opportunity to correct his past mistake.

But he needed to find a chance to ask Merlin and Alice's opinion—whether they'd let Chairman Dawson help change their status from nominal spouses to partners among registered adventurers.

Rossetti was bored sitting in the carriage, and Da Vinci had also drifted into a deep reading trance, so he went to amuse Chris.

Coincidentally, Chris was feeling quite proud, and performed the rhyme Merlin had taught her, kicking her little legs and spinning around as she sang—

"Summer quietly passes away, leaving little secrets, pressing you down, not letting you breathe~"

Hearing Chris sing such a bizarre rhyme, Rossetti felt a cold sweat bead on his forehead, thinking complicatedly: Why does this song sound so terrible? Who taught it?

But Rossetti didn't want to hurt the little one's self-esteem, so he swallowed his words and offered a forced compliment instead.

"So amazing~ Miss Chris, who taught you this song? It's really so unique~"

"Hmph hmph~" Little Chris put her hands on her hips and said proudly, "Daddy taught it!"

"Oh, it's Daddy, no wonder it's so amazing, hahaha."

Rossetti forced a smile, wondering in his heart whether Merlin and Alice were really okay with raising children this way. What kind of nonsense was he teaching!

Alice heard her precious daughter's words, the vein on her forehead twitching visibly. She glared at Merlin and whispered, "What indecent stuff have you been teaching Chris while I was gone?"

"Huh? What's indecent about it?" Merlin asked back blankly.

"Only you would do something like that! Don't I know it well enough?" Alice felt Chris couldn't possibly learn this garbage—what if she turned out to be as shameless as Merlin?

A bead of cold sweat rolled down Merlin's forehead.

"Don't bring up my dark history, give me some face."

"Can't you teach her something else?" Alice grumbled resentfully. "Other kids her age are already learning refined painting and music. Ours is still learning the songs you sang when you were a host!"

"I'm not incapable of teaching other things," Merlin said helplessly.

"My teacher already tested her before. Chris has no talent for cultivating mana or battle aura. From now on, she'll just be an ordinary child," Alice said, putting on a motherly face and worrying about Chris's future.

"It's fine. Not learning magic or martial arts isn't a bad thing. Being ordinary is nice too," Merlin said. He didn't think much of it; some things can't be forced.

"Although it's less burdensome without needing to cultivate magic and martial skills, just knowing Chris will fall behind other people's children makes me so unwilling to accept it!"

Alice grew quite huffy and said firmly, "When we get back, I definitely need to find a way to properly nurture Chris. Even if she has no cultivation talent, I'll make her a prodigy in other areas. Yes! That decision is made!"

"Shouldn't we ask Chris's opinion?" Merlin asked tentatively, seeing Alice's full momentum.

"I'm her mother; I wouldn't harm her. Do I need to ask her opinion on things I decide?" Alice said with a completely serious expression.

"???" Merlin's expression turned strange, and he thought oddly in his heart—so this is what happens when a dragon-slaying hero ultimately becomes a dragon! What difference was there between Alice's attitude toward Chris now and her own teacher's attitude toward her when she was young?!

Meanwhile, Rossetti was still continuing to amuse Chris. "Do your parents fight often at home?"

"Not at all! Mommy and Daddy are very loving!" Little Chris retorted puffed up. "When Mommy isn't home, I keep missing her every day. I couldn't sleep until very late every night, and after a few days I couldn't help but go out looking for Mommy!"

Alice's face flushed. She had assumed that when she wasn't home, Merlin would be overjoyed, since he always complained about liking to meddle in other people's affairs and feeling trapped at home. But hearing Chris's words seemed somewhat different from what she had imagined.

{End}
{This}
{God}
{Site}

Merlin snatched Chris up from the ground in a flash, putting on a serious expression. "How did I teach you to speak? Food can be eaten carelessly, but words cannot be spoken carelessly."

Chris pouted grievously. "Chris isn't speaking carelessly! Mommy also says those things—when we've been with Grandma recently, she always says Daddy is super handsome, and that she likes spending time with Daddy. Mommy also said Daddy is a gentle person, and that she really likes—"

"Huh?" Merlin's face darkened. What was this? Was it something he'd said just to coax Claude away?

"Eek!!!"

Alice looked as though she'd been struck by lightning. She hadn't expected her private words with her teacher to be spilled by Chris, and in an instant she was so ashamed she wished she could dig a hole and hide.

So Alice quickly snatched Chris from Merlin's arms and said to her with a stern face, "Don't talk nonsense. Mommy never said those things. Those were dreams you had while sleeping. Do you understand? Don't treat dreams as reality from now on."

Chris sat on Alice's lap, feeling even more aggrieved. At such a young age, she didn't understand what wrong she'd done. She was telling the truth, yet being treated like a bad child who lies. Being Mom and Dad's baby was so hard!

Rossetti frowned, his expression strange. What were these two doing? Chris felt caught right in the middle, caught between them, under so much pressure.

"Hmph!" Cloelia, sitting not far away, snorted coldly. No matter what the family of three did, she could smell the sour sweetness in the air. Being excluded made her extremely annoyed. If not for Alice and Chris's relationship, she really wanted to stab that stinky man Merlin with her sword.

Old Taylor redirected his gaze toward Cloelia opposite him and asked with a smile, "I've heard you're Alice's teacher who lives on the Great Snow Mountain. Your student is truly excellent. From that naive wandering girl she once was to the independent adventurer she is today, she has experienced a great deal."

"My student—I know her well enough myself. No need for you to evaluate her. Also, I don't like speaking with men. Can you keep quiet?" Cloelia said coldly, clearly having no desire to communicate with anyone.

Old Taylor felt a trace of embarrassment. He had wanted to chat with Alice's teacher, but didn't expect the person to be so peculiarly temperamental. "Haha, well then I won't disturb you further. But I notice they seem more and more like a couple. I wonder if that's a good thing or a bad one? Clearly back then they held great hostility toward each other and could fight at any moment."

"Huh? More and more like a couple? What do you mean by that?" Cloelia suddenly lifted her head.

"Don't you know? Merlin and Alice aren't formally married. They're only listed as spouses in the Adventurers Guild records," Old Taylor said in surprise.

Cloelia's brows suddenly furrowed. It was as though a bolt of thunder had exploded above her head. She had inadvertently overheard something incredible!

So Cloelia's expression grew serious. She deliberately lowered her voice and secretly began communicating with Old Taylor, behind everyone's backs.

"Not formally married?"

"Please tell me the details of this. I'm very interested."

(-ω-)
<<<END SOURCE>>>

title: Chapter 8 — Show-Off Convention (Part 1)
content:
Chapter 8 — Show-Off Convention (Part 1)

Volume 27 · Chapter 8

The carriage carrying Rexham and his party slowly rolled into Budapest.

As the capital of the Greater Austro-Hungarian Empire, the city was bustling with liveliness, rivaling even the prosperity of London.

With the Adventurers' Grand Tournament about to begin, the city had already entered a festive frenzy. The thick celebratory atmosphere was everywhere—street vendors had started hawking their stockpiled Austro-Hungarian local specialties. Many citizens even waved flags, cheering for their favorite adventurers.

This intense tournament atmosphere infected everyone who arrived in Budapest. It was clear just how much attention the quadrennial Adventurers' Grand Tournament commanded—it was nothing short of a celebration for the human world.

The carriage stopped in front of the designated inn arranged by the Adventurers' Headquarters. This was the most luxurious inn in Budapest, often hosting nobles visiting the city. From afar, it shimmered with golden splendor, its grandeur rivaling that of a royal palace.

To ensure the smooth running of the Adventurers' Grand Tournament, this place was responsible for receiving outstanding adventurers from around the world, allowing them to rest fully before giving their all in the competition.

As soon as Rexham and his group disembarked, they saw a large group of adventurers brawling right in front of the inn.

Originally rivals in the tournament, none were willing to back down. After just a few heated words, they had come to blows, as if determined to settle their differences before the competition even began.

The inn’s servants cowered inside, too afraid to come out. They watched in terror as the wild clashes of fighting spirit and magical surges raged outside, shaking the very air.

"You trash adventurer, how dare you show your face at the tournament? Aren’t you afraid of embarrassing yourself?"

"What right do you have to say that? You’re the trash one! You can’t even kill a Porcupine Beast!"

"Shut up! Let me show you how strong I am now! Eat a Fireball!"

"Damn it! Sneak attack?! Typical of you! I’ll let you have one move, but don’t make excuses when you lose!"

Adventurers from who-knows-where were locked in a chaotic melee, their numbers adding up to over a hundred. The large-scale brawl was so intense it could have already caught the attention of the Austro-Hungarian Knights.

Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh! Magic and fighting spirit clashed repeatedly in the air. The magnificent inn now seemed on the verge of collapse under the chaos of a hundred-person battle.

Merlin looked at the utter mayhem and wondered, *What the hell are these people doing? Do they have that much bad blood?*

"Go! Go! Go!" Chris, far from being bothered by the chaos, found it all amusing. She actually started cheering on the brawling adventurers.

Alice quickly scooped up little Chris, her expression serious. "Now’s not the time for cheering. Behave."

Chris pouted, looking wronged, her silly hair drooping.

"Hmph! Just like always, adventurers are nothing but a loose, disunited bunch." Claudia commented with a cold snort through her nose.

"Oh~" Karl scratched his head, rubbing his hands together with a grin. "There are quite a few familiar faces in this tournament. Looks like I can finally get some revenge~"

"Don’t cause trouble." Old Taylor, worried his son might charge into the fray, calmly advised, "Let’s wait for the kingdom’s knights to handle this."

Rumble, rumble—another heavy carriage came to a stop beside Rexham’s group. The adventurers from Vestyevo had arrived. Guild President Ligachev, accompanied by Tanya and his attendants, stepped out of the carriage. At the sight of the massive brawl before him, he couldn’t help but furrow his brows.

"Seriously? The moment we get here, it’s already this explosive. If they’ve got this much energy, why not save it for the tournament? *Burp~*" Ligachev belched, swaying his empty bottle.

Tanya, standing behind him, frowned as she took in the chaotic scene. Her mood instantly soured.

Then, under the watchful eyes of the crowd, Tanya stepped into the chaotic throng, clenching her fists.

Bare-handed, she slammed the ground in fury. A series of deafening cracks echoed—

The earth beneath Tanya’s feet split apart, the fractures spreading rapidly outward, forming a shocking, gaping chasm.
