The powerful shockwave from her punch forced the brawling adventurers back. Some even lost their balance in the gust, landing hard on their backsides.

"Quiet down."

With just those words, Tanya single-handedly brought the chaos to a halt. The outstanding adventurers from around the world stared at the terrifying chasm in the ground, their faces filled with shock and fear. No one dared to speak loudly anymore—only hushed whispers remained.

"S-She’s Tanya! The Tanya from Vestyevo!"

"I heard she killed a powerful beast known as the Mountain God. And just recently, she single-handedly wiped out the Dark Guild, *Black Frost Eye*!"

"This girl’s a top contender for the championship. We can’t afford to provoke her..."

Though Tanya was a relatively new adventurer, her reputation had already spread far and wide. The mere mention of her name sent a chill through every adventurer present.

"Hmm?" Merlin looked at the golden-haired girl who had silenced the crowd with her overwhelming presence. She looked young, yet to possess such strength was undeniably impressive.

"She’s Tanya?" Karl, usually brimming with confidence, couldn’t help but exclaim in awe at Tanya’s display of power. "Her strength is seriously insane. Are all the new faces in this tournament monsters?"

"According to Hobbes, she’s the one with the highest bets in the underground gambling scene. If she didn’t have the skills, she wouldn’t be here." Old Taylor’s expression was grim, feeling the weight of the pressure.

"Tanya! Well done!" Ligachev, drunk as he was, gave a thumbs-up.

An attendant quickly stepped forward and whispered, "President, sober up a bit. Tanya just destroyed part of the street—we’ll have to pay for the damages."

"Ah?! Pay?!" Ligachev sobered up instantly at the mention of money. The thought of compensation made him wince—he felt Tanya had been too reckless.

"Get out of the way! Don’t block the road!"

A furious shout rang out. Several adventurers were sent flying like cannonballs, crashing into the inn’s front doors with a bang, shattering them to pieces.

Boz, the guild president of Katowice, had arrived with his three elite subordinates—Noe, Shawn, and Gabriel. The three ace adventurers of the Katowice Guild strode forward with overwhelming presence.

They made no effort to hide the disdain in their eyes. Anyone who dared stand in their way was kicked aside without hesitation.

Boz followed behind them, a faint, almost imperceptible smile playing at the corners of his mouth. Clearly, he took great pride in seeing his trained adventurers scare everyone into silence, tacitly approving of their rude behavior.

The other adventurers seethed in silence. After all, the Katowice Guild had placed second in the last tournament—no one dared to provoke them lightly. Even if they had never fought Noe, Shawn, or Gabriel before, they still didn’t dare underestimate them.

Merlin smirked, tilting his head. "These guys... their noses are practically in the clouds."

"Mama?" Chris looked up at Alice, whose expression had darkened.

Alice glared at the three of them, especially Noe. A surge of anger rose within her—she hadn’t forgotten what had happened that day. She had to find a way to get back at them.

Noe spotted Alice. The corner of his mouth curled up into a cold smirk, not bothering to take his former opponent seriously.

At the same time, Noe’s gaze fell on Tanya. His eyes gleamed with anticipation. Right in front of her, he made an unmistakably provocative gesture—

He dragged his hand across his own throat, miming a slit throat.

title: Chapter 9 — The Grand Display of Arrogance (Part 2)
content:
Chapter 9 — The Grand Display of Arrogance (Part 2)

Volume 27 · Chapter 9

Noah made an overtly provocative gesture at Tanya, as if to say—

Don’t let me run into you on the arena floor, or you’re dead.

In the face of Noah’s naked provocation, Tanya showed no reaction at all, staring at him with a blank expression, treating this nose-in-the-air fellow as if he were air itself.

Tanya’s attitude set Noah’s teeth on edge. He had been counting her as his main rival for the championship, yet she ignored him as though he didn’t exist.

Noah lowered his head, his face darkening as he ground his teeth in silent fury. Just wait. You’ll notice me soon enough. We’ll see who wins.

Tanya truly didn’t give Noah a second thought; she dismissed him as a clown trying to pick a fight. There were plenty who wanted to challenge her, but Noah wasn’t qualified—not yet.

Noah strode into the inn in a storm with Shawn and Gabriel, and not a single adventurer dared step forward to block their path, fearing they’d provoke the trio into beating them to a pulp.

Boz watched the cowed adventurers with smug satisfaction, already striking a victor’s pose even though the competition hadn’t begun.

He spotted old Taylor among the crowd, smirked inwardly, and walked over, putting on the air of an old friend to exchange pleasantries.

“Master Taylor? Four years without seeing you—still holding up well?”

Old Taylor smiled faintly, neither humble nor haughty. “I’m not dead yet.”

“Hahaha! Master Taylor’s still got that sense of humor.” Boz eyed the aged Taylor meaningfully. “You’re no spring chicken anymore. When do you plan to retire?”

“Though my body’s shot, I can still fight another ten years. As for you—you’re wasting your talents as guildmaster. Without you in the competition, can Kattowitz really take off?” Old Taylor asked with loaded intent.

The seemingly mild exchange carried a faint tang of gunpowder in the air.

Boz had intended to cow Taylor, but the old man showed no fear at all, even sneering that his guild lacked talent.

“Master Taylor, you flatter me. My guild is brimming with talent, and we’ve made thorough preparations for this tournament. I visited you recently, bringing an adventurer I’ve trained to spar with Miss Alice. Too bad you weren’t there—you’d have seen a fascinating duel end in under two seconds.”

Alice’s face darkened at the veiled insult, a vein throbbing on her forehead as Boz’s backhanded praise struck home.

“I already know about that ‘circle duel.’ It’s not to be taken seriously. Alice isn’t skilled in cramped alley fights anyway. You prepared well, but it was all cheap tricks.”

“Oh~ Master Taylor’s tongue is still as sharp as ever.” Boz’s face darkened, chuckling lightly. “I wonder which three champions Raxum is sending this time? Not just Miss Alice, I hope?”

“Impossible. Our guild has plenty of talent. We’ve carefully selected these three…” Old Taylor glanced at the people beside him and introduced them simply. “My son Karl, Alice, and Merlin. Don’t be too shocked when you see them on the field.”

Boz eyed the three skeptically, turning their names over in his mind—

Karl? Taylor’s son, but mediocre at best—no threat.
Alice? Famous, but already defeated. Noah wouldn’t break a sweat.
Merlin? A black-iron adventurer thrown in among the three? What the hell?

Boz’s expression turned odd. He thought Taylor was joking. If it was true, then Raxum must be scraping the bottom of the barrel, tossing in some random adventurer to pad the numbers.

“Hah. Are you serious?”

“Of course.” Old Taylor said confidently.

“Fine. I hope you do well.” Boz forced a smile and turned away, his earlier impression of Raxum’s competitiveness shattered.

“Hah, what a poser…” Riga chortled, weaving over with a drunken grin.

“Master Taylor! I’ve long heard of your Thunderclap Fighting Technique! I’m Riga Levchenko, guildmaster of Vistyevo—pleasure to meet you!”

“You’re too kind. Your guild’s Tanya is quite the force—I’ve heard whispers, even as a half-retired old man.” Old Taylor replied humbly, finding the drunkard easier to deal with than Boz.

“No, no, no! Our Tanya’s all talk—just a rookie with a big reputation but no skill. Besides, this is Vistyevo’s first time in the tournament; we never dared show our faces before. Please go easy on us little guilds out there, hahaha~” Riga scratched his bald head, grinning in a way that made him look endearingly foolish.

Old Taylor let out a dry chuckle, realizing the score. Those two—Boz and Riga—one a poser, the other a faker. Neither of them were any good.

Tanya watched her guildmaster from afar, her gaze drifting to Merlin. After a careful once-over, she quickly lost interest—

So this is the guy the guildmaster told me to watch out for?

The silver-haired swordsman beside him did catch her eye, though…

Never mind.

The carriage of the London Adventurers Guild rolled into the outskirts of Budapest.

Gregory arrived with Elia and Vice-Guildmaster Veyland.

Since only Elia was competing, Gregory felt far lighter than old Taylor.

“Nom nom nom nom…” Elia gnawed on a roasted leg of lamb in the carriage, her mouth stretched to ridiculous widths as if afraid someone would steal it.

Veyland always found Elia’s eating habits horrifying, like watching a starving ghost reincarnated. “We’re almost there. Stop eating. You’ve nearly finished all the food we brought. Just one person is eating us out of house and home.”

Gregory had packed the massive carriage with food to keep Elia in peak condition, spoiling her rotten.

Elia wiped grease from her mouth.

“Me…?” Veyland’s mouth twitched. “You’re just a freeloader who eats and does nothing. You haven’t earned much for the guild, yet you still make demands.”

“I can’t help eating. I’m still a kid. I need to grow.” Elia said shamelessly.

“Wake up. You’re a thirty-something auntie. Stop pretending to be young.” Veyland frowned.

“Nom nom nom…” Elia ignored his scowl, chewing as she spoke. “Teacher, I heard there’s a dragon-person in this tournament besides me. I’m interested in her.”

“Oh? The swordswoman Alice from Raxum—Taylor really hit the jackpot with her.” Gregory rasped.

“I ate a Saint Dragon’s core. She ate one too. I’ve never fought my own kind before…” Elia paused mid-chew, her eyes flashing. “It’s got me curious to beat her.”

“I wonder which of us two dragon-people is stronger?”

(n -_.)?

title: Chapter 10 — Giant Alchemy Furnace (Add More)
content:
Chapter 10 — Giant Alchemy Furnace (Add More)

Volume 27 · Chapter 10

"Without a doubt, that magic swordsman named Alice, although she also possesses the power of a great dragon, could not be your match." Gregory paused, then lowered his voice. "You are a dragon warrior in final form. You should have a little more confidence in yourself."

"Is that so?" Aelia lifted her head and said expressionlessly, "But I don't want to use the power of a dragon warrior against her. That would be boring. It's rare to meet someone who also possesses dragon bloodline power. I want to have some fun with her."

"In this tournament, your real enemy is not that magic swordsman, but someone else." Gregory said mysteriously.

"Who?" Aelia asked curiously.

"The champion of the previous tournament. He is mute. His name is Cronos."

"Hm? What kind of person is that guy? I don't seem to recall my master ever mentioning him."

"He's an enigmatic fellow. Born deformed with only one arm, his face is ugly, he has no nose, his mouth is on his forehead while his eyes are on his chin. He's withdrawn and never communicates with anyone, always alone." Gregory recalled as he spoke.

"Hearing that... sounds like a disgusting guy." Aelia felt a trace of nausea.

"Don't judge a book by its cover. Four years ago he defeated countless opponents and easily won the championship, and he looked almost effortless about it," Gregory frowned.

"Yeah, Cronos's strength is unfathomable. I don't think anyone is stronger than him in summoning arts. I wonder where he made his contracts? He possesses countless powerful summoned beasts. Four years ago I fought against him; the opponent summoned a bizarre swordsman and defeated me. Throughout the whole battle, Cronos was like someone watching a play..." Vice President Weilan said with lingering fear.

"After last year's tournament, the arbiters unanimously agreed that Cronos had the strength of a Purple Gold-ranked adventurer. I deeply agree with that judgment as well, but that strange-natured guy—"

Gregory shook his head. "He remained unmoved when faced with the opportunity to be promoted to Purple Gold-ranked adventurer. He completely ignored the arbiters' goodwill. It seemed as though he simply enjoyed watching his opponents get beaten until they cowered in defeat. He had no interest whatsoever in fame or wealth. I even felt that Cronos was just purely teasing his enemies."

"Someone with the strength of a Purple Gold-ranked adventurer? Then I'm afraid..." Aelia felt a touch of pressure. If he was roughly at the same level as her master, then she probably wasn't his match either.

"Don't be afraid. You're a dragon warrior. You have a chance to win against Cronos. After all, he's just a summoner. As long as you dodge his summons and defeat his actual body, you can win." Gregory had already figured out a plan for Aelia.

"I can only do my best..." Aelia took a deep breath and pressed on, "Since he's last year's champion, he must come from a major guild, right?"

"A major guild? Ha..." Gregory smiled without answering.

"Cronos doesn't belong to any guild at all. The guild he's registered under is just a listing guild—no guild master, no business, not even a base of operations." Vice President Weilan helped explain.

"Huh?" Aelia felt as though she'd heard something unbelievable. What kind of adventurer is that? A one-man operation?

"Cronos's registered guild only has himself as a member. Although he is indeed an adventurer, he's quite the oddity..."

In the vast Arminius Arena of Budapest.

At this moment, the arena that had been entirely built by Batouri was already complete.

Only now did Batouri vaguely begin to understand what Flamel was trying to accomplish.

The entire underground of the arena had been hollowed out, with dense pipelines crisscrossing and connecting to the crystal balls above that broadcast the tournament to the entire world.

Following the numerous pipelines downward, all the metallic pipes converged into a single enormous furnace.

So the underground of the entire Arminius Arena had been transformed by Flamel into something commonly used by alchemists—a gigantic alchemical furnace!

Beneath the arena, Flamel carefully inspected each stage of the alchemical furnace to ensure nothing would go wrong.

Batouri followed behind Flamel, filled with extreme loathing and hatred toward this man. The thought of ambushing him had surged into his mind more than once.

But whenever he saw the red gem around Flamel's neck, Batouri had to suppress his vengeful impulses. He was deeply wary of that red gem. Last time, it was that gem that had glowed—and the fatal blow that should have killed Flamel ended up landing on himself instead.

After Flamel finished inspecting every section, he nodded satisfactorily. "Not bad. Thank you for your trouble, madam. You truly built the alchemical furnace beneath the arena exactly according to the blueprints I provided."

"What are you trying to do? Are you planning to use the alchemical furnace to sabotage the adventurers' grand event?" Batouri speculated.

"No, no, no. I hope they can compete to their heart's content—the more intense, the better." Flamel wore a mysterious smile.

"What? How does that benefit you?" Batouri furrowed his brow.

"You really don't understand alchemy at all, do you, madam?" Flamel chuckled, looking at the massive alchemical furnace before him. "This furnace is designed to absorb magical power and battle energy. When the adventurers compete above, all the magical power and battle energy they release will be absorbed by the broadcast crystal balls and then concentrated within this furnace. The adventurers competing above will expend more power than usual..."

"—..."

Batouri suddenly understood. All the participants were outstanding adventurers, none of whom were weak in terms of strength.

All the magical power expended by the adventurers during their matches would be concentrated within the furnace?

What an immense amount of power! What exactly was the Phoenix organization plotting? They needed such massive support of magical power and battle energy.

"You want to steal the adventurers' power? What exactly are you planning?!"

"Madam, for your own safety, I urge you not to ask so deeply. It has nothing to do with you." Flamel smiled calmly. "You only need to know that our Phoenix will bring a transformation to the world. This is by no means a bad thing. We have gathered together people from different factions with vastly different ideals but the same destination. We all share similar goals to achieve..."

Batouri dared not probe further. Regarding the mysterious dark organization Phoenix, she had unconsciously developed a considerable fear.

Unlike other dark guilds, Phoenix never burned, killed, or plundered for money by any means necessary.

Both the Orc King Sarit and the alchemical genius Flamel before her were individuals of remarkable skill.

Yet they all possessed an indescribable centripetal force, serving that mysterious phoenix.

Batouri felt he couldn't continue to be led around by the nose, or he'd sink deeper and deeper. He couldn't help but want to kill Flamel again; his sharp nails emerged.

"I know you want to kill me, madam, but I advise you not to waste your effort." Flamel turned around, pointing to the red gem on his neck, a relaxed smile on his face.

"Do you know what this is?"

"This is the substance used to construct the bodies of the Three Fates. The Philosopher's Stone."

"It represents supreme laws and truth, the origin of all things."

"No matter how you try to kill me, I can use it to reverse reality..."

title: Chapter 11 — Back on Track
content:
Chapter 11 — Back on Track

Volume 27 · Chapter 11

"Even though this Philosopher's Stone was made by me and is not the real thing, with many flaws, I believe it will be more than enough to deal with you, Madam..."

Flamel's attainments in alchemy had long since far surpassed his own teacher, Democritus.

Even in terms of understanding and talent for alchemy, he could crush ten Da Vincis without breaking a sweat.

To Flamel, Da Vinci was nothing more than a stubborn little junior sister who only liked reading books and had no other praiseworthy qualities.

Flamel had studied alchemy since childhood. With his outstanding ideas and bold character, his achievements had long since surpassed most alchemy masters. The spirit of creation and adventure he advocated in alchemy was something Da Vinci completely lacked.

Thus, Flamel had seen through Da Vinci long ago. In his heart, he believed this bookworm of a junior sister would never achieve greatness.

"The Philosopher's... Bathory may not understand alchemy at all, but she is well-traveled and has heard of such things. It is a sacred object pursued by countless alchemists."

Flamel touched the fake Philosopher's Stone on his chest and said meaningfully, "The true Philosopher's Stone can peer into the truths of the world. It is more precious than any treasure."

"So, Madam, do not waste your effort."

"Thinking about killing me is fine, but taking action will only bring misfortune upon yourself."

"You merely inherited one-third of the divine power of the Godchild Cain, and the Godchild itself is nothing but a creation of the Goddess of Light."

"Since you, Madam, know nothing about alchemy, allow me to share a highly secret historical fact with you."

"The Three Great Sages, formed by the Philosopher's Stone, created the current Goddess of Light..."

"In other words, even the lofty Maria cannot escape the rules and truths of this world!"

Lexham's travelers settled into the hotel.

Everyone was assigned a room. However, since Merlin and Alice were a couple of adventurers, they were assumed to be husband and wife, so the family of three was reunited after a long time.

This made little Chris extremely happy. As soon as she entered, she started dancing and spinning in front of her parents.

But Alice recalled what had just happened. Before entering, Teacher Claudia had suddenly stopped her, looking serious, and said she wanted to meet her tonight to discuss something very important.

Alice couldn't fathom her teacher's intentions. She wondered what could be so serious that she needed to meet her in the middle of the night. Maybe it was about her training that Teacher Claudia was worried about, hence the special reminder.

Chris jumped up and down on the soft bed, looking particularly happy. She didn't care about her parents' competition at all and treated this trip as a fun outing.

"Chris, don't jump on the bed with your shoes on. Get down." Alice pretended to be angry, as she had been correcting Chris's unlikable habits since she was little.

"Okay~"

Chris, afraid of making her mother angry, obediently climbed down from the bed. However, she forgot how she had jumped up in the first place and found the bed a bit too high.

Her short little legs flailed about at the edge of the bed but couldn't reach the floor just a few centimeters below.

Chris began to panic, feeling as if she were standing at the edge of a bottomless cliff. She refused to get down and even started crying for help.

"Dad! Dad! Save me! It's too high..."

Merlin sighed and picked up Chris, who was about to fall off the bed. "If it's too high, how did you jump up here in the first place?"

"I... I forgot?" Chris looked a bit silly, sticking out her little tongue. "Ehe~ ★"

Merlin smiled knowingly. He thought that it would be fine for this girl to live happily as an ordinary person. Besides, with him around, he didn't expect her to become very powerful in the future. "Are you hungry? Dad will make you something good to eat."

"Waah!" Chris drooled a little but then looked down at her own round belly and said shyly, "But Big Chest Sister fed me a lot of yummy food on the carriage~"

"Big Chest Sister?" Merlin frowned, thinking hard. He guessed Chris was referring to Rosetti.

"Don't call her Big Chest Sister. Just call her Sister Rosetti." Alice corrected seriously.

"But when I call her Big Chest Sister, she seems so happy~" Chris said in a babyish voice.

Alice's face darkened. She felt uncomfortable inside, wondering what it would feel like to be called Big Chest Sister. Hearing that Rosetti was so pleased with the nickname, it must feel like being praised...

Three knocks echoed at the door. Alice curiously went to open it, only to find Guild President Old Taylor had come alone.

"President? What's the matter?"

"There's something quite important I need to discuss with the two of you alone."

Old Taylor smiled kindly. He wanted to talk to Merlin and Alice about correcting the errors in their adventurer information. This was a rare opportunity.

After all, Old Taylor knew that Alice owed the Holy Church a considerable amount of money. As a married couple of adventurers, their assets, income, and debts were shared.

So Old Taylor felt somewhat guilty towards Merlin, thinking he had tricked him. Now, it seemed he could still make amends.

But at the time, Old Taylor had seen that although Merlin and Alice were hostile towards each other, they looked like old lovers reuniting, with a complicated past.

Old Taylor had gone with the flow, thinking he was doing a good deed. Who would have thought it would turn out like this?

"Grandpa Taylor!"

As soon as Chris saw Old Taylor, she beamed with joy. She ran over and suddenly displayed an incredible leap!

With her short legs, she jumped and grabbed Old Taylor's white beard, swinging from his aged body.

"Ow... haha..." Old Taylor felt a slight pain from Chris pulling his beard, but he was still quite happy. He was an old man and had always loved children.

"Ah!" Alice was shocked by her precious daughter's behavior.

"Stop it at once, Chris!"

Late at night, the oil lamp emitted a dim yellow light. Old Taylor sat together with Merlin and Alice.

As for Chris, probably exhausted from a day of travel, she was fast asleep in her mother's arms, biting her finger, perhaps dreaming of something pleasant.

"President, what important matter brings you here so late?" Merlin asked curiously.

"Is it about tomorrow's competition?" Alice guessed.

"No, it's about the two of you." Old Taylor leaned on his cane and smiled.

"The two of us?"

Merlin and Alice exchanged a glance, both unable to figure out Old Taylor's intentions.

"You two are not married, but people always mistake you for a couple, which must have caused a lot of trouble, right? It's all my fault for being muddle-headed. I shouldn't have taken the liberty back then. I apologize to you both now." Old Taylor said sincerely.

"President..." Alice glanced at Merlin and, seeing he didn't say anything, continued, "Actually, it hasn't caused that much trouble..."

"You may not say it, but I indeed made a mistake." Old Taylor showed a righteous expression, then changed the subject. "However, there is a good opportunity now to correct your false marital status."

"Do you want to correct the wrong information and get back on the right track?"

title: Chapter 12 — Still More Chapters
content:
Chapter 12 — Still More Chapters

Volume 27 · Chapter 12

“Back to the original state?”

Merlin and Alice were both startled by Old Tyler’s words, clearly having never considered returning to their initial situation.

If this had happened a year ago, the two of them would have been overjoyed, eagerly wishing to dissolve their fake marriage and regain their freedom.

But now, with Merlin and Alice each harboring their own schemes, returning to their former relationship was far from simple.

“Exactly. Eliminating your fake adventurer couple status would reduce a lot of awkwardness, wouldn’t it?” Old Tyler paused, saying seriously, “This is a rare opportunity. Mr. Dawson, the chairman of the Adventurers Guild headquarters, is in Budapest. You two should find a chance to visit him with me, explain the situation in detail, and Mr. Dawson can modify your adventurer information and issue new adventurer licenses. Modifying adventurer information isn’t easy—only Mr. Dawson has the authority to make changes, and meeting him is difficult. He only makes public appearances during the Adventurers Tournament…”

The two exchanged a glance, their eyes filled with hesitation.

They’d been husband and wife for over a year, gradually growing accustomed to it. Now, modifying the information…

Though they appeared hesitant, their inner thoughts were actually opposite—

Alice, her face flushed, thought, We’ve been together for over a year now, there’s no need to change it! If we correct this relationship, I won’t be able to call myself Mrs. Merlin anymore. This guy will probably run wild, starting to flirt everywhere! We can’t change it!

Merlin, stroking his chin, thought, Changing back to the correct adventurer information is a good thing! It just feels a bit like I’m letting Alice down? But I’m a charming villain—I robbed things by my own strength, why should I have to pay back debts together with Alice? Change it! I want my freedom back!

“Then…”

“Alright!”

Alice had intended to politely decline Old Tyler’s offer, but before she could even speak, the heartless Merlin suddenly slapped his thigh and jumped up joyfully!

“You…”

“I said alright! Isn’t this great? I’ve been suffocating under some damn debt, now I can be free~” Merlin’s face was full of excitement, long tired of bearing such a heavy debt. Life was just too exhausting!

Seeing Merlin’s ecstatic joy, Old Tyler felt he’d done a good deed. “Haha, then tomorrow, you two come with me…”

“Wait! Chairman!” Alice quickly stopped Old Tyler, her expression serious. “This isn’t just Merlin’s business; it’s ours too. Chairman, don’t just listen to Merlin’s opinion. You should consider mine as well!”

“Uh… well…” Old Tyler frowned. Though Alice was right, on closer thought, Merlin was the one taking the big loss. He didn’t know the history behind their grudge.

“Alice, what do you mean? You don’t want me to gain freedom?” Merlin glared sideways at Alice, full of resentment. “What a vicious woman! (SF Light Novel)”

“…Vicious woman?” Alice gritted her teeth angrily. “How can you say that? Aren’t you the most vicious one?”

“Huh? What did I do?” Merlin raised an eyebrow.

“You’re planning to leave all that debt for me to pay alone?” The vein on Alice’s forehead throbbed.

“Alice, after spending so much time together, I think you’re a very hardworking person.” Merlin nodded approvingly, then shamelessly encouraged her, “I believe you’ll be able to pay off the debt within your lifetime! Glorious to earn it with your own hands! Shameful to rely on others!”

“…You! You’re the most thick-skinned guy I’ve ever met in my life!” Alice, like a lit fuse, grabbed Merlin’s neck in anger and started shaking him wildly. “I ended up in this situation because of you! Don’t you remember what shameless things you did to me on the beach? Remember it, you bastard! Don’t think you can just walk away! Give back that precious thing of mine!”

Merlin, expressionless, felt dizzy from the shaking, tears of regret already streaming down his face—

So it really couldn’t be helped? Two years ago…

I shouldn’t have grabbed Alice to be a boat-pulling slave.

I shouldn’t have been so handsy and snatched her armor after going ashore.

And I definitely shouldn’t have been so foolish as to run off with this woman to become adventurers!

Merlin sighed deeply, feeling terrible. He’d finally escaped the Demon Lord Palace, only to fall into another deep pit afterward. He was truly a professional good Samaritan.

Old Tyler listened, completely bewildered. Though he didn’t know the full story between Merlin and Alice from two years ago, from the fragmented clues, he couldn’t help but speculate.

Shameless things? Precious things?……

Could it be that Merlin seduced and then abandoned her? What a jerk!

Any relationship not aimed at marriage is just playing around. It seemed Merlin wasn’t so honest after all…

Old Tyler secretly sighed. As a moral elder, he couldn’t let Alice suffer. Merlin needed to take responsibility.

“Stop, Alice.” Merlin suddenly spoke.

“What? Do you have something else to say? I won’t agree if you try to run away alone.” Alice puffed her cheeks, thinking that even if Merlin returned to the demon race’s home, she wouldn’t let him off.

“Cough, cough!” Merlin cleared his throat softly, saying earnestly, “Alice, think about it—carrying this debt together is exhausting for both of me. Me being free isn’t a bad thing. I’m not trying to abandon you and run away. After all… I’m a very responsible, good man~”

“Do you think I’d believe your lies? You’ve used plenty of sweet talk already.” Alice said expressionlessly, seeing through Merlin’s tricks long ago.

Merlin, failing to trick her, rolled his eyes. “I’ve only ever used sweet talk with you.”

“Grrr…” Alice glared at him angrily. “We can’t correct our adventurer couple status now. We need to maintain it even more, understand?”

“Is that really necessary?” A few dark lines slid down Merlin’s forehead.

“It’s very necessary.”

Alice said seriously, picking up the sleeping Chris in her arms and showing Merlin the little one.

Chris slept soundly, a bubble of snot coming out of her nose, expanding and contracting with her breath, completely unaware of how important this discussion was for her.

Alice looked at Merlin, and to make him abandon his idea of living it up, she had no choice but to play her ultimate trump card—the child!

“You’re the father now, you know.” (1")/

title: Chapter 13 — Opening (Bonus Update)
content:
Chapter 13 — Opening (Bonus Update)

Volume 27 · Chapter 13

"Uh! You bring up Chris at a time like this?!" Merlin was startled, but seeing his precious daughter sleeping sweetly, all his selfish thoughts were quickly suppressed.

"I'm serious..." Alice said with a straight face, emphasizing her point, "We should ask Chris what she thinks about canceling the couple adventurer pairing, right? Regardless, she is our child, and she is innocent!"

...Merlin's expression darkened. He thought that ever since Alice became a mother, she had never once asked Chris's opinion, yet now she was respecting Chris's wishes? That was too fake!

"As parents, we should give our child a complete family. If we don't even have a marital relationship, how will Chris feel? She'd become very insecure, wouldn't she?" Alice's gaze drifted, all her little schemes written plainly on her face. "I'm not doing this on purpose to maintain a fake marital relationship. This is all for Chris's sake. Didn't you say you had a sense of responsibility? Show it to me..."

"...Merlin looked over at little Chris, who was sleeping so deeply she was drooling bubbles, and his feelings were complex.

Although Merlin somewhat enjoyed being with Alice, this kind of thing didn't conflict with avoiding his debts.

But considering Chris was still too young, Merlin felt Alice had a point. Even a fake marriage had to be maintained, and he would have to carry this debt!

Old Taylor wiped the cold sweat from his forehead and also felt this matter was becoming increasingly difficult to handle. Chris was still so young—she wouldn't understand the misunderstanding from back then at all, and she absolutely wouldn't allow her parents to separate.

At my age, I really shouldn't have meddled in this. It would've been better to play dead, right?

E Light Novel

Why did my hand get so itchy back then? Why did I have to write "couple" next to their names?

Deep into the night, both Merlin and Chris were fast asleep, but Alice got up in the middle of the night.

Alice remembered her teacher's instruction—that she needed to visit her late at night when everyone was quiet.

What could her teacher want to tell her?

Could it be teaching her some more martial arts techniques again?

Alice muttered to herself, quietly leaving the room to avoid waking Merlin and Chris.

When Alice knocked and entered Teacher Crody's room alone, she found her teacher indeed wasn't sleeping, but sitting by the light of an oil lamp, deep in thought.

"Teacher, I'm here. What's so urgent that we need to talk secretly?"

Crody raised her head, looked at Alice, and said calmly, "Sit down. There are some things I wish to discuss with you properly."

"Hmm?" Alice grew suspicious. She rarely saw her teacher so serious. "...What is it?"

"I already know everything about you. You're not married, right? Chris isn't your biological child—she was created using both of your blood through rare magic, correct?" Crody wasted no time, launching a direct hit!

"Ah?!" Alice was badly frightened, her chair trembling beneath her. "...That's not true! I—I've been married to Merlin for a long time!"

"You're still lying to me at a time like this? I truly raised you in vain..." Crody sighed.

"...Alice saw that her teacher's demeanor wasn't feigned and she clearly knew the truth, so she grumbled unhappily, "Who told you these things?"

"Your guild master, I believe his name was Taylor..." Crody didn't hide it.

"So annoying!"

Alice clenched her fists, thinking that old guild master really couldn't keep his mouth shut. He'd just come dragging up old grievances, and yet he couldn't live quietly as a retired elder?

"...I simply didn't want to return to the Great Snow Mountain with you. I wasn't deliberately trying to deceive you."

"What's wrong with returning to the Great Snow Mountain with me? Looking at you now, your strength has improved, but you're just as immature as before," Crody said firmly.

"Teacher, you always think I'm a child who'll never grow up. I'm not a child anymore. Whether I'm mature isn't something you can decide in one sentence!" Alice said seriously.

"If you were truly mature, would you be with an Iron-ranked adventurer?" Crody posed a soul-piercing question. "The gap between your statuses is so vast—it's simply unsuitable."

"Whether it's suitable or not is my decision," Alice said stubbornly, locking eyes with Crody. "Besides, there's a reason why Merlin can only remain an Iron-ranked adventurer. It's not what you think it is."

"At this point, you're still making excuses for that man. I'm not here to hear your feeble explanations—I've come to give you an ultimatum." Crody's gaze turned icy. Using her teacher's tone, she commanded, "Since you two aren't truly married, after this tournament is over, stop being an adventurer and part ways with that man. Come back to the Great Snow Mountain with me and Chris—I will raise her into an outstanding person."

"I won't!" Alice refused to yield.

"Then don't blame me for using certain means against that man..." Crody's tone turned grim, clearly pressuring Alice.

Alice's face went pale. The last thing she wanted to see was Merlin fighting her teacher, and it wasn't for any other reason—

Alice was afraid Merlin would hit too hard and leave her teacher bedridden for a long time....

Three days later, the adventurers' grand ceremony opened!

Outstanding adventurers from across the world gathered in the vast Amnius Arena.

The stands were packed to capacity, with many having traveled far to support their favorite adventurers. They waved flags, cheering loudly for the guild—with London and Katowice being the most spirited!

The spectacular scene of a sea of people was truly astonishing. This was the largest celebration in the human world, and even buying a single ticket was extremely difficult.

Outside, scalpers had even driven the opening ceremony tickets up to five hundred gold coins apiece, making a hefty profit off the festival's excitement!

A massive crystal sphere hung suspended above Amnius Arena, broadcasting the grand opening ceremony live to the entire world!

Boom, boom, boom—several cannon shots rang out, and colorful smoke bloomed in the sky above the arena, just like fireworks, pushing the atmosphere of the venue to its peak.

Above the audience stands was the arbitration committee's presiding dais, with seating on both sides prepared for invited guests.

The five arbitration committee members from the Adventurers Guild headquarters took the stage first. They came to the front of the dais and waved to all the spectators and competing adventurers, instantly triggering enormous cheers and applause—more enthusiastic than ever before.

Mr. Dawson, the chairman of the Arbitration Committee, stepped forward and delivered the opening speech on behalf of the other members. He solemnly took out his prepared manuscript and began reading—

"Cough, cough!"

"Autumn brings refreshing coolness, and osmanthus fills the air with fragrance~"

"At this season when farmers joyfully welcome the harvest, we welcome the long-awaited show-off convention."

"Upholding the noble spirit of friendship first, competition second, we will display our results, showcase our skills, show off our style..."

Below, Merlin was attending the tournament for the first time, but just hearing these opening remarks made him frown and feel drowsy—

Damn it!

Why does this feel so much like an elementary school opening ceremony?

(┬＿┬)

title: Chapter 14 — Inheriting a Magic Family
content:
Chapter 14 — Inheriting a Magic Family

Volume 27 · Chapter 14

Two hours later—

Old Mr. Dawson was still carrying on with his childish antics, his mouth flapping endlessly. He rambled from the history of the Adventurers Guild’s founding to the legendary tales of adventurers, even dragging out stories about the goldfish he kept at home.

This left the adventurers below rolling their eyes repeatedly. They were completely unimpressed by Old Mr. Dawson’s boring speech and simply wished this part would end quickly.

The audience had long since lost their initial enthusiasm. Some sat blankly, others dozed off, and a few looked around restlessly. It felt like an old charlatan was endlessly chattering in their ears—absolute torture!

“How much longer is he going to talk?” Merlin groaned, his face twisted in discomfort. He had thought it would end quickly, but instead, he had been standing under the blazing sun for two whole hours. “No one wants to hear about his pet goldfish.”

“Indeed, the chairman does talk too much.”
Alice nodded in agreement, feeling that everyone’s patience was being severely tested.

She looked down at Chris and saw that the little girl had already succumbed to boredom and dozed off.

Alice found it both amusing and exasperating. She thought that even if Chris had magical talent, she might just end up being a child who slept all day in magic school.

Unfortunately, Alice believed Chris had no magical aptitude at all and couldn’t even attend a magic school.

If she did, Alice could have used her status as a foreign Thorn Knight to send Chris to Britain’s most prestigious magic academy, where she could study the finest magic alongside a group of noble children.

...

Old Taylor’s face showed an embarrassed expression as he whispered, “Everyone, please be patient. Mr. Dawson does tend to ramble a bit, but if you bear with it, it’ll be over soon.”

“Two hours without a break…” Karl chuckled, lowering his head in helplessness. “At the opening ceremony of the last tournament, Dawson went on about the turtle he kept at home. He talked from start to finish until the sun set, and the audience was so fed up they demanded refunds.”

Hearing Karl’s words, Merlin couldn’t help but break out in a cold sweat. Looking at Old Mr. Dawson on the stage, spittle flying from his mouth, he thought, *So this is just the beginning of his speech?* Hurry up and just announce the start of the tournament already!

Not far away, little Johnson, short in stature, had gotten lost in the crowd. He frantically scratched his head, desperately searching for his father, Old Johnson.

Little Johnson had a severe sense of direction, so his father didn’t trust him to go alone. He had come to Budapest with his son to take care of all his needs.

For this tournament, Little Johnson had prepared for a long time. Old Johnson was also worried that his son might not find the venue, leading to an embarrassing forfeit.

Little Johnson was no longer the same as before. His strength had undergone a qualitative leap, advancing by bounds and bounds.

Although his father didn’t fully approve, at Little Johnson’s earnest request, he had the magical power container, passed down through generations of genius ancestors, implanted into his own body.

Now, with the support of his ancestors’ magical power furnace, not only was his strength improving every day, but his cultivation had also become easier. He could even, at the cost of his lifespan, forcibly tap into the power accumulated in the furnace, causing his strength to skyrocket to an unimaginable level in a short time.

Little Johnson’s primary goal was no longer to win the tournament but to steadily cultivate and fully absorb his ancestors’ magical power furnace into his own strength. If he succeeded, he could become one of the few top-tier mages in the world, or even the very best.

However, Little Johnson was young and hot-blooded. He still held a grudge against Zikarillo for stealing his prey, and he secretly vowed to teach that half-elf mage a lesson in the tournament!

Little Johnson looked around nervously, not wanting anyone to notice he was lost and become a laughingstock. But he still caught sight of Merlin nearby, staring at him with a meaningful look.

“What’s wrong? Lost again?” Merlin ignored the awkward atmosphere. He didn’t need to think to know what was troubling this brat.

“I am not! This time I came with my father!” Little Johnson was flustered, trying to emphasize that with an adult present, there was no way he could be lost.

“Oh~? Then where is your father?” Merlin asked with a strange expression.

...
Little Johnson realized he had said too much. His face turned red at a visible speed.

“So you *are* lost, huh? Should we make an announcement that you’re missing?” Merlin said, barely suppressing a laugh.

Little Johnson gritted his teeth and marched up to Merlin, displeased. “Shut up! Don’t treat me like a child! I’ll crush you underfoot sooner or later! The way you’re so carefree, if you’d run into me before the preliminary rounds, you’d have been eliminated already. Otherwise, even if I win the tournament, it won’t mean much, huh!”

“Is that so? Then good luck.”
Merlin looked at the blustering Little Johnson with a detached tone.

Still, he could see that his own strength had left a deep impression on Little Johnson.

It seemed that when Merlin had faced off against the alchemist Democritus, it had left quite a psychological shadow on this teenager.

“What’s with that attitude? I’m not the same as before. If you underestimate me, you’ll regret it.” Little Johnson said meaningfully, his eyes revealing a hint of confidence.

“Hmm?”
Merlin examined Little Johnson with interest. He could see that compared to when they had met in the Magical Beast Forest, the boy’s aura and presence had condensed significantly. Clearly, he had been training intensely over the past month, just like Alice.

But the next second, Merlin sensed something was off. A normal person should have a single magical aura, the innate source of a mage’s power, honed through constant cultivation.

Yet when Merlin observed Little Johnson up close, he made a shocking discovery. This brat actually had… not just one, but *hundreds* of different auras converging into one, forming a magical source unlike that of a normal mage!

The surging, overwhelming magic, the terrifyingly uncontrollable fluctuations in aura and presence—it was so staggering that even Merlin couldn’t help but furrow his brows slightly, catching a whiff of the dangerous scent of a powerful opponent.

What had this kid done to himself? Why did he feel so… unnatural?

One person… why did he possess hundreds of different auras and magical sources?

Before, he had never noticed anything strange about Little Johnson. He had just seemed like a gifted young mage.

But… why did it feel like hundreds of powerful mages were standing before him, pressing down on him?

Merlin couldn’t figure it out. It was as if the Little Johnson in front of him wasn’t a single person, but an entire *legion* of mage knights bearing down on him.

...

Little Johnson let out a cold snort, a hint of pride in his voice. He finally felt a bit of confidence returning in front of Merlin.

He slowly lifted his head, and behind him, hundreds of auras began to swirl, materializing into various figures…

Their gazes were sharp, carrying the bearing of those who looked down upon all others. They were the ancestors of the Johnson family, once legendary magical prodigies who had shaken the very course of history!

Little Johnson, the young heir to a magical legacy, stood before Merlin, having inherited the power of his forebears.

“Merlin…”
“Do you think *I* am worthy of a fight with you now?”

title: Chapter 15 — Another World
content:
Chapter 15 — Another World

Volume 27 · Chapter 15

Merlin examined little Henry—how could one person possess hundreds of different, overwhelming auras, and yet not reject a single one? Instead, they harmonized perfectly, making his power even stronger...

He felt his time away from the Demon Lord Palace hadn’t been wasted. Today, he’d truly learned something new! So this world still had such extraordinary mages!

Merlin pondered for a moment. Given little Henry’s age, it was unlikely he could fully control this power—whether he could even use Divine Power was uncertain.

Against mages, it was usually difficult for them to pose a real threat to Merlin. Only after reaching the pseudo-god stage, when one could wield partial Divine Power, could they bypass Merlin’s magic immunity to some extent.

But Merlin had already experienced Divine Power before. Though its might was indeed terrifying, it still wasn’t enough to threaten him.

"What’s wrong?" Little Johnson struck a smug pose, hands on his hips. "Uncle Merlin’s silent—are you scared?"

"Not at all. It’s just sad to see you try so hard, only to be defeated in the end." Merlin sighed quietly.

"...What did you say?!" Little Johnson clenched his fists. "Just you wait! I’ll make sure you regret this!"

Alice watched as Little Johnson stomped his feet in frustration at Merlin’s words. She thought, *Does Merlin really need to provoke him like this? He’s always crushing Little Johnson’s confidence...*

Just as Alice, standing to the side, was about to say something, the Chris in her arms suddenly woke up from the noise.

Little Chris rubbed her eyes in Alice’s arms and saw Little Johnson baring his teeth at her father, looking as if he were facing a great enemy.

"It’s Big Brother Johnson~!"

Chris’s eyes lit up. She wriggled free from Alice’s arms and dashed excitedly toward Little Johnson.

The tiny Chris grabbed onto Johnson’s clothes with both hands, her eyes sparkling with admiration for the older boy.

"Eya! Big Brother Johnson~!"

"...Little Johnson’s face turned red. Even though he wasn’t an adult either, he still wasn’t used to being clung to by a child even younger than himself. "...Let go of me! I don’t have time to play with a little brat like you!"

"Hm?"

Alice looked slightly surprised. As a mother, she knew Chris was a little shy and wouldn’t willingly get too close to strangers.

After thinking it over, she realized—probably when Merlin had lost Chris, the little girl had formed a bond with Johnson.

Watching Chris’s happy expression, Alice could tell she really wanted to play with someone her own age.

Alice silently reflected on herself. Chris was always with her and Merlin, making it hard for her to interact with other children her age. That clearly wasn’t good, but unfortunately, there weren’t many kids around Chris’s age in Rexham.

But when Merlin saw Chris clinging to Little Johnson, his reaction was different. A sudden, sour feeling welled up inside him. The overprotective father’s instincts were written all over his face—

*What the hell is this?*

Why is Chris clinging to this brat?

Is this punk more appealing to her than me, her own father?!

No! I refuse to accept this! I’ll crush anyone who tries to take my precious daughter away!

Don’t think that just because you protected her for a while, you can get close to her! I’ll never allow it!

Merlin’s face darkened. He mechanically stretched out his arms, picked up little Chris from the ground, and glared at Johnson with hostility.

"Back off! Don’t you dare try to seduce my daughter!"

"Ah?!" Little Johnson looked awkward. *Isn’t it the little brat clinging to me? Who would even try to seduce a kid with a messed-up mind? Don’t underestimate me!*

"Hmph! You’re not even fully grown, and you’re trying to get close to my daughter? Ask me first!" Merlin held Chris, putting on the overbearing, intimidating aura of a protective dad.

"...Little Johnson wanted to explain.

"What do you mean, explain? I don’t approve of this engagement! Unless you can defeat me, I won’t allow my daughter to marry anyone!" Merlin glared fiercely, as if he wanted to kick Little Johnson into the sky.

"Stop it! You’re overthinking things!" Alice couldn’t bear to watch anymore. She smacked Merlin’s neck in frustration. While she understood his love for Chris, he was being ridiculous. "Chris is too young to have any romantic thoughts! Stop making up nonsense! She just wants to make friends. Don’t ruin her enthusiasm!"

"Make friends?" Merlin furrowed his brows, eyeing Little Johnson suspiciously. "As a responsible father, I don’t allow Chris to have male friends..."

"Are you crazy?" Alice was stunned, unable to comprehend. "Wake up! You don’t sound like a responsible father—you sound like a perverted one!"

"I don’t care! Any man who tries to get close to Chris will have to step over my dead body first!" Merlin snarled.

Alice fell silent, her face grim, a deep worry for Chris’s future rising in her heart.

"Daddy~ Johnson Big Brother is a good person! He only gets angry when he talks to you! In the forest, Johnson Big Brother was really kind..." Chris said in her childish voice.

"...I was not kind! It was you, the little brat, crying and whining the whole time—it was annoying!" Little Johnson refused to acknowledge it, determined to maintain his pride.

"...What?!" Merlin’s heart ached even more when he heard Chris actually defending Little Johnson. *She’s only about two years old, and she’s already taking a strange man’s side?!* This was unacceptable! He had to keep a close watch on her!

Alice shot Merlin a look, then silently approached Little Johnson, sincerely thanking him. "Last time in the Magical Beast Forest, thank you for taking care of Chris. Merlin here isn’t good with words, but he’s also grateful to you."

"Hmph!" Little Johnson lifted his nose. "Who needs your thanks? A true strong man doesn’t need useless gratitude!"

"..." Alice forced a smile, her anger flaring at Little Johnson’s attitude. *This... really is unlikable, isn’t it?*

---

In the distance, a strange figure in a black robe limped over, concealing his face.

Unlike the others around him, who were at least Gold-rank, this man, like Merlin, had a Black Iron Adventurer’s badge around his neck.

He was the strongest competitor in this tournament, as Gregory had mentioned—the naturally deformed and bizarre summoner, Crono.

In the vast arena, though packed with people, only Merlin and Crono stood out as utterly out of place, utterly unique.

As a gathering of adventurers, every guild sent their strongest, making Black Iron—a bottom-tier rank—extremely rare.

Unlike Merlin, who sought to improve himself, Crono was a loner with a reclusive personality. He had refused the chance to become a Mythril-rank adventurer and had never even considered replacing his Black Iron badge.

Crono was born deformed—even his legs were a problem. One was usable, while the other was withered like a stick, as if it would snap with a single kick, forcing him to walk with a limp.

His exposed arms were covered in fleshy growths, resembling toad skin, which made people feel sick just looking at them.

Fortunately, Crono was different from Merlin. As the previous champion, despite being a Black Iron adventurer, his reputation was well-known. No one dared to underestimate him, and many even stepped aside for him, whispering behind his back.

Crono suddenly stopped, looking at Merlin and Alice in the distance—or rather, his gaze locked onto the adorable Chris in Merlin’s arms!

His deformed body trembled as if he had discovered something incredible. A strange, clicking sound came from his throat.

The pair of eyes growing from his chin rolled wildly. Once they landed on Chris, he couldn’t look away—

*What terrifying vitality!*

If I take her back, our world can be saved!

Even if I can’t find the black box that connects to another world, I can still ensure the survival of my homeland!

title: Chapter 16 — Iron Plate
content:
Chapter 16 — Iron Plate

Volume 27 · Chapter 16

Clauno's sudden appearance made the surrounding adventurers tense up.

Those new to the tournament for the first time were fine, but the adventurers who had experience with the tournament all changed expression drastically upon seeing Clauno's eerie figure.

Everyone knew Clauno was a strange person, solitary and aloof—had anyone ever seen him communicate with others in his line of work?

In the previous tournament, Clauno would stand on stage each time without moving, relying on summoned strange creatures to sweep through many famous adventurers near and far, pressing down so many traditional powerhouses that they couldn't lift their heads, becoming a hot figure four years ago.

Although Clauno had once been at the height of his glory, because he was very low-key, after four years his fame had faded considerably—but after a gap of four years, with the Adventurers' Competitive Tournament being held once again, this monster who had swept through the powerhouses was once again recalled by many adventurers...

On the surface, it seemed that super rookies like Zikatilo, Aria, and Tanya were the hot favorites to win the championship, but many adventurers knew clearly in their hearts that only Clauno was the most terrifying existence—he was the previous champion, after all!

A rookie adventurer who saw Clauno couldn't resist pointing and whispering behind his back,

"A cripple is coming to the tournament too? Really isn't afraid of death, this guy...

Hearing the discussion behind him, Clauno suddenly eerily turned his head 180 degrees, giving that adventurer a cold glance.

The rookie adventurer's spine instantly went cold, a sense of fear welling up from within. Seeing the eyes growing on Clauno's chin and his ugly face, he wasn't just startled—more than that, from the other's gaze, he felt his own insignificance...

The person beside him immediately covered his mouth, quietly warning, "Don't talk nonsense, that's Clauno, the previous tournament champion. If you anger him, nobody can protect you!"

The rookie adventurer broke out in a cold sweat. Hearing that it was the previous tournament champion, he thought with lingering fear, no wonder there was such a powerful sense of oppression, but...

Clauno couldn't be bothered with others' discussions. Right now, in his eyes, there was only that little girl radiating life force—Chris.

Although he couldn't figure out why a small child would possess such terrifying life force, he could no longer hide the greed in his eyes!

If he could bring Chris back to his homeland, then the other world on the verge of collapse would be saved!

Clauno grew restless, his figure suddenly bending into something like a bow shape, approaching Chris in Merlin's arms at a speed difficult for the naked eye to detect, unable to resist extending his demonic claw.

With his homeland's survival at stake, he couldn't care about so much—if he didn't act now, when would he?

To save his homeland, Clauno had wandered this world for ten years, and today he had finally found a way—how could he possibly let it slip by?

TT =

The opportunity before him was rare! The little girl was held in the arms of a black-iron adventurer—Clauno thought he could crush this sort of trash with a finger, then snatch the little girl and flee back to his homeland—

Hmph! I don't even put purple-gold adventurers in my eyes—who in this arena could stop me?!

Tanya was below listening to the chairman's speech, half asleep, when she suddenly sensed a strange energy fluctuation and snapped her eyes open.

Even Tanya found it difficult to see Clauno's figure clearly—she could only see a dark mass constantly rushing toward Merlin.

Merlin was still trying to shoo away that little brat Johnson, to keep his precious daughter away from this fellow. Little Chris was laughing exceptionally happily, completely unaware of the approaching danger.

But Merlin was Merlin after all—a man who had been through countless battles, who had hovered on the edge of death innumerable times tempering his sword-drawing technique.

With him present, who could harm a single hair on Chris?

A flash of lightning suddenly crossed Merlin's mind. As a father, instinct made his whole body tense, and without hesitation he wanted to draw his blade and slash.

"Ding—"

A crisp ring—although he hadn't drawn the blade completely, driven by instinct Merlin had pulled Banri Garan out just a tiny fraction.

Clauno, rushing forward at extreme speed, froze stiffly on the spot, his demonic claw reaching toward Chris unable to advance even half an inch, his gaze filled with disbelief—

No one noticed me—why did he notice?

This terrifying reaction speed—if it's instinct, then that's truly frightening!

In ten years I've encountered many powerful humans, and I don't even fear purple-gold adventurers among humans—

Why can't I see through this human before me! This is a black-iron adventurer?

No! Something's wrong!

In the span of a lightning flash, Clauno thought many things, secretly regretting his recklessness—but it was already too late.

His arm covered in fleshy tumors suddenly split open with countless wounds, blood spraying, his palm dangling limply, like a marionette whose strings had been cut—clearly in that brief instant, his hand tendons had been severed by Merlin!

"Ah!" Chris was terrified, covering her eyes and burying her little head in her daddy's chest.

All of this happened too fast, so fast that most people didn't notice at all that the previous champion Clauno had been thoroughly rebuffed by Merlin—only those around Merlin saw this scene.

Clauno lightning-fast withdrew his arm into his sleeve, to prevent others from seeing his ill intentions, the eyes growing on his chin narrowing slightly...

Alice furrowed her brow, frightened into a shudder by Clauno's deformed appearance—just what kind of person would grow up like this?

Beside her, little Johnson became alert, recognizing the previous champion Clauno—this bizarre fellow coming over definitely meant no good!

Merlin returned the katana he'd drawn a small portion of back into its sheath, but his hand didn't leave it, still pressing on Banri Garan's hilt. His face like frost, he asked coldly, "Sir, what business do you have?"

The mouth on Clauno's forehead suddenly revealed a smile. He hid his injured arm behind his back, gave Merlin and the others a slight polite bow to show his goodwill, then without looking back limped away...

"Strange fellow..." Alice watched Clauno's departing back, not knowing what he had just been trying to do—to the point of forcing Merlin to nearly draw his blade to kill.

/

"You should be careful." Little Johnson kindly warned, then suddenly said seriously, "This guy is the previous champion, his strength is unfathomable. Last time, quite a few adventurers were beaten until they couldn't even fight back. It seems you've been targeted by him."

"Oh? Interesting..." Merlin smiled, watching Clauno's distant figure, secretly growing wary in his heart. What a strange person—why did I just instinctively sense danger? It seems this opponent poses some threat.

"Really? But just now the other party seemed quite friendly." Alice looked at the frightened Chris, couldn't resist pinching her little cheek, "It's not because the baby is cute, and that person wanted to come touch her, and then Merlin instinctively hurt him? You're way too sensitive."

Merlin didn't speak, thinking—friendly? Why did I feel I was in danger? I don't trust my eyes; I trust my instincts more.

"In any case, being careful is never wrong." Little Johnson had always believed Clauno was hiding some secret—his bizarre behavior always made people wary.

Clauno limped out of the arena, hiding his still-bleeding arm in his sleeve, his expression turning grave—

That one... is a bit interesting~

Like me, a black-iron adventurer, yet possessing no small amount of strength.

I'm afraid in his eyes, the so-called outstanding adventurers in this arena are nothing but ants...

Only I can do battle with him!

title: Chapter 17 — Just Do It and Be Done
content:
Chapter 17 — Just Do It and Be Done

Volume 27 · Chapter 17

Klauno lowered his eyelids. Seeing that his plan to abduct Chris would not be easily accomplished, he began to devise another scheme in his mind.

He had originally thought that this Adventurers' Tournament would be as simple as the last one. He never expected that among the many adventurers, someone like Merlin would be hiding.

From the brief exchange just now, although Klauno could not fully grasp Merlin's strength, he could already tell that this man was extraordinary and would definitely make it to the finals. There was a good chance they would meet on the stage.

So Klauno decided to go all out on the stage, kill Merlin on the spot, and remove the obstacle to his plan of abducting Chris.

Even though the tournament rules forbade taking lives, occasional accidents were not impossible...

Klauno thought to himself, then turned his head and glanced at Merlin with a cold gaze. *Enjoy your last moments of happiness, foolish man.*

It seemed that this little episode had not been noticed by many, but Tanya, who was watching from afar, had seen everything.

She had just caught a glimpse of Merlin’s brief display of skill, and it left her somewhat astonished.

Klauno had hidden himself well just now. With that speed, ordinary people would never react in time. There were so many outstanding adventurers present, yet not a single one had noticed the deformed man sneaking up?

And yet, he had been spotted by a mere Iron-rank adventurer? To have such reaction speed was absolutely not the capability of some low-tier, mediocre adventurer.

Tanya’s doubts grew. Normally silent, she broke her usual habit and asked the drunken guild president beside her.

"President, who is that man?"

"Hmm?" Ligachev followed Tanya’s gaze and saw the deformed, limping man leaving the arena. "Oh! Klauno! The champion of the last tournament. You must be careful—he’s not someone to be trifled with. Among the adventurers who can rival you this time, I think only that ugly fellow can do it."

"Is that so?"

Tanya’s gaze sharpened, but she did not continue watching Klauno. Instead, she looked at Merlin in the distance with a puzzled expression.

She had always considered Merlin a joke, never taking this minor character seriously. But now, her thoughts subtly shifted.

The previous champion, Klauno?

He had actually been outmaneuvered by an unknown Iron-rank adventurer?

That guy named Merlin... didn’t seem ordinary at all...

Little Johnson didn’t want to waste time. He needed to meet up with his father, so as he left, he warned them, "That Klauno is bizarre. There’s very little information about him. I don’t think that reclusive freak would approach you without a reason, so..."

Merlin watched Little Johnson’s retreating figure, deep in thought. He guessed that the man was probably targeting him, not Chris. Otherwise, he wouldn’t have sensed the danger so immediately.

But Merlin couldn’t figure it out—he was just an unknown, minor adventurer. Why would a former champion, among so many adventurers, specifically choose to try and harm him?

Chris had been scared to tears by Klauno just now, not just because of the scene where his tendons had been severed, but also because of his grotesque appearance. She buried her face in Merlin’s chest, too afraid to open her eyes.

"...Daddy, that man’s eyes were on his chin. It was so scary..."

"Uh..." Merlin was at a loss, holding Chris and not knowing what to say. *A person’s appearance is given by their parents; it’s not something they can control.*

Seeing Merlin’s embarrassment, Alice took Chris from him and soothed her, "Don’t cry, don’t cry. You’re crying like a little kitten. So what if he looked a little strange?"

...Chris pursed her little lips, never wanting to see that man again. She had never imagined someone could look like that.

Carl noticed Chris’s distress and walked over to ask, "What’s wrong? Did something happen?"

"It’s nothing. Just now, a man named Klauno scared her." Alice explained.

"Klauno?" Mr. Carl furrowed his brows, thinking for a moment before it clicked. "Klauno! The champion of the last tournament!"

"That’s right. Johnson said the same thing just now..." Alice thought to herself, *That guy must be really strong. It feels like everyone except me and Merlin knows about him.*

"Klauno is a strange one, and not a good person. You all should stay away from him." Mr. Carl advised in a senior’s tone.

"What? Has that guy done something bad?" Alice asked curiously.

"In the last tournament, every adventurer who fought against him ended up severely injured. He hits too hard. That guy seems to enjoy seeing others in a pitiful state." Mr. Carl said seriously.

"Is he very strong?" Merlin asked.

"Last year’s champion—how could he not be strong? I can’t even gauge his strength. He won all his matches too easily." Mr. Carl shook his head, then changed the subject. "But the monsters Klauno summons are all very powerful, with extremely troublesome abilities..."

"Oh? What abilities?" Merlin’s interest was slightly piqued.

"Those summons can devour magic and fighting spirit. Many capable adventurers have suffered greatly because of this, left with almost no power to resist." Mr. Carl said in a low voice.

"Devour magic and fighting spirit..." Merlin suddenly frowned. This ability felt familiar. He thought to himself—

This deformed man named Klauno...

Could he be connected to the Chaos Clan from the Mysterious Sea?

On the other side, on the podium, Old Man Dawson finally reached the end of his speech and loudly announced the opening of the Adventurers' Tournament.

"Adventurers were born 784 years ago. Through wind and rain, hardships and trials, they have walked to this day, giving rise to many heroic and moving tales!"

"We must continue to carry forward the spirit of adventure, fearless and free, so that all adventurers may become an indispensable force in protecting the world!"

"I declare the 193rd Adventurers' Tournament officially open!!!"

Boom, boom, boom—fireworks exploded in the sky once more. The previously sluggish crowd cheered again.

They weren’t cheering for the opening of the tournament, but rather for Dawson finally finishing his long, tedious speech.

Dawson nodded in satisfaction. Seeing the enthusiastic response, he felt his speech was well-written and decided he would use the same script next time.

"For fairness, the tournament will use a one-on-one duel system."

"Each guild may send up to three adventurers to participate. The final ranking will be determined by the best result among the three representatives."

Merlin listened and smiled. *One-on-one duels? It’s a bit of a waste of time, but it’s not impossible.*

So, each guild could send one to three adventurers, and regardless of the results, only the best placement among the three would count as the guild’s final score?

Wasn’t this system tailor-made for him? Carl and Alice could just step down and rest. He alone could defeat all the guilds!

Champion? Guaranteed!

Mr. Dawson on the podium explained the competition rules and precautions in detail, but Merlin had already lost interest. He found the tournament child’s play.

Noticing this, Alice reminded him, "Merlin, the chairman is explaining the rules. Listen carefully."

"There’s no need..." Merlin scoffed lightly, smiling indifferently. "What kind of nonsense rules are these?"

"Just get it done."

title: Chapter 18 — The Inherited Armor Reappears
content:
Chapter 18 — The Inherited Armor Reappears

Volume 27 · Chapter 18

Merlin thought this competition was simple for him. Since he could win the championship on his own, relying on himself alone was more than enough.

On the podium, Mr. Dawson had nearly finished explaining the competition rules. Aside from first-time adventurers, most people had little interest in this segment.

"This tournament, like all previous ones, will use a lottery draw to determine matchups, and there will be byes set aside so that the lucky ones can advance directly to the top eight...."

Merlin's brows furrowed slightly. He had assumed everyone would punch their way through with brute force, not expecting any byes. If someone drew a lucky one, they might achieve a high ranking in the tournament purely through fortune.

"A bye? I can advance to the next round without even fighting...."

"Don't be surprised, Merlin. You should know that luck is also a form of strength," Mr. Taylor said with a half-smile.

Merlin instinctively glanced at Alice beside him. This guy always had absurdly good luck — he might not even need to lift a finger and could still reach the top eight. How easy would that be?

The Adventurer Competition was a grand event in the human world. The reason byes existed was because adventurer guilds across the regions were highly uneven.

Some guilds were packed with powerful fighters, while others didn't even have the courage to enter the tournament. The arbitration committee, considering this situation, had specially reserved one of the top eight spots for a lucky draw.

If a weak guild happened to draw the bye, their ranking would be locked in the top eight ahead of time, meaning they wouldn't have come for nothing.

This was the arbitration committee's goodwill, but was that really the case?

"Hah, I'd rather not have that kind of luck. It's no good for an adventurer," Mr. Karl suddenly spoke up.

"What do you mean? Advancing to the top eight without even fighting — isn't that a good thing?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"Only weak cowards would hope to draw a bye," Mr. Karl said seriously. "Merlin, this is a rare opportunity for every adventurer to showcase themselves. Every match is broadcast to the entire world, letting everyone recognize and remember you. That is far more important than some so-called ranking."

.....Merlin's eyebrow twitched as he slowly caught on. This competition was a super stage, and everyone wanted to go up and show themselves. Drawing a bye meant losing that chance. While it might let weaklings get good results, it also crushed their opportunity to become famous through battle.

"As for the top eight, most people only respect the seven who earned their spots through sheer strength. As for that seemingly lucky one? Nobody remembers them at all. They'd rather become a laughingstock." Mr. Karl paused and continued, "The Adventurer Competition has been held many times, and very few people who drew a bye ever made a name for themselves — unless they defeated their opponents and advanced to the top four. Only then will people acknowledge them."

"I see."

Merlin nodded to himself.

"Actually, being ignored after drawing a bye and losing the chance to showcase yourself isn't the worst of it. The worst is facing scorn and criticism." Mr. Karl looked at Merlin and explained, "If only one person reached the top eight through luck while the other seven were all impressive powerhouses, that person who drew the bye would be looked down upon by countless people. Most who drew byes and seemed lucky — even though they got decent rankings — ended up choosing to withdraw from the competition."

Alice lowered her head, lost in thought. So whoever drew the bye was actually the unluckiest person. That definitely wouldn't be her. Everyone wanted to showcase themselves — who would want to lie back and enter the top eight only to be looked down upon?

"Merlin, I've known you for quite some time and understand you somewhat. Please don't even think about drawing a bye. This tournament is your chance to make a name for yourself." Mr. Karl said with some concern.

"Don't worry, I know exactly what to do. I want to fight through all the adventurers and stand on the highest podium," Merlin said confidently.

After Mr. Dawson finished explaining all the competition rules from the podium, he quietly put away his speech notes.

Next came another important part of the opening ceremony — announcing the distinguished guests in attendance.

After all, this was the capital of the human world. Without a few heavyweight figures showing up, it would look rather shabby.

"Next, let us welcome our distinguished guests. The first!"

"The family patriarch whose wealth surpasses the world and whose net worth is immeasurable, Mr. Rothschild!"

The moment his words fell, the crowd erupted in thunderous applause. Some even shamelessly started shouting "Dad!" with their eyes turning into gold coins.

The Rothschild family was a household name, known to everyone!

Their business spanned every industry, from trading a single apple to dealing in rare treasures and pseudo-artifacts. Their presence could be found almost everywhere.

As a commercial family, they terrifyingly controlled more than half of the wealth in the human kingdoms. Even some royal families borrowed from them to ease their pressures.

Just how terrifying this family was could be seen. The fact that the patriarch himself had come in person was equivalent to several kings arriving. The weight of this tournament was evident.

"Wow, the head of the Rothschild family. Amazing."

Alice couldn't help but exclaim. Starting with such a heavyweight bomb, this was the first time she'd ever seen the world's richest man appear in person.

"Tch!"

Merlin felt a bit uncomfortable in his heart. Regarding the Rothschild family, the only thing he knew was that all the horse racing tracks in the world were owned by them.

Thinking back to the past, he had snatched the legendary hero armor passed down through generations from Alice, sold it for tens of millions of gold coins, and then threw it all directly into the horse racing tracks, letting them make a fortune.

Now, thinking back, Merlin felt a bit irrational. He had always wanted to soar to the top, but in selling the legendary armor, he had also lost himself in the process.

Little Chris saw her father frowning and couldn't help but ask, "Mom, Dad looks really upset...."

Alice glanced at Merlin and said sarcastically, "Your dad is a diamond member of the Rothschild family. Pretty impressive~"

"Uh!" Merlin, having his past exposed in front of his daughter, stammered to cover his embarrassment, "That kind of rotten stuff, I actually didn't want it."

"Hmph!" Alice sniffed. She thought that with Chris around, Merlin should behave himself a bit more, right?

An extremely aged man slowly walked out from behind the podium to meet everyone, followed by an extraordinary-looking guard.

Although the Rothschild patriarch was the richest man in the world, his clothing was unexpectedly plain, no different from an ordinary person. In fact, he didn't have a single piece of jewelry on his entire body.

But this old man's eyes were sharp and bright. Wherever he passed, people felt considerable pressure. As the head of a family, even with his restrained aura, nobody dared to look down on him.

Just one gesture from the Rothschild, and countless godsons and goddaughters would fight until their heads were broken just to get close to him.

Rothschild looked extremely old, leaning on a cane, his back hunched as if his spine could snap at any moment. He didn't seem like he had much time left.

The guard behind him, however, was striking — sword-like eyebrows, star-bright eyes, clad in pristine, magnificent armor, with a cape fluttering behind him....

Although this magnificent armor had undergone some changes....

But Alice still recognized it at a glance.

It was the legendary hero's sacred armor that Merlin had robbed away!!

title: Chapter 19 — Alfonso
content:
Chapter 19 — Alfonso

Volume 27 · Chapter 19

“No...no way! ?” Alice widened her eyes, staring at Rothschild's back and the guards, especially the familiar armor on their backs! Her heart was already shocked.

Hero....Hero's inheritance armor! ? It's already in the Rothschild family's hands!

Although the armor has changed a lot, I can still recognize it at a glance!

“Mom? What's wrong?” Chris raised her little head and asked, feeling that mom's mood was a bit strange.

“.......Alice forced a smile and turned to Merlin, whispering, “Merlin, who did you sell my armor to?”

“Huh?” Merlin didn't know why Alice suddenly asked this, but he still answered honestly, "I remember a well-dressed merchant."

“But why did it end up in the Rothschild family's hands?” Alice frowned and asked.

“No way? You're just guessing, right?” Merlin was surprised and asked.

Alice leaned in and glanced at the guards on the dais, “That guy's armor is the Hero's inheritance armor...
