Though life energy was extremely rare, Merlin knew it all too well. It was only today that he realized his constant slaughtering was not the essence—what truly mattered was the theft of life energy!

"Chris..."

Alice looked at her daughter with disbelief. She had always assumed she was just a spoiled little baby throwing tantrums, but feeling that immense life energy, she now realized Chris was far from ordinary!

Yet this was merely the tip of the iceberg regarding the life energy contained within Chris. If her full potential were truly unleashed, it would likely cause no small stir throughout the entire human world.

Though Alice had no idea why Chris possessed this power, she instinctively felt that it could not be separated from the elf race.

The blazing radiance emanating from the Elf King's fingertips gradually dimmed. The ritual was nearing its end; the inheritance of the elf race had already been received by the young Chris.

He felt a slight shock internally, finding the inheritance ritual far too smooth. Even though it was not the complete inheritance of the elf race—merely knowledge of the elven life branch—the inheritance ceremony would normally encounter significant obstacles for someone without elven bloodline, and in severe cases would drive the recipient's mind into madness!

Yet Chris showed none of that. Instead, she completed the ritual with complete ease! ?

This sent a chill through the Elf King's heart. He could only speculate that the life energy within Chris, as the source of all things, was far too powerful, allowing her to perfectly receive even the elven inheritance. His confusion deepened. What exactly was the origin of this child born from the mysterious stone?

With the ritual finished, the surging life energy in the room dissipated. Chris's eyes rolled back silently, and she fainted into Alice's arms, letting out steady "shoo shoo" breaths.

"Chris!" Alice saw her daughter faint and wore a face full of worry. What was going on?

The Elf King let out a long sigh and said calmly, "Don't worry, she's fine. She simply absorbed too much knowledge at once and is exhausted. She'll be bouncing around by tomorrow morning."

"...right." Alice felt relieved, looking at little Chris in her arms who was sucking her finger, her expression a mixture of doting affection and gratification.

Merlin stood nearby quietly observing Chris. He touched his chest as the sensation of the heart curse being affected gradually faded away.

So I've been surviving by constantly plundering life energy?

But Chris is still far too weak right now to be of any real use to me.

Though it can alleviate the curse, it cannot possibly cure it completely.

Merlin shook his head and recalled the golden spike driven into his heart. Only by removing that could the problem be彻底 resolved.

Still, Merlin wasn't without gains either. Seeing that life energy had slightly shaken the curse, perhaps if the life energy were powerful enough, that spike embedded deep within his heart could be extracted?

At this moment, no one noticed that outside the room's window, greedy eyes were staring fixedly at Chris.

Crono hung upside down from the eaves like a bat, shrinks wrapping his head forward, secretly peering at everything happening inside the room.

His eyes were filled with bloodshot veins, pupils constricted, and seeing the life energy Chris had just emitted made him overflow with excitement—

Take this child back, and even if I haven't found the box, the Demon Lord of Another World will still praise me greatly!!!

The next morning, the Adventurer Competition officially began, and everyone drew lots for their upcoming opponents.

Naturally, a few "lucky ones" emerged—adventurers who drew the bye slot, advancing directly to the quarterfinals without competing.

Almost all eyes converged on the dark-iron ranked adventurer who had stolen the spotlight yesterday, eager to find out who he would face next.

Merlin looked at the lot in his hand and involuntarily let out a bitter smile. It was the seemingly lucky but actually most unfortunate "bye."

What does this mean? Among so many lots, I happened to draw the most awkward one.....

Merlin had been quite excited today, thinking he would make a stunning debut, awe the crowd—but now he'd have to sit on the bench until the quarterfinals?

Old Mr. Dawson gave Merlin a meaningful look. He had also wanted to see what skills Merlin possessed to befriend so many nobles, but it seemed he would just have to wait patiently. He loudly announced.

"Merlin Lucifield from Rexem has drawn the lucky bye lot! Congratulations to Rexem for advancing to the quarterfinals without a fight!!!"

The moment he finished speaking, laughter and mocking jeers erupted from the audience stands and among the adventurers. Everyone held nothing but hostility toward this dark-iron noob who had leached off someone powerful just yesterday, and now he'd drawn another "lucky" lot.

It only made people feel more convinced he was a deadbeat who crawled into the quarterfinals on luck alone, unworthy of being mentioned in the same breath as other adventurers. So what if you know nobles? On the battlefield, strength is the only truth!

"Look, look! The adventurer who clung to a rich patron yesterday drew the lucky lot. Not only is he good at leeching, he's skilled at drawing lots too~ Looks like he's advancing to the quarterfinals without lifting a finger!"

"Bastard! Someone like that has the nerve to enter a competition? Doesn't he have any shame? Consider himself lucky, or I'd have beaten him until his head was split open, showing those nobles what real power looks like!"

"Pah! How many fighters are there in that bunch of cross-eyed adventurers from Rexem? That pale-faced dark-iron boy is nothing but a lucky winner. I suspect the nobles rig the draw to protect his pride."

"What good is rigging? Once we reach the quarterfinals, this guy will still get thoroughly beaten. Didn't you see the adventurers from Katowice yesterday wanting to devour him alive? He'll be lucky to walk away with his life this time."

Boz listened to the surrounding chatter. Though his face remained neutral, inside he was grinning from ear to ear.

A dark-iron rookie who was dragged into the competition at random—he shouldn't be listed alongside other adventurers or steal the spotlight?

These doubts and insults were exactly what this person deserved.

Boz had already disliked Merlin since yesterday's incident, and now hearing so many people mock him made him feel wonderfully satisfied!

"Forget it, he got lucky. Let him wait in his quarterfinal seat. When the time comes, I'll stab several holes through him with my sword!" Noa said viciously through his teeth.

"That damn thing—I'm going to trample him beneath my feet so Princess Margaret can see exactly how useless he is..." Gabrielle cracked his knuckles, his battle spirit already burning.

"Fight whoever you want. Last night the Guild Master said no holding back against him. If you kill him, just say you lost control of your power," Sean said, glaring coldly at Merlin on the arena.

Sigh.... Little Johnson sighed. "Uncle's too unlucky. Drawing the bye means no chance to show off. I was really looking forward to seeing his sword-drawing technique."

"With Lord Merlin's strength, he wouldn't possibly stop at the quarterfinals. He's a descendant of the gods, after all~" Old John stroked his beard, still spinning the tale of divine descent. Hearing the surrounding voices belittling Merlin, he sighed.

"When the quarterfinals arrive, all those who now despise Lord Merlin will be blushing and rendered speechless.

The more arrogant they are now, the more ashamed they'll be later.

title: Chapter 30 — Old Friend
content:
Chapter 30 — Old Friend

Volume 27 · Chapter 30

Old John still hadn't forgotten that Merlin might be a descendant of a deity, capable of bursting forth with astonishing battle power without needing any magic or battle aura.

This power likely had long since departed from the two major systems of magic and battle aura. With so many adventurers on the field, there probably weren't many who could contend with Merlin.

He felt that if his son could fully master the power of the magic furnace, perhaps he could spar with Merlin...

Old John felt a bit regretful. He had long heard his son say that Merlin was very powerful, and he was just about to witness it in person—yet he could only wait until the top eight match to have the chance.

However, Old John wasn't in a hurry. If his son wasn't exaggerating, then Merlin would surely soar into the sky and shock the masses within the top eight match!

"What a pity, this guy actually drew a bye position, and stepped straight into the top eight seats." Ligachev hiccuped and shook his head, then looked toward his side, "Tanya, don't be in a hurry, good food isn't afraid of being late."

Tanya remained silent, feeling a bit disappointed. Yesterday, after witnessing Crono suffer a loss and the nobles actively courting favor, this had greatly increased her interest in Merlin, and she hoped to face him on the very first day.

Too bad this wish came to naught. Tanya silently sighed, and had to shift her target to other people—Cronos, who was the opponent she had been looking forward to the most.

Cronos sat in a corner of the arena, not communicating with anyone, his eyes occasionally glancing at the little girl Alice was holding in her arms, yet he dared not make a move because he feared Merlin.

Zikatalio gazed at Merlin on the arena, not disliking him, but seeing that the Elf King had been particularly fond of Merlin yesterday, he felt very unbalanced.

As a half-elf born of human and elf blood, Zikatalio inherently needed a sense of belonging, and had inexplicable emotions toward other elves.

Zikatalio wanted to gain a sense of recognition, recognition from the elf race, just like the adventurers in Manchester City were willing to accept himself.

So Zikatalio took Merlin as an opponent; he wanted to defeat this man in front of the Elf King, thereby making that group of arrogant elves look at this half-elf with new eyes.

"...Alice sighed, thinking that Merlin encountering such a thing was really unlucky, but there was still a chance to prove oneself in the top eight match."

Chris curled up in Alice's arms, sucking his thumb and appearing somewhat tired. After last night's inheritance ceremony, this little guy seemed even more inclined to sleep than usual.

The Elf King explained that this was a normal phenomenon. The inheritance of the God Corelon was unlike anything else, and Chris was currently digesting new knowledge and power; in a few days, she would be bouncing about with energy.

Alice had to temporarily set aside her doubts, watching the little guy who only woke up for meals, and the rest of the time was sound asleep, making her feel that there was much less fun.

Hearing the chatter around him, Karl, who had a somewhat straightforward temper, drank a couple of cups and said, "What the hell are all you idiots talking about in here? Come out and let me take a look!"

The voices around him instantly quieted down a bit. Karl, after all, had participated in many large-scale competitions, and the top hundred players still had some reputation that could intimidate some weaker adventurers.

"Karl, enough..." Old Taylor frowned and forced out a thread of a smile, "This also counts as us of Rekham having pre-determined the top eight, counting as... good news?"

On the audience seats, Clodiaia shook her head, feeling very disappointed, thinking one—

- Early on, that girl Alice forced me to come watch the match, I thought there would be a surprise?

It turned out was just to see this useless man enter the top eight through luck?

Too naive. The arena is a place where strength speaks, what use is luck?

Clodiaia felt that Alice had been blinded by love, how could such a person protect her? It would be safer to just obediently return to the Great Snow Mountain with herself.

Just then, a sudden voice interrupted Clodiaia's train of thought, catching the usually steady woman off guard—

"Hah~, didn't expect to meet you here, it's really been a long time"

The lewd old sorceress Xesi suddenly appeared beside Clodiaia, wearing a meaningful expression, carefully examining the "old friend" of yesteryear.

This time Xesi came to Budapest because her student Susan was also participating in the competition, so as a teacher, she came to supervise the battle, hoping Susan could achieve good results and not bring shame to herself.

Although Susan's talent was not good, after several months of training by Xesi, her strength was already incomparable to before, at least having the standard to compete for the top hundred of the competition, she was full of confidence!

Xesi glanced at Clodiaia for a moment, feeling that "old friend" besides having aged a bit, still emitted the same aura of keeping others at a distance, and she couldn't help but reveal a sneering smile—

"You old thing, dirt clod."

"What did you say? Bitch..." Clodiaia snapped back to her senses, and immediately the veins on her forehead jumped, seeing her arch-enemy having no good expression, especially the mocking attitude, which made her very angry.

The two of them had never gotten along, and after so many years without seeing each other, coming straight out, there was a strong smell of gunpowder, with no intention of sitting down and catching up properly.

"Hahaha~" Xesi covered her mouth and laughed, seeing Clodiaia's flustered expression, her heart was even more delighted, "You really haven't changed? And from before having no charm, now even crow's feet have appeared, it's really pitiful~"

"What did you say?" Clodiaia gritted her teeth, the hand holding the sword trembling non-stop, "Don't think that everyone's stomach is full of flower guts like you, I am a person who dwells in training, the body is merely an stinky skin bag, I don't care!"

"Oh? Really?" Xesi narrowed her eyes, speaking triumphantly, "With your current state, not to mention me who is beautiful, even if it's just one percent of mine, you should just admit it gracefully, right? Your pretended calm look is really ugly, hah~"

Clodiaia twisted her mouth corner, speaking indifferentl, "The things from back then I have long forgotten, the person who could be hooked by you, must not be a good thing."

"Oy~, such a strong sour taste, it suffocated me." Xesi fanned the air in front of her nose, revealing a winner's posture, I heard you hid in the Great Snow Mountain, haven't gotten married, living alone is not comfortable, right? Old and widowed, how pitiful~"

"Oh? Didn't you get married? I bet you this kind of person isn't much stronger than me." Clodiaia coldly said.

Xesi was at a loss, a few black lines sliding down her forehead, embarrassedly saying, "You're meddling too much in my business?"

"Hah, I'm still puzzled what you're delighted about?" Clodiaia coldly laughed, her gaze contemptuous, "You're really the same old way, your strength isn't good, piled up with trivial matters, clearly an insecure and pitiful person~"

"Your strength isn't good? You really dare say that." Xesi's face gradually cooled down, countless toxins stirring.

"Want to fight? I'll accompany you to the end." Clodiaia drew out her sword, which was like autumn water, and immediately a chilly wind stirred up.

title: Chapter 31 — Opening Battle
content:
Chapter 31 — Opening Battle

Volume 27 · Chapter 31

Two people instantly flared with palpable hostility, their power clashing in the air between them.

They had always been mortal enemies, once even cutting each other down in a bloody duel over the same man.

Decades later, they still met as adversaries, each itching to prove who stood higher.

The crowd sensed the danger and quickly backed away, leaving a wide, empty ring around them—like a stage set for their duel.

All eyes were on Chris, whose Purple Gold Adventurer status drew gasps of admiration. Purple Gold Adventurers were rare, most hiding like dragons, so seeing one in person was the kind of thing ordinary folk bragged about for years.

Just as they were about to clash, a swirling black vortex tore open between them, as if connecting to some hidden realm.

Gregory emerged from it, his hunched, aged frame wreathed in a rasping laugh.

"I thought someone was causing trouble here. So it's you, Chris. Long time no see."

"You old coot. I figured that Great Swordsman finally killed you off," Chris said, her tone easing but still laced with sarcasm.

"Hahaha! I never expected that swordsman to strike so fiercely. My mistake." Gregory paused, then added, "Thanks for the potion. Without it, I might still be unconscious."

"Don’t expect that luck again. I won’t keep cleaning up after you," Chris scoffed, unimpressed by his gratitude.

Gregory gave an awkward chuckle and turned to the woman beside him. "So you must be the recluse from the Great Snow Mountain I’ve heard so much about?"

Claudia let out a cold laugh. "I’m sure it wasn’t anything nice."

"Oh no, no, no..." Gregory waved a hand, speaking slowly. "Chris said you were her favorite person. She trained so hard, hoping one day you’d need her."

"Huh?" Claudia’s expression twisted in disbelief. After knowing Chris for decades, she knew the woman would sooner eat her own tongue than say something like that.

"Mr. Gregory, what nonsense are you spouting?" Chris forced a smile, her eyes flashing with murderous intent. "I’ve never said anything like that."

"You said it after drinking too much," Gregory replied seriously.

"How could I ever drink that much? You must have misheard, right?" Chris’s smile turned ghastly, green veins crawling across her face like creeping poison. Her expression was serene, yet utterly terrifying.

"Cough! Cough..." Gregory coughed sharply, then muttered, "Ah... I must have misremembered. My apologies. My old brain isn’t what it used to be..."

Hearing that, the green veins on Chris’s face receded. Otherwise, no one knew what extreme measures she might have taken.

"Regardless of your feud, I hope you can restrain yourselves during the competition. This is the Adventurers Guild’s grand event every four years—no one wants it ruined, right?" Gregory said in a conciliatory tone.

"That’s true. I came here to watch my dear apprentice," Chris sneered.

"Your apprentice is competing too?" Gregory sounded surprised. He knew she had a student, though her talent wasn’t stellar.

"Of course. My apprentice belongs to a small guild. I sent her here to gain experience," Chris said, her gaze flicking challengingly toward Claudia. "My apprentice is far stronger than someone else’s student. If they meet, I’ll crush them into the dirt!"

"Is that so? I’ll be waiting," Claudia replied indifferently, convinced Chris made a poor teacher and her student couldn’t be much good.

Gregory, however, was concerned. If Chris’s student was strong, she might become a rival for Alice. He’d have to keep an eye on her.

On the arena, Merlin stared at the "bye" slip in his hand, both amused and annoyed by the murmurs around him. He’d somehow earned a new nickname—

"Lying-On-His-Laurels King!"

He ignored the jeers and tossed the slip onto the ground before turning to face the dense crowd ahead.

"You lot calling me the Lying-On-His-Laurels King..."

"Just wait."

"I’ll make you take those words back. I’ll show you how blind you’ve been!"

His declaration drew stunned reactions. Merlin was already hated enough, but now he’d climbed even higher on the hate list, with insults flying from all sides.

"Arrogant! Who’s ever seen someone waltz into the quarterfinals just by sitting around? Shameless!"

"Yeah, does he really think he’s strong enough? Just some Iron-rank adventurer—this is a joke, right?"

"Not everyone’s like last year’s champion, Krono. Some people have lost all sense of their own limits..."

Boze smirked to himself, thinking, Go ahead and strut. This is your last hurrah before the real beating starts.

Noah, Shawn, and Gabriel rolled their eyes, vowing to break Merlin’s legs so he’d never strut again.

Many adventurers saw Merlin as nothing more than prey—easy pickings for those seeking favor with the nobility. To them, he wasn’t a rival; he was a fat, helpless target.

Old Man Dawson watched Merlin’s back and nodded. He didn’t know how strong the boy really was, but his fearless defiance in the face of doubt wasn’t something everyone could muster. This man deserved attention.

With the draw complete, the Adventurers Guild Tournament officially began.

Since the competitors ranged from weak to strong, the early matches lacked intensity, so attendance was low.

Even major guests like the Rothschilds’ guards had already left, though a few still lingered in secret to protect their master.

Susan fidgeted nervously below the arena, her bottles clinking as she adjusted them. This was her first tournament, and she was a wreck.

Across from her stood a grizzled veteran who shot her a dismissive glance, supremely confident in his victory.

As the opening match, the stakes were higher than usual—if it wasn’t exciting, interest would plummet.

"See that? That’s my apprentice!" Chris shouted excitedly from the stands, her voice carrying to Susan. "Susan, show them what you’ve got! You’re my disciple!"

Susan’s body stiffened in terror, her face draining of color under the weight of so many eyes.

...I’m so nervous...

All my teacher taught me was potion-making...

If I forfeit now, she’ll lock me in the basement for sure...

Sorry, everyone! I got busy with weddings and ended up working until past 8 PM. My bad!

title: Chapter 32 — Atonement (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 32 — Atonement (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 27 · Chapter 32

Susan: Although I’m a disciple of the Purple Gold Adventurer, following Sersi hasn’t taught me any combat skills; it’s all about how to configure potions.
Now the teacher has forced me onto the arena, it’s like being thrown onto a stage with no preparation.
But Susan has learned quite a few offensive potions, ready to use them in the match.
As for whether I can win? It all depends on…
Sersi saw Susan on the arena lacking confidence, feeling oddly displeased. What is this girl afraid of? Show some confidence, otherwise my face as a teacher will be ruined!
“Is that your disciple? She doesn’t look very good,” Kloedia sneered, thinking Susan was far inferior to Alice.
“I’ve seen your student Alice; she’s not that great, but she found a good man~” Sersi retorted, unwilling to back down.
Upon hearing Sersi say Alice found a good man, Kloedia suddenly frowned, not feeling that Sersi was praising Merlin, but rather thinking the other was mocking herself.
On the dais, several members of the Arbitration Committee were critiquing the two contestants.
Tall member: “Both seem like unremarkable adventurers? Not much to watch.”
Chairman Dawson: “Who said that? That girl named Susan is Sersi’s disciple.”
Fat member: “Really? Sersi is an old witch; her disciple must also be a master of skills.”
Chairman Dawson: “Of course, Susan will definitely win this match, and it will end quickly, right?”
The referee signaled the two contestants to walk to the center of the arena, to say pre-battle declarations, commonly known as “trash talk,” an essential part to make the match more intense and please the audience.
Susan became increasingly nervous; her steps began to feel light, and before she even reached the opponent, she performed a grand salute—
A flat ground fall; a seemingly impossible situation occurred, Susan’s potion belt at her waist shattered into dust…
“Ah… Sersi’s face in the audience turned green, her expression froze on her face.”
“Haha…” Kloedia chuckled, “Your disciple seems not very smart…”
Susan, in the end, gasped, looking at the shattered potions on the ground, completely losing her offensive means.
So Susan stiffly approached the opponent, bowed deeply, and uttered a three-part exit phrase.
“Sorry, sorry for the trouble, farewell!”
The opposing adventurer looked utterly confused, not knowing what had happened? Somehow he had won the first victory? He hadn’t even made a move!
Susan’s ability to win depended entirely on potions, but the potions shattered—what else could she do? She could only awkwardly lose without fighting.
The referee watched Susan quickly escape from the arena, with a blank expression, and announced the opponent’s victory. As the opening match, it ended too quickly!
“Susan!!!” Sersi trembled all over, feeling her face ruined, especially in front of her dead rival.
“Oh wow~ your disciple is amazing? Leaving so fast is also something… I look at you, you scoundrel, with new respect, hahaha…” Kloedia seized the opportunity, wildly mocking Sersi.
Sersi rolled her eyes, feeling speechless about her incompetent disciple; she had taught so many things, but in real combat none were used.
r牡力U
On the dais, Mr. Dawson was very embarrassed; he had favored Susan, but she had “nursed” him to death? He coughed lightly and said…
“Cough cough! Mistake, mistake. I didn’t expect Sersi’s disciple to have no combat experience. We can look forward to the second match, Reksum’s Carl versus Manchester’s Bertlem.”
Short member: “Oh! Both of them have participated in several major competitions, very experienced!”
Thin member: “Yes, it must be a very exciting match. Carl’s Thunder Shock Fighting Technique is formidable, and Bertlem’s Earth Magic is extraordinary!”
“Hahaha, I think it won’t be exciting; it should be a match with no suspense, Bertlem will win.” Mr. Dawson said with confidence.
“What? Does the chairman not know that the Taylor family’s Thunder Shock Fighting Technique is very powerful? A match without suspense seems unlikely?” the short member said in surprise.
“Carl reached the top hundred in the last competition, but ultimately lost to Bertlem, so his chances were high. Moreover, I heard Bertlem had trained hard for four years; his strength is probably stronger. Carl may lose even faster this time.” Mr. Dawson’s analysis was reasonable.
After the two entered the stage, the old rival looked especially red-eyed, especially Carl, whose mind was full of revenge for past humiliation.
The opposing Bertlem seemed incredibly relaxed; after all, he was facing the previous season’s defeated subordinate right from the start, what a lucky break.
“Haha, long time no see, Carl brother. I didn’t expect to face you right away and eliminate you so quickly. Truly unexpected!”
Carl’s veins on his forehead throbbed frequently; he sneered,
“Four years, and I still don’t see any progress from you; your verbal skills have improved, though.”
“Is that so? If you’re not satisfied, come and try; maybe I’m only good at verbal skills.” Bertlem tightened his grip on the wand.
“Stop the chatter, show the real power under your hand!” Carl’s hand held a rugged black‑gold gauntlet, suddenly shook.
Both are Saint‑tier Secret Silver Adventurers; at first glance, the difference in strength is not large.
But in the last competition, Carl lost to Bertlem in ten seconds; it was a very humiliating incident.
The referee, after the two finished trash talk, raised his hand and loudly announced “The match begins.” The audience erupted in cheers.
Clearly, both are famous adventurers; this match tugged at countless…
Below, old Taylor’s palms were full of sweat, very worried about Carl’s condition. Four years ago, a ten‑second defeat; what will happen after four years? Let’s see if the Thunder Shock Sword Technique can create miracles!
“Drink!” Carl’s whole body exploded with fighting spirit, like a dazzling…
“Just like before, the momentum is good, but the power is insufficient!” Bertlem also…
As Bertlem swung his wand, the hard ground beneath his feet suddenly turned into something like water, soft, able to change shape at will!?
The soft ground spun, instantly rising to the sky,…
On the massive arena, it unleashed a rock tsunami, the momentum surging, the shadow covering half the arena!
Bertlem didn’t hold back; he launched a big move, intending to strike first, using fierce attacks to crush Carl directly!
Carl roared, his hands like claws, swinging in the air; the rock tsunami instantly shattered, torn to dust. “Show some real skill! Bertlem!”

But he was not panicked; he raised his wand, arms open…
The magic within him surged to the peak—
“As you wish!”
The earth trembled…
Boom boom boom…

title: Chapter 33 — Drawing to a Close
content:
Chapter 33 — Drawing to a Close

Volume 27 · Chapter 33

One hundred massive rock arms crisscrossed each other, enveloping the tiny Kal in their grasp—the disparity in power was visible to the naked eye!

"This victory, I'll accept it!" Bertrem sneered, raising his magic staff high before bringing it down heavily....

As if responding in unison, the dense cluster of rock arms crashed down upon Kal with crushing force!

A deafening roar echoed endlessly as the colossal rock arms seemed to descend into madness, pounding the ground like swatting mosquitoes!

Spectators in the stands paled with shock, feeling the earth tremble beneath them, utterly awestruck by Bertrem's terrifying power!

This was Bertrem's strongest technique—the enormous rock palms possessed staggering destructive power, making enemies feel as though they were besieged by fifty rock giants.

Even with considerable skill, one would hardly escape such widespread attacks.

At the presiding dais, Old Man Dawson shook his head, "Well? I told you so. This is a match with a vast gap in ability."

Skinny Committee Member: "Indeed, it seems Bertrem has grown much stronger over these four years. Kal has no room to resist at all."

Tall Committee Member: "Rhexum can probably only hope for that swordsman this time. There might be a surprise."

Crack—

A golden thunderbolt exploded, and the crisscrossing rock arms shattered as though cut by a blade.

Blinding lightning surged skyward, making it almost painful to look at!

The shocking thunder converged and transformed into a razor-sharp edge, charging irresistibly toward the bewildered Bertrem.

"No...impossible?!" Bertrem screamed in terror, instantly engulfed by the lightning's brilliance.

The arbitrator committee members at the dais leapt to their feet in fright, staring at the arena shrouded in thunder, speechless, unable to comprehend what had happened.

Merlin's face remained calm and expressionless. He could see traces of iaijutsu within Kal's bare-handed martial art—just a hint of drawn-sword technique. He wondered if he was being secretly studied and learned from? This technique had nearly cost his subordinates their lives, proving truly dangerous.

The president committee members exchanged bewildered glances. Old Man Dawson's face flushed uncomfortably, with nearly every prediction failing—making explanation impossible.

Chubby Committee Member: "Chairman, your predictions were inaccurate. Rhexum's guild is clearly quite strong."

Short Committee Member: "True. This Kal appears far stronger than last year. He might have a chance to become a purple-gold ranked adventurer in our lifetime."

Dawson felt extremely embarrassed, thinking that Rhexum's Adventurers Guild was at mid-tier levels. Why had this generation suddenly become so strong?

Everyone discussed the swift power of the Thunder Strike style, unaware this was merely superficial knowledge Old Taylor had received from Merlin.

What if Merlin demonstrated his own drawn-sword strike? What expressions would this crowd wear?

Over half a month passed, and the Adventurer Competition continued without end, growing hotter as it neared its conclusion.

Unlike the mixed-bag competition at the opening, the later matches became extraordinarily intense!

Each adventurer possessed their signature technique, making easy victories difficult. Almost every contest featured evenly matched opponents.

The arena remained packed to capacity. Streets and alleys across all human territories buzzed with discussions about the adventurers—

"Who's that guy? So powerful!"

"Have you never watched the competition before? That's Kal, using his family's Thunder Strike style."

"I couldn't even see clearly. The lightning flashed, and the opponent was defeated. Truly frightening."

Originally, Rhexum's unfavorable reputation due to Merlin had slightly improved because of Kal's outstanding performance.

Clodia slowly closed her eyes, pondering silently. What technique was that just now? So powerful—clearly beyond Saint-tier. She never expected a small place like Rhexum to have people with profound martial arts understanding?

Old Taylor exhaled deeply, watching his son defeat his earlier rival. He felt genuine joy and gratitude toward Merlin. Without Merlin's inspiration, the family's Thunder Strike style might never have reached new heights.

"Was that... the Thunder Strike style?" Alice furrowed her brow. She had seen the guild master demonstrate it long ago, but this time felt different—sharper, more lethal?

Alice had been cutting through obstacles over the past half month, advancing triumphantly and frequently defeating strong opponents, showing clear trends toward early championship locking.

Though Kal had been eliminated in the top 32, Alice's performance remained excellent, steadily approaching the final matches.

Seeing Alice receive countless flowers and applause, Merlin—normally just the water-boy—grew restless, hoping for his turn to teach these show-offs a lesson.

Meanwhile, at the arena, a mithril-ranked adventurer knelt on the ground, teeth clenched: "...I lost."

Alice sheathed her slender sword as the golden ice shards covering the ground melted instantly. "Well fought."

The referee nodded and announced loudly—

"Congratulations to Alice·Clodia for breaking into the top eight first!"

title: Chapter 34 — The Battle for the Top Eight Reaches Fever Pitch
content:
Chapter 34 — The Battle for the Top Eight Reaches Fever Pitch

Volume 27 · Chapter 34

"The demon swordswoman from Rexem is so strong! Her power seems bottomless!"

"I heard she possesses the power of a giant dragon, but hasn't used it yet. She clearly still has trump cards up her sleeve!"

"This is extraordinary! With that demon swordswoman around, I feel Rexem really has a chance to take the championship!"

"Now I get why that Iron-rank adventurer was so arrogant at the start. Turns out she's got her wife backing her up. Can't mess with them~"

Cheers and enthusiastic applause kept echoing from the stands. Nobody held back their praise for Alice, regarding her as Rexem's most promising competitor.

Little Chris jumped down from Merlin's embrace and happily did circles below the arena, proud to have such a powerful mom. "Mom won again~ Mom's so awesome~"

Alice picked up Chris and teased, "You sure know how to flatter."

After inheriting the Elf race legacy, Chris's body had gradually returned to normal, and she was slowly learning to master the massive life force within her.

However, Merlin and Alice hadn't noticed anything particularly strange about Chris. Her appetite had grown somewhat, and occasionally she would mutter to herself about seeing little sprite-like creatures among the elements, like fireflies.

This scared Merlin and Alice, who feared their daughter might have some mental issue. It wasn't until they consulted the Elf King that they finally understood.

Chris was gradually learning the Elf race's innate talent: the ability to communicate with and command the element sprites that are invisible and intangible.

The ability to communicate with the elements in the air was the elves' enormous advantage and also the reason so many powerful mages kept emerging from their race.

Merlin's expression darkened. Seeing Chris so proud of Alice only made him more unsettled. What the hell? Was his image as a father growing smaller in his daughter's eyes?

Over half a month passed, and as Alice kept winning, Merlin felt increasing pressure. Many people's impression of him had morphed from just a freeloader into someone who thrived in the public eye solely through nepotism.

"Merlin, don't worry. Your turn's coming up soon," Mr. Carl said, walking over and patting Merlin on the shoulder.

"I know," Merlin replied calmly. Today they'd narrow it down to the top eight, and tomorrow would be his day to shine!

Carl had been sadly eliminated in the round of 32. He looked at his injured right arm and said helplessly, "I can only cheer you on from here. It's up to you and Alice from now on. What an amazing sight it would be if you two met in the final."

Alice's winning streak had greatly boosted Rexem's morale. Even Crody from the stands nodded with satisfaction, looking at Cessy beside her and saying, "Well? Can my student be called outstanding or not?"

"Hmph, she's just okay. The opponents she's faced have been average. Your student hasn't yet met a truly troublesome opponent." Cessy smirked coldly. "Among all the fighters in this tournament, there are really only two or three who can actually fight. The rest are just fillers. You won't see real differences until the quarterfinals or semifinals."

The two had been chatting privately a lot recently. Though they might still clash at any moment, they were no longer as impulsive as they used to be.

Because of Alice's outstanding performance, Crody felt like she'd completely outshone her longtime rival, basking in a sense of triumph she'd never experienced before.

In contrast, Cessy, whose prized student Susan had been swiftly defeated, felt the frustration of being suppressed by her archenemy. She was secretly looking forward to Rexem's Adventurers Guild falling apart.

Susan, avoiding everyone's gaze, obediently stayed by Cessy's side. She'd been thoroughly scolded by her master these past few days and probably wouldn't get a chance to play around once they returned to the forest.

Just thinking about being locked in confinement and forced into hellish training by her master after returning made Susan feel like she couldn't breathe. She didn't dare talk back to her master anymore.

"What do you mean by that? Are you saying my student can't win the championship?" Crody scoffed. She had taught Alice the swordsmanship of the Great Snow Mountain. While she couldn't claim Alice would sweep all the adventurers present, she was confident in her championship potential.

"I think the champion might be some unexpected guy," Cessy said mysteriously, her peripheral glance falling on Merlin below the stands. She thought: this guy had the courage to storm into the mysterious Sea Realm and the ability to survive and return. He was far from ordinary. Those people who wanted to thoroughly humiliate him in the quarterfinals were in for quite a headache~

"ROAR~"

A giant dragon's roar made everyone present shudder, their terrified eyes fixed on the tiny figure on the arena.

The fierce quarterfinal qualification matches continued. After Alice advanced, the second spot in the top eight was immediately locked in as well!

Aria wiped the corner of her mouth, half-asleep she scratched her little belly and let out a satisfied burp.

"Uh!" Alice's expression flickered with surprise, because she could clearly sense the power of a kindred being. That massive roar and breath attack had left her opponent completely unable to defend, defeated in an instant.

The referee's voice was slightly hoarse as he looked at Aria, unable to imagine how such terrifying power could be unleashed from such a small body.

He stiffly announced Aria's victory, and another member of the top eight was born. The crowd erupted into murmurs.

"That... that was dragon breath just now, right? It definitely was!"

"One open its mouth and the opponent is gone? This is too exaggerated! She must've been holding back during the earlier matches?"

"I didn't expect besides the demon swordswoman from Rexem, another person wielding giant dragon power has appeared? This is getting even better!"

Aria smacked her lips, her gaze landing on Alice below the arena. She made a stiff face, then wobbled off the stage.

Alice frowned, wondering if someone besides herself had obtained the inheritance crystal. But what was with those little horns on her head? Could it be from being corrupted by the dragon's power...

"Hmm?" Merlin, seeing Aria, felt a twinge of surprise. He had never imagined a second person would be lucky enough to find an inheritance crystal. Aria's sudden display of power was truly astonishing!

"So this is your trump card, Gregory..." Old Taylor squinted, gazing at the towering old man in the distance. He thought to himself: fortunately, he still had Merlin hidden up his sleeve. Otherwise, Alice alone probably wouldn't have been able to hold the line.

Then, Noah and Gabriel, two of Boz's proud warriors, both defeated their respective opponents and advanced to the top eight in one stroke!

The supporters of the Katowice Guild in the stands erupted in thunderous cheers, rallying for Katowice.

With two Katowice members now among the top eight, the traditional powerhouse guild remained formidable.

Although Rexem also had two people in the top eight, Merlin had long since been ignored by everyone.

Boz, down below, showed a long-unseen smile. As long as his disciple Sean could also win, the top eight would feature three Katowice members—a massive advantage.

After the arena was cleaned, the referee announced the next match.

Super Nova Tanya vs. Gem Flow's sole heir, Sean!

title: Chapter 35 — Extra Chapter: Two in One
content:
Chapter 35 — Extra Chapter: Two in One

Volume 27 · Chapter 35

The adventurers of Rexium gathered in front of the big screen in the public office. “Alice this time faces many strong opponents? I saw in the quarterfinals that the elimination rate was quite high.” Hobbs said, holding his wine cup, shaking his head. “What nonsense are you talking? Alice will definitely beat all her opponents into a bloody mess, just watch!” Lucilia said sternly, , even knowing that the quarterfinals are full of strong contenders, besides Merlin everyone has real skill, but she still believes Alice can keep winning. Hobbs smiled without speaking, although Alice's strength is now quite good, , but those who can make it to the quarterfinals are all fierce as tigers, not so easy to win the championship. Mini sat beside Hobbs, despite having no interest in the adventurers' tournament, being able to eat good food here made her much quieter. “Next match is Tanya versus Sean, who do you think will win?” Lucilia asked tentatively, thinking Hobbs' evaluation of famous adventurer leaders was spot‑on, clearly he had some insider info. “Not easy to say” Hobbs put down his wine cup, showing a thoughtful expression, the two opponents were already on the stage on the big screen. “Not easy to say?” Lucilia felt surprised, it was the first time she saw Hobbs unable to predict a match result; before he got almost all right, he must have made a lot in the underground casino. , the previous tournament Boz was incredibly strong, no need to elaborate; if it weren't for running into that freak Chrono, he would surely have been champion.” Hobbs paused, then analyzed, “If Sean can perform well, his win rate is still quite high; gem magic is not only powerful but also versatile, able to handle many situations.” “Really?” Lucilia recalled Boz in the previous tournament using gem magic to unleash various powerful attacks, indeed very hard to deal with. Although called gems, they are actually crystallized magical elements of various attributes, each containing nearly terrifying magical power! She secretly reached for the wine cup, but was stopped in time. Lucilia saw out of the corner of her eye Mini sneaking a wine cup while the adults weren't looking, “Kids aren't allowed to drink alcohol, don't learn from your dad.” “Mmm~!” Mini puffed her cheeks, not happy about Lucilia's interruption. At that moment, the Rexium adventurers watching the match erupted in a commotion, loudly discussing in disbelief— “Won? ! So fast! “Sean hasn't even made a move! “—I didn't even see clearly, how did Sean just lose? !” Hobbs and Lucilia simultaneously lifted their heads, eyes fixed on the magic screen of the live broadcast, feeling incredulous— One second the two were just on the stage, the next second they lost? ! The arena fell silent. Almost everyone thought it would be an evenly matched fight, but reality was Tanya knocked Sean out with a single punch. Boz's face turned green down below; how could Sean, who had studied gluttony magic with him for so long, not even get a chance to cast? Boz's gaze gradually darkened; he had thought Tanya as a newcomer was just average, maybe hyped up, but he didn't expect her strength to be so terrifying! Noah and Gabriel looked shocked, feeling a hint of fear toward Tanya on the stage; she would be the strongest competitor in the quarterfinals! Sean, as Boz's disciple, was stronger than Noah and Gabriel, yet he lost in one round, making Noah and Gabriel even more terrified. “Great job! Tanya!” Ligajov cheered from below, having smoothly entered the quarterfinals; this was his first time participating and he achieved such a result. He was very satisfied! Tanya looked at the dazed Sean on the ground, coldly saying, “So weak, if the upcoming opponents are all like you, I'll be too disappointed.” The whole arena fell into silence, many people still stunned by Tanya, only snapping back after the next match ended. Adventurers facing the previous champion Chrono chose not to fight but to forfeit, letting Chrono win without a battle. Chrono participated in a total of 34 matches this tournament; thirty opponents chose to forfeit, only four iron‑willed dared to face him, resulting in all being beaten to a near‑death state, who would still dare to go head‑to‑head with him? Most adventurers drew Chrono as their opponent, considered themselves unlucky, and chose to surrender as the best option, after all they couldn't win anyway. “Yeah, but it's normal; don't look at Chrono being a black‑iron adventurer, he's last year's champion, even the violet‑gold adventurers can't beat him.” “It's very likely Chrono will win again this time, after all his summoned beasts are too powerful.” The arbitration committee on the presidential platform fell silent collectively; opponents forfeiting was expected, after all few adventurers can share the stage with Chrono. The final match of the quarterfinals arrived, Little Johnson's opponent was the half‑elf mage Zikatiro who had humiliated him in the Magic Beast Forest; he had been waiting for this moment for a long time. The two could be called enemies meeting, eyes red with hatred, as soon as they stepped onto the stage the air was filled with a thick smell of gunpowder— “I didn't expect to meet you; I thought you had already been eliminated earlier.” Zikatiro wore a robe, still unwilling to show his pointed ears, “Cut the crap, I'll beat you so you can't get up in the Magic Beast Forest and take back my prey, , you'll pay the price!” Little Johnson said confidently. “Oh? You still hold a grudge over that? Truly an immature little brat?” Zikatiro sneered, “You want to occupy that magic beast crystal core, but first see if you have the ability.” “Hmph, go ahead and be smug here, , I'll make you cry soon!” Little Johnson assumed his stance, his magic ring emitting rays of light. The referee on stage, seeing the time was right, loudly announced the start of the match! As soon as the words fell, Little Johnson struck first, launching a fierce attack— See Little Johnson's hand quickly fuse fire and light elements, the air instantly burst with thunder and explosion sounds. Scorching fire and sharp lightning formed a terrifying storm, roaring toward Zikatiro! “Trivial tricks!” Zikatiro's hand conjured a sharp shadow scythe, with a swing he dispersed Little Johnson's attack, then charged forward aiming for a quick finish. Little Johnson, in panic, mimicked Zikatiro's magic, likewise creating a shadow scythe in his hand to block the fierce assault. Their saint‑tier magic power collided wildly, the shadow scythes in their hands kept spitting sparks, seemingly unable to decide a winner quickly. “Copying others' magic? Do you think it's fun? Such childish tricks, don't embarrass yourself in front of me.” Zikatiro gave a mocking smile. “Childish tricks? Ahaha~” Little Johnson blocked Zikatiro's scythe with his right hand, while his left hand suddenly created a second shadow scythe aiming to slash Zikatiro's neck! In the panic he still had a few strands of hair cut off! Little Johnson's specialty is imitation; he can return the same magic with even greater power! “You're fast!” Little Johnson showed a smug smile, “Your magic is pretty useful.” Zikatiro at this moment had to seriously consider this young mage, realizing he needed to get serious to deal with this opponent. Because he cannot use ordinary magic, the opponent can fully use an enhanced counterattack, draining him would likely cause problems. So Zikatiro changed his usual attitude, his expression turned serious, he took off his hood, revealing his dark elf appearance, his pointed ears twitching. Although many know Zikatiro is a half‑elf, seeing his true face still drew gasps from the audience, after all mixed‑blood is rare. “Do you think you can copy all magic?” Zikatiro asked coldly. “Exactly, I can do it; as long as you use magical power, I can copy it.” Little Johnson said proudly. “What about elf magic then? Zikatiro finally got serious, thinking he must defeat this opponent with all his might. Elf magic is nearly impossible for humans to learn. Unless one has elf blood, or like Chris, received orthodox inheritance, it's possible. oE this term cure Zikatiro seized this point, wanting to use the elf magic he doesn't particularly like to crush Little Johnson directly. See Zikatiro clenching both hands, the magical pressure that had been suppressed all along kept rising, until it could barely stop at the ancestral level! On the presidential platform, seeing Zikatiro reveal his true self, the committee members exclaimed in surprise. Tall committee member: “Zikatiro is getting serious now? Johnson will suffer, he'll probably lose terribly.” Fat committee member: “Chairman, how do you view this match?” “How to view?” Old Mr. Dawson stroked his beard, chest full of confidence, saying, “Although Zikato's elf magic is strong, this match father is a friend, last night we chatted and learned some secrets~” The match John will surely win, because I and he are sworn brothers, using effect, fresh photo wild, with dark elf Alicia Wang network cultivation magic the same, just become Zikatiro released countless elf magic light bolts shooting out, power slightly inferior. The density of the magic light bolts was such that even a fly couldn't dodge, they blanketed the sky, pressing down, the whole stage shrouded in black light. “Johnson lost” T Karl shook his head, feeling regretful, “If he had a few more years of training, he would surely be unmatched in the world, but he's still too young.” “Not certain.” Merlin gave a bland evaluation, after all the magical pressure on Little Johnson's body is of an unknown kind, that fused colossus hasn't been used yet. “How about elf magic? I can do it too!” Little Johnson roared, his internal magic furnace burst forth with dazzling light and pressure, his whole body covered in magical runes! Magic only elves can use, he actually managed to imitate it again! With the support of the magic furnace, his power even surpassed Zikatiro's. The Johnson family, magical geniuses run in the blood; countless ancestors' wisdom condensed into the magic furnace, enhancing strength is not just a little bit. Elf magic, though powerful, is nothing; the Johnson ancestors a hundred years ago could already use it, even comprehended magic to produce attacks comparable to ancestral‑level power, this is just using 1% of the magic furnace's power. Their magic barrages frenziedly clashed, the arena sky kept erupting with explosions, everyone's heads buzzed! “Ugh!” Zikatiro exclaimed in shock, he hadn't expected Little Johnson's strength to increase so much in a short time! suppressing himself Although Little Johnson's imitative magic is a bit stronger than Zikatiro's, in a short time they are deadlocked, hard to decide a winner. We must decide the winner quickly! Thus in desperation, Little Johnson forgot his father's advice, again increased the output of his internal magic furnace to 2% power. The magic light bolts suddenly surged, Little Johnson's whole body was enveloped in terrifying magical amplification, as if becoming the brightest sun in the arena. “I will win!!” Zikatiro's attacks were scattered, the dense assaults loomed over his head, next second he would be defeated! But Little Johnson suddenly lost focus, collapsed to the ground, the terrifying magic light barrage also dissipated. With Little Johnson's current strength, he cannot fully utilize the magic furnace; 19% is the limit, unfortunately he was too impatient. The arena fell silent for three seconds, then a wave of doubtful voices rose; the referee barely came to his senses, just moments ago everyone thought Little Johnson had already won. “...Zikatiro, victory!” He gazed at the now unconscious Little Johnson, his expression complex; although he won, it felt like a lucky win, he felt a bit ashamed! John Johnson hurried onto the stage, helped up his son to check him over, secretly breathed a sigh of relief, good thing it was just a faint from the magic furnace's power. Old Johnson felt sorry for his son; there was no need to push so hard, but this child has been competitive since childhood, he really wanted to win. Merlin shook his head, said blandly, On the presidential platform, the arbitration committee members looked at each other, Old Mr. Dawson , Mr.浦靠 also looked very awkward. Skinny committee member: “Chairman, how did it suddenly turn out like this? You said Johnson was sure to win?” “......I won't speak anymore...” Old Mr. Dawson's face turned red, thinking— This mouth of mine... really kills whoever it speaks to. The quarterfinals ended; tomorrow will be the even fiercer semifinals. On the stage, Chairman Dawson spoke at length— “Alice, Noah, Gabriel, Tanya, Chrono, Elaria, Zikatiro, Merlin—” “Congratulations to the above contestants, becoming this tournament's quarterfinalists!” External link , please feel honored for this! All past quarterfinalists are extremely strong adventurers; see you as you gather your moves to mirror each other. The audience burst into enthusiastic applause, because tomorrow is the highly anticipated semifinal battle, intensity likely beyond imagination. Of course the most excited is still Merlin down below, because he can tomorrow go on stage to educate this bunch of show‑offs, how could he not be excited? “Then let's begin the semifinal draw ceremony, please invite the first contestant Merlin to come up and draw his opponent.” Old Mr. Dawson ......Merlin lightly smiled as he walked onto the stage, casually drew a slip, which clearly read “Noah” on it— Tsk tsk tsk, truly fate's cruel joke~ You once said I wasn't qualified to challenge you? So what now? (heart?

title: Chapter 36 — Margaret's Gift
content:
Chapter 36 — Margaret's Gift

Volume 27 · Chapter 36

Merlin looked at the slip of paper in his hand and laughed to himself inside. He had finally waited for this moment!

He had already found Noé rather annoying, and for him to draw Noé right at the start—wasn't this plainly handing him an opportunity?

Merlin shot a sharp look toward Noé down below the arena, filled with anticipation for tomorrow.

Let's see whose blade-drawing speed is faster—his own, or that bullshit supersonic swordsmanship!

Old Mr. Dawson glanced at the draw Merlin had pulled and loudly announced to everyone, "Mr. Merlin's opponent is Sir Noé from the Katowice Guild!"

The news instantly spread throughout the entire arena. Many people regarded Merlin with the mindset of watching a clown and couldn't resist starting to mock him from the stands.

Merlin himself had relied entirely on luck to jump straight into the quarterfinals, and many people didn't have high hopes for him at all. They all thought he was just a spineless coward who was good at currying favor with the powerful.

Moreover, the semifinals were now approaching. Anyone who had reached this point was an adventurer with formidable strength, and a guy who survived by clinging to bigger names would surely be beaten badly.

Many people seemed to already see Merlin being thoroughly humiliated tomorrow, turning him into a joke that would spread far and wide—maybe never able to hold his head up again for the rest of his life.

"Hah, this guy is really unlucky, drawing Noé. If he had drawn Alice, the demon swordswoman from the same guild, he might have suffered less beatings~"

"I've heard Noé privately disdains this Iron-rank adventurer. Looks like there's going to be a good show tomorrow. How about we bet on how many bones he'll break?"

"Noé will defeat him without even breaking a sweat. His supersonic swordsmanship is superb! The speed of his strikes is something our eyes can't even follow!"

Listening to the gossip around him, Noé down below couldn't help but feel a bit carried away, thinking everyone was telling the truth, that he was simply this powerful and could handle someone like Merlin with ease...

Sorry, he wouldn't even need to draw a second sword to take his life!

When Noé learned his opponent for tomorrow was Merlin, his heart had already burst with joy. He felt incredibly fortunate—this was as if heaven itself favored him, lifting him straight into the semifinal bracket!

Originally, after seeing Sean rendered completely defenseless in front of Tanya, Noé had been quite anxious, fearing his opponent might be this super新星. But instead, it was the soft-bellied merman Merlin!

This made Noé extremely happy. If there weren't so many people around, he might have jumped up and down with joy right on the spot.

"Hey, you're way too lucky! You managed to pick the weakest opponent to face~" Gabrielle curled her lip. "I'll congratulate you on reaching the semifinals early then."

Sigh, how boring. Noé was pleased inside but put on a helpless expression on the surface. "If I had to face a strong enemy, I might have some interest. But someone like this? How dull~"

Sean hung his head, his face gloomy, with a hint of bitterness in his heart. As Boz's only disciple, he had been defeated disgracefully. Noé might turn out to be the top-performing adventurer from Katowice this time, and he would surely receive the guild master's favor upon returning.

Because of Sean's defeat, Boz had been in a poor mood, but seeing that Noé's opponent was Merlin and that he would steadily reach the semifinals…

This cheered Boz up considerably. He admitted that he had underestimated the rising star Tanya, but as long as he could secure second place in this tournament, it would still be pretty good!

Next, the other adventurers also drew their opponents for tomorrow. Everyone wore different expressions—some joyful, some worried.

Alice's opponent was Elia. As someone who could also wield the power of the dragon race, she felt a certain curiosity toward that seemingly young person.

Gabrielle's opponent was Cronus. Facing the previous champion, he felt enormous pressure and secretly sensed that the quarterfinals might be his endpoint.

Tanya's opponent was Zikatiro. However, Tanya had no interest in Zikatiro, showing a hint of regret on her face. She would have preferred to face Merlin or Cronus.

The lottery ceremony ended, and everyone prepared to return and rest well to deal with tomorrow's matches. The audience also began to disperse.

But suddenly, a small插曲 interrupted everyone's thoughts. Margaret lifted her skirt and ran toward the arena stage. Blaise's expression was a mixture of wanting to cry and being speechless as he tried to stop the princess from causing any trouble.

"Your Highness! Calm down a bit, don't do this! I won't be able to explain myself when we get back!"

The Adventurer Competition had entered its final stage. More than half a month had passed, and since most of the guest attendees had appeared at the opening ceremony, several had already left.

Elizabeth, burdened by immense pressure and not wanting to encounter Merlin, had left with her loyal knight Morrison just a week later.

McReady, the bodyguard of Rothschild—the world's richest man—had also departed to tend to the young master of his family, though powerful guards remained to secretly protect the family head.

The remaining guests all intended to watch until the end, wanting to know who would be this year's champion!

Margaret hurriedly stepped onto the arena stage and loudly announced something to all the adventurers—

"Ladies and gentlemen, forgive my interruption. The Adventurer Competition is a quadrennial event, and tomorrow we will welcome the semifinal matches. A contest without any prizes is very boring, so I will bestow some blessings upon the eventual champion~"

All the adventurers saw the beautiful French princess come onto the stage and turned to look, drawing many people's attention.

After all, a beautiful princess was always the most dazzling presence wherever she went. Moreover, Margaret's beauty was truly mesmerizing.

Hearing that Margaret was offering a blessing to the champion, many perked up their ears and couldn't help but fantasize—would it be something like giving herself in marriage or something similar?

"Cough cough!" Margaret cleared her throat and said with a serious expression, "Whoever becomes champion may kiss me."

Blaise's eyes rolled back as soon as he heard this, nearly fainting outright. "Your Highness, you must not! You cannot do this! His Majesty will be angry if he finds out!"

"Shut up. This is something I have decided." Margaret shot Blaise a glare, thinking to herself that Father had assigned Blaise to keep an eye on her—it was so annoying!

Those adventurers eliminated from the competition below the stage immediately started banging their chests and wailing in regret, especially the men who were filled with remorse. If they had known the champion would earn the chance to kiss the princess, countless people would have risked their lives!

It was a pity that she only revealed this now. This group of eliminated adventurers had no chance anymore. They felt they had missed the opportunity to kiss the most beautiful woman in all of France. How could they not be regretful?

Most of the male adventurers who had entered the top eight showed no interest at all. Only Noé and Gabrielle seemed like they had been injected with adrenaline—

Noé: "Kissing the French princess!? I can do it! This is clearly a blessing prepared just for me!"

Gabrielle: "Damn it! It looks like I need to go all-out against Cronus this time! Her Highness Margaret's kiss is mine!"

"Tch!" Merlin, seeing Margaret on the stage fixating on him, felt a wave of bewilderment. What is this troublesome woman doing? She's killing all my motivation to win the championship!

Alice of course knew Margaret's little scheme, and her face darkened immediately. Anger seemed to喷 from her eyes.

She wanted nothing more than to overturn the jar of jealousy in her heart right on Margaret's head, then kick this fox spirit who was harassing Merlin up to heaven!

At this moment, Alice had never felt so desirous of the championship before. An illusion surged within her—as if her combat power had increased a hundredfold!

"You fox spirit. Things I haven't even done yet—you won't get your way..."

"Mom... so scary."

Little Chris shivered in her mother's arms, having never seen such a terrifying mother before, like a powder keg that could explode at any moment.

"Hehe~" Margaret stood on the stage, her gaze fixed meaningfully on Merlin, already calculating her little scheme in her heart.

Lord Merlin, you must work hard!

I'll be waiting for you on the championship podium!!!

title: Chapter 37 — Battle for the Top Four!
content:
Chapter 37 — Battle for the Top Four!

Volume 27 · Chapter 37

Adventurers pounded their chests in frustration, feeling utterly devastated at having missed the chance to grow close to Princess Margaret.

But the spectators were thrilled instead—everyone loved a story about a strong man winning the princess's favor, the kind of rags-to-riches tale that had people cheering.

Alice's gaze turned hostile as she stared at Merlin without speaking, seeming intent on peering into whatever he was thinking.

"Don't look at me, I don't know anything..." Merlin's eyes darted away, his heart racing with panic.

Above the arena, the robed Florentia sat at the highest seat, nearly imperceptible to all, taking a crunching bite of apple as he looked down upon the crowd that seemed like ants.

His plan was progressing steadily and smoothly—he had already amassed a vast amount of magical power and battle aura, and was drawing close to completing his task.

Over a month had passed, yet no one had discovered Florentia's plan. Some adventurers had noticed they were consuming more power than usual, but it wasn't so dramatic as to warrant concern.

Florentia chewed his apple, a trace of contempt in his gaze, like a chessmaster looking down upon countless tiny pawns, all at his disposal.

*Come on, push yourselves harder~*

You foolish adventurers...

In the most luxurious inn of Budapest, once a place that accommodated adventurers from all corners of the world, the atmosphere had grown noticeably冷清.

Since the tournament had moved into its latter half, most of the eliminated adventurers hadn't lingered—they had slunk off in defeat.

On the rooftop of the inn at this hour, Claudius and her arch-rival Celia stood at the highest point, taking in the beautiful night scenery.

They had talked through a lot over the past month; the fire from when they first met had cooled considerably. At the very least, they could now sit and have a proper conversation.

"It's really surprising," Celia sighed. "I thought that once you left the Palace Guard, I'd have no competition left, and you'd rocket through the ranks in the Kingdom of Spain—hopefully becoming at least a Holy Knight~"

"You're overthinking it," Claudius said calmly, lowering her head. "I have no desire for power or status. I only wish to find a stable place to settle."

"Really? I'm not so sure," Celia said teasingly.

"Believe what you want," Claudius sniffed.

"Back when we were in the Palace Guard, you were my captain—and you made sure to take advantage of your position to pick on me constantly, all while claiming you had no interest in power?" Celia ground her teeth.

"Well..." Claudius paused, then spoke seriously. "The Palace Guard is a disciplined force. Once you arrived, the atmosphere deteriorated terribly. So many guards spent their days circling around you instead of doing their duties—something was bound to go wrong eventually. If you hadn't worn such revealing clothes back then, there wouldn't have been so many troubles!"

"Haha..." Celia chuckled smugly. "Isn't that just proof of my overwhelming charm? Or are you jealous of me?"

"Absurd. Would I be jealous of someone who sells themselves like that?" Claudius's forehead vein throbbed faintly.

"You're just stubborn," Celia said, as if she saw right through her, then continued. "Now that I've left, no one is disturbing the Palace Guard's discipline anymore. So why did you end up leaving? Did something happen after I departed?"

"..." Claudius parted her lips slightly, her expression flickering through several changes, clearly reluctant to voice the secret in her heart. She swallowed. "Nothing much. The Palace Guard's duties were too heavy, and I didn't enjoy it, so I specifically resigned and chose to live in seclusion on the Great Snow Mountain..."

"Is that so?" Celia frowned, half-believing. She had never seen Claudius dislike busy work—on the contrary, she seemed to thrive on it.

"And what about you?" Claudius turned to look at Celia curiously. "Did you become an adventurer after leaving the Palace Guard?"

"I suppose so. I wandered around for six years, and only took up adventuring because I had nothing better to do. It's relaxed, pays well—why not?" Celia stretched lazily.

"You still haven't a single aspiration in life," Claudius shook her head, then changed the subject. "But in these past twenty-odd years, the adventurer world has developed rapidly. They used to be little more than a ragtag band of mercenaries—hardly any competent ones among them. After watching quite a few matches, I've noticed quite a number of remarkably skilled adventurers have emerged."

"Of course," Celia curled her lip in smug satisfaction. "The adventurer ranks have expanded fivefold compared to twenty years ago. Their quality and scale are incomparable to mercenaries. Still, only a handful of Purple-Gold adventurers can truly represent the pinnacle of strength."

"As for this adventurer tournament... who do you think will take the championship?" Claudius couldn't resist asking again.

"Don't bother hoping—your student certainly won't win. This time, I believe the champion will undoubtedly be a man," Celia said mysteriously.

"Oh?" Claudius sounded unconvinced. "Who?"

"You'll find out tomorrow..." Celia wore an enigmatic smile. Having watched the competition unfold this whole time, she already had her answer firmly in mind—

That man who had single-handedly entered the deadly domain of the Mysterious Sea and survived—was undoubtedly the most capable contender of all!

That night, Claudius returned to her room to find Alice was already waiting there.

Alice had been restless these past few days, as if a thorn was lodged in her heart, since her teacher had forced her back to university.

With the adventurer tournament drawing to a close, if she didn't protest soon, she feared she'd lose her chance entirely.

Unable to hold back any longer, Alice had come to Claudius's room tonight to make her stance clear.

Regardless of the outcome, once the tournament ended, Alice would not follow Claudius back to the Great Snow Mountain.

"It's so late—why aren't you resting? Aren't you competing tomorrow?" Claudius asked in surprise.

"I..."

Alice was somewhat nervous, but she lifted her head and said, "Teacher, even after the tournament ends, I won't be going back to the Great Snow Mountain with you."

Hearing this, Claudius's expression darkened immediately, and she spoke sharply. "Why do you insist on staying by that man's side? Have you been blinded by love?"

"No." Alice furrowed her brow and replied seriously. "This is my own choice. I'm not blinded—I want to be with him."

Claudius took a deep breath, unable to fathom what kind of bewitching potion Merlin had fed her student to make them so resolute.

"I'm not a child anymore. I hope you'll grant me some freedom," Alice said, lowering her head, her voice trembling slightly. "I will never forget your kindness to me—raising me, teaching me magic and swordsmanship. But I will not compromise on this, no matter what."

"What is there about that sort of person worth clinging to? The best choice is to return with me to the Great Snow Mountain. How long have you been out in the world? Do you really think you've established yourself?" Anger edging into Claudius's words.

"I won't go back with you. That is my bottom line." Alice lifted her head, her gaze turning resolute. "If you force me to return, I will resist to the end."

"..." Claudius was rendered speechless by anger, with an unsettling feeling that the cabbage she'd nurtured for over twenty years had finally been snatched by a pig—

*I'm so angry. Can that man even protect you properly? Just come back to the Great Snow Mountain with me—that's the only way you'll be safe...*

Morning arrived. Crimson sunlight crested the horizon, its radiance illuminating the entire Amiunius Arena.

Boom, boom, boom—several cannon salutes echoed, and the crowd erupted into deafening cheers. All the invited VIP guests had arrived, aside from Queen Elizabeth.

The competition had reached its boiling point, moments away from deciding the final four!

title: Chapter 38 — The Greatest Enemy (Continued)
content:
Chapter 38 — The Greatest Enemy (Continued)

Volume 27 · Chapter 38

The quarterfinals were completely different from before. The adventurers who made it to this round almost all possessed genuine, verifiable strength.

So the attention and importance they commanded were incomparable. Weighty guests who had not shown up before now sat comfortably in the guest seating area, ready to watch the battle for the final eight!

Rothschild and the Elf King sat side by side, smiling broadly and saying something repeatedly. It seemed he wanted very much to expand his family's business across the United Kingdom.

However, the Elf King's attitude appeared rather lukewarm. He was not particularly impressed by this billionaire. He had only come for Merlin and wanted to see Merlin's "performance."

Margaret did not sit properly in the guest seating area. She stood up, constantly looking around in all directions, her attention entirely fixed on Merlin. The thought of being able to kiss Merlin meant she hadn't slept at all the previous night.

Blaze wore a mournful expression. Because Margaret had acted on her own authority, he felt he would face questioning when they returned. He deeply regretted having followed Margaret here.

The only one different was the young State Preceptor Alfonso on stage. He sat alone in his chair with his eyes closed, as if cut off from the world. Nothing around him concerned him at all.

Old Man Dawson came to the presiding platform and loudly announced, "The tournament is drawing increasingly close to its end. The battles are becoming ever more intense. I hope the competitors who have advanced to the final eight will give it their all and show the world their brilliance. I declare... the competition begins!!!"

Alice slowly rose and handed Chris into Merlin's care. "I'm going now."

"Oh, be careful." Merlin looked up. He had spent the whole night carving a wooden sword prototype from a wooden stick, and he was still working on it.

"Go for it, Mom! Chris will cheer for Mom, just like Dad does!" Little Chris tilted her small head, her expression full of earnestness. The ahoge on her head swayed back and forth like a glow stick.

"Mhm!" Alice nodded, then turned and walked toward the ring.

Chris looked down at Merlin and asked curiously, "Dad, what are you doing?"

"I'm making a wooden sword," Merlin said with a smile. The small knife continuously scraped across the wooden stick, flakes of wood falling to the ground layer by layer.

"Why do you need to make a wooden sword?" Chris bit her finger, puzzled in her heart.

"Because...!" Merlin lifted Chris up and placed her on his lap. "Because Dad needs to let certain people know that they are not worthy of me going all out."

"Wah~" Chris's eyes filled with little stars. She thought Dad was about to make some big news. "Chris wants a wooden sword too!"

"Huh? Sure. I'll make you an even more beautiful one when we get back." Merlin patted his daughter's small head.

Alice stepped onto the ring and looked at her opponent this time: Aelia, the London Guild's ace, who also possessed Dragon King power.

When the audience saw two competitors who had been unstoppable from the very beginning, they could not determine between themselves who was stronger.

"I think Alice might be a bit more powerful. I heard she shattered a celestial body. That kind of strength... probably only a Gold-tier adventurer can have."

"Not necessarily. Although Aelia is not very famous, she is a student of Grandmaster Gregory the Platinum-tier adventurer. She probably has terrifying power she has not yet revealed."

"The first competitor is still a disciple of the old witch Circe, didn't she lose? I'll bet on Rexham's Alice instead."

On the presiding platform, a few arbiters started egging each other on, hoping Old Man Dawson would offer a prediction to demonstrate the prowess of the legendary "cursed milk" seer.

Chubby Arber, "President, take a guess. Who will win?"

Skinny Arber, "Exactly. Once the President speaks, we'll know~"

Old Man Dawson rolled his eyes. Teased like this, he felt somewhat embarrassed, so he began to think...

Since "cursed milk" always meant whoever he predicted would lose, couldn't he just reverse it this time?

Alice was well-known and powerful enough, but Aelia was a newcomer. Although she was Gregory's disciple, I don't know much about her.

After careful thought, Old Man Dawson decided to try a reverse operation, attempting to shake off his "cursed milk" label.

"Aelia will win!"

With the quarterfinals, old Tyler and the father-and-son Karl were clearly unable to help much. They could only pin their hopes on Merlin and Alice.

So the father and son took seats in the audience area. Rosetti and da Vinci had also come, appearing to have specifically stopped by after finishing their own affairs.

"Our opponent is Gregory's student. Do you know anything about her background, old man?" Karl asked anxiously.

"Yesterday I spoke with Gregory privately. The old fellow finally stopped hiding and revealed something useful." Old Tyler paused, then spoke gravely. "That girl named Aelia was personally raised by Gregory. She swallowed the Earth Sacred Dragon's treasure, something called an inheritance crystal? She possesses Dragon King power like Alice's. Her strength is terrifying, and she hasn't yet revealed her true power."

"Huh? Isn't that very similar to Alice?" Karl furrowed his brow and muttered to himself. "Frost Sacred Dragon versus Earth Sacred Dragon? It's hard to tell who is stronger. I feel their pressure is quite close. But the other side is just a child, so Alice has a higher chance of winning, right?"

"Don't judge by appearance. She is actually in her thirties, older than Alice." Old Tyler sensed a threat and lowered his voice. "If you let your guard down because she looks like a child, you'll suffer greatly."

"I see..." Karl felt a trace of pressure and began to doubt whether Alice could win.

"The most terrifying thing is the black dragon blood..." Old Tyler suddenly muttered.

"What is black dragon blood?" Karl was completely baffled and had never heard of it.

"Last night Gregory told me about the legend of the Dragon Warrior. People who obtain Dragon King power through an inheritance crystal have existed since the Age of the Gods. They need black dragon blood to complete their final transformation." Old Tyler lowered his head, deep in thought. "This adventurer Aelia has obtained black dragon blood and completed her final transformation to become a Dragon Warrior from the Age of the Gods. More precisely, it is man-made black dragon blood crafted by Gregory, which can approach a true legendary item. I'm afraid Alice will face a formidable enemy this time!"

Gregory had always excelled at ancient magic from bygone peoples and was very knowledgeable about information from the Age of the Gods. The inheritance crystal, the Dragon Warrior, Nidhogg's blood — he knew them all.

Even Master Craudys, the Twisted Thorn Knight Support Master, felt inferior to him and was willing to call Gregory a "Master." For Gregory to produce man-made black dragon blood was not impossible at all!

A long time ago, after Gregory luckily obtained the Earth Sacred Dragon's inheritance crystal, he dreamed of creating a Dragon Warrior from the Age of the Gods. Now that dream had finally come true.
