The drawing slash friction against the air produced a metallic trembling sound, like a ferocious beast roaring, shaking space to the verge of tearing!

The ferocious onslaught of Otherworldly King fists was instantly shattered to pieces, green blood spraying into the sky!

The residual might of the draw didn't stop — arena walls collapsed, the earth cracked, leaving a mess as if trampled by a wild beast...

Fortunately, most of the audience had already been scared off, otherwise Merlin's attack would have caused collateral damage.

It seems compared to the vampires with their powerful regeneration, the Otherworldly King falls just short — unable to pull off regeneration from a sliver of health.

But this is merely one of the Otherworldly King's arms, yet it forced Merlin to get serious?

If the overlord of Watford descended in his true body, just how terrifying would his strength be?

Merlin returned Banri Garan to its sheath, thinking this monster was far stronger than Crono — is it really just a summoned creature?

The entire venue fell silent, everyone staring at Merlin with incredulous gazes, their hearts unable to calm for a long time.

Whether they accepted it or not, once Merlin got serious, the massive power gap drove them to despair and submission...

Few among those present dared guarantee they could have withstood the Otherworldly King's attack just now.

Yet Merlin not only faced it head-on, he even pulled off a counter-kill?!

"Tch!" Merlin stood up, stowing Banri Garan, "Thought it was some unkillable existence? Turns out it's nothing special!"

The arbitration committee members on the dais stared at each other in dismay, some even doubting their own eyes—

Fat committee member: "We've lost! Every single one who could beat Lexington lost to Merlin?"

Tall committee member: "Even Crono lost, and Crono possessed the strength of a Violet-Gold Adventurer..."

Short committee member: "What do we do now? Are we really going to award the tournament's first-place adventurer title to him?"

Thin committee member: "Chairman, how should this be handled? This Merlin... is obviously more than qualified to serve as a Violet-Gold Adventurer..."

Old Mr. Dawson's expression hesitated, not answering quickly, feeling the situation was tricky, but he acknowledged Merlin was probably the best candidate for the new Violet-Gold Adventurer!

Big mouth, small belly.

".......A bit too strong, isn't he? The Adventurer Tournament is for playing around, right?" Vice President Wayland's face turned iron-green.

"From today onward, I fear the Lexington Adventurers Guild will become a paramount existence because of this man." Gregory assessed calmly.

Merlin glanced around, coldly laughing as he loudly challenged everyone, "Lexington's 'lie-flat-and-win king'? Are you talking about me?"

The adventurers present and the very few remaining audience members all fell silent, playing dumb, as if they'd forgotten how they'd disparaged Merlin before.

Merlin alone had fought through six of the tournament's eight finalists — no exaggeration, this was equivalent to single-handedly sweeping away all participating adventurers!

Seeing this scene, who still had the guts to belittle Merlin? Lexington's "lie-flat-and-win king"? Clearly he's Lexington's massive powerhouse!

"Lord Merlin! Ahhh! Lord Merlin!!!" Margaret cheered nonstop in the guest seats like a fangirl; nobody else had reacted much, but she was already climaxing?

Blaze's expression grew complex, thinking: Mr. Merlin, who had almost no pressure radiating from him, is actually this strong?!

Seems I misunderstood Her Highness's intention — recruiting a powerhouse like this is precisely what best serves the royal family's interests, isn't it?

As expected of the Princess, her vision sees further than mine. For the royal family's benefit, she'd seduce a married... no, not shameful at all~

Blaze stopped yapping, deciding to return and report to the old king — this Merlin is a rare talent, one man equal to a million soldiers!

The Elven King remained calm and collected, having long anticipated the result — with no one on the field comparable to his brother Ashdor, how could anyone contend with a Demon Lord-level opponent?

Though the final summoner was indeed stunning, his skills seemed lacking — he could only summon a single arm, unable to unleash true power.

"With Mr. Merlin standing on Your Majesty's side, surely leaders with ill intentions in the alliance wouldn't dare act rashly?" Sylph said happily.

"Indeed, that was my purpose in coming here." The Elven King smiled. Though he couldn't bring Chris back, gaining Merlin's support counted as a bountiful harvest!

Rothschild's aged frame stood at the front, gaze locked on Merlin, his heart deeply shaken.

Though he was neither warrior nor mage, he could still tell — if it were his guard McCready, he absolutely couldn't have withstood Crono's summoned creature just now!

No wonder this Black Iron adventurer earned so much royal favor, didn't even put this old man in his eyes — turns out he possesses such terrifying strength...

Rothschild's look toward Merlin changed, gaining several degrees of awe, even starting to calculate how much money it would take to hire an adventurer like Merlin?

Alfonso wasn't very interested in Merlin, looking away — but his eyes suddenly caught a familiar figure, making his whole body go extremely tense—

It's her?! Twenty-odd years ago... the knight by Josephine's side?!

Claudia watched Merlin, her opinion of him changing at this moment — she had to face the man Alice had chosen squarely.

He... he's actually this strong?!

His usual slack demeanor completely hid it!

Alice's judgment isn't so bad after all — she actually found gold dust in the sand!

With him guarding her side, perhaps Alice would be safer — all my worries were unnecessary...

Even though Claudia acknowledged Merlin, she still felt very uncomfortable inside. After all, he was a child she'd raised from little, and his sudden departure was hard to bear.

But seeing Merlin possess strength that nearly swept all adventurers, letting Alice stay by his side might not be a bad thing?

Claudia sighed, suddenly feeling a scorching gaze fixed on her. She looked up to discover Alfonso's cold, sinister eyes.

Alfonso!

Why is he here?!

z(°O°l)

title: Chapter 48 — The Disruptor (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 48 — The Disruptor (Extra Chapter)

Volume 27 · Chapter 48

Claudia, in her panic, lowered her head to hide her appearance and hurriedly left the arena.

She recalled the night twenty years ago, when Princess Josephine's throat was pierced and she fell into a pool of blood.

Even as the corpse grew cold, she still tightly protected the sleeping daughter...

Claudia secretly regretted leaving the Great Snow Mountain; she should have stayed on the peak forever, cut off from the outside world.

Only then could she sever ties with the past and let all grievances dissipate.

Unfortunately, Claudia couldn't resist her longing for Alice, still couldn't help herself, and met the enemy that frightened her.

Alfonso showed a deep, secretive smile, thinking: twenty years had passed, he thought she and the little princess were dead, but today's harvest was so great, really didn't come for nothing!

The entire arena was in a mess, with few spectators left in the stands; probably no one expected it to end up like this?

"...So Merlin beat all the adventurers?" Mr. Carl sweat dropped from his forehead, never having seen an adventurer go this wild in the tournament.

"Not sure, depends on how the Arbitration Committee judges..." Old Taylor said awkwardly, thought Merlin would play by the rules, but the result was too shocking.

Rosetti felt like an idiot; Merlin and Hobbs drinking and bragging was still fresh in her mind, how did he suddenly become such a powerful big shot?

Originally everyone misunderstood Merlin; if someone with such strength lives off a sugar daddy, then are there any people in this world who don't?

No wonder Alice's progress was so fast; turns out she already hugged the big shot's thigh...

Now Rosetti's mind was full of: does the big shot's thigh still need accessories? Remember to save me a spot!

Rosetti looked at Taylor father and son beside her, seeing they weren't surprised, couldn't help asking.

"You... already knew about Merlin...?"

Mr. Carl nodded, "Yeah, knew long ago."

Old Taylor stroked his beard, "This... you know why I chose Merlin to compete, right?"

"Knew all along, why didn't you say it earlier? Made us think Merlin was just some guy who idles around every day..." Rosetti said with some dissatisfaction.

"Saying it out only works if you believe it," Mr. Carl gave a slight bitter smile, no magic or combat power yet so strong, such abnormal things even if said, few would believe, only seeing is believing!

"...Indeed..." Rosetti's expression became awkward, thinking if not for seeing it with her own eyes, she really couldn't believe it, a person who gambles on horses and borrows money for booze daily, who was actually a peerless powerhouse!

Da Vinci secretly glanced sideways, suddenly noticing Flamel had left without knowing when?

She "sprang" up, alertly looking around, searching for Flamel's traces.

"Da Vinci? Did you see? Merlin actually..."

"Later!"

Rosetti wanted to share her feelings about this person with Da Vinci, but who knew she was extremely nervous now, hurriedly leaving the stands toward the arena ruins.

Da Vinci somewhat understood Flamel; this seemingly polite guy actually had evil intentions, to complete his goal would do anything!

Rosetti looked at Da Vinci leaving the stands in surprise, muttered, "What's wrong with her? Did something happen?"

Chris saw Merlin display divine might, happy beyond words, jumped from Alice's arms, came to the arena ruins, "Dad! Dad! I also want to learn that move you used..."

"Ha ha~" Merlin turned around, looking at his beloved daughter, gave a thumbs up boasting, "How about it? Dad's awesome right!"

"Super awesome~" Chris responded with two thumbs up, like giving her dad a like?

But Alice's expression turned slightly worried, thinking what to do? This Merlin guy will win the championship right? After that isn't he going to have to deal with Margareta...

Alice shook her head vigorously, disagreed absolutely, at that time must do a "child warning" or something, she's Chris's mom, no one else can take advantage!

Da Vinci suddenly stumbled running from the stands, shouting loudly, "Mr. Merlin! Leave quickly!"

"Huh?" Merlin looked up, confused, looking at Da Vinci, didn't know what happened?

Suddenly, a wave of heat came from under the arena ruins—

Merlin sensed something wrong, smelled danger, pupils constricted, expression retreated rapidly!

With a thunderous explosion, flames shot into the arena sky, scaring the arbitration committee members off their chairs!

"Chris!"

Alice's face changed, rushed to Chris's side, hugged daughter tightly in arms, shocked watching the rolling flames and heat waves in the sky.

Chris hugged her head crouching in mom's arms, obviously scared stiff, fortunately hadn't gotten on the arena just now, otherwise big trouble!

Almost no one knew what happened? Could it be someone else unconvinced, standing on the arena?

Flames dispersed, Flamel appeared in mid-air, holding a golden shining crystal in hand, extremely similar to Alice's fused ice crystal.

This was all the magic and combat power collected from start to now, fused together by alchemy into a crystallization of pure power.

Although Flamel's plan was interfered by Merlin, he still barely completed the task, originally wanted to collect more, but the broadcast crystal shattered, conditions didn't allow.

"Glad I completed the task, otherwise I wouldn't know how to report to the President..." Flamel smiled, putting away the crystallized power, looking down at all astonished adventurers.

Old Mr. Dawson got up from the ground, looked up, immediately startled, "Flamel!? A member of the dark guild Phoenix, how did you appear here!?"

In the arena, some recognized Flamel; his wanted poster had long been posted on the commission boards of every guild worldwide.

Inhumane alchemy experiments, teasing nobles of various countries, creating chimeras by combining humans and beasts, various evils long spread to every corner.

Alice looked at Flamel in mid-air with hostility, looked down at shivering Chris, anger in her heart even greater.

"Who are you?" Merlin asked calmly, "Also unconvinced? Come to challenge me?"

"Don't misunderstand." Flamel crossed his arms, facing Merlin without fear, even smirked and teased—

"I'm not interested in brutes.

"Even if I win

"Wouldn't have any sense of achievement."

title: Chapter 49 — No Way Out
content:
Chapter 49 — No Way Out

Volume 27 · Chapter 49

Merlin looked surprised and said calmly, "You're very confident."

"I watched your match. Your strength is indeed good, but in my eyes, it's not much." Flamel said with a half-smile. He wasn't afraid of powerful enemies anyway.

"Who is this guy?" Alice asked, holding a frightened Chris, her tone full of hostility.

At that moment, Mr. Dawson suddenly stepped forward and loudly announced the quest to all the adventurers present--

"This person is a cadre of the Dark Guild Phoenix, Flamel!"

"As inheritors of adventurers, we absolutely cannot tolerate someone who destroys the adventurer spirit!"

"Everyone, attack together! Let's capture this villain from the Dark Guild and bring him to justice!!"

"Looks like... I don't need to introduce myself anymore." Flamel gave a self-deprecating smile, thinking that since the mission was already complete, there was no need for him to linger.

Suddenly, a firebird appeared in front of Flamel, spinning continuously to form a portal leading to an unknown direction.

This was the same scene as when the former Beast King left. It seemed that Phoenix members all possessed the ability to teleport at any time.

Seeing Flamel, who had disrupted the Adventurer Competition, trying to escape, the adventurers could no longer sit still and charged forward all at once!

"So you come and go as you please? You Dark Guild people are too arrogant!!"

"Leave your life behind! To dare appear openly before us adventurers, you must have already accepted your death!"

"Flamel? You're the famous alchemist in the Dark Guild? Let me see what you've got!"

A large group of adventurers, responding to Chairman Dawson's call, united to capture Flamel directly.

Many of them were Mithril-rank adventurers, and at the very least Gold-rank, each possessing considerable strength.

Moreover, Flamel's head was worth a lot of money. If they could defeat this villain, it would be a brilliant turnaround for all the adventurers!

The adventurers charged up to Flamel, their diverse martial arts and magic unleashing all at once toward the Dark Guild cadre!

A series of sneers appeared on Flamel's face. He didn't take this group of small fry seriously at all and merely sneered, "You think you can stop me? That's the funniest joke I've ever heard!"

Before the words had even finished echoing, a dark shadow appeared out of nowhere, like a nimble black serpent, constantly weaving through the charging adventurers.

Then came a barrage of screams. Wherever the black serpent passed, adventurers were sliced cleanly in half, blood mist filling the air...

The charging adventurers were nearly wiped out by the black serpent. Those behind hesitated in fear, and no one dared to clash with Flamel.

The nimble black serpent climbed over Flamel's body, its entire surface covered with crimson eyes, blinking one after another, looking rather eerie. It continuously flicked its bright red tongue, as if taunting the death-defying adventurers.

This was Flamel's alchemical beast, fused with the mysterious Philosopher's Stone, possessing extraordinary power. Even a Saint-tier expert could easily lose their life before it!

"An alchemical beast!?" Da Vinci's eyes widened. She thought that indeed Flamel and her teacher had taken the same path, creating ferocious monsters for him to command. Looking at this alchemical beast's extraordinary strength, who knew what method Flamel used to raise it?

"You bunch of death-defying ants, why bother?" Flamel delayed entering the portal, instead sadistically playing with the adventurers present.

"You're clearly surrounded by us and yet you still dare to talk big? ! Let me experience your techniques!"

Karl's entire body was wrapped in lightning fighting aura, and at a speed too fast for the naked eye to track, he shot toward Flamel, catching the alchemical beast off guard as well.

The Shocking Thunder Fist was renowned for its ferocity. Its ultra-fast speed was its advantage, and凭借 this, it could catch most opponents off guard!

"Hmm?! " A trace of panic flashed through Flamel's eyes. He never expected someone could get this close to him!

"Hiss! " Karl pressed his fingers together into a blade shape and unleashed Shocking Thunder Iai Slash, ruthlessly striking toward Flamel's chest.

Blood splattered in all directions. Flamel suffered severe injuries, his chest torn open, letting out a piercing scream, his facial features twisted.

But just when everyone thought this guy was dead, the pseudo-Philosopher's Stone on Flamel's chest lit up with an eerie red glow, too blinding to look at directly!

When the red glow faded, Karl's body fell limply. The wound that should have appeared on Flamel strangely manifested on Karl's chest instead.

"Plop." Karl, heavily injured, crashed to the ground. Blood streamed from his torn chest, and the look in his eyes toward Flamel was filled with utter disbelief!

"The Philosopher's Stone!? " Da Vinci, who had always been calm, couldn't help but gasp! Although she could sense that this Philosopher's Stone was different from the legends, the fact that it could twist reality was already very close to the truly legendary Philosopher's Stone recorded in ancient texts! She could never have imagined that this legendary divine artifact had truly been created by Flamel! She had only thought Flamel had found the correct research direction for the Philosopher's Stone!

"Karl!" Old Taylor rushed over anxiously, continuously checking his son's injuries. He had lived more than half his life, yet he still couldn't understand why the wound that should have appeared on Flamel inexplicably appeared on Karl instead!

"Da Vinci, are you alright?" Rosetti also hurried over.

"I... I'm fine..." Da Vinci lowered her head, an overwhelming sense of inferiority rising within her. She and Flamel came from the same teacher, yet they were as far apart as heaven and earth. Their accomplishments in alchemy were incomparable!

"So this is Flamel? Your classmate back then?" Rosetti raised her head, repeatedly sizing up Flamel.

"That's right." Da Vinci frowned and whispered, "I knew he wasn't a good person, but I never expected him to join the Dark Guild."

Flamel looked at the ground covered with heavily injured adventurers, curled his lips into a teasing smile, "You really brought this on yourselves. I hope you'll have some self-awareness in the future. Goodbye, foolish adventurers."

After saying that, Flamel turned and left, slowly walking toward the portal. Before departing, he didn't forget to cast a deep look at Da Vinci, as a farewell to an old acquaintance.

On the chairman's podium, the arbitration committee members were each like ants on a hot pan, anxious and flustered--

The fat committee member: "What should we do? Are we really just going to let this Dark Guild cadre leave!?"

The thin committee member: "Shame! This is the shame of our Adventurer Association!"

The tall committee member: "If this gets out, we'll lose all face."

The short committee member: "Right! If we can't even handle a Dark Guild, how can employers still trust us adventurers?"

Just when everyone was helpless against Flamel, Merlin suddenly leaped into the air, closing the distance to the enemy at a speed even faster than Karl's!

Flamel's toe had already stepped into the portal, completely caught off guard that someone would still block him at this moment. He saw Merlin's face, cold as ice, "Huh? !"

Merlin suddenly pressed his hand against Flamel's face, pinning his entire body from the sky down onto the ground. With a loud "boom," a wave of wind and sand erupted.

"Want to leave?"

"Did you ask me first?"

title: Chapter 50 — Bomb Feast (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 50 — Bomb Feast (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 27 · Chapter 50

Flamel's eyes widened in shock, never having expected such a situation to arise.

Someone could actually evade all his senses and suppress him?

Flamel had to reassess Merlin. If he didn't rely on the Philosopher's Stone, he probably couldn't win.

Merlin pinned Flamel to the ground, leaving him unable to move. "Do you really think you can leave?"

Flamel gradually calmed down, then suddenly smiled and pulled a black metallic orb from his robes. "That's right, I do think so."

Merlin's attention was drawn to the metallic orb in Flamel's hand. Suddenly, many spikes popped out from the sphere, and it lit up with a red glow as a dangerous power rapidly expanded.

At the critical moment, Merlin quickly retreated. With a thunderous boom, a massive explosion sent a towering wave of heat surging upward, and Flamel was engulfed in raging flames.

The shockwave swept across the entire arena, and the wild wind it kicked up made it hard for anyone to keep their eyes open. Da Vinci was secretly alarmed—

What a terrifying alchemical bomb. If it detonated at close range, even a Saint-tier powerhouse's body probably couldn't withstand it...

Merlin steadied himself and looked at the explosion before him, frowning slightly. "Is he a madman?"

Flamel detonating the bomb at such close range—wouldn't that kill even himself?

If he weren't mentally unhinged, who would do something so dangerous!

Yet the truth was just that bizarre. After the flames of the explosion dispersed, Flamel stood perfectly fine at the center of the blast, not even his clothes disheveled.

Such an uncanny sight made almost everyone believe Flamel had a body of steel. Only Da Vinci knew in his heart that surviving the explosion unscathed meant he had likely used the power of the Philosopher's Stone again.

Flamel wore a smile on his face, slowly raising his head amid the smoke. "I admit, among all these adventurers, you've got some real skill."

Merlin frowned and didn't respond. He gradually noticed too—the source of all the strangeness was the red object on Flamel's neck.

"But I advise you not to provoke me. Otherwise it's easy for both sides to suffer heavy losses, and that doesn't serve your interests or mine, does it?" Flamel said in a low voice, trying to make Merlin avoid a fight to the death with him.

"Do you think I believe your nonsense?" Merlin suddenly assumed a sword-drawing stance, his gaze turning sharp, and his figure vanished from where he stood!

"You really want to die together with me?!!" Flamel became frenzied, clutching the slightly cool Philosopher's Stone on his neck for dear life, as if he had some trump card that could drag Merlin down to hell with him?

The piercing wind stopped. Merlin stood right before Flamel's eyes, the blade of Banri Garan resting on his forehead, less than three centimeters away!

If Flamel had been just a bit slower, his body would have been split in two by Merlin, and the final outcome would have become unpredictable.

The reason Merlin stopped wasn't because he believed Flamel's words, but because in that instant, he sensed a trace of danger.

The Philosopher's Stone on Flamel's neck kept flickering with an eerie light, which forced Merlin to calm down. If he had attacked recklessly just now, who the hell knew what would have happened afterward?

"That's more like it. We have no grudge against each other, so why fight to the bloody end?" Flamel was drenched in sweat, tightly gripping the Philosopher's Stone on his neck—this was the thing that kept him alive. "What you really should do is worry about everyone else's safety, not tangle with me here!"

"What do you mean?" Merlin narrowed his eyes, his tone threatening.

Flamel laughed, speaking in a low voice. "You didn't think I left nothing behind, did you? Before you all came to the arena, I had already prepared gifts for all of you..."

As soon as the words left his mouth, the rubble of the arena platform began to shake. The alchemical furnace that had originally been beneath the platform suddenly burst out, flying into the sky!

Everyone stared at the alchemical furnace, a vague sense of foreboding rising in their hearts...

Before everyone's eyes, the alchemical furnace began to break apart into metallic spheres, identical to the alchemical bomb Flamel had just detonated, and in great numbers—they began raining down in dense clusters.

"Alchemical bombs!" Da Vinci cried out in alarm, recalling the power from just now. Did Flamel intend to blast the entire arena into the sky!?

"What do we do!? There are too many of them!" Rossetti's voice was filled with despair. There was clearly no time to stop them now!

Merlin watched the dense swarm of alchemical bombs in the sky, spikes popping out and red lights flaring, as if they could detonate at any moment and kill nearly everyone present!

"There are three thousand six hundred and seventy-nine alchemical bombs in total. Even if all you adventurers present worked together to resist, you couldn't stop this many. The Aminius Arena will be blasted hundreds of feet into the air!" Flamel's expression turned fanatical as he spoke rapidly. "By then, this centuries-old monument will cease to exist, leaving only ruins! And only Saint-tier powerhouses will barely survive—everyone else will die!!!"

"You bastard..." Merlin's face darkened. He hadn't expected Flamel to take everyone hostage!

"Think about it. How many Saint-tier powerhouses are present? Most are ordinary people. So many ordinary spectators will die in this disaster." Flamel's smile turned wicked. "It's all because of you! You forced me to do this! Everyone will be buried with me!"

"You want to die..." Merlin suddenly gripped Banri Garan tightly, barely able to restrain his killing intent.

Flamel felt a jolt of fear in his heart. He suddenly realized the man before him didn't care about the lives of others, so he could only change tack. "At a time like this, you're still clinging to me!? Think about your child, not even three years old yet, right? What a pity if they died in this disaster! There's still time! I'm afraid you're the only one here who can save them!"

Merlin's killing intent didn't diminish. He truly had no heroic tendencies, but protecting children struck right at his weak spot.

"What are you hesitating for!? Do you want to fight me to the death and let everyone perish here? Or hurry and save your wife and child?" Flamel was gambling that Merlin was definitely not iron-hearted. As long as he had an opening, he could retreat safely. "Choose! You don't have much time!"

Watching the three thousand-plus alchemical bombs about to fall from the sky, Merlin suddenly withdrew his hand blade. At a time like this, he truly couldn't fight Flamel to the bitter end.

Flamel had won his gamble. He gasped for breath heavily, his legs having gone weak from fright just now—he'd really thought he would be cut down right there.

A portal suddenly lit up behind him. Flamel clutched the Philosopher's Stone tightly and stepped inside.

Before leaving, Flamel turned back and revealed a meaningful smile, looking at those panic-stricken adventurers—

"Go die, all of you, foolish adventurers..."

"Three thousand six hundred and seventy-nine alchemical bombs, covering the entire Aminius Arena. How could this fireworks feast possibly be stopped?"

"That blond man will probably only be able to protect his own wife and child."

"As for the others—"

"Just enjoy the might of alchemical weaponry before you die~"

title: Chapter 51 — God-Man
content:
Chapter 51 — God-Man

Volume 27 · Chapter 51

The alchemy bombs in the sky slowly fell, flashing red light connecting into a sheet, revealing a dangerous aura!

Thousands of bombs are about to explode, the entire Aminius arena will become ruins.

Those present include capable adventurers, and many civilians who failed to escape the arena in time; they may be reduced to bones in the first moment of the explosion!

Only Saint-tier powerhouses might survive, relying on their strong physiques, perhaps they could endure the blast.

Everyone at this moment is in chaos, survival instinct driving them to rush frantically to escape the arena--

Short committee member: "Chairman! Run quickly! If we don't run now, it'll be too late!"

Fat committee member: "Yeah! We just saw the power of the bombs; this time it's not just one, but thousands!"

The other two committee members also agreed, this place is no longer safe; only by diving into the basement now might we barely escape.

"You all go..." Dawson the old chairman's expression turned grave, "As chairman, if even one person cannot leave, I will stay here until the very last moment! Being forced to this point by the dark guild's officials is a disgrace to our Adventurers' Guild!"

The four committee members stared at each other, the situation is urgent yet they are even more panicked than the civilians, indeed losing face of the Arbitration Committee!

Encouraged by Chairman Dawson's words, several committee members stood firmly beside him, wanting to show everyone that they fear nothing from the dark guild.

"Your Highness! Follow me quickly, I can still keep you safe!" Blaise said in panic.

"What's there to fear? With Lord Merlin here, nothing could happen!" Margaret said confidently.

"..." Blaise's head swelled a circle, feeling Margaret was like a fanatic follower of Merlin, "The situation isn't the same—those are thousands of bombs; even if Merlin is stronger, it's hard to stop them all!"

"Mom?" Chris curiously lifted her head, feeling something off around her.

"It's okay, don't be scared.

Alice pressed Chris's little head against her chest, not letting her see the dangerous situation at the moment.

Chris didn't know what had happened? She obediently closed her eyes and curled up in Alice's embrace.

Alice lifted her head, face as cold as frost, gazing at the bombs in the sky, mobilizing all her battle qi and magic power, preparing to give it her all, at least ensuring Chris's safety.

With a continuous "humming" vibration sound, thousands of alchemy bombs in the sky flashed with intense white light, making it hard to keep eyes open!

Merlin suddenly returned, pulling Alice directly into his arms and loudly said, "Lower your head! Alice!

"Ah!?" Alice felt a pang of panic, instinctively burying her head in Merlin's chest, her mind going blank.

Boom boom boom

The explosion began, a thunderous blast that plunged the chaotic arena into silence!

Blinding light followed by raging flames rolling down from the sky, threatening to devour the entire arena!

The massive shockwave hadn't even hit the ground before it shattered the earth.

This apocalyptic scene caused almost everyone to stop in their tracks, abandoning any will to survive, leaving only despair in their hearts.

At the same time, Merlin held Alice, his expression stern, raising his arms high, drawing upon the earth spirit power deep within his spirit!

The repulsive space activated, a huge repulsion field unfurled like an umbrella, swiftly covering the upper sky of the entire arena!

The repulsive space can block most things; the repulsion field Merlin created with his own strength is equivalent to a massive shield!

Covering the whole arena is already the limit of what Merlin can do, yet it can save everyone inside the arena!

The explosion triggered by thousands of alchemy bombs violently assaulted Merlin's repulsive space shield, letting everyone see the astonishing sight of flames raging high yet unable to breach the arena....

Merlin gritted his teeth, barely maintaining the repulsive space; the earth spirit's power is limited, far inferior to his own strength.

Leaning in Merlin's embrace, Alice's face inexplicably turned red? At such close proximity, she could hear Merlin's heartbeat.

No one knows what Alice was thinking in this critical moment, as if she had forgotten she was in such a dire situation?

"......How is this possible!?" Blaise stared wide-eyed, unable to imagine Merlin could deploy such a huge repulsive space! Is he a dual cultivator of martial arts and magic? Not only is his martial power heavenly, but his magic has reached terrifying levels!

"Not surprising, he's the man I favor; each time he brings me delight!" Margaret glanced at Blaise with a teasing look, saying, "You heard what I said? With Lord Merlin here, how could there be danger?"

The Elf King's face showed a hint of doubt, thinking Merlin couldn't use magic? Where did he learn such high-level repulsive space?

The arbitration committee members on the presidium, seeing Merlin turn the tide, had already begun joyfully waving their arms and legs—

Thin committee member: "Heavens! He can actually cast such a large-scale earth magic!?"

Short committee member: "We... we're saved!? It's practically like a dream!"

Tall committee member: "I never thought that, among adventurers, such an outstanding existence would appear from reminiscing about the past!"

Fat committee member: "This is a blessing for the Adventurers' Guild since its founding! Surely the founder would also feel relieved!"

...." Chairman Dawson, older than the other committee members, remained much calmer, saying nothing, instead sighing inwardly—

...He's a divine person!?

At the same moment in Rexelmu, compared to the chaos in Budapest, this small town remained as peaceful as ever.

The Rexelmu guild was packed; many adventurers temporarily halted their work, all to watch the final results of the tournament.

Yet so many people stared blankly at the magic screen filled with snowflakes, feeling bored, they really wanted to know how the tournament was going?

Not long ago, everyone saw Merlin alone challenging the three aces of the Cathovitz guild, when suddenly a black shadow struck, and the magic screen stayed stuck in snowflake status.

Everyone thought the live broadcast had malfunctioned and would be fixed soon, but even now no live feed from the arena has come through, so nobody knows what actually happened there

"How is it going? Merlin challenged the three aces of Cathovitz, I'm really curious!"

"Who knows? Maybe he was badly injured and withdrew; Merlin is indeed too overconfident."

"Yeah, that's the ace of the world's second guild; Merlin probably can't beat even one of them."

Lucia and others were equally curious, but the magic screen never showed live footage, making her anxious.

She glanced at Hobbes, who was calmly peeling an apple for little Mimi, and couldn't help but ask.

"Hobbes, why does Mr. Merlin challenge three people? Isn't he afraid of death?"

"Who knows~" Hobbes shrugged, smiling without speaking.

"Geez, how is it going? This is really making me curious..... Lucia furrowed her brow, feeling irritated and restless—

Mr. Merlin actually has the courage to challenge the Cathovitz aces?

I also don't know if he can win in the end....

But just now Mr. Merlin seemed to have repelled that guy named Noel, smashing the live broadcast crystal?

Being able to repel the Cathovitz guild's ace surely indicates he possesses considerable strength.

Grandfather and father both favor Mr. Merlin; could he truly be a low-key powerhouse!?

(w -_.)/?

title: Chapter 52 — Sudden Departure (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 52 — Sudden Departure (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 27 · Chapter 52

Crisis reported—although some viewers were injured in the chaos, the vast majority survived against all odds.

The Amunius Arena was soon surrounded by Budapest's garrison, who began investigating a series of incidents.

The Emperor of Austria-Hungary learned that a dark guild executive had secretly infiltrated here; his crown nearly fell off, feeling he had brushed shoulders with death.

Fortunately, Phoenix wasn't coming for him; otherwise, in this vast Budapest, how many could stand against Flamel?

The Emperor ordered the garrison and knights to investigate the matter thoroughly and give him a satisfactory answer.

The guards discovered secrets beneath the arena platform. After Flamel left, he left behind scattered alchemical apparatus—everything indicated that sabotaging the tournament had been premeditated.

As the person responsible for building the tournament arena, Countess Bartori became the suspect in the guards' investigation.

Building a temporary alchemy lab underground in the Amunius Arena—Flamel couldn't have hidden that from everyone.

The guards began suspecting that Lady Bartori had colluded with Flamel of the dark guild, and some secrets gradually came to light.

When Merlin and Alice returned to the inn, they found a letter left by Claudria in their room—

"My dear student Alice, I'm glad to see you can stand on your own, growing from a tearful child into a mature person.

"I've observed for a long time—you're right, Merlin is a good person. If you like him, you can be with him; I won't stop you."

"I hope you can live well, raise Chris properly, and let her grow up to be like you—a righteous person."

"I didn't come to disrupt your peaceful life; I just couldn't stop worrying about you after so long apart."

"But now it seems my worry was unnecessary—you can survive in this cruel world on your own."

"There's no need for me to stay any longer. By the time you read this letter, I'll already be on my way back to the Great Snow Mountain."

"Wish you happiness, Alice. As your teacher, one last piece of advice—"

"Never return to the Great Snow Mountain. Just live carefree from now on."

Seeing the letter left by her teacher Claudria, Alice frowned, feeling inexplicably sad.

Earlier she'd been wishing the teacher would leave quickly, but now she felt a little reluctant to let go.

Alice thought her teacher's last sentence telling her not to return to the Great Snow Mountain was just an angry remark—maybe she had really upset the teacher.

Although the letter acknowledged Merlin, it was probably after seeing his strength in the match that her perspective changed.

But leaving only a letter and rushing off without a word, Alice always felt her teacher was too angry to even say goodbye, so she returned to the Great Snow Mountain without meeting her.

"...Maybe that's a bit much..."

"What's wrong?" Merlin came over, seeing Alice's face looked terrible, thinking something had happened.

"...Planning...?" Alice put Claudria's letter away, not wanting Merlin to see it.

"Hiding what? Let me see?" Merlin asked curiously.

"It's a letter left by my teacher." Alice answered truthfully.

"A letter?" Merlin was surprised, wondering why leave a letter out of nowhere? -2

"My teacher has already left." Alice explained.

"Left?" Merlin secretly sighed with relief. Don't mention the pressure lately—it's been so long since he fought with Alice that he was unaccustomed to it. "Good riddance! Finally gone, your teacher should be gone, you should be happy! Why the long face? We don't have to act tired anymore, right? I was almost worn out recently."

"You!?" Alice stared at Merlin, then sighed, "I think I drove the teacher away. I feel a bit sorry for her."

"Earlier you couldn't wait to send her back to the Great Snow Mountain yourself. Now you're regretting it—what were you thinking?" Merlin was a bit impatient, secretly thinking Alice was a troublesome guy.

"...The situation is different!" Alice retorted huffily, looking at the letter in her hand. "When I get a chance, I'll go back to the Great Snow Mountain to see her and apologize to the teacher."

"When your teacher was here, why wouldn't she talk to her properly?" Merlin asked with a helpless tone.

"Well... she didn't talk to me properly either. I... Alice muttered angrily, then changed the subject: "How's Chris?"

"She's asleep. Should be scared." Merlin looked at Chris sleeping soundly on the big bed.

"I didn't expect this to happen. Didn't you kill that dark guild member back then?" Alice asked curiously.

"No. The red stone on that guy was too weird; I sensed a hint of danger. The situation was dangerous—I couldn't afford to gamble." Merlin answered calmly.

PSE2小治

Alice carefully recalled the situation, speaking thoughtfully: "Also... Da Vinci knows something? She seemed to recognize that person..."

Outside Budapest, Claudria had walked far.

It seemed Claudria wasn't joking; for some reason, she had to leave as soon as possible.

However, upon learning Claudria had left suddenly, Sercy followed silently behind her.

"Go back, Sercy, no need to see me off." Claudria stopped and turned back.

"So soon back to the Great Snow Mountain? Only a short while and you're returning—did you keep a lover up there?" Sercy smiled, saying with meaningful teasing.

"Don't joke around, I'm serious." Claudria grew serious.

Sercy was startled, asking suspiciously, "Did something happen? That's why you're in such a hurry? I don't like you, but if you ask, I can help~"

Claudria showed a look of wanting to speak but stopping, not wanting to drag Sercy in. She shook her head helplessly. "Nothing happened. I just find the outside boring; it's easier in the Great Snow Mountain."

"Is that so?" Sercy lowered her head, muttering, "It's rare to meet again, shouldn't we have a few more drinks..."

Claudria looked at Sercy and said in a low voice, "I do have something I need your help with."

"Oh?" Sercy instantly became excited, saying triumphantly, "You actually have something to ask me? Rare to see you so humble. Say it. For the sake of us working together before, I can agree."

Claudria wasn't angry at Sercy's triumph. It might be the last time they met before leaving. "When necessary, can you help my student Alice?"

"Alice...?" Sercy paused, then continued, "Isn't she the student you're proud of? She needs my help?"

"What I mean is, if someday she falls into crisis, I hope you won't stand by and do nothing." Claudria's expression was serious, her attitude very sincere.

Sercy had never seen such Claudria, so sincerely pleading. She had to become serious too. "Alright, I will."

"Goodbye, Sercy. I hope we can meet again. I don't like your personality, but I know you're a kind person."

"Ah? Hearing that from your mouth is a bit disgusting..."

Sercy watched Claudria's departing back, growing more puzzled. This was the first time her mortal enemy had said something nice.

After knowing each other so long, Sercy had never felt Claudria act so abnormally as today, leaving her unable to understand.

Claudria walked with her head down toward the Great Snow Mountain, her face darkening. She began thinking—

Alfonso's henchmen should have left too.

This black dragon priest won't let me go...

title: Chapter 53 — The Hunt
content:
Chapter 53 — The Hunt

Volume 27 · Chapter 53

Half a month later, at a southern port of the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

Claudia was about to board a ship back to the Holy Roman Empire, avoiding Alfonso's clutches.

However, because she had traveled through the night, Claudia was a bit fatigued, so she decided to rest for a moment in a certain tavern.

At this moment, it was deep in the night, and the tavern had very few patrons. Counting Claudia, there were only four people, one of whom was the tavern owner.

Claudia changed into a robe, pressing her hat down low, not wanting anyone to see her. She lowered her head and dozed off listlessly.

"Customer, your black coffee is ready." The tavern owner, a young woman with a friendly smile, placed the black coffee in front of Claudia.

"Thank you." Claudia responded lightly. She needed to stay awake to escape Alfonso's clutches, so she needed something to perk herself up.

"You look very tired. Would you like to go up to the restroom to rest?" The tavern owner asked with concern.

"No, I'll leave as soon as I finish my coffee." Claudia said without lifting her head.

"In such a hurry? Where is the customer going? Perhaps I can help." The tavern owner gave a friendly smile, looking worried about the traveler in front of her.

"Not needed, thank you for your kindness." Claudia said coldly.

SFA

Not a novel..........

The tavern owner's kindness was rejected, making her feel a bit awkward. She walked away obediently.

Claudia slightly relaxed when she saw no one around, massaged her glabella, and took a deep breath.

She felt [that she had already escaped very happily, and Alfonso's clutches should have been left behind by her....

Claudia picked up the black coffee, habitually sniffed it, and suddenly widened her eyes, staring at the coffee unwilling to drink it.

As someone who had close ties with the old witch Cessie, Claudia had often been exposed to various poisons in the past. She believed it was very hard to find someone who understood pharmacology better than Cessie.

Just from sniffing the black coffee, Claudia immediately noticed that the smell was a bit off. This coffee clearly had something added to it!

How could a normal tavern put drugs in a customer's drink?! Very likely, Alfonso's men had found her!

Thinking of this, Claudia felt as if she had fallen into an ice cave. A bone-chilling coldness penetrated deep into her marrow. She hadn't expected to escape so quickly, yet still hadn't fully shaken off Alfonso's shadow.

Claudia silently set down the black coffee, lifted her head, and surveyed everyone in the tavern. Her hand was already secretly gripping the sword hilt.

"Customer, what's wrong? Why aren't you drinking a sip? Is it because my coffee doesn't suit your taste?" The tavern owner's expression was anxious, unaware that she was actually a bloodthirsty assassin who swallows bones whole.

Claudia fell silent for a moment, lifted her head, and said coldly, "Did Alfonso have you wait here?"

The tavern owner's smile stiffened. She slowly walked out and said, "No wonder you are the court sword saint from back then. The poison we put is already very discreet. I didn't expect you to still notice."

As soon as the words fell, the two male customers standing in the tavern stood up, slowly drawing out two short blades with cold light from behind.

These three were here for Claudia. The true owner of the tavern had long since * * dropped dead, and they were disguised, staring at Claudia to deliver her to them.

"...." Claudia sighed, saying helplessly, "Still haunting me, aren't you? To hunt me, I have also exerted great effort."

"Less talk, obediently go with us to see Lord Alfonso, otherwise you won't think about leaving here!" The tavern owner's face was cold as she threatened.

The two male assassins behind her silently tightened their short knives, and the atmosphere became oppressive, as if a fight would break out at any moment!

"You guys, Alfonso's men, actually have the courage to threaten me?" Claudia lifted her eyelids, her tone carrying a hint of annoyance.

"We've heard Lord Alfonso talk about you. You were the most trusted knight beside Queen Josephine many years ago, the first swordsman of the Spanish Kingdom. On the night of the coup over twenty years ago, you fled the palace with Princess Diana in the middle of the night, killing countless people on the way. Even the strongest griffin knight team of the kingdom was wiped out in one night, and the blood dyed the city walls red..." The tavern owner said with deep meaning.

"Since you know, why dare use such a despicable method of poisoning against me?" Claudia's gaze revealed a hint of killing intent.

"People die for wealth, birds die for food. You should know this principle?" The tavern owner paused and added, "Lord Alfonso is not just the prime minister now. He possesses unparalleled power, controls everything in the kingdom, and even the little king is just his puppet. Why don't you join Lord Alfonso together? He will definitely reuse you, granting you endless honor and wealth~"

"Hahaha..." Claudia laughed coldly, saying firmly, "One day, I will put Alfonso's head on Queen Josephine's tombstone!"

"You are truly a foolish person." The tavern owner shook her head in pity, then her expression turned grotesque. "Say! Where is Princess Diana?! I want to offer her to the great black dragon priest, Lord Alfonso!"

"After I kill you, I can tell you..." Claudia laughed coldly, a chill radiating from her body.

"Seeking death!" The three assassins attacked simultaneously, their blades pressing against Claudia's throat!

This tavern located in the southern port, in the middle of the night, burst forth with brilliant white light....

As the sky was slightly bright, a group of people entered this remote tavern.

Three corpses lay on the ground, clearly the assassins lying in ambush here.

Claudia's whereabouts were unknown. Obviously, under the encirclement of the three, she killed them back and safely escaped.

Alfonso stood at the forefront, covering his mouth and nose with a handkerchief, apparently having some fastidiousness about cleanliness. Behind him stood a group of subordinates dressed as assassins, each exuding a cold breath, already accustomed to seeing dead people.

Alfonso continuously inspected the scene. Seeing that there was no chaos here, his heart immediately concluded -

The fight ended very quickly. The strength gap between the three and Claudia was too large; they didn't even have a chance to resist.

"Adult! All of them were throat-cut with a sword. The opponent's sword was very fast, looking very difficult to deal with." One of the assassins investigated the bodies and reported to Alfonso.

Alfonso watched the bodies emit a smell, frequently frowning. He knew that with these three people, he definitely couldn't catch Claudia, but he still hoped to delay a bit. The result, however, was not satisfactory.

"Adult, do you want to chase quickly? Maybe you can catch him?" An assassin subordinate suggested.

Alfonso touched the black coffee cup with the back of his hand, then closed his eyes in disappointment, "Forget it. The coffee has gone cold, and Claudia has already run far away."

"...What now?" The assassin subordinate asked.

"The port here leads to the Holy Roman Empire. Deploy all forces to search in Rome." Alfonso did not tighten up; his expression was disgusted, constantly wiping his backhand with his hand.

Damnable woman, you really think you can escape?__

If you don't hand over Diana, I'll make you wish you were dead!

title: Chapter 54 — Targeted (Extra)
content:
Chapter 54 — Targeted (Extra)

Volume 27 · Chapter 54

The wealthiest person of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, in Budapest, the interrogation room was dimly lit.
There was only a table and two chairs; in the cramped space, only three people were present, making the empty room feel uncomfortable.
Only the small window on the pallid wall, letting in a breeze, kept one from feeling that this was a prison.
This place is specifically used to interrogate political prisoners, where suspects are detained.
Countess Bathory was summoned here; she sat upright, and even though she hadn't slept all night, she still maintained the elegance of a noblewoman.
The man opposite her had a pallid complexion, almost blending with the surrounding white walls, looking frail and sickly.
His name was Deas, the chief grand knight of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, his status comparable to that of Mesfield in Britain, both being highly prestigious honorary knights.
Deas possessed extraordinary ability, valued by the Austro-Hungarian emperor, and he commanded the capital's guard; moreover, he could remain long at the emperor's side as a close knight, his position esteemed.
However, Deas's health was poor, plagued by illness; though only in his thirties, his appearance already approached fifty, and he daily battled his disease.
The Austro-Hungarian emperor sympathized with him, so he would never assign Deas to important matters, for Deas was among the few strong enough to deter foreign enemies.
But recently, a series of events have left the Austro-Hungarian emperor unable to rest or eat, constantly feeling that the malefactors of the Dark Guild will come after him.
Therefore, he had no choice but to send Deas to personally investigate this matter; however, after Deas summoned Countess Bathory for interrogation all night,
He gained nothing at all.
This left Deas feeling troubled; all signs indicated that the countess before him was connected to the Dark Guild, but as a noble she could not be tortured, so he could only persist in questioning.
“Countess, you still refuse to tell the truth? Actually we already know everything; it's just that your relationship with His Majesty is ambiguous, and we merely want to see your attitude.”
“I am innocent, and have no relation to Phenix.” Countess Bathory said haughtily.
“Cough, cough!” Deas frowned, coughing violently, his face turning even paler.
“Sir, would you like to rest a bit?” the knight subordinate said worriedly.
Deas waved his hands repeatedly, indicating he was fine, and stared at Bathory asking, “Since you claim you have no connection to the Dark Guild, you should all the more tell the truth, so as to prove you have no connection to the Dark Guild.”
“Everything I said is true, Lord Deas, why do you always think I'm lying?” Bathory replied without changing her expression.
“All the clues point to you, the evidence is mountainous.” Deas suppressed his coughing urge and said solemnly, “You are the person in charge of the Adventurers' Tournament venue; without your permission, how did the Dark Guild build an alchemy laboratory beneath the arena? Don't tell you know nothing at all.”
“I truly am unaware; Phenix is the largest dark organization, with eyes everywhere, fully capable of secretly building an alchemy underground room while evading me.” Bathory paused, speaking earnestly, “Moreover, I am merely the person in charge; I do not constantly monitor the Amineus Arena, and being suddenly implicated in this matter leaves me helpless; Lord Deas, you should be able to understand my feelings, right?”
“Countess, you are truly cunning.” Deas sighed, speaking calmly, “Do you think feigning pity before me will earn my sympathy?”
“Enough....” Bathory sighed, “You have suspected me all night yet produced no evidence; isn't that excessive? Are you trying to use this threat to make me submit?”
“Countess, you misunderstand me; you continually deceive me with lies, making me feel very uncomfortable.” Deas took out a black notebook from his pocket, continually flipping pages, “Besides your connection to the Dark Guild, we have also discovered that your attendants frequently slip in and out of the slave market at midnight, periodically bringing slaves to your estate—this is highly irregular; I really want to ask, what exactly are you doing in private?”
“....” Bathory broke out in a cold sweat involuntarily, not expecting Deas to uncover this; she was very worried that her vampire identity would be exposed before everyone.
Deas stared at Bathory, interestedly asking, “Do you perhaps use magic or martial arts?”
“How… how could that be? I… I am merely an ordinary…” Bathory replied nervously.
“Oh? Ordinary?” Deas paused, speaking indirectly, “We discovered a secret chamber in your bedroom, filled with piles of human skeletons and bearing signs of a struggle, almost as if you had once kept beasts—”
“I know nothing about… it might have been something my husband made before he died?” Bathory looked left and right, absolutely denying it.
“It seems the countess lacks sincerity.” Deas slowly stood up, his gaze turning serious, “Let's talk another time; if you are willing to confess everything truthfully, I can at any time clear your name.”
Next, Bathory was taken to a room without windows, even the door made of cast steel.
Though it appeared well-furnished with complete amenities, it was actually a prison used to confine ordinary people.
“Countess, just stay here and calm down for a few days; contact me when you have figured things out.” Deas said meaningfully.
“One”
Bathory's face fell; although as one of the three original bloodlines she could escape this wretched place at any time, she needed to pretend to be an ordinary person.
Thus Bathory sat on the bed with a cold expression, preparing to stall Deas, believing that as long as no solid evidence was produced, she would remain the radiant Countess Bathory.
Seeing things had come to this, the knight subordinate whispered, “Sir, the emperor only wanted you to ask a few questions; isn't it improper to detain the countess now?”
“No need to worry on the emperor's side; Countess Bathory definitely has a problem. Releasing her would only be more dangerous; if she were an ordinary person, she would break within days and confess the truth; if not, she would flee, further proving her words are false.” Deas appeared confident, then couldn't help but cough violently, “Cough, cough!”
“Sir, please take care of your health.” The knight subordinate whispered.
“It's fine, just an old ailment.” Deas gave a wry smile and shook his head.
“She… she how did she get out! ? She escaped from that bottle! No! Impossible!”
Originally normal Bathory suddenly became like a madman in the room, covering her head with a look of terror.
Bathory's face turned pale as she stumbled to the door, her eyes reddened, and she began to mutter through the bars.
“I've been discovered! Someone wants to kill me! That terrible monster will probably find me soon!”
Deas suddenly grew serious, thinking Bathory was revealing an important clue, “Who? Who wants to harm you? Speak clearly.”
“....” Bathory wanted to speak but stopped, lacking the courage to utter that name; however she realized this prison was now actually the safest place, she could not face the danger alone, but could rely on the Austro-Hungarian Empire's power, “I am the countess's wife, the emperor's lover; you must protect my safety, quickly bring strong people here, the more the better, preferably vampire hunters or the Holy Church's temple knights.”
In the mysterious cave, pitch black, one cannot see their hand in front of their face.
But suddenly a pair of scarlet eyes lit up, shining brilliantly in the darkness.
Wave after wave of Cain's laughter echoed from the depths, like a soul‑reaping demon from hell—
“I found you, you hiding little mouse A:”=
“Everything I once gave you, I will take back!”

title: Chapter 55 — Busy Merlin
content:
Chapter 55 — Busy Merlin

Volume 27 · Chapter 55

Since the adventurers' tournament was interrupted, no one knows how it ended.

Most people don't know that Merlin broke through many adventurers, and they certainly don't know that a dark guild, Phoenix, appeared at the end.

News about the adventurers' tournament seemed to stop abruptly. Half a month passed, and the Adventurers' Association still hadn't given a reasonable explanation for the tournament's interruption?

However, Merlin's influence in a small scope indeed increased a lot. Many people came to visit, wanting to see what the adventurer who defeated many strong people looks like.

But all these troubles were rejected by Merlin. He doesn't have extra energy to deal with those who come out of admiration.

Most of them only heard about these things from the survivors of the Amelius Arena, not having seen it with their own eyes.

So some believe it, and some don't, thinking those survivors are probably delusional.

As the saying goes, seeing is believing, and Merlin doesn't want to bother with such things? Unless his head is broken, it's impossible to show off a visitor.

As long as those self-important adventurers don't look down on him, Merlin's purpose is achieved.

This half month, Merlin had to explain many problems to some people, including the earth magic he unleashed at the end.

Among them, Rosetti was the most diligent, asking east and west like a curious baby, pouring tea and water, with very obvious intentions of pleasing.

After witnessing Merlin's power, Rosetti began to have some admiration in her heart, elevating the previously unremarkable Merlin to the height of an idol.

SER novel

In this room, Da Vinci and Rosetti and Merlin's family were discussing alchemy.

"Mr. Merlin, drink tea. This is a top-grade tea that I and Da Vinci specially brought. You must try it." Rosetti said enthusiastically.

"...." A few black lines slid down Merlin's forehead. He thought this girl seems to have become much more diligent? Very uncomfortable.

"Rosetti, don't do that. We are friends, let's interact as before." Alice muttered in her heart, feeling a bit uncomfortable. It's fine if a man is diligent, but now there are suddenly many women being diligent around Merlin, which makes her feel very uncomfortable.

Chris, who was sitting on Alice's legs, looked at Mom, then looked at Rosetti, and said straightly, "Big-chested sister don't need to please Dad so much, looking like a sycophant, Mom was a bit angry last night~"

"Shut up, if you say anything more?" Alice was startled, quickly covering Chris's small mouth.

"Hmm?" The tuft of hair on Chris's head turned into a question mark, wondering if she said something wrong again?

Rosetti's face looked a bit ugly. She believes that children's words are indisputably honest, so she couldn't help but sneer, "Alice, how can you be so polite to me? You aren't just licking and positioning, are you? =

"What did you say! ?" Alice's self-esteem was greatly stimulated. She raised her head and showed a gritting-teeth expression, thinking when she ever licked Alice? Or usurped the position? It's so ugly!

".....

Merlin impatiently smacked his lips, secretly regretting making such a big splash in the arena recently. One trouble after another...

It's not that female adventurers broke their heads wanting to see Merlin, or the local wealthy merchants of Budapes want to befriend Merlin.

Even Rothschild, the world's richest man, put down his stance; he invited Merlin to have dinner together, too bad Merlin has no interest.

Knowing that, the opportunity to have dinner with Rothschild, this billionaire, is not common, and even many people spend a lot of money to buy such an opportunity, but Merlin is not tempted at all?

Because there are too many troubles, Merlin recently feels a bit depressed, thinking that after leaving Budapes, maybe he can return to a normal life.

After a long silence, Da Vinci broke the argument between Rosetti and Alice, "Mr. Merlin, you said you have no battle aura and magic power, yet you were able to explode with that power on the field?"

"Exactly, didn't you already see it?" Merlin answered casually.

"This doesn't conform to common sense." Da Vinci puzzled lowered his head, suddenly remembering his single-lens glasses cracked twice. "Could it be that any ordinary person can have your such power?"

"Right! Right! Mr. Merlin, you seem to like the action of drawing a sword. I still haven't seen a person like you, using a low-level martial skill of a performative nature, yet can release such power!" Rosetti's eyes are like little stars, her face full of admiration. "If possible, can you teach me?"

"Impossible. If it could be taught, I would have accepted students long ago.

Merlin answered helplessly, thinking that being born with skill points, even if said out, no one would understand, unless one is a transmigrator like himself.

However, Merlin, to appease Rosetti, still gave a gentle explanation.

"My techniques have extremely high requirements on aptitude. Even if learned, one must endure endless hardships, nine deaths out of ten. I am a lucky person among lucky ones.

"Is that so..." Rosetti sighed disappointedly, thinking that learning a martial technique might cost one's life, so better not learn it.

Da Vinci became more and more curious about Merlin, asking, "Saying that... Mr. Merlin has never said where he comes from? Having such a unique martial technique, it must be from a very magical place, right? =

"Ah? This... " Merlin became slightly nervous. Total can't say he comes from the Death Swamp. "I come from a place you are not familiar with. The specific details involve my privacy, so let's not ask.

"Understood." Da Vinci lowered his head. Since Merlin wouldn't say, she couldn't rudely ask further, but doubts arose in her heart.

"Actually, I have some questions I want to ask Da Vinci...

"What about the executive of the dark guild? He had a strange red stone hanging on his neck. What is it?" Merlin curiously asked.

"That is a sacred object in alchemy, called the Philosopher's Stone. In alchemy, it is the essence of the world."

Da Vinci simply recounted the Philosopher's Stone, involving the basics of alchemy and the legend of the three great alchemists.

To let Merlin understand, Da Vinci didn't go deep into the explanation, basically just touching the surface.

"Originally that thing called Philosopher's... Merlin sighed, "At that time I felt a hint of danger from that thing. Originally in alchemy, that thing is used for creation.

"Not..." Da Vinci paused, seriously analyzing, "Flamel's Philosopher's Stone should be a substandard product, although it can also turn reality, but obviously cannot be compared with the true relic, otherwise he shouldn't fear Mr. Merlin...

In the temporary meeting room of the Adventurers' Arbitration Committee, five members are here discussing the issue of the final result of the adventurers' tournament.

After the chaos, the tournament's external announcement is temporarily suspended.

But half a month passed, the committee must give the world audience an explanation.

No matter what, this kind of thing cannot be delayed, and it's necessary to announce the result of this tournament externally.

Old Mr. Dawson frowned, feeling a headache, asking the other members present one by one.

"Do you have any opinions to say out loud?"

"Although this tournament had twists and turns, we must give everyone a result."

"Champion...

"Who should it be given to?

(-"-)

title: Chapter 56 — The World's Strongest Adventurer (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 56 — The World's Strongest Adventurer (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 27 · Chapter 56

Facing the chairman's question, the four arbitration committee members fell silent, finding the situation before them incredibly troublesome.

Since Merlin had defeated six of the eight quarterfinalists all by himself, this had almost completely overturned the tournament system.

Then Flamel from Phénix came along and stirred up more trouble, leaving the arena in ruins, making it impossible to hold any more matches.

Old Mr. Dawson looked at his colleagues and spoke earnestly:

"The tournament has been halted for half a month, and the Amnius Arena is severely damaged. It will likely be unusable for half a year."

"Moreover, several of the eight quarterfinalist adventurers are in critical condition, and their recovery will take a long time. It's practically impossible to hold another competition."

"We now need to announce the rankings to everyone based on each guild's current tournament results..."

It must be admitted, the situation was indeed very bad. No one had expected someone like Merlin to appear and treat the tournament rules with such disregard.

This was the first time the arbitration committee had encountered such a situation, and it was truly not easy to produce an answer that would make everyone satisfied.

The fat member said, "Adventurer Merlin really gave us all a surprise. He defeated six of the eight quarterfinalists and even beat the previous champion. His strength is truly formidable. How about we just choose Merlin to be this tournament's champion?"

"This..." Old Mr. Dawson hesitated. He felt Merlin was more than qualified to become champion—there was no doubt about that—but he feared it would be hard to make everyone accept it.

The short member said, "No, we can't choose Merlin as champion. He is a breaker of tournament rules. He clearly violated them."

The thin member agreed: "Indeed, one person challenging all eight quarterfinalist adventurers does not conform to the tournament rules. Selecting a rule-breaking participant as champion... I'm afraid that wouldn't be appropriate."

The fat member nodded: "Adventurer Merlin is indeed unsuitable. If he becomes champion, won't the tournament descend into chaos from now on?"

The four of them looked at Chairman Dawson, wondering what he was thinking.

After a moment of silence, Old Mr. Dawson spoke in a deep voice:

"As a rule-violating adventurer, Merlin indeed should not receive the championship. Otherwise, more adventurers will violate the rules in the future."

"But the fact remains that Merlin possesses the strength to win the championship, and he deserves respect."

"How about we do it this way. I think most people will be satisfied..."

"Rexem takes first place in this tournament, and all other guilds share second place. What does everyone think?"

The four arbitration committee members began discussing among themselves. Sharing second place had never happened before, and no one knew whether people would accept such an arrangement.

But at this point, a re-match was impossible, and they had to give the outside world a result as soon as possible. Sharing second place wasn't necessarily a bad option.

The short member asked, "Chairman, who do you plan to select as this tournament's champion adventurer?"

"Alice. She defeated Aelia to advance to the semifinals. As the only one who advanced from the entire field, she should rightfully receive the title of champion adventurer." Old Mr. Dawson said confidently. "Besides, Rexem taking first place also shows充分respect for adventurer Merlin. We can kill two birds with one stone."

The other arbitration committee members discussed it briefly and felt this method was workable, so they nodded in agreement.

This way, they wouldn't offend the powerful Merlin, and selecting Alice—the only one who had advanced—would satisfy the public.

The tall member said, "I'm only worried that Merlin might be dissatisfied. Chairman, how about giving Merlin the opportunity to claim the Purple Gold adventurer rank this time?"

"To make him a Purple Gold adventurer? That would be wasting his talent..." Old Mr. Dawson sighed.

The thin member said, "Purple Gold adventurer is the highest honor. How is that wasting his talent? Most people will never reach that level in their entire lives."

The fat member said, "Does the chairman mean to... give that to him!?"

"That's right. Merlin defeated six of the eight quarterfinalists on his own, effectively sweeping through all the adventurers. Tell me, which Purple Gold adventurer could do such a thing? Even the previous champion Clano, who possessed Purple Gold-level strength, was defeated by him. What do you all think? Is it appropriate to let Merlin become a Purple Gold adventurer?" Old Mr. Dawson paused and said meaningfully:

"I'm afraid only Merlin is qualified to hold that honor..."

"The World's Strongest Adventurer!"

On the 23rd, people all over the world saw the live broadcast of the tournament again.

But there was no competition held—directly to the award ceremony!?

After the tournament had been suspended for half a month, the results were simply announced outright, which left many people confused.

Some even felt this edition of the tournament was too much of a farce, with results coming out inexplicably.

However, upon seeing the champion, most people accepted it reluctantly, after all, Alice was the only one everyone knew had advanced to the semifinals.

"Congratulations to the Rexem Adventurer's Guild for taking first place in this tournament!!!"

Chairman Dawson loudly announced the results to everyone, and warm applause erupted from the crowd. They felt it was well-deserved, although some didn't understand.

Big shots from various industries expressed their congratulations. As the head of Rexem, old Taylor became the center of attention.

From this moment on, Rexem was no longer some obscure little guild—it was now the world's number one guild, renowned far and wide!

Alice, as the champion adventurer, stood somewhat awkwardly on the highest step of the podium. She was clearly not used to being watched by so many people. She stiffly raised the golden trophy—

"...Oh!!!"

Below, Aelia, Noah, Gabriel, Clano, Tanya, and Cagliostro all sat with dark expressions, silent and refusing to say a word.

Aelia and Cardovich's group were suffering the most. As traditional powerhouse adventurers, they had been utterly crushed in this tournament, losing disgracefully.

Aelia secretly glanced up at Alice, deeply resentful in her heart. She felt that if she had the chance, she would definitely defeat her with her own hands! She was an ultimate-stage dragon warrior! Losing to an amateur was nothing short of a disgrace!

Gabriel asked, "Where did the guild master and Sean go? Won't they even attend the award ceremony?"

Noah replied, "The guild master said it would be too humiliating, so they're not coming."

Gabriel said, "Aren't we second place this time too? We didn't advance or fall behind. What's so shameful about that?"

Noah said, "People will always remember first place. Who remembers second place? The guild master can't accept it and took Sean away for secret training. They'll definitely get their revenge in the future."

Clano kept his head down the entire time in silence, but his mind was churning. It seemed capturing that child was impossible. He still needed to find the black box. A single arm of the Otherworldly King was nowhere near enough to handle this man. He had to think of another method.

Cagliostro's mood was extremely low. In the end, he still hadn't fulfilled his adoptive father's wish. He cursed Merlin for appearing out of nowhere like a god. He had never anticipated this situation. It seemed he wasn't strong enough and hadn't worked hard enough. One day, he would surely avenge this humiliation!

Tanya's gaze fixed on Merlin below, her heart pounding fiercely. It wasn't the excitement of a girl's budding romance, but rather an intense murderous intent that refused to subside. She didn't know why, but she felt that defeating Merlin was her destiny! This was an unprecedented, overwhelming sensation.

"Mama~ Mama~ Ma da~" Chris, riding on Merlin's shoulders, kept waving her chubby little hand, cheering for Alice.

"...Merlin smiled. Although he wasn't the champion adventurer, Rexem had taken first place. All in all, it wasn't bad."

Even though Alice had become the spotlight's champion adventurer, some rumors still spread.

The champion adventurer of the 193rd tournament was actually someone else. That glory belonged to a little-known Iron-ranked adventurer...

title: Chapter 57 — Fulfill
content:
Chapter 57 — Fulfill

Volume 27 · Chapter 57

In the Rexheim Adventurers Guild, everyone held their breath.
Upon hearing Chairman Dawson announce that Rexheim had won first place in this competition, the guild instantly burst into cheers.
The Rexheim adventurers jumped for joy; winning first place meant that this originally inconspicuous small guild leapt to become a top-tier existence.
At that point, there will surely be many opportunities to make big money, more and more high-quality commissions will come one after another, and even many strong individuals will join the Rexheim Guild!
In this competition, Rexheim can be said to have turned from a salted fish into a dragon, making everyone look at them anew-
“Heavens, am I dreaming? We won? We actually won!?” Lucian couldn't believe her ears; only after seeing Alice as the champion adventurer did she confirm that this---everything was really true?
“....Really or fake?” Arnold seemed down for a moment, his mood improved quite a bit, “Miss Alice... actually the champion adventurer of this competition? !”
“I never expected it to be Alice, totally beyond my expectations....” Hobbs said with an embarrassed expression.
“I thought... making it into the top fifty would be nice enough? But we directly brought back the champion, unbelievable....” Arnold secretly pinched himself -, feeling the pain, realizing it wasn’t a dream.
“Top fifty? You useless wretch, what's wrong with us getting first? This is well-deserved! Alice has the strength to win, I knew it all along!” Lucian crossed her arms; dissatisfied rebuttal, now the Rexheim Guild is world number---, can't say discouraging words!
“....Of course I saw it too, after all, that's Miss Alice~” Arnold lifted his head, showing a look of eager anticipation, “No wonder she's my goddess, truly extraordinary, so charming~”
“What are you doing? You haven't given up yet? Normal people would have given up by now; I can't help but admire your perseverance in clinging on....” Hobbs raised his eyebrows.
“No, I've given up.” Arnold gave a helpless laugh.
“Pfft!” Hobbs spat out his beer in surprise, asking, “What? Even you, this dense blockhead, know how to give up? Don't, keep persisting! As long as you keep clinging on, your dream will come true someday; believe in yourself!”
"Arnold couldn't know about Hobbs'---dirty thoughts, feeling dejected, he said, “Lately I've thought a lot; I really am not worthy of Miss Alice. Rather than clinging on, I should wish Miss Alice happiness.”
Lucian's forehead instantly filled with black lines like a waterfall; she comforted, saying, “If you can figure it out, that's great. Even if you can't be with Alice, staying friends and admiring her is fine.”
“Hopefully that's the case.” Arnold sighed, narcissistically saying, “Ah~, I'm indeed a handsome, charming, sentimental man destined to have irresistible allure with nowhere to put it....”
“No, you're just sucking up to the end with nothing to show for it.” Hobbs put his arm around Arnold's shoulder, speaking seriously, “Don't cry, stand up and masturbate!”
“Hobbs....” Arnold deeply moved,
“Indeed, you're my good brother!” U
“Alice brought us the championship; this is a great joy for our guild!” Lucian crossed her arms, telling all adventurers, so today's drinks, I'll foot the bill!
“Really!? ” Hobbs, as if injected with adrenaline, kicked Arnold beside him to the ground, stood up and said, “I want ten cups”
The awards ceremony scene, Old Taylor's eyes were cloudy, showing a tendency to tear up.
After taking over the guild management from the previous chairman for over thirty years, he finally achieved a respectable result.
Being able to win this competition, Old Taylor felt that his painstaking management was all worthwhile!
“First? Unexpected, I thought because Merlin fouled, our guild could only get a place and that would be fine.” Karl exclaimed, unable to hide the joy on his face, feeling that today he really raised his eyebrows and let out a sigh of relief!
“Regardless, the result is good.” Old Taylor nodded with a smile.
“Seeing Alice holding the cup above, I'm a bit jealous, hah.... Karl scratched his own hair, envious of Alice, lamenting that the waves behind push forward the waves ahead, he himself is almost dying on the beach.
“Congratulations, Taylor.” Gregory walked over to congratulate.
“Haha, this is Britain's honor, we should share the joy.” Old Taylor said politely.
“You're right, but your guild has also risen to prominence; it will only become more noticeable.” Gregory paused, speaking meaningfully, “I didn't expect you to hide so deep; turns out your guild has such a terrifying existence; you've found a treasure, Taylor.”
