title: Chapter 19 — Incense Offering to the Squad Leader
content:
Chapter 19 — Incense Offering to the Squad Leader

Volume 28 · Chapter 19

"Calm down, Merlin!" Alice swiftly grabbed Merlin, afraid he would ruin his precious daughter's image among her little friends. "They're just a group of kids!"

"It's precisely because Chris is just a kid without the ability to discern right from wrong—what if she gets kidnapped? Let go of me!" Merlin exclaimed emotionally, already imagining the scene of his carefully raised daughter being taken away by some big oaf in the future. As her father, he wouldn't allow it!

"You're thinking too much!" Alice was startled by Merlin's words. "Kids don't have such weird thoughts. Besides, as a father, shouldn't you give your daughter freedom?"

"I don't care! Anyone who wants to take Chris away will have to defeat me first!" Merlin declared fiercely.

"Ah? So Chris will have to stay by your side forever?" Alice frowned, wondering if anyone could defeat such a pervert.

"This is even better, I don't mind!" Merlin had long since made up his mind to raise Chris for life. What's wrong with her staying by his side?

"You're crazy!" Alice raised her small fist and pounded Merlin's forehead. "Be normal for once! Chris needs to grow up, and you'll become a hindrance to her!"

"...Merlin gradually calmed down upon hearing this, thinking that Chris indeed needed more tempering. If he protected her for life, wouldn't she become useless without her parents' protection?

"Those two boys don't understand anything. Who doesn't like pretty people? It's just instinct, don't overthink it." Alice sighed and soothed Merlin's agitated emotions.

Merlin could only quiet down, continuing to watch the kids from the shadows. He thought to himself, it seems he had underestimated his precious daughter's charm—she would attract attention wherever she went...

Chris felt somewhat at a loss facing the enthusiastic questions from her two little friends, appearing still shy and unaccustomed to others' fervor.

Thus, Chris quickly put on the big gray wolf headgear her father had brought back, which made her feel safe and less shy when interacting with unfamiliar friends.

Little Minnie glanced at Chris behind her and said seriously, "You two, that's enough. She's timid, and you're scaring her."

"Is...is that so? We just wanted to welcome the new member of the Knights' Order." Four-Eyes replied awkwardly.

"Since she's a new member, if you have any trouble in the future, tell me. I'm the strongest in the Knights' Order—everyone fears me~" Snot-Nose boasted proudly.

"Shut up! You can't even beat me, and people fear you because your nose is always running, it's too dirty!" Minnie couldn't help but mock him.

"Who said that?!" Snot-Nose's face turned red as he frantically rebutted.

"Hehe...Chris giggled behind Minnie, finding these little friends interesting and more fun than the adults she had met.

"If any of you can fight, I, the acting captain, will acknowledge you!" Minnie brandished her small fist proudly. "How about it? Who dares to challenge?"

"We've never heard you become the acting captain before?" Four-Eyes rubbed his eyes, not very convinced.

"Yeah, you just appointed yourself. We only recognize the first captain!" Snot-Nose retorted.

"When the captain returns, you two should give up." Minnie shook her head and sighed, showing a regretful expression. "The captain...he will never come back..."

"Huh? What happened?" Snot-Nose asked curiously.

"Could it be...the captain betrayed the revolution!" Four-Eyes guessed anxiously.

"No, it's the captain..." Minnie became sentimental, using exaggerated acting skills. "The captain has left us forever!"

Four-Eyes and Snot-Nose were immediately shocked, then lowered their heads in mourning, thinking the captain must have sacrificed himself for the revolution, killed by the evil adults.

To them, Little Merlin was their spiritual leader. Without Little Merlin, the Watermelon Knights' Order was like a soulless body.

"Don't lose heart, the dream of resisting the evil adults must continue. Revolutions succeed through sacrifice, and the captain has set an example for us!" Minnie clenched her fist and spoke passionately. "We must inherit the captain's will and preserve his revolutionary spirit. Countless companions like us need to be rescued, we can't give up!"

"That's right! We absolutely can't let the captain's sacrifice be in vain!" Snot-Nose excitedly agreed.

"The captain...was so great, so glorious..." Four-Eyes secretly wiped away tears.

Minnie squatted down, picked up some mud from the ground, and casually molded a small mud figure that looked majestic.

She didn't forget to pose it dramatically, recreating the scene when Little Merlin had declared the children's revolution.

Minnie nodded in satisfaction, placing the mud figure on a wine barrel, then turned to her friends and said, "Let's pay our respects to the great revolutionary pioneer. Although the captain has left us, his revolutionary spirit will live on forever. He's not dead, but lives in our hearts!"

The three kids went forward to offer incense to Little Merlin's mud figure, then pretended to mourn for three minutes. To outsiders, it might seem like Little Merlin had really passed away, and the children were commemorating their companion.

"Huh?" Little Chris didn't understand what everyone was doing and began to bow to the small mud figure, innocently following her friends in offering incense to her own father.

In the shadows, Merlin and Alice looked at each other with strange expressions, lowering their heads in silence, both feeling embarrassed by the kids' imagination.

It seemed Merlin had underestimated his position in the children's hearts, as they had even held a memorial service for him on the spot—just short of dancing on his grave!

"...Merlin, they...they think you're dead and are offering incense to you..." Alice said hesitantly, able to sense Merlin's gloomy mood.

"I see, you don't need to tell me." Merlin covered his darkening face, never expecting to be surrounded by children offering incense to him.

"This is...you're so unfortunate in life and death..." Alice whispered, looking down.

"Alice, please forget this matter quickly. Don't tell Chris that I'm the captain of the Watermelon Knights' Order. Please preserve my dignity as a father..." Merlin said bitterly. If Chris found out, wouldn't his reputation as a father be ruined?

"...I understand." Alice nodded heavily, thinking it was more important to protect the child's father's dignity at this time.

Merlin lifted his head, gazing at the few white clouds in the blue sky, squeezing out a few murky tears from the corners of his eyes.

I'm not dead! Don't offer incense to me!

This is too much...

Even my precious daughter is voluntarily offering incense to mourn me.

I'm so moved—she's such a "filial" child.

Waaah...(.

title: Chapter 20 — First Step
content:
Chapter 20 — First Step

Volume 28 · Chapter 20

Seeing everyone immersed in sorrow, Xiao Minnie hastily began to self-proclaim, "Our Gua Wa Zi Knights have a two-month history. Even if the captain is gone, we can't easily disband. But such a large organization can't become a loose sand without a leader. Conveniently, my abilities are outstanding, and I'm quite interested, so from now on, I'll take on the captain's duties. Does anyone object?"

"I disagree!" Four-Eyes adjusted his glasses, "You say your abilities are outstanding? I haven't seen it. Being a captain requires a wise person, and I'm the most suitable candidate."

"Yeah, Minnie, you can't just declare yourself captain." Nose-Picker chimed in from the side.

"If you're not convinced, come out and duel! The captain should be the strongest among us!" Xiao Minnie clenched her small fists, ready to let these two guys taste her power!

"Hmph! Brute!" Four-Eyes, knowing he wasn't a match, looked down on Minnie's straightforwardness.

"What did you say?! Believe it or not, I'll smash your glasses!" Minnie rolled up her sleeves, glaring fiercely.

"Stop fighting, shouldn't we vote fairly for the captain? Why don't we have a show of hands?" Nose-Picker suggested from the side.

"Okay, whoever supports me as captain, raise your hand!" As soon as Minnie finished speaking, she realized only she had raised her hand, ending up voting for herself. The atmosphere became awkward, and Minnie quickly raised Little Chris's small hand beside her, shamelessly saying, "See? Two to two! What do you say now?"

"Chris just joined the knights and doesn't understand anything. Her vote doesn't count!" Four-Eyes questioned.

"Yeah, Chris is a newcomer." Nose-Picker paused, continuing, "Moreover, a captain should know magic. Can you?"

"......"

Xiao Minnie was speechless. She had been pestering her father for a long time, but still couldn't learn magic. It wasn't that Hobbs didn't want to teach her, but Minnie had no talent, and no matter how hard she tried, she couldn't cast spells. As her father, Hobbs didn't have the heart to discourage her, saying she could learn when she grew up. This made Xiao Minnie still hold a glimmer of hope, thinking she just couldn't learn magic temporarily.

"Who says I can't?!"

"Then show us if you can!" Four-Eyes looked at Minnie with interest.

"You... Hmph! Look!" Xiao Minnie spat on the ground, boasting, "See! This is... Dragon Bullet Technique!"

"Don't treat us like fools!" Four-Eyes and Nose-Picker shouted in exasperation, their minds blown by Minnie's attempt to deceive them.

"Tch! You're so troublesome..." Xiao Minnie pouted, thinking about how to convince her two companions. At this moment, Little Chris, wearing a big gray wolf headgear, timidly raised her small hand and whispered, "Actually... actually I know magic..."

"!!!"

The three children were simultaneously shocked. They hadn't expected that Chris, who looked younger than them, could actually use magic?

"....I only know a little..." Chris said softly.

"You... you can actually use magic?!" Minnie jumped in surprise. If it was true, she had really struck gold! The Gua Wa Zi Knights finally had someone who could use magic!

"What kind of magic do you know? Water or fire?" Four-Eyes quickly leaned in.

"Can you show us? I've only seen the fortune teller in the alley use magic. He said I often eat my own snot..." Nose-Picker paused, speaking seriously, "I was shocked! His prediction was too accurate! But he took all my pocket money. Seeing magic is too expensive..."

Chris looked at her companions' expectant eyes, closed her eyes quietly, and tried to mobilize the power within her body.

The little girl had received the orthodox life-force inheritance of the elf tribe for some time but had never managed to use magic.

However, Chris could clearly feel something like a river flowing within her body, constantly flowing in the dead of night...

After hearing her mother's explanation, Chris thought that thing might be magic. She was uncertain in her heart.

In the distance, Merlin and Alice, the father-daughter pair, were worried sick. Seeing Chris about to demonstrate magic to her companions, they were startled.

"Has Chris ever used magic in front of you?"

Merlin asked anxiously.

"Not once. Every time she comes bouncing to me to show off her magic, it's just her stomach growling with hunger..." Alice was tense inside. If Chris couldn't cast magic, wouldn't she lose face in front of her companions?

"What should we do? She... she really doesn't know magic, does she?" Merlin furrowed his brows, thinking that the inheritance from the Elf King couldn't be fake. Why couldn't Chris learn magic now?

The few companions stared at Chris in silence, afraid of disturbing the little magician's spellcasting.

They still had some doubts in their hearts. After all, Chris was too young. Which child of her age could use magic?

"Whoosh~ whoosh~"

Little Chris took a deep breath, trying to follow the instructions in her mind to guide the river within her body out.

Though Chris looked very nervous, her parents in the distance were even more anxious.

Chris had never managed to cast magic in front of her parents. Could she succeed in front of her companions?

Suddenly, Chris opened her chubby little hands, and a faint emerald light flickered from the center of her palms...

Immediately, a small sprite emitting light appeared. It had no features or strength, its entire body composed of mysterious life force. The emerald sprite flapped its cicada wings, flew to Chris's forehead, lightly kissed her, and then dispersed into sparkling stars.

Little Chris was exhausted, sweating profusely, and plopped down on the ground. For a young child like her, materializing life force was already a difficult task.

"Whoosh... I'm dead tired..."

"Ah!"

Merlin and Alice screamed excitedly in the shadows, instinctively embracing each other.

They had thought Chris couldn't possibly succeed, but unexpectedly received a pleasant surprise!

Merlin, the old father, had tears of joy in his eyes. Though he didn't expect Chris to excel, the possibility of her learning magic was a remarkable progress for his daughter!

Alice thought her careful teaching hadn't been in vain, and today they reaped the rewards. Chris had finally taken her first step in learning magic.

Merlin: "This is a small step for Chris, but a giant leap for our family!"

Alice: "She... she actually learned it! She really did!"

The two excitedly looked at each other, suddenly realizing they were embracing. Their bodies were almost merging into one.

Alice's face flushed with two red clouds, her hand on Merlin's chest clearly feeling his rapid heartbeat.

Merlin was equally embarrassed, his eyes darting around, his arm around Alice's waist feeling her softness.

Though they hadn't hugged for long, they separated like they had been electrocuted, each adjusting their clothes.

Merlin: "We... should celebrate..."

Alice: "...Yes... (~_*)

title: Chapter 21 — Daughter Inherits Father's Legacy (Updated)
content:
Chapter 21 — Daughter Inherits Father's Legacy (Updated)

Volume 28 · Chapter 21

The mouths of the little ones turned into an 'O' shape as they witnessed Chris's magic just now, already admiring her wholeheartedly. Don't think Chris merely summoned a glowing little sprite; to these kids who've never seen the world, it's already a very impressive feat.

The scene fell into silence; the three kids stared at Chris without speaking, their gazes gaining a few more degrees of respect and admiration.

...Chris was still breathing heavily, this being her first attempt at guiding the power within her body, not yet proficient, causing... '...Little Mini spoke incoherently, her voice hoarse as she asked, 'You actually really can use magic?'

Chris slowly stood up, adjusted her big wolf headgear, then brushed off the dust on her little dress. 'I've only just learned not long ago; usually my mother teaches me~'

'...Little Mini felt envy, jealousy, and hatred, wondering why Chris's mother is so amazing while her own father can't teach her anything.'

'That's amazing! What was that glowing thing just now? It looks so pretty!' Four-Eyes was very excited; it was his first time seeing magic up close, and he didn't know that one could manifest life-element power into a little sprite—such profound magic, he could only call it a 'bug.'

'I... I've never seen such beautiful magic before; is it really that great?' Snotty eagerly asked.

'I-.' Little Chris flinched, tapped her own head, 'I don't know either! I'll have to ask my mother when I get back.'

'Who's your mother? She sounds... really amazing...' Four-Eyes curiously inquired.

'My mother is awesome; she's a Champion Adventurer, hehe~' Little Chris said proudly.

'Champion Adventurer? I heard my uncle say that this time's Champion Adventurer is from our Rex...' Snotty recalled, seeming not to remember clearly.

'Could your mother be Alice... Claudiyah?!' Four-Eyes clearly remembered who the tournament champion was, having watched the whole match.

'Yeah, my mother's name is exactly that!,' Little Chris became lively, not expecting that her newly met friends would know her mother's name? It seems her mother is indeed a famous figure near and far.

'Goodness! Your mother is actually Rex's big shot, the Champion Adventurer!' Four-Eyes sucked in a breath of cold air, frightened.

'It's actually the Champion Adventurer herself who knows, no wonder Little Chris can use magic at such a young age, so amazing....' Snotty's face was full of envy.

Feeling the envious gazes of her companions, Chris felt a bit embarrassed; fortunately she wore the headgear, otherwise her blushing little face would be visible. 'Actually my mother isn't that strong; my father is the strong one, my mother is just strict~'

Little Mini changed her previous overbearing attitude, her face full of envy for Chris, until she realized: the showing off she'd done in front of Chris was how childish? Chris is the daughter of a Champion Adventurer, she doesn't care about those trivial things she boasted about! Turns out the woman who kidnapped the team leader, so amazing, is actually the renowned Champion Adventurer?! Little Mini pondered for a moment, then stepped up to Chris, solemnly taking out the team leader's token, the demon sword Banri Garan toy.

'Chris! Take this! From today on, you are the new captain of the Melon Kids Knight Squad! Remember to inherit the former captain's legacy; we will oppose those evil adults! Hope you can devote yourself to the great revolutionary cause!'

'? ? ?' Little Chris didn't quite understand, but feeling it was awesome, she nodded vigorously, '...Oh!'

'Remember our ultimate move "I'm still a kid!" Mini paused, imitating Little Merlin's style, saying, 'The former captain once said, as long as we say this phrase, we will be invincible, undefeated; lightly, those adults will feel ashamed and guilty; heavily, they'll get a cerebral hemorrhage! We'll go wild causing trouble, letting those adults know our might!'

'Exactly, the Melon Kids Knight Squad was formed to protect us kids!' Four-Eyes was emotionally charged, feeling the knight squad had revived.

'Someday we'll be the masters of the world.' Snotty wiped his nose, thinking that now the knight squad also has a magician; saying it out will surely scare Rex's little bullies into wetting their pants.

Little Chris didn't understand what they were talking about; she just felt happy to have a new toy. Looking at the toy sword resembling her father's in her hand, Little Chris's face turned red, and she resolved to show it off to her dad when she got home.

Alice darkened her face, hearing those brats feeding Chris nonsense, her mood instantly turned sour: 'Merlin, what have you been teaching these kids? If Chris follows suit and learns badly, turning into a mischievous little brat, what do we do?'

'I... I didn't expect it to turn out like this...' Merlin covered his darkened face, never imagining that his offhand remark would be taken as scripture by a bunch of little brats, leading to him shooting himself in the foot— that... in some sense, Chris inheriting her father's business counts as her following in his footsteps? I founded the Melon Kids Knight Squad, now inherited by Chris; this really is a resignation story....

In the Rex Adventurers Guild, Lucia was chatting with Rosetti who had come for a drink. Lucia wiped her wine cup, recalling the doubts during the tournament. She suddenly remembered: Rosetti wasn't present at the scene, right? What happened? She must know! 'Rosetti, can I ask you something?' 'Oh? What is it?' Rosetti set down her cup, smiling knowingly, 'Is it some rich merchant's son sending you flowers again?' 'No, be serious.' Lucia puffed her cheeks, not wanting to be teased about that all the time. 'Alright, ask.' Rosetti put away her joking demeanor, trying to look serious. 'How did Mr. Merlin's challenge against the Cathowits adventurers turn out? I wasn't at the scene; midway I suddenly couldn't see anything; do you know what happened then?' Lucia looked curious, really wanting to know what happened back then. 'You don't know? Didn't your dad tell you?' Rosetti asked incredulously. 'No, my dad and grandpa said some nonsensical things.' Lucia recalled, her father and grandfather's attitudes seemed like they had a secret. 'You don't know, then I'll tell you; believe it or not, it's up to you, but such things, if not witnessed personally, ordinary people would hardly believe.' Rosetti paused, adopting an extremely serious expression. 'Mr. Merlin at that time challenged the Cathowits adventurers, beating their three trump cards to shreds; the broadcast crystal happened to break during the fight.' 'Actually, in this tournament, the true Champion Adventurer should have been Mr. Merlin; among the top eight, six were defeated by him.... (.o.)r - If something comes up I have to go to the hospital, so it's a bit forced. The surgery will start tomorrow morning; afterward I should be able to relax. Tomorrow I'll see if I can get the update out quickly, sorry.'

title: Chapter 22 — Invitation
content:
Chapter 22 — Invitation

Volume 28 · Chapter 22

Lucia frowned, struggling to believe her own ears. "Merlin, he defeated six out of the eight finalists in the tournament?" "Yeah, he even surprised the Dark Adventurers Guild members. The situation was quite chaotic. Merlin challenged everyone present, and no one dared to step onto the stage." Rossetti calmly drank a large bottle of beer, recalling the scene, which still left her in awe.

Lucia looked skeptical, one side believing Rossetti wouldn't lie, the other side thinking that Merlin, who often got drunk with Hobbs, was a super powerful being, making such a feat too extraordinary.

"You mean... it's all true? The live broadcast crystal broke, and all these incredible things happened." "What would I gain by lying? If I hadn't been there, even if someone told me, I might not believe it either. But the facts are that, except for Alice and Aeria, the other six were seriously injured by Merlin, making them unable to continue." Rossetti set down her empty beer bottle, saying with a touch of regret, "Only Merlin broke the tournament rules, so the arbitration committee couldn't award him the championship. Otherwise... Merlin would have caused a huge sensation. The champion of this tournament is another black-iron adventurer."

"Wow... it's so incredible..." Lucia's smile froze, feeling these words even more magical than the fairy tales she used to hear as a child.

"It doesn't matter whether you believe it or not. Maybe Karl knows that even if he says it, many people will doubt it, so he won't go around宣扬. Let's just let things take their natural course." Rossetti paused, adding, "If you can see Merlin's sword-drawing skills, you'll be amazed. I've never seen anyone refine sword-drawing to such a great extent in my life!"

Lucia was slightly shaken after hearing this, as not only Rossetti but also her grandfather and parents looked at Merlin with special favor, always finding ways to accommodate him, giving him a green light for everything.

Merlin, who usually had a mischievous smile, couldn't possibly be an extremely terrifying strong being, could he?

Lucia became even more curious, thinking about how to boldly approach Merlin and let him demonstrate the incredible sword-drawing skills Rossetti mentioned.

"I'll go to the bathroom and get me another beer." Rossetti waved her hand and walked directly to the back of the guild, temporarily leaving.

Lucia nodded absentmindedly and poured another beer for Rossetti, her mind completely immersed in the thought of Merlin, who had transformed from a mischievous person into a powerful being who swept through the adventurers.

She thought Alice becoming a pillar of the guild was fine, as Alice was upright and had a good reputation, and going out could represent the positive image of the entire Rekthum.

However, Merlin, who was immersed in horse racing and often went to shady places with his friends to drink, would probably make the image of the Rekthum adventurers even worse, wouldn't he?

At this moment, Arnold walked in from outside and sat directly in Rossetti's original seat. "Where is Hobbs? Isn't he in the guild today?"

Lucia rolled her eyes and said in a bad mood, "Who knows where he went? Probably went to get drunk with Captain Price of the Guards..."

"Is that so? I was going to drag him to take on a commission..." Arnold said casually.

"What commission?" Lucia raised her head in surprise. In Arnold's eyes, Arnold and Hobbs were the lazy and unproductive people in the guild, and now they were actively striving, which was unexpected.

"Go to the Demon Forest to collect some demon wolf pelts. It's a bit difficult for a world-first guild adventurer to say I have a 0% success rate, hehe~" Lucia dryly smiled and didn't express any hope, saying, "You two, with your knowledge of these demons, going there is useless, and it's like giving the village a face. It's better to stay out of trouble."

"What are you saying? Don't look down on people, okay?" This little prince wants to complete a mission, so he doesn't want to be ranked at the bottom of the adventurers in the guild, losing the face of the noble family. After the Duke, he often boasts to others that he is an adventurer in the guild, which is also a matter of face for him."

Lucia smiled and said nothing, thinking Arnold and Hobbs were a pair of useless individuals, and Hobbs was not as capable as he seemed. Maybe there was someone who wanted to complete a mission, just to avoid being ranked at the bottom of the adventurers in the guild, losing the face of the noble family.

Arnold proudly showed off his father's approval, as if he had already seen the look of pride in his father's eyes, looking forward to the day when everyone would look down on the arrogant and proud rich boy, daring to say they were a noble family's adventurer.

Arnold calmly picked up Rossetti's beer and drank it without hesitation, assuming it was prepared for himself by Lucia.

"This beer is Rossetti's!" Lucia said. "Wait..."

"Huh?" Arnold suddenly stood up, looking around, "Oh! Rossetti's!" He spat out the beer and ran away, "10 gold coins to find it!"

Seeing Arnold's panicked escape, Lucia laughed and said, "What a pathetic person..."

"She's still afraid of me." Rossetti sighed, feeling a bit lost, wondering what she had done to him. Lucia asked in confusion.

"It's a bit difficult to explain. I thought about it, and I performed artificial respiration to save him when he was drowning in the turbulent river two years ago, and I pulled Arnold out of the water. If it weren't for me, he would have died early."

Rossetti sighed, thinking about herself, wondering when Arnold would finally become a decent person. She looked at herself and wondered if she was an irresponsible person. "Have you tried to change your carefree attitude?"

Arnold likes Alice, who is diligent and hardworking. Maybe you will become a pure person one day, like Alice." Lucia said enthusiastically. Rossetti smiled and said nothing, thinking that under the current situation, she probably wouldn't have the chance to explain.

A postman rushed in from outside and handed Lucia a letter, "Hello, here is a registered letter for you!"

Lucia opened the envelope and looked at it, "Hmm? A purple card, she jumped in surprise as she took it out from inside.

Adventurer's Guild, urgent business, purple gold adventurer.

title: Chapter 23 — Island Kingdom
content:
Chapter 23 — Island Kingdom

Volume 28 · Chapter 23

In Merlin's home, Chris was playing with her new toy on the side—a wooden carving of the Banri Garan, which was much lighter than the real thing. Even a child like Chris could easily swing it around, and obviously, compared to the genuine royal artifact of the First Demon Lord Palace, she still preferred this toy.

Little Chris put on a serious face, imitating Merlin, drawing her sword and slashing the air with fierce momentum, as if facing a formidable opponent, while letting out loud “whoosh” breaths.

The president of Rexel, Old Taylor, personally paid a visit, saying he had something important to discuss.

So Alice let Chris go play by herself for a while, then she and Merlin began discussing important matters with Old Taylor.

Alice carefully read the invitation letter, let out a sigh; the gist wasn’t much—it was simply an invitation for Alice and Merlin to go together to Denmark to undergo the trial for promotion to purple‑gold adventurer.

It also explained that the opportunity was rare; if they gave it up, there would be no second chance.

The status of purple‑gold adventurers is exalted and extremely rare; to this day only five have been selected, representing the top combat power of the entire adventurer industry.

Looking at Gregory and the old witch Sesi makes it clear that the existing five purple‑gold adventurers must all be possessors of secret techniques.

They have eccentric personalities, keep a low profile, and hardly ever appear in the public eye; to hire them for work, probably only the Rothschild family, the world’s richest, has the financial means.

Upon reaching the purple‑gold level, one cannot be swayed merely by money; far more is required.

For Merlin and Alice, this is a good opportunity to climb higher and come into contact with the rare powerhouses of the industry.

“I basically understand the matter of becoming a purple‑gold adventurer; it looks like a very precious opportunity.”

“Yeah, you’re the champion adventurer of this tournament, so getting a chance to be promoted to purple‑gold adventurer isn’t surprising.” Old Taylor nodded and said slowly, “Purple‑gold adventurers are the highest honor in the industry; those who receive this honor have always been geniuses among geniuses.”

“......” Merlin stroked his chin, thinking, “Geniuses among geniuses? That’s a bit exaggerated, isn’t it? Whether it’s Gregory or Sesi, I feel they’re just average, though their strength really can go a few rounds with a Demon Lord.”

“If you can pass this trial, it will produce Rexel’s first‑ever purple‑gold adventurer, which would be great publicity for our guild and a very honorable thing. So I hope you take this seriously and succeed in the trial.” Old Taylor spoke gently, having lived half a lifetime, finally meeting people like Alice and Merlin; being able to witness the birth of a purple‑gold adventurer in his guild also meant his life hadn’t been wasted!

“Really?” Alice stared at the invitation on the table for a moment, then nodded and said, “I know. I’ll do my best to become a purple‑gold adventurer; I’m still very interested.”

“Haha, that’s good. I’ll greet Chairman Dawson for you; the Arbitration Committee shouldn’t make things difficult for you.” Old Taylor hoped he could be of some help, then shifted the topic: “Merlin, you’ve also been invited to this promotion trial; it seems the Arbitration Committee holds you in high regard.”

“Oh?” Merlin tilted his head, thinking that swapping his black‑iron badge for a purple‑gold one wouldn’t be bad at all~

“Although you broke the rules in the tournament and didn’t get the champion adventurer title, your strength is undeniable, and the Arbitration Committee has seen that, so they naturally want you to take the trial.” Old Taylor paused, then added, “When you were first registered as a black‑iron adventurer, it was just industry rule, but rules are dead while people are alive; this trial is a good chance to prove yourself—I believe becoming a purple‑gold adventurer won’t be difficult for you.”

“Oh la~” Merlin felt moved; the black‑iron adventurer’s proof had always been a burden on him. If he exchanged it for a shining purple‑gold proof, he wouldn’t even need to lift a finger—just flash the badge and a crowd would shut up. How wonderful!

“It’s quite possible our guild will have two purple‑gold adventurers; that would shake the whole industry.” Old Taylor wore an expectant expression. Rexel had just become the world’s number one guild; if it gained two purple‑gold members, the Rexel Adventurers Guild would undoubtedly become a powerful guild with deep roots—far more impressive than just being called the “number one strongest guild,” ten times over!

“Um... President...” Alice curiously asked, “What is the trial for becoming a purple‑gold adventurer?”

“I’m not really sure either, since this is also the first time I’ve seen an invitation.” Old Taylor gave an embarrassed shake of the head; he had never received an invitation before. If it weren’t for Merlin and Alice, he might not even know what an invitation looks like. “But I’ve heard the trial is very tough; those who succeed in becoming purple‑gold adventurers rarely talk about it, and those who fail apparently also suffer serious injuries and are left with considerable psychological trauma.”

“... Is that so?” Alice felt a hint of pressure after hearing that, thinking—what kind of trial could leave challengers with psychological scars...

A month later, Merlin and Alice appeared in the Kingdom of Denmark.

This country was far weaker than Britain or France; its land area was tiny, an inconspicuous island nation in the human world that survived mainly on maritime trade. If it weren’t for the fact that the North Sea monster Kraken had once appeared here, probably few people would have heard of it, because its presence was just too low.

However, in the hearts of all adventurers, this place is truly a holy land—not only because it is where the Adventurers’ Headquarters is located, handling information for big and small adventurer guilds worldwide, but also because the Adventurers’ Tomb lies here as well. The proofs of all deceased adventurers are sent here; each morning they bathe in the sunrise, allowing their souls to rest. Thus, for adventurers, the Kingdom of Denmark is not merely the location of the headquarters; it is also the final resting place and endpoint of life.

Because it lies near the sea, the kingdom’s streets are filled with fishmongers, their stalls a riot of colors that, seen through little Chris’s eyes, seemed to open up a whole new world.

Merlin and Alice stood behind, quietly watching their beloved daughter squatting by the washbasin, her eyes full of longing for the ocean world.

Little Chris plucked up her courage, reached out her small hand to touch the big fish in the water, but the fish slipped away, slick and smooth.

“Wow~ secret” Chris felt very novel, marveling that the world still had slippery creatures, and her courage grew accordingly.

Seeing Chris hold her breath and—she just—grab the big fish out of the water, laughing nonstop with “hehehe.”

The big fish, which is usually bullied by the fish sellers, now being bullied by a melon‑headed brat? Instantly she felt indignant.

With a crackling sound, the big fish twisted its slippery body, flicked its tail and gave Chris a series of slaps, then dove into the basin, still blowing bubbles to taunt her.

“Guh...” Chris covered her sore, numb little face, feeling terribly wronged, and tearfully turned to complain—

“Chris was bullied by the fish, and it even laughed at me, saying ‘quick help me hit it,’ wuu...”

title: Chapter 24 — Going in Circles
content:
Chapter 24 — Going in Circles

Volume 28 · Chapter 24

Seeing little Chris looking wronged and upset, just like a child who had been bullied outside, crying and running home for a hug, Merlin laughed and slowly squatted down, asking, “Why did you provoke this fish for no reason?” “I… I just wanted to touch it, but it hit me,” little Chris said, pressing her lips together, her cheeks slightly red and swollen. “…” Alice covered her mouth and chuckled, “Hahaha, your daughter is usually fine, but sometimes she’s so silly…” Tears burst forth, red‑eyed she flung herself into Merlin’s arms, “Mommy doesn’t love me anymore, wuwuwu.” “Dad, are you going to cry or not?” Merlin picked up Chris, patted her back, and said, “Boss, this fish… how much?” The fish vendor replied, “Here I’ll grill it fresh for you, ten copper coins.” “We’ll take it, just this one, we must let it know its place is as food.” The fish bubbling in the water basin, Merlin pointed at the big fish’s eyes— they rolled, sinking into despair as the water surface was covered with dead fish, floating… “Hehe! Ah!” The arrogant, taunting big fish was now… in Alice’s hand, fragrant and crispy, turned into Chris’s… fire mouth: edges all oily. “Little one, want to eat?” Merlin looked at Chris in his arms, asking. “Fragrant~” Chris giggled, bringing the fish to Merlin’s lips, answering in a soft, childish voice, “Daddy, tasty!” “Used it.” Merlin shook his head, not interested. “If Daddy won’t eat, then give Mommy a bite,” Chris teased. “No, give it to Daddy, Mommy just… I’m still… humph!” Chris puffed her cheeks, still not forgetting what had just happened. Alice felt a bit disappointed, “This guy still remembers…” Thinking, “Mommy kisses me and I’ll give you…” … Chris’s little mouth rose up, instead demanding Alice… came over. Alice touched Chris’s little head, feeling— the second daughter was still quite happy, apparently sensing… only novel things. She liked seeing… Next, Alice originally thought not to bring Chris, but leaving her at home with no one to look after, so she had to bring this little guy. Since this is a trial organized by the Arbitration Committee, there shouldn’t be any danger, Merlin and Alice should feel reassured. They still… the guild president said, “This trial is quite difficult, you’d better prepare.” Alice whispered to Merlin, “What’s that? Just a promotion trial, how hard can it be? I think it’s just a walkthrough, how big a chance is there to get promoted?” Merlin said nonchalantly, “Then just…” “Be serious, don’t think it’s too easy,” Alice reminded sternly. “Don’t you want to prove your black iron rank?” “What? How could you not want to?” Merlin paused, “Anyway, the trial, for me it’s… continued… the difficulty, for you it’s not necessarily…” “What do you mean? Don’t look…” “I’m fine, I’m definitely fine.” … Alice puffed her cheeks, feeling Merlin’s contempt… “Not…?” Merlin gave her a meaningful look. “Alice, actually you just need to follow me and you can steadily complete the trial. Absolutely… don’t treat me as useless once you leave me.” Alice stared coldly, “Isn’t that the fact?” Merlin retorted, Alice’s face covered with a layer of frost, Merlin’s smug expression made her seethe, “We’ll see, humph!” The Adventurers Guild headquarters, the tallest building nearby, easy to spot. Its magnificent… side hung with guild flags from all over the world, at a glance you know this is the place for all adventurers, making people… Rexhelm had just won the tournament’s… the very center is Rexhelm’s guild flag, announcing to everyone who is now the industry’s leader… “Is this really here? I thought it would be a shabby place.” Merlin thought the headquarters would be shabby, but the guild actually works in some rundown house. Actually it’s the adventurers’ headquarters, how could it be shabby? The headquarters collects annual fees from guilds worldwide, this is already a substantial income. … Alice explained beside him. Alice snuggled into Merlin’s chest, feeling… everything unfamiliar, subconsciously becoming old… many… peaceful… inside she recalled the hurried footsteps… the arbitration committee actually came out personally to greet them. “Two, we’ve been waiting a long time, you finally came.” Dawson saw Merlin really coming to participate in the trial, his expression… actually this trial’s target is Merlin. The committee will focus… “Alice? Consider it buy one get one… since she’s a champion adventurer without an invitation…” … The old man hurried forward, warmly shaking hands, this enthusiasm made Merlin feel… … “Your Excellency Merlin, I am Dawson of the Arbitration Committee, they are all committee members. The chairman… behind him, four tall, short, fat, thin committee members… showed kind smiles, nodding to Merlin… Merlin felt wary, as if he’d walked into a wolf pack as a little sheep, the big wolves’ saliva almost dripping… “Compared to enthusiasm, it’s either treachery or theft!” … Merlin thought in his heart, feeling this trial might not be simple, perhaps the Arbitration Committee has other motives… “Hello, I heard from the guild president…” … “SF light novel said chairman 5…” … “Hahaha! Taylor that old guy, actually…” … introduced me, rare~’ Dawson the old man laughed heartily, “I’m essentially a… experienced merchant, though not good at management, after I took over… all over the place bloomed, scale at least expanded tenfold, can be called…” … “Sounds impressive…” Merlin gave a polite reply. “No matter how impressive, it can’t compare to you, Mr. Merlin— you became famous on the battlefield, achieved almost impossible feats, your prowess we all see…” … “If we give you the champion adventurer award for violating the rules first, it would break the rules, also hard to… hope you can understand.” Dawson said, apologizing face to face. … Committee member: “Yeah, not giving you the champion award was unavoidable.” … Committee member: “With Mr. Merlin’s strength, even ten champion adventurers’ honors couldn’t match his.” … Alice stood aside, almost invisible, the committee members circled Merlin, going round and round, as if there wasn’t such a big person? Noticing… this bunch of sycophants wildly wagging their tails at Merlin… Merlin could be an adventurer, basically the whole industry’s… … Alice couldn’t help but sneak a glance, rolling her eyes back… thinking back when she brought Merlin into this… … Now she’s the most lackluster champion adventurer in history…?

title: Chapter 25 — Land of the Holy Spirit's Suffering (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 25 — Land of the Holy Spirit's Suffering (Bonus)

Volume 28 · Chapter 25

"This is the Adventurers Guild headquarters, with a history spanning a hundred years since its founding by the first adventurers."

"Actually, at the beginning, adventurers were just a small group of like-minded people who didn't amount to much and were largely ignored."

"Don't laugh, but the earliest adventurer groups were even considered mountain bandits by the royal family, not even on par with mercenaries."

"It wasn't until the founder of the adventurers established basic rules for the industry that the situation improved somewhat."

"We adventurers and mercenaries are similar in that we take money for jobs, but we absolutely won't participate in any organization's struggles. We are free people, belonging to no particular faction."

"If an adventurer wants to get involved in conflicts, it's entirely up to their personal stance and has nothing to do with the adventurer industry as a whole."

"Although adventurers have extremely high freedom, serving everyone, we also have a bottom line - we can't do things that harm heaven and earth. This is the fundamental difference between us and the Dark Guild."

"After long-term development, today's adventurers have become an undeniable force in the world, a trusted organization among the common people, earning countless praise and applause..."

Chairman Dawson and the arbitration committee members walked ahead, leading Merlin's family on a tour of the Adventurers Guild headquarters while recounting the history of adventurers.

As chairman, Dawson was extremely familiar with the history of adventurers, treating the entire headquarters like his home. Whenever important guests visited, he couldn't help but tell stories about adventurers.

Dawson hoped adventurers could shed their past image burdens, making all forces in the world take notice, transforming adventurers into warriors fighting for freedom rather than a disorganized mob.

"I know not everyone in the adventurer ranks is good; many have done evil things in the past. But I hope they can change themselves after joining adventurers. This is also an opportunity for many who have strayed to turn back..."

Originally, Merlin was following behind, listening drowsily, but upon hearing this, he perked up, his heart tightening as he glanced at Chairman Dawson walking ahead. He thought Dawson was indirectly criticizing him, hinting at his past as an evil ruler. It turned out he was being overly sensitive.

Merlin was still somewhat concerned. Although adventurers wouldn't investigate members' pasts, he was the embodiment of evil. Who knew if the adventurer industry could still tolerate him?

In stark contrast, Alice and Chris were listening with great interest, finding the adventurers' past fascinating. It was indeed no easy feat to achieve their current scale.

Little Chris hid in Alice's arms, her silly hair swaying back and forth, treating Dawson's stories as mere tales.

"Mommy, were you guys considered big bad eggs back then?"

"Uh... not exactly. That was in the early days..."

Alice answered with a sheepish smile, thinking to herself that she wasn't from that era, so how could she know what adventurers were initially considered?

However, Alice somewhat understood. When an unknown organization suddenly appears on someone else's turf, those in power would naturally feel uneasy.

Just like Elgin, the great swordsman, who was continuously pursued by the royal family. If not for his overwhelming strength, he might have been imprisoned long ago.

Merlin had no interest in history. Looking at the people bustling around him, busy to the point of exhaustion, they wore uniforms similar to the committee members, carrying many scrolls everywhere - clearly the headquarters' staff.

The guild's operations seemed simple on the surface but were actually quite complex. Publishing a single commission often required the efforts of many headquarters staff.

Merlin, who had never been here before, had always thought it was easy to just take a quest from the guild and get paid.

"Chairman, I'm not very interested in history. Could you tell us about the trials we'll face next instead?"

"Ah? I thought you liked hearing these things..." Dawson chuckled awkwardly before turning serious. "Becoming a Purple Gold adventurer, the highest honor in the industry, won't be easy."

"What exactly... is it?" Alice asked, feeling some pressure upon hearing Dawson's words. With so many adventurers, yet only five Purple Gold ones, the difficulty was imaginable.

"It's a strange place, said to be where Raphael, one of the Seven Archangels, fell and suffered. It's a place the Heavenly Realm uses to punish its own kind. A certain cardinal once speculated that there might be a secret passage connecting the Heavenly Realm to the mortal world, but it can only be traversed by one person." Dawson explained slowly.

"Oh?" Merlin's ears perked up slightly, thinking of the Seven Archangels - weren't they the seven commanders of the Holy War? Countless demons had died at their hands...

"So the place is completely different from the outside world, inhabited by savage residents who are completely isolated from the outside, living primitively, even with cannibalistic habits. They're entirely unlike us..."

Chairman Dawson paused before continuing, "What you need to do is kill their chieftain and bring back his head. That's how you succeed."

"It sounds... not that difficult?" Alice pondered, just needing to eliminate a savage chieftain.

"Miss Alice, I hope you take this seriously. It's easy to get into danger there." Dawson turned to look at Alice seriously. "The place is called the Holy Spirit's Suffering Ground because no matter how strong you are outside, your power will be greatly weakened on the island, making you almost like an ordinary person. Your proud magic and martial skills might not be of much use. You'll have to rely on basic combat and magic. To complete this task, you'll need wisdom, not brute force. The current five Purple Gold adventurers have all passed this test..."

"Ah?! Our strength will be greatly weakened there? What kind of place is this?" Alice was shocked, thinking that if high-level martial skills and magic couldn't be used, wouldn't she have to engage in close combat with those savages?

Merlin remained silent, thinking that if his power was weakened there, and it was related to the Holy Spirit, he really didn't want to go...

Chairman Dawson stopped and turned to face Merlin and Alice, his harmless smile now seeming somewhat sinister.

"I think you two must have heard something before coming. Very few adventurers have succeeded in the trial. Many have died inside, and even those who survive are haunted by shadows for life."

"You don't think I'm joking, do you?"

"Even if you're incredibly powerful outside, on that island, you'll become a weak ordinary person."

"To be blunt, whether you can even defeat the savages there is uncertain..."

Regarding this month's sparse updates

I just accompanied my family to the hospital today. I know this month's updates have been lacking, and I apologize for everyone's support.

I don't know if you've experienced taking care of someone in bed, but with even a slight movement, I have to get up immediately to check. Writing has been intermittent.

So this month is indeed my fault. In November, I'll make up for it as much as I can.

Also, when I update less, you can go check out the manga. It's quite good.

After all, pictures are more intuitive than text, with certain advantages.

Even if you've read it, you can still go look at the manga to imagine the scenes, right?

Plus, the manga has many beautifully drawn character illustrations.

Also, Pineapple Circle is holding a lottery again, for a set of family standing figures. If you're interested, go support it - you might win!

Little Merlin

title: Chapter 25 — The Slow-Time Island
content:
Chapter 25 — The Slow-Time Island

Volume 28 · Chapter 25

"That's the place. Are you two ready?"

Mr. Danson led Merlin and Alice to the center of the headquarters building. The room here was spacious, and everything was constructed from sturdy rock.

On the floor were patterns resembling whirlpools, which looked like a magic circle, yet there was not the slightest magical fluctuation. It was more like a mysterious mechanism.

Merlin looked at the empty room without saying anything. He felt a bit uneasy—if his own power was also being weakened here, then it seemed he'd end up having a tavern brawl with a bunch of barbarians...

Little Chris looked around and sensed something odd about the atmosphere, so she bit her lip and whispered, "Mommy, how about we go home?"

".....Alice seemed hesitant. After coming all this way, wouldn't it be a waste to leave without even trying?"

"If you two are ready, just stand in the center of the room, and we can send you to the trial location right away." Mr. Danson said.

Alice looked down at her beloved daughter, feeling worried. She had heard from Chairman Danson that this trial was quite dangerous. With Chris by her side, she feared she wouldn't be able to take proper care of her.

No matter what, Alice really didn't like Chris being in danger. If she had known it would be like this, she should have asked the old chairman to take care of her daughter for a while.

The other committee members seemed to have picked up on Alice's concern, so they stepped forward to explain—

Short Committee Member: "Miss Alice, if you're worried about the baby's safety, you can leave her here temporarily."

Skinny Committee Member: "Yeah, the trial location isn't very safe. Bringing a child along would probably be quite inconvenient. We'll take good care of her."

*Chirp...*

Little Chris immediately showed a reluctant expression, grabbing Alice's arm with both hands and unconsciously tightening her grip.

Obviously she didn't want to be separated from her parents, even if it was just for a few days.

But Chris had also learned to read the room. She figured her parents had important business to attend to, and she couldn't be selfish. Being good would mean not putting pressure on her parents.

Merlin and Alice watched their dejected daughter, and they couldn't help feeling a pang of guilt. Who knew how long the trial would take? A week? A month?

Chris was still so young. If she couldn't see her parents for a long time, she'd definitely end up crying and throwing tantrums.

"Haha, you two don't need to worry too much. That island is actually quite strange—the flow of time is much slower compared to the outside world." Mr. Danson paused, smiling as he explained, "A month on that island is equivalent to just one day in the outside world."

"Oh my! There's really such a place!"

Merlin was greatly surprised. He immediately thought, "This is a place perfectly suited for cultivation! With time moving so slowly, one day of training there would equal thirty days in the outside world!"

With just a short amount of time, those with similar talents—warriors or mages—could become Saint-tier.

Merlin was amazed but quickly calmed down. He listened as Mr. Danson said the island was very dangerous, and that anyone who went there would have their strength greatly diminished. They'd constantly have to worry about being killed by the barbarians on the island. Thinking about it that way, it didn't seem like a good place for cultivation at all.

If it were suitable for cultivation, the barbarians on the island should have long since learned cultivation techniques, and there should be experts everywhere. Clearly, things weren't as simple as he imagined.

"That place was accidentally discovered by the founder of the Adventurers, who left his own name there. To be precise, it's private land belonging to the Adventurers Headquarters. Later, it became a secret base used to test adventurers." Mr. Danson turned to Merlin and explained slowly, "When the founder of the Adventurers first set foot on the island, he discovered its peculiarity—time didn't match the outside world at all. He once considered using it as his secret cultivation spot, but later found it wouldn't work. The strength of people on the island would be restricted, plus there were threats from barbarians. The air contained no magical energy or combat spirit, making it impossible to cultivate there."

Merlin nodded, his guesses mostly confirmed. Since it wasn't suitable for cultivation, the barbarians on the island were probably uncivilized, not knowing any magic or martial arts. They likely only had simple primitive hunting skills.

Alice looked at her well-behaved daughter in her arms, her maternal love overflowing. If what Chairman Danson said was true, then it was fine. She and Merlin would go take the trial, and Chris wouldn't have to wait long outside.

Little Chris seemed to have sensed Alice's thoughts, so she quickly put away her unhappy expression, putting on a brave face, "Daddy and Mommy go do your important business. Chris will stay here good and quiet!"

Alice looked at her daughter's forced composure and felt a wave of warmth in her heart. She gently kissed Chris's forehead, "Wait for us here. Don't run around, and don't cause trouble for others. Understand?"

"Mm-hmm. Mm... Chris nodded like a little chick pecking at grain, biting her lip and not willing to express her reluctance, afraid of burdening her parents.

Alice gently put Chris down, leaving her in the care of several committee members for a while. Then, with a serious expression, she called out to Merlin, "Let's go..."

Merlin took a deep breath and followed Alice to the center of the room. He could clearly feel the whirlpool patterns beneath his feet beginning to vibrate slightly, as if there were great currents surging underneath.

"How are we supposed to get to that island? Don't they give us a boat?"

"No need to make it so complicated. This room itself is the passage to that island. We'll reach it very quickly." Mr. Danson gave a reassuring smile.

"...Is that so?" Merlin couldn't help feeling uneasy. This sensation was not unlike falling into water.

Mr. Danson walked to a mechanism and gripped the wooden lever, "Well then, you two—good luck!"

The moment the words left his mouth, Merlin felt his feet go light. The floor carved with whirlpool patterns suddenly vanished, revealing raging rapids below, with no idea where they led!

Seeing this, both of them were stunned for a moment, then their bodies fell uncontrollably. They never would have imagined that the so-called "secret passage" would wash them away.

Alice: "Aaaah!"

Merlin: "Oh my god! I can't swim! I $#@*&%! ! !"

With a loud "plunk," the sound of their fall into the water echoed, and the entire room fell completely silent. Merlin and Alice would drift along the underground river to that mysterious island.

Little Chris saw that her parents had disappeared, feeling very sad. Her cowlick had lost all its spirit, and she silently prayed that her parents would come back soon.

"That...?" Mr. Danson looked up, puzzled, "Did you hear that just now? Mr. Merlin said he can't swim?"

The committee members looked at each other and shook their heads, saying they hadn't heard clearly. But in the end, Merlin's curse was very distinct.

"Haha..." Mr. Danson laughed heartily, his tone teasing, "Mr. Merlin defeated six of the eight finalists—he's a rare super strongman."

"Can't swim?"

"Obviously that's impossible! I was just kidding. (@~Vo)

title: Chapter 27 — Trial on the Desolate Island (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 27 — Trial on the Desolate Island (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 28 · Chapter 27

Seagulls skimmed across the sky. A crab crawled onto the beach, walking sideways, only to be swept back by the waves. Merlin, drenched and weak, lay sprawled on the sand, unconscious, his fingers twitching—meaning he hadn't drowned was already a stroke of luck.

If he had known reaching here required swimming, Merlin would never have agreed to this trial—he might have lost his life. Unfortunately, the realization came too late. He didn't know how much dark river water he had swallowed before reaching this mysterious island.

The moment he fell into the dark river, Merlin had already "greeted" the Arbitration Committee's ancestors eighteen generations over...

Across the beach lay dense jungle, dimly lit, making it hard to know what lurked within. Yet from the depths emerged a pitch-black, barely clad figure.

His body was lean and muscular, built for sprinting through forests. Against his jet-black skin, only his eyes gleamed brightly. Adorned with eerie white bones, animal hides, and leaves barely covering his shameful parts—he was a complete wild man, Mo Yang.

Seeing an outsider charge onto the beach, he shivered, gripped his spear, and approached Merlin.

"A lulu? Lu lu ya ka!" The savage saw Merlin motionless, his face lighting up—he thought dinner was served.

Still cautious, he poked Merlin's behind with his stone spear...

"Si! L!" Merlin jolted awake at the pain, glaring around with a fierce expression. "Lu lu ka?!?" The savage, frightened, dropped his spear and scurried back into the jungle—probably thinking Merlin was fierce prey he couldn't handle alone.

"Damn...
Merlin gritted his teeth, clutching his aching buttocks as he slowly rose, feeling incredibly heavy and sore.

Hardly straightening up, Merlin's stomach churned, and he vomited seawater mixed with a small fish that hopped alive on the sand.

After retching, Merlin felt somewhat better, trembling with relief. Thank goodness he'd survived—those bastards from the Arbitration Committee were trying to kill him!

Fuming, Merlin surveyed the unfamiliar surroundings. He didn't know how long he'd been unconscious, only feeling dizzy and groggy. A massive boulder stood out nearby, carved with a name—
"Robin Hood"

Merlin froze at the name, then gradually snapped back to reality, recalling Chairman Dawson's words. Whoever left their name on that stone must be the founder of the adventurer industry, right?

So I've reached the trial grounds.

Merlin took a deep breath, gazing at the empty beach and dense jungle. In the distance, a pyramid stood in the forest—the island's most majestic structure.

That must be where the savages gather. If I take out their chief, I'll have completed the trial...

For some reason, I sensed a force on this island I despised. Could there really be a living Saint-tier being here?

Wait! Why was I the only one washed ashore? Where's Alice?!

Merlin looked around frantically, but the vast beach held no one—no sign of Alice anywhere. He worried, guessing Alice might have been swept elsewhere. Should he go find her first?

Just as Merlin decided, footsteps echoed from the jungle ahead—a horde of dark-skinned savages charged out with stone weapons.

"Hmm?!" Merlin frowned, adopting a defensive stance. That cowardly little guy who went back probably couldn't handle him, so he rallied his savage companions to capture Merlin alive.

The savages surrounded Merlin, spears aimed at him, afraid he'd escape—this was tonight's feast.

Merlin scanned the savages coldly, laughing. "A rabble. Still thinking of taking me on? Move aside if you don't want to die—I only want the chief's head."

The savages glanced at each other, unable to understand a word, then advanced menacingly.

"Looking for death? I'll grant your wish!"

Merlin's gaze hardened, pulling his katana to his front before slashing at the air—

The savages were intimidated by Merlin's aura, but seeing nothing happen, they burst out laughing, thinking the prey was all show and no substance, maybe a few screws loose.

Merlin froze, shocked. My... my power... why isn't it working?! What the hell?!

He quickly calmed down, recalling Chairman Dawson's warning: no matter how strong you are outside, your power is greatly weakened upon entering the island!

Merlin had held onto a sliver of hope, but he'd fallen for it too. His proud sword slash had lost most of its effectiveness on this island!

The weakening power was stronger than expected—even Merlin couldn't escape it. This forced him to take the island's secrets seriously.

Seeing Merlin as no real threat, the savages surged forward to capture their prey. Unable to use his sword slash, Merlin had to be careful even against ordinary savages—one slip and he'd be caught.

Thankfully, Merlin had solid fundamentals. Even without the sword slash, his basic swordsmanship was excellent—he could barely handle these barbarians.

Merlin swung Banri Garan, his figure darting as he unleashed a Five Strike Slash! Blade light flashed. Five grotesque blood flowers erupted among the savages, who twitched and died on the ground.

"Come if you dare!" Merlin growled. His ragged appearance clashed with his arrogant attitude—his eyes like those of a cornered wolf.

Seeing how vicious Merlin was, they'd killed five companions in one move. Fear gripped their hearts. They dared not attack Merlin, yet refused to leave, as if waiting for something.

"Wulala!!!"
A roar broke the silence, followed by thunderous footsteps. The savages before Merlin were kicked flying, their bodies torn and bloody.

A towering savage over three meters tall appeared, wearing a fanged mask and a skull necklace, as if displaying his achievements! He was the first warrior among the savages, possessing unimaginable strength. At his appearance, the others stood in awe, parting to let him through.

He stamped his foot, patted his massive belly, brandished his stone hammer, and roared at Merlin. "Wulu (Look at this skinny outsider)"

Merlin looked at the plump, burly enemy before him. A cold sweat dripped from his forehead as he silently gripped the rusted katana—

I never felt Banri Garan so heavy before. (oo)

title: Chapter 28 — Giant Spirit
content:
Chapter 28 — Giant Spirit

Volume 28 · Chapter 28

Merlin privately speculated that the brute force of the barbarian warrior in front of him, emanating from his overwhelmingly powerful aura, was on par with that of a mid-tier warrior if assessed outside.

But on this island, even such a strong presence was quite formidable, capable of becoming the champion of the entire barbarian group.

Merlin finally understood why the adventurers who participated in the trial, even those lucky enough to survive, would be left with psychological trauma—

Since the adventurers who participated in the trial were all outstanding elites strong in ability back home, they would be weakened into cripples by a mysterious power after setting foot on this island.

From a powerful figure who could summon winds and rain to an ordinary person who struggled even to lift a weapon, this psychological gap—probably not everyone could endure it.

And then to be humiliated by this bunch of trash-like barbarians—years of hard cultivation arriving on this island, yet almost completely useless? Who could bear that?

If it weren't for the suppression of the mysterious power, even Mr. Carl could run rampant on this island!

But this was after all the barbarians' home turf. They could easily bully outsiders who arrived on the island. The participants' foundational strength here was extremely poor.

Merlin assessed his own condition. It wasn't that he couldn't execute the Drawn Sword Strike—he could, but its power had weakened significantly. Under the current circumstances, he felt he could probably handle high-tier opponents.

"Ho! Ho! Ho!"

The surrounding barbarians began constantly beating their stone weapons, making roaring encouragement sounds from their mouths. The scene instantly transformed into a primal duel ceremony.

The barbarians were all eagerly awaiting the first champion's performance.

P SF Light Novel

The burly barbarian first champion, hearing the surrounding encouragement, grinned wide to reveal his yellowed teeth, his battle intent surging.

"Huge guy, you think you're my opponent?"

Merlin's eyes sharpened.

"Rururururu!!!"

The barbarian first champion didn't waste any words. He raised the heavy stone hammer in his hands and smashed down with a terrifying roar.

Merlin had been prepared long ago. He sidestepped and rolled, narrowly avoiding this crushing blow by the width of his shoulder!

"BOOM!" A deafening crash echoed as the heavy stone hammer slammed into the beach, sinking deep, kicking up dust in every direction.

Merlin sneered inwardly, thinking his guess was correct—these guys knew no martial technique. All brute strength, absolutely no skill whatsoever!

Taking advantage of the moment when the barbarian champion was struggling to pull his stone hammer free, Merlin ran at full speed. Relying on his nimble footwork, he darted behind the enemy and with two swift slashes, severed the barbarian champion's Achilles tendons. The barbarian champion let out a pained cry, his legs buckling uncontrollably as he collapsed to his knees, his lower body completely numb.

Merlin slowly approached the enemy's side and said coldly, "Foolish..."

The barbarian champion was drenched in cold sweat, his eyes behind the mask flashing with terror. "Wurrurulula (Despicable foreigner)!!!"

Merlin couldn't understand what he was saying. To establish authority through a public execution as a warning, he raised his blade and decapitated him in one stroke.

"Squelch"—gushing blood sprayed like a fountain. The barbarian champion's headless corpse shuddered several times before going still.

Watching the rolling head, these barbarians were scared senseless. In their gazes at Merlin, a touch of awe emerged.

No matter how ignorant these barbarians were, fearing what was powerful was instinct. The principle of submitting to the strong—they understood that well enough.

...Merlin secretly exhaled a long breath. His goal of killing the chicken to scare the monkey had been achieved. If a huge crowd of barbarians had charged at him recklessly without fear of death, his current state would have made things truly troublesome. Even back home, it was possible to kill a Saint-tier expert using human wave tactics—and the same applied here.

Just as Merlin was about to decide where to go next, he suddenly realized a massive shadow had enveloped his feet, and a sound of splitting air came down from above!

A colossal fist descended like Mount Tai crushing downward, carrying overwhelming, irresistible momentum.

Merlin couldn't see anything in the direction of his gaze—only that falling iron fist. He couldn't fathom his current state at this moment, nor could he determine where this attack had come from?

"Uh!"

The sky-covering iron fist crashed down with a thunderous impact. The entire island trembled with rumbling shakes, and the kicked-up dust shot toward the sky, making it feel as if night had fallen.

The barbarians all dropped to their knees, continuously bowing their heads, muttering prayers in their mouths—like people in ancient times praying to the gods of heaven, their hearts filled with reverence and awe toward the power of nature.

The turmoil lasted for a while before subsiding. The giant fist slowly retracted. Merlin lay face-down on the ground, unconscious—beaten badly by that single strike.

In the distance, near the direction of the forest pyramid, a tall giant had appeared without anyone noticing. Roughly estimated, it must have been close to 200 feet tall, impossible to make out its full figure.

Its entire body was naked, its skin snow-white, covered with exaggerated muscle lines. Weirdly, it lacked any gender characteristics.

On both of its thick wrists were golden bracelets carved with complex characters, continuously radiating a holy aura.

This giant wore a crown atop its head. Its enormous pure white wings, with just a slight flap, caused the entire island to tremble endlessly!

It gradually parted its massive lips, exhaling gusts of foul air that slowly formed thick clouds, looking exactly like the heavens worshipped by ignorant humans...

A trace of cool liquid entered his throat, continuously nourishing his internal organs. It made one couldn't help but marvel—how could such sweet spring water exist in this world?

Merlin suddenly jolted awake, his entire body tensed, his vigilance toward his surroundings pushed to the extreme!

He instinctively reached for his waist toward Banri Garan, but grasped only empty air. Surprise flashed through his heart—Where's my sword?!

The surroundings appeared to be inside a palace, although simple, it still exuded an aura of majesty. The table was filled with all sorts of delicious fruits.

Many of the young barbarian women, startled awake by Merlin, retreated to the corners, eyeing him curiously.

Although these women had dark skin, they had fiery figures—and even though each was completely naked, none of them seemed to mind.

Merlin remained alert inside, unsure where he had been brought. Logically speaking, shouldn't these barbarians have eaten him by now?

At this moment, Merlin lifted his head and finally saw on the high platform a masked short man playing with Banri Garan, unable to pull it from its sheath no matter how hard he tried, jumping around like a clown.

Seeing that this dwarf wore an ornate feathered crown, and those around him were deeply respectful,不敢 raising their heads to look at him, Merlin grew suspicious in his heart—couldn't this be the chieftain of the barbarians?

"Hey! That sword is mine. Give it back."

"???" The dwarf chieftain paused, glanced at Merlin below, and showed absolutely no intention of returning Banri Garan.

Instead, he sat upright on his high seat, looked down on Merlin from above, and frequently emitted mocking "giggle giggle" laughs.

"Shorty, just you wait. I'll definitely chop your head off..." Merlin muttered under his breath, irritated inside, contemplating how to take down the guy in front of him.

A strange gleam flashed in his eyes. He raised his hands and clapped twice—"slap slap"—as if some kind of secret signal.

The fiery-figured women in the corner surged out all at once, carrying fine wine and meat, swarming around Merlin like songbirds. The skull necklace of the warrior was順勢 placed around Merlin's neck as the symbol of first place—?!

title: Chapter 29 — Betrayal Revolution
content:
Chapter 29 — Betrayal Revolution

Volume 28 · Chapter 29

Merlin stared at the skull necklace hanging from his neck,

His expression strange, muttering to himself, "What does this mean?

"Lululu, la lululu, kaka wu."

The dwarf chieftain stood on the platform, saying a bunch of things that people couldn't understand. It seemed he had seen Merlin kill his first hero, so he felt reluctant to part with such talent,

And wanted to bring Merlin over to his side?

"This???"

Merlin was full of doubts. Although it was hard to understand the barbarian's words, he could still barely grasp their meaning.

He tried his best to suppress the shock in his heart and weighed the gap in strength between himself and this chieftain.

Although outside, Merlin could easily kill this chieftain, but with his strength weakened, it would probably take some time to complete the trial.

There was no doubt that the sacred giant that appeared earlier was probably the incarnation of this dwarf chieftain. Merlin asked himself that his current state was poor, and he couldn't defeat it.

It seemed that President Daxun was right. It wasn't simple to force through the trial with brute force. He needed to calm down and think of other methods.

Merlin glanced at the Banri Garan beside the dwarf chieftain. His own sword had been confiscated by the other party, which was the first time he had encountered such a situation.

"Lululaka wu..."

The dwarf chieftain whispered some orders to the servant beside him. Immediately afterward, the seductive woman around Merlin dispersed, leaving a dazed Merlin.

The sound of waves fluctuating on the strings rang out. Two beautiful women slowly walked out from behind the platform. They were ten times more attractive than the maids earlier, truly rare beauties!

The white silk couldn't hide their extremely sexy figures, and the "sharp weapons" on their chests were about to burst out. Countless male servants around them couldn't help but swallow saliva and couldn't move their eyes.

Accompanied by charming music, the two women full of exotic charm danced gracefully, moving left and right to Merlin's side.

Merlin's expression was strange. He had originally thought these barbarians would roast him alive, but instead he was greeted by a string of sugar-coated bombs.

He was always soft-hearted and not tough. The dwarf chieftain, in order to win Merlin over, even shared his beautiful concubines with Merlin.

This made Merlin very embarrassed. He was here to take the chieftain's head!

Merlin's eyes darted around, not knowing what choices he was making in his heart.

At this moment, Merlin only felt the two temptresses beside him were constantly teasing him, their slender waists like flexible snakes, rubbing against him.

This...

Isn't this making me make a mistake, betraying the revolutionary friendship between me and Alice?

Several days later, in another place far from the center of the island, there was a village.

Although the people here looked exactly the same as the barbarians, they seemed much gentler. They didn't look like other barbarians who wielded weapons and liked to shout and fight. Everyone was quietly busy with their own business.

Even many children were playing outside the thatched houses. Inside a grass hut,

The unconscious Alice lay quietly, breathing evenly, but never woke up.

Although it was hard to tell exactly how long Alice had been on the island, judging from her haggard appearance, it should be no less than a week.

Compared to the unfortunate Merlin, who directly encountered a group of cruel barbarians, Alice seemed much luckier. She met kind-hearted barbarians and was carried to a small village while unconscious for recuperation.

A little girl with dark skin, wearing simple animal hides, about seven or eight years old, was holding a basket and sprinkling unknown green leaves on Alice's head, giving her some green.

The green leaves emitted a faint fragrance, probably some kind of primitive healing method. The unconscious Alice inhaled this every day.

Alice's eyelids fluttered a few times, then slowly opened her eyes. She felt heavy and sore all over, obviously having suffered a lot in the dark river.

What met her eyes was the dilapidated grass hut, and then that dark-skinned little girl.

Where is this place? Who is this child?

The barbarian little girl saw Alice's eyes open and stared at her, the basket in her hand fell to the ground, and she ran out and shouted.

"Kalu lululu!"

Listening to the completely incomprehensible language, Alice felt a wave of headache. She slowly got up and surveyed her surroundings, her memory flooding back like a tide.

Right! I participated in the trial, entered the dark river, and was sent here.

If I didn't guess wrong, this place should be the target of the mission, the island where the barbarians are.

Alice immediately tightened up, became vigilant, seeing many fragrant green leaves beside her. She remembered what President Daxun said, that the barbarians on the island practiced cannibalism and had the habit of eating people.

What are these barbarians putting so many leaves beside me? Is it incense for eating me?

Alice broke out in a cold sweat, completely not knowing how long she had been unconscious, but the unfamiliar environment made her very nervous. She quickly found her Light Mantra and prepared for a desperate counterattack.

At this moment, a large group of barbarians rushed in from the outside. There were men, women, and children among them, with dark skin and shining eyes, all staring at Alice as if they were very curious about this stranger.

"What do you want?"

Alice's nerves were tense. She quickly drew her sharp sword and tried to cast magic, hoping the barbarians would retreat in the face of difficulty.

But before Alice could react, she was completely stunned. She felt her body was empty, with not a shred of magic or combat energy, no different from an ordinary person. She couldn't cast magic or martial arts at all.

"...What's going on? Where did my power go?"

Alice stared with wide eyes in disbelief, barely recalling President Daxun's advice that no matter how strong she was outside, her strength would be greatly suppressed on the island.

"Is it..."

Alice lifted her head and looked at the strong barbarians in front of her. A chill ran down her spine.

After being weakened by the mysterious force on the island, her strength was now far below Merlin's, probably even unable to defeat a low or middle-tier warrior.

If so many people attacked Alice, she felt that it would be very difficult to resist.

Alice refused to surrender to these cannibalistic barbarians, holding her thin sword without letting go, facing the barbarians.

But at this moment, an old barbarian slowly walked out from the crowd, white-haired and thin-boned, with strange tattoos all over his body.

"Friend... lulaka... calm... cotton~~"

The old barbarian, unafraid of death, came to Alice's sword, trying to communicate in his native language mixed with foreign words, while constantly gesturing, hoping Alice would calm down and relax.

"Huh?" Alice frowned, looking at the frail old man, thinking that barbarians could also speak our language? Although it was a bit awkward, like the level of a few-year-old infant.

"Friend..." The old barbarian waved his hand, pointing at Alice's thin sword.

"...Not..."

"First... to come here, friend..."

title: Chapter 30 — Dark Creature (Bonus Chapter)
