Chapter 30 — Dark Creature (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 28 · Chapter 30

"Ah?" Alice was stunned, barely grasping the barbarian elder's meaning; she realized she wasn't the first outsider to come here. "We..." the barbarian elder waved his hands, insisting he wasn't a bad person. Alice hesitated, observing the barbarians—though they looked fierce, their demeanor resembled ordinary villagers. Moreover, she wasn't the first to contact them; perhaps earlier adventurers who came for the trial had already gotten along with them. Alice slowly lowered her thin sword, but remained wary, not fully trusting them. "What do you want?" "……" the barbarian elder pointed at Alice, indicating that the barbarians had saved her. "Beach… you didn’t wake up." Alice stared, thinking that when she fainted, it might have been these barbarians who rescued her. Doubtful, she picked up a green leaf from the ground and smelled it; it felt refreshing, not harmful. Alice surveyed the barbarians, wondering if Chairman Dao’s claim that the islanders eat raw meat and blood, having cannibal habits, was true—they didn’t seem evil. "Are you the only one who can speak the outside language?" The barbarian elder nodded repeatedly, trying to explain, pointing at Alice: "Someone like you has come before…" "Oh…" Alice nodded; it seemed the barbarian elder understood outside prophecies because other adventurers had visited before, he’d learned a bit, though his speech was still awkward and communication was a bit tiring. "Okay?" the barbarian elder patted his chest, asking. "Ah! Oh! Aside from being a bit tired, I’m fine." Alice gradually let down her guard, showing a gentle smile. The barbarian elder signaled his people to bring fresh fruit to Alice, speaking clearly: "Please." Alice looked at the colorful fruits, some she had never seen before. She had thought this place would be beast‑like monsters, but instead received warm hospitality. Alice wondered where Merlin was and blurted out, "Have you seen a blond guy with a cheap‑looking face?" The barbarian elder shook his head honestly: "Only discovered me one?" Alice worried—Merlin couldn’t swim, she didn’t know what might happen to him, wondering if he had arrived here. The barbarian elder seemed to understand her concern and said, "…… here, what should we do?" Alice hesitated, worried that these barbarians and the trial’s chief’s faction… she concealed part of the truth: "I want to see your chief; I have something to discuss." As soon as she spoke, the barbarians inside the house changed expression, even the elder was frightened. The chief residing in the temple is a god who likes to eat people, especially infants—traits similar to dark creatures. This barbarian chief probably isn’t human, right? The barbarians are narrow‑minded; they mistook dark creatures for lofty gods, imitating that chief, they too began eating people. What an inhumane habit! Alice lowered her head in thought, feeling the island’s situation differed from what Chairman Dao had said; these barbarians were stupid but pure‑hearted, merely misled by that so‑called "god". Seeing the island’s facts weren’t what she imagined, Alice grew much calmer; killing the island’s chief would not be easy. "Actually, I came to kill your chief." The barbarian elder trembled, dancing in place, warning of death if provoked… (the text becomes garbled here)… he continued his awkward advice, and Alice didn’t hear… these people are merely narrow‑minded, taking it as truth, thinking… the object as god worship. Generally the suppressive force of dark creatures is so strong that… after all there must be especially powerful beings here… perhaps it’s only high‑level magic that the chief… finds an opportunity to kill the opponent… still… master, as long as oneself… can do… After resting three days, Alice’s body had basically recovered; she prepared to go look for Merlin, then… set out to complete… that distant pyramid, magnificent she discovered… in the forest it stood out strikingly, like climbing… magnificent, in this forest… the sky’s ladder. The barbarian elder… the elder spoke awkwardly, but although barbarian… through gestures and words Alice understood some things… about the pyramid, in the elder grandfather’s this magnificent… it already existed. In grandfather’s era… the god… possessed unimaginable… inside lived… requiring barbarians to offer… divine power, it wants… children. And, including oneself… the barbarians fear the god’s power here… backward… cannot resist, can only constantly pray for infants… amount, dare not… bring to the temple… child won’t be taken by the god… temple? The elder’s meaning to Alice regarding this temple… the temple’s function roughly is a prison… she guessed seven or eight parts… used to imprison great… people Alice can’t guess, but this great sin… according to Dao Chairman’s info, won’t be… seven great… angels maybe? Outside has another name, after all here… Holy Land of Suffering… determined to go to the mysterious pyramid, she Alice decided… coming here also makes her think of meeting… if Merlin… might go to an obvious landmark building… self will meet, very likely… construction… possibly meet there, don’t ask Alice why two people have… so think? ask because husband and wife… Alice why will… heart‑to‑heart. She put away her thin sword; when leaving Alice took a few gold coins, although not knowing if they could be used, but also counted as her… repayment to the barbarians. Afterwards, Alice saw the little girl who had been with her when she fainted, big dark eyes… always taking care of her. Eyes were sizing up… and 0… this outsider wants to do what little girl not… tell elder… go? think not… Alice made a shushing gesture… not make noise, smiling took out three… from her bosom to let the little girl not… girl, this originally used to coax Ke… piece of candy give to little… west, didn’t expect to be useful. Alice happily east… little child never ate such thing barbarian’s… mouth, instantly conquered the little girl, candy just slipped in… never eaten such sweet thing! girl, she never ate… Alice’s gaze, full of awe… little girl looks… almost kneels on ground, giving this outsider… worship little stars… to make this outsider a slave… The elder softly asked, "What’s your… Alice good… name?" Doesn’t understand, but clever, guesses little girl hears… (some gibberish) meaning replies, Ou… something. Alice’s gentle expression solidified… outside burnt inside tender, thinks, what on face, struck by lightning… can’t stand… ghost? basically no record… Alice still had leisure to ask barbarian little… at this moment Alice… yet hasn’t realized danger approaching… girl’s name… In the woods nearby, already have… from god village surroundings… come here, will be swept… temple’s servants surround… empty… claws among, also has one… familiar figure… this group of chiefs… Not long ago, chief’s subordinate first brave just became…"

title: Chapter 31 — The Witch's Little Help
content:
Chapter 31 — The Witch's Little Help

Volume 28 · Chapter 31

Alice tried chatting with the savage girl for a few sentences, then prepared to quietly leave and head alone toward that pyramid. She had heard countless times from the savage elders that the temple was extremely dangerous and not to go there.

Alice worried that these pure-hearted savages would block her, so she chose to slip away silently to meet the chieftain called a 'god.' But as Alice was seeing off the little girl, she hadn't even left the village when she ran into the elder who had just come out of the thatched hut.

The savage elder examined Alice up and down, asking, 'Where... are you going?' Alice sighed helplessly, thinking, 'Just my luck,' and said in a firm tone, 'I want to go to the temple to meet your chieftain. I know it's dangerous, but I must go. Thank you for your care these past days, but I have to go.' After the elder understood, he sighed deeply and could only shake his head helplessly, 'Misplaced outsider, like you, you have a mission; I respect that.'

Alice stared, thinking that those adventurers who came for the trial like her had made the same choice, resolutely stepping onto the road to the temple. Though this was nothing unusual, wanting to become a platinum adventurer meant one had to overcome this hurdle.

The savage elder undid the belt around his waist, pulled out an ancient potion and a yellowed letter, saying, 'Take them!' 'Huh?' Alice looked at the elder's determined eyes, feeling doubtful, took them, and examined the golden potion. 'Long ago, an outsider like you came here... the... plague... very.' The elder spoke in broken language mixed with gestures, continually telling Alice something: 'She healed us, saved this place, she is our... great benefactor! Grateful, very grateful...' 'Really?' Alice nodded, barely understanding. So the adventurers who came before for the trial had cured the village's illness—no wonder the savages treated me so kindly; I was just benefiting from that. Looking at the yellowed letter, Alice felt a bit eerie—just a glance told her it was likely over fifty years old, though time here differs from the outside; perhaps twenty years have passed outside. '...The elder pointed at the potion and letter in Alice's hand, seriously saying, 'She left it. She said that when a fortunate outsider comes, give it to them.' 'Oh~' Alice understood: this potion and letter were deliberately left here by a predecessor adventurer to give later comers a little help. Driven by curiosity, Alice opened the dust‑sealed letter; since it was left by a senior, it was easy to read— '[Congratulations, lucky one, seeing this letter means you have reached the place I once lingered at SF light novel. If I'm not mistaken, the plague there has already disappeared and the pure‑hearted savages have warmly welcomed you, right? Anyone who can set foot on that island must be taking the platinum promotion trial; are you perhaps frustrated because you can't unleash your true power? Since you've reached this village, it's fate. As a senior, I can help you with a small favor; whether you become a new platinum adventurer depends on you. I stayed on this island for a while, investigated some things—this place possesses a mysterious power that weakens outsiders' strength and an almost terrifying holy aura. Usually the stronger the one who comes here, the greater the weakening, especially for demons, undead, dark mages—those who wield dark power suffer the most. If you are such a person, absolutely do not try to brute‑force your way through the trial, or you will die miserably. My trial task was merely to escape from here; I don't know what yours is. But I know you now want to restore your power, and I can give you a little help here. That potion I personally prepared, mixed with artificial holy spirit blood, can instantly cancel that mysterious power. Remember, after drinking the potion you have only one chance to use magic and martial skills—use it wisely. Wishing you success, lucky little one; don't tell the Arbitration Committee about this, after all it's a bit of cheating~ J (≥V≤)> J'

Alice put the letter away with a strange expression, not realizing it was left by the old witch 'Sesi.' Sesi had also taken the platinum adventurer trial, befriended the savage villagers, and helped them dispel the plague. That's why the savages are so friendly to Alice—entirely thanks to Sesi's help. It seems the trial tasks differ; for Alice and Merlin it became slaying the chieftain, a high‑difficulty task that feels a bit unfair. Alice still thanked Sesi's predecessor, but looking at the golden potion she pondered: This potion lets me use magic and martial arts only once—feels a bit little. I don't know if I can kill the chieftain in one blow; if I can't, that would be awful... From Sesi's letter I gathered the chieftain isn't a dark creature—I guessed wrong? Alice couldn't figure it out, so she stashed the potion, planning to sneak to the pyramid, find Merlin, and consider other things.

However, just as Alice was about to bid farewell to the elder, chaos erupted in the village— 'Balarulu!!!' A group of savages from the temple arrived, shouting rudely, attitudes arrogant, they kept flipping over the frail thatched huts. Wielding stone‑crafted weapons, they showed off, continually scattering the pure villagers, yet they snatched away the young children. Among them was the little girl who had tended to Alice while she was unconscious, now being hoisted by the chieftain's minions, trembling. It appears the chieftain's lackeys periodically snatch some little girls from the island to offer to the 'god' chieftain, praying for favorable weather. Now it finally fell on this remote village to be raided, but the savages didn't know— an outsider was also here? 'Hisahahah!' The village elder turned pale with fright, rushed forward, pleading with the temple guards. 'Hahahaha!' The guards didn't buy it, shouted abuse at the elder, knocked him to the ground, and a crowd began kicking the old man nonstop... Seeing this, Alice's face instantly darkened; she silently drew the thin sword at her waist and shouted loudly, 'Stop! You bunch of shameless bastards!'

title: Chapter 32 — Traitor Merlin (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 32 — Traitor Merlin (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 28 · Chapter 32

The temple guards’ attention was drawn by Alice’s scolding; they picked up their weapons and surrounded her, showing off. Even some barbarians looked at Alice with lewd eyes; even if they didn’t know the meaning, they could guess it was vulgar language. These barbarians from the temple often saw the chief’s meat and wine pools; suddenly seeing such a fair‑skinned woman, they naturally had wild imaginations. Alice’s face grew uglier, she gripped her thin sword, looking at the surrounding barbarians; she had lived in this village for a few days, received much care; facing this, she naturally couldn’t stand by! A bold temple guard with a grin walked forward, extending a salacious hand to tease Alice. But Alice’s eyes turned cold, a flash of cold light, and the bold barbarian’s salacious hand was directly chopped off! Fresh blood spurted; the injured temple guard looked at his severed hand, cold sweat pouring, wailing as he rolled on the ground. “Ka‑lu‑lu!!!” Other barbarians seeing their companion severely injured shouted angrily, no longer daring to underestimate Alice, they raised stone‑made weapons and swarmed. Alice was quick‑eyed and quick‑handed; her thin sword, even without any magic or battle aura, was still incredibly sharp, as if alive, splashing blood wherever it went! Alice’s foundation was very weak, but not long ago, under the devilish training of teacher Claudia, her basic strength was greatly compensated. Otherwise, if Alice had directly joined the Purple Gold Adventurer’s trial, she would likely have been defeated early in the barbarians’ siege. The barbarians had not undergone orthodox martial training; facing Alice they were clumsy, suffering successive defeats. After just a few rounds, Alice had beaten them black and blue, her thin sword puncturing many holes in their bodies, though thanks to their strong physiques, there was no mortal danger. Yet the barbarians, despite having good physiques, had a very embarrassing flaw: they were timid. After suffering at Alice’s hands, these temple guards felt afraid, only daring to shout from afar, not daring to approach. “Leave here! Otherwise I won’t hold back!” Alice raised her hand, the gleaming cold light of the Holy Chant. At the moment the temple guards were torn between advancing and retreating, the looting large force slowly arrived here. In the midst of the crowd, a sedan chair woven from vines was being carried, on which sat a great figure. Around his neck hung a skull necklace symbolizing the first warrior; he wore a grass skirt, barefoot, lounging there, his blond hair, black face, white skin appearing especially mismatched, also quite weird. Amid the escort of many temple guards, this first warrior slowly stepped down, looked up to see Alice holding her sword opposite him, obviously stunned, “???” “Ah?” Alice furrowed her brows, she could immediately smell the cheap, nasty odor emanating from Merlin’s body; no matter how he disguised herself, she could recognize him: “Merlin, what are you doing? Did you think going to Wakanda would make me not recognize you?” “....” Merlin was at a loss, blurted out instinctively, “No way? You can still recognize me like this?” “Nonsense! Even if you turned to ash I’d still recognize you!” Alice didn’t understand what Merlin was up to, but seeing him mingling with that bunch of savage barbarians made her inexplicably angry. Merlin wanted to speak but stopped, thinking how much Alice must hate him? That’s too exaggerated! “Why are you smearing black paint on your face? Playing tricks!” Alice muttered. “This is ash from the furnace, I deliberately applied it…” Merlin rubbed his face with his hand, gave Alice a knock. Alice frowned tighter, her doubts growing, “What exactly are you up to?” Just as Merlin was about to answer, he noticed the temple guards around him staring at him with strange eyes, making him wary; he instantly changed into clothes and put on a cold expression. “Merlin?” Alice sensed something odd, Merlin was not his usual self, seeming to care a lot about the barbarians’ gazes? Merlin’s gaze turned cold, he swept his eyes over the temple guards, loudly shouting, “Front wheel not turning, rear wheel turning maybe blah blah!” The temple guards seemed to understand, they all stood solemnly, made way for a path, and faced Merlin with a salute. Alice was completely bewildered, she asked in surprise, “Merlin, what nonsense are you spouting? ???” Merlin didn’t answer, suddenly rushed forward and punched Alice in the abdomen. Alice had no guard against Merlin, caught off guard by the sudden thunderous blow! “Cough!!!” Alice cried out in pain, her eyes filled with disbelief, she never imagined Merlin would attack her! She clutched Merlin’s arm tightly, wanting to ask, but her consciousness gradually blurred, she fell into unconsciousness. Merlin hurriedly supported the fallen Alice, opened his mouth slightly but wanted to say more then stopped, finally sighed, still said nothing… When Alice barely woke up, she felt she had slept soundly, swaying gently. She slowly opened her eyes to see lush green leaves and dim starlight. A wave of soreness came from her abdomen, instantly clearing her mind; her first thought was: Merlin has betrayed me! He betrayed me! He’s already wearing the same pants as the temple chief! No wonder he changed into barbarian garb, even blackened his face—just to get along with the barbarians more easily! I thought we had steadfast revolutionary camaraderie, but I never expected it to be so fragile; upon arriving on the island, in minutes he defected—this betrayal speed is too fast! Alice felt heartbroken, wanting to cry but no tears, feeling she’d been screwed by Merlin, unable to fathom what method the chief used to directly turn Merlin against her. She looked around in panic, discovering she was bound to a pole, only her buttocks could move, her hands tied poorly by two barbarians lifting her. This resembled barbarians returning from a hunt laden with game; Alice was like a piglet about to be placed on the fire to be roasted and eaten. Now Alice was utterly panicked, tears almost flowing, recalling the barbarians’ tradition of eating humans made her even more desperate. Meanwhile, Merlin sat like an old gentleman on the sedan chair ahead, leisurely whistling, appearing quite happy, having fully blended with the surrounding barbarians. Seeing Merlin like that, Alice’s heart sank halfway, a bitter surge rose in her stomach, she began shouting at Merlin: “Merlin!!!” “You heartless traitor....” “Let me down!!!”

title: Chapter 33 — Torture
content:
Chapter 33 — Torture

Volume 28 · Chapter 33

“Merlin!!! ” Alice started to cause a ruckus,
but her power was suppressed, and being tied up she couldn't move,
she could only shout uselessly.
.....Merlin clicked his tongue impatiently, lounging
on the sedan chair, “You're so noisy, behave
yourself, stop yelling, what's the use?”

“What?!!!” Alice seethed, thinking Merlin had truly changed
his temperament, become part of the barbarians, disregarding all past
feelings and just grabbing her.
“What's wrong with me? Any problem?” Merlin turned
his head, showing a smug smile, seeing Alice suffer made him feel
all-around comfortable~

“You heartless white-eyed wolf!” Alice bit her lip,
glowering at Merlin with resentment, “I did so much for you,
and now you betray me, even drag me here—what do you mean?”
“What do you mean?” Merlin chuckled
and countered, “You can't figure it out yourself?”

“Me?!!!” Alice rolled her eyes in anger,
“You're blind, I thought you were someone with
principles and limits….
“Hahaha~” Merlin burst out laughing
meaningfully, “Believing demons have principles
and limits, you're really naive, Alice~”

......Alice let out mournful wails from her throat,
seeing Merlin soft on the outside but hard inside, she immediately
spoke in a grievous tone, “Merlin, are you really this heartless?
Think of Chris, and….”
“Ah? Don't give me that, if you talk more I'll
eat you~” Merlin threatened, turning his head mysteriously,
“These barbarian folks do eat people, especially someone
with delicate skin like you—if you provoke them, I can't
save you.”

“Merlin! What exactly are you trying to do?!!” Alice
seeing soft and hard tactics both useless, became furious,
“If you're going to side with these barbarians, I….”
“Ah? What do you want?” Merlin raised his
eyebrows, thinking Alice was like this, could there be
any countermeasure left?
“I will definitely make you look bad!” Alice
threw out a harsh line, hoping Merlin realized she was
truly angry; if she got pissed, she'd take the potion
and fight Merlin to the death!
“Yo yo yo, you scared me~” Merlin
shook his head, completely disregarding Alice's words—
“This stinky woman is all tied up and still dares
to threaten me?
Looks like I need to give her a taste of her own
medicine to make her behave—”

Due to the night being too late, the temple's raiding
party didn't return to the Pyramid Temple, but chose to
camp midway.
The barbarians began to busy themselves, they lit
a bonfire and then danced around the fire with an
eerie dance.
Unaware Alice, seeing the barbarians act
strangely, muttering to themselves, seemed like a
large cult gathering!
Alice shivered, a bad feeling rose in her
heart—what are these people doing? It's like
they're having an epileptic fit—light novel

Suddenly, the group dancing around the bonfire
stopped dead, all eyes hungry fixed on the helpless
Alice.
In the night, matching the dim yellow firelight,
the barbarians' eyes flashed with red glints—how
terrifying!
“Eee!!!” Alice screamed, feeling
she'd been stared down by a bunch of zombies,
“You—you what do you want?!! Don't mess
around! ....I.
Alice couldn't even finish her sentence before
being—-a horde of barbarians cheered and lifted
her up, directly placing her over the bonfire
It seemed that deep into the night, the barbarians
could no longer bear their hunger, finally
couldn't resist moving against Alice, wanting to
roast her and eat her outright?
Alice had never experienced such a thing; scared
out of her wits, she regretted coming to this
godforsaken place.
Although she knew these barbarians had a
cannibalistic custom, when it actually came to
her, anyone would feel fear.
Alice only felt the flames below scorching her
buttocks, she instinctively began to cry out—
“Hot hot hot hot hot….
“Merlin! You really came?
“I really misjudged! I actually believed
someone like you!”
The barbarians didn't understand what Alice
was saying, they began dancing around her on the
bonfire, frequently letting out primitive cries
like sparks.
Flickering fire embers floated upward, the
barbarians' swaying silhouettes were like
primitive people before a meal, offering thanks
to the sky god.
Seeing Alice in such a miserable state over the
fire, Lin “pfft” laughed out loud, a day without
tormenting Alice would make him feel uneasy~

Merlin saw Alice had suffered enough,
so he put on a stern face and stepped out, speaking
with a commanding tone—
“Kebabut! Wulu lu lu si keba la la, ye
ai sha lu lu
(Stop! This woman will be offered to the
great sky god tomorrow; before that I need to
tame her tonight.)
The barbarians heard, exchanged glances, and
quickly lowered Alice from the bonfire, after all
Merlin is the first warrior, his status far above
theirs.
Many barbarians also exchanged glances with
that… eye signal, they all knew what would
happen tonight—so-called taming the prey is
something everyone understands~
This is barbarian custom: female captives
are conquered by the strongest barbarian before
being handed to the chieftain.
It's to protect the chieftain's safety, to prevent
female barbarians from rebelling and assassinating
him in the temple.
As the current first warrior, Merlin naturally
has the full right to enjoy this privilege; other
barbarians lack the guts to contend with the first
warrior.
Alice was set down, tears of grievance rolling
in her eyes, her butt feeling a burning sensation… “Hmph,
knowing to behave now?” Merlin grinned
cheekily, heartless, “The flashy world dazzles
the eyes; without strength, don't go showing off~”

Alice fumed, glaring at Merlin, already
hated this guy to the core, “Merlin, you bastard!
I'm not done with you!
After the temporary camp settled down, Merlin
hogtied Alice and carried her into the only
tent, preparing to tame the little wildcat.
“Pa cha” Alice was flung by Merlin's cold
hands onto a crude bed woven of grass, then—he
gave a nasty grin and stared at her.
.Me......Alice turned her head, gritting
her teeth, the thought of mutual destruction with
Merlin had crossed her mind.
“Hahaha~” Merlin laughed heartily,
taunting, “How's it, Alice? Didn't expect
that, huh? You've fallen into my hands again,
are you happy?”
“.." Alice narrowed her eyes, her mouth
making grinding noises, she pondered how to
take revenge.

“Oh dear, this is truly fate, I am your
nemesis~” Merlin crossed his arms, shaking
his head and swaying, saying, “This isn't the
sea, I don't need you to suffer as a slave
rowing a boat—tell me, how should I torment
you properly?”
Alice sprang up at once, though bound
tight, she still bared her teeth, clack clack
clack lunged at Merlin to bite—
“Merlin! I'm going to fight you!!!”. . .(NIajN谷

title: Chapter 34 — Show the Dagger When the Truth Is Revealed
content:
Chapter 34 — Show the Dagger When the Truth Is Revealed

Volume 28 · Chapter 34

Alice lunged at Merlin, baring her teeth, showing off her might, wanting him to know how formidable she was. However, she was already tightly bound; for Alice to resist Merlin was nothing short of a fool's dream. Merlin easily raised his hand and pressed it against Alice's forehead, leaving her unable to move an inch; she could only express her protest by constantly grinding her teeth. "Ha, you still want to bite me? How naive~" "Merlin! I'll fight you to the death!" Alice glared, having cursed Merlin countless times in her heart. Merlin snorted coldly, shoved Alice onto the bed, and said, "Behave, you filthy woman, don't force me to get rough." "Ouch!" Alice cried as Merlin's toss hurt her; instantly a surge of resentment filled her heart, she turned and shouted, "Merlin! You bastard king...." Before Alice could finish her tirade, Merlin suddenly lunged forward, pressing the flailing Alice beneath him, his expression turning serious: "Shhh! If you don't want to die, keep quiet...." "Ah???" Alice's gaze went blank as she looked at Merlin's stern, serious demeanor, seemingly returning to his usual attitude, which made her somewhat regain her senses: Could it be that he has something he fears others hearing, hence his harshness toward her? Strangely, he's gotten close with the barbarians, acting as if they're not acquainted... Could Merlin be deliberately hiding something? Only when alone can he speak the truth? novel Alice furrowed her brows, watching Merlin press her down; her cheeks flushed, her eyes darting about. "...What...?" Merlin glanced furtively outside the tent, then lowered his head to whisper near Alice's ear: "If you stay quiet, I can untie your ropes; if you refuse to cooperate, neither of us will benefit." "...Mmm~~~" Alice felt her ears heat up, waves of hot air blowing on them made her whole body itch, her mind went blank, unable to think. They rarely were this close; under Merlin's male hormonal aura, she felt like a startled fawn, her heart pounding. "Huh?" Merlin noticed Alice trembling beneath him, her face flushed, eyes shut, not speaking: "What's wrong? Can't you hear me?" Alice barely regained composure, desperately suppressing her agitation, only hoping Merlin wouldn't stay on top of her, otherwise her thoughts would be a mess: "I... I know..." "Alright, don't cause trouble..." Merlin emphasized again, reaching his hand beneath her, feeling around a few times, and undid the tight ropes binding her. As soon as Alice regained freedom, her long-suppressed fury surged up; she grabbed Merlin's throat: "Merlin! You actually treated me like that..." novel Merlin's face changed in alarm; he quickly pinned Alice's flailing hands, while his other hand instinctively slipped into her clothing!?!? "Merlin! .......Alice stared at this scene, dumbfounded, never imagining Merlin would grope her!" In fact, Alice had overthought it; Merlin merely pulled out the magical chest pad from her clothing and, out of curiosity, gave it a couple of squeezes— "Oh? So this is how it feels, like a water-filled balloon..." "!!!" Alice's face turned crimson with disbelief; her private item was in Merlin's hand, being toyed with, the immense shame made her explode on the spot: "...Give it back! You pervert!" "Ah? Say another insult and I'll listen?" Merlin pressed Alice, rendering her immobile, his eyes full of provocation. "Lewd... cry?!!" Alice hadn't finished speaking when Merlin shoved the magical chest pad into her mouth to stop her tongue. Aside from when Merlin two years ago conscripted her as a laborer to row a boat, Alice had never suffered such humiliation; she instantly struggled, wanting to fight Merlin to the death! murmur!!! "You had a chance and didn't take it? Then don't blame me—just stay tied up." Merlin sighed, picked up the rope, and retied the uncooperative Alice; at least this way she wouldn't cause him trouble. It seems Merlin went a bit overboard; now Alice is fuming, so he can only explain the situation first, then consider untying her. Merlin brushed dust off his hands, slowly rose, and looked at Alice with sympathy: "Since you won't cooperate honestly, just stay like this for now; when you calm down, I'll untie your ropes...." murmur! murmur murmur!!! The tightly bound Alice rolled her eyes in anger, writhing on the grass bed like a silkworm pupa. Now she couldn't even speak; she was just a petty little sulker, full of grievance but powerless. Merlin leisurely grabbed a chair from beside, sat butt-first facing Alice, then grinned at her: "I know you're full of doubts now, thinking I'm a traitor who bullied you along the way; you must hate me to death by now." murmur! Alice nodded heavily, not hiding her feelings. "Haha~" Merlin stroked his chin, smirking: "Great, why do I inexplicably feel pleased whenever I see you angry?" Alice gave Merlin a huge eye-roll, nearly fainting from anger. "However you think, I did these things out of necessity." Merlin paused, showing a helpless expression: "Of course, this is merely a temporary measure; a true man knows when to yield and when to stand firm; only those who laugh last are victors. You surely don't think my character would be to grovel and kneel, becoming one of the barbarians, do you?" "..." Alice's face was expressionless; she thought Merlin's temperament had changed drastically—there must be another reason—but his unbridled bullying of her was actually him taking revenge? ! Too much! "I've already contacted that chieftain; his strength on this island is absolutely dominion-level. Wanting to complete this trial by killing that chieftain, the difficulty is likely no less than an ordinary person challenging a Saint-tier powerhouse." Merlin lowered his gaze to his hands, dejectedly saying: "Since arriving on the island, my power has been severely weakened; outside, that chieftain would be nothing before me, but here, in direct confrontation, there's basically no chance of victory—not even my demon sword Banri Garan remains mine; that little dwarf has claimed it for himself." Alice fell silent, her eyes flickering, recalling the message left by Senior Seysi: this island bears a terrifying holy aura, its suppressive effect on dark beings is most evident; indeed even Merlin couldn't escape it. "Even if we joined forces in our current state, trying to defeat that chieftain head‑on would be nearly impossible." Merlin paused, lowered his voice, speaking mysteriously: "So, to complete the trial.... we must resort to underhanded tactics; do you understand what I mean? @"

title: Chapter 35 — The Dagger Unveiled②
content:
Chapter 35 — The Dagger Unveiled②

Volume 28 · Chapter 35

Alice, who was tightly bound, gradually calmed down, realizing that Merlin was treating her this way because he had his own plan to complete the trial. But the bullying she suffered on the way was Merlin's fault—clearly he was taking the opportunity to bully her for fun. Alice thought about it, and facing Merlin's questioning, she could only nod, indicating she basically understood the situation. "That's right, so don't blame me for bullying you on the way..." Merlin rubbed the black soot on his face and said in a helpless tone, "It's all to throw people off the scent. You and I are both outsiders; if I'm too nice to you, these savages will get suspicious." "You don't know how much effort I put into gaining the chief's trust, letting him lower his guard." "I don't want my plan ruined by your noise and fuss—otherwise all my previous effort would be wasted." Given Merlin's personality, he would never bow and scrape to anyone; that would be an insult to him. But when Merlin was a child, his family was destroyed and he wandered with his sister Lilith, enduring humiliation and hardship far worse than now. To escape the island and kill the chief to complete the promotion trial, brute force head-on is useless. Alice's eyes rolled, she blinked repeatedly, realizing Merlin's intent and gradually grew quieter. "Actually, I didn't know you were in that village. I was just going to grab anyone at random, but I ended up finding you~" Merlin gave Alice a meaningful look. "Since that's the case, things are easier now. You just need to cooperate with me from inside and outside; we have a seventy percent chance of defeating that chief. As for the remaining savages, they're just a leaderless rabble—not worth worrying about." Alice fell silent, pondering Merlin's "inside and outside cooperation," but unsure how to do it, so she asked, "Um?" Merlin stepped up to Alice, pointed at her nose, and said, "I've already told you the general plan. You should know our current situation. If we don't cooperate well, we might never leave this island. If you understand, blink your eyes." Alice thought, then blinked rapidly, her eyelashes fluttering, eager to properly "communicate" with Merlin. "Very well, I warn you—don't mess around." Merlin reminded her again, then took out the chest pad from Alice's mouth and untied the ropes. "Awooo!!!" Having just gained freedom, Alice became dishonest, seizing the chance to open her mouth and bite Merlin's hand hard. Just as Alice felt pleased, finally letting out a breath... she discovered Merlin showed no reaction, not even a cry of pain, as if he had expected it all along? Alice curiously lifted her eyelids, seeing Merlin expressionlessly gazing at her, speaking in a weary tone. "Feeling better? Did that vent your anger? If not, you can just... " Alice felt embarrassed, seeing Merlin's casual bullying demeanor, her resentment largely faded. She wasn't necessarily looking to cause trouble for Merlin; it was just that her butt was about to get roasted over the campfire, and she held a grudge... Alice released her bite, raised her fists and hammered Merlin's chest several times, then crossed her arms angrily and fell silent. Merlin curled his lip, wiped the saliva from his hand, and said seriously, "You don't appreciate good intentions. I'm giving you a lesson, actually saving you—do you know the savages' custom? They eat anyone who defies the chief's rule; only the obedient survive. If it weren't for me, you'd already be skewered over the fire and roasted~" "Then... Alice was at a loss for words, dissatisfied, muttering, 'You can't treat me like this—no conscience—I thought you had betrayed me.' 'Heh... Merlin smirked, 'If I liked betraying, you'd have been sold off by me several times already, maybe even counting my money for me.' 'Shut up, I'm going to bite you!' Alice bared her teeth, ready to try. 'No, let's talk properly.' Merlin paused, then continued seriously, 'You already understand what I intend to do, so I need you to cooperate with me.' 'How should I cooperate?' Alice asked, thinking Merlin usually acts arrogantly and recklessly, but this is the first time she's seen him so methodical—perhaps the island's mysterious suppressive force really gives him a headache. 'I've earned the chief's trust and can stay close to him. During this time I didn't just learn the savages' language; I also learned some things.' Merlin said solemnly. 'Oh? I thought you'd just be wearing grass skirts and dancing around the fire with the savages...' Alice remained expressionless, thinking this was normal for Merlin. 'What do you think I'm taking you for? Looking down on me?' Merlin gave Alice a sideways glance. 'That chief is mysterious; every so often he needs to hold a sacrificial ritual at the deepest altar of the temple, so he goes around capturing young women, slashing open their chests with a knife, and eating their hearts. I and these savages go out raiding for this very purpose—to help the chief find young women for sacrifice.' Alice froze, staring into Merlin's eyes. 'You... you don't intend to offer me as a sacrifice, do you?' 'Exactly! You're really sharp~' Merlin's grin grew wild, praising Alice's comprehension. '......' Alice's face darkened, she gritted her teeth and said, 'I don't believe you! I'm not going!' 'You're just pretending to be a sacrifice—don't be so rigid, okay?' Merlin frowned, seeing Alice unwilling to cooperate, and quickly tried sweet talk: 'How could I harm my own wife and offer you up? It's all just to get out of this damned place.' Alice's face flushed, her heartbeat quickened, she raised her small fist as if to punch, shouting, 'Who—who is your wife?' 'In name only.' Merlin raised his eyebrows. Alice's forehead veins bulged, she jumped twice, then slammed a heavy punch into Merlin's chest, shouting, 'Go die!' 'Even if I'm only your nominal wife, I can't harm you—our revolutionary friendship will last forever, comrade!' Merlin clenched his fist, resolute, then leaned toward Alice, blinking his eyes. 'If you don't believe me, take a look at my pure little eyes—are they genuine or not?' 'Got eye gunk, disgusting...' Alice rolled her eyes. 'Ah, sorry, I've been having insomnia lately...' Merlin rubbed his eyes, cleared his throat to hide his embarrassment—'Anyway, as long as you cooperate with me, we can still kill that chief.' 'I'll bring you before the chief; when the sacrificial ceremony takes place, that'll be the best moment to strike.' 'We'll team up, chop off that little guy's head—you think that's awesome, huh~?' (?+

title: Chapter 36 — The Dagger Revealed ③ (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 36 — The Dagger Revealed ③ (Bonus)

Volume 28 · Chapter 36

Alice let out a light hum, speaking nonchalantly, “No need to team up, I can handle it myself.” “Ah?” Merlin frowned, “Who gave you that confidence? Didn’t you hear me speaking? That chief, it seems he has the power to enlarge himself; with our current state, if we don’t team up for a sneak attack we simply can’t oppose him.” “Really?” Alice took out a holy spirit medicine device from her bosom, shaking it in front of Merlin~. “What is it?” Merlin asked doubtfully. Alice told Merlin the full story of the holy spirit potion left by Seysi. After listening, Merlin took the potion and examined it, holding it as if it were a treasure, his eyes almost popping out. On this island, a bottle of potion that can restore one’s strength is extremely precious; even if its effect works only once, it is worth a fortune. This potion can solve the most troubling problem for adventurers taking the trial—being unable to unleash their own strength—and from this alone one can see its unparalleled value. “You’re not talking nonsense, are you? This potion can let a person recover strength once on the island?” Merlin looked at the potion in his hand, feeling a bit suspicious, as if he had obtained a cheat device. “Believe it or not, I’m not lying; this is something Seysi senior left behind in the village when she participated in the trial.” Alice said, huffing. “That old woman’s medicine…. Merlin believed a few points, still deeply trusting the old witch’s alchemy skills, ‘If it really works, why not let me drink it? I could split the whole island.’ cc. “You’re not supposed to follow the plan?” Alice teased. “If I could use the drawing‑slash sword, the plan would be meaningless; I’d just rush in.” Merlin said confidently. Alice shrugged her shoulders, thinking indeed as she had expected—Merlin was willing to proceed step by step according to the plan, only acting when trouble arose. “Seysi senior’s note said this potion contains rare artificially made holy spirit blood; can you really drink it?” “What nonsense, why can’t I drink it?” Merlin pulled the potion stopper, brought it to his nose to sniff, then immediately rolled his eyes, “My goodness, what is this? It’s disgusting; I feel I’d die if I drank it.” .. “I already told you, there’s artificially made holy spirit blood; you, a demon, definitely can’t use it, right?” Alice sighed. “This smell makes me nauseous, I can’t stand it; you have it.” Merlin replaced the stopper and returned the holy spirit potion to Alice one by one. “Since we have this bottle of potion, things become much easier; I will assist you from the side to defeat the chief.” “As for now?” “We keep putting on a show for those barbarians to watch.” “What act?” Alice looked utterly confused. “According to barbarian custom, when encountering an unwilling offering, the strongest warrior must conquer them before they can be presented to the chief.” Merlin paused, then said solemnly, “So to avoid arousing suspicion among the outside barbarians, I need to conquer you tonight—you’re an adult, you should understand.” “...Con‑con‑con‑quer!?” Alice was frightened, her face flushing red, she instinctively tugged at her skirt, “What nonsense are you spouting?! I warn you, don’t mess around… if you… if you… please… my…” “Pa—” a sharp sound interrupted Alice’s thoughts; she dazedly lifted her head, seeing Merlin slapping his own thigh with his palm. Pat‑pat, pat‑pat‑pat‑pat‑pat‑pat— Merlin expressionlessly slapped his thigh, accompanied by a steady rhythm that grew increasingly intense. “Cry, quickly cry, Alice, the sadder the better—like being bullied yet unable to resist, feeling humiliated.” “What?!?” Alice’s face was blank, completely unaware of what Merlin was doing, only feeling embarrassed! “Do it for those barbarians outside to hear; as long as you cry, it proves I’m conquering you, so they’ll feel reassured; otherwise tomorrow might cause trouble.” Merlin said sternly, not joking. Both of us are outsiders; if we spend the whole night in harmony, those barbarians will inevitably suspect something. If tomorrow someone secretly tells the chief, Merlin’s plan might not go as smoothly as imagined. “...I won’t be able to?” Alice felt a bit flustered, thinking Merlin’s request strange. “Tsk!” Merlin clicked his tongue lowly, “Think back to how I treated you before—that enslavement of you rowing for three days and three nights, that humiliation—do you recall it?” “......Alice watched Merlin slap his thigh repeatedly, pat‑pat‑pat, and could only try to cry a little— “Sniffle?” Outside, the barbarians sneakily gathered at the edge of the tent, under the cover of night they seemed to have become invisible, only able to see their constantly grinning big white teeth. When they heard the pat‑pat‑pat sounds and Alice’s crying from inside, the barbarians all showed grim grins and raised their thumbs— “Still the first warrior is awesome~” Early the next morning, Merlin led Alice out of the tent. Alice wore an unwilling expression, while Merlin bore the victor’s posture, smiling and waving at the other barbarians. The barbarians chatted with eyebrows flying, their envious eyes undisguised, truly believing the first warrior had conquered a foreign woman last night. Merlin wanted these temple guards to believe he had already conquered Alice and could directly take her to see the chief. Thus he placed his hand dishonestly on Alice’s shoulder, pulling her close, like the barbarians displaying that she was now his property. Alice felt a bit unable to bear it, and instinctively blurted, “What are you doing!?” As soon as she said that, the scene fell silent; the temple guards looked at Merlin with suspicion. Alice’s resistant attitude aroused the barbarians’ doubts, wondering if last night Merlin hadn’t followed the rules. Merlin’s smile stiffened on his face, a bit embarrassed as he quietly said, “Alice, cooperate a bit—the chief won’t allow dangerous persons near him.” “....Alice wanted to speak but held back, looking at the doubtful gazes of the barbarians before her, she could only force a smile that didn’t reach her eyes, resting her head against Merlin’s chest, feigning a dead‑hearted appearance. In fact Alice wasn’t resisting; it’s just that everything is fake now, making her feel a bit unhappy. Alice actually wanted to be affectionate with Merlin, but this guy completely lacks romance, the psychological gap is enormous! The barbarians saw Alice yesterday like a little wildcat, today docile, and firmly believed in Merlin’s—this first‑warrior’s—‘ability’. They raised their thumbs, lavishing praise without reserve, already regarding Merlin as a loyal warrior of the temple. “Norala la mukua (you’re brave)!” .....Merlin gave a dry laugh, secretly letting out a breath—how much suffering he endured last night, only he knows. Nonsense! Could I not be brave? Both my thighs have been slapped red and swollen by myself, and they’re still trembling now! (缶。云)

title: Chapter 37 — Victory or Defeat
content:
Chapter 37 — Victory or Defeat

Volume 28 · Chapter 37

The raiding party returned to the temple, and Merlin, as the first Hero, received a warm welcome from the Chieftain. Women in attendance danced to the music, their lively rhythms infectious to every single person. As the island's ruler, the Chieftain repeatedly offered to pour wine for Merlin with great enthusiasm, clearly admiring him. In truth, the Chieftain was simply pleased to have one more useful dog at his side. He had initially suspected Merlin wasn't truly loyal, so he planted several spies among them. After hearing the reports from the spies, he finally relaxed his guard around this outsider. On the way there, Merlin had clearly shown his dedication and loyalty to the Chieftain, which was likely the only way these savages would stay on their guard. Merlin was somewhat distracted, thinking about how to kill the Chieftain during the sacrifice and how to assist Alice. "Ka-ku ba ya, lu-lu ye ba ka (My Hero, what are you thinking?)" the dwarf Chieftain asked curiously, noticing Merlin's absent-mindedness. Merlin didn't answer but flashed a friendly smile and quickly bowed to offer a toast, behaving very obediently. The dwarf Chieftain laughed it off, assuming Merlin wasn't yet familiar with the savages' language and didn't take it to heart. Merlin's face was bright with a smile, his eyes already fixed on the Banri Garan sword at the Chieftain's waist, thinking, "Smile, tomorrow is your day of death..." Late at night, Merlin went to the prison where Alice was held, guarded by several temple sentries who feared the sacrifice might escape. In the cage, Alice looked gloomy, having expected that being quiet would grant him freedom, but after coming to the temple with Merlin, he still had to remain in the cage. This left Alice feeling somewhat dissatisfied, though he wasn't worried Merlin would betray him as a pervert, he couldn't help but feel uneasy. Alice looked up at the magnificent pyramid under the moonlight, this building filled with mystery, its dark interior impossible to decipher what lay within. "Gu-lu lu." Alice's stomach rumbled; he hadn't eaten anything all day. Hunger made him dizzy and lightheaded, even prompting thoughts of gnawing his fingernails. He felt embarrassed, thinking, "Merlin really isn't considerate, leaving me here while he goes off to feast, does he even have any food for me?" Alice lay down in the cage, boredly staring at the sky, starting to count stars, hoping to distract himself from the hunger. Merlin quietly approached, ordered several temple guards to leave, and took over Alice's watch alone. The guards nodded and complied, staying nearby but not too far away, continuing to monitor. Merlin looked at Alice in the cage, who was counting stars with his fingers, completely unaware of his arrival. He then pulled out a large chicken leg from his belongings, waving it in front of Alice. "Yum yum!?" Alice sat up immediately upon smelling it, the fragrant aroma lingering in his nose, making his mouth water. "You're pretty honest, I thought you'd be bawling and screaming in that cage, greeting all your ancestors for eighteen generations~" Merlin grinned, satisfied with Alice's behavior. "Stop wasting time, just give it to me, I'm starving!" Alice angrily said, reaching out from the cage to pull at Merlin. "I'll just call out 'Dad,' I've heard that~" Merlin couldn't help but start teasing Alice. "You're dreaming! My face turned red with anger, retorting, "I'm actively cooperating with you, do you have time to mess with me? If you let me get in my way, I'll treat you the same way!" "Hey!" Merlin felt a chill down his spine, recalling how Alice had often bullied him as a child, maybe it would happen again, so he quickly waved it off, "Here you go, don't think I'm mistreating you, look at your prickly little self~" "Hmph~!" Alice huffed, took the chicken leg, and started eating it, not caring about table manners in this situation. "Eat a bit, the sacrifice starts tomorrow morning," Merlin paused, speaking in a low voice to explain the sacrifice process, "I'll lead you to the altar. There'll only be you, me, and the Chieftain present. Once the altar doors close, that's when we strike." "Is that so? Could I defeat that Chieftain with my current strength?" Alice had never seen the "deity" among the savages, so he wasn't clear on the specifics. "Should be nine times out of ten...," Merlin's voice wavered slightly, no longer as resolute as usual. Alice raised an eyebrow, puzzled, asking tentatively, "You mean... you don't have a solid plan?" "This island reeks of a disturbing aura everywhere, making me feel utterly uncomfortable, like..." Merlin took a deep breath, furrowing his brow, "Like living in a huge prison, very oppressive." "Especially the depths of this temple..." The sun had just broken through the horizon when the Chieftain impatiently began the sacrifice ritual. Merlin carried Alice, bound with ropes, leading him toward the deepest altar within the temple. Alice's hands were tied up, showing a deadpan expression of someone who'd given up all hope of resistance, but inside he was plotting to kill the Chieftain. As a first-timer in the temple, Alice curiously looked around, noticing strange characters on the walls, feeling a strange sense of familiarity. This sense of déjà vu made him feel as if he'd seen it yesterday, though he couldn't explain what the wall writings meant. The deeper they went into the temple, the more Alice felt his heart racing, the stairs seemed endless, beneath the magnificent pyramid temple lay something even grander! The stone doors slowly opened, pushed by the temple guards. Merlin led Alice into the altar chamber, which was a resurrection altar. In the center was a black, bottomless pit that reeked of putrid blood, making one sick to the stomach! The terrifying pit seemed to be the heart of the entire temple, faint ghostly sobs echoing from the depths. The altar platform held a long-cold girl's corpse, her lifeless eyes staring at the ceiling in a expression of terror. The dwarf Chieftain's knife sliced through the corpse's chest, the sound of the incision made everyone's hair stand on end! The dwarf Chieftain held his hands cupped, presenting a slightly beating heart, tilted his head back, and with his mask automatically opening, he swallowed the girl's heart whole, even licking his lips as if savoring a delicious meal! It was clear that Alice was the next sacrifice, facing the same fate. Merlin and Alice's faces turned pale, having underestimated this savage leader's bloodthirstiness! The doors of the altar slowly closed, Merlin realized an opportunity, silently cutting the ropes binding Alice's hands, and handing the light sword to him. The satisfied Chieftain wiped his mouth clean, pushed the previous sacrifice's body into the abyss below, devoured it completely, and prepared for the next delicious meal. But just as the dwarf Chieftain turned around, he saw Alice holding the sword, her eyes filled with malice. He couldn't understand, where had his Hero gone? Why was a sacrifice wielding a sword in the sacred altar? "Lu-lu ka!?" Merlin leaped from the shadows onto the altar, quickly embracing the dwarf Chieftain from behind, immobilizing him completely, creating the perfect conditions for Alice to strike, then shouting, "Alice! Attack!" Success or failure lies here.

title: Chapter 38 — Altar Abyss
content:
Chapter 38 — Altar Abyss

Volume 28 · Chapter 38

“Alice! ! !” Merlin roared,

The opportunity vanished in a flash.

If not caught, who knows what power this seemingly small dwarf chief harbors?

Merlin had seen with his own eyes, a mountain-like iron fist, even with greatly suppressed strength, probably only a sudden surprise attack, hitting the opponent before they could react, might have a chance to win!

“I know!”

Alice finished the Holy Spirit potion in her hand, threw the bottle to the ground and smashed it to pieces, thinking—

There is only one chance, I can only use magic or martial arts once.

If it fails, I and Merlin can only here with the enemy fight to the death like a beast in a cage!

Alice felt the potion in her abdomen like a flame burning fiercely, long-lost power quickly revived, gradually filling her entire body.

Golden douqi and magic power burst forth simultaneously, like a floodgate opening, unstoppable!

Alice gripped the slender sword in her hand, killing intent showed in her eyes, leaping from the ground, in a flash of lightning, she killed in front of the dwarf chief.

“Drink!

Alice shouted angrily, like a goddess descending, her majestic and sacred voice ringing, making people's eardrums hum.

Saint-tier magic power and battle aura all gathered on the sword blade, instantly erupting in a blinding ten-thousand-foot light!

Alice gritted her teeth, the Holy Spirit potion's effect was surprisingly potent, she could already feel her power receding like a tide again.

Fortunately, Alice seized the opportunity, at the last moment, thrusting the sword named "Radiant Lament" out everything happened too fast and suddenly, by the time the dwarf chief came to his senses, he was already plunged into extreme peril, with death but no life!

The dwarf chief tried to struggle and escape, but Merlin held him tight, unable to move, the whole person seeming to become a target?

“No one can make me submit, you are no exception Merlin's devilish voice came out, the dwarf chief's face turned ashen, his eyes overflowing with intense hatred, muttering some unintelligible nonsense.

Just when Alice's sword blade was less than two nail widths from the dwarf chief's eyes—

“Boom!

A huge explosion sound rang out, divine white light was blindingly dazzling, the entire underground altar was ravaged by the shockwave, becoming precarious!

Merlin only felt a wave of heat assault him, his body unable to withstand, flew backward heavily, crashing into the wall.

Luckily the altar was sturdy enough, otherwise it would have been destroyed in the explosion already.

....What?

Merlin dragged his sore body up slowly, lifting his head yet seeing a-

Giant, sturdy pure white body, filling the entire space.

Behind it, huge white wings, radiating a sacred aura.

Due to the limited space of the altar, the wings could not unfold, difficult to reappear the imposing manner from the first face!

Looking at the suddenly appearing nearly 200-foot giant before him, Merlin's pupils shrank, his heart pounding wildly.

Up close, invisible pressure could even make an ordinary person go mad on the spot, completely losing combat capability of course, purely being big is not enough to make Merlin act strangely, he had killed monsters bigger than the one in front of him.

Merlin acted strangely because he finally saw the giant's true form up close, a title emerging from deep within—

“Holy Spirit!

A creature from the heavens, a slave created by the Goddess of Light Maria, the most loyal guardian of the heavens, almost all possessing terrifying strength.

Whether strength or potential, they far surpass any race in the mundane world, the most perfect beings created by the goddess.

At the same time, also enemies of the demon race, the stars that demons fear, the main force of the heavens in the holy war....

When Merlin saw this Holy Spirit giant at that moment, even though the demon blood in his body was extremely thin, he still aroused boundless fighting intent, and a strong desire to kill the other. This is the instinct of a demon, from distant ancestors' call, constantly driving them to kill.

Every drop of Merlin's blood was agitated, like boiling water about to boil, completely different from the Holy Spirit corpse he had seen before, this one is alive!

The Holy Spirit giant slightly moved his body, but alas, the altar space was limited, fundamentally unable to fully accommodate his huge body, the ground always trembling.

The red eyes behind his mask gazed at the hand-sized Alice in front of him, reflecting her silhouette.

The Holy Spirit giant grabbed Alice with one hand, and supported the ground with the other, spitting out clusters of turbid air, apparently a simple-minded, four-limbed developed tool-type Holy Spirit.

“..... Prison Warden of the Exile, Buru

“Sin, accept... baptism, towards.

Goddess

“Confession.

The Holy Spirit giant didn't know what he was babbling about?

Discontinuous and completely unintelligible, like a robot with a broken program.

Alice fell into terror, her mind went blank, not even knowing the guy in front was a Holy Spirit: I have sin? What sin do I have? Were those girls who had their hearts cut out guilty? What a joke..

Alice gritted her teeth, beginning to struggle frantically, but the effect of the Holy Spirit potion from Cersi had already dissipated, resisting the Holy Spirit giant was sheer madness.

“Let me go! You bastard! You can only run rampant here, what's the point!"

....."..

The Holy Spirit giant fell silent, the gaze behind his mask calm, but suddenly increased his strength, beginning to punish Alice.

The power of splitting mountains and crushing stone began to squeeze Alice, on the Holy Spirit giant's hand, she was like an ant that could be casually crushed!

If it were outside, Alice had the capability to contend with the Holy Spirit giant.

But here, in the prison of the exiled god-spirit servants, even the ability to reach the heavens would be suppressed, no wonder it's rumored to be a place used to imprison angels.

“Ahhhhhhhhh) xianxia novel.

Alice wailed upwards, the great pain making her expression twist, all her bones making crackling sounds.

Who knows how many bones were broken under the Holy Spirit giant's "light" pinch?

Alice only felt her body pressed by several more great mountains, terrifying power ravaging, making her consciousness hazy even prone to dissipation.

“Alice! ?’

Merlin urgently called out, in his anxiety, he didn't have time to think much, his body moving involuntarily.

If nothing is done? Alice might very well be squeezed to death alive by the Holy Spirit giant!

Merlin enduring the soreness all over his body, flipping over the altar platform, taking the giant's dissection knife handy, gripping it tightly.

Then Merlin glared angrily, tracing along the giant's foot sole, pulling leg hair, climbing all the way up, fiercely stabbing the dagger in his hand toward the giant's knee, only hearing “pu ti”

“Wuuu wuuu wuuu!!!”

Pain came, the Holy Spirit giant thought he was stung by a bee momentarily, instantly falling into a rage, his arms wide open, crazy and disorderly, bringing up gale-force winds.

The Holy Spirit giant looked down, Merlin hanging on his knee, holding a dagger, instantly becoming furious!

Under the Holy Spirit giant's anger, Alice was thrown into the altar's deep abyss!

Alice's face was blank, her body uncontrollably falling into the terrifying abyss, everything irrecoverable one-

“Merlin!

Alice

title: Chapter 39 — Fierce Battle
content:
Chapter 39 — Fierce Battle

Volume 28 · Chapter 39

Merlin watched helplessly as Alice fell into the abyss, unable to stop her. He didn't know what dangers lay in that bottomless pit, but he knew that every time the Spirit Giant sacrificed a victim, it would toss the corpse down there, as if the space were infinite and could never be filled. Merlin didn't know whether Alice was dead or alive after falling into the abyss, and the current situation was beyond his expectations.

"Aaahhh!"

Enraged, the Spirit Giant threw Alice into the abyss, then noticed Merlin, the traitor who had dared to treat this foreigner kindly. How could it not hate him? It wanted to flay this foreigner alive and tear him apart limb from limb!

The Spirit Giant raised its massive palm and brought it crashing down on Merlin's knees, intent on killing him.

"You! Are guilty!!!"

Merlin was preoccupied with Alice's situation and hadn't been paying attention to his surroundings. Here, unlike the outside world, a mysterious force suppressing strength would turn anyone who set foot on this island into a fragile ordinary person. Outside, Merlin and Alice could rely on their own power to deal with most enemies, but here they had to be cautious even against hordes of barbarians. No wonder so many powerful adventurers failed the trial. It wasn't that everyone possessed the talent of an ant envying an elephant.

By the time Merlin realized what was happening, the Spirit Giant's attack had already reached him. It was too late to dodge as the massive iron palm slammed toward him, blocking out the sky. Merlin's face was ashen, and the violent wind pressure made his cheeks spasm. He gritted his teeth and endured the blow.

In an instant, the tiny Merlin was sent flying by the Spirit Giant's iron palm, crashing to the ground like a cannonball, leaving a trail of blood droplets in midair. Before the Spirit Giant, Merlin looked pitifully small. They were simply not on the same level.

"......"

Merlin's bones were nearly broken as he pulled himself up from the ground, wiping blood from the corner of his mouth. That slap alone was enough to knock out half of Merlin's life force.

Looking at the enormous Spirit Giant before him, even Merlin felt a trace of helplessness and cursed himself for coming to this cursed place. The Spirit Giant loomed over Merlin like an ant, its throat rumbling like thunder.

"Kneel, sinner."

Merlin glanced at the furious Spirit Giant, then at the bottomless abyss, and broke into a grim smile.

"...Heh heh..."

"Kneel?"

"You're not worthy."

"You're just a worm from the heavens, nothing more than a guard dog here."

"Even if your master came personally, he wouldn't be this arrogant!"

Furious, the Spirit Giant's mask cracked, and the muscles on its pure white body tensed like stone. It was enraged by Merlin's disrespectful words—how dare someone scorn the almighty Goddess? Such heretics must die!

Roaring, the Spirit Giant raised both iron fists, combining them into one, and golden bracelets on its wrists erupted with blinding light, radiating an intimidating aura.

"Sinner! Die!!!"

"Bang!" With a tremendous crash, the Spirit Giant's iron fist descended like divine retribution, hammering the earth.

In an instant, the ground shook and a massive crater was blasted into the earth. It turned out the altar was suspended in midair above the abyss, no different from a city floating in the sky.

Fortunately, despite the Spirit Giant's massive size, its speed was somewhat sluggish. Merlin, with his small and nimble body, could still spar with this brute. He couldn't check on Alice's condition or escape, so he had no choice but to fight the Spirit Giant to the death on the altar. Only by killing the Spirit Giant would he have a chance to leave the temple alive.

Merlin tightly gripped his dagger, darting and weaving with agility, constantly evading the Spirit Giant's attacks. The Spirit Giant grew larger and angrier, while Merlin buzzed around it like an annoying fly.

It wasn't a great threat, but it was certainly irritating!

The Spirit Giant roared and howled, gradually losing its composure, swinging its iron fists wildly and smashing the altar in a rage, desperate to tear Merlin apart.

Merlin's eyes narrowed, sensing an opportunity. He quickly climbed onto the Spirit Giant's body and raced across its massive form.

"Huh?"

Enraged, the Spirit Giant raised its palm and began to strike itself, slapping itself repeatedly until its whole body itched unbearably. This futile tactic of hurting itself while harming no one was exactly what Merlin had been waiting for. Even though their strength gap was enormous, there was still room to maneuver.

Merlin climbed onto the Spirit Giant's face and leaped up, no longer hiding, but directly plunging his dagger into the Spirit Giant's eye!

"Go blind!"

With a "squelch," the dagger pierced the flesh, and the Spirit Giant let out an earsplitting wail, clutching its bleeding eye and rolling on the ground. Its massive body tumbled and rolled, threatening to bring the entire altar crashing down.

"Sinner! Sinner! Cursed thing! Die! Die!"

Hearing the Spirit Giant's wail, Merlin felt the situation spiraling out of control. He tried to move away from the brute, but as fate would have it, the Spirit Giant's wild swing accidentally struck him.

"How?!" Merlin was stunned. His fragile body cracked with a "snap," bones breaking as he was slammed into the ground.

The Spirit Giant's remaining eye rolled around wildly, spotting Merlin lying on the ground like a piece of mud. It opened its mouth in a grotesque grin.

It hadn't expected that after all this struggle, it still couldn't catch Merlin, only to accidentally catch this novel. The Spirit Giant raised its combined fists again, its pure white body radiating sacred light, and brought its twisted form down upon the wounded Merlin.

"You! Are guilty!!!"

"...h..."

Merlin was battered all over, his internal organs bruised, his body heavy with pain. He could barely stand as the devastating blow descended, the fierce wind pressure threatening to shatter his very soul.

Merlin sighed deeply, glanced at the bottomless abyss in the distance, and broke into a grim smile, saying:

"For years, I've roamed the world, undefeated wherever I went."

"Yet in the end, I never expected..."

"I would be tripped up by a worm from the heavens."

With a tremendous rumble, the earth shook and the heavens were struck. Merlin, unfortunately, failed to evade the Spirit Giant's fatal blow.

The massive hammer fell, and golden light soared into the sky, tearing the earth apart and reaching toward the heavens.

The sturdy pyramid outside cracked and splintered, nearly collapsing.

The ignorant barbarians, witnessing this spectacular scene, trembled in fear and knelt in worship, utterly awed by the "god's" power.

This was the absolute authority of the warden. For a mortal to challenge a god was nothing more than a joke.

title: Chapter 40 — Light's Liberation (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 40 — Light's Liberation (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 28 · Chapter 40

"Merlin!!!"

In the unfathomably deep abyss, Alice plummeted rapidly downward, growing ever farther from the glowing entrance, until she dissolved into countless specks of starlight.

A howling gale swept past Alice's ears, drowning out all other sounds. She couldn't tell how long she had been falling.

Alice could only clearly sense that with each passing moment of her descent, the scent of blood grew thicker—making it hard to breathe.

What should she do? Was she really going to die from this fall?

But this abyss seemed bottomless. How much longer would she keep falling...

Alice's heart raced. She had underestimated the abyss's depth and vastness, far beyond her imagination.

This made Alice wonder: what exactly was being held captive in this pitch-black abyss? Was it merely a morgue for sacrifices?

A flicker of light danced in the dark abyss, like a lone star in the deep night sky, radiating a sacred glow.

As Alice continued to fall, she felt waves of divine breath washing over her like ocean tides—

That... what is that thing?

With the help of the sacred light, Alice finally managed to make out the scene below.

Countless black chains crisscrossed, weaving into a chaotic, massive net.

The chains intertwined in endless complexity, making it impossible to discern where they originated. Yet the core of the chain-net was clearly visible.

Each chain was bound to something—a pair of broken saintly wings, pure white and unmarred, constantly dispelling the darkness of the abyss.

Below lay a mountain of bones, densely packed. She couldn't imagine how many people that giant saintly spirit had killed.

The pair of sacred wings had no master, as if torn off by force, with dried flesh still clinging to the bone ends.

The closer Alice drew to the saintly wings, the more she felt an oppressive pressure tenfold stronger than anything outside, making it hard to breathe, her chest as if weighed down by a boulder.

Was this the source of the island's mysterious suppression?

Incredible... it was these pure white wings...

Alice muttered in her heart, when suddenly a shrill ghostly wail echoed around her. The killed sacrifices had become vengeful spirits, gathering in groups and hovering through the abyss.

The vengeful spirits wailed and howled, sounding like newborns crying, rushing madly toward the falling Alice.

Countless vengeful spirits surged like a river, accompanied by a stench of blood, intent on killing any living being that entered the abyss.

"Ah!"

Alice panicked. If these spirits came for her, she wouldn't stand a chance—her soul would be devoured.

Fortunately, at that moment, the Light Sigh in Alice's hand erupted in a burst of sacred radiance, driving the spirits away.

These spirits, upon touching the lingering glow of the Light Sigh, scattered like mice before a cat.

Those who couldn't escape in time dissolved into wisps of smoke, vanishing completely.

The Fine Sword Light Sigh was naturally the bane of dark creatures. These spirits had picked the wrong prey.

Alice let out a sigh of relief, thinking she had survived—when suddenly the Light Sigh in her hand went out of control.

This had never happened before. Alice was terrified, wondering if her weapon had come to life.

"Hey! ...What are you doing!?"

The Light Sigh grabbed Alice and plunged at full speed toward the saintly wings bound by countless chains.

Alice was frightened, letting out a string of shrieks, her mind racing with wild thoughts. She was starting to doubt whether that thing was even her weapon.

"Ouch!"

The Light Sigh landed and slowed down, tossing Alice onto the ground, leaving its master covered in mud.

Alice quickly got up and spat out the mud, only to see her weapon, the Light Sigh, slowly approaching the pair of saintly wings.

The sacred wings emitted a warm glow, yet below them lay a mountain of bones—an entirely contradictory scene in a single frame.

The Light Sigh floated in midair, spinning in circles, and cleanly severed the chains binding the saintly wings.

Whoosh! The freed saintly wings unfurled, their light exploding a hundredfold! The magnificent wings caused the distant spirits to retreat in terror.

"...What just happened?" Alice's mind went blank, sitting there like a fool.

The Fine Sword Light Sigh began to spin, like a rapidly rotating top, whipping up a fierce vortex.

The saintly wings began to disintegrate, feathers falling one by one, merging into the magnificent whirlwind, accompanied by a brilliant flash of light.

When Alice opened her eyes again, a brand-new Fine Sword Light Sigh stood before her.

Beneath its originally ordinary appearance, it had become far more magnificent...

Golden sacred scriptures appeared on the blade, and the sword guard had transformed into two swirling wings. The entire fine sword had changed so drastically that Alice could no longer recognize it.

The new Light Sigh bathed in holy light descended slowly. Alice faintly heard the chimes of the heavens, nearly making her soul drift away.

The Light Sigh hovered before Alice, as if calling out to her.

With a hesitant heart, Alice reached out and grasped the new Light Sigh. Instantly, she felt a surge of heroic exhilaration, as if leading a grand cavalry charging across the battlefield.

The neighing of warhorses and the sparks of clashing weapons echoed faintly behind Alice, as an invincible host of saintly spirits materialized behind her.

They circled around the Light Sigh, and wherever the sword edges passed, all became scorched earth.

The spirits that had been swirling around, vanished on the spot—souls scattered, ascending to the heavens.

Alice clearly felt that after the pair of saintly wings disappeared, her strength gradually returned, and the mysterious suppressing force that had covered the entire island dissipated like smoke.

It seemed those wings were the source of everything, but they had already been absorbed by the Light Sigh...

Alice carefully examined her new weapon. Whether in luster or quality, it was now completely different, elevated beyond recognition. Her heart pounded wildly.

Was this a divine artifact?!

Outside, a golden light soared into the sky!

The entire pyramid temple collapsed under the giant saintly spirit's strike, caving in on itself!

Splintered stones sprayed from the altar, winds howled, leaving behind a scene of utter devastation.

The giant saintly spirit stood rigid, fists clenched, slamming them onto the ground, frozen in an odd pose—completely motionless.

Under the colossal weight of that giant fist, Merlin had one hand raised above his head, somehow resisting the enemy's fatal blow.

Merlin's single hand withstood the giant saintly spirit's iron fist, while his other hand was loosely clenched, his face etched with confusion.

Strange... had his strength returned? This was too sudden.

Merlin's head spun. The oppressive feeling he had been carrying seemed to have vanished. He wasn't sure what had just happened.

The giant saintly spirit's eyes behind the mask were uncertain. With his small brain, he couldn't possibly imagine why he couldn't kill such a tiny ant.

Merlin's face broke into a wicked grin. He threw a punch directly at the giant saintly spirit's clenched fist, meeting the bulky opponent head-on in a clash.

Crack! With a single blow, all ten fingers of the giant saintly spirit snapped and twisted, his palms revealing sharp white bones, and golden blood spurted out.

The giant saintly spirit let out a mournful wail, collapsing in agony onto the cold ground. The bones in his palms were likely shattered by Merlin's strike.

Merlin lowered his fist, blew off the dust, and his gaze turned sinister and cold. The primal desire to hunt saints burned ever stronger within him.

"The worms of the heavens... it seems..."

"You need to reacquaint yourself with me?"

title: Chapter 41 — Raphael's Holy Wings
content:
Chapter 41 — Raphael's Holy Wings

Volume 28 · Chapter 41

The giant spirit collapsed in agony upon the ground, his hand bones shattered, his head crushed, his form twisted as if just hammered, his palms unable to clench into fists. Merlin's gaze was sharp; his whole body felt an unprecedented smoothness, without the suppression of mysterious power—who could still subdue this great demon lord? 'You want me to submit? Who gave you the guts? Even if your master stood before me today demanding my submission, you'd have to weigh whether you have the ability!'

The giant spirit stared at Merlin with terrified eyes, his whole body trembling incessantly, his heart filled with extreme unease. Had Merlin just spoken those words, the spirit would surely have felt his faith insulted and would have flown into a rage to counterattack Merlin. But now, the giant spirit was like a mute, daring not to refute Merlin's words.

The giant spirit originally thought Merlin was like other outsiders—merely a humble human with a bit of strength, not worth a glance before the great heavenly realm. But he was wrong: Merlin was more ferocious and powerful than previous outsiders, actually able to injure them, such holy spirits, so easily. Created by the goddess herself, this perfect being's holy body was shattered by humans—this is no different from the demons' conduct; only demons would mercilessly slaughter holy spirits.

The giant spirit realized that the ant‑like man before him was extremely dangerous; a moment's carelessness could cost him his life. 'You're merely a sentinel guarding this place, yet you dare provoke me? Only your leader is qualified to speak with me. As for you?' Merlin slowly approached the giant spirit, stopped, 'Seeing me, the chief of the seven demon monarchs, shouldn't you kneel to show respect?'

The dull‑witted giant spirit's expression froze—upon hearing 'chief of the seven demon monarchs,' he was momentarily unable to comprehend. Normal demons have a noticeable odor and horns, but Merlin before him was completely different? Suddenly, an immense pressure came, as if a huge mountain had appeared out of nowhere and pressed upon the giant spirit's body, causing his entire frame to sink, nearly making him unable to breathe. Despite the giant spirit's sturdy, massive body, he could not resist the sudden gravity and fell with a 'thud' onto his knees before Merlin, his knees merging with the ground.

'This is about right...' Merlin looked at the giant spirit, coldly smiling, 'Now do you understand your position? Maggots of the heavenly realm...' 'Ah ah ah ah ah! Sinner! You deserve to die!' The giant spirit, provoked by Merlin's words, could no longer think, beaten with rage, he pounded his chest and stamped his feet, wishing to tear Merlin apart.
