The surging anger in his chest could not be contained; the giant spirit raised his fists and hammered wildly, boom boom boom, iron fists shaking the earth, shattered stones flying like knives in the gale. 'Hah! Futile rage.' Merlin raised his hand, activated the repulsion space, centering on himself, excluding everything.

The giant spirit's body was flung by the repulsion, heavily striking the sharp walls of the altar, emitting mournful wails. Merlin leapt up, soaring above the giant spirit's head, activating the gravity space! The giant spirit, dazed from Merlin's blow, had not yet recovered when a powerful pull lifted him, floating above the altar.

Merlin's fist had long been ready; as soon as the giant spirit was pulled in, Merlin punched his chest. Space distorted, the collision of fist and chest erupted with thunderous blast, shaking the ground and sending stones flying. The giant spirit's pupils contracted, his breath stopped abruptly, blood flowed from his seven orifices, an arc‑shaped depression appeared on his chest, like the mark left by a meteor striking the ground.

A sharp tearing sound rang out, space surged; the giant spirit's massive body could actually shoot out like a bullet! With a booming crash, the floor separating the altar from the abyss was shattered by the giant spirit's impact! Merlin stepped upon the giant spirit's body and together they plunged into the abyss...

Alice looked at the new light chant in her hand, growing more doubtful. She remembered Merlin saying her sword was sealed—had it been released now? What exactly were those pure white wings that appeared just now? Could this truly be a place where holy spirits suffer? This sword... could it not be tied to the heavenly realm by countless threads? Alice's doubts piled up; the light chant was taken from her teacher Claudia, she herself didn't know its origin; perhaps the teacher would know something? Too bad she had already returned to the great snow mountain. Although Alice knew divine power restrained dark beings especially well, even Merlin couldn't escape the fate of being stabbed, so the owner of these wings must have an extraordinary background.

Alice recalled that Chairman Dawson said this place was the legendary site of Raphael's suffering. As a former Hero, Alice had some knowledge of the Light Church's stories. Raphael, one of the seven archangels before the goddess, representing mercy. Due to his own personality, among the archangels he had no notable achievements. Other archangels had glorious feats in the holy wars, but Raphael was merely the leader of the heavenly medical corps, akin to a logistics officer. In the Light Church's tales, Raphael was charged with disrespect for improper speech, marginalized and pushed to the edge. Thus, in the stories now spread by the Light Church, Raphael's name is almost impossible to find, gradually becoming a transparent, dispensable archangel. If Alice remembered correctly, the Light Church recorded that the powers of the seven archangels before the goddess were inherited from the goddess's body; each possessed extraordinary power, and Raphael happened to have inherited the goddess's holy wings. No way? The light chant just absorbed something that was exactly the holy wings Raphael received from the goddess. But... where did the true archangel Raphael go? To discard such a precious thing... Alice couldn't fathom throwing away the holy wings; in the Light Church's stories, generally only those who willingly fall and betray do such things, and without exception they are punished, even becoming demons' lackeys.

While Alice was puzzled, a 'bang'—a huge roar shattered the silence of the abyss. The giant spirit fell from above, his massive body tumbling continuously. !! Alice was startled, gripping her slender sword tightly, yet saw the giant spirit on the brink of death, his chest caved in, not knowing how many bones were broken. This guy... up there had been bullied by Merlin not lightly. Merlin saw Alice, sliding down from the giant spirit's body— 'What's going on?' 'I thought you were already dead...' 'You're still alive...'

title: Chapter 42 — Heaven Is Not Paradise
content:
Chapter 42 — Heaven Is Not Paradise

Volume 28 · Chapter 42

Alice rolled her eyes after listening to Merlin’s teasing, feeling discontented. "Who died? Are you really hoping I’m dead?" "That’s not what I meant. It’s best that you’re fine. I wanted to come down quickly to check on your situation, but this big guy wouldn’t let me go," Merlin said helplessly, pointing at the giant saint spirit behind him. He sighed inwardly, thinking that Alice’s luck was indeed extraordinary; she always managed to turn danger into safety at critical moments.

"Hmph!" Alice snorted coldly, explaining calmly, "I barely survived too. I almost got smashed into pulp."

"My strength seems to have recovered. Have you recovered as well?" Merlin asked curiously, puzzled about what had happened.

"That’s right." Alice nodded seriously. "This place is strange. There’s a pile of pure white wings here, seemingly emitting some mysterious suppressive force."

"Pure white wings?" Merlin frowned, looking around in confusion. All he saw were countless black chains and mountains of bones. "Where?"

Alice raised the new Sword of Light Lamentation for Merlin to see. "It’s been absorbed by my sword. Isn’t that amazing?"

"It was absorbed?"

Merlin’s mind was full of questions as he curiously examined the slender sword in Alice’s hand. A sense of resistance and aversion arose spontaneously.

Just looking at the sharp edge of the Sword of Light Lamentation made him feel a hint of danger, instinctively becoming alert. This mysterious weapon, originally the bane of dark creatures, had now awakened and strengthened, its power even greater. Even Merlin had to be cautious.

"Can I take a look?"

"Sure..."

Seeing Merlin’s interest, Alice handed over the Sword of Light Lamentation, wondering if Merlin knew something about it. But as soon as Merlin took the new Sword of Light Lamentation, he felt a burning pain deep in his bones!

Tinkle, tinkle. Merlin instinctively dropped the slender sword on the ground, noticing that his palm was already burned, with wisps of white smoke rising.

"Ouch, how powerful. Before, there was no problem holding this sword, but now just touching it causes unbearable pain."

What kind of weapon is this blade? How do I feel like it’s specifically designed to slaughter demons? ... Merlin! What’s wrong? Are you okay? Alice asked worriedly, leaning in to look.

"I’m fine. What a powerful weapon," Merlin said with a frown. "If a dark creature were pierced by it, they wouldn’t survive."

"Really?" Alice picked up the Sword of Light Lamentation, examining it closely. "Is this a divine artifact?"

"Judging by its luster and quality, it should be close..." Merlin’s expression was serious. (He thought that if it could easily injure him, it probably wasn’t just a pseudo-divine artifact.)

Alice became even more puzzled. How does the teacher have a divine artifact? The weapon she uses herself isn’t of this quality.

Merlin scrutinized the bottom of the abyss and asked, "Alice, where is this place? Do you know?"

"Not very clear, but Mr. Dawson said this is the legendary place of suffering for saint spirits." Alice paused and continued, "Perhaps this place is truly used to punish saint spirits who have sinned. In the stories of the Holy Church, Archangel Raphael was punished for disobeying the goddess and might really be imprisoned here?"

"Heh heh, it seems the heavenly realm people aspire to isn’t such a perfect place after all. There are still conflicts, and the goddess actually built a prison to eliminate dissenters." Merlin sneered inwardly. So-called high-ranking saint spirits weren’t much nobler than demons; they also had desires and used similar means to eliminate rivals!

"What’s with that sour tone? Do you hate the heavenly realm so much?" Alice couldn’t help but counter.

"Hate... not really. After all, I didn’t experience the holy war between saint spirits and demons, but I definitely despise it. The heavenly realm is the epitome of hypocrisy."

Merlin looked at Alice seriously and said—

"They call plundering ‘punishing evil and promoting good,’ killing ‘judging sin,’ and torturing others ‘repentance.’”

"How hypocritical is that? We demons don’t bother with such pretentious things. If we bully someone, we just bully them without any reason."

"??? " Alice’s eyes widened strangely. "You demons are unreasonable? Don’t think this is something to be proud of!"

"I’m just speaking the truth. The saint spirits of the heavenly realm are even more ruthless than we demons. I’ve seen in the history books of the demon race that during the Demon Era, although demons were arrogant and disrespectful, they had their own code of conduct and didn’t exterminate weaker races. But the saint spirits of the heavenly realm wanted us completely wiped out." Merlin paused and added, "If it weren’t for the demons’ desperate resistance, this world might not have demons anymore."

"... Really?" Alice was surprised. The history she saw in the Holy Church wasn’t like this—it depicted the demon race as tyrannical and the goddess sending saint spirits to overthrow their brutal rule. "There’s no need for me to lie. It’s said that the war between saint spirits and demons was extremely fierce. The demon race’s strong ones were slaughtered until now, with a huge disparity in strength. Only a few lords can intimidate the goddess’s lackeys in the mortal world."

That war cost the demon race dearly, nearly leading to their extinction...

"So exaggerated? Your demon race... isn’t full of powerful beings?" Alice asked in shock, wondering why the histories recorded by the Holy Church and the demon race differed so much. The Holy Church said demons were full of threats, and as long as they existed, the world would never be peaceful. Demons would eventually return to enslave humanity, so their image was always portrayed as immensely powerful to make believers feel anxious.

"During the Demon Era, there were indeed many powerful beings, not much different from the entire saint spirit army..." Merlin nodded, then changed the subject. "But the saint spirits’ suppression of demons was too strong. They were created by the God of Light solely to slaughter demons. They’re practically the natural enemies of demons."

"No way?" Alice was half-believing, half-doubting, wondering if Merlin was exaggerating. Could demons have natural enemies?

"I didn’t experience the holy war, so I don’t know the specifics, but Belial of the Seventh Demon Lord Palace is the only remaining original lord. Only he has personally experienced the horror of the saint spirits," Merlin said with a slightly suppressed tone.

"Belial... " Alice furrowed her brows. "Is that the Demon Lord who lived from the Demon Era to now? I heard he’s a deeply hidden lord, the most unfathomable among the Demon Lords!"

"Almost wiped out our race, slaughtered countless demons, and finally portrayed himself as the righteous army, winning everyone’s cheers and applause." Merlin looked at Alice with a smile that wasn’t quite a smile, saying meaningfully—

"Do you think the saint spirits of the heavenly realm are hypocritical enough?"

"Demons merely enslave human bodies, while saint spirits enslave human thoughts and souls....

title: Chapter 43 — Giant Counterattack (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 43 — Giant Counterattack (Bonus)

Volume 28 · Chapter 43

“I... I don’t know what to say...”

Alice stood frozen, unable to decide who was right, her mind muddled.

From Alice’s perspective, although the Holy Church had its problems, it was indeed an organization that protected humans from dark creatures, and it had made many sacrifices for that purpose.

“You say the Saint Spirits were created specifically to fight demons and have a clear advantage over you, but I saw you defeat that giant quite easily.”

Merlin looked at the dying giant Saint Spirit behind him, shrugged his shoulders, “Him? He’s probably just a gatekeeper from the heavens. A leader-level Saint Spirit might actually be able to fight me for a few rounds~”

Alice was about to ask Merlin another question when, suddenly, the dying giant Saint Spirit stood up again.

The mask of the giant Saint Spirit cracked, revealing a half-face that looked utterly terrifying.

The bottom of the abyss was vast, unlike the cramped altar, where the giant Saint Spirit could finally unleash its true power.

“Holy Wings! Return the Holy Wings! You are sinners, unworthy to possess them!!!”

“Still alive?” Merlin frowned slightly, not expecting this big guy to be so tough. He should have been dead by now!

“Holy...”

This was Alice’s first time seeing a Saint Spirit. Even during her time as a Hero in the Holy Church, she had only seen pictures.

Earlier on the altar, she had been too panicked to realize that this giant was the guardian of the Holy Church!

The terrifying appearance of the giant Saint Spirit was completely different from the gentle and kind Saint Spirits she had seen in pictures, full of aggression!

Alice couldn’t help but doubt. The Holy Church had always preached that Saint Spirits were kind and just beings, angels who protected humans and steadfast peacekeepers!

But now, Alice was shaken. The giant Saint Spirit in front of her was not only fierce but also killed humans and devoured their hearts! This was far from the image of a human protector!

It seemed that the Saint Spirits were portrayed as very noble and righteous by the Holy Church, but reality wasn’t entirely like that. There were still unknown dark sides.

“Only Raphael has the right to possess it! Return it!!!” The giant Saint Spirit pounded its chest in fury, as if guarding the Holy Wings was his mission.

“...” Alice was embarrassed, thinking this must be the place where the Archangel was imprisoned! The Holy Elegy absorbed the power of the Saint Spirit to activate!

“Return it? Nice try. We’re not just taking the treasure you’re guarding, we’re also taking your life.” Merlin coldly replied, determined to complete the robbery. This wasn’t called robbery; against enemies, it was called taking spoils of war.

“Sinners! Return it!”

The giant Saint Spirit was furious, only repeating the same words, its mind set solely on reclaiming the holy relic, unaware that it had already been absorbed by Alice’s weapon?

The golden bracelet on its wrist broke, its bones cracked with a popping sound, and its massive body split open, the flesh and skin tearing apart like a meat flower exploded by a bomb!

The Holy Wings inherited from the goddess by Raphael might be the giant Saint Spirit’s lifeline. Seeing it being taken, it decided to fight to the death no matter what!

From the split flesh, the giant Saint Spirit grew four new strong arms, and its wings behind it expanded with a loud sound—

A six-armed giant Saint Spirit appeared before Merlin and Alice, its terrifying aura overwhelming the surroundings!

Alice looked at the mighty six-armed Saint Spirit standing on the stinking mountain of corpses, her heart growing more uncertain...

If a creature like this could be called a human protector, what was the difference between the so-called Saint Spirits and demons!

“Alice, kill him, and bring back his head.” Merlin rubbed his hands together, eager to fight. The Banri Garan wasn’t with him, and he had no other sword to replace it, so he had to go in directly.

“I... I will!” Alice, whether for completing the trial or for avenging the victims, had to kill this Saint Spirit today!

“Ugh!!!”

The giant Saint Spirit roared, raising its six arms and smashing them down on the tiny Merlin and Alice with a series of loud thuds!

Six iron fists were fired at once, like bullets from a machine gun,轰击 everything in front of them!

The ground shook, white bones flying into the sky with the stench of decay, and deep craters were formed wherever the iron fists landed!

In just a few seconds, the ground at the bottom of the abyss had already become as scarred as the surface of the moon.

After Merlin and Alice had restored their strength, they were no longer helpless like before and had many ways to deal with the giant Saint Spirit—

They both jumped aside to avoid the giant Saint Spirit’s iron fist attacks.

Merlin picked up a black chain on the ground, wrapped it around his arm as a temporary weapon, similar to a boxing glove.

As the giant Saint Spirit’s iron fist struck, Merlin gritted his teeth and raised the chain-fist to clash directly with the Saint Spirit!

An explosion-like sound shook the space slightly, and one of the giant Saint Spirit’s arms was instantly crippled, its bones broken by Merlin.

Don’t be fooled by the giant Saint Spirit’s seemingly powerful appearance. Compared to Merlin’s physical strength, the difference was enormous.

It was like a big block of tofu trying to crush a pebble into powder—it was ridiculous.

The giant Saint Spirit let out a pained roar, becoming even more wary of Merlin. This tiny ant-like figure contained an unimaginable power!

The giant Saint Spirit flapped its wings and took to the air, trying to create distance from Merlin, no longer daring to clash head-on, and instead unleashing a fierce hurricane.

“Damn it!”

Merlin was blown backward continuously by the hurricane, but would he let the giant Saint Spirit’s plan succeed?

He quickly unfastened the black chain on his arm and swung it with force, drawing a perfect arc and successfully latching onto the giant Saint Spirit’s neck.

The giant Saint Spirit’s breathing hitched, and in terror, it flew higher and higher, trying to escape Merlin’s chain restraint.

Merlin wouldn’t give him a chance! He pulled hard, dragging the giant Saint Spirit soaring high into the sky down to him, then delivered a powerful punch to its face!

“Want to run? Dream on!”

The giant Saint Spirit let out a pained cry, several of its teeth flying out.

The unfortunate giant Saint Spirit had just landed when Alice, holding the fine sword Holy Elegy, came in for a finishing blow. A flash of cold light, and the giant Saint Spirit’s heart was pierced. Its face turned ashen, and its massive body collapsed, its face still showing a look of不甘.

“You... won’t escape...”

“Huh?” Alice looked at the giant Saint Spirit’s body gradually cooling down, not paying it much mind, and instead looked at the Holy Elegy in her hand. The sword had become sharper than before. Probably, a dragon’s scales would be no more than a layer of window paper in front of it.

“Alice! Get away!” Merlin suddenly roared, his expression anxious.

Alice looked up and saw that the giant Saint Spirit, whose eyes had already lost their luster, chose to self-destruct in its final moment, wanting to bury the two outsiders here forever!

The giant Saint Spirit’s body emitted a ten-thousand-zhang glow, transforming into a pure golden energy body. It instantly contracted, causing the temperature in the abyss to skyrocket, comparable to a small sun.

Boom!!!

Violent, destructive, scorching... A massive explosion.

title: Chapter 44 — Embracing Underwater (Sorry for the late update)
content:
Chapter 44 — Embracing Underwater (Sorry for the late update)

Volume 28 · Chapter 44

Giant Spirit's energy body shrank into a small light ball,
yet it twisted space into a vortex!

The power of the explosion was enough to burn the entire abyss to cinders!

Terrifying flames rose like demonic beasts, roaring and flourishing, devouring heaven and earth!

The intense impact also lifted the ground, and the surroundings were leveled to flat earth in almost an instant.

Alice retreated in the chaos, but was struck by the first shockwave, her whole body making cracking sounds as her bones rattled, and her consciousness grew blurred.

"Alice!

Fortunately, Merlin had foreseen the danger in advance and hurried over to Alice's side, holding her in his arms.

Facing the blast of fire, Merlin quickly cast a repulsion space as a barrier against the explosion. The giant Spirit's self-destruction was evidently far stronger than Flaer's alchemy bomb. Merlin only felt a gale blow across his cheeks, making his whole body somewhat numb.

The flames of the self-destruction continuously collided with the repulsion barrier. Merlin felt his hands trembling; he had actually been forcibly repelled by the explosion!?

Before the explosion danger ended, the abyss's ground somehow couldn't hold up first, and with a crash it collapsed—

"What!?"

Merlin's footing vanished, and he fell toward the deeper depths, not expecting such a situation.

He heard a deafening roar from below. Looking down, it was a surging underground lake!

Merlin was startled, thinking to himself, "Could it be that I'm going to fall into the water again? Not dying under the giant Spirit's fist, but being drowned by water, isn't that right?" SF Light Novel

Plop!

The two of them fell into the water together and were dragged into the depths by the underground lake's current. Above, the explosion continued, and the flames instantly boiled the surface layer of the water toward the lake!

The dark depths of the lake were illuminated by the light of the flames—a crimson sunset-like scene...

The ice-cold bone-piercing lake water made Merlin feel a chill. He struggled desperately to swim up, but continued to sink deeper into the lake.

As Merlin's body trembled, a series of gases came out of his mouth, making him look like a dandelion, at the mercy of the lake's dark current.

Alice, who was originally blurred in consciousness, was stimulated greatly after falling into the ice-cold bone-piercing lake water, and quickly regained awareness.

Alice held her breath and looked around in the water. Seeing that Merlin had gone limp and was sinking, she was greatly alarmed—

Merlin!?

Alice didn't have time to think of much else; she quickly swam toward Merlin and pulled him back, not letting him continue to drift with the waves.

At this moment, Merlin's situation was quite bad. If this continued, there would be a danger to his life. The water here was too deep, unlike the relatively shallow dark river.

Alice was anxious in her heart and had to find a way to save Merlin. She stared at Merlin, her expression somewhat complex.

At such a time, who could guess what Alice was thinking? Only she herself knew best.

Alice's gaze became much calmer, as if she had made some determination. Then she closed her eyes and directly kissed Merlin's lips, delivering the oxygen in her mouth to him.

The two embraced in the ice-cold bone-piercing lake water. Behind them, the raging sea of fire seemed to roar unwillingly, dyeing the depths of the underground lake red...

In a daze, Merlin suddenly opened his eyes. Seeing Alice so close, he clearly felt a boost in spirit, as if he had been badly frightened.

Looking at Alice's vivid eyelashes, it seems that besides saving Merlin, there doesn't seem to be any other intent?

Alice supported Merlin's cheek and continuously delivered life-saving air to him through the kiss.

Merlin's mind was in a turmoil. Suddenly, his gaze focused, and he opened his arms, casting repulsion space in the water, trying to create a safe zone.

The repulsion space centered on Merlin was like a transparent glass ball, constantly colliding, isolating the ice-cold bone-piercing lake water around the two of them outside...

A few days later, the commotion caused by the two had gradually subsided, and the events at the temple had spread throughout the island. The oppressed commoners, upon learning that the chief had died, began a rebellion. They captured the temple guards who usually acted arrogantly and put an end to their man-eating practices.

This sinful small island seemed to have returned to normal, except that the giant Spirit's self-destruction had left no corpse behind...

Merlin and Alice failed to obtain the chief's head; who knows if it counts as completing the trial?

When Alice slowly woke up, her head ached terribly. She slowly got up and kept rubbing her temples.

"Here is SF Light Novel.

Alice looked around her surroundings. She was lying in a thatched hut where the barbarians lived, seeing a scene that was somewhat familiar.

She realized she had probably been rescued back to that friendly barbarian settlement. She must have been rescued by someone?

Alice thought of Merlin, not knowing how he was doing? She felt an urgent desire to see him.

Just then, Merlin pulled back the curtain and walked in from outside, carrying a dead wild boar on his back.

It seemed that after the commotion ended, Merlin had brought Alice here, so she could rest well and eat and drink for several days for free.

As for just now? Merlin went out hunting. Putting a good spin on it, he had a really good experience experiencing the barbarians' life.

Actually, Merlin was because he had eaten and drunk for free at the village for several days, and his heart wasn't very comfortable, so he went out hunting just to slightly repay this group of good-hearted barbarians.

After all, Merlin realized these guys were really behind, completely relying on the sky to eat. If they couldn't catch prey, they could only starve.

Their lives weren't easy either; they still entertained Merlin with big fish and meat, which was already fulfilling one's duty. There was no reason to eat and drink for free, huh?

At this time, Merlin had already changed into a clean face, finally no longer needing to dress up as a barbarian and restoring his former spirit.

"Oh? You're awake?" Merlin saw Alice sitting on the grass mat staring at him, smiling as he put down the wild boar on his back. "I still thought you would be unconscious for several days. Didn't expect you to wake up so quickly."

"You—what do you mean?" Alice furrowed her beautiful brows and asked in a huff.

"You were proven to have been hit by the explosion's impact, and recovering so quickly, you have to say you're too lucky~" Merlin's tone was teasing, and he sat down big and casual beside Alice.

"Hmph!" Alice let out a light hum. "Looking at your tone, you're not happy about my misfortune, are you?"

"Although I am indeed happy when I see you suffer, this is the truth...." Merlin nodded seriously.

"...??!" Alice widened her eyes, grinding her teeth in anger.

"But on the principle issue, I won't gloat over others' misfortune~" Merlin suddenly changed the subject, clutching his chest and speaking seriously. "You almost lost your life just now. What is there to be happy about? If you die, I wouldn't have one of the great pleasures of life."

"I...." Alice was about to burst out a profanity, but her whole body ached.

"Just lie down honestly. Your injuries haven't healed yet. After a period of recuperation, if you get injured again from being angered, that wouldn't be good." Merlin helped Alice lie down slowly, and even took the time to tidy up Alice's messy bangs in front of her forehead.

"Huh?" Alice's expression became even stranger, and the look she gave Merlin was not quite the same. Two small red spots appeared on her face—

This fellow....

How come he seems to have become much more gentle toward me?

title: Chapter 45 — Not the First Time
content:
Chapter 45 — Not the First Time

Volume 28 · Chapter 45

This is not the first time.

SOURCE TEXT:
<<<BEGIN SOURCE>>>
Alice covered half her face with a blanket, her eyes filled with suspicion as she stared at Merlin, wondering if he was up to something.

Was he plotting something?

Recalling Merlin’s usual gentle and considerate nature, she thought he must have had some ulterior motive.

“Why are you looking at me with such a suspicious gaze?”

Merlin felt embarrassed, as if Alice was guarding against something.

........Alice shook her head, wondering if she was overthinking things. Maybe Merlin was just being friendly?

Merlin didn’t say much, but he remembered the underwater scene and still felt a little embarrassed. Now he felt inexplicably nervous when talking to Alice.

The village’s barbarian elder walked in, holding two items: Merlin’s Banri Garan sword and a broken mask.
“We searched for a long time and only found these two.”
“Oh, it’s great that we could find my sword. Thank you for your hard work,” Merlin said, taking the Banri Garan and drawing the blade. He held the weapon that saved his life, feeling much more at ease. He had been worried sick about not having the Banri Garan around for a while.

“What did you ask them to do for you?” Alice asked curiously.

“I just asked them to help search for my sword in the temple. The chief blew himself up, and the place was a mess. I’m not very familiar with the temple, so this old guy volunteered to call the tribe to help me find it.”

Merlin looked at the Banri Garan and tied it to his waist. “I’m glad I didn’t lose it, otherwise I would have gone crazy. This power is my lifeline!” he said.

Alice looked at the Banri Garan on Merlin’s waist. She had always known that this sword was the King’s artifact from the Demon Lord’s Palace, used to signify the monarch’s identity, and seemed to have no other purpose.

Merlin treated the Banri Garan as a treasure, which made Alice a little suspicious. Was Merlin still brooding over his dismissal?

“This... Merlin picked up the broken mask and gradually realized it was the chief’s mask. It had survived the explosion, so it must be made of special material!”

“It’s... a god’s thing, on the edge of the earth,” the barbarian elder explained nearby, “-.-. symbol.... god!”

“A symbol of the god?” Merlin frowned, then suddenly understood and laughed, “Great stuff! We didn’t work in vain after all!”

“What happened?” Alice became curious, wondering if the mask was some kind of treasure.

“Did you forget? Our mission was to take the chief’s head back. But after he blew himself up, not even a hair was left. Where can we get the chief’s head? Isn’t the trial over then?” Merlin held up the broken chief’s mask and shook it, “This was the mask the chief wore, symbolizing his status. Bringing it back can prove that we killed him.”

“Is that so?” Alice lowered her head and thought about it, agreeing that Merlin had a point. Without the chief’s head, at least they needed a token to prove it.

“With this, I can definitely become a Golden Adventurer, right?” Merlin looked at the broken mask in his hand and started daydreaming.
Wearing the Golden Adventurer badge, he would enjoy the crazy admiration of his friends.
<<<END SOURCE>>>

title: Chapter 46 — Shifting the Balance (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 46 — Shifting the Balance (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 28 · Chapter 46

“...You... you’re talking nonsense What?”“Are you slandering me for joking? “Too pathetic, Merlin…. Alice furrowed her brows, thinking Merlin didn’t even care about her at all? He actually slandered her Not a first kiss, yet putting on an all‑knowing look “I’m not talking nonsense, you really aren’t experiencing your first kiss—I witnessed it myself.” Merlin crossed his arms, looking serious. Alice was bewildered, seeing Merlin’s expression she couldn’t tell if he was joking, so she couldn’t help but start wildly imagining— Having witnessed it firsthand? Could Merlin have clairvoyance, having seen me kiss my teacher’s vulture when I was young? Wait! Merlin said the feeling of my lips was very familiar? Could it be… I don’t know when, while I was unconscious or asleep, he secretly kissed me? ! Thinking this, Alice’s face instantly flushed again, never imagining that the superficially proper Merlin would do such shameless things! “....How could you do this! ? ...... ....What should I say?” Seeing Alice’s strange behavior, Merlin asked in surprise, “Did you misunderstand something?” “....What could I misunderstand?” Alice lowered her head, her heart fluttering, showing a bit of shy maiden attitude, “You’re such a thick‑skinned guy, why sneak around…” “Hold on!” Merlin raised his hand to stop Alice from continuing her fantasies, speaking sternly, “I conduct myself openly; when would I need to sneak around? Clearly it was you who took the initiative? “What! ? I took the initiative, I would willingly…………” Alice’s face turned ugly, thinking Merlin was slandering her purity “Exactly, that was a long time ago. When we first arrived at Rexel, you drank alcohol, went berserk, almost wrecked the guild, and then you stumbled over to me, drunk and crazy, and kissed me.” Merlin stroked his chin, boasting, “If I think about it, I’ve really lost out—letting you succeed, what a bargain for you~ “………Alice became incoherent, unable to believe this fact, No way! ! You’re not lying to me, are you? !” “Why would I lie to you? Everyone saw it then; if you don’t believe me, go ask the guild—because you made a drunken spectacle, nobody wanted to embarrass you, so they kept quiet.” Merlin sighed, gazing at Alice with deep meaning, “You even stuck your tongue in; I never dreamed you’d be so uninhibited… haha~” “Yah! ! !” Alice clutched her head and screamed, as if struck by a great shock, unable to believe Merlin’s words—that she really behaved that horribly when drunk! Light novel “Calm down, it’s no big deal; kissing won’t get you pregnant, right?” Merlin tried to comfort Alice. Alice suddenly lifted her eyes, filled with hostility; if looks could kill, Merlin would probably be dead many times over. “Cough cough!” Merlin quickly coughed twice to cover his embarrassment, “I mean… you don’t need to worry about it…. “Hmph!” Alice snorted coldly, dissatisfied with Merlin’s attitude; although it was unintentional, they had indeed been intimate twice! Does Merlin have no thought at all? I haven’t even gotten angry much—aren’t these hints obvious enough? Is he truly oblivious to my feelings, or is he pretending not to notice? Alice fumed, turning her head away, watching Merlin smooth things over, her anger growing. “....What are you thinking? After all… in the end, is our relationship strange? “We’re just friends… more like partners…. ” Merlin had just spoken when he saw the undisguised disappointment in Alice’s brows, so he hastily blushed and added, “Of course… in my eyes, you’re more important than all these people… … probably?” “……” Alice hearing Merlin say that, two little blushes appeared on her face, her resentment fading considerably— She didn’t press further, afraid Merlin would admit outright that they were just friends. Perhaps this state of being friends‑plus, lovers‑not‑yet‑full is the best choice…. At the Adventurers’ Headquarters, Chris wasn’t afraid of catching a chill, just sitting on the outside steps. Her two chubby little hands held her face, brows furrowed, looking very unhappy. As Chairman Dawson said, the time on the island bears no relation to the outside world. Merlin and Alice had spent over a month on the island while only a day and a half passed outside. Even so, little Chris couldn’t bear missing her parents; she started out cheerful, but after just one night she became low‑spirited, unable to eat. Chris wondered how her parents were doing? No news at all, although Chairman Dawson, like a kind old grandfather, kept reassuring her there was no problem. But Chris couldn’t see her parents, couldn’t take in the reassurance; every half hour she’d waddle over to ask why her parents still hadn’t returned. Chairman Dawson still underestimated a child’s dependence on her parents, already thinking of using something else to divert Chris’s attention. “Child, go inside and wait; your dad and mom are rare powerhouses, they should be able to return safely.” “No! I want to wait here for them!” Chris showed a stubborn expression, apparently fearing she’d become an unwanted orphan, just like those kids she’d seen in the orphanage before. “……” Old Chairman Dawson felt a headache coming; if Chris caught a chill outside and got sick, he’d have a hard time explaining to Merlin and Alice. Just as Chairman Dawson was at a loss, Chris’s downcast eyes suddenly regained a spark, and she couldn’t help but smile—happier than seeing a cream cake. Chris jumped up from the steps, her short legs pattering, she flung herself into Alice’s arms, “Mom! “Ha…. ” Alice held the baby girl, looked her over, saw nothing wrong, then reassured herself and kissed her, “I’ve missed you so much—have you missed Mom?” “Missed… missed, of course I missed Dad too~” Chris returned to her parents’ side, instantly regaining her usual spirit. “Missed me? Come give Dad a kiss!” Merlin lifted Chris over; the little one “patsch” planted a kiss on him, making him overjoyed. “Returned safe and sound? Really rare,” Old Chairman Dawson watched Merlin and Alice, nodded silently, thinking—since they came back alive, the trial is practically a sure win. For thirty years, the Purple Gold Adventurers have always had only five…. Looking at this lineup, starting today we’ll have to change it!”

title: Chapter 47 — The Strongest of the Present Age
content:
Chapter 47 — The Strongest of the Present Age

Volume 28 · Chapter 47

After Merlin and Alice returned, they handed the broken chief's mask to the Arbitration Committee. After verification, it proved that the two had successfully killed the chief on the island. Although the two did not obtain the chief's head, the mask representing the status was sufficient to explain the matter, as the mask and the head had equal persuasive power.

The Arbitration Committee unanimously approved Merlin and Alice's trial and decided to formally grant them the highest honor of adventurers!

Inside the Adventurers' Headquarters, all the arbitration committee members were present, with solemn expressions, as if conducting an important ceremony. Chairman Dawson came forward holding an exquisite small box and said to Alice seriously, "Miss Alice, congratulations on becoming the sixth platinum adventurer, this is the highest honor among adventurers. Please do not forget the adventurers' creed, stay true to your original heart, and let the spirit of adventure shine with your strength." "Thank you." Alice received the box granted by Chairman Dawson, opened it, and inside lay the already-prepared platinum adventurer's certificate. Apart from the material and the symbol of status being different, the information on it had not changed at all.

From today onward, Alice became a member of the platinum adventurers, and at the same time the youngest among them.

In the history of the adventurers' industry, there has never been someone as young as Alice who has already attained the industry's highest honor.

Alice is young, yet she has already reached this status, a height that many cannot reach in a lifetime. Now Alice can say that she is an existence that cannot be looked down upon anywhere in the world.

"Is this the platinum adventurer's certificate?" Alice took the platinum certificate in her hand and looked at it; the dazzling metal luster was extremely dazzling. She used to think that reaching the silver adventurer rank was already the limit, never imagining that she would one day become an extremely rare platinum adventurer?

"Mommy, it's sparkly, so pretty~" Little Chris grabbed Alice's thigh, wanting to take it to look. "Here, don't lose it." Alice handed the platinum adventurer's certificate to her beloved daughter to play with for a while. "Hehe!" Chris looked at the platinum certificate in her hand, her big eyes blinking, obviously loving it, simply thinking that anything shiny is good.

"Is it pretty?" Alice asked curiously. "Pretty~" Chris replied in a childish voice, clutching the platinum certificate, looking exactly like a miser.

"Then you can try harder later to get your own platinum certificate, how about that?" Alice squatted down and rubbed Chris's little head.

"Hehe~" The little tuft on Chris's head swayed back and forth, seeming not to understand Alice's encouragement.

Merlin, watching from the side, felt envious, so he quickly coughed twice to draw the attention of the arbitration committee.

"Then... what about mine? I also passed the platinum trial, why don't I have my platinum certificate?" Merlin's face could no longer contain his excitement; he feared he would have to jump from black iron straight to platinum, skipping several levels.

Chairman Dawson and the several arbitration committee members looked at each other, their expressions turning serious and solemn, and he spoke solemnly.

"Mr. Merlin, please come with us for a moment."

title: Chapter 48 — Overlook
content:
Chapter 48 — Overlook

Volume 28 · Chapter 48

Other arbitration committee members echoed in agreement, not sparing any praise for Merlin— The chubby committee member said: “The chair is right, the purple‑gold adventurers have wronged you; only the strongest adventurer is worthy of you.” The tall committee member said: “The proof of the strongest adventurer is only one, meaning you are unique, your status far surpasses that of purple‑gold adventurers.” The short committee member said: “This proof of the strongest adventurer is extremely precious; since the adventurer rating system was established, besides the founder Robin Hood, no one has ever obtained this title. You are, after the founder, the only one who can receive this honor!” The thin committee member said: “Mr. Merlin, your performance in the competition is evident to all; the title of strongest adventurer is truly deserved.” The committee members took turns expressing their sincere congratulations to Merlin; from now on he is the strongest representative in the industry! Obviously this strongest adventurer proof looks plain and unremarkable, but in fact it represents the highest honor of adventurers! Since the adventurer industry was established a century ago, besides the founder Robin Hood, only Merlin has been able to obtain the title of strongest adventurer. Don’t listen to the committee members’ sweet words; Merlin’s face showed only stupor, not a hint of joy, wondering if these old guys were just fooling him? Merlin looked at the wooden plaque in his hand; its actual weight was even less than that of black iron! F light novel Just this? Is this considered the highest honor of the adventurer week? After all this effort, I just got a wooden plaque?! I won’t just casually find a piece of wood to make a wooden plaque?! ? Just because it’s the founder’s thing, does that make it incredibly precious? Merlin felt a bit disappointed, having waited so long in vain. “You... are you sure this rotten wooden plaque is the highest honor of adventurers? ? ?” “Absolutely certain!” said Elder Dawson, pausing, then explained in a sincere tone: “Mr. Merlin, you don’t know that when the adventurers were first established they were impoverished and down on their luck; founder Robin Hood was merely a petty thug from the market, with no money at all, so Robin Hood, to make himself look a bit more formal, wrote his name on a wooden plaque and gave himself the title of strongest adventurer, thus opening the first page of adventurer history... Merlin’s face remained expressionless, the corners of his mouth twitching wildly, thinking: What the hell is this strongest adventurer? Pure self‑entertainment! After all this fuss, I’m on the same level as a market thug! Are these old guys definitely not insulting me?! “Don’t look at this wooden plaque as plain and ordinary; it actually carries extraordinary significance! It is the very first adventurer proof in history, hand‑crafted by founder Robin Hood, and only an adventurer whose status equals that of the founder may possess it.” Chairman Dawson patted Merlin’s shoulder, speaking earnestly: “As the strongest representative of adventurers, you must bear this banner.” Saying this, Merlin’s face turned black in an instant— “Pa‑cha!” he flung the strongest adventurer proof to the ground— “You’re messing with me!!!” “!!!” Seeing Merlin throw away something so precious, the arbitration committee members were startled, their faces turning pale, and they panicked. “Mr. Merlin, don’t do that!” Chairman Dawson hurriedly picked up the wooden plaque, blew off the dust, and said: “This truly is the highest honor of adventurers; why don’t you believe it?” “Only a fool would believe a broken wooden plaque is proof of the strongest adventurer; hurry up and give me a purple‑gold adventurer proof!” Merlin said, face grim, thinking that after all his effort to come here, not only did he not level up, but his black iron had regressed to a wooden plaque—this isn’t a joke, is it?! “Mr. Merlin, you can’t tell good from bad; this seemingly ordinary wooden plaque is worth countless purple‑gold adventurer proofs!” Elder Dawson was almost in tears, saying: “Come on, don’t treat me like a three‑year‑old; even if you praise this thing to the heavens, what use is it? Outsiders don’t recognize it, and if they mistake me for someone who carves his own adventurer proof just for fun, what then?” Merlin said coldly, making it clear he wouldn’t accept it: “What’s the point of strongest or not if others don’t recognize it?” ;“Mr. Merlin, this item’s preciousness exceeds your imagination; although indeed very few people know of the existence of the strongest adventurer proof, the purple‑gold adventurers do!” Chairman Dawson took a deep breath, calmed his emotions, and said: “I just said the proof is of leader‑level; you still don’t get it? Because with it, you have the authority to dispatch purple‑gold adventurers to assist you in handling various matters.” Merlin’s eyes widened in surprise; he had always thought that upon reaching the purple‑gold adventurer tier, it would be nearly impossible to hire them to do work. Just like the old witch Circe who can brew potions—when she asks for a bottle, she has to speak sweetly and lower her posture. When she’s in a bad mood, they simply ignore you~ Who would have thought that this seemingly insignificant little wooden plaque could actually command this group of people?! Merlin finally realized how precious the strongest adventurer proof is; purple‑gold adventurers are near‑top‑tier power among humans, and being able to command them means he need fear no force of any human nation! “Really… really?” “Of course, but this requires coordination from the arbitration committee; you must not abuse your authority, after all, among the purple‑gold adventurers there are many with eccentric personalities.” Chairman Dawson spoke tactfully and handed the strongest adventurer proof to Merlin. “…Is that so?” Merlin stared at the unremarkable little wooden plaque in his hand, thinking that although there are certain restrictions, it is still precious enough; even if the purple‑gold adventurers are lofty, they still ought to show me respect, right? “It won’t be long before the other few purple‑gold adventurers learn that a new strongest adventurer has been born.” Chairman Dawson, seeing Merlin not refuse, secretly breathed a sigh of relief— Although Mr. Merlin has become the strongest adventurer, others may not necessarily be convinced. The sky gradually darkened; the prosperous capital of the British Kingdom, London, was shrouded in the glow of players’ lights. It has been a long time since the last internal disturbance; people seem to have gradually forgotten the fear of that time. They believe that no matter what disaster strikes, the kingdom is under the protection of the Thorn Knights, so nothing will go wrong. Even if the Thorn Knights cannot handle something, there is still that powerful, mysterious Elf‑king great swordsman. Many already regard the great swordsman as Britain’s guardian, not knowing that he is actually the demon lord who makes countless humans tremble with fear. Dong, dong, dong— . The lofty, solemn clock tower rang out with melodious chimes, announcing the formal arrival of night. At the tower’s peak, the biting wind howled; at this moment, a waning moon drifted through the clouds. By the dim moonlight, one could faintly make out three figures of different forms standing there…. Demons! Their scarlet eyes gazed down upon the city.

title: Chapter 49 — Night Raid (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 49 — Night Raid (Extra Chapter)

Volume 28 · Chapter 49

All three demons are Mammon's capable subordinates. Before the Second Holy War even broke out, they infiltrated Britain to carry out assassinations. Mammon's goal was to weaken Britain before the war, paving the way for victory in the Holy War. The demons, clad in black robes, stood atop the clock tower, overlooking the royal capital, as if contemplating something. Bifrons, an artistically inclined demon, is Mammon's official painter; his status in the Third Demon Lord's Palace is no less than that of Ose, a near‑madman. Falgor, a killing machine that only knows how to obey Mammon's orders, looks bulky and clumsy but is actually the fastest demon in the Third Demon Lord's Palace—he can sever an enemy's head in a breath. Hampa, the assassin specially assigned by Mammon to deal with troublesome individuals, is also the most skilled at assassination in this operation; he is said to be adept at reading people's expressions and is highly favored by Mammon. These three demons are undoubtedly of demon officer rank, equal in status to the Seven Generals under Merlin, and they hold important positions in the Demon Lord's Palace. Mammon sent them to Britain, determined to inflict a heavy blow on Britain before the war, so that Queen Elizabeth would have to wash her neck and wait for him! '—Isn't this a fairly prosperous nation among humans?' Bifrons' voice was melodious. 'Yes, this is Great Britain; it's my first time here, and it really looks prosperous.' Hampa sincerely sighed, unable to deny that humans are still stronger in this era. 'Hmph! A bunch of lowly two‑legged sheep, they stole our wealth to build prosperity—this should have been ours!' Bifrons' tone turned resentful. 'There's nothing we can do; the holy spirits of heaven refuse to die, and if these humans hadn't received heaven's aid, who could rival us in the demon age?' Hampa sneered, his sinister laugh making one's hair stand on end. 'After all, we failed to become the rule‑makers, letting humans slip through the cracks.' Bifrons sighed. 'Kill!' Falgor growled lowly, though he speaks little, he is already eager to begin the mission. 'Don't rush; we need to be careful and try to kill as many of the kingdom's strong warriors as possible.' Bifrons soothed the irate Falgor, lowering his voice: according to the intelligence I received, the kingdom's strongest knight order is the Purple Rose Knights, led by twelve Thorn Knights, said to have suffered heavy losses in the internal strife; they are knights dedicated to serving the royal family, and when the Holy War breaks out they will surely be the core of the kingdom's resistance, so why not start with these so‑called Thorn Knights?' 'I have no objection, but the stronger the foe we take down, the better for us,' Hampa remarked, intentionally or not. 'What do you mean?' Bifrons looked at his companion. 'I've heard there's a man called Elgin the Great Swordsman in this kingdom, renowned far and wide, supposedly very formidable; if we could kill him, wouldn't that greatly dampen Britain's morale?' Hampa paused, then said solemnly, 'Killing him alone would be worth killing a million soldiers.' 'Haha, Elgin the Great Swordsman? I've heard that name, but it's a pity~' Bifrons shook his head. 'How so?' Hampa frowned. 'That Elgin the Great Swordsman fellow—his whereabouts are uncertain; I've inquired around, and up to now it seems no one has seen his true face; finding him might be harder than killing him.' Bifrons answered with a half‑smile. 'What a pity~' Hampa sighed helplessly, 'I had hoped to cross swords with that great swordsman on this trip; I really want to see just how strong the human powerhouse hyped up really is.' 'If luck is on our side, we might get a chance,' Bifrons slowly rose, gazing at the distant, lantern‑lit palace, 'Then let's begin the operation; after success we'll meet at the palace, and if we can directly slay Britain's queen, Lord Mammon will surely be pleased.' 'Kill!!!' Falgor roared, his murderous heart stirring. 'It won't be that easy; the queen surely has strong guards around her, so it won't be simple to pull off.' Hampa hesitated, feeling Bifrons' plan wasn't very steady. 'What's there to fear? Before coming I investigated for a long time—there are only four Thorn Knights alive in Britain's capital; we'll split up and take out three first, then regroup.' Bifrons looked at Hampa, meaningfully saying, 'Do you think the remaining Thorn Knight, at the last moment, has the power to block the three of us working together?' .... Hampa had no reply; if things really go as smoothly as Bifrons said, then taking the queen's head would be as easy as reaching into a bag!' 'Don't worry, everything will go smoothly—we'll march to the palace, behead the queen, and return to offer her head to Mammon...' Bifrons narrowed his eyes, chest full of confidence, saying, 'This Holy War' 'We've already won half!' In the capital's alleys, the twelfth Thorn Knight, Cladi, after finishing his discussion with the queen, was preparing to return to his lodgings to rest. The capital had not yet received news that the second Thorn Knight, Seth, had died; everyone assumed he was still out training. Cladi, as a support master among the knights and also a learned man, loved traveling to study ancient knowledge. Just now, Cladi had already asked the queen for permission to leave, planning to depart the capital tomorrow to seek stronger ancient magic. Having been granted leave, Cladi was in good spirits, yet he saw a figure by the roadside—a person wrapped in a robe, drawing, looking rather mysterious. 'A street‑corner painter?' Cladi thought, paying it no mind, and simply walked past, thinking the fellow was just someone scraping a living by begging for food. The black‑robed painter's brush stroked the sketchbook, drawing something? When Cladi was about to walk away, he suddenly heard, 'Sir, please stay.' 'Huh?' Cladi paused, turning to look behind him. 'What do you think of my painting?' Bifrons slowly removed his hat, revealing a hideous face; the horns on his head symbolized his status! 'A demon?!' Cladi's eyes widened in shock, unable to fathom how a demon could have infiltrated the capital! Bifrons held up the sketchpad, on which was drawn Cladi himself, exactly matching his current startled expression—as if Bifrons had foreseen everything; the oil‑painted Cladi was lifelike, as if Cladi's soul had been imprinted upon it. 'Evil spirit!' Cladi snapped back to alert, instantly summoning his wand to fight the demon. But Bifrons moved faster; with a red brush he lightly stroked Cladi's neck on the portrait in the painting. '?? !' Cladi's body was instantly severed—his head flew off into the air, blood spraying incessantly, the scene too horrific to behold. 'Huh‑huh...' Bifrons chuckled, gazing at Cladi's lifeless head with a faint smile, 'First one, done.'

title: Chapter 50 — The Crow
content:
Chapter 50 — The Crow

Volume 28 · Chapter 50

Bifurons looked at Cladi lying on the ground, his expression showing no concealment of contempt as he lightly remarked—

“Is this the Thorn Knight of the Kingdom of Britain? ‘Tch! He’s utterly no match.
“If this level counts as strong among humans, then who could withstand Lord Mammon’s iron hooves?”

Bifurons shook his head; the initial clash instantly killed a Thorn Knight, making him feel it was too easy.

Originally Bifurons thought each Thorn Knight could conquer and fight well, and wiping out this group would require some effort.

As it turned out, the leaders of the famed strongest knight order of Britain had only this much strength?

Bifurons felt a bit disappointed, thinking Lord Mammon’s caution was excessive; he could simply let the demon cadres swarm out and wipe out Britain!

It seems Bifurons, although he gathered much intel, did not know that the twelfth‑ranked Thorn Knight Cladi was the worst at fighting among the knights.

Being able to kill Cladi only shows that Bifurons’s assassination was successful, but it does not prove he is stronger than Cladi……

Bifurons kicked Cladi’s corpse aside, gazed at the distant splendid palace, and muttered to himself:

“Maybe this time I can really take the human queen’s head, bring it back and offer it to Lord Mammon.”
“I don’t know how the others are doing; they should be just as smooth as me….”

title: Chapter 51 — Rakshasa
content:
Chapter 51 — Rakshasa

Volume 28 · Chapter 51

“Demon!?” Morrison saw Hanpa’s appearance, his heart jolted; he had considered various possible evil forces that might infiltrate the royal capital, but he never expected a demon could sneak in! Normally demons always stay in the Demon Lord’s palace area, never leaving their activity range. Yet now they suddenly appear in a human nation? This situation inevitably calls for vigilance. Morrison tried to calm his shock, staring coldly at Hanpa, asking in an icy tone, “Are you a subordinate of Demon Lord Mammon? What are you doing here?” Hanpa laughed, his shoulders shaking, his contemptuous eyes not hidden at all, replying, “Guess?” “Surely not a friendly visit?” Morrison couldn’t guess, but being targeted by a demon is definitely not good. “Hahaha, what did you do to provoke Lord Mammon? You surely aren’t unaware, are you?” Hanpa’s attitude was arrogant; he appropriately reminded, “Did your people steal something and refuse to return it to Lord Mammon?” Morrison felt doubtful, but immediately recalled Sis’s demon armor—the former great swordsman Elfkin Sis had gone back, saying not returning Mammon’s things would definitely bring retribution. In the past, the low‑key demon suddenly appearing in the royal capital, Morrison thought it must be related to the demon armor matter. Hanpa sneered, “Demon armor—'You obviously know that yourselves, don’t you?’ Since you had the guts to steal Lord Mammon’s things, prepare to pay the corresponding price.” Morrison said calmly, “The demon armor isn’t in the royal capital; you came for nothing.” Hanpa continued, “We already retrieved the treasure, but Lord Mammon’s anger hasn’t subsided; you need your whole kingdom to bear it~” He conveyed Mammon’s meaning—actually the preciousness of the demon armor is far insufficient to spark a war. Mammon merely wants to find a noble pretext to occupy Britain, making it seem reasonable. Morrison froze, hearing that the demon armor had been retrieved back, that would mean— “What have you done to Sis?!” “Oh~, that guy who stole the armor is called Sis, huh? Too bad, he’s been eaten until not even a bone remains—” Hanpa’s face showed a… uh! Morrison hearing Sis had been harmed, his heart clenched, he instantly flew into rage, secretly regretting he shouldn’t have persuaded him to abandon that ominous demon armor. Hanpa locked eyes with Morrison, as if reading his mind, “Angry? Want to tear me to pieces to avenge your comrade? Hahaha, interesting~” “Die!” Morrison roared, his fighting spirit gradually turning into a violent red, directly entering the second state of Rakshasa Ghost! His whole body’s skin turned crimson, veins bulging, straining his loose combat uniform, windless yet automatic! Morrison kicked off the floor, his form instantly becoming a red bolt of lightning, blinking to Hanpa’s face, a dense barrage of fists shot out, swish‑swish, so fast only shadows could be caught, the density such that even a fly couldn’t dodge! “Hahaha, useless, none of your thoughts can escape my eyes!” Hanpa faced Morrison’s fierce attack, utterly unfazed, still laughing wildly? Only see Hanpa’s form turn into a ghost; with just a slight adjustment of his body he could easily dodge the torrent of fists, truly like a loach—slippery, impossible to grasp! Morrison grew more shocked, even feeling as if multiple directions were reading his thoughts, each punch landing where the opponent knew exactly! “Left! Right! Right! Left! Above!” dodging Morrison’s fists, he even deliberately announced his predictions, almost no difference, as if deliberately mocking the opponent, “Hahaha! You’re truly a blockhead, so simple it makes one pity you, your thoughts are so easy to see through!” “Shut your stinking mouth!!” Morrison’s body paused, then he gathered power and unleashed a straight punch, speed increased tenfold; even if Hanpa dodged, he likely couldn’t escape unscathed! A boom rang out in the air—Morrison’s fist struck Hanpa’s abdomen, the violent red fighting spirit surged even more wildly, striking his thin frame. “Cough!” Hanpa’s expression twisted, he coughed up blood, his face showing disbelief. “Disappear!” Morrison roared, swinging his fist and blasting Hanpa into the air! But before Morrison could even catch his breath, Hanpa’s body in mid‑air turned into countless crows, cawing as they scattered in all directions. “?!?” Morrison furrowed his brows, thinking, Did he just escape? Are demons really this easy to deal with? Suddenly, a dagger pierced from Morrison’s back, straight into his… a yellow‑clad figure? The blade seemed to emerge from his chest; Morrison watched, his face showing terror as his life began to ebb away. …… “I told you, none of your thoughts escape my eyes; dealing with a simple‑minded fool like you is truly easy~” Behind Morrison, Hanpa slowly poked his head out, his scarlet eyes flashing with the light of seeing into evil hearts. Trickles of blood ran along the dagger… Morrison’s mind began to blur… This demon can read my thoughts; there’s no way I could fail to win? No! I must not let it leave here alive, otherwise the consequences would be unimaginable. Morrison, weary‑eyed, gripped the dagger lodged in his chest, slowly turned his head to glare at Hanpa. “eL”, Hanpa felt astonished, trying to withdraw his dagger, but it wouldn’t budge? He secretly thought, this lowly human—has he gone mad? Morrison’s body reddened further, like after being bathed in blood, his crimson fighting spirit gradually consuming him. Thud‑thud‑thud, a series of penetrating sounds burst from deep within Morrison’s body, dense bone spurs shot out, aiming straight at Hanpa’s eyes! Hanpa gasped, hastily dropping his weapon and stumbling backward; his cheek accidentally… Morrison, with the bone‑spurred dagger still lodged in his chest, pointed at Hanpa without a glance, his eyes empty and lifeless. He turned to face Hanpa. “What… thing…?” Hanpa’s forehead slipped a cold bead of sweat, as if he’d seen a hellish ghost! The violent crimson fighting spirit shot up to the heavens, roaring angrily at Hanpa. Morrison was forced into the Rakshasa Ghost state. In the deep night of the royal capital, seemingly quiet yet with undercurrents, Mesfield led a squad of knights on patrol, when suddenly they saw crimson fighting spirit slash through the night sky, a monster‑like pressure spreading out. She was very familiar with Morrison’s martial arts; the Rakshasa Ghost’s pressure could only be this terrifying, like a mad bull rampaging through the capital. “Morrison?” Mesfield furrowed his brows, realizing that the seemingly calm night was already fraught with danger; he immediately ordered the knights, “Follow me!” 0Y
