Although none of them were valuable things. But for Chris, they were priceless. Treasures that no amount of money could replace~

Chris rummaged through the basket, showing a troubled expression, after a long while she took out a rattle and handed it to Pudoum behind her.

“Here you play!”

“Me?” Pudoum became puzzled. He looked at the rattle in his hand, wasn't that just a toy little kids would like?

“We are friends! These things are all given to me by mom, they are my treasures, only friends can play with me, you are the second friend who can touch my treasures, the first is Sister Minnie-” Chris said in a baby voice, meticulously tidying up the messy things in the basket.

Pudoum looked at the dusty rattle in his hand, his heart was a mixture of five flavors, hot tears uncontrollably welled up in his eyes.

He wasn't crying with joy because he received a gift from the little master, but purely moved.

Having served Merlin, this iron rooster boss, for many years, it was bitter to the point of never receiving a gift; playing with the little master for a while could get "friendship proof", this gap was not generally huge!

The little master was actually so understanding and reasonable, knowing at such a young age not to mistreat subordinates, the future is limitless! The demons of the First Demon Lord Palace will absolutely be willing to sell their lives for the little master!

Pudoum suppressed the impulse to cry, placed the toy rattle on his chest, and would cherish this "friendship proof" very much.

“Little master please rest assured, this humble one is willing to go up mountains of knives and down seas of fire for you, absolutely without a single bit of resentment! Your future self will definitely become a very excellent Demon Lord!”

“Ah...?” Little Chris looked blank, she simply couldn't understand what Pudoum was saying, thinking it was just lending Pudoum brother a toy, why would he be moved like this? Pudoum is so pitiful, was he bullied by Dad?

Besides being too young, having an innocent and kind nature and other shortcomings. She seemed to have already preliminarily demonstrated the aptitude to become a Demon Lord.

Suddenly a shadow covered little Chris's head. Lilith suddenly came to Chris's front like a ghost, looking down at her from above.

“Eh?” Little Chris raised her head, puzzledly blinking her big eyes.

Lilith narrowed her eyes, the thought of murdering Chris became increasingly heavy, a flash of light in her hand and a whip appeared, planning to strangle Chris while Merlin and Alice were not paying attention——

Little guy don't blame me, it's because you're mom's relation, you can't be left!

Pudoum was scared pale. He hadn't expected Lilith to be so bold, taking advantage of Merlin and Alice being busy in the kitchen, she actually planned to be unfavorable to Chris! ?

“Lilith-sama! What are you doing? Please don't act rashly!”

“Shut up, I absolutely don't recognize the bastard of my brother and the female Hero! She can't stay! Otherwise...” Lilith gripped the cold whip in her hand, gritting her teeth and said, “Otherwise my brother will never be able to return to my side…”

“Uh!” Pudoum was horrified, feeling Lilith had gone mad. In order to split up His Majesty and the female Hero, had she already started using unscrupulous means! ?

Clearly the little guy was already in mortal danger. But she herself was completely unaware. She simply thought Lilith was her aunt.

Little Chris lowered her head, started rummaging through her "treasure box" again, suddenly taking out an empty milk bottle! ?

“Auntie~!”

*???

Lilith looked at the empty milk bottle in her hand, her heart was full of surprise and doubt, not clear what the little guy wanted to do?

She looked at the rattle in Pudoum's hand, and immediately understood, this was "friendship proof"

Obviously Chris had used this milk bottle, and actually handed it to herself, did this mean——

I am in this child's eyes. My status is comparable to... her mother? Is that what it means?

Lilith's stance shifted in an instant. The leather whip in her hand became incredibly heavy.

“Here you go, auntie!” Chris smiled; revealing her baby teeth.

Lilith heard Chris call her aunt from the bottom of her heart, her heart seemed to be broken into pieces at once, she had to re-examine the little guy——

title: Chapter 13 — Demon-Sealing Jar
content:
Chapter 13 — Demon-Sealing Jar

Volume 29 · Chapter 13

"You are talking about the thing that I am with Alice, right?" Merlin thought for a moment and knew that Pudo would definitely bring it up. "Your Majesty, I understand." Pudo bowed, his eyes worried, saying that if the Elders' Council found out, the entire demon race would probably not let you roam outside, and might accuse you of violating taboos and punish you.

"We are not married, nor are we together with humans. Didn't I explain that clearly?" Merlin replied in surprise, thinking that as long as the true situation was known, it would be clear that he and Alice are not husband and wife.

"I trust your character, Your Majesty, and I know you won't lie about such matters, but those high‑ranking elders won't believe it." Pudo frowned seriously, thinking that Merlin was indeed still the youngest Demon Lord and didn't understand how deep the Elders' Council's influence was.

"Why wouldn't they believe it? Do they think I secretly fraternize with humans?" Merlin snorted, secretly looking down on the Elders' Council as nothing more than a bunch of old men selling themselves.

"Because of the existence of the little master, no one will believe you." Pudo emphasized.

Merlin suddenly fell silent, feeling a slight headache, realizing why Pudo was so worried: it was because of Chris's existence.

Even if the Elders' Council only hears one side, if they learn that he fathered a child with a human and claims no relation to humans, only ghosts would believe it!

"You and that female hero already have a daughter. That is an indisputable fact. With just that, the Elders' Council has reason to charge you." Pudo paused, hoping Merlin understood his situation: being with humans is taboo for demons, especially given your special status as the former arrogant monarch, and you are likely to be convicted of a serious crime... Ha. Merlin smiled, turned around, and said, "The Elders' Council, a bunch of ragtag people! If they just drive me away, fine, but they also want my life?"

"Your Majesty knows better than I do. The Elders' Council's high status is naturally because they have the power to balance all Demon Lords; otherwise, the several Demon Lords would have overwhelming strength. How could they listen to the Elders' Council?" Pudo asked anxiously.

"What do you mean?" Merlin thought, stroking his chin, and said, "Are you referring to the two artifacts left by the Demon God?"

"That's right. The Demon God is our ancestor and our creator. Although demons have evolved and the connection to the Demon God has diminished, it still has some influence on us, and those two artifacts he left are part of that." Pudo paused, then slowly explained.

The first one is called Tiel Feng, the Tear of the Great Creation. Legend says that although this artifact is powerful, it is a cursed blade; all its holders have met tragic ends, and it leads its bearer toward destruction.

"Now this demon sword belongs to Mammon; he considers it his strongest weapon. When drawn, its tearing divine power is almost unbeatable, even the great merchant Shang Zhan An feared Mammon's demon sword."

"Oh?" Merlin tilted his head thoughtfully, thinking that Mammon actually possessed such a powerful thing? He had never seen him use it.

"The second artifact is the capital that allows the Elders' Council to balance all Demon Lords: the Demon-Sealing Cauldron!" Pudo's expression grew much more serious. He continued, "This Demon-Sealing Cauldron was created by the Demon God's hand. In the distant age of the gods, the Demon God used this artifact to toy with and command his own people. All those who dared to defy the Demon God..."

"The Demon-Sealing Cauldron—Merlin had heard of this artifact, displayed on the Elders' Council's high platform, demonstrating their authority."

This artifact is considered a bane to demons, even the Great Demon Lords fear it greatly.

But Merlin didn't know much; he thought, even if it is an artifact, what does it matter? Could it really seal him?

"I don't think the Elders' Council has the Demon-Sealing Cauldron, so they would dare to mess with me. Besides, it's just a sealing artifact. Can it really hold me?" The brave warrior said, admiring him, but you don't know. Pudo frowned, emphasizing that the Demon-Sealing Cauldron is an artifact to deal with demons. Though your bloodline is thin, you still have demon blood. Even a slight one would be sealed by this cauldron, almost impossible to resist.

"Going to ...?" Merlin snorted, "Don't overthink, Pudo. Even if this cauldron is powerful, can it beat my sword? Don't worry."

Pudo was both rich and restrained; seeing Merlin's confident heart, he thought the ruler was too young to know how powerful the Demon-Sealing Cauldron was; it's something no demon can resist.

"Moreover, I believe that as long as I present the truth and prove my innocence, the Elders' Council would not dare to do anything to me." Merlin thought he was upright and straight. He feared the old elders would trouble him. Pudo lowered his head, said no more, knowing Merlin's proud nature, and just wanted this not to be known to the Elders' Council, otherwise things would become unmanageable.

"Pudo, how many years have you followed me?" Merlin suddenly laughed and asked.

"Not many—hundreds of years." Pudo answered.

Time passes quickly; I still remember the early days, carrying Lilith on the streets, and you took her in. Merlin felt the cold night air and sighed, saying, "I remember it was the same season, just entering winter, the ground was covered in frost. If you hadn't taken us in, Lilith and I would probably have frozen to death..."

"Your Majesty, don't bring up these matters; they mean nothing. I'm just an ordinary demon who disapproves of treacherous ministers and tyrants. Meeting you allowed me to rise." Pudo sighed, staying by Merlin's side.

"If needed, I am willing to die for you."

The next day, early in the morning, the household erupted into chaos. Alice and Lilith began a new round of sharp conflict.

"What! You two demons, you want to take Chris alone out!?"

"No! I will absolutely not agree!"

"I see you are getting more and more demanding. Do you have no good intentions?"

Alice, wearing an apron, holding a spatula for breakfast, pointed at Lilith and Pudo, wishing to split those two hateful demons in half!

Early in the morning, Lilith said she wanted to take Chris out for fun, and that her aunt and niece were somewhat unfamiliar, needing more time together.

This undoubtedly struck Alice's sensitive nerves. Observing Lilith's recent behavior, she always keeps washing her precious daughter, which is a rhythm of bringing Chris into the evil path!

Lilith paid no attention to Alice's question. She rolled her eyes and said, "I'm just taking my lovely niece out for fun. Why do you, a human woman, need to interfere? Are you insecure? Afraid I'll run Chris away?"

"I am insecure! I see you have no good intentions! You only want Chris to learn the ring!" Alice's eyes blazed, gripping the spatula.

"Release Chris immediately; she is my daughter!"

"Do you really think she will become one of your demons? Dream!"

"I've endured you for a long time; don't force me!"

title: Chapter 14 — Demon Cultivation
content:
Chapter 14 — Demon Cultivation

Volume 29 · Chapter 14

"What are you going to do about it?" Lilith reached down and scooped up the little Chris from the ground, speaking in a disdainful tone. "Chris is from Lucifer's family, and someday she'll be taking my brother's place..."

"Brother, you should really rein in this female Hero. Don't you think she's being a bit too arrogant?" Lilith's voice dripped with sarcasm.

"We're not being hostile at all. We just want to take Miss Hero out for a bit of fun. Please don't worry, we wouldn't dream of harming Miss Chris," Priddy puffed out his chest and declared with a guarantee.

"No way! I won't let Chris get too close to you!" Alice firmly refused.

"Mommy—Chris wiggled in Lilith's arms, pleading, "Actually, I want to play with Auntie. Auntie isn't a bad person, see—"

"Ah?!" Alice's breath caught. She hadn't expected her usually well-behaved daughter to suddenly undermine herself like this, leaving her with a feeling of being abandoned by everyone. "You're so young, how do you know who's good and who's bad? Go back inside and behave yourself!"

"But—" Chris opened her mouth to argue, feeling uncomfortable inside. She thought her mother was being too suspicious of Aunt Lilith.

"There's no 'but' about it, Chris. You need to listen to what your mother says," Alice pointed at Lilith with a serious expression. "This one isn't worth your trust. Don't let her corrupt you!"

"Hey! Hero, don't push your luck. Keep talking like that and you'll see what happens!" Lilith's veins bulged as fury flashed across her face.

Alice was about to give Lilith a piece of her mind when—Merlin, who had been silently standing there, suddenly raised his hand to stop the argument.

Merlin gave a dark look. He was getting tired of his sister and Alice's bickering; though he did notice how pitiful little Chris looked, he asked gently—

"Chris, do you want to go out and play with Aunt Lilith?"

"Want to~" Chris nodded eagerly. "Auntie says she'll buy me treats and tell me stories!"

"Oh really." Merlin nodded, waved his hand dismissively, and said, "Then let her go. Just make sure you come back before dark."

"Merlin!" Alice stared at Merlin in disbelief. Deep down, she felt Chris shouldn't be having close contact with demons, and letting Chris go out with Lilith was like pushing her precious daughter into a fire pit.

"It's fine, I'm just taking Chris out for a bit of fun. Don't be so sensitive," Merlin turned around and said to Alice with a reassuring tone.

"But—" Alice's expression flickered with conflicting emotions, and she stomped her foot in frustration.

"Still, Brother is so reasonable," Lilith smiled. Cradling the joyful little Chris, she walked out.

"Remember, don't cause any trouble outside. This is human territory, and if we're not careful, it could spark a conflict," Merlin sternly reminded them.

"Rest assured, Your Majesty. I'll keep a close eye on Lady Lilith, and we'll be back with Miss Chris in no time," Priddy declared confidently.

As Lilith left, she couldn't resist giving Alice a mocking salute, wearing a triumphant expression.

Alice's jaw twitched with anger as she glared daggers at Merlin. "What do you mean, letting Chris grow up to be an heir to your Demon Lord Palace?!"

"No, no, that's not what I meant. How could Chris be an heir to the Demon Lord Palace? She's still too young," Merlin laughed in surprise.

"To think my sister and your underlings have been going on about Chris these past few days, telling her all about the demon race!" Alice paused, her heart filled with worry. "If this keeps up, I'm afraid our little one will be corrupted!"

"Haha, no, that won't happen. They just simply like Chris. Don't imagine things that aren't true," Merlin laughed and comforted her. Lately, with Lilith's arrival, Alice had indeed become increasingly paranoid.

"You—"

Alice looked at Merlin with a strange expression, thinking this guy was being too biased toward Lilith, not even considering what was best for his own precious daughter.

So Alice took off her apron, threw it at Merlin's face, and stormed back to her bedroom in a huff, slamming the door shut with a loud bang.

"This is unbearable!"

"This—"

Merlin picked the apron off his face, looked at Alice's tightly closed door, and wore an expression of complete innocence—

Looks like I should get Lilith to leave as soon as possible.

Truly, two tigers can't share the same mountain.

A tigress mother.

Lilith walked down the street holding Chris's small hand, with Priddy quietly following behind.

Today, taking Chris out wasn't just for a simple outing.

Lilith looked at her niece Chris, who was just like a naive little sweetheart, and thought to herself—if this continues, she'll be bullied even after returning to the demon race!

So they wanted Chris to understand what it meant to be a proper demon, and how a demon should live.

Lilith planned to demonstrate to Chris what a real demon was.

Little Chris took small steps, struggling to keep up with Lilith's pace. She asked curiously, "Auntie, where are we going to play today?"

Lilith looked at the little girl beside her and said seriously, "Today, you need to learn how to be a proper demon, a real demon, just like your father."

"Demon? Like Daddy?" Chris looked up with suspicion, recalling her daily life with Merlin. In a soft voice, she said, "Is it the kind where you cook every day, help Mommy with housework, and stay up late telling me bedtime stories?"

"?" Lilith was stunned, rethinking the question, "Does Daddy really do all those things?"

"Mm-hmm, Daddy's really hardworking," little Chris nodded vigorously, feeling proud of Merlin.

"Good grief," Priddy's face turned strange. He had never imagined that the word "hardworking" would ever be associated with Merlin, especially in his daughter's eyes. The Demon Lord was supposed to be more cold-blooded and cruel—at least a little more fearsome!

Lilith couldn't hide her displeasure. She thought, "My brother is a traitor among demons. No wonder the Elders expelled him." She suppressed her annoyance and asked, "Auntie won't mention your father anymore. Auntie wants to ask you, do you know what a proper demon should do?"

"Huh?"

Chris was full of question marks. This question really stumped her—nobody had ever taught her.

Suddenly, Chris's eyes lit up. She looked up with a flushed, excited face and answered eagerly, "A demon should obediently wash their neck, waiting for the glorious Hero to arrive and chop off their head!"

"!" Lilith's face instantly darkened. She instinctively asked, "Who taught you that?"

"Mommy did. Mommy told me stories about the Church. The Heroes in those stories are so awesome!" little Chris's eyes were filled with admiration.

"Damn it!" Lilith's anger flared as she clenched her teeth, thinking to herself—

That damn Hero, our sworn enemy, yet she's so contemptible to us.

No good! I need to make Chris understand that she's the heir to the Great Demon Lord!

Step one: teach Chris how to do evil things.

The most evil thing?" Little Chris showed hesitation, very afraid, saying, "Mommy doesn't let me do bad things. Being a bad kid will get me spanked on the butt..."

"Impossible. It's definitely because that female Hero has been teaching Chris every day. Otherwise, a normal child would already be tearing the roof off the house by now!" Lilith shook her head, unwilling to give up.

"If the young master were a scheming child, she would indeed integrate into the demon race more easily, but in my opinion, she simply has no talent for doing bad things at all." Pudom spoke from the heart. Aside from Chris looking somewhat like Merlin, he really couldn't see anything about her that resembled a demon.

"Does doing bad things require talent? Isn't that something you're born knowing how to do?" Lilith glanced at Chris's bouncing figure ahead and whispered, "Don't worry. As long as we guide her a little, Chris is young and very easy to handle."

"I implore you, Lady Lilith, not to go too far, or it will be difficult to explain to His Majesty when we return." Pudom said seriously.

"What's there to fear? My brother won't say anything. It's just that female Hero who talks too much." Lilith rolled her eyes. The thought of that female Hero opposing her made her angry.

Lilith and Pudom were leading Chris along the street when they passed a bread vendor's stall and faintly caught snippets of conversation about demons—

"Have you heard? London was attacked by demons late at night not long ago. It really scared Queen Elizabeth!"

That's right! The capital has been on high alert recently, and scrutiny of outsiders has grown increasingly strict. Something big must have happened.

Lilith immediately stopped in her tracks, her curiosity drawing her gaze toward the bread stall nearby, where several humans were gathered, animatedly discussing the recent demon night raid on the capital.

Hobbs had a red nose and clutched a bottle of alcohol in his hand, listening intently beside them. He seemed quite interested in the recent demon night raid incident.

"It seems the news has been sealed off. Something must have happened. Otherwise, there'd be no need for the queen to suppress the news. She seems afraid of the demon night raid being made public."

"Nonsense! Nothing happened. It was just a few demons sneaking into the capital. What chance do a few flies have of stirring up trouble in Britain? Impossible!"

" judging by your tone, do you know some inside information?"

"Of course! A friend of a friend serves as a vanguard knight in the Magnolia Knight Order. He said several demons did indeed raid the palace recently, but the disturbance was quickly quelled, and the few bold demons were easily slain by the Thorn Knights! There was no real chaos at all."

The group chattered at the bread stall, secretly praising the Thorn Knights as still formidable. As the guardians of the palace, even demons who came raiding couldn't threaten the kingdom's security in the slightest.

Hobbs "glug glug glug" downed several mouthfuls of alcohol. With the alcohol loosening his tongue, he gradually became reckless. "Easily slaying a few demons who came to raid at night? That story the queen pushed out doesn't even need a draft anymore, does it?"

"Oh? Does Hobbs have reliable information then? There's no one in all of Lexham more well-informed than you." The bread vendor's eyes lit up. Judging by Hobbs's tone, he clearly knew something.

"Listen. Easily slaying invading demons? Sounds completely fake. And you people actually believe it? If it was a night raid, then these couldn't be ordinary demons. They'd either specialize in night combat and assassination, or be powerful demons." Hobbs paused, his drunken eyes glazing over as he added, "The Holy Church has deep roots, right? They've been fighting the demon race for so long and haven't destroyed them. How could Britain possibly match the Holy Church's profound foundations? And easily slaying invading demons? Ridiculous."

The vendors looked at each other, finding Hobbs's words very reasonable. No matter how powerful Britain was, facing demons would hardly be an easy victory.

To satisfy their curiosity, and relying on their knowledge of Hobbs, the vendors each took out a few silver coins and stuffed them into Hobbs's bottle.

"Ah, Hobbs, can you guess what happened that night of the demon raid? Tell us all~"

"I don't know what happened that night." Hobbs collected everyone's silver coins, smiling as he tucked them into his chest. "I only know that Queen Elizabeth is currently very panicked. She's probably reached the point of being unable to sleep at night."

Lilith withdrew her gaze and didn't continue listening to these small fry pontificate, but she was puzzled—

Demons raided the British queen's palace? What nonsense!

She was, after all, a acting Demon Lord. Who in their right mind would launch an attack on a human kingdom?

Due to the blood pool seal in the Demon Lord Palace, the demon race's strategy had always been passive defense. They typically would not take the initiative to attack.

Even when striking back externally, they would never target human kingdoms. They specifically attacked only the Holy Church as an organization.

Provoking a human kingdom would only draw them closer to the Church of Light, strengthening their ties. Wouldn't that just be helping the Holy Church grow stronger?

The demon race's attitude toward human kingdoms had always been one of vigilance and hostility, but toward the Holy Church it was absolute incompatibility—life and death enemies.

If any foolish demon actually attacked a human kingdom, it would immediately shatter the delicate balance between demons and humans.

As the Pope in the Roman divine hierarchy, he would laugh himself awake from his dreams. Demons truly becoming the human threat that the charlatans claimed needed to be destroyed.

Lilith's heart churned with unease. She felt that demons raiding a human kingdom was unlikely. Could the demon race truly have such a foolish ruler?

Pudom leaned over and lowered his voice. "These street riffraff probably haven't seen a real demon in their entire lives. Just listen to what they say and don't take it seriously."

"You're right. When I left, the demon race was clearly very calm. How could something happen so quickly?" Lilith smiled and shook her head.

"It's very likely another rumor spread by the Church of Light's charlatans to create panic in the kingdom and force more people to become believers. Besides, the idea of demons raiding a human queen—" Pudom paused, smiling. "It's too unbelievable. I don't believe there's any demon ruler among the monarchs who is so reckless and careless of consequences."

"I don't believe it either." Lilith furrowed her brows and thought carefully for a moment.

"What if this is true?"

"It could lead to an all-out war between the demon race and humans."

"If it comes to that, it would be the Second Holy War."

title: Chapter 17 — Talentless
content:
Chapter 17 — Talentless

Volume 29 · Chapter 17

Little Chris spotted Lilith and Pudding chatting at the back and, curious, ran over to ask, "Auntie, what are you two talking about?"

"Nothing much. You're still young. There are many things you don't need to know." Lilith scooped Chris up from the ground.

"Auntie, it's a bit cold outside. Let's go back, won't we? Daddy will have all the food prepared." Little Chris said, her heart racing with excitement.

Lilith hesitated, pouting, "No, that won't do. If we go back now, it'll look like we gave up halfway. You must learn to do bad things. Only then can you fit in with the demon race."

"But Aunt Lilith, I won't do bad things. Mommy never taught me to," Little Chris said, wearing a very uncomfortable expression.

Lilith frowned, thinking, *Alice's influence on this kid is too great. She can't even do bad things. How can she become the heir of the Lucifer family?*

"Lady Lilith, I think we should give up. The young master might just not have this kind of talent. Let's go with the flow," Pudding said from the side, believing Chris might simply be naturally this way.

"No, that's not right. Chris is family. How could she be this innocent and kind? In the demon race, such a personality would get bullied to death. Lilith frowned, complaining inwardly. It's all because of that female Hero! Chris's temperament is probably inherited from her mother. Otherwise, how could she be so weak?"

Pudding's expression shifted, thinking, *If Chris truly becomes Lucifer the Fourth, she'll have many of Merlin's old subordinates supporting her. Even if Chris is weak-tempered, there probably aren't many demons who could bully her.*

Lilith scanned the area and spotted an elderly white-haired woman sitting on a street chair, resting, with several small cakes beside her.

This made Lilith's eyes light up. She knelt down to look Chris in the eye and decided to give her a test.

"Chris, do you want to become a Great Demon Lord like your father?"

Chris blinked her big eyes and nodded, "I do!"

Lilith pointed toward the elderly woman, putting on a serious face, "Go eat that old lady's cakes. If you succeed, it proves you're truly a child of the Lucifer family and have the qualities to inherit the throne!"

"That... that's..." Chris looked far away at the resting elderly woman and showed a reluctant expression, "That's the landlady!"

"The landlady?" Lilith was puzzled, thinking, *Is my brother still renting a place to live?*

"Yes, the landlady. She comes by every once in a while to collect rent. She even brings me candy," Chris's little cowlick bounced happily.

"Very well. We're going to rob this landlady. Let's go! Be brave!" Lilith patted Chris's little butt and encouraged her from behind.

"But Aunt Lilith, the landlady is kind to me," Chris hesitated.

"Chris, as a demon you must be ruthless. Don't be easily swayed by emotions. To become an excellent demon like your father, you must abandon many unrealistic ideas," Lilith said with a strong tone.

"But Aunt Lilith, I'm really struggling. I don't really like doing things that make people dislike me, but I still admire Daddy so much and want to gain Aunt Lilith's recognition and praise."

"Come on, come on, don't be afraid. Aunt Lilith will always stand behind you and protect you. If that old hag dares to bully you, I'll torture her to death!" Lilith pushed Chris forward, making all sorts of faces to encourage her niece to be brave.

The landlady was in the middle of closing her eyes to rest. The cakes beside her were freshly bought, and the elderly woman's head lolled as she tried to sleep.

Then—

*Complete!*

*Complete!*

*Complete!*

*Complete!*

"All these cakes that I've been eating every day are mine!"

The landlady was startled awake, adjusted her reading glasses, and upon seeing Chris, broke into a warm smile.

"Chris, you came out alone? Where are your parents?"

Chris's face turned pale. This was her first robbery and she was terrified, "I-I came out with Aunt Lilith."

"Aunt Lilith?" The landlady was surprised and followed Chris's gaze. Upon seeing Lilith and Pudding's messy expressions, her look changed.

"Oh my, I'm here to rob you. I'm going to eat all these little cakes!" Little Chris stood with her hands on her hips, putting on the most fierce expression she could muster.

The landlady smiled and looked at the little kid's silly, fierce expression, then slowly said, "You're not suited to being bad. A long time ago, you weren't suited either. Whenever you lied, you'd become extremely restless; your face would turn red. If this world has any absolutely kind beings, I'd think of you first."

"Huh?" Chris tilted her head, completely not understanding what the landlady was saying. Only when she was alone with the landlady would she say such mystical things.

"Come here. Eat as much as you want." The landlady picked Chris up and placed her on her lap, then handed her a small cake.

Chris looked at the cake in her hand, feeling sweet inside, but still couldn't help but emphasize, "This... this is a robbery, landlady. After I eat this, I won't come back!"

"If all bandits were like this, they'd probably be out of work and dead long ago. You're still too young," the landlady said, looking down at Chris sitting on her lap.

"What does a real bandit look like?" Chris, holding her cake, asked curiously.

"They're all vicious people who would do you great harm. They'd hit and scold you," the landlady replied with a smile.

"Huh!" Chris remembered her experience with the civilian kidnapper and immediately felt chills, "Chris doesn't want to do that. Chris doesn't want to be a fierce bad person."

"Although I don't know why you suddenly started talking about robbery, you should stop it in the future. The old you was very likable," the landlady said, tidying Chris's hair like a grandmother taking care of her granddaughter.

"I... I just want Daddy to be proud of me," Chris looked down, saying in a sullen voice. The landlady sighed at the innocent child.

"The landlady always says how good the old me was. Does that mean she's seen me before? But I've never seen her before!" Chris patted her head and asked curiously.

"I've seen a child very similar to you. Would you like to hear that child's story?" The landlady teased. "...Want to hear it?"

Chris felt like she was being given food and then asked to listen to a story. If she didn't repay the favor, it would be too selfish.

Alice had always taught the kid to repay kindness with kindness.

So little Chris stood up, stood on the street chair, and gently swayed her head, then started patting the landlady's back!

The landlady was surprised, glanced at Chris, then looked at her with a kind smile and slowly began to tell the story.

"That child's personality is very similar to yours. Her name was Abel, full of sparkle, beloved by everyone around her. She had a sister named Cain, and their fates were completely opposite."

In the distance, Lilith and Pudding saw Chris eating someone else's food and then patting the landlady's back. They were both stunned in place.

Pudding: "Lady Lilith, let's give up. This child doesn't have the talent to become a Demon Lord."

Lilith: "What the hell! Why can't she learn to be a demon?!"

Pudding: "Although the young master doesn't have the talent to be a demon, we can be certain that in the future, she'll be a filial child."

(^-^)

PS: Demon King event, just place the free little heart on Merlin (the dog-faced one). Give Merlin more praise points, thank you very much. Also, more updates.

title: Chapter 18 — Everyone, please give Merlin a free little heart, thanks!
content:
Chapter 18 — Everyone, please give Merlin a free little heart, thanks!

Volume 29 · Chapter 18

At home, a strange guest arrived — Jacob, the young master of the Rothschild family.

Merlin and Alice, seeing a visitor at the door, gave a simple reception.

As the son of the richest man, Jacob had his nose in the air. After entering and scanning the room, he revealed a look of contempt.

Jacob had probably never stayed in such a shabby place from childhood to adulthood. To him, Merlin and Alice's home could no longer be described as merely crude.

Jacob had heard that poor people all lived in slums; he feared the filthy room before him was exactly such a gathering place for the destitute.

If Merlin and Alice knew what Jacob was thinking at this moment, they would likely be furious enough to kick this arrogant young master out immediately.

Jacob was fairly handsome, having inherited the Rothschild family's youthful bearing. His well-proportioned physique showed at a glance that he was neither a warrior nor a mage, merely an ordinary person.

Although Jacob appeared to dress plainly, every item on his body was custom-made by artisans with meticulous care; the cost was probably beyond what ordinary people could imagine.

Jacob had not brought a large retinue this time, only some guards.

After all, with Macready accompanying him, there was hardly any danger to be encountered.

The moment Jacob stepped down from the carriage and saw the remote town of Rexham, he felt instant disgust, thinking his father must be sick in the head to send him to such a place.

Did a remote little town like this really have a powerhouse who required him to come personally and invite?

Jacob felt uneasy. Along the way he had heard some rumors: the most famous powerhouse in Rexham used to be a Mithril adventurer named Karl, but now it was a female magic swordsman named Alice.

She had not only won the tournament championship and the adventurer title, but was also a foreign Thorn Knight personally decorated by Elizabeth, and recently had successfully been promoted to Platinum adventurer.

Jacob regarded this rumored magic swordsman with a measure of new respect. For a remote place like Rexham to produce such a powerhouse was already no easy feat.

After arriving at the two's home, Jacob appeared somewhat ill at ease. Looking at the furnishings, he could sense an air of "poverty" everywhere.

Jacob covered his mouth and nose with a handkerchief, as if breathing in too much "poor people's air" would kill him on the spot.

Merlin.

Alice: "That..."

Seeing Jacob standing beside the table for a long time yet refusing to sit down, looking like he minded something, the two exchanged glances.

Macready hurried forward and explained calmly, "My apologies. Young Master Jacob has never been to the slums, much less to such a shabby place. He is having a hard time adapting for the moment, and we hope you two can understand."

Merlin and Alice's faces both darkened after hearing Macready's explanation, feeling they had been looked down on by a rude rich brat.

Although Rexham was a bit remote, it hardly deserved to be called a slum.

The two lived here every day and would never find it shabby. Jacob's haughty attitude from the get-go was repulsive.

Macready couldn't help glancing at Merlin a couple more times. He thought: So this is the person the family head designated? Can't see anything exceptional about him. The family head must be getting old and senile. But that magic swordsman next to him looks like she has some skill; she might become an asset for exploring the ruins.

A maid walked in from outside and spread a fine silk cloth on the chair. Jacob's expression improved slightly, and only then did he sit down with relief.

Alice: "This guy is a bit too full of himself, treating our place like a garbage dump? Just because his family has a few stinking coins, what's so great about that?"

Merlin: "Probably a rich family's young master who's never left home in his life. Looking at his behavior, he's probably reached the point where he looks down on everyone."

The two whispered. Jacob's first impression was terrible. If not for the sake of his father's immense financial power, he would probably have been kicked out already.

Jacob lowered the handkerchief covering his mouth and nose, looked at Merlin and Alice, and took a deep breath —

"I am the eldest son of the Rothschild family. You two may call me Young Master Jacob. I am here on my father's orders to find a powerful outside aide."

"Actually, it's just a private commission, right?"

Alice asked with a fake smile, feeling the Jacob before her was too arrogant; his every word and deed exuded a sense of superiority.

She had thought that as her status rose, becoming a Platinum adventurer would earn her more respect. But this rich young master didn't seem to buy it at all.

At the Platinum adventurer level, they could no longer be easily driven by money; whether they would assist depended entirely on mood.

Alice felt a bit resentful. If this rich young master had come for her, his attitude was simply too terrible.

"More or less." Jacob leaned lazily in the chair, glancing at his nails.

"Cough cough!" Finding Jacob displeasing, Alice couldn't help needling him. "Hiring a Platinum adventurer like me is very expensive, and not guaranteed to be accepted either."

"I've hated one thing since childhood: people mentioning money in front of me. That stuff has no value to me. I can have as much as I want." Jacob raised his head and said seriously. "The things you people pursue are nothing but a pile of useless stones before me. I have no interest in money!"

Macready looked at Jacob and translated beside him, "The young master means: don't use your annual income to challenge his daily allowance. Anything that can be solved with money is not a problem..."

"This... this guy." Merlin's mouth twitched nonstop as he muttered, "What a thick nouveau riche stench. How much does he look down on people?"

"Y-yeah." Alice lowered her head slightly, grumbling in dissatisfaction. "I'm a Platinum adventurer too, yet he completely doesn't put me in his eyes."

"Platinum? So what? I'm the strongest adventurer, and he didn't put me in his eyes either?" Merlin paused, then said quietly, "This arrogant guy clearly hasn't been beaten down by society... You... what are you doing?" Alice sensed Merlin was getting angry; surely he wouldn't jump up and punch the richest man's son right here?

"I'm going to give him a hard time, make him understand a principle: having money doesn't mean you can do whatever you want!" Merlin took a deep breath, narrowing his eyes. "At your and my level, if we're still played like puppets by money, it's too pathetic!" "You're right! We absolutely can't waver. So what if he has money? This guy should first learn what respect means!" Alice nodded in agreement, planning to refuse all of Jacob's requests.

"Hey! You, the man reeking of poverty all over." Jacob slowly straightened his waist, staring into Merlin's eyes, asking with an air of disdain —

"You're Merlin, right?"

"Looks like..."

"Even more useless than I imagined."

title: Chapter 19 — Careful Heart (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 19 — Careful Heart (Extra Chapter)

Volume 29 · Chapter 19

You said what? The veins on Merlin's forehead were clearly visible, and his hands under the table were clenched into fists. Read! ? Alice glanced at Merlin, then at Jacob, thinking he hadn't come to find her; she realized she had overthought it. Probably Rothschild had seen Merlin's strength at the tournament himself, so whenever trouble arose he would think of Merlin. But his son Jacob seemed unaware of Merlin's situation, his cheerful tone lacking any respect. Merlin had already been very patient; if the person before him were Rothschild himself, he certainly wouldn't have dared to mock himself. Unfortunately Rothschild was infirm, so he sent his foolish son over? If Merlin didn't consider Rothschild's increased respect for him, he might have on the spot taught the arrogant Jacob a lesson. A sigh escaped McReady, who chuckled secretly, feeling delighted; he had anticipated Merlin would be insulted by the young master, after all, who lets a mere black‑iron adventurer compete for his livelihood? He deserved it! Jacob sat up straight, looking at Merlin with interest, and said, 'I say you're even more useless than I imagined; my father sent me far away just to see you. I thought the person my father named would surely be a radiant strongman or an extraordinary genius, but you're just a person reeking of poverty.' 'An ordinary person, do you need to rely on that beautiful mage lady beside you for everything?' 'Your father,' Merlin said, his face darkening, his voice low, 'Didn't you tell me beforehand what attitude I should use when speaking to you?' 'No need to mention him; he's already old.' Jacob pointed at his own belly, smiling, 'As he ages, his father's head becomes muddled, often making wrong judgments. Although I don't know how a lowly fellow like you made my father look at you differently, here your disguise won't work.' McReady felt extremely pleased; everything Jacob said was what he thought. A nobody, how did he make the lord favor him more? He must have used some underhanded means! 'Ha,' Merlin snorted coldly, calmly asking, 'You little young master, coming all this way, surely not just to show off your superiority and also to insult me, this lowly trash?' 'No,' Jacob replied, 'I'm simply here to carry out my father's task: bring you to the family estate as a guest.' He paused, face full of pride, and asked, 'Do you know Jewel City? There are many expensively built mansions; that's my home. Many people dream of living there for a night, but you don't even have the qualification to sweep the floors there~' 'Finished? If so, leave quickly; I really don't want to be a guest at your house.' Merlin lowered his head, speaking nonchalantly, 'How rich your Rothschild family is has nothing to do with me.' 'Yeah, if there's nothing else, just leave our house. Letting the Rothschild young master see filthy peasant scum isn't hurting your eyes, is it?' Alice said sarcastically, with hidden barbs, 'Then we won't keep you either; hurry back to Jewel City!' Seeing Merlin and Alice both issue the expulsion order, Jacob, usually calm, became somewhat tense. Although he liked to talk big, deep down he still feared his father greatly. Inviting Merlin to Jewel City is the lord's command; if Jacob fails, he'll be embarrassed upon return. Lightly he'd be scolded, severely he'd face family punishment; either is something Jacob's fragile heart can't bear. Jacob's face looked awful. As someone of noble birth, always surrounded by people, when has he ever eaten a closed‑door meal? You sure want to kick me out? Do you know how rare it is to be a guest in Jewel City? Not everyone can receive our family's hospitality. McReady hoped to see Merlin reject the lord's olive branch, but didn't want to suddenly have a competitor in front of the lord. So McReady hurriedly leaned close to Jacob's ear, lowered his voice, and urged, 'Young master, I think we should forget it. These lowly bastards have never seen the world; they don't know what our Rothschild invitation means. That's wealth!' 'No good,' Jacob frowned, 'How will I explain to father when I return?' The lord merely hopes the plan to seek divine relics can have one more capable assistant to ensure success. McReady paused, then added, 'The young master has so much money; why bother with a black‑iron adventurer? Just shout outside, and naturally many strongmen will rush to work for you. As long as you find strong people willing to help us, the lord won't blame you but will praise you.' Jacob frowned, grew doubtful, finally shook his head: 'No! Father named this guy; regardless of whether he has real talent, I will bring him back. Father's words, I just need to follow them; no need to act on my own and stir up trouble.' 'Um, that's still follow the young master's words.' McReady smiled, feeling disappointed, failing to persuade Jacob to give up recruiting Merlin… Jacob young master, you're still too young, do you really think money lets you do as you please? Someone like me, who early on grew indifferent to money, wanting to use money to make me an ox or horse is too naïve. Merlin laughed and shook his head, his tone full of disdain for the corrupt monopoly class. 'Exactly, thinking money can bring us peace, at least we must first understand that people should respect each other!' Alice wholeheartedly agreed with Merlin; it was the first time she saw Merlin possess such noble integrity, unmoved by money. Jacob didn't speak, but clapped his hands twice; immediately a group of people entered from outside, each holding a black box. He signaled the servants to open a black box; inside were neatly placed ten expensive crystal cards! Merlin and Alice had seen such precious items before; each card worth 500,000 gold coins; ten equals— five million gold coins! As expected, the son of world income; his generosity almost made Merlin and Alice's eyes pop out! 'You you you you Merlin stared at the box with the ten crystal cards worth five million, becoming somewhat incoherent. 'What do you take me for? Money is just... just dung! I would cling to dung? Don't look down on me. Ignorant young master__.' 'Pa‑ta' Jacob expressionlessly snapped his fingers; the second servant opened a black box, inside were ten alert cards of equal value. Now facing Merlin is ten million wealth. He faintly feels suffocated, dry‑mouthed, looking at the gleaming crystal cards makes him a bit dizzy‑ 'I... I'm not that kind of person. Wealth doesn't matter. Although dung sometimes tastes okay, eating too much will surely make you sick.' 'Pa‑da' Jacob understood the nonsense, again expressionlessly snapped his fingers; the third servant slowly opened a black box— Sorry, in my eyes there's no such thing as an unsuccessful negotiation— 'Not successful?' 'Just because the money given isn't enough.'

title: Chapter 20 — Exploration Team
content:
Chapter 20 — Exploration Team

Volume 29 · Chapter 20

Alice remained silent beside him, already stunned into silence by the Rothschild family's wealth.

Now that Alice had risen, with the increase in strength and status, earning money would become easier and easier.

It was said that adventurers' private commissions were very profitable, but this had already completely exceeded Alice's imagination.

Although a price of ten thousand was far less than the debt she had originally owed the Church, Alice had never imagined that one day she would receive such a profitable task, completing it directly turning her into a life winner, from then on never having to worry about money again!

Alice was still too young to compare with the Rothschild family's financial capabilities. No wonder she was a creditor of many royal families.

Driven by curiosity, Alice secretly glanced at Merlin beside her, discovering that this fellow's face was dark and his eyes were bright!

Alice was puzzled in her heart. Normally, at this moment, Merlin would already have drooling eyes and be moved, so why was he sitting upright like a proper person today?

Under Jacob's instruction, the servants slowly opened the third black box. Looking at the wealth in front of them being piled up to the figure of one million five hundred thousand!

Jacob's back was already wet with cold sweat. Thinking he had encountered a true iron-headed child, someone who wouldn't be swayed by money?

Wealth on the table. This was already the limit the son of a billionaire could produce. It was originally a gift prepared in advance by Rothschild for hiring Merlin.

Damn it! With so much money, really no thoughts at all?

Even if the rulers of the major kingdoms saw these riches, they wouldn't be completely uninterested. A lowly adventurer like this

Jacob's complexion grew uglier. Looking at Merlin, his gaze changed quite a bit. He felt he had met an opponent.

Wait a moment! "Merlin suddenly broke the silence, maintaining his facial expression as if he had something to say?

Jacob instantly secretly sighed a breath of relief, smiling and asking, "Changed your mind?"

"How could I surrender to money? I am also a man full of spirit. Would a small amount of copper smell make me lower my head? I think you are dreaming!" Merlin said firmly.

"Are you sure?" Jacob felt something was wrong. If Merlin wouldn't go back with him, his father wouldn't be able to handle it there. Originally, his father looked down on him, always thinking he was a useless fellow. If he couldn't even handle this small matter, wouldn't his father be even more disappointed?

"Merlin--" Alice looked at the Merlin beside her, feeling that this fellow had suddenly become unfamiliar, and his image seemed to have become much taller?

'Actually, whether it's money or not doesn't matter. I'm not very interested in money. I'm just a kind-hearted person. When someone asks me, I can't bear to refuse do you understand?" Merlin said seriously, but his hands weren't idle, desperately pulling the crystal card inside the black box toward himself.

Alice looked at his face. Watching Merlin, she didn't know what to say, "Merlin, your integrity

"What? Too little? Everyone heard. My lover said money, too, little~ Merlin feigned a look of indifference, speaking seriously. "Alice. I've said many times. Be a person who is real and straightforward. Don't be so stingy. How can you be like this? Someone like me, a kind-hearted person, when seeing someone in difficulty, must certainly extend a helping hand without compensation! I am truly unworthy of you who care about a fly's worth of benefits. Why can't you learn more from me, and at any time offer a little love, making everything around you become better?"

"Huh? ? ?" Alice's face turned red from being lectured by Merlin, harboring a belly of dirty words, not daring to say them out loud, "You TM are really good at being cheap.

Going

ˇ complete ˇ

ˇ this ˇ

ˇ god ˇ

ˇ station ˇ

Jacob and McCreedy gazed at Alice in turn, their eyes full of contempt, while thinking in their hearts—

This magic soldier looks upright and righteous, but in the end is a greedy fellow?

Conversely, the lowly adventurer beside him looks like a cunning fellow, unexpected but a real person!

Jacob secretly rejoiced, good thing this time he wasn't hiring this magic creator, otherwise with the other's lion's roar, he really couldn't do the things assigned by his father.

Alice gritted her teeth, resentfully thinking at Merlin, angry that her whole body was trembling, thinking just with Merlin's appearance, is he really kind-hearted?

Pfft! This fellow's number of actively helping others can be counted on one hand. Without benefits, he wouldn't even get up early!

Alice felt Merlin was clearly stealing her persona. Truly shameless to a degree ordinary people couldn't reach!

"Cough cough!" Merlin ignored Alice's resentful gaze beside him; transferring the topic said, "I don't know, Young Master Jacob. Wanting to send me to the warehouse for what purpose?"

"Tell you also no problem." Jacob paused, then slowly said, "In fact, we formed a team to explore the ruins of the gods, but we lack strong support. My father set his sights on you."

"Oh? Exploring the ruins of the gods."

Alice saw Merlin about to leave.

Traces, ran, her heart couldn't help but worry.

The guardian of the ruins was the giant of the Northern Sea.

This book was first published on EZ看书, claiming to be the absolute ruler of the seas, a legend.

But Merlin was awkward because he couldn't swim.

He wasn't good at fighting in the sea.

Even if he could defeat Clarus, there was still a danger of drowning.

This "Anhui Feng" space ring was born in the heavens, possessing a kind of strange resurrection power, a lifeline in dangerous situations.

Alice hesitated for two nights, thinking this ring, if worn by Merlin, might at any moment pull Merlin back from danger.

Merlin looked at the ring in Alice's hand, his heart filled with rejection. "The faint aura on this ring makes me very uncomfortable."

Alice forcibly pushed the "Anjieji" ring into Merlin's hand. Only this way would she feel at ease after Merlin left.

Merlin frowned, taking the ring. Although it was a gift from the heavens, it wasn't something he couldn't use. It was just that it felt very sacred.

"Then," Alice looked at Merlin, speaking earnestly, "come back safely."

Merlin's expression was awkward, his face flushed. "It won't take long."

They had always gone out together, like shadows. Now they had to part, which made Alice feel a bit unaccustomed. There were so many things she wanted to say but hadn't said yet.

Merlin looked down, frowning, feeling pressured. It made him feel like a foolish kid going out for the first time alone.

Little Chris looked at Merlin, then at Alice, and said loudly, "Come back soon, otherwise Mom will scold you. A mom in her menopause is really scary!"

"!!!" Alice's face turned red quickly. She hurriedly grabbed Chris and covered the little mouth. "What are you saying again? Don't talk nonsense!"

"Doctor?" Little Chris was confused. Why couldn't she just say what was on her mind? Dad would definitely miss him!

"Ugh," Merlin helplessly shook his head, saying in a low voice, "Is it because I'm leaving and not coming back? How could that be possible?"

While waiting for Merlin, Zhou and Alice were exchanging glances.

Pudo was awkward.

"Are you saying something? We're not being affectionate, we're just saying goodbye before the mission," Merlin's face turned black, feeling more like a third wheel than ever.

"Hey!" Liliangang handed the transmission device to Alice, her hands on her hips, glaring at Alice. "Take good care of Chris at home. She's the only one of our demon race. If there's any problem, you'll have to prepare to apologize yourself."

Alice smiled politely but didn't mean it, hugging her precious daughter tightly. "What are you? When did I ever admit that Chris is your demon's only one?"

"Ah? The female hero's only one?" Liliangang's face immediately turned difficult.

"Time is short, hurry up!" Merlin, seeing Liliangang and Alice about to fight, quickly pulled Liliangang away.

"Chris, Auntie will bring you some delicious food," Liliangang kept saying to the little girl.

"Yay~" Chris happily waved her little hand, but noticing Alice's bad mood, she quickly became quiet, covering her little mouth and not daring to make a sound.

Alice watched Merlin leave.

This guy was always careless. Without her around, could he really manage?

Merlin looked at the ring "Anzhoujian" in his palm, subconsciously smiled, thinking maybe this was how Alice expressed her feelings? She was afraid he wouldn't come back.

Far away, Yakubo had been waiting impatiently. Seeing Merlin approach, he directly asked, "Did you finish the mission?"

Merlin nodded.

title: Chapter 23 — Declaration of War from Mammon (Bonus Chapter, Free Hearts for Friends)

Chapter 23 — Declaration of War from Mammon (Bonus Chapter, Free Hearts for Friends)

Volume 29 · Chapter 23

Merlin's face alternated between blue and white, his hand instinctively reaching for the sword at his waist. He felt an urge to strike down Lilith. "Wait, you two, don't be so agitated," Merlin soothed, turning to address the scene. "Am I not allowed to enter the Gemstone City just because of these two?"

"Merlin, please make it clear," Macready sneered, glancing at Lilith and Pudding with disdain. "Is it you the Rothschild family is wary of, or someone else? Don't think that just anyone can meet the master of the house."

"What did you say?!" Lilith's face turned fierce as she stepped forward. Pudding seemed sullen but was secretly brewing magic behind his back.

Seeing the situation getting out of hand, Merlin suppressed the agitated Lilith and Pudding, turning to say, "Since they can't go, I won't go either. The Gemstone City is the domain of the world's richest man; we commoners naturally can't aspire to it. Let's leave."

As Merlin and the others turned to leave, Macready felt extremely pleased. He hadn't expected Merlin's temper to be so large, that just a few words would send him away. He had thought it would take a lot of effort to drive Merlin away, but it was surprisingly easy.

Jacob, though looking down on Merlin as a mere Jianghu swindler who had gained his father's favor, knew clearly that if Merlin didn't visit, his father would definitely blame him.

Thus, Jacob hurriedly opened his mouth to stop them. "Please wait!"

"Oh? Does Young Master Jacob have something to say?" Merlin turned back, a meaningful smile on his face, having anticipated they would try to retain him.

"You can be my guest; I have no objections." Jacob nodded in agreement.

"Is that so? But what about your guard?" Merlin looked at Macready with interest.

Macready's face fell as he quickly lowered his head, whispering, "Young Master, this isn't good. The old master invited him personally and didn't permit him to bring companions. If something happens, the old master will blame you."

"He won't return with me, and Father will blame me just the same." Jacob glanced at Macready casually. "It's just two attendants; what's the big deal? With you here, could they possibly cause trouble?"

Macready, though pleased by Jacob's trust in him, still didn't want this "swindler" Merlin to disrupt the family's peace. "Young Master is right, but..."

"Just stop talking." Jacob interrupted Macready. "Let me handle this matter fully."

"Yes, Young Master." Macready's brows furrowed, though unhappy, he didn't dare disobey.

"You all go to the carriage in the back; I don't like sharing the same air as strangers." Jacob sighed, thinking, Who wants to breathe the same air as poor people?

Lilith felt these people's attitude was terrible and couldn't help but complain to Merlin, "Brother, these lowly people are too arrogant. We should give them a lesson!"

"Yes, Your Majesty, I never thought that originally weak humans would be so overbearing?"

Pudding chimed in from the side, "Today is really an eye-opener!"

"Ha ha, humans aren't the livestock you think they are. Like us, they have all kinds of people, naturally including some narrow-minded frogs in the well." Merlin wasn't bothered, treating this as a common occurrence.

"But Brother, you're the Great Demon Lord. In the demon realm, who dares to show such contempt for you? Outside, even trash would jump up?" Lilith was very indignant. "Brother, you should let them see the Great Demon Lord's might. If not, these two-legged creatures will fly to the sky! Don't you know how powerful our demon race is? We mustn't always lower our tails!"

"Your Majesty, I think Lilith is right. Sometimes, your magnanimity won't be appreciated by others and might even make some small fries overstep." Pudding spoke seriously for Merlin. "Your Majesty is what kind of person? The first king who could suppress the Crusade Army and defeat the Pope. Now, even a small guard dares to be rude to you? Isn't this taking advantage of your kindness?"

"Damn it! How can they be so disrespectful to Brother? I hate that I can't cut out his tongue. If it were me, he would already be dead. Brother is just too kind." Lilith kept urging, hoping Merlin would show his demonic might and let these insignificant people see the power of the Great Demon Lord.

With Alice not by his side, Merlin was slightly influenced by Lilith and Pudding's words, even feeling they had some reason.

Merlin looked at Macready, who didn't hide his contempt. He thought, This little guard is making things difficult for me. Did I offend him somehow? If not, I really need to "educate" him properly.

Macready also looked at Merlin, thinking, What are they whispering about? They must be harboring evil intentions. There's plenty of time on the road; I'll have the chance to make this lowly adventurer roll away.

Now, even a good-for-nothing like him wants to climb into the Rothschild family? With me here, not even a fly can enter the magnificent palace.

Under Elizabeth's control, the kingdom had barely restored peace recently.

Although some clever people had noticed the kingdom's danger, overall it was still under Elizabeth's control.

Elizabeth constantly sent out many spies to gather information on demons outside, preventing a large-scale invasion.

Under such heavy mental pressure, Elizabeth had become very tired, not sleeping for several days and nights as she tightly guarded the kingdom's defensive lines.

But today, Elizabeth received a letter from the Third Demon Lord Palace's Mammon.

"Dear Queen Elizabeth,

I am the embodiment of poverty, Mammon.

Your subordinate, Cedric, stole my treasure, this despicable act angering me.

Although he has paid with his life, my anger won't be so easily extinguished.

You must take responsibility for your subordinate's actions and hand over the entire Kingdom of Britain as compensation.

You have three days to respond. Surrender, protect your people, or face war. The people of Britain will be annihilated!"

Elizabeth's body trembled with rage as she slowly put down Mammon's letter, growling, "This is all just an excuse. Mammon just wants to invade the kingdom and slaughter the hardworking people of Britain!"

"This isn't even a letter, it's a blatant declaration of war!"

It would take some time to reach Britain's coastline.

However, Mamon had long since calculated—

in so short a time, Elizabeth could hardly organize a decent defense line,

and even if she sought reinforcements, she would struggle to get much help.

The "Alliance of Races" that Mamon worried about

was nothing but a mirage—

such a threat did not exist.

He did not believe that selfish humans would unite against him,

risking extinction to stand with the Britannian Kingdom.

Hidden within the demon armor,

Mamon appeared more mysterious than ever.

Even his old subordinates could not see his true face,

leaving the demons uneasy and anxious.

Mamon stood on the war chariot, slowly unrolling the map,

glancing at his position, a hint of unease crossing his heart—

Leviathan, don't try to challenge my dignity at a time like this.

Let my army pass the strait,

or you will pay dearly for your recklessness.

The Third Demon Lord Palace's army,

though striking straight toward Britain like a sharp blade,

on the way there lay a formidable obstacle—

"the Strait of Messina."

The Strait of Messina,

also known as the "Sea Monster Strait,"

was inhabited by human-faced birds with claws sharp enough to tear through a knight's armor,

like a gourmet slicing through a creature's belly, devouring its organs.

The evil spirits serving the protective king Leviathan

were not what they feared most—

what truly horrified them was the spirits' singing.

When the sea spirits used their voices to sing a heavenly melody,

it meant everyone would be claimed by the sea.

Legends passed down to this day tell sailors:

"When you hear the angelic song, abandon all resistance,

go appreciate the melody after the ship wrecks on the rocks,

write your last will upon the stone before death,

place it in a bottle, and let it drift—

or your body will be devoured by ugly ghouls,

not a single bone left!"

This saying has spread through nightmares, becoming sailors' folklore.

The North Sea Giant seemed to have swallowed many sailors alive,

yet the sea spirits had spread tales of their terror far and wide,

making people feel as if they were witnessing the horror firsthand!

Whenever the sea spirits began to sing that haunting melody,

it foretold the doom of any ship passing through the "Strait of Messina."

Fear had been endured by countless sailors—

for the "Strait of Messina" was Leviathan's territory,

and only by passing through it could a fleet sail safely.

Thus, for the Third Demon Lord Palace's army

to march straight toward Britain,

the "Strait of Messina" was an unavoidable path!

Though Mamon did not wish to provoke Leviathan,

detouring around the "Strait of Messina" would cost enormous time and resources.

After carefully weighing the pros and cons,

Mamon decided to take his chances—

perhaps Leviathan would let them pass.

The Strait of Messina sat before the Sixth Demon Lord Palace,

guarded by a fortress built upon the sea,

impregnable and difficult to assault.

The Holy Church had attacked it several times,

and every single time, the Saint-tier warriors returned empty-handed.

Leviathan, roaming the seas so freely,

was a foe no one could deal with—

who could find a way against it?

Therefore, the Sixth Demon Lord Palace,

known as the "Strongest Fortress" among the demon race,

had withstood the most attacks,

yet remained unscathed—

a feat worthy of its reputation.

But the fortress guarding Leviathan's Demon Lord Palace,

though called the "Strongest Fortress,"

had become somewhat hollow now,

for its glory had been quietly eroded by Melin.

The deep foundation and heritage that Melin possessed

with his profound knightly arts

had shattered the Saint-tier warriors, leaving them fleeing in disarray.

Melin's Second Demon Lord Palace

was far more worthy of the title "Strongest Fortress."

In the garden behind the Demon Lord Palace,

perhaps a short-statured youth,

among a circle of teenagers,

was watering the flowers with single-minded focus.

He wore dirty clothes,

a straw hat shading his face,

completely absorbed in his work.

This boy looked no older than a playful child,

yet doing the work of an elderly gardener—

it was enough to make one bewildered.

Just then, a sea spirit descended from the sky,

"Screech!" Its claws crushed the yellow roses

the youth had tended with his own hands.

The creature broke the silence, flapping its wings in panic,

kneeling with a terrified expression,

reporting frantically to the boy's slightly trembling back.

Spray from the seawater splashed warmly,

suddenly turning violent—

the sea spirit's claws, like sharp blades,

stabbed straight at the single-eyed creature,

the buzzing sound making one's hair stand on end.

"Impossible!" The sea spirit cried out in terror,

its voice suspended in the air.

Leviathan stood motionless,

looking at the sea spirit among the yellow roses,

"Who allowed you to enter this garden?

Besides me, no one else can appreciate the beauty here.

You crushed my precious roses—

that shall be your death sentence."

"Your Majesty! The situation is dire—

your subordinate had no choice but to barge in!

The sea spirit stared at the figure suspended in midair,

panicking as it reported—

"The greedy lord Mamon's

army has entered my territory!"
