title: Chapter 26 — Alert
content:
Chapter 26 — Alert

Volume 29 · Chapter 26

Here's a translation that follows all the rules:

"Mafa led the army of the Third Demon Palace, and the passage into the Messina Strait was about to be breached!" A jellyfish-like creature inside the sea felt its heart skip a beat, and the water blades before it trembled as if they might take his life at any moment. "The opponent is almost armed to the teeth, coming with such an aggressive aura—they clearly didn't come here for peace, but are heading straight for us!" Under the threat of death, this sea jelly fired its連珠 (continuous) attack, not even opening its mouth before explaining the situation. It presented the threat currently facing the First Demon Palace, with the current situation displayed before Tantalus. ★First★Release★EZ看书★

A sharp sword suspended before the jellyfish, swiftly cutting through, forcing this wretched creature to beg for its life. Hearing the news that Mafa's army had entered the land of Bar, Tantalus showed no reaction. Instead, he grew even more calm, pouring yellow wine over a cluster of yellow roses.

Tantalus's subordinates saw Tantalus's indifferent reaction and hurriedly said anxiously, "Your Majesty? The situation is critical. If Mafa's army enters the Messina Strait, we won't be able to stop it in time." Tantalus turned his back to the jellyfish, leisurely watering flowers. With deliberate, slow movements, "This Mafa, this money-grubber, what does he think he's doing, coming to my place?" Though Tantalus and Mafa are both leaders of the demon race, there is no friendship worth mentioning between Demon Lords. Behind closed doors, they are engaged in open and secret struggles, each wanting to carve a piece of meat off the other's body. If not for the existence of the Council of Elders, they wouldn't need to worry about other forces interfering, and the demon race would have started a civil war long ago.

Such a relationship has no familial bond; it's as if the Council of Elders had forcibly bound them together. As long as they are still fighting to the death, the internal strife between Demon Lords—similar to the friendship between Merlin and Asmodeus—is tacitly permitted among the Demon Lords. Among several Demon Lords, this is considered an extremely early occurrence.

The jellyfish's subordinates felt heavy-hearted listening to Tantalus's utter indifference. In the demon race, Mafa is notorious for his bad reputation. He's known as the "Iron Rooster" who forcibly takes others' treasures but doesn't allow others to covet his treasures; he is the Demon Lord with the most inflated ambition and desire.

"Your Majesty, are you really planning to let Mafa's army enter our territory?"

"What's the difference?" Tantalus retorted, not regarding Mafa in the least.

"Mafa has always had wolf-like ambitions and greedy desires, which are clearly evident. If his army is allowed to come to our grounds, it's like bringing a wolf into the room." The jellyfish subordinates paused, speaking sternly, "The Strait of Messina, which we guard, is of great geographical importance. All commercial ships must pay us a toll to pass safely; otherwise, they can only bypass the strait. Only by occupying this place can we easily return to gold, enough to plunder the entire demon race's demons. Would Mafa really be willing to miss this?"

Tantalus's heart trembled, and he suddenly lifted his head. Though he appears as a young creature, his eyes seem to peer into the depths of the abyss, radiating cold vigilance. He knows very well that Mafa's mouth is huge; there is nothing he wouldn't covet.

Now occupied by the Sixth Demon Lord Tantalus, the Messina Strait, with its geographical position so advantageous, is practically a treasure trove of wealth. Greedy Mafa surely has reason to covet it.

"Now that Mafa's army is coming with such momentum, it's probably not just ordinary training," Tantalus made a serious judgment.

Tantalus lowered his own visor, and though his body appears that of a youth, it suddenly radiates the aura of a high-ranking being, lofty and hard to approach, "Gather all demons in the Demon Palace capable of fighting now; let's go meet this old friend."

"Death!"

Only the serpent-necked sea dragon on the warship continuously roared, Mafa leading the demon army, constantly approaching the Messina Strait, almost pressing against the gate of Tantalus's First Demon Palace!

The crisis before them seemed as if Mafa held a hunting bow, pressing against Tantalus's mind, forcing him to take a stance on the battlefield?

Mafa's heart was filled with worry, and he clearly knew Tantalus's true attitude.

Regardless of whether Tantalus agrees to assist him, the Messina Strait is a must-pass place!

To attack Britain, one must first gain control of the Messina Strait—

This is because the strait is a throat passage; it's the necessary route for the Southern States to go to Britain. As long as one occupies here, to a large degree, one can isolate the Britain Kingdom, making it difficult for southern forces to lend aid. Especially the unnamed church of Rome, Mafa dislikes the Orthodox Church's aid to Britain; letting them complete that round alliance of hands will inevitably increase Mafa's losses.

If the Church dares to send reinforcements of Temple Knights, Mafa, who occupies the strait, has the capability to block the Temple Knights, letting them watch Britain become their own territory.

Secondly, the Third Demon Palace is too far away. If Mafa wants to win this war, he needs two jump points, becoming a temporary headquarters, and can continuously apply pressure to the Britain Kingdom.

The combination of these two factors prompted Mafa to decide to take a risky gamble, whether Tantalus agrees or not, he must temporarily seize control of Tantalus's First Demon Palace.

Mafa's army gathered at the entrance of the strait, temporarily stopping their advance, breathing out after a while, patiently waiting for Tantalus to come talk personally.

But who could wait that long? Tantalus did not appear; instead, his jellyfish subordinates came late?

The jellyfish subordinates trembled their wings, lightly touching the sea surface to stabilize their bodies, and slowly lifted their heads, seeing the giant sea dragon with a neck like a snake staring at them, they immediately felt a strong sense of pressure.

Hidden within the demon armor was "Mafa," seeing that Tantalus did not appear, he sent out only a jellyfish subordinate. This clearly means he doesn't put himself in his eyes, showing no respect at all!

"How can it be just you? Where's your master? Let Tantalus come see me personally! I have some things I want to talk about face to face with him!"

"Very sorry, I'm just delivering a message on behalf of His Majesty." The jellyfish subordinate's tone was firm, gritting his teeth and saying, "Mafa, your greatness and bravery make us submit. Although the Hai Lian clan follows Tantalus, we still feel admiration for you."

"Spouting rainbow farts, what did Tantalus say?!" Mafa could not hide his irritation in his heart.

"Tantalus hopes you withdraw your army immediately; since today's matter hasn't happened yet, if you really want to calm down and talk with the Majesty, please change the time and come to the sea alone single-handedly." The jellyfish subordinate's tone was serious, indicating Tantalus's attitude, and that he won't be intimidated by Mafa's power.

After hearing this, Mafa's heavy helmet suddenly turned cold, as if looking from a very far place at everything "Seeking death 112"

title: Chapter 27 — Kin Raise Blades
content:
Chapter 27 — Kin Raise Blades

Volume 29 · Chapter 27

After hearing Leviathan's cold reply, Mammon was furious, feeling looked down upon by Leviathan. The situation was delicate; Mammon did not want to openly clash with such a strong enemy as Leviathan, and if he did not resort to some underhanded tactics, a direct confrontation would hardly allow him to defeat the sea demon lord Leviathan. However, Mammon now wanted to negotiate with Leviathan, peacefully resolve the conflict, have Leviathan assist him soon, and make the Strait of Messina a temporary base for his legion. But Leviathan completely ignored Mammon, not even giving him a chance to sit down and negotiate, making the situation worse. The demons' mutual scheming began to show, as Elizabeth had predicted—wanting the demons to unite was nearly impossible; from start to finish they harbored grudges and basically did not trust each other. As long as the demon lords did not sincerely combine their strength, they were like a sleeping tiger—threat to the human‑dominated world was not great, of course except for Merlin, that unbeatable special existence. Although Mammon only wanted Leviathan's assistance, temporarily renting the territory of the First Demon Lord Palace, Leviathan could hardly believe such "nonsense"; who could guarantee that Mammon, whose desires were huge, would not seize this opportunity to occupy Leviathan's territory, allow Mammon's army to enter the Strait of Messina and station many demon troops there—equivalent to inviting wolves into his home, causing trouble; Leviathan would not allow himself to have such a presence in his eyes. Facing this grim situation, Mammon felt immense pressure; his time was running out, he could not afford to waste time sparring with Leviathan here—his battle letter had already fallen into the hands of the human King An, and delaying only let the Britannia kingdom recover its name, his three subordinates would have died in vain. Originally Mammon had planned a quick victory, to crush the seemingly strong Britannia so they could not even raise a hand, war emphasizing speed. During the stalemate between Mammon and Leviathan, if Britannia organized strong defenses or reinforcements arrived, Mammon would suffer huge losses. Control of the Strait of Messina was extremely important, it was a crucial phase of the war; every minute here Mammon felt his heart roasting on fire, each second costing his life. Mammon, not dead, explained to the sea: "I have no interest in your territory, nor will I invade the Strait of Messina; I only hope to get a piece of land to temporarily settle. Leviathan, that short‑sighted fellow, could it be that his inner self differs from his outward appearance? Do you think I would occupy here for no reason? Don't underestimate my ambition!" The sea demon's subordinate slightly lifted his head, smiling intentionally or unintentionally, saying: "That's still undecided; it's because your ambition is too vast, so we must be on guard—after all, in front of you, only talking about benefits, not trust, all demons understand this clearly." Mammon's face turned cold; hearing it sounded like praise, but actually it was mocking him as an ambitious, reckless small fry. Even Leviathan's subordinates dared to sneer at him, showing no respect for their lord; how could Mammon, who was usually flattered by the lowly, endure this? The demon lord's sensibility could not tolerate lowly lesser demons provoking! In his fury, Mammon pulled the reins, the sea serpent before his chariot roared, kicking up hundred‑meter waves—"Give you a chance to live! Let Leviathan come out and meet me; I have a secret matter to discuss privately, otherwise don't blame me for being impolite." The sea demon's subordinate, resolute and fearless of death, saw Mammon's furious appearance and increasingly believed the other harbored ulterior motives: "My lord Ba Jing has spoken clearly; please leave quickly. If you act recklessly, you will not only be punished by the Council of Elders, but also witness the bravery of the demons of the First Demon Lord Palace." The sea demon's words were powerful, both soft and hard; not only invoking pressure from the Council of Elders, but also showing that Leviathan's Demon Lord Palace feared not Mammon—would Mammon swallow this bait? He frowned, then gave his reply. As soon as the words fell, the captive sea dragon opened its bloody maw and sprayed at the defenseless sea demon; powerful water bubbles fell from the sky like countless sharp water blades woven into a net, blasting the sea demon before all demons of both sides. Mammon's demon soldiers behind saw this, all slightly injured; they did not expect such a terrible situation—peaceful use of the strait was utterly wishful. The sea demon lurking in the sea saw his kin Ba Jing harmed by Mammon, his eyes widened; he never imagined the lord of greed would go so berserk! No trace of kinship remained; he could at any moment pick up a blade and slash his kin—truly a cold‑blooded lord who talks only of profit. As the saying goes, when beating a dog you still look at its owner—Mammon's harming of Leviathan's subordinates was like slaughtering pigs and dogs without scruple; when would he regard Leviathan as an equal? Only Mammon knew he was forced by circumstances, with no other choice. To win the holy war and gain huge benefits, he had already staked much of his wealth; he had reached the point where he could not afford to lose. The Strait of Messina must be taken; delay would cause the war to slip from his control; he could not afford to waste time with Leviathan here—violence was the most effective, direct solution. Most demon lords were conservative pacifists who defended emptiness; Leviathan was one of them; even if Mammon could meet Leviathan face‑to‑face to negotiate, it would be hard to sway him to assist; moreover, he might leak the plan to the Council of Elders, and if the holy war failed to ignite, the Council would suppress it. Thus Mammon's heart hardened—since Leviathan would not give him a chance to negotiate, don't blame him for being ruthless. Now even if Mammon said he did not want to invade the First Demon Lord Palace's territory, Leviathan would never believe him—today there would surely be a fierce battle—"Leviathan this baby‑faced monster dares to show up before us! All day we must let him feel our might—launch an all‑out assault! Take control of the Strait of Messina, make the First Demon Lord Palace our stepping stone!" Mammon's men raised their arms, shouting, summoning the troops behind to charge, wanting to quickly seize the First Demon Lord Palace. The demons had never experienced killing their own kin hand‑to‑hand; they were at a loss, only knowing that going out meant slaughtering humans, but could it be that we were fighting fellow demons? However, everyone were Mammon's subordinates; those who could fight alongside the demon lords were loyal and steadfast, would not question Mammon's orders. The Third Demon Lord Palace's army began a full‑scale assault on the Strait of Messina, its banner pointing straight at Leviathan's Great Demon Lord Palace! Killing intent filled the air; demons mounted the strait, their shouts shook the heavens, an unstoppable force crushed any obstruction; the magic cannons on the warships repeatedly launched, boom boom, shells flying, fire filling the sky. Mammon's Demon Lord Palace was indeed the wealthiest among demons; even his demon troops were stronger than those of other Demon Lord Palaces. At first glance, it seemed like a sunset rhythm—suddenly! A heavenly, ethereal voice sang! The sea demons flew into the sky, circling above the enemies' heads; with a beautiful melody they separated out a death‑like realm.

title: Chapter 28 — Demon Lord of the Sea
content:
Chapter 28 — Demon Lord of the Sea

Volume 29 · Chapter 28

The Siren Queens' songs rose simultaneously, melodious and rising and falling, high and low notes intertwining to compose a concert that field workers could not hear. ★First★ release ★EZ Reading★ Like colliding golden spears and iron horses, like the majesty of a rainbow returning, like the tranquility of a small bridge over flowing water—the melodies blended together without seeming abrupt, instead encompassing ten thousand homes into an intoxicating allure!

Listen for a while and your consciousness gets dragged into abyss-like dreams, your body like a puppet with severed strings, limp and listless.

Seemingly songs with no attacking power, yet able to subtly lead enemies to the path of death—truly horrifying!

Mamon's army was indeed powerful. Throughout the entire demon race, their combat power and equipment ranked among the top. Against sea creatures, brute force gave them absolute advantage.

But those frail sea creatures actually relied on their own songs to successfully cut off Mamon's unstoppable momentum.

Demons hearing the heavenly melody became like drunk men, breaking free from Mamon's control and running amok.

They sank into the sea, killing each other, treating comrades as enemies, showing no mercy whatsoever.

Demons on warships lost all reason, laughing madly and turning the ship's wheel—right before huge reefs they couldn't see.

Fires erupted everywhere on the battlefield. The warships' mage cannons fired indiscriminately, and warships kept crashing onto the reefs.

The aggressive demon vanguard legion fell into chaos under the Siren Queens' songs.

The Sixth Demon Lord Palace's decline was instantly reversed—the sea creatures singing in the sky watched Mamon's pawns slaughter each other.

On the war chariot, Mamon's face turned black. Seeing his subordinates so pathetic, played with by the sea creatures like a child with ants, he instantly erupted in fury.

But thinking carefully, his army was strong with robust soldiers and excellent equipment. Against sea creatures specializing in mental attacks, he truly had no good countermeasures.

Fortunately, Mamon himself was strong enough—this level of mental attack only made him feel somewhat irritated.

Watching his army in chaos, Mamon violently pulled the reins, and the snake-necked sea dragon reared its head and long-roared to the sky.

"Roar!!!"

Terrific sound waves echoed through the sky, bursting the sea creatures' ears bloody and sending them falling from the heights.

Demons awoke from their dreams,茫然 looking around, seemingly unclear what had just happened.

Snake-necked sea dragons were powerful sea beasts, far stronger than the Siren Queens. This roar not only repelled the sea creatures but freed demons from the songs' harassment.

"You bunch of trash! You low-level demons, singing songs and you're played around like that—you deserve to be my slaves?! Still resisting the Siren Queens' songs? Haven't you cut off your own ears?!"

Mamon shouted curses, using the insults to stir the mad dogs' fighting spirit. Demons hearing the curses, immense shame forced them to quickly regroup—some even cut off their own ears.

Mamon's army morale greatly boosted, charged again, battle cries shaking the sky, constantly approaching Leviathan's lair.

The sea creatures were like frightened birds, fleeing in all directions, the Demon Lord Palace retreating. With that sea dragon present, their songs didn't work.

Originally the Demon Lord Palace demons wanted to persuade Mamon to retreat, but who knew Mamon would fight without restraint—caught off guard and suffering greatly!

The sea creatures were also demons from the Demon Lord Palace, temporarily assembled—how could they resist Mamon's regular army?

Leviathan's elite subordinates were mostly still in the palace, waiting for news of Mamon's retreat. Who would have thought the returning sea creatures looked terrified, as if something big had happened?

Mamon having messed with his wife, might as well not rest—with the vanguard directly occupying Leviathan's lair, the rest could be dealt with later!

Demon pawns just stepped into the Demon Lord Palace's range—suddenly the ground shook violently, winds and clouds changed!

Huge dark clouds above gathered into a massive vortex! The sea became restless, constantly raising huge tsunami waves. Mamon's warships swayed, some flipped directly.

The snake-necked sea dragon seemed to sense this terrifying upper predator, became uneasy and trembled, plunging its long neck into the sea.

Standing on the war chariot, Mamon felt something was wrong, body swaying, cold sweat sliding down its forehead.

"It's... the Sea Demon Lord Leviathan?!"

Crackling! Accompanied by thunder and lightning, the demons ahead hugged their heads and knelt, trembling with fear—everyone knew that creature called the sea beast was not something a small character could handle.

The rotating clouds were peeled apart, slowly revealing a dragon-like head, looking incredibly huge. If it fell, the entire strait would disappear from the map!

The seemingly wide strait, compared to Leviathan's head, was only about the size of a rice ball. Not to mention most of the sea demon lord's body hidden in the deep sea—its head was already above the clouds!

With ordinary people's small brains, it's hard to imagine Leviathan's enormity and terror.

Buzz—Space trembled. Leviathan opened its two blood-red big eyes. In the dim sky and earth, they rivaled three big red lanterns glowing—gorgeous and bizarre. Those not killed on the spot had extremely high psychological resilience!

Part of Leviathan's body surfaced. Its scaled body, snake-like and agile, easily surrounded Mamon and his army within the strait, not planning to let any escape.

Looking at Leviathan's snake body, towering and imposing like solid walls—the entire Strait of Messina was shrouded in huge shadows.

Mamon stiffly looked around. Himself and the vanguard seemed to already be in a cage, now like trapped beasts, uneasy—

"Could it be...?"

Leviathan appearing in this form to meet him—was it wanting to fight to the death? Demon lords showing true form without doubt meant real anger. Like Asmodeus's Fly King form, rarely shown to humans. Who would have thought the feared sea demon was a horned little child?

Mamon suppressed his unease, acting calm and shouting loudly.

"Leviathan, you finally agree to meet me. Sorry for messing up your courtyard, don't mind. Let's talk seriously. Actually I'm not here to occupy your territory—just hope you can help..."

"Killed my subordinates and still stand before me. Do you think I'll believe your ghost words? Drop dead!"

Leviathan's voice like rolling thunder, eyes full of anger, opened its mouth that swallows heaven and earth, red mist surging from the fang-filled deep throat.

At this moment, everyone was shocked—even Mamon wasn't calm anymore, clearly feeling the opponent's real anger.

"Leviathan! You dare?!"

Earth-shaking, the sky and earth darkened further.

From Leviathan's mouth erupted a crimson destruction cannon, sweeping the entire sea area.

Terrifying power—even gods would retreat. No matter how advanced alchemy, cannot create such power magic cannons!

Mamon screamed repeatedly. In the crimson mist, the destructive power made demon armor cry for help. As for Mamon's pawns?

In an instant, demons, warships, snake-necked sea dragons—all turned to ash!

I'll write an extra update now, everyone be careful with your hearts and give gifts, thanks!

title: Chapter 29 — Tyrfing
content:
Chapter 29 — Tyrfing

Volume 29 · Chapter 29

Thunder rolled through the churning clouds, lightning stitching across the sky while smoke and mist clung to the air. The aftershocks of the attack slowly faded, yet the sea refused to calm.

Mammon's advance guard had been annihilated the instant Leviathan appeared, not a single one able to fight back. That proud sea serpent had lost all will the moment it sensed Leviathan's aura.

Mammon's army was powerful, their equipment top-grade, yet against a Demon Lord enraged, resistance was impossible—the gap in strength was simply too vast.

"Ka... cough, cough..."

Violent coughing echoed across the beach as Mammon crawled out from beneath heavy armor, his body utterly weak, draped in seaweed, a sorry sight.

The demon armor covering him was already cracked all over; not being turned to dust by Leviathan's strike was luck in itself.

This battered appearance bore no resemblance to the majestic king he'd been moments ago—more like a stranded general.

Mammon rose slowly, scanning the surroundings. Scorched earth met his eyes everywhere, corpses burning, most reduced to rubble by Leviathan's bombardment.

Behind the thick helmet his expression was hidden, but his sighs revealed a foul mood—defeated before the fight even began.

Leviathan, growing bolder, had killed my vanguard. If not for this armor, I might not have survived either.

Mammon lifted his head, staring at the sky. Leviathan's massive head filled his vision, and fury boiled in his chest.

Leviathan's two red lantern eyes flashed with uncertainty. He'd thought his attack had made Mammon fear him, that he couldn't resolve Mammon's power and had only saved his troops through force.

But reality was clear—the Mammon before him was weaker than imagined. This was still only Main-tier strength.

What puzzled Leviathan was the aura emanating from the armor—it belonged to Mammon himself.

Leviathan's great eyes darted, staring at the Mammon before him. The thick armor wrapped him completely, not even eyes visible. Considering Mammon's cunning and his collection of strange toys, Leviathan suddenly saw through it.

"Hiding behind the scenes while sending your own warriors to die—that's your style, you shameless lowlife!"

"Ha ha." A low laugh came from Mammon. "Thanks for sending a puppet to see me. You're still the same—a cowardly rat. So you fear me that much?"

Leviathan's voice thundered across the sky.

"Pu, pu, pu." Mammon coughed and laughed bitterly. Since he'd been seen through, there was no point hiding any longer. "You know this kind of trick fools most lords, but not you. Pity my work still has flaws."

Before Leviathan, Mammon slowly removed his helmet, revealing an empty head. Even inside the demon armor, there was nothing—empty.

Mammon wasn't inside the armor at all. He didn't even know where he was!

From the very beginning, Mammon had never been here. No demons had fought. It was merely an empty demon armor shell, moving on Mammon's command.

Compared to when the dead demon had worn it, the armor had changed greatly—more majestic and solemn, its power greatly amplified, even carrying Mammon's own aura. Leviathan had almost been fooled.

"How? Do you like my little toy?"

Leviathan snorted, the very sky trembling. "Hmph! Imitating Meyr as a headless knight?"

"Only that brain-dead guy can be imitated! Don't compare an idiot to me!" Mammon snapped, then immediately switched to a smug tone. "This armor's been reforged by me, infused with my blood. I've established a blood link. It can't fully replicate my power, but it's close. Impressive?"

Leviathan's eyes narrowed slightly. The world around them dimmed a touch. No wonder he couldn't sense Mammon from the start—the armor already had a blood link to Mammon, hence the same Demon Lord aura. If this armor could truly match that level...

A legion infinitely close to Demon Lord strength. Terrifying?

If Mammon could truly achieve this, it would deter any power in the world.

"I have no interest in your toy. You attacked my territory and slaughtered my troops—you should be prepared for a blood battle. See?"

"I advise you to calm down—" Mammon's voice echoed from inside the demon armor.

"I have no intention of killing your troops, nor of seizing your territory. I only hope you'll help me—hand over the Strait of Messina for a time."

"Oh? Another public topic?" Leviathan was shocked. Daring to ignore the Elder Council and strike openly—what was Mammon plotting?

"Holy War! The Third Holy War! I'll be the one to start it! The era of demons will return, and I—"

Mammon removed his helmet, spread his arms, and declared with boundless passion, "will gain the wealth of humans!"

"You're out of your mind? War? The First Generation haven't died enough?" Leviathan was so startled he jumped, watching Mammon's series of mad moves—this wasn't a joke.

"The world only has two kinds of beings—cowards who are prey, and heroes who are predators. I am the hero. We cowards are your opposite. I will surely stand at the peak as the predator, and your era will become my prey!"

Mammon paused, then said coldly, "You have only two choices. Assist the demon race and benefit me—I'll use the Messina Strait as a springboard to attack the human kingdoms. Otherwise, I'll remove you from the Demon Lord's throne."

"You're an incorrigible idiot, Mammon!" Leviathan panicked, rage surging. "The demon race's recovery to this point wasn't easy. Your actions are无异 to pushing the demon race into an abyss. If the heavens awaken, there'll be no return! The Elder Council will seal you in a pot, and they'll never let you out!"

"When I return victorious, all my kin will understand my intentions. They'll thank me for tearing apart the false peace."

Mammon paused, then let slip a sea rumor. "Beelzebub already stands on my side."

"The Elder Council—how can they stop me? Beelzebub actually..."

Leviathan was truly stunned. The usually low-key Beelzebub standing with Mammon, this madman? That was no good sign.

Beelzebub, as the only original Demon Lord, possessed unfathomable power, vast experience, and claws reaching everywhere in the demon race. The Elder Council obeyed him!

No wonder Mammon had been so reckless. Had he prepared this long ago? Were Mammon and Beelzebub enough? Would the demon race fall into a war trough and decline from this?

Anxiety gripped Leviathan. He felt the demon race's situation was dire, teetering on the brink of extinction.

"Where are you? Before this is controllable, I'll bite off your head! Not just to avenge my subordinates, but to crush your ambitions in the cradle!"

Meanwhile, far from the strait, in Mammon's old nest, the Third Demon Palace.

"Where am I? Haha." Mammon, dressed in magnificent robes, rose slowly from the throne and walked out toward the palace gates.

His capable subordinate Ose followed respectfully behind, head bowed, silent.

Mammon had never actually left the palace—he'd been in the nest the whole time. Yet Leviathan had been fooled by his puppet?

Outside the palace, Mammon's cold gaze fixed on the distant direction of the Third Demon Palace.

He raised his hand to the sky. Lightning cracked across the void. In Mammon's hand appeared a peculiarly shaped sword—one of two relics left by the ancestor demon god, a true artifact. Tyrfing!!!

title: Chapter 33 — In Trouble

Chapter 33 — In Trouble

Volume 29 · Chapter 33

The priest was not an elderly man.

He looked quite young, probably just a novice priest from the Church. The novice priest glanced at Bares's disheveled appearance and couldn't help but feel a silent contempt. *I don't believe you!* Where were those purified evil souls? They'd all been purified into the bed, right? How could someone like him possibly be a Temple Knight? It seemed the clergymen around the Holy Father weren't that impressive after all.

Though the novice priest cursed inwardly, he wore an understanding smile on his face, not daring to offend Bares easily.

As a noble Temple Knight Commander, Bares would receive respect and preferential treatment no matter which church he visited. Even if he broke the commandments, it would be done utmost effort to conceal it; otherwise, not only Bares, but the entire Holy Church would lose face.

What was a female knight doing in such a dirty place? If this got out, it would cause quite a stir, and might even tarnish the glorious image of all the priests.

"Understood, Commander Bares. You are leading by example, sacrificing your own body to save the sinful souls of these fallen women. No wonder you're the Temple Knight Commander, a true model for clergymen of our generation."

"Hmm, not bad."

Bares nodded in satisfaction, thinking this young novice priest was quite well-behaved and had a bright future ahead. For a moment, he felt a bit puffed up with flattery.

But who knew, before the young priest finished speaking, he added, "Commander Bares, your deeds here should be reported to the Holy Father. He will surely reward you."

Bares's face changed. He quickly put on a serious expression. "Cough, cough! That's unnecessary. As a Temple Knight, I've long cast aside worldly insults and dedicated my body and soul to the Goddess. No matter how great the achievement, I care not for it. There's no need to boast about it."

"Oh? Is that so? Commander Bares's enlightenment is truly admirable. No wonder you're always by the Holy Father's side." The novice priest smiled faintly, not intending to expose him further.

"Let's put that aside. Didn't you say you had urgent business with me? What is it? Speak."

Bares relaxed, slouched in his chair, and popped a grape into his mouth.

"Last night, a carrier pigeon brought a secret letter from the Holy Father, addressed specifically to you." The novice priest pulled out a red envelope from his chest. It seemed to have been sealed with a spell.

"Hmm? A secret letter from the Holy Father?" Bares's expression changed drastically, his eyes immediately turning serious. He quickly swallowed the grape and took the letter.

The exalted Holy Father rarely wrote letters himself; usually, the Cardinals wrote them on his behalf.

One didn't need to think to know that a letter personally written by the Holy Father must contain something of utmost importance, allowing no room for carelessness.

Although Bares was a carefree man, he held the Holy Father in the highest reverence and would never show the slightest neglect.

Bares made a few hand gestures in front of the secret envelope, and it directly turned to ashes, leaving the sealed letter intact.

These gestures were the password to open the secret letter, known only to high-ranking clergymen like Cardinals and Knight Commanders. Ordinary people who received such a letter without knowing the gestures would only cause it to self-destruct, making it impossible to uncover its contents.

Bares read the Holy Father's secret letter with great seriousness. The furrow between his eyebrows deepened, as if he had encountered a troublesome matter.

The novice priest dared not speak beside him, but was very curious about the letter's contents. For the Holy Father to write personally, it must be something extraordinary!

After reading the letter, Bares immediately used his battle qi to shred the paper into pieces, preventing a third party from seeing its contents. His worried brow gradually relaxed.

"I originally thought that after playing around out here, I'd be punished upon returning. But it turns out I accidentally did a good deed. It seems I don't need to return so eagerly after all."

"Commander Bares, what do you mean?" the novice priest asked, puzzled.

Bares's smile was profound as he looked at the novice priest, clearly not intending to reveal the letter's contents to anyone. After all, this insignificant priest didn't have the clearance to know such top-level secrets.

Actually, the letter's contents weren't that secret. It roughly said that the Holy Father hoped Bares wouldn't rush back to Rome, but instead stay in Britain to assist Queen Elizabeth, in case a large-scale demon invasion occurred. The Holy See would try to send reinforcements to rejoin Bares as soon as possible.

Though the letter was brief, Bares still sensed the danger hidden beneath the calm.

"Father, has the demon race been acting unsettled lately?"

"I haven't heard anything like that, but recently the sea has been sealed off with spells. It's not easy to leave Britain. I heard it's not safe to go out to sea lately?" the novice priest shared the recent rumors.

"Indeed." Bares nodded knowingly, thinking the situation was worse than he had imagined. The demon race, which usually adopted a defensive strategy, was now unusually taking the initiative to attack humans? This was unprecedented!

"Does Commander Bares know what's happening? Could you perhaps share some information?" the novice priest asked eagerly.

"Don't worry your heart out. We are the messengers of God, and all disasters will stay away from us. You must firmly believe in this point." Bares patted the young priest's shoulder, speaking animatedly. "The Holy Father didn't say much in the letter, just that there's a beautiful lady who needs my help. I must uphold the knightly spirit, pull that beautiful lady out of the mire, and let her see how powerful my cannons are. Oh ho ho~"

Some time later, at the edge of the ocean, a fishing boat was working here.

Two sturdy fishermen were busy, energetically pulling the net from the sea.

"So heavy!" one fisherman grunted through clenched teeth.

"This is a good thing, we're sure to have a great haul today!" the other fisherman shouted.

The two of them poured sweat, using all their strength to pull the net, convinced they'd catch a big fish today.

After a while, with a "splash" sound, the net was pulled up. No big fish appeared. Instead, a completely naked young boy was hauled up, wrapped in a small school of fish.

The boy's eyes were tightly shut, in a coma, oblivious to everything around him. He was none other than the fallen Demon Lord of the sea, Leviathan!

"Dem... demon?!"

One fisherman's face turned pale with shock.

"Damn it! Don't you see it has horns?!" the other fisherman struck the first one, looking at the boy in the net. He tried poking Leviathan twice with a pole, but got no response. "It's clearly a demon, but it's injured. Quick, get the axe!"

The first fisherman, stammering, pointed at the boy in the net, "Kill it! They say demons are all evil!"

"Kill your ass!" the second fisherman hit him again. Looking at the boy in the net, his eyes showed a hint of greed. "A lone demon is rare. If we sell it to the Rothschild Merchant Guild, we'll make a fortune!"

"Look how clean and fair-skinned it is. It'll satisfy quite a few rich old men's strange fetishes."

"You

"Although master values you, say you in competition continuously defeated opponents—but I believe these weren't seen by master, just hearsay. The competition was interrupted in prelims, almost no one knows what happened."

"Rumor champion adventurer is someone else? Laugh to death—such rumor exists, see how ignorant people are~"

"I think master values you, wouldn't harm the real champion—that's you right?"

"You guess?" Merlin face calm smile, quietly watching McReddie perform.

"No need to guess—master old, judgment not like before, believe such absurd rumor?" McReddie shook head sighed, posed friendly.

"Private investigation, always unknown small adventurer, no great ability—advise return now, don't expose at master, then bad outcome. Lose face small, lose life not worth~"

"Is that so?" Merlin tilted head, asked confusedly. "Want to see how I lose life?"

Heard this, McReddie face black instantly, gaze became fierce. In his eyes, Merlin shameless—reached this地步, not admit cheating, instead pose all in control!

McReddie can't stand this type—want harmonious steal livelihood before master? Truly fearless.

"Don't think I don't know what you're thinking—just eyeing Rothschild wealth, want to extort?"

"Tell you, dream! No chance. At gem city too late to regret!"

"I'll tear your fake mask before master, let master see your true face—we'll see."

McReddie angry, left with sleeve flip—didn't expect Merlin like plaster? Can't drive away. Decided no chance for Merlin, at master, how to shame country bumpkin!

McReddie didn't know—rumor from prelims, real champion is someone else, that's Merlin, all true!

Merlin face calm, watched McReddie leave, couldn't help cold laugh—

"Ignorance"

title: Chapter 35 — Leader (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 35 — Leader (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 29 · Chapter 35

Chris watched as McLeod swaggered away, and her expression became unreadable. "Brother, are you really just letting him walk away like that?"

"Hmm?" Merlin turned toward Lilith, thinking that this woman couldn’t sit still for a second and was itching to draw her sword and slaughter every last one of them.

"Ugh, this bastard just rode roughshod over us! We should teach him a lesson, brother. Are you a turtle? Can you really take this?"

Lilith was furious, hoping her brother would show some backbone.

"You’re right, Your Highness. Lilith is absolutely correct. Your current attitude is far too lenient. You can’t coddle these people—they need to fear you. The more they fear you, the better," Prometheus muttered beside him, thinking Merlin was being far too soft and that this situation called for a demon’s ruthless approach—anyone who didn’t kneel deserved to be crushed.

"Actually, we’re here to see Lord Roschilde, and that old man isn’t bad. It’s just the clowns jumping around him that are the problem."

Merlin’s tone was indifferent, ignoring McLeod’s provocation and giving Roschilde’s faction some face.

Besides, Merlin genuinely wanted to join the ruins exploration team. Whatever treasures were inside, he was deeply curious.

McLeod leaned in and whispered to Jacob, "Fourth Uncle, look at this guy—he’s got Lord Roschilde wrapped around his finger. I tried, but it’s no use. This fraudster’s pretty sharp, like he’s convinced himself he’s some big shot."

Jacob’s face flickered with concern. "You’re sure he’s just some backwoods adventurer?"

"Of course I’m sure! Do you not trust me, Fourth Uncle?"

McLeod’s voice was sharp with defiance.

"How could I not trust you? Your strength—I know it well. Even with the family’s full resources, you’re only this powerful. There aren’t many who could beat you, and if you say he’s just some con artist from the sticks, I won’t doubt you. It’s just…" Jacob paused, his tone skeptical. "My father might be getting old, but he’s a sharp businessman. He’s never misjudged a person in his life. If he’s putting so much effort into this, then…"

"Fourth Uncle, you have nothing to worry about. When we’re in front of Lord Roschilde, I’ll make sure this fraudster’s true colors show."

McLeod puffed out his chest with confidence.

"Let these petty thieves know—Roschilde’s money isn’t something they can just take!"

After arriving in the Gemstone City, Merlin stood there, stunned.

Not a single brick in the entire mansion—every surface was covered in gemstones! The whole place sparkled blindingly, and anyone seeing it for the first time might go temporarily blind.

Was this even a house for people to live in? It looked more like something a god would inhabit!

Only the obscenely wealthy—those with no idea how to spend their money—would build something so extravagant.

Though they’d heard rumors about the Roschilde family’s wealth, no one truly grasped just how rich they were. But looking at the opulence of Gemstone City now, it was clear.

Lilith was left speechless. This place was far grander than the Demon Lord Palace! The jewels stored there probably weren’t even worth as much as the smallest slab of stone here!

"Your Majesty, where did the owner of this place come from? This is just… too extravagant," Prometheus tried to stay composed, but he was still stunned.

"This is the wealthiest merchant in the world," Merlin said, staring at the lavish mansion. A cold realization settled in his mind—he had seriously underestimated Roschilde’s fortune. The little advantage he’d taken earlier was nothing compared to this.

Now, he finally understood the true meaning of exploitation and greed. A fire of rage burned in his chest, and he wanted to scream four words:

Prometheus’s eyes lit up, and he quickly pulled out *Merlin’s Sayings*, scribbling down the four characters—

Merlin grabbed Prometheus by the throat and shouted furiously, "Erase it! Now! This is robbery—stealing from the rich to help the poor! You idiot!"

Merlin was warmly received by Roschilde, though Jacob clearly looked down on him. But the wealthy patriarch had already decided that Merlin was the kind of talent money couldn’t buy.

Seated in the grand hall, they prepared to discuss the ruins exploration team.

"Merlin, coming here in person is truly an honor for our humble household!" Roschilde bowed his head, clearly having something to ask.

"Humble household?"

Merlin coughed, thinking—what kind of "humble" was this? Everything he saw here was priceless.

"Merlin—"

"Enough. No more empty flattery. Just get to the point."

Merlin cut Roschilde off, having no patience for meaningless pleasantries. He only wanted to know about the ruins.

Seeing Merlin’s arrogant demeanor in front of the family patriarch made McLeod seethe with frustration. His face darkened as he snapped, "You backwoods Brit, watch how you speak to the family head! Don’t get too big for your boots—"

"McLeod, shut up!"

Merlin was a guest here, and you have no right to speak like that!" Roschilde quickly intervened, afraid Merlin would storm out in anger.

Seeing McLeod get shut down, Lilith and Prometheus exchanged smug glances, thinking this old man was far more pathetic than their own guards. They knew clinging to Merlin’s coattails was the way to get ahead!

McLeod’s face turned an even darker shade of green. He clenched his fists, saying nothing, but in his mind, he fumed—how could the family head treat this fraudulent backwoods adventurer so well? He’d served loyally for years, yet this nobody was getting all the attention!

Roschilde was present, so Jacob, the fourth uncle, kept a low profile, quietly observing. He wondered—if this man could make McLeod, his father’s trusted aide, look so insignificant, then Merlin must have a serious background.

"Merlin, don’t take it to heart. McLeod is just my guard—he’s used to things," Roschilde explained.

"Does it matter if he’s just a guard? He’s still just noise in the corner," Merlin said indifferently, spreading his hands.

"You—!" McLeod’s face twisted in fury, convinced Merlin was just lording it over him because Roschilde was backing him.

Merlin ignored McLeod’s darkening expression and subtly glanced toward the older man.

"Since you’re putting so much effort into organizing this ruins exploration team, I assume you’ve already obtained the key to entering the ruins, correct?"

"Merlin, you know about the additional conditions for entering the ruins?"

Roschilde was genuinely surprised.

"Of course." Merlin thought—how would I know? It’s just that Da Vinci’s knowledge is vast, and I’ve only skimmed some demon race texts, mostly historical stuff.

"If Merlin is so direct, then I’ll be just as honest. Yes, I have the key. As long as we follow the navigation chart to the ruins’ location, the key will let us in."

Roschilde paused, then continued slowly.

"But this ruin isn’t something to be taken lightly. The journey is filled with unknown dangers, and success isn’t guaranteed.

"Especially the North Sea Leviathan—it’s the guardian of the ruins. Human strength alone won’t be enough to defeat it."

"So the exploration team must be strong enough. And you think I’m the best choice to lead it!"

Merlin nodded after hearing this, understanding Roschilde’s intentions—he wanted to use Merlin’s strength to succeed in retrieving the treasure from the ruins.

"I’ve fought the North Sea Leviathan before."

"I don’t consider it the biggest obstacle in exploring the ruins.

"Though I was at its mercy in the sea, on land, I can crush it in seconds with a single punch."

Merlin smirked.

title: Chapter 36 — Clear-cut Raid
content:
Chapter 36 — Clear-cut Raid

Volume 29 · Chapter 36

"Hmph!" After listening to Merlin's explanation, McReddy couldn't help but let out a cold snort, thinking: truly bragging without any basis, not even a shred of humility, and daring to team up with the North Sea Kraken? What a joke—if this country bumpkin adventurer could really fight the North Sea Kraken, would he still be alive and running his mouth? Probably doesn't even know how truly powerful the North Sea Kraken is! Such trash, even a kraken would spit it out—no one wants it!

McReddy looked at Merlin with disdain, thinking this country bumpkin had no sense of humility. But when Rothschild heard that Merlin actually had experience fighting the North Sea Kraken, his face lit up with excitement—he felt like he'd struck gold.

Very few people in this world had actually seen the North Sea Kraken with their own eyes. Even experienced old sailors had likely only heard rumors. The Kraken's power, passed down through countless mouths, had long been mythologized in their hearts—an almost invincible existence on the seas.

To obtain the treasures in the Ruins of the Gods, the North Sea Kraken was an obstacle that must be overcome. So the expedition team must be composed of powerful members with rich sailing knowledge, and the leader must possess extraordinary courage, ideally remaining calm when facing the terrifying Kraken.

At this moment, Merlin's value stood out—he was strong enough and had actually fought that legendary monster. Such a person was harder to find than a needle in a haystack. Was there any better choice for leader of the Ruins of the Gods expedition than Merlin?

"Mr. Merlin, are you serious? You fought the North Sea Kraken?"
"Of course I'm serious, though my condition wasn't great at the time—I only barely scraped by." Merlin answered nonchalantly.

"That's incredible too. How many humans who've seen the North Sea Kraken haven't escaped from its claws?" Rothschild's eyes sparkled with excitement. "Mr. Merlin truly surprises me, always making me underestimate you. Having this precious experience is enough to greatly increase the expedition's success rate!"

"You flatter me," Merlin smiled, thinking it wasn't a big deal. After all, he'd been restricted on the ship at the time.

Podom and Lilith stared in astonishment. Merlin casually mentioning such an experience shocked both of them. On the surface, Merlin seemed like someone just trying to save face abroad, but actually it wasn't like that at all...

If Merlin revealed all his experiences and opponents, everyone present would probably drop their jaws in awe, prostrate themselves in admiration. The scales of enemies he'd faced—whether the legendary strongest Burning Legion, or the Dark Elf King Asmodeus, and other sovereign-level figures—were all slain by Merlin.

Pulling out any one of them would make everyone present gulp down a mouthful of cold air, marveling at Merlin's legendary experiences. An ordinary person who'd faced even one of Merlin's enemies could boast for life, become famous, and be a hero in countless hearts.

But to Merlin, none of this was worth boasting about—just a bunch of rural bullies jumping around before him, dying with a flick of his wrist for peace and quiet.

Lilith, curious, whispered: "Brother, you've really seen the North Sea Kraken?"
"Seen it." Merlin nodded.
"Compared to the Leviathan, how is it?" Lilith pressed.
"Hmm," Merlin thought for a few seconds, whispering, "Hard to say. Both are monsters that roam the seas, both tricky for me. Killing them isn't hard, but I might suffer too."

Lilith's face turned serious, wondering what "not hard" meant in her brother's mouth! On the open sea, the Leviathan was nearly invincible—this North Sea Kraken's reputation probably surpassed even the Leviathan.

"Your Majesty, I have a question—is what you're discussing the ruins of the gods, their dwelling place?" Podom wasn't interested in the Kraken much, but the ruins fascinated him. He'd read many books; the gods' dwelling was like a fairyland.

Merlin nodded, confirming Podom's guess. Anyway, he'd find out eventually.

Podom fell silent, his mind racing. No wonder His Majesty gathered this rabble—the goal was the Ruins of the Gods? With one divine artifact he could dominate a region; if His Majesty had three true divine artifacts, wouldn't the Demon Lord Palace rise to dominate the demon race in an instant?

Thinking this, Podom's smile turned lecherous, saliva flowing freely, already composing a new passage for the "Merlin Quotations."

"Haha, Mr. Merlin truly lives up to being one of the few strong people I've ever met—not only is your strength peerless, but your humility too. I truly admire you!" Rothschild praised Merlin sincerely. "You're a smart person, so I won't beat around the bush. I hope you'll lead the ruins expedition team—so name your price."

Merlin smiled, took a deep breath—time to discuss the split. He thought for a moment, weighing it, then held up five fingers. "Five million!"

Rothschild immediately frowned. This price was astronomical—even the richest man felt some pressure. Such a price would make Merlin the highest-paid adventurer in history. And quoting the rich wasn't something every adventurer dared do—Merlin was indeed rare.

McReddy saw Merlin's price, his face darkening. Thinking this country bumpkin had the audacity to name such a price on the spot! Was he worth it? The master would never agree to this unreasonable demand!

Rothschild: "Fine, I agree to this price."

McReddy: "What???"

Rothschild calculated mentally—yes, Merlin was expensive, but considering his value, it was勉强worth it. After all, the treasures in the ruins were still monetary.

McReddy thought Merlin's price was already outrageous, but then an even more bizarre thing happened—

"Wait, you misunderstood. That's not what I meant." Merlin shook his head. Five fingers didn't mean five million. "What I mean is, from the ruins, whatever we take, based on value, I want fifty percent."

The moment these words left his mouth, the three opposite them turned pale as ghosts, nearly choking on their own spit.

Merlin wasn't just "selling himself"—this was outright barbaric bullying. This condition for the Rothschild family was "humiliation."

Before Rothschild's father could say anything, McReddy behind him couldn't sit still—he stood up and shouted:

"Country bumpkin, you're robbing me! (▼皿▼)"

title: Chapter 37 — Asking for Death
content:
Chapter 37 — Asking for Death

Volume 29 · Chapter 37

"You're nothing but a hired adventurer, and you dare to name a price for exploring the ruins right off the bat? Have you no bottom line? No adventurer has ever dared to throw such an absurd figure at the Rothschild family!" McReddy couldn't hold back and jumped in to rebut, seeing Merlin go further and further off the rails, even throwing out what was practically "robbery" conditions.

The Rothschild family's influence was enormous; as a great family they controlled the economic lifelines of numerous human nations, but the wind would still give them face.

This adventurer from the countryside could brag all he wanted, but to come out swinging with such an outrageous demand from the start—clearly he didn't put the family's massive power in his eyes! If Merlin actually had real talent, fine, but with that kind of trash he thought he could name such a high price? It was just the rhythm of a one-time grab-and-run!

McReddy gritted his teeth in hatred and decided he'd find a way to stop this "suicidal" transaction no matter what.

Lilith, protecting the Rothschild patriarch Merlin, chose silence at this moment and didn't stop McReddy's rude move. In her view, the conditions Merlin offered were indeed absurd, even feeling like he was crapping on their heads.

"You Merlin, even if you're experienced and powerful, you can't just blurt things out like that!"

Rothschild had been a merchant his whole life and had never encountered someone like Merlin. He felt somewhat that the price Merlin named was too steep, so he let McReddy's discourtesy slide—making a fuss was fine.

Rothschild felt he should let Merlin know he wasn't weak and not anyone could share a drink with him.

Seeing McReddy's aggressive stance and having endured the cold sarcasm all the way, Lilith couldn't hold back any longer and wanted to teach this despicable human a lesson. "Who do you think you are?" Opening this price was completely reasonable. Besides, Brother agreeing to join the expedition team was already doing them a huge favor—normally, it'd take a few more bribes to get Brother to lift a finger! What a drag!

Lilith stood up angrily, surging momentum toward McReddy.

"What's the big deal? My brother just wants half the shares, not all of them. That's already being very generous to you! Stop bellowing here—what choice do you even have?"

"Hey, Lilith," Merlin's face grew awkward, thinking he looked like a bandit himself; he still couldn't bear to shut out opposing opinions entirely.

"Hah! Your brother is just a nobody adventurer from the countryside! Demanding to explore the ruins like that, aren't you afraid of bursting yourself? His value is at most running errands on the expedition team. Such a price—he's qualified?" McReddy rolled his eyes.

"How can he not be qualified! You're a frog at the bottom of a well—probably haven't seen a powerhouse like my brother your whole life! Say it and I'm afraid I'll scare you to death—my brother—"

Lilith subconsciously wanted to reveal Merlin's Demon Lord identity to scare these ignorant humans.

But the moment Lilith opened her mouth, Pompeii blocked her, stopping her from accidentally causing a disaster. "Lilith, don't go blabbing about that, or it'll bring trouble to His Majesty. We're demons—if these humans find out, there'll probably be big trouble."

Hearing Pompeii's low reminder, Lilith gradually calmed down. Almost selling her brother out—all because of that guard's face-picking attitude earlier, resentment had been building up inside her.

"Hmph! Why no more talking? Realized the reality?" McReddy said triumphantly, feeling he'd successfully intimidated these country-bumpkin old foxes.

Rothschild, seeing things had reached a proper conclusion, coughed twice to play the good host. "McReddy, say a few words, don't be so rude to guests."

McReddy shut his mouth with a smirk, thinking after making such a scene, this bunch probably wouldn't push further? Clearly a bunch of vagrants and drunks trying to extort money—pathetic!

"Merlin, what do you think—maybe you could change the conditions?" Rothschild probed tentatively.

"No need. Looks like you have no sincerity either—forget about joining the expedition team." Merlin stood up directly, telling Lilith and Pompeii, "Let's go."

"What?! " Pompeii froze, and once he figured out the situation, he followed Merlin in shock, thinking—those are ruins we're talking about, just giving up like that?

"Yeah! Brother is so powerful, why suffer here?" Lilith hurried after Merlin, turning back to spit an insult, "You're all just a bunch of country bumpkins who've never seen the world—regret it!"

Seeing Merlin leave so decisively, Rothschild nodded and walked away, but his heart still burned with unease. "Merlin, wait—stay!" Jacob had been silent the whole time; seeing Merlin leave, he sneered inwardly—just like McReddy said, still just a con artist running scams everywhere. No benefits gained so he left; if he truly had ability, would he tolerate others bothering him repeatedly?

Rothschild's heart sank afterward, having overestimated Merlin's patience. Recalling Merlin's performance at the Amenius Arena, it was still vivid in his mind.

Without Merlin's help, what use were his mountains of gold?

"Master, don't be angry. That guy's just a fraud—where would he get any real power? I've observed him for days; not a single trace of power fluctuation. Just an old nobody with no talent." McReddy suppressed his grin, seizing the chance to spit out what was in his belly. "You're old now, hard to guard against such small tricks. Should've let me help you."

Rothschild pointed at McReddy, speechless, eyes rolling white. McReddy was a genius warrior nurtured by the family, always confident in his own words.

But now because of Merlin, his beloved watchdog actually thought he was senile? Let it go—this is it then?!

"Master, don't worry. Exploring the ruins—I'll take full responsibility, guarantee I won't disappoint your expectations!" McReddy looked at Merlin's back, grinding his teeth in sarcasm. "I've seen plenty of frauds like this—don't know how many little rats are eyeing your wealth. If it weren't for you holding me back, I'd have challenged him right now and exposed his true colors instantly!"

Merlin, who had walked to the far end, heard this sentence and suddenly stopped, laughing as he turned back. "Hah—I didn't know any stray cat or dog could challenge me now?"

"What? You still don't believe it? Believe it or not I flick my fingers and turn that weak frame of yours into a wreck!"

McReddy's pupils contracted—he suddenly stepped forward, his killing intent bursting out from his body.

"You just left like that—I can let you off."

"Now turning around to provoke me—that's asking for your own death!"

title: Chapter 38 — Want to Play with the Controls?
content:
Chapter 38 — Want to Play with the Controls?

Volume 29 · Chapter 38

Yamir scowled. "You don't know how powerful McCreedy is. He's the kind of prodigy we've never produced in our family. Don't be fooled by his lack of fame; he's always been guarding his father, and he's probably stronger than any of the powerful warriors you've seen outside."

"Oh? So a rich family's bodyguard is so powerful? My brother would bow his head and lick his tail when he sees me, and this bodyguard is the same!"

"That's right. You all have such narrow minds. Warriors built with money aren't anything special. Most of them are just showy faces."

Lilith and Pudohai laughed, making Yamir feel even more superior. They thought it was funny how he was showing off his superiority.

It was like how little kids in kindergarten play, being stupid and ignorant. How could they not laugh at that?

"Heroic pillow? Ha, you're the first to call McCreedy that." Yamir paused, then said proudly, "To cultivate McCreedy, you can't imagine how much effort and money we've spent."

"We chose the top thirty children from the Rothschild Orphanage, and McCreedy was one of them. He has incredible talent in martial arts. At the age of thirteen, he was already a high-tier cultivator, and even if he didn't cultivate, he could become a Saint-tier warrior within two years."

"A Saint-tier warrior at fifteen? Even outside, that's a prodigy that would make the royal family take notice."

Lilith scoffed and didn't bother to respond, but she couldn't deny that McCreedy's talent was impressive. At fifteen, he could reach Saint-tier, which was indeed a prodigy.

Pudohai was amazed at how much humans could learn compared to other races. That was undeniable. However, he regretted that their lifespan was too short. Even with cultivation, they still couldn't match the longevity of other races.

"We spent a lot of money buying the most beneficial cultivation techniques, powerful magic arts, and rare magic beast cores, and we poured them all into McCreedy. He's the elite warrior built with money." Yamir's two "guards" knew how expensive McCreedy was and how much money was needed to cultivate such a strong warrior.

"The process of becoming a warrior is not just about money. Warriors built with money are not worth mentioning. It's like plucking a plant to help it grow, which may seem fruitful, but it also stifles its potential. That's not a good thing. I dare to say that in terms of strength, your warriors don't have a single advantage."

Pudohai was confident that these human beings were rich but knew little about warriors. They only knew about accumulating resources.

If warriors could be easily accumulated with money, the world would have been in a state of endless resource wars. To prevent the rise of strong warriors, people would fight over limited resources. However, it is said that true warriors must go through hardships that ordinary people cannot endure. Who knows what he went through to rewrite his oppressed fate?

"Hmph, I think you're just jealous. You poor people like to find confidence in your mouths."

Yamir sneered at Pudohai's words, "You don't understand McCreedy. To strengthen him, we bought rare powerful magic arts for him to learn. Each one can easily defeat a thousand elite knights. I dare to say that McCreedy is the person with the most magic arts in the world. His strength is far beyond your imagination. We'll see."

The Rothschild old man was fully focused on McCreedy, hoping he would grow stronger and surpass Merlin. After that, he would stop Merlin's cultivation and start finding ways to lower the "requirements" Merlin proposed. If the duel couldn't be decided quickly, Rothschild believed that McCreedy would find it difficult to defeat Merlin.

The family guards watched the two warriors in the middle and couldn't help but whisper among themselves.

"That British warrior is too bold to challenge McCreedy. He should know how powerful McCreedy is."

"Too many people underestimate McCreedy. Because McCreedy is just the family's bodyguard and has no fame outside, they think he's easy to defeat. As a result, they don't even recognize McCreedy."

"That's right. McCreedy is too good at playing the fool. Last year, there was a British knight named Sir Adrian who was defeated by McCreedy and couldn't even lift his head."

"Another person who was tricked by McCreedy's playing the fool. Do you think he can handle it?"

"I bet three moves. Within three moves, this fool will be lying on the ground."

"Three moves? You're too confident about that fool. I bet one move."

The chattering among the onlookers didn't affect Merlin, but it made him even more calm. He looked at McCreedy with a serious expression and touched the Banri Garan at his waist.

McCreedy smirked and prepared for the attack, examining Merlin's appearance. In his heart, he scoffed at this fool. Where is his cultivation? He doesn't have a single ounce of cultivation knowledge. He's just a complete amateur!

This trash, it's disgusting to me!

Let me show you my skills.

The duel began! McCreedy couldn't hold back his excitement and started first.

"Die!"

The crowd watching McCreedy's performance felt as if they were being beaten down.

Suddenly, everything blurred, and he found himself looking down at his own headless body and Merlin's rapidly advancing sword.

"Did I die? ? ?"

"My turn hasn't come yet."

title: Chapter 40 — Three Days Until Departure (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 40 — Three Days Until Departure (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 29 · Chapter 40

McReddie's head fell to the ground, his face frozen in a confused death expression. ★First release★ EZReading★

Merlin, having absorbed all the life force into Banri Garan, slowly sheathed the demon sword back into its scabbard and shoved it into his belt. McReddie's headless corpse crashed to the ground, blood spreading.

"I warned you already. My sword is fast."

Their duel had reached its peak, ending almost in the blink of an eye.

Quite a few people hadn't even seen what happened because they'd blinked. Suddenly McReddie had been split head from body, leaving behind a crowd of stunned onlookers.

"He—he killed Lord McReddie! How did this happen in rural Britain!"

"Truly one move, it's over. Lord McReddie is finished."

"Too fast. Couldn't see clearly at all. One shadow passed and McReddie was—"

The guards erupted into chaos in the distance. No one had expected this outcome. McReddie, who was supposed to win, had been flipped in an instant. The opponent's strength was stronger than McReddie's—no, transcended him. A crushing disparity in power.

Many watched Merlin's figure, unable to hide the unease in their hearts. They now knew this uninvited "headless green" was no good.

"Ah~ I almost didn't see that." Pandom's heart raced with excitement. Rarely seeing Merlin draw his sword, he quickly pulled out his "Merlin's Record" and warmly began writing new entries.

"I'm so fast! Done in one second!"

Luckily Merlin didn't see. If he found out Pandom was fabricating again, he'd flip his lid.

"Brother Jin~" Lilith's eyes were full of stars, completely unashamed of her admiration for the strong. She tilted her head to provoke the little rich kids. "Now you know who's stronger, right? Just annoyed at you self-righteous ignorant fools—"

Jacob, tooth aching, was speechless. His eyes were glued to Merlin's figure and wouldn't move away.

He deeply realized how stupid his mistake had been—cold sarcasm toward Merlin. The opponent hadn't even bothered fighting back, which was already generous. Not to mention the opponent's strength crushed McReddie's. A truly fierce character. With such power, there was no need to look down on him, this rich kid.

The more Jacob thought, the colder his back grew. A wave of relief washed over him—lucky to have survived. His mind had only one thought: convinced! Heartily convinced of Merlin!

Though Jacob, this young master, could barely maintain his composure, the old family patriarch over there had already gone pale.

Rothschild's face went stiff, his mouth quivering, staring at McReddie's corpse still steaming. He seemed stunned.

He had planned to call off the duel once McReddie gained the advantage. He hadn't even gotten to the official fight. McReddie had died on the spot—everything happened too fast.

Thinking of the enormous cost of raising McReddie, Rothschild felt physical pain. He knew how hard it was to raise a Saint-tier powerhouse. McReddie dead—all effort wasted.

Ultimately, Rothschild was a merchant. His second thought wasn't about losing his guard, but about the money he'd invested in McReddie.

Rothschild had thought he could use McReddie to suppress Merlin and gain more profit. Instead, he'd bitten off more than he could chew.

Merlin approached Rothschild and said calmly, "Sorry. The sword was too fast, couldn't stop. Hit your guard. I didn't want that either, but what I said before was clear. He insisted on challenging me."

"You!?" Rothschild pointed at Merlin, body stiff, face cycling through expressions until a smile harder than crying appeared. Through gritted teeth: "Damn! McReddie challenging you was overestimating himself!"

Hearing this, Lilith and Pandom were both stunned. They looked at the human elder in disbelief—killed his close guard, then applauded?

Even Merlin slightly raised an eyebrow, unable to guess what trick the old man was playing.

Only Jacob kept his head down, not daring to breathe. He knew clearly—his father's heart was bleeding. If it were him, he definitely wouldn't let this slide. But Merlin was too strong. Tearing faces was too foolish.

Though McReddie had cost a lot, seeming precious, the Rothschild family could use money to raise such a powerhouse. They could definitely raise a second McReddie—not impossible.

Now McReddie was dead. Clashing with Merlin over a dead man didn't suit the family's interests.

"Merlin-sama's strength is evident to all. My guard was narrow-minded, repeatedly provoking you. This is his own doing's end." Rothschild immediately abandoned all revenge thoughts, using McReddie's death to try pleasing Merlin. "Besides, duels are full-force fights. Casualties are normal. You needn't apologize."

"Hmm?" Merlin meaningfully sized up Rothschild several times. This old fox was too good at reading the wind. McReddie dead, immediately changed his face.

"Since so, I won't disturb further. Lilith, let's go."

Merlin didn't hesitate, pulling Lilith and Pandom along, planning to leave.

From start to finish, Merlin had never taken McReddie seriously—just a small interlude.

Seeing this, Rothschild's heart immediately started panicking. Now McReddie was dead. If Merlin left too, there'd be no one to lead the ruin exploration team.

In urgency, Rothschild hurriedly called out to Merlin, face smiling warmly. "Merlin-sama, please stay. Why willing leave? No interest in the ruins?"

Merlin stopped, slowly反问. "Of course interested. Only regret you can't give a satisfactory price."

"Price negotiable. As Rothschild..." Holding back rage, nodding hard. "Someone with资格 to split profits evenly—meaning ruin loot fifty-fifty? Can!"

"Oh?" Merlin watched Rothschild with interest. "I didn't force you. All voluntary, right?"

Rothschild smiled, brain probably already calculating. Could he not agree? Must somehow make McReddie dead—besides Merlin, what other choice?

"When does the exploration team depart?" Merlin asked curiously.

"Three days later. Team prepared much, just lacking an experienced leader. Now with Merlin-sama here, nothing to worry." Rothschild's face was full of urgency.

"Three days later?" Merlin slightly frowned, feeling a trace of fatigue. Time too short. Why was this old fox so willing? No trick, right?
