title: Chapter 8 — Knight Awakens
content:
Chapter 8 — Knight Awakens

Volume 30 · Chapter 8

Displaying such flippant words?

I'm seriously starting to doubt whether you're actually the Grand Master of the Knights Templar!"

Catherine stomped forward in anger. In this grand hall, who else would dare to proposition the queen? Clearly, the person in question held no regard for the British monarch.

Although Elizabeth was gentle by nature, she was after all the Ruler of Britannia. In terms of status, she was in no way inferior to the Pope of the Holy Roman Church.

For even a mere Templar knight to dare to covet Queen Elizabeth's beauty? This showed just how arrogant the entire Church had become!

"I am of course the Grand Master, a genuine one~" Baleston grinned broadly, his greedy eyes sweeping up and down over Catherine. "I didn't even notice just now—your figure is quite good as well. I wonder if you'd be interested in spending a wonderful night with me?"

Catherine bit her lips until they whitened, unconsciously gripping her magic staff tightly. An impulse to kill Baleston outright rose to her forehead.

"Sir, please restrain yourself. This is the royal palace, not somewhere you can run wild!" Chapman placed his hand on the sword at his waist. He found this so-called good knight far too inflated in his own importance. Did he think the royal palace was just any place?

"How could I be running wild? I was merely suggesting that Your Majesty, since you are still a believer of the Church, might want to accept aid. I was simply offering Her Majesty the queen a second option."

Baleston paid no mind to the hostility from Catherine and Chapman. In his eyes, these two were not worth looking at.

On his way to the palace, he had not yet encountered any strong opponent worthy of matching him.

This made him ever more reckless, filling his heart with fearlessness, daring to casually proposition the queen.

Now that the sea was blocked by demons and the Pope was far too distant, it only provided convenient conditions for Baleston to act recklessly.

Elizabeth kept a cold face for a while, then forced a slight smile. "You are indeed a humorous man. If you truly can repel the demon army, it would not be too late to discuss this matter later."

Overjoyed and smug, he said, "Does this count as you agreeing?"

Elizabeth smiled without speaking, rose directly, and left without another word to Baleston, the shameless rogue. Seething inwardly, he wondered why the Church would send such trash to provide aid. Was the Pope trying to humiliate him?

Catherine closed her eyes, staring at Baleston below who was dancing about with delight. Even through her eyelids, she could feel intense killing intent. But she did not make a rash move, instead silently following Elizabeth.

Baleston was in high spirits, indulging in self-satisfaction on the spot, thinking he could soon win the woman over. He didn't forget to blow a kiss toward Elizabeth's receding figure. "Mmm~ Beautiful queen, I will make you experience love unlike anything before!"

"How could such a shameless person exist in the Holy Church?" Chapman asked angrily.

"Beautiful women love heroes. Your Majesty the queen has been alone for so many years—can you say she hasn't felt lonely?" Baleston pointed to himself, shaking his head. "A man as excellent as me, what woman wouldn't be moved? I'm merely proactively responding to Her Majesty's expectations."

"If you continue being this rude, you will definitely pay a price. I hope you restrain yourself, or you will regret it!" Noticing he was outmatched by Baleston, Chapman threw down those words and left angrily.

"Hmph~" Baleston stood in place, sneering coldly, paying no mind to the accusations around him. With the Pope's restraint gone, he had clearly let himself run wild, his mind full of Elizabeth's mature, delicate figure.

Elizabeth left the hall without a word, walking quickly. Though she said nothing outwardly, she was already angered by Baleston inside.

Catherine followed behind the queen silently, but could no longer contain herself, whispering softly, "This scoundrel is too outrageous. Should we give him some punishment?"

"Forget it, there's no need. He is a man of the Church." Elizabeth answered coldly.

"Your Majesty, are you really going to agree to this bastard's demands? This is an unmasked humiliation!" Catherine said anxiously.

"I won't win by accepting such unreasonable demands. But right now, we need this man. He is indeed the Grand Master of the Knights Templar, and may be able to halt the demons' advance." Elizabeth's tone was helpless. If not for the critical moment of needing people, how could she have tolerated Baleston's humiliation? Everyone around her seemed to be as terrifying as Lord Elgin the great swordsman.

Catherine fell silent. She had to admit the queen's consideration was correct. Right now was a time of needing people; even a problematic man was still a useful one.

"I respect your judgment, but if he pushes his luck further, I won't be able to tolerate it."

In the quiet bedroom, Merlin, who had been in a coma for a long time, finally slowly opened his eyes.

Looking at the familiar ceiling, he easily recognized it as the queen's room.

After Merlin was severely injured, Elizabeth had arranged for him to rest quietly in the palace, where conditions were much better, and also to prevent demons from launching another sneak attack.

A wave of pain rushed over him, and Merlin instantly recalled the night the demons attacked. Cold sweat broke out over his body, and he sat up on the bed, clutching his splitting headache.

"Windsor?!"

Elizabeth had been waiting right beside him. Seeing Merlin wake up, she was both startled and overjoyed, hurrying over to ask warmly.

Merlin had accompanied Elizabeth since childhood. Their emotional bond and relationship were extraordinary.

Elizabeth carefully examined Merlin, worrying there might be other unhealed injuries.

"How are you feeling? Is there anywhere else that still hurts? Anything else uncomfortable?"

Seeing Elizabeth, Merlin's panicked emotions stabilized somewhat. She lifted the bandage on his forehead and frowned slightly. "How long was I unconscious?"

"A long time. About two days. You were severely injured at the time. If treatment hadn't been timely, it could have been fatal." Elizabeth still felt lingering fear recalling those two nights.

"Two days?!?" Merlin's expression was shocked. He had never had such a long coma before. Had he closed his eyes and reopened them only to find two days had passed?

Elizabeth saw Merlin's blank expression. Although his spirit had awakened, his thinking was still very confused.

"Stop overthinking. The matter has already passed. You need to rest well. Don't worry about other things."

"Demons!" Merlin's expression grew grave, his voice agitated. "Demons! It was a demon attack that night! What happened?! I only remember giving my all to kill the enemy! Then what happened?!"

"This—"

Elizabeth looked at the somewhat disoriented Merlin, her heart softening. She didn't know where to begin. Besides, Merlin was usually close to Morrison and Clarence. News of their deaths had just reached him upon waking—telling him now seemed somewhat inappropriate.

Compared to the hesitant Elizabeth, Katherine was far more rational. She spoke directly and coldly.

"The demons who attacked that night numbered three in total. You killed one, and the other two were personally killed by me in the palace."

"Is that so?" Merlin's head was a bit clouded. He thought the demons that attacked were very strong, that he had fought them to the death against just one. Katherine casually killed the other two? Were those two demons comparatively weak? Impossible. This Katherine was hiding her strength too deeply!

"Also..." Katherine leaned against the wall, meeting his gaze, and said solemnly—

"They had already been martyred that night."

title: Chapter 9 — Entrust (Extra)

Chapter 9 — Entrust (Extra)

Volume 30 · Chapter 9

Teacher wove?" Mersefield's face was filled with disbelief, because he thought he had misheard. ★First★Release★EZ Read Books★ The face had not also been unconscious for almost two teams, resulting in two companions dying in battle? Mersefield's mind went blank; Morrison was not weak, especially when he exploded with full force, he could still fight against demons. Although Cadri couldn't fight, his experience was the richest among the thorn knights; being killed likely meant he was ambushed. In Mersefield's eyes, both were excellent knight companions; hearing they had died felt like a dream. "Yes, they weren't lucky enough to survive. Cadri teacher was ambushed on his way home, Morrison was surrounded by two demons in the martial field, that night the most fortunate Catherine spoke without any ripple, as if narrating something unrelated to herself. "May it be like this." Mersefield's expression fell into a dull stupor, his mind continuously replaying Morrison and Cadri's usual appearances and smiles, like a lantern flashing one after another in his brain. Morrison is a very talented fighter, although Mersefield usually looks down on his lazy attitude, he is prone to loneliness and likes to confide in me. Whenever he has free time, Morrison chats endlessly by Mersefield's side, talking about everything like a麻翟 (some kind of bird?), constantly chirping. Mersefield doesn't dislike this talkative guy; rather, it's because Morrison experiences interesting things every day, and facing him makes me feel a bit envious. Teacher Cadri is even more kind and approachable; although he looks young, he holds the highest prestige in the knight order. Cadri, who loves traveling and exploring, always brings back new knowledge and insights, teaching the knowledge of cultivation to each purple orchid knight, sharing everything openly. Mersefield once received sword instruction from Cadri; even if Cadri wasn't a famous sword master, the sword knowledge of later generations he passed on was immensely beneficial to me. Cadri is called the auxiliary master; his field can compare to a holy-stage army. His loss is undoubtedly the greatest loss to the knight order. If Cadri were still here, relying on his powerful auxiliary magic, we might not be unable to face the demons head-on. Seelin saw Mersefield's dazed state and said nothing, thinking he needed time to process the information. Kase will give Mersefield a chance to rest; given the current crisis, I hope Mersefield can pick up his sword soon. "The three demons that night came from the Third Demon Lord's Palace of Mammon; this greedy demon lord, Feng Sai, stole its treasure, declaring war on our entire Pendragon; now demons are trampling our land, advancing two steps toward the royal capital—can you understand how dire the situation is?" Mersefield barely understood the situation, clenched his fists silently, "Although Ese Gold Sword Hero is a despicable scoundrel, he does indeed know demons well; as he often said, occupying Mammon's things is not good; perhaps we should..." "Originally we should have taken a hard stance and made Sai Duan return the stolen detailed armor to its rightful owner, right?" Pia Selin helped Mersefield finish his sentence, "Don't be naive, Ese Jing Gold Sword Hero merely has a bit of foresight; Your Majesty is correct, even if Sai Duan hadn't stolen Mammon's armor, demons would still come knocking; as humans, this reason is enough; Sai's matter merely gave demons a noble pretext." Mersefield lowered his head, thought for a long time, and stubbornly tried to stand despite his injuries, "No... I can't keep recuperating; I need to go fight the demons." "Enough." Elizabeth pressed Mersefield down, speaking earnestly, "Ash, you've done enough; now the most important thing is to properly cultivate." "But" Mersefield objected strongly, "The demon army will arrive soon; are we to let Catherine face them alone?" Elizabeth grabbed Mersefield's hand, "Besides Catherine, there are others who can help you endure, such as the Holy Temple Knight Commander Bale, or Alice from Rexia Sea, he is a foreign thorn knight; news of the battle with demons has just spread; if he knows, he should come to support soon." "Alice, little rent" Mersefield recalled the active performer in Farisi, recently also making waves in the adventurer industry, truly a powerful aid. "Windsor, this isn't something you should worry about; you need quiet rest now; later there may be more important things." Elizabeth said seriously. "What more important things?" Mersefield raised his head in surprise, feeling the queen's palm warm, the matter probably not simple. "I trust all thorn knights, but you are the one I trust most; I can unreservedly entrust my life to you, just as your father once entrusted you to me when you were young, you took up the role of apprentice knight to guard me; this trust is more important than life itself." Elizabeth paused, looking into Mersefield's eyes seriously, "You are not only my knight, but also the one I have watched grow from childhood." "Your Majesty, what exactly do you want to say?" Mersefield felt inexplicably nervous, never seeing Elizabeth so solemn. "I have decided to entrust the fate of the kingdom to you." Elizabeth pressed her hand down, solemnly saying, "This is the secret of the rise and fall of the Pendragon dynasty." "The current situation is dangerous; this is a war between humans, and also a confrontation between humans and demons; the losing side will only face utter annihilation." "So we can no longer hide; we desperately need power to oppose the demons, and we need a trump card to contend with Mammon." "That is a true royal artifact." Rexia, in the Adventurers Guild, panic spread. The news that demons had declared war on Pendragon quickly reached Rexia this small place. Streets and alleys no longer talked about Ese Gold Sword Hero, nor did anyone mention the champion adventurer Alice; people were like outdated internet jokes, hot for a while then soon forgotten. Now everyone cares more about whether Pendragon can win this war against the demon race; if internal human conflict is merely a change of rulers, then the war between humans and demons is a great purge massacre, even more dangerous! "Have you heard? The demon army broke through the Portland defense line, the king trampled all towns and villages, straight toward the capital!" "It seems the stationed royal armies everywhere are beginning to gather toward the capital, and nobles are also raising troops." "This demon horde comes with great force; we don't know if we can win; it seems the church's charlatans weren't talking nonsense—demons truly are our greatest enemy; we should eradicate them early, lest future troubles arise!" Around the adventurers, discussions varied; Hub was relaxed beyond compare, raising his cup and gulping down several "ton ton ton", letting out a belch, muttering— "Hehe, interesting. "The fire has burned to the queen's buttocks?" "This time the opponent is the demon king; Ge Li helped the kingdom get through the difficult times with Ese Gold Sword Hero, but now there's no news of him, he has vanished." "Without the help of the sword record, I want to see how Pendragon gets through the hardship."

title: Chapter 10 — Being Watched
content:
Chapter 10 — Being Watched

Volume 30 · Chapter 10

"Gloating over others' misfortune?" Lucasia frowned, glaring with big eyes. "The kingdom is about to fall into war—how can you still laugh? Don't you know that with this situation, the guild won't have any business? It'll go bankrupt sooner or later."

"What I'm saying is the truth. All the discussion here won't change the difficult situation. Those Thorn Knights are unreliable, and the Elgin Grand Swordsman has no news at all?" Hobbs smacked his lips, stroking his beard and mumbling, "Maybe Elgin Grand Swordsman has already left Britain. Now Her Majesty the Queen is in a panic, with no one available by her side, causing the situation to be passive."

"How do you know Elgin Grand Swordsman left Britain?" Lucasia crossed her arms and questioned, not quite agreeing with the hopeless Hobbs. "I was just guessing," Hobbs shrugged.

"Hey! Don't make wild guesses here in front of everyone. Elgin Grand Swordsman must still be somewhere in Britain—maybe he'll appear at a crucial moment and pull the Kingdom of Britain out of danger again." Lucasia's tone was firm, filled with expectation for the miracle-like Elgin Grand Swordsman.

"Heh, I hope so. If the capital falls, this place will become dangerous too. When the time comes, don't forget to pay the guild an evacuation fee~" Hobbs had no courage and was already preparing to flee.

"Hmph! You have no trace of manly spirit, Hobbs!" Lucasia clenched her small fists, speaking passionately, "Demons are still invading our land! Facing evil forces, shouldn't we fight to the end!"

"Lucasia, are you kidding? We're adventurers, or soldiers serving the kingdom. Why get involved? Nothing matters more than our own lives~" Hobbs replied matter-of-factly.

"Hey! Enemies are demons, not humans. They won't care if adventurers are neutral—any human gets slaughtered. This isn't just a royal matter; it concerns every person living in the Kingdom of Britain."

On this side, Lucasia and Hobbs argued endlessly, while Carl quietly discussed the current situation—

"Da Vinci and Rosalind left Britain just now, and by the next breath the whole kingdom was under martial law. They successfully dodged this turmoil—truly lucky." Carl sighed beside them.

"Yeah, in this situation, those who left Britain early are the lucky ones. Unlike us, we can only stay here." Old Taylor leaned on his cane, shaking his head and sighing.

"Old man, do you think the royal family can get through this?" Carl asked his father curiously. He'd heard from various channels that this demon invasion was unstoppable!

"I can't judge, but I heard the Third Demon Lord Palace sent out their full force. The number of fleets alone is countless. After landing successfully, it's like entering an empty city. No one can stop them. Their goal must be to capture London." Old Taylor spoke in a low voice, his expression very grave.

"Sounds very urgent. If the capital falls, our town will be exposed to the demons' sight." Carl felt a headache coming. If London fell, Wales, right next to Britain, wouldn't be safe either—it'd become the third target the demon army wanted to invade.

"This is exactly the crisis? This concerns the life and death of every British person. Even the London Adventurers Guild can't sit idle." Old Taylor emphasized seriously.

"Oh? Will Morgan Gregory lead adventurers to participate in this kingdom defense battle?" Carl asked in surprise, feeling some doubt.

"From what I know about Gregory, he used to be a court mage who took care of the British royal family. Even now as an adventurer, he wouldn't abandon the British dynasty." Old Taylor paused and added, "Besides, the enemy this time is demons, not humans. I heard demons burn, kill, and plunder along the way, leaving no survivors. Our adventurers' neutral stance means nothing against demons—they want to erase us from British soil."

"Too cold-blooded. Is this what demons are?" Carl's brow was locked in worry, his hot blood urging him to charge into battle. "The church's god also says demons are dangerous. Their existence is like a time bomb. If not cleared early, they'll threaten humanity's safety. Before I was half-believing, half-doubting because demons only operated in their own territory with no intention of expanding. Now I believe it—demons are truly dangerous."

"If I had realized the danger of demons earlier, I might not have become an adventurer, but instead signed up as a Temple Knight, contributing my strength to守护 world peace!" Carl clenched his fists, regretting his past judgment. "I really want to support the capital now—maybe I can help the Queen who's struggling!"

"Calm down, you kid. The capital is full of hidden talents, far more capable than you. If they can't stop the demon army, you going there would just be throwing your life away." Old Taylor spoke in a craftsman's tone, pouring cold water on Carl—because he himself wasn't much better, dying from being swept up by hot blood would be too stupid.

"But maybe I can help?" Carl looked at his firm fists, his heart churning.

"Don't be so impulsive. If the capital falls, Lakeshire needs you even more." Old Taylor patted Carl's shoulder, speaking earnestly, "You should look forward to Alice. She's an external knight. Maybe she's already packing to head to the capital. With Alice's strength, she can fully represent us and go to support."

Not far from Alice's house, there was a small bakery. Freshly baked bread was highly praised, always snatched up by neighbors.

But these past few days, a guest always came on time to buy some fresh bread—that was the manager of the Secret Cottage, Helena.

Ding dong, Helena as always walked into the bakery on time. Her beautiful smile illuminated the place, and her beauty alone was enough to brighten the small bakery.

"Miss Helena? You're here? Haha, same as usual?" The baker was very enthusiastic seeing Helena.

"Yes, thank you." Helena slightly bowed, exposing a powerful figure line that made people's blood boil!

"Uh!" The baker's eyes went wide, feeling a nosebleed urge, so his face turned red and he turned away quickly, afraid of being scolded by his wife. "Heh, wait a moment, fresh bread will be out soon!"

Helena smiled lightly, her eyes suddenly turning cold as she stared at the bakery window. Across was Merlin and Alice's home.

"That girl should be leaving soon, right? Maybe it's time to take action."

title: Chapter 11 — Long-Unseen Friend
content:
Chapter 11 — Long-Unseen Friend

Volume 30 · Chapter 11

In the corner of the bakery, sipping coffee, Helen had no interest in the bread at this little shop. She was only here to keep an eye on Merlin and Alice for a while. This wasn't her original intention, but she had accepted the order from the demon lord's master to monitor Merlin's family and report everything to Asmodeus.
After Asmodeus's last falling out with Merlin, they hadn't been in contact for a long time, but that didn't mean he knew nothing about Merlin. Through Helen's reports, Asmodeus learned of Merlin's recent situation. He hadn't abandoned his only friend, and even entertained the idea of pulling his friend out of the mire.
Asmodeus knew Merlin had violated the demon taboo, but there was still room for maneuver—living with a beastwoman wasn't a big deal, and even if the elders found out, he could find some excuse to get past it. However, once Asmodeus learned that Merlin and the beastwoman had a baby, he felt a twinge of unease. If Merlin and the beastwoman had no fruit of their love, there might still be a way to appease the elders, but now that they had a child, it was irrefutable proof. No matter how Merlin defended himself, the elders would never believe he hadn't broken the taboo; he would surely receive severe punishment and be forever marked in the demon cauldron. To prevent Merlin from stepping into that abyss, Asmodeus resolved to take him in hand, sever all his ties, and nip the danger in the bud.
Helen knew Asmodeus was planning something, and though she hesitated, thinking of the exiled Lucifer made her resolve firm. Perhaps in Helen's heart she harbored a vague, hard-to-define feeling for Merlin, and she did not look favorably on romances between demons and humans. After observing Merlin leave, Helen saw Alice staying home to look after Chris, rarely going out, and she hadn't gotten much from her surveillance. Just as Helen thought today would be as usual, a carriage bearing the insignia of the Weiwei family pulled up outside, instantly catching her attention.
From the carriage stepped a female attendant in servant's garb and a knight with a heroic bearing, who were chatting with each other. These two were none other than the long‑missed daughter of the Grand Duke of Xu bei, Cecilia, and the knight Kai from her domain.
Helen set down her pen, the tension in her chest finally easing. She thought things were turning out as expected. As an foreign thorn‑knight, Alice might have enough freedom, but when the demon army pressed hard, she would certainly not be able to stay out of it. Alice would very likely leave the Rexqi circle tomorrow, and this news ought to be reported to Asmodeus. 'Wow, it feels like ages since I've been to Rexsi!' Cecilia exclaimed as she dismounted, remembering that her last visit to this small town had been ages ago.
'You're just too busy; the duke keeps raising his expectations for you, entrusting you with more and more affairs, so you've lost a bit of freedom, but after all it's a good thing.' Said respectfully while on duty. 'That's right, it's all thanks to Lord Merlin's blessing—I don't even know if he's home right now.' Cecilia thought with a little anticipation. 'He should be in? Alice's little... her astonishing performance isn't just the championship of the adventurer's tournament; she's also a purple‑gold adventurer. Ordinary commissions might not catch her eye, and she'll probably be as busy as before.' Kai said confidently. 'Really?' Cecilia nodded, sourly saying, 'Alice's luck is truly great—she's improved so much in such a short time, she's become someone I have to look up to; I'm sure she's had plenty of help from Lord Merlin.'
Kai gave an embarrassed laugh and tried to console her, 'Cecilia, you shouldn't be like that; Alice's team has made such progress, we ought to congratulate her.' Cecilia pouted, 'Never mind Alice's position; I'm still not convinced.' 'When we see Alice's little group, I hope your manner of speaking improves—this is the duke's entrustment.' The one beside her, trying to soothe, said, 'After all this, his strength has also increased; though not as exaggerated as Alice's, he has at least reached the high‑peak level.' Cecilia, however, had made no progress; she poured all her energy into managing the family business, becoming a powerhouse in the world, which was not his dream. The two tidied themselves up and went forward to knock, but there was no response from inside. 'Nobody home?' Cecilia frowned. 'Should we go see if they're out on duty?' Kai wondered, uneasy because they hadn't been given prior notice; they might have missed Merlin and Alice.
Just then, little Chris was humming a tune, hopping home, and when she arrived she saw two strangers standing outside the house, their faces grim. Cecilia: '???' Little Chris, who was by nature a bit timid, frightened by the two adults, turned and ran back crying, calling for her mother or father to protect her. 'Wah wah.' 'Why are you crying? I told you not to run.' Alice lowered her head, helpless with her baby; the child clung tightly to Kai's thigh and wouldn't let go, while the grandmother pointed at the stranger outside. Mother and daughter had merely gone out to buy vegetables, not gone far, which caused Cecilia and Kai to miss seeing them.
Alice lifted her head and saw Cecilia and Kai's familiar faces; she was a little stunned, almost dropping the potato she was holding. 'You guys? Really rare visitors.' Cecilia quickly coughed twice, composed herself, and said, 'Long time no see.' 'Alice, you look more beautiful than ever.' Kai, who was more eloquent than Cecilia, said, his words full of respect for the strong. 'Haha, I didn't expect you two back—do you have something urgent?' Alice, seeing these familiar friends, was still quite pleased. 'Indeed we have something, but let's talk about it after we go inside.' Kai said mysteriously. Cecilia had been eyeing little Chris from the start, thinking the child looked a bit… 'Whose child is this?' 'Huh?' Alice lowered her head, looked at the girl who resembled a koala bear, then realized, 'This is my daughter, Chris. Chris, call uncle…' Little Chris, shy, hugged Alice's leg and shrank back, whispering in a mosquito‑like voice, 'Uncle…' 'Ah???' Cecilia's head felt as if it had been struck, buzzing, as she continually compared Chris and Alice. 'Group?!!' Both were at a loss, stammering, 'Your daughter—that is also Lord Merlin's…' 'Too unexpected—I never imagined…' (if dan)

content:
Chapter 12 — Surging Hatred (Extra Chapter)

Volume 30 · Chapter 12

Miss Alice and Merlin were already parents under Father Snow's roof.

Cecilia sat in Mother's lap, staring at the child cradled in her arms with wide-eyed wonder, filled with curiosity. ★First release★ EZ reading★

Kyle had always thought it impossible for either of them to become parents within three years, but reality slapped him in the face so hard he could only sigh inwardly—

I'm still too young. I underestimated the intensity of a lone man and woman, dry wood and blazing fire.

"Chris, right? As your child, I'm sure you'll surely rise to greatness in the future, with extraordinary accomplishments. I was just wondering—this child looks so much like you, Alice, so adorable at such a young age. When you grow up, won't you be a great beauty? I'll cut my own head off!"

"Huh?" Alice was naturally pleased when someone praised her daughter, "Did you hear that? You're going to be a beauty someday."

"Chris? Beautiful?"

Little Chris pointed to herself and happily showed off her chubby cheeks, "Does that make Mom pretty too? Hehe!"

Alice smiled and patted Chris's little head, "You haven't learned half as many serious things as you've learned these sweet words."

"Pfft! Alice, you clearly used to secretly despise Merlin in your heart back then, didn't you? And now look—before you know it, you even have a child. You really are one of those people who say one thing but do another." Cecilia held a teacup, her eyes full of teasing, never forgetting how Alice and Merlin's relationship initially seemed ordinary, with constant bickering.

"What do you mean 'say one thing but do another'?!" Alice's face flushed red, unable to resist defending herself, "Actually, this child was an accident—"

Kyle and Cecilia's expressions instantly changed, their faces seeming to wander into dangerous territory, as if they were misinterpreting the information in that "accident."

"Are you two going to let your imaginations run wild? The accident was purely an accident," Alice emphasized seriously, then suddenly changed the subject, "What brought you here suddenly? If it's about Merlin, he's not home."

"Huh? Merlin isn't home?" Cecilia stood up in surprise, wondering why she hadn't seen Merlin's figure all this time.

"He's not. He left last month and went to be hired by the Rothschild family," Alice explained simply.

"Oh! What a pity! I thought I could see Merlin-sama's heroic bearing after all. If I had known, I would've come myself." Cecilia rubbed her forehead, feeling deeply disappointed that she couldn't meet her idol.

"What a regret. If you had come earlier, I could've arranged for you to see him." Alice gave a half-smile.

"I also want to see Dad~" Little Chris's ahoge twitched.

"If you behave yourself a bit more, maybe Dad will come back early."

Alice lowered her head and looked at the child moving in her arms, "Aren't you supposed to be practicing magic? If you learn the most basic healing spell, Dad will fly right back."

"But magic is hard~" Chris's ahoge instantly lost its energy. Learning magic required completing a lot of homework Alice had left behind, both boring and tedious.

"Oh, Merlin-sama isn't home? What a pity. Actually, you should also be able to guess why we've come, right?" Kyle asked, raising his head.

"Is it about the demon invasion of Britain? It's been all over the place lately. I don't know the situation at the frontlines." Alice was clearly well-informed, having heard fragments of this news recently.

"That's right. The demons are extremely vicious. Wherever they tread, the land turns barren, humans are slaughtered at will—even the old, weak, women, and children are not spared. This isn't merely a war, but genocide."

Kyle's face grew grave, clearly sharing the deep hatred for demons.

This was the first time the demon race had expanded beyond their territory since the human race descended upon the world. Previously, most people had only heard the Holy Church's clergymen preaching about the demon threat theory, never imagining it would all become true.

Within a short period, the number of followers of the Worshipers of the Demon God within Great Britain surged dramatically. Church priests became unusually active, seizing the opportunity to expand the Church's influence.

The believers were willing to believe that as long as they devoutly dedicated themselves to the Goddess of Light, they could successfully avoid the demons' attacks.

Looking across the entire human world, the originally divided human kingdoms, upon learning of the demons' expansion, all showed trends toward forming alliances centered around the Worshipers of the Demon God.

The Holy Church had spent countless efforts but could never achieve its dream of unifying the world through religion. Under the Demon Lord's influence, a faint prototype of a unified coalition was quietly emerging.

In such an environment, humanity's fear of demons drew them together, and the force that twisted them into a single rope was what the Worshipers of the Demon God called "faith."

Even a little knight like Kyle had been influenced by the Church's propaganda, now perceiving the demon race as a great threat. If everyone didn't unite, there was no way to resist.

Mermon had obviously realized this long ago, but he wanted to bind the entire demon race to his chariot. Quickly seizing Britain, using rich war spoils to tell the Council of Elders and all the demons—

The human era has ended. Demons existing on barren lands, barely surviving, can turn their fortunes around. Continuing to hesitate will leave nothing but scraps—everything will be eaten by me, Mermon.

By using tremendous benefits to tempt the demons into war, Mermon himself could plunder vast wealth in the chaos. In the end, he would become the head of the Seven Princes, the leader of the entire demon race!

But little Chris didn't understand any of this. Recently she had encountered quite a few demons, and hearing Chris say those words about demons, she couldn't help but indignantly refute—

"What Chris said is wrong. Demons aren't all big bad guys! Most of those stories are just lies spread by the books!"

Merlin, hearing Chris's inexplicable remarks, asked in astonishment, "You—you've never seen demons, have you?"

"How could I not have?! They have horns growing on their heads and look weird. Just not long ago..." Little Chris placed her fingers on top of her head, pretending to grow her own horns.

"Hahaha, this child is talking nonsense again. You two don't mind, haha~" Alice tightly covered Chris's small mouth, scolding her for starting to talk nonsense the moment she let her guard down.

"It's fine, casual remarks from a child. Children are all innocent." Chris laughed awkwardly, not taking it to heart, thinking it was just a child babbling nonsense.

Cecilia looked at the young and lovely Chris, her heart filled with affection, "Children are all like this. I used to say strange things too when I was little, trying to catch Father's attention, though none of it was malicious."

"That's exactly it, haha~" Alice smiled and placed her treasure daughter on the ground, instantly radiating a touch of maternal authority, "Don't talk nonsense, understood? Go play somewhere else. Mom needs to discuss some things."

Little Chris realized she had done something wrong, like a deflated little bun, and waddled into the pile of drying clothes to sulk in isolation.

Alice secretly exhaled, wiping the cold sweat from her forehead, her heart still trembling—

I forgot that Chris would still talk nonsense. I almost had an accident! She completely forgot that guests had come to the house.

Now the entire Great Britain was full of hostility toward demons, with hatred growing ever more intense.

If word got out that demons frequently visited my place? Both Merlin and I would be in big trouble.

title: Chapter 13 — Collecting Rent
content:
Chapter 13 — Collecting Rent

Volume 30 · Chapter 13

She said, "Miss Alice, since you have already heard the news of the demon race invasion, you must understand that the current situation is very dangerous. We have been asked by Lord Furang to go reinforce the kingdom's army in fighting the demons."

"Yes, Alice, you alone among all of Wales are an outsider thorn knight personally commissioned by the queen. The fighting on the front lines is currently very tense, and they need your strength very much. In all of Wales, it is very difficult to find anyone more powerful than you. Alice, you are no longer the silent, lowly adventurer you used to be." Ezkanshu. Alice lowered her head, a bit hesitant in her heart, many concerns clouding her thoughts regarding this matter.

"Little Miss Alice, I understand you are merely an outsider thorn knight. Although you hold a status similar to that of a thorn knight, the two cannot be compared. You bear no responsibility to the royal family, and there is no need for you to sacrifice your life to protect this kingdom. You possess great freedom, so to speak more importantly—" She paused. "You have chosen to live on this land, which also counts as part of the British Kingdom. Our homeland is under threat to your very existence as well. If the people of Britain can unite as one, they are capable of withstanding the demon race's forces. Your strength cannot be missing from this."

Alice slightly furrowed her brows, did not respond, and instead chose silence, thinking over many matters in her heart. I wonder if Merlin knows about this? If he does, which side would he be on? The news of the demon race invading Britain was too sudden; she had not prepared at all. Her subordinates had asked her to leave Britain, but she had never once considered the possibility of opposing Merlin again.

Alice felt caught between a rock and a hard place. Although she most wished to consult with Merlin, the circumstances did not allow it now. But there was one thing she was certain of—Alice still stood on the human阵营 side, while Merlin still had not managed to shake off the shadow of the demon race. Seeing Alice hesitate without making a decision, Selene glanced at little Chris beside her and reminded her, "Alice, this war concerns every single person's survival in the kingdom. No one can stay aloof and preserve themselves. If the royal capital falls, the outcome across all of Wales will not be good either. It will surely become a feast ground left for the demons."

"Has it already become this dire?" Alice felt quite surprised. Hadn't she thought the demons finding it not so easy to conquer the royal capital?

"To be honest with you, I heard some inside information from my father. Before the war even began, the Seventh Knight Morrison and the Third Knight Clady had already fallen in battle. Even the First Knight Mesfield, it is said, has already fallen into a severe and comatose state. That night's sneak attack dealt devastating damage to the kingdom's defensive forces." Selene disclosed all the secret intelligence she had gathered from her father. "These matters are kingdom secrets. Her Majesty the Queen does not wish for the kingdom to fall into chaos and turmoil, so she kept them hidden. If this news were known by everyone, morale would only grow worse."

Alice had only seen the knights a few times before; from what she could tell, they seemed like cheerful people. To think they had already passed away... "Don't you want to see Chris grow up safely in this war? If the royal capital falls, Wales will face the mighty demon race entirely on its own." Selene unveiled the bleak situation plainly. She did not understand what Alice was hesitating over. Even for Chris's safety, she should join this campaign.

With Alice's personality, she would never simply fold her arms and do nothing. She only cared deeply about what Merlin thought. If Merlin supported the demon race's expansion ambitions, then without a doubt she would once again stand on the opposite side from Merlin. What would happen to young Chris then? This child is innocent, after all. But she could not contact Merlin at the moment. There was not much time left for Alice to ponder. Selene's words precisely mirrored her own worries—rather than letting the flames of war spread to Wales, it was better to send reinforcements to the front lines beforehand.

"Providing支援 to the front lines is not impossible, but with Merlin not here, I need to look after this child. I have no frontline combat experience, so I simply cannot—"

"Is that so?"

Indeed, that was a problem. "If Selene and I do not go to the front lines, we will definitely help you look after the child."

Both fell into awkward silence. If Alice went to支援 the front lines, who would take care of little Chris? No parents would be willing to see their child placed in danger.

"Then how about this—" Selene thought for a moment and suggested going to her father to ask if a female servant could help look after Chris for a period of time.

"No, you saw just now at the doorway. The poor souls—if it weren't someone familiar, they probably couldn't even finish a meal." Alice could barely manage to have a caretaker from the committee look after Chris for a few days. If those others came, they would become even more haggard. It made this adoptive mother terribly worried. Selene sighed. If Chris's matter could not be properly settled, Alice certainly would not be able to支援 the front lines.

Alice pondered for a long time, sighed, and said softly, "Please return first. I need to think carefully. I will give you an answer tomorrow."

That night, Alice cooked for Chris. Chris mentioned that Daddy's cooking tasted better, but even when Mama cooked, she would happily finish every bite. She used the spoon aggressively, constantly shoveling food into her mouth, making continuous slurping sounds. Naturally, whenever children are hungry, they eat ravenously.

"Take it slow. No one is competing with you for food. And don't make such loud noises—it's quite impolite." Alice, like a worried mother whose heart was knotted, kept nagging beside her.

"Xi-ba-to-mi-xi!" Little Chris looked up and smiled. Her mouth was stuffed to the brim with oily food. It was unclear whether she had actually absorbed anything her mother said.

Alice sighed and urged firmly, "Chris, you need to remember one thing. No matter what guests come to the house, especially those from Daddy's side—"

"Why?" Auntie treats me well! Chris raised her small spoon in protest.

Alice hesitated, then explained, "Not everyone in this world is like Daddy and Auntie, genuinely good to you. People outside believe demons are rotten to the core. So you must be even more careful, understood?"

Chris thought about it for a moment. Thinking it would cause trouble for Daddy, she nodded vigorously like a chick pecking at rice. "E-e-e~ I know~"

Alice smiled and reached out to pat Chris's head. At that moment, a knock sounded from outside the door. Such a late hour—who could it be? Could it be Selene and her father again?

Curious, Alice rose to open the door. Standing outside was the landlord.

"Time to pay the rent, Alice."

title: Chapter 14 — Frontline Support
content:
Chapter 14 — Frontline Support

Volume 30 · Chapter 14

Alice had forgotten about this matter while taking care of Chris, and she was surprised that Mrs. Fang remembered it so clearly. EZ read books "It's not a good thing to drag the rent, Alice Miss, you are now a famous adventurer and should pay attention to your reputation." Mrs. Fang smiled and said "I'm very sorry, I'll go to enjoy it right now." Alice felt very embarrassed, no matter how high her current status was, the fear of the landlord had become a habit. Before Alice was pressed by debt and couldn't drink water, she was always chased by the landlord to pay rent, which made her feel that she was short in height now. Little Chris stood up her ears, heard the sound of the landlord, and happily jumped down from the chair, ran over and blinked her big eyes at Mrs. Fang, "It's Grandma~!" "Oh? You're very spirited, it seems you've been eating well, haha" Mrs. Fang saw Chris, and her expression was full of affection, and the whole area was different. She put her old hands into the basket and took out a few candies to give to Chris, "Take it, don't be angry with Grandma." "Mmm~" Little Chris held the candy in her hands and proudly looked at Alice beside her, as if showing something. Alice's face turned black, wondering what the child was proud of? Was she showing that she was easier to get others' favor? It was really strange that Mrs. Fang was too good to Chris, every time she came, she would give her candy, was it that the old people were more fond of children? "Chris, how does Dad teach you? Or is it not allowed to accept others' things freely?" "Okay, it's just a few candies, Alice Miss, you don't have to be so strict as Mom, it will make the child more timid." Mrs. Fang bent down and touched Chris's little head. "This" Alice was about to speak, but she saw that Chris did not dislike Mrs. Fang's touch, her small hair on her head swayed left and right, like a dog's tail, which was very active and obviously happy. Obviously, Chris had been in contact with Mrs. Fang many times without Alice's knowledge, and she would not fear this old lady because she would give herself good things to eat. Chris was still a child, keeping her innocence and purity, and would not be as careful as adults, as long as she could eat well, that was enough. Alice looked down at her beloved daughter and suddenly felt moved, and tentatively asked, "Chris, do you like Grandma?" "Like~!" Little Chris answered without hesitation, swaying in place with her two small hands. Mrs. Fang smiled but said nothing, but she was already happy. Alice saw that, silent, and made a certain decision. "Landlord" "I would like to ask you for a favor, Alice is going with Cecil and Kel to the front line to support the kingdom's war against the demon race." The innocent Chris only knew this news in the morning, and she was stunned, and then she asked herself, "Do you like Grandma?" What does it mean! Little Chris was very regretful, if she had known this, she would never say she liked Grandma. Alice thought a lot last night, originally wanted to let the companions in the guild help take care of it, but she was very worried that this group of people were careless and negligent, and Chris was not very close to them. After seeing Mrs. Fang and Chris's close relationship, Alice felt very relieved, and Chris was willing to accept others' things, which was based on trust. "Mom, where are you going? Are you going to leave Chris?" Chris stubbornly raised her little face, her eyes wide open, her face like a crystal, and because she was small, she could only grab Alice's boot, afraid that she would be left. Alice's heart was tight, her voice was calm, but she couldn't hide the reluctance, "Mom won't leave you, mom will just go out for a while, and will come back soon." "Dad also said so, but now he hasn't come back." Chris's lips moved, and she was already very strong without crying. "Mom didn't lie to you, dad and mom will come back soon, you are our treasure, we can't leave you." Alice comforted her, wiped the tears on Chris's face, "You should grow up quickly and learn to face all things by yourself, parents can't provide a safe harbor for children, you will eventually face the storm alone, do you understand, Chris?" "Yes." Little Chris reddened her eyes and nodded, not quite understanding. Alice tried to maintain calm and give Chris confidence, and helped her organize her clothes, "Mom leaving you is temporary, after the chaos is calmed, mom promises you, I will come back as soon as possible." "Pull the string! Mom pulls the string, the Buddha says that as long as you pull the string, you won't change your mind." Chris stubbornly stretched out her little thumb. "Alice was stunned, she didn't expect Chris to believe this, so she forced a smile and touched Chris's thumb, "Okay, mom promises you that everything she says will be fulfilled." Far away, Kel saw the scene of the mother and daughter's separation, and felt a wave of guilt, "I feel guilty, aren't we not supposed to come and find Alice?" "Don't say it out loud, it's like we're being mean, the child must hate us." Cecil muttered softly, feeling a little regretful. Please Mrs. Fang seriously, and respectfully asked, "This child is temporarily entrusted to you, she is not very obedient at night, she will kick the quilt, and someone needs to cover it, otherwise she will catch a cold, she is a picky eater, but if she eats too much, it's not good, I hope you can keep an eye on her." "Alice" Mrs. Fang interrupted Alice's words, she looked like she didn't want to let Chris go to the front line, and she didn't know what to do. "Sorry," Alice's brows knitted, and she was speechless. "Don't worry, there's nothing to worry about." Mrs. Fang pulled Chris's small hand, and Alice's mind was at ease. "Thank you." Alice bowed her head slightly and turned to leave, she dared not look back, her heart was trembling. Chris couldn't help but want to follow Alice, but she was held back by Mrs. Fang, and she only heard Mrs. Fang's voice say, "The child has unlimited potential, even the gods will praise you, early on, they will be proud of you, don't show a cowardly look, this will make your dad, mom very big." Little Chris bit her lip, looking at Alice's departing figure, lowered her head and was silent, everyone knew what the little girl was thinking. In the pastry shop next door, Helen stood in front of the window, watching everything far away. "Helen, is your bag ready? Helen, is your bag ready? No matter how the pastry shop boss called, Helen's eyes didn't blink, like she had lost her soul. It's true that she left here, it seems that I can't rest.

title: Chapter 15 — Remove the Extra Chapter
content:
Chapter 15 — Remove the Extra Chapter

Volume 30 · Chapter 15

Kyle and Cecilia seemed a bit excited, after all, they were participating in a war worthy of being recorded in the history of the kingdom. Cecilia's father, the Duke, had long since sent private armies and supplies to the front line for reinforcement. The collapse of the Potter defense line left the capital directly exposed to the sight of the demon army. The demons would crush their path, pressing straight toward the capital. Many regions knew clearly that whether the capital could be defended related to the fate of the Britannia Kingdom; the strength of the entire kingdom was converging on the capital.

"To deal with demons, my light magic should be useful, right?" Cecilia felt uncertain in her heart.

"Young lady, you should be more confident. You are representing the Ducal region in this expedition," Kyle encouraged her from the side.

"I know, but I have no experience dealing with demons. I don't know..." Cecilia hoped Alice could give some advice, but seeing Alice's state made her instantly startled. "Alice! Pull yourself together!"

Alice was spiritless, her eyes hollow and lifeless, like a puppet that lost its soul. She stood muttering to herself by the field, her whole person looking terrible—

"Will that child actually eat well? Will she still cry secretly at night? Will she be unable to resist herself and run away from home? I regret it so much, I should never have agreed to support the front line."

"You're being too dramatic! Weren't you encouraging the child to be independent before leaving? How can you change your mind so quickly!" Cecilia was shocked by Alice's state. They had only just left Reuther, yet Alice had already become this way. Before even fighting the demons, she had already lost the battle of morale.

"There's no choice, that child rarely leaves me. I feel like this matter won't end in just a day or two. If it drags on, I'm so worried," Alice said, leaning her head against the field, her heart not at peace.

"Alice, dear, don't say such discouraging words. Since she has left Reuther, you should think about how to quickly defeat the demons. Driving the demons out of Britannia not only ensures your daughter's safety but also helps countless citizens of Britannia!" Kyle clenched his fists, hoping to use words to motivate her.

"I understand the logic, but I'm still worried. After all, parents wouldn't understand my feelings," Alice responded dejectedly.

Cecilia and Kyle fell silent, feeling a strange hurt in their hearts, as if being mocked by Alice. They looked at each other, sensing something—even though Alice had left Reuther, why had she become this state? "Except for his subordinates, who would agree that this child is a member of the demon race?" Asmodeus said coldly, unable to feel the sadness again.

"Cheer up! Alice, we should still consider how to repel the demons as quickly as possible. Can you also deal with them?" Kyle said with high spirits.

"Yes, have you ever seen demons? I heard they are very powerful, we must definitely be careful," Cecilia said, hoping to shift Alice's attention.

"So Alice, being so experienced, has actually dealt with demons?" Cecilia's heart was very surprised. Alice closed her mouth, not knowing how to answer—how powerful could they be?

"I was once a Hero, but I have never fought against demons," Merlin had not mentioned Reuther, the secret basement of the cottage.

Helena was using a remote communication device, constantly reporting the situation to Asmodeus. Upon learning that Alice had left Reuther and had not encountered the human old woman, he remained silent for a long time.

"Just as I thought. Putting children in danger is a common ailment of humans, and even a manifestation of weakness."

"This is completely different from the concept of our demon race. We constantly torture the descendants to eliminate all the weak and useless."

"Relying on this cold-blooded method will make the demons stronger and stronger. In a comfortable environment, one cannot cultivate true warriors," Helena nodded in agreement, saying "Your Majesty is right."

"That human woman's strength is increasing too fast; you couldn't act right under her eyes. But now the opportunity has come. Killing a child without a protector is much easier. Don't tell me you can't even handle a human old woman?" Asmodeus's image on the screen looked somewhat worried.

"Killing that child is not difficult for me. That old woman is just a landlord, she poses no threat. But I have some doubts," Helena interrupted.

"At such a time, do you still have doubts?" Asmodeus asked.

"That child is after all the offspring of Lucifer, possessing the bloodline of the first Demon Lords. Acting rashly will..." Helena did not dare continue speaking.

"Do you think the hybrid of demon and lowly human is of the same kind?" Asmodeus countered.

"I do not agree," Helena answered firmly.

"That is true. Except for Lucifer's former subordinates, who would agree that this child is a member of the demon race? No one will accept," Asmodeus said indifferently.

"Doing this is excessive; it will anger Lucifer. How about letting the Holy Church handle this matter most fairly?" Helena suggested.

"Helena, do you want to kill my friend? Lucifer has already broken the taboo! The Holy Church will definitely not let him go!" Asmodeus paused for a moment, then said slowly, "He is my friend. I only regretted when his soul was sealed. Such seeds that break the taboo are still allowed to exist. We are helping him leave the swamp."

"If the matter leaks, there is a very high possibility of a direct conflict with Lucifer," Helena expressed her concern.

"I already know that Mars is attacking Britannia. We can completely throw this blame on Mars, or pick a random scapegoat. This is very easy. What you need to do is leave no survivors," Asmodeus instructed.

Helena thought for a moment, then silently closed her eyes, "I know."

"Did you get the talisman I sent someone to give you?" Asmodeus asked curiously.

"It's here," Helena took out a button-like medallion from her waist, which had black patterns carved on it.

title: Chapter 16 — Silent Flow
content:
Chapter 16 — Silent Flow

Volume 30 · Chapter 16

"What? You all remembered my instructions?" "?" Asmodi discovered Hai Helen was absent‑minded. Helen woke up as if from a dream, silently placing the talisman in her bosom and lowering her head she answered, "I remember, but I have a problem." "What problem?" "The demons have already begun a large‑scale assault on the human kingdoms; does the council know of this news?" Helen asked curiously, feeling that the demons were acting recklessly and wondering why no one was restraining them. Asmodius pondered for a moment and replied seriously, "The demons' movements are too great; in fact the elders learned of this long ago. They have repeatedly proposed sanctions to stop the demons from dragging the entire demon race into the abyss of war, but some elders disagree, and even those who support the Bell faction have begun to back the demons' external expansion. Now the council is in utter chaos, roughly divided into two factions—radicals and conservatives—locked in fierce argument." "If we let the demons continue like this? Before we only needed to oppose the Holy Church's power, but now we might have to oppose all races; this would be an early external war, a slight mistake could turn into a second Holy War!" Helen worried, not approving of the demons' current behavior. "I understand what you say, but this is the situation; the council's opinions are not unified, so we cannot use the Demon‑Sealing Vase to sanction the demons. I can't even think of… [garbled] … smiling, he said, 'The Bell faction, which usually stays out of worldly affairs, will suddenly intervene in this matter, letting the elders who support it stand with the demons, openly supporting their external expansion.' 'Just thinking of the Bell faction's wealthy region becoming the demons' supporters?' Helen felt a hint of despair; the council has many Bell faction regions, and if the demons gain their support they could act without restraint. 'The meeting has been convened; I have already received the notice. At that time several demon lords will together discuss how to handle the demons' external expansion.' Asmodius paused, regretfully saying, 'Unfortunately the demon lords are not all present; the demons will certainly not attend, Lucifer has been expelled, his substitute as acting demon lord lacks the ability to bear great responsibility; at that time no one will heed the suggestions of the Second Demon Lord Palace; they have gradually been sidelined.' Helen lowered her head, gathered courage, and asked, 'Your Majesty, have you not thought of stopping the demons' large‑scale [something]?' Asmodius's eyes suddenly turned serious, gazing at Helen, 'What are you thinking, Helen? Living too long in the human world has made your mindset…' [garbled] Helen exclaimed, 'Impossible!' She knelt, explaining, 'I merely think the demons' current behavior is dangerous and will affect us.' Asmodius's expression softened a bit, and he patiently replied, 'Helen, the relationships among demon lords are very complex; you cannot understand. Now the demons are like a good child; if you dare provoke them, it will surely bring disaster. Moreover, the demons are like a precious gem; if they lose, the whole demon race will suffer; if they win, the responsibility will fall on them themselves; I have no loss, possibly even gain; why should I stop the demons?' 'But Your Majesty, have you always opposed the demons' external expansion?' Helen asked, puzzled. Asmodius said, 'Helen, you should be less naive, think more rationally. Most demon lords are indeed conservative pacifists, out of consideration for demon race stability, not because they don't want to seize more wealth. Now a madman is willing to make his ambition realistic, showing all demons the possibility of successful external expansion; is that still a good thing? If the demons become the second demon to eat the crab, will other demon lords still firmly oppose war?' Asmodius explained the reason: 'In the face of huge profits, even pacifist demon lords will be moved to act.' He continued, 'Let me tell you two things: The demons are now so arrogant that opposing them is like opposing an enemy; Leviathan has been expelled by the demons and has taken over the Great Demon Lord Palace; the outside world seems to think Leviathan and the demons have joined forces, but that's not the case; now the demons actually control two Demon Lord Palaces.' Helen then realized that Leviathan's territory had been seized, the demons had also taken over their kin's territory, truly as said! 'Don't spread this around; we just need to observe history.' Asmodius opened his fan—'Your duty is to guard that child; I will wait for you at midnight, at the madam's house…' The house is not big nor small; inside, everything is filled with an old‑fashioned atmosphere, not as good as Merlin and Alice's house, resembling a quiet cottage away from the bustling town. Usually the landlady lives here alone, with not much furniture, appearing very simple. Although there hasn't been a lively child for a while, it's not quite sufficient, yet we still add a little morning joy to the house. The landlady, wearing old clothes at the time of her death, sits in a chair, weaving by weak candlelight, thread moving in rhythm, her technique exquisite. She suddenly lifts her head, recalling Alice's parting advice, puts down the needlework, slowly stands, picks up the oil lamp, and walks into the small room on the left. Chris is curled up in the infant bed, breathing evenly, obviously asleep deeply; in his arms he holds the head of a big gray wolf, the small mechanical toy Merlin gave his daughter. It seems even if Chris reluctantly accepts his parents' absence, he still needs to hold something retaining his parents' scent to sleep peacefully. The landlady lifts the oil lamp, checks the sleeping Chris, sees that indeed the blanket has been kicked to the edge, so she smiles and helps tuck the blanket back, the child, who was formerly very quiet… The landlady after tucking the blanket, turns and sees the withered four‑season grass on the table, feeling moved. After Alice left, Chris suddenly gave up his habit of playing poorly, spending all day practicing magic as a slave. Perhaps the child also understands that if he cannot become strong, his parents' departure will surely not arrange for himself. Chris's goal is to revive the withered ginger leaf grass, this is the most basic method to practice magic, it's the family love Alice left for her daughter. Alice does not expect Chris to make a stunning sound; she only needs him to lay a solid foundation, firm his steps, first learn to use the simplest life system. The landlady looks at the withered ginger's four grasses for a while, shows a faint smile, gently buys and leaves. She returns to her rocking chair, continues spinning thread, weaving the thick forest for the system. The nourishing soup flows silently, seeping in through the construction, this technique flow is terrifyingly quiet, no sound of ants, flowing through the gaps in the floor.

title: Chapter 17 — One Woman Holds the Pass
content:
Chapter 17 — One Woman Holds the Pass

Volume 30 · Chapter 17

Silently and effortlessly, Helena slipped into the house, her movements as quiet as a ghost. She observed the landlady, Mrs. Fong, from the shadows, her eyes fixed on the old woman's frail figure as she slowly made her way towards Chris's bedroom.

Helena wasn't one to kill indiscriminately, but if her actions were discovered, she would have no choice but to silence Mrs. Fong. The old woman sat peacefully in her rocking chair, knitting, seemingly oblivious to Helena's presence.

Under the cover of darkness, Helena moved like a phantom, the bedroom door just within reach. Suddenly, a sharp "whoosh" cut through the air as a knitting needle shot out, embedding itself in the floorboards and blocking Helena's path.

Helena's eyes widened in surprise as she stared at the needle. Could this elderly landlady be a warrior or a magician? Her previous investigations had turned up no evidence of Mrs. Fong possessing any martial or magical abilities—just an ordinary human living a quiet life in Reksum.

Helena hesitated, unsure if she should act. She watched as Mrs. Fong, her eyes cloudy with age, fumbled about, searching for her missing needle. "I'm getting old," the old woman muttered, "can't even knit a simple pair of socks properly."

Helena relaxed slightly, thinking it might have been just a coincidence. Perhaps the old woman had simply misjudged her throw. With renewed caution, Helena sidestepped the needle and continued towards the bedroom, intent on dealing with the sleeping Chris.

But before she could reach the door, another "whoosh" sounded, and a second needle was embedded in the bedroom door. Helena's doubts vanished—this was no ordinary human. The old woman was deliberately blocking her path, and Helena could sense the faint ripple of magic in the air as Mrs. Fong wove a mysterious spell, sealing the bedroom with a barrier.

If Helena didn't eliminate Mrs. Fong first, she wouldn't be able to breach the barrier and harm Chris. The room was now completely isolated, not even a sound could penetrate the magical seal. Helena felt a shiver run down her spine as she realized the depth of Mrs. Fong's magical prowess. Even Katherine, the Thorn Knight, couldn't construct barriers so swiftly.

Helena decided to reveal herself, her body materializing from the shadows like water taking form. "I didn't expect to find a magician of your caliber in a small place like Reksum," she said, her voice dripping with malice.

Mrs. Fong set aside her knitting, removed her reading glasses, and regarded Helena calmly. "You're the owner of the secret inn, aren't you? Why sneak in so late without knocking? I thought we had an intruder."

"Don't play dumb," Helena sneered, her hands weaving intricate patterns as razor-sharp water blades formed around her. "You should have stayed out of this. Now, you won't have the chance to write your will."

"I've always known the secret inn harbored demons," Mrs. Fong said, her expression turning serious. "But I thought you were just passing through, not here to cause harm. That child in the bedroom is just a kid—why won't you leave her alone?"

"None of your business!" Helena snarled, her brow furrowed in anger. With a swift motion, she sent a wave of water blades slashing towards Mrs. Fong's throat.

The old woman raised a finger, and the space around her rippled, effortlessly dispelling Helena's attack. "You're still too weak to face me. Leave now, and I'll pretend this never happened."

Helena's eyes flashed with anger as she summoned a ferocious water demon, its form coalescing from the air to attack Mrs. Fong. But the old woman remained unfazed, her fingers tracing circles in the air as chains materialized, binding the demon and sending it crashing to the ground. Another chain wrapped around Helena's neck, constricting with an otherworldly force.

"Divine magic!" Helena exclaimed, her eyes widening in shock. Mrs. Fong was no human—she was a Saint, a natural enemy of demons.

With a swift motion, Mrs. Fong tightened the chains and flung Helena across the room. "My home doesn't welcome evil like you!"

The door exploded as Helena crashed through it, her body rolling across the ground before coming to a stop. She coughed violently, clutching her throat where the holy chains had burned her skin.

Mrs. Fong emerged from the house, her small frame radiating an aura of quiet power. She crushed the remnants of the door beneath her feet, her eyes filled with contempt as she gazed at Helena.

Helena's face twisted in rage, her body beginning to transform as dark wings and horns emerged, revealing her true form as a fallen angel.

"So you're a Saint," Helena spat.

Mrs. Fong smiled, her eyes glinting with amusement. "And what of it?"

With a casual gesture, she summoned a nearby broom, its handle standing upright as she grasped it firmly, exuding an aura of unwavering determination.

Helena felt an unfamiliar pressure, knowing that Saints were the Goddess of Light's chosen warriors, specifically designed to counter demons. In a realm where magic was suppressed, defeating a Saint would be nearly impossible unless one possessed overwhelming power.

Helena sensed that Mrs. Fong's strength surpassed her own, though the old woman's aura was so subdued it was hard to gauge her true level. For the first time, Helena felt uncertain, torn between completing her mission for Asmodeus and the fear inspired by the Saint before her.

"Are you afraid? Do you want to run away?" Mrs. Fong asked, her voice calm and detached. "You can leave anytime. I won't chase you, as long as you abandon your plans to harm that child. We can pretend this never happened."

Helena's eyes narrowed, her mind racing. She had never encountered a Saint so powerful, yet so composed. The old woman's words were laced with a quiet confidence that made Helena's blood run cold.

"In my day, my opponents were the legendary First Demon Lords," Mrs. Fong continued, her eyes glinting with a hint of nostalgia. "You're not even worth my attention, a mere demon of no consequence."

title: Chapter 18 — Demon Lord's Shadow (Extra)
content:
Chapter 18 — Demon Lord's Shadow (Extra)

Volume 30 · Chapter 18

Is it you, acting on behalf of the Demon Lord?

That is an existence from an era without beginning or end, an ancient monster!

The Heavenly Realm's great army cannot possibly mobilize casually — only twice have they done so, and the second time was during the Holy War.

At that time, the Holy Spirit Legion launched a massive invasion, waging a protracted war against the demon race at the height of its prosperity.

Perhaps when the Holy War ended, the Lord did not return to the Heavenly Realm, but chose to remain in the mortal world. Such a thing is not impossible.

Acting on behalf of the Demon Lord.

An opponent — that old hag's status in the Holy Spirit Legion must be extraordinarily high!

Helena's expression turned grave.

Fear gripped her entire brain, yet a sliver of doubt remained — if the old woman before her eyes was a high-ranking figure in the Holy Spirit Legion, how could she be in a place like Rex's town?

Under normal circumstances, the Holy Spirit Legion's bigwigs are all... they should be enshrined and worshipped by the Holy Church as Saints, in the heavens above. Their nobility is unimaginable.

Although Helena was not entirely certain whether the opponent was merely an ordinary Holy Spirit who failed to return to the Heavenly Realm after contending with the First Demon Lords, she was now desperately displaying her powerful side, wanting to sell herself.

Spirit? Opening her mouth to compare herself with the Demon Lords — the implication of submission is far too obvious!

Helena condensed the magic power throughout her body until it grew dense.

Her left hand drew the bow, her right hand condensed an arrow vibrating with a raging torrent, madly absorbing the magic power from her entire body.

"Let me test you with my strongest magic!"

"Have the demons of today grown rusty like leftover snow? Or has peace lasted too long, making you forget your own unforgivable sins?" The landlady's expression turned ugly.

Helena did not answer, simply releasing the bowstring. The raging torrent arrow flew — "Go!"

A sound that shook the eardrums and stung the eyes. This was the most powerful magic Helena could currently unleash, meant to force the old hag to reveal her strength!

The landlady faced the oncoming torrent arrow and instantly formed a massive water wall. The landlady's entire being was swallowed into it!

"Come, let me see if you can find a way out of my magic!"

The raging torrent seemed summoned, beginning to spin rapidly. A terrifyingly powerful water dragon took shape. The water dragon's body twisted and cut wildly; even a giant dragon caught in the chaotic currents would be shredded to pieces.

However, a bizarre scene occurred.

The terrifying water dragon vortex was... the landlady merely...

One saw this seemingly powerless old woman wave her hand, and the water dragon, as if stripped of the control that tore through the air, began to be manipulated at will by the landlady. "!?" Helena's eyes widened in shock.

Her own magic power was actually being used by the opponent. This degree of magic control was truly inconceivable!

"This level... playing conductor with me? Demons truly are a generation... a music conductor, waving the baton at will, and all magic submits to control." Helena's water dragon vortex — hit wherever pointed!

In that instant, the landlady's cloudy eyes flashed with brilliance. She backhanded and sent Helena's water dragon vortex flying back.

"Impossible!" Helena's face changed drastically. She had always used this as a trump card, yet when facing her own move, she could do nothing!

"Ah!" Helena's complexion turned pale as autumn. Watching the surging water dragon come crashing down, she had already given up thinking.

In that split second, a pitch-black shield suddenly flew from Helena's body, expanding into the surroundings. Dense black mist coiled around the shadow, drifting in midair like a chaotic dream. It was Asmodeus's shadow.

The black shadow — only then did Helena barely react. "Asmodeus!?"

Asmodeus's shadow did not turn to look at Helena's wretched state, but faced the raging torrent water dragon with a casually raised hand — a light push, pointing to the sky.

In the distance, *tick-tock, tick-tock*, small droplets fell.

Helena's prized trump card, before the Demon Lords, shattered in an instant. The gap in strength was...

Asmodeus's shadow released its hand. Though it had no physical body, merely a shadow, within the black mist one could still see...

"A shield that can bear my power is precious. Use it well before it breaks."

Helena felt deeply ashamed, cold sweat soaking her back. "I... I'm sorry... Is it that difficult? Will it really let you... gather?" Asmodeus's shadow... its tone seemed different from before, carrying a few threads of coldness and ethereality.

That old man... I find it hard to approach that child. Helena unexpectedly spoke words like...

"Oh? The one we overlooked... is the old hag still a character?"

Resembling a housewife's final moments, resembling a missionary playing mysterious tricks.

Where is the strength that could drive Helena to such a desperate strait?

A Holy Spirit?

A doubtful answer.

"Holy Spirit? The successive Demon Lords'... interesting."

Asmodeus's shadow examined the landlady, a smile in its eyes. "You say you are... a woman, a female... one of the Seven Saint Elders?"

The landlady brushed off the chaotic debris at her feet with a casual sweep, a smile that did not reach her eyes. "An old woman who lives off the meager earnings of the bottom-rung masses in this dilapidated house. If you insist I am a Saint Elder, I won't deny it. Better than those disrespectful, mystifying missionaries."

Asmodeus's shadow cut her off. "I loathe all things ugly. Your wrinkle-covered face, your decaying body..."

"Accompany you to a dignified death — that is the opportunity I give you. Before me, you have no right to ask why?"
