title: Chapter 21 — Starlight Through the Mist
content:
Chapter 21 — Starlight Through the Mist

Volume 30 · Chapter 21

Looking thoughtful, [someone] asked, "Could it be that Your Majesty already has some clue?"

"Probably not wrong. I used to think that legend was fabricated by the Holy Church's charlatans, but thinking about it now, it does seem somewhat plausible." Asmodeus had an answer in his heart.

"Yah? Could it be a very well-known Holy Spirit?" Helena recalled many enemies of the demon race.

"That's right. One of the seven Spirits standing before the throne — Raphael." Asmodeus paused and said softly, "It is said that after the Holy War, the Spirit army also suffered heavy losses. Some Spirits began to question the goddess's decisions, and Raphael was one of them. She made inappropriate remarks in front of the goddess and was punished and imprisoned."

"So that old man is Raphael!? The Archangel of Compassion?" Helena found it hard to believe that such a noble Spirit Chief would be relegated to the mortal world.

"Needn't be so surprised. This is not impossible." Asmodeus thought for a moment and smiled. "It seems heavenly Spirits can fall even lower than I imagined~"

"Since the opponent is a Spirit Chief, should we try to eliminate him?" Helena considered that Raphael in the mortal world was a threat, and demons and Spirits were natural enemies.

"No need to make a fuss over a banished angel. In a sense, he has already stood on the opposite side of the goddess. The enemy of my enemy is my friend. Keeping him alive is far more valuable than killing him. Besides, we have no real conflict of interest." Asmodeus felt that the landlady Raphael had considerable utility value. Even a lofty Spirit Chief couldn't stand the goddess's actions — it went without saying that the goddess truly had problems!

"But... won't he secretly tell Master Merlin about what happened tonight?" Helena was very worried. If Merlin knew Asmodeus had acted擅自 to try to eliminate Chris, it might make the relationship between the two rulers even more tense.

Asmodeus thought carefully and said decisively, "I bet he won't say anything about tonight."

"Why?" Helena asked.

"If he really is a Spirit Chief, no one would know that the person who should have been imprisoned suddenly appeared in the mortal world. It's obvious he escaped on his own. How would he dare to easily publicize his true identity? Unless he wants to return to the cage of the heavens again." Asmodeus laid out the logical chain of his deduction. Recalling what had just happened, Raphael hadn't admitted his identity at all; instead, he kept indicating he hoped things wouldn't escalate. All signs pointed to Raphael wanting to live on as an ordinary human landlady. With that aged body, how much longer could this Spirit Chief survive?

But Asmodeus still harbored some doubts. He couldn't figure out the reasoning behind it —

A Spirit Chief as grand as him, risking exposure of his identity, to protect a human girl and a child? Really?

Could Angels truly be this kind-hearted?

He didn't believe it. What exactly was hidden within?

On the vast sea, a modified merchant ship sailed steadily.

It was nighttime. Merlin deliberately ordered the fleet to slow down, seeking stability over speed, to avoid sudden dangers in the darkness.

Merlin didn't care about reaching the ruins quickly, but he had to stay safe. After all, once entering the sea fog zone, the compasses had already failed and couldn't provide accurate direction for the fleet.

Although Leviathan was providing guidance, even the Demon Lord of the seas hadn't been everywhere — clearly he had never been here before. The closer they got to the ruins' location, the more isolated and secluded it felt.

Even Leviathan couldn't help but sigh, surprised that such a place existed in this world. Without the guidance of the route chart, who could find their way here?

Merlin stood on deck with a worried expression. The fleet had been sailing through the fog zone for three days and nights and still hadn't located the exact position of the ruins.

If they delayed much longer, the expedition team would run into serious problems. Before encountering any sea beast threats, they might starve or die of thirst on the ship — after all, there were no supplies to replenish during the voyage.

Leviathan was also growing restless and couldn't help voicing his speculation. "I think we're lost in the fog. We haven't made any progress these past few days; we've been going in circles!"

Merlin turned his head and asked, "Are you sure we're going in circles?"

"Intuition." Leviathan responded with just two words. Based on his experience dealing with the sea, the fleet was indeed circling in the fog.

Merlin didn't respond. Instead, he looked at the pale mist before him and checked the compass in his hand, which was spinning wildly. He thought the ruins route chart was a bit misleading — it only provided a rough direction, not the precise location. Getting into the ruins really wasn't that simple.

"What's your intuition worth?" Lilith hopped out and glared at Leviathan. "My brother is the Chosen One! Following my brother won't lead us astray."

"Taking risks on the treacherous sea isn't a game. One wrong move and you'll lose your life. Your brother isn't any kind of Chosen One — on the open sea, he's just an idiot." Leviathan said unkindly.

"What did you say!? Don't forget that your safety right now depends on my brother's protection. Careful or I'll throw you into the sea to feed the beasts!" Lilith retorted, hands on her hips.

"That's exactly why I despise you siblings — you can't even read the situation. Not only that, you keep making things worse. It was the same a hundred years ago. As descendants of the first generation monarchs, how could you let noble demons occupy the Demon Lord Palace? How did Her Majesty end up with two stupid kids like you?" Leviathan snorted, looking down on Merlin and Lilith from the bottom of his heart.

"Brother! Did you hear that? This sea beast is too arrogant. We should throw him into the sea right now!" Lilith was furious and kept urging Merlin to deal with Leviathan.

Merlin was swayed back and forth by Lilith but remained unresponsive. With the current situation causing him so much headache, he had no energy to comfort her. Besides, Leviathan was right — if he were the Chosen One, what would he need a route chart for? Wouldn't he just close his eyes and steer the ship?

"If your brother were the Chosen One, we wouldn't be going in circles in the fog. Heaven would give us signs, but it hasn't~" Leviathan shrugged.

"If heaven gave my brother a sign, would you bark like a dog?" Lilith countered resentfully.

"Oh sure, something impossible~" Leviathan said smugly, mocking the foolish Lilith. Finding the ruins' location in a fog where compasses failed — how much luck would that take?

Suddenly, Puduo, who had been silent the whole time, shouted loudly and pointed at the distant sky. "Your Majesty, look! Over there! There are stars!"

Leviathan's expression changed drastically. He raised his head abruptly and followed Puduo's finger to look —

Three bizarre red stars formed a triangle in the sky. Their light was exceptionally prominent in the western heavens, even piercing through the clouds.

The Three Sages — the three brightest stars in the western sky — were hailed by astrologers as the symbol of fate.

Originally created to commemorate the three goddesses who wove fate in mythology, they were also the origin of alchemy, the Three Fates, named with "death"!

The Three Sages appeared in the western night sky once every three thousand years, and could only exist for a single night!

Few people in their lifetime could witness such a spectacle, yet Merlin had the fortune to see it.

title: Chapter 22 — Causality Weapon
content:
Chapter 22 — Causality Weapon

Volume 30 · Chapter 22

After a while, Cecilia and her group were about to arrive at the capital of Britain. Due to the late hour, everyone decided to rest at an inn along the way and continue their journey the next morning. They hadn't eaten much all day, so they made do with the simple meals available at the small inn.

This small inn wasn't any famous restaurant, but it could still provide some basic home-cooked meals to barely sustain travelers.

Cecilia looked around, her face showing some displeasure. "This place is so dirty, isn't there anywhere cleaner?"

"Little Yuan, we're traveling, good inns are hard to come by. Just make do for one night, okay?" Kay said with a helpless expression beside her.

"Yeah, when we're on the road, we shouldn't have such high demands. As long as it provides shelter, that's good enough." Alice nodded in agreement, already accustomed to this kind of life.

Cecilia fell silent, thinking to herself that she wasn't being pretentious, she just wanted decent living conditions. Was this demand too high?

This small inn, at this late hour, had a few other scattered travelers besides Cecilia's group, seemingly refugees from the south who had fled with large and small luggage.

"I heard Surrey has fallen?"

"Yes, the demons broke through the defenses. The lord of Surrey even had his head cut off."

"So tragic! Did everyone manage to escape?"

"Those who could run did, the elderly, weak, sick, and disabled were left behind to fend for themselves. I was one of the lucky ones who escaped quickly."

Alice, upon hearing this, faintly sensed a crisis. Surrey was very close to the capital; if it had fallen, the capital was clearly exposed to the demons' line of sight.

This urgent situation was somewhat beyond Alice's expectations. She had underestimated the demons' powerful offensive. The Mages' army had only just landed a few days ago, and now Surrey had already fallen. The next step would probably be a direct attack on Britain's capital.

Alice couldn't help but worry, unsure if she could block the demons' offensive.

Let's set aside Merlin, that weirdo, and talk about the Besieged City Alice had personally seen.

Alice had faced the Besieged City before, wanting to challenge it extremely, even though she had made great progress since then.

Although she hadn't seen the Demon Lord of that place, it was likely not weaker than the Besieged City.

"What a pity, previously the Rothschild family was recruiting experienced sailors everywhere. I didn't go. If I had known Britain would encounter this situation, I would have applied. Now I'm left worrying."

"Is that so? Do they need that many crew members?"

"Seems like it. I didn't go, so I'm not too clear on the specifics."

"How strange? The Rothschild family is incredibly wealthy, why would they need to recruit so many?"

"This operation must be extremely dangerous. Otherwise, they wouldn't offer such high salaries."

Hearing the conversation between the two people behind her, Alice couldn't help but think of Merlin again. If he were here now, perhaps he would have a way to persuade the demons' army to retreat.

Thinking of this, Alice secretly clasped her hands together, praying in her heart for Merlin's safety, hoping everything was going smoothly for him and that he wouldn't encounter any difficulties, and could return quickly.

Meanwhile, far away in Britain, Alice had just activated the Causality Law Weapon. As she wandered in circles in the fog, feeling dizzy, Merlin suddenly saw a celestial phenomenon that appeared only once every three thousand years!

The Three Sages' Stars were extremely unusual, able to pierce through the fog. According to the position of the king star, the expedition team could determine their direction.

"What is that?" Merlin wondered at the three faint red stars shining in the royal sky, having never heard of such a phenomenon before.

"Your Majesty! These are the Three Sages' Stars, a spectacle that appears only once every several thousand years! Whenever these three stars appear, all the stars in the western sky will dim, and only these three will shine brightly throughout the night. They symbolize the three goddesses who wove fate during the era of the gods. In astrology, they even hold a high position in predicting fate!"

Pudom, who was slightly older than Merlin, happened to have some knowledge of astrology and knew how important the Three Sages' Stars were in that field.

Throughout history, there have been few powerful astrologers who, although they didn't possess the Sealed King's prophetic abilities, could calculate the grand evolution of history based on the positions of the stars in the sky!

For example, the ancient kingdom that was destroyed years ago had a mysterious astrologer during its heyday who, based on the position of the Three Sages' Stars, predicted the kingdom's downfall and the rise of a place called the Pillar Realm!

As can be seen, these three stars were not ordinary stars, possessing many secrets. No wonder Pudom was so excited; it was also his first time seeing such a phenomenon.

"The Three Fates"

Merlin had heard this name before, from Da Vinci's stories, which seemed to hold an extremely high status and had a deep connection with alchemy.

"Your Majesty doesn't know about the Three Fates?" Pudom saw Merlin's puzzled expression and felt extremely surprised.

"I'm quite familiar. The demon race's records don't mention much about this."

Merlin sincerely replied, thinking that although the demon race's records were numerous, they mostly started from the era of the gods, Odin. Even the prophets who greatly influenced the demon race were only briefly mentioned.

"I once heard my father tell a story about how the ancient gods, including Odin, weren't originally that powerful, and the world was in a more chaotic state. However, he found the source of the World Tree, the Fountain of Life, and the three goddesses who constantly wove fate beside it. Odin offered his right eye to the goddess of fate and, under their guidance, gained unparalleled power, establishing the powerful Aesir tribe and becoming the king of the gods."

Pudom gazed at the three stars shining in the distance, sighing, "These three stars are named after those three goddesses, commemorating the three mysterious and profound goddesses who wove fate. The Three Sages' Stars!"

Merlin nodded vaguely, thinking that this sounded like the three goddesses were like a system, manipulating fate? Was this possible?

"This is good news, Your Majesty! The Three Sages' Stars are in the west. Now, with the heavy fog, we can use the position of the stars to determine our location and accurately find the location of the ruins. It will be easy!"

Pudom excitedly said, the Three Sages' Stars were rarely seen, and since there was no astrologer present, they couldn't obtain more valuable information. However, they could serve as a reference to determine their current position.

"Brother is indeed extraordinary. A celestial phenomenon that appears once every three thousand years, and you've seen it so easily~" Lilith's eyes were filled with admiration as she glanced at Beelzebub.

"I told you! My brother is the chosen one. Whenever he encounters difficulties, he'll always turn misfortune into fortune!"

Beelzebub stared at the three stars in the sky, feeling extremely astonished. This was too coincidental?

Just as he was worrying about not being able to find the location of the ruins, the Three Sages' Stars, which appeared once every three thousand years, suddenly emerged. Beelzebub felt it was extremely unbelievable. He had just set up the flag, and it immediately came true, as if he had struck gold.

"Woof woof woof!"

"Woof!"

Volume 30 · Chapter 23

"Such good luck?" Merlin rubbed his chin, a bit puzzled. He had never had such good fortune before. Just when he was worried about not knowing the direction, a star that appears only once every three thousand years had pointed the way!

He couldn't help but sigh in his heart. Why had he never won a horse race before? Why had his luck suddenly returned at this moment? Don't use up all your luck for a lifetime in one go.

"Need I even ask? It's certainly because His Majesty has been blessed by the ancestors of the demon race. Even a star of the Sage King, which appears only once every three thousand years, has been encountered. This clearly shows you are the chosen one~" Pudohai flattered from the side.

"Right, with my brother here, what difficulties could there be? Throw away the navigation map and sail blindly with your eyes closed, and we'll still reach our destination!" Lilith was deeply convinced of this.

Merlin quickly stuck his fake beard tightly. Regarding his subordinates' flattery, he still felt quite pleased.

"???" Guowitan, standing beside him, was so angry his nose was crooked. He thought Merlin this little guy must have hit the jackpot, otherwise such a coincidence was impossible.

Merlin looked down at the navigation map, compared it with the direction of the Sage King's three stars in the sky, and with his hands on his hips, pointed to the sky and shouted loudly—

"We are very close to the gods' ruins. Order the crew to proceed at full speed toward the direction of the three stars!"

Early in the morning, Merlin was snoring loudly in the captain's cabin, wearing a cute lion pajama and hugging a pillow.

A loud knocking sound interrupted Merlin's beautiful dream. He got up with sleepy eyes, unlocked the two locks on the door, and with great effort, finally opened it.

Why were there two locks on the door? It was because Lilith often came to bother him at night, so Merlin, to be prepared for any eventuality, had tied the captain's cabin door up tightly.

After opening the door, a short Leviathan stood outside, looking serious and said, "It's already noon. Are you going to sleep until when?"

"Ah~~~~~" Seeing it was Guowitan, Merlin yawned long and said carelessly, "What's the rush? It's still early in the afternoon. Let me sleep until evening."

"This morning, the crew found this on the deck," Guowitan said, throwing a strangely shaped fish on the ground, his expression becoming more serious.

This fish was about the size of a palm, its body covered in steel-like scales, its teeth as sharp as剃刀, and it was cold-blooded. Its two pectoral fins were large, like small wings that could fly?

Merlin had never seen such a creature before and was very surprised. He carefully lifted it from the ground by its tail.

The fish's eyes turned red, it twisted its body wildly, trying to break free. Its sharp teeth kept biting the air, almost biting Merlin's fingers!

Merlin suddenly became a bit more alert, secretly marveling at the creature's aggressive nature. Even out of water for the morning, its vitality was still so active.

"What is this?"

"A ancestor of the man-eating Leviathan, the Blade-toothed Beast," Guowitan calmly replied.

"Blade-toothed Beast?" Merlin looked at the little creature in his hand. Its teeth were indeed sharp, not too big, but its mouth took up two-thirds of its body. Its strong outline suggested its biting power was terrifying!

"The Blade-toothed Beast is an ancient creature that lived in the Stone Age. They move in groups, and usually, if you see one, it means there are tens of thousands hiding in the deep water. Their aggressiveness is strong, and their biting force is extremely terrifying. Even the sharpest blades and weapons are just snacks to them. The dragons of the Giant Dragon Era were proud of their tough scales, but if they fell into the sea and were surrounded by a group of Blade-toothed Beasts, within a few seconds, they would certainly become nothing but a clean skeleton."

"Oh?" Merlin's expression changed, and he gained a new understanding of the little creature in his hand. One Blade-toothed Beast wasn't scary, what was scary was hundreds of thousands of them. "How do you know this?"

"When I was young, I saw this ancient creature. My father once tried to tame a group of Blade-toothed Beasts to block the elves from approaching the Black Sea Strait, but he failed."

Guowitan paused and explained, "These executioners have no brains. In their eyes, there are only edible things and inedible things. When they encounter powerful sea creatures, they will actively avoid them. All weak sea creatures are just snacks, without exception."

Merlin shook the Blade-toothed Beast in his hand. "Truly a clever little thing, even the first-generation Leviathan couldn't handle it~"

"Logically speaking, such ancient creatures should have gone extinct by now. My father went through great effort to find just a few of them," Guowitan looked up and said seriously. "Finding one on our deck is not a good omen!"

Lamia didn't want anyone to know her identity—she just wanted to keep pretending to be a normal human.

But Merlin casually revealed her vampire identity, making her feel very upset.

Lamia stared into Merlin's eyes, thinking deeply about whether to tear off the pretense.

"Captain, how did you know my identity?"

"Such things—I suspected from the moment I held your hand. You vampires prowl at night like vampires but pretend to be mummies during the day. Anyone who's had contact with vampires would naturally think of your kind, right?" Merlin said without courtesy.

"You've had contact with vampires?" Lamia felt somewhat surprised. Normally, aside from dedicated vampire hunters, others rarely had contact with hidden vampires. She never imagined Merlin had fought alongside Dracula—she thought this man had merely encountered Elizabeth Báthory.

"I've fought creatures like you several times. Your body temperature is terrifyingly low, like the dead. No matter how you hide, it's hard to conceal the bloodlust emanating from you." Merlin laughed coldly, revealing that vampires' gazes toward humans were filled with desire, eager to bite through a human's aorta.

"Leader! Stop talking to them! They know our identities. If this gets out, it's dangerous for us. The Church's inquisitors will come!" Vadier stood up, drawing his sword from his waist, the atmosphere filling with tension. He couldn't allow the news that the entire mercenary group were vampires to spread—back in the human world, they'd have no place to hide!

Mahade, tall and strong, though not eloquent, gripped his axe tightly, veins popping on his hands—essentially agreeing with Vadier's judgment. "Now we should throw all of them overboard to the fish!"

"Calm down," Lamia said coldly, glancing at her two subordinates. If they tore off each other's masks now, the treasures in the ruins might be lost. "What do you want? What do you want from us?"

"No no, no misunderstanding. I know your identity—I'm telling you not to keep pretending. Every expedition team has their own motives. Now we're on the same ship. Tearing off each other's masks benefits no one, right?" Merlin paused. "Besides, we've already admitted to being demons—our intentions are clear. You don't want your identities exposed, and neither do we. Let's cooperate to enter the ruins of the gods. What's wrong with that? After the expedition, we go our separate ways. Pretend this never happened. You're still the leader of your mercenary group, and I'll still be a low-life adventurer."

Merlin's heart wavered, but he still said: "Let me be clear upfront—I don't want the Rothschild family's wealth. I want a share of the treasures in the ruins."

"However, in this game, only those with enough strength deserve to be players. You barely qualify—the rewards from the ruins are yours for the taking." Merlin promised, though he still needed to figure out how to prevent others from causing trouble and bring reinforcements in.

"Hah! Barely qualifying? With our leader's help, you couldn't enter the ruins of the gods!" Vadier pointed his knife at Merlin, dissatisfied. "And you speak so confidently—who knows if you keep your word? What dog shit are you? Put the knife down, or you'll die a terrible death! Do you really think you're someone? You vampires—even in the dark, you're the lowest of the low! Creatures that lack quality, history, and heritage—yet you dare to look down on us?"

Chris crossed her arms and started yelling. "Listen up! Our great demon race has always been the most trustworthy! Our promises are worth more than silver! And my brother is the Demon Lord! The famous arrogant sovereign—he's made the Church's crusade army piss themselves in fear countless times! My brother's promises can't be measured in money!"

"You!?" Vadier's face turned purple with rage. He realized he couldn't argue with this female demon. "Leader, these demons—"

Lamia interrupted, not wanting to fight Merlin. If not for Chris being here, the situation would be unimaginable. This carefree little ship captain... was actually a Demon Lord? The arrogant sovereign—the one who single-handedly pushed the Church back ten years. He's said to be unremarkable in appearance, his cruelty reaching its peak. Facing the Church's crusade army, he never leaves survivors. The number of Templars who died under this Demon Lord's hands is countless. He's the Church's most dangerous enemy. After a hundred years, there was no news of him—he was hiding in this world of demons. Having her face this famous Great Demon Lord was obviously very difficult—she could only barely hold her composure.

Jacob crouched in the corner of the innermost ship, pale as a ghost. This once-proud young master felt like a black sheep that wandered into a wolf pack. The wolves were discussing how to eat him, arguing heatedly. Jacob was terrified. On this ship, it's either man-eating demons or fish on a cutting board. How was he supposed to survive? What kind of people are these? They don't even look at me, and they're already dividing up prey in front of me. I thought Merlin and I were the same—humans. After that outburst, it turns out I'm the fattest sheep in the flock!

Now Jacob was filled with despair. Clinging to Merlin's leg wasn't enough to survive—he prayed Merlin wouldn't eat him when he wasn't looking.

"Your Majesty! I can't hold on much longer!" Udo maintained the last layer of holy shield, which was already cracking. The blade-toothed beasts grew increasingly excited, their scarred faces pressing against the shield!

"Lamia, little one, what do you think?" Merlin gripped his sword, saying if he couldn't make it, none of the three vampires would escape either. Now there was no Holy Sword Mistilteinn—otherwise they'd bargain with the vampires. No other choice—they're here.

Lamia looked at Merlin's serious eyes, sighed, and stood up. Vadier looked confused, thinking Lamia shouldn't help demons.

Lamia said nothing, walking to the stern, watching the blade-toothed beasts gathering wildly. She said calmly: "Whatever treasures are in the ruins... they should have my share too."

Lamia drew a crimson short knife, cutting her finger. Dripping blood into the sea, drop by drop. How powerful is a vampire's life force?

A single drop of Lamia's blood instantly stained the entire sea! The crazed blade-toothed beasts inhaled Lamia's blood, gradually growing quiet, becoming puppet-type subordinates—relying on this powerful vampire's bloodline to command them.

title: Chapter 28 — I Arrange Myself
content:
Chapter 28 — I Arrange Myself

Volume 30 · Chapter 28

Lamia, as one of the three ancestral vampires, inherited Cain's formidable life force. Her blood possesses the ability to corrupt lower creatures, making the weak her subordinates. While Dracula can create numerous offspring, Lamia can do the same, though she has no desire to. Her blood spreads like a plague among the fish, continuously capturing the fierce blade-toothed beasts and subjugating them to her will.

In just a moment, those fearless and ferocious blade-toothed beasts became significantly calmer. Their eyes, once filled with bloodlust, now showed confusion. Clearly, after being infected by Lamia's blood, their hunting instincts had been suppressed. With a mere thought, Lamia, leveraging her high-tier vampire blood, controlled the infected blade-toothed beasts to attack other uncorrupted ones. The sea seemed to boil as millions of blade-toothed beasts turned on each other underwater, each one like an ant on a hot stove, thrashing on the surface, filling the air with a heavy scent of blood.

Puduo was greatly startled, his face showing exhaustion. He had exhausted himself trying to subdue these monsters, yet Lamia had resolved the crisis with just a drop of blood.

"See? This is the power of the团长 (Leader)! You self-important demons, learn from this!" Vadie stood tall and proud, looking very pleased.

Merlin didn't feel like competing with this guy, but he still admired the vampire's ability. A single drop of blood could enslave ten thousand blade-toothed beasts, undoubtedly making Lamia a being very close to Dracula.

Merlin hadn't even had time to relax when a splash suddenly came from behind him. He turned around in surprise to see Jacob, terrified out of his wits, fearing he would be eaten by these hungry wolves. As soon as he saw the blade-toothed beasts were controlled, he immediately chose to jump off the lifeboat to escape.

Jacob couldn't trust these dark creatures. Before, they had let him live, but now that he knew their identities, would they allow him to continue living? So Jacob made a quick decision, jumping off the lifeboat, intending to find a safe place on his own. He would never be with a group of ruthless dark creatures; they were more dangerous than the blade-toothed beasts!

"I don't want to die! I want to live! Demons and vampires, who would want to be with them?"

"Definitely, I'll be eaten! Maybe they'll even use me as bait!"

"Even if I drown, it's better than being eaten until nothing remains!"

Jacob's eyes were filled with a strong will to survive. Even though there was no land nearby and he might drown, he refused to stay on the lifeboat.

He used all his strength, flailing his arms wildly, giving off the impression of a swimming champion.

It seemed that although Jacob was a spoiled rich kid, he hadn't neglected to practice survival skills.

"Hmph, this coward," Merlin said, watching Jacob's clumsy form in the water, his mouth twisting. "Lilith, get him."

"Sure thing," Lilith said, whipping her long鞭 (whip). With a "whoosh," it wrapped around Jacob's neck and pulled him up with force, sending the young master flying into the air.

"You big fat pig!"

"After showing off in front of us for so long, do you think you can run away?"

With the crisis over, the lifeboat steadily moved toward the western sea. The millions of blade-toothed beasts had been enslaved and were now working as laborers under Lamia's command.

The lifeboat sliced through the water, with a large number of blade-toothed beasts below helping to push it forward, making the speed very fast. With these blade-toothed beasts' help, the task of exploring the ruins could continue.

Lamia sat quietly on the edge, gently stroking the fat hand of a blade-toothed beast, treating it like a pet to pass the time.

Previously, this group of creatures had been extremely fierce, but now in Lamia's hands, they were as docile as dogs, showing no aggression at all.

Jacob, drenched and shivering, sat in the corner. Puduo was watching him, a malicious smile on his face.

Luo Yu didn't need to hide his special mark anymore; Puduo was in a very good mood. He usually saw this young master as arrogant, but now he could finally get his revenge.

Jacob sat stiffly, his body trembling, not daring to make a sound, afraid of attracting the attention of these "monsters."

He was so scared his intestines felt green. He shouldn't have approached these wolves in sheep's clothing, leading himself into this dangerous situation!

How would these dark creatures deal with him? There was no food on the lifeboat now, and he was the only human. What would happen?

Jacob's face grew increasingly pale. Even though he hadn't done anything wrong, he was terrified. He forced himself to glance around furtively.

Puduo had a malicious smile, writing something on his head with his special mark on "Merlin's Sayings."

Lilith played with her whip, her face showing excitement, as if preparing to whip Jacob to death.

Mahmoud, though not speaking much, still showed his sharp fangs at Jacob, constantly warning him.

Vadie was wiping his sharp blade, coldly humming at Jacob, his eyes flickering.

All of this, in Jacob's eyes, became a terrifying scenario. Jacob thought, Puduo was writing his will, Lilith would whip him to death, Mahmoud would suck his blood dry and make it into preservable meat, and finally, Vadie would cut open his body and everyone would share it!

Merlin cleared his throat, trying to appear serious. "Young master Jacob,"

"I'm so doomed!" Jacob, hearing Merlin's voice, was instantly struck by lightning. He thought he was about to be sentenced to death by the Demon Lord and had only one last chance to leave a final message.

"I shouldn't have been so foolish to come to this place!"

"I shouldn't have been so stupid to get on this pirate ship full of bandits!"

"Besides having a bit more pocket money, I seem to be useless!"

"Since childhood, I've lived in my father's shadow. No one thinks I have any merits. The only thing I can boast about is being the son of the Roschilde family!"

"I don't want this. I envy those who achieve things through their own efforts, unlike me, who has no choice but to return to inherit a hundred million fortune and enjoy the envious looks of others!"

"I've already prepared to end my sinful life. When you eat me, please add more spicy seasoning and less salt. That might be more delicious. This is my final contribution."

Merlin's expression was stunned, a bit dazed by Jacob's long monologue. "You calm down first. It's not what you think."

Jacob's eyes immediately welled up with tears, feeling like he had been given a second life. He pitifully said, "I knew it, Master Merlin wouldn't eat me. In my eyes, you've always been an excellent demon, ah, no, an excellent demon lord, completely different from those brutal demons in the stories. You truly deserve to be the King of the Demon Race, with the finest character and temperament. If I were female, I would definitely fall in love with you疯狂ly!"

"Still, still, you seem to have misunderstood," Merlin waved his hands repeatedly.

"Ah? What misunderstanding?" Jacob asked, his face full of confusion.

"Does adding more spicy seasoning and less salt really make the meat more delicious?"

Merlin put away his serious expression and revealed a mysterious smile.

"Originally, I didn't want to eat you, but what you said seems quite convincing~"

"Hmm! You've convinced me! You're truly a little genius!" Jacob: "d

(j)

title: Chapter 29 — It's Here
content:
Chapter 29 — It's Here

Volume 30 · Chapter 29

"Your Majesty makes a good point. We've always eaten it this way, to be honest the meat is just so-so, a bit sour, with a little less salt and more chili. This way of eating, I've never heard of it before." Pudouhai showed interest, nodding his head.

"This young master has tender skin and delicate flesh, definitely better than those fishermen. Raised so plump, and then slaughtered, what a waste?" Lilith's gaze was like looking at a turkey in a normal demon's eyes, just another food on the wall.

"The meat is yours, the blood is ours. Actually, I've long wanted to bite through his throat, I just don't know if his blood has the same strong smell of money?" Mendiye sharpened his knife menacingly.

"Four districts are still waiting! Mahamud was silent and taciturn, but still indicated that Jacob was basically enough to eat!

Listening to these 'monsters' discussing him, Jacob shrank back in fear, continuously retreating, his face suddenly losing all color. He had thought Merlin would show mercy and spare him, but instead, they were more interested in eating him!

Jacob 'thudded' to the ground, immediately wailing loudly, like a pig being slaughtered.

"I don't want to die! My meat isn't even good, it's sour, please spare me, great masters! I can help you deceive my father, he'll definitely give you a lot of money!"

Merlin looked at this 'great son' with interest, calmly asking, "Do you want to die?"

"Yes! Merlin, as long as you let me live, I swear to be your horse for life!" Jacob crawled up, tightly hugging Merlin's leg.

"But we can't easily let you go. You know our identities, letting you go back would be troublesome for us~" Merlin said meaningfully.

"Eh! Jacob's eyes widened, realizing where he had gone wrong. He shouldn't have known these things!

No wonder these demons and vampires wanted to eat him, they were afraid he'd go back and expose their identities! Whether it was the adventurer Merlin or the mercenary group, they all lived among humans as evil beings. They definitely didn't want their identities exposed, which would disrupt their lives. So to avoid exposure, they had to kill him to be at ease!

Jacob thought more and felt his life hanging by a thread, depending on whether he could stand on the right side!

"Merlin! I swear to heaven, I won't utter a single word about your affairs after I go back! This secret, I'll take to my grave!"

"Oh? Is that so? How can I trust you? As far as I know, only the dead can keep secrets." Merlin hinted at Jacob.

"Then I can too! If you don't believe me, you can kill me anytime!" Jacob's tone was extremely firm.

"Interesting~" Merlin smiled, continuing, "But if you go around talking, killing you would be useless, wouldn't it?"

"Merlin, how could I dare? I still want my life! If I betray you, you can destroy my family at any time!" Jacob showed a sincere gaze, believing that with Merlin's abilities, the truth would be hard to stop. Moreover, if he went back alive, he could be a loyal servant by Merlin's side. Once the old man passed away, the entire Roschilde family would be at Merlin's beck and call.

"You're quite a filial son." Merlin said awkwardly.

"I'm my father's only son, the inheritance won't go to anyone else! The business empire I've worked hard to build, in the end, it's all mine!" Jacob said confidently, without a shred of shame.

Merlin didn't bother to comment on Jacob's character, instead asking seriously, "Is what you said true?"

"Of course! If there's one false word, Merlin, you can turn me to ashes, I swear!" Jacob stared, making an oath.

"Hmph, remember not to cause trouble, listen to my orders, otherwise next time you encounter such monsters, I won't save you~" Merlin turned away, temporarily sparing Jacob.

"Yes yes yes, whatever Merlin says, I'll obey!" Jacob nodded like a chick pecking rice, his heart slightly relieved. He didn't have the guts to betray Merlin; being targeted by such a powerful being, escaping to the ends of the earth would be useless.

Actually, Merlin didn't have any intention of killing Jacob to silence him. This kind of timid person was easiest to control; with a little intimidation, they'd become obedient. If Jacob died, it would be of no benefit to Merlin. As for Roschilde senior, no matter how he valued wealth, he wouldn't treat his only bloodline as mere wealth.

Merlin could kill the old man's guards at will, but touching his son would require more consideration. It wasn't that Merlin feared Roschilde, but rather, seeing the potential wealth, he decided to give the old man some face.

Moreover, Jacob would become the future head of the Roschilde family, and their influence would become a helpful force in Merlin's hands.

Leviathan watched the three vampires with great interest, "You vampires, where does your power come from? I've seen some dark cult scriptures, they recorded the story of the fallen god's enemy. Your power is very similar to it, could it be related to the sealed Cain?"

"None of your business." Lamia stroked the knife-toothed beast on her leg, not wanting to reveal the truth about the vampire clan.

"Hmph! What secret can't be told? You must have seen the sealed Cain in the holy vessel! In the southern forest of the Franclaren Plains, in the mysterious temple deep within..." Merlin's tone was full of meaning, deducing that Lamia possessed terrifying power, able to control countless knife-toothed beasts with just a drop of blood. This power, inferior only to Dracula's, must be closely related to the three ancestral bloodlines of Cain!

Lamia was shocked, suddenly lifting her head, feeling that this demon king was full of mystery, knowing even such things!

"How did you know..."

Before Lamia could ask, the sky suddenly boomed with thunder, the knife-toothed beasts propelling the ship seemed to sense a powerful and terrifying existence, all diving into the depths of the sea.

Even Lamia's bloodline couldn't suppress the beasts' fear, these fearless creatures actually showed a terrified expression?

"What happened? What's going on?" Lilith was full of question marks, only feeling the sky and earth change color, the sea becoming turbulent.

Leviathan's face changed dramatically, warning, "Something's coming! Lamia and the other two vampires stood up, entering a state of readiness. Their instincts sensed the impending danger!

Jacob quickly hid behind everyone, silently praying to the gods, realizing the danger of this journey far exceeded his imagination.

Merlin's face was cold, watching the abnormal sky, the black sea, the dark clouds connecting, with occasional terrifying waves rising in the distance. It didn't look like an ordinary storm.

This scene was familiar...

"Your Majesty, look ahead, there's an island!" Pudoum pointed to a small island not far away, covered in bushes, blown eastward by the wind, even uprooted!

Merlin grabbed the oar and threw it to Pudoum and the others with strength, saying seriously, "Quick! We must land on the island, we absolutely can't stay on the sea!"

"Your Majesty, what's wrong? You seem very tense." Pudoum held the oar, asking curiously.

Merlin's expression was serious, the familiar scene before him making him immediately recall a terrifying existence...

"It's coming.

s■

Sorry everyone, I'm really sorry. It's busy during the New Year period, and I'm worried. It'll be better after tonight, I hope you understand. Also, wishing everyone a happy New Year, may everything go smoothly this year."

title: Chapter 30 — The Entrance Is Nearby
content:
Chapter 30 — The Entrance Is Nearby

Volume 30 · Chapter 30

In the lifeboat, several of the stronger individuals were desperately hauling on their oars, racing toward the small island amid the storm's howling front. But the sea was no longer calm; waves crashed relentlessly against the tiny craft as if随时 ready to capsize it.

The lifeboat advanced with enormous difficulty across the tossing seas, and whether they would reach the island safely remained uncertain.

They exerted every ounce of strength, nearly snapping the oars in half, yet reaching the island ahead still seemed far too difficult.

After all, this was merely a small lifeboat — nothing like a sturdy warship or merchant vessel. In the storm, it was as vulnerable as a falling feather.

Merlin stared fixedly at the island ahead. As long as they reached land, confronting the Kraken wasn't impossible, but drifting on the open ocean put them at a glaring disadvantage.

Merlin's Earth Spirit mana was still slowly recovering, making it difficult to replicate the powerful propulsion he had used to escape the Saber-Toothed Beast. They could only inch closer to the island through sheer manpower.

Putdown, Vadier, and Mahmud were all rowing with their lives on the line. After painstakingly advancing perhaps ten meters, the waves would push them back five.

Merlin sensed disaster if things continued this way. If they had Medusa, the Chaos King, perhaps they could temporarily control the Kraken for a time — but Medusa's head had already been stolen by pirates.

Dark clouds rolled across the horizon as the storm grew ever more ferocious, a somber gloom spreading through the sky.

Right then, in the pitch-black deep sea, the Kraken — the nightmare of countless sailors — was likely closing in on their tiny lifeboat.

Or rather, on this group of death-seeking, greedy souls who wished to plunder various ruins.

Unlike the others' tension, Leviathan appeared far calmer, scanning their surroundings with what seemed like the faintest hint of excitement at Kraken's arrival.

"Merlin, even I know the Kraken is coming. How did you know?"

"When I traveled to that mysterious sea zone, I encountered one once. The scene then matched this exactly," Merlin replied gravely.

"You've also been to such a鬼 place? Seems like you homebodies go through quite a lot after getting fired," Leviathan said, somewhat surprised. Mysterious sea zones were among the most dangerous places on earth, few willing to explore them.

"If given the chance, I'd prefer to remain a homebody forever. Unfortunately, circumstances didn't allow it," Merlin replied with a touch of helplessness.

Leviathan glanced at Merlin curiously, tilting his head. "How did you escape the Kraken last time?"

"I barely escaped. Actually, I've never understood why the Kraken appears in random places occasionally. Isn't it supposed to guard ruins?"

This question had plagued Merlin for some time, making it hard to discern the sea monster's behavioral patterns.

"My father once told me that the Kraken is a creature that serves the ancient gods. Its duty isn't merely guarding ruins — it exists to maintain the统治 of the gods themselves. When it suddenly appears in odd places, it likely senses threats to the gods and goes to eliminate the source. But Kraken should well know the era of the ancient gods long ended."

Leviathan frowned, recalling his initial teachings.

Merlin listened with great astonishment, uncertain whether Leviathan's words were true. Yet the first-generation demons were very close to the era of the gods, so their greater understanding of the Kraken was unquestionable.

If the Kraken were an immature monster that still believed it lived in the gods' era, then its appearance in Norway three hundred years ago — had there been a powerful being capable of rivaling the ancient gods then?

And during the incident in the mysterious sea zone, he had already slain the ruler there, the Chaos King. He hadn't encountered any monsters that could truly rival the gods.

A wave of unease washed over Merlin. He had been in this world for quite some time now, yet his understanding of the world remained limited to what books told him — superficial at best. Perhaps he had never truly encountered a powerful existence.

"If at full strength, could you handle this monster?"

"Full strength?" Leviathan gave a bitter smile. "Though I'm hailed as the Demon Lord of the Seas, confronting a monster on this level isn't easy. My chance of victory is only forty percent. What about you?"

"No chance," Merlin answered honestly.

"Hah! I thought you'd at least have around thirty percent. Guess not." Leviathan shook his head, clearly disappointed.

"I said no chance on the open sea. But on land, my chance—" Merlin looked at Leviathan and replied seriously, "is sixty percent."

"Huh?" Leviathan blinked, somewhat suspicious. Didn't Merlin know when to humble himself? Was the difference between sea and land really that great?

"Hmm! What's there to be surprised about? My brother was never suited for naval combat anyway," Lilith interjected from the side.

"Are you all still discussing how to face the Kraken head-on? At a time like this, wouldn't it be better to flee?" Lahmia suddenly spoke up.

"Retreating without fighting doesn't suit our demon nature!" Chris turned to emphasize.

"That's precisely why many of you demons are such stubborn fools. I don't dislike it though," Lahmia shrugged.

"Miss Lahmia may not understand. If we weren't stubborn and unyielding, we'd have been wiped out long ago. At times, stubbornness isn't necessarily a bad thing," Merlin explained.

"Suit yourselves. The three of us have no intention of fighting the Kraken. Such a creature holds no meaning for us. You may die here, but we can easily survive thanks to our resilient vitality." Lahmia made her stance clear, strongly opposing direct confrontation with the Kraken.

"Not wanting to fight? That's not up to you to decide. It depends on whether that monster will let us go."

Hardly had Merlin finished speaking when a deafening roar echoed — like a deep-sea leviathan bellowing — shaking the very surface of the sea and sending towering waves surging upward.

Soundwaves crashed over them like a storm. Everyone aboard the lifeboat paled. Those with weaker physiques, like Lilith, felt their heads split with pain, ringing in their ears.

In the end, Kraken had caught up to Merlin's group. As the guardian of the godly ruins, it would never allow vermin to随意 enter sacred grounds.

Bang! Several enormous tentacles erupted from the sea surface — massive and thick as pillars reaching the heavens. Though they moved slowly, none would dare underestimate Kraken's power.

Looking around, the tiny lifeboat seemed completely surrounded at the center of Kraken's tentacles, with no escape route whatsoever. Any slight movement would see them swept into the monster's grasp.

"This is Kraken. First time I've seen it with my own eyes," Leviathan said grimly, silently clenching his fists.

Putdown licked his dry lips, tossed his oar aside, and said awkwardly, "Your Majesty, we can no longer reach the island ahead."

"Brother?" Lilith felt a flicker of fear. She knew her brother's combat prowess at sea was limited. Even her trust in Merlin wavered, tinged with danger.

"There's no need to fear!" Merlin gazed at the despair-inducing Kraken, his expression filled with resolve, and shouted loudly,

"Encountering the Kraken isn't necessarily a bad thing!"

"At the very least—"

"It proves we came to the right place. The entrance to the various ruins is nearby!"

title: Chapter 31 — Sea Overlord vs Land Overlord?
content:
Chapter 31 — Sea Overlord vs Land Overlord?

Volume 30 · Chapter 31

"Right here?" Merlin looked around the sea, only to find nothing but the vast ocean and a tiny, isolated island. There didn’t seem to be anything else nearby. Where exactly was the entrance to the ruins?

"What proof do you have?" Lamia demanded sternly. "We’re already within the attack range of the North Sea Leviathan. If you’re trying to calm everyone with lies at a time like this, none of us will make it out alive. ★First★Release★EZRead★"

"Proof? I’m just going by my intuition," Merlin replied. "We’ve sailed this far, and according to the navigation charts, we should have arrived by now. The fact that we’ve suddenly run into this monster suggests the entrance to the ruins might be nearby!"

Even if the entrance was close, though, how were they supposed to get inside? That was another problem entirely.

"Even if the entrance is nearby, how do we get in?" Lamia snapped, her frustration boiling over. "Captain, you’re being far too reckless! Do you really expect some nonexistent goddess of luck to solve everything for you?"

"All of you, quiet down!" Lilith barked, turning to scold them. The moment the North Sea Leviathan appeared, the people on the lifeboat had fallen into despair. They hadn’t even faced the Kraken head-on yet, and already, their morale was crumbling.

"Exactly. A monster like the North Sea Leviathan—apart from our lord, there isn’t a single person on this ship who could stand against it." Pudom gave up on resisting and placed all his hope in Merlin.

Belial shot Merlin a meaningful glance. Deep down, he still had no confidence in this third-generation Demon Lord. Even he himself couldn’t claim to be able to completely defeat the Kraken.

"Tch! Relying on this inexperienced captain is like digging our own graves!" Vadiye scoffed, unable to resist mocking Merlin. "Sure, he might be famous, the Demon Lord who’s stood against the Holy Church countless times with sheer power. But facing the North Sea Leviathan? That’s a joke. And this is its territory—its home turf!"

"Vadiye’s right," Mahakal nodded heavily. This was a life-or-death moment. They couldn’t entrust their lives to someone so unreliable.

"You again, spouting nonsense!" Lilith’s anger flared at the sound of Vadiye’s voice. "Have you already forgotten how my brother just saved everyone from the school of fish?"

"Hah! What brother? It was our captain who saved you!" Vadiye retorted, lifting his chin proudly.

"You saying what?" Lilith rolled up her sleeves, ready to lunge at Vadiye and throw hands.

"Calm down, Lilith," Pudom quickly stepped in to block her. "Don’t stoop to the level of these lowly creatures."

"Hahaha!" Merlin burst into laughter, then turned to Lamia, the vampire queen, and teased, "You all have no imagination. The Kraken hasn’t even fully shown itself, and you’re already this shaken? It’s just an oversized octopus. Haven’t you eaten octopus before? It’s not a god—just one of the gods’ dim-witted janitors! What makes you think it’s invincible?"

His tone was filled with confidence. But did he really not understand the Kraken’s reputation? For countless epochs, it had been the nightmare of the seas, a scourge that had crushed every challenger. How could he dismiss it so easily? Just because he was a Demon Lord? Did he truly believe that being a once-in-a-millennium prodigy made him invincible? Lamia’s expression turned grave, and she even used the dismissive term "kid" to mock him. "Don’t be so naive."

"This is the first time anyone’s called me *naive*," Merlin said, straightening up. He stepped to the bow of the ship and unbuckled the demon sword Banri Garan from his waist.

"Watch closely, you ignorant vampires," he declared. "I didn’t become Demon Lord just because I’m Lucifer’s grandson. That’s far too simple."

The sky darkened as if night had fallen in an instant. The sea was no longer calm—under the Kraken’s agitation, terrifying waves surged repeatedly.

Perhaps to the North Sea Leviathan, the creatures on the lifeboat were nothing more than ants, insignificant specks.

This nightmare of the sea, which had tormented humanity for ages, had never had its true form witnessed. Every record of it described only its terrifying tentacles.

The Kraken’s body was submerged deep in the abyss, its massive tentacles lashing out viciously toward the tiny lifeboat. Clearly, it wouldn’t tolerate even this grain of sand in its eye. The thick, colossal tentacles stretched like pillars connecting sea and sky. Even before they struck, they radiated a suffocating terror.

The small lifeboat was engulfed in shadow. Even with extraordinary abilities, escape from such a devastating, large-scale attack seemed impossible.

Pudom gulped, his heart pounding with fear. *Was that a tentacle?* It looked more like an entire mountain crashing down on them!

Lilith’s mind went blank. *Run? How?* There was nowhere to go. *We’re doomed.*

Leviathan watched Merlin, a thought crossing his mind. *Wasn’t Vevean supposed to dote on this kid?* Normally, with Merlin’s lowly bloodline, no high-ranking demon mother would have cared for him—he should’ve been abandoned as a child. But since Vevean, that madwoman, had placed such importance on him… perhaps he really was different?

Leviathan’s expression turned solemn. *Unless… Merlin still has untapped potential.* If the Iaijutsu he had displayed before all the Demon Lords was his limit, then defeating the North Sea Leviathan would be nothing but a pipe dream.

Merlin stood alone at the bow, gripping his sword tightly as he faced the horrifying spectacle before him. The Kraken’s tentacle came crashing down, whipping up a wave over ten meters high.

With a thunderous roar, it struck like a warship charging headlong into battle, reckless and unstoppable.

A cold sweat broke out on Lamia’s forehead as she watched Merlin’s resolute back. She was stunned. Instead of fleeing, he had chosen to meet the Kraken’s onslaught head-on. She had to admit, the guy had guts. But if he failed, they’d all be buried with him.

*Shing—*

The crisp, melodic sound of a sword being drawn rang out. Merlin had no other choice. This was the perfect moment to strike with Iaijutsu!

Facing the ferocious North Sea Leviathan, Merlin didn’t unleash his full power. Instead, he desperately suppressed the violent energy of his draw-cut.

Merlin wanted to strike the Kraken head-on while also preserving the lifeboat beneath him. It was an incredibly difficult balance, but he had to try.

Defeating the North Sea Leviathan *and* keeping the lifeboat intact—that was the perfect outcome Merlin had set in his mind.

The draw-cut unleashed a shockwave that surpassed even the Kraken’s momentum. The sheer force of the strike shot forward like a blade slicing through the void.

The pressure of the attack was so intense that it warped space itself, turning the faces of Lamia and the three vampires behind him pale with terror.

The Iaijutsu split the sea in three. The Kraken’s terrifying tentacle, along with the towering waves, were all cleaved apart.

The Kraken’s blood instantly dyed the seawater red. The nightmare of the sea, which had tormented humanity for so long, had just met a land-based nightmare even more terrifying.

Lamia’s lips trembled. Her mind was a tangled mess. All her knowledge, all her experience—none of it mattered in the face of such overwhelming power.

"Sure is an amateur magician."
