title: Chapter 32 — Relic Reaction
content:
Chapter 32 — Relic Reaction

Volume 30 · Chapter 32

A massive North Sea Kraken's severed limb fell into the depths of the ocean with a splash, sending up a towering wave.

Its blood churned wildly in the sea, dyeing the waters a deep crimson in an instant.

The Kraken, which had always bullied humans without restraint, thought these insignificant creatures on a tiny lifeboat would be just as easy to crush. It assumed a few swings of its tentacles would send the cowardly humans flying, their souls scattering in terror.

But this so-called scourge of humanity, which had tormented countless people, had finally met its match. The moment it attacked, it suffered a heavy blow.

The North Sea Kraken, deep in the ocean, thrashed in agony after losing a tentacle. Its pained roars, like the calls of a whale, echoed through the heavens and earth, shaking the sea into violent waves.

And this was the result of Merlin constantly suppressing his power after drawing his sword. If not for the need to protect the last lifeboat, had he unleashed his full strength on land, the terrifying Kraken might have been split in half on the spot!

Merlin worriedly looked down at the lifeboat beneath him. Apart from some loose planks and minor leaks caused by the aftershocks of his Iaijutsu, it was still mostly intact. He secretly let out a sigh of relief—

Phew! Good, good. His control over his strength was still precise.

The Iaijutsu he had just used was slightly stronger than when he and Alice had first encountered the Sea Serpent Dragon years ago. He had feared the entire bow of the ship would collapse, but fortunately, no major problems arose.

It seemed the Kraken had learned its lesson. It should know by now that he wasn’t to be trifled with. Not only had he scared off the North Sea Kraken, but he had also protected the last lifeboat. How satisfying~

With that thought, Merlin’s face broke into a small smile. He returned the demon sword Banri Garan to its scabbard and turned to the stunned crowd.

"How was that? As I said before, the Kraken is just an oversized squid! The so-called 'invincible legends' are nothing more than exaggerated tales passed down by word of mouth!"

Leviathan stared at Merlin, feeling that he understood this young Demon Lord less and less. Back when Merlin had inherited the throne and displayed his skills to all the Demon Lords, he had clearly held back.

"Of course, what’s so strange about that? As long as I could prove I had what it took to sit on the Demon Lord’s throne, that was enough." Merlin lifted his head, recalling the past, and casually flicked his finger. "Back then, I probably only used a fraction of my strength to gain your recognition."

"A fraction?!"

Leviathan was horrified, unable to tell if Merlin was serious. If it was true, then it was truly terrifying!

Back then, Merlin, a mere youngster, had declared he would demonstrate his ultimate skill—the Iaijutsu—and was met with ridicule from all the Demon Lords. It had even become a joke among the entire demon race. Demons believed that if Merlin became their ruler, he would lower the prestige of all Demon Lords.

After all, anyone with even a passing knowledge of swordsmanship knew that Iaijutsu was just flashy showmanship—good for looking impressive when drawing a sword or impressing ignorant girls, but utterly useless in actual combat. It was nothing more than a low-tier sword technique.

That day, Merlin had arrived at the barren plains of the Sea of Death with his sword. The other Demon Lords had gathered to laugh at him, but the result had stunned them all—

What seemed like a useless Iaijutsu had unleashed terrifying destructive power. The Mountain of the Throne was leveled to the ground, leaving behind the magnificent Orkney Trench.

None of the Demon Lords had expected such a flashy sword technique to possess such overwhelming might. Just how much determination and effort had it taken to refine Iaijutsu to such a level?

Leviathan took a deep, chilled breath. If a fraction of his power could intimidate a monster like the North Sea Kraken, what would happen if he went all out? She couldn’t even imagine.

"Your magic pales in comparison to your swordsmanship. You truly are a master swordsman." Lamia couldn’t help but admire him. Such powerful sword techniques were rare—she had only seen two others like it.

"I’ve always said I’m an amateur mage. Magic? What’s that? I don’t really understand it." Merlin shrugged, telling the truth. He genuinely knew nothing about magic. The only reason he could use some earth and lightning spells now was because of the magic beast core from the Spirit of the Earth.

But in the eyes of others, it seemed different. Lamia thought Merlin was just showing off his strength.

Gravity magic was already considered an easily controllable force within earth magic. And with the power Merlin had displayed, it was enough to make even professional mages bow their heads in shame!

"Hmph~" Lilith couldn’t help but lift her nose, glancing at Vadye. "Well? Do you still doubt my brother’s strength?"

Vadye coughed lightly, awkwardly looking away. His fear of Merlin was genuine. That single slash could have killed him a hundred times over. "Not bad, I suppose. After all, you *are* a legendary Demon Lord. Cutting off one of the Kraken’s tentacles is impressive... but you didn’t even kill it. What’s there to be proud of?"

"Our lord was protecting the ship!" Pudong glared at Vadye, thinking this guy was just being stubborn after getting off easy. "If you had jumped into the sea to feed the fish, our lord could’ve chopped the Kraken to pieces in two minutes!"

"Merlin! That monster seems to have gone mad!"

Jacob, who had been closely observing the sea, suddenly shouted. The North Sea Kraken had fallen into a rage!

Merlin’s expression turned serious again as he looked at the enraged sea monster—

The Kraken, having suffered a heavy blow, wasn’t retreating. Instead, it had grown even angrier. It seemed unafraid of Merlin’s Iaijutsu and was determined to make these ignorant fools pay the price!

The pained Kraken thrashed in the water, creating violent waves that crashed down one after another. How could a small lifeboat withstand such a force? It was instantly shattered, and everyone was thrown into the sea!

After a while, Pudong was the first to surface. He wiped the salty, fishy seawater from his face and shouted anxiously, "Everyone! Are you alright? Say something!"

"I-I-I-I’m alive! I’m still alive!" Jacob was lucky enough to be near the wreckage of the lifeboat and clung tightly to a plank.

Lamia, Vadye, and Mehamu quickly surfaced one after another, their faces filled with panic. Even with their powerful vitality, they couldn’t help but feel the situation was dire.

Lilith treaded water, looking around in all directions, her heart filled with worry. "Where’s my brother? Pudong! Where’s my brother? He can’t swim!"

"Your Majesty?! I don’t see him!" Pudong panicked, turning his head in every direction.

"Here." Leviathan carried Merlin to the surface. After the lifeboat was destroyed, she had saved Merlin’s life. She was an excellent swimmer—she could drift at sea for days without a problem, unlike Merlin, who was like a drowning rat.

"Cough—"

Merlin was weak, his entire body drenched, looking utterly miserable. He didn’t even know how much of the foul, fishy seawater he had swallowed. He had nearly lost consciousness.

"Brother! Are you okay?!" Lilith asked worriedly. She thought, *This old problem again—fighting at sea is too dangerous for him!*

Merlin gritted his teeth, resenting the Kraken. He wished he could drag it onto land and settle the score properly!

"What do we do now? The Kraken is right beneath us! If we don’t do something, we might get eaten!" Lamia gritted her teeth. Even with infinite regeneration, being swallowed by the North Sea Kraken would be inescapable!

Merlin looked around, his gaze falling on a distant small island. He bitterly smiled to himself. *So this is how we die...*

Suddenly, Jacob let out a pained shout, drawing everyone’s attention—

"Hot! So hot! It’s burning!"

Jacob frantically clawed at his chest, his face contorted in pain. The relic fragment hanging around his neck suddenly glowed with a brilliant golden light!

This was the item Roschild had given to his son, a necessary tool for entering various ruins. And now, it was finally reacting!

The relic fragment shot into the sky, and since it was around Jacob’s neck, it lifted him up with it.

"Merlin! Save me! Save me!"

title: Chapter 33 — A Little Push (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 33 — A Little Push (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 30 · Chapter 33

"Merlin, you big—

I'm about to—"

The relic fragment dangled Jacob from the neck, dragging him skyward. The cord bit into his throat, choking him as if he were being hanged. Jacob’s face flushed crimson, his eyes bulged, and his legs kicked wildly, searching for solid ground that wasn’t there.

This relic fragment carried the immense force of countless worlds. As it neared the divine ruins, it naturally sensed a mysterious call, yearning to return to its rightful place.

"???" Merlin stared at Jacob in bewilderment, not even considering saving the young master. Instead, he wondered what kind of mysterious force was pulling him.

A hollow melody echoed through the air, like a saint gently plucking harp strings in a temple. A point of light flared, then spread outward like an electric current.

Countless stars began to move in an orderly dance, gradually forming a faint, translucent colossal wall.

The intricate paths on its surface were clearly visible, resembling a vast and complex labyrinth. The magnificent wall left everyone in awe—

What kind of mighty civilization could have built such a wondrous barrier?

Unfortunately, this masterpiece of a wall had an obvious flaw. Right above everyone’s heads was a glaring, irregular hole, ruining its perfection.

Fragments similar to the one around Jacob’s neck floated nearby, and the edges of the hole were riddled with shocking cracks, as if it had been shattered by force.

"That is...?!" Klamia furrowed her brows. She had never seen such a sight before, and doubt filled her mind.

"What kind of wall is this? Could it be a sky city?" Vadiye’s mind raced with possibilities.

A powerful pull emanated from the hole, suggesting that inside the wall lay an enormous space.

Poor Jacob, it seemed no one cared about him. Helpless, he was dragged toward the massive hole.

"Down there—that’s the entrance to the ruins!" someone shouted. "Everyone, get inside!"

Before anyone could figure out how to enter, the ruins themselves extended an invitation.

The hole’s pull suddenly intensified, even sucking up seawater into its inky depths.

"What’s happening?!!" Lilith’s expression froze as she was yanked from the sea, flying toward the hole in the wall. She could only press down her skirt, her limbs flailing in panic.

"S-Situation!" Pudohai, overwhelmed by the immense force, lost control of his body and tumbled head over heels into the air.

Klamia, Vadiye, and the vampire king Mehaymed didn’t resist at all. Their only thought was to escape the North Sea Leviathan’s wrath as far as possible, so they followed Jacob into the hole.

Merlin was in poor condition, but fortunately, Leviathan knew his state and dragged him along.

The two burst from the sea’s surface, using the powerful pull to soar toward the mysterious hole—until suddenly, the situation took a turn for the worse.

The raging sea began to churn, forming a massive whirlpool. Kraken, having barely recovered, was in a furious rage. A few ants dared to intrude into the sacred home of its descendants?!

A massive "landmass" of seaweed, coral, and flesh rose from the water—a gaping maw lined with rows of jagged teeth, a living meat grinder!

Kraken inhaled sharply. Leviathan and Merlin, at the rear, were the first to suffer. Unable to reach the hole in the sky, they were instead pulled toward the Leviathan’s gaping mouth, descending rapidly.

Below them yawned the blood-red abyss of its throat. How could the North Sea Leviathan allow these ants to run wild before its eyes, let alone trespass into the sacred ruins?

"Damn it!" Leviathan’s face paled. The closer they fell, the stronger Kraken’s pull became. At this rate, they’d end up as its snack!

"Mutual destruction?" Merlin’s face twisted in a grimace as he tightened his grip on Banri Garan, ready to strike down the North Sea Leviathan. If he was going to die here, this monster wouldn’t live either.

"Your Majesty!!!" Pudohai let out a desperate cry before vanishing into the darkness of the hole.

"Brother?!" Lilith saw Merlin being dragged down and her heart filled with both worry and frustration. She swiftly lashed out with her whip, barely managing to wrap it around Merlin’s wrist. "Hold on! Come up!"

For a moment, a stalemate formed. The two were caught between the pull of the hole in the wall and Kraken’s gaping maw.

Lilith yanked hard on her whip, straining with all her might to pull Merlin and Leviathan free from Kraken’s grasp.

But as a mage, how much strength could Lilith possibly have? Not only could she not save them, her own body began to descend as well!

Leviathan looked down at the enraged North Sea Leviathan, then back at Merlin. If this continued, they were all doomed.

"Lilith! Push harder!" Merlin shouted urgently.

"I’m trying!!!" Lilith gritted her teeth, but how could she possibly match the strength of a sea monster? A single sneeze from it could shatter her bones.

Leviathan took a deep breath, as if making a decision. It pulled Merlin closer, its voice eerily calm.

"Don’t rush me. She can’t save us. If we keep this up, we’ll all end up as Kraken’s meal."

"It looks like this is the end for me. Promise me one thing."

"Huh?" Merlin stared at Leviathan in shock, sensing the gravity in its tone, its demeanor, its words.

"If you make it out of here alive, give Mammon a piece of my mind. Better yet, knock out those ugly fangs of his. I’ve never liked that guy, especially that big, hideous mouth of his."

Leviathan paused, then added indifferently, "I’m from the same era as your mother, you know. You should call me Uncle Levi. Compared to me, you’re still young. You have far more potential than I ever did. I’ll admit, I used to look down on you—some demon reborn through charm magic, acting like Merlin’s heir as if it were a joke. But after getting to know you, maybe I was wrong. You have what it takes to become a greater demon. Who knows? You might even surpass your old man, the first Lucifer, the one called the strongest swordsman among demons."

"Hey, what kind of flag are you setting up here?!" Merlin glared at Leviathan, a growing sense of unease creeping over him.

"Flag? What’s that? Your mother always said you’ve been spouting nonsense since you were little. Seems she was right." Leviathan chuckled, then mustered every last bit of strength. With a sudden, powerful shove against Merlin’s back, it sent him flying out of Kraken’s reach and toward the hole in the ruins.

Merlin shot upward like a cannonball, straight for the entrance.

Lilith cried out as, freed from the weight of Leviathan and Merlin, her body surged upward once more.

A violent gale howled, icy droplets sprayed upward, and lightning tore across the sky.

Merlin turned, horrified, to look below. Leviathan, drained of strength, was being pulled into Kraken’s maw. The toothed abyss clamped shut without hesitation, swallowing the Sea Demon King whole.

If Leviathan hadn’t done that... Merlin might never have escaped Kraken’s blood-red jaws.

"LEVIATHAN!!!"

The North Sea Leviathan had only managed to devour three of the "ants," which did little to sate its rage. It roared furiously at the sky, its massive tentacles lashing out, churning the sea into chaos.

But apart from Leviathan, everyone else had successfully entered the divine ruins. There was nothing it could do.

title: Chapter 34 — Fall of Sarre County
content:
Chapter 34 — Fall of Sarre County

Volume 30 · Chapter 34

The Saly County, adjacent to the royal capital London, was primarily an agricultural region renowned for its high-quality military wool, famous far and wide.

The lord of Saly County was not only a wise and peaceful ruler but also a devout follower of the Amitabha Sect. Every year, he donated generously to the church. Yet, the Holy Church he had always believed in had not come to his aid in his darkest hour. The Benevolent Goddess of Light, the spiritual pillar of countless believers, seemed like a nonexistent entity, never appearing. The land of Saly County had already fallen under the control of the demon race. Looking north, the only unoccupied place left was the royal capital of Britain!

The devout lord, even on his deathbed, had been praying, but in the end, even his entire family had their heads chopped off by demons and hung on the city walls, declaring the brutality and terror of the demon race.

The demon army’s iron hooves crushed all in their path, advancing at a speed that could only be described as lightning-fast, swiftly occupying and controlling human cities along the way.

Even if they occasionally encountered resistance, how could these ragtag humans possibly resist the regular army of the demon race? They were crushed in minutes!

From the Portly Defense Line to now, in just ten short days, the demons had already reached Saly County. There was little difference between this and the gates of the royal capital.

If the demon race could also capture the royal capital London, it would mark the preliminary completion of their mission. They could declare that Britain was on the verge of collapse, that the royal authority had crumbled, and that the demon race had already begun to control the entire Kingdom of Britain.

Recently, the demon race had heard voices of accusation from the Council of Elders. Even with Belial secretly helping him, Asmodeus still felt considerable pressure!

Asmodeus, in collusion with others like Sammael, had proposed that the demon race immediately retreat and accept the judgment of the Council of Elders, to be imprisoned in the Abyss for reflection.

This infuriated Mammon. He left his subordinates behind and cursed the other Demon Lords viciously, even digging up a pile of old grievances. In his eyes, Asmodeus was nothing but a product of recent propagation, a fool with a muddled mind!

And Asmodeus, surrounded by female demons day and night, had a warped psychology and couldn’t even tell whether he was male or female!

Even the cunning Sammael wasn’t spared, called a brainless warrior by Mammon—so stupid he couldn’t even keep his own head!

The corrupt Mammon, in a hysterical outburst, slandered the other rulers. In truth, he was afraid. The joint proposal from the three Demon Lords carried great weight.

If Belial couldn’t hold up under the pressure from the Council of Elders, and Mammon still insisted on invading Britain, he might have already been thrown into the Abyss, becoming a laughingstock among the demon race.

But there were only a few days left. As long as they could take the royal capital of Britain, everything would change. Mammon would present his accumulated victories to the faces of his opponents, silencing them all.

Mammon’s army plundered wherever they went, slaughtering humans who couldn’t escape, taking all their wealth, leaving not a single gold coin behind.

Ridiculously, the looting along the way had gone smoothly, with almost no encounter with powerful resistance.

Even the few resisting forces were just hastily assembled groups of territorial guards and militias, utterly powerless against the demonic iron hooves.

The only ones who could resist were the Adventurers Guilds scattered across the world!

Mammon’s strategy did not consider the neutrality of adventurers. As long as they were human, the demons would swing their slaughtering blades without hesitation.

This clearly threatened the survival of the adventurers. Regardless of their stance, when faced with the demonic threat, they would rise up in resistance!

This was not an internal power struggle among humans. Even if adventurers wanted to preserve themselves, they had to see if Mammon would give them that chance.

When attacking Saly County, Mammon’s army encountered their first setback. The most fierce resistance did not come from the lord’s army but from these rough-and-tumble adventurers.

As soon as Mammon’s army set foot in Saly County, they were ambushed by adventurers. Under the leadership of the Saly Adventurers Guild’s president, Mammon lost twenty-four soldiers and two Saint-tier subordinates.

From the start of the war, the demon army had been smooth sailing, conquering cities without obstacle. But the closer they got to the royal capital, the stronger the resistance became, even threatening the safety of the demon executives.

Upon hearing the news of his subordinates’ deaths, Mammon flew into a rage.

All adventurers in Saly County, from the highest-ranked to the lowest black iron, were captured and forced to kneel in front of the lord’s mansion to accept the “just” trial.

The adventurers were all tied up, kneeling on the ground, with demon executioners behind them, their blades gleaming coldly, ready to pierce flesh!

On the city walls, the heads of Saly County’s lord and his entire family were hung high. Looking closely, among the bloodstained snow, there were even the heads of infants, their blood barely dried.

At the front was the president of the Saly Adventurers Guild, a revered Saint-tier powerhouse in the region. It was he who had led the adventurers in resistance, piercing the throat of a demon executive with his sword.

His head of white hair was disheveled, but his body was exceptionally sturdy, making even young men in their twenties feel inferior. His eyes burned with rage as he glared at Mammon, who sat on a chair, his teeth grinding audibly.

Mammon was always clad in that heavy demon armor. Under the thick helmet, no one could see his expression.

Even his wife, Belial, standing respectfully beside him, dared not guess what he was thinking. She didn’t know how her husband would deal with these lowly humans.

“You killed my subordinates,” Mammon said, facing the old man.

The president of the Saly Guild let out a cold laugh. “It was me. I personally pierced that bastard’s throat and slaughtered a few demon brats along the way!”

Mammon tapped his fingers on the armrest, slowly standing up and approaching the old man. He looked down at him and asked, “Why did you do this?”

“Hah!” The old president of Saly County laughed aloud. “Does the high and mighty Demon Lord not understand the ways of the world? You slaughter us without reason—do we need a reason to slaughter you in return?!”

“You misunderstand me,” Mammon said from behind his heavy armor. “My meaning is, you are all going to die anyway. Why bother with this meaningless resistance? Why won’t you just accept your fate of death? The lives of my subordinates are far more precious than the lives of you cattle. Do you really think that by resisting, you can escape becoming food?”

“Hmph, so the Demon Lord is such a foolish existence,” the old president said after a pause, coldly. “Even if we are cattle, we will peck out your eyes before we die! This is no ordinary war. We are well aware of your actions—plundering wealth is one thing, but you kill people on sight, even children! You intend to exterminate us. No human would survive your slaughter. Wouldn’t resisting be the only sane choice?!”

Hearing these words, the demons’ expressions turned extremely ugly, filled with great anger toward the old adventurer.

If a fish on the chopping block suddenly jumped up and said the same thing, even a chef would see it as a threat.

*Clap clap clap—*

Mammon didn’t seem angry. Instead, he applauded the man, his tone full of meaning. “Good, very good.”

“Resist? Resist what?”

“I can’t help but admire the integrity of the humans below. I even feel a hint of respect for you.”

“But you seem to misunderstand something.” Mammon’s voice turned cold. “We demons are not raised to be scared. An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth.”

“This is our eternal and unchanging tradition.”

title: Chapter 35 — The Old Knight Captain
content:
Chapter 35 — The Old Knight Captain

Volume 30 · Chapter 35

Mamen reached out and snatched the mithril Adventurer’s Proof from the neck of the old guildmaster of Saly County. He glanced at the name on it.

"Merlin Vinson. I’ll remember your name. Let everyone know what happens to those who defy me."

"Rest in peace. You won’t be the first to die by my hand. Next will be the adventurers here. You lot—you could have run, yet you chose to stay and resist. Do you not value your own lives? Or are you blaming me for being heartless and ruthless? There’s no way out for you."

Mamen tossed the heavy helmet aside, obscuring his expression. The old man before him, though filthy and disheveled, had a gaze as firm as the stars.

"Demon Lord, your greed and ambition will never succeed. Even if more of us die, the world will learn of your atrocities. The adventurers will resist you everywhere. I, Merlin Vinson, may be weak now, but..." His voice was hoarse yet unyielding. "A single spark can start a prairie fire."

Mamen swung his sword in a vicious arc, and the old guildmaster’s head flew off, blood spraying everywhere. The body collapsed, and the demon soldiers dragged it away, leaving a pool of blood in the sand.

"Even if you spark a fire, it’s nothing but a feeble flame before me. Pathetic, insignificant humans. The rest of you adventurers—" The remaining captives knelt on the ground, staring at the corpse in silent grief.

Mamen’s eyes burned with cold fury. "The lives of these adventurers mean nothing. If they resist even slightly, they’ll be put to death." He turned to his demon underlings. "If we let them go now, they’ll pick up their weapons and fight us to the death!"

He grabbed the old man’s head by the hair. "Hang this on the city gates alongside the lord’s. Let all humans who dare defy me see their fate!" His voice was thick with rage as he drove his sword into the ground before him. The demons around him bowed their heads.

"Your Majesty, what of the remaining adventurers?" one of them asked.

"Burn them alive," Mamen ordered calmly.

The demons obeyed, dousing the adventurers in oil and setting them ablaze. Screams erupted as the flames roared, illuminating the demon lord’s palace. Even from a distance, one could see the writhing, burning figures and hear their agonized cries.

There were too many adventurers. If humans had witnessed this earlier, their souls would have fled in terror.

Belial, Mamen’s wife, stepped forward, her voice low. "Your Majesty, is this... wise?"

Mamen turned to her. "What’s unwise about it?"

"Adventurers are a neutral force in the world. They value their independence. If you slaughter them everywhere, it may provoke the other guilds. If they unite in retaliation, it could become a headache for us."

Belial voiced her concerns. "Without defenses, if we can’t control this land, won’t it be even worse? If we bypass the adventurers and focus on the kingdom, won’t they just stir up trouble in our rear? This is the second war we’ve fought. We must prioritize the extermination of humanity. Any human is a potential threat and must be eliminated."

Mamen paused, then said, "Occupying territory is secondary. The true way to rule is to crush all hidden threats. That’s what we must do."

Belial hesitated but didn’t dare to argue further in front of Mamen. She simply bowed her head. "The situation is indeed delicate. We’ve advanced from the Stritri Coast in just ten days, capturing Saly County with minimal losses. But today, we’ve suffered casualties among our soldiers. If the next battle is this difficult..."

Mamen gazed into the distance, pondering. "It will only get harder. More and more humans will resist. Next time, we might face even stronger foes like this old man."

Belial probed carefully. "He was strong, yes, but in the eyes of a true powerhouse like you, he’s nothing more than an ant."

Mamen’s expression darkened. "True. But even ants can be troublesome in large numbers. Have you noticed something odd?"

Belial frowned. "Since the war began, the humans should have sent reinforcements, but they haven’t. The only explanation is that our sudden advance caught them off guard. That human queen must have abandoned the outlying regions to focus on defending the capital."

Mamen nodded. "Exactly. She’s gathered all her forces in the royal capital. So the real battle... will be at the capital."

Belial knitted her brows. "Then can we truly succeed? If we can’t take the capital, the entire kingdom will remain a thorn in our side."

Mamen’s gaze hardened. "The current situation doesn’t allow for failure. In just a few days, that queen has prepared something. I want to see what it is."

---

In a secluded mansion on the outskirts of the capital, the Mesfield estate, two figures sat quietly by the fireplace late at night, sipping tea and discussing recent events.

"Your Majesty," the old man in the wheelchair said, "the situation in Saly County is dire. It’s already fallen to the demons. The forces surrounding us must be preparing for something. We need to act quickly."

Mesfield’s face was etched with worry. "The demons’ advance is far more aggressive than the kingdom anticipated. At a time like this, with internal strife, the only path is to resist the demons with all our strength. There’s no other way."

The old man in the wheelchair sighed. "The king’s orders came swiftly and in secret. I still don’t know what’s happening."

He glanced at the time. "It’s getting late. I should return to the palace."

"Take care on your way," Mesfield said. "Your leg is still injured. Let the servants help you. If you’re hungry, have them prepare something."

The old man chuckled. "Still worrying about me, Mesfield? I may be old, but my child—" His voice grew solemn. "The Mesfield family has served the royal line for generations. Loyalty to the king is more important than our own lives. Remember that, no matter the circumstances, protecting Her Majesty’s safety comes first."

"I understand," Mesfield replied.

After the old man left, Mesfield turned his wheelchair and made his way to a hidden compartment in the study. Inside, he carefully retrieved an ancient, dust-covered longsword. As he drew it from its sheath, the blade gleamed in the firelight, revealing intricate engravings of thunder and roses—the mark of the most mysterious order, the Thorned Knights.

The old knight commander stared at the sword, his expression grave. "The kingdom is in crisis... Where is Leon now?"

A faint, bitter smile crossed his face. "I suppose he’s still training that disciple of his, Michael."

title: Chapter 36 — The Knights' Stain
content:
Chapter 36 — The Knights' Stain

Volume 30 · Chapter 36

Royal Capital, Violet Thorn Knights

In the knights' cemetery, two new graves had appeared—belonging to Crade and Morrison.

All fallen knights were buried here, a sacred site where the order held annual memorials.

An old man in tattered clothes was sweeping dust from the tombstones. When he lifted his head and saw Crade and Morrison’s markers, he couldn’t help but let out a heavy sigh.

“Never thought… you two would end up here. How many Thorn Knights are left?”

This old man was Leonhard, the former First Knight. Severe injuries had forced him to retire from the Violet Thorn Knights, and he had since become the cemetery’s caretaker.

Ever since his only disciple, Millet, had died, Leonhard had never left the graveyard. Day after day, he swept the tombs tirelessly, as if in remembrance of something.

Leonhard stared at the tombstones, recalling memories of Morrison and Crade.

Morrison and his disciple Millet had a terrible relationship. Though they bickered constantly, Millet privately admired Morrison, believing him to be an outstanding knight. If only Morrison had shown more interest in swordsmanship, Leonhard might have taken him as a second disciple and passed down his techniques.

As for Crade—he was undeniably the kindest in the order. The oldest among them, with the longest service as a Thorn Knight, his knowledge was vast, and he was the most dependable in the hearts of all knights.

Rumor had it Crade wanted to compile his research on ancient magic into a book, a tome on magic across the ages. But he never finished. That dream was buried with him.

Leonhard withdrew his gaze, mourning the two young knights in his heart. He couldn’t help but worry about the kingdom’s safety. With so few knights left, could they really stop the demons’ advance?

“Old man, what’s the point of you staying here? They’re already dead.”
From the shadows, Meifield’s father pushed his wheelchair forward, his lap holding his beloved sword.

“Rebakov, you sneaky bastard. Why have you suddenly come here? Young knights keep dying, yet you don’t even show up to pay your respects. At this rate, the Thorn Knights will be wiped out!”

Leonhard’s face darkened with anger. Meeting an old friend brought no joy—only bitterness.

“As knights, we must be prepared to lay down our lives. Dying in battle is their honor, their very purpose. To rest in this land is proof they were true knights. I admire these young men from the bottom of my heart.”

“If your daughter dies, I hope you still have the heart to say that!” Leonhard clenched the broom in his hand, fury burning in his voice.

“If my daughter dies protecting the royal family, I will shed tears of pride. She will have fulfilled her duty as a knight, living up to the Meifield name.” Rebakov’s gaze was firm. This was no joke—it was the creed passed down through generations of his family, who had always served the royals.

“You’re still the same—heartless, incapable of empathy. Don’t you ever think of finding a solution? Do you *want* to see young knights keep dying?”

“Hmph. I was once a Thorn Knight, just like you. Now we’re both retired, powerless. If there were a way to save those young lives, do you think I’d just stand by?” Rebakov paused, helpless. “The moment they became Thorn Knights, they accepted that death might come at any time. You know this as well as I do.”

“I *do* know. But I pray that day never comes.” Leonhard pointed at Millet’s tombstone, grief in his voice. “Millet… I raised that boy with my own hands. He sacrificed himself to protect the queen. I can’t accept it. He had such a bright future ahead of him.”

“Leonhard, shut up. You’re too easily swayed by emotion. That wasn’t stupidity—it was great wisdom! I’ve heard about Millet. He lived up to the name of Thorn Knight. Your disciple was *better* than you!” Rebakov’s face, weathered by years of wind and rain, remained cold.

“Your callousness now is no different from when you personally slaughtered the six senior Thorn Knights. Those knights—just like me—were heroes who helped the late king found this kingdom. Yet you, who fought beside them, raised your blade against them. You’re a traitor. The royal family refuses to even speak your name. The only reason they haven’t exiled you is because you’re old, no longer a threat. They probably hope you’ll just disappear. You are the greatest stain on the Violet Thorn Knights!”

Leonhard’s eyes twitched with rage as he recalled Rebakov’s unforgivable crime.

Among the three Knight Captains of the Violet Thorn Knights, Rebakov was the most mysterious. He never appeared in the order, and the queen refused to utter his name. It was as if he were a ghost, a title held by a man who no longer existed.

And that man was Meifield’s father—the very same Rebakov who had once killed six Thorn Knights in a single night. Those knights had been founding heroes, veterans who had followed the late king into battle. Their deaths had once shaken the entire kingdom.

No one had expected Rebakov, the most loyal of them all, to turn on his comrades in one night. Many of them had been his closest friends, the kind who would trust each other with their backs in battle.

Because of this atrocious scandal, Rebakov was abandoned by all. The royal family never trusted him again. Even Meifield herself didn’t know her own father was that disgraced Knight Captain.

“Bullshit! Not a single one of those senior Thorn Knights was innocent! They flaunted their status as founding heroes, doing whatever they pleased, throwing the entire kingdom into chaos. In some ways, their power even surpassed the late king’s. It was only a matter of time before their ambition grew. They were a ticking time bomb for this nation. I merely did what the late king *wanted* to do but didn’t dare. Gregor can vouch for me—he was the late king’s court mage at the time!”

Rebakov defended himself furiously, convinced everyone misunderstood him.

“And yet, how many years has it been since the royal family last summoned you? You live in the capital, yet you haven’t even been granted an audience with the queen in all this time. Do you still not see the truth? Your so-called ‘loyalty’ has brought nothing but disaster to this kingdom!” Leonhard roared.

“My loyalty has withstood every trial. That is undeniable. You have no right to question my decisions.”

Rebakov suppressed his anger, speaking patiently. “I didn’t come here to argue with you.”

“Right now, our kingdom’s land is being trampled by the demon race. Though we’re old, we still have value.”

“I ask you now, Leonhard—as a knight, do you want to spend your remaining years tending graves… or come with me to challenge the Demon Lord? Even if it means dying on the battlefield.”

title: Chapter 37 — Impossible
content:
Chapter 37 — Impossible

Volume 30 · Chapter 37

In the cemetery, cold winds howled,

Two old comrades gazed at each other.

Though Raybakov had never been favored by the royal family,
his passion had never cooled. He hoped that in his twilight years,
he could still contribute to the kingdom.

Now was the time when the kingdom needed men like him.
Raybakov believed the kingdom required his service.
He wanted to end his life of being cold-shouldered by the royals,
and this was the perfect opportunity.

Leonard remained silent for a long time,
hesitant to give Raybakov an answer.
At the root of it all, he simply didn’t trust this leader of the Thorn Knights,
who was also a high-ranking noble.
He cared deeply for every knight under his command,
treating all of them like family.

But Raybakov had, without the late king’s permission,
personally executed a fellow knight.
This had undeniably crossed Leonard’s line.

In Leonard’s eyes,
Raybakov was now a marginalized figure, discarded by the kingdom.
Who knew if he was still hiding things from the queen,
making reckless decisions behind her back.

"You’ve already been sidelined, Raybakov.
No one needs a cripple like you.
Right now, you should be sitting by the fireplace, warming yourself,
wishing for your daughter’s happiness—
not dying on the battlefield."

"Your situation isn’t any different from mine.
Decades ago, you were gravely wounded by the enemy,
and you’ve never fully recovered.
Even raising a sword must be a struggle for you, right?
In others’ eyes, we’re both cripples."

Leonard looked gaunt, his clothes clinging to his frame in the wind,
so much so that his ribs were visible.
It was clear how frail the old man’s body had become.
"I’m nothing like you, a cold-hearted bastard.
At least the queen visits me every year.
She’d never bother with you."

"Elizabeth has been close to you since she was little.
That doesn’t prove anything.
My daughter is highly valued by the queen.
That’s more than enough for me."
Raybakov’s expression remained cold.
He turned his wheelchair around.
"Think carefully, Leonard.
Don’t you want to join me?"

"Are you just trying to drag me into the mud?
Forget it.
I will *never* work with you."
Leonard’s tone was firm and decisive.

"Then rot here with these corpses.
You used to be the kingdom’s greatest knight,
but now you’re nothing but a cowardly rat.
I misjudged you.
Turns out you’re just a spineless wretch."
Raybakov spun his wheelchair around and left,
still muttering curses as he went.
"Demons are about to surround the capital.
The Thorn Knights are nearly wiped out.
This is the time for old men like us to step up.
But your own injuries have you retreating,
trembling in fear, not even daring to face the demons.
Who was it that said, *‘As long as I draw breath, I will defend this kingdom from invasion’*?
You don’t deserve to guard this tomb."

"Wait.
Just because I won’t cooperate with *you*
doesn’t mean I won’t take action."

"Hm?"
Raybakov stopped and turned back to look at the ragged old man.

"Let’s test it, then.
Can you still wield a sword?"

"Of course.
My hands aren’t broken.
What about you?"

"I’ve always been stronger than you.
Even now, in my old age."

---

Meanwhile, in the underground tunnels beneath the royal palace.

The spiral staircase seemed endless,
stretching straight down into the pitch-black abyss.

The steps were damp, slick with moss,
and cracked from years of neglect,
making them look treacherous.

In the darkness of the underground,
the sound of the subterranean river echoed,
reverberating through the vast, empty space.

Mestfield and Elizabeth walked one in front of the other,
carefully holding up a torch as they descended.

Returning here filled Elizabeth with complicated emotions.
She had once been imprisoned in this very place for many years,
until Merlin had stumbled upon her by chance and rescued her.
If not for that, she might have spent the rest of her life here.

Elizabeth instinctively felt a pang of disgust.
Recalling her time here—
days spent in endless darkness, never even seeing the sun—
she couldn’t help but shiver.
Her foot suddenly slipped, and she let out a startled cry!

Mestfield reacted swiftly, steadying her.
"Your Majesty, be careful.
The stairs here are slippery."

Elizabeth gave an apologetic smile,
then simply took Mestfield’s hand and continued walking.
"By the way, how many times have you been here?"

"Once.
To be honest, I was shocked to learn
that such a massive space existed beneath the palace.
I never would’ve imagined it."
Mestfield held the torch high, his voice uncertain.

"This is a royal secret.
Only the royal family would know about it.
I was once imprisoned here myself.
If I had a choice, I wouldn’t want to come back."
Elizabeth looked around.

"Wait—you were *imprisoned* here during those missing years?"
Mestfield furrowed his brow, displeased.
"Her Majesty should’ve punished Isabella properly.
What she did was unforgivable."

"There was no need for that.
It was partly my own fault.
I only asked that she mind her own business and live quietly.
That was enough."
Elizabeth thought of Isabella, still under house arrest.
Stripped of power, she posed no threat.

"Your Majesty is too kind.
Sometimes, I wish you’d be stricter."
Mestfield emphasized.

"I *can* be strict.
For example, if Miguel doesn’t finish his lessons,
I *do* get angry."
Elizabeth puffed out her cheeks in an exaggerated display of anger.

Mestfield looked at Elizabeth, who had zero intimidation factor,
and awkwardly commented,
"I don’t think Princess Miguel fears you at all.
If anything, she’ll just keep slacking off."

"Ahhh, you have to hit me *this* hard? That’s too cruel!"
Elizabeth laughed bitterly, looking at Mestfield.
Since they were alone, she couldn’t resist her curiosity.
"Mesa, how long have you been a knight?"

"Hmm… it’s been over a decade.
I earned my squire’s qualifications when I was very young."

"Have you ever regretted becoming *my* knight?"
Elizabeth was genuinely curious.
She didn’t know what Mestfield truly thought.

"How could I regret it?
Loyalty is the most essential quality of a knight.
Besides, I’m a Mestfield.
My family has always pledged itself to the royal family.
Being able to protect you is the very meaning of my knighthood."
Mestfield spoke with solemn conviction.

Elizabeth felt Mestfield’s answer was too formal, too by-the-book.
"Mesa, it’s just the two of us here.
You don’t have to be so serious.
Sometimes I think knights give their lives to their masters too completely.
If one day you wanted to leave, I’d definitely allow it."

"Please, don’t say things like that.
I would never leave you.
Have I done something wrong?"
Mestfield stopped walking and turned back to face her.

"No, it’s not that.
I’ve just… thought a lot about the life of a knight.
It’s not as glamorous as it seems.
Many stories end in tragedy.
I remember when you were assigned to me, you were still so small.
You were shy, and when you saw me, you’d blush.
I treated you like a little pearl.
Becoming my knight… has it been a heavy burden for you?
Have you lost a lot of the happiness an ordinary person should have?"

"An ordinary person’s happiness… like what?"

"Like…"
Elizabeth pondered for a moment, then suddenly had an idea.
"Romance!
Knights aren’t supposed to fall in love willy-nilly, right?
That’d be troublesome."

"R-Romance…?"
Mestfield’s expression turned bewildered.

"Really?
Mesa, have you *never* met someone you liked?
You know, the kind of person who makes your heart race when you see them,
leaves you tongue-tied, sends your blood boiling,
the kind you can’t stop thinking about?"
Elizabeth gave an example, trying to help Mestfield understand.

"Heart racing… tongue-tied… blood boiling… constantly thinking about them…"
Mestfield froze, recalling something.
His face unconsciously flushed red—

*This… this sounds exactly like…*
*That damn swordmaster, Aurelian!*
*So… I actually like that guy?*

*Impossible… impossible…*
*No way…*
