title: Chapter 38 — Royal Guardian
content:
Chapter 38 — Royal Guardian

Volume 30 · Chapter 38

By the faint light of the torch, Elizabeth still managed to get a clear look at Mesphield's expression. She was surprised and asked, "What is this?"

"Is that possible?" Elizabeth asked, her eyes wide. "Have you found someone you like? Who is it? Have I met him before?"

"What does he look like? What's his personality like? What's his family background? The kind of man who can attract you definitely isn't some random guy, right?"

Mesphield was overwhelmed by the string of questions, shaking his head like a dog shaking off water. "No, no, it's impossible. I'm the King's knight. How could I be entangled in emotional issues? I don't even like any man."

Elizabeth looked at Mesphield with a strange expression, her eyes filled with suspicion. "Really? Well, Windsor, even if you have someone you like, you can tell me. I'll support you. You don't have to be so tense. After all, I'm pretty close to you. I can help you give some advice and give you a hand. I don't want my knight to be taken away by some random guy."

"Please believe me, such a thing is impossible. My wish is to always be by your side," Mesphield said, his face earnest as he explained with emotion.

"Is that so?" Elizabeth pursed her lips and stopped pressing further. Her mind was racing. It was strange. Even Elizabeth showed a sign of being at a loss. Looking at her reaction, it was like a girl in her adolescence. Was it just my imagination?

Mesphield lowered his head, feeling guilty. How could he like that damn bastard who kept cursing him? It must be a hallucination. After all, there was only one man left in the world, Earl Eldrin. They were also sworn enemies. If he were to be taken away by such a despicable man, it would be a great disgrace to my knightly career.

The two continued down the steps. The closer they got to the underground, the louder the sound of the underground river became, and the temperature also became abnormally cold.

Mesphield was confused. Because he didn't trust Elizabeth's reason, he hadn't yet carefully considered why he had come here. However, Mesphield had already sensed the abundance of water elements in the air, as if there was an extremely powerful creature existing in the distance.

"Then, what am I doing here, and what are you doing here?" Elizabeth hesitated for a moment, then thought it was safe to say. "I want to entrust you with the kingdom's secret treasure."

"The kingdom's secret treasure?" Mesphield's eyes widened in surprise.

"You know about the water nymphs in the lake, right? They were the guardian spirits of the founding emperor of Britain, possessing considerable divinity and wisdom. They have always played a role similar to our royal family's guardian deity," Elizabeth said softly.

"I know. Isabella once used the water nymphs in the lake to deal with Earl Eldrin. But that was just a clone," Mesphield recalled the incident. Although it was just a clone, its power was still formidable. It had almost wiped out the private army of the Duke.

"Indeed, don't擅自 request it. Because according to the covenant between the founding emperor and it, for many years, it has been forbidden to disturb it again," Elizabeth showed a hint of regret.

The water nymphs are essentially magical beings. We still have to beg them, Mesphield frowned, thinking it would be too much for the queen to frown at them, which would be a great loss of face.

Water nymphs are extremely rare magical beings. They have evolved through elements into a wise entity that has existed for countless ages. They are incomparable to ordinary magical creatures that only know how to kill. Moreover, among magical creatures, the water nymphs in the lake are the most温和 in nature. They have never attacked anyone without reason. The founding emperor and they became friends," Elizabeth revealed the secret.

"What about this water nymph's power? Has it already been used against the demon race's attack? Maybe Mesphield can still help," Mesphield asked.

"Of course, according to the covenant, the nymphs can help us. But there's another way. That is to take the treasure from the lake and subdue the water nymphs," Elizabeth's expression became serious.

Mesphield was confused. He had accompanied Elizabeth for so many years and had never heard of a mysterious treasure in the underground lake.

"It is a divine weapon held by the founding emperor. Because of this treasure, the kingdom was able to overthrow the previous Britannia Kingdom," Elizabeth paused.

"Windsor, how much do you know about divine weapons?" Mesphield frowned, thinking carefully before answering. "I know a little. I've occasionally heard of so-called divine weapons or treasures, but most of them are fake. The real divine weapons are said to exist, but they are mostly in stories. Some are made by divine beings themselves, some are crafted by master artisans, and some are naturally formed. But they all have one thing in common: they possess power akin to that of a god. Even if a common person obtained such power, it would be terrifying."

"You're being too modest. In fact, you already understand a lot. The treasure in the lake is a genuine divine weapon. It is the true source of our kingdom's power in the world," Elizabeth looked at Mesphield's eyes.

Mesphield was suddenly stunned. He had never imagined that Britannia possessed such a divine weapon. If it was real, then what was there to fear from the greedy Demon Lord?

"I've made the decision to bring you here. This is a major matter. I'm entrusting this important treasure to you. You are my most loyal knight. Only you can carry it. I'll feel at ease," Elizabeth looked directly at Mesphield and said with great seriousness.

The divine weapon was a king's sword. Initially, there was a stone that was naturally formed. After years of being polished by the sun and moon, it became a great treasure. After the water nymphs discovered it, they used their own life and divinity to establish a connection with it. After a long time of refinement, the king's sword had become increasingly sharp. In the dark, it emitted a cold, icy glow.

Mesphield felt a bit tense, sensing the danger around him. The queen was going to entrust the kingdom's most precious treasure to him. Although he appeared calm on the surface, he felt an unexpected pressure. He was afraid he would disappoint the queen's trust.

Under Elizabeth's call, the lake's surface began to stir. A whirlpool appeared, and a giant figure emerged, its skin blue and shimmering. It was covered in magic, like a sealed monster. The water nymph reappeared.

It looked at Elizabeth calmly. "I am the legitimate heir of the Gerbert lineage. What business do you have coming here at night to disturb me?"

"If you want to use your own death to threaten me, it's useless," Elizabeth said.

title: Chapter 39 — Drowned in the Lake
content:
Chapter 39 — Drowned in the Lake

Volume 30 · Chapter 39

Lake water nymph's gaze was cold and unfeeling.

It seemed to contain only the fifth district of its own, and perhaps it considered the founding king Gilbert of the Bertram dynasty as a friend. ★First★Release★EZ See Book★Until His Submerged Fairies Were Very Plain, Moreover Because They Had Signed a Contract with a Stranger, It Needed to Follow the Stranger's Pact to Help the Royal Family Once in Times of Difficulty. Although the Lake Water Nymph Belonged to the Gentle Wood-Type Among Elemental Spirits in Elemental Magic, It Was Not Certain That It Had Any Good Feelings Toward Humans. Bertram Was Probably One of the Few Exceptions.

Because Isabella Had Once Threatened the Lake Water Nymph with Her Own Body, Making It More Resistant Toward the Royalty, Even Though the Person Standing Before It Right Now Was the Legitimate Heir.

"So late still coming to disturb you, I'm very sorry." Isabella lowered her posture and said softly, "Last time I used such a proactive method to make you assist us, she has certainly reflected well afterwards. I hope you won't hold it against her."

The Lake Water Nymph Stared at Isabella, Feeling That the Legitimate Heir Before Her Had a Gentler Personality Than the Ancestors of the Chosen One, "No fat, My First Connection With You Has a Predetermined Fate, We Must Step In When Our Lives Are Threatened, To Help the Next Generation, This Is Something I Must Fulfill, But If You Still Want to Bother Me Tonight, Even If You Die Before Me, I Will Also Absolutely Still Help You."

Melfiard's Face Slightly Changed and Looked Unpleasant. Thinking That Even Though the Lake Water Nymph Had Once Been a Partner of the Former King, And Was Also a Guardian of the Royalty, This Malicious Attitude Was Too Much. After All, It Was Only a Magical Beast, Even If Its Temperament Was Gentle, It Was Not Good in Any Way.

"So I Did Not Come to Bother You Beforehand, But There Is Something Else." Isabella Said Embarrassedly.

The Lake Water Nymph's Body, Composed of Inconsequential Matter, Became Ethereal, and Surprisedly Asked, "What Thing? If It's a Problem Caused by the Church, Then Forget It, I Have No Interest in Becoming a Teacher for Humans, Nor Am I Their Nanny."

"Actually I Want to Take Out the Treasure from the Lake." Isabella's Expression Was Serious.

The Lake Water Nymph Had Always Been in a State of Unmoved Waves, But Its Emotions Suddenly Fluctuated, Tone Astonished, "You Really Want to Take Out the Treasure Sitting There? Isabella Nodded Hardly, Managing to Reveal a Few Points of Royal Queenly Severity, "I Want the Name of the King of Britain, to Grant the King's Might to My Knight."

This Statement Was Like a Painting, The Air Became Condensed, Silent to the Point That the Loudly Flowing Underground Water Stopped. The威严 Emitted by the Lake Water Nymph Was Very Terrifying, Originally It Already Had an Extremely High Species, It Seemed to Have Somehow Mastered a Bit of Divine Power. Although It Seemed Easy for Isabella to Say Such a Thing, But the Lake Water Nymph and Bertram Were Very Clear, This Matter Was Weighty, Far More Important Than Entrusting the Kingdom's Fate to an Outsider.

The Lake Water Nymph Examined Isabella's Face, Questioning, "You Are the Direct Descendant of Bertram, and Also the Queen of Britain, This Kind of Situation Is Still a Joke, Are You Really Decided?"

"Right, The Kingdom Now Needs the Power of the Artifact, Giving It to My Loyal Knight, Is My After Careful Consideration, There Is No One More Suitable Than Bertram." Isabella Had Already Made Up Her Mind Early On, Wanting to Give the Kingdom's Strongest Weapon to the Directly Loyal Knight to Use.

"Although You Are the Current Britain's King, You Look Not Mature Enough, Liking Bertram's Calmness of Emotional Matters, You Haven't Learned Any of It at All." The Lake Water Nymph's Emotion Was Somewhat Unspoken, A Trace of Good Feelings Toward Isabella's Face Suddenly Vanished, "I Suggest You Not Give the Treasures from the Lake to the Knight, He Is an Outsider, and Still Bertram's Descendant, As Long as the Old Man Has a Bit of Aberrant Heart, Bertram's Two-Handedly Built Foundation Will Be Destroyed in an Instant."

"Although Windsor Is Not a Member of the Royalty, and She Is Absolutely Not an Outsider District, I Have Always Regarded Bertram as My Own, Without Any Difference From My Own Kin." Isabella's Tone and Color Were Firm, Seeming Not to Change the Decision She Made.

Deep in His Heart Moved, Bertram Could See What Pressure Isabella Was Shouldering, Only Then Making Such a Decision. If He Still Believed in Himself, How Could He Teach This Power to His Own Hands.

"Bertram Had Once Been So Talented and Beautiful, How Come Your Younger Generations Are So Incompetate, It Really Took a Lot of His Heart and Blood."

The Lake Water Nymph Became Somewhat Angry, Feeling That Isabella Was Too Foolish, Emotional Matters Would Destroy the Foundation of the Emperor, "The King's Might Should Not Be Given to an Outsider, You Can Consider Using It Yourself."

"If I Had the Talent to Become a King, I Would Definitely Try to Master This Treasure, Unfortunately I Don't Have This Ability, I Was Weak and Sickly Since Childhood, Only Able to Envy Others' Eyes, Watching Others Use Martial Arts or Magic." Isabella Expressed Regret.

"Do You Not Have Descendants? Or Also Have No Talent to Become Sword King?" The Lake Water Nymph Curiously Teased.

"Yes, Mi Ge Is That Kid Made of Clay Is Quite Good." Isabella's Expression Was Non-Face Embarrassing. Those Who Could Cultivate Magic Power Were Originally a Minority, Coincidentally, the Entire Britain's Royal Family, Did Not Have This Talent, Perhaps It Was Suitable Emperor Bertram Did Something, Encountered Retribution.

"Hardly Believable, Bertram Was Once Known Far and Near as an Unparalleled Strong One, His Sorcery Was Unreachable by Anyone, How Come It Came to Here, It Became So Incompetent, If He Knew You Guys Had Become Like This, I Swear That Guy Would Definitely Crawl Out of Hell, Scolding You Until Your Blood Flowed." The Lake Water Nymph's Expression on the Face Was Strange, Not Expecting That Its Own Partner's Descendants, Each One Had Become So Useless Looking at a Stronger's Descendants, Who Would Still Be Strong.

"For This I Am Also Very Sorry, So I Hope to Give the Treasure to My Knight Isabella Paused, Then Slowly Said, "Now the Demon Army Is Besieging the Capital, the Situation Is Becoming More and More Dangerous, At This Time Only Obtaining the Artifact's Power, Might Have a Chance to Fight the Demon Lord's Monarch, As the Still Britain's King, I Have the Right to Decide the Belonging of That Which Is Taken."

"You Have the Right to Decide What Use, But Can You Get the Artifact's Recognition, It Completely Depends on Bertram Himself." The Lake Water Nymph Looked Toward Melfiard, Inner Heart Did Not Look Forward to This Female Knight, Unless He and the King's Might Owner Bertram Had Some Similarities.

"So Heavy to the Artifact's Manifestation, What Intention" Melfiard Surprisedly Asked, Still Thinking It Was Just Bringing Over a Divine Weapon to Use, Not Expecting It to Be So Troublesome.

"You Will Know Soon. The Lake Water Nymph's Voice Had Just Fallen, Waving His Hand and Lifting Up a Giant Wave, Directly Wrapping Melfiard.

Melfiard Let Out a Voice of Surprise, Clearly Knowing This Magical Beast Wanted to Do Something, But Before It Could React, It Was Dragged Into the Cold Lake Water.

Isabella's Face Was Worried, And Unlike the Calm Lake Surface, The Interior of the Pool Was Slightly Unpleasantly Unstable One One.

"Definitely Succeed, Area Isabella."

In the Late Night London Adventurers Guild, Everyone Had Not Slept, But Gathered in the Large Hall. Adventurers Gathered Below, Various Discussions, Some Feelings of Fear, Some Solemn, Some Worried. Everyone Was Waiting for the Guild Master Gregory, He Was Going to Announce Something.

title: Chapter 40 — Adventurers Join the Battle!
content:
Chapter 40 — Adventurers Join the Battle!

Volume 30 · Chapter 40

If Kuo Xi's information is accurate, the entire Surrey County has already fallen.

"Then this is even worse than I thought. If the whole county is lost, there's no way we can survive this."

"The demon race must know that although adventurers are divided, we are a massive neutral force."

"How could you possibly think those demons would consider such things? They're not capable of it. They wouldn't even spare children."

The adventurers below were discussing nonstop, all feeling extremely panicked because the demon army was about to attack the capital city.

Since the demons began their invasion, they had been unstoppable, advancing without resistance. It seemed the demon army was invincible.

In addition, the clergy of the Holy Church, in an effort to expand their influence, had deliberately portrayed the demon race as overwhelmingly powerful.

This led to many people being terrified even before the battle began, believing the demon army was invincible and no one could stop them.

Alice, who had small dragon horns on her head, opened her large mouth, which was completely disproportionate to her small body, and swallowed an entire turkey whole.

Then, her small mouth clicked like a machine gun, spitting out the chicken bones.

The entire guild's adventurers were very anxious, but Alice seemed completely relaxed, as if she didn't care about the fate of the Kingdom of Britain at all. Her mind was only on whether the food in the warehouse was still enough during the war.

The vice president, Shulan, had been frowning for days, very worried that the war would affect the guild and threaten the safety of the London adventurers. He glanced at Alice and immediately turned red with anger.

"Eat, eat, eat! All you know is to eat! You should at least show a little tension! The demons are about to attack, and then there won't even be chicken for you to eat!"

"Ah," Alice, who had been eating, suddenly stopped, "Is that really true?"

"Are you still making excuses? Surrey County has already fallen. We don't even know what happened to the adventurers' guild there. If the demons are targeting not just the kingdom but all of humanity, then we are also in great danger. The demons will not only attack us but also plunder our supplies. Do you still want to eat turkey? You're dreaming!" Shulan said seriously, thinking Alice was still a good guild member, but she valued food too much. The cost of feeding her was too expensive, and she was always indifferent to matters other than food.

"If the demons want to fight me for food, I'll bite them to death," Alice said, opening her mouth and showing her sharp canines in a display of bravado.

"Ugh," Shulan felt a headache coming on, thinking that this idiot would only take things seriously when her food was threatened.

He had thought that after Alice lost to Alice of Leicester in the competition, she would收敛 her lazy attitude and become more diligent and serious, but there was no change at all.

Looking at Alice, he spoke in a senior's tone, "You're both human-dragons. You lost to the demon sword user from Leicester in the competition. Shouldn't you reflect on that? You still think about eating all day. You should train harder."

"Vice President, you nag me every day. It's annoying. I'm tired of you. I don't want to talk to you," Alice said expressionlessly, turning her head away coldly.

"Moreover, Alice of Leicester is just good at swordsmanship. When it comes to using dragon power, she can't compare to me."

"Because of your attitude, you were defeated by adventurers from a small place like Leicester. You really should have some self-awareness," Shulan thought, seeing that Alice showed no sign of reforming. He sighed heavily, becoming even more worried about the guild's current situation.

Now that the demons had already approached the capital, if they couldn't avoid this war, Alice seemed to be of little use.

Just as Shulan was thinking about how to help the guild through this crisis, the old guild master, Gregory, who had been away, slowly walked onto the stage.

Seeing the master return, the adventurers below immediately quieted down, as if they had found their mainstay. No one was more trustworthy than Gregory.

Gregory cleared his throat and looked around at everyone, announcing in a calm tone, "Surrey County has been completely fallen. The demons didn't consider the adventurers' position at all. They burned all the adventurers in Surrey County alive. My old friend Vincent from the guild also died in the turmoil. The demons cut off his head and hung it on the city gate along with the head of the lord of Surrey County."

At the news, the adventurers immediately erupted in chaos. Those who had been clinging to hope were now completely desperate. They had hoped the demons would still target the adventurers, but now it seemed like a naive thought.

"I told you what would happen. The demons want to wipe out our race and restore their demonic era. What the priests in the church said was right."

"All the adventurers in Surrey County are dead. Those cruel demons want to fight us to the death!"

"The demons are so rampant. Don't they fear that the entire world's adventurers will unite and retaliate?"

Gregory looked at the chaotic guild members below. This reaction was exactly what he had expected.

Because of the many wars, adventurers had always maintained a neutral stance and had survived many times. Everyone had gotten used to it.

But this time was different. It was no longer a conflict between humans, but a struggle between races.

In such a situation, being prudent was useless.

"Everyone, please calm down. This matter, we cannot remain indifferent."

"We must take the fate of our Surrey County comrades as a warning and abandon any侥幸 psychology."

"This is not a conflict between humans, but a survival battle between humans and the demon race."

"No matter where you run, it will be useless. Only resistance is the final way out."

"Therefore, I declare that the London Adventurers' Guild will unite with the kingdom and fully support this defense war."

"If you don't want to participate, you are not forced. Those who don't want to fight can leave the capital city tonight. It's entirely up to you."

The London Guild had a very strong overall strength and also considered the existence of individual powerful adventurers. They were much stronger than the guild in Leicester.

If most of the adventurers responded to Gregory's call, it would undoubtedly inject a strong heart into the defense of Britain.

The adventurers below were whispering. At such a time, being cowardly and avoiding battle was shameful. Who would risk their lives to fight demons? But there were certainly people who thought about the long term.

"Running away now is useless. Isn't this a war between humans and demons? If Britain falls, the demons will come again. It won't benefit anyone. We will all be slaves to the demon race. Is it better to live a humble life as a demon's slave?"

Adam spoke up in the crowd, thinking that if Britain lost, fleeing to anywhere would be the same.

"Yes, fleeing now can ensure safety, but if we are later caught by the demons, we will still die. Why not fight together with the kingdom? We still have a chance to win. Why not fight?"

Leila very much agreed with Adam's words.

"Ugh," Alice sighed, chewing on a large chicken leg, "No one knows what to do at a time like this."

The guild became even more heated. The willingness to fight was high, and many responded.

Shulan saw this and silently exhaled, his earlier worries dissipating.

The guild master was willing to lead the entire guild into battle, and with the kingdom's strength, the oncoming demons didn't seem so terrifying.

Early in the morning, a carriage stopped in front of the palace.

Alice got off the carriage and looked at the majestic palace, feeling that she hadn't been here for a long time.

"Have we arrived at the palace?"

title: Chapter 41 — Three Cuts First (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 41 — Three Cuts First (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 30 · Chapter 41

After Mesphield was dragged into the lake by the lake spirits, Elizabeth did not stay in the underground lake but chose to return to the palace to deal with a mountain of troubles. Elizabeth believed the lake spirits would not harm Mesphield, and whether or not he could retrieve the treasure hidden in the lake depended on his own abilities; she couldn't help him at all.

In the morning, Elizabeth received news that a foreign thorn knight had arrived in the capital. She didn't bother to dress up and hurried to the grand hall to welcome them.

Since Alice was a foreign thorn knight and had no obligation to fight for the kingdom, Elizabeth had always hesitated whether to write to Alice. But this morning, good news arrived—Alice had come here herself, probably to support the front lines.

Elizabeth was overjoyed. After the fall of Surrey, the capital had already been under the iron hooves of demons. Any additional forces would naturally increase their chances of victory.

Catherine led Alice and the others into the grand hall. "Your Majesty, they've arrived."

Alice, Cecilia, and the others bowed respectfully. Seeing this, Elizabeth quickly said, "This is an emergency. We don't need to go through all these formalities. The fact that you've all come here at such a time proves you are all loyal warriors of Britain."

"Your Majesty, my father has been unwell recently and couldn't come in person, but he sent me with the most elite forces from the Rose family to provide support." After arriving in the capital, Cecilia had already counted the troops. Each was an outstanding elite from her family, and they were no less formidable than the Thorn Blossom Knight团's knights.

"Having a daughter as excellent as you, your family is bound to flourish. Entrusting you with such an important mission means you'll likely become the future leader of the Rose family," Elizabeth said with a honeyed compliment.

Cecilia felt her status was being acknowledged as the future matriarch of her family, which made her feel like she was being officially designated for the role. Katherine was delighted, knowing Cecilia's dream was to become the matriarch of the Rose family. If they won the war, it would be a done deal.

Elizabeth turned to Alice, suddenly showing some emotion. "Miss Alice, I'm glad you've come. I had considered writing to you but was worried it might be a bother."

Alice, seeing the queen so high above, felt it was too much. "It's not a bother at all."

"Foreign knights are just a title, Your Majesty can't command you," Catherine suddenly spoke up. "I've always thought foreign knights had no standing, but in times of national crisis, you're willing to come and help. I must admit, I have a new respect for foreign knights. You are truly a just person."

Alice felt a bit guilty being praised and quickly clenched her fists, her righteous spirit burning fiercely. "That's right! The demons are rampant. How could I sit idly by? Any decent person would stop them from acting recklessly."

Catherine was slightly surprised, looking at Alice's sincere eyes and feeling an unexpected fondness. This hatred for evil was hard to fake.

In truth, Alice was like this—kind-hearted, genuine, and fond of fighting for justice, which had earned her the nickname "The Little Guardian of Justice" from Merlin.

"According to our scouts, the demon race has already advanced again and is heading toward the capital. They're expected to arrive here in about three days. Miss Alice, do you have the confidence to fight the demons?" Elizabeth asked tentatively. It wasn't that she doubted Alice's strength, but Merlin was too耀眼. How could even the brightest star compare to the sun?

"Your Majesty, please rest assured. I have the confidence to face the demons directly and have extensive experience," Alice said seriously. She thought, as long as I can repel Mammon's army, that should be enough. If I really had to face Mammon himself, I wouldn't have that confidence. If Merlin were here, he might understand what's happening inside the demon race and why they suddenly started expanding outward.

"Your experience with demons is impressive. Demons aren't something you can just run into. Did you perhaps have another profession before becoming an adventurer that involved dealing with demons?" Catherine asked suspiciously.

"This..." Alice became nervous, a few drops of cold sweat sliding down her forehead. She realized she had said too much and was revealing her secrets.

She couldn't say she had once been a Hero who fought demons, that unfortunate 233rd generation who was "defeated" by the Demon Lord. She couldn't reveal that there was a Great Demon Lord in her family, who they argued every day, had fights, and bickered constantly.

Alice looked down, thinking for a moment, then said in a very serious tone, "I have a friend who was once a member of the Holy Church."

"Brave and unyielding in the face of the Demon Lord, fighting until the very end, one of the greatest Heroes of all time."

"Beautiful, her suitors had circled the world, even the brutal Demon Lord had fallen at her feet."

"Kind, no one could bear to harm her, even heaven silently protected her with luck. She was a lucky girl."

"Most importantly, she had a pair of large breasts, I bet they were at least E-cup. Very attractive."

"She's my friend, and we often talked about demons, so that's why my experience is so rich. I can consider myself an expert in dealing with demons."

Everyone was stunned, unable to tell if it was true or false.

After all, Alice had been mixing with Merlin every day and seemed to have learned the skill of talking nonsense.

No wonder Joan of Arc thought the pure-hearted Alice had been corrupted by Merlin, an heretic. It seemed there was some truth to that.

"May I ask, which generation was your friend?" Elizabeth was full of doubts. Such a perfect Hero shouldn't be an unknown.

"It was the 233rd generation," Alice replied confidently.

"Your Majesty, that was the unfortunate female Hero who was toyed with and killed by the brutal 13th monarch. A few years ago, she left from the Bristol port of our kingdom to lead a crusade against the Second Demon Lord Palace. I think everyone died in the Death Marsh. It was very tragic," Catherine reminded her from the side.

"Oh," Elizabeth feigned surprise, though she hadn't actually remembered. The Church considered Alice the most failed Hero in history and was ashamed to mention her, so the outside world knew about the event but had little information about that 233rd generation Hero. "What a pity, Alice, my condolences for your brave friend."

"No, no, Your Majesty, I don't think she was brave. I heard she chose to flee when facing the Demon Lord, but she didn't escape. That doesn't count as bravery, just a lack of courage," Catherine said from the side.

"Er," Alice felt like her heart had been stabbed. It was true.

Elizabeth: "Then your beautiful friend?"

Catherine: "No, that female Hero didn't seem beautiful either. The crusade team had ten thousand men and only one woman. No one pursued her."

"Ugh," Alice covered her chest, feeling like she'd been stabbed again. It seemed even the gender ratio couldn't save her, as there were no women to be attracted to her.

Elizabeth: "Then your kind friend?"

Catherine: "Kindness is even less likely. A few years ago, I represented you on a mission to the Holy Roman Empire and heard some rumors. That 233rd generation female Hero actually joined the Church to earn a living because she was broke. To put it bluntly, she wasn't particularly kind, just a opportunist."

"Phew," Alice spat out a mouthful of old blood. The third blow hit the mark, hurting her little heart. Was there more to say?

Why would they do this to her?

title: Chapter 42 — The Final Rest
content:
Chapter 42 — The Final Rest

Volume 30 · Chapter 42

Ali Xiao Cheng. What's wrong?

You look pale.

It's as if you've been hit hard, struggling to accept this fact. After so many years, it was finally possible to see each other's faces, but the situation had already become unmanageable. The wish couldn't be fulfilled.

Chang Yun felt that beneath the queen's calm exterior, the connection to the forest was more than just a simple need.

Was it really just because of the forest?

After that, the Kais and the Cecilia family's elite forces, temporarily allied with the Church, had already begun to sense the tension.

The Holy Church could feel the unease on the commercial front, where the two sides were evenly matched.

For Aitong, this royal court was a place of danger. He decided to leave warmheartedly.

Aitong clearly followed his own path.

A little bit of worry.

To hide the determination in his eyes,

Here, Barres was still thinking of me.

The rider on the side飘.

A capable, kind-hearted Aitong Xiao Cheng.

title: Chapter 43 — On the Verge of Explosion
content:
Chapter 43 — On the Verge of Explosion

Volume 30 · Chapter 43

Don't Block the Way!

As soon as Alice spotted Barese, she felt a wave of disgust. "What are you doing here?"

"Sorry, the demons are trampling this land, and I've been ordered by His Holiness the Pope to come reinforce the Kingdom of Britain. Looks like I don't have to return to the Holy Cavalry after all — I can keep enjoying myself out here."

A teasing smile crossed Barese's face. He was glad to have extra time outside. ★See★ the★ latest★ chapters★ on★ Baidu★ search★ EZ Reading★

He didn't care whether the Kingdom of Britain would win this defensive war. He just wanted to find excuses to get close to all sorts of women.

Barese was still thinking that if the defense war succeeded, wouldn't he and Her Majesty the Queen share a splendid night together?

"The Holy Church actually sent someone like you to provide support — what a misfortune for the kingdom," Alice said coldly.

"The elite ranks of the entire Templar Knight force are formidable. How can you call it a misfortune? Rather, with me here, our chances of defeating that greedy Demon Lord have increased considerably," Barrestad said with an arrogant tone.

"Hehe, I hope when you encounter the real Demon Lord on the battlefield, you won't cower and slink away with your tail between your legs. You represent the Holy Church — don't let the Pope lose face because of you," Alice said sarcastically, thinking that these Knights Commander of the Holy Church always act superior. Their first duty is to protect the Pope's safety. Though they've encountered demons before, they've probably never truly faced a Demon Lord.

"Pfft pfft pfft, Alice, I think you're delusional. Do you really think I'm as weak as you were back then? The ten-thousand-strong Templar Knight army was wiped out in the Dead Bog. Only you barely survived and ran away in disarray, isn't that right?" Barrestad raised an eyebrow.

"What did you say?" Alice frowned, anger flashing in her eyes.

"Oh dear, even if you didn't slink away in disgrace, you certainly must have knelt on the ground, crying and begging that young arrogant monarch for mercy, right?" Barrestad spread his arms, believing that the only reason Alice survived in that campaign was by crawling and showing pity. Otherwise, given the well-known ferocious nature of the Great Demon Lords, how could they have spared the Hero?

"Shut your filthy mouth!" Alice snarled, pointing at Barese's nose. "Someone like you who hides inside the temple — have you ever seen the real Demon Lords? They're beings beyond comprehension, you know?"

"Although I haven't seen the real Demon Lords, if it weren't for protecting His Holiness the Pope, I'd have the qualifications to become a Hero and forge my own legend," Barese said smugly.

"You think listening to some rumors about the Demon Lords makes you capable of defeating them? You're too naive. Living sheltered in the temple, you know nothing at all. You should join a raid party at least once and see for yourself what the Demon Lords are truly like," Alice looked away, too lazy to argue with a "greenhouse flower" like Barese.

"To be honest, I understand the Demon Lords' strength. After all, the Holy Church invested considerable effort but couldn't eradicate them. But I've never thought of defeating the Demon Lords — however, there's still a chance to drive them back." Barre said with confidence. With the combined strength of the entire Kingdom of Britain, driving the demons back to the Demon Lord Palace shouldn't be impossible.

"There won't be such an opportunity." Alice said coldly. "Get lost. I don't want to talk to someone like you. Don't block my way."

"Don't be so cold. It's rare we meet — want to grab a drink together?" Barre said enthusiastically.

Alice kicked the door open with her foot, pushed her luggage inside, and turned back to curse, "Stay away from me. Go drink yourself — have a few more to steel your courage. Just don't end up unable to even walk when you see the Demon Lord."

"Haha, you're still so funny, Alice." Barese took it all in stride and teased, "After the defense war ends, would you, former Hero, be interested in returning to the Holy Church with me?"

Alice angrily drew her sword and pressed it against Barese's neck. In a cold voice she said, "I have no interest in returning to the Holy Church, and don't bring up the fact that I was once the Hero, or I'll fight you to the death."

Barese looked at the bone-chilling sword edge at his neck and nodded nervously. "Alright, no problem."

"Hmph." Alice snorted sharply, slammed the door heavily behind her, and finally got rid of Barese's harassment.

"Sigh, bringing up that she was once the Hero didn't bother her before, why is she reacting so strongly today?" Barese was puzzled in his heart. He had no idea that something had just happened in the main hall. Alice was simply worried her dark past would be exposed.

Suddenly, Barese's gaze changed strangely as he recalled the sword blade in Alice's hand — the sacred wing-shaped hilt and the intricate mysterious runes etched along the blade.

Strange, that symbol on Alice's hand... why does it feel familiar? Where have I seen it before?

Pitch black — the pitch blackness from the bottom of the lake.

The icy coldness made Merlinfield shudder all over as he suddenly opened his eyes.

What came into view were strange-shaped stones everywhere, making anyone unable to help but marvel.

There, on top of the tallest bizarre stone, a stone sword was inserted, covered in moss and holes.

It looked utterly ordinary. If placed outside, anyone would find it hard to imagine that this stone sword, fused with the rock, was once the treasure of Britain's founding emperor.

Merlinfield茫然ly slowly stood up and surveyed his unfamiliar surroundings, as if an independent barrier at the bottom of the lake had isolated him from the outside world.

"This is the resting place of Egbert's soul, and also where the Sword of the King is hidden." The lake sprite floated in mid-air.

"That Sword of the King..." Merlinfield gazed at the stone sword, his heart stirring. To not disappoint the Queen's trust, he must retrieve this treasure.

"Correct, this is a naturally formed divine artifact. I discovered it at the bottom of a certain abyss. Initially it was just a prototype, but through my polishing it gradually became this sharp blade. Its first owner was Britain's founding emperor, Egbert." The lake sprite looked at the divine artifact connected to its spirit and replied, "A hundred years ago, the previous kingdom on this land was incredibly powerful — considered the most prominent nation among humans. Egbert was merely the son of a small-town wealthy man and a concubine. If not for obtaining this divine artifact, Britain certainly could never have succeeded in its founding. If you want to wield it, you not only need sufficient strength, but also the will to inherit Egbert's legacy and defend every inch of British soil with your life."

Merlinfield looked at the mottled traces on the stone sword, the heavy aura of history rushing toward him. This sword was not merely a weapon; it was more like the proof of Britain's royal authority.

"I know. I am already a knight of Britain."

"Although you are the person favored by the current queen of Britain, whether you can pull the sword depends entirely on you. When you pull it, turbulent currents will arise — you must endure pain that others cannot bear," the lake sprite kindly warned.

Merlinfield nodded and, walking resolutely along the strangely shaped stones, approached the elevated stone sword. Summoning his courage, he grasped the hilt of the stone sword. Just like knives and swords, turbulent currents erupted from below, tearing his armor to shreds.

A few days later, the sky was no longer clear but suddenly darkened, the temperature dropping sharply overnight. The sky made people breathless, with thick, suffocating dark clouds.

Cold snowwind blew, striking armor and producing dense clinking sounds. The invincible iron cavalry of the Holy Church and the defending army of the Britons gathered ten miles away from the kingdom's capital. The defense battle of the British capital, on the verge of erupting...

title: Chapter 44 — Battle Begins!
content:
Chapter 44 — Battle Begins!

Volume 30 · Chapter 44

The neatly arrayed kingdom army stood in the cold wind, facing off against a massive gathering of ferocious demons outside the capital. After several days of forced marches, the demons had already invaded the capital's perimeter. With just one order from Mamon, the war would erupt at any moment.

Everyone in the capital was praying for the kingdom's army, hoping they could successfully resist the evil forces. Even most of the adventurers in Ishtar, though they didn't look as organized as the kingdom's army, shouldn't be underestimated for their strength.

The kingdom's knights wore stern expressions. Although they lacked experience fighting demons, over the past few days, everyone had been educated about demons, learning that they weren't invincible.

Under the biting cold wind that made it hard to keep one's eyes open, the demon army stretched out endlessly before them. The demons' furious roars and terrifying visages made one's heart quail.

If it weren't for the special training the defending soldiers had undergone, the ordinary army would have lost their will to fight at the mere sight of the demons.

Among the demon camp, aside from ordinary demons, there were many enormous creatures: giant demons bigger than small giants, assault beasts resembling war chariots, and numerous terrifying demons lurking underground.

Upon closer inspection, mixed among the ordinary demons were many of Mamon's Saint-tier subordinates. Their eyes were distinctly different from those of ordinary demons, and they exuded an aura that made even experienced killers wary of approaching them.

In comparison, the kingdom's army seemed somewhat inferior, having only hastily gathered the elite forces in the capital. They were no match for Mamon's full strength. This sudden landing operation had clearly disrupted Ishtar's prepared deployments.

The atmosphere among the adventurers was tense. Everyone gripped their weapons tightly, gazing at the endless demon army, instinctively feeling fear.

Vice President Shuran felt immense pressure, calculating the disparity in strength between the two sides. He feared the defending army was at a disadvantage, and victory would depend on the strength of the elites in both camps.

"Such a large number of demons... far beyond my imagination," Shuran muttered.

"What's wrong, Vice President? Scared witless?" Adam joked, tuning his lute.

"Don't speak nonsense," Shuran retorted sternly. "If we were scared, we'd have retreated already. We're facing demons, and not just any - the top-tier poverty demon king. Looking at those demons in the distance, he said in a low voice, "We must make these dog-eyed creatures know we're not to be underestimated."

"You've become quite eloquent," Shuran thought to himself, seeing Adam as a somewhat pretentious young man.

"I've studied many heroic tales sung by bards, most of which praise heroes of various eras. Now, the chance to become the protagonist of such tales is right before us," Adam said with a smile, seemingly excited.

"That's right, Vice President. If you're afraid, hide behind me. Though I'm not particularly interested in protecting these residents, I don't want to lose this lucrative job as an adventurer. I dream of returning to my hometown and becoming a farmer when I'm old," Rainier said, loading his gun with bullets infused with Saint-tier magic.

"I don't need your encouragement. I'm not just the Vice President, but also an excellent swordsman," Shuran said seriously, gripping his military sword tightly.

"I'm hungry," Chariya said, looking down at her slightly protruding belly, remembering she hadn't eaten breakfast.

"Shut up!" Shuran scolded.

Gregory, the President, stood silently in his gray robes, gazing into the distance with an unusually serious expression.

Alice, amidst the crowd, recalled the familiar scene before her. It reminded her of when she was with Mamon, though the First Demon Lord Palace's forces were far stronger than the Third Demon Lord Palace's.

"Chapman, are you curious?" Alice asked.

Chapman thought for a moment before responding.

Suddenly, a demon messenger appeared before the kingdom's army. "Surrender immediately! Put down your arms and we'll spare your lives. Otherwise, you'll all become our food!" The demon's words had barely finished when an arrow pierced its left temple, and it fell to the ground.

Chapman, mounted on a fine horse, drew his longbow and shot the arrow with deadly precision.

"We'll send you to hell!" A loud cheer erupted from the kingdom's army, and the soldiers, inspired by Chapman's shot, prepared for battle against the demons.

The demon messenger's death enraged the demon army, and they awaited Mamon's order to charge.

Mamon, standing at the rear in his demonic armor, sat atop a chariot, his eyes gleaming with excitement. "How bold," he said with a laugh. "The human queen really thinks she can resist me? How amusing."

Beliar, beside Mamon, sneered. "I'll annihilate these humans without leaving a single one alive."

With a signal, the demon army charged forward like a raging tide, their bloodlust unstoppable. The kingdom's army raised their shields, bracing for impact.

[Author's note: This chapter continues from the previous ones, with some effects similar to Merlin's. The story will unfold further in the next chapters. If there are any issues, I'll revise them promptly. The entire volume has been completed, and I hope you'll enjoy the rest of the story.]

title: Chapter 45 — Turmoil
content:
Chapter 45 — Turmoil

Volume 30 · Chapter 45

The knights raised their heavy tower shields, forming a defensive line as solid as a bronze wall or an iron rampart. Facing the charging demons, everyone held their breath, some even trembling as they forced themselves to stay calm.

The shield surfaces were studded with sharp iron spikes, a fearless charge—but this was a path to certain death.

Facing such a vast horde of demons, maddened with excitement, how long could they hold?

In the first wave of the assault, the demons’ faces twisted into grotesque snarls, their eyes devoid of fear—only the mad desire to slaughter every human in sight.

They swung bizarre weapons, hurling their bodies against the rounded shields. Blood and severed limbs danced in the air.

A series of *puchi* and *kisha* sounds rang out—the spikes piercing demon flesh, splitting bone.

The knights behind the shields heard it all, and a chill ran down their spines.

What kind of madness had Mammon instilled in his soldiers? These demons didn’t fear death at all. They used their own bodies to block the spikes, paving the way for the demons behind with their corpses.

If demons had always been such fearless warriors, it was unimaginable how the Holy Church had ever won the Holy War in the past.

More and more demons crashed into the shield wall, enduring wave after wave of impact. The knights’ strain multiplied, their entire bodies pressed against the shields, yet they still kept retreating.

Seeing this, the spearmen behind the front lines began their counterattack. Through the gaps in the shields, they thrust their spears forward.

The spears, resting on the shield bearers’ shoulder guards, shot out in a flurry, striking sparks as they skewered the demons outside the shield wall.

Demon corpses piled up endlessly. The knights knew full well that the demon horde seemed endless. The charging demons were nothing more than cannon fodder, trampling a path for the main force behind them.

The knights barely withstood the first wave, but what followed were the demons soaring through the air—

They flapped their crude membrane wings, gliding over the knight formation, and hurled black powder canisters down. Violent explosions erupted, inflicting mass casualties on the knights behind the shields.

The kingdom’s army fell into chaos. The soldiers in the rear were nothing like the heavily armored frontline knights. They were either impaled by shrapnel or burned alive by flames.

As the overall commander, Chapmann immediately issued a counterattack order. The magic knights of the Bauhinia Knight Order waved their staves, launching a barrage of Fireball spells into the sky, annihilating the demons dropping the powder canisters.

But even when those winged demons were blasted apart, the falling powder canisters still exploded among the ranks, causing damage. They carried out their suicide attacks without hesitation.

The momentum of the demon charge had weakened. The short blade knights of the Bauhinia Knight Order made their move. They stepped forward, using the shoulders of the shield knights as footholds, and leapt into the air.

The short blade knights, light on their feet, swung their blades midair, cutting down the flying demons one by one. The powder canisters exploded among the demon ranks.

After landing, the knights moved with agile grace. Their short blades sent arcs of blood flying into the air, mixing with the pure white snowflakes. The pressure on the great shield knights lessened significantly.

From the rear, Alice watched the battle unfold and couldn’t help but marvel. The Bauhinia Knight Order truly lived up to its reputation as the kingdom’s most elite knight order. Their combat strength and coordination were both unparalleled.

A deafening roar shook the heavens as the dense demon ranks lit up with a fierce white glow.

A super-high-output magic cannon had fired. The blast carried an aura of destruction, sweeping toward them with terrifying force.

The demons, heedless of friend or foe, only sought to break through the knights’ defenses. The cannon fire obliterated the charging demon fodder in an instant.

The rear shield knights had no time to react. The short blade knights quickly raised their small round shields, spinning them rapidly. A blue barrier flared to life.

The shields connected seamlessly, forming an impenetrable barrier of magic. They urgently erected this defense to withstand the super-high-output magic cannon.

The knights’ round shields were all alchemical weapons, crafted by Elizabeth in just a few days at great cost to reinforce the Bauhinia Knight Order.

The defensive power of the alchemical shields was in no way inferior to the heavy tower shields—it even far surpassed them.

The magic cannon’s blast collided with the alchemical shields, erupting in a massive explosion. Flames soared into the sky, nearly scorching the clouds above.

As the dust and smoke cleared, an even more dangerous situation emerged. Three monstrous siege beasts, no one knew when they had arrived, now stood before the knights.

The demons were not fools. They too had a way to tear through the knights’ defenses. The magic cannon fire had only been a feint to cover the advance of the siege beasts.

The three siege beasts charged forward, their heavy bodies shaking the earth with every step, each stomp sending tremors through the ground.

The frontline short blade and great shield knights were scattered—some crushed to death by the siege beasts, others trampled under their massive hooves.

The siege beasts resembled dragons, their entire bodies encased in tough, scale-like armor that made them nearly invulnerable to normal blades.

The siege beasts’ charge showed no signs of slowing. They trampled into the dense ranks of the kingdom’s army. The bone blades on their sides cut soldiers in half at the waist, while the mace-like tails crushed heavily armored knights into bloody pulps. Wherever they passed, only corpses remained.

The demons riding the siege beasts spotted Chapmann as the commander. They swung their chain hammers, aiming for him.

In the chaos, Chapmann was thrown from his warhorse. The chain hammer grazed past his nose, nearly taking his head off.

Chapmann scrambled to his feet, frowning. The defensive line had been breached. From here on out, it would be a direct melee with the demons.

A gunshot rang out. One of the siege beasts in the rear had its head blown apart, half its body already blasted open. Sparks flew, and the stench of charred flesh filled the air.

Leire held a hunting rifle, stepping on the corpse of a siege beast as he leapt into the air. He aimed the barrel at the most densely packed demon soldiers in the distance.

“Let’s see who’s more vicious.”

The hunting rifle fired. Under the amplification of Saint-tier magic, the alchemical bullet’s power was monstrous—no weaker than a standard magic cannon. It blasted a swath of demons into ash, leaving behind scorched, cracked earth.

Adams, strumming his lute, charged into the demon ranks, singing and dancing as he went. The oppressive might of a Saint-tier being radiated outward.

The demons seemed bewitched, surrounding Adams as they began to dance stiffly, their bodies no longer under their control—as if possessed.

Adams’ fingers plucked the lute strings. In an instant, the demons’ heads exploded one after another, their bodies collapsing into headless corpses.

A massive brawl erupted. The demons and Britannia’s resistance forces clashed violently. Either a human’s neck was bitten through, or a demon’s heart was pierced by a blade.

Alice also sprang into action. Wielding her sacred greatsword, she conjured a sliding ice ramp out of thin air. Stepping onto it, she surfed across the battlefield like a wave, endlessly reaping demon lives.

At this moment, Alice was the most formidable presence in the battle against the demons. Her blade, paired with the ice spikes, swept through hordes of demons, unstoppable.

Even the fearless demon soldiers felt a pang of terror at the sight of her. Many were scared into retreat.

From the far rear, Beelzebub watched Alice, who was deftly harvesting demon lives. She turned to Mammon’s subordinates and ordered:

“Go. Kill every threatening human. Leave none alive.”

“That insolent bitch is mine.”

“I will rip out her heart and make her regret ever setting foot here to die.”

title: Chapter 46 — Breaking Into the Demon Camp (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 46 — Breaking Into the Demon Camp (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 30 · Chapter 46

The defense army of Pili Gu and the demons began a frontal melee, the battlefield fell into extreme chaos. EZ reading book knights and demons fought you die me in the wind and snow, initially relying on excellent equipment could still hammer those ordinary demons until their heads were broken and blood flowed. Then when Mammon's troops joined the battle, the defense army showed a decline, began to suffer successive defeats, the situation was not optimistic. Originally the ground was covered with white snow, but now it was largely dyed red, making it difficult to distinguish whether the bodies on the ground were human or demonic, the painful wails were drowned out by angry roars, the hatred in both sides' eyes could only be appeased by killing the opponent completely. The clashing of weapons rang in the ears, in the chaotic battlefield, the vice president of the book was entangled by Mammon's fruit-position subordinates. The demon officer was tall, his body wrapped in rusted mirror armor, the special horn on his head was broken by someone in the melee. Shulan held a sword and continuously resisted the demon officer, but was frequently knocked back by the opponent's tiger-tiger-feng warhammer, his hands almost shattered. Although both were Saint-tier strength, obviously the demon officer was stronger by a bit, and in combat he was braver than humans. The demon officer made Shulan kneel on one knee, sneered, 'Lowly human adventurer, opposing Mammon's heavenly realm, is your most foolish...' 'Are you?' The sore mouth of the resident showed his teeth, the sword was full of notches. The breath of the Earth Holy Dragon came like bullets, countless small stones like bullets pierced the demon officer, turning him into minced meat on the spot. In the distance, Elyria closed her mouth but still couldn't help making a sound of indigestion. The strength of Mammon's third demon lord palace is indeed vast; just reaching Saint-tier strength demon officers possess a township position. This is more than double that of the first demon lord palace, showing how wealthy Mammon is among the demon race. This group of powerful demons, almost all participated in this war; even with the kingdom's army aided by adventurers, resisting them is still under great pressure. If at this moment the twelfth thorn knight Claud were still alive, perhaps he could temporarily boost everyone's strength and quickly turn the situation. Unfortunately this assisting adult was ambushed before the battle and injured on the right side, otherwise he would certainly make Mammon feel very uneasy. The knight commander Chapmann swung his sword, angrily cut off the demon's head, then immediately went weak and knelt on one knee, murmuring. Not only Chapmann, but the entire Purple Orchid Flower Knight Corps' knights were about to exhaust their stamina; if this continues, only death awaits. Chapmann raised his head, sharp and doubtful, looking at the chaotic battle ahead, feeling somewhat pessimistic; so far even the Demon Lord hasn't been seen, the kingdom's hastily gathered elites, could it still not be enough to force that greedy monarch to personally join the battle? The vice team leader knight shouted a warning. Chapmann came to his senses, noticing the ground beneath his feet cracking and trembling, with a rumbling roar the earth collapsed. The ground knew it had been hollowed out by some monster; at this moment it suddenly caved into the deep dark underground, a giant sand worm shaped like an earthworm drilled out, opened its blood-filled mouth full of teeth, and swallowed Chapmann whole. This giant sand worm demon is extremely troublesome, moving furtively underground; when it appears it often can seize knights before they react, after eating a few prey it immediately retreats into the deep pit where no one dares to go, no one knows exactly what dangers lie underground. The sand worm demon after eating Chapmann immediately shrank back underground, continuing to follow me below the national standard. Suddenly several sand worm demons appeared on the battlefield; their appearance undoubtedly brought great pressure to the hearts of all kingdom soldiers, nobody dared to look and see if they were not the next to fall. 'Round team leader, come quickly, ah vice team leader was dragged away by the sand worm' the knight shouted anxiously, hoping a few people would come help, Chapmann as the commander of the defense battle, if he died it would be a big problem, the kingdom's soldiers would all fall into chaos. Suddenly a figure jumped into the pit left by the sand worm, leaving the knights puzzled, nobody knew who had the guts to jump down. In the distance, that huge sand worm demon just emerged from the ground, writhing in panic on the surface, trying to throw out the person in its mouth. Alice was inside the sand worm's blood-filled mouth, she reached in and made the monster emit painful howls. Seeing Chapmann eaten, Alice decisively chose to jump into the dangerous pit to rescue, so that the whole kingdom army would not be leaderless. Alice bit her, used her body to prop open the sand worm's huge mouth, freed a hand to create razor-sharp ice spikes out of thin air, continuously swinging, the demon clan turned into countless chunks of flesh in the bloody minced meat, Alice got to the army body covered in sticky liquid Chapmann, fortunately the rescue was timely, otherwise she would have been dissolved by the sand worm. Alice helped Chapmann up, worriedly asked, 'How are you, can you still stand?' 'Chapmann you have awakened, seeing Alice I put my mind at ease, 'Very sorry, Alice little rent, answer your trouble'' Another demon officer was taken down by Adams and Lei Ni together, his burly body collapsed to the ground, chest pierced by both. Adams and Lei Ni panted heavily, their mouths dry, breathing heavily to take down this demon officer, their magic power was exhausted. Lei Ni: 'Go to hell, demon ha' Adams: 'Although a bit troublesome, demon officers are just like dead' Just then a small fireball fell from the sky, seeming insignificant but upon landing it revealed terrifying power. The explosion sent up waves of flame reaching the heavens, making the rolling clouds heavier, the scorching heat instantly vaporized three miles of snow. The heat wave's shockwave forced both sides to regain a little calm, they lay on the ground to avoid being drawn into the fire's center. Lei Ni and Adam, two Saint-tier powerhouses, turned to ash in the flames, without even having time to scream they were instantly killed. From the fire emerged a graceful demon lady, her scarlet river-like long skirt matching the horn on her head, as if she were born beautiful in the flames. Beibei Yaer stepped forward slowly, exuding a terrifying aura of the sect, as Mammon's wife, although not a descendant of the first Demon Lord, she is also a noble of the demon race; whether in power or lineage, she far surpasses ordinary demon officers, noble demons in the demon race are second only to the monarch. Beibei Yaer could not hide her excitement, her eyes in the fire fixed on Alice, full of the pleasure of the impending hunt. 'You seem to be the stronger one in the rebel army, just right to be my opponent.' 'I will make you truly feel the fear that comes from the depths of the soul.' In the demon rear, Mammon, fully covered in demon absolute armor, sat on a temporary throne observing the battle situation. If it weren't for this situation, the kingdom's defending army would be slaughtered completely, just a matter of time. Suddenly a mysterious voice broke the silence of the rear, putting the demons on alert. 'Let the subordinates fight on the front lines while you hide in the rear watching the show, indeed as the rumors say, the greedy monarch is a coward like a mouse.' Mammon remained calm, leaning on his face he asked, 'Who are you, daring to trespass my forbidden ground?' 'I am still the captain of the Holy Temple Knight Corps, Barres, specially came to subdue you.' Barres wore holy armor, his arms holding his helmet, strode forward. The sudden appearance of Barres caused the demons to commotion, who would have thought a madman would dare to rush into the demon camp. Barres ignored all demons, treating this place as his own territory, came before Mammon one by one. 'You are clearly in absolute safety in the rear, yet you still wear heavy armor, just how afraid are you?' 'Take off that ridiculous head.' 'Old man, take a look at the greedy demon lord's face, just how ugly is it.' s Hope everyone gives some points, keep practicing, keep updating. I hand over the updates, everyone writes, updates without end.

title: Chapter 47 — Brief Clash
content:
Chapter 47 — Brief Clash

Volume 30 · Chapter 47

Barres had extreme confidence in his own strength, if still for the sake of protecting the Pope's safety, he thought he might become a renowned Hero who would become renowned under heaven, great size; the cannon fodder-like demons on the battlefield could not arouse Barres's interest, he went around all the demons' sight lines, alone rushed into the demon army's camp. In Barres's eyes, only the Demon Lord was a true opponent; having never seen a true Demon Lord, he wanted to know how the Holy Church, after spending countless efforts, could have an undead demon race king, what kind of existence it was. From an outsider's view, Barres seemed like a brainless idiot, but he had not failed to consider the Demon Lord's strength, which far surpassed his own possibility; therefore Barres had long prepared, carrying a precious item bestowed by the Pope, a scroll that could instantly randomly transfer during battle. This expensive item was scarce in number; previously, a staff member had used the red-clothed Archbishop's stored transfer scroll, managing to escape from Merlin's hands, with outstanding effect. Because he had a life-saving item, Barres appeared not panicky, full of confidence coming to the demon's lair; even if he couldn't win, fleeing immediately posed no problem. The demons stationed in the camp saw humans boldly rushing in, and moreover arrogantly speaking rudely to Mali, they instantly became furious and surrounded Barres. Barres looked at the sharp weapons pointed at him, and the demons' eyes that seemed eager to chop him into pieces, he suddenly sneered, "Demon Lord, your dogs are truly obedient; it seems you have sent your capable subordinates to the battlefield, leaving only this field of trash to guard you; I really came at the right time, I advise you to let them retreat, they are not my opponents, coming forward is just pointless death." The demons hearing this insulting talk all had their anger flare up; if they still needed to obey Mali's orders under the Demon Lord's command, they would immediately hack Barres to death. Sitting on the temporary throne, Ma Wu appeared very calm, displeased, not disturbed by Barres's remarks, and waved his hand. "All retreat, this sneaky sneaky fruit-sneaky mouse that sneaked in is not enough to threaten me." The demons glanced at each other, hesitated a moment, then chose to obey orders and retreated, but did not go far, staring at Barres with eyes full of lingering resentment. "I pose no threat to you," Barres said, looking at Ma Wu, surprised in the net, himself beginning to assassinate, yet the other showed no panic at all. "Even if you are the Captain of the Holy Temple King's Knights, in front of me you are still just a little shrimp," Ma Men lazily sat on the throne, using his hand to touch his head. "Little shrimp, believe it or not, I will immediately pull you down from the throne and beat your waist." "You also deserve it," Ma Men replied, facing the field, continuing, "Not wanting, in my eyes you Bar are already a dead person, and also your Pope, he should now be sitting on needles, unable to sleep at night, waiting for the destruction of the extreme peak, then it will be the turn of the Holy Roman, I will personally enter the temple, destroy the statue of Maliya, as if you notify the Pope, let him write his will in advance." "The timid ghost in the belly, your mouth skills are quite fierce, other demons will also be like you," Barres put on his helmet, the country gradually changed to A. "Hah, you bunch of ignorant church area, merely dogs cultivated by the goddess in the wind world, truly taking yourselves as roots," Ma Men paused, his tone calm, saying, "Who gave you the courage to stand alone before me?" "I am just bored staying in the temple too long, wanting to personally taste a demon king's four-field jade." Barres gained momentum, set up his offensive stance. Ma Men nodded, meaningfully saying, "Interesting reply." As the words fell, Barres suddenly attacked, his whole body radiating golden light like a fierce beast erupting, the air exploded like a beast's roar. Barres stepped on the ground with his feet, cracking the earth, his whole body seemed to merge with the blade, the sharp killing intent frightened the surrounding demons to retreat continuously; the crisp sound of Barres's blade striking Ma Wu's side, immediately collided with an invisible black barrier, no matter how hard he pushed, he could not reduce the distance. Barres, as the Captain of the Holy Temple Knights, his body's holy augmentation equipment against evil forces was twice as effective, his strength could be said to be rarely strong, being called a knight specialized against demons is not an exaggeration. However, during Barres's full-force assault, Ma Men made no movement and could not harm Barres even a bit; who knows how formidable this black mysterious barrier's defense is; seeing this, could it be a rare defensive item? As they say, the treasures hoarded by the greedy Demon Lord are quite valuable; now it seems the rumors are not exaggerated, overall feeling this guy wears all kinds of strange odd trinkets all over his body. "This is the laughable strength of the Pope's bodyguard; seeing you, I instantly have confidence that I could behead the Pope amidst ten thousand troops." Ma Men said sarcastically, raising his right hand, the blood-colored bell on his wrist suddenly trembled, emitting a piercing screech, the sound wave distorted space. Barres stared wide-eyed in shock, quickly retreated, but was still hit by the sound wave; his splendid armor and state were all damaged, shattered into pieces. The blood bell on Ma Men's wrist seems also an unattainable treasure, possessing strong breaking power, shattering all kinds of weapons and armor into fragments. Barres fell to the ground, quickly got up; superficially he seemed uninjured, but he himself clearly knew that just now the screeching sound wave had shaken his five viscera into severe injury; he wanted to vomit blood but swallowed it down himself. "Do you still want to come for the reward of daring to stand alone before me? I can give you a partial map, I will not turn your corpse into military rations for the demons to eat." Ma Men said mockingly. Barres expressionless, resolute, his hands crossed, he posed an exaggerated stance, "Is the Demon Lord very mighty? In my eyes it's just this; open your eyes wide and watch the demon spawn; this is the ultimate sword technique I have cultivated with my life's energy, no one can survive after this move, greedy Demon Lord, are you ready to perish with me?" Accompanied by Barres's hoarse, forceful roar, his eyes showed the spirit of preparing to die heroically, like a god suddenly erupting with unparalleled fierce light. Combined with Barres's self-destruct proclamation and the sun-like light in the field, the demons in the camp were terrified, thinking a huge explosion was imminent, everything before them would be flattened. Although demons are usually fearless of death, in hard collision they still feared the reckless; many demons dropped their armor and fled. However they did not know that this was merely Barres's simple flashbang, causing no damage; all claims of ultimate sword technique are false. After the brief clash, Barres had a deep understanding of the Demon Lord; he realized that fighting alone he absolutely could not match the Demon Lord. Ma Men did not need to use magic or martial arts; relying on his collected rare "toys," he was enough to beat Barres to the point of looking for teeth; choosing to flee was the best strategy. Barres smiled smugly, secretly tore the random transfer scroll, silently closed his eyes, preparing to slip away. "Farewell, Demon Lord, this great lord decides to spare you for now; sooner or later I will personally cut off your dog's head."

title: Chapter 48 — Pecking the Eyes (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 48 — Pecking the Eyes (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 30 · Chapter 48

The frontlines were a chaotic melee between demons and British knights, the battle spiraling into a white-hot stalemate.

The demons had underestimated the knights of Britannia. Their resolve to defend their homeland far exceeded what the demons had anticipated.

The ferocious demons pressed forward relentlessly, but the more they advanced, the fiercer the knights’ resistance became.

Though it seemed the kingdom’s forces were steadily retreating, Asmodeus’s legions were suffering heavy losses as well.

Nie Chongtian’s flames turned the battlefield crimson, scorching waves of heat sweeping across the land as molten lava surged toward the enemy ranks.

Belial’s power was overwhelming. Alice struggled to match her, her ice walls barely holding against the extreme heat of the infernal flames.

Only by fusing magic and battle aura into golden crystalline barriers could she withstand Belial’s fire—but the strain on Alice’s strength was immense.

With Demon Lord Asmodeus still nowhere in sight, if she exhausted both her magic and battle aura in this duel with Belial, Alice knew the idea of defeating Asmodeus through sheer willpower was nothing but a pipe dream.

Alice, a newly ranked Violet Gold adventurer, had earned her reputation through real skill. She was no longer the inexperienced rookie she once was, but even so, facing multiple powerful foes in succession was still a daunting challenge.

Fire and ice clashed violently, thick plumes of steam billowing across the battlefield. The flames in Belial’s hands roared, crackling with a mocking voice, “What’s wrong? You were putting up quite a fight earlier. Now you’re hesitating—are you trying to save some strength for my husband? Let me tell you, that’s impossible. Before you ever lay eyes on him, I’ll break you slowly, piece by piece.”

“Hah… hah…”

Alice crouched behind her golden fusion ice barrier, panting. The battle against Belial was draining her.

Right now, she desperately wished someone would come to her aid. Otherwise, killing this female demon might end in mutual destruction.

Being entangled by Belial left Alice frustrated. She couldn’t help but wonder—why did every female demon seem to despise her? What had she done to earn such universal resentment?

Whether it was Lilith, Ophelia, or Helen, they all treated her with open hostility. Even this sudden appearance of Belial was no different. Maybe this was karma for slaying the Demon Race’s king.

Seeing no reinforcements arriving, Alice thought of Bares, the Saint Knight Captain. If he were here, the pressure on her would ease considerably. But who knew where that man had wandered off to now?

Her frustration surged. That unreliable bastard—where the hell was he? The battle was this dire, and he still hadn’t shown up to help!

What a worthless piece of trash. She should’ve known better than to expect anything from him.

Thinking about his usual behavior, he was probably off flirting with some cheap woman right now.

It infuriated her. She cursed him under her breath—sooner or later, that man would get what was coming to him, dying under some woman’s skirt.

“Stop cowering like a turtle! Get out here!” Belial roared, hurling a massive fireball. The explosion shattered the ice barrier, sending cracks spiderwebbing across its surface.

The moment the ice wall was consumed by flames, Alice leapt out, her expression icy as she locked eyes with Belial. If no one was coming to help, she’d have to kill this demoness herself.

Belial smirked as Alice emerged. “There we go. Stop hiding like a rat. If you’re a knight, then face me in a proper duel.”

Alice let out a low growl, her eyes burning with a golden radiance as her body transformed, enveloped in a blizzard—she had assumed the form of the Frost Saint Dragon. Her furious gaze bored into Belial.

The temperature on the battlefield plummeted once more. Knights and demons alike suffered in the extreme contrast of fire and ice.

“That’s right. This is how it should be. Only when you give it your all does it bring me any joy.” Belial’s laughter grew more excited. With a flick of her hand, she conjured nine colossal fireballs, each the size of a boulder, raining down from the sky like meteors.

The air was scorching, so dry that even a single breath felt like inhaling flames.

The nine fireballs radiated terrifying power, the ground trembling beneath their descent as if they sought to incinerate every living thing in their path.

This was Belial’s strongest spell—its range was vast. She didn’t care about her own forces below; in fact, she preferred annihilating both the demon cannon fodder and the human kingdom’s army together.

But Alice couldn’t stand by and watch the kingdom’s forces be wiped out. She flapped her frost-laden dragon wings, steeling herself to intercept the fireballs.

The Frost Saint Dragon, with its natural advantage over fire, closed in on the fireballs. Without extreme fire resistance, anything in their path would’ve been reduced to ash long before reaching them.

Once she confirmed the fireballs would no longer threaten the kingdom’s forces below, the Frost Saint Dragon spread its wings wide, unleashing a dazzling white light that clashed head-on with the fireballs.

To prevent the kingdom’s army from being obliterated, the Frost Saint Dragon deployed its ultimate arcane spell—Galactic Descent. A frigid radiance continuously eroded the nine fireballs.

Alice’s adventures and efforts along the way had not been in vain. In the past, she would’ve never dreamed of confronting such a powerful spell head-on.

But now, her strength allowed her to clash evenly with a noble demon second only to the Demon Lord. It was proof of how far she had come.

“Still trying to protect those pathetic kingdom soldiers? You really are naive.” Belial sneered, seeing Alice attempt to block her spell. She raised a hand, crimson light flaring as she prepared to pour more magic into crushing the Frost Saint Dragon.

Just then, a small, black-clad figure appeared behind Belial, its tiny frame encased in heavy, pitch-black armor that radiated an overwhelming draconic might, sending shivers down the spines of the lesser demons on the battlefield.

The one who had come to Alice’s aid was none other than Ailes in her Dragon Warrior form. After taking down several demon officers, she had deliberately come to deal with Belial.

“Adamant… Breaker…”

*CRASH!*

Ailes’s hammer struck Belial’s back with brutal force, the impact so violent it sent a shockwave through the air like thunder.

Belial’s face twisted in agony, her features contorted in pain. Her spine nearly snapped under the blow, and her body plummeted, crashing into the ground and carving a human-shaped crater into the earth.

Bares’s lips curled into a smug, satisfied smile. As he slowly opened his eyes, the first thing that came into focus was a painfully familiar sight—his feet standing on the freshly torn remnants of a scroll, surrounded by leering demons.

Bares had never even left the demon camp. The entire time, he had been putting on a farce right in front of the demons.

What the hell? How had his escape failed? Had the scroll teleported him somewhere else?

No—there was no way. How could he be this unlucky?

Bares lowered his head, staring at the shredded scroll fragments on the ground. The edges still bore the lipstick marks left by the women.

It turned out that while Bares had been indulging in pleasure with those greedy women, they had, while he slept, ransacked his belongings.

Upon finding the rare Random Teleportation Scroll, the women had stolen it and sold it in the black market for an exorbitant price.

And the scroll Bares had just torn up? It was nothing but a worthless fake the women had prepared to swindle gullible customers like him.

Bares’s gaze turned vacant, as if his very soul had taken a heavy blow. His mind grew fuzzy as he recalled the countless warnings he’d received over the years.

The demons stared at him with looks of utter bewilderment, completely clueless as to what kind of act this arrogant human was trying to pull.

Seated on his throne, Asmodeus tapped the armrest three times, his voice heavy with implication. “You were just saying something about cutting off whose head?”

Bares’s face paled. He realized his body was slowly stiffening, an unnatural chill seeping into his bones.

The road is long, the goose is fat—
the goose plucks the eye.

In the end, this man still died under a woman’s skirt.
