title: Chapter 49 — Elemental Body
content:
Chapter 49 — Elemental Body

Volume 30 · Chapter 49

The nine scorching fireballs, moments from falling, gradually dissolved beneath the Frost Dragon's icy river of extinguished flames, leaving not a trace. The kingdom army below breathed a collective sigh of relief. Had Belial's great flame magic rained down upon them, the kingdom forces would have suffered catastrophic losses.

Belial crawled up from the center of the ground where it had cracked open, wiping the blood at the corner of his mouth. That previous strike had nearly shattered every bone in his body. Alice, who had entered her pseudo-dragon warrior state, possessed extraordinarily terrifying power amplification. Her seemingly petite frame had become the most fearsome weapon on the battlefield.

"You insignificant humans, how dare you defy me!"

"Oh? Is that so?"

The pseudo-dragon warrior Alice landed heavily, lifted her head, and immediately activated a high-tier earth法则—gravitational space. She did not give Belial even the slighest chance to recover.

"I am a high noble of the demon race! You will pay for this!"

Belial could no longer control his own body. Drawn toward Alice by gravity, he immediately took a crushing blow, his body flying backward like a cannonball.

Though Alice was not a true dragon, her sheer force made Belial feel immense pressure. Once caught in gravitational space, it was extremely difficult to break free.

Alice unleashed relentless, indiscriminate continuous strikes. Before Belial's body even hit the ground, he was pulled back to Alice's side and struck again. And again. Belial was repeatedly hammered by Alice's heavy fists, a scene most bizarre to witness—the female demon like a ping-pong ball tethered by a string, pulled back, struck away, the cycle repeating without end.

In merely a few blinks of an eye, the pitiful Belial had already endured dozens of Alice's crushing punches and still had not died, prompting observers to marvel at her tenacious vitality.

"Human, you—"

"Stop it, damn you! I want—"

"I want to kill you, and I also—"

Belial's anguished screams came ceaselessly, yet each was invariably cut short by another of Alice's fists. The demons watching from a distance stared in dumbfounded horror, daring not to advance a single step.

Having dealt with the nine giant fireballs, Alice saw this scene and a thrill of excitement rose in her heart. So this kid is actually this ferocious?

"Die, hell demon!"

Alice once again drew Belial toward her, gathered all her strength into the tip of her fist, and struck with brutal force. If this punch connected with Belial, she was confident she would shatter the female demon's body to pieces.

Suddenly, a wave of heat swept over her. Ash-filled haze filled Alice's vision. She clearly felt her fist punching through empty air, dealing no substantial damage.

Alice's fist had indeed passed through Belial's body, but her opponent had already undergone a transformation.

Her entire body was now composed of flames, devoid of any solid form. The horns upon her head burned a fiery red, resembling molten steel.

"Hmm?" Alice looked at the fist that had pierced Belial's body. Her opponent had become a flame without physical substance—there was clearly no way to inflict any harm.

"Go on then, little one. Weren't you so fierce?" Belial's burning eyes were piercing and sharp.

A raging torrent of flames erupted around her, turning the sky crimson.

Alice emerged from the fire, black smoke rising from her body, pain flickering across her expression. Her dragon armor had been scorched and blistered by the intense heat, burning agonizingly.

She had somewhat underestimated this female demon. She had expected to finish things quickly, but that was no longer possible.

"Are you alright?" The Frost Saint Dragon hovered above Alice, speaking with concern. "This female demon is very strong. If you let your guard down, you'll suffer."

"A body made of cannons—quite unusual. My punches can't connect with her." Alice sounded somewhat frustrated. Her greatest strength lay in close-quarters combat, which proved utterly ineffective against Belial.

"Can't connect? Could it be that in that state, she possesses immunity to physical attacks?" Alice mused. If Belial's body was composed of fire elements, physical strikes would indeed be useless, no different from punching empty air.

"That's very likely. My punch clearly went through her body, yet she's still alive and kicking." Alice frowned.

"If that's the case, let's go all out with magic together," Alice suggested. The enemy surely couldn't be immune to magic as well. Even Merlin didn't possess such absolute resistance.

The two joined forces, unleashing water and earth elemental dragon breath simultaneously toward Belial in the sky.

The combined dragon auras of the Ice Saint Dragon and Earth Saint Dragon merged, producing an intimidation so profound it made onlookers gasp. Even if the strongest of the dragon lineage, the Explosive Dragon King, were present, facing the combined might of the two, it would rationally choose to withdraw.

The twin dragons' roars echoed across the entire battlefield. Numerous feral demons, their eyes bloodshot, instinctively glanced upward in terror.

Lanlan slashed down another demon with her military saber, widened her eyes, and looked up. "The combined power of two Saint Dragons is actually this terrifying..."

Ice and earth elemental dragon breath merged overhead, instantly forming the phantom of a colossal dragon, roaring as it surged toward Belial.

When the ice shards and flying sand cleared, Belial floated in the air completely unharmed. That devastating magical barrage had failed to scratch her.

"..." Alice was utterly astonished, her pupils contracting, her mind struggling to comprehend how a combined dragon breath attack could leave not a single mark upon her.

"Impossible." Alice's brows drew together tightly. Physical and magical attacks alike failed to harm Belial. Was she truly invincible?

"Your power does impress me greatly, but this level of strength is still insufficient to kill me." Belial raised her hand and conjured a scorching flame storm, engulfing both Alice and Alice within it. The flames swallowed their figures whole.

The Frost Saint Dragon's dragon transformation state dissipated. Alice endured the searing heat, tossed about in the flame storm like dead leaves, entirely at Belial's mercy.

In the chaos, Alice seized her companion's wrist and dragged her to a relatively safer position. To withstand the flame storm, Alice erected a thick rock wall, but Belial's power was so overwhelming that the wall itself was at risk of melting.

"So you've taken to hiding like a turtle. And here I thought lowly humans were brave and tough." Belial's body bathed in flames, she declared proudly, "To die by my hand is your honor. My family has always been courted by the various Demon Lords. Had we not failed to participate in the construction of the initial Blood Pool Seal, our place among the Demon Lords would have been assured."

"Elemental body transformation is our family's secret art. It allows me to evade a vast array of attacks, placing me in an unbeatable position."

"No matter how severe the injuries you inflict, I can rapidly absorb fire elements to heal myself."

"Come out and face your death willingly. You cannot defeat me. Unless you can cause the fire elements in the air to vanish—that would be nothing short of fantasy."

The two hidden behind the rock wall suddenly felt tremendous pressure. Belial's words were effectively a claim of invincibility.

Making fire elements completely disappear was something fundamentally impossible. Elements permeated every corner of the world, varying in density. As long as fire elements existed across a broad area, Belial could never be killed. No wonder her previous attacks had consistently failed to land a blow—it was not dual immunity but rather the use of fire elements to repair her body.

"Damn it." Alice clenched her teeth. "If she can still regenerate, then I truly have no means to defeat her."

Alice lowered her head and pondered for a moment. Glancing at the glowing sword in her hand, her heart stirred. She silently tightened her grip upon it.

"As long as she remains a demon... then she can be killed."

I've caught a cold and have a slight fever. I'm absolutely terrified right now.

title: Chapter 50 — Restraint
content:
Chapter 50 — Restraint

Volume 30 · Chapter 50

Alice and Ailia hid behind a rock wall that was about to melt.

Outside, the scorching firestorm continued to rage.

If this went on, it was only a matter of time before Belial burned them both to death.

Alice stared at the transformed *Mumyōtan* in her hands. This weapon had always possessed the power to restrain creatures of darkness. Now, after awakening to sacred energy, its divine aura had grown even more potent, and its restraining ability had strengthened significantly.

Though Alice didn’t know the origins of *Mumyōtan*, the fact that Chris had hidden it under her bed suggested it was an extremely precious item.

After countless battles, Alice found that the awakened *Light’s Lament* suited her perfectly—fighting demons with it was as easy as cutting melons.

“This monster can constantly regenerate its body. Are you really confident you can kill it?” Ailia turned her head and asked doubtfully.

“I can try.” Alice withdrew her gaze, tightened her grip on *Mumyōtan*, and didn’t make any absolute promises.

“If you don’t have enough confidence, maybe we should give up.” Ailia shook her head, not very supportive of taking reckless actions.

“We can’t just hide here doing nothing. We should finish it off quickly before it threatens the kingdom’s army.” Alice spoke seriously.

“Where do you get that confidence? What if you fail?” Ailia frowned and retorted.

“Mine.” Alice raised the sword in her hand and said earnestly, “It deals tremendous damage to dark creatures. As long as it’s still a demon, it should work.”

Ailia watched the melting rock wall. At this point, they had no choice but to try. So she nodded. “Fine, I’ll cover you.”

“Still hiding?”

Belial floated arrogantly in midair, his entire form like a wicked flame spirit. A surging inferno gradually ignited in his raised hand. “How boring. If that’s the case, I’ll just burn you both to death.”

The moment he finished speaking, Alice endured the searing firestorm and leapt out from behind the rock wall, glaring at Belial with fury.

“Oh? You’ve come out. I thought you’d keep playing turtle forever.” Belial sneered.

“We’ll see how long you stay smug.”

Alice suddenly dashed forward with agile movements, gripping the holy sword tightly as she closed in on Belial in the sky.

She decided to plunge *Mumyōtan* into Belial’s chest, hoping the awakened blade could deliver a devastating wound to the demon.

“Foolish. You still think you can get close to me? Do you want to turn to ash that badly?” Belial was infuriated that a mere human dared challenge him. He summoned a barrage of fireballs, hurling them at the approaching Alice.

Alice had already prepared for this. With her nimble movements, she continuously dodged Belial’s magical assaults. Fireballs exploded all around her, and flames nearly blinded everyone’s vision.

Ailia didn’t stand idly by either. Along Alice’s path, she rapidly constructed rock walls to help block the majority of the magical attacks.

“So annoying!” Belial felt like Alice was a slippery rat—no matter how he struck, he couldn’t land a hit. Finally losing patience, he mobilized all his magic, preparing to incinerate Alice with a large-scale spell.

The sky turned a deep crimson as flame-like clouds churned. An overwhelming pressure surged forward—Belial intended to burn the entire battlefield to nothing.

Ailia slammed her hands into the ground. Beneath Alice’s feet, an infinitely extending stone pillar erupted, launching her high into the air toward Belial.

“Hah! Coming to your own doom?”

Belial swung both arms, and from the crimson clouds, a tidal wave of roaring flames descended, warping the very space around them. Below, whether demon or knight, all were terrified by this apocalyptic firestorm, which seemed capable of reducing everything to ashes.

Alice felt immense pressure. She wasn’t sure if she could successfully drive *Mumyōtan* into Belial’s chest. Doubt gnawed at her.

In desperation, Alice leapt from the tall stone pillar, the tip of her sword aimed directly at Belial’s chest.

The swirling fire demon bared its fangs and claws, roaring as it surged toward the tiny Alice. The heat scorched her face.

This is bad—Belial’s magic is faster than I thought. At this rate, even if I don’t manage to stab the sword into his chest, I’ll be burned severely.

Alice was enveloped in the attack’s range. A cold sweat broke out on her back. Belial’s magic was too fast; closing the distance was incredibly difficult.

But she had already come this far. There was no room for regret. Alice gritted her teeth, exerted all her strength, and hurled the sword in her hand.

Alice looked up. Under the barrage of flames, there was nowhere to hide. She swiftly raised both hands, creating a massive ice shield.

*Sssss*—the collision of ice and fire produced a hissing sound as steam rose into the sky. The hastily formed giant ice barrier was visibly cracking and shattering.

“As expected, a normal ice shield can’t hold up.” Alice’s magic and fighting spirit were severely depleted. Creating a reinforced ice crystal barrier was difficult enough, let alone expecting a simple ice construct to withstand Belial’s flames.

*Boom!* The massive ice shield shattered.

Alice braced herself for severe burns, but the raging flames were somehow kept at bay.

She lowered her head in surprise. Below, Ailia was casting a spatial magic barrier to protect her. The barrier, formed from pure force, had become an invisible shield, safeguarding Alice and the kingdom’s knights beneath.

The fire demon continuously struck the force barrier, pressing Alice down from the sky until she crashed heavily into the ground.

The thrown *Mumyōtan* pierced through Belial’s chest, arcing beautifully through the air before landing blade-first in the dirt.

Belial hadn’t even bothered to defend—he hadn’t taken the desperate throw seriously. Could such a last-ditch attack really do any damage?

With his ability to constantly absorb fire essence to regenerate his body, even if he couldn’t defeat his enemies, he wouldn’t lose. It was a shameless skill that ensured he could never be defeated.

“Pathetic. I can endlessly repair my body, but you only have one life. You think you can kill me?”

“Hm? What’s this?”

The smug Belial’s brows furrowed deeply, his expression turning to panic as he looked down at his chest.

On his seemingly invulnerable flame body, where the sword had pierced, a small white scar remained—unhealed.

The tiny wound rapidly expanded, visibly devouring Belial’s flame essence.

“This… this is impossible! I won’t be injured!”

“I am an immortal existence! I can endlessly repair my body!”

“You despicable humans—what have you done to me?!”

“No—”

As if the sword had pierced through Belial’s very soul, his face twisted in agony. With a final roar, he exploded and perished.

The fiery explosion lit up the sky with a straight line of light. Once again, the battlefield began to snow—though this time, the flakes were stained black with ash.

title: Chapter 51 — The Might of Greed
content:
Chapter 51 — The Might of Greed

Volume 30 · Chapter 51

"The female demon is dead!"

"The greatest threat on the battlefield is gone!"

"Start counterattacking now!"

"Lead the knights to the demon lord's base and chop off the head of the Greedy Demon Lord Mamon!"

As Chapman's shouts echoed across the battlefield, the Kingdom's army, which had been retreating step by step, was greatly encouraged and began fighting back desperately against the demons.

Under Chapman's leadership, the demons dropped their armor and weapons, fleeing toward the demon lord's base.

With Beelzebub and the other demon executives dead, the demons lost their backbone and naturally regained some sense of reason, no longer daring to resist the overwhelmingly victorious Kingdom army.

"Vice President," Lilith let out a long sigh, her worried expression easing as she watched the situation. It seemed the defensive battle could really be won—just defeat the final enemy, the Greedy Lord Mamon.

Alice pulled the unnamed lament embedded in the ground, holding the blade carefully. She couldn't help but sigh—

After changing form, this truly was a divine artifact. Besides being more comfortable to wield, nothing else seemed to have changed.

But now, I'm a bit suspicious. The original unnamed lament—

was a weapon sealed with mysterious power. Although it always had the ability to restrain dark objects, this ability has become absurdly exaggerated now.

I just wanted to injure Beelzebub, but ended up killing him outright.

This isn't simply about restraining dark creatures anymore—this is a murderous weapon forged specifically to kill dark beings.

Alice watched the cold light radiating from the blade. Even she could feel the holy energy emanating from the sword, filled with an impure taste.

"You really did it."

"My fists weren't effective at all."

Alice came to Lilith's side, her eyes full of surprise.

"Alice—"

Alice tapped the blade in her hand, hesitating whether to say that what she held was a genuine divine weapon, specifically designed for dark beings.

Chapman led the knights charging toward the demon lord's base, preparing to face that greedy demon lord.

Only when this battle truly ends will the conflict be over. Otherwise, once the demons regroup, they'll attack again.

The knights' morale revived, chasing the demons all the way, determined to drive them out of the Kingdom of Britain in one breath.

But those fleeing demons suddenly stopped, no longer retreating. Instead, they turned around, revealing vicious expressions.

Chapman was shocked, unable to understand why the retreating demons had suddenly regrouped and turned back to fight to the death.

A black object fell from the sky, landing near Chapman's feet.

Chapman looked closely—what lay in his hand was Barryduan's severed head.

This paladin knight, whom he'd disliked, had sworn boldly before the queen, as if defeating the demon army was easy.

But who knew that after so long, he'd appeared alone and been killed by demons.

This was the reinforcements the Church sent—utterly useless.

Seeing Barryduan die so easily as a Temple Knight Captain, Chapman even doubted the Church's sincerity in supporting Britain. He couldn't fathom how someone who thought they could act recklessly before the demon lord and still escape alive had such brazen audacity.

Suddenly, thunder roared across the silent sky. Several lightning bolts, like serpents, ravaged the Kingdom army, causing massive casualties.

Chapman and the knights trembled in fear, staring at the scorched earth wrought by the lightning.

"What is this?"

At the center of the scorched earth, a figure wrapped in heavy armor rose slowly. The thick helm obscured their face.

The oppressive aura radiating from the armored body was terrifying. This power alone could crush Beelzebub—who else could it be but the Greedy Demon Lord?

Mamon's figure was bathed in lightning, and wherever he looked, everyone trembled.

"The Greedy Demon Lord Mamon—"

Chapman shouted a warning, but the demonic pressure made him feel suffocated.

Alice looked at the armor-clad figure and felt this immense pressure—it belonged to the Demon Lord, no doubt. Compared to the demon lord's true form, they were not even close.

"If you could kill Beelzebub, I admit I underestimated you."

Mamon spread his hands, speaking with deep meaning, "But flattering you won't do. Being forced out by you is your greatest achievement. Feel honored, though honestly, what kind of stray dog thinks it can become my enemy?"

Alice frowned, thinking the attitude in his eyes was exactly like Merlin's.

Do demon lords really see humans as worthless?

When it was her turn, Lilith remained absolutely calm and took the initiative to attack the demon lord.

Lilith's motivation wasn't anything else—just the food stored in the guild's warehouse.

If Mamon took the capital, all the grain in the warehouse would belong to him, seized by the demon army.

Food—Lilith became abnormally brave, her fear of the demon lord completely gone.

"Oh, a truly audacious guy. Fighting back under my pressure—courageous, I'll give you that." Mamon said, sounding like praise but actually slow, biting sarcasm.

"The food in the guild's warehouse is mine."

Alice suddenly charged before Mamon, mobilizing all her strength, her expression furious.

Anyone who dared touch her food was—without question—dead.

"What food?" Mamon tilted his head, utterly confused.

"Relying on this guy to fight for the guild or the people? I'm too naive, Vice President."

The dragon-riding state of Alice amplified her power to astonishing levels. In the entire human world, few could withstand her full-power attack.

The raging dragon unleashed dragon pressure that stunned the demons—not a single one dared rush forward to protect Mamon.

In a short time, Alice piled thousands of times gravity onto her fists. If she struck, it would be like countless mountains crashing down on the enemy—incomparable power.

The air exploded. Alice's gravity-enhanced fist slammed toward Mamon's chest, aiming to kill the demon lord instantly.

Storms raged. The ground beneath the clash cracked, fissures spreading outward. The nearby royal city shook.

"This power—"

Chapman was blown away, utterly stunned. He felt Lilith was even more terrifying than the demon lord.

"Such a strong strike."

Alice covered her face with her hand. The storm's stinging pain made her eyes water.

When the storm and tremors ceased, everyone opened their eyes—only to find Mamon completely unharmed, standing firm against the second blow with one hand.

"Alice—"

Lilith's mind went blank, unable to believe her eyes. All her strength had been useless.

Just how powerful was this existence?

Mamon wiggled his fingers and threw a counter punch at Lilith's chest. The earth trembled, distorted, and sand flew everywhere.

The dragon-riding armor shattered completely.

Lilith's small body sank into the ground.

To kill Lilith, Mamon needed only one more strike.

title: Chapter 52 — Waste (Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 52 — Waste (Extra Chapter)

Volume 30 · Chapter 52

Aria collapsed onto the cracked earth, her eyes glassy and empty. She had intended to strike first, but it had all been anticipated by her enemy. Despite the enormous gap in their levels, Aria and the Demon Lord were separated by an unbridgeable chasm — as different as heaven and earth. Two gods' tier, while not comparable to true gods, had already begun to wield powers that gods possessed. How could they be challenged so casually?

"I'm confused. Why do people keep brazenly coming to challenge me? Don't you truly believe the Demon Lord's majesty is something your lowly human kind can provoke?" Mamon tilted her head, her tone full of puzzlement, suspecting the Holy Church was brainwashing humanity and failing to engrave the terror of the Demon Lord deep into every person's heart.

Aria lay on the ground coughing, nearly choking. Her entire body was so broken she couldn't count how many bones had shattered — if not for the dragon warrior's armor being tough enough, she would have died countless times over.

"Still alive, you human thief who stole the dragon race's power? You're tougher than I expected." Mamon teased, lifting her right foot, about to crush Aria's skull. "Let me see you off, poor little thing."

"Damn it!"

Vice Guildmaster Shuli was burning with anxiety. Not caring about the danger, he rushed out to save the near-dead Aria. If things continued like this, the future successor would surely die.

Although Shuli's actions and decisions were quick enough, it was still too late. He watched helplessly as Aria was about to die beneath Mamon's foot.

Just then, someone faster than Shuli moved to rescue the endangered Aria.

Seeing Aria in danger, Alice didn't hesitate at all and charged straight in.

The situation was extremely urgent. Alice had no extra choices, so she directly unleashed her ultimate technique, the third form of the Great Snow Mountain Sword Art — the strongest single-target attack.

The third form of the Great Snow Mountain Sword Art required Alice to pour all her magic power and battle aura into her sword. It was generally used as a finishing move or in desperate situations.

Because after using "Heaven Splitting," Alice would fall into an awkward state of dual exhaustion from both magic power and battle aura, losing her combat ability entirely.

So during her confrontation with Berial, Alice had held back all along, waiting for Mamon to appear so she could use her ultimate technique to decide the outcome.

Paired with the awakened divine weapon Bright Lament, Alice felt that even if she couldn't defeat Mamon, she should at least severely wound her opponent — forcing the demon race to withdraw would be the best possible outcome.

Alice descended like a deity from the heavens. Pale golden magic and battle aura surged toward Bright Lament, and the fierce pressure made Mamon grow alert.

"Hmm?" Mamon looked up at the charging Alice and sneered, "Humans are so naive. Charging head-on — do you really think an attack at this level can break through the defense of my Absolute Armor?"

"Demon, die!"

Alice let out a furious scream, gripping her sword tightly and stabbing downward at Mamon.

Bright Lament's blade crashed violently against the black barrier that materialized out of thin air. Sparks from the friction sprayed back, and the intense shockwave made everyone unable to look directly.

Mamon let out a startled cry, realizing that while Alice's strength was weaker than hers, the power of her technique was indeed alarming.

The earth beneath Mamon's feet churned like ocean waves. The mysterious black barrier was extremely hard, and Alice's sword couldn't tear through this layer of defense.

Shuli, sharp-eyed and quick-moving, took advantage of the clash between Mamon and Alice to drag Aria — who was hanging by a thread — out to a safe area for refuge.

"Are you okay?"

"I'm... fine..."

Shuli saw that Aria could barely speak, and without needing to guess he knew this gluttonous girl's condition was dire. The fact that she still had a breath in her was sheer luck.

The clash continued, stuck in a stalemate. Mamon, watching the furious Alice, still had the mood to tease, "Your technique is somewhat interesting. Where did it come from? It doesn't feel like an academy sword style."

"Hah!" Alice gritted her teeth, constantly increasing her strength, hoping to tear through Mamon's defense. She simply ignored the other's taunts.

"You'll just be wasting effort. Your attacks have no effect at all. How could my defense be something you can break?"

Mamon's voice suddenly cut off — she had heard a faint cracking sound.

"Krrrk..."

Mamon's attitude grew serious. She looked closely and saw that the impact of the Heaven Splitting technique had caused tiny cracks on the black barrier, and they were spreading continuously.

This black barrier was actually a defensive item, one of Mamon's treasured collections, capable of providing defense with no blind spots whatsoever.

Although it couldn't withstand attacks from a Demon Lord of the same tier, defending against a bunch of disorganized mobs was more than sufficient.

Mamon was quite surprised in her heart that Alice's power could damage a defensive item — she had underestimated the full-strength offensive capability of Alice's technique.

Alice bit down hard on her teeth and went all in, successfully piercing through the black barrier. Bright Lament's blade went straight for Mamon's heart.

The sacred power emitted by the sword inherently had extremely strong suppression over evil forces. The razor-sharp blade pierced through the thick outer layer of demonic armor as easily as tearing through window paper.

After awakening, Bright Lament not only dealt double damage to dark creatures, but could also dispel items that weakened evil power. Tearing through the Demon Lord's defense continuously was easy.

Mamon was greatly alarmed. The seemingly weak-looking Alice had actually made her feel a sense of mortal threat. Her power exceeded expectations — even the demonic armor couldn't block it.

In a panic, Mamon showed a hint of fluster. She leaned her body backward and swung her reverse hand, punching Alice in the face and stopping the enemy's attack in time.

"Human, don't push your luck!"

Alice left a trail of blood spray in midair, then fell onto the cold, frozen ground far away.

She raised her head and glared at Mamon, gripping her sword tightly, feeling the agonizing pain of her internal organs being displaced.

Alice's vision was somewhat blurry. Pushing herself to the limit, she still hadn't succeeded in severely wounding the greedy Demon Lord.

Mamon looked down at her pierced outer demonic armor, which was hissing with white smoke rising. This life-threatening defense had been invaded by sacred power, and it too let out a pained wail.

By rights, demonic armor was far stronger than defensive items, but under that sword's attack, it had become so fragile.

Her beloved toy was damaged, and Mamon's heart surged with fury. She realized the enemy's sword was somewhat special, then approached the gravely wounded Alice.

Mamon carefully observed the Bright Lament in Alice's hand. Although she couldn't determine this sword's origins, from its aura and quality she could tell it was similar to her own demon sword.

"I'm quite surprised that the Britannia Kingdom has two divine weapons. Unfortunately, the sacred aura on it is poison to me, so I can't use it for myself."

Alice, lying on the ground, gritted her teeth enduring the excruciating pain and whispered, "You won't succeed."

"Hah, that's for you to say."

Mamon waved her hand, and instantly a sword bathed in lightning appeared. The razor-sharp blade pointed straight at Alice.

"Even if you hold a divine weapon, it won't be of much use. You don't know how to use this treasure at all — keeping it on you is pure waste."

"But I admit, you're a dangerous human woman. You should be eliminated first."

"See you on the road. Watch closely from within hell as I trample your lot."

title: Chapter 54 — Looking for Monthly Tickets (Extra Update)
content:
Chapter 54 — Looking for Monthly Tickets (Extra Update)

Volume 30 · Chapter 54

Mammon stood stiffly in the center of the battlefield, his head low and silent, his body drunk and sluggish. Being captured by humans was an immense humiliation for him. If he knew how it felt to be mocked by monkeys, he could imagine his current state of mind.

"Adventurers do seem harder to deal with than ordinary insects."
"Don't be so arrogant, old man."
"You think you can block me? That's just your illusion."
"That absurd black hole magic might have perfectly protected you, but I'll let you know what it's like."

Mammon raised his hand, and a crimson war axe appeared in it, its enormous form filling people's hearts with dread, as if it had been spat out of a demon's mouth. This was one of their treasures, capable of withstanding gale-force winds, and its power was comparable to that of an entire army.

Mammon raised his war axe, and a blood-colored storm arose, tearing open the clouds in the sky. The Royal Army was forced to retreat continuously.

"Another strange thing, the Demon Lord's toy is really cool." Gregori muttered, his eyes wide with newfound appreciation for the Demon Lord's wealth. The artifact he had just pulled out was a sensation in another world, a treasure coveted by great powers. Although it was rare to see two of them, Mammon himself possessed such treasures, which was quite shocking.

"Kill you."
"Really?"

Gregori raised his magic wand, and his magic power surged to the limit, summoning a massive black hole in the sky.

Meteorites like fireballs began to fall densely, striking Mammon on the battlefield.

Boom, boom, boom, the explosions were continuous, and the meteorites' impact was formidable. The ground instantly became a crater, with Mammon being thrown up and down like a ball, being beaten around at will, and in an instant thrown into the underworld.

"Indeed, the Guildmaster." The Guildmaster's forehead dripped with cold sweat, looking down at the unconscious Alice, thinking that against the Demon Lord, the Guildmaster must step in.

The meteorites stopped falling, and the battlefield was filled with craters. Mammon seemed to have broken bones, his body in terrible condition, surrounded by numerous meteorites.

"Is it over?" All the knights in the army wondered this, even though the Demon Lord was motionless, his intimidation was still present. No one was sure if the mighty Mammon would die.

Indeed, Mammon remained motionless, and suddenly his hand twitched, and he slowly got up from the ground, muttering, "Your magic is very strong. I'll compliment you a bit."

"That's amazing. Even after such a strong attack, you can still get up." Pudohai was shocked and discolored, feeling that the Demon Lord's defensive power was too terrifying.

Gregori's wrinkled face remained calm, not expecting to easily defeat the Demon Lord. He raised his magic wand again, aiming at the black hole in the sky.

Rumble, rumble, from the black hole in the sky, a mountain-sized meteorite suddenly appeared, falling toward the battlefield.

Under the shadow of the meteorite, both humans and demons were plunged into darkness, and the entire sky was lit up by flames.

The giant meteorite attack was enough to destroy this area completely, and the ground could even be lifted into the sky.

"Looks quite impressive, but it has no effect on me." Mammon roared angrily, raising his blood-colored war axe toward the sky. The mountain-sized giant meteorite was easily cut into three pieces.

He thought he had resolved this crisis, but behind the second giant meteorite, there was a third one falling.

"Still more."

A mountain-sized meteorite fell to the ground, hitting Mammon and causing a giant roar that left everyone in the scene stunned, only the echo of the roar remaining. Fire and impact waves lifted the hard ground, as if waves were moving, breaking the Royal Army and demons into further distances.

"Is this the power of the Guild?" "This is the power of adventurers." No wonder it is revered by the world. Such powerful strength was like that of a god." Chapman gasped in awe, already impressed by Gregori's power. Having such a strong ally protecting the kingdom was the luckiest thing that could happen.

Cracks appeared on the giant meteorite pressing down on Mammon. Mammon raised his blood-colored war axe, and the storm cut the meteorite into fragments. The demon armor on Mammon's body also had numerous cracks and sparks, obviously suffering significant damage from continuous attacks.

"Still not dead." They couldn't believe their own eyes, being hit by a giant meteorite and still standing up, this was how terrifying the defensive power was.

Mammon took a deep breath and said calmly, "I withdraw my statement that you are ordinary people. Your power is qualified to challenge me, but only just."

Gregori's expression became serious, seeing that Mammon was still alive, he was a bit surprised, but he still had a trump card.

He inserted his magic wand into the ground, spread his arms, and released a surge of magic power. The numerous meteorite fragments on the ground began to float, surrounding Mammon, making it impossible for even a sparrow to escape from such a dense meteorite formation.

"What is this?" Mammon's heart skipped a beat, staring in awe.

Numerous meteorite fragments were attacking Mammon, with him as the center, the meteorite fragments quickly forming new meteorites.

Mammon felt he couldn't defend himself, frantically trying to escape, but the numerous meteorite fragments were still being dragged into new meteorites.

"Old man, you are too arrogant. You lowly humans, dare to harm me. I will kill you." Mammon let out a desperate scream, with his exposed arms wrapped in meteorite fragments, quickly forming a magnificent meteorite pyramid on the battlefield. The soldiers of the Royal Army, looking at the black pyramid that appeared out of nowhere, thought it was a miracle.

To prevent Mammon from getting up again, Gregori did not stop, raising his magic wand, continuously distorting the space, using the top-level magic of space cutting.

Space cutting was an attack that distorted and tore space, with a destructive power that was the top level among all attribute magics. Even divine artifacts could not withstand the tearing of space.

Gregori swung his magic wand, and in an instant, he released 64056 intersecting space cuts, directly consuming the vast magic power, leaving him nearly exhausted.

The magnificent meteorite pyramid was cut by space cuts, instantly breaking into numerous small fragments, falling onto the battlefield, and Mammon was still alive inside.

Gregori sat on the cold ground, panting heavily, the consumption was great, with only a trace of magic power left, making his movements extremely difficult.

Looking at the numerous meteorite fragments scattered on the battlefield, Gregori's old face showed a few satisfied smiles.

"Master," Chapman shouted loudly, the image of the Guildmaster Gregori, sincerely admiring, "Gregori Master is too strong. My idol is the Elgin sword family, but now I feel that I am too inferior. In the entire kingdom, only Gregori Master deserves to be called great."

The army looked at the chaotic battlefield, and just as they relaxed, they discovered an anomaly. There was a black shadow behind Gregori. The Demon Lord was still alive. The Demon Lord had gotten up again. The little fool.

Mammon, clad in demon armor, stood behind Gregori, his body emitting a faint electric glow, staring at the old man. "Do you think you've won me, old man?"

"Uh."

Gregori was shocked, turning around suddenly, seeing that the Demon Lord was unharmed, his heart filled with great fear.

Why was he still alive? The Demon Lord's armor was almost broken, and he should have no defensive power left. How did he suddenly repair and become like new?

The unblemished armor, was it really the Demon Lord? Why did it not feel like the same person?

Gregori's face paled, "Splash," his magic power was nearly exhausted, and the Demon Lord was still unharmed.

This scene brought Gregori extreme fear, and even as the Guildmaster, he was not very calm.

What kind of existence is the Demon Lord? Is it a monster that no matter how hard humans try, they cannot defeat?

Chapman saw Mammon still alive, and suddenly felt like he had lost his soul, his sword fell to the ground, and a bitter smile spread across his face. "No matter how hard we try, we humans cannot defeat the Demon Lord."

"Haha, old man, this is not over yet."

title: Chapter 56 — Large Serving, Two for One, Seeking Popularity Votes
content:
Chapter 56 — Large Serving, Two for One, Seeking Popularity Votes

Volume 30 · Chapter 56

"Gregory, that old mentor of mine... he couldn't even inflict a serious wound on the Demon Lord. No wonder. Even from this far away, I can feel the enormous pressure radiating from the Demon Lord." ★ Look ★ for ★ the ★ latest ★ chapters ★ on ★ Baidu ★ search ★ EZ Reading. "Evil King..."

"That old monster has reached the end of his rope, dragging his useless body around. Gregory's defeat was nothing unexpected." Rebakov paused, his expression serious. "But we must be careful. Given our current state, we only have one chance to defeat the Demon Lord."

"I haven't even swung my sword properly yet, and I'm already feeling a bit..." Leonard grunted, rubbing his sore arm.

"Hmm."

Mamon examined the two elderly figures before him. Though their aura was not weak, it was clearly faltering. It was obvious that these were two severely wounded old men who were about to meet their end.

This made Mamon laugh coldly in his heart. Has the Kingdom of Britain really sent only these old men to fight?

"Sir Leonard, Sir Rebakov!" Chapman shouted from behind, not wanting to see these aging knights meet death. "Your bodies can't keep up with the Demon Lord's movements anymore. Return!"

"If the kingdom even sends retired old men to the battlefield, this is a disgrace to us young knights!"

"Silence, Chapman!" Leonard glared. "This isn't about you sympathizing with me, you brat. You haven't even reached maturity yet."

"Chapman's expression shifted. He didn't know how to respond to the elderly knight's face. He was truly just a youngster."

"We old guys will all die eventually. Rather than meekly accepting our fate, we should offer up whatever value we have left. If the knights can die on the battlefield, it would be the greatest regret of our lives."

Leonard spoke with determination, as if he were already dead and didn't care about his own life.

"Right behind me, young knights!" Chapman's expression changed. He clenched his fist tightly. The current situation was very dangerous, and there was no one else to rely on. Perhaps they could only place their hopes on the aging knight.

"Well said, Leonard. I knew I didn't make a mistake. Your loyalty to the kingdom is unmatched among the Thorn Knights. Only you and I could understand each other." Rebakov looked at his own withered hand, his expression deep. "It's wonderful to be able to fight on the battlefield again. I suddenly feel younger."

"I feel the same. I was tired of cleaning up graves anyway. Knights should fight until their very last breath." Leonard drew his sword, letting it fall to the ground with a clang. "Even if we die, the young knights will carry the Blackthorn banner further."

Mamon let out a cold laugh. "The queen has already run out of options? You dare send these two old farts to face me? Is this your way of expressing defiance?"

"Evil King of the demons, the crimes you have committed against the Kingdom of Britain are unforgivable. You will pay the price!" Rebakov's face was filled with rage, his fists clenched so tightly that his nails left crescents in his palms.

"The price? I don't even know how many sins I've committed. Where's the so-called fate's judgment?" Mamon thought for a moment, then burst into wild laughter. "As the king of the demon race, who dares to judge me? The so-called Goddess of Light crawling up to her pedestal, the so-called fate's judgment—this is just psychological comfort for you weak humans!"

"Insolent Demon Lord, your ambitions will never be realized!" Leonard's frail body was pierced through. Since he was already so old, he couldn't sustain prolonged combat. He could only give everything he had, using the fastest technique to attack Mamon.

Leonard's star technique was too refined and swift, completely beyond the old veteran's level. In an instant, the entire area was engulfed in burning stars, impossible to see his figure with the naked eye.

Leonard and Mamon collided in a burst of light and fire. Mamon wielded his lightning blade continuously, trying to suppress Leonard's star technique. Though some of it was unusual, "Even if you're old and dying, your strength isn't small."

Leonard unleashed all his remaining strength. He thought, to kill the Demon Lord, piercing through its heart would be the safest bet. Only when the Demon Lord's heart stops beating can it truly die. But Mamon was wrapped in thick demon armor, like a piece of iron devoid of any weak points, giving the enemy no opportunity.

Mamon sneered coldly, his left hand gripping his war blade, and slashed at Leonard's neck, cutting it clean off.

Under the sunlight, Leonard's head fell to the ground. He quickly dodged the blade's edge, but Mamon was faster. With a single thrust, he pierced through Leonard's shoulder.

"Oh, you're fast. Otherwise your head would have been gone." Mamon felt a bit regretful.

"Leonard's back..." Rebakov roared, his beloved treasure sword appearing in his hand. A large amount of condensed golden light shot out, aimed at Mamon.

The scene was filled with wild explosions. Mamon was blasted away by the massive golden light, though his old body still held up. Together with Rebakov, they were not without fighting strength.

Mamon's face twitched slightly. His armor was dented but showed no real damage. "Are you two just scratching an itch?"

Rebakov gritted his teeth, sitting in his wheelchair, feeling frustrated. "Why is it that when I was your age, the power wasn't this strong?"

"We've really grown old," Leonard admitted reluctantly. "This is the reality. We can only make this bastard pay with our lives. My whole body is covered in aches, and I can't last much longer."

"If this is your limit, I advise you to give up. To be honest, fighting against you like this, I'm already bored." Mamon yawned, putting on a very bored expression. "But I'll let you wake up properly. I'll use my full strength with the star technique, swinging my blade at a speed that's terrifyingly fast, like countless demons falling from the sky."

The crisp sound of metal rang out continuously. Leonard moved rapidly around Mamon, his sword rain completely surrounding him.

Rebakov was not idle either. He launched a barrage of sword strikes at Mamon, forcing this Demon Lord to constantly defend against the attacks. Mamon quickly swung his war blade and other weapons, defending against the two-pronged assault. Yet he still felt the attacks coming back at him, difficult to handle. Several times he nearly suffered a major loss. If it weren't for the demon armor protecting him, he would have been seriously injured.

"Perhaps..." Chapman saw the knight's ferocity, successfully suppressing Mamon. A glimmer of hope ignited in his heart.

"I really hate people who overstep their bounds. Humans are like flies buzzing around. I'm going to die."

Mamon grew increasingly angry at the two old men still being able to suppress him. He predicted where Leonard would appear next, then struck out.

"Thunder!" The lightning blade successfully pierced through Leonard's heart. Blood sprayed onto Mamon's armor.

The battle came to an end. Besides being able to delay the Demon Lord's destruction of the country, there was nothing else they could do.

Leonard hung on the sword, watching his life slowly drain away as his wounds contracted.

"Sir Knight!" Chapman stood up, trying to rush forward, but the pain from his wounds made him collapse in the mud.

Rebakov pushed his wheelchair frantically, not wanting to see his old friend leave before himself.

"Is this really surprising? I can see your every move." Mamon's expression was triumphant, the lightning blade piercing through Leonard's body, releasing a fierce electrical current, torturing this old man.

"Ugh, ahh, ahhh!" Leonard screamed in agony as he was electrocuted. His body turned black and charred. This pain made him feel as though his soul had left his body.

Yet under such unbearable pain, Leonard suddenly bit his teeth hard, resisting rather than retreating. He embraced Mamon with his body, hoping to give his companion a chance to kill him.

"Rebakov, quickly!" Mamon was startled, his face turning slightly pale. He hadn't expected this old man to still have such fight in him.

"Hmm." Rebakov suddenly stopped. But even if Leonard said nothing, he understood his friend's meaning.

Leonard hoped Rebakov would join him and Mamon together, piercing through them. Only this chance could kill Mamon.

Rebakov was a knight who valued the kingdom above all else. Everyone thought he was ruthless and pragmatic. But in reality, he was not like that. He also treasured friendship and emotions, but in the face of the kingdom's interests, these seemed insignificant.

If it could calm the situation and save countless lives, he would not hesitate to swing his blade.

"Once I killed a Thorn Knight companion, I was ostracized by everyone. I became a nameless knight even within the knight order."

"I only wanted to clear my name before I died, to make it clear to everyone that I never betrayed the kingdom, and I am still the most loyal knight."

"Even at this point, do you still want to give me this chance? Or do you want to kill your own friend with your own hands? How tragic."

Years ago in Britain, the king sat on the throne. On his face was a mix of anger and shame.

"The seventh Thorn Knight was greedy, embezzling all the military funds of the Blackthorn Knights, and declaring himself the leader of the knight order."

"The eighth Thorn Knight's nephew committed murder, but was mysteriously acquitted in the shadows, which I find hard to believe."

"The ninth Thorn Knight colluded with the Spanish king, and the design plans for our warships mysteriously ended up in the Spanish kingdom."

"The tenth Thorn Knight established a knight alliance, even going so far as to mine magic crystals from the demon forest without authorization."

Rebakov knelt on the ground, listening to these shocking stories about the Thorn Knights. He was hearing about these new faces for the first time, such as the young Thorn Knight Kratos, who possessed unique power and extensive knowledge, a model for the younger generation of knights.

The names Albert mentioned were all national heroes, each with remarkable military achievements.

Rebakov's expression was complex. He should have devoted himself to the king and established a stable order. The wild ambitions of these people were troubling. "Even one of them has touched the bottom line of the kingdom."

"After hearing all this, what do you think?" Albert asked.

Rebakov's face was grim. "These things are indeed hard to deal with. You all have experienced hardships together. We must not give up on building our ideal new country."

Albert paused, then continued. "But absolutely not in the way these villains have done. I understand your intentions, but I still believe in you, Rebakov."

"Rebakov."

"Your family has been knightly for generations. You have always been by my side. Even when I raised my flag, you could feel your loyalty."

Albert stared at Rebakov's eyes. "The more privileges you gain, the more unstable the kingdom becomes. I don't know how long this peaceful situation can last. I hope all of this is just empty words."

Rebakov silently tightened his grip on his sword hilt.

Several days later, late at night, at a Thorn Knight's residence. Blood everywhere.

"Why did Sir... die in a pool of blood?"

"Of course we are friends, and even comrades. But I must threaten the kingdom's stability, even if it means more innocent deaths." Rebakov's face was dark red, standing amid the blood.

"All the effort we put into building this country, all the blood we shed—was it all for nothing? Without us, there would be no Britain!"

Rebakov remained expressionless. "You have privileges, but you are not the master of the country. Even the king is not, so how could we be?"

"We overthrew the previous regime. If it weren't for them donating money and children, we wouldn't have been able to walk this far, stepping over countless corpses."

"You're too naive. We have more people and resources. Just endure a little longer on the battlefield."

The ninth Thorn Knight's breath grew weaker. He continued, "You have already taken my wife. Let me go."

"I'm grateful you saved me before, but you must die." Rebakov's voice was cold and emotionless, chilling to the bone.

"Rebakov, you're just a cold-blooded killer. You'll end up in hell. I'll bring you back from the pile of corpses." The ninth Thorn Knight's face turned cold, letting out a final bitter laugh.

The next night, the ninth Thorn Knight's death was confirmed. Most people still couldn't believe it. In the palace, in front of all the nobles and officials, King Albert faced the trial of his relative, the ninth Thorn Knight.

Although he executed his relative, the ninth Thorn Knight, Rebakov still made a statement. The minister sighed. "Minister Rebakov, why did you kill the ninth Thorn Knight? What reason do you have?"

"What reason? I was just following the king's orders."

"Is that so? You are the founding minister of the kingdom, a hero of great merit. How could you..."

The nobles and ministers in the palace were immediately enraged, accusing him of acting without authority. Even the younger knights began to speak up, not tolerating Rebakov's behavior of currying favor with the king.

"Do you really think you're above the law, Rebakov?"

"I won't punish you." The king said.

Egorbert's face flushed with rage, his brows knitting tightly together.

"You killed a fellow demon," he said, "and you should be hanged for it."

The kingdom had succeeded in its single aim; I could avenge you with death, and you are no longer an ordinary person.

"From this day forth, I shall decree the hereditary knightly titles, and the Thorn Knights may not hold office, may not trade, may not scheme. Those who rebel will be executed without mercy."

"I hope to build this place where the nobles run rampant — no, that is impossible. Lebabekof, on this cold day, as it was before, and as it is now, even if we descend into hell, it will not change. Let me bear this name until my life reaches its end."

The wheelchair, facing forward toward Magog, even though he has lost both legs, still unleashes the strength of his military body, forcing this old king to rise.

"The Demon Lord, I command you to come out," he roared, his eyes blazing with fury, thrusting his beloved Leonard's body and Magog's heart together in a charge.

Looking at his own chest pierced through, the military officer swayed unsteadily, his voice filled with disbelief.

"I can't believe I would..."

title: Chapter 57 — Admit

Chapter 57 — Admit

Volume 30 · Chapter 57

The mysterious underground lake's depths were isolated by an ancient magical barrier, forming a relatively tranquil zone. Yet at its very center, the icy lake churned like blades, ceaselessly battering Windsor Mesfield as she struggled to pull the stone sword free.

To retrieve the kingdom's treasure, Mesfield had no idea how long she had endured this torment. Her armor was already in tatters, and jagged wounds covered her body.

Even the lake spirit watching coldly from a distance couldn't help but admire the knight's unyielding will. The weaker ordinary creatures in the area didn't dare approach, trembling in the currents.

Mesfield gritted her teeth, enduring the blade-like water as she poured every ounce of strength into pulling the stone sword from the coral and seaweed-encrusted rock.

Yet for some reason, this stone sword was sealed here by some power. Even as Mesfield exhausted her last bit of strength, she couldn't budge it an inch.

Ssshhh— the current sliced open Mesfield's arms, the dense wounds too gruesome to look at. Even the faint outlines of veins and white bone were visible.

Why is this stone sword so stubborn? I've nearly spent all my strength, and all I have to show for it is a body full of wounds. Could it be... that it doesn't recognize me? Damn it, this can't be!

The demonic beast tide was threatening the kingdom's safety. The queen had high expectations for her. She couldn't just give up and die here.

Queen Elizabeth's expectations had become the unwavering faith in Mesfield's heart. If she couldn't retrieve the King's Sword, she would have no face to return to the queen.

The lake spirit couldn't bear to watch any longer. In a gentle voice, it advised, "Give up. The King's Sword doesn't recognize you. No matter how hard you try, you won't succeed. If you keep this up, you'll only lose your life."

"I still have to return to the kingdom. I need this power. If I can't bring it back, the consequences will be unthinkable." Mesfield clenched her teeth and said resolutely, "I can't give up now."

The lake spirit fell silent, watching Mesfield's back. Humans were always so obsessed with power, even at the cost of their lives. Clearly, this wasn't rational.

Mesfield continued her efforts, but her consciousness began to blur, her body swaying unsteadily. Just at that moment, a wisp of white mist drifted from the stone sword, coiling around it like a snake.

This spiritual mist seemed like some kind of spirit, as if it were gazing at Mesfield with invisible eyes.

"Who are you?"

This voice suddenly echoed in Mesfield's mind, startling her.

She looked around, but the lake spirit showed no reaction. Only she could hear this voice.

Mesfield forced herself to calm down, examining the spirit on the stone sword, certain it belonged to someone.

"I... I am the Chief Thorn Knight of the Kingdom of Britain."

"The Chief Thorn Knight looks so young. Has Leonhard already died?" the unknown spirit asked.

Mesfield's heart jolted. How did he know about Knight Commander Leonhard? Could he be from the Kingdom of Britain?

"He... suffered serious injuries and his strength is no longer what it once was. He retired long ago."

"That's good. It's good to rest, to enjoy life. Is he still as melancholic as before?" The unknown spirit seemed curious about the outside world, peppering Mesfield with questions.

Mesfield remained on guard and didn't answer. Instead, she questioned, "Who are you? Why have you become a spirit and linger here?"

"Oh, I almost forgot. You're so young, you wouldn't recognize my voice." The unknown spirit paused, then suddenly spoke with a solemn tone, "I am Egbert, the founding emperor of Britain. Now you should understand."

"Egbert..." Mesfield's eyes widened. She never would have dreamed that Emperor Egbert's spirit still existed in this world. "Why are you here? Are you trapped?"

"Not at all. I am merely continuing to guard the King's Sword, to prevent it from being stolen by others." Egbert's spirit softly replied, "You are not of the royal bloodline. Normally, I wouldn't allow you to take the King's Sword."

"It was Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth who ordered me to retrieve this sword and use it to repel the invading demon race. Time is already very tight." Mesfield said seriously.

"Queen Elizabeth entrusted the King's Sword to you?" Egbert was extremely shocked. He hadn't expected his descendant to hand over the divine artifact to an outsider. What kind of trust had Elizabeth placed in her to make such a decision beyond the bonds of blood? "Knight, what is your name?"

"Windsor Mesfield."

"Mesfield... still exists?" Egbert's spirit flickered, his emotions becoming unstable. "Is Raykov your ancestor?"

"He is my father." Mesfield calmly replied.

"Is he still alive? How is his health?" Egbert asked tentatively.

"Alive. Apart from occasional backaches, his body is still quite hardy." Mesfield recalled.

Egbert's spirit fell into silence. No one knew what the founding emperor was contemplating.

"Child, grasp the King's Sword. I will help you pull it free." Elizabeth's eyes were not wrong. This treasure should only be entrusted to you to safeguard the kingdom's security. "Only you, a member of the Mesfield family, are worthy of the King's Sword. Your family's loyalty is beyond doubt."

Mesfield's head spun. Before she could figure out what was happening, the previously unmoving stone sword began to tremble.

"This... this is..."

"One more push, child." Egbert's spirit encouraged Mesfield, helping her obtain the King's Sword.

Mesfield endured the pain from the currents, steeling herself as she mustered the last bit of strength in her body.

Whoosh— the current erupted like a geyser, piercing through the lake's magical barrier.

With Egbert's help, Mesfield successfully pulled the stone sword free. She collapsed to her knees, gasping for breath.

Her heart was in turmoil. She... she had actually succeeded? Even though she wasn't of his bloodline, Egbert had still acknowledged this outsider.

Mesfield looked at the stone sword in her hands. Though its surface was pitted and battered, she could clearly sense the immense and mysterious power contained within.

"This is the King's Sword..."

"Child, take it out. My spirit is about to dissipate." Egbert's spirit gradually turned into specks of light, vanishing into the air.

"Before I leave, I hope that when you go out, you can apologize to your father on my behalf."

"His heart has carried too many heavy burdens. In my eyes, your father was always the most outstanding knight. No one could compare to him."

"I truly admired him from the bottom of my heart. You should also feel proud to have such a father."

title: Chapter 58 — Empty
content:
Chapter 58 — Empty

Volume 30 · Chapter 58

“I can even do that?”

“Still ‘possible’?”

Mammon remained expressionless, looking down at his own chest where the blade had pierced through. His body was shaking uncontrollably.

He hadn’t expected that an old man who looked like he was about to be buried would be so crazy.

Mammon paid for his underestimation with a direct stab to the heart.

Fortunately, the armor was strong enough to block the attack.

Leonid smiled with satisfaction, having fulfilled his wish, then tilted his head and breathed his last.

Rybakov’s face was dark and heavy, like an iron-blooded warrior.

“I told you you’d suffer the consequences of fate. The Demon Lord’s palace will be your grave.”

“Damn it!”

Chapman’s dry lips moved, his eyes filled with deep regret. He never dreamed that the elderly knight commander would succeed where all the young knights had failed.

“Did we finally die?” The vice-president’s mood was extremely excited. The defeat of Demon Lord Mammon meant this campaign had finally come to an end.

The severely injured knights heard Chapman’s shout and cheered, the sound of victory echoing across the field.

While some creatures with early-stage regeneration abilities were recovering, most of the wounded were lying on the ground.

“The Demon Lord is dead. As the Demon Lord, I will be killed by the humans I despise.” Mammon’s voice was hoarse, sounding like he was on the verge of death. But suddenly, he burst into laughter. “Are you kidding? You fools are playing with me!”

“Huh?” Rybakov’s expression changed, cold sweat running down his forehead. “His heart has already been pierced.”

Mammon raised the sword in his hand, creating a bloody storm that tore Leonid’s corpse to shreds. The old man’s body was cut into large wounds, blood spraying everywhere.

“Why? Why is he still alive even though his heart was pierced? Is he an immortal monster?”

Chapman poured a bucket of cold water on himself, feeling that this was against all logic.

The knights’ excitement instantly cooled. If the Demon Lord could survive a heart stab, what chance did they have? With such heavy casualties, the situation was becoming increasingly dangerous.

The heavy helmet of the demonic armor fell to the ground, revealing Mammon’s “true face.”

Inside the massive armor was nothing but empty space. Mammon wasn’t there at all.

No wonder even Rybakov’s stab to the heart didn’t kill him. He hadn’t been on the battlefield; he had been in a safe, unknown location, watching his minions and the humans fight.

Mammon, who was considered the most rational and fearful of all the Demon Lords, would never appear in a dangerous place.

“Ah, you found out. I was just trying to tease you a little longer. It’s all because this helmet is too heavy.”

Mammon dusted off the armor and put it back on.

The atmosphere of the kingdom’s army turned deadly, as if they were facing a headless knight.

The empty armor dealt a massive blow to everyone’s morale. They hadn’t even seen the real face of the enemy.

“What the hell?” Chapman’s eyes twitched. He couldn’t believe what he was seeing. “We’ve been fighting for days, and it was just a suit of armor?”

“What kind of Demon Lord is this? He’s using his toys to force us into a corner?”

“What kind of existence are we dealing with?”

“I’m very pleased with your reaction. You’ve clearly understood the gap between us. Although this armor is just my toy, its power is infinitely close to my own. Isn’t that amazing?” Mammon said sarcastically. “In the end, you ants can’t kill me. You’re desperate enough to send an old man to fight me. I’m disappointed.”

Rybakov’s body shook violently, as if he was holding on by a thread.

“What’s going on? Is he still alive? This guy has incredible vitality.” Mammon looked coldly at the dying Rybakov, finding him annoying.

Chapman finally noticed this unfamiliar old man. “Who is he? Why is he here with the knight commander?”

Mammon grabbed Rybakov’s head roughly, lifting him off the ground.

“Old man, why don’t you enjoy your retirement? Why come here to fight me?”

Rybakov’s head was about to split, but he spoke with dignity. “You’re trampling on our land. I must kill you.”

“Oh? You’re so determined. You must have accepted death, right?”

A hawk’s cry echoed in the sky, and a black eagle flew over the battlefield, dropping a figure.

Mesfield had just received the King’s Sword and rushed to the battlefield without resting.

She was wearing tattered clothes, her wounds wrapped in rags, looking extremely disheveled.

“Mesfield! You’re here!” Chapman dragged his injured body over. Seeing the reliable first knight, his despair eased.

“What’s the situation?” Mesfield asked, panting.

“It’s not good. We’ve suffered heavy losses. Master Gregory, Commander Leonid, Lady Alice, and many other strong adventurers and knights have been defeated.” Chapman said gravely.

“What?!” Mesfield was shocked. These people were much stronger than her. If they couldn’t beat the Demon Lord, what chance did she have?

“The Demon Lord hasn’t appeared. I don’t know where he is. The thing on the battlefield is his armor, which is incredibly powerful.” Chapman explained.

“We can’t even beat his armor?” Mesfield was incredulous. How strong was this Demon Lord?

She looked up and saw her father being held by the Demon Lord.

“Father!” Chapman was startled. He didn’t expect the old knight to be Mesfield’s father.

Mesfield was furious. Without thinking about the odds, she rushed to save her father.

Seeing her father dying, Mesfield was desperate. She ran to Mammon and pointed her sword at him.

“Release my father, you despicable Demon Lord!”

“Your father?” Mammon looked at Mesfield and then at Rybakov. A dark thought crossed his mind.

“Interesting. Very interesting.”

“I’ll let your father go. On one condition: you cut your own throat in front of me. Use your life to save his.”

“Humans love to talk about family and emotion. Let me see how much that’s worth in reality.”

“I love it when emotions are crushed by reality.”

Mesfield’s eyes widened in horror. She couldn’t believe what she was hearing.

“You... you monster!”

“I’m not a monster. I’m just a Demon Lord. You’re the one who brought this on yourself by attacking me.” Mammon smiled coldly. “So, what’s it going to be? Your father’s life, or your own?”
