title: Chapter 60 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter (Double Happiness)
content:
Chapter 60 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter (Double Happiness)

Volume 30 · Chapter 60

Mammon and Melphist's strength had increased to a visible degree. Although Melphist's current strength was still stagnant, he had the capital to counter Mammon. Chapman looked at the stone sword in Melphist's hand, feeling suspicious. "Where did that weapon come from? I remember it was Melphist's weapon."

Although the King's Sword was a powerful weapon, the extent of its power was still unknown. Compared to Mammon, a strong existence who was a god himself and a mature user of the Seed of the Devil, Melphist seemed too young. "This sword will absolutely be able to punish all crimes, and it will be used to clear all sins every day."

Mammon said with a strong tone, "Is that so? I like that weapon. After I conquer the entire Britain, it will eventually become mine. I will put it in my treasure trove and make it my most precious collection." Mammon did not hide his greed, and if he could obtain the divine artifact, it would become even more powerful.

Melphist, holding the stone sword, quickly approached Mammon and launched a series of consecutive attacks. "How's that?" Mammon, wearing heavy armor, did not slow down at all. "You should recognize your own status. You are just livestock, and livestock should have the appearance of livestock."

The stone sword grazed Mammon's ear and instantly struck his chest. Mammon was knocked to the ground, and his eyes saw Melphist pursuing him relentlessly. "Don't hold back. Do you think you can save Britain from its doomed fate?" Mammon sang in a low voice, and the devil's armor on his arms rotated, forming two black spikes that stabbed towards Melphist like spears.

One of the spikes pierced Melphist's shoulder, and blood splattered everywhere. "Can this make you calm down?" Mammon said with a cold smile. "Let's make a deal. Hand over the stone sword, and I..." "This sword will only be inserted into your chest," Melphist said, gritting his teeth and breaking off the spike that had pierced his shoulder. The pain was alleviated by his anger.

"You know, your father was also a guy who wasn't afraid of death. I really dislike you guys who cling to death and won't let go." Mammon said, listening to the devil's whispers, and suddenly appeared in front of Melphist. The stone sword shone with a golden aura and struck down.

Mammon was shocked and raised his arms to block, but was knocked to the ground by the stone sword. The massive force made him flip over, and he struggled to get up. "Will you be able to turn your anger into strength?" Mammon got up, looking at his broken arms, and suddenly a large amount of black smoke rose, and the devil's armor was repaired.

"If you want to die, I can fulfill your wish." As soon as Mammon finished speaking, he took out a magic wand with a green gemstone at the tip, and a large amount of magic elements were released from the wand. "Britain's divine artifact is indeed very powerful. I won't engage in close combat with you. This artifact is called the Phoenix Wind Blade. I will use it to attack you from a distance."

Melphist's Saint-tier aura burst out, and he fearlessly charged towards Mammon. "Ha, you're too arrogant." Mammon raised the magic wand, and the sound of cutting through the air was heard. A large number of high-pressure wind blades swept across the battlefield.

"Ugh" Melphist was hit by the wind blades and retreated continuously. His original injuries were not fully healed and had become even more severe, with blood flowing everywhere. If Melphist were to approach Mammon again, he would definitely be cut into pieces by the wind blades.

The crazy wind and high-pressure wind blades cut through the battlefield, leaving scars on the ground. The Crusade Army's knights were unable to withstand the attack. Many knights were cut into pieces, and their armor was useless. Chapman retreated in shock, his face covered in wounds.

"What kind of power is this?" Chapman asked, shocked. "This is the power of the Demon Lord. It's enough to threaten the safety of a kingdom."

Mammon's expression was crazy with excitement. "This is the power of Britain's divine artifact. Although it's not as powerful as my own, it's an artifact that can attack on a large scale. If I could obtain it, I could make up for my weaknesses."

Melphist, with a fierce determination, raised the King's Sword to its highest point. The sky was torn apart, and a massive destruction beam shot out, destroying everything in its path. The beam burned everything, leaving no ashes or residue.

In just one attack, Mammon's devil army was swept away by the divine artifact's power. The three large mountains in the distance were pierced through, and the heat wave rose. "This... how is this possible?" Mammon was attacked head-on, and the damage exceeded the devil armor's self-repair limit.

Mammon's body was covered in wounds, and he looked like a blood-soaked person. He had forced himself to use the divine artifact, resulting in his shoulders and several tendons being broken. He lost his combat ability on the spot.

Although Melphist's method was successful in defeating Mammon's substitute, it was a narrow victory. Chapman looked at the scene before him, which seemed like the wrath of the heavens.

"If this were to be used against the kingdom's army, wouldn't it be instantly annihilated?" Chapman asked. "What is the origin of that divine artifact?"

The vice president, Veran, said, "Its power is enough to threaten the safety of a kingdom."

Melphist coughed out a few mouthfuls of blood. Despite his severe injuries and dizziness, he still held the King's Sword tightly. Melphist felt extremely tired and just wanted to rest.

In the distant Magic Mirror Sea Strait, the true Mammon was sitting safely on the magic throne in the Demon Lord Palace, surrounded by his subordinates. They watched the events on the battlefield through a magic mirror.

Mammon, who was unable to put himself in danger, was enjoying the show. The deaths of the devils and knights were just a drama to him.

When Mammon's substitute was destroyed, Osie's heart was filled with worry. This proved that the plan to defend Britain had failed, and they would have to face the punishment of the Elder Council.

Mammon stood up from the magic throne, applauding enthusiastically. "It's too exciting. The performance of those who fought to the death is worthy of my praise."

"The divine artifact of Britain is indeed powerful. Although its destructive power is not as great as mine, it's an artifact that can attack on a large scale. If I could obtain it, I could make up for my weaknesses."

Mammon said with a smile, "I really like that divine artifact."

Osie said, "But, Your Majesty, the plan has failed. You will have to face the Elder Council's punishment."

Mammon laughed and said, "Failure is not in my dictionary. I have prepared multiple substitutes for this battle. You think I would be so foolish as to only prepare one or two?"

Mammon sat back on the magic throne, laughing. "It's time to let those people experience true despair."

On the battlefield, the kingdom's army was cleaning up the aftermath. They collected the bodies of their comrades and held a funeral for the heroes who had died.

When they went to pick up Melphist, they found that he had fainted from his severe injuries. It would take many days to heal his wounds.

Chapman looked at the countless bodies on the battlefield and felt a deep sense of sorrow. He hated war and knew how many people had lost their lives in it, including his father.

Although they had won the battle, the joy was short-lived. The pain and regret that followed were unbearable.

The kingdom of Britain had suffered heavy losses, sacrificing many strong warriors, and had only defeated one of Mammon's substitutes. The true Demon Lord had not appeared.

The victory was bittersweet, and the survivors were left to mourn their losses.

Chapman was asked by the vice president, "How is Melphist's condition?"

Chapman replied, "It's severe. If we're not careful, half of the team might not be able to move."

The vice president said, "So severe? Melphist's bravery is admirable. I don't have the courage to face the Demon Lord alone."

Veran bowed his head, sincerely expressing his fear.

Chapman said, "It's human nature to fear such a powerful existence. We will give our greatest support. Besides, if we weren't afraid, we would have died long ago. The Holy Church's people, like Barre, are all talk and no action."

Chapman frowned, feeling that the Holy Church was not reliable.

Veran had never seen the Holy Church's people like this before. "They're so arrogant, but in the end, they're just pitiful guys who get educated by the Demon Lord."

Chapman shook his head, not wanting to mention that person. "How is Elania's condition? I see that she's also injured."

Veran replied, "She's been sent to the back to receive treatment. As long as she can eat well, she'll recover quickly." Veran was not worried about Elania but was concerned about the food in the guild's warehouse.

Chapman asked, "What will happen to the guild after this?"

Just then, a loud noise broke the short silence, and a large amount of dark mist appeared on the battlefield.

"What's going on?" Veran asked, shocked, his eyes wide with fear.

Chapman said, "I don't know. Suddenly, there are countless devil armors with evil auras."

The devil armors stood on the battlefield, their numbers too great to count. They seemed like a regular army, and their simultaneous movement was like a well-trained team.

The devil armors opened their mouths, and their voices overlapped, creating a strange and terrifying sound. Everyone's hair stood on end, and they felt a chill run down their spines.

"You think you've won? Don't be so naive, humans."

The devil armors said, "Don't rush to collect the bodies. You've used up so much effort and resources to defeat my substitute. I'll give you a round of applause."

Mammon's voice came from the devil armors, "Looking at your efforts, I'll barely praise you. But next, I'll let you experience true despair."

"The mirror armor substitutes have strength close to my true body, and their numbers are..."

The devil armors continued, "You'll soon understand the true meaning of despair."

title: Chapter 61 — Life Flows Again
content:
Chapter 61 — Life Flows Again

Volume 30 · Chapter 61

<<<BEGIN ENGLISH TRANSLATION>>>
“You,”

“Still think you have a chance against me?”

I’ve staked my home and snow on this, how could I possibly let failure happen?

Ten thousand sets of demonic armor

appeared densely packed in the center of the battlefield,

like an invincible demon army.

Each unique-looking demon

armor established a blood bond with Mammon,

so even if one head was cut off,

the void-tier armor clone would still move.

Because the clones inherited Mammon’s power,

each possessed near-Mammon-level strength,

and their combined demonic pressure overwhelmed

the British kingdom’s army.

You barely defeated two clone faces,

but now facing you is a vast army of ten thousand.

The power gap is so large that even the surviving knight king

fell into despair. The knights who had resisted

looked at the armor legion and fell silent,

with no scream of fear — they had lost all hope.

“We sacrificed so much to defeat the clone,

but fifteen thousand of them exist?” Chapman’s throat dried up,

his face showing bitter disappointment. “We can’ thought we could win;

is heaven really out to destroy Britain?”

“Ten thousand clones all as strong as the first one? That’s impossible.

The demons in the palace never had such power.

These clones are stronger than the most elite units.”

Shuri felt a chill. To defeat Mammon,

the kingdom had no chance — it was pure wishful thinking.

The strong warriors were all severely injured,

completely unable to fight.

Moreover, Mammon could control ten thousand clones,

showing his immense mental power.

“Maybe he’s bluffing — one person controlling so many clones

should reduce focus. The actual power might be weaker than before,

otherwise it’s against common sense.”

“Chapman, gather the injured knights to fight — there might be a chance.”

But Chapman stared blankly at the battlefield, trembling.

He was too scared to organize any resistance.

In his eyes, Mammon’s giant figure loomed over the entire kingdom,

playing with them like toys, crushing all resistance.

The other knights weren’t much better — they just wanted to die quickly

and escape the despair.

Mammon had achieved his goal: by repeatedly torturing rebels,

he left deep psychological scars.

Once the fear spread across the kingdom,

he could conquer other regions without effort.

“Shuri gripped his sword, forehead sweating.

‘I’m the only one left, but I have no confidence.’”

“This is boring — you’ve all become sitting ducks.

I expected you to defend your kingdom and attack me again,

but I overestimated you.”

As he spoke, the demon armor clones opened their arms,

and the evil ghost reliefs on their chests came alive,

opening mouths to suck in air.

The magic elements in the air condensed into black balls

on their chests, radiating intense malice.

Who knows how powerful these concentrated energy bombs are?

Shuri saw the scene as if in slow motion:

dense bombs exploding, lighting up the sky.

Mammon was going to blow the British Isles to pieces.

The armor fired the bombs, and the surviving knights

were instantly vaporized. The explosion revealed countless

limbs and flesh flying, blood everywhere.

The gruesome sight made Shuri vomit.

He couldn’t believe he’d become a victim of those bombs.

It was all over.

Chapman saw his comrades explode and collapsed,

blaming himself. “I should have fought harder — we might have had a chance.”

“Hahaha, that was easy! You gave up resistance?

I’m enjoying the thrill of slaughter — firing spells to reap lives.”

The desperate knights wrote their wills in the bomb fire,

then buried them in dirt, waiting to die.

But this was just the passive side of the ice mountain.

Most didn’t even have time to write wills before being killed by Mammon’s barrage.

“It’s over. Someone must stand up.”

Shuri drew his sword, ready to provoke Mammon,

when a strong magic force swept the sky,

creating a black hole above the corpse of Sir Gregory.

“Stop,” Mammon ordered the clones, looking surprised.

“This magic — there’s a survivor?”

From the black net, massive amounts of magic flowed out,

gathering on Gregory’s body.

Such a large concentration of magic threatened even Mammon,

who wondered if the old man was absorbing the black hole’s magic.

Suddenly, the surge of magic might break the seal,

revealing the true nature of this anomaly.

Could it be Sir Gregory?

Chapman’s eyes rekindled with hope.

“It’s true — the guild master didn’t lie.

He said he reached the limit but passed on the magic,

stopping time on his body to survive,

though his power hasn’t improved for years due to the black hole absorbing it.

I thought he was joking, but now I see.”

Chapman couldn’t understand how the strongest mage

could have such a side effect.

“That’s why his power fluctuates — the black hole eats his magic.

But magic can be recovered. I’ve learned the ancient demon king’s secret.”

Shuri stroked his beard, recalling Gregory’s teachings.

“He’s definitely going to fight to the death — using centuries of stored magic.

Once the time stops, he’ll face the end of his lifespan

and the side effects of the ancient magic.”

“The side effect is that the black hole eats your magic.

All magic has a price.”

Shuri paused, whispering, “The guild master told me about the ancient magic,

warning me about the punishment for reviving lost knowledge.

His black hole magic has a side effect — if I remember right,

it’s called ‘The Hero Behind the Mask.’”

title: Chapter 62 — Newborn Body
content:
Chapter 62 — Newborn Body

Volume 30 · Chapter 62

“It’s true. Besides the guild master, I’ve met other practitioners of ancient magic, and they all suffer from side effects to some degree.

The Twelfth Thorn Knight, Mr. Cladi, is a close friend of the guild master, and he’s also studied ancient magic. He has side effects too.

This kind of thing seems irreversible. If you want to learn the power of the ancient ancestors, you must pay a price.” Wylan spoke with a serious expression, implying that the rule of equivalent exchange always exists when trading certain costs for power.

“Mr. Cladi also practices ancient magic?” Chapman recalled, having only heard that Cladi possessed the power to instantly strengthen the weak. “Why is ancient magic so special? I see so many magicians who are perfectly normal.”

“You can guess. Who were the spells and martial arts created by the ancient ancestors meant to fight against?” Wylan asked rhetorically.

Chapman furrowed his brow. Although his knowledge was limited, he sensed a clue. “Could it be against the ancient…”

“You’re right. They were created to fight against the gods who ruled the world in ancient times. The oppressed ancestors developed these spells and martial arts to rebel. Calling them ‘god-slaying skills’ isn’t inaccurate.” Wylan paused, his expression grave. “It’s normal to pay a price to control god-slaying power, but the guild master’s side effect is a bit too embarrassing.”

“I see.” Chapman勉强 understood Wylan’s explanation, but he couldn’t help but wonder what other costs there were besides turning into a woman. If the price were too severe, it would indeed be an evil thing, which is why Master Gregory advised against learning it.

“The guild master hid this for so long, but in the end, he couldn’t escape the fate of gender reversal. And after unleashing all his power, I wonder how many years he has left to live.” Wylan’s tone was melancholic, guessing that Gregory’s lifespan was likely less than five years. In such a short time, expecting the immature Alia to inherit his legacy would be difficult.

A massive black hole swirled in the sky, pouring vast amounts of mana into Gregory’s corpse, returning all the magic stored over a hundred years.

“What a rich supply of mana. That old guy, he really surprised me.” Mammon couldn’t help but take the situation more seriously. Infusing such a large amount of mana into a single person would surely boost their power significantly!

Crackling sounds of air shattering echoed as Gregory’s skin gradually turned black and dry, eventually cracking open entirely.

The fragments of skin fell like a broken eggshell, revealing the life within — a new beginning.

A slender arm emerged first, its white skin as soft as a baby’s. At first glance, this did not belong to the aged Gregory; it was clearly a woman’s arm.

“Ah! This, this…” Chapman swallowed nervously, his heart racing. Just looking at this arm confirmed that what Wylan said was true!

From the withered, shattered corpse of Gregory, a young woman slowly sat up. She appeared to be in her twenties, with long black hair cascading like a waterfall, reaching just past her hips. Her features were only vaguely similar to the old man’s.

The young woman was completely naked, her empty eyes regaining some luster as she looked around, clearly disoriented by her surroundings.

“Is this Master Gregory?” Chapman stared at the naked woman curled on the ground, his face flushing involuntarily. He was stunned, struggling to believe that this was the esteemed Purple Gold Adventurer.

“It must be him. I’m too familiar with him. Even the aura of his mana is the same.” Wylan’s face darkened as he looked at the naked, reborn guild master, unable to control the nosebleed that started to flow.

“Hey! You’re bleeding from your nose. Are you okay?” Chapman asked, concerned.

“Ah, sorry. I must be too excited.” Wylan quickly wiped the blood, embarrassed.

“You must have some evil thoughts, right? That’s your guild master! He was always a kind old man, and you’re… you’re…” Chapman looked at Wylan with disapproval, struggling to find the words. “You’re a shameless pervert, Sir Wylan!”

“Shut up! How can you say that? Mr. Chapman, control yourself. Look at your face — it’s red as a monkey’s butt!” Wylan retorted angrily.

“I…” Chapman, feeling guilty, tried to explain. “I always blush when I see naked women. It’s an involuntary reaction — perfectly normal!”

“Me too!” Wylan defended himself while bleeding. “I’ve always dreamed of working under a beautiful boss. Now that dream has come true, and I’m bleeding from excitement. What’s the problem?”

The two men, both overwhelmed by their reactions, glared at each other, realizing there was no point in accusing one another. After all, this was Master Gregory — a real old man before. Thinking of this calmed their agitated minds.

Chapman: “No matter what, that’s the esteemed Master Gregory, right?”

Wylan: “Yeah, yeah. No matter what the guild master looks like, it won’t shake my respect for him. But this new look is definitely better — working under a beauty is a completely different feeling.”

Chapman: “You?!”

The reborn Gregory slowly stood up, ignoring the shocked stares of the knights as she stood naked in the cold wind.

She flexed her hands, trying to get used to her new, youthful body, which was clearly more agile and sensitive than her old one.

Looking down at her chest, she poked the new lumps with her fingers, feeling a headache coming on.

“Sigh. In the end, I couldn’t escape the side effects of ancient magic. All my efforts were in vain. To wake up, I had to reclaim all the mana swallowed by the black hole. If I had just kept maintaining my state, the stored mana would have been enough for immortality, and the side effects would have been avoided. What a shame…”

Gregory picked up her tattered gray robe and put it on, covering her naked body. Although she didn’t care much about the knights’ stares, she still had to consider the awkwardness of the situation.

Mammon’s voice echoed across the battlefield: “Your pressure has undergone a qualitative change, rising to a new level. You’re touching the heels of a pseudo-god. How does it feel? Do you think you’re different from the rest of the world?”

“Feel? There’s no big deal. It just gives me more confidence to drive you out of the kingdom.”

Gregory’s voice was no longer old; it was now a clear, feminine tone.

title: Chapter 63 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 63 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 30 · Chapter 63

“As the second-generation Demon Lord, Mammon was already a powerful pseudo-god from the moment he inherited the Third Demon Lord Palace. His control over divine power and raw strength are top-tier.

Although Gregory’s power has increased significantly after recovering, compared to Mammon, he is still a novice who can only pose minor threats.

Even within the same power level, Gregory and Mammon are not on the same plane — Mammon’s raw strength is far superior, an overwhelming advantage.

‘Does the Demon Lord plan to conquer the Kingdom of Britain with these toys? Your true body should still be in the Demon Lord Palace. If you came to me in person, I might fear you, but a group of clones trying to scare me is too condescending,’ Gregory said expressionlessly.

‘My preparations are foolproof. You don’t seem to understand what establishing a blood bond with me means. Each clone can achieve near-identical strength to my true body, and combined, they are even stronger than me. With your current power, you’re barely on par with one of my clones — but you’re facing a hundred thousand of them,’ Mammon paused, then asked, ‘I don’t have full confidence either, but facing a hundred thousand clones firing together, do you think you stand a chance?’

‘Sounds impressive, but the ancient magic I practice was created by our ancestors to fight the gods — it’s also effective against demons,’ Gregory said as he summoned his beloved staff. The wood on the staff instantly shattered, leaving only the dark red gem at the tip that amplifies magic power.

‘Arrogant! Let me see if you can actually block it!’

As soon as Mammon finished speaking, the chests of the hundred thousand demonic armor clones lit up with countless purple-black beams, all aimed at Gregory!

The violent pressure storm raged again, and the magic bullets wove into a dense barrage net, reminding everyone present of the despair they had felt before.

‘Watch out, President! Those magic bullets are very powerful!’ Wylan shouted in concern.

Boom boom boom — the prepared magic bullets were fired, all converging on Gregory’s single point — this was far more powerful than the random bombardment earlier!

Gregory’s expression turned serious. The dark red gem in his hand glowed brightly, and instantly, over thirty thousand small black holes appeared in front of him, absorbing the incoming magic bullets one-to-one.

Creating thirty thousand black holes for defense was already Gregory’s limit!

But Mammon’s clones were too numerous — even after absorbing thirty thousand concentrated magic bullets, seventy thousand were still heading toward Gregory!

The gem in Gregory’s hand began to spin, and the thirty thousand absorbed magic bullets were sent back through the black holes!

Rumble —

Explosions echoed across the sky, shaking the knights’ feet and creating a massive shockwave that distorted space and flattened the surrounding mountains.

It wasn’t just the thirty thousand magic bullets canceling each other out — Gregory used the explosion’s shockwave to form an invisible defense barrier, successfully withstanding the clones’ combined attack.

However, because Gregory’s power was significantly weaker than Mammon’s, he couldn’t block perfectly — many magic bullets still fell, but lost accuracy due to the explosion.

A few exploded near Gregory, but none were direct hits, and he narrowly escaped.

‘He blocked it? He really blocked it!’ Wylan was incredulous — he couldn’t fathom the president’s strength anymore!

Gregory stood in the firelight, appearing calm on the surface, but was actually drenched in sweat —

He had reached his limit, yet still couldn’t fully resist Mammon’s attack. Even touching the heels of a pseudo-god, he was no match for the Demon Lord.

‘Oh? Not bad — your magic is indeed tricky, but now...!’

Mammon was enraged by Gregory’s resistance and launched a second, even more ferocious attack without giving him time to recover.

In just a few blinks, a massive energy ball formed by a hundred thousand magic bullets hovered over the battlefield!

The entire area was enveloped by this super-large magic bullet, which appeared brighter than the sun to the knights, instantly evaporating all moisture from the ground. The air’s mana elements were not just turbulent — they were actually materializing and being sucked into the energy ball, making it grow larger.

‘Your black holes have a limit. If you want to see my true body, survive this attack, and I’ll grant you that chance!’

With Mammon’s taunt, the massive concentrated magic bullet descended, aiming to crush Gregory with overwhelming force.

Gregory sighed, knowing he was doomed — to challenge the King of Demons, one must be at least one level stronger.

He snapped his fingers, and black holes appeared under the surviving knights’ feet, teleporting them away.

‘Wylan, take the survivors and leave. Tell Queen Elizabeth that the Royal Army is defeated and cannot resist.’

Wylan, sinking into the black hole, asked anxiously, ‘What about you, President?’

‘I can leave anytime — I can’t beat Mammon, but he can’t trap me either.’ Gregory looked at the falling magic bullet and said firmly, ‘I need to stay here and buy time for those who are alive.’

‘But...’ Wylan was emotional but determined, ‘President, you must come back alive. Without you, I can’t handle that glutton Aria!’

‘I know.’

After sending the survivors away, Gregory raised the dark red gem and summoned an unprecedentedly large black hole.

The super-large magic bullet was slowly swallowed by the black hole, and the collision of forces caused spatial collapse, with electric sparks flashing in the sky.

As Mammon predicted, the black hole had a limit — it couldn’t absorb such a massive force.

Gregory gritted his teeth and held on, but the dark red gem cracked and shattered.

His newly regenerated body also began to collapse, bleeding from all orifices, and his internal organs were severely damaged —

In the palace, due to lack of personnel, the Rose Family knights took over the duties of the Thistle Knights to protect the queen.

Cecilia and Kyle did not go to the front lines to fight the demons directly, but they had to guard the palace to prevent demons from infiltrating.

Because of the previous demon night attack that killed two Thistle Knights, the palace defenses were now tighter — anyone approaching the queen, regardless of status, was subject to inspection.

Elizabeth stood on the palace lookout tower, shivering in the cold wind, anxiously awaiting news from the front.

The frequent explosions in the distance made her uneasy, and a sense of foreboding grew.

The eighth Thistle Knight, Catherine, was the queen’s personal guard. She had already set up over thirty protective barriers around the palace — if demons tried to sneak in again, they would be doomed.

Seeing Elizabeth trembling in the wind, Catherine approached and said, ‘Your Majesty, please go back and rest. I’ll handle this.’

‘No, I want to stay here,’ Elizabeth waved off Catherine’s offer.

Catherine thought for a moment and said reassuringly, ‘You don’t need to worry too much. Mesfield has the Sword of Kings and rushed to the battlefield immediately. We also have Master Gregory helping us. There shouldn’t be a problem — even a Demon Lord can’t defeat the combined strength of the kingdom.’

‘You don’t understand. The demons once dominated an era, surpassing all other races. As their king, he must have unexpected tricks,’ Elizabeth frowned, unsure what kind of determination the Greedy Demon Lord had brought to this war.

Suddenly, a massive explosion shook the sky —

Smoke and flames tore a hole in the clouds, and a mushroom-like black cloud rose, making the people in the capital think the apocalypse had arrived.

‘What is that...’ Elizabeth stared in shock, unsure what had happened on the battlefield.

The shockwave hit, knocking many defending Rose Knights off their feet.

‘Your Majesty!’

Catherine quickly shielded Elizabeth, struggling to keep her eyes open against the strong wind —

What kind of power was this? What was happening on the front lines?

After the shockwave subsided, Catherine turned to check on Elizabeth.

‘Your Majesty, are you okay? Injured?’

‘No... I’m fine, thank you,’ Elizabeth said, trying to stay calm — she couldn’t show weakness in front of the knights.

‘Bad news, Your Majesty!’ Cecilia and Kyle entered, ‘The latest report says the Royal Army has been defeated! Master Gregory is trying to hold off the demons!’

‘The citizens of the capital are being evacuated to Wales. Please leave with us immediately — time is running out!’ Kyle added urgently.

‘Defeated? But...’ Catherine was surprised — even with so many strong fighters, they couldn’t stop the Demon Lord? What kind of being were they fighting?

‘Yes, the losses are severe. Only a small group survived and were teleported here. Wylan said Master Gregory won’t last long, and the capital is no longer safe — we must evacuate,’ Kyle explained seriously.

‘Your Majesty, let’s go now. The demons will reach the palace soon, and it will be too late. Please don’t think about staying — if you die, the kingdom is truly lost. As long as you live, many will still follow you,’ Cecilia said, trying to suppress her anxiety.

Hearing this, Elizabeth felt a heavy blow — this defense had nearly exhausted the kingdom’s resources, and even the artifact left by the previous king couldn’t help. What could stop the kingdom from falling?

The Greedy Demon Lord would likely take the rest of the territory — it was only a matter of time.

Elizabeth’s vision darkened, and she almost fainted, but Catherine caught her.

‘Your Majesty, stay strong! It’s just one failure — we still have a chance!’

‘I’m fine, really. Thank you,’ Elizabeth steadied herself, forcing a smile.

‘There is good news — the Church and the Kingdom of France have formed an alliance and are on their way. If they break through the demon blockade at sea, they can support us, and the Greedy Demon Lord will be attacked from both sides — we can defeat them then,’ Cecilia said, offering hope.

‘Is that reliable?’ Catherine asked cautiously.

‘Yes, the priest from the London church sent me this message. The Church won’t abandon any believer of the Goddess,’ Cecilia said confidently.

‘Those clerics are usually annoying, but they’re reliable in a pinch. I might consider becoming a believer later,’ Kyle joked.

‘Then you’ll be kicked out of the Rose Family. Your loyalty should be to the Rose banner, not some god. I won’t allow my knights to worship anything else,’ Cecilia glared at him.

‘Sorry, I was joking,’ Kyle scratched his head, embarrassed.

‘Your Majesty, you heard that — it’s good news. Let’s retreat to Wales for now,’ Catherine suggested.

Elizabeth remained silent, not fooled by the “good news.” She understood the situation better than others — the support depended on breaking the sea blockade, and the Greedy Demon Lord wouldn’t have overlooked that.

The French and Church alliance would likely face something even more terrifying.

Just as Elizabeth suspected, Mammon had planned everything — the Sixth Demon Lord Palace, guarded by Mammon himself, awaited the alliance.

Elizabeth smiled optimistically, but inside she was deeply worried. No one understood the kingdom’s plight better than her — the capital, never lost before, was about to fall under her watch.

If only Merlin were here — perhaps he could help.

The story continues...

title: Chapter 1 — Escape
content:
Chapter 1 — Escape

Volume 31 · Chapter 1

The innermost room was especially mysterious, not only sealed by a magical barrier, but even the railings were made of the same material as the shackles used in the seal magic. Anyone imprisoned here would be strictly guarded; even if they possessed heavenly abilities outside, their power would be severely limited here, unable to exert any ability. This is the most mysterious prison of the Kingdom of Britain; normally those taken in are either strong individuals with utilitarian value, or political criminals with deep backgrounds. The former prince of the previous kingdom who attempted to overthrow British rule, Kopofeier, was imprisoned here, under strict surveillance every day. Because Elizabeth wanted to know the secrets of the former kingdom—why a dynasty that should have long collapsed rose overnight, having made contact with some extremely evil force and gained massive support—She was curious about this, hoping to learn what exactly had happened inside, perhaps to bring great benefit to the kingdom. However, no matter what methods Elizabeth used, Kopofeier refused to divulge even a bit of information, completely denying that the former kingdom had signed a contract with Hell, becoming lackeys of the undead. Faced with Kopofeier who would yield to neither soft nor hard measures, Elizabeth could only choose to imprison him, hoping time would make this remnant of the former kingdom change his mind. Yet Elizabeth never imagined that one day the capital would fall, occupied by demons.

In the cell, Kopofeier faced the wall, kneeling on the cold floor, muttering incoherently, “Ah~ Great Satan, I have done my best to follow your instructions, but the plan failed, ruined by that damned Elgin the Great Swordsman.” “Please rest assured, no matter how the human queen treats you, I swear I will never reveal even a hint of your secrets; I am willing to take all secrets to the grave, hoping you can continue to trust me.” “As for your army being wiped out, I feel deeply sorry; I never imagined that great swordsman’s strength would be so terrifying, showing no fear of the Burning Legion; even now, recalling it makes my heart race with dread. To accomplish your grand endeavor, that man must be on guard.”

A lot of time has passed, yet Merlin’s terrifying appearance still casts a huge psychological shadow over Kopofeier; whenever he recalls it, his whole body trembles and cold sweat pours forth. Kopofeier has awakened countless nights from his dreams, dreaming repeatedly of that terrifying great swordsman brandishing a blade and chasing him. He lamented sadly that he was born out of time; if that Elgin the Great Swordsman did not exist, the fallen former kingdom would have already been successfully revived by him!

Suddenly, from the far end of the southern corridor of the prison came a series of ragged breaths; a figure darted past, reeking of strong alcohol. Kopofeier turned his head in surprise, seeing the jailer who managed this prison fumbling along the far wall, his appearance highly abnormal. This jailer loved drink as his life; normally he was responsible for bringing Kopofeier something to eat, but each time it was moldy bread or rotten meat, as long as he didn’t starve. Kopofeier detested this man, yet he also feared provoking the drunkard and getting beaten; he hadn’t eaten anything all day, his stomach growling. “Can’t you give me something to eat?” “Shut up, old fool! Now isn’t the time to bother with you! If you’re hungry, eat your own shit!” The jailer heard Kopofeier’s voice and shouted furiously, “Just stay put here; before long the demons will gnaw your bones clean!” “Uh…” Kopofeier was startled by the jailer’s attitude, feeling it was worse than usual; he sensed something was off—had something happened outside? Demons? What demons? “I’m damned to have run into this; if I’d known I wouldn’t have drunk so much, now the main force has already withdrawn, only I am abandoned here—damn it! I don’t want to die…” The drunken jailer muttered curses under his breath, having located a brick in the wall, his face lit up with joy. He drew the dagger at his waist, pried the brick out completely, and reached into the wall to pull out a sack of gold coins! “Found it! These are all tips from visitors; I absolutely can’t lose them.” “Huh?” Kopofeier grew more suspicious, wondering why the jailer was acting like he was fleeing. The jailer at the tavern walked up to Kopofeier’s cell, grinning smugly, and said, “Just stay here and wait to die; guarding a guy like you gets me no profit, better you die early so I don’t waste my time.” “What’s happening out there?” Kopofeier asked tentatively. “You’ll find out soon.” The jailer flashed a mysterious smile, turned to leave, but his body suddenly froze; he stared wide‑eyed, trembling, and said— “Impossible… did I forget to lock the door when I came in?” “Damn it! Why am I so unlucky?!” “Don’t come near! Don’t come near!!” Accompanied by a howl, a sturdy figure lunged forward, ripping open the jailer who was paralyzed by fear, disemboweling him!

Kopofeier stared wide‑eyed in horror, his heart leaping to his throat; a pitch‑black creature with horns on its head greedily gnawed at the jailer’s flesh, emitting a sickening sound. “A… a demon?” A flood of questions surged through Kopofeier’s mind: why would a demon appear openly in the British capital? This was utterly abnormal! Yet Kopofeier, having seen great storms, quickly calmed; his eyes fixed on the jailer’s corpse, the key hanging from his waist within reach. He swallowed nervously, watching the ravenous demon feast, realizing that once the demon finished it would surely turn on him—if he didn’t flee, death was certain. Thus Kopofeier steeled himself, silently reaching through the iron bars, his heart pounding like a frantic drum, until he finally grasped the key to freedom. ◊ Freed, Kopofeier stumbled out of the prison, and what met his eyes was the British capital shrouded in flames, its peaceful visage vanished, replaced by a hellish landscape! Raging fire spread across the capital; those who couldn’t flee scattered in panic, while hungry demons circled the sky, ready to hunt humans. This was no longer the prosperous capital of Britain, but a hunting ground for demons. Seeing this, Kopofeier’s face darkened as he fell silent for a long moment, then he flung his arms wide and let out a wild, unrestrained laugh— “Hahahahaha!!!” “How wonderful! This is exactly the scene I dreamed of!” “Egbert that country bumpkin, who built his kingdom by deceiving hearts, finally got his comeuppance!” “The great lord of Hell did not abandon the former kingdom; Satan has always secretly blessed me!”

PSB Sorry, I’m fine; I just didn’t sleep for 24 hours yesterday, forcibly adjusted my biological clock to morning updates, and there will be an extra chapter later.

title: Chapter 2 — Viper (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 2 — Viper (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 31 · Chapter 2

On an unnamed small island somewhere in the Mediterranean, a dirty pirate slowly rowed a small boat to shore.
On the boat lay a priest bound tightly, shivering and curled up, constantly making a "wu wu" sound trying to call for help.
On the shore, another pirate with messy hair was responsible for reception, apparently doing something important.
On this desolate, uninhabited island, it was surprising that someone would come here.
The priest was roughly thrown onto the shore, immediately terrified, crawling like an earthworm, "wu wu!!!"
"You bastard actually found a priest? Where did you find him?" The messy-haired pirate was very surprised; this isolated island was remote, finding a priest wasn't easy.
"Around this island are places where birds don't even poop; finding a priest is really a hassle. I finally discovered a small fishing village, and the priest happened to live there, daily treating the fishermen's injuries. Without a word, I knocked him out with a stick and tied him up." The dirty pirate proudly said, feeling impressive. "Don't worry, this priest just woke up not long ago; he has no idea where we are."
"That's good; it seems the young master's eyes can be saved." The messy-haired pirate nodded.
"The young master's eyes were gouged out. Wanting to successfully transplant those monster-like eyes—will it succeed? At first glance, they aren't human eyes." The dirty pirate felt uneasy.
"What else can we do? This is the young master's decision; we shouldn't nitpick. Besides, if it succeeds, it'll be good for him." The messy-haired pirate paused, then continued,
"The young master is just an ordinary person with no talent for magic or battle aura; this has always been his regret. If he could gain the power of those eyes, successfully slay the great swordsman Elgin and avenge Redbeard captain, the plan would advance further!" "That's true. Since that hateful great swordsman killed two captains, our Redbeard pirate crew has been teetering on the edge of disbandment. If the young master hadn't returned in time to take over, we'd likely have scattered, each going home to farm."
The dirty pirate sighed.
"Yeah, back when our Redbeard pirate crew was mighty—wherever we went we plundered, we swept the seas unstoppable, even several kingdoms' navies couldn't handle us. But that's all in the past." The messy-haired pirate wore a nostalgic expression of past glory.
"With the young master's talent and ambition, he will surely lead us out of the slump." The dirty pirate full of confidence shifted the topic, asking, "But I don't understand why the captain originally cast the young master out?"
"You don't get it; this is the captain's love for the young master. We pirates are desperate souls with our heads hanging on our belts, not allowing any burden. The young master, being ordinary, is a drag on us, and kids could lose their lives at any moment." The messy-haired pirate recalled slowly, "Remember the captain sent the young master to a reliable old subordinate in the Ice Sea to be raised, and every year he sent a large amount of support funds. For an adoptive son with no blood relation, this is already benevolent and righteous. Surely the young master can feel the captain's love. Don't forget, the young master is an orphan; his wicked mother once placed him in a wooden tub and set him adrift at sea for who knows how long, nearly freezing to death. It was the captain himself who pulled him back from the brink of death. That the young master lives is a tremendous fortune."
I marveled in my heart—originally, the young master of Lochiri had such an extraordinary background!
"You're not an old pirate in the crew; many things you don't know. Don't go spreading the young master's business around, got it?" The messy-haired pirate gave a warning.
"Understood, I'll keep my mouth shut!" The dirty pirate bared his big teeth.
The messy-haired pirate looked down at the priest coldly and said, "Untie this priest; he can't run away anyway. Look how scared he is, he's about to piss himself~"
The dirty pirate responded, pulling out the smelly sock stuffed in the priest's mouth, grinning wickedly as he stared at him, "Priest?"
"Don't! Don't kill me! I have no money, I'm poor!" The elderly priest begged pitifully, mysteriously bound here, already scared silly.
"Don't be nervous; we won't harm you. We just need you to do a favor. After it's done, I'll send you back, how about that?" The dirty pirate said with a meaningful tone.
"What... what favor?" The priest asked anxiously.
"Help our young master Lochiri transplant a pair of eyes…"
◊
A few days later, in the crude wooden hut on the island, a group of pirates gathered.
Lochiri said nothing, sitting in the center of the crowd, his eyes covered with thick gauze.
It seemed after several days of slavery, the eye transplant basically succeeded, though it was unknown if problems would arise.
"Did it succeed?" The dirty pirate felt excited, "If our young master can't see, I'll chop off your head!"
"I... I" The priest wanted to cry but had no tears, feeling how unlucky he was, entangled by these pirates.
"Be quiet, don't disturb the priest. Even if it fails, it's fine—changing eyes for such a crazy thing, few would do it." The silent Lochiri suddenly spoke.
Upon hearing that, the priest breathed a sigh of relief, feeling this pirate was secretly more agreeable and polite, just wondering why he'd hang out with pirates.
"If we calculate the time, the gauze should be ready to remove. Although I can't guarantee success, logically there shouldn't be any problems."
"Quick! Quickly remove it, let us see!" The dirty pirate urged from the side.
The priest couldn't resist the pirates' urging, so he slowly unwound the gauze from Lochiri's eyes layer by layer.
Lochiri frowned, seeming to feel somewhat uncomfortable, hesitating to open his eyes.
"Now you can slowly open your eyes—can you see anything? If you can, that would be a great success."
As soon as the words fell, Lochiri suddenly opened his eyes—scarlet pupils, narrow and eerie, suddenly emitting strange otherworldly power!
The old priest's body instantly froze in place, beginning to petrify at a visible speed, gradually turning into a lifelike statue.
"No... no!!!"
The priest's completely petrified body twisted, his face showing fear and unease; even a world-class sculptor could hardly carve such a realistic feeling!
Seeing this horrifying scene, the pirates all turned their gaze away, too afraid to look at Lochiri, worrying they'd be the next unlucky one turned into an immobile stone.
Lochiri's eyes had been injured by Merlin, nearly blind; to see again and gain greater power, he chose to take the risk, gouging out the eyes of the Chaos King Medusa's head and having the priest transplant them onto himself.
Medusa's pupils once again emitted astonishing power; undoubtedly the transplant plan was a great success!
Lochiri showed a hint of mad laughter, using the brand-new Medusa eyes, he saw a world completely different from before.
Those scarlet eyes hiding killing intent were like the most deadly poisonous snake.

title: Chapter 3 — Wind Reversal
content:
Chapter 3 — Wind Reversal

Volume 31 · Chapter 3

Luo Qili obtained brand-new eyes, the power of Medusa continuously manifested, making him feel unprecedented **!

He had never felt that these pirate subordinates were so weak; he felt as if he was a predator at the top of the food chain.

With just a blink, Luo Qili could eliminate everyone present; few could resist the power from this other world.

“Is this the feeling of having power? So wonderful, hahaha”

Luo Qili looked at his own hands, let out a low laugh, and satisfiedly covered his eyes to prevent accidentally harming others.

“Everyone, turn around; I won't accidentally harm you.”

The pirates, uncertain, secretly glanced at Luo Qili; seeing that he had already covered his eyes, they immediately relaxed.

They all knew how powerful those petrifying eyes were; as long as you stared into them, you would instantly turn into stone!

“Young master, how does it feel?” the dirty pirate asked.

“Very good; this feeling of mastering power makes me addicted.” Luo Qili, with his eyes covered, seemed very excited.

“Could it be that you, young master, have confidence to defeat Elgin the great swordsman?” the dirty pirate's eyes lit up.

“As long as I can stare into his eyes, I have a good chance of killing him!” Luo Qili said with confidence,

Hearing Luo Qili speak with such confidence, the pirates' faces lit up with joy; they felt that their hard days were over, and that the young master would soon inherit Redbeard's will and resume fighting on the seas.

“With you, young master, saying that, what are we afraid of? Just follow you and it's fine. Should we now start looking everywhere for Elgin the great swordsman?”

“Don’t rush. To kill Elgin the great swordsman, we first need to strengthen our power. With our current state of barely having enough food, how can we even match him?” Luo Qili thought that the current preparation was insufficient; rushing to find Elgin would be like sending a head to the enemy.

“What then? Rob? Our crew is no longer as strong as before; even slightly stronger merchant ships are hard to deal with.” The dirty pirate was very upset, his scalp almost scratching to the point of bleeding.

“Do we, barefoot ones, fear those who wear shoes? Even if we don't rob passing merchant ships, we still have a chance to become rich overnight!” The messy pirate suddenly spoke.

“Oh? Do you have any idea?” Luo Qili asked curiously.

“I heard that the greedy Demon Lord of the demon race launched a war against Britain, fighting fiercely. Now the Third Demon Lord Palace is in a state of defensive emptiness. If we set our hearts firmly, we can definitely obtain a large amount of treasure. As far as I know, the greedy Demon Lord is the richest among the demon race, and his hoard of treasures is countless! If we succeed, our Redbeard pirate crew will soar to the skies!” The messy pirate spoke with a firm tone.

“Loot the Third Demon Lord Palace where the greedy Demon Lord is?” Luo Qili lazily sat on the chair, rested his face, and suddenly laughed.

“Sounds a bit interesting.”

◊

Britain's capital city, the chaotic slaughter had already been explained; the humans who had no time to escape were killed to the bone by the demons.

Britain's capital, with a history of over four hundred years, was occupied by demons overnight and became the territory of the Third Demon Lord Palace. This was not just the loss of a city; the capital represented royal sovereignty, and losing it symbolized the failure of the monarchy, greatly shaking the public's confidence in the British kingdom.

On the magnificent throne of the palace, the human figures were gone, replaced by ferocious demons. They curiously surveyed the surroundings, feeling somewhat uneasy about the new base.

Mamon's demon armor avatar openly sat on the throne that belonged to Elizabeth, and the joy of success made it very proud, believing it had become the new emperor of Britain.

Mamon believed that the fleeing Elizabeth would be unable to organize a stronger force again, and that the entire British territory would be annexed.

It was only a matter of time.

Through the magic mirror, the real Mamon had already seen all the situation in the Sixth Demon Lord Palace—

Mamon was delighted, laughed, and picked up a bottle of wine, the first step of the plan

has been completed. Next, just wait for other Demon Lords to join; the demon race's power will swarm out, making it even easier. Just lie down and count the money.

“Ouse, go get a wine glass yourself, join me for a drink; today is worth celebrating.”

“Congratulations, Your Majesty, on successfully occupying Britain's capital. The human royal family is scrambling in fear; they will lose all confidence, and the kingdom is now only name and no substance!” Ouse said with excitement. The victory of the defense brought great benefits, not only expanding the Third Demon Lord Palace's sphere of influence, but also severely damaging human confidence, and Mamon's influence in the Elders' Council would increase. Now who would still question the correctness of Mamon's external war? Perhaps now other Demon Lords are like ants on a hot pan, eager to join in and share a portion!

“That is natural; those who offend me will not have a good outcome!” Mamon smiled with a deep meaning.

“Other Demon Lords may now be envious, wishing to ignore the Elders' Council and join you in launching war. Unfortunately, if Lord Leviathan could cooperate obediently, not only would there be meat to eat, but also plenty to satisfy. Ouse sighed, thinking that it was all the other Demon Lords' lack of trust in Mamon; otherwise everyone could earn a full pot in the war.”

“Leviathan is a self-made victim; his hostility towards me is no less than any enemy. If he had even a little trust in me, he would fall into this fate.” Mamon's face was grim; he did not want to bring up Leviathan at this joyous moment.

“But Lord Leviathan, being a descendant of the first Demon Lord, I hope Your Majesty does not quarrel too harshly with him, for the seal of the Blood Pool is stable and concerns the survival of our entire demon race.” Ouse advised beside him.

You will also be seen by all demons as the sole leader, for you bravely broke the demon race's passive state of being attacked.” Ouse's eyes shone with reverence; in his eyes, Mamon had become a hero saving the demon race!

“You’re right.” Mamon raised his wine glass to Ouse, his gaze deep, thinking—

The stubborn conservative faction of the Elders' Council must have stopped arguing, right?

A few Demon Lords who insist on peace, if they don't join me, they will inevitably become a joke for the entire demon race.

It won’t be long before all of Britain's lands belong to me; even that artifact stone sword will be taken into my possession.

With both artifacts in hand, who can still fight me?

title: Chapter 4 — Problem Children
content:
Chapter 4 — Problem Children

Volume 31 · Chapter 4

“This organization was founded by the seven original Demon Lords to prevent any single demon palace from becoming too powerful and disrupting the internal balance of the demon race.

It also mediates internal disputes and stops reckless demons from leading the entire race down the wrong path.

If the demon race is compared to a large machine, the Council of Elders is the fuse that prevents a meltdown, the institution safeguarding against extinction.

The Council possesses the most powerful weapon against demons, the 'Seal Demon Jar'. Because of this, the Demon Lords fear the elders and dare not break the rules arbitrarily.

Without the Council, the Demon Lords would fight each other, and the demon race would likely collapse into fragmented factions.

Currently, the Council is in uproar, with members nearly coming to blows over who is right.

'Mammon has violated the rules set by the original Demon Lords by launching an external war. This is detrimental to us and will eventually drag us all into the conflict. Mammon must be punished for his actions!'

'You old-fashioned fools! Mammon is the savior of the demon race. Only he can pull us out of this downward spiral. Is passive defense the only correct strategy?'

'Exactly! Those humans are becoming more aggressive, frequently sending armies to harass the demon palaces. We must strike first!'

'The only ones attacking us are the Church of Light. Other human kingdoms are not involved. But Mammon's reckless war will alert these kingdoms. If they form a human alliance, we will suffer losses worse than the Holy War!'

The elders are split into two factions, arguing fiercely without reaching a consensus.

Because of the heavy losses from the war with the heavens, the original rule was for the demon race to adopt a defensive strategy. Mammon should be immediately imprisoned in the Seal Demon Jar for punishment.

However, the only surviving original Demon Lord, Belial, has suddenly begun supporting Mammon's actions, causing endless debate between the progressive and conservative factions.

Belial has significant influence in the Council, with many members being his students. While he cannot dictate the decision, his seniority allows him to disrupt the proceedings.

At the center of the Council is a seat for the Chief Judge, who summarizes the opinions of the majority and makes the final decision.

The old demon sitting there is very short, barely visible above the chair. His long white beard hangs to his waist as he closes the thick 'Demon Race Code'.

This old demon is named Caprio, a former gardener for the first Demon Lord, Lucifer, from a fallen noble family.

As a youth, Caprio had no combat ability but bravely fought in the war and survived. Through hard work, he became the Chief Judge of the Council in his old age, known for his fairness.

Despite his loyalty to the first palace, Caprio personally approved the exile of Lucifer III, demonstrating his impartiality.

Watching the arguing elders, Caprio slams the table in anger.

'Quiet down! This is the Council, not a marketplace! Your bickering solves nothing!'

Once everyone is silent, Caprio nods and clears his throat. 'According to the rules left by the original Demon Lords, Mammon has committed a serious crime. He launched an expansion war without authorization, seized the sixth palace, and caused Leviathan to disappear. These are grounds for imprisonment in the Seal Demon Jar. I have zero tolerance for those who ignore the Council. Furthermore, Asmodeus, Samael, and Beelzebub have all accused Mammon. Let's hear what the Demon Lords have to say.'

Behind Caprio are seven large mirrors, magical communication devices linked to each palace.

Three mirrors light up: Lust, Wrath, and Gluttony.

'How do I use this mirror?' Samael, the Wrath Demon, is so muscular that only his chest is visible.

The elders stare uncomfortably at the male demon's bare chest.

Samael fiddles with the device before stepping back, revealing his face — or rather, his helmet.

He removes the helmet to show a neck with no head. 'Ah, I forgot. I don't have a head. No wonder I can't figure this out.'

An elder with a brain aneurysm shouts, 'Samael! Put your clothes on! No one wants to see your muscles! As a Demon Lord, you must maintain your dignity! Don't run around naked in public! It embarrasses the entire race!'

'Sister, why haven't you come back? Without my sister, I feel like I'm dying!' Beelzebub cries, clutching a pillow with his sister Miranda's image.

Because Miranda is helping the first palace maintain the blood pool seal, Beelzebub cannot see her until Lilith returns.

His tears and snot soak the pillow as he wails, 'Sister, come back! I miss you! I'll do anything if you stay!'

The brain-aneurysm elder says, 'Beelzebub! Be strong! You are a Demon Lord! Don't be so weak! No matter how much you love your sister, this is unacceptable! You must show the ferocity and coldness of a demon king! Stop making a fool of yourself!'

'Hmm? I haven't worn these stockings long, and they're already tearing. Unpleasant.' Asmodeus looks at his damaged black stockings with displeasure.

He had dressed up for the meeting, and any imperfection annoys him.

'Kill the tailor who made these. He's useless.'

The brain-aneurysm elder exclaims, 'Asmodeus! What are you wearing? You are a male Demon Lord! Don't dress like a street vendor! It's shameful! You are insulting the image of demons!'

'Oh, it's Elder Hagu. How's your brain aneurysm? Your son gave me all your wealth to dine with me. Can you still afford to eat?' Asmodeus teases, waving his fan.

'You!' Hagu explodes and dies from the shock.

'Sigh,' Caprio wipes his sweat. 'Why are the second-generation Demon Lords such problem children?'

title: Chapter 5 — First Demon Lord Belial (Monthly Ticket Bonus Update)
content:
Chapter 5 — First Demon Lord Belial (Monthly Ticket Bonus Update)

Volume 31 · Chapter 5

“I'm furious.”

“Cough, cough. I ask that the Demon Lord Majesties express their opinions. The Council of Elders is currently unable to provide a satisfactory response regarding Mammon's unauthorized declaration of war.” Capriolo spoke with a serious expression, hoping the three Demon Lords would take the matter seriously.

Asmodeus straightened his clothing. “I declare my position. I believe Mammon's actions are too dangerous and will drag the entire demon race into the quagmire of war. I suspect he intends to incite a second Holy War, but we suffered significant setbacks in the first one, as I'm sure the elders remember. We cannot afford to lose. To prevent the worst-case scenario, I suggest imprisoning Mammon in the Demon-Sealing Urn. As for his Third Demon Lord Palace? Since Mammon has no siblings or offspring, we should ask Beelzebub's sister to manage it.”

“What!? My adorable sister again! Does she think my sister is a tool? I will never agree. Whoever dares to take Miranda away from me, I'll rip their head off!” Beelzebub exploded in anger. He had only agreed to help manage the First Demon Lord Palace as a favor to Merlin for his assistance in the Kingdom of France.

“Don't be so stingy. There are plenty of female demons more capable than your sister. Why are you so obsessed with your own sibling? Honestly, it's a bit disgusting.” Asmodeus waved his fan.

“Disgusting? You dare call me disgusting? You perverted freak, spit!” Beelzebub spat on the mirror, but since the two palaces were separated by a vast distance, it had no effect on Asmodeus.

“What is Lord Beelzebub's opinion?” Capriolo turned to the enraged Beelzebub.

“I do not support Mammon's war. He's always been a sly, fat coward. He's probably just trying to drag us all down with him. I don't care about the punishment; I'd love to see Mammon get his ass kicked by the humans and come crawling back to apologize. After all, excluding all other factors, Mammon is the weakest of the Demon Lords. And...” Beelzebub paused, taking a deep breath, “I will not let my sister Miranda clean up Mammon's mess! Do you elders understand me?”

“Yes.” Capriolo nodded, then turned to the silent Wrath Demon Lord. “Lord Samael, what is your opinion?”

“Asking me is useless. Thinking is a luxury for me, since I lost my head.” Samael touched the empty space at his neck, wondering how he had lost his skull. “However, I do not like Mammon's behavior. Those who do not follow the rules must be punished. My father and the other original Demon Lords established the rules for the demon race. Anyone who challenges them is my enemy.”

“I see.” Capriolo nodded, understanding Samael's stance. He then addressed the entire council. “The opinions of the three Demon Lords are clear. You have all heard them. While I hate to admit it, the era of our dominance is over. Attempting to expand outward is extremely disadvantageous for us. Therefore, we should punish Mammon and maintain the defensive strategy set by the original Demon Lords.”

The fact that all three Demon Lords shared the same opinion carried significant weight, causing the conservative elders to breathe a sigh of relief. If a full-scale war like the first Holy War were to break out, the demon race would have to risk everything, and defeat would mean extinction.

Suddenly, the mirror on the far right lit up, connecting to the Seventh Demon Lord Palace.

“Capriolo, are you serious when you say our era is over?”

The aged voice of Belial echoed through the room, capturing the attention of all the elders. As the only surviving original Demon Lord and a founder of the Council, he was a legendary figure not to be taken lightly. Even the second-generation Demon Lords—Samael, Asmodeus, and Beelzebub—could not help but shift uncomfortably in his presence. They were mere children compared to this ancient being, the most senior member of the demon race.

title: Chapter 5 — First Demon Lord Belial (Monthly Vote Bonus, Part 2)
content:
Chapter 5 — First Demon Lord Belial (Monthly Vote Bonus, Part 2)

Volume 31 · Chapter 5

The aura of the First Demon Lord was too overwhelming, far beyond what the other young Demon Lords could compare to.

"We have simply turned a new page; it does not mean our era has passed, do you understand?" Bael's authoritative voice echoed through the council of elders. In the mirror, he sat on a weathered stone throne, leaning on a cane, dressed impeccably in a suit and tie, his hair combed meticulously, like an old gentleman. However, due to the dim lighting, his expression and features were indistinct.

"Understood, understood," Caprio said nervously, fidgeting with his long white beard.

"Although prosperity has departed from us, who can be certain that new prosperity will not descend upon us? Can the elders present be certain?" Bael's gaze swept over all the demons below.

The conservative faction, who had been clamoring for peace, lowered their heads in unison, daring not to confront Bael. Even Caprio chose silence at this moment, offering no objections.

After reprimanding the elders, Bael suddenly turned to the other three Demon Lords. "You three young upstarts, have you been living too comfortably, forgetting that we are constantly under the dual threat of humans and the heavens? I witnessed with my own eyes how your predecessors fought to the death against the saints, using their flesh and blood to protect the last embers of the demon race. And you? You have not inherited even a shred of the backbone of those who passed away. You only think about living better for yourselves. Comfort has truly worn down your teeth, causing you to lose the ambition you should have. To be honest, in terms of bloody combat, each of you is stronger than little Mammon, but in terms of capability, you are not even half as good as him."

Samuel: "I don't have a brain, you know."

Asmodeus: "We are also considering the overall interests of the demon race, Uncle Bael."

Beelzebub: "Are you talking to me in that lecturing tone!? Don't act like an old man trying to show off your experience in front of me. I don't buy that! Stop whining through the mirror! If you're not satisfied, come out of the Demon Lord Palace and let's settle this in person!"

"Oh~, only when you're angry do I remember your father. But you truly don't possess any of your father's other virtues." Bael spoke in a teasing tone.

"What did you say? Just because you fought alongside my father, what's so great about that! &*#◎￥%丨" Beelzebub, furious, began pounding the mirror, his mouth spewing profanities.

[Qiu Shu Bang is the only site with the fastest updates for this novel]

Bael ignored Beelzebub, treating it as a child cursing in the street. He changed the subject, saying, "Don't think I spend most of my time sleeping; I am fully aware of every move the demon race makes. You claim to be considering the overall interests of the demon race, but have you ever thought about how long we have been confined within the Demon Lord Palace? The number of demons increases every day. We need more land and resources to survive. If we don't expand outward, do you have any other way to feed the ever-growing population of demons?"

"That doesn't mean we should solve it through war, right? Isn't Mammon's approach binding the entire demon race to his war cart?" Asmodeus said indirectly.

"Yes, yes, Great Demon Lord Bael, if Mammon fails, it will have a tremendous impact on us. We cannot bear that cost." Caprio's expression grew more serious.

"You are overestimating humans. Without the protection of the heavens, humans are just a group of mice that can be crushed at will. We have been biding our time for so long, and the power we have accumulated is already enough to replace humans. Mammon is not a fool; he simply took a step ahead of all of you present." Bael rubbed the cane in his hands, speaking with profound meaning—

"I just received news that Mammon has successfully occupied the capital of Britain."

"The royal family has fled with a large number of people. This kingdom is already a dead man walking. It is only a matter of time before it is incorporated into our demon race's territory."

"Regarding this news"

"What are your thoughts, you young Demon Lords?"

title: Chapter 6 — Too Late
content:
Chapter 6 — Too Late

Volume 31 · Chapter 6

“The Third Demon Lord Palace conquered the Kingdom of Britannia single-handedly in such a short time? As far as I know, Britannia is no small country.”

“Since Lord Belial announced it, the news must be accurate. Humans aren’t as strong as we thought — they’re practically defenseless!”

“With the royal city captured by Lord Mammon, doesn’t that mean the entire Kingdom of Britannia will be devoured by the Third Demon Lord Palace?”

The elders debated endlessly, Mammon’s victory acting like a shot of adrenaline that sent the entire demon race into a frenzy.

Once they learned Mammon was the first to seize the prize, how could other demon lords remain idle?

The major powers of the demon race would transform into hungry wolves, hunting humans relentlessly and expanding their territories.

The radical elders were overjoyed — Mammon’s win meant the era of demons being on the defensive was over.

But the conservative elders remained skeptical, doubting the truth of the news and fearing Mammon’s reckless actions might trigger a full-scale holy war between humans and demons.

“Lord Belial, is all this true?” Capriolo asked, sweating.

“Would I lie about something that affects the future of our race? Mammon’s subordinates are already treating the royal palace of Britannia as a playground, shipping its wealth back to the Third Demon Lord Palace.” Belial’s tone brooked no argument.

“This…”

Capriolo lowered his head — Mammon’s victory was the final straw for the demon race’s conservative faction.

The radicals gained immense power, and the entire demon world was enveloped in war fever.

Moreover, the defensive strategy had been set by the seven original rulers. Belial, as one of them, advocating for expansion, dealt a heavy blow to the conservatives.

“So, Lord Belial supports Mammon’s external expansion?”

“No,” Belial replied firmly from the shadows of the mirror. “I support the entire demon race expanding outward now, completely abandoning the old defensive strategy.”

“What?!?” Capriolo gasped. “Lord Belial, do you understand what it means for the whole demon race to expand?”

“Of course — it’s the Second Holy War!” Belial paused, then addressed all the elders: “Our days of cowering in the demon palaces while humans harass us are over. The era has abandoned the lowly humans. It’s time to reclaim what was once ours.”

The radicals erupted in cheers — Belial’s stance aligned perfectly with theirs.

The frequent crusades by the human church had long fueled anger among demons, who dreamed of teaching humans a painful lesson.

“If we go to full war, can the demon race afford to lose? Have you considered the consequences?” Capriolo frowned, believing expansion was too risky.

“Humans are just vassals of the heavens — not our true enemies. We’re unlikely to lose against them.” Belial said calmly.

“But what if our activity draws attention from the heavens? If the holy war begins, the saints might intervene again!” Capriolo worried.

“Capriolo, you’re ignorant. Do you think the gates between heaven and earth open easily? Even if we enslave all humans, the heavens won’t open wide and send armies like last time. Do you think only we suffered in the last holy war?” Belial retorted condescendingly.

The radicals shouted their agreement — clearly, Capriolo couldn’t hold back the demons from their path.

“You stubborn fools should wake up. The defensive strategy was only temporary. With our current strength, we no longer need it. Excessive comfort is dangerous — it erodes our spirit, turning us into hedonistic wastes. We need a war to restore our confidence.” Belial softened his tone, urging them: “Vote now, Capriolo. Let the council decide.”

The demon elders below were already excited — neutrals were shifting to support expansion, leaving conservatives as the minority.

“This moment has finally arrived! We must make those arrogant humans pay — show them who rules this world!”

“The Church of Light killed our children without mercy — we must return the favor, eye for eye!”

“Undoubtedly, Mammon is the most excellent among us. He’s set the example — the end of humans is near!”

Capriolo looked at the passionate elders and sighed. “There’s no need to vote, Lord Belial…”

“Then from now on, any demon who opposes or interferes with the demon race’s expansion will be considered a traitor to our revival and punished accordingly — agreed?” Belial said darkly.

“This is the will of the entire demon race — I have no objection,” Capriolo conceded, knowing he couldn’t stop this as just the arbiter.

“What about you three? Still think preserving peace is important? If you don’t fight while young, there’s no future. Act fast — or Mammon will eat everything and leave you nothing,” Belial joked, his image fading from the mirror.

Asmodeus, Beelzebub, and Samael remained silent, their moods complex.

Finally, Asmodeus spoke: “What do you think?”

“I don’t like war — I just want my head back,” Samael said, uninterested in fighting but eager to stop being headless.

“Beelzebub?” Asmodeus pressed.

“What else? Prepare the army and join the Second Holy War. We can’t let Mammon hog all the spoils,” Beelzebub decided, then asked, “You’re in, right, Asmodeus?”

◊

In the Mediterranean, a merchant ship sailed toward the Rothschild family’s island.

Due to the war between demons and Britannia, sea trade was crippled — even boat fares were ten times normal.

The First Demon Lord Palace’s intelligence officer, Xiu, stood on deck, dressed as a traveler with coat and hat, hiding his identity.

He didn’t want trouble in these tense times — human hatred for demons was at an all-time high.

Xiu gazed at the horizon, eager to reach the Rothschilds and inform Merlin of the demon situation.

Suddenly, a black crow landed on his shoulder — a sign of urgent contact.

As an intelligence officer, Xiu had spies across the demon world, communicating via crows.

He read the message and paled — the Second Holy War had begun!

All demon forces would unite against humans, and dissenters would be treated as traitors.

“This is bad! The tide is turning faster than I expected. Even if I find the lord, it’s too late to stop this. If he intervenes, he’ll be labeled a traitor.”

title: Chapter 7 — Asgard Ruins
content:
Chapter 7 — Asgard Ruins

Volume 31 · Chapter 7

Merlin woke from his coma, feeling parched and aching all over.
He rubbed his eyes, looked around, and unexpectedly discovered he was in a world completely different from the outside—a—vast ruin, with nothing but the remains of ancient buildings before his eyes! Towering stone pillars stood straight up to the sky, as if this place had once been a temple?
Half of the ruin's broken walls were buried in yellow sand, but from the exquisite carvings and magnificent building complexes, one could still glimpse how prosperous it once was!
Strangely, there was something like a "sun" in the sky, not as scorching as the real sun, but with a comfortable temperature.
It was a huge rotating glass sphere, emitting intense white light that illuminated everywhere, as if it had endless energy, keeping this world in perpetual daylight?
Beneath that "sun" stood an unparalleled towering giant tree, so immense that human imagination could hardly picture such a tree!
Soaring into the clouds, looking up you couldn't see the top; before the giant tree, Merlin was no longer just an ant—he was barely a speck of dust one could barely make out!
Unfortunately, this giant tree had long lost its life and withered away, leaving only lifeless branches stretching underground, with no sign of where its roots were.
The giant tree before Merlin's eyes was even larger than he imagined; perhaps only the topmost branch protrudes from this land, while the main body of the tree still lies underground!
"What the hell is this place? Did I get it wrong? Could it really be the dwelling of the ancient gods, the ruins of Asgard...?"
Merlin could hardly believe his eyes; he nervously swallowed saliva, thinking it wasn't urgent to figure out the situation right now—first priority was to find everyone.
So Merlin lowered his head and searched in the sand; fortunately, not far away he found Lilith lying motionless on the ground.
Before being sucked into the gods' relic, Lilith had been gripping Merlin tightly, so it was natural they were close.
"Lilith! Lilith, are you okay?"
Merlin hurriedly lifted his sister from the sand, shaking her little face repeatedly, feeling very worried.
Lilith slowly woke up, exhausted, on the verge of death, saying, "Brother... brother... I... I can't hold on..."
"Hey! Don't joke! You're not made of glass!" Merlin said sternly, examining her for a while but seeing no injury; perhaps she had suffered some mental harm in the gods' relic?
"I... I only have one wish left," Lilith gave a bitter smile, tears glistening, "Before I die, brother, can you kiss me?"
Merlin's face darkened instantly; he slapped her face hard with a big palm, saying, "I see you're daydreaming—be realistic!"
"Wuwu! Brother is a big idiot! I'm about to die and you won't grant my wish! Is there a more cold-hearted brother than you!?" Lilith gritted her teeth, jumped up in anger.
"You're not exactly lacking spirit; where does the dying look come from?" Merlin said, sweating.
"I don't care!" Lilith opened her mouth, biting his arm weakly to vent her anger.
Merlin frowned, used to Lilith's temper, soothed, "Stay quiet; we're in an unknown place, there might be danger—first we need to find the others."
Merlin thought, "Pudum, Jacob, and those three vampires—where did they go? Didn't they fly far away? That would be troublesome." He felt a headache; the vampires' life or death didn't matter, but Pudum and Jacob themselves needed more looking after.
Suddenly, a sandbag bulged in front of Lilith, as if some monster were about to burst out.
This frightened Lilith; she hid behind Merlin, obviously noticing the strangeness of this world.
"Brother! There's a monster!"
"Huh?" Merlin instinctively gripped the demon sword Banri Garan at his waist, on guard; this was originally the domain of the ancient gods—who could say no ancient god had survived?
"Wow! Pudum successfully crawled out from layers of sand, almost suffocated inside, he spat out the fool from his mouth: 'Ptooey! Finally out! I thought I would die holding my breath...'"
