"Pudum, it's you," Merlin said expressionlessly, "Good, it was just a false alarm; I feel a bit relieved."
"Your Majesty! You're safe, that's great! Before being sucked in here, I saw you being restrained by the North Sea Giant Monster; I thought Pudum seeing you safe would be overjoyed."
"Shut up! You bastard, appearing suddenly without a heads-up just scared me! Go die! Go die! Go die!" Lilith lifted her leg and kicked Pudum's butt.
"Sorry, I didn't think that much," Pudum said embarrassedly, scratching his sand-covered hair, looking around, and asked, "Where is Lord Leviathan? Why don't I see him?"
Speaking of Leviathan, Merlin's expression shifted slightly; not feeling great, but he honestly said, "To bring me in, it failed to arrive here and was instead eaten alive by the North Sea Giant Monster."
"Lord Leviathan met with disaster!?" Pudum exclaimed, having not seen Leviathan push Merlin away, himself sucking into the Kraken's blood pool big mouth; hearing this, he was shocked: "This is no small matter; if Lord Leviathan has an accident, the whole demon race will be severely affected."
Lilith crossed her arms, saying, "That Leviathan guy was just a stray dog, taken in by my brother; repaying him is fine, no big deal."
"Don't say that, Lilith," Merlin said sternly, "I also feel regret for Leviathan; it's a fact that it saved me at the last moment; no matter what, I will help it fulfill its last wish—that's all I can do—but for now, we must focus on surviving."
"Your Majesty said......"
Pudum nodded in agreement, began observing his surroundings: many towering stone pillars made him sigh repeatedly.
What great civilization once existed here, yet vanished overnight; able to build such a majestic city, now people probably can't achieve that!
Pudum gazed at the sky, instantly became excited, delightedly turned to Merlin and said:
"That must be the sun from myth, handcrafted by the ancient gods; it never falls, letting the gods bask in eternal sunlight!"
"Exactly! This is the residence of the ancient gods!"
"Your Majesty, look at that huge towering giant tree; if I'm not mistaken, eighty percent it's the world tree that once built the ancient world!"
"This is so exciting! The land beneath our feet has also been trodden by the demon race's prophet!"
"To be able to step on the same land as the great prophet, breathe the same air—what an honor!"

title: Chapter 8 — Desert Ship
content:
Chapter 8 — Desert Ship

Volume 31 · Chapter 8

The rotating glass ball caused a moment of surprise in his heart. Could the sun also be created? How powerful must the ancient gods have been?

"You're muttering to yourself again?" Lilith's left eyebrow twitched in anger as she struggled to understand Pudom's enthusiasm for studying demon race history.★首★发★EZ看书★

"Lilith, we're standing in a place our ancestors once visited! Isn't that exciting enough?" Pudom's hand pressed against his chest as his heart pounded with excitement.

"And then?" Lilith tilted her head, unwilling to delve into complicated history.

"Look at that ancient tree that once bore the world. Now it's withered and dead. It was the work of that prophet. He personally cut the roots, bringing destruction to the high and mighty ancient gods. He freed the world from their control. Our prophet was the greatest contributor! Even the groups that have always been hostile to us don't hesitate to praise the prophet's achievements in the records!" Pudom took a deep breath, gazing at the magnificent tree, imagining the prophet's battles with the ancient gods centuries ago. How majestic that must have been. "If the prophet were still alive, our demon race would be invincible. Who would dare challenge us?"

Lilith looked at Merlin beside her and whispered, "Brother, don't you think Pudom is a bit too old-fashioned? He's just like an elder."

"There's nothing strange about it. Pudom has been the secretary in the Demon Lord Palace for a long time. He just likes to study these things." Merlin replied calmly, listening to Pudom's narration. The giant tree over there is frequently mentioned in various documents. It's called the World Tree, said to be the origin of all things, a sacred object!

Unfortunately, it shows no signs of life. At first glance, it's just a large, rotten tree. What must it have looked like when it was lush and full of life?

What was the prophet's background? His actions had such a profound impact on the world that his shadow can still be seen everywhere now.

Pudom interrupted Merlin's thoughts and said loudly, "According to legend, the one-eyed king of the gods, Odin, lived at the top of the World Tree. If we want to find valuable things, we must go up there!"

"Go up?" Merlin's head ached immediately, looking at the World Tree that stretched endlessly into the clouds. His heart sank at the thought of the effort required to climb it. After all, no one's magic power and physical strength are limitless.

"That's too high, isn't it?" Lilith gazed at the World Tree that pierced the clouds, feeling even more fatigued.

"If we don't go up and see, aren't we wasting our time? The garden where the king of the gods resides is something many people dream of seeing! Now the opportunity is right in front of us!" Pudom's eyes sparkled with excitement as his strong desire to learn drove him.

"I think it's a bit too demanding." Merlin also wanted to go, but the conditions were too harsh.

Suddenly, a familiar voice echoed from behind Merlin.

"You finally woke up? It's not easy to find you."

Lamia, along with her subordinates Vadiye and Mahamud, walked toward them, followed by Jacob, who was timidly.

They had woken up a few days earlier than Merlin and his group and had not rushed to look for others. Instead, they had thoroughly searched the surrounding area.

This was Lamia's personal initiative. She wanted to search the area before being spotted by demons, in case there were valuable treasures she could secretly acquire.

After all, this was a place where ancient gods once lived, yet not even a single gold coin was found?

Disappointed, Lamia had to bring her two subordinates to look for the traces of demons, picking up Jacob, who was hiding in a jar pretending to be dead.

If not for the vampires' heightened sensitivity to human scent, they might not have discovered Jacob.

Lamia's decision to actively seek out demons to reunite was not out of "teamwork" considerations. She had witnessed the strength of Merlin and his group and believed they would be valuable allies.

In this dangerous place filled with unknown dangers, having strong allies would be extremely important!

"What is it? You found us? You really have the foresight to come here, don't you? You've always been reluctant to contribute." Lilith scoffed, not liking the three vampires.

"Are you saying we haven't contributed? What can we do if we're just following you, brother?" Lilith said with disdain.

"That's called contribution? You're just following me, aren't you?" Lilith said with disdain.

"Enough of this. Let's not dwell on it." Lamia calmed her subordinates, not bothering to argue with Lilith. Her value was not even a fraction of her brother's.

"Merlin!!!" Jacob saw Merlin suddenly and burst into tears, hugging his leg tightly. He had been in constant fear for days, not even daring to sleep, and was relieved to be found. The three vampires had threatened to drain his blood. "Woo, I'm so relieved to see you. I've been in constant fear these days, not even daring to sleep. I was almost picked up by them, and they even said they would drink my blood. Woo."

"That's right?" Merlin didn't find it surprising at all. After all, Jacob was a tasty human in the eyes of vampires. "If we're too hungry, we might even cut you open. There's no way around it. In the whole team, you're the only one who looks somewhat edible."

"Uh! ! !" Jacob was startled and quickly hid on the side, trembling. "Don't say that, Merlin, I've always respected you from the bottom of my heart. How could you possibly cut me open? Ha, ha, ha."

"If you keep making noise, I might just cut you open. To be honest, the food we found has already been thrown into the sea, and we're still a bit hungry." Merlin smiled kindly at Jacob.

"! ! !" Jacob quickly covered his mouth, thinking, "Oh no, these hungry wolves are not reliable! I've become walking food!"

Merlin looked at Lamia and said without expression, "Welcome back, Lamia. Although we have successfully entered the ruins of the gods, there are still unknown dangers. I believe we need to continue cooperating."

"I also think so, Magic King, no, should I call you Demon Lord?" Lamia remained calm on the surface but was filled with distrust in her eyes.

"It doesn't matter what you call me. That's not important. I'm sure Lamia has been here for a few days already, right? Have you searched the area thoroughly? Have you found anything?" Merlin politely asked Lamia if she had discovered any valuable items.

Lamia glanced at Merlin, understanding the meaning behind his words. She scoffed coldly and truthfully said,

"If I had found something significant, why would I come back to find you? Wouldn't it be better for me to take it and leave?"

"I've searched all the surrounding areas, and there's nothing. This place is like a lifeless wasteland."

"However, I found a strange ship while coming here, stopped in the yellow sand about a hundred miles away."

title: Chapter 9 — Flying Ship
content:
Chapter 9 — Flying Ship

Volume 31 · Chapter 9

Only a strangely shaped warship stood towering in the desert, its hull appearing very large, yet mostly buried by yellow sand.

Everyone gazed up at the ship's bow protruding above the sandy sea, like an ancient vessel about to sink, its massive shadow looming over them.

"It's this one," Lamia stopped, turning back to say, "Nearby, only this ship looks very strange. Clearly everything else has rotted away, yet most of it remains intact—a vessel that can be used for several eras without maintenance. It's unimaginable."

"Maybe... maybe just an ancient warship? Just a bit more durable," Jacob said timidly, offering his opinion.

"Are you an idiot!? A warship that doesn't rot for several eras—can you call that 'a bit more durable'?" Vadier scolded impatiently.

"I'm sorry, I won't say anything more," Jacob shrank back, trembling, too afraid to approach this group of dark creatures.

Pudom especially loved ancient things. Seeing this strangely shaped warship, he immediately fell in love with it, gently stroking the ancient wooden material. "The wood used to build this ship is extraordinary! Harder and more corrosion-resistant than ordinary wood, and lighter too! But I wonder what kind of tree it was made from—too strange:·"

"Nothing strange about it? Maybe during the Gods' Era, there was a river here. Having ships isn't strange," Lilith didn't see anything special.

"Unfortunately, we investigated long ago. There's no trace of any river ever existing here—that's the strange part about this ship appearing here." Vadier glanced at Lilith with a contemptuous look.

"What's with that condescending attitude? Want to fight? No river, so where's the ship—did it not sail in water, but fly in the sky?" Lilith's whip stirred in her hand.

Merlin quietly examined the strange giant ship before him, ancient aura rushing toward him.

Though its general form wasn't much different from sailing at sea, there were two gathered sails on either side, looking like folded wings?

Combining Vadier's information—no trace of a river ever existing here—there was probably only one possibility.

"Maybe this ship was meant for flying."

"Eh? Brother, are you serious???" Lilith asked in surprise, unable to imagine a sea vessel soaring in the sky.

"Deep-sea fish can grow wings and leap out of the water to glide briefly—what's impossible about a ship going to the sky?" Merlin countered.

"That's impossible! Ships are meant for sailing the sea!" Lilith said stubbornly, unable to shift her thinking for a moment.

"The materials used to build this ship are very light. If placed at sea, they couldn't withstand the waves—this was clearly prepared for flight," Merlin speculated based on his experience.

"Your Majesty is right. This ship suddenly appearing in the homeland of the ancient gods is too strange. Moreover, the ship's patterns don't match here—clearly two different cultures. I'm sure this warship isn't from Asgard but brought by an outsider. As for who, very likely the allied forces that fought against the gods, since not every race has the ability to fly:·" Pudom said slowly, guessing many things in his heart.

"As you say, very possible. Besides the goblin clan, I can't imagine who else would fantasize about flying ships? And the ancient gods' oppression was too severe—goblins participating in the rebellion isn't strange." Pudom nodded in agreement.

"Stop discussing these things and get on the ship to investigate." Merlin decided to board and take a close look.

〇

After everyone boarded and explored, besides a thick layer of sand, there didn't seem to be anything noteworthy.

Merlin let Lilith and Pudom go check the cabin for any new findings.

Lamia also let her two subordinates search on their own. Only Jacob hid nearby, trembling, constantly praying these dark creatures wouldn't get hungry.

With nothing to do, Jacob examined the ancient ship, feeling doubly disappointed. He had thought the Gods' ruins were full of treasures, but it turned out incredibly desolate, seemingly nothing valuable?

If Jacob brought back a pile of sand, he'd probably make old Rothschild furious on the spot. After preparing so long for this treasure hunt, he'd get nothing.

Jacob accidentally found a box by his feet. Curious, he opened it and found several dust-covered round bottles inside, black as mines.

What are these things?

Jacob picked up a bottle, opened the cork, and familiar scent immediately hit his nose—wine! And the smell was very strong and mellow!

Wine brewed in the Gods' Era, still perfectly preserved until today—amazing!

Jacob swallowed saliva instinctively. After being stranded for days without alcohol, his mouth was dry—how could he resist?

So he sneaked a look around, saw no one paying attention, took a small sip, and immediately felt his whole body burning like fire, filled with power.

"What is this!? Unexpectedly delicious! Different from any wine I've had—this liquor is both strong and refreshing!"

"What's going on? These dark creatures don't look so scary anymore. I'm so excited:·"

"Could this wine stimulate the spirit, eliminate fear, and strengthen the body? That's a rare treasure!"

"Gods' Era wine—just a sip could sell for tens of thousands of gold coins? Truly a treasure!"

Merlin didn't bother noticing Jacob, but carefully investigated the ancient ship. From the traces left by the disguise—

This ship had experienced a great battle. Everywhere there were signs of destruction, sword and blade wounds everywhere.

Weapons scattered on the ground, even after hundreds of thousands of years, remained sharp, flashing cold light!

Picking up any sharp blade at random, it would be rare quality outside, and significantly stronger too.

If this equipment was standard issue in the Gods' Era, those ancient people must have been extraordinary in combat!

However, these weren't enough to catch Merlin's attention. He was already drawn to the altar in the center of the deck. In the center of the platform was an embedded crystal, like burned-out coal turned white-gray.

"What is this?"

Merlin reached out to touch and test it, but a gust of wind blew, and the crystal on the altar instantly turned to dust, vanishing into the air, leaving only a square recess.

What was that just now? Looks a bit like a magic crystal loaded into a magi-cannon.

Just as Merlin was puzzled, Lamia suddenly came to him alone. Though wearing a veil, her gaze clearly had something on her mind.

"Mr. Merlin, any findings?"

"No," Merlin straightened up, looking at this beautiful vampire.

"I wonder if you could give us a chance to talk properly?" Lamia said meaningfully. Now that no one was around, it was the perfect opportunity to ask about that matter.

"Haha, Miss Lamia still has questions for me?" Merlin grinned.

"Of course—the secret in the Holy Grail in the southern forest of the French Glen Plain," Lamia asked impatiently, hoping Merlin would honestly reveal everything—

"You know about it, don't you?"

title: Chapter 10 — The Instigator
content:
Chapter 10 — The Instigator

Volume 31 · Chapter 10

”That sickening smile,” Lamia said with a flat expression. “As the King of Demons, you wouldn’t still be interested in a vampire like me, would you? Or do you want to taste something uniquely fresh?”

“Pfft!” Merlin nearly spat out a mouthful of blood. “Who’d be interested in you!? Do I look that filthy and disgusting?”

“Because your smile is gross,” Lamia replied bluntly.

“Uh…” Merlin instinctively touched his face. “Is my smile really that untrustworthy? But the cold, aloof persona doesn’t suit me either.”

“With your nasty, annoying personality, no woman would like you — except maybe your stupid sister. Poor thing,” Lamia said, her gaze filled with contempt.

“Who says that!? I have tons of admirers, and I even have a kid — the kind who can go buy soy sauce on their own!” Merlin retorted angrily.

“You’re serious? You’re married and have a child?” Lamia found this hard to believe. She thought no woman could tolerate such a terrible personality.

“Yeah, my daughter is super cute. She sleeps on me every day, and follows me everywhere when we go out,” Merlin said proudly, though he felt a twinge of worry about Alice caring for Chris alone at home.

“Which blind woman would love you? I genuinely pity her,” Lamia said sincerely.

“None of your business!” Merlin’s veins bulged. Although he wasn’t sure how Alice felt, he didn’t think he was that bad.

Lamia thought for a moment and suggested, “If you answer my questions, you can choose the treasure found here first — how’s that?”

“Sounds good,” Merlin considered for a bit and nodded. “What do you want to know?”

“Why do you know so much about vampires? You don’t look like a vampire hunter,” Lamia asked, curious. Normally, only hunters could spot vampires in a crowd.

“Long story. I’m a banished Demon Lord, but also an adventurer. I’ve taken missions to deal with vampires before, so I’m quite familiar with them,” Merlin explained. “Lamia, you’re a noble among vampires, right? I heard from a priest about how you left the forest and became monsters. Besides you, there’s Bathory and Dracula — the three founders. But I personally killed Dracula.”

“You killed Dracula?” Lamia looked shocked.

“Yes, my mission was to kill Dracula. He was causing trouble in France, but he ran into me,” Merlin boasted. “Since I killed your companion, do you hate me?”

“Well…” Lamia fell silent, realizing that Cain’s power had revived because of this man.

She glared at Merlin with anger. While she and Bathory had tricked Cain for power, they had successfully weakened him. Now, because of Merlin’s interference, Cain was recovering — which would bring disaster to the world.

Lamia took a deep breath, trying to suppress her rage. “No, we split ways long ago due to different beliefs. I and Bathory wanted to live quietly among humans, but Dracula’s ambition grew with his immortality. He wanted to build his own utopia.”

“I see,” Merlin nodded. As a demon living among humans, he understood the loneliness that could drive one mad.

“Dracula brought this on himself. If he’d given up his fantasy, he wouldn’t have been hunted down,” Lamia sighed. “Since you mentioned the holy bottle, you must know about Cain. What do you know about her?”

“Enough to be dangerous. We had close contact for a while. At first, she was like an abandoned child, but later became a ruthless monster — eating people without spitting out bones,” Merlin said meaningfully.

“Like an abandoned child?” Lamia was confused. That didn’t match the Cain she knew.

“Problem? When I first met Cain, she was harmless — like an orphan. But for some reason, she almost killed me later. It’s not a pleasant memory,” Merlin frowned, recalling how Cain used Alice and his kindness.

Lamia realized something: after she and Bathory stole Cain’s power, it damaged her mentally. And since Merlin killed Dracula, Cain was recovering and likely wanted to kill them to reclaim her full power.

“Merlin, Cain was sealed in the holy bottle. How did she get free? The Cain we saw was at her peak — she couldn’t have broken the seal on her own.”

“That might be my fault,” Merlin scratched his cheek awkwardly. “I did open the bottle…”

“Why would you open it? A careful person wouldn’t touch an unknown artifact,” Lamia asked, eyes bloodshot.

“If you find a valuable-looking bottle while treasure hunting, wouldn’t you want to see what’s inside? It’s irresistible!” Merlin shrugged confidently.

“So it’s all your fault!” Lamia trembled, her undead aura flaring. Bats circled overhead.

“You’re the cause of all this!” (ir^a^)

title: Chapter 11 — Good Mood
content:
Chapter 11 — Good Mood

Volume 31 · Chapter 11

”Of course.”

Lamia’s emotions became highly unstable; she hated Merlin’s foolish behavior to the core. ★First★Release★EZ Reading★

Becoming a vampire from a human was already difficult enough to survive among humans.

Now that Cain has gained freedom and his power is recovering, he will surely come after her, leaving no path for survival!

What does Dracula’s dream of building an ideal kingdom matter? Cain’s freedom poses a hundred times greater danger than Dracula!

If Dracula’s threat was limited to the Kingdom of France, Cain’s is global.

The revival of such a world-enemy monster benefits no one — especially not Lamia.

“Oh,” Merlin said, noticing Lamia’s panic. He was puzzled — he hadn’t understood the relationship between these three original vampires and Cain. One was a loyal subordinate, but now it seems different: Lamia fears Cain’s freedom and harbors deep hostility. “Your power comes from Cain, right? Why the anxiety?”

“Because... we obtained our power through deception. Cain hates us with a passion. Once free, she’ll kill us and reclaim her immortal divinity.” Lamia paused, gritting her teeth. “You killed Dracula, fine — but you also released Cain from the holy bottle? If Cain is a bomb destroying the world, you lit the fuse. Nothing can stop it now.”

Merlin fell silent, realizing the truth in Lamia’s words. He now understood why the initially timid Cain suddenly became aggressive.

He had killed Dracula, who stole Cain’s power, and simultaneously revived Cain’s strength.

To restore her peak state, Cain would hunt down the other two deceivers to reclaim her immortal divinity.

Merlin’s expression darkened as he realized he had unleashed a terrifying force. No wonder Lamia looked like she wanted to devour him.

“As long as Cain stayed in the bottle, everyone would be safe. But you — killing Dracula to save France is one thing, but you created a monster a hundred times worse than Dracula.”

Lamia’s immortal power surged, and the bats emitted piercing screeches. She even considered suicide to take Merlin with her.

Jacob ignored the commotion, drunk and lying on the deck, laughing to himself.

“We’ve struggled to survive, yet you push us to our doom. You think Cain’s immortality is wonderful? No! It’s a curse — constant bloodlust, fear of human hunters, living in terror forever!”

“Oh, so what? It’s not me suffering,” Merlin replied coldly, pushing Lamia’s patience to its limit.

Without hesitation, Lamia’s immortal power transformed into flowing blood, bathing her body. The pressure of a pseudo-god shook the deck.

But before she could attack, Merlin struck first — his ghostly figure closed the gap instantly, pinning her down.

Lamia’s pupils shrank in shock. She had underestimated Merlin’s close-combat strength; at this range, she was helpless.

With Merlin’s power, once within reach, counterattacks were trivial — the mage wouldn’t even finish a syllable before being pinned.

“You can’t kill me,” Lamia said, feigning calm. “Don’t waste your energy.”

“Really? I don’t know how the sun created by the ancient gods differs from the real one, but I believe...” Merlin slid his hand down Lamia’s neck, brushing her breasts with his fingertips. “If I strip you naked and expose you to the sun, you won’t be so calm.”

“Ugh...” Lamia’s eyes flashed with fear. “Your baseness exceeds my expectations.”

“I don’t want to be this way — don’t keep reminding me I’m a demon,” Merlin smirked.

“You think after pushing us to despair, you can still be polite? I came to find an artifact to fight Cain, not to meet you,” Lamia said, eyes cold.

“You’d better behave. Even if I released Cain, we can still cooperate — enemies of my enemy are my friends,” Merlin said earnestly. “You want to fight Cain, so do I. I won’t forget that smug face.”

Lamia calmed slightly. Facing Cain alone was risky, but with the Demon Lord’s help, she might survive.

Cain’s freedom was inevitable; fighting Merlin wouldn’t change that. Cooperation was more logical.

“You want an artifact to fight Cain? I can help,” Merlin nodded. “Killing Cain is our common goal.”

Suddenly, noise erupted from the cabin — the search party returned.

“Brother! Look what I found!”

“No, me and Mahamud found it!”

“Your Majesty, this is...”

Pudom held up a mysterious black cube. Seeing Merlin embracing Lamia, hand on her chest, the air froze.

The crew stared in disbelief — had Merlin seduced the cold vampire while they were gone? This was clearly a private moment interrupted.

Silence reigned for three seconds. No one believed their eyes — how could Merlin and Lamia be together so quickly? It defied logic.

“Your Majesty...” Pudom stammered, avoiding eye contact. “You’re in high spirits.”

(??ω?? ?)

title: Chapter 12 — Another Masterpiece by the Goblin Race
content:
Chapter 12 — Another Masterpiece by the Goblin Race

Volume 31 · Chapter 12

”Your Majesty, please show some restraint. This is not the time to flirt with women. Free-first-release → [EZ Reading]”

“Brother! What are you doing?!” Lilith, seeing this, was furious and rushed toward Merlin, “So you deliberately sent us away to seduce a wild woman? I see through you! You’re a complete pig! You’ve already hooked up with someone else in such a short time? I’m breaking down!”

“No, no! It’s a misunderstanding! A misunderstanding!”

Merlin let go of the Lamia as if electrocuted. He hadn’t even noticed — what did it feel like to grab her chest?

He only remembered discussing Cain with the Lamia seriously. He knew nothing else!

But the Lamia was even stranger — she was clearly taken advantage of, yet she didn’t say a word?

“What ‘hooked up with someone else’? Don’t think of nonsense! Your brother is a decent person!!!”

“Pfft! Decent? Your hand was on her chest, and you say you’re decent? Disgusting!” Lilith couldn’t help but spit at Merlin.

“This, this was unavoidable! It was a reflex, a male instinct! I couldn’t control myself!” Merlin explained desperately, sweating profusely, “Moreover, I only did it to prevent Miss Lamia from acting rashly — there was no intention to take advantage of her!”

“You’re using such a weak excuse — what’s the difference between this and a drunken mistake? If you want to prove your innocence, then touch me too — that way I’ll believe you.” Lilith said as she pulled open her chest clothes and forced Merlin’s hand into her bosom.

“Stop it, you brat. You just want to satisfy your own perverted desires, don’t you?” Merlin’s veins bulged as he pulled his hand back with force.

“Don’t waste words, brother. Touching me will prove your innocence — put your hand in here obediently.” Lilith’s face darkened, and she gritted her teeth, wishing she could bleed Merlin’s “dirty hand.”

“Let go of me, or I’ll lose my temper and teach you a lesson. You’re grown up now, and I haven’t disciplined you in a long time — don’t push me.” Merlin frowned, sweating, full of threat.

While Merlin and Lilith were locked in a stalemate, Vadya and Mahamud exploded on the spot!

In their eyes, the Lamia was a sacred goddess — how could they tolerate her being defiled?

“Shameless pervert!? Don’t think you can bully people just because you’re the Demon Lord — I’ll fight you!” Vadya drew her curved knife from her waist.

“Ugh!” Mahamud’s strong body shook, and he immediately picked up his sharp axe, ready to fight Merlin to the death.

“Cough, don’t get so excited.” The Lamia blushed slightly, “These are all misunderstandings.”

“Misunderstandings?” Vadya paused, worried, “Are you okay? Did this bastard bully you while we were away?”

The Lamia hesitated, “No, nothing happened.”

Seeing the Lamia didn’t care and said it was a misunderstanding, Vadya and Mahamud calmed down immediately — though they still glared at Merlin with hostility.

The Lamia recalled Merlin’s earlier suggestion and felt tempted. Facing Cain’s threat, having the Demon King’s help would boost her confidence. Perhaps she could find an artifact here to counter Cain.

Merlin: “I, refuse!”

Podom looked at Merlin and Lilith and rushed to stop the quarreling siblings, “Cough! Your Majesty, Lady Lilith, don’t argue. Now isn’t the time to dwell on these trivialities. Even if Your Majesty touched Miss Lamia’s chest, you can touch mine too — I welcome your warm palm anytime.”

Merlin shuddered and gasped, “Podom, don’t provoke me — I’ll kill you.”

“Tch!” Lilith let go of Merlin, feeling her brother was corrupted by the human woman — his mind wasn’t on his cute sister. How could she win him back?

“Your Majesty, look what we found in the cabin!” Podom handed Merlin a square black crystal.

“This is?” Merlin held the crystal, sensing dense magic energy within — if released, the power would be unimaginable!

“We found this in a warehouse. It looks exactly like the artificial crystals that power magic cannons! I’m sure this strange ship was built by the Goblin race!” Podom declared confidently.

“Oh? Why?” Merlin asked, surprised.

“Because the original magic cannon prototype was created by Goblins. All later cannons are based on their design.” Podom was excited, “Finding this confirms the ship uses similar propulsion to magic cannons — it can power the cannon, so it can power the ship!”

Merlin stared at the coal-like crystal, remembering the central altar on deck with similar death crystals — but they turned to dust when blown by the wind.

Could it be that the ship isn’t stuck due to a malfunction, but because it ran out of energy?

Merlin rushed to the central altar, carefully brushed off the dust, and placed the crystal in the slot.

Everyone held their breath, watching for a minute —

“Nothing’s happening? Did we get it wrong?” Merlin looked at Podom.

Just then, the crystal ignited, and the ship’s magic circuits lit up — like waking a sleeping mechanical beast!

“It won’t explode, will it?” Merlin asked Podom nervously.

“Well, magic cannons do have a small chance of exploding...” Podom wiped his sweat.

“???” Merlin stared at Podom, tempted to abandon ship.

Rumbling sounds filled the ship, and it began to shake violently — as if ready to burst.

Jacob, half-drunk, woke up and lay flat on the deck, “What’s happening!? Is it the end of the world?”

The ship, buried in sand, rose into the sky, shaking off the sand. Its sails unfolded, especially the side sails, flapping like wings and creating windstorms!

Clearly, this ship wasn’t meant for sailing — it was built for aerial combat against ancient gods!

The strong airflow forced everyone to cling to supports to stay upright.

Jacob, gripping the railing, watched the ground shrink — his worldview shattered.

As a merchant’s son, he smelled money — this ship was priceless, beyond gold or silver.

A flying vessel that carries many people, similar to magic cannons — if studied, it could revolutionize transportation!

No more slow ships or horses — flying is faster!

Jacob was thrilled, forgetting fear. He planned to build his own business and impress his father.

He even named it: Jacob Aviation.

title: Chapter 13 — World Within the Stomach (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 13 — World Within the Stomach (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 31 · Chapter 13

”I’ve already heard the sound of countless gold coins falling into my pocket. If I can achieve something, how could my father still look down on me?”

“If I can successfully bring this sky ship back and research the technology inside, then this trip to the Ruins of the Gods will be worth it!”

“Building Jacob Aviation isn’t enough — I need to turn it into a popular mode of transportation for the masses, with first-class, business, and economy cabins to earn money from all levels. Free-first-release → [EZ Reading]”

“I can also build super-luxury sky ships for wealthy private owners, or organize world-travel tours on sky ships — endless ways to make money! These are all small fortunes!”

Jacob’s eyes have turned into gold coins, his heart racing with ambition. He feels he’s about to surpass his father and reach a new peak in life.

The mysterious sky ship rises to a certain height and hovers steadily in the air, ceasing its agitation.

Everyone marvels at the view below — the barren Ruins of the Gods are laid out before them.

Lilith: “It’s really a flying ship? We don’t need to ride dragons or griffins to soar through the sky?”

Pudom: “I knew it! This thing is amazing! Why didn’t such a great invention survive from the Age of Gods?”

Lamia: “Goblins aren’t good at fighting, but their minds are extraordinary. This flying ship is probably just one of their wild creations.”

Vadie: “Wow! This thing is incredible! With this, we can go anywhere we want, anytime!”

Everyone inspects the sky ship with curious eyes, tapping and touching — it feels like something from another world.

What was the Age of Gods really like? With today’s imagination, it’s hard to reconstruct that era.

Merlin approaches the helm, looking at the rudder — it seems no different from a regular boat?

But after a slight attempt, Merlin discovers that operating the sky ship isn’t difficult — in fact, it’s quite user-friendly.

Unlike a ship sailing on the sea, the sky ship’s rudder not only turns left and right but also moves up and down: lifting it makes the ship descend, pushing it down makes the ship rise.

As for the many levers beside it? Merlin doesn’t dare touch them randomly — he just got this vehicle, he doesn’t want to break it.

Merlin gazes at the distant giant World Tree and makes up his mind. He shouts to everyone:

“Next, we’ll head to the top of that tree to find the Garden of the King of Gods. Since there’s nothing here, let’s go to the top and see!”

“The Garden of the King of Gods?” Lamia frowns, wondering what lies above the clouds?

Gurgle... The green liquid emits a faint fluorescence.

The surroundings are pitch-black, yet one can hear thunder-like breathing — heavy and urgent.

Leviathan’s body floats in the green lake, surrounded by piles of sea monster bones and wrecked human ships, many corroded to black, emitting a strong stench.

This is an isolated place — the stomach of the Kraken, where eaten creatures are digested.

Anything falling into the green acid is corroded to nothing; even if it escapes to shore, it’s decomposed by the acidic air.

The unconscious Leviathan suddenly opens its eyes, looking around in confusion —

The darkness stretches endlessly, only the pulsing flesh walls with sharp spikes are visible overhead.

A floating sea monster corpse smokes and sinks into the acid lake.

Leviathan immediately becomes alert, realizing it’s not dead yet — but this place is extremely dangerous. Even the sea monster’s corpse was decomposed.

It struggles to swim toward the shore, but finds half its body submerged in acid is paralyzed — no strength at all.

Leviathan can only use one hand and one leg to swim, trying to reach land to escape the acid’s corrosion.

Looking at the countless bones on the shore, many had the same idea but failed.

Leviathan has no time to think — it just knows the shore is safer. But its strength is limited, and its body is severely corroded.

Escaping to shore is a luxury. Leviathan loses all strength, consciousness fading, feeling no pain — its flesh is already gone.

Suddenly, a plesiosaur eaten by the Kraken leaps out of the acid lake, flailing wildly.

Its body is skeletal, but its blood vessels still move its organs — horrifying!

This is the plesiosaur’s final struggle before death, emitting a silent cry as it sinks back into the lake.

But in its unconscious flailing, it accidentally saves Leviathan!

The waves from the plesiosaur’s struggle push Leviathan toward the shore!

“Cough cough!”

Leviathan watches the plesiosaur die tragically, fear overwhelming it. The flame of survival burns in its chest.

It crawls up, seeing half its body charred black.

Gently scratching reveals white bones — flesh turned to sticky, stinking mud.

It feels no pain, only a drifting consciousness — this body is a puppet driven by spirit.

Looking at the dark, pitted “ground” with occasional acid geysers, touching it reveals the Kraken’s pulse and faint heartbeat.

Leviathan bites its lip to stay awake, eyes brightening. It limps over bones into the unknown darkness —

“I don’t want to die.”

“I must...”

“I must find...”

Outside, the dark clouds remain, the sea churns.

The Kraken’s tentacles wave above the water, like a destructive demon.

No sea creature dares approach the angry Kraken — it’s terrifying.

It stays, waiting for the mice to come out —

No one can peek into the secrets of ancient gods. Only the dead can.

It won’t let anyone who disturbs the gods’ sleep leave alive.

title: Chapter 14 — Odin's Castle
content:
Chapter 14 — Odin's Castle

Volume 31 · Chapter 14

Jacob was very curious about this, so he volunteered to be the driver and quickly mastered the basic piloting skills of the airship. He imagined how, after returning, he could mass-produce the airship and promote this new mode of travel; future captains might not just be sailors braving the seas, but also those who could command the skies. As the airship continued to rise, the distance to the top of the World Tree grew ever closer—. Pudom raised a monocular and faintly saw a structure atop the World Tree that looked like a castle, "Your Majesty, quick look! It really exists! The garden of the King of Gods! It's right there!" "Huh?" Merlin took the monocular from Pudom, examined it closely, and indeed saw that the ancient building was that one? "Exactly! There's no mistake—being able to dwell at the world's summit, aside from the god-king who reigns over all beings, who else would have such authority?" Pudom answered affirmatively. Merlin fell silent, thinking Pudom made perfect sense: the World Tree, as the life source sustaining the ancient world, to reside at its peak carried an obvious symbolic meaning. The lower one goes on the World Tree, the more lowly and base the races become, even unworthy of sharing a place with the ancient gods—this fits perfectly with the class rules of the Age of Gods. "Everyone, get ready—we’ll be there soon. I hope you don’t let your guard down, for we still can’t confirm whether the ruins are safe." "Let me have a look," Lilith snatched the monocular, and upon gazing she couldn’t help feeling disappointed: "What garden of the King of Gods? It looks dilapidated, like a barren vegetable patch." "You think you’re here for sightseeing?" Merlin frowned and tapped Lilith on the head. Wadie, hearing this, was unconvinced and muttered under his breath, "Tch, we’ve been here so long and haven’t seen a single living thing—what danger could there be? We’ve come for nothing; aside from the ruined city remnants, there’s nothing at all." "Yeah," Mahmoud nodded glumly in agreement, equally disappointed, having thought that countless seekers would find treasures scattered throughout the gods’ relics, yet reality turned out to be utterly barren. "We haven’t searched every corner here yet; perhaps the precious treasures are hidden away. Next we’ll head to Odin’s palace to investigate—maybe we’ll find something." Lamia pondered, feeling strangely that they’d found nothing upon entry—it was as if the place had already been looted clean, not even a fragment of a divine artifact in sight. The ancient gods possessed mighty artifacts—Thor’s hammer Mjölnir, the strength belt Megingjörð, the wolf‑binding chain Gleipnir, and so on—where did all these famed treasures from myth end up? If Lamia could obtain even one of those, she’d have confidence to face Cain who comes knocking, but things don’t look promising. Wadie’s eyes darted like a thief’s as he whispered, "Lady Lamia, if you really find an artifact later, should we immediately betray and flee with the treasure? Though we can’t beat that Demon Lord, escaping should be no problem." "It depends on the situation," Lamia replied with an inscrutable answer, wondering whether to suddenly betray—this hinges on whether an irreconcilable conflict of interests will arise. After half a day’s flight, the airship drew near the garden of the King of Gods; up close, they could finally make out the full appearance of the building’s ruins—. Countless shattered bricks drifted aimlessly, the entire massive structure levitating in midair like a ruined skycastle! It sits above the World Tree’s summit, signifying the lofty responsibility of ruling over all beings, and representing the supreme realm that lowly mortals can never attain. Although its majesty has now vanished, reduced to what looks like a grand ruin, the towering spires and weathered steps still allow a glimpse of the ancient gods’ former glory. The airship slowly descended onto the floating castle’s ground, and everyone disembarked, curiously surveying the ancient surroundings. "This is the garden of the King of Gods, but it looks rather shabby, doesn’t it?" Merlin furrowed his brow, suddenly feeling like he’d have to treasure‑hunt in a trash heap. "Exactly, what kind of garden is this? I only see weeds everywhere." Lilith kicked a stone on the ground at random, discovering it didn’t fall but floated in the air, which surprised her; she guessed the whole castle was built from this levitating stone. "No, no, that’s not right—with the twilight of the gods arriving, this place must have suffered massive destruction; it couldn’t possibly be as bright and splendid as the myths describe. What we can see now is surely just the tip of the iceberg of the garden." Pudom pointed at the castle’s spire before him, speaking gently, "Lady Lilith, you should use your imagination: behold this majestic floating castle, enlarge it tenfold—can’t you picture how glorious it must have been in the Age of Gods?" "I hadn’t imagined that, thanks—I can only picture the ancient gods living up there without minding the wind." Lilith answered offhandedly. "Uh," Pudom blushed, feeling like he was preaching to the choir—Lilith could never grasp the cultural value each brick here embodies. "Let’s go inside the castle to have a look, but we need to leave someone to watch the airship." Merlin’s gaze swept over the group, hoping someone would volunteer. "We definitely won’t stay behind to watch the ship—don’t count on it," Wadie hastily protested, saying that going in to hunt for treasure is exciting, but staying to guard the airship is out of the question. Lamia said nothing, effectively agreeing with Wadie’s attitude; she was very eager to know what secrets lay in the dwelling of the Demon Lord Odin. Just as Merlin was pondering whether to have Lilith stay behind, Jacob sprang forward, volunteering, "Me! I can stay behind to watch the airship! Go ahead and investigate—I’ll be perfectly fine here, and besides, there might be danger inside; if I came along I’d only drag you down." "Oh? Really no problem handing it to you? You won’t take the ship and run off midway?" Merlin questioned skeptically. "Impossible! If I didn’t follow your orders here, I couldn’t even survive!" Jacob hurried to defend himself, breaking into a cold sweat. "Alright, let Jacob stay behind; we’re off." After Merlin and the others left, Jacob secretly let out a breath of relief, having temporarily escaped the dreadful dark creatures. Jacob merely wanted to take this opportunity to tinker with the airship a bit, and

title: Chapter 15 — Odin's Throne (More Updates Coming Soon)
content:
Chapter 15 — Odin's Throne (More Updates Coming Soon)

Volume 31 · Chapter 15

Lilith stared at the goddess statue's eyes together with the others, but didn't feel anything unusual. "No, it must be your imagination."

"It's not that, I really feel like I'm being watched, like the statue is staring at me." Lilith furrowed her brow, feeling an inexplicable unease.

"You're scaring yourself, statues are just dead objects without any life, how could they be staring at you?" Pudom thought Lilith was overthinking, perhaps due to fatigue, and needed rest.

"Is that so?" Lilith doubted herself, wondering if she was being too sensitive, and curiously asked, "Do you know what this statue is carved as?"

Pudom thought carefully, hesitating before saying, "I'm not too sure, but it should be a Valkyrie?"

"Valkyrie, what's that?" Lilith asked in surprise.

"They're the maidservants who attend to Odin after death, also known as female warriors. The Valkyries are brave and skilled in battle, wearing armor forged from swan feathers, riding warhorses to easily reap the lives of enemies. They were the vanguard of the ancient gods in oppressing the lower races, constantly killing those who resisted Odin and sending the plundered souls to Valhalla to cultivate loyal monsters who would only fight for Odin." Pudom recalled the records of Valkyries he had seen in ancient texts, which weren't very detailed.

"Hey, Lilith, Pudom, what are you two doing? I won't wait for you if you don't catch up."

Merlin walked halfway and saw Lilith and Pudom still standing at the door examining the statue, so he couldn't help but urge them.

"Coming, coming, brother is so impatient, are you afraid I'll get lost? Hehe" Lilith threw aside her previous unease and hurriedly chased after Merlin.

Pudom glanced at the Valkyrie statue again, muttering to himself, "Being stared at by a lifeless stone statue? How is that possible?"

After everyone entered the castle, the two Valkyrie statues at the entrance suddenly moved eerily.

Their sharp fingernails scratched the walls, emitting ear-piercing tearing sounds, as they stretched their necks and gazed at the group's backs with hollow eyes.

The light inside the castle was very dim, with hazy sunlight filtering down from the high windows.

A thick layer of dust had accumulated to the thickness of a fingernail, and it was unknown how long it had been since anyone had visited.

The internal corridor was winding and narrow, leading continuously upward through the castle. The old stairs were covered in mottled marks, and withered vines crawled all over the walls.

What puzzled everyone was that the further they went, the more lifelike stone statues they encountered, with increasingly rich movements and expressions.

Some covered their faces and wept, some stood facing the walls in contemplation, while others struck beautiful dance poses, as if intentionally drawing the attention of outsiders.

The Valkyrie statues crowded the stairs, forcing Merlin's group to push through them and continue upward.

Merlin was forced to squeeze between two statues, and when he looked up, he saw a grotesque face with a mouth stretched to the ears and ugly, serrated teeth.

But this was just a statue, seemingly carved to intimidate intruders. Merlin barely regained his composure, and the situation reminded him of the petrified followers of the King of Chaos, equally lifelike.

"Why are there so many sculptures here? Wouldn't they be in the way?" Merlin couldn't help but ask.

Lamia examined the statues before her, sighing, "These sculptures look very realistic, perhaps the ancient gods liked them?"

"I think this pile of statues is useless. Who would put them on the stairs as decorations? It's inexplicable." Merlin said irritably.

"Yes, it's really puzzling. This is the residence of the King of Gods, yet they've placed so many useless statues here." Lilith nodded vigorously in agreement.

"Your Majesty, could it be that someone came here before us and intentionally placed the statues in our path?" Pudom hesitated, speaking in a speculative tone. "After entering the ruins, we haven't found anything good except for that sky ship. It's too strange."

Merlin's expression turned awkward upon hearing this. If there was nothing here, wouldn't he have come in vain?

"It's unlikely. This place is completely sealed off from the outside, and it's impossible to enter casually, unless some ancient gods survived after the Twilight of the Gods."

"Right, it's unlikely. Haha" Pudom wiped the cold sweat from his face, unwilling to believe such an absurd possibility.

The group ignored the statues on the road and continued toward the castle's highest point with apprehensive hearts.

Until they saw a magnificent great hall, everyone stopped. The heavy doors had long been destroyed.

The circular great hall looked quite grand, with walls carved with countless ancient gods, as if countless eyes were staring at the intruders.

The floor was in disarray, with signs of destruction everywhere. Several shocking sword marks had torn through the sturdy hall, making it hard to imagine what had happened here.

On the dome of the hall was a beautiful and intricate mural, recording the great achievements of the God-King Odin. Although the mural was largely destroyed, parts of it could still be seen – Odin, thirsty for power, rode his eight-legged divine steed Sleipnir alone to the bottom of the World Tree in the land of giants, where he met the three goddesses who wove fate.

To drink from the Fountain of Life and gain power surpassing all living things, Odin personally dug out his sharp right eye and offered it to the three goddesses. This opened the curtain on the ancient gods' rule.

The longer one looked at the mural, the easier it was to become immersed and unconsciously feel reverence for the God-King Odin, seeing how this ancient god had made great sacrifices for his people.

"This should be the castle's core great hall," Merlin speculated.

"Undoubtedly, it must be where Odin held court," Lamia replied confidently.

"Your Majesty, look over there!" Pudom excitedly pointed ahead.

Following Pudom's direction, they saw a majestic throne shining with silver light.

Golden sunlight shone down from the skylight above, enveloping the throne in a sacred aura.

The beautifully carved patterns were full of ancient charm, making one's heart tremble at a glance.

Anyone who saw this would be extremely excited. In the era of the gods, this throne belonged only to Odin, symbolizing his rule over all races.

Merlin and Lamia walked forward to examine it, possibly the most valuable discovery since entering the ruins. However, the throne seemed to be merely symbolic, without any actual power.

"Wow, I want to sit on it and take a look!" Lilith looked at Odin's throne with great interest.

"Tsk, don't mess around. What if there's a trap?" Merlin thought it unwise and preferred caution, having learned from his experience with Cain.

Lamia gently stroked the massive throne, slightly furrowing her brow. "The stone material is unusual, this coldness could freeze blood instantly."

"Of course it's not ordinary! Look at the craftsmanship of these ancient master artisans, the natural beauty. Legend has it that Odin's throne was carved from a single piece of Sealing Stone!"

"Sealing Stone, do you know? That's an extremely rare and precious mineral from the era of the gods!"

title: Chapter 16 — !Box (I Apologize, I Am Guilty)
content:
Chapter 16 — !Box (I Apologize, I Am Guilty)

Volume 31 · Chapter 16

”i 丨

參 · ·

Merlin listened as Pudom explained that the massive throne was forged from a God-Slaying Stone, and his heart sank. This was one of the three materials needed to forge the sword Mistilteinn!

He had been searching everywhere for clues about the God-Slaying Stone, and now it had been discovered during an exploration of the ruins.

Odin had painstakingly acquired a whole block of the stone and turned it into a throne symbolizing his rule, but in doing so, he had inadvertently given Merlin a huge advantage.

Merlin looked at the giant throne before him, thinking that its weight was more than enough to forge Mistilteinn — perhaps even too much.

Lamia stared at Odin’s throne, her mind racing. If this thing truly had the power to nullify resurrection, healing, and recovery, forging it into a sharp weapon might give her an edge against Cain. The True Ancestor’s greatest strength was his immortality; if she could suppress that, her chances of winning would improve significantly.

“Your Majesty! This is a rare treasure — we must take it back to the First Demon Lord Palace!” Pudom suggested, turning around. Bringing Odin’s throne would be a major coup.

Merlin nodded, but Lamia beat him to the punch: “Mr. Merlin isn’t planning to keep this throne for himself, is he?”

Merlin shot Lamia a displeased look. Writing blank checks is easy, but when it comes to actually splitting the loot, things get complicated.

“Yeah! This belongs to everyone who sees it! You can’t just take it back to your palace without asking us!” Vadye snapped, glaring at the demons with hostility.

“Greedy demons,” Mahamud rumbled, sensing trouble and gripping his axe tightly.

“Are you rebelling?! We saw this throne first — it’s ours! Do you want to fight?!” Lilith brandished her whip.

“I hope you’ll calm down. You’re just mercenaries hired by the Rothschilds — you get paid in gold, not a share of the spoils from the God’s Ruins,” Pudom said sternly.

The atmosphere grew tense as both sides argued over who owned Odin’s throne.

“Don’t be so nervous. Let me ask: what does Lady Lamia need this throne for? It’s not a divine artifact or anything like that, right?” Merlin asked cautiously.

“I need to forge a weapon from the God-Slaying Stone — it’s critical,” Lamia replied sharply.

“I see,” Merlin nodded. It seemed Lamia had the same idea — using the stone to fight Cain.

“Your Majesty, we can’t give this up. The God-Slaying Stone is extremely rare, and this is the throne of the King of Gods — it has immense symbolic value,” Pudom argued against letting go.

“It doesn’t matter what it symbolizes — to me, it’s just a material. I’m only interested in the God-Slaying Stone,” Merlin paused, then turned to Lamia: “How about we split it?”

Lamia considered the offer. Even half the throne would be enough to forge a weapon, and pushing for more might anger Merlin. “Fine,” she agreed.

“Your Majesty, that’s not a good idea!” Pudom frowned.

“Yeah, it’s clearly ours!” Lilith glared at the vampires.

“This is my decision,” Merlin said firmly. Since Lamia was also targeting Cain, sharing the stone wasn’t a bad deal — their interests aligned. Plus, there was plenty of stone; while more is always better, without a specific use beyond Mistilteinn, the extra wouldn’t be that useful.

After weighing the options, Merlin decided to split Odin’s throne with Lamia — it wasn’t a huge loss.

“Step back,” he ordered.

Pudom and Lilith reluctantly obeyed, though they weren’t happy about it.

Merlin assumed a sword-drawing stance and, with lightning speed, sliced the massive throne in half.

“Ah, what a shame,” Pudom sighed. This was Odin’s throne — it had historical significance, and now it was broken.

Merlin stored his half in the Angel Ring’s spatial pocket, while Lamia had Mahamud carry the other half away.

Vadye, pleased with the haul, scanned the area for more treasures. Suddenly, he noticed a Valkyrie statue nearby pointing at him.

“Mahamud, look behind us — was there a statue here when we came in?”

Mahamud turned and tilted his head: “I don’t remember.”

“That’s weird,” Vadye muttered, brushing it off as paranoia. But as he turned back, he heard a voice:

“Everything you have is mine now.”

The Valkyrie statue moved, its nails piercing Vadye’s chest and its hand gripping his throat. His body began to merge with the stone — he was being consumed.

Vadye’s eyes widened in horror. What is this thing? It’s eating me! I’m a vampire — I should be immortal! Why isn’t my healing working? It’s like it’s erasing my existence.

He tried to scream for help, but no sound came out. He reached for Mahamud, but couldn’t reach him.

Meanwhile, Merlin was about to leave when he spotted a dusty black box hidden behind the throne. It looked insignificant, but its location suggested it was valuable.

Everyone gathered around.

“Your Majesty, there must be a treasure in there!” Pudom said excitedly.

“Brother, open it! It could be a divine weapon!” Lilith’s eyes sparkled.

Lamia watched intently, wondering what the box contained — likely a ring or dagger.

“Don’t rush me — let me see what’s inside,” Merlin said, picking up the box and blowing off the dust. He opened it slowly, revealing...

...a small, unassuming item. But before anyone could react, the statue behind them finished consuming Vadye, and the group turned to see the empty space where he had been.

The tension shifted from the box to the statue — and the mystery of what had just happened to Vadye.

title: Chapter 17 — Blood Letter (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 17 — Blood Letter (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 31 · Chapter 17

Constantly wondering what precious treasure was inside?
Since it was hidden behind the throne, it was probably hidden by Odin himself, so it must be something rare. Free-first-release→[EZ reading]
Lamia had already begun searching her memory; according to the myths that have been passed down, there are many small artifacts, such as the iron glove Yngriper, the dripping Dropnir, the charming necklace Brishgaman, etc.
"Your Majesty, we definitely struck it rich!" Pudom exclaimed excitedly, waiting to be blinded.
"Hurry up! Brother, Lilith is urging anxiously beside you."
"Don't rush me!"
Gee ya ya
With a series of scraping sounds, the black box was slowly opened. Merlin glanced inside, his expression immediately slumped, and he had a bad premonition.
Everyone craned their heads to look inside the box, but there was nothing exciting at all?
What shiny artifact? It simply didn't exist; only a blood-stained rag lay inside.
"Huh?" Lamia frowned, unable to tell what it was, wondering if any myth mentioned an artifact being a piece of rag.
"What is this??" Lilith put on a stern face, feeling very disappointed; at a glance it wasn't anything precious.
"Could it be Odin's black history, like when he got old he would wet the bed, so he hid the sheets, not wanting anyone to see?" Pudom boldly guessed; if the King of Gods were still alive, he might be furious to death!
"Does your King of Gods urinate blood? This isn't bedwetting; it's practically a terminal illness!" Merlin rolled his eyes, unable to tolerate Pudom's wild imagination.
"Uh, I guess that's also true," Pudom embarrassedly scratched his cheek.
Merlin was in a bad mood, looking at the rag in the box; although he didn't know what it was, it was probably not what they hoped for.
So Merlin took out the rag, unfolded it, and discovered densely written characters on it—it was actually a blood-written document—
"Don't bother looking for any artifacts; there aren't any here. Most artifacts fell together with the ancient gods, and only a few remain."
"I advise you to leave quickly; the ruins are more dangerous than you imagine."
~j\心 those stone statues; they are formed from the grudges of the ancient gods, immortal and indestructible.
"Remember, stare at them, don't blink."
After reading the blood-written message on the rag, Merlin froze on the spot, his face gradually darkening; a sense of fear welled up, sending chills down his spine.
Others also looked at the writing on the rag, but their reaction wasn't as strong as Merlin's; instead they showed a puzzled expression.
"What does this say? It feels really weird; Lamia has never seen such strange characters."
"The characters are neat and square; they couldn't be the ancient gods' writing, right?" Pudom mused, stroking his chin.
"It looks like ghostly talismans; what is this??" Lilith felt that whatever was written up there was mysterious; not understanding it made her angry.
Indeed, among those present, aside from Merlin himself, no one could understand the writing on the rag.
Because the script used to write it is not this world's common serpentine font, but rather a block character from another world—
Simplified Chinese!
As a transmigrator, Merlin is extremely familiar with simplified Chinese; he is also a man who suffered through nine years of compulsory education, so of course he could instantly understand the content on the rag.
Lilith, Pudom, Lamia, and Mahamud, the natives, how could they possibly understand simplified Chinese from another world?
Although each race has its own script, with the advent of the human era, the twisted serpentine script became the world's common written language.
[.All-net.]
[.Update.]
[.Fastest.]
[——Chase/——]
[——20070;——]
[ ,。幚/。, ]
"I think" Pudom pondered for a moment, speaking with certainty, "This must be the ancient gods' script; there's no mistake. After all, there are too many tribes in the world, each with its own writing, so it's normal we can't understand the ancient gods' writing."
"Yes, that's right! We just don't know what it says." Lilith said regretfully.
"No, this is human writing, genuinely from some ancient civilization." Merlin emphasized sternly with a straight face.
"Ah?! Your Majesty, how do you know? Why are you so certain?" Pudom asked in shock.
"Don't ask, I just know." Merlin said solemnly.
"Brother, you couldn't possibly understand it, right?" Lilith gave a doubtful look, thinking Merlin usually reads a lot, but he couldn't possibly have learned all the races' scripts; could it just be a coincidence?
"He can read it."
Everyone looked at Merlin with strange eyes, thinking he wasn't a well-read scholar, how could he outright claim these block characters were human culture?
At this moment, Merlin likewise felt uneasy, his gaze filled with worry, because he realized a serious problem—
Besides himself, there is another transmigrator in this world, and they come from the same place!
This matter gave Merlin a great shock; he had always believed he was the world's only transmigrator, but seeing the writing on the rag made him clear-headed.
As everyone knows, transmigrators often carry cheat abilities, frequently using a godlike grass-cutting mode to clear otherworldly dungeons; Merlin himself also obtained a unique ability.
Merlin couldn't figure out what kind of heaven-shaking power this other transmigrator possessed, nor did he know whether they were friend or foe! This is the most crucial!
If this person is an enemy, Merlin would have to find a way to kill them, but killing a transmigrator is far harder than slaying an otherworldly powerhouse.
"What does it say?" Lamia asked curiously.
"It says there are no artifacts here; don't waste time, let us leave quickly, be careful of the stone statues outside?" Merlin gave a simple narration.
Hearing this, everyone recalled the many eerie stone statues on the way here, and they all turned their heads to look.
All they saw was the Valkyrie statue standing silently behind them, covering its mouth with a dignified pose.
"Huh? Strange, when we just entered the hall, were there stone statues?" Lilith always felt something was off.
"No! There were absolutely no stone statues in the hall just now; I remember clearly, they should be outside the hall, I remember clearly!" Pudom said fearfully; his memory is excellent, such a thing shouldn't be a misremembering.
"Uh!" Merlin's face darkened, his eyes suddenly turned sharp; various abnormal signs put him on alert, as some danger began to quietly approach!
Lamia looked around and finally discovered that Vadye had vanished without a trace, scanning the entire hall and seeing not even a shadow—'Vadye?'
"Where did Vadye go?!"
"Why did it suddenly disappear?!"

title: Chapter 18 — Encirclement
content:
Chapter 18 — Encirclement

Volume 31 · Chapter 18

Even Lilith was a bit puzzled, why didn't Vadiye argue with himself and become so quiet?
Lamia searched everywhere but couldn't find Vadiye's silhouette, a bad premonition rising in her heart. "Mahmud, did you see Vadiye? Just now you were always together, right?"
"Just now he was still there" Mahmud scratched his head foolishly, equally puzzled saying, "Strange·"
"What exactly happened?" Lamia frowned, anxious, acting alone at this critical moment is dangerous.
Merlin recalled the warning on the torn cloth, telling himself to be careful of these stone statues, and the statues that should have been standing outside suddenly appeared in the hall, obviously someone had moved them!
"Podom, are you sure there were no stone statues in the hall when we just entered?"
"Your Majesty, I'm sure, I'd stake my head on it." Podom said firmly.
Merlin somewhat trusted Podom, feeling that his subordinate wouldn't spout nonsense at such a time, so he boldly walked up to the stone statue that had suddenly appeared in the hall.
The Valkyrie stone statue stood motionless, hand along its lips like a dignified maiden, appearing completely ordinary, utterly a lifeless statue.
But now all these strange things point to this stone statue, forcing everyone to suspect that there must be other beings in the castle, extremely dangerous, possibly related to Vadiye's sudden disappearance!
Merlin stared fixedly at the statue's empty, lifeless eyes, pondering possibilities—who moved the statue here? Even the mysterious traveler who wrote the bloody message on the cloth warned him to be careful of these guys.
This stone statue looks harmless; it must have been moved here by someone. Besides us, there must be a more dangerous presence here. Lamia's expression tightened, facing a great enemy: "I don't want to believe it, but Vadiye may have been killed! He is extremely loyal to me; without my orders, he would never act alone!"
"We just spoke with Vadiye; Mahmud, though not eloquent, shows a hint of sorrow, unwilling to believe his companion met harm."
"What Miss Lamia said is very possible, and the enemy lurking in the dark likely already has its eyes on us, possessing strong concealment ability, moving the outdoor stone statues inside and killing Vadiye, yet we didn't notice? It could completely evade all our senses! And these stone statues are probably the enemy's attack tools!" Podom said sternly, his analysis spot-on: "Such an assassin-type enemy, we must be extra careful; a slight lapse will produce new victims!"
"Stone statue looks harmless? Is that really the case?"
Although Podom had analyzed the situation thoroughly, Merlin still tended to believe that mysterious traveler.
After all, travelers often carry extraordinary abilities, and their stance toward other worlds tends to be neutral.
Merlin's gaze calmed, then he suddenly pushed the blade of the demon sword Banri Garan out a bit with his thumb.
A murderous sword aura swished forth, shattering the dignified stone statue into pieces, the neat fragments thudding to the ground.
But after the statue was destroyed, nothing happened; everything remained very calm.
"Eh, it really seems just ordinary stone."
Merlin turned back with an embarrassed expression, puzzled, that mysterious traveler clearly warned him to be careful of the stone statues, but what exactly did he mean?
After destroying the statue, it was just a pile of ordinary stone—what's there to be careful about?
"Your Majesty, my guess is correct; the stone statues are merely killing tools, the real enemy still hides in the dark! That torn cloth warning us to be careful of the stone statues might be hinting that if we avoid the statues, we won't suffer the enemy's ambush." Podom thought this possibility very high.
"Really?" Merlin doubted, then decisively said: "We can't keep staying here; we need to leave quickly."
Before his words faded, Lilith suddenly screamed in fear; she had only blinked, and saw a dark, mysterious object standing behind Merlin. "Brother! Behind you!"
Merlin turned back in surprise, his pupils trembling with fear, he instinctively stepped back two steps, only to see the destroyed stone statue restored intact, its movements renewed, its face grim, extending sharp claws to stab at Merlin.
If Lilith hadn't noticed suddenly, the stone statue might have devoured Merlin's life force like it did Vadiye, erasing him!
The stone statue stood again; Merlin felt a chill on his back, even though he had destroyed the statue, it instantly recovered and stood up.
There was no recovery process; just a blink, the destroyed stone statue restored and tried to kill Merlin!
"What!?" Lamia also jumped, thinking someone was hiding, never expecting these stone statues to be the most dangerous presence!
"No way!? These stone statues are really alive!" Podom showed disbelief, his earlier guesses completely overturned, the enemy is these seemingly ordinary stone statues!
"I told you! When we first entered, I always felt watched—it's these stone statues!" Lilith now finally understood why she felt uneasy after entering the castle.
"Indeed, that makes sense; we should indeed be more careful. Vadiye very likely met his end this way—these stone statues move silently, only active when not observed, freezing when watched." Merlin's gaze fixed on the Valkyrie stone statue, feeling this thing is truly troublesome.
"Too cunning! If not for the reminder on the torn cloth, who would discover these stone statues are so dangerous?" Podom felt lingering fear, breaking into a sweat.
Merlin nodded in strong agreement: if that mysterious traveler hadn't reminded us, who would notice these seemingly ordinary stone statues? One would just glance and move on.
However Merlin also realized that the mysterious traveler who left the warning here was not a bad person; rather, invisibly he saved everyone's lives!
"But who exactly is the other party? Why leave important information here? Merlin has no clue at all."
"Everyone better stay alert; judging from the situation, these stone statues are the resentment of ancient gods incarnate, possessing immortality, and since Vadiye is clearly an immortal bloodline yet he was killed, this proves the statues can destroy an immortal body! Their killing method is unique!" Merlin combined all current information, roughly analyzing the enemy's traits.
"Brother! Outside" Lilith instinctively lifted her head, seeing more stone statues suddenly appear in the hall, each different, standing... "They've started coming in from outside!" "We're surrounded!"
