title: Chapter 19 — Method
content:
Chapter 19 — Method

Volume 31 · Chapter 19

The statues varied in form, completely blocking the castle's exit, obviously intending not to let outsiders escape.
tsk…:·
Merlin felt a slight trouble; from the fact that the statues recovered in the blink of an eye just now, it seemed this group of statues was not afraid of his sword slash, and as long as he was a little inattentive, they could instantly recover.
Facing such a troublesome opponent like a stubborn plaster, Merlin really didn't want to clash head‑on; he had to find a way to leave the castle at once.
"This place is too dangerous! However, if we don't stare at them, they will surely attack us, but if we keep staring, we simply cannot leave!" Lamia said anxiously; the situation made her feel utterly terrified, and even Vadiye had been killed, so her proud immortal power probably wouldn't work either!
"Be careful, Podom!" Lily suddenly shouted a warning.
While everyone was focused on the large number of statues at the hall entrance, the very first statue that had entered took the opportunity to move, coming within a single step of killing Podom.
These statues, born from the grudges of ancient gods, not only possess the trait of immortality, but also exist as monsters that feed on life force; a moment's inattention and they will silently slay their prey.
Podom broke out in a cold sweat, frantically retreating backward, feeling an icy chill on the back of his neck: "These bastards, can't you take your eyes off them even for a moment?!"
"Brother! Ahead! The statues outside the door have moved again!" Lily glanced at the first statue that had entered, and as a result the statues blocking the entrance surged forward wildly, surrounding everyone.
"!!" Merlin stared in shock; a large number of statues stood ten paces away, already very close to killing everyone.
"What should we do, Lady Lamia?" Mahamud held his great axe, not knowing how to handle the current situation.
"I don't know either; if we try to force an escape, these statues will surely chase us from behind—Vadiye wasn't weak, and he didn't even make a sound before dying, who knows what method they used?" Lamia's face turned pale; her intuition told her that forcing an escape would be even more dangerous.
"No way? They can't be killed, and their speed is as fast as instantaneous movement—are we supposed to be worn to death here?!" Podom gritted his teeth, his emotions somewhat unstable.
"Brother! Think of a solution! Standoff here won't work!" Lily looked at the surrounding statues; although each was dignified and beautiful, it made her scalp tingle.
"I've already started thinking," Merlin said solemnly, trying to maintain composure.
An atmosphere of unease and fear spread, and everyone felt an unprecedented tension.
Whether demon or vampire, none can live without blinking, especially under this tense, oppressive atmosphere, causing everyone's blink frequency to increase even more!
One could see the statues start to jerk and jump through space, steadily closing in on the surrounded outsiders, the danger distance shrinking—eight steps, six steps, four steps. In Merlin's view, the picture looked like dropped frames, needing a blink to make the statues' movement appear smooth. Even so, their motions resembled a wound‑up rusty puppet, the eerie movement deepening the horror. The statues were now only two steps from the people, about to devour and erase the outsiders' lives; Merlin realized this couldn't continue—the greater the tension, the quicker the death.
"If you want to live, don't blink! Stay calm!!!" Merlin's loud warning startled the others, but it succeeded in steadying their emotions; the statues halted at a distance of two steps.
"Not blink? That's not possible; we can't hold out that long." Lamia said uneasily.
"Yes, Your Majesty, that request is a bit difficult, but holding out for a while is still doable." Podom said embarrassedly.
"Holding out for a while will be enough!" Merlin said solemnly.
"Brother, do you have a plan?" Lily asked curiously.
"Well, there's a method we can try: as long as a living being stares at them, the statues cannot move; so perhaps the statues themselves are alive? If we make them stare at each other, they might fall into an infinite loop, rendering each unable to move." Merlin voiced his idea; he couldn't guarantee it would work, but it was worth a try.
"I see; if the statues are alive, then mutual staring would put them in a state of mutual surveillance—as long as they can see each other, they could never move. What a clever idea!" Lamia's eyes lit up; she gave Merlin a meaningful look, having thought him a brute, but now it seemed not entirely so.
"Oh!" Podom clenched his fists, staring at the statues without daring to look away; His Majesty's words made perfect sense, worth a try. Merlin thought the statues' rules were similar to the "1, 2, 3, wooden person" game played in kindergarten, with comparable elements—"The statues that came from outside number twenty‑three; plus the first one that entered, making twenty‑four in total."
"Having an even number is great; if there were an extra one it would be troublesome. From now on, everyone should do as I say."
"Lily, find a relatively high spot inside the hall and figure out how to get all twenty‑four statues into your field of view; they've all gathered together now, so it's not hard for one person to widen their vision and keep an eye on twenty‑four statues."
"Everyone, like me, must not blink, covering Lily until she finds a suitable position:·" "Received|"
Lily blinked desperately to relieve herself, then hurried to find a higher spot in the hall. She climbed onto a relatively high abandoned fountain pedestal; because the statues stood densely to hunt outsiders, the twenty‑four statues were easily within her view. Lily quickly counted them, confirmed there was no problem, and immediately reported truthfully to her brother.
"Brother! I've done as you said; now I can see all the statues in the hall, none missing!"
"Then from now on you must not blink, hold out as long as you can; the others can relax a bit." Merlin said solemnly.
Everyone let out a collective sigh of relief; with Lily watching from above, the statues indeed remained motionless. "Hurry up! I feel like I'm about to blink, it's unbearable!" Lily complained, feeling her eyes sore and painful.
"Alright, let's get to work; Lily can't hold out much longer, everyone place the statues in pairs so their lines of sight meet." Merlin paused, looking at the varied statues before him—"Don't be afraid; at this distance the statues aren't attacking, proving they pose no threat in their petrified state."
"Move quickly, let's escape this damned place."

title: Chapter 20 — Parting Ways
content:
Chapter 20 — Parting Ways

Volume 31 · Chapter 20

Merlin and Podom each carried a statue and placed them together, trying to make them face each other.
If Merlin's idea is correct, then the statues staring at each other will fall into a state where they can never move, of course assuming they can both see each other.
Here Merlin and Podom were busy working, while over there Lamia led Mahmud past the statues and headed straight for the doors of the hall.
Podom saw this and immediately spoke up to stop them: "Hey! Miss Lamia, what are you doing? Why aren't you coming over to help?"
Merlin lifted his head, watching Lamia and Mahmud stop outside the hall doors, and a bad feeling rose in his heart—could it be that they saw no danger and now wanted to abandon the others and think about escaping?
Lamia then leisurely turned, lifted her skirt in a salute, and said, "Thank you for your care; we'll be taking our leave now."
"What are you doing? Hurry up and come help! If I weren't here watching, you wouldn't even have a chance to catch your breath—"
Upon hearing this, Lilith immediately became unhappy; she was barely surviving the danger by staring at the twenty-four statues, and if she stopped staring—
—wouldn't we all be doomed?
"Yeah, we haven't fully gotten past the danger yet; you'd better not burn the bridge after crossing the river. After we deal with these statues, wouldn't it be better for everyone to leave safely together?" Podom said, utterly bewildered.
"I came here to seek treasure, but since there isn't any, I naturally have no reason to stay. After barely stabilizing these dangerous statues, if I don't leave now, am I an idiot? I've never fully trusted you demons." Lamia said calmly, having judged that the demons were restrained here, she chose to leave. "Moreover, the idea that making the statues face each other can break them is just speculation; if it fails, we'll be stuck here forever, and I see no reason to give up my chance to escape."
"Using me to escape is truly despicable! I really regret not kicking you vampires off the ship before entering the ruins!" Lilith shouted angrily, and because she couldn't blink, her eyes grew even more sore.
"Indeed, you lot aren't trustworthy, abandoning us here while you flee." Podom's magic surged, and he felt an urge to strike and teach them a lesson.
"I haven't forced you to stay here, have you? You could completely leave that demon lady here and go with us; want to consider it?" Lamia said with a meaningful tone, having noticed that Lilith was already bound here, she chose—
—to take the opportunity to leave.
"What did you say?" Podom jumped at Lamia's words; it wasn't a bad idea, but his loyalty prevented him from doing such a thing.
"What nonsense are you spouting!? Wanting to sacrifice me—you'll surely die!" Lilith felt a bit panicked and instinctively called out to her brother: "Brother, you wouldn't do that, would you?"
Merlin didn't bother to answer; although he often fought and scolded his sister, he could never abandon her—clearly Lamia was trying to provoke him.
"Miss Lamia, I really underestimated you; you are truly a person who puts profit above all."
"I'm merely making the decision most advantageous to myself at the right moment; you would prioritize protecting your demon comrades, and I likewise will protect my own subordinates. My subordinate Vadiye has already fallen, and I cannot allow Mahmud to also be endangered. If the one who just stood at the rear were your subordinate, I believe you would certainly empathize with my feelings." Lamia had resolved to part ways here; the ruins were fraught with danger, and since there was an escape opportunity, how could she choose to give it up?
"Cain will surely kill you sooner or later; don't you want my help? I've seen Cain myself—you can't defeat her alone, but with my assistance your odds would be great." Merlin suddenly said, hoping to temporarily stall Lamia.
"That condition is indeed tempting, but these statues are too dangerous; if your method fails, it will inevitably sacrifice someone, and I won't take that risk." Lamia touched the half of the God‑Seizing Stone Throne behind Mahmud's back and said, "My goal in entering the ruins has, in a sense, been achieved—the weapons forged from the God‑Seizing Stone will be my greatest reliance in defeating Cain."
"Believe me, you will die." Merlin said in a grave tone; he clearly remembered that Cain had used some unknown method to copy his and Alice's abilities, and is no longer something that can be defeated with just a God‑Seizing Stone weapon.
"You'd better first assess your own situation; finding a way to leave here alive is what you should worry about." Lamia turned coldly, not looking back, and said, "Mahmud, let's go."
Merlin's eye twitched; seeing Lamia unwilling to cooperate, he couldn't help but grip the hilt of his waist‑borne knife, wanting to act.
Although Merlin lacked Mister‑Potin's blessing and thus could hardly kill a vampire of Lamia's level, he could still make her feel a suffocating pain.
"Mr. Merlin, don't waste time; your sister looks like she's about to give out." Lamia reminded him without turning back; she didn't fear Merlin, but worried that Merlin would spare no expense to drag her down with him to mutual destruction.
"Brother, my eyes feel so sore, I really want to blink," Lilith complained, already beginning to desperately prop up her eyelids with both hands.
"Ugh!" Merlin couldn't suppress his anger and couldn't afford to waste time arguing with Lamia—
"Podom! Let's move faster!"
"Lilith, hold on a bit longer!"
Outside, on the airship.
Without the threat of dark creatures, Jacob gained a brief freedom and could finally act recklessly.
Glug‑glug‑glug‑glug‑glug, Jacob gulped down the era‑of‑gods strong liquor, his face turning bright red.
"Burp."
"Damn dark creatures, not even putting me in their sights?"
"Just because you're strong doesn't mean you're amazing—I'm the son of the world's richest man!"
"When this young master gets back, I'll bury you all with money! Merlin will have to obediently lick my shoes!"
Jacob was already quite drunk, his speech incoherent; emboldened by the alcohol, he dared even to criticize Merlin.
He staggered to his feet holding the bottle, stroked the airship's rudder, and couldn't help but show excitement on his face.
"What a great thing, hehehe—future Jacob Airways will be famous worldwide! Everyone will be proud to board the airship!"
"What are these things used for?"
The drunken Jacob eyed the various levers beside the rudder; normally he wouldn't dare to mess with them, but now it's different—
Jacob giggled and haphazardly manipulated the airship's levers; the click‑clack of turning gears rang nonstop, as if some mechanism had been activated.
With a thunderous roar, the airship shuddered; a hatch suddenly opened on the deck, and a huge ancient magic cannon slowly rose.
"What the—??" Jacob, frightened, clung to his bottle and ducked into
—the corner, sobering up a bit.
One could see the gears around the ancient magic cannon turning nonstop, directly aiming the barrel at the artificial sun in the sky, boom—
—a tremendous blast; the ancient magic cannon's power exceeds that of France's legendary magic cannon by a third, twisting the surrounding space slightly!
Golden cannonfire shot out, comparable to a volcanic lava plume shooting tens of thousands of feet into the sky, striking the sun forged by the ancient gods!
As they watched the ruin world plunge into endless darkness, Jacob, clutching his bottle, broke out in a cold sweat—
"Ah!!!"
"The…"
"Sun… gone?"

title: Chapter 21 — Darkness Descends (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 21 — Darkness Descends (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 31 · Chapter 21

The entire ruin world instantly plunged into pitch-black darkness, the light so dim that one could not see their own hand even at close range.

Jacob trembled all over, feeling as though he had committed a grave error, wondering in his heart whether Merlin would kill him upon his return.

A massive sound of cracking echoed through the air as the sky fractured further. Where the God-Created Sun had once been, a void appeared, with fierce winds constantly rushing out from it and the sound of waves audible in the distance.

Jacob suddenly felt a chilling breeze sweep past his head, allowing him to barely make out the figures of Mahmud and Lamia flying straight toward the void.

"Miss Lamia! The ship is here! What are you doing?" Jacob shouted loudly, but received no response. "Strange? Why aren't you paying attention to me?"

Mahmud spread huge crimson membrane wings on his back; despite his sturdy build, he remained incredibly swift even while carrying half of the Throne of Sealing Stone.

Lamia sat on Mahmud's shoulder, constantly urging her subordinates to fly toward the crack in the sky. If she guessed correctly, that was the exit of the ruins.

The two had escaped the main hall very smoothly, as the statues within the passage were almost entirely concentrated in the main hall, making returning along the same path completely safe.

If there had been any statue blocking the way during their retreat, neither Lamia nor Mahmud would have been able to leave the castle so easily.

Originally, Lamia had planned to find a way to locate the exit of the ruins after escaping, but unexpectedly, an intoxicated Jacob had pointed the way for her!

"Lady Lamia, is that really the exit?" Mahmud asked, carrying Lamia and the Sealing Stone, feeling somewhat uneasy in his heart.

"It should be correct. We entered from the sea, and faint sounds of waves can be heard coming from within the crack; it should connect to the outside world," Lamia stated definitively.

Mahmud responded with a low hum, fully stirring the blood wings on his back, while Lamia gently stroked the Sealing Stone, thinking— With this stone, I have the conditions to kill Cain. Who should I look for to help me forge weapons after we get out? Time was running short.

Due to the overly dim sky, Jacob could only judge by shadows that Mahmud and Lamia had disappeared into the crack in the sky, causing a thought to strike him.

No way? Is the crack in the sky the exit?

If I sneak away now piloting the Sky Ship, it seems I can achieve safety.

No, no, no. If Lord Merlin returns and finds that I slipped away, he definitely won't let me off.

But I've caused such a huge disaster; even if I stay here, it seems Lord Merlin wouldn't spare me anyway, right?

The timid Jacob felt anxious, pondered for a long time, and finally decided to play a trick of "creating something out of nothing." He looked at the wine bottle in his hand, gritted his teeth, and smashed it against his own head.

*Thud.* Jacob swayed unsteadily, sticking out his tongue with stars dancing before his eyes, feigning dizziness and collapsing to the ground to create the illusion of having been attacked by enemies.

Time returned to before the destruction of the God-Created Sun. Because Lamia had left with Mahmud, there were not enough people in the main hall, causing Merlin and Pudom to frantically move the statues, making them face each other.

"Brother, hurry up!" Lilith supported her heavy eyelids with both hands, her eyeballs nearly rolling back. "I feel like my vision is getting a bit blurry..."

"Lilith! Hold on! Almost! It'll be over soon!" Merlin carried the heavy statue, not forgetting to encourage Lilith.

"Your Majesty, I-I'm a magician, my physical stamina is really, really poor," Pudom leaned against the statue, sweating profusely and breathing heavily; after moving just the tenth statue, he was already exhausted to this state.

"Put some effort into it! Didn't you say your family has practiced martial arts for generations, with everyone being a strong warrior?! Now is the time to show some usefulness!" Merlin was so angry his nose seemed crooked.

"That is true, but among our family, only I am a magician. When I first learned to use magic, my father once thought I was the illegitimate child of my mother and the uncle next door," Pudom wiped the sweat from his face, feeling very embarrassed.

"Cut the nonsense, get to work!" Merlin urged loudly.

"Yes... yes..." Pudom answered weakly, not forgetting to mutter a curse under his breath. "Those damn vampires, truly low-level dark creatures without any historical heritage..."

[♂EZ Reading♂is♂the♂only♂site♂with♂the♂fastest♂updates♂for♂this♂novel♂]

The two raced against time, striving hard, and finally, before Lilith could hold on any longer, they arranged twenty-four pairs of statues facing each other, their eyes staring directly at one another—

Merlin examined everything again, and after confirming there were no problems, said, "Lilith, relax a bit, it's done."

"I'm finally dead tired," Lilith collapsed from the abandoned fountain pedestal, her delicate body falling limp.

Merlin stared closely at the twenty-four statues, then tried blinking his eyes, discovering that this method worked; the statues facing each other did not move at all!

Although the statues varied in form, their empty, lifeless eyes gazed at each other, causing them to mutually confirm each other's presence and preventing them from breaking free from their petrified state.

Pudom also tried blinking his eyes and was instantly overjoyed. "It worked? These statues are staring at each other and really won't move?! Your Majesty is truly a genius! Hahaha!"

"What is this?" Merlin secretly exhaled in relief in his heart, glad that his hypothesis was correct. Although these statues transformed from the grudges of ancient gods were dangerous, their weaknesses were equally obvious.

"Brother! While those vampires haven't gone far, let's chase them out and settle the score!" Lilith, recalling Lamia's expression before leaving, wished she could tear the other woman apart.

Just as Merlin was about to speak, a thunderous roar suddenly disrupted the quiet castle. Outside, Jacob had inadvertently triggered the ancient magical cannon, destroying the God-Created Sun.

The entire castle began to rumble violently, fine dust and gravel rattling down, hitting Lilith on her forehead.

"W-what's going on???"

Before the words had finished falling, the entire ruin world plunged into darkness, including the castle itself, which became pitch black with not a single ray of light visible.

Lost in the absence of light, the statues could no longer see each other and began to regain their freedom. The stable situation they had painstakingly established was shattered in an instant.

Moreover, what was even more fatal was that Merlin, Pudom, and Lilith also couldn't see the statues. This gave the monsters complete liberation, as darkness was the perfect breeding ground for their rampage—

The originally facing statues regained their freedom in the darkness, awakening from their petrified state. They stretched their limbs recklessly, their arms rubbing against each other, producing dense *rustling* sounds.

The statues revealed sinister smiles, turning their gazes toward the three intruders, with mocking laughter echoing around them. They could no longer restrain their hunger and wanted to enjoy a delicious dinner.

"Your Majesty, I don't feel quite right," Pudom moved closer to Merlin.

Lilith couldn't see anything, but the strange noises coming from around her made her scalp tingle. "Brother, can they move freely in the night?"

"This is bad." Merlin bit his lower lip, realizing the situation had exceeded his expectations. The sudden darkness had created the most perfect environment for the statues' activity—in the pitch-black night where one cannot see their own hand, these monsters were invincible.

title: Chapter 22 — Kraken's Heart
content:
Chapter 22 — Kraken's Heart

Volume 31 · Chapter 22

A rustling sound echoed from all directions, growing steadily closer.

A bead of cold sweat slid down Merlin's forehead as he realized he had been completely surrounded; every escape route had been sealed off.

The stone statues were monsters that fed on life force—God only knew how long they had starved within this castle. Seeing fresh prey, they all seemed utterly frenzied.

"Brother, what do we do?" Lilith tugged at Merlin's sleeve repeatedly, clearly in a panic.

"These monsters can't be killed, and even vampires with immortality can't withstand them. How are we supposed to fight this?" Puthum felt a chill run through him, keeping watch over the pitch-black surroundings.

"Calm down. We won't die here—at least we can still take a chance. It all depends on whether we're lucky or not," Merlin said gravely.

"Take a chance? Ugh." Puthum's eye twitched. Having served Merlin for so many years, if he remembered correctly, Merlin's luck had always been terrible.

"Get close to me!"

The stone statues' mocking voices closed in. Merlin snarled and slashed his sword viciously at the ground beneath his feet. With a crackling sound, the floor split apart, revealing a gaping fissure.

According to the castle's structure, the main hall was at the very top, so if they jumped down through the broken floor, they could temporarily shake off the threat of the stone statues.

However, Merlin had no idea whether the underground was safe—whether even more ferocious monsters than the stone statues were guarding below. That would all depend on luck.

Accompanied by Lilith's continuous cries of alarm, Merlin and the others kept falling, the rushing wind howling in their ears, until they finally crashed onto something much harder.

Merlin gritted his teeth and slowly got up. Looking around at the pitch-black darkness, he couldn't judge his position within the castle at all—

"Lilith! Puthum! Are you alright?"

"My—my butt hurts so much!" came Lilith's voice from nearby.

"Your Majesty, in the future, please give me some warning beforehand so I can mentally prepare. I almost landed face-first just now," Puthum responded with clear resentment.

"I was just worried the stone statues could understand what we're saying, which would have ruined the plan," Merlin said. From their voices, he judged that Lilith and Puthum were right nearby, and he finally felt somewhat reassured.

"Where are we?" Puthum asked anxiously.

"Not sure. Probably the bottom floor of the castle?" Merlin guessed. He faintly caught a pungent lamp oil smell in the air and followed it by touch, bumping into a cold wall.

The wall was pitted and curved?

After thinking carefully, Merlin guessed these were the pillars supporting the castle. He continued grope along the side and suddenly grasped a wooden stick hanging on the wall.

A wooden stick? A thick lamp oil smell? This was...

Merlin's heart quickened. He quickly rubbed the stick in his hand against the wall. *Spark*—a flame burst forth. As expected, it was a torch!

After the Divine Sun was destroyed, the ruins fell into deep darkness. Finding a torch was more precious than discovering a divine artifact!

With the torch's light, the stone statues wouldn't dare approach easily, greatly limiting their ability to move freely.

"Hahaha! We have light!" Merlin laughed, feeling considerably relieved. He turned around ready to show Lilith and Puthum, but found the two of them sitting motionless on the cold ground—

Stone statues stood all around them in every direction. Since the torch's range of illumination was limited, they couldn't even count how many there were!

Judging by the dim shadows from afar, there were definitely no fewer than a hundred, almost filling the entire field of view, creating an illusion of being inside a Terracotta Army pit.

What was worse, the stone statues were all covering their hollow, lifeless eyes with their hands—the old trick of making them stare at each other was no longer effective!

Lilith and Puthum stared blankly at the stone statues surrounding them, so terrified that their legs went weak and they struggled even to stand.

Merlin's heart felt as though it had fallen into an bottomless abyss, his entire body going cold from head to toe. His luck really was bad to a certain degree—the area below was more dangerous than the main hall, and the number of stone statues had multiplied several times over!

"Have these bastards gotten smarter? Covering their eyes means they're afraid we'll pull the same trick again..."

Lilith snapped out of her daze, scrambling up on hands and knees and clinging to Merlin anxiously. "There are even more stone statues down here than above! We can't get out of this one, can we?"

Puthum blankly pulled out the *Book of Merlin's Sayings*, his hands trembling as he said, "I never imagined we'd be putting a period on it so soon..."

"Ugh..." Merlin's brows locked together like a knot, suppressing his nervousness as he quietly listened to his surroundings. A subtle breeze brushed against his cheek, and suddenly an idea formed in his mind—

"Lilith, Puthum, both of you stay calm. We still have a chance."

"Your Majesty, there are too many stone statues here for us to keep track of. Can we really escape?" Puthum was deeply skeptical, finding it hard to believe this was possible.

"Y-yeah, I don't know why it's dark out, but we only have one torch and the illuminated area is very small," Lilith also looked deeply worried.

"Listen to me first. A full circle is 360 degrees, and our binocular vision range is about 124 degrees. As long as we form a circle and use the torch's light, we can monitor all directions at once. We just need to be careful when moving," Merlin explained his plan concisely.

Lilith勉强 understood what Merlin meant but still said, "But where is the exit around here?"

"There." Merlin pointed to a direction in the darkness and said seriously, "Where there's wind, there's most likely an exit."

***

Inside the body of the Kraken, Leviathan dragged his battered corpse, limping forward through the vast blood vessels.

Leviathan supported himself against the hard flesh walls, and upon touch, he could feel the Kraken's powerful heartbeat.

He stopped and looked ahead. *Thump, thump, thump.* The heavy heartbeat pulsed steadily.

After searching relentlessly, Leviathan had finally found what he was looking for: using the Kraken's heart to repair his own body.

Leviathan's consciousness had long begun to blur. His body felt endlessly exhausted, unable to sense any pain at all. Though his frame was already riddled with wounds, half corroded away,

the current Leviathan was near death. He was holding on purely by sheer willpower, forcing his consciousness from dissipating. Any person would sigh that this was a miracle!

Leviathan's gaze was unfocused. After passing through an opening while supporting himself on the walls, the space suddenly opened up before him—a massive chamber, with countless thick blood vessels connecting to a pitch-black mass of flesh.

This was the Kraken's heart, its *thump, thump, thump* beating powerfully. An inexplicable energy radiated from within.

Seeing that black heart, Leviathan's scattered eyes gradually cleared somewhat, like a traveler in a desert discovering an oasis. His adrenaline surged rapidly. Biting his teeth, he used his remaining arm to stab fiercely into the heart—

"I…"

"I'm going to live…"

title: Chapter 23 — Sea Monster Melee
content:
Chapter 23 — Sea Monster Melee

Volume 31 · Chapter 23

Dark clouds rolled, lightning flashed, and a crack appeared in the sky. Mahamud shook his blood wings, carrying Lamia out through the crack!

The Kraken had been waiting for the rats to emerge from the ruins. Seeing Lamia and Mahamud, it immediately became excited, waving its tentacles to surround them, wanting to kill all outsiders peeking at the ruins' secrets!

Eight huge tentacles swept across the sea, splashing layers of waves, blocking Lamia and Mahamud's escape route from eight directions. Endless shadows loomed over their heads.

"!?!" A drop of cold sweat rolled down Lamia's forehead. She hadn't expected this. "After so long, the Kraken still hasn't left?! The ruins are almost empty, what is it obsessed with?!"

"What do we do? Master Lamia, no way out!" Mahamud hovered in the air, feeling enormous pressure.

Suddenly, the Kraken stopped attacking and retracted all its tentacles.

It let out a deafening roar of pain, its massive body rolling in the sea as if the entire ocean were boiling, constantly churning.

The Kraken's pain didn't seem fake. The monster had gone crazy. Normally lurking in the deep sea, it had now surfaced unprecedentedly to reveal its true form—

A head the size of a mountain gradually appeared, covered in black meat spines, two lantern-like big eyes glowing with red light, terrifying!

"Wh-What's happening?" Lamia wondered. She hadn't attacked the Kraken at all, so why was it in such pain?

Through the lightning's glow, they could vaguely see something being expelled from the Kraken's body into the pitch-black seawater—dragon-shaped, small in size.

"Kraken, it's... female? It lays eggs?" Mahamud looked weird, unsure if his guess was right.

"Uh..." Lamia tightened her face. Though she didn't want to admit Mahamud's guess, it really did look like laying eggs. "Wait! Something's wrong!"

The dragon-shaped creature expelled from its body kept swelling in the deep sea. In a flash of lightning, it had already grown to a size no inferior to the Kraken!

This wasn't the Kraken's egg at all, but a sea monster similar to the Kraken!

"Pu!" Waves shot up to over a hundred feet into the sky. As the water spray scattered, a pitch-black sea dragon appeared out of nowhere!

The sea-dragon-like monster roared to the heavens, as if venting resentment accumulated deep within. Its scales shone brilliantly in the darkness!

It spread twelve huge membrane wings behind it, thick demonic horns on its head—this was the fully powered Leviathan!

Leviathan had eaten the Kraken's heart. Its overall strength had even enhanced compared to before, not inferior to the Kraken by much.

Betrayed by despicable outsiders, the Kraken's rage surged. It wrapped its tentacles around Leviathan's body and dragged it into the sea.

Leviathan didn't back down either. Its snake-like body wrapped around the Kraken, biting its head with teeth.

The two monsters fought bloody slaughter in the sea, causing massive waves, white foam mixed with blood rolling endlessly.

The Kraken shrieked, slashing open Leviathan's blood-filled mouth with one palm. Eight tentacles moved together, trying to lock the enemy's movements.

Leviathan was secretly shocked. Having eaten its heart, why was it still so energetic? What tenacious vitality! No wonder no one dared provoke this monster at sea!

In desperation, Leviathan lifted its head high. Twelve eyes suddenly opened, its whole body glowing red, gathering toward its mouth. A stream of flame continuously rose!

Leviathan didn't believe the heartless Kraken could still be so powerful. It prepared to defeat the enemy with a fierce attack. No matter how tenacious the vitality, without a heart there would be an effect.

The completed Demon Light Cannon shot out. At the critical moment, the Kraken used its powerful tentacles to whip Leviathan's head hard, forcing the cannon off course, shooting into the empty sea beside them!

The light swept directly across the sea plane, immediately causing a violent explosion. Seawater sprayed into the sky, forming a kilometer-high water wall!

Mahamud and Lamia swayed in the turbulence, barely maintaining flight.

Lamia watched the two sea monsters fight, feeling very fearful. With her own eyes, she couldn't see the complete bodies of the Kraken and Leviathan at all.

Having lived so long, Lamia had never seen such terrifying monsters fighting. It was as if they were going to overturn the world!

"Mahamud, let's leave quickly! Their fight is too intense. If we wait any longer, we'll get caught in it!"

In the castle of Odin's Garden within the Ruins of the Gods.

Merlin, Lilith, and Podom formed a circle, staring outward at the maximum range they could see.

The three moved slowly outside the castle by torchlight. They dared not blink, staring hard at their surroundings.

As soon as they blinked, stone statues would approach, entering the torchlight range, trying to kill the outsiders.

Within the torchlight range it was quiet, but in the darkness beyond the torchlight, sounds of statues moving frequently echoed, chasing the three relentlessly.

Lilith: "Brother, I want to blink..."

Podom: "Your Majesty, I want to..."

"Hold on, you should be leaving the castle soon. Now if you blink, they'll move quickly over—faster than you imagine." Sweat had long seeped through Merlin's forehead. This was not the time to relax.

"Can we really escape?" Lilith doubted, feeling countless eyes staring at her from the darkness.

"Possible. As long as we escape the castle, there won't be so many statues outside." Merlin said seriously.

Merlin held the torch high. The three moved slowly with the wind in the darkness, finally reaching the castle entrance from before.

On both sides outside the door, two tall Valkyrie statues stood, seemingly lifeless, motionless even in the darkness.

"Temporarily safe." Merlin stopped walking. Worried the large group of statues behind would catch up, he said without turning back, "You go first. I'll watch from behind."

"What? Let's go together!" Lilith was unwilling to slip away first, leaving Merlin here.

"You and Podom board the ship first. I'll catch up after. Don't worry, nothing will happen." Merlin paused, staring tightly at the darkness in the corridor. The small entrance provided a big advantage—just watch one direction, and the statues couldn't rush out—

"Your speed is too slow. You'll drag me down."

"I can escape on my own, but with you it would be trouble."

title: Chapter 24 — The Fish That Got Away
content:
Chapter 24 — The Fish That Got Away

Volume 31 · Chapter 24

”Enough with the maybe, do you know how much effort I have to disperse to take care of you all? You being safe is the biggest help to me.” Merlin’s tone became much harsher.

”Yeah, Alice-sama, the Queen is right. We shouldn’t drag the Queen down anymore. Let’s get back to the airship sooner, and the Queen will feel much more at ease.” Pudom agreed from the side.

”Then, brother, remember to come back quickly. I’ll meet you on the ship.” Lililys frowned, then turned and left with Pudom.

Merlin stood alone at the castle entrance, holding a torch, staring intently forward in case statues rushed out from the castle, to make way for Lililys and Pudom.

Pudom and Lililys returned to the airship at the fastest speed. They secretly heaved a sigh of relief that the lamia hadn’t stolen the airship, otherwise there would be quite a bit of trouble.

At this moment, the four crystals on the altar on the deck were burning fiercely, bringing light to the airship, making the two returnees feel much more at ease—

Lililys searched about and couldn’t find Jacob’s figure. That rich man’s silly son? Where did he go! ³

”Over there!” Pudom saw the unconscious Jacob lying on the cold floor, so he hurried forward and slapped him twice awake! Wake up! Wake up! ³

Jacob’s two cheeks instantly swelled up. He slowly woke up, looking utterly confused,” You guys came back? ³

”How did you end up fainting here? What happened?” Lililys asked directly.

”I I” Jacob stammered, organizing his words in his mind, just about to speak when Pudom beat him to it.

”I got it! It must be that vampire Lamia who knocked you unconscious, right?” Pudom thought this was very possible.

Jacob’s eyes instantly lit up, and he nodded vigorously,” Exactly! It was Lamia and that big guy. They suddenly boarded the ship and wanted to use the magic cannon. I tried to stop them, but I couldn’t! Look! They destroyed the sun here, and then followed the crack in the sky and left…”

”Damn vampires! I should have killed it earlier! Almost got us killed!” Lililys was anxious with regret, wanting to bite Lamia to death.

”These vampires, too despicable!” Pudom looked up at the crack in the sky,” But since they left from there, it should be the exit of the ruins. Now we can save a lot of searching time.” ”Where is that Merlin adult? I don’t see him.” Jacob curiously looked around, but didn’t see Merlin’s figure.

”His Majesty will be back soon.” Pudom looked toward the castle, waiting for Merlin to return, and then leave this ghostly place together. 9674;

Merlin stood at the castle entrance, though everything was quiet within the torchlight.

But in the darkness, the low roars of the statues occasionally came, evidently because they couldn’t eat fresh flesh, they had become very anxious.

Merlin felt the time was almost up. Lililys and Pudom had already safely reached the airship, waiting for him to return.

So Merlin inserted the torch into the ground, allowing himself to clearly see the situation at the castle entrance, in case the statues rushed out regardless of anything.

And he himself walked backward very cautiously, his gaze always fixed on the castle entrance.

Merlin planned to walk backward far enough, then turn around and rush back to the airship at full speed. Because the statues’ movement was similar to instant teleportation, their speed was extremely fast. The most stable way was to create enough safe distance so the statues couldn’t catch up.

However, while Merlin was walking backward, he somehow tripped and fell face-first.

It turned out that the two statues outside had been ambushing there. Seeing Merlin walking backward without looking behind, they deliberately stretched out a leg to trip him.

Merlin quickly climbed up from the ground and suddenly turned his head, discovering that when he fell, the torch inserted into the ground had been extinguished by the statues.

In the darkness, all the statues regained their freedom of movement. Even the two giant statues outside began to stretch their muscles and bones, and blurry shadows enveloped above Merlin’s head.

Large sweat pearls slid down Merlin’s forehead. He decisively chose to turn his head and run. In the dark, looking at the statues behind him while walking backward was meaningless!

Merlin, sprinting at full speed, left a trailing shadow at the spot. Like an arrow released from a string, he was already a hundred meters away in one step!

Hearing the sound chasing from behind, getting closer and closer, Merlin’s heart sank. He really had underestimated this group of statues too much.

Merlin was already very close to the position where the airship was docked. The statues behind were biting hard. To prevent these monsters from boarding the ship, the airship had to take off early, and then he could think of other ways to get on.

”Start the airship quickly! ! ! ³

”Huh? Sounds like brother’s voice?” Lililys twitched her ears. From the sound, she felt Merlin was already very close.

Pudom heard the signal coming from the darkness and immediately kicked Jacob,” Didn’t you hear! Quick, go start the ship!”

Jacob crawled and scrambled to the driver’s seat, making the airship slowly rise. From time to time, he looked toward the castle direction, finding that the sky was too dark, and the entire ruin was like a piece of chaos.

Lililys stood at the edge of the ship. In a daze, she saw a figure rushing over quickly. She immediately whipped her whip, precisely wrapping it around Merlin’s waist.

”Come up!”

As the airship rose, Lililys also pulled Merlin from the ground. The group continuously moved higher and escaped.

Merlin lowered his head slightly. In the blur, he discovered that many statues, because they were chasing too urgently, had already fallen from the suspended garden.

He had just barely let out a sigh of relief, but then felt his feet grabbed by something. Looking down, his face changed dramatically—

Blurry statue shadows, as if building a human ladder below, hard-knockedly dragging their companions up. The topmost statue had already grabbed Merlin’s foot, and many black shadows were climbing up!

”Tch!” Merlin only felt a chill run down his spine. These monsters would eventually climb onto the ship!

Lililys was desperately trying to pull Merlin up. Suddenly she felt Merlin below was incredibly heavy, almost pulling her down too. She had to use her feet to support the ship board,” Why is it suddenly so heavy?! Pudom, come help!”

”Ah?” Pudom realized something was wrong and hurriedly went over, gritting his teeth and helping to pull. But below, so many statues were grabbing Merlin, how could two mages pull him up?

The rising airship was also affected, unable to continue climbing, being pulled hard by the statues, the ship’s body began to vibrate violently, at risk of failure at any moment.

Merlin made a decisive move, pulling out his sword and slashing at his own foot. The sharp killing intent sword qi shattered the statue grabbing him below. Not seeking to kill them, only to temporarily escape.

Although the statues recovered very quickly, the short time was enough for Merlin to escape, and the airship began to climb rapidly. The stone human figures below collapsed thunderously.

Merlin looked at the gradually receding suspended garden below. His heart finally settled, and his desire to obtain Mist’s wish became even stronger.

After successfully boarding the ship, Lililys was overjoyed and threw herself into Merlin’s arms, worriedly asking,” Brother, how are you? Any injuries?”

”Are you okay, Your Majesty,” Pudom said with lingering fear.

”I’m fine, pretty good.” Merlin smiled, raising a thumb at everyone,” Finally we can leave this ghostly place. It seems the countless-chased gods’ ruins are just a mirage like existence.”

Everyone thought they were already safe. However—

One statue had secretly boarded the ship, clinging to the bottom of the airship.

The black environment provided the best cover for it, and even Merlin didn’t notice this missed fish.

Its hollow eyes scanned about, and it began to move stealthily.

title: Chapter 25 — Capture
content:
Chapter 25 — Capture

Volume 31 · Chapter 25

Merlin looked at the ring of "Angel" in his hand and felt that after all this busyness, the收获 wasn't much.

The most useful thing was finding a large chunk of Divine-Deification Stone, so two of the three materials needed to forge Mistilteinn were already obtained. The last one he still lacked was a god's soul.

Where on earth was he supposed to find this ghostly thing? Merlin had absolutely no idea. Was he really expected to hunt down a god somewhere and kill it?

As far as Merlin knew, the recognized gods were the Goddess of the Heavenly Realm and the ruler of the Underworld, but both of them resided in other planes.

As for the mortal world? Merlin only knew that the demon race ancestors sealed beneath the Blood Pool possessed the status of gods and belonged to the camp of the Ancient Gods.

Merlin had no intention of going after the ancestors beneath the Blood Pool seal. If he meddled with that seal, he'd risk becoming a sinner for all generations.

Whether or not he could defeat the First Ancestor was another matter. The trouble was that all the first-generation demons were connected by bloodline to the Demon Gods. If a Demon God were killed, all the first-generation demons would die along with it.

Merlin, a third-generation demon, had nothing to worry about himself, but he had to consider the old-timers within the demon race—some first-generation demons were still alive.

Puthom stood quietly on the deck, gazing afar at the ruin world immersed in darkness, lost in thought.

"Puthom, what are you spacing out for?" Lilith asked curiously.

"I-I'm fine," Puthom turned around awkwardly and said meaningfully, "This is a place where the Prophet once fought. After we leave, we'll never see it again."

"Oh? You admire the Prophet that much?" Lilith raised an eyebrow.

"No, no, no, I admire Your Majesty the most, but the Prophet is a special existence. His deeds still have a huge impact today." Puthom paused and said melancholy, "It's just a pity that the demon race's records contain very little about the Prophet. Why is there no detailed biography even of such a great demon? It's too strange."

"What's strange about that? Perhaps during the Holy War at the end of the Demon Era, many important books were burned. My mother once told me that the Holy War was extremely fierce. The demons, in their rush to flee to the Demon Lord Palace for refuge, only brought food with them. Books were long since burned for warmth along the way. Most of the books in the demon race's library now have been recompiled based on the memories of some elders." Lilith felt that the scarce records about the Prophet were normal; after all, the demon race had suffered a great catastrophe.

"That's true. If there's a chance, I must collect everything about the Prophet and tell the young demons stories about this great demon." Puthom made up his mind; he had always dreamed of becoming a disseminator of culture.

"How long has the Prophet been gone? Such a vague figure isn't worth understanding." Lilith shrugged and came over to Merlin's side. "Right, big brother〜"

"Huh? What?" Merlin was still thinking about Mistilteinn and hadn't paid attention to Puthom and Lilith's casual chat at all.

"What are you thinking about? Surely not that human wild woman again?! Damn brother!" Lilith angrily grabbed Merlin's clothes.

"Let go! What nonsense is that?" Merlin frowned, thinking that once they left the ruins, he'd have to find a way to coax Lilith back.

Just as the siblings were about to start fighting, Jacob, who was piloting the skyship, suddenly shouted,

"Lord Merlin! We're out!"

Merlin pushed away the clingy Lilith and discovered the skyship had passed through the crack and left the ruins.

The skyship sailed through the sky, with rolling dark clouds appearing extremely oppressive, and occasional lightning flashing within the cloud layers.

"Pfft!" A sound like a depth charge echoed, and a hundred-foot wall of water splashed into the sky!

Merlin came to the edge of the skyship and looked down, plainly seeing Leviathan and the Kraken engaged in a deathmatch. Although Kraken had the upper hand slightly, it would be hard to determine a winner in the short term.

Leviathan and the Kraken entwined and tore at each other, the two monsters churning up the sea endlessly. Terrifying waves spread outward, and the small island that had appeared earlier was long submerged.

"Leviathan?!"

"Huh?" Lilith quickly came over, her eyes wide. "This guy isn't dead?"

"It looks like Lord Leviathan has recovered his strength? How did he manage that?" Puthom was puzzled in his heart.

"This guy's vitality is tougher than I imagined." Merlin observed his surroundings and found that the waters around were all pitch-black like ink; his ability to provide assistance was limited. "I need to think of something to help him."

"Lord Merlin, um, that stone statue—did you bring it aboard?" Jacob suddenly said in a confused tone.

"Stone statue? What stone statue?" Merlin asked in surprise, then his eyes widened in horror—

That escaped stone statue had quietly climbed aboard and suddenly appeared on the祭台 (altar) on the skyship's deck, its hand already pressing against the four-sided crystal that provided energy for the ship.

"N-no way…! They actually followed us aboard?!" Lilith's face went pale in an instant. She hadn't expected stone statues to come onto the ship!

"It—it seems to be trying to destroy the magic power source created by the goblins!" Puthom cried out anxiously.

Before the words had finished, the blazing four-sided crystal in the stone statue's hand was instantly extinguished!

With the light from the magic power source gone, the surroundings became dim and dark.

The skyship simultaneously lost its energy source, and after violent shaking, it began to rapidly plummet. At this altitude, hitting the sea surface would shatter them to pieces!

"The ship isn't responding! " Jacob panicked,

frantically pressing the helm, but the skyship didn't rise at all, continuing to fall toward the sea surface.

Merlin's expression grew grave. In the gloomy sky beneath the rolling dark clouds, he could no longer find the shadow of that stone statue. It must be lurking in the dark, beginning to hunt.

Aside from the threat of the stone statue, the skyship's descent was equally dangerous. If they couldn't stop it in time, everyone would be within the attack range of the Kraken.

Occasional flashes of lightning lit up the sky, giving a brief glimpse of the surroundings. The stone statue appeared from time to time, each time striking a different bizarre pose, making it impossible to accurately judge its position.

"Brother! Should we bailskip the ship?!" Lilith suddenly asked.

"No! Too dangerous!" Merlin gritted his teeth and ordered, "Puthom, go fix the magic power source! Lilith, you assist Puthom and watch out for the stone statue! The priority is to repair the skyship!"

Puthom acknowledged and stumbled over to begin checking the four-sided crystal, with Lilith following behind to help keep watch.

Merlin tried his best to stay calm, his eyes fixed on Jacob in the pilot's seat. He reasoned that the stone statue would definitely target the weakest person!

He was relatively strong, and Lilith and Puthom together were harder to deal with, so the easiest target for the stone statue should logically be Jacob.

But just behind Merlin, a chilling voice suddenly sounded—

"Everything about you… belongs to me now."

title: Chapter 26 — The Curse's Secret
content:
Chapter 26 — The Curse's Secret

Volume 31 · Chapter 26

Merlin slightly turned his head and saw the smile on the statue, which proved that his body was fusing into the statue. He never expected the enemy to come straight for him instead of going for the soft persimmon!

He could clearly feel his life force being devoured by the statue. No wonder even vampires couldn't resist; their surging life force was the best food for the statue!

At this moment, Pudom was looking down at the status of the four crystals, hoping to save the airship. Lilith was standing by to prevent the statue from attacking Pudom. ★EZ look book★EZ look book★EZ look book★

Jacob had no effect at all, clutching the helm and trembling all over. He kept praying in his heart, hoping to survive by luck.

Merlin tried to seek help, but no matter how he shouted, his throat couldn't make a sound. His life force being devoured left him exhausted, and even struggling seemed powerless.

He finally knew how Wadiya died silently. Being entangled by this kind of monster, it was basically hard to escape, and life would be completely devoured by the invisible consumption.

This feeling was very similar to when Cain bit into it; life force was rapidly flowing away.

If it continued, being devoured by the statue would mean death, and triggering the curse after life force was exhausted would also mean death!

What to do? No one noticed my situation at all. Am I really going to die at the hands of this humble monster?

Merlin recalled the "Angie" ring. No matter how much of its sacred aura he disliked, now was not the time to complain!

So Merlin tried to grope in his pocket with his powerless hand. But at this time, the statue's erosion had reached the heart area.

Thump——

Merlin instantly felt his soul leave his body. Indeed, the curse on the heart was triggered, and the severe pain made his head unable to think.

The Angie ring slid out of Merlin's pocket, ding ding dong dong, falling to the ground, about three steps away from him!

But just a short distance of three steps, for Merlin at this moment, was also an uncrossable abyss!

Merlin's consciousness began to blur, and his heart became inactive. Trying to beat it once was incredibly difficult.

"Zo... lost..."

"Hmm?" Lilith heard the sound of the ring falling and tentatively called out, "Brother? Are you okay?"

"Okay! It's fine!" Pudom shouted, and he reassembled all the shattered crystals that the statue had crushed, allowing the magic source to activate again.

At the moment when the airship was about to crash into the sea, it suddenly erupted with huge upward force, causing the ship to start rising rapidly.

Jacob hurriedly lifted his head, looking at the airship rising continuously, beaming with joy. "Good? Goodness! Thank you for the blessing! I thought..."

The four crystals reignited with blazing flames. Remember this firelight, Lilith saw Merlin's state, "Brother!"

"This monster!" Pudom roared, and a magic book appeared in his hand.

Merlin's mind was already blurred, and his heart was almost stopping. His life force was almost being sucked dry by the statue.

"No! We must separate Brother from the statue!" Lilith waved the whip in her hand, lashing at the statue that was almost fused with Merlin.

Suddenly, a gale rose, making it hard for everyone to open their eyes. From Merlin's heart area, a brilliant golden light shot out, directly splitting a hole in the cloud layer of the sky!

A powerful artifact pressure made Pudom and Lilith both surprised. Even the Leviathan and the North Sea Monster fighting fiercely in the sea felt it!

The Leviathan lifted its huge head, noticing the airship in the sky. It wondered if it was Lucifer and the others? What was this pressure?

The North Sea Monster's big eyes, like red lanterns, rolled around. This pressure made it very agitated, becoming extremely berserk, struggling to break free from Leviathan's entanglement!

Obviously, compared to the Leviathan in front of it, the Kraken was more interested in the people on the ship, especially after feeling this unnamed pressure!

"What is this??" Jacob broke out in cold sweat, looking at the light appearing from Merlin's chest, and the whole person sat on the ground in fright.

Among the golden light, the statue let out a mournful cry, seeming to be very afraid, and its body gradually began to melt.

It fearfully pushed Merlin away, turning into a pile of mud and jumping into the pitch-black sea from the airship, instantly vanishing.

The light dispersed, and Merlin, powerless, fell to the ground. His clothes had been burned and ruined by the light, and the horrifying wound at the heart position on his chest was "hissing" and emitting white smoke.

"Brother!" Lilith rushed over and carefully checked Merlin's state, finding that her brother was lifeless, and immediately felt her eye sockets tighten, having an urge to cry, "What to do? I already... already can't feel any heartbeat..."

The statue had almost sucked dry Merlin's life force, directly triggering the curse.

If it weren't for the thing hidden deep in Merlin's heart releasing energy at the last moment, his body would probably have been completely cold by now.

"Lilith-sama, what was that just now?" Pudom walked over doubtfully, vaguely feeling that things weren't simple.

"Don't ask, Pudom." Lilith irritably responded, looking at Merlin's extremely dangerous situation, we must find a way!

"But..." Pudom was still curious.

" I said don't ask! Did you not hear me?!" Lilith angrily scolded.

"phew" Pudom knew he had touched something he shouldn't, so he hurriedly changed the topic, "The Majesty's life signs are becoming increasingly weak..."

As the Majesty's sister, Lilith was very familiar with Merlin's situation and knew that Merlin's heart had a curse. Looking at Merlin's current state, the curse must have been triggered!

In this critical situation, Lilith set her sights on the Banri Garan at Merlin's waist. She suddenly had an idea: if she used the Banri Garan to sacrifice herself, maybe she could save Merlin in time. After all, the Banri Garan had the power to seize life force, and the condition was Saint-tier or above; she also met the condition!

Disappointed, Lilith had to give up. Her legs went soft, and she knelt on the ground, looking at her brother's gradually cooling body, resenting her own incompetence.

"What is this?"

The North Sea Monster noticed the airship and directly couldn't help but stretch out a huge tentacle, smashing towards the airship, wanting to crush this eye-catching thing into pieces!

The Leviathan was greatly alarmed in its heart. On one hand, it entangled the North Sea Monster to restrict it, and on the other hand, it heavily slapped the sea surface with its huge tail, splashing waves hundreds of feet high!

The waves rushing straight up directly hit the hull of the airship, pushing it far away. Due to the Leviathan using too much force, the whole ship was almost knocked down!

Under the impact of the waves, the airship shook and vibrated. Lilith and the others couldn't stand steadily, falling to the ground. Merlin, lying on the ground, was even bumped up, falling from the airship into the deep sea!

"Brother!!"

In a certain mysterious cave, he met a mysterious person.

A golden flashing chisel was stabbed into his heart, granting him an unchanging destiny to move forward on the road of slaughter.

title: Chapter 27 — Twin Kings Counterattack the Kraken
content:
Chapter 27 — Twin Kings Counterattack the Kraken

Volume 31 · Chapter 27

Here it is famed as a forbidden land where demons enter but never exit, filled with toxic miasma and ferocious beasts. No demon would dare approach.

However, this place is also the burial ground of the first Lucifer, who was hailed as the strongest swordsman in history. In the last period before his death, he went alone to the valley, and ever since, there has been no news.

No one knows why the first Lucifer, instead of enjoying his last days properly, chose to enter the despair-ridden abyss gorge, where danger lurks. The reason is probably known only to him himself.

Young Merlin set out on a journey to train in the despair abyss to defeat the demon aristocracy and reclaim his mother Princess Vivian's throne, but he unexpectedly entered a hidden cave—

He met a mysterious man shrouded in a black robe, sitting cross-legged on a rock, unaware of how long he had lived in the cave, his body almost fused with the rock.

Young Merlin was weak at that time, and looking at him, there was not the slightest sign of becoming a swordsman. Compared to his peers, he was also a frail and sickly lot.

With such a weak body, it was a miracle that he could survive in the dangerous despair abyss.

Young Merlin looked at the mysterious person sitting on the rock. He had waist-length hair that dragged on the ground, making it hard to see his face, but one could feel a sharp, dangerous gaze more formidable than any beast.

"Hey! Who are you! You're being so mysterious here, and you don't look like a demon. This should be the territory of the demon race, and outsiders are not allowed to appear here!"

The mysterious man shuddered all over, slowly lifted his head, and stared at young Merlin without speaking. That sharp gaze seemed to look right through him in an instant.

"Eh! What is it! Stop acting mysterious, stand up and brush your hair aside, let me see if you're a person or a ghost!" Young Merlin reached for his waist, preparing to use his dagger for defense.

Swish...

The mysterious man's figure turned into a ghost, instantly appearing in front of young Merlin. This eerie speed was impossible to catch with the naked eye!

Young Merlin was greatly startled in his heart, and pulled out his dagger, intending to stab the mysterious man. "Die! Die!"

The strength gap between the two was vast, and the mysterious man easily grabbed young Merlin's wrist, twisting it lightly, and the dagger clattered and fell to the ground.

"Ugh, it hurts!" Young Merlin broke out in cold sweat all over. Unconsciously, he felt he might die here!

The mysterious man grabbed young Merlin's neck with one hand and threw him against the cold wall. From his embrace, he took out a gleaming golden cone, and a formidable artifact pressure spread out.

Young Merlin felt a suffocating sensation. No matter how he struggled, he could not escape this skinny palm. He desperately scratched the other's arm, but the other remained motionless, "Let go, let go of me!"

"My time is running out. What I say next is very important to you. Listen well."

"You have power that is truly real, but the conditions to freely control it are extremely harsh."

"One is to obtain a divine fragment and become the controller of the world's laws. Another is to put yourself in a dying state."

"If one of these two conditions is met, you can use the suppressed power at will."

"Remember this: never waver from your original thoughts. Only a coward would hesitate. Some people's sacrifice is the inevitable fate, and you cannot resist..."

As the voice fell, the mysterious man held the golden cone and fiercely stabbed it into young Merlin's heart, pushing it into his body.

"Mmm!"

Young Merlin suddenly opened his eyes, bubbled out a few bubbles, and continuously floated upward.

The surroundings were a pitch-black deep sea. Leviathan and the North Sea Monster were fighting with extreme intensity, and the dull thuds frequently echoed in his ears.

Young Merlin watched the sea surface where lightning flashed, and the waves kept surging. A small boat was hovering nearby. He felt his heart was paralyzed, his limbs lacked strength, and he could only keep falling.

Suddenly, red light lit up in the deep sea. The North Sea Monster's lantern-like large eyes fixed on the tiny Merlin in the sea. Its eight limbs swung together, twisting and rushing toward its prey.

[.Full-.]

[.New-.]

[.Fast-.]

[——Pursuit/——]

[——20070;——]

[,.K/,.]

At a critical moment, Leviathan sped through the deep sea, its huge body causing ripples. It opened its blood basin of a mouth and, without hesitation, swallowed Merlin.

The North Sea Monster's tentacles struck Leviathan, it cried out in pain, and continuously retreated, moving toward the sea surface.

Young Merlin reluctantly opened his eyes. The surroundings were all pink oral cavity interiors, and under his feet was a soft, huge pad, apparently Leviathan's tongue.

"Where is this?"

Young Merlin was just about to climb up, when suddenly his heart started to convulse, as if being tightly squeezed, about to crack!

He immediately lay on the ground, taking big breaths, which barely made him feel more comfortable.

The curse pain had long surpassed the past, and was becoming increasingly frequent. Young Merlin had already realized that his remaining life was limited, and he must rely on the power of Banri Garan to survive.

"You're in my mouth. If I just slightly move my tongue, you'll go into my stomach. How about it? Are you afraid?" Leviathan's voice echoed.

"This cold joke" Young Merlin grabbed his chest, and even forcing himself to endure, it was still painful, showing his teeth.

"You are in a very bad state now. Did something happen? Seeing you fall from that ship, I thought you came to support me, but you ended up falling into the sea and couldn't come up. You don't know how to swim, are you crazy?" Leviathan's tone was full of resentment. He had just thought that Merlin was about to come to help, and he was excited for a moment, who knew Merlin was just a burden, making himself get hit by a combo from the North Sea Monster, and his whole body hurt.

" I have nothing wrong with me" Young Merlin barely squeezed out a smile, but under the frequent convulsions of his heart, it made him look uglier than crying.

"Really? You're not made of mud, so why are you so weak after falling into the sea?" Leviathan was a bit suspicious, thinking that even if Merlin didn't know how to swim, it was too exaggerated.

"I'm fine." Young Merlin frowned and emphasized again, not intending to reveal his secret to others. Only Lilith knew about his cursed condition.

"Well, we must think of a way to kill the Kraken. This guy has gone mad and won't let us leave alive." Levianta had been fighting the North Sea Monster for a long time, and discovered that this monster was even more difficult to deal with than he had imagined!

Young Merlin endured the torture of his heart and gradually calmed down. His time was running out. "Can you drag the North Sea Monster out of the sea? Even if it's just for a moment."

"As long as it's just to make the Kraken temporarily leave the sea, is that okay?" Leviathan pondered for a moment and responded.

"I can try, but I can't guarantee success." It's weight is far beyond mine."

title: Chapter 28 — Sea Battle (Monthly Ticket Update)
content:
Chapter 28 — Sea Battle (Monthly Ticket Update)

Volume 31 · Chapter 28

Actually, it had already begun to ponder how to drag the Kraken's massive body out of the sea. Yet, attempting to lift a monster heavier than itself was, of course, an unimaginable feat.

The Kraken pursued relentlessly behind it, its eight thick tentacles flailing wildly, like a demon lost in a frenzy.

Having repeatedly been provoked by outsiders, the Kraken had gradually lost its reason, its sole desire being to slaughter this group of death-defying enemies!

The enemies who had previously fought it to the death were now fleeing wildly, which only fueled the Kraken's competitive spirit, making the tearing apart of its foes its singular thought.

Looking up at the sky from the deep sea, the wandering lightning seemed like a giant dragon roaring, but once it reached the depths, it became异常 quiet.

Two colossal monsters tangled in the sea, their slight movements capable of stirring up towering waves on the surface.

The Leviathan dashed upward, and as it was about to breach the surface, it glanced back at the Kraken's distance—

Seems about right.

The Leviathan suddenly abandoned its escape, turning instead like a galloping horse, charging head-on toward the oncoming Kraken.

The Kraken's gaze shifted, sensing something was amiss, and it hastily spread all its tentacles to prepare for the clash!

The Leviathan's body twisted and turned, avoiding a direct confrontation with the Kraken, instead using its long form to circle the enemy.

After gauging the distance, the Leviathan immediately began to constrict its body, binding the Kraken tightly and rendering it immobile.

The Kraken's eyes flickered slightly, and it used the saw-toothed, meat-grinder-like teeth beneath it to viciously tear into the Leviathan's body.

In an instant, a thick cloud of blood filled the deep sea, continuously spreading outward.

The Leviathan's action was essentially using itself as bait. With one bite, the Kraken tore open its flesh, causing its eyes to throb with pain.

But even as it was being torn by the Kraken, the Leviathan did not relax its binding of the enemy, gritting its teeth as it dragged the Kraken toward the surface, intending to haul the monster out.

On the skyship, after Merlin fell into the dangerous sea, everyone had long since panicked.

" It's over! We're doomed! Brother can't swim, and he's in terrible shape, he's definitely going to die! " Lilith cried hysterically, her eyelids swollen into red balls.

" Milady Lilith, calm down. With His Majesty's luck, he will surely turn misfortune into good fortune! I don't believe His Majesty will be easily killed! " Pudom comforted her endlessly, wanting to jump in to rescue Merlin, but with the two giant sea monsters fighting so intensely, such an action would clearly be irrational.

" But Brother's luck has always been terribly bad! He can't possibly turn misfortune into good fortune! "

Lilith's eyes reddened, and she cried even harder. She knew Pudom didn't understand the situation at all.

Even if Brother miraculously wasn't drowned, without the vitality to sustain the heart curse, activating it would still kill him!

Merlin was currently in crisis, shrouded in danger. He would either be tortured to death by the curse or drowned in the sea.

" This, this... " Pudom blushed, having to admit that Merlin's bad luck was indeed a fact. He had even begun to entertain thoughts of self-sacrifice. Should he jump into the sea, use the magic book to replicate the "Rasengan" technique, and go down with the Kraken? But even if he did, what good would it do? Merlin still wouldn't be saved.

" What should we do? " Jacob stood nearby at a loss, feeling helpless. Although he had initially hoped all these dark creatures would die, he owed his survival to Merlin's care, so he couldn't help but feel somewhat worried.

" No! I have to go and pull Brother out! I can't hesitate here! " Lilith stood up, ready to jump off the skyship to rescue Merlin from the deep sea.

Seeing this, Pudom quickly stopped Lilith, persuading her, " Milady Lilith, please calm down! His Majesty is already in grave danger. If you also fall into peril, what will happen to the Demon Lord Palace? All the demons of the First Demon Lord Palace will be doomed! You must think of the other demons, not just yourself! You are the last precious seed of the Lucifer clan! "

" Step aside! I don't care! If you dare to stop me, I won't be gentle! " Lilith yanked hard at the whip in her hand.

" Uh! Stay here, then. I'll go! This kind of mission is best left to us subordinates! " Pudom patted his chest, having no choice but to jump into the sea himself to try.

But suddenly, with a "whoosh" sound, the Leviathan emerged from the splashing waves, its twelve eyes gleaming with a ferocious light.

" Lord Leviathan? " Pudom saw that the Leviathan seemed injured, its condition dire.

Lilith didn't see Merlin's figure, and her anger flared instantly. She wouldn't care about others' lives. " Damn Leviathan, what were you doing diving just now? Didn't you see my brother fell? Even though my brother took you in, you only cared about fighting, you little runt! If you don't save my brother, wait until you're exhausted and get eaten by the Kraken! "

The Leviathan couldn't hear Lilith's scolding or her calling it a "little runt." In its eyes, only the Kraken was the enemy.

The Leviathan suddenly spread the twelve membranous wings on its back, flapping with all its might, slowly beginning to ascend.

The Kraken frantically tore at the Leviathan's body, but because it was bound and constricted, its massive body began to be exposed above the sea surface!

The Kraken's body was even heavier than the Leviathan's. Even if the Leviathan used all its strength, it couldn't fully drag the enemy out of the sea.

Half of the Kraken's body had already been pulled out of the sea by the Leviathan. This was the absolute limit of what it could achieve; it was impossible to completely drag the enemy out.

The Kraken was both shocked and furious. It faintly understood what the Leviathan intended. The sea was its home ground; leaving it would be dangerous!

The Kraken extended its eight powerful tentacles, all wrapping around the Leviathan's neck, continuously increasing the force, attempting to strangle its opponent!

A wave of suffocation hit. The Leviathan had done its best to complete its task. It opened its great mouth, " I'm leaving it to you... before it strangles me... "

" Phew, rest assured... "

Merlin's figure appeared in the Leviathan's mouth, holding onto its teeth, looking down at the Kraken below.

Compared to the Leviathan's sharp teeth, he was as tiny as an ant, appearing extremely small.

Merlin leaped down, landing on top of the Kraken's head, its two enormous eyes fixing on him simultaneously, filled with wariness.

" Look! Look, Milady Lilith! It's His Majesty! " Pudom exclaimed with great joy.

" It's Brother! Brother is still alive for now! Thank goodness! " Lilith's eyes sparkled, her heart finally relieved.

" Lili— " Before Merlin could call out, his heart twisted with pain. He could only grit his teeth. " Lilith! "

" Huh? " Lilith was taken aback. Between siblings, no extra communication was needed. She immediately understood. She turned and picked up the Banri Garan, throwing it toward Merlin.

" Brother! Catch! "

Merlin aimed for the demon sword descending from the sky, but the Kraken's crimson giant eyes beneath him rolled around wildly, and one of the eight tentacles wrapped around the Leviathan's neck broke free.

The Kraken swung its tentacle viciously at the flying Banri Garan, sending it flying off somewhere unknown.

The atmosphere on the skyship turned dead and silent. Half a second later—

Lilith: " Aaaaaahhhhh! "

Pudom: " Aaaaaahhhhh! "

This monster isn’t stupid, it’s guarding us as much as possible!” Pdom said with a stern expression, thinking that the North Sea Giant Ogre looked like a big, somewhat clumsy brute, but unexpectedly shrewd.

title: Chapter 30 — Old Huo the Information Broker
content:
Chapter 30 — Old Huo the Information Broker

Volume 31 · Chapter 30

He covered his eyes with a blindfold, only worried that the petrification power might accidentally injure his own men. Not only that, without needing a telescope, he could see much farther and had gained night vision.

Although the pirate fleet of Lochly was still some distance from Mammon's stronghold, standing on the deck, he could clearly see conditions several kilometers away even in the dark.

To put it bluntly, even the patterns on a fly's wings several kilometers away, Lochly could see clearly with Medusa's eyes.

At this moment, in Lochly's eyes, the island a kilometer away was very calm, with only a small number of demons active, which perfectly matched the intelligence that Mammon was busy launching a war against Britain and the entire Third Demon Lord Palace was weakly defended!

A pleasant smile involuntarily appeared on Lochly's face. In the current situation, the Third Demon Lord Palace was like meat delivered straight to his mouth. As a pirate's son who lived by plunder, how could he possibly give up such a good opportunity?

He had already begun planning in his heart — where to land most safely, then clear out the stationed demons at the fastest speed, rush into the Third Demon Lord Palace, and claim all of that Greed King's wealth as his own!

If the rumors about the Greed Demon Lord being extremely wealthy were true, as long as this plunder plan succeeded, Lochly would quickly complete his faction's accumulation, expand and forge a powerful pirate fleet, and once again raise high the flag of the Red Beard Pirate Crew. All of this would become his capital for later confronting the great swordmaster Elgin.

"Master, how is it? Is the Third Demon Lord Palace's defense really that weak right now?" The messy-haired pirate stood beside Lochly and asked in a low voice. "To be honest, I'm not sure about the reliability of this intelligence source. The information was bought from a drunkard in Rexham, Britain, but other informants say many major pieces of news can be obtained from him, and they're basically all true. I think there's a high probability it should be fine."

"Hey! Are you out of your mind? We've already brought our people into the Third Demon Lord's territory, and now you're saying you're unsure? Isn't that digging a hole for yourself?" The filthy pirate had a quick temper, and hearing such unreliable talk, he was immediately displeased.

"I also heard for the first time from others that there's a very capable informant in Rexham, and I bought some information there." The messy-haired pirate emphasized, "I just can't be certain that the information provided by that informant is completely accurate."

"Oh? An informant from Rexham? Seems that person really has some skill." Lochly nodded and answered calmly. "Don't worry, that informant didn't sell false information, it's all true. I can see conditions a kilometer away, and the Third Demon Lord Palace's defenses are indeed weak, full of loopholes, about on par with a small town. With the men we brought, even a frontal assault would be no problem."

"Hahaha!" The filthy pirate was very battle-hungry and said with great delight, "We're going to get a huge windfall tonight! If it weren't for that Greed Demon Lord being busy fighting Britain to the death, would there be such a good opportunity? Usually this area is very dangerous. Aside from those stupid donkeys from the Holy Church, no one dares to come here and tempt fate."

"As long as the intelligence is correct, otherwise my money would have been wasted. That informant in Rexham really has two tricks up his sleeve — how does he know so much about the demon race? Truly a remarkable person. Even though the demon race and human nations are nearly isolated from each other, making it hard for information to leak out." The messy-haired pirate clicked his tongue in amazement, unable to imagine why a small adventurer in Rexham would have such precise intelligence sources. Indeed, no ordinary informant could achieve this.

Lochly slightly frowned and began to entertain other thoughts in his heart, so he asked, "Besides being a Rexham adventurer, does that informant have any other information?"

"About this..." The messy-haired pirate thought carefully for a moment, then shook his head. "Seems there's no other information.
