"Moreover, that sword-drawing technique's power is too great; although I have mastered it, I may only be able to wield a few levels of power? It also depends on my physical condition."
"Is it enough?" Dickteping nodded with lingering fear, thinking that even if he couldn't match the First Demon Lord, Cain's strength using the sword-drawing technique should not be far off.
"You've worked hard these days; I can feel your loyalty." Cain looked down on Dickteping from above: "As long as you willingly work for me, I won't treat you poorly."
Dickteping's heart moved, he raised his head sincerely saying, "Yes! I am willing to go through fire and water for you! Both body and soul belong to you." "You profit-seeking wretch, such a blunt oath of loyalty makes me uneasy~" Cain said meaningfully, not fully trusting this halfway turncoat.
"My words come from the heart! I will absolutely not have even a hint of deceit toward you!" Dickteping knelt on the ground, cold sweat beading on his forehead, lamenting how he could make Cain relax his vigilance; this guy's suspicious nature is too troublesome.
"Considering your diligent duty guarding here, I can barely trust you; but if you show any sign of betraying me, I think you should know your own fate." Cain's tone carried a threat.
"Understood!" Dickteping hastily nodded vigorously, but inside he thought, if not afraid of being killed by you, I would have long since reorganized my mercenary band to roam and enjoy myself; don't think you can always control me; when the opportunity comes, I will surely fire the God-Sealing Stone's bullets into your heart!
Cain lifted his head to gaze into the distance, cold waves washing the smooth rock face, he frowned puzzled: "What happened here? Weren't there three villages at the foot of the mountain before? How are they now gone?"
"Master is immersed in cultivation, not really aware of recent events." Dickteping paused, then slowly said: "Not long ago, the Greedy Monarch and the Extreme Monarch of the demon race fought; the two demon lords battled darkening sky and earth; I don't know what the Greedy Monarch used, but he sliced open the sea, and we here were caught in the aftermath; three villages instantly vaporized."
"So that's how it is; instantly piercing the sea, its power still able to affect such a wide range; this demon lord's tool is not simple." Cain fell into thought, his scarlet eyes darting left and right, wondering what he was pondering.
"Indeed not simple; I still remember that day the sky turned color, everywhere were ghostly laughter and wolf howls, truly frightening; demon lords are monstrous beings." Dickteping sighed, saying even if he had an undead body and Flame Demon's power, he wouldn't dare provoke such a powerful demon lord; he could never win.
"~Degree King very scary?" Cain asked expressionlessly.
"Of course they're scary! They're basically like seven gunpowder kegs capable of blowing up the world; as far as I know, no human who provokes them survives." Dickteping knew the Holy Church often crusades against demons; Heroes change every few years, like harvesting leeks, batch after batch; one can imagine how many Heroes have died, yet Demon Lords still stand unharmed across the world.
"You think demon lords are scary because you're too insignificant." Cain paused, his tone icy: "Do you know what a Holy Spirit is?" "Holy Spirit?" Dickteping thought carefully; he himself wasn't a church believer, so he didn't know about such beings.
"They are like me, lifeforms created by our mother; they are not only our mother's loyal guards, but also born as natural enemies to slay demons." Cain took a deep breath, as if reminiscing his former life in heaven: "There is one called Archangel Uriel, skilled at forging various weapons; on his furnace are hammered-in several demon heads, without exception, they belong to the first few demon lords; while they were alive they dominated the mortal world, after death they are merely ornaments on the furnace; demon lord? Where exactly is it scary?"
"Hmph" Dickteping didn't know history, nor understand what a Holy Spirit was; he couldn't comprehend what Cain was saying; but he could clearly sense the contempt from a higher dimension towards mortal world demon lords.
"The demon lords you humans fear are nothing more than wild dogs with slightly sharper teeth, just a bit more dangerous than other creatures." Cain gazed out at the turbulent sea before him, calmly said: "Go find me a sword; let's go see the Greedy Demon Lord..."
"Ah? Is this not okay?" Dickteping hesitated a bit; honestly he didn't want to provoke a demon lord, and also worried that at a critical moment Cain might sell him out.
"What's there to fear? You just need to stand by and watch; I'll let you see the demon lord toyed with like a bug until death." Cain's face showed a creepy smile.
"Ask... but" Dickteping nervously swallowed saliva, "Shouldn't you be quickly reclaiming your Undying Divine Power? No need to go looking for trouble with the demon race."
"I can sense the whereabouts of the remaining two deceivers; they cannot escape my grasp." Cain was not in a hurry, but had other ideas: "The reason I seek that Greedy Sovereign is because I suspect he possesses a divine artifact; to contend with my mother, I need to be fully prepared, and the artifact is also something I need."
◇
In the capital of Britain, Mammon's army marched mightily out of the city toward Wales. The demons in the sky howled; the initial victory raised their fighting spirit to the peak.
Tens of thousands of demon armors, densely packed, formed a tight formation, trampling the kingdom's land with mighty momentum.
Relying on the armor legion, Mammon could sweep away all kingdoms' blocking forces; even the royal capital couldn't stop this force; Wales' fall is merely a matter of time―-
Mammon further boasted to his subordinates: contributing to Britain's capital takes two weeks; contributing to Wales takes only five days!.

title: Chapter 42 — Wales on the Brink of Crisis
content:
Chapter 42 — Wales on the Brink of Crisis

Volume 31 · Chapter 42

Many adventurers felt fear. Although there were no reports of demons attacking Wales yet, given its proximity to England, it was highly likely that the demons’ next target would be here.

The people of Wales were well aware that if the demon army could not even be stopped by the royal capital, then defending their own land would be incredibly difficult.

Although the local lord of Wales, Duke Rose, had a reputation for bravery and martial prowess, he struggled to calm the public’s emotions. Many citizens had packed their belongings and fled northward toward the rest of the kingdom.

Since the entire Kingdom of Britannia had been blockaded at sea by Mammon, cutting off all contact with the outside world, people seemed to have nowhere to go but north. However, the First Demon Lord Palace still existed in the Orkney Strait to the north.

The Kingdom of Britannia now found itself surrounded on all sides; fleeing only delayed the inevitable end.

“President, the demon army might be arriving soon. Rhyl is becoming very dangerous. We’re preparing to return to our hometowns for refuge. Sorry about this.”

Several adventurers, carrying their luggage, bid farewell to Old Taylor before turning to leave the Adventurers Guild. Since adventurers maintained a neutral stance, such choices were understandable.

Although they were all subjects of the Kingdom of Britannia, when disaster struck, preserving one’s life was instinctive. Not every adventurer possessed the resolve to die alongside the kingdom.

“Sigh,” Old Taylor sighed, not stopping any adventurer from seeking refuge. He respected their choices, but with more and more people leaving the guild recently, he worried the guild wouldn’t survive much longer. “Everyone has left. The guild is getting quieter and quieter, looking like it might close down anytime. I’ve managed this guild for so many years, yet I’ve never encountered a situation like this before.”

Lucia looked at the desolate guild hall and felt uneasy. Due to the war, everyone was busy fleeing, leaving no work available. She stepped forward to comfort him. “Grandpa, it’s okay. The royal capital has fallen, and Wales probably won’t hold out long either. Right now, everyone is thinking about how far they can escape.”

“True, adventurers are hardly loyal servants of the kingdom. Choosing to save themselves at times like this is understandable. But the entire kingdom is already blockaded. Unless we repel the demon attacks, escaping anywhere will make no difference. Why won’t they listen to my advice?” Old Taylor angrily tapped his cane, unable to understand why the adventurers in the guild were so short-sighted.

“Grandpa, don’t get angry. Even the Magnolia Knights in the royal capital couldn’t stop the demon army. What could adventurers below Mithril rank possibly achieve? It’s better to return home for refuge.” Lucia gently patted Old Taylor’s back.

“I really hope this turmoil ends soon. Karl has been summoned by Count Austin; I suspect he wants him to reinforce the Welsh front lines.” Old Taylor speculated in his heart.

“Alice also left Rhyl earlier. It seems she went to support the defense of the royal capital, but she hasn’t returned since. Please don’t let anything happen to her.” Lucia was somewhat worried, as it had been a long time since they heard news from Alice.

“There should be no problem. Alice has grown rapidly and is now a Purple Gold adventurer. Even if she can’t win against the demons, retreating unharmed should be fine.” Old Taylor felt reassured, doubting that demons had the power to instantly kill a Purple Gold adventurer. “However, if even Alice and the London adventurers couldn’t hold back the fierce demon advance, they’ll be tough opponents to deal with.”

“Hehe, President, things aren’t peaceful lately. I want to go back to my hometown to check things out. Is that okay?” Hobbs grinned, trying to slip away.

“Get lost! I’ve never heard you mention having any relatives. Rhyl is your hometown. What’s wrong with staying? The guild needs manpower right now.” Lucia shooed Hobbs away, refusing to let him leave the guild without permission.

“Hmph~” Hobbs pursed his lips and said dissatisfiedly, “Everyone is scared of death now. I’m scared too.”

Just as Lucia was about to lecture Hobbs properly, Alice stumbled into the guild, dragging her luggage behind her.

Alice’s injuries had not fully healed; bandages wrapped around her body. Worried about her daughter Chris, she had declined Cecilia’s kind offer to continue recuperating at her house and returned to Rhyl overnight.

Having traveled through the night, Alice was exhausted upon her return. As soon as she entered, she leaned against the doorframe, breathing heavily. Fine beads of sweat slid down her cheeks.

Seeing Alice return from the front lines in such poor condition, everyone gasped in surprise—

“Alice?!”

◇

*Gulp, gulp, gulp.* Alice drained the water from her cup, parched from the journey. “Slow down, don’t rush.” Lucia brought another glass of water for Alice.

“Ha! Revived!” Alice set down the cup, letting out a long breath, wiping her mouth. Her body felt much more comfortable. “Did you participate in the kingdom’s defense battle? How was it?” Hobbs asked enthusiastically.

“What else could it be? You must know by now, right? The royal capital has fallen. Her Majesty the Queen has escaped to Wales and is temporarily staying at Duke Rose’s mansion.” Alice replied briefly.

“What exactly happened? I heard that even Gregory Master, a Purple Gold adventurer from the London Guild, went into battle. How could they possibly lose?” Lucia thought that the president of the London Guild was exceptionally powerful; even facing a Demon Lord, defeat shouldn’t come so easily.

“Regarding the specifics…” Alice hesitated but frowned as she recounted the events. “Her Majesty organized a quite strong force. Besides the Magnolia Knight Order and the Thorns Knights, elite forces from various regions participated, along with many adventurers from the London Guild. In the end, they were all defeated by the Demon Lord’s clone. Although Mr. Gregory managed to stall, he remained suppressed throughout.”

“Defeated by the Demon Lord’s clone? Does that mean the Demon Lord himself didn’t appear during the attack on the royal capital?!” Old Taylor sensed something significant.

“Um… yes…” Alice almost didn’t want to admit it. With so many strong fighters deployed, even the true Demon Lord failed to show up. “The Greed Demon Lord did not appear at all. Relying solely on clones—or rather, numerous clones—they easily crushed the kingdom’s defense forces.”

“Alice, you are not only an honorary Thorns Knight but also a Purple Gold adventurer. Did you lose so easily? That was just a clone of the Demon Lord, not the real body.” Hobbs’ expression turned playful.

“What could I do?! Do you think clones are weak? They’re super strong! Anyway, someone who hasn’t been to the front line shouldn’t stand there making sarcastic remarks!” Alice’s face flushed red, and she angrily turned to snap back at Hobbs, unable to tolerate his mocking tone. She lowered her gaze to her Light Aria—

“Actually, there was a chance to win. I just wasn’t skilled enough.”

“If my swordsmanship were as refined as my teacher’s, I definitely could have pierced through the Demon Lord’s heart.”

title: Chapter 43 — The Power of White Bone and Raw Flesh
content:
Chapter 43 — The Power of White Bone and Raw Flesh

Volume 31 · Chapter 43

“The situation is not optimistic; if we continue like this, won’t we even lose the guild?” Lucia said, worried and frowning, “Father might still go to support the Duke of Roses, but even so many strong ones can’t stop the demon legion—Father going there won’t make any difference.”

“Let Mr. Carl stay in Rexhelm; going to support is too dangerous. In the defense battle, I saw many Saint-tier adventurers torn apart by demons.” Alice said solemnly, advising against Carl going into danger; if he could break through Saint-tier, he could still be of some use.

“What can we do? Who else in the kingdom can stop this?” Old Taylor sighed deeply; the guild was his life’s work for half a lifetime—what a pity to lose it like that.

“It’s not that there’s no one; if Elgin the Great Swordsman steps forward, there might be a chance. This guy once turned the kingdom upside down, even Master Gregory was knocked to his sickbed with a single punch.” Hobbs suddenly brought up a person.

“Indeed! If Elgin the Great Swordsman takes action, he might be able to stop the Pang tribe’s army, saving both the kingdom and Wales!” Lucia recalled this hero of the British Kingdom, recalling the man’s past achievements; it’s still quite possible to drag the kingdom out of the mire.

“But that great swordsman has had no news for a long time; his whereabouts are uncertain, making him hard to find. Moreover, the capital’s fall hasn’t shown him—either he’s fallen out with the royal family, or he’s no longer in the British Kingdom.” Old Taylor had also kept an eye on Elgin the Great Swordsman for a while; unfortunately, we still can’t find him now.

“Elgin the Great Swordsman? I don’t believe he left this land; a man so full of justice couldn’t possibly stand by while demons slaughter indiscriminately. Perhaps he’ll appear suddenly—this man, as free as the wind, always turns the tide at the crucial moment, then vanishes without a trace.” Alice sighed, recalling how she used to admire Elgin the Great Swordsman every day; she really was young back then.

Hobbs couldn’t help laughing and asked, “Hehe, Alice, are you close with Elgin the Great Swordsman? How can you be sure he’s quite a just person?”

“I—I mean, I’ve seen him a few times; he has a unique aura! You know what intuition is? Just one glance from afar, and I can feel his blazing heart of justice!” Alice’s face flushed red as she kept rebutting Hobbs’s teasing.

“Oh, it’s all just your own guess~” Hobbs shook his head, drinking to himself. “Shut up.” Alice stood up, picking up her luggage—

“I want to go see Chris; given how dangerous the situation is now, the guild president should consider closing the guild at this time and evacuating to a safe area in the north.”◇

In Rexhelm, in the landlady’s yard, an old and a young live quietly together.

During this time, little Chris trains hard every day to help her parents later; she’s very diligent. Before, when Alice supervised her, Chris would find ways to avoid her mother’s gaze and sneak off to play with her favorite things.

But now that Alice isn’t around, Chris has become extremely industrious, already able to skillfully revive the wilted chrysanthemums in the flowerpot, making them full of life.

The landlady wears a thick fur coat, shoveling snow in the yard, occasionally glancing at Chris not far away. This little one is happily playing with the landlady’s pet dog, her bell-like laughter ringing out from time to time.

Seeing Chris so happy—a rare sight—the landlady secretly breathed a sigh of relief; this child has been overexerting herself in training lately, even speaking less, so she took the chance while shoveling snow to let the little one out to play.

Because the landlady’s home is somewhat far from the Rexhelm guild, and Chris is focused on her training, she hasn’t seen her friends Mini, Four-Eyes, and Snot Bug for a long time.

Fortunately, the landlady keeps a small brown dog named Huahua; its coat isn’t great, and its right leg is lame, but it’s still full of energy and knows how to win Chris’s favor.

Chris wears a thick fur coat, with a fluffy ear muff on her head; she looks like a juvenile chubby penguin, and even rolling in the snow makes her seem a bit bulky.

“Huahua! Roll over!”

Chris struck a pose like an animal trainer, giving orders to the dog, hoping not to lose to her mother’s dignity, she could conquer this “evil dog” named Huahua. The dog wagged its tail, rolled wildly in the snow, then stood up and shook off the snow on its body, all of which splattered onto Chris’s face. “Ugh!!!” Little Chris hurriedly wiped the mud off her face, put on an angry look, and said, “Huahua, behave! Sit down!”

“Woof!” the dog barked, obediently sitting in place, its tail wagging energetically, sweeping clean the snow behind it.

“Huh?” Chris saw the dog’s right leg rotting, her heart sank, she looked up and asked, “Grandma, what’s wrong with Huahua’s leg? It looks weird…”

“Oh~” The landlady set down her work, turned around smiling, and said, “Huahua has been disobedient since small; she fell from the roof and broke her leg, but luckily it’s only one leg—otherwise it would have been troublesome.”

“” Chris looked at the obedient dog, thought for a moment, then said in a childish voice, “Huahua! Lie down!” “Huh?” The dog pondered a while, then lay flat in the snow, exposing its belly to Chris, showing submission.*shush!* Chris crouched, took off her gloves, and aimed her hands at the dog’s broken leg, her expression serious.

A hum, a pleasant buzzing sounded; Chris’s hand emitted a pale green life force, gently nourishing the dog’s body.

A tiny sprite, the embodiment of the life element, slowly appeared, circling Chris as it flew, lightly kissing her forehead before entering the dog’s broken leg.

The dog lying on the ground let out a comfortable “woo-woo-woo”; its body grew warm, especially the lame right leg feeling tingly, as if bones were growing and flesh regenerating.

“Huh” Chris exhaled, wiped the sweat from her forehead; being so young, healing a dog’s broken leg took all her strength. The dog tried to stand up, found its injured leg healed, and its whole body brimming with power.

It jumped around excitedly for a while, overjoyed, leaping into Chris’s arms and licking her face with its tongue. “Woof-woof, stop, don’t do that—little Chris can’t handle this enthusiastic dog; her face is already covered in drool—“I—I smell last night’s leftover food! So stinky!”

~~o(>_<)o~~

title: Chapter 44 — Realization (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 44 — Realization (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 31 · Chapter 44

Suddenly the little female puppy noticed something? It stopped, turned around, and looked outside the yard, whining nonstop, “Woof! Woof woof!”
“Huh?” Chris curiously lifted her head, seeing a somewhat confused and tired figure standing outside the door, wearing a warm cloak and carrying luggage. Alice put down her own luggage, took off her hat and bent down, greeting her daughter, “Chris, it’s mom, mom’s back.”
Chris was first dazed like a wooden chicken, then became emotionally agitated, finally biting her lower lip in grievance, crystal-clear tears swirling in her eyes who knows how many times.
The little one held back the urge to cry, got up from the snow, waddled on her two short legs like radishes, and dashed straight into Alice’s arms. “Don’t cry, don’t cry, crying will make you look like a little spotted cat.”
Alice was still feeling tired, but as soon as she picked up her daughter, she felt her whole body fill with strength. Seeing Chris looking so wronged, her heart was a mix of emotions.
However, feeling that her daughter was a bit heavier than before, she relaxed a little, realizing that Chris hadn’t been wronged at all; instead, she had been doing well staying with the landlady, and the food was surely good.
“Mom, I missed you so much.” Chris lifted her little mouth and kissed Alice’s cheek. The speed was like a chick pecking grain, “pat pat” nonstop.
“Enough, enough, don’t be like a woodpecker, mom isn’t wood.” Alice sighed, yet felt warm inside. After being apart for so long, her daughter seemed to have become even more clingy to her.
“No way, mom wasn’t here this whole time, I need to kiss her back to make it fair.” Chris’s face showed seriousness and earnestness, feeling that Alice’s absence owed her something?
“What’s up? I just saw you and the dog being all lovey-dovey, not that hot?” Alice retorted.
“No, that’s different!” Chris chubby little hands waved as she defended herself, then suddenly remembering something, her little body shuddered, she put on a stern face, puffed out her cheeks, and showed an angry expression, “Hmph~!”
“Who made you angry again? As soon as mom comes back you put on a sour face?” Alice felt a bead of cold sweat slide down her forehead, wondering why her daughter’s mood changed so quickly.
“Mom left me here without looking back, and every night when I think of it I get angry. I can’t be too warm toward mom, otherwise she’ll get a taste of sweetness and abandon me again.” Chris crossed her arms, turned her face aside, and snorted from her nose.
“No way, what’s going on in that little head of yours?”
Alice poked Chris’s forehead, thinking why her daughter loved to daydream so much; it must be inheriting Merlin’s traits, while the baby inheriting her are always strengths! Uh! Right! Exactly!
If Merlin knew Alice was throwing dirt at him so naturally, he’d surely roll his eyes, and when dealing with Alice’s daydreams, he’d feel even worse.
“Mom definitely needs to reflect on herself, ah…” Chris, in her mother’s arms, struck a pose of a little adult, occasionally squinting to sneak a glance at Alice’s expression.
“Fine, fine, mom will reflect on herself, you pesky little rascal.” Alice pinched Chris’s little cheek, thinking that after not seeing each other for so long, her daughter had already learned to argue with her; if she doesn’t behave, she’ll get a spanking sooner or later.
“Daddy! Daddy, where are you?” Chris looked around, but couldn’t see Merlin’s silhouette.
“Ah, Alice’s gaze became evasive, she felt panicked and didn’t know how to answer her daughter; she could only keep hoping, “Soon, your dad will be back soon.”
“町-一” Chris stared at her mother expressionlessly, this excuse she’d heard countless times—dad never actually came back. “Trust me, ah! You little thing, don’t you even believe your mom’s words?” Alice immediately turned serious, trying to make Chris submit. “Whimper” little Chris felt wronged, resting her chin on Alice’s shoulder, muttering, “Just having mom back makes me happy…
“…” Alice was left speechful, feeling melancholy, she gently patted the little one’s back to soothe her, not even knowing Merlin’s whereabouts—there was nothing she could do.
“Congratulations on returning safely, Miss Alice.” The landlady greeted with a smile.
“Thank you for taking care of Chris for so long, didn’t cause you any trouble, did you?” Every time Alice faced the landlady she felt some pressure, the fear of rent demands constantly surging in her heart.
“What are you talking about? I’m just an old guy living here alone every day; having Chris keep me company is actually quite nice.” The landlady set down her iron shovel and called out to Alice—
“Hurry inside. It’s freezing out—◇
In the evening, Chris and her mother stayed close for a long while before reluctantly falling asleep in Alice’s arms.
The kettle boiled on the stove, the flames lit up the landlady’s and Alice’s faces; it was rare to have a chance for the two to sit knee-to-knee and chat.
“Things are like this: although the current situation is too dangerous, I guess I can’t really help much, after all I was crushed badly in front of the demons, plus I was worried about Chris, so I hurried back.”
Alice told the landlady about her various efforts supporting the kingdom’s defense, while looking at the adorable Chris, she tidied up the girl’s somewhat messy hair.
The little one slept soundly, because Alice had returned, she was much quieter than usual, curled up on her mom’s leg, her little nose making a “hiss hiss hiss” breathing sound.
“You being able to return safely is good, but are the demons really that strong? Even the kingdom’s army can’t resist them; I’ve lived on this land half my life and have never seen such a thing.” The landlady held her hot tea, looking at Alice with a kind face.
“Indeed, they’re very strong—I can’t even beat my own doppelgänger; if I faced the true form of a stronger Demon Lord, I’d probably only have the option to flee.” Alice gave a wry smile, thinking of Merlin, “But I’ve seen even stronger demons, beings that cannot be defeated; I’ve tried countless times to beat him, finally gave up, I can’t imagine what his defeat would look like~
“Don’t say that, Alice, you’re stronger than anyone; as long as you want something, nothing is impossible. Believe me, from the first time I saw you, I thought your potential was limitless—becoming a purple‑gold adventurer at such a young age proves it.” The landlady encouraged warmly.
“Thank you, but things aren’t as simple as you think.” Alice forced a smile, thinking that Gregory was the true purple‑gold adventurer, while she had received some help from Merlin; the landlady was just an ordinary old lady who wouldn’t understand these matters.
“What are your plans next?” the landlady asked curiously.
“On the road I’ve seen too many poor people harmed by demons—orphans whose parents were killed, wives who lost their husbands, elders who starved to death by the roadside. So many want to struggle to survive; I feel I can contribute a little to change this, but I can’t let go of Chris, she’s still so young, I’m torn…” Alice frowned, the firelight showing her grave expression, her heart torn between two sides.
The landlady set down her tea cup, her aged hand reaching out to Alice, speaking encouragingly, “Miss Alice, kindness is your strongest weapon; everyone will stand behind you to support you, the great Goddess of Light will bless you, she will be your firm backing.”
“Ah, thank you for the encouragement, I feel much better.” Alice’s smile was a bit stiff, she thought in amazement—being able to say such things, the landlady must be a devout follower of the Light Church, something she hadn’t noticed before.
