title: Chapter 45 — Light Born in Sin
content:
Chapter 45 — Light Born in Sin

Volume 31 · Chapter 45

Following the landlady's suggestion, Alice decided to temporarily stay here with Chris until Merlin returns.
Alice learned that her daughter had preliminarily mastered magic and could treat minor injuries, so she praised the little one profusely. For someone Chris's age, being able to use life force to heal others already counts as having quite a good talent.
Alice recalled her own childhood; at Chris's age, she herself didn't know any magic at all, merely running errands behind the teacher.
At that moment, inside the house, the mother and daughter fell into a deep sleep, Alice holding the little one, letting her head rest on her arm.
Chris hadn't slept this peacefully in a long time; her nose twitched, her little paw touched her mother's tablet, and she immediately started talking in her sleep, “Dad's back, hehe…
The landlady raised the oil lamp, secretly gazing at the sleeping mother and daughter, then quietly closed the door.
She slowly approached Alice's luggage, placed the oil lamp on the table, and casually picked up the Light Chant. As the slender sword was drawn, it emitted a faint tremor, the blade flashing with a cold light that reflected the landlady's cloudy eyes. This splendid divine instrument trembled incessantly in the landlady's hand, as if responding to something?
The landlady furrowed her brows, examining the Light Chant in her hand repeatedly, finding no damage. She wondered, 'A holy sword has already awakened and is intact, so why can't it even kill the Demon Lord's substitute?'
This is abnormal; the Light Chant is a divine weapon forged by Goddess Maria with great effort, possessing perfect power to restrain dark creatures. If I recall correctly, the goddess once said this weapon was created to slay the prophets of the demon race, so how could it fail to kill a substitute? Even if it were enough to slay the Demon King, it should have plenty to spare—
Alice isn't using it?
The landlady scrutinized the Light Chant, deciding to secretly help Alice a bit—at the very least to let her know where this weapon's strength lies and how to better wield it.
Only see the landlady gripping the blade of the Light Chant with her calloused hand; the cold edge pierced skin and flesh, and the holy spirit's blood slowly seeped away with a hissing sound.
The body of the Light Chant trembled slightly, greedily absorbing the holy spirit's blood◇
All was dark; consciousness drifted in the vast expanse, with no sound at all, as if the world before creation. A faint light gradually brightened, like fireflies' specks, slowly expanding into the blazing source of the sun.
Within that holy light, a figure resembling a woman slowly emerged, she cleaved the darkness of the chaotic world and planted a seed upon the sinful land.
Time flew like a shuttle; in an instant, ten thousand years passed. The seed broke through the soil, exuding unmatched vigor; though it seemed small, it contained immense power.
The holy woman looked down upon the sapling growing in the sinful land, without hesitation she slit her arm artery, and blood gushed forth like a river.
The surging flood of blood poured from the heavens, irrigating the sinful land; part nourished the 'sloth' sapling, while another part gave birth to hideous demons.
“Revenge, revenge, revenge…
The hideous demons dragged their mutilated bodies across the sinful land, mechanically twisting their necks, constantly repeating those two words, as if that were their only thought.
Nourished by the blood, the sapling grew; after who knows how many tens of thousands of years, it became a massive plant, full of vigor, bringing a splash of color to the otherwise monotonous chaotic world.
However, the flower bud of the distant plant remained tightly shut, refusing to bloom; its roots, entrenched in the sinful land, sprouted and swept the surroundings, plunging it into 'anger,' stirring the chaotic world into unrest.
The massive plant frequently roared at the demons, it 'envied' those hideous demons, diverting its own nutrients, which prevented it from continuing to grow.
The woman bathed in holy light let out a long sigh, as if deeply disappointed by the sting, she slowly turned to leave, and the chaotic world once again fell into darkness.
The hideous-looking demons, seeing this, couldn't help but panic; they stared at each other stiffly, and driven by the mother's immense will, they lined up and marched orderly to their deaths.
Although the demons were utterly hideous, they possessed a beautiful spirit of sacrifice, willingly offering their bodies as fertilizer for the giant plant, only hoping that the holy mother would turn back.
The giant plant rolled up the hideous demons and shoved them into its mouth; 'arrogance' gazed upon life, seeing only food, caring nothing for the lives of the hideous demons.
The demons' wails now became extraordinarily pleasant; the crunching of bones and flesh being chewed turned into an accompaniment.
However, the hideous demons were devoured to the last; even after binge-eating, they remained unsatisfied, and the flower bud atop the giant plant did not open. It turned its gaze toward the woman bathed in light, openly displaying its 'greed' in the daylight, still craving more.
The holy woman removed her clothing, revealing her perfect **, completely naked in the chaotic world; this body, beautiful enough to be breathless, became a striking sight upon the sinful land.
The evil giant plant stared agape, dominated by 'lust'; at this moment it finally felt satisfied, the flower bud atop its head burst open violently, representing the blade of light, born from its sinful-filled body, and flew into the holy woman's hand.
““Revenge, for my sister, kill the evil prophet
The tiny, pitiful demon lay on the ground, its lower part already devoured; seeing the smile on the holy woman's face, it contentedly closed its eyes, “Mom…◇
““Mom! Mom?!”“! !？”
Alice suddenly opened her eyes, her back already drenched in cold sweat; this bizarre dream left her feeling terrified beyond measure, as if she had spent tens of thousands of years in the dream.
She hastily got up, breathing deeply, trying to recall the dream's details, but waves of pain shot into her mind, making it hard to summon many details; even the holy woman's face was instantly forgotten completely.
““Mom? What's wrong? Are you feeling unwell?” Chris stretched out her little hand and touched her mother's forehead.
Alice looked at her adorable daughter beside her, realized it was morning, and forced a smile: “Mom's fine, Mom's okay, just had a nightmare.”
““Having a dream? Chris also has nightmares! The cream cake was eaten by Sister Mini, scared me into crying.” Little Chris said solemnly, recounting her nightmare.
““Is that so? So you also have things you're afraid of?” Alice rubbed her daughter's little head.
““Mom just now was really scary, kept trembling nonstop; I thought Mom was sick,” Chris said in a childish voice, recalling the situation, still feeling uneasy.
““Mom isn't sick, really just a nightmare; if I scared you, it shows you're not brave enough.” Alice looked at Chris with a face full of affection, yet her heart was uneasy—
What exactly is this bizarre dream? Why does the blade born from that monster's body feel somewhat familiar?

title: Chapter 46 — Internal Decay
content:
Chapter 46 — Internal Decay

Volume 31 · Chapter 46

She had already given Alice some hints the night before; whether she could master the method of wielding the Light Cantata depended on her own comprehension. What Alice saw that night was not a simple dream, but the entire creation process of the Light Cantata.

To wield this light blade born of a sinful land, not knowing its origins and the evil nature hidden beneath its holy appearance makes it impossible to control.

The landlady gave Alice considerable guidance; if she still cannot wield the Light Cantata, it only shows that Alice cannot become the wielder of this divine artifact.

“Granny! I want to help you chop wood~” Little Chris came running over, hopping and skipping, her cheeks red from the cold.

“No need, you're still too small; you don't need to do this work yet.” The landlady bent down, her kind face stroking Chris's head. “Huh?~ Chris noticed the bandage on the landlady's hand, not knowing when she got injured, “Granny, what happened to your hand?”

“This?” The landlady lowered her gaze to her injured right hand, smiling, “I accidentally cut myself on a sharp piece of wood; I really am getting old, sometimes I don’t even notice.”

“I-I can heal Granny! It’ll be better in no time!” Chris raised her hands, showing an eager expression; although she had no experience healing others, she really wanted to try.

“Forget this small injury; it’s nothing serious.” The landlady squatted down, looking at the young Chris, speaking seriously, “Your power is extremely precious; it can arouse others’ greed, so don’t reveal yourself lightly—kindness is easily exploited.”

“~Huh?” Little Chris scratched her head, half-understanding; although she didn’t fully grasp the landlady’s words, she kept nodding in response. On the other side, Alice stood in the snow, her expression complex as she examined the Light Cantata in her hand, her eyes showing a hint of disgust. She had already realized the connection between last night’s dream and the Light Cantata; it was likely that the artifact itself had actively sent this information to her. Alice had no idea where the Light Cantata came from; she only knew it was something she had stolen, a hidden sword her teacher kept under the bed.

However, Alice now understands the Light Cantata a bit more, but to know the details she must ask the teacher in person—perhaps the teacher knows even more. Alice has always liked the Light Cantata, believing it to be a righteous sword radiating holy aura from head to toe; yet after grasping its true nature, she feels an unprecedented revulsion.

Beneath the Light Cantata’s gleaming exterior lies an evil weapon empowered by the Seven Deadly Sins—pride, wrath, greed, lust, gluttony, envy, and sloth.

The source of all evil in the world stems from these seven sins; it is an eternal doctrine upheld by countless dark creatures.

The very process of the Light Cantata’s creation destines it to be an evil weapon; no matter how bright and splendid its appearance, its essence is a poisonous blade that achieves its goals through evil power.

Alice already knows how to wield the Light Cantata, but she feels uncomfortable about the filth and ugliness hidden beneath its holy façade; without a doubt, this is an evil blade—.

Good people find it hard to wield the Light Cantata, while evil people wield it with ease; the wielder’s negative emotions are its finest nourishment.

Just like that pure woman in the dream, whose words betray a burning fire of revenge—using evil to counter evil is the key to mastering the Light Cantata. No matter who created the Light Cantata, Alice can tell that the creator was an extremely extreme person.

◇

The capital of Wales, the manor of the Rose Duke, has already become Elizabeth’s temporary palace.

In the conference room, Elizabeth sat at the head, with the Rose Duke and several other Welsh nobles seated below.

Everyone felt somewhat uneasy, discussing how to resist the upcoming assault of the demon legion; clearly Wales was on the brink of collapse. “According to the latest news, the minions of the Greed King are swiftly advancing toward Wales; they will likely arrive soon.”

“What can we do? Our forces are clearly insufficient—even the Purple Chrysanthemum Knights can’t hold back the demons, let alone us!”

“Yes, the total number of Saint-tier warriors we can muster in all of Wales is at most eight—far fewer than the forces assembled for the capital’s defense; an army to fight the demons would practically be a suicide mission.”

“What are the adventurers all over Wales doing? Their guilds can barely hold on—why aren’t they coming to help us? If we had a few more powerful adventurers like Master Gregory, the demons wouldn’t be a threat.”

“How could we possibly rely on those adventurers at a time like this? They have no faith, nor any willingness to sacrifice for the kingdom; this so-called neutral faction only looks out for its own interests. Upon hearing of the heavy casualties in the London guild, the frightened ones all fled, and in recent days many Welsh adventurers have escaped northward—they simply don’t care whether Wales survives.”

“In the end, we still can’t rely on them—why not just surrender and negotiate with the Greed Demon Lord, ceding the entire English region to him? Perhaps that would stop the current crisis.”

“Lord Slate, is that not alright?”

“What’s wrong with that? Sacrificing England could protect the entire British Kingdom; it’s clearly not a losing deal. If we keep going like this, the kingdom will cease to exist!”

“Lord Slate makes some sense; if the Greed Demon Lord accepts those terms, the war could end, and everyone can see the demon race’s strength…”

The nobles in power in Wales began to argue in the conference room; even suggesting “surrender~” as a way to get through this predicament shows how desperate they have become.

Elizabeth lowered her head, her face growing ever grimmer; after arriving here she found the Welsh nobles a disorganized bunch, unable to muster a strong resistance—if this continues, Wales’s fall is only a matter of time.

Seeing more and more nobles agree to surrender to the demon race, the Rose Duke, face cold, sprang to his feet, drew the sword at his waist, approached the noble named Slate, and pressed his head onto the table.

“Lord Slate, at a time like this you’re still spreading rumors, already offending Her Majesty’s dignity; advocating the division of the kingdom’s lands is moreover a crime of high treason!”

“Your Grace! No, I didn’t mean that!” “You must take responsibility for your words and actions!”

With one stroke, the Rose Duke severed Slate’s noble’s head; blood spattered across the conference table, and the other nobles were so frightened their faces paled, not daring to breathe.

Slate’s headless corpse fell to the ground, the pouch at his waist slipping loose, a flood of coins clattering as they rolled across the floor.

The Rose Duke was slightly surprised, picking up the blood‑stained coin at his foot; he found it differed from the kingdom’s issued currency, bearing the effigy of Mammon—though Mammon’s army had not yet set foot in Wales, its claws had already reached out, unseen, beginning to corrode the kingdom from within.

title: Chapter 47 — Focused Response
content:
Chapter 47 — Focused Response

Volume 31 · Chapter 47

The Duke of Roses gazed at the gold coin emblazoned with the image of Mammon in his hand, feeling a surge of surprise. At first, he had only intended to kill a chicken to scare the monkeys, to make all the nobles abandon their "surrender" thoughts. He had never expected that with a single slash, he would hook himself a big fish.

This man, sharp as a blade, lifted his head and swept his gaze across every noble's eyes. Not a single one dared to meet his stare; they all seemed to harbor unspeakable secrets deep within their hearts.

Mammon's influence had already seeped into the very heart of the kingdom. He had cultivated some powerful nobles as his lackeys, attempting to split the kingdom from within and effortlessly bring Britannia into his grasp.

Such despicable and sneaky tactics were exactly like Mammon's usual methods—hiding safely behind the scenes, letting others do his bidding, achieving his own goals through the simplest means possible.

The Duke of Roses looked at the nobles before him. If one noble had betrayed the kingdom, there were bound to be more traitors, just like icebergs floating on the water—most of them hidden beneath the surface where no one could see.

The nobles in this conference room were deciding the kingdom's future. Perhaps among them, many had already been bought by Mammon. How could discussing how to pull the kingdom out of the mud possibly yield good results?

Although the Duke of Savoy knew all this, he had no intention of dragging out all the traitors to kill them. With Mammon's wicked army about to march on the capital, this was precisely the time to use people. Randomly killing nobles would cause panic and weaken the kingdom's strength—clearly not worth the cost.

The conference room fell silent. Everyone was scheming, waiting for the Duke of Roses to speak. His heart grew resolute as he placed the gold coin on the table, wanting the nobles to see clearly the faces of the traitors.

"Sleet is a traitor! His heart has been corrupted by demons, and he has lost his loyalty to the kingdom! He and his family will be forever reviled!"

Elizabeth's face went pale as she looked at the bloodstained Mammon gold coin, her heart filled with fear. Could it be that the demon army's rapid advance to the capital meant that, before Mammon launched his war, he had already begun infiltrating the kingdom's interior, buying numerous local nobles? Otherwise, why would the demons' invasion proceed so smoothly? For the sake of occupying Britannia's land, how much preparation had this Demon Lord made?

Katherine's eyes gradually grew cold as she looked at the noble's corpse on the ground. She spoke sternly, "To conspire with demons and betray the kingdom—such people are not worth sparing. If you continue to spread or endorse surrender to the demons, then you are all comrades of traitors. Dividing the kingdom will be punished as treason, and your families will bear joint responsibility."

Upon hearing the Thorn Knight's warning, the nobles of Wales were terrified, their faces changing drastically. They began spitting on the corpse of the deceased Sleet, declaring their positions—

"Sleet, the spineless wretch, actually thought about surrendering to the demons? Such a foolish idea coming from him is truly a disgrace to Wales!" "I saw it coming long ago. While the kingdom is in peril, he doesn't even lift a finger. He has clearly betrayed the kingdom. I remember he has two sons—let's execute them all together!"

"Surrender only emboldens the demons' arrogance. We should risk everything and fight the demons to the death!"

The Duke of Roses watched the nobles begin to declare their loyalty, then sneered coldly, "Since you all are willing to share the kingdom's fate, then entrust your armies to me for unified command. Only by uniting all forces can we possibly withstand the demons' invasion. I assume there are no objections?"

To prevent nobles like Sleet from stabbing them in the back at a crucial moment, the Duke of Roses decided to sideline the nobles present, concentrating all their armies under his own command.

Nobles who lost their private armies were probably no better than commoners. Even if bought by Mammon, they would hardly cause much trouble. "If there are no objections, then you may all leave."

How could those nobles dare to object? Those who had objections had just had their heads chopped off, and now they were supposed to meekly hand over their assets to keep the peace? After numerous Welsh nobles signed the agreement with the Duke of Roses, they fled the conference room like rats fleeing a sinking ship.

The Duke of Roses let out a sigh of relief and knelt before Elizabeth on one knee, "Your Majesty, please forgive this bold move. I had no choice but to take such drastic measures to keep those with ill intentions in check."

"You need not blame yourself; I understand," Elizabeth helped the Duke of Roses to his feet. "The House of Roses was a founding contributor to the kingdom. In times of crisis, you have remained loyal. I am truly pleased."

"Your Majesty, rest assured. I will personally lead the knights to repel the demons' invasion. If Wales falls, it will also mean my life has reached its end."

◇

As evening fell, the conference room was thick with the stench of blood. The Duke of Roses remained alone for a long time, watching the sunset outside the window, the dying sun glowing red like blood. Cecilia and Kyle received their father's summons, hearing that there was something important to discuss, so they hurriedly made their way there.

Quietly pushing open the door, Cecilia caught a whiff of a strange odor and, with a nervous heart, stepped into the grand conference room.

Kyle, who was no stranger to battle, immediately grew vigilant upon catching the scent of blood. He scanned his surroundings—apart from the Duke of Roses' retreating silhouette, there was nothing unusual.

"Father, what summons brings us here?"

Cecilia cautiously approached the Duke of Savoy, her instincts filled with fear toward this father from childhood, recalling his harsh beatings when she was young. Even now, her legs would go weak.

When her foot stepped on something sticky, she looked down—and froze in place. The headless body of a noble emitted a subtle odor, the congealed blood having solidified into a sticky mess beneath her foot.

Cecilia instinctively wanted to scream, but quickly covered her mouth. Her father despised weakness above all else, and she did not wish to lose composure in front of him. "Just a minute too late." The imposing figure of the Duke of Roses turned around, his gaze as cold as ice as he looked at Cecilia.

"I apologize, Father." Cecilia dared not look at the corpse on the ground, fighting back the urge to vomit.

The Duke of Roses took a deep breath and ordered, "Kyle, dispose of the body. Tonight, confiscate all of Sleet's assets."

"Yes, sir." Kyle gave a slight bow and called over two guards to carry away the noble's headless corpse.

In the vast conference room, only father and daughter remained, with no warmth of familial affection—instead, the atmosphere had grown colder than ever.

title: Chapter 48 — Gregory's Awkwardness (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 48 — Gregory's Awkwardness (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 31 · Chapter 48

"I'm twenty-one..." Cecilia lowered her head, feeling somewhat disappointed that her father couldn't even remember her own age.

"Twenty-one? So you're already an adult. Seeing your usual foolish behavior, I always thought you were still a child." Duke Rose's tone was flat.

"Mmm," Cecilia secretly clenched her fists. She had long ceased to be a child; her coming-of-age ceremony was years ago, and she remembered Father never attended it.

"Compared to your older brother and sister, you are a complete failure. Up to now you've achieved nothing. You are part of the family yet never strive for progress, always seeking help from others when facing difficulties, never thinking about making yourself better. When will you ever learn to stand on your own?" Duke Rose scolded mercilessly.

"I..." Cecilia had a belly full of rage, but in front of her father she dared not erupt, could only endure silently. She felt that when she tried hard, Father never saw it, only picking at her small faults to scold her. It was unfair.

"Sigh," Duke Rose took a breath, his expression melancholy, as if many words were stuck in his throat, very uncomfortable in his heart. "I once had some expectations for you, but you have disappointed me greatly."

"Hmm?" Cecilia raised her head in astonishment, feeling if she had heard wrong. Father had never praised her since childhood; scoldings were plenty, but expectations?

"The situation is very dangerous. The kingdom's fate hangs by a thread; Wales has become fat for the demons. I will personally lead troops into the demon realm." Duke Rose tapped the white paper on the table with his finger, speaking seriously. "This is my will. I've already written it. If I unfortunately die for the country, you will inherit my title and become Wales's new lord. I have no demands on you, only that you place the lives of the people first. After Wales falls, you must lead them to survive."

"!?" Cecilia was stunned, never expecting Father called her to discuss a will? And Father, who always looked down on her, actually chose her as the heir! By rights it shouldn't be her at all; it should be the more excellent older brother and sister.

Duke Rose, no matter how strong he appeared, knew clearly in his heart that Wales was already on the brink of falling.

Writing the will in advance wasn't to show he was prepared to sacrifice, but to prevent chaos in Wales after his death, passing the title to his youngest daughter to avoid unnecessary disputes.

"Your older brother and sister, though excellent, are profit-driven and lack a loving heart. They are unsuited to rule a territory. If they take over Wales, they will only deepen the poverty and suffering of the commoners, and the territory will fall into chaos sooner or later."

"Not that..." Cecilia was too agitated to speak. Inheriting the title and becoming the youngest duchess was her dream come true. She had long despised her arrogant father and wanted to make him look at her differently. Happiness came too suddenly, making it hard to believe.

Duke Rose came to Cecilia's side, reaching out to touch his daughter's hair, trying to show some affection.

"Always scolding you, you must hate me, right? I just..."

Duke Rose stopped himself, his hand hovering before he could touch his daughter. Any words expressing "love" would never come out of this man's mouth, even at death.

Duke Rose silently lowered his arm, his gaze turning cold and serious again, and walked straight out of the meeting room without another word to Cecilia. Silence returned to the room. Cecilia stood there in a daze for a long time, picking up the "will" on the table, her mood becoming complicated.

She had imagined countless ways she might inherit the title, never expecting it would be like this.

The dream opportunity was right before her eyes, yet Cecilia suddenly felt it held no allure. It tasted like charity. If possible, she didn't want this will to take effect—

If Lord Merlin were still in Wales, all problems could be solved easily, right? ◇

In a secluded room of the duke's mansion, Master Gregory, now a woman, lay in bed recovering her body.

In the battle against the 100,000 Mammon decoys, to buy time for the royal family and civilians to evacuate, she fought a desperate battle with the decoys.

Although she escaped at the last moment, her body suffered severe injuries, barely able to move on her own. She needed long rest to recover.

Gregory stroked her jet-black long hair and the excess flesh on her chest, sighing helplessly. Clearly she couldn't adapt to this new body in the short term.

Though she looked much younger, the female body felt too subtle, even somewhat shameful? Especially when others stared at her, she wanted to find a crack in the ground to crawl into.

Gregory worried. After all, she was a master revered by thousands. Now she was a woman. How would she face others from now on? Would she lose all her authority?

"... Weilan, taking care of Gregory beside her, saw her fussing with her hair and rubbing her chest, his face instantly darkened, falling into silence.

"Ding—" Little Ailia beside the bed stared at Gregory with wide eyes. Every move her teacher made now filled her with amazement, a feeling she had never had before.

Gregory noticed their strange looks, frowned in surprise, and asked straightforwardly, "What are you two staring at? Is it wrong for me to be a woman?"

"Not that..." Weilan's old face flushed red, hard to speak. He couldn't say directly that no woman would constantly rub her own chest—it was too out of place.

"Are you really my teacher? I'm very suspicious now," Ailia tiptoed and leaned on the bed, her eyes full of curiosity.

"I'm obviously your teacher. What's there to doubt? It's just that studying ancient magic changed my gender. Your magic was taught by me, the dragon lineage crystal was given by me. I remember your birthday, favorite food, and that you like kicking off the blankets while sleeping..." Gregory listed Ailia's habits to prove she was the real person.

"Uh, really teacher?" Ailia trembled, mustering courage to say directly—"Teacher, can you stop touching your chest? It's too awkward."

"The image of you as a respectable old man keeps appearing in my mind, but now you look like a pervert..." (w)

title: Chapter 49 — Regret
content:
Chapter 49 — Regret

Volume 31 · Chapter 49

“Teacher, does rubbing your own breasts feel comfortable?” Alice looked down at her completely undeveloped, flat chest and said helplessly, “It’s a pity I don’t have any; there’s no way for me to experience it.”

“Uh!” Gregory looked down and saw his hand resting on his breast. He quickly pulled it away as if shocked by electricity, covering his embarrassment with a cough. “Cough! I-I’m just having some trouble adjusting to this body. Being female is really not easy; you actually have to be dragged down by such excess flesh…”

“By the way, Teacher, you’re already quite old, so you shouldn’t have any desires left, right? Why are you rubbing your breasts so enthusiastically? I can’t figure it out~” Alice scratched her head, saying whatever came to mind.

“What… what… what nonsense are you asking?! Don’t be disrespectful, you rebellious disciple! Do you really want to embarrass the President so badly!?” Welan’s face turned dark, and he glared fiercely at Alice from below.

Gregory cried silently without speaking, wondering in his heart whether his appearance now had completely lost all authority in front of others. His glorious and majestic master image was shattered into pieces everywhere.

“I’m just curious about Teacher’s current state; I’m not intentionally trying to embarrass him!” Alice retorted, then turned around and continued, “Teacher looks so young now; you’re already considered a mature beauty. I don’t even know whether to call you Teacher or Older Sister, nyaa~~”

Gregory looked down at his useless student, who was already drooling and showing a lecherous smile. He deeply regretted releasing his power and allowing his life to flow again. The side effects of studying ancient magic had altered his entire physical structure.

“Teacher must not understand anything about women. You can openly come and ask me for advice. From now on, I plan to sleep together with Teacher, hehe~” Alice’s eyes narrowed into crescents like moons. Puffing out her chest, she began to educate her own teacher.

“Stop it right now!” Welan could bear it no longer and angrily slapped Alice on the head. “What can the President possibly learn from someone with a body that won’t develop?!”

“I don’t care! I just want to feel how Teacher’s breasts feel! What’s wrong with that?”

Alice bared her teeth ferociously at Welan and reached out with both small hands to pat Gregory’s breasts twice with a slap. The fullness on Gregory’s chest jiggled up and down, appearing incredibly elastic, instantly stunning everyone present.

“Ahhh!!!” Welan felt as though struck by lightning. He immediately lifted Alice off the ground. “You despicable guy, you actually got there before me!” “Put me down, or I’ll bite you?!” Alice wore a fierce expression, feeling that the Vice President was annoyingly naggy every day.

Gregory’s expression was stern, his face reaching the peak of ugliness. How had he, the dignified President of an Adventurers Guild, ever endured such treatment? Thus, he severely reprimanded them— “Enough! All of you get out! I want to be alone for a while.”

Seeing that Gregory’s expression and tone were not joking, the two realized they had angered the President. They hastily offered apologetic smiles and left. Welan: “It’s all your fault for being disrespectful, which made the President so angry. You should be locked up for reflection.” Alice: “Nonsense. Isn’t it because you were interfering nearby, preventing me from getting close to Teacher? You’re the one who should reflect!”

Listening to their bickering grow fainter and fainter, Gregory suddenly breathed a sigh of relief. Looking at this unfamiliar body, his heart was filled with mixed emotions. His lifetime reputation was ruined like this. Wouldn’t other adventurers joke about him whenever they had the chance?

Gregory planned to think of some way to re-establish his prestige. He couldn’t let this female body destroy his tall and imposing image. Thud, thud, thud. Welan pushed open the door and, for some unknown reason, returned. He looked at Gregory with a troubled expression.

“Didn’t I say I wanted to be quiet by myself? Why did you come back?” Gregory frowned.

“It’s not that, President. Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth has come to visit you.”

◇

In the room, Elizabeth sat on a chair, looking at Gregory’s female form. Her expression became somewhat unnatural. Could this really be Master Gregory? Why had he changed into this appearance? Was he originally female?

Elizabeth stared at Gregory for a long time, her heart filled with various doubts. Finally, unable to hold back, she asked, “Master Gregory?”

“Yes, it is me. There’s no need to doubt in your heart; it is indeed me.” Gregory saw through Elizabeth’s thoughts at a glance and decided to be straightforward.

Elizabeth’s mouth twitched, greatly startled. It really was Master Gregory. Wasn’t he supposed to be an elderly man? Why was he a young woman? Hadn’t even the founding emperor of the kingdom been deceived?

“You probably want to laugh at me, right? Don’t suppress yourself; laugh out loud. Anyway, I’ve already gotten used to it,” Gregory said calmly.

“No, no, no. How could I mock you? I just have some questions. Master, weren’t you originally female?” Elizabeth voiced the question in her heart.

“You’re overthinking it.” Gregory lowered his head and spoke slowly. “I am male. This current appearance is a side effect of practicing ancient magic.”

“Side effect?” Elizabeth put on a confused look, knowing nothing about magic.

“Actually, my lifespan had already nearly reached its end. I merely used ancient magic to pause the flow of my life, extending it by sacrificing mana. When I regained my mana, the price of practicing ancient magic would backlash upon me. As you can see, I turned into a woman.” Gregory smiled at Elizabeth and added, “My remaining life is very short; I can probably only live for about ten more years. This is my final period. Back then, I was a grandmaster of magic whose fame shook the continent; every move I made made the former Kingdom tremble with fear. Unexpectedly, my ten thousand years ended so absurdly, destined to die in the identity of a woman. People might ridicule me, perhaps?”

“…” Elizabeth fell silent. She had come to visit Gregory to check on his condition, hoping he might help the Kingdom fight once more. Who else besides Gregory could currently oppose the Demon Lord?

“You came to see me wanting me to act again to resist the invading demons, didn’t you?” Gregory stated directly. “It’s not that,” Elizabeth tried to explain, but Gregory interrupted her.

“There’s no need to be embarrassed; I understand everything. Egbert was my most outstanding student. Back then, he was merely a fugitive hunted by the former Kingdom. I taught him magic, never thinking he could overthrow the rule of the former Kingdom. Unexpectedly, he truly achieved it. He is indeed an astonishing person. I feel infinitely proud to have such a student. Both you sisters inherited some of his qualities, which brings me great comfort.” Gregory paused, his eyes flashing with distant memories. “Before your father passed away, he summoned me and entrusted you to my care, hoping I would look after you at critical moments. This was my beloved disciple’s only dying wish, so I helped you as much as possible. But as you can see, my current situation makes it impossible for me to even rely on myself to walk in the short term. It’s very regrettable…”

Elizabeth understood Gregory’s situation and forced a slight smile. “Master, please don’t blame yourself. Just rest and recover your health. I will handle all matters.”

“Carrying all the pressure alone truly resembles your father.” A smile appeared on Gregory’s face as he said meaningfully, “If only I had obtained the proof of the strongest adventurer. At times like this, I could contact other Purple Gold-ranked adventurers for assistance.”

“There are many extraordinary and interesting individuals among them. Defeating the Demon Lord is not impossible. Unfortunately, standing at the pinnacle of adventurers…” “Is not me.”

title: Chapter 50 — Borrowing Strength
content:
Chapter 50 — Borrowing Strength

Volume 31 · Chapter 50

I'm still some distance from being the strongest adventurer; even among a few purple-gold adventurers, there are some whose backgrounds I can't fathom." Gregory lowered his head and speculated, "Those who can obtain the Proof of the Strongest Adventurer must be flawless superpowers—beings that surpass purple-gold adventurers, capable of easily shifting the world's balance."
"What is the Proof of the Strongest Adventurer?" Elizabeth, who had some knowledge of the adventurer industry, knew the top rank was purple-gold, but this was the first time she'd heard of such proof.
"That is something left behind by the industry's founder, Robin Hood, representing the rise and fall of the adventurer trade; it is of great significance. Later, this proof is only awarded to the strongest adventurer within the industry, and like the Arbitration Committee, it grants partial authority to allocate purple-gold adventurers." Gregory explained patiently.
"I see..." Elizabeth nodded in understanding, thinking that if she had the Proof of the Strongest Adventurer, couldn't she have other purple-gold adventurers assist Britain? This item is truly precious; once one reaches the purple-gold level, they cannot be commanded merely by money.
The two thought it was incredibly precious, unaware that in Merlin's eyes it was nothing more than worthless rotten wood, long ago tossed into his household storeroom to gather dust.
"The current crisis is indeed hard to stop, but I feel there is someone who can resolve the kingdom's peril..." Gregory's tone grew much more serious.
"Who?" Elizabeth eagerly pressed.
"The great swordsman of Elgin." Gregory paused, then continued, "I once had a brief clash with him, suffering a considerable loss. Though I can't be certain, I feel his strength is extraordinary, faintly above mine; if he were to act, he could surely prevent Wales' downfall."
"This" Elizabeth gave an ugly smile, unable to voice the bitterness filling her heart.
She naturally knew she should seek the Elgin swordsman's aid, but he simply isn't in Britain, so asking would be useless.
"I've heard a bit about what happened after the Elgin swordsman; letting such a dangerous individual go free, you must have had contact with him, right? As the ruler of the kingdom, I don't believe you know nothing about his background." Gregory's gaze was like a torch, as if he had already seen through Elizabeth's thoughts.
"Hmm" Elizabeth felt a bit embarrassed, not knowing how to answer Gregory.
"It's fine if you don't want to say; since the capital fell and that man never appeared, he must have run into trouble, right?" Gregory asked again, while Elizabeth remained silent, finding it inconvenient to reveal anything about Merlin.
"It seems true." Gregory pondered for a moment, considering how to resist the demons, then said, "Then we can only place our hope on the kingdom's artifact."
"The King's Sword?" Elizabeth recalled the artifact entrusted to Mesfield, but unfortunately it couldn't alter the fact of the kingdom's fall.
"Exactly, since Mesfield has earned the King's Sword's acknowledgment, it shows she possesses the same potential as Egbert—capable of destroying a demon lord's doppelgänger, and thus capable of taking down more." Gregory furrowed his brow, speculating on various possibilities—
"I have seen Egbert unleash the power of this artifact; its might is astonishing, a rare weapon capable of large-scale destruction." "It's a pity Mesfield lacks sufficient strength; otherwise she would surely have defeated the demons and driven them from the kingdom's lands."
◇
In the dead of night, within the frontline camp of Wales.
Mesfield found a secluded spot to intensify her training; her stone sword danced through the dark with vigorous vigor.
She was drenched in sweat, panting, her wounds not yet fully healed; such frenzied training would only worsen her condition.
Yet she did not wish to disappoint the queen's expectations; her heart burned even more with vengeful fire, yearning to avenge her father as soon as possible.
Mesfield grew so exhausted she dropped to one knee, leaning on her stone sword to support her weary body; she could feel her fighting spirit draining wildly with each swing.
Although the artifact can enable the weak to leap to a level matching the strong, the power required is equally terrifying; it cannot be simply mastered.
Mesfield secretly resented her own weakness, unable to fully master the artifact and unleash its true power to avenge her father.
"How exactly can I unleash its true power?"
As her words fell, vapor began to rise from the stone sword, spreading through the air and gradually forming the graceful figure of a woman. The Lake Fairy floated before Mesfield, gazing at her with sympathetic eyes, saying, "Training has always been about steady progress; your haste will only backfire."
"I don't have that much time to take it slow; I must quickly unleash the artifact's power to avenge my father!" Mesfield lifted her head angrily.
"You, so easily ruled by hatred, how did you earn Egbert's acknowledgment?" The Lake Fairy shook her head, speaking calmly, "With your current strength, it's impossible to perfectly wield the King's Sword's power; even a single use would leave you drained and faint, showing your strength is not equal to the sword's—like an ant trying to carry a mountain."
"Then tell me what I should do! If even you don't know, don't spout useless remarks here!" Mesfield snapped, thinking the Lake Fairy was merely a beast inhabiting the stone sword, aside from retorting, it had done nothing to help.
"I greatly admire my first master, Egbert; he is someone who can stay calm in any situation, never complaining even when he falls." The Lake Fairy circled Mesfield, observing her, and said, "I'm curious why he would acknowledge you, when you share no resemblance at all."
"It's nothing to do with you!" Mesfield, irritated, glared at the Lake Fairy.
"It's fine either way; although you've become the new master of the King's Sword, I won't acknowledge you, but I believe Egbert—he is certainly not swayed by emotion—you must possess some potential." The Lake Fairy whispered softly into Mesfield's ear.
"What exactly are you trying to say? Are you just here to mock me?" Mesfield gripped her stone sword tightly. The Lake Fairy fluttered away, fixing her gaze on Mesfield's eyes, and slowly said—
"I am a magical beast formed from the elements, a pure fusion of force; its surging power exceeds your imagination." "Therefore I can lend you that force, but you must pay an equivalent price."
Ps■
Normally we give extra chapters for monthly tickets; illness periods are an exception. I truly am not intentionally doing one chapter a day—don't you get it?
I'm the author; who would go against subscribers? More writing, more rewards—I'll add a chapter soon.

title: Chapter 51 — Punish the Vulture (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 51 — Punish the Vulture (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 31 · Chapter 51

Of course, don't measure me with ordinary magical beasts. Like me, a pure elemental being, if you're willing, we can merge with humans. The lake fairy explained.

Mersfield lowered his head, thought, and seriously asked, "What is the price?" The lake fairy replied, "Your soul after death will belong to me, becoming my important sustenance."

The lake fairy stated the condition; although she is essentially a magical beast, despite her considerable wisdom and divinity, she cannot avoid needing humans as food for her growth, just like ordinary beasts.

Although the lake fairy does not appear as bloody and crude as ordinary magical beasts, and is rather picky, consuming only human souls, her essence remains unchanged.

"This is our agreement; when you unfortunately die, you must fulfill this promise."

Mersfield fell silent at once; the price of offering one's soul is heavy enough, and she does not know where a person's soul goes after death, but nobody would agree to have their soul eaten by a magical beast.

Suddenly Mersfield recalled the founding emperor Egbert, who after handing over the King's Sword to himself had his soul scattered; could the lake fairy be behind this?

"Was the founding emperor also making this deal with you..."

"That's right, but I promised him that I would not consume his soul until the King's Sword found a new master; later he gave the artifact to you, and we fulfilled the promise..."

The lake fairy said calmly, confirming Mersfield's suspicion: Egbert, to quickly gain great power, overthrew the previous kingdom's rule and made a deal with the lake fairy.

Mersfield felt a tinge of fear, instinctively clenched his fists, his heart grew uneasy, and he hesitated to respond to the lake fairy's terms.

"I am not forcing you; it's entirely up to your own will. If you want to gain great power in a short time, you must pay some price. Of course, if you prefer to rely on yourself and progress gradually, that's also fine—I will not interfere with your choice." The lake fairy's voice seemed to possess some magic, continually touching Mersfield's nerves.

"Why do you take human souls as food? Shouldn't magical beasts eat flesh and blood?" Mersfield was filled with doubt. "The biggest difference between me and other magical beasts is that I possess the ability to communicate with humans through rock energy, as well as divinity. To break free from the beast's shell, I must continually cultivate my divinity, elevating myself to an entirely new realm. Human souls have a strong allure for me, especially those with great potential; that is what I need most." The lake fairy paused, then spread her arms like a deity, saying, "However, I do not like to twist your will. I am very interested in humans; although your lifespans are short, you possess strong talent and unusual adaptability, which I admire. Therefore, if humans reject my proposed deal, I will not forcibly consume your souls."

Mersfield barely understood the lake fairy's meaning; to her, a human soul might be like a medicine that greatly enhances power, making it a deity she dreams of.

"Can you answer me a question? Where exactly do human souls go after death?"

"I also only half-understand this question. Although I have lived a long time and possessed consciousness since the age of the gods, back then I had no physical form, merely a mass of flowing water element, yet I could still sense external events." The lake fairy paused, then said slowly, "In the age of the gods, the souls of all deceased beings were imprisoned by the ancient gods in the Hall of Heroes, becoming food for the god-king's kept pets. Later, when the Twilight of the Gods arrived, souls fell into chaos, wandering everywhere. This condition persisted for a long time until two humans became the only remaining deities in heaven and earth, changed the world's rules, and became the architects of the new world order—this is why the human era arrived."

"Only two remaining deities?" Mersfield had never heard of these things; the lake fairy, who has lived through several epochs, could be called a living fossil recording history.

"Even if you don't know the Church of Light, you should have heard their name; although most of the Church of Light's stories have been beautified or exaggerated, some are indeed true. The only two remaining deities are Satan and Maria—one is the ruler of Hell, the other the master of Heaven." The lake fairy glanced at Mersfield and continued, "Under the new world's rules, the souls of all deceased beings go to Hell, where they suffer the cruel torment of the fiery deity."

"Isn't that wrong? Good people after death go to Heaven's blissful pure land, which everyone acknowledges!" Mersfield objected. "That's a lie; all things after death go to Hell—that's the truth. Not only humans, but all kinds—demons, dragons, elves, etc.—their souls ultimately end up in Hell." The lake fairy said emphatically, "Given your human abilities, it's hard to see this fact; don't think that being alive is painful, and that dying and going to Hell only brings pain a hundred or a thousand times greater. Why do undead calamities often occur? Because they desperately want to escape..."

Mersfield, upon hearing the lake fairy's facts, felt his worldview shaken. "What does it mean to be devoured by you?" "It means your existence will completely vanish; however, this occurs after your death. When you suffer torment in Hell's lava, with no one hearing your cries, you will find that being devoured by me is also a mercy." The lake fairy said gently.

Mersfield took a deep breath; the night's winter chill was quite cold, and his fiery heart gradually calmed. After a long while—"I accept your terms."

◇

In the Strait of Messina, inside the Sixth Degree Palace, tonight a special "guest" was escorted in—a large number of ragged pirates. The leader of the pirates was slender, looking like a noble's young master, out of place among the other pirates.

Luo Qili's eyes were blindfolded, his whole body bound in chains unable to move, while demons behind him kept shoving him and cursing.

"Move it! Don't dawdle! Dare to sneak attack us, rats of the Demon Lord Palace? See how Lord Mammon will deal with you! I'll make you wish you were dead!!"

He shouted!!

Luo Qili gritted his teeth; he was about to meet that greedy Demon Lord, his unease reaching its peak, constantly thinking how to escape this damned place!

He hated himself for making a grave mistake in judgment, falling for Mammon's scheme—the third Demon Lord Palace, which appeared defenseless, actually had traps laid long ago, waiting for him to walk into.

If he had been a bit more cautious, sending part of the pirates to feign an attack, he could have avoided this outcome; it's all his fault for being blinded by Mammon's treasure.

Luo Qili was ruthlessly shoved to the ground by the demons, two spears pinning him down so he couldn't rise; he faintly felt the terrifying aura of the Demon Lord. Mammon, seated on the Leviathan throne, slowly rose, looked down upon this gang of reckless pirates, and suddenly let out a cold chuckle, his expression amused, saying—

"Ha, a bunch of seafaring vultures that only deserve to eat carrion, dare to scheme against me?"

title: Chapter 52 — The Defense of Wales
content:
Chapter 52 — The Defense of Wales

Volume 31 · Chapter 52

"You lowly pirates, who gave you the courage to reach your hands toward me? If I'm not mistaken, there must be a mastermind behind you, right? The Holy Church? The Queen of Britannia? Or Leviathan?"

"Hahaha, I really got played." Loki lay on the ground sneering, "I thought you possessed extraordinary wisdom, seeing through my every move. Turns out you're just paranoid? What nonsense about the Holy Church, the Queen? The mastermind is me. Taking advantage of the chaos to plunder your Demon Lord Palace was my idea. The fact that you possess vast wealth is known to all; no instigation needed — plenty of people have their eyes on your riches. Didn't you call us vultures craving carrion? That's right, the scent of carrion wafts from you, which is why you attracted us."

"So you're saying I'm a dead man?" Mammon asked with an amused expression.

"Good comprehension, Demon Lord. Don't think only we have designs on you. You've stirred up such a commotion that even more people will covet your treasure. Plenty of opportunists looking to fish in troubled waters. I can see your death drawing nearer and nearer..." Loki let out bursts of mocking laughter, cursing Mammon like a madman.

"A bunch of bold pirates, clearly at death's door yet still spouting bewildering nonsense here, seeking death!" The Demon Lord's personal guard Ose, hearing Loki's demonic curses, stepped forward in rage, wanting to chop off Loki's head to make an example of him.

"Don't be impulsive. A cornered beast spouts delirious ravings before death; no one would take it seriously. Besides cursing, what other tricks do they have up their sleeves?" Mammon stopped Ose, saying with great interest, "Look at these pathetic pirates, already nearly scared out of their wits. I love the expressions they make when plunged into despair — so entertaining~"

"But Your Majesty..." Ose hesitated somewhat.

"Fucas is my capable subordinate. Having him guard the Demon Lord Palace, normally there wouldn't be any issues. But I heard he inexplicably turned to stone. Look at these weak pirates — not one is a match for Fucas, yet they managed to infiltrate the Demon Lord Palace and plunder it. There's definitely something fishy going on." Mammon stared at Loki below, musing, "That guy seems very confident in his own eyes? Ose, go take off his eye patch. Remember to be careful — don't make eye contact."

"As you command." Ose bowed slightly, approached Loki, grabbed his hair from behind, lifted his head, and tore off the eye patch. A pair of sharp, narrow eyes like a venomous snake's gleamed with purple light. Powerful otherworldly energy radiated outward, making the demons feel deeply uncomfortable all over.

"Argh!" Loki's face twisted savagely. He had wanted to seize the chance to kill the Greed Demon Lord, but Mammon had long been prepared and refused to meet his gaze, instead turning his back to the pirates and observing him through a mirror. "Didn't expect the Demon Lord to actually be a cowardly rat, lacking even the courage to turn around and look me in the eye. Laughable~"

"Say whatever you like. Being careful never hurts. You think a few words can provoke me? Save your breath." Mammon faced away from Loki, observing him through the mirror in his hand, finally solving the mystery in his heart. "So that's how it is? You relied on those eyes to kill my subordinate, right? Truly a dangerous fellow."

Ose glanced at the back of Loki's head, feeling a trace of fear in his heart. Fucas's strength was not beneath his own, yet he died at this human's hands. A single glance could turn a person to stone — what kind of power is this?

"Your eyes emit power from a mysterious otherworld. Although I don't know much about otherworlds, I know creatures from otherworlds are all dangerous. Where did you get those eyes? Could it be you're a running dog of the mysterious otherworld?" Mammon's mind was full of doubts; he knew very little about the mysterious otherworld.

"You think I'd tell you?" Loki said with a cold laugh.

"Doesn't matter if you don't say." A smug smile appeared on Mammon's face as he loudly commanded, "The war against Wales is about to begin. For now, lock up this bunch of pirates."

"After I completely take down the Kingdom of Britannia, I'll use these pirates' flesh and blood to reward my army. Remember to scrub them clean, otherwise the stench on pirates will make them hard to swallow."

"As for you? Those eyes with petrification power belong to me now. They'll become one of my collectibles. I'll take good care of them..." ◇

Several days later, Mammon's army had already set foot in Wales. The demons swept aside all opposition, capturing cities and seizing territory along the way, pressing straight toward Cardiff, Wales. To defend Wales, Duke Rose personally led troops to resist the demons' advance, fighting them until the world darkened.

The fierce flames of war between the two sides engulfed nearly half of Wales. They fought for three days and three nights without a victor emerging.

Because Wrexham was a remote small town, it wasn't too heavily affected, yet everyone remained in a state of panic, fearing the town might be destroyed overnight.

However, at Count Austin's earnest request, Old President Taylor's son Carl voluntarily joined the defense battle to protect Wales, throwing himself into slaughter alongside the demons.

Despite the Rose Duke's leadership, the garrison corps stationed in Wales and the Rose family's private army fought bravely, they still couldn't stop the demons' offensive. Danger had already approached Wales's most fortified city.

Great fires stretched for miles. Where the demons trampled, only ruins remained. They would not spare a single living human, steadfastly executing Mammon's plan to exterminate humanity.

Gunpowder smoke permeated the air. Though it was still daytime, the rolling thick smoke that rose into the sky never dissipated, casting the heavens into a gloomy dimness.

Shouts of killing shook the heavens on the battlefield. The demons, having captured the capital, were in high spirits — each one excited as if injected with chicken blood — causing the Welsh defense forces to suffer heavy casualties, retreating step by step.

Although the demon army's losses were also significant, under Mammon's incitement, they had long forgotten what "death" meant. They only knew that the more they killed, the richer the rewards.

In the demons' eyes, human lives were no longer useless livestock, but walking merits one by one, representing the possibility of overnight wealth.

Carl transformed into a golden lightning tiger on the battlefield, killing an ordinary demon with each punch. His terrifying destructive power was enough to pierce through their bodies.

He discovered these demons could not be killed no matter how many he slew. Like a flood, they came in an endless stream. Before he could even catch his breath, a swarm of demons would surround and attack him.

Carl had already fought a bloody battle for three days and three nights without sleep. The fighting spirit within his body was nearly exhausted. If this continued, he would be surrounded to death by ordinary demons —

Terrible. They simply can't hold the line. The number of demons is three times that of the Welsh defense forces!

title: Chapter 53 — Solar Slash
content:
Chapter 53 — Solar Slash

Volume 31 · Chapter 53

Karl stomped his foot suddenly, releasing the last bit of battle aura within him; instantly golden lightning flickered, pushing back all the demons that had surrounded him. His battle aura exhausted, he fell into extreme weakness, dropping to one knee, he glanced back at the distant city, thinking it could not be held; after Cadfael was occupied, the demons could attack Rexham in a day or two. With Rexham's feeble defenses, it was even less possible to block the demon army; facing the demons, the townsfolk had no option even to surrender. Karl sighed, hearing the demons' charge; after barely repelling them, they quickly organized another wave of attack, a mighty surge came forward. The Duke of Rose led from the front, commanding the soldiers to clash fiercely with the brutal demons; his sword‑swinging figure was heavy and powerless, clearly his stamina had reached its limit and he could barely hold on. Usually aloof, the duke now looked grimy and disheveled, his battle‑uniform reduced to rags hanging on him, stained with much demon blood. After slashing two ordinary demons in succession, the Duke of Rose's breathing grew ragged, his vision darkened, he seemed to fall backward, his consciousness becoming increasingly hazy. Kael suddenly appeared behind the duke, quickly supporting him, "Your Grace? Are you alright?" Seeing Kael, the duke regained a bit of consciousness and demanded, "Why are you here? Shouldn't you be guarding Cecilia's side?" "Miss Cecilia said she doesn't need protection, she asked me to look after you; she's very worried about your situation." Kael explained. "When did I fall to the point where Cecilia has to worry about me?" the duke sighed, speaking sternly, "Given the current situation, we cannot hold out; go tell Her Majesty the Queen to have them flee northward now." "But what about you?" Kael thought returning would be hard to explain to Cecilia. "I can still fight; as the lord of Wales, I will share the fate of this land. As long as I live, I will not allow demons to run rampant on my territory." The duke pushed Kael away, his eyes fixed on the charging demons, ready to rally the soldiers to join forces and block them. Kael watched the duke's swaying frame, obviously at the end of his tether, unable to last much longer. Woo— A thunder‑like horn blast rang out; the demons that had launched the charge halted, scattering to both sides, clearing a wide passage. A legion of a hundred thousand demon‑armored stand‑ins for the Demon Lord appeared on the battlefield, a vast steel torrent, advancing with murderous aura. The vanguard demons had fulfilled their mission, having consumed most of Wales' defending forces in preparation for the demon‑armored legion; now it was up to the armor stand‑ins to clean up the remnants and completely raze Wales' most prosperous city. Each demon armor bore a pressure close to Mammon's true form; when a hundred thousand of them stacked, the sheer dreadful pressure alone already surpassed Mammon's own. The defenders of Wales saw the neat ranks of armor pressing in, felt the suffocating pressure, and instantly abandoned resistance, their minds went blank, standing motionless, not even noticing their swords slipping from their hands. Such a disparity in strength needed no clash; on the spot it was enough to break everyone's will, and they finally understood why the capital had fallen—when any human kingdom faces the armor legion, successfully holding the land is a rare occurrence. "Your Grace?" Kael noticed the duke's body trembling, looking at the armor legion, his cracked lips moved, yet he could not utter a word. The duke closed his eyes, sighed, and said, "The gap is too great; with this force, the demons have doomed the kingdom." Uh Kael saw the duke had already given up, anxiety welled up in him—could nothing be stopped? Mammon's armor stand‑ins rose into the air, floating in the sky; they lifted both hands, gathering powerful magic bolts. For a moment the magic bolts formed a spectacular light curtain, instantly spreading across the whole sky, a violent storm was whipped up, the aura of destruction made hearts tremble! Boom! A hundred thousand stand‑in magic bolts poured down, bathing the entire battlefield in crimson light, just as the duke's defeat was sealed. A giant black‑sided eagle swept over the battlefield; with a mighty eagle cry, a huge water curtain unfurled instantly, blocking the hundred thousand magic bolts from outside. The magic bolts struck the water curtain, huge explosions boomed repeatedly, the ground beneath the soldiers' feet rumbled. Meresfield descended from the heavens, his gaze different from before, as if filled with firm resolve. "Lord Meresfield?!" Kael stared in shock; a few days ago this first knight had said he was going into seclusion, yet when the war began he was nowhere to be found—unexpectedly he appeared at the critical moment? "Lend me your strength," Meresfield's inner power suddenly burst forth with tremendous pressure, his whole body gradually turning liquid; though his appearance differed from the lake fairy, his likeness was seventy‑percent similar! "What is this?" Karl stared at Meresfield's strange state, feeling greatly astonished, for he could sense a hint of beast‑like aura! Meresfield had formed a contract with the lake fairy; due to limited time, he had completed only the first stage of fusion. Nevertheless, relying on the lake fairy's power, Meresfield's strength broke through the Saint tier and entered the Ancestral realm. The increase in strength was plain to see; Meresfield will unleash even greater power from the King's Sword, and with the divine artifact he will have the qualification to challenge Mammon. The lake fairy willingly fused with Meresfield, unlike Diktapin, Merlin, and Tanya, who seized elemental beast power by slaughter, causing the beasts' consciousness and divinity to vanish. The lake fairy, however, volunteers to merge with humanity; it not only grants the host power but also shares its divinity with Meresfield, causing her whole being to undergo a transformation. Meresfield appeared on the battlefield in a new guise; in the distant Sixth Demon Lord Palace, Mammon watched all this, his voice echoing over the battlefield—"To defeat me, have you sunk to borrowing the power of beasts? The knights of Britain are truly laughable~" "Shut up! Demon Lord! The time to repay debts has come!" Meresfield raised his stone sword high, pointing it at the dense ranks of armor stand‑ins—crack crack crack, the sound of shattering rang out; fine fissures appeared on the stone sword, the stone layer on the blade began to peel off, gradually revealing the true form within! The blade, wholly golden, bore natural patterns engraved all over, possessing the exquisite beauty of nature's own craftsmanship! It constantly exudes a pressure akin to that of a deity; upon appearance it commands all eyes, shining brilliantly even in the gloomy sky, as if even the sun could not compare with it? The King's Sword, Britain's national treasure, finally reveals its true form here.

title: Chapter 54 — Darkness Nemesis (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 54 — Darkness Nemesis (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 31 · Chapter 54

I heard my grandfather say that the sword is called the King's Blade, it is the treasure of the founding emperor Egbert, which helped him defeat the previous kingdom and establish Britain, making a huge contribution. The once-famous undead legion was obliterated by this sword, forging an immortal legend. The royal family regards it as the symbol of national power, an unequivocal treasure of the state……" Duchess Rose said slowly, her expression continuously shifting, her emotions unable to calm for a long time.
凯尔 looked at the King's Blade in Mesfilde's hand, indeed feeling the aura of a king, the light on the sword attracting everyone's gaze.
"I always thought this treasure had been buried with the founding emperor, but I never expected the queen to take it out and even give it to the first knight?" Duchess Rose paused, then sighed, saying, "It seems in the queen's eyes, Lord Mesfilde is more trustworthy than her own kin."
"Oh? Your strength has increased a lot in a short time; do you really think you can wield this divine artifact and defeat me?" Asmodeus's voice echoed across the battlefield, his tone dripping with mockery.
"Shut up!"
Mesfilde let out an angry shout, wildly pouring his fighting spirit into the King's Blade in his hand, causing the blade to tremble continuously.
With a crack, the King's Blade underwent a strange change, splitting from the middle line of the blade, the separated area filled with countless currents connecting.
Dense currents began to gather at the center of the separated blade, forming a tiny condensed mass of divine power, increasing the artifact's majesty tenfold!
Mesfilde could clearly feel that the power of the King's Blade had been unleashed, becoming increasingly difficult to control.
"“Die! Demon Lord!""
As soon as the words fell, Mesfilde raised the King's Blade, aiming at the area where Asmodeus had the most armor substitutes, and the condensed divine power erupted! A terrifyingly powerful heat cannon shot from the King's Blade, with a wide coverage, enveloping most of the enemies in scorching heat. Wherever the heat cannon passed, everything turned to ash; those demons were instantly vaporized just by a glance. This blast dealt Asmodeus heavy losses, directly obliterating tens of thousands of armor substitutes, tearing a hole in the encirclement. Feeling the artifact's residual might, Karl stared wide-eyed, “What kind of power is this?!”
"I see now, I finally understand why the undead legion was destroyed; this treasure's power is so great it could even kill a god." Duchess Sylvia's forehead beaded with cold sweat, thinking that Britain still had its heritage, it was impossible that in the face of a large-scale invasion they would have no trump card at all.
Karl gazed at Mesfilde's war-god-like figure; the King's Blade in his hand, after firing, emitted a faint white glow—this was no ordinary blade, but a portable magical cannon of artifact level!
"As I expected, this divine artifact's power is astonishing." Asmodeus paused, his tone filling with anger, "I will surely obtain it; no one who destroys my toy can still jump around alive—you will pay the price."
After becoming enraged, Asmodeus went mad, wanting to quickly kill the enemy holding the divine artifact before him, so he used the move that had left Grigory powerless to retaliate.
The remaining demon armor numbered roughly sixty thousand; their chests lit up again, forming magic bolts that gathered together, creating a massive, astonishingly powerful super magic mass!
Grigory could do nothing against this terrifyingly powerful attack; it nearly blasted the entire royal capital's land into the sky.
However, after losing a large number of demon armors, the super magic bolt's power and pressure greatly weakened, far less than when Grigory faced it, yet still not to be underestimated.
""Shout!“ Mesfilde, despite feeling somewhat lacking in stamina, gritted his teeth and raised the King's Blade again, preparing to unleash a second divine power cannon, but was stopped by the lake fairy inside him.
Lake Fairy: "Stop, your fighting spirit is about to run out; you can't support a second swing, forcing it will backfire on you, you'll regret it."
Mesfilde: "I don't care about that; if I lose here, Wales will also fall, we must decide the outcome here!" Just as Mesfilde was about to stubbornly continue swinging for a second blade, a biting cold wind swept in; although it was midwinter, this sea wind felt as if it came from a more dreadful polar region, cold enough to dull one's thoughts.
After Alice mastered the true usage of the Bright Chant, she also hurried overnight from Rexham to support; fortunately she arrived at the critical moment, no matter what she could not allow Asmodeus to continue ravaging this land; since Merlin is absent, she can only rely on herself to resolve the kingdom's crisis.
"Alice?!"
Karl spotted Alice's figure, his heart filled with doubt; after hearing his father's account, he still thought Alice wouldn't come to support, but would take her daughter north to seek refuge.
It seems Karl still doesn't understand Alice; that blazing heart of justice has never been extinguished—how could she possibly stand by and watch countless innocents perish without helping?
Alice rushed straight to the battlefield's center, shed the warm cloak draped over her, drew the sharp slender sword Bright Chant from her waist, and went into battle lightly. Only seeing her leap up, a swing of her hand caused the ground to sprout golden ice pillars that seemed alive.
Alice stepped upon the winding, twisting ice pillars and shot straight into the sky, her agile figure like a surfer, directly reaching the clouds and vanishing from sight. “What is she up to?” Karl wondered, unable to understand Alice's actions, thinking perhaps she was just passing by to make a presence known.
Suddenly, the sky filled with dark clouds began to shimmer with kindness, crackling lightning fluttering within the clouds, faintly revealing the shadows of countless unknown creatures.
Asmodeus suddenly became alert, sensing a faint strange unease, and immediately shifted his target, launching the super magic charge he had been preparing for a long time straight into the sky!
"Ugh! Why is the demon lord no longer attacking us?" Karl's expression was incredulous; he couldn't comprehend Asmodeus's thinking—clearly, pressing the attack would let Wales fall, yet the enemy suddenly changed its target.
"It's afraid." Duchess Rose quickly sensed something amiss, solemnly saying, "The demon lord realizes there is something more dangerous than us!" "No way, Miss Alice," Karl exclaimed in astonishment.
Boom boom boom, the clouds above the demon armor legion were dispersed, Alice bathed in holy light descended from the heavens, comparable to a valkyrie punishing evil.
As soon as she appeared, she gave her all, employing her strongest sword technique, the third form of the Snow Mountain Sword Art—"Opening Heaven"—and unleashing the true power of the Bright Chant—
Resounding holy songs intertwined, and following behind Alice descending from the heavens was indeed a magnificent army of a million holy spirits!
