As Mammon, the Demon Lord of Greed, its vindictive nature showed clearly, consistently adhering to the belief that no one could take advantage of it. The Seven Kings Conference would be its stage for turning things around.

The Seven Kings Conference was the most fundamental meeting in the demon race, spearheaded by the Elder Council and held every fifty years. All seven demon monarchs must attend in person, mainly to discuss the future development of the demon race and conduct periodic summaries.

Merlin had only attended this special meeting once and remembered being fiercely reprimanded by the elders—they said Merlin lacked grand ambitions and was unworthy of being a proud monarch, that he would lead the First Demon Lord Palace into an abyss, and frequently compared him to Vivian, believing he hadn't inherited a single excellence from his strong mother, and that lowly demons born purely through succubus power were simply incapable ofShouldering important responsibilities.

Merlin naturally held no fondness for the Seven Kings Conference, but such meetings concerned the fate of every demon lord. All rulers of the demon palaces were required to attend; otherwise, they would provoke immense dissatisfaction from the Elder Council.

Just thinking about the punishment Merlin would receive at the Seven Kings Conference slightly improved Mammon's heavy mood. It prepared to temporarily leave Leviathan's territory—in case it ran into Leviathan, there might yet be another battle.

"So this is the current Demon Lord? Truly disappointing, like a stray dog~"

In the empty ruins of the Demon Lord Palace, the voice of a girl suddenly echoed, like a fairy's whisper reverberating in Mammon's ears. "Eh!?" Mammon's entire body bristled, and it sharply turned around—

A black-haired, red-eyed girl was sitting nonchalantly upon the Demon Lord's throne, wearing a black frilly dress suited to her age. She crossed her legs, looking down from above at the startled Mammon, a mocking smile on her face—clearly not regarding the Demon Lord with any respect.

The suddenly appearing girl was none other than Cain, who had just left the isolated island not long ago. She had discovered the Demon Lord Palace was already in great disarray, entering without the slightest effort, and even daring to sit ostentatiously upon the Demon Lord's position.

However, she didn't find Dexter's figure anywhere nearby—likely he was observing from close by, waiting to see how his "master" would toy with the Demon Lord.

Mammon's heart pounded wildly. If that对方 hadn't spoken, it never would have noticed—and if it wanted to kill itself, perhaps it could have succeeded just now! "Who are you!?"

"Cain." Cain smiled and stated her name, then realized the other party likely didn't know her, so she changed her answer—"Right, you probably don't recognize me?"

"Just call me the Progenitor of the Vampire Race instead…"

title: Chapter 66 — Piercing
content:
Chapter 66 — Piercing

Volume 31 · Chapter 66

Mammon frowned, sinking into deep confusion, completely unable to understand Cain, unable to tell whether this suddenly appeared guy was enemy or friend? However, it had still heard of the existence of vampires; according to human fashion, like demons, both belonged to the camp of dark creatures.

But Mammon's understanding of vampires was limited to variant creatures appearing among humans, similar to a bizarre race appearing from infection with some epidemic disease. Mammon suppressed the doubts in its heart, staring at this mysterious girl; the other party sitting so casually on the Demon Lord's position had already violated taboos.

After a quick moment of thought, since Mammon didn't understand the enemy, it didn't dare to act rashly; moreover, the other party had approached silently, likely a troublesome character.

"You suddenly came before me, exactly what is it you want?"

"That knife in your hand..." Cain slowly stood up from the throne, speaking bluntly, "Hand it over to me, and I'll let you live."

"Ah?" Mammon raised its eyebrows, thinking it had misheard. Tyrfing was its lifeline, absolutely impossible to hand over. This was the first time it had seen anyone lay hands on Tyrfing. "Are you joking?"

"Do I look like I'm joking?" Cain held an ordinary fine-steel longsword, slowly descending the platform. "Demons don't always like making deals? Then let's make a deal too—use the divine artifact in your hand to exchange for your own life from me—"

"What did you say?" Mammon's face instantly became extremely ugly. Being bullied by Merlin, another monarch, was one thing, but now what stray dogs and cats dared to jump out and ride on its head? Absolutely outrageous!

"Choose: die? Or hand over the divine artifact in your hand? You'd better think carefully, otherwise you might not see tomorrow's sun..." Cain gazed into Mammon's eyes—undoubtedly forcing Mammon to submit.

~Ha ha ha, Mammon let out bursts of low laughter, speaking in a self-deprecating tone—

"How utterly failed I've become? Now all kinds of messy guys dare to have designs on me. Truly laughable."

"You're nothing but a despicable creature that survives by parasitizing on humans. You've never even existed in the long river of history. Why do you have the courage to stand before me?"

"I am the greedy monarch of the demon race, one of the Seven Kings! Absolutely not some poor wretch that anyone can pick on!" "You came at exactly the right time—I'm already in a foul mood, might as well slaughter you to vent my anger!" "Seems like you're not very smart, but rather very foolish." Cain shook its head, a glimmer of pity flashing in its deep eyes.

"Don't underestimate me! Tiny mosquito!" Mammon's face was hideous, its huge body trembling, raising Tyrfing in its hand and slashing down at Cain with power! Accompanied by howls like ghosts and wolves crying, the terrifying silhouettes of evil spirits appeared suddenly, interweaving into a sharp cutting net that shrouded Cain in death's shadow!

The fierce evil spirit storm cut the ground beneath Cain into countless small squares. A normal person would probably have been killed by the sharp wind blades long ago, yet she stood motionless, a smile on her face, as if mocking Mammon.

Only then did one see Cain grip the hilt of the longsword at its waist, instantly drawing the blade. A killing aura similar to Merlin's erupted, shattering the evil spirit cutting net released by Tyrfing!

The solid ground and the walls of the Demon Lord Palace both showed shocking sword marks in the unseen. This scene seemed as if it had just happened, as if replaying once more?

"This!?!" Mammon was greatly alarmed, taking a step back in panic. A strong sense of déjà vu made it suspicious. "Impossible!? The exact same drawing sword technique! How could you possibly have Lucifer's drawing sword technique!? Who exactly are you!~"

^Oh? Lucifer? Haha" Cain laughed very happily, speaking with meaningful mockery. "So that's why this world is so small. Originally he is the first monarch of the Ting clan! Interesting! Really too interesting! I've always wondered why someone who looks ordinary would possess such terrifying power! If it's the Demon King, it all makes sense! A proud demon lord, actually living at the bottom of the human world as an adventurer? How laughable!"

~Uh..." A drop of cold sweat slid down Mammon's forehead, thinking what crazy nonsense this madman was spouting?

"Since you asked why I have Lucifer's drawing sword technique, I'll tell you..." Cain bent slightly at the waist, waterfall-like black hair slipping off its shoulders, revealing a seemingly "innocent" smile. "He's my dad, okay? Can you believe that answer?"

"Boring lies. As long as Lucifer wants, there would be plenty of beautiful women in the demon race. Why would he lower himself to breed a child with a despicable vampire? This would bring shame to his ancestors!" Mammon didn't believe Cain's nonsense at all, because the holes were too big.

"Actually, you're already a corpse. Does it matter whether you believe it or not?" Cain said with a teasing tone.

Mammon fell silent, its expression grave, feeling immense pressure. The other party having Lucifer's drawing sword technique was beyond its expectations—just how far had she mastered Lucifer's drawing sword technique? If it was not inferior at all, it definitely couldn't win.

Worst of all was its body—severe injuries from fighting Lucifer. Now it had to deal with a powerful vampire? Without using some despicable means, it was impossible.

Mammon carefully analyzed the current situation, suddenly its face darkened. It held Tyrfing across its chest and said in a low tone. "I accept your conditions. You can take this Tyrfing. My current state is terrible, I have no strength to fight anymore."

"You really gave up the thought of resisting?" Cain's smile deepened, its deep crimson eyes like an abyss, making it hard for others to see what it was thinking.

"I give up, come take it." Mammon answered with a blank face, but its heart was active. Although Lucifer's drawing sword technique was overbearing and extremely powerful, it still had some small weaknesses. Drawing the sword required certain distance and space; as long as the distance was close enough, that was Mammon's home turf! Wait for death, dog shit True Ancestor! It wouldn't let Cain use the drawing sword technique!

Suddenly, a chilling cold wind swept past. Mammon's heart was instantly pierced from behind! Mammon stared in horror, eyes wide, looking at the fine-steel longsword that pierced its heart, its brain blank!

It trembled all over, turning its head slightly back, seeing Cain behind it with a bizarre smile. An ordinary fine-steel longsword had pierced through its heart. "You..."

"Do you think I don't know what you were thinking?" Cain paused, its mouth stretching to its ears, making it look even more terrifying—"*You were thinking of tricking me closer, then taking the chance to kill me"

"It must be like that, right?! I can see it all!"

"I won't believe anyone! Including the mother who created me!"

title: Chapter 67 — The Ultimate Cold (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 67 — The Ultimate Cold (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 31 · Chapter 67

Mammon's eyes showed fear and unease; the intense pain from his heart left him unable to move—just a moment ago he was in front of me, why did he suddenly appear behind me? Even though it was only an instant, I could feel her presence vanish completely! No matter how fast one is, this is impossible; even space magic should leave a magical fluctuation. How did she do it? With this uncanny ability to appear and disappear, none of my attacks can reach her! Mammon realized the gravity of the situation; he felt like a lost ant being toyed with by Cain, their strengths not even on the same level. “Since you’re so cunning, I won’t let you off easily either. What treasure gives the most peace of mind when used? Of course, it’s one without an owner—you must understand that, right?” Cain asked with a smile. “Shout!” Mammon swung Tirfing angrily behind him, but he couldn’t touch Cain at all. Cain lightly tipped his toes and in the blink of an eye opened a safety distance of several dozen meters, wearing a smug grin. Mammon’s vision went black; his bulky body swayed and collapsed heavily. He had to prop himself up with Tirfing, black blood gushing continuously from his chest. His heart suffered such a severe fatal wound that healing before death was virtually impossible. Although he had some decent regenerative ability, it wasn’t strong enough to heal a pierced heart. Mammon breathed heavily, cold sweat pouring from his back, clearly feeling his life draining away. Pressing on his chest wound did nothing, and his consciousness began to blur. “Take a look at your pitiful state—I really want to hold up a mirror so you can see yourself~” Cain revealed a hint of pitying gloom. “Don’t… don’t get too happy too soon…” Mammon wearily retorted, forcing himself to appear fine, but his weak tone had already exposed his condition—what should I do? If this continues, I’ll really die; I must think of another way to deal with this monster. Mammon gritted his teeth, suddenly glaring wide-eyed as if mustering a last burst of strength, ignoring his grievously wounded heart, he focused everything into Tirfing. “Even if I die! I won’t let you go! Let’s all go to hell together!!!” Mammon poured all his remaining strength into Tirfing, instantly unleashing a rending storm that swept across the ruins of the Demon Lord Palace. A huge evil spirit phantom began to manifest, roaring angrily at Cain like a drowned ghost desperately trying to drag the enemy down to share its doom. It seemed Mammon had been driven to a dead end, willing to stake everything, dragging Cain down with him in a mutual destruction, hoping to regain his dignity at the last moment. The sharp airflow sliced a few strands of Cain’s hair, yet she remained calm and composed, “Is this the last desperate counterattack of a dying wild dog?” “Fall beneath the blade of Tirfing!” Mammon glared furiously, then brought down his demon blade with terrifying rending power that would move even the gods. However, unexpectedly… Mammon’s attack was not aimed at Cain at all, because he had no confidence he could kill this unfathomable foe. The swing of Tirfing happened to be directed toward the entrance of the Demon Lord Palace. Mammon cherished his life too much to seek mutual destruction; instead he deliberately struck outward, hoping to create a huge commotion that would draw attention and bring reinforcements— Lucifer surely hasn’t gone far; if we make enough noise here, he’ll definitely notice the abnormality! After my defeat, there couldn’t still be such fierce fighting here; this would arouse Lucifer’s suspicion and make him return to check the situation. Then, out of kinship, Lucifer would lend me aid, and I could survive! I can’t possibly defeat this monster; only Lucifer might be able to. Mammon’s all‑or‑nothing attack was actually aimed at the soaring Merlin—a plea for help, his only chance to survive. But Mammon’s actions, just as suspicious as Cain’s, would she not notice? Seeing Mammon’s attack about to trigger a massive explosion in the Demon Lord Palace, Cain’s expression remained calm. She let out a cold snort, took a step forward, and the surrounding world underwent a complete transformation— Cold, ultimate cold! A temperature beyond imagination’s reach! Only one who truly grasps the laws of the world can touch this mysterious realm! In Cain’s eyes, the world had changed into a silent, ice‑bound dead world—though it looked no different from reality, here there was no life, no sound, not even the flow of time remained. Cain was like a lone traveler wandering through this frozen world; the entire Demon Lord Palace was sealed in ice, the ground beneath her feet gleamed like a mirror, reflecting her image. Cain approached Mammon unhurriedly; at this moment the greedy Mammon had become an ice statue, still holding Tirfing poised to slash outward toward the Demon Lord Palace’s exit, lifelike. This is exactly what the white dragon Alfad said in the Ancestral Dragon Holy Hall—the law of ultimate cold! Ultimate cold isn’t merely about freezing people; reaching its true extreme means it can freeze everything, even time itself. Under Cain’s display, time had actually stopped, but as the controller of this law, she could still move freely within the frozen world. It seems Cain used this interval to have learned everything about Alice—even her future potential—inside out! “Poor wretch…” Cain admired Mammon’s ice sculpture for a moment, then suddenly unleashed a draw‑and‑cut slash, splitting Mammon’s body in two at the chest. Although Mammon still appeared intact and unharmed, he could already be declared dead; all that was needed was— Cain raised her hand, snapped her fingers with a crisp “pa,” and the icy world instantly shattered; ice crystals scattered into the air and vanished, and the frozen time resumed flowing. Mammon’s wish for rescue was nipped in the bud; his all‑out assault was interrupted, and facing Cain he had no room to resist. “All your thoughts I’ve seen through; in a sense we’re alike, but sadly you’re destined to be devoured by me—down to the last bone fragment.” Cain gave a faint smile. “Cough!” Mammon coughed up blood; from the corner of his eye he saw his body already split in two at the chest, his consciousness fading rapidly—again this situation? No warning at all, it just appeared! By the time he realized, he had already been slashed! It’s as if, in my unawareness, I had received a fatal blow beforehand! What a terrifying monster this is!! Mammon’s blood sprayed across the Demon Lord Palace floor; the two halves of his corpse collapsed, his eyes already dull, and even in death he never understood how he’d been defeated. Cain looked at Mammon’s corpse on the ground, let out an indifferent snort from her nose, and remarked— “Is this the Demon King? Compared to the first‑generation Demon Lords, he’s nowhere near the same—with this strength, how could he fight my mother?” “In the end, he’s just a joke.”

title: Chapter 68 — Abandoned Refined Steel
content:
Chapter 68 — Abandoned Refined Steel

Volume 31 · Chapter 68

The flames flickered and faded, and Dick Trice's figure slowly materialized. He gazed down at Mammon's corpse, a deep shock churning within him that refused to settle.

Could the King of Demons really fall so easily?

Now's power seemed to have far surpassed his initial days—his growth rate was truly astonishing!

The mighty Greedy Monarch couldn't hold out for three rounds against Nao—was I really going to benefit from this monster?

Dick Trice felt a deep unease. Nao's strength had exceeded his expectations. He understood all too well the danger of serving her. But once you've drawn the bow, there's no calling back the arrow. Now that he'd boarded Nao's ship, it would be hard to escape her.

Dick Trice had originally thought Nao was joking when she said she'd toy with the Demon Lord until death. He hadn't expected it all to be true—Mammon showed no resistance at all in Nao's hands.

In Dick Trice's understanding, the rulers of the Porphyria clan were among the strongest in this world. Yet that notion had been effortlessly crushed by Nao. He could no longer read his own master at all.

"What are you thinking? How does it feel to stare at this for so long?" Nao asked, her tone laced with meaning.

"Ah!" Dick Trice broke into a cold sweat, quickly kneeling on the ground, trembling as he spoke, "Your power sweeps all before it—you can play with even a Demon Lord at will. I admire you from the bottom of my heart! No matter what happens, I will serve you loyally..."

"Hmph!" Nao scoffed lightly, saying calmly, "You're being too clever—I hate people who try to be sly in front of me—"

"This..." Dick Trice dodged and weaved, embarrassed, "I'm just overwhelmed by your greatness..."

"It's not that impressive. If I reclaim all the divine power of the undead, I'll make a qualitative leap. Only then will I barely be worthy of standing against my mother..." Nao sighed, "To challenge my mother, my current strength still isn't enough."

"Barley enough?" Dick Trice was uncertain in his heart. What exactly did this monster want to do? She could already kill a Demon Lord, yet still felt unsatisfied—he couldn't see where her limits lay!

"This guy is surprisingly weak~" Nao bent down to look at Mammon's corpse, sneering, "He's weak to the core, so dependent on his divine artifact. Once that blade stops working for him, he's destined to die by my hand."

Dick Trice looked down and saw the gleaming Tyrfing on the ground, a sinister aura swirling around it. "Is this the divine artifact? Somehow... I don't feel so good..."

Tyrfing. Nao picked up the demon sword and held it in her hand, examining it carefully, then said slowly—

"A blade destined to bring ruin to its wielder?"

"How interesting."

"I'm already at rock bottom—could it make me even more refined than I am now?"

Nao and Dick Trice quickly left the Demon Lord Palace. In the ruined city, only Mammon's cold corpse remained. *Gulp.* Suddenly, a series of hurried footsteps echoed, and a familiar figure returned. Mammon's personal guard, Osay, had been punched by Merlin and had only just awakened now.

Osay limped toward the ruins of the Demon Lord Palace, eager in his heart to learn the outcome of the battle between the two Demon Lords. Whether win or lose, it would determine the current situation.

When Osay reached the center of the ruins and saw Mammon's body severed in two, he was horrified, his eyes widening.

He fell to the ground, crawling on hands and knees to Mammon's side. After checking, he found Mammon's heart pierced by a blade and no longer beating, his body cleanly severed by a sharp edge—he was already dead through and through!

Osay grieved, kneeling beside Mammon with his lips tightly closed, tears streaming down like beads about to snap, *plink plink* falling to the ground. For a man to be reduced to tears, it showed how deeply Mammon's death had struck him.

He had always hoped a ruler would rise to lead the demons in fighting back against humanity. Mammon was that hero who dared to challenge the rules. Osay inwardly admired Mammon, regarding him as the only master worth serving.

Yet all of this had been destroyed by Lucifer III. His dreams had faded with Mammon's death.

Osay had assumed that between Mammon and Lucifer, at least one would end up severely wounded—but absolutely no Demon Lord would die. No matter how they fought, they wouldn't endanger each other's lives. This was the consensus among the rulers. Anyone who violated it would face the harshest punishment from the Council of Elders!

Osay threw a punch into the ground, his eyes reddened not from anger but from fury. He lifted Mammon's body, intending to take his master back to the Third Demon Lord Palace first. "Lucifer III, truly an impulsive and reckless destabilizing factor. Your Majesty was right."

"I'll definitely avenge you, master, and make Lucifer III pay a painful price!"

Nao and Dick Trice quickly left the Demon Lord Palace. In the ruined city, only Mammon's cold corpse remained. *Gulp.* Suddenly, a series of hurried footsteps echoed, and a familiar figure returned. Mammon's personal guard, Osay, had been punched by Merlin and had only just awakened now.

Osay limped toward the ruins of the Demon Lord Palace, eager in his heart to learn the outcome of the battle between the two Demon Lords. Whether win or lose, it would determine the current situation.

When Osay reached the center of the ruins and saw Mammon's body severed in two, he was horrified, his eyes widening.

He fell to the ground, crawling on hands and knees to Mammon's side. After checking, he found Mammon's heart pierced by a blade and no longer beating, his body cleanly severed by a sharp edge—he was already dead through and through!

Osay grieved, kneeling beside Mammon with his lips tightly closed, tears streaming down like beads about to snap, *plink plink* falling to the ground. For a man to be reduced to tears, it showed how deeply Mammon's death had struck him.

He had always hoped a ruler would rise to lead the demons in fighting back against humanity. Mammon was that hero who dared to challenge the rules. Osay inwardly admired Mammon, regarding him as the only master worth serving.

Yet all of this had been destroyed by Lucifer III. His dreams had faded with Mammon's death.

Osay had assumed that between Mammon and Lucifer, at least one would end up severely wounded—but absolutely no Demon Lord would die. No matter how they fought, they wouldn't endanger each other's lives. This was the consensus among the rulers. Anyone who violated it would face the harshest punishment from the Council of Elders!

Osay threw a punch into the ground, his eyes reddened not from anger but from fury. He lifted Mammon's body, intending to take his master back to the Third Demon Lord Palace first. "Lucifer III, truly an impulsive and reckless destabilizing factor. Your Majesty was right."

"I'll definitely avenge you, master, and make Lucifer III pay a painful price!"

"Just leave it here. I've been a captain for a few days—at least I won't get lost at sea."

Merlin boarded his small boat, preparing to leave the Mexican Strait and return to Rexford in the Kingdom of Britain. It had been so long since he'd been back—his precious daughter was probably worried sick by now.

Leviathan led the sea demons in seeing Merlin off. Though it didn't say it aloud, it had helped Merlin greatly, and it would remember this kindness and repay it someday.

~What kind of captain are you? You can't even read a sea chart.

"Ha." Merlin held the oar and forced a laugh, waving his hand, "These are all trivial matters. Besides, the turmoil has already settled. I should leave now. Mammon is probably making his way back to the Third Demon Lord Palace, then hiding away for a long time, too scared to come out."

"The matter isn't over yet. Our interference with the Council of Elders' decision will surely cause some dissatisfaction. Perhaps the elders are figuring out how to punish us?" Leviathan worried.

"Those old fogeys aren't worth mentioning. They certainly don't want the demon race to fall into chaos, killing each other. Besides, we're just unlucky fellows on the same boat. If the Council of Elders wants to go after two Demon Lords, they'll have plenty of reservations." Merlin reasoned.

"Later, I'll contact Asmodeus and Baphomet, get them to side with us. It might help this whole thing blow over." Leviathan paused, then added, "But we need to be careful. The upcoming Seven King Conference will likely bring this up. From what I know, Mammon isn't the type to give up easily—he's bound to make a scene at the conference."

"Whatever. I have no fondness for the Seven King Conference. And with my current exile status, I'm not even sure I have the right to attend." Merlin swung his oar, heading toward the Kingdom of Britain. "Farewell!"

Leviathan watched the lonely little boat disappear into the sunset on the horizon, thinking—Lucifer, the real battle is only just beginning. We'll face enormous pressure from the Council of Elders.

In the ruins of the Sixth Demon Lord Palace, Leviathan looked at his destroyed home and sighed helplessly. Did Lucifer and Mammon really fight so fiercely? It was as if they wanted to tear down my palace.

Leviathan felt a bit uncomfortable, but he could still accept it. The Demon Lord Palace was just a symbol. The core was the blood pool seal underground. As long as the seal remained intact, there wouldn't be any major problems.

Mammon's blood on the ground had long since dried. Leviathan traced the terrifying bloodstains, imagining how brutal the fight between Lucifer and Mammon must have been. Suddenly, he sensed something amiss. He picked up the refined steel blade left behind by Nao, and fell into deep confusion—

A common-quality weapon? Mammon wouldn't need this, right? It doesn't seem to be Lucifer's side sword either.

Strange—why is it here? It shouldn't be.

To Be Continued

Epilogue

This volume concludes the demon race arc. The gaps to fill in the next volume are quite large, and all the foreshadowing you've been waiting for will finally begin to unfold.

Also, I noticed the reader who comments every day about eating candy—I see you. Let's push forward when it's time, no need to rush.

Today I planned out the content for this volume and organized all the gaps to fill.

It seems many of you aren't happy about Mammon's death. But I already wrote it—Mammon's true strength is the weakest among Demon Lords. He relies on his divine artifact to act with impunity.

Tyrfing's power was nullified by the draw technique, so it was destined to die.

Moreover, Nao has time-stop—this is a skill that Alice will learn in the future. Some say it's weak, but I think it's not weak at all. In fact, it's even overpowered.

Those of you with monthly tickets, please cast your votes. Thank you, *gargle gargle*~

(Qin w "Tai)

title: Chapter 1 — Eerie
content:
Chapter 1 — Eerie

Volume 32 · Chapter 1

A hundred years ago, Lucifer II Vivian fell in defeat, and after the young Merlin encountered hardship, he escaped the First Demon Lord Palace with his sister Lilith. This land, sacred to the demon race since ancient times, had briefly fallen into the hands of the Holy Church, but the occupation lasted only a week. During those seven days, the Spear Hero O'Brien investigated as many of the demons' internal secrets as possible, giving the Holy Church firsthand intelligence; thanks to this achievement, he became the twelfth legendary hero in history. Later devout believers also called him the last true Hero, for after several hundred years no hero ever received this honor again, nor could anyone match his accomplishments. On the seventh day of the First Demon Lord Palace's fall, the Holy Temple Knights had turned the place upside down, almost looting everything of value and gathering many secrets of the demon race, when suddenly a knight accidentally discovered an underground passage in the Demon Lord Palace, immediately catching O'Brien's attention, and he promptly went to investigate—"I really thought the demons were that poor, but I didn't expect there to be such a huge space beneath the Demon Lord Palace; there must be plenty of treasure, don't you think, Lord O'Brien?" a red‑clad cardinal exclaimed, his face full of excitement, looking at the stern hero beside him. This man was Giovanni, the most influential red‑clad cardinal in the Holy Church at present and also the planner of this campaign against the First Demon Lord Palace. As the old pope grew older and neared his return to heaven, power struggles within the Holy Church intensified. Yet thanks to his enormous influence, Giovanni gradually stepped into the forefront, quietly becoming the strongest contender for the next papacy. Although four or five other red‑clad cardinals were also competing with him, after the successful assault on the First Demon Lord Palace, the papal seat seemed to have no suspense. "What treasure could the demons possibly have hoarded on such barren land? There must be something far more important hidden here," O'Brien replied coldly, apparently not wanting to converse further with the cardinal. The Holy Temple Knights advanced deeper into the underground of the Demon Lord Palace, hearing a faint sound like a rushing river, and the stench of blood grew stronger the lower they went. "No matter what, we have gained a lot this time, and besides, you defeated Lucifer II Vivian—such merit is enough to make you the first person in history, and you will surely be named a legendary hero by His Holiness the Pope; this is the highest honor, and then your status will be only below the Pope, aren't you pleased?" Giovanni asked meaningfully. "I have no interest in such empty fame; only when facing a true strong one can I possibly break through myself, and that is my pursuit," O'Brien paused, then added, "Moreover, I remain skeptical about defeating that female demon Lucifer II Vivian; her strength differs greatly from the rumors, and she hardly possesses the ability to resist foreign invaders while also being able to match wits and courage with other demon lords—I feel I have been used, and she may be hiding some secret." "Lord O'Brien, what are you saying? Are you subtly boasting that you are too strong, so Lucifer II Vivian is not worth mentioning? I must say, your way of self‑praise is really refreshing and unconventional," Giovanni said with a smile beside him. "I don't agree that I am too strong; in this campaign I expected the demon lord to force me to release my power, but she was defeated too easily, which makes me suspect she might be plotting something," O'Brien said sternly. "No matter what Lucifer II Vivian might be scheming, I saw her pierced through by your spear with my own eyes—that is enough; could a corpse still think? We can move freely in the Demon Lord Palace, which already proves she is indeed dead," Giovanni replied dismissively, thinking O'Brien was just playing mysterious. "It seems I and the cardinal are not of the same kind; some ideas cannot be completely alike," O'Brien responded coldly. "As a contributor to this campaign, you shouldn't wander off in your thoughts; when you stand before the Pope, you must definitely exaggerate the results of this battle, and don't forget to mention my name—whether you can gain the Pope's trust, I can rely entirely on you, Lord O'Brien," Giovanni said with deep meaning, hoping O'Brien would not forget to mention his own contribution when reporting to the Pope. "I will fulfill my duty," O'Brien replied coldly, willing only to report honestly, not to embellish the facts. "Shout!" Giovanni flicked his lips, a hint of dissatisfaction flashing in the depths of his eyes, thinking, "A mere warrior, what's the fuss? Without my meticulous plans, how could the campaign have gone so smoothly?" When the party reached the lowest part of the Demon Lord Palace, they were stunned by the sight before them—a magnificent blood pool flowing like lava, a bizarre vortex swirling the blood up into midair, with no clue what lay beneath the pool. The heavy smell of blood hit them, causing the Holy Temple Knights to feel dizzy and begin vomiting nonstop. "These damned demons, what are they stockpiling all this blood for? How many lives must they kill?" Giovanni stared wide‑eyed in shock at the blood pool, repeatedly gesturing with his fingers on his chest, praying not to be entangled by misfortune. O'Brien calmly observed the scene; dense runes covered all the walls, and after a brief consideration he said, "If I am not mistaken, this is some kind of sealing spell; I don't know how much effort the demons expended to construct such a grand sealing formation, but what is hidden below?" "No matter what is down there! This must certainly be an evil ritual; it must be eradicated at once! In a world shrouded by the Goddess of Light, such filth is absolutely not allowed!" Giovanni declared. "This is important; I believe destroying this place requires reporting to His Majesty the Pope, for the demons have built a massive sealing formation here, and there must be a reason for its existence," O'Brien frowned, feeling it better not to act rashly. "I am the commander of this campaign; such matters need not be reported to the Pope—I now order you to destroy this at once!" Giovanni glared at O'Brien, believing his authority was being challenged. Although O'Brien is a Hero with exalted status, his authority does not surpass that of a red‑clad cardinal, especially since Giovanni was personally appointed by the Pope as the commander of this campaign and thus naturally has the right to demand O'Brien's obedience. "O'Brien, what are you hesitating about? Has your faith in the Goddess already deteriorated?" Giovanni demanded, his face full of alarm. O'Brien remained silent, let out a helpless sigh, then suddenly leapt up, his fighting spirit pressure rising step by step, wielding what seemed to be a false divine artifact, the Scarlet Enchantress— He thrust his spear with all his might into the blood‑pool seal, intending to destroy the vast sealing formation from within. A bit of pressure, the information is also quite heavy; to connect the previous several million words into a coherent narrative is slow and difficult, please bear with us.

title: Chapter 2 — Hidden Danger
content:
Chapter 2 — Hidden Danger

Volume 32 · Chapter 2

The spear of Oubairen, infused with power, flew in a straight line into the blood pool. At once, like a dragon stirring the sea, it churned the entire blood pool, turning it upside down and causing it to surge and roil.

Although the blood pool's seal appeared vast and imposing, Oubairen had every confidence in destroying it. Moreover, every sealing formation had a single core. Once that core was destroyed, no matter how powerful the sealing technique, it would collapse instantly from within.

"In a world protected by the Goddess, there's still such an evil ritual? This is outright contempt for our Holy Church. You despicable demons will surely pay the price for your actions!" Jiugen traced symbols in the air above his chest, muttering curses against the demons.

Yet things didn't go as smoothly as planned. With a "pu" sound, the crimson demon princess flew back into Oubairen's hand, and the blood pool's seal remained unbroken.

Jiugen's face twisted with disbelief as he demanded sternly, "What are you doing? Why haven't you destroyed this evil ritual yet? Do you have any doubts?"

"That's strange." Oubairen suddenly furrowed his brow, his expression uncertain.

"What's strange?" Jiugen couldn't understand why Oubairen, usually swift and decisive, was now hesitating.

"Below the blood pool, there's not a single living thing. My spear can't detect the faintest ripple of a soul, proving it's completely empty down there!" Oubairen's brow was tightly knit as he said doubtfully, "The demon race built such a massive seal—surely they wouldn't seal just a corpse, would they?"

"Ah?" Jiugen realized something was off and stared at the blood pool. "It does sound strange. Could it be that this was all just to mislead us outsiders? That would be a terrible waste."

"There's another possibility." Oubairen's face grew grim.

"What?" Jiugen pressed.

"Originally, there was an extremely powerful monster sealed here. But that monster secretly slipped away without breaking the seal. The whole process was silent and undetectable—even the Demon Lords didn't notice. Otherwise, this blood pool wouldn't still exist." Oubairen voiced his speculation, unable to fathom what kind of monster could escape from such a formidable sealing technique.

"No way? The demons sealed such a powerful monster and I've never heard of it." Jiugen fell into thought. There had never been any intelligence suggesting that the Demon Lord Palace had such a powerful seal beneath it.

Suddenly, a temple knight rushed over and reported loudly, "Bad news! Bishop-sama! The temple has sent emergency intelligence! Other Demon Lord Palaces have already dispatched troops to reinforce us. The Demon Lords themselves might even come in person!"

"What?!?!" Jiugen was startled, but after thinking it over, he immediately commanded, "Order the knights to pack their gear. We must withdraw from here immediately!"

"We can't face the assault of multiple Demon Lords with our current preparations."

A century later, the secrets beneath the demons' blood pool remained a mystery.

The Hero of the Spear from that era might have been the only one who noticed the blood pool's oddities.

Even now, the Demon Lords treated the blood pool with extreme caution, fearing that breaking the seal would awaken the demons' ancestors.

Yet whether the demons' ancestors still remained in the blood pool, no demon could confirm.

Mammon's destruction threw the entire Third Demon Lord Palace into chaos. The demons stationed in the royal capital of Britannia were overrun by the kingdom's army overnight, and the city was retaken.

The defeated demons fled by small boats, not knowing how long they would drift at sea before returning to the Third Demon Lord Palace.

The unstoppable Mammon army collapsed like a house of cards in the blink of an eye, forced to abandon their ambitions of conquering human kingdoms.

Unfortunately, few knew that it was Merlin who had defeated Mammon. Many kingdom soldiers still believed it was through the unity of the entire realm that they had triumphed over the Demon Lord.

It was laughable how the Holy Church had reaped rich rewards from this war. Having contributed little, they still managed to gain a large number of devout followers in Britannia, cashing in handsomely from the conflict.

The believers firmly believed this was the Goddess of Light intervening from the heavens to save Britannia and humanity, rather than relying on the kingdom's own strength.

The sudden surge in church followers caught Elizabeth's attention and made her somewhat displeased. The greater the Church's influence, the more it threatened her position.

Yet the kingdom had barely reclaimed its lost territory, and Elizabeth had no time to deal with the Church's opportunistic moves.

In the palace, Katherine held a stack of files and reported on the kingdom's recent situation to Elizabeth.

"Your Majesty, all demons have been driven from the kingdom's soil. The destroyed towns and villages are gradually beginning reconstruction." Katherine reported seriously.

"Good. What about Windsor's situation?" Elizabeth inquired.

"After driving the demons out of the coastal waters, she immediately ordered soldiers to begin rebuilding the coastal fortresses. Based on Mesfilfield's report, she probably won't return to the capital for some time." Katherine recalled the message from Mesfilfield.

"Windsor did the right thing. The demons have only been temporarily driven out. They might return for a second invasion, so we must take this opportunity to prepare our defenses." Elizabeth nodded, approving of Mesfilfield's actions.

"Also, there's news from the French kingdom. They say the joint expeditionary force hasn't achieved any substantial victory, but the demons may have fallen into internal strife." Katherine looked up and explained, "This news seems credible. Mesfilfield's letter mentions that the kingdom's naval blockade has been lifted."

"Internal strife?" Elizabeth pondered for a moment before responding, "If all this is true, it's good news for us. We'll have enough time to prepare and prevent the demons from launching a second invasion."

"Interestingly, there's a letter from the Church." Katherine's expression turned sly. "The Church claims that under their temple knights' heroic assault, they successfully broke the demons' naval blockade. They also proposed that all beings are children of the Goddess, and hoped that Your Majesty would formally join the Church as a distinguished believer, becoming an excellent representative of the Goddess in the mortal world under Her radiant light."

"The Church is always good at distorting facts, and their words can't be trusted. They claim to be humanity's protectors, yet they held back even during the demon invasion." Elizabeth sighed, feeling as though she had gained yet another enemy.

"Recently, the number of church followers in the kingdom has surged. This doesn't seem like a good sign. At the urging of some priests, many believers have expressed hopes that Your Majesty might also join the Church, with undertones of kidnapping." Katherine paused, worried, "The Church has been preaching that only the ruler appointed by the Goddess is legitimate. Those pagan rulers are merely abandoned by the Goddess. Many small nations with large populations of believers would face internal unrest if they didn't accept this doctrine. Without the Pope personally crowning the ruler, they might be torn apart by angry mobs."

"This is a great trouble." Elizabeth rubbed her temples, massaging her pressure point, and said with a headache, "Divine right of kings?"

"My power was not granted by the Goddess. It was bought by my ancestors with blood."

title: Chapter 3 — Will Add More
content:
Chapter 3 — Will Add More

Volume 32 · Chapter 3

"Your Majesty is right. The church fellows have ulterior motives, wanting to steal the fruits through underhanded means. With the increase of the Goddess of Light's followers within the kingdom, it's something we can't afford to ignore," said Kaivielin Zan. He believed that they needed to curb the development of religious forces within the kingdom as much as possible. "The power of religion is no small matter. Its existence is more dangerous than unstable factors like the great swordsman Elgin. If the number of believers within the kingdom reaches a certain point, the kingdom will be in name only. Just a word from the Pope in the Vatican Cathedral, and they'll rebel, overthrowing your rule."

"This..."

Elizabeth fell into deep thought. Elgin the great swordsman was like a cactus; although somewhat dangerous, he wouldn't harm anyone unless provoked. However, allowing the church to grow within the kingdom was akin to a slow poison. If not stopped in time, it would be fatal—far more dangerous than Elgin the great swordsman!

Elizabeth felt she couldn't let the church succeed with its 'boiling frog' strategy. She had to take some measures to stop it.

"Order it down. Temporarily cut off all support to the church. The number of churches within the kingdom must not continue to increase. Except for specific occasions, gatherings of the Goddess of Light's followers will be considered illegal assemblies and will be immediately dispersed."

"Your Majesty, your method treats the symptoms but not the root cause. I believe we should expel some of the priests who spread rumors from Britannia and arrest the Cardinal residing in the kingdom. Let the Pope in the Vatican see our firm stance. I'm sure the church will then become more restrained," Kaixin offered a tougher strategy.

"That's too harsh. It will only make the believers rebellious, causing the kingdom to fall into turmoil again. Moreover, being too tough on the church won't do us any good," Elizabeth paused, continuing, "The church's influence is immense. Followers are everywhere, across various industries and social classes—from kings holding real power to starving commoners. If our hardline stance angers the church, we'll be seen as enemies of the goddess and become targets for all believers worldwide. That would be difficult to manage."

"What should we do then? We can't just let the church expand within the kingdom, can we?" Kaixin frowned, finding the matter difficult. The power of religion was vast and far-reaching, like a poison corroding people's hearts. People preferred to believe in an intangible god rather than a tangible leader.

"My refusal alone will suffice. The Pope is a smart man. There's no benefit for him to openly confront me. I believe he'll become more restrained afterward." Elizabeth lowered her head, thinking for a moment before saying, "To completely eliminate the danger brought by religious forces, people need to believe in me, not so-called deities. Perhaps I haven't done enough yet."

"No, you've done very well," Kaixin sighed, indignantly saying, "The hateful church always wants everyone to believe in their so-called deity to achieve the ambition of unifying the human world. The once mighty Carolingian Dynasty is the best example. The foolish young emperor, to gain the church's support, even gave Rome's land to the Pope, leading to the church becoming the actual controller of Rome while the royal family exists in name only."

"I remember all these things, and I will never forget. The church is as evil as the demon race, but it's much more cunning," Elizabeth knew she faced enemies not only from the invading demons but also from the church's influence.

"I'm relieved you remain clear-headed. There's one more thing," Kaixin took out a letter, speaking seriously, "Besides exaggerating their battle results, the Vatican has also sent over a secret letter."

"Hmm? Let me see it."

Elizabeth opened the envelope of the secret letter and carefully read its contents, her eyes and expression changing continuously.

She furrowed her brow, burned the secret letter with a candle until it turned to ashes, and said with a worried look—

"The old Pope in the Vatican Cathedral is coming soon."

In Rexham, Merlin finally returned here with his luggage.

Just entering the town, he heard someone calling him—a disheveled captain of the guards came running excitedly.

"Brother Merlin! It's been so long since I last saw you! Where have you been fooling around these days?"

Price, the captain of the guards in Rexham Town, waved at Merlin with a smile, like seeing an old friend after a long time, feeling very close.

Merlin chuckled dryly, explaining, "What do you mean 'fooling around'? I went to work. I've been outside the kingdom recently and just got back."

"Oh~, my old friend, you're really lucky. Not long ago, the kingdom experienced a demon invasion, and many people died. The demon army fought from England all the way to Wales, scaring me half to death!" Price still felt lingering fear when recalling it.

"I've already heard about it outside. Unfortunately, I couldn't return in time," Merlin smiled faintly.

"What are you talking about? If you had come back then, it would have been suicide. I envied you guys who were outside so much at that time," Price emphasized seriously, then changed the subject, "Actually, when the demons attacked Wales, I ate a bag of laxatives and pretended to be sick, barely getting through. Otherwise, Earl Austin would have surely sent me to the front line, and I wouldn't have survived."

"To have a guard captain like you protecting the town, it's truly fortunate," Merlin commented with a meaningful tone.

"Truly, Brother Merlin, you understand me best. Hehe." Price gave Merlin a thumbs-up, saying in agreement, "Recently, Miss Alice has been incredibly impressive. Everyone's talking about how she teamed up with the first knight to repel the demon army. Who would have thought that Miss Alice, who used to drag her luggage around looking for a place to rent, would achieve such success today? You should step up too, or you'll feel pressured."

Merlin wore a half-smile, half-laugh expression, thinking to himself, who knows what he had done? If Alice's achievement was cutting the grass, then defeating Mammon was uprooting the roots.

"Since you're back, call Hobbs over for a drink when you have time. But we can't go to Helena's secret little house anymore," Price said regretfully.

"Hmm? What happened?" Merlin asked curiously.

"I don't know if it's because of the war, but Helena's secret little house has closed down and hasn't reopened. I wonder if the sweet Miss Helena will ever come back?" Price reminisced about being scolded and whipped by Helena in the past.

Merlin lowered his head and pondered deeply, speculating on various possibilities—

Helena suddenly leaving Rexham must be due to something happening on Asmodeus's side?

Considering the recent impact of Mammon, could it be that Asmodeus is preparing for war?

Unfortunately, everything has already ended. Now, I am the only demon secretly lurking in Rexham.

title: Chapter 4 — Sour (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 4 — Sour (Bonus)

Volume 32 · Chapter 4

Merlin walked down the streets of Rexham with his luggage; although the town had become somewhat chaotic after the war's panic, overall it hadn't been destroyed and still looked familiar.

“This little rundown place hasn't suffered any demon attacks; it seems Chris should still be safe, with no danger.” Merlin sighed, having unknowingly lived in this small town for a long time, secretly feeling a familiarity akin to the Demon Lord's Palace.

Arriving at his doorstep, Merlin reached out to knock, but his arm froze mid-air, hesitating to knock, his expression complex—after being away for several months, he suddenly forgot how to face Alice and his precious daughter.

After thinking it over, Merlin decided to swallow his pride and knocked three times on the door—

“Come on!” came Alice's voice from inside. After a moment, Alice, wearing home clothes, walked to the door, poked her head out, and saw Merlin standing outside. She froze, her eyes flashing with complex emotion, shifting from anger to tenderness, her brows furrowed as she refused to say a word.

Alice, why are you putting on a sour face the moment we meet? I barely made it back.” Merlin unconsciously let a big bead of sweat slide down his forehead, his eyes darting, his heart pounding.

“Do you even remember to come back?” Alice said, her face stern, coldly.

“This mission turned out far more troublesome than I imagined; I ran into other situations along the way, so I'm later than planned.” Merlin kept explaining why he had been gone for months, hoping for Alice's understanding.

But before Merlin could finish his sentence, something bumped into his chest, and a familiar, fresh scent drifted into his nose, instantly calming the restlessness that had plagued him all along the way.

“Eh?!” Merlin's face showed surprise as he looked down at Alice lunging into his arms; her silky silver hair shone with a beautiful luster, instantly leaving him dazed, his mind going blank for a moment.

In fact, Merlin had imagined many possible scenarios on his way home—being scolded, blamed, accused—but he never expected her to suddenly throw herself into his arms.

Given Merlin's understanding of Alice's personality, she should never give him a pleasant face; she ought to take the moral high ground and criticize him—that would be normal.

But now—Merlin stiffened like a rusted robot, not knowing what to say; he could only stand rigidly, even wondering in his mind, 'When things go awry, there must be something fishy!' What scheme is Alice plotting? Surely she isn't hatching some devious conspiracy!

Alice was quite agitated, unable to control her strength, she dug her nails into Merlin's back, making him furrow his brows.

Merlin became increasingly convinced that Alice was taking the opportunity to retaliate, no longer needing verbal reprimands but instead directly using her hands to torment him.

Alice pressed her forehead against Merlin's chest, preventing him from seeing her expression; he suspected she might be revealing a smug, evil smile after succeeding.

Yet Alice, with her cheeks flushed red, lowered her head and said nothing, her feelings becoming extremely complex—she blamed Merlin for taking so long to return, exceeding their agreed time, but upon seeing him in person, her resentment largely faded, her wistful mood turning into joy.

However, Alice had her own pride; she would never admit that seeing Merlin made her extremely happy, and would instead force herself to put on a stern façade.

“What are you doing?” Merlin's eyes twitched wildly, the pain from being pinched in the back shooting through him.

“I didn't do anything!” Alice said, her face flushed and stammering, still thinking, 'What should I do? I accidentally lost control and hugged him—will Merlin notice my feelings? Might he hug me back and maybe even kiss…?! What am I thinking?! As a girl I should be reserved; how embarrassing—I'm not that kind of loose person!’

“Let go already—how long are you going to keep at it? Do you have to rip the flesh off my back to be satisfied?” Merlin showed a pained expression, bewildered that merely being a month late warranted such treatment.

“Ah?!” Alice blinked, realizing how hard she had grabbed, quickly pushed Merlin away, stepped back with her face red, not knowing how to explain.

“Hiss~” Merlin rubbed the meat on his lower back, sighed, and asked, “What's your problem? Do you have a grudge against me?”

“No, it's not like that!” Alice explained frantically, wondering why things had turned out this way—this wasn't her intention at all!

“Tsk! No wonder you're petty—you hold a grudge over the tiniest thing.” Merlin sneered, his face full of disdain.

“Ah? I’m petty? According to our agreement, you should have been back last month, yet you're a whole month late! No— that… I” Merlin broke out in a sweat, realizing he was right—this was the real Alice; everything before had been fake.

“What do you mean, 'what you'? If you made a mistake, you should stand there and take your punishment—are you even a man?” Alice shouted, hands on her hips, glaring at Merlin.

Mmmmmm Merlin felt the immense pressure; an unreasonable woman is the most deadly!

“Look! Have you run out of excuses? I knew you'd find a reason for being late—do you have any idea how exhausting it is for me to take care of Chris alone?” Alice poured out her grievances, finally finding a target for her resentment.

“Pfft! Chris is so obedient—how could it be that tiring?” Merlin spread his hands.

“What did you say? ? ?” Alice frowned, silently cursing Merlin as an irresponsible oaf.

Just as the two had barely seen each other and were about to launch into a century-long shouting match, a little kid waddled out of the house on his short, turnip-like legs, 'thump-thump-thump'—

“Dada! Daddy's back!” Chris chirped, calling out 'daddy' from afar, so excited that the little one ran outside barefoot. Little Chris tried to jump into Merlin's arms, but her short legs wouldn't cooperate; she could only attempt a tiny three-centimeter hop in place, then clung to Merlin's thigh, rubbing against it nonstop, feeling her father's familiar scent, and she was overjoyed.

Upon seeing his precious daughter, Merlin instantly transformed into a doting father; the spirit of an old dad possessed him, and he spread his arms with a smile, saying, “Come, Chris! Let Daddy give you kisses, hugs, and lift you high—it's been so long, you must have missed me, right? Actually, Daddy also feels guilty—

Alice stared at Merlin, her heart feeling like a tipped-over vinegar jar, sour and sour— “Why! Why is there such a big difference in how you treat me and Chris?! I also want to be kissed, hugged, and lifted high—why am I not allowed to?”
