title: Chapter 5 — Temple of Maria
content:
Chapter 5 — Temple of Maria

Volume 32 · Chapter 5

"Clears throat!"

Alice couldn't bear to watch anymore, so she coughed lightly, thinking that the moment Chris saw Merlin, she had forgotten everything Alice had told her.

The mother and daughter had privately agreed that when Merlin returned, they wouldn't give him a good face; otherwise, if he got a taste of the sweetness, maybe he'd start hanging out outside more often?

Hearing her mother's cough, the delighted little Chris trembled all over, immediately recalling what Alice had instructed her to do, and gradually calmed down.

Only to see the little thing place her hands on Merlin's thigh, standing seriously beside Alice with a puffed-up expression staring at Merlin, as if she had two small buns stuffed in her mouth.

Merlin was very surprised in his heart; he had even bent down, but his precious daughter had slipped away?——
Alice must have taught Chris something! This vicious woman wants to destroy our father-daughter relationship!?

Merlin was a bit reluctant to give up, clapped his hands, revealed a kind old father expression, and asked Chris affectionately,
"What's wrong? Come to Dad over here."

Little Chris thought for a moment, imitating Alice's posture beside her, hands on hips, pouting her lips, "Hmph~!"

"? ? ?" Merlin had question marks in his head, seeing that his precious daughter was angry at him. She followed Alice around every day and had learned her angry expression perfectly! Just like young Alice!

"Pfu~" Alice saw her daughter's cute appearance and couldn't help laughing, feeling that Merlin should reflect on himself.

"Hey! What did you tell Chris? Did you say a lot of bad things behind my back?" The vein on Merlin's forehead jumped.

"Hmph!" Alice turned her face away, completely ignoring Merlin's dissatisfaction.

"Mama didn't say Dad's bad words, it's all Dad's fault for coming back so late. I ask Mama every day when Dad will be back, and she always says 'soon'." Chris's hair antenna swung around, saying angrily, "Chris feels deceived, mmm!"

"Merlin felt ashamed and embarrassedly explained, 'I know, it's Dad's fault. Can't I apologize? Don't learn your mother's petty habit.'"

Chris: "Hmph~!"
Alice: "Hmph~!"

The mother and daughter seemed to have coordinated everything, deliberately wanting to put some pressure on the newly returned Merlin. However, he couldn't accept this "double happiness"—clearly one Alice was enough, but his precious daughter had started learning her mother's temper.

"Spit!" Merlin clutched his forehead with a headache, sighing helplessly—
Damn it, the baby already allied with her mother to gang up on me.
This brat Chris, I only left for a few months and she defected.

Located in the Vatican of the Holy Roman Empire, the Maria Cathedral is the holy land in the hearts of all Light Faith believers, a pure and clean place without a speck of dirt.

Originally, Rome was a powerful nation in the human world, actively expanding outward with territory spanning the Mediterranean Sea. But with internal strife and church corruption, this nation was constantly divided and had long lost its former glory.

Since the foolish young Roman emperor donated land to the Pope, the Roman royal family had become a mere existence in name only, forced to be a puppet manipulated by the Light Faith and barely surviving.

Although the Roman emperor received the Pope's recognition and was proclaimed the goddess's manager in the mortal world, he had no rights—everything in Rome required the Pope's decision.

In this nation of numerous believers, no one trusted the ruler. The Pope, as the goddess's representative on earth, was the true leader, and every word might convey the goddess's meaning.

Did the Pope truly convey the goddess's meaning? Or was he issuing orders in the goddess's name? Probably only he himself knew.

The magnificent Maria Cathedral was shrouded in sacred radiance. There was no night here, always bright as day. The neat stairs were not stained with a speck of dust, and vivid saintly images were everywhere.

There was also a huge, somewhat damaged statue of the Goddess of Light standing behind the cathedral. Although her face was blurred, there was a faint divine pressure that made people dare not look directly at her.

At the feet of the goddess statue were seven saintly stone statues, representing the seven virtues preached by the church. They were seven great saints who had made remarkable contributions in the Holy War, some even sacrificing their lives for the arrival of the human era.

The cathedral's radiance had dimmed considerably compared to before. The Holy Dragon Avis once soared above, but unfortunately it was now imprisoned in the First Demon Lord Palace.

Inside the Maria Cathedral, touching hymns echoed, and light filtered through the surrounding colored glass, enveloping the entire interior in brilliant colors. Looking at the colored shadows reflected on the ground, it seemed to record the story of the goddess banishing demons—

An old man wearing gorgeous priestly robes stood quietly, wearing a tall hat embedded with rubies, holding a pastoral staff, listening intently to the visitor's confession.
This person was the current Pope of the Light Faith, Goegegen, who had the achievement of once attacking and capturing the First Demon Lord Palace together with the Spear Hero O'Brien for seven days.

As the only Pope in history to have entered the interior of the Demon Lord Palace, Goegegen had profound influence within the church and held a lofty status similar to "father" in the hearts of believers.

Unfortunately, the aged Goegegen was now too old, long losing his former heroic posture. By ordinary human lifespan standards, the fact that he was still alive was already the greatest miracle.

Joan of Arc, returned from the combined fleet, upon seeing the Pope, first reported the specific circumstances of facing Leviathan and confessed the mistakes she had made—

Joan knelt on the ground, hands clasped tightly against her chest, piously confessing, "Princess Marguerite deduced that the demon race had fallen into internal strife. We originally planned to attempt capturing the Sixth Demon Lord Palace, but that evil Demon Lord who caused countless people to perish in the sea suddenly appeared, disrupting our plans and causing the soldiers to lose morale. As an Inquisitor of Heresy, I have seen countless evil things, but never anything like Leviathan. It was simply like the source of evil reeking of stench. Though it wasn't my first time facing a Demon Lord, I admit I felt unprecedented fear. I am deeply ashamed and unworthy to be a warrior of the goddess."

"Oh, my child, you needn't blame yourself. Fear stems from human instinct; it's not a shameful thing. Moreover, the sea is Leviathan's home field. The pressure from its huge body is incomparable to other Demon Lords." Goegegen lifted Joan from the ground, patted her shoulder, and said lovingly, "You had the courage to face that terrible Demon Lord. That's already excellent. Not only the strong are worthy to be Maria's warriors; any devout believer can. And you are clearly a qualified defender of the goddess. The goddess will surely protect you—"

"Thank you for your guidance, but I want too much to prove my ability. My friend Alice is being corrupted by heretics. I must do something to make her realize her mistakes." Joan said with worry on her face, revealing her heart to the Pope.

"Don't worry, Joan. Piety can infect everyone. Your wish will eventually come true. Alice, as a former Hero, has a pure and kind heart. Like you, she's a good child. Though she isn't devout enough to the goddess yet, there's still a chance to correct her mistakes." Goegegen lowered his head and said solemnly—

"In a few days, you can visit the Kingdom of Britain with me."
"On my behalf, greet Alice and give her this thing."
"The Goddess's embrace is her final resting place."

Sorry, I need to organize too much information.
Yesterday I organized the outline and found that it's not just the demon race story in this volume; there are other plot holes in this section too. The Seven Kings Meeting isn't the main body of this volume yet.
Then I couldn't start writing for a long time—first because it's hard to write, second because the arrangement wasn't good so I couldn't write. If bugs appear, it's hard to fix.
This is the second time I've said it's hard to write. It's really hard. Compared to before, it's completely different. For example, before it was deriving answers from problems, but now it's reverse-engineering problems from answers. It feels different.
So after reading this volume, you'll know. The Seven Kings Meeting is there too, but filling Alice's plot hole is more interesting than the Seven Kings Meeting.
I'll update again later.

title: Chapter 5 — Great Enemy (Bonus)
content:
Chapter 5 — Great Enemy (Bonus)

Volume 32 · Chapter 5

On the steps of Maria's Temple, a middle-aged man with a horrifying scar on his face, clad in mighty armor, was heading to the temple to see the Pope.
His name is Blackford, Grand Knight Commander of the Holy Knight Order, holding the same rank as Barres.
Unlike Barres, who is full of petty schemes, Blackford is strict with himself and exacting in all matters.
Although he is the venerable Grand Knight Commander of the Holy Knight Order, he lives like an ascetic; his abilities in every aspect surpass Barres, and his prestige within the Holy Knight Order is extremely high.
If Barres is a playboy posing as a knight commander, then Blackford is the genuine sword of the Church, the man worshipped in the hearts of the Holy Knights.
Blackford possesses a will of steel; he is among the few who survived the war against the corrupt king.
He once participated in the war against the Second Demon Lord Palace; when facing the headless demon lord Samael, his sword pierced his left eye and went through his skull, yet he relied on his steel will to escape from the Second Demon Lord Palace.
After returning alive, Blackford refused any treatment to restore his left eye's vision; he regards this scar as his medal of honor, wants the damage inflicted by the demon lord to remain forever on his body, looks in the mirror every day to remind himself that the demon race's danger has not vanished, and swears to leave an indelible scar on Samael's body someday.
Because of this, in the eyes of the Holy Knights, Blackford is practically the embodiment of steel, a model and exemplar for the entire Holy Knight Order.
What is Barres? He merely relied on his outstanding cultivation talent to become knight commander, arrogant, doing as he pleases, looking down on others, constantly harassing pious nuns, and has never even seen a true demon lord.
The evaluations of the two knight commanders within the order are polarized to an extreme; clearly, Blackford is the true knight commander recognized in the hearts of the knights.
After entering the temple, Blackford saw the Pope standing with his hands behind his back, his complexion not looking good; he knelt on one knee with a grim expression.
"Your Majesty, I have come."
"I just received news that Barres seems to have died in the Britain defense?" Pope Ji'ougen slowly turned around.
"Yes, Barres is already dead; he was too young, lacked a deep understanding of the demon lord's strength, rashly challenged the greedy demon lord Mammon, and unfortunately met a miserable end at the demon's..." Blackford answered euphemistically, looking down on Barres, who stood on equal footing with him, for his talent made him overconfident, and such an outcome was expected.
"I really shouldn't have let Barres leave the Vatican; he possesses outstanding talent; if he could calm down and cultivate, his future achievements might not fall below Owen Brian's, and he could succeed you in leading the Holy Knight Order." Pope Ji'ougen sighed, a piece removed from his hand.
Blackford felt uneasy; he had not yet grown old enough to set aside his sword, yet the Pope had already begun scouting his replacement, wondering wherein he fell short compared to the young knight; besides talent, what merits does Barres have? A man like him leading the Holy Knight Order would surely turn the Goddess's warriors into bandits.
"Your Majesty, even if Barres is gone, I will still wholeheartedly aid the Church's safety; his death does not affect the..."
"Blackford, you actually hate Barres a lot? Despite your youth you became Grand Knight Commander and still possess considerable strength; no matter how you look at it, he will surpass you." Pope Ji'ougen asked with deep meaning.
"We are all knights who have offered our souls to the Goddess; all our lives we must fight heretics; we are comrades in the same trench; I am not jealous." Blackford said reluctantly.
"Don't use such hypocritical words to conceal yourself; I have lived so long that just from your eyes I can see your thoughts." Pope Ji'ougen lowered his gaze at Blackford and said calmly.
"Although Barres's death will not affect the overall situation, our Church has lost a valiant warrior; this is an irreplaceable loss."
"Everything is because Barres was young and hot‑headed, too impulsive; even if he had a hint of reverence for the strong, he would not have ended up like this." Blackford lamented.
"You are right; although demons are our enemies, after a long struggle we must recognize their strength; a reverence for the strong is extremely important; if I had known this earlier, the Church would not have come to this point." Pope Ji'ougen paused, his aged face gaining a touch of worry.
"Now Lucifer III, when I and Owen Brian attacked the First Demon Lord Palace back then, he was merely a humble, weak young demon; if I had been firmer, he would have died in my hands long ago; how could I have given him the chance to grow into today’s great enemy capable of shaking the foundations of the Church?"
Blackford frowned, feeling that whenever the Pope mentioned Lucifer III he gritted his teeth; it seemed Lucifer III, as the youngest monarch of the demon race, inflicts greater harm on the Church than the previous demon lords.
"All the blame lies with Owen Brian for being too soft, refusing to kill young life, even if it is a demon; if he had listened to me, the Church would have already completed the plan to unify the human world." Pope Ji'ougen's kindly visage vanished, replaced by hideous madness.
"When Lucifer III took the stage, I admit I underestimated this little fellow who almost died by my hand; in the war against Lucifer III we poured vast material and financial resources, yet everything ended in failure! For decades we have never won a single battle! Even because of frequent defeats, our Church's influence once shrank to the vicinity of Rome alone!"
"Your Majesty, please stay calm." Blackford saw the Pope's emotions rising, quickly stood and helped him sit to rest.
"Lucifer III is our greatest enemy; he is the stumbling block in our unification of human nations; I missed the best opportunity to kill him." Pope Ji'ougen trembled, breathed heavily, his old hands shaking incessantly.
"Your Majesty, do not dwell on these matters; I have not completely failed; there is still opportunity, as long as the Church's influence spreads to all human nations, then even if Lucifer III is strong, he cannot withstand the joint crusade of the human alliance." Blackford comforted the old man before him.
"You are right, human alliance..." Pope Ji'ougen drew a deep breath, calming himself.
"Let the world be shrouded in the Goddess's light, form an alliance, share faith in the one true God; that is the key to eradicate demons."
"This time the demons actively invaded Britain; we must make good use of..."

title: Chapter 6 — Celestial Aid
content:
Chapter 6 — Celestial Aid

Volume 32 · Chapter 6

"Your Majesty is right. This time the demon race attacked the Britannian Kingdom, and our followers are growing day by day, especially in Britannia, where the Church's influence has almost reached the level of the royal family." Blackford wore a slight smile on his face. Far from thinking it was bad that the demons invaded, he actually believed it was a good thing beneficial to the Church. "Under the atmosphere of panic, religious faith became the spiritual pillar for the weak. However, it seems the royal family of Britannia doesn't welcome us?"

"Oh? Something happened recently?" Gienger's mustache twitched.

"Queen Elizabeth tried to suppress the Church's development in Britannia. A few days ago, she cut off funding to the Church and forbade the construction of new churches. Followers are not allowed to gather privately, and so on." Blackford paused and spoke in a low voice, "It seems this queen is determined to go against us. Your Majesty, shouldn't we take some measures?"

"Not yet. Don't act rashly. If Elizabeth is truly determined to oppose us, she wouldn't do it in such a half-hearted manner. She's showing me her strength, not letting me extend my hand onto Britannian soil." Gienger easily understood Elizabeth's meaning and continued, "We haven't been stable in Britannia, and it's not suitable to fight with the royal family."

"Then what should we do? Britannia, as one of the stronger nations in the human world, is bound to be our target." Blackford sighed with worry.

"I'll go visit Britannia and speak with Elizabeth personally. It's a pity the demons seem to have made a truce. If we continue fighting, or expand the influence of the war, the plan for the human alliance will be easier to implement." Gienger felt the current situation was somewhat delicate.

"But according to the intelligence, the demons have all withdrawn from Britannia, and the frantic preparations at other Demon Lord Palaces have also stopped. It seems there won't be any large-scale external expansion?" Blackford said in a low voice.

"I don't think this is simple. The invasion of Britannia may just be the beginning, and a fiercer storm is about to come." Gienger had been dealing with demons his whole life and had a deep understanding of their nature.

"A storm?" Blackford looked doubtful and asked in surprise, "Isn't the failure in Britannia enough to make the demons calm down?"

"Blackford, there's a saying among the demons: an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. They won't retreat just because of failure. They'll only think about how to retaliate. In the distant demon era, we relied on the help of the heavens to defeat the powerful demons. They won't be content to live in barren land forever. Even after tens of thousands of years, the desire for revenge will not fade." Gienger said seriously. This wasn't a conclusion he had drawn himself, but the experience left behind by every pope.

Blackford's face changed color. If it was really as the Pope said, then the war hadn't ended yet, and what Britannia had experienced was just the beginning.

"We must be fully prepared. If the demons launch a strong counterattack later, we'll take the opportunity to spread the Church's influence to every corner of the world, unifying the world under the Church's banner in the name of the Goddess." Gienger paused and added, "This is not only the original goal of the Church's founding, but also the wish of the Goddess Maria. After all, besides the demons, there are also Satan's lackeys secretly struggling with us."

"But with the Church's current strength... it might be difficult..." Blackford started to speak but then stopped. The Church's development has been in decline, only slightly improved recently due to the demons' external expansion.

"More than ten years ago, I received a revelation from the Goddess in a dream, saying that a powerful saint has come to the mortal world. Unfortunately, there are no clues." Gienger thought deeply.

"A powerful saint? Could it be one of the seven virtues of the Holy War?" Blackford asked in shock.

"This can't be confirmed yet. But if we can find it, it will surely become a powerful force to eliminate the demons."

At home, after returning, Merlin took a comfortable hot bath, relieving all his fatigue.

Just as he walked out of the bathroom, little Chris ran over with a pile of clothes, speaking in a coaxing voice, "Daddy, while you were away, I washed all your dirty clothes~"

"Huh? Really?" Merlin squatted down, looking at the crumpled clothes that were obviously not clean, "How did you wash them?"

"How? With water!" Chris said proudly.

*Sound*

Merlin awkwardly laughed, thinking, 'I didn't even know to use water to wash clothes?'

Chris was still so young, of course she wouldn't do any housework. These dirty clothes were probably just stepped on with feet carelessly?

He didn't pay attention to such things. Whether clean or not, it was the child's intention, and he had to encourage her.

So Merlin extended his warm hand, patted Chris's little head, and pressed his forehead against the child's.

"Chris has grown up so much. She's already learned to help with housework. The clothes are very clean! Awesome! When I was your age, I couldn't do as much as you. Good children should be rewarded. Tomorrow, Daddy will take you out to buy some delicious food. How about that?"

"Heehee~" Chris laughed like a blooming flower under Merlin's care, her little face flushed red.

Merlin picked up the child and found Chris had grown a bit heavier than before. It seemed she hadn't been mistreated at home. "In the future, don't force yourself to do things. If you feel tired, just let Mommy help you."

"Not tired at all. Daddy's socks smell a bit bad. Mommy threw up." Little Chris said with a naive face.

Merlin felt like his heart had been stabbed with a knife. He thought, 'This is bad! My dignity as a father is being challenged!'

Usually, they did their own laundry, but Merlin generally waited a long time before doing it, only acting when Alice urged him. He never expected the "treasure" he had hidden for so long to be discovered by Chris.

Merlin quickly coughed to mask his embarrassment and began to use various lies to coax the underage girl.

"Cough, cough! This is a test left by Daddy for you. If you can overcome the stench and wash Daddy's socks clean, it proves you have an indomitable will. Congratulations on passing the test. You're really worthy of being my daughter. Daddy is very proud of you!"

"Huh??" Chris was full of question marks, feeling like something was wrong, but still put on a happy face, with stars in her eyes, "Oh~★"

"Heh." Merlin laughed with satisfaction, thinking, 'Indeed, children are the easiest to deceive.'

Chris happily puckered up her small mouth and gave Merlin's face a "paqi" kiss.

Alice happened to walk out of the kitchen with a plate in her hand, seeing the two of them being affectionate, she raised an eyebrow—

They've only been apart for a short while and already started being affectionate?

Seriously, Chris has already forgotten what I said.

All my efforts to take care of her can't compare to Merlin's casual praise?

Ugh, so annoying.

title: Chapter 7 — Abnormal (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 7 — Abnormal (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 32 · Chapter 7

"Daddy, are you happy while you're away?" Merlin flicked Chris's little nose.

"Not happy!" Chris pouted, sticking out her cheeks, but then suddenly changed the subject. "But Auntie Landlady has been so kind to me, feeding me delicious food every day, and there's also Flower."

"Huh?"

Merlin wondered if Chris had stayed with the landlady for a while. It seemed Alice hadn't brought her along when supporting the British front lines—probably worried about danger. Who was Flower?

"She's the landlady's pet puppy, super cute, always licking my face, hehe~" Chris showed off her baby teeth, and the cowlick on her head bounced along.

Dog Merlin was embarrassed, thinking Chris actually liked small animals quite a bit. But they didn't keep dogs at home. Still, since she liked them so much, maybe they should get one?

"While Daddy and Mama are away, Chris has been working hard every day, practicing magic. It was me who healed Flower's broken leg." Chris lifted her face, beaming with pride as if she'd accomplished something grand.

"Have you already learned healing magic?"

Merlin was taken aback. In his understanding, no child as young as Chris could even grasp magic. Even someone like young Johnson was considered a rare genius at that age.

Chris had been practicing diligently every day by the landlady's side to help her parents. It showed that even at such a young age, she displayed a persistence similar to Alice's. He couldn't tell if that was a good thing or not.

Merlin lifted Chris into his arms, praising her generously without reserve.

"Amazing, this is wonderful news. Maybe my little princess is a magic genius, and she'll achieve great things in the future."

"Hehe~" Chris was overjoyed, wiggling her short arms and legs. "Daddy, let me show you—maybe I can heal the scar on your body too!"

"Oh?"

Merlin felt something stir in his heart. He recalled how the Elf King had once praised Chris for possessing an awe-inspiring life force. That mysterious power seemed to be what countless monsters pursued.

Even Merlin himself needed it desperately. If he couldn't rely on the demon sword Banri Garan to steal enemies' life force, he probably wouldn't have survived until today.

Merlin held Chris close and decided to give it a try, curious to see just how far the little one had mastered her magic.

"Alright, let's give it a shot. But Daddy's scars aren't easy to heal, so don't get your hopes up too high."

"Dad doesn't believe in me! I'll definitely succeed!" Chris pouted and waved her tiny fists.

Merlin found his daughter's seriousness amusing. It wasn't such an important matter, yet she took it so earnestly.

Little Chris looked determined, closed her eyes to concentrate, and placed her small hands on Merlin's scarred chest. Suddenly, a surge of immense life energy poured into him, rushing into his chest.

"!!?"

Merlin's face changed instantly as he felt something akin to the sensation of killing enemies with the Banri Garan.

Though Chris was still too weak and the feeling was faint, her power was indeed alleviating the damage caused by the curse.

No wonder the stone statues, vampires, and demons in the ruins were drawn to life force. This was the very source of survival!

If Chris were to wield this power openly, it would likely cause all sorts of trouble.

But Merlin's curse couldn't be fully cured. The life energy could only provide limited relief.

Moreover, Merlin didn't intend to offload his burdens onto the young Chris. He didn't want to keep his daughter bound to him just so he could survive. He hoped Chris could live a free life.

After the spell was cast, little Chris felt dizzy. Even a simple healing spell made her exhausted. She opened her eyes and looked up, only to find the scar on Merlin's chest still there—her efforts had been in vain.

Chris was instantly disappointed, tears welling up in her eyes. She felt so helpless—able to heal Flower's leg but not her father's scar.

"Don't cry! Why are you crying?" Merlin saw his daughter suddenly burst into tears and quickly hugged her, bouncing her around.

"I'm so useless! I could heal Flower's leg, but I can't heal Daddy's scar." Tears streamed down Chris's face. She had thought she could help her parents with their troubles, but in the end, she could only heal small animals.

"Who says you're useless?" Merlin thought quickly, putting on a confident facade. "After your treatment, Daddy feels full of energy and great!"

"Really? But Daddy's scar is still there." Chris looked up at him with a pout.

"Of course it's true. As long as you keep working hard at learning magic, Daddy's scar will eventually be healed by you. Just believe in Daddy!" Merlin gave a thumbs-up and encouraged his daughter with conviction.

"Yay~" Chris's spirits lifted, and the disheveled cowlick on her head seemed to spring back to life with energy.

"What are you two idiots laughing at each other for? It's time for dinner." Alice saw Merlin holding Chris, both of them smiling foolishly at each other like a pair of fools.

Chris had grown just as carefree as Merlin.

At the dinner table, the atmosphere turned a bit awkward. Since Alice was still holding a grudge, she kept a stern expression.

Chris also behaved much more quietly at the table, intimidated by her strict mother's presence, not daring to break the silence carelessly.

Merlin picked up his bowl and glanced sideways, noticing Alice glaring at him with resentment, her face clearly hoping he would reflect on his late return.

"Hmph!" Alice muttered coldly and turned her gaze elsewhere.

Merlin furrowed his brow, thinking, "She's really holding a grudge. It's only been a month late, so I'll just brush it off with a few words." He put down his bowl and said with a playful grin.

"Haha, Alice, you've been taking care of Chris all by yourself. Must be exhausting, right? Thank you for your hard work. Without me, your life must be a mess, huh?"

"Huh?" Alice turned her head to look at him, her expression a cold smile. "Why would I be tired? Taking care of Chris alone is so easy for me. After all, I already knew you were unreliable, so I've long since made my peace with it."

Merlin's eye twitched. He thought, "This woman—I've already stepped back, yet she still doesn't buy it?"

"That's not true!" Chris quickly looked up and argued. "After Daddy left, Mama got really tired. Every day she talks to herself, calling out Daddy's name. Mama misses you so much!"

"Oh? Is that so, Alice?" Merlin's expression turned sly, his smile growing more mocking.

Don't make things up! I spend every day cursing him! Alice quickly defended herself, her cheeks flushing with two red blooms.

"I'm not lying." Chris immediately looked hurt. "Daddy's socks really stink, but Mama still washed them by hand, hehe~"

"Uh, Alice," Merlin was surprised, looking at Alice with embarrassment, thinking, "This guy actually does the laundry for me? Hard to believe!"

"Ahhh~" Alice, overwhelmed by her daughter's relentless teasing, suddenly felt her face flush crimson, her whole body trembling with embarrassment.

"And also—" Chris lifted her head, her expression tinged with confusion.

"After Daddy left, Mama did some strange things."

"I saw Mama hugging Daddy's pillow, rolling around on the bed, sniffing it over and over again."

title: Chapter 9 — Little Spy
content:
Chapter 9 — Little Spy

Volume 32 · Chapter 9

Merlin's expression turned weird, looking at Alice with suspicion. He couldn't figure out what Alice was doing hugging his pillow while he was away. Sounded like a pervert.

Alice's delicate body trembled, lowering her head but ears already red. Embarrassed by daughter's "revelation", how could she be tough with Merlin now?

"Alice, that..." Merlin wanted to speak but stopped.

"Shut up! It didn't happen! All Chris's nonsense! She often treats dreams as reality, must be hallucinating!" Alice looked up, stern-faced, refusing to admit.

"Nonsense?" Merlin frowned. In his impression, Chris never lied.

"Mom accuses me again, I didn't make it up!" Chris puffed up, feeling wronged, always labeled a "liar" by mother.

"Speak less, eat more. Why can't you shut your mouth even while eating?" Alice said seriously, worried Chris wouldn't stop blurting things.

"Hmph!" Little Chris huffed, lowering head, pretending nothing happened.

"Alice, are you having some mental issues?" Merlin looked pitying, remembering the head maid of the Demon Lord Palace, Alice was trending toward perverted too.

"You're the one with mental issues!" Alice was furious, arms crossed glaring at Merlin. "Impossible to do such shameless things! Don't underestimate me!"

Is that so? Merlin thought, sweating. If he asks more, she'll explode. Never mind, pretend not to know.

"You think I can't survive without you? Joke! I can manage everything perfectly. Of course I won't feel uncomfortable because you're gone. Actually I'm happy, like a burden lifted~" Alice insisted she didn't need Merlin, living alone was cozy.

"Haha." Merlin chuckled dryly. How could he let Alice ride on his head? So he countered, "Funny, I'm the same. This time out alone was great. Without you, ears are quiet. Without your nagging, I understood freedom*. If not for Chris, I wouldn't come back so fast. Must play outside for years..."

Alice gritted teeth, smile ugly. "Fine, since you like freedom, keep hanging out outside. Chris already adapted to your absence, I fully agree!"

"Ahe, I didn't come back for you. For my cute daughter. Your agreement doesn't matter. I won't care about your feelings~" Merlin smirked, shrugged, careless look.

Alice seeing Merlin's shameless look, angry, wanted to smash his head in beef soup!

"Dad always lies." Chris looked up again, confused.

"Where did Dad lie?" Merlin asked strangely.

"Dad clearly cares about Mom." Chris chewed food, unclear speech.

"Ah?" Alice froze, staring suspiciously.

"Haha!" Merlin scratched head, laughing to cover embarrassment. "Impossible? Unless sun rises from west."

"But Dad brought gifts back for Mom, I know~" Chris said babyishly.

"Gifts?" Alice didn't believe Merlin had such thoughts. After so long, she knew this bastard too well.

"What gifts? Don't joke." Merlin avoided eyes.

Seeing Merlin deny, Chris didn't even wipe food from mouth, jumped from chair, short radish legs running to bedroom, searching luggage.

Soon after, Chris came out, waving a bunch of vibrant tulips. Different from ordinary, more lush, fragrance overflowed. Winter, season of withering, blooming tulips impossible.

"This!" Chris put tulips on Alice's lap, smiling. "I secretly checked Dad's luggage, there was this? Chris is young, no need for flowers. Dad must have brought specially for Mom!"

"This..." Alice looked at tulips, looked up quietly. "Really for me?"

Merlin tilted head, didn't know what to say, extremely awkward. Caught off guard—

Actually on way to Sixth Demon Lord Palace, Merlin found Leviathan's garden. Tulips cultivated by Leviathan, high quality, never wither, even broken lives long, truly strange!

Leaving, Merlin thought away so long, Alice alone caring for Chris must be hard. So shamelessly asked Leviathan for a bunch tulips, prepared for Alice.

Leviathan knew Merlin didn't love flowers, but didn't ask, picked best tulips.

These were Leviathan's treasures, given unconditionally. This youngest king's image improved in Leviathan's eyes, at least not hated outsider.

Merlin wanted to give Alice upon meeting, but kept delaying, embarrassed. Couldn't cross "dignity hurdle".

Know Merlin never gave flowers to girls, except certain crossdresser. Asking him give flowers to Alice daily quarreling, too hard.

Merlin already gave up, didn't expect cute daughter curious secretly snoop luggage? Probably thought he'd bring toys. Now embarrassing.

"Those... picked randomly on road, you like give you."

"嘻嘻~" Chris grinned, like seeing through everything.

Merlin's face turned red, pretended angry: "Laugh what? Don't snoop Dad's luggage anymore, like little spy following me."

Alice looked at tulips, silent, pretty face blushed—

Picked randomly on road? Won't lie.

Cold winter, where find blooming tulips?

Getting these flowers, Merlin must have put thought?

Annoying, why not give earlier? I wouldn't refuse.

(mwm)

title: Chapter 10 — Extra Yarn
content:
Chapter 10 — Extra Yarn

Volume 32 · Chapter 10

Alice's mood was rather complicated—this was the first time Merlin had ever given her flowers.

Never mind what Merlin was really thinking—at the very least, he had finally learned to understand her difficulties.

Alice's face turned red as she lowered her head and giggled silently. *Merlin wasn't beyond saving after all.*

They had been living together for a long time. Although Merlin had only brought a bunch of flowers, it was a huge step in their relationship. This smiling gesture made Alice realize she still held a place in Merlin's heart.

Alice's gaze flickered. Inside, she was somewhat resentful. *If you prepared flowers, just give them to me directly! Why wait until Chris exposes the lie to admit it? It's just flowers—why so many reservations?*

Chris climbed up Merlin's leg and poked his cheek with her small hand. "Daddy's face is red? Daddy is shy~"

"No no no, the room is too hot. I'm not embarrassed." Merlin waved his hand awkwardly, somewhat unable to withstand the girl's teasing.

Alice secretly lifted her head and saw Merlin's face was indeed slightly flushed. She couldn't help but wonder—this guy whose face was thicker than city walls, could he also get shy? He had never turned red around other girls before. What was there to be embarrassed about? We aren't strangers.

Merlin caught Alice's gaze in his peripheral vision. Seeing she seemed unaffected, he grew even more awkward. *Did she not like what I prepared? Did I bring the wrong thing?* Alice didn't seem like the type to fancy these flashy trinkets.

"Uh, if you don't like them, just throw them away. I picked them randomly anyway—nothing valuable."

"No—" Alice lifted her head in panic, words catching in her throat. "I—I didn't say I didn't like them."

"Tch." Merlin smirked. *God knows if she likes them or not—zero reaction.*

"Actually…" Alice lowered her head and thought for a moment, then spoke in a voice no louder than a mosquito. "I kind of like them."

Though Alice's voice was tiny, Merlin heard it. His gaze darted away. He scratched his hair, deliberately acting casual, trying not to seem like he cared about Alice's opinion.

"Is that so? Glad you like them. I—I only brought them on a whim."

"Hm?" Alice lifted her head, seeing Merlin's usual slovenly posture. Her old habit kicked in. "I like them, but you didn't come back on time—that's your fault. I said it didn't matter to me if you returned or not, but Chris nags me about it every day. It's annoying."

"I did my best," Merlin said, feeling he had ridden as fast as he could all the way back.

Little Chris, hearing her mother always use her as a shield, felt terribly displeased. So she said in a sweet, aggrieved voice, "It's not just me who misses Daddy. Mommy misses him too, you know."

"That's not true. I'm not the one—" Alice looked away, pretending to know nothing.

"But Mommy always lights a lamp in the middle of the night to knit a sweater for Daddy. I can't sleep~" Chris tilted her face upward, equally feeling wronged.

"Sweater?!" Merlin's mind went blank. He had never heard of this.

"You're making things up again. Eat your meal, then go back to your room. Don't talk nonsense in front of adults." Alice frowned, putting on the stern-mother act.

"Hmph—"

Chris's face puffed up like a steamed bun. She felt the whole family's black pot had been dumped on her alone, so she stomped back into the bedroom and rummaged through drawers.

In no time she pulled out two sweaters—one small, the other clearly much wider, obviously not meant for a child or a woman.

"This is Mommy's for me!" Chris waved the small sweater, then held up the wider one. "This is Mommy's for Daddy. Daddy's sweater is complicated—Mommy stays up late every night working on it~"

"What are you doing? Put that back right now!" Alice was struck like by lightning, leaping up from her chair. Her face flushed red, as if still steaming. Her daughter had completely destroyed her last shred of dignity!

Chris was entirely unfazed by Alice's ugly expression. She bounced over to Merlin's side and handed him the wide sweater. "Daddy, try it on. Mommy probably doesn't know if it fits you. She guesses Daddy's figure every night by trying it on herself. I watched until I was tired!"

"Stop it! You're getting more and more disobedient!" Alice was mortified beside them, but the little girl was like a loose horse that couldn't be reined in.

Merlin looked at the sweater in his hand, utterly shocked. In his eyes, the carefree Alice would never be able to do this kind of handiwork! She was good with swords and spears, sure—but knitting?

His mood turned extremely complicated. Alice's knitting wasn't great—barely passable—but the fact that she had prepared winter clothes for him carried real meaning.

Besides, Alice should know demon body temperature differs from humans'. He wasn't afraid of cold. The sweater was, for Merlin, a rather pointless thing.

Merlin stroked the soft wool, glanced up at the "petrified" Alice, and asked, "For me?"

"Hmph~"

Alice gave a light huff—neither confirming nor denying. She hardened her face into an expression of total indifference to whatever anyone thought.

Actually, Alice had seen the weather turning cold and wanted to knit a warm garment for young Chris. Though Chris didn't feel particularly cold, there is a kind of cold called "your mom thinks you're cold."

While buying yarn, Alice thought of Merlin. After a series of internal debates, she decided to knit one for him too—the kind of cold called "your wife thinks you're cold."

Alice didn't expect Merlin to be grateful. She just hoped that if he wore it, the two of them would look more like a couple.

Originally Alice had planned to find an opportunity and bestow it upon him with a superior attitude. She never expected the little brat to rebel so directly and just blurt it out—completely ruining her plan.

"If you like it, wear it. I only planned to knit one for Chris to keep her warm. But I bought too much yarn, so I—so I just knitted one for you too. It was incidental! I didn't—I didn't specifically prepare it for you—"

"? ? ?" Merlin's mind was flooded with question marks. He felt Alice was insulting his intelligence.

*Too much yarn? The yarn bought for Chris's sweater—the extra portion could knit one for an adult male?*

*That's logical. Quite convincing, actually.*

*Do you think I'm three years old?!*

title: Chapter 11 — Unextinguishable
content:
Chapter 11 — Unextinguishable

Volume 32 · Chapter 11

Alice glanced sideways at Merlin, not knowing in her heart whether he liked it, which made her very nervous. Merlin looked at the sweater Alice had knitted with her own hands, feeling that Alice had also put a lot of thought into it. If it's really as Chris said, that she's been knitting every night lately, Merlin feels quite embarrassed about this thing, feeling somewhat unworthy. Alice withdrew her gaze, wondering whether he liked it or not, why he wouldn't say a word. "When did you learn to knit a sweater?" Merlin asked curiously, thinking that Alice practices sword and spear every day, so she shouldn't have time to learn such a thing. "I've been learning from the landlady recently; her skill is much better than mine." Alice answered truthfully. "The landlady..." Merlin sighed, thinking about the people around Alice, it seemed only the landlady had the mood to teach her knitting. "That..." Alice wanted to say something but stopped, speaking in a lofty tone, "Don't force yourself too much; if you really don't like it or it doesn't fit well, just throw it away, after all my knitting is also pretty bad." Merlin pressed his lips, raised his head, his old face turned red, and he replied in a low voice, "It's pretty good, I... I actually like it quite a bit." Alice lowered her head in a fluster; on the surface she was cold, but inside she was already bursting with joy; it seemed these days hadn't been wasted effort. "Thank you, and you still thought of me." Merlin said, steeling himself, even if he hadn't put on the sweater, it still felt warm. "Alice grew more flustered; Merlin's expressions of gratitude were few and far between, and now he said it so bluntly, making her heart race quite a bit, and it's not something precious, so there's no need to..." Both lowered their heads at the same time, neither daring to look directly into the other's eyes, the atmosphere mysteriously became a bit odd. They each thought the other didn't care much about them, but their precious daughter smashed the window paper wildly, exposing the truth, so they could no longer hide everything in their hearts as before. Little Chris glanced at Merlin, then looked up at Alice, giggling nonstop, "Although Mom and Dad always argue on the surface, in private they're each more honest than the last, hehe~" "You're talking nonsense again! What could a little kid possibly understand?" Alice sternly scolded her daughter. "Yeah, it's been a few months since we last saw you, and you've become more and more mischievous." Merlin said with a stern face. "Hmph..." Chris puffed out her cheeks, waving her little hands angrily, feeling wronged, as if she had inexplicably been blamed by her parents— It seems Mom and Dad only become very harmonious when they're scolding me; clearly I didn't do anything wrong, it's just that Mom and Dad are too impatient! Late at night, Chris, having played too happily after the family gathering, couldn't help but fall asleep early. Alice came out of the bedroom, gently closed the door, afraid to wake the sleeping little one. "Has Chris already fallen asleep?" Merlin asked, raising his head. "Mm, when you came back she was very happy, she accidentally got overexcited and slept more soundly than usual." Alice explained, and by the faint light of the oil lamp she saw that at some point Merlin had already put on the sweater she had knitted for him; it looked like there was no discomfort. This sweater was knitted by Alice according to her memory of Merlin's build; although it couldn't match his figure exactly, it was basically close enough. Merlin's thick-skinned attitude made Alice feel even more embarrassed; she quietly sat beside Merlin and whispered— "Does the sweater still fit?" "Huh?" Merlin lowered his head to look at his new sweater, a flash of embarrassment crossed his face, "It's good, the size fits well, thanks for remembering what size I wear." "This I can still remember," Alice said, instinctively tugging at her nightgown, a bit annoyed. "You know, right? I don't need warmth; a demon's body temperature is different from humans'." Merlin asked curiously. "You also know I have no interest in flowers, right?" Alice glanced at Merlin. "Merlin was at a loss for words, as if he'd been caught with his hands in the cookie jar, and fell silent." The oil lamp emitted a yellowish glow; the two people in front stared at the floor for a long time, like a young couple arguing. Alice glanced at Merlin from the corner of her eye and said in a very soft voice, "I know you don't need warmth, I just simply wanted to knit you a sweater." "I'm similar; if I don't bring something, I'd feel embarrassed, giving flowers to any girl is never a mistake," Merlin explained hesitantly. "Why would you feel embarrassed?" Alice looked at Merlin in surprise. "I'm not someone without empathy; taking care of Chris alone would surely be tough, I'm quite aware of that." Merlin said, lowering his head. Alice's face turned slightly red, she muttered, "Actually it's fine; mainly because you're suddenly not around, I'm not quite used to living alone." "!!?" Merlin stared at Alice in shock; actually he wasn't used to it either, it turned out Alice felt the same way. Alice felt extremely uneasy under Merlin's fiery gaze, "Don't misunderstand, I mean the household chores that used to be done by two people now fall to one person." "That's how it is." Merlin nodded, almost misunderstanding Alice's meaning; he thought he wasn't that important in Alice's eyes. Alice felt a cold sweat on her forehead; fortunately the dim light hid it, her heart was pounding, she was nervous to death, because not having seen him for a while she felt Merlin was different, perhaps the freshness of their long separation hadn't worn off yet. "You must have a lot of things you want to ask me, right?" Merlin said solemnly, knowing Alice would surely have doubts about recent events. "Exactly, why did the demon race suddenly launch a war against the human kingdom lately? Even if you're outside, you must know about this, right?" Alice frowned; she had always wanted to ask Merlin if he knew any inside information. "Indeed it's this matter? It's a long story; actually regarding the demons' attack on the Britannia Kingdom, I too was very surprised; I only just learned the details not long ago." In the following time, Merlin recounted his experiences during this period, including his struggle with Mammon over the relics. Although Merlin didn't tell Alice too many secrets of the demon race, he still revealed a little-known aspect of the demons— "The demon race has always believed in an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth." "Unless the demons are completely exterminated, the fire of revenge will never be extinguished." "The heavy blows suffered in the holy war have inflicted irreparable wounds on the demons." "It seems we successfully defended the Demon Lord's Palace, but without a doubt we suffered a crushing defeat." "When people thought the demons would only hole up in the Demon Lord's Palace, barely surviving, in fact they had already begun preparing their revenge plot, determined to take back everything they had lost; the pain the holy spirits inflicted on the demon race will also be repaid by humanity."

title: Chapter 12 — Traveling Fortune Teller
content:
Chapter 12 — Traveling Fortune Teller

Volume 32 · Chapter 12

Things were actually like this.

Alice listened to Merlin's words and only then realized how many things had recently happened inside the demon race. The reason she came back late was because on the way she still had to handle the greedy Demon Lord's matters.

Thinking of this, Alice couldn't help but feel a bit guilty, feeling that Merlin was already very tired, and coming back to face her cute temper was indeed not right.

"The series of victories Maen obtained in Britain successfully ignited the invisible gunpowder barrel of the demon race. The Council - passed the strategy of large-scale expansion." Merlin paused and continued, "If they win, then the world will return to the demon era again, and all demons will enjoy the fruits of victory."

Alice furrowed her brows, feeling that this matter seemed not bad for Merlin, so why did he stop it?

"You wouldn't be very happy, would you?"

"Alice, I'm not the same as you. I don't have the awareness to save others. I stopped because the demon race cannot bear the price of defeat." Merlin lowered his head and said softly, "Even if there's only a one-in-ten-thousand chance of defeat, the entire demon race will cease to exist. Although I have been exiled, I don't want to see my people go down a hopeless path."

Alice lowered her head, thinking that finally Merlin still cannot let go of his family?

"Alice, do you think I'm very strong?" Merlin suddenly asked.

"Let me think about it." Alice thought carefully and nodded, "Of course you are strong. Don't you have confidence?"

"But I can't be certain that there's no existence in this world that can defeat me. Although I lived in the human realm for a long time, I still can't confidently say I've seen all strong humans. For this reason, starting a war out of the blue is really too much of a stretch." Merlin sighed and suddenly added, "Besides, there are some other original..."

"What?" Alice curiously followed up.

"Merlin originally wanted to say that if he stands on the Council's side, then he would be Alice's enemy. But he hesitated and couldn't say it out, instead replacing it with using his daughter as a shield, 'I hope Chris can live as a human alone, and I don't want her to be too entangled with the demon race. It's not a good thing?'"

"Why?" Alice moved in her heart, intentionally or unintentionally saying, "I see your subordinates, they seem to like her a lot."

"Because they are my subordinates, so they will unconditionally accept it. If it were other demons, they would absolutely not tolerate Chris's existence. They would try their best to erase her. If the world returns to the demon era again, Chris would have no survival space at all. I don't want to see this happen." Merlin could no longer just consider himself; he had to think more about his cute daughter.

Alice thought for a while, and said in a huff, "I think your sister also very much wants to bring Chris to the Demon Lord Palace, to cultivate a fourth Lucifer or something."

"This is impossible. The Demon Lord Palace is like a cage. Once you become a monarch, you might never be able to leave the Demon Lord Palace for the rest of your life. Chris is still a child. Making her a canary in a cage, losing her freedom at such a young age, is too cruel for her." Merlin spoke his heart's truth, never intending to cultivate Chris into a Demon Lord.

"Didn't expect you to think so much for Chris? I'm glad, Merlin." Alice showed a smile, and the hanging heart seemed to settle down.

"What's the big deal? No matter where Chris comes from, I have to be worthy of her calling me dad. This child always makes people worry. Her power will attract the greed of countless people." Merlin said with concern.

Alice thinks that with herself and Merlin, there are very few people who can hurt Chris. She pondered for a moment, and couldn't help but ask, "Merlin, are you now standing among the human camp?"

"I'm not too sure." Merlin slightly furrowed his brows. His situation is quite special. Before crossing over, he was human; after crossing over, he became a demon? He can't give an answer as to whether there are more demons or more humans; perhaps it's half and half.

"If, I mean, if, the situation deteriorates to the extreme, will you fight for the demon race?" Alice was very concerned about this question.

"Perhaps yes, perhaps no." Merlin's answer was ambiguous. He turned the topic— "What about you? Do you want to be a justice little guard and oppose me? I don't mind. It's not like I haven't bullied you once before."

"Don't look down on me! Humph~!" Alice glared at Merlin and hesitated, saying, "At the very least, I will consider your feelings, and standing opposite you is not what I want to see. But if demons really enslave humans, I probably can't just sit by and do nothing. Even for Chris's sake, I would pick up my sword."

Merlin deeply looked at Alice. She could consider her own feelings, which was already the maximum compromise.

"Don't worry. Full-scale war hasn't broken out yet. I have already stopped Maen. I believe the many elders of the demon race will also calm down."

title: Chapter 13 — Ouroboros
content:
Chapter 13 — Ouroboros

Volume 32 · Chapter 13

What the heck? It's fortune-telling again, another one of those swindlers trying to get free food and drink.
Merlin frowned slightly, not really believing in fortune-telling; it's completely just using psychological suggestion to make others believe what he says.
He thinks few people possess precognitive insight; you can't just find such people casually on the street.
Having seen the hints of the demon prophets in the gods' relics, Merlin's view on precognition and fate has somewhat changed; he doesn't completely disbelieve prophecies, but he needs to personally experience their truthfulness—like this roadside fortune-telling stall, obviously fake without thinking.
"Let's go in and have a look! It looks interesting?" Alice suddenly clapped her hands, wanting to go in and play.
"Huh? No need for that? You still believe this? It's just a liar spouting nonsense; anyone who believes it has a problem in the head." Merlin didn't really want to go in; seeing those mystic swindlers annoyed him.
"What does it matter? Anyway, we have nothing else to do; might as well go in and play, maybe the fortune-teller inside is actually accurate~" Although Alice doesn't really believe in fortune-telling either, she suggests going in to play.
"Forget it; knowing it's a trap, jumping in anyway is really stupid." Merlin shook his head.
"Dad, go in and have a look; maybe there's lots of fun stuff in there." Chris tugged at Merlin's side, her eyes glittering with curious little stars.
"By the way, Chris seems never to have known what fortune-telling is; let's go in and let her learn about it." Alice said with a smile.
"This." Merlin thought a bit, then nodded, "Alright, let's see what the fortune-teller inside is capable of."
Upon entering the temporary small tent, a mysterious aura immediately hit us.
Smoke swirled, light dim, the top of the tent seemed to have stars, shining brightly downwards.
All around hung many strange props—starfish, dead lizards, livestock skulls, etc.
Since it's a traveling fortune-telling stall, there isn't much inside—just a wool rug and a table, with a transparent crystal ball placed on it, looking rather eerie.
After the family of three entered and looked around, they felt the fortune-telling stall was distinctive, lacking much of the usual mystic paraphernalia, and instead had a touch of simplicity.
"It doesn't seem to have anything special; compared to ordinary fortune-telling stalls, it's obviously too shabby," Merlin whispered his evaluation, not noticing any danger here.
"This fortune-teller seems to be doing business while traveling; that's already not bad." Alice understood, saying, "A makeshift tent can't compare to a finely decorated shop."
Chris's little head wiggled back and forth, she was very curious about everything here, poking and prodding, trying to stick her small hand into the dead lizard's mouth, deliberately showing a pained expression as if she had really been bitten.
"What are you doing? Don't touch things randomly; outside you need to know manners." Alice took her daughter's hand away and sternly admonished.
"Mom, what is fortune-telling?" Chris was very puzzled, the cowlick on her head turning into a question mark.
"Fortune-telling is just a game where you can see a person's past and future." Alice mixed the game and fortune-telling together, hoping Chris would regard it as a game rather than take fortune-telling seriously.
"A game?" Little Chris tilted her head and immediately giggled, "Can it see how much cream cake I'll eat in the future?"
"Maybe it can~" Alice affectionately rubbed Chris's little nose.
"Welcome to the fortune-telling stall, I'm Olo Bus, a traveling fortune-teller; let me say upfront: my fortune-telling cannot be precise about a single matter, I can only discern some things from macroscopic revelations."
Suddenly a deep voice sounded; the smoke inside the fortune-telling stall, as if obeying a command, drifted apart to both sides—
A fortune-teller in a long robe sat cross-legged, wearing a huge antelope skull resembling a mask on his head; on that skull, he had painted with blood a strange eye pattern, as if it could see through everything.
As soon as this fortune-teller appeared, the sounds inside the tent almost all vanished; the noisy crowd outside couldn't be heard at all in here.
Merlin scrutinized Olo Bus, thinking, "What kind of fortune-teller is this? Right off the bat he says his fortune-telling isn't accurate—isn't that just driving customers away? What a weird guy."
Chris felt the antelope skull was somewhat scary; she instinctively shrank into Merlin's embrace, yet couldn't help blinking her eyes and sneaking glances at the fortune-teller.
"Dad, this uncle looks really weird?"
"Don't be afraid, people who do fortune-telling all like this attire." Alice withdrew her gaze, proactively introducing, "I'm Alice, and this is Merlin."
"Is that so? Then what exactly do you two wish to know?" Olo Bus asked in a low tone.
"This." Alice lifted her head, thinking carefully; ordinary people who come for fortune-telling either ask about future luck or future love life—maybe it's better to keep it simple?
After pondering left and right, Alice decided to ask about future love life, such as who her future husband would be, what he'd look like, and whether she and Merlin would end up together.
Don't look at Alice's serious exterior; she also cares about these little-girl questions. Even if fortune-telling is a scam, as long as the fortune-teller says she and Merlin will become a true married couple, she'll choose to believe it and happily pay.
Humans will choose to believe what they want; most fortune-tellers, by reading expressions and catering to clients, will earn money as long as the clients are happy.
"Then I'll ask." "I'll go first." Before Alice could say what she wanted to ask, Merlin had already set his daughter down, plopped himself down in front of the fortune-teller, his fierce glare like he was looking at an enemy.
"Ah? I should go first, right? I just figured out what I wanted to ask." Alice pouted dissatisfied, thinking she had no interest in fortune-telling before, but after coming in she's even more eager than me.
"It's all the same; let me go first to test this fortune-teller's abilities." Merlin stared at the mysterious Olo Bus, speaking with deep meaning, "No problem, right, fortune-teller sir?"
"No problem, everyone who comes in is a customer." Olo Bus showed no emotion at all.
"I heard you can not only see the future but also glimpse the past? Then I'll give it a try." Merlin paused, his eyes turning sharp, and said solemnly,

title: Chapter 14 — True Skill
content:
Chapter 14 — True Skill

Volume 32 · Chapter 14

"TheHero Behind the Mask, it seems you don't believe I have the ability to see through certain things." Olof Bus lowered his head, his goat mask seeming ready to fall off at any moment. "Then please place your hand on the crystal ball. I'll see some accurate things from within."

"Very well." Merlin wore a teasing smile as he placed his hand on the crystal ball. It felt icy cold, and he was thinking about how to expose this fortune-teller's tricks.

Little Chris sat obediently on Merlin's lap, her hands resting on the table, watching everything with curious eyes. In the mysterious and eerie atmosphere, she had grown much quieter.

As Merlin's hand touched the crystal ball, wisps of mist suddenly rose within the previously transparent sphere, constantly rolling and forming various shapes.

Merlin didn't have much in-depth study of divination, and couldn't understand what those misty symbols meant. He could only watch the fortune-teller become serious, each breath accompanied by a rumbling sound.

The massive goat skull on Olof Bus's head vibrated, and the single eye symbol on it glowed faintly, as if awakening a new eye that could see through everything within the crystal ball.

After a long while, Olof Bus lowered his head. The mysterious aura around him dissipated instantly. It seemed the divination was over.

"How was it? Can you tell?" Merlin withdrew his hand and regarded the fortune-teller with meaningful eyes.

"Your situation is somewhat special. I can't accurately determine your past. The crystal ball lets me see certain illusions, and everyone's is different. Some people make me see vast skies, others make me see unique fictional worlds. But yours is not ordinary—it carries a hint of reality, which makes it impossible for me to give you a definite answer." Olof Bus's tone was filled with hesitation, putting him in an awkward position regarding Merlin's case.

"Huh?" Chris tilted her head, her cowlick turning into a question mark. She had expected the mysterious uncle to say something interesting, but instead got nothing.

Alice was puzzled inwardly. She had never encountered such a fortune-teller before—one who wouldn't say anything at all. Could it really be as Merlin said, just a fraud who runs around swindling money?

"What exactly did you see? Why don't you say it out loud?"

"Haha, of course you're a fraud who lives off others. Fortune-teller, aren't you afraid I'll expose your lack of real abilities? Admit it—divination is all fake tricks." Merlin's face broke into a triumphant smile, feeling like he had caught the scammer in a tight spot.

"Divination isn't fake. It can't reveal accurate things, but it can glimpse the general direction." Olof Bus explained.

"Stop hiding it. Since you say divination isn't fake, then tell me about my past. What's the point of all this mystery?" Merlin sneered.

Olof Bus fell silent for a moment. Facing Merlin's skepticism, he could only slowly say,

"In your illusions, I saw iron birds flying in the sky, iron monsters floating in the water, and iron wild beasts running on the roads without tiring. Square grids were everywhere, as if this were a special world maintained by countless gears."

"I've seen many strange illusions before. Once someone made me see a world that had lost all colors, where there was only black and white, exuding a tremendous sense of melancholy. Another time someone made me see peculiar creatures—entirely gray, with large heads and eyes but very short stature, as if they were strange beings from the cracks of the world. But all of these lacked a sense of reality."

"But you are different. The illusions you showed me made me feel the reality, as if I had personally experienced and built them."

Upon hearing this, Merlin suddenly shivered, his face changing dramatically. He stared intently at the fortune-teller, his heart filled with doubt. Could it be that he had actually encountered a real one this time?

"Dad?" Chris lifted her head and looked at Merlin curiously. It was obvious she could sense her father's emotional fluctuations.

Merlin's expression grew serious. In his heart, he guessed that the fortune-teller before him truly could see through things, even peeling back the events before his reincarnation.

Without a doubt, this man named Olof Bus had some real ability—he had directly seen the scenes from before Merlin's reincarnation.

The iron birds were airplanes, the iron monsters were warships or boats, and those tireless iron beasts must be cars. These things absolutely could not be conceived by people of another world. They were special transportation tools that only a world without magic and martial energy could develop.

Merlin was frightened by this fortune-teller. He had come here just to play around, but nearly had his whole bottom line exposed.

"What are these 'iron birds flying in the sky'? What kind of weird thing is that?" Alice asked in confusion.

"Alice, come here." Merlin's tone turned serious as he called Alice over to whisper something.

"What's wrong? You seem so secretive." Alice noticed Merlin's face looked a bit off.

"This fortune-teller named Olof Bus is a bit strange." Merlin whispered, stealing a glance at Olof Bus behind them.

"What's strange about him?" Alice asked in surprise.

"This guy has some real ability—he can actually see some things." Merlin stated his conclusion.

"Really?" Alice's interest was piqued, and she couldn't help but ask, "What did he see about you? What do you mean by 'iron birds'?"

"Don't ask so many questions. Just ask him something simple. With someone whose background is unknown like this, it's better not to let him see too much."

Merlin couldn't suppress his worry. He felt this fortune-teller was quite frightening. If his secrets were exposed and exploited, that would be terrible.

"Okay, I understand." Alice grasped Merlin's meaning. It was clear that this mysterious fortune-teller couldn't be trusted, and they should be more cautious.

The two returned to their seats, sitting in front of Olof Bus. Unlike before when Merlin and Alice were laughing and joking around, they now appeared noticeably more serious.

"Are you satisfied with the divination I've done for you?"

"Cough!" Merlin cleared his throat to mask his awkwardness, putting on a polite smile. "Fortune-teller, you do have some real ability. I admit that. If I've offended you in any way just now, please don't take it to heart."

"There's no need to be polite. I've seen many people similar to you, but in the end they all end up being very courteous to me." Olof Bus let out a warm laugh.

Merlin lowered his head, a drop of cold sweat sliding down his temple. He thought to himself, this air of superiority and confidence was truly unpleasant.

"So, what else would you like to have divined?" Olof Bus asked patiently.

"I want to know..." Alice, remembering Merlin's warning, decided not to pry into the future or the past. Instead, she chose a question that was very much in line with a young girl's heart—

"I want to know who my future husband will be?"

"What kind of person is he?"

title: Chapter 15 — Future Divination (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 15 — Future Divination (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 32 · Chapter 15

"If Sir can divine it, I hope you can tell me." After saying that, Alice glanced furtively at Merlin beside her, wondering if he also cared about this question. Actually Alice already had an idea; if the fortune-teller didn't say it was Merlin, she would flip the table and leave, not giving any money. Alice mainly just wanted some psychological reassurance; if the fortune-teller said she and Merlin would definitely be together in the future, then it would surely be true! Merlin furrowed his brows, suspicious, wondering why Alice was asking this. It was strange, but it was indeed an ordinary question that wouldn't reveal too many secrets. Although Merlin appeared indifferent, his ears had already perked up, ready to hear what the fortune-teller would say. "This is the most common question from female clients; I can give you some answers. Please gaze into the crystal ball with your eyes," Eurolobus said softly. "Do I not need to touch it with my hand?" Alice asked, raising her head in confusion. "Divining the future and the past are different; a person's body is like a diary, recording the complete past, and touching the crystal ball makes it more accurate, but the future is different—human eyes are the key to seeing the future." Eurolobus paused, then added, "Fortune-tellers do not have the ability to foresee the future; only oneself can see past and future. We merely use divination to help others see the thread connecting the present and the future." "Okay." Alice, feeling dazed, followed the fortune-teller's instruction and focused her gaze on the crystal ball on the table— The originally clear crystal ball rose again with mist, forming eerie vortices that subtly drew one's consciousness into them. The antelope skull on Eurolobus's head glowed faintly again, as if time had fallen into a brief pause. Alice felt her head a little dizzy, swaying slightly; she closed her eyes and rubbed her temples, saying, "This feeling—" "Hey! Are you alright?" Merlin hurriedly supported Alice, eyeing Eurolobus suspiciously. "Don't worry, she's fine; divination requires peering into the soul, it's just a brief dizziness," Eurolobus explained. Merlin relaxed a bit, but still felt a hint of wariness toward the fortune-teller before him—someone who could discern that he was a transmigrator was extremely dangerous no matter how you looked at it. Alice quickly recovered and eagerly asked, "How? What's the result?" "The result is rather vague; whether you believe it or not is up to you," Eurolobus organized his words and said slowly, "Your future husband is a non-human being; beneath his seemingly carefree exterior lies a warm heart." Merlin furrowed his brows, thinking, "Could this be referring to me?" "Huh?!" Upon hearing the words "non-human," Alice's eyes lit up; she thought it was probably Merlin—she and Merlin were destined to be together! Pay! I must give this fortune-teller a generous reward! "He has sun-like blond hair and a unique charm that attracts women, though he is overly upright; although he has many peach blossoms, his true love is singular and unshakeable," Eurolobus added calmly. Merlin's gaze began to dart away, thinking, "It must definitely be me! Blond hair, attractive to women—this isn't exactly describing me? Could it be that I and Alice will become a true husband and wife in the future?" "Huh?" Little Chris twitched her bangs curiously, wondering if she should lift her head to look at her mom and dad. Alice could no longer hide her excitement, feeling that the fortune-teller was talking about Merlin! These traits matched Merlin too perfectly; it was clearly referring to the same person! The two unconsciously stole a glance at each other; the moment their eyes met, it was as if sparks flew in the air. Merlin and Alice simultaneously averted their gazes, each lowering their heads slightly flustered, fearing that their little secret would be discovered by the other. Eurolobus's divination undoubtedly exposed the two's secrets, leaving Merlin and Alice somewhat unable to look each other in the eye. "Most—" Eurolobus paused, then said his final sentence: "Your future husband is a one-eyed person." "Ah?!" Upon hearing this, Alice's eyes widened as if struck by lightning; "Fortune-teller sir, you didn't get it wrong, did you?" "No, I saw the future exactly like this," Eurolobus said solemnly. "Alice couldn't help but start doubting, thinking how could her future husband be one-eyed? Merlin clearly isn't; did I get something wrong?" "Huh?" Merlin stroked his chin suspiciously, thinking that the one-eyed man couldn't be himself; if the fortune-teller was right, then he and Alice would have no chance? Or perhaps he would lose his own eyes in the future? "It's definitely you who got it wrong!" Alice glanced at Merlin, unwilling to accept it, saying, "How could my future husband be one-eyed?! Are you spouting nonsense?" "Clients who come to the divination house all like to hear what they want to hear, but I'm different—I only speak the facts I see." Eurolobus answered sincerely. "You?!’ Alice flared up, refusing to believe the fortune-teller's result; clearly he had just said it was Merlin, yet now it turned into a one-eyed non-human!" "Alice, calm down, let me try," Merlin soothed Alice, then turned his head toward Eurolobus, wanting to see what the fortune-teller could discern from him. "Hmph~!" Alice glared at the fortune-teller, fuming, thinking such a swindler wasn't worth even a copper coin. "So what would you like to ask, sir?" Eurolobus merely looked at Merlin's eyes. "Just like before, what will my future wife be like? I hope you can give a convincing answer," Merlin asked the same question as Alice. "!!?" Alice instantly became tense, worried that the one who would end up with Merlin wasn't her; she instinctively clutched Chris in her arms. ".Mom, you're holding too tight—little Chris is being squeezed so hard she can barely breathe, her face showing discomfort." Eurolobus applied the same ritual he had just used on Alice to Merlin. Merlin felt waves of dizziness; the ritual kept sinking into the misty vortex within the crystal ball, and he wondered what kind of force this was. It felt like having taken some kind of stimulant... "Your wife is a high-ranking human—cold on the outside, warm within; beneath her fragile exterior lies an indomitable spirit, possessing the resolve to save others at the cost of herself, and she is very..." Eurolobus said slowly. "Oh?" Merlin stroked his chin, thinking without doubt that this was clearly hinting at Alice; there was no mistake! Alice, holding her daughter, felt uncontrollable blushes rise on her face; she was both excited and thrilled—this time it must be right, it's talking about me! Indeed I am Merlin's wife! How embarrassing! Eurolobus took a deep breath and spoke his final words— "She will end her life by suicide."

title: Chapter 16 — Son of Belial
content:
Chapter 16 — Son of Belial

Volume 32 · Chapter 16

Merlin's face darkened immediately upon hearing this. The description at the front was indeed not too different from Alice's, but the last sentence was seriously problematic.

Based on Merlin's understanding of Alice's personality, no matter when, she would never choose such a weak suicide. This clearly didn't match Alice's consistent character.

"Huh?!?" Alice was furious, thinking such a weak person couldn't possibly be herself. "I thought you were a diviner with some real ability, but turns out you just spout nonsense!"

"Sorry, I'm not making things up—I'm seeing the facts." Olovbas emphasized seriously.

"This is such a boring divination game, let's go back!" Alice stood up angrily, picked up Chris and left the tent.

"Mommy?" Little Chris looked up, wondering why her mother was so angry.

Merlin also stood up slowly, feeling around in his pocket. Only three pathetic copper coins remained. With a dismissive flick, he tossed them to the other party and said, "So all your previous divinations of my past were just wild guesses? I guess I was giving you too much credit. Three copper coins—don't think they're too few. Your abilities aren't that great, and honestly, you shouldn't have received even one."

Olovbas didn't respond. But just as Merlin was about to leave the tent, he suddenly called out, "Wait."

"Huh? Anything else?" Merlin turned back curiously.

"From the divination, I can see you'll encounter trouble soon. I'm giving you a piece of advice." Olovbas paused, then said seriously, "Don't be stubborn and wake up. Take an early turn for the better, lest you commit a great mistake. Throughout history, anyone who breaks the rules has never met a good end."

Merlin was puzzled, as if someone were deliberately trying to scare him. "Why are you telling me these things?"

"Because..." Olovbas thought for a moment, then whispered, "we share similar thoughts. We're both miserable wretches who refuse to live in a cage."

Merlin raised an eyebrow, deep in thought, but still pulled aside the curtain and left the tent.

The divination room fell silent once more, with wisps of mist curling around and hiding Olovbas again. Yet inside, a sigh could be heard.

Olovbas removed the heavy ram's head headdress, revealing his true face. To everyone's shock, demonic horns sprouted from his head!

His appearance was quite grotesque, with a single enormous eye staring from his face. He was a demon born with one eye!

Olovbas wasn't an ordinary demon. He was the son of the Sloth Demon Lord Belial, possessing demon lord-level strength comparable to other second-generation rulers.

Since the first Belial never stepped down, Olovbas had always been the designated heir of the Seventh Demon Lord Palace. Unfortunately, he was a bastard, and few knew of his existence. Even within the demon race, no demon knew about him. Everyone assumed that Belial, being so old, had never produced any offspring.

Olovbas had been living in the shadow of his father, the first ruler, since birth. Like a transparent demon, he lived within the demon race, like a puppet dancing to his father Belial's whims. To him, identity was something optional.

However, Olovbas was different from ordinary demons. He disliked fighting and killing. Despite possessing formidable strength, he loved painting, music, and divination, like an artist trapped within the demon race.

Due to living under his father Belial's pressure for years, Olovbas intensely hated the Demon Lord Palace. It deprived him of the chance to explore the outside world. Without new inspiration, he couldn't advance further in his art.

Olovbas clearly remembered that as a child in the Demon Lord Palace, he had a friend he could talk to. Unfortunately, she was a captured human slave. To sever his connection to the outside world and make her a compliant tool, Belial killed her. Olovbas hated his father from the bottom of his heart, yet had no choice but to obey orders.

The reason he suddenly came to Rexterrum was also Belial's command—to investigate the matter of Lucifer III fathering a child with a human and hand over the evidence to him.

After the Merlin family entered the tent, their every word and action had already been recorded by the crystal on the table. This would become the ironclad evidence to punish Merlin!
