Olovbas had heard of Lucifer III's name before, but never expected him to be with a human. In his eyes—

Merlin was his own kind, both despising life within the cage of the Demon Lord Palace.

The difference was that Merlin had successfully broken out of the cage, while he couldn't escape.

Originally, he shouldn't have given Merlin those words of advice. But out of pity, he still warned him. Whether Merlin believed it or not was another matter entirely.

This was Olovbas's first time leaving the Demon Lord Palace in his life. He had much to reflect on. Along the way, he had seen all sorts of people. Many couldn't accept their miserable fates and cursed him as a fraud—

"As my father said, humans are incapable of facing their own hypocrisy."

The night before, snow had just fallen, and the entire Rexterrum was cloaked in silver.

The Merlin family didn't head home immediately. Instead, they went to the square to continue playing with Chris.

"Hey hey~ hey hey~"

Little Chris, wearing fluffy earmuffs and gloves, was energetically rolling snowballs on the ground. Her cheeks were red from the cold, clearly planning to build a snowman before going home with her parents.

Merlin and Alice watched their daughter from a distance. But having just come out of the divination room, both of them were in a bad mood.

They had thought that Olovbas, as a diviner, would sugarcoat things for money. Instead, he fed them a load of nonsense. How could they not feel uncomfortable?

"That diviner just spouts nonsense! I'm so angry!" Alice's brows were tightly knitted, her mind in turmoil. She wondered if the diviner's prediction that Merlin's future wife wasn't herself was real. Was she really the kind of person who would be weak enough to commit suicide?

"I told you not to go into that divination place, they're all swindlers. Believe me now?" Merlin shrugged with his hands.

"I just wanted to let Chris experience the charm of divination. Who would have thought we'd run into this?" Alice was full of resentment, then shifted the topic and asked, "Merlin, do you believe what that diviner said?"

"..." Merlin recalled Olovbas's final words of advice before leaving, hesitated, and said, "I can't answer that either. But he's a pretty peculiar guy."

"Really?" Alice looked down, couldn't help but mutter, "I thought the first half of the divination was about you."

"Huh?" Merlin was taken aback, suddenly his face flushed red, hard to tell if it was from the cold or not. "Actually, I thought it was you too."

The two of them, caught off guard, suddenly exchanged words. The atmosphere instantly became tense and awkward. Neither dared to look directly into the other's eyes.

Merlin: "No way? Alice hopes the future husband is me?"

Alice: "Mmm? Merlin has the same thoughts as me?"

Merlin sneakily glanced at Alice, who was sitting on the low rock. Wrapped in her fluffy scarf, her current expression was hidden from view. "Ah, this is really embarrassing. I'm sorry. I guess I really scared you. After all, you hate me so much."

"That's not true!"

"Huh? ??"

"Alice desperately looked down, almost burying herself in her own chest. Her two hands were tangled together, her ears red as she said, "I don't hate you that much."

"If the future husband predicted by the divination is you, I actually..."

(o/w\.)

title: Chapter 17 — Visit
content:
Chapter 17 — Visit

Volume 32 · Chapter 17

Alice hung her head, speaking in a soft voice, but Merlin was right beside her and heard every word clearly.

In truth, Alice didn't want to say something so embarrassing, but Merlin actually thought she detested him? In her panic, Alice had to explain, to make it clear that while she might be a little annoyed with Merlin, it was nowhere near the level of hatred.

Merlin's gaze flickered away, his eyes drifting to their daughter who was building a snowman. He thought, so Alice doesn't really hate me after all? Maybe I've been overthinking things all along?

"I wasn't saying you're the only one I could rely on in the future," Alice stared at her own flushed face, explaining guiltily, as if she'd been caught stealing, "I just meant that... you're not exactly unacceptable either."

"I know, no need to emphasize it." Merlin calmed his restless mind, still sensing a shift in Alice's attitude. At first, she'd clearly wanted him to scram back to the demon race ASAP. When had that changed?

"It's just that I didn't want you to misunderstand!" Alice explained awkwardly, trying to sound casual as she asked, "By the way, when I was fortune-telling for you, your future wife turned out to look a lot like me."

"There's no way, right? A guy as energetic as you wouldn't be so weak as to end his own life, would he?" Merlin shrugged, speaking candidly, "I don't think so either."

Alice hung her head, feeling gloomy, thinking, According to the fortune-telling, Merlin and I can't be together?

"But I thought of one possibility, though it's very low..." Merlin suddenly emphasized.

"What?" Alice looked up, curiosity piqued.

"If we end up as husband and wife, and the fortune-telling is about us, then the future is truly pitch black. I'll lose my eyes, and you'll kill yourself." Merlin paused, voicing the suspicion in his heart, "After all, fortune-telling is about future results. We can't know what will happen. Perhaps we'll face unprecedented difficulties."

Alice frowned, thinking deeply. If that fortune-teller's prediction was accurate, then even if she and Merlin ended up together, their fate would be tragic? She strongly disliked stories that ended in tragedy, and would rather believe it wasn't true.

"No! It's all nonsense from that fortune-teller. I should tear down his tent!"

"I think the same way," Merlin said with a relieved smile, thinking, That guy managed to see I'm a transmigrator? Probably just a blind cat catching a dead mouse, guessing randomly. He's deliberately trying to scare me and Alice, then conveniently selling us talismans to change our luck.

Little Chris was rolling in the snow, stacking two snowballs together, breathing heavily from exhaustion.

This little fellow had no idea what kind of mental struggle her parents were going through.

In Chris's eyes, finishing the little snowman early was far more interesting than watching two "exasperating people" play psychological games.

Alice hung her head, unsure if Merlin even considered the possibility of them being together in the future. After agonizing for a long time, she finally mustered the courage to ask indirectly, "Merlin, we've lived together for a long time now. Do you dislike me?"

"Huh?" Merlin was stunned for a moment, then replied, "At first, I did dislike you, but after getting used to it, it's not bad."

"What do you mean, 'not bad'?!" Alice glared at him angrily, raising her head.

"It means, after spending more time together, I've come to think you're a pretty good person. Although sometimes you're a bit slow," Merlin lowered his head, rubbing his nose, trying to appear calm, "Cough, cough, I actually like it quite a lot."

Alice's face instantly flushed crimson. She lowered her head in panic, her heart pounding. Was this... a confession?!

The two scheming individuals sat on their chairs, their gazes fixed on different places. Anyone could see that both of them were "harboring ulterior motives," each desperately trying to hide something.

Alice's entire mind was occupied with the phrase "like it quite a lot." She wondered if she should respond, to say that she also "liked him quite a lot." At this moment, her heart was sweet, and she was even trembling with excitement.

"Hmm?" Merlin noticed Alice hanging her head and shivering beside him, wondering if she felt unwell. After hesitating for a moment, he swallowed nervously under great pressure and grabbed Alice's hand.

"Ahhh?!" Alice's hand was suddenly held in Merlin's palm. The unexpected physical contact made her flustered, and she even let out a cute, startled cry.

Merlin immediately frowned, thinking, What kind of reaction is that? It's just a touch. Why did she make a sound like a little child?

Alice was completely stiff, her eyes a chaotic mess, trembling even more violently. Her mind was racing. What was Merlin doing? He actually held my hand? So forward? Has he finally realized my hint? What should I do next? I can't think straight anymore!

"Why are you shaking?" Merlin asked in surprise.

"It's nothing!" Alice blushed deeply, feeling the warmth from Merlin's palm. She lowered her head shyly, hesitating, "M-maybe it's just too cold? I feel a bit uncomfortable."

Merlin felt Alice's hand was a bit cool, but it was very soft and comfortable to hold. He pushed his chaotic thoughts aside and said seriously, "Is that so? Remember to drink more hot water."

Alice looked up in shock: "? ? ?"

Two months later, Britain received its first distinguished guest after the war.

The current Pope, Gion, led the Knights Templar along with many esteemed cardinals, arriving for a visit to Britain.

After capturing the capital, Mammon hadn't destroyed it extensively. Instead, he planned to use it as a new base, so the British royal city was preserved well and was fully repaired in just over a month.

This was the first major visitor since the end of war, an event of great significance. Moreover, the Pope brought an exceptionally grand entourage, clearly demonstrating the sincerity and attitude of his visit.

In the eyes of the world, the Pope was the earthly representative of the Goddess Maria. Every word and action represented the divine will, and countless believers loved the Pope even more than their own relatives.

Elizabeth, representing the royal power, understood the Pope's purpose for this visit. It was nothing more than an opportunity to hold legitimate religious activities in the Kingdom of Britain.

The Church claimed to be offering comfort to post-war Britain, letting everyone feel the warmth of the Goddess. Privately, they notified believers to gather in the royal city to welcome the Pope.

Due to the Pope's visit, an unprecedented religious fervor swept through the Kingdom of Britain. A vast number of believers, unafraid of the biting cold, even came barefoot to the royal city just to catch a glimpse of him.

Watching her subjects, old men who had contributed nothing to the kingdom, kneeling devoutly—Elizabeth instinctively clenched her fist, a hint of coldness flashing in her eyes. She felt the very foundation of the royal family being shaken.

title: Chapter 18 — Friendly Visit (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 18 — Friendly Visit (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 32 · Chapter 18

Despite knowing the Church's ambitions were vast, Elizabeth still gave the Pope full respect—

The central avenue leading straight into the palace within the royal city was paved with flowers; on either side of the street, flags of the Holy Church were planted.

Countless pilgrims who had come from all over the kingdom gathered here, kneeling devoutly on the ground, chanting the doctrines on their lips, and worshiping the elderly man on the float with reverence.

The knights' squadron entered through the city gate, rather than going straight to the palace; their expressions were solemn, to guard against evil-minded people.

Behind the knights' squadron were a group of cardinals in red robes, looking pleased as they surveyed the Britons, believing in their hearts that the Church's influence had already penetrated deep into the kingdom's interior. They were certain that this place would soon become land favored by the Goddess, as long as the Queen was obedient, she would have the right to be personally crowned by the Pope.

Sitting on the float was an elderly man; his face was kind, smiling and waving at the pilgrims below, radiating a sacred light that instantly dispersed the haze of war that the pilgrims had experienced not long ago.

Just as the float had left, some fervent pilgrims were unwilling to let it end, desperately chasing after it in the hope of catching another glimpse of the Goddess's earthly proxy.

The crowded crowds gave the kingdom's soldiers a headache. The pilgrims' fervent beliefs truly frightened them. Though these people had never shouted so passionately for the Queen's name before, the Church had obtained trust merely by opening their mouths and fabricating illusions.

It might not take much for the Pope to say a word, and the pilgrims would donate their entire property, or even die without issue—the soldiers believed this wholeheartedly.

For this welcoming ceremony before him, Gioreon found it very good. He could see that Elizabeth had conveyed her meaning, allowing the pilgrims to hold the activity meant that this widowed Queen did not want to fall out with him.

Blakfort stood solemnly by the Pope's side; as the Knight Captain, he had to remain by his side without a step away.

"Your Majesty, this Elizabeth Queen doesn't seem like our enemy. Being able to organize such a grand welcome ceremony shows that she still respects the Church."

"Foolish!" Gioreon continued to maintain a gentle smile, waving at the pilgrims, but his tone held a bit of anger. Speaking in a voice only the two of them could hear, "Don't be deceived by this illusion. Elizabeth is merely using this method to stabilize the Kingdom's peace. She is inherently on guard against us. If it weren't for the war causing the sudden increase of pilgrims here, how could we receive such treatment?"

Blakfort gradually came to his senses, realizing he was indeed not good at intrigue.

"Don't think she's our friend just because you sense a bit of kindness. The Queen's such a warm welcome, creating a peaceful illusion, is perhaps utilizing my influence to stabilize the post-war Kingdom?" Gioreon paused, speaking with a smile that didn't reach his eyes, "Religion was born initially to stabilize people's hearts, with no other purpose. Who would have thought it would become the thing rulers fear most today?"

Blakfort remained silent, thinking he shouldn't know too much. This was a game between the Church and the Kingdom of Britain.

"Whatever Elizabeth Queen does, in my eyes it's hypocritical kindness. If we talk about interests, only then can we see her true face," Gioreon whispered, continuously smiling and responding to the pilgrims' shouts. Merely because of one war between demons and the human Kingdom, the Church's power had rapidly expanded on this land—this was absolutely no business loss.

The pilgrims cheered the Pope's hot scene, seeming to have become a legitimate religious activity again, making many Holy Knights feel as if they were in Rome.

Undoubtedly, this was the power of religion. The methods of controlling people's hearts were a hundred times stronger than royalty. The great cohesion formed by the Church would pull the royalty from the top of rights down into the deep abyss, turning them into the Church's slaves—this undoubtedly touched Elizabeth's bottom line.

On the high platform of the palace, Elizabeth observed this grand parade gathering. Seeing her subjects kneeling and worshiping the Pope, her heart felt as if she had been ruthlessly stabbed by a needle. The prickling sensation made her whole body turn cold.

"The despicable bastards of the Church! We planned to meet the Pope secretly, yet they spread this matter extensively, causing a religious frenzy to erupt recently in the Kingdom!" Katherine frowned, dissatisfiedly saying, "Look at this group of foolish pilgrims. Treating the Pope more enthusiastically than their own kin."

Elizabeth kept a cold face without speaking, but inside she was clear: she had been played by the Church. Making so many pilgrims gather here seemed to be that elderly Pope wanting to give her a warning, demonstrating how terrifying his calling power was. With just one word, the Kingdom could fall into chaos in an instant, or even pull her down from the throne.

"Katherine, the forces of the Holy Church within the Kingdom must be suppressed. If left alone, I fear they will be more dangerous than the demon race. We cannot continue to treat them with a gentle attitude," Katherine seriously suggested, once a war had quickly gathered many believers in a short time, afterwards there would surely be endless troubles!

"I understand this truth, but the Kingdom had just experienced a demon invasion. It is precisely the time when all things need to be revitalized. Now is not suitable for suppressing the Church; it would only cause the peace so hardly obtained to vanish," Elizabeth voiced her concern from her heart.

Katherine's words failed, realizing her suggestion was not mature enough. The Queen was considering the issue from the overall perspective, "But Your Majesty, the Church's matter must be handled. Their power is rapidly rising in the Kingdom, which will threaten your safety."

"The next step is to discuss this. I don't want to stand on opposite sides with the Church, but I cannot let them bewitch people's hearts here," Elizabeth stated her attitude.

"If Your Majesty needs me to do some secret things, however dirty, I will go complete them for you," Katherine gave a slight bow. She wasn't the straightforward type like Messfield.

Elizabeth said nothing: thinking it wasn't to the point of having to assassinate the Pope yet. If she really did that, it would be kicking a hornet's nest, giving the Church a reason to cause trouble.

"Here here! I am everyone's old friend, Bella from the London Post, today is an important day for the Pope's visit. I bet the pilgrims of Britain are about to go crazy? We are fortunate to interview the Cardinal accompanying this time, Mr. Scott of the French Cathedral. Reporter Bella handed the microphone to a Cardinal with a face full of smiles.

Scott: "Good everyone, I am the Bishop of St. Oswald's Cathedral, Scott.

Bella: "Mr. Scott, there have been some rumors recently. The Church's rapid development in the Kingdom is a threat to Her Majesty the Queen's safety? I wonder if that is the case?"

Scott: "How could it be? This time it's just a friendly visit. After all, the great Goddess pities all humans, and our Church is the same. Britain has just experienced battles, and it is precisely when we clergy need to come forward to console the wounded souls."

Bella: "Another thing, many pilgrims are clamoring for the Queen to join the Church. What is your view on this?"

Scott: "Hahaha, believing in the Goddess is a glorious thing. If Her Majesty the Queen is willing, that is naturally a good thing. If the high-born Queen becomes a believer of the Goddess, she will surely be blessed by the Goddess, and the national fortune will surely prosper. If the Queen is inconvenient, Her Highness Princess Michelle is also eligible."

Bella: "The Light Church's classics have been inflated to 998 gold coins a copy. Isn't that a bit over the top?"

Scott: "About this, cough cough! The Bishop's personally signed parchment classics are limited edition sales! Far they can ward off disasters and avoid harm, completely getting rid of the harm from demons! Near at hand they can be transformed into bricks, letting evil spirits fully feel the heaviness of Church culture! Original price 9998! Now the fire-sale price is only 998! As long as everyone hasn't heard wrong, just 998, limited edition classics to take home!"

"Shocking!" Bella reclaimed the microphone, staring with wide eyes, saying, "A low-quality Cardinal openly enriching himself! Trying to deceive the beautiful and ignorant young woman into the Church! Even her underage daughter is not spared! Is this a distortion of human nature, or a moral collapse!"

"Uh!" Scott the Bishop was ashamed, frightened pale, fearing that speaking more would bring shame to the Church—

"What kind of shameless reporter from a third-rate newspaper are you? ? ?"

title: Chapter 19 — Integrate Humanity
content:
Chapter 19 — Integrate Humanity

Volume 32 · Chapter 19

Due to the pope's visit, the Britannia Kingdom recently experienced a religious craze.

Even a small place like Reckham could not escape it; the most excited were the believers and priests. They boldly took to the streets, loudly proclaiming the benefits of believing in the Light Church. To cooperate with this event, the church's flag was raised in the town.

Essentially just a negotiation of interests, it evolved into a grand festival of sorts, showing the enormous influence the church has in people's hearts.

Seeing church flags everywhere, Merlin felt uncomfortable all over. Indeed, Maemon's external expansion war had a counter-effect, causing the church's power to grow rapidly in a short time, already beginning to affect his life.

If Merlin hadn't timely stopped the demons from falling into the war mire, the church would probably soon use the power of religion to unite the human world into one whole, becoming the strongest enemy in demon history. It's easy to imagine that then, the demons' survival environment would be a hundred times harsher than now!

The demons would be further maligned by the church, becoming the public enemy of all humanity. As long as there is a common enemy, an alliance is inevitable.

Although Merlin only knows the superficial history of the demons, he still clearly knows why the demons ruled for so long during the Demon Era. It was because humans were divided into multiple countries back then; any single kingdom taken out alone would be crushed, and they were also full of suspicion and unable to unite. It was only after the gates of the heavens opened that the situation changed.

Even now, with the gates of the heavens closed, the human world still hasn't managed to achieve unity—on the surface they are peaceful, but privately there are many interest conflicts. This relatively stable state is the worst environment for demon survival.

In the Adventurers Guild, many people were watching the pope's visit parade live broadcast, frequently exclaiming in admiration—

To receive such a high-standard welcome from Queen Elizabeth, Pope Geon is the second heavyweight visitor after the Elf King.

Although the pope's visit to Britannia was not the first time; at the founding of the kingdom, when Egbert was enthroned, the previous pope had once witnessed the birth of the new dynasty as a guest.

But giving the current Pope Geon such high-standard treatment, contrary to the norm, has made many people speculate when the relationship between the royalty and the church became so hot?

"Thump thump thump." Hopkins poured several mouthfuls of spirits into his mouth, patted Merlin's shoulder beside him, "Now the church's scriptures have been driven up to 998 gold coins— even selling out, it's simply extortion! Merlin, what do you think?

"Stupid people are too many," Merlin's indifferent evaluation; he hadn't blown boasts or chatted with Hopkins in a long time.

Right! It's truly just stupid people! A group of cowards were scared silly by the demon invasion not long ago, thinking that when demons come, they would flee in fear holding the scriptures? Naive~" Hopkins burped from drinking, continuing, "I regret it, if I had stocked up on basic scriptures beforehand, they'd have multiplied several times in just a few minutes! I might become the richest person in Reckham in one night~"

"Even if you buy them back, this thing is only bought by believers. How many believers are there in Reckham? I don't see that many. There are many fake believers though." Merlin's calm evaluation said, "Can one scripture really drive away demons? If it were that simple, the demons would have been wiped out by the church long ago. How would they still be alive and kicking today?"

"Haha, you look at it very thoroughly," Hopkins raised an eyebrow, "But the royalty used to treat the church very coldly. Now they've become so enthusiastic—don't you find it strange?"

"Not really strange, it must be related to the recent increase in believers within the kingdom." Merlin recalled his experiences over this period, combining with Elizabeth's cautious character, and had an answer in his heart.

"? Merlin's words seem to have some truth, before the kingdom's defense war, Reckham basically had few believers, but recently we can always run into them. It's the same here; other larger towns needn't even be mentioned. The number of believers will surely surprise—Mr. Karl, holding a wine cup, muttered from the side.

"Originally, you all noticed it; the royalty's complete reversal in attitude toward the church means our queen is afraid of Hopkins' meaningful words.

"? Judging by your tone, do you know some inside information?" Merlin narrowed his eyes, warningly looking at Hopkins next to him, the social butterfly of Reckham, whose news was so well-informed, as if there was nothing he didn't know.

"I've only heard a bit of rumor, don't take it seriously, just listen to it as a story." Hopkins paused, putting down the wine glass in his hand, "Our queen is afraid that under the church's instigation, the kingdom will fall into chaos, so she's taken this unprecedented attitude of being favorable toward the church. Actually, everything we see is a performance, is for the believers within the kingdom to see, making them think the royalty and the church are very friendly. Don't look down on those devout believers; as long as the pope guides them a little, they'll do very crazy things.

Mr. Karl frowned, worriedly saying, "So just because the demons invaded, the number of believers in the kingdom has already increased to a level that even the queen fears? This isn't good news; I don't like those stubborn believers.

Merlin silently drank a sip of wine; he felt he had underestimated the subsequent influence of Maemon. If the whole world were believers of the Light Church, besides the Southern United Kingdom, everywhere would be the demons' enemies.

"Actually, the pope's visit this time has impure motives; only a fool would believe he came to appease the believers after the war." Hopkins said mysteriously.

"? You even know why the pope came?" Mr. Karl was astonished looking at Hopkins, puzzled, saying, "Hopkins, where do your messages come from? I've hardly seen you leave Reckham. Did you have some secret pathway? How about sharing it?"

"I don't have any secret pathway. Such a simple thing; just by looking at the church's history a little, one can make a deduction." Hopkins smiled and continued, "The church became the actual controller of Rome through brainwashing. Such a hand-over-fist thing, they've done it once and can't stop."

What does that mean?" Mr. Karl's straightforward brain couldn't quite understand Hopkins' meaning.

"The church must want to continue controlling other kingdoms through the same means, and finally, relying on faith, complete the integration of the human world." Hopkins simply and clearly explained, "I'm certain this old pope came to Britannia to talk these things with our queen, and will make a big article out of the kingdom being invaded by demons."

Merlin's complexion changed; he hadn't perceived it before, but hearing Hopkins say this, he immediately became concerned—

Could it be? The church's cunningness is beyond my expectation.

They want to utilize the influence of Maemon's war to realize their ambition of integrating the human world?

If the church completes this plan, undoubtedly the conflict will evolve into a holy war of that level.

The scale is not inferior to the First Holy War; ultimately, only one race among humans and demons can continue to exist.

title: Chapter 20 — The Hypocritical Visit
content:
Chapter 20 — The Hypocritical Visit

Volume 32 · Chapter 20

Hearing you say that, the Church's people really are terrifying. Mr. Karl sighed sincerely. If the whole world were followers of the Religion of Light—

then they must be insane.

"It's not impossible for things to reach that state, but the probability is quite low." Hobbs shook his head back and forth, then suddenly changed the subject. "But with this current Pope, there's added chance of success."

"Oh? The current Pope's name is John Giogion, right?" Mr. Karl looked up at the kind-faced old man in the magic screen. "Is he very different from past popes?"

"This old man once, when he was young, led the Knights Templar Crusade Army to successfully breach the First Demon Lord Palace. That's the only time in the Holy Church's history that they occupied the demon race's stronghold. It lasted only seven days, but it proves he possesses extraordinary ability." A faint smile appeared on Hobbs's face as he stole a glance at Merlin. "Pope Giogion is like a double-edged sword. Under his governance, the Church prospered like never before, but it also fell into today's bleak state. Without a doubt, he is completely different from all previous popes."

Hearing Hobbs's gossip, Merlin's usually calm heart suddenly stirred. The wine in his cup spilled onto the table. He looked up at the triumphant old man on the screen, and long-buried memories slowly surfaced—

So it's him. That red-robed cardinal who used to hide behind the Hero of the Spear.

He was such a timid coward back then, and now he's become Pope? What irony.

Humans age so quickly. He's so old now I barely recognize him.

In the palace's reception room, unlike the grandeur of the palace itself, every decoration here exuded warmth, clearly designed to make visiting guests feel relaxed and at ease.

Representatives from both the Church and the kingdom sat on either side, listening in solemn silence as the Pope and Queen conversed—

"Your Holiness, it is my great honor that you graced us with a visit." Elizabeth nodded in greeting, her smile flawless.

"Your Majesty is too kind. To receive such a warm welcome overwhelms me. I thought you wouldn't welcome an old man like me, haha." The Pope's white beard quivered with laughter.

"No way! We are all subjects of the Goddess Maria, fellow humans, so of course I would treat you with warmth. Moreover, as the Goddess's representative on earth, I dare not show even the slightest disrespect." Elizabeth spared no praise, flattering the other party.

"That's not quite right. Since we are all subjects of the Goddess, then we should be equal. Please don't treat me specially just because I'm Pope. All devout believers of the Goddess are representatives. This old man is merely one of them." Giogion elevated all believers to his own level, immediately displaying broad-mindedness, drawing quiet approval from the bishops behind him.

"You're right. The Goddess's radiance shines upon every corner of the mortal world. As fellow subjects, there is no hierarchy." Elizabeth's smile didn't reach her eyes. She didn't at all acknowledge that followers of the Religion of Light were superior in any way, and she silently sensed Giogion's cunning—he had set a trap in his words. If she agreed with the Pope's statement, the negative repercussions could be enormous.

"This visit from the Holy Church comes after many years. I remember the last time I came, I wasn't yet so decrepit that I couldn't walk on my own. But now I'm old, unable to stand without someone to support me. Human life is far too fragile. If not for the faith in the Goddess uniting us, how would we ever welcome humanity's golden age?" Giogion stressed earnestly, hoping Elizabeth would concede this point.

"There's some truth to what you say. Britannia has always firmly supported the Church's spread of faith, allowing more people to feel the Goddess's care." Elizabeth's reply sidestepped the point entirely, omitting any mention of her recent measures opposing the Church.

Catherine, standing behind the Queen, listened and couldn't help but furrow her brow slightly. Thinking that all of this was empty diplomatic chatter, wouldn't discussing matters this way be exhausting?

"Recently, the demon race invaded Britannia, leaving indelible scars upon this land. I am deeply sympathetic toward this. The atrocities of those demons keep me awake at night, and I imagine Your Majesty shares that experience, already knowing that our Church's preaching—that demons are humanity's greatest enemy—is no falsehood, but fact." Giogion began making his move regarding the matter of war with the demon race.

Elizabeth nodded, her face sporting an innocent-looking smile, though inwardly she thought: Demons may not be good people, but neither are the Church's followers.

"Therefore, as the ancient and ever-standing enemy of demons, our Church needs more of your support. Eradicating the demon race as soon as possible is our shared hope." Giogion paused, emphasizing, "As long as even one demon remains, humanity cannot find peace."

Catherine frowned slightly. Though she knew the Pope's words were insincere, she had to admit the threat from the demon race was immense. Such rhetoric playing on people's anxieties was indeed very effective.

"You're right." Elizabeth agreed with the stance of eliminating the demon race, but felt the Church wouldn't necessarily act on it. "Then, what level of support do you need?"

"This old man's words don't carry weight. That depends on Your Majesty's sincerity." Giogion smiled meaningfully. This tactic of using demon threats as leverage to extort through talk always worked for him.

Elizabeth's smile turned strained. She faintly smelled the scent of the lion demanding a fortune, thinking: As expected, the Pope's personal visit is definitely more than just about money—

"Everyone, withdraw. Let me speak with the Pope alone."

Giogion nodded, smiling at the red-robed bishops and Blackfort. "You all go wait outside as well. Next, I will discuss matters of fighting the demon race with Her Majesty."

Both parties quickly left the reception room, turning it into a private chamber. Knights guarded the doors, ensuring not even a fly could enter.

The atmosphere inside instantly turned icy. Silence stretched to a terrifying degree. With no onlookers around, both Giogion and Elizabeth dropped their hypocritical masks, becoming far more genuine.

Though Giogion still wore a full smile, Elizabeth's expression had grown serious and cold. In her eyes, the Church was simply a group of bandits draped in religious garb—the only difference being that the Church's charlatans were better with words.

"Your Majesty, why do you look so stern? Your expression now is truly frightening. Is this still the beautiful Queen of Britannia? If your subjects saw this, they would surely be disappointed." Giogion's tone made one uncomfortable.

"Please stop playing your unpleasant games. Without sincerity, nothing can be accomplished." Elizabeth's expression remained flat, but anger flashed deep in her eyes.

"Let us cast aside those useless hypocritical masks and have a serious discussion."

"What exactly do you wish to obtain, Your Holiness?"

title: Chapter 21 — Interest Negotiation
content:
Chapter 21 — Interest Negotiation

Volume 32 · Chapter 21

“Haha, Your Majesty the Queen, don't show such a frightening gaze; our Holy Church is absolutely not your enemy, but rather a group devoted to protecting humanity.” Jiogen said with a smile, the wrinkles on his face gathered together, to the point that his eyes were no longer visible.
“It's a pity, I am not a believer of the Church; I don't believe that sentence. Please drop the pretense, don't think a few words can deceive my eyes.” Elizabeth said solemnly.
“Actually I have always thought you are a person with deep thoughts, not likely to reveal your true side easily; I didn't expect you to be even simpler than I imagined.” Jiogen remained calm, his tone like teasing a child.
“Mr. Pope, this is the Kingdom of Britain, not the Holy Rome you have seized; I am the master here, you are merely my guest. If a guest does not know courtesy, I can expel you at any time.” Elizabeth's words carried a hint of threat.
“Oh?” Jiogen opened his eyes, sizing up Elizabeth, “Since I became Pope, I have seen many kingdom rulers; most are reverent toward me, and no monarch dares to speak to me in this tone, because they all know well the consequences of opposing the Church.”
“Sorry, Britain is not within the Church's sphere of influence; I need not act according to your looks.” Elizabeth responded firmly.
“Britain is not within the Church's sphere of influence? Really? Perhaps it was so before, but not now. Listen carefully, I can still hear devout believers outside shouting my name; they refuse to leave, merely hoping to behold the divine radiance from me, this goddess's agent.” Jiogen wiped the smile from his face, his expression turning grim, “If you want to drive me out, you must ask whether your people agree.” Elizabeth's face turned black in an instant, feeling the Pope's threat, as he used religious power to pressure her, hoping she would become an obedient puppet!
“Before, the Kingdom of Britain was indeed not within the Church's sphere of influence; the number of believers was not large, and my influence on this land was extremely limited. But now it's different, my Queen—” Jiogen paused, his tone low, “After experiencing the devil's rampage, this land has become riddled with wounds; people no longer believe the Queen can protect their safety, and they have realized the Church's long-standing correctness in fighting the demon race, so the number of believers here has surged to a terrifying extent in a short time. As long as your people believe only the Church can eliminate demons and save humanity from fear, frankly speaking, I am the invisible master of this land, and also their spiritual refuge.”
“Nonsense!” Elizabeth angrily stood up, her whole body trembling with rage, “This land was won by my ancestors and a host of knights who overthrew the previous kingdom's tyranny; every inch of soil flows with our blood! Your Church is unworthy to be the master of this land!”
“It's not for you to decide; it's for the people living on this land to decide. If a ruler has no trust in the eyes of the populace, then he is not a ruler but a clown wearing a crown—I'm sure you understand this principle.” Jiogen paused, his smile deepening, “If it weren't for this war ending too quickly, and you barely salvaging a shred of face at the last moment, you would have long lost the land your ancestors won.”
“I do not agree with what you say; your attitude now is to be my enemy. The warriors of Britain fear neither demons nor the knights from the Holy Temple.” Elizabeth's face turned pale, and she instinctively clenched her fists.
“Your Majesty the Queen, the demons have just been driven from this land not long ago; I don't believe you have the courage to oppose the Church, and mutual loss is not what we wish to see, right?” Jiogen lowered his head and spoke softly, “Moreover, you are not opposing the Church alone, but the entire realm of the Church's influence; when dealing with heretics, we never show mercy.” Elizabeth had no reply; it felt as if her inner thoughts had been seen through by this old Pope. Given the situation, she certainly dare not oppose the Church, for if the demon race launched a counterattack, the kingdom would immediately face the danger of two powerful foes.
“Your Majesty, I can sense your inner fear; after all, the surge of believers makes it normal for rulers to feel uneasy. You are not the first king to hysterically shout at me.” Jiogen, having seen such scenes many times, said calmly with terrifying words: “Although your kingdom has not yet reached the point of nationwide faith, I only need one sentence, and your nation will fall into crisis; the angry populace will personally push their queen onto the guillotine. I presume you do not wish to end up like that, do you?”
“Your vileness has already exceeded my expectations; I never imagined that the seemingly kind and amiable Pope would harbor such filthy evil in his heart—even bandits are more virtuous than you.” Elizabeth glared angrily at Jiogen.
“Your assessment is not correct; all human lands were taken from the demons with the help of the great goddess of heaven; all wealth should belong to Mary. As the goddess's agent in the mortal world, I have the right to temporarily reclaim these riches; please do not equate me with those vulgar bandits.” Jiogen emphasized, not liking to be equated with bandits, “If you still wish to continue as ruler, I permit you to join the Church as an honorary believer; under the dual blessing of divine and royal authority, your kingdom will surely become more stable and prosperous.”
“Using the goddess's name to satisfy your own desires—this is the true face of your Church, right? Don't expect me to bow and scrape before you like those petty southern kingdoms, you scoundrel.” Elizabeth fixed her gaze on Jiogen, exuding the dignity of a superior, cold and terrifying, “Every successor of Britain is required to remember forever: never relinquish an inch of land; as the master of the kingdom, one must likewise have the resolve to perish together with the enemy. I will not allow the Church to run rampant here; even at the risk of national ruin, I will not let you sit comfortably in the Vatican's St. Peter's Basilica and pray!”
Jiogen's murky eyes flashed with a hint of fear; he had never seen such a stubborn ruler before—previously those rulers would yield after a little pressure. But this approach does not work against Elizabeth; indeed, she even resists with the idea of mutual destruction. Such a frenzied opponent puts considerable pressure on Jiogen; if he truly drives her to desperation, he has no doubt Elizabeth would raise arms and fight the Church. The Church has barely recovered some vitality recently; if it still has to expend energy on internal war, that would not serve Jiogen's interests—
“Oh~, Your Majesty the Queen, your inner strength surpasses your outward appearance, making me feel genuine admiration; if I have offended you in any way just now, I hope for your forgiveness.”
“Perhaps there is a misunderstanding between us; I have said from the start that we are not enemies, right? Even if you are unwilling to become a glorious believer, that's fine, but you need to sign an alliance agreement.”
“Refusing to become a believer is your bottom line; then this agreement is my bottom line.”

title: Chapter 22 — Joan's Doubt
content:
Chapter 22 — Joan's Doubt

Volume 32 · Chapter 22

Alliance agreement?

Elizabeth was surprised; given the size of the Holy Church, there really was no need for any alliance.

Exactly, an alliance formed by humans; if in the future they face great danger, alliance members must unite to jointly resist difficulties.

Ji Ougen said calmly.

What evil scheme are you cooking up again?

Elizabeth distrusted him from the bottom of her heart.

Please, Your Majesty Queen, do not worry; joining the alliance is absolutely not a bad thing, just as you recently experienced the demon invasion, because you are not an alliance member, we cannot fully assist you, but if you join the alliance, should you encounter similar situations again, you will not only receive help from the Holy Church, but also aid from other alliance members; fighting demons alone is extremely difficult, Your Majesty should know this better than I.

Ji Ougen said.

Listening to Ji Ougen's explanation, Elizabeth couldn't help but frown, having to admit that what he said made sense.

Having just experienced Mammon's trampling, Elizabeth deeply understood the helplessness when facing the Demon Lord; a single kingdom's strength is hard to pose a threat to the demon race, but when several kingdoms unite, they gain the capital to counterbalance.

However, Elizabeth could not determine whether this was the Pope's scheme.

Your tricks won't fool me; the alliance established by the Holy Church must be led by you, right?

Not at all; the human alliance has no leader; everyone must trust each other and act according to the treaty.

Ji Ougen took out an old parchment from his bosom and handed it to Elizabeth, saying, "Please take a look yourself."

Elizabeth opened it and saw that the parchment contained an introduction to the human alliance, with roughly over a hundred stipulated rules.

Many kingdoms have already signed treaties with the Holy Church, most of them southern countries surrounding Rome; on it also clearly appears the name of Margaret, Princess of the French royal succession.

When France was controlled by the blood clan, Margaret, lacking any support, had no choice but to turn to the Church, accepting the Pope's secret baptism, becoming a devout believer and signing the alliance treaty, thereby gaining the Church's support; when resisting vampires, the Templar Knights became her trump card.

Seeing that France was also in the alliance, Elizabeth felt a hint of astonishment; although she had heard that Margaret was close to the Church, she never imagined she had become a believer.

Your Majesty Queen, I have already shown my sincerity; shouldn't you also step back a bit? Joining the alliance first requires acknowledging the Goddess as the sole faith; I won't force you, but I hope you won't overly interfere with the Church's future development in Britain.

Ji Ougen stated the condition; even if Elizabeth refuses to join the Church, it's fine, but she must become a member of the alliance; with Britain's inclusion, the Church's influence in the north will further expand, which is crucial for the Church's future development.

As the Church takes root in the northern countries, the Church of Light will break free from the sphere centered on Rome and achieve a pattern where religion truly influences the human world.

In Ji Ougen's view, a monarch like Elizabeth, once the timing is ripe, can at any moment be replaced by an obedient person.

Elizabeth stared at the treaty in her hand, deep in hesitation; however, the Pope is so pushy that if she refuses, she might immediately turn hostile.

Signing the treaty will undoubtedly bring strong protection in the short term, but Elizabeth does not believe the alliance members will strictly follow the over a hundred treaty clauses.

If she does not stop the Church's development in Britain, she fears it will become even harder to control later; what should she do?

Ji Ougen beamed, returning to the appearance of a kind old man; no matter what Elizabeth chooses, the Church will reap great benefits.

"I hope Your Majesty Queen will heed my advice; with your foresight and insight, you will surely make the correct choice."

"Using the human alliance to resist future dangers is the trend of the times."

Rexham, the home of Merlin and Alice.

Since Merlin is currently hanging out with Hobbs, Alice is alone at home, but just now an unexpected guest suddenly arrived—

Joan of Arc, carrying a mission from Pope Ji Ougen, suddenly visited, coming as a friend.

Alice is now widely known as a strong fighter; anyone who inquires in Rexham knows where she lives, so Joan easily found the place.

At this moment, Joan sat stiffly in a chair, her gaze wandering over Alice's home; everywhere she could sense the aura of heretics, making her feel very uncomfortable.

She believed that a household devoted to the Goddess must have a stone statue of the Goddess and also need a scripture; the first thing each morning should be to take the scripture and pray to the Goddess's stone statue.

However, Joan did not find these things, indicating that the great Goddess is not important in Alice's heart.

Although Joan knows Alice is a pseudo-believer, she still feels uncomfortable; clearly she is more devout, yet she has not received the Goddess's due attention.

By chance, Joan discovered a child's toy on the ground? She couldn't help but feel shocked—

Why does Alice's house have children's things?

Could there be a child living here besides that heretic?

Joan never even thought about having children, because not much time has passed since their last meeting; it's almost impossible for Alice and that detestable heretic to have given birth to a child.

Have something to drink." Alice handed Joan a cup of water, sat opposite her, and asked, "Where are you coming from? France?"

No.

Joan withdrew her gaze, lowering her head with a slightly embarrassed look; perhaps it was an illusion? Alice before her seemed to have gained a touch of maternal radiance, clearly a trait of a mother who already has children.

She could vaguely recall that during the late night at the French royal palace, Alice had told her something; she felt she had done something unnecessary, causing Alice to be not very pleased.

However, she felt no regret whatsoever; heretics were originally her enemies, and even if her assassination attempt on Merlin angered Alice, it would not change her stance.

I am following the Pope's entourage, coming directly from the Vatican; my focus is no longer in France, but I have been directly assigned to the temple, responsible for interrogating the heretics brought in.

Alice slightly frowned, feeling that Joan exuded the aura of a fervent believer, seemingly more severe than before, speaking in a rigid tone: "Surely it must be very hard?"

The hardship is my own affair; I don't need the sympathy of a pseudo-believer." Joan answered solemnly.

”。Alice's embarrassed gaze darted away, thinking she had done nothing wrong, why speak to me in the tone of interrogating a criminal? At least we were companions in the Hero Candidate Training Camp.

You have something here that makes me suspicious." Joan looked at the scattered toys on the floor and asked sternly—

Why do you have children's things here?

(一“)

title: Chapter 23 — Demon City
content:
Chapter 23 — Demon City

Volume 32 · Chapter 23

Ah, that… Alice glanced at the toy her daughter dropped on the ground, embarrassed, she said, ‘It’s my daughter’s toy, this little one was called out to play by other kids.’ Jeanne’s mind went blank for three seconds, thinking she misheard, ‘Ah???’ ‘Really.’ Alice tidied up Chris’s toys, constantly complaining, saying she had told her many times, no matter what, she should put her things away, but then she forgets immediately. ‘Your daughter?’ Jeanne’s expression instantly turned serious, she never imagined Alice was already a mother! ‘Yeah, her name is Chris, she’s a very cute kid, but she’s not home now, it’s a pity you can’t see her.’ Alice’s face showed a hint of apology. ‘Ugh!’ Jeanne felt a heavy blow to her chest, at a loss she sat on the chair, ‘Is it you and that heretic’s child?!’ Don’t always call him a heretic; his name is Merlin. I know you are an interrogator specialized in dealing with heretics, but don’t always look at non‑believers through tinted glasses. Alice repeatedly responded that Merlin being called a heretic made her uncomfortable; in the church, ‘heretic’ is a derogatory term. Jeanne’s shocked expression froze on her face; for a moment her heart was in turmoil, she didn’t know where to start complaining about this— Alice already had a child with that detestable heretic? Calculating the time, that child should still be under one year old; could he already be walking? Clearly the last time we met, Alice’s relationship with the heretic hadn’t reached the point of having a child; why did it develop so quickly in such a short time? Am I not too late? Alice and the heretic have sunk deeper, already become a family of three; now letting Alice return to the church, isn’t it impossible? Jeanne’s face instantly turned ugly; in her view, Alice appeared very foolish, bearing a child with a filthy heretic—doesn’t she feel extremely ashamed? Once a Hero who fought for the Goddess, finally choosing to be with a heretic—what an ironic thing. ‘Alice, are you satisfied with your current life?’ ‘This’ Alice thought a bit, smiled and answered, ‘Of course, I feel happy now; besides the extra worries after becoming a mother, everything is fine.’ Jeanne kept a dark face, silent; she was speechless at Alice’s reply, realizing that whatever she said would be useless and only make Alice more resistant; when competing for the Hero position, she herself lost to this kind of person—this is practically an insult to herself; clearly she is more devout to the Goddess than Alice, yet she hasn’t received the due reward! ‘By the way, Jeanne, you suddenly came to see me—is there something important?’ Alice looked at Jeanne, thinking that someone like her, an opportunist, in the eyes of devout believers, must be a terrible existence; if there were no matter, Jeanne wouldn’t come as a guest. ‘This is a secret letter personally written by His Holiness the Pope, I’m here to deliver it to you, farewell.’ Jeanne no longer wanted to say another word to Alice, so she stood up directly to leave, believing Alice had been corrupted by the heretic beyond redemption, no matter how she tried to persuade, it would be hard to bring her back to the Goddess’s embrace. Alice looked astonished at the sealed letter in her hand, lifted her head, ‘You’re leaving so quickly—don’t you want to keep chatting?’ ‘There’s no need for that; I originally thought you were merely bewitched by the heretic, which is why you resisted returning to the Church, but now I see clearly,’ you indeed have no reverence for the Goddess at all, and are the same kind of person as those heretics.’ Jeanne said coldly, turning away without looking back and pushing the door open to leave. She had no intention of wasting more time on Alice. Alice furrowed her brows, thinking she couldn’t communicate well with Jeanne; this kind of devout believer who regards faith as more important than life, their thinking is fundamentally different from ordinary people. Probably in Jeanne’s worldview, people without faith are sinful, forever destined to live in dire straits; she cannot understand what Alice means by ‘happiness’ exactly. Alice silently opened the Pope’s secret letter, carefully examined its contents, her expression gradually turning strange— ‘That benevolent Pope really is full of sincerity.’ The Seventh Demon Lord’s Palace is located in a remote desert. Here the population is sparse, called the Sea of Death; the vast desert around has no human countries at all. Even merchants heading toward the mysterious eastern lands are unwilling to pass through here, because there are constant terrifying sandstorms, and even evil mirages continually lure people to death. Even elite human armies, upon entering the Sea of Death, would likely not survive more than seven days; the shifting sand makes soldiers’ steps difficult, the scorching sun makes moisture evaporate quickly; the cold night wind is fiercer than Siberia’s, and there are countless poisonous insects and beasts that have survived here. The Sea of Death is the natural barrier of the Seventh Demon Lord’s Palace, making this the safest demon territory, almost impossible to conquer. Looking at history, aside from the Holy Spirit Legion of the first Holy War, no force has ever posed a threat here; the Church’s attacks on the Seventh Demon Lord’s Palace have been zero; all past popes know the Seventh Demon Lord’s Palace is the toughest bone to crack, and they never considered attacking Belial. The first monarch Belial’s Seventh Demon Lord’s Palace, relying on the natural barrier’s advantage, successfully preserved a large number of ancient texts, culture, and military from the Demon Era. If the Third Demon Lord’s Palace of Mammon is called the wealthiest among demons, then the Seventh Demon Lord’s Palace is the most unfathomable place, even there are rumors that the Seventh Demon Lord’s Palace’s strength and foundation exceed the combined total of the other six Demon Lord Palaces. In the depths of the sea of sand one can see the most wondrous scenery; here remains the landscape left from the demons’ prosperous era, a demon town, with unique spire‑like buildings standing like trees, towering black walls make one feel as if in a dark fortress; many demons live freely in the city just like humans. From this prosperous demon city, one can faintly glimpse the era of the Demon Age; many demons lived this way all over the world; they built prosperous cities, using their culture to continually influence other peoples; unfortunately all of this vanished in smoke during the Holy War, only leaving behind ice. In the center of the demon city stands the Seventh Demon Lord’s Palace; its ancient architecture towers majestically, emitting a unique pressure that intimidates all directions— Although the one with white hair is old, he nevertheless holds his book meticulously, leaning on a cane, lazily sitting on the throne, eyes closed, feigning sleep— dozing, his huge horns flickering with tiny flames. Compared to other demon lords’ encounters, the seventh monarch seems to be a perfectionist, dressing himself splendidly from head to toe, his shoes are shining; beneath the Western suit attire lies the soul of an old gentleman. A weary traveler from outside the hall came forward; Olobus arrived at the throne’s base, set his luggage on the ground, then knelt on one knee, and spoke solemnly— ‘Father, I have returned.’

title: Chapter 24 — Demon Lord Father and Son (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 24 — Demon Lord Father and Son (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 32 · Chapter 24

Belial slowly opened his eyes, the flames wandering on his horns swaying, his green eyes gazing at his son.
As the sole surviving first‑generation monarch from the holy war among the demons, Belial’s age is already very great, yet from this old demon one feels no sense of aging; his whole body exudes a mysterious vitality.
He slowly straightened his waist, adjusted his sitting posture on the throne, his hands gripping the silver‑black metal staff, and a kind smile appeared on his face.
“Welcome home, Europa, you’ve worked hard.”
“It’s not really hard, thank you for your concern.” Europa knelt on one knee, head lowered, responding.
Belial asked softly, “How does it feel to leave the Demon Lord Palace for the first time to go out and adventure? Is it like what you had hoped for?”
Europa replied calmly, “Not really. Father is right, most humans are actually hypocritical and unable to face themselves; after more contact, I feel extremely bored. They are completely different from the slaves I encountered as a child, lacking any sincerity, and even lacking the courage to face themselves.”
Belial looked down at his son from above, his green eyes flashing with displeasure, and asked, “Do you still keep thinking about that female slave who was brought to the Demon Lord Palace?”
Europa explained, “It’s not that I can’t forget …”
Belial frowned rarely and asked, “Could it be that you like that slave?”
Europa kept his head down, silent, his face showing no reaction, as if he hadn’t heard.
Belial said disappointedly, “Is it hatred you feel toward me? Blaming me for not killing your so‑called friend? She is a filthy human, and moreover a lowly slave. As my son, how can you get too close to such dirty things? She will taint your pure soul; you don’t need friends, nor extra emotions. You only need to know that you are my son, must obey my orders completely, and everything you have is given by me, including your life.” Belial stared at Europa kneeling below, his tone disappointed, “I thought you had already forgotten that worm‑like humble slave, but I didn’t expect you still to remember. Clearly we once shared her flesh and blood together—it was sour, not tasty.”
Europa’s hitherto calm body twitched slightly, veins bulging on his hands, angry blood rushing to his head, but only for an instant before quickly subsiding, returning to calm.
Europa said, “I don’t like that slave girl, only …”
Belial asked intriguingly, “Only what?”
Europa replied, “I have always held a bit of curiosity toward humans. Their lifespans are so short, why do they create beautiful paintings, moving melodies, splendid poems? These arts require time to mature, yet I cannot produce such achievements within a hundred years, while they can. Consequently I must admit a fact: human imagination far surpasses ours.”
Belial asked seriously, “You really like these utterly boring things—is that what you gained from wandering out this time?”
Europa answered honestly, “Yes, I have collected a great many human folk songs and many verses sung by bards; I really like these things.”
Belial said, “You are my son; don’t learn too much human culture. You just need to know obedience is enough. I don’t want you to grasp too much knowledge; the smarter a person is, the harder they are to control.”
Europa nodded, saying, “I will be careful, Father,” and chose to comply.
Belial frowned slightly, displeased, “You smell of dust, disgusting. I don’t like dirty things appearing before me. Why didn’t you bathe and change before coming to see me? Is there such urgency?”
Europa took out a crystal ball from his luggage and said lowly, “I have finished the task Father entrusted to me; I must hand this over to you personally.”
Belial gestured, and the crystal ball flew into his hand. He deliberately placed a clean handkerchief on it before reluctantly examining it. The images of Merlin, Alice, and their family of three appeared vividly inside the crystal ball.
Belial laughed, “Hahaha, good, good, you completed the task very well.”
“With your concealment ability, Lucifer III could not possibly discover you are a demon.”
“Is that the human woman who is with Lucifer III? She looks quite interesting~”
“And that child—he actually has no demon traits at all, just like Lucifer III.”
Europa kept his head down, not speaking, thinking that the images recorded in the crystal ball would be used as evidence by his father. This youngest monarch of the demon race would likely not escape the harshest punishment.
Belial suddenly asked, “Europa, since you have seen it with your own eyes, in your view, has Lucifer III already violated the demon taboo?”
Europa pondered for a long time and gave a puzzling answer, “Yes, but also no.”
Belial raised his eyebrows in confusion, “What does that mean?”
Europa said seriously, “The fact that this young monarch has had offspring with humans is true, but whether he married a human, I remain doubtful.”
Belial pressed, “Why? What is there to doubt?”
Europa answered, “From observing his various reactions, Lucifer III has not had sexual intercourse with a human.”
Belial murmured, “Hmm?”
Belial stared at the crystal ball, thinking, Since he hasn’t married and coupled with a human woman, where did this child come from? Could it have popped out of a stone crack?
Belial continued, “Regardless of the circumstances, since he truly has offspring, Lucifer III has already violated the taboo; punishment by the elder council is inevitable.”
Europa suddenly lifted his head and said, “Father, I have a question.”
Belial: “Speak.”
Europa asked, “Why do you target this young monarch? The First Demon Lord Palace seems to have no grudge against us. I think Father, as the noble first‑generation demon lord, need not hate a third‑generation lord so intensely, yet you pay special attention to Lucifer III—this seems abnormal.”
Belial replied meaningfully, “Some things you do not necessarily need to know.”
Europa hesitated, saying, “After brief contact, I saw that Merlin is not a completely wicked person: from what I glimpsed of his past, this young monarch values family, cares for his subordinates, and is an excellent ruler; aside from not being proactive in opposing humans, I can’t find any major flaw. Why would he be expelled by the elder council and become a thorn in your eye?”
Belial scrutinized his son, questioning, “Your doubts have multiplied—did Lucifer III say something to you?”
Belial said, “Europa, you are my son; you should not be hiding anything from me.” Then
Belial continued, “You should know your own fate.”

title: Chapter 25 — Found
content:
Chapter 25 — Found

Volume 32 · Chapter 25

"I have had no extra communication with that young third‑generation monarch; you are overthinking it." Europabuss lowered his head, hoping to dispel his father's doubts.

From Belial's various behaviors, Europabuss thought his father was being excessive; if not for some deep hatred, why would he make things difficult for an exiled demon lord? No matter from which angle, Merlin, that young third‑generation monarch, poses no threat to Belial at all.

"I simply think Lucifer III is not a completely wicked fellow; do you and he have some misunderstanding?" Belial relaxed a bit, gazing at his son, saying meaningfully: "Since you want to know the reason, why don't you try divining yourself? You might get an answer; you've always been confident in your own divination, right? Come, try divining my fate."

"Europabuss remained silent, as if there were some taboo, unwilling to use divination to peek into others' thoughts." "What's wrong? What are you hesitating about?" Belial asked with interest.

"Fate is something sacred yet unchangeable; I always hold a reverent heart toward fate; even if divination reveals the future, it only adds to my worries." Europabuss paused, then continued—

"So my divination will adhere to two principles. First, without permission, I will not arbitrarily invade others' privacy. Second, I will absolutely not divine my own fate or that of my relatives. No matter what difficulties lie ahead on the foggy path of the future, I will choose to accept them calmly; sometimes being kept in the dark might actually be a blessing."

"However, regarding this matter of Lucifer III, it's different for you, Father; you've gone to great lengths to scheme against a defeated, exiled demon lord, which doesn't match your esteemed status among the demons; it's practically like dealing with the enemy you fear most in your life."

Belial lazily leaned on the throne, facing Europabuss's objection; this cleanliness‑obsessed "old gentleman" chose silence, and for a long stretch of time gave no response, merely staring expressionlessly at his son.

Europabuss broke out in a cold sweat on his forehead; the immense pressure emanating from his father made him feel extremely panicked; he knew he had touched his father's bottom line, and might well incur his father's wrath, but if he didn't clarify this matter, he wouldn't resign himself.

"In some respects, you have an enigmatic stubbornness; since you want to know so badly, I'll tell you, but these matters are temporarily confidential; under no circumstances should you leak them." Belial withdrew his terrifying aura, making an unprecedented concession: "I had long noticed Lucifer III's abnormality; after Vivian died, her son hastily inherited her mantle, becoming the first third‑generation monarch among the demons, but his temperament is too bizarre, not fitting in with normal demons; he clearly harbors alien intentions toward the demon race, a dangerous factor within the group."

Europabuss frowned upon hearing this, because he had divined Merlin's past and never seen any betrayal of the demon race; his father's words made him very doubtful. If merely because this third‑generation monarch's hostility toward humans isn't strong enough, one would judge him to have ulterior motives, Europabuss thought this was making a mountain out of a molehill.

"Not long ago I received secret news from the Third Demon Lord's Palace: Mammon is dead, slain outright by Lucifer III, causing the war against the human kingdoms to collapse; the newly established demon territory, painstakingly built, has been trampled by humans to utter ruin, and the elders' recently devised expansion plan must be temporarily shelved." Belial lowered his head, looking at Europabuss and said, "All this stems from the very Lucifer III you deem harmless; do you still consider him a member of the demon race?"

Europabuss staggered, hearing such shocking news for the first time; the demon race's youngest monarch openly defied the Council of Elders and personally slew the illustrious Mammon. This is no longer a trivial matter; it is tantamount to being an enemy of the entire demon race. However, Europabuss wavered, for from his divination of Merlin's past he saw no indication that he could commit such a grave treason.

"Lucifer III, lacking maternal guidance from childhood, has undoubtedly become a breaker of rules; he is the greatest threat the demon race will soon face, and his actions bring shame upon Vivian." Belial sighed, speaking solemnly: "As the eldest monarch among the demons, I must bear the responsibility of safeguarding demonic security; therefore this traitor Lucifer III cannot be left unchecked, my son, do you understand?"

After Europabuss left, the oppressive Demon Lord's Palace regained its quiet.

Belial gazed at the empty hall, lifted his head toward the crystal‑like dome, and suddenly let out a cold laugh. The gleaming palace dome resembled a mirror, faintly reflecting his own blurry silhouette.

"Your son is very obedient; I've trained him to be a handy tool, and he works quite well." "He needs no extra emotions; he just needs to follow my orders, making him more loyal than any servant." "It's a pity this fellow has become less honest; should we destroy him? If a tool isn't handy, just replace it."

"I'm in a good mood today, because the suffering I've endured is finally coming to an end."

A few days later, the distant southern Alps' snowy mountains.

In winter, the environment here becomes even harsher; blizzards rage incessantly, and clear skies are extremely rare; to see a sunny day once a week is already considered good.

During this period, all activities nearly come to a halt; the village at the mountain's base seems cut off from the world; such dreadful weather even causes merchant caravans to suspend their business, unwilling to venture into the blizzard, lest they lose their lives.

Even the most experienced guides must wait for clear weather before daring to cross this great snowy mountain.

Yet at this moment, the isolated village at the foot of the snowy mountains received a group of unwelcome visitors.

A contingent of nearly a hundred people, dust‑laden, entered the village; at once the neighing of horses startled many villagers. They wore neat black attire, with insignias resembling a sun and a bull on their chests; each bore sharp weapons, appearing to belong to the same organization.

Had their conduct not been relatively polite and they not avoided drawing too much attention, the villagers would have instinctively regarded this group as a band of brigands or horse bandits.

Although the village's defensive strength is weak, some villagers have spontaneously formed a militia; when faced with a band of robbers, they will certainly resist to the death.

The leading black‑clad figure reined in his horse, brought the steed to a halt, tore off the black veil covering his face, and revealed his features—turns out to be the guest who once appeared at the Adventurers' Tournament, the royal preceptor of the Kingdom of Spain, the Black Dragon Priest Alfonso.

Alfonso, with dark circles under his eyes looking somewhat weary, gazed afar at the majestic, endless snowy mountains behind the village, narrowed his eyes slightly— "Do you think you can escape my grasp?"

"Claudia."

title: Chapter 26 — Faint Traces
content:
Chapter 26 — Faint Traces

Volume 32 · Chapter 26

Alfonso gazed into the distance at the great snow mountain not far from the village, the winding narrow path buried under snow, the sheer cliffs and precipices inevitably inspiring fear, even the heavy clouds could only linger on the mountainside.
The snow mountain hidden in the blizzard resembled a hedgehog covered in spikes, refusing any visitors.
How dangerous the snow mountain is in deep winter—even a three‑year‑old villager knows it, and a normal person would never choose to climb it in this season.
Yet the unexpected guests who suddenly arrived in the village seemed unaware of this fact.
A group of strangers in black clothes gathered in the village, drawing many eyes; the villagers stood not far away, chatting with interest as outsiders.
In this closed‑off village outsiders were rare; most were merchants wanting to cross the great snow mountain.
Alfonso and his assassin squad suddenly appeared, conspicuously out of place among the locals.
Looking at a bunch of foolish villagers wearing thick leather coats and with red‑cheeked faces, Alfonso felt a surge of displeasure; as a prominent figure of the Kingdom of Spain, to be stared at like a monkey by these peasants was nothing short of a white swan falling into a flock of ducks.
“Is Claudia really on this snow mountain? Is the information reliable?”
“Lord Alfonso, this is a guess made by my subordinates; the probability is very high!” a subordinate with a gloomy gaze stepped forward, his tone suggesting he was an officer of the assassin squad.
“A guess?” Alfonso frowned, breathing the same air as the lowly villagers, which made him nauseous. “Just because of a guess you have to specially notify me to come in person? Are you all idiots? Can’t you clarify things before making plans?”
“My lord, you know Claudia’s strength well; no one in the assassin squad can match her. Probably only you can defeat her. To prevent her from escaping again, you must act yourself.” the vulture‑type subordinate said sincerely, worried that reckless action would not only fail to capture Claudia but also scare her off.
“Hmph, if she isn’t on this snow mountain, you and your subordinates had better prepare to die in apology.” Alfonso snorted coldly.
“I am willing to take responsibility. Since I invited you, I naturally have some confidence; this snow mountain is almost cut off from the world, which makes it very suitable for Claudia to… ” the solemn vulture subordinate said.
“Really?”
Alfonso again looked toward the snow‑capped peaks in the wind and snow. He had searched for Claudia for over twenty years with no result, even beginning to suspect she was dead.
Until not long ago, a fleeting glimpse at the Adventurer’s Tournament rekindled his long‑dormant hope.
If Claudia truly hid in such a harsh, isolated snow mountain, it would indeed be hard to expose her whereabouts.
“We have been following your orders, continually searching for Claudia’s traces, but once we traced the trail to the nearest port we lost the clue—Claudia seemed to have vanished into thin air.” the vulture officer paused, then continued, “Later one of my sharper subordinates happened to learn that there is a long‑standing rumor about the village at the foot of this snow mountain that seems suspicious.”
“What rumor?” Alfonso’s interest was piqued.
“On this snow mountain lives a swordsman of extraordinary skill, eccentric and unwilling to see strangers, who has lived alone on the mountain all this time, his attire and appearance somewhat different from ordinary people.” the vulture subordinate lowered his voice mysteriously, “Further investigation revealed that this mountain swordsman is also someone who moved here to live over twenty years ago, which coincides closely with the time Claudia fled the court.”
A strange light flashed in Alfonso’s eyes, as if he had discovered something momentous—
“Notify everyone to rest in the village for one night.”
Because merchant caravans often come to the village, there are many inns and taverns; Alfonso’s party chose one that looked relatively clean.
The innkeeper was a woman over forty, broad‑shouldered and thick‑waisted, resembling a brown bear that spends winter in the forest—someone who has lived all her life in the bitter cold, speaking with a hearty frankness, not yielding to men in the slightest.
“What? You want to inquire about that swordsman on the snow mountain?”
“Exactly. We came because we heard his name, wishing to pay a visit, though we know little about him.” Alfonso did not reveal his true purpose, lest he startle the quarry.
“Ha ha, how rare—someone actually wants to visit the Snow Mountain Sword Saint! That person does have some fame near the great snow mountain, but outside he is hardly known.” The hearty innkeeper laughed; it was the first time she had seen anyone wanting to visit the Sword Saint of the snow mountain.
“Snow Mountain Sword Saint?” Alfonso frowned slightly.
“That’s the person you’re looking for. We don’t know her real name, but seeing her superb swordsmanship we call her the Snow Mountain Sword Saint—simple and easy to understand.” The innkeeper patiently explained, then shifted tone, “But usually no one comes to see her… and yet today so many have shown up.”
Seeing the innkeeper’s suspicion, Alfonso explained, “We are from the Kingdom of Spain’s knightly order, seeking a master swordsman to teach the young knights swordsmanship. Hearing that a reclusive expert lives here, we have come despite the hardship, with no ill intent.”
“The Kingdom of Spain?” The innkeeper’s eyes lit up; even though the village is isolated, she had heard of a kingdom famed alongside Britain, likewise possessing an extremely powerful navy.
“Exactly, this is the king’s teacher, Lord Alfonso.” The vulture subordinate interjected.
“The king’s teacher? I never imagined you’d be such distinguished guests; I thought you came from some merchants’ guild.” Upon hearing they were the king’s teacher, the innkeeper instantly became enthusiastic, having finally encountered a person of such stature. “You’ve truly come to the right place—the Sword Saint living on the snow mountain is formidable. She has helped our village overcome many crises; single‑handedly she can drive off invading monster hordes, her sword strike can shatter mountains and split the earth—she is practically a deity!”
Alfonso’s face remained expressionless. The innkeeper thought defeating monsters was impressive, but to him it was trivial—a huge gap between the outlook of the lowly and that of the exalted. “Then does that Sword Saint live alone all the time? Is there anyone else with her? For example, a child?”
“Well…” The innkeeper began to enjoy herself, putting on an air of not wanting to speak, as if any big shot who came here would be a clueless outsider, and there was no reason not to show “sincerity.”
Alfonso caught on; a flicker of disgust crossed his eyes, feeling extorted, but pressing matters prevented him from arguing with this peasant woman.
Alfonso gave his subordinate a glance; the vulture subordinate produced a few gold coins from his pocket and placed them on the table.
“If you know anything, madam, please tell us.”
“Certainly.” The innkeeper pocketed the coins, feeling them with her hand to tell real from fake, her eyebrows jumping with delight. “It doesn’t seem like just one person lives on the summit; I heard she has a child with her. This I heard over ten years ago, so the child must be grown by now.”
“!!!” Alfonso’s eyes widened at those words, his mind beginning to speculate—
“What a coincidence; everything fits together perfectly.”
“The person living on the snow mountain is probably Claudia.”
“As for the child beside her—could it be the little princess I have been searching for, Diana?”

title: Chapter 27 — The Guide
content:
Chapter 27 — The Guide

Volume 32 · Chapter 27

Alfonso's expression grew excited, and he unconsciously clenched his fist, feeling that he had finally found traces.

Many clues all pointed to the strong person living on the snowy mountain. He didn't believe there would be such a coincidence, and perhaps soon he could bring back the lost princess to the kingdom.

Alfonso decided to set off immediately tomorrow morning to see whether that mysterious Snowy Mountain Sword Saint was actually Claudia.

"However, wanting to see the Snowy Mountain Sword Saint now might be somewhat difficult." The innkeeper suddenly poured a bucket of cold water.

Why? The members of the Crimson asked in surprise.
