"Because right now the snowy mountain is in the season of continuous blizzards, and the paths up the mountain have been buried in snow. This group of outsiders wanting to climb up, I fear they will soon be trapped in a snow cave in the mountain, and they definitely won't find the Snowy Mountain Sword Saint." The innkeeper clearly pointed out the difficulty, and the winter snowy mountain is dangerous, this group of native locals knows best.

Alfonso thought that with his own strength, the harsh environment is not a problem, but he was a bit worried about attracting other people's attention. If he accidentally alarmed the swordsman on the snowy mountain, it would be more trouble than it's worth.

Except... the innkeeper suddenly changed the subject, but refused to say the rest of the sentence.

The members of the Crimson instantly saw through the other's intention, and threw out a few more gold coins again, "You really are a person who is insatiable. We shouldn't have chosen to settle down here."

"Don't say that, just now was the fee for probing information, now it's the introduction fee." The innkeeper happily collected the money and seriously said, "If you all insist on choosing this period to climb the snowy mountain, then you need an experienced guide, to prevent getting lost in the snowy mountain, this is very important. Anyone who doesn't believe in evil, outsiders without a guide leading the way, as far as I know, none of them came back alive."

"Could it be that you have a good guide to introduce to us?" The members of the Crimson asked tentatively.

"Certainly. The old cowherd Nick, no one knows the snowy mountain better than him. He was born on the mountain, the snowy mountain is as familiar to him as his own home. If you find him as a guide, you will definitely not get lost in the snowy mountain. Even if you encounter danger, he has rich experience to let you survive in the snowy mountain." The innkeeper confidently recommended a guide.

"Old Nick..." Alfonso fell into thought, deciding to temporarily hire this person to secretly take him up the mountain. If the Snowy Mountain Sword Saint really was Claudia, then she would have a hard time taking flight!

In the inn, the dim lights flickered, and a huge shadow enveloped an old man's face.

Old Nick was forcibly dragged over in the middle of the night by Alfonso's assassins, facing a group of people who looked ferocious.

He was extremely uneasy in his heart, sitting stiffly on the chair, trembling all over, not daring to lift his head, only daring to glance at this group of black-clothed people with his peripheral vision.

Old Nick was born on the snowy mountain as a herdsman. Since he was young, he has lived here, and is very familiar with every blade of grass and tree. Later, when merchants found him to be a guide, he gradually gave up his original life.

This person loves this land from the bottom of his heart. Even if he doesn't herd anymore now, he will raise yaks at home. These creatures that live in cold regions have alertness that humans don't have. Following them, one can survive even in the most dangerous extreme cold regions, and can be called spirits in the snowy mountain.

"Are you Old Nick?" Alfonso asked coldly.

Old Nick nodded nervously, not knowing what these people were doing, or why they forcibly brought him over.

"Can you take us mountain climbing tomorrow morning, no problem?" Alfonso said expressionlessly.

"Mountain climbing? No, no!" Old Nick was frightened pale, shaking his head repeatedly, refusing, "Now is the season of frequent blizzards, climbing the mountain would be courting death. At the very least, we have to wait until the spring season, until the blizzards stop."

"I heard you aren't the most experienced guide here? Taking us up the mountain shouldn't be difficult, right?" Alfonso asked doubtfully.

"The blizzard will bewilder our eyes. Even yaks sometimes get the direction wrong. The snowy mountain in winter is like a hell filled with evil spirits. Even with rich experience, there are many dangers. This group of outsiders really doesn't know how terrible the blizzard is." Old Nick opened his eyes wide, hoping these outsiders would give up the dangerous idea.

"We aren't people with fragile constitutions. The blizzard isn't much of a threat. We just need a pathfinder." Alfonso saw through this. This elderly guide was treating them as ordinary people. In fact, Old Nick should be more concerned about his own safety.

"Absolutely not! Climbing the mountain forcibly during the blizzard season is disrespectful to the mountain god, and will be severely punished. Those who anger the mountain god won't have a good ending." Old Nick shook his head frantically, muttering in his mouth.

The members of the Crimson immediately threw a heavy black bag at Old Nick, coldly saying, "Is this enough to appease the mountain god's anger?"

Old Nick was suddenly stunned. He carefully untied the black bag, and immediately his eyes, dazzled by the golden light, could barely keep open. A whole bag of gold, he had never seen so much money in his life.

Thus Old Nick went through a bout of ideological struggle, deciding to take the risk. He immediately changed his mouth and said.

"Oh~ My goodness, gentlemen are the most generous people I've seen in my life. Even the richest merchants can't compare to your high responsibility. Although the mountain god has a bad temper, he won't reject generous clients."

The next morning, Alfonso and the other assassins were already ready. They had sharpened their sharp knives until they gleamed coldly, looking like they were going to have a fierce battle.

To please these generous clients, Old Nick also brought out his beloved herd of yaks to carry the assassins' luggage. To be able to survive in the mountain amidst the raging blizzard, these spirits from the snowy mountain are indispensable.

Fortunately, when they got up early, the blizzard had temporarily subsided, not as fierce as yesterday, and the main body of the snowy mountain was almost visible.

Seeing this situation, Old Nick thought it was the mountain god blessing him, a good omen. So he knelt on the ground immediately, kowtowing continuously towards the majestic snowy mountain.

The assassins heard faint sounds of mockery, as if they saw ignorant monkeys. There wasn't anyone among them with strength below the high tier. The raging blizzard was just like powerful hail. Although in the eyes of ordinary people, it's completely not the same thing.

After Old Nick finished kowtowing, he handed his cowhide wine pouch to Alfonso, flatteringly saying, "Sir, have a sip. It's cold on the snowy mountain, and this liquor can warm the body."

Alfonso unconsciously took the wine pouch, looking at the black bottle mouth, and showed a few parts of distaste and disgust, feeling that this dirty pouch contains inferior wine. How can I touch such a thing?

Alfonso, as a black dragon priest, although still in human form, has inherited some of Nidhogg's power. His character has long been influenced, approaching infinitely the true dragon, the proud and inflated dragon. How could he drink water offered by rats?

"Sir, don't you know what you're doing on the snowy mountain? You don't look like a merchant." Old Nick curiously inquired.

"You want to see her? Of course it's fine. The Snowy Mountain Sword Saint is my恩师 (mentor/master). Every time I feel tired from climbing the mountain, I'll go to her place to rest. The Snowy Mountain Sword Saint is like the daughter of the mountain god, kind and beautiful."

"Kind and beautiful?" Alfonso let out a scoff.

"However, the Snowy Mountain Sword Saint doesn't like strangers. Do you know her? If you don't know her, you'll definitely get beaten out. At that time, I won't be able to help."

Old Nick stated the ugly words beforehand.

"If I haven't mistaken the person, we certainly know her." Alfonso gazed at the snowy mountain with deep meaning.

"Still very familiar old friends..."

title: Chapter 28 — Attack
content:
Chapter 28 — Attack

Volume 32 · Chapter 28

The vast Great Snow Mountain, white snow and ice, thick accumulated snow wrapping the mountain body.

Stepping down with one foot, the snow is deep enough to submerge the knees, and the bone-chilling cold immediately spreads throughout the body.

Although the fierce blizzard has stopped, the piercing cold wind still blows like a knife, bringing piercing pain.

A team of horses and men marches in line, constantly heading toward the mountain peak. Their steps are laborious, the snow hinders their progress, and they follow several yaks carrying luggage, stepping on hoof prints as they advance.

The assassination team members underestimated the harsh environment of the Snow Mountain. Even though they possess martial arts skills and their constitution is several times stronger than ordinary people, they still feel the terror of the cold. Many are beginning to breathe heavily, and this is only the beginning. If another blizzard comes, they probably won't be able to take another step.

Old Nick leads the foremost yak, his wrinkled face red as he gulps down a mouthful of strong liquor, feeling refreshed all over. Seeing the group of ignorant foreigners behind him, he feels a sense of satisfaction in his heart. Now do they know how terrible the winter Snow Mountain is?

Although most of the assassination team members feel embarrassed, Alfonso and the elders remain composed and unperturbed. The thick snow cannot hinder their steps at all.

"Gentlemen, put in more effort! Although the Mountain God has specially stopped the blizzard for us, He won't protect us for long. Look at the clouds in the sky; the blizzard will continue to attack at midnight. If we are lucky, we can reach the Snow Mountain Sword Saint's residence by evening, and spend the night there," Old Nick says, leading the yak. "Although the Snow Mountain Sword Saint is a kind and beautiful lady, she has never liked being disturbed. If you don't want to freeze to death in the blizzard, when you see her, definitely don't provoke her. Even if you are her friends, she will drive us out."

Alfonso has a cold face and doesn't take these words to heart. He only wants to find out if the Snow Mountain Sword Saint is Claudia.

"There are some fierce snowmen living on the Snow Mountain. They often come down the mountain after a blizzard to forage for food. Everyone must not make loud noises, otherwise they might attract these monsters. Who knows, they might eat us," Old Nick kindly reminds, continuing, "This group of snowmen has always lived deep in the Snow Mountain. But during winter, when they can't find food, they often come out to attack humans. They have bodies with boundless strength, and sharp claws that can easily disembowel a person. I have personally seen a Saint-tier powerhouse in a caravan being torn apart alive by snowmen. Everyone, be very careful."

Alfonso couldn't help but frown, thinking, Snowmen? Magical beasts living in the Snow Mountain? Rumors say it has the seeds of a watermelon and the mouth of a griffin...

Just as Old Nick had finished speaking, a member of the assassination team at the end of the line accidentally slips, nearly losing his footing and falling off the cliff. His luggage falls with him, clattering as it lands at the bottom of the cliff.

Although this sound is not loud in normal circumstances, in the snow mountains surrounding on all sides, it is like a sudden clap of thunder!

"What are you doing?" Old Nick is frightened, sweat pouring from his head. He turns around and whispers, "I told you to be quiet. Such a loud noise will attract the snowmen."

The member who slipped has a pale face, trembling and explaining, "Adult, it wasn't intentional!"

Alfonso closes his eyes helplessly, feeling some regret in his heart for bringing so many people up the mountain. Coming alone would have been completely fine. Having more people is just a burden, but the assassination team are all disciples I personally cultivated, so it's not to the point of mass slaughter over this.

Suddenly, a series of footsteps are heard around them, treading on the snow with a creaking sound, the speed is not normal, as if some flying beast is approaching in the mountain.

Old Nick perks up his ears and listens, his face instantly changing. "The sound is of snowmen! They have discovered us!"

Dozens of snowmen, exuding hungry roars, appear in everyone's vision——

They are over two meters tall, their bodies covered in white fur, their strong arms thicker than their legs, black nails in their hands like knives, deeply embedded in the rock walls.

At first glance, this group of snowmen resembles monkeys, but they are staring at a black human face, their hungry eyes constantly scanning the outsiders from the Snow Mountain.

The assassination team members stand ready, each brandishing their weapons, preparing for a fierce battle. Having received special training, they are not afraid at all of magical beast attacks.

The grim snowmen climb on the rock walls, their agile silhouettes seemingly proclaiming that they are the masters here. Soon, they quickly approach this group of outsiders from all directions.

In the eyes of these snowmen, humans are just slightly more troublesome tofu residue. As long as they lightly scratch with their claws, they can crush them.

In a critical moment, Old Nick is so frightened that his mind goes blank, directly hiding behind the yak, praying to escape a calamity.

Alfonso frowns, suddenly opening his eyes wide, a powerful dragon's might radiating out. "Disappear, beasts emitting a stench!"

This unique dragon's might is different from others, like a monarch standing at the top of the dragon race. Even if six true dragons were present, they would be driven away by fear.

The approaching snowmen stop one by one under the dragon's might, feeling the threat of death. Instinctively, they scatter and flee. Even if they are hungry, they have no courage to capture a powerful giant dragon.

Old Nick climbs out from behind the yak, looks at Alfonso, then at the fleeing snowmen, and an inexplicable ominous feeling surges in his heart.

Using just eyes to frighten magical beasts, even the Snow Mountain Sword Saint cannot do this. Is this really her old friend?

"Clack"

Claudia chops wood with an axe, splitting it into two halves. It's already getting close to the evening, and the warm light gradually fades. The blizzard begins to brew again.

A double-colored bald vulture perched on a stick nearby, leisurely using its beak to peck at insects on its body.

Claudia leans on the axe head, taking a brief rest. Her thoughts involuntarily drift to Alice...

How is that dead girl now? The Snow Mountain in winter has no caravans passing by. I know nothing about recent events in the outside world.

Perhaps I have already forgotten me, this teacher? Every day mixing with that blond smelly man, it's enough to make me furious! Why does it feel like the cabbage I laboriously raised has been dug away by a thief?

If I hadn't bumped into Alfonso, I could have walked around outside more. I really want to bring Chris back to keep me company. How detestable!

Claudia clenches her fists, feeling frustrated in her mind, her head full of thoughts of the lonely old person being abandoned. She desperately wants to catch Alice right away to teach her a lesson.

"Gulu!" The double-colored bald vulture suddenly calls out, flapping its wings, as if saying something?

Claudia looks up in confusion, gazing at the mountain pass. She is surprised. People would come up the mountain in this season? Who is it?

As a large number of shadows slowly appear in the wind and snow, they are dressed in black, leading yaks, and slowly approaching the small wooden house...

Is it a caravan?

Wait! This attire

Is the assassination team cultivated by Alfonso!

title: Chapter 29 — Queen's Death (Monthly Bonus)
content:
Chapter 29 — Queen's Death (Monthly Bonus)

Volume 32 · Chapter 29

Claudia's eyebrows suddenly knitted together; she hadn't expected Alfonso's lackeys to find her here. Obviously, when she was fleeing, she had done everything to avoid leaving any trace, yet she was still discovered. The summit of the great snow mountain was a natural hiding place, almost isolated from the world; could living here still be found? Claudia couldn't imagine how extensive Alfonso's intelligence network was; after maintaining this secret residence for so long, it was ultimately exposed to Alfonso's view. Old Nick led the yak, unaware of her, and didn't realize she had led the wolf pack to her benefactor's presence, still enthusiastically greeting, "How have you been lately? They said you're an old friend wanting to see you, so I brought them here." Claudia forced a stiff smile, not knowing what to say—old friend? Indeed an old friend, the kind she'd dreamed of putting to death. Seeing Claudia, Alfonso was already trembling with excitement, meaning they were only one step away from finding Princess Diana. Alfonso stepped forward, rudely shoving Old Nick aside, showing no respect whatsoever. Old Nick plopped onto the snow, bewildered, lifting his head, full of doubt, feeling that the man who had been polite before now turned sinister? After finding Claudia, Old Nick was worthless, an ant that could be killed at any moment. Alfonso removed his heavy hood, revealing his face; his signature dark circles grew even more grim. "Claudia, long time no see," Alfonso said. Claudia uttered the name of the man who could wake her from her dreams; just a glance exchanged, and it felt as if they were thrown back to the night of the palace coup twenty years ago. Alfonso still looked youthful, his whole body emanating an uncomfortable gloomy aura. Yet Claudia had aged considerably—besides the marks of time, she also exuded the mystery of a sword sheathed. Claudia's eye twitched; she struggled to suppress her tumultuous emotions. At this close distance, she knew her twenty-plus years of flight had ended today. Their gazes locked, and even onlookers felt the overwhelming hostility; a dangerous atmosphere spread— the assassination squad members retreated one after another, knowing they were no match for the palace sword saint; only Alfonso possessed the strength to oppose her. Old Nick stood up dazedly; even though he was a guide who knew little, he still sensed the thick smell of gunpowder, wondering if he'd done something terrible—this certainly wasn't how old friends meet, but rather like mortal enemies! Driven by survival instinct, Old Nick had to abandon his yak, slipping away silently, hoping to leave quickly. Among those present, only Old Nick was an ordinary person; no one paid attention to his comings and goings. After finding Claudia, he had passively "completed" "Over twenty years have passed since you left Spain; I never imagined we'd meet again after such a long time," Alfonso sighed. "Yeah, I'm just a knight who served Queen Josephine; to have you miss me so much, I don't know if that's an honor," Claudia said meaningfully. "You're not an ordinary knight; you're the kingdom's strongest swordsman, the object of admiration for all knights. With a mere wave of your arm, countless warriors would follow you. The old king trusted you greatly, which is why he assigned you to protect his beloved woman," Alfonso said, smiling as he recalled past events. "How ridiculous—who is this 'most beloved' person? If the king had any affection for the queen, he wouldn't let you run wild!" Claudia's face could no longer contain her anger; she gritted her teeth and said, "You were nothing but a starving astrologer on the roadside! A complete fraud! Don't forget, it was the queen's charity that gave you food to survive, and she even recommended you to the king when you had nowhere else to turn!" "I haven't forgotten that beautiful woman; she was so kind that I can never forget her. In my life I've never seen anyone as perfect as Queen Josephine—so perfect that I wanted to ruin her with my own hands. I still remember that night of the palace coup, when I personally plunged a dagger into her heart. At that moment, the queen's expression was utter surprise, as if she never imagined I would betray her—such a foolish woman who trusted others so easily, truly amusing~" Alfonso's smile gradually turned evil, as if deliberately displaying his glorious deeds; he didn't see it as shameful, but rather felt he had relied on his ability to reach where he is today. "Claudia clenched her fists, her eyes twitching wildly, driven to the limit by Alfonso's provocation. "I shouldn't have laughed so obviously, sorry," Alfonso said, covering his mouth with his hand to hide his grin, then withdrawing his smile. "Queen Josephine was merely one of the people I used; she was a stepping stone on my climb to the pinnacle of power. Aside from her excessive kindness, I hold no extra feelings toward her. This isn't my fault; it's the nature of kind people to become food—if I don't eat them, someone else will, so she should thank me for not letting her suffer more before death." "Nonsense!" Claudia gestured, and a sword as clear as autumn water flew out from the house. Under Alfonso's provocation, she entertained the thought of mutual destruction—she wanted to settle all grudges on the snow mountain. Claudia knew Alfonso's strength; if she could defeat him she wouldn't have fled for so many years, so mutual destruction was the best outcome, and she absolutely must not let him see Alice. "Oh? You're still just as explosive as before—set off with a single spark, too easily impulsive," Alfonso said, shaking his head with a smile, defending himself. "I know you hate me intensely, but the order came from His Majesty the King; he wanted Queen Josephine removed, and I was merely carrying out the command." "Back then the King was already old and somewhat muddled, and you was his most trusted person; without a doubt, you bewitched the King! Even that three‑year drought was surely your doing!" Claudia had long suspected the truth of those past events. "Haha, that three‑year drought—recalling it still feels fresh; countless died, the whole kingdom was on the verge of collapsing under the scorching sun—but this wasn't my doing. With my power I couldn't create a disaster of that magnitude; the three‑year drought was a genuine natural disaster. I admit I called Queen Josephine a cursed witch who brought disaster—" Alfonso reminisced, then suddenly flashed a playful grin and shouted— "Yet just seven days after I killed Queen Josephine, the kingdom received sweet rain!" "What does that prove?" "It's heaven's will! Killing the beautiful queen! Not me"

title: Chapter 30 — Breath as Sword
content:
Chapter 30 — Breath as Sword

Volume 32 · Chapter 30

"So many years, your lying personality hasn't changed at all, Claudia. Alfonso certainly doesn't believe Alphonso's words, this guy who originally sneaked into the court by cheating and deceiving, it seems he's never told the truth, constantly using lies to achieve his own desires, using his life-saving benefactor..."

"Shame? What is shame?" Alfonso paused, smiling and asking, "You—definitely haven't experienced the feeling of almost starving to death, have I? I've lived since childhood in the slums, every day thinking about how to survive. During the day, I'm rummaging through leftover food in the garbage dump, or going to steal things. At night, I have to pull clients for those heavily made-up women, and when I get home, I get beaten by my drunk and tipsy father. It's practically a hellish life. If I felt shame, I simply couldn't survive in the slums. Someone like Queen Josephine would have been eaten long ago, not even leaving bone fragments."

"Claudia saw the intense hatred in Alfonso's eyes. What kind of environment could produce such a purely malicious creature devoid of humanity?"

"I was very envious of those people who had tens of thousands of coins when I was young. It seemed everyone would be kind to them, always showing flattering smiles. I didn't want everyone to be full of malice toward me. Seeing me was like seeing a cockroach, everyone wanting to step on me to death with their feet. I dreamed of changing all this, becoming a person who played with others' lives, and repaying the torture I received tenfold to others."

"Alfonso spread his arms, radiating dragon might. 'Now I've done it. After Queen Josephine died half a year ago, King His Majesty also passed away. I brought the youngest prince to the throne, and as the prince's teacher until he comes of age, I'm holding the entire kingdom's fate in my hands. Look, Claudia, this is a height you can never reach.'"

"In my eyes, you're just a rat from the sewers. Even if you fly up to the sky, you're still just a bat confined in the darkness." Claudia's calm evaluation: No matter how noble Alfonso's status is, she cannot shake off the identity of a despicable thief in her heart."

Alfonso's face suddenly darkened, his faint self-esteem severely stabbed. "So many years haven't seen each other. I originally wanted to chat nicely with you as a friend, but it seems you don't give me a chance."

"You're not worthy." Claudia said coldly.

"Where is Diana? I must find her." Alfonso gave up on communicating with Claudia.

Suddenly, a fierce cold wind rose up. Claudia drew the Autumn Water sword, and with a speed that left no time to cover one's ears, she stabbed toward Alfonso. Today, someone must forever lie here!"

A black, wide law barrier instantly formed in front of Alfonso, warding off Claudia's stab, making it impossible for the sword blade to advance even a millimeter. He laughed out loud, "Hahaha, how much do you hate me? Are you dreaming of killing me every day?"

"Since the moment you betrayed the Queen, I've constantly been thinking about how to kill you. Not just in dreams, but wanting you to pay the price in blood every moment!" The holy-rank battle aura and magic power on Claudia's body forcibly pushed the sword blade in a few points!

"I've always appreciated your clear-cut likes and dislikes, like a warm hearth, always attracting others. However, back then you couldn't defeat me, you could only flee miserably everywhere. Now you still can't defeat me. Actually, I really want to give you a way out, as long as you obediently hand over Diana."

Alfonso said softly, whether to kill Claudia wasn't important, finding Diana was the most critical thing.

"Dream on, I won't tell you any news about Diana. I've long planned to bring all secrets to the grave."

Claudia's Autumn Water sword flickered with chilling light, and once again thrust forward, already approaching Alfonso's heart position.

Watching the magic barrier gradually develop cracks, Alfonso's face darkened, and he said sinisterly, "Since you want to die so much, I can send you on your way this time. This time, you won't luckily slip away from my hands like over twenty years ago."

As the voice fell, the dangerously fragile magic barrier was detonated, the strong impact forcing Claudia back over ten steps before barely stopping, making it hard to approach Alfonso.

Black mist rose in waves, dispersing the drifting wind and snow. Alfonso's body grew dense black scales, his scarlet sharp eyes exuding fierce killing intent. The pseudo-god level dragon might had a terrifying oppressive force. Those assassination team members far away didn't dare breathe.

Claudia watched Alfonso's changes, thinking that this eerie pressure was far higher than a dragon's pressure, simply not an existence of another dimension!

Alfonso's gaze condensed, and with a wave of his arm, a surge of black flames rose up, dispersing the thick clouds in the sky, making the impending blizzard disappear without a trace.

As the circles gradually shrank, the black flames also quickly gathered and condensed, gradually forming— a line that couldn't be seen with the naked eye, condensing and guarding fire elements. This control over magic power had already reached a terrifying level!

Alfonso lightly waved his finger a few times, the golden ice wheel collapsed directly, and a large amount of white ice chips poured down.

"Give up, Claudia, no matter how hard you try it's useless. Why don't you tell me Diana's whereabouts? Maybe you can suffer less in death."

"Dream on!" Claudia's Autumn Water sword hooked out flower-like sword patterns, and a large amount of golden fusion ice crystals surged forth. A wave of her hand created a hundred infinitely extending golden ice cavalry spears.

Thump, thump, thump. The golden ice cavalry spears kept inserting into the ground, forming a lush ice forest in a short time.

A wave of her arm, Alfonso turned the large area of ice spear forest into flat ground, his face gradually becoming ugly.

"You're looking for..."

Alfonso waved the focused flame thread in his hand, its length suddenly increasing several times, lightning-like threads pressing toward Claudia's throat!

In her extremity, Claudia's finger seals changed again. She suddenly inhaled, and immediately a metallic clashing sound came from her mouth. Countless sword shadows hidden in her breath shot out!

The air sword occasionally flashed chilling light, and its power was enormous, simply like a tsunami composed of knives and swords, cutting the focused flame thread into pieces, surging straight toward Alfonso.

Huh! ? "Alfonso was startled, never having seen such a bizarre technique. It wasn't battle aura and magic power at all, it seemed like...

This move "Exhaling as a sword" is one that Claudia once learned from a mysterious Eastern master. It's not magic or martial arts, but—

Sorcery.

title: Chapter 31 — Shattering the Chains
content:
Chapter 31 — Shattering the Chains

Volume 32 · Chapter 31

Claudia used her breath as a sword, instantly creating air currents like giant waves. Countless air swords emitted a vibrating sound, aggressively attacking Alfonso.

Alfonso frowned, seeing that wherever the air currents passed, the ground was riddled with numerous sliced cracks. Even these air swords were incredibly sharp!

Having followed that mysterious Eastern elder, Claudia had not learned many secret arts and had only mastered the basics of breathing and respiration. She had seen that Eastern elder use breath as a sword, and his power was far greater than hers—he could blow several great mountains into ash with a single breath!

However, being able to perform the immortal art of using breath as a sword through self-study made Claudia something of a genius. The secret methods of respiration had long been integrated into her Snowy Mountain Sword Technique. The three sword moves used by Alice were perfected sword skills that faintly bore the shadow of Eastern secret arts.

As the breath-swords attacked, Alfonso was caught within the air currents. Invisible air swords continuously struck his body, and in the blink of an eye, numerous shocking wounds appeared. His thigh was pierced, and blood flowed all over the ground.

Seeing Alfonso show signs of decline, kneeling on one knee and being frantically tortured by the vortex, the members of the assassination squad couldn't help but feel worried. Could Alfonso actually lose to a fleeing Court Sword Saint?

"Claudia, do you think you can defeat me with these eerie tricks? You must be dreaming!"

Alfonso gritted his teeth, enduring the damage brought by the air swords, and extended pitch-black dragon wings from his back!

With a violent vibration, he whipped up a storm of black flames, blasting away all the air swords Claudia had blown out!

Claudia was knocked back, large areas of her body scorched by the flames, hissing with burns.

She felt immense pressure; the opponent's strength was far above her own, and she couldn't gain the slightest advantage!

Alfonso vibrated his dragon wings and soared into the air. Flames ignited in both hands as he sneered and unleashed a violent bombardment upon Claudia!

A large number of pitch-black fireballs emitted heat waves; as if they had eyes, they chased Claudia and detonated.

A series of whistling sounds rang out. The aftershocks of the explosions made the entire great snowy mountain shake. Alfonso's subordinates watching from the sidelines were in a panic, feeling that this place could vanish from the map at any moment!

Claudia's figure was agile, layers of golden ice crystals forming beneath her feet. She was as flexible as a fox amidst the artillery fire, but Alfonso's flame bombardment was too fierce; even a tiny gap would be affected.

A pitch-black fireball traced an eerie line and struck Claudia squarely in the abdomen. Before she could react, the fire element collided violently. With a loud boom, the exploding flames engulfed her figure.

Alfonso stopped his attack and floated in the air, saying with a smile, "Now you've tasted the bitterness, haven't you? If you realize that the gap between us is insurmountable, then obediently tell me Diana's whereabouts, otherwise I will stop showing mercy."

As the flames dissipated, half of Claudia's face was unrecognizable, and half of her body had been consumed by the flames, becoming charred. She used her sword to support her body, kneeling on the ground motionless.

"I... won't tell you."

"Don't resist, you have already lost."

Alfonso flicked his fingers. Invisible threads had long since been tied to Claudia, holding her life completely in his hand.

This thread, formed from focused flames, connected from Alfonso's hand all the way to Claudia's chest, as if it had pierced into her body and bound her heart.

With a single thought from Alfonso, the flame thread would burn Claudia's heart to ashes. This was a situation of certain death!

"Stop stubbornly holding on, Claudia. If you don't want to feel the pain of your heart being scorched, then tell me Diana's whereabouts. Perhaps I will leave you a path to live."

Claudia saw an inconspicuous thread extending from her heart and realized her life was in Alfonso's hands.

"The fire will burn your heart first, then spread through your entire body, and finally, even your bones will turn to ash. This way of dying is painful no matter how you look at it, so obediently submit to me," Alfonso said in a low voice. His voice seemed to possess a certain magic, continuously eroding Claudia's will.

Claudia gritted her teeth. She had long expected this situation and had reached a resolution. "I will not submit to you, even if I die."

Alfonso's expression suddenly darkened. He said coldly, "You really haven't changed a bit, just as stubborn as before. Perhaps only pain will make you change your mind?"

As soon as he finished speaking, black flames traveled along the invisible thread, spreading into the interior of Claudia's body and beginning to frantically burn her heart!

Claudia's pupils contracted, and her delicate body shuddered. A heart-wrenching pain surged from her heart, causing her to collapse on the ground and convulse.

Claudia was drenched in cold sweat. The intense pain distorted her features. She clutched her chest tightly but was powerless; this invisible flame thread could not be cut!

"It's very painful, isn't it? Then tell me Diana's whereabouts, and I will immediately stop your torture. Is that child really worth you risking your life for?" Alfonso asked in confusion.

"She is..." Claudia endured the burning of her heart, nearly crushing her own teeth.

"Diana is the consort's child, not yours. Why are you so obsessed?" Alfonso frowned, his patience nearly exhausted.

"I am... a knight! I swore to protect Consort Josephine," Claudia lay on the ground, her voice becoming smaller and smaller. "I failed to protect her... I feel great guilt... I must protect Diana."

"Foolish thought, feeling guilt for a dead person." Alfonso snorted coldly, sneering at the so-called knightly spirit.

"I... raised Diana. She is my child. I will absolutely not let her suffer..." Claudia gritted her teeth and looked up, saying wretchedly, "Don't think everyone... is like you."

"You brought this on yourself, Claudia." Alfonso's gaze condensed, and the intensity of the flames burning her heart suddenly increased. Although he didn't intend to kill Claudia before obtaining Diana's whereabouts, he didn't mind torturing her viciously.

Claudia immediately let out bursts of wailing; the pain of her burning heart had become unbearable.

Despite being supposedly powerless to resist, she relied on her will to stand up once more.

Claudia's face was grim. She stood with her head lowered in the blizzard, looking like a dead person.

"Hmm?" Alfonso felt somewhat surprised. Logically, no one should be able to stand up while their heart was being burned.

Claudia released her Saint-tier shackles, unleashing her entire potential at this moment.

Golden battle qi and magic overflowed from her body, the color gradually dimming toward transparency, like a transparent torch in the dark night, exceptionally dazzling. The blizzard behind her became even more violent!

Claudia's pressure climbed rapidly. In just a few blinks of an eye, her power surged unstoppably, pressing straight toward the realm of a Pseudo-God!

"What the hell is this?" Alfonso's expression became horrified, unable to comprehend Claudia's condition—

Someone who was originally at the peak of the Saint-tier had their strength expand rapidly, crossing an entire major level?

This was simply impossible!

PS:

Don't misunderstand, we won't tell a story that blends East and West, because that doesn't fit the preference of most readers. Many come here for fantasy. If I suddenly pull out an Eastern map, the content volume would be too large, and the elements wouldn't blend well, so I won't write it that way. The mysterious East is just to flesh out the world-building and form a complete map.

Right now I just want to fill the holes and finish. The world-building is already quite complete and doesn't need further expansion; it just indicates that a communication channel similar to the Silk Road exists. There is no intention of having Guan Yu fight Qin Qiong.

It seems everyone is very afraid that I'll keep digging new holes. Where are there new holes now? I'm just filling old ones. I have no need to dig new holes; the pressure of filling them is already very high.

Also, it's the beginning of the month, so I'm asking everyone for some monthly tickets. There will be extra updates shortly.

title: Chapter 32 — Skeletal Obsession (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 32 — Skeletal Obsession (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 32 · Chapter 32

Claudia's oppressive pressure rapidly rose, magic and battle aura raging, forming a blizzard fiercer than that of the great snow mountain. Claudia, who had abandoned suppressing her power, completely broke through the Saint-tier shackles, her strength increasing at a visible speed, like a person shedding a heavy burden and running even more fiercely! This is a unique use of power, a secret known to very few; sometimes layers of power restriction are not a bad thing, but rather become an aid to cultivation. By capping her strength at the Saint-tier and continually suppressing herself, constantly accumulating power, when released, her strength will rapidly rise to an astonishing degree, riding the momentum to reach a realm she dare not imagine; the more she suppresses her power, the more obvious the increase after liberation! At this moment Claudia is like a pool constantly storing water; when the barrier is broken, the long-accumulated flood will pour out, and the momentum released instantly cannot compare to the usual gradual accumulation. Claudia felt an unprecedented power; her heavy body became extraordinarily light, even Alfonso was shocked by the degree of her short-term power surge—- What method did she use? How could she raise her own strength to this extent in such a short time? "Alfonso, I will not let you threaten Diana, nor can I forgive your betrayal of Queen Josephine; I have always been thinking about how to kill you, having honed my swordsmanship for over twenty years, today finally comes the moment to verify the results!" The disheveled Claudia raised her head, lifting her Autumn Water Sword in hand, "Kill you—one sword is enough!" "Oh? You think one sword can kill me? You're dreaming!" Alfonso felt an inexplicable pressure but remained calm, hooking his own finger, "Don't forget, your life is still in my hands." "I do not fear death, but I will make you realize that you are ultimately just a rat in the sewer. Claudia adjusted her breathing, merging magic, battle aura, and breathing into one, gathering them upon the Autumn Water Sword; this will be her all-or-nothing strike. Being able to fuse three different powers, Claudia can be called the first in history; this achievement alone is enough to found a new school. Claudia's whole body was enveloped in a faint light, her Autumn Water Sword shining with a blinding radiance, the blizzard becoming even more violent. " This pressure made Alfonso sense danger and fear, hesitating whether to kill Claudia now. Claudia gave Alfonso no time to think; in her heart she only wanted to avenge Queen Josephine and let Diana forever leave the court intrigues, living happily as an ordinary person. She moved, instantly creating countless afterimages, each shadow tracing a sword flower, overlapping to form a kaleidoscopic sight before Alfonso's eyes! Claudia's all-or-nothing move had only one chance to succeed in killing Alfonso; their life-and-death clash would be decided in the blink of an eye. Hand signs continuously changed, step after step, lotus blossoms forming underfoot; Claudia's each step left behind a sparkling, crystal-clear ice lotus, the three different powers perfectly fused in her hand. Each step brought her closer to Alfonso, their distance seeming nonexistent; after seven steps would be a throat-sealing killing strike! Alfonso unconsciously broke into a cold sweat, his eyes twitched, feeling Claudia's footwork terrifying—not like she was walking toward him, but as if he were being drawn to her, the vast ground seeming to shrink to a fingertip! When Claudia reached her sixth step, the blade of the Autumn Water Sword was only a step away from Alfonso, Alfonso finally lost his composure, shouting in panic— "This is your doing, Claudia!!!" Invisible flame threads ignited instantly, burning Claudia's heart to ashes! Even her body suffered damage; black flames erupted from within, engulfing Claudia's body, leaving only a charred skeleton. Claudia's blackened skeleton still held its pose, wanting to finish the seventh step and seal Alfonso's throat with one sword—it seemed there was no chance left; her soul and consciousness had already turned to ash. Alfonso drenched in cold sweat, gasping heavily to calm his terrified heart, looking at Claudia's sword-wielding skeleton, he couldn't help but burst out laughing, "Hahaha, you got what you deserved, Claudia. "This is all your own fault; if you had just obediently told me Diana's whereabouts, you might not have died." "You're still so foolish, your head full of a single stubborn thought; even if you understood a little flexibility, you wouldn't have ended up like this! "For Queen Josephine's sake, what do you gain by dying? You gain nothing! "Do you think you can protect Diana by sacrificing your life to guard Josephine's child? Can this truly make up for your past negligence? "It's utterly ridiculous! Even if you refuse to reveal Diana's whereabouts until death, I still have other ways to find her; your death is utterly worthless!" Alfonso was terrified by Claudia's recent aura, he roared wildly at the skeleton, trying to ease his fear. For a moment he felt facing that sword meant certain death! Alfonso exhaled, his fear eased, looking at Claudia's remaining blackened skeleton, he shook his head with a smile, "Not worth it; kind people ultimately become others' prey—a truth I understood since childhood." Suddenly, the already-dead Claudia, clearly nothing but a blackened skeleton, walked out the seventh step before everyone's eyes, and a final ice lotus bloomed! Seven steps to seal the throat— Unfortunately the final killing blow was not realized; the sword that should have sealed Alfonso's throat instead struck his shoulder— What the hell!!" Alfonso stared speechless, his words garbled from fright; Claudia was not some undead creature, yet after death she completed the final motion, successfully wounding him! If not witnessed firsthand, no one would believe such an unimaginable thing could happen. What immense obsession and willpower it takes to make one's dead skeleton move! Alfonso could not imagine how much hatred Claudia harbored toward him to reach this point! He kept stumbling backward, lacking any courage to approach the skeleton; suddenly a sharp pain came from his shoulder wound— Looking closely, the cold poison formed from magic, battle aura, and breathing had entered his body through the wound, relentlessly ravaging him. Alfonso's face turned deathly pale; instantly his whole body was covered in a layer of frost, his body gradually stiffening, he collapsed to the ground, shivering uncontrollably. Members of the assassination squad rushed over, seeing Alfonso's condition—clearly the cold poison had entered his body and could not be stopped. "Lord Alfonso!" "How are you, Lord?" "Lord!??" Alfonso curled his stiffened body, eyes vacant, shivering as he said, "We're cold Cold Ding ding ding, the Autumn Water Sword fell to the ground, Claudia's blackened skeleton turned to ash, drifting into the raging blizzard sky— a faint voice, as if from a soul, echoed— Alice, farewell forever,"

title: Chapter 33 — Astrologer in the Slums①
content:
Chapter 33 — Astrologer in the Slums①

Volume 32 · Chapter 33

Thirty-plus years ago, a boy from a slum called Sovito in the Kingdom of Spain, by chance, saw a black dragon, Nidhogg, that had survived from the mythic era, and his fate suddenly changed. It was a hot summer, the boy and his friends enjoyed catching dragonflies together, but he got separated from his friends and fell into a mysterious canyon, where there was a pitch-black cave—"Little brat, after Ragnarok, you are the only human I have seen; I saw hatred in your eyes, as well as the desire to grasp power." "You must hate your lowly origins and wish to change, right?" "You are a lucky little guy; if you become my servant, I will fulfill your ambition and let your power reign over all beings." Alfonso as a child stood terrified at the cave mouth, wearing ragged, dirty clothes, without even a proper pair of shoes on his feet. He was terrified, hearing the voice from the cave, wondering if he had encountered a man-eating monster? Suddenly, in the dark cave, two huge eyes lit up, scarlet narrow pupils, as if seeing into Alfonso's soul. "Ah!" young Alfonso was so frightened his soul left his body; he plopped onto the ground and scrambled away, shouting, "Monster! Man-eating monster! Who will come save me!" The giant eyes in the cave slowly closed, a faint grinding of teeth could be heard, a helpless sigh—"You will surely return." "Because you have envious eyes, you are destined to live a tragic life." "When faced with something you like but cannot obtain, you will destroy it yourself." Ten years passed, the boy grew up but never left the slum. In the strictly hierarchical Kingdom of Spain, one's birth determined many people's lives. There were almost no upward channels for the poor to escape hunger and achieve class mobility. The nobles valued wealth more than their own lives, refusing to give even a grain of food to the poor; to these exalted lords, the poor in the slums were worthless, no matter how many died, there would always be someone to enslave them, and the whole kingdom lay under an oppressive atmosphere. The slum's environment was worse than outside; it was completely different, with its own unique survival law: the weak are prey to the strong. Even children took pride in deceit and theft, not only avoiding punishment but being praised for their cleverness. Thugs and ruffians ran rampant; youths were mostly petty thugs, with no jobs, relying on scams to barely survive, forming gangs that many in the slum feared. The slum was like a giant trash can, filled with countless people willing to degenerate; almost every day something shocking happened, perhaps because they lacked the ability to change their situation, or had already adapted to sewer life. Young Alfonso, like countless other youths in the slum, became an idle gangster, swaggering with a group of youths. Having just joined the gang, Alfonso had no status; he was a newcomer, and everyone tried to squeeze some profit out of him. The gang's thugs swaggered down the street; many hurriedly lowered their heads or quickly dodged; facing demons, they lacked even the courage to raise their heads and stare straight, as if they were the masters of the entire slum. Following at the rear of the group, Alfonso couldn't help but show a hint of pride; he had found a sense of belonging in the gang—this is the slum's rule: if you don't act domineering, you will surely be bullied. Alfonso believed he would make his mark in the gang; if he became boss, a few streets would all be his—how imposing! Surely that is what it feels like to be a cut above the rest? Young Alfonso had little contact with the world outside the slum; with his limited experience, his only dream was to leave the slum and become like those nobles, able to trample on the poor at will. "Tomorrow is the time to demand protection money from these people; without us, who will guarantee their safe business? Recently the boss keeps complaining that money is getting scarcer; if this continues, I won't even be able to keep my teeth," said a fierce thug, spitting on the ground as if threatening the people on this street. "Yeah, the street is getting more unstable; if you don't pay, watch out for your business being smashed; don't wait until your rice bowl is broken before regretting!" His sidekick immediately put his hands on his hips, using his eyes to scan the street residents like a fox borrowing a tiger's might. The fierce thug frowned slightly, turned back and saw Alfonso staring blankly at an alley, "Alfonso, what are you doing? At a time like this you should be threatening these lowly wretches!" "Sorry, I suddenly have something to do; we can talk about collecting protection money tomorrow." Alfonso put on an apologetic smile; though his clothes were still ragged, at least he now had a decent pair of big leather shoes, though they looked quite old, possibly secondhand. "Huh?" the fierce thug was not pleased, but didn't press further: "Fine, you've only been in the gang a few days; anyway, don't forget to bring two silver coins tomorrow to give me." "But I already paid the membership fee," Alfonso said earnestly. "Are you an idiot? I need to bring someone like you, a newcomer, to give you a learning opportunity; it's not free—these two silver coins are tuition; you understand?" the fierce thug glared at Alfonso. Alfonso lowered his head, gave no reply, choosing to swallow his anger. After the thugs left, Alfonso alone entered the alley; at the far end was a quiet bookstall, its owner an old man wearing glasses, who seemed out of place among the savage slum residents. These books were a杂乱 collection, randomly gathered by the bookstore owner; since few in the slum could read, the owner could barely make a living. As a child, Alfonso had learned multiple languages under his mother's education; sadly his mother died of illness when he was very young, which he regretted deeply. This place was like Alfonso's secret base—quiet, mysterious, undisturbed; borrowing books here for free had become part of his life. Even the bookstall owner had grown accustomed to it, for it was rare to find someone in the slum who shared his love of reading. Alfonso came to the stall, skillfully picked up the book on astrology, and began reading it seriously. This was his recent favorite; astrology claims that by observing the stars one can glimpse many things' fates; feeling guilty about himself, he wanted to know whether his future could allow him to escape the slum; perhaps astrology could let him see the future ahead of time. The bookstall owner put down his newspaper, adjusted his glasses, and carefully looked at Alfonso: "You're here, Alfonso? You always just look and never buy; I'm about to run out of books for you to read." "I haven't found anything I particularly like yet," Alfonso defended himself. "You really like making excuses for yourself," the owner paused, then continued, "You've been really interested in astrology lately?" "Well, it says a lot about the connection between stars and fate," Alfonso started to say something interesting but swallowed it, "It looks okay, but still rather boring." "Haha, most astrology is useless; if it were useful it wouldn't have ended up in my hands; fate isn't that easy to peek at," the owner scoffed. Alfonso felt a bit disappointed; he still somewhat believed in astrology theory. "You're young; you really don't need to believe in fate or such things," the owner shook his head, "Have you joined a gang lately?" "Yeah, but I won't just bully others," Alfonso quickly emphasized. "Don't hang out with those people; they're souls already damned, beyond saving, they'll never leave the slum in this lifetime; but you're different—you might still have a chance to get out and live a better life." The owner paused, sighing, "If you had the ability, who would want to stay in such a awful place? This book is yours." Alfonso furrowed his brows, looked at the astrology book in his hand, thoughtfully lifted his head, and thought—I'm not like them? Late at night, the red-light district in the slum was especially lively, akin to the rich's backyard. With just a little money, you could sleep with a beautiful woman in the slum, which felt extremely cheap. Don't underestimate any heavily made-up woman; they are the most profitable profession here. Within the red-light district, you can witness the most extreme things: on one side, starving paupers; on the other, extravagant luxury to the point of paper‑wrapped gold and intoxication. Alfonso was a young pimp, his sole source of income; he had grown used to keeping his head low and eyes down to earn a meager commission. Tonight, Alfonso, thanks to his eloquence, successfully landed a gig, introducing two voluptuous women to a wealthy merchant, making his peers envious, all beginning to feel jealous and resentful. But when it came time to collect the commission, Alfonso was dumbfounded—only three miserable copper coins—so he hurriedly called out to the merchant. "Please wait a moment, sir." "Huh? Anything else?" the pot‑bellied merchant turned around, his left‑arm‑right‑arm embrace resembling a local emperor, forming a stark contrast with the skinny, weak Alfonso. "Your commission seems off; the market minimum is at least one silver coin, of course I'm not complaining you gave too little, but I think you're so high‑and‑mighty you certainly wouldn't begrudge a few silver coins; just consider it almsgiving for a poor wretch like me; the great goddess—will surely bless you." Alfonso slightly bowed, lowering his posture, and served up a string of flattery. Normally, customers would be restrained by dignity in front of the women and would readily pay. But tonight this customer was different; obviously he wouldn't fall for that. The merchant's face darkened, veins throbbing on his forehead, he kicked Alfonso to the ground and pointed at his nose, shouting—"A few copper coins is already my greatest charity; what more do you want?" "Surely, as a poor wretch from the slum, you'll never shake off your greedy nature." Originally I wanted to explain, but then I thought I shouldn't explain the plot arbitrarily. Doubting Claudia's death can be checked by reading several times; I've said it from the start, basically there's no problem as you all claim. Alfonso is the pursuer, strong. Claudia is the evader, aware of her weakness, and knows that mutual destruction is the best outcome. When they meet, I wrote that since Alfonso already bumped into her, escaping is impossible; at this point she can only fight desperately, running is out of the question. On the contrary, Alfonso, in order to learn Diana's whereabouts, refuses to go all‑out against Claudia, holding back against her; even if Claudia erupts from the start, she still can't win, only dying faster. If Claudia could beat Alfonso, what was the point of her fleeing for twenty years? Moreover, it's not certain Claudia lost; I haven't finished the plot yet; when I do, we'll see whether the Claudia who has honed a sword for twenty years wins or loses. All of the above is in the original; you can look back; opening with plot twists, what should I say? Don't let your fondness for the teacher character make you upset about her death and stir up drama, putting pressure on me. I am the author; I have a bottom line; facing pressure I will only conclude, never change the outline even if beaten to death. If you like the teacher character too much, I can make her non‑dead in the outline for my next book, but Claudia was designed to die from the start; that can't be changed. This is the first time I've killed a character from the protagonist's camp; before, only villains died, giving readers a different feeling. If it's too painful, I apologize, but I cannot change the outline; this is the limit; Claudia's death affects a series of later plot points, serving to reveal the first layer of Alice's background. Understanding forever!

title: Chapter 34 — Slum Astrologer 2
content:
Chapter 34 — Slum Astrologer 2

Volume 32 · Chapter 34

Alfonso was kicked to the ground by the rich merchant, and the book on astrology in his arms also fell out; he never expected to encounter such an unreasonable guest.
The surrounding young pimps saw Alfonso being punished, and instead of coming to help, they gloated from the side——
“You got slapped for sticking your nose up, huh? You totally deserved it”
“Yeah, relying on your flattery, you've stolen how much business from us?”
“He deserves a lesson; otherwise he won't learn.”
In the slums, the law of the jungle prevails; mutual help is simply a joke. They wish Alfonso would disappear at once, and stop always
here stealing our livelihood.
The rich merchant smirked, looking down on Alfonso with arrogance, showing off his power in front of the weak, which made him very pleased.
“Huh?”
Unintentionally, the merchant saw the astrology book fallen on the ground, curiously picked it up and glanced at it, his face showing a disdainful smile.
“Astrology? Someone would actually read this without a book? No way—”
“Give it back!” Alfonso sprang up from the ground, his eyes filled with hostility.
“Hahaha, you're not studying astrology to peek at fate, hoping to know if you can turn your life around, are you?” The merchant threw the astrology book like trash
onto the ground, sneering, ‘Give up, you bunch of poor ghosts living in the slums; you’ll never be able to change your fate,’
‘What would happen if a sewer rat appeared on the bustling streets? It would be beaten to death, young man.’
The two heavily made-up women beside the merchant immediately snickered; in their eyes, this young pimp was daydreaming, and besides the slums, no place would welcome people like him.
the slums, nowhere would welcome people from here.
Alfonso lowered his head, his face grim; his sole wish was trampled, and his self-esteem was sharply wounded—
However, he did not resist, because he was too humble and had no courage.
Before him stood the tall rich merchant, possessing a status he could never attain.
Resistance would only bring fierce retaliation.
That night, returning home, Alfonso faced the moment he feared most each day: confronting his alcoholic father.
Alfonso once had a complete family; although they lived in poverty, they were very harmonious.
Until his mother died, his father's temperament changed drastically, drinking to the point of utter drunkenness every day.
Whenever he was slightly displeased, his father would lash Alfonso with a belt; insults and beatings filled his entire adolescence.
Alfonso handed over the money he earned today to his father—only a pitiful three copper coins, far less than before.
The drunken father furrowed his brows, looking at the pitiful three copper coins in his hand, and demanded, ‘Just this much?’
Hmm, today's guest…
“Pa!” a crisp sound rang out; the father didn't wait for Alfonso to finish explaining, and slapped him across the face, grumbling.
“Useless thing, always making excuses for yourself! I raised you for nothing—you’re completely useless! Why did I even raise you?”
What?
Alfonso covered his swollen cheeks, stunned and unable to speak.
“You what you! Remember you owe me; now that you're this big, you should repay me! Why are you so useless?” The father gulped down several
mouthfuls of strong liquor, turned and walked toward his room, cursing, “If you can't earn even a single silver coin tomorrow, don't come back—home
has no need for a worthless person.”
The room's door was slammed shut; Alfonso lifted his head, his eyes showing no concealment of hatred, and he instinctively clenched his fists, knuckles turning white.
Late at night, returning to his room, Alfonso lingered, unwilling to sleep, holding his pen but hesitating to write a single word in his diary.
Alfonso had the habit of writing a diary to record his daily life; this was the moment of calmest mind in his day, but today's ordeal
, left him unsure how to record it.
After thinking for a long time, Alfonso, filled with disgust, wrote a sentence in his diary——
“Every inch of land in the slums exudes a filthy and ugly stench; this area, which should have disappeared, holds no value whatsoever.”
At the same moment, in the cave of the mysterious canyon, the black dragon slowly opened its eyes.
At dawn, a ray of sunlight peeked over the horizon, but the slums, which ought to have been bustling and noisy, had become eerily silent, a heavy scent of blood filling every
corner—
Only man-eating locusts were incessantly gnawing at the corpses of the poor; though each insect is tiny, their vast numbers constitute a
disaster.
Vast swarms of locusts gathered in the sky, blocking sunlight from reaching the slums, like a demonic cloud wildly dancing in the heavens.
Alfonso stood alone on the slum street, expression stiff, eyes vacant, watching the hellish scene in the slums; the man-eating locusts
seemed not to notice him, scattering away.
He didn't know what had happened; he only knew that after opening his door, everything outside had changed——
He saw his father being gnawed by the locusts down to bare bones, collapsed in a pool of blood outside the door, as if trying to wake himself?
He saw the merchant from last night, clothes disheveled, entrails devoured clean, his face still bearing the terror of his final moments.
He saw the gang's thugs lying dead in the street, and even the bookstall owner perished in the disaster; his old spectacles were shattered into countless fragments.
Alfonso stood in the bloody wind, his body gradually turning cold and shivering; each breath of the blood‑laden air made him feel waves of nausea—
A surge of despair was gnawing at his heart; last night's diary entry had been mere venting, yet it became reality—the slums had truly been utterly destroyed.
Alfonso didn't know whether this was his fault, having caused the death of that kind bookstall owner, but he thought perhaps it wasn't such a bad thing?
The entire slum turned overnight into a natural graveyard; Alfonso's wish was finally fulfilled——
He left the slums where he had lived all his life, but looking back, he saw only himself alive.
In the capital of the Spanish Kingdom, within the extraordinarily luxurious palace, a solemn investiture ceremony was being held.
The renowned court sword saint Claudia formally relinquished her post as captain of the royal guard; she no longer served the king directly, but became the exclusive knight of the beautiful
queen.
