title: Chapter 35 — The Astrologer in the Slums ③ (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 35 — The Astrologer in the Slums ③ (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 32 · Chapter 35

“I will.

Clodagh's firm response officially made her a knight of Josephine, the queen's consort, with the duty of protecting her safety as her first mission.

In the Spanish kingdom, where the gap between the rich and the poor was enormous, there were few avenues for upward mobility, and one's social class was determined at birth.

Clodagh, however, was an object of admiration for many, a kind of spiritual leader who was always chasing, because she was one of the rare people who had succeeded in rising from the common folk to the nobility, and her achievement in a kingdom with a strict class system was truly remarkable.

Clodagh's situation was similar to Alfonso's, as they were both born into poor families in the slums and spent their childhoods in poverty.

But Clodagh was far luckier than Alfonso, as her poor parents gave her everything they could, and she even met a mysterious Eastern elder who opened her path to cultivation. Even her friends were sincere and kind.

Clodagh had never felt inferior or envious of others' wealth because of her humble origins. She believed that everything could be earned with her own hands, without needing to beg for recognition from others.

Through relentless practice of her swordsmanship, challenging and learning from many swordsmanship experts, she gradually developed a swordsmanship centered on mysterious Eastern breathing techniques, becoming a Saint-tier cultivator. After defeating the king's chief knight in a duel, she gained fame and became the captain of the royal guard.

Although Clodagh was not yet ready to claim that she was the strongest swordsman in the kingdom, her strength was still among the top tier. The title "Court Sword Saint" became well-known throughout the kingdom.

Clodagh's experiences were seen by the people as a living example of an inspirational story, lighting a beacon for all the lower classes.

“Rise, brave knight.” Josephine, the queen's consort, sheathed the sword resting on Clodagh's shoulder and gently helped her up. “From today onwards, you will be with me, but you must listen to me. Being a knight is not like being the captain of the royal guard, where you can be easily angered. You must be elegant and noble.”

Clodagh smiled helplessly. She had known Josephine for a long time, not just for the first time.

In the royal guard, only she came from the slums, so even though she had climbed to her current position through her own efforts, she was still discriminated against because of her humble origins, often being called a thief from the lower class and easily angered, just to protect herself.

Josephine, the queen's consort, was curious about Clodagh from the slums and often sought her out to chat, learning many things she had never known before, and became very familiar with her.

Clodagh was well aware that Josephine was not "stupid," nor was her kindness an act. She was truly too naive, like a child who had never encountered the harshness of the outside world.

However, it was undeniable that Clodagh willingly became Josephine's knight out of genuine affection for her, as Josephine was the only one, besides the few friends in the guard, who truly wanted to understand her.

“Don't make it so serious, be happy. You should express your emotions through singing and dancing.”

“Singing and dancing, I decline.”

“A shy child, how adorable.”

“You're the one who's a child.”

Several months later, in the bustling city, Alfonso, starving and penniless, came here hoping to find more opportunities to survive.

Alfonso, who had never left the slums, was stunned by the grandeur and bustle of the city. He had never seen so many elegantly dressed gentlemen and ladies walking on the streets, as if everyone here was wealthy and there were no poor people.

Grand and beautiful buildings lined both sides, the windows of the shops were spotless, and even the tiles on the ground were neatly arranged like a work of art. Alfonso, dressed in rags, stood out and everyone unconsciously avoided him.

Alfonso was very hungry, his stomach had been growling all night, and he tried to get some relief bread from the church, but the amount was too little and he was not even eligible for it.

His eyes were fixed on a nearby bakery, watching the freshly baked bread displayed outside, his mouth watering continuously, and he could no longer hold back. Only survival could bring him a future.

Alfonso had the thought of stealing, which was nothing to him in the slums, where people survived by stealing. It was only the fault of these people for leaving their food carelessly outside, which would inevitably be stolen.

Thus, Alfonso gathered his courage and boldly walked over, seizing the opportunity when no one was looking to touch the warm bread, the warmth spreading throughout his body, and the aroma almost made him shout with excitement.

But suddenly, a hand as strong as a vice gripped Alfonso's arm, stopping him from stealing, and he unconsciously lifted his pale and terrified face to see the baker's angry expression.

“Wretched foreigner! You, a youngster, have already learned to steal?”

“I should take you to the guards and have them break your hands!”

title: Chapter 36 — The Astrologer in the Slums IV
content:
Chapter 36 — The Astrologer in the Slums IV

Volume 32 · Chapter 36

Alfonso's face turned pale with fear; looking at the baker's burly build, he knew he wasn't a match for him.

"There are always outsiders like you who don't know the rules here. If I don't teach you a lesson, you'll think the capital is just like the countryside, where you can steal whatever you please!" The baker glared viciously at Alfonso, clearly not a first-time offender.

Alfonso thought for a moment and decided to find a way to escape. If he didn't, being sent to the guard squad for interrogation would mean more than just having his hands broken—he'd be permanently banished from here.

"Respected sir, perhaps there's been a misunderstanding?"

"What misunderstanding? I've already caught you! Still looking for excuses?" The baker shouted.

"Please don't slander me. I wasn't stealing; I just wanted to see how these freshly baked bread tasted, and I have money." Alfonso said in a serious tone, looking rather pompous, like an actual guest.

"Hmm? You have money?" The baker frowned, eyeing the sickly, malnourished Alfonso with deep suspicion.

"Of course! Just because I dress shabbily, do you think I don't have money to buy bread? Treating your guests like this shows no respect at all—your shop deserves to be condemned!" Alfonso stared into the baker's eyes without a trace of fear.

The baker immediately grew nervous, glancing around to see if anyone noticed. "Oh~ Generous guest, I was too rude. I apologize for my behavior. Freshly baked bread is just two copper coins. Would you like a bag? But you'd better pay first."

Alfonso frowned, knowing full well the baker didn't believe him and wanted the money upfront before letting him take the bread.

After hesitating for a moment, Alfonso patted his chest, pretending to pull out money, but his fist was clenched tightly, hiding the true situation from the baker.

"The money is in my hand."

"Hmm?"

The baker lowered his head slightly, unsure whether Alfonso was actually holding two copper coins.

Just as he was about to ask, Alfonso suddenly attacked, jabbing two fingers from deep within his fist, striking the baker's eyes!

"Aa! You wretched country bumpkin! How dare you..." The baker frantically rubbed his throbbing eyes, tears blurring his vision.

After succeeding, Alfonso was swift-handed and sharp-eyed, snatching a few bread and stuffing them into his mouth, then turning to run. Behind him came frequent vulgar curses.

Today was the day Princess Josephine went out for a stroll, though naturally the range was limited to within the capital.

Even if she wanted to leave the capital to see the outside world, countless guards would stop her and not let her leave.

A large number of guards had cleared the streets in advance and arranged everything, warning residents not to do anything discourteous, and even brought in some extras to play residents.

All arrangements revolved around what would make the princess happy, and absolutely no dirty, reckless, or stupid person was allowed to appear in her line of sight.

The guards followed behind Princess Josephine at a distance—not too close, not too far—always on alert for emergencies.

Although Princess Josephine didn't like being stared at by a crowd whenever she went out, she had no say in it. All guards had received the king's orders not to stray too far, no matter what she said.

However, ever since Princess Josephine had her own personal knight, things had improved greatly. With Clodia's strength, most dangers could be handled, which also secretly relieved the other guards—they didn't have to be as tense as before.

Residents came out of their homes, waving at the beautiful and kind princess. Many children even gathered around, their eyes sparkling with starlight.

Though Princess Josephine was like a canary in a cage, she unexpectedly easily won the people's affection. Most people liked her and were grateful for her frequent handouts, considering her to be nearly perfect.

"Can you have the guards behind you leave? They look so fierce and might scare the residents."

"Absolutely not." Clodia immediately vetoed it, explaining, "These guards are arranged by His Majesty to protect you. They're not bad people. How can I let them leave so easily? Besides, the residents of the capital adore you—they'll understand."

"It's uncomfortable to be stared at." Princess Josephine puffed her cheeks, huffing, "Clodia, aren't you my knight? With you protecting me, it's fine. Send them back~"

Hearing the princess's pouty, acting-spoiled tone, Clodia felt a headache coming on. She kept a stern face and said, "Danger is everywhere. The more people protecting you, the better. Please stop being childish; this is very difficult for me."

"Hmph~!" Princess Josephine huffed, turning her head away, pretending to be upset. "As my knight, you should think of a solution! With you here, why do we need so many guards? Doesn't that make you look useless?"

"Ah!?" Clodia frowned, feeling very helpless about the princess's capriciousness. "That's completely different! Please understand me—stop throwing a child's tantrum."

"Hmphda~!" Princess Josephine ignored her completely, secretly watching Clodia's reaction. Seeing Clodia at a loss, she found it amusing.

Clodia's face darkened. She had to go along with the princess's temper and said softly, "I can't let them leave, but I can make them stay farther away."

"That's doable, isn't it? No wonder you're my knight—so reliable~" Princess Josephine immediately cheered up, spinning around in circles.

"Don't make things so difficult for me." Clodia sighed, feeling a bit nostalgic for her days in the guard squad, which had been much easier than being a knight.

Suddenly, Alfonso, who had stolen bread and was running around, broke into the sight of the strolling party.

Behind him, the burly baker successfully caught up to Alfonso, pinning him to the ground, where he struggled helplessly. The stolen bread fell to the ground.

Alfonso, already starving with his chest against his back, had no strength to escape the baker's pursuit and was quickly caught.

The guards encountered the emergency and rushed forward, protecting Princess Josephine in the center.

Even Clodia gripped her sword hilt, staring fixedly at Alfonso and the baker, her gaze sharp as a drawn blade.

Only Princess Josephine, because of her "dazed" nature, remained calm and collected, looking at them with curious eyes, completely unaware of what was happening?

But she found it quite novel—she had never encountered such a thing during her outings, which had always been so peaceful.

Watching the two men wrestle, Princess Josephine thought it was great—there were actually such thrilling things in the world?

The baker pressed Alfonso's head down, his eyes red and swollen, cursing viciously, "You brat! How dare you hurt me! I won't let you off today!"

"Sir, please listen to my explanation. I can apologize..." Alfonso panicked, seeing the baker's vicious face in his peripheral vision, feeling his hands were doomed.

The baker wouldn't listen to any explanation, already furious—

"Shut up!"

"You country bumpkins! Always lying! I won't believe a single word you say!"

title: Chapter 37 — The Astrologer in the Slums ⑤ (Additional Chapter for Monthly Votes)
content:
Chapter 37 — The Astrologer in the Slums ⑤ (Additional Chapter for Monthly Votes)

Volume 32 · Chapter 37

The enraged bakery owner raised his fist, ready to give this outsider a thorough beating.

Alfonso instinctively closed his eyes, already resigned to being brutally beaten. But suddenly, a stern voice rang out—

"Halt! Such crude behavior is not allowed in the presence of the noble princess!"

Claudia ordered the palace guards to immediately surround the two intruders. Their sharp spears glinted menacingly, halting the impending violence.

The bakery owner looked up in surprise. Seeing himself surrounded by guards with spears pointed at him, he quickly regained his composure, realizing the gravity of his mistake.

Thus, the burly bakery owner immediately knelt on the ground, not daring to raise his head, and began to plead his case.

"I am very sorry. My rude behavior has startled the beautiful Princess Josephine. I beg you, noble knights, to forgive my transgression."

Princess Josephine approached, accompanied by Claudia, and scrutinized the bakery owner. Curiously, she asked, "Why fight on the street? Isn't peaceful coexistence better?"

The bakery owner lowered his head hesitantly and said, "Noble princess, I know your kindness touches everyone in the city, but please hear me out. This outsider started it all. He stole my bread and refused to pay, causing me unnecessary loss. My bakery is a small business, and I cannot tolerate theft. I hope you can forgive me."

"Steal bread?" Princess Josephine curiously examined Alfonso, intrigued by this disheveled stranger.

Claudia, however, suddenly frowned. Her first impression of Alfonso was not good. Unlike the princess, she had common sense and could tell from his attire that he came from a terrible living environment.

Especially when she saw Alfonso stand up after being saved, dusting off his clothes with a clear-headed expression, showing no shame for his theft—she knew he was a criminal!

Claudia had no liking for people without a sense of honor; they were soulless husks.

Princess Josephine picked up the dirty black bread from the ground. It wasn't an expensive food item, and such fare was barely edible, meant only to stave off hunger.

"To fight over a few cheap loaves? I can't understand it. They're not valuable."

The bakery owner hesitated, thinking it wasn't about cost but theft!

Princess Josephine removed her earring from her left ear and handed it to the bakery owner without hesitation. "This should be enough to buy those loaves, right?"

Claudia stepped forward to stop her, reminding the princess that she shouldn't be kind to a thief.

"It's fine; I have plenty of pretty jewelry," Princess Josephine replied, questioning why an expensive earring should be used to buy cheap black bread.

The bakery owner hesitated, unsure if he should accept it. But the earring was made of precious purple crystal, and even a small piece could buy ten bakeries.

"What? Is it not enough?" Princess Josephine questioned.

"It's enough, enough!" The bakery owner hurriedly nodded, accepting the purple crystal earring. "Thank you, Your Highness. I will remember your generosity."

Princess Josephine picked up the bread from the ground, dusted it off, and handed it to Alfonso personally.

"Eat it; you must be very hungry."

Alfonso looked up in surprise. When he saw Princess Josephine, his eyes lit up.

He could swear that Princess Josephine was the most beautiful person he had ever seen. Her angelic smile deeply moved him.

The princess seemed to possess some kind of magic. Her inner kindness and innocence drew people in effortlessly.

Alfonso stared at the princess speechlessly, momentarily forgetting his hunger. If he hadn't seen it with his own eyes, he wouldn't believe that there were truly kind people who would help someone from the slums.

"Don't you want to eat?" Princess Josephine frowned.

Alfonso snapped back to reality, hesitated for a moment while staring at the bread in the princess's hand, then couldn't resist his hunger any longer. He rudely snatched the bread and wolfed it down, disregarding his appearance.

Princess Josephine was a bit startled. She had never seen anyone eat so fearfully and instinctively took a step back.

"Your Highness, don't get too close to this unknown person. He might be dangerous," Claudia warned, protecting the princess and not wanting her near this thief.

"It's okay. Look how pitiful he is. He looks like he hasn't eaten for days. He must be starving," Princess Josephine said sympathetically.

"Let me talk to him," Claudia volunteered, worried that the innocent princess might be swayed. "Where are you from?"

Alfonso stopped eating, hesitated, and answered, "Sovieto."

"Sovieto?" Claudia frowned instantly, recalling the recent locust disaster there. Everyone seemed to have died overnight, yet here was a survivor.

"Where is Sovieto?" Princess Josephine asked softly.

"A slum," Claudia replied, though she didn't mention its recent calamity.

"It's a slum? Isn't that where you come from?" Princess Josephine remembered Claudia's stories about life in the slums, which were far from pleasant. Few managed to leave, making her sympathize with young Alfonso.

Seeing the princess pity the thief, Claudia grew concerned. Being from the slums herself, she knew the character of those who lived there.

Lack of honor was normal; survival often pushed people to their moral limits. Not everyone could escape like Claudia did through effort and talent.

"As an outsider, you dare to steal openly here? You should be punished by imperial law!"

Alfonso was startled and quickly stood up, hiding the bread behind his back. "Honorable knight, I had no choice. If I didn't steal, I would starve. Please forgive me."

"That's no excuse for theft. With hands and feet, you could earn food through labor instead of resorting to despicable means. No excuse changes the fact that you've committed a crime!" Claudia's tone was severe, pressing Alfonso so hard he couldn't lift his head. She knew mercy was misplaced here.

Cold sweat trickled down Alfonso's forehead. He detested this female knight, especially her strict attitude, reminiscent of wealthy merchants!

"You're right. No matter what, you shouldn't steal. There seems to be a church nearby. Didn't you go there for alms bread?" Princess Josephine asked, puzzled.

"Noble lady, I'm poor and weak, and an outsider. I can't receive alms bread. Please understand," Alfonso replied sadly.

Princess Josephine thought for a moment and said earnestly, "If you can't get bread, why not eat a more luxurious cake instead?"

Claudia: "!!!"

Alfonso: "???"

The recent content is actually an Alice side story, originally planned for over forty episodes but heavily cut and compressed into eight.

Normally, there would be many more characters and internal stories within the Spanish kingdom.

After the massive cuts, only three characters are focused on, and even then, only key representative events are described. The old Spanish king doesn't even deserve a name.

In this tiny space, I'm trying to portray three characters. Readers previously knew little about Alfonso and Claudia beyond their names and rough identities. Princess Josephine fared even worse, existing mostly in paintings and dialogues.

Since these three characters relate to Alice, completing their stories fills in much of Alice's background.

I mentioned writing two side stories before; this is one of them, now condensed into eight episodes.

The princess character has historical references. Those who recognize them will see the original, while others can enjoy the story as is. This is a shortcut due to limited space, allowing historical figures to be described more vividly without wasting too much ink.

This plot concludes tomorrow. Forty-plus episodes condensed into eight—it's moving quickly.

title: Chapter 38 — The Astrologer in the Slums ⑥
content:
Chapter 38 — The Astrologer in the Slums ⑥

Volume 32 · Chapter 38

Clodia sighed helplessly. She knew Princess Josefina's personality well, so hearing such stupid words was not unexpected.

Princess Josefina had no ill intentions; she simply believed that for someone who couldn't eat bread, eating cake was normal. It was clear that her understanding of the outside world was limited to what she had seen.

But these words hit Alfonso like a ton of bricks—

A noble princess could actually say such things? How ignorant the nobility were of the lower classes!

It was because people like this ruled the kingdom that so many slums came into being.

Alfonso's face darkened. He felt insulted—forget expensive cake, even cheap black bread wasn't something he could eat every day.

"What's wrong? Why isn't anyone speaking?" Princess Josefina asked strangely.

"Nothing, Your Highness."

Clodia gave an awkward smile. She was used to the princess's startling remarks and wouldn't deliberately correct her mistakes.

After putting away her smile, Clodia stared at Alfonso, her expression stern again, and said sharply:

"Whatever your reasons, theft is theft. But since you've luckily encountered Your Highness, this can be forgiven. You'd best leave the capital—this isn't a place for idle people like you."

Alfonso frowned. He had only just left the slums—did he have to go back?

Having seen the capital's wealth, Alfonso no longer wanted to return to that hell.

Even being a vagrant here was a hundred times better than living in the slums.

Clodia's words deeply hurt Alfonso's pride. He hadn't offended this knight—why was she targeting him?

"I'm not an idle person. Please don't make assumptions about me."

"If you're not idle, how did you go steal?" Clodia took a deep breath and said seriously, "I know your kind well—people from the slums are mostly despicable creatures with no moral bottom line in pursuit of profit."

Alfonso clenched his fists silently. He had to admit it was true, but he couldn't accept it. To regain his dignity, he couldn't help but start lying: "I'm an astrologer from the slums. I live by my own abilities—I'm definitely not the kind of despicable person you described!"

"An astrologer?" Clodia looked utterly disdainful. In her eyes, those who predicted the future by the stars were all frauds.

"Yeah, I'm quite famous in the slums." Alfonso didn't even blush while lying—he had only read one stall book about astrology.

"You're a famous astrologer?" Princess Josefina immediately became interested, her eyes sparkling—

"Sounds like you're quite impressive."

Princess Josefina had always been deeply interested in astrology, just like girls fascinated by zodiac mysteries—she was no exception.

Alfonso's claim of being a famous astrologer happened to strike the princess's curiosity.

Although Clodia strongly opposed it, believing Alfonso was definitely a fraud, she still invited Alfonso into the palace at Josefina's request.

Alfonso was overwhelmed with gratitude. He never expected to have access to royalty, but this was undoubtedly fate's chance to turn his life around. If he seized it, maybe he could climb to the position he dreamed of.

Although Alfonso wasn't a real astrologer, relying on the stall books he'd read and his excellent eloquence, he successfully deceived Princess Josefina and made her believe his prophecies deeply.

Alfonso was very cunning—he never predicted anything within ten years, because when the time passed and the prophecy didn't come true, his wonderful life in the palace would end, and he'd even be sent to the guillotine.

So Alfonso only pretended to predict things ten years ahead, describing them vividly. Using people's hope for a better future, he deceived others into believing him. Invincible, he quickly established himself in court and became a favorite beside Princess Josefina.

All of this fell within Clodia's eyes. She firmly believed Alfonso was a fraud, using layer upon layer of lies to seek his own benefit.

Unfortunately, Clodia had no evidence and couldn't slander others before the princess at will. She could only wait for Alfonso's lies to collapse under their own weight—but that would take ten years.

As Alfonso's fame in court grew, he gradually attracted the old king's attention. This "astrologer" from the slums saw the kingdom's supreme ruler for the first time—

In the palace, Alfonso knelt on the ground, too afraid to raise his head. He was terrified his lies would be exposed.

"This is the astrologer you mentioned?" The old king examined the tiny Alfonso.

"Correct. Though he comes from the slums, his astrological prophecies are quite accurate. He said I might receive the Goddess's blessing in ten years—"

"Princess Josefina believes this completely. She doesn't know these were all Alfonso's random guesses."

"Oh?"

The old king narrowed his eyes. He wasn't as easily deceived as Princess Josefina and the court nobles.

As a monarch, the old king had seen countless frauds and easily noticed some problems with Alfonso.

Princess Josefina was a devout believer. Regarding receiving the Goddess's blessing ten years later, she naturally chose to believe completely.

And he specifically said ten years later—such a long time. No one could guarantee that this slum astrologer would still be in court ten years later.

After thinking for a moment, the old king decided to test the astrologer recommended by the princess to see if he truly had ability.

"Mr. Alfonso, recently there have been rumors about you in court. I hear you can predict the future through the night stars?"

"Yes, Your Majesty." Alfonso's voice trembled.

"But you always predict things ten years away. Can't you predict recent events?" the old king asked.

"It might be difficult," Alfonso stammered, his heart sinking as he wondered if his scheme had been seen through.

"What's so difficult? Can't you do it? I've heard that powerful astrologers can know tomorrow's events by the stars. If you can't, is it because your ability is insufficient? The court won't keep idle people." The old king was subtly asking Alfonso to leave. If it weren't for the princess's recommendation, he might have been thrown out immediately.

Alfonso broke out in a cold sweat. He understood the king's meaning, and his heart became extremely tense.

Though he had lived in the court for a short time, he was deeply addicted to this luxurious life of food and clothing!

Having lived in fear of poverty since birth, he couldn't bear to leave the court now. Letting him return to the slums was worse than killing him.

Alfonso gritted his teeth, and with a rush of blood to his head, he raised his gaze and stared straight into the king's eyes, speaking seriously.

"If Your Majesty insists on having me predict recent events, it's not impossible."

"Oh? Go ahead." The old king became somewhat interested.

"In these past few days I observed the stars and found that within half a month, there will definitely be an earthquake in the north of the kingdom!" Alfonso said randomly—he didn't know if it would happen.

"An earthquake in the north?" The old king smiled, stroking his beard with interest, but didn't take it seriously. "An interesting prophecy. If this doesn't happen within half a month, what do you think should be done?"

Alfonso had no way out now. He frowned and said in a low voice—

"If the prophecy doesn't come true, I'll walk to the guillotine myself."

title: Chapter 39 — The Astrologer in the Slums 7
content:
Chapter 39 — The Astrologer in the Slums 7

Volume 32 · Chapter 39

Seven days had passed, and the northern part of the kingdom remained peaceful, with no disasters occurring.

Since making the bet with the old king, Alfonso had never left his room.

Alfonso knew his prophecy was a fabrication, and that there would be no earthquake in the north. If the deadline passed, he would lose his head on the chopping block!

He was terrified of being pushed to the guillotine by the angry king and kept praying for a miracle to occur.

Alfonso felt extremely tired and fell asleep in his fear. He dreamed of his childhood—

Because he had no decent shoes, he was bullied by his peers, and by coincidence, he entered a valley where he met a mysterious creature hiding in a cave.

Everything around him was so familiar, making him recall the fear he had faced as a child. The difference was that he was no longer a child who knew nothing.

A cold night breeze blew, making Alfonso feel cold. He instinctively shrank his body, and a sharp pain shot through his feet. He looked down and saw that his shoes were gone, and sharp stones were pricking his feet.

Everything seemed so real, almost like he had truly returned here, not like it was a dream.

Alfonso stood at the cave entrance, sweating, and looked around, unable to distinguish between reality and dreams. He wanted to escape, but his body wouldn't move.

"I knew you would come back, little ghost."

A deep voice echoed from the depths of the mountain cave. Two lantern-like eyes glowed in the darkness.

The tiny Alfonso felt the immense dragon's power and was terrified, sitting down on the ground, unable to speak.

"Is your life already at a dead end? If you want to continue living and not give up your comfortable life, then come in and let's talk."

As soon as the words fell, Alfonso's stiff body regained its freedom. His first thought was to turn and run. He didn't know what the creature in the cave was, only feeling fear and despair spreading through his body.

However, Alfonso ran only six or seven steps before stopping. He realized that running away wouldn't help, and if the time ran out, he would lose his head and truly say goodbye to his comfortable life, ultimately unable to escape the fate from the sewers.

After thinking for a long time, Alfonso resolutely chose to enter the cave.

Walking barefoot for an unknown length of time, he finally reached the deepest part of the narrow passage and saw a vast space and the creature's full form—

It was the head of a massive black dragon lying on the ground, without a body, only the head, as if it had been neatly severed from the neck.

Each of its teeth was as large and sharp as mountains, and its long whiskers covered the entire ground. Even the small nostrils seemed to bring a gale, ready to sweep him into the sky at any moment.

"You are?"

"I am the creator of the great dragon race, the black dragon who craves the waters under the world tree, Nidhogg."

Alfonso didn't understand, but since he could communicate, he gradually calmed down. "Why are you here?"

"Because that vile demonic seer betrayed me, stole my fruit, destroyed my body, and brought ruin to the entire era. Perhaps I am the only one who survived from the ancient gods."

Nidhogg's enormous eyes rolled, looking very weak.

Alfonso was confused and didn't care about this matter. He only wanted to know, "Can you help me?"

"What humans pursue are those boring things, which are nothing to me."

Nidhogg paused and said seriously, "I can give you my blood and power, making you my servant and one of the top humans, playing with the weak and lowly. Isn't that what you want?"

Alfonso's cold sweat flowed down his forehead, and his ugly heart was exposed.

"But there is a condition. As my servant, you must be absolutely loyal and help me find someone with divine nature. I need their souls to repair my shattered body. If you find a suitable sacrifice, give this to him."

A green pendant appeared out of nowhere and fell gently into Alfonso's hand. A warm breath passed through it.

Alfonso stared at the pendant in his hand, not seeing anything unusual, no different from ordinary decorations. However, he faintly felt that whoever has this thing will have a mark on their soul.

"What is your answer?"

"I am willing to be your servant, as long as you help me! I will accept any condition!"

"I knew I didn't make a mistake."

Nidhogg let out a cold laugh and opened his enormous mouth, sucking Alfonso into the abyss.

Alfonso woke up from his sleep, looked around the room, and realized he had never left it. Everything that happened seemed like a dream?

He slowly raised his hand and spread his fingers. The green pendant that appeared in his dream was lying quietly in his palm.

He slowly spread his other hand, and a small black flame was burning in his palm, with terrifying dragon power spreading out.

Alfonso couldn't help but smile. He finally realized it wasn't a dream, that he had established a connection with Nidhogg and possessed extraordinary power, no longer the same as before.

"Auntie! King's Majesty is urgently summoning you!"

A maid rushed in, sweating profusely.

"What happened?"

"Last night, an earthquake occurred in a city in the north, causing great damage."

"!?" Alfonso's eyes widened, and he clenched his fists tightly. He couldn't hide his joy—

From this moment on, he was no longer the refugee from the slums but a real astrologer.

Since his prophecy came true, an earthquake indeed occurred in the northern part of the kingdom. Alfonso was personally honored by the king and firmly established himself in the palace. Not only did he gain the trust of the queen, but even the king began to believe in this astrologer from the slums.

As he walked out of the grand hall, Alfonso was full of confidence, his smile impossible to contain. He had already started dreaming of how to enjoy the glorious life ahead, aiming to become the most powerful and wealthy person in the kingdom.

"What are you smiling about? You're just a rat in the sewers, and even if you fly, you're just a bat in the dark."

"Uh!"

Alfonso frowned and turned to see that Clodagh had been waiting here, her eyes filled with hostility. "It's the Sword Saint, I'm just happy to be recognized by His Majesty, please don't misunderstand."

Clodagh walked closer to Alfonso. "Don't think you can deceive everyone. You can't deceive me. I know you're a complete fraud, hiding here, not wanting to return to the slums, right?"

"What are you talking about? I don't understand."

"Before, you were just a weak ordinary person, but now I feel a strange magic power in you. What did you experience in these few days?"

Clodagh walked around Alfonso, continuing to press, "The earthquake in the north is suspicious. Are you meddling in it? Are there others helping you? You're not alone, but a group of frauds. What's your real purpose in entering the palace?"

"Sword Saint, please don't accuse me without evidence. I am now the astrologer trusted by His Majesty. Maybe I can predict your future rebellion tonight by observing the stars? I can also frame you."

Clodagh's face darkened, pointing at Alfonso's nose—

"I will catch your fox tail, watch this."

title: Chapter 40 — Astrologer in the Slums 7.5 (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 40 — Astrologer in the Slums 7.5 (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 32 · Chapter 40

Three years have passed, and Alfonso has accurately predicted over thirty events based on the stars - the eruption of the Ted Peak volcano. The large-scale struggle for sea power by the British fleet. The nationwide uprising army formed by the slums. A thirty-year unprecedented flood occurred in the south. And so on. Alfonso has accurately predicted every single one of these events, allowing the kingdom to avoid countless dangers and losses that would have been astronomical in number.

Thanks to his numerous brilliant predictions, Alfonso has become the most prominent figure in the kingdom, with a status only second to the old king. His power has rapidly expanded, and he is now almost omnipotent. The old king has even established a massive astrology tower for Alfonso, hoping that he will continue to serve the kingdom and make sacrifices for its prosperity. Alfonso has become a VIP among the nobles, and they are willing to send him vast amounts of treasure in exchange for his predictions of their futures.

For three years, Alfonso has enjoyed unparalleled wealth and luxury, completely forgetting the poverty and hunger of his life in the slums. However, it is not because Alfonso can truly see the future through the stars that his predictions are so accurate. There is always his shadow lurking behind the disasters, using the power of the black dragon Nidhöggr to predict and then create the disasters. How could his accuracy be low?

Due to his frequent successful predictions, most people have come to believe in Alfonso's words, but there are still a few dissenters who question him - Claudie is one of them. She has always been searching for evidence that Alfonso is behind the disasters, believing that the kingdom has become more turbulent since he arrived at the palace. However, Alfonso is too cunning, and he has never left any clues. Claudie is suspicious that there must be a powerful evil force supporting him outside the palace, but she has been unable to find any leads.

It is precisely because of people like Claudie that the kingdom has not fallen completely under Alfonso's control. Although Alfonso is predicting and creating disasters, the only thing he has not predicted is the three-year drought, during which the entire kingdom has not seen a single drop of rain. This is not Alfonso's doing, but rather a genuine punishment from heaven, causing widespread famine and disaster. The kingdom is already in a state of turmoil, and the people are suffering greatly.

The kind Queen Josephine has been constantly calling on the nobles to donate money and food to help the disaster-stricken people, but the response has been lukewarm, and some have even been offended. Wealth is the sacred cake that the nobles have guarded for generations, and they are not willing to give it up unless they are forced to.

In the queen's bedroom, Queen Josephine is pregnant and is expected to give birth soon. Her guards have also been increased. Claudie looks at the soon-to-be mother with mixed feelings, happy that she is becoming a great mother, but worried that the child is born in a time of great turmoil.

"Hey, Claudie, should I call my daughter 'sister' or 'aunt'?" Queen Josephine asks with a smile, stroking her swollen belly.

"Uh, I think 'sister' would be better," Claudie replies, blushing. She prefers to be called sister, as being called aunt would be embarrassing, given that she is not yet married.

"It's okay to call me 'mom' too," Queen Josephine says suddenly.

"No way, that's not possible," Claudie says firmly. "I'm just your knight, and I shouldn't be called mom."

"Actually, it's because you're my knight that you might also have to take care of her, so you're kind of like a half-mom," Queen Josephine says with a smile.

"Uh, I don't know what to say," Claudie says, her face red. She doesn't dislike children, but she doesn't want to be compared to the queen.

"I think this child is special," Queen Josephine says, looking at her belly with a loving expression. "I've been having a dream lately, where a woman with a radiant aura gives me a baby girl and a holy sword. I think that woman must be the goddess, and maybe my prayers have finally been answered. This child might be a gift from the goddess."

"Uh, what's going on?" Claudie asks, raising an eyebrow. She thinks that the queen must be dreaming because of her devout faith.

"Anyway, what should I name this child?" Queen Josephine asks, thinking carefully. "How about Diana? It's a lovely name, and I think she'll like it."

Claudie smiles, but there's a hint of sadness in her eyes. She has something she wants to say, but she's afraid of disturbing the queen's mood.

"Hey, Claudie, do you have something you want to tell me?" Queen Josephine asks, looking at her with a knowing expression.

"Uh, actually, I do," Claudie says, hesitating. "The palace is not very peaceful right now, because you've been calling on the nobles to donate money to help the drought-stricken people. This has upset some of the nobles, and they might see you as a threat.

"I know all this," Queen Josephine says calmly. "But I have to do something to help the people. They're suffering greatly, and I don't want to just sit back and do nothing. If I don't speak out, who else will? The nobles are only looking out for their own interests, and they don't care about the people."

Claudie's eyes well up with tears, and she doesn't know what to say. She's from the slums, and she knows how the people suffer. She's always hated the nobles for their arrogance and selfishness, but she's learned to see the good in them through Queen Josephine.

Claudie is only worried that speaking out for the people might put the queen in danger.

"I'm not afraid of danger, because I have you to protect me," Queen Josephine says, smiling. "Will you always be there to fight for me?"

"Of course, I'll uphold the oath of a knight and fight for you until the end," Claudie says firmly.

Half a month later, Princess Diana was born safely. At the same time, a brilliant meteor streaked across the sky, falling to the ground in the capital city, causing a commotion.

In the palace, Queen Josephine held her newborn daughter in her arms, beaming with joy, and her heart was filled with happiness. The old king looked on, smiling, and temporarily forgot about the kingdom's troubles, focusing on caring for the newborn princess.

The birth of a new life brought a breath of fresh air to the stagnant palace, and the atmosphere began to improve. Alfonso, who was standing nearby, looked at Queen Josephine's baby with a rare smile, and he didn't seem to dislike the queen at all. In fact, he had a deep respect for her.

After three years in the palace, Alfonso had seen the true faces of the nobles, but Queen Josephine was different. Her kindness was pure and untainted.

"Alfonso, sir, could you make a prediction for my daughter Diana?" the old king asked, excitedly.

"Ah, no need for a prediction," Alfonso said, hesitating. "The little princess's future will be filled with happiness and good fortune. This is a lucky charm that will protect her from any disasters."

On the other side, Claudie led the palace guards to investigate the fallen meteor. The ground was scorched, and the buildings around it had been consumed by flames. Claudie wrinkled her brow, looking at the fire that refused to die out, and decided to enter the crater alone.

"You all stay here and wait for me," Claudie said, commanding the guards.

"Be careful, Your Highness," one of the guards warned.

Claudie took a deep breath and walked into the smoke, where a thin ice wall appeared, protecting her from the heat. The crater was a mess, with holes and craters everywhere. She carefully approached the center of the crater, where a red-hot stone glowed with a faint holy light. A holy sword, shining with a dull light, stood upright in the stone, emitting a divine aura.

This was a phenomenon that Claudie had never seen before, and she couldn't understand what it was. However, she sensed that something was not right.

Claudie remembered Queen Josephine's words about the woman with a radiant aura carrying a baby girl and a holy sword in her dream. She felt a chill run down her spine - could it be that everything was connected?

The goddess, who was only mentioned in the scriptures, would she really interact with the queen? What was the goddess's plan, or was it just a coincidence?

Sorry, I'm still writing, and it's 3:40 AM. I still have 2000 words to go, and I wanted to finish this chapter in one go. I fell asleep this morning and started writing again, hoping to finish it quickly. Please vote for me, friends! _(:3」∠)_

title: Chapter 41 — The Astrologer from the Slums ⑧
content:
Chapter 41 — The Astrologer from the Slums ⑧

Volume 32 · Chapter 41

The three-year-long drought showed no signs of stopping.

The old king had tried every possible method, but the scorching sun and the lack of rain persisted. In some places, water had become more expensive than gold.

Masses of refugees were forced to leave their homes and seek new water sources, making the kingdom extremely dangerous. Frequent rebellions occurred, and soldiers were dispatched to suppress them.

The old king realized the dire situation but was powerless to change it. The kingdom's crisis was no longer solvable with money but required a long-overdue rain, otherwise, his rule would be in grave danger.

At night, on the towering astrological platform, the old king gathered with a group of nobles, hoping that Alfonso would use astrology to predict how long it would take for a large rain to come.

Alfonso stood alone in the center of the astrological platform, gazing at the vast starry sky, pretending to be mysterious and not speaking for a long time.

He had decided to sacrifice the child of his benefactor to the black dragon for his own benefit.

However, this matter had to be done seamlessly without drawing attention to himself.

After gaining his current position, he couldn't use force to take the newly born Diana from Queen Josephine, as that would put him in a passive position.

The only method was to use a borrowed knife to kill.

Alfonso decided in his heart to pour dirt on Queen Josephine, accusing her of being a wicked witch who had brought the three-year drought. Only by killing her would the disaster end.

He was very clear that if Queen Josephine didn't die, he had no chance to take Diana.

Once the queen died, Diana would lose favor and become the child of a wicked witch, facing the disdain of the court. At that time, he could easily take the infant's life.

In addition to the old king, there were many nobles present, and Queen Josephine had been advocating that the nobles should donate to the disaster relief. This group of people had already touched their cake, and they would certainly not help the queen speak, but rather support pushing her into the abyss.

Alfonso's face showed a barely noticeable smile. Except for the old king, no one here spoke in favor of the queen.

"How long will it take for the kingdom to have a big rain?" the old king asked patiently.

"Your Majesty, I saw the kingdom heading towards ruin, and this land will become a wasteland, never seeing a drop of rain again," Alfonso answered seriously.

This statement caused not only the old king but also the nobles to panic. If the kingdom were to perish and become a wasteland, the wealth they guarded would be worthless.

"How is this possible? The kingdom is at an end? It will never rain again? This is impossible," the old king could not believe his ears.

"Your Majesty, I will not lie to you. Everything is true. I only tell you the answer of the starry omens accurately," Alfonso bowed slightly, maintaining his humility.

The old king felt dizzy and faint, almost passing out on the spot, "What have we done wrong? Why are we facing such punishment?"

"Your Majesty, I dare to speak frankly, this great drought is man-made," Alfonso suddenly emphasized.

"Who?" the old king's gaze became sharp.

"I dare not say, this person has a favor for me. If I say it, it would be the cowardly and lowly act of betraying my benefactor. Please, Your Majesty, understand," Alfonso pretended to be very difficult.

"Don't you have any favor for me? Not saying it is harming me, and I will be beheaded. Don't have any hesitation, say it boldly," the old king pressed, eager to know who was causing the disaster.

Alfonso swallowed nervously, "It's Queen Josephine."

When the nobles heard this name, they became chaotic and no longer quiet. No one expected the kind and simple queen to have the power to cause a three-year drought.

The old king's face darkened, not believing these words, "Are you not talking nonsense? How is this possible!"

Alfonso immediately knelt on one knee and said in a low voice, "Queen Josephine has been very kind to me and has once helped the starving me. I will never slander Queen Josephine. The starry omens reveal that Queen Josephine is a wicked witch, and it is she who brought the disaster to this land. If possible, I hope this will never be true."

The word "witch" caused the nobles around to erupt. Because everyone knew that witches were wicked beings, and they often brought disasters. They were different from magicians, and they often harm people around them in a subtle way. The number of witches burned alive by the Church was countless.

The old king's face was dark, and he couldn't speak, and he began to be suspicious. "Your Majesty, please make a decision, we don't have much time left. The people are struggling in water and fire."

"Yes, the number of disaster victims in the kingdom is increasing, and they will eventually threaten your safety. Don't abandon your country built by your ancestors because of a woman."

"Your Majesty, don't hesitate any longer, order the execution of Queen Josephine. The wicked witch is destroying our kingdom."

These nobles could no longer tolerate the queen touching their bottom line, and they were deeply convinced of Alfonso's "astrology," all wanting to kill the queen to protect their wealth.

Alfonso secretly lifted his head and saw the old king's rigid expression, his inner defense seemed to have been destroyed.

Facing the loved woman and the country inherited for generations?

Any normal ruler knows how to choose.

In the royal palace, Queen Josephine gently rocked the baby's cradle, Diana had fallen asleep, occasionally kicking her short legs.

Queen Josephine was full of love, feeling that her little baby was beautiful without any flaws. She reached out and lightly touched Diana's nose, saying softly.

"You have to grow up quickly, otherwise, I will grow old first and become less beautiful."

Diana twitched her little nose a few times, her baby body twisted, and continued to sleep in an uncomfortable but comfortable posture.

Queen Josephine smiled, feeling that Diana would grow up to be a big and carefree child, just like herself, not being particular, and maybe a little silly?

Footsteps came, and Alfonso came alone to the royal palace, kneeling on one knee, "Queen Josephine."

"Alfonso? Why are you here? Is there anything I can help you with?" Queen Josephine asked curiously, not noticing the approaching danger.

Alfonso hesitated, he had just received the order to assassinate Queen Josephine tonight, and the old king had made his choice.

"Is it to see Diana?" Queen Josephine said, "Yes, but don't wake her up."

Alfonso looked at Diana, who was fast asleep, and the pendant he had given her was still neatly worn around her neck.

The two of them stared at the small infant for a long time, and both were very quiet.

Alfonso was hesitant because he knew this was the last time he could be with the queen, and maybe he would never meet someone who could accept him again, even though he also believed that the kind queen should not suffer fate.

But kind people are destined to be eaten, this is the rule he has recognized in the slums, even if he doesn't kill Queen Josephine, those nobles will eventually harass her, maybe one day.

I am just ending the queen's fate earlier, dying in my hands is better than dying in the hands of those nobles, at least there is dignity in leaving.

"Your Majesty, I have always been fond of you, from the first time I saw you, I was deeply attracted to you. Seeing your smile is the happiest thing for me."

"Hmm?" Queen Josephine raised her head in surprise, smiling and teasing, "Why are you saying these strange words? You are not like you, Alfonso. You and Claudette are like brothers and sisters to me, and I also like you, but unfortunately, your relationship is not good, I have never been able to understand."

"Brother?" Alfonso lowered his head, feeling a layer of mist in his eyes, he unconsciously pulled back the knife in his sleeve, "I am honored."

"What's wrong?" Queen Josephine frowned and stood up in front of Alfonso, "Why are you crying? You are very strange today. Is there anything you are not happy about?"

"Thank you for your care and concern all this time. Your favor, I will never forget. If your soul can ascend to heaven, I am willing to sink into the lava of hell to redeem you," Alfonso suddenly lifted his head, and the poisoned knife in his sleeve, "Pitui"- The knife pierced Queen Josephine's chest.

Queen Josephine was shocked, lowered her head, and saw the blood flowing down the knife onto the carpet, her vision quickly blurred, and she felt no pain at all, only clearly knowing that her life was ending.

The knife was coated with paralytic poison, and it would not cause any pain when entering the body. This was the only mercy Alfonso had for Queen Josephine.

Alfonso saw that Queen Josephine had no defense against him, and his sense of guilt was heavier, he didn't know how much the queen trusted him, killing her was as simple as killing an ant.

"Your Majesty, I actually always liked you, from the first time I saw you, I was deeply attracted to you. Seeing your smile is the happiest thing for me."

"Hmm?" Queen Josephine raised her head in surprise, smiling and teasing, "Why are you saying these strange words? You are not like you, Alfonso. You and Claudette are like brothers and sisters to me, and I also like you, but unfortunately, your relationship is not good, I have never been able to understand."

"Brother?" Alfonso lowered his head, feeling a layer of mist in his eyes, he unconsciously pulled back the knife in his sleeve, "I am honored."

"What's wrong?" Queen Josephine frowned and stood up in front of Alfonso, "Why are you crying? You are very strange today. Is there anything you are not happy about?"

"Thank you for your care and concern all this time. Your favor, I will never forget. If your soul can ascend to heaven, I am willing to sink into the lava of hell to redeem you," Alfonso suddenly lifted his head, and the poisoned knife in his sleeve, "Pitui"- The knife pierced Queen Josephine's chest.

Queen Josephine was shocked, lowered her head, and saw the blood flowing down the knife onto the carpet, her vision quickly blurred, and she felt no pain at all, only clearly knowing that her life was ending.

The knife was coated with paralytic poison, and it would not cause any pain when entering the body. This was the only mercy Alfonso had for Queen Josephine.

Alfonso saw that Queen Josephine had no defense against him, and his sense of guilt was heavier, he didn't know how much the queen trusted him, killing her was as simple as killing an ant.

"Your Majesty, even if you are a bit stupid, you don't understand that when the poor can't even eat bread, expensive cakes are a dream. But I hope you can be happy when you leave, I sincerely ask for your forgiveness, everything is because I couldn't catch up."

Bang.

The door was kicked open violently, and Claudette, who had already known all the secrets, came to the royal palace to find out that Alfonso had led the assassination team to the queen's palace tonight.

She suddenly realized that something was wrong and rushed here alone, only to be late by a step.

Claudette just entered the door and saw Alfonso pulling the knife out of Queen Josephine's chest and throwing the body coldly on the ground.

The queen lying in the blood pool, her eyes wide open, her body twitching slightly, and her gaze quickly becoming cold and lifeless.

Claudette was horrified at what she saw, her face pale, and her mind was "boom," as if an explosion had occurred, making her thinking blank.

She had thought that the queen was kind to Alfonso, and this guy, even if he was a fraud, would not harm the queen's life, but she underestimated Alfonso's level of depravity.

She cursed herself for being powerless, and she had sworn to protect Queen Josephine, but she couldn't fulfill her vow. If she could find evidence that Alfonso was a fraud, maybe the queen would not die.

Claudette stared at Alfonso's eyes, anger causing her expression to freeze, and a stock of evil fire rose in her heart.

"You came? Unfortunately, you only ate a little and couldn't protect the queen. You are indeed a negligent knight."

"Alfonso!!!"

Claudette picked up the Saint-tier combat energy and magic power, which exploded violently, like a mountain avalanche of anger, unstoppable.

She drew her sword from her waist, Light Chant, accompanied by a below-zero blizzard, and unsheathed her sword, aiming for Alfonso's throat.

"Hmph."

Alfonso coldly sneered, inheriting the blood and power of the black dragon Nidhogg, his strength was already at the pseudo-god level, and Claudette was a weakling in front of him.

A dragon's aura spread out, and Alfonso easily blocked the sword with his knife and then sprayed out scorching black flames with his other hand.

An explosion occurred, black flames set the royal palace on fire, waking up the sleeping little princess Diana, and her cries echoed in the cradle, making the cradle unstable.

Claudette was smoking black, and she heavily collided with the wall, and only one strike left her seriously injured, and her hand holding the sword kept shaking.

This was her first fight with Alfonso, and she didn't expect that his strength was terrifying to this extent, and she couldn't defeat him.

"Don't be so impulsive, Claudette, these are all the decisions made by the king and nobles together."

"Shut up! You are a traitor! I curse you to hell!"

Claudette got up from the ground with her injuries, listening to Diana's cries, and her heart was anxious.

Suddenly, she swung her sword, and golden sea waves from all directions attacked, the walls of the royal palace were covered with frost.

Alfonso was about to counterattack, but he found that this technique was not attacking him but restricting his movements. The sea waves formed an ice wall, separating him and the cradle of Diana.

Seeing the danger, Alfonso suddenly swung his arm, easily breaking the ice wall apart. He looked closely and found that Claudette and the cradle of Diana had disappeared.

Alfonso felt blood rushing to his head, angry, and his veins stood out.

"If I don't get Diana, all my efforts will be in vain."

"Come!"

Several black shadows appeared out of nowhere, all of them were the elite of the assassination team that Alfonso had cultivated, each with excellent strength.

"Claudette has been seriously injured and should not be far away. Go and bring back the Diana Princess, don't let them leave the city."

Tonight's city was filled with the smell of blood, and even the full moon in the sky was stained red.

Claudette, with her injuries, carried the baby princess, fought bravely, and killed more than a hundred assassination team elites and several of Alfonso's teeth with her seriously injured body, her hands were almost as long as the sword.

Finally, with the help of some of her colleagues who resisted Alfonso, she successfully escaped from the turbulent Spain with Diana.

Several months later, the vast Alps snow mountain, the green grass below the mountain was lush and spring-like.

A tired traveler with a sword at his waist, carefully carrying a baby, came to this place.

Claudette was full of injuries, and it was a miracle that she could walk here. Her face was full of fatigue.

She looked down at the baby in her arms, who seemed to be a bit hungry, sucking her fingers, the appearance was cute.

Claudette managed to show a smile, but when she thought of the deceased Queen Josephine, she felt very guilty, and she was a powerless knight.

She wanted to hide in the Alps forever until she could defeat Alfonso, on the one hand, raising the queen's child, and on the other hand, continuing to practice and improve her strength.

Claudette did not give up her wish to avenge the queen, but after seeing Alfonso's strength, she was unsure if she could complete this wish in her lifetime, and she was very uncertain.

Claudette, who had seen the ugly side of the palace, realized a truth, wealth does not necessarily make people happy, and living a normal life peacefully may be a life that most people cannot achieve.

Claudette did not want the child in her arms to be involved in the palace struggle, and she hoped that Diana would grow up as an ordinary person and not follow the path of Queen Josephine, full of misfortune.

She saw the green pendant around Diana's neck, and to break away from the past, she wanted to throw it away.

After hesitating for a moment, Claudette did not do so, Diana had lost her mother, and maybe this thing was the only memory, and she couldn't become Diana's real mother.

"Alice."

"Dear Princess, this is your new name, do you like it?"

"I will guard you as I guarded your mother until the last moment of my life."

"This time, I will not leave any regrets, I swear."

title: Chapter 42 — Invitation
content:
Chapter 42 — Invitation

Volume 32 · Chapter 42

Midnight, Alice woke up from her sleep, as if she had just heard a call from her teacher.

A vague sense of unease surged to her heart, making her very uneasy, as if something bad had happened.

Alice recalled that her teacher had left in a hurry, leaving a letter and then leaving, and as she knew her teacher, if it wasn't a troublesome matter, how would she easily compromise?

Alice didn't sleep either, sitting on the bed, thinking whether she should go and continue talking to her teacher. Her rebellious attitude might have made her very angry, so she left suddenly.

Moreover, Alice wanted to ask her teacher about the Light Chants, why her teacher collected a divine artifact, where this thing came from, and there might be more unknown secrets.

Alice looked down at her little girl, who was sleeping soundly in a four-legged position, completely in a carefree state.

She smiled and helped the little girl cover the blanket that had been kicked off. Chris immediately smiled like a flower, drooling from the corners of her mouth, and she didn't know what she had dreamed of.

Alice's gaze turned to Merlin on the other side, and she found that this guy was staring at her with his eyes wide open, and in the dark room, he was shining, which scared her to death.

"Wow! What are you doing? Staring at me all night like a thief."

"That's what you should say, right?" Merlin quietly got up, frowned, "You don't sleep at all, what are you doing sneaking around?"

"Alice's face turned red, hesitantly answered, "I can't sleep."

"What's the matter? You, this nervous person, will worry about something."

"Shut up, the nervous person is you, I'm not the same as you, a heartless person."

"So, what are you worrying about?" Merlin slightly adjusted his posture.

"It's about my teacher. Last time, she left in a hurry after leaving a letter, I always feel like she might be angry. I don't want to make things too tense with my teacher, some things should be talked about."

"Ah~, that bitter and cruel old woman, I thought you would stand up to your teacher, but you surrendered so quickly."

"My teacher is not bitter and cruel, just too strict in her requirements. Since I was little, I would be severely scolded by her if I made a mistake, and it was all for my good."

Alice looked down, recalling past events, "Except for being very strict in training, my teacher has no place that I dislike. She will stay with me for a long time when I'm sick, and when I'm unhappy, she will tell me stories. The bitter and cruel is just the surface, my teacher is a good person, and I like her very much."

"Oh? So it's like that?" Merlin scratched his chin, asked, "By the way, you've never talked about your mother, haven't you always been with your teacher?"

"It's not that I don't want to talk, but I've never seen her. Since I can remember, there has only been my teacher beside me. I remember," Alice thought carefully and said embarrassedly, "My teacher said I was picked up from the garbage."

"Hah!" Merlin couldn't help but laugh out loud, "Don't laugh, this must be fake, think carefully, it's impossible, right?"

"Okay, I won't laugh," Merlin put away his laughter, not wanting to start a war with Alice in the middle of the night, "Have you ever thought about looking for your real parents?"

"I also thought about it when I was little, but now it's okay, I'm used to it, after all, I'm also an abandoned person."

Alice frowned, looked down at her neck, and the green pendant, with a bit of complaint, "I don't need my father and mother."

Merlin recalled some things from a long time ago, seeing a mother and daughter portrait in Captain Dennis, named Queen Josephine holding a baby, and a green pendant similar to Alice appeared in the painting.

"Alice, have you ever thought that you might be a noble princess?"

"What? Why are you asking this?" Alice was surprised.

"Captain Dennis remembers, right? He once thought that because of the pendant on your neck, there was a lost little princess." Merlin pretended to be casual.

"This thing I've already forgotten, how can it be? Which princess would be like me and suffer so much?" Alice hesitated and mocked, "Moreover, if I were a princess of a certain country, I wouldn't mix with a demon, which would be a loss of identity, huh~!"

"Princess is what? I was the Demon Lord, and the princesses of humans wanted to kidnap me as many times as they could, they were not worthy of washing my feet."

Merlin grinned and said sarcastically, "Looking at how close we are, I can give you special treatment, just call me dad three times a day."

"You're dreaming!" Alice's face turned black, and if it weren't for fear of waking up Chris, it would have been a century-long argument.

"What sound?" Merlin suddenly stood up, his expression turned alert.

"What sound?" Alice asked in confusion.

"You listen carefully, it seems to be the living room outside." Merlin frowned, thinking whether thieves had broken into the house. But which thief would dare to break into the home of the Ujie Chiji Knight?

"You didn't hear wrong, right?" Alice became serious, carefully listening, and faint "creak" sounds came from outside the bedroom.

The two looked at each other and realized that something had come into the house, and it was not knocking.

Merlin and Alice held oil lamps and quietly walked out of the bedroom, using the dim light of the lamp.

They saw the black crow that suddenly appeared in the home, with blood-red eyes looking around, finally staring at Merlin.

Red-eyed crows are the most commonly used messengers in the demon race. Their sudden appearance here means that the demon race has come to the door.

The crow suddenly took off, flapping its wings towards Merlin, quickly transformed into a letter, and slowly fell into his hand.

Merlin's expression immediately turned ugly, staring at the black letter in his hand, the seal on the black wax came from the Council of Elders.

"Merlin, what is this?" Alice asked curiously, not understanding the weight of the letter, only the seven most powerful demons in the demon race could receive this letter.

Merlin licked his dry lips and answered reluctantly.

"The invitation to the Seven Kings' Conference.

"I thought the Council of Elders would not invite me to attend after I was exiled, but I didn't expect."

title: Chapter 43 — Heading
content:
Chapter 43 — Heading

Volume 32 · Chapter 43

“Seven Kings Conference? Is it that important?” Alice looked at Merlin's invitation in astonishment, feeling it must be something important.

"It is somewhat important; this conference is the most stringent discussion within the demon race, where all monarchs must appear in person to summarize the previous stage of development and plan for the next stage. It could be said to be a meeting concerning the fate of every demon." Merlin simply explained, saying he didn't really want to attend, but the matter with Mammon should not be over yet.

"I didn't realize the demon race still had such a strict meeting." Alice sighed, still thinking the demon race was just each fighting for themselves.

"What's there to be surprised about? If the demon race were just a loose sand, they probably wouldn't have survived to today; it's just that the monarchs of the few demon palaces have only ordinary relations." Merlin shrugged his shoulders and continued, "But I'm still quite surprised; given the Elder Council's attitude toward me, they shouldn't want me to attend this meeting, but instead have Lilith act on my full authority. I didn't expect I'd still have to go on this trip."

"Really?" Alice lowered her head slightly, a vague discomfort rising in her heart. "Are you going to leave alone again?"

"This" Merlin looked at the invitation, fell silent for a moment, "Although I don't really want to attend this conference, I still have to go."

"Why? Do you have some unavoidable reason?" Alice asked, frowning.

"Any demon who receives an invitation and does not attend the meeting will be deemed a traitor, as I said before—this conference is no ordinary affair; all monarchs must attend." Merlin paused, then added, "Besides, I am not representing myself alone, but the entire First Demon Lord Palace's demons—my sister and a host of subordinates. If I don't attend, things will go badly; the First Demon Lord Palace would have no one else who could speak for them in the meeting. I hope you can understand, Alice."

"Alice lowered her head without speaking, always feeling Merlin drifting further away, always having to handle things alone, yet she had no reason to stop him." "Of course I understand, it's just that Chris will complain."

Merlin thought of his precious daughter and sighed helplessly, "I'm also sorry; the responsibility of looking after Chris has fallen entirely on you, but don't worry—I'll be back soon. The meeting won't take long; it's much easier than searching for the gods' relics."

Seeing Merlin's resolve to go, Alice knew saying anything would be useless, so she lifted her head, feigning an annoyed expression, "I'll believe you—this once, the last time."

Merlin secretly let out a sigh of relief, hesitated a moment, then voiced his concern, "Actually, this Seven Kings Conference is different from before; there may be some turbulence."

"What do you mean? Could there be some danger?" Alice asked in surprise.

"The demon race has just experienced a major upheaval; Mammon withdrew his forces from Britain and retreated to the Third Demon Lord Palace, which does not mean he has abandoned his ambition to expand territory. Most demons are still in a war frenzy; I personally thwarted Mammon's plan, pouring a bucket of cold water on the Elder Council—this matter hasn't Merlin took a deep breath, as for what the Seven Kings Conference will discuss, he already has some guesses—"

"This conference is very likely to bring up this matter."

"That faction of radical demons probably doesn't look kindly on me."

"Perhaps I need to personally reason with them."

Early morning, the sky still dark, winter sky gray and overcast, the town of Rexham shrouded in fog.

Merlin hadn't slept all night, chatting with Alice for a long time, deciding to attend this Seven Kings Conference—not just for the benefit of the First Demon Lord Palace, but also because he and Leviathan are in the same trench.

If the Elder Council takes the opportunity to punish Leviathan for interfering with the demon race's external expansion plans, Merlin will surely oppose this, supporting Leviathan in the name of the First Demon Lord Palace and preventing the radical faction in the council from condemning Leviathan.

Although Merlin is also the chief culprit in interfering with the external expansion plan, his status as an exiled monarch means that even if he faces punishment, it would not be as severe as Leviathan's.

Merlin had promised Leviathan this when he left the Mexico Strait; now is the time to fulfill that promise.

Alice also didn't sleep all night, though she wasn't bothered by the Seven Kings Conference; she thought Merlin would be leaving again soon, and their time together was short—spending it in deep sleep would be a waste.

Even if they talked about boring things, Alice thought it was far better than facing the fact that Merlin would leave as soon as she woke up; they might not see each other for several months.

Like a responsible little wife, Alice helped Merlin prepare his travel gear, making sure everything was covered; she didn't want him to be tangled up in trivialities on the road, and it would be even better if he could notice her thoughtfulness.

They didn't wake Chris, because if she knew Merlin was leaving again, she might not be able to go; so Alice chose to keep it from her daughter, and seeing Merlin off before dawn.

Merlin slung his pack onto his back, turned back and said, "Don't worry, it should be over soon."

Watching Merlin lightly dressed, ready to set off, Alice said softly, "It's so cold; should you add another layer?"

"That won't be necessary; I'm not afraid of the cold, moreover—Merlin touched his chest, his old face blushing as he said, 'The sweater you knitted I'm already wearing inside; it feels quite warm.'"

"! !?"

Alice hastily lowered her head; two blushes quickly rose on her face, feeling very shy.

She had thought Merlin would never say anything even if he wore the sweater she knitted herself; the result—

Alice took out a money pouch from behind her, handed it to Merlin, and said with a serious expression.

"This is the round-trip fare; you must not waste it, or buy a bunch of useless things."

"Don't worry, I won't go buying those things anymore." Merlin put away the money pouch, thinking he could finally bid farewell to his penniless days—was this Alice's concession to him?

"Remember to take care of yourself; if anything happens, let me know." Alice earnestly reminded.

"I'm not a child; you don't need to worry so much—just take care of yourself and Chris." Merlin grinned, and besides, I'll remind you.

"During this period, you'd better not come into contact with any demons, even my subordinates."

"Why?" Alice asked, raising her head in confusion.

"This is for your own good; demons and humans are ultimately different." Merlin answered tactfully, merely worried that the Elder Council's intelligence network is formidable—if I'm not around, it might possibly threaten the safety of mother and daughter.

"I understand." Alice nodded, not pursuing the reason, believing Merlin wouldn't harm her.

"By the way, take this.* Merlin handed Alice the 'Anjelier' ring, thinking wearing it on his hand would be of little use, the holy aura too offensive to him."

"I don't need it; you must wear it, just in case something happens—maybe."

"Alice." Merlin cut her off, his expression turning grave.

"This ring is somewhat useless to me; if I face an opponent I cannot defeat, reviving multiple times yields the same result, but for you it is quite useful."

"Do you know who I worry about most after I leave?"

"The person I miss most is still"

title: Chapter 44 — Sorry for the Late Update
content:
Chapter 44 — Sorry for the Late Update

Volume 32 · Chapter 44

Alice, your heart felt like it was being struck, and your face quickly turned red.

Was it me you were worried about? What does this mean? Am I that important to him?

Alice lowered her head nervously, feeling like Merlin might be hinting at something. Suddenly saying these strange things.

You and the child, Merlin completed the sentence in a big breath.

"Huh??"

Alice looked up blankly, thinking Merlin was most concerned about her alone. But now, including the baby, it was a completely different vibe.

It's true... I knew.

Alice sighed silently, already prepared for this, otherwise she might have been killed by Merlin.

"Okay, I understand. I'll avoid contact with demons for a while."

"That's it." Merlin's eyes darted around, scratching his nose. "I'm leaving?"

Alice's hands twitched together, whispering, "Be careful on the way."

Merlin nodded and turned toward the exit of the Ruksa town.

Alice watched Merlin's back, feeling an uncontrollable sense of loss. It might be a long time before they see each other again, and if something special happens, Merlin might only return even later.

But Merlin hadn't walked far when he suddenly turned back, staring at Alice without speaking, as if he had something in his stomach that he couldn't say.

"What's going on?" Alice was surprised, thinking Merlin didn't want to leave.

"Alice,"

Merlin frowned, hesitating to speak. He lied to Alice, and participating in the Seven Kings Conference wasn't easy. Even if they united with Leviathan, the negotiation weight wasn't enough. He knew the danger of the Seven Kings Conference and said it lightly to avoid making Alice too worried.

Merlin didn't know Alice's true feelings, but from some small things, he could tell she cared about him in an unusual way. So Merlin wanted to try to get closer to the real Alice. If it didn't work, he would slip away and return to his original self, forgetting everything that happened today.

The invincible First Demon Lord, who was surprisingly timid in pursuing a girl, only dared to do this at the moment of departure.

Merlin's feelings at the moment were the same as when he gave Asmodeus flowers, very tense. Talking about love was fine, but talking about feelings was like a coward.

Alice saw Merlin not saying anything, just standing there, like a telephone pole, and couldn't help but ask, "What's the matter? You're a bit strange today."

Merlin's face was stern and didn't answer, as if he was about to go to war, like a suicide squad charging forward.

Merlin put down his shoulder bag and didn't give Alice a chance to speak, directly pulling her into his arms and hugging her deeply.

"Ah?!!"

Alice's forehead hit Merlin's chest, feeling a bit painful, and her thoughts were already extremely difficult to think about.

Her cheeks were burning red, her body was stiff like wood, and her hands, which had nowhere to place, were pressed against Merlin's stomach.

Pushing Merlin away, she didn't want to.

Not pushing Merlin away, it didn't seem right either?

If Alice were a powerless girl, she might have been taken advantage of by a pervert. Hesitant, she didn't move in Merlin's arms, even when sleeping, she was usually so obedient.

Merlin's face was pressed against Alice's hair, with his eyes tightly closed. As soon as Alice pushed him away, he would immediately slip away, returning and not mentioning this incident, as if it never happened.

Fortunately, Alice was already disoriented, and being hugged by Merlin without hesitation, she was like a rabbit being carried by a big gray wolf, feeling dead.

Merlin let go of Alice, his eyes darting around, scratching his own hair, "Well,"

Alice came to her senses, feeling confused and disoriented, covering her mouth, staring at Merlin with an unbelievable look, "What are you doing?!"

"There's no other meaning, just" Merlin paused, whispering, "I wanted to hug you at the moment of departure."

"Ah? ? ?" Alice's mind was filled with question marks, her heart was about to jump out of her chest. In a panic, she pushed Merlin, "Hurry up. Chris is about to wake up, don't linger!"
