So what if ten thousandfold gravity suppression? Samael's physical strength had already exceeded the normal demon category. He tanked it without issue. Terrifying demigod-level pressure was rampaging — yet it was highly unstable, constantly wavering between pseudo-god and demigod tiers!

"Huh?!?" Merlin's eyes widened. He realized he had encountered his own kind — they were all monsters!

Samael instantly teleported in front of Merlin, grabbed his head with a massive hand, and violently slammed him toward the ground —

"Die!!!"

title: Chapter 55 — Council of the Seven Kings ①
content:
Chapter 55 — Council of the Seven Kings ①

Volume 32 · Chapter 55

Here's a translation that follows all the rules:

Slam—

Samiel grabbed Merlin's head and pressed it hard into the dirt, forcing him to have intimate contact with the filthy soil.

Merlin often used such insulting moves, yet today he was on the receiving end?

With a deafening roar, Merlin's heavy skull struck the ground's hard rocks, and the ground instantly sank!

With his true form opened, Samiel's power received an explosive increase; a single arm's strength was enough to completely suppress Merlin.

"Die."

Sound

Merlin's head was completely enveloped under Samiel's palm, his life had fallen into the enemy's hands, his breathing gradually became difficult, his gaze

staring at the angry monster before him, a furnace of anger burning in his abdomen, reflecting his own shadow.

Belial leaned on a staff, fanning the dust around himself with a handkerchief, then covering his mouth and nose, unable to hide the joy within him; in his eyes, Merlin had already walked into a dead end—

Not to be underestimated, being a monster that survived even after having its head cut off by its own younger brother; indeed extraordinary. Though its strength had long been greatly diminished, it could still preserve such deep power? If it hadn't encountered these misfortunes, perhaps it could have approached Methystos, the first arrogant monarch hailed as the strongest swordsman.

Consciousness began to become precarious. Merlin refused to give up, so he clenched his teeth, veins on his body bursting forth, his hands gripping Samiel's wrist, slowly lifting his palm off his face.

Samiel felt a hint of astonishment, not expecting Merlin, in this state, to still have the strength to resist himself?

Thus, angered, the flames on Samiel's body grew stronger, increasing the power on his hand. The unstable demigod pressure was immense, causing the ground beneath his feet to rumble, cracks spreading, rocks and stones blasted into the air, and Merlin only felt his head was about to explode.

"Enough already? If this continues, Samiel will really kill Lucifer, we must think of a way to stop it!" Leviathan whispered to Asmodeus, feeling Merlin had fallen into absolute passivity, and Samiel's loss of control might cause trouble!

"Forget it, I advise you not to meddle in other people's affairs. Belial and the other demon elders are watching us. If we dare to interfere in this matter, we won't have anything good to eat. We might even get beaten as traitors together with Merlin," Asmodeus shook his head.

"But..." Leviathan hesitated, knowing Merlin had committed a taboo, but he didn't think it was an irreparable thing. If Merlin were willing to sever ties with humans and return, everything could be discussed. But now, it seemed there was no room for maneuver anymore.

A sound of breaking the air rang out, the demon sword Banri Garan was thrown over by someone unknown, spinning in the air, circling toward Merlin and Samiel here!

Hmm? Who's meddling in secret? !

Belial alertly surveyed the surroundings, and after discovering the council had become a ruin, the scene was already in chaos, making it not easy to notice who threw the sword toward Merlin.

But in a daze, Belial saw a fallen angel with a missing arm hiding behind the ruins, secretly observing here. It was Helena, who had left Rukham!

Helena came here as a follower of Asmodeus, witnessing everything that happened. She had the courage to retrieve the Banri Garan and throw it to Merlin, definitely because her hand had received Asmodeus's secret order; everything was completed secretly in the chaos, leaving no traces.

Samiel immediately became alert, raising his extra arm to swing at the flying Banri Garan, but he missed. Everything was an illusion; there was nothing flying toward it!

With Samiel's strength, falling for an illusion was difficult. Those present who could confuse him, probably only one demon!

Samiel's attention was quickly drawn to Asmodeus, suspecting he had just cast a spell on himself. Seizing the opportunity, he released an illusion, though not powerful magic, only some interference, but it was enough to turn the tide.

Asmodeus's face didn't redden nor his heart race, looking into his mirror as if nothing had happened, making it hard to suspect him.

"What did you do?" Belial coldly looked at Asmodeus. In his eyes, Samiel suddenly punching the air for no reason—however one thought about it, someone must be up to mischief!

"Huh? What? I'm applying makeup, what can I do?" Asmodeus feigned a surprised expression, swearing he wouldn't admit to scheming against Samiel.

Belial couldn't produce any evidence, so he could only swallow this bitter breath. If Asmodeus had used magic, he could sense it immediately, but just now's misdirection was too strange; if one wasn't fully concentrated, it was undetectable.

Leviathan dropped a few black lines on his forehead, secretly asking, "Was it you? Just now you used an illusion on Samiel?"

You think so, that's that." Asmodeus replied lowly.

"You're really cunning, even I was fooled." Leviathan furrowed his brow. He had previously said he wouldn't meddle in other people's affairs, but it turned out he had secretly acted all along.

The true Banri Garan drew an arc in midair, safely falling into Merlin's hand. He looked at his beloved sword in astonishment, unbelieving that even at this moment, someone would willingly help him.

Black feathers slowly fell down. Merlin, out of the corner of his eye, saw Helena hiding behind the ruins. He immediately understood what was going on.

Seeing that Merlin had obtained the weapon, Helena thought to transform into a wisp of black smoke and disappear from her original position. She couldn't stay here any longer, lest other demon elders find trouble for her.

Merlin tightly gripped the Banri Garan in his hand. Though he didn't want to admit it: in a crisis, his "old love" was still reliable!

Merlin gritted his teeth and struggled to pull the blade of Banri Garan out a slice. Terrifying killing sword qi fiercely struck the dazed and chaotic Samiel, leaving dense knife marks on the ground. Samiel sensed the danger and quickly retreated from Merlin, but he was still slashed by the chaotic sword qi. A moment slower, and he might have lost his life.

Samiel barely stabilized his massive body, looking at his hands stained with his own black blood, falling into numbness. Besides his despicable brother, no one had ever been able to harm its body.

Cough—

Merlin climbed up from the ground, his face covered in dust, unhurriedly securing Banri Garan around his waist. "Ready to welcome your own defeat, Samiel?"

Samiel clenched all six arms into fists, emitting an angry roar. The damage to his body had already reached the bottom limit.

Flame membrane wings opened, the furnace in his abdomen burning fiercely. In an instant, the surroundings were transformed into a lava hell!

Samiel's unstable demigod pressure became extremely irritable, like a giant that had swallowed the sky awakening. His entire body's muscles were jumping rhythmically.

Merlin's expression was stern. He lightly stroked the sword handle, flipped it over, took a step backward, and assumed a drawing stance. A wisp of pale luster spurted from between his teeth—

"Hah—"

title: Chapter 56 — Council of Seven Kings Part II (Monthly Subscription Bonus)
content:
Chapter 56 — Council of Seven Kings Part II (Monthly Subscription Bonus)

Volume 32 · Chapter 56

Merlin and Samael locked cold gazes, and everything around them seemed to freeze, the silence terrifying.

Both Demon Lords understood that the outcome of their clash would be decided in an instant.

"Kill!!!"

Samael, overcome by rage, couldn't contain his surging fury and shattered the stalemate first.

A terrifying demigod-level pressure rolled in like a storm surge, and even from far away Merlin felt the piercing heat wash over him!

Samael vibrated his twelve flame-silk wings behind him, soaring into the sky and bringing a blazing firestorm upward, scorching the clouds red.

His crimson body almost merged with the molten furnace burning in his abdomen. The overwhelming fury made Merlin's eye twitch imperceptibly, forcing him to grip the hilt of his sword tighter!

Samael dove down, flying nearly skimming the ground, and flames roared up from all six strong arms, leaving nothing but scorched lava in his wake.

Merlin narrowed his eyes and flicked his fingers lightly against the hilt, producing a crisp "ting" sound as Banri Garan trembled faintly along its length.

The swirling dust parted slowly, and Merlin's figure was already gone from where he stood, moving so fast it was almost teleportation as he flashed directly in front of Samael.

Both were reckless and fearless monsters, and in their duel they showed no hesitation at all. Neither retreated an inch; instead, they closed in head-on for direct combat.

Merlin gripped the hilt tightly, his gaze coldly fixed on Samael at close range as though ready to draw his blade and deliver a fatal strike at any moment.

Samael suddenly felt a flicker of panic. Not wanting to be struck first by Merlin, he chose to strike preemptively, both fists wreathed in flame surging forward to hammer down on the returning Merlin!

Boom! The rapid explosions echoed across the earth, and the ground trembled continuously in anguish!

Rubble and dust slowly settled, and Samael realized all his attacks had missed, leaving behind countless craters on the ground.

Merlin had perfectly evaded every attack. The astonishing spectacle made Samael deeply doubt what he was seeing, and it muttered in bewilderment, "How did you... how did you do that?"

In the struggle on the mental level, Samael who struck first had already lost, temporarily stripped of all ability to resist Merlin. All it could hope for was its physique to withstand the iaijutsu strike. But could it truly endure it?

Merlin had already stepped halfway into Samael's forbidden territory. His towering and muscular frame now seemed clumsy and bulky, giving the opponent every advantage.

The moment had arrived. Banri Garan left its scabbard. Back edge as cutting edge, the drawing slash —

Merlin's figure flashed past Samael as he drew his blade, and his foot slammed hard against the ground to halt his charging form.

Samael stood dazed where it was, its massive build making anyone hesitate to approach rashly. No one knew whether it had truly withstood Merlin's iaijutsu or not.

"Who won?" Leviathan asked, not quite following the fight. The duel had ended too quickly — it was over in an instant.

"Do you need to ask?" Asmodeus observed Samael's condition from afar, able to feel the overwhelming fury rapidly dissipating.

Merlin didn't even turn his head and calmly returned his sword to its scabbard before responding coolly —

"Never think you're still the prodigy you once were. Your era is long past. Being defeated by me is nothing to be ashamed of."

Crack! Crack! Crack! The sound of breaking bones rang out continuously. Samael's body twisted to an incomprehensible degree, its enormous frame beginning to shrink.

That single strike from just now had instantly hit七八 joints across Samael's entire body, rendering this headless Demon Lord completely incapable of movement.

If Samael were a puppet, then its joints would be like the threads connecting its wooden pieces. Once those threads were severed, how could the puppet possibly still move?

Samael was deeply unwilling to accept this, yet its heavy body crashed to the ground, finding even moving a finger incredibly difficult.

Merlin hadn't killed Samael — in the end, he didn't wish to slaughter his own kind. If he had truly killed Samael, he would have become nothing more than a traitor who destroyed his own race.

Beelzebub slowly closed his eyes and continued playing dead on the ground, thinking to himself how fortunate he was for not stubbornly clashing to the death against Lucifer earlier. Otherwise, he'd be lying on the ground just like Samael, unable to move at all.

With Samael defeated, Leviathan swallowed hard. It felt it could duel Merlin at least in the sea, but on land it stood virtually no chance. "Among our second-generation monarchs, could there really be no one left who can defeat him?"

"Seems so," Asmodeus muttered, a bead of cold sweat trickling down his forehead, then adding, "Though it might be possible she — Vivian."

"Are you kidding?" Leviathan found that hard to swallow. Vivian had been defeated by the Hero. How could she possibly be Merlin's match?

"Samael lost his head, which greatly reduced his power and also stripped away most of his ability to think. Losing to Lucifer was a matter of course. But Vivian is different. Her talent isn't inferior to Samael's. If she were still alive, she might have been able to rein in her son." Asmodeus reasoned. Vivian and Samael were the twin stars of the second-generation Demon Lords, both possessing remarkable talent. In theory, their achievements should have been close to those of the great first-generation Demon Lords.

"Vivian died at the hands of the Holy Church's Hero. Compared to Samael, her talent was like a fabrication entirely. There's nothing comparable about it," Leviathan objected incredulously.

"I harbor doubts about Vivian's death. She possessed such immense potential, yet became the first monarch in history to fall to a Hero's hand. Don't you find that suspicious? If Mammon had died at the hands of a Hero, I wouldn't be surprised in the least," Asmodeus said pointedly.

"Huh...?" Leviathan's brows furrowed, unable to help but recall certain events from back then. Upon hearing the news of Vivian's defeat, he had also been shocked and briefly suspected whether the Holy Church's power had already grown to such a degree that it could breed a Hero capable of killing Vivian. But now that he thought about it, there seemed to be some questionable points.

Berial stared at Merlin's figure, his unease growing within him.

Samael had been defeated. He had almost dominated Lucifer just now, only to lose so thoroughly?

What was he supposed to do now? They couldn't defeat Lucifer the Third with a drawn sword!

He had to think of some way to get the Referee to deploy the Demonic Sealing Pot.

Berial's gaze fell on Caprio, who was hiding behind a rock, wondering what pretext he could use to force the other to hand over the Demonic Sealing Pot.

Suddenly, Merlin's figure appeared before Berial, blocking his line of sight. That piercing gaze sent a chill rising from the depths of his soul.

"Hmm?"

Without another word, Merlin drew his blade directly. The blade scraping against the scabbard sent sparks flying. This highly respected first-generation Demon Lord — what schemes lay in his mind? He was always trying to drag the demon race into the quagmire of war, and had the audacity to slander him as a "traitor." How could he let him off so easily?

"Hmph."

Berial sneered. Facing Merlin's iaijutsu, he still maintained his composure. Instead of advancing, he retreated — closing in on Merlin with an eerie bodily movement!

He forcefully shoved the half-drawn Banri Garan back into its scabbard!

One of Berial's hands pressed against the top of the hilt to prevent Merlin from drawing, while his other hand had already clamped onto Merlin's throat —

"Young man, don't be so impulsive. You'll pay for your recklessness."

title: Chapter 57 — Seven Kings' Meeting III
content:
Chapter 57 — Seven Kings' Meeting III

Volume 32 · Chapter 57

The draw-and-slash wasn't unleashed. Merlin felt a jolt of astonishment, wondering inwardly —

Strange. This is my first time fighting Belial, so why does it understand my iaijutsu so well? It even knows the weak point inherent to the draw-cut.

Merlin found it inconceivable. No enemy had ever realized that before. This was the first time his draw-and-slash had been interrupted mid-execution.

Belial's left hand pinned the hilt of Banri Garan, his right hand clamped around Merlin's throat, wearing a half-smile that looked as if he had already seen through every one of Merlin's moves.

Merlin didn't dare move rashly for the moment. Belial's sharp fingers sank deeper into his flesh; at this rate his throat would be crushed first.

"Hmm?" Belial stared into Merlin's eyes, taunting, "You look surprised. Is it because you couldn't defeat me in one blow, and you're puzzled?"

"What nonsense are you spouting?"

Merlin shot back, his gaze shifting instantly. He stomped the ground hard with his right foot, sprang up, and drove a kick straight between Belial's legs!

"Eek—" Asmodeus frowned, unable to bear watching.

Too brutal. Leviathan hurriedly lowered his head. What had been a solemn occasion turned awkward in an instant.

The ball-shattering atmosphere made every demon's jaw drop, a chill running through their crotches. Who would have guessed a noble monarch would use such a shameless move? No different from thugs brawling in a tavern!

"Gah???" Belial's face twisted hideously, eyeballs nearly popping from their sockets. Agony from his groin blanked his mind. He never expected Merlin to sink this low! A Demon Lord's glory and dignity had long been tossed into the trash.

Merlin pressed the advantage without a word, dropping into a half-crouch and drawing the blade in an instant with the spine as the edge. The hardened spine slammed into Belial's abdomen, and the air erupted like a bomb, sending concentric shockwaves rippling out of nowhere!

Belial spat a mouthful of old blood and shot backward with a "whoosh," smashing a massive wall to rubble.

A single strike, and Belial was grievously wounded. Who knew how many bones were shattered inside him? He lay on the ground, barely breathing.

"Nothing but framing, trying to kill me — what exactly is your goal?" Merlin sheathed his sword, questioning in a grave tone.

*Cough.* Belial staggered to his feet, wiping blood from the corner of his mouth with a handkerchief, laughing miserably. "Truly remarkable. The young ones nowadays, each more formidable than the last."

"Answer my question." Merlin stepped forward, pressing him.

"Why target you? Because you violated the demon race's taboo. A traitor, to be killed by all." Belial's lips curled up, convinced Merlin was the worst traitor in demon history.

"I admit I was with a human woman." Merlin paused, emphasizing, "But Mammon's death has nothing to me. I didn't do it."

"What gibberish is this? That's a sophistry that dodges the real issue. Your word alone — who would believe you? Would a murderer be stupid enough to run into the street shouting 'I'm not the killer'?" Belial drew a deep breath, suppressing the pain of his broken bones. "Even if you didn't kill Mammon, you loved a human and sired a child. That violates the demon race's taboo — grounds enough for execution. Ironclad proof, Lucifer..."

"That child's origin is strange. Not what you think." Merlin stressed seriously.

"What's left to quibble about now? Will the elders listen to your lies?" Belial pointed at Merlin, bluntly: "Precisely because you colluded with humans, you had ample motive to murder Mammon. Hope you understand — I don't doubt for a second you'd have the courage to slay your own kin to protect your wife and child."

"Seems there's no room for negotiation left." Merlin sighed, turned, and walked away. "I won't fear your pursuit. However many come, I'll kill that many. My patience has limits. Next time we meet, it won't be the blade's spine striking you. If you want to judge me, you'd best weigh your own strength first."

"Hey! Lucifer!" Leviathan tried to stop Merlin, feeling his attitude was wrong.

"Don't call me that name anymore." Merlin halted, looked back. "I'm an exiled failure, unworthy to stand alongside you. Better make a clean break. Each walk our own path, and we'll leave each other alone from now on."

"Haha." Belial laughed, shaking his head. "Lucifer, you really think you can sever all ties with the demon race? Dream on. A demon is a demon. Even death can't change your birth. Once your identity is exposed, you'll be a rat crossing the street — everyone shouting to beat you. The human realm isn't your home, and it's certainly no sanctuary where you can survive."

"That's none of your business. I only know next time I see you, I'll take your head." Merlin's voice was ice-cold.

"You think you can leave here today? How naive." Belial's words carried a clear warning.

"What? You want to die?" Merlin's gaze turned frigid, fixed on Belial, hand unconsciously tightening on the blade at his waist.

Belial sneered repeatedly, one hand pointing to heaven, one to earth. The pressure of the Divine Realm exploded outward. Wisps of nearly translucent golden mana rose endlessly, surging toward the sky.

"Hmm?" Merlin went on instant alert, ears ringing, sensing an overwhelmingly dangerous presence!

The pressure Belial radiated held an overwhelming advantage over Samael — they couldn't even be compared. This was likely the absolute limit of power a mortal creature could reach: stepping into the Divine Realm!

The demon race's prosperity rested on the seven Divine Realm monarchs holding the line. As the sole surviving first-generation Demon Lord, Belial's strength was beyond question. It was his existence that allowed the demon race to endure and carry the glory of the Demon Age to this day!

The Divine Realm was a realm countless people fantasized about. No longer a level one could assault through talent alone — it required no small measure of luck to achieve.

Reaching this realm, one's power could truly be called that of a living god. Mana and battle aura were virtually infinite, never exhausted. Even the precious Divine Power could be used at will. An existence of strength beyond countless people's reach.

The Divine Realm was the watershed between mortal flesh and godhood, cleaving all mundane beings apart. Those who crossed that threshold became controllers who swayed the world. Those who couldn't were merely slightly stronger mortals.

Belial commanded vast power in the demon race and the devotion of countless demons not through noble character or charisma, but through genuine, tyrannical strength!

"That move — is it the Sin Domain?!" Asmodeus's eyes widened in shock, body trembling involuntarily.

"What?" Leviathan's head was full of question marks, not quite understanding what Asmodeus meant.

"Legend says those who step into the Divine Realm gain the ability to open worlds, to create their own rule-based powers with their own hands, like a Creator." Asmodeus paused, swallowing nervously —

"The Sin Domain is a land of death Belial created with his own hands. Within his own domain..."

"He is an invincible god!"

title: Chapter 58 — Seven Kings Meeting ④
content:
Chapter 58 — Seven Kings Meeting ④

Volume 32 · Chapter 58

“According to what I know, Sin Domain is Belial's strongest ultimate skill. Those trapped inside will be eternally scorched by karmic fire; no one can come out alive. It should be considered a sealing technique with no weaknesses.” Asmodeus paused, continuing to recall, “In that previous brutal holy war, Belial used Sin Domain to seal a great number of holy spirits, even a powerful holy spirit leader was burned to ashes within Sin Domain.” Leviathan stared at Belial in shock, sweating and muttering, “Lucifer, isn't he going to be terribly unlucky?” “Lucifer! Be careful! Don't get trapped in Belial's domain, otherwise you might never escape!” Asmodeus, in his urgency, didn't care about anything else and loudly reminded Merlin. Merlin listened with a head full of question marks; obviously he didn't know much about Belial, had no idea how dangerous he was, but since Asmodeus reminded him, he couldn't help but become much more serious, wanting to see what Belial was up to. The surging Divine Power swept fiercely around, making Merlin realize that the old man before him was an enemy he had never seen before! The Dark Elf King Ashmodor in the pseudo‑god realm, when facing any enemy, would not casually use Divine Power with limited uses; even as a demigod, Samael could only use Divine Power freely within a limited time. But Belial, who had already stepped into the god realm, had no such limits; his Divine Power was nearly infinite, a mere gesture could cause heaven and earth to change. Merlin's magic immunity was completely ineffective against Belial; this would inevitably turn into a fist‑to‑flesh brawl. The power of the god realm summoned black raging winds, their howls comparable to a monster's roar, forcing many demons to retreat. The sky was covered with dark clouds, from time to time thunderous booms echoed, vortices churned heaven and earth, madly devouring space! The ground beneath Belial's feet began to melt, scorching magma rose in layers, a huge red magic circle appeared out of nowhere, slowly rotating! That overwhelming god‑realm pressure caused several demon lords to drastically change their faces; they realized Belial was serious—this wasn't an operation to capture Merlin, but preparation to kill him! “This chilling killing intent…” Merlin furrowed his brows, his teeth clenched and grinding, he had no concept of gods; until now he had only seen the skeleton left by the elf god Kurelion, but the Belial before him was completely different from that lifeless skeleton! He had no doubt that he was facing a living, true god! All along Merlin never thought he could become an opponent of a god; until this moment, he gained some understanding of so‑called gods, believing those lofty beings looking down on all life were not that remarkable— they too would bleed, they too would suffer miserable cries, they too could be slain by greater foes! Those who stand atop the food chain ruling all life with power, using the title “god” to deceive the ignorant, deserve no worship or respect! Merlin's rebellious heart was fully ignited; an uncontrollable impulse surged in his chest, wanting to drag those high‑and‑mighty clowns down from their pedestals, rip off their masks to show all beings their ugly, filthy true faces—whether they deserved respect or not! Undoubtedly Merlin's veins boiled with god‑slaying blood; such rebels possess a distinctive, independent personality—anti‑rule, anti‑tradition, anti‑covenant, they must overturn everything they find displeasing. Historically, most similar individuals were considered madmen, polarized: either traitors to rules or pioneers of the age. What they share is only the land they've walked, leaving behind only devastation and flowing blood— Merlin had made up his mind: whoever blocks his path today will be sent to the underworld by his own hand. Although it's unknown just how strong Belial truly is, Merlin is willing to be the one who steps forward to challenge authority—whether gods are invincible? That answer will only come after he cuts them down! Merlin has already sensed Belial's killing intent; since the opponent shows no mercy, he will give his all— The elders all think I'm a demon race traitor who killed Mammon, right? Fine, then I'll truly slay a monarch for you to see—I'll accept being a traitor! “Lucifer, let you see what happens when you defy my will!” Belial shouted—his immaculate uniform fluttered in the gale, two fingers pointing in different directions traced—suddenly! Behind Belial, space split open, a massive towering stone gate appeared, the scorching aura of sin filling heaven and earth! “The Gate of Sin Domain” Asmodeus's face turned grim, his whole body shivered, “I've never seen this before; the rumors about Belial are indeed true.” Leviathan was stunned, eyes unblinking fixed on the Gate of Sin Domain; even from afar he could feel a wave of heat. The Gate of Sin Domain is enormous, its top nearly reaching the clouds; countless demons at its feet look like ants. The tightly shut door panels are covered in dense carvings; upon closer look they are records of that brutal holy war, demons and holy spirits carved lifelike, as if they could come alive at any moment. Just from the carvings one can feel the cruelty of that holy war—both sides' forces had eyes red with killing, lives became the cheapest thing. The topmost content is especially striking: the lofty goddess descended with world‑destroying divine punishment; six brave first‑generation demon lords burned themselves to desperately resist the fate of extermination; Belial, as an elder, guarded the demon race's infants and raised them—this side of the carving fully displays the cruelty of the holy war, enough to make even those sharp‑tongued demon‑race elders tear up. Belial slowly opened his eyes, standing straight before the massive Gate of Sin Domain, assuming the posture of a judge looking down on Merlin— “Lucifer, you have no retreat left; using force to defy the elders' sanctions is how foolish an act? Your sins are too heavy; I will, in the name of the first‑generation monarch, pronounce your death sentence!” “Has it come to the point of irreconcilable enmity?” Asmodeus lowered his face, hesitating whether to help; this time Merlin probably truly can't escape, Belial has already executed the elders' sanction in their place. Leviathan watched the lonely figure in the arena, noticing Merlin trembling all over, “Lucifer, are you finally feeling afraid? I thought he was a fearless lunatic.” Asmodeus followed Leviathan's gaze, glanced over, and said meaningfully, “It's not fear— the pressure of the god realm breeds despair, leaving no spark of resistance; Merlin's whole body trembles, he grips his sword hilt, assumes a draw stance, the corner of his mouth unconsciously twitches— That's not fear, it's an unprecedented excitement! He can clearly feel the rebellious heart in his chest screaming nonstop! The god‑slaying blood boiling in his veins! Never in his life has Merlin felt such a sensation; his whole body boils with it! “This… is what it feels like to slay a god?”

title: Chapter 59 — The Seven Kings' Council ① (Monthly Ticket Bonus Update)
content:
Chapter 59 — The Seven Kings' Council ① (Monthly Ticket Bonus Update)

Volume 32 · Chapter 59

Merlin had always been looking forward to being killed by a true powerhouse, whether from easing the curse on his heart or from the sense of accomplishment of defeating an opponent, he was extremely

obsessed.

He didn't care much for opponents he'd defeated before, and they were hard to keep memorized.

But Belial was different. This Demon Lord who had stepped into the Divine Realm obviously already qualified to be Merlin's opponent.

"Lucifer, I sentence you to be confined within my Domain of Sin until your soul is burned away, so that your sins may be cleansed!"

Belial's gaze was sharp as he tossed a handkerchief toward Merlin. The blood-stained cloth danced through the air like a butterfly, gradually turning into filthy ash.

Suddenly, the Door of Sin behind Belial emitted thunderous rumblings, and the tightly closed stone door gradually swung—

Leviathan nervously swallowed. "What's with this ominous feeling?"

"Let's back away. If we get dragged into Belial's Domain of Sin for no reason, we're dead for certain." Asmodeus warned sternly.

Once the Door of Sin opened, nothing inside could be seen. Only endless crimson karmic flames were burning fiercely. Staring at it too long would cause one's consciousness to sink imperceptibly into it!

Crackle! Accompanied by periodic booms, countless flame arms stretched out from the karmic flames inside the door. They writhed rapidly, moving at extraordinary speed toward Merlin, trying to pull him into the Domain of Sin!

Merlin's eye twitched violently. He sprang up from the ground, using repulsive spatial techniques to rotate through the air and dodge, barely escaping the grasping karmic flame hands through narrow gaps.

Massive flame arms slammed into the ground with loud thuds, triggering tremendously powerful explosions. Everything they passed through became scorched wasteland.

The karmic flames were composed of Divine Power. Merlin's magic immunity was useless against these things; he could only rely on alertness to dodge!

Watching the flame arms below his feet that had missed their mark, a drop of cold sweat slid down Merlin's forehead. Attacks formed from Divine Power were sure to harm him. He needed to be careful!

The karmic flame hands were thoroughly unwilling to have missed capturing Merlin. They began dancing wildly again, crisscrossing each other to form a formation resembling a flame net, determined not to let him slip away.

Before long, the flame net made of arms closed in from all directions, further pushing Merlin toward the Door of Sin!

In desperation, Merlin swiftly drew his blade and sliced the flame net into pieces. Even terrifying Divine Power was completely obliterated beneath his sword, giving him enormous confidence—

Slaying gods was not impossible!

"Fascinating! Belial! Only an enemy like you is worthy! Hahaha!"

Merlin laughed wildly, so excited he could barely restrain his emotions. Compared to enemies he'd encountered before, only Belial could bring him this kind of enjoyment.

Belial's expression darkened immediately. He began secretly manipulating the flame hands, wanting to see how long Merlin could stay so arrogant!

As soon as Merlin landed, massive karmic flames erupted from the ground all around him with thumping sounds. They quickly converged, forming a karmic flame hand many times larger than before, and crashed down toward Merlin with a tremendous force!

"It's useless." Merlin sneered and slashed the karmic flame hand in one stroke once more. Countless small flames drifted around him like stars in the night sky.

However, this time the dispersed karmic flames did not dissipate. Instead, they rapidly collided, and the flames flared up enormously!

Small fireballs formed chains, binding Merlin's limbs and refusing to let him sheathe Banri Garan.

The Sword of Drawing required the blade to continuously gather momentum within the scabbard. Without that process, the iai draw strike could not be unleashed. Belial had actually seen through this!

"!??"

Merlin stared in shock, unable to believe Belial had set so many traps for him. One wrong step and he'd step on a landmine. Suspicion churned within him. Just how thoroughly had this old man studied his sword-drawing techniques? They were fighting for the first time—there was no way he should be able to discern so many things!

"Hehe~" A satisfied grin spread across Belial's face. "A version of you who can't use the iai draw is completely harmless!"

Before the words had finished falling, a giant flame arm emerged from the Door of Sin and seized Merlin in a single grip without any hesitation, dragging him straight into the chamber!

This happened so quickly that Merlin didn't even have time to resist, leaving Asmodeus and Leviathan stunned in place.

Rummmble——

The Door of Sin slowly closed, sealing the exit completely. No one knew what kind of torture Merlin would suffer within the Domain of Sin, but judging from what Asmodeus had said, he would surely suffer greatly!

"Finally—" Belial muttered with a dark face, then suddenly raised his head, his inner elation impossible to hide—

Hehehehahaha!!!

Finally, I've actually done it! I was right all along—toppling them from within is the correct approach!

With the greatest obstacle cleared, who else could possibly threaten me? No one!

It's over. Today is a day I will never forget. My soul and body will both—

Burning, unbearable, excruciating heat. His body felt like it was about to melt away.

Darkness, an endless darkness without end in sight. His consciousness kept falling deeper into the abyss.

Sin, an ever-present sin that drove people mad. His spirit was undergoing relentless torment and affliction.

Even souls here would turn to ashes. Perhaps death was the best release.

Merlin's eyes snapped open. Pain from being burned coursed through his entire body. Biting his teeth, he pushed himself up from the ground and discovered his body was slowly disintegrating into ash.

Looking around, this was a world composed entirely of crimson karmic flames. No matter where he stood, the flames scorched him. There was nowhere to hide.

Flowing lava and ruins filled every direction. Bones were piled in every corner, especially those of spirits and humans—clearly they had all been Belial's primary enemies.

Merlin picked up his blade and sheathed it, carefully surveying the area. It looked like a independently created miniature world, specifically designed to imprison and execute those who defied Belial's will.

Look at this group of pitiful wretches below his feet whose very souls had been extinguished, leaving only bones behind. This might well be Merlin's own ultimate fate.

The situation before him couldn't help but remind Merlin of his battle against the vampire Carmilla. That woman had similarly used her magic to create the Blood Moon Marsh—a dead zone of sorts.

But Belial and Carmilla were completely different and couldn't be compared in the same breath—

Carmilla's Blood Moon Marsh took an existing dead zone and turned it into her toy, continuously nourishing the marsh with her magic.

Belial's Domain of Sin, however, was created ex nihilo using Divine Power, rivaling a true world.

In terms of danger level, power, or intensity? Someone like Carmilla's Blood Moon Marsh couldn't even be shown on the same stage. The gap between them was like the unbridgeable chasm between mortals and gods—as vast as the universe itself.

Merlin gasped sharply from the pain, looking down at his hands as they were continuously scorched by karmic flames. Faint white bone could be seen beneath. He subconsciously clenched his fists and gritted his teeth, thinking—

I must find a way to leave this place!

Otherwise, going on like this—

I might end up keeping company with all these bones scattered across the ground!

Damn old man. Does he really think he can keep me caged?

It's time to show him the iai draw that severs heaven and earth.

Dear readers, please throw some monthly tickets my way. Thank you, thank you!

Throwing monthly tickets is truly such an aloof way of communicating.

It gives the author absolutely no chance to make excuses or procrastinate with babbling.

It's just wildly slapping the author's face with monthly tickets, pointing at his nose and telling him—

"Cut the chatter and give me more updates."

_(°w°)∠)_

title: Chapter 60 — Seven Kings Meeting 6
content:
Chapter 60 — Seven Kings Meeting 6

Volume 32 · Chapter 60

“Slash!”

The Iai Slash erupted with a killing aura of sword intent beyond imagination, churning the Sin Domain upside down. This small world trembled endlessly under Merlin’s blade.

The earth beneath his feet collapsed and shattered, as if a chasm-like rift appeared on the ground, extending all the way to the end of the Sin Domain!

The sky was forcibly split open by a massive crack, faintly revealing gaps in space, while a fierce storm temporarily suppressed the karmic fire within the Sin Domain!

By all rights, the Sin Domain should have completely collapsed after suffering such severe trauma, but when Merlin looked up, he found that the severed sky and the crumbling earth had rapidly repaired themselves to their original state, failing to disintegrate as he had expected.

"As expected, getting out of here isn't that simple. This place is completely different from the Blood Moon Swamp; it cannot be destroyed so easily."

Merlin frowned tightly, sheathing his sword and thinking carefully. Since the Sin Domain could repair itself, destroying this place would be too difficult for him.

According to Merlin's own speculation, the Sin Domain should be directly connected to Belial. As long as Belial outside did not die, the Sin Domain would use Belial's Divine Power to repair itself infinitely.

"Tsk! What a hassle."

Merlin couldn't help but complain. If he couldn't even leave this place himself, how could he make a move against Belial in the outside world?

Asmodeus and Leviathan definitely wouldn't easily become enemies with Belial. Was he really going to be trapped here forever?

Merlin examined his own condition and realized that under the scorching of the karmic fire, his physical body might turn to ash first.

Just as Merlin stood there at a loss, accompanied by the sound of the wind, a strange voice suddenly emerged.

"Sigh—"

"Hm?"

Merlin subconsciously raised his head, staring in one direction, puzzled in his heart. Who let out that sigh? No way? Is there anyone else alive here besides me?

He found it hard to imagine that in a world constantly burned by karmic fire, there could still be living creatures. He didn't know what kind of creature had let out that sigh.

After some thought, Merlin decided to investigate first. Since he couldn't think of a way to leave the Sin Domain for now, perhaps following the sound of this sigh might lead to some clues?

Having made up his mind, Merlin quickly moved toward the direction the wind came from, crossing numerous cliffs and precipices, until he finally made a new discovery in the core area of the Sin Domain—

On top of a spire sat a huge black cross, with many crows circling overhead, making阵阵 "waah—waah" calls, sounding very creepy and making Merlin feel quite uncomfortable.

A horned demon grew at the intersection of the black cross, with only its shoulders and above remaining; the rest of its body had been swallowed by the black cross and merged into one.

This old-looking demon was different from normal living demons, emitting white light and smoke all over its body. It appeared to have no physical form, being merely a soul without a body.

The hungry crows had long pecked open the demon soul's head, orderly devouring the essence within its brain, each one wolfing it down greedily.

Strangely enough, the flesh and blood on the demon soul seemed endless; the parts eaten by the crows would always grow back again.

The demon soul hung its head listlessly, occasionally letting out a deep sigh. Regardless of the crows pecking at it, one could hardly see any pain on its face; it had obviously grown accustomed to this state of torment.

When seeing this demon soul, Merlin stared in shock, subconsciously gripping the hilt of his sword at his waist, looking as if facing a formidable enemy.

"Belial..."

One crow, unable to get food, flapped its wings and flew in front of the demon soul, frantically pecking at its eyes, trying to dig them out and eat them.

The demon soul began to resist, but with no hands and most of its body swallowed by the black cross, it could only shake its head and roar continuously.

"Stop it! You beasts, don't eat my eyes! Forgive me, why must I suffer this torment!"

No matter how the demon soul resisted, it could hardly stop the crows from pecking open its eyes. The mournful horns of pain made people unable to bear looking directly.

Merlin frowned, his tense mood easing slightly, feeling that something was wrong—

Wait a minute!

Is this unlucky old man really Belial?

Compared to that arrogant old guy outside the Sin Domain, the difference is too great!

If this is Belial, then who is the person fighting him outside the Sin Domain?

It looks like the soul is trapped here, but who is controlling Belial's body?

A flood of questions surged into his mind. Merlin couldn't get accurate answers, but seeing this demon soul so miserable, it seemed to pose no threat, so he boldly walked closer.

Merlin couldn't figure out the relationship between this demon soul, which looked extremely similar to Belial, and the Belial wreaking havoc outside. Could Belial have a twin brother? Having lived among the demon race for so long, he had never heard that Belial had siblings.

"Let me go... You swallow my soul every day, why... why aren't you satisfied yet..." The demon soul begged humbly, its gaze empty and lifeless, clearly having completely broken down mentally and physically.

Whoosh—

A stone flew at extreme speed, instantly killing the crow that was pecking at the eyes.

Seeing this, the other crows fled in terror, daring not to approach the fierce-looking Merlin.

Merlin walked to the bottom of the huge black cross, looking up at the demon soul trapped inside. Getting closer, he could see more clearly.

The tormented demon soul also raised its head to examine Merlin. Since no humans had been imprisoned in the Sin Domain for a long time, it seemed somewhat puzzled, looking dazed, like an elderly person with dementia observing an outsider.

However, not long after, a hint of emotion flowed across its stiff, aged face, and some color returned to the depths of its empty eyes, as if recalling something?

"Merlin Lucifer, son of Vivian, the second Pride Demon Lord. Why are you appearing here?"

"Hm?" Merlin became even more puzzled. If the other party could recognize him, then it obviously had a connection with Belial.

"Ah..." Belial slowly opened his eyes wide, his state gradually becoming clear. "In my memory, you were still a child. I didn't expect... you've grown this big already? How long have I been locked up here? Thousands of years? Tens of thousands of years?"

Merlin's expression turned very serious, realizing that things were not simple. Belial's Seventh Demon Lord Palace had likely undergone changes long ago, though the entire demon race remained unaware.

"Please answer my question seriously. Who are you?"

"Who am I?" The demon soul pondered, its eyes gradually shimmering with light, answering in a tone full of majesty—

"I remember now..."

"I am the Master of the Seventh Demon Lord Palace, the first King representing Sloth!"

"Belial MacBelial!"

title: Chapter 61 — Seven Kings' Council ⑦
content:
Chapter 61 — Seven Kings' Council ⑦

Volume 32 · Chapter 61

"Belial!" Merlin was quite startled, unconsciously taking a step back. If this was the real Belial, then who exactly was the guy fighting him outside?!

"What's with that reaction? Do I look that scary?" Belial's soul gaze was full of confusion.

"Are you sure everything you're saying is true?" Merlin didn't relax his guard, but instead wanted to figure out the situation. "Before I was dragged into the Sin Domain, I was fighting Belial to a standstill outside. You say you're the real Belial, then who is the guy out there?!"

"Oh? I see, I understand." Belial's soul eyes widened in shock. Listening to Merlin's doubts, it instantly figured out what had happened. "Has Behemoth finally made a move on you?"

"Behemoth? Who is that?" Merlin furrowed his brows and pressed.

"You, as Vivian's son, have already come into contact with the Blood Pool Seal beneath the Demon Lord Palace, right?" Belial seemed unaware that Vivian was gone and that Merlin had already inherited the throne.

"Of course. Isn't it the seal that imprisons a Demon God? Known as the ancestor of the entire demon race," Merlin answered solemnly.

"That's exactly it. Behemoth is the name of that Demon God, the title of the very first demon in history, and an outstanding figure among the ancient gods' faction." Belial's soul paused, then continued. "My body was long ago occupied by Behemoth. I know nothing about what happens outside."

Merlin broke into a sweat, finding Belial's words hard to believe. "You… say… your body has been taken over by something else? How long exactly have you been trapped here?"

"How long? I can't remember clearly, but I do remember you. Back then you were still an infant in Vivian's arms." Belial could only give a rough estimate, completely unaware of what Behemoth had done with its body.

Merlin staggered and did a quick calculation. Belial had likely been locked in the Sin Domain for nearly two hundred years. If everything he said were true, then he truly knew nothing about outside affairs. "You're joking, right? The Blood Pool Seal is still perfectly intact, with absolutely no abnormalities. How could the Demon God Behemoth possibly take over your body?"

"Indeed, no one noticed. I only realized something was wrong after Behemoth seized my body. The Blood Pool Seal isn't as intact as you see it—there are already hidden cracks in the seal," Belial replied sorrowfully.

"No way? All seven Demon Lord Palaces strictly maintain the seal, never showing the slightest negligence," Merlin rebutted.

"In that ancient Holy War, when the battle between demons and spirits reached its final moment, the great doors of the Heavenly Realm were about to close. That exalted Goddess personally unleashed divine punishment. This immense power could have destroyed all seven Demon Lord Palaces, dooming the demons to extinction. But under your grandfather's leadership, joining other monarchs who had stepped into the God Realm, they burned their own lives to avert that fate."

"Without a doubt, your grandfather and the six other monarchs are the saviors of the demon race. They gave their lives to guard the last ember. My strength is nowhere near worthy of standing beside them. As the youngest and weakest of the first-generation monarchs, I was ordered to survive—to lead the remaining demons in rebuilding our homeland. Because even after the war ended, the Goddess's agents left in the mortal world would never abandon their desire to exterminate the demon race. We needed a powerful demon who had reached the God Realm to deter enemies and also to protect the young demons so they could grow up quickly."

"I still remember that day vividly; I will never forget. The divine punishment that descended from the depths of the Heavenly Realm's great doors boiled the sky itself. Wherever the light shone, all life was instantly vaporized. It was a slaughter with no suspense. I watched helplessly as my companions turned to ash. Your grandfather, together with the other monarchs, sacrificed themselves to barely hold back the Goddess's wrath. It was so tragic—they were actually quite decent fellows."

Merlin furrowed his brows. Although he knew Belial was dodging the question, he could still sense a hint of desolation in his words. These matters, Vivian as his mother had hardly ever spoken of. Perhaps it was because he had been too young back then?

"Sorry, it's been a long time since anyone came to talk to me. I unintentionally went on and on. Just consider it an old man's rambling." Belial's soul felt somewhat weary, realizing he shouldn't have said those useless things.

"It's fine. Even if you don't say it, I would have found out sooner or later," Merlin replied calmly, thinking that this guy had been locked up for too long. Suddenly encountering someone to talk to, it was natural that he'd lose control.

"When the Goddess unleashed her punishment, the force kept slamming head-on into the Demon Lord Palaces. Even though your grandfather managed to barely fend off the attack, it still jolted the Blood Pool Seal considerably. I suspect that's when the seal cracked, giving Behemoth an opportunity to exploit," Belial's soul speculated. These were all things it only realized after its body was taken over.

"So the Demon God is no longer in the seal, right?" Merlin thought the current situation was extremely serious, pertaining to the survival of the demon race.

"To be precise, Behemoth's physical body remains within the Blood Pool Seal, but its soul has already escaped and seized my body," Belial's soul explained.

"The soul escaped?" Merlin felt somewhat puzzled.

"That's right. I think you should know that the first-generation demons and Behemoth, their creator, share an absolute bloodline connection. From the second generation onward, that connection grows progressively weaker. So although Behemoth's death would trigger a chain reaction, only I, a first-generation demon, would die together with it. Demons of the second generation and beyond would not be affected." Belial's soul paused, then continued. "I once heard your grandfather say that the Prophet had considered killing Behemoth, but the demon race would be instantly wiped out. The only option was to seal it beneath the Blood Pool, then, after continually breeding to sever the bloodline connection, kill Behemoth. Who would have thought its soul would escape first?"

"Since it has already taken over your body, could my body also be seized at any moment?" Merlin felt worried, and the thought alone made him nauseous.

"Don't be so nervous. Behemoth can possess only a very limited number of bodies, and it can only seize those of the first-generation demons who share its bloodline. You, as a third-generation demon, and the other second-generation demons, are all relatively safe. Old guys like me are already rare among the demon race—the future belongs to you young demons," Belial's soul sighed.

"I see." Merlin slightly relaxed his tension, lifted his head and said solemnly, "Now I understand. I've been wondering all along why someone as venerable as you would constantly target me, forcing me to go all out. If someone has taken over your body, then I won't hold back anymore."

"Behemoth targeting you was the right choice." Belial's soul fell silent for a moment, then asked curiously—

"Has your mother Vivian ever told you about the prophecy left by the Prophet?"

title: Chapter 62 — Seven Kings Conference 8 (Monthly Bonus)
content:
Chapter 62 — Seven Kings Conference 8 (Monthly Bonus)

Volume 32 · Chapter 62

"This one—" Merlin hesitated, thinking the prophet's prophecy probably wasn't the one he had found in the Ruins of the Gods. Besides, back when he was a kid, his mom never used to talk about this stuff.

"Looks like it doesn't." Beelzebub's soul read the answer from Merlin's expression. "Vivian probably didn't want you to bear too much pressure. She wanted you to have a carefree childhood, which is why she kept those things hidden. Your mother was more responsible than any other demon parent in the race. You're lucky."

??? Merlin's mind was full of question marks. Based on his own firsthand childhood experiences, that was completely not the case!

"There are three parts to the prophet's prophecy." Beelzebub paused, then spoke solemnly—

"The first: the mortal world will face a severe crisis, with danger coming from all sides. For the demon race to continue, the seven Demon Lord Palaces must unite, choose a defensible stronghold, and under no circumstances should they get involved in any conflicts unless absolutely forced to. Otherwise, they will bring about the destiny of destruction."

"The second: Behemot will break free from its seal in the future, leading the demon race to destruction. The daughter of Mephisto will give birth to a boy, who will completely end the gloom that has overshadowed our ancestors."

"The third..." Beelzebub paused. "I'm sorry, this one is quite secretive. I don't know it. It seems only your grandfather Mephisto knows."

"The prophet again?"

Merlin couldn't help but frown. Everything related to the demon race seemed to have some connection to this being in one way or another. The prophet's shadow appeared everywhere, and countless threads of clues all pointed to this demon that had once existed.

But recalling the tattered cloth from the Ruins of the Gods, Merlin had some faith in these prophecies. After all, he had personally experienced the accuracy of the prophet's predictions.

What exactly was the third prophecy? It was strange that even Beelzebub, as the First Demon Lord, didn't know it.

"The events we're experiencing now might be the prophet's second prophecy. The demon mentioned that will end the gloom overshadowing our ancestors probably refers to you. After all, you're Vivian's only son." Beelzebub stared into Merlin's eyes and said solemnly, "Having you locked away in the Domain of Sin—Behemot out there might already be jumping for joy. I don't know how it learned the contents of the prophecy, but it knows you're a threat, so targeting you is hardly surprising. Anyone facing their greatest threat would choose to eliminate them first."

Merlin lowered his head and asked quietly, "Who exactly is the prophet? How does he know so much?"

"Unfortunately, I cannot answer that question. During the Era of the Gods, I was still an infant with limited cognitive ability. Perhaps I've seen him, but I can't recall. By the time I grew up, the prophet had long disappeared. They say he entered the Despair Gorge within the Death Swamp, but Mephisto claims the prophet is not actually there." Beelzebub's soul lifted and gazed into the distance, speaking dreamily. "I think he was a unique demon, with thinking completely different from ours. In that distant era, demons were merely exploited servants of Behemot, born to奉献 everything to him. But the prophet's appearance changed all of this, freeing us from our cage. To the ancient gods, he was an executioner and a destroyer, but to us, he was undoubtedly the pioneer of a new era—a great existence that can never be erased."

Listening to Beelzebub's narration, Merlin again thought of the one who had cursed him in Despair Gorge. Was that really the prophet who had profoundly impacted the demon race? And what exactly was that thing that had pierced his heart?

"Even you were locked in the Domain of Sin, so the situation outside must already be quite dire. Behemot has used my body to do many detestable things. You must leave here." Beelzebub's soul swayed as if making some decision. "I won't doubt the prophet's prediction. The demon capable of stopping Behemot is probably only you."

Merlin immediately became serious. Though he didn't want to admit it, everything seemed true.

But what exactly should he do to save the demon race from the brink of destruction? Was it enough to just kill Behemot?

Merlin felt he should be able to do it, but he didn't know what kind of monster the creator of the demon race was. If it possessed a monstrous regenerative ability similar to a vampire, he feared that with Banri Garan in his hands, he恐怕 wouldn't be able to kill it.

"I know. I'll go stop Behemot. But for now... let me release you first. We'll leave together."

From Beelzebub's words, it seemed he knew how to leave the Domain of Sin, which put Merlin at ease. It was more important to first free Beelzebub's soul from the pitch-black cross, but Beelzebub refused—

"I can no longer leave here."

"Huh? Why?" Merlin was startled.

"This was originally the world I created to deal with those ferocious Holy Spirits, but I never expected it would become my burial ground." Beelzebub's soul lowered his head, his spirits drooping. "The control of the Domain of Sin isn't in my hands—it's under Behemot's control. My soul has merged with this land, becoming fertilizer to sustain it. But you still have a chance to leave. As long as my soul is completely destroyed, the Domain of Sin will naturally collapse."

Merlin's eyes widened in astonishment, startled by Beelzebub's words. Was he asking him to personally destroy Beelzebub's soul?

"I deeply regret it. I've been struggling in the Domain of Sin, hoping to see my son before my soul is extinguished. Unfortunately, this ultimately remains my unreasonable hope." Beelzebub let out a deep sigh.

"Your son?" Merlin understood the family relationships of the Demon Lords. Where did Beelzebub have a son?

"Yes, his name is Orobas Beelzebub. He's a very unworthy son. He doesn't like killing but is passionate about art and divination. If not for the horns on his head, he wouldn't look like a demon at all. I never made his existence public because I thought he lacked the ability to inherit my legacy. But that doesn't stop me from loving him deeply." Beelzebub's eyes brightened somewhat as he spoke of his son.

Merlin recalled the fortune teller he had encountered in Lexam not long ago, and everything suddenly became clear. He wondered whether he should tell Beelzebub about this. Orobas had already become Behemot's pawn. Would revealing it only make him suffer more?

"If I hadn't held onto a glimmer of hope in my heart, I might have chosen to destroy my soul long ago. But after seeing you, I know that's no longer possible. Will you grant my request, young son of Vivian?" Beelzebub's soul looked at Merlin, his eyes filled with a touch of pleading.

"Please speak." Merlin perked up his ears. This might already be his dying wish.

"Find Orobas and tell him I'm willing to give him freedom. If he wants to stay with the demon race, then inherit my position. If he wishes to leave the demon race, I hope the other demons won't stop him. Let him leave quietly and pursue the life he desires. I have nothing left to give him. Freedom is the most precious gift I can offer now." Beelzebub closed his eyes. These were the final words left for Orobas.

"I understand. I will definitely convey this to Orobas." Merlin nodded, unable to describe the emotions churning within him.

Perhaps this was what being a father meant—silently dedicating one's entire life, only revealing vulnerability in death's final moments.

title: Chapter 63 — Seven Kings Meeting 9
content:
Chapter 63 — Seven Kings Meeting 9

Volume 32 · Chapter 63

Merlin was also a father, so naturally he could empathize with Beelzebub's state of mind at this moment.

If his own life were reaching its end, perhaps he would have made the same choice as Beelzebub.

Alice would surely do the same — leaving all the good things for Chris.

Merlin did not want to reach this point himself. If at all possible, before Chris grew up, he could not possibly leave casually.

Beelzebub's soul had already made its choice, and Merlin did not stop him, because the entire demon race was teetering on the brink of destruction under Behemoth's guidance, and he had more important matters to attend to.

Merlin showed a trace of sympathy, wanting to say something comforting before parting, but his lips moved for a long time without a single word coming out.

"Don't make such a gloomy face. I've simply made the most correct choice, just like your grandfather. I once deeply regretted not being able to stand with them, but today I have no longer any attachment to life. If my death can stop Behemoth's ambitions, then death will have been worthwhile. I can finally meet those old friends again. As for what happens next, I leave it to you."

Merlin remembered with complicated feelings, watching as Beelzebub's soul began to burn. The terrifying Sin Domain was crumbling before their eyes at an unmistakable pace.

Beelzebub's soul lifted its head, gazing at the cracking and collapsing sky of the Sin Domain. "That despicable bastard Behemoth knew I was here and yet still locked you in the Sin Domain. It must have assumed I wouldn't abandon the hope of staying alive and would instead choose to drag out my existence. It truly underestimated me."

Merlin watched Beelzebub's soul gradually turn to ash and dissipate. In the end, he still couldn't bring himself to say anything — he could only feel his shoulders grow a little heavier.

If I had known about all this when I was young, I would've run faster than anyone else.

◆

The Sin Domain gate towered into the clouds. Merlin had been sealed inside the Sin Domain for some time now.

Beelzebub, whose body had been taken over by Behemoth, stood before the gate. The fact that he disposed of Merlin without lifting a finger left all the demons deeply surprised.

Lucifer III, who appeared to casually trample on the Council of Elders' dignity, was nothing more than a green kid in front of Beelzebub.

"Lucifer… do you think he can still come out?" Leviatan asked, uncertain and wary. Honestly, it hoped Merlin could escape the Sin Domain — otherwise, would the entire demon race fall under Beelzebub's sole control?

"It's impossible, right? The Sin Domain consumed Beelzebub's lifelong efforts. He would only use it as a last resort. I'm afraid Merlin won't take long before he turns to ash within the Sin Domain," Asmodeus speculated. At this moment, it truly couldn't help at all, and it was also worried about offending Beelzebub. What if it got locked inside the Sin Domain itself? Wouldn't that be even worse?

"What should we do now? Just let it end like this? Look at those elders sucking up to Beelzebub. In the future, we might all have to obey him," Leviatan said with deep concern, hesitating over whether to make a move.

"Lucifer defeated Samael and was locked away in the Sin Domain himself. If we defy Beelzebub, our fate will be the same. For now, it's best not to provoke Beelzebub's authority. We can think of another way later," Asmodeus responded calmly. Charging at Beelzebub, who stood backed by the Sin Domain gate, was tantamount to throwing oneself to one's death.

"Darn it, this Seven Kings meeting has been even more chaotic than I imagined," Leviatan said, unwilling to accept it.

ZzZ — Beelzebub, who had been pretending to be unconscious, was actually already asleep? It clearly had no intention of meddlinfurther, its head brimful of nothing but hurrying back to the Demon Lord Palace to wallow with its younger sister.

Those demon elders who had originally been lying low to avoid trouble now emerged one by one, having seen that Merlin had been dealt with, showering Beelzebub with unreserved praise —

"Your Majesty Beelzebub, you truly are the great First Demon. You handled that traitor Lucifer in just a couple of moves."

"Yes, with you here, the demon race will never face any threat. Who in this world could possibly rival you?"

"Please, Your Majesty Beelzebub, take charge and crush those who dare oppose the Council of Elders. We cannot let them grow any more reckless."

The demon elders supporting Beelzebub wore their excitement openly. Having dealt with Lucifer sent a clear message — it served as a cautionary example, and the elders began taking sides one after another.

Chief Judge Caprio's expression grew anxious. Merlin had been locked inside the Sin Domain and might lose his life. How was he supposed to face the deceased Mephisto? Even Vivian would blame him for failing to handle the matter properly.

Beelzebub basked in the endless praise from countless elders, its gaze drifting toward Asmodeus and Leviatan in the distance.

Lucifer III had been dealt with. What should it do next?

Should it first free the body sealed beneath the Blood Pool, or take the opportunity to eliminate the other Second Generation rulers and further concentrate the demon race's power into its own hands?

Just as Beelzebub was pondering its next move, Caprio stepped forward and suggested with a humble attitude.

"Respected Your Majesty Beelzebub, isn't it too severe to lock His Majesty Lucifer away in the Sin Domain? Detaining him would suffice. Perhaps with proper negotiation, his mindset could change. Surely you also know that he is a descendant of the First Generation rulers…"

"Hmm?" Beelzebub scrutinized Caprio. This old fellow always seemed to be speaking on Merlin's behalf, which had already drawn its attention. "What are you talking about? Are Lucifer's crimes something a conversation could resolve? He has betrayed us! Moreover, there is suspicion that he killed his own kin to shield that worthless spawn born of his union with a human!"

Caprio broke into a cold sweat. Indeed, he dared not flatly deny such accusations.

"You seem to be showing a lot of favoritism toward Lucifer III, don't you?" Beelzebub narrowed its eyes, its expression full of suspicion.

"That's not it at all. I merely believe the demon race should not suffer further losses. His Majesty Mammon is already dead. Must His Majesty Lucifer die as well? This does not serve our long-term interests," Caprio said nervously.

"Caprio, do you know your place?" Beelzebub patted the other's shoulder and spoke softly. "You are the Chief Judge of the Council of Elders. You must be fair and just. Otherwise, any demon could replace you. You spare no effort in defending Lucifer III. Could it be that you are colluding with the demon race's traitors?"

Caprio immediately fell silent. He realized he had been too hasty and had already crossed Beelzebub's bottom line.

"You must stay within your duties and not overstep," Beelzebub paused and said sternly. "Lucifer III is no longer on our side. He has fallen into madness and is not worth your defense. Only by completely eradicating him can we eliminate the threat forever."

Suddenly —

The Sin Domain gate behind Beelzebub began to tremble violently, the thunderous roar deafening!

Crack! Countless cracks appeared out of nowhere, and the massive gate collapsed in an instant.

Beelzebub turned to look at the Sin Domain gate, which was on the verge of total collapse. A single drop of cold sweat slid from its chin.

"What… what's happening?"

title: Chapter 64 — Seven Kings Conference 20 (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 64 — Seven Kings Conference 20 (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 32 · Chapter 64

“The Sin Realm is collapsing?!” Asmodeus showed an incredulous expression, thinking, could this all be Merlin's doing? “Hey, Asmodeus, you said those trapped in the Sin Realm, the rotten eggs, could never get out, right? What's going on now?” Leviathan was utterly dumbfounded, suspecting Asmodeus was again trying to deceive him. “I don't know what's happening either! I wasn't imprisoned in the Sin Realm; I only know that the Sin Realm is a terrifying world created single-handedly by Belial, and even many powerful holy spirits couldn't escape from it!” Asmodeus responded in shock. If even the Sin Realm can't hold Merlin, aside from the Sealing Vase, he can't think of anything else that could restrain Merlin. “What the?!” Caprio trembled all over, the karmic fire of the Sin Realm spewing everywhere, causing the demon elders to hide again, not daring to show their heads. They had thought Merlin was already trapped, but it turned out everything was an illusion! The gate of the Sin Realm collapsed with a boom, dust shooting up to the sky, and a figure slowly emerged from the smoke and dust, exactly as everyone expected—Merlin. “Inside the Sin Realm, it's more interesting than I imagined; you've let me learn a lot of things.” “Ugh!” Belial's face turned grim, a cold sweat instantly appeared on his forehead, thinking— How did Lucifer destroy the Sin Realm? Could it be... could it be him! He wouldn't hesitate to destroy his own soul, just to send this guy out! Doesn't he want to see his own son again?! Damn lowly servant, dare to defy my will! Merlin calmly stared at Belial, asking meaningfully, “Is this body useful? Your vile trick really fooled quite a few people.” Belial's expression turned serious, a flicker of panic in his eyes, realizing Merlin had discovered his secret; he absolutely couldn't let Merlin speak, or it would ruin his plan—he must resort to some means. What Merlin said left many demons bewildered, unsure what he meant; even Asmodeus and Leviathan were very puzzled— Leviathan: “What is Lucifer saying? I can't understand.” Asmodeus: “Who knows what he's saying? Is he mocking Belial for being old?” Merlin looked at the false Belial, let out a cold laugh, and said loudly, “Everyone listen up, this noble original monarch Belial before us is actually—” Before Merlin could finish, Belial lost his rationality and launched first, shouting, “Who allowed you, a traitor, to speak here?! Don't think that just because you escaped the Sin Realm you can trample rules at will; I, on behalf of the demon race, will utterly annihilate you!” Only see Belial condense a scarlet flaming spear with Divine Power, the scorching karmic fire blowing toward them! Belial unhesitatingly hurled it at Merlin, giving Merlin no chance to speak the facts, why would he let his plan proceed smoothly? He won't allow Merlin to come out and interfere with himself! The flaming spear radiated intense heat and heat waves, shooting straight; Merlin instantly sidestepped and rolled, barely avoiding the terrifying attack, his expression turning angry as he sneered— “Are you feeling guilty? What are you nervous about?” “Executing a traitor like you, what do I have to feel guilty about? At this point, do you still want to find excuses for your betrayal through lies?!” Belial's face didn't redden, his heart didn't race; his tone was righteous and solemn. “Putting on airs.” Merlin's face darkened, thinking the opponent obviously didn't want to give him any chance to speak the truth; if so, he could only first kill this bastard. “Caprio!” Belial said sternly, “You've seen it—Lucifer III shows no remorse at all, only growing more arrogant, his eyes hold no demon race; he is our disgrace! We must subject him to the harshest judgment; hurry and bring out the Sealing Vase to suppress him—if left unchecked, the consequences would be unimaginable!” Caprio was very hesitant, not wanting to just casually use the Sealing Vase. “Don't hesitate any longer! The fate of our clan is in your hands; I'll hold him back—before this mad traitor launches a massive slaughter against our kin, you'd better act quickly.” Belial's body, accompanied by the scarlet karmic fire, underwent some changes, revealing his true form hidden beneath the gentlemanly guise—pitch-black skin, a body as thin as firewood, the demon horns on his head becoming sharper! His legs had vanished, replaced by a long, slender tail covered in scales. His eyes emitted a crimson glow, eerily strange; each breath could summon the power of sinful fire. Behind him, the huge membranous wings flapped, instantly lifting him into the air, preparing for an endless battle with Merlin. This Caprio stood there, torn left and right, hesitating whether to use the Sealing Vase; he had been pushed to the edge of a cliff and must make the right choice. This divine artifact is a treasure left by the demon race's creator Behemoth; after the demons gained freedom, it has never been used, more like a Sword of Damocles to restrain the Demon Lords. Because the Sealing Vase exists, the Demon Lords won't fight each other or cause big trouble; it has the ability to restrict Demon Lords' behavior. Although the Elder Council often mentions this artifact, giving the monarchs a proper warning, more often than not when faced with conflict they still choose negotiation, never reaching the point where they must use the Sealing Vase. But at this moment Caprio couldn't make up his mind; as a former subordinate of Mephistopheles, he didn't want to make things difficult for Merlin, yet sitting in the chair of chief judge, he isn't allowed to overly favor Mephistopheles' descendant; if the situation reaches an irreparable point, he might let Lucifer III become the first demon sealed in the vase. The Sealing Vase has always been hidden in an unknown mysterious place; only the chief judges of each generation of the Elder Council know how to summon and use it. Belial hasn't exaggerated; the fate of the demon race truly lies in Caprio's hands, entirely depending on how this short, elderly demon decides. “Strange, why did Belial suddenly become so agitated?” Asmodeus muttered puzzledly. “Really?” Leviathan curiously looked toward the sky. “Belial is usually consistently calm to the point of frightening me, but now…” Asmodeus's eyes flickered with a hint of confusion. Belial's terrifying, monstrous form floated above Merlin's head, arms suddenly flung wide, countless flaming spears filling the sky, giving Merlin no chance to escape! The divine aura's pressure completely enveloped the area; Belial looked down upon Merlin's bare upper body, like a god gazing at tiny ants— “Lucifer III, I, in the name of the original monarch, will pass the harshest judgment on those who have fallen into betrayal— carry out the most cruel judgment!”

title: Chapter 65 — Seven Kings Meeting ①
content:
Chapter 65 — Seven Kings Meeting ①

Volume 32 · Chapter 65

Belial hovered high in the air, looking terrifying with a demonic appearance, as if a god suspended in the sky.

With a light flick of its finger, countless flame spears began to fall simultaneously, leaving Merlin no chance to escape!

The scarlet hellfire burned the sky clear and bright, the terrifying divinity pressure weighed down, making people's hearts feel heavy with tension!

Yet facing the countless flame spears, Merlin remained calm and composed. This attack was far inferior to the sin domain just now. Belial clearly had no cards left to play—

"If you're a guy, then you don't need to be so cautious."

Merlin's gaze suddenly turned cold. He drew the demon sword Banri Garan from his waist and danced in place, consecutively severing several flame spears. These attacks were completely useless against him.

Countless flame spears were thrust upside-down into the ground, like several torches burning with crimson light. Merlin tightly gripped the handle of his waist sword, assuming a ready stance for drawing his sword, his eyes staring fixedly at Belial in the sky!

Lil showed a few looks of panic on his face, realizing that Merlin was a very troublesome opponent.

"Die!"

Merlin shouted angrily, leaping up from a low position. At a speed that defied common sense, he quickly approached Belial!

"Don't come over! I am the first ruler who towers above everyone! Did you really go mad? You killed Maemon, and now you won't even spare me! You killed Maemon, why not satisfied, and now you won't let me go!"

Belial's gaze turned fearful. It continuously retreated backward, facing Merlin's imposing manner. Immediately, Belial clasped his hands together. The flame spears inserted into the ground were instantly exploded!

Towering flames blasted the earth into pieces. Billowing hellfire shot up into the sky. In the blink of an eye, both Merlin and Belial were swallowed up. A huge fire pillar dispersed the clouds. The extreme heat made no one dare approach easily; even a strong person would turn to ash in the flames!

"Hahaha!" Belial did not retreat. It laughed wildly, bathing in the flames and feeling very comfortable. But Merlin certainly did not feel the same. He worried that he might have already been eroded by the hellfire, and now he was probably in a state of serious injury. "Deserved! Your techniques I had already seen through, I know exactly what you're thinking! Fighting with me? You're dreaming!"

"Is that so?"

Merlin's voice came from the vast sea of fire. The smile on Belial's face instantly froze. This was completely different from what it had anticipated!

*Clang!* A righteous killing wind split the vast sea of fire into two. Belial's scheme had no effect on Merlin; he had already guarded against the other's cunning and deceit!

While Belial was at a loss, Merlin had already killed in front of him. The demon sword Banri Garan was drawn out, emitting a frightening sound of metal clashing. Stop! Killing me brings you no benefit; it will only increase your sins. Is it because of a lowly human that you want to raise your sword against me?

I am but a god-tier demon of the demon race, the last one remaining. Do you know what it means if I die?!!

"What does it matter? Even if you are a true god, you will die here today!"

Merlin was unwilling to let the fake Belial get away with it. He resolutely and suddenly drew his sword, striking Belial to death!
