The grim demon head rotated and flew up. Fresh blood spurted out. The headless body swayed and fell from the sky.

Belial's head fell right in front of the demon elders. They all had pale faces, already scared stiff. No one expected that the only god-tier demon king of the demon race would be defeated so effortlessly by the youngest monarch? Who knows what kind of monster Lucifer the Third really was, which they had always looked down upon.

At this moment, the many demon elders looking at Merlin's eyes had changed. After killing Belial, Merlin was undoubtedly the strongest monarch among the demons now. The title of the first among the seven kings was truly deserved!

Fear surfaced from the bottom of the elders' hearts. They no longer had the courage to point fingers at this young monarch. Not accounting for things after the fact was already a grace shown to the elders by Merlin.

Leviathan looked bewildered. He murmured, "Lucifer has gone mad? He actually really killed Belial! What's going on with Asmodeus?"

"I don't know either." Asmodeus frowned, unable to understand what Merlin was doing now. If Maemon's death still had some doubt, then killing Belial on the spot was an admission of being a "traitor"!

"Is that so? Did Lucifer really betray us? You should have seen it, right? When he killed Belial, he didn't even blink his eyes! "Leviathan couldn't understand this matter.

Asmodeus fell silent, puzzledly thinking, Merlin, what on earth are you thinking? Killing Belial in front of all the elders now means no one can exonerate you!

"Lucifer really doesn't show mercy to his own kind, maybe Maemon's death..." Leviathan started to waver, doubting which side Merlin's stance truly stood on.

Capriorio was so shocked he couldn't speak. Belial's death gave it a huge shock, making it hard to believe this fact.

It recalled Belial's previous words, even wondering if Merlin really had gone crazy!

Openly killing other monarchs on the territory of the elder meeting! This inevitably makes one suspect that Maemon's death is also inseparable from Merlin.

Plus Merlin cavorting with humans and even fathering offspring. Countless clues all point to the fact that betraying the demon race is not disputable for Merlin.

Capriorio unconsciously clenched his fist, secretly blaming himself. If he hadn't protected Merlin, perhaps Belial wouldn't have sacrificed. He had originally thought it was just slandering Merlin, but now it seems maybe not.

Merlin fell from the sky. After confirming Belial was dead, he let out a sigh of relief. But suddenly he noticed the gazes around him, filled with suspicion and fear.

"What kind of eyes are these?"

"Stop!" Leviathan couldn't help but step forward directly, questioning, "Lucifer, what are you doing! ? Why kill Belial! If it's just like defeating Samel, you can defeat it. Belial is the only god-tier demon among us, intimidating countless enemies with malicious intentions toward the demon race. Without hesitation, you killed it. Do you have any consideration for the interests of all demons! I now very much doubt your stance!"

"Oh?" Hearing Leviathan's impassioned questioning, Merlin was not surprised. He knew he needed to explain this matter.

"Answer me, Lucifer. Which side are you on? Are we your friends? Or have you betrayed us, becoming an enemy on the human side!" Leviathan asked seriously.

"I am not your enemy, and I did not kill Belial. I just got rid of the bastard occupying Belial's body." Merlin frankly explained.

"What do you mean? Leviathan followed up.

"Belial had long since died. His soul was imprisoned in the sin domain. The Belial seen by everyone was just a husk controlled by Behemoth!

Hearing the name "Behemoth," all the demons present gasped, unwilling to recall this terrible name. His matter should be forever sealed in the deepest part of the blood pool.

"Ah?" Leviathan found it hard to believe Merlin's explanation, because the blood pool seal had always been strictly maintained, and absolute problems would not occur. The imprisoned Behemoth could still control other demons? It sounded very absurd. They had never seen Belial's imprisoned soul. Relying on just a mouth, it had almost no persuasive power.

Merlin stated the facts. The surrounding suspicious gazes did not weaken. He had to seek help, "Asmodeus, you should be the one who knows me best. I won't lie about this kind of thing. Believe me!"

"I will believe you, but will other demons believe you?" Asmodeus asked back. He would unconditionally trust Merlin because today's Merlin and Belial were both a bit abnormal, but how other demons thought was beyond his control.

"All lies! Lucifer the Third, you despicable traitor! Don't make excuses for your crimes! To mix with that human woman, you actually invented such a ridiculous story that Belial Belial was controlled by Behemoth! All defenses are just to conceal the fact that you killed your own kin!" A robed demon elder suddenly stepped forward. His righteous aura instantly became the focus of the whole scene—

Stupid Lucifer the Third, you think I died? Naive~

It seems Belial didn't tell you, I can freely seize the body of the first demon.

Among the demon elders present, one third flowed with the blood of the first demon. They could become my puppets at any time!

It's become hard to write, everyone's pardon. The content of the seven kings meeting should end tomorrow.

title: Chapter 66 — Seven Kings Meeting 2
content:
Chapter 66 — Seven Kings Meeting 2

Volume 32 · Chapter 66

“What did you say?” Merlin’s face darkened as he stared at the gray‑robed demon elder, having spoken the truth, yet still not being understood.
“The demon creator Behemoth was sealed by the prophet himself beneath the blood pool—how could he possibly control Belial? This is nothing but your baseless ramblings!”
The gray‑robed demon elder’s haughty accusation made him inwardly gleeful—
You foolish wretch, killing Belial was the worst mistake you could make!
Everything is going exactly as I planned; haven’t you realized it yet? You’ve already stepped into the gauntlet I designed for you!
I never thought a few monarchs could completely suppress you; the Demon Sealing Vessel is what I’ve been after all along.

“During the Holy War, the seal on the blood pool had already cracked; Behemoth abandoned his body and his soul escaped—these are what Belial, imprisoned in the Sin Lands, told me personally.” Merlin explained solemnly, hoping to earn the trust of the demons present.
“The seal was laid down by the great prophet himself—how could it be so easily damaged? Moreover, the Goddess’s hounds failed to capture the Demon Lord’s Palace during the Holy War, so how could a crack have appeared?” The gray‑robed demon elder narrowed his murky eyes and said meaningfully, “Don’t make excuses for yourself, Lucifer III. You’re just looking for a reason to justifiably kill your kin—isn’t it that anyone who opposes you gets framed as a puppet controlled by Behemoth?!”

Faced with the questioning, Merlin fell silent, fearing that aside from Asmodeus, none of the demons present would believe his words.
Since the Seven Kings’ Conference began, Merlin had been labeled as a suspect in Mammon’s murder, a traitor who colluded with humans, and so on—the seeds of distrust were planted from the very start. Who would unconditionally trust a kinslayer who betrayed his own kind?
Merlin felt he had been set up; Behemoth had planned everything from before the Seven Kings’ Conference, executing step by step to ultimately drive him to oppose the demon race.

“Merlin…” Asmodeus frowned, wanting to help but powerless.
“Lucifer, which side are you really on?” Leviathan demanded with a stern face, already unable to tell whether Merlin was friend or foe.
“Chief Judge! If Lucifer III killed Belial before our very eyes and betrayed the demon race, that is an indisputable fact; his sins are unforgivable. Letting him go will only bring us greater harm—quickly bring out the Demon Sealing Vessel and seal his soul!” the gray‑robed demon elder shouted, raising his arms, beginning to pressure Caprio to produce the Demon Sealing Vessel: “As long as the council possesses the Demon Sealing Vessel, dignity and limits will not allow Lucifer to provoke us; he must receive the punishment he deserves!”

At that moment, Merlin’s eyes were filled with enemies; someone took the lead, and the other demon elders naturally refused to fall behind.
Although Merlin’s overwhelming power had frightened the elders, the presence of the Demon Sealing Vessel erased their fear—
“Caprio, quickly imprison Lucifer in the Demon Sealing Vessel—what are you hesitating for? Could you also be colluding with humans?
“Lucifer III is so arrogant; he might even use Behemoth’s control over other demons as an excuse to continually slaughter our kin—he must be severely punished!”
“Mammon and Belial are dead at his hands—who will be the next monarch? The council’s purpose is to maintain demonic stability; now is the time to employ the Demon Sealing Vessel!”

Caprio’s face turned pale as he listened to the elders’ accusations, cold sweat pouring down; he even began to believe their words, wondering whether Merlin was fabricating excuses to deliberately slay other demon lords.
The gray‑robed demon elder couldn’t help but chuckle. “Excellent, just as I expected. Under this immense pressure, Caprio will surely produce the Demon Sealing Vessel—I’ve already won! Because—
I am not only able to possess Caprio’s body, I also know how to wield the Demon Sealing Vessel; this artifact was meant to be mine.”

Merlin fixed his gaze on the gray‑robed demon elder, silently gripping the hilt of his blade, recalling what Belial had once said—
“Behemoth can possess only a limited number of bodies, and can only seize those of the primordial demons who share his bloodline.”
Now I understand—even if I killed Belial, Behemoth would not perish; he would merely take another vessel.
Luring me into killing Belial is a trap, meant to make all demons hostile toward me and isolate me completely within the demon realm—isn’t that right?
Perhaps Mammon’s death was also this bastard’s doing.
After all this, Behemoth’s goal is not to drive the demon race to ruin; from the very start he has been coming after me.
He is afraid—perhaps not of me, but of the prophet’s prophecy coming true, that I will end his life. For that reason, in his eyes I am the primary obstacle that must be eliminated first.

What should I do next to stop Behemoth?
After the recent turmoil, the elders have suffered heavy casualties; among those present, the primordial demons similar to Belial number roughly a dozen.
It seems there’s no other way—someone must step forward as the executioner to prevent Behemoth from seizing control of the demon race, and clearly I am the most suitable candidate.
To keep the demon realm from falling into Behemoth’s hands, I must slay the primordial demons present; I may end up imprisoned in the Demon Sealing Vessel, but we have reached the point where there is no alternative.

Merlin’s eyes turned icy; he could faintly tell that this gray‑robed demon elder was Behemoth’s new puppet.
“You really underestimated me—is the trick of killing with a borrowed blade fun?”
“What are you saying?” sweat beaded on the gray‑robed demon elder’s forehead as he sensed Merlin’s gaze shifting oddly.
Merlin’s form became a flash of lightning; in an instant he stood before the elder and cleaved him in two with a single stroke, drawing his blade without hesitation. Before anyone could react, the elder fell dead on the spot.
“You are Behemoth—did you think I wouldn’t know?”
"!! !"

Everyone was shocked; no one expected Merlin to be this bold—right after slaying Belial, he now begins massacring the council elders!
Throughout demon history, there has never been a ruffian like Merlin; it seems he has reached the point of looking down on everything.

Merlin suddenly turned his blade on his own kin again, plunging the demons into chaos once more; in their eyes, Lucifer III had gone mad—aside from locking him in the Demon Sealing Vessel, what else could stop him?
“Huh—” Asmodeus stared wide‑eyed, utterly unable to comprehend Merlin’s actions; if Merlin’s words were true, he couldn’t help but suspect that Merlin had been possessed by Behemoth—how could he commit such insanity?
“Lucifer! Stop it!” Leviathan clenched his fists, feeling he must halt Merlin’s wanton slaughter.

Merlin stood silent, face cold, his eyes fixed on the few primordial elders; with the demon sword Banri Garan he mercilessly reaped the lives of his kin—
In a single blink he cut down an elder; blood and screams followed in succession, he had become an unfeeling executioner—
Slaughter them all!
Kill every primordial demon present!
Leave that vile Behemoth nowhere to hide!

title: Chapter 67 — Seven Kings Conference ③
content:
Chapter 67 — Seven Kings Conference ③

Volume 32 · Chapter 67

Merlin began a frenzied slaughter of the elders, his gaze fixed tightly on those few primordial demons.
The demons present never imagined Merlin would openly kill an elder!
This is no longer merely challenging the bottom line of the Elder Council; it is directly making enemies of all demons!
In a short time, seven or eight demon elders had already fallen under Merlin's blade, while the remaining few were terrified, their faces turning pale as they fled with heads tucked.
Where? !Behemoth! When I kill the last primordial demon elder, I'll see where you can run to!
Merlin had made up his mind to drag Behemoth out; he didn't believe Behemoth, without a body, would still not reveal his true form.
Leviathan's face grew uglier, he clenched his fists silently, thinking Merlin was truly mad and he must step in to stop him.
"Caprio! What are you doing? Hurry up and take out the Demon-Sealing Vessel! Lucifer III is wantonly slaughtering the elders! How many demons must die before you realize your hesitation will kill how many demons?-
A black-robed demon shouted angrily, and before his words finished Merlin chopped off his head, giving him no chance to incite the other demons—
This guy! He's so decisive! He'd rather kill all the primordial demons present than not force me out! I underestimated his resolve!"
Behemoth had become flustered; in his estimation, Merlin would never choose such an extreme method even in dire danger, yet he still underestimated Merlin!
Seeing the situation uncontrollable, many demon elders began pressuring Caprio to bring out the Demon-Sealing Vessel to intimidate Lucifer III and stop him from continuing to slaughter the Elder Council members.
"Chief Arbiter! If you don't subdue Lucifer III, the Elder Council will be wiped out!"
"Although Lucifer III is a noble primordial descendant, he now threatens the survival of our race!
"Caprio! Don't shield him just because you were once a subordinate of Mephistopheles! If the Elder Council is destroyed, you will be a sinner of our race!"
Caprio's small stature stood firm, facing overwhelming pressure, he had no choice but to adopt some countermeasures.
As the Chief Arbiter of the Elder Council, he must be fair and just, with the demon race's interests at core; at this moment Caprio must make the choice he believes is correct.
Merlin's eyes locked onto Caprio, knowing he too was a primordial demon and once was his grandfather's old subordinate.
Yet at this moment Merlin showed no hesitation, charging straight at Caprio, ready to quickly end his life.
Even the Elder Council's Chief Arbiter is a target of Merlin's slaughter, leaving all demons unsettled, especially Leviathan.
Speak of the devil—
Just as Merlin was about to slay Caprio, several water columns came from all directions, instantly engulfing him and forming a huge floating water prison!
"I've called you my assistant already, Lucifer!" Leviathan shouted angrily, thinking Merlin's behavior was excessive!
Trapped in the water prison, Merlin spat out a few bubbles, a heavy sense of oppression surging; Leviathan's water magic restrained him notably.
In desperation, Merlin quickly unfurled the Repulse Space, causing the water prison imprisoning him to wildly expand, hoping to burst free from the tenacious water magic.
The huge water prison grew larger and larger, like a giant bubble suspended in midair, ready to explode at any moment!
Seeing this, Leviathan immediately increased his power, engaging Merlin in a direct confrontation, not wanting Merlin to continue acting recklessly.
"You'd better calm down! I won't allow you to randomly kill our kin!
The earth began to tremble slightly, a six-pointed star magic array appeared in the center of the council ruins, and all demons' gazes turned toward it.
The demon race's most mysterious treasure, the Demon-Sealing Vessel, slowly appeared before everyone's eyes.
The Demon-Sealing Vessel is pitch-black, a four‑sided shape with edges and corners, each face carved with hideous demonic visages—
A terrifying dark aura emanated from the Vessel; as soon as it appeared countless demons felt fear, an instinct from demon bloodline.
Hesitant, Caprio made his choice: temporarily use the Demon-Sealing Vessel to seal Merlin's soul, preventing him from further slaughtering kin; only thus could the demon race avoid greater loss.
After the Age of Gods ended, the Demon-Sealing Vessel had never been used; besides its strong deterrent effect letting Behemoth better control the demons, it has a fatal flaw—
Its cooldown lasts a hundred years; after use, the Vessel becomes ineffective for a century.
That is why past Chief Arbiters of the Elder Council are reluctant to use the Vessel—once lost, they cannot control internal emergencies of the demon race for a hundred years.
Caprio thought he was fulfilling his duty as Chief Arbiter, unaware that summoning the Demon-Sealing Vessel would push the demon race into the abyss; this is not Merlin's failure but the utter defeat of all demons of the demon race!
Eons‑old demon race, not destroyed by external foes, yet facing annihilation from internal suspicion—all this was within Behemoth's expectations.
"Is this the Demon-Sealing Vessel?" Asmodeus said, also seeing it for the first time; if anything in the world could emit the purest dark power, it would surely be this Demon-Sealing Vessel.
"Terrible!" Merlin's eyes widened, realizing the situation was irredeemable; he mustered all his strength, trying to burst the water prison and slash Caprio down in one strike, "Leviathan! You pig teammate! Quickly stop Caprio! No! He isn't Caprio, he's a puppet controlled by Behemoth!"
"You're spouting nonsense! —while madly slaughtering elders, —while shouting they're possessed by Behemoth, now you're slandering the Chief Arbiter as a puppet too, treating others as fools has its limits! Indeed, whoever is unfavorable to you, you swing your blade at them, right? ?Leviathan also unleashed his full power, even using Divine Power to maintain the water prison, refusing to let Merlin out.
Merlin, under Leviathan's suppression, could only fully activate Repulse Space to resist, unable to draw his hand to wield his blade; a feeling of irritation rose in his heart.
"I'm being made to cry by you Qin, my mindset exploded!"
Asmodeus narrowed his eyes, thinking Merlin's appearance didn't look like a senseless elder slaughter.
Yet while shouting the elders were possessed by Behemoth, —while hacking them down, anyone would see him as a lunatic?
Asmodeus looked toward Caprio, who had summoned the Demon-Sealing Vessel, and suddenly noticed something odd.
Caprio clutched his head, showing a painful expression, swaying in place; he gradually steadied himself, lifted his head, his eyes shifting suddenly to a hideous, mad glare.
Merlin:"!!!"
Leviathan:"???"
Asmodeus:"Something's wrong!"
Beelzebub: ZZz
The Demon-Sealing Vessel rang with a bell, its black divine pressure sweeping the field, piercing every demon's body.
"How long have I been unconscious?" Samael slowly opened his eyes, discovering his soul had left his body, drifting away from his headless corpse,
"Am I dead??"
Except for Caprio, who was controlled by Behemoth, all demons' souls were torn from their bodies, drifting helplessly in midair.
"Pig teammate! Pig teammate! Pig teammate! Go die!!!" Merlin gritted his teeth in hatred, frantically slapping Leviathan's face, but they were all souls now, unable to touch.
"Hey! Caprio! Did you accidentally injure yourself? ?" Leviathan still hadn't reacted.
"Doomed" Asmodeus frowned, pressed his forehead, sighing, feeling the situation had reached its worst.
"Hehehehe! Prepare to fall into eternal slumber in the Demon-Sealing Vessel; I'll make good use of the bodies you left behind. After countless eons, the demon race has returned to my hands!" The Behemoth‑controlled Caprio jeered loudly, flung open the lid of the Demon-Sealing Vessel—
All current demon monarchs, as well as numerous high‑authority elders, were sealed inside the Vessel.

title: Chapter 68 — The World Inside the Pot
content:
Chapter 68 — The World Inside the Pot

Volume 32 · Chapter 68

A large number of demon souls wandering in the air were all sucked into the floating sealing demon pot.
The monarchs and elders of the demon race's council, none could escape, all were sealed.
Behemoth-controlled Caprio slowly placed the lid on the sealing demon pot, putting an end to his long-planned scheme——
“It's over, so what's next”
Caprio narrowed his eyes, staring at the Demon Lord's body lying sprawled on the ground, deciding to make good use of it.
“First go free the demon god's body sealed in the blood pool, then take over the seven Demon Lord Palaces.”
“As for the Demon Lords' bodies, just obediently become my pawns, okay?”
“I will mercifully give them blood, which will surely let a few little guys greatly increase their strength in the short term .”
Caprio muttered to himself, his eyes already smiling into a slit: his gaze fell on Merlin's body——
“Especially this guy, I will take good care of him.”
“Even he has become my puppet; who else could threaten me?”
The sealing demon pot that has been used enters a hundred-year cooldown and cannot be opened again.
During this time the sealing demon pot will lose all function; the demons' souls must remain sealed inside for a hundred years before they might regain freedom, this
also requires someone to open the sealing demon pot after a hundred years, and the external body must not suffer fatal injury, otherwise the body dies and the souls inside the pot will also
be destroyed along with it.
The demons' bodies are actually still alive; only their souls have been taken, putting the bodies into a death-like state, giving Behemoth great room to
operate.
But if after a hundred years no one can open the sealing demon pot, then Merlin and the host of demons must accept the reality that their souls will be forever trapped in the pot
inside.
This is a severe blow to all demons; if forever trapped in the pot, it would be better to die, but in soul form they find it very hard to
commit suicide.
The sealing demon pot is a personal divine artifact forged by Behemoth himself, used in the age of gods to rule over his demon subjects, continually oppressing the demons
to serve him; this good life lasted until the prophet appeared and then ended.
The world inside the pot is pitch black, with no sense of time or space; only consciousness can barely exist, and many demons' souls glow faintly
drifting in the empty world--
Merlin saw his own body like smoke, emitting a faint glow, his heart filled with vexation.
He never imagined he could see his own soul before birth; this feeling is very subtle.
“What the hell! ?What is Caprio thinking! ?Why are we even locked in here!“ Leviathan, looking at his soul state, couldn't help but
burst out shouting.
““You haven't realized yet? We've all been schemed by Caprio.“ Asmodeus's soul drifted to and fro in the pitch‑black space.”
“.”
““Why… why scheme against us? We have no grudge with the council.“ Leviathan”
““What exactly is going on? I need””
““Probably what Lucifer said is true; Behemoth, even while sealed, can still control us, and the Caprio judge has already become
Behemoth's puppet, so to free himself from the seal, locking us all in the sealing demon pot is no problem.“ Asmodeus explained offhandedly,””
explanation, he lowered his gaze to look at his own skirt, revealing a meaningful expression.
“Ah! ?Truly unbelievable! How could this be possible? Behemoth, though sealed, can still control us; using the sealing demon pot to lock us in
isn't that pointless? With his power he could just kill us all outright,“ Leviathan said, utterly baffled, this is obviously a roundabout way.”
““According to what Merlin said before, the demons Behemoth can control must meet certain conditions; I only now understand that Merlin isn't indiscriminately slaughtering demons,
his victims are the old-timers—Belial, Caprio and some elders—all of whom are first‑generation demons, which
is the key; Behemoth cannot control us second‑generation demons, so he needs the sealing demon pot.“ Asmodeus voiced his speculation,””
came, adding, “Don't ask me about everything; although your body is still a brat, is your mind also at a child's level?”
“Er!“ Leviathan's face turned red, feeling humiliated by Asmodeus, “Don't insult me! Watch out, I'll rip your mouth apart!“”
““Come on then; we're all souls now, no bodies left—do I still fear you'll strike? In this pot world, whoever has the sharpest tongue is the boss~”
the one with the sharpest mouth is the big boss~” Asmodeus gloated, mocking Leviathan.”
“Tch!“ Leviathan swung his fists at the air angrily, saying regretfully, “So does that mean I helped the enemy? When Merlin slaughtered the elders
, I shouldn't have intervened.””
““Sure, you do have a bit of self‑awareness~” Asmodeus chuckled, saying slowly, “You are a complete pig teammate,
if Merlin had just succeeded in killing Caprio, at least we wouldn't have been locked in the sealing demon pot; Behemoth went to all this trouble, presumably because
he didn't know where the sealing demon pot was hidden; only when Caprio himself produced it did he dare to seize its body.”
So that's how it is; I apologize for my stupid behavior that harmed everyone.“ Leviathan lowered his head sheepishly, but still
defended himself, saying, “But I couldn't help it; Merlin just looked like he was massacring the elders, his eyes blood‑red, and to prevent greater harm to the demon race
I had to step forward to stop all this; who could have imagined Behemoth so cunning, seeing through us so clearly?””
““I agree with you; the demon race, if the seven Demon Lord Palaces unite, need not fear most external forces, but internal strife and division
are extremely serious, and that is the greatest threat; Behemoth spotted a bit of it and thus began to undermine us from within, first by colluding with Mammon, forcing
it to take an opposing stance, then framing and isolating Lucifer, step by step weakening our strength, the whole process flawless.”
Asmodeus paused, then slowly ventured a speculation—
““Behemoth being able to see us so clearly could not have been accomplished overnight.”
“I think”
““Behemoth has been with us for a long time; perhaps Belial's body was already taken over, Merlin didn't also say that? In the Sin Region
he saw Belial's soul.””
““Mainly it's you, this pig teammate, who's too hateful; you can't just mind your own business like me; without the right answer, any action
is foolish; Merlin just needs to slaughter all first‑generation demons, then Behemoth's soul will have nowhere to hide, and once it appears the truth will be clear,
will we still be trapped in the pot? You should learn from Beelzebub that idiot, who sleeps and knows nothing, besides constantly wanting to be close to his sister,
doesn't bother with anything else; although he's stupid, at least he won't sabotage things.”
“Huh? !“ The drowsy Beelzebub suddenly opened his eyes, instinctively alert to his surroundings—
“I think I heard someone calling me an idiot.“
“Who is it? Come out! Watch me not beat you into an idiot! ”
(HA▲

title: Chapter 69 — The Pot‑Splitting Meeting
content:
Chapter 69 — The Pot‑Splitting Meeting

Volume 32 · Chapter 69

"It's Leviathan," Asmodeus said in a goading tone. "It says you're a useless fool~"

"What! ? Even a little shorty wants to ride on top of me?" Beelzebub bared his teeth in a grimace, preparing to give Leviathan a lesson, but then discovered he had already lost his body and become a wandering soul—

"Uh???"

"What's going on?"

"I just took a little nap and then I died?"

Leviathan silently sighed, thinking this guy was beyond saving; he was indeed a complete idiot. He didn't even know how he'd gotten sealed inside the Demon-Sealing Pot, completely unreliable.

"Oh my god! Am I really going to die so young? A monarch who dies from taking a nap—I'll definitely be nailed to the demon race's pillar of shame, right? Is there a more embarrassing way to die than this?" Beelzebub terrifiedly covered his head, his expression flustered. "I haven't even seen Miranda for the last time—was that it? If I'm gone, my little sister will definitely get bullied by the other demons! Nooo!"

"Cut it out! At a time like this, you're still worrying about your sister?" Leviathan interrupted Beelzebub exasperatedly, feeling that they should be working together to figure out how to escape the pot.

Beelzebub frowned and looked around, seeing a large crowd of familiar faces—all in a wandering soul state. "What happened? Did the upper echelons of the demon race get wiped out in one go? Why is everyone here?"

"Yeah, we were all caught in one net."

Leviathan briefly summarized what had happened not long ago for Beelzebub, hoping he would understand what was going on.

Beelzebub listened for a while and nodded. Now he understood what had happened and couldn't help but lament along with the others.

"I only took a little nap, and so much happened? The situation feels incredibly serious. Without our leadership, won't the demon race be at Beelzebub's mercy?"

"That's exactly it. We must find a way to stop Behemoth, otherwise the demon race will be in danger!" Leviathan said in a very serious tone.

"Yeah, my little sister is still waiting for me back at the Demon Lord Palace. If I'm trapped here forever, what'll happen to her all alone?" Beelzebub looked up, tears shimmering in his eyes. "Miranda, big brother wants—"

"Enough! Are you never going to stop!? The entire demon race is on the brink right now, and you only care about your sister? You're one of the Seven Princes, have some awareness!" Leviathan was so angry at Beelzebub his nose was practically crooked; he couldn't understand why he was stuck working alongside this guy.

"Shorty, shut up already. You're so annoying, chirping nonstop. Who cares about the demon race? I just hope Miranda is safe and sound." Beelzebub picked at his ear, his face full of disgust.

Leviathan had a splitting headache. With a guy like Beelzebub around, how could the demon race ever unite?

"Face it, this is all your fault for meddling in things that weren't your business, causing all of us to get sealed in this Demon-Sealing Pot, right?" Beelzebub flashed a meaningfully knowing smile and teased, "Such a pig teammate~"

"Tch!" Leviathan's face flushed red. Being mocked by anyone was fine, but not by a fool like Beelzebub. "You've got some nerve! You're a pig teammate yourself! You were the first one to charge up and block Lucifer! If Lucifer had explained things clearly, maybe it wouldn't have ended up like this!"

"No way. Behemoth kept manipulating the First Generation demons precisely to deny Lucifer any chance to explain. Besides, in that situation, even if the truth came out, the number of demons who would believe him could be counted on one hand. Don't forget, the Elder Council operates on majority rule. If Merlin could've turned things around on his own, he wouldn't have chosen such an extreme method as slaughtering the First Generation demons. He had no choice either," Asmodeus said calmly.

"Asmodeus, what's the point of saying all this now? This is all hindsight." Leviathan rolled his eyes.

"I admit I'm talking after the fact. I even once suspected that Merlin was truly mad, but—" Asmodeus suddenly shifted his tone and said mockingly, "I wouldn't do something so stupid at a critical moment like you did~"

Leviathan was speechless; he did bear some responsibility.

Meanwhile, Satan, who had been quietly drifting nearby, had heard all of Asmodeus's analysis. His mind grew much clearer, and he even recalled something from long ago—

"So we were all manipulated. The sealed Behemoth, using Berial's body, started undermining the demon race from the inside long ago, forcing us to distrust each other. What a vicious scheme. In the current situation, none of us can shirk responsibility."

"Samael speaks correctly. If Behemoth destroys the demon race, then all of us here are complicit in Behemoth's actions." Asmodeus nodded in agreement.

"Who would've guessed Berial would become a puppet of the Demon God? If I weren't trapped in this pot right now, I would never believe a respected First Generation Prince would have his body seized and used by Behemoth." Samael paused and then sincerely said loudly, "Lucifer, I apologize for my rashness."

Merlin sat alone in a corner not far away. Ever since entering the Demon-Sealing Pot, he had been in a self-imposed withdrawal, unwilling to speak at all.

But Merlin felt there was no point in saying anything anymore. Asmodeus's analysis was all correct; it basically reflected reality.

Faced with Samael's apology, Merlin didn't respond at all. He just sat in the corner, stuck in his withdrawal, like a block of wood that couldn't hear anything.

On the surface Merlin appeared very calm, but internally he was already quite annoyed. These pig teammates had ruined everything and he was too exhausted to even be angry. He was already sealed inside—what else could he do? Might as well survive one more day. After he died, let the flood come. He just couldn't help but worry about Alice and his adorable daughter.

In this soul state, Merlin couldn't use any martial techniques or magic. He was powerless against the current situation and had already given up.

Thinking that the rest of his life would be spent mixed in with this bunch, Merlin felt a touch of不甘. It would've been more satisfying to let the curse flare up and kill him outright.

All the demons were watching Merlin. Seeing this, Leviathan hesitated for a moment, then felt he also needed to apologize, so he walked up and said humbly, "Lucifer, are you upset? Why hold a grudge? We'll definitely get out of here, please don't give up! Show the same spirit you displayed when you risked your life to slay the sea monster! It was my fault for locking you in the water dungeon—I'm very sorry."

Merlin sat expressionlessly on the ground, slowly raising his heavy-lidded eyes to glance at Leviathan—

GNU

Leviathan: "????"

(.:?o)??

title: Chapter 70 — Forgotten Contract (Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 70 — Forgotten Contract (Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter)

Volume 32 · Chapter 70

"I’ve already been betrayed by you guys—what’s the point of apologizing now?"

Merlin’s voice was filled with helplessness. What else could they do? They couldn’t even touch each other in their soul forms, let alone fight Leviathan.

It was impossible.

Even if Merlin was full of resentment, he had no choice but to accept this group of incompetent teammates. If apologies were useful, he wouldn’t have been so depressed for so long.

"Cough, cough!" Leviathan quickly coughed to cover his embarrassment. "Don’t be so discouraged. We’re not without chances. Everyone believes us now. Let’s work together and we’ll definitely turn the situation around!"

The atmosphere suddenly fell silent for three seconds, and no one responded to Leviathan—

"Hey! Why don’t you say something?!"

"Turn the situation around? That’s easier said than done," Asmodeus sneered. "Leviathan is already old, yet he’s still so naive." Beelzebub shook his head, thinking Leviathan was talking nonsense. "Everyone was sealed in a jar, and they still wanted to turn the situation around? They couldn’t even send a message to the outside world."

"If you keep acting like this, we might never get out of here! Are we really going to survive in this hellhole forever?" Leviathan said indignantly.

"So, do you have a way to escape from the sealing jar?" Asmodeus asked skeptically, trying his luck.

"Well..." Leviathan fell into deep thought and finally gave an awkward answer. "Don’t be so rigid in your thinking. What if the sealing jar is shattered? Wouldn’t we regain our freedom then?"

"You’re hopeless, Leviathan," Asmodeus sighed and explained. "The sealing jar is a divine artifact, forged by Behemoth himself during the Age of Gods. Do you think it’s like a vase on your bedside table that will break if you drop it?"

Leviathan was speechless and felt that his idea wasn’t very reliable.

"In fact, the sealing jar is of divine quality, and its durability is probably beyond our imagination. Whether it’s being dropped or facing extremely strong attacks, it’s impossible to damage the jar. It’s more realistic to hope that Behemoth will have a change of heart and release us voluntarily than to rely on the sealing jar being destroyed," Asmodeus shrugged helplessly.

"How could Behemoth ever release us? Are we really going to be trapped in this hellhole forever?" Leviathan was extremely frustrated. It would be better to fight and die against Behemoth than to be trapped and die in the jar. It was too humiliating.

"Of course, destruction isn’t impossible. I sense extremely pure dark power from the sealing jar. If there were an artifact of pure light power, it might be able to destroy the sealing jar. Of course, this is only theoretically possible. Any opposing elemental powers are each other’s nemesis," Asmodeus shared his thoughts.

Merlin slightly furrowed his brow. Asmodeus’ words caught his attention. If there was an artifact of pure light power...

The slender sword in Alice’s hand seemed to have a very strong aura of light. Could it destroy the sealing jar?

Merlin smiled bitterly and shook his head, thinking that this matter couldn’t be left to Alice. Even if they could contact the outside world—which they couldn’t—Alice’s strength was no match for Behemoth, let alone getting her to touch the sealing jar.

"Oh! You, a man pretending to be a woman, I didn’t expect you to be so reliable. Isn’t there a way?" Beelzebub suddenly became excited.

"Don’t get too excited. I only said there was a possibility. The probability of success is so low it’s negligible. Even if there was someone with a light-type divine artifact who was willing to destroy the sealing jar, in our current isolated state, we can’t contact the outside world at all. It’s just a fantasy," Asmodeus paused and continued. "Right now, it’s better for us to pray that the sealing jar falls into someone else’s hands."

"Why? If the sealing jar falls into someone else’s hands, can we regain our freedom?" Leviathan asked curiously.

"No, but it’s better than leaving it in Behemoth’s hands. After the sealing jar is used, it can’t be used again for at least a hundred years, and it can’t be opened either. If it can’t be destroyed, then we’ll be trapped here for a hundred years. A hundred years from now, if some kid happens to find and open the sealing jar by chance, we can return to our bodies and regain our freedom," Asmodeus floated lazily in the air, smiling as he spoke.

Unfortunately, this probability was also very low, but it was more realistic than destroying the sealing jar.

"A hundred years? Our demon lifespan is long, and a hundred years might just be a blink of an eye. This is barely acceptable," Samael nodded, seemingly already prepared to be trapped in the jar for a hundred years.

"What the hell! A hundred years is a long time! If I can’t see my sister for a hundred years, it’s better to kill me!" Beelzebub was furious and panicked.

"Yeah, who knows what the outside world will be like in the future?" Leviathan frowned miserably.

Although Merlin didn’t speak, he also couldn’t accept the idea that his precious daughter might not recognize him after a hundred years. How could that be?

"Instead of worrying about how to leave the sealing jar, we should worry more about the fate of the demon race," Asmodeus said meaningfully.

"What do you mean?" Beelzebub asked impatiently.

"The outside world doesn’t know that we’ve been sealed in the jar, and they don’t know what happened. The demons can’t possibly know about Behemoth’s affairs. In this situation, isn’t this giving Behemoth the most comfortable breeding ground? He can fabricate any lies he wants, and the fate of all demons will be played with at his will. Maybe it won’t take a hundred years for the demon race to perish..." Asmodeus said worriedly.

The demons in the jar all lowered their heads, and the atmosphere suddenly became eerily quiet. They didn’t have much to do with each other in the jar, but the entire demon race was in danger under Behemoth’s shadow at any time, and they wouldn’t have the chance to peacefully survive in the jar for a hundred years.

"If only there was a way to contact the outside world," Asmodeus muttered to himself. Suddenly, his mind lit up as he remembered something important. He quickly asked, "Merlin! I remember you and Helena signed a slave contract, right? Did you bring that contract with you?"

"What? Why bring up that? That contract?" Merlin’s face turned red, and he said softly, "After I ate that parchment, I don’t know where it is. I haven’t seen it since. It’s probably still in my stomach and hasn’t been digested yet."

"Yes! That’s it! As the master, you should be able to directly contact Helena from the outside world!" Asmodeus became excited and said loudly, "Although the sealing jar is isolated from the outside world, it can’t isolate the power of the contract!"

Merlin was suddenly stunned. He never thought that the parchment he had randomly eaten would become the trump card to turn the situation around—

"What?"

In fact, Helena was worried about the situation at the Council of Elders and had returned here after leaving.
This allowed her to luckily avoid being sealed in the jar.
What she saw before her was the Council of Elders, which had been reduced to ruins, no longer resembling its former glory. The ground was covered with traces of destruction, and she couldn’t imagine what kind of fierce battle had taken place here.
What puzzled her was that all the monarchs had disappeared, and the ground was covered with the bodies of the demon elders, all of whom looked like they were dead.
After a detailed inspection, Helena found that the demon elders still had heartbeats, but no matter how she called out to them, she couldn’t wake them up. They seemed to have become walking corpses.
"What exactly happened here? Where did the monarchs go?"
Helena was full of questions and couldn’t understand what was happening in front of her. Suddenly, her body stiffened and she couldn’t move. At the same time, a familiar voice echoed in her mind. She couldn’t resist this force and could only listen quietly—
Merlin: "Helena? Can you hear me? Hey, hey, hey! Still can’t?"
Helena: "This voice? Your Majesty Lucifer? Where is my lord?"
Merlin: "Huh?! Don’t worry about these things for now. My communication with you is very unstable, and this might be our only chance! Don’t ask any questions. You just need to believe what I’m about to say. Right now, the future of the demon race might depend entirely on you."
■To be continued

title: Chapter 1 — Land of Suffering
content:
Chapter 1 — Land of Suffering

Volume 33 · Chapter 1

Located in the southern part of the world, near France, the Kingdom of Spain suffers from constant internal strife due to the excessive concentration of noble rights and wealth, with the aristocracy grasping all major and minor affairs of the state.

This leads to a huge gap between rich and poor; the number and scale of the impoverished citizens are unmatched in the world, and the kingdom is even mocked as a paradise for the rich and a hell for the poor. It is clear that among human nations, Spain is an extremely unstable kingdom.

The kingdom is perpetually in a state of turmoil, with rebellions breaking out frequently. Whenever natural disasters strike, they inevitably spark conflict between commoners and nobles. No nation treats its subjects as Spain does, crushing all dissent with overwhelming force.

Ten years ago, the old king ordered the execution of his beloved concubine, which plunged him into deep depression until he eventually died. On his deathbed, he personally appointed the astrologer Alfonso as chancellor, and since he could not find Princess Diana, he passed the throne to his newborn youngest son Amadeo, making a toddler who could not yet speak the new king of Spain.

Before passing away, the old king repeatedly urged Alfonso to serve as Amadeo's teacher and faithfully assist him until he came of age, so as to maintain the kingdom's peace and stability.

The old king placed almost unconditional trust in Alfonso. Back when Alfonso had accused Princess Josephine of being an evil witch, the old man had harbored doubts and secretly prepared alternative plans—if the great drought had not been lifted after Josephine's death, Alfonso would have surely met his end. But as if fate willed it, the long-awaited rain arrived three days after the princess's death, and from that point on the old king's trust in Alfonso reached its absolute peak. Whatever Alfonso said was taken as a matter concerning the kingdom's fate itself.

After the old king's death, the kingdom quietly changed hands. Alfonso became Spain's actual ruler. Rather than faithfully serving the young king Amadeo, he completely sidelined the monarch and concentrated all power into his own hands.

The same decree signed by King Amadeo carried no weight; only those bearing Alfonso's signature would be carried out. Amadeo clearly held no status in the kingdom and could only survive by clinging to Alfonso's side.

Even outsiders understood Amadeo's predicament well. At grand events like the Adventurers Guild tournament, invitations went directly to Alfonso rather than the king. Who truly ruled Spain? This was no longer a secret. Perhaps only the ten-year-old Amadeo himself remained in the dark.

Born in the slums, Alfonso made no moves to help the poor after seizing control of the entire kingdom. Many had believed he was a "Dragon-Slaying Hero" who would transform the nation, but no one expected he would ultimately become an even more ferocious "evil dragon."

To consolidate his position, Alfonso allied with numerous deeply entrenched nobles and more brazenly exploited the populace, causing widespread resentment and frequent unrest throughout the land.

Perhaps in Alfonso's eyes, he was different—he was long gone past being the destitute boy from the slums who couldn't even afford shoes, with no ties to that vile and filthy rabble. The slums reeked of evil and sin, and if he did not continue to exploit them, they would be worthless.

With the protection of the black dragon Nidhogg, it was feared that no one could shake Alfonso's current position.

At this very moment, within the royal court, a regular session was underway.

Seated on the throne was a boy with unmistakably childish features, the ten-year-old puppet king Amadeo.

Amadeo sat grinning and swinging his legs on the throne, as though nothing in the world concerned him in the slightest.

In the solemn atmosphere of the court, this young king seemed completely out of place, looking every bit the child who had turned an important session into a game.

Standing beside him was a stern knight named Diaz de Vivar, formerly a member of the royal guard. As a young squire he had trained under Claudia, and later, due to his outstanding skill and bravery in battle, he earned the royal family's favor and became King Amadeo's personal guard knight.

After the royal sword saint Claudia's "betrayal," the young Vivar was deeply bewildered. Having studied under Claudia, he found it hard to believe the noble female knight would ever break her oath. He harbored suspicion toward Alfonso and attempted to investigate certain events from back then, but was thwarted by layer upon layer of obstacles, and the matter eventually fizzled out.

Vivar came from a noble family and possessed a pure, upright soul. He was trusted by countless knights within the court, his standing nearly approaching that of Claudia in former days.

Alfonso sat one step below Amadeo, for he was not merely the chancellor but also the king's mentor—a position symbolizing authority second only to the sovereign.

"Lord Capreis, the session has concluded. Do you still have anything to say?"

In the vast hall, only an elderly man named Capreis remained; all the other nobles had already departed.

Capreis was the kingdom's current finance minister. On that fateful night of turmoil, it had been he who secretly escorted Claudia away from the capital. The two were friends, both suspecting that Alfonso was orchestrating disasters behind the scenes—though they had never found any concrete evidence.

"Your Majesty, the current taxes are far too heavy for those in the slums. They can hardly afford even the cheapest black bread anymore. If this continues, those people will begin to doubt your capability and may secretly organize to assassinate you. I pray Your Majesty might ease the tax burden somewhat. Those people would surely be grateful for your generosity and mercy and abandon their thoughts of rebellion..."

"I don't quite understand." Amadeo tilted his small head and asked innocently, "If they can't afford cheap black bread, why not eat more delicious cake?"

Alfonso was momentarily stunned, reminded of a familiar figure. "Your Majesty, cake is far more expensive than black bread. If they cannot even afford bread, then cake is merely an empty hope."

"Huh? Is that really the case?" Amadeo widened his eyes, finding it hard to believe. "I know nothing about such matters. They should be left to the teacher to decide. After all, I am still a child and lack the teacher's wisdom. The teacher will handle everything for me."

Capreis bowed, a hint of dissatisfaction crossing his face. The king was already ten years old and still knew nothing, so foolish that everything had to be handled by Alfonso. What was the point of even having a king?

"Is this matter truly so difficult to handle, Lord Capreis?" Alfonso asked with a serious tone.

"Yes. Recently, there have already been quite a few cases of mass disturbances in various regions. I fear they will sooner or later escalate into large-scale rebellion. Therefore, reducing the tax burden is imperative."

"Taxes cannot be reduced. Using the kingdom's land, drinking its water, breathing its sweet air—paying money to the kingdom's master is only natural, is it not?" Alfonso paused, then spoke meaningfully.

"If the poor cannot pay their taxes on time, what value do they have left? It would be better if they simply disappeared."

"We have a strong military and need not fear any rebellion. This is a good thing—it gives us reason to eliminate all the slums."

"Rest assured, Lord Capreis. I understand the poor very well."

"Kill all who dare rebel, slaughter as many as there are, and those wretches will naturally be filled with terror."

"Once the slum dwellers come to realize their fate, they will resign themselves to living like foul-smelling rats in the sewers, continuing to scrape by. They will never again dare to face the glaring sunlight."

The new volume will have more content to process, so please bear with us a little.

title: Chapter 2 — TITLE: Everyone Has Their Own Plans
content:
Chapter 2 — TITLE: Everyone Has Their Own Plans

Volume 33 · Chapter 2

Alfonso's cold-blooded remarks sent chills through Caprice, leaving him momentarily unsure how to respond.

Caprice had assumed that Alfonso, coming from the same slums as himself, would harbour some shred of compassion for the lower classes—only to discover he had overestimated him. Alfonso simply wanted to squeeze every last drop of value from the slums before discarding them.

"Lord Alfonso, wouldn't it be unwise to handle this matter exactly as you've commanded?"

"Lord Caprice, do you have an objection?" Alfonso countered sharply.

"Your iron-fisted policies will only provoke fiercer resistance and won't solve the problem at its root. They will likely spark the dissatisfaction of everyone except the nobility, which would be extremely detrimental to the kingdom's stability." Caprice, unwilling to let it go, argued his case firmly. "Looking throughout human history, leaders who have governed the lower classes through cruel methods all met dismal ends—"

"Oh?" Alfonso let out a cold laugh, asking with apparent interest, "And what do you suggest we do instead to make the kingdom more stable?"

"Reduce the tax burden, and in Your Majesty's name, unite the nobles to distribute relief funds, ensuring the poor don't starve to death. Only then will the kingdom truly be stable. Laziness is human nature—if their bellies are full, who would willingly lead a riot?" Caprice paused, then continued, "Besides, Your Majesty is already ten years old. It's time to accomplish something and establish an image of a sovereign in the hearts of all his subjects."

"Foolish. There was once someone who shared your naive thinking, only to be ruthlessly betrayed by the nobles. Your Majesty is still very young. If your advice were adopted, it would surely spark discontent among the nobles. If any danger were to arise, Lord Caprice, could you bear the responsibility?" Alfonso's tone turned stern, thick with threat. He had no intention of letting the young king Amadeo step into the spotlight—being a mere puppet would suffice.

Caprice was rendered speechless and lowered his head. "I had no other intention; I was only thinking of the kingdom's stability."

"Unless I knew you had always been faithful to Your Majesty, I might have suspected you of conspiring to harm him!"

Alfonso painted the matter in extremely grave terms, slapping a enormous accusation onto Caprice's head and leaving him gasping for breath. He had only offered a suggestion—how had he been turned into a traitor?

"Rebels across various regions need not concern you. Round up all the ringleaders and execute them. In no time, the unrest will be quelled. Even if it escalates into a large-scale rebellion, we have elite troops ready to crush it. Don't ever bring this up again. Slums should not exist in the first place—if given the opportunity, all the large and small slums throughout the kingdom will be dealt with. That filthy, foul-smelling bunch is utterly worthless."

"Your Majesty, may I ask your thoughts on this?" Caprice clung to a sliver of hope, hoping the young king might exercise his royal authority rather than simply obey Alfonso in everything.

"Me?" Amadeo bit his finger and pondered for a moment, then smiled. "I think Teacher is right. Let's do exactly as Teacher says—Teacher never makes mistakes."

A smug smile spread across Alfonso's face. Glancing sideways at Caprice, he thought to himself that someone relying on seniority to challenge him stood no chance against him. Amadeo would only listen to him.

Caprice silently closed his eyes and let out a heavy sigh. He had grown somewhat despondent about this nation—continued down this path and its destruction was only a matter of time.

He couldn't simply stand by and watch Alfonso plunge the entire kingdom into chaos. He had to find some way to stop it.

The foremost problem was the young king Amadeo, who had become nothing but Alfonso's puppet, entirely lacking the ability to think independently. How could such a vast nation be entrusted to a puppet? The young king had to be replaced, and an heir with his own convictions chosen instead.

However, the late king had only two children—one, Diana, who had gone missing, and the other, Amadeo.

Caprice decided to investigate Diana. According to the late king's original wishes, Diana had been the designated heir, the future Queen of Spain—it was only because she had been taken away by Clodia that the throne fell to Amadeo.

Although Clodia had fled the capital over twenty years ago without telling anyone where she was going, leaving no one to know Diana's whereabouts, Caprice had recently heard some interesting matters from his old friend Captain Dennis—

That there was a female adventurer whose appearance and age somewhat resembled the missing Princess Diana, and who wore a pendant bearing the royal family crest.

Although it was no uncommon occurrence for maids to steal palace belongings and sell them outside, so their identities could not be confirmed, Caprice felt this matter was worth exploiting. Perhaps he could use it to dethrone Amadeo and place this female adventurer on the throne, making her his own puppet.

Caprice knew this plan was exceedingly dangerous, but the kingdom was certain to perish under Alfonso's hands. It might as well be him who steered the nation back onto the right path, honouring the late king's final wishes and building a thriving realm.

If not for having harboured a slight expectation of Amadeo, Caprice would never have tolerated Alfonso for so long. Now he had given up all hope. For the fate of the kingdom, Amadeo—who lacked any conviction of his own—had to be removed.

"Lord Alfonso, may I ask one final question?"

"Hmm?" Alfonso raised his head in surprise.

"You, who also came from the slums—don't you feel the slightest pity for the poor? Now that you are the chancellor, shouldn't you be the one to change this injustice?" Caprice asked an extremely sarcastic question. No one in the court dared mention Alfonso's origin anymore—this was clearly a mockery!

As expected, Alfonso's expression darkened instantly, a sharp killing intent flashing deep within his eyes, as though a thief disguised as a noble in fine garments had been forcibly stripped bare before the eyes of all.

Enraged, Alfonso could barely control his emotions, causing Clodia's cold poison to spread rapidly through his body—his hands turned frostbitten and blue-purple!

Fortunately, Alfonso quickly suppressed the cold poison within him and regained his composure—but all of this fell into the eyes of his personal guard knight Vival, who took note of it.

Alfonso took a deep breath and answered in an unquestionable tone—

"I am different from them."

With the meeting concluded, the young king Amadeo, accompanied by his personal guard knight Vival, left the grand hall, ready to slip out of the palace and have some fun outside.

"La la la~"

Amadeo hopped along, looking utterly carefree and happy—his escorts were long accustomed to such behavior.

Only after evading the gaze of all his escorts did Amadeo's smile vanish, his expression turning unusually serious. At merely ten years old, an air of authority radiated from deep within his eyes.

"Vival, is there something you'd like to tell me?"

"Yes." Vival glanced around, confirming there were no spies of Alfonso in sight, before daring to respond—

"Alfonso... was injured."

title: Chapter 3 — There's an Extra Chapter
content:
Chapter 3 — There's an Extra Chapter

Volume 33 · Chapter 3

"Are you serious? You didn't mistake it, did you?"

Amadeo asked in surprise. In his eyes, Alfonso was not only high-ranking and powerful but also an extremely formidable mage, so there were probably very few people who could injure him.

"It's true, Your Majesty." Vival bowed slightly and said softly, "And it seems quite severe."

"Is that so?" Amadeo frowned and pondered carefully, making it hard to tell what scheme the young king, who had just turned twenty years old, was plotting in his mind.

"Just now, Alfonso was provoked by Caples and suffered severe frostbite on his hand. Although it lasted only an instant, I saw it clearly. This is a symptom brought on by cold poison invading the body. Alfonso will likely need to devote himself entirely to suppressing the cold poison to ease his deteriorating condition." Vival spoke in earnest.

"Oh?" Amadeo rested his chin on his hand, puzzled, and asked, "Can you defeat Alfonso?"

"No, I have no chance of victory at all. With my strength, I might not even survive one exchange against Alfonso." Vival paused and added, "However, if Alfonso is severely injured enough, I might have a chance to fight him."

"What are the odds?" Amadeo pressed.

"One percent." Vival answered sincerely.

"Then isn't that essentially impossible to win?" Amadeo sighed and countered, "Alfonso is so powerful. Who injured him so badly?"

"I don't know, but Alfonso recently led the assassination squad away from the kingdom for a while. Perhaps he encountered a very troublesome opponent somewhere?" Vival speculated. He could not confirm who had injured Alfonso.

"Alfonso being injured might be a good opportunity for me."

Amadeo subconsciously clenched his fist, a deep hatred flashing in his eyes. He was clearly not as foolish as others perceived him to be.

He had been playing the fool for a very long time. Since childhood, he had followed Alfonso's arrangements in everything. Even the slightest disagreement would arouse Alfonso's suspicion and could make his situation even more dangerous.

Although pretending to be a stupid fool was exhausting and disappointed the council of elderly ministers, at the very least it could lull Alfonso into letting his guard down.

Only then could Amadeo continue sitting on the throne without worrying about being killed by Alfonso on any given day. Only by老实 acting like a stupid puppet could he make the enemies who sought to harm him drop their vigilance.

When Amadeo was young, he understood nothing and thought Alfonso was simply fulfilling his duties as a teacher and handling everything on behalf of someone with zero experience. He saw nothing wrong with it. But three years ago, an incident made him wake up and realize how dangerous his situation truly was —

A group of lowly female servants were gossiping in private, saying that he was not the legitimate heir of the kingdom, and that his older sister Diana, who had been kidnapped by a female knight when she was young, was the true heir.

Amadeo, who had been doted on by everyone, had never endured such an insult in his life. Upon learning this, he flew into a rage and ordered his guards to execute those few rabble-rousing maids, but not a single person obeyed the king's command. It was only when Alfonso stepped forward that those chattering maids were punished.

From that moment on, Amadeo's view of Alfonso changed. A layer of fear was added. The teacher who seemed to care for him deeply was actually the most dangerous person by his side. His fate had already been controlled by this amiable-looking man.

It was like having a vicious tiger beside him. When it was not hungry, it could let him live one more day; when it was hungry, it could eat him up in minutes to fill its belly.

Amadeo had always been waiting for an opportunity to reclaim his power. But Alfonso's influence in the kingdom was too vast, concentrating nearly all the nobility. Bringing him down easily was practically impossible.

Everywhere around him were Alfonso's spies. Every move he made would be reported back. He even knew what Amadeo had eaten and how many times he had been to the toilet — Alfonso was fully aware of everything.

This made Amadeo feel a profound sense of powerlessness. He desperately needed to cultivate his own trusted people. So, using the excuse of "wanting a companion to play with," he rejected the people Alfonso had recommended and chose Vival, who had a clean background, an upright character, and no connection to Alfonso whatsoever, to be his personal guard knight. Vival was the only person he could trust.

The only way Amadeo could think of to turn the tables was to kill Alfonso. The guy's lowly origin from the slums was a fatal weakness. The nobility had not fully submitted to him. As long as Alfonso died, all the factions attached to him would collapse in an instant.

"Vival, I can no longer wait. Let's prepare to make our move."

"Huh!"

Shock appeared on Vival's face. He had served Amadeo for three years, and finally, the moment to act had arrived.

At first, Vival had not been keen on becoming Amadeo's knight precisely because he was a puppet controlled by Alfonso. Following such a master meant there was no future, equivalent to yielding to Alfonso, no different from those sycophantic lapdogs.

However, after getting to know him more deeply, Vival changed his mind. Amadeo harbored considerable ambition and had always been in a state of enduring hardship to achieve a great goal. He genuinely wanted to change the country, which was completely different from the rumors labeling him a "foolish king."

"Your Majesty, are you certain? If we act now, there will be no turning back."

"I know. I have made my resolve. This is a gamble with our lives as the stakes. I will die sooner or later anyway — perhaps I'll be killed by Alfonso and replaced on some random day. It's merely a question of when. If we win, our future is bright. If we lose, we simply die. Why not fight for it? If we give up this opportunity, we may never have another chance to kill Alfonso, and we will inevitably be eliminated by him sooner or later." Amadeo raised his head and stared into Vival's eyes.

Vival was stunned for a moment. He realized the moment that would determine their fate had come. Whether the shadow笼罩ing the kingdom by Alfonso could be dispersed — it all depended on whether the upcoming plan would succeed.

Alfonso's power was growing stronger by the day. When his authority reached its peak, he would surely kill Amadeo, who would have lost all value, and take the Spanish throne for himself.

If Vival's judgment was correct, Alfonso's injury was extremely severe and had reached a point where he could not afford to be distracted at all. Striking him decisively now would inevitably trap him both inside and out, greatly increasing the odds of killing him.

If they failed to seize this opportunity, killing Alfonso in the future would be far more difficult.

Vival immediately knelt on one knee, placed his right hand over his chest, and responded with the tone of an oath.

"I understand, Your Majesty. I swear upon my soul to serve you forever."

"Our lives are now bound together. There is no way back. This is a battle we cannot afford to lose." Amadeo paused and asked, "Have you prepared everything?"

"Yes, I have been preparing all along. I have already contacted several Saint-tier experts from the royal guard. They are trustworthy and have long harbored resentment toward Alfonso. They are willing to fight for you." Vival lowered his head and answered firmly.

"You think a handful of people like you can defeat Alfonso? That will still be very difficult." Amadeo showed a worried expression, feeling the preparations were still insufficient.

"Your Majesty need not worry. I have written a letter to contact a senior who once worked in the royal guard. If she is willing to help, we have nine chances out of ten of killing Alfonso!" Vival said confidently.

"Who?" Amadeo asked in confusion.

"Her name is Circe. After leaving the guard, she became a Purple Gold-ranked adventurer and is known as the Potion Witch. Although she has a quirky personality, she is a highly reliable person." Vival lowered his head, appearing to have some undisclosed circumstances.

However —

"Adventurers have always followed the rule of not interfering in any political struggles. I wonder if she is willing to make an exception to assist us?"

title: Chapter 4 — Bird Language
content:
Chapter 4 — Bird Language

Volume 33 · Chapter 4

The port of the Holy Roman Empire had a merchant ship flying the Rose family flag slowly approaching the dock.

Alice was originally going to take a passenger ship with Chris to the Great Snow Mountain, but on the way she unexpectedly met Captain Dennis, whom she had not seen for a long time, and learned that he was transporting goods to the Kingdom of Spain and would stop in Rome for a while along the way.

Actually, Alice did not like to trouble others, but under Captain Dennis's enthusiastic invitation, it was not easy to refuse, so she took a ride on the favorable wind ship.

Captain Dennis held Merlin in genuine respect, and in his treatment of his wife and children, he would naturally be slack in the slightest, even giving up his own captain's quarters for Alice and Chris to live in alone.

To Captain Dennis, maintaining a good relationship with Merlin had always been an invisible huge wealth. He had always had the habit of making friends everywhere, especially with an "adventurer" like Merlin who had no affiliation with any force.

The merchant ship continued to approach the wharf, sea gulls were circling in the sky, and the splendid Roman buildings stood tall, giving a feeling of a new intellectual renaissance, full of vigorous vitality.

However cunning and base the Holy Church might be, within its governed area, a prosperous scene could always appear.

Little Chris wriggled in her mother's arms, very excited to see new things, reaching out her small hands toward the sky and grabbing randomly, wanting to pull the sea gulls circling above into her arms, "So many pigeons~"

"That is a sea gull, we will dock soon, be good and don't cause trouble." Alice put on a stern look.

"Sea gull?" Chris tilted her small head, she couldn't tell the difference at all, "I want to touch them."

"Forget it, only those domesticated pigeons will let you touch them. Normal animals are afraid of humans and won't approach easily." Alice helplessly explained. On the way, Chris's naughty nature was fully exposed, and there was never a completely quiet moment.

"Mom is lying again, all small animals can understand my words, and they like to get close to me. The dog at Grandma's house is like that too!" Chris said unhappily.

Alice rolled her eyes, thinking the little thing was talking nonsense again; to this day, it was still unclear if she was a human being? The nature of dogs is to be close to humans.

"Pigeon, pigeon, come quickly to me, let me touch, come quickly" Chris waved her fat little hand, constantly calling out.

Alice dryly laughed, waiting for her beloved daughter to make a fool of herself, and then crying and asking herself why?

But who would have thought that under Chris's call, the sea gulls hovering near the port suddenly gathered together and rushed over with mighty momentum, looking as if they had been mentally controlled by someone, and actually flew in an orderly direction toward the slowly approaching merchant ship.

"Uh!" Alice subconsciously thought there was a sudden attack, and immediately took a defensive posture.

The surging sea gulls quickly scattered and flew high into the sky, leaving white feathers slowly falling, making Alice feel at a loss, not understanding if this group of birds had gone crazy?

Alice was worried that her beloved daughter would be frightened, preparing to comfort her for a few words, but when she lowered her head, she found that a small sea gull had already landed on Chris's hands, folding its wings and looking very well-behaved.

"Mommy, look, they can understand what I'm saying~" Chris's face smiled like a flower.

Alice had a complex expression, said nothing, thinking that this must be a coincidence, with so many birds, there would always be one that is relatively silly, just happened to be discovered by Chris.

Chris was serious, communicating with the sea gull as if it were a person, "gugu"

The small sea gull tilted its head, spread its wings and fluttered its feathers, emitting a low chirp, as if responding to Chris?

Alice's face instantly turned dark, wondering if her own eyes had a problem, her cute daughter was actually speaking pigeon language with a sea gull—

My precious daughter hasn't gone crazy, has she? When exactly did her head become abnormal?

"Mom, it says it's a sea gull, not a pigeon!" Chris said innocently.

What a nonsense! Alice suspected that her daughter was putting on airs, and she didn't believe Chris could speak bird language at all.

"Gugu gugu gugu!" Chris continued communicating with the small sea gull, then turned her head and said, "It says Mommy doesn't have Chris cute, Mommy is fierce, looking at it just means an old maid, is Mommy really that?"

"Hah!" Alice's veins on her forehead twitched, being angered enough, she flashed and grabbed the small sea gull coldly, "Although sea gull meat is not good to eat, but I don't mind roasting it and swallowing it."

The small sea gull immediately flipped its eyes and was scared unconscious, and even Chris shivered and dared not make a sound, immediately pretending to be a good baby, and would not dare to translate randomly afterwards.

"Haha, Miss Alice." Captain Dennis had already stood behind her, laughing, "Perhaps your child can really communicate with animals, animals have always been particularly tolerant of human children, perhaps at a very young age, possessing some potential, it's a pity that they lose it when they grow up."

"You are joking, they are just children talking nonsense." Alice embarrassedly smiled, putting down the sea gull in her hand, too lazy to bother with a silly bird, "Thank you for willing to take us here, Chris, quickly thank Uncle Dennis."

"Thank you, Big Hat Uncle." Little Chris very shyly responded, shrinking into her mother's arms, still a bit timid.

"Big Hat?" Captain Dennis looked at his old naval hat on his head, faintly smiling, "Haha, it seems I have a new nickname now?"

Alice looked at Chris helplessly, the little thing always liked to call people by features, could it be because she couldn't remember names? It was really impolite.

"Miss Alice, you don't need to be so polite. I survived from the mysterious sea thanks to Captain Merlin's care, this little favor cannot compensate for Captain Merlin's kindness, moreover we are transporting goods to Spain, passing through Rome originally needed to stay here for a while, this is just a small effort, moreover with Purple Gold Adventurer accompanying us, we don't need to pay money, where is there such a cheap thing?" Captain Dennis was very polite.

"Merlin..." Alice slightly furrowed her brows, thinking how he was doing over there? After returning, should we properly talk about the relationship between us? Now it's a bit inexplicable.

"True like Dennis looking at Alice's figure, couldn't help but let out a sigh.

"What?" Alice was surprised and raised her head.

"Cough cough!" Captain Dennis hurriedly coughed lightly to cover up the embarrassment, and smiled bitterly—

"Sorry I was a bit out of sorts, your beautiful appearance always makes me recall someone."

"Occasionally in a daze, your figures

"Always overlap together, perhaps it's a coincidence?"
