title: Chapter 5 — Snow in the Homeland (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 5 — Snow in the Homeland (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 33 · Chapter 5

"Who are you? Do I resemble someone you know?" Alice asked curiously, always feeling that Captain Dennis was looking for someone's shadow in me. "Yes, that's Josephine, the former queen of the Spanish Kingdom. You share many similarities," Captain Dennis said slowly. "That queen." Alice smiled, thinking she always managed to cause this captain's misunderstanding, even though she had no relation to any kingdom's royalty, having grown up in the snow mountains since childhood, and didn't know why Captain Dennis kept linking her with Queen Josephine. "Your appearances are somewhat similar, and your personalities are also somewhat alike; both are gentle people who hold strong compassion for the weak, always willing to lend a hand in any situation," Captain Dennis said with a smile. Alice blushed a little, feeling she wasn't as outstanding as he said, always feeling it was others, "You seem to miss that queen very much? Could it be that you were quite acquainted?" "Acquainted? When I was young in Spain I was just a nobody, an officer in the kingdom's fleet; how could I possibly have been acquainted with the noble queen? I only saw her from afar once," Captain Dennis recalled. "So you fell for her?" Alice could still see something; Captain Dennis's eyes when mentioning the queen were different each time, clearly the look of admiration. "Hahaha" Dennis stumbled over his words, couldn't help laughing, subconsciously stroking his white beard, "I don't deny having some admiration for Queen Josephine; after all, the queen is a very beautiful person, but I feel more of a heartfelt respect for her—yes, respect." "Respect..." Alice grew doubtful; in her impression, Mr. Dennis was a very lofty person, capable of making this experienced captain feel subdued; only someone strong and upright could achieve that; perhaps the queen had some extraordinary quality? "The queen is actually a very ordinary woman, born into a noble family, hardly ever exposed to the outside world; I heard she often utters foolish remarks, completely incomprehensible," Captain Dennis shook his head. "It sounds like the queen has quite a problem?" Alice said, embarrassed. "That's true, but precisely because of that she stands out." Captain Dennis paused, then said in a low voice, "The Spanish Kingdom is a country where the lower and upper classes are completely isolated, with an enormous wealth gap, possessing the world's largest and most numerous slums, so many see it as a paradise for the rich and a hell for the poor. In such an environment, Queen Josephine, with her noble status, chose to pity the lowly—hard to imagine she endured such pressure amidst the prevailing decadence of the court; this spirit deeply moved me." Alice fell silent, listening to Captain Dennis's narration; this queen really is a fine person, capable of acting contrary to her status in such a harsh environment, which should also be considered a risky move. "Perhaps because of Queen Josephine's actions, she angered many authorities, causing internal strife in the court that led to her assassination; in fact she had no need to concern herself with those lowly peasants; if she lived like other nobles, she might have continued to live well." Captain Dennis slowly removed his naval cap, his gaze turning regretful, "A kind person like the queen should not meet misfortune—this is fate's injustice. Even if everyone forgets, I will never forget her warm smile; just a distant glance is enough for any conscientious person to remember forever." Understanding why you respect the queen, however... Alice nodded, explaining tactfully, "Since childhood I have followed my teacher in sword practice; my teacher once said I am an orphan abandoned by my parents; as for the pendant on my neck, perhaps my parents once served as servants in the Spanish royal court? The pendant is merely some compensation given to those who adopted me, so I have no relation to that queen." "I know, and I hope you can forgive my presumption," Captain Dennis said, bowing slightly to express apology. "Actually, when I was little I also dreamed of being a princess or the like, but now thinking about it it's really childish—what princess would spend all day fighting like me?" Alice said in a teasing tone. "Little Chris's eyes lit up, the cowlick on her head swaying, 'If Mom is a princess, then Chris is a little princess too! Hehe~'" "Nice try, you're impossible; don't keep talking to animals all day, or people will think you're an idiot." Alice said sternly, tapping her daughter's head. Captain Dennis, looking at Alice and her daughter, thought it might just be a coincidence, because Miss Alice is always full of justice, making me have some illusion? Alice took Chris's little hand and came to the foot of the Great Snow Mountain; the village not far away was already near. As a child she had come to the village many times, helping Teacher Claudya purchase daily necessities, and got along fairly well with the villagers. It had been many years since she last returned; Alice found that hardly anything had changed, possibly because the place is too isolated, with outsiders rarely coming besides merchants—. From the chimneys of the little houses, thin cooking smoke continuously rose, adding vitality to this dead, cold place; the wind swept snowflakes, making it seem not so icy. "Cold?" Alice asked, pulling her warm coat tighter and lowering her head with concern. "Not cold, I'm about to see grandma, I'm so happy~" Little Chris waved her hands, her whole body already wrapped like a little zongzi, like a fluffy ball wobbling behind her mom. "After seeing grandma, don't be mischievous, listen to Mom, okay?" Alice squatted down, helping her daughter tidy her clothes. "Mm-hmm!" Little Chris nodded like a pecking chick, still thinking about the toys grandma would make. Ding-ling-ling—. At that moment, a jingling bell rang; the experienced guide Old Nick, driving a herd of yaks toward the village, his face frozen red, his beard covered with a layer of ice shards, his expression heavy without a hint of a smile, as if his heart were full of worries? Old Nick lowered his head, absentmindedly following the yak herd past Alice and her mother, not even realizing there were people nearby—showing his mind had long since drifted from his beloved yaks. Alice instantly recognized this old man—the guide who often led caravans across the Great Snow Mountain; as a child he used to sneakily carry candy up the mountain for her from her teacher, a person very popular with children as a herder. She could never forget that as a child she most looked forward to Old Nick leading the caravan up the mountain, because she would always see the novel goods the caravan brought, and also be able to secretly enjoy the sweet candies. Childhood Alice spent her days tediously practicing swordsmanship; Old Nick was one of the few who could give her pleasant memories, naturally her recollection remains fresh—. "Uncle Nick?" "Uncle Nick!!" "It's me! You haven't forgotten me, have you?"

title: Chapter 6 — Childhood Secret
content:
Chapter 6 — Childhood Secret

Volume 33 · Chapter 6

"Alice?"

Old Nick stopped his steps, lifted his head blankly, and saw Alice's face suddenly broke into a smile. Wrinkles from old age were all squeezed together.

Although she hadn't seen each other for so many years, Alice looked much more mature compared to before, but that clear gaze had not changed at all.

Old Nick was happy inside. Before this, he hadn't known where Alice, who had been accompanying the Snow Mountain Sword Saint all along, had gone? He also hadn't dared to ask with a thick skin.

Meeting again, he couldn't help but look her over carefully.

Actually, Old Nick was a lonely old man with no relatives, so he liked children very much. Every time he passed by the top of the Snow Mountain, he would bring some candies for Alice, completely treating her as his own granddaughter to dote on.

"It's me. Hasn't it been so long that you can't recognize me?" Alice awkwardly smiled, thinking that her changes shouldn't be that big, right?

"It's really you! I thought I had the wrong person. You look much more mature now, completely not a little girl anymore." Old Nick laughed up, looking at Alice with eyes full of affection.

"Let me see..." Alice lowered her head a bit embarrassedly, thinking that when she left the Snow Mountain, she wasn't really a little girl, was she? She was already an adult.

Old Nick noticed the little Chris hiding behind Alice, and his eyes instantly lit up. With a face full of surprise, he said, "You've already become a mom? ! Goodness! Am I dreaming? The change is too big!"

"Yes, I've already become a mom. This is my daughter, called Chris." Alice pulled her daughter forward and said softly, "Come, Chris, call Uncle Nick."

"Huh?" Little Chris lifted her head, blinked her big eyes, and said, "Rancher grandfather!"

"Call Grandpa Nick, don't give people random nicknames." Alice immediately furrowed her face and said seriously.

"No problem, Rancher grandfather is also nice, hahaha." Old Nick rummaged in his arms, a regretful expression on his face, and said, "Ever since you left, I wouldn't keep candies on me anymore, what a pity."

"It's okay, Uncle Nick. This child doesn't like candy very much. You don't need to be so polite." Alice said in a comforting tone.

"Hmph! ! !" Little Chris pouted, as if protesting to mom in her heart. I like it! Who said I don't like it!

This child is really cute, and she looks very much like you when you were young. In the future, she must be a great beauty." Old Nick laughed and praised, then changed the subject and asked, "Is there something this time you came back? We haven't seen each other in a long time, do you want to go to my house as a guest, and have a cup of hot tea to warm up?"

"Don't need to. This time I came to visit my teacher, because there are some things we must talk about well." Alice became embarrassed.

Hearing that Alice came back to visit Clodya, Old Nick's face instantly changed. The head clouded by joy quickly cooled down.

Since Clodya's death, he had been very self-blaming, feeling that the death of the Snow Mountain Sword Saint had something to do with him. If he hadn't brought that group of people with ulterior motives up the mountain, maybe the tragedy wouldn't have happened?

Although he was also deceived by Alfonso, he truly thought that group of guys weren't bad people, but old friends of Clodya's. But the fact that he became an accomplice to the crime was something he couldn't explain.

Now that Alice came back to visit her teacher, he didn't know how to tell her this. An inexplicable huge pressure surged up in his heart.

Old Nick's expression was calm, and he lowered his head silently, hesitating whether to tell Alice this painful thing. He felt that once Alice heard the news, she would definitely find it very hard to accept.

"What's wrong? Your face looks a bit ugly." Alice asked in puzzlement.

"Nothing haha." Old Nick dryly laughed, deciding to still invite Alice to his house as a guest. After all, they couldn't see Clodya on the mountain anymore, "The time is not early anymore. Now going up the mountain is not convenient. Why don't you rest at my place for a while? It won't delay much of your time."

Alice felt the kindness was hard to refuse. She thought, anyway, she had already reached the foot of the Snow Mountain. It was easy to see the teacher. It wasn't worth wasting this time. Moreover, Uncle Nick had been so good to her. If she refused, it would be a bit unworthy.

In the warm small wooden house, many beast heads were hung on the walls. The environment looked quite simple. No matter how fierce the wind outside was, it completely didn't affect the temperature inside the house.

The flames in the hearth were burning vigorously. Alice and Old Nick were sitting at the wooden table, happily discussing.

Little Chris was standing on a chair, sticking out her little tongue and licking once the hot goat milk in the cup. Suddenly she felt it was hot, and quickly pulled her tongue back, covering her small mouth and humming unhappily, showing a pitiful look that wanted to drink but was afraid of it being hot.

Alice surveyed the surroundings and sighed, saying, "This is the first time I've come to your house as a guest. Before, my teacher was very strict and didn't allow me to go down the mountain randomly."

"I know, your teacher's temper is very weird. Every time I go up the mountain, I have to remind the caravan people not to provoke your teacher, otherwise, when the blizzard comes at night, they will definitely kick us out of the wooden house, hahaha." Old Nick recalled the past things.

"I am very grateful for your care. If it weren't for you, I might never have known that there was such a vast world outside the Snow Mountain. My teacher only taught me cultivation and never told me about things outside the Snow Mountain." Alice smiled helplessly, thinking in her heart that besides being too strict, her teacher had no other flaws.

"Your teachers are all for your own good, after all, the outside is full of dangers. Your teacher has always wanted to protect you." Old Nick said tactfully.

"I know." Alice paused, then said lowly, "I'm no longer a child. I should have some freedom, no matter how much."

"This isn't constraining you. I can understand your teacher's mood. Perhaps when you reach a certain age, you will understand. Your teacher just doesn't hope you get hurt at all, so she does this. She loves you deeply." Old Nick said with deep meaning.

"Is that so?" Alice thought carefully, looking at the cute daughter beside her. It seemed indeed so. If one day Chris had to leave alone, she probably wouldn't agree, fearing she would be bullied without her protection.

"Tell you a secret. Your teacher has repeatedly instructed me not to tell anyone. Actually, the candies you secretly ate from me when you were a child were meant by your teacher. She has already paid me, she just didn't want you to know." Old Nick lowered his head tactfully, and said, "Your teacher might be different from what you think. She is not strict, on the contrary, she will silently protect you."

"Huh? It was my teacher's intention?"

Alice was startled and stared wide-eyed. When she was a child, she had to eat candies from her teacher with her heart in her mouth, secretly and furtively. She didn't expect that she knew all along, and even paid money?

Alice's mood was complex after discovering this childhood secret. She didn't know what to say for a while. Although she was cheated by the teacher, her heart was warm, and she could vaguely feel Clodya's silent care for her.

Alice frowned and thought of when she was a child secretly eating candies, and the teacher was hiding in the dark laughing. Suddenly she felt very foolish.

"Why go to such trouble? Candy and stuff..."

"Why not just buy it directly for me? Just to maintain your strict image? Tsk tsk!"

"The teacher is a bad-hearted person."

title: Chapter 7 — Rock Pile Beneath the Snow Mountain
content:
Chapter 7 — Rock Pile Beneath the Snow Mountain

Volume 33 · Chapter 7

“I think your teacher uses this method to urge you to progress constantly. You are now a mother, so you should understand that sometimes you need to be strict, otherwise children won’t listen.” Old Nick said softly.

“It’s like that! That’s right!” Alice frowned at Chris, who made a mischievous face at her mother. Her expression turned serious.

“I hope you don’t misunderstand. Your teacher is actually a very kind person, but she needs to pretend to be strict. Maybe she has her own reasons.” Old Nick didn’t want Alice to think badly of her teacher, because Klodija was already dead. If she was still complaining to her beloved student, that would be too pitiful.

“I understand, but Nick uncle, you seem strange today. I remember you were afraid of my teacher. Why are you talking so much about her today?” Alice asked curiously.

Old Nick was at a loss for words, feeling it was time to reveal the truth. He took a deep breath and said, “Alice, you don’t need to go to the mountain. Even if you climb up, you won’t see your teacher.”

“What? Why? Is my teacher not on the mountain, temporarily away for some reason?” Alice frowned, her voice filled with doubt. “It’s strange. Apart from me, she doesn’t seem to have anyone she must see. If it’s not important, she shouldn’t leave.”

“Alice, it’s not what you think. Your teacher has…” Old Nick swallowed hard, feeling a great pressure in his chest.

Alice noticed something was wrong and became serious, asking, “Are you hiding something? Where is my teacher?”

“Your teacher…”

The air in the little cottage seemed to freeze, lasting for a full five seconds of silence. The fire in the fireplace was almost out, the flames dimming.

Little Chris noticed the sudden change in atmosphere and looked up, seeing her mother’s face darken to an extreme. She had never seen her mother look like this before. It was an expression she rarely saw, even when she was naughty and made her mother angry.

“Mommy?”

Alice broke the silence with a dry laugh, using a mocking tone. “Nick uncle, don’t play this joke. I’m not a child anymore. I can see through pranks, and this one isn’t funny at all. You’d better not use me for your amusement. I won’t fall for it.”

Old Nick’s cracked lips moved, but he didn’t know how to explain the situation to make Alice accept the reality. He could imagine how devastated Alice would be when she found out about her teacher’s death.

It wasn’t that Alice didn’t believe the news, but rather that she didn’t want to believe it. How could that woman, who was as strong as a monster and could break through any limit at any time, die? Unless a huge meteorite fell directly on her head, but that probability was even lower than Merlin winning a horse race.

“You’re an ordinary person, so you probably don’t know how strong my teacher is. She’s not just a Saint-tier saint; she’s a monster who can break through limits at any time. You should never imagine how powerful that old woman is. How could she die? This is a boring joke, and I can easily see through it.”

“Alice, it’s not a joke. Your teacher is really dead. She was killed by a very dark man. I buried her at the foot of the snow mountain.” Old Nick’s expression was serious, his eyes filled with sincerity, not wanting Alice to think the news was a joke or a boring prank.

Alice’s face remained emotionless and grew even paler. Her eyes became hollow.

She didn’t say anything, not knowing what to say.

She only knew that she would no longer hear her teacher’s voice urging her to train hard and warning her of all the unknown dangers.

She would no longer hear her teacher’s stories to make her fall asleep during the stormy nights.

And the things she used to do, like secretly buying her candy when she was a child, would all be a memory.

Her vision began to blur, as if a layer of clear glass had covered her eyes, flowing and moving gently.

The blizzard came, with snowflakes like feathers dancing with the wind like knives.

Looking up, the sky seemed endless, a dark vortex pouring snow and ice onto the filthy world.

This season, where everything seemed to be in a state of stagnation, was indeed not a happy one.

A small mound stood at the foot of the vast snow mountain, now covered in thick layers of snow. It was an easily forgotten, simple grave, hidden under the snow and wind, blending with the great snow mountain.

If it weren’t for the autumn water sword stuck in the grave, forming a simple tombstone, no one would have known that a swordsman was buried here.

A rare white-feathered vulture, with its wings spread wide, swooped down from the sky and landed on the hilt of the autumn water sword. It opened its white wings and made a “gaga” sound, as if telling the story of its owner’s misfortune.

Alice, wrapped in a warm cloak, stood in the blizzard, staring at the unremarkable grave. Her face was frozen, her emotions showing no movement.

Normally, Alice’s face would show her thoughts, but when it came to her teacher’s departure, she forgot how to express her feelings.

She had come here with Chris to see her teacher, Klodija, and express her thoughts, but instead, she found a pile of stones and a hurriedly left letter that had become a final goodbye.

Alice clenched her fists, her nails digging into her palms, her face muscles twitching, and her teeth grinding.

“Why…”

?） “Monthly ticket bonus update, monthly ticket bonus update, monthly ticket bonus update!”

Volume 33 · Chapter 8

Fifteen years ago, Alice was only five or six, but under Claudia's guidance she could already perform decent basic sword techniques. Though not a stunning genius, compared to ordinary children it was already quite good.

That was a night when a blizzard struck, with howling winds outside like wolves standing under the moon and howling long and loud, causing unease and bewilderment.

Inside the wooden cabin at the snow mountain's peak, candlelight flickered dimly, barely dispelling the endless darkness, and a gentle voice came from within, telling a story—

"The frog lifted its pitiful round eyes and said in a pleading tone, 'Please, dear princess, only your kiss can break the curse the evil witch has placed on me.' The beautiful princess was moved by its urgent plea; she bent down, picked up the slippery creature, and kissed the little frog, ._

Claudia slowly closed the storybook, not finishing the old-fashioned fairy tale, but deliberately stopping at a cliffhanger, so the young Alice would continue working hard at her training.

When Alice was young, Claudia coaxed and tricked her into hard training. The teacher had promised that if she trained seriously every day, she'd tell her these moving stories every night.

Alice worked hard foolishly to know the ending of the princess and prince's story, so she could hear their happy ending.

"What happens next? Hurry up and say it! Don't always stop at such an uncomfortable place! It's really annoying!" Little Alice with her ponytail pouted in protest. "The rest depends on your performance. If you complete one hundred sword training sessions tomorrow, I'll continue the story." Claudia placed the thick book aside and urged seriously, "It's late. Go to sleep. If you don't obey, not only will you have no story, but tomorrow's chicken leg will be mine—you'll only get the chicken butt."

"Hmph!" Little Alice was so angry her face turned red, rolling on the wooden bed, feeling like the most pitiful girl, bullied by the teacher every day.

"Go to sleep. Don't make me say it twice." Claudia's face was stern, her tone authoritative.

"The teacher has a mean heart! Always staring at me to bully me!" Little Alice lay stiffly on the bed, looking at the rough roof, feeling indignant.

"Sigh, I'm thinking of you. If you don't become strong, you'll be bullied. I can leave you the chicken butt; anyone else wouldn't even give you the chicken bones." Claudia covered Alice with a thick blanket and prepared to rest.

"You just scare me. Where are all those dangers? Merchants and Uncle Nick are so nice whenever caravans pass—way better than the teacher!" Little Alice complained naively.

Claudia glanced at Alice, shook her head, and explained, "Human hearts are hidden behind bellies; you can't judge good and evil from appearances. They're nice to you only because of me? If I were as weak as you, I'd probably be driven out by those greedy merchants."

"I won't believe you! It's all to make me listen to you!" Young Alice already had strong rebellious tendencies.

"Believe it or not. Later you'll realize I'm right." Claudia didn't want to argue; she knew she was right.

"If I were a princess, how nice!" Little Alice sighed suddenly.

"Hmm?" Claudia was startled. "Why would you think that?"

"Because noble princesses seem happy every day, doing nothing, just finding princes to fall in love with. I want that life. Princesses don't have to practice swordsmanship boringly every day or be tormented by you, teacher!" Alice complained resentfully.

"Do you think being a princess is easy? You must learn etiquette rigorously; even sneezing at a ball gets punished. Do you like this?" Claudia paused, speaking as someone experienced. "Court life isn't as beautiful as you imagine. Those inside spend their lives scheming, danger like living among wolves. Ordinary people are easier to satisfy, getting simple happiness—something courtiers never get."

"Teacher, why do you know this? Did you live in the court before?" Alice asked curiously.

"Something like that. Bad memories. I don't want you to envy court life—that's my old path." Claudia stroked Alice's head. Actually she didn't want Alice to follow Princess Josephine's path—unhappy and losing her life.

Alice thought and whispered, "I just want to be a princess. Sounds so noble, exciting~"

Claudia smiled softly. "Silly child, you've always been a noble princess."

"Really?" Alice widened her eyes.

"At least in my eyes, yes." Claudia hesitated, answering sincerely—

"Really, teacher won't lie."

The terrible blizzard stopped. Warm sunlight shone, but couldn't dispel the cold in her heart.

Alice stood by Claudia's grave for three days and nights, refusing water from Old Nick. Snow piled on her shoulders and head, knees submerged.

She stared blankly at the teacher's Autumn Water Sword, perhaps crying secretly—frost on her eyelashes and eye sockets.

Three days passed like a revolving lantern for Alice, recalling childhood memories—

Alice always knew Claudia cared, but refused to say it. Her terrible personality couldn't easily express love. Even after the teacher died, she couldn't say thanks.

To Alice, parents were cold, alien words. But teacher Claudia was beside her—bond transcending blood.

Her mother's image was always vague, now clear—Claudia's face.

Old Nick came with food and water. Blizzard stopped, he brought little Chris too, hoping Alice would eat for the child's sake.

Seeing Alice by the grave, Nick sighed, blaming himself for bringing people up the mountain. Guilt tormented him; he wanted to make amends.

Chris hadn't seen her mother for three days, dying to see her. Seeing Alice nearby, she ran over with her short legs.

She didn't care about cold snow in her boots, running to Alice, hugging her legs, eyes full of joy.

"Mommy~"

Alice looked down at her daughter; her hollow eyes gained color—the only warmth in three days.

She realized she was not just a mother but her daughter's sanctuary. Before Chris could protect herself, Alice must protect this cute one—no harm must come to her.

She couldn't show weakness; that would make Chris uneasy. She had to be a mother.

"I suppose when the teacher took care of me, it was the same, right?"

Alice understood Claudia's intentions. Strictness was the best wish—hoping she'd grow up fast.

Perhaps when the teacher wrote that last letter, she was in a good mood, not angry but relieved. Alice had found her right destination, could rely on herself, so the teacher could leave with peace of mind.

Alice picked up Chris, looking at her. If Chris left one day, she'd be disappointed, but more happy—Chris could find her own destination.

Chris saw frost on Alice's eyebrows, wiping it clean, feeling Mom's mood wasn't good. She didn't understand what happened.

"Mommy? What are you doing here?"

"Me?" Alice thought, forcing a smile. "Oh, I'm talking to your grandma."

"Grandma?" Chris looked at the grave. "Grandma is inside?"

Alice shook her head. "No, grandma went to another world."

"Will she come back? When?" Chris asked.

Alice hesitated. Chris was too young to understand the dead never return. "Maybe a long time. But... she might come in a dream."

"Will grandma be happy in the other world?" Chris asked confusedly.

"Of course. The other world is full of happiness. No more unruly students. She can finally rest." Alice fabricated lies.

Chris frowned. "Is that true?"

Alice's eyes turned red, suppressing sadness, using Claudia's words.

"Really, Mommy won't lie."

Old Nick saw them talking. Though he didn't know what, Alice looked much better.

Good omen. He secretly sighed in relief, carrying beef jerky and goat milk, whispering to Alice.

"Alice, eat something. You haven't eaten in three days. I'm sorry about your teacher, but it's happened. Don't let the dead affect your health."

"Thanks, Uncle Nick. I'm not hungry." Alice turned; calm eyes burning with anger—

"I hope you'll tell me truthfully—who killed my teacher?"

title: Chapter 9 — Seeking the Truth
content:
Chapter 9 — Seeking the Truth

Volume 33 · Chapter 9

Old Nick sighed, lowered his head, and lacked the courage to meet Alice's eyes as he spoke in a tone of self-reproach.

"Actually, I'm not entirely clear on the details either, but they said they were very familiar with your teacher, old friends.

"I thought everything they said was true and didn't think much of it, so I led them up the mountain to find your teacher, but I never expected...

"I am at fault. If I had refused to be their guide, perhaps your teacher wouldn't have come to this. I'm sorry."

Alice slowly closed her eyes. Though there was some resentment in her heart, she knew this was not Old Nick's fault. He was just a herdsman who understood nothing and had been deceived.

"Uncle Nick, I won't blame you. You were also a victim. That group took advantage of your warmth and kindness. Although you were the one who led them up the mountain, you had no ill intent."

"Ever since your teacher passed away, I've been filled with shame. She once helped our village survive many crises. Without her help, our village might have been buried under heavy snow years ago. And yet... I became an accomplice to that group." Old Nick kept his head lowered, not knowing how to explain in a way that would ease the guilt in his heart.

"It's alright. Perhaps this was my teacher's inescapable fate. But I must make the murderer pay the price. This is the only thing I can do as her student. Please tell me everything you know about the murderer." Alice emphasized solemnly.

"This..." Old Nick furrowed his brows, trying his best to recall details about that group, and said slowly, "I remember the man at the front was very powerful. He could frighten away a fierce snowman with just a glance. He gave off a very gloomy impression, with very dark circles under his eyes."

"Dark circles under his eyes?" Alice couldn't help but ponder. She felt she had seen someone similar somewhere before, but she just couldn't remember where.

"Oh right!" Old Nick suddenly raised his head, as if remembering something very important, and hurriedly said, "The innkeeper at the village inn mentioned they came from the Kingdom of Spain. They wanted to find your teacher to train young knights. The leader was named Alfonso, the king's royal tutor! That's right! I wouldn't forget. That night I was so excited I couldn't sleep, thinking I'd hosted a wealthy guest."

"Alfonso... Kingdom of Spain..." Alice couldn't help but furrow her brows. She thought of the royal tutor who had attended the Adventurer Competition as a guest. The image of the murderer in her mind grew clearer.

— Could he be the one who killed my teacher?

— Why would he do this?

— Could they have some hidden grudge?

Regardless, I must make this man pay with his blood for the blood he spilled!

Two days later, at the port of Rome, the rose family's banner flew once more, and Dennis's merchant ship set sail again.

The merchant fleet had finished repairs at the port of Rome. Their next destination — and the final stop of this journey — was the Kingdom of Spain, where the goods from Britannia would fetch a very good price.

"Men! Move it, or we won't make the delivery on time. If the Duke punishes us, don't say I didn't give you a friendly warning!"

Captain Dennis scolded harshly, ordering all the sailors to get to work quickly. Before sunset, the merchant ship had already left the port of Rome far behind.

Alice stood on the deck, watching the fiery red sunset gradually sink below the horizon. Little Chris in her arms was drowsy and couldn't help but doze off, her entire petite body curled up in her mother's embrace.

Captain Dennis quietly approached and asked softly, "Miss Alice, has something happened? Ever since you returned, your expression hasn't been good. If there's any difficulty that needs help, you can tell me."

"It's nothing. You're overthinking it. I just want to go to Spain."

Alice shook her head. She had no intention of telling anyone about her teacher's matter. Besides, her purpose for this trip was to kill Alfonso and avenge her teacher — it was best if no one else knew.

Alfonso's status was very special. He was the king's royal tutor, holding an exalted position in the Kingdom of Spain. Killing someone of such authority would likely cause considerable trouble.

But Alice had already made up her mind. Based on the clues she had obtained from Old Nick, the murderer of her teacher was this Spanish royal tutor.

Although Alice did not fear authority and would never hesitate, she was no longer alone now. She had her lovely daughter and had to consider the child's feelings.

So Alice decided to kill Alfonso in secret. If that failed, she would resort to more extreme measures. Although this approach would bring considerable trouble, with her identities as a Foreign Thorn Knight and a Purple Gold adventurer, she would surely receive dual protection from both the queen and the Adventurers Guild upon returning to the Kingdom of Britannia.

"Perhaps you have friends in Spain?" Captain Dennis asked curiously, feeling that Alice didn't seem to be on any kind of mission this time. She hadn't mentioned going to the Kingdom of Spain from the very beginning.

"No. I just want to take Chris around and see the sights. Anyway, after Merlin returned to his hometown, there's hardly anyone at home. I occasionally want to travel around a bit." Alice said with a smile, turning her assassination plan into what sounded like a pleasant trip.

"I see. Then you should have a good time. There's a very lively bullfighting festival there. Just be careful not to go near the slums or similar areas, or you might run into some trouble." Captain Dennis offered his kind advice.

"Why? Is there danger in the slums?" Alice asked curiously.

"No, no, no. You've misunderstood. For the people in the slums, Miss Alice would be the danger." Captain Dennis waved his hands repeatedly and continued, "As I've said before, Spain is a poor man's hell. The slums are where the lowest of the low gather. That place is full of sinister dealings. It might ruin the good mood of your journey."

"I see. I understand." Alice nodded.

"If you need anything in the Kingdom of Spain, please feel free to contact me. Although I've been away from that land for a long time, I still have some old friends who can help you resolve most troubles." Captain Dennis removed his hat and bowed slightly, feeling it was necessary to provide Alice and her daughter with as much convenience as possible while Merlin was absent.

"Thank you for your generosity." Alice replied politely, then turned and carried the sleeping little Chris in her arms, continuing to gaze at the distant sunset. The sea had already turned a deep crimson —

My teacher once mentioned living in a royal court. That most likely means the Kingdom of Spain.

The pendant around my neck also bears the Spanish royal family's crest.

If my teacher wasn't deliberately lying to me, this clearly belonged to my mother.

It seems things are not so simple. What exactly has my teacher been hiding from me?

I want to know the truth of everything.

title: Chapter 10 — Introduction (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 10 — Introduction (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 33 · Chapter 10

In a mysterious cave in the wilderness, the black dragon that remained only as a head was on its last breaths, its condition worse than even twenty-odd years ago. Every breath came with violent coughing.

Clearly, Nidhogg had been barely sustaining its life all along. Without a god-tier soul as a sacrifice, its life was nearly at its end, yet it still lived far longer than any human.

Nidhogg had already realized its remaining life was measured in only a few centuries more. If it did not receive a sacrifice soon, it would surely die. Its temper had begun to grow extremely irritable, frequently roaring in mindless fury.

Time for this great black dragon was running short. It could tolerate the incompetent Alfonso no longer — why hadn't a fresh sacrifice been delivered to it yet? It even began to suspect it had chosen the wrong servant.

Alfonso knelt on one knee without even lifting his head. Every so often he had to come here to report the recent situation. He could feel the black dragon's patience nearly worn out. If he failed to fulfill the agreement, he would face the cruelest punishment.

"Not long ago I found Ignis Clodia, but unfortunately she would not reveal Diana's whereabouts even at the cost of her life. I was unable to bring your sacrifice back. However, please rest assured. Give me a little more time, and I will surely not disappoint you."

"Not disappoint me? How many times have I heard this same answer?" Nidhogg's eyes flared with rage, its fanged maw opening wide as it roared, scorching black flames rising. "It's been twenty-odd years, Alfonso! How incompetent must you be to have taken twenty-odd years and still not have brought a sacrifice before me!? My patience is nearly exhausted!"

"I'm sorry. If not for Clodia blocking me, I would have long since brought the sacrifice to you. Please give me one more chance!" Alfonso frowned, not daring in the slightest to go against the black dragon's will.

"Opportunities are reserved for those who are prepared. A human who has deceived me for over twenty years — do you still deserve my trust?" Nidhogg's tone was filled with deep disappointment, growing ever less trusting of this somewhat cunning human.

"Give me three more years. If I cannot find Diana, I will offer my life in atonement!" Alfonso said through gritted teeth, setting his final deadline.

Seeing Alfonso still seemed sincere, Nidhogg's attitude softened slightly. With a weary voice it said, "My life is nearly at its end. The time left for you is also running short. No matter what means you use, you must bring that human named Diana before me. Do you understand?"

"I understand!" Alfonso clenched his fist unconsciously.

Nidhogg narrowed its eyes and said meaningfully, "Do not think that once I die, you will gain your freedom. You are my servant, your body carries my blood. Before I draw my last breath, one thought from me is all it takes to destroy your soul. Those who attempt to betray me will come to no good end."

Alfonso lowered his head, but his pupils contracted in terror. He had indeed harbored similar thoughts, but he did not realize that after receiving the black dragon's power, both his body and soul no longer belonged to him. If he could not find a sacrifice, the black dragon would drag him into hell before dying itself.

Nidhogg's words clearly sealed off all of Alfonso's escape routes, leaving him no way out. Over twenty-odd years without finding a sacrifice — the black dragon had to suspect whether Alfonso was deliberately dragging things out, hoping to wear it down to death.

"The reason I chose you as my servant is because even at a young age you possessed eyes full of desire. Everything you have today was given by me, and naturally I have the means to take it all away. I imagine you would not want to abandon wealth and luxury to roll back into the slums to live, would you? Then devote yourself entirely to serving me."

Alfonso said nothing, his fists clenching unconsciously with a crunching sound. Before the black dragon, he had no dignity at all.

"Look at those boots of yours — spotlessly clean. It makes me nostalgic. Once upon a time you were so poor you couldn't even afford boots, standing barefoot on the ground."

After several days at sea, the Puwei family's merchant ship arrived at its destination, reaching the port of the Spanish Kingdom.

Since it was already late, Alice and Chris disembarked early and found an inn near the port, planning to spend the entire night thinking about how to approach Alfonso.

Captain Dennis commanded the crew to unload the cargo, which would all be handed over to the local merchant guild the next day. Once the money was collected, they would return to Britannia.

"Be careful! The cargo inside is precious. If anything is damaged, the cost will be deducted from your commission!"

"Excuse me, are you Captain Dennis of the Welsh Rose family?"

Captain Dennis turned around in surprise at being called, seeing a middle-aged man dressed as a servant. "That's me. What is it?"

"My master is an old friend of yours. Please come to the carriage to catch up." The servant gestured toward a carriage parked not far away, its ornate decorations clearly marking it as something no ordinary person could own.

Captain Dennis hesitated, reasoning that if they claimed to be an old friend, they must be someone quite familiar. After all, he had lived in Spain for many years.

Following the servant to the carriage, the kingdom's Minister of Finance, Capless, had long been waiting inside and warmly greeted Dennis.

"Long time no see, my old friend."

"Capless? How strange — what are you doing here?" Captain Dennis asked in astonishment.

"I'm here to welcome you, my friend." Capless smiled.

"You, the Minister of Finance, hold such a high and powerful position — how could you possibly have the leisure to welcome me? We may be old friends, but I know you well enough, old fox. You would never be this enthusiastic." Captain Dennis removed his worn navy cap.

"Don't be so cold, Dennis. Back when we served together in the navy, we were brothers who trusted each other completely. No matter what I've become now, I'm still your good friend." Capless looked up, reminiscing.

"I dare not waste your time as finance minister. Even if we're friends, a letter now and then will suffice." Captain Dennis surveyed the luxurious carriage and sighed inwardly that his once-frugal brother had learned to enjoy life. "Speak. What do you need me for? I don't believe you would come all the way from the distant capital just to welcome me."

"As always, you understand me best. Then I won't beat around the bush." Capless paused and said in a serious tone, "Alphonso has completely taken control of the court. His Majesty Amadeo is too young and has no opinions of his own — major and minor matters alike are all handed over to Alphonso to handle. If this continues, this nation will be finished. I cannot stand idly by and watch the Spanish Kingdom sink into endless chaos. Dennis, you are my most trusted friend. I need your help."

"Are you mad? I no longer belong to this land. I am now a captain serving His Grace the Duke of Wales. I cannot provide you with any assistance — that would be a betrayal of His Grace." Dennis paused and said disappointedly, "I once loved this land too. But after Princess Josephine died, my heart went cold. This place is full of injustice toward good people."

"Don't misunderstand, Dennis. I'm not asking you to join me in adventure — I simply hope you can help me introduce someone to me." Capless said mysteriously.

"Who?"

"That adventurer you mentioned in your letter—" Capless leaned close to Dennis and spoke in a very low voice, "you said you saw someone who greatly resembled Princess Josephine, and that she wore a pendant bearing the royal court emblem. If I recall correctly, her name was Alice, right?"

title: Chapter 11 — Beautiful Diana, Your Majesty
content:
Chapter 11 — Beautiful Diana, Your Majesty

Volume 33 · Chapter 11

"You want Miss Alice's help?" Captain Dennis became somewhat nervous and asked, "What exactly are you planning to do?"

"I want King Amadeo to voluntarily abdicate the throne and hand the country over to someone who can truly bring prosperity to this land." Capriles was completely open about his intentions in front of Captain Dennis.

Captain Dennis stared at him in astonishment and said sternly, "You're absolutely crazy. No one will agree with what you're doing."

"Dennis, you've been away from this country for too long and have no idea how hard the people living here truly suffer. The upper classes exploit the lower classes endlessly. Simply staying alive is already a kind of luck. This is your homeland — are you really going to stand by and watch it fall apart?" Capriles's gaze was sharp; he had already made up his mind and would not listen to anyone's advice.

"But your approach is despicable!" Captain Dennis frowned deeply and said in a low voice, "You're coercing an underage king into abdicating. This isn't salvation — it's outright betrayal. You're no longer the old friend I knew, Capriles."

"I know my ideas are extremely radical, but I have no choice. I'm willing to bear a lifetime of infamy in exchange for the survival of millions. The days when even black bread is unaffordable will forever be a thing of the past." Capriles paused and continued, "His Majesty Amadeo has no will of his own. A king like him is merely a figurehead with no real value. He'll only ever be used by despicable scum like Alfonso. The king has become an accomplice in Alfonso's ruin of this land. Before the kingdom is destroyed, I still have a chance to change everything."

"You actually have such thoughts? Then you and Alfonso are no different — you're both traitors with ulterior motives." Captain Dennis stressed.

"No, we are absolutely not the same. I sincerely want to lead this land toward prosperity, while Alfonso certainly doesn't think that way." Capriles countered and then continued in an imploring tone, "I beg you, Dennis. In times like this, only you can help me."

Captain Dennis fell silent. He was indeed moved by Capriles's spirit of self-sacrifice. Just then, Alice happened to be staying at a nearby inn.

Captain Dennis worried that Capriles's plan might be dangerous and that something could happen to Alice. He couldn't face Merlin if that happened. However, he was only going to make an introduction. The final decision would rest with Alice herself.

Late at night in the inn, Alice helped tuck the sleeping little Chris under the blanket. The little one clung tightly to the pillow, sleeping soundly, as if nothing happening in the world could affect her. She couldn't sense any pressure at all.

Innocent Chris still thought the world was as peaceful as ever. Grandmother Cloadia had merely gone somewhere far away and probably wouldn't be back for some time. Maybe someday soon she would suddenly appear, bringing the novel toys she'd promised.

Perhaps Chris would indeed only meet Grandmother Cloadia in her dreams. That part of what Alice had said was true. The little one was too young to temporarily understand the bitterness in her mother's heart.

Alice came to the small table in the room and sat down. Dennis had already brought Capriles to the door, saying there was something very important to discuss.

"Mr. Capriles, is it? What important matter do you have for me? Although I am an adventurer, I'm not in the mood to take on any missions right now."

Captain Dennis glanced over at Capriles beside him and noticed that the old man was trembling, his eyes wide open. By the light of the oil lamp, he could see the unrestrained excitement in his eyes.

"Exactly! So much alike! At least five or six parts similar!" Capriles looked at Captain Dennis and said excitedly, "For a moment, I even thought Princess Consort Josephine had come back to life! I had thought you were exaggerating in your letter, but it turns out it matches reality almost perfectly!"

"That princess consort again..." Alice wore a helpless smile. How much did she resemble that inexplicable woman? Why did both Dennis and this mysterious old man get so excited upon seeing her?

"Capriles, be serious. Don't be rude in front of Miss Alice. I'm already doing the maximum I can by introducing you. If you don't respect Miss Alice, I'll press a musket against your forehead and tell you to get out!" Captain Dennis warned with a face full of annoyance.

"Ahem!" Capriles quickly gave a light cough and said with deep apology, "I'm very sorry. I was just a bit too excited. Miss Alice's appearance does seem somewhat familiar. Although she doesn't entirely resemble Princess Consort Josephine, some features are indeed very similar. I believe anyone who has ever seen the princess consort would be drawn to Miss Alice."

"Is that so?" Alice furrowed her brow slightly, thinking that on this journey she felt like she'd been pulled into some troublesome matter, constantly hearing the name of that deceased princess consort along the way.

"Miss Alice, please forgive my excitement. I harbor no ill will toward you." Capriles set aside his status and adopted a humble posture.

"It's fine. What do you need from me?" Alice was full of confusion. She had already heard from Dennis that the old man before her was the Minister of Finance of the Spanish Kingdom, which already counted him as a close attendant to the king.

"I want to ask you to save this country." Capriles's gaze was sincere and his tone resolute.

"???" Alice was completely bewildered. She had expected something simple, but instead got a huge bombshell. "Are you joking? Save the country? Are you sure you're清醒 right now? I'm an adventurer and won't get involved in mere factional struggles. My stance is neutrality. I'll avoid crossing boundaries whenever possible."

"Miss Alice, this country has already reached the edge of destruction. The evil State Preceptor Alfonso has bewitched the king and ruthlessly oppressed the common people. If we don't act swiftly, many lives will be lost in the ensuing riots. If you're willing to help me, you'll be saving the entire Spanish Kingdom and sparing countless people from this disaster." Capriles painted the situation in extremely dire terms, hoping to arouse the other party's attention.

At the mention of "Alfonso," Alice's eyes shifted instantly. He was precisely the enemy she was looking for.

From Capriles's description, Alice barely grasped the current situation. The seemingly peaceful Spanish Kingdom already harbored extremely serious hidden dangers, and the mastermind behind everything was that State Preceptor Alfonso!

It seemed there were quite a few of Alfonso's enemies within the kingdom. Perhaps she didn't need to act through covert assassination. She could ally with Alfonso's enemies instead. This would avenge her teacher and rescue the suffering commoners of Spain — two objectives achieved with a single move.

Alice thought over this in her heart and felt that Capriles's visit was bringing her an opportunity — a chance to quickly infiltrate the Spanish royal court.

"What do you want me to do to help?"

"You need to pretend to be the little Spanish princess who was kidnapped over twenty years ago. I will rally a coalition of ministers opposed to Alfonso, using the argument that the current king is illegitimate to dethrone him." Capriles paused and stated it concisely.

"Then, we will declare you as the legitimate first-order heir and顺势 push you to the pinnacle of power."

"You, His Majesty, the Beautiful Diana..."

"The future new Queen of the entire Spanish Kingdom!"

title: Chapter 12 — Approach
content:
Chapter 12 — Approach

Volume 33 · Chapter 12

"What are you saying?"

Alice was shocked by Caples's words. She had never considered the possibility of becoming queen; hearing such a thing seemed utterly unbelievable.

Captain Dennis was equally astounded. In his eyes, his old friend had become a madman—daring to even think such thoughts? Wanting Alice to impersonate the missing Princess Diana and depose the current king, Amedeo? Although Caples's original intention was for the prosperity of the kingdom, this clearly crossed the底线 of a subject's loyalty. Without question, it was an act of treason against the king.

"Caples, have you lost your mind? Asking Miss Alice to become queen?"

"Don't be so nervous, Dennis. I simply want Miss Alice to impersonate Princess Diana and remove that incompetent king, Amedeo, from the throne. It's not as if I'm handing this land over to Miss Alice to manage. Perhaps she would only need to serve as a nominal queen afterward," Caples explained meaningfully.

"If Amedeo abdicates, are you certain Alfonso will stop bringing ruin upon this land? Who dares guarantee there won't be a second Amedeo?" Dennis questioned strongly.

"Anyone with their own convictions would be better than Amedeo. Alfonso hasn't yet reached a position where he can cover the court with one hand. Spain needs a true ruler, not a puppet manipulated by others," Caples countered seriously.

"If your meaning is not for Miss Alice to truly become queen, then who will manage this country?" Dennis asked, puzzled. According to Caples's plan, Alice only needed to help him depose Amedeo and nothing else.

"Does that even need to be asked? I will fully inherit the late king's will and lead Spain into an era of prosperity," Caples responded firmly.

"You..." Captain Dennis was completely at a loss for words. He had originally thought Caples genuinely wanted to do something good, but instead he intended to overthrow the late king's appointed heir and become the true ruler of this land himself. No matter how ornate the words used to disguise it, this was clearly "treason," something no one could tolerate!

"As long as I obtain sufficient power, I will carry out a reform from top to bottom across the kingdom, completely changing the lawless situation of the nobles. By then, everyone will have enough to eat. The rich man's paradise and the poor man's hell will become things of the past," Caples said excitedly, already imagining a brand new Spain in his mind.

"What you're doing is no different from Alfonso's behavior. I don't recommend you do something so reckless," Captain Dennis said, somewhat regretting that he had offered to make the introduction.

"I know I currently look like a villain with ulterior motives, but my future achievements will be no less than those of Spain's founding emperor. Many people will thank me for changing Spain," Caples said, staring into Dennis's eyes. Having already made up his mind, how could he possibly listen to others' advice?

"Miss Alice, don't agree to this. This matter is too dangerous. I don't recommend you get involved. I deeply regret introducing such a madman to you," Captain Dennis gritted his teeth.

Alice: "No, I am willing to agree to this."

"???" Captain Dennis's eyes widened in shock. He asked in astonishment, "Sister Alice, are you serious?"

"Yes, I am willing to assist this old gentleman. Impersonating a princess is something I have little experience with, but I can give it a try."

Alice had not rejected Caples's crazy proposal. Instead, she was willing to use this method to get close to Alfonso in order to help her teacher seek revenge.

Although Caples's proposal was quite reckless, Alice felt it wouldn't be a bad thing for most people. Perhaps only the nobility would suffer losses.

"Miss Alice, if your false identity is exposed, it could be extremely dangerous. Have you considered that?" Captain Dennis asked anxiously, hoping Alice wouldn't take such a risk. If something went wrong, he might end up taking the blame.

"Don't worry, Dennis. With Miss Alice's appearance, who would doubt? As long as Miss Alice firmly claims she is Diana, no one will be able to spot anything suspicious. Even if she is discovered, I will guarantee with my own life that Miss Alice will escape unharmed," Caples gave his assurance. Having long known that nobody would dare impersonate a royal heir, he had naturally prepared an escape route for Alice in advance. If it succeeded, everyone would be happy. If it failed, he would bear full responsibility.

"You'll definitely be torn apart by five horses," Captain Dennis frowned.

"I have come to terms with that," Caples responded calmly.

Alice lowered her head and carefully thought through the situation, a few thoughts gradually forming in her mind:

Alfonso was able to defeat my teacher, so his strength must be considerable. Perhaps I am not his match.

But as it stands now, Alfonso has many enemies. Perhaps I can try to borrow their power.

Should I impersonate a princess then? Speaking of which, what are princesses in stories usually like?

With my personality, I'd never pass as a noble. I'd probably slip up pretty easily, wouldn't I?

The next morning, Alice briefly bid farewell to Captain Dennis and, accompanied by her daughter, boarded Caples's carriage and headed toward Spain's capital.

Little Chris sat on her mother's lap, curiously looking around. Ever since following Alice away from Rexham, every day had been full of new experiences and encountering different people.

"Be good and don't touch things randomly," Alice instructed, looking down at the little one.

Little Chris reluctantly pulled her hand back and asked curiously, "Mommy, where are we going?"

"To Spain's capital city," Alice patiently explained.

"What are we going there for?" Chris's ahoge wobbled.

Alice hesitated for a moment. She couldn't exactly say they were going to stage a coup, so she gave a tactful answer, "Mommy is going to play the role of a princess."

"A princess???" Little Chris's eyes lit up, her excited baby teeth showing. "Mommy is going to be a princess? Then does that make Chris a little princess too? Does that mean I don't have to train anymore and can just sleep all day and eat endless little cakes?"

Alice facepalmed inwardly. Her precious daughter looked just like her father in her pursuit of comfort. "What kind of sweet dream are you having? No matter what happens, you should always work hard at your training. Mommy isn't a princess, and you're not a little princess either."

"Hmph!" Little Chris puffed out her cheeks and retorted indignantly, "That's not true! Aunt Lilith said I'm a little princess of the Lucifer family! Among the demon race, there are so many——!"

Alice swiftly covered Chris's small mouth, completely defeated by the little one. A cold sweat broke out on the back of her neck.

Seeing that Caples across from them merely smiled kindly and had noticed nothing, Alice finally breathed a sigh of relief:

Really fed up with this. At the slightest carelessness, the kid starts spouting nonsense.

Does she want everyone to know she's the Demon Lord's daughter?

If someone with intentions heard this, it would bring trouble!

title: Chapter 13 — The Princess Returns
content:
Chapter 13 — The Princess Returns

Volume 33 · Chapter 13

Chris had her mouth covered and couldn't speak, realizing she seemed to have said the wrong thing again, so like a deflated balloon she fell silent and sullen. "Miss Alice's child looks quite lively; it reminds me of my own granddaughter, both just as cheerful." Caprice said with a smile. "This child always likes to blab nonsense and never listens at all." Alice glared at Chris, noting that they weren't at home and careless talk could cause trouble; fortunately Caprice wasn't a devout follower, otherwise hearing the words "demon race" would make him overly sensitive. "Children are like that; just be patient with them." Caprice barely paid attention to Chris's remarks, adding, "But your child might actually become a little princess, hahaha." "Huh?" Alice looked bewildered, not quite understanding what Caprice meant. "If the plan goes smoothly, you could become the nominal queen of Spain, and your child would naturally become a little princess." Caprice found the title amusing. "I don't want to be a queen, nor enter any noble circles; I hope you understand—I only agreed to pretend to be a princess. As for becoming a nominal queen, I will not agree." Alice said sternly. Caprice hesitated, seeing that Alice had no desire to live at court, and grew somewhat troubled. If Amadeo abdicates smoothly without taking up a new ruler, it would cause complications, but he isn't worried; even if Alice doesn't intend to become the new queen, he could nominate other royal relatives he favors. Caprice felt that Alice risking so much to pose as a princess was already the greatest help she could give him. "Very well, I will do my utmost to ensure this doesn't disrupt your life. Speaking of which, as an adventurer, how much should I pay you this time? To be honest, I'm not like those greedy nobles—I don't possess astonishing wealth, but as long as your price is reasonable, I can accept it." "I don't need any payment." Alice replied calmly. "You don't want payment?" Caprice thought he'd misheard; it was his first time meeting an adventurer who asked for no reward—must be a purple‑gold powerhouse? Indeed, completely different from ordinary adventurers, seemingly no longer obsessed with wealth. "Then what do you want? Surely you won't help me for free?" "You might as well tell me about Alfonso; I'm interested in him." Alice wanted to learn about her enemy in advance. "Alfonso..." Caprice, though doubtful, slowly said, "Alfonso is a wicked, cunning man who came from the slums, possessing exceptionally powerful astrology. Thanks to this talent he gained the royal family's favor and gradually rose to his current position. Over two years ago the kingdom suffered frequent disasters; I suspected these were his doing, though I had no evidence." Alice couldn't help but frown, not really believing such precognition could convince the royal family. Could Alfonso's astrology be that accurate? This makes one suspect everything is a self-directed drama. "If you ever encounter Alfonso, never believe a word he says. This selfish, self‑serving scoundrel would likely harm you for his own gain; please be careful." Caprice warned seriously, adding, "I originally planned to send people to protect your safety, but you're a purple‑gold adventurer—my people would only get in your way." "I understand." Alice nodded, thinking that before she makes a move, the state preceptor Alfonso might strike first, so she must stay alert. "Miss Alice, please lower the carriage curtains; we're about to pass through the slums." Caprice kindly reminded. "Why lower the curtains?" Alice asked in surprise. "Some things you see will affect your mood; after all, people living in the slums behave in ways that make others uncomfortable." Caprice said tactfully. "No need; let me take a look." Alice refused Caprice's suggestion. From the moment they entered the slum district, the scene before her eyes suddenly shifted—clean streets vanished, replaced by barren land and a foul river filled with trash. Houses became extremely scarce, mostly chaotic shanties like tents; people in ragged clothes idled about, some not even possessing a proper pair of shoes. Beggars were everywhere, along with gangs of idle youths ruthlessly snatching others' belongings; some even saw Alice sitting in the luxurious carriage, mistaking her for a noblewoman, and whistled like hooligans. Alice had seen slums before, but a place as chaotic as this one in Spain was truly the first time; it looked like a lawless wasteland with no rules whatsoever. She had once heard from her instructor Claudia that she herself had lived in the slums as a child; perhaps it was just such a place. Claudia managed to become a loyal, dutiful knight and teacher in such awful conditions, showing how difficult it had been. "Excuse the sight, Miss Alice; such places are common throughout the kingdom. The nobles never pay attention to these folks, only wanting them to fend for themselves." Caprice lowered his head, sighing helplessly, "Once there was a beautiful queen who wanted to help these people, but because she touched the nobles' interests she brought death upon herself. What I now wish to do is the same as that queen; perhaps I too will die, but I won't fear it, so I hope you will fully assist me. You're not just helping me—you're helping countless suffering lower‑class people in Spain." Alice gave no reply, but judging by her nature she would inevitably find herself at the center of this upheaval's vortex. A few days later in the palace's rear garden, Amadeo kept two ferocious lions in a cage as toys for his boredom. He would only toss a piece of meat into the cage; the two hungry lions would then fight over the food, their heads bloody. The fiercer the lions fought, the happier Amadeo laughed; sometimes he even threw death‑row inmates into the cage—this was his favorite bloody spectacle. Amadeo admired the lions' tearing and fighting, feeling it resembled the struggle between Caprice and Alfonso, yet he never considered that without the cage's restraint he himself would become the lions' prey. The royal guard knight Vivar walked up silently behind Amadeo, saying nothing, already having received some secret news. "How did things go?" Amadeo asked quietly. "Cecilia has replied, saying she has already left the royal guard and does not wish to be dragged into any court intrigue, so she refused our invitation." Vivar said with regret. "Damn!" Amadeo's mood turned terrible, gritting his teeth, "These high‑and‑mighty adventurers will eventually pay the price: they actually refused me? Is my reward not enough?" "Your Majesty, purple‑gold adventurers can no longer be moved by money; as long as they nod, countless people want to hire them." Vivar explained. "Without reinforcements, how can we kill Alfonso? What if his injury heals after a while?" Amadeo fumed, unable to endure any longer. "I and the other knights are willing to fight to the death for Your Majesty." Vivar declared firmly. "Enough." Amadeo impatiently waved his hand, "I'll think of another way later; you keep contacting others to see if anyone is willing to help us." "Yes." Vivar bowed slightly, then shifted tone, "There is one more important matter." "What?" Amadeo, absent‑minded, thought there was nothing left, nothing worse than Cecilia refusing to help. "The finance minister Caprice recently..." Vivar paused, then reported carefully, "He says he has already found your sister." "The princess Diana, missing for over twenty years." Give monthly tickets, and there will be bonus updates!

title: Chapter 14 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter
content:
Chapter 14 — Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter

Volume 33 · Chapter 14

Amadeo’s expression froze on his face as he twisted his head around. “What are you saying?”

“Capuleus has found your sister—Princess Diana, who has been missing for over twenty years.” Vival repeated the news, already guessing Amadeo’s reaction. After all, the late king had designated young Princess Diana as the heir to the throne, and her reappearance posed an enormous threat to Amadeo.

“Is this news accurate? Where did you hear it?” Amadeo demanded.

“It’s accurate. Capuleus himself told me. Princess Diana is currently staying at the residence of the Minister of Finance,” Vival reported honestly, adding, “Recently, Capuleus invited a group of the late king’s former ministers to his home. I suspect he’s plotting something against you.”

Amadeo took a deep breath. Though only ten years old, he remained eerily composed, showing no sign of panic.

Even without Vival saying it outright, Amadeo knew exactly what Capuleus intended. If Diana had been found, the question of succession would inevitably arise.

The reason he had invited so many old ministers was likely to prepare for what was coming next. Given Capuleus’s upright nature, he had probably long since grown intolerant of Amadeo’s incompetence.

Amadeo’s lips curled into a faint smile as he noticed the two lions in their cage, both staring at him hungrily.

“This is the so-called ‘extremes meet’? Sometimes, the most loyal people are even more dangerous than the deceitful ones.”

Vival realized Amadeo had understood everything—how to navigate this crisis would depend on whether Amadeo could find balance in this precarious situation, even if both sides were enemies who could exploit each other.

“Vival, do you think the Diana Capuleus found is the real one?” Amadeo asked casually.

“I’m not sure, but I doubt it. Diana was taken by the royal knight-saint of old. Unless it’s someone from her own side, no one has any credibility. I can’t confirm whether Capuleus just found some woman who looks similar and is passing her off as the long-lost Princess Diana—twenty years missing—to discredit you and strike at Alfonso. He has the motive,” Vival said bluntly.

“Exactly. Impersonating royal heirs is a serious crime, and I don’t want Capuleus to go too far. Without his restraint, Alfonso would truly rule everything in the shadows,” Amadeo said, standing up and stretching lazily. “Things are getting more interesting by the minute. If anything, this isn’t just my crisis—it’s a golden opportunity for us to fish in troubled waters.”

“I’ve lasted this long under Alfonso’s shadow, and I’m not the kind who can be easily replaced.”

“Have the lions in the cage killed. I’ve grown tired of them.”

After days of preparation, Capuleus had united all the late king’s loyalists. These men were either devoted to the former monarch or disapproved of Alfonso. They shared a single goal: to depose the indecisive Amadeo and crush Alfonso’s influence in the court.

Capuleus believed everything was perfectly arranged—all that remained was to declare Amadeo’s succession illegitimate. The royal court’s routine meeting resumed once more.

Alfonso, seated beside Amadeo, clearly knew something was amiss. His gaze lingered meaningfully on Capuleus below.

The respected old Minister of Finance stepped forward, standing beneath the throne, and spoke loudly.

“Your Majesty, how do you assess your own abilities? Do you believe you can govern Spain and lead the kingdom to prosperity?”

“Capuleus, why are you asking this?” Amadeo feigned ignorance, spreading his hands wide. “Of course I’m outstanding. Under my rule, isn’t the kingdom already peaceful enough?”

“No, in fact, since you ascended the throne, the country has only grown worse—riots and famines are frequent. Shouldn’t you reflect on yourself?” Capuleus said sternly.

“Why should I reflect? What does this have to do with me?” Amadeo shrugged. “There’s no one else as capable as me.”

Capuleus’s face darkened with fury. It was because of your shortsightedness that the kingdom has fallen into such despair. You don’t deserve to rule this land.

“Capuleus, do you know what you’re saying? Dare you question me!” Amadeo scowled, rising from his throne in anger.

“You’re not the legitimate heir! You should step down and let the rightful successor take the throne,” Capuleus declared confidently. At least half of the assembled ministers supported him.

“Nonsense! If I’m not legitimate, then who is? You?” Amadeo pointed furiously at Capuleus, shouting like a flustered child. “Guards! Kill this old man! He dares slander me!”

“Your Majesty, please calm yourself. This is not a place for arguing,” Alfonso said smoothly, countering, “Capuleus, if you claim the king is not the legitimate heir, then who do you say *is* the rightful successor?”

“Of course, it’s Spain’s first princess—Princess Diana. She was the designated heir to the throne,” Capuleus announced loudly.

“What a pity. Princess Diana was betrayed and taken by the royal knight-saint twenty years ago, and there’s been no trace of her since. She’s likely already dead,” Alfonso shook his head.

“No, in fact, I *have* found the long-lost Princess Diana. She’s been alive all this time.”

Capuleus revealed his long-planned scheme, stunning the unaware nobles in the court. Many believed it impossible—how could someone who had searched for years finally find her now?

The nobles below murmured among themselves, some convinced Capuleus was mad, while those in the know remained confident.

*Dadada—*

Footsteps echoed from outside the hall. Alice stepped forward, surveying the crowd before her gaze settled on her enemy in power.

Alfonso.

You’ll pay for this.

title: Chapter 15 — Unmasking the Fake
content:
Chapter 15 — Unmasking the Fake

Volume 33 · Chapter 15

Alice's eyes were filled with anger as she finally saw the enemy who had killed her teacher Claudia, but now she could not act rashly; she still lacked confidence to defeat Alfonso, so she temporarily needed to actively cooperate with Caples to fulfill their agreed-upon matter.
Since Alice has already seen Alfonso, she will not worry about him escaping; she will surely find a way to make Alfonso pay blood for blood!
When Alice appeared before everyone's eyes, the ministers of authority couldn't help but exclaim in astonishment; the first glance was indeed stunning enough, reminding many of the deceased witch queen.
Although Caples had not yet given a detailed introduction, upon seeing Alice herself, some nobles already believed seven or eight tenths; perhaps this is the long-lost princess—.
"Heavens! Her gaze truly resembles Queen Josephine!"
"Caples isn't crazy; he actually found Princess Diana! Unbelievable!"
"If Princess Diana is still alive, calculating her age, she's roughly about this size."
The solemn court seemed to explode, becoming somewhat chaotic; Diana's sudden appearance left people unable to accept this reality quickly.
The knight Vival guarding the king noticed Alice's gold-plated adventurer proof, and couldn't help but suspect: Is Princess Diana a gold-tier adventurer? That's obviously impossible! Even if the court sword saint personally instructed her, she couldn't become a gold-tier adventurer at such a young age; she must be impersonating the princess!.
Alfonso appeared calm on the surface, but deep in his eyes he revealed undisguised ecstasy, always waiting for this moment; he fully understood Caples's plot—.
"Hooked!"
"Stupid Caples, do you think I wouldn't know what you're thinking?"
"My spy network spans all of Spain; your every move cannot escape my eyes!"
"You want to find someone to impersonate Diana, using the chance to pull my puppet down from the throne? That's a dream!"
"Look who you've found? An adventurer living in Britain; you probably didn't expect I once saw her in the Adventurers' Tournament?"
"I was also attracted by her appearance, but she couldn't be Diana; although she shares the surname with Ignis, it's too common—you could find over twenty people named Claudia in any slum!"
"Given Ignis's conservative nature, he would never allow Diana to leave his side to become a conspicuous adventurer; instead he would arrange for her to live in seclusion, only then could he evade my pursuit."
"Caples, you old fox, to confuse me you've really gone to trouble, even making this fake wear a similar pendant? That's a 'gift' I personally gave her."
"If I hadn't known everything beforehand, I might really have been fooled by you; achieving this level deserves praise~"
"But now everything is over; it's time to put an end to our two-person struggle. I've long prepared for your scheme; watch me expose all these conspiracies, using the charge of 'rebellion' to eradicate you and your faction in the court."
Alfonso took a deep breath, feeling his whole spirit refreshed; he never imagined removing his own thorn would be so easy.
"You really are Diana? My sister?" the young king Amadeo asked doubtfully.
Alice lifted her gaze toward this ten-year-old child, hard to imagine he is a kingdom's ruler; "Exactly, I am Diana."
"Impossible! You should be dead! Impossible you're still alive!" Amadeo excitedly sat down on the ground.
Alice slightly furrowed her brows, thinking that Princess Diana truly had bad luck; even her brother wishes she were dead—perhaps this is why the teacher disliked court life? Familial affection has already completely changed.
"Teacher!" Amadeo put on a helpless look, at this moment always pleading to Alfonso, "Please help me! I have no sister! Diana is dead; she must be fake!"
"Your Majesty, please rest assured; I will reveal the truth, not allowing anyone to threaten your safety. If this Princess Diana is fake, then certain people harbor ill intentions and should be executed." Alfonso said calmly, his gaze intentionally or unintentionally toward Caples.
"Lord Alfonso, your suspicion is normal, but this person is indeed the lost princess; there is no doubt about that." Caples paused, then spoke sharply, "According to the late king's original intention, the heir of this land is the princess, not the underage Amadeo."
Upon hearing this, many ministers supporting Caples stood up in agreement, believing he was right; the kingdom should rightfully be handed to the designated legitimate heir, not a clueless little brat.
"After Princess Diana was abducted by the court sword saint, she suffered no abuse; on the contrary, she received meticulous care. For these twenty-plus years she has lived as an ordinary person, yet through her own efforts she became the youngest gold-tier adventurer in history, proving she possesses extraordinary ability. If Princess Diana could inherit the throne, the deceased former king would surely feel relieved as well." Caples spoke slowly; these words are all his own fabrication, only one step away from plan success. "Since His Majesty Amadeo lacks governing ability, why not abdicate the throne and hand it to the already adult Princess Diana, letting her become Spain's first queen in history, leading us to prosperity."
"Lord Caples, whether this woman before us is truly the lost Princess Diana cannot be decided solely by your personal approval; at present you have not produced any convincing evidence, how can we believe your words?" Alfonso's expression was half-smile, Caples's remarks were entirely within his expectations.
"What more evidence is needed? Surely you can also notice that Princess Diana bears some resemblance to the late Queen Josephine, and she also wears a pendant engraved with the royal micro-mark; these are already sufficient to prove her identity, why do you refuse to accept the facts?" Caples asked confidently, convinced Alfonso could find no flaw.
"Lord Caples, are you treating me like a child to play with? Appearance-wise, the world has too many people; not having a look-alike would be strange. As for the pendant bearing the royal crest, I could easily forge such a thing; moreover, palace servants occasionally smuggle out royal goods to sell outside, which is common. Your reasons cannot convince me." Caples smiled.
"Lord Alfonso, are you perhaps being a bit overly argumentative?" Caples's face darkened.
"Well, since you insist she is Princess Diana, Alfonso slowly rose, speaking mysteriously

title: Chapter 16 — Orc Tribe Witchcraft
content:
Chapter 16 — Orc Tribe Witchcraft

Volume 33 · Chapter 16

Kaplais faced overwhelming pressure; if he acted too hastily, he would likely reveal a flaw, so he feigned composure and asked, "How does Lord Alfonso intend to proceed with the identification? Surely you won't rely on your supposedly miraculous astrology, will you?"

"My astrology cannot determine parentage, but there is another method—one that is very accurate." Alfonso said meaningfully.

"What method?" Kaplais grew somewhat nervous, worried that Alfonso might prove Diana was an impostor.

"The beastman race possesses a peculiar form of shamanic art. Using the bones of one's forefathers, one can prove one's offspring."
