Alice's gaze was firm. She tightly gripped Alfonso's wrist and frantically sent the fused power of magic and battle aura into the enemy's body.

"You killed my beloved teacher! This hatred cannot be dispelled even if I kill you! You scum, who constantly bring misfortune to innocent people! You should disappear from this world!"

"Hah!?"

Alfonso felt unprecedented panic. He could sense that something bone-chilling was being poured into his body. The cold poison seemed to have been stimulated and instantly became restless!

He realized that his state had reached a dangerously extreme point. His body was almost completely eroded and wasted by the cold poison, and his consciousness was gradually becoming blurred and sluggish.

Using the cold poison to kill Alfonso was indeed the most direct and effective method; it was the final straw that broke the camel's back.

"I don't want to die! ! !"

Alfonso let out a hysterical roar. Like everyone else who had reached the end of the road, his eyes were filled with fear and helplessness.

Hot black flames exploded like a bomb, centered on Alfonso, and the strong impact ruthlessly pushed Alice back dozens of steps!

"Huh! Why can such a fierce power still be used!?" Alice barely stabilized her form, her eyes fixed on the man bathing in black flames. Logically, someone who had been eroded by cold poison to this extent should have long since died; it was impossible for him to have any movement! What was so terrifying about this obsession!?

Alfonso's expression froze. His whole body was stiff, standing on the spot, with a layer of frost covering his body. No matter how hot the black flames were, they could not rescue him from the cold.

His body had been completely frozen by the cold poison, gradually becoming a living ice sculpture. Even making a sound was very difficult—

"Not wanting to die, I've only just made it to where I am today. I don't want to lose all of this. I want to continue living, enjoy the power of controlling the fate of others.

I am truly a rat from the sewer, but I am not the same as other dirty companions. My dream. is to live in the sunlight."

"Josef's son, is our retribution?"

Alice unconsciously furrowed her brows, thinking this was Alfonso's confession before death?

In a scene of ruins, the black flames were slowly extinguishing, and Alfonso, covered in frost, stood in the center. He had lost all combat ability. Despair and helplessness like a child, could only quietly wait for death to come.

"You have never had the experience of not being able to afford boots, of having your feet cut by stones every day?"

"You have never felt the pain of being beaten by your father every night, of having no food for three days, of having to steal things and eat rat meat to survive?"

"Do you have the experience of waking up every day, feeling genuinely happy, and being grateful to be alive, even though it is a painful life, but cherishing the opportunity to open your eyes again?"

"You haven't had any of that. You were born immersed in the indulgence of wealth and food, and you will never suffer any hardship. Your parents love you more than they love themselves; not even your teacher Ignius would risk his life to protect you. Why are you so lucky?"

"Shut up! No matter what you say, it cannot wash away the sins you have committed! I will absolutely not sympathize with a guy like you!"

Alice angrily pointed her sword at Alfonso and said sternly, "My teacher and you are the same; both came from the slums. But she gained the respect of everyone through her own efforts! And you are just a bastard who uses other people's kindness! Fate is fair! Don't find excuses for your despicableness!"

"Hahaha, fate will never have absolute fairness. Some people own everything just after birth, while no matter how hard others try, they will be abandoned by the times. The suffering your teacher endured, she just wouldn't tell you. One day, you will also understand."

Alfonso's gaze gradually became scattered. His life had already come to an end. "Good people become prey, just like your mother. The killer of hers is not me, it is the unfair fate. I sincerely respect her; she gave me the courage to live in the sunlight. Rather than waiting for her to be brutally killed by others, it is better for me to personally give her a death without pain."

"Hah!" Alice listened to Alfonso's words, and her heart was filled with anger. Just how pathological does a person have to be to say such things?

"You have some things in common with your deceased mother, such as thinking things too simply. Do you really think you won?"

Alfonso looked at Alice, his tone full of deep meaning.

"Huh!?" Alice immediately became wary, tightly gripping the fine sword in her hand, suspecting that Alfonso still had some bottom card.

Alfonso, whose cold poison had already completely eroded him, had almost become a dead, silent ice sculpture. A blood color was dyed in his deep eyes. He used all the last strength of his body and twitched his right hand's index finger, launching a final counterattack before death!

Suddenly, a wave of heat came. An invisible black flame thread, at some unknown time, had successfully connected to Alice's chest, wrapping only around her heart!

"What is this!?" Alice only felt a coldness surge down her spine. Her heart sent out waves of burning pain. Her life was now controlled by the enemy!

"The true winner is me." Alfonso's ferocious gaze fixed on Alice firmly, his tone like a hellish reaper.

"Diana, please good experience the pain your teacher experienced before death."

title: Chapter 28 — The Gloom Dissipates
content:
Chapter 28 — The Gloom Dissipates

Volume 33 · Chapter 28

The ground trembled and a massive explosion erupted—within moments, half the palace collapsed, giant silhouettes shifting through the dust, while scorching black flames soared into the sky.

The commotion had triggered panic across the entire capital city. Most people were unaware of what had actually transpired within the palace; it appeared as though they had been struck by an enemy attack, leaving everyone uneasy.

Except for a handful of the most powerful individuals, the rest remained oblivious to the sweeping changes quietly taking place.

Vivian gripped his cherished sword, standing alone at the critical path leading to the royal chambers, seemingly blocking passage to prevent anyone from interfering with the battle raging behind him.

Though Vivian knew that Alice and Asmodeus's fight would create a massive disturbance, the current situation far exceeded his expectations—this had already reached a point where it was common knowledge.

Upon learning of what had occurred here, Asmodeus's trained eagles would certainly not stand by; they would rush to support their master.

Vivian's duty was to halt this group, ensuring Asmodeus remained isolated and unable to interfere with Alice's revenge.

Click-clack, the sound of hurried footsteps echoed from the far end of the corridor—clearly, many people were rapidly approaching!

Vivian lifted his head, calmly opening his eyes to see a horde of black-robed assassins charging forward in urgent haste.

These assassins, bred by Asmodeus, each possessed unique skills and were utterly loyal to him. Within the court's hierarchy, they were notorious as a privileged faction, executing Asmodeus's orders without hesitation, using any means necessary—even daring to roam freely within the palace itself.

Upon seeing Vivian standing at the center of the corridor, blocking their path, the assassins had no choice but to halt and confront this knight—

"You have the King's decree: no one is permitted to pass through here, or face charges of treason," Vivian spoke calmly, his voice carrying authority without anger. "Go back, you Asmodeus's eagles. If you lay down your weapons now, the merciful King might spare your lives—though that would be the wiser choice."

A senior assassin stepped forward from the crowd, approaching Vivian. "Did you set some kind of trap to sabotage Asmodeus? The disturbance in the palace is far from normal!"

"I have no reason to explain myself, only that your days of misfortune are over. If you choose to embrace the light, you might still survive," Vivian replied unflinchingly, his expression devoid of emotion.

"You're what, exactly?" the assassin snapped, irritation evident. "Do you think yourself some noble knight? You're merely a puppet of the powerless king."

A flash of anger crossed Vivian's eyes—when had he, a member of a proud knightly lineage, become the target of such degradation? These heartless scum, devoid of any faith, wielded Asmodeus's protection as a shield and weapon—how dare they stand before him with such arrogance!

"We serve Asmodeus, you fool knight. You'd better be careful," the assassin sneered, leaning closer. "You know Asmodeus is the most powerful in this kingdom. If you don't behave, when I face Asmodeus, you'll be dead~"

"I think you're mistaken. The most noble person in this kingdom is Emperor Adonai, not Asmodeus," Vivian said with deliberate emphasis.

"Adonai that hairless brat is nothing! Everyone, even three-year-olds know Asmodeus is the true ruler of this kingdom!"

The assassin paused, then mockingly added, "Do you think waving around a puppet will scare me?"

"I advise you to retract those words and stop speaking recklessly about the King of Spain!" Vivian's gaze turned icy, a killing intent surging through his body.

"How do I care if I speak recklessly?!" the assassin scoffed, showing no regard for Vivian, extending his hand to push him aside. "Get out of my way! If Asmodeus is in trouble, you won't even have ten heads to count!"

Clang!

Vivian drew his sword in an instant, a wave of Saint-tier aura erupted, and his blade cleaved the assassin's head from his shoulders without hesitation.

"You dare challenge me!? Do you not wish to live?!"

The other assassins were stunned beyond belief—they hadn't expected a servant to the incompetent king to have such courage, daring to openly defy Asmodeus. Several of them quickly drew their weapons and launched a counterattack, surrounding Vivian, determined to teach this reckless knight the consequences of offending Asmodeus.

Vivian remained remarkably calm. Among these assassins, few posed a real threat to him. A scattered few of Asmodeus's key subordinates were likely already entangled with his trusted palace guards, meaning they weren't formidable opponents.

Adonai's meticulously planned scheme had anticipated nearly every contingency; there would be no mistakes here. Asmodeus's eagles were, in fact, in dire straits.

Vivian's blade quickly crystallized into a layer of ice, bearing the style of the Snow Mountain sword techniques. Though he didn't wish for Alice to fully inherit Curodia's staff, he had received some instruction from her.

The cold knight surged into the fray, cutting down seven of the strongest assassins in quick succession, moving like a nimble snow leopard, each strike a killing blow.

The remaining assassins were utterly demoralized—Vivian's resolve was unshakable. They'd grown arrogant for too long, rarely encountering someone as steadfast as him.

Vivian straightened his back, flicked the blood from his sword, and coldly declared, "No one is permitted to pass through here! All who attempt it will be executed on the spot!"

"Vivian! You dare lay hands on me! Asmodeus will punish you! Wait for us! Your arrogance won't last long!"

The assassins, still unwilling to accept defeat, tried to intimidate Vivian by invoking Asmodeus, too afraid to engage in combat, lest they end up like the previous few—corpses beneath his blade.

Suddenly, a contingent of palace guards surged in from outside, following the plan. Many were Vivian's old acquaintances, and they surrounded Asmodeus's eagles, forming a pincer movement that completely cut off their retreat.

"Lay down your weapons! You have only one choice now: plead for Emperor Adonai's mercy. The fog shrouding Asmodeus above the palace will cease to exist from this moment!"

The assassins continued their clatter of weapons hitting the ground as they surrendered, abandoning all resistance against Asmodeus's minions. Vivian led the elite palace guard forces, racing swiftly toward the royal chambers to support Alice.

The tremors and explosions had ceased, leaving the entire palace in an eerie silence. Vivian couldn't determine who had emerged victorious—he needed to see for himself.

If Alice failed, Vivian would lead the palace guard's finest warriors into a life-or-death battle against Asmodeus. Even if they perished together, it was a risk he was willing to take!

Upon reaching the scene, Vivian was met with a shocking sight: Asmodeus stood amidst the rubble, encased in ice, his body frozen solid. Alice stood calmly with her back to everyone, her sword sheathed, seemingly unwilling to deliver a final killing blow.

Vivian realized Asmodeus was in terrible condition—the perfect moment to end his life. He shouted fervently, "Lady Danna! What are you doing? Hurry and strike Asmodeus down!"

Alice paused, slowly turning around. She glanced at the man frozen to death before her and replied calmly, "Don't be so nervous. He's already dead."

title: Chapter 29 — Sleepless Night (Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets)
content:
Chapter 29 — Sleepless Night (Bonus Chapter for Monthly Tickets)

Volume 33 · Chapter 29

"A dead??"

Vival's expression grew dazed, staring at Alfonso's corpse, frozen to death, for a long time, and indeed saw all traces of life gone.

But at first glance, it was hard to see that the man who had wreaked havoc on the kingdom for over twenty years was truly dead; his body still maintained a vivid appearance.

The shadow of fear that had shrouded countless hearts was thus destroyed to death by the cold poison, a feeling brimming with irony.

If Vival had not seen it with his own eyes, he too would have found it hard to believe that such a powerful magician as Alfonso could die at the hands of cold poison.

"He really is dead. The kingdom has finally been rid of this man."

Alice looked at Alfonso's corpse, unable to say a word. The heavy burden on her heart was gone, but for a moment she had lost all her goals, growing somewhat desolate.

Even though she had helped her teacher and birth mother achieve revenge, she still could not feel happy. Those who deeply loved her were gone and would never return to her side; killing Alfonso could not change this fact.

Alfonso's death could not heal the wounds in Alice's heart; she could only rely on time to slowly mend them.

Actually, at the moment those invisible black flame threads had connected to her heart, Alice had believed she was certain to die, destined to perish together with that madman.

But Alfonso no longer had any energy left to crush Alice's heart. Lifting even a finger had become exceptionally difficult, and he ultimately perished, frozen to death on the spot, full of regret.

Alfonso's wish to take Alice down with him was nothing more than an obsession; he had received his due punishment.

"Princess Diana, you truly live up to being a Purple Gold adventurer. Even though Alfonso was severely injured, the fact that you defeated him leaves no doubt about your strength." Vival said, praising her, filled with conviction regarding Alice as the youngest Purple Gold adventurer in history.

"No, you've misunderstood. It wasn't me who defeated him—it was my teacher. I merely succeeded by treading the path my teacher had paved." Alice answered seriously.

"Is that so?" A bead of cold sweat slowly trickled down Vival's forehead. He thought that Princess Diana was excellent in every aspect. Undoubtedly, after Alfonso's death, she was His Majesty Amedeo's greatest threat; he still could not afford to let his guard down.

Ignis, Duchess Claudya, this loyal knight who hailed from the slums, had spent over twenty years honing a single sword technique to protect the young princess and kill Alfonso to avenge the queen mother.

It now seemed she had not failed, but had successfully fulfilled all her missions as a knight.

Perhaps Alfonso had already died on the Great Snow Mountain, and merely wanted to return to this land for one last look.

That evening, only a few hours after Alfonso's death, his former supporters already sensed something was amiss, because after the turmoil in the palace, everything seemed abnormally quiet.

This group of nobles who supported Alfonso could maintain their稳固 positions only by relying on their sharp instincts; they knew well that beneath the calmest lake surface often lurked ferocious monsters!

Amedeo would naturally not let this rare opportunity slip away. He ordered Vival to lead trusted members of the court guard and carry out ruthless killings against those nobles who were not loyal to him.

Now was the moment of court chaos. The ten-year-old young king wanted to concentrate all power into his own hands this very night, becoming the true master of this land.

A bloody purge began secretly throughout the court, from top to bottom. The once-arrogant nobles had all become fish on Amedeo's chopping block, ripe for his slaughter.

Within a single night, the nobles' boundless wealth was entirely confiscated. Stripped of these possessions, the noble lords would likely fare worse than rats in the slums!

Amedeo knew that after Alfonso's death, Diana had become his greatest threat. But he had no intention of harming his own sister. Instead, he chose to secretly slaughter her supporters—a princess stripped of all support and completely hollowed out was nothing more than a princess. Without real power, she could not threaten his rule.

Aside from Alfonso's supporters, some special people also could not escape misfortune: the loyal guardians who deeply loved this land!

Amedeo did not need them. He needed people who would submit and swear allegiance to him, so all obstacles had to be cleared away for the future.

This ambitious young king wanted to swiftly and secretly purge the court in a single night, accomplishing what generations had failed to do, and clench the supreme power tightly in his own hands!

When Alice woke the next day, the transformation was already over. Even if she wanted to intervene, she would have no opportunity.

At the residence of the Minister of Finance, Caprice was scribbling furiously in his room, drafting plans for a new Kingdom of Spain, with proposal after proposal emerging. He hoped to provide useful advice to the king.

If these plans were adopted, the lower classes of the kingdom would bear far less pressure, and there would no longer be need to worry about a single cheap piece of dark bread. This land would walk the path of prosperity, striding forward toward becoming a human powerhouse!

This was Caprice's lifelong dream. He deeply loved this land and was willing to dedicate everything he had.

Caprice had already learned of Alfonso's death through secret channels. He grew exceptionally excited; his old rival had finally fallen, and there was no news more uplifting than this!

He believed his era had finally arrived. He could implement sweeping reforms in the kingdom and become a hero in Spanish history!

As for who would be king, Caprice felt it made little difference. Now that Alfonso was dead, even the young King Amedeo would rely heavily on him.

"Excellent! With these reforms, Spain will enter a new era under my guidance!"

Suddenly, the room's door was forcibly broken open. Vival, leading a group of court guards, walked in with grim expressions.

"Vival? What are you doing here?" Caprice asked in surprise.

Vival approached Caprice, produced a document personally signed by Amedeo, and said without ceremony, "Caprice, you have been found guilty of persecuting members of the royal family. You are sentenced to death."

"What?! Caprice was startled, his face drained of color, his whole body trembling as he stammered, "This... this is impossible! How can I be sentenced to death! I am a meritorious official!"

"Please keep your voice down. Her Highness Diana's daughter is sleeping soundly in the next room. This matter has nothing to do with the child. I hope you do not wake her." Vival warned in a merciless tone.

Caprice grew agitated, frantically tearing at his white hair. "I have been utterly loyal to the kingdom, with never a hint of betrayal in my heart. No one is more loyal than me! Look! I'm still writing reform plans for the kingdom, wanting to contribute to the future of this land!"

"I understand your feelings. Your love for this land fills me with sincere admiration." Vival bowed slightly and said.

"I have never persecuted members of the royal family. This is a false accusation against me! I have clearly dedicated everything I have, and yet I am to meet this fate? This is unfair! Why me?!" Bloodshot eyes filled Caprice's face as he asked hysterically.

"It is true that you are loyal to this land, but you are not loyal to His Majesty Amedeo. That is the crime you have committed." Vival paused, then said coldly, "Proceed."

Caprice had nothing left to say. He slumped onto the ground, despair overflowing from his gaze, looking like a living dead man.

The pitch-black sky, dotted with stars—

Carts loaded with the bodies of executed nobles were transported outside the capital for burning.

Those aristocrats who had been supremely magnificent in life were, after death, nothing more than piled ashes. They were hardly nobler than lowborn people; the only difference might be that they had more grease in their bellies, making their flames burn more brilliantly.

The raging fire continuously scorched the white-haired corpses, thick smoke rolling skyward, obscuring the bright moonlight.

Tonight was destined to be a bloody, sleepless night.

title: Chapter 30 — Memorial
content:
Chapter 30 — Memorial

Volume 33 · Chapter 30

The sky was just beginning to lighten when the Kingdom of Spain underwent earth-shaking changes overnight. A large number of nobles were secretly executed, and all power was concentrated in the hands of the ten-year-old king.

Amedeo's decade-long life as a puppet was finally over, and he welcomed the most brilliant moment of his life, becoming the true master of this ancient land.

In the royal council hall at that moment, Amedeo gazed calmly at the throne, impossible for anyone to guess what he was thinking.

Perhaps even Amedeo himself could hardly believe he had truly succeeded; in just one night, he had eliminated all obstacles and accomplished what generations before him had failed to do, regaining full control of power.

Although Amedeo was not yet old, he was considered the most resolute king in Spanish history, turning over a new page for the kingdom.

The royal guard knight Vival stood quietly behind Amedeo, head bowed in silence, unwilling to disturb him.

Vival's heart was equally stirred. He had personally witnessed Amedeo's steady climb from a humble puppet to the pinnacle of power in the kingdom. This journey had been filled with hardships, and only he could understand the humiliations the young king had endured.

Amedeo did not turn around. His voice was neither sad nor joyful as he asked, "Vival, is everything done?"

"Yes, everything has been handled flawlessly. One hundred and fourteen people were executed tonight — ninety-three nobles and their families, twenty-one wealthy merchants. They were all followers of Alfonso or people who refused to pledge allegiance to you. All the bodies have been burned." Vival paused, then added firmly, "Without a doubt, You are now the most honored person on this land. No one can compare with you."

"What about the casualties among the palace guards?" Amedeo pressed.

"Three died in the line of duty, twenty-four were wounded. This loss is entirely acceptable. The guards at those nobles' residences — while a few were decently strong, the strongest among them had only just entered Saint-tier. Their strength was no match for the palace guard." Vival explained.

"Very good. You carried out my orders well. Give those who died a proper burial, and reward the guards who participated in tonight's operation generously." Amedeo's tension eased. The大局 was settled, and he was the greatest winner.

"As you command. I will handle it exactly as you instructed." Vival bowed deeply.

"How is Diana's daughter?" Amedeo suddenly remembered.

"I have already escorted her to Her Highness Diana's side. You need not worry. When I executed Caprais, I kept it discreet, so she did not see anything bloody." Vival answered truthfully.

Amedeo fell silent, his expression shifting between light and dark as he muttered, "I regret it somewhat."

"Hmm? Are you dissatisfied with my work?" Vival raised his head in confusion.

"No. I regret sending Diana's daughter to her mother. She should have stayed by my side for now — she might prove useful." Amedeo's meaning was clear: he intended to use Chris as a hostage, for he could not bring himself to fully trust Alice.

"Your Majesty, can you still not fully trust Diana? She has clearly expressed her position — she came here solely to seek revenge and has no ambition for the throne. Before this, she was merely willing to be used by Caprais in order to get close to Alfonso." Vival furrowed his brows, feeling that Amedeo was being overly suspicious.

"The reason I have survived to this day is because of caution. I cannot completely trust this sister who suddenly returned. Would you trust her words?" Amedeo stared into Vival's eyes and countered.

"Well..." Vival's gaze wavered as he slowly replied, "No, I cannot. But I am willing to trust Senior Ignis. The disciple she taught must be upright and honest. I suggest you take Her Highness Diana to the imperial cemetery tomorrow to pay respects to Queen Consort Josephine. Use this opportunity to have a proper conversation. Both you and Her Highness Diana have the right to inherit the throne. Please, do not fight each other. That is not what the late king would have wanted to see."

Amedeo thought about it for a moment, then nodded. "Very well. Alfonso has been eliminated, and the kingdom has ushered in a new era. This is indeed a time to pay respects to our ancestors. You will invite Her Highness Diana on my behalf tomorrow."

"Understood." Vival bowed humbly. He thought that from now on this would likely be a matter between Amedeo and Diana alone, and there was nothing more he could do to help.

Amedeo, so young, showed traces of weariness. He slumped heavily onto the cold, hard throne, gazing ahead. Morning sunlight streamed in, casting the entire hall in an intensely vivid red.

"Vival, you've worked hard. I sincerely thank you."

"Uh!" Vival's eyes widened in surprise. After a long silence, he said, "No, Your Majesty. I was merely doing as you commanded. I do not deserve your thanks."

"You do." Amedeo said flatly, his eyes somewhat dull. "Before, when I sat here, I felt only fear, always worried that the nobles below would conspire to kill me. But now things are different. My heart is profoundly calm. It turns out a stone throne is simply uncomfortable to sit on, no matter how many gems decorate it — that cannot be changed."

Vival said nothing, realizing that Amedeo's state of mind had changed. Though he had sat on the throne often, only now did he know that it was actually uncomfortable — hard and cold.

"Did Caprais say anything before he died? Was he hysterically shouting that he was wronged?" Amedeo asked with mild interest.

"Yes, just as Your Majesty described. He did become highly agitated, claiming he不应have received such unfair treatment." Vival shook his head as he answered.

"I knew it. Actually, I had considered重用Caprais after eliminating Alfonso — promoting him to chancellor. It's a pity he crossed my底线 and wanted to pull me off the throne." Amedeo sighed, a sympathetic smile on his face.

Vival took out a thick notebook from his chest and handed it to Amedeo. "This is the reform plan Caprais wrote before he died. I believe it has some value, so I brought it back."

"As expected of Caprais, he truly has talent. These suggestions would ease tensions between the various classes and make the kingdom more stable. However—" Amedeo crossed out Caprais's name in the notebook and wrote his own in its place, saying meaningfully, "The people do not need to give gratitude to a dead man. They should thank me instead."

The royal cemetery was where all deceased Spanish royalty were laid to rest, a place to honor one's ancestors.

Rows of white tombstones rose from the lawns, with numerous lifelike statues standing behind them, recording what they looked like in life.

In the most secluded corner of the cemetery stood a female statue draped in white veil. Her beautiful face attracted countless gazes and appeared utterly sacred. The name inscribed on the tombstone below was that of the late Queen Consort Josephine.

Surrounded by many guards, Amedeo brought Alice and her daughter to pay respects to the deceased beautiful queen.

Alice held her young daughter's small hand as they stood beneath the queen's statue, gazing at her birth mother. That beautiful, pure face — no wonder so many found her unforgettable.

Little Chris understood nothing. She stood on the ground, sucking on her fingers, curiously looking around at this strange place she had never seen before.

Alice frowned in surprise and noticed a bouquet of blooming wild roses placed before Queen Consort Josephine's tombstone, clearly indicating someone had already come to pay respects. "Has anyone come to visit my mother recently?"

"Well..." Amedeo took a deep breath and answered calmly, "Alfonso. He was the only one who frequently came to visit Queen Consort Josephine."

title: Chapter 31 — A Later Update: Begging for Monthly Tickets
content:
Chapter 31 — A Later Update: Begging for Monthly Tickets

Volume 33 · Chapter 31

“In the eyes of many people, Queen Josephine is an evil witch, and even after her death, almost no one is willing to come and pay their respects to her, however Alfonso is an exception; he often comes here alone, always standing silently before the tombstone for a long time, completely making it impossible to fathom what he is thinking.”

Amadio inspected the statue of Queen Josephine. These things were all accidentally known to him; he also couldn't understand why Alfonso's behavior was so contradictory? He had personally killed the Queen, yet often came here alone to ponder. Based on Amadio's understanding of Alfonso, he shouldn't be the type to feel regret so easily, unless this man who came out of the slums still harbored lingering feelings for the dead Queen, of course this was just a guess.

“After the Queen's death, many people disagreed with burying her here, saying she was a disgrace in the kingdom's history; letting everyone in the royal family be ashamed if she were entombed in the royal mausoleum. I remember at that time some people tried to exploit the situation and wanted to dig up your mother's corpse from here, but in the end they were all stopped by Alfonso. It's somewhat ironic that the Queen wasn't disturbed after her death, and in a sense, it's thanks to Alfonso's help. Truly laughable, the murderer becoming the Queen's definite guardian after her death.”

Alice listened to Amadio's words and couldn't help but frown. She picked up a handful of wild roses from before the tombstone, and her mood became quite complex; her mind was full of Alfonso's grimacing expression—

What does this mean? Repentance?

Hard to imagine that a man who would stop at nothing for his own desires, a selfish man, would feel remorse for his actions

“In your eyes, is Alfonso a bad person?” Amadio suddenly asked.

“Of course! He is an evil person beyond redemption; even if I kill him personally, I cannot quell the anger in my heart. Wasn't it the same in your eyes?” Alice asked in surprise, in any case she could not forgive Alfonso, no matter if he repented for his crimes; such a despicable bastard did not deserve forgiveness from anyone.

“In my eyes, it might be a bit different from yours. I think Alfonso is a person of mixed good and bad, not purely evil, at least that is what I think.”

“Amadio said with deep meaning.”

“What are you talking nonsense about? He couldn't possibly have a good side; that is just an illusion of yours.” Alice firmly rebutted.

“I left my mother when I was three years old, and followed Alfonso to learn many things. He taught me not to be weakly kind, for it is very easy to become someone else's prey; I have this engraved in my heart, and it has become the creed of my life.” Amadio paused, expressionless, and said, “So in my eyes, Alfonso is not purely bad; it is he who has made me what I am today.”

“It seems we have many things we cannot agree on.” Alice completely did not agree with Amadio's words.

“That is normal; you have always followed that knight teacher's life. If you had grown up in the court, you would have the same thoughts as me.” Amadio responded casually.

Alice did not like her brother at all; he was completely not like a child just over ten years old, but rather like a belly full of bad water and a schemer, and there was simply no talking to him.

Not long ago, Vivaldi came to find Alice and said he wanted to take her to祭 her birth mother, and she thought this little king was showing favor to her. Now it seemed this was probably not the case.

Little Chris completely couldn't hear what the adults were talking about; she just found the densely packed statues here interesting, and couldn't help but point at Queen Josephine's statue and ask, “Mom, who is this? Why does she look a bit like Mom?”

“Ah?” Alice thought for a moment, squatted down and kindly said, “She is your mother's mother, that is your maternal grandmother.”

“Your mother's mother?” Chris activated her little brain, trying to understand this, “That is a bigger mother than Mom, that is Grandma, right?”

“This” Alice's expression was awkward, she cute daughter's head, and said helplessly, “However you understand it is fine, as long as the meaning isn't too far off.”

“Haha~” The little guy Chris was spinning on the ground, happily asking, “Mom, why is the big mom hiding in such a small stone house and not willing to come out to see us?”

Alice's eyes felt a bit uncomfortable, a sour feeling arose in her heart, and she could only answer gently, “Your maternal grandmother and your Aunt Claudia have all gone to the same place.”

“Hmm?” Little Chris became aggrieved, unable to understand this kind of thing, “Why did the big mom and the aunt-in-law have to go there?”

“One day you will understand, believe me.” Alice said seriously.

“But I have so many things I want to say to the big mom, must I only be able to do so in dreams?” Chris lowered her head, looking very disappointed.

Alice looked at her daughter's disappointed expression, and couldn't bear to see her like this, so she pointed at the tombstone and said, “You can try speaking to the tombstone; your maternal grandmother and aunt-in-law can all hear your voice?”

“Really?” Little Chris became excited, the hair on her head seeming to be charged, standing straight up.

“Of course it is true; didn't I say I wouldn't lie to you?” Alice kissed her daughter on the forehead.

Chris smiled openly and immediately ran to Queen Josephine's tombstone, facing the cold tombstone, and said in a very small voice—

“Big mom, big mom, can you hear me?”

“Can I see Auntie at Big mom's place? I can give up toys, I want Auntie to come see me; I miss her a bit.”

“Is Big mom as pretty as the statue? Will I be as pretty as you when I grow up?”

“And, and, every time I play too much, I get spanked by Mom; can't you also spank Mom's bottom? Help me get some revenge! Otherwise it's only me being bullied, that's unfair; I I am willing to split the cake with you half, isn't that sincere? This was taught by Dad~”

Alice stood quietly behind her daughter; Chris was still too young to understand the meaning of death. If possible, she hoped her daughter could have a childhood without any gray areas.

Amadio looked at the little girl foolishly talking to herself in front of the tombstone; his heart was not pleasant, and he said in a tone of sigh, “After all, a person is only considered a person during childhood, without having to worry about everything, and can every day live in happiness; truly enviable.”

“You are also a child?” Alice asked in surprise.

“? ? ?” A flicker of surprise appeared in Amadio's eyes; he shook his head and said, “No, I am not. From the moment I left my mother's side, I was no longer.”

“In my eyes, you are indeed still a child, whether in your inner self or your outer appearance.” Alice said softly.

“! ! !” Amadio's gaze became peculiar; he lowered his head and was silent for a long time, and then said—

“Alice Clodya, the foreign thorn knight of Britain, I will not acknowledge you.”

“My older sister Diana, had already died over two years ago.”

title: Chapter 32 — Origin
content:
Chapter 32 — Origin

Volume 33 · Chapter 32

Amadeo was clever enough to understand what Alice had meant by her words.

In Alice's eyes, Amadeo was still a "child," and she spoke from an elder's perspective.

Though Alice did not like her gloomy younger brother, she recognized him as family.

So Amadeo's gaze grew complicated, for he was unwilling to accept this truth.

"No matter how much you resemble Diana, you could never truly become her. I suppose Alfonso also secretly tampered with the beastmen's sorcery, didn't he?"

Alice slowly closed her eyes, understanding Amadeo's meaning just as well. She had never intended to stay here, nor did she hold any interest in the throne.

As Alice had said, she would honor her teacher Claudya's wishes and live on as an ordinary person.

"It is as you say. The beastmen's sorcery is entirely unreliable."

Their exchange, though seemingly unrelated, had already amounted to each revealing their stance. Neither spoke directly, yet both understood perfectly.

Amadeo had no wish for Diana to return, for she would threaten his position, so he would not acknowledge Alice's identity.

And Alice responded by declaring her complete lack of interest in the throne, hoping Amadeo would lower his guard.

"My elder sister Diana has been missing for over twenty years. Even if she returns alive, she is hardly suited to inherit the throne. Perhaps she has become a powerful swordsman now, but outstanding personal ability does not mean one can govern a kingdom smoothly. Those are two different things." Amadeo paused and tapped his chest. "I am more suited to inherit the throne than Diana, am I not?"

"Perhaps you are right." Alice smiled, took a deep breath, and spoke slowly. "When I was young, I once dreamed of becoming a beautiful princess, because I thought that both a prince's and a princess's life was happy. But after meeting you, I suddenly felt ridiculous. If I lived like you, I would probably go mad sooner or later. I pity you, having lost your true self at such a young age."

"I do not need anyone's sympathy. This was my own choice." Amadeo already knew Alice's stance, and the doubts in his heart gradually dissipated.

Alice was silent for a moment before asking, "May I come back in the future?"

"It would be best if you did not return. If possible, I wish we never meet again. This is not only for my sake, but also for the peace of the kingdom. This land does not need two claimants to the throne." Amadeo said this gravely, drawing a clear line between himself and Alice.

"For the sake of peace?" Alice frowned slightly, suspicious.

"However, if you wish to visit Queen Consort Josephine or need any assistance, you may return at any time. I can make an exception and offer you some help." Amadeo did not burn every bridge and still gave Alice some assurance.

"I see. The fact that I am allowed to visit Josephine is already more than enough." Alice let out a long breath, feeling the weight finally lift from her heart.

Amadeo took a thick diary from his chest and handed it to Alice personally. "This is a diary seized from Alfonso's home. It records many interesting things, including secrets surrounding the death of the late Queen Consort Josephine. I think you will find it quite interesting."

Alice accepted Alfonso's diary. It appeared quite heavy, likely rather old, and contained simple records of everything Alfonso experienced after turning seventeen.

Amadeo did not linger there. After handing the diary to Alice, he turned to leave.

Between the two heirs of the Kingdom of Spain, there had been no cruel struggle. Instead, the royal conflict had been resolved through peaceful means.

Alice looked up at Amadeo's thin retreating back and, in that moment, thought of many things. Recalling the slums she had seen along the way, she could not help but call out loudly, "Amadeo, will you be a good king?"

Amadeo stopped and turned around in surprise. After deep thought, he answered, "I cannot guarantee that. I can only promise that I will do better than our parents..."

Alice lowered her head, finding the answer barely acceptable. If an idealist like herself became Queen of Spain, she doubted she could do any better than her parents either.

After Amadeo left, only Alice and Chris remained before Queen Consort Josephine's tombstone. She was well aware that although Alfonso was the murderer who killed her teacher and birth mother, he was not the true mastermind behind everything.

Alice had already sensed the existence of the Black Dragon, which most likely hid somewhere within this land. She had successfully absorbed the Black Dragon blood flowing within Alfonso, completing her final transformation.

On Alice's left hand, dark veins could be seen faintly beneath her meridians, winding around her arm like tree roots.

Alice stared at the diary in her hands. It was very important to her. She might find answers inside it — the very source of all this turmoil, the hiding place of the Black Dragon Nidhogg.

Seven days later, the turmoil among the upper echelons of the Kingdom of Spain had essentially subsided, and the court returned to stability.

The ten-year-old young king Amadeo had shaken off his fate as a puppet and become the recognized supreme ruler of this land. A king holding real power while still a minor was unprecedented in human history — Amadeo had set a precedent.

Just as everyone assumed the young king would launch sweeping reforms across the war-torn land, he did something many could not understand —

secretly assembling a large number of elite troops, he marched westward!

Nobody knew what Amadeo was thinking. At a time like this, waging war would only make an already terrible situation worse for the kingdom.

Yet the young king now held overwhelming power, able to sway everything with a single word. The surviving nobles in the court were all trembling with fear,不敢 daring to voice even a shred of opposition.

Actually, Amadeo had also learned of the Black Dragon's existence. To prevent a second Alfonso from arising, he had to eliminate the root of all chaos by any means necessary. That was the highest priority, far more important than reforming the kingdom.

Amadeo did not want his throne to grow cold before enemies like Alfonso appeared again, so he dispatched Vivald with elite forces to fully assist Alice in destroying the Black Dragon.

Deep within the dark cave, the sleeping Black Dragon suddenly opened its eyes. Its sharp pupils gazed toward the distance. Though it retained only a head and its aura had grown increasingly weak, it still managed to survive stubbornly —

"I smell the scent of prey. A divine soul. Did Alfonso succeed?"

"No! Too many. Why are so many humans gathering nearby?!"

PSI 1

Um, does anyone believe me when I say the power went out in the middle of the night yesterday?

title: Chapter 33 — Infiltrating the Valley's Depths
content:
Chapter 33 — Infiltrating the Valley's Depths

Volume 33 · Chapter 33

"Why are so many humans suddenly approaching here?"

Black Dragon Nidhogg's expression turned from wary to uncertain, bordering on panic, unable to determine exactly what was happening outside.

This was its hiding place, located in the middle of nowhere. Under normal circumstances, only a handful of people would pass by nearby, but suddenly a large number of humans were pouring toward this area all at once—that was clearly abnormal!

As the creator of the dragon race, the black dragon appeared formidable, but after being severely injured by the demon race's prophet during the era of the gods, it had been reduced to nothing more than a lone head clinging to life. Its power and majesty had long since faded from their former peak.

Nidhogg worried that certain ill-intentioned humans might have set their sights on it. That would only make things more dangerous. Trapped as a mere head, it could not leave the cave. If discovered, it would be left in a very disadvantageous position!

Although Nidhogg did not fear insignificant humans, it had certainly heard the story of ants biting an elephant to death.

Occasional individual human strong ones were not worth worrying about, but a legion composed of human elites? Even Nidhogg, having lost its body, would find them troublesome.

Black Dragon Nidhogg considered various possibilities, trying to guess what this enormous group of humans drawing near was after—

"Could it be that Alfonso betrayed me?"

"Impossible, he doesn't have the courage for that. I could kill him at any time."

"I can sense that among so many souls, there is one possessing extremely high divinity. It's clearly the most suitable sacrifice for repairing my body!"

"Has something happened to Alfonso?"

Black Dragon Nidhogg attempted to sense Alfonso's presence, only to find that all connection with its servant had been severed, as though he had completely vanished from this world.

Now Nidhogg finally began to catch clues about what was happening. The humans outside were very likely coming for itself. Alfonso was already dead, and his death had exposed its hiding place!

"Stupid Alfonso, good for nothing but causing failure—what a waste! It's bad enough that he died himself, but why did he have to expose my secrets?"

Black Dragon Nidhogg ground its teeth, its eyes turning vicious, and suppressed growls echoed frequently through the deep cave.

There was no way out. Not a single one of the humans gathered outside could be allowed to live!

Before successfully repairing my body, I absolutely cannot appear in full view. Otherwise, those who once betrayed me—their children—will undoubtedly resort to any means to kill me.

Above the canyon cave, a Spanish elite force of exactly 150,000 soldiers stood in formation nearby.

They were arranged in disciplined combat formations, well-trained and clearly distinct from ordinary troops, strictly obeying their officers' commands.

Their equipment was also extremely fine. In order to carry out the task of exterminating the black dragon, the soldiers were thoroughly prepared, armed down to their teeth, and even several high-power magitech cannons meant for siege warfare had been pushed to this location.

From above, the dark sea of troops looked enormous, like a mobile fortress of steel. To completely eliminate future threats, Amadeo spared nothing, deploying every available military force at his disposal to fully assist Alice in hunting down the black dragon.

Unfortunately, Amadeo had only recently seized real power and had not yet fully grasped the entirety of the kingdom's accumulated strength. He could temporarily only muster these forces. Though only 150,000 strong, that was enough for a rather large-scale war.

Moreover, every one of these soldiers had been rigorously selected; the minimum standard was a low-rank mage or warrior. Their actual combat effectiveness was no less than a large ordinary army of 400,000.

Vival, the supreme commander of this crusade, sat astride a noble steed, patiently reading through "Alfonso's diary" while carefully studying the surrounding terrain. With certainty, he said—

"The canyon recorded in the diary should be here without a doubt. If I'm not mistaken, this entire area was Alfonso's hometown. A few kilometers away there used to be a slum, but unfortunately it was destroyed overnight by those horrific man-eating locust swarms. Alfonso came from there."

"Is that so?"

Alice, riding her warhorse, gazed across the desolate land, expanding her perception range as far as possible. Yet she could not detect the slightest trace of dragon aura. This was unusual.

She couldn't help but wonder whether the events Alfonso described in his diary were true or false. Was Black Dragon Nidhogg really here?

Normally, Alice, as a humanoid dragon—considered a kindred of dragons—would find it not difficult to sense another dragon's presence.

If Alfonso had not lied in his diary, then Black Dragon Nidhogg had completely concealed its aura to prevent others from finding it.

Alice withdrew her gaze and looked toward a spectacular canyon not far away, as if sliced clean through by a blade, cleaving the earth in two. An indescribable sense of familiarity washed over her.

"Is the evil black dragon really here? Aside from desolate land and bottomless canyons, I can't see so much as a shadow of any dragon. Have we made a mistake? Perhaps missed some crucial clue…"

"Ahem!" Vival covered his embarrassment with a light cough, instinctively about to address Alice as "Your Highness Diana," but quickly realized he should not, so he changed his words: "Miss Alice, we followed the clues from the diary to reach here. There shouldn't be any mistake. The diary didn't specify the black dragon's exact hiding place, only mentioning the vicinity of the canyon."

"That's strange. Where exactly is it hiding? Not the slightest trace of aura can be detected. A black dragon should be enormous; it shouldn't be possible for it to be completely concealed."

Alice furrowed her brows, considering a possibility. "Could it be that we startled it, so before we even arrived, it took the opportunity to flee?"

"That's impossible. The diary described some details about the black dragon—it has already lost its body and exists only as a head. I don't believe a dragon stripped of its body still has any ability to move." Vival voiced his speculation.

Alice fell silent, her eyes locking onto the magnificent canyon not far away, and said sternly, "Send people to conduct a thorough search of this area. Don't miss a single suspicious spot."

"Yes, I'll handle it right away. You may return to camp and rest. We should complete the search before nightfall." Vival suggested.

"No, I intend to search the bottom of the canyon myself. That could also be where the black dragon is hiding." Alice said earnestly.

"That hardly seems appropriate. Leave such matters to us. Moreover, the canyon bottom might harbor unknown dangers. If anything were to happen to you, we could never answer to His Majesty." Vival's expression was troubled. Although Amadeo refused to acknowledge Alice as Sister Diana, he could not deny their blood relation. Even without the princess title, she was a genuine member of the royal family.

"It's precisely because the bottom may hold danger that I need to investigate it myself." Alice looked at Vival and said meaningfully—

"Do you take me for a花瓶?"

"Please don't lump me in with those noble ladies who faint at the slightest provocation during ballrooms."

title: Chapter 34 — Black Dragon Blood
content:
Chapter 34 — Black Dragon Blood

Volume 33 · Chapter 34

At Alice's request, Vival led many soldiers to search around the canyon.
Alice herself went alone to the dangerous bottom of the canyon, wanting to see if there were any clues in the deepest part.
Because the bottom of the canyon is unknown and could present unexpected dangers, Alice, being the strongest in the group, naturally wouldn't let a group of soldiers go deeper here.
Alice leapt down, landing smoothly at the designated spot, looked up, and found that the canyon was deeper than she imagined, the distance to the top exceeding a thousand meters, and the space was extremely narrow, making it hard for sunlight to reach here.
Hard to imagine the legendary Black Dragon hiding in such a place, but if Alfonso wasn't lying in his diary and the Black Dragon had already lost its body, then this place would indeed be very suitable for hiding.
Alice took a deep breath, slowly stood up from the ground, surveyed the environment at the bottom of the canyon, the surrounding rock walls were black, looking like scorched earth after being burned by fierce fire, which was somewhat abnormal—
Driven by curiosity, Alice scraped a piece of stone from the surface of the rock wall, and when she gently squeezed it, it crumbled into powder?
Alice immediately frowned; this didn't look like a volcanic area, why was the land scorched like this? It was probably only possible through external intervention.
Remember, the flame Alfonso used was black and extremely hot, easily melting the earth; perhaps the Black Dragon used the same kind of power.
Alice slowly drew the slender sword from her waist, alert and vigilant around her, increasingly believing that the Black Dragon might be hiding nearby.
She carefully walked toward the depths of the canyon, trying not to make any sound, vaguely sensing unusual waves of high heat assaulting her, making sweat pour down her back—
At the huge cave entrance, appearing at the deepest part of the canyon, the dim light made it impossible to see what was inside?
A surging scorching breath rushed at her, as if a massive creature lurked inside; each breath made outsiders shiver.
After stopping, Alice examined the suspicious cave before her; the closer she got, the more intense the heat became, and she couldn't help but wonder if she had not arrived at a volcano's mouth?
Alice instinctively felt a tinge of fear; the pressure from her bloodline, it was obvious that deeper in the cave there were stronger kindred than herself—
This is indeed the place! No wonder no breath could be sensed outside the canyon; it was hidden so deep!
Alice instinctively trembled all over, so frightened that it was hard to move her feet; she had no doubt that the terrifying Black Dragon was inside, and had no courage to go into the cave alone.
She thought the correct approach should be to contact Vival and the outside army, let them assist her in jointly annihilating the Black Dragon; alone, it would probably be impossible to succeed.
Alice swallowed nervously, her gaze fixed on the cave, quietly retreated backward, planning to temporarily leave the bottom of the canyon, devise a perfect plan before acting.
“Since you've come, why not come in and take a look? Humble human.”
“Uh!”
Alice stared wide-eyed in shock, certain she hadn't misheard; the voice came from deep within the cave, clearly the other party had sensed her arrival.
You Black Dragon Nidhogg? !
“Indeed, you came to see me? Then why not stay forever…”
Alice quickly turned her back, wanting to leave the place temporarily; it was obvious the Black Dragon had prepared, an abrupt attack would be more dangerous!
How could the Black Dragon Nidhogg give me an escape chance, especially when it sensed that the other party's soul possessed a very pure divine nature, it would more likely not let me—
The Black Dragon, after being heavily wounded and barely surviving for several epochs, dreamed of restoring its body, reappearing in its peak form; the joy of offering itself to those who came was far greater than the panic exposed in front of many!
As long as it could successfully obtain Alice's soul, it would use its great form to make the world feel despair under shadow again; those dragon-blooded who had betrayed would suffer the cruelest punishment!
Alice felt the ground beneath her shaking violently, as if something terrifying was about to attack from behind; she looked back—
She saw a blood spring rushing out from the deep black cave, like a torrent from the mountain top, unstoppable!
The blood spring seemed to have eyes, heading straight for Alice as she fled, sealing all her escape routes!
“This black dragon blood?”
Alice furrowed her brow, cold sweat dripping, realizing that the blood spring was indeed the Black Dragon's blood; the blood in her body was also restless, becoming very uneasy, as if responding to the Black Dragon as a 'father'!
Fortunately, the Frost Saint Dragon was not a first-generation dragon-blooded; otherwise, the Black Dragon could have used bloodline suppression to command Alice at will, manipulating her body and mind.
Alice, surrounded by the blood spring, in a hurry, swung her slender sword forward, cutting a crimson icy ripple!
Finally, a passage was cut in the blood spring; before Alice could escape, it repaired in an instant, blood springs surged from all directions, unstoppable, even the sky was completely sealed.
“Damn! Can't escape!”
Alice gritted her teeth, resisting as best she could,
but was still swallowed by the blood spring, dragged forcefully into the deep cave.
<>
Outside the canyon, Vival supervised the soldiers' work, his gaze inevitably turning toward the nearby fractured canyon.
“Calculating the time, Miss Alice…
…will something have happened?”
Vival wondered in his mind, constantly calculating the time, speculating that Alice should have returned.
He began to worry; if Alice had not returned, he would have to bring someone to the bottom of the canyon to search,
Vival did not want…
Vival did not want Alice to encounter any danger, especially when he was accompanying her; even if he were a personal guard of Amadio, he could not escape severe punishment.
Boom boom—
The entire canyon area began to shake violently, suddenly startling Vival and the soldiers.
“Earthquake?!!
Just as the words ended, from the distant fractured canyon, a magnificent blood-colored fountain rose to the sky, splashing into the 800-foot high air.
The huge shadow of the blood spring covered everyone’s heads, making the soldiers, in a daze, think they had entered darkness; death had approached them!
The imposing might of the Black Dragon, unrestrained, terrified the living beings of this land; despair filled every soldier’s heart.
Vival’s stunned expression froze on his face; he had no idea where this strange blood spring came from, but with his rich combat experience, he immediately reacted—
“Alert! !!

title: Chapter 35 — The Black Dragon's Whisper
content:
Chapter 35 — The Black Dragon's Whisper

Volume 33 · Chapter 35

At Vival's command, the soldiers quickly gathered, raising their heavy shields and forming an impregnable defensive formation. If they were ordinary soldiers, they would likely be frightened stupid and lose all morale at the instant the blood spring gushed forth, but this elite unit could still remain calm at that moment. A formation of 150,000 soldiers stood crowded together, holding their positions, eyes fixed on the spectacular blood spring soaring into the sky. "What the hell is this?" Vival felt like facing a great enemy, cold sweat sliding down his cheeks as he sensed the terrifying pressure of the black dragon, his body shivering. He couldn't help worrying about Alice, who had gone deep into the canyon's bottom, hoping she was unharmed, and before Alice returned, no one could leave this place without permission. The blood spring sprayed wildly across the sky, gradually falling from the heavens; countless meatballs resembling embryos floated in the air, looking extremely eerie, their surfaces covered with fine blood vessels that pulsed rhythmically, as if some living life was being nurtured inside. "? ? !" Vival's eyes twitched, a sense of foreboding rising in his heart; having never seen such a scene in his life, he could hardly believe his own eyes. Numerous meatballs began to swell rapidly, growing visible to the naked eye; within a few breaths they had multiplied in size several times over, gradually turning into gigantic dragons lacking scales, composed solely of raw, red flesh. As the ancestor of the dragon race, the Black Dragon Nidhogg was fully capable of using its own blood to create powerful dragonkin; the once invincible great dragon race was born this way, and now this tiny group of humans fortunately witnessed the process firsthand! The dragonkin born of the Black Dragon's blood appeared especially grotesque; lacking scales, their skin clearly revealed the muscle tissue and pulsing meridians, and even the membrane wings on their backs were somewhat transparent and immature. A multitude of spontaneously generated dragons appeared out of thin air, instantly exuding a mighty dragon aura; the pressure from a higher species made Vival and the soldiers tremble with fear. "This dragon? How... pathetic..." Vival stammered, his eyes widened in horror. The magical energy in the air became agitated; a hovering dragon breathed upon the tiny human soldiers below, a massive fire pillar condensed, setting the sky ablaze red, as if a laser swept across the soldiers' formation— Boom boom boom! A series of explosions rang out; the watertight defensive line was shattered by the dragon's breath, the immense power causing heavy casualties among the soldiers. Scorching heat rose, red sparks drifting with the hot wind; Vival stood dazed on a stretch of scorched earth, watching soldiers collapsed on the ground crying out in pain, realizing that the two sides were not on the same level of strength. Just a single dragon breath dealt massive damage to the kingdom's elite forces; if the dragons in the sky attacked simultaneously, the result could very well be total annihilation. Vival licked his dry lips, knowing he could not retreat under any circumstances—first, because Alice had not returned; second, if they withdrew, those terrifying dragons would quickly ignite war across the entire kingdom, and Amadeo's throne was not yet secure; any losses would only become more severe. A brief moment of thought gave Vival courage; he instinctively clenched his fist, pointed his sword at the floating dragons in the sky, and, gritting his teeth, gave the order— "Don't be afraid! Charge forward! Don't let these ugly lizards scare you!" "They have no scales, obviously their defense isn't strong; our magic cannons should be able to blast them down!" The soldiers, encouraged, gradually shook off their fear and quickly began to carry out Vival's orders. The cavalry surged forward first, discarding their heavy spears and using longbows to shoot arrows at the dragons in the sky, frequently harassing the enemy. The few magic cannons at the rear were swiftly pushed forward, bringing all the dragons flying in the sky within range— "Fire! Let these naked-ass lizards taste our might!" In the winding, narrow passage of the cave, the blood spring entangled Alice as it continually plunged deeper, directly bringing her before the Black Dragon Nidhogg! Alice felt the blood spring had stopped; seizing the opportunity, she spun her thin sword once, freezing and shattering the flowing blood spring! This time the blood spring did not surge again to entangle Alice; most of it had already been used to create the newborn dragons, to deal with the outside human soldiers. The Black Dragon Nidhogg only wanted to meet Alice alone, and did not wish to be disturbed by a swarm of insignificant ants while enjoying the offering. Alice rose nervously, her doubtful gaze scanning the unfamiliar surroundings; the cavern walls were covered in crimson membranes, veins throbbing densely, and beneath her feet lay soft, weed-like hairs—all of them the whiskers of the Black Dragon Nidhogg. The enormous black dragon's head lay still upon the ground, having fused with this cave six, the cavern seeming like a part of its body. Nidhogg's lantern-like narrow eyes greedily fixed on the slender Alice; in the darkness they resembled two suns flashing with the light of death. Black Nidhogg Alice's lips trembled, her pupils contracted, thinking she had seen some monster; her legs involuntarily went weak. Alice swore that the black dragon before her was, aside from Merlin, the second thing in her life capable of making her soul feel fear; this was merely a head, and if the black dragon were in its prime, it would be an existence as terrifying as...? Alice dared not think further, for that would cause her last shred of fighting spirit to collapse; without lifting a finger, she would already suffer a pathetic defeat. "Somewhat familiar, huh? Why..." The Black Dragon Nidhogg's eyes flashed with doubt as it exhaled a scorching breath from its nostrils. "Shout!" Alice clenched her teeth, gripped her thin sword, suppressing the immense fear within, and thought about how to defeat the black dragon before her. "Have we met before? Human..." the Black Dragon Nidhogg asked; Alice's appearance gave it a sense of déjà vu. "What nonsense are you spouting? I've never seen you before." Alice replied firmly, a sheen of cold sweat already on her back, her teeth unconsciously chattering; facing the black dragon's immense pressure, perhaps only she herself truly understood. "No, I am absolutely not seeing you for the first time; there is no mistake.* The Black Dragon Nidhogg's large eyeballs rolled about, trying to search its memory for something extremely distant; "Oh~, I remember now; I never expected it to be you—could this be fate's arrangement? If not, then this world would be too small." "What are you talking about? I can't understand a word." Alice frowned, wondering if the black dragon's mind had a problem. "Don't play dumb; your clumsy acting makes me sick." The Black Dragon Nidhogg paused, speaking in an insulting tone— "Could it be that you really forgot me?" "As the lowly plaything in the palm of OJ, the humiliation of being wantonly toyed with"

title: Chapter 36 — Warrior Born to Slay Gods
content:
Chapter 36 — Warrior Born to Slay Gods

Volume 33 · Chapter 36

Alice listened with utter confusion, wondering if Nidhogg had somehow mistaken her for someone else.

"You haven’t changed at all," the black dragon sneered, his tone dripping with mockery. "You’re still so good at playing the weak, pitiful victim to win over the ancient gods. That’s all you’re capable of. Because of that, humanity has suffered endlessly in the depths. But you’re clever enough to succeed—just barely. He paused, his voice dripping with contempt. "You sold your own dignity, allying yourself with that demon race prophet. Don’t you feel like a filthy whore? No principles, no thoughts of your own, not even a shred of shame—just a bitch begging for scraps from the strong."

"Wait—are you talking about me?" Alice interrupted, her voice sharp with disbelief. "I’m Alice."

"I won’t be fooled," Nidhogg scoffed, his massive jaws dripping with bloodlust. "You think you can trick me? I’m no fool like that boastful old idiot Odin." His voice twisted with derision. "You’re one of the ancient gods, the weakest of them all. Why betray your own kind?"

"Couldn’t you just keep playing Odin’s little pet? Wouldn’t that have been easier? You’d still be the Mother of Mankind, the great leader."

"Oh, right—I almost forgot. There’s also that traitorous elf god, Korylon, and his lot. They betrayed the ancient gods too. I’ll never understand how that demon race prophet could have such power—strong enough to unite you all in rebellion."

"You mean Maria?" Alice’s confusion deepened. The titles "Mother of Mankind" and "Leader of Humanity" were enough to piece together who he was talking about.

"Don’t play dumb with me!" Nidhogg’s patience snapped. His bloodshot eyes burned with fury as he roared, "You *are* Maria!"

Alice’s breath caught. The stench of blood and decay rolled off the monstrous dragon, its overwhelming presence threatening to crush her will.

"Did you get what you wanted from allying with the demon race prophet?" Nidhogg sneered. "After the Twilight of the Gods, so few ancient gods survived. My servants told me you and that cowardly Lucifer became the rulers of life and death, dictating the new world’s rules. How ironic—you, the weakest of them all, became the biggest winner. Odin would never have imagined that his pathetic pet would one day rise to his level. *Hahaha!*"

Alice scoffed, unable to stomach the dragon’s insults. She had nothing to do with the vague, mythic Maria—just another deity worshipped by the Holy Church.

"Did I hit a nerve?" Nidhogg smirked, his eyes narrowing. "No matter how much you change, in my eyes, you’re still that spineless bitch crawling before Odin. Did you really think using the demon race prophet’s power would elevate you? How naive."

Alice’s expression darkened. No matter how she explained, the dragon had already made up his mind.

She herself was just as baffled. Why would Nidhogg associate her with the Goddess of Light? Had he been holed up in his cave too long, his mind rotting away?

"Maria," Nidhogg purred, his massive jaws unhinging with a wet, clicking sound. "I’ll give you one chance. Surrender your soul to me. Let me absorb you. Prove your worth."

Alice’s blood boiled. The dragon’s words were filthy, arrogant—she couldn’t stand it.

A colossal golden ice blade materialized in the air above Nidhogg’s head, suspended as she swung it with all her might. The weapon crashed down with unstoppable force.

The black dragon wasn’t at full strength—just a broken head, barely able to move. If he wouldn’t let her escape, then she’d fight.

Alice had weighed her options carefully. If Nidhogg had been at his peak, she never would have attacked.

The frozen blade plummeted, striking true. A gale of biting wind erupted, sweeping through the cavern and freezing the red rock walls with frost.

Before the cold could dissipate, scorching heat surged upward. The ice-and-fire clash was unbearable. The blade melted at visible speed.

Nidhogg was engulfed in searing black flames, Alice’s ice power utterly useless against this divine might. The heat dwarfed even Alfonso’s—ten times hotter, nearly solar in intensity.

The dragon let out a deep, mocking laugh. "Hahaha, Maria. Even as the world’s ruler, you’re still the weakest ancient god. Why did your power regress so badly? You’re no better than a mortal now."

Alice raised her blade, *Light’s Elegy*, and closed her eyes, entering a meditative state. The inherited crystal within her had fully dissolved, and an unfamiliar force surged violently through her veins.

She hadn’t expected to kill Nidhogg easily—she just needed time to test her new power.

Her eyes snapped open. A wave of extreme cold erupted, suppressing the black flames for a moment. The cavern became a frozen tomb. A sleek, armored exoskeleton formed over her skin, and massive ice wings unfurled from her back.

The transformation was complete.

A warrior from the Goddess Era, who had once defied the ancient gods, stood before them once more!
