title: Chapter 37 — Cave Battle
content:
Chapter 37 — Cave Battle

Volume 33 · Chapter 37

The dragon's roar echoed through the deep cave, the bone-chilling blizzard obscuring one's vision and forcing the black dragon's flames to retreat somewhat.

Alice's body manifested a magnificent battle armor similar to Alice's, and although the appearance was very similar, there were still significant differences—

The battle armor formed around the Ice Frost Sacred Dragon as its core, colored mostly blue and white compared to Alice's Earth Sacred Dragon, giving off an even more bone-piercing chill.

In addition, Alice had obtained true black dragon blood, while Alice had promoted to a dragon warrior using artificial black dragon blood. Both in terms of the armor's defense and the degree of power amplification, they were simply not on the same level.

From the outside, the battle armor born from bathing in true black dragon blood looked more splendid and intricate, even granting the wielder steel-like wings that provided rare flight capability.

If Alice had become a pseudo dragon warrior through artificial black dragon blood, then Alice was the real deal—a true dragon warrior, her image exactly matching those of the ancient era of the gods.

Dragon warriors, as products of humanity borrowing the power of dragons, had from their inception been the vanguard against the ancient gods, making enormous sacrifices for the victory of Ragnarok.

Legend held they were the most perfect beings transcending dragons itself, where human exceptional talent and dragon's formidable physique complemented each other, achieving an extreme harmony that granted them the power to wage war against the ancient gods.

After several epochs, the warriors who had once heroically fought the ancient gods had long turned to dust, yet today they returned to the world's gaze once more.

As the only dragon warrior alive today, Alice also bore the mission of slaying the ancient god Nidhogg. Perhaps this was the destiny no dragon warrior throughout the ages could escape!

"Dragon Warrior."

Nidhogg the Black Dragon observed Alice's transformation without a trace of panic. He had already harbored some suspicions. "As I suspected—from the moment you entered, I faintly sensed an anomalous dragonblood power. So that's how it is. It seems Alfonso truly died, and you obtained my blood from him, correct?"

"Die."

Alice slowly opened her eyes. Her own strength had undergone a qualitative leap, and as she released the pressure of her pseudo-divine realm, much of the fear she'd felt when confronting the black dragon dissipated.

After ascending to the pseudo-divine realm, the colors of her magic power and fighting aura had grown increasingly dim, trending toward discarding ostentation and returning to simplicity—ultimately becoming transparent.

Even the fused ice crystals she created gradually dulled, resembling ordinary ice yet remarkably free of impurities, incredibly pure!

Moreover, Alice could now touch upon the power of laws, using Divine Power with limited charges within a finite timeframe.

She had received the dragon clan's legacy in the Ancestral Dragon Sanctuary and had never forgotten it. Now the time had come to reap some of its fruits.

Armed with dragon lineage, Great Snow Mountain swordsmanship, warrior battle armor, and the precious divine sword that counteracted dark-type creatures in hand—

Much like how ordinary pseudo-divine powers were formidable yet robed in mere cloth, Alice upon reaching the pseudo-divine realm already possessed a full set of divine gear.

The true combat power Alice could unleash likely exceeded the pseudo-divine tier; she might well have a chance to triumph before Nidhogg the Black Dragon.

"You are the source of all these tragedies. Not only must I avenge my dead kin—I must fulfill the pact made with the dragon clan and rescue them from your shadow."

"What? Have you made some deal with those dragonblood traitors? Working for those betrayers isn't exactly a good thing. From the moment they betrayed me, I never intended to let them go." Nidhogg the Black Dragon paused, his gaze becoming ferocious as he said, "I'll use their blood to extinguish the rage that has burned within me for several epochs!"

"I'm sorry, but you'll die taking that rage with you." Alice gripped the slender sword in her hand firmly. The dragon aura emanating from her pseudo-divine realm didn't falter before Nidhogg—it only grew sharper.

"Hahaha, laughable~" Nidhogg the Black Dragon sneered, his tone playful. "You're merely a thief of power. Don't tell me you actually think you can stand against me? Maria, you disappoint me greatly. After such an endless flood of time, you haven't improved at all? Have you truly become a main god?"

Alice no longer wished to explain she wasn't the Goddess of Light. She launched a fierce assault instead!

Her steel wings unfurled behind her, emitting roars akin to engines, and a terrifying ice storm swept across every corner of the cave!

With a "swish," Alice shot forth like an arrow from a bowstring, flashing with cold brilliance before appearing instantly before the black dragon.

"Foolish. Though I now have only a head, you're far too weak to shake me!" Nidhogg the Black Dragon let out an angry roar.

Alice's graceful figure danced in the cold wind, becoming a conductor of "ice and snow." She perfectly inherited Crody's Great Snow Mountain swordsmanship, and with the first form—"Sword Control"—she wielded it effortlessly.

Wherever the tip of her light-infused blade Song of Light reached, wind and snow trailed faithfully, conjuring countless razor-sharp ice swords that gleamed with crystalline cold radiance, shrouding the space above and enveloping the black dragon's head.

Alice's figure was enchanting; though clad in battle armor, she resembled a valkyrie, radiating heroic spirit. She spun in midair, executing several fierce sword arcs!

The sky-full of ice swords responded in unison, revolving around their master to form a torrential river of swords of overwhelming momentum, the surging current carrying an almost death-dealing aura.

The ice sword torrent struck from all directions, launching a simultaneous assault on Nidhogg the Black Dragon. The dense sounds of cleaving air were enough to throw any foe into disarray.

"Amusing swordsmanship, but useless!"

Nidhogg the Black Dragon's eyes shifted. Despite his head being severed and immobile, he still retained some of his ancient god prowess.

The temperature around him surged instantly, causing the surrounding rock walls to begin melting. He slightly opened his jaws and exhaled a foul breath, scattering the dust about him.

Every speck of black flame grew upon contact with wind, and within blinks of an eye a wall of flames centered on the black dragon formed, perfectly enclosing his defenses within.

The surging sword torrent rushed forward, piercing madly into the black flame wall, only to be melted away completely in moments—like a clay figurine sinking into the sea, vanishing without a trace!

The fire wall immediately shifted, gradually converging into a single point before erupting with a scorching black flame ray that swept toward Alice in the sky!

Alice's heart lurched. Swiftly she executed the second form of the Great Snow Mountain swordsmanship, "Mountain Shaker"—before the black flame ray struck, an enormous iceberg condensed beneath her feet.

Rumbling like thunder, the iceberg crashed down like a meteor. Its presence caused the temperature to plummet once more; normally, enemies would grow sluggish and their bodies slowly corroded by the cold poison.

But Nidhogg the Black Dragon was entirely unaffected. The black flame ray swept past and pierced through the magnificent iceberg on the spot—the gap in power was starkly clear!

The iceberg struck by the black flame erupted in thick steam that billowed overhead, refusing to dissipate. Alice's figure vanished from sight.

"Hmph, no matter how you resist, you cannot change your fate of becoming my sacrifice." Nidhogg the Black Dragon sneered.

Suddenly, an inexplicable sacred power brewed within the thick steam. Alice, instead of retreating, charged forward—bursting from the steam, she wielded Song of Light and dove from the sky toward the black dragon.

All of her pseudo-divine magic power and fighting aura were instantly drawn out and concentrated upon the blade in her hands—the Great Snow Mountain swordsmanship's strongest technique, the third form—"Heaven Splitting!"

Following behind Alice were countless heroic warriors gleaming with sacred light—the Legion of the Holy Spirit descended from the sky alongside the wielder of Song of Light, launching a fearless charge—

"Nidhogg! Your death has come!"

(I posted this image before—if you haven't seen it, you probably skimmed past it. Flip back and you'll find it.)

title: Chapter 38 — Father and Son (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 38 — Father and Son (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 33 · Chapter 38

Alice descended like a deity, wishing to inflict the cruelest punishment upon her foes; her whole body bathed in the light emanating from her, and wherever she passed almost turned into eternal frozen ground.
This was not merely the third form of the Great Snow Mountain Sword Technique, but a finishing move infused with traces of divine power, further bolstered by the artifact.
Behind her, the valiant Holy Spirit Legion surged forth in mighty numbers, assisting the user of the Radiant Chant in clearing all obstacles; their charge was unstoppable.
The dark, deep river cavern seemed as if the gates of heaven had been opened; holy light and icy cold wind merged together, and the overwhelming pressure caused the entire canyon to tremble.
Alice had once relied on this very move, together with Mesfield, to crush the army that Mara was proud of, and she had full confidence in the power of the artifact.
The black dragon Nidhogg lying on the ground twitched its eyelids wildly; facing such an attack, it even felt a hint of fear.
If it were in its prime form, it would naturally not be afraid, but now it is different—it has sensed the approaching danger.
Amidst the shining light, Alice led countless holy spirit souls descending from the heavens, like a tiger coming down the mountain, unstoppable; the sharp blade in her hand truly sliced through space.
The black dragon Nidhogg inhaled sharply, strained to lift its head, and split open its blood‑filled maw, where a tiny black flame flickered.
In the next instant, scorching black flame spewed from the dragon’s mouth, launching a full‑force assault at Alice hovering in the sky.
This was the true black dragon breath; its power far surpassed Alfonso’s, the thick black flame breath resembling a pillar holding up the sky, with crimson lava flowing everywhere on the rock walls and ground.
"Shout!" Alice did not retreat her brows; instead she exerted all her strength to resist the dragon’s breath, determined to decide the victor with the enemy.
Boom—two mighty forces collided violently in mid‑air, entering a brief stalemate; the shockwave of the opposing explosion nearly caused the cavern to collapse!
Cold and scorching heat, two completely different forces, appeared in the cavern together, creating two utterly contrasting scenes in the same place.
Supported by the holy spirits, Alice’s blade continually tore apart the flames spewing from the dragon’s breath, drawing ever closer to Nidhogg.
Suddenly Nidhogg’s eyes widened in fury; the power of its breath surged, increasing tenfold, and the flames engulfed Alice.
This was pure force suppressing the enemy; despite Alice’s many buffs, there remained a certain gap to defeat the crippled black dragon.
The myriad holy spirits instantly vanished without a trace; Alice endured the burning pain, her body smoking black as she fell from the sky, and her sturdy Dragon Warrior battle armor showed many cracks.
"Useless resistance," the black dragon Nidhogg slowly closed its maw, its eyes filled with disdain, thinking itself a mighty ancient god, yet still being ridden by the weakest of ancient gods?
Alice hit the ground with a "thud," suffering burns all over; worse, she could not muster any strength at all, like a sick tiger—sharp fangs but no power to lunge at the foe.
This is the side effect of the finishing move: the third form of the Great Snow Mountain Sword Technique, "Opening Heaven," rapidly drains the user’s strength, concentrating it into the weapon.
Although the sword technique is extremely powerful and normally used as a final move to end an enemy’s life, its side effect is equally obvious.
It is a somewhat "gamble"-like sword skill; betting one’s life often yields miraculous results, but if it fails, the user ends up as meat on the enemy’s chopping block.
Alice failed to slay the black dragon, thus suffering the backlash of the sword technique; she knows how perilous it is when her magic and battle qi are nearly exhausted.
Her breathing grew short, her armor felt extraordinarily heavy; without the armor’s protection, she might have perished in the dragon’s breath just moments ago.
Alice pondered how to survive this crisis; she could barely stand, but could no longer use any magic or martial arts—how could she fight the black dragon? Perhaps she could only die here.
"Disappear, Maria; I only need your soul," the black dragon Nidhogg declared, condensing a fireball and hurling it mercilessly at Alice, intending to deliver a fatal blow.
Alice helplessly closed her eyes, seeming to accept her fate; the "Angelei" ring on her hand was useless—even if she stood up again, what good would it do? She would still be killed again by the black dragon.
Boom! A violent explosion rang out; black flames swept into the sky, scorching everything in the cavern; Alice, struck by this blow, would surely be unable to withstand it.
In the blaze of the black flame, Alice would turn to ash; her soul, with nowhere to go, would leave her body and, before entering hell, be swallowed into the dragon’s belly.
But suddenly, the black dragon Nidhogg grew uneasy, sensing that besides itself and Alice, a third power existed; it let out an angry low growl—
"Huh? Whose is this familiar pressure? Who dares to ruin my fun?"
The thick black flame dissipated, revealing Alice’s figure; she was not dead, but unharmed, half‑crouched on the ground, breathing wearily, utterly unaware of what had happened.
Before Alice appeared a brilliant, radiant barrier of light; it successfully protected her and blocked the dragon’s final attack.
Alice opened her eyes dazedly, looking at the light barrier, wondering in her heart who had saved her.
"It's you! It's really you, Alfad!" the black dragon Nidhogg roared hysterically, its large eyes brimming with hatred.
A colossal dragon phantom appeared behind Alice; its light wings could dispel evil spirits, its posture graceful and gaze gentle—it was the master of the Ancestral Dragon Temple, the remnant soul of the White Dragon Alfad.
Alfad’s soul cannot leave the Ancestral Dragon Temple; the phantom behind Alice is actually a trace of divine thought he had planted in her earlier, which was awakened upon sensing the dragon’s aura.
Upon seeing Alice, Alfad faintly believed that this petite human would put an end to the dragon race’s age‑old destiny, so he had left a trace of divine thought in her, hoping to obtain the place where the black dragon would be slain.
Especially after Alfad realized Alice was connected to the ancient human gods, he came to regard her as exceptionally special and was willing to stake some chips on her.
The White Dragon Alfad slowly opened his eyes, seeing only a black dragon’s head remaining; he was very calm, resembling the miserable appearance of a "father," and he had long known this.
"Long time no see, dear father; I’m glad you still remember me."
Alice lifted her gaze to the beautiful form of the White Dragon, her eyes full of doubt and astonishment; she was at a loss and asked—
"Alfad?!"
"Why have you appeared here??"

title: Chapter 39 — Alice: Come, let me buff you
content:
Chapter 39 — Alice: Come, let me buff you

Volume 33 · Chapter 39

White Dragon Alphad slightly lowered his head, his eyes showing a hint of kindness, “Nice to see you again, beautiful human lady, your strength has skyrocketed You can already glimpse some divine power, congratulations ." "? ? ?“Alice looked puzzled, if I remember correctly, Alphad shouldn't be able to leave the Ancestral Dragon Sanctuary at will. “I cannot leave the Ancestral Dragon Sanctuary, nor can I truly appear before you; this is merely a phantom formed by divine thought. From the moment you left the Ancestral Dragon Sanctuary, my divine thought has been lurking within you, and when you find the black dragon, it will be triggered. White Dragon Alphad gave a brief explanation, he merely felt that Alice was different, possessing extraordinary potential. The dragon clan actively entrusted its legacy and hope to humanity, and Alice is the first in history to do so. As the clan chief of the dragon race, Alphad is willing to stake his chips on Alice, to make a grand gamble. "Divine thought? What exactly are you planning?“Alice asked in surprise, thinking that her life might be monitored, she felt a chill run down her spine! "I want to help you defeat the black dragon, lend you the divine power I, I mean the power left by Alphad.“White Dragon paused, his phantom swaying, this state cannot last long,“Our dragon race is the bloodline created by Nidhogg; no one understands it better than we do. To defeat our father? We are indispensable. You are the sole human who has inherited the dragon clan’s mission; I am willing to place all my chips on you, regarding you as my closest kin. Alice hesitated, but the situation before her left no room for refusal,“Then what must I do?“ “The current Nidhogg is not fearsome; its body has been drained of all value by the demon prophets, producing countless dragon warriors to fight the ancient gods, leaving only a feeble head. Killing him is not as difficult as you imagine. “Ah? ? ?“Alice became a bit flustered, thinking even if only a head remains, where is the weakness? Clearly it’s utterly strong! “The power left by Alphad is enough to utterly destroy Nidhogg’s head; listen closely to what follows.“White Dragon narrowed his eyes, communicating secretly via divine thought,“I will imbue this mighty power onto your sword blade; as long as you can pierce Nidhogg’s body with it, you will thereby rend its soul. Opportunity comes only once; before the enchantment expires, seize it well.” “After Alice listened silently, she instinctively gripped her slender sword tighter; although she can no longer use martial arts or magic, her body can still move somewhat; if she strikes the black dragon, she can gain victory through Alphad’s power! “Alphad!!!“The black dragon Nidhogg roared hysterically, furious to the point of losing control,“You treacherous wretch! I regarded you as my most trusted confidant, yet you abandon me in my hour of need and even seek to harm me—why treat me thus?! Why?!” “We are all dragon offspring you created with your own hands, yet you never thought to treat us kindly, only knowing to ruthlessly exploit our worth to satisfy your filthy desires; the clansmen have all contemplated rebellion, and the demon prophet is merely a spark that ignited a powder keg.“White Dragon Alphad, merely the black dragon’s eyes, spoke solemnly,“We wish to break free from your bonds and obtain the freedom to decide our own fate.“ “Hahaha, what a ridiculous excuse, Alphad—this is merely your ambition, wanting to take my place and become an exploiter like me!“The black dragon Nidhogg sneered. “Alphad indeed harbors similar thoughts, but unlike you, he is far more merciful.“White Dragon replied in an observer’s tone. “A bunch of hollow righteous nonsense!“The black dragon Nidhogg growled, threateningly asking,“You truly don’t believe you can kill me and replace me, do you?““Slaying you is the mission of all dragonkind; as long as you live, we can never rest in peace.“White Dragon Alphad answered. “Just relying on her?“The black dragon Nidhogg glanced at the tiny Alice, clearly contemptuous. “Exactly.“White Dragon affirmed,“Even if we fail, we will have learned your position, and the dragon offspring will come wave after wave to assault you until you are utterly slain, then they will cease; given your current state, you probably cannot leave this place, right?“ “Your wish will never come true, Alphad! I will devour her, restore my lost form, and then eradicate all of you traitors!“The black dragon Nidhogg, emotions heightened, unleashed the most vicious curse,“I will never forgive you; I who created you with my own hands can also destroy you with my own hands—wait for me!“ White Dragon Alphad ignored him, instead leaving his final words,“It’s up to you, beautiful human lady; only you can succeed in killing it, I have no doubt.” As his voice faded, the white dragon’s phantom dissipated into specks of starlight, seemingly leaving nothing behind? Yet Alice stared wide‑eyed in shock; terrifying divine power surged from her holy chant in her hand—evidently the enchantment had already been completed subtly! All of this was done so secretly that the black dragon noticed nothing; he remained unaware that Alice’s slender sword had already become the instrument capable of ending his life! Alice understood implicitly, acting naturally; if the black dragon saw through her ruse, he would likely become wary, leaving no chance to approach him. The power left by Alphad lay hidden in the deepest part of the holy chant; only Alice could clearly sense its presence, and the scales of victory tipped once more. “Did you run away?“The black dragon Nidhogg gazed at Alice, lightly saying,“You are merely a pawn used by them, abandoned here—how pitiful.“ Alice shed the heavy dragon‑combat armor weighing her down, lightening her body, and gritting her teeth launched a frontal charge at the black dragon! Without the power’s boost, Alice could only fight like an ordinary person; in the black dragon’s eyes she seemed like a simpleton, utterly harmless. “Have you given up? Charging in with a hundred flaws is just suicide.“ The black dragon Nidhogg snorted disdainfully, regarding Alice as a defenseless lamb, and casually summoned a black fireball that blasted toward her. Alice’s heart leapt; she tried desperately to dodge, but in her current state it was impossible—without magic or battle aura, her movement slowed to a crawl! Boom! The black fireball exploded, flames rising incessantly! Alice cried out in pain as part of her body suffered severe injury, yet fortunately she was not killed; her slender sword was also flung away, blown by the explosion’s shockwave high into the air. Charred burns covered her body; Alice gritted her teeth and pressed on, her vision beginning to blur, wanting to stab the black dragon—almost impossible—she couldn’t help but pray inwardly— Damn! Can’t I even do this with my current body? Please, even if I could just nick it once! “Foolish creature, become my offering willingly; my time is short, if I don’t quickly restore my form, those traitors will surely come knocking.“ The black dragon Nidhogg focused entirely on Alice, opening his blood‑filled maw, extending his foul‑smelling tongue, scooping up the offering from the ground and slowly drawing it into his mouth—— Suddenly, a cracking sound rang out as the shattered air vibrated; the flung‑away slender sword, the holy chant, fell down and pierced precisely into the black dragon’s right eye!

title: Chapter 40 — Encroachment
content:
Chapter 40 — Encroachment

Volume 33 · Chapter 40

"!!?"

Black dragon Nidhogg felt a sharp sting in his right eye, a wave of astonishment rising in his heart. He never thought something so absurd would happen to himself.

Even Alice widened her eyes in bewilderment, looking completely confused. The fine sword, Bright Chanson, had been blown away by an explosion and, after falling, had precisely pierced the black dragon's eye. What kind of luck was this?

Even if Bright Chanson had struck the scales on the black dragon's body, it couldn't have done the slightest harm to it. But instead, it had somehow hit its most vulnerable eye!

The black dragon hadn't yet realized the severity of the situation. He didn't think an eye wound would be fatal and continued to curse carelessly.

"It seems my luck isn't great today. I even got sand in my eye."

Before the words had even finished leaving his mouth, the enchanted Bright Chanson began to display its lethal power. The white dragon's divine power concealed within ferociously damaged the black dragon's skull, and it even started to devour his fragile soul!

The excruciating pain made the black dragon shudder violently, his facial scales bristling upward. Under the devastation of the white dragon's divine power, he desperately wanted to remove the fine sword embedded in his right eye as quickly as possible, otherwise, before he could devour Alice, he might lose his own life first!

"What is this?! Alpha! What did you do?! How could you collude with an outsider to harm me!"

Black dragon Nidhogg became frenzied, roaring angrily up at the heavens, constantly wriggling his head, hoping to temporarily relieve the pain of his soul being devoured.

The Bright Chanson piercing the black dragon's right eye was clearly not deep enough to instantly end its life. Given enough time, it should still be possible to force the fine sword out from the right eye!

Seeing the black dragon being tortured to death, Alice realized her opportunity had come. Seizing the chance, she broke free from Nidhogg's restraint. After regaining her freedom of movement, she didn't flee at all. Instead, she bravely leaped up, climbed onto the top of the black dragon's head, stepped on the sharp and pointed dragon scales, and ran with all her strength toward Nidhogg's right eye!

The black dragon's remaining left eye rolled wildly around. Seeing Alice's actions, he roared loudly, "Don't even think about it! You want to kill me with just yourself!?"

"That's right! That's exactly what I'm thinking!"

Alice suppressed her exhaustion. At a moment like this, she couldn't afford the slightest negligence. Between her and the black dragon, only one of them could leave the cave alive. Either she would become a sacrifice, or the black dragon would recover to its full strength and bring catastrophic disaster to the outside world!

"Darn! You're nothing but someone who can only cling to others..."

Black dragon Nidhogg gritted his teeth, looking down on Maria with utter contempt from the bottom of his heart. He couldn't tolerate such a lowly weakling bouncing around on his head.

So the black dragon凭空 conjured a black flame ball, laced with terrifying divine power, and blasted it straight at Alice on top of his head, intending to burn her alive with the black flames!

Alice currently had no way to make any defense. Her magic power and fighting aura were both completely exhausted. She could only respond in the state of an ordinary person.

The scorching hot black flame ball came thundering toward her. Alice's hair tips had already been ignited by the extreme heat. A trace of despair flashed through her eyes—she simply couldn't avoid it.

But at this critical moment, the white dragon Alpha's barrier appeared once again, surrounding Alice and protecting her!

"Alpha!!!"

The black dragon Nidhogg let out a hysterical scream, already driven mad with rage by his own "son." "I will eliminate every single traitor starting with you!"

The black flame ball collided violently with the radiant barrier. Already weakened from withstanding two previous attacks, the barrier couldn't possibly defend against the black dragon's flames. In less than two seconds, it was blasted to pieces!

But Alpha's radiant barrier had bought Alice precious time to escape. She could be seen leaping with all her strength, flipping through the air above the black dragon's right eye—

Alice saw her own reflection in the black dragon's grotesque eye, as well as the fine sword Bright Chanson piercing straight into the center of its sharp pupil, with the hilt and half the blade protruding outside.

Time seemed to have fallen into a sluggish standstill. Every breath felt like it stretched across several hours. Both sides' spirits were stretched to their absolute limits!

Alice seized this long-awaited opportunity and, using all her strength, stomped downward with everything she had. One foot landed on the hilt of Bright Chanson, and with a "splash," she drove the complete blade deep into the black dragon's right eye!

"I won!"

Silence. An unsettling silence.

The black dragon Nidhogg suddenly grew much quieter, his entire head frozen rigid in place, as if his soul had been lost.

Boom! The white dragon's divine power finally erupted completely, piercing through the black dragon's head. Brilliant light gushed from all seven of his orifices!

No agonizing screams, no vicious curses, and not even a trace of regret. Everything appeared so calm.

Black dragon Nidhogg slowly lowered his proud head and lay motionless on the ground. His life was fleeing at a speed visible to the naked eye.

The white dragon's divine power concealed deep within the fine sword Bright Chanson had successfully devoured his soul. All that remained was a hollow shell, and his consciousness was about to vanish entirely.

Alice retrieved the fine sword, still deeply embedded in the black dragon's right eye, and landed on the ground. She still dared not relax her vigilance, staring dead at every move the black dragon made.

She was terribly afraid the black dragon would raise its head again. If that happened, she truly would have no options left and could only obediently stand there and wait to die!

She stared for a very long time before she could believe the creator of this dragon race had died. Only then could she finally catch her breath—

She looked at her trembling hands that wouldn't stop shaking, barely able to grip the sword anymore. Her body went completely limp, and she dropped to her knees on the spot, gasping for air in huge mouthfuls. Cold sweat poured from her pores like tap water, gushing down relentlessly.

The black dragon Nidhogg was the strongest enemy Alice had ever faced besides Merlin. The difficulty level was beyond her wildest imagination. Without the assistance of the white dragon Alpha, she really wouldn't have been able to win.

"Is that so? So that's how it is? I never expected things to turn out this..."

"Ugh!"

Alice heard the black dragon's dying voice, and her body instantly felt as if struck by lightning, freezing stiff on the spot.

By all rights, Alpha had no reason to deceive her. The black dragon had suffered devastating injuries and should absolutely be dead. Why could it still speak?!

Alice twisted her neck like a wooden puppet and glanced at the black dragon's head lying on the ground beside her. She discovered its severely injured right eye had already rotted away, yet it was still staring at her!

"Look at your pathetic state. Just like a cowardly rat. I can't believe Alpha would choose to place his chips on you? But I have to admit, this time it won the gamble." The black dragon Nidhogg paused, his tone exceedingly calm, as if he no longer had the ability to launch any attacks.

"It seems I was mistaken. You're not Maria. Her eyes could never be as innocent as yours."

"A fine sword accidentally blown away could precisely pierce my right eye. Not many people possess this kind of luck."

"I already know who you are."

"Can't take it anymore, I really want to make a joke, 2333!"

Black dragon: You're Lightning Gabaa!

title: Chapter 41 — Never-Extinguishing Black Flame (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 41 — Never-Extinguishing Black Flame (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 33 · Chapter 41

The dying black dragon Nidhogg looked straight at Alice, yet slowly closed its eyes. "Forget it, who you are no longer matters. My existence is about to vanish from this world completely—"

Alice listened to the black dragon's words half-believing, half-doubting, unable to determine whether it was deliberately lying to make her let down her guard.

She gripped the slender sword in her hand tightly, putting on an act as though she were ready to strike the black dragon at any moment.

But Alice knew perfectly well herself that this was merely pretense. The enchantment from the white dragon Alfar had already faded.

"I never imagined I would die at your hands. I have experienced only four defeats in my life. The first was against Odin, the King of Gods. The second was against Vedrfolnir, the phoenix dwelling at the summit of Yggdrasil. The third was against a demon prophet of mysterious origins. And the last—no, to be precise, I lost to my own son Alfar. This is an unforgivable shame to me, a stain upon the glory I have borne throughout my life. I can accept defeat by a true strong warrior, but I cannot be felled by a mere weakling—"

Alice could no longer make sense of what the black dragon was muttering to itself. Secretly, she checked her own condition. Her mana and combat aura had recovered slightly. She hesitated about whether to continue attacking the black dragon.

"I will make an exception and give you one chance. Run. The faster, the better." Black dragon Nidhogg's breathing grew weaker and weaker as it spoke to itself. "I will detonate my own body, and everything in the surroundings will be destroyed by me. This place will soon be shrouded in my flames, which will never extinguish."

Alice subconsciously took a step back, finding it hard to believe what the black dragon said and suspecting a trap.

"What are you hesitating for? Are you suspicious of my words? Then I can't be blamed. Dragging you along to die alongside me doesn't sound like a bad idea either."

The moment the black dragon finished speaking, the black flame reignited across its entire head pressed against the ground. This black flame was different from before—its temperature and oppressive force were far stronger, and it continued to expand relentlessly!

Alice finally realized the black dragon had not been lying. With no other choice in the emergency, she turned around and broke into a sprint toward the cave exit. She did not doubt for a moment that even a slight delay would see her devoured by the swelling black flame.

The black dragon had abandoned all its obsessions, choosing self-detonation to end its own life. In the future, perhaps only this land of unextinguishable black flame would serve as proof that it had once existed.

"Yes! Run! Let me enjoy one final look at your wretched figure. That is how a weakling ought to react! I'm sorry I deceived you. Actually, even if you run as fast as you can, you still cannot escape my flames. Stay behind and keep me company in death! Mwahahaha!"

Alice ran frantically toward the cave exit, yet she could still feel the constantly expanding black flame power behind her. This entire canyon would likely be destroyed in an instant!

Rumble rumble rumble—

Just as the black dragon had said, it gave Alice no opportunity to escape, instantly detonating its remaining skull and unleashing a terrifying massive explosion!

Black flames radiated a suffocating aura of despair, devouring a vast expanse of land in the blink of an eye. The deep cave also began to collapse along with it!

Alice was once again thrust into a desperate situation by the black dragon. Terrifying shockwaves, carrying black flame in their wake, pursued her relentlessly from behind, far faster than her own speed.

This was Nidhogg's final strength, so naturally it had no lingering concerns whatsoever. It simply wanted to drag some unfortunate souls along before dying, which is why its assault became exceptionally vicious!

Alice's brows knitted tightly, a bead of cold sweat sliding down her forehead. There was still quite a distance to the cave exit. She feared she would be swallowed by the explosion before she could escape the cave at all!

What should she do? I'm wearing Anjel's [ring]—it seems I could survive this catastrophe. But based on what the black dragon just said, the black flame will completely devour everything here and never extinguish?

That makes things troublesome. If I can rely on "Anjel" to awaken just once, but I'm still trapped inside the unextinguishable black flame, it seems completely useless!

I must completely escape this explosion zone, but there's simply no time!

Alice clenched her teeth and sped up as much as possible, yet the little mana and combat aura she had barely recovered was entirely insufficient to support her escape.

The exploding black flame was drawing closer and closer, already nipping at Alice's heels, about to swallow her up like a ravenous beast!

"The ultimate extreme of cold is not these furs. When your power reaches a certain level, you can even freeze time and space."

At this critical moment, Alice suddenly remembered words the white dragon Alfar had once spoken—secret techniques regarding the manipulation of law-level power.

What was the ultimate extreme of cold? To say it could merely make one feel cold was far too shallow. The ultimate extreme of cold had far more versatile applications; it could even freeze the ethereal and ephemeral time and space.

Alice did not understand the words the white dragon Alfar had said, always feeling that the other was hinting at some important secret, yet unable to grasp the crux of it.

"The ultimate extreme of cold, the ultimate extreme of cold—what exactly is it?! What do I need to do?!"

Alice had been driven to incoherence by anxiety. The black flame behind her was already burning her boots, leaving her no more time to ponder.

It was all because she had entered the pseudo-divine境界 far too briefly, still understanding nothing, with no responsible teacher to guide her step by step.

The black flame pressing closer and closer swelled upward, letting out阵阵 death-dealing roars, lunging fiercely at Alice!

In desperation, Alice tightly shut her eyes. A bead of cold sweat slipped down her cheek. Without a second thought, she activated the power that transcended mana and combat aura—Divine Power—

"Stop!!!"

With that utterance, an inexplicable and extreme coldness spread outward from Alice as its center. When she opened her eyes again, the world had seemingly transformed, becoming a frozen domain shrouded in bitter cold.

Alice gazed blankly at the scene before her. She had no idea at all how she had managed it—she had muddled her way out of danger.

The surrounding walls, the stones splattered on the ground, the exploding black flame rising upward, and even the corpse fragments of the black dragon's skull after its self-detonation were all wrapped in crystal-clear ice, motionless!

It looked like a dead, lifeless realm of silence. Alice had become the only living being here. There was only ice and snow in this place, and time and space no longer flowed.

Alice had thought Divine Power had completely frozen this area. But right before her eyes, that single bead of cold sweat she had just shed had also crystallized into an ice bead. When she gently touched it, it immediately returned to its original position, unable to move freely.

No way? Has time—has time really stopped? This is the power of the law of the ultimate extreme of cold—

Alice spoke to herself in an incredulous tone. Though she dared not believe what she was seeing with her own eyes, it seemed that time had indeed come to a halt. The roaring black flame behind her had lost all of its intimidating power.

滴答. The frozen, suspended cold sweat had somehow recovered, splashing onto Alice's feet. She looked down in astonishment, but before she could process what was happening, a string of changes descended upon her!

Crack crack crack—

The frozen, dead world was rapidly shattering. Those black flames became active again. The paused explosion seemed unaffected and continued its destruction, meaning that time had begun to flow once more.

Alice's heart jolted with alarm. She turned around and continued sprinting toward the cave exit, the black flame behind her roaring in relentless pursuit—

Freezing the world lasts far shorter than I had imagined!

As expected, my current strength still cannot be flexibly utilized?

title: Chapter 42 — Escape
content:
Chapter 42 — Escape

Volume 33 · Chapter 42

Outside the canyon, the royal guard knight Vival led an elite army of 150,000 in a frontal clash against the dragons created by the black dragon. After a brief engagement, although the soldiers suffered heavy casualties, they had not been completely crushed by the dragons, and the battle settled into a tense stalemate.

These dragons, born from the black dragon's blood, lacked the strong defensive scales; despite their decent combat power, they would still be turned into pincushions by arrows under the soldiers' siege.

Dozens of soldiers frantically operated the magic cannons, a powerful war tool far superior to arrows, but their aim was poor, and the dragons soaring in the sky were more agile than they had imagined.

The scaleless dragons were entirely blood‑red, their skin as delicate as a newborn's, appearing quite fragile. Yet the flames they spewed from their mouths were utterly unlike their appearance, their destructive power not to be underestimated. Each dragon breath swept across the battlefield, instantly burying hundreds of well‑equipped soldiers in a sea of fire.

Boom— the magic cannon fired, a fierce tongue of flame bursting from the muzzle, the powerful recoil kicking up thick dust on the ground. Although the dragons moved agilely, they still had to watch for the soldiers' arrows and could not completely evade the cannon's attacks. One poisoned dragon twisted in midair to dodge, yet was pierced through its membrane wing by the cannon fire, losing balance and plummeting from the sky. With shouts of killing, the soldiers hiding on the ground surged forward, using their swords to rip open the dragon's belly. Even as it died, the dragon was unwilling, its breath sweeping along the ground in a frenzy, instantly turning many soldiers into casualties. The two sides were locked in a bloody melee; even if a hundred soldiers could barely pile up to kill one dragon, they gained no advantage.

Vival, mounted on his horse, looked grim; he realized that continuing like this would be highly unfavorable—the dragons were numerous and held a great advantage. Before all the dragons could be wiped out, a force of fifty thousand elite troops might be exhausted, which was not the outcome he wanted. Vival sought reinforcements; the nearest garrison surely had stationed troops, and calculating the time, it would take about a day and night to arrive—clearly too late.

A dragon in the sky noticed Vival, who was dazed on his horse, circled a few times, then suddenly dove down, its bloody maw wide enough to swallow both man and horse. Vival snapped back to attention, his brows furrowed; he seized the moment, leapt from his horse's back, and with his sword drew a cold arc, severing the dragon's head. The headless dragon's corpse rolled on the ground, twitching incessantly, its blood spraying like a fountain and staining the barren earth red.

Vival slowly rose to his feet, gazing toward the nearby canyon, his mind turning to how to break the current crisis—Why hasn't Princess Diane returned? She must have encountered some danger! Alfonso was indeed not lying in his diary; that ancient black dragon is hiding nearby. Perhaps Princess Diane has already met it at the bottom of the valley; I must bring people to support her. Vival's head ached—he was being held back by these dragons, unable to leave, making it unrealistic to go to the valley's bottom to aid Alice.

A soldier dressed as a staff officer ran over, his face worried, and said, "Lord Vival, we should temporarily withdraw and request reinforcements from the garrison of the nearby town; the number of evil dragons exceeds our expectations, and if we continue we may die here."

"Are you afraid of death?" Vival demanded sternly.

"No," the staff soldier replied, sweating coldly, explaining, "We are all warriors loyal to His Majesty Amadio; if we all die here, would His Majesty's position in the court be affected?"

Vival fell silent, unable to deny that this was indeed a possibility; the army now fighting were all His Majesty Amadio's foundation, and if they were exhausted, it might arouse the ambitions of certain nobles. A king's authority needs military backing; a ruler lacking strength can easily be replaced by those wielding heavy arms—a very realistic problem. Although the court had just undergone the "Great Purge" not long ago, making the nobles more obedient than before, they might not truly be willing to be commanded and summoned by a mere ten‑year‑old child.

Vival couldn't help but feel inclined to retreat, but Alice had not yet returned; if he left now, he would still have no way to explain himself to His Majesty Amadio upon his return.

Just as Vival was torn between options, a thunderous explosion rang out across the sky and the ground beneath his feet shook violently—What was that? An earthquake? Vival and some soldiers stumbled, unsure why such a startling blast had suddenly sounded, feeling as if it came from underground.

The dragons soaring in the sky burst apart one after another, forming brilliant, bloody fireworks that vanished without a trace. They were direct servants spawned from the black dragon's blood; after Nidhogg's self‑destruction, they naturally could not survive.

"Alert! Alert!!!" Vival shouted loudly; the scattered soldiers regrouped, forming a flawless defensive line.

Although the dragon threat had disappeared, the violent earthquake left everyone feeling uneasy, forcing them to stay on high alert.

Not far off in the canyon's depths, a pitch‑black light flared up, followed by a demonic eruption of black fire! Torrents of black flame blazed, writhing their scorching forms, fiercely burning the canyon until even the distant horizon was completely engulfed in fire.

The ground beneath their feet slowly melted, flowing lava rolling like waves; every soldier felt as if they stood at the heart of a furnace, their armor growing ever hotter.

Vival, you see the terrifying black flame spreading toward the sky, bloody red filling the horizon. In the scorching black flame, a strange glint of cold light suddenly appeared; Alice gritted her teeth and charged through the layers of flame, her steel wings roaring like an engine. She used "Time Stop" to gain a chance to escape, successfully fleeing the explosion's center and returning to the safe zone. Her dragon warrior armor indeed helped greatly, resisting much of the black flame's scorching. Just as Alice escaped, her dragon warrior armor could not hold, melting away into streams of ice and snow that vanished. Having lost her flight ability, Alice plummeted from high altitude onto the scorching ground; she lay there motionless, obviously her strength had been exhausted for a long time.

Vival, accompanied by the soldiers, rushed over and helped Alice up, calling, "Alice! Alice!?"

In her dazed fatigue, Alice opened her eyes a slit, glanced at Vival, said nothing, and promptly fainted.

"Hey, are you alright?" Vival frowned, staring at the unending black flames before him, unable to comprehend what had happened.

"What exactly did she go through?"

title: Chapter 43 — Steel Vest
content:
Chapter 43 — Steel Vest

Volume 33 · Chapter 43

In the depths of the Ancestral Dragon Temple, the remnant of the White Dragon Alphard stood here, gazing into the distance, feeling that the Black Dragon Nidhogg had already disappeared. This proved it had guessed correctly, successfully fulfilling Alphard's last wish; Nidhogg's death meant the dragon race truly gained freedom. "It seems we have won; I indeed did not misjudge the person. To slay an ancient god like Nidhogg, we really had to resort to special means," said the White Dragon Alphard softly. "Is it over? It feels unreal. Have we truly freed ourselves from the creators' influence?" The Blazing Flame Dragon King lowered his head, looking at his own hands as if in a dream. Slaying the black dragon is the mission of all dragonkind, yet humans accomplished it, which sounds utterly ironic. "No need to doubt, my child. You are not the first-generation dragonkin; your connection with Nidhogg has weakened, so not feeling its death is normal. Believe me, from this moment on, we have broken free of Nidhogg's shackles and have the right to control our own destiny," said the White Dragon Alphard in the tone of an elder. "It's a pity I couldn't be of much help," the Blazing Flame Dragon King paused, somewhat regretful. "I cannot understand why weak humans could defeat the black dragon. We clearly invested great effort, yet still failed, letting insignificant humans aid us—I cannot accept it, feeling deep shame." "Do not look down on any race, including humans. Arrogance is the poison leading to extinction; countless histories have fully proven this. Although human strength is far inferior to ours, they also possess advantages we lack," said the White Dragon Alphard, lowering his head to look at his successor. "To be precise, that girl is not truly a human in the ordinary sense; she is a member of the ancient gods' faction." "Could it be... could she truly be humanity's guardian deity, Maria?" the Blazing Flame Dragon King frowned, tangled in speech. "This is hard to believe. Now is the era of humans; Maria, as the chief god, why has she become so weak?" "It's not what you think. She is merely a slowly sprouting seed, possibly growing into a lovely flower like before, or possibly becoming something entirely different—this needs time to be tested," said the White Dragon Alphard, uttering an inscrutable remark, and admonished solemnly— "You need not know too much; this is not a good thing. Do not let yourself and the dragonkin be drawn into any conflict." "After I depart, you shall assume the role of chieftain, ensuring the dragonkin continue to propagate, not becoming dust vanished in history." "Although I am merely a lingering soul, this is Alphard's final wish lingering in my heart; I hope you can bear this responsibility." "I have wandered the world for a long time, seeing many seemingly powerful races march toward extinction. Aside from some ancient texts, no one remembers them." "Therefore I do not wish that after my departure, the dragonkin also walk the path to extinction—only a clan that continually adapts to change can thrive steadily." "Are you leaving?" asked the Blazing Flame Dragon King, astonished, obviously not yet prepared to inherit the chieftainship. "Indeed, I share a bloodline bond with Nidhogg; if it dies, I cannot continue to survive—this is unavoidable," said the White Dragon Alphard wearily, gently. "Alman, you and the holy dragon Igor symbolizing darkness are both our dragonkin's finest warriors. I hope you do not feel sorrow for my departure; instead, bless my passing, for death is a fortunate release for me." Upon hearing the name "Igor," the verification dragon warrior Alman's veins bulged, his anger barely contained. "Please do not mention that name; he is unworthy of being called a dragon warrior—he is a filthy traitor." "I know your relationship with Igor is poor, but he possesses the highest talent among dragonkin, undeniable; even his strength surpasses yours. It's only regrettable that on the path of pursuing power he lost himself; otherwise he would surely have become our pride. Nowadays the era is increasingly unsuitable for foreign races to survive; we should not continue to regard Igor as an enemy, but try to accept him," said the White Dragon Alphard earnestly. The Blazing Flame Dragon King remained silent, not denying that Alphard's suggestion from a broader perspective was excellent, yet he still could not accept a filthy traitor. "Alman, your shortcoming is a quick temper, which makes you lose reason; you need to restrain yourself, and at critical moments you may also seek aid from the Elf King Sindadil, whose wisdom can help you overcome difficulties; you should listen to his counsel more often," instructed the White Dragon Alphard regarding his afterwords. "I understand," replied the Blazing Flame Dragon King in a low voice. "Then it's entrusted to you—do not let me down, Alman." As his words fell, the souls of the White Dragon and the other great dragons within the temple instantly turned into specks of starlight, scattering away without a trace. In the dark Ancestral Dragon Temple, deathly silence reigned; only Alman stood alone there, flames flickering on his body. The unconscious Alice was escorted back to the palace, attended by a group of maidservants. Although her injuries were not light, under the treatment of several palace healers she began to gradually improve. Alice's main problem was exhaustion of power, which cannot be healed; she can only slowly rest and recover. After a full seven days, Alice slowly opened her eyes, unable to recall what she had experienced during the final escape. Upon waking, Alice saw her adorable daughter's head, struggling with big eyes fixed on her, seemingly not having left her side during this time. The little one, seeing her mother open her eyes, leapt with joy, thrusting her head into Alice's chest, "Mom!" "Cough!" Alice just woke up, her head still not clear, and immediately took her daughter's rocket-like headbutt, nearly choked by the saliva in her throat—this little one is a thoughtful cotton-padded jacket? Clearly it's spiked counterblade armor! "Mom! Mom! You finally woke up! I thought I'd go look for grandma and the others, they didn't want me, Mingming," little Chris's watery eyes like a reservoir, tears continuously spilling, obviously these seven days she had worried to the point of near breakdown. Seeing her daughter cry bitterly, Alice hurriedly endured the pain all over her body, sat up from the bed, picked up Chris to help wipe her tears, "Why are you crying? Mom isn't hurt, is she?" "It's all Mom's fault for not waking up; every day a crowd of people swirl around you, I don't even know how Mom is doing, and nobody wants to talk to me, just sniveling," little Chris pouted, feeling both aggrieved and upset, here nobody even wants to pay attention to a little brat, right?" A dense black line fell on Alice's forehead as she asked, "How long was Mom unconscious?" "I don't know either; I've been hiding in Mom's blanket all along, afraid bad people might approach," little Chris said with red-rimmed eyes. "What bad people could there be here? You're overthinking it," Alice sighed, thinking her daughter should rest well, not end up looking this exhausted. "No way!" little Chris immediately put on a stern face, pretending to be an adult, patting her nonexistent biceps— "Dad isn't around; Chris must take up responsibility and become Mom's guardian!" "Usually she's a thoughtful cotton-padded jacket, but at crucial moments she must become a steel little vest!" "Hmph!" 9("^")f

title: Chapter 44 — Dangerous Situation
content:
Chapter 44 — Dangerous Situation

Volume 33 · Chapter 44

Alice looked at her daughter putting on a "little adult" act, couldn't help laughing, "What ability do you have to protect Mom? Not causing trouble would already be good."
"Can't! Mom looks down on people!" Little Chris, not satisfied, waved her arms, like a pufferfish stimulated, her cheeks puffed up a round.
"At the very least, I can make those bad guys dare not easily approach Mom."
"Really?" Alice lifted her daughter, teasingly said, "You only know simple healing spells, right?"
"Who said that? I can also bite, like the flower of the landlady grandma's house." Chris opened her small mouth, showing her not-yet-grown baby teeth.
"Chewing a radish is already hard, yet you bite people?"
"Alright, don't deliberately put on this fierce look, Mom's fine." Alice held her daughter in her arms, gently touching her little head.
"Chris is afraid of losing Mom, will Mom abandon Chris like the grandmas and go to another world?" Little Chris's eyes turned red as she nuzzled into Mom's embrace.
"How could that be? You're thinking too much, Mom will never leave you, Mom swears." Alice looked lovingly at her daughter, thinking this might be the first time Chris has seen her injured self, she's still so young, these days she must be very uneasy, no wonder she's putting on a strong front.
"Mom, can we go home? Outside is too dangerous, maybe Dad is already waiting for us at home." Chris whispered in a tiny voice.
"Yeah, go home, we'll leave tomorrow."

Outside the room, Vival quietly closed the door, not wanting to disturb Alice and her daughter, lowered his voice to Amadeo beside him—
"Your Majesty, we came at a bad time; Miss Alice just woke up."
"Really, then forget it, don't disturb them." Amadeo said helplessly, he had wanted to check on Alice's condition, but since she's already awake, there should be no serious problem.
"Your Majesty, are you sure you don't want to go in? This might be the last—" Vival licked his dry lips, gritting his teeth, "the last chance to communicate with your sister."
Amadeo gave Vival a sharp glance, emphasizing, "She is not my sister."
"Although you're right, please forgive my meddling; regardless of whether you acknowledge it, blood ties cannot be severed. Your cold treatment of Princess Diana may not be a good thing."
Vival had been by Amadeo's side for a long time, knew this young king well, believed Amadeo had many things he wanted to say to Alice.
In a sense, Amadeo is indeed not the legitimate heir of the kingdom; he seized the throne from Alice through a series of means.
Vival knew Amadeo had been disliked by the old king since childhood, left his mother at a very young age, is extremely lacking in familial affection; suddenly a half-sister appeared, it's impossible for him not to have some fantasies.
"This is an internal royal matter, unrelated to you, so don't say these useless words." Amadeo said coldly.
"Do you really have nothing to say to her?" Vival's expression showed some disbelief.
"No, I've said everything I needed to say; I hope she never appears before me again, that would be good for everyone." Amadeo answered solemnly.
"Your Majesty, your vigilance is too extreme. During this period of contact, I believe Princess Diana poses no threat to you; she is not greedy, nor does she harbor grand ambitions, her gaze limited to what she sees." Vival paused, then continued sincerely, "Moreover, Princess Diana possesses considerable strength; she could become a powerful aid for the kingdom, have you really not considered keeping her?"
Amadeo's eyes darted, he fell silent for a long time, "What's the point of thinking about it? Her heart isn't on this land, but on someone."
"Are you referring to Princess Diana's husband?" Vival frowned, unable to stop fantasizing, "I'm curious what kind of person he is." However, their child is somewhat strange.
"Me? That little crybaby who only wails?" Amadeo slightly furrowed his brows.
"Yes, according to other palace healers, that child's healing spell outperforms theirs combined; originally the healers predicted Princess Diana would need over a month to recover, but now it only took seven days, which is truly astonishing." Vival pointed out the suspicious detail, noting that Chris seemed somewhat abnormal.
Amadeo stroked his chin, thought for a while, "It seems not only you, but I too am growing more curious about the man beside her."

In a mysterious place, darkness without a hint of sunlight; as if isolated from the world, a cage.
An old man, skinny as a bone, hunched over, holding a dim yellow oil lamp, heading to the darkest depths.
His temples streaked with white, a demonic horn on his head broken off, wearing tattered hemp clothes, walking as if constantly wriggling forward on the ground.
This demon is the last unseen official of the First Demon Lord Palace, one of the Seven Generals, named Abaddon, also the biological father of the chief maid Ophelia.
Abaddon is the strongest official in the First Demon Lord Palace; from a young age he served the first Lucifer Mephistopheles, later took charge of Vivian's life, and has always held the position of chief steward of the Demon Lord Palace.
After Vivian faked her death, Abaddon, as her absolutely loyal confidant, followed her out of the Demon Lord Palace, continuing to monitor all movements of the demon race, truthfully reporting external news to Vivian.
Abaddon brought the oil lamp to the deepest part, where he saw that noble female demon, the formidable woman who gives countless demons a headache, Vivian the Second, Lucifer.
Vivian had her back to Abaddon, twelve black wings folded behind her, facing the wall with eyes closed, deep in thought, making it hard to guess what she's thinking.
Abaddon gently placed the oil lamp on the ground, tidied his ragged clothes a bit, then slowly knelt before Vivian, "Your Majesty."
Hearing Abaddon's voice, Vivian slowly opened her ruby-like eyes, coldly asking, "Abaddon, any new news?"
Abaddon prostrated on the ground, lowered his head deeply, and truthfully reported the recent turmoil of the demon race—
"The demon realm has undergone a huge change; Behemoth is about to awaken, the situation is irreversible."
"Your Majesty, what you feared has already happened; we must take action."

title: Chapter 45 — Unexpected
content:
Chapter 45 — Unexpected

Volume 33 · Chapter 45

The prophet's predictions are obviously unavoidable; the content of the second prediction has already come to pass." Vivian sighed, having long been mentally prepared for what happened to the demon race, "Where exactly has Behemoth's soul taken refuge?"

"Just as you suspected back then, after Behemoth's soul escaped, it is most likely to have possessed the first demon Belial, and Belial probably lost control of his own body long ago." Abaddon guessed.

"Exactly as I thought; when I sensed that Behemoth's soul had fled the blood pool, I realized the prophet's second prediction had begun. At that time I suspected Belial, but as the sole surviving first demon, his prestige and seniority among demons are too deep; even if I voiced my suspicion, few monarchs would believe me. To prevent the demon race from falling under Behemoth's control, I had to fake my death, leave the Demon Lord Palace, abandon my children, and leave behind a spark of future resistance."

Vivian's icy expression flickered slightly; she obviously missed her two children dearly, but back then, forced by circumstances, she had to prioritize the greater good and make the right choice for the whole race.

The start of the prophet's second prediction means that if the ancestor of all demons, Behemoth, were to revive from the blood pool, it would bring an unimaginable disaster to the demon race.

However, at that time Vivian could not be certain that Behemoth could only possess first-generation demons; she even suspected that all demons, including monarchs, might become Behemoth's puppets.

Even if she had pointed her suspicion at Belial, she could not firmly hold that guess, because Belial, as the sole surviving first demon, was a comrade of her father Mephistopheles in the Holy War and holds immense significance for the entire demon race.

Without concrete evidence, most demons would not believe that Belial, the kindly elder who led the demon race through its darkest period, would become a puppet manipulated by Behemoth, the key to its resurrection.

During that time of internal and external troubles, only Vivian knew how perilous the demon race's situation was—like a lone person bearing immense pressure, participating in an unfair werewolf game where any fellow villager could be a savage werewolf, yet she had no way to single out the werewolf from the villagers, while the cunning werewolf could secretly stir in the darkness, gradually pushing all villagers toward a dangerous abyss.

Moreover, the Holy Church of Light was about to undergo the ceremony of passing the papacy from old to new, with many qualified papal successors frequently active, seeking more chips, they intensified their crusade against the demon race beyond before.

In this predicament surrounded by strong enemies, Vivian dared not publicize the fact that Behemoth's soul had slipped away, for it would cause fierce internal turmoil among the demons; the demons of the seven Demon Lord Palaces would fall into endless suspicion, unable to unite against the threat from the Holy Church, and if the demon race were destroyed by humans, the loss would be far greater than if destroyed by Behemoth.

After considering multiple aspects, Vivian firmly believed the prophet's predictions left behind; since Behemoth's resurrection cannot be stopped, it is better to prepare in advance for this disaster. She did two things:

First, she used the Gun Hero O'Brien's fake death to distance herself from the crisis-ridden demon interior, waiting for Behemoth to reveal herself, after which she would become a vital force against the enemy.

Second, she sought ways to drive her two children out of the Demon Lord Palace, away from the demon race's most dangerous vortex, so that even if Behemoth acted, it would hardly harm the siblings.

Especially Merlin, as the child foretold in the prophecy capable of slaying Behemoth, must not encounter any problems; ideally, before Behemoth voluntarily steps forward, he should never return to the demon race.

Although Vivian cannot be sure whether Behemoth knows the prophecy's content, this is already her utmost protection as a mother for her children; she does not wish to place the pressure of opposing Behemoth on her own children.

"Your Majesty, I know you deeply miss Merlin and Princess Lilith, but helping the entire demon race survive the crisis is more important; I'm sure the two princes will understand your hardship once they learn the truth." Abaddon spoke in a comforting tone.

"I hope so. After I left, they suffered greatly, and I feel guilty about it; perhaps from the very beginning I was not a qualified mother." Vivian said sorrowfully, lowering her voice, "Especially my son; back then I was not well versed in succubus power, and when I conceived Merlin there was a mistake, resulting in his demon bloodline being extremely thin after birth—he lacks even some demon traits—and he has received many cold stares from his peers since childhood, a responsibility I cannot shirk."

"You needn't dwell on it; Merlin's past discrimination is over. The demon race venerates strength, and thanks to the formidable power he displays as an adult, few demons dare to confront him directly." Abaddon lowered his head, recalling, "Merlin as a child was indeed as weak as a human; I once doubted whether he was truly your son. As it turns out, I was mistaken."

"Let's not talk about these matters now." Vivian set aside her sorrowful expression, shifted the topic, "Behemoth has revealed himself; what reactions do the other monarchs of the Demon Lord Palaces have?"

"It's a total rout. Behemoth is manipulating Belial's body, and during this Seven Kings Conference he used the Demon-Sealing Vessel, sealing all the monarchs inside." Abaddon reported truthfully.

"A bunch of fools, completely unreliable; they could never be my aid. However, the Demon-Sealing Vessel has already been used, which is good news for us—Behemoth has lost a powerful trump card, and I now have no lingering worries." Vivian paused, then said confidently, "It's time to bring my son back. According to the prophet's prediction, he is capable of defeating Behemoth. Where is he? Surely he's not still fooling around in the human realms?"

"That Merlin was also sealed inside the vessel." Abaddon said with a hint of embarrassment.

The atmosphere fell into silence, an oppressive quiet that made everyone uneasy, and after a long while—

"Why did this idiot go to the Seven Kings Conference? Didn't you already contact the Elder Council's judge Capriò and secretly arrange for Merlin's exile?" Vivian grew a little angry; this was completely contrary to her expectations.

"Indeed, Merlin had been exiled, yet he still participated in this Seven Kings Conference. You should know in your heart that Lilith lacks the ability to become the true master of the First Demon Lord Palace; she cannot stand in for Merlin at the conference. I suspect Merlin attended as the King of Exile to protect the First Demon Lord Palace." Abaddon speculated.

"Previously he reclaimed the throne of the First Demon Lord Palace, and now he's attending the Seven Kings Conference again—why does Merlin refuse to obey my will? He always does the unexpected, just like when he was a child, disobedient, and I always feel there is some distance between him and me, as if he were a stranger." Vivian scratched her head, looking very irritated; the rebellious son's behavior often contradicts her expectations.

"Your Majesty, what should we do now? To rescue Merlin, we must break the Demon-Sealing Vessel, but that is very difficult." Abaddon hesitated to ask.

"The situation has already surpassed my expectations; perhaps we need to borrow the enemy's power to have a chance to salvage the current state." Vivian lifted her head, already forming a new idea.

"The enemy's power?" Abaddon looked doubtful.

"Exactly. Behemoth will not be content to remain confined to the Demon Lord Palace; it will surely reclaim everything that once belonged to it, which will affect human interests. I have always believed the Holy Church hides something; their power is certainly not limited to what we see. Perhaps that lofty goddess left them some legacy. We need to harness the Holy Church's power to oppose Behemoth, and meanwhile probe the limits of those charlatans." Vivian furrowed her brow and said slowly, "The confrontation between the demon god and the Holy Church might very well be the 234th crusade, its scale possibly rivaling that ancient Holy War."

"The 234th crusade?" Abaddon frowned tightly, feeling the situation extremely grave. "Your Majesty, if we can rescue Merlin, do you truly believe he can defeat Behemoth? I have some doubts—are you perhaps placing too much faith in the prophet's predictions?"

"Not so." Vivian turned her head slightly, locking eyes with Abaddon, speaking meaningfully—

"I am not believing the prophet; I am believing my own son."

To Be Continued
