title: Chapter 1 — The Era Ends (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 1 — The Era Ends (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 34 · Chapter 1

At the end of the ancient Demon Age, the brutal holy war between demons and humanity had reached its final moments.

Deep within the gates between Heaven and the mortal world, sacred bells rang incessantly, shaking the demons so they could barely sleep.

The passage between the two worlds was about to close, entering a lengthy cooling period during which it could not be reopened for a very long time.

The participating seraphs scrambled to fly toward the Heavenly Gate, eager to return early, terrified of being the last one left behind.

The mortal world, filled with original sin, was unsuitable for these holy beings to survive in; their power continually drained here.

Although the seraph legion seemed to hold an overwhelming advantage, failing to fully conquer the Demon Lord Palace did not mean they had won the war.

Not only had the demons suffered unprecedented losses, but the seraph legion had also sustained heavy casualties — four of the seraphs representing the Seven Virtues had died in the war.

Only three survived: Michael, the supreme commander of the seraph legion; Uriel, the master smith; and Raphael, the chief healer.

War had ignited massive flames across the mortal world, flames that refused to die down for a long time. The vast land was completely shrouded in thick smoke.

Raphael's graceful figure floated in the sky as she gazed at the land reddened by fire, feeling countless lives fading away.

She lingered outside the gate rather than returning to Heaven. As a seraph, how could she possibly feel compassion for demons?

Destroying an era always came with bloodshed and sacrifice; this holy war utterly destroyed the demons' dominion in the mortal world.

A seraph behind her, with six blood-red wings on her back, soared past Raphael at tremendous speed, still clutching two demon heads in her hands.

Raphael couldn't help but frown and call out sharply, "Uriel! What are you doing?!"

"Hmm?" Uriel stopped and turned back, questioning coldly, "Do you have a problem?"

"What is it you're holding?" Raphael's gaze turned severe.

"This?" Uriel glanced down at the demon heads she carried, answering indifferently, "The head of that filthy Demon Lord — what else? I'm taking them back to Heaven to embed in my forge as decorations."

"Never mind something like that! We've already gained the upper hand; there's no need to insult the enemy's corpse. Such cruel methods don't suit our seraphs' conduct! Throw away their heads!" Raphael's tone was extremely serious; she truly could not bear Uriel's bloody hobby.

"I refuse. These are my war trophies. Why should I throw them away? Better mind your own business, useless Raphael." Uriel paused and said without expression, "It's all because your work wasn't up to par. Otherwise, why would so many seraph comrades have fallen? You should reflect on yourself."

"You!" Raphael ground her silver teeth, instinctively clenching her fists.

Uriel was utterly cold and paid no mind to the meddling Raphael, carrying her "trophies" as she swiftly flew toward the Heavenly Gate.

Raphael continued gazing at the burning land below, her heart beginning to waver, convinced this war was a mistake and that Heaven had gained nothing substantial from it.

Holy light flashed as Michael arrived beside Raphael, clad in holy armor blessed by the Goddess, wielding the holy flame sword of justice. He was tall and burly with a handsome face and sharp, bright eyes.

"Raphael, what are you dawdling for? Hurry back to Heaven. The Goddess has already issued her divine punishment. Once the gate closes, this place will turn to ashes, and no one can escape being cleansed!"

"I have objections to this war." Raphael replied firmly.

"What did you say? The holy war is to liberate the oppressed humans; it is a just war led by the Goddess. What objections could you possibly have?" Michael spoke with ringing authority, like an upright and incorruptible knight. "Don't forget — the Goddess is humanity's protector, and we are her servants. You have no right whatsoever to question the great Lord of Heaven."

"This war was a mistake! We were only interfering with the mortal world's natural order! This is not a just war; it's a mass cleansing merely to exterminate one species!" Raphael stared directly into Michael's eyes, her emotions growing agitated. "Look at our enemies — they've been driven to desperation. Even children have been sent onto the battlefield. How could we bear to swing our blades at the young among the demons? Must demons necessarily be evil? Evil is merely what the Goddess told us. We never once tried to understand them! Rather than the demons… we seem much more like executioners!"

*Smack!* Michael's face darkened as he delivered a stinging slap across Raphael's face, then growled coldly, "Enough! The Goddess's words are beyond question. Demons are the most evil existence. Do not harbor even an iota of pity toward them. I'll pretend I never heard those words. When you return to Heaven, watch your speech carefully, or you'll know the consequences. Stop being so foolish, Raphael —"

"Ah!" Raphael covered her cheek, an undercurrent of unwillingness flashing deep within her eyes —

She could vaguely sense that this brutal holy war was the Goddess's way of creating a warmbed more suitable for human existence.

Perhaps she wasn't entirely accurate. Maybe humanity was merely an insignificant backdrop.

The divine punishment sent down by the Goddess of Light already blanketed the skies above. The blinding holy light shrouded this land for seven days and seven nights without ever fading.

Not only the demons, but even humanity nearly forgot what night looked like, as though the world had experienced an extraordinarily long day.

The Almighty's power could no longer be described merely as terrifying; it seemed to have merged with nature itself. The scorching aura made all creatures tremble in fear.

If you didn't know what the end of the world looked like, then the scene unfolding now was the best description possible.

The Demon Lords who had barely survived gathered in the demon city where the Seventh Demon Lord resided. Clearly, their remaining time was short.

"We have successfully defended the seven Demon Lord Palaces, but that high-and-mighty bitch clearly does not intend to let us go. The divine punishment is aimed squarely at us. This final strike will instantly destroy all seven Demon Lord Palaces. Behemoth within the Blood Pool Seal may also regain his freedom. So we must make a choice: burn the souls within our divine realms and stop this divine punishment!"

The speaking demon was enormous in stature, with horns like a crown upon his head, his immense pressure making the surrounding divine-realm Demon Lords pale in comparison.

He was Merlin's grandfather, the first-generation Lucifer Mephisto, the undisputed leader in all demons' hearts and also the strongest demon swordsman.

Mephisto's voice was full of power; at his waist hung two long blades — one pitch black like charcoal, the other the crimson Banri Garan.

The demon race now faced a critical moment of life and death: either extinction, or survival at any cost.

After hearing Mephisto's decision, the surrounding divine-realm rulers from each of the other Demon Lord Palaces had no objections; they were already prepared to sacrifice themselves for the future of the demon race.

Every demon present revealed relieved smiles. None showed any fear of death. This was perhaps the most united moment among the Demon Lords.

However, one demon could not help but jump out and protest —

"Wait a minute! Why aren't you including me? Is it because I'm the weakest among you that I'm not worthy to stand alongside you?!"

At that time, Belial was very young; compared to the other Demon Lords, he truly seemed much more immature, with noticeable gaps in every aspect.

"Belial, I have watched you grow up. Of course you have the right to stand with us. But your task is to survive." Mephisto slowly approached Belial.

"What do you mean? Are you calling me a coward?" Belial's brows furrowed tightly, his pride feeling insulted.

"Not at all. The burden on your shoulders is heavier than any of ours. After the holy war ends, the era belonging to the demons will also draw to a close. That bitch's believers remaining in the mortal world will be eyeing us greedily." Mephisto patted Belial's shoulder like an older brother, speaking earnestly, "The future of the demon race needs you. You must lead the young demons through the most difficult period."

"But…" Belial felt uncomfortable, having difficulty accepting this.

"Please, Belial." Mephisto's tone left no room for doubt as he untied the Banri Garan from his waist, his eyes showing nostalgia —

"Hand it over to my daughter Vivian, and tell her this:

'Whoever can pull out the Banri Garan is the true master of the First Demon Lord Palace.'

"No — it should be the true master of the entire demon race, for its former wielder

'was the strongest demon in history!'"

title: Chapter 2 — The Prophecy Begins
content:
Chapter 2 — The Prophecy Begins

Volume 34 · Chapter 2

The young Belial took hold of the demon sword Banri Garan with both hands, looking at the ancient red scabbard, he couldn't help but recall the man—who personally established the system of seven Demon Lord Palaces governing separately, and even defeated Behemoth, rescuing the demons from dictatorial rule. Unfortunately, at that time Belial was still an infant in swaddling clothes, unable to witness the great prophet who commanded the winds and clouds. Mephistopheles' eyes flashed with a hint of nostalgia, his tone sorrowful as he said, "I truly wish to see the prophet once more, but there is no longer any chance." "Isn't it useless? After Ragnarok, it has completely disappeared, and it didn't even appear in this Holy War." Belial said with a furrowed brow, speaking softly. "I merely feel some regret." Mephistopheles gripped the long sword at his waist, seriously instructing, "After this, everything is up to you." Belial said nothing, instead lowering his head and closing his eyes; at this moment, any words of pleading would seem too childish. The surviving demons will follow Belial, rebuild their homeland devastated after the Holy War, and must also guard against the followers of the goddess. Led by Mephistopheles, several Demon Lords embarked on the mortal path, no matter the cost, to stop the divine punishment descending from Heaven. Belial can no longer recall the details of that time, only vaguely remembering that the light of divine punishment shrouded the sky, yet it never directly struck the Seven Demon Lord Palaces. After the Holy War ended, Mephistopheles dragged his mutilated body back to the Valley of Despair in the Death Marshes, where he soon died alone and lonely. However, the immense destructive power of the divine punishment has already caused faint, hardly noticeable cracks to appear in the blood pool seal formed by the Seven Demon Lord Palaces. The brutal war has become history; the few surviving demons continue to reproduce, attempting to restore the prosperous scene of the demon era. The vacant Demon Lord positions were soon filled by demons of blood relation, who continued to maintain the stability of the blood pool seal. Belial inherited the will of the first monarchs, successfully helping the entire demon race through the most difficult period, preventing external forces from succeeding. Time flew; with the aid of the Heavenly Goddess, weak humanity successfully ushered in its own era, the Human Era! In the ancient First Demon Lord Palace, the chief steward Abaddon hurried to the main hall, his hair neatly combed, his black-and-white butler attire also quite meticulous. Only a few demons know the prophet's prophecy, as the original Demon Lords collectively sacrificed themselves in the Holy War, leaving the new generation of demons rarely aware of the prophecy's existence. However, Vivian had heard the prophecy's content from her father Mephistopheles since she was very young, and she has never forgotten it. From Mephistopheles' words, Vivian could barely grasp the prophet's greatness, a demon worthy of complete trust. Therefore Vivian kept the prophecy's content firmly in mind, and from time to time she would go to carefully examine whether Behemoth in the blood pool showed any abnormality. If the prophet's second prophecy were to certainly appear, then the blood pool would show some special signs in advance, allowing Vivian to prepare ahead of time. Abaddon hurried to the main hall, approached Vivian who was reading, and said in a very low voice, "Your Majesty, something has happened." "Huh?" Vivian's calm face rippled; she quickly closed her book and asked, "What's wrong?" Abaddon looked around warily and answered carefully, "There is a problem with the blood pool seal. During the recent routine inspection, I found that although Behemoth's body is still present, its soul cannot be found at all, as if only an empty shell remains." "Behemoth's soul is gone? Is that really true?" Vivian realized the situation was turning bad. "Absolutely certain; I have checked repeatedly, Behemoth's soul is indeed not in the seal, and I don't know when it escaped the blood pool." Abaddon's tone was very serious. Vivian sat on the chair, silently silent for five seconds, then slowly rose and paced back and forth in the room, her expression becoming anxious: "Prophecy! This is the prophet's second prophecy! Indeed it has begun to happen; I fear Behemoth's awakening cannot be stopped." "Your Majesty, please calm down; I never believe in prophecies, as they only make people panic." Abaddon soothed Vivian's uneasy feelings. "Abaddon, you don't understand; the prophet's predictions are absolutely true, even my father firmly believes them, Behemoth's soul escaping the blood pool is sufficient proof of this." Vivian rubbed her temples, her mind full of thoughts on what to do now; the demon race has not been crushed by external forces, yet it may very well collapse from within. "Do we still have a chance? Behemoth hasn't completely broken the seal; it merely had its soul escape, and its power is far less than we imagined." Abaddon said calmly. "That's exactly what you said." Vivian took a breath, trying to calm herself, "Behemoth's soul escaping the blood pool is already a fact; it surely wants to completely free itself from the seal—what do you think it will do?" "I think it won't leave the demon race, but will hide within the demons' interior; Behemoth is the creator of demons, and its soul is very likely to seize another demon's body, then openly move about before our eyes." Abaddon voiced his suspicion, though he could not be entirely certain. "You mean that after Behemoth's soul escapes, any demon could possibly become its puppet?" Vivian's face turned grim; the situation was even more troublesome than she imagined. "That's right, including your children, they could possibly be possessed by Behemoth." Abaddon's eyes grew heavy, hoping Vivian would realize the harsh reality. "My lovely children?" Vivian's gaze fell into deep doubt as she looked out the room's window—she saw her two children, Merlin and Lilith in their youth. The Demon Lord Palace's rear garden was in full bloom, the weather clear, and from time to time came the sound of silver bell-like laughter. In his youth, Merlin stood in the center of the lawn, tightly gripping a toy wooden sword tucked at his waist, his eyes fixed firmly on the wildflowers ahead. Merlin took a deep breath, clenched his teeth, his ruby-like eyes flashing with lightning, and unleashed a vigorous drawing slash! The toy wooden staff whooshed as it swung, stirring a gentle breeze; the wildflowers before him swayed slightly, and the move he had been preparing for half a moment had no power at all. Merlin's face instantly darkened; he stared blankly at the wooden sword in his hand, gritting his teeth in anger, and violently threw the wooden sword to the ground—"I must be the only time traveler ever deceived!" "What 999-level drawing technique that destroys heaven and earth?" "And! All of it is utter bullshit! Completely useless!" (十A▲)

title: Chapter 3 — High Noble Demon (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 3 — High Noble Demon (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 34 · Chapter 3

The teenage Merlin was full of frustration, chopping the wooden sword under his feet. Since he came over, he had tried countless times.

No success at all.

The earth-shattering draw-slash technique? Doesn't exist. In Merlin's hands, it's just posing, completely useless.

Actually, during the transmigration process, countless dazzling skills were laid before Merlin, all far more powerful than the draw-slash—

Such as Phantom Sword Dance, Extreme Ghost Sword Technique, Death Tombstone, Magic Hell Blood Sacrifice, Thunder Wave Sword

These all exist, and Merlin could easily learn a skill of very high level. Destroying heaven and earth is simply too easy.

However, at that time, Merlin's mind was full of tricky moves, his eyes were dazzled, wanting to learn many skills, the more the better—

Operation like a tiger with wings, unleashing a gorgeous combo, finally striking a cool pose. Wouldn't it be delicious?

Merlin first fixated on the draw-slash skill, as if it had infinite magic power tempting him, the reason being just one word, Cool!

Especially after slashing the enemy and slowly sheathing the sword, he desperately wanted to write "arrogant and cool" on his face!

Faced with such a must-have skill for showing off, how could Merlin reject it? A pitiful person thoroughly poisoned by various audiovisual works, that's him.

Wishing for a bright future, Merlin excitedly clicked the draw-slash skill, but the result wasn't as simple as he thought—

9999 skill points, all poured into the draw-slash skill—one single skill, truly like opening a script—

One press, 999 and all points spent!

Merlin was dumbfounded on the spot, staring wide-eyed, unable to accept reality, feeling that he had learned only one draw-slash skill after half a search? Isn't this extortion!

"Brother is fooling around again, still practicing that draw-slash, it's completely useless." Young Lilith beside him accompanied him. At that time, she was still an adorable loli, and her mouth wasn't as toxic as now.

"Hah!" Merlin's heart was stabbed by a knife, angry and frustrated, shouting, "Shut up! Do you need me to管? I like draw-slash, okay?"

"Brother is so strange, why waste time on useless martial arts? Mom already said, draw-slash is a sword technique for sword beginners, even can not learn, because it has no use, just used to quickly put away weapons." Lilith's little face was full of confusion, unable to understand why her brother was so stubborn.

Merlin's temple veins twitched, completely not wanting to mind Lilith, completely just a kid with no teeth long in, "Why so much nonsense? Did you finish your homework? If not finished, I'll tell mom and let her punish you."

"Narrow-minded brother, hehehe~" Lilith stuck out her tongue, making a face at Merlin.

"This Merlin has a ugly complexion, unconsciously clenched his fists. If his strength was sufficient, he wouldn't have to suffer. Minor protection law wouldn't protect Lilith either."

"Brother hasn't learned anything till now, looks like he can't become a warrior or mage, maybe in the future he can only be a ordinary demon." Lil patted her little hand, and in front of her a magic wolf appeared, looking not ferocious, but like a cute puppy wagging its tail, "But I have already learned to summon a familiar, brother even if he is a useless fellow, in the future I will take good care of you!"

"Pfft!" Merlin spat out a mouthful of blood on the spot, his body swaying, unable to accept this reality, even his silly little sister has learned to sign a familiar contract, and he knows nothing? The biggest failure in life!

"Actually, His Majesty Merlin doesn't need to be discouraged, there's still hope, and quite a few demons grasped斗气 and magic power after adulthood." Maid long Ophelia showed a beautiful smile, like a considerate older sister, encouraging Merlin.

Hearing these words, Merlin's mood improved a lot, but when he raised his head and saw the speaker was Ophelia, his previously somewhat eased mood sank to the bottom again.

Merlin knew he was different from these demons. Before transmigration, he was a genuine human, the livestock that demons called him.

After coming here, somehow a group of ferocious demons appeared by his side. Anyone would have a hard time easily accepting this situation.

The somewhat unfamiliar little sister Lilith, this little point all day clinging to him, very sticky, causing Merlin to have no personal space at all.

And that motherly figure, the surface very strict mother Vivian, actually is a demon with overwhelming maternal love, often doing things that Merlin cannot understand.

Although Merlin cannot fully understand the customs of the demon race, as a mother's love for her son, sometimes it can be misunderstood, even vaguely crossing boundaries.

Because of the transmigrator's memories; sometimes Merlin feels very unfamiliar with the people around him, even if he has lived with the demon race for a long time, he cannot completely open his heart to break the barrier.

The thoughts and three views of demons are completely at odds with humans, this makes Merlin cannot fully adapt to the demon race life, completely out of place, especially facing an existence like Ophelia.

Ophelia appears dignified and beautiful, but actually. her gaze at Merlin is already filled with desire, greedy saliva almost dripping from the corner of her mouth.

She lightly caresses her flushed cheeks, having a mysterious possessive desire for the young Merlin, sinking into it unable to extricate herself—

The cute Merlin殿下, so perfect a male, every word and deed is completely different from other demons, what charm is this?

Future Merlin殿下, must be a handsome beauty, right? Is my type!

Grow up quickly, now the grade, sister I really can't bear to lay hands on ah, oh hahaha

"! ! ?" Merlin felt a chill on his back, having no courage to look Ophelia in the eyes, his whole body trembling, thinking, again. again come! I'm so scared now, who comes to save me?

"His Majesty Merlin, are you practicing swordsmanship again?"

Suddenly, a male demon in gorgeous clothes, draped in a purple robe, walked over. His hair was layered like waves, and even on the demon's horns were hung dazzling gold rings.

This demon's name was Almon, one of Vivian's capable subordinates, born into a noble demon family. Regardless of strength or background, he was nearly perfect.

The family Almon belonged to, although not royalty, unable to participate in the blood pool sealing's establishment, but its behind-the-scenes family background, reputation was almost already very close to the high and mighty royalty.

As the only heir of the family, Almon was even more like the center of attention, in the First Demon Lord Palace, besides Vivian, no demon could constrain him

* Merlin deeply furrowed his brows, having no good feelings toward Almon, this was the demon he hated most in the Demon Lord Palace, because Almon always mocked his thin demon bloodline, saying he looked like a human livestock. If not for Vivian's son, he would have been killed at birth.

"You really have a slow head, why are you so fond of that useless draw-slash? Just wasting time." Almon looked down at the young Merlin, not concealing his disdain at all, his tone mocking—

"When I was your age, I was already a outstanding high-level demon. Look at you?

"Tsk tsk tsk, truly hard for me to look at, actually can't use magic power and斗气."

"Do you really flow the blood of the strongest demon swordsman Mefisto? Don't think that because you are Vivian's son, you can inherit the First Demon Lord Palace?"

"Impossible. You are at most a bastard born with succubus power, any Demon Lord Palace monarch, don't have such a failure as you.

"Even "

"Doesn't have a single proper demon horn~"

In? Brothers, come a month
