title: Chapter 4 — The Greatest Suspect
content:
Chapter 4 — The Greatest Suspect

Volume 34 · Chapter 4

Amon tilted his head slightly and leaned close to Merlin's ear, speaking in a voice only the two of them could hear as he sneered, "Your mother cannot protect you forever. The Lord Lucifer will soon fall into decline because of you."

"Hush!" Young Merlin shoved Amon away, reprimanding him angrily, "Stay away from me! You have no right to mock and ridicule me!"

"Get out of here! We're not welcome to you!" Lilith ran up in front of Merlin, hands on her hips, issuing commands.

"Why do you harbor so much hostility toward me? I'm only doing this to motivate His Highness Merlin." Amon shrugged helplessly, putting on an innocent expression.

"What happened to my brother has nothing to do with you! Go away! Annoying guy!" *Lilith said full of hostility.

"Are you deaf? Amon, you're not welcome here, go do your own thing." Ophelia warned with an unfriendly expression.

"Haha, truly ungrateful hearts." Amon laughed, walking over beside Ophelia and asking in a low voice, "I clearly wrote you so many letters, why won't you ever reply to me?"

"Because I have no interest in ** wild dogs." Ophelia answered without courtesy, looking down on this rising talent who relied on family power from the bottom of her heart.

"You should understand that agreeing to my proposal would bring tremendous benefits to both you and your father Abaddon. Aren't you at all tempted?" Amon asked meaningfully.

"Look at your behavior yourself? Wanting to marry me as your wife, you're not qualified enough." Ophelia's expression darkened, wishing she could spit directly on Amon's face right then and there.

Hmph! What a pity to waste that skin of yours. Amon's gaze swept over Ophelia's fiery figure, unable to hide the greed on his face.

"Believe it. Ophelia's eyes flashed with sinister red light, killing intent surging as she said—

"If you dare look at me with those eyes again, I'll gouge your eyeballs out."

Vivian, in the study, withdrew her gaze and began pondering over the information that Abaddon had speculated about.

She slightly raised her head, and in the way she looked at Abaddon, a trace of suspicion gradually emerged.

"If Beelzebub's soul can possess any demon's body, and even my children cannot escape, then..."

"Could you also become Beelzebub's puppet? Or perhaps, the one standing before me now is not Abaddon, but Beelzebub."

"To achieve your unspeakable purposes, you provided me with a bunch of false advice, misleading me to suspect my own child. This is very possible, right?"

"Similarly, if you haven't become Beelzebub's puppet, haven't you ever suspected that I, the current me, might be Beelzebub?"

With these words, the atmosphere in the study immediately turned icy. An endless chain of suspicion was forged, and deep mutual trust was随时 on the verge of collapse.

Vivian stared into Abaddon's eyes, and for the first time raised her guard against her loyal subordinate. At times like this, it seemed no one could be trusted.

Abaddon's gaze flickered with suspicion. Indeed, he was somewhat suspicious of the current Vivian, but he was unwilling to believe it.

If Vivian had already become Beelzebub's puppet, then the First Demon Lord Palace would fall immediately—

"I won't believe that you've become Beelzebub's puppet." Abaddon said firmly.

"Why? What grounds do you have?" Vivian questioned coldly.

"If Beelzebub had occupied your body, it would certainly steal all your memories and have thorough knowledge of the prophet's predictions. His Highness Merlin, as the prophesied child destined to end Beelzebub, would become Beelzebub's top priority target to eliminate. As long as you still deeply love your child, then you cannot possibly be a puppet possessed by Beelzebub." Abaddon presented his logic, which indeed had sufficient basis.

Vivian's expression softened slightly, and she nodded. "What you said is correct. Only those who want to kill my son harbor the greatest suspicion."

"However, I have no evidence to clear my own suspicion." Abaddon knelt on one knee, took out the poison-tainted dagger from his chest, and held it out with both hands before Vivian. "If you suspect I'm Beelzebub's puppet, please kill me anytime. I won't resist at all. Only then can you rest assured."

Vivian looked expressionlessly at her old servant kneeling before her. Abaddon was one of the few subordinates who knew her very well, and she was unwilling to suspect him.

The current situation was dire. Apart from herself, every demon bore some suspicion. Slaughter all the demons, and indeed Beelzebub could be unmasked.

But was there anything more terrible than this thought? To root out Beelzebub and start murdering her own loyal subordinates—that was far too foolish.

Vivian carefully recalled everything she knew about Beelzebub, hoping to find a breakthrough. She wanted to identify where Beelzebub was lurking without crippling the demon race.

"Rise, Abaddon. I won't suspect you. I know you too well. As long as you behave even slightly abnormally, I can easily detect it."

". " Abaddon looked up, feeling that Vivian's approach was not rational enough.

"I think your thinking is somewhat flawed. The fact that Beelzebub can possess any demon's body needs to be verified."

Vivian returned to her chair, regaining her usual calm.

"What is Your Majesty's plan?" Abaddon stood up and respectfully took his position nearby.

"What was the prophet's purpose in establishing the blood pool seal? It was to buy time for the demon race to continue reproducing, wasn't it? Because if Beelzebub had been killed back then, all the First Generation Demons would have died along with it, meaning none of us would exist today. This proves that Beelzebub shares a strong bloodline connection with the First Generation Demons and possesses absolute control over them." Vivian already had some conjectures in mind.

"So you mean Beelzebub is most likely to possess the bodies of the First Generation Demons?" Abaddon thought about it and believed this possibility was quite high.

"There aren't many First Generation Demons still alive now. They hold high positions and great power, mostly concentrated in the Council of Elders, but who exactly is it?"

Vivian picked up the hot coffee on the tea table, remained silent for a long while, then spoke a name. "I believe among the First Generation Demons, Berial bears the greatest suspicion. Let's look at this from Beelzebub's perspective. Berial, as a First Generation ruler with extremely high prestige, possesses tremendous strength and unparalleled authority among the demons. Who else is more suitable to be a puppet? I cannot think of a second candidate."

"Berial? This... this is impossible! Berial is a ruler who participated in the Holy War and is respected by many demons as an elder. He led the demon race to repel countless external invasions. How could such a meritorious Demon Lord possibly become Beelzebub's puppet?" Abaddon found it hard to believe, shaking his head repeatedly.

"Haha." Vivian laughed out loud right there, looking at Abaddon and answering with increasing conviction—

"See? Even you think so~"

"Then the suspicion of Berial having his body possessed becomes even greater."

title: Chapter 5 — Closed-off Childhood (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 5 — Closed-off Childhood (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 34 · Chapter 5

Eh? ? ?' Abaddon froze, his mind full of question marks, then immediately reacted and slapped his forehead hard. Because Belial's prestige is extremely high and he is not easily suspected, he is more likely to become Behemoth's target. Moreover, as the first-generation Demon Lord, once Behemoth occupies his body, it will be easier to think of a way to break free from the seal's restrictions. This is completely reverse thinking; the person least likely to become Behemoth's puppet is exactly the best target for it. Abaddon took a deep breath, feeling Vivian's line of thought was correct and worth verifying. "That's how it is; Belial seems to have the greatest suspicion, and I was just blinded." "This is just a guess; we need further verification, we need a way to determine Belial's current state." Vivian furrowed her brows, thinking about how to verify her hypothesis. "Why not use the prophet's prophecy?" Abaddon thought of a method to confirm whether Belial has been possessed. "Huh? Tell me." Vivian pressed. Abaddon slightly bowed and slowly said his idea: "For this Seven Kings Council, why not bring Prince Merlin along? That would let the other monarchs meet him, and also create an opportunity for Prince Merlin and Belial to be alone. If Belial has already become Behemoth's puppet, he will surely show hostility toward this prophesied son, Prince Merlin, which would be enough to verify your idea." "That..." Vivian looked troubled, hesitating over Abaddon's suggestion, as if worried about something. "Your Majesty, do you think my plan is inappropriate?" Abaddon asked, surprised. "No, I'm just worried about Merlin." Vivian furrowed her brows, her gaze turning again to the window. "Are you perhaps worried about Prince Merlin's safety? With your strength, even if Belial lashes out on the spot, you could keep him safe and sound." Abaddon said confidently; Vivian and Samuel are called the geniuses of the second-generation demons, and though their strength may not match Belial's, protecting Merlin is more than enough. "You misunderstand, Abaddon; I'm worried about Merlin's self-esteem being hurt." Vivian paused, her expression difficult, and said, "You know, this child's demon blood is too diluted, so he was born without any demon traits, making him a freak among demons. Normally, a congenitally defective demon infant should be abandoned in the wilderness early on and not live to Merlin's age." "Why did you choose to keep Prince Merlin? Is it because you went soft?" Abaddon asked, puzzled. "No, I just think Merlin is special; he never cried from birth, his gaze is unlike that of a normal infant, showing a maturity beyond his years, plus the prophet's prophecy, which gave me some hope, so I decided to continue raising him." Vivian said in a low voice. "Really?" Abaddon thought Merlin sounded a bit special, but Merlin has shown no outstanding talent so far, and whether he truly is the prophesied son who can defeat Behemoth is doubtful. "This child might be somewhat autistic; he never spoke to me as a child, always very solitary, only talking a bit more with his sister. This huge sense of estrangement often makes me doubt whether Merlin is really my son. As a mother, I feel like a failure." Vivian rubbed her temples, a shadow already in her heart. "Abaddon had a bead of cold sweat on his forehead, recalling that Merlin and Vivian had only started trying to communicate in the past few decades. "So, because of his thin bloodline, Merlin will face much discrimination and rejection; this child is psychologically sensitive. The First Demon Lord Palace is my domain, so he would fare better there, but if he leaves? I worry his self-esteem won't hold up." Vivian lowered her head, not wanting Merlin to casually leave the Demon Lord Palace, especially since the Seven Kings Council consists of high-ranking demons, and Merlin would likely face even harsher hostility. "Your Majesty, you should prioritize the big picture; no matter how much you love him, you must know you cannot protect Prince Merlin forever. He must bravely step out and learn to survive; weak demons will ultimately be eliminated." Abaddon said earnestly, typical demon thinking. Vivian sighed deeply, obviously unable to make an easy decision.

Late at night, in the spacious bathroom of the Demon Lord Palace. Merlin lifted a basin filled with warm water and poured it over his head; thick steam filled the air, and his resentment over the day's events slowly—. That demon named Amon is just a bastard, always occasionally humiliating me! If it weren't for the officials of the Demon Lord Palace, I would have killed him! What's so arrogant about it? Remember that! Merlin imagined in his mind Amon kneeling on the ground, various pleas in his daydreams, but the reality is that aside from being Vivian's son, hardly any demon takes him seriously. This is the law of the jungle among demons; even if Merlin is a prince, it changes nothing—without strength, he can only endure countless stares here. In fact, Merlin himself is puzzled; clearly, after crossing over, he has never provoked any demon, yet Amon constantly mocks and insults him, to the point of unbearable. Merlin's inner longing for great power grows stronger; even his sister Lilith surpasses him, forever relying on his mother's protection—this is unrealistic among demons. "Am I... the biggest failure of a transmigrator? Why am I living so suffocated?" Merlin looked at the large mirror not far away; his wet hair matched his youthful frame, making him look like a sorry failure. He reached behind and touched his own scalp, imagining himself like other demons, growing sharp horns—maybe that would change the situation? Useless; with this appearance here, I am just an unacceptable oddball, like a freak. Why did I transmigrate into a demon? If I were a human, how great that would be. Merlin slumped his head, feeling stifled to death, resenting those transmigration stories that are all lies, having become an unlucky victim.

The— The bathroom door creaked open; Vivian walked in wrapped in a towel, though the steam was hazy, it could not conceal her sensual, fiery mature figure. Like a fully ripe, big red cherry, juicy and tempting, just a glance is enough to make one's blood boil. "Merlin? You're here?" "Ah! !" Merlin jumped as if struck by lightning, quickly grabbed the wooden basin from the floor, shyly covering his body, his eyes darting about, panicking. "Why are you inexplicably shy?" Vivian saw Merlin's reaction and chuckled lightly, tugged at her towel, and gestured, "Come over, since we've met, let's do this together. "Speaking of which, we haven't had a proper chat in a long time.

title: Chapter 6 — Uh, this
content:
Chapter 6 — Uh, this

Volume 34 · Chapter 6

. Don't bother! I'm not a kid anymore, I can wash myself! Merlin shrank into the corner, stammering in answer, his little heart thumping wildly, terrified to the extreme.

"What nonsense are you talking about? In Mom's eyes, you're always a child."

Vivian propped her hands on her hips. Her white skin was a bit blinding, and under the cover of misty steam, it was even more alluring.

She stood naked and carefree right in front of Merlin, not at all avoiding her son's gaze, and she didn't think there was anything wrong with it.

In her eyes, Merlin was her own son—what secrets could there be? Being able to see each other openly represented mutual trust.

Demons' notions of male and female differences were, although not too different from humans, far more open, with far fewer rules and constraints.

Seeing Merlin shielding his shameful parts with a wooden basin, looking flustered and uneasy, Vivian couldn't help but feel both annoyed and amused.

"You child, what are you shy about? Is there anything embarrassing in front of Mom? Come over quickly, let me take a good look at you."

"Th-that! Mom, don't treat me like a child! I think it's very shameful to be seen openly by you!" Merlin's excited face turned red, doing his best to avoid this.

"Huh? What's your reaction? It's almost like a human," Vivian slightly furrowed her brow, unable to understand why Merlin would be so resistant. After all, demons do this all the time.

"I... Merlin wanted to say something but glanced at Vivian's fiery, mature, sensual curves, hurriedly turning his head away, thinking—

I'm a human! Demons' incredibly open views on male and female relations are simply unacceptable!

Please spare me, I don't want to become a pervert!

That's not some sexy older sister, but my Mom! !

If Merlin were truly a demon, he probably wouldn't mind bathing with his mother, because normal demons wouldn't find it strange.

The awkward part is that Merlin is a transmigrator, and his worldview is still that of a modern human. Bathing with his mother after reaching a certain age is simply an incomprehensible ethical issue!

Moreover, Merlin has always had some estrangement from the suddenly appeared mother and sister. Although he has already accepted that he has become a member of the demons in this other world, accepting "strange" relatives is evidently not easy, and this probably requires a very long process to adapt.

In the body of teenage Merlin, there is actually the soul of a modern human male. Facing a mature woman with a fiery figure, beautiful countenance, and standing stark naked before him—would he have no reaction that a male should have?

At this moment, I suppose only Merlin himself knows best in his heart. However, his nervous motion of using a wooden basin to cover his crotch is enough to make people daydream, and extra explanations are useless.

Vivian couldn't help but frown, feigning an angry expression, and her tone also added a bit of severity, "Did you misbehave again? Why are you so resistant to Mom?"

"Not really, I, I don't reject you, I just... I hope I can have some privacy space," Merlin felt guilty, his eyes darting about, speaking with insufficient breath, and his voice getting smaller and smaller.

"You are my beloved son, what privacy can you have in front of me?" Vivian spoke in a manner that was utterly reasonable and serious, "Hurry up and come over, don't make Mom angry, disobedient children will be punished."

Merlin stared wide-eyed in astonishment. At this moment, his mood was like a victim—he had no power to resist Vivian, so he could only choose to listen obediently.

Only to see him moving his steps muddily and dejectedly, like a bride who had received grievances, coming deeply low-headed to his mother's side, the wooden basin covering his crotch clamped down even tighter.

Merlin dared not raise his head randomly, because he would easily see the fragrant and tempting scene below, which would only make him more uncomfortable.

Vivian lowered her head, looked at the wooden basin that Merlin was clamping down on tightly, and increasingly felt that her son's psychology had issues, so she said softly, why cover that spot? Take it off, isn't it fine?

"No!" Merlin kept his eyes tightly closed, his emotions becoming agitated, "This is my last dignity! Don't force me! No matter what, I will never take the wooden basin off!"

Vivian was startled, seeing Merlin's such a huge reaction, she also didn't dare to force him easily, "Sit down, let Mom wash your back first."

Merlin finally breathed a sigh of relief, feeling he had escaped a calamity. If the wooden basin were forcibly taken off, he would no longer be able to live, and he would face his mother with no shame.

However, Vivian became suspicious in her mind. Why did Merlin cover that area so tightly? Could it be that he hasn't developed all these years, afraid she would laugh at him?

Merlin sat obediently on the small stool, but the wooden basin between his legs was still clamped down tightly, not daring to relax his vigilance for a moment, his skinny body tightened into a power pole.

However, Merlin had his back to Vivian, which made him feel much more at ease; he didn't have to constantly be stimulated by her white and delicate body, leading to his last moral line collapsing.

Vivian first used warm water to wet Merlin's back, then took a soft and suitable towel, gently wiping his body tenderly, "How's the pressure?"

"It's quite good," Merlin sat up straight, his little heart seemingly being pestered by countless ants, it was terribly itchy!

"Then that's good, I haven't given you a back rub in a long time, do you remember when you and Lilith were little, I would wash you like this? Lilith was very clingy, wouldn't wash with you unless she cried nonstop, truly nostalgic~" Vivian's face radiated maternal light, recalling things from a long time ago.

Merlin said nothing, his head a mess of thoughts. When he was small, that was fine, he was still a little kid. But now is different, he has already developed into an adult demon, and bathing with his mother? What a shameful thing!

"You've got quite a bit of muscle on your body, you've grown up, time has passed quickly, unknowingly shedding your former immaturity, about to become a little gentleman~" Vivian said in a teasing tone.

Merlin's eyebrows on his head jumped wildly, thinking: If you know this, why not treat me as a child? Why still—

appearing stark naked before me! ? Are you looking down on me!

"In a few days Mom has to attend the Demon Race's Seven Kings Conference, do you want to go with Mom?" Vivian asked with a hesitant heart.

"Seven Kings Conference? Merlin hesitated, with his own very weak strength, he really didn't have the courage to leave the Demon Lord Palace.

"You're already a little gentleman, you should start trying to contact the outside world. The Seven Kings Conference can see other Demon Lord Palace demons, which is very helpful for your growth," Vivian didn't want her son to have any pressure, depicting the Seven Kings Conference as a gathering.

Merlin fell into thought. Since he was born, he had never left the Demon Lord Palace. He had always been very curious about the world outside the Demon Lord Palace. Hearing his mother Vivian's description, Merlin was quite moved. Being able to see demons from other Demon Lord Palaces would definitely be a novel experience!

Also not... impossible

"Haha, this is really Mom's good son! Truly a small adult with responsibility!"

Vivian was overjoyed, unable to help but hug Merlin from behind into a spring-light-filled embrace, repeatedly kissing his forehead.

Merlin's expression was blank, forced to perform, he instantly petrified, feeling his mother's slippery skin, soft embrace, and it lightly rubbing against his back.

Suddenly giving rise to an illusion of being immersed in surging waves, freely wandering in the ocean of passion and maturity, surrounded by fiery and bright light—

Ah!

Ah this!

This mysterious sensation? ? ?

Z(°△II)

title: Chapter 7 — Falling in Love (Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter)
content:
Chapter 7 — Falling in Love (Monthly Ticket Extra Chapter)

Volume 34 · Chapter 7

“Wow wow wow!!!”
Merlin couldn't stand this? He jumped up from the small stool with a "teng", naked buttocks, shouting loudly, and frantically fled out of the bathroom.
The scene was horrible to behold; no one would have imagined that this demon boy who would flee in embarrassment even in front of his mother would one day become the youngest third‑generation monarch among the demons?

“Merlin”
Vivian tried calling out to the fleeing Merlin, she was utterly disheveled in the wind, completely unaware of what was happening? It was just hugging her own son, how could she provoke such a huge reaction?
She couldn't help but lower her head, starting to wonder wildly, suspecting that perhaps Merlin had grown a bit, entered the so‑called “rebellious phase”, and began to reject her as his mother.
“Good grief, what did I do wrong? Why does this child always oppose me? Could my parenting methods be flawed .”

Outside the bathroom door, Merlin didn't care if anyone was in the corridor; he ran bare‑bottomed with all his might, just wanting to get back to his room as soon as possible—he would never choose this time to bathe again.
In the corner, Ophelir was wrapped in a scarf, looking resentfully at the fleeing Merlin, angrily biting the towel in her hands with her teeth, full of resentment thinking——
Damn! I didn't expect to be outpaced by Her Majesty Vivian; I wasted a great opportunity.

A few days later, before the Seven Kings Conference officially began, the council hall had already gathered a large number of demons—either monarchs or close aides and friends of the monarchs, many high‑ranking demon elders.
The demons, taking advantage of the time before the recollection began, each sought out old friends, occasionally embracing to catch up, or passionately expressing their political views.
The venue looked quite lively; without a doubt, the demons who could attend this meeting were the top tier of the demon race, and the meeting's outcome would determine the demon race's future direction.
Beelzebub held a photo of his sister Miranda in his hand, staring at it for a long time, then suddenly stuck out his tongue and licked—leaving layers of flowing saliva, “Miranda, big brother loves you! Wait for me at home, after this conference I'll return as fast as I can! Believe in big brother!”
This extreme sister‑complex disgusting act immediately drew dissatisfaction from a surrounding group of demons, even causing psychological discomfort.
Even if one misses one's sister terribly, one wouldn't resort to such disgraceful behavior, and besides, Beelzebub hasn't been apart from his sister for long.
“Ah~ Miranda, my longing for you in my heart has already flooded like a flood~” Beelzebub pressed his sister's photo against his chest, his whole self immersed in fantasy.
“Beelzebub, enough already, don't be so disgusting—I feel like throwing up.” Leviathan said with an ugly face.
“Shut up, little shrimp! What I do is my freedom; want to criticize me? Wait until you're over 1.5 meters tall first.” Beelzebub said with a mocking grin.
“Tch! Remember this, you'll starve to death only spitting flies.” Leviathan's veins on his forehead twitched wildly.
“Beelzebub, although your behavior hasn't broken demon race rules, your obsessive infatuation with your sister is indeed nauseating.” Samael's voice was deep, as he silently evaluated.
“Not speaking doesn't make you a mute, Samael—still, take care of yourself. Have you recovered your head? Maybe your skull is being kicked around like a ball by your own brother, hahaha.” Beelzebub, forced to attend the Seven Kings Conference and already in a bad mood, went on a tirade against the other monarchs, “You can't even manage your own younger brother—you're a total failure; I think your brother is more suited to be the Wrath Monarch.”
Leviathan tried to intervene; if Samael were provoked by Beelzebub, the council hall would likely vanish instantly, causing a huge uproar—however—
Samael stood calmly in place, his hands with nowhere to rest scratched at his chest hair, and calmly replied, “I have no brain; what you say is all correct.”
“Good heavens!” Leviathan rubbed his forehead, sighing, thinking, what kind of freaks are these monsters? Already hopeless? Why do I have to work with them?

Vivian changed into an extremely dignified long dress and gracefully walked toward the center of the hall, with young Merlin following behind her—this was his first time coming to such a place.
Merlin walked timidly behind his mother, curiously observing the passing demons, and couldn't help but marvel, “Is this the Seven Kings Conference? So many powerful demons—aside from the First Demon Lord Palace, there are actually this many demons existing!”
This was Merlin's first contact with demons outside the Demon Lord Palace; his mood was a little excited. The knowledge he had gained from books paled in comparison to the shock of seeing it with his own eyes, and at this moment, regarding the other world he found himself in, he gained many new insights!
Vivian took Merlin's uneasy hand, lowered her head and asked, “How are you? Nervous?”
“Not nervous, I find this quite interesting.” Merlin replied politely, indeed it was more entertaining than staying in the First Demon Lord Palace.
“That’s good.”
Vivian nodded, seeing that Merlin wasn't stage‑frightened, she relaxed considerably—until a discordant voice sounded up ahead—
“Isn't that Vivian? Long time no see, your butt's gotten bigger again, though it's still not as cute as my sister. If my sister were a hundred points, I could give you a passing sixty~”
Not far away, Beelzebub flashed a mocking smile; he and Vivian never got along—every time they met he had to sneer before he could be satisfied.
Vivian's forehead veins throbbed, anger surged, she barely managed a strained smile, “Oh? It's you, you who love excrement‑eating flies—didn't you go fight the stray dogs over eating poop this time?”
“I am the Fly King, and I don't actually like eating excrement.” Beelzebub earnestly corrected her mistake.
“Sorry, it seems I remembered wrong—you're just the foul‑smelling trash that likes to eat your sister's excrement, right?” Vivian put on an expression of sudden realization.
“You you you .” Beelzebub shook his trembling hands, furious, “Are you spying on my thoughts?”
“Hey! You really did that?” Leviathan's face turned pale, frightened badly.
“No! I just thought about it!” Beelzebub frantically defended himself.
“Leviathan, it's been a while—you haven't grown at all, have you?” Vivian stroked Merlin's hair, speaking meaningfully, “You're about the same height as my underage son; maybe you two could become good friends.”
“Don't push it too far!” Leviathan gritted his teeth, hating when people tease him about his height.
“I'm not bullying you; I actually envy you. I heard the human nations have amusement parks, grand theaters, circuses—free for kids. If you get the chance, you and my son could go together, and maybe even get an extra two‑piece L‑kids set~” Vivian gave Leviathan an encouraging thumbs‑up.
“Leviathan's face turned black as charcoal; not only was he rendered speechless by the retort, he even developed a strong interest in that kids’ set.”
“Samael~” Vivian flashed a “kind” smile, her eyes filled with deep meaning.
*That one.* Samael reached his hand toward the empty space above his neck, completely unable to touch his head, “I haven't said a word.”
“Hmph! You're being honest; today I'll let you off.”
Vivian snorted coldly; after losing his head, Samael's strength plummeted, his influence among demons weakened greatly, and now she is the strongest among the second‑generation demons.
Waves of intense oppressive pressure made the surrounding demons struggle to breathe; several monarchs stayed silent, pretending to be pacifists as if nothing were wrong.
“I'm not in a good mood today; don't provoke me, otherwise I'll sew your mouths shut with needle and thread.”

Merlin lowered his head, obediently following close behind Vivian, trembling as he thought——
This is my mother; her gentility and dignity are all an act.
The truth is, she is a formidable female demon with an extremely vicious mouth!
I realized this long ago—behaving well is my survival strategy!
Among the demons, Vivian is trouble that no one willingly provokes; no demon has ever gained an advantage from her.
Occasionally a few iron‑headed brats like Beelzebub appear, they get scolded until their blood boils, and in the end they can only swallow their anger.
Of course Vivian doesn't direct foul language at everyone—for example, when facing the former subordinates of Mephistopheles—
“Vivian, long time no see, how are you?” The presiding judge Caprio walked over with a smile; this short‑sized demon old man always looks amusing no matter when you see him.
“I'm fine, Uncle Caprio.” Vivian answered gently.
“What is this?” Caprio, since Mephistopheles' death, has never returned to the First Demon Lord Palace, knows little about its internal affairs, and has never seen Merlin.
“This is my son, Merlin.” Vivian introduced enthusiastically.
“This is Merlin? We're meeting for the first time.” Caprio's eyes shifted from initial excitement to disappointment, because Merlin's bloodline is thin and lacks demon traits, so he could only offer a polite compliment, “Your son is very healthy.”
Vivian smiled without speaking, then turned to Merlin and said, “Mother needs to discuss some important matters here; you help me deliver this invitation personally to the Sloth Monarch Belial—can you do that?”
“Just delivering a letter? No problem.” Merlin nodded, then turned and left to search for Belial in the hall.
Vivian watched Merlin's retreating back, her smile fading, she decided to follow him from behind to observe all of Belial's reactions to Merlin——
So
What will the result be?

Merlin today is the ? time seeing other monarchs—normally he had only seen them in paintings, but they are still easy to recognize.
After accepting Vivian's task, Merlin wandered the hall, trying to locate Belial's figure and hand over the invitation.
All along Merlin tried asking nearby demons, but absolutely no one was willing to engage with him, not even to make contact.
The reason is that Merlin lacks demon traits; amidst a hall full of demons he is like an outsider—if someone claimed he was a human who had sneaked in, demons would believe it.
If it weren't for the many demon elders knowing Merlin is Vivian's son, he would likely have encountered danger here already.
Under the pressure Vivian brought, no demon dared to move against Merlin, but shunning him posed no problem.
Merlin felt countless discriminating eyes staring at him from behind, like needles pricking his heart, making him feel awful.
Although he had never sensed such hostility while in the First Demon Lord Palace, once he left his comfort zone he finally realized his situation.
Without Vivian's protection, the weak Merlin trying to survive on his own in the demon realm would basically be impossible.
Merlin's self‑esteem suffered a severe blow, yet now he has no capacity to resist at all; he can only endure the contemptuous glances and low‑muttered insults——
He unconsciously clenched his fists, his eyes turned rebellious, his yearning for power intensified again, dreaming of changing the status quo——
Merlin gave up seeking help from other demons, relying solely on his own persistent search to possibly find Belial.
“Where is he anyway? He probably isn't even around here—what a troublesome old geezer.”
In a daze, Merlin noticed amidst the crowd of demons a stunningly beautiful female demon so gorgeous it could make one suffocate.
Amidst a waterfall‑like blaze of crimson hair grew two horns like works of art; her bewitching, alluring eyes continually drew in the souls of onlookers.
Her outfit perfectly accentuated a heroic femininity, and the folding fan in her hand added a touch of mysterious Eastern charm—she was practically a superstar!
Asmodeus, like Merlin, is also an outsider among demons; because of her feminine appearance she was criticized by the elder council, yet no one can deny her beauty.
Merlin had once seen Asmodeus's portrait in the library of the First Demon Lord Palace, but upon seeing the Lust Monarch herself he discovered she was even more beautiful than the painting—every smile was breathtakingly lovely.
Is there any woman in this world more beautiful than Asmodeus? Merlin believes that's impossible; Asmodeus has already reached the “pinnacle of femininity,” he is the very embodiment of the word “beautiful”!
Merlin's eyes burned with the fire of desire, like a starving wolf he fixed his gaze on the distant Asmodeus, even unconsciously gulping saliva—missing even a glance felt like a huge loss.
The Asmodeus among the elders seemed to sense Merlin's scorching stare, subconsciously glanced over, and saw he was merely an underage brat.
Thus Asmodeus covered her mouth and nose with her fan, smiled kindly at the distant Merlin, and her captivating eyes pierced straight into the depths of his soul!
Thump thump!
The young Merlin thought that smile had saved him; his heart pounded violently, as if struck by lightning, and on the spot he fell into a pink river of love, unable to pull himself out.
Merlin is willing to swear on his soul that Asmodeus is the most perfect woman he has seen since coming to this other world—any flirtatious trash cannot compare to him——
Is this the feeling of a racing heart?
I'm truly lucky to have met the most beautiful woman in this world!
Don't say it, Mom—I want to marry him, right now! Immediately! At once!
To be blunt, I've already thought up a name for our child!
(o●u▼.)

title: Chapter 8 — Too manly
content:
Chapter 8 — Too manly

Volume 34 · Chapter 8

Merlin looked like a first-time lover who had just fallen for a "girl," and his legs went weak at the sight.

His first encounter with Asmodeus had given Merlin a huge shock, giving him a whole new understanding of "beauty."

Merlin stood dumbfounded in place, completely ignoring the demons around him, staring at Asmodeus from afar. He believed this was the biggest gain since arriving at the Seven Kings Conference.

"Where did this little demon come from? Get lost! Don't block the way!"

Merlin suddenly felt his back pushed, and—oh, he fell to the ground on the spot, waking up from an unrealistic fantasy.

He was indignant in his heart. Why treat himself so brutally? Even if he blocked the road, couldn't he just pat his shoulder?

Merlin furrowed his brows, his ugly face turning up, and his angry gaze instantly—condensed.

Wearing expensive silk all over his body, adorned with countless precious jewels, with a plump figure and a haughty expression—this was the greedy Demon Lord, Ma Men!

Beside Ma Men, Oset followed silently. Seeing Merlin fall to the ground, he let out a doubtful sound from his mouth, seeming to recognize him?

"Tch! Where did this hairless kid come from, daring to block my way?" Ma Men's mood turned extremely bad. His high-altitude gaze was full of contempt. "Wait, why don't you have horns? This is the Elder Council, the demon race's territory. How could a human dare to strut around here?"

Merlin gritted his teeth, climbing up from the ground under huge pressure, angrily retorting, "I'm not human!"

"Hmm?" Ma Men felt a curiosity rise in his heart, carefully examining Merlin. Indeed, this little demon didn't look like a human, but didn't look like a demon either.

Behind Ma Men, Oset hurried forward and whispered in Ma Men's ear, "Your Majesty, he seems to be Princess Vivian's son. You didn't forget, did you? Princess Vivian didn't marry any demon, but chose to use succubus power to get herself pregnant. Rumors say she gave birth to a male infant, apparently a thin-blooded inferior product."

"Oh~" Ma Men listened to Oset's introduction, and couldn't help but show a meaningful smile on his face. "So you are Princess Vivian's son, born using succubus power. Trash."

"Eh!" Merlin stared wide-eyed in disbelief, deeply stabbed in his self-esteem by Ma Men, especially the word "trash." "Take back your words!"

"Hahaha, really foolish little ghost~" Ma Men found this little dot of Merlin somewhat interesting, and said in a low voice, mocking, "You're not trash, then who is trash? Look well at your surroundings. Besides you, is there another demon without horns?"

"Just horns, it doesn't prove anything." Merlin answered unwillingly.

"Naive. Not having horns proves your bloodline is too lowly. Under normal circumstances, a congenital defective demon like you should be thrown out to the wild to feed wolves." Ma Men paused, speaking with deep meaning. "Believe me, you can't survive in the demon race. This place will never accept you. Although you are currently protected by Princess Vivian, she can't protect you forever. When you come of age, you will be driven out of the First Demon Lord Palace immediately."

"Rubbish! Even without horns, I can still become Demon King in the future!" Merlin's face turned dark. He didn't expect Ma Men to be so bitter and hateful.

"This is the most laughable remark I've ever heard." Ma Men laughed, his shoulders shaking. The mole on his face also trembled along with his face. "Do you think becoming a Lord is a simple matter? If your strength isn't up to par, you'll never reach this throne. A weak inferior product like you will eventually be replaced by other demons."

Merlin's eye twitched, and he unconsciously clenched his fist. His inner anger had reached its peak, but he couldn't do anything about Ma Men. He could only mutter, "Fatso."

"Hmm?" Ma Men heard Merlin's swear word, and his expression instantly turned cold. He directly gave him a big slap.

Smack—

Merlin covered his cheek, sitting on the ground with a plump butt, gritting his teeth and staring at Ma Men, "You!"

"Looks like Princess Vivian didn't teach you any courtesy?" Ma Men lowered his palm, very much liking Merlin's angry yet impotent gaze. "If you have any dissatisfaction, you can let Princess Vivian come find me personally. As for you? You aren't qualified to talk with me."

Merlin lowered his head, his eyes wishing he could carve a piece of flesh from Ma Men. He had to suppress his unwillingness deep in his heart, knowing well the huge strength gap between him and Ma Men. In the demon race, the weak had no right to speak.

The demon elders around Merlin cast cold glances at him. Ma Men had done things they dared not do. Seeing Merlin secretly suffer a loss, they were secretly delighted in private. The Elder Council was truly not a place for just anyone.

Merlin had a blank expression. All the experiences he had in the Elder Council had deeply hurt his dignity. He had deeply recorded all the things he had experienced in the Elder Council. If he had the chance in the future, he would definitely take revenge and never be a tortoise immortal forever.

Just as Merlin was preparing to get up from the ground, someone extended a helping hand to the isolated him. It was Asmodeus, who had come at some unknown time.

Asmodeus saw everything that happened here. He wasn't sympathizing with Merlin, he just found Princess Vivian's son very interesting and wanted to try contacting him.

Huh—

Merlin got a close look at Asmodeus's absolutely beautiful face, and instantly felt a suffocating sensation, his heart rate accelerating, and his face turning red visibly.

Asmodeus tilted his head, not understanding Merlin's dumbfounded reaction. He himself was not as vicious as Ma Men. Was he scared to the point he couldn't even speak properly?

Merlin very shyly gripped Asmodeus's hand and stood up, his heart excited beyond measure, his restless blood rushing to his forehead—

Touch it!

Is this the hand of a "girl"?

No! It's the hand of the most beautiful "girl" in another world!

It's actually so smooth. I gained! I gained!

Although it was just a simple touch, it was a great progress in my life!

No wonder the protagonists in TV dramas have girls surrounding them. I finally also experienced such a life!

Merlin was indeed careful, standing in front of Asmodeus, excited to the point he couldn't speak. His mind was full of marriage!

Marry me! Marry me!

Ding—

Suddenly, the bell rang in the conference hall. This was the signal that the meeting was about to start, obviously there wasn't much time left.

Merlin lowered his head and looked at the invitation in his hand. Although he really wanted to stay with Asmodeus for a while longer, his mother's task was more important.

If he couldn't even do something as simple as sending a message, then he would truly be good for nothing.

Merlin put aside his chaotic thoughts, raised his head and looked at Asmodeus, considering this lustful monarch to be different from others, his behavior was extremely kind.

"That, I'm looking for the lazy Demon Lord Belial. Do you know where it is?"

Asmodeus was suddenly stunned, lifting his head to look around, using his hand to point accurately at Merlin, telling him where Belial was.

Merlin had no time to waste. He ran in the direction Asmodeus indicated, suddenly winning his steps, excitedly saying, "Thank you. I'm Merlin. You are the most beautiful female demon I've ever seen."

"Merlin? Princess Vivian's son has already grown up." Asmodeus muttered in a rough voice, watching Merlin leave, then silently took out a makeup box, took out a razor, and shaved the hair on his face in front of many demons—

"Oh my~ This little guy actually called me the most beautiful female, demon?"

"Great, in the demon race there are actually demons who don't know I'm a male? It feels really nice."

"Spit! Why does hair on my face grow so fast? It'll grow out in a while."

End of chapter.

title: Chapter 9 — Silent Contest (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 9 — Silent Contest (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 34 · Chapter 9

As anticipated by Vivian, after Belhomos flexibly escaped from the blood pool, he had indeed successfully occupied Beryl's body.

And as Beryl, he participated in this Seven Kings Conference, wanting to understand how the demon race had developed after being sealed for so long.

Belhomos was very glad that the demons had reproduced to this day, otherwise there would not have been an opportunity to regain freedom again.

Beryl, whose body had been seized by the Demon God, stood outside the Elder Council, gazing at the continuous mountains in the distance, thinking about future matters—

Was the Seven Demon Lord Palace system established by the sage? Let each monarch of the demon race guard the blood pool seals at the seven key points, ensuring the seal is foolproof.

To deal with me, that mysterious sage must have really worked hard, thinking I would never be able to escape from the blood pool?

How laughable.

The Elders must have appeared to maintain the stability of the seal. If any problem arises among the seven monarchs, the Elders will step forward to quell it, forcing all monarchs to be unable to run wild.

If it could run stably, indeed there would be no flaws, unfortunately, demons were created by my own hand, I know their nature too well.

As long as the demons have a point of divergence, they might unite. They will suspect each other, and fight to the death for interests.

Only when a suddenly appearing strong enough to suppress all demons uses force, might the demons' struggle be terminated, just like that mysterious sage last year.

A trace of hatred flashed in Belhomos's eyes, recalling the sage who sealed him, a humiliation he would never forget.

However, this demon creator is very glad; from various channels, he has already learned that the sage disappeared, which removes any obstacle from the road to re-enslaving all demons.

Belhomos has no doubt that he is the outstanding one among the ancient god faction, but after seeing that sage, he involuntarily doubted himself, and even lacked the courage to face the sage.

Belhomos let out a breath, feeling he already understood the current era well enough, and could begin his plan to completely lift the seal.

Now I have a basic grasp of all the situations of the demon race, and since the sage is no longer there, it seems there is no one who can block me.

Undoubtedly, after several epochs, the demon race will return to my hands again.

After the conference ends, first go and destroy the seal of the Seventh Demon Lord Palace. The seven key points of the blood pool—if any one of them is destroyed, I will completely escape the seal and gain freedom.

I am starting to look forward to it. When the demons see their father again, what expression will they show?

Belhomos believes that once he recovers his freedom, no demon in the demon race is his opponent, not even the strongest Beryl, who has already been dealt with.

All demon lords fear the God-sealing Vessel, but it has no effect on Belhomos's true body, for he is the owner and creator of the God-sealing Vessel.

Seeing Belhomos's confident appearance, it is obvious he does not know the prophecy left by the sage, and Vivian has not realized that even if she occupies a demon's body, she cannot read memories.

"Are you Uncle Beryl?"

A voice sounded out of the blue, interrupting Belhomos's thoughts. He slowly turned around and saw the young Merlin.

"Right, I am Beryl, uh!!!"

When Belhomos saw Merlin, he was instantly stunned. A trace of horror flashed in his eyes, and fear spread through his body, forcing him to retreat half a step!

"Are you okay?" Merlin curiously inspected Beryl, wondering why this only remaining venerable founding monarch reacted this way? Seems very afraid of me?

Belhomos stared at Merlin with wide eyes, stammering in reply:

"This is an invitation from my mother, Vivian, wanting to give you a chance to visit the First Demon Lord Palace as a guest." Merlin handed the invitation letter with both hands, but discovered that Beryl was distracted, standing in a daze.

Belhomos became very uneasy. A drop of cold sweat even slid down his forehead. His whole body was like a lion on guard, ready to attack Merlin at any moment—

Damn it! Although it looks very young, and the temperament and feeling are different, but why are the eyes so similar to the sage? I won't believe this is a coincidence. That mysterious bastard— he will definitely have set a trap for me!

This kid, might have some connection with the sage! My feeling won't be wrong!

"Did you hear me? The invitation." Merlin waved his hand in front of Beryl's eyes, thinking this old fellow doesn't look up to me? Treating me like air?

Belhomos narrowed his eyes, abandoning all plans to break the seal, and instead placed getting rid of the child in front as the top priority!

If the child in front has some connection with the sage, then even if Belhomos escapes the seal, it would be of no use; only by eliminating him can he feel at ease.

Belhomos's face turned gloomy, and he reached out to touch Merlin's head, intending to kill him on the spot to prevent future problems.

"Hmm?" Merlin frowned in confusion, not realizing that death was quietly approaching!

Not far away, Vivian was hiding in the shadows, her eyes fixed here, observing all of Beryl's movements.

Magic was quietly concocting within Vivian's body. As long as Beryl had any attacking tendency, she would instantly save Merlin.

This was a silent struggle around Merlin. Whether Belhomos lurking inside Beryl could be confirmed depended entirely on what the other party would do!

However, facts proved that Vivian underestimated Belhomos's alertness and patience. After so much difficulty for the soul to escape the blood pool, how could it easily expose itself?

Unable to control the entire demon race and win the final victory, Belhomos would absolutely not expose any flaw, disguising himself until the very last moment!

Belhomos's aged hand hovered over Merlin's head, the killing intent quietly dissipating, his gaze falling into hesitation—

Wait, if I kill him here, I will be easily suspected.

This child is not an ordinary demon, but Vivian's son.

If I make a move, I probably cannot explain this matter, and might even expose myself.

All the high-level demons are nearby, which is too dangerous for me, obviously not worth doing.

Belhomos was right. If it attacked Merlin here, Vivian would expose everything about it at the Seven Kings Conference.

Wanting to use Beryl's body to fight against all the demon lords gathered here obviously lacks strength.

Moreover, the God-sealing Vessel exists. Although it has no effect on its true body, since it occupies Beryl's body!

And the matter of seizing the founding demon's body will also surface. If Belhomos wants to find a next usable puppet, it might not be so easy.

Although Belhomos very much wants to kill Merlin now and eliminate the future trouble, he cannot make a move here, or rather, he cannot make a move personally, which would arouse other demons' suspicion.

Only to see Belhomos withdraw all his killing intent, revealing a kindly smile on his face, and gently stroke Merlin's hair—

"You are truly a good child."

title: Chapter 10 — Shake
content:
Chapter 10 — Shake

Volume 34 · Chapter 10

“What is your name?” Behemoth asked.

“Merlin Lucifel,” Merlin answered honestly, thinking that not all monarchs were strange figures. Berial and Asmodeus were both fine, at least they seemed kind.

“Good name,” Behemoth nodded, remembering Merlin's name deeply. “Your eyes are beautiful. Has anyone ever told you that you resemble a great figure from the demon race?”

“Ah? Who?” Merlin furrowed his brows in confusion. No one had ever said he looked like someone or other.

“The Prophet,” Behemoth gazed at Merlin's eyes, hoping to see something.

“Who is the Prophet?” Merlin scratched his head in surprise, unable to understand Berial's words.

Seeing that Merlin didn't react as Behemoth had expected, doubt began to creep into his mind. Could this child have no connection to the Prophet? No, he couldn't jump to conclusions yet.

“The Prophet is a demon I respect. It did many things that changed the history of the demon race.”

“Sorry, I don't know him, nor have I heard of him,” Merlin shrugged his shoulders, showing a regretful expression.

“It's fine. You may go back. Tell your mother that if I have time, I will visit her,” Behemoth smiled.

Merlin left with his head down, secretly glancing at Berial. He thought Berial had a good personality, but there was an inexplicable sense of dissonance.

Behemoth smiled as he watched Merlin leave, but his face grew increasingly gloomy, a heavy killing intent rising in his heart—

Before I completely break free from the seal's control, I must find a way to eliminate this child first, no matter what.

Whether or not he has a connection to that Prophet, I will not allow any obstacles to appear in the future.

Vivian, hiding in the shadows, dispersed the magic she had been gathering for a long time. The expected event did not happen, causing a great动摇 in her heart—

Didn't he act?

Does that mean Behemoth isn't in Berial?

Where exactly did my guess go wrong?

A few days after returning to the First Demon Lord Palace, Vivian still couldn't sleep at night, instead thinking by the dim oil lamp.

She didn't believe that Behemoth, knowing about the prophecy, would have no intention of acting against Merlin.

Other than Behemoth not being in Berial, there seemed to be no other explanation for this.

Abaddon respectfully accompanied Vivian, hesitantly saying, “Could it be that Berial really has no problems? Our deductions weren't accurate. Where exactly did the problem arise?”

Vivian had been thinking for many days and gradually realized a major mistake, “The problem lies in our assumption that Behemoth can steal memories.”

“Why?” Abaddon asked curiously.

“If I were Behemoth and could read the puppet's memories, I would occupy the body of the Chief Judge Caprio, use the Sealing Vessel to capture the high-ranking demons of the demon race, and then destroy the Blood Pool Seal to gain complete freedom,” Vivian paused, then said solemnly, “However, the recent Seven Kings' Meeting ended smoothly. Doesn't that seem strange? Don't forget, only the历代 judges know where the Sealing Vessel is hidden. Behemoth's inaction already proves it can't read memories.”

“So, if only a few demons who know the prophecy remain silent, then the Prophet's prophecy will never be known to it,” Abaddon said in a low voice.

“That's uncertain. Mainly, I have to blame myself. I once mentioned to several other demons that Merlin is the child of the prophecy. As long as Behemoth is patient enough, it wouldn't be difficult for it to find out the content of the prophecy,” Vivian sighed. She had told some demons that Merlin was the child mentioned in the Prophet's prophecy.

Abaddon was at a loss for words, feeling the situation had become extremely complicated, “Then, since Berial didn't attack Prince Merlin, does that mean it's no longer a suspect?”

“Not necessarily. As long as it's a first-generation demon, it's impossible to clear all suspicion, because whether Behemoth knows the content of the Prophet's prophecy is an uncertain factor,” Vivian rubbed her temples, feeling very headache.

“Assuming Behemoth knows the prophecy, but it didn't attack Prince Merlin, wouldn't that prove Berial's innocence?” Abaddon asked in surprise.

“No. At that time, there were demon elders and many monarchs nearby. It might have been afraid that attacking Merlin would expose its identity, so it chose to continue hiding. This possibility still exists. With Berial's strength, it's clearly not capable of fighting all the high-ranking demons of the demon race,” Vivian lowered her head and spoke of her original plan, “If Berial had attacked Merlin at that time, things would have been much easier. Boldly attacking the child of the Prophet's prophecy would have been enough evidence. I would have exposed everything about Behemoth and联合 other monarchs to suppress Berial at the Seven Kings' Meeting. Even if it could continuously occupy the bodies of first-generation demons, it would be useless. We could imprison all first-generation demons and examine them one by one, eventually catching Behemoth.”

After hearing Vivian's words, Abaddon sighed in his heart. The key issue was still the lack of evidence. If they arbitrarily accused Berial of being a puppet without evidence, Vivian would definitely become a laughingstock at the Seven Kings' Meeting. Few demons would be willing to believe this.

Vivian frowned, suddenly saying, “Actually, I've already started to doubt that Berial has become a puppet.”

“Why? Didn't you just say that any first-generation demon can't be cleared of suspicion?” Abaddon widened his eyes in surprise.

“Assume that before the Seven Kings' Meeting, Behemoth had already occupied Berial's body, was adapting to life in this era, and collecting all usable information. Then, after the Seven Kings' Meeting, it should have had no reason to continue hiding. You see, if Behemoth completely breaks free from the seal, no one in the demon race can be its match, not even the Sealing Vessel would be effective against it. It could easily achieve its goal,” Vivian took a deep breath and said in confusion, “But several days have already passed, and the Blood Pool Seal remains stable, showing no abnormalities. If Berial had become a puppet, I can't understand why the seal hasn't been destroyed yet?”

Abaddon suddenly realized this was indeed abnormal, “What is Behemoth hesitating about? We completely don't know who it's in. Perhaps we should directly announce the news and let all demons increase their vigilance.”

“No! That's the worst course of action. Do you remember when we suspected each other? If the news is announced, the demon race will immediately fall into chaos, with endless mutual suspicion,” Vivian rejected the suggestion, saying slowly, “Now is exactly the period of the papacy transition. A group of the Goddess of Light's lackeys are constantly attacking various Demon Lord Palaces to establish merit. If demons can't unite, it will be even more dangerous.”

Abaddon sighed wearily, “What exactly should we do to avoid this crisis?”

Time passed slowly, the room was silent, the dim light casting the shadows of the two people.

Vivian remained silent for a long time, feeling she had reached a dead end. She slowly closed her eyes—

“Indeed, the Prophet's prophecy is irreversible. It will eventually happen.”

“Perhaps we should wait for the right时机 and place all our hopes in the future.”

title: Chapter 11 — Feigning Death
content:
Chapter 11 — Feigning Death

Volume 34 · Chapter 11

"Future prospects?" Abaddon couldn't understand what Vivian meant.

"That's right, since we can't drag Behemoth out, we might as well prepare in advance." Vivian said meaningfully.

"What do you plan to do?" Abaddon asked curiously.

"I plan to abandon the First Demon Lord Palace." Vivian replied seriously.

"This..." Abaddon was startled, his breath catching, and said in a low voice, "This isn't good, is it? Abandoning the First Demon Lord Palace is a major matter, I hope you'll think it over carefully."

"If we can't find Behemoth, the demon race will become very dangerous. Leaving the Demon Lord Palace is actually the safest option." Vivian had already made her preparations. If Behemoth successfully broke free from its seal, then leaving the Demon Lord Palace would make her the force that could save the demon race. It was much better than staying in the Demon Lord Palace waiting to be caught.

Seeing Vivian's determined gaze, Abaddon knew she had made up her mind, so he asked, "Do you already have a specific strategy?"

"Yes, I plan to use the upcoming Crusade Army's attack. I'll fake my death at the hands of the Gun Hero, O'Brian, and cut off all connections with the demon race. Let all the demons, including the hidden Behemoth, believe I've died in battle." Vivian slowly explained her plan, using the Church's power to fabricate a lie of death.

"This probably won't fool the other demons, will it? The entire demon race knows you're a genius among the second-generation demons. With enough time, your strength will eventually be comparable to the first-generation rulers. Who would believe you'd be defeated so easily by a human Hero? Unless that Gun Hero is also extremely powerful, it would be hard to dispel all the demons' doubts." Abaddon felt this plan was too fake. Vivian, known as a genius among the second-generation demons, being killed by a human Hero was hard to believe.

"As far as I know, the Crusade Army led by the Gun Hero O'Brian is about to enter the Death Swamp. His strength isn't weak; he's said to be the most likely candidate to become the new Legendary Hero. If I'm defeated by him, there shouldn't be many demons who would suspect I faked my death." Vivian speculated.

"But I've heard this Hero is only at the peak of the Saint-tier, completely insignificant compared to you." Abaddon was astonished, frowning. If O'Brian could defeat Vivian, it would be the greatest upset in demon history.

"Strength isn't just about appearances. Having the qualifications to become a Legendary Hero means he's definitely more than just a Saint-tier peak. Besides, we can make some arrangements..." Vivian paused, then asked, "I had you catch a three-eyed snake two days ago, did you bring it?"

"I brought it. I've already successfully tamed it."

Abaddon lifted his arm, and a black, writhing snake slowly crawled out from his sleeve. Its sharp, beady eyes were alert, its red tongue flicking in and out as it emitted a cold "hiss" sound.

The three-eyed snake was a type of magical beast. Although its power wasn't great, and its intimidation factor couldn't compare to other magical beasts, it had the ability to move silently in the dark. Moreover, its venom was extremely potent!

Anyone bitten by a three-eyed snake would have their internal organs begin to rot, and their magic and qi would wildly leak out, making it hard to gather them. It was practically the best killer among magical beasts for dealing with warriors and mages!

Weaker prey would die within seven days of being bitten, while stronger individuals could recover by resting and slowly expelling the toxins from their bodies.

"Your Majesty, what do you need this snake for? To be honest, it doesn't smell very good."

"If I'm poisoned and then defeated by the Gun Hero, the credibility of my fake death will be much higher. There will be very few demons who would suspect this." Vivian's gaze became resolute as she rolled up her sleeve, revealing her pale wrist.

Abaddon stared in shock, thinking Vivian was risking her life. "Your Majesty, this is too dangerous! If you're poisoned by the three-eyed snake, you'll need a long time to recover. Going to fight the Gun Hero in this state would be no different from seeking death!"

"If even you think so, other demons will also deeply believe in my death. This is exactly the result I want." Vivian said solemnly.

"You're joking with your own life. I don't recommend doing something so dangerous. What if something goes wrong? The consequences would be unbearable. Can't you just pretend to be poisoned?" Abaddon shook his head repeatedly, unable to accept Vivian's idea.

"Do you think pretending to be poisoned could deceive the eyes of other demons?" Vivian retorted, then continued to reassure him, "Don't worry, Abaddon. Even if I'm poisoned, I can still escape from the Hero's hands. That's not difficult for me."

Abaddon's brows were tightly furrowed, hesitating to carry out Vivian's orders.

"Abaddon, this is an order. You need to do as I say. This is my choice, and I've made all the necessary mental preparations." Vivian's tone turned severe, her sharp gaze allowing no room for doubt.

"You're crazy."

Abaddon gritted his teeth and gave the order to the three-eyed snake in his sleeve. The snake's head glowed with a crimson light, and a third, eerie eye appeared!

The three-eyed snake twisted its body, baring its sharp fangs, and bit down on Vivian's pale wrist. The venom quickly entered her body.

The next day, the entire First Demon Lord Palace knew the news: Vivian had been bitten by a three-eyed snake while resting the previous night and needed a long period of recuperation.

At Vivian's bedside, Merlin and Lilith had come to visit their mother.

At this time, Vivian had already been poisoned and looked extremely pale and tired.

If Vivian were to collapse during this period, the demons of the First Demon Lord Palace would all be in danger.

Lilith stood by the bed, tightly holding Vivian's cold hand. "Mom, how are you feeling? Are you uncomfortable?"

"It's nothing serious. I just need to rest for a while, don't worry so much." Vivian forced a faint smile.

"Why are you being so careful?" Merlin's eyes were anxious, unsure how to help Vivian alleviate her pain.

"Maybe I've been too tired lately and didn't notice the poisonous snake entering the room." Vivian's tone was helpless, her exhaustion impossible to conceal.

Merlin fell silent, thinking that if only he could help his mother share the burden, but unfortunately, he could do nothing.

"Your Highnesses, being poisoned by a three-eyed snake requires rest. If you don't have any important matters, please don't disturb your mother." Abaddon stepped forward, speaking solemnly.

"Then, Mom, we'll come visit you again after you've rested. You have to get better!" Lilith jumped down from the bed and quietly walked out.

Merlin hesitated for a long time before saying in a very awkward tone, "You should rest well. I'll take good care of Lilith and make sure she doesn't cause any trouble."

"Then I'll leave it to you." Vivian smiled, watching her children leave before her expression suddenly turned serious. "Abaddon, spread the news of my poisoning. Let the other Demon Lord Palaces know as well."

"Understood." Abaddon slightly bowed his head, then hesitated before asking, "Is this really worth it? Have you considered what will happen to the two young masters?"

"They must leave the Demon Lord Palace, especially Merlin. Before Behemoth reveals itself, it's safer for him to live outside. I won't be able to protect this child forever. Perhaps it's time for him to go outside and gain some experience. With his current state, wanting to defeat Behemoth is like a joke."

"Aren't you going to tell them about your fake death?"

"Abaddon, you must understand that only a lie that can deceive one's own people can make the enemy deeply believe it."

title: Chapter 12 — Mission
content:
Chapter 12 — Mission

Volume 34 · Chapter 12

A few days passed, but Vivian, poisoned by the snake venom, showed no sign of improvement and still had not appeared before the demons.

The toxin of the three-eyed snake isn't easily expelled; it requires a long period of rest, at least half a year.

Merlin felt he should do something for Vivian, so these past few days he frequently ran to the library, hoping to find a quick solution to the snake poison.

That day, Ophelia lay in wait halfway along the road and again saw Merlin rushing to the library, unable to suppress an evil smile on her face—

Recently Lord Merlin has been fond of going to the library; perhaps I can take advantage of that to create an opportunity for us to be alone.

Running into each other in the library—what a romantic encounter!

Our relationship will surely make rapid progress! Ohohoho~

“Ophelia.

While Ophelia was daydreaming, someone suddenly called from behind; she turned in surprise and saw her strict father, Abaddon.

Ophelia didn't much like this rigid father, thinking Abaddon was an old-fashioned stick-in-the-mud who couldn't adapt.

“Who did I think it was? Oh, it's you. What do you need? I respect you, Father.”

“Abaddon hesitated a moment; his normally stern demeanor made him a bit nervous in front of Ophelia. “I'm not here to scold you; I just have something important to say.”

“Who would believe that? Every time you call me, it's just to scold me. I really don't understand what you have against me.” Ophelia pouted, not wanting to talk to her father.

“I just hope you become more outstanding so you can succeed me someday.” Abaddon said solemnly.

“Sorry, I'm not interested.” Ophelia curled the corner of her mouth; she'd heard this kind of talk so often her ears were calloused.

Abaddon sighed, gave up on trying to talk to his daughter, and instead asked seriously, “Is your relationship with Lord Merlin that good?”

“Huh?” Ophelia blinked, then immediately replied confidently, “Of course. Lord Merlin and I are very close—he's always clinging to me, calling me ‘Ophelia-sister,’ and I can't shake him off, humph~”

“Really? I didn't expect Lord Merlin to be so odd, actually getting along well with you.” Abaddon sounded surprised, clearly Vivian as Merlin's mother had never managed to bridge the gap.

“Maybe that's just his unique charm?” Ophelia flipped her hair, feeling quite pleased.

“Then this task is yours to handle.” Abaddon produced a mysterious object tightly wrapped in black cloth and handed it to Ophelia.

“What is this? If it's troublesome, I won't bother with it.” Ophelia muttered discontentedly.

“This is an item left by the prophet of the age of the gods, called the demon sword Banri Garan, now serving as a token representing the arrogant ruler.” Abaddon unwrapped the black cloth, revealing an antiquated, unassuming red-lacquered long blade.

Ophelia examined Banri Garan. Though she had heard of it, this was her first time seeing the genuine article—far more ordinary than she imagined, hard to picture this katana as a royal artifact. “Banri Garan doesn't look like anything precious.”

“Don't underestimate this blade; it's the only thing left by the mysterious prophet, and it's one of the two blades he kept at his side. Legend says it has the power to devour enemies' lives and can summon scorching flames comparable to the sun.” Abaddon said solemnly, though he had never witnessed Banri Garan's power himself; still, from the fragmented information left behind, one could tell the blade was extraordinary.

“If it's that powerful, why have I never seen Queen Vivian use it? It seems even the former king Mephistopheles never used it either.” Ophelia wondered, puzzled that such a mighty weapon had never been wielded by any of the lustful rulers throughout history.

“Banri Garan cannot be drawn by just anyone; to this day only that prophet himself has been able to unsheathe the blade—Mephistopheles and Queen Vivian have both tried, and clearly they cannot use this weapon.” Abaddon's gaze slid over the scabbard of Banri Garan, already marked with the blotches of time, “However, thanks to its original owner, it holds extraordinary significance for the entire demon race, which is why it has been preserved intact to this day and serves as the symbol of the lord of the First Demon Lord Palace.”

“A weapon that can't be used? That's just a useless ornament, right~” Ophelia shrugged, thinking her father was exaggerating.

“Not exactly. Aside from that mysterious prophet, no one can be certain that Banri Garan won't have a new master in the future—no one can guarantee it. The former king Mephistopheles once said…” Abaddon recalled, speaking slowly, “Whoever can draw Banri Garan is the true lord of the First Demon Lord Palace, a demon capable of rivaling the great prophet as the strongest.”

“??? Ophelia didn't believe such mystical nonsense; since neither Mephistopheles nor Vivian could wield Banri Garan, it's unlikely any demon will ever be able to. “It sounds like something important that should be kept by Queen Vivian herself—why did you take it out to show off? Is there no problem?”

“It was Queen Vivian who told me to take it out.” Abaddon dragged Banri Garan, his gaze fixed on his daughter. “Ophelia, this is yours to keep.”

“Huh? What did you say? Give it to me?” Ophelia pointed at herself, incredulous. “Why me? You wouldn't think I'm the strongest demon capable of pulling it out, would you?!”

“What nonsense are you spouting? Can't you have a bit of self-awareness? How could you possibly be the strongest demon? I've never even dreamed of such a thing; with your personality, if you could serve beside the strongest demon without suspicion, that'd be good enough, yet you still dream of becoming Banri Garan's master? You'd be better off washing a few more dishes each day.” Abaddon scowled, reprimanding her, unable to fathom where Ophelia got such confidence.

“Tch!” Ophelia flicked her lips in annoyance, her pride trampled by Abaddon, feeling deep shame, still thinking her father had changed, unprecedentedly giving her encouragement.

“This is Queen Vivian's wish; I believe you are the best choice to temporarily safeguard Banri Garan, and handing it to you will put my mind at ease.”

Abaddon lowered his head, speaking with dignified tone, “Remember, Banri Garan is crucial; at a critical moment, even if you sacrifice your life, you must not let it come to harm.”

Ophelia furrowed her brows, unable to see how this trinket could be worth more than her life, but her father's authority kept her from retorting, “Do you want me to keep it forever?”

“Not at all. If the future Lord Merlin can stand on his own, then you will personally hand Banri Garan over to him—that is your mission.”

“Lord Merlin standing on his own?” Ophelia's expression grew complex, unable to stop herself from muttering inwardly,

“Isn't that just saying I have to keep it all along?”

“No difference, really.”

title: Chapter 13 — Sanctuary Shattered
content:
Chapter 13 — Sanctuary Shattered

Volume 34 · Chapter 13

In the Demon Lord Palace's library, Merlin fetched many books on pharmacology, hoping to find information on how to counteract the three-eyed snake venom, but he had been holed up in the library for many days with no gain at all, and even his sister Lilith called him a bookworm. Merlin expressionlessly closed the heavy books, leaned wearily against the chair, and stared at the gloomy ceiling. “Indeed… still no good,” Merlin realized he didn’t know much about this world; his strength was lacking, and his knowledge was also deficient to a certain extent. After all, he wasn’t some war god, divine doctor, or academic prodigy who had crossed over—just an ordinary high school student who wanted to make waves in another world, which was as fanciful as Arabian Nights. Although Merlin knew some modern methods for treating snake venom, such as obtaining serum from venomous snakes, he had no idea how to actually make it. Ding dong dong— a noisy sound came, interrupting Merlin’s thoughts; he followed the noise and saw a hunchbacked ugly demon who had accidentally knocked over a water bucket. Merlin frowned; although he had lived in the Demon Lord Palace for a long time, the demon before him felt completely unfamiliar, as if he had never seen it before— does this demon even exist in the Demon Lord Palace? With such a distinctive appearance, I shouldn’t have no impression of it. The ugly demon scrambled up from the ground in fear, just about to tidy the water bucket and mop, but seeing Merlin approach, it hastily bowed low and said humbly, “I’m very sorry, I was momentarily careless and disturbed your reading; please give me a moment, I’ll clean this up right away.” “It’s alright, are you a demon of the First Demon Lord Palace?” Merlin asked curiously. “Yes, I am the demon specifically assigned to clean the library,” the ugly demon replied very respectfully. “What’s your name?” Merlin pressed, if it were a cadre‑type demon I shouldn’t be unaware of it. The ugly demon hesitated, nervously saying, “I am the descendant of a sinner; my filthy name is not worthy of your knowing.” Merlin’s mind filled with question marks; he couldn’t understand the world’s natives’ mindset of ingraining class distinctions into their bones. The wealth and glory created by ancestors are easily passed down to descendants, and birth in a sense decides many things. With the mindset of a civilized world, Merlin could not accept such a thing; such backward notions probably only appear in history books. “Can’t you at least lift your head so I can see you?” “My appearance is very ugly; it would inevitably affect your mood, so that would be improper,” the ugly demon lowered its head even further, so humble it didn’t even dare to raise its head. Merlin felt helpless but had no intention of forcing anyone; since it wouldn’t say anything, he let it be. Thus Merlin took out a pure white handkerchief from his pocket and handed it to the ugly demon. “Here, wipe the sewage off your face; thank you for cleaning the library.” “Eh!” the ugly demon was flattered, trembling all over, “This isn’t proper; I’m not worthy of your kindness.” Merlin took a deep breath, his patience wearing thin, “Why all the nonsense? It’s just a handkerchief—don’t make me repeat myself.” The ugly demon hesitated, but under pressure accepted Merlin’s kindness, though it didn’t use the handkerchief to wipe its face; instead it clutched it silently in its palm, afraid to dirty it. Merlin returned to his seat, pondering who this demon really was, though he couldn’t force it to reveal its name. Although the Demon Lord Palace had many low‑rank demons that could be this humble, aside from this one he truly couldn’t find a second. In the vast library, only Merlin remained once again; he resumed reading and偶然 discovered something new in an ancient text— Who is this inheritance crystal? It said it has a high probability of appearing in a dragon’s body and can grant the consumer dragon power. That’s exactly what I want! If I could eat this, would I become stronger? Merlin’s eyes lit up, his heart stirred with eager desire; craving power, upon learning this he became unusually excited. “Your Highness Merlin!” Blackman suddenly appeared, plopping down beside Merlin with a careless grin, “Why are you still reading? How about going hunting? It’s far more fun than holed up in the library~” Merlin glanced at the smirking Blackman; in the whole Demon Lord Palace only this guy had the thickest skin, seemingly not taking his princely status to heart at all. Although Merlin knew Blackman meant no harm and was far kinder than the ever‑insulting Amon, he still couldn’t adapt to his noisy, simple‑minded nature. “I don’t want to go; stop bothering me.” “Your Highness, demons don’t like bookworms; only a strong physique can attract countless demons’ gazes,” Blackman said, crossing his arms, his muscles tensing like boulders. “Get lost; I like quiet,” Merlin replied expressionlessly. “You don’t like a strong physique? Or do you prefer a soft, feminine figure?
