Then I’ll just…,” Blackman slipped his hand into his own trousers, earnestly saying, “Whatever you like, I have it.” “Stop!” Merlin’s face turned pale at the thought of seeing such an eyesore; “You’re fine as is; don’t just reach into your trousers in front of me, it’s disgusting!” “What’s disgusting…,” Blackman felt uneasy, so he said awkwardly, “You’ve been holed up in the library these days; it’s a bit worrying—Lilith keeps pestering you to play with her every day.” “I’m not a child; how could I possibly spend all day playing with Lilith?” Merlin answered sternly, then suddenly shifted the topic, “By the way, what’s the name of the slave who cleans the library?” “Huh?” Blackman immediately wiped the smile off his face, “Did you see that ugly demon named Dulu? Did it say anything strange to you?” “No,” Merlin shook his head, silently noting the name Dulu—indeed he had never heard of this demon before. “Good, I advise you to stay away from it; demons in the Demon Lord Palace don’t like approaching this guy; in short, it’s just an unpleasant ugly monster,” Blackman replied hesitantly. “Why do the demons shun it?” Merlin felt a pang of empathy, his interest sparked. “Because its father was a deserter in the holy war; in demon society deserters are cowards, easily despised and rejected; as the child of a deserter, Dulu may be competent and qualified for a cadre position, but it can never be trusted with important duties and is relegated to menial tasks like cleaning the library,” Blackman paused, sighing, “I think Dulu also knows it’s unlikable, so it rarely appears before other demons; even when cleaning the library it chooses times when no one is around, so your encountering it really surprised me.” Merlin lowered his head, unsure how to judge this; he thought, the child of a deserter—not only honor but also stigma is inherited by descendants; people in this other world live harder than I imagined. After Blackman left, Merlin pondered for a long time; he still felt sympathy for Dulu’s plight. With Merlin’s mindset, he truly couldn’t understand that ancestors’ sins should be borne by their innocent descendants. Moreover, although Merlin’s situation in the Demon Lord Palace is far better than Dulu’s, he too faces exclusion and discrimination. In a way, Merlin sees a kindred spirit in Dulu, so sympathy arises unbidden. Suddenly, the figure of the intelligence officer Shu emerged from the shadow of a massive bookshelf, holding a book. Shu constantly follows Merlin’s side; in the Demon Lord Palace he also handles Merlin’s safety, acting as a hidden guard. Compared to Ophelia’s fervent, almost obsessive care, Shu appears far colder; he only shows up when Merlin’s life is in danger, otherwise he’s as absent as non‑existent air. Although Shu’s care isn’t meticulous, he is indeed Merlin’s favorite demon because he grants him ample freedom and privacy, and he is the most decent‑behaved demon among them! In the First Demon Lord Palace, finding a demon with a normal personality is probably only clear to Merlin himself, which makes Shu exceptionally rare and precious. “Your Highness, are you thinking about Dulu?” Shu asked softly without looking up. “Exactly,” Merlin lifted his head and replied, “I feel it’s quite an interesting fellow.” Shu’s icy goat‑like eyes shifted as he murmured lowly, “I think you’d better not dwell on these matters, and certainly avoid getting close to Dulu.” “Why?” Merlin turned his head in surprise; if Blackman said that it wouldn’t be strange, but Shu saying the same is odd. “Because it bears a stain,” Shu answered succinctly. “That’s its father’s stain, not its own, right?” Merlin spread his hands. “Your view is overly naïve; offspring not only inherit their parents’ blood but also inherit their parents’ spirit—this is undeniable, just like my and Ophelia’s families, which have always served the monarch, regarding the protection of the monarch as a lifelong mission, even sacrificing one’s lives, and this spirit is passed down generation after generation; but Dulu is different—its father was a deserter, so it can only inherit the cowardly spirit, destined to be a weakling devoid of any faith, merely a walking corpse driven by desire,” Shu explained with reason and evidence, adding, “Therefore Dulu is not worthy of your trust—a deserter’s son will only betray you at the crucial moment.” “My view differs from yours,” Merlin smiled at Shu, meaningfully saying, “I believe every new life is like a blank sheet of paper, not necessarily influenced by one’s parents; it is we who write upon that blank page.” Shu remained silent for a long time, then evaluated, “Your idea is unique; I can’t judge whether it’s correct.” Merlin gave a dry laugh, happily saying, “Shu, chatting with you makes me happy; other demons have such strange personalities, only you are truly normal.” “Thank you for your praise; indeed I am the most reliable demon in the Demon Lord Palace,” Shu lowered his head, silently flipping a page of the yellow book hidden behind the ancient texts— on it was depicted a lifelike muscular man stepping out of the forest, commonly known as the forest0 fairy. Merlin had thought he could live a long time under his mother’s protection, but disaster had already descended unnoticed. Vivian, poisoned by snake venom, was defeated in person by the Spear Hero O’Brien; her soul seemed to have been burned to ash by fire. Nearly desperate Merlin shielded his frightened sister Lilith behind him and gazed up at the great shadow that had dominated his life— O’Brien wielded the spear named “Scarlet Enchantress,” coldly pointing at Merlin; the chill of death made him gasp— “Weak demon child…” The space is limited, so the demons of the Demon Lord Palace can only be written this much; there’s no chance to continue. The plot of assaulting the First Demon Lord Palace is skipped outright—I’ve already covered it earlier, so no repetition; interested readers can flip back. All previously detailed events are omitted as they’ve been covered; no need to repeat them. Moreover, some details may deviate because the viewpoint differs, revealing points never disclosed before. Also, this volume isn’t long, roughly similar to the Slum Astrologer, and will finish soon. Lastly, please cast your monthly vote. 9('w' )9

title: Chapter 14 — Revealed Ambition
content:
Chapter 14 — Revealed Ambition

Volume 34 · Chapter 14

The Crusade Army led by O’Brien successfully defeated the ruler of the First Demon Lord Palace, Lucifer II Vivian.

They created new history in a single stroke; for the first time, the Holy Church had succeeded in killing a Demon Lord and occupied the Demon Lord Palace.

When the news reached the Vatican Temple, the believers held grand celebration ceremonies to commemorate this historic moment.

Without a doubt, O’Brien would firmly become the second legendary Hero, forever recorded on the temple walls, enjoying the highest honor of the Holy Church.

Geogen, the Cardinal who accompanied the expedition, also secured his due筹码 (leverage), establishing merits sufficient to defeat other candidates for the papal succession.

As long as no serious problems arose, Geogen’s appointment as the new Pope was a foregone conclusion; no one could threaten him.

After Vivian’s defeat, the demons of the First Demon Lord Palace fell into chaos. These creatures, who usually appeared fierce, were now fleeing in disarray.

The arrogant O’Brien did not kill Merlin and Lilith but instead spared two demon cubs.

In his eyes, killing two helpless children was the act of a petty person, which would soil his noble soul.

Thus, under Xiu’s cover, Merlin and Lilith escaped the Demon Lord Palace and temporarily lived in a safe place.

The Templars ruthlessly plundered the Demon Lord Palace, destroying anything they couldn’t carry on the spot. Within just a few days, the place was unrecognizable.

Geogen and O’Brien even discovered a secret the demons had hidden: a massive blood pool buried deep beneath the Demon Lord Palace.

This disaster at the First Demon Lord Palace did not last long. Upon learning of Vivian’s defeat, the Elder Council quickly notified the rulers of the other Demon Lord Palaces, immediately organizing a demonic coalition that advanced majestically toward the Swamp of Death.

Worried that other Demon Lords might arrive soon to reinforce, and under immense pressure, Geogen ordered the Templars to evacuate the Swamp of Death immediately to avoid direct confrontation with the demonic coalition.

Although O’Brien did not want to abandon the First Demon Lord Palace he had so hard-won, he was forced to agree to the retreat after Geogen reprimanded him.

For Geogen, occupying the Demon Lord Palace held little significance; he had already secured the leverage needed to compete for the papacy and saw no need to allow the Templar Order to suffer greater losses.

The war ended in just seven days. The Church of Light achieved an unprecedented victory, obtaining a large amount of valuable items from the First Demon Lord Palace.

In the Elder Council Chamber, the giant magic mirrors used to communicate with the rulers of each Demon Lord Palace all lit up, discussing the matter.

The demon replacing Vivian at the meeting was Amun, a high-ranking official with immense status and prestige. He had clearly become the noble most qualified to temporarily take over the First Demon Lord Palace besides Vivian himself—

“Since the Church’s army has withdrawn from the Swamp of Death, we can catch our breath for a moment.” Leviathan paused, then spoke solemnly, “Fortunately, those bastards didn’t destroy the Blood Pool seal. Otherwise, the consequences would have been unimaginable.”

“Exactly. The Demon Lord Palace is merely an empty shell; what truly matters is the Blood Pool seal. I haven’t slept in days since hearing the news of Vivian’s death. If the terrifying creature in the Blood Pool escapes, we’re all doomed.” Beelzebub yawned tiredly. Knowing Vivian had died brought him no sympathy; in fact, he felt some schadenfreude. Maintaining the stability of the Blood Pool seal was more important than anything else.

Belial remained expressionless within the magic mirror. Except for Vivian, none of the rulers yet realized that Behemoth’s soul had escaped.

“This is strange. With Vivian’s powerful strength, it seems none of you here, aside from Uncle Belial, could match her. How could she be defeated by a human Hero?” Asmodeus’s look of suspicion grew heavier. He found it hard to believe, feeling there was something suspicious about it.

“Indeed. Is that Hero named O’Brien so powerful that he could defeat us single-handedly?” Leviatan asked in surprise. He had killed Heroes before; most of their strength was mediocre.

“Powerful my foot. I personally killed the Church’s so-called Legendary Hero. Although his strength was much higher than ordinary Heroes, it still wasn’t enough to threaten our lives.” Mammon suddenly interjected. Hearing that Vivian died at the hands of a Hero seemed absurd to him.

“How exactly did Vivian lose? Was she mocking us?” Beelzebub frowned, believing this matter should be investigated thoroughly.

“Cough! cough!” Amun cleared his throat twice, speaking on behalf of the rulers. He felt very nervous. “Actually, Your Majesty Vivian was accidentally bitten by a Three-Eyed Snake before engaging the Hero, and had ingested snake venom.”

“Hmm? I seem to recall hearing about this. If Vivian contracted snake venom, causing her mana to dissipate, then losing to the Hero wouldn’t be surprising.” Samael remained silent for a long time before suddenly remembering he had casually heard news of Vivian being bitten by a snake recently.

“No way? That vicious female hooligan who made even dragons tremble got bitten by a snake???” Beelzebub’s face clearly showed disbelief.

“The Three-Eyed Snake is a magical beast with secretive movements. If one isn’t careful, it’s indeed easy to get bitten. There’s nothing strange about that.” Asmodeus explained softly.

“What were you subordinates doing when Vivian fought the Hero? Why didn’t you help? Are you all useless?” Leviatan loudly questioned, venting his resentment onto Amun.

“That Hero named O’Brien proposed a one-on-one challenge, which Your Majesty Vivian accepted. We really couldn’t interfere.” Amun answered nervously.

Mammon couldn’t help but burst out laughing on the spot. “Hahaha, why fight one-on-one when you can brawl in a group? There really are such stupid guys~”

“In that case, Vivian’s death wasn’t undeserved. But honestly, I’ve always disliked that stinking woman~” Beelzebub hummed.

“Beelzebub, watch your words. Vivian is our comrade. Her passing should make us feel sorrow, not schadenfreude.” Samael said in a very serious tone.

“None of my business~” Beelzebub shrugged carelessly. “Is there anything else? If not, I’m going on a picnic with my sister. Don’t waste my precious time.”

“Don’t leave so hastily. We still need to help handle matters following the loss of the First Demon Lord Palace. Now that Vivian is dead, we must find a successor.” Asmodeus called out to Beelzebub.

“I remember Vivian had two children, right? Either one could inherit. The main thing is maintaining the Blood Pool seal regularly.” Beelzebub said impatiently.

“Your Honors, actually, both princes went missing during the chaos and cannot currently take over the First Demon Lord Palace. Moreover, they are young and lack judgment regarding affairs; it may not be suitable for them to inherit the throne right now.” Amun suddenly emphasized, hoping to dispel the thoughts of the Demon Lords present.

“What should we do? It won’t do for no one to inherit the Demon Lord Palace?” Leviatan frowned tightly. Without anyone maintaining the Blood Pool seal, it was a dangerous situation.

A smile gradually spread across Amun’s face. He felt it was time to reveal the ambition he had harbored deep in his heart for years—

“If Your Majesties have no objections, I can temporarily take over the Demon Lord Palace and serve as the Acting Demon Lord.”

title: Chapter 15 — The Dove Occupying the Magpie's Nest (Monthly Ticket Bonus Update)
content:
Chapter 15 — The Dove Occupying the Magpie's Nest (Monthly Ticket Bonus Update)

Volume 34 · Chapter 15

As soon as Amon finished speaking, the atmosphere in the Elder Council fell silent, with no one willing to respond to the topic.
Even Chief Arbiter Caprio frowned, thinking Amon's words were highly inappropriate, as the Demon Lord is not a position just anyone can hold.
Even as an acting Demon Lord, one must possess royal bloodline; it simply isn't the turn of other demons to take the role.
"Hahaha!" Mammon laughed, bluntly disparaging, "What kind of lowly creature are you? Is the monarch's throne something you can lay your hands on?"
"Hmph! Someone like you, a minor figure, would never appear here under normal circumstances; don't you understand that?" Beelzebub said mockingly, not even considering Amon worthy of attention—his presence here is completely out of place.
Amon broke out in nervous cold sweat, lacking any courage to rebut the monarchs' ridicule, saying, "Your Majesties have misunderstood; I mean to temporarily act as Demon Lord, and if I find the missing two Highnesses, I will immediately step down."
"Even if it were the right to temporarily act as monarch, it's not your turn; why not let Beelzebub's sister Miranda take over the First Demon Lord Palace?" Leviathan said bluntly.
"Shut up! Don't drag everything onto my adorable Miranda; she's my sister, not a tool in your eyes!" Beelzebub snapped angrily, "Taking on the role of acting Demon Lord certainly isn't a matter of a day or two, and wanting to see my sister would become difficult; I could never bear this responsibility, even if beaten to death."
"Until Viviane's child is found, who will manage the First Demon Lord Palace is indeed a problem," Samael mused, feeling that a temporary agent is indeed needed.
Caprio, who knows the First Demon Lord Palace well and also knows Amon is unreliable, questioned, "Where is Abaddon? If we must choose an acting Demon Lord, he would be more suitable."
Amon's eyes flashed with dissatisfaction; looking at Caprio, he felt hatred so intense it seemed only sheepish, "I also don't know; after the Demon Lord Palace was seized, I don't know where he went, and he hasn't returned to this day."
"Caprio thought the situation was getting troublesome, letting Amon take over the First Demon Lord Palace? He's very uneasy.
"Isn't it good if someone volunteers to take on this responsibility?"
Beelzebub's body occupied by Behemoth, Belial remained silent for a long time, then suddenly spoke in agreement with Amon's proposal.
This caused all the monarchs to fall silent, not daring to oppose outright, wanting to hear what this venerable, esteemed first monarch thought.
Amon excitedly lifted his head, his eyes unable to hide his joy; he never expected the highly esteemed Belial would suddenly support him.
"Since nobody wants to clean up this mess, why not leave it to Amon to handle? His family is a prominent noble house, having earned meritorious service in the Holy War; acting as the Pride Monarch temporarily does not violate demonkind's rules." Behemoth, imitating Belial's tone, spoke on behalf of the other monarchs and made the decision: "Viviane's child is still a minor; logically, they should not have left the Death Swamp area. Why not let Amon send people to search for them, and during this time temporarily entrust him with the administration of the First Demon Lord Palace?"
"Wait a moment, if Amon takes on the Demon Lord duties, who will maintain the stability of the blood pool seal?" Leviathan raised a question.
"I can offer some help; you need not worry. With me present, the blood pool seal will encounter no issues." Behemoth gave an affirmative reply.
Since the first monarch Belial had spoken, the other monarchs and elders present chose silence, with no one questioning his decision.
They probably never imagined that Belial is no longer that venerable elder, and even the habitual troublemaker Beelzebub did not refute this decision.
"I will surely handle this matter well and will not disappoint Your Majesties' expectations," Amon promised excitedly, having already taken the first step toward his dream.
Behemoth's eyes showed a hint of anticipation; he believed Viviane's death was a heaven-sent opportunity for him to intervene in the affairs of the First Demon Lord Palace—
He had been worrying about finding no excuse to kill that child, but the opportunity delivered itself.
Until I deal with Viviane's son, I will not expose myself.
If I were to personally reside in the First Demon Lord Palace, I would inevitably arouse suspicion from the other monarchs, but I can cultivate my own pawn—this fool Amon has utilitarian value.
In the secret chamber of the First Demon Lord Palace, the emergency meeting concluded.
Amon stood before the magic mirror, took a breath, clenched his trembling hands into fists, and immediately felt the allure of power.
Although he is merely a temporary acting Demon Lord, he already regards himself as the true Pride Monarch in his heart.
He has no intention of obediently retrieving Merlin and Lilith; on the contrary, he harbors murderous intent toward the siblings.
Now that Viviane is dead, the siblings and the blood pool seal have become obstacles on Amon's path to kingship.
Only by handling these two matters well can he sit securely on the throne and become the true new Pride Monarch.
Behind him, Ophelia and Blackwell's faces were grim, because the other monarchs had arbitrarily decided to entrust the First Demon Lord Palace to Amon for management—this is clearly not a reasonable decision.
Amon slowly turned around, scrutinizing Ophelia and Blackwell; next, he needs to suppress dissent within the Demon Lord Palace and continually consolidate his position.
"Amon! Her Majesty Viviane is gone; the most important thing now is to find the two Highnesses!" Blackwell warned solemnly.
"Are you instructing me on what to do? When I say to search for the two Highnesses, that's what counts," Amon said haughtily.
"You! ?" Blackwell felt a bit annoyed; the other party shows no concern for Merlin and Lilith's safety.
"When the Holy Temple knights stormed the Demon Lord Palace, it was so chaotic; perhaps the two Highnesses met with misfortune on the road~" Amon said with a meaningful tone.
"What nonsense are you spouting?! I personally saw Shu escorting them away, with Shu protecting them; as long as they don't run into a Hero, how could they possibly meet misfortune!" Ophelia shouted angrily.
"That's not necessarily certain; the area around the Death Swamp often has powerful demons and beasts roaming; if something goes wrong, Amon's lips gradually curled upward, his smile growing increasingly arrogant."
"Amon, you wouldn't really consider yourself the master of the Demon Lord Palace, would you?" Blackwell clenched his fists, his eyes showing growing hostility.
"I am clearly the master here, acknowledged by the other six monarchs; do you disagree?" Amon provoked by raising his chin.
"Merlin and Lilith Highnesses are the true masters; you are not. If you refuse to bring back the two Highnesses, don't blame me for being impolite!" Blackwell's body crackled with electricity that flowed across his flesh.
"Whether to retrieve the two Highnesses depends on my mood; besides, His Majesty Belial has already promised to assist in maintaining the blood pool seal, and I have plenty of time~" Amon idly toyed with his fingers, having no intention of seeking Merlin and Lilith; if they died outside, that would be even better.
Blackwell narrowed his eyes, deeply provoked to the point of unbearable; his electricity—flash—came upon Amon in an instant, both fists gathering lightning and thunder that erupted with a deafening roar—
"Amon!
"You despicable wretch, you don't deserve to stay here!"

title: Chapter 16 — In Name Only
content:
Chapter 16 — In Name Only

Volume 34 · Chapter 16

Lightning flashed, filling the entire secret chamber, and Blakeman, unable to endure any longer, launched an extremely swift assault on Amon on the spot.

Amon was remarkably calm, paying Blakeman no mind at all, lifted his arm and released a pale gold aura shockwave!

"Give me some quiet." As soon as the words left his mouth, the aura shockwave rushed straight into Blakeman's chest, blasting it away mercilessly, leaving a blood streak lingering in midair.

With Amon's sect-level power, there was no pressure in dealing with the Saint-tier Blakeman; a simple lift of his hand could defeat him.

In the First Demon Lord Palace, there were only two demons of sect-level strength, one was Ophelia's father Abaddon, and the other was A...

Now that Vivian had died, Abaddon had mysteriously disappeared, and Amon, having obtained the authority of acting Demon Lord, had become an entity that seemed to cover the sky in the Demon Lord Palace.

With a great crash, Blakeman slammed heavily against the thick walls of the secret chamber, leaving spiderweb-like cracks on the surface.

Blood spilled from Blakeman's mouth corners, his whole body collapsed on the ground, and in the blink of an eye he was defeated by Amon, clutching his chest, unsure how many bones had broken.

Ophelia, worried, hurriedly went forward to check, turned back angrily and shouted, "Amon! Are you mad! ?"

"This isn't my fault, it was the one that struck first at me." Amon spread his hands and put on an innocent look.

"Traitor. Vivian's Majesty has just left, and you can't help but show your fox tail." Blakeman, clutching his chest, cursed harshly, "As long as Merlin and Lilith are fine, your ambition will never be realized, no demon will acknowledge you as the master of this place!"

"Hmph, this isn't up to you. If you don't want to die, you'd better behave. I am now the high ruler." Amon said smugly.

"Pfft! You don't deserve it!" Blakeman spat a mouthful of blood onto the ground.

"It doesn't matter if you don't acknowledge me; someone is willing to admit it." Amon shouted toward the outside of the secret chamber, "Come in."

The door of the secret chamber was slowly opened, and a demon, all in tattered black robes, with a very ugly appearance, slowly walked in from outside. He was the unappreciated deserter's son, Duru!

After seeing Amon, Duru voluntarily knelt before him, expressing his loyalty, with a series of actions without hesitation, as if he had already given up all dignity.

"Hahaha," Amon, somewhat excited, provocatively said, "Did you all hear? It called me Majesty, that's right! I am the third arrogant monarch!"

"Tsk! Duru! Don't you have any dignity? To kneel before Amon? No wonder you are not appreciated, you are as low as a slave!" Ophelia angrily cursed.

Duru was expressionless, as if he hadn't heard, completely ignoring Ophelia's curses, still kneeling before Amon like a loyal servant.

"Duru, would you be willing to humble yourself before me? I won't care about the stains on you like Vivian, and will even give you the opportunity to build your career." Amon asked in a solemn tone.

"I am willing to wholeheartedly serve you, becoming your sharpest blade, that is my lifelong mission." Duru answered in a low voice.

"Very good, you two should also learn well. What's wrong with serving me? I will be more generous and merciful than Vivian, especially you, Ophelia. Amon's eyes revealed greedy desire, speaking seductively, "The queen's position will always be reserved for you, until you change your heart and agree to marry me."

"Dream on!" Ophelia gritted her teeth angrily, thinking that if her father were still alive, it would be better, how could she let Amon run wild here?

Amon left satisfied, clearing all opposition was only a matter of time. He was confident that he could rely on the 'acting' label to become the true Demon Lord.

From the reaction at the meeting, the noble first monarch Belial was willing to help him, which made Amon dream many fantasies.

The more Blakeman looked at Duru, the angrier he became, enduring the severe pain from his chest, he sarcastically said, "Indeed, a deserter's son, truly unworthy of trust. It's right that Vivian's Majesty doesn't appreciate you."

"That's right, I am a deserter's son, innately a coward, who will betray at critical moments." Duru slowly rose from the ground, his gaze ominously looking back at Blakeman, "Then can you answer me a question? Is Amon not perfect in your eyes? Born into a distinguished noble family, serving the Demon Lord Palace's master for generations, how could he betray? Is he not like me, a deserter's son?"

Blakeman was at a loss on the spot, not knowing how to answer Duru's question.

After a little over half a rain, the blood pool seal beneath the First Demon Lord Palace was wildly restless, always at risk of total collapse.

With a drop of blood injected, the restless blood pool instantly calmed.

The mysterious man sent from the Seventh Demon Lord Palace, hidden in a heavy black robe, successfully steadied the seal, then drew his arm back into his sleeve.

Amon meekly followed behind, staring in astonishment, "Who are you, really?"

"My name is Olobasis, son of Belial." Olobasis removed the hat from his head, revealing twisted horns and a huge single eye.

In order to intervene in matters of the First Demon Lord Palace, Behemoth sent Olobasis as his representative to come here, to secretly communicate some matters with Amon.

Although Olobasis seemed to come only to help maintain the stability of the blood pool seal, in reality he came with Behemoth's will, needing to make Amon a pawn.

Since Olobasis had been strictly controlled by Belial from a young age, he had lost his own will, becoming a pure tool, firmly believing that as long as he obeyed his father's words, he would not err.

But what he didn't know was that his father was no longer Belial, but a puppet under Behemoth's control; all the commands he now executes come from the monster beneath the blood pool.

"Son of Belial? Does he have children?" Amon had never heard that Belial had any offspring.

"What are you doubting?" Olobasis, feeling displeased, released pseudo-divine pressure, instantly making Amon gasp for breath!

"I dare not! I have no doubt about your identity!" Amon sweated coldly, thinking perhaps he was a bastard? Why was there no trace of disappearance.

"This time I came here, besides helping you maintain the blood pool seal, I also brought some words my father wants to tell you."

"What does His Majesty Belial want to tell you?" Amon asked cautiously.

Olobasis leaned close to Amon, staring into his eyes, "Do you want to become the true arrogant monarch?"

"Uh!" Amon stared wide-eyed, a drop of cold sweat sliding across his forehead, feeling uncertain about this question.

What does this mean? Is this a test of me?

title: Chapter 17 — Fallen Prince
content:
Chapter 17 — Fallen Prince

Volume 34 · Chapter 17

Amon dared not answer this question casually; he could not tell what stance Belial held, so he could only say politely,
“Becoming a true Sovereign of Pride? I may not have the strength or qualifications for it, but if conditions allow, I can reluctantly bear this heavy responsibility.”
Europath took out a crystal ball and piled it on Amon's face; inside, thick smoke rose, vaguely probing into his secret.
“You are hypocritical, obsessed with power since childhood; your family's elders have high hopes for you, wishing you to reach a higher place.”
“You envy Vivian for being able to sit on the Demon Lord's throne, effortlessly manipulating the fate of countless demons.”
“You envy Vivian's children for being able to inherit this power, thinking they] have no right to become Demon Lord.”
“You think you are more suitable than them, am I right?”
“! ! ?” Amon tightly shut his mouth, instinctively stepping back, not expecting the other to so easily uncover his secret, even past events!
“Don't be so nervous; my father is not your enemy. If you want to become the master here, he will even help you.” Europath said in a low voice.
“You're not lying to me, are you?” Amon found it hard to believe Europath's words; his ancestors had not participated in building the blood pool seal, and becoming a Demon Lord itself is extremely difficult.
“I have no reason to lie to you; I am merely conveying my father's meaning.” Europath answered expressionlessly.
Amon lowered his head, thought for a long time, cautiously looked around, “Exactly, I want to become a true Sovereign of Pride; how does Your Majesty Belial wish to help me?”
“My father is the first Sovereign; he holds great influence in the council. Making you a true Sovereign of Pride is not difficult, provided you need to do one thing.” Europath said meaningfully.
“What do you want me to do?” Amon's face turned serious.
“Kill Vivian's son.” Europath answered calmly.
“This? ? ?” Amon was startled, his expression extremely tense; he had considered killing Merlin, but doing so would surely cause an uproar among the entire demon race; imprisonment would obviously be more appropriate, “Isn't that not good?”
“What are you hesitating about? Don't you want to remove the obstacle on your path to kingship? I can see you want to do that.” Europath paused, then leaned close to Amon's ear and urged, -
“Don't have any scruples; my father will protect you.”
“Do not let a third party know these words; otherwise, what awaits you is not the Demon Lord's throne, but a cold death.”

Meanwhile, in Ophelia's room, Xiu had secretly returned alone to the Demon Lord's Palace to check whether the situation was safe.
As a result, from Ophelia's narration, Xiu learned of Amon's ambition, the current state of the Demon Lord's Palace in the ruins, and realized that this place was no longer safe.
“Heh, Amon's wolfish ambition—actually trying to seize the throne at such a time, completely disregarding the two Highnesses; he must be eliminated.” Xiu's tone was calm, yet one could still feel intense killing intent.
“Don't be impulsive; we are no match for Amon, and besides, he has already gained the approval of other monarchs, which is troublesome.” Ophelia said helplessly.
“Other monarchs have no right to interfere in the affairs of the First Demon Lord's Palace; even if Amon gains approval, it is useless.” Xiu emphasized sternly.
“Provided we have the capital to refute other monarchs, right?” Ophelia lowered her head, sadly saying, “His Majesty Vivian is already gone; our Demon Lord's Palace is at the mercy of other monarchs, unavoidable.”
“If Abaddon were here, Amon would not be so reckless; where did he go?” Xiu, who was already quite well-informed as an officer, actually had no idea either.
“I don't know.” Ophelia sighed, then suddenly felt something, “How is Merlin's Hall?”
“It's fine; the death of Her Majesty Vivian has dealt him a considerable blow; he needs time to slowly recover.” Xiu answered in a comforting tone, knowing Ophelia had always cared about Merlin.
“That's right; Merlin Highness lost his mother before reaching adulthood—this blow is too heavy.” Ophelia, listless, lowered her head, then hurriedly opened the wardrobe beside her, took out the mysterious item tightly wrapped in black cloth, “Take this away and give it to Merlin Highness.”
“What is this?” Xiu frowned in confusion.
“The Banri Garan, symbolizing the Sovereign of Pride's royal artifact.” Ophelia answered solemnly.
“Um!” Xiu shuddered, astonished, asking, “Such a precious item, why is it in your hands?”
“I am merely keeping it temporarily; Amon wants to become the true master here, and he will surely desire this item; I can no longer safeguard it.” Ophelia gripped the Banri Garan tightly, lifted her head, and instructed, “You must take it out of the Demon Lord's Palace; only then can Amon's desire to possess the royal artifact be extinguished.”
Xiu understood the gravity of the situation, thus hurriedly stowed the Banri Garan, asking, “What will you do next? Will you stay in the Demon Lord's Palace?”
“I have my own plans; if even I leave, who will still oppose Amon?” Ophelia said solemnly.
Xiu faintly sensed something; judging from Ophelia's expression, he guessed she intended to spare no cost, to fight Amon to the bitter end, to prevent him from taking the throne.
“Why are you still dawdling here? Hurry up and leave! Amon knows you took Merlin and Lilith; he knows that if you return, he will inevitably interrogate you about their whereabouts.” Ophelia hastily pushed Xiu out the door, hesitantly uttering her last words—
“Xiu, please take care of Merlin Highness; I entrust him to you.”

The Death Marsh region is not large, yet it still contains some villages and tribes; among the demons there are naturally civilians unskilled in combat.
Before the Holy Temple Knights stormed the Demon Lord's Palace, Xiu took advantage of the chaos to bring Merlin and Lilith to a safe place, namely this small demon village—
a hidden stable where Merlin and Lilith had been hiding for a long time; after the Demon Lord's Palace was breached, the Death Marsh fell into chaos.
The siblings never dared to leave this place; seven days ago, Xiu still accompanied them, regularly bringing food and water from outside.
But since Xiu said he would go out to gather news, he has not returned, and no one knows where he went.
The siblings are thirsty and hungry, yet they must endure the stench of horse dung, lacking the courage to step outside, for who knows whether it is safe out there?
Merlin's expression was blank, like a soulless corpse sitting on a haystack, his mind filled with the memory of Olivier pointing a spear at his head.
Although so much time has passed, he still cannot emerge from that man's shadow—that was the moment closest to death he has ever experienced!
Even the Hero's contemptuous gaze has been deeply etched into Merlin's mind; he does not even deserve to die beneath that spear.
Such humiliation is something ordinary people cannot comprehend; Merlin loathes his own inadequacy, and this feeling has become stronger than before.
At that time, Merlin noticed nothing amiss, believing his mother Vivian truly died at Olivier's hands, with not the slightest doubt.
Lilith also kept crying, knowing that hunger would wash away grief, she had to accept the ‘fact’ that Vivian had died.
Gurgle—
Lilith clutched her small belly, already hungry to the point of dizziness; she lifted her head, looking at the listless Merlin, “Brother, I'm hungry.”
Merlin came to his senses, looking at his two-year-old sister, “Yeah, Xiu hasn't returned for two days; should we keep waiting? Going out now is too dangerous.”
“But…” Lilith stared at her constantly growling stomach, feeling a bit embarrassed.
Merlin lowered his head; he himself was also hungry, yet he lacked the courage to leave the stable.
Lilith lowered her head, playing with her familiar, the magical wolf puppy rolling on the ground, “I want Mom; if Mom were still here, that would be good.”
*Erk!* Merlin became somewhat flustered; he even failed to take care of his young sister properly, his self-blame growing, “Lilith, stay here; I'll go out for a while.”
Lilith panicked, quickly grabbing Merlin's sleeve, tears streaming, “Brother, where are you going? Don't leave me! Mom isn't here, . . .”
“What are you doing? I'm just going out to find some food.” Merlin replied awkwardly, thinking he wasn't the kind of brother who would abandon his younger sister in hard times.
“No need, I'm not hungry.” Lilith pouted her little mouth, not wanting her brother to leave her side even a step.
“No need to put on a brave front; I'm just going to find food, I'll be back soon.” Merlin frowned, explaining.
“It would be better if I went; you can't do anything, at crucial moments you're useless, maybe you won't even find food.” Lilith said sadly.
Merlin's face darkened; now even his clingy little sister looked down on him, so he angrily shook off Lilith's hand, “I said I can do it! I definitely can! You stay here and wait obediently!”
Brother bro! *Lilith watched Merlin angrily leave the stable, not daring to chase after him, only able to stomp her feet in place in anxiety.
Merlin's self-esteem was deeply wounded; to prove he was not useless, he wandered around this small village, hoping to find something to fill his stomach.
But the Death Marsh had just experienced war; demons in the village were few, and even food had been taken by fleeing demons, making food a precious commodity.
Merlin clutched his stomach, searching the empty village, rummaging through boxes and trash heaps, not even finding a breadcrumb.
Yet Merlin unexpectedly discovered a squad of Demon Lord's Palace soldiers interrogating villagers, which excited him.
Demon soldiers appearing on patrol meant the war had ended, the Demon Lord's Palace had restored order!
Merlin thought he could bring Lilith back home, so he rushed over eagerly, wanting to greet the demon soldiers.
Just as Merlin opened his mouth, a mysterious person dragged him into an alley, covering his mouth tightly so he could not make a sound.
At that moment Merlin trembled all over with fear, his mind completely dominated by terror, a feeling of suffocation surged up—
Who!?
Who wants to harm me!

title: Chapter 18 — Dwelling
content:
Chapter 18 — Dwelling

Volume 34 · Chapter 18

Merlin was terrified, thinking he had encountered some bad guys right after leaving the stable, but quickly realized that the person behind him was Shu.

Shu looked extremely vigilant, his eyes occasionally stealing glances at the demon soldiers outside the alley, worried about being discovered.

Merlin’s heart was filled with shock and doubt; he couldn’t understand Shu’s current behavior. As a cadre of the Demon Lord Palace, why would he fear demon soldiers?

Shu slowly set Merlin down, putting a finger to his lips in a gesture to be quiet.

“...”

“Shu, what are you doing?”

Merlin questioned in confusion. Seeing how cautious Shu was, he immediately dared not speak loudly, wanting to figure out what was happening.

“Your Highness, I will explain to you in a moment.”

Shu carefully led Merlin back to the stable, avoiding the demon soldiers throughout the entire journey.

When Lilith saw her brother return with Shu, she could hardly hide her joy. “Shu! You’re finally back? Where have you been these past two days?”

Shu stared outside for a long time. Seeing no one following them, he finally felt safe closing the stable door. “I returned to the Demon Lord Palace these past two days to investigate recent events.”

“Is that so? How is things at the Demon Lord Palace?” Lilish asked excitedly. She really wanted to go home now.

“The situation is not optimistic,” Shu answered tactfully.

“Huh?” Lilith widened her eyes in bewilderment, and her hungry little stomach made an untimely rumble.

Shu paused slightly, then quickly took out biscuits from his reserves. “Your Highness must be hungry by now. Eat something first.”

“What does ‘the situation is not optimistic’ mean?” Merlin was already completely baffled and urgently wanted to know the answer.

“Amon has received recognition from other monarchs and become the acting monarch. Currently, control of the Demon Lord Palace is in its hands.” Shu paused, explaining concisely. “According to Ophelia, Amon, in order to become the true master of the Demon Lord Palace, might act against you. The group of soldiers just now were sent to find you. If I hadn’t taken emergency measures, you might have been forcibly brought back to the Demon Lord Palace, falling into danger!”

“Uh!” Merlin’s face turned extremely ugly. Recalling Amon’s ugly visage, anger surged in his heart. He had long suspected that Amon was no good! Now it was taking advantage of Mother’s death to occupy the Demon Lord Palace!

“Shu, can we not go back then?” Lilith asked pitifully.

“That’s right. If Your Highnesses return now, I cannot imagine how Amon would treat you.” Shu said solemnly. He worried that speaking too bluntly would frighten Merlin and Lilith. If Amon was determined to claim kingship, Merlin and Lilith would not survive.

“This bastard Amon! I’ll settle scores with him!” Merlin waved his fists angrily, unable to swallow this grievance.

“Your Highness, please calm down. The demon race is not a group that reasons with words. If your fists aren’t hard enough, no one will listen to you.” Shu paused, then spoke in an encouraging tone. “It would be better for you to swallow this grievance for now and wait for the right opportunity.”

“...” Merlin looked at his own fists, doubting whether he would ever get the chance to settle scores with Amon. He was almost an adult yet still hadn’t learned magic or martial arts. Would there ever be a day when his fists became hard?

“Are we homeless? What should we do...” Lilith became very sad, lowering her head and sobbing.

“Lilith, Your Highness, do not be sad. We can temporarily stay at a friend’s house. This way, we can live peacefully and avoid Amon’s search...”

A dilapidated carriage was traveling through the remote areas of the Death Swamp.

In the distance, mountains stretched endlessly, presenting a pitch-black color like ink.

The shapes of the peaks were peculiar, like sharp fangs charging toward the sky sealed by dark clouds.

From afar, it looked as if a monster had opened its bloody maw, wanting to swallow the entire sky into its belly.

Merlin lay inside the carriage, curiously gazing at the eerie scenery here. “Shu, where is that place?”

Shu pulled the carriage reins, glancing slightly. “That is Despair Canyon. It is plagued by severe weather year-round, and the dark clouds above never disperse. Legend says toxic miasma fills it, and terrifying monsters are everywhere. In short, it is a very dangerous forbidden zone. Your Highness, absolutely do not approach it.”

“Forbidden zone...” Merlin muttered, his hand subconsciously gripping his chest. Suddenly, he felt an inexplicable sensation calling to him.

“Brother wouldn’t go to dangerous places. Brother is afraid of dying,” Lilith innocently murmured beside him.

“So noisy. You’re the one who’s afraid of dying.” Merlin glared at his sister, then asked about the next matter. “Shu, who is this friend you mentioned? What’s their name?”

“Its name is Pudom. His father was also a cadre of the Demon Lord Palace. Unfortunately, he died during the Holy War. My assassination techniques were learned from his father.” Shu said while recalling.

“Pudom.” Merlin noted the name and pressed further. “What kind of demon is it?”

“It lost its family at a young age. Although it inherited its father’s title and lived without worry, its personality became rather strange.” Shu frowned, stopping himself from making predictions. “How should I put it? Pudom did not inherit his father’s strengths; instead, he became very cowardly. He dislikes any conflict and is devoted to researching art and history. Presumably, you also know that art and history are considered the most useless things in the eyes of all demons.”

“I see.” Merlin nodded. Indeed, the demon race only highly valued strength. Having undergone the baptism of the Holy War, the weakness of the demon race was beyond imagination. Who had the leisure to engage in art and history?

“Therefore, Pudom chose to leave the Demon Lord Palace and settled in the most remote part of the Death Swamp. We will live here. Amon’s henchmen probably won’t search this far.” Shu planned to live here for a long time, waiting for the opportunity to return to the First Demon Lord Palace.

Before nightfall, the people on the carriage arrived at their destination.

In this desolate wilderness, two small wooden houses appeared. Flowers and grass were planted in the yard, adding more vitality.

Amidst the vast plain, this solitary house stood out conspicuously. It was hard to imagine what kind of person would live in such a ghostly place.

Shu parked the carriage outside the yard and led Merlin and Lilith to the front door, gently ringing the bell hanging outside.

Ding ling ling—

After a while, the door opened, and a very sloppy demon walked out. He wore high-prescription glasses, had an unkempt beard that he never trimmed, and even had a quill pen hanging from his horns.

Merlin examined the other party. Presumably, this was Pudom mentioned by Shu. He indeed looked different from normal demons, like a nerd immersed in a library.

“Who is it?” Pudom yawned, looking closely. “Shu? What are you doing coming here? I hate it when people disturb my quiet life.”

“Pudom, many things have happened at the Demon Lord Palace. Her Majesty Vivian is dead, and Amon took the opportunity to seize power.” Shu pulled Merlin and Lilith behind him slightly and said seriously. “Now both Your Highnesses are homeless. We need to stay at your place.”

“What!? I disagree! This is my home, not a refugee camp! Nor a nursery!” Pudom picked up a broom nearby and scolded the group of demons. “Leave here! You are not welcome here. By disturbing my work compiling the history of the demon race, you are my enemies!”

Shu’s face turned black instantly, the veins on his forehead throbbing. Without mercy, he punched Pudom directly in the eye socket, shattering the high-prescription glasses.

“Please come in! Please come in~” Pudom changed his usual demeanor, showing a flattering smile. With broken glasses and dark circles under his eyes, he enthusiastically welcomed them. “Don’t stand on ceremony. Stay as long as you want. I’ll go prepare pastries for everyone to enjoy right away~”

*Merlin’s expression became awkward, his eye twitching continuously. He thought, No wonder demons think art and history are useless. Seems there’s some truth to that?

(π π)

title: Chapter 19 — Hot on the Heels
content:
Chapter 19 — Hot on the Heels

Volume 34 · Chapter 19

In the room, Merlin and Lilith had grown quite exhausted over this period, and after filling their stomachs, they couldn’t help but fall into a deep sleep.

Seeing that the siblings had rested, Xiu quietly closed the door and came to the living room, where he found Pudom applying ice packs to his swollen eyes with an annoyed expression on his face.

A huge colorful portrait hung on the wall of the living room; a male demon in formal wear stood majestically, who appeared to be Pudom’s deceased father, as well as Xiu’s senior.

“I’ve caused you trouble, Pudom. I’m very grateful for letting us stay here.” Xiu did not mention his use of force at all.

“Tch!” Pudom glanced at Xiu and said dissatisfiedly, “Don’t offer such insincere thanks. I don’t like being disturbed by others. Letting you in was forced upon me!”

“In any case, I sincerely thank you. At times like these, besides your place, I don’t know where else it would be safe to take Her Highnesses. Your home is remote; I think Ammon’s lackeys wouldn’t search here either.” Xiu walked around with his hands behind his back, surveying the surroundings. The floor was piled high with various books, messier than he had imagined.

“I don’t want to get involved in any troubles. I just want to live quietly alone. Besides, I have already left the Demon Lord Palace. Now I am just a minor noble with an empty title. Why would I have the leisure to care about matters concerning the Demon Lord Palace?” Pudom snorted impatiently.

“Are you still holding a grudge about what happened back then? Actually, no one doubts your abilities. They only object to your hobbies. If you want to become a cadre, you must have the ability to protect the Demon Lord Palace. Martial power is far more useful than all sorts of random arts and history,” Xiu said in a low voice.

“If you still think this way, then I have nothing more to say. I was always dispensable anyway. Not good at fighting, I only preferred staying in the library. How could a nerd like me deserve to become a cadre of the Demon Lord Palace? I remember you said that, didn’t you? Choosing to leave the Demon Lord Palace was the most correct decision I ever made.” Pudom sneered, his resentment clearly written on his face.

“Is there anything wrong with those words? As long as I wanted to, I could kick you out anytime. You can’t even protect your own property.” Xiu shook his head, unable to understand why Pudom couldn’t grasp this logic.

“Get out! I don’t want to hear your goat-like voice anymore.” Pudom’s face flushed red with anger. He was fundamentally different from these demons who worshipped martial power.

“If you had focused on training, you wouldn’t be hiding in this ghost hole now. Your father once praised me about you, saying you possessed excellent magical talent. Why did you end up like this?” Xiu sighed, feeling that Pudom held good cards but played them terribly.

“What does it have to do with you? Tell me, how long are you going to stay here? When the time is up, take them away. I’m not a male nanny in a nursery.” Pudom gritted his teeth.

“Pity, we might have to stay for a long time, until we have the opportunity to return to the Demon Lord Palace.” Xiu shrugged, making it clear he intended to occupy Pudom’s house for the long term.

Pudom covered his face, despair sinking into his heart. He had been living alone nicely before, but now he had to support three masters. “What exactly happened in the Demon Lord Palace? Why are so many troubles arising?”

Xiu looked up and calmly recounted everything recent regarding the First Demon Lord Palace, allowing Pudom to fully understand what Merlin and Lilith had experienced, as well as many hidden dangers.

“That’s how things stand. To protect Her Highnesses, I had no choice but to bring them here to hide.”

“Ammon indeed couldn’t resist revealing his ambition. I saw early on that he was eyeing the throne of the Demon Lord. It’s a pity that if Her Majesty Vivian were here, he would never have a chance.” Pudom smiled, then changed the subject and asked, “However, Her Majesty Vivian being defeated by the Hero is quite unexpected.”

“Her Majesty Vivian had already been poisoned by snake venom at that time and could not fight at full strength, giving the Holy Church an opportunity to strike.” Xiu explained.

“That doesn’t add up. Her Majesty Vivian was the strongest among the second generation of demons, her strength capable of touching the divine realm. Even poisoned by the Three-Eyed Snake, she shouldn’t have been defeated by the Hero. Could it be that the man wielding the spear has reached a level where all the demon cadres combined couldn’t beat him?” Pudom asked suspiciously.

“This…” Xiu was momentarily speechless. He had indeed sensed something unusual, feeling that he lacked some key information. “The Spear-wielding Hero’s strength is indeed much stronger than ordinary Saint-tier individuals.”

“Hmm?” Pudom frowned, unable to help but doubt whether Vivian’s death was real or fake.

Xiu picked up the scattered books on the ground, flipped through them casually, and asked curiously, “Are you still compiling the history of the demon race?”

“Yes. A族群 without historical accumulation is like a message bottle drifting on the sea, completely at the mercy of fate, never knowing where it will drift.” Pudom muttered poetically, adding, “But this task is too difficult. After the Holy War, a large number of precious ancient texts were destroyed by war fires. The history of the demon race has suffered breaks. Even if I organize the history, it’s mostly me making things up based on some stories.”

“In the end, isn’t it useless?” Xiu responded bluntly.

“Uh!” Pudom lost face somewhat and changed the topic, “Actually, I have a new idea now. I want to write a biography about the demons of the new era.”

“Demons of the new era?” Xiu was confused.

“That’s right. A masterpiece to inspire countless young demons.” Pudom dreamed aloud, speaking slowly, “But I haven’t found a suitable subject yet. At the very least, he should possess potential comparable to that great prophet.”

This two-story small wooden house located in the desolate wilderness became a haven for Merlin and Lilith.

The siblings spent several months of peaceful life here for the first time in a long while, gradually forgetting those unhappy memories.

Although it was only a short few months, Pudom had become quite familiar with Merlin and Lilith, gradually adapting to living together.

Merlin stood in the yard, staring blankly at the wooden sword in his hand. He remained unwilling to give up; his craving for power continued to torment him.

Pudom watered the roses in the yard with a jug of flower wine, occasionally glancing at Merlin. He felt this young little prince was strange. Compared to Lilith, he was far too mature, always staring blankly at the wooden sword alone.

“Brother Pudom! Look at the paper boat I folded!” Lilith had made a mess of Pudom’s study, even tearing apart precious books to make toys.

“Ahh!” Pudom looked as if struck by lightning, saying with pain on his face, “Don’t tear my books randomly!”

On the second-floor attic, Xiu stood straight by the window, occasionally observing the funny incidents happening in the yard, but paying more attention to vigilantly watching the distant situation.

Xiu did not relax any alertness, still worrying that Ammon’s subordinates might find this place and destroy this hard-won peace.

However, several months had passed, and the area near Despair Canyon remained calm. Xiu had to wonder if Ammon had given up searching for Merlin and Lilith?

Yet, when Xiu shifted his gaze from Pudom, he suddenly spotted a team of demon soldiers forming a group, quickly approaching this location!

Xiu widened his eyes in shock and hurriedly pushed open the attic window, shouting into the yard, “Pudom! Quickly bring Her Highnesses inside the house!”

Pudom turned around, “What’s wrong? Why are you panicking?”

“It’s Ammon! His lackeys have tracked down here!”

title: Chapter 20 — Golden Strands of Hair
content:
Chapter 20 — Golden Strands of Hair

Volume 34 · Chapter 20

Accompanied by a knock at the door, Pudom steeled himself, feigning calm as he opened the door. The leader of the demon soldiers who had come to wrap things up here was none other than Dulu, who had sworn allegiance to Amon. Pudom's eyes shifted instantly; having long lingered in the Demon Lord's Palace library, he naturally recognized this disfavored deserter's son. "Dulu?" "Lord Baron, I'm sorry to disturb your life," Dulu said, bowing slightly, his gaze occasionally sweeping the interior. "What do you want?" Pudom glanced at the demon soldiers before him, his heart on guard. "We are acting on His Majesty Amon's orders to search your residence," Dulu replied solemnly. "His Majesty Amon? Hah, what right does that fellow have to be called 'Your Majesty'?" Pudom's tone was full of contempt, never acknowledging that. "His Majesty Amon is recognized by the Elder Council as the acting Demon Lord, so of course he has the right to be called Majesty. I hope Lord Baron can understand; the master of the First Demon Lord Palace is no longer the Lucifer family," Dulu said meaningfully. "Hmph, on what grounds do you search my house?" Pudom struck a noble pose, challenging the demon soldiers. "We are looking for Viviane's child, conducting a carpet‑search of the entire Death Marsh region; we hope you will cooperate fully," Dulu stated bluntly. "And if I refuse?" Pudom did not want to let these demons in. "Then we can only assume you are hiding Viviane's child and will have you taken to the Demon Lord Palace for His Majesty Amon's personal judgment," Dulu said, his eyes turning cold, giving Pudom no chance to refuse. Pudom stared silently at Dulu; though he was a Saint‑tier mage, he was not skilled in combat and was no match for Dulu. The demon soldiers behind him instinctively gripped the swords at their waists; if Pudom dared to refuse, they would strike immediately. Even if he joined forces with Xiu to take down these demons, Amon of the Demon Lord Palace would soon learn of it, and finding another hiding place would be far from easy. The situation placed unprecedented pressure on Pudom. Under that immense pressure, the demons were allowed inside by Pudom. The soldiers searched the first floor and the basement, while Dulu went up to the attic on the second floor to investigate. Pudom followed closely behind Dulu, hoping to disrupt him and prevent him from finding any trace of Merlin and Lilith. After reaching the attic, Dulu casually flipped through the space under the bed and the sofa, glancing around nonchalantly. Though his visage was ugly, his twisted features nearly covering his eyes, his gaze was as sharp as an eagle's. "Lord Baron, you live in such a place—don't you feel lonely?" "How could I not? I've grown accustomed to it," Pudom replied offhandedly, appearing calm while his heart raced; Merlin and Lilith were indeed hidden in the second‑floor attic, and Dulu's direct approach there surprised him somewhat. "Why won't you return to live in the Demon Lord Palace? Conditions here are harsh, nowhere near as comfortable as the palace," Dulu asked curiously. "I prefer a solitary, quiet life; the Demon Lord Palace is too chaotic and clearly unsuitable for me," Pudom said, his eyes darting, unsure why Dulu was probing his personal affairs. "I heard you once wanted to become an official of the Demon Lord Palace, but because you were devoted to art and history you never gained favor, so you left in a huff. Viviane's era is over, and now His Majesty Amon is the master of the Demon Lord Palace; if you were willing to serve His Majesty Amon, you would surely be reused," Dulu said with deep meaning, as if extending an olive branch. "Heh, what is Amon? Why should I swear loyalty to him? What a joke—I'm not like you; to wash away my ancestors' stains I wouldn't hesitate to become Amon's dog," Pudom retorted aggressively, giving Dulu no pleasant expression. "That's right," Dulu nodded, showing no reaction to Pudom's sarcasm, not even anger. This made Pudom's brows knit tightly; he thought, Dulu's temper is so good? No wonder he willingly serves Amon—this fellow has lost all dignity. Dulu wandered about the attic room, then suddenly stopped, bent down, and picked up a golden hair from the floor, clearly different from Pudom's own hair color. "It seems you've been lying~" "What do you mean?" Pudom asked, startled. Dulu turned, waving the golden hair in front of Pudom, demanding, "You're not living alone here, are you? Whose hair is this? I recall Prince Merlin's hair is just as radiant." "Eh!" Pudom suddenly grew tense; though he had hastily erased all traces of Merlin and Lilith's presence, he was tripped up by a single hard‑to‑notice strand. "Actually, Viviane's child is hidden in your house, right?" Dulu's eyes pierced Pudom like a needle, stabbing straight into his heart. Pudom couldn't fathom how Dulu had spotted such an insignificant hair; his meticulousness was almost terrifying. "Misunderstanding! You've misunderstood! How could they be hiding in my house? I merely keep a cat with golden fur!" "A cat?" Dulu nodded, stepping heavily as he examined the surroundings, the attic floorboards creaking under his steps, his fingertips brushing over furniture until they stopped before an old wardrobe. "!!?" Pudom's heart gave a jolt, cold sweat soaking his back—indeed, Merlin and Lilith were hidden in the deepest part of the wardrobe. When he saw Dulu's hand grip the wardrobe handle, ready to pull it open, he could no longer hold back and struck first. He summoned a magic book out of thin air; as it unfolded, its pages fluttered with a "clatter‑clatter" sound—he had to strike first! Dulu would not give Pudom a chance to resist; from beneath his heavy black robe shot a black chain, like a snake, instantly wrapping around him. The chain's tip bore a sharp spike, coated in poison, swaying before Pudom's eyes, ready at any moment to pierce his skull. "What!?" Pudom exclaimed, watching the poisonous spike sway, fear gripping him—he was no match for Dulu. "Don't get so worked up, Lord Baron; your reaction is just as if you really had hidden Viviane's child," Dulu said, then suddenly flung open the wardrobe door, his face twisted as he snarled, "It's right here in this wardrobe!" "Tch!" Bound and unable to move, Pudom could only watch as Dulu flung the wardrobe doors wide, his nerves stretched to the breaking point— What now? Dulu might kill Merlin and Lilith on the spot! Xiu!? Pudom lifted his head and saw Xiu already completely concealed in the shadows of the ceiling, dagger in hand, darting toward Dulu, ready to kill him. Dulu threw open the wardrobe, shoved the clothes aside, and finally revealed Merlin and Lilith; a hideous grin spread across his grotesque face. Merlin clutched the trembling Lilith, their gazes vacant as they stared at Dulu; the brother and sister resembled two helpless stray dogs. Dulu's figure blocked out all light; only his vicious eyes remained, radiating terrifying slaughter.

title: Chapter 21 — Change Destiny (Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 21 — Change Destiny (Bonus Chapter)

Volume 34 · Chapter 21

“Brother
Lilith was terrified, lacking the courage to lift her head, she couldn't help but nuzzle into Merlin's embrace.

Merlin's lips moved, but he dared not make a sound, even though Du Lu had already discovered their hiding place.

A shadow loomed over the siblings' heads; their fate had completely fallen into Du Lu's hands.

Du Lu looked down on Merlin from above; the once high and mighty prince had now been reduced to livestock for slaughter.

It had never imagined a day when it could stand above Merlin's head, yet the scene before it felt like a dream.

Du Lu stared fixedly into Merlin's eyes; the immense pressure radiating from it made the siblings feel suffocated!

Merlin's pupils contracted and trembled continuously as he recalled once again the fear brought by the spear-wielding Hero, and the immense humiliation of being unable to control his own fate—

Here it comes again! This feeling of powerlessness again! I am so base that I can't even control my own life or death!

Even if I abandon all dignity and kneel to beg for mercy, whether I can survive still depends on others' expressions.

Such a humiliating life is not what I want!

Xiu's assassination technique had reached perfection, almost completely concealing his presence, even the faint beat of his heart.

It hung silently and soundlessly above Du Lu's head, using an invisible thread attached to the ceiling to suspend his body in midair, like—

—a hanged man.

The dagger in Xiu's hand flashed with a cold light; at such close range, he was confident he could strike Du Lu down—

The situation was too perilous; Xiu had no other choice. Even if exposing their hideout carried risk, he had to act, for if Du Lu were to strike Merlin and Lilith down directly, regret would come too late.

However, in the next instant, Du Lu's action caused Xiu to hesitate, preventing him from driving the dagger into the opponent's neck—

All that could be seen was Du Lu saying nothing, silently closing the wardrobe door, making no move to attack Merlin and Lilith.

This .“Pu Duo Mu gaped in disbelief, unable to trust his eyes; this was completely unlike what he had imagined! Since Du Lu had sworn allegiance to Amon, there was no reason to spare Merlin and Lilith!

Xiu's reaction was half a beat slower, sinking into deep doubt; he couldn't understand why, after discovering Merlin and Lilith, Du Lu would act as if nothing had happened—this was abnormal!

At that moment, the demon soldiers had already searched the lower floor and basement, finding nothing, so they all swarmed up to the second-floor attic.

“Du Lu sir, the first floor and basement are clear; how about here?”

Du Lu put away the chains binding Pu Duo Mu, looked at the demon soldiers, and said, “I haven't found anything either; it seems the two Highnesses are not here.”

Merlin, hiding in the wardrobe, had cold sweat soaking his white shirt; he tugged at his hair, his feelings in turmoil—

Du Lu led the demon soldiers away from Pu Duo Mu's home, paused, and carefully took out a white handkerchief from his bosom—the very one Merlin had given him.

Du Lu had never brought himself to use this white handkerchief; instead, he treasured it, always keeping it on his person.

Due to his unfortunate origins, Du Lu had never received any gift before; thus this white handkerchief held a meaning far from simple for him.

Among all demons who shunned Du Lu's Demon Lord Palace, only Merlin, the high and mighty prince, was willing to lower his guard and bestow upon him care he had never known.

Even if this care was merely pitying alms, to Du Lu it was extraordinarily precious.

Du Lu turned his gaze toward the attic window; he had no intention of telling Amon about Merlin and Lilith's whereabouts, hoping the siblings could live peacefully here.

In the attic, Pu Duo Mu and Xiu stared at the departing Du Lu; they had not yet recovered from their shock, and Du Lu's words and deeds left them unable to comprehend—

This person who had abandoned all dignity to serve Amon actually, at the crucial moment, provided cover for Merlin and Lilith?

“Xiu, what does Du Lu mean? He clearly saw the two Highnesses hiding in the wardrobe, so why deny this?” Pu Duo Mu asked, suspicious and uncertain.

“I don't know either.” Xiu replied in a low voice.

“Which side is this bastard really on?” Pu Duo Mu's expression grew grave as he worried, “Now that we haven't exposed the two Highnesses' location, will he report to Amon when he returns? We should hurry and pack up to leave.”

“No, Du Lu has no motive to do that.” Xiu thought, if Du Lu wanted to act against the two Highnesses, he wouldn't have just now concealed the truth—

Is every new life a blank sheet?

Perhaps we were mistaken—

After a week passed, Pu Duo Mu's home returned to calm; indeed, after Du Lu left, no demon came knocking.

Amon had been deceived; a carpet‑search of the entire Death Marsh turned up no trace of Merlin, and he even suspected the siblings had taken a ship out of the marsh and were wandering in human lands.

The darkness beneath the lamp formed a safeguard for Merlin and Lilith's safety; they need not worry about Amon's minions coming to search, and could continue living here.

However, after experiencing this, Merlin's heart grew ever more eager for power; he did not wish to remain forever holed up in this two‑story wooden hut.

Late at night, after bathing, Merlin wiped his damp hair, expressionless, as he walked toward his room; passing the study, he happened to overhear Xiu and Pu Duo Mu conversing—

Pu Duo Mu said: “Merlin Highness is already this age; he probably won't be able to learn magic or martial arts anymore, and wanting to return to the Demon Lord Palace? That's nearly impossible.”

Xiu said: “Merlin Highness is a demon of the Lucifer lineage; perhaps he possesses a unique talent, so we cannot jump to conclusions just because he hasn't come of age yet.”

Pu Duo Mu said: “Lilith Highness can already summon familiars, yet Merlin Highness can do nothing at all—this is clearly abnormal. Think of the first Lucifer Mephistopheles, what a terrifying swordsman he was! Her Majesty Vivian is likewise a genius; how come, by the time of Merlin Highness's generation, he amounts to nothing?”

Xiu said: “Talent in cultivation is ultimately a matter of luck; not everyone has the ability to learn magic or martial arts. Perhaps Merlin Highness will metamorphose like a butterfly when he reaches adulthood.”

Pu Duo Mu said: “Xiu, you should know better than I that this is nearly impossible; Merlin Highness at this age is destined to be an ordinary demon.”

Xiu said: “That's not certain; legend says the vanished great Prophet was an ordinary demon without magic or battle aura, yet he still became a figure who changed history?”

Pu Duo Mu said: “That's an exception; do you really believe Merlin Highness could stand shoulder‑to‑shoulder with the Prophet?”

Xiu said: “I'm merely saying there is a possibility; if Merlin Highness could find the vanished Prophet and receive his guidance, perhaps fate would become completely different.”

Pu Duo Mu said: “Finding the Prophet? What a joke—he's been gone for ages; even when the demon race was nearly wiped out, he never reappeared. Face it, he has left this world.”

Xiu said: “If the Prophet has already left this world, why did the former king Mephistopheles, on his deathbed, insist on seeking him?”

Pu Duo Mu said: “That's just a rumor, claiming the Prophet retreated into Despair Canyon, and the former king Mephistopheles merely went to try his luck.”

Bang!

Merlin excitedly flung open the study door, widened his eyes, as if grasping at the last straw of salvation, and loudly demanded—

“Where is the person you spoke of?

“Is he in Despair Canyon?

“I will definitely go!”

title: Chapter 22 — Seeking Power
content:
Chapter 22 — Seeking Power

Volume 34 · Chapter 22

“Your Majesty?” Xiu stood up from the chair, surprised, asking, “Why are you still awake so late?”

“I heard everything you said; the guy you mentioned is in the Despair Canyon, right?” Merlin eagerly pressed, unwilling to let go of this opportunity that could change his fate.

*That was just a joke between me and Pudom, don’t take it seriously.” Xiu quickly gave Pudom a look.

“Yeah! We were just chatting casually, haha.” Pudom gave a dry laugh.

“Answer me, Xiu, if I can find that prophet living in the Despair Canyon, can I become strong?” Merlin pressed step by step.

“Xiu hesitated, then answered hesitantly, “I suppose so?”

“I will go to the Despair Canyon and find him!” Merlin’s eyes became resolute, and he made the decision on the spot.

“Huh?” Pudom was startled, shaking his head wildly, “Please calm down! Don’t be so impulsive—do you know how dangerous your idea is?”

“I don’t know, but I must become stronger; I can’t give up this opportunity!” Merlin replied seriously.

“That’s the Despair Canyon—the only unexplored dead zone in the Death Marsh; any demon who enters dies, and no one has ever walked out alive.” Pudom explained solemnly, adding that recklessly entering the Despair Canyon is tantamount to suicide.

“I don’t fear death; I fear more not having the right to choose death. I’m willing to give it a try.” Merlin’s gambling mindset flared again—better to risk his life than continue living in misery.

“Your Highness, do you realize what you’re saying?” Xiu asked sternly.

“I’m quite clear. If I back down now, I may never be able to retake the First Demon Lord’s Hall.” Merlin locked eyes with Xiu, firmly saying, “I have no choice left. Would you be willing to take care of me for life? Even if you would, I couldn’t accept such a life.”

“But— Pudom was about to continue persuading, but Xiu stopped him. The goat demon fell silent for a long time, then nodded— “I understand. I respect your decision, Your Highness.”

The next day, at dawn, Pudom and Xiu escorted Merlin out of his home.

Because they were worried Lilis would cause a scene, they didn’t let Merlin leave easily, so they had to keep it secret from her for now.

They chose to depart while Lilis was still asleep, so she wouldn’t discover Merlin’s plan to risk his life.

“Your Highness, this is the Banri Garan, symbolizing the tyrant king’s royal implement, once the weapon of a great prophet. In the Despair Canyon it may give you some guidance—please keep it safe.” Xiu personally handed the katana to Merlin; it is the only item that can connect him to the prophet.

“Sure, I’ll keep it close.” Merlin, being underage and not tall enough, could only sling the Banri Garan across his back; though it looks light, it’s actually quite heavy.

“Once you enter the Despair Canyon, you must be extra careful—it’s riddled with danger, not just deadly beasts everywhere, but also deep swamps and toxic miasma that require vigilance.” Xiu kept reminding him, unable to fully put his mind at ease.

“Believe me, I will be the first demon to walk out alive from the Despair Canyon; Lilis, please take care of her.” Merlin said sincerely.

“Rest assured, we will look after Her Highness Lilis.”

Xiu and Pudom watched Merlin depart toward the distant Despair Canyon, where black, menacing peaks loomed and the sky occasionally flashed with lightning—a place the sun never reaches.

“Is this really alright? His Highness Merlin might die in there.” Pudom frowned.

“This is His Highness’s own choice; compared to death, he cannot bear living like a worthless waste.” Xiu’s tone showed no wavering—clearly he was more accepting than Pudom.

“That’s the Despair Canyon—even a true Demon Lord couldn’t get out; His Highness Merlin must be mad to go looking for a prophet.” Pudom sighed, having lost all hope.

“That’s how demons are—the weak have no space to survive; they might as well die. This is a trial His Highness Merlin must face alone; he must learn how to become a true demon.” Xiu said meaningfully.

“Your cold-heartedness frightens me; we should start preparing a coffin for His Highness Merlin right away.”

“No need to prepare; His Highness Merlin will return. He is a child of the Lucifer family, and Mephisto will bless him.”

A few days later, Merlin had successfully entered the Despair Canyon, yet the situation he encountered was worse than imagined.

The Banri Garan on his back gave no guidance at all, nor did any ancestors bless him; he could only rely on himself to survive in this perilous place.

The dangers in the canyon exceeded imagination—even insignificant poisonous insects could kill him; seemingly harmless white mist could rot millennium-old trees; a moment’s carelessness would sink him into a swamp from which he could never climb out.

Moreover, an astonishing number of demons inhabit the canyon, desperately craving the flesh of outside beings, having long grown tired of their own kind.

The scent Merlin emits is a huge stimulus to any beast, driving them into a frenzy.

Poor Merlin hadn’t rested in ages; he only dared to take brief naps, constantly worrying that if he fell asleep he’d be bitten by poisonous insects or targeted by ferocious beasts.

He dared not eat anything from the forest at random, nor drink from seemingly clear streams, for he could not tell whether they were poisonous.

At that moment, Merlin was spotted by a demon beast; he fled in terror through the forest, glancing back occasionally as dense trees were snapped apart one after another!

“Damn it! Can’t the trees stop it?!”

A massive spiked boar roared as it chased Merlin, its blade-like spikes covering its body, its sharp tusks flashing with icy light!

This demon, a fusion of boar and hedgehog, resembled a colossal war chariot—six stories tall—rumbling as it ran, crushing all trees in its path!

As a high‑rank demon, the spiked boar relied on its full‑body spikes to contend with Saint‑tier beasts, and its aura drove away the weaker monsters nearby.

Most beasts lack intelligence, yet their survival instinct prevents them from approaching the frenzied spiked boar.

Merlin relied on his slight build to dart through the forest, but he could not escape the spiked boar’s pursuit; any obstacle it simply crushed, making it a veritable bully that rampaged through the woods.

Suddenly, Merlin felt his foot give way, as if stepping on mud, but his legs were instantly swallowed; looking down, a chill ran through him—

“A swamp!”

title: Chapter 23 — Afraid.jpg
content:
Chapter 23 — Afraid.jpg

Volume 34 · Chapter 23

Merlin felt violent trembling beneath his feet, and he turned his head in terror to look behind him, discovering the frenzied giant boar had smashed through three massive trees in succession, barreling toward him with a thunderous rumble!

If it charged at him with such overwhelming momentum, before his body was crushed to pieces, he would be impaled through and through by those sharp spikes, leaving gaping wounds that bled incessantly!

"This is bad!"

Merlin's life hung by a thread. He desperately tried to keep running, but the mud beneath his feet clung stubbornly to his legs, holding him fast.

Driven by an intense will to survive, Merlin summoned every ounce of strength he had and forced himself to take a single step forward.

But the situation only grew worse. Merlin sank again, and the swamp now reached his waist!

His face went pale, his breathing grew shallow, and he dared not move carelessly. The more he struggled in the mire, the deeper he sank!

His body was slowly descending further. Even if he were lucky enough to avoid being gored to death by the demon beast, he would eventually be completely swallowed by the swamp.

"Roar—"

Suddenly, a furious roar echoed from deep within the forest, and a massive silhouette loomed over Merlin's head, pitch-black and impossible to make out clearly!

Merlin stared up in shock, his mouth falling open. A second demon beast had appeared, likely drawn by the prospect of food. This creature radiated a terrifying pressure, its entire body covered in black fur, resembling a massively powerful giant ape!

It was enormous, easily over a hundred feet tall. Though its fur concealed much of its form, the tightly coiled muscles across its body were still clearly visible.

The sight of this demon beast struck Merlin as oddly familiar, strikingly similar to that movie he had once seen: a black gorilla rearing up and roaring atop the Empire State Building...

The black-furred giant ape descended from the sky with a loud "thud," landing near Merlin and planting its limbs on the ground, shielding him beneath its massive frame.

A cold sweat broke out across Merlin's forehead. He thought that if these two demon beasts ended up destroying each other, perhaps he might still have a chance to survive.
