But the black-furred giant ape was clearly far too powerful compared to the spiked boar. It slammed its powerful arms into the ground, sending shards of stone flying in all directions, as if issuing a warning.

The spiked boar did indeed come to an abrupt halt. Its beady eyes scanned the giant ape—or rather, glanced at the tiny, insignificant Merlin beneath it—and it clearly didn't want to give up on such a delicious meal.

"Roar! Roar!" The black-furred giant ape repeatedly let out low growls, baring its sharp fangs ferociously, its threat unmistakable.

The spiked boar instinctively took a step back, lacking the courage to fight the giant ape. But in the end, greed overpowered fear. It pawed at the ground with its hooves, beginning to gather momentum!

In the Despair Canyon, outsiders were rare. A tasty morsel like Merlin was an irresistible temptation for these demon beasts.

Seeing that the enemy wouldn't give up, the black-furred giant ape slightly raised its powerful upper body and angrily pounded its own rock-hard chest with both fists!

The spiked boar launched its charge, trampling deep cracks into the earth, flailing the sharp tusks from its mouth in wild arcs!

The two colossal monsters slammed into each other with earth-shaking force, the ground trembling violently. Merlin watched, stunned, feeling as though the swamp was swallowing him even faster.

The black-furred giant ape gripped the boar's tusks tightly with both hands. When the boar's charge finally stopped, it freed one hand and brought its massive steel-like fist crashing down onto the boar's beady eye.

After three consecutive strikes, the spiked boar could no longer endure the punishment. It instinctively threw open its mouth in a scream, its eye sunken deep into its skull from the brutal blows.

Taking advantage of the opening, the black-furred giant ape shoved its hand directly into the boar's belly. Then, with a wet "rip" sound—

The spiked boar's tongue, along with its internal organs and intestines, was torn completely out of its body by the giant beast!

Blood sprayed everywhere. Merlin stood speechless, horrified by the brutal scene before him, something he had never witnessed before!

The clash between the two demon beasts ended quickly. The black-furred giant ape's strength utterly crushed its opponent; there was no suspense to the contest.

The giant ape discarded the boar's corpse and pulled the half-submerged Merlin out of the swamp, lifting him up to its face for a closer inspection.

Merlin, covered in mud and swamp water, was held aloft like a tiny insect by the giant ape. Staring into its eyes, his soul nearly fled his body from terror, his mind filled with nothing but the image of being devoured alive.

"Roar."

The black-furred giant ape let out a low growl, leaning close to Merlin and sniffing him with intense curiosity, seeming quite interested in this little fellow.

Could Merlin withstand this? His nerves were stretched to the absolute limit, and he passed out on the spot—

I, a transmigrator of great renown, am actually going to die in the mouth of a gorilla!

When Merlin opened his eyes again, he was jolted awake by the irresistible aroma of roasting meat. He was starving to the point of madness.

Upon waking, Merlin found himself lying on a messy pile of grass. This place seemed to be the black-furred giant ape's dwelling!

All around him were black rocks and volcanic formations, with scorching lava slowly oozing down from the peak, waves of heat washing over him.

He spotted the black-furred giant ape roasting the meat of the freshly killed wild boar over a fire. All the sharp spines had been carefully removed.

"???"

Merlin rubbed his eyes, wondering if he was seeing things. Normal demon beasts typically devoured their prey raw, fur and blood, but this gorilla was actually using fire to cook its meal before eating? Was this really something a demon beast would do?

If the black-furred giant ape unzipped its fur and a human giant stepped out, Merlin would have been willing to believe it, for the use of fire was a symbol of intelligence.

Then, the giant ape began rummaging through bottles and jars nearby, taking out some unknown seasonings and sprinkling them evenly over the roasted boar meat.

Watching this scene unfold, Merlin's mouth twitched uncontrollably. He couldn't believe what he was seeing and thought to himself—

My goodness! It's even adding seasoning?! Who the hell taught it to do that?!

After arriving in this world for so long, he had never imagined encountering such refined eating habits in a demon beast!

This had to be a mistake. Weren't demon beasts supposed to be mindless monsters?

Given how bizarre the whole situation was, Merlin concluded that this giant ape was far more dangerous than any other demon beast. While it was busy roasting meat, he should slip away as quickly as possible.

Merlin glanced back at the demon sword Banri Garan, then carefully climbed down from the grass pile, inching step by step toward the distant forest, terrified of alerting the black-furred giant ape.

"Roar—"

A low growl rang out. Merlin's face turned deathly pale, and he was forced to freeze in place, his entire body as if petrified, unable to move a muscle.

It wasn't that he truly couldn't move; he was simply too scared to take another step.

He believed this gorilla moved with terrifying speed and agility. Unless he could put more than a kilometer between himself and the creature, he might as well just resign himself to waiting for death.

Merlin stiffly turned his head and saw that the black-furred giant ape had noticed he was awake. It was waving at him like a person, then patting the empty space beside itself, gesturing for him to sit obediently nearby.

"Roar roar! Roar roar!"

Merlin's expression froze on his face. Cold sweat poured down from his head in an instant, his spirit thoroughly shattered.

What the hell!

Do you want to toy with me before eating me?!

Just kill me if you're going to kill me! Give me a quick death!

What is this supposed to be?! Do you think I was scared into submission?!

Merlin obediently sat beside the black-furred giant ape, his posture extremely rigid, trembling nonstop.

The little guy didn't dare look at the colossal beast beside him at all. He was even forcing himself to hold back a fart.

o((O. O))o

title: Chapter 24 — The Big Shot's Thick and Sexy Leg Hair
content:
Chapter 24 — The Big Shot's Thick and Sexy Leg Hair

Volume 34 · Chapter 24

The black-furred giant ape tore off the wild boar's elbow with brute force, enthusiastically tossing it in front of Merlin, its nose constantly letting out a "humm" sound, indicating that the little one should eat while it's hot. Although this chimpanzee's cooking skills and techniques aren't superb, the well-cooked boar meat combined with mysterious spices gives off an aroma that makes mouths water! The huge pork elbow is as tall as a small hill, its surface flowing with glossy oil, its color showing layers of rosy red, constantly stimulating the diners' taste buds! Merlin could only lift his head to gaze up, barely able to take in the massive pork elbow; he startled and retreated, his buttocks landing on the ground, thinking, "Is this meant for people to eat? No one could possibly finish it all!" Wait! Could this chimpanzee's intention be to fatten me up before killing me? ? ? Merlin eyed the black-furred giant ape suspiciously, worried that eating too much would get him slaughtered like a pig—better to stay hungry. The black-furred giant ape noticed Merlin wasn't eating, lowered its head in surprise, let out a low growl, and shoved the enormous pork elbow closer to Merlin. "Roar" Merlin felt the pressure mount, fearing to anger the hulk beside him, so he swallowed his saliva and decided to eat just a little to stave off hunger. He hadn't eaten in days, his stomach growling fiercely, and he could hardly resist the temptation of food. Moreover, he didn't intend to overeat; just eating half his fill to fill his stomach shouldn't make him fat. Merlin leapt up like a starving tiger pouncing on a sheep, directly starting to tear and bite the huge pork elbow, like a wretched soul reincarnated with a ferocious eating style. One bite in, he couldn't even pierce the boar's skin, but the meat was cooked just right, and with the seasoning it was delicious to die for! Compared to Merlin, the black-furred giant ape beside him was obviously far more unrestrained; its sharp teeth tore and chewed the boar meat, making gurgling sounds, and it quickly cleaned out the pig's head, leaving nothing behind—indeed, it hadn't even eaten its fill? Merlin lay on the pork elbow, bewildered, lifting his head, suddenly feeling that this big gorilla didn't seem like a bad guy after all, and decided to try communicating— "Hey, can you understand what I'm saying?" The black-furred giant ape lifted its head, stopped gnawing on the pig's trotter in its hand, looked down at Merlin, and then nodded, "Roar." Merlin furrowed his brow, thinking indeed this creature wasn't low in intelligence; it could understand his words, "Why did you save me?" The black-furred giant ape scratched its head, seemingly recalling something, pointed at Merlin, and uttered, "Roar roar roar, roar roar" ??? Merlin's mind filled with question marks; he completely couldn't understand what the other was saying. Then it struck him—he took down the demon sword Banri Garan from his back and asked, "Is it because of this?" The black-furred giant ape stared at the demon sword Banri Garan, startled, nodded, then shook its head again, leaving its meaning unclear. Merlin grew even more puzzled; just moments ago he could communicate with nods for yes and shakes for no, but now the ape both nodded and shook, leaving him confused. Nevertheless, Merlin clearly sensed that the black-furred giant ape reacted to the demon sword Banri Garan, which proved at least one thing. "Is there a demon called the Prophet living here?" This time the black-furred giant ape fell silent for a long time, sitting foolishly on the ground, scratching its head incessantly, making it hard to guess what it was thinking. "Huh?" Merlin, baffled by the ape, couldn't help but press on, "I must see him; do you know where he is?" The black-furred giant ape shook its head, indicating it knew nothing; no matter how Merlin pressed, it gave no response, unwilling to answer any question. Merlin calmed down, realizing one thing: this ape had definitely seen the Prophet, otherwise it wouldn't react to the demon sword Banri Garan. It seemed the Prophet's hermitage in Despair Canyon wasn't just a rumor; at the very least, the Prophet had lived here. As for why this black-furred giant ape saved him—most likely because Merlin carried the demon sword Banri Garan. Thus, the relationship between this magical beast and the Prophet wasn't bad; they might even be friends. Merlin pondered various possibilities, observing the ape's behavior; it showed no intention to harm him, appearing very friendly. At this moment Merlin couldn't help but entertain a little thought: he originally struggled to survive in Despair Canyon; if the black-furred giant ape could shield him, that would be fantastic. "Cough cough! What's your name? Can you tell me?" "Roar roar." The black-furred giant ape let out two low growls, seemingly stating its name, but Merlin couldn't understand? "What the heck?" Merlin felt embarrassed, thinking, "What kind of name is 'roar roar'? I'm really stupid; it's a demon, how could it possibly have a name!" "If you don't mind, I'll give you a name—how about... how about King Kong?" "Roar?" The black-furred giant ape's ears perked up, it bared its teeth to show delight, its huge body bounced in place, pounding its chest with both fists, letting out a melodious roar. "What's going on? Merlin felt bewildered; he couldn't understand why the ape was so happy—could this actually be its name? Perhaps it hadn't been called that in a long time. King Kong gently placed Merlin in his palm, lifted him to eye level for close inspection; Merlin in the giant's hand was like a movable action figure. "I am Merlin Lucifer; anyway, we've now met each other. As friends, we should help each other—do you understand?" King Kong let out a low growl, brought its nose close to Merlin and sniffed nonstop, as if searching for a familiar scent from memory. Merlin suddenly shuddered all over, feeling a strange sense of familiarity in this scene—just like in the movie where King Kong loves to hold the heroine in his hand and stare at her endlessly— A wave of inexplicable melodramatic emotion surged in his heart; no matter what, Merlin couldn't accept a romantic entanglement crossing species with a non-human being. Merlin scrambled onto King Kong's palm, looked down carefully, trying to determine whether the black-furred ape before him was male or female— Thank goodness it's male. Hold on! Even if it's male, that doesn't seem safe either! Merlin lived with this ape named King Kong for a while, discovering that beneath its simple-minded exterior lay a petty, mischievous soul. King Kong's combat power was extremely formidable; most demons basically went down with a single punch, easier than bullying kids. Whenever he stood on the mountain peak and let out a roar, the beasts in his territory would flee in terror, daring not to step onto his turf—truly the overlord of Despair Canyon! King Kong's neighbor was a two-headed dragon demon named Chimera; whenever Chimera went out foraging, King Kong would sneak into its nest, steal eggs, and boil them to eat. This guy thoroughly enjoyed the thrill of theft; after being discovered by Chimera and getting beaten up, he would still snatch away the whole clutch of eggs. As a result, this poor two-headed dragon demon never managed to produce offspring, facing the prospect of extinction, and harbored immense resentment toward King Kong. Under King Kong's protection, Merlin managed to survive in Despair Canyon—food was so abundant he couldn't finish it all, and he could follow King Kong to thrash all the demons that had previously bullied his little friends— Thrilling~~~ Living by clinging to a thigh was just this plain and unadorned, yet monotonous.

title: Chapter 25 — Body Tempering
content:
Chapter 25 — Body Tempering

Volume 34 · Chapter 25

Hot magma slowly flowed from the volcano's summit, forming a huge lava lake not far from King Kong's grass nest.

King Kong, relying on his thick skin and flesh, would soak in the lava almost every day, looking extremely pleased, though he didn't know what good it did.

Merlin watched King Kong soaking in the lava and thought this monster was indeed fierce, using boiling lava as bathwater. "Roar!" King Kong waved at Merlin, gesturing for him to come down and soak together. "Ugh! No way! I can't!" Merlin was frightened, waving his hands frantically; his small frame couldn't take the strain—soaking in lava would burn him to death. However, the simple-minded King Kong obviously didn't realize this, thinking Merlin could also soak in the lava. So King Kong lifted Merlin from the shore, intending to throw him into the lava to get him used to it. Merlin cried out in alarm, his face turning bright red with tension; just getting near the rolling lava, he could smell the scent of his own eyebrows and hair burning— "Ahhh! Stop! I can't! I'll die!" Merlin struggled desperately, for if he fell into the lava he would surely be reduced to ashes. King Kong lifted Merlin to his eye level, scrutinizing him, scratching his head in puzzlement, seemingly unable to understand why Merlin was so weak— he couldn't even adapt to lava.

In the dense forest, King Kong's massive body continually weaved through the trees, his agile form moving at astonishing speed. Merlin lay atop King Kong's head, clutching the fur tightly, the wind whistling past his ears nonstop, "Where are you taking me?" King Kong lowered his head and hurried on, having no mind to answer Merlin's question, weaving through layers of forest until a towering black tree appeared before his eyes. This unique tree was extraordinarily remarkable, far larger than most of the ten-thousand-year-old trees in the Despair Canyon, resembling a sky‑holding pillar covered in bright red leaves, which stood out starkly amid the lush jungle. "What is that?" Merlin frowned, unable to fathom where King Kong had brought him; but he was certainly not going to see the prophet. King Kong had already made it clear that he didn't know where the prophet was, and no matter how much he was pressed, he refused to answer that question. During this time Merlin could only follow behind King Kong, trying to track the prophet's footsteps, yet he found nothing at all. As they drew nearer to the black giant tree, Merlin felt his breathing grow difficult, as if a heavy stone pressed on his chest, forcing him to take deep breaths. All magical elements in the air were continually dispelled by this tree, seemingly unable to merge with any magical power. Upon reaching the foot of the black giant tree, Merlin observed more closely and discovered that transparent oil was slowly seeping from the tree's trunk? The ground beneath his feet was also harder than elsewhere; the flowing oil merged with the soil and, after solidifying, formed mysterious crystals. "King Kong, what is this?" Merlin asked, puzzled. "Roar, roar—" King Kong rose to his feet, using both hands to spread the oil from the black giant tree evenly over his chest. The seemingly viscous tree oil was quickly absorbed completely by King Kong's flesh; his skin took on a steel‑like sheen, and even his hair became brighter. Merlin's heart stirred; he had noticed something unusual, so he cautiously dabbed a bit of the tree oil onto his arm. After the oil seeped into his skin, a mysterious force surged within his body, continually strengthening his flesh. Merlin was overjoyed; he carefully examined the arm he had anointed with the tree oil and found it far tougher than before, faintly glowing with the sheen of solidified crystal oil. "There's something this miraculous! Why am I still hesitating?" Merlin grew excited; the tree oil on the black giant tree could strengthen the body—a rare treasure, an opportunity not to be missed. Thus Merlin shamelessly took off his pants, intending to smear the tree oil over every inch of his body. After being fortified by the mysterious tree oil, Merlin finally gained the ability to soak in the lava, although it was still scalding hot and he had to grit his teeth, but at least he no longer had to worry about being burned to death. No wonder King Kong loved bathing in lava so much—it turned out to have great benefits— If one likens the body to steel, then soaking in lava is like continual hammering, purging useless impurities and making the body as pure as refined steel. Moreover, the lava promotes absorption of the tree oil, enhancing the bodily strengthening effect. The tree oil of the black giant tree combined with lava tempering forms a complete body‑forging secret, a condition found only in the Despair Canyon. Merlin began his path to growing stronger: by day he anointed his body with the tree oil, by night he soaked in the lava to further temper himself. King Kong also tried to teach Merlin some simple martial techniques, even deliberately beating other demons half‑to‑death and then handing them over to Merlin to deal with, so that Merlin would learn how to fight demons and overcome his fear. Since Merlin was still underage and his small stature made swords inconvenient, he ground monster bones into a dagger as a temporary weapon. As for the demon sword Banri Garan on his back, Merlin had already tried it—he couldn't draw the blade, so it could only serve as ornament. This harsh life lasted half a year; the scrawny Merlin became sturdy, his body acquiring a certain degree of strength. "Ha!" Merlin shouted, punching a stone three men high until it was covered in cracks. This wasn't battle aura, just pure bodily strength; after half a year of effort, Merlin's physical strength had become enough to match a low‑rank warrior. Though it would be insignificant before true experts, for Merlin it was tremendous progress—at the very least he now possessed the power to resist. King Kong stood on all fours, silent beside him, eyes fixed on Merlin, wondering what he was thinking? "How about it? Am I still…?" Merlin rested his hands on his hips, savoring the fruits of his labor, "**Why aren't you speaking? Aren't you happy for me?" Seeing Merlin lift him onto his head, King Kong let out a mute grunt and swiftly scrambled up the volcano's peak, believing the time had ripened. "Hey! Where are you taking me?" Unlike the heat at the base, the summit was cold, the wind cutting like a blade. After reaching the top, King Kong kept searching for something, scanning all around until he finally locked onto a direction. "What's wrong? Is something the matter?" Merlin stood at King Kong's feet, curiously inquiring. King Kong reached out his hand, pointing at a spot, as if trying to tell Merlin something important. Following the direction of King Kong's finger, Merlin faintly made out a barren mountain in the distance, its slopes sparsely treed; had he not been standing on the volcano's summit, he would hardly have noticed it. "You mean that desolate mountain?" King Kong nodded vigorously, gently pushing Merlin's back with his palm, giving various hints that he should go have a look, his gaze turning urgent. "Do you want me to go there? Won't you come with me?" Merlin worried, for with his own strength, having King Kong by his side would be his only hope of making it there. King Kong shook his head, clearly indicating he would not accompany him, which left Merlin utterly puzzled— What did he mean? What lay there? Even King Kong dared not approach it casually.

title: Chapter 26 — Awakening
content:
Chapter 26 — Awakening

Volume 34 · Chapter 26

According to Jin Gang's guidance, Merlin went alone to a distant desolate mountain, not knowing what existed there.
Based on past experience, Merlin believed Jin Gang was hinting that there was a secret to becoming stronger there.
So Merlin didn't doubt much, cautiously arrived at the foot of the desolate mountain and discovered a cave on the mountainside.
At the cave entrance, Merlin hesitated a little, fearing unknown majesty inside, but driven by his urgent desire to gain power, he gritted his teeth and went in.

When he reached the deepest part, Merlin discovered a mysterious man with a waterfall of golden hair and a messy beard covering his features, making it hard to tell who he was.
Merlin's heart jumped in shock; he couldn't imagine that besides himself, there was another human in the Despair Canyon—this was a major discovery!

Since Merlin couldn't tell whether the man was friend or foe, he cautiously asked a question, but the man completely ignored him.
The mysterious man lifted his head, without a word stepped forward, grabbed Merlin's throat and shoved him against the wall, holding a sharp, golden‑glinting cone.
Merlin was terrified, instinctively thinking he would die there; he struggled desperately, but still couldn't escape the man's magic staff.
The mysterious man said a lot, but Merlin was too nervous to hear most of it—
The golden cone emitted sunlight‑like light, fiercely piercing deep into Merlin's heart.
Drip, water droplets splashed onto the wet rocks.

Merlin woke from his coma, his whole body feeling as if he'd touched high voltage, sore all over.
He recalled what happened before losing consciousness, quickly sat up from the ground, and examined his body.
"What the hell?!!!"
Merlin let out a piercing scream, lowered his head to look at his chest, stunned by what he saw—
A fist‑sized scar appeared at his heart, blood had just clumped into lumps, a mysterious force continuously gathered toward his heart, breath rapidly contracting!
Countless blood threads appeared on Merlin's body, connecting to the heart scar, looking like a bright red spider web.
Merlin was greatly frightened, trembling all over; he thought he should be dead, why could he wake up with a hole punched in his heart?
Thump—thump—
The injured heart began to beat, accompanied by unimaginable pain that made his soul feel torn apart!
Merlin's face turned pale, he clutched his chest and bent over; cold sweat "swish" poured out, making his whole body twitch.
"What's wrong?"
Merlin lay on the ground in pain, the immense pain from his heart making him think he might die at any moment.
He had no doubt that if his body hadn't been tempered, he might be painfully killed here.
Merlin clenched his fists, gritted his teeth, wanting Jin Gang's help, so he stumbled toward the cave exit, thinking—
No! If this continues, my heart will hurt until it stops beating; I must find a way to stop it!

Merlin crawled out of the cave in a near‑crawling manner; the pain from his heart grew worse, possibly making it impossible to return to Jin Gang's side.
"Jin Gang, Jin Gang, help me!"
Merlin tried to call Jin Gang for aid, but his weak state made his voice faint, and it unexpectedly attracted an enemy.
A gust of fierce wind blew; Merlin thought Jin Gang had come to pick him up, excitedly lifted his head, but his joyful expression froze on his face.
It wasn't Jin Gang, but Jin Gang's enemy, the double‑headed dragon demon Chimera!
Since Chimera had always been robbed of its eggs and wanted revenge, seeing a little one beside Jin Gang caught its attention.
Chimera had been looking for a chance to eat Merlin and let Jin Gang experience similar suffering, but had never found the opportunity.
Today, however, Chimera discovered Merlin had left Jin Gang alone and come here, so it had already set an ambush outside the cave.
Chimera spread its vast membrane wings, stirring up a violent storm that uprooted nearby trees; its two heads swayed wildly, scarlet eyes flashing with anger!
Its strength in the Despair Canyon was immense, second only to the thick‑skinned Jin Gang; each time it judged from the sky, other magical beasts dared not raise their heads.
Merlin gazed up at Chimera's figure, sinking into deep despair—his heart had just been pierced, and now he ran straight into a magical beast; his bad luck was obvious.
"Hiss—"
Chimera let out a piercing roar, unlike a true dragon's roar, more like a mix of snake and monkey.
Merlin was scared out of his wits; his legs went weak and he plopped onto the ground, unable to flee before Chimera, only able to stare blankly.
The heart‑wrenching pain intensified, breathing became difficult; Merlin found he could exhale but not inhale—clearly a sign of imminent death—
Is everything over? Am I going to die in this damned place!
No! This isn't what I want! I came to become stronger, not to be food for demons!
Lilith and the others are still waiting for me! They expect me to grow strong and bring them back to the Demon Lord Palace!
I can't die so pathetically! I must return to the Demon Lord Palace and sit on the throne that rightfully belongs to me!

Merlin's forehead veins bulged, his teeth almost shattered from clenching; facing the crisis, he could only forcibly draw the demon sword Banri Garan from his back to use as a weapon.
He half‑squatted on the ground, assumed a perfect sword‑drawing stance, gazed up at the terrifying Chimera, and a tiny spark ignited in the depths of his despair.
"Don't provoke me! You'll regret it!"
Chimera sneered and growled, its two heads spewing red‑black flames like cannon fire!
The scorching flames swept over, making trees and grass visibly wither and self‑ignite, more than enough to burn the enemy to ash.
The two flames merged at the center, instantly transforming into a ten‑fold‑stronger flame tsunami that surged toward Merlin with crushing force!
Merlin was about to draw his sword, but found he couldn't use Banri Garan at all—the blade was stuck fast in its scabbard.
"Shout!
Merlin was unwilling; he slowly closed his eyes, as if resigning to wait for death—
But in his mind, he desperately recalled the countless times he'd practiced the sword‑drawing slash.
Through years of training, his muscles had memorized every detail; he knew it inside out.
His gambling instinct flared again; he bet everything on the sword‑drawing technique, convinced he was a transmigrator with built‑in skill points.
Merlin shut his eyes tightly, gathered all his strength in his right hand, and tried once more to pull out Banri Garan; the silent blade finally gave a faint tremor—
"I am a transmigrator!
"How dare you not even let me draw my sword?!!"

title: Chapter 27 — Leaving the Mountain
content:
Chapter 27 — Leaving the Mountain

Volume 34 · Chapter 27

“Clang!”

The Banri Garan was successfully drawn from its sheath, accompanied by a sharp, clear sound.

This weapon, once wielded by the prophet, was being revealed to the world again after several millennia.

Drawing the Banri Garan meant that Merlin had become its new master — a fact that, if known to the demon race, would surely cause a massive stir.

The Banri Garan was not just a symbol of the proud monarch; it was also a link to the great prophet who had once changed the history of the demons.

Merlin kept his eyes closed throughout the process, unsure if the draw had succeeded, and lacking the courage to open his eyes to see the result.

He could faintly feel the intense pain in his heart diminishing, and slowly opened a crack in his eyelids, his face turning pale.

“Ugh!”

The chimera stood rigidly before him, its scarlet eyes fixed on him with a gaze full of resentment that did not fade.

Merlin looked up at the chimera, his mind blank, his lips moving without making a sound, instinctively stepping back.

“Tear!” The chimera’s massive body split in two from the middle, collapsing into two pools of flesh on the ground — it had been killed instantly by the draw.

Merlin looked down at his own body, noticing that the blood vessels had disappeared, leaving only the scars.

He then glanced at the Banri Garan in his hand — the ancient blade was chipped and rusted, looking like a piece of scrap metal that no one would pick up off the street.

In that moment, he understood many things: the past life of frustration and oppression would become a part of his history.

Time flew by, and decades passed.

Merlin continued to live in the Valley of Despair, growing from a thin boy into a tall, strong adult demon.

He was no longer the weakling that everyone could bully; he was now a true monster with explosive power in every movement.

The naivety and innocence in his eyes had been replaced by a fierce, sharp gaze that resembled red gemstones.

These decades were not spent idly — he had worked tirelessly to increase his strength, practicing the draw technique on the volcano almost daily until he could fully control the power of the slash.

He also continued to temper his body with mysterious tree oil and lava, though the effects of this secret method had become negligible.

From the initial fear of dying in the dangerous valley, he had become the undisputed ruler, walking freely without fear.

He had paid a price that few could imagine.

As an adult, Merlin was the true master of the Valley of Despair, turning this place feared by demons into his private playground.

However, he discovered that he was cursed — his heart would shrink violently at regular intervals, causing pain that woke him from sleep.

Fortunately, Merlin knew how to alleviate this: by using the Banri Garan to steal the life force of other creatures, temporarily stabilizing the curse.

The many powerful monsters in the valley became the foundation for his survival, and countless had fallen to his blade.

Late at night, the sky over the valley was always foggy, never showing the moon or stars. Merlin and King Kong soaked in the lava, groaning with pleasure.

“King Kong, do you really not know who that guy in the cave is? Isn’t he the prophet?”

In response to Merlin’s question, King Kong shook his head repeatedly, expressing ignorance — perhaps he didn’t know, or perhaps he didn’t want to answer.

This was not the first time Merlin had asked; every time he inquired about the mysterious man, the simple-minded King Kong would deny knowing.

Over the decades, Merlin had tried to investigate, but found no answers, and eventually gave up.

Although he suspected the man was the missing great prophet — after all, his grandfather, Mephisto, had risked everything to come here, likely to see the prophet — there was no concrete evidence.

With no opponents left in the valley, Merlin felt a sense of emptiness from being at the top, lacking any motivation to stay.

He believed the time was right to return to the Demon Lord Palace and settle the score with Amon, reclaiming what was rightfully his.

After all, Vivian was his mother, and her legacy should belong to him and Lilith, not to any outsider.

Looking down at King Kong, his loyal companion who had supported him during the hardest times, Merlin felt a deep friendship.

“King Kong, I’m about to leave here.”

“Roar?” King Kong shivered, the calm lava rippling, and after a long silence, he gave Merlin a thumbs-up in encouragement.

“You’re not coming with me?” Merlin asked, hoping to bring King Kong to the palace.

King Kong shook his head, pointing to the grass on the shore and growling — he wanted to stay.

“I see, this is your home. Staying here is a good choice.” Merlin smiled, understanding that as a monster, King Kong might not be safe outside, where hunters prey on beasts. The valley was a safe haven.

“I’ll come back to visit you, old friend.”

In the First Demon Lord Palace, the mysterious blood pool seal remained intact.

Amon had been the acting Demon Lord for a long time, suppressing dissent and consolidating power.

Even though some demons questioned his legitimacy, they were forced to remain silent under his high-pressure rule.

Over time, more and more demons accepted him, seeing no harm in him being the Proud Monarch.

In the past decades, Amon had successfully repelled three crusades from the Holy Church, boosting his prestige both internally and externally.

If the issue of Merlin and Lilith’s disappearance could not be resolved, Amon would be the only candidate for the position.

Amon felt the time was ripe — the opposition was silenced, and all that was needed was a grand ceremony to declare him the true Demon Lord, removing the “acting” label.

“Lord Orobas, isn’t Lord Belial supposed to help me? Has he spoken to the other Demon Lords about my abilities?”

“Rest assured, your performance in repelling the crusades has earned you praise. There is no one else who can compete with you for the title of Proud Monarch.” Orobas replied calmly.

“I am the true master of the palace now. Vivian’s old followers have been suppressed, and there are no more opponents.” Amon said confidently. “I think now is the perfect time to hold a ceremony and officially take the throne. I hope Lord Belial will support me so that the other Demon Lords and the Council will recognize me.”

Orobas turned, frowning.

“Why the rush? You still haven’t found Vivian’s children. As long as they are alive, you cannot sit on the throne.”

title: Chapter 28 — Return (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 28 — Return (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 34 · Chapter 28

"Why am I unable to sit still? Can't you see? Now in this Demon Lord Palace, only I have the final say." Amon's face was grim, not very convinced, he said, "Vivian's children have been missing for decades; how could they possibly threaten me?"

"The demon race's rule system was established by the first few Demon Lords and prophets; Vivian's children are descendants of the first Demon Lords. As long as they remain alive, the rules are hard to break. To have other Demon Lords acknowledge you as the new Arrogant Sovereign, the precondition is that Vivian's children never appear; otherwise, acknowledging you would be tantamount to denying themselves." Europa said solemnly.

"Amon hesitated; he himself was not familiar with the first Demon Lord's descendants, which indeed is the problem. 'If you insist on becoming the true Arrogant Sovereign now, it will inevitably provoke the dissatisfaction of Vivian's old faction, and the First Demon Lord Palace will fall into civil war. Clearly you are already the ruler here; the empty title of monarch doesn't matter.' Europa said in a persuasive tone.

'This is different; an acting Demon Lord is always just an acting one. I want to obtain a status equal to that of other Demon Lords.' Amon, unwilling to give up, said arrogantly, 'Vivian's old faction is nothing to fear; whoever dares to step forward to stop me, I'll just kill them.'

'Your lack of regard for others will eventually be your own downfall.' Europa paused, emphasizing, 'Do not assume my father will fully assist you; you have not yet completed the task of killing Merlin.' 'I now just want to quickly finish the task assigned by His Majesty Belial.' Amon laughed, slowly saying, 'They siblings are very likely already fled to the human nations; with my identity as acting Demon Lord, it would be difficult to dispatch demons to infiltrate human territory to search for them, but if I were truly the Arrogant Sovereign? I could mobilize more power, surely I could soon find their clues.' Europa stared at Amon's eyes, silently turned back to stare at the blood pool, coldly saying —— 'You will bear the consequences.'

On the outskirts of the Despair Canyon, in Pudum's two-story wooden cottage. Xiu was holding a hot coffee, leaning against the bookshelf, gazing out the window, worrying almost every day about Merlin's condition, once even wanting to bring Pudum into the Despair Canyon to investigate. But the area called the Dead Land is dangerous; Xiu and Pudum cannot guarantee they could come out alive if anything happened— who would take care of Lilith? Under these circumstances, Xiu and Pudum dare not act rashly; they can only stay here obediently, patiently waiting for news of Merlin, and in the blink of an eye, several decades have passed—

Pudum was tidying the books on the table, suddenly stopped, and said with deep meaning, 'Time really flies; His Highness Merlin has been away for decades.' 'Yes, it really is fast.' Xiu sighed, saying that for humans a few decades might be long, but for demons it's still okay. 'Careful calculation: if His Highness is still alive, he should be an adult by now?' Pudum raised his head to ask. 'Exactly, he already entered the stage of adult demons a few years ago; it's a pity he's not by our side, not even having a coming-of-age ceremony,' Xiu let out a sigh. 'It's such a pity.' Pudum shook his head, having to face a fact: 'Several decades have passed, and His Highness still has no news at all. Although I don't want to admit it, is His Highness...?' 'Don't indulge in wild thoughts, Pudum; it won't happen, he will surely return alive.' Xiu said with a firm tone. 'What makes you so certain?' Pudum frowned. 'Because I am willing to believe that His Highness can.' Xiu gazed out the window at the scenery. 'Again, you know full well that His Highness Merlin has no self-preservation ability; entering the Despair Canyon is a near-certain death, a matter of countless deaths versus a slim chance of survival, not something you can just believe and come out alive.' Pudum paused, emphasizing, 'Think about the countless ferocious monsters in the Despair Canyon; any one of them could take Merlin's life! For an immature, weak demon, the odds of survival inside are virtually zero!' 'So what? As long as I haven't personally seen Merlin's corpse, then he must be alive.' Xiu turned his head, locking eyes with Pudum and saying. 'You're too stubborn, Xiu.' Pudum shook his head and sighed, seriously saying, 'You keep using sweet words to coax Princess Lilith, but sooner or later the truth will come out. If Merlin never returns, do you understand what severe blow she would suffer?' 'I harbor no malice; I merely gave Princess Lilith hope, which will keep her anticipating tomorrow. She has already lost her mother; if she also loses her brother, that would be the deadliest blow.' Xiu said very seriously, not wanting to see Lilith become lifeless. 'This can only be concealed for a while; Merlin has been missing for decades, and Princess Lilith may have already sensed something.' Pudum lowered his head, remorsefully saying—— 'Perhaps we should never have agreed to let Merlin go to the Despair Canyon; that was a rash decision.'

In the courtyard, Lilith sat alone on the swing, swaying back and forth, gazing toward the distant Despair Canyon, unable to help but let out a wistful sigh. Lilith has grown a lot; she is no longer the petite figure she once was. Although she hasn't reached adulthood yet and her height isn't impressive, she can be considered a young lady now. After Merlin left, Lilith felt extremely heartbroken, crying for a long time before accepting the fact that her brother was no longer by her side. She once tried to sneak into the Despair Canyon to find her brother, but halfway she was caught by Xiu and brought back, after which she was confined to the small courtyard, not allowed to leave freely. Lilith doesn't know how dangerous the Despair Canyon is; she simply wants to see Merlin. Xiu does not allow Vivian's two children to set foot in that perilous forbidden land. Although Xiu constantly tells Lilith that Merlin will surely return, after so much time has passed, she can't help but develop many doubts, wondering if her brother has encountered danger. 'Lilith!' Merlin's voice suddenly rang out; Lilith jerked, startled, showing a helpless smile, thinking she was having an auditory hallucination again. Such things happen often; Lilith would occasionally hear her brother's voice, search everywhere, but find nothing. 'You've grown quite a bit, haven't you? You're almost up to my shoulder; it seems Xiu and Pudum really have been taking good care of you.' 'Huh?' This was the first time she had experienced such an auditory hallucination repeatedly; Lilith jerked her head up, and Merlin's figure immediately came into view. Having lived year-round in the Despair Canyon, Merlin's clothes were already tattered; after returning, he wore a grass skirt, held the demon sword Banri Garan in his hand, his hair messy like a bird's nest, completely the appearance of a wild mountain man. Lilith gasped, eyes wide open, unable to believe what she saw, staring blankly at the suddenly appearing Merlin, even wondering if she hadn't yet woken up. 'Why aren't you reacting at all?' Merlin bent down, pinched Lilith's little cheek, teasing— 'Don't you recognize me? I'm your brother.' 'Don't pretend; wake up quickly.' ("w") Friend, do you have a ticket?

title: Chapter 29 — Coronation Ceremony
content:
Chapter 29 — Coronation Ceremony

Volume 34 · Chapter 29

“Brother?!!” Lilith woke up as if from a dream, her little face aching from being pulled, her eyes gradually turning red. She was at a loss, her feelings becoming extremely complicated. Even though she had imagined countless times what her brother’s return would look like, when Merlin actually stood before her, she still couldn’t quell the turmoil in her heart. Lilith eagerly threw herself into Merlin’s embrace, her hands unconsciously scratching his back, afraid that the brother who had finally returned would disappear. “Where did you go? Why did you abandon me? …” “Ha …” Merlin gave an embarrassed smile, lowering his head to look at his sister, “I didn’t intentionally abandon you; to end the life of fleeing, I had to make my own choice.” “Even if you had to go to the Despair Canyon, couldn’t you have told me beforehand?” Lilith said, her tone full of resentment. “If I had told you, would you still have let me leave? Don’t be so sad, look, I’m fine, aren’t I?” Merlin scratched his head, thinking that since he had come back alive, there was no need to dwell on the past. “That’s a different matter,” Lilith pouted, still dissatisfied — A sudden rush of footsteps sounded, Podom burst out of the house barefoot, eyes wide as he carefully examined Merlin. Although Merlin’s appearance had changed somewhat after adulthood, one could still recognize him at a glance — this was the boy who had once entered the Despair Canyon alone decades ago! “Your Highness! You really are back?! ?” “Get out of the way!” Xiu, anxious, kicked Podom aside who was blocking the front, swiftly came before Merlin, gripping his shoulders tightly, moved, he said — “It’s true! Not a ghost! You succeeded! You really walked out of the Despair Canyon!” ““Merlin looked embarrassed, speechless, saying, “How could I be a ghost? Do you really think I would definitely die in the canyon? You’re underestimating me too much.” “No no no! I didn’t mean that!” Xiu waved his hands repeatedly, explaining, “You should know, no demon has ever left the Despair Canyon alive; you are the first demon to succeed.” “Is that so?” Merlin thought for a moment; he was the only demon who had ever left the Despair Canyon alive, thus making history. “Congratulations on your safe return. To be honest, if you had still sent no word, I and Podom would have gone mad.” Xiu finally could speak frankly, usually he had been using lies to create the illusion that Merlin was still alive. “Actually I could have returned earlier, but I always felt my strength was insufficient, so I needed to keep training, which is why I came back so late.” Merlin explained sheepishly. “Your Highness! Your Highness!” Podom came over, face full of excitement, asking, “Did you really live in the Despair Canyon for decades? What is it like in there?” “That’s hard to explain in a short while.” Merlin scratched his cheek awkwardly, thinking the Despair Canyon held many wondrous things completely unlike the outside; without three days and nights, it couldn’t be made clear. “Then did you meet the Prophet? Or perhaps the remains of your grandfather Mephistopheles?” Podom was very interested in these things, eager for an answer. “No.” Merlin answered truthfully; not to mention the Prophet, he didn’t even know where Mephistopheles had died in the Despair Canyon; the area was overrun with magical beasts, his flesh would have long been devoured. “Podom! That’s enough, my brother has just returned, don’t ask so many questions.” Lilith scolded dissatisfiedly. “Right right right! It’s my fault for overstepping.” Podom gave an embarrassed laugh; indeed now wasn’t the time to ask about everything. “Brother …” Lilith sized up her brother, unable to help swallowing, “You’ve become much stronger, just the type I like~” “Behave yourself.” Merlin said with a dark face. “Huh? Brother, what’s this?” Lilith pointed at the shocking scar on Merlin’s chest, “How did you get this scar?” “This …” Merlin lowered his head to look, his expression hesitant, debating whether to reveal the curse that had afflicted him. “Let’s go inside to talk; don’t stand here. I’ll go prepare a lavish dinner to celebrate your return properly.” Podom rolled up his sleeves, ready to welcome Merlin. “No need for all that trouble; time is short, let’s set out.” Merlin stopped Podom, because there were more important matters to attend to. “Where to? Do you still have other business?” Xiu asked in surprise. “Return to the Demon Lord Palace; it’s time to settle accounts with Ammon. I will personally take back what was lost back then.” Merlin said solemnly. “Ah? Your Highness, don’t rush; you’ve only just come of age, can you really defeat Ammon?” Podom frowned, worried, unable to gauge Merlin’s current strength — there wasn’t even a hint of pressure. “Yeah, brother, even if you want to return to the Demon Lord Palace, you need sufficient strength.” Lilith also doubted; aside from becoming much stronger, she saw no essential change in Merlin compared to before. “Your Highness, I suggest you discuss this properly with us; don’t make such a rash decision.” Xiu shook his head, believing that even as an adult, Merlin’s mindset hadn’t matured much and he was still prone to being impulsive. “Don’t worry, Ammon is just a minor figure; defeating him isn’t hard, believe me.” Merlin spoke with confidence; in the Despair Canyon there were many magical beasts stronger than Ammon, and though he once thought Ammon formidable, now he sees him as insignificant. Xiu and Podom stared at each other, baffled by where Merlin’s confidence came from — the two of them together couldn’t even beat Ammon, yet Merlin called him a minor role? Merlin stepped before Podom, firmly grasped his hand, and sincerely said, “Podom, come with me; I need you.” “Ah …” Podom, flattered and flustered, said, “I’m not skilled at combat; I only do useless things.” “No, I believe art and history are important; they carry the spirit of countless predecessors and give proper guidance to the younger generation. You possess a rare talent!” Merlin looked into Podom’s eyes, speaking from the heart, “You are my person; come with me, for the future Demon Lord Palace cannot do without you.” Podom’s face turned red, unsure how to reply; he felt the wording sounded a bit off, as if the meaning wasn’t quite right. A few days later, the Demon Lord Palace held an unprecedented event — the coronation of the King of Pride. To sit upon the throne of the Pride Demon Lord and become the first demon lord not descended from the original monarch’s line, Ammon had exerted great effort, finally awaiting this crucial day! All nobles and officials of the First Demon Lord Palace gathered in the main hall, whispering among themselves under Ammon’s oppressive pressure, daring only to speak softly about this matter. Ammon wanted exactly this effect: to sit firmly upon the demon lord’s throne before all demons, compelling them to accept this fact. Boom — — The heavy doors of the main hall were slowly opened; Ammon, clad in splendid attire, appeared before the eyes of all — the new king was about to be born! Everyone, the monthly votes are powerful, keep the updates coming!

title: Chapter 30 — Return to the Demon Lord Palace (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)
content:
Chapter 30 — Return to the Demon Lord Palace (Monthly Ticket Bonus Chapter)

Volume 34 · Chapter 30

The demons bowed their heads upon seeing Amon, silencing their murmurs for fear of drawing its attention.

After years of suppression, there were no longer any open opponents of Amon within the Demon Lord Palace; they could only criticize it in secret.

Amon’s gaze was sharp as it swept over the guests present, nodding in satisfaction. All the demons who were supposed to be here had arrived, and they would witness this historic moment with their own eyes.

Blackman lowered his head and whispered, “Looking at that bastard’s smug expression, I really want to smash his skull with a hammer.”

“Calm down. It’s not the right time to act yet,” Ophelia replied in a low voice.

“I underestimated its courage. I thought this guy wouldn’t dare truly sit on the throne and would always manage the Demon Lord Palace as an acting Demon Lord. I didn’t expect…” Blackman gritted his teeth, veins throbbing on his forehead, “that it would trample on the bottom line so easily.”

“Heamon repelled several crusades by the Holy Church, and its reputation outside has grown higher and higher. Presumably, the other lords are turning a blind eye to it becoming the new Demon Lord of Pride, which is why it dares to act recklessly,” Ophelia speculated, feeling that the other lords were kicking them while they were down, treating the First Demon Lord Palace as a toy to be manipulated at will.

“Amon’s ancestors were not the First Demon Lord. What right does it have to inherit the throne? This is blatant usurpation. He is the greatest traitor in the history of the First Demon Lord Palace,” Blackman cursed under his breath, his teeth itching with hatred.

“Amon will not succeed. Today is its death day,” Ophelia said coldly, sinister killing intent flashing in her eyes.

“Is it true that you are marrying him?” Blackman looked at Ophelia suspiciously, worried that she was walking into a tiger’s den.

“Of course it’s false. I just wanted to get close to him. We’ll take him out in a moment,” Ophelia said, already prepared.

“Don’t worry, I’m ready too.” Blackman had long since placed his hand inside his pants, ready at any moment.

Ophelia rolled her eyes. Under normal circumstances, she would never cooperate with Blackman, but aside from him, no other demon was willing to risk rebelling against Amon now.

“Even if we join forces, we probably can’t beat Amon, right? Its strength is far above ours,” Blackman said with great concern.

“At a time like this, are you still afraid of death?” Ophelia said disdainfully, pulling out the tip of a dagger from her sleeve. “Look at what this is?”

“A dagger? Do you intend to assassinate Amon? That won’t succeed; its vigilance is very high,” Blackman frowned deeply.

“This is a dagger coated with the venom of a three-eyed snake. As long as I can make a small cut, we’ve won,” Ophelia narrowed her eyes. She was not unprepared.

Blackman stared in astonishment, finally understanding why Ophelia had agreed to marry Amon. It was to use the poisoned dagger to wound Amon; making a small cut still offered a chance.

Surrounded by numerous demon guards, Amon slowly entered the center of the arena, nodding respectfully to the demon nobles on both sides, examining its subjects like a king.

This was the most spotlighted moment in Amon’s life. It thoroughly enjoyed being surrounded by countless demons. After becoming the new Lord of Pride, it would change the rules of the demon race.

Only descendants of the First Demon Lord would be able to inherit the Demon Lord Palace; that era would become history. Any demon would have the opportunity to become the master of the demon race.

Amon glanced at Ophelia, feeling pleased. Today, it would not only announce its formal ascension as the Demon Lord of Pride but also announce that Ophelia would become its bride.

Success in both career and love—this was what one might call a winner in life.

“Everyone!” Amon stood on the high platform, gently stroking the throne of the Demon Lord of Pride, and announced loudly, “Decades have passed, and the two princes remain missing without news. If this continues, our First Demon Lord Palace may suffer huge impacts. As the acting Demon Lord, I have done my utmost to protect the safety of the palace, which everyone has witnessed. However, I am merely a temporary proxy, lacking authority over many matters, which has led to the First Demon Lord Palace becoming increasingly marginalized among the demons. Considering the interests of all the demons present, I declare! I will become the next Lord of Pride, inheriting Lucifer’s name as Demon Lord!”

Upon hearing this, the demons below fell silent. There was no applause or cheering, as if they already knew Amon intended to do this.

Some demons felt extremely dissatisfied because Amon did not have the qualification, yet they feared retaliation.

Tru stood quite far forward. Having lowered his dignity to swear allegiance to Amon had indeed earned him重用 (heavy use/prominence), but this was not what he wanted. The stain of being the son of a deserter had not been cleared; instead, he was despised even more by other demons.

Regarding the reaction of the demons below, Amon felt indifferent, having expected it all along. “There is another happy matter. Miss Ophelia has accepted my proposal. She will become my wife and help me handle internal affairs of the Demon Lord Palace. I hope everyone will fully cooperate.”

Under the gaze of numerous demons, Ophelia, dressed in magnificent attire and holding the hem of her skirt, slowly walked up the steps to the high platform, standing beside Amon.

Many demons had never heard of this matter. Ophelia, as a former subordinate of Vivian, agreeing to marry Amon was considered very unexpected.

“Our couple will join hands to create a better future for the First Demon Lord together.”

“You’re dreaming!”

Seizing this opportunity, Ophelia’s dagger, coated in snake venom, popped out from her sleeve. With lightning speed, she fiercely thrust it toward Amon’s chest.

Amon’s eyes widened in shock, pupils contracting rapidly. It had not anticipated Ophelia would attack in such a setting and could not dodge the assassination attempt!

Ding—

A crisp sound rang out. Ophelia was stunned into speechlessness. The dagger had indeed pierced Amon’s chest, but it was blocked by some sturdy armor, unable to harm the opponent!

Amon’s face turned dark instantly. It slapped Ophelia across the face, sending her flying to the ground.

“Ugh!” Ophelia covered her cheek, a trickle of blood escaping the corner of her mouth, looking at Amon in disbelief.

“Did you think I would be unprepared? Ophelia,” Amon tore open its inner lining, revealing black-gold armor underneath. The dagger could not penetrate it.

Seeing Ophelia in trouble, Blackman below had no choice but to step forward with grim determination.

Having completed the transformation from male to female, Blackman’s crotch had transformed into a heavy thunder warhammer. Its body assumed a demonic posture, covered in green scales, with membranous wings spread wide!

Blackman leaped into the air, bathed in the light of lightning, sparks of electricity spraying from its eyes, resembling a God of Thunder!

Blackman’s feminine figure was graceful and fiery. In the blink of an eye, it appeared before Amon, wielding the Thunder Demon Warhammer wildly, repeatedly striking at the enemy’s head!

“Is that it?”

Amon showed contempt, easily dodging Blackman’s lethal attacks. The two were not on the same level of power.

Blackman gritted its teeth, growing increasingly impatient in its heart. It spun in the air, gathering countless bolts of lightning toward the sky.

Saint-tier battle aura condensed into lightning focused on the warhammer. Blackman’s pressure reached its peak, clearly intending to fight to the death.

Thunder exploded like heavenly punishment sent by gods. The demons below panicked, not expecting Ophelia and Blackman to suddenly attack!

Blackman descended from the sky, the Thunder Demon Warhammer in its hands radiating brilliant light, almost merging with the thunder itself, smashing down with full force onto Amon’s head.

“Die! Amon! You traitor!”

Amon sneered, not bothering to dodge. It simply tilted its head, letting the Thunder Demon Warhammer strike its left shoulder.

Bang! The lightning raised a massive shockwave, causing the earth beneath Amon’s feet to tremble and shattering all the walls of the hall!

Normally, suffering such a fierce attack from Blackman would leave one crippled on the spot, if not dead!

Yet Amon stood there as if nothing had happened, tilting its neck to look quietly at Blackman, a mocking smile playing on its lips.

“This is impossible?!” Blackman was greatly shocked, unable to believe the fact that after a full-power strike, the opponent had only suffered minor scratches!

“Blackman, you really haven’t learned your lesson, have you?”

Amon’s gaze condensed. Its fist shot out, hitting Blackman in the chest, sinking deep into its flesh. Countless bones broke, and its internal organs were nearly shattered by the impact.

Blackman coughed up a mouthful of blood, its body flying backward like a cannonball, crashing through and breaking the pillars supporting the Demon Lord Palace, buried deep beneath the ruins, its life and death unknown.

“Tch!” Ophelia got up from the ground, stretching her mouth to the roots of her ears, spewing green venom from the depths of her throat at incredible speed! It could melt rock and metal instantly!

Amon had anticipated this, spinning around to avoid Ophelia’s attack, then appearing before her, grabbing her throat with both hands and lifting her off the ground forcefully.

Ophelia’s feet left the ground. She struggled desperately, scratching red marks on Amon’s arms, but still couldn’t escape this madman.

“I liked you so much. Why don’t you understand? Always hurting me again and again in this way,” Amon asked seriously, its expression puzzled.

“You’re unworthy!” Ophelia answered through gritted teeth.

Amon’s face turned “swish” black, its features twisted with uncontrollable anger. “Then disappear, Ophelia. You forced me to do this.”

Ophelia clearly felt Amon’s grip tightening. Her breathing became increasingly difficult, her voice growing hoarse. “Ah… ah…”

As Ophelia’s neck was about to be snapped by Amon’s own hands, the demons below bowed their heads in silence, filled with fear of Amon.

Whoever dared to speak up and stop Amon’s brutality at this moment would surely die!

“Stop it, Amon!”

A reprimand came from outside. Amon paused abruptly, its eyeballs rolling as it wondered who had such guts to jump out and seek death after dealing with two opponents consecutively!

Merlin walked openly into the great hall, stepping on the crimson carpet, appearing before all the demons.

He stopped, ignoring the shocked gazes around him, looked up at Amon on the high platform, and said expressionlessly:

“Let go of Ophelia.”

“You should consider me your enemy.”

“Do you enjoy bullying the weak? Is that all you’re capable of?”

title: Chapter 31 — Reckoning
content:
Chapter 31 — Reckoning

Volume 34 · Chapter 31

Although Merlin's appearance changed greatly after reaching adulthood, some unique features remained, and the demons of the Demon Lord's Palace easily recognized him.

Merlin, who had disappeared for several decades, suddenly appeared at the moment when Amon was preparing to formally become the Sovereign of Pride, causing the demons present to be greatly astonished—
"His Highness the Prince! You've grown so big?"
"Where has he been all these years? Why is there no news at all?"
"His return now is not a good thing; Amon will kill him."
Merlin turned a deaf ear to the demons' gossip; he came this time to inherit the legacy left by his mother, Vivian.
Xiu, Podom, and Lilith were stationed outside by Merlin to prevent any idle interferers from disrupting his confrontation with Amon.
Xiu and Podom wanted to help Merlin fight Amon together, but he refused them.
Now Merlin is full of confidence in his own strength; Amon, who once seemed a formidable foe, now appears insignificant.

Du Lu stared wide-eyed in shock, never expecting Merlin to return on his own—Amon's forces in the Demon Lord's Palace are immense; this is clearly not a wise move!
Amon froze in place, his expression stunned, his eyes locked on Merlin's face, his inner turmoil raging like a storm, unable to calm for a long time.
Clearly he had sent many subordinates to search everywhere for Merlin with no result, yet he never imagined Merlin would show up at his doorstep seeking death!
Amon couldn't fathom it: if Merlin were willing to hide as a turtle in the human realms, he might live out his life in peace—why come back? Is he just tired of living?
"Oh~, Your Highness the Prince, how have you returned?"

Amon tossed Ophelia aside, then with perfect form bowed toward Merlin.
"Cough cough!" Ophelia's consciousness was hazy; she vaguely saw Merlin's silhouette and instantly grew excited, "Your Highness—"
"I have nothing wrong with returning; this is my home," Merlin replied righteously.
"You're right, this is your home, but that's all in the past," Amon said, revealing a meaningful smile, "Now the master of the Demon Lord's Palace is me."
"It's a pity you're only a temporary administrator," Merlin emphasized.
"No, you've been gone for decades; when the Demon Lord's Palace faced foreign invasion and was in grave danger, you contributed nothing—it was I! I led the demons to prevent the Palace from falling again." Amon paused, then said loudly, "In a sense, I saved the demons present! Acting Demon Lord? What a joke—I am clearly the true Demon Lord!"
"Why can't I return after disappearing for decades? You know better than I do," Merlin asked expressionlessly, locking eyes with Amon.
"What nonsense are you spouting? I've never given up searching for you all these years; all the demons can testify for me," Amon sneered, curling his lips, "Your Highness, are you implying I want to harm you? That's a ridiculous slander; you merely see that I've made the Demon Lord's Palace thrive and have come back to reap the rewards, right?"

"Amon shamelessly turned the tables, making Merlin feel deep disgust; thus he patiently said, 'You have devoted yourself wholeheartedly to the Demon Lord's Palace, and I am truly grateful for your great contribution—thank you for your hard work.'
'I don't need false encouragement; I only wish you would stay away forever, for I am the most suitable heir to the Demon Lord's throne. When you abandoned the Demon Lord's Palace, you already relinquished your right to the crown.' Amon paused, seeing that Merlin remained ordinary even after adulthood, and pressed further, 'Do you think you can bear the burden of the Demon Lord? With your strength, you can't even defeat my pet dog, let alone face the countless Holy Temple Knights' invasion.'"

"Give it up; you could never become the Sovereign of Pride—no demon would acknowledge you," Merlin issued his final warning.
"Who says that? Who opposes me?" Amon glanced over the demons; all fell silent, then added, "Several other monarchs have already recognized my ability; my becoming the third Sovereign of Pride is undoubtedly the will of the masses!"

"Other monarchs have no authority to decide the successor of the First Demon Lord's Palace; don't put on a tiger's act here—your poor acting is disgusting."
Merlin collected his stern expression and smiled, "Since you so desire to be the Demon Lord, I'll give you one chance."
"What do you mean?" Amon demanded from above.
"Kill me! If you succeed in killing me, you will be the third-generation Lucifer!" Merlin replied firmly.

These words caused an uproar in the hall; the demons shouted in shock, thinking Merlin was playing with fire—
"Did I hear correctly? Prince Merlin wants to challenge Amon? Or is it a life-or-death duel?"
"This is insane; Prince Merlin still uses magic and martial arts—isn't this just suicide?"
"If Prince Merlin were willing to negotiate with Amon, there might still be a chance—why make such a foolish decision?"
Many demons looked at Merlin with suspicion, believing that as long as he submitted to Amon, he could continue living in the Demon Lord's Palace.

Amon examined Merlin, feeling no pressure at all, even wanting to laugh—this isn't just handing over the Demon Lord's throne to me for free, is it?
"Is that really true?"
"Of course it is; I swear by the name of Mephistopheles' descendant that if I die by your hand, there is no doubt you are more fit to become the Demon Lord." Merlin spoke earnestly, placing the throne of the First Demon Lord's Palace on the betting table.

"Fine! Although you've made no progress in strength, your boldness surprises me," Amon said, growing eager; all the demons heard Merlin's words—this is their chance, not only to easily become the Demon Lord but also to openly kill Merlin and fulfill Belial's task!
"Your Highness! Don't do this! This is Amon's trap! You can't defeat him!" Ophelia staggered up

title: Chapter 32 — New King
content:
Chapter 32 — New King

Volume 34 · Chapter 32

Amon immediately found himself suppressed by Merlin as soon as he appeared, causing the whole scene to fall silent; the demons stared at each other in shock, none daring to speak casually. The demons who had previously belittled him also shut their mouths, realizing something was off. Amon’s great strength was obvious to all, yet he had suffered a loss at Merlin’s hands—how could that be normal? The demons began to wonder what Merlin had experienced over these past decades, transforming from a weak prince into a powerful demon capable of suppressing Amon with a single punch. “…Did I see wrong? Wasn’t His Highness that strong before? Amon is actually being suppressed,” Ophelia lowered her head in a daze, hardly able to believe her eyes; the former Merlin had always needed protection, but now he could stand on his own! Her heart fluttered, thinking Merlin had become even more perfect—exactly the man of her dreams~ A mysterious blush rose on Ophelia’s face, delighted by Merlin’s growth, her mind filled with thoughts of how she could become the youngest queen in demon history. “Hahaha,” accompanied by a series of chilling cold laughs, Amon crawled up from the ruins, his body undergoing a huge change as he revealed his true demon form. His skin turned emerald green, bone spurs sprouted across his back, and his face grew much more hideous, resembling a lizard. Unlike other high‑ranking demons, he had no membranous wings, only horns on his head that were far larger than those of ordinary demons. It is well known that demons reveal their true selves to better unleash their power. Amon had always looked down on Merlin, this greenhouse‑grown flower, but now he could not afford to take him lightly. “Interesting, it seems Your Highness has made some progress over these decades, learning quite a bit~” “I’ll give you a chance—submit to me, and I’ll spare your life.” Merlin’s attitude was icy, as if mocking Amon’s ignorance. “I could submit to your mother Vivian, but I cannot submit to you, because you’re unworthy. Take a good look—in every way, you fall short of me.” Amon spread his hands, speaking arrogantly. “That was the past; times have changed, Amon.” Merlin emphasized sternly. “Hehehe, don’t get cocky just because you grabbed a small advantage; in truth your power has already reached the peak of the Saint‑tier, hasn’t it? You deliberately pretended to be weak to lure me in—how despicable.” Amon snarled, believing he had fallen into a trap. “Huh?” Merlin tilted his head, puzzled, thinking Amon had misunderstood; just now it was pure physical strength—what people call “great strength works wonders!” “I won’t give you another chance to trick yourself, Your Highness.” Amon dropped to all fours, looking exactly like a lizard; his muscles bulged like balloons, instantly swelling and flashing a metallic luster. He bared his sharp fangs, the Zongjing battle aura surged wildly, shattering the surrounding floorboards. Boom! Amon shot forward like an arrow from a bow, radiating the ferocity of a hungry tiger pouncing on a sheep, and threw a straight punch at Merlin’s face, kicking up a biting gust of wind. “Are you still underestimating me?” Merlin’s eyes narrowed; he retreated, took a stance, and thrust his right fist forward without retreating, directly colliding with Amon. The two fists smashed together, erupting with a thunder‑like boom; the violent shockwave flung all nearby demons flying. Crack! Amon was sent sprawling, crashing hard to the ground; the pale white bones in his arm had already pierced through, and Merlin broke it on the spot. He struggled to rise from the ground, looked at his now‑useless arm, and let it hang limp. Amon lifted his head toward Merlin, his eyes twitching wildly, a surge of fear welling up as he finally realized something was wrong. “You bunch of bastards, what are you looking at?! Why aren’t you joining me to crush him?! Have you forgotten the favors I’ve given you?!” Amon screamed hysterically, hoping for the demons’ help, feeling he couldn’t beat Merlin. The surrounding demons lowered their heads, pretending not to hear, with no intention of intervening. Amon had done too many evil deeds in his quest to become Demon Lord, ruthlessly suppressing other demons, which left him isolated—some of his supporters were eager to lend a hand, but Du Lu blocked them with poison‑coated chains, refusing to let them interfere. Seeing this, Amon flew into a rage: “Du Lu! What are you doing? Do you want to rebel?!” “Lord Amon, I mean no harm; I only wish this duel to be fair and just, for it concerns who will become the master of the First Demon Lord Palace.” Du Lu replied calmly. “Sure enough, you’re the son of a deserter, betraying me at the crucial moment—you’ll go to hell!” Amon cursed madly. “Even you think that way, I’m sorry.” Du Lu silently closed his eyes. “No one will help you, Amon; this situation is entirely of your own making.” Merlin said blandly. “Shut up! I don’t need help—I can kill you myself! Do you think I’ll come to you begging for mercy in tears? Dream on!” The Zongjing battle aura shot skyward; Amon sucked in a breath, exhaled a thick black mist that instantly filled the hall, plunging all demons into utter darkness. Merlin stood in the center of the blackness, seeing nothing around him, as if he’d entered another world; even his perception plummeted. Swish! A heavy blow from Amon struck Merlin’s back, burning pain making him frown, unable to locate his opponent. “Hehehe, how’s that? This is my secret technique! In my domain you can’t find my position, while I can toy with you to death!” Amon’s triumphant voice echoed from all directions: “In my eyes you’re forever a useless thing; if not for Vivian’s protection, you’d have long been cast out as beast fodder.” Merlin didn’t answer; instead he gripped his left hand’s Banri Garan, ready to deliver a fatal blow to end the duel, closing his eyes to sense his surroundings. “Tsk tsk tsk, still obsessed with the draw‑cut technique? I’ve told you countless times—it’s just a useless beginner’s sword skill, truly disappointing. You’re not only weak, but also foolish~” Amon kept jeering. “Actually you also disappoint me; with your strength, in the Despair Canyon you’d only be fit as low‑grade prey.” Merlin paused, then added, “My draw‑cut technique is far more terrifying than you imagine.” As soon as he finished speaking, Merlin suddenly drew his sword; the rusted blade scraped violently against the scabbard, sending up bright sparks and a clear, trembling resonance that stirred the soul. Accompanied by the flash of fire, the dark smoke‑filled world was instantly sliced by a shining blade; the killing sword intent let out a death‑piercing shriek. The thick black mist dissipated, and the demons stared blankly around—there stood Amon, upright in his original spot, while Merlin had his back to them. A red line appeared on Amon’s neck; before the eyes of all, his head fell off, his life completely stripped away by Banri Garan, becoming nourishment for Merlin’s survival. Amon had countless times mocked Merlin for his obsession with the draw‑cut technique; he never imagined he himself would die by that very beginner’s skill. Merlin, before all the demons, slowly returned Banri Garan to its sheath, then turned to gaze at Amon’s corpse; the gloom in his heart vanished completely. Amon’s slight against Merlin had been a grudge long festering in his heart; now this detestable wretch finally received his due punishment. “We didn’t get it wrong, did we? Banri Garan has been drawn! Everyone, quickly look at the weapon in His Highness Merlin’s hand!” “It’s true! After countless ages, Banri Garan has found a new master!” “Mephistopheles once said: whoever can draw Banri Garan is the true master of the First Demon Lord Palace!” The sight of Merlin wielding Banri Garan shocked the demons immensely; they muttered incoherently, their eyes filled only with endless awe. Since the great prophet, Banri Garan had never been drawn by anyone—yet Vivian’s son succeeded! If this news spreads, it will surely shake the entire demon race, for Banri Garan’s significance is extraordinary. It is the relic left by that great prophet; only one who is not an ordinary demon but a genius‑level demon with immense potential can wield it. Blackman clenched his teeth, crawled out of the ruins, weakly leaned against the wall, and gazed far at Merlin’s figure: “He’s appeared—this is the true master of the First Demon Lord Palace, no wonder it’s His Highness; I wasn’t mistaken…” Ophelia stared again, dumbfounded, standing like a wooden puppet, her shocked expression frozen on her face, her mind plunged into endless chaos. Today Merlin had given her too many shocks; successive mental blows made her suspect that the Merlin before her was an impostor. Ophelia’s mind kept replaying her father’s voice: the one who can draw Banri Garan is the strongest… demon. Merlin gazed at the throne on the high platform under the demons’ watch, stepped up the stairs one by one, and ascended. He gently stroked the throne belonging to the arrogant lord, recalling the sight of his mother Vivian once seated there. Turning around, he saw all the demons watching him, so without hesitation he took the seat of the Demon Lord. Gripping the hilt of Banri Garan with both hands, his expression solemn, a faint aura of demonic majesty appeared between his brows, and he said in a deep voice: “You all have two choices.” “Submit to me.” “Or” “die.” Merlin assumed the role of the arrogant lord; the immense pressure radiating from him made the demons feel breathless. No one doubted Merlin, for he was Vivian’s son and moreover the one who had drawn the extraordinarily significant Banri Garan. Thud thud thud, the demons below fell like dominoes, dropping to their knees, burying their heads deep in their chests, showing Merlin the utmost respect and loyalty! Even the wounded Blackman, gritting his teeth through the pain, forced himself to kneel far away, bowing to Merlin, hoping his loyalty would reach Merlin’s eyes. Ophelia came to her senses, lifted her skirt, knelt before Merlin, and kissed the back of his hand, swearing: “I pledge my soul to serve you forever, until my life’s end, O great king of sloth.” Merlin sat on the throne, looking down upon the kneeling demons, arrogantly lifting his chin. He was the lord of the Death Marsh, master of the fate of every living thing on this land—enjoying the sweetness of authority while bearing the bitterness of responsibility. Merlin noticed that, although all demons had submitted to him, one demon still stood; he sternly questioned, “Du Lu, are you really unwilling to submit to me?” Du Lu’s legs went weak; he trembled as he fell to the ground, pressing his ugly face firmly against the cold floor— “If your exalted self doesn’t despise me, then I am humbly honored…”

title: Chapter 33 — Merlin Kneels, Begging Everyone Not to Look!
content:
Chapter 33 — Merlin Kneels, Begging Everyone Not to Look!

Volume 34 · Chapter 33

Merlin smoothly became the new arrogant monarch, inheriting the title of Demon Lord Lucifer, and quickly integrated all the major forces within the First Demon Lord Palace. After Amon's death, Merlin did not settle scores with his supporters but forgave their crimes. Even Du鲁, who once served Amon, became an important cadre of the Demon Lord Palace and was given important responsibilities. Through a series of tough-on-the-outside, soft-on-the-inside measures, the scattered demons were reunited, fully demonstrating Merlin's benevolence and majesty. The demons who followed Amon all switched sides, swearing eternal loyalty to the youngest monarch in demon history. Many demon nobles, in order to survive, voluntarily relinquished their hereditary titles and offered up the wealth they had accumulated over generations with both hands. The First Demon Lord Palace, which had been continually marginalized, finally halted its decline after Merlin's return and regained its footing within the demon realm.

The demon race has an unwritten rule: any newly enthroned monarch must display their strength to gain recognition from other demon lords. This is not only an opportunity to establish the new king's image, but also a chance to fully show off their 'muscles' to deter other demons from harboring ill intentions.
