The news that Merlin successfully drew the demon sword Banri Garan spread like wildfire, quickly reaching the ears of other demon lords. To see the new master of Banri Garan with their own eyes, several monarchs attended the banquet hosted by the First Demon Lord Palace with invitations. At the gathering, under the gaze of countless demons, Merlin displayed part of the power of his 999-level sword-drawing technique. That single slash directly altered the topography of the Death Marsh, carving out a spectacular sight in the Orkney Strait—a massive trench named 'Lucifer's Abyss'! Seeing Merlin's displayed strength, the other demon lords may have scoffed outwardly, but deep inside they felt a growing dread. Especially Beleth, who was being manipulated by Behemoth, appeared calm on the surface, yet his heart was already churning with a tremendous wave—Indeed, as I expected, to obtain true freedom, one must first eliminate

That night at the gathering, Merlin plucked up the courage to invite Asmodeus to a rendezvous in the rear garden, wishing to express his endless love. It had been decades, yet Merlin could never forget Asmodeus's beauty; his memory remained frozen at the Seven Kings Conference. He had always dreamed of winning Asmodeus over, and having come to this other world for so long, he had never fixated on any 'woman'—Asmodeus was his sole dream lover. Coincidentally, Asmodeus also attended the First Demon Lord Palace's gathering; Merlin considered this his home turf and felt he must seize the opportunity to leave himself with an incomparably romantic memory~

"Your Majesty, the roses you wanted are ready." Pudom came running over excitedly and handed the freshly prepared roses to Merlin. "Not bad!" Merlin patted Pudom on the shoulder, gazing at the roses in his hand, imagining Asmodeus's shy look—surely it would be breathtakingly beautiful! Lilith immediately became alert, sternly questioning, "Brother, what do you need the roses for?" "What need to ask? Obviously, His Majesty has fallen for a lady!" Pudom clasped his hands together, sighing, "Roses are the symbol of love~" "Is that really true, brother?" Lilith threw her hands on her hips in exasperation, a thousand objections racing through her mind! "It's true; tonight I intend to confess to Asmodeus and win her over to become my wife." Merlin inhaled the scent of the roses, his face blissful. Pudom: "???" Lilith: "!!!"

"Hey! What's with those expressions? Shouldn't you be blessing me?" Merlin frowned, finding their reaction strange. "Brother, .you .you're serious?" Lilith's expression turned complex. "Of course it's true; don't doubt it—I've fallen deeply in love with Asmodeus, and no matter what method I use, I will definitely marry her (him)!" Merlin spoke with firm resolve, as if swearing. "Your Majesty, perhaps you should reconsider a little?" Pudom trembled nervously. "No need, Asmodeus is already waiting for me; I have no time to chat with you—just wait for my good news." Merlin waved his hand, strode toward the rear garden, then suddenly stopped, wondering, "Strange, Lilith, why aren't you causing trouble this time? Usually when a female demon approaches me, you often fly off the handle." Lilith thought for a moment, clenched her fists to cheer her brother on, "This time I support you, go for it, brother! You must succeed!"

The moonlight was like water, the night garden immersed in starlight, the drifting fragrance easily arousing desire. Asmodeus stood in the center of the garden, pacing back and forth calmly; moonlight shone on her black long dress, a beauty sufficient to make all blooming flowers pale in comparison. She had no idea what Vivian's son secretly wanted from her, assuming it was some important matter requiring a private discussion.

"Ah~, so beautiful." Merlin gazed at Asmodeus's silhouette from afar, heart fluttering nervously as he stepped forward, "Sorry I'm late; have you been waiting here long? Asmodeus lifted her head to glance at Merlin—then immediately smiled, shook her head, not angry at all; in fact she had only just arrived. Merlin's heart fluttered like a deer; the person he likes, in his eyes, undergoes infinite idealization; even a head shake becomes an endearing, unpretentious virtue. The atmosphere was quite nice; Merlin summoned his courage, swiftly drew the rose hidden behind his back, and personally offered it to Asmodeus, his eyes darting about. "?“Asmodeus looked at the rose in her hand, face full of confusion, vaguely sensing that something was off, wondering why flowers were being given— or perhaps it was a very special rose! "To be frank, from the moment I first saw you, my heart was stolen by you and has never returned; Merlin stammered, nervous to the point of forgetting his lines, so he secretly pulled out a small note from his pocket, glanced at it, and said, 'Ah~! I am the forest, you are the little bird, joyfully chirping among my branches; I am the river, you are the little fish, swimming to and fro in my waves; we will always be together, never parting! I have deeply fallen in love with you, Asmodeus; please accept my ardent affection!' "???"

Asmodeus stared wide-eyed in disbelief, never expecting Merlin to pull this stunt; struck dumbfounded on the spot, her expression turned panicked. She glanced at the rose in her hand, then at Merlin's sincere eyes, repeated this three times before falling silent for a while, then answered in a gruff voice— 'Brother, are you serious? I don't mind either way.' 'I would never have agreed to you originally, but your overly sentimental love poem moved me.' 'Life is short; why not give it a try?'

title: Chapter 34 — Dark History
content:
Chapter 34 — Dark History

Volume 34 · Chapter 34

Asmodeus's rough voice echoed in Merlin's ears for a long time, like a bucket of cold water poured from head to toe, instantly making him shiver and snap back to reality.

Merlin pointed at Asmodeus, wanting to say something but stopping himself. After organizing his thoughts for a long time in his heart, he cleared his throat and asked in a polite tone, "So, um, are you male?"

"That's right, I'm male. Did I ever say I was a female demon?" Asmodeus put on an innocent expression, as if Merlin falling for it had nothing to do with him.

"Ah—"

Merlin was somewhat at a loss for words, cold sweat sliding down his forehead. He never expected that another world would also have the absurd cross-dressing culture!

At this moment, Merlin felt struck by a bolt from the blue. His dream lover of decades was shattered in an instant! What replaced it was sheer terror!

Merlin's sexual orientation was absolutely fine. He had been completely bewitched by Asmodeus's appearance, and his views on love had suffered a devastating blow!

"I thought you called me for something important. I didn't expect it was to express your long-hidden passionate love for me. Have you even picked a wedding date?" Asmodeus asked meaningfully.

"No, no, no! You've misunderstood! What passionate love? That doesn't exist!" Merlin was losing face. His face felt hot and burning. Just recalling that incredibly greasy confession poem made him wish he could burrow into a crack in the ground!

"What's there to misunderstand? Weren't you just reciting that poem very passionately?" Asmodeus tilted his head curiously.

"Well—" Merlin tore the prepared little note into shreds and pretended nothing had happened. "What poem? I don't remember anything like that at all."

"What about this rose?" Asmodeus shook the rose in his hand. The chill it radiated couldn't be faked.

Merlin snatched the rose back in terror, threw it with all his might into the water jar, scratched his head and gave a nervous laugh. "Hahaha, sorry, this flower isn't for you. I just wanted you to take a look. How could I possibly give a rose to a man?"

"Then what you said about loving me so much—was that all fake too?" Asmodeus asked with a complicated expression, thinking this young demon changed his tune far too quickly.

"I'm very sorry!" Merlin was forced to bow and apologize, speaking with great sincerity. "There's been a considerable misunderstanding between us. Let's just pretend nothing happened just now. I wish you a good night's dream. Farewell!"

Asmodeus was taken aback. He watched Merlin flee the scene as if his life depended on it, clearly afraid that anyone else in the demon race would witness what had happened tonight. Otherwise, the dignity he had worked so hard to build would be completely ruined!

"Tsk tsk~" Asmodeus clicked his tongue and shook his head, making a sarcastic remark. "Before, you didn't know I was male and were enthusiastic to death. Now that you know, you're disgusted by me.果然, blondes really do tend to be scumbags~"

"Ugh!" Merlin's face turned dark instantly. Stimulated to the point of trembling all over, veins bulging on his forehead, he turned around and shouted back, "What does being a scumbag have to do with this!? You're a male demon! Why are you wearing a skirt!? That's terrifying, you know!?"

"What? This is my hobby. Don't I look beautiful in a skirt? Please answer me honestly." Asmodeus showed a meaningful smile, very curious about what Merlin was thinking right now.

Merlin's old face flushed red as he answered, then immediately flipped his expression. "But that's completely a different matter! You're a male! Wearing a skirt to seduce me is fraud! I'm the victim here!"

"What's the harm? We could totally try dating. If you don't try, how would you know it wouldn't work?" Asmodeus spread his hands.

Merlin's heart pounded. It was impossible not to feel even a flicker of attraction, but in the end he shook his head frantically. "Save it. I already know the truth. Even if you try to tempt me, it's useless. I won't take the bait!"

"What a pity. You're not the first demon to express love for me. Among so many suitors, I only agreed to you~" Asmodeus waved the small fan in his hand, looking at Merlin with a half-smile.

"Shut up! Don't even think about tricking me into your trap! You bastard who deceived my feelings!" Merlin cursed loudly and left without looking back.

"???" Asmodeus was very confused. What did he do to deceive Merlin's feelings? Wasn't it Merlin himself who was bewitched by his appearance? Ah! This uncontainable charm of mine is simply original sin~

The evening breeze blew gently.

Merlin looked utterly dazed. He felt he had already lost his face. The cold wind slapped directly against his bones, making him shiver.

This was his first love in his life. He never expected it to end so briefly.

He had thought he was about to experience a romantic story, but at the final sprint on the highway, he had crashed and fallen off a cliff!

His dream lover of decades was actually a rough guy? Who could understand such a massive shock? It was enough to inflict irreparable trauma on his views on love!

In the future, Merlin might discover that he was not the only victim. There were many more fools who would follow after, infatuated with Asmodeus, only to meet miserable ends.

Merlin considered this his dark history. He hoped no one would ever bring it up again. He would never easily fall in love with anyone again. He had even become immune to all beautiful appearances—

"Fuck! I almost got turned gay! He's a man, why dress so flamboyantly!?"

"I'll never believe in love again!"

"Hahaha—" Lilith, hiding in the distance, laughed heartlessly, clutching her stomach. "You all saw that, right? My brother has been infatuated with a male for decades! Look how delightfully dazed he is! I reckon after taking this blow, no matter how many fox spirits are around him, he'll find it hard to be moved, right?"

*Waaah* Ophelia sadly bit into her handkerchief with her teeth. She couldn't figure out where she had lost. How could a cross-dressing male demon seduce Merlin while she couldn't!?

"Poor His Majesty. His first love was a man. What a painful blow." Pudom shook his head and sighed, taking out the *Merlin Quotes* and permanently recording everything Merlin had just said.

The news that the First Demon Lord Palace had produced a third-generation ruler reached the Vatican Temple.

The Pope believed that Lucifer III had only just taken the throne, with an unstable foundation and shallow roots. It was the perfect opportunity for a focused strike, one that could further weaken the demon race's power.

Thus, the Holy Church continuously dispatched Crusade Armies toward the Swamp of Death, hoping to take advantage of the third ruler's inexperience and once again seize the Demon Lord Palace, uncovering all the secrets of the Blood Pool.

However, the Holy Church's calculations were wrong. The Temple Knights and Heroes faced the new master of the demon sword Banri Garan, the strongest demon of the new era, the truly invincible Great Demon Lord!

A nightmare lasting several years was only just beginning. The Pope failed to realize that this erroneous decision would bring unprecedented, catastrophic losses to the Holy Light Church—

The Temple Knight army surged into the territory of the First Demon Lord Palace in full force. The dragon that had originally patrolled above the Holy Light Temple also joined this war.

The Holy Light Dragon A维斯 shook his pure white wings, roaring as he swept through the demon army, becoming the most dazzling presence on the battlefield. He descended from the sky and proudly approached Merlin.

"You must be Lucifer III? Surrender! You're far too weak to even qualify as my enemy! Under my dragon's might, the weak will only be scared witless!"

"Oh?" Merlin showed a meaningful smile, stroking the hilt of Banri Garan with his left hand and suggesting—

"Actually, our Demon Lord Palace is short a watchdog. I wonder if you'd be interested?"

To Be Continued

Author's Note

Hey bro, you there? Got a monthly ticket?

This volume is wrapping up. I'm mainly filling in the plot threads about the Demon Lord Palace, the demon executives, Merlin's youth, Belphog, and Vivian. If I don't explain things here, the demon race arc's conclusion will be confusing, because Vivian's series of actions won't make sense to everyone.

It's a good time to tie up all the loose ends from before in one go and clarify the previously confusing parts.

The next volume is the final part of the demon race arc, and also the conclusion to all the demon-related plots so far. Let me give you a little spoiler—

Spouses turn against each other!

title: Chapter 1 — Crisis Approaching
content:
Chapter 1 — Crisis Approaching

Volume 35 · Chapter 1

The mysterious blood pool at the bottom of the First Demon Lord Palace; at this moment, the seal has become extremely unstable, with blood surging and churning nonstop. As a drop of Lilith's blood was injected, the blood pool seal, which should have immediately returned to calm, showed no reaction? This left Lilith and the demons puzzled, unsure what went wrong with the blood pool seal. Under normal circumstances, only a drop of Lilith's blood would stabilize the blood pool seal, but today it seems to have encountered some unexpected special situation? Lilith gazed at the turbulent blood pool, as if it might collapse from within at any moment, she furrowed her brows deeply, 'What is going on? Why isn't my blood working?' 'Strange! What exactly is wrong with the blood pool seal? It has been extremely unsettled since the Seven Kings Conference.' Ophelia accompanied Lilith by her side, looking puzzled. 'This is not normal!' Lilith gritted her teeth, realizing something was off, 'Any news from the other Demon Lord Palaces? Could it be that their blood pool seals are also unable to calm down like ours?' 'No, the other Demon Lord Palaces have been very quiet lately, and no news has come through.' Ophelia answered truthfully. Lilith lowered her head, thinking carefully for a while, 'Too abnormal; the Seven Kings Conference ended some time ago, yet we still don't know what was discussed at the meeting.' 'Indeed very abnormal; normally, after the Seven Kings Conference makes its decisions, each Demon Lord Palace receives the news within three days, but now it's unusually quiet.' Ophelia grew suspicious, at this moment it's unclear whether the Seven Kings Conference has truly ended or not; logically, a meeting couldn't possibly go on this long. 'Could it be that something happened in the Council of Elders?' Lilith couldn't be sure, wanting to hear Ophelia's opinion. 'That's unlikely; during the Seven Kings Conference, the monarchs were all in the Council of Elders, what could go wrong?' Ophelia shook her head, thinking that the demons gathered together, who would dare to stir up trouble by eating a bear's heart and leopard's gall? The church attacking the Demon Lord Palace while they're distracted is possible. 'Yeah, my brother went to attend the conference, so nothing could go wrong, but .' Lilith covered her chest with her hand, her expression complex, saying, 'My heart feels very uneasy.' 'Your unease is probably related to the blood pool seal; don't put so much pressure on yourself, let Podum come take a look later; he's well-versed and has deep knowledge of the demon race's past, he might know something.' Ophelia thought of Podum, suspecting the blood pool seal is just a minor issue. Lilith glanced again at the surging blood pool, nodded, 'That's all we can do for now.' 'Lilith Your Highness! I have urgent matters!' Blake Yan rushed over anxiously, his face worried, his speech starting to stutter. 'Speak slowly, don't panic, what kind of conduct is this?!' Lilith reprimanded dissatisfied. 'Blake Man took a deep breath, suppressing his inner anxiety, 'An official from the Fourth Demon Lord Palace insists on seeing you immediately.' 'What? Why would a demon from the Fourth Demon Lord Palace come to our territory?' Lilith's face showed a hint of displeasure. 'She says she just escaped from the Council of Elders, the turmoil that occurred at the Seven Kings Conference must be told to you, and there's also something about His Majesty Merlin.' Blake Man reported solemnly, and even under further questioning the other party refused to speak. 'My brother's matter?' Lilith lowered her head, thinking, then asked, 'What is her name?' '.' Blake Man recalled, then answered, 'Helena!' In the main hall, Lilith sat on the throne and saw the suddenly arriving Helena. She looked anxious, obviously the situation is now extremely dangerous, every minute matters for the fate of the demon race. After leaving the Council of Elders, Helena completely lost contact with Merlin, the Demon Sealing Vessel is very likely already taken away. If the distance is too great, trying to communicate through the master-servant contract via mental link is not an easy thing. Upon seeing Lilith, Helena briefly explained the situation to her, trying to let her quickly understand what happened at the Seven Kings Conference. After hearing Helena's account, Lilith finally learned that the Seven Kings Conference had descended into chaos, Belphegor's soul had already escaped the blood pool seal, manipulating the first demons behind the scenes to stir up trouble— No wonder my blood has no effect on the seal anymore, I can't continue to maintain the stability of the blood pool. It's very likely that Belphegor is tampering with some Demon Lord Palace, striving to free his own body as well! When Belphegor's soul and body remerge, he will truly gain freedom, completely breaking free from the seal's restrictions. However, all of this seems already too late to stop; all the monarchs' souls have been imprisoned, the situation has completely turned in Belphegor's favor. Moreover, the blood pool seal consists of seven points; Belphegor only needs to destroy one point to liberate himself, which is not difficult! Lilith 'leapt' up from the throne, tense, demanding, 'You said my brother is locked inside the Demon Sealing Vessel?!' 'Yes, the other monarchs are also locked inside, along with a host of elders.' Helena explained. 'What are we to do? My brother and the other monarchs are locked inside the Demon Sealing Vessel; does that mean the entire demon race is doomed?' Lilith's face turned pale, feeling the apocalypse of the demon race had arrived, her mind plunged into chaos. 'The instability of the blood pool seal is a sign that Belphegor is about to gain freedom; wanting to stop Belphegor from returning to his body, time has already run out.' Helena paused, then emphasized seriously, 'Those locked in the vessel cannot provide any help; we can only rely on ourselves, make preparations in advance.' 'Belphegor what - hammer smash his head, so that His Majesty Merlin can gain freedom?' Blake Man shouted angrily. 'You're dreaming, Blake Man; Belphegor is the ancestor of demons, the creator of the demon race, a powerful entity in the Ancient Gods faction, a single glance could make you vanish from this world.' Xiu stood in the shadows, leaning against a stone pillar. 'What then? His Majesty Merlin has already met misfortune; are we to just wait for death?' Blake Man responded dissatisfied. 'Yeah, we must find a way to save His Majesty Merlin; the demon race has reached the brink of destruction, only His Majesty can possibly defeat Belphegor, for Belphegor is the one who set the original seal, while His Majesty is the new master of the demon sword Banri Garan; there might be some connection here.' Ophelia recalled past events, the deceased Vivian had once said Merlin was different. 'I don't deny His Majesty's strength, but I think defeating Belphegor is an unknown.' Tru poured a bucket of cold water over everyone. 'Tru, what do you mean? Do you not acknowledge His Majesty's strength?' Blake Man questioned with a hint of anger in his eyes. 'I don't mean that; His Majesty's strength is evident to all, but this time the enemy .' Tru paused, glanced, then lifted his hideously ugly face— 'It is the Ancient God, the creator of the demon race.' 'The former monarchs could only resign themselves to being enslaved by it; its power will far surpass our imagination.' Brothers; have extra chapters, cough 1 monthly ticket

title: Chapter 2 — Entrustment (Monthly Ticket Extra)
content:
Chapter 2 — Entrustment (Monthly Ticket Extra)

Volume 35 · Chapter 2

Even if we rescue His Majesty Merlin, can he really defeat Behemoth? With our level we cannot possibly predict. Duran paused, then continued, “If you think about it carefully, it seems only the Great Prophet can suppress Behemoth. If His Majesty Merlin could defeat it, then his potential must be infinitely close to that of the Great Prophet; His Majesty Merlin possesses power not inferior to the Great Prophet—is that possible?” Upon saying this, all the demons present fell silent; the significance of the prophet is extraordinary, comparing Merlin to that great figure does seem a bit far‑fetched—. “Duran, do you mean we shouldn’t rescue His Majesty Merlin?” Blackman demanded, his face stern. “No, what I mean is that rescuing His Majesty Merlin may not be the right choice; we might not be able to pull the demon race back from the brink of crisis.” Duran said calmly, not that he doesn’t want to save Merlin, but he fears we cannot change the outcome. “Duran’s idea is not wrong; it is rational. Now the survival of the demon race is the main issue.” Xiu nodded, adding that from a big‑picture perspective there’s no problem, but the key issue is the object to which Merlin and his ilk have sworn undying loyalty. “What does the demon race have to do with me? I just want my brother!” Lilith shouted angrily. “I share Lilith’s opinion.” Ophelia stepped forward, her expression solemn, and said, “Moreover, I believe only His Majesty can defeat Behemoth; if even His Majesty cannot do it, then other monarchs have even less hope.” “I agree!” Podum raised his hand and said solemnly, “His Majesty Merlin is the only demon who has walked out of the Despair Canyon alive and even earned the acknowledgment of the Prophet’s relic; perhaps His Majesty is the Prophet’s successor, which is why Behemoth fears him greatly.” “That’s merely speculation,” Duran emphasized. “No, I once heard Her Majesty Vivian say that Merlin is the demon foretold in the Prophet’s prophecy, capable of preventing the demon race’s doom.” Ophelia couldn’t recall the exact details of that time, but the general idea remains. “Is that prophecy really true?” Xiu asked, raising his eyebrows in surprise. “Ophelia, do you know the exact content of the Prophet’s prophecy? Legend says the Prophet left three prophecies, but few demons seem to know them.” Podum suddenly became interested; he combed through the ancient texts of the Du tribe, but never found the specific content of the Prophet’s prophecy. “I don’t know the specifics either; I only happened to hear Her Majesty Vivian mention it once.” Ophelia explained. “This prophecy should be true; at the Seven Kings Council, Belial, manipulated by Behemoth, kept targeting His Majesty Merlin, hoping he would vanish on the spot—there can only be one reason for that.” Helena lifted her head and said seriously, “Behemoth fears His Majesty Merlin.” The demons in the hall fell silent again, so quiet that you could hear a pin drop; they vaguely sensed the crux of the matter. If we could successfully free the monarchs sealed in the vessel, the situation could instantly turn around and the demon race would overcome the immediate crisis. However, to free the monarchs we would have to clash head‑on with Behemoth, which is clearly not a wise idea—. “After Behemoth locked the monarchs in the vessel, he wouldn’t openly carry it around; he must have hidden it, so we must find the Demon‑Sealing Vessel.” Xiu sighed helplessly and said, “But now the demon race is in chaos, and my intelligence network has ceased to function.” “Give it up, Xiu; even if we found the Demon‑Sealing Vessel, it would be useless.” Podum shook his head and explained, “After the Demon‑Sealing Vessel is used, it enters a long sealed period and can only be used once; whether from inside or outside, it cannot be opened again. Some ancient texts say this item was specially crafted by Behemoth to deal with disobedient servants, so even if we obtained the Demon‑Sealing Vessel we couldn’t free the monarchs.” “Can’t we just destroy it?” Blackman asked, puzzled. “Impossible; the Demon‑Sealing Vessel is forged from the purest dark power, extremely sturdy. Even a god‑level being of unimaginable strength would find it hard to destroy this artifact.” Podum gave an embarrassed laugh. “It’s not that there’s no chance at all; His Majesty Merlin told me some things—the Demon‑Sealing Vessel is not indestructible.” Helena paused, recalling the human woman who had long accompanied Merlin— “We must hurry to Rexum.” After Behemoth’s revival, all the Demon Lord Palaces will be in name only; the souls of countless demons wander inside the Demon‑Sealing Vessel. They have no idea what’s happening outside, nor any sense of time, so they don’t know how long they’ve been imprisoned. The headless Samael sits motionless on the ground, dazedly staring off, appearing far calmer than the other demon lords. “How long have we been locked up here? Has it already been over a hundred years?” Beelzebub drifted about, listless. “Are you living in a dream? It’s just—only a few months have passed,” Leviathan retorted sharply from beside him. “Good heavens! A life without Miranda’s company feels like an eternity; I’d rather be dead!” Beelzebub tore at his hair in anguish, lamenting, “Is it still possible for me to beg Behemoth for mercy?” “Hey! Show some spine! We’re all in the same boat—if you grovel to Behemoth and become a traitor, Miranda will look down on you too!” Leviathan was startled and quickly steadied Beelzebub’s emotions. Asmodeus saw Beelzebub on the verge of madness, shook his head helplessly, and approached Merlin, asking, “How’s it going? Can you still contact Helena?” Merlin replied, “I can’t; I’ve tried many times.” He sighed softly, “I’ve already told her everything; perhaps she is now figuring out how to rescue us.” “Don’t worry,” Asmodeus continued after a pause, shifting his tone, “among my many subordinates, Helena is the most capable and efficient.” “But are you really placing your hope in humans?” Merlin countered, “Do you have any other option?” Asmodeus worried, “Is that woman named Alice trustworthy? Like other demons, I find it hard to believe in humans.” Merlin fell silent for a moment, then nodded, “She is a very reliable person; aside from her, I can’t think of anyone else capable of destroying the Demon‑Sealing Vessel.” Asmodeus pressed, “Is her weapon really that miraculous?” Merlin answered, “Of course; my tempered flesh would even be scorched by contact. Recalling the changes in the Light Chant, after the seal was broken that slender sword became ever sharper, possessing ample deterrence against dark beings.” Asmodeus’s eyes flickered, his doubts growing: “A weapon sealed layer upon layer, imbued with holy light’s aura?” He mused, “It doesn’t look like anything of this world; it could well have come from the lofty heavens.” “Such a precious treasure, yet it lies in human hands—and moreover, it belongs to the former Hero.” Merlin, do you really think such a coincidence could happen?

title: Chapter 3 — Ancient Threat
content:
Chapter 3 — Ancient Threat

Volume 35 · Chapter 3

Merlin froze abruptly, recalling everything about Alice—there was indeed some connection to that Heavenly Sovereign, especially evident in the oil painting left by Cain.

But Merlin was unwilling to believe it; he preferred to think Cain had confused the Goddess's appearance with Alice's by mistake.

"What are you trying to say?"

"After the Holy War ended, the gates of Heaven closed, and the Goddess could hardly interfere directly in the mortal realm. But I believe she won't give up—she could cultivate a follower in the mortal world, and thus create her own puppet." Asmodeus made a bold conjecture, remembering the landlady in Rextham, and felt things were not simple.

Merlin was silent for a long time, then said calmly, "You're overthinking it. She's just a human. Her connection to the Church was just a misunderstanding. She left the Church long ago."

"Asmodeus saw through Merlin's thoughts and questioned, 'You've already realized she's extraordinary, you're just unwilling to admit it, aren't you?'"

"Asmodeus, stop daydreaming. The Heavenly Sovereign isn't an idiot—why would He cultivate such a weak puppet? Besides luck, she has no outstanding abilities. As for the divine artifact in her hand? It actually belongs to her teacher. If I hadn't pointed it out, she'd never realize how precious it is." Merlin paused, thinking: if Alice had a direct connection to the Goddess of Light, how could she have lived so miserably? Driven out by the Church, she should have been worshipped by a bunch of holy men instead.

"Oh~" Asmodeus's expression turned playful, deliberately drawing the other Demon Lords' attention. "I see. You like that human woman, so you're unwilling to think the worst."

The nearby Sovereigns all looked over, interested in Merlin's answer, wanting to see where his true stance lay.

Although this matter was exploited by Behemoth, it was true that Merlin and the human woman had produced offspring together.

Merlin stared into Asmodeus's eyes for a long time, then nodded. "I won't deny it."

"Why can't you let go of a human woman? So many beautiful female demons couldn't hold you back—surely I'm not an option?" Asmodeus volunteered.

"Save it." Merlin replied with a dark face, thinking it was completely different.

"How ruthless. I was your dream sweetheart once—you even wrote me love poems I still remember to this day." Asmodeus wore a smug, half-smiling expression.

"Don't, don't, don't mention it. We can still be friends." Merlin panicked; every time his dark history was brought up, his spirit became extremely tense.

"Lucifer, you should know this in your heart—being with a human is forbidden. I warned you before, yet you still made a mistake." Beelzebub crossed his arms and said coldly, "Your child is the most unfortunate. Having committed no sin, they face danger. Under normal circumstances, such human-demon hybrids are not allowed to exist and would be hunted endlessly."

Merlin's temple veins throbbed. He threatened coldly, "Whoever dares to harm my child—I guarantee they won't see tomorrow's sun. Even you lot, I won't show mercy."

The Demon Lords fell silent. Having consecutively defeated Samael and Belial, Merlin's formidable power was proven—not only was he very young, but his strength even faintly surpassed that of the First-Generation Sovereigns.

Now the other Demon Lord Palaces had no courage to look down on Merlin. Regarding his retaliatory words, they didn't doubt for a second that he had the guts to do it.

Asmodeus's gaze shifted evasively. Previously, to help Merlin eliminate threats, he had indeed planned to kill Chris—but then discovered another secret.

That landlady wasn't an ordinary human, but a Holy Spirit that had survived in the mortal realm for a long time!

Originally, Asmodeus wanted to tell Merlin this and discuss it to uncover the landlady's origins.

But seeing Merlin's utterly resolute attitude, he immediately abandoned that thought.

Asmodeus decided to bury this secret forever, preventing Merlin from noticing he had once tried to kill Chris.

"Don't misunderstand, Lucifer." Leviathan paused, explaining kindly. "The rule that demons cannot be with humans exists for the continued propagation of our race. Especially for us descendants of the First-Generation Demon Lords, it's stricter. This is mainly to preserve our bloodline and maintain the stability of the Blood Pool Seal. Hybrid demons probably lack such ability."

"Rules aren't set in stone. As long as it doesn't affect the stability of our race, adjustments aren't impossible." Samael suddenly spoke. With Merlin's current strength, his fists were indeed powerful enough to qualify for changing demon customs to some extent. Even if he made mistakes, he could be forgiven. However, maintaining racial stability was an unshakable bottom line—

"The hybrid child can stay, but she won't receive fair treatment among demons. As for that human woman? She can never be accepted."

"In the Demon Era, unions between demons and humans happened frequently. The appearance of hybrid demons would pollute our bloodline and disrupt demon stability.

"To solve this, demons back then came up with a good method: the moment a human woman became pregnant was her death sentence—she would be killed directly.

"This way, no filthy half-breed would ever be born, and demons wouldn't have to suppress their desires."

"You should learn from your ancestors' methods, Lucifer."

"Sorry, I can't accept such a cruel practice." Merlin shook his head, disagreeing with the method of transferring pain onto others for amusement—

Indeed, I'm different from this bunch.

No matter how long I live among demons, I can never become truly evil.

The Demon City where the Seventh Demon Lord Palace stood.

The one-eyed Orobas was quietly waving his paintbrush on a canvas in a room within the Demon Lord Palace castle, gradually painting a lifelike landscape.

Looking closely, the painting depicted the view outside the window—an altar opposite the Demon Lord Palace, where the Blood Pool Seal was located.

Orobas pulled his gaze from the demon-sealing vase beside him. His face was expressionless, like a tool, with no emotion leaking from the depths of his eyes.

It suddenly dipped its paintbrush into crimson dye. Its arm bent like a spiritual serpent, swinging fiercely toward the canvas—but stopped at the last moment?

Orobas closed his eyes, questioning deeply in his heart what he was about to do. The voice of "Father" echoed incessantly in his mind—

"Orobas, you don't need to think. Just do as I say. You are my son, and my most handy tool. After the Seven Kings' Conference, you will destroy the Blood Pool Seal, then dedicate everything to great Behemoth, serving it unto death."

"I understand."

Orobas opened his eyes. There was no more hesitation or doubt in his heart. Firmly, he used his paintbrush to "scratch" a crimson streak across the canvas, like a scarlet lightning bolt striking the altar!

As Orobas lowered his paintbrush, wind and clouds surged outside instantly. A red lightning bolt descended from the depths of the dark clouds, directly striking the altar hiding the Blood Pool Seal!

Rumble—

Thunder exploded. The Blood Pool deep within the altar was destroyed, and Behemoth was completely freed.

It slowly opened its eyes, making the world tremble under the intimidation of the ancient demon god.

title: Chapter 4 — Demon Blood Erosion
content:
Chapter 4 — Demon Blood Erosion

Volume 35 · Chapter 4

The super seal formed by the seven demon palaces was instantly shattered, and the ancient demon god that had lain dormant for ages awoke at once!

Because the seven blood pools are interconnected, the destruction of the blood pool in the demon city caused the blood pools in the other demon palaces to lose their effect as well.

Behemoth's awakening triggered a violent quake; the massive demon city rumbled, and countless buildings collapsed.

The weak demons had no inkling of the impending disaster; they fled in terror, fearing they would be caught up.

Many demons were either buried under rubble or fell into the fissures that split the ground, their fate unknown.

The demon city, which had never suffered damage since the age of the gods, was heavily devastated after Behemoth's awakening; over half of the ancient city was destroyed.

Suddenly! A brilliant red ray shot up from the blood pool deep within the altar, piercing straight into the high heavens like a scarlet sword cleaving the long night.

The fleeing demons gazed upon this horrifying sight, as if heaven and earth had been dyed a layer of blood‑red, eerie yet alluring.

Black clouds appeared out of nowhere, continually swirling into a vortex; in the blink of an eye, rolling black clouds spread over the demon city’s sky, blocking out the sunlight.

The thick black clouds parted in several places, faintly revealing human‑shaped visages; their burning eyes snapped open, slightly smiling, as if mocking the escaping demons.

A jagged giant mouth suddenly opened, spewing scorching flame breath that sucked every living demon in the demon city into it.

Looking up, one could see the demons frantically struggling inside Behemoth’s mouth, flames incessantly scorching their bodies and souls, unable to escape death.

Sharp, painful screams echoed over the demon city; the despair the demons faced is unimaginable—just hearing their cries sends a chill down the spine.

Behemoth had just awakened and was ravenously hungry; it cared not what it ate, even the creatures it had itself created received no mercy.

As the saying goes, ‘Tigers do not eat their cubs,’ but Behemoth seems to lack that notion; it only knows that demons taste bad, far inferior to humans.

Behemoth appears incorporeal, merely a mass of black cloud filled with flames capable of burning souls; firelight spews from its features.

"Hahaha, I’m free at last! I’ve finally escaped the control of that bastard prophet. In a world without other ancient gods, this is practically the paradise I’ve dreamed of!"

"Eurolab士 arrived at the altar, folded back his membrane wings, slowly descended from the sky, and knelt on one knee, ‘Great Behemoth, I am willing to obey my father’s will and die in loyalty to you.’"

"Behemoth gradually adapted to the new world; its eyes within the cloud noticed Eurolab士, and the corners of its mouth twitched upward. ‘Very well, I accept your loyalty, Eurolab士. You are the perfect tool—I favor you.’"

"Eurolab士 hesitated, unsure whether what he was doing was right, but still said in a low voice, ‘I am merely carrying out my father’s task, not voluntarily serving you.’"

"It’s fine; as long as you know you’re an emotionless tool, that’s enough. Belial is dead; now you just need to obey my orders, and your father will surely be proud of you." Behemoth kept tempting Eurolab士, already delighted at the prospect of training him into the handiest tool—indeed the right thing to do!

"I understand." Eurolab士’s eyes turned hollow, a hint of doubt deep inside; Behemoth’s tone and voice reminded him exactly of his father, which was too strange.

"Behemoth looked over the ruined demon city and slowly said, ‘My survival requires more fertile land, preferably the world’s center; this place is too barren, only usable as a temporary outpost.’"

"The world’s center is the Vatican, headquarters of the Holy Church, with fertile land suited for you." Eurolab士 suggested.

"That’s an excellent idea: turn the holy city where countless believers hold sacred into demon territory, pollute the purity they long for, and spiritually crush their faith—sounds fun~" Behemoth felt moved, thinking, ‘But before that, I need to use my own blood to create loyal demon servants; most demons have already slipped from my control, so I can’t use them.’"

"Time may be short; your awakening has caused great turmoil; remnants of demons from the other demon palaces will unite to resist you, and humans have already noticed your existence—they won’t sit idle." Eurolab士 had already glimpsed some future; no race will tolerate an ancient god’s awakening, and Behemoth has become the world’s public enemy of this era.

"Hehehe, no matter how many resisters come, they’re useless; they’ll just become food to fill my belly; all obstacles are gone; no resister can threaten me." Behemoth chuckled nonstop, Merlin’s soul already sealed in a jar; in the mortal world there is no opponent; he gazed at the blood pool deep in the altar, ‘Moreover, I don’t even need to act—’

The destroyed altar’s deepest part, the blood pool surged wildly, turning from bright red to pitch black; Behemoth’s blood contaminated it, like a huge ink pool.

Several soulless demon lords have become mere puppets, completely soaked in Behemoth’s demon‑god blood, continually eroded.

Behemoth’s blood seems to possess infinite magic, frenziedly flowing into the demon lords’ bodies, remodeling and strengthening their power; after completion they will become loyal puppets.

Although the demon lords awaken again as soulless shells, their power will surge enormously, far stronger than before.

What’s puzzling is that the demon‑god blood flowing into Merlin’s body is the most—by no exaggeration, more than the total amount swallowed by the other demon lords combined, even seeming insufficient!

This odd phenomenon baffles Behemoth, which emits doubtful sounds; after a brief thought, it finds the reason, eyes light up with excitement, thinking—

"It turns out his demon bloodline is inherently thin, so he needs more of my blood to remold, and he accepts my blood more easily than other demons!"

"Such a heavenly advantage lets him gain more of the power I bestow; just how strong he’ll become is hard to guess for now."

"But it’s so thrilling! My arch‑enemy will be completely under my control; the sole enemy that could threaten me has become my puppet!"

"What could be more fun than this?"

Behemoth’s blazing eyes revealed a thick smile; anticipation for Merlin in the blood pool grew; it opened its hideous maw, the fire of desire burning fiercely inside.

"Merlin Lucifer, you are worthy to inherit all of me, becoming my second body."

"We"

"will merge into the perfect being!"

Everyone knows that in the setting demons have relatively grotesque, terrifying appearances—that is their true form.

Now Merlin also has that, but words can never match the vividness of a picture.

Thus I need to commission an artist; hiring an artist costs a lot of money~

To be able to draw Merlin’s demonic appearance, you all understand, right?

"Crazy hint!"

1 ticket

title: Chapter 5 — Demon Gathering Place
content:
Chapter 5 — Demon Gathering Place

Volume 35 · Chapter 5

The revival of Behemoth caused a tremendous upheaval across the world!

The blood pools of the Demon Lord Palaces scattered across the world's corners all collapsed!

Crimson light spewed from the seven Demon Lord Palaces, shooting straight into the heavens, dyeing the sky an eerie blood-red.

Looking down from beyond the heavens, one could see seven red points lighting up the world map like shining stars, connected together forming a colossal sealing array!

At that moment, deafening thunder rumbled continuously from the sky, the world's continents violently trembled, the effect vast enough that even the distant Southern United Kingdom could feel faint tremors.

As the eerie red light faded, Behemoth escaped the seal of the Seventh Demon Lord Palace and successfully gained freedom.

Behemoth's revival brought about all kinds of anomalies; the whole world could perceive it, and the rulers of each kingdom also faintly sensed the arrival of disaster.

This was no longer merely a crisis for the demon race; once Behemoth took control of the demons, it would inevitably turn its guns toward prosperous humanity.

At the Vatican's temple, the very elderly Pope Ji'ougen stood outside, gazing at that streak of scarlet on the distant horizon, and smelled the danger.

‘What should come has come.’ Beside him, the Holy Temple Knight Commander Blakefort stood guard silently, 'Your Holiness, what is happening? I faintly feel a very evil power watching us.'

'It is the apocalypse, humanity's apocalypse has arrived; no one can escape this calamity, perhaps we should write our wills in advance.' Pope Ji'ougen's face darkened, as if he already knew what had happened.

'That serious?' Blakefort gazed at the blood-red horizon, his heart tightening.

'Something major has happened among the demons; they ultimately failed to guard the seal, letting the terrifying monster inside escape.' Pope Ji'ougen let out a sigh.

'A monster? Your Majesty, what are you referring to?' Blakefort was completely bewildered.

'Behemoth, the ancient demon god who lived in the Land of Fire during the Age of Gods, possessing incomparably mighty power, is the creator of the demons.' Pope Ji'ougen paused, recalling ancient memories: 'A hundred years ago I, together with the Gun Hero O'Brien, successfully seized the First Demon Lord Palace, and in the deepest underground we discovered a blood-soaked pool, the tip of the ancient seal's iceberg; in that pool we found a slumbering monster. Initially I and O'Brien did not know what it was, but later, upon returning to the temple and consulting extensive records on demon history, we realized that monster was the terrifying ancient demon god.'

'An ancient demon god.' Blakefort broke out in a cold sweat on his forehead; such powerful ancient gods from the Age of Gods are nearly invincible now—who could defeat them? In a sense, the demon prophets who brought twilight to the Age of Gods are great era founders; otherwise, who knows how long the world would have lasted under the rule of those ancient gods.

'It must be that, starting from the demons' abnormal external expansion earlier, their insides have already become a complete mess, even the ancient demon god has awakened—one can imagine how dire the situation is.' Pope Ji'ougen frowned, perplexed by the current situation.

'This is merely the demons' apocalypse; what does it have to do with us?' Blakefort asked, puzzled.

'Foolish, if the demons fall, can we really escape unscathed? That ancient demon god will not spare humanity; it will surely seek to enslave all races.' Pope Ji'ougen lowered his head and said solemnly, 'The demons are indeed our enemies, but now the heavens have almost completely severed ties with us; we must rely on ourselves to survive. Therefore, rather than exterminating the demons, it is better to use them, shaping them into humanity's common enemy, so we can more easily employ religious power to unite the divided human forces.'

'Blakefort wanted to speak but held back; the Pope's words clearly violate doctrine, not putting the extermination of demons first but instead obsessing over controlling all human kingdoms—no wonder the long-standing crusade against demons has never achieved total annihilation, resembling a political spectacle; obviously concentrating all forces on a single Demon Lord Palace would be more effective, yet they always disperse their strength.'

'I know what you're thinking, Fort; you are someone I trust, so I can speak frankly.' Pope Ji'ougen glanced at the knight beside him and said meaningfully, 'Faith in the Goddess Mary is just a worthless pile of dogshit, merely a beautiful story fabricated for the ignorant to immerse themselves in; the goddess has abandoned us, leaving us to fend for ourselves in the mortal world. I do not wish to utterly exterminate the demons precisely to maintain a certain balance, allowing more believers to survive; when you have the chance to sit in my position, you will do the same.'

Blakefort lowered his head, giving no reply; as the Holy Temple Knight who often accompanies the Pope, he indeed knows more secrets and clearly understands that those fervent believers are merely brainwashed tools.

No matter how devout one's faith in the Goddess Mary, they receive no favor, only being continually exploited by clear-minded followers, squeezing out the last bit of their worth.

Helping the goddess exterminate demons brings no benefit; if humanity loses its recognized enemy, does the church still have a reason to exist? After countless years of painstaking effort, the Holy Light Church has become the world's largest organization; should it disappear, the greatest loss of interest would be this group residing in the temple—the core leadership.

Can faith be eaten as food? Obviously not.

Blakefort understands this logic, yet each time he sees the devout eyes of those believers, he feels that this group lost in dreams is truly pitiable.

'I too was once a devout believer; after hearing the previous pope's dying words, I changed my mind.' Pope Ji'ougen turned to look at the knight's eyes and said softly, 'Bares is a genius, I favor him greatly, but only in strength; you are different—your mature steadiness makes you more suited to inherit my position, do you understand? My child.'

'Eh!' Blakefort stared wide-eyed, hearing the Pope's implication that he himself is the chosen successor to the papacy!

'If we can successfully get through this crisis, I hope you can shoulder greater responsibility.' Pope Ji'ougen turned away, gazing at the blood-red sky, and said slowly—

'As for the present? We need to immediately prepare for war and select a hero to carry out the 234th crusade against the demons.'

Rexham, the sun slowly set.

After a journey of over half a month, Alice carried Chris in the carriage back here, wondering whether Merlin had already returned.

Little Chris, upon returning to Rexham, felt as if she had come home, happily hop

title: Chapter 6 — In a Mess
content:
Chapter 6 — In a Mess

Volume 35 · Chapter 6

The room was messed up by the demons; the home that was originally neat and clean when they left has now become a garbage dump.

The demons of the First Demon Lord Palace came here a few days early, so as not to cause trouble in the human lands, they eat and live here entirely.

Alice, who had just returned home, once thought she might have gone to the wrong place; only after confirming several times did she dare to shout loudly.

Alice's veins on her forehead throbbed wildly as she held her cute daughter; seeing the messy home, a nameless fire instantly rose in her heart, feeling the demons were acting too recklessly!

"This is my home! I hope you can understand this point? Making it like a trash heap, doesn't your conscience hurt?"

Helena sipped her red tea in small mouthfuls, secretly letting out a breath, thinking Alice had finally returned, otherwise things would be more troublesome. "Hey! Why aren't you speaking? Don't you guys dare to explain?"

Alice had a terrible headache; normally one or two demons visiting would be fine, but this time a large group came! No matter how you say it, she is the mistress of this place, yet they just moved in casually, as if they didn't even regard her! Moreover, these demons didn't properly conceal their traces, causing the people of Rexrem to be panic-stricken, everywhere searching for demons' silhouettes.

"Ugh!" Blake man hastily picked up the shattered plate from the floor and hid it behind his back, showing an apologetic smile, "Miss Alice, you're back? . them that Pudom's eyes darted about, the walls were smeared with a pile of meaningless graffiti; he quickly put down his paintbrush, forcing himself to ask, . how how? This little chicken pecking rice picture"

Duru stood gloomily in the corner, spitting out a chair leg from his mouth, coldly saying, "Are you the human woman living with His Majesty Merlin? Sorry, we're too hungry and dare not go out; this town is full of people. A few days ago Blake man went out to find some wine to drink and almost got caught by the town guards."

"That was an accident!" Blake man protested indignantly.

Xiu looked at the mess all over the floor, lightly coughing and saying, "Cough! Miss Alice, please don't mind; we didn't intentionally make it like this." "Yahahaha! ! !"

Suddenly, a wanton, sharp laugh came from the bathroom, making one's scalp tingle. Ophelia rushed out of the bathroom, holding a foul-smelling old sock, her face glowing with excitement. "Look what I found! This is His Majesty's sock!" "Why are you so sure?" Duru questioned gloomily. "I'm too familiar with His Majesty's scent! Hmm, it's this smell, definitely not wrong!" Ophelia sniffed the sock, saw Alice returning in the corner of her eye, quickly hid the sock, "What the hell? This human woman who seduced His Majesty is back? A fox spirit who only plays tricks! Don't think you can forever bind His Majesty's heart, tsk!" Helena's cup trembled, black lines like a waterfall fell on her forehead; she didn't dare speak casually, thinking the demons of the First Demon Lord Palace were all weirdos; compared to them, her master's cross-dressing habit is nothing.

"You..." Alice's face turned ashen, trembling with anger, a chilling aura slowly emanating, "Pay up! All broken things must be compensated! If you don't pay, none of you can leave!"

"Oh? How nice, this human is really enthusiastic; if we refuse compensation, wouldn't we be able to stay here forever?" Duru spotted the key point, even scoundrels would call it expert! "Your idea isn't bad; since the First Demon Lord Palace has had an incident and we can't go back, using this as the new Demon Lord Palace seems quite good," Xiu said, stroking his goat beard, nodding repeatedly.

Alice underestimated the demons' thick skin; her expression grew increasingly stern as she shouted harshly, "Get out! Don't let me see you! Disappear from my sight quickly!"

Lilith slammed the table, rose up, kept her boots on and stepped onto the sofa, hands on hips, saying arrogantly, "What right do you have? ! This is my brother's house! We can come whenever we want!"

"Tsk! This is my home." Alice emphasized, "Of course, Merlin has the right to stay here, but you do not."

"Ridiculous! Where my brother can live, we can live too! Besides, this place has long been a . branch of the First Demon Lord Palace!" Lilith decided without courtesy to requisition this place.

"Huh? A branch? Who said that? Is that just your own opinion?" Alice forced a smile, thinking Merlin still hasn't come out to manage his sister; she's become arrogant to the point of heaven.

"What do you say? This is our secret stronghold in the human lands!" Lilith said with her nose in the air, mocking, "Just a mere human; don't think that because you successfully seduced my brother, I'll fear you!"

"My patience has its limits." Alice said, seething cold; that expensive sofa, bought specially so Merlin could sleep comfortably, is now being wildly trampled by Lilith's boots, making her feel a pang of pain.

"Shout! Want to hit me?" Lilith rolled up her sleeves, preparing to rally the other demons to gang up and thoroughly suppress this human woman's spirit.

Helena's cup trembled even more violently, red tea spilling onto the carpet; she thought we came to ask Alice for help, not to fight! Have these demons already forgotten important matters?!

"Auntie! Auntie!" Chris spotted Lilith, happily the little tuft on her head wiggling, she broke free from her mother's embrace, toddling on her short carrot-like legs toward the auntie she hadn't seen in a long time.

Lilith saw the enthusiastic little one running over, immediately switched her expression, jumped off the sofa, lovingly bent down and opened her arms, "Come, to auntie here, let auntie give you a good hug."

Little Chris's short legs had just taken two steps when Alice snatched her back, "Huh?" "Hey! Stupid human! What are you doing? Chris hasn't seen me in ages, I can't hug her? ! She's a member of our Lucifer family!" Lilith flew into a rage, thinking Alice was a vicious woman using the child to manipulate her.

Alice seemed to have noticed something, thus she held Chris in front of herself as a shield; Lilith changed her expression again. "Cutie, have you missed auntie? Chirp chirp chirp~"

After Alice put her precious daughter down, Lilith immediately returned to normal, her expression ferocious as she scolded, "Vile human woman! If I get the chance, I'll make you wish you were dead!"

After repeating this four or five times, Lilith's expression kept switching, the muscles on her face beginning to feel numb, realizing she was being toyed with by Alice. "Enough! Is it ever going to end! Don't treat the child as a toy! You're a trashy mother!"

Alice's face showed a meaningful smile; realizing these demons were only rejecting her, not Chris, she felt somewhat relieved.

"Excuse me, could you two calm down a bit?" Helena, unable to bear it any longer, set down her tea cup, rose and gave a polite slight bow—

"Princess Lilith, we have an urgent matter; regardless of your conflict with Miss Alice, we now need to exercise restraint."

"Miss Alice, I've lived in Rexrem for a long time; you should know me well."

"Now the demon race faces difficulties; we are at our wit's end and desperately need your help."

title: Chapter 7 — Power of Lies (Monthly Ticket Bonus)
content:
Chapter 7 — Power of Lies (Monthly Ticket Bonus)

Volume 35 · Chapter 7

Young Chris was temporarily sent away, playing around with the other demons of the Demon Lord's Palace.
Helen pulled Lilith and Alice aside, secretly discussing important matters.
Little Chris sat quietly on the floor, her big eyes darting as she surveyed the surrounding demons, noticing many unfamiliar faces this time.
Although the little one had already seen quite a few demons, she still thought their appearances were bizarre and grotesque; aside from all having horns, they shared no other common features.
"Oh!!! " Blake Man, seeing Chris for the first time, got excited, lay on the ground, leaned in to observe the little master— "This is the little master!!"
"That's right, she is His Majesty's child, named Chris." Pudom introduced from beside, already quite familiar with Chris.
"Chris? " Blake Man nodded, suddenly feeling that even young Merlin had no appeal anymore. "He's just like a cute porcelain doll; he will definitely be a great beauty in the future!"
"Heehee~" Chris chubby little hands rose, the cowlick on her head swaying left and right, she was very happy to receive the praise.
Blake Man felt as if struck by an arrow, unable to restrain a lecherous grin, saliva almost dripping, he chuckled, "Hehe, hehehehehe~".
"Blake Man! Put away that disgusting grin! You'll scare her!" Ophelia kicked Blake Man flying, then picked Chris up from the ground, "Wow! She's really cute, looking at her eyes, she's exactly like His Majesty when he was little, just missing a bit of that nasty feeling~".
"Princess Chris is still a child; how could she have that nasty feeling?" Pudom explained helplessly.
Ophelia leaned in to sniff, her eyes instantly lighting up, "Good grief! No mistake, this is His Majesty's child; even the smell is somewhat similar!".
"Do we even need to smell? Just by the princess's big eyes, we can identify her." Pudom said calmly.
"Love it, love it; if we could bring her back to the demon realm and hold her while sleeping each night, wouldn't we be able to dream of His Majesty Merlin every day?" Ophelia's eyes burned with fervor, her heart itching to act.
"Ophelia, calm down; we can't decide on this matter." Pudom broke into a cold sweat, afraid that this crazy woman would do something shocking.
"Ophelia, Chris remembered the name of the demon big sister before her, waving her hands, "Ophelia sister! You're so pretty! Among the demons I've seen, you're the prettiest!".
"Ah!" Ophelia felt as if struck by an arrow, blush rising on her cheeks, she said embarrassedly, "Your sweet talk is just like His Majesty when he was little, sister, sister calling nonstop, really, why do we have to live in this place? Wouldn't it be better to return to the Demon Lord's Palace?".
"We need to see what His Majesty decides; you must not act rashly." Pudom said nervously.
"Ophelia sister~" Chris's cowlick swayed as she couldn't help asking, "Where's Dad? Sister, didn't you see Dad?".
This question instantly left several demons stunned; they knew Merlin's current situation but didn't know how to answer.
Pudom secretly shook his head at Ophelia, indicating she shouldn't speak randomly about this; at the very least, young Chris shouldn't be told.
Ophelia hesitated a moment, forced a smile onto her face, trying to keep her tone steady, "His Majesty is tied up with some matters; he should be back soon, so don't rush".
"Yeah! Just temporarily tied up!" Pudom echoed from beside.
Chris lowered her head, obviously disappointed, her little cowlick losing all spirit; whenever she asked about her father, the people around seemed to have unified their response, all giving similar answers.
Xiu and Du Lu stood not far away, not approaching to tease Chris like the other demons, but watching from a distance.
"You're not going to go see Princess Chris?"
"I don't like kids; they're too much trouble." Du Lu replied in a low voice.
"Are you worried your appearance would scare her?" Xiu asked calmly.
"Young children will cry when they see me." Du Lu said helplessly.
"That child is very much like His Majesty; she wouldn't judge by appearance. My goat face is ugly enough, yet she wasn't scared and instead asked if I eat grass." Xiu recalled this embarrassing incident.
"Really?" Du Lu gazed at Chris, speaking indifferently, "I can imagine your embarrassment at that time."
Because Alice and Lilith's relationship is terribly bad, Helen must shoulder the role of mediator, trying to maintain a peaceful talk atmosphere.
Helen, as a capable subordinate of Asmodeus, without her, Lilith and the other demons would never be able to sit down and have a proper talk with Alice.
"What!?"
Alice jumped up excitedly, disbelief filling her eyes; after hearing Helen's account, she already learned of Merlin's situation.
No wonder Merlin acted strangely when he left this time; he must have realized the danger of the Seven Kings Conference!
But Alice didn't think much of it then, assuming Merlin was just attending a normal demon realm meeting, which wouldn't be dangerous.
Moreover, Merlin's strength far exceeded Alice's imagination; being subdued by an ancient artifact was something she couldn't have conceived.
"Keep your voice down, don't let Chris hear; she's still young and shouldn't know about this." Lilith furrowed her brows, emphasizing in a low voice.
Alice froze; Merlin's perilous situation indeed shouldn't be told to Chris, as it would only make the young daughter worry more.
As a mother, Alice didn't want Chris to feel anxious because of Merlin's situation; this news must be kept from her.
Chris, lacking any combat ability, couldn't help anyway; knowing this would only make her fret.
Alice slowly sat down, thinking a lot, feeling very worried about Merlin's condition, not knowing how to handle it for a while.
"Merlin, actually sealed inside a divine artifact—what can we do?"
"This is also why we came to find you, Miss Alice." Helen said sincerely.
"What should I do?" Alice urged, unable to determine whether Merlin being locked in the Demon-Sealing Vase would pose any danger.
"Break the Demon-Sealing Vase, free the souls of all imprisoned monarchs." Helen said bluntly.
"Break the Demon-Sealing Vase?" Alice exclaimed in surprise.
"Yes, only you could possibly do this." Helen paused, hesitating; in order to get Alice to wholeheartedly help, even willing to sacrifice her life, she decided to fabricate a lie, striking straight at the soft spot in Alice's heart——
"His Majesty Merlin says he deeply loves you and firmly believes that only you can free him from the Demon-Sealing Vase."
The previous chapter mainly focused on daily life scenes after a long absence, specially catering to friends who enjoy everyday stories.
After all, everyone likes different points; I can only add bits within a reasonable range.
Some like side-character stories, others don't, finding them unappealing; it's purely a matter of personal taste.
The main plot begins to advance; since this part is suitable for daily life, I wrote it, skipping the earlier parts that weren't fitting.
Finally, it's the end of the month; do you still have monthly tickets? Weren't many friends saying they'd give me theirs at month's end? I haven't seen them yet; if not given, they'll expire,

title: Chapter 8 — Sorry, I was delayed yesterday due to an urgent matter.
content:
Chapter 8 — Sorry, I was delayed yesterday due to an urgent matter.

Volume 35 · Chapter 8

Helena could not be sure whether Alice would risk everything to save Merlin and free all the sealed monarchs from the jar.
After all, they were facing an ancient demon god; Behemoth's strength cannot be compared to ordinary foes, and its danger is practically a matter of life and death!
Couples are supposed to be birds of the same forest, but when disaster strikes, they often fly apart—something Helena has seen many times; when true difficulty arises, love becomes extremely fragile.
So Helena decided to fabricate this lie, using love to dazed Alice's mind, so she could spare no effort in rescuing the monarchs.
In fact, Helena still underestimated Alice; even without resorting to such despicable tactics, she would never stand by and watch someone die—she treats everyone this way, let alone Merlin?
"Huh? He really said that?" Alice, hearing Helena's words, felt very doubtful; given her understanding of Merlin, this seemed unlikely, unless it was a dream.
"Helena, are you talking nonsense? How could my brother possibly say such mushy things to a human woman?" Lilith jumped up in anger, unable to believe it; from childhood she had hardly ever seen Merlin express affection to anyone, the only exception being when he confessed to Asmodeus in the back garden.
"It’s absolutely true; King Merlin said exactly that, and I have no need to lie." Helena put on a serious expression and continued to fan the flames, "He also said that Miss Alice is his true love; after living together for so long, he’s been very happy, but regrets not being able to express his feelings. If possible, he intends to return and formally marry Miss Alice."
"Marriage?!!" Alice’s eyes widened in shock, her face instantly flushing red, steam practically puffing from her ears; she crossed her legs over her hands, revealing a nervous, bashful demeanor, "Marriage? I’m not prepared at all—this is far too sudden."
"Ah!!!" Lilith furiously grabbed her own hair, feeling as if struck by a bolt from the blue, her head about to split, "Impossible! Impossible! How could my brother do something like this? It must be fake!"
"Princess Lilith, please calm down; these are King Merlin’s own words." Helena paused, then spoke soothingly, "Besides, it’s only natural for King Merlin and Miss Alice to have developed feelings after being together for so long; it’s not that surprising." Alice felt her face both painful and hot, likely flushed badly; though she barely kept her composure, her heart was already blooming with joy—It’s no wonder Merlin acted strangely when he was leaving, even hugging me on his own initiative. Maybe he actually wanted to confess to me then, but just couldn’t bring himself to say it. How shy can he be? He could have just said it outright. If he’d given me a heads‑up, I wouldn’t mind marrying him. Alice’s feelings were mixed: she had some resentment toward Merlin, yet also a hint of sweet, secret delight; she now really wanted to see Merlin and talk this over properly.
Helena had no idea that her inadvertent action had unintentionally torn the veil between Merlin and Alice, making it hard to imagine what their next meeting would look like.
Seeing Alice’s smug expression, Lilith grew displeased and couldn’t help shouting, "What are you so happy about? Don’t think you’ll end up together! I will never agree—give it up, you wicked human woman!"
"Does it matter whether you agree or not? Haven’t you heard?" Alice lowered her head bashfully, embarrassed, and said, "Merlin Merlin loves me—sigh, this charm of mine that has nowhere to go, should I accept Merlin’s feelings?"
"Pah! What charm does a washboard have? Stop being delusional here!" Lilith refused to believe it, even if losing to Asmodeus in women’s clothing was bad enough, losing to a washboard is simply absurd!
"What did you say? I, I’m putting in all my effort to squeeze out a— I do have something! I’m definitely not a washboard!" Alice’s face turned cold; she utterly detested being called a washboard.
"Please, you two, keep it under control." Helena trembled at the side, feeling pressured being in the middle, "The most important thing now is to rescue King Merlin and the other monarchs sealed in the jar."
"Ugh! Having to rely on a human is nothing short of our disgrace!" Lilith muttered through gritted teeth.
"Don’t worry, I’ll do everything I can to free Merlin from the jar—after all..." Alice glanced at Lilith with a challenging gaze, provoking her, "It’s the duty of a future wife, after all~"
Helena felt a bit relieved, thinking her lie had worked, and quickly asked, "Miss Alice, could you show me the sword you carry?"
"No problem." Alice drew the slender sword Light’s Lament, this artifact radiating holy aura from head to toe, displaying it before the demons.
Helena was about to reach out to touch Light’s Lament, but suddenly, for no apparent reason, she pulled her hand back; she felt an terrifying holy radiance, and any casual touch would surely burn her. This was merely the sword’s aura in a calm state—one can only imagine how much its pressure would increase when actually used.
"The holy aura emanating from it is no inferior to that of the Demon‑Sealing Jar; using the light attribute to counter darkness should be able to destroy the jar,"
"But what?" Alice slipped the slender sword back into its sheath, asking in surprise.
"Miss Alice, what level have your abilities reached now?" Helena asked eagerly.
Alice’s body exuded a chilling aura; releasing the pressure of a pseudo‑god realm in a tiny area, this accounted for her full strength.
Lilith felt a mix of amusement and astonishment as she stared at Alice, thinking, "How long has it been? This woman has already become strong enough to fight a Demon Lord on equal terms?! Why has her power grown so quickly?"
Helena was equally surprised, but her face showed a hint of disappointment as she slowly said, "Miss Alice, your strength is no longer weak, yet it is still far from enough to rescue King Merlin."
Alice furrowed her brows and asked, "Why?"
"To destroy the Demon‑Sealing Jar, one must face the ancient demon god Behemoth—the creator of the demon race; only a great prophet in history has been able to suppress it. Do you truly have confidence in defeating such a mighty ancient god?" Helena probed.
"Hah! Impossible? She’s barely qualified to hand the monarchs their shoes; if she could beat Behemoth, it would only be if the goddess of luck permanently stood by her side~" Lilith muttered sourly from the side.
Alice said nothing, merely lowering her head to ponder; she indeed lacked the strength to confront the ancient god head‑on, and without the White Dragon clan chief’s help she couldn’t even defeat the crippled ancient god Nid in Ge, let alone a fully powered Behemoth— it seemed saving Merlin wouldn’t be as simple as she’d thought; relying on herself alone probably wouldn’t work.
Late at night, Alice came alone to the courtyard and gazed up at the myriad stars.
She wanted to find allies to jointly attack Behemoth, which would be far better than hoping to do it alone.
After thinking it over, the force most likely to give full support seemed to be only the demons’ sworn enemy, the Holy Church of Light.
Alice lowered her head and looked at the pope’s handwritten letter she held; her heart began to stir with eager anticipation—
With this letter, she could return to the Vatican sanctuary at any time and once again become the focus of everyone’s attention as the Hero.

title: Chapter 9 — Hero Candidate (Yesterday's Update)
content:
Chapter 9 — Hero Candidate (Yesterday's Update)

Volume 35 · Chapter 9

One month later, to deal with the impending crisis, resist the awakening ancient Demon God, and protect the peace of the mortal world...

Almost all human kingdoms had become highly alert. During this period, they frantically expanded their militaries and prepared for war, reinforcing city walls and fortresses in an extremely short time.

However, humanity remained in a fragmented state. Everyone hoped to escape this disaster unscathed, without any unity in confronting the threat from the ancient god.

Many kingdoms that had signed the "Human Alliance" pact with the Church did not respond to the Church's call to consolidate most of their forces under the Church's command. Instead, each played their own calculations, hoping to gain profit from the disaster.

This infuriated Pope George, who once wanted to incite believers around the world to rise in rebellion, to teach those disobedient rulers a lesson and make them willingly hand over their power.

The only ones who could respond and support the Church were several kingdoms within the sphere of the Holy Roman势力. The Church wielded great influence in these regions.

As for the northern areas, even those that had signed the "Human Alliance" pact mostly started playing dumb, as if they hadn't heard Pope George's call.

Britain, Prussia, France and the like were all watching and waiting for now. There was no way they would easily hand over the forces guarding their kingdoms to the Church.

George knew very well that Behemoth had only just awakened. The demon race was not yet completely unified internally, and surely many demons unwilling to be enslaved would rebel.

This was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity — they could use the remnants of the demon race's strength to deliver a crushing blow against the ancient Demon God before it had firmly taken root, and at the same time weaken the demon race, robbing them of any possibility of rising again.

However, Pope George's long-planned "Human Alliance" could achieve very limited results at such a critical moment. He hadn't expected those respectable-looking rulers to have no sense of contract at all, refusing to fully support the Church's actions according to the agreement.

If George had known earlier that these lofty royal families were just playing dumb, he would certainly have incited the believers to overthrow them, choosing puppets loyal to the Church to take over each kingdom. It wouldn't have come to this isolated struggle.

"These bastards!" Pope George tore Elizabeth's letter into shreds, cursing angrily. "They actually say they need to rebuild towns destroyed by demons and can't send hands to assist! Elizabeth recently recruited a powerful mercenary company to reinforce the army, and now they're saying they're short-staffed?!"

Blackford hesitated and asked, "What about France? They've always respected the Church."

"Hmph! They only respect the Church on the surface, and their skill at passing the buck is first-rate!" Pope George's face darkened, his brows furrowed. "France replied yesterday. Princess Margaret said her father was ill and she couldn't make decisions, telling us to wait patiently. Other than the Church's territories, almost all kingdoms gave similar responses. They'd rather let the mortal world be shrouded in the ancient Demon God's shadow than take out their own resources. How ridiculous!"

"This is too much. Our Knights Templar have died at every corner of the world fighting against the dark forces, and yet they refuse to contribute even a fraction of strength to the Church?" Blackford was somewhat indignant, clearly feeling this was deeply unfair.

"These arrogant royal families wish nothing more than our deaths. The Church has so many believers, constantly threatening their rule. I suspect they'd be more than happy to see us suffer heavy losses," Pope George ground out through clenched teeth.

"Perhaps we could seek some aid from the Adventurers Guild..." Blackford suggested.

"A bunch of rabble can't be relied upon. If it doesn't affect them directly, adventurers will only shout slogans of freedom and watch from the sidelines," Pope George said, furious, falling into a violent coughing fit.

Blackford quickly supported George and helped him sit down, comforting him, "Please take care of your health. We will surely find a way."

"It's no use. We can only rely on ourselves. Time is running short. If that ancient Demon God establishes a firm foothold, we'll lose our chance to defeat it." Pope George's brows tightened, and a thought struck him. "Unless we can lure it to the cathedral..."

"If we were to use the power left by the Goddess, it would surely shake our very foundations. I fear we'd no longer be able to resist the threat from hell afterward," Blackford strongly advised against this.

George stared into Blackford's eyes and said solemnly, "I have no choice if I want the Human Alliance to succeed. Only when humanity becomes a community is there any chance of resisting all dangers."

Blackford shuddered, awed by George's resolute will. Perhaps he wasn't a devout believer of the Goddess, but he was unquestionably a pioneer standing on humanity's side.

At that moment, a Knight Templar walked in and leaned close to Blackford's ear, whispering something. Blackford's expression suddenly changed drastically. "What?"

"What happened?" Pope George asked in confusion.

Blackford licked his dry lips and said softly, "Former Hero Alice Claudya has suddenly returned to the cathedral's training ground. Many young people are practicing magic and martial arts there, constantly sparring with one another."

The news of the 234th Hero Subjugation selection had already spread like wildfire. Many believers of considerable strength were itching to try their luck, hoping to become names recorded in history.

Dying in battle for the great Goddess was an honor for any believer. They cherished the opportunity to swing their swords for the Goddess and deeply practiced the mission of protecting humanity.

On the battlefield, every demon they slayed was a trophy to show off upon return and proof of their devout faith. Demon heads were the best medals of merit.
